text:
The pizza is terrible, but if you need a place to watch a game or just down some pitchers, this place works.

Oh, and the pasta is even worse than the pizza.
Food here is very consistent and good for a quick lunch or dinner. I usually order the garlic bread and salad; however, their pizza, especially the bbq chicken, is pretty good too.

Meh.

I got the Chicken Parmesan. The noodles and sauce both seemed to be sub-par quality. Chicken wasn't too bad though. I wish I would have gotten pizza or something, but I thought the Chicken Parm would be better.

The place is well decorated, however. So that was nice. 

It's convenient. But it's college food and not at its best.

A cheap place to stop in and get lunch if you have class on the north side.  I miss the other location.  A lot of times they will have a lunch special available and it's in your best interest to take advantage of it when you're tired of eating Fat Slice.

I come here every few months, usually to see a show at Impact Theater (their space is in La Val's basement).  The pizza is OK, though not spectacular.  Last week, my wife & I ordered a medium LaVal's special (Pepperoni, Salami, Linguica, Beef, Black Olives, Sausage, Mushrooms, Bell Peppers and Onions).  It was good and filling, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here if it wasn't for the shows.

During the school year, the place is very busy with students on Friday and Saturday nights.  But there is seating outdoors if the weather is nice.

I don't like La Val's. the pizza here is just not very good. The pasta dishes are meh and personally I've had better. They're a good place for college students but I don't like eating here. I try to avoid it. 

The only thing they got going for them is the place is awesome. Sitting inside is nice, its a bit loud especially during big games. It's got large booths and plenty of space for big large groups including post review session hang outs.

I like thin crust pizza, and la val's has the thinnest crust in berkeley! Their creative toppings and pizza combinations are really worth trying! If you are a pizza lover, you'll like this place! It's definitely worth making a trip out here to try their pizza! And if you are lazy, get it delivered :)  (FREE DELIVERY!! YAY for LAZY PEOPLE!!)

If you're on the north side of campus and want a quick lunch and don't want La Burrita, this is the place to go! This place is also good for group dinners too. They sell pizzas by the slice, and have lots of variety. I really like the Athenian slice! The pizzas can take a while to come out though

Their margherita pizza is great! Don't get their pastas--they're badly made, I can make way better pasta. There's sports on and a pool table. The prices are good but unfortunately there's no discount for buying in bulk really.

Decent pizza place. Great for groups b/c it's so spacious. It's a step above the sketchy Fat Slice and Blondie's. I like their combo pizzas, but after having tasted more gourmet pizzas like Zachary's and Cheeseboard's, you'd never go back to La Val's. I mainly went there for convenience after slaving over a stubborn program in Soda Hall, back in the college days...

I think they have the best pizza in Berkeley!  But get there before lunch because the line goes out the door. The price is unbeatable, $2.50 for a slice and a soda and their thin crust it deeelish!!  mmmmm...  the margharita slice is my favorite! They put tons of garlic!

This is a nice La Val's. It has big screen TVs playing sports and a pool table in the back. The pizza is just ok as always, but the garlic bread is delicious. 

Back in the days it was nice to take a break from the dreariness of Soda Hall have dinner, and play a game of pool, before going back to program.

It is unfortunate the north side LaVals (on euclid) shares the same name w/ the others (albany and south side) because it is so much better.  The menu there is different and much improved.  The pizza is thin crust and delic including great combos like blt. The toppings are really good. You can also get a slice and a drink for 2.99.  It's awesome. And there is lots of room unlike any other restaurant near north side campus.

fast, fun, and has a nice vibe with outdoor seating and pool tables and such. thin crust ftw. 
great for a pre-concert meal because it's in walking distance to the Greek! :)
The pizza is yummy, great crust, decent portion of toppings. The salads are good as are their sandwiches. Spacious inside. Cheap prices.
Not a bad place. The kitchen is the same for la burrita. The food was delicious and the price very reasonable. However, the wait was long. I came here on a monday night.
Pizza was good, if you're willing to eat in a construction site. Can't blame them for staying open during their "seismic retrofit" but it's not a very pleasant dining experience.

VERY good prices here. Especially on their pizzas; I like to get the personal pizzas. You can get discount from berkeley good life as well. The slices are large and scrumptious. Not GREAT, but average quality. The pastas are pretty good, too.

I have been here a few times, and I have always been happy with the food.  It is good, but not memorable.  Although, the garlic bread is really good!  What is nice about La Val's is the really big seating area with the big screen tv.  It is a great place to watch games. There is also a pinball machine!

NASTY pizza. Had a few slices here for dinner and the crust ruined the entire pizza. To start, the top of the pizza had about a liter of grease sitting on top of the cheese. Unless you grabbed a few paper towels to dry up the grease, the pizza is simply inedible. The crust, like the top of the pizza, was equally, if not more disgusting. It was thin (less than 2mm I would say) and almost soaked through with grease. The kind folks of La Val might argue that it's high quality olive oil they're using, but in the end, it comes down to how it tastes, not the quality of ingredients you use that you'll get judged on. For me, the taste was not there. 

I would recommend somewhere like Little Caesers over La Vals.

Ah, La Vals. My sanctuary on the Northside. The only place that sells beer on tap--sometimes warm, but we figured it out, so don't get Bass there-- within super close walking distance to GSPP & Haviland Hall. The place that has yummy slices and salads and where MPP's, Engineering PhD's, J-School peeps and Social Welfare folk glare at each other as we try to compare who has the heaviest workload (Engineers always win, except in the rare occasion when an Electrical Engineering and Computer Science student emerges from the dark programming hole that is Soda Hall). It is also the only place that has ESPN playing on the Northside, so I was able to run over there and check the scores during the playoffs. 

Within walking distance also to my house, but why bother walking when they deliver in friggin' 20 minutes?!!?!?!? Always super fast delivery. If you want to dine in there are multiple TV's and a pool table. Weekends there is theater in the basement, but I have yet to experience that for no good reason at all. 

Simply put, La Val's is our go-to for pizza delivery, and a favorite congregating spot on the Northside.

Northside restaurants are like hidden gems because a lot of Cal students either don't know about them or are too lazy to make the trip up there. Fools.
La Val's is very affordable Italian food that doesn't skimp on portions and is packed with flavor. 
Broccoli and Chicken Penne: Definitely recommend! The chicken was very flavorful and and the penne was cooked perfectly. The garlic bread that comes with it was mediocre. I've had much better but whatevs.

Just went here for lunch with a couple of friends. We went at lunchtime, so there was a pretty long line. Never fear though. The line moves fast. We decided to split a medium between me (girl) plus 2 guys. Each pizza is cut into 8 pieces.

Unfortunately, we waited a good while before we got our pizza. Probably, all the people who ordered single slices got theirs before our whole pizza. *NOTE: buy slices during rush hour. It's much faster.

Another thing, individual slices come from their XL pizzas, meaning they are HUGE. Makes me giddy just thinking about it. Wish I had gotten that instead, but the medium was still good, albeit probably not enough for the 3 of us.

I love the VEGGIE/GARDEN pizza here. It is AMAZING (although for juiciness and more substantial-ness, I'd go for Blondie's)

The Athenian is tasty too, but I still don't really like olives, and the only cheese being a couple sprinkles of feta = lacking.

BBQ chicken pizza = delicious, lots of chicken chunks.

Thin crust, yummeh. Throw on oregano, parmesan cheese, and red pepper flakes and you're good.

I want to come back to try some pasta and sandwiches sometime (combo coupon deals from BerkeleyGoodLife.com).

Goods: Fast (relatively), big slices, yummy, good ingredients, big menu, nice seating with TVs and cool wall decor
Bads: waited a bit for a whole pizza during rush hour, medium not enough for 3 people

This is the default option. Not sure where to go? Empty fridge, need food but too tired to think? The pizza is hot and fast, cheap food and drinks. It's nothing special but so easy. The default option. 
There are multiple big screen TVs to watch while waiting or eating. Dining with a group or solo is no problem. 
The pizza itself - yeh it's fine. You can buy slices of premade or whole pizzas with your choice combination.
Great pizza and salads!

I used to come here a ton for their individual-sized pizza specials. It's ~$5.70 with tax and a free drink. The BBQ chicken is my favorite. The pizzas take awhile to make, so I usually order my pizza online and walk over to pick it up. They lost my online order once (although it was fairly crowded for a weekend night), and I haven't gone as often since that experience. It's pretty good pizza for the price.

Extra Large Athenian for pick-up please!!!!

I wish they delivered to downtown Oakland.

I love this place, especially hung over on a Sunday to watch football with all of my friends.  The pizza is above average but nothing to yell about.  The dough comes crunchy and they have A LOT of toppings.  But the true reason why this place is great is its atmosphere and location.

Its got...
-Two T.V.'s (one flat screen and another huge projection screen)
-A pool table
-A couple video games
-Large seating areas 

The prices are also good.

Not the greatest pizza I've ever had, but they give you a huge slice and a soda for really cheap.  I wasn't happy when they raised the price to $2.99, but that just makes for less change I have to carry around the rest of the day.  Happy hour is fun too, especially when you split a pitcher right before lab, going to class buzzed is always fun.
I've had their pizza delivered to my apartment and the pizza was so delicious that I couldn't wait to eat the leftovers the next day for lunch.

I like this place... they have good pizzas and have reasonable prices... To make it even better, they have coupons online that you can print out and bring with you... I'm always up for $3 off my pizza!

Pros:
Chicken afredo
BBQ chicken pizza
Big TV+ one small LCD TV
Pool table
Typical Classic pizza place, good for hanging out with friends/classmates.

Cons:
The seats/table are kinda old and there is an odd smell in the restaurant.
Really damn good pizza.  But the pastas are terrible and overpriced.

Pretty relaxing place to go and eat pizza - I like the ambiance! There's a giant TV that plays sports all the time and it just feel very cozy inside. Their pizza a little less expensive than some of the other places I've been too, and I like how obviously handmade they are (each slice is not perfect slice-shape, but is huge)!

La Vals pizza is good and cheap! The veggie is refreshing with slices of zucchini. I enjoy the online ordering option, makes it very easy to order and pick up dinner. Also, the prices are awesome, both for slices and for whole pizzas. Nice beer selection and the garden salad isn't bad. I wonder how busy this place will get when UCB starts :(

I was rather disappointed being new to Btown, and discovering there are no Mountain Mike's or Papa John's nearby, and that the first few pizza places I called don't deliver.

I finally found La Val's number. Ordered an easy pep and ground sausage for my first dinner in my new apartment- very good, and very cheap and quick. I ordered and the delivery guy showed up in less than 30 mins (it was a Thursday night after 8pm). Medium w/ 2 tops only $13-sweet!

Go La Val's! You got yourselves a new custy!!

The atmosphere is nice, but the pizza was certainly nothing to come back for.  I'd much rather have Blondie's or Fat Slice.  They have a big screen TV so people tend to congregate to watch the current game.  They do have plenty of seating, but with video games and a big screen TV all in the same area, it can tend to get loud.

I used to have a roommate who felt that LaVal's had the best pizza in Berkeley, mostly due to its superior sauce compared to its competitors. I have tried LaVal's a number of times over the years, and I'm sad to report that it's a clear third (at most) in the Berkeley area (not including Zachary's, which is like comparing Filet Mignon to McDonald's $1 Double Cheeseburger).

For me, it's third amongst the pedestrian pizza places - Fat Slice and Blondie's. (I don't think it's a coincidence that LaVal's is the only one that had to close up shop on the South Side). Anyway, back to my original point, my friend stated that they had good sauce... sadly, however, I have trouble finding the pizza sauce on the slices I recently had. They were dry, undersauced (even if the sauce was good), and under-cheesed.

Overall, sub-par.

Good value and ambiance in the splendor of the Northside.  Go for the La Val's Special.  Their pizza is thin crust and always fresh tasting.  It's no Cheeseboard, but it is orders of magnitude better than Domino's.  The Chicken Parmigiana or Alfredo pastas are decent and reasonably priced in an area of Berkeley without much Italian food.  The meatball sandwich was good, so it's also a good place to go if you are on the northside and have a Point Break hankering.

i've only been to this place once, but I think it nice and will probably come back another time before leaving Berkeley.

I unfortunately did not try the pizza, but I can say that the hot sandwich is tasty.  I got the turkey one, but I'm sure others are equally nice.  The sandwiches are not big portion, but are pretty good.

The ambiance is great, but the real reason people go to restaurants --- the food --- absolutely stinks. The sandwiches have too much bread and not enough quality, and the pizza is worse than Domino's.

The only redeeming feature of this place is that it's open late in Northside Berkeley.

La Val's Special isn't really anything special, but it's filling and shameless. The crust of this mini pizza is just the right thickness (not thick) and the tomato sauce tastes like a hot tomato on bread yummmm
+ they give you a free drink with the mini pizza.

They have reasonable prices for their salads and sides. I tried the spicy chicken wings and they're decent.

The lunch line can get long pretty quickly, but you can also call ahead for your pizza. I called ten minutes before I got there and it was ready by the time I was in line to pay for it. If you're in the area, stop by, but don't go too out of your way to try the menu.

They also have televisions and guitar hero! Check online for coupons.
I have no major complaints or raves about La Val's. The pizza is okay. The prices are okay. I mostly come here to use their change machine.

They have about 20+ things on tap. And if you don't count things that aren't beer (e.g., Bud) they still have about 12+ beers on tap. That made me really happy. The casual pizza/beer atmosphere was wonderful for a late dinner last night. The folks were really nice and the customers weren't super crazy either like you'd expect sometimes in a college town. Also they have things like pool tables and arcade machines, which made them pretty awesome in my book.

The pizza was really good. We had a special pizza with feta, tomato and basil and a basket of fried mushroos and zuccini. The wait was reasonable for a pizza made from scratch. The pizza was delicious but surprisingly not filling. Similarly the veggies came in pretty small portions. The prices were okay, but not great either. Hence the 4 stars.

On game day we wandered miserably downtown, every institution packed with a line with raging Vols. The only open spot was a couple of stools in the basement at Blake's. no no no no.  We walked across campus, to northside to la val's, found immediate seating at a picnic table under a shady tree. Perfect. The median age was 10-20 years -- or more -- orlder than the undergrads on telegraph, but well we're not undergrads anymore.  Cheap pitchers and thin crust pizza.

All non-pizza dishes are utterly tasteless.  That's not as bad as actually tasting bad, as they just have no taste whatsoever.

The pizza is okay, at best.  Some would say that the pizza quality is directly proportional to the time you have to spend soaking grease off the top.  I suppose it would asymptote to some maximum goodness level.  Unfortunately, this level is not terribly high. 

This place is serviceable because it is convenient and fairly cheap.  That free drink crap is bs, though.  If you order two slices, they try to give you a "free" large drink to go with it.  If you insist that you do not want the "free" drink, they charge you less...most of the time.  Sometimes the cashier is just too lazy to type in the change.

Used to my favorite pizza, must be new ownership because I'd go so far as to say: 
LA VAL'S SUCKS NOW.

We ordered a thick crust pizza  and I've had a La Val's thick crust many times before....it was always amazing, this was NOT a thick crust. 

We ordered it with tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, garlic and cilantro, half with pepperoni (my fiance is a vegetarian),

The tomatoes were half white, obviously not ripened yet....I tasted no garlic and there was barely ANY cilantro...the cilantro that was on there was chopped up stems more than anything. When you pay $1.50 for something that comes in 2 bushels for $0.99, there should at least be some cilantro leaves on there. It was a soppy thin crust with barely any flavor.  Not at all the La Val's I remember. Not at all.

Anyways, I thought it was an extremely poor excuse for a pizza, and I will never eat there again.  

Don't you restaurants know there's Yelp out there?!?!?!
i only eat here when i'm watching football, and for that. it's fine, just very average pizza, especially when cheeseboard is just down the hill...

When I was living in Foothill my first year at Berkeley, it was hard to find good, affordable places to eat. Living on a student's budget can be tough, but Euclid had a few decent places to go for a study break with friends. La Val's has a decent selection of pizza and pasta, and if you want to sit with a book and eat or go with friends for a cheap night out, it's pretty good. The fettucini alfredo was creamy and al dente, but I wouldn't make a habit of eating here. The food is pretty heavy.
Great spot for a casual quick lunch.

I did a show at Impact Theatre (underneath La Vals) and ate here most nights before the show with the cast to hang out. It is nothing amazing... but a good place to hang out at. Big TVs for sporting events and a good atmosphere.
I remember the Barbecue Chicken and the two veggie pizzas being good. The sandwiches are awesome also.

La Val's doesn't have absolutely amazing pizza, but it's huge and has good flavor. 

A GIA-NORMOUS slice of cheese and some brew for $6 buckaroo's. . .not too shabby, especially if you're taking a study break and want to grab some pizza, maybe watch some of the playoffs.

Quick and friendly service - my only qualm is that you can not customize your own individual slice; they only sell mini pies. . .

Nice place to fuel up and study.
So good!  I've ordered from them twice now, and both times everyone who was with me loved it.   Fast and delicious.

La Val's has wonderful pizza!  It's thin and crispy with delicious toppings (always try their slice of the day, or try the greek slice with feta and olives!), and the personal slices are as big as your head.  It's cheap too.  
They also have good beer on tap, and quite reasonably priced pitchers.  Did I mention the big screen tv's in the dining area?  They always have the big games playing and who doesn't want to watch some sports action with a great pizza and a round of beers??
Excellent prices, I must say again.  Bring your buddies here for a great evening.

The best pizza in Berkeley. I usually get the Athenian and the vegetarian ones. They are both excellent, inexpensive (with coupon) and fresh ingredients. But then again I do not understand the obsession with the cheeseboard (eating on that little strip of grass next to the exhaust pipes of passing cars???). I like it better than the Cheeseboard and Gioia, these other two places come next in my list in the area of Berkeley.
Good pizza, that's just it. Good pizza, not great pizza. Good beer and TV's for watching sports makes this place a good place to hang out. Not overly impressed but I'd go back.

La Val's doesn't really do much wrong. It has a great pizza lunch deal, $5ish sandwiches hot/cold, and plenty of seating with nice TV's. In addition they will take my prized American Express card.

That said, nothing there is really...memorable. It's a pizza/sandwich/pasta/salad place that provides fair value and decent food. If I'm too busy thinking about more important things to agonize about where to eat, La Val's is a place to go.

Plus they're open til 10p, which is rare on Northside.

Ack! More delicious pizza! I had 3 slices and am getting fat!

Who cares about the rest of the menu? PIZZA = #1 favorite food of all time!

Value + taste + quality = a great lunch spot.  Nice NY style thin crust dough with some chew to it.  Good sauce, plenty of toppings plus a nicer newly remodeled dining area full of wannabe Euro trash soccer fans watching futbol on the bigscreen (okay, I guess there are a lot of foreign students on this side of campus and Soccer is the most played sport in the world).  Under 4 bucks for a giant meal sized slice and a soda.

Pizza, beer, cheap prices, big ass TV; I'm definitely a fan. I grabbed lunch here very often during my summer spent at Cal and the food was good every single time. You can get a big combo slice for $2.75+tax and it comes with a free small drink during lunch hours. They also have salads and pasta on their menu and according to people eating with me, those items are well prepared too but I can only opine on the pizza. 
Try the athenian, it was surprisingly good!

There is plenty of seating space in and around the place and they even have a few arcade machines and pool table.

Celebratory beer!   The husband passed his qualifying exams, PhD. here we come!!  We grabbed two pints and shared a slice of pepperoni for $10.  It was the perfect end to a really long weekend.  They have a lot of beer on tap for cheap and the pizza was big enough for two people for a snack.  Not much for ambiance but, let's be honest, it doesn't matter.
Pizza is just average, however they have a good lunch special I always bought while attending Cal.

A good place to watch sports on the large-flat screen television and have a beer.  And the food is better than one might think.  Both the pizzas and pastas are decent -- think the quality of higher-end frozen dinners.  They won't wow you, but you'll be reasonably happy.  Much better than the La Val's on the south side of campus.
Great pizza, good "Slide of the Day" deals, and good seating to sit and enjoy.  This is one of the few places I've been in the Bay Area that served pizza that reminds me of thin-crust NY pizza!

What a great deal. $3.50 for a slice of pizza and drink. 

The pizza was really good and doesn't have a ton of bread like Fat Slice on telegraph. The ingredients seemed like they were higher quality. 
Will come back to try their pasta some time.

I've had two of their hot sandwiches, the Veggie and the Chicken Parmesan. I usually love love love breaded and deep fried chicken, but the Chicken Parmesan was just.. ehhh for me. But, the Veggie sandwich is really really good! Watch out for the red onions though, a little overpowering, unless you like it like that. 

They have a good variety in pizzas, check out the Classic BLT & the Margarita!

I feel this Rating system is inadequate for one of my favorite neighborhood restaurant. 

Their "Caezar's Chicken Pizza" under specialty pizza is a must have if you are a meat eater. 
If you are a college student, La Val's is a great option for late-night, Sunday eating. I know my hunger have been filled many times by their incredible late-night deals. 

I recommend getting a "Good Life Guide to Berkeley" book and using their couples in there to save some money.

Taste: 3
Value: 4
Service: 3

I've been to La Val's a couple times, maybe 5-7 times total? Their pizza by the slice is absolutely huge, and two slices look almost as big as an entire medium pizza. Their La Val's special pizza is all right, but definitely not as good as Cheeseboard. Still, it's reasonably cheap and close by campus, so at least it's convenient.

I've tried their grilled chicken sandwich, and it's not bad given it's only $5. Today, I decided to drop by since I was out of cash, and ended up ordering the California club special (turkey, bacon, and avocado). The sandwich was pretty well made, and it was nice that they toasted the bread. However, my sandwich barely had any avocado in it.

It usually takes a while to get food here, so if you go when there's a line, be prepared to wait at least 10-15 minutes for your food to arrive after you order.

La Val's is amazing. Although I can never bring myself to schlep up to Northside, it's definitely a place I should go more often. 

The lunch specials are amazing. The prices are just right and the food is pretty good. While the pasta portions are a bit too small for my taste, I am a Southsider used to Gypsy's, it's still definitely good grub. I'd say the food is better than Gypsy's too. I also feel like less of a fatty when I get my pizza from La Val's rather than Blondie's or Fat Slice. The pizzas are thin-crusted and less oily which are pluses in my book!

What makes this place amazing though is how big it is. There's indoor and outdoor seating. Indoor seating has access to pretty sweet flat screen TVs where you can catch highlights of Sports Center or just chat away with people you're with. If you want to bring back your inner child, you can show off your pinball skills while you wait for food too.

The only thing that annoys me is that their beer is kinda warm. What's up with that bro?!

Had to go see a play for my theatre class. Walked through the door and smelled the Pizza. My sister, some friends, and i all were starving after teh play ended. So we decided to try the Pizza and it was SO GOOD!!! It was a big slice tons of peperoni and chesse on it... If im ever in the area again, I no where im stopping to get some food!!

The pizza is mediocre at best, but hell their slice special during lunch makes it hard to beat. There are a lot of seats, but even during lunch it is packed. Go any other time and it is average eats but quick seat finding.
I adore the huge $2.50 slices of cheese pizza. They're so good! Veggie's not bad, too. Stay away from the margherita!
Lavals South side has been closed for two years.

The slices are extremely greasy and not really that great. Half the time the wait for them is just as long as anything else or even longer. They need to get some industrial engineers to optimize their work flow or something. The minis are quite tasty and good for the price. Pasta is decent, not great but not bad. Sandwiches are surprisingly good, but they are cheap for a reason - you'll need to way something else too if type especially hungry.
The place smelled like a farm and the pizza crust tasted like a carpet.  Only reason it got another star is because of its location.
Had an order of the Pesto and Penne (~$7): eggplant, red onions, & mushroom in pesto sauce. Food was delicious, staff was orderly, and the ambiance was fun.
Good pizza, convenient location.

The pizza is decent so I enjoy going her for lunch every once in a while. They have lots of pasta dishes too which are reasonably priced. It's a good place to catch some sports events, especially soccer.

So, this place was better when I was a little kid and they still had that dirty green carpet and the photo-wallpaper of the campus. their pizza was DEFINITELY better in the past, and they're pasta has been better too. either way though, it's always going to be my favorite place to go to after CAL games. that will NEVER change, no matter how disgusting it seems to get.

Eh, I only come here when I HAVE to. I like pizza when it's good!

Call ahead to order in advance! Works especially well during peak hours when there's a 10+ long person line. 

Also, coupons in the Berkeley Good Life booklet online!

I go to LaVals because they are always playing fantastic music.

Oh, Kavita S - you must be too busy to listen to music. You are so important.

Pros:
-fine for a quick beer and a slice with the classmates or on your way to something else
-cheap

Cons:
-pizza is just mediocre
-pasta dishes are NOT very good
-like everything on Euclid, the place gets crazy crowded at games and events
-service can take a while depending on what you order
I am not really a fan of their pizza and other foods, but their sandwiches are actually quite good.  The torpedo sub is particularly delicious.

Since I work on the north side of the Cal campus, I've been to La Vals about a billion and a half times. I've also gotten delivery 2 or 3 times. Eat in if you can. The pizza here is very decent, but is the best when it's freshly baked and hasn't been sitting in a delivery car for 20 minutes. My husband and I discovered probably the best deal for food here with the "mini" pizza. The "mini" is actually probably 9-10 inches in diameter. You get a free soda with it too! Get a side green salad and you have a nice little meal, all for about $8. This is a steal, really. They also have pizza by the slice for $3-4. These are good, but not as good as freshly baked crust as they just reheat it in their oven. There are a lot of paninis and pastas on the menu, all of which I think are kind of meh. So to sum up: go for a fresh pizza. Very tasty, lots of options!
I'd give it a solid 3.5/5, but I'll round up to 4.

We ordered from here 3 times for takeout and will no longer order from them again. The pizza was mediocre and the pasta was terrible. Each time we ordered from them the 3 different drivers got lost and we had to walk two blocks to find them down the street. We order takeout quite a bit from other places and they have never gotten lost or had a problem finding our place. The food is not worth the effort of playing hide and seek with the delivery drivers.

For delivery, these guys are THE best!  The pizza's always hot, fresh, and often, very fast!  We order from them about once a week.  The kids love the cheeze pizza, and I personally love my latest creation of sausage, fresh basil, fresh tomato, and garlic.  Oh yeah!  The sauce, cheese, and crust (thin) are always consistently good.  And so much improved from my Cal days, way back when...

I never thought I would, but I'm kind of hooked on this pizza. It's thin and crispy and delicious. Over on North campus every time it's pizza it's always la val's, which actually makes me excited when i hear "pizza" at an event. yum. sometimes the people taking the order are a little inefficient, and the people making the food are also a little inefficient, but you don't have to wait terribly long. The seating is great and open and airy. the lunch special is really the deal. one giant slice and a drink for 3.25 inc tax. i get hungry just thinking about it now...
there's something about the yeasty taste of the crust that i just love at this place....
Doesn't compete with Zachary's Pizza, deep dish or normal pizza

This review is dedicated to MK & AK.

I didn't get to eat here as much as I wanted to because of the distance. (I'm pretty lazy.) But this place is pretty awesome.

This is what I recommend that you do:
1) Make two awesome friends, and find a date you guys can spend at least 3 hours together.
2) Get tickets online (cheaper!) to watch Disassembly at the Impact Theatre. (It's inside La Val's. You can even order food if you arrive early for the show and take food downstairs. It's really cozy.)
3) If you live more than 5 blocks away, drive to Euclid and street park. It's free around dinner time. (Hopefully one of your friends drive. :D )
4) Watch the show. Laugh, cry, and be confused. The experience is totally worth $10! :D (We all meant to go for the past 4 years, but didn't really get to until our last.)
5) Try to order the pear cider only to find out that it's not carried anymore. Hopefully, your friend knows the manager. He'll mix some lemonade, cider, and wine for you and your friends instead for FREEE!
6) Order hot wings, medium sized pizza (half La Val's Special, half Garden Delight), and Chicken Alfredo.
7) BEAST on all the delicious food! YUMZ! (The pasta is especially good, not too greasy or salty.)

I've pretty much tried all the pizzas (delivered) and La Val's aren't the best in Berkeley (After all, how can places compete with gourmet pizzas like Cheeseboard, Little Star, and Zachary's?). 3 stars. But the experience of watching a show and eating afterwards makes La Val's 5 stars! Dine-in at least once, and don't just order pizza. Make sure to order some appetizers and pasta too. You'll be coming back for more. :D
Pizza was excellent. Great pricing. Good beer to boot, along with watching the world cup. You can't go wrong.

Have to agree with Shane H. (7/6/2011) about baaaaaaad delivered pizza.  I have fond memories of La Val's from years past.  Not any longer.  Delivery was prompt; I'll give them that.  But, I'm not sure the pizza was fully cooked when it left the restaurant.  It was certainly lukewarm by the time it got to us.  And, I'm not that far away.  Saw no evidence that the pizza was kept in the type of thermal heat bags that Round Table and Domino's use.  Good Caesar salad though.  I think the food can still be great.  It's not a good delivery option.

Cool place to come grab a brew and bite after classes.  While pizza isn't very hard to screw up, La Val's definitely serves up quite a decent pie.  The portions are great for the amount you pay, and they have a decent selection of beers on tap.  Definitely a great 'hangout' spot, but entirely too 'forgettable'.

Don't know why everyone is so down on La Val's.. this place is keeping me alive through college! lol. The pizza is great. I love thin crust, though. A lot of ppl complain they don't like La Val's b/c it's not deep dish... Anyway, love the location and the atmosphere of this place. Love, love, love the option to order online. I pop in an order while I'm studying, and by the time I get there it's waiting for me!

La Val's is great.

Good pizza, not too expensive, beers on tap.

It is NOT the center of student-life and NOT the first place to go if you are visiting Berkeley, but locals consider it a go-to when they just want some quick pizza on a regular night, and you want it to taste good without costing too much. 

I definitely do not consider this to be NY-style pizza (which is awful, I don't understand why anyone who has had California-style pizza would ever want that super-thin grease-loaded crap).  This is much closer to Round Table with rising crust, not too much sauce or cheese, some seasoning and a good selection of toppings.  

It is definitely not healthy, but you won't feel overly bloated after eating two slices.

This is a great lunch pizza place. Tasty pizza if you're like me and into thin toothy crust. (Toothy? Yes, I've been reading too much Cook's Illustrated.) The Athenian slice is excellent. It's also cheap ($6.50 for a soda and two slices), and you can sit outside in the courtyard on nice days.

Oh, and don't be fooled by the line to the register at lunch. If you're getting a slice instead of a fresh pizza, it's remarkably quick (usually a good bit quicker that getting a burrito next door.)

I try and take perspective in to rating a place, and for a pizza place in the Bay Area, this comes highly recommended. The Bay doesn't do pizza well, and when it does it's either a million dollars, or Chicago style (or both). Not always of course, but it's not this area's strength. 

This place gets 4 stars because it serves enormous (!!) slices of New York style at a fantastic price. If this place was in San Jose, I'd probably eat there twice a week. a pitcher of Spaten Munich was 10.75, and the selection of higher end beers was great. 

good pizza, great portions, awesome prices.

Decent all around. None of the food really stands out as far as pizza and pasta go. 

The restaurant itself is very nice and is a good place to bring a group together which is refreshing especially compared to places in the north side asian ghetto. Very convenient for people living on north side as well. 

Kind of annoying that they charge 50 cents for ranch though.

Good enough pizza!
As my friend puts it, La Val's serves bad pizza, but that is precisely what makes it taste good. It has a cardboard-like consistency, but that is was it so endearing about it.

Since I moved to California I have been looking for good pizza...in my quest I came across La Val's in Berkeley after flying into OAK the other night.  My girlfriend and I drove around UC's campus thinking there must be a great hole-in-the wall joint.  La Val's sort of fits the bill.  The place was nothing spectacular- a bit stale actually with lots of tan tile.  The service at the counter was very good, but the pizza was only average.  Beer prices were about $3.50 which doesn't seem too bad these days.

They had Mexican soccer blaring on the tv's and there was a contingent of soccer fans in the place.  I think we will keep searching for the area's best pizza though.

One nice thing about this place is that you can order pizza by the slice.

Again...service was great, food was average, ambiance was average.

mmmm. i like this b/c it reminds me of ny pizza, nice and thin, easy on the sauce and cheese. they have a credit card minimum so bring cash. fountain drinks = free refills.

free small drink with mini pizza order!

Great place for kids and adults to go together. The setting is fun and open, there's a pool table and it's not too noisy and loud despite all the activity.  The pizza is not good though...too much cheese, soggy crust...but it's all about the atmosphere, and about how open it is for kids and family.
Great lunch spot, pretty cheap, great pizza, lots of other stuff, good beer selection.

I have nothing new to add to Jill K's review ;-) 

That is exactly why I go to La Val's: to watch Cal games. If grease is what you crave, then you might as well pick up a burrito from next door.
i like it.  pizza is good, salad is good.  patio is a nice relaxing place to have a slice and a beer.

The food here isn't very good.  The pizza is nowhere near as good as Blondie's or fat slice and the sandwiches/pasta dishes are not the greatest.  Yet I've eaten here dozens of times but that's only because it's a block from where I used to work, at Etcheverry, and you can only eat burritos four times a week.  The fifth day you gotta diversify.  I wouldn't go back now that I don't work there and there are way better choices near campus than this.

Decent pasta (broccoli chicken penne), decent pizza (bbq chicken), good location, and they deliver to the lounge* on the third floor of Cory. I like to come in here between classes sometimes for a quick bite.

*Pro-tip: pizza makes a 6 hour problem set session much more tolerable.

La Val's isn't the best pizza, but it's good for what it is. Reasonably priced pizza and pasta, good beer pitcher prices and a Large seating area! The slice and drink combo seems to be the popular things a fat slice and a soda for $2.99. Although I don't drink soda, I just buy a slice and a bottle of water. They will give you a free cup for water if you ask for it, but it's always the bum cups (kids size). Kids sizes used to be synonomous with Fun size, not in this case. Here's a tip. You may think it's cheaper to get 2 big slices of pizza for just over 5 bucks, but it may not always be the best choice. The personal size pizza shouldn't be neglected. For under $5 you can get a 3 or 4 topping personal pizza that is fresh and hot out of the oven that tastes way better than the individual slices. It is a rare occasion to order a single slice and have it fresh from the oven. They bake them and they leave them sitting on the big wooden table in the back. Then when someone orders one, they throw it back into the oven and "reheat" it. Anytime you reheat pizza, it will taste exactly that way, horrible/not quite as good as the fresh thing. The first thing I do when I come in is walk over to the little pickup window and look over at the wooden table to see if the pizza slices are fresh or old, if they are old I will order a personal size or go for some pasta. I can't stand crummy reheated pizza, even if it is 2.59+tax. I'll pay a couple dollars more for something that is fresh and tasty. One of my favorite pasta dishes to order is the Pesto and Pollo. It's fettucini tossed with mushrooms in a pesto cream sauce, served with two pieces of garlic bread. Very tasty for just over 5 bucks. I had the broccoli & chicken pasta with the walnut sauce but I wasn't quite as impressed with it. La Val's is good, but isn't the best. It just does what it does. It's a "not-too-shabby" kind of place.

4 stars for their thin-crust Athenian with feta cheese in place of mozzarella; tasty, feta tangy and very nice. Props for having a personal size pizza, the mini, for about the cost of a couple slices.

If I were rating solely based on the quality of food, La Val's would probably only get three stars.  But the value is really good--Phil H.'s review was right on--the pizza isn't absolutely amazing, but the slices are HUGE and still taste good.  If you're a fan of big, floppy, greasy, pizza, you'll like La Val's.

But there are other reasons to like La Val's...$3.25 pints of decent beer (Anchor Steam, Sierra Nevada, Newcastle, etc) is pretty hard to beat, and the big screen tv's are a nice touch.

It isn't the best pizza in Berkeley, not by a long shot, but it is convenient and a good value for the price.

Go online and use their coupons. They've raised their prices a little though. I used to get two medium pizzas up to 3 toppings or their specials for $15. It's now $17. $23 for 2 larges with coupon. Doh! Free delivery though, so yay!

La Val's has good "New York Pizza", but it probably isn't actually anywhere close to the real stuff. Thin crust style pizza that's not too greasy, but tastes great. I don't feel guilty afterwards. I don't recommend anything else than their pizzas because their pasta and salads are super bland.

Great for getting a group together because they have plenty of seating. Big TV's to watch sports also.

I enjoy the BBQ chicken the most. They have a good daily special deal for two slices and a drink at lunch, but there tends to be a long line. Go try it!

I came upon this place late one evening, wandering around the Berkeley campus looking for a relaxing spot to get something to eat. It was near closing time, and I approached the counter and asked for a slice of cheese pizza and a pint of Fat Tire. A friendly cashier told me that they didn't have any cheese left, but she guessed that I was a vegetarian and recommended the Athena instead. I took her advice. The beer was $3.00 and the pizza was $2-something. I was very pleasantly surprised by the pizza, which was a New York-style big floppy slice, full of flavor with every bite. The Fat Tire complemented it well. 

I also tried the pepperoni, which was spicy and yummy, and the ham & pineapple, which I didn't care for at all. 

I can say that I left happy.
Great pizza and chicken wings! GREAT PRICES!

La Vals pizza would be the place to go if you are on Northside and are looking for a moderately priced decent-tasting pizza.
I must say that the pizza here has certainly grown on me since I spend a lot of my nights in the nearby Soda hall working on programming/research. This place is open till midnights on weekdays and that means that it is sometimes the only place that one can grab a bite during those nights spent in the nearby engineering buildings. 
The pizza itself can either be ordered in slices or as a whole. The slices are huge but really thin. The whole pizzas tend to be more even and are quite tasty ( try the barbecue chicken) 
This place also serves chicken wings which tend to be really oily and hence not to my taste ( i would prefer Vinnie's for the wings ). 
The pastas are good too. I would recommend the Chicken alfredo pasta. 
The place has a nice vibe to it and is classier than most places in berkeley ( that have a hippie feel to them). 
They also have a great selection of beer on tap and this is a good place to chill with a beer while having a slice of pizza with friends.
And they also show NFL games on their HD TVs.

Great pizza! Tastes way better than Fat Slice and any delivery place. The prices are great. The only thing is .... it's on north side! For those of us who live on southside, it is a pain to make the trek across campus, but if you're on northside, definitely hit up La Val's. 

Btw, quick unknown fact to many, La Val's has great pasta!

My wife and I went to France (Provance) a couple of years ago and fell in love with the Pizza's over there.  Very fresh thin crust with a few tasty and delicate toppings. Pizza is almost a staple there with pizza trucks everywhere like we have Taco trucks here.  
     Upscale resturants all have Pizza on the menu.  Ever since returning we've looked for that unique experience back here.  We found it.................LaVals.  Check out the Atheanian and the Margretta for a uniquely European experience.  All the speciality pizza's are likewise as good.  
    The service and decor are ok but the pizza is to die for.  Even better at home the next day...........leftovers...........yum.

Two great reasons why I come to this joint: 1) delivery during finals week and 2) away Cal football games!!!

Good selection of pizza.  I love light pizzas that don't make you feel groggy afterward; that being said, my personal favorites are the Athenian and the "Hula" Hawaiian.  Beware that the olives in the Athenian are not the typical black olives, they're the fresher and stronger flavored ones. Yummm!

For away Cal games, many students who live on Northside make the trek here to watch, eat and drink here (yep! this place sells booze!! beer on tap)  This place can get super crowded so come early to get a table with a prime viewing location of the big screen.  GO BEARS!!

I went here a couple times for group meetings when I was going to Cal, but those were the only times, and I always wished the group leader had better taste! The pizzas and pastas all kind of taste the same, and are greasy in a bad way, and I do like some things really greasy when they are done right!
This is a good little place. I had some veggie delight and some BBQ chicken pizza. It was solid. Apparently, it's legendary. I don't know exactly why, but I'd eat it again.

Mozzarella sticks are not worth the splurge.

Yet, these folks make a mean pasta dish.  Pesto with veggies FTW.

I will certainly think about trying their pizza.

Quick, well-priced, and tasty.

Seriously though. This is some pretty dang good pizza. I've tried every specialty flavor and they're all pretty bomb from the Hula, to the California, to the Athenian, but let me tell you... The LaVal's Special and BBQ Chicken pizza are to die for. Its seriously delicious. I'm salivating just thinking about it.

To be objective it is pretty greasy and if thats not  what you're looking for GO EAT A FREAKING SALAD! Stop looking for a healthy pizza. What is wrong with you. That's not a pizza then. It's just tomato soup with bread in it. So this is a normal pizza, which happens to be greasy, obviously!

You can also build your own pastas too, but let me tell you their menu of pastas are also really good.

But once again... Let me tell you, yet again... BBQ Chicken Pizza. LaVal's Special. DO IT! I tried to eat less and limit myself to 4 pizzas, but... I couldn't stop and ate like 9 slices today. Simply delicious! :)

the Great,
GumZ

I need to start going up to Northside more often. Why? The food is freaking amazing^^ Example? LA VAL'S PIZZA!!

So, I absolutelyyy LOVE pizza. LOL I know I can eat it everyday if I had to. Okay, maybe NOT everyday but you get the idea... Anywhoo, the people that took my order were SO nice. I mean, they told me about how I can get a "buy 1 medium pizza and get 1 medium pizza free" coupon. I mean, who does that? Don't they want to make money? Nice people. Nice. People. =)

We ordered BBQ Chicken & La Val's Special. (Mediums ~$12) It was perfect. Just perfect. I went with 2 other friends and we had leftovers. I usually try to watch myself and eat 2 pizzas BUT nope. I had like 4 slices. NOM NOM NOM:P
It's closed and there were many reasons why this is as it should be. Food, atmosphere, customer base, location, etc.

I never thought pizza could actually taste bad, but at LaVal's, it' does! There is some strange flavor in their dough that I can't quite put my finger on but it tastes like all sorts of assery! Frozen pizza is even better than this poor excuse for a restaurant. The seats are uncomfortable. It's too noisy to have a conversation. And it's swarming with annoying Cal students. I can't think of anything worse.

At least this location is better than the one on Southside? That's about the most positive thing I can say about this place. I ate here a lot when I was an undergraduate - mostly because there wasn't anywhere else to eat on Northside. Back in my day there was still a theater group downstairs. Starting sentences with "back in my day" makes me sound like I'm walking with a cane and holding up an ear horn.

Their pizza cheese is a mozzarella/cheddar blend, and I am vehemently against any cheddar on my pizza. At least you have a sunny view of the courtyard and Euclid St. while eating.
Their subterranean theatre restores my faith in humanity. Their all veggie combo restores my faith in antacids. Their tv sets restore my faith in NCAA basketball.

La Vals is like Gypsie's healthier little brother. They use less salt, oil and butter, but it still tastes delicious. I like their vegetarian pizza because it doesn't leave me feeling guilty, but it does leave me satisfied. If it wasn't so far away, I would attempt to come here more often.

P.S., it's cheap!

La Val's...

I actually don't care too much for this place. It's just meehh, nothing special at all. In fact, I could be a little too greasy and salty for me. It is nothing memorable at all. I could care less.

But they are pretty good at delivering on time. And they have a bunch of coupons on their website. Those are the only 2 good things I could say about them.

This place has the 2nd WORSE caesar salad that I've ever had. The portion was hearty for a small and it looked like it would be epic. However, despite its misleading appearance, the salad was not very enjoyable. The dressing was mediocre, but the lettuce was of poor quality and there were barely any leaves.just stalks.

I also ordered a mini pepperoni and sausage. I'm a New Yorker so I'm highly critical of pizzerias, but this place is actually good. Yes the pizza is a bit salty and greasy, but it's a pizzeria not a gourmet restaurant so I wasn't put off by that. The sauce, crust and meats were.all made to perfection and had good flavors. If I'm on this side of town again, I'm likely to stop by again. This pizza is definitely better than anything available in Downtown Berkeley!!

Even though this place isn't over-hyped like Cheeseboard or Zachary's, I actually really like their pizza! I'm not a huge pizza fan, but I love their thin-crusted pizza, not to mention the HUGE serving size. A slice of pizza is almost as big as a mini pizza! If you get the mini, they give you a FREE drink. I usually get the hula, Hawaiian pizza. They always make is right after you order, so the pizza is always warm and fresh! 

Lots of space and a good place to chill, catch up, grab a bite w/ friends and colleagues.

We were thinking of getting burgers for dinner, but changed our mind when we saw this place. The pizzas were decently priced and they had a good selection of beers on tap.

I wanted something traditional, so my friends and I got the medium margherita pizza. The crust was perfectly baked and thin and the pizza tasted good, but I do wish that more sauce was on it.

I have to admit that I had better pizza, but I was satisfied with my meal. If I was a college student, I definitely come here for a quick meal between classes. Can't go wrong with pizza and a pint of Fat Tire.
thank you for showing soccer and letting us come in to watch before the kitchen opens!!! you rock!!!

La Vals is a pizza joint on the Euclid Avenue strip, a sleepy looking area well served by restaurants and coffee houses.  Decent number of beers on tap and if you're into sports you can check out several games at once.  Actually haven't had pizza here but they have good sanwiches, salads, etc as well.
Their margarita pizza is good. Very garlicy and salty, I likey. Their pizzas are huge and they have coupons on their website so you get pretty good deals.

Loud, but fun place to go out with friends or even have parties. 

The Point:
Try a mini pizza,  be adventurous in your topping choice. 
The seafood pastas are excellent. 
The fried veggies (mushroom,  zucchini)  are extremely salty and the batter is drowned in pepper. 
Ranch is excellent.  
I love ranch...  enjoy

Starving Student with a knack for pool?  OK, go to North Side and up Euclid...
I really like the pizza here.  Also, a big screen TV.  However, lots of football worshippers cheering.  Loudly.  The pool table is awesome.
That's all.

If you're a science major in Cal, chances are you will have to spend a good chunk of your day near the Hearst Mining circle for your classes. Unfortunately this spot is hella far from the South Side gourmet ghetto but fear not because your ready-to-go culinary options isn't limited to the vending machines and FSM. What I love about La Val's is mainly the crust/bread. The sauce, cheese, and toppings are okay but I think for cheap pizza (let's face it this is no zachary's) the quality is all about equal at every store (Blondie's, Fat Slice, etc). So it comes down to personal preference. For me, the dough/bread at Blondie's sucks! Its texture is AWFUL. However I love La Val's thin crispy texture. Plus for about 3.25 you get a free small drink with a huge slice. So not only is the lunch super tasty and pretty cheap but they don't try to milk you extra for the soda. So good food and being close to my classes makes it a winner in my books.

Large slices and different choices of toppings make for an OK pizza experience. There is ample seating indoors, but usually large tables that make you look like a loner or a douche when sitting alone, so bring a friend!

Slices are made to order or reheated from a giant pizza, but it all tastes the same once it comes out of the oven.

La Val's Pizza is a great place to eat.  The specialty pizzas are very tasty, and I've had them all.  I like my crust thin, and it's perfect here.  The personal pizza combo with a soda is under $6, and the pizza is the same size as a $12 dollar pizza elsewhere.  There is also a large selection of pasta and sandwiches, which also never disappoint.  It can be crowded during lunch, but there is outdoor seating.

La Vals, I love you.

You and your greasy, cheesy, melty-hot pizza goodness.  You and your bland, but not unpleasant chicken alfredo.  You are not the best pizza place around, but you are convenient, you are cheap and you ARE good.

Daily special prices can't be beat- a soda and a slice bigger than my face for five bucks?  Sign me up!  La Vals has a neat variety of fancy-shmancy pizzas for adventurous folks like me, while also having the boring, but tasty tried-and-trues for people like my husband.

I work on campus, just down the hill from Euclid, and sometimes, it is nothing more than proximity that drives my business to the doors of La Vals, but I never leave disappointed in what I've ordered.

So I have been to La Val's twice for dinner & a show. (Impact Theater does plays in the basement theater).
The pizza is good.... this past time I got the combo slice. Slices are the way to go because you can try multiple toppings! 
We also shared a large salad- it was fresh and the dressing (vinaigrette) was tasty. It was a hearty salad--- no wilty iceberg here! 
There is a good selection of beer & a few wines (They gave me a generous pour) as well as sodas. 
There are a variety of areas to sit with TVs--- but for us the important part was that you can take your food down to eat in the theatre while you watch the show. 
La Val's is totally fun and affordable. It can be crowded- so take your patience.
It is a Berkeley must taste!

Today, I had one of those days.  You know, those days when you just cannot take a break.  Today I was stuck on campus until 10:40PM working on a group project.  And of course I am cramming, because after all I am an engineering student, which means that I work better under pressure.  Anyways, due to my late evening I was forced to get dinner at La Val's.  I had the special with feta cheese instead of salami.  It was a decent pie, but not anything spectacular.  It definitely isn't anything to hike up the hill for.  They do have a nice selection of beer on tap, but if you don't mind drinking in the ally, the Quickie Marts nearby have the same beers, plus some especially good ones, for much less.

I spend a lot of time on the north side of the UC campus so I have made countless visits to La Val's. When I'm looking for a cheap and quick bite to eat, this is one of the go-to places. They give you a relatively large slice of pizza for only 3-4 dollars and that's usually enough to keep me satisfied til my next meal. I've tried the pasta and salad here as well and they were ok. Nothing too special. I mainly go here to grab slices of pizza. Not a bad option if you're stuck on Euclid looking for a bite to eat!

First heard about this place from my parents-- they went to see a play, and then went to La Val's afterwards to top it off.  Or was it the other way around?  DOESN'T MATTER.  Anyway.  They brought home leftovers and it was literally the best pasta I've had in my life, something with marina sauce.  THE. BEST.  

So I went with my buddy Rob to give it a try.  Pretty empty on a Friday night, so I get the feeling it's not exactly a bumpin' college hangout~* but it had a few people studying, a family, and some quiet conversation.  Interesting space.  Very little decorating, but a Pirates of the Caribbean pinball machine, Time Crisis 3, and a pool table.  Staff is relatively friendly, always a plus.

Rob got a slice of pizza-- which was huge-- and a pastrami sandwich, I got the linguini with shrimp, eagerly anticipating more of The Best Pasta I'd Had In My Life... and was sorely disappointed.  Not because the food was bad, but because I had ordered the wrong dish.  Still though, it was amazing-- buttery sauce without being overwhelming, nice shrimp.  Didn't quite get why we needed olives, but hey, whatever works.  The garlic bread it came with was fantastic, though they were both end pieces (say what?!).  

Rob wasn't a big fan of his pizza, but he seemed to dig the sandwich well enough.  You'd have to ask him.

Definitely a place you could bring friends to, provided it's not a really crowded night.  There's a plasma TV and plenty of space.  Super affordable food, and it's damn good on top of that.  

Having had a dish besides what I got that I thought was stellar, along with a dish that I thought was pretty good, I'd put this place up there pretty high.  Points to La Val's!

This place is pretty ok for grabbing lunch near campus--the veggie sandwich is fine. Good place for getting an afternoon beer, too, and has large tvs if you want to catch the game. And a pool table! The tables are large, too, if you need to grade some papers while you eat.

I love this place! My friends recommended La Val's as a very nice Italian restaurant, so when I visited for the first time, I expected big bucks. But that was quite the contrary. HUGE servings, $3 pizza and $7-8 pasta is pretty darn reasonable. I've had their pizzas, pastas, and salads, and none of them failed to impress me.

Another (a bit more person) reason I love La Val's is their service. I always take my friends to La Val's for their birthdays, and for a good reason, too. Free drinks hehe ;)

The crust of the pizza is divine - a really tasty thin crust that's both crispy and doughy. The toppings seem fresh and they don't murder the vegetables on the pizzas. I enjoyed the mushroom and spinach slice. The pasta is good too, and the portions are generous.
My friends take me here to watch Cal football games. The food is average but the pitchers are cheap and the they have a large screen TV.

A friend and I ordered a pizza for delivery last night and we waited 90 minutes for that pizza (and a side salad that we HAD to order to get it delivered).  By the time we got the pizza, it was soggy and lukewarm.  You know how it is . . . when you want pizza, you want pizza!

We called the place twice checking on the order.  It just sucked - I wish that wasn't my first experience with them.  

Soggy Pizza -- I can't really even judge that pizza, can I?  Since it was the box's fault . . . but it's NOT the box's fault - it was the delivery strategy . . . Perhaps invest in a GPS (so the blame isn't on bad directions) - we were only 1 mile away.

So . . . 2 stars for service . . .

You can find me here before making the hike up to Memorial Stadium for CAL football. Good pizza for the price, great pitchers of beer at a reasonable  price. A nice place to meet friends for the game, get there early though, the tables will be taken. You don't want to be the guy in Cal hat holding a pizza and pitcher looking for a place to sit?

Seriously, this place is amazing!
For a "mini" which is about the size of any pizza place's small, it is only about $3.99 (for cheese) or $4.50 (for pep!)
And, all pizzas come with a free refill drink. How can you go wrong?
On a budget? Want good pizza? Need some grub between classes?
Hello? La Val's Pizza is the place!

This place serves:

- The blandest fettuccine alfredo I've ever had. No amount of parmesan cheese was able to save that dish.
- The soggiest, least-appetizing Greek salad ever.
- Mediocre Athenian (Greek-topping) pizza.

It's amazing how even La Burrita next door serves more appetizing fare than La Val's.

The best lunch place around campus. They have reasonably priced good quality food throughout the board. Salads, Sandwiches, Pizza, Pasta.
I come here every week with colleagues and as there is a Mexican place connected and with the benches outside it's perfect.

Jenna, you are way too nice. I never ate there, but judging from your experience, it must have been awful! I ordered delivery after receiving a coupon and there is one thing that stands out - the sauce is nasty. I can't get past the sauce. Maybe I'll give them another shot sometime - their prices are quite low afterall - but for now, two stars.

La Val's is a good campus pizza joint -- it's cheap, they have huge slices, and when you buy a slice or a personal pizza it comes with a free drink. $3.50 for lunch (slice + 16oz drink) can't be beaten on the Northside. My favorite slice is the Athenian but the combination and hawaiian slices are also good.
BBQ chicken doesn't come in slices but if you "splurge" for a personal pizza (5.50 with drink) it can be yours. Delicious.
That said:
-1/2 star for greasiness (yes, it is possible to make pizza that doesn't drip grease)
-1/2 star for putting my friend's slice and my slice in the same, tiny pizza box on a day when we had to take our pizza to go. They stacked my pizza on top of his so I ended up getting grease all over my hands and face 10 min before I had to give a presentation. Mostly my fault I guess but they could have definitely done a better packaging job.

I've been forced to go here far too many times (darn Northside classes!).

Avoid the flat and oily pizza!

NEVER get the eggplant parmesean sandwich! NEVER. They don't do anything with the eggplant. No cooking whatsoever. They just slice it into two strips, place it in a sandwich, and expect it to cook as they toast the bread. It made me gag when I ate it.

This place is a sleazy pizza joint. Expect to see tons of people stopping by solo just to grab a cheap-ish bite to eat. I'd say the price range is around $3-10. So yes, it is very college and purse friendly. But that is about it.

La Val's is a totally unremarkable take on thin-crust pizza, but it's not without its saving graces. They've got an inexpensive lunch special, a selection of beer, and a pinball machine. There's also a lot of space and the game's always on, which is unique on the Northside.

So don't worry that the pizza's lacking; there are other reasons to come here.

Eating here is awesome. Eating the food here is not so awesome.

Allow me to explain. The environment is fun and cool, especially for college students and sports fans. It's fun to watch football games here, hang out with friends, get pitchers of beer, and just have a great time.  A great time, at least, until you order the pizza. I'm not saying the pizza is outright horrible or unedible, it's just not very good. I wish they would allow you to bring Blondie's or Fat Slice in, cuz then it would be awesome.

I don't love La Val's, but it has the distinct advantage of being convenient.  They have a fine small selection of beers on tap, a good variety of pizzas and plenty of space for large groups and study sessions.

This place is great. I used to frequent the LaVal's on Durant and once that place closed down I made the switch to the Euclid one.

LaVals has a lot of space. Plenty of booths and seating.

The food is a steal (in my opinion). Slices run you about 2.50-3$, but for those who might take two or three slices to get full, I suggest the pastas. Their pastas are dense and filling, also served with two slices of garlic bread. The garlic bread is just alright, a little dry, but still good for sopping up pasta sauce.

A tidbit: you can add chicken/meat to veggie pastas. Definitely delicious.

When I lived in Berkeley, La Val's was one of my favorite places to grab a slice of pizza.  The food is reasonably priced (it's cheaper than Blondie's) and the slices are large.  The flavor isn't bad either.  I like the pizza's sauce and its texture.  I'd describe the texture as more thin/crunchy than thick/chewy.   On the whole, the pizza is on the thin side.  (But it's not super thin, like some pizza can get.)  When you bite through it, the top half of the pizza (which contains the dough, cheese, and toppings) is soft; the bottom half (which is the crust) is crunchy.  So, to complete your bite, you have to firmly bite downward at the end.  The other nice thing about this place is that it is quite clean and it has an open feel to it.  This is a nice change from the grimier, darker joints on Telegraph.  On the whole, this is a great place to enjoy some pizza and beer (there are a number of options on tap).

La Vals is not for the picky or the weak stomach(ed) and here's why.. 

Since I live on the north side of campus, I often find myself going to La Vals. It is pretty big, has comfortable seating, a big TV  and open till about 10:30ish.

I have always accepted the food as being mediocre and gulped it down without complaining (for the aforementioned reasons). However, the last two times that I have been to La Vals, I have been exceedingly disappointed.

Incident 1

Call and ordered food for take out ( 2 slices of cheese pizza, one tuna melt on sourdough roll). I was informed that it would be ready in 15-30 minutes. Within 15 minutes I was standing in line, waiting for my food. 
Needless to say it was not ready in fact, they informed me that they were out of cheese pizza slices altogether.  I am still wondering why they failed to mention this over the phone. 

All in all, after waiting for about 30 minutes in La Vals, I came home with a cold tuna melt with tonnes of mayo on it and a seemingly stale cheese pizza.  

Incident 2

Went to La Vals and Ordered  Shrimp Alfredo and once again, a slice of cheese pizza and a tuna melt on sourdough roll (some people never learn!)

The pizza slice was stale, the tuna melt was given on wheat bread despite it saying clearly on the receipt that it should be on a sourdough roll and it had a little black insect crawling on it, before eventually disappearing into the deluge of mayo.

Despite the pasta having an inch of oil at the bottom, it was delicious!! Unfortunately, it did not quite agree with my tummy and I had to suffer unnecessary gas, cramps and the cherry on top, diarrhea.

I hope La Vals starts to pay more attention to it's food quality and the health of it's customers.

La Val's is never my first choice. Actually, La Val's is never my second choice. La Val's is always rather low except on days when I too am feeling rather depressed. Then La Val's fills the void in my heart in a pinch.

In essence, La Val's is the sort of place I think to go when I want a large piece of grease covered carbs only half a block from my house. It's usually when you're having a bad time with a relationship or work or other aspects in your life. It's days when your dinner would be nothing more than coffee, cigarettes, whiskey and aspirin, but you have decided to be intelligent and substantiate it with something a bit more satisfying. Those are the days that inspire me to go to La Val's.

I found myself at La Val's on Sunday for one of the reasons listed above. I ordered the Hawaiian pizza slice, which weirds me out a bit because it has regular bacon and green peppers as well (and not nearly enough pineapple). They didn't heat up the slice as much as I would have liked and in retrospect, I should have gotten the entirely greasy pepperoni because it is always a safe bet. I also ordered their small garlic cheese bread, which was a large serving but really not good (how you screw up garlic cheese bread, I'm still not quite sure).

The inside is nice. Large TVs, videogames and billiards -- but the service is absolute crap. It's the sort of place I only go for takeout because there are much better places to hang out or watch a game.

And some days, you just need greasy takeout to fill that stupid void in your soul.

Damn you inner fat child. Damn you 8 year old self that still thinks eating your problems away is the answer to everything.

2nd only to Gioia's for pizza in Berkeley.

If you want tomato sauce on yer pie you better ask for it because it's not automatic.

La Val's is an institution and I feel guilty for even dissing it.  But I have to be honest.  I owe it to Yelp and to my elite status!

Okay, when I was in law school, I had so much La Val's pizza.  That's because it's the only place that APALSA could afford ("Come to the APALSA meeting today - free food! "  How many times did I come to these meetings only to get disappointed when I saw those four boxes of La Val's pizza).    Let's face it.  It's cheap pizza for the masses.  

There's no nuance here.  It's cardboard crust and gooey cheese definitely sustained me during law school, but I haven't been back since l graduated from law school...I will give La Val's one thing:  it's cheap.  And Cheap is always good.  My Asian genes will always appreciate cheap, and when you're a student, you really don't have much choice!  

One plus for La Val's is that the Euclid location has a huge screen T.V. where you can watch baseball games and hang out with friends (I think the Durant location closed down).  I know this sounds snotty but my hubby wanted to go in there during a game when we were hanging out and I made him order food elsewhere for us (Bongo Burger, I think), and then we watched the game from outside the storefront window!  That's how opposed I am to eating La Val's.

La Val's, you fed me during law school and I'll always be thankful...but man, I sure had to down those slices of pizza with lots of coke.

Probably one of the worst pizza places in Berkeley.  I only went here when I was forced by other friends.  They do have a huge big screen and cheap beer.  So eh, I guess if you're into sports and beer, this was the place to be.

La Val's was my first exposure to pizza in California. Coming from the pizza capital of America (Beverly, Massachusetts), pizza in La Vals is perfectly analogous to burritos in Beverly. Awful. It's as if La Vals had only heard of pizza -- bread, sauce, cheese, toppings "sure, we can do that" -- before opening a pizzeria. I'd put it head-to-head with the pizza my elementary school served on Fridays, and there you lost half your cheese to the wax paper.

Bonus star because the beer is cheap and the TV is large.

It was sweet the time I came here with my buddies and one of my friends, who was prone to goofball mistakes, accidentally sprinkles sugar all over his slice, thinking it was salt.  (Not sure how you'd make that mistake or why you'd even need to put salt on a slice of friggin' La Val's pizza for that matter.)  He freaked out and got all frustrated and mad at himself. Sweet!!!

For the price they offer it's a good quality. Of course, it's not culinary masterpieces but it's eatable, it's very close to the campus, it's very fast and they always have pretty cheap lunch specials. I go there with my little daughter sometimes, it's super convenient, she plays outside in the little outdoor seating area while I eat. I would give them four stars for convenience and low prices but the food is little bit too oily, so only three.

I've only been here for lunch, but it looks as if it can be a fun place for late-night hangouts or for weekend games.  I've had the Barbecue Chicken (mini) and it is certainly more than enough for one person.  It comes with a complimentary drink with unlimited refills.  Not the cleanest place, but there is outdoor seating, which is nice if you are in a group and other people want to order from La Burrita.

I've been away from Berkeley for awhile..but the places I always hit when I'm there are

1)La Vals Pizza on Euclid
2)Steven's Korean BBQ on Durant
3)Top Dogg on Durant
4)Liu's Kitchen on Solano in El Cerrito

These 4 places make Berkeley worth coming too EVERY time..I just can't get these flavors and textures and foods at THIS PRICE in the South Bay.

LaVals was my favorite pizza place in the bay area for thin slices.

I went to school here in Berkeley and lived on the crazier south side where LaVals had their second store.  Every day at lunch..I'd get a coupon for a slice and free drink for 2.50.   You can't beat that!

Ah..college has since gone and the south side LaVals has since gone as well.

The only one that remains is the one on North side Berkeley on Euclid. North Side doesn't have the crazy homeless guys or the rastafarian white kids w/blonde dreads...

Just has the geeky undergrads who probably would be on the VH1 show "the pick up artist".  

The pizza at lavals?

It's like larger slices of round table pizza but crispier and a stronger sauce.

I love saucey food.   LaVals tomatoe sauce is so good...combined w/a combo slice w/the veggies and sausage and pepperoni hitting you all at once..it really satisfies the palette.

The thinner LaVals pizza totally give you way more flavor than say Blondies or Fat Slice on South Side.   Blondies and Fat Slice are known more for SIZE than TASTE.  They end up tasting very doughy in the end...while La vals gives you a slight crunch w/your toppings..

Alright so this place has decent food. Personally I love their pizza, but if I had to compare it to somewhere else I would say that it tasted most like a pizza you buy at the market and pop into your oven but better. They give your large slices and at a great price.

The four star rating is more weighted on the theater and shows downstairs. I've been able to catch a couple shows downstairs and it's an experience like no other. The shows feel intimate and enthralling because of the structure of the small downstairs.

Despite it's name, the Pizza isn't why I go to La Val's. It's close to home, on the North-side of campus, and usually open late. While the Pizza is okay, especially for the price, for me the real magic of La Val's happens with the other selections on the menu. 

The Pizza is satisfying, but if you want the best La Val's has to offer... try the salads, pastas, and sandwiches. I usually will order a sandwich and the spinach salad, which comes loaded with onions, bleu cheese, tomatoes and balsamic vinaigrette.

There's plenty of seating, a big screen TV usually showing a sporting event, and a pool table. Drinks are reasonably priced also.

La Val's seems like your typical college hangout pizza spot, complete with big tv's to watch sports and a pool table, but the food is just meh. I've tried their pizza and while you get huge slices for what you pay, the quality is just okay and I'd MUCH prefer Cheeseboard which is the same price. I've also had the Veggie Sandwich (provolone, avocado, cucumber, lettuce, tomato, onion) which comes with a side of potato salad, but there's nothing special going on with that either. I don't really like potato salad in general, but sadly they don't let you substitute anything for it. 

There's lots of space and tables, so it's a good place if you have a large group or want to catch a sports game, but I probably wouldn't come here unless other friends wanted to since there's so many better choices around the area.

Like many others have said, La Val's is just...eh. It's not the best pizza around, but it's the only pizza place on North Side. There's much better places in downtown, and you can't go wrong with Blondie's or Fat Slice on Telegraph.

The last time I was here, my professor treated the whole class out after our final project design expo. 40+ starving engineers in one room is quite a sight to see. Every time a pizza would come out, half the room would sprint to the table in hopes of getting a slice. Unlimited soft drinks made the heat that much more bearable as well. As an area for large groups, La Val's works perfectly, with plenty of tables and lot of room for movement.

The pizza is pretty mediocre, though. They have pretty decent variety, but sometimes it feels like you're just eating a frozen pizza you bought from Safeway. Let's just say I don't think they'll ever be able to pull off a thin crust pizza. Having said that though, try it for yourself because when it comes to pizza, personal choice is king.

Great place for pizza but unfortunately nothing compared to Cheeseboard.
