The only thing I've ordered here is the hot pot bibimbap.  But it is amazing.  They have daily specials so on wednedays the bibimbap is under 7 dollars after tax.

Service is always relatively quick, and staff relatively friendly.  No credit for purchases under $10.
Okay Korean food. Always gives me a tummyache but maybe I just have a weak tummy...I recommend going to that mom&pop's korean restaurant near parker and telegraph.

Wow, this is far worse than your "average" korean food. I've only eaten once here and ordered some kind of clear-noodle soup. It was ridiculously bland. The banchan was also tasteless (too "fresh" and not fermented enough). I was quite disappointed. Although, I'm surprised that it has a lot of customers; they're Koreans too. You'd think that they have a higher standard of what Korean food should tastes like. Go figure.

I'm Korean, so I can say that they have THE BEST Korean food in this town.
The lady in cashier is quite polite, and my only gripe with them is their location and name of the place.
Can't they be more creative on naming??? does "T-toust" give some sense to someone that they are serving great authentic Korean food?

Toust is my go-to for Korean food because it's in such a convenient location, clean, bright, and has better food than the other Korean options nearby.  Plus, they have a different special every day Monday through Friday (Monday is bi bim bap and Wednesday is hot pot bi bim bap), and it's hard to resist a huge bowl of bi bim bap for sub $6.  Their tofu soups, ramen, and bulgogi are also tasty!

Your meal also always comes with six small sides, which is actually not too common among some of the other fast-food-like Korean places around the area.  Some of the sides vary each time, so there's always something new to try!

Overall, it's pretty average Korean food, but definitely the best around the area.  The service is always lighting fast, and I have never had to wait more than a few minutes for my food to arrive.  It's a little on the expensive side for a place around campus, but if you get a special, totally worth it.

I have only recently discovered T-Toust. I have been in Berkeley for 3 years now and had never tried it. I tried it for the first time this semester and I have come to love it. The Spicy Chicken is amazing. The big salad that come on the side is also extremely delicious. I have no idea what the dressing is, but I enjoy it very much. The soup, which comes with every meal, is decent. It is a little over-priced and will not accept debit/credit card unless you spend at least $15. It is self-serve for water, silverware, and other things. You also bus your own table. Overall, the only reason I return to T-Toust is the food!

This is my number one go to spot for Korean food at Berkeley, but that's just because they are close and I love Korean food, even if it's not the best. I had some misses here, but one dish that has never failed me is their hot pot beef soup...mmm it's so good!

I got their seafood tofu soup once because it was on their daily specials, and ewwww....no taste whatsoever! I was so disappointed. And I also tried their bi-bim-bap. It was A-Ok, not bad, not the greatest, good enough. 

I really wish Berkeley had some gooooddddddddd Korean food. Please, someone open up a place--I will give you a lot of business.
alright. still berkeley korean food. small weird place with clear plastic chairs and bright orange and green walls. food is meh - had seafood soondubu

This place is a little pricier than i'd like to spend on lunch or dinner, but it seems to be in line with other Korean restaurants. A nice place to have a casual meal. The ramen and bim bim bap are all I've ever gotten from there and I'm always satisfied, especially with all the yummy sides they give you. Really convenient spot when you're near sproul and want some good eats.

Keep in mind that four stars is my rating based on berkeley standards (which is like two notches below my LA standards)  But anyways,  I really like Steve's down the street but when you're not feeling like a total carnivore, I recommend this place for decent korean cuisine.  They offer more banchan than neighboring korean restaurants and a quieter, more appropriate ambiance for someone who really just wants to enjoy their meal.  I had the hot stone bibimbap and while this place didn't wow me with it, it didn't disappoint me either.  The portion size is adequate and like most places around here you pay first and clean up yourself, so no tip is needed. (YAY.)  I'd come here again for some tofu soup when berkeley starts to freeze up.

I kind of like this place, maybe because the other korean places near campus sucks (except Bear's ramen). A little bit pricey compare to the other restaurants in Berkeley, food is alright, I really like their spicy pork. Beef fried rice is too salty, their ramen is good though.

The first time I came here for lunch with friends, my dish was the last to arrive of my party, and I found a bug in it. Whe on I informed the waitress, she took the dish back and I again waited for my meal. During my wait, the manager came out and offered a free appetizer and an apology. Unfortunately the dish was spicy, but it was a nice gesture :) 

My second time here, I had lunch with a one of my friends who was part of the original group of friends in the first visit. This time I ordered a soon tofu. As soon as my order came and was placed on the table, a moth decides to "suicide dive" straight into my tofu. Again, I had to have this dish taken back, and the staff was very nice.

My friend jokes that I always have the worst experience here, especially when I eat in. After that, my other friend and I always order out, I don't eat in at this place any more. But the food is very good!

This is not fancy food, just Korean comfort-food favorites for not a lot of money, just a couple steps from campus.  I also love the trendy phonetic name that doesn't make much sense :)

Uninspired but completely serviceable banchan- usually some kimchi, potato salad, fish cake, and vegetables.  Every time I've gone, I've stuck with their soups- sundubu, budaejjigae, dwenjang jjigae.  These have all been tasty and homey, really hit the spot.  They also have bibimbap, which I tried once and it was pretty good (maybe nothing to write home about, but definitely a decent rendition)

I came to Toust at the recommendation of my friend.  It was the day of the Big Game - Cal vs. Stanford.  After the football game, everywhere was crowded.  My floormates and I couldn't find a place that wasn't packed.  But I knew a place tucked into Sather Lane that had good Korean food (my friend told me).  We went in.  We were greeted graciously by a waitress, who arranged the tables for 8 of us.  

I ordered the Galbi (Beef Rib) Tofu Soup, Spicy.  It was a large portion that definitely filled me up.  My floormates ordered the Bi Bim Bap, Ramen, etc.  They all looked good.  The Bi Bim Bap is very large, but bland - use plenty of hot sauce.  In addition to the usual Korean appetizers, the waitress gave COMPLIMENTARY Galbi/Beef Ribs for our entire table!  It could have used more sauce, but hey it was on the house.  How sweet of them!  Prices are very reasonable and they have specials of the day when certain dishes are discounts ($1-2 off).  I'm definitely coming back again.

Atmosphere: very simple, nothing special

Food quality: They have a few excellent dishes but their entire menu is not impressive. The kalbi is by far my favorite. Their stews e.g. seafood/tofu stew, is pretty good too! 

Price worthiness: worth the price!

Service: the lady is really sweet, but there isn't much service besides her bringing you the food, though self serve is pretty typical in Berkeley.

overall I really enjoy this place, and definitely recommend it to the average berkeley student! But if you are a visitor or tourist looking for gourmet food this is not the place to go~

Came here with a friend during lunch hour and it was pretty busy. I ordered the Bulgogi plate (#2) for $7.95 and it came out within minutes. Yay for being fast.

The banchan was just ok... They had a short selection with only kimchi, fish cake, bean sprouts, and seasoned potatoes. Wish they had more. I remember a couple years back when I came here, they had 6 and they were very generous with the amount they gave you.

The bulgogi was a bit underseasoned/undermarinated and a bit undercooked which was kinda sad. Asides from the bulgogi, you get a mound of rice and some lettuce dressed in sweet mayo. Not the most filling plate, nor the most tasty, but it passes.

I would come here again, but I would definitely try something else.

The service is horrible and the food is decent.  It's a good place to go if you're really craving Korean food, but if you want to get better food, go to Oakland (down Telegraph).  I had the Tofu soup, and it wasn't as good as most tofu soup I've had before.  I felt that the soup was a little watery.  The bulgogi wrap is an interesting concept.  It doesn't taste bad, but it doesn't taste amazing either.

For some reason, I always thought this was the best Korean place in walking distance from campus, but after eating it again a couple of days ago, that has changed. I got the bi bim bap to go and it was eh. My friends' food was eh. Maybe it's because we got it to go? Last semester their food was way better with more flavor.

I wish there was better Korean food right around Berkeley campus, but there just isnt. Good thing about this place is you can get a nice hot tofu soup when the weather is chilly outside. I always get the Galbi tofu soup! Comes with a portion of rice and if you eat in, they give you side dishes! Their bibimbap is decent--definitely check out their daily deals because dishes are cheaper.

I've definitely tried better tofu soup, but this place will have to suffice!

So after craving Korean food for oh so long I thought I'd give Toust a try again after not having eaten it since freshman year where i thought it would hit the spot. 

ordered a beef hot pot and was....disappointed. the soup just lacked flavor. :/. the people who work there are always really nice so I def give them some props for having good customer service but the food itself wasn't great. Also they gave less appetizer things. and they weren't as good. overall this place is just A-ok. I wish it was great i really do, especially since there's a lack of good Korean food in Berkeley but this place isn't awesome. It just kind of fulfills the Korean food craving.

I've always wondered if other Asian people got annoyed with the wave of sort-of-chic/wannabe-fancy Asian or Asian fusions (e.g., Le Colonial or P.F. Chang) places (that I ever-so-rudely say are "for the gringos"). Do white people get annoyed when Asians are serving up traditional "white people" food?

when it comes to most restaurants, I have to admit, I like the shi-shi factor. I like it when places look nice, or have a certain hip quality. But when it comes to "ethnic" food - mainly Asian or Mexican, I want the opposite. If a place isn't a little bit grungy, it just don't seem right... Maybe it's my anti-assimilation attitudes, maybe it's because I don't want to high overhead to be passed on to the menu, maybe it's just my reverse snobbery... (yeah, it's probably that)

So I tried T-toust yesterday, after passing by a number of times. Based on the look and feel of it, i thought it was a sandwich place (also the sign that says "sandwiches!" sort of threw me off). Apparently, it's a korean restaurant that also serves sandwiches. It has all the basic stuff - tofu soup, noodles, bulgogi, along with sandwiches.

I had a beef tofu soup, which is hard for me to resist - especially when it's only like 6 bucks. It wasn't bad, especially since there just aren't many korean places in the area with tofu soup. But my friend had the bulgogi... and that was a bit disappointing. It tastes more like it was boiled than it was grilled. and on top of that (literally), they put a bunch of "stuff" like mushrooms and peppers... 

All the while, my friend and I were talking about how it was interesting that it had the look of a franchise or mini-chain (e.g., no misspellings on their menus), but the feel of a small business. The place was and is usually packed, so there's definitely the market for this type of food. And even though to me, it seemed like it was "for the gringos", it was mostly Asians in da house.

So this leads me back to my original question: is it just me?... probably...

Anyway, the menu isn't quite authentic, and it's not dirty enough to feel like a genuine Asian restaurant, but the food is decent, though not exactly spectacular. more importantly it's cheap, and pretty close to campus.

This place is "okay" Korean food. Lots of college students will come here for lunch or dinner and they give a lot of food for what you pay for. I've definitely had better Korean, but what can you expect near campus?

I came here a second time as my friend was having a noodle obession. I ordered the beef and rice and it was delicious. The service was better and faster the second time around. During lunch time, this place is ridiculously busy and make sure you bring cash since there's a minimum unless you order over $10.

Toust. How the eff do you say that? My friends either pronounce it as "toast" or "tao-oost." LOL

I usually prefer other Korean restaurants than Toust but recently... I've been craving it. I went here today and ordered the BBQ Chicken. They give you SO. MUCH. FOOD. Like, I can never finish the whole thing... kinda sad because it doesn't taste the same when you togo it. Hmm, Toust is affordable && they have their daily specials for like a dollar cheaper! (For example: Bibimbap Mondays -A lot of my friends get this.) So far, everything I've tried (bulgogi, spicy tofu soup, bibimbap, kimchi fried rice, and ramen) have been good. Toust has yummy banchans (side dishes) too^^. What else? Service is nice... the interior is VERY Korean aha. Justt go and try it~

Right as I walked in, I was bombarded with the high shrieks and laughter that are so essential to Korean girls. I'm Korean so I have it in me too.

Korean girls know Korean food. And we come here because Toust makes it the best, as far as Berkeley goes, which isn't much.

I got the daily special, the beef tofu soup, which was pretty decent. It had huge chunks of carrot and zucchini, something I've never seen before. I heard they put frozen vegetables in the kimchi fried rice, which is a bit weird. But I tried it at home and it came out pretty good! 

Anyways, I didn't get the egg that I usually love cracking directly into my soup bowl, but I didn't mind. I usually have enough cholesterol intake for the day anyways. The beef was fatty, and it kept getting stuck in my teeth, which was pretty annoying. But I used a little toothpick, and it made me feel like an old Korean man. 

The side dishes were sparse, and one of them was canned corn! Suh-weet. It actually tasted good. But you can never go wrong with canned corn. 

Here's a toast to Toust!
Well done for attempting to keep up the well-deserved dignity of Korean food!

t-toust? how do we pronouce it?? TAOst, TOHst, TWOst...no idea. and why is there a t in front of it??? anyways, onto the review. I got the bulgogi sandwich, and i was thinking to compare the sandwiches from here and Espresso Experience (see my review). These sandwiches have major differences. The Bulgogi "toust" comes with bulgogi, a fried egg, cabbage and what seemed to be cheese. These ingredients really didn't mesh well. On top of that the bulgogi was not really the best quality meat. The flavor was not that great either. The bread was pretty good, but that couldn't make up for the poor quality meat and awkward flavors. One good thing is that they come with a free bag of chips, and if you get it to-go, they have a pretty fancy bag and box. So Espresso Experience wins the sandwich battle hands down. I would probably come back here to try something more Korean. 3 stars.

Food was $8 or $9.  I don't remember exactly.

Not only was I really hungry, but I was planning on playing tennis later that night, so I was ready to put down some serious calories.  Upon my friend's suggestion, we came to Toust, er, apparently T-Toust.

You may immediately notice the brutally fluorescent cafeteria lighting and cheap, but clean cafeteria furniture.  Please do not try to adjust your eyes, it's futile.  Nothing on the tables, which were largely filled, or the menu spoke to me, so I went with bibim bap, a safe bet.  I was incorrect.  The beef was, well, quite bad.  However, they did something remarkable with the egg by managing to cook it to the exact threshold where it would hold together and look vaguely more like a fried egg than a raw one.  The dish wasn't nearly hot enough to cook the egg, so I cautiously moved the egg over, being careful not to spill the nearly raw yolk everywhere.  This, by the way, is coming from a guy who likes his Eggs Benedict runny.

I heard that their soups are better, and their ban chan wasn't bad.  I guess you don't have to compete too hard to outclass Gomnaru or Steve's.

I don't think I ordered T-Toust's best dish (I got ddukbokki) 'cause I thought it was just ok. I found their ddukbokki kinda on the sweet side. It's good, but I think Espresso Experience's ddukbokki beats T-Toust's. 

I heard their sundubu is really good so I'll try that next time and write another review.

Very mediocre Korean homestyle 'comfort' food at slightly high price.  The food here honestly isn't terrible, but with so much foot traffic from students (it's located directly in Sather Lane), there are many more affordable options when you weigh the taste/portion/cost.  The only thing that saves it is that they have a rotating special every day of the week, in which a normal priced item becomes slightly discounted.  Not bad, but definitely forgettable.

This place was a solid 5 stars before they changed management.  They used to have these "Korean Burritos" which were seriously the best stuff ever.  Imagine a burrito on the outside, but inside is Korean rice, with some edamame and plenty of bulgoki and an amazing dipping sauce.  Those burritos kept warm for HOURS.  

I took my friends that go to UCSD to eat those burritos and before they changed the management and took the burritos off the menu, my friends would make the trip to Berkeley just to eat them. 

Sadly those days are in the past and this place is just okay.  Not horrible, but a little over priced for the quality.  I guess I shouldn't compare this place to My Tofu House in San Francisco, because that place is truly the best Korean food. 

I've tried a lot of their dishes but nothing was a standout.  Their dumplings are way too oily though.  Everything else is safe to order.

If you order Korean tofu here, make sure you order the spiciest option if you want even a hint of flavor. My girlfriend ordered the mild and regretted that decision. 

We ordered the beef tofu soup, and there wasn't really any beef or tofu, mostly zucchini. They didn't supply a raw egg for us, which I thought was standard in Korean restaurants. Side dishes were also lacking: there's only kimchi, potatoes and fish cake. Needless to say we were pretty disappointed. 

However, given the lackluster Korean tofu places around Berkeley, this one is relatively good. The Korean restaurant on Telegraph and Blake is slightly better, but this one is cheaper and suits students better with its price and proximity to campus.

Worst tofu soup I've ever had. No flavor in soup, tasted just like hot water. I got the tofu soup w/ kalbi - they just throw a piece of unmarinated short rib into the soup w/ some vegetables. The meat might have just been boiled in the water because I could barely chew off the meat. I gave up and just left it.

I love this place! Number one Korean restaurant in Berkeley (in my opinion)! The servers are suuuper nice and the food is decent enough considering they're catering to college students. When my friends want to eat Korean food for the first time, I always take them here. :))))))

I got the Kimchi soup which was a NO GO. But the people I went with got some good stuff. The Bi Bim Bab was tasty and the hit of the day was definitely the hot pot beef. If you eat meat, do yourself and favor and just order this. Heads up about the cashier who is probably the owner. Classic micromanager, he told us where to sit even though there were free tables to spare and was pushy about ordering even though there was not a line waiting. Food was good...would return in a blue moon.

I had a hard time deciding between 3 and 4 stars for this place, so I think it's fair to give it 3.5 stars.

Definitely an average experience for Korean food at Berkeley, but I think this is the best Korean restaurant you will find in the area. They offer a discount on the regular Bi Bim Bap on Mondays I believe, so come then if you want to save a little bit on your meal.

Campus food stop.

I ordered the bibimbap. Beware of the red pepper sauce! It's peppery! and none too tasty. But the bibimbap, just a mixture of raw things + ground meat + a fried egg, was okay. I can't complain. It was just okay. Maybe they could've used fresher vegetables? Added more meat? I'm not saying one shouldn't order it, but at the same time, I would suggest one order something else, and only get the bibimbap out of indecision (probably what I experienced).

I guess the selection was varied and all, but I don't know.  Finding good korean food in the bay always sparks contentious debates in my circle of friends. I don't know if Toust even makes the debate list..
The place has cheap food, it's clean,..but it's just a place to go when you see someone for a lunch date and want to talk more than you want to try out a restaurant.

Very good, large, cheap food. However, the ambiance of Sather Lane is unappealing. Sometimes stinky smells waft into the window, so I would not sit by the window if I were you. However, the four side dishes are adequate and the food is large and affordable. The specials are a pretty good deal as well. The tofu soup was definitely acceptable. The seafood is nasty, though. Anyway, I can't wait to go back and try the bi bim bap!

I must first say that I have the lowest spice tolerance or close to no spice tolerance. This place serves some spicy food. If you are one that can handle it and want to test your taste buds, here's the place to go.

I came here on a cold weekend with my girlfriend after our tennis tournament because we were craving something warm and soup like. Suddenly we decided upon this place. Now needless to say we got some spicy food. 

I got their hot beef soup and I asked for the least amount of spice possible and i ended up drinking 3-4 glasses of water and eating tons of rice and leaving with a mouth filled with spice. The food was pretty good though.

This place does come with a price and in my opinion is a tad over priced for the proportion they give. Now I don't know if its normal for korean places to give small proportions, but for $8 for a hot beef soup, I was expecting something a little bigger. The size of the bowl was small. My gf order something else and her bowl was about 1/3 of the size. I am disappointed with the serving size but amazed at the spice they put into their food.

If there is ever a craving for spice or me wanting to boost up my spice tolerance this is the place you'll find me.

I would come to this place when I was in need of a little bit more quality than Steve's down the street. My usual favorite was the spicy BBQ pork, and it never failed to satsify. Toust also provides a wealth of sides, with unlimited refills for those with a heavy appetite. I've also tried the soon tofu and spicy beef soup, all very satisfying.

However if you're looking for quantity over quality and want a lot of meat, I would say Steve's in Asian Ghetto would be the best choice.

I came here for lunch Saturday after class, and I thought it was very delicious.  I had the dduk-mandoo-gook (dumpling and rice cake soup) and my friend had the soon doobu (soft tofu soup).  Both felt very homemade, and it was neither too sweet nor salty.  The lady at the counter was very friendly and attentive.  The self serve water and utensils were clean, as was the place overall.  I'm not from the Berkeley area so I can't give a local's perspective, but as a visitor from SF it's a place I'd definitely recommend.

T-Toust  sells korean eats on the cheap. average price  7  there is a daily special in the 6.35-6.50 range. the usual popular korean dishes are served here.

drill: order placed at counter, pay in advance, food brought to table.

eats: bi bim  bap(7.35)
-fried egg, sliced red cabbage, carrots, bean sprouts,cabbage, schredded beef, lettuce
over short grain rice
-3 banchan(kimchi, potato, veggie)
-plentiful to eat, nothing special, hot sauce so so.

banchan:
-amigo assistant in kitchen
-food came out in 5 minutes.
-cash only?
This place's side dishes gave me food poisoning. Enough said.

This is my favorite place for Korean food by the UC Berkeley Campus. I've come here a couple times now, and each time trying a bunch of different things. I noticed that their food quality can be inconsistent at times, but it's never bad. It just ranges from good, to OHH that's REALLLY good. 

What I do love about T-Toust is their salads. I NEVER ate salad before this place. They have the best dressing and I'm still trying to figure out what it is. (Please let me know if you know!) I always finish their complimentary salads!

This place is good. I always love end up loving their food, and their complimentary salad keeps me coming back. Too bad I'm leaving Berkeley, but T-Toust, I want you to know that you made me fall in love with salad. Life changing dressing right there.

Star deductions for using Styrofoam and plastic for to-go orders...tsk...tsk...but I do like that they pack the seasoned rice in a separate container, so you can better control the starch intake. 

The name is a bit odd, yet amusing and dramatic: "T-Toust! Never Before" and warmly reminds me of nonsensical, cutesy English translations found on imported Japan town stationary and toys. 

Lots of Koreans eating here is a good sign. Although it used to be a cool spot for Americanish grub about a year ago, it's new incarnation has grown on me. What I like most about T-Toust is that they include about six different side snacks with each entree, ranging from salty, sweet, hot, to fishy -- which add a lot of variation to the dishes. 

I've had Bi Bim Bap, Grilled Pork, and today the Spicy Chicken. Of the three, I like the Bi Bim Bap most, but the others were satisfying as well. 

Each serving is enough to feed a Cal football player, or two regular people, OR double as lunch AND dinner! Go there when your appetite is big and your change is low.

This Korean restaurant caters to the UC Berkeley college crowd, since it's basically across the street and sandwiched between the campus and a dorm. However, the restaurant is very clean and bright and trendy. I like the yellow walls and the Korean magazines they leave out if you want to read them.

The food is good! It's not the very best Korean food you'll ever have, but the daily specials are a good choice if you're going there for the first time. And I like anything that comes in a claypot.

Their customer service is excellent. They make a conscious effort to keep everything clean and tidy. And they always serve you Korean side dishes as a service.

As a Korean-American who grew up on the cooking of her fobby Korean mother and on the restaurants of Koreatown, LA, there is no way that I could give a Korean restaurant in Berkeley more than three stars. Sorry, Toust. However, Toust is actually not that bad. It's decent Korean food really close to campus. 

They have daily specials where they knock off ~$1 the regular price. Today was bibimbap Monday! It was a large portion and it was not that bad. Price: $6.91 (including tax). One thing that I do like about the place is that it has the feel of a trendy Korean restaurant. Clean interior and quick service. Definitely better than Bear Ramen and Kimchi Garden!

Good place to stop on those times you want to catch up with your Korean friend or when you're really craving Korean food.

TIPS:
1) Green Tea bags by the hot/cold water dispenser! 
2) Order the daily specials: cheaper!

I come here every month or so for my fixing of bibimbap, since it's so close to campus and on Wednesdays, the hot pot bibimbap is only 6.59 + tax! I haven't tried anything else here, but the bibimbap is decent. Their service is great and it includes a couple side dishes as well!

It sucks that they recently added a 50 cent credit card charge...

This is a cool little place to eat at. I got the dumpling soup for lunch. The dumplings were alright. They looked like they were the frozen kinds you get from the store. The soup was so delicious though! Mmm... 
I noticed that other places with the same food cost a few dollars less than this place, but I don't know about the quality of their food so... eh.

I've walked by Sather Lane a few times and never gotten to try out Toust, so I finally did during finals week!

I ordered the beef ramen and seafood pancakes. The ramen was a little too spicy for me, but the seafood pancakes smelled & tasted delicious! I definitely, definitely recommend them!

Overall though, I felt that Toust was a bit too pricey for the portion sizes; Kimchi Garden is definitely a better bet (:

OK, don't get me wrong. Toust is probably one of the best/only korean joints within walking distance of campus. And, as a cal alum and still lingering near cal, I do appreciate Toust for what it is. But, it always disappoints me. Maybe because I'm accustomed to being treated as a queen at other typical korean restaurants (I live near the k-town hub in oakland). So yes, bring me my 15 tiny dishes noooooow. Then, I'll be satisfied.

Specials are a good deal.

Not a bad lunch spot.

I generally don't eat Korean food that often but one of my favorite dishes is spicy rice cake aka ddukboki. The ddukboki here wasn't that great though...it wasn't spicy at all and the taste got pretty tedious. I felt sad that ddukboki wasn't my favorite dish anymore but maybe it's just because the quality here wasn't great.

I came here for lunch on a whim, and got the veggie + tofu bibimbap. AMAZING. It was seriously the best bibimbap I've ever had--well-marinated tofu, really fresh mushrooms and mung beans. The little dish of marinated/pickled veggies were very tasty too, as was the miso soup.  

For some reason businesses in this little tunnel have always seemed offputting, and I never would have gone in if I hadn't been starrrving, but man, I'm so glad I did! I'll be back.

This place hit the spot after an afternoon of boozing over at Bear's Lair.  I ordered the bibimbap and it came sizzling hot in a clay pot.  Yum.  I also liked that they served those Korean appetizers along with your meal.  Service and ambience are nothing special, but if you're looking for good Korean food at a reasonable price, this place has got that covered.

this place is pretty decent... the servings are adequate, they could give more, but the food is well-made and the service is great. i had the bim bim bap, which was pretty good (especially with a lot of the red pepper sauce)- i like that the veggies that came with it were also well seasoned- they had a hint of sesame oil. one serving came out to $8 with tax, so i can't expect too much. definitely coming back, if only for their well- cooked rice- compared to crossroads and cafe 3's soggy messes.

bring cash though cuz the minimum charge is $10

BARF.

T-Toust = disgrace to Korean food. 
Who cares if the meal is cheap if you've paid money to shovel trash in your mouth? Soon tofu was nasty, goopy (omg! what the ..?!!?!)  and full of MSG-tasting something.... and the spicy pork dish.... oh my. Barf. Looks and feels raw. I was scared for my health and my life. I was mad that I had to sit there and chew on this ugly, stupid food that I make better myself. And I was even more mad that I had just paid these people for disgusting food and I couldn't get a refund. Haha. Refund for food. Ridiculous, I know. But that's how I felt. 

You know what's worse? They market this as Korean food. That is sad. So, so sad. What a horrible dishonor to the great name of Korean cuisine. 

"Toust,.. youuu... dis-honooorrrr... ouurrr famiryyy....."

ok, maybe i was being too adventurous. cold noodles on a hot day. yea, it sounded pretty appealing. it was alright until it got too salty. maybe ill try the tofu soup next time

they need to feed me more side dishes. and the thing that looked and tasted like potato salad.... yea that wasnt korean...

Honestly, the main reason I come here is the proximity to my workplace. The food is decent, service is quick and there are reasonably priced daily specials. Fortunately, my favorite Korean dish (bibim bap) is usually offered twice a week as a special. Korean restaurants typically offer many side dishes (banchan) to complement your meal, as many as 8-12. T-Toust only offers three: kimchi, potatoes, and fishcake. 

It's a solid "3" in the star department. Not great, not bad, but....average.

Best Korean food next to campus. There's Steve's BBQ in the Ghetto, but that place should be renamed Jose's. Haven't seen a Korean working the cash register or kitchen over there in a while. But this place, T-Toust (no idea why they do that T-T thing), is pretty legit. Prices have gone up recently, and it was a shock when I went there earlier tonight with a friend (really fobby Korean guy) and saw that bi-bim-bap (mixed rice with vegetables and meat) was $7+. I was a little disappointed the meat in the bi-bim-bap wasn't bulgogi (marinated beef) but marinated ground beef. That's cool and all, but it's a little cheap... 

Anyway, they serve purple/white mixed rice which is really yum, and even healthy too. There's real Koreans working the cashiers and the kitchen, which gives an authentic sort of Korean cuisine. I like the place, and so do the fobs. I see them there a lot. Big thumbs up.

i was so ready to love this place, seriously, i was psyched.  it's cold outside i have a cold in my nose all i wanted was some hot spicy soup, and when i walked by this place which looked all family-y and had funky chairs and displayed lots of pictures of hot spicy soups on the walls i was sure it was exactly what i wanted.  
i ordered the kim chee ramen.  it was sick.  seriously.  i ate some of the broth and the cabbage but the noodle and flavoring were certainly from a 25 cent package.  the flavoring packet flavor made it all grainy and gross... so disappointing.  the rice, which looked delicious, was cold.  ok i know part of the point is to pour your soup over it/put some in your soup but it was cold!!! not just not warm, actually cold.  and the little snacky delicious dishes which are always my favorite part of korean food were actually inedible.  the kim chee, the seaweed salad, the potatoes were the worst i've ever had and believe me i'm not a closet korean food snob out to sabotage everyone not serving the goumet variety, i wasnt expecting anything fancy, just something i'd want to eat. 
i never really write bad reviews, but this place made me so sad i felt like it was my duty.  i'm broke, so, taking myself out to lunch (even if is was a $7 lunch) is kind of a luxury for me these days and it sucks to waste that on a meal like this one.

Where do you go when you have the budget of an undergraduate college student?  Duh - you go to where all the kids are going, near UC Berkeley's campus.  Thanks to glowing endorsements by Aimee L. and Patrick M., my friend and I decided to head to lunch in Berkeley for the day and try the much lauded T-Toust...much to the appreciation of our pocketbooks - we had an enormous lunch for two for less than $14.  

We shared the Yuk Gae Jang (Beef Stew) and the Bulgogi (barbecued meat), and partook in the free banchan and two nice sized bowls of rice.  Pretty good stuff...the bulgogi had great flavor (although it was a little tougher than I prefer), and the Yuk Gae Jang was deliciously spicy, with tender chunks of beef and really yummy pieces of kosari (fern), bean sprouts, and mushrooms.  Everything was served quickly and piping hot, and I couldn't eat again until much, much later that evening.  

Why don't we have good, cheap Korean places like this in SF?  Why?!?!

Very average Korean food with over average portions with very average prices coming from an incredibly average campus eatery. With this my review is DONE.

Well, maybe not. The name is weird. It doesn't make sense. I guess its easy to remember though. The decor is forgettable. The same goes for the service. The food really isn't as "good as mom makes it", but definitely has enough authenticity to whet your Korean food craving. Try the usual crowd favorites of soondubu (soft tofu soup) or bibimbap (umm a bowl of mixed rice, veggies, and meat?)

Theres nothing really here that makes the place stand out, either good or bad. I would of totally forgot I ate here, except for the receipt I found in my desk. Hmm.

I guess I'm not a big fan of Korean food when it comes to eating out, at least it wouldn't be the first thing to come to mind. But I met a friend here for lunch and the food was ok. I got the beef entree, which came with soup, a small side of salad, and rice, including the side pickled dishes.  It was a lot of food, and it seems like this place is populated with a lot of Cal students...perhaps because of the affordable prices.

I LOVE THIS PLACE. I love all its kimchijigae type stuff and I love Korean food in general so I  come here around once or twice a week. I would say they are probably cheaper/average price-wise but their food is really good. The staff is friendly as well and there's little wait time making it convenient.

I'm sad that one of the guys, Justin, doesn't seem to be around anymore but the new people are pretty awesome dude. One of the older servers always holds up a box of candy when Im ready to leave and goes "Candy?!" with a huge smile. It makes my day. 

Bibimbap, Kimchijigae, Kalbi, Bulgolgi... all good choices at Toust. If you want a soup thats not spicy... you should get the Beef Soup. Lots a flavor and quite sweet and quite a bit of meat.  :)

I would like to know where the korean-food lovers get their korean food. This place is crap compared to samwon or oghane or many many other places in Oakland, but where else can you get decent korean food that's walking distance from campus? I guess Bear Ramen is alright. Steve's is far worse than this place. The service is pretty fast and i can get a tofu soup and rice for about 7 bux.

So please tell me where to get better korean food that's walking distance from campus. Or maybe ur mom vacuum seals bags of home-made korean food for you.

I feel like I haven't earned the right to review this place yet, having yet to try one of their delicious-looking "tousts." I can say however, that this is very unlikely to be "The Healthiest Food" in Berkeley, as their flyers claim. Are fried potatoes sandwiched in bread really healthy? Bacon in bread? Hmmm...
This aside, I tried the Japchae one night--waited for about 20 minutes to get my food and was late to my Decal. The inside of this place is cute, very modern, with lots of Korean Cal students. 
The Japchae was pretty good, lots of veggies and all...I enjoyed it...nothing to write home about though. Next time I'll try one of those healthy tousts.

Food around campus needs to be judged by a different set of standards, and I guess I should add that a 3-star is a campus 4 1/2 stars.  It's designed for college students and the occasional tourist, and should be inexpensive, tasty, relatively nutritious, and quick.   T-Toust fills the bill nicely.  I don't speak Korean (big surprise there), but I suspect that the little square character with the T IS the name, and they also spell it out for us Anglos.  

They have an extensive menu, featuring the usual Korean specialties plus a few more unusual items, with their daily specials a couple of dollars cheaper than on the regular menu. At lunch time patrons are cheek by jowl and waiting, with only one amazingly efficient and overworked young woman taking orders, serving, cleaning tables, moving the 3 chile sauce bottles from table to table, and running the register, so one might say the service is not the best,  although if I were looking for an employee, I'd hire her in a heartbeat.

The food was fresh and clean, well prepared, perhaps not entirely inspired, but by campus standards, sparklingly good.  My hot pot bi bim bap to go featured separate compartments for the little side nibbles typical of Korean meals, the rice & veggies were tasty, and a generous cup of chile sauce was included to counteract the mildness of the flavors (again, good for the spice-tolerance-impaired average patron).  One of my new go-to places, fo sho.  I do wish they'd get a little greener with their to-go containers...

This place used to have some pretty nifty sandwiches and wraps on their menu in addition to their Korean dishes, but they decided to strike that out one day....

and I don't mind!

Everyone made such a big deal about them not offering the sandwiches and wraps anymore that their popularity has gone down, but let's focus on what they are better at making anyway. I've always ordered the Korean dishes even when those other items were offered.

Their hot tofu soup is damn spicy and always comes out piping hot. The bulogi comes out pretty sizzling too. The bibimbop is a good size. Everything is fairly cheap. Sure it's not gourmet, but it's good quality for its price. What's not to like?

Taste: 2
Value: 4
Service: -

Had this place cater for an event, and I thought Joshuya had a lot of rice on their sushi. The sushi was very mediocre, but then again, maybe their specialty rolls are better. However, based on my experience, you should only come here if you want cheap, very mediocre sushi.
Good Sushi, really good price for students.

Tako kept me alive during college. I would never order "real" sushi or anything raw here, but the golden california roll is TOO good, and if you've only got, say, your last $4 to your name crumpled up in your pocket, you can at least keep the dizzy spells away for a little while. People say this place is really gross or bad sushi, WELL DUH. It's not a sushi joint in my eyes; it's more like a Burger King that just happens to serve japanese cuisine rather than cheeseburgers. And it's damn good and beats the hell out of spending your last $4 on a flat of Top Ramen.

i have forgotten how cheap things are in Berkeley.  That deserves at least 2 stars.  

Well, in addition to that, the sushi is pretty good and I highly recommend their popcorn bite salmon, really nifty and yummy appetizer.  

We ordered that and 4 roll for three of us and still had leftover. So they have pretty big quantity.  In term of the quality, I am pretty happy with it.  2 of our order were fried/cooked, so I can say to its entirety that the fish are fresh, but the ones I had were good.
the spider rolls are good, as are the teriyaki chicken bowls.  i just wish they served sake.  the portions tend to vary in size, but mostly its pretty filling. :)

This place is definitely a great, hidden staple on the UC Berkeley campus. I came here recently from San Jose CA, for a birthday dinner with about 20 guests. This place wasn't very big so I didn't expect fast service or the greatest of quality... I was wrong. We ordered party platters in advance and as soon as we walked through the door, they were bringing the finished food out to our table. We got 2 huge plates of teriyaki chicken, 2 huge containers of katsu chicken, and 2 huge platters of california rolls, and shrimp tempura rolls, and 2 huge bowls of sesame seed white rice. The food we ordered was more than enough and our bill came out to about $10 per person. Now onto the food.... IT'S AMAZING! The teriyaki chicken was so flavorful and not overly sweet. Definitely a good balance of chicken flavor and sweet teriyaki sauce. The katsu chicken was crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside and wasn't overly oily. The katsu sauce it came with was a bit too tangy for me but that was easily countered by the sesame seed white rice, which had a rich sesame seed flavor but didn't over-power the rice at all. The california rolls were definitely good and probably the best quality of california roll I have had in the bay area. I didn't get to try much of the shrimp tempura roll though because I had already filled up on everything else. From what I remember though it was good, but I have had better. Another thing I really liked was that the staff didn't snicker or humorously make fun of me when I asked for a fork because I don't know how to use chopsticks.

Pretty good food at rock bottom prices.   We went to Tako Sushi around 9 and ended up splitting the pork tonkatsu donburi.  It came with miso soup and a fried egg mixture that included imitation crab.  Our waiter was super nice considering we split a 5$ meal and had a lingering after-dinner conversation.

Liked their sake. Sushi was good for typical restaurant sushi. Nice looking dining area (a date spot maybe?), but I thought it was a little expensive for the quality and amount of food you get. It's probably my fault though. Came here with the $50 gift certificate coupon from restaurant.com :) So, you have to spend over $100 and there's 18% gratuity. Not bad right? We chose items up to $100 but with the sake and hidden gratuity, it came out to be 30 bucks per person for 4 people. Not a bad considering I was stuffed, but I came with the impression that it was going to be a cheap meal. Impression aside,  food was good, just good. Not amazing.

Super cheap. I mean, really really cheap. Just get rolls and you'll be safe.

Perhaps I was a poor college student with no taste buds, but I liked the food here.

Are you serious?  Or are you people just starving?  
I'll admit, I've ate here too.  But BEWARE.  My friend had to run for the bathroom with explosive diarrhea before the check even got to the table.  I was wise enough not to eat the raw fish.  My favorite thing to order was the miso soup and a rice.  The total came out to $2.  That's how you eat starving student style.  It's cheap, but at the expense of your personal health.  Who knows what type of worms that live in that quality of raw fish.  Most of you are smart UC Berkeley students, use your brain when it comes to this stuff.  Get a burrito at La Burrita instead.

Although I give this place a one star, I used to go here quite often until I couldn't take it anymore...yes this place is very cheap and for the food they serve I think it should be cheaper. 

Good for students like me since the price is low and the portion is pretty big. But, the quality is very very very bad...I don't think I have ever eaten such low quality sushi in my entire life lol. After first few visits, I realized this place is not for sushi or sashimi...more for teriyaki and donburi (but they are whatever too) 

I am kind of crazy about sushi, and I know my fresh fish...but this place is so so bad. I never go to this place anymore I think it's just a waste of money.

Nonetheless, the owner lady is very nice :)

I'm pretty picky with sushi and this place just doesn't do it for me. After having eaten good sushi/sashimi, its hard for me to go back to places like Tako Sushi. Quality of their food can definitely be improved. Not sure if the price they charge is worth it. I'd recommend that sushi lovers avoid this place.

I wish Yelp would allow negative stars. 

The miso soup came in a stained plastic bowl with a VERY strong aroma of ... bleach. If you are going to use bleach, can you AT LEAST make sure my bowl is not covered with brown stains?? The health department should shut down the place based on that alone.

As for the sushi, let's just say I hope what I ate was fish. =/

My friend and I stuffed ourselves with 28 pieces of suhi for both of us, and after tax it was only around $17. The services is quite good-- the waitress always made sure our glasses were filled with their lemon water and she offered to take a picture of us when she noticed my friend was taking photos of the sushi. Though their sushi isn't the best, it does taste decent.

For the price paid, and the proximity to campus, the sushi is not bad. I always get the caterpillar roll and I like it. Of course, there are much better places, but if you don't wanna go far from campus, then Tako Sushi is adequate

Literally waited 30 minutes for a Beef Teriyaki Roll and Baja roll. We weren't even served any miso soup, and when we asked the waitress about it, she said it didn't come with the meal. What crap is that. You should have given us soup anyways because we were waiting so long. I pretty much finished drinking my glass of water by the time the sushi came out. 

Waited 30 minutes for some sushi and ate it in 10. I rather go to a sushi place, wait for a a longer time but know that my food is gonna be good! We waited a long time for bad sushi!

Went here a second time during lunch. They were super busy and the service was extremely slow. Ordered the Bento box which wasn't very good. But the portions were huge. The green tea tasted pretty bad also. They ran out of the wings I ordered so they had to downgrade my order of 8 to an order of 5.

I used to go weekly, but now I visit Tako only every few months. Judging from the reactions of friends and family, Tako Sushi's food appeals best for those who like cooked Japanese food and not to tastes for premium raw sushi. I'm definitely in the former group of patrons: my favorite items are the Teriyaki chicken bowl and sushi rolls, the shiitaki rolls, and the tasty miso soup :-) Friends/family have complained on several occasions that the raw sushi is not very fresh.

Food aside, the location is great, the late hours are very convenient, and there's usually ample seating. Service is usually very slow and inattentive. The place is *probably* hygienic, but it's pretty dirty with food stains decorating the walls.

The service is very slow. I have seen students leaving out of impatience. The sushis are excelent, in the Chinese-Korean style (dragons, tempuras sushis, rainbow, etc), and their miso soup is really creamy and rich. I highly recommend the vegetarian sushi.
Just ok food.

Tako sushi is definitely a great place to go if you don't want to pay too much for your sushi! If you are introducing someone to sushi, you might want to take them here.

I definitely prefer Joshuya's on Dwight, but this place is great for the price.

Sushi quality is not very good, but they make up for it with a huge selection and relatively good prices, with some student friendly specials to boot. Many of the rolls are actually pretty tasty, but it lacks poise.

We LOVE Tako Sushi! 

There's a sort of mental equation you do every time you go out to eat that helps you calculate whether the food you're eating is as good as the money you spent on it. Sometimes, there's a happy medium where you feel like you ate well and paid a fair price; sometimes, you know you were overcharged for mediocre food; and sometimes, on very rare occasions, you feel like you got a total steal and scored pretty good food for next to nothing.

That latter scenario is how I feel about Tako. The food isn't the most-friggin-amazing-oh-my-god sushi you'll ever eat, but it's damn tasty. Hits the spot. And the prices are ridiculously low, especially for sushi.

Plus, the staff are all super friendly.

I highly recommend this place and go there all the time, myself.

Awful.  Atrocious.  Ick.  I used to eat here all through college, but went about six months ago and had to send stuff back.  Some of the fish looked like what I imagine the small intestine to look like.  Avoid this place like the plague unless you like eating questionable (at best) raw fish.

If you're not incredibly picky about your sushi, and you like a variety of rolls to choose from, tako sushi is a good choice. My sister and I have come here to eat a few times and it's been tasty and relatively  well priced.  Check out their takeout partner nude sushi as well.

I refuse to feel ashamed for loving this place! 

Tako Sushi is cheap AND good. I can't attest for the sashimi or nigiri but I will guarantee that the rolls are great.  My favorites are the shrimp tempura, california and salmon skin rolls. 

Oh and what can I say about the salad dressing they have?!?! It's delicious. More then once have I considered stealing the bottle (message me if you know the recipe).
Likes: their cheap spider rolls and quick service.  Nice place to grab lunch or take out.

This is my go to sushi place when I want cheap sushi rolls. How can you blame a poor college student?

They serve free miso soup and the lady waiter is usually very attentive.

Oh, the sound of Tako sushi right now makes me feel slightly ill.. If you are looking for a quick fix of bad, but cheap sushi.. Tako might suit you. Otherwise, if you're looking to survive, look elsewhere.

When I came here, I made the terrible, terrible mistake of ordering something that resembled kimbap. I know, I know! Seriously mistake. It was probably the worst experience I've had a Japanese restaurant. The mushrooms did not taste right, and the yellow cucumbers were so dry and stale. I also had a spicy tuna roll. Not only was it not spicy, but it didn't even taste like it had fish in it. 

Granted, prices here are really cheap. But for not much more, you could get waaay better sushi. I am being pretty generous here with two stars, and I'm not picky! I promise!

Fast service. Nice seating area with outside seating! An extensive menu of rolls. Fish that won't make you sick. And a wait staff that looks to please you -- all of these can be found at Tako Sushi, at -- here's the kicker -- affordable prices!

You won't get sick like you may from the food in the Asian Ghetto. And your wallet won't turn into a feather, like it will down the street at Norikonoko or Joshu-ya Sushi Boat. Tako Sushi is convenient, tasty, and priced right -- and the perfect fix if you want to get your Japanese on, on a frequent basis.

I get sashimi. Or udon. It's always tasty at Tako Sushi. And they even subbed out my rice for extra green salad. Woh yeah, baby. I can't comment too heavily on the quality of their chicken, but their fish and their veggies are great. In my opinion, Tako Sushi is underrated. It's sushi at a value-price, and they do value-priced sushi RIGHT.

This is a nice place for college students to grab lunch, dinner or both. The price is very student friendly and the portions that they serve are worth the price paid.  I never really looked into the restaurant until one of my friends told me that she bought kimchi fried rice for only $4. So I decided to go and find some food the next day with a couple of other friends, although I did not order the kimchi fried rice, I was able to get a pretty good deal from the "starving student" section of the menu. Went back again a few days later with another group of friends and ordered a giant bento box.

    As a college student and a customer, the pricing and the size of the dish captures my attention, but the taste matters too. I would not say that the food was bad, but it is definitely not great, some dishes are better than others. 
     The curry fish katsu was mediocre, the curry was not what I expected, but the fish katsu was cooked pretty well, the fish maintained its moisture and it was crispy at the same time. 
      The teriyaki with tempora bento box was pretty good over all, and the portion was enough for two meals. However the salad that came with the bento box was drenched in dressing, I felt a bit overwhelmed by the dressing(maybe tone down on the dressing?). One bad egg can mess up the entire batch of cookies.

Tako Sushi is a crowded little sushi shop that catered to the poor college students.  The quality isn't too great, but its cheap, although over the years, the sushi roll size is slowly getting smaller.  I guess they need to skim the money somewhere to survive in this economy.  The starving student special are pretty good as fillers.

I remember back in the days we would order 100 piece of california rolls for only about $30, which to us is a better alternative to lure students to your club meetings since its better than pizza which everyone is sick of, since you get that for free almost everywhere in college.

However, throughout the years, my value of food changes.  The quality outweighs the quantity and price now.  Thus, I have to say farewell to Tako sushi, I might come visit one of those days when I am starving but forgot my credit card and debit card while strapped for cash.  Till then, au revoir~

Delicious, affordable sushi with extremely friendly service. Our waiter tried to give us back the tip, saying it was too much,  which only made me want to tip him more! We thoroughly enjoyed our dinner...thanks, Tako!
i went back and ordered some simpler sushi. friends got ramen. still, nothing special. good service and cheap cheap cheap though. makes it A-OK in my book.

I love Tako sushi. Sometimes I crave it and drive all the way to Berkeley just to get a roll or some bulgogi. It's delicious and relatively cheap. Granted, they've got un-traditional types of sushi that make sushi purists cringe, and every time I go there someone in the table next to me is telling their sushi virgin of a friend, "have you ever had raw fish? Really, it's not that bad." If that sort of thing bothers you, you probably won't like Tako Sushi. But if you can get around that, try coming here. This place just has the best food.

Please note, I've been to Japan thrice and even lived there for a brief spell, so I do know what real sushi is supposed to taste like. =)
Good price and very good food. Parking sucks and some tables have poor lighting

Only three stars? Tako sushi has always been one of my favorite reasonably priced sushi places; even when I'm back home in the South Bay I find myself wanting to drive up to Berkeley to get some Tako Sushi. I have yet to have a bad experience with them; they have always politely greeted me at the door and checked on me frequently at the table. The food has always been up to my standards for what I'm paying too - you can't complain much when the most you pay for a roll is $7.99.
I love this place. Its super cheap and delicious. Everyone should try the Lion King roll, its amazing. This place is way better than Joshuya  sushi.

An intestinal tract hardened by years of Asian street food has apparently helped my ability to digest mediocre sushi of questionable quality. I'm satisfied with the variety and value obtained for the price here. I usually aim for about $10-$11 between a deluxe roll and a simple "stomach filler" roll: 

main order: a $8.99 Dynamite Roll or Cherry Blossom, or $8.49 Ashby Roll, Pink Dragon, Rainbow Roll, any of which could be a meal in itself (certainly a lunch)

+ an additional cheap veggie roll, $1.79 for kappa maki, avocado-cucumber roll, or a four-piece California roll

I'm usually quite full and the final bill doesn't hurt TOO much.

My choice of fish is nothing fancy -- just tuna and salmon for the raw stuff, and tempura shrimp. I like octopus and scallop and clam as well, but I would never order these here, as I question the freshness of less popular ingredients. I only stick to maki rolls, and never get sashimi or nigiri, as I think that's the way to get more bang for your buck.

I've ordered some of the appetizers before, and never been impressed. Edamame is way too cheap to buy and prepare on your own, and not worth what you pay for a tiny dish in the store. Their gyoza are wimpy and dry and probably not made in-house. I like fried tempura with udon, but since learning to make my own, I've come to realize how bland theirs can be. The biggest disappointment was their agedashi tofu, which had no flavor or personality whatsoever (yes I know, it's tofu, but it DOES have a distinct taste and texture when done well).

The service is as sterile as the Christian contemporary they broadcast on the stereo, but it's sufficient. I think I've gotten a few free bowls of miso out of them when I've ordered "enough" (though there's nothing in the menu or on the walls to indicate what that magical threshold might be).

Come if you're stuck on campus and are craving sushi but you're not expecting much. Don't forget your punch card. At $5 a punch spread over 63 holes ($315), it's going to take a loooot of sushi to earn yourself a free meal.

Their menu is huge, which is bad for the indecisive eater, such as yours truly. I'd had their sushi--which is really good--in the past, so I decided to try a plate and got the salmon teriyaki. The entree came with three generous cuts of salmon smothered in sweet teriyaki sauce, a mound of rice, and salad with what I think was a dressing that included that asian-type of mayonnaise. The fish was okay, but not fresh tasting. Total plus tip came out to $11, pricey for food that is yummy but average.  

Ultimate conclusion: I would stick to the sushi! Also, their miso soup is pretty salty. Random fact: they are the same owners of Nude Sushi.
Best Sushi in East Bay and very affordable!

Looking for cheap and good sushi..the place to go. 
I enjoy coming here to get cheap rolls like the cal roll or godzilla..
the fish isn't as fresh as it can get..but the miso soup here rocks! 
But they're specialty rolls are also very delicious as well...
me and my brother come here and he can fill himself up with less than $20 ..mind you my brother is a serious weight lifter with a HUGE appetite.. pretty nifty =] 
mmm...i always crave this place..mmm

I dont  know why i ate here! i've stayed away for such a long time but today i had sushi here. it was a bit pricy for what i got..... a lot of mushy rice and ends not meeting. The walls were dirty... eww.  This reminded me of the first time i made sushi.  when i tried picking up the sushi it was stuck to the plate so it all fell apart. 


I had to ask for the lady to give me ginger! WTF!

i've had better. they do delivery i think, which is cool if you're hungover and don't want to drive or walk, but i don't know if sushi is good for one suffering from a hangover. 

the restrooms suck.

First off, I just want to say that I have a different standard when it comes to sushi in Berkeley versus sushi back down in socal where I'm from. In Berkeley, I don't/can't expect a lot, especially for japanese food. You're either gonna get really expensive japanese food that just tastes ok, nothing special, or you're going to get a pretty good deal on japanese food that tastes just as good.That's kinda what Tako Sushi is for me~

I'd say that it's the best deal out of the other sushi places on southside of campus, so whenever I want japanese food (my favorite~!), Tako is my default :)

Service - good
Music - christian, i like!
Food - good
Location - good

Very cheap, late-night sushi.

We've been here several times over the past year and it's our go-to place whenever we're stuck on the East Bay.  A is a Cal alum, so he knows all of the affordable places to eat near campus.  

Most people get the rolls-- California, tuna, hamachi-- but it's usually in the bento box meal.  

The food is what you would expect in a college town.  Value sushi in Berkeley... that's talking about Tako!

This place is always a must when I go to Berkeley. I know it's not the most appealing place, but I love the ramen. It's probably just an ordinary pack of ramen that they use... but the pot they serve it in is so cool and they use the right amount of spices. As for the sushi, I wouldn't know... I never got it, but whenever I look at another persons plate I would imagine it to be good. The prices are cheap...

This place is my favorite sushi restaurants in Berkeley only because of its price. If you're a broke college student and aren't too picky about your sushi then this place is the best! Their best deal is their teriyaki chicken bowl for only 5 dollars which is a very generous size. Their rolls range from 7-10 dollars and their also decently sized but if the restaurant is crowded, their slow in making the rolls. Moreover, the waitress can also be rude if you keep asking her for stuff. Try to get the guy working there as your waiter instead. I gave this place 5 stars pretty much solely on its price and food portion.
A very diverse menu and one iof the better tasting and healthier eating options on Telegraph.

Tako was where I learned to like sushi and it has not disappointed me in my 4 years at Cal. I go about twice a month and the service and food are always good. It's definitely the best quality to price ratio. I try to try new places, especially since I moved to North Side, but I'm always disappointed by quality or price. I know that there is better sushi out there, but I am perfectly satisfied with Tako. The BF and I can get ridiculously full off $30 and I've yet to find a better shiitake role.

Decent food, good prices. I'm vegan and I like my sushi simple. I got an AAA roll (avocado, asparagus and tofu) for around $4.00 for 8 pieces. It was just enough food for me, and if I wanted an even cheaper meal, I could go for a cucumber or avo roll for less than $3.00. Their menu is a little bit overwhelming and confusing, and sometimes service can take a while though.

This place is close to campus and fulfills all my sushi needs. I come here ALOT, and it has never failed me. Prices are the best, and the sushi is of excellent quality (Compared to that other place in asian ghetto, which is overpriced and has horrible sushi...)

The selection is also great, service is good, and I really can't complain about anything here!

OK sushi. 

Price is decent, but it's obvious that the rice used isn't sushi rice, or hasn't been cooked with sushi vinegar - it's more just like plain rice rolled with the fillings.

Still, it's cheap so if you want sushi and don't care about the type of rice, you should come here!

I once at a meal here and paid solely with the few dollars found in my pants pocket and the change in my car.  The rolls here are pretty damn cheap, especially the more common ones like California Roll. You do get what you pay for -- the fish is not the best and the rolls sometimes fall apart. But really, when you are low on cash and desperately in need of sushi, this will certainly satisfy the craving. Avocado lovers take note -- practically every "fancy" roll seems to be slathered in it. This is not a problem for me since I absolutely love avocado.

I made a stop in Berkeley recently to visit an old friend while on a roadtrip. We ended up getting sushi here that night and it was pretty good. I wish I could remember more about the place but I was in a rush and on a road trip but for a vegetarian like me it had more than enough food to make me happy.

Good sushi for great prices you can't go wrong with Tako Sushi. Probably the cheapest Japanese restaurant I have been to so far and if I ever crave sushi this is always the place to go. Offers sit down and take out I always tend to call ahead to pick up food whenever possible. If you're in the area and in need of a cheap place to eat Tako is the place for you

This is the best sushi place for the reasons that follow: It is super cheap for sushi. The sushi is huge! They have a huge selection. And everyone who works there is awesome. It is amazing. This is by far my favorite sushi place ever! Also, they do not have alcohol, but you can bring in your own! How fucking rad!

I was pleasantly surprised at how cheap the menu was, how fast and friendly the service was, and, of the few rolls that I got, how fresh everything was.  I got there at 7:25, and was out by 7:55 after a combo dinner and some extra rolls.  

What do they say- you can have fast, cheap, and good, but only 2 of them?

I don't know if this is a destination place (like secret sushi in Cole Valley), but it sure is nice to know of a half-decent sushi joint on Telly.  

I'll be back.

I love sushi. I took Japanese in college based in large part on my plan to go to Japan and gorge myself on the food. 
The downside to having regular cravings for raw fish is that sushi grade is always costly at the store and restaurant sushi has a terrible price to calories ratio. I know fish is expensive, but I just feel some places unnecessarily inflate prices based on the luxurious stigma that sushi has in this country. I mean, when tiny vegetarian sushi rolls of shiitake or kampyo rarely go for under $4, there's something off with the pricing model. 

Thank God for Tako Sushi

Tako delivers a consistently good quality at an incredibly low price. There is an extensive variety of rolls for under and around $5 and they are all decently good. If you are just in the mood for simple rolls with decent quality fish you can get full off of sushi for around $10. For example, one of my usuals, the crazy horse, includes 4 types of fish in generous amounts in a good sized 8 piece roll for $5 even. 

If you're trying to impress a date or if you're a sushi snob, stay away. Otherwise, tuck away your culinary preconceptions and enjoy good food at a great price. 

Thank you Tako for allowing me to satisfy my regular cravings and still save up for my trans-pacific flight.

Ok--kind of a toss-up.  2.5 or 3.   I go with a three star due to the nice staff.
Noise level is LOUD (darn students) and prices a bit high for lunch.

Is my go-to place near UC Berkeley....yup. a person can get in and out in less then a hour.

As much as I love sushi, This is a great  place for a budget. specially for college students. We all know that college students are broke. lol. Decent price and the sushi is great! service is good, and for me walking distance from my cousin work place (which is right next door).

One of my favorite restaurants during my four years at Berkeley. I was such a loyal customer that I burned through at least two stamp cards, each card holding proof of least $300 worth of purchases (oh my god I came here a lot...). 

Best budget meal in my opinion: besides the starving student specials, I really like their udon. They have a few options and I make sure that there is both meat and veggies in my udon soup. (should be the chicken udon). Comes with a house salad instead of miso soup. If you are super hungry, for an extra dollar you get four California rolls with your udon! Protein, check; veggies, check; carbs, check; sushi, check. 

My favorite sushi roll is the cherry blossom because it is chalk full of good raw fish. Sushi rolls come with miso soup. However, lately they raised prices so I have not been getting their sushi as much.

Tako Sushi is one of the many mediocre sushi places in Berkeley.  The prices are average, and serving sizes are a little above average.  Service is abhorrent though.  I was here in a group of five friends for lunch, and we were seated right away.  I ordered a bento box lunch and some spring rolls as an appetizer.  My sushi portion of the bento box came before anybody else got their food.  Then everybody else got their meals and sushi, but I still had nothing.  My bento box finally came when everybody else was finishing their food.  My appetizer came after my meal, when we were ready to leave.  
On top of that, the food wasn't even that good.
The waitress also spilled water from the pitcher on one of the people in our group and didn't even apologize.
There are better sushi places to go for higher quality food at the same costs.

Im a gal from napa county and being from napa you must know what amazing food is. Im sorrounded by restaurants such as morimoto and the oxbow public market which has small venues of tasty food. I must say im a fan of Tako sushi because its Waaay affordable and its kinda nice to get out of the country side and get into a lil nice city such as berkeley. The staff always acomodates me with special requests. All im saying great for a low budget sushi with great flavors!!

To be fair I'll give an EXTRA star...

I've been here about 3-5 times and every time except for today I had a decent time with their service and food. But never the ambiance. It's a freaking Japanese restaurant and not a taqueria! So toning down the Hispanic music wouldn't be too much to ask for, is it? After all people come here for the 'Japanese' cuisine, right?

I've tasted their beef, chicken, sushi, noodles, soup and they were all OKAY. Nothing here tasted fresh like other sushi bars I've visited.

My recent trip though has change my opinion. On a previous trip I ordered their chicken udon which really filled me up so I got a plain one today plus four CA rolls for 8$ As soon as I finished the plain udon I got the tingling senatation down my throat.. you know, the one where you know you're going to be sick. I thought nothing of it but now I am feeling it. My head hurts and I am sore all after eating that udon.  The noodles this time weren't that good at all and I wasn't enjoying the dashi.

When I left one of the Latino cooks mumbled something to me in what sounded like Japanese?? I don't know but after today I'm never going back no mater how cheap this place is. I'll put my health first.

Solid place to hit up for cheap, good sushi.

Favorites: Lion King & Crunchy Roll. These two stand out the most and taste the best.

It's definitely fits within the college budget and lifestyle. You don't need to walk too far if you live in the Units, and it's better than a lot of the other food options available. I don't recommend eating in the outdoor setting at the back unless you're wearing a jacket though.
While the Japanese soups are not amazing, they have the best and the cheapest Salmon I have had in Berkeley.

Used to have some of the best miso soup I've ever tasted and awesome Cherry Blossom rolls. The quality, however, has unfortunatley been deteriorating in the past year... Catch it while you still can. Friendly service.

Cheap sushi here. There is nothing special about this place. Its close to campus and is relatively quick which are about the only upsides to this joint. The fish is not fresh and everything starts tasting the same after a few bites. I used to come here a lot during my first few years of college but there is not comparison in the average to good sushi places.

You are all crazy Tako Sushi is the most amazing place ever! I love sushi more than anything but it's hard to get my fix with the good stuff on a budget.  But incredibly, Tako is delicious, cheap, and really fast! I don't know how it's possible to achieve all of these things so thoroughly, but Tako must have magic elves because it does!
First time here. Average pricing, good taste. Got a rainbow roll and it was great. I will probably return in the future. Recommended.
I'm a stern believer that you shouldn't waste your money on food that is not good. And this sushi is simply disgusting.
cheap, sit-down.  feels like i'm getting gipped every time i pay them tip.  the food is at best mediocre, considering the other japanese alternatives nearby.

Thank you Tako Sushi for letting me eat sushi on my limited budget during my undergrad years. Your cheap spicy salmon, spicy tuna, and spicy hamachi let me have my sushi fix without breaking the bank. Sometimes, though, I did get sad when I would discover scales in my salmon rolls. :( Other than that, while you weren't providing the most "quality" sushi, you gave me bang for my buck and for that I'll be forever grateful.

Inexpensive food but with sushi especially, you get what you pay for. I have often left with a churning, upset stomach. Very often the fish served is at room temperature which is frightening when it is not cooked. Doug you must eat there, enjoy and I hope you haves strong tummy.

I use to eat here a lot when I would visit Berkeley. There was a period when I would eat here every week. HAA. I've tried most of the sushi spots in town and this by far is the best spot. CHEAP too. The prices really suit the college kids. Anyway, the rainbow roll and lion king roll are my favorites.

I went here with my best friend and it wasn't really busy at all. We were seated at the very back of the restaurant, but we didnt mind, although it was actually pretty hot back there..Anyways we just ordered the daily specials because they looked pretty yummy. Definitely not the best sushi I've tasted but it was a pretty good deal. Our server was really nice , The bill was pretty decent. The bathroom is kinda sketchy though, so if ya gotta go, just hold it!

Good (+ lots of vegetarian options to choose from). 
Cheap. 
Quick service. 
And Convenient location (close to a ton of shops and UCB).

Its been about two years since I went to Tako Sushi, and every time I drive by it on my way someplace else on Telegraph, I am surprised that it has not been shut down by the Board of Health.

The last time I went was around 2 years ago, so it might have changed, but considering some current reviews, it doesn't sound like the experience is too different.

Let me be as delicate as I can: intense, cramping, disgusting indigestion. Both times.

Fool me once, Tako Sushi, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me.

Go here for their hungry student deals! Kimchi fried rice or ramen for a lot cheaper than you'd find somewhere else around campus.

This place is good. It won't be the best sushi you've ever had, but it satisfies the cravings when they hit. Extra bonus that it's so close to the UC Berkeley campus. They have a wide variety of dishes: bento boxes, curry, sushi rolls, nigiri, sashimi, or ramen.

Quick and to the point. It's also a good place to sit and hang out since the restaurant is clean and pretty aesthetically appealing.

Recent reviewers seem to have enjoyed it, but every time I went there when I was going to Cal I left determined not to return. There are a lot of sushi restaurants in the area, and no good reason to go to Tako.

perfect for the college student on a budget

If i were a millionaire i would probably give this place 2 and a half stars since i can probably afford high quality sushi, but since i'm a regular poor college student who always seems to be in debt tako sushi is good enough for me.

The rolls aren't outrageously cheap, but if you come with some friends and order those boats, that should be plenty to fill everyone up.

Theres also some korean aspects to the menu and interesting appetizers like the salmon bites... which are ok, but if you don't like fried things then just don't give it a chance

Their fish isn't very fresh, and the chefs often don't know what's what. That said, it fills the yearning that you have in your heart for sushi, and it's quite affordable.

The combination plates on the back of the menu are a great deal and are highly recommended if you're with at least one other person.

Also, if you're in Berkeley, they will deliver for free if your order is above a particular price. They deliver until 4 AM!

The food at this place is alright. If you are hungry and looking for something cheap to eat this is perfect for you. Service was okay, the food came pretty fast. The waiter was a bit rude. They need to clean their walls more often, I see a lot of grease and gnats randomly flying.
