First of all, you can't get away with a restaurant that has a contradictory name and a misspelling like that. Tako Sushi. They don't even have any tacos there! -___- Just kidding... But in all honesty this place is the epitome of whatever.

With my experiences the waiters tend to look unengaged and unenthusiastic, which leads to an undelicious experience. The wait for my simple food took too long, but it was cheap!

So basically everything here kind of sucks. You pay for what you get and I'm pretty awesome so I like to treat myself to amazing sushi for a dollar or two extra. I mean if you're looking for something cheap and don't mind it tasting cheap then you just found your spot. So here you go. Go and check-in here, but as for me I'm going to Kansai or any other sushi spot.

*Going home to eat ramen to flush out this gross Tako Sushi*

the Great,
GumZ

I have always loved this place because of their prices.  Given their fish isn't the freshest and the place might need a little cleaning, but you get what you pay for.

The sushi is really cheap and you definitely get your money's worth.  ;)

The place is definitely a "cheap sushi" place.  I wouldn't credit the place with anything more than providing that.

One of my friends had gotten sick from their order, although I seemed completely unaffected by my unagi and dynamite rolls.  They do seem to have a wide selection of house specialty rolls and such at affordable prices.

Service on the other hand, was very lacking.  I never received the hot tea I ordered, although they were kind enough to discount more than the cost of the tea when I asked them about it.

Cheap sushi places need to serve alcohol so you can ignore the quality.  This place -- unfortunately didn't offer anything.

Still a bit confused about the name of this place, whether it is still Tako Sushi or Nude Sushi.  I received two checks with both names on it.
There is no sushi here.

Super cheap sushi a la korean christian music environment.   Rock it out, you know you like it when you can get cho-gochoojang on the side with anything you eat.  Party platters are great for large groups and is easy on the pocket book.

5 years ago when I stepped foot in here I was not a sushi fan, left being one. Its great! Fast, no pricey, and are willing to change anything to make it the way you like it.

 The only thing I dont like here was the red snapper they had, it was nasty and tasted like dirt. Other then that its amazing!

My friend used to work here and made a lot of the sushi, he's Mexican by the way... i' not racist or want to sound ignorant but if i am in a Japanese restaurant i expect it t o be authentic!! 

it is still very delicious none the less! 
very courteous staff but it has gotten worse during the last couple of years, i recommend it Early in the day, otherwise the food and tea taste like it has been left out all day long!! 

the deluxe California rolls *drrrrrrrrrrrroooooooooooolll* very very very scrumptious! 

my friend complained about the tea... but he was just being bitchy that day, i don't eat sushi any where else!! 

one time my friends and i had a sushi party here and we ate about $60 worth of sushi!! damn that was a great day... one of my friends who is allergic to fish ate some sushi & got sick, but what we didn't tell him was he didn't eat fish, he had a chicken tricky roll.... mind over matter i guess!!

I'm too scared to touch the real sushi here and the bentos are way overpriced for the poor quality so the only thing I get from here are the California Rolls.  The roomies and I purchased 100 piece Cali Roll party platters for dinner a few times during our run at Cal and let me tell ya, it's the best.  Oddly enough ordering two 50 piece party platters is cheaper than ordering one 100 piece party platter.  Silly.

Went there for a business club meeting. Spent $20 on a bento box and thought it was totally not worth the money.

The sushi are not made skillfully. But then again, I looked at the other items, at this price, you really can't complain.

Go if you have tolerance for cheap Japanese food.

Why they call it Octopus Sushi?  I don't know....

What I do know, is that I love that they give a good amount of sushi...great options and creativity, and it tastes yummtastic!!

This is my go-to place for cheap sushi - honestly, I would probably pick Manpuku over this if I lived closer to Manpuku though. Anyways...

The rolls here are ridiculously cheap! It's really popular because of its good location on Telegraph. They have Berkeley Specials in the middle of the menu, where you can get 2 rolls (12-16 pieces, depending on what roll) for around $6. The only thing is, you don't have many options for the 2 rolls. My friends also often get their bento boxes (which are around $10) because the portions are pretty big. 

If you want really high quality service or sushi, I wouldn't recommend coming here, because it always seems like there is only 2 waiters max for the whole restaurant, which has both indoor and outdoor seating. The place is almost always packed, too! However, if you are just looking to get your sushi fix and are on a budget, this is a really good place to go

Came here for a late lunch, and the food was barely acceptable. One of my pet peeves is unevenly cut sushi; it just looks messy and cheap. The rolls I got were all different sizes and about ready to fall apart. I ordered spicy hamachi (8 for $3.99) and california rolls (4 for $1.79). I swear they gave me red snapper instead of hamachi, although the pieces were cut so tiny it was hard to confirm. It had a funny taste, like it was dipped in tequila. Very little fish, although I guess I get what I paid for. If I come here again, I'll probably get stuff other than sushi. But that's a pretty big if.
They might as well deputize Tako Sushi as an extention of the campus food service. Frequented by many, loved by few, despite it's questionable quality, price keeps Tako a UCB institution.

Eh, weak. I like the fact that it's cheap but the sushi is low quality and the rice it's wrapped up in generally falls apart. I don't know if they're using the proper rice. It's close to the UCB campus so it's very convenient if you're a student.

Well... All was great, except that the music was SO loud that a conversation was hard and, to boot, it was that low-quality, stage-type, church-gone-pop music. Not anti-Christian or anything, but "Jesus" screamed in my ear for an hour was not what I came here for. Odd.

Just OK...

Service is soooo slow I was about to leave after waiting for almost an hour. Service sucked and it wasn't even that good. 

Miso soup is pathetic...no TOFU :(

I find this place to provide cheap, edible sushi and this was one of the first restaurants I frequented as a freshman at UC Berkeley when I found most of the cafeteria items to be offensive to my gustatory sensations.  I typically ordered the California rolls topped with eel, an eel roll with cucumber, the crazy monkey roll, or some variation thereof.  Later on I developed a predilection for the negihama roll.  Tekka rolls made for a light afternoon snack.  One problem I do have with the way they prepare the rolls is that the rice is too mushy.  Another complaint I have is that the volume of rice is too large compared to the filling.  The roll should be small enough that it can fit inside one's mouth with room to spare (some things can be "offensively big.")  Sushi is a delicate cuisine and should be delicately presented.  That said, this place isn't a gourmet sushi bar in midtown Tokyo, so what can you expect?

I've never ordered the nigiri sushi for eat-in but I've ordered from the getnudesushi.com menu (delivery during off hours) which satisfied my late night sushi cravings.  

The bento boxes are voluminous and the tempura a la carte (shrimp or veggie) is pretty tasty, though tempura is usually pretty harmless (I've rarely had inedible tempura at a Japanese restaurant before, since there's a standard formula for preparing it).  

I think this is a great place if you're not terribly picky about the quality of your sushi and it's conveniently located near campus.  And the best part about the place is that it's probably the cheapest place for sushi in Berkeley.

Reasonable price
Good service
Good food
Great place for students

Come here at least once a week.. as bad as this place is, it is convenient.  

The service is okay.  The food is okay.  The restaurant atmosphere is okay. 

Tako has a starving student special menu and the items on there are all very cheap.  If you don't care about the quality, taste- and nutrient-wise, then this is definitely the spot!

What really bugs me about this place is their packaging for take-outs.  As far as I can recall, most sushi places I have been to separate the warm/hot sushi from the cold ones (like a baked roll from a nigiri).  Tako not only puts them in the same bag, but the same box..  By the time I get home, the rainbow roll would be like.. half cooked.

I come here for sushi about once every two weeks on average. The service is pretty horrible every time, but the cheap delicious sushi and usual lack of a wait is why I keep coming back!

Don't come if you're a group larger than 6. I usually come with just one friend or in a group of four. It's pretty cramped space-wise, and you can expect to bump knees with your friends at the table.

I would recommend the Crunchy Delight roll or the Oakland roll; those are my two favorites! For an appetizer, stick with the classic edamame and the provided miso soup. Drink your water slowly, because it will probably not get refilled. Also, you sometimes have to ask for ginger (they don't always remember to bring it) so make sure you do that when you order.

The tip is included now, probably because no one was tipping.

Don't come here if you're looking for a nice restaurant experience, but this is a really fun place to go with a group of friends on a budget!

Not bad, not great. Nothing special but definitely good value. 
I had the chicken katsu curry with rice... huge serving and only $5. 
They also add bbq sauce - kind of quirky, but it works ok and made it a unique katsu currry.

I have to preface this review saying I am somewhat of a sushi snob in general.  That said, this place was pretty good.  

I went here the other night because the place I regularly go to was closed for the evening and my back-up place was too.  

I wouldn't reccommend the nigiri because some of the fish wasn't so good; however, in the rolls, it was pretty good.  The agadashi tofu was also huge and pretty good.  Try the Godzilla.

I used to come here on my way home from class to pick up an order of California Roll or something quick.  The sushi is not great here.  I recall getting a Philadelphia Roll once, and the smoked salmon had a very unusual chewy texture.  I know I must sound like I don't know my sushi (ordering a Cali Roll or Philly Roll), but I usually get sashimi elsewhere, not here at Tako.

Evan's Thoughts

To be honest Tako Sushi, or Tako Tako as my friends like to call it, is frankly an odd place.  You walk in and aren't sure if you can just sit down somewhere or if you are supposed to be seated.  Then you look at the menu and see plates of 100 pcs. of sushi for $25, and to make it more confusing you are never without the constant background Christian Rock/Gospel music.  Now I'd say me and the big guy are pretty good, but 2 hours of Christian music gave me some slight indigestion.

Besides the odd environment, everything else was fairly good.  I got the chicken teriyaki bento box (chicken, rice, tempura, and salad) with a side of california rolls.  The bento box was good, but the CA rolls screamed "imitation crab" to me.

If you're looking for a cheap sushi place in Berkeley, I would recommend you come here.  But I might also suggest you bring some ear plugs.

My first taste of sushi took place here about a year and a half ago. Back then when I didn't know what "good sushi" tasted like, this place was the bomb! Now that I have tried many different sushi places, I realized that the sushi here tastes awful. I couldn't even get through half a lion king roll (my favorite). If you were starving and wanted to save money, then sure, come here. If you're looking for some fantastic tasting sushi, go somewhere else. That karaoke underground sushi place a block away has really tasty sushi (kind of pricey though). A few things I do like about this place is that it's so clean and the staff are so friendly and attentive. I must say their appetizers taste really good and are extremely affordable. I tried the popcorn chicken and the tempura vegetables and shrimp. Both are delicious and not oily. I think I could come back here just for the appetizers, not the sushi.

The sushi here was bland and truly meh. I didn't trust the place enough to try anything raw. It's only real saving grace is the cheapness. Even then I prefer to pay more to not have soy sauce+miso soup with some tofu leftovers and seaweed scraps. Or old rolls where the rice was starting to get hard.

Japanese food for cheap. That pretty much sums up Tako Sushi. For $20, the amount that you might pay to eat at a good restaurant counting appetizer, entree, and drink, you can get a party tray at Tako. Finally some place that makes sushi affordable for poor college kids,.

I got the No Name Roll here and it was better than I would've imagined. There was more than a microscopic amount of fish which is common for sushi places around Berkeley, the roll is about 10 pieces, it was tempera battered and finally, it was  topped with some Sirracha sauce. It's definitely something I haven't had anywhere else. 

Dining in, the place feels really cozy. Most tables are sized for two so there isn't much space for large parties, thus less of overly noisy conversation. The service is really fast, and on top of that, you get complimentary soup and tea :)

The prices are the lowest you can get for sushi it seems.  The first time I went there I ordered special B or something like that and I braced myself for the worst.  Then my order came and it was actually good.  I was amazed.  

So I have gone back to this place perhaps 20 times when I want cheap sushi and I am already in the area.  Parking sucks in the area bigtime.

The sushi is not the best.  Sevice is not the best, seems like too many customers and not enough employees in a little place.

I used to go to this place when it was something else.  I forget what it used to be but I remember the layout with the bathroom in the back.  God my memory sucks, lol.

Anyways, if you are in the area and want inexpensive sushi that won't make you sick...go for it.  It's a steal.  Large servings.  interesting customers.  Rich women having lunch who like to eat cheap, students, artists, all sorts of people.

When we were in Berkeley, it took us a year or two to find this place. 
Once we found it, we ate there once a week for a year!
Their servings are ridiculously generous, 
the prices are dirt cheap 
and this was overall my favorite sushi place in the area.

You don't necessarily eat hear for the atmosphere, just the solid food, good convo w/friends, and the price!

We did notice that the evening cook staff seems better than the lunch staff. 
Also, do take advantage of the till 2am delivery service (wish we still could!)

Located conveniently close to the UC Berkeley campus, Tako Sushi is a nice place to stop by for lunch. Ordered a bento box with chicken teriyaki, vegetable tempura, and 5 pieces salmon sashimi  for a little over $9, #65 Oishii Roll, and #54 Cherry Blossom. The Cherry Blossom has salmon and avocado topped with fresh Tuna. I poked out the raw fish and avocado, leaving behind the rice. The Oishii is covered in a cream sauce but taste pretty good. 

The portions and amount of rice used for the sushi rolls will fill you up fast. I could have shared the bento with my friend and been full. Needless to say there were leftovers. The service was average, but the waiters were busy during the lunch rush. Miso soup also came with our meal. Tako Sushi reminds me of the slightly pricey San Francisco Kiki or Kitaro. 

What I recommend:
-- Nice sushi lunch spot close to campus

Meh. Decent sushi for Berkeley on Telegraph. At best, it's better than the sushi they sell at GBC and the Den. That's not saying much. It's simple and I liked it for that reason and you could probably eat here if you had an hour break with a friend... but after my first year in college, I never really wanted to come back. Just overall service and quality went down. Bleh. Don't settle for this place, there are better Japanese joints in Berkeley!

The best when it comes to budget sushi.

I've been here before, and I will come here again.  I'm quite looking forward to it.  

The last time I was here was actually my first time.  Pleasant company in tow, and we were already pleasantly inebriated when we arrived.  We were also in the mood for some sushi.

There was a bit of a wait time (less than 10 min), which was slightly annoying because I was really hungry.  I can look past that as it was a dinner rush.  When we were finally seated, the staff apologized for the wait and was quick to take our order.

The Sashimi Special was only $13.99 and very plentiful for 2 to share...more delicate of a cut, which I like.  I also had the spider roll...only $4.99 and very satisfactory...I was definitely making "mmmm" sounds and happy dancing a bit in my chair.

My dinner companion was super hungry so he got the chicken teriyaki bento.  Plentiful portions for the price and pretty good according to him.

One more thing that I can recall loving is the salad dressing...hint of peanut flavoring that was creamy and delish!!!  I drank what was left in my salad bowl.

The only downer was that I could not order any sake to go with my meal.  Other than that I was pleasantly surprised and satiated from my experience here.

I used to go here when it was cheaper but now they've raised prices so I'd rather go somewhere for better sushi. Their CA rolls are pretty nasty and one day when I was waiting for my to go order I saw someone wheel in some frozen fish so freshness isn't a big thing here -_-

Food is okay. I've had better Japanese food. It's not as expensive as Joshuya's but the food quality is quite distinguishable, unfortunately.

But why am I complaining...they're supposed to be open till 10pm. 

10 P.M. my butt.

Not tooooo upset because at least it means they're treating their workers well (not working them overtime), but from a customer's perspective, not too cool. My friend and I practically ran here from the BART so we can make it on time (got there at 9:30) but they refused to serve us because it was too close to closing. Boo.

So , I'm not Japanese so I will/can not comment on the authenticity of this place. 
I have been here a couple of times and must say that i do like their sushi rolls. 
+1 star for their good service. This is one of the few places in berkeley where you will be served food, you are also given a complementary bowl of Miso soup that keeps you nice and warm till you await the arrival of your food. Though I must complain that the food does indeed take quite a while to come to you ( a friend of mine waited a whole 1/2 hour for his california roll).
+2 stars for quality of food. I recommend the Golden california roll, the Chicken teriyaki roll or the Caterpillar roll. I did not like their chicken teriyaki bowl though and felt that it was too bland , lacking any teriyaki sauce whatsoever. 
+1 star for their pricing which is reasonable in my opinion.
-1 star for the fact that it does get quite crowded on weekends and even on weekday nights and you might have to wait quite some time before you are seated.

Well, like others have said, it's not true Japanese cuisine or exceedingly authentic. However, it's very cheap, always edible (except for the chicken teriyaki, I find that iffy, but I love the tempura and specialty rolls). Also, their students specials are nice! 

The waiters are always very pleasant too, and they have the most awesome California rolls ever. The vegetable tempura is great, and now that their specialty rolls are only $7.99 AND they have $4.99 donburi specials as well as lunch bentos, what more can you ask for?

(Pasted menu for reference)

Donburi (dish over rice, with a bowl of miso soup) = 4.99
Oyako (chicken and egg)
Tonkatsu (egg over fried pork cutlet)
Chicken Katsu (egg over fried chicken cutlet)
Bulgolgi (egg over marinated beef)
Veggie (vegetables and egg. Vegetables are usually carrots, string beans, broccoli, mushroom and something like potato)

Lunch Bento (Green salad, rice, miso soup) = 8.99
Chicken teriyaki + tempura
Tonkatsu + tempura
Bulgolgi + tempura

With choice of: CA rolls (4), salmon sashimi (3), gyoza (2) or tuna sashimi (3) 

Vegetarian Lunch Bento
Agedashi tofu + edamame
Vegetable Tempura + edamame
Steamed vegetables + edamame

With choice of: egg roll (2), Avocado-Cucumber roll (4), Fried veggie roll (4) or steamed vegetables. 

I've loved this restaurant since freshman year, and I still love it. It's awesome. And they do take credit card too!

I haven't had sushi at too many places, but this place seemed fairly average. Price was about 7 for what left me medium full, and it tasted okay. Our on campus club had gotten them before and I don't know if it's just that the officers knew what to order better or if there was some deal what, but we were able to get an exorbitant amount of food for very cheap. So yeah, personal dining is okay but look into it for a club meeting.

Of the sushi places here around the Berkeley campus, I think this is the best place. The sushi is pretty good and the prices are cheap for what sushi usually is. The service is good and the waiters/waitresses are very nice.
the quality of the food is compatible with the price. I usually go there for cold soba. I also like some of their sushi rolls but avoid those $3-4 dollar rolls.

Decent sushi rolls. Great prices. Waitress is super nice. 

I ordered the Dragon Roll, which tasted like it should; I've tasted better, but for the affordable price, you get what you pay for.

Good sushi for cheap. Being the cheap college student that I am, I aim for the cheapest spicy or fried roll on the menu as those kind of rolls are the most filling. So I get something like a tempura fried cali roll with sriricha hot sauce squeezed on top for a lil over $5, yum

It's open late. i suppose that is one credit i can give this place. The sushi tastes like they got it from a Safeway, and the soup seems like it's made from those powdered packets that you can buy at said Safeway. I've been there a few times and everytime i was disappointed with the quality of the sushi i was given. Granted the prices are as low as you can get with sushi.

Strictly and dissapointingly average Japanese food joint.  It's cheap, decent, kept clean, and the staff is friendly.  Can get crowded (because of it's closeness to campus), but other than that there is nothing exceptional.  Meh, go around the corner to Joshuya, it's much better.  And if your a fatty hankering for sushi in the late-night hours, call Nude Sushi!  There are better places out there (as mentioned above) -- average with a impotent capital C.

Good food and sushi. It's got a cheaper section for starving, college students. I usually like to get the kimchi fried rice to-go. The sushi's decent and filling. I also got the chicken udon. The broth was watery and tasteless, so I had to add soy sauce. The to-go menu is great! Note that if your order isn't over $7, then you will get charged for using a credit/debit card, so bring cash!

Update: Tako no longer has the $7.99 roll specials, where every special roll was $7.99, now its back to regular pricing, whihc kinda makes it not worth the money. Its a sad day for cheap sushi in Berkeley... :(
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

After 4th check-in:
I am going to change my view on the sushi.
The Philly Roll which includes smoked salmon, adds a nice kick and the $5 price tag is reasonable. 
Dinner: One philly roll and a salmon popper are more than enough for a hungry student, even though it may seem decievingly small at first. For around $12
P.S. Free miso for orders of $10 or more per person.
Service: isn't the best, there is only one lady that works no matter how busy it is. And you don't get taken care of right away. I did happen to see two waiters today, but still very slow service.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The appetizer salmon & tuna poppers are really good and as the name suggests, fried. They are served with a spicy and creamy sacue that naturally compliments the fried goodness. 

Not a big fan of the sushi. i like the environment. They do play Christian music, reminding me of Chick-fil-A.

SUPER slow.

I wouldn't say the food is terrible, but it's very very whatevs, if you know what I mean. 

If you've ever ordered Nude sushi in Berkeley, they basically taste exactly the same.  It's very mediocre sushi, nothing special and never something I'd crave for.  

There are better choices around Berkeley..try Manpuku on College Ave.
Good sushi for a good price. May not be the best in town, but you get for what you pay for and a bargain indeed it is.
When I am in Berkeley this is my favorite sushi spot its cheap and yummy. People are nice and service is good.

This sushi restaurant caters to cheap college students.  That being said, you get what you pay for: cheap sushi = poor quality rolls/fish.  If you're tolerant of sub-mediocre to mediocre quality sushi, try this place out, but if you have the slightest appreciation for quality sushi, their sushi here will disappoint you.

I recommend getting the traditional Japanese food entrees instead.  The entrees are also decently priced (cheaper if there happens to be a student special), but good part is that the entrees are more wholesome and fulfilling than their poorly made sushis.  

I like to order the tempura udon; it's not amazing but it's satisfying.  It's a very simple dish so I think it's overpriced for what it is but it's still relatively cheap (less than $10).  The udon is soft and there's a good variety of tempura.  Advice: ask for the tempura on the side.  They serve the tempura in the udon so it gets soggy real fast.

Tako Sushi is solid. Definitely not the best sushi I have had but its so close and so cheap. I usually stick to simple rolls like spicy tuna and avocado cucumber to keep the price even lower! If you dine in there they give you miso soup for free! I also have had a weird dessert here that was pretty good! It was like a Japanese ice cream sandwich? It was in the shape of a fish and it was filled with red bean ice cream! They  gave us a discount on it because apparently nobody ever gets them! 

One of the best deals this place has are their sushi platters. They are pretty cheap, have lots of variety, and feed a lot of people. They are perfect for game days or a post finals sushi and sake bomb party.

PROS:
Dirt cheap

CONS:
FOOD POISONED the 3 times I was dragged there by my friends
Sushi was TINY
Dirty and disgusting inside and outside on patio

For the price and location I give it a 5. The sushi I'd give a 3 or 4. Portions are great for the price. Really no complaints. Owners and employees are very nice. I worked for their sister restaurant Nude Sushi a while back.
Very Very Very average Jap food, but hell its pretty cheap for lunch!

Haven't been here in a while...so this may not be current anymore.

Reasonably priced sushi/Japanese food near campus will definitely win you a decent following.  And for students to be able to spend what few dollars they have on decent food is definitely a plus.

The value is definitely there...the portions are pretty generous for what you pay, and they have a decent variety of cheaper rolls.  They dont have the super high end items that you would find in a quality Japanese restaurant, but they do offer the bulk of "traditional" rolls.  

As for the taste, you wouldn't confuse this with quality sushi/sashimi.  One of my standby orders was their Hana Roll Combo, which included Unagi Roll, Shrimp Tempura Roll, and California Roll.  The food was pretty "okay"...wasn't butchered but wasn't overwhelming.  In essence, you kinda do get what you pay for (but a little better).  However, it did exactly what a college student would want - fill you up for cheap.  

You could do much better by drifting further away from campus...but that's always easier said than done for students.  With that in mind, three stars for the overall value, despite the lack of quality in their food and underwhelming taste.
Yes Yes. Cheap prices, yummy sushi, nuff said. To those who complain the guys making sushi are hispanic and its a sushi place, really who gives a damn? Good sushi is good sushi

Considering other options on Telegraph, you have better options than Tako Sushi. If you are craving sushi, Jashu-Ya or Norikonoko has better quality sushi, cleaner facilities and non-Christian music. Bottom line, if you are late for class, craving sushi, you will get supermarket quality here. 

Also if you go online to GetNudeSushi.com, the same sushi is prepared here. 
I think they overcharge on the 2-piece nigiri rolls. They have good combinations and deals, go with those, they are cheaper. 

Fast. Christian. Sushi

so it's not the GREATEST.

but it's cheap...and on a student budget...that makes it that much more delicious.

the miso soup is bomb, no matter what everyone says here.

the service could definitely be better, but it's not necessarily bad at all.


just beware...a lot of rolls come with teriyaki sauce on them without saying it on the menu.

nevertheless...this place is still a favorite.

This is some decent sushi for the price paid. My guy introduced me to this place and I feel they deserve more credit. We come here once a month or every other month and order hella sushi and always pay less than $30... You cant beat that price. Their sushi is pretty good too (especially cherry bomb and oakland roll...mmmm).. I also love their salmon bites! Yum! So going here next week!!
Not the best sushi, but you can't expect that much for this price. But then again, who wants to save money when ingesting raw fish? Hummmm.... maybe I should order some teriyaki instead....

get a pineapple roll! (that's where the 4-star comes from) this place is fair-priced & close to campus & pretty good w/ their service.
 
most of their foods are 3-stars tho: their fish is not the best and their other rolls are so-so...
yea it's cheap but it's not japanese food or whatsoever, came here once, and that's it for me. Don't even bother to try.... it's that bad...

Pros:
-as cheap as sushi gets
-convenient location

-Cons:
-NO alcohol !!
-big student crowd (like, the bad kind of studenty... as in: no sake !!)

Wtf is up with their mushy ass sushi rice?  And they use A LOT of rice in their rolls too, so it's like a mushy mess when you eat it.  Why the hell do my friends always want to go back there?

The people there are nice, but the food really isn't that good.  I think everything would be much tastier if they fixed their mushy rice problem.

And how cheap are they?  They don't even include ginger on the plate.  I know most people throw it out, but at least ask if we want any!  It's so hard to get the waiter's attention sometimes to get ginger, so I wish they would ask.  

I think Berkeley Sushi House is better than this place for sure.

Pretty damn good for cheap, quick sushi for lunch. The rolls range between $3-8, which for sushi is dirt cheap. 

I wouldn't go here for a fancy dinner or gourmet meal, but it sure beats some other local options for a quick meal of 2-3 rolls.

The rolls are usually HUGE and pretty fresh and there's lots of variety. I usually get one of the bowls (usually tempura, just because I'm slightly obsessed with fried, crunchy things) and one roll. That's even enough for me and I've been known to out-eat my 6'+ ft male friends :-)

Looking for cheap sushi? This is your place! In fact, they've even got a section on their menu labeled "Student Specials," aka cheap dishes. I had one of these: kimchi fried rice. It wasn't the best, nor was it really spicy, but it was a decent portion for ~$5. The rice was really mushy (too much water), but mixing it with the miso soup made it taste alright. Their sushi is okay, not extraordinary, but good. Btw, this place is on the small side, so don't plan to bring in large parties.

I don't think I'm very picky with my sushi places since I don't eat it too often. I like the Godzilla roll here, it's my favorite! Service is ok. Takes a while for the food to get done sometimes, so if I get to go, I call in before picking up.

I was introduced to Tako by a good friend. Hold in the wall with good, cheap eats. 

I always order the Oakland Roll which is worth the drive from Uptown Oakland. I've only had a not so great experience with it once (mid-week).

I recently tried the California Roll and it was very good also.  I've also had the salmon skin roll and gyoza - both good.

You can't beat the fact they are Christians and they have a loyalty program where you can $$ off when you acrue enough stamps.

The cooked items seem to look hit or miss in nature. I would stick to whatever "regular" you find suits your fancy.

The food is cheap here, although the portions are relatively small so I feel like I have to order more and thus end up spending more.  The rolls and entrees are just OK - the main pull for Tako Sushi is the location right near campus & relatively cheap prices (especially the student lunch special).  I used to come here sometimes in between classes, but rarely went out of my way to eat here for dinner, unless someone was visiting me and wanted cheap sushi.  Overall, Tako Sushi is not bad...2 1/2 stars for food quality, plus that extra 1/2 star for cost effectiveness.  And it's a heck of a lot better than the sushi at GBC...

The food is nothing special, but I liked that they had starving student specials posted on the door. That makes it affordable for a college student like myself.

If you're looking for an authentic Japanese restaurant...then this is not the right place. Otherwise if you want a cheap eat then this is a good spot for the money.

The sushi is decent and they have a pretty good variety. I like the spicy california, philly, and spider roll. If you don't like sushi they also have bento boxes and noodles. It's really close to campus and affordable.

Tako Sushi has been my go-to lunch place for a long time. As a student at UC Berkeley, I could call their number and order while still on campus, and pick up my order by the time I walked there. I recommend the Baja Roll or Dynamite Roll, and their Udon soup tasty! I think of it as more of a lunch place because it's not usually crowded, and they have great, quick service.
All I have to say is the spicy tuna pleases my very picky boyfriend. We always get it as take out so I can't say anything for dining there. You couldn't ask for better pricing!

stopped in for lunch one school day, ordered a sushi combo (nigiri).  all of the fish was unfresh -- tasted bad, chewy consistency.  didn't finish the food, won't return.  if you're looking for quick sushi near campus, the store in the durant food court is a better bet.

Could be a 3-star rating but I'm not crazy about this place. I pretty much only go here because it's cheap sushi and it's very convenient when I'm too lazy to walk anywhere else.

I always order: Crunchy Delight and Lion King. These rolls are usually a hit or miss for me and it varies whenever I come here. 

The party trays are worth it though! Order those for big groups.

When I'm on a tight budget, I love coming here to eat. The food is quick and easy and they've got a wonderful selection of sushi to choose from. I love the service and the atmosphere. It might look small, but once you get past the counter, there's more room.

When it comes to sushi, my standards are about average, and if you can give it to me cheap I'm sold.  However, at the end of the day it is still raw fish, so compared to other foods I guess I probably am a little pickier.  I have had some damn good cheap sushi in my life, though (Coach Sushi and Ginza in Oakland!!!), and this is not on the list at all.  My rolls were lukewarm, which always weirds me out because it means they aren't refrigerating the raw fish and the salmon was hard and still had bits of skin on it.  Plus the typical boring rolls were ok priced (California, Philadelphia, $6 or so) but anything more interesting was priced more around $8-10, which then is getting into more expensive territory where I feel like I might as well go somewhere nicer.

The service was fast and the miso soup was delicious ($1!) so that was good.  I might come back to try something cooked, they have good looking lunch specials with tempura or teriyaka for $5.  The egg rolls were greasy and just filled with bean sprouts (or so it seemed) - pass on them even though they're only $3.

.....on second thought, after writing this review soon after I arrived home, i got sick sick sick and just had to go from 2 stars to 1 star.

I completely forgot this place existed. I was craving sushi, but didn't want to go all the way down Elmwood for Manpuku and Berkeley Sushi House is awful.

I got the Ghirashi (Chirashi?) which was good for its price. I was comfortably full, and didn't get tired of the raw fish taste. My boyfriend got HDB (?) Some Korean dish that had raw fish, a Korean sauce over vegetables and rice. He said it was better than he expected. We also tried the Popcorn Tuna which was pretty good. We asked for it a bit raw, but it was thoroughly cooked. 

I tried a Melona Bar for the first time here. Yummy! 

Bonus: They take credit cards!

The sushi here is not that good, as far as california-style rolls go.  They always seem to be lacking in flavor and the ingredients taste cheap.  The rolls are still pretty expensive too.

I give this place 3 stars because the non-sushi items are a good deal.  Quality-wise they're exactly "A-OK" and dirt cheap.  Check out the student specials - not bad for 4-5 bucks!  Good place to grab a cheap meal with pretty good waiter service.  The restaurant decor is pretty cute too.

The Short:
Good for cheap Japanese eats, but don't expect too much in terms of quality (or sanitation). Would've been 3-stars for the food, but seeing some small mice run around near the entrance is not something I want to see. They'd be headed for a 1-star instantly, but I'll give them a little leeway since the place is located on Telegraph and the side of the street is just lined with trash cans. The fish is not the freshest, so I would recommend the cooked rolls. But beware of the California Rolls, they're loaded with mayo. Overall, I enjoy the food, but I'd only come here if I really need a Japanese fix! Also good if you're looking for a party platter of sushi because they give the best deal on sushi platters.

Recommendations:
- Chicken Teriyaki Roll.

Pros:
+ Cheap eats, a lot of special deals to help you save some $$$ on sushi.
+ Good selection of sushi rolls and entrees.

Cons:
- Food quality is meh. Don't be expecting anything spectacular.
- Not the most sanitary place.
I love this place! The lady who runs it is super nice. Their green tea tastes delicious and their prices are amazing. I only go to Tako when I'm craving sushi in Berkeley.

cheap, chill, and straight to the point sushi joint.  had the salmon skin roll (yum!), oishii roll, and crab/shrimp/avo/crispies roll.  definitely one of those spots i'd go back to when i'm kickin it around telegraph. i can't really say much on service being that we we're one of the last customers there an hour before they closed.  the tea could've been hotter but then again it might've been because of the late hour.

I can't believe what people are expecting for what they pay!! 
this place is cheap and has a good location near UC campus. 
their donburi(egg and typically, deep fried meet on rice with sauce) is only 5 bucks and is filling. it tastes pretty good too. 
their rolls and sushi aren't that great but it's definitely not bad considering the price. 
and who cares if the amigos are rolling makis!
authenticity?? boy... you're on the wrong side of the neighborhood and too cheap.

As a vegetarian, I'm a huge fan of taco sushi: they have plenty of veggie-friendly options. 

The last two times I went to Tako Sushi,I ordered the veggie crunchy (one time sit-in one time take out.) It doesnt take long to make. The service at Tako Sushi is TERRIBLE (but I dont mind since i'm getting a fair price), so they bring out food as soon as its done (instead of bringing everything out together). They describe the sauce on the veggie crunchy as a "special sauce" which is sweet and tangy, but think/syrup-like, which makes the crunchy bits on the sushi a bit soggy after a while. 

The nice thing about Tako Sushi was when I ordered over the phone, and told them I'd be there in 10 mins, my order had JUST finished cooking. They didnt wait for me to get there to start on my order. Some places in Berkeley dont want to waste food incase a customer didnt show up, but I like that Tako Sushi didnt mind. 

Overall, the food was great, the service was mediocre, but worth the low price.
Good Sushi at Good Prices. Had some Tuna and Salmon Nigiri and both tasted very fresh and good.

Their sushi was pretty delicious, but nothing fancy or spectacular.  However, I love their katsu curry.  The pork was fried to the perfection and the taste was amazing.  For only $4.99 (under starving student menu), I had enough food for 2 meals.  Their gyoza was somewhat disappointing.  I could tell that they re-deep fried the frozen gyoza using old oil because it was greasy, tasteless and saturated with fat.

Overall, don't order gyoza and your life will be ok.  Your money is worth here.  The service was pretty fast, and the staff was very polite and patient to us taking forever to decide what to order.

FOOD:
1. Miso soup - Hm, barely any tofu chunks in there.
2. Philly Roll - Ok, but their rice isn't good. It reminds me of old mushy rice.
3. Caterpillar Roll - It's okayyy, but lacks flavor. =/


SERVICE:
Decent, but the servers seem timid.

ATMOSPHERE:
1. Has nice Asian blossom painted all over the wall, but overall atmosphere is just alright.

Definitely just an "OK" place.  The service was very good, and everyone working there was very nice, but the sushi tasted just like it cost, cheap.  I don't know what it was but the dragon roll and CA roll I had bites of had a funny taste to it.  And believe it or not, they messed up Udon.  Udon is just soup and shouldn't be that hard to make.  The chicken (I ordered chicken Udon) wasn't cooked, and was very fatty.  The only other thing added was noodles and chives. That's it.  

All in all, cheap prices and nice people should be the attraction for eating here.

I can't promise you it's freshness nor quality of certain items.  However, you really can't complain for the dirt cheap pricing and fast service.  for a college dive and a fast food substitute, two thumbs up.

BAD BAD BAD SUSHI 
when you go to Sushi restaurant, you expect to see some Japanese (at least Asian) guy working in the kitchen,
but you won't see any Asians(besides the servers) in this place

food is not even that cheap, and the quality is very poor
last time when I ordered, the Tuna was pink and the Salmon had a faded orange color
they were so THIN that i was able to see the rise through those fishes

their gingers are not fresh, and it takes a long time to get your food

I did not get sick from eating the sushi rolls here, but I did make a conscious decision to stay away from anything raw.  And for the price, service and decor, this made me happy.  The very reasonable prices also made me happy.  I like when prices reflect value, no matter how small that value may be.  

The menu is epic and I only skimmed through before getting tired and distracted by the cherry blossoms painted on the wall.  Perhaps, a superficial move to create a Japanese-feel next to the Mexican men preparing sushi rolls.  Hey, I'm into international cuisine!

They charged a 15% gratuity on a party of two, which made sense since the servers are probably paid poorly by the hour and the place is located right next to a public university campus. 

Would I return?  I have frequented this place for years before they repainted and redesigned.  Convenience and not being in the mood for pizza or crepes is a strong motivator.

I have been here so many times.  This is where I come for inexpensive sushi.  The rice for the sushi is sweeter than at most places, but I like it.  I think their sushi is  delicious and their prices can't be beat!  The service is usually great except one time, a lady server asked if we wanted our change back from the bill and I thought that was kind of strange.  They also play music that praises god all the time, so that can either be a plus or a minus depending on the patron.

Service is kind of slow because they have so few workers. But the sushi selection is huge, workers are very friendly...definitely worth coming back to! 

You HAVE TO try the Popcorn Salmon...they are SO good!! 
And I love the Hawaiian Roll - if you like raw salmon with a pinch of lemon then you would love this!!

The sushi is decent. Since the price is relatively cheaper, for the price you're paying, I think it's pretty decent. 

I would recommend getting the deluxe party tray or one of those special trays and split with people. It's more worth it that way. I liked their lambada roll and unagi roll. It's a good place to go if you're not willing to shell out too much money for good sushi.

This is the best cheap sushi in Berkeley near campus. 

Granted, its not the best quality, but you get what you pay for. 

I really like the simple rolls; crazy horse and crazy monkey rolls.
Its not the best sushi, but it is really cheap.  Anyone that says this is good sushi has not eaten good sushi before.
this place is a little small. the food is good. the peoples are okay, but you can definitely find better.

Decent sushi. Very affordable for college students. Its not the best sushi but it certainly fills your appetite and way much more than its worth. They have cute decorations on the wall and a very nice place to hang out with your friends. My suggestion is to order all you want at once cause when it gets crowded the longer you have to wait for your food!!

err this place scares me. why would you go to a sushi place that you don't trust?! that's like asking for food poisoning. i do trust the COOKED fish rolls...like the one with siracha on top..i forget what it's called but it's deep fried which makes it a little less questionable. i guess.

I had Tako sushi for the first time today and I was quite pleased with the roll and the price. I ordered the Godzilla, which was basically an unagi roll deep fried. I got 10 pieces (even though the menu says 8) for 5.40 before tax and tip. The price definitely made my roll more delicious, but even objectively, I would have enjoyed my sushi roll. I definitely recommend the Godzilla, which is what I had.

However, my friend had a less satisfactory order. his don katsu donburri had some really gross egg thing on top of it that looked gray and just not appetizing. also, his don katsu was soggy and not crisp and the meat was very chewy. stay away from the donburri.. but his salmon popcorn (appetizer) was pretty good! you can't really go wrong with deep fry 

i was happy with the price, variety, and overall quality of the food. i can definitely see myself coming here more often

Decently priced

but not one of the greatest sushi places ive been to

if you want a cheaper sushi place go here but if your looking for a legit sushi place i wouldnt recommend tako

This was my mine and my husbands first time having sushi so I don't have much to compare it to. It's a little hole in the wall next to Blakes on Telegraph. Nothing fancy and the decor seemed very old. Tables were a little sticky.
We had the Oakland Roll and the teryaki bbq roll. They were both delicous and great amount for the price. I had the soft shell crab tempura for appetizer, unfortunately it was tastseless, very plain for crab. Did not get adventurous enough for the sashimi but maybe next time.
The menu is huge there is something for everyone. The service was very attentive considering it was packed on a Saturday night and there were only 2 serviers running around. I would have given it more stars if they served saki! But we will be back for sure.
Reasonable, pretty good, tasty sushi for $42 for 6 people (party platter)
Just fine.

Pretty good sushi at reasonable prices. I agree with many others that Manpuku on College Ave (Elmwood area) is a little bit better and cheaper too. But Tako Sushi is just really conveniently located next to campus and great for grabbing a quick lunch or sushi cravings at 10pm. It gets crowded here sometimes during lunch but service is quick and we never had to wait too long for our food. We've ordered party trays from Tako Sushi many times and they are always ready when they're supposed to, and the sushi is always tasty andd fresh.

People expecting a culinary delight by campus need to move over! The restaurants here cater to what the students want -- cheap and filling good and boy, does Tako Sushi deliver! I'm not even trying to insult the place, it's really what I want!

I love their starving student specials. Kim chi fried rice sounded really weird to me but it ended up being pretty tasty. I can't stand kim chi but I decided to give it a shot figuring, what do I have to lose for the price? It ended up being fantastic and filling, especially with the free miso soup . I have also had their curry with chicken katsu, which is pretty good. There was a pretty fair amount of chicken katsu, although I think the curry was too watery for my taste. It wasn't very watery but I do like my curry to have a sort of thick and starchy consistency rather than a thin soup but maybe that's just me!

Either way, I would have to say I would come back! You get what you pay for and I really do like my food fast (relatively), convenient (close to campus), and cheap!

The Nigiri is AWFUL! Cold, chewy and chunky and not even sliced thick or evenly... it was literally placed on the rice- no forming the fish and rice into a unified Nigiri unit... ugh

The staff makes me feel like I'm home (nice Korean people) but the sushi chefs are probably not trained (at all) in the technique/art of making Sushi

Come here for a Chicken Teriyaki Bowl with California Rolls, and maybe some Popcorn Chicken or Gyoza

DO NOT COME HERE FOR anything that requires quality fish/meat

There are so many other options near campus:
Joshuya Sushi
CU Sushi
Kirala
Sushi Sho
All I get is the nigiri lunch special.  this is my go to sushi place to go to while i'm at school.  i have no allegiance though, so something moves closer to school, i'll probably go there.

Vegan review! - Kinda pricey, but the food is decent. The woman who took my order was nice enough to, without my asking, replace my salad with a salad without dressing (the salad dressing has mayonnaise, which goes against my vegan diet). 

I paid about $8 for a veggie bento box and I was definitely full at the end. You get a nice heaping of rice and more than enough edamame for your liking :O

Affordable sushi, good service. Good place to go for sushi if you crave sushi and are near campus. Some Korean-style selections (kimchi sushi). Enjoy getting the larger sushi rolls (good value for the price!). I miss coming to this place with my friends as an undergrad..

The service has never been great, but the cheap tasty sushi makes up for it. I LOVE all of the vegetarian options, Tako has obviously put effort into creating veggie rolls that are just as complex and yummy as the fishy ones.
Cheap and quick sushi for hungry college students.
Nice fresh fish and seaweed. Excellent service and great prices.
not the tastiest BUT cheap and cheap

I dont think I'll be coming back. I actually used to come here a lot when I was in high school and it took me all of HS and the few random times I came here to fill out the stamp card. It literally requires you to have like ~50 stamps.  

Free miso. 

Most of their rolls are pretty unmemorable. If you are craving some cheap sushi, I suggest Manpuku on college instead.

Oh. And my friend found a hair in his sushi here. Yums. not.

The prices are cheap, but the sushi is so so. Also if you don't buy an entree, you don't get miso soup...which is not very cool. In most sushi places I've been to, this is a given. It also can get crowded during lunchtime, and the wait to me is not worth it.

I eat here all the time. It's a good deal for the price, and good if you're really hungry. Some of the maki rolls are less than two dollars, and pretty much everything vegetarian is cheap. The Miso soup, as far as I know, is vegan. 

Minuses:
1. Either the fried veggie roll is just awfully salty, or they just pour regular soy sauce in the low sodium soy sauce bottles. 
2. They are always playing Christian music. Or Jack Johnson. 

I am not sure how the meat or fish rolls are, as I am a vegan. 

Apparently they also deliver.

First thing I noticed was the place looked a little dingy from the outside, but although a bit cramped the inside was decent. My friend and I came here for lunch and I was happy to notice that almost all the items on the menu were super affordable. 

Now if it wasn't for the service I would have given more stars, since the food itself wasn't horrible. We had an hour for lunch which we thought would be more than enough (especially since the two of us can eat pretty fast). But it took forever and when my friend's dish came out it ended up being the wrong order. At this point my order still hadn't shown up, and the guy had to basically take our orders over again. I had to end up getting my katsu don to-go....fail.

Knowing that college student, like myself, often decide where to eat by looking at the number after dollar sign, Tako is nice to lower its price to fit my need.  HOWEVER, if the lowering of price result in using stickier rice instead of sushi rice and weird seasoning to make some sort of sweet/slimy rolls with fishy filling, that is ABSOLUTELY not authentic and wrong as a sushi restaurant.  
I ordered the hana sushi special (S3?) the tobiko on the rolls weren't fresh and lose the fullness of being the eggs of fishes, the california roll is too sweet than it should be.  The rolls are loosely wrapped, and I am not even going to tell the discovery of bugs in my water!  Tako!  It is nice knowing you, and now I will start avoiding you!

I have a secret confession to make. I don't like the sushi here. I like the food here though. I ate sushi? Yeah. huh? I know, it sounds weird but this is a decent place to get not-exactly-authentic sushi rolls at a decent price in a neighborhood where you can't find a much better alternative in the way of solving a sushi jones. In the end, this place isn't bad. However, use with caution.

I used to love this place. It has gone so far downhill that I will not spend money here anymore. Although the rolls are cheap, I'd rather save my money until I can afford more quality rolls at a better place.  Food isn't flavorful or fresh, which is dangerous for a sushi place. The chicken teriyaki is totally chewy and the quality is the meat is just abysmal. 

It's just no good anymore... unless, of course, you have no standards for sushi.

Not good. Do not go! All that waits for you at Tako Sushi is a line, super sub-par asian food, small portion sizes, and if you get something cooked and beefy, overcooked beef. I will not go here ever ever again. This place might as well be part of the Asian Ghetto (I go there as infrequently as possible!!).

This place is horrible. 
And I'm sure most people just come here because it is cheap. 
I've had a lot better food EVERYWHERE else I've been. 
No thanks, I'll spend a few extra dollars to get better food and service. 
The employees here are rude and do not care how they treat you because tip is already included. 
I just wanted to throw my soy sauce at the one young waitress with horrible teeth when I asked for ponzu sauce and she gave me this thick gross sauce. 
And when I told here it was not ponzu sauce she told me it was. 
Excuse me, I am not stupid. 
And ! After she gives us our miso soup with no spoons, I asked for spoons for the whole table. 
She brings one. 
I don't understand, you want us all to share? 
Please. 
The eggrolls have nothing in them except oil. 
I can make better ramen from the packages. 
The wings are disgusting.
Everything about this experience makes me so upset I just want to stand outside this place and tell everyone not to go in.

Mexican people making all the rolls and sushi = stamp of authenticity! They put the REAL in REAL CRAB meat here. 

Okay so, stay away from the sushi unless you don't mind unhappy rolls. Why are they unhappy? Because they fall apart and form a big frown on your plate. :(. Sad sushi roll.

Rolls make me sad and nigiri is like bubble-gum chewy. Sigh.

So what's even good here? The entrees, actually. Well, they're the only thing that's left getting.

Chicken teriyaki bowl is a typical quick fix of protein (YEAH PROTEIN) and carbs. I actually prefer the teriyaki salmon steak, but I rarely come here anymore because the prices are hardly worth it.

I think the only thing Tako is actually good for is catering sushi, because the prices are pretty reasonable if you get 50+ pieces. If I remember correctly, it was something around the range of $20. Quality still leaves more to be desired though.

The upshot: this place is cheap. I got a combination of like twelve rolls for like nine dollars. The downside: the fish was super poor quality-really not good. The edamame was hairy and the salad was brown. Yucky!

Took forever with our food! And they messed up the order! The guy that works there is a bit too much. He acts like he knows everything. Giving me sushi that was suppose to go to the table next to us, then accusing me to have miscommunicated with the lady who took our order. Then re-entered our order, making everybody who came after us get their food first. We got our lunch break at 12pm. Got there at 12:10pm. Ordered by 12:15pm. Didnt get food until 12:47pm. Had to pack and get it togo. 

Terrible. Good luck staying in business with all the competition in Berkeley.

This place is sake bomb good!!!

Tako offers by far the cheapest sushi in Berkeley, which is enough reason to jump for joy and pig out like a sumo wrestler. 

I was a little skeptical at first about eating at this sushi house because it's a little hole in the wall restaurant, right next to a college, and it's off of Telegraph Ave (which is one of the dirtiest streets in Berkeley even after street cleaning days).  This definitely does not qualify for the ideal place you would want to go and eat raw fish at.  However; dirty hippies aside, Tako offers great food, plentiful portions, and cheap prices which is why this place is considered a "tasteful sensation" in my book.   The service could be better, and at times gets extremely slow because there is only one server trying to please to thousands of UC Berkeley students; but she does the best she can.  The sushi rolls are prepared where you can see them, which is probably the most important aspect to consider when eating sushi because you know it was prepared freshly.  And although they have Mexicans rolling up the sushi (which some people consider a lack of authenticity), I have learned that Mexicans are the best chefs in the world.  I don't know of any restaurant that doesn't have a Mexican chef, and that's just stating the facts.  

Tako Sushi has a brilliant aroma of Japanese cuisine, and there is nothing better than the feel and taste of masago snapping against your teeth.

Only came here a few times and only because my friends wanted to come here. Honestly, this is the last sushi place that I want to go to. 

I ordered sushi from here, and the quality of the fish was not that great and the unagi got a lot of bones in them... Another time, my friend and I ordered two baked rolls... and the one I had just tasted like california rolls drenched in mayo. 

I also tried the kimchi friend rice, thinking that since it seems to be korean owned, the korean food should be good. But I was soooo wrong.... the kimchi was really sour, and it taste like they just poured tobasco sauce onto the rice to make it spicy. And they also threw in cheap hot dogs pieces. but i guess... since it was under the "poor student" menu. I also tried the kimbap and that was ok, but not great.

The service here varies... sometimes they are attentive, but most of the time they are not. And if you ask them to separate the sushi rolls that my friend and I were taking "to go" they would look disappointed and a bit hesitant...

(+) Delivery service runs until 2-3am
(+) Lion King roll is the most cost effective method to get full with good sushi!
(+) Miso soup comes with each dish

(-) Sitting down at this restaurant typically gets far to busy during weekends and they only have one waiter

I do not recommend eating here. I tried some of my friend's California rolls and they were okay, but when I tasted the teriyaki chicken that I ordered it had a weird ammonia taste. :P Also after my friend ate his steak (I forget what the Japanese name is) he felt sick. 

The place may be cheap but it is not worth your money.

My boyfriend Derek said it best about this place: "Seems like there should be a reminder posted on the door that says 'Make sure to check your order; accuracy cannot be guaranteed.'"

I first went to Tako Sushi when I was a freshman (I'm now graduated) and what I really liked was how many vegetarian options they have.   Other pros about the place: it's pretty cheap and it's close to campus, so it was always an easy place to meet up for lunch.

A friend and I have been meeting there every week for lunch lately.  They kept getting her order wrong (the ashby roll) by putting the fake crab meat in it, which she hates.

Then one night I went there with Derek and ordered the fresh veggie roll, took a bite, and realized they also slipped the fake crab meat in THAT.  I almost gagged.  They gave me a new roll and for free, but other than that, definitely didn't seem to care that they just gave a vegetarian meat and could have had a much worse health situation on their hands.  (Longtime vegetarians do not well with meat.)  Since then, I've always checked the veggie roll before eating it. 

Now I know I've should have checked everything -- today when my friend and I met up, I ordered the fresh veggie roll and the veggie crunchy roll.  They gave me the chicken teriyaki crunchy roll instead, which from above looks exactly like the veggie roll.  I bit into it and nope, not the veggie crunchy roll.  The main waiter (the guy with glasses that is always there) definitely didn't care very much and said he had nothing to do with the order.  Fine, but if your restaurant consistently has problems getting orders right at ALL (and this has nothing to do with the quality of the roll), then you do have something to do with this.  Fix this.  I've had a bad stomachache for the rest of the day.  (Also, they gave me this one for free, but didn't bother to write up a new check so it was included in the tax.  Cheap!)

Now I know to always check everything, but it's a pity you can't just trust it. 

Oh and lastly, they always play TERRIBLE Christian music.  The only good thing is you can make fun of it.

Additional bad service today (04/29/2010): One of the waitresses gave our order to another table, that table didn't notice it looked NOTHING like their order, and started digging in.  The male waiter (the one always there with the glasses and bald head) then actually gave us the roll that they started to eat.  Really?  He thankfully took it away, made a new one, and gave us a small discount.  One reason I like when they mess up -- more discounts for us.

Tako Sushi is great for that quick fix for sushi; it's quite cheap but you pay for what you get.  There are a lot of rolls to choose from but nothing has every stuck out to me ever since I first starting going here over three years ago.  I do like the kim pop and futo maki roll, since I love pickled daikon (like a radish) and it's around $3-$4 each roll!  We usually get cooked rolls here (I don't trust raw fish at a restaurant aimed at starving students with starving student prices and specials).  The BF once got a chicken donburi bowl, which he called "different" but acceptable.  I usually get the miso soup just because it's cheap but there's hardly any tofu or seaweed in it =( The servers are nice but not friendly; they are usually rushed.  Don't expect anything crazy here, but give it a try if you need a quick fix.

Sigh...here we go. First, I have been coming here for 4 years, so I have a lot to say. 

The food is decent for a vegetarian. I normally order their vegetarian lunch/dinner. So this will be off that food.

Pro: 
   -Decent veggy food
   -kinda pretty inside
   -prices are decent...

Con:
   -if you do take out, no miso soup. 
   -if you ask for the miso soup, expect to pay an extra $1 for the "container", even though its supposed to be in your meal already.  
         -I'm paying $8.99 for the vegetarian dinner..and you wanna charge me an extra $1 for a container? seriously?? These "containers" are a little soup thing that cost like 1 penny...
   -sauce is an extra $.50-.75..wtf??
   -spacy older asian lady who doesn't pay attention while I'm ordering:
          -First, she either looks off or fiddles around with her back turned to the side while ordering! Rude!! (at least the young man, i'm guessing her son, is really nice).
   -play christian music. 
   -wait time for food is +20 min. 

Overall, I avoid this place. I really wanted sushi tonight, so i went in there, and she was like, "miso not included"...I asked her if she could do it cause i'm paying for it, and she was like...No, extra $1. to hell with that...

Oh yeah, min $7 credit card...

I have been going to this place for years and it is by far the best bang for your buck. If you go here, ask for Joon! He is the nicest guy ever! This is my favorite place to get Lion King Rolls, and actually, it's the only sushi place that makes the Lion King exactly how I like it.

I go in there so often that Joon knows that I like my "philly roll" with fried salmon skin too! TRY IT!!

Enjoy!

I went today (Monday) to Tako Sushi, and it was my first time in Berkley. It was actually pretty crowded, surprisingly! However, there was only one poor guy waiting tables!!! Hence, the service was quite slow. He was very nice though and I'm sure making bank off of tips!!! But either way, not okay to have ONE server for a whole restaurant with a ton of chefs!!! 

So my friend and I ended up sharing the tempura chicken maki roll and the spicy dragon roll. In the tempura chicken teriyaki roll, when they mean topped with "crunchies", they mean CRUNCHIES! It wasn't bad, but on top of the deep fried heaven on the outside, it was a bit much. My friend and I concluded that especially on the end pieces, it gets a bit heavy and you end up feeling like you are eating a ton of fried batter! The spicy dragon roll really wasn't spicy at all, so if you're looking for a kick, don't get this (and I have a very low spice-tolerance so I mean it!) Although, the spicy tuna filling is delicious, I feel like it had the same problem as the tempura one, where the end pieces were just all fried and no filling! 

Overall, the pricing isn't too bad and it is definitely filling for sushi. I wouldn't necessarily come back unless I was a local though (I had better sushi elsewhere).

The sushi is affordable.  Nothing spectacular, but what did it for me was the zaru soba!

It's on the limited student budget portion, but it was by far the best thing we ordered! (on a hot day that is).  It was a huge portion of cold soba with a side of tempura and soba sauce.

Service-it was ok.

I'd come back if I'm too lazy to go south side of campus for CU Sushi.

Berkeley passed local ordinance 111252:  No high-quality eateries should be located at the part of Telegraph Avenue across the street from the UC campus.  Just cheap places with dishes that taste accordingly.  Exhibit A:  Tako Sushi.  I've spent a fair amount of time at Tako Sushi, again, mostly for convenience.  Sushi rolls here are actually pretty small, but at least they're affordable.  You can get enough to get your fill without breaking your wallet.  Quality is okay, just a tad better than sushi from all-you-can eat places.  For a restaurant that caters to students, however, they can be quite slow.  Overall, there are worse places to go, but don't lose sleep if you don't get to visit.

I'm not picky when it comes to food (I eat just about everything)...

But their Karaage (listed as Karaake on the menu, last time I checked) was absolutely terrible... I mean, instead of pieces of chicken, they fried whole wings and drums... I 
ended up tossing 70%+ into the trash can... 

I've been here about 7 times total (I don't know why I keep coming back... Convenient location?), but the Karaage episode will deter me from ever coming back...

The price is reasonable... Taste falls short...

The quality here is kind of hit or miss.  Some days it is pretty good and I am mostly satisfied but other days, it is not so good and if it weren't for the dirt cheap price, I would be mad.  Nevertheless, I recommend avoiding dinners here with abundant raw fish and sticking with their cooked dishes and their rolls.  Don't come here with high expectations...  It is mediocre Japanese food at a cheap price.

Affordable Japanese food, I guess you get what you pay for.

Service/Decor: There are a few tables inside and you might end up waiting to find a table, but chances are waits won't be long. Nice waiters, but food comes out a little slow. Japanese pictures on the walls, OK to come here with friends.

Food: Yeah, when I say you get what you pay for, it's definitely true. For one, you don't get tea with your meal, which is a complete letdown. I always expect tea at a Japanese restaurant but you have to pay extra here. 

The menu's pretty vast, from nigiri, rolls, various combos, tonkatsu, makis, desserts, etc. A lot of things are really cheap. For $20 you can get a 50 piece tray of california rolls, which is pretty neat (think you have to call in and order this). Rolls fall within the $7-$9 range, and sushi specials are around $11-12. There is a pretty meager amount of fish on the rolls and the presentation is absolutely horrendous. The fish does not taste very fresh (got the Nigiri special, resulted in a sheepish trip to the restroom), but in a cooked roll it would probably taste fine. Not much of a fan of this place.

The best simple california rolls anywhere!  Most of their rolls are mediocre, but the caterpillar, spider, and lion king are delicious.  They also have good party platters, just call a day in advance.

I'm not a sushi connoisseur, I usually get california rolls because for one, at Tako sushi they are ridiculously cheap. Like less than $2 for four of them, which, for a student, is a pretty good deal.

Their california rolls aren't bad which is why if it was just based on those and price this place would get five stars from me (their tempura isn't bad either).

HOWEVER, let's go through the list of things that kinda suck about this place:

1. The service. There is this one waitress who is hands down the surliest woman I have ever had the misfortune of coming into contact with. Every time me and my friends come or even if I drop in by myself this woman is just not friendly. I'm antisocial and awkward so my standards of friendliness are pretty low, basically if you seem nicer than me, you're friendly. I try to be nice to people who serve me my food because after all they're serving me, but this woman...I just don't get it, I smile, I get a blank stare from her, I try to catch her eye if our table needs something and she will look straight at me and turn her back and walk away O.O I always tip her well so I just don't understand it. BEWARE the mean asian lady, if you get a guy server you should be fine though, the bald asian guy with glasses is always super nice and efficient.

2. Don't get popcorn anything here. It's not like normal popcorn chicken, it's really mostly just composed of their fried batter, barely any meat if there's meat at all in it, and served with weird, gross [imo] sauce.

3. Over-priced Edammame. I've been to way better sushi places than this and the Edammame has never been so much for so little. I love Edammame I could eat it all day which is why it always makes me sad when I can't have it here.

4. If you're taking sushi to go be careful, the wait time can range anywhere from 3-20 minutes so it may not be a good idea for a fast sushi fix before class.

Sushi here is very well cooked and the prices are reasonable! Miso soup comes with some things but only costs 1.00 and is pretty good. 

The only downside to this place is the waitress who can be a bit iffy at times...it's like she has mood swings.

 My friend and I have always been good customers and used to Tip but after she began being super rude we stopped tipping her. But we always make sure to tip the other older woman and the guy that sometimes 
works there. 

Decor: The space isn't too big so they have a lot of things just stacked up and covered with pieces of cloth which don't do a really good job of hiding the boxes...I think with a little bit of paint and a better job of hiding all the stuff; the place would look a bit better. :)

We were hopeful, but were disappointed. We got the dynamite roll. It tasted a bit too fishy and was a glob of goo in my mouth. I legitimately spit it out and asked to get a different roll. So, props to the staff for good customer service and making us a new roll; a spicy tuna roll. The tuna was super dark and mushy. Disappointed again. The girls to the right and left of us got some big ol' plates of something else. Those looked good, maybe that's a better bet than sushi.

Sidenote: I am not a picky eater - even when it comes to Sushi. One of my favorite places has $3 rolls that are pre made and I love them.

You get what you pay for at this place.

The prices are cheap, but the quality of the food leaves something to be desired.  I've had much better (and I mean much much better) sushi at other places that are just as cheap as Tako (Manpuku, Geta).  The Miso soup was probably the most disappointing part of it.

The service though was the worst part.  The place was pretty empty when my friend and I were there and yet it still took forever for the waitress to come over to our table.

I'm never coming here again.  I almost contemplated giving it two stars because of the cheapness of the sushi, but then I decided that was too generous.

Poorly run sushi joint with overpriced stinky sushi. The worst sushi I ever had - the fish was not fresh. From the texture, we were very sure it was frozen and then thawed. 

I ordered a rainbow roll and it took them 30 minutes to make it. Were they busy defrosting the fish in the kitchen???Hmm. 

Finally the roll arrived and within 30 secs the waitress brought us the check. Alright,  super SLOW to make the roll, but super quick to ask their customer to pay. The waitress even had that grumpy look on her when she dropped the bill, WTF!! 

We had a large group so I didn't want to be nasty but restaurant like that should just be closed! The only reason for its existence is its location - students like us eat whatever. Btw, I don't even think the food is cheap. I got way better sushi at similar price in San Jose/Fremont.

One last thing: people in that restaurant are not even Japanese, they look and sound like Korean.

Nothing turned out right at this place. Enough said.

Great late. I don't recommend this place for sushi but for a cheap price and a decent taste?? Why not! I came here last night with my gf for dinner and as I walked in I noticed the Mexican guys rolling the sushi... Uhmmmmm.

Ok well that was awkward. The spot is tiny but once you hit the back there's space. There is also an outdoor seating for those who love berkeleys trashy nature lol. 

I ordered the lion king roll which wasn't deep fried or toasted. It actually didn't even taste like it? I also ordered the Kim chee fried rice for $3.50. This was worth it..I wish there was more egg though. Overall, the food is a C+, the service is a B+, and the ambiance is a C. 

To tell the truth, I would still come back lol

Cheap food.  Wayyy too clean, smells like cleaners.  The food is good lunch food, not sure if I would go for dinner.  Their value is very good, if I were to go for sushi for lunch again, I would go back.  I just really hope they won't smell like cleaners again; otherwise, I will never go back again.  Tip:  if you like ramen and you are a poor student, get their starving student special!  It is only $5 with a choice of meat and egg!

my FAVORITE sushi place in berkeley!

all sushi rolls are 7.99 or less! how awesome is that, esp for a student like me!

all the other sushi places arnt as good as Tako. Joshuya's is way too pricy and sushi house in the asian ghetto has no taste. tako sushi is the way to go! their best sushi platter (if you like sashimi) is the Temperance platter, more sashimi/good rolls for your money! It says on the menu to order a day in advance, but you can just call a couple hours before pick up and they'll have it ready :] 

the waitress there is super nice too! she is always smiling and she even let us eat our crepes at the restaurant (we bought it at crepes a gogo). she's also really good about giving out separate checks, which is great cuz i never have cash haha. One thing though, if you order to-go, it sort of takes a while. Once, i ordered to-go right after a table ordered the huge boat, and it took forever-- but it was just bad timing :/ 

nonetheless, my sushi cravings are satisfied, and so is my budget! :)

So I'm reviewing Nude Sushi, which is basically Tako Sushi anyway.  Where else can you get sushi at 3 in the morning when you're totally hammered and need to eat a bunch of raw fish? And they're so fast too. I think.  My perception of time is usually pretty messed up when I order from them.  Anyway the food is pretty good, but I wouldn't go there if every other sushi place wasn't closed.

I'm giving this place five stars because they managed to combine my favorite two foods ever: PINEAPPLE and SUSHI. This roll had so much flavor at such a good price that I almost cried... tears of JOY! AHHHH.

Plus they have such an extensive menu & vegetarian options so you can keep coming back for more! Also, they miso soup that comes with the roll is a nice touch. They even gave miso soup to my friends who didn't even order anything! 

The workers were so friendly :) And I thought the service was fast. If I ever come back to Berkeley, I'll make sure to come back here for my sushi fix.

Tako Sushi, let me count the ways... starting from zero.

+1 for the portions and sizes of rolls
-1 for the fact that they don't taste good
+1 because of the super low prices
-1 because I know now why the prices are so low
+1 good service
