-1 horrible dining experience, was that a roach?
+1 for being open super late

Lets just stop there.

The thing that makes this place valuable is that it is dirt cheap and on Telegraph. Getting there is more trouble than it is worth though. I don't like driving/parking around Telegraph around dinner time and Berkeley has so many other places worth the drive. What IS awesome though is www.getnudesuhi.com. Getnude is the internet-based sushi delivery service that is run out of Tako until 4 am. Who needs to eat at nasty Denny's when they can have sushi delivered? (Berkeley only.) Oddly enough, the price is not horrible for delivery. Error rate is low because you never talk to anyone. It's very amazon.com--you add rolls to cart. Don't drive to this place; make them drive to you.

nude sushi (their sister company) is better, even at 2a. 

im not saying that it was bad, but the rolls i ordered took about 35 minutes and were not tightly wrapped. they came apart as soon as my chopsticks touched it. and some were cut super fat. 

while waiting for my to-go order, i had a chance to check out the ambiance. its pretty dingy in there, but they tried to paint some cherry tree branches on the dirty ceiling. its a bit odd to hear mexican music in a sushi place, but i guess its to please the guys making your food. the manager was nice and appreciated the tip i gave him. 

try: asparagus, avocado or cucumber-avocado roll.

Tako's a centerpiece for convenience but it's hit-or-miss in terms of quality.  It's right next to campus, the service is very friendly, and the food is just right for the college budget.

They often used to play Christian worship music but recently switched to subtle instrumentals.  You wouldn't know they were Christian unless you happened to grow up in church and you knew all the lyrics (like, um ... me).  One could easily confuse the music for ambiguously classical, or (maybe?) Southeast Asian, or (maybe?) just Generic Restaurant Ambiance.

Four times out of ten, you're going to get some fish that must have been sitting around in the open at least 4 days before they decided, "Hey, we should seriously cut that up and try to feed it to somebody."

Also, I always smell like soy sauce once I leave.  It only ever happens at Tako.

If you're hungry, and want sushi, you know, nothing too fancy, decent, rolls, Tako's a good place to start.

They have an extensive list of maki (sushi rolls) that are reasonably priced for what you get, all the expensive rolls have dropped to $7-9 max.  They have your classic rainbow, dragon, cherry blossom, caterpillar rolls, crunch, lion king, etc. and even have some rolls that I think are their original ideas (or at least a rarities), such as the deep fried godzilla roll, the baja roll, the pineapple roll and more!

I'd recommend trying a roll that you haven't seen before that looks good to you, it's a nice change from your general sushi choices.

The nigiri is OK, but if you're looking for nigiri/sashimi, Tako isn't your place, their rolls are fine though.

Or if you're pretty hungry, look toward the starving student special, the chicken katsu curry is decent, and you get a ton!  Get that + a roll or two, and that's a pretty large meal that will fill you up =P

N-A-S-T-Y!

I came here with a friend for lunch and I was so excited to see how cheap everything was! However... my excitement ended right there.

The service wasn't that great...we were waiting for at least 15 minutes before someone came over to take our order. 

I ordered some curry dish (forgot the name) but it was a lunch special for less than $5. The first bite was pretty good and then I just felt sick the more I ate.

but OMG THE WORST PART...YOU SHOULD READ THIS BEFORE YOU DECIDE IF YOU WANT TO GO:

When she brought out our miso soup, we already started drinking it and she comes back after like 3 minutes, TAKES OUR SOUP FROM US AND GIVES IT TO THE CUSTOMERS A COUPLE TABLES AWAY FROM US...WTF?! Both my friend and I were in utter shock...we didn't even know what to say??!?! WHO DOES THAT????

Omg, so nasty. Never going back!

This is just my opinion.. but I like tako sushi better than Joshuya's down the street...but looking at other recent reviews.. maybe tako sushi got worst?

I've been here many times.. a local japanese sushi joint where all the college kids/group meetings/group dinners happen.  and of course I've been here for all those many reasons also.

It's a close by and convenient sit-in restaurant.  Sushi house in asian ghetto is convenient too but too small of a place compared to tako sushi.  They do cater.. they have party plates if you order ahead of time.

Their bento boxes are pretty good for my taste.. i never finish it.

This is hands-down my favorite FAVORITE cheap sushi place. For a while we were going there every Friday night.

Great for groups, and they have outdoor seating in the back. About a 10 minute walk from bart, and if you arrive at exactly 6pm, you can park right outside on telegraph.

The menu is excellent- there are 86 different rolls, all with photos. Plus a whole assortment of other stuff.

The Fiesta roll is awesome, Sunset roll is awesome, No Name roll is great, Veggie Caterpillar, Lion King, Veggie Crunchy... ahh they have so many good rolls.
And all the rolls all huge.
And none of the rolls are over $7.99.

(They do offer a lot of sauce-covered or deep fried rolls, but they have the healthy ones too. And they're always happy to leave off the sauce or put it on the side.)

Also they are really really nice here! Sometimes they give you free appetizers, and they have a frequent buyer card, and they'll remember you and that you prefer low-sodium soy sauce, and they're just wonderful.

Plus the cherry blossoms painted on the wall are pretty :)


Favorite (cheap) sushi place. Ever.

okay okay, not the BEST sushi in the world, perhaps not even in the neighborhood - but the location is great, and the prices are very reasonable.  I always order way more than me or my date can eat.  however, don't order the fried chicken, it was simply terrible (and it came after our meal, even though we ordered it first).  As for the sushi, $1.50 for an avocado roll!!!  everytime i'm craving sushi (and sushi house is too damn far - or im too damn drunk to drive to alameda) tako sushi is right there - easy and cheap.

One of my old college hangouts on Telegraph Avenue dating back to freshman year with affordable sushi, a great staff and great food for the price. I came back recently and was impressed by the stability of the prices and the reliability of the menu. I'm a creature of habit and always go for the chicken teriyaki roll and cucumber roll and it's reliably delicious.
It's pretty gross here.

I love Tako Sushi. Been here maybe 3 or 4 times and every time the sushi is great. It's exactly the same as sushi in WC, just half the price. The service is a little slow but the unchanging quality of food makes up for it.

When I'm in Berkeley and craving sushi, this is the place I head to.

At one point when I was a student at Berkeley I ate here every day for about two weeks straight. They have the cheapest, best tasting rolls I have ever come across. When I used to go they had like $1.25 California rolls that actually tasted good. They have a huge selection of rolls and all their veggie rolls are especially good.

The prices here are cheap, and that's probably because it's so close to the UC Berkeley campus. It has dim lighting and okay decor (the painted walls are the most interesting part). And the food and the customer service is okay to good, not great but definitely not bad.

Everything might just be okay, but the strengths of Tako Sushi is its location, its convenience, and that it makes late night deliveries.

dirt cheap and i've never had a problem with the service (but then, i always get take out).  they have the *best* california rolls i've had (california rolls, golden california rolls, and spicy california rolls).  i tried their ngiri and other rolls once but was displeased--i think a good rule of thumb is to steer clear of the fish dishes at cheap eats.  but the cally rolls are sooooo damn good!  definitely one of my favorite lunch stops on telegraph.

15.00 for lunch.. Imma cool wid that.. Yeah.. Not the best sushi in the world.. But hey.. You get what u generally pay for..

Great for snacks in between meals.. But wouldn't bet the bank for a nite out and rollin thru here..

I love that when you walk in you hear mariachi music, so they get a star for that. the prices are freakin' awesome. I mean definitely not an authentic sushi joint. You'll find "sushi" that are deep fried, with chicken teriyaki, etc. but hey, what else do you expect blocks from a college? I was walking by and got a fried tempura battered California roll, and it was delicious. Me and my boyfriend devoured that puppy.

I used to come here a lot with my friends. It has, however, gone downhill over the past two years. It just doesn't taste as fresh anymore. And some of the rolls have way too much rice on them (and the rice is clumpy at that). I do like their chicken katsu/chicken teriyaki, but this should not be a justification for a sushi place. 

This is just a good place to get a quick sushi fix if you're feeling hungry and not particularly picky. Their starving student specials are good deals but again, clumpy rice is not good. Otherwise, Joshuya's a few blocks away is a better option (albeit more expensive) for a sit-down sushi experience.

Tako doesn't judge me (too much) when I order 2 or 3 rolls to-go with one set of chopsticks and I appreciate that, I do. And I also appreciate their relatively cheap Lion King rolls although I admit that it's probably the only thing I still order, along with an occasional Baja roll when I'm feeling particularly ~adventurous~. 

There's a reason for that: unfortunately, Tako is one of the few places in the world that has made a spicy tuna roll I did not enjoy. I didn't just not enjoy it -- I found it to be repulsively and disturbingly sweet/fruity. Maybe it was an off day, I don't know. How do you mess up a spicy tuna roll??? I used to order their popcorn salmon, but it's getting more and more bready and less and less... fishy. And their chicken karaage is kinda like a tasteless and oilier (is that possible?) version of the stuff you can get at a Chinese supermarket deli -- that is to say, not chicken karaage. 

I'll give credit where credit is due though. Although on the sweeter side, their Lion King rolls reaaaaalllllyyyyy hit the spot.

I don't dig the Christian pop music that's on repeat, but I don't eat in that often. The food comes a lot more quickly if you just call them and pick up your order.

You know, whenever I go to a place without Yelping it first, I can't help but think to myself as I eat there, "You know, I bet this place it a ___ star on Yelp".

I was right again. 2.5 to 3 what what I guessed, and that was spot-on. "Great prices for bad sushi" is what Tatyana said, and that's a bullseye. We too found it REALLY loud, unclean, our servers were very nice but VERY slow... and the fish wasn't the freshest.

It would be two stars, but it was really cheap, so it's three. 'Nuff said.

Sushi here isn't that cheap :c

Or at least, not the sushi rolls we ordered haha.

My friend and I came here on a Friday noon for our lunch munch session. The seating is plentiful but cramped. We were given menus, water, and complimentary miso soup. We then ordered:

#71: CRUNCHY DELIGHT: shrimp tempura, crab, avocado, topped with crunchies [8 pieces | $7.99]
- My favorite! Recommended by my friend as well.
- I adored the crunchies (LOOOL), and the pieces were filling! Avocado was decently fresh, and the crab was fairly tasty. The crab overpowered the shrimp tempura, though.

#29: CHICKEN TERIYAKI ROLL: BBQ chicken with avocado, topped with teriyaki sauce [8 pieces | $4.59]
- My second favorite! Chicken is tasty, and the avocado is a good pair! Digging the teriyaki sauce with sesame seeds on top. Simple and cheap is the way to go!

#64: DYNAMITE ROLL: deep-fried spicy salmon, cucumber, topped with crab and spicy sauce [9 pieces | $9.59]
- My least favorite. I wouldn't recommend it.
- I liked that the roll was deep-fried, as the crispy outside complimented the softness of the rice and crab. But the salmon. It was gross. The texture was tough, and the spiciness was too sharp. You would bite into the crunchy shell, enjoy the crab piled on top, and then struggle to chew the resistant salmon filling. Dislike.

Our total before tax came to $24.11, which wasn't as cheap as what I anticipated. But, we came out full and satisfied. And we DID order a lot. What can I say, my friend is a glutton.

Good food (can't say anything about the freshness of fish though, since we only ordered cooked spicy salmon), decent prices, kind of slow service (took about 12 minutes, although it was during the lunch hour), and complimentary miso soup. I recommend the Crunchy Delight and the Chicken Teriyaki Rolls, but AVOID the Dynamite Roll!

One of Berkeley's more popular Japanese restaurants, if only because South Siders are too lazy to walk more than a couple of blocks to find the really good stuff.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: two stars.

The sushi is pretty good if you are a fan of sushi. However, after I was introduced to the magic of sashimi by my friend, sushi just seems bland. With that new perspective, I can only call Tako's sushi average. What can I say, I tend to prefer simplicity over the complex monstrosities that most sushi rolls have become. At the very least, Tako doesn't douse their rolls in soy sauce, avocado, tempura batter, and hot sauce.

Everything else is average as well. The miso soup is good, but nothing that can't be made at home. 

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: One star.

A clean restaurant on Telegraph is always good for one star.

Ate at Tako once with 2 of my friends. I was surprised at how cheap the prices were and how the rolls looked proportional to their prices. I didn't have the chance to order the rolls, (only tried the CA roll, which tasted like any typical CA roll...) so we ordered the Donburi for around 4dollars, Kimchi Fried Rice for around 3dollars, and Chicken Teriyaki Boll w/ 4 CA rolls for around 6dollars. Pretty cheap for lunch, I may say.
The Donburi was pleasing and full. The chicken was very crunchy and it seemed to have a sweet BBQ sauce to it. On top of that, they had rice on the bottom and a fried egg with vegetables in it. I would recommend getting it again if you stop by for a quick-fix for your hunger. The bowl isn't super big, but it isn't super small too.
The Kimchi Fried Rice was good, but had too much of a sour and spicy taste. After eating half the rice, my friend got sick of it and we had to ditch the plate of rice. Maybe it was the fact that the rice didn't taste like it was made of Kimchi, and tasted more of a Mexican-styled rice?
The Chicken Teriyaki Rice bowl was the same...Like any other, but also very fulfilling. However, there's much better sushi places out there who have bigger portions and cheaper rice bowls then what we ordered.
The miso soup was salty, but we never had miso soup in our life so we didn't have a say in this.
Overall, it was pretty alright, but I'll go back next time for the rolls to try it out instead of ordering entrees. The Starving Student Specials seem promising though, so I recommend Berkeley students to go there during lunch hours for a cheap, filling meal!

Someone once told me the title 'Tako Sushi' was a play on 'Taco Sushi' since they have Hispanics (or Mexicans.. I don't remember which was the pc one) making the sushi. Whether thats true are not, I'm not sure. But its stuck in my mind. 

The sushi is small, not fresh, and sorta put together. Emphasis on 'sorta.' If you don't hold it right (or sometimes just touch it), it'll fall apart leaving the artificial whatever filling in the middle and a lace of seaweed and rice somewhere near it.  

2* since its doing well enough feeding college students without functioning tongues.

This place was my first sushi meal at Berkeley.  Actually I wanted to add an additional half star.  I love nigiri shushi so always orded rainbow roll (california roll with various raw fish on top of it)  It was cheap and the quality was not bad too.

*I was starving when I ate here.  I am also from Oklahoma, where we are landlocked into frozen fish territory.  Think about these two biases when you read my review.*

Tako Sushi was pretty good.  It was not as good as sushi I'd have later on my weekend in the Bay Area, not even close, but it was a great stop-gap between UC and the BART station.  The rolls are ridiculously huge, which is unappealing to me, but they were not too bad taste-wise, and were fresher than I'm used to.

Service wasn't bad, and I didn't notice the Christian music.  (This is also probably because Oral Roberts University and I share a hometown.  Ew.)

Tako Sushi is awesome. Its the only place where I can actually get full off of sushi for under $10. Seriously, sushi is usually very expensive and one 5 piece roll could cost almost $8 and be a mere snack. However at Tako they give you 6-8 pieces and most rolls are between $3-8 (the more expensive ones are more fancy and more filling, plus they give you at least 8 pieces). The specialty rolls are around $8 but the California rolls I believe are only about $1.75 as are some of the vegetarian rolls. Others maki rolls like tekka maki or spicy salmon are around $3-4 for 8 pieces for most. Very good prices for sushi if you ask me! The sushi has always tasted very good and fresh to me and the male server is super nice. Gyoza and eggrolls are always really good and very well priced! A must try if you want some delicious, cheap sushi in Berkeley.

Wow. So I went here last night with my gf and some friends, straight passed up on Fat Slice like it was the thing to do only because I had been craving sushi all week. Needless to say I was utterly disappointed.

I understand the point of stepping outside the box to make imaginative rolls but seriously who the hell puts ketchup on sushi? That's like.. .. ok its so ridiculous that I can't even come up with a metaphor. Lame. 

We had 

Oishii
Spicy Sweet Roll 
Seaweed salad
Chicken Teriyaki bento
Bear roll [? I think]

The sushi was cold, and very bland in taste. Soon after dinner me and my gf had stomach aches, GROSS lol. Oh and don't bother coming here if you expect to have a cold bottle of Sapporo, because they don't serve any alcohol. 

The prices were reasonable, the tab came out to $40 something for the 4 of us.. even so, next time I'll think twice about passing on greasy crispy pepperoni pizza.

Tako Sushi sells cheap sushi/food for berkeley students. little decor.  exists besides some music.

Sampling: '
-"Ghirashi (as it appears on menu) lunch 12.99
-miso soup: like any other j restaurant. not a lot of msg.
-salad: miso dressing over lettuce
-chirashi contained 1 ebi, 6 salmon, 5 maguro, 2 hamachi, 2 suzuki, a dap of seaweed
-white ginger and sliced daikon(radish)
-lots of nicely vinegared sushi rice provided..


temaki:
-service ok , biz slow
-quality ok, quantity a value.

Tako sushi is the place to go in Berkeley for super cheap and delicious sushi. Everytime i go there with me and my buddies, we order literally 20 rolls to split 6 ways and we all play 15 bucks. Now that, is REALLY cheap and its good. I crave Tako now.

I don't know why people like the place so much.  All I have to say is, you get what you pay for.  I came here frequently for the seaweed salad, california roll, and spider roll before I became a sushi snob.  That being said, those things I just listed are still pretty okay here.

Other menu items i've tried:
miso soup - i actually really like it here!  they always give you a bowl when you dine in.
popcorn chicken - i was obsessed with these at one point in my life!  love them, and love the sauce.  they are crunchy, mushy, and spicy, all at the same time.  very tasty!
tempura - pretty decent.  i like the dipping sauce.
edamamme - good.  i mean, what else can i say about steamed soy beans?
sashimi - leaves something to be desired.

Rolls:
poki roll - i like it!  spicy tuna roll topped with seaweed salad.  i just really like poki.
new york roll - not very memorable.
philly roll - good.
spider roll - the soft shell crab is soft, and it's topped with masago.  i really enjoy the spider roll here.
spicy california roll - whoa, really spicy.
oishii roll - pretty good.
baja roll - pretty good also.
stuffed oranges - spicy scallops wrapped with fresh salmon.  for some reason i expected more and was oddly disappointed.
lion king roll - i really like this one.  baked salmon on top of california roll.  i think maybe it's the baked salmon and the sauce.

The people who work here are friendly.  They charge like $0.25 for extra hot sauce when you order take-out (uh, lame).  I only come in here once in a while now (during finals, and when i'm starving), and I think they have new people working here.  They're not as nice as the people who have been working there for a long time.

Don't come in during peak hours.  Not only will it take forever for you to get your food (for both dine-in and take-out), the service is super sucky (since there are so many people).  There's a $7 minimum for credit cards.

The atmosphere is bleh, but what do you expect from a place on Telegraph Ave.?

It's just cheap.  There's nothing else to it.  It's okay at first, but I always find myself struggling to finish the roll.  That's the worst part, having to finish it, because I was raised by parents who would regularly bring up the topic of starving children at the dinner table.  So, waste not want not, but we all know leftover sushi is nasty stuff.  In a perverse way, it's good thing, because by the time I finish, my sushi cravings are quelled for a considerable amount of time - sushi is an expensive taste, anyway - if only because I swear to myself that I'll never want sushi ever again.

The rolls are big - dont worry, they'll fill you up good.  Regular-grade, crumbly rice and fish that's neither fresh nor good quality.  Menu consists mostly of sushi restaurant staples.  The specials look complicated and intimidating.  

But hey, we're poor college students.  At this point in our lives, not many of us can afford to have good taste, and Tako Sushi is cheap, near campus, and does the job.  Hell, it even has a side menu explicitly labed "starving student menu" filled with various carbocide options priced $7 and under that will keep your stomach happy.  And I appreciate the free sodium (or miso) soup.  No matter the quality, I'll continue to be a patron once every blue moon, to add a little variety to southside dining options.

Ehhh... This place kinda sucks, but I still go there regularly because it's the best sushi place that's close enough to my work to be able to eat lunch at. I've never had a problem with service but I've only ever gotten takeout. The prices aren't really all that cheap when you compare them to other sushi places... For example, their "Golden Bear Tutoring Roll" (avocado/salmon with masago on the outside) is $4--just the same as at Sushi House (theirs is called the "Oregon roll")--but far inferior in quality. The salmon is often mushy, in multiple pieces, and sometimes has weird tough grey skin-like layers on it. The rolls are often not very well put-together & will fall apart when you try to pick them up. Sometimes the food is better than others. It's edible, but not great by any stretch of the imagination. Their miso soup is pretty good though.

2/13/07: Okay, I need to edit this because the last time I went there, which was several months ago, I got a salmon/avocado roll in which the avocado was CRUNCHY and there was a weird crunchy bit on the salmon too. Yuck! I haven't gone back since.

5/7/07: Breaking my vow to myself to never return, I went to Tako sushi for lunch on Friday. I have never regretted anything more. I took a picture of what they try to pass off as "salmon" and I'll try to post it here. Unfortunately I got my food to go and was too damn lazy to return it when I opened the box and saw how awful it was. No more Tako Sushi for me, ever. I mean it this time. I wish I could give it negative 4 stars.

On a sushi scale of 1-10, Tako gets about a 2, just barely pulling ahead of pre-made supermarket sushi. Ick.

This is a cheap, fast sushi place geared toward starving students. In fact, they have 'starving student' deals, which is a big selling point for some of my friends.

For what it is, it's very good! Service is fast and cheery, and I've had different kinds of donburi and sushi, and it's all been fine. It's a good place to get full cheaply.

Tremendous taste coupled with tremendous value! On a student budget, what more could you ask for? If you come here with a sophisticated sushi palate expecting something more than Americanized "sushi," don't waste your time and money. You'll find tasty food here, but nothing even remotely authentic.

Almost everything I've tried has exceeded my expectations, especially for the price: bento boxes, chicken teriyaki, spring rolls, nigiri, and of course, the sushi rolls. The fish is surprisingly fresh -- in fact, this is where I had my first taste of raw fish, so it can't be that horrifying, right? Even their side dishes are great. The salad has a wonderful, unique dressing and the miso soup is always hot and yummy.

The classic California roll was my first experience with sushi, and I've never had a better California roll since. I prefer rolls with imitation crab salad as opposed to whole chunks of crab. I heard that they put sugar in the rice on the rolls, which disturbs me, but it does help explain why the rolls are so delicious. Most of the other assortments I've tried have also been orgasmic, particularly the Baja, Oishii, Sunrise, Dragon, Caterpillar, and Spider rolls. I like the mayonnaise-based sauces they drizzle on them, too. The combination of flavors are always great.

In addition to the amazing food, you'll barely be done with your soup before your entrée arrives, and the waiters are very attentive, refilling your water as needed. The decor is great for a hole-in-the-wall, too. Cute paintings on the walls and non-ghetto tables.

The only disappointing item I've had was the potstickers, which were too crispy for my tastes, and if I recall correctly, they were served with a sauce that did not complement the taste well at all. Other minor negatives include the Christian music, which seems like subtle brainwashing and kind of creeps me out. I suppose this explains why they're closed Sunday. This also sucks, but as long as you make a mental note to not go on Sundays, it isn't a big deal at all. And finally, there's something inherently wrong with Mexican music coming from the kitchen of a Japanese restaurant. Then again, what the hell do I care who makes the food as long as it's good?

To summarize: HELLZ FUCKING YES. I've since had far more expensive sushi assuming I'll get what I pay for, but honestly I'd choose Tako Sushi over the overpriced alternatives any day of the week. I just moved to Sacramento and even the "good" Japanese restaurants up here don't live up to the legendary Tako Sushi. I'll always have my memories, I guess. Also, it took me awhile to figure this out, but you can order the same items from Nude Sushi (http://www.getnudesushi.com) and have them delivered to your door until 3 AM. I know it seems to good to be true, but it's no joke: you can enjoy Tako Sushi at almost any hour of the day! For those of us melting into the couch with a bad case of the munchies, I can't imagine anything better. Whoever thought of the concept of late-night delivery sushi is a genius, plain and simple.

Well, what are you waiting for? Get your ass over here already and fall in love.

Wait, WHAT?! Did somebody say "decent" sushi? Fool, you're obviously trippin (imo)!

I knew I shouldn't have followed my friends here when they were craving for sushi. I ordered some sashimi and a Dragon roll. The sashimi was the most disgusting and filthiest piece of fish I ever put in my mouth (no homo)! The instant it touched my tongue, it felt numb... I've never encountered this feeling, and it felt as if it killed my taste buds. So the Dragon roll was very bland due to my taste buds dying. 

But like everyone has said, "you get what you paid for." --Exactly what it is. You get nothing more, nothing less out of this crap like that.

Summary:
Cheap prices = low quality, enough said.

2 Brief Points:

1. Nasty
2. Waste of money

Oh by the way, they charged me 16 or 18% (forgot which one) gratuity for having a party of 6.. even though I was eating with 2 people... and 4 girls from the other table were my friends, so I said hi. They just assumed we were a "party" despite the tables being 5 meters away from each other.

The sushi is just okay, but the price is unbeatable! I'm not super picky with my sushi, and actually just enjoy the california rolls you can get at Costco. So I really don't have much to say about the quality of the rolls.

My favorites are the:
- bay scallop, 
- dragon roll, and 
- california rolls (when I'm not that hungry)

The bay scallop is baked so it takes a little longer for them to make, but everything in this goes together really well. It's essentially a california roll topped with scallops, this orange sauce, and masago. They're really generous with the masago, and soy sauce isn't really necessary, which makes it easier to eat :)

I do like coming here for sushi because it's cheaper, but my friends who are picky tend to stay away.

This place must hire very talented sushi artists beacuse they made the boot on which I gnawed taste exactly like fish!  Honestly, it was probably the best boot I have ever eaten.

I have only patronized this establishment on one occasion, mostly because i am not partial to un-food.  But if you like that sort of thing, I would highly recommend this place.  It is very inexpensive and you will leave with a feeling of ~mehhhh~ that will stay with you all day.

They are kind enough to wrap each piece of debris with about three inches of soggy rice and stale seaweed.  It blew the competition out of the water - there's no way I will ever eat from the garbage can behind Kip's after tasting the food here!  It's almost as good as Safeway sushi cerca 11 pm on a Thursday night.

Thank you, Tako, for enlightening me to the new lows of fast fish.

Gonna have to add my voice to the others here. I have NO IDEA what the people rating 5 and 4 stars were smoking. SERIOUSLY. This place is the epitome of starving college student lowest grade sushi. Transplanting this restaurant anywhere else with a decent sushi appreciating crowd would probably make it implode from the gravitational pull of its own suckiness. Srsly.

I remember coming here when I was a wee freshman loooooong ago. I was the only one who ordered sushi out of my friends. I figured why visit a sushi restaurant and order something like a terikaki bento? Made no sense to me. It was too bad for me that the logic that usually served me well backfired on me and helped my friends whom I thought made a dumb choice. The sushi was terrible.

I made the mistake of visiting a couple of more times during my undergrad years. I guess I am a sucker for pain. 3 stars for their OK non-sushi dishes and 2 stars (pushing it even at that) for their bad sushi. Even Tako Sushi doesn't deserve a 1 star bad buffet sushi rating. At least they have humans making it here (albeit badly).

Anytime I'm short on cash and can't make up my mind where I want to go, Tako is the first place that comes to mind.
I've been going here for a while now and while the food is not always great, I've always had great customer service and cheap prices!
For about two months solid, me and my best friend would go eat there every wednesday night before doing photos for EPR (at Blake's), usually getting there an hour or 30 minutes before they closed. Even with being so late, the owner (?) would always give us excellent service and our food was delivered relatively quickly (depending on how many people were there).

All in all I recommend this place especially for people who are new to sushi and would like to experience a wide range of dishes without shelling out lots of $, but if you're looking for outstanding taste you'd better head out to San Francisco for the best of the best.

Man oh man how I wish they served tacos at this place. When a friend told me we were going to go to Tako Sushi I got so freaking excited. I mean, taco sushi? How much better can it get?! But. alas, it was not meant to be and unfortunately there were no seaweed covered tacos or rice and beans rolls. Talk about fusion right?

There's not much to say about this place except that it is a solid C student. They did have a decent selection of food and a lot of people seemed to be waiting for takeout but it wasn't anything special. Not bad per se, just not special. If you're looking for better sushi then I'm sure there are better places in Berkeley. If you're looking for polenta udon then you're gonna have to look.....wow I don't even know where to start. END OF REVIEW

This place has great prices for bad sushi. If you are a starving student, you will find yourself right at home here. It was a mistake for me to come here as the place is loud and un-clean (to put it mildly), service is terrible (I had to approach the server to remind her we were ready to order), sushi is below average. I think the only reason this place is still around is because typically students can eat here cheap.

Because the place was not the cleanest, we wanted to sit at an outside patio. It was closed. We were seated next to the table with a very loud couple of friends who where laughing so loud my ear drums were about to pop. 

And what's worse, this place does not serve alcohol. What???

Such a disappointment.

Solid one star for great wall painting of sakura branches.

I love Tako Sushi for its starving student specials!  It really is perfect for college students.  You can get a filling and delicious meal for 4 bucks!  I've had ramen and katsu chicken off the starving student menu and ended up full with left-overs.  I was really surprised to get so much food for the little I was paying.  The food isn't really high end or fancy, but you still get a lot for your money.
The environment in Tako sushi is a little cramped and loud, but not too bothersome.  The waiters are also pretty friendly for the most part.

i'm almost embarrassed to say...i like this place. 
(i heard very bad things about it) 
the "fancy" rolls aren't all THAT cheap, but open up the menu and you get a ton of nontraditional rolls for less than $5. 
my bf and i got the chicken teriyaki roll, kappa maki, a korean-style roll, salmon maki, and one with deep fried shrimp and vegetables. my favorite was the last one...forgot its name. the sushi is sliced very thin, which i like cause i can actually fit the whole thing in my mouth. 
a downside is that the sushi took quite a while for them to prepare...and there was no complimentary miso soup, salad, or soy beans to munch on...
note: the adzuki (red bean) ice cream is a MUST have for dessert.

I'm here to spread some Tako Sushi Love!

I remember college days studying in the back of tako sushi. and nibbling my way through whatever mediocre Japanese fare I decided to munch on for virtually no money.

I remember late drunken nights and ordering sushi to come to my co-op far into the the night/earliest morning.

Tako sushi has always had fantastic deals, craving satisfying food, and great hours.

The service is always a bit aloof, but for these prices, what more do you expect?

Since my college days, they added a "starving students" menu which even as a "not starving, young working professional" I ordered from and had a lovely bowl of ramen with veggies and tofu for less than $5.  

It is what it is, and if you accept that, you will love it.

I usually spend $15-20 here, but you can spend a third of that if you're a reasonable person.

I have to assume that the owners of this place are the LEAST subtle people on the planet.

*Inside the owner's brain*
This place doesn't look Japanese enough.  We should slap a cherry blossom tree up on the wall.  Also, a lot of these students are poor, so we should probably have a "poor student" section of the menu and discount all of our rolls to a consistent price.  However, we don't want people to think our food is sub-par, so we should probably deep fry our less delicious rolls and then plate our sushi on dishes that say "delicious" on them in Japanese.

*Back to my brain*
All of the above, hilariously, is true.  I like this place because it does well in a special Japanese restaurant category that I have: Mediocre fish, but a lot of food for the price.  I recommend trying the less than healthy deep fried salmon bites and steering generally clear of anything raw.  Good luck!

Tako sushi was my go-to sushi joint in Berkeley for years, that is until Manpuku came around.

Situated in the space next to Fat Slice, Tako has really inexpensive combo lunches which will run about the same as a slice next door. I think at the time they were exclusively for Cal students but I was actually in high school when I frequented this place the most. Not a place I'd particularly credit for their fresh sashimi, they do have a good selection of rolls to please both the sushi newbie and sushi experimenter. Not particular on the presentation or innovativeness, Tako will fill you up on the cheap, and that's about it. Not a destination, but definitely a staple if you live nearby and/or are a student. They're open late, too!

Let's first acknowledge that this restaurant is located in a college town and is made for poor college students on tight budgets. Though the quality isn't top notch, the sushi here is cheap and the rolls are large. There is a large selection of rolls and other dishes as well. I think I've tried half of their menu already. I always enjoy eating here.

If you are a student, go for the student specials!
$5 kimchi fried rice

-sketchy restroom

just gonna say it right off the bat: Sushi connoisseurs, stay away.  I just don't want to hear, "This isn't genuine Edo-style sushi." Yeah? And you're not exactly genuine Edo-style either, so shut 'yer rice hole. 

That said, I like this place. I like this place for the same reason as Mad Fish: it's dirt cheap. However, unlike my stance at Mad Fish, I'm plenty comfortable ordering raw fish items here. I've never received any raw fish here that didn't taste fresh. The food is, at it's worst, on par with what you pay. At it's best, this place is truly enjoyable.

I don't plug this place hardcore because I've only been here two times. But the amount of food you get (especially in the combos) is more than worth the cash. The owner(?) is a really nice guy and those fellas roll a fat ol' roll.

I was searching for a began bakery everywhere and I stumbled upon this cute little spot. It took my friend and I about 10 min (there were so so many toppings to chose from). The staff were generous and allowed us to try the frosting flavors. They even handed out samples which were absolutely delish; I had to ask the lady making them if they were really vegan. Of course they were! Lol, I got a custom cinnamon bun with caramel frosting, strawberries, almonds, and brownie. It was amazing! Definitely going back there!

Can't believe it took me so long to come here! Well, no, I can. I don't often get over to East Bay for all the tasty vegan treats they hide away. But thanks to the recent Living Social offer for Cinnaholic, I finally hauled my arse over. I was not disappointed.

So. many. ingredients. I really couldn't take it all in the first time, so I went with a couple of the pre-designed specials, Cookie dough and oreo cheesecake. Not only were both quite excellent, they still tasted good after a couple days (I was saving them for my gf's bday.)

I need to go back here soon.

DIBS ON FRANCHISE RIGHTS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  

nuff said...

Lemme start off by saying there's an overwhelming amount of icing and topping choices here! If you're indecisive like I am, go for the basic roll and prepare to savor every last bite. Since their rolls are vegan, it makes eating there feel like a healthy indulgence. They offer a student discount too, so if you're a student remember to bring a school ID!
love it!!

The rolls here are absolutely delicious. I ordered the mocha almond specialty roll, and while absolutely scrumptious, I think a simple roll would be equally satisfying. I didn't even realize the place was catering to the vegan lifestyle until I realized there wasn't any milk to wash my roll down. We will definitely be back very soon.

all you need to know about cinnaholic is that if you are ever, for any reason, for any amount of time, even remotely close to berkeley that you absolutely must come here. if you have to decide between gas and cinnaholic, you choose cinnaholic and walk. it is so incredibly delicious to the point where it is blissfully overwhelming. i had the smores roll and it was out of control sensational. i purchased a cookie dough caramel roll and the special which was some sort of brownie roll to go. i am compelled to keep rambling on about how good they are but it is a fruitless effort as everything to say about them has already been articulated and there are no proper words to describe just how amazing this place is.
this place was pretty good for being vegan.  Not sure if I would be back but if you are Vegan definitely worth checking out.

When a former co-worker told me this place was opening in Berkeley, I knew I had to visit a.s.a.p.  When I actually got here, I ended up gawking at the high price of cinnamon rolls that are quite possibly larger than my stomach, featuring toppings that look like they would lead to an early sugary death.  After much consideration and patience from a kind employee, I settled on a still gigantic, yet cheaper, vegan chocolate chip cookie to split with the boyfriend.  It was a decent experience, but those rolls are just plain scary looking.

**These cinnamon rolls are so good that Cinnaholic is one of the places I immediately think about when I imagine what I'll miss when I move out of the area one day**

I used to love Cinnabon. It was my favorite part of going to the airport- besides getting to go somewhere of course. Now, the notion of Cinnabon... *shiver*. The first time I went to Cinnaholic, I had no idea they were vegan. I just knew they were the best cinnamon rolls I'd had in a long, long time. I've been such a fan that I even sent a dozen of their rolls to a friend on the east coast, as a gift. Fresh and delicious is what these rolls are.

Went in for my free birthday roll. 
I got the old school with almond frosting and strawberries. Noms. The almond frosting was good and flavorful but not too overbearing. The strawberries were fresh. And its free since it was my birthday Cant complain there! 

Service is always really friendly and quick.

I found my new love and its name is Cinnaholic.... I went to Berkeley over the weekend but before doing so, I went yelpin', searching for vegan restaurants and bakeries. Well I came across Cinnaholic and made it my goal to go there. I walked in expecting to see pre-made cinnamon buns and other baked stuff, but didn't see much until looking at the menu and realizing we get to create our own. I asked the employee (who was actually one of the owners) if they had anything vegan, and to my surprise he said "everything is vegan." My eyes lit up (even though i'm not even a vegan myself.) There were so many delicious sounding frosting and topping options, but I kept it simple with original vanilla frosting, fresh bananas, and shredded coconut. This was one of the tastiest things ever! I couldn't believe there was no animal product in it whatsoever. The cinnamon bun was fresh and soft, and even the coconut was so fresh tasting.

When it was time to pay I got a little nervous because I didn't see an atm machine anywhere around the counter, but turned out they use an ipad with a little high tech credit card processor. I even got to sign my signature with my finger. Haha, I just loved it. 

So the sad part about this is that I live an hour and a half away in Sacramento and will not be able to visit my love as much as I would hope. But I now have even more reason to go to Berkeley more often : )

Went to Cinnaholic's today and ordered one of their speciality rolls (smores) and it was soooooooooooooooo amazing!

My sister who is a non-vegan, and lactose intolerant really enjoyed hers as well (speciality peach pie roll)

I never considered myself a fan of cinnamon rolls (even before I was vegan) ... but the rolls at Cinnaholic are yummy enough to make me rethink that.  **Love all the frosting choices** And the brownies are huge and delicious!  

This is definitely the bakery for feminists (since no female animals were exploited for their milk or eggs) and male rights people too (since commonly male chicks can't lay eggs so are suffocated or ground alive, and baby male calves don't produce milk but can be crammed in a hutch and slaughtered prematurely as veal).  Vegan cinnamon rolls & brownies avoid all that nonsense :-D

INCREDIBLE! Cinnaholic is a true gem of Berkeley. I was never much into cinnamon rolls before, but after one trip here I was addicted. Not only are they mind-boggingly delicious, their products are also environmentally friendly and 100% vegan. Kickass places like Cinnaholic make being a vegan in the bay area as easy as eating...well, a cinnamon roll ;)
Haven't had a Cinnamon roll since I became vegan, over three years ago. Not sure how they do it and don't really care......Amazing!! THANK YOU!!

These are honestly the best cinnamon rolls I've ever had.  They're sweet without going overboard and there are so many topping options that you could never get bored.  Having said that, I always end up getting the same thing; almond frosting with chocolate chip cookie dough.  My god, it's heavenly.  I dream about these cinnamon rolls and make special trips to the East Bay for them.

This place has plenty of good reviews and I wholeheartedly agree. I didn't even realize it was a vegan place until we got there. We had a groupon and I'm guilty of indulging myself in cinnabons when I go to the mall, but seeing how this is about 1/3 the calories and 1/2 the fat, I will definitely like coming here whenever I get to come home!

Although it seems to take at least 15 minutes to get your order, it's well worth the wait to get these fresh out of the oven cinnamon buns. I love the smores and oreo flavor, and the rocky road one is also yummy. Old fashioned it just good on its own but my boyfriend got his with berries and it tasted even better. You have plenty of choices for frosting and toppings so there are a bunch of flavors that make this even better than sprinkles and anyone that knows me knows I love cupcakes! 

We went twice during thanksgiving break, and had that for our after dinner dessert. Christmas break will be my next visit =)

A delicious decadent treat that's not for the undecided.  There are so many toppings to choose from the faint of heart can easily be overwhelmed.  So tasty, and a great place for vegans and non-vegans alike. The smell of sweetness & cinnamon circles the block and lures you in. A warm cinnamon roll drizzled in frosting on a cold day is a fantastic treat.

Best cinnamon rolls ever. My favorite roll is the "chocolate chip cookie dough w/ macadamia nut frosting". I've tried their brownie roll & oreo cookie roll, their awesome too. Baby buns are just as awesome, good for sharing.

Since my first review I have become a full blown Cinnaholic addict. I think they needed to work out a few kinks regarding supply and demand. I've been almost every week in the last month and have gotten fresh, hot rolls on each visit. The new expanded hours help out a lot, since I live further east it is much easier to get out there before closing time.

I would love a vegan cream cheese frosting option. The $4 specials of the day are awesome and I've already gotten my free cinnamon roll from the customer loyalty card!
omg is all I can say.

It is like someone read my mind and said: "yes, we will create a restaurant that only serves right-out-of-the-oven, customized, vegan cinnamon rolls."

This place is wonderful, everytime I go there is never a line and they always bake the rolls fresh to order. Get the mocha almond or butter pecan...or any of them!

I also love how they have little soy milks to drink with your roll! I bring vegan and non-vegan friends here often and everyone loves them!

Worth the trip to Berkely - again and again!

I stood in line on opening day to try some more of Cinnaholic's tasty vegan cinnamon rolls.  I was able to try creations such as peanut butter and jelly, banana walnut, cookie dough and more.  I forgot all about the plain cinnamon roll.  I've been back one more time since their grand opening and this time I tried the special of the day, and made my own with banana frosting and fresh raspberries and bananas on top.  I can't say enough about how friendly the entire work staff was and how patient they were with me while trying to decide what flavors I wanted to try.  I'm still amazed at how delicious each bite is, and what amazes me even more is that each roll is completely vegan!  Who would have thought!  I've made a promise to treat myself at least once a month.  In fact, I have a BART trip to Berkeley planned for Friday just to treat myself to another amazing creation by the staff at Cinnaholic.  Thank you

I think you have to be vegan to truly appreciate the cinnamon rolls here OR maybe I should have just gotten the oreo explosion instead of the classic OR maybe I just miss butter, but if your diet does not allow for it, then enjoy.
Pretty Good. I need to try other topings.

Absolutely delicious! My whole non-vegan family loved them. They all thought they were delicious. I wish they had been open when I was at berkeley. I would have been there every morning. Now I live in LA but apparently they ship :)

Cinnaholic is so overwhelming for me! I'm not used to having so many options let alone amazing dessert options! I went in there, stared at the huge variety on the menu and freaked and got a mini bun! The portions are HUGE and you can place tons of items on top of your vinnabon including vegan marshmallows, caramel, fruit, candy, everything!

The worker in there was super nice too. He told me all the best vegan restaurants and chatted about the town for a while. Customers helped me find amazing SF coffee too. This place was really good, friendly, and all vegan! This is a definite spot to hit while in town!
Warm, delicious cinnamon rolls with enough choices of toppings to satisfy any sweet tooth....AND they're vegan! I shared a "S'mores" and it was amazing. Can't wait to try some other flavors!
These rolls just keep gtetting better and better. Thank you Cinnaholic, for turning my frown, upside down!

There really isn't anything wrong with a 3-star review, but for some reason, it hurts me to do this one.  I walked in and ordered two rolls based on photographs on Yelp.

 - Strawberry-Strawberry
 - Maple-Hazelnut

They were fine cinnamon rolls, but really were overly gooed and way too sweet.  However, the girl behind the counter seemed to put in so much love into the rolls as she meticulously measured, mixed, and arranged my frosting and toppings.  It was like a trance that caused me to reach for my wallet and even finding that the smallest bill available was a $5, I still dropped it into the tip jar.

The texture of the roll was not bad at all, but it wasn't amazing.  I'm not sure I'll be back, but I really wanted to like it.

Really, really good. I just got a regular cinnamon roll with caramel frosting. It was delicious. I wish I got into Berkeley more often, but when I do, definitely coming here for a treat! Love all the possible flavor combinations!
My fav: Smores, PBJ & rockyroad!!

Im not usually a cinnamon fan BUT BOY, was this pretty good! I ordered the chocolate chip cookie dough and it was pretty DE. LI. CIOUS. It was pretty darn sweet though but if you have a sweet tooth like me, its not a big deal. 

They have so many great selections I wish I can taste them all! I think I am now a Cinnaholic and I will be back to get my fix soon!

Vegan cinnamon rolls that taste better than most cinnamon rolls, you say? Duh. 

So many flavors! I had the blueberry pie, and it was a dream. I asked for less frosting and sugary topping, and I was given extra fresh blueberries without having to ask (yay!) 

Hubs had the cookie dough, and it made him admit it was damn good (he's not a hippie like me). 

Nice service. Great idea. Love you, Berkeley.

decadent in the best possible way. A true taste sensation! Some of the best treats you will ever have. My only complaint is that sometimes the music is too raucous and loud but otherwise everything else about this place is great.

This place gets a five because I lucked out when I went for the first time and had the pleasure of getting my Cinnamon Roll right out of the oven!! I had the Banana Frosting w/ Gingersnaps pieces and brown sugar crumble..Also an Old Skool Roll...Amazing..I'll keep going back to have as many flavor combinations!!!

YUMMY and Vegan!!!!

Friendly service, yummy additions and creations for us Cinnaholics! Can be a wait since its one or two people working and a line can build up quick. But its delicious!

What I ate: Cinnamon bun with maple glaze topped with fresh strawberries
Visit date: November 27, 2011
First time? I keep coming back for more.

Drool. Cinnaholic is fabulous! Their buns are fluffy perfection. They are consistently delicious and oh so warm when served. I think their buns have gotten smaller (or their containers have gotten bigger!) but they are still enough to fill you and are worth the price. The first time I came, I had just gotten my wisdom teeth yanked out so I enjoyed a bun with double the coffee glaze. Their buns are soft enough that my poor healing mouth was able to bite and chew them. The second time I came, I think I put too much sweet on my bun -- coffee glaze with brownie topping. Still though, the bun was so good; I just took off some of the brownie bits. This third time was definitely the charm. I've officially found my favorite combo (so far at least): maple glaze with fresh strawberries. The same fluffy bun, a sweet (but not too sweet) glaze and succulent strawberries slices.

All my sister could say as she ate her cinnamon bun was "Oh my gosh, this is so good" and variations of that phrase.

This place was a great find on my brief visit to Berkeley. Ah, the warm, doughy, delicious vegan health food. Right. I thought the prices were a bit high but it was so good. Staff was also very friendly and seemed happy. They have compostable containers but one improvement could be the introduction of reusable plates if you're eating at one of their tables outside. Bring your own container.

"I can't believe it's not butter!"  That's what I thought after I finished my amazing coconut topped, hazelnut iced cinnamon roll.  When I stepped in, I was greeted happily by young man.  He let me know that I could ask him any questions, but being my shy self, I couldn't strike up a conversation.  I loved the clean look of the place, and the smell was mouth-watering.  Plus, I think all students get a discount (at least when I showed him my Peralta ID).  These make going vegan just a bit easier!

I work at the Cal Ticket Office and I didn't really have a lunch. I was looking for a quick snack with a half hour between getting off work and going to class about five minutes away.

So I agree to just check this place out and give it a shot. If anything, I too was overwhelmed by the massive display of buns. If there was a whiteboard with suggestions, it would at least help me process what to have for the first time or what seemed like the day's special.

On to the roll...
FOOD: 8/10
It wasn't quite fluffy as cinnamons are generally portrayed on TV and I didn't know it was vegan until after it was long gone and I was scrolling through reviews. But despite being a tad too sweet, I thoroughly enjoyed the bun. I left kind of a hurry but went back to get a fork and a few napkins (good choice in retrospect).

SERVICE: 10/10
The people behind the counter are very nice. Really, there's not much to comment on when I'm in and out of the store in less than a few minutes. Maybe just remind customers of the utensils and napkins prior to a potentially messy dessert?

Overall, I enjoyed myself. I felt like a winner too when they gave me a frequent buyer card. Thanks, Cinnaholic.

I wasn't in the mood for a huge roll, but I was curious to try out this legendary vegan cinnamon roll shop, so I stopped in and got a "baby bun," a two-bite pastry which was the perfect size for impulse sampling. I paid an extra quarter to doll it up with maple frosting and walnuts, and it was the best $1.50 I spent today. 

My fancied-up baby bun was tasty and satisfying. I was surprised by how rich the flavor was, especially since my favorite home recipe is little more than a thinly veiled vector for butter. The bun itself was a good balance of sweet and spice, though the dominant flavors were from the nuts and frosting. This bun is definitely meant to be a palette for the many intriguing topping options, which is where Cinnaholic displays their creativity and where the fun is to be had.

The only factor that makes me unlikely to become a regular is the concept. Truth be told, when I want to customize, I bake my own pastries, and I go to bakeries when I want choices made for me. If I baked less, I might come here more. But I may return for another taste test anyway, to steal ideas!

You know, maybe I am the only one, but the cinnamon rolls were not that good. They were OVER the top sugary and lacked any other flavor. The combination ones (chocolate chip, etc) are WAY too sweet. The cinnamon rolls are not tender and slice like butter (like they should). I won't return.

Vegan cinnamon rolls. Need I say more?

Anyway, I've only been here a handful of times, and each time, the customizable cinnamon rolls are absolutely fresh and amazing. 

Seriously. Go. Now. Take your sweetheart out, or fuck it, take yourself out and treat yourself to an amazing cinnamon roll, that is fresh, and happens to be completely vegan. 

I would give the place 5 stars....But I have qualms with some that work there, and that's as far as I'll go into that.

If the cinnamon rolls weren't so pricy for cinnamon rolls, I would be coming here much much more often!! It is perfect for anyone who has a sweet tooth and loves cinnamon as much as I do. They have fresh toppings, and you can choose whatever you want to put on it.  Also, they have different flavors for icing! I got blackberry icing with blackberry toppings and it was delicious!

I got two specialty cinnamon rolls (mocha almond and banana) with the Groupon I bought.  The service was friendly and quick, and the rolls (which I got to-go) were verrrry sweet.  Maybe it would have tasted better if I had eaten them right away instead of hours later, in which case... my bad.

Don't let the word vegan scare you off.  Let it motivate you to drop what you're doing right now and rush down to this place.  Simply the best and most amazing cinnamon roll (with maple frosting and blueberries) that I have ever had.

Oh my god, they're vegan?? You would honestly NEVER know that these hot, delicious melting buns of glee lack eggs and dairy! I've seen pictures of vegan cinnamon rolls online and they always look like pieces of inedible cardboard speckled with bird seed, and to be honest, if I would have known the place was vegan, I was have steered clear. However, you look at these buns and they look fantastic! On top of that, you can create your own combo, choose your own icing and toppings, and ours came straight from the oven. We decided on the original bun with butter pecan frosting and it was warm, ooey, gooey, deliciousness.

I heard about Cinnaholic from some of my vegan buddies and was so excited to try it! After going out to dinner and a movie with my boyfriend we stopped by for desert and I just could not decided on a flavor because there were so many! After starring at the different flavors and toppings for 5 minutes I just decided to get 4 mini ones with whatever flavors and toppings I looked at first. I ended up getting a cream soda flavored frosting with strawberries, caramel flavored frosting with cookie dough, coffee flavored frosting with brownies, and a pumpkin spice frosting with some more pumpkin spice on top, and my boyfriend got a big cinnamon roll with peanut butter and bananas. They were sooooooooooo gooooood! The gentleman who served us was really nice and helpful as well. I will definitely come back whenever I get the chance!

A friend had told me about this place as she now works and lives in Berkeley.  I went last week and was truly amazed.  The cinnamon roll itself was warm and fresh and cinnamon-y.  Heavenly.  Much better than a Cinnabon Diabetes Treat for sure and the price was very good.

I got one with root beer icing and marshmallows while my friend got one with chocolate all over it.  I didn't try his but it looked delicious and he finished it in minutes so I'd say that's good.  Mine didn't quite taste like root beer but it was so good that I didn't even care.  I want to go back and try out their other options now because they have quite the variety.  S'mores will be next for sure.

It's also incredibly easy to get to from the Downtown Berkeley BART Station which is a huge plus.

Pros: The best fresh-baked, customizable cinnamon bun I've ever had anywhere. Friendly service. Everything they sell is vegan, though you wouldn't have known unless someone told you.

Cons: Decor is sterile for my taste. Venue is very small. Coffee, though available, is not  listed on overhead menu.

Good stuff. 

After dinner at Herbivore, the roomie and I hopped over here for a quick dessert.

I first heard about them from Groupon, then from The Vegan Zombie. And they looked so good, with such a variety of flavors. 

I got the Apple pie specialty roll and my friend got the old school roll. They were awesome! The ONLY thing off was the weird taste from the bread. Almost a yeasty flavor...perhaps from whatever egg replacer they use?Idk. But still effing delicious. 

Yes, Id say a regular cinnamon roll tastes better, but these are mo' bettah cause they are made well, by people who are doing GOOD. (for the earth ;) )

I am so glad I live 45 minutes away from this place, or I might decide to visit a bit too frequently!  For the benefit of my waistline and my wallet, this place has reserved a spot on my "special treat" list. 
It's so nice to be able to walk in to a bakery of any kind and be able to order straight off the menu without making certain the items are vegan.  Add that sense of ease to a menu of crazy toppings and delicious frosting flavors, and I am a huge fan!
The rolls are quite good and not overly sweet even when topped with things like maple frosting, chocolate chips and pecans.  The customization is nice, but kind overwhelming to make a decision.  I think next time I will go in with a plan or stick with the tried-and-true vanilla.  It looks delicious!

Cinnaholic - a little slice of vegan heaven. The rolls are always delicious and you can go there 100 times and get a different frosting/topping combo each time. The specialty rolls are also very good. I usually get the daily special for 4 bucks. Make sure you get a punch card for a free roll!

My favorite is a cinnamon roll with cookie dough chunks! Sooo freaking delicious and I definitely would come back to this place! 

The guy who helped me was really helpful and friendly.

I love how you can customize your own cinnamon roll too :)

This place is amazing!! The cinnamon rolls are soooooo good!! I like that they are healthier than the other cinnamon rolls sold at other places, doesn't make me feel so guilty! 

I tried the classic roll with vanilla frosting and almond topping. My boyfriend tried it with the banana frosting and both were delicious! 

For those that rated this place 3 stars because they said these cinnamon rolls are too sweet...uh hello!?!? they are cinnamon rolls! they are suppose to be sweet! If you don't want it so sweet then don't get a sweet topping! stick with the classic. 

The people are nice too, very friendly! I would definitely recommend this place to anyone with a sweet tooth and that are calorie conscious!
Great (nearly overwhelming) selection of frostings and toppings.  And their daily specials keep me coming back with combinations I would never come up with.  And this is coming from a non-vegan.
Straight up delicious, and you wouldn't even know they're vegan. They freeze great too.

Stay away if you know what's good for you. ;) This place could be dangerous. I could do some damage in here for sure. The cinnamon roll is real good as is the brownie. You wouldn't believe it was vegan. Hella expensive though.

Delicious. And stick with old school....mucking it up with all the other options just kind of makes it a vegan Fenton's...and we really don't need that, now do we? 

I've been here before but this time had a Groupon, and after ordering two rolls, the very nice server-dude let us know there was extra $$ from our $10 Groupon, so we got a caramel flavored frosting shot to just check it out. Gotta say....wouldn't choose flavored frosting again. Just didn't seem right...nor did it blow me away. It just kinda tasted like what it was - added flavor droplets in the regular frosting.

The biggest problem here is that my 11-year-old daughter and I agreed that we really only need to come here once a year....it's that decadent. And she's a sweet-a-holic (now, where'd she get THAT from?)

Not too many five stars given on my first visit, Cinnaholic is worth all five! Simple menu, cinnamon rolls, not so simple is the toppings. We tried the banana cinnamon roll, brownie cinnamon roll and chocolate chip cookie dough cinnamon roll. 
I wasn't going to eat the whole thing, couldn't stop. Make this a must on your list, and it is all vegan!
Cinna-licious! They have picture updates to twitter and Instagram to put that daily craving-something-tasty feeling into overdrive.
Love this place.  Mmm almond icing with berries on top.

Vegan or not, these rolls are pretty tasty and worth a try if you're in the area. Got the original and Oreo with a price tag of $9.25. Kinda pricey for 2 pastries but at least I can cross another bookmark off my list.

I can't believe they're vegan. These are so good: a full dose of gooey, sweet-but-not-artificial, fluffy, delicious yummyness. I didn't think I could eat that much frosting (I had an old-fashioned) but ended up licking my fingers. Even my vegan-food-hating sweetie was convinced.

The only thing they need now is take-in trays for work... you know, the kind you can bring to meetings. Slightly smaller buns in a 12 pack, with frosting on the side maybe? So you can pass them around and people can take them without sticky fingers... we could create a whole new world of happy workers.

I seriously hate going to and being in Berkeley.  Always have probably always will.  

But...seeing as I was in El Cerrito one Saturday afternoon I decided to venture over to try Cinnaholic.  The pictures looked so good on the website and I'm always looking for vegan dessert options.

There are soooo many toppings and sauces to choose from.  I couldn't even begin to decide, so I had a specialty roll instead.

My Smores cinnamon roll was heavy and warm.  Not to sweet or heavy and quite large.

The counter person was really cool and helpful and parking wasn't a problem on a Saturday afternoon.

Great service, and a great vegan treat when I feel like veggin' out. Certainly doesn't taste like "health food", which explains why it's a tad pricey.

3 Stars for Food + 1 Star for the Misfits Posters
Have a "hybrid moment" at Cinnaholic, yo.

Once you walk in the store, it is as if your nose went to heaven.

Their rolls are pretty delicious, though it was a little sweet for me (my sweet tooth is not as intense a others, personal taste :p) I had the irish creme w/ hazelnuts. The outer part of the roll was nice and crunchy which is not like traditional cinnamon rolls but I personally love crunchy.

The only thing I didn't like about Cinnaholic is the price. With the Cal student discount, the most most basic roll (the "old skool" or something) is 3.50. Anything remotely fancier is 4-5 ish. As a student, that's a bit too much for a cinnamon roll. I suppose it is a more "premium" dessert because it is vegan, but I'm not vegan so it doesn't matter to me.
best cinnamon rolls ever.. we had smores, choc chip, and apple pie. i wish they'd have one in sf.. :)

The cinnamon buns are big. There are a lot of different flavors and toppings, it's pretty hard to decide on one order. Though when you get your order, the toppings are actually pretty small. I ordered strawberry topping and ended up with only 2-3 tiny pieces of strawberry.

The cinnamon bun itself is soft on the inside, crispy on the outside, and very strong in cinnamon flavor. With icing on top it's a bit on the sweet side, so I got tired of the taste fairly quickly.

Overall a very good place for dessert and hang out, better than your typical cinnamon bun for sure.

I love this place! I don't want to repeat what all the other 5 star reviews have said, but I do want to let people know that if you don't like a lot of frosting, simply ask to have it light. This is what we always do (heck, we're vegans in our forties), and the staff is so obliging. They always show it to us and ask if it looks right. So whether you like lots of gooey frosting or just a little, and whether you're vegan or not, check this place out!

Cinnaholic may well be the best reason to visit Berkeley. Don't get your bun to go; eat it right there so it's warm and gooey from the oven. Get the caramel or coffee frosting, top it with fruit and/or brownies. If this doesn't make you swoon you are a hopeless nihilist who doesn't like food. 

A lot of people complain about the price, but they sell huge vegan chocolate chip cookies for only $2 a piece, and they're moist and chewy and chock-full of chocolate chips. Mmmm...

shockingly enough, this place is vegan. i didn't know that such a place could be vegan-friendly, but i should know better; it's berkeley.

they have pretty much every topping you can imagine, and there's nothing better than digging into the freshly topped, heated rolls. i like to get the frosting shots, which are exactly what they sound like. 

my favorite frosting is the maple one, but i've had others too and liked them (i have been here on several occasions. it's quite an indulgence). also, get your roll with oreos!!!

I went with three friends, we each got something different and found everything very delicious.  The one semi criticism is that we found the peanut butter frosting to overpower the flavors of the brownie topping.

Who ever thought vegan cinnamon rolls could taste so good?!

I tried the cookie dough specialty roll and man was it delicious! After I tried it I just kept craving it day after day until I dragged my friend back there with me to get another one. The rolls are really moist and soft and the frosting isn't too heavy, though it is really sweet. 

Only downside? $5 for specialty rolls. A bit pricey for the average poor college student :(

Cinnamon rolls get a bad rap, simply because there are so many awful ones out there. It's gotten to the point where comedians like Louis CK are sickened at the sight of the things, ashamed to be even seen eating one.

These people haven't had a cinnamon roll at Cinnaholic. Made fresh to order and coming out extremely soft, this shop definitely has the ma-and-pa look down, albeit one that's a lot more trendy. The toppings are all over the map too, ranging from coffee syrup to candy cane bits. Rolls come out to about $5 a pop, which is about on par with Ici's and the other sweet shops of the world.

Still, it's a cinnamon bun. You'll enjoy every bite, but be ready to have the sugar high/crash of your life.

All vegan cinnamon rolls with a huge variety of toppings and flavored frostings. I had a regular roll with almond frosting. So yummy. Just Yum! Definitely coming back. Which is good because they have a stamp card so you can earn a free roll. Parking was kind of annoying because it's so close to campus. Definitely recommend this place!

This place is awesome!!! My friend took me here for a sweet breakfast treat yesterday! I must say, this place is truly 5 stars. In reading previous reviews, everyone kept complaining about the price, but in my opinion the price is right on, for location, and for a non-corporate theme 4-5 dollars is dead on market price. You can not compare Cinnabon to this place. Cinnabon is a place where everything is processed and ordered in large quantities. This locally owned shop not only bakes everything fresh, the owner hand picks all the ingredients himself.
It was love at first bite. This is the best cinnamon roll I have ever had. Every bite was mouth watering and delicious. I love you Cinnaholic. See you in The City some day!
Been here once, definitely going back!!! I had the smores cinnabon, sooo yummy!!!

FRESH BAKED MADE TO ORDER!!!!!!!!!! I HAD GOT A BUNCH FOR THE OFFICE AND IT WAS A HIT!!!!!!!! They are pretty good and moist. My fav was the blueberry cheesecake. Try them you will never look at cinnamon rolls the SAME!

I love being able to customize things, especially food! Cinnaholic is trendy and innovative. Being able to pick the flavor frosting and the toppings in your cinnamon roll enhances the experience! This place definitely goes a step further than cinnabon.

I got a cinnamon roll with almond frosting and blueberry topping. The blueberry is fresh and the cinnamon roll was warm so the room temperature frosting melted a bit on it. I wish the cinnamon roll was warmer because I like my frosting to be sticky and almost liquidy.

The cinnamon roll itself is really fluffy! Service was also good and they let me sample different frosting flavors (which was really helpful because I'm so indecisive)!

Some extra perks... this place is vegan and if you show your student ID (doesn't have to be a berkeley one) you can get a discount!

I finally made it here as a pretty new vegan and my review is sort of mixed.  LOVED the roll.  Liked the frosting - when it was hot.  As it cooled, it had kind of a metallic taste to me.  (I got the vanilla frosting with apples on top.)  Now I've never been a huge sweets person so maybe next time I'll just ask for light frosting becuase I really did love the basic roll.  And the price was great for the size.

The smores rolls are my favorite, but you can't go wrong with an old skool roll! They're fresh and amazing and keep on the counter for a day or so (microwave them for 30 seconds if they're cold!), if they survive that long.

This is one of my top five favorite bay area businesses. I'm vegan but even if I wasn't, I'd keep coming back to this place for cinnamon rolls. They're amazing.

PS: if you're ever in a pinch for vegan marshmallows, they sell Dandies!

Amazing!
This should be the standard for any place with baked goods (whether it's rolls, cakes, doughnuts).

I first tasted these when I spotted them for sale at a Vegan Bakesale in SF.  After that--- I was hooked.

What makes this place great is having the choice of any frosting and any topping.... peach, pumpkin, lemon, maple, chocolate, butterscotch, blueberry frosting, etc... etc... topped with freshly sliced peaches, strawberries or Oreo cookies.  And even better, its Vegan and made-to-order.

The staff is great too!

I don't live in Berkeley but it's worth the drive over the bridge and then some.

Cinnamon rolls at their best...and i'm speaking as a carb hater. 

I actually found out that the rolls were vegan after i had it, so even more props (: You should always do your own toppings even though they have premade ones for you. I told the cashier that i want something coffee-ey and she told me to get coffee frosting (yes you get to choose your own frosting) and i put hazelnut and chocolate chips on it. I would actually suggest NOT to get over 2 toppings, these buns have so many flavors to them already that you might get tired of the sweetness real fast if you have too much going on. The duration of 10 minutes i was there, i've heard people just ordering the originial cinnonmon rolls, and i can see why 'cause they are really soft and the vanilla frosting is just right. 

Will definitely go back and try fruity toppings (:!

You will forget about these rolls being vegan the second you take a bite. Get the original or coffee frosting with oreos and Dandies and/or cookie dough. Someday I'm going to be more adventurous with my topping choices, but I'm comfortable with routine when it tastes this good.

The staff are all super friendly. We even got ourselves a free roll because the baker accidentally drizzled it with chocolate chips to the original customer's dismay (heathen).

I'm hoping they'll start to make gluten-free rolls so I can take my mom here someday!

I brought three dozen with various frostings and toppings to my non-veg*an co-workers this morning and they loved them.  And though I had heard and read about Cinnaholic's buns for a long time, this was the first time I tried them myself.  Excellent!  What's more, the service was fantastic, extra effort was made to have them be ready for pick up as soon as the store opened.  Thanks, Justin and the rest of the Cinnaholic crew.

I was impressed!

my cousin works near this spot and have ranted on how good it was. I thought it was just any other cinnabon type of shop, like the ones at the mall? 

Anyways, she took me here after having a lunch/dinner. 
so their menu was wow! think of it like a coldstone for cinnabons! There were so many to choose from, from toppings to frostings and etc.! They had their own classics such as rocky road. 

Very hard to choose... so i decided to make my own. I had a regular cinnabon topped with brownie and cookie dough!---SOOOO GOOD!

get this, it is VEGAN!--say to be a healthy type of cinnabon..minus my toppings of course lol!

IT WAS SOOO GOOD! glad someone took the idea of make your own healthy cinnabon!

also, i was able to use my groupon! the staff was nice! i think one of them was the owner?

Oh. My. Gosh. I cannot explain the joy I felt this morning. 

First of all, I've been DYING to go here for a 'lil sumpin' scrumptious for months. Let me make this clear, I've been looking for an excuse just to drive there for a three dollar pastry. I live in Sacramento, call me crazy but yes it was worth it. 

So, walking in I saw they had posters of Johnny Cash, and a cut little display case showing some of the creations of cinnamon buns. And then I saw the giant chalk menu board which I couldn't even comprehend since it was too early in the day and I still hadn't recovered from the night before. BUT, next time I want to taste EVERYTHING THEY HAVE. Yes, I do need to use caps to emphasize this because after eating the daily special I wanted to buy a dozen more in all different flavors and greedily stash them in my freezer. It was that good.
