Back before they remodeled, I came here a couple times. In terms of Korean food, I think this place is the second best near the Berkeley campus, after Koryo. Their spicy chicken plate is quite good, which comes with an okay salad and plenty of rice.

However, I have to give them two stars simply because the cashier told me that they take credit card, then proceeded to charge me 75 cents extra without telling me. First off, that's illegal. Second, you should at least tell me about it if you're going to charge me.

Typical watered down Korean food catering to a clientele that clearly doesn't give a damn. The Mexicans are the only people cooking these days. Ramen was mediocre. I always get the spicy chicken kimchi fried rice but I wouldn't recommend it really. It's just good to get when you are in a hurry.

If you're feeling cold, always consider bulgogi at Gomnaru as a wholesome and filling meal, especially in winter. They serve you the dish steaming hot and bubbling, so it really is quite awesome to have when you can't feel your face and fingers. And they are courteous:  the owner, a middle aged man, serves you like no other. He replaced my friends soup free of charge because it was too spicy. Lunch specials are very reasonably priced. And best of all, unlimited rice!

I've only ever ordered two items from this place: the spicy BBQ chicken and the soft tofu soup. 

The spicy BBQ chicken is absolutely delicious!!! The flavor is yum yum yum! However, the rice varies, often times it's too dry. 

The soft tofu soup on the other hand....was very very bland. It was pretty much just a bowl of slightly salty water with bits of tofu and other ingredients floating around. 

I give it 4 stars solely for their spicy BBQ chicken dish. I can't really comment on the other food items. The owners are nice, though.

I think many people hate this place not because of its food taste but its relative expensive price among restaurants in this north side food court. However I do admit that some of their dishes do not taste that great with its price; however, if you have their daily specials for dinner, it's worth it. I always order their Yoo Gae Jang and I like the owner to make that dish (if you have someone else making it, it might not taste as good as it should be). Also this place had changed its owner since winter of 2010. The old Gomnaru was really bad but I think the new one is pretty good, considering this is the only restaurant I will go in "north side asian ghetto"

*Spicy barbeque chicken* -- it's an addiction.  I like the southside Gomnaru on Durant better than the one on Hearst.  Comes on a bed of rice with forgettable miso soup and a deep fried slice of potato.  This is a great place to come for lunch; the monster television in the background is oddly soothing.
The food was okay, but nothing to make me want to come back. The food came out one dish at a time, which is very annoying when you are sitting with six persons. The service was friendly, though.

after being disappointed by the majority of the restaurants in the asian ghetto on durant, i was pleasantly surprised by the food at gomnaru. really excellent value. inexepensive, generous portions, flavorful food, great selection and personable staff.  

i ordered the spicy bbq chicken with kimchi fried rice. for about $5 or $6 i received several chicken fillets and a serving of kimchi fried rice that comprised of half of my plate. the meal also came with an order of miso soup and self-serve kimchi, which wasn't the best quality (the kimchi in the fried rice was far better) but it was a nice accompaniment for my meal. i had more than enough food for two meals, and enjoyed my leftovers the next day.
Spicy chicken... Good size portion. No kimchi :(

Definitely Americanized (lettuce in bibimbap??), but still pretty good fast food. A little on the expensive side in my opinion, because I think you could get better Korean fast food that's more authentic at Bear Ramen in Southside Asian Ghetto.

Today I had the BBQ Chicken with Kimchi Fried Rice, and the chicken was really good, but the fried rice was SWIMMING in oil. I couldn't finish it...it wasn't bad but Bear Ramen's kimchi fried rice w/ spam is much better. Oh yeah, my dish also came with a fried tempura potato. That was surprising...but it was good (and very oily...are we seeing a theme here?).

My friend had the japchae (fried noodles), which was pretty oily but was really good. It comes over rice. And my other friend had the bibimbap, and like I said...it had lettuce in it?! It was okay, but I'm REALLY picky about bibimbap and only like the dolsot bibimbap at Sura.

How do you screw up delicious Korean Short Ribs (Kal Bi) and Bulgogi?! Basically, marinate the meat and grill it! I do it all the time at Palace BBQ in Cupertino, CA (excellent place). When my friend and I went there, both our meat dishes were as dry as a desert. Mine had so much vein and fat that I was unable to chew through the rubbery mess. Also, the waitress never served us water so that we could use to wash away the weird taste of their meat. I don't know what kind of sauce they use, but it may not be legal in the U.S. Please save yourself $13 and your appetite and never come here.
Oh my! This place has gone downhill since 2003 when it was at least okay. The spicy chicken plate is still okay. Be forewarned about everything else.

Ghal-bi (short ribs) plate was too fatty and the overall flavor was unsatisfactory.  Portions are good, but then again the price ain't exactly a bargain.  Steve's on the Southside is marginally better, but for real Korean food, go to New Korea House on 1620 Post St. in San Francisco.
The one on southside is much better.  This one is not very reliable.

Ever since I discovered this place my freshman year, I've eaten here every chance I've gotten. Their spicy bbq chicken is a simple dish, but oh so delicious. Sure it's just chicken on top of rice with a small side of lettuce, but you get a deep fried piece of potato and a bowl of miso soup if you elect to eat in. For the adventurous type, you can upgrade to kimchi fried rice, but it's just extra sodium and cabbage IMO. If you go during the busy hours, they cook the chicken fresh, but if you're eating in the in-between hours, expect your food to be microwaved/reheated in some fashion.

The best Korean place I've been to so far in Berkeley.  The side dishes are good (includes japchae!), much better than Toust where one of them was canned corn... I came here for dinner and had the spicy chicken.  It was served on sizzling stoneware and the seasoning was perfect.  My friends thought their food was too spicy though so maybe it's just me.  The waitress was very nice, and the setting was clean and cozy (they play SBS on the TV!)
Gone way downhill with new owners. Everything is bland, miso soup has nothing in common with any miso soup I've had. Looks and tastes like dirty water.  Cheap korean pre-ccooked fast food..

I lived on Northside as a Cal undergrad for 4 years, and I have to say that the most memorable comfort meal I've ever had was Gomnaru's spicy pork. Whenever I had a craving for meat--and lots of it--the spicy pork was always there to satisfy. What's more, the spicy pork is almost always prepared very quickly, and Gomnaru packs you more than you (should) eat in one sitting. Consequently, the $5 Spicy Pork dinner often became the $5 dinner+late night or $5 dinner+next day's lunch.

Prices have gone up recently about half a buck, but you still get heaps of rice (I've taken spare rice home more than once to use in other meals), that crazy piece of tempura, and some decent kim chee. In theory the soup is only for dine-in, but if you ask nicely, you can sip on it while you wait for take-out.

The BBQ chicken is decent, but a bit dry sometimes...stick with the pork. Keep in mind they don't take credit but will do your debit card with some silly fee.

Parking is terrible except at night or on weekends...this is mostly student fare.

Edit: Went to this place yesterday afternoon, new guy at the counter, they removed some stuff, and some new signs. Most importantly, the spicy pork tasted really old. In addition, I ended up spending nearly 9 bucks there, when you count the Arizona tea (marked on can as 99 cents, owner charged me more than that) and the 50 cent fee for using my Visa credit card. The dining room was depressingly dark, the potato was soggy instead of crispy, and the pork was boring. The kimchi had gone from freshly placed-on-plate to a communal kimchi tub placed next to the utensils. All in all, Gomnaru has gone from a 5* to a 2.5*, and I'm rounding down.

Compared to Steve's on the "south side Asian ghetto" this place would get 5 stars.  I will have to agree with certain people in that the portions are not so great... I do have a hearty appetite and sometimes it just doesn't cut it.  Ive tried the spicy chicken plate from Gomnaru.  Chicken portion wasn't so great, but it was tasty, somewhat spicy, and moist. I've also had the tofu pot here and I think its the only one they serve.  The tofu was good, but just like everything else it lacked much tofu in it.

Although I've had much better Korean food in Irvine, Gomnaru is one of the better Korean restaurants in Berkeley. It's right across the street from the north side of the UC Berkeley campus, convenient to eat at between classes or just to walk to if you live on North Side.

All of the dishes are excellent, and I have to note that the side dishes that come with the meal are my favorite! Every time I go to Gomnaru they have a different assortment of sides (which are always delicious) so meals never get boring.

Recently they added more items to their lunch menu (there's a bigger selection for lunch than dinner, so it's a great place for lunch). Pricewise it's not too bad, and definitely worth your money (between $8-15 per meal for one person). I love their stone pot bibimbap and their Korean BBQ wrap (this one is only served at lunch), which is like a tortilla with noodles, bulgogi, rice, and some veggies. I also recommend the spicy chicken and spicy pork. For cold days try the soups or ramen!

The thing I love the most about Gomnaru is their tea! Their barley tea has such an addictive flavor! The tea is complimentary with a meal and I can't help but go for another refill since it balances out the meal so well.

Unfortunately the south-side Gomnaru has been replaced by Kimchee Garden, so only north-side has Gomnaru now.

The portions are great here for the BBQ chicken and the pork plates. I recommend getting the BBQ chicken spicy otherwise the straight up-grilled version is a little bland. The spicy version isn't very spicy either, but adds good flavor.

Nothing particularly tastes Korean here except for the kimchee based flavors, but it does taste reasonably good for the price. You get whatever meat, rice, salad, kimchee, and a little fried potato for their plates. Consistent the times I've been here so no complaints. It's college food so don't expect crazy good stuff.

I recommend 'Gal-bee' and 'Gal bee tang'
All so good.

my friends ate 'beef bi bim bab' and 'bbq chicken'  and they were also yummy, too.

I ate here a long time ago so I don't exactly remember what I ordered, but it was something along the lines of beef and veggies. They have huge portions would could easily have lasted me 2 meals. The price is moderate, I think I paid around $9. For next time, i think i'll order the meat only and rice combo since I wasnt so fond of the bean sprouts.
The spicy chicken is freakin amazing and the portion is great. Comes with rice, soup, and salad as well all for 6$. Great deal.

I noticed that this restaurant got a complete makeover recently and their tables, chairs, and menu have been completely replaced with nicer looking materials. I came here twice to have their Bi Bim Bap before the new management and their beef platter after the new management took over, and both items were not that memorable. The nicer new look can be deceiving.

Gomnaru gives you decent Korean BBQ and they give you more than any other Korean place I've seen. Lots of chicken, potato and self-serve kim-chi. It's at least a $1 or $2 cheaper than any other Korean place nearby. 

The only problem is that they pre-make all the BBQ at one time, so if you get in at a bad time you get cold chicken, which is lame.

Do not get the ramen, one time I saw that all they were doing was taking one of those korean pre-packaged packets that cost like $2 at local asian supermarkets. 

The mainly rely on students buying food, so they are closed during the summer/winter breaks for the campus.

Compared to the rest of the "asian" food in this area... how could I not give this a 5-star? =P They have changed their food presentation a bit, with the sizzling plate, but it's still a good amount of meat (maybe a little less than before, but oh well?) and it's too bad that there's no more miso soup and salad... I kinda liked the way they did it before. But I will accept the more korean-ized korean food, haha, the kong na mul is yum, but kim chi I will not touch.

Spicy chicken is great. I recommend it, with spicy pork coming in second. As for the soon du bu, it's aiite. Nice to watch TV while eating too! Although who picks the channels? *grumbles...*

This cold weather makes me crave soup. I was on northside and I figured. Why not get some tofu soup! I had a meeting in 20 minutes so I couldnt dine in which made me sad because I was thinking of all the side dishes I would miss out on. Wah. 

After I got my order, I was pleasantly surprised to find the side dishes in its own container, separated by foil so the sauces dont mix! YAY! 

I got the Kim Chi Soft Tofu Soup and the portion was HUGE. I could not finish the soup and can make a meal out of what is left over if I made some more rice.  YAY!!!

The only NAY out of this meal was that the tofu soup was too oily in a it-stained-my-white-spoon kind of way. :( Wah. If it wasnt for this, I would have given Gomnaru 4 stars.

I used to think this place was great. But, then again, I also would make fun of my Korean-American girlfriend for the food she ate. Then, finally, she made me eat real korean food. Wow. My mind was totally blown. Sudobu, kalbi, pan-chan, whatever - it's all awesome. 

But, gomnaru, sadly, my new discovery of what real korean food tastes like has opened my eyes to your mediocre ways. You may provide me with huge amounts of cheap food (esp. the chicken & kimchi fried rice), but you're quality and flavor could satisfy me again.

Also, don't get the soup. It's really not good. Like some kind of chicken broth with potato starch to thicken it. Eww.

The food is okay for the price. 

There is a definite Korean vibe about this place, as it blasts Korean music while you eat. 

If you're ever on the north side of campus, gomnaru is not a bad choice for cheap lunch!

I had the three item lunch special. 
--spicy pork (interesting flavor, not traditional though, seems like a fusion)
--bqq and spicy chicken -- bbq ckn was blah, the spicy chicken was interesting and surprisingly very spicy
-- butternut squash chicken stew: was very flavorful and very spicy as well.

For $7.50ish, I would recommend you give it a shot, not an everyday eatery though. 

Interior is very cozy.

Good food and really affordable prices. They've raised the prices a little and cut down on the portions, but it's still a solid choice any day of the week.

Nothing beats a nice hot tofu soup when it's raining and cold outside.

(trying out Yale romanization cuz yelp still only allows latin characters)

Looking for a place to live in the city, and staying with the in-laws.  It was pretty trying, and I was exhausted.  Asked the interwebs for the closest korean restaurant, and here we go to gomnaru.

The owner & cook were both really pleasant.  The teevee was playing some korean variety show.  The whole thing made me really wanna be in 'pwusan' (where at least I know how to find an apartment....)  i asked them to make me 'toincang ccikay', and they said they would.

came out, looked good, had 'cokay' in it.  Sadly tho, the food tasted just like the only korean restaurant in Nuremberg.  I'm starting to think that korean restaurateurs try to americanize their food by replacing 'myelchi' and 'ces' with salt and chicken stock.

i mean, i gobbled it down, but i'm not sure i'm gonna go back.  i wonder if there's something here that doesn't just taste salty.

The spicy BBQ chicken plate is very good here.  It's really cheap ($5) and has a lot of meat. Everything else is fairly decent, but I really don't see a reason to come here and not order the BBQ chicken. Plus, I really prefer Berkel Berkel for bibimbob anyways. I also like to come here since it is fairly quiet compared to the asian ghetto.

Overall, you could do much worse for $5 in Berkeley.

I got a three item combo to go and it was a hot mess, literally. I got the doppoki (hot rice cake), spicy chicken stew, and the fish cake soup. When I opened up the box of food...it was just a red saucy mess. 

The doppoki and spicy chicken stew were a big let down. The flavor was really bland and the chicken was super dry. The sauce for both of them was watery and wasn't even very spicy. 

The fish cake soup was better, but wasn't good enough for me to really want it again. The broth was flavorful and light as were the fish cakes themselves, but I've definitely still had better. 

I don't understand how so many people flock here for lunch all the time. Just because you're a college student, it doesn't mean you can't get quality food. For sure, the food here is cheap...but even still, I won't be coming back.
Way better than freaking Steve's not Korean BBQ. The combo bbq plate for lunch is about $6.50 and gets you beef, chicken AND pork ... the best korean within walking distance of campus hands down.

I reeally wish this place were better, because I live and work so close!  The food is just ok, but is always ridiculously salty, which I really can't stand when I'm guzzling gallons of water hours afterward.  I've had some really good meals and other meals that weren't satisfying in flavor.

I'll go back cuz it's there and it's ok, but not something to go out of the way for.

I used to eat here every other day for lunch during my college years.  Bring back memories of BBQ chicken and spicy chicken, I still remember the days when you got couple pennies back from a Lincoln.  The fried potato pieces, the tender chicken, the crispy salad all danced in my mouth while I sit in the back of the lecture hall.  At the same while having classmates stare at me lustfully, hoping I will spare a small portion of my treasure.

However, the cooking went downhill ever since they try to open another one on southside of campus, probably cuz lack of concentration of the cooks, or change of management.

Now, the southside Gomnaru went out of business, while the northside one recovered slightly back to the glory of olden days.  I do try to relive my college days thru the cooking, but its now slightly off.  I guess it still gets 4 stars for nostalgic's sake.

I came here hungry so despite the fact it is cheap, I found that the portions were small. I ordered the spicy pork and potstickers. The pork was spicy but the rice helps kick it down a notch. The potstickers were just ok. They had a few tables inside which is where we sat. Outside was crazy busy. So if you want a table, come early or plan on table crashing with a stranger.

It is a rare occasion that I don't finish mine, and my girlfriend's meal. The food was horrible! I ended up leaving half of my bi bim bap, and didn't even attempt to eat any of my girlfriend's wrap. I don't know a lot about Korean cuisine, but my meal had some kind of twig and leaf paste...I am assuming it's some kind of North Korean delicacy.

2.5

Came here for lunch. I got my food 2 minutes after I ordered it. That either means it was someone's old order or everything was pre-made.   I would forgive them if the food was good, but it was so plain, I regretted walking up the hill to get this.  Save your money and walk across campus to the other Gomnaru. The food tastes better and it's fresh.

Still a good option for lunch on the weekdays, but food quality is inconsistent. The combo lunch boxes are pretty good value and you can get a good meal with a good variety. The chapchae, fish cake soup, vegetable curry, spicy chicken, and spicy pork are all good options. 

During dinner and the weekends they offer waiter service, but service can be quite sporadic when the owners are not there.

3.5 stars.  Have gotten the BBQ chicken plate  twice.  Chicken was a little dry both times.  The first time it was topped off with a sauce which was nice, no sauce the second time so it lacked flavor.  Price is okay, but please ditch the styrofoam containers!

Gomnaru fed me 1-2 times a week 3 years at Berkeley.  The complex that it's in probably provided half my meals.  They have relatively inexpensive meals, large portions, friendly service, and everything is good!  I think I had their spicy chicken almost every time.

Tucked in a small corner of the food court, I was attracted to it by the Yelp sticker,  Service was ok and since I ate at the table outside, I didn't get much help besides my food being served.  I do like the fact that customers can use a big coke cup and refill hot tea as much as we'd like.  Tried the Bul Go Kee lunch set, the beef came in a bowl with onions and pepper, it was ok but for $10, I was hoping for a little better.

Excuse me, I don't mean to be rude, but I'm ****ing you up.   

What happened to thus memorable place,  if you are gonna switch owners and change the menu why don't they rename the restaurant?

This place used to serve this unique thinly sliced spicy chicken that was so tender and juicy. Not to mention it was five bucks.  This was five year ago.  

I understand if the prices went up to like, 7-8 bux, which is still 40% ish increase.  No. That's too low. Now it's almost 11 bucks if u tip. 

11 bucks for what?  For garbage served on a hot plate. the chicken was thick, dry, and painfully spicy.  It wasn't a tasty spicy like spicy cheetos.  It was like eating paper with sriracha sauce. 

I give them one star because the staff were nice. But clueless.   

Sorry, please rename this restaurant.

The 2 item lunch is by far the fastest food to be served in the NorthSide Asian Ghetto area. There is plenty of food and it comes with miso and kimchi. I ordered the bbq chicken and korean noodles and it took less than 5 minutes. The food quality is fresh and the service is excellent.

TLDR; Fast service and good food.

When I want to get filled up and only have $5 in my pocket then I stroll out of my lab and into Gomnaru. The bbq chicken is plentiful and very tasty, but man does it stick to my stomach! I have to make sure I don't need to bike home or do anything productive after eating here. I think they've opened a location on the Southside too.

I've never been here before the new management but i come here all the time now even though its a little inconvenient for me. I love their bi bim bap because its a healthy enjoyable meal, the spicy pork with salad is delicious! And the soft tofu soup is a great boiling hot clay pot dish for a rainy day. The prices are pretty average and reasonable i think, from $6 to $8 for lunch =)

Well I've only tried their spicy barbecue chicken, but I see no reason to get anything else, I love it every time.  The wait usually isn't too long either, even when they get busy during lunch, and they give you a lot of food for just over 5 bucks.  If you're on the north side of campus it's definitely one of the better places to go.
spicy chicken --- @ $5
The food at gomnaru was definitely much better before they changed management.
All I eat here is the spicy BBQ chicken.  Thats it.  I love it so much I have dreams about it.  They used to sell it raw and seasoned so you can make it at home when I was coaching at Cal.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Dropped by here for a group dinner before a group meeting. We had purchased the MunchonMe deal about an hour beforehand and were excited to devour.

The prices here are more expensive than what I normally see at Korean restaurants, but then again, I don't eat at the many Korean places that aren't all-you-can-eats. The menus are laid underneath the plastic table top for convenience!

We sat down at our table, and the waitress brought us all water. We wanted barley tea, but we weren't sure if it was self-service near the counter or waiter-serviced. We eventually asked our waitress, who brought our tea over.

The banchan are provided with your meal rather than before you meal, which was a bit disappointing for our hungry group. The originally served 5 banchan: tofu, kimchi, bean sprouts (spicy and non-spicy), and rice cakes. The rice cakes were delicious! When we requested a second round of banchan, they included a 6th banchan of stir-fried carrots, zucchini, broccoli, and cabbage. Also yummy!

|| F O O D || 

Beef jap-chae dinner special: Glass noodles, cabbage, bell peppers, carrots, beef, onions, rice, soybean soup [$9 normally, $6.75 through Munchonme]
- Soybean soup was decent.
Two mounds of white rice with sesame sprinkled on top. Lots of rice! Lots of starch @___@
- A large portion of japchae with large pieces of beef! I still wish they had more beef though.
- The seasoning and balance of veggies and sauce was well-done.

|| C L O S U R E ||

The food was good and the service was fast, but without the MunchOnMe, I find it to be pretty pricey. I probably wouldn't return.

Decent Korean Food.
Decent Lunch Menu.
Decent Spicy Chicken.
Decent Service.
Decent Prices.

I'd say this place is pretty decent.

Spicy bbq chicken was the reason why I grubbed here a few times. That and public policy classes at the Goldman School in North side. 

While it satisfies a craving, sometimes the chicken comes out 'soggy' and void of tenderness. It's kinda gross actually, feels uncooked (even though the establishment swears its well cooked). 

+ Rice dishes comes with miso soup, salad, and fried potato
-  Bland salad, dressing is too watery
+ Fried potato is the best complement on the dish
-  Miso soup is only warm sometimes, needs to be hot for it to be good
-  Need to work on professionalism and hygiene - dirty front area and the cashier is known to work without his shoes or socks on (ack!)

Final Call:
If I'm on this side of campus and have that occasional craving, I'll be back. Otherwise, the competing Thai restaurants in the area gets my dough.
The best Korean BBQ near campus.  Large amounts of meat.  My favorite dishes are the BBQ chicken and the bimbimbap.

*Under new management*

I ate here w/ a couple of friends. Small but gets the job done. We ordered BBQ Pork Sandwich w/ cheese (reminds me of a Korean version of Viet sandwiches, comes with salad), kal-gook-soo (Korean noodle soup), BBQ chicken, pan-chan (Korean side dishes, kimchee being the most important). Washed it all down with hot tea. Everything was delish. 

They also serve fusion dishes that are influenced by Mexican and American cuisines such as Korean style burritos w/ choice of bulgogi, spicy pork, and chicken and sandwiches w/ same choices of meat.

There are several indoor seating w/ TV, K-Pop (aka cool music) and outdoor seating. 

Overall I'd come back as a repeat customer. Don't miss out if you want tasty, authentic family style Korean food in Berkeley area and for reasonable prices!

Pretty good, but honestly it takes about 9+ bucks to get enough food to be full. It's really not worth going to when there are so many other choices right next to it. 

If you MUST go here, the spicy chicken with kimchi fried rice is pretty good. But seriously, it's probably not worth it - they reduced the amount of food they give out and it's a bummer that they did.

edit: Against my better judgment I went back there. They didn't have prices listed so I just ordered a normal chicken with rice type thing. It cost 10 dollars... :( It's my fault for not asking beforehand, but I won't be doing that again.

disclaimer: they did have a "special" for a vegetarian meal for ~8, so that is more reasonable, especially if it is for something that you are interested in trying!

It's interesting to see the different star ratings for this place... it's like people either love it or hate it.  There are definitely some terrible Korean food establishments (Sorabol??) but this is definitely not one of them.  Deep in the depths of a North Berkeley alley-esque food court that doesn't see as much foot traffic as Shattuck or Telegraph, it's a hidden treasure!  What I had:

Kalgooksoo: Knife cut noodles in a soothing and comforting broth made me melt in my seat.  They put shredded seaweed and all the traditional ingredients like the shredded veggies, potatoes, and meat.  This is my favorite thing on the menu. MMM!!

Soft tofu soup: Came out bubbling hot in the classic stone pot with chewy beef and spicy veggies soaked in the delicious broth.  Smothered it over my rice and went to town.  Nyams!!

Bulgogi+Spicy Pork+Spicy Chicken: Flavorful, spicy, chewy yumminess.  Get in my belly.

Seafood pancake: I always get this at any Korean restaurant as an appetizer.  (It's hard to mess up on this, I think, so it's safe to order anywhere.)  Nailed it!  

The painting that surrounds the interior is nuts.  I can't imagine how someone painted it by hand and with such details!  Makes me feel like I stepped back in time to a distant village in the homeland preparing to feast on wholesome, traditional Korean cuisine.  (Minus the kpop playing softly in the background or the flat screen TV)  I left smiling from ear to ear and a bag of leftovers.  Hope to come back soon!  :)

if you are Korean, you hate this place.

If you are an American of Korean descent, you kind of sort of hate this place.

If you are a non-Korean who is familiar with Korean cuisine, you will hate this place.

The rest might find this place palatable. 

At the risk of sounding malicious, though I wish no ill to the business, seriously, Gomnaru? You really need to step up your game because this is comparable to the Americanized Chinese food-- Korean version, only worse because for the price, I expect better.

Try this place if you want some quick bite to eat (since there really aren't many Korean restaurants near the north side of the campus). But if you're new to the cuisine, don't expect to be wooed by this "experience" because trust me. You won't be.

The only item that I've ever ordered from this place is the Spicy BBQ Chicken.  It's a very simple dish: 2 or 3 BBQ chicken thighs seasoned with a pizazz of spiciness served all over rice, garnished with an unsatisfying small pile of lettuce...but it's ok! b/c it's topped off with a tasty deep-fried slice of potato!  It's a good portioned meal; some days if I miss lunch, I eat here at 3pm and it keeps me full until late at night

Back in the days (2 years ago?) I would eat here quite often because of the cheap prices, but they've raised their prices since then.  When I'm low on cash, I get iffy about spending my money here because I can get a more flavorful, eye-appealing chicken dish next door at Camille.  But variety is good and I would still consider coming here for the spicy BBQ chicken.

Additional Tip: If you really like the deep-friend potato, ask for an extra one!  They'll give you one with no extra cost!

High-quantity, mediocre Korean food. I go there for the big screen TVs.

BBQ spicy chicken is a safe bet.
Decent food at reasonable prices, but hot damn, an unreasonable amount of msg.
Great place! Their lunch specials are cheap, especially with a prepaid punch card. Lots of choices and very quick if you need to dash off back to Cory/SDH/Soda.

The spicy BBQ chicken is awesome.  The portion is huge and it's super cheap.  North side food can't compare to south side food, but the spicy BBQ chicken is one of my staples between engineering classes.

My friends love eating in this little area because it's cheap and nearby. I was in Boston for awhile and had awful Korean food, so I was hoping to get some good Korean food to compensate.

I was hungry, so this place did the job for me, but it was by no means the Korean food I was hoping for. I ordered a two-item combo with spicy pork and jap chae. Pork was a little tough and the seasoning was kinda... off? It wasn't as flavorful as I expected it to be. The jap chae was good though, the noodles were the perfect consistency. Rice was a good consistency too. Portions are big.

I'm not crossing this place off, but if I find myself here again I'm going to get a different meat.
This place was my favorite student lunch restaurant. It's at the very end of the North Campus Food Ghetto. They have excellent bibimbap and their lunch special BBQ dishes are pretty good.

This is my favorite Korean BBQ place near campus and I have eaten here about a billion times. The food is always really good and they give HUGE portions of meat. I love the spicy BBQ chicken! The portions are so big it makes two meals for me so for $5.30 I get two lunches. That is hard to beat!

Addition: This last time I went I was 30 cents short on change to pay for my meal and he said it was fine and I just gave him $5. Super friendly staff!
I lived off Gomnaru while I was a student at Berkeley.  I have since moved to San Francisco and all other Korean places I've tried here are not only less tasty, but also pricier.

Gomnaru, on the northside, definitely enjoys a slightly better ambiance than eateries on the south side.  Came here today and tried their bibimbap w/beef.  
Serving was pretty big, with lots of veggies and meat on top.  Not crazy about the lettuce in there but I just got that out of the way first.  After a while I realized that it was pretty oily...which I'm not really used to in bibimbap.  
My friend got kimchi fried rice...I think I've had better kimchi fried rice in a Taiwanese restaurant...but the accompanying meat was good [chicken]...not too dry :)
At $6.50 after tax, it wasn't a steal, but was on par with other campus places.  
My search for decent bibimbap in the area goes on!

Tried this place today and it was just OK. I didn't love it or hate it. They didn't have the lunch special because it was Sunday so my girlfriend and I ordered the Bulgogi Beef from the dinner menu instead.  When we sat down my girlfriends spoon was dirty and we had to ask for another one but the waitress brought her a new one promptly. The food came quickly but the portions are really small for the price. The beef was also kind of bland but the sauce on the bottom was very flavorful so you have to saturate the rice with the soupy sauce for it to taste good. Moreover, their small appetizer dishes did not have a variety. It was mostly pickled dishes and didn't come with Kim Chee which is what I love most about Korean restaurants. Overall this restaurant was decent and I would come back to try their lunch special if I were in the area but wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

Compared to their southside location, this place is unbelievably hit-or-miss. Their spicy pork plate can range from bland and mild to painfully spicy. The volume of toppings they serve on the bibimbap varies quite significantly. And worst of all, the meat tastes slightly undercooked sometimes, which is rather unsettling.

They have a television screen in the back dining area, usually showing ESPN, but on occasion, gems like MTV's "True Life: I Want the Perfect Body".

After the remodeling they had a year ago, this place looks pretty cool. It's the "coolest" place to have lunch in Asian Ghetto (north side) because they use foam letters for their menu.

Come for the daily lunch special: $5.99 for 2 items, $6.99 for 3! Friendly, generous portions. Best of all, it's not cash only, while all of the rest of them are.

For lunch, it's sort of school-lunch-y-Chipotle-y style. They have trays of food. You choose, and they scoop. 

This is a three primarily for the value-- for lunch. We would avoid coming here for dinner. It's a lot more expensive, and the portions are smaller. And the stuff tastes way worse, for some reason.

Once we had a really good gomtang there, but then we never found it on the menu again. And when we asked the people about it, they didn't know what we were talking about. 

HOW MYSTERIOUS.

Small Korean joint in the Hearst Food Court, the Northside version of the Durant Asian Ghetto (http://www.yelp.com/biz/durant-square---asian-ghetto-berkeley). Short menu with a few K-BBQ items, stews (chi gae), soon dubu, and bibimbap (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/4D7IdtyRjH8qxcsHaz1-GA?select=gDQtE0BP4olsZ5YgCOVJqQ).

I saw a BBQ Trio deal from MunchOnMe so gave them a try wondering how they compared to Southside Steve's BBQ (http://www.yelp.com/biz/steves-bar-b-que-berkeley#hrid:obMqk9kLh4q87ZtN3QXMpQ).

5 banchan came out first with some kimchi, fish cakes, tempura veggies, honey potatoes, and seaweed salad (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/4D7IdtyRjH8qxcsHaz1-GA?select=gNFtNfb7RUE7eXbDGsh-UA). The BBQ Trio had some sesame seed dusted rice and a miso dressed salad (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/4D7IdtyRjH8qxcsHaz1-GA?select=3wwlt4sGpaiOHfY6SVDULw).

Much better quality than Steve's. Lean cuts of reasonably juicy meat (chicken was a bit dry). They did give me spicy beef instead of spicy pork, but I can live with that. Also, fresher kimchi / better banchan than Steve's. Came with a small bowl of miso soup.

Serving size was smaller (maybe due to deal?), but I think worth it for the better ingredients.

Starving student scale: 4+ stars
Korean food scale: 3 stars

mmhhmm this place is gooood and fast korean food! you woulda never guessed, considering its in the ghetto with stores around it that are a-ok to eat. 
It's so close to campus, right across the street, and I only ate here bc it's the only place that accepts credit cards, which is a plus! for those who don't carry cash.
Since its more like an express place where everything is premade, I expected it to be like those chinese stations with food ready for your choosing and the quality to be minimal, but it really did surpass my expectations! not only that, but it was one of the best korean food I tasted around berkeley for a cheap price, considering how expensive korean food is. I got the 2 dished for around 6.50, which is kinda expensive there considering the t.c. garden which has 4$ meals (but no credit card accepted)
I got the spicy chicken, which was soo good, and the dok bok ki, which was surprisingly okay since I thought leaving it in a hot metal tub would overcook it and make it soggy, but it wasnt! kimchi was spicy and good too, but they didn't give me free miso soup like the other review indicated. unlimited tea and water for your liking, and it really does make you full! I wouldn't suggest eating the dok buk gi with rice and spicy chicken though, tastes a bit off, but try something else. They always give you an egg if you order it though.
The atmosphere is surprisingly comfy though considering it is at the ghetto.

I used to love this place when I was an engineer at Cal.  I've gone back a few times since and, after a few ownership changes, it's just not the same.  The spicy pork used to be my standby, and their menu used to be simple -- basically 5 or 6 plates that people ordered, and a couple of other things that people didn't really order.  Now they have a very elaborate menu, with 20 choices and combination plates and numerous things that aren't very Korean. The spicy pork was still good, but not as good as before, and the portion size is MUCH smaller than it used to be.  I'm still a fan, but I long for those good old days...

This place used to be a 5-star cheap Korean place back when it was owned by that old Korean guy and his one Mexican ho who was the chef. 

Now it has been replaced by a younger guy who cares more about marketing and decorations than food. He buffed up the menu and pictures and dumbed down the food. 

Let me tell you what you get if you order ramen: 
-Soup
-Ramen
-Green onions
-Tiny portion (about 8-16 ounces)

You used to get a BIG portion of: 
-Soup
-Ramen
-Delicious real carrots and vegetables and spices
-Meat of your choice

Let me tell you what you get if you order Bi bim bab: 
-Tiny strips of fake egg (excuse me? I've had Bi Bim Bab before and I am not a Bi Bim Bab N00B. I know that it is supposed to have a real DRIZZLING fried egg on top!)
-Way cheaper vegetables than the standard plate
-Way less meat than the standard plate

This used to be quality dining, but now it ain't. 

This review is for 6 months ago. If the restaurant has changed since then, this review will not reflect those changes.

I came to the one on Durant, by the Asian ghetto. The portions here actually aren't that huge...or maybe I eat too much because I finished the whole bibimbab ($6). It was delicious, with beef mixed in all sorts of unidentifiable vegetables (but hey, they tasted good). Came with a little side of okay miso soup.
The downside: Our food took quite a while, even though there was hardly anyone else in the restaurant. My friend said that his BBQ chicken plate was "okay." It looked sort of boring to me. Chicken and rice, yay.
Also, I would like my bimbimbab ten times more if it were served in one of those sizzling stone bowls that make the bottom of the rice/other stuff all nice and crunchy. yum.

Finally tried this place for lunch after living next to it for 3 years now...and I kinda regret it...

Food: 
Tofu soup: WAY TOO MUCH SPICY OIL in the soup. There was literally a highly unhealthy layer or red spicy oil that covered the very top of the soup. It wasn't too spicy but it just looked disgusting. It completely coated the spoon I was using and the rice I was trying to eat with it. Kinda over did it. I couldn't really even concentrate on what I was eating I was so distracted with how disgusting it looked. 

Service: 
None, you order at the counter and your number gets called when your order is ready

Ambiance: 
Kinda a small, hole in the wall place. Very dim and shady looking. If there weren't so many people eating there for a quick fast korean food lunch meal, it would CREEP me out to eat there. 

Price: 
The tofu soup was $7 which was ok for tofu soup but NOT ok for the quality that was served. 

Overall:
NOT COMING BACK. Sorry.

Ok, I rarely do updates on reviews.  In fact, I've only done one other than this one.

Tried Gomnaru again because I was craving Korean and this is the closest place from my building.

This time I got the beef bibimbap to-go.  It was actually pretty decent!  Lots of food (and not skimpy on the bulgogi) and it tasted surprisingly good.  I guess I can't write off Gomnaru after all!  Will have to give it another try sometime soon to see what else I can get.

I had a banging plate o' Korean food for under 7 bucks.  I can't tell you if it was high quality, but I can tell you it was tasty and just the right amount of spicy for this white boy.  It's a shame I never wandered in here before when I was a Berkeley resident.

Oh Gomnaru, why are you my favorite Berkeley restaurant?  When we first met you were all I ever wanted in a restaurant.  You were quick, delicious, and oh so inexpensive.  Just 5 dollars would satisfy all my needs.  Sure you have a host of other options, Bulgogi, dumplings,  Fried Noodles, and soups.  But 9 out of 10 times I was lured in by your siren song that still calls out to me now: BBQ Spicy Chicken.  I can see it clearly flattened pieces of deliciously marinated chicken, dancing on top of a bed of white rice.  All accompanied by a small side salad, croquette, and miso soup.  If I asked I you kindly you even gave me refills on rice and soup.  I was in love.

Remember the good times we had together? The countless times I caught Monday Night Football as I finished class, how I had free reign to your TV when we had our alone time.  I even supported all your crazy decisions when you decided to open up a Southside location.  I defended you even when others said you changed for the worse.  But, as time went on you started to abuse me.  The croquette, the amount of rice and even the chicken shrank.  What did I do to upset you?  I still defended you though.  Even when you hit me with a price raise, and promised never to do it to me again.  So I came back time after time even as you hit me with another and another.  My 5 dollar meal now cost me 5.95, what was I going to do with that extra nickel?  Give it to you of course.

Oh Gomnaru I'm not trying to tell the world why I hate you.  I'm telling the world that I love you in spite of our your flaws.  Because when times were tough you were always there for me.  On a rainy berkeley day there's nowhere I'd dine with than you.  You and your bottomless miso soup (if I asked), endless rice (if I asked), self serve kimchi, free water, free tea, and cable television.  No your dirty carpet and furniture from the Seventies won't win any beauty pageants, but you've won my heart.

Yours Forever,
Andrew F.

Where has this taco truck gone!

I haven't seen this little gem in months! The employees in the truck were always SO nice and the food was very reasonably priced!
Once I just wanted chips and guac (my fave) but it's not on the menu. So they gave me a huge bowel of guac and a bag (like market bag) full of chips for $3. 

I miss it :(

Good, quick, cheap bite to eat.  I stop here once a month or so.  The tacos de lengua are my favorite.  Considering it's hard to find a really great Mexican joint in south Berkeley, this place earns extra points.

Like someone else said, they're always super friendly--somewhat rare in this part of town.

I haven't been in Berkeley for several months, so I don't know if this yellow and blue trailer is still here, but if it is, EAT THERE! The tacos are amazing at a very low price (2 for $3 if I remember correctly?? with chips). They stack the toppings on these tacos too so you definitely get your money's worth. Best part is you can wash down this delicious snack with imported Mexican sodas that use actual sugar instead of corn syrup so they taste so much better.

When I frequented the UC taco truck, it was run by a father and his teenage son, and they were always friendly, quick, and the food was consistently amazing every time. 

I would eat here over those other places on Telegraph any day.

This is the most authentic mexican food you can get in Berkeley. Not like that fake chipotle stuff (even though i like chipotle). The service is excellent and the prices are cheap. They have great combo deals. if you haven't been here, you are seriously missing out.

This is the best mexican food around UC campus.

$1/taco!! amazing! Comes with radishes and carrots and all that goodness.

Not many vegetarian options, I don't think, but few mexican places do.

For the price and convenience, this place hits the mark.  The tacos aren't the best ever, but for the price they are.  Now offering free range organic meats for an extra 75 cents.  Also, Mexicoke!  Ah, the real sugar sabor with my tacos...perfect quick lunch!

This taco truck is a bit camouflaged because of its location - the big, green Desi Dog truck next to it definitely attracts the eye. However, if you are looking for a good, cheap meal, the taco truck can provide that for you. The portions are not huge, but big enough. Prices are great, and I wasn't even charged tax!

Looking for a quick bite, I saw this taco truck coming back from class, so why not right? I got the 4 tacos for $5 and the regular burrito for $5.50. 

Honestly, NOT GOOD. The burrito was full of rice, very little meat whatsoever. There was no taste to the burrito at all. As for tacos, I got two al pastor, one carna asada, and one chicken. Al pastor is a traditional Mexican pork that I love, but al pastor at this place tasted like leftover barbecue! It didn't even resemble what al pastor taste like. As for the carna asada and chicken, they both lacked flavor, masked by the flood of salsa they poured on my taco. It felt like i was eating just salsa in a tortilla at one point. HORRIBLE. They get 2 stars instead of 1 star because of their convenient location and price. But paying not a lot for terrible food isn't really worth it. 

Save your taste buds the horror, save some money, go somewhere else.

OH MY! I just had three carne asada tacos yesterday for dinner, basically six, for three dollars. Absolutely DELICIOUS!!!! Seriously, these guys are super nice and its one of the best taco places in town!

This little truck on the soutside of the UC Berkeley campus is great.  The tamales (vegetarian and meat) are nicely cooked , soft corn and taste very good with verde salsa.  Also, one tamale only costs $1.50 and they are very filling.  

Beyond the wonderful tamale, they serve a variety of tacos (vegetarian and meat) on SOFT corn tortillas - for those like me who don't like crunchy shells digging into your gums.  Every variety of taco comes with guacamole and fresh vegetables - not too common for your average fast food joint.

Don't know too much about the meat, but others who go with me say that it is fantastic.  So if you are ever in Berkeley during the week between 11-4 and are hungry this place serves good, cheap Mexican food.

It took me a while to finally get around to trying the taco truck, and it took me a while to find this listing on Yelp...

But it was all worth it!! Mmm...delicoius street tacos with a variety of meats of your choosing.

I got a single pork taco with a pork tamal for lunch. I think a single taco is $1.25 (4 for $5) and they come with guac!! The tamal was around $2? It was soooo good, and pretty big. The pork in the taco was a little on the dry side, but it didn't detract too much attention away from the taste. I'll have to try marinated pork sometime.

Quick, easy, delicious, AND cheap lunch! That's hard to find around Berkeley...I'm definitely coming here again. I'm just surprised there aren't more reviews! I guess most people just pass by it thinking they'll try it later, like me...or they can't find this Yelp listing...

If I remember correctly, there's a sign for happy hour tacos 4-7pm? Maybe another Yelper will post about it?

How can you not love a taco truck?  Actually, I can think of many ways you can not love a taco truck, but this one's got everything about right.  Friendly guy?  Check.  They make it fast?  Check.  When they get it wrong, they're good about fixing it?  Check.  There are a bunch of people hanging out around it, proving that it's good.  Check.

Gotta love it.

It's lunch time and you're walking on Bancroft Ave, eager to get something to eat but not looking to fork over more than $5.  Out of the corner of your eye you see a shanty looking trailer next to the flamboyantly green Desi Dog truck and you say to yourself, "This decrepit Taco Truck must be horrible."

WRONG!

The Taco Truck is one of the greatest eateries on campus!  Okay, so it might seem like a shady trailer that houses a kitchen, but once you get passed that you'll discover that the food here is quite delicious.

While I was a studemt at Cal, I would frequent the Taco Truck during my lunch break - maybe about four times a month.  As previously mentioned, the portions there are quite adequate for the price you're paying.  My favorite thing to get at the truck were the Tamales - available in chicken, pork, and possibly a few other varieties of meat - and a glass bottle of Mexican Coca Cola.

I haven't been to the truck since I graduated, but at the time I was going Tamales cost about $1.75 each!  I'm sure the price has probably gone up, but I bet it'll still be cheaper than any of the closest Mexican eateries nearby.

There are a lot of things that I miss about Cal post-graduation, and my Taco Truck Tamales are just one of them.  Once you get over the fact that it's just a trailer, you'll find some good Mexican food waiting for you!

Breakdown:

Food: 9
Price: 9
Service: 8
Atmosphere: 8
Lasting Appeal: 10

Total: 44/50... but I'm going to round up and give them 5 stars because they deserve your service!

Cheaper than Chipotle and tastes better than Chipotle. Comon, Chipotle isn't real Mexican food at all! The people in the Taco Truck are always so nice.

Their regular burritos are $4.75 without tax but you can order a "Super Burrito" which is not on the menu. It comes out to $6 flat and is just as big as the Chipotle burrito if you're really hungry. It tastes way better too because their meat isn't sitting inside a steam tub all day.

They cook everything to order, make everything there on the spot, and have two different agua frescas each day, usually horchata and some other fruit juice. Their meat isn't being heated in a steam tub. They get it out and cook it on their griddle inside so it's moist and juicy.

I recommend the Carnitas, Al Pastor (marinated pork), and the Lengua (Tongue) as fillings. Thank you Taco Truck for bein' real!

its my 4th year and today I've finally gotten around to giving this shady lil taco truck a try. boy have I been missing out; the food is cooked to order in that tiny lil kitchen and its dirt cheap!

$1.25 a taco or get 2 tacos w/ chips, salsa, and water for $3. 
$5 gets you 4 tacos w/ chips&salsa or a nice hot torta. 
and they also have tamales, burritos, quesidillas, etc etc... pretty extensive for a closet size trailer.

I ordered the 4 tacos ($5 flat) - 2 carnitaa, 1 tilapia, 1pork. they were all out of the al pastor, chicken, and carne asada which was too bad and I wasnt brave enough to try the beef tongue or whats not. next time! but these were definitely delicious (better than La Ba) authentic Mexican tacos and I'll definitely be back to get one of their toasty looking tortas. FAVORITE NEW LUNCH SPOT!

I think people underestimate the value of food trucks on campus and this one is a gem. If you're looking for something cheap and on the go, this is it. While the hot dog truck next to it receives more attention, this is where it's at. The service is nice and everything is made to order. The al pastor is good here and the carne asada is not bad, though the carnitas is just as dry as usual. For such a little truck, they even carry a couple of agua frescas and horchata too, which I usually stop by to get when I'm passing by. Plus, it's one of the cutest taco trucks I've ever seen, not industrial looking at all...

People need to show this invisible taco truck some lOoOove, because the Desi dog truck next door is just such a damn obnoxious attention whore with too much bling (yes, I'm talkin' 'bout those LED lights and its recent makeover). Honestly now, hotdogs with mystery meat or authentic tacos with carne asada?! 

4 doubled-up tacos for $5, with choice of meat + lettuce, tomatoes, and slices of lime and radishes. I posted a picture to do this truck some justice.
Good Chinese food.  Quick service and good portion sizes.   Not exactly healthy.
Cheap Chinese food.  Food quality is alright. Got the sweet and sour chicken.  Meat is tough.  Less oil, which is good.  Self serve restaurant.

Usually I just take my order to go, and for $10, it's more than enough to keep me full for the rest of the day. Be warned if you're paying with a card, because they will charge you a fee. You might want to pay with cash, if you can get the chance.

As far as taste goes, I have no complaints. It won't make you a die-hard fan of the place, but it'll definitely fill up an empty stomach.

I think the greatest aspect about this place is the casual atmosphere, though. If you wanted to talk and eat with someone, this would be the place to do it. The din of background conversations, the easy lighting--it makes for a 4-star friendly atmosphere, though the food is only 3.

Located in the asian ghetto, the food here wasnt too bad. I believe its due to the extremely fast service. It was moderately priced, but lacked a lot of the meat. And trust me, none of the food matches the pictures. They take debit/credit card, unlike most of the other places located in there. One strange thing was that when you were done with your food, there was no where to put your orange tray away. Oh well.

Sorry Mandarin House. I used to really enjoy dropping in and getting some quick, cheap, tasty chinese food with you. But not after today. Finding one hair in my chowmein was pretty gross, but something I could overlook for all the cheap and tasty clean meals you've given me to before. People have hair, I get it, it happens. But another one in a separate item? Sorry, but that just suggests uncleanliness. I sort of have a black list for places where I find hairs in my food (I'm looking at you Ramonas Cafe), and sadly, Mandarin House, you are now on the list. 

What shall I do for my cheap chinese fix now? I'm not sure. Probably just walk a little bit extra down to Great China. Damn they're lunch specials are cheap, tasty, and even bigger. I will miss your huge pot stickers, though. Farewell, my friend.

I would eat ramen before going to Mandarin House (actually, I have). The customer service is pretty bad--the lady is always rude to me and would talk about me in Chinese to her husband (or at least, the man who works there that I assume is her husband). She did this until I spoke IN CHINESE to her (and thus realized that I knew everything she had said). The food is horribly greasy and pretty bad.

Mandarin House was a staple restaurant for me as a student at Cal and was part of my weekly rotation.  It's simple Chinese food for poor students and they load it up on salt and grease to fuel your educational endeavors.  This is my close to campus Chinese food of choice and if you're smart you'll make it yours as well!

This place is so so, prices are decent, food is ok, Not spectacular, but compared to other asian food places around the bay area it's sub-par to say the least. Service is decent, speed of prepardness is decent as well.  Not horrible, not great. end of story

This place is OK. A good choice if you're eating with friends in the Asian ghetto. The menu is expansive, and the little lady who runs this place is awesome. The food is decent (especially the soup). I wouldn't call Mandarin House a destination by any means, but it's certainly an acceptable choice if you're wondering where to go in the food court.

it's in asian ghetto... what can i say?

however, if u order the right things, you actually get pretty authentic chinese food. don't order any of that stereotypical sweet and sour pork or sesame chicken... order beef chow fun or their fried rice. those are pretty authentic tasting. BUT i have experienced on occasions where even the authentic food was just plain... not too great.

I have have decent food here before, but to be honest, the only reason I ever come is that they accept credit cards and Thai Basil next door does not. Tonight was different. I ordered the Dry-cooked Chicken, and was really disappointed. For $9 I got some warm rice with bone-in chicken on it. Or maybe that's chicken-in bone. 75-80% of the "chicken" was bone, 10% fat and skin, and the rest meat. Disgusting.

Pros:
a lot of chioces
Mediocre chinese food...

Cons:
Relatively small plate compare to Chang Luong Restaurant (2nd floor on durant)
Drinks are so so

The food here is cheap but not all tasty. Had the Beijing spare ribs, and it tasted like it had a lot of sugar. The Indonesian fried rice was dull and bland. We ordered the red bean ice and were given a disgusting  concoction of milk tea with red beans (you call that red bean ice?!). When we asked the server (and/or owner?) if that was supposed to be red bean ice, he had no idea what we were talking about. As a naive freshman I also tried their pandan waffles, and that was less than spectacular (waffle was not hot and crispy off the waffle maker!). Came in here twice and never went back.

It's alright, but I've definitely had better Chinese food. I always get the Ma Po Tofu, and it always lacks flavor - not to mention that it's not even prepared the way Ma Po Tofu traditionally is (spicy, lots of flavor, ground meat mixed in).

Let me just put it this way:
I love noodles. I would eat ANY kind of noodles. Fried, boiled, steamed, baked, etc. You get the idea.

I ordered the chow mein here, thinking that it would be AWESOME (voted best Chinese food by Berkeley students -- but EVERYTHING in the Asian Ghetto is voted the best of whatever).

I threw it away after one bite. I really wanted to give it to a homeless guy (there were like 10 across the street), but I thought they'd get furious and chuck it at my face.

Sorry, it was HORRIBLE.

PS: the dumplings here were soggy and BLAH as well.

Ordered: 
BBQ Pork Fried Rice + Boba milk tea

BBQ Pork Rice ($5.75)
Large quantity, tastes cheap, might give me a stomach ache, but filling!

Boba milk tea (2.50):
Boba balls were mushy, milk tea was cloyingly (ridiculously) sweet, offensive to my mouth.

Overall cost: $9.10
And I have no idea how that happened. Tax shouldn't be that much more.

Still has a credit card minimum (which is now illegal).
Normally this place is decent, but I came on a busy lunch day and I was really upset that my food took over 45-minutes to prepare. I wouldn't have came if I knew they'd take this long.

A staple of the Asian Ghetto.  I love all their breaded chicken dishes (Sesame and Sezchuan especially).  The chicken itself is of much better quality than MANY fast Chinese spots.  

This place is cheap and tasty at the same time, a must eat for any Cal student (or friends visiting from out of town).

However, don't assume this is the typical Four stars.  It's all relative to other places like it.  One of my favorite spots around campus FO SHO.

Living in San Francisco's Hayes Valley, there's a lack of decent, no-frills, cheap restaurants.  They are all expensive and haughty (except for Flippers). And, nothing is worth hopping on a crowded bus or walking to. 

That is why I really envy you Berkeley people. The area surrounding your campus is a plethora of cheap, semi-delicious (who cares when you're hungry right, all tastes the same) dining. 

That being said, this place hit the spot. Yes, it's greasy. But IT IS Chinese food for godsakes! I had the tofu and pork rice plate for dinner and fried onion pancake as an appetizer. They were both very well portioned  and delicious. I could barely finish both and brought a couple slices of the onion pancake home.

This place is not horrible, nor is it the best Chinese food I've had.  
I don't know what you guys are talking about, but this place was worth the trip from S.F. Not that we went strictly to Berkeley just to eat here.  But I'm just saying, if you're in the area might as well stop by if you're hankering for some good and cheap Chinese. 

Added bonus: Its open super late, like to 12/1 am.

I came up here to visit a friend and was taken out to the infamous Asian Ghetto for dinner.  After spending like 20934809284 hours deciding where to eat, I thought I take a chance on Mandarin House *sound music*!  The service was cute as the elderly lady was friendly and wasn't afraid to joke around with us.

However, i was in the mood for spicy beef, so she recommended Szhechuan Beef with extra spice.  Unfortunately, the beef was not spicy AT ALL.  Maybe next time, I should tell her to dump the entire bottle of spice in it! :)

So most of the food here is pretty average except for the pan fried noodle with chicken.  OMG!  It's the only dish at this place that rivals Lotus House, but it is by far the best thing they have!

The food is greasy and cheap, which is great for after that late night of partying and general debauchery that we students engage in.  Service is fine, but there is a little bit of a language barrier if you don't speak Mandarin and need to ask for anything complicated.

I've been coming here for years, and probably will continue to.  As long as they don't stop serving pan fried noodle that is...

It was okay.
I ordered the tofu curry jauntz.
It was like 6 bucks during lunch. It was okay.
The curry tasted good though! Everything else was kind of meh!
I didn't even get a Fortune Cookie! SMDH shaking my head

They're one of the last restaurants left in Durant Square from back when I attended Berkeley.  Taste of Taipei is gone, so is Tokyo Station.

I used to frequent Mandarin House often as a student, and seeing the grumpy lady behind the counter was strangely comforting for me (perhaps I missed home?).  Well, I took my family there today for a trip down memory lane, and the same lady was still there!!!  I excitedly told me son that this was the same lady that used to work here 10 years ago, to which he replied, "Wow, she must be old."

I tried to remember what dish I used to get when I came here, but I couldn't remember.  We ordered a soup, a fried rice, and mushroom chicken (which ended up being a rice dish too), and my wife and I and our two kids couldn't finish the food.  Talk about big portions!!!  All for under $20, too.  (Dang it, I just remembered, I forgot to tip!!  I guess we'll have to go back again.)

The seaweed egg drop soup was yummy!

I've given this place a few tries and have faced the same disappointment each and every time, bad-not sure what the hell is in there-food.

The last, and final, time I was there I ordered some Mongolian beef chow mein. It came out looking like the typical dish, greasy and glowing orange from the hot peppers. I took a bite and was like "blechhh this doesn't taste like any mongolian beef i've ever had before!" It had a strange flavor that i could not pin point at the time of consumption, but as I left I realized what it was, it tasted like a BURRITO!!! Now I'm not trying to hate on burritos because I think they're very tasty; however I expect Chinese food to taste like, well, Chinese food!

That's about all I had to say on the matter, good day.

In my endeavors to find cheap Chinese food. I found it! But usually when I look for cheap Chinese food. I don't expect it to taste so cheap or even be a little overpriced. The only part that was cheap about Mandarin house was the quality of the food. Pretty terrible...

I'm a big fan of dirty Chinese food, but this just wasn't on par with any Chinese places I know. They charge a dollar extra to do half chow-mein and half rice, which is just absurd! And the service here is slow and has that Asian demeaning not so friendly vibe to it. Haha.

The only thing I liked about it was that it was Chinese food and Chinese food always tastes good. But in terms of price, taste, and service. It was no good. No second visits ever again.

the Great,
GumZ

Cheap and fast chinese food when you're near Asian Ghetto. Period. 

The only thing I order here is their BBQ pork fried rice ($6.31) only because I LOVE BBQ pork but I simply can not find a place up at Berkeley that sells it...Which is indeed a seriously depressing matter that I have no solution to at this moment. However, even though it's bbq pork fried rice, they have a tendency to DICE the damn bbq pork. Other than that, the fried rice is mediocre but very filling and your food comes out very fast. 

I did try their boba one time, but please don't get it. I beg of you. The milk tea boba is disgusting to be honest. The boba was mushy and sludgy and had a hard tap water after taste. What the f***? *insert no me gusta meme* 

The one good thing is that they do accept card here unlike the other half of Asian Ghetto. And you could probably eat here everyday for as long as Gandalf lived and not be able to try out the entire menu. That's if you're able to read it of course. PLEASE MAKE THE FONT BIGGER. Might as well have a braille menu, right? I guess I'm just bashing on the restaurant now, but their fried rice isn't too bad. I'd take Thai Basil over it if their line was shorter.
of late i've noticed the portion size has been bigger.  The dishes are still hit or miss, but i've found the peking spareribs to be a solid choice.

I really wanted cheap, fast Chinese food because my fridge was very very empty towards the end of the week. 

I got cheap. And I got fast. But I did not get tasty. 

My order: Mongolian Beef Fried Rice. What I got: little bits of beef (barely marinated), tossed in overly greasy rice soaked in soy sauce with frozen peas and carrots mixed in. Instead of flavoring the beef, they threw in some sort of spice to make the rice more flavorful, but it was not the type of Mongolian flavor I expected. I was sadly disappointed because I could have probably whipped up the same dish in my apartment. 

Next time, I'll head over to Lotus House for some more authentic, tasty Chinese food that won't break the bank.

Cheap chinese food.  Enough said.  

But I sometimes go back to Mandarin House because the food lines are so much longer at other restaurants in the Asian Ghetto.  My last trip there, I was really craving some cheap and fast boba milk tea and the lines were out the door at Sweetheart and Quickly.  But the boba balls were undercooked and grainy inside ... gross.

Was craving roast duck, so I decided to give this place a try since my friends were across the street at the Curry House.  Why didn't I just eat with them?  Basically for 7 bucks, i was served a container with steam rice, and 6 little pieces of roast duck.  Of the 6 pieces, only 2 had meat on them as the other 4 consisted of the neck area.  Plus, instead of chinese broccoli, and i get the american broccoli.  We are in a chinese restaurant aren't we? 
Never will i come back, as this makes it 2 for 2 in horrible Chinese food experiences.  The icing on the cake is the scowl and horrible attitudes on the faces of the 2 ladies working the counter!  
Never Again!

Cheap Chinese that fills the void with hefty portions. The Kung Pao chicken won't win any awards but the chow mein and sweet and sour chicken is decent. 

A very good fit for the college student on a budget.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Why? I'm a third year Cal student who has spent a ton of money and tried every single Asian Ghetto/ Durant Square restaurant.

Please do not support this business, it needs to go out of business because it serves the most god awful food ever. I've read all the other reviews that give it more than one star.

Yes, they have a gigantic menu with decent/cheap prices and they sell little snacks and blended mocha drinks but all of the food is just awful. Have I tried all the things on their menu? No. But I can say that all their food has a similar dull and tasteless flavor. I tried their noodle soup and I was literally just drinking water and oil. There was no flavor whatsoever. I tried the chicken chow mein and it was just greasy, crappy, and pumped full of MSG. Even then it was still tasteless, so I chucked it into the trash within a few bites.

You may wonder why I even went back to this restaurant if it was so awful and the reason is that I'm a reasonable enough person so I wanted to give it a second/third/fourth chance as I visit the Ghetto daily. Well, every single visit was STILL a tasteless nightmare. Time obviously does nothing to the quality of food here.

Bottom Line: Terrible American Chinese food. Please do not believe the other reviews that claim this place is at least decent and do not dare to try this place. Unless you have sub-human standards for food, in that case I suggest that you try dog food before this place.

Update: Had a friend insist on trying this place and I could see the disappointment in his eyes after he had his "Mongolian beef", he vowed never to go here again.

I used to live in the dorm up the street, and I got takeout here quite often. Then one day, I realized it was more out of habit than the desire to eat Mandarin House's food.

They make all of the usual Chinese foods, but none of them are done well. Their boba is also terrible. If you absolutely need a Chinese food fix, and can't walk outside of a 1 block radius of "Asian ghetto" (the local name for this block of restaurants) this is passable. But I'd rather eat at one of the many other restaurants.

everything else sucks EXCEPT Szechuan chicken. 

oh and get the frequent customer stamp card. after 12 stamps u can get a free meal!

This is a standard, cheap, Chinese restaurant.  Nothing else to say really...  Sorry about the lack of a witty six paragraph Yelp review.  The only thing that really stood out about my experience was that they got my normal spring roll order mixed up with the next table's vegetarian spring roll order.  Pretend that there was a sitcom scene where a vegan accidentally ate meat and flipped out, instead of the reality where I caught the mistake before entertainment ensued.
It's okay.  I usually get the orange chicken.  Portions are huge though and cheap.  Egg drop soup is decent too.

I've eaten all kinds of Chinese food - cheap, nasty, good, expensive, authentic, fake...everything. The worst Chinese food I've ever had was in Los Alamos, New Mexico, where I had an orange colored hot and sour soup with weird contents inside. That was the worst.  This probably isn't the #2 worst, but I can't think of anything in recent memory to dethrone its status. 

The food isn't that good for starters. I've tried to eat and smile because I've got food in my tummy, but it doesn't happen.  I've eaten it sober and it sucks. I've eaten it drunk and it sucks. I've had stuff off their menu and the food was whatever. I've had their lunch set and that was whatever as well.

This is one of the few Chinese spots that has stuck around for a long time now, so some people must like something about this place. There isn't much as an option for Chinese food in the UC campus area. As much as I dislike Panda Express (come on Lower Sproul!), I'd prefer them over Mandarin House.
I had the Mongolian beef, spicy, and it was really great. What really impressed me was the service, the little old lady who took my order was very nice to me.

This is NOT a go-to place in the Berkeley kid's repertoire. I used to only come here because my friends didn't really like trying new places, as they were used to Asian food. They have your basic Mandarin-style Chinese fare, but it's pretty expensive and greasy, not to mention heavy on the salt. Other times, it's kind of bland, like their tofu dishes. Avoid if possible. It's not cheap Chinese food; it's just Chinese food.

I eat here to throw in a bit of variety when I get tired of the other places. I'm never really that impressed when I eat here but it isn't bad either. Typical chinese food. Lots of menu items - though a lot of them are the same thing with just pork instead of chicken, etc

I had just moved into the Berkeley area for summer school and was in need for Chinese food that reminded me of home. So, I decided to give this place a try since it looked just like the restaurants in the San Gabriel Valley. It was the worst decision ever. I ordered a minced beef over rice and the vegetables that they used were clearly from a can and not freshly prepared. The sauce they had used was definitely bland and it did not reflect minced beef at all in any way. However, i still decided to give this place two starts since there was free tea and the food still satisfied my asian food cravings. However, the price and the food don't match so be wary when coming here.

Pretty good cheap food for a quick meal. 

Very fast service and nice people here.

the orange chicken and general tso chicken is really good

I used to come here pretty often a couple years ago. Now I only come here against my will, as in, whoever I'm with wants to eat here. Their fried rice used to win me over. It was so damn good. It was eggy and packed with flavor. Now its bad...really bad. It's like it has no seasoning on it anymore. The ma po tofu tastes different too...like it's old or something. They only decent thing they have now is the breaded chicken dishes...probably b/c you can't really f up  breaded chicken.

I am only giving this place a 3 because I really enjoy the fried Mandarin pork chop. However, the price is outrageous and they are quite slow in comparison to their neighboring shops. 

Last time i went there, I didn't know it cost more money to substitute noodle for rice. "substitute" actually means getting the eggroll and noodle. The lady didn't explained the price fluctuation clearly to me! Before I could have said I wanted rice instead, she already swipe my creditcard and I am $10 poorer opposed to $6-something.

Go to Viet Nam Village if you can, it's only right across and it's cheaper.
Big portions, TERRIBLE FOOD. Tastes like under-seasoned overcooked food from chinese places at the mall.

The Honest Truth: My least visited place in Asian ghetto.  I would definitely recommend lotus house or happy valley for chinese food. Similar prices to the rest of asian ghetto, but the food isn't that great.  Even their white rice is dry and the rice they use is long grain, not the typical short grain (stickier rice).

The Details: The only times I come here are to buy a 1$ arizona iced tea or when everything else in Asian ghetto is really busy.  Their szechwan chicken is decent, but again, the rice is not very good.  I think the thing that makes it different than the other places is that their flavor isn't very good. I would definitely choose Thai basil, gypsy's or bear ramen first. Now their food isn't flat out horrible, and it would still fill you up for a meal, but I've definitely experienced better.
Everything tasted the same with no taste whatsoever! Terrible.

This is fake Chinese food at its finest. As a Berkeley student I came here maybe a few times because they have a good seating area and ambiance inside, but I generally avoided this place because their food was sub-par. Too watery, too salty, didn't taste fresh or right. You know that uncomfortable salty "mehh" aftertaste? You get that a lot here.

I only came here twice and I don't know why, but they're when I'm starving. The portions are not exceptional for the prices and the quality is only a little better than Panda Express. For a place like Mandarin House, I think it's extremely disappointing to be compared to the staple Americanized "Taco Bell" of Chinese food. To say the least their prices sure reflect they want to be seen as "better" than typical fast food.

That being said, they are very fast at getting out their food. Mandarin House can be summed up as the identity crisis between not knowing if it's a fast food restaurant or a sit down, more family style Chinese place you remember going to when you were younger. I would appreciate it more if they slowed down, did a better job, and didn't poop out their orders in five minutes.

But some people (esp college students) like fast food, but then I would recommend not pricing it and selling it as though it were the food you ate at family reunions in Shanghai. Oh, yeah the dim sum? Appreciate the option, but you could make it less obvious you were scalping us on a 100% markup (it's over $3 a piece, bought at around MAX 2 something, but I'd expect it to be even cheaper at around 1.00 or 1.50 at 99ranch. All in all, they're laughing all the way to the bank.

I'm not sure what to say about this place, but I've been coming here almost every night for the past two months so I felt I should write a review!
The lady who works at the counter is insanely adorable. I like her. I buy dim sum from her. Dim sum can never be bad, but the flour part of it...is a bit stale.
I got the fried fish and fries yesterday night. It looked a lot better in the photo... the fish breading was too hard. The fries were good though.
The rice dishes here are decent, I'd rather go to kips for the price though.
The porridge is overpriced!
