However, I love the mexican soda here. Seriously, try the pineapple soda in the fridge drink section. You will never turn back to any other....the fourth star is for the cheaper drinks here compared to other places in azn ghetto. And the pineapple soda.
I should note though, that there is a six dollar minimum for a credit card purchase. So bring a dollar fifty in cash to get that mexican pineapple soda!
This place was like any other Asian Ghetto restaurant. Portions are fine, affordable... but it wasn't anything great. Their boba was okay too...

I honestly expected more. I ordered a plate of Orange Chicken with fried rice. Maybe I'm just an idiot and don't know anything about Chinese food, but even an idiot knows what Orange Chicken is supposed to look like... Anyway, it was as if they took a chicken breast, cut it up into rectangular pieces, and covered it in cooked orange juice. Not good. I really did try to eat it, but I physically couldn't. The fried rice was slightly less disappointing, but the egg roll was absolutely tasteless. However, I'm giving Mandarin House the benefit of the doubt since my friends had a better experience, and actually touched their food. Thus, the rating stands at three stars. If I ever find the urge to return, I will attempt to make a better choice (as if Orange Chicken isn't generic enough to be decent tasting), and hope it lives up to my current rating.

Taste: 2
Value: 2
Service: 2

Wow, I can't believe I came here enough times my freshman year to buy a discount card. I remember the prices being a lot cheaper and the food being better. 

After not going back for over two years, I decided to go here to grab something quick to eat. It was pretty bad. The soup I got was totally not worth the money. The broth was watery and the noodles were really bland. Probably won't be coming here ever again.

If you're starving and don't care what you eat, come here because it's cheap and the serving portion is big. 

Other than that, don't come here, really. You can totally get better Chinese food elsewhere around Berkeley; this place just isn't it. Everything I had was coated with MSG so they all tasted the same to me...I couldn't tell what I was eating. 

Pass.

I've had very mixed feeling about this place after going here a bit last year.
I ordered their fried rice plates a lot last year.

But one of the weirdest feeling I get after I eat here is that I'm full. But not the feeling of being full after you ate a good meal. It feels more like they added some chemicals to the food or something, I don't know...

Prices are a little on the costly side, but still a decent place to eat at the Asian Ghetto.

Found in the Asian ghetto. A few tables inside and a tv screen usually with sports playing. It has to-go prepared as you would see I'm fast food places like panda express, but you can also order off the menu. They have a pretty wide range of choices.

Service:
It's an Asian restaurant so I never expect the service to be anything but rude and silent. I was right. They don't really offer you much service. They take your order and bring it to you. You have to refill your own drinks and grab your own condiments. 

Food:
Decent. A little bland, but it's just like anything other lower hole in the wall Chinese places. But it's cheap. Decent portions. And they accept credit card with no extra charge. And their close to cal.

Note: I did regurgitate their after a couple of hours, but I was sick that day so I wasn't sure if it was because of my sickness or the food. I had the dumpling noodle soup. I thought it was make me feel better.

Overall: 
I wouldn't recommend this place. Especially if you plan to travel to try it. I understand it's simple for students to grab and go, but definitely not a place to go the distance for.
I love the huge menu, so it's always exciting choosing what to get, but it all tastes the same and doesn't really stand out flavorwise. It's really not that great. But it's usually plenty to eat.

Go to Lotus House next door.

Had Szechuan Shrimp, Curry Chicken, and Hot and Sour soup. The only one that was good was Szechuan Shrimp. Curry chicken was way too gingery...it just didn't taste right. I've had better hot and sour soup. 

Not coming back, rather go to Lotus House. The only reason why we chose Mandarin House was because we didn't have cash.

Meh.  I've had way better, but I guess it did the job of filling me up. 
No one was in here when I walked in.
Service was Meh. 

Probably would not come back.

Great amount of Chinese food for a cheap price. I usually get their combo chou mien with sesame chicken and it lasts THREE meals!!
Their orange chicken is very disappointing, it basically consists of chicken katsu with yucky orange sauce.

Just not good at all. Stopped there one night and it was really empty, but it still took about 25 minutes to get my food. I ordered tofu with eggplant, and the tofu was overfried and too chewy. Gave me a bit of a stomachache too.

This rating requires a story.  Once I tried cooking mongolian beef at home.  I was disappointed with the results.  But at that point I hadn't eaten mongolian beef in many months, and I wasn't sure if I did it incorrectly or if my memory of mongolian beef was better than it actually is.  So I decided to go out to a Chinese restaurant to see what it should be, to compare it to my first-time rendition.  And this was the place I ended up at.  And it tasted nearly the same.  And I still didn't like it.  Since I hadn't been to this place much before, I decided to give my recipe another point of comparison and went to a Chinese restaurant elsewhere that people actually recommend.  And I enjoyed its beef.  And thus I learned that my rendition was indeed bad and in the process learned something about this restaurant...
Food there is simple and decent.

A friend and I ate here once. We ordered BBQ pork and roast duck, two characteristic Asian fast food dishes that can be found at nearly every Chinese grocery store and countless shop windows in Oakland and SF Chinatowns.

First, we had to wait a really long time for the food. When if finally came, it was really bland, definitely the worst BBQ pork and roast duck I can ever remember getting and they are like my favorite dishes to order!

I will never eat here again and I advise you not to either unless you have no idea how the dishes are supposed to take and want to be wowed by your next experience...?

Located in the back of Durant Ghetto, Mandarin House has been here forever.  It was where I had my first meal in Berkeley back when I was a mere high school kid.  

I am pretty sure if I wrote this review back in my college years I would rank it 4 stars.  However, as I grew, the value changes.  Being cheap and have large serving size isn't the main concern anymore, while taste and the decor start to matter.

I still like this place for the sake of memories, and its still cheap and taste decent with good portions.  However, having my tongue trained for slightly higher taste, I keep thinking the food here is becoming a bit too greasy.  (I ordered mongolian beef this time)

Maybe next time when I come back I would order some other old time favors, the pan fried chicken, the beef stew noodle, and the pork and mushroom over rice.  Just to see if they are as I remembered.

What I ate: Mongolian beef chow mein
Visit date: October 9, 2011
First time? No.

Back in the college years, I used to crave the Mongolian beef chow mein. I have no idea why I wanted it this time because I can no longer eat like a college kid, but I did. What's great about Mandarin House (and other Asian Ghetto establishments) is that they are open late. We got there slightly before 1a and the place was still bustling with patrons. It's not the best Chinese food (it could even be one of the worst), but hey, it's food when you're hungry, no other place is open and you're too lazy to cook. They also have a long menu so you should find at least one thing you might want to try. Even though I give them just two stars, I wouldn't be surprised if I went back again for late night snacks.
food does not taste good even though it has hella msg in it. the servers are very unfriendly except the middle aged woman who works there

solid, dirt cheap chinese food in the asian ghetto.  if i were still a student, i'd love this kind of place.  don't do in here expecting any gourmet food.  it's obviously low quality, but you get what you pay for.  it's an order of magnitude preferable to Panda Express, but is clearly below any real Chinese you'd get in a reasonable restaurant, but then again, you wouldn't get these prices in a real restaurant.

i'm rating for their tapioca drinks, not necessarily their food.  of all the places in berkeley, their tapioca tea drinks is the best to me.  i go there for my taro with milk team and tapioca, sometimes warm, sometimes cold.  it is quite a treat at less than $3.

the ambience is more restaurant-ish and not that great -- the counter seats at the tapioca ordering section is more for waiting at than for sitting at to drink your beverage.  it could be better, but it is a college-town (UC Berkeley) dive after all.

warning: parking is not fun.  take bart, the bus, ride a bicycle, or a motorcycle/scooter!

oh, you. 

your mediocre chinese food sustained me many a night while up studying and/or drinking (yes, sometimes i did both of those things at the same time). 

i miss those days, living across the street from you, trying to avoid the froth of homeless and drunks and students bubbling in the street while still, you know, kind of being one (minus the homeless part). 

mandarin house makes okay chinese food. and sometimes it's just what you want.

Cheap and open late, but almost everyone I know who's eater here more than once has gotten sick.  If you went there regularly it was just an inevitability.  But then again, sometimes you just need late-night crappy chinese and in the DFG ( Durant food ghetto) your choices start to dwindle at 2am

Are you fucking kidding me?! They MICROWAVED my wontons for my wonton noodle soup. I SAW.

As a horrified first-hand witness, I charge thee GUILTY of 
Inappropriate 
Kitchen 
Demeanor. 

[/end case]

This has got to be hands-down the WORST Chinese food I have EVER had. And judging by the reviews, I'm not the only one who thinks this way. While the price may or may not entice some broke college students, beware; it is not worth the price and eating here will give you more to cry about than your shitty midterm scores.

The soup was disgustingly flavorless and the rice that comes with your entree tastes like snot. Never ever coming back here again, I don't know how it's still in business. This is the one place to avoid in the Asian Ghetto, quite possibly all of the East Bay!!

99.9999% of the time, when you've got Berkeley and cheap Chinese food, it's going to a big, fat, NO.

Without Mandarin House I would've died while living in the dorms. Once I tried the "pan fried chicken" I hardly ever ordered anything else. The staff was always really nice too. Except for the mean, old, ugly lady. I guess being ugly for 40+ years really takes its toll.

One time I was sitting in this restaurant, stretching with my arms back over my head, and I accidentally punched the owner (old chinese woman) right in the eye.  She still served me after that, even though she always looked pissed. 

This place is awesome.  As soon as I got sick of the food that my dorm served (which was quick), I ventured up durant.  Also well known for their tapioca tea drinks, the mongolian beef, szechuan chicken, and generals chicken were my favorites.. big portions and not too expensive.

I'm Chinese, or if you'd like, I'm Taiwanese. I love the food of my culture, whether it's Shanghai style, Hong Kong's own, or Taiwan's ambrosia. It enrages me when Chinese people think they can run a Chinese restaurant in California just because they're Chinese.

This is one of those places. Honestly, it's like somebody slapped the panda from Panda Express, and out of sheer shock he threw up onto a plate. That's what they serve here.

One time, I assume they must have run out of beef because I ordered a beef chow mein for takeout and when I got home, there was absolutely no beef in it. Instead, there was a lot of soy sauce to make it appear darker as if there were some ground beef. There was no beef.

No matter what the price, I wouldn't spend my hard-earned cash here. It's not worth trying and definitely not worthy of the beautiful "Asian Ghetto" that is this plaza. Even broke college students must have their standards.

Besides Great China, Mandarin Garden, and Taiwan Restaurant, the three of which are barely passable, this is the only decent Chinese joint within the immediate Southside of campus. 

Your choice here does matter a ton. The picture menu doesn't always correlate to what is served, but it does help give some perspective. Overall, the rice plates are all overpriced and should be avoided.

However, the rice stick noodle soups and "chef specialties" deserve a positive mention. For one, I rarely see people ordering these. The dishes are a little more expensive, which probably wards off a lot of individual diners, but they're far more satisfying in terms of size and taste. #10, the fried tofu topped with combination meat, for example, is delicious. The tofu is fresh and fried to the right consistency, and the meat is incredibly tender. 

Their flat rice noodles are also some of the best I've had, period. I don't know how they can keep it so fresh-tasting, but it is at least equivalent, if not superior to the kind you get at pho restaurants around the bay. The soup bases themselves are okay and more hearty/less salty than the other options around.

Mandarin House at least strives for balanced seasoning, which helps it avoid the heavy-handed Chinese take-out quality that possess most of the other options in this price range. For that and the fact that I only got diarrhea once out of a couple dozen times here, 4 stars.

I used to go here all the time when I was in school in Berkley.  I love this place.  Anytime I craved egg rolls this was THE place.  Best and biggest egg rolls I ever had.  Plus, the price is awesome for us poor students.  Mandarin or sesame chicken lunch combos were pretty good too.  I think I remember it being about $5.  I haven't been here for a while, but hopefully I could make a trip soon.  

I usually take the grub and go back to my apartment.  It's usually packed and I was always in a hurry to get back to studying.  So as for ambience haha verrry casual.  It's just good, cheap food.  What more can I say.

Ok yuck! This place is not Chinese food. It's fried, oily, and gross.

Do not come.

Overpriced Dim Sum, the cheapest item was almost $3.

This place was 3rd choice on the plaza, after our first 2 locations had already closed and we only wanted a snack, not a full sit down experience.

We ordered 3 dim sum items all were pretty average. Food quality was below par, for the price.

Dirty bathroom in alleyway across the plaza... avoid using the bathroom if you can!!

After getting a set meal for 2 on nob hill that was enough for 2 meals for the same price, this place had a lot to answer for.

I have to say that these bad reviews surprise me, but I guess not too much should surprise me in this Yelp World we live in. This was one of my GO-TO spots while in school. 

I used to grub at this place ALL the time, I never ordered anything other than Szechuan Spicy. Almost always got it to go and took it back to my house or made a pledge go on a food run for me. I am sure its not authentic, but I don't think that's what they are going for... 

MY GO-TO DISH: Szechuan Chicken Spicy.

The only good thing about the food here is the large portion size. I've definitely had better "whitewashed" Chinese food. Used to like their orange chicken a lot, but I developed food poisoning the last time I ate here and haven't gone back since. 

Pay cash here to avoid the fee they have for credit cards.

Cheap, fast, tasty Chinese food, perfect for the average Berkeley student.  Try the Mongolian Beef, General Chicken, or Sesame Chicken.  This review might be jaded by fond memories of College, though... :)

Aaaah Asian Ghetto. The go-to place for cheap and delicious Asian food. Too bad Mandarin House doesn't fall into the second description. 

I've been coming here ever since freshman year, but I tend to skip over Mandarin House and head straight to Thai Basil or Steve's Korean BBQ. Today I decided I haven't had Mandarin House in a while, so I decided to give it a try. They have 5 daily specials, and you would think that as specials, they would be cheaper than the rest. Not true here.

I got the Mango Chicken Rice, which pretty much ruined it all for me. It was finally sunny in Berkeley, I was having one of the most relaxing days in a long time, and then this piece of crap came my way. I have no idea what they do with the rice, but it's probably the worst I've had. Extremely dry and very low quality rice. The chicken was alright, but I've definitely had better. There was way too many vegetables in there, especially zucchini, which I'm not a big fan of. The mango sauce tasted very bland and had barely any flavor in it whatsoever.

2 stars only because I remember eating here before and it wasn't as bad as this experience. Sorry Mandarin House, but I'm going to have to skip out on you for a while until I have a strange urge to come back.

Mandarin House is awful. I would go here and keep trying to give it another shot, but as someone else said, it's not authentic, healthy, or even good. I would try to give specific dishes, but it's just as true to tell you that I've had many different things here and they're all just really bad.

The last straw for me is when I ordered szeshwan chicken and was served sesame chicken and she refused to remake my dish.

I reserve this for when I have the unusual craving for the worse Chinese I can possibly find. But even after I eat it, I'm dissatisfied because it's worse than I expected.

Cost/person to do it right: $7

I probably come here about once a month--when I've exhausted other nearby lunch options and want something Chinese-ish.  Here's the thing: standing alone, the food isn't good.  However, if you're looking for something close on the South Side, Have a craving for something better than Panda Express, don't want to spend a lot, and desire a shit ton of food, Mandarin House will satisfy.

First, it is probably appropriate to say that the regular employees and I are friendly, so I might get bigger than average portions, but they're still big even if they hate you (I promise).  That being said, you'll want to eat-in to get the pretty decent soup, which is included, before a meal.  It's kinda nice.  Also, be aware that a lot of dishes here flat out suck.  i won't go into an extensive listing, but there are some bad ones.  What I can say, however, is that the general's chicken that they do is pretty good and will satisfy your salty, sweet, and fried cravings simultaneously, and maybe with a vengeance.  For the portion and the price, the quality of this dish is better than it needs to be to bring customers back through the door--especially that close to UCB.

Verdict: Same price as PandaEx, but much better.  Beyond that, nothing special.

Exhausted student/worker getting off at class late in the evening looking for  hot big bowl of wanton mien w/ charsiu. (Maybe some other ingredients if the price is right.) 
Must have clear hot broth and fairly firm noodles.
Wontons must not fall apart when being handles by chopsticks.
Chaursiu must be soft, juicy and sweet.
I'm willing to be flexible with the cost.

Mandarin House?
Not quite.
Next?

Visit 1: House Special Combination: chicken, pork, beef, shrimp, vegetables in brown sauce in a big silver bowl + rice - it was great!

Visit 2: House Special Chow Mein: I got food poisoning - It was bad.

Visit 3: Mongolian Chicken Chow Mein: I got food poisoning - goddamnit!

I stopped going after the third visit. This place is a hit or miss I guess. It's your typical really bad chinese food, but some of the dishes can be done right if you're craving some of your favorite killers like sweet and sour pork. I recommend Chang Luong over Mandarin House for anything I guess.

i heard that this place makes people sick...but i've eaten there 3x, been fine so far.
the menu goes on and on...it takes me about 10 minutes to decide what to get. i've had the pan-fried tomato beef noodles, bbq chow fun (which came with lots of yummy sprouts), and a chicken, fish, and eggplant stir-fry. these were all about $6-7, and very satisfying, coming from someone who's been eating Chinese food for all her life.
i wanted to try the 3 dish lunch special ($5) but the pre-cooked food looked greasy and gross.

It would be a compliment to say this place is more than mediocre. I've never eaten anything on the menu that even got close to surprising my taste buds. They have a shockingly HUGE menu selection, its like the took the yumminess of their food and spread it throughout the entire 200 menu items they have listed. Sometimes the cashier won't even know what you're ordering and will question whether the item you want is on the menu. However I do enjoy the soup that comes with your meal if you eat in, I also like the large wide screen TVs where they play the news and sports.

they advertise crepes on their window, and so i decided to try this place instead of going across the street to crepes a go-go.  worst idea ever.

what i got was not a crepe at all.  it was this little 6" diameter piece of "crepe" that was made out of fried chicken batter.  i asked for a strawberry & banana crepe, but they loaded it up with chocolate, ice cream & whipped cream from a can.  it looked really unappealing.  the ice cream, whipped cream, and chocolate was all melted and oozed into one disgusting mixture to make the crepe ever more disgusting.  also, it's not folded into a crepe, it's basically all the crap piled onto a piece of hardened nasty fried batter thing.

also, the strawberries tasted like chinese food.  

i don't know about their real food items, but i can tell you that their crepes blow.

Eh, their Chinese food is too... fast and Americanized for me, and by fast I mean too much oil and MSG. I've only been here once and I ordered their porridge-- I don't recommend their porridge. Service was okay, but I don't think I'd come here again, but maybe it's because the dish I ordered wasn't so good. My sister ordered their Peking duck with rice, I think, and she and her friend loved it.

What Mandarin House is not: - authentic - healthy - fast - 

What makes Mandarin House still awesome:  - tasty - cheap - hugo portions -

I used to go here literally every night during freshman year. Biggest bang for your college buck, and while as I mention above, it's not super-fast, it also means it comes out piping hot (and crispy - of course I'm talking about my two faves, General Tso's chicken and orange chicken). It also means it hasn't been sitting around under a hot lamp like the offerings from the dollar chinese places.

Great food, clean, and the lady behind the counter has been there as long as I've been going there (11 years), so you know she knows what she's doing. Highly recommended as a great college Chinese food joint.

Just good old Chinese fast food for cheap.  They give large portions.  I always get the item + rice meals and they give you tons of rice, which I love.  

The food quality over all is really just decent.  If you're jonesing for cheap, greasy, questionably authentic Chines food (which I do, on occasion), then this is the place for you.  Meal prices range from 5 to 7 dollars.

I have also had the noodle soups in the past and I highly recommend you skip it and go for a rice dish.  The soup broth was super bland, as were the vegetables and meat on top of it.  If you're looking for noodles, just hop on over to Bear Ramen across the way.

They do serve boba but I have yet to try it.  I probably will someday and will update this review accordingly.

If you're looking for quality and you have time, ditch this place and go to Great China.

This place is so disgusting that I wish I could give it no stars...a little hyperbole, but seriously, this place sucks. 

I ordered Orange Chicken on my first visit...I know, I know- a really uncultured decision, but I just had a craving for it. Anyways, since I got it to-go, I didn't peer into the box to see what I had gotten. Thus, I waited till I got home to get some soggy battered chicken (that I REALLY think was microwaved) half soaked in the Orange Chicken sauce...To add insult to injury, the sauce was disgusting and tasted like diluted orange jelly. GROSS! 

I've went a few other times to try other stuff too (you'd think I got a hint) Mongolian Beef- sucks. Chicken and Mushrooms- sucks. Broccoli beef- sucks. It's all terrible. I've NEVER, in my life, had chinese food this bad. 

I do, however, have a confession: I do go back to get their XO Sauce Pan Fried Noodle. It's actually doable...but its still very mediocre, I just like it. If you see me in there eating my pan-fried noodle-  just let me alone to bask in my shame and lets pretend you never read this review. 

P.S- I don't know if this is a faux pas to talk about other restaurants in a bad review about another, but if you're digging something of Asian flavor, remember that they don't call this shopping plaza "the Asian ghetto" for nothing. I really like Thai Basil, and I kinda like Steve's Korean and the Sushi place (forget its name)
3 words: CHEAP. FAST. GRUBBY.

I literally was eating here almost every monday and wednesday when I traveled to Berekeley and loved every hot dog filled moment of it. I wish the hot link was hotter (spice wise) but that can easily be rectified by an ample smathering of hot russian mustard. By the time i leave the door and get to BART, that dog is gone. Now, if they can start wrapping bacon around their dogs and grill them mexican style, I'd be in heaven.

this is the same chain as the durant one.  same review.  hard to mess this kinda thing up.

if you want a hot dog, come here.  the end.

ok i'll say more.  the selection is huge.  the sausages and hot dogs are good.  and i love the selection of mustards.

it's hot dogs plain and simple.

As hot dog places go, pretty awesome.  They have a very wide selection, and almost all of them are great.  I used to eat at the one on north side seriously four times a week, since it was right next to Soda Hall.  This is the least ranty of the locations, and the most accessible to tourists- perhaps not a coincindence?

However remember- it just serves hot dogs.  Which is great if you are young and getting lots of exercise, but all that fat and meat does catch up with you.  Just a warning there.

Top Dog is also a "only in Berkeley" type of thing, because it's run by Libertarians.  This means there are ranty diatribes all over the walls about how the government is trying to oppress you by making you pay for roads and the fire department.  And how global warming is a myth being used to silence Freedom Lovers.  So that is a bit obnoxious.

I'm not sure but I think the dude working the counter is "leasing" the entire business while he's there, in keeping with the Libertarian principles of the place.  Whatever the reason, he has a bit of flexibility; you can cut deals with him for buying dogs in quantity."

I would give it a 5 star for the durant location but we couldn't make it to there from the bart station.
Eating here brought back great memories of my time in college making late night runs to fill up on one of the best dogs around.  
I can't believe that the prices haven't changed too much either.
Everyone in our party enjoyed the dog

Good sausages. They use french bread instead of buns. -:) Chili is ok. They do not offer fries at this location (not sure of this is a chain) so they told us to get fries from the burger joint next door! Friendly staff.

Normally I would reserve dogs for late night sustenance, only when there is adequate alcohol in my system to destroy any memory and feeling of nausea caused by eating processed meats. 
However, as part of my lunchtime challenge, this is the final venue to on the street to be sampled. 
I chose the chicken lemon dog. Really I should have bought 3 to call it a meal, since they are quite small dogs. The taste wasn't terrible, I would probably consider it an acceptable option after a couple of drinks.
Doode, I have to say they have good stuff. Cannot beat the German sausages, but it is good enough. I'm giving a 4 stars.

Top dog is a great place to satisfy the need of a really juicy, yummy hot dog craving. I live in SF and find myself at Top dog whenever im in the East Bay. They are friendly people who cook up a dog quickly and offer all the original toppings. Everyone should check this place out. Be ready to look for parking though.
had the bockworst and it was so so good. very juicy and flavorful. i really enjoyed the sesame roll that it came on too. top it off with some sauerkraut and you got yourself a damn good lunch.

Dropped into Top Dog for the very first time before the CAL UCLA game.  The 4 stars is for the cheap hot dog!  It's pretty delicious and I'd say if you are hungry make sure you get more than one (they really aren't that big).  The only downside to this spot is that it's super disorganized when they get busy.  You line up to the right to order and then the guy makes you pay upfront or makes you pay when you get your hot dog.  Wait to the left hand side for them to call your order, which everyone is waiting for their order!  How do you even know if they're calling you?  I mean there's only so many things on the menu.  I'd definitely come back but perhaps not on such a busy day!

Just kidding!

I stopped by the Durant venue the other day to get my monthly hot dog fix and was happily surprised by the new and extremely friendly grill-chef. It made the dog a million times better... 

So pleased.

Best Hot Dog place! Everytime I go there I think I'll only need one hot dog, but after I'm done with my hot dog, I always want another!!! My vegan friend ate a veggie hot dog there and was convinced it was real meat.

Although the sausages are pretty good, I think paying almost 3 bux for a hot dog is ridiculous, unless it's enough to fill you up.

Therefore, when you end up having to get two dogs, plus something to drink, it puts you at about $6. $6 is a tad too much to pay for a meal that consists solely of bread and sausage.

Love this freakin' place!!! The bf and I always have to grab a dog or two whenever we make it to the Cal Football games. He' s the one that introduced me to this establishment and since then I have been hooked. The chicken apple sausage and the hot link dogs are the one's I always get.

Oh! what's awesome is that you could purchase a dozen of their dogs (any flavor) and they give you free buns to go with them.

I'm a native Chicagoan so a love of hot dogs/polishes/bratwurst is pretty much in my blood.  So I periodically get a craving for a good dog. I always think, "Oh I should go to Top Dog. It's a hot dog joint and they should be good there." I however always seem to forget how disappointed I always am. 
Here's my list of reasons why: 
1) No respectable hot dog would be seen within ten feet of a french roll. Hot dogs belong on hot dog buns. 
2) I'm pretty sure I could make better sauerkraut myself. 
3) The best part about hot dogs is they're cheap and filling. These, however, are neither without having 2 and thats six bucks. 

So long story short: They're okay but you west coasters have a LOT to learn about proper hot dogs and other meats that come in casing.
Smoked Chicken Apple make ya holla! =]

It's a top dog that's for sure. Amazing bread. Amazing mustard and sauerkraut. Amazing top of the line garlic bratwurst? I don't even remember what I had but it was juicy, had plenty of snap to it and delightfully flavorful....

THAT BEING SAID, if I wasn't trying to do a whirlwind tour of Berkeley, I would definitely have not come as let's face it $3 for a hot dog is kinda pricey, especially if you compare it to Costco (not saying quality is a comparison) where you can get a polish and a drink for $1.50. It's a different experience, but to me, a hot dog is still a hot dog.

Guy at the counter was giving me some attitude too, but not a huge deal as he was still fast and efficient.

I like this one because there are plenty of seats outside and inside for you to enjoy your dog. The taste is just as good as the other 2. Open till 2AM? since when....I've walked there drunk and the ish was closed... (this was back in April 06)..

Top Dog!

Hey, late night food. A sausage for every stripe (brat, italian, kosher, chicken, polish....) and they actually have sauerkraut and REAL mustard in several spicy and brown varieties (not that sickening suburban yellow stuff that causes Alzheimer's and Neo-con political philosophy).

Why aren't sausages Americans'  favorite food?

This a good value place that is very consistent. A hot dog place with few frills outside of some awesome libertarian cartoons, posters, etc. I've been here many times when I'm on the go and want a cheap meal. The selection of sausages is great and there is a nice variety of toppings. It's a bit greasy and not exactly a great place to sit and eat and the menu is limited, but that's not really a fault considering they don't try to be anything but a hot dog place. Definitely worth a visit.

Top Dog gets a lot of rave reviews from Berkeley denizens, but I would typically rather eat a grilled up Johnsonville Brat from the supermarket. And as stated by another reviewer, $3 for a hot dog seems a bit much. Maybe you're just paying for all the libertarian propoganda plastered on the walls. That said, the variety of dog flavors is a big plus.

i had never had a veggie dog (the wienie) at top dog until yesterday, and it's honestly not too bad.  i used to always get the chicken dogs here, but my bf wanted to try the veggie dog yesterday.  it's a bit more crumbly than other dogs, since it's made of soy and gluten, but the flavoring was pretty good.  after you glob on the spicy russian sauce, onions, and jalapenos, anything tastes pretty good anyway!
Best Hot Dog in the Universe. Try the Veggie--delicious!!!!

Great, great dogs. I had the chicken dog with apple and garlic...holy crap yum. Can't get much better for a hot dog place. I also really like that they include tax in the prices. Gigantic dogs and the guy serving us was really friendly too. A really good experience.

Came here long ago with the bearded hipster Fabio. We had several dogs and all were good. This location is not as cool as the one on Durant though since the one on Durant is far more popular but this location does have a lot more space and it has really cool stuff up on the walls. You know, the kind of stuff you especially like to read when you are recognizing how unfair the world can be. I'm sure that those of you studying right now know this and well, those of us that already have our degrees once enjoyed it too...well, many of us anyway.... How can you beat a socially conscious hot dog joint? You just can't! I recommend the Lemon Chicken and Smoked Chicken Apple dogs. I believe there is one called Linguica which is also very good! I highly recommend Top Dog!

This is a good Top Dog location, but this review is about the restaurant in general.

Don't get me wrong, the dogs are good.  There's a good variety, and everything they do is solid, but they're just so tiny.  To get a decent meal, you have to have at least two dogs.  Three if you're super hungry.  While one is pretty cheap, two is enough money to make me choose other options.  I'd like some sort of happy medium, but it just isn't there.

It's a good snack though, and I'm probably a little biased because I prefer a Chicago-style dog.

Certainly a little jewel in Berkeley, came here after some business at UC Berk and came here.  Gotta say, $3 for a hot dog here is the best $3 ever spent.  I forgot the name of the hot dog i ordered but it was pretty good, it felt as if it had a hint of wasabi, so I would get the occasional wasabi "burn" when have you experienced that from a hot dog.  I'd definitely come back to this place if I'm in the area.  Gotta try them all.  it's a small place with a chill atmosphere and these guys have revamp'd what a hot dog can be.  KUDOS!

same as every other top dog.  Unlike the one on durant this one takes card and has an indoor seating area.  It's also much less crowded.

can't go wrong with a hot link

avoid the russian mustard at all costs.

I went to top dog tonight for the first time and it was delicious. Normally I wouldn't give a grimy place with unfriendly cashiers five stars but top dog has a lot going for it: 1. it has a variety of hot dogs and sausages including low fat and vegetarian options 2. its super fast and 3. its cheap as hell. I don't care what the other reviews say, if I can eat dinner (a tasty one for that matter) for $2.75 that's a bargain. If you live in the bay area trek over to hippy-ville or San Jose because top dog is a must.

Cheap and Delicious. What more could one want? Although there's no shortage of good and affordable eats in Berkeley, this is a fan favorite for a reason.

Only con I find is that the portion sizes are small. I usually order two or three dogs when I go, to get full. It is good for a light snack or lunch. 

Recommend:

- Bockwurst: for a clean mild flavor
- Bratwurst: classic taste
- Calabrese: spicy fans

*Random Fact- For those that have been to the one across from UCI Irvine, this is the original location.
Not quite the same as the good old Durant Top Dog, this one is still really good and not as packed. Great dogs. Oh man. So good. And cheap too! Recommended.

I've been going here for years but last night the guy behind the counter, with slicked back hair, decided to ignore my order and make me wait twice as long to get my food. A woman ordered five minutes after me and we got our food at the same time. He spent his time talking on the phone and watching a DVD. Top Dog... get your employees in check.

Top Dog always has good hot dogs. I am disappointed by the disgruntled workers who are often not too polite. The hot dogs are a bit overpriced, especially if you want a chili cheese dog... $3.75 just seems too much for me. On the plus side, all sodas have free refills. Open 'til 2 AM... Hadn't heard that before... definitely gotta check it out.
I no longer eat meat so I can only rate the veggie dog and potato salad.  Well the potato salad might be the best potato salad I've ever eaten.  The vegie dog is so-so.

Quick, delicious*, and reasonable.

Some typical eccentric Berkeley-style rants on the window, but otherwise a good experience. Bar at window seems to be ergonomically cut to prevent mess. Me likes.


*Top dog claims to be the best in the Universe. Perhaps, top in Berkeley, not in Universe. Place on Haight St. SF is better. All time best dog for me was in Vienna. A  wiener thrusted into a fresh sour demi-bagette, can't top that.

Oh I loved I got off work in Oakland and road the bus all the way to Berkeley just for this it made my day! I had bockwurst their tender juicy flavor does it for me every time.  I also met an interesting friendly man from Monterey  and a guy from my itty bitty hometown of victorville. A strange and wonderful night.

mmm I love top dog. I like coming to this location better than the one on Durant because its less crowded, cleaner and offers inside seating. Still want to say that the LINGUICA is DEEEEELICIOUS and everyone shoudl try it.

This place is a great option for cheap food near the campus. 

My personal favorite is the bockwurst, made from 1/2 pork, 1/2 veal, milk, and eggs.
A good place, and void of the usualy "I couldn't care less about you" kind of service we all expect from Top Dog. It took a while to get his attention, but when I did he was cool.

Today was a nice pleasant day to walk around Berkeley and grab a hot dog for a quick bite.  But after I placed my order for a top dog, the disinterested and clearly bored female cook/cashier/cleaner/whatever placed my dog to the hot side of the grill, took my cash and gave me change.  Then she came out from behind the counter to wipe up the wet puddled sticky dirty floor below the clogged, overflowing soda machine basin.  She wiped dry the floors with paper towels then wiped off spilled ketchup, mustard and other mess on the counters.  I thought this was great that she cares to clean up after messy customers.  But then she went back behind the counter and emptied hot dog bread rolls to toast on the grill.  OMG...she didn't WASH her bare hands after taking my order, making change, wiping dry the pooled floors and dirty counters.  Then she starts touching bread, utensils to serve dogs, soda cups, potato salad and the paper wrapping my top dog!!!  G-R-O-S-S to the MAX!!!  

I couldn't believe this health code violation happening right before my eyes.  I was speechless when she handed over my top dog.  I just took the top dog, walked out to the sidewalk and tossed it into the garbage bin.  I hope the homeless didn't bite into that trashed dog and get sick.  Sorry but I warned you here.  Try the other Top Dog locations, maybe the workers wash their hands over there before serving your food.

YUM! 

Ordered the Calabrese... hot spicy Italian sausage ;)  Loved the buns. 
Fairly crowded, but the wait wasn't too long. Lives up to its name "Top Dog" and the reviews were right! 

Also had a bite of my friends Lemon Chicken... low in sodium and fat but STILL soooo tasty. I wanna try it all!!

(Don't use the restroom here, it's nastaayy)

I usually love top dog because it's affordable, simple, and quite delicious. However, the one here on North Side seems to lack in the customer service department. 

A friend from Irvine came to visit and since she was in great hunger, I decided to take her top dog - a must have before leaving Berkeley. My friend felt shy about ordering the Mango Habenero because it was hard for her to pronounce so I ended up ordering for her. When he asked "What would you like" to my friend, she told him that I already said her order. He gave her this mean, stoic look and said "okay...". 

He did not once smile at us and took him a while to realize that we were ready to pay him. He had a whole atmosphere of "I hate my life" expression on his face. Seriously, if you don't want to work there, don't. Also, for future customers, if you want a sincere customer service with good hot dogs, go to the one on Durant.

I love hot dogs, and Top Dog is definitely the best place to get a dog in Berkeley. There are a variety of different dogs available - everything from your standard beef frankfurter to bratwurst to hot links - and the whole place has a no-fuss vibe that makes it quick and easy when you need a quick bite on the run. My two quibbles are 1) as delicious as the buns are, they're a little too big -- as silly as it may sound, I personally standard hot dog buns and 2) they only have chili with beans in - call me crazy, but I think the best chili cheese dogs/burger/fries use bean-less chili. Neither of those things are enough to keep me from stopping in regularly, though, and plus, they have RC cola!
Affordable and quick hot dogs. I am a fan!

I rarely regret going veg but this place can do it! In college, I used to stumble up here for a hot link with spicy mustard at least once a week. Now, I do come in from time to time because, bless their souls, they do have a veggie dog. But, what I really want is a vegetarian version of the hot link. Please please please someone invent this and bring it to Top Dog ASAP!
For $3 it was actually the best value meal I've ever had in the bay area.  What's special about this hot dog place vs any other dog is that they use good bread and not  the ordinary junk you get.
They have good Vegan Dogs.  THe owner is a cool dude.  It has been a staple of mine since the 80's.  Yes I am old you young fucks.... I was in my 30's in the 90's HA!

I can't knock a $3 hot dog and I am definitely not going to start now.  
For three bucks, these dogs are tasty!  I have only tried the Bird Dog, which satisfies my spicy cravings and the Chicken Apple.  I am a sucker for anything tasting like breakfast.
The best thing is that these things are portable.  I can see a student devouring one of these things, right before class or anybody heading for the bus or the BART.  
If you go, try the Lunch Bag Special:  A dog, bag of chips and a small soda for $4.95.  Can't beat that and still feel full :)

The chicken apple sausage was delicious. I love that they toast the buns on the grill. On the side, they have the usual ketchup and mustard condiments and a few more  (relish, onions, jalapeño). It was $3 even.

Summary based on many visits:
--classic TD menu 
--ok service, so not like Southside and even somewhat better than Northside
--parking challenging, but not impossible
--consider avoiding weekdays at lunch when BHS students abound

Excellent spot before and/or after a show at the Greek to get a hot dog...  You can eat it while walking up the hill to the concert venue; it will give you energy for the walk and/or the live musical concert.  

Pork is good for you.  

These are good quality hot dogs too...  Equiv to Nathans, Boars Head, or Hebrew National...  Friendly service also, the lady that helped me was really nice.
Yum. Quick. $3 hot dogs. Personally recommend chicken apple. :) Top Dog and Hot Links are quite popular as well.

yay my first review!

my bf's been to TD before in berekley just not this location. i ordered the smokey chicken apple and he got the hot link. the sausages itself isnt that big but its pretty yummmmy! the hot link wasnt too spicy. personally, i liked the chicken apple better because there are bits of apple in it! it was on a soft bagette like bread which i find more tasty than plain hotbdug buns. $3 flat for each hotdog. not too bad, but i would need to eat 2 to be satisfied.i didnt have any problem with the service since i went when it wasnt too busy.

also, you can also order these wienies in BULK! in case you wanna bbq them at home while watching a game with your friends or something!

i would come here again when i visit the uc campus! :]

Absolutely the best; bar none. Many dog/sausage choices, all delicious. Excellent buns, excellent toppings, mind blowingly cheap. The chili is good too, I can't bring myself to have the chili on the dog, because the dog and toppings are so good on their own.

Of the 3 Top Dogs around Berkeley, this one feels more like a restaurant.  Its decent place to study, being the only one with table and chairs, thus even though the sausages here are pricey, ($3 per sasuage)  but if you treat it as rent for the table, its justified.

My theory that Top Dog taste better after midnight still stands, since despite having the same supplier and training as the southside top dogs.  This top dog doesn't taste as flavorful as the southside one after midnight.  Maybe they saved the best sausage cooker for the late night shift there.

I've been doing TD for 30 years,and love these places, but this is just not a well run TD.

The person behind the counter has a major attitude problem towards customers.

I have twice eaten there ,the first time,the counter person didn't call out the order loud enough for me to hear,so instead of calling it out again,it sat there and got cold.

I had to go to the counter and ask where was my order.

Same thing today,but I watched this time and was able to discern her calling out the order.

If you are more than 5 feet away ,you won't hear the order.

I paid in cash,but counter person wouldn't accept payment unless I placed all the bills in correct order.

I realize that good help is hard to find and this is a shining example af the shortage.

Won't be back to this location again. .

Downtown Oakland  ,Hearst and Durant are fine ,this one sucks.

I would love to give Top Dog a higher score, but I was very disappointed last time.

Don't get me wrong that their food is not good. It's delicious. I love their Calabrese and Lemon Chicken. Very juicy and flavorful. The downside is that the hot dog looked more like a sausage now than a hot dog. I remembered few years back, the hot dog is the same size as the bun. Few weeks ago, my Calabrese was half the size of my bun. I might as well just make a sandwich with ketchup and mustard than pay $3 for a bite of the juicy goodies.

Props for this one to open late in the downtown area where nothing else is open. Props for the spaciousness and tables.
Love this location because it is located in downtown Berkeley. Love the hot dogs.

I dig it! Had the bratwurst and the garlic dog and the sausages are really, really strongly flavored! Toppings are all the same (you add) and there's like two tables outside but you can sit on the curb or in front of the student union or really anywhere in the city and look normal (considering the number of college students/hobos--hey, what's the difference in terms of appearance, right?).

But they're very, very fast and it just feels like a niche, hole-in-the-wall college shop. Great.
All Top Dogs serve great dogs. This location is convenient to downtown, but for the full Top Dog experience, I recommend the Northside and Southside ones for their better (hotdog stand) ambience.

We were here for an international conference. It was such a great experience! Because of the cheap price ($3 for each dog), I got 2, the 'top dog' and the 'lemon chicken' dog. They tasted delicious, and the person helping us was extremely professional and kind toward her customers. I like how the tax is already calculated in the price, so we don't have to worry about the hassle of receiving change. Great place to bring a small group of people to eat.

The only bad thing was that the tables were dirty as there was only one staff on shift...
Very affordable and a quick bite to eat. I always come here when I visit and get their Hot Link which is bursting with flavor and love the kick.

I don't normally eat hot dogs, but I can't turn down a Top Dog hot dog.  I ate it on a dare after my piercing and I've been a fan ever since.  

Top Dog kicks Pink's and Nathan's Hot Dog arse anyday!

First glance of the bun made me a little worried. It looked like it was going to be tough. I was glad it was not! The size helps hold the condiments, too. Their sauerkraut is warm, which is different from other places. I like it!

I'm giving this place 4 stars because they carry varieties of hot dogs. I got the all beef and it has that snap that I was looking for. It's cheap, too. So this is definitely not a gourmet hot dog, but it's the simplicity that makes this place special.
Every time I come here.. I always have to order two dogs.. It's that good! Even my son who's a picky eater ordered two..

I love this place.  Every time I'm in the area I'll try to make an effort to grab a bite to eat here.  

I usually stack up on Garlic Frankfurters and RC Cola.  It hits the spot.

Who can't pass up the chance to have a hot dog, any kind of hot dog, for three bucks? You can have your choice of bratwurst, hot links, or polish and it would still be the same price.

Better yet, you really don't have to wait long for them to be prepared. The cook has all the different varieties laid out in front of him. You just tell him what you want and he rolls it right on out onto the stove. And everything is cooked perfectly. There is no burnt sides,  over cooked outsides and under cook insides, or cooked insides but tough as leather outsides. They are just the right temp to eat and juice.

And to top it all off, free condiments. I find nothing more frustration than to have to pay extra to have sauerkraut or relish on your dog.

When I go to the Bank of America across the street it is so hard for me not to go over and get a beef frank.  I want one right now.  

This location is one of the larger ones (there's room for more than 3 people to stand) and they have stools facing the window so you can people-watch as you eat.

Don't really understand why everyone loves this place, but I decided to try this a few months ago with my roommate. It was early in the afternoon, so there were only a couple of people in the restaurant. I think the woman working there was having her time of the month if you get what I mean because she angrily told me that she had to cook my dog separately because I ordered the veggie one. I patiently waited for my dog, and when it arrived, I was expecting fireworks to go off in my mouth but there were none whatsoever. The hot dog was a bit overpriced, and I was still hungry after eating one. The bread was nothing exceptional either. Probably won't come here again unless I'm especially craving a hot dog.
It'sTop Dog. There's not much more you can say.

The hotdog maker chick behind the counter could use some cheering up, but the food we got was great.  Don't expect a smile... I've seen goth kids with perkier attitudes, but whatever... she made us a mean lunch that was delicious.

I think this is my favorite top dog of the three that are around campus. Aren't they all the same, you ask? No. They're not.

There are two other top dogs: one on Durant (southside) and Hearst (northside). This top dog doesn't get as crowded as the one on Durant, and the cooks are less demanding and intimidating (if you've been to the one on Durant, you know EXACTLY who/what I'm talking about). Also, since it's not as crowded, I can order my Wienie (...it's a veggie dog for all those sickos out there) and ask that it be cooked with separate tongs and on a clean area of the grill. The cooks are usually okay with these requests, but I do get a raised eyebrows once in a while. There is outdoor and indoor seating, which southside TD doesn't have.

The dog itself is really good, and there is unlimited refills on the drinks (unlike Southside TD)! Take advantage of the condiment bar; they have sauerkraut, ketchup, mustard, dijon mustard, onions and mayo (I think).

Finally, if you're planning a barbaque and don't want to serve taste-less hotdogs that come in packs of 300 from where ever you like to shop, you can buy dogs (in packs of 6 or so) from top dog and impress all your friends, frenemies, and co-workers...or satisfy your inner hot dog junkie.

great sausages and dogs, but the service is horrible. I guess they carry the zeitgeist mission statement: treat your customers like crap and hope they return. They most likely survive on college students living on a budget, but still take some pride in your job and if you hate it that much go work somewhere else. Its too easy to be negetive and a hater these days, being nice is way cooler :)

The kielbasa is my favorite.  People talk up the lemon chicken, but I think it's a bit overrated.  Kielbasa or chicken apple sausage.  I am a bit of a purist and was surprised to find that you can get them with chili and cheese...which wasn't ever an option at the location on the Southside.  I still love the surly service too.  :-)
Very cheap and very delicious! Only thing is it's cash only :( Like Justin R. says, the portions are kind of small but other than that it's a great place!

The hot dog is flavorful and can stand on its own. Doesn't need chile or any other gimmick to register on your taste buds. I recommend the Russian mustard as a complement. I'm comfortable in saying that its the most flavorful hotdog I've had so far. 

Using a French roll instead of a bun is a nice touch - most vendors will cheap out and give you the dry Styrofoam grocery store picnic buns. 

It hits the spot when you're on the go and need something to get you through between meals. 

I can't get over paying $3 for a hot dog - I should get a movie or a ballgame with my hotdog at the price. 

Lucky for TD, there isn't a Costco near by.
A cheap snack or meal: bockwurst, tater salad, and drink. Five bucks.
Very simple......very cheap.......very good!!!! I definitely prefer grilled dawgs to steamed ones. Can't go wrong here.
Just hot dogs!

I've always wanted to like Top Dog, but I just don't.
The food sounds really tasty....Lemon Chicken, Linguica,  Smoked Chicken Apple Sausage...etc. But I've never left Top Dog thinking, "That was awesome!"
To me, one hot dog doesn't do it, you need two. And as a couple, 4 hotdogs at $3 a piece...and that's without a drink.
I simply don't think it's worth it.

...But I am tempted every time I walk by because it does smell damn good.

This place has generous portions, and the price is low! Not to mention these are authentic sausages from a Co. in the City, and taste very good. served with hoagie rolls and your choice of condiments. The vegetarian version is blissful as well, and processed at the same factory. Some soda varieties taste kind of flat or under carbonated, but the Diet Coke and Coca-Cola are never without fail Cash only folks
What?!?  Gourmet Hot Dogs? Open till 2am? Yes. It is all true.
Top dog is amazing, especially at 2 am

Ever since I discovered Top Dog (catered) at a bbq lunch, I was addicted. The price is wonderful ($3!!) and the dogs delicious. My favorite is the Smoked Chicken Apple. I always tell myself that I should try something else for once, but I end up getting the chicken apple anyway. A few days ago was my first time at this particular location, and I liked it! Very roomy and plenty of places to sit (compared to south side/north side top dogs) aaaand super close to the west side of campus. Also, I found out about this doggie bag deal where you can get a dog + chips + drink for only $4.75! The dogs at this location were not cooked to the point of charring a bit like the other locations I've been to, but it was still delish. Top Dog (any location) is definitely my go-to place for hot dogs!

Things are OK here.  Mediocre at best, in my opinion.  $3+ for a hot dog depending on the variety you pick.  Soda is a $1.50.  I understand they have to pay rent, but it's fairly expensive for what it is.  And one hot dog isn't enough for me (I'm an average sized person) -so I got two.  $7.50 for two [small] hot dogs and a soda?  Steep.

As for the quality of the food ... it's OK.  I've taste way better, for what it is worth.  The bread to sausage ratio is too high, and the bread is nothing special at that.

I'd only come here if I was really in a scrape for food.  I don't personally understand the hype and rave reviews this place has.

Just as good as Top Dog 1, a little less anarchist but just as tasty.  They make up for the lack of politics by having free refils on all sodas, plus RC on tap.  OK, i guess Royal Crown Cola is a bit anarchist, but it's so tasty.

It's been  more than 25 years since our late night post drinking runs took us to the Top Dog on Durant.  It wasn't as much for the delicious dogs as it was for the event and the experience - watching the guy behind the counter remember the orders of all 20 people packed in at 2AM after the bars closed.

I had an opportunity to be in Berkeley this week and I have had plans to make my way south to the Durant Top Dog.  I was thrilled to find Top Dog as I walked up from BART to the campus.  I immediately stopped and fulfilled my carving - a Bratwurst with onions and Hot Russian mustard.  I've been all over the world and have still not found a sausage as good and satisfying.  $3.  Such a deal.  I had unfiltered AJ for old times sake and went on my way - almost euphorically happy.  

I went on campus for a few hours, completed my meeting and headed back to BART - passing by Top Dog again.  TWO Top Dogs in one day?  Dare I?  It may be forever before I get one again so I indulged in my 2nd favorite dog - the spicy Keilbasa, again with onions and Hot Russian mustard.    Should the two dogs cause a heart attack at least I knew I had been in heaven...

When my friend and I went to see Bloc Party at the Greek, we needed to stop and get some food. My friend having never been to Top Dog (and this being one of the few places that were conveniently on our path from the BART to the Greek), we stopped by to get her a dog.

When she said she'd never had a top dog before, I told her that I wished I could have taken her to the "original" one first, because to eat top dog is an experience that transcends the actual ingestinal act. You get to order dogs with jargony lingo, and you get see people berated for taking too long to make their choice (or actually get berated yourself), and you can gawk in awe of how one person can remember so many orders accurately without jotting a single note. These are among the rites of passage in the Berkeley community. If you don't christen yourself at the original Top Dog, you're just cheating yourself.

But alas, this top dog, while it has tasty hot dogs, is nowhere near the same as the original. They're relatively polite... they're clean, and spacious and you don't have to eat on the street.

I never thought I'd be complaining about a "nice" eating establishment, but I am. So the 3 stars are obviously with respect to the original top dog and top dog experience, but by all means, if you need a good hot dog, come here.
I would have starved at 2am in my twenties if it wasn't for Top Dog.

if you live in Berkeley or have ever lived in Berkeley then you know. If not, that's your loss. I'm serious. Hot dogs are not supposed to be this good. Top Dog is the perfect college food; its open at all conceivable hours, cheap and quick. One, two, three, four, five stars.

So, I visited this small dog joint last year... I probably should have written a review then, so as to capture the sensory details of the crackling and juices.

Now, if I recall correctly, there is no topping (my bad) this joint: the Bockwurst has a nice snap to it when you bite into it. The interior of the building is the quaint type you'll encounter along Durant Avenue, unique to Berkeley's college town, the one with age and character. I would describe it as a no-frills, more-substance-than-style enclosed hot dog stand (more than a restaurant, as it is cramped), but that is by no means a bad thing. The condiments are nice, but overall the quality of the sausage grilled atop the flat steel tabletop is the most amazing thing about the place. My memory of the place is quite fond; perhaps the crisp Berkeley air or the munchies contributed to the overall ambiance of the Top Dog experience, but there it is.

Unlike the pretentious, cookie-cutter chain restaurants of Orange County, Top Dog truly stands out. The grillmen are expert, probably from decades of experience, and take their trade seriously.
The food is rich in history, flavor, and texture; but cheap in price (a rare quality where I currently hail from---Irvine, I'm eyeballin' ye -_-).

if I ever do visit Berkeley again, I will *most definitely* drop by Top Dog and post an updated review. :)

I work in the Cal area and had time to kill before a basketball game, so I decided to grab dinner here on the way instead of paying insane prices for sub par food at the arena. 

I had not one, but two top dogs. Indulge me. grill-toasted sourdough bread and juicy juicy sausages are a winning combination. The past time I was here I ordered the Kielbasa and the bockwurst. Flavorful and just the right amount of spices. They've got tons of other sausages to choose from. Something for everyone. 

Do yourself a favor. If you're gonna go to top dog, then go big. I was doing myself a disservice by ordering a chicken dog the first two times. The lowdown and greasy items will give you more bang for your buck.

Man oh man.. this is the only spot i go to when im in berkeley late at  nite... they have the best hot dogs ever... not just any hot dogs but they have all kind like lemon chicken dogs...even tho i mite have been drunk all the times i ate there but even if i was sober the place is the bomb... its a small crack in the wall. look for the line of drunk people..

I've been to three Top Dog locations, but I'm writing about this one because I went last night.  This particularly TD was significantly less clausterphobic than other locations.  I frequent the Dog for the Bratwurst.  There are big signs mentioning that they feature Saag's, a sign that I could go to the grocery store and buy the same item.  But who has the time to roast a dog over the grill all day?  not me.  I'll keep coming for the toasty buns-and at $2.75, I'm unlikely to go broke any time soon.

Any bratwurst/bockburst combination with whatever condiments you desire is a win. I do prefer the Top Dog on south side though, but simply because it has a bit more character. 

Tip: Don't get the chili and cheese, no matter how tempting it sounds. The cheese is not melted and the chili is... beany. 

Bon appétit!
This is the same as all of the other top dogs around campus.  It is a pretty good hot dog, but pretty pricey.

I don't know if I was here on an off day (Friday evening after Beat the Clock, a fine Berkeley tradition), but the bun was undertoasted, the ketchup was watery, and I was left very unsatisfied and wishing I had swung by the Durant location instead.

Ambiance and Customer service definitely make a difference!
I have issues with the people on Durant.... 

I know, I know. Same hot dogs right? And that still stays the same. I'm used to dirty, greasy, greasy greasy illegal bacon wrapped hot dogs. But Center Street Top Dog, you're definitely better than Durant. Anytime. 
The girl behind the counter was chill, so didn't mind that my boyfriend and I had luggage with us (we were off to the airport), and served us really quick and with a smile :) 
He liked it too. And if there is anyone who is picky about food, its my boyfriend.
Also, there's a place to sit! It doesn't harbor the manic oh-god-stop-touching-me-I -just-wanna-get-a-hot-dog claustrophobia feel that I get on Durant. It's real chill here. We just hung out here for a while until it was time to go, since it was raining outside.

Yay top dog (on Center!)

The best hot dog I have ever had, the flavors and everything worked out very good. Honestly it is step up from a hot dog seller on the street, with a nice store front. 

Then again I was trying to get a quick lunch to go for work so I might have been hungry, but regardless this was still the best dog I have ever had and I have had many bland not so appetizing dogs in my life. 

The best part is that they cook it right in front of you, so I thoroughly like that as well. Have not found another place that makes such good dogs.

Let me start by saying that if you're looking to go to Top Dog for some brilliant out-of-this-world sausage experience, you might be disappointed.

Don't get me wrong, the sausages are great but they are not what make Top Dog stand out.  Myself, my other half, my parents & also my friends all like this joint so much because it is quick, made to order, & cheap.  My personal favorite thing is the French bread roll.  The boyfriend's personal favorite thing...the sausage casing.  Yeah, I think that's weird too, but it makes sense.  The crispiness of the sausage casing @ Top Dog makes it so that you always get a clean bit of bun & sausage.  None of that tugging around nonsense.

If you like hot dogs, you've got to give this place a go.  There are several locations so no excuses!
Good veggie wiener! Big and not overcooked (a big mistake with many fake dogs), with a little spice. Reasonable prices.

I love this place!! I actually ate three hot dogs in one day and would have gotten a fourth one if my friend didn't stop me.  The classic all beef is good, but the lemon chicken is even better and even better than that is the Bratwurst.  The place is smaller than my closet, but runs like a well oiled machine.  Can't beat the tub of sauerkraut on the side either.

Sausages, sauerkraut and mustard: the requirements for an awesome hot dog.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: three stars.

Tog Dog's appeal is not so much in the preparation of the food as it is in the ingredients used. The rolls are not tasteless Wonderbread rolls, and the sausages are not your usual beef franks.

Just a sampling of the selection: Calabrese, Kielbasa, Bratwurst and Chicken & Apple.

The kicker is the vat of sauerkraut. It is not a hot dog without it.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: one star.

Center Street Top Dog definitely takes after the more upscale downtown Berkeley atmosphere. There is actually room for more than a few people at a time inside, and with high tables and stools, you can actually sit down and read a newspaper with your dog.

Top Dog is another place that I just love, not necessary because they are the best restaurant, but because they've decided to focus on one thing - making tasty hot dogs!  And boy do they make a tasty hot dog!  They have this giant griddle that has the magically ability to cook the hot dogs perfectly (crazy-hot inside, but only slightly crispy on the outside).  They also toast the buns to give it that "Wow I wish I took the time to toast my own buns when I was cooking hot dogs but I don't and that's why I'm going to Top Dog" feel!  They also have a wide variety (re: flavors/seasonings) of dogs you can get, if you want to get "wild and crazy" with your hot dog experience.  

As for the restaurant itself, it's quite small; perhaps only 2-3 tall tables (the kind you can just eat while standing up) and a small counter.  They also have a few outside tables, if you wish to flaunt your delicious hot dog-ness to those walking by.  Inside the atmosphere is quite "Berkeley-esq", in that it's got local art and political statements thrown haphazardly (yet artistically) about.  

Another great aspect of Top Dog, they are very inexpensive!  Most of their hot dogs are within the $3.00 to $4.00 range (tax included).  So, you can easily have a very filling meal for around $10.00, drink included.  Speaking of drinks, I would be remiss in not mentioning the fresh apple juice they have - it is crazy!  Keep in mind, there have been times I've gone in to get my "Dog n' Juice" and the apple juice has been sold out.  So, if apple juice is going to be on your "try-it" list (and it should), go in early!  

I'm giving Top Dog 5 "Dog" stars, because when you want a hot dog, they serve the best.  Their prices are very reasonable and the staff has always been friendly and efficient.

Let's begin in 1988. I'm a freshman at Cal and living in the Unit 1 dorms. Though I'm living on the meal plan, sometimes late at night I get cravings that can't be satisfied by whatever I have in my teeny dorm fridge. So off I go to the Top Dog on Durant. The mean and surly guy behind the counter often regales customers with funny stories of his awful ex-wife.

Cut to 2005: I find myself back in Berkeley on a regular basis, and a much younger guy is running the grill at the Center St. location. I stop going because, frankly, the guy is an asshat, and we nearly got into it once over my inability to say the entire name of the particular dog I want.

Cut to 2007: I'm still in downtown Berkeley, and the asshat got fired a year or so ago. The successive grillers are much more amiable. I'm back to going there more regularly.

The dogs, of course, have always been great. Bummer that they no longer have pickles, but some things aren't forever.

Top Dog it is!  

I can see why it's all the rage.  

I had the Calabrese and the Italian sausage was spicy and tasty.  The grill-toasted bread was warm and crusty...a perfect complement to Top Dog!

I'll be back for more! :)

I'm not quite sure what the buzz was about. It was a hot dog. The bread was really nice, about 10x better than a regular hot dog bun, but the hot dog itself was maybe just a touch above average. Still, I think of a hot dog as a super-cheap ($1.00) item, so for $3.00 it should really blow me away, and it didn't do that. Also, I thought of it as a super-fast jump-in, grab-one, jump-out item and I waited ten minutes... so... yeah... a mixed bag, Top Dog...

The dogs are good, the deal's good, but the Center St owner can be a jerk.  My wife and I used to go there once sometimes even twice a week (good after working out).  Never again.

It was November.  Freezing.  It's 10pm, we were all shivering, my hands were so cold they hurt.  The music was blasting unusually loud, which normally I don't care about, it's his place, his music, whatever.  We sit down OUTSIDE as far away as possible.  The windows were open so it was just as freezing inside the place as outside.  Whatever.

My friends and I tried to talk-- yet the music was so loud this was impossible except for yelling "what" three times.  We try for several minutes and fail because of the owner's music.  So finally I slide one of the the windows closed put some glass between us and the music so we could talk.  The other window few feet from us was still wide open.

The owner gets up, walks all the way over, and re-opens the window.  

And turns the music up.  

And if that wasn't enough, when I get up to get my Calabrese dog after that, it's burnt.  Sometimes they're a little crispy and slightly black, whatever, this was way past that.  It was over half black and like bark.  My wife's too.  Almost inedible, not by shi-shi Bay Area standards, but by any standards.

I was too mad to argue at that point.  

I've never gone back.  He cooks them all day for years, he knew he'd burned it.

Yes, part of Top Dog is rebel "buck the system" attitude, but when the owner goes that far out of his way to annoy regular customers that were busy going out of their way for his precious lifestyle-- so much for that.

I went here four times because:

1) I love sausage
2) I wanted to try many sausages
3) I wanted to make sure my distaste was not just my distaste for the libertarian propaganda plastered all over the walls

BUT I feel as if I can safely say that I am not a fan of top dog despite my bias. I had three main problems:

1) The bread-to-meat ratio was much too high
2) The servers always seemed extremely unhappy to be there and were rude to customers
3) The sausages were average at best. They do not compare to Rosemunde's or the ones at Taylor's in Oakland.

O-VER-RATE-ED!
Nothing to add, except don't order the linguisa. It's gross. Everything else is good.

Sausage is a wonderful thing for people who like their meats.  For the locals who like Top Dog, you might want to try this particular location in downtown Berkeley.  I know there are purists who have to have theirs from the hole-in-the-wall on Durant.  That location has to keep the grill temp on high because of the heavy volume of orders.  That means the sausages come out with a noticeable crust of blackened meat.  My doctor friends point out that you're in an entire new level of unhealthiness when you get into heavy charring.  Me, I just don't like the taste of burnt meat.  The downtown location keeps the grill at a temp that keeps the charring light so you taste all that sausagey goodness.

For out-of-towners who need something quick, cheap, and not-so-nutritious, you can't go wrong.  The sausages are well-made at the respective factories and the flat-grilling makes them yummy.  They say that you don't want to know how sausages are made.  Then doubly so for these puppies, because I don't want anything to ruin the experience.  Everyone has their favorites.  Mine is the linguica.

Here's something very few people know about the linguica at Top Dog.  It comes from a not-so-laudable pedigree.  The recipe was taken from the now deceased "Sausage King."  If you haven't followed Bay Area news in the last 10 years or so, the "King" died on death row, sentenced after killing 3 meat inspectors.  

I pieced this together when I discovered the linguica had the texture of hardening cement when this guy was on trial.  The old ones came back after his sentencing but with a little less flavor.

I guess it's true, you really don't want to know how your sausages are made.  If there's anything good to come out of this tragedy is that someone rescued the recipe.  Thank goodness, too, because it's so freakin' delish.  The pork is practically fluffy in that sausage casing.  Nice spice and pillowed by Top Dog's grilled bun.  Now you know the lore, go git one.

I suppose, given a choice, I would want a sausage made in conformance with the health codes than one that skirts the rule of law.  Imagine, though, the violations in the creation, storage, and preparation of Spain's jamon.  Perhaps, some lenience should be given to old-world recipes.  I'm hoping there's a version of the linguica I loved still sold in Portugal.

Hot dogs are amazing, and this place certainly serves up a good weiner. (Nyuck nyuck)

Good, fast, cheap and delish.

MMMM! Polka Kielbasa, with a mountain of hot sour kraut!!! Linguica. I love me some Top Dog. Of course I'd worry about an establishment that can't make a decent hot dog. I'd eat one every day, if I wasn't worried about having a heart attack at an early age.
The people are cool there and the prices are the best.

Move over stanley's, Top Dog is the BAW$. 

This place is amazing. You MUST come here. You have no excuse especially when it's only $3 for a hotdog. REALLY? How is this possible!? This amazing meal for less than $5 with drink. Sent by God himself, I'm sure.

I had the hotlink, and boy it was delicious. A nice amount of spice, but be careful 'cause this is the SRZ BUSINESS. 

Considering moving to Berkeley JUST for this and Ici!

Everything is delicious. I love EVERYTHING Top Dog has to offer, but I tend to gravitate towards Chicken Apple/Brown Mustard + RC cola combo.  mmmmm....

As a student, Top Dog was my inexpensive pick-me-up after miserable classes on North Side.  Now , as an alum, the one on Center is much more accessible when going to bball games.  Quality seems pretty much the same at all of the Berkeley locations -- no bad experiences yet!

As the name implies, one can purchase cylindrical rods of meat here, often referred to as "tube-steaks". This establishment focuses solely on tube-steaks, and thus there are a variety of different types to try.

I found my order (bratwurst) to be tasty and filling. Nothing that changed my life or my perspective on role of intestine-encased food stuffs, but still very satisfying. This alone would have merited a 4 start rating in my mind. However, a few things hold me back from giving this establishment this sort of honors.

1 - The tables and counters were a bit on the dirty side. I think this is largely because they only give you a piece of wax paper with your item, and no plate, tray, or place mat was immediately available. So, if you stuff your bun to the max with relish, onions, and the like and you explode everywhere (like I did), that food shrapnel is going all over the table.

2 - I sort of expected that, for fast food hot dogs, the cheapest dog I could get would be $2 or $2.50. However, the lowest the prices went was $3. Now, most of the options were $3, so you can just order something a bit fancier and it's completely reasonable. However, considering how cheap regular old vanilla hot dogs are in general, I was kind of hoping for a lower floor for the prices.

3 - The music was a tad grating, though this might have been just bad luck and they normally have a string quartet playing there at most times for all I know.

4 - I found myself in need of washing my hands after consuming my consumable, but the establishment didn't have a bathroom.
