Top Dog shares a space w/ the adjacent Mexican restaurant, where I was able to find hygiene satisfaction...but his technically might have been an abuse of their washroom, as I didn't buy nothin' there. Double negative.

All that aside, if you're looking for a cheap meal that fills you up and makes your mouth pretty happy, check Top Dog out. Just might wanna back a wet nap or two.

Wow, I have not been to this Top Dog in forever, but now that Douche L. won't be going there because of the mean ol' Libertarian propaganda and NRA posters (?) I'm gonna go there twice for every one time he ever went!  

I recall the sauerkraut being excellent at this location.  Just the thing before an afternoon of straw-purchasing ammunition for the neighborhood youths.

Edit: 

I have been informed that Douche L. does not mention Obama Sock Puppets or Hillary Nut Crackers in his review.  That is true; he mentions them in another review: http://www.yelp.com/biz/greetings-oakland#hrid:JQ7ieD2XbJmqWEUunED5RA.   I certainly did not make up Obama Sock Puppets and had no idea those existed until I read that review.  Hilllary Nut Crackers, OTOH, I knew about and I still want to collect all of them.  In any case, I feel it is my duty to continue to mention them because they are so witty and exemplify a delightfully irreverent branch of political Americana.

If you ask Berkeley students or residents where you should eat, you inevitably get "Top Dog" as an answer.  

I go here once in awhile, and I like the fact that they have a bigger location, so you can actually sit down.  I've only had the lemon chicken dog, but I really like it, though I'm not much of a hot dog aficionado.

The one downside to Top Dog is the price.  $3 for a hot dog is a bit too much :(

When your mom gives you thumbs up on eating a weiner, you know you entered a whole new dimension of eats....the smoked apple sausage was awesome, the bits of apples were huge and the sesame bun was nicely toasty and hot.

The server was rather gruff, especially when I asked how big the dogs were just cause I don't want to get too big a serving since I'm sick...dude kept repeating himself over and over like a broken record that all the dogs were the same size...I know it's the same size...you already told me but I'm asking about something else...don't treat me like the UC kids still roaming around...I'm not the type to take that kinda shite 'tude from anyone *glares with glinty eyes*...the extra star is only cause your food is actually good.
Parking is crappy, but then you're near the campus so just drop your car off at the free 2 hour areas and truck on over.

Since I moved to Berkeley last year, everybody has been telling me about the amazing Top Dog. I finally got a chance to go there, but I wasn't that impressed. Maybe it was over-hyped and I expected so much more. They do have great hot dogs, but it is not amazing.

I didn't know about this Top Dog location until I passed it up while walking to the Greek Theater for a Jason Mraz concert. I got the German Frankfurter just so I could have something to tie me over during the 2.5 hour concert. It was tasty and manageable to eat while walking. I've always liked the bread they use.

It's obviously not as busy as the original location and you get the same product. Hot dogs probably will never get played out as a quick/cheap meal.
I ordered the hot links and it was great! I loved it. I knew it wasn't going to be that spicy but they do have jalapeños.

I can think of no more satisfying snack than one of the oh so delicious lemon chicken dogs at this fine establishment. It really is hard to beat a warm, satisfying mouthful of juicy, delicately flavored chicken wrapped up in a tasty bun after a long day of classes. Oh, but, rest assured, the lemon chicken isn't the only delectable item on the menu. If heaven were populated with sausages, Top Dog would be God's right hand man, managing all those luscious links with grace and ease. It seems like most people I know like going there after a night of drinking, but for me, it's a treat best enjoyed sober.

Every time I wear my Top Dog shirt, people ask me if I work there--I don't know if it's my love for Top Dog that shows, or if it's everyone else's love for Top Dog that makes them want to talk about it.  This location on Center Street is the one I frequent the most, when I need a pre- or post-movie snack.  Top Dog serves a world of sausages, including their all-beef Top Dog hotdog, kielbasa, bratwurst, bockwurst, chicken, veggie, etc.  Their buns aren't the typical squishy hotdog buns--they have a nice chew and a little bit of a crust.  I cannot play favorites here, but if I had to choose, I'd have to say the kielbasa is the pick of the litter--it's got a nice snap in the skin and very bold flavor.  I also like the delicate bockwurst as well.  The veggie dog has a nice, spicy bite to it, so don't pass it over, either.  You can add your own condiments and dressings (onions, sauerkraut, relish) to taste; you can have them put chili on your dog, but I've never tried that because it's pretty satisfying as is.  (I get my chili dog fix from Pink's.)  Aside from the fabulous sausages and the lovable logo, I adore Top Dog because they have RC cola on tap.  That, to me, is a mark of fine taste.

I love that I can grab a spicy cal or yummy birddog on the way to BART from campus!  A hot dog with spicy mustard and a lemonade!  What a treat for a quick bite! 

I have been eating these TOP DOGS since freshman year 1989 (one of the causes of the gaining of the freshman 10-15 lbs).  And why I needed to lay off of them towards the end of my college career... but have since found myself craving one from time to time.  What a great location to find myself once in a while seeing those sizzling dogs cookin' then savoring every juicy bite.  

Top Dog is as Berkeley as hippies, oski the bear, nobel prize winners, peoples park, and horrible losing Cal football teams with overpaid coaches who take solid in year by year replays of "the Play!"

Go Top Dog.

Top Dog is a simple place with a long tradition.  This particular location is very convenient if you're popping in off of BART to catch a basketball game, but it's not their best.  If you want tradition go to north side and sit down amongst the anarchy articles and radical literature in a classic hot dog hovel.

In any case, the food seems to be the same at all of the locations so I need not repeat myself.  My order is normally 2 hots, a german and a hot, german and a brat, hot and a brat, etc...  All of their sausages are good, and the spicy Russian mustard and onions are cheap but delicious.  Top Dog is not exactly the fastest, but it's the best hot dog and sausage stand in Northern California and maybe the best in the world.

If you wear a Top Dog shirt outside of Berkeley you will attract fellow sausage lovers (not women or homosexuals, eating sausage you pig) who will throw you high fives or stop and chat about their days at Cal.

Top Dog has almost everything a degenerate Cal student needs, except beer.  I don't know if they have alcohol but they used to sell smokes.

For what it is, this is a great place to pick up a quick meal. I think we had like 10 minutes to eat before the show we wanted to see was going to start. We inhaled a dog apiece, some potato salad and were good to go.

I stuck with the regular (all beef) frankfurter but I was told the chicken apple was the bomb. That's next on the list, along with the lousiana hot links and brats.

First of all, I have to say that my sausage bar is set pretty high since i have the privilege of living super close to some frickin' awesome sausage places.  So my experience is tainted.

So, on my visit to Top Dog I had the bockwurst, 'cause i love that vealy stuff.  It looks like the sausages are partially precooked, but I'm not 100% sure about that, they were hanging out next to the grill.  Anywho, after the short wait for "cooking" I found my sausage tasted OK, probably about as good as a store bought one; I think it was a Saag's sausage since there is a Saag's advert prominently displayed in the dining area (they also serve Molinari sausage, probably their Italian, and I think Schwartz' fine sausages).  I liked that the buns were not your average hotdog bun, but a sesame studded bun.  I was about to have a conniption becuase I initially didn't see any sauerkraut, but then opened my eyes and saw a cool kraut warmer chock full of kraut right in front of me.  There also was four different mustards (and ketchup, obviously for hosers) some onions, sweet relish, and jalepenos; overall not a bad condiment collection.  MM had a veggie dog, she said it was mealy, not so good.  And their chili is three bean.  I didn't have any but I prefer zero bean chili.

The whole setup of TD is pretty efficient, nice little seating area, grill, big menu, soda and condiment  section on the side.  Simple menu with dogs, chips, drinks and not much else.  One wall is adorned with signed black and white photos of some celebrities, I had no idea who any of them were, some news articles and other political seeming stuff.

I love sausage places and although i don't think that Top Dog is necessarily tops, at 3 bucks a pop, this ain't too bad a place to git your tube steak fix.

Like the Top Dog on Hearst which is where I'd go if I parked in the area for a show, this TD is for if I take the Bart. Not many places open after shows on this stretch where you can get a quick bite to eat before hitting the public transit for the night. Frankfurter fix on the way to the Center street station!

Top Dog! How could I forget about my dogs?!

Love the Chicken Lemon and the OG Top Dog itself. The bread is delicious.

Though the dogs at this place is supposedly not "as good" as some proclaim as the original Top Dog on Durant, it's somewhat tucked-away location more than makes up for it.

$3/dog.  It's not Costco price, but not Costco either.  Much better flavor!

I love the buns and the condiments.  I had the Calabrese each time.  I love that one.  Their Hot Link is really spicy, but flavorful too.

Be careful, it can be addicting.  But then again, you have RC cola to wash it down.

Likes: Lemon chicken and smoked apple chicken top dogs are the best.  Bun is toasted to a perfect crisp.  Self-help yourselves to the condiments on the side.

Dislikes: It saddens me to watch the price go up over the years.

This place should be like Starbucks, with one on every corner. Hot dogs have a bad reputation, but Top Dog makes bad taste so good. 

The place is a stones throw away from campus and the restaurant is about the size of a large bedroom. Top Dog offers between 10-15 different dogs with side dish options of potato salad and three-bean chili. I ordered the only vegetarian dog on the menu, which was conveniently called, "The Weenie." Taking no offense to the name of the dog, when I got the thing, I piled it mile high with condiments. The dog was encased with a perfectly toasted bun, and when I smelled the dog I knew I was in for a pleasurable experience. 

What an understatement! This thing was amazing. After a few bites, I had to slow down my chewing and concentrate on what I was eating. My taste buds have never felt this way before. You know when in the movies a father is given his baby for the first time and the look on his face makes time slow down around him and he focuses in on his newborn? I had that moment! Okay, maybe a slight exaggeration, but this thing was really good. For a moment there I questioned my nine years of dedication to vegetarianism because if "The Weenie," tasted this good, the others could be just as good or better.

I recommend Top Dog to anyone with taste buds. If you are a student or not, somehow find three dollars and skip on over to Top Dog. These dogs will rock your world.

I'm all about a place where you can get a whole lunch for under $5 (dog, chips and soda for $4.75). The hot dogs are delicious, the bread is delicious, and that spicy mustard almost made me pass out. 

There's not a whole of seating, but you really don't need a full-out dining room if you're a hot dog joint. Just grab and go. If you can find a tiny corner, take it and read all the interesting articles and literature posted around the walls. 

You really cannot go wrong here. A definite quick lunch stop.

Personally, I find Top Dog to be the perfect place to grab lunch. Close to work (for me, at least), cheap, easy, tasty, and above all not too heavy and filling, so I don't feel like I'm going to fall into the typical food coma at my desk after the lunch hour.

All I gotta say is $3 HOT!!Link!
I recommend

Beyond the oft-closed Original Kaspers, there are two places to get a hot dog in Berkeley/Oakland: 
Top Dog
Casper's

Top Dog's a little better, but once someone at Casper's gave us an extra bunless-dog for our dogs.

Gotta get a top dog loaded up with onions, ketchup, mustard, relish and scarf it down.  Get a second.  All the dogs and sausages are good, they are grilled with a bite, juicy on the inside, yummy roll.  Get a doggie bag for five bucks for a good lunch.  I challenge you to buy one for one of the hungry homeless people that are on the sidewalk.  Some of them have not eaten in a while and it will make you feel good about yourself!  :)

There are many locations of Top Dog around UCB's campus and I've only been to two.  One being at this location and the other being on Durant.  The nice thing about the Center location is that it does have a little bit more space here than at the other location so if you actually want to stick around and eat, I would recommend going there.  Also, they also accept credit cards for purchases $5 or more, so if you don't ever have cash in the wallet, Center would be the right location to go.  However, the people that work at the Durant location are a hoot to sit and talk to, so I definitely would check that location out as well.

I've tried a few different dogs at Top Dog and the one that I keep going back to eating would be the hot link.  The hot link is the kind of spicy that the more you eat, the more spicy it gets.  I've also tried the Bird Dog and the Linguica and I enjoyed both but they didn't compare to eating the Hot Link.

I think the thing that makes Top Dog so good would be the roll that they use at the hot dog bun.  It's like a french roll that is toasted, slightly sweet, and goes really well with the dog.

Hot dog is $3, chips are $1, and a small soda is another $1.  Very budget meals.  One might not be enough for big eaters so I would recommend either getting a chili cheese dog or else doing 2 dogs.

I had the "top dog frankfurter" as an appetizer before eating dinner at Brazil Cafe.  I was watching Bourdain last night and he was in chicago eating a red hot hot dog.  It looked good so I was craving one all day.  For $3 you get a weiner in a french roll.  I felt I could make this at my house for less than $3.  I probably should have ordered the chicken apple sausage but I judge a place based on the basic dog that should be good.  It was definitely good but costco is also good and cheap.

One location on is on Northside, a lot smaller, another on Durant.  This one has at least some seating.  Great for between-class cravings or a late night bite.  And it's like half a block, literally, from BART.  I remember my favorite being the Polish dogs, but I haven't been here since I was at Cal.  A Berkeley institution for sure.

I heart you, Top Dog. When it comes to the classic American hot dogs and buns, you will forever be my top choice/top dog. 

My favorite is the smoked chicken apple sausage; ahh, tasty, smokey flavor with little apple bits (or perhaps, I imagined it, b/c I'm so head over heels for this place). I think the bun at Top Dog is probably my favorite hot dog bun...ever. It's not your filmsy hot dog buns that turn out mushy after you dress your dog with condiments. Nope, this bun can withstand any amount of mustard, ketchup, relish, etc.., plus, it's got sesame seeds sprinkled all over and it's toasted. 

Anyway, for $3, Top Dog is the best. And no, don't compare Top Dog to Costco hot dog/polish sausage... sure it's cheaper at Costco and you get a drink, but you get what you paid for. So, no, there is no comparison. End of story. Or maybe I'm a little biased, because this place is such a Berkeley establishment and well-received among Cal students.

P.S. There's another location on Durant (across from the Asian Ghetto), but this place is closer to BART and it has actual seating. The Durant location is often swarmed with undergrads, especially in the wee hours after a night out.

Not being a hot dog aficionado I can't rave too much about this place, but they seem to do their dogs right, and people I talk to who are more into their long fleshy meats than I seem to love this place.

Top Dog is a Berkeley institution. You can't be from the 510 and/or a Cal student and not know about this place. It's a simple, no-fuss, hotdog/links joint. Everything is $3. The sauerkraut is warm. The bread is not some limp junky store-bought bun, but very quality, and toasted with a sprinkling of sesame seeds. There's propaganda plastered all over the walls (love Berkeley). They make all their dogs in-house and as much of a carnivore as I tend to be, there's something to be said about the fact that I constantly crave their delicious veggie dog (lovingly named "The Weenie"), unlike most veggie products which are horrid, rubbery and astringent tasting (I'm really holding back here), it's actually so delicious that I forget about the fact that I'm not eating any part of a lovely animal. But not to fear, everything else porky (and chicken-y or turkey, as well) on their menu is also delicious, plump, juicy - and, of course, there's nothing like that first bite into that crunchy casing.

There are several locations in B-town, and while the Center St. location is not nearly as infamous as their Durant Ave. one, a few notables: this one has actual seating, they take card (the rest are all cash-only, I believe), and they are much closer to Bart.

This past Saturday nothing tasted better than the sweet victory and dominating performance by Cal over Stanford in the Big Game to win back the Axe, but Top Dog came close. 

Top Dog is definitely an institution centered around The Institution and is one of my favorite spots in the Bay Area to grab a dog. Any one of their locations around the Cal campus has some of the best Game Day grub if you aren't going to a tailgate party prior to the game.

The hot Russian mustard is hotter than the Louisianna hot link! Whew! Spicier than a mail order Balkan bride versus a red headed Ragin Cajun! 

Bigger and cleaner than the original on the south side on Durant! Plus it has a view window to watch Center street passersby, which is a step up the food chain than the south side homeless hippies. 

Still all the charm of an Appalachian trailer park family barbeque, but now with more healthier choices besides a Top, Bock, or Kiel from the old days! Lemon-chicken dog? Isn't that a Chinese delicacy?

Also unlike Durant Street, there are actually more than 2 stools to sit and mouth that wiener between your lips! 

But like Durant, there is still that stainless tub of relish, and that crockpot full of warm sauerkraut! But I do miss the "Vote for Malarkey" bumper sticker of Top Dog #1.

Ah, sweet memories of Berkeley are not complete without the Top Dog experience revisited regularly.

Top Dog is the best hot dog joint around, hands down.  The owner is cool & I usually got good service from the other folks who work there too.  However, I decided after the recent Virginia Tech shooting not to go there anymore because of all the gun/NRA/libertarian propaganda they have on the walls.  it's a tough choice, but as a consumer and as a citizen of this country, I have the freedom as well as the obligation to vote with my dollar every day.
4 - 1/2 STARS?!?  They're just frickin hot dogs!  Good selection of them though.

Mmmm top dog, there's nothing like you on this side of the tunnel.  Shhh! But don't tell your competators that sell your sausages over here.

Nothing compares to the way you guys do it, even my boyfriend who thought I was nuts before taking him here is now a believer.

I'm all about the lemon chicken, so damn good!

Finally, a non-SF review!!! Yay, I have a LIFE outside of the city!

Being a Cal alum I KNOW the institution that is Top Dog. For years I had to resort to going to the teensy tiny counter on Durant Street, endured standing outside in the cold since there was nowhere to stand and I always went there after midnight, and practiced being apathetic to all the loonies that hang around Telegraph. But it was all worth it to have the best sausages ever (my personal favs: lemon chicken, smoked chicken apple, calabrese, top dog)

With the opening of the Center Street location, that all changed! This place is so much roomier, with actual biased-cut counter eating space, and a real TV to watch. And now that I don't live in Berkeley anymore, it's less than a block from the downtown BART station. I make it my routine to always stop by Top Dog whenever I visit Berkeley. And it can get crowded on game days for sure. My recent visits saw a tall guy with long blond hair and a petite Asian girl working the best team: he would shout at the top of his lungs to get people to order and work the grill, and she would count up the totals at the cash register and handle the $$$. Never did I see they falter when the line got long or if people were shouting multiple orders at them. They always managed to keep the orders on track. Such efficiency and work ethic.

If you're craving for late-night snack in Berkeley, Top Dog's your place.

the top dog here doesn't have all the political literature on the walls that the durant location has. there's also some seating here. the menu here is the usual litter of dogs.  

sampling: bockwurst(3) german style sausage made of  pork and veal
-fresh taste. russian hot mustard crowded out any flavoring bockwurst had.
-4 types of mustard, relish, sauerkrauft, onions, ketchup available for toppings
-ready within minutes. dogs pregrilled.

leftovers:
-dogs made by schwarz meats.
-this locale near bart station.
-people often get bratwurst and bockwurst mixed up
-fast, friendly, efficient service.

The purists are going to hate me...

frank/sausage/weiner/dog/brat/link - What ever you call the grilled delights, you are sure to find one that you like at Top Dog. 

I've been to Top Dog on several occasions and can safely say that they've mastered the art of grilling a frank/sausage/weiner/dog/brat/link.  

On one occasion I had the standard fare (a hot dog) and it was pretty darn good. On another occasion I ordered the spicy link (in an inebriated state of being) and all I can recall, was sitting in the passenger seat on the way home saying - "it's good.. but it's so spicy." 

Translation: It must have been pretty spicy if was complaining about the heat  - especially after a night of "imbibification" rituals.

When I was in Aruba, I was suckered in to eating a frikandel and it was amazing.  Granted it was real (mystery) meat and there's something about mayo that adds that little extra kick.  I went in to Top Dog hoping for some kind of substitute, some kind of in between so I don't have to find a dutch food stand somewhere.  But I guess I got the wrong thing.

I ordered a veggie dog and loaded it up with sauerkraut and hot Russian mustard, a jalapeno, and a drop of ketchup (there was no mayo in sight).  I took a bite and it made my nose burn and my eyes water a bit, (great mustard!!!), but the sausage itself was disappointing.  Granted it was a veggie dog with wheat gluten and stuff but I've had some pretty good veggie dogs that didn't have such a strange texture.  This one resembled...chopped up eraser.  It was coarse and not exactly firm, chewy but crumbly.  In the end, I ate it for the condiments.  

I was disappointed in my choice.  I'm still looking for a frikandel.  If I go back to Top Dog, I hope I am no longer a veggie and will think about ordering something with meat in it.  Because the veggie sucked.  And they were so proud of it, too.  All these signs on the walls saying, "Finally, our new and tasty veggie dog $3."  If they start having frikandels, I'll totally eat it, mystery meat or no.

Ohhh yummy yummy i love their veggie wienie.  I could eat 20 a day.  I would get fatter and fatter but enjoy every bite ooo ahhh yummwah
love's it!

My childhood dream came true!

As a kid, I would leaf through Archies and imagine sharing a hot dog with Jughead. I share many of his traits, I am lazy, laid-back, can sleep through exam preps and end up getting good scores, and love love food so much so that I earned "garfield' as a nickname.

I would talk to my parents about American food, and they would discourage me by saying- 'ohh, but it has meat in it, and is probably bland!'.

 I loved the burgers I ate in McD's after liberalization in India. Moved here after marriage and continued to enjoy my burgers.

Hotdogs remained on my list. Was walking out of school and decided why not step in and try the veggie. 

The 'top dog' made me go mmmmm! It was my first but will not be my last!

Hot Dog, Chips and a Drink
Doggy Bag= $5.00
Where else can you go and get a pretty decent meal for $5 bucks?

The inside embodies the Berkeley character. Political cartoons and clipped news paper decorated throughout the small interior's walls and counter tops. My favorite is the full-page article about our government; illustrated as if it were a twisted science project..

The cooks are nice, and the atmosphere is very easy and casual. They aren't afraid to speak their mind, and they strike me as nothing but down-to-earth.

There are a huge variety of dogs you can choose to put on a grilled bun. Self-serve toppings include relish, onions, and sauerkraut. Ketchup, yellow mustard, and deli mustard also included. The result is at least as good as any dog you'll get at a ballpark.

I recommend the  regular "top dog." It's prepared perfectly and can  be eaten alone, it's that good! .....  I'm salivating right now thinking about it.

Man, once you've had a top dog it is so hard to pass by the opportunity to have another.

I must warn the address listed on this review is for the one that is not open as late (maybe til 10 on weeknights, 11 or 12 on weekends?) as the one on DURANT AVE--this is where the drunks go, and it's where I recommend you go if you plan on being drunk. 

My first experience with Top Dog was when I was a little intoxicated and a friend decided I needed the hot dog of my life. I had a Calbreze (a "Cal" for the informed) which was intensely satisfying.

I must also mention and compliment the work ethic, attitude, and dependability of the staff at top dog, especially the durant ave location. Despite a seemingly endless line of people waiting to pick up or order their hot dogs, and the quick cash-dealings, this man kept track of who ordered what, who ordered before who, who paid and who didn't--he handled the drunk people like a pro, and kept his responsabilities in check with seemingly little effort and NO PAPER. Even if you aren't a meat eater, I'd recommend sitting outside this joint on a busy drinking night just to watch the staff in action--it's really quite impressive.

Top Dog is #1
The veggie dog covered in sauerkraut, the extra hot beaver brand Russian mustard, relish, and a few onions is a good time for my mouth.
a really really really good time.
I love that Top Dog is around, and I can get a delicious hot dog, and sit in the window seat and watch people walking down the street (while mustard drips down my chin)
good times. 
This is my favorite Top Dog- second fave is on Durrant, and third fave is the one in Big Longs.

As much as I love my 1.50 polish sausage and soft drink combo from Costco. Nothing says Berkeley like Top Dog #5! The price is right. Under 3 dollars for a chicken and apple sausage that was oh so tasty. 

I never knew there was a #5 until a couple weeks ago. This place used to be a smoothie joint when I lived in the area. Nevertheless same good quality as the 2 other ones I had frequented.

Being a wiener seems to be a prerequisite to working at this location... but I guess interacting with surly staff is part of the experience for some people. The sausages are delicious: they are grilled to the point of juicy perfection and served on an ample toasted bun. Perfect for grabbing quick nourishment while on the go.

Compared to all its other locations in the city, this one has some more waiting room and is located in a more comfortable environment. It's close to major transit lines and it's right smack dab in downtown. There is even some seating inside. As for service, it's just a tiny notch better, but workers' temper is just as short and food is no better. Food is relatively fast. Overall, it's just OK.

Dinner date for under $10?  Top Dog!

Ok so I wouldn't suggest coming here on a 1st date unless you know you're about to date a hot dog fanatic, but Husband and I have been together for a decade and a half- no romantic restaurant needed for every date- and we're both hotdog fanatics!  

My favs- Lemon Chicken & Polish!  So hard not to get both!

I put on lots of saurkraut- thems the veggies!

This location manages to maintain the fringe charm of the original, wihtout the slimy grunge feeling.  Besides, it's near Games of Berkeley, also a great place for us to wander on a date and compare favorite games from our childhood & discuss what games we want out daughter to grow up with.

The Calabrese sausage here is perfectly porky goodness.  Nicely grilled with a bit of char, instead of horribly steamed or - eek - boiled, it has snap, is juicy and was bursting with savoriness for ever and a touch of spice.  

The sausage-griller guy there just gave it to me when I said I didn't want the bun - from his hot tongs to my greedy  hands - a kind of sweet awesomeness one usually only finds in their own back yard.  Three bucks worth of bliss. I'm so glad that I ducked in by myself and had one, even though the other people I was walking around with that day didn't want one. Ha, missed out....

He said that they either order their sausages from Chicago, or the people who make them have some kind of  Chicago connection.  If this is indeed true I am pissed the hell off, because I've lived in Chicago for several years now and I have never had a sausage here as good as the one I had there.

I think I've tried every dog on the menu here, and on my most recent visit I got a chance to reaffirm my unholy love for the tubular meat product that Top Dog slings so well.

I think my all time favorites here are the hot link and the bird dog. The hot link, especially when it gets that nice burn on it, snaps satisfyingly. The slight heat of the meat is also really enjoyable. I love cilantro, so getting that bite of cilantro from the bird dog always makes me really happy.

My wife was semi-disappointed by the veggie dog here, but I can't really speak to its quality, since I refused to try it based on the principle that veggie dogs are fucking awful in every conceivable way.

The first time I came to Top Dog I made the mistake of slathering way too much of the Russian mustard on my hot dog, and though it wasn't spicy, my sinuses cleared out to the max. Since then, I put a thinner smear of it on my hot dog, and pile on jalapenos for heat.

Now we're back on track. When visitors ask "what is there to eat in the city of Berkeley?" some of the locals will say "Top Dog, dog!"

Matt knew that this top-flight popular hangout for college students is a "must eat." Since Berkeley is a city with many opportunities, Matt wanted to explore other options to dine. And with Berkeley being hit or miss for choosing "yours truly" to eat, dining at Top Dog came at an ideal time. 

There are 12 different varieties of dogs to choose from. (No, Matt is not Kobayashi or Joey Chestnut and didn't eat all of them at one time!). He bought the Lemon-Chicken and the Calabrese dog. Each cooked wiener is $3.00 each and placed in a toasty warm-bun. The Lemon-Chicken was very lean and tangy with the lemon-flavor. The spicy Calabrese dog is Pork wiener with paprika and fennel. Just by describing this dog, you can easily tell that it was spicy and flavorful. 

The condiment section was well-stocked and colorful at the midday. Matt loaded up the freshest and necessary topping to make the 2 hot-dogs very hearty. 

Coming to Top-Dog for lunch was very settled, unlike the weekend, where you'll wait an eternity to get your dog. Also, if you're a visitor to the city of Berkeley like Matt, you can't leave without having a "Top Dog".

Yay!  I'm a fan!

All dogs are priced at $3 a pop at prime location?!  Wow!

I'm a fan of hot dogs, just not a real big fan.  I seldom crave for a good dog, it's one of those like when I see it, I'll get it type of deal.

BF brought me here since I didn't have much craving for anything, and a dog sounded good.  And the "I CAN'T BELIEVE YOU HAVEN'T TRIED TOP DOG" look on his face ensured me that the dog should be heavenly delicious.  I trust his taste.

So we venture off to Berkeley, drove by Durant Ave, saw no parking, and headed to this Center street location to test our parking luck.  

Yep Center street location was meant to be, we got rock star parking.  And there were seats!  

Two perfectly grilled chicken apple dogs later (one for the bf, and one for me), we were yearning for more!

I got myself a Lemon Chicken (low sodium, low fat?) guiltless pleasure?!  COUNT ME IN!  The bf got a garlic frankfurter.   We pretty much devoured the dogs within minutes.  They were THAT good.  

Sausage were juicyly grilled to perfection, sitting on top of the toasted bun.  I dressed my dog with some hot sauerkraut, little bit of horseradish, and some jalapeno.  No ketchup needed.  

BF went back to order the 3rd dog (Kielbasa), as I gave him the jealous glare....  WHY DO MEN HAVE MORE STOMACHE SPACE IN GENERAL?!  I want a 3rd dog!  I just can't fit another bite!  DAYAMSIT!

I actually managed to take another bite.  Kielbasa was GOOD~!  Meaty and hearty! 

On our way back, the only thing in my mind was... which dog should I try next on the next visit....

An amigo gave me a double recommendation: 1. Top Dog is top dog; 2. Order (then eat) the Bird Dog (turkey sausage with red and green peppers).

I ordered over the phone and dude I talked with was super nice. He said that we has about to be bombarded with high school students, but would hold my (insert your euphemism here for h-dog/sausage). I walked over and it was hot and ready - like any dog should be. The dude who took my order took my money and had great interpersonal skills. He made waiting in line fun.

I got back to High Trek Adventure's world headquarters and was smitten. I would double recommend Top Dog and the Bird Dog to anyone.

"Believe what you're told, there'd be chaos if everybody thought for themselves".

This is only one of many political messages posted around the walls of every Top Dog in Berkeley. At the bottom right corner of each poster is also a little price tag to reflect the oxymoron of a decor filled with leftist messages for sale while the business operates on a fordist model that produces the world's best hot dogs. I used to spend a lot of time at the original location on Durant Ave. but tonight I had to check this place out for the first time. In the past, my usuals were bird dog (turkey), bockwurst (pork & veal), hot link (beef & 4 peppers), linguica (smoked pork), and bratwurst (pork). Nowadays I don't eat hot dogs as often anymore but these are still my favorites of all time.

Tonight I ordered the lemon chicken and it was another case of oxymoron because it was 100% flavor and low fat, low sodium, and no preservatives. I thought to myself, "What a twisted way of taking the best of a socially conscious hot dog and make use of capitalism as a distributive mechanism for the masses?!" I think the owner of Tog Dog is onto something, don't you think? With a total of twelve different types of hot dogs to choose from, each are just $3.

With tons of juicy flavors supported by a hint of garlic and palpable lemon, my hot dog was served on a warm French roll fresh off the griddle, leaving enough room to hold lots of ketchup and spicy brown muster while I piled on the warm sauerkraut. Yum! My lemon chicken was truly awesome and there's no other hot dogs like it, period. 

For 75 cents more, you can upgrade your order into a three bean chili dog so that might be something worthwhile to consider. Service was friendly and everybody was welcomed and treated with respect. I would love to be back and to have a chance to visit their other locations. Love this place!

Their lemon-chicken hot dog is simply the best! 
Period! 
(dontcha just hate that word? I know I used an exclamation mark and not a period --- if you're gonna be pedantic about it) 

Just the thought of their warm lightly-toasted sesame roll wrapped around the simple yet fabulous lemon chicken sausage sets my salivatory glands going into overdrive. I like mine without the sauerkraut or relish and opt for a dash of the mustard. The toasty roll with the "pop"-y sausage are a match made in heaven !

The chicken-apple too is pretty good, but my hard earned money is always on the lemon-chicken !

Ummmmm ... if hot dogs died and went to heaven, this place is it.

The Wienie is really good.  It's really good.  Really good.  R-E-A-L-L-Y G-O-O-D.

The Wienie, in case you don't know, is Top Dog's veggie dog.  Now, veggie dogs are notoriously hit or miss.  Whereas veggie burgers generally run the gamut from the bland to the amazing, veggie dogs are usually either atrocious/inedible or decent.  So it's normally a greater risk ordering a veggie dog than it is ordering a veggie burger; and because the sizes vary, it's almost always safer for your tastebuds, wallet, and appetite to opt for the burger over the dog.  And conveniently, Bongo Burger is just a couple of doors down from Top Dog on Center, so normally, I would advise you to play it safe--except you shouldn't.

Walk on down to Top Dog, right now, and order a Wienie.  If you're lucky, you'll get the worker who seems mean but isn't.  She's all business, and although her demands might seem, well, demanding, she's really just trying to be efficient.  She'll ask whether you want your Wienie grilled separately from the meat, and although she'll say it will take ten minutes, it's well worth it.  It probably won't take a full ten minutes, but even if it does, you'll get to witness her utter expertise as she juggles multiple confused customers' faltering orders.

Spending extra time in here will also quickly clue you in to the fact that Top Dog's owner is a libertarian.  Not a conservative Republican or any kind of Republican, really, but an honest-to-goodness libertarian.  There are actually quite a few of them in Berkeley, which isn't really as surprising at it seems at first.  Spend some time reading the posters on the walls; and then, when your Wienie is ready and you've finished loading it with mustard and the excellent relish they have, walk home and spend the seven minutes it takes to decide once and for all that libertarianism is clearly the most naive, unrealistic, and prone-to-nativism political philosophy there is.

But it's all right, because Top Dog will still be here the next time you walk down Center Street.  And it will still offer RC Cola in its fountain.  (Honestly.)  And there will still be the signed glossies of not-quite-famous libertarians on the walls.  And there will still be signs reminding you that using a water cup for soda is stealing and that taxes are stealing, for that matter.  But does Top Dog pay taxes?  If the sales tax is figured into the menu price, it does.  So is Top Dog stealing from me on behalf of the oppressive government?  Maybe, but I don't consider taxes theft, and I don't use water cups for soda, and I won't hold a place's politics against it--at least not a place that serves one of the best veggie dogs I've ever had.

I love this place! Every time I have been there the food was delicious and all of the salads packed with great flavors that went well together. The sodas are also perfectly flavored with fruit but not cloyingly sweet. I will be coming here alot.
Hands down, the most delicious food in Berkeley.
Fresh ingredients, adequate portions and sensible prices. Service is friendly and the location is unbeatable.

Probably THE cutest coffee place/cafe in Berkeley. I loved the decor and modernness to the place! Pretty quiet with lots of natural lighting, so a great study spot. 

I got a pour-over coffee for $3.50.. a bit pricey for a small, but it was really good! I don't remember the name, but it was some blend of dark chocolate/nutty flavor, I think.


Definitely a hidden gem in Berkeley :)

I love the location of Babette's and the food ingredients are always fresh and wholesome. My espresso, however, was pretty bad. 

And they have changed the portion size for salads. I paid about $7.50 for some orzo and some baby broccoli. I was expecting two filled bowls, as they usually serve their side salads in, and I got two little piles on a plate. An embarrassing amount of food. I should have sent it back.... It tasted great, but was waaaaaay too small. I think they did not make enough food for the day and were trying to skimp on portions.

Babette is a treasure, and manages to combine everything I look for in a study spot in one place, with free, quick wi-fi, excellent coffee that is both smooth and strong, without giving the jitters, friendly staff, and divine baked goods. The scone that I had was flakey and rich with nice, simple flavours, however, if you are veggi or vegan make sure to ask if the baker is using lard, butter or vegatable shortning.

Perfect lunch at Babette. A sunny afternoon, delicious glass of Austrian rosé, super friendly staff and sumptuous food. Minimal, thoughtfully designed seasonal menu has something for everyone. A hidden gem that is now permanently on my radar!

I stopped by because I wanted to try something other than cafe strada as I was walking up Bancroft. My $3 iced coffee was mediocre at best... A pitcher sits out unrefrigerated on the counter and they pour it over ice. Hmmm.

A better selection of food than the prior Remedy.  Hearty, tasty soup. ($5 bowl) Nice vegetable salads. ($3 for 1; $8 for all 3).  Good serving sizes -- just right for lunch.  Haven't tried the sandwiches yet since they're a bit more expensive ($9-10), but I think they come with a side salad?  Decent tea selection, though a brewed chai would be nice.  One quibble: cut the fig bars into equal-sized pieces!  My money should buy just as much as someone else's.  Oh, and bake a little longer... the bottom crust needed it.

Food is fantastic, espresso drinks were excellent and beautifully presented, deserts were irresistible!  Love that the menu changes regularly.  They focus on local foods from the farmers' market, so everything is fresh and tasty.  Gazpacho was just right, obviously made with some of the best heirloom tomatoes ever; pulled pork sandwich was amazing and served on perhaps the best roll I've ever had with a side of pickled veggies that complimented the sandwich perfectly.  The place is nice, clean, has a sort of neuvo/retro thing going on, and is quiet enough for a conversation or a meeting.  Indoor and outdoor seating are both great, as you're surrounded by the Berkeley Art Museum, which is a great architectural exhibit on its own.  Highly recommended!

The Babette barista who just prepared my pot of Derjeeling tea filled the tea strainer to brim with tea leaves and now my drink is unpalatably strong and bitter. This place certainly has potential and I wish them well but at least one of the employees needs a remedial course on tea.

Babette conveniently located for those visiting the Pacific Art Museum or passersby on Durant. 

The pulled pork tacos with yam tasted okay, but too pricey. The advertised mango salsa was nonexistent. Instead I had pickled radishes and vegetables that had too much sauce, which the taco absorbed, resulting in a sour experience.

Strawberry Tart tastes so good! Not too sweet yet fresh and only $1.50. Great for a sweet tooth.

This place is more of a "lets grab coffee" kind of place rather than a "lets hit the books" joint. Modern, hipster vibe. 

I got a strawberry rhubarb tart w/ brown butter. It was almost $4 which felt a little pricey, but I really liked it and it eased the pain for the test I was studying for.

I couldnt get over their checkout technology - ipad, sign with your finger, swipe the credit card on this little attachment on top of the ipad - very cool. 

Towards closing time they played music from star wars and indiana jones, which I thought was hilarious and pretty unique.

Personally for me, the cafe just didn't feel very cozy, which is why I won't be back to study, but I still think it's a cute little spot that's worth a trip to check out.

Just stopped in yesterday, surprised to see that Remedy had changed names. Had the shepherd's pie and it was great. Individual brewed coffee was good too, but maybe not worth the price. Shared an excellent chocolate tart.

When the French Onion tart arrived with about 5 leaves of a mixed green salad, my hungry heart sank.  I've had more generous appetizers and this was supposed to be lunch??11  $9.00.  It was, however, adequately tasty, with plenty of onion and a flaky if soggy crust.  The latte was less than generous and somewhat watery, however, the apple strudel-like pastry was top-notch.  But pricy at $4.00.  No price advertised on the tea, but that was $3.00 for a tiny pot (maybe I could have asked for a refill?).

Though I wouldn't use the "h" word, the decor and clean, airy, ambiance were pleasant, esp. with the plants embedded in the wall.  If you were on or near campus and wanted a bit more "grown up" place to have lunch (other than the student-oriented places), this would be it.  However, with so many other restaurants in Berkeley and North Oakland that deliver good food AND good value, this will not be a return place for me.

I stopped by Babette Cafe today, originally intending to pick up a cup of coffee from Strada, but realizing that I had no cash. 

I was very pleasantly surprised. The bright orange and green color scheme and modern decor was a refreshing change from all of the places in Berkeley that I've been to so many times. The staff was really friendly and joked around with me while I waited for my coffee, and tried some of the pastries. The pastry was really delicious, and the mocha that I ordered was okay. It seemed a little watered down. 

Overall I really like the ambience here, and would definitely come back here to study and try more menu items.

New favorite study spot near campus - a hipstery little slice of heaven. 

Pros:
- The food is really good. I highly recommend the salad choices of the day, though I've noticed it's much more economical to get 1 for $3.00 versus 3 for $9.00 as the single serving ends up being really big and a better bang for your buck. Yes, I'm cheap.
- Very friendly and cute staff
- I feel cool hanging out in an art museum
- Delicious remedy coffee
- Good Cal wireless
- Clean, modern space that you never want to leave

Cons:
- Service is really slow. Yes, I like that you use an iPad and Square instead of a register but it takes a really long time to check out...
- Expensive! $3.50 for a cappuccino and at least $9 for lunch

I live across the street from this delightful gem in Berkeley. Its very homey, I love going in.  They make home baked deliciousness and some seriously tasty coffee.  You pay for what you get here, so it isn't a bargain per se, but its worth it to treat yourself right.

Haven't had a meal here yet, I am lookin forward to it!

Awesome little hipster coffee/breakfast/lunch spot attached to the Berkeley Art Museum. I can't tell you how often I've been stopping by this place lately. I'm SUPER obsessed with their breakfast options! The menu is said to change weekly, but the breakfast menu has been the same for the past few months..

This is what I'd recommend: 

For BREAKFAST:
* Depending on how hungry you are, I'd say order the BACON, EGG AND CHEDDAR SANDWICH if you're super hungry, and the POACHED EGGS WITH GREENS if you're moderately hungry. The BACON, EGG AND CHEDDAR SANDWICH is tantalizing! The toast is perfectly crisp and compliments the Bacon, Egg and Cheddar incredibly well. The egg in the sandwich isn't too runny but perfect with some yolkiness which is perfect with the toast and bacon combination. To die for. The POACHED EGGS WITH GREENS is a healthier option, and the greens are perfectly seasoned and have a pleasantly sour taste to them. Perfect. The poached egg is super delicate as well.

Lunch is alright. It's a little on the pricier side but I do enjoy the prepared salads that they make. Fresh, flavorful, and healthy. What more could you ask for?

As for drinks, i LOVE THAT THEY SERVE VERVE AND RITUAL COFFEES! Soooo bomb. I usually keep it simple by getting the iced coffee, though. The baristas are super adorable and really sweet as well. One of them told me about a little drink called the GIBRALTAR, which is totally worth trying if you're into cappuccinos but in a shot version.

This place is amaaazing! I come here every weekend for either a soup or lunch entree, and the food never fails to make me swoon. :) I am a huge fan of their homemade grapefruit soda--it is so good & tastes so refreshing! I recently tried a wine soaked tart/pastry (I can't remember the name), and it simply was heaven. They are always changing up their menu, and I love trying out the new selections. I love the food, love the people--I love everything about Babette!

YUM. pricey but good.

- beet tart
- pulled pork tacos with mango salsa
- gallete? fruity plum tartlet

And the blood orange grapefruit soda was delicious.

Remedy has come and gone; now Babette has rushed in to take Remedy's place; today is Day Six of the new operation. Babette is worth a look.  Superficially, we have Remedy Bis, but the caterers who have taken over the location are likely to be offering breakfast and lunch items that differ from Remedy's.

The coffee is still Ritual's.  They're doing pour-overs of the Ritual "Chely" for $3.50.

Hours are 8-4:30 during the week.

Babette--the name is sassy and classy at the same time. The cafe has a really nice color scheme and design. Ordering can be a little hectic, especially if they're busy. They use an app on their ipad if you want to pay with credit card or if you want your receipt emailed to you, but older people have a hard time figuring out how to use this.

The food is pretty good--I got the spring veggies ($3) with ginger dressing. It had peas, red onion, asparagus and mushrooms. I thought that the portion was small, but this little bowl is actually quite filling--not to mention delicious. All the ingredients tasted fresh, and even though I don't usually like food strongly flavored ginger, their vinaigrette left a clean, yet tangy aftertaste. It's food like this that makes me consider being vegetarian! They also had a lot of really tasty looking pastries--apple galettes, plum tarts?, scones, cookies, and fig bars, all which are made in house! 

Anyways, four stars for now because I've only been here a couple of times and haven't tried their coffee, but I will certainly have to come back for their fig bars (yum).

P.S. Their music is awesome--nice mix of stuff, everyone's friendly, and there's airbears access

YUM! Just picked up an excellent scone (cacao nibs and orange) that had the perfect scone texture and the flavors were delightful. I also tested out their iced tea (which is my caffeinated beverage of choice 99% of the time) which was tasty, fresh and strongly brewed - just how I like it!

Can't wait to come back for lunch which looks impressive (at the top of the menu board today was pulled pork and I do loves me some pork products! veggie folks they had things on there for you, too)

So glad Babette moved into this area of Berkeley, wishing them great success!

Philz coffee definitely made me a coffee addict and I've started to diverge from Philz and try some other places. Stumbled upon here today actually while on my way to Strada and the phrase "Ritual Coffee" captured my attention. Looked interesting, so I decided to check it out. It's located right inside the art museum. The ambience is really nice, kind of like Gourmet Ghetto and not your typical college town coffee shop. They have 3 selections of coffee and I tried to ask the barista what they were but he was not very helpful :( and barely answered my questions. 

I just ordered the brazilian one (forgot the name). The coffee was surprising and extremely smooth. I definitely want to come back here next time to try the other coffee and hopefully will receive a more welcome service. Also, the entire time I was there, I kept smelling aroma of food cooking from their kitchen and it smelled so delicious but they didn't have a menu for food so I wasn't actually sure if they serve food as well. 

Interesting little hidden place.

Terrible. I walked in today because I was looking for a quick place to get dinner to go, and I was craving a quesadilla. And how can you possibly mess up a quesadilla? It's so simple. I didn't think it was possible, but today, Pancho's proved me wrong.

The steak quesadilla comes with choice of beans, tomatoes, sour cream, guac, and lettuce. Also comes with a small bag of chips and two dips. But the quesadilla? The steak was really dry, and there was barely any cheese. I had to drench it in the sour cream and guac to get it to be more moist. I'm pretty sure steak isn't supposed to be dry and tough, but rather tender and juicy.

Also, cashier refused to make eye contact with me for some reason whole time I was ordering. I have no idea why. I'm pretty sure there wasn't anything on my face. For a place that was fairly empty (~6pm), I felt pretty darn unwelcome.

Will not be back.

Better than La Burrita in my opinion. The salsa is very fresh, the burritos are actually pretty good and there's a lot of it. Alas their nachos are smaller and thus inferior to La Burrita, and when it comes to eating nacho's its more about quantity over quality, so what's even the point?

Great veggie burritos and great portions. Fills you up.
Interesting salsa flavor, actually spicy if you get the hottest one.

Nice simple menu with inexpensive but creative options.  I got the "Souper Burrito", which was delicious & really filling - definitely got my money's worth.  The food was fresh & hot, and the employees were friendly.

Not a bad place, but nothing spectacular. They were out of the special (stuffed peppers) at 6pm on a friday night - weird? The nachos were pretty good, for their price. Nice solid chips, but definitely not enough salsa.  It's pretty cheap so I guess you can't expect too much, and it gets the mexican-food-craving job done.

Late one Wednesday night in Berkeley, everything is closed... except for this place... Panchos... used to be Japanese Snacks here or wait Yokohama Station.... which for years was a Berkeley institute in itself...

Anyways, Im starving, and well, Top Dog is ok, and La Burrita I don't like.... so this place it is....

I have to say that I rarely give ratings this low. but the food was quite awful. The chips were good. But beyond that, I got two tacos for $5.50... and while the carne asada beef was manageable, they heaped piles of salsa onto the tacos, essentially turning the whole thing into a large mushy, dripping salsa dip....

Now, the salsa in and of itself was not the best tasting, and you throw that onto a taco, and it was completely ruined. It's the equivalent of putting mustard on your taco....

Never going back there again... I guess La Burrita it is...

I tried this place for the first time cuz I got a 50% off coupon from the campuscred.
The food was mediocre and the price was average.

the customer service was pretty bad
the guy doesnt seem to care about his customers at all.

I would probably choose la burrita over this place because la burrita offers you more variety on salsa while panchos only has one salsa.

I'm giving this the "Yay! I'm a fan rating."
Call me crazy but I like their burritos more than those from LaBurrita because I find that here their burritos are a little meatier/solid than those from LaBurrita
In addition, their Salsa is really good not to mention the "spicy" variety is legitimately hot. 
I've had their Pancho's burritos and tried their enchildas both of which were huge, delicious, and appropriately spiced. 
Both the chicken and the steak seemed good. 
In addition it's not too bad on the price point, especially if you have a press pass from Cal that gets you free chips and guac.

WATER Service (5/5):
Self-Serve. 

Food (4/5):
Watergirl LOVES these burritos. In my opinion, chicken never tastes good in burritos, however I must say, this is the only time that chicken is acceptable in a burrito. It might be the tasty Orange Sauce (they call it Hot Sauce, we call it Orange) we ask for on the side, but goddamn these burritos are pretty good. Seriously guys, smother your burrito in this sauce before biting in to it. SO GOOD. The chicken and beef burrito are $6.50 ish, the steak is $7 I think. 

Hours (5/5):
OPEN LATE. Yeah, this is great for the MOO Cows that are hungry past dinner, late night snacks, and early early morning binges. I admit, the only reason I decided to try this place was because it happened to be open during one of my desperate Cow moments. moo moo moo

I'm spoiled when getting Mexican food, and Pancho's was A-OK.  Nothing great about it and nothing bad.  I tried their carne asada burrito, and I'm not used to having beans + rice in it (San Diego spoils me!).  They also offered mild or spicy salsa.  Spicy, isn't very spicy at all rather a kick.  However, I'd eat here once in a while.  I think its better than La Burrita down the street.  Take home message - its meh.

Mexican food, prepared by Mexicans, in the Asian Ghetto. While it sounds like a match made in heaven, it's really not. You get big portions, but I remember a distinct smell coming from my burrito that made me want to throw it away and get food elsewhere.

Pancho's is the remedy for late-night hunger in the UC campus area. I usually order the enchilada plate and I have yet to be unsatisfied. The complimentary chips and salsa are nice and their "spicy" sauce is truly spicy, and I'm accustomed to spicy food because of my Indian roots. One good thing about this place is that you will always leave full, which is a really good aspect considering I am a college student. 

The only reason that I wouldn't give this place a 5 is because of their extremely slow service. Other than that, this is the place to be at if you're hungry, craving Mexican food and low on money.

When its 1:30 am during finals week, you're only running on three hours of sleep and a sandwich you had twelve hours ago, you'll  be thankful Pancho's exists. I think the only other places open around that time are Top Dog and Kin Pin Donuts. I was never a big fan of hot dogs or donuts. 

Also they're open until 2:30 am! Who else does that? 

Rice, Beans, three enchiladas for less than $8. You can't beat it. Of course not the same quality as you would get at a real sit down restaurant but its good when compared to other places around South Side.

Great price, decent, bordering on great, food. I almost always order the cheese enchiladas, which have been somewhat inconsistent in prep (sometimes the cheese is not melted completely) but the spicy sauce is great! Not your typical sauce (as I don't often care for enchilada sauce) but quite tasty. Great place for vegetarians!

I never understood how my friends could even possibly like this place. The only reason I came here once was because this was the only place open that late at the Asian Ghetto (and King Pin Donuts).

I had 4 enchiladas covered with who knows what sauce I ordered because I couldn't even understand the menu/what they were saying.

It's just awful...at least they tried.

Not sure why, but seems fresher and healthier than La Burrita and Chiptole (all places have their worth somewhere). Probably how green and crispy their lettuce is.  Great value for the price- I'm always full after eating there and I've got a huge appetite- I'm 200lbs and very active. If you're strapped for money and want / need a lot of food, go to Pancho's

It's decent. The cheaper the meat the worse it is. A chicken burrito lacks good flavor while their steak dishes are pretty damn good. Really if you're looking for a $4 meal than this isn't the place to go. Want a decent burrrito and tons of sides for a little more? Go nuts. The best Mexican food is going to be at any hole in the wall restaurant in a Mexican community (or taco truck), but for Berkeley this is okay.

Little pricer than La Burrita, but you get more food.

Wow. Berkeley has no good late night Mexican food. This place AND La Burrita are both bad. This place puts peas in the Spanish rice. PEAS!!! Too bad Gordos isn't open late. Honestly, I would probably cab it to Oakland or even SF for a late night/drunken burrito.

This is the first Berkeley restaurant that has ever let me down. 

Well, there was that one time at Naan N' Curry when my food had this massive chicken bone in it, but Pancho's makes Naan look like the French Laundry.

Pancho's Mexican food was not just bland... it was disgusting. I ordered a steak quesadilla to eat at the place with a friend. The refried beans were flavorless except for a very bizarre skunky/tin-can flavor, so I abandoned those. Unfortunately, that flavor was present in EVERY BITE OF THE MEAL.

The tortilla was perfectly white, leading me to believe that it had been microwaved, and the salsa was indecipherably flavorless.

Pancho: if you go out of business, you deserve it! Your food is bland and tastes like chemicals.

Berkeley residents: It's a shame that Mario's is going out of business, but this place is no replacement! Go to La Burrita instead...

Poor quality ingredients, small burritos, unfriendly staff, need I say more?

I went here once, I had a terrible burrito served to me. I decided to give it another shot, I had the quesidilla, and it still did not taste very fresh, it was not spiced at all. I was basically eating supermarket cheese thrown on with grilled unspiced chicken on a tortilla. It was horrid.

I would rather go across the street to La Burrita.

I got the steak burrito.  It was very good!!!  I'm only giving it
a 4 stars because there was not enough cheese in it.  They give strips
of beef which actually tasted good.  Much better than La 
Burrita

Pancho is a pretty standard burrito place. The price is great for what you get. The burritos and other food is pretty good, the meat isn't the greatest highest quality meat and they don't cook it all that well but honestly the thing that makes this place is the salsa, they have damn good salsa. 

La Burrita is freaking terrible, grease and nastiness. Chipotle is just as good as this place but lacks that same flavor this salsa has. If I only combine Chipotle's ingredients with Pancho's salsa.

My friend is a big fan of this place so she took me here for a late dinner.  We split a steak quesadilla -- not just any quesadilla, a MASSIVE quesadilla stuffed to the edges with steak and served with beans, guacamole, salsa, sour cream and lettuce.  Not to mention we got chips and salsa while we waited for our food -- chips very on par with a certain popular restaurant across the street (a.k.a. La Burrita).  The two of us together didn't even finish.

The prices are way cheap considering what you get.  Our quesadilla was only $5.50.  I haven't tried their other items, but my friend tells me the portions are very large overall and everything looked decently priced.  

Sadly, this place always seems empty!  Honestly, why wait in line at La Burrita when you can sit down at Poncho's right across the street?  To me, the food is just as good and cheaper.  Hopefully I've got you converted at this point - I know I am!

I'd to give the place one star so I can help bring the average down, but I have more integrity than that.  This place is pretty terrible.  For people to say it's the "best burrito" around is pretty appalling.

I saw a show at the Greek Theatre and was craving a burrito afterwards.  La Burrita had a huge line so I went to this joint instead.  It's like a glorified Taco Bell.  Poor quality ingredients and the salsa isn't even that great.  If La Burrita is anything close to this quality, I guess you should skip out on getting burritos in the campus area altogether because this place is pretty bad.

I should have known when I saw the place was in a food court.

Came here for the first time and I liked the chicken burrito. The sauces within the burrito gave a lot of flavor with each bite. On this solo experience, I'd take it over La Burrita. The chips provided with the burrito was very tasty in addition to that salsa they included. I don't know what it was and it was a weird color, but damn, it was making my mouth burn. I'd give it four stars, but one star off because there were two or three pieces of charred chicken in the burrito. 

I'll likely return if I pass by Asian Ghetto, but it's a place that definitely doesn't stand out in my mind with all the other restaurants in the area.

When I get tired of white-washed burritos from Chipotle, I usually come here. I typically get the steak quesadilla, which is $6.25, and comes with chips, salsa, beans, and guacamole. The food seems quite good in my opinion and it usually comes pretty quickly.

I had the chicken fajitas and I really liked them. Not a huge amount of food in the league of Steve's but definitely enough for a dinner (I'm a pretty big guy). My friend had the steak burrito and didn't finish it. And, really, fajitas for $6.50? That's pretty damn good.

It started out as a late night trip to Top Dog ... cause after 3 weeks in China and being jet lagged out of my mind, I was craving meat and something non Chinese.  Like a beacon in the night, a burrito called out to me and we ended up here.  The burrifto was the size of a small child which fed me for 3 meals ... it's meant to feed starving college students - so quantity over quality, but it hit the spot that night for this weary traveler.

Thank god for places that are open late.

I am confused by the bad reviews on here. Pancho's is my favorite burrito place!! I usually order the Rojos Fajitas and they are delicious, and you get free chips! The quantity of food offered for the price is significantly larger than that of other burrito places (including chipotle) and the taste and quality are supreme. Not to mention, the workers here are sooooo friendly. I have nothing negative to say about this place!!

I wonder why anybody would go to chipotle when this place exists nearby. It is significantly better quality and quantity for the price than chipotle.
nom nom nom...I get the veggie burrito..and I am stuffed! total was $5.98, and served for lunch and dinner! The guy was super nice, and got my order right!

I like it fine but they consistently mess up my order with no effort to correct the mistake.

One cool thing about the place is they usually give you more food if you speak Spanish.  Keep that in mind if you know the language.

There are so many better Mexican options.  LaBurrito is just as good, Chipotle is comparable.  But if you are really looking for awesome Mexican, go to GORDO's on Channing and Telegraph.  You will not be disappointed.

Personally, I'm not a fan of this place.  Their burritos lack flavor and seem a little dry.  Although it's not terrible, compared to all the good food places in the Asian Ghetto you'd definitely be better off eating somewhere else.  

Overall:  I've had much, much better Mexican food.  However, it's cheap, fast, and OPEN LATE so if you've got the late night cravings it's one of the only places left to go.

Panchos might seem like a great alternative to the nearby La Burrita for grabbing Mexican food at a low price but it does not live up to one's expectations.
The restaurant is clean and that's about the only thing good about it.
I had a steak burrito. The steak was a bit overdone and bland. It was spiced too much and i felt as if i was eating a burrito filled with jalapenos and rubber. The chips felt stale and weren't enjoyable at all. 
I also give Panchos a 1 star rating since me and my friend were kept waiting at the counter for our food for an incredibly long time and the burritos that were mean't for us were instead given to two women who had come after us (it seemed as if the manager/owner had no interest in serving us food while he did definitely show a lot of interest in the fairer sex)
i've only had the nachos which were AWESOME!!!! takes a while though. try calling in and ordering in advance in order to expedite the process.
Heck yea.Best damn mexican food closest to campus. Sweet employees very friendly and generous. Very reasonable prices. The guacamole....

Very nice people here. Always greet with a smile and a little small talk. I love how I can also order a custom order like having a single taco or replacing their three taco plate with Mexican Tacos unlike other places like La Burrita that don't stray at all from their menu. They are also very generous with their chips and salsa.

Had an order of the Veggie Burrito (~$6): veggies, rice, cheese, black beans, sour cream, pico de gallo, & corn salsa in a tortilla. Food was delicious, staff was social, and the ambiance was familiar.

GARBAGE. 
This place takes absolutely no pride in their food. How can you mess up a bean & cheese burrito? Come to Pancho's in Berkeley CA on Durant and find out. The food here literally made me sick. I woke up to stabbing pains in my stomach. There was also suspicious communication between the goateed cashier and the cook that rolled his eyes when I ordered my "food". Pancho's is dirty. The employees probably don't wash their hands after they pick their butts and noses here. They probably touch their balls and your money then use those same unwashed hands to make your food. I think they are selling food that is spoiled. This place should not be in business. 
SPEND YOUR MONEY ELSEWHERE.

I always come here for an open chicken burrito or their nachos. The serving size is huuuge whenever I go and it's under 7 bucks! Another great thing about this place is they're open late, so if you're up for the walk you can just head on over to asian ghetto and get some food

The beef in the beef burrito tasted f***in' weird. 
Watching them construct the burrito slowly and haphazardly like they don't know what they are doing... painful.  

2 stars because the chips that the come with are delicious and aplenty... but you know they're only that good because they are DRENCHED in oil.

La Burrita FTW. this place blows.
Bland and tasteless. Dirt would excite your mouth more than what they're calling food...
update: ive been going there alot recently, and the people who work there now are hella chill. they hook it up with the hot sauce, and damn those cheese quesedillas with veggies are great
My steak burrito was mediocre; the lettuce was wilted, and it was tiny, for a $7 burrito.  The worst part is that my bag of chips SMELLED STRONGLY OF BLEACH.

My absolute favorite place for burritos and nachos in Berkeley. This place is sooo much better than La Burrita in every way. It's cleaner, has a better ambiance, more friendly employees who don't judge you when you've had too much to drink on a thursday night, and most importantly it tastes waaay better. I don't understand why people still go to La Burrita when Pancho's literally right across the street.

Since Pancho's in SF is pretty awesome, I decided to try this place instead of going to the always good Thai Basil. The great thing about the SF one is that they have a ton of specialty burritos like BBQ chicken (i know it sounds weird as hell but you have to try it!) and a fajita burrito; However, THIS Pancho's had only 2 Types of burritos...meat or no meat. LAME.

Secondly, they DON'T have Carnitas...so I ended up ordering a grilled chicken burrito. It took a long time to get it, and it was so lifeless and bland words do not do it justice. The salsa had no taste, the chicken had no taste...it pretty much felt like a burrito i'd make myself using premade ingredients from Walmart or something...However, their chips were good tasting and super thin, like they should be so +1 star, and +1 more because I didn't get sick like i did with Chipotle.

Burrito Places in berkeley (from best to worst, note: I haven't tried berkeley gordo's yet):
1. That place on Center next to top dog.
2. La Burrita
3. Pancho's
4. Chipotle

The servers at Panchos are very patient, unlike la burrito. I forgot what i had, which is the whole point of yelp, but in my defense, it was in the middle column, somewhere near the middle top of the column and it was something that came in a pack of 3. The choices were beef, chicken, or cheese. I like how they let you mix and match. That's always nice. I had 2 chickens and 1 beef togo. It was pretty good, I liked it. The beef was eh, but then again, I don't really like red meat. I USED to. I got everything in beef, but when I got to Berkeley, it stopped being appealing, probably bc everyone eats so healthy. Anyway, the chicken was good, but the flavor was definitely masked under the huge mounds of guac and sour cream. Do they even look at how much they put in? I could tell there was a nice flavor though. Came with the usual beans and rice. Overall, it was good and cheap for the quantity you get as well as quality. Nice job Panchos. The only cons i have is they dont let you get your own salsa and they put way too much guac & sour cream on it. Way to make it soggy and lose some flavor Panchos. I only had it once, but for some reason, I have a craving to go back, weird. Maybe my pallet thought it was better than I remember.
If pancho's left, I'd be sad. It would mean back to la bu...joy.
Good quesidillas and enchiladas. But one time the quesidilla was really greasy. There was a lot of residual oil left over from the cooking pan in my food!!!

Service: 4/5
Food: 5/5
Wait: 2/5
Price: $
Presentation of food: 3/5
Presentation of restaurant: 3/5
Overall: 4/5

I had their Open Chicken Burrito late night last night for the first time, i had never had any burrito called 'OPEN' burrito? so i thot i try it, which was funny. cuz all it was, was that there was a FAT GAP WHOLE in the middle of the burrito! hahha... i was pretty amused at that fact, cute name for it. but any who, while we and most of the people we're all drunk and NOT SOBER. This burrito HIT THE SPOT im tellin you. if you're hungry and had not yet had anything to eat such like dinner, you WILL DEF. get full after this burrito. The sauce they had that came with the tortilla chips they gave you was THE BOMB. my bf had accidentally spilled his so i had to share mine which i barely had any cuz his drunk self gobbled most of it down! the line was out the door by the time i was thinking to ask for another sauce. lol. so i rather not. cutting off drunk people for some sauce? yea.... no. i rather stay alive than to get drunk sucker punch'd over some sauce. hahah... great place to grab mexican grub tho!

I had probably the worst nachos of my entire life here.  The nachos consisted of partially stale chips covered in cheese, seemingly two day old rice and beans, a stray piece of corn here and there, and jalapenos.  I also found a pea rolling around on my plate. The nachos were placed on a paper plate and tossed in the microwave for a few minutes then served to me covered in aluminum foil.  Granted, it was only $4, so I guess you get what you pay for.  But still, I guarantee there's better cheap Mexican food in the area than this place has to offer.  I will say that the service was friendly.

I was feeling like Mexican one day and I noticed that Pancho's had opened up in the Asian Ghetto. I'm not really a fan of La Burrita and I wanted to try this place so I let my stand-by of gut-busting burritos at Chipotle wait another day or two. 

The first thing that I noticed about Pancho's was how small it was. The second thing I noticed was how it actually had the nicest decor of all the restaurants in the Asian Ghetto. Now we're not talking about fireplaces and people to rub your feet while you look at fabulous marble columns and what not in the restaurant but it definitely looked nice. It wasn't ghetto looking like some of the other restaurants here (perhaps Gypsy's aside). 

The burrito was average-sized and just rather average. I liked it but it didn't blow my mind away. I had a steak burrito for about $6. For that price, I would rather go to Chipotle but it was great to try it out. At least it came out quickly and I saw what was being put into my burrito, which always is a plus.

To do it right: $6

Finally, Mexican food in the Asian Ghetto.  Now this place officially has THE most absurdly random assortment conceivable.  I love it.

My first, and only, visit to Pancho's was shortly after they opened.  I ordered a chicken quesadilla, which was fine, reasonably priced, and reasonably filling.  Not amazing, but about what you'd expect.  They did, however, supply me with enough guacamole and sour cream to get through the thing--points for that.  Other than that not really too exciting or groundbreaking as far as food goes.

The fantastic part of this experience was watching the assistant manager wrestle with the credit card machine:

Asst. Man.: Swipe, beep, beep, beep.  Befuddled look.  Swipe, beep.  Awkward grin.  Swipe, beep, beep, beep, beep, beep!  Silence.

(this goes on for ~2 minutes solid)

Me (putting him out of misery): I think you have to type in the code on the back.

Success!

I'm not docking any points for credit card fumbling.  It was simultaneously a very sad and entertaining thing to behold.

Final Say: You're eating in a place called the "Asian Ghetto" and now you're going to have standards?

P.S. I'm not sure which box to check for "Accepts Credit Cards." j/k, j/k.

Mixed feelings about this place. My mom and I both got the chicken salad. She was on a time crunch and we figured salads would be the quickest. Wroooong. We waited 30 minutes for two salads. (lettuce, chicken, tomatoes, olives, cheese, salsa, guac)

That had barely any lettuce in them -_-. uh hello it's a salad, yes? Minus one star for freaking forgetting my guac!!!! t-_-t 

any-who. The long wait and lack of lettuce and guac turned me off but I must admit, the salad was really tasty. And the chips and salsa that came with it were good too!

This is the only Mexican food you should ever allow yourself to eat on Southside (unless you're going to "trek" out to Gordo's, by lazy Southside standards).  La Burrita across the street is... *shudders*, and Pancho's is not only much less objectionable, but actually pretty tasty!

The quesadillas here are very tasty and filling, and the burritos are good, too.  The meat is tasty, the salsa is deliciously spicy (if you ask for spicy), and it's quicker than some of the other restaurants nearby.

If you want to eat Mexican food on Southside, look no further!

Welcome to Pancho's: The new late night clusterfuck.
