Since La Burrita closes at 2AM, Pancho's has decided to stay open, much to it's own workers' demise. You can see their faces of agony at 2:30AM with hordes of drunken students yelling "BURRRITTOOOOOO."

At this point into the night, people will eat just about anything so it really doesn't matter what you get, but I think the steak is a bit better than the chicken.

If your goal is to get in and out of the place the fastest, get tacos, quesadillas, or burritos. DO NOT ORDER NACHOS. I made the mistake of ordering nachos and waited a good bit longer.

See you there on Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays.

Panchos is a very average Mexican place as far as Berkeley standards go. Better than La Burrita, worse than Chipotle (yes it's Mexican), worse than Gordos, worse than Durant cafe, and...yeah.

The burritos here are pretty good, but the super nachos freaked me out. Olives? I don't know about that. I haven't really seen olives used in any Mexican dish ever. It just don't make no sense. It's actually disgusting.

As a Socal native, I was surprised that I even stepped foot in a Norcal Mexican restaurant. 

My friends and I were originally headed to La Burrita (which is no bueno btw), but luckily they were closed early, so we stumbled into Pancho's. 

Surprisingly enough, the food was actually pretty good, and the workers are pretty nice! We ordered chicken quesadillas and super nachos, both of which came with a ton of food. They aren't skimpy with portions.

Pancho's also gets an extra star for convenience. It's located in the Asian Ghetto, which is about 2 minutes from campus. Hooray!

All orders come with chips and salsa, but we ran out so I asked the worker for some extra chips and he gave me an entire basket of chips, free of charge! (Tip: converse with them in Spanish to increase your chances of free chips)

Also, the hot salsa they give you creeps up on you. It's SO spicy and my mouth was on fire by the end of the meal.

I would definitely come back if I'm craving Mexican food in Berkeley. It may not compare to the Mexican food in San Diego, but it's damn good for Berkeley standards!

If it were 2am and I had to choose between La Burrita, I ... wouldn't know where to go.  Maybe I'd be indecisive until 2:15, which is after La Burrita closes but before this place closes. The nice thing about Pancho's is that you can see colors in your veggies.   A little watery though.
If you get a burrito here you will probably be disappointed. But the fajitas and enchiladas are literally out of this world. Pancho's has become one of my favorite places in Berkeley.

One very late Thursday, my friend and I had made it back to the East Bay from a club in the city when we were craving some food. To our complete surprise, *everything* in the Durant food court was closed! We saw some kids happily leaving Pancho's with food, but they told us it was closed already. 

We enter Panchos and although they were in the middle of cleaning and had definitely closed for the night, they decided to serve us. You could tell they had cleaned the stove and put everything away, but they still offered to cook for us! We ordered 2 super burritos. We didn't have a choice of meat, so unfortunately it was just ground beef it seemed (something I would have never ordered - I'm more of an al pastor girl).

I believe if I had a meat choice I preferred, it would have been one pretty good burrito! They rolled each of our burritos with TWO tortillas! They layered in plenty of guacamole and sour cream and all the fixings! This burrito lasted me for THREE meals! For a frame of reference, I usually just have a stub of "normal" burrito`left over. It was amazing! I reheated it in the oven and put in some extra cheese and salsa, and my reheated burrito suddenly turned in to one AMAZING burrito!

I've only been here once, so I'm not sure if we got some sort of special hookup, but man did we get our money's worth! 

The chips were really good too and the salsa is definitely homemade.
The only reason it gets 2 stars is because it's open super late, and I've gone there several time for that reason alone.  These are some really awful burritos though.  Go to La Burrita instead.

I've gone all over the bay area looking for something that would resemble 'real' Mexican food, only to be faced with heartbreak and despair.  My general complaint is that the restaurants I've been to disguise the taco's flavor with things like lettuce, sour cream, and cheese (SAY WHAT?!?)

Just when all hope was lost, I walked into Panchos, ordered the Pancho's Three tacos... and heard an angelic chorus sing.


Meh, actually no.  

But Pancho's Mexican food is really as good as it gets (in the bay area).  Their tortillas don't have that nasty packaged smell, and their ingredients taste REAL  (notice the emphasis on REAL).  Their beans don't seem to come out straight out of the can,and  their tomato + guacamole are delectably fresh.  Their quesadillas are big and fill you up.  

The customer service is OK;  before 6 pm two ladies are working- they're Ok,
but then, two guys serve their shift, and they are super funny and friendly :)  

The cashier dude in the afternoon has messed up my order a couple times, but I'll survive; the food and the cooks' friendliness balance those mix-ups.

Ooooh!  I recommend their hot sauce!  Sooo tasty and spicy- it does give you a swift kick in the pants.

I too am confused by all the poor reviews here.  First, I've never encountered a rude worker there but the food seems pretty good to me too.  The burrito I get is the "Pancho's Burrito" with steak and black beans.  The steak always has a nicely grilled/char flavor.  However, the real star here is the salsa -- it's nicely spiced, has great flavor, and this interesting almost-creamy texture.  The last time I went, I was sad that they gave me guacamole with my chips instead of salsa but oh well. 

Regardless of the reviews, I think the burrito here is better than El Farolito (http://www.yelp.com/biz/el-farolito-san-francisco-2) as the not only is the meat better, but it's less greasy and I'd even say that the salsa is better.  El Farolito has wonderful salsas (especially that cilantro-infused green one), but Pancho's one salsa is better than any one salsa at El Farolito.

Anyone who is unsure, I really think you should try the Pancho's burrito with steak and black beans and compare it side-by-side to the El Farolito burrito with carne asada.  I really think you'll see it my way!

So this is a new place in the "Asian Ghetto". I ordered a chicken quesadilla and for it's price, its not too bad. Very filling and the chicken at least had a little bit of flavor. I will agree with the other review, in that the salsa was a little plain. Definitely seemed not homemade, but who am I to judge?? I think I paid close to $6 and I could barely finish. I probably would come here again if I felt like cheap Mexican food, but more likely I would just cross the street anyway to get La Burrita.

Solid steak burrito for ~$6. Now I can say that I've tried a burrito from every Mexican joint in the Telegraph area, I think. Pancho's burritos are more expensive, but way larger than Gordo's. My only negative point is that the food, especially the chips, was really salty, and unevenly so. Do they put MSG in the food? I find I'm never a huge fan of restaurant chips anyhow, though, so I can skip them in the future. I was extremely thirsty after devouring that monster of a burrito and regretted not trying a Jarritos for the first time with it. I'm hoping that the saltiness was a one-time fluke--I'll find out if I come back someday. A major pro is that they include cheese in the burrito, which is more commonly becoming an extra charge at other places. Nonsense!

Tip: don't finish the whole thing and then go to the bollywood class at the gym, not that anyone with common sense (not me) would. Ugh, I'm still so full...and thirsty...

I have no idea why people are hating on Pancho's.  The people there are super duper nice and don't growl at you like the dudes do at La Burrita.  

Get the Ranchero Burrito to share with at least one other famished person.  It's damn good.  Steak burrito covered with a spicy tomato-based ranchero sauce and melted cheese topped with sour cream and guacamole for under $8.  This thing is bigger than half the size of a plastic square take out container.   They actually reheat their meat, unlike the freaking Tostada I got at La Buritta the last time I went.  

Love this place.  It's open later than Taco Bell... lol

I don't think this place is as bad as people have been saying...it definitely took me a while to get around to trying it because the other places in Asian Ghetto appeal to me much more. Two of my friends come here quite frequently though, so I'll incorporate what they think too.

First of all, the decor is really nice. I must say, this is the only restaurant in the Asian Ghetto that actually cares about how it looks. Sombreros hanging all along the walls, an interesting bench...

Now about the food. I got the chicken tacos with guacamole and salsa (which was basically a chunky tomato salsa, not spicy at all even though it was called "mild"). I got one on a flour tortilla and the other on corn. The tacos are definitely packed to the max, and props to you if you can eat one without dropping anything. It was quite a messy lunch I had...definitely not a place you'd want to go on a first date. ;)

My friends said that this place is always like a surprise, especially in terms of salsa. You never know what salsa you're going to get. Today we had the chunky diced tomatoes, and that was the first time my friend said he's seen that. He didn't really like the salsa today, so I guess it's usually better. And you're supposed to get chips and salsa with your taco order, which we did, but the salsa that comes with that will be a surprise too. My friend also said that sometimes when he gets an order to go, they won't include the chips, so it's a surprise whether they include the chips or not. (I guess he doesn't check before he leaves...)

My other friend got a quesadilla today, which for some reason took a long time, but she really liked it and said the ingredients were fresh and yummy. The portion size was huge and she ended up taking most of it home.

Overall, I think this place is not bad, but it's definitely not high going to be high on my list of choices when I go to Asian Ghetto. It's not a place I would crave. If I wanted Mexican, I think I would rather go to Chipotle or the Taco Truck near the MLK Student Union. This place might be a little healthier though...but I could be wrong.

It's CHEAP though. $6.42 for tacos/chips PLUS a Snapple. And they take credit cards (not AmEx though).

Okay, so I really don't want to give them just 1 star, but their customer service is horrendous! I came in here around 10pm after my 7pm final last spring and I ordered a some sort of steak burrito (don't remember which). So I ordered, the cashier repeated my order exactly, and I confirmed. The guy swiped my credit card, but then looked confused and swiped again. At first,  I thought there was just an error with the machine, so I didn't say anything. After his second swipe, the receipt printed out and I signed it. Cool. 

He went to the back and the other worker started preparing my burrito. He looked back at me and then looked down at the burrito, then back up towards my direction again. I thought he was looking at someone behind me so I turned around, but no one was there. Eventually he gives me my burrito, I take it back to my apartment to eat. The dude gave me chicken in my burrito! I paid more for steak only to get chicken!! I need my STEAK! I'm okay with mistakes sometimes, but his continuous glances at me while he prepared my burrito made me think they ran out of steak and so he decided to just do a chicken. The problem doesn't just stop there...

A week later, I check my credit card statement, and it shows that my credit card was charged twice for that transaction. Wait...I'm paying two times the price of a steak burrito for one  chicken burrito?! Hell no.  I called Panchos requesting credit back because I only ordered once. The guy I spoke to had a very very thick accent which was hard to understand. He eventually managed to tell me to call back to speak to the manager. I asked what time the manager will be back and he said around noon. So I called around noon and the same guy picks up. I ask to speak to the manager and he said he is the manager. WTF?  Anyway, so I explained the situation again and he tells me to come in with my credit card statement and receipt. I was out of town at the time so that wasn't possible...plus, how would me bringing a receipt prove that I only bought one--not two--burritos during that time? The guy kept making excuses and I got tired of it. I wanted to resolve this easily with him so he wouldn't have to deal with credit card companies, but he gave me so much trouble I just said screw it and asked Chase to deal with it. I eventually got my money back, but it shouldn't have been that hard. If they had competent workers and better customer service, maybe all of this could have been avoided.

Other than their horrendous service, their burritos are okay. I still prefer Cafe Durant ($5 happy hour (large) burritos!!), Chipotle, and La Burrita more. I've never been back since they decided to be pricks about a measly $8.

Even for student budget food, this one is a tough sell for me. 

They have a burrito called the 'Souper' burrito which, quite literally, sits in a flood of cheesy corn, peas, and tomato water. The steak is tough and the tortilla is soggy. For around $7 it's a fair price, plus you get a bag of chips... but I think i'll pass on this the next time I'm in the Asian Ghetto.

A nice quaint place in the middle of the Chemistry plaza on the Berkeley campus!

After seeing the inflation that Cal Dining did by raising the price of everything, this place is actually pretty cheap.

The people that work here are really nice, and they usually have only a short line usually.

So I have to star this review by saying that I love all 3 of the people that work here.  There are two incredibly friendly Brazilian women that love helping me practice my Portuguese (which basically suffices to order coffee, say I'm hungry and/or tired, and not much else).  There's also another guy there who's also very friendly, always has a story about his girlfriend keeping him in line, and tells me "not to work too hard."  Something's nice about this kind of coffee ritual.

Ok, so here's the deal: the coffee costs $1 if you bring your own mug.  Do I really need to say more.  It's not Folger's and it's not Blue Bottle, but somewhere in between.  I recommend going in the morning, when they do a ton of business, and then the coffee is always fresh.  The bagels are also pretty good.  I've never tried any of their other food, but my coworkers like it.  

It's totally hidden in the courtyard between Tan and HIldebrandt.  Yelp has it's location wrong, so make sure you find it!  Just remember that thank you is "Obrigado" in Portuguese.

Love me some Coffee Lab - Coffee Lab guy and Coffee Lab lady are the nicest people in the world, solid assortment of baked goods, and $1 coffee if you bring a mug. Hard (impossible?) to beat on campus! Not just saying that because I work in CoC...

This place happens to be in the center of all my classes. It is hidden in Hilderbrand Hall so I'll bet you couldn't find it if you want to - which I may add is a plus for me. The folks in charge are the HAPPIEST FRIENDLIEST people I have seen. Coffee sucks. Everything else is cool. THE PASTRIES ARE DELISH: go for the pumpkin muffin or the cinnamon bun. Since this place is so small, taxes don't apply. I love paying EXACTLY one dollar for water or two dollars for a donut. Screw you Starbucks for charging me $3.04 for a late that other day.

Bummers: Doesn't take credit cards / Limited seating (outdoor).

cash only. but if youre stuck on campus, this is your best bet. (its between tan and lewis.)

they serve coffee drinks, pastries and sandwiches. kind of pricey for what you get.

This place is awesome. It's way cheaper than other places on campus, coffee, tea, and the pumpkin muffins are great, and the people working there are nicer than anyone else you'll encounter on campus. It's cash only, but there's an ATM really close nearby.

The best kept secret of the College of Chemistry!

If you're low on cash they have a small coffee that's like a couple shot glasses in size for $1. It's like a caffeine boost no more no less, which is pretty cool, because then you won't have to go to the bathroom in an hour. They also have donuts, which is exciting. Least pretentious eatery on campus?

Thank goodness this is on my way to all my classes at Haas. Jimmy Fifo's idea of coffee is rather poor. The Coffee Lab is where you should get coffee in this area of the campus. Even FSM's coffee (which is always quite burnt, unusually smoky, and incredibly "runs"-inducing) can't beat this place. 

I come in here in the morning to be able to endure my lengthy day of classes. I don't know how they make coffee, but they're doing it right. The 2 people who are always here are very nice. What keeps me coming back is the coffee quality. It's bold, smooth, and rich (maybe 3/4 of the quality of coffee godsend, Blue Bottle Coffee). I'm picky when it comes to coffee; the Coffee Lab does it right. I usually get a regular coffee or a latte. The lattes are amazing. It's sad that this place doesn't have as long as a line as FSM. Those FSMers don't know what they're missing.

Thought I start out with basics. For better or worse this is the closest establishment to where I spend way too much time that provides the necessities - caffeine and sugar. As I work both early and late the hours are definitely limiting. It would also be nice of the coffee was a bit less bitter. However, now that the undergrads are back the line is nice and short in comparison to the B-school and Yali's. Most importantly the staff are great and they keep the undergrads from stealing the seminar coffee and donuts!

The coffee is foul swill, especially towards closing time at *3:00 PM* employees are nice, though, so 2 stars. Pay extra for ice? Maybe you could drop a few bucks on an icemaker.  Worst of all, however, is the lady guarding the pre-seminar donuts and coffee like a hawk, if you have something, and take a step in any direction but towards the seminar, her sonic assult will teach you  a new definition of the word "pain".

Finally -  the department isnt paying you to feed us PB&J on stale government bread, I see those donuts you have stashed back there.

One of UCB's many on campus restaurants where you can spend your mealpoints. Everything here is overpriced and unless you have points, I wouldn't recommend coming here. 

The dimsum here is not good at all, so though it might be tempting, I would highly recommend not getting it.

The lines are always out the door cause freshman need to eat and mealpoints they need to spend. The cashiers are usually cranky, but in the rare case that the place is empty, they're not too bad. 

Go somewhere else unless you have mealpoints.

Bitch fucked up my sandwich. 

Also, the three people after me got their sandwiches before I did. 

Next time - go to Peet's. They have Dutch Crunch (!!)and a valid line system.
This place is great for students living off meal points. The paninis are probably the best lunch food you can spend your meal points on. The lines during lunch time however can get ugly...

As an architecture student, I am forced to descend upon Ramona's from my higher studio floor when I crave sustenance. Mostly coffee, which they do a good job of stocking. 

Other good things: 
-Location. Right at the entrance to campus, easy to find (though I don't think there is a sign out front?)
-Coffee.
-Paninis are good until you've eaten them a couple dozen times.
-Dim Sum! Oh, this wonderful little option that they added to their menu on Tuesdays and Thursday is great! Probably because it's one of the more cheaper options for getting a meal there.

Bad Things:
-Service. Man, I don't know what has gotten to some of the older ladies that work there, but they are consistently rude and pushy. I understand there are a lot of people in the line at times, but it does no good to snap. My boyfriend once paid for a sandwich and made the mistake of asking if they took cash. The aggravated response he got back made him hesitant to return.

-Price. If you're not paying with meal points, then there are a whole lot of other, more affordable options. $6.25 for a sandwich? $4 for a cup of fruit? 

-Stinginess. I don't know how else to describe the employee's extreme fear of you stealing condiments, napkins and utensils. They now hide their napkins, keep their utensils behind the counter, and guard the condiment table like a hawk. Oftentimes this has you searching for where they've put the forks on any given day...

Conclusion: 
If you've got a few extra minutes to walk down Bancroft, or over to the Haas Pavilion, I would really suggest it!

Not very competent workers, slow service, terribly inefficient system for the cash register line, the food is so-so, definitely campus food, the only thing they got going for them is the dim sum which is only on tuesdays and thursday and they only have 2 choices each day! what a rip. anyways, if you can, go elsewhere

Ugh. This morning, I was juggling my huge umbrella, purse, and hot oatmeal and a banana at the register. I told the cashier that I was also getting a coffee so she could charge me for it.

But she curtly told me to go get the coffee and then come back to pay, despite me clearly struggling with all the junk I was holding. Uh, I'm paying up front for something I may or may not get and you're telling me that I need to go back and add to my already bothersome load?

Rude and illogical. Too things I hate.

I used to love their Paninis as a freshman. I eventually got tired of them, but no doubt they probably have the best Paninis among campus restaurants (excluding Zeb Cafe of law school). Usually at least one place to sit in, although I noticed no power plugs, so probably won't be charging your netbook here. 

Tuesdays I believe are dimsum days, and their pork shumai is pretty good. A little expensive though, but 1 serving gives you 2 shumai.

Eh.
If you really want a panini, I strongly advise going over to Crossroads and just making your own with their panini press - this place does them just fine, but they really aren't that big enough for a full meal. 
That said, there's a pretty reasonable selection of sides and chips (one of the only places on campus I know where one can find the always-rare cottage cheese [$2.10] and baby carrots [$2.50]), ignoring the fact they're pretty expensive. 
Staff seemed polite but pretty tired out when I went in during a slow period during the day, although I had to argue with the checkout guy who insisted my sandwich was marked for extra $ for guacamole when I hadn't asked for it in the first place. 
Not the nicest interior (not very welcoming at all) but the outdoor seating is fine. Tends to get busy (I've heard) during lunchtime so watch out.

Ramonas has dim sum every day now! And the quality of their dim sum has definitely gotten better. I especially looooove their pork buns on Thursdays... they're all I look forward to. 

Still, I hate the long waits and the bad service. The paninis also still take days, and the lines are even more ridiculous now because they have combined the dim sum and the rice bowl lines. 

Try to go during a time when it isn't bombarded by dozens and dozens of people. won't make the paninis come out any faster, but at least you can enjoy your dim sum in peace :)

For on-campus food, Ramona's is top notch. The coffee is fresh and always stocked, their chicken bowls and panini are tasty, and they get extra points for the convenience factor. The staff are always really friendly and put a smile on my face when I'm so frantically busy I forget to. WIth ample seating and plenty of power outlets it's Ramona's FTW if you're a student or a nostalgic alumni.

The food here is good and it is the only place on this corner of campus. It just gets really expensive though if you buy both a food item and a drink. I guess this place seemed a lot better back in the day when I had a meal plan.

Convenient place to grab lunch (and usually super quick unless you get caught in the lunch rush. Then it can take forever waiting in the cashier lines). I've only really had their rice bowls here and they're surprisingly good (I always get brown rice, nom nom). Plus unlike all the other restaurants nearby they accept cc so that's nice when I'm not carrying cash.

I'm surprised no one else has written anything for Ramona's already. Last semester, my first semester at Cal, I dined here before my NES class in Kroeber. It's conveniently located on the eastern side of campus near Haas and the Unit 1 & 2 residence halls. The chicken (and vegetable) rice bowls are very tasty if you choose to get the sweet & sour and teriyaki sauces.

The line for the panini station can get congested quickly, especially during lunch and passing time. This goes for the rice bowl line as well as the checkout line. 

This semester, Ramona's has dim sum every Tuesday and Thursday. On Tuesdays, it's pork siu mai (pork dumplings) and pot stickers. On Thursdays, it's ha gao (shrimp dumpling) and BBQ pork buns (cha siew bao). I find it odd that the sign says har gao and the receipt says har goa. Language tension right there. 

Aside from food, there are plenty of drinks from the standard collection of Coca-Cola brand. Definitely pick up one of the Gold Peak iced teas! Hidden on a neglected wall are the energy/granola/power bars and the ice cream sandwich/bar collection. There are also plenty of chips and a small variety of fruits and pastries. Hot coffee and tea are also available. Let's not forget the conveniently located sweets right next to the checkout stand. There is seating and small tables beyond the checkout stands and outside seating as well, which is great on a warm, sunny day. This semester, to cut down on utensil hoarders, the forks/spoons/knives are now behind the panini and rice bowl station. Sometimes they don't even have them out and hand them to you with your order. I'm going to miss coming here when I don't have meal points. One more thing, they have scan trons and blue exam booklets available as well. Basically a condensed GBC.

MAGIC PANINI GRIL!!!

Seriously, I love getting morning bagels on my way to class. Depending on if I'm at Haas or Wheeler, I'll get my bagels from either Ramona's or GBC. The panini grill does a much better job of toasting/crisping the bagel/bread and everything tastes so FLUFFY. (It's so fluffy I'm gonna die!!!!!)

Seriously love this place. Plus it's meal points, which we don't treat as real money anyway -___-

The manager here is a stingy, incompetent, FAT bitch!  She yelled at me once for trying to take two chopsticks, as if I was stealing from her own children's mouths!!!  I'm pretty sure it was her idea to move all the condiments and utensils behind the ricebowl/sandwich counter.  Honestly, how much could a fork made of corn, the cheapest substance in America, possibly cost?!?! 

This place always has a massive line for bowls or sandwiches, so it's impossible to flag someone down just to give you a stupid spoon if you bought a to-go item.  Considering the price of everything and the sub-mediocre quality of the food, this is absolutely ridiculous.  

Even if you're paying in points, a meal plan is a huge rip off, residential or non-residential.  So seriously Cal Dining, you can at least stop acting like students are criminals - YOU are the criminals for forcing students into scam meal plans!

I got the mushroom burger combo which came with fries and a soda.

The burger was super tasty. The bun was toasty warm, the burger itself was nice and grilled tasting. The toppings were super yum - sauteed mushrooms, melty cheese, fresh lettuce and tomatoes, and just the amount of of ketchup, mayo, and mustard that I like.

I really liked the fries, too. They weren't overly greasy or salty. Very crispy, warm, and tasty. Also, cute and crinkly.

The service was fast and friendly, and the atmosphere of the place was simple and comfortable. A nice place to people watch out the window as well.

I also thought the price was good compared to other places.

Currently my fav burger place.
Great value for breakfast!

My two favorite things: tasty and cheap.

When I'm in Berkeley and don't feel like going to Top Dog, I'll go Bongo Burger.

Just today, I had the combination #7 for $8.75 plus tax.  It was a Persian burger, fries, and a small soda.  The Persian burger is seasoned ground lamb in the shape of a rectangle to match the shape of the tasty toasted roll that surrounds the meat.  Lettuce and tomato is also in the sandwich.  Very tasty.  I normally don't eat lamb but this lamb was very good.  Even the fries were very tasty.  

Bongo Burger also has hamburgers, cheeseburgers, and steak sandwiches as well as falafels, hummus, mediterranean salads,and  shish kabob plates.  I've had the hamburgers and falafels in the past and they have all been good.

Since I had my meal shortly after 10 AM, I was tempted by their breakfast combinations.  For $4.80, I could have had two eggs any style, bacon, homefries, toast, and jam.  Or the same without meat for $3.05.  I'll have to get breakfast next time.

It was okay. I was leery because of its proximity to the campus (most food is overly priced and just gross--the perils of having college students as your clientele.) 

Anyway, I made it in just before the lunch rush. It wasn't crowded, although it quickly became so. The cashier seemed slightly impatient when I took my time, but was prompt and efficient. It was only 11:30, so I didn't quite feel like lunch would go down well with my stomach (darn not eating a proper breakfast!)

I ordered a hummus sandwich and a small Sprite. It kinda ticked me off that it was nearly 6 dollars, but the combo meals certainly look like good deals. The sandwich was okay, although the pita bread started falling apart and I started getting sandwich sauce/liquid all over my hands. I decided to give up and threw out the rest. 

Still, it seems popular with students and workers. It was relatively clean and the food came out pretty quickly. I'll keep this place in mind when I'm in the area.

I like Bongo Burger.  It's a little pricy for a burger place, but I think the food is worth it.  I got the persian burger special.  It is pretty big and enough for two meals.  I like their fries too.  This location is pretty good as well.  It was crowded, but it wasn't hard to find seating even though it was lunch time.  I hear they do a decent black bean burger as well.

Ok maybe this is just me but I get really turned off by cashiers who have no where to go, nothing to do, and still find the time to look at you like you're insane when you only have $10 to spend and can't decide between the fifteen choices on the menu.  Eh, maybe it's just me...

As far as the food goes, the fries were delicious.  The sheer size of the "Mushroom Burger" made me recall the ginormous creatures I've seen in only magazines.  The bun was a fresh-from-the-bakery-quality sesame bun: perfectly crusty on the outside, chewy and soft on the inside, with more sesame seeds than I've ever seen on any burger joint bun.  

But when I go out to have a hamburger, I go out to have a damn-good hamburger.  And the Niman Ranch patty did have a beefier flavor than any you'll find at your typical burger stop, but ultimately, it was underseasoned, and that was tough to look past.

It sounds like I would have been better off with the falafel.  And I wouldn't pass up the opportunity to go again.

I don't get the hype. This is probably because I didn't have a "real" burger. I tried the half lamb burger, and I asked for it plain, thinking the lamb would be filling enough and not wanting mayo and all that other stuff on my burger. Mistake. 

1. The "burger" was a very thin rectangular patty of lamb, and was SO SALTY. 
2. Also, I got it in a pita, and the pita was thin and stale. 
3. I also don't get the appeal of their crinkle cut fries - those were not french fries I would waste any calories on - they were thin, and sort of limp and soggy  (I like my fries very crispy and hot)

I won't be back unless there really is nowhere else to go - there are too many other good burger places in Berkeley. For an AMAZING lamb burger (that's a real burger, not a tiny condensed rectangular patty), go to Free House (at least it was really good back when it was Adagia).
It lacks ambiance, but the price is right. I also like that they have some different types of burgers, like the "persion burger". The french rolls are delicious, fries barely mediocre.
Damn fine burger and good fries.  The prices are reasonable and despite a lunch time crowd, they're as quick as you can expect them to be.

When you're an undergrad at Berkeley you're bound by how far your feet can take you, no In-n-Outs for those of us without cars!  So Bongo Burger is that substitute for you.  Although I prefer Barney's, Bongo Burger is a quick pick me upper with a dash of grease.  I had their mushroom burger and it was good.  I also noticed my heart hurt a little bit more and decided to forfeit the bus ride for a hike home instead.

I absolutely love Bongo Burger! I usually come here to get burgers over the summer. One thing I always get is their classic cheeseburger meal. The portions are quite reasonable for a burger, fries, and small soda. Their food is always fresh and delicious. It gets crowded in here at lunch hours, but the line moves by pretty fast. Bongo Burger was definitely worth my $8!

The portions are really big and pretty tasty, though my falafel got rather dry and tasteless after awhile. Still it's really cheap and the food tastes pretty authentic to me. The fries were good though and once again HUGE portions. Still, it's hard to mess up fries. My own real complaint is that it's very annoying to sit near the door on a windy day because it doesn't shut itself.

This place is pretty awesome. Decent variety of burgers, the fries are tasty, and they let you take your own ranch dressing sauce! Hell YES! Burgers are around 6 bucks each and fries are about 2 do if you want the full experience it'll be a bit pricier than any place with a dollar menu, but it's with checking out.

I liked this place okay. 

At the suggestion of someone at my hotel I had my first Berkeley meal at Bongo Burger. 

A 1/2 falafel, fries and a drink was about $7 which I thought was a fair price. The woman working isn't overly friendly but I guess she's okay. 

My favorite part of the meal -- skinny crinkle cut fries...very tasty. All and all a solid, cheap meal.

Black bean burger is the best I've ever had.  And it tastes amazing every single time I have it.  Add in some crinkle cut fries and watch out.

Not overly impressed with anything else on the menu really and that's the downer.  The breakfast is ok, and I kind of like the turkey burger.  I've had the Mediterranean plate and it was fine.  So that's why the 3 stars.

The smell of dirty grease when I walked in should have been a clue, but Bongo had been recommended so I wanted to try it. This has to be the worst burger I've ever had at a place that "specializes" in burgers.  The most flavorful item on the sandwich was the lettuce. The burger was so flat it could have passed for a tortilla. There was a tiny sprinkle of processed shredded cheese on the cheeseburger. The crinkle cut fries were crispy but cold, and there is no way I will go back

Well done burger. No fancy schmancy creations here ala goat cheese and sundried tomatoes, just standard, meaty, fresh ham-NOM-NOM-NOM -burger. I had my doubts but I was glad I got get my burger fix here. 

Pricing is pretty standard, and I honestly haven't eaten crinkle fries since elementary school but everything is cooked well and nice and filling. 

I am interested in trying their mediterranean stuff as well.
I love the mushroom burger here! add some of their ranch dressing into it well I think its ranch and your good to go! Great place if your in search of a quick bite.

Bongo Burger is an affordable, accessible place to satisfy a burger craving! At first I wasn't a fan of how bread-y their burgers are, but after multiple visits I grew to appreciate their food. I'm yet to try any of the middle eastern dishes on their menu, but I'm confident that they'd be tasty as well.

Best Falafel around especially for $4.50. The fries are good and always hot. We call the hamburgers the "All Day Burger" because it literally takes all day to eat one because they are so big. Pastries have to get the boot but everything else is good.
good but not great falaffel. sufficiently filling, good price, reasonable taste, but missing that "je ne sais quoi" that bumps food from good to great.  nonetheless, i will be back!
This is the same as all of the other Bongo Burgers.  Good turkey burger, but the rest is pretty standard.  I don't really like their middle eastern entrees.

After hemming and hawing over this for far too long, I'm pleased to declare Bongo Burger my Berkeley burger favorite. As much as I like places like Amanda's, Barney's, Al's and the newly-opened Burgermeister, Bongo is more consistently delicious than all of them combined. The cheese to burger ratio is always exactly right, and holy crap, their crinkle cut fries are AMAZING. They pretty much do everything right here - the only minus is that its proximity to campus makes it ridiculously crowded at lunch time.

I love this place. When I work from home I go there once a week. If I am not working from home, I sometimes go there on the weekends.
The meat they use is good, much better than at other non-chain restaurants.
I like the Persian burger and their fries. It is good food, fast and fairly cheap.

OK, I have this thing going where I'm trying to decide if Bongo Burger or Burgmeister is the best. Theses places are several blocks away from each other.  I have went back to both a few times and I'm still up in the air. The burger is good, but a little on the thin side. 

The bun is huge and I noticed the same guy slamming meat on the grill is the same one touching my burgers, so I am concerned about getting sick. Now for under $8, you can get burger, fri, and a small drink. 

They also serve breakfast which I have yet to try. There seems to be tons of eating places near by so probably good to try them all. The staff is kind of blah, blah. No music, no tv and ambiance is non existent.

The do have several other good looking things on the menu I would like to try as well. I still think Nations Hamburgers are the best. You be the judge.

I def like this place a lot. This burger joint has an interesting middle eastern vibe to it. They sell different kinds of burgers with flavorful toppings including falafel. The service was a bit bland here but the food was actually well done! I ordered the turkey burger and it included crinkled cut fries which I don'd see anymore in any burger joint. These fries were interesting and very unique. I also enjoyed the freshly grated cut lettuce in the burger. The turkey was very flavorful. I enjoyed how the buns on the burger was lightly toasted in a way where the burger was held tightly packed. 

The place was spotless and the condiments were clean such as the ketchup and ranch bottle. 

I would come back here again for another burger!

Hella good!  Luv the skinny crinkle cut fries.  Had the #1(mushroom & swiss burger) add bacon which came w/ fries and a drink.  It was really good, tho i agree with some other reviewers in that it's a little bread-y but overall a great burger.  

Great Value! My total w/ tax was just under $10 which i thought was well worth it for the quality of food I got, especially since i recently spent close to $8 for a crappy Burger King combo last week.

Solid Burgers with Niman Ranch meat means you're getting something delicious without completely trashing yourself on processed food.  It's a really good burger at a good price.  It's not hard to see why they're doing good business and expanding.

Service is quick and effective, though seating can be limited at busy times, or when weather is poor and outside seating is limited.

I don't do the veggie stuff, but the meat is top notch.  This is my go-to place to get lunch when I'm on campus.
The only lamb I eat is in a Persian burger - anyone know the seasoning they use to cut out the gamey flavor? I see paprika flakes, but there's got to be more....

So so service, considerably long wait, okay food. The veggie burger is good, the homefries were okay but the bell peppers were not fresh and were overdone, and I found the mushroom burger sloppy and plain tasting. The ranch they have is delicious, especially with the regular fries. Prices, location, and seating are decent though. A good eatery for a vegetarian student.

Meh. I ordered a Bacon Burger w/ onion rings. The rings were good. The bun was past its prime and dry, but I'm glad they grilled it. The meat was untasty -- yeah that's right, untasty. 

I'd go again to try this Persian (ground lamb) burger everyone else has raved about. Might add some hummus too. We shall see if I ever make it back, however, since my burger cravings come about once every six months or more.

I tried their mushroom burger and California Omelet. The burger is quite good but the omelet is nothing special. Both items are very greasy. Their prices are not that cheap; for example, the Mushroom Burger combo costs $9.

The cashier is really unfriendly.

Before I happened across this place, I used to spend my lunches at Blondie's Pizza. Now, there's nothing wrong with you, Blondie's Pizza -- I ain't hatin', you know we're still cool -- but eating a slice of pizza every day can get old, fast. I needed something new. 

I was wary of Bongo Burger at first. I stumbled in and shyly ordered the first thing on their menu -- the number one. The mushroom burger. I sat at a window seat and waited. It was done. I grabbed it, took it back to my table, and -- and this part, I'll never forget -- the moment I smelled it, I knew. I knew it was the one. 

Indeed, my nose has never let me down before, and this time was no exception. Their mushroom burger was fantastic. Thus began a beautiful relationship. I texted Blondie's the breakup letter. We still see each other sometimes, when Bongo's line is too long, but it's just -- it's not the same. Blondie's is my silver medal, and I think it knows. Anyway, the mushroom burger -- it's truly grand. I used to get one every time I was in town, before I started eating healthier. Oh, who am I kidding -- I still get one all the time. I have no self control and it's just so delicious. ;_;

It's a tiny restaurant, though. When it gets busy, seating can be damn near impossible. I feel so bad for the nice people working, because it seems like they get overwhelmed by the sheer amount of business the place gets. 

In all seriousness, the food and the people who cook it are what truly matters, and this place really hits the nail on the head. Great chefs, friendly cashiers, excellent food -- all around, this is a great place to eat. Kudos, Bongo. Keep on stylin'.

hands down BEST burger place I've been too.  This beats In-N-Out, Fentons, the small burger joints, Mel's diner, anything! I got the spicy chicken burger. omg, the bun, the dressing, the flavor.  I can't stop thinking about it after I had it! AMAZING

I was craving a burger when I got out of class and decided to make my way to Bongo Burger since I have never been. I wasn't expecting it to be anything great but it was a damn good burger.

I paid $8.37 total for a #6 meal which comes with a fat juicy turkey burger, crinkle-cut fries, and a small soda. The turkey burger was sooo juicy and flavorful! & surprisingly pretty big! They use a different kind of bun - more of a crusty roll than your regular smushy hamburger buns... they don't get as soggy and hold the burger together better.

My go-to burger joint!

Bongo uses Niman Ranch beef, which matters to me. And their prices are cheap. And I have had Bongo Burger jags when I have eaten there at least once a week. But I might be done with them now. Yeah,they are cheap but I'd like a meatier burger. They will sell you a second patty for $2.75 and I am willing to pay $2.75 for the added amount of beef but I want a thicker patty, not two of their very skinny ones. I want a thick hunk of beef. If they just grill two of their skinny burgers, it's completely different than grilling one thick patty.

I won't go to Burgermeister:  their prices are gouging, altho they use good beef, also use Niman Ranch. . .

Now I go to Phil'sSliders. At Phil's, you get tiny two ounce FAT meat patties cooked medium rare for two bucks. If I pop four bucks, I get four ounces of beef, which is what you get in a standard Bongo Burger but the meat is pink in the middle, the patty is thick. .. you get the same amount of beef, the beef is arguably a higher quality than Niman Ranch. .. 

Good bye Bongo.
six words: persian burger and crinkle fries, YUM!
Best burger spot to eat around downtown Berkeley. A little expensive but worth it. Its pretty crowded from 1115 - 1230 on the weekdays so avoid that timeslot, service is REALLY slow.

The Short:
Having eaten at all 3 Bongo Burgers near the UC Berkeley campus (North, South, and West side), I have to say they do a good job keeping their flavors consistent. Come here if you have a burger craving and want to enjoy a nice sit-and-eat with a friend.

 If you're looking for a large and satisfying burger, Bongo can help get you satiated with their generously sized burgers. These are filled with chopped lettuce, tomato, and a large Niman Ranch patty smothered with something that resembles Thousand Island dressing. These burgers don't taste like your traditional American burger though-- the buns are slightly crispier and ketchup and mustard does not come standard (or least in non-noticeable amounts). Despite this, they still taste good, but not good enough to keep me coming back for more. The fries are very delicious-- cooked well and definitely crispy.

My mine gripes would be the prices of their additions (adding cheese costs $0.75) and the price of their other offerings like the Persian Burger. Their breakfast menu is nothing stellar-- offering the standard toast (not that well made), eggs (decent), and potatoes (meh).

Service is nothing out of the ordinary, and the decor of the restaurants are comfortable for sitting and chatting. 

Recommendations:
- Cheeseburger Meal

Pros:
- A nice twist on the American Burger (crispier bun, shredded lettuce, wide patty).
- Beef is from Niman Ranch (I like higher grade beefs, they taste better in my opinion).
- Fries are golden brown and crispy.

Cons:
- Other food offerings are pricey.
- Additions don't come cheap.
- Average-at-best breakfast menu.
had the black bean burger. it's a vegetarian burger patty served on two thick onion buns. decent taste and fill, but could use more spice.

My boss told me to go here when I first came to Berkeley.  The first thing I had here was the Persian Burger.  It was a hoagie filled with tomato, shredded lettuce, and grilled lamb.  Oh so good!  I loved it so much the first time that every time since, I have gotten the Persian Burger.  One time I did try my boyfriends Mushroom Burger, and that was equally delightful.  The best thing about this place is that they don't make their patties too thick.

I got the half Persian burger when I read all the rave reviews for it.

The flavor was pretty good (I love lamb) but I felt a little jipped when I saw the lamb patty stick out and thought "wow, they don't skimp on the meat." As I started eating, I noticed that they actually just pushed the patty outward and the inside portion of the bread didn't actually have lamb in it. 

I shall try their beef burgers next.

Tiny burger joint. The food wasn't too bad, the fries were different and good. However the drinks were tiny and packed with ice. If you want a refill, they charge you. A little pricey for what you get, which is decent at best. The place is very tiny on a very busy street, so seating is limited. There are better options out there
I LOVE the Persian burger, with some of that ranch sauce...MMmmmm TASTE GOOOOOD!

These burgers are really good, but I have one compliant... the fries taste almost HEALTHY, and I don't want that. I want big greasy fries that make your hands all slippery when you try to pick up your soda to wash down the salt that's just coated your mouth.

I like this Bongo Burger better than the one on Dwight because it feels so much cleaner which is kinda a big deal for me.

On that note, the service is much friendlier here but the burgers are pretty much the same! Personally, it takes 1.5 burgers to fill me up at Bongo so I like to get 2 and save half for a late night snack!

Got a recommendation to get the Persian Burger and it was great.  Made with lamb meat and is huge with plenty of lettuce and spices.  My daughter got the Bongo salad which is only $3.50 but could have been a whole meal.  It was a very Middle Eastern creation and tasty.

Great food, large portions and cheap pricing.
Honestly, this place is exactly the same as the Bongo on Northside and on Southside. Except for the outdoor seating. The outdoor seating makes the greatest difference.

Great spin on hamburgers! I love their Persian Burger. It's in a long roll with a thin pattie of lamb. It's flavorful, moist, and delicious! Their fries are excellent, as well as their mushroom burger. Everything is great here.

I had the All-American burger. The buns were well-toasted and  the beef patty had good beef flavor. I'm not sure what to make of the fries, since they came in a sort of jagged shape that suggests they may not be freshly made. But on this, I couldn't tell. I thought my meal was kind of expensive, and I would like them to make thicker hamburger patties.
Well, they have a Persian Burger which is simply the best. It is so good I rarely ever order anything else. And if you are Persian: They also have Doogh, but you have to ask for it.

I have gone to this place for burgers for more than two decades, and I have not been disappointed once. The hamburger is juicy and perfectly charbroiled, the fries are crisp, the tabouleh salad well spiced. I lalso like the so-called Persian Burger, which is done with lamb, though at times I find it dries out. At under ten dollars, an excellent value!

I don't understand why this only has 3.5 stars. I really love this place. I never really understood what the Persian Burger was, so curious about all the reviews on it, I tried it out myself. It is sooo good and HUGE. When you get it, looks like a sub, but when you unravel it, you realize its fattyness. mmMmm. I also liked the fries. While they look like regular crinkle fries, something about them makes them taste almost like they were dipped in corn dog batter (completely reminds me of something you would get from a fair). Great location too! Steps away from campus, the BART, and Shattuck shops... I really don't understand where it COULD go wrong!

Coming from a very good burger city (Seattle), it was a good, hearty burger. Liked the sauce and toppings, but wasn't mind-blowing. Definitely above-average, and good for a quick eat. Also, centrally located to downtown Berkeley on University Ave (the location I visited).  

Biggest disappointment were the fries. They tasted like they were the frozen crinkled kind you get at Safeway.

For hearing so much about the Persian burger, I was expecting it to be something really exotic (like a GardenBurger!), but it's just lamb.

I don't know how I feel about eating baby animals, though adult animals I'm fine with, so I opted for the turkey burger deal (about $7 with a drink and fries) and it was rather scrumptious (though it could have been baby turkey for all I know). It left me satisfied without feeling too heavy, and another plus, easy to bite into, which is good for someone with no teeth (or something like that). 

Stop in if you want a filling, reasonably-priced meal.

The neighborhood standard for a nice fat juicy burger! The prices have gone up but the quality has stayed constant. Near campus and easy to get to. At times the service seems indifferent, but all in all great experience.

Big, generous, juicy, and packed with burger flavor.  This is an unpretentious place that makes an excellent burger.  Also lots of less traditional burgers to try. If you are walking along Center St. during lunchtime....YUM.

Bongo Burger is a great place to dine. All three branches are awesome, but I go to the one on Center the most. They're all basically the same thing. The food is fantastic, especially the Persian burger. And fries. And onion rings. And everything. Tip: the half-sized Persian burger costs significantly less, but it's almost as big as the full-size so if you want to save some money, I recommend doing that.

Short and sweet review.

To be honest, I only really get the falafel 1/2 sandwich and fries here. Both are excellent and imho the fries are the best of their type.

Th eating environment is fast-food'ish but the food is a cut above. Very reliable and consistent.

Had lunch here today. Good size burger that tasted good, and fries that tasted even better. Combo meal for about $8 with a drink, so not too bad. 

I probably could have given them a 4 if they had my favorite burger - Hawaiian (pineapple with teriyaki sauce....YUM). Other than that they did have a good selection of meats to have instead of beef.

On the the way from BART to the Game.  Check.
Serves Niman Ranch Beef.  Check.
Cheap.  Check.

So, I confess that I got the Falafel sandwich and it was tasty.  The falafel (is the plural of "falafel" just "falafel"?) were hot, crispy and moist inside.  I don't think that these things had been sitting around in a pool of oil for a long time.  The lettuce is just iceberg (not my thing) but the freshly fried greaseless falafel made up for the average fixings.

I love Bongo Burger! Almost every time I come here, I get the mushroom burger. The meat is nice and juicy and the mushrooms are smothered in sauce. It hits the spot every time.

One time, I had their falafel and it was not as good as their burgers. I would recommend that if anyone orders falafel, they should order the half falafel rather than the full falafel because the full one is too big for one serving. Also, most of the pita is filled with lettuce and tomatoes rather than falafel. Oh well, I guess there's a reason this place is called Bongo Burger and not Bongo Falafel.

Good burgers! + tasty crispy onion rings - nasty employee attitude (and this is not just once, this happens everytime I come here) = 2 Stars.  The only way I'll eat a Bongo burger is if I get a friend to get it for me, so I won't be offended by their horrible customer service. Lol!

Bongo Burger served me literally the worst bacon I've ever ate in my entire life. It was unpalatable. If I weren't in a rush, I would've gone back and complained. Bacon is an easy meat to cook. For $6.04, I expected better -- I literally could've got superior bacon from McDonald's.

I was originally going to give a four-star review, but the star of my bacon cheeseburger -- the bacon -- was the stringiest, toughest, most gristly mess I've ever eaten. It felt like chewing on a knot of floss and boogers. Absolutely terrible. And no flavor, either.

The burger patties themselves are of respectable quality (Niman Ranch, which to my mind sold out a long time ago) and the other ingredients were also adequate, if not delectable. I do appreciate the toasted sesame bun that comes with each burger. Service was friendly and the venue, while spartan, does have nice, large tables that are good for groups and working lunches.

I usually get breakfast from here.  In their morning specials, you can get scrambled eggs, potatoes and toast for $3-$5.  I usually call and place the order and pick up after 10 minutes.  The food is cooked right in front, and it's worth paying the price.  The customer service staff is very unfriendly and gladly I wasn't the only one that noticed.

I went to Bongo Burger this weekend specifically for the falafel sandwich, and I wasn't disappointed.  As suggested by my friend who has been here many times, i got the half falafel with hummus and american cheese.

Even though I had been warned not to get the full falafel I had my moment of doubt as to whether a half order would do it for me.  A half order comes with two falafel patties in a pita and stuffed with veggies and sauce, the full order is four falafel patties.  I thought for sure the patties would be tiny and not filling.  I was wrong.  The half order was plenty enough and the falafel patties really do stick to your ribs for the rest of the day.

I also got some onion rings with my order and those were pretty damn tasty.  They are very similar to Carl's Jr. onion rings, for a point of reference.  Their fries are crinkle cut but on the small side.  They aren't like the big fat crinkle cut fries that you had back in the high school cafeteria.  They were tasty though.

I'm definitely going to take the BART ride up to Berkeley more often, and maybe even try to make a lunch run from the FiDi to have the falafel again.  I want to also make an effort to try their other items.

Overall the little place was nice, conveniently located just a short walk from the Downtown Berkeley BART station, and the price is very resonable ($3.25 for a half order, $3.95 for a full order).  With more visits and a better idea of what everything else tastes like I may add a star.

Saw this place while walking around the city, and decided to try it out with a couple friends. All three of us ordered the bacon cheeseburger meal, which came with krinkle cut fries, and a small drink. The burger itself was great, the meat was really juicy. The one thing about it that I didn't like was the fact that they used bits of bacon rather than strips of bacon; however one of my friends really liked that, so to each his own I guess. The fries were wonderfully cooked; they were crispy on the outside, but were still soft on the inside. I also really liked the fact that they had ranch squeeze bottles set out along with the usual ketchup bottles. The drink was just a drink, but I was upset by the fact that they filled it to the brim with ice, so that there was barely any soda in it (I don't really like soda so it wasn't THAT big a deal to me, but it might suck for others). On top of the fact that you dont get soda, they don't provide refills, but again it didn't bother me that much. I say it's definitely worth going to.

Bongo Burger=Good Burger. I've only had burgers here twice but both times they were excellent. The first time was in between finals so it definitely helped me maintain my mental sanity. The second time was for late lunch. I've tried the All-American Burger, Mushroom Burger, and fries. All were great! I liked the Mushroom Burger over the All-American (too plain for me). Also, I've tried a bite of the turkey burger and it had a really awesome taste! And usually, I don't like turkey-Thanksgiving or not! The sauce on the burger makes it worthwhile. Not expensive either. Around $5 for a burger. Also, the toasted sesame bun...mmmm mmm! I like how they have a decent selection of "regular" burgers and then different ones too-like the black bean burger! Next time, I'm going to have to try the Persian burger!

Randomly chose to try this place for dinner while walking through Berkeley... not great, but not bad either.  It definitely has some sort of Persian influence ... not sure how the name "Bongo Burger" fits in anywhere...

Anyway, on to the food.  The menu seemed appetizing.  The food was mediocre.  Better than dining commons, but not by much.  The burger was pretty dry and overcooked, but greasy at the same time.  The french fries look like they came from the grocery store's frozen-food section.  But in spite of it all, as I polished off my meal, I found myself liking it more, and it really didn't taste that bad.  Just enough to get three stars.

It's a pretty small place, maybe half a dozen small tables.  and because it's downtown Berkeley, there's no parking.  But it's close to the Bart station!

Their burgers and fries leave a lot to be desired, even if it is "student prices". I prefer Jack in the Crack.
Though their breakfast is perfect, if you want a good high cholesterol, carbohydrate and protein fix to start your day. Thats pretty my only reason to go there. Not to many places on that block serves up breakfast.

4 stars for the turkey burgers
1 star for customer service

*Nothing else needs to be said*

Everyone in Berkeley has had a delicious experience at Bongo Burger, and this reviewer is no exception!  Here are some highlights of the place:

Awesome:
1. Persian Burger - so good.  I'm not a fan of lamb, but their Persian burger does not taste strange at all.  The bread is extremely fresh and crispy, and the veggies are all crisp and delicious.  Try it, at least once!
2. Fries - they know how to make fries the right way.  The fries are crinkle cut and are way better than any Ore-Ida fries (although I like those too).  These will disappear into your tummy in no time.

Good:
1. Cheeseburger - Niman Ranch beef = good.  The buns are just perfect and everything just tastes great together.  They're made-to-order, so paying a dollar or two more than McD's is totally worth it.
2. Mushroom Burger - not bad.  This is a pretty standard mushroom burger, which also means that it needs more mushrooms!  It's a good, safe pick, but won't blow you away.  (head over to Rocky's for some delish mushroom burgers!)

Every time we come here, they are super friendly and super quick.  The location at Center St. closes early (8pm I think?), so you've gotta eat earlier to catch a meal.  Parking's kind of sucky at night, so take-out is always an option and it tastes just as good at home!
Doesn't taste like anything special to me... I guess its better than fast food... but just barely.

We were in Berkley after driving down the coast from Bodega Bay and desperately wanted beef. My friend and I stumbled into this places and ordered some burgers. Both of ours were good and the fries were crispy and yummy. Good? Yes. Sublime? No. Value? Yes. I'd god back if I was on that side of campus again. 2 stars with leanings towards 2.5 if it were an option.

I guess the Persian burger is the one OK thing I've tried here, but it's kind of flavorless and really not that good. Which makes this place kind of like that "hole-in-the-wall with great food" minus the great food.

I can understand hitting up Bongo Burger on Dwight or Euclid if you're an undergrad who doesn't know any better or doesn't venture west of Oxford St. But here, you're just steps away from real food, for crying out loud!

Not was I was expecting.  

When I was in high school and I was part of that annoying dance/theater crowd that had rehearsals until late in to the night (8pm), we would sometimes come here during a break or right before.  The half falaffels were huge and enough for the whole night, the fries were mealy and delicious and the burgers looked juicy (I never got one).  It was ridiculously cheap too.  

Well, the prices have gone up and the quality has gone down.  The only thing that looked worth it in the place was the hot dog that was $0.25 more than top dog but twice as big.  The persian burgers looked thin and limp.  The regular burger that I saw some guy eating looked good.  It was the size of a large grapefruit.  He enjoyed it with relish but alas I was too shy to go over and ask for a bite.  

I almost got the fries except when I looked over at that same guy's tray, his fries looked skinnier than they used to.  I think crinkle cut fries shouldn't be too skinny because the extra surface area already makes them crisper.  I was never a big fan of the over fried crunchy fry so I decided not to get them.  

The sandwich was not so good.  It was bland.  And it had too much mayo.  There was ample lettuce and tomato so they get an extra star fro that.  But the absence of anything else, the filling I ordered, was disappointing.  Ok, it wasn't absent, just very very little of it.  Nothing to sink my teeth in to except the salad.  

It made me want to go home an have a salad sandwich like Rob would make me except his also has slices of cucumber, pepper, and a little salt.  Yummy.  

This sandwich filled me up so I'm glad I didn't buy the french fries.  So now I feel unjustly full but disappointed at the same time.  Why is that?  How can that be?  I feel like I wasted valuable real estate in my stomach for something that was not worthy of being digested.  

Maybe I'll get the hot dog next time.
got this a couple times. i thought their burgers were dry! both locations!!

4.11.2009

For the past week, I've already eaten Thai twice and Persian once, so I wanted something different and my colleagues said this was good, which was why I phoned in my order for pick up. They said it'll take about five minutes, but I was expecting them to take longer because it was lunch hour, but they really meant five minutes because when I picked it up in 15, my food was luke warm. 

When I arrived to the somewhat empty place, the lady at the counter had her eyes closed and I had to say excuse me twice before I got her attention, and a group of male workers were playing with their electronic devices toward the back. It was a Saturday, so UCB students weren't around, which was why so many restaurants close during the weekends. 

I saw a bigger than average commercial worthy assembled All-American Burger which I appreciated because some places (such as the fast food chains) don't and when you try to pick it up things slide and drop. I peeked under the bun to see what was in there: a lot of lettuce, a little bit of tomato, very little grilled onion, which I finally found underneath the bed of lettuce. I wished they gave more onions and ketchup. 

This didn't compare to Rico's. The burger lacked flavor because it was diluted by the very generous portion of lettuce that wilted by the time I ate so no crunch, but I could still mildly taste the ripeness of the tomato and ketchup with a hint of beef from the very thin, dry beef patty.

Wow... I was really disappointed. I have been hearing how good Bongo Burger is for YEARS, in particular (what is now called...) the Persian burger. So I finally made it down to the Center Street shop, hungry and ready to be wowed, but left feeling letdown. So when we went in, the place was empty, but it seemed as though a million and a half people followed us in. I thought that was a good sign as I waited for my food. My first impression of the meal was that the burger was super long. It looked good! I started off by munching on some fries. They were neither good nor bad. They were just fries. Sorta crispy. VERY salty. But whatever, right? Rarely do you go to a burger joint JUST for the fries. So I took a bite of the burger... the anticipated moment and... blaaaaaaah. My burger (overall) was dry, as if there was no sauce/mayo/mustard... nothing. And because the meat is thin (not that I am complaining about the meat), it just wasn't enough to add any kind of moisture to the burger as a whole. AND... I can only assume they toasted their rolls with a nuclear toaster of some sort because that puppy was TOASTED. So much to the point that it hurt the roof of my mouth. :( To end on a good note however, I did think that the meat on the burger (Persian) was VERY tasty! Just wish the rest of the burger was as good as it was!
Very similar to the Euclid location but cleaner and friendlier. Black bean veggie burger is where its at. Crispy french fries are also amazing.
Tried the black bean burger and though I'm not a vegeterian by any stretch of the imagination, it was different and fun. I liked it.

This place does everything on their menu right.

The turkey burger has a healthy feel while still being satisfying.

The bacon cheeseburger is a calorie splurge no doubt, but ohhh is it worth it (don't eat this every day though)

The falafel is okay, nothing spectacular unfortunately, but considering the strength of their other offerings I don't fault them too much because some times you just want a filling meal without killing bambi or her friends, that is when the full falafel comes in.  

The breakfast special used to be the deal of the century but since has crept up in price.  Still though two eggs toast and some tasty potatoes for around $4 is not too shabby at all.

Finally the Persian burger, quite delish, with nice peppery grilled flavor with just enough lather of mayo on a french roll.  Wonderful!

Expect not to be greeted or acknowledged by the depressed/crabby cashier, a middle aged woman. 
Bad service aside, this place is pretty good. I've had just hummus, and the Eggplant plate. Sadly, the 2 slices of eggplant in this were tiny and overwhelmed by grease and cheese. The rest of the plate, however, was wonderfully refreshing. Tabouleh with crispy shredded lettuce, lots of hummus, and  pita bread, which I wished they had toasted.
I would go back and order something else, without eggplant.

Plenty of places make burgers but this is easily one of the best burgers in Berkeley. The cheeseburger is a delight: a generous, flame broiled beef patty topped with cheese on a crispy, toasted sesame seed bun with slathered with just enough condiments, piled with the right amount of fresh veggies. Simple yet awesome stuff. Their fries are crinkle cut fries, lightly salted, perfectly crisp on the outside and mealy on the inside. 

Go here for your Berkeley burger fix. You won't be sorry.

I don't eat burgers often but I had a severe craving for one the other day. Bongo Burger popped up, was walking distance from home, seemed like a solid lil spot.

Stopped in for a lil lunch date with my hubby and we ordered up two American Burgers with cheese and one order of fries. The burger was legit, flavorful, well done. Fries were also good, they were the crinkle kind. The bun on the burger was a bit burned, but other than that, the place was good. The menu seems good and has some vegetarian options as well. Staff seemed nice.
Burgers are average and fries are okay. If you must have a burger on your way to class from the Bart station, give this place a try....You prolly won't come here THAT often

My first review is  for one of my favorite restaurants ever.  I have been coming here since the early 90's.  At first I was just a teenager looking for some fries, but now my standard order is a persian burger with fries, and either coke or coffee. (and yes, the coffee sucks, but caffeine is caffeiene, lol.) I'm Greek, so even though not exactly Persian, I do like my lamb very much, and I know the right and wrong way to cook it, and Bongo Burger consistently gets it right.  It isn't "cheap" but if you get the whole Persian Burger you'll have another amazing meal the next day or whenever.  My first love there, the fries, are still quite tasty  I got them with ranch even before they had it in a squeeze bottle, so  maybe the trend came from me?:)  Since I'm a salt fiend I  don't mind the saltiness of the fries, but i do taste them now to make sure they don't need more salt.:)  I have had their beef burger once, and it was ok, but the lamb is where it is at for me.

One note, I never come here if I'm in a hurry.  Everything seems to be freshly made which is good, but that also means it may take a minute for it to come out.  I allow myself 45 minutes to a hour for lunch here.  I also use a wheelchair, and can't  bring my own food to the table . (unless I want to wear it, lol.) and they have been very helpful, and I think know my likes enough to know what condiments I like with my lamby goodness.   The resturant isn't spacious but I can fit fine in my wheelchir without blocking anyone. (once I order.)   I might  think twice about coming with another wheelchair user is it may get cramped, but have never tried.   If I lived in Berkeley, I  would come here even more often!

So, Bongo Burger is really named after me...JLo ain't got nothin' on me...but that's another story.  And not one I will tell here.  

Ah...I digress, yet again.  Sorry, back to the review.  

This place is crowded at regular lunch times, but if you go just a little earlier you can beat the crowd.  Located on Center about 1/2 a block from Cal, you will find this place to reflect the college culture it is surrounded by.  

Good and reasonably priced for a burger joint.  I usually get the Turkey burger lunch deal (burger, fries and soda) for $6.  Occasionally the turkey burgers can be a little dry.  The black bean burger I have been told is excellent, coming from some vegan/vegetarian friends.  The beef burgers are tasty as well.  Fries are yummy.  Onion rings doubly so.  

I will miss you Bongo Burger...

1.  They don't wash their trays.  Take from that what you will.  

2.  Their half-falafel sandwich is about as messy as a burrito without the bottom folded in.  The bread always breaks and the fillings fall all over the place.  That being said, it's very delicious and probably the best falafel I've ever had.  

3.  They serve that High-C pink lemonade that I like.  

If I'm in the area, I usually come here when I get sick of Saturn Cafe.

I usually get the mushroom burger or just their normal burger (I think they call it an American burger...?). The burgers are pretty good. The way they make their buns is actually pretty good. It's sorta toasty but soft. The fries are also pretty good. I think the only thing it has going for it is that it's close to campus...because, honestly, I'd take In-N-Out Burgers over this any day of the week.

The 1-star rating pertains to their breakfast food.  I tried their 'two-eggs-and-two sausages' breakfast meal that came with 2 slices of toast and some potatoes.  The eggs were nothing out of the ordinary, and same with the sausages.  The toast was average, and they only gave me enough jam to use on one slice.  Now, their potatoes... let me just say they are the worst potatoes I've had in a long time; they were SOGGY.  I would think they are supposed to be fried in a skillet, as most potatoes are at breakfast places, but these were just hot and soggy, like they came straight out of a pot of water.  I'm never going there again for breakfast.

Was up here on business and met customer for lunch. Way better than average fast food.  Fresh squeezed OJ and carrot juice, make a nice choice.  I had a great Persian Burger and my buddy had a MED. plate, very good.  I'll definitely eat here again, next time at CAL on business....
Still just fast food and a fast food atmosphere...

Passing by the door and have heard from locals (I'm not from CA) that this is a great local place to grab a burger. I finally broke down and went there for a burger and some fries. The Burger was real hamburger meat and cooked right there in front of you. I recommend getting one with everything on it, makes it taste incredible. It is a good burger when it is "dripping" down your hand! The fries were the crinkle kind with the right amount of salt, I'm English so I added vinegar and let me just tell you I was in heaven! I would go back and try the different things they have on their menu. The service was average, however if it was a sunny day and lunch hour I can image it being busy.

Five stars for Bongo Burger...
I love this place...
I love the tahini, falafel, tabouleh,Dolma, salad, 
the fried things (fries, onion rings are very crispy and super good)
the black bean burger (even though I love the other things more and rarely get this- it IS really really good)
I still like this place, and have not outgrown it even after all of these years.

I've been lunching on Center Street, off and on, for almost six years now.  I've tried most of the non-chain places between Shattuck and Oxford, and even some of the chains.  I've fallen in love with establishments that closed, and then I fell in love (or infatuation) with their replacements, only to be disappointed when they predictably closed.

Top Dog and Bongo Burger were the only real holdouts, and I don't have an excuse for that.  OK, for Top Dog maybe I did (who wants to order a Wienie anyway?), but I bit that bullet before the new year, so what kept me from Bongo Burger all this time?

Pure stupidity.

Yes, they have burgers, but they also have a very decent black-bean burger, and they have crinkle-cut fries.  But what I liked most about my meal was the bun.  I'm not usually one to comment on buns except to criticize them for being too small for the burger, but this one was ample enough and delicious to boot.

I'm coming back to try the falafel.  Boo for only having Coke products in the fountain, but yea for some really sweet service.

Inna & I had lunch here today, pretty tasty.  I had the no. 3 w/o onions.  Decent burger on a nicely toasted sesame seed bun.  Fries were good.  Very crowded, but we were able to get a table before our order was up.  Thanks, Inna!

Good burgers with the steam grill taste. Crinkle cut fries just like you used to get at school cafeterias. And a surprisingly tasty mediterranean plate. And all pretty cheap. 

Now if they only had the original chalupas/taco boat or tater tots, this could be like my elementary school cafeteria and I'd give them five stars!

There are times when being Iranian can be a bit embarrassing; '79 Hostage Crisis, Salman Rushdie Fatwa, The Anti-Holocaust Convention; The Black Cats. And then there are times when being Iranian fills me with pride, and one of those times is when I'm sippin' down a doogh at Bongo Burger. 

Sia introduced me to this place during his brief stint living somewhere other than our parents' house in Fresno. Then I started school and Bongo Burger became a second home. Delicious burgers, delicious fries. Their doogh isn't on the menu, guys. You gotta be in the know. 

When I graduated from college all my family came up to watch me walk. Afterwards my Dad rounded us all up and walked us over to Bongo Burger. You shoulda seen us; a bunch of browner than white, lighter than Arab, clucking Iranians pouring into the Iranian burger joint to celebrate the completion of my American education. I'll go ahead and throw that experience up on the "Proud to be Iranian" side of my ethnic-experience tally board.

Maybe somebody should get Ahmadinejad a Bongo Burger doogh. Maybe that's all the guy needs to chill the fuck out a little bit.
This was/is one of my favorite Berkeley lunch spots.  Relatively cheap, healthy (black bean/turkey burgers, hummus and pita), and easy, plus everyone that works there is super nice.

bongo has falafel too. went for the 1/3 lb.  niman ranch burger (4.25)
-medium rare, a little red, very tender meat
-lettuce, tomato, mayo, mustard. 
-added a cup of tahnini(?)  sauce available on the counter.
best $5 spent on a burger!
5 stars!

crumbs:
-cooked to order, 10 minutes.
-cheese not needed. saved .75 cents...

I would give this place 10 stars if I could. I don't even eat meat (ESPECIALLY not lamb), and I can easily kill a persian burger here.
