stop reading this, and run to the nearest branch and get yourself a mind-blowingly delicious persian burger (don't waste your time on a regular burger either).

Tried the Bongo for the first time today.  The standard cheeseburger is great. It comes on a Sesame seed bun with Niman ranch meat. Yum

The fries are standard frozen fare, nothing special. 
What really sucks is soda refills are 65 cents. Please! It only costs you 5 cents.
If I go back soon I will only get the hamburger! Enough said!

Meh...I found this place to be just average.  My food was good enough to eat and cheap, but there wasn't anything overly special about it.  I ordered the falafel plate and all I was thinking was that when I get the one at Trader Joe's I get hummus.  Yeah...it really wasn't better than that.

All that being said, if I have somebody cool to hang out with, I'd go there again...but not if they ever raise the prices.

Matt was in the East Bay for a work-related project. He went to one of many popular hangouts lunch spots for UC Berkeley students. Some of the restaurants are attention- getters for strangers, but a jewel to city-locals and college students, depending where they dine. 

Matt went to one of the city's institution for lunch, which is Bongo Burgers. The busy burger joint is small with a few tables and located not too far from the campus and the adjoining strip of the city of Berkeley.

The Mushroom-Swiss burger meal (#1) is what Matt had for lunch. The $7.50 combo meal had the custom-made burger with melted Swiss-cheese and Grilled Mushrooms compressed in a puffy hamburger bun. Matt has been on a burger-binge lately. The burger wasn't too oily, leaving no drippings and a mess on his uniform or his tray, but the patty was thinner than other recent places Matt has been to back home. Nevertheless, it's "just" a good burger, but not worthy of a 5-star.

The meal also comes with a small tray of thinly-cut and crispy French fries and a 16oz fountain soda. (Diet-Coke).

There are 3 locations for this city's burger place. And to avoid the rowdiness of the crowd in the weekends, this location closes at 8pm every-night. This place also accepts credit-cards and of course cash, in which Matt paid with. Are you surprised?

Matt was enjoying his meal while looking at the students and future Nobel Peace-Prize candidates walking up and down on one of the Berkeley's busy streets.

I thought this place was pretty good. I mean for $4-5 you can get a perfectly sized serving of Chinese food. The food isn't even that bad. I'm a college student with no job, so I was happy to eat here. 

Definitely take advantage of their lunch and dinner specials.

This is going to be a horrible, short review but I'm dead tired from a long night of a meeting. SHK deserves higher but the service is not astounding. I like that there is happy hour but the selection can be better. Drinks are average. 

The wait for the food is absolutely horrendous. Today, the drinks came way after the food. Sometimes the food wait is as bad as 30-45 minutes.

Great happy hour specials for food - 3-5 dollars for all that greasy Cantonese food goodness that I've missed from LA. The space is large and informal, so if I were still an undergrad at Cal, I would have totally used this place to meet up with friends or munch on something while frantically catching up on reading. Wait, did I actually do any reading as an undergrad? I suppose that's irrelevant.

I've only eaten here once myself freshman year, and I wouldn't bother to write a review for this place had it not been several unfavorable interactions in the past few days. Yesterday, my friend got lunch to go, and the cashier lady promptly pulled out a plate of old food sitting on the counter to heat up and serve to him. Apparently, someone earlier in the day got a wrong order. To screw something up, then give another customer the leftovers is doubly bad. They gave him a free milk tea to make up for it, I guess. Secondly, today a bunch of my friends came to eat after our final, and I joined with a sandwich I bought elsewhere. Famished, I happily started in on my meal when one of the workers told me that I wasn't allowed to eat outside food in their restaurant. Okay, I understand the no-outside-food rule if it's a classy establishment, but Sun Hong Kong? Really? Plus, there were no less than nine other people with me, all of whom ordered food. Lastly, when my friends finished and were about to pay, the cashier said that one of the girls in our group (who left earlier with others) did not pay for her entree. I myself am skeptical that she simply did not pay for her food, but even so, how can they be so unorganized that they can't charge a large-ish party for food correctly? Totally unprofessional. Their food also looks completely unappetizing. This place grosses me out, period.

My roommate and I only eat here when we feel like we're broke and we miss food from Hong Kong (like the actual place). The place has dirt cheap food, especially during happy hour. I usually order their bake dish, which takes a little longer to come. They give very generous portions as well. 

But really, for you non-broke people, there really is no reason for you to come here.

"I'm at Sun Hong Kong B***!!!!" 

You can't beat their happy hour

I RAFF U RUZE

This place is the bomb .

If you know what's up, you go to SHK.

Well, how about horrendous wait time, meh food, and bleh service that requires a 15% tip? 

Food: consistently blah. It seems every dish that they make has some sort of ... well, error. Sacha beef on rice - beef tastes more like shoe leather. Fried rice - clumps of white rice scattered around ... hm. Fried HK style noodles - doesn't hold a candle to Lotus house.

Seriously there are better choices right there across Telegraph.

Just okay - I've only really come here during Happy Hours, so I've gotten good deals on food & drink during then. They give decent portions and the food tastes alright. People working don't seem to ever be happy though.

Going here for a late lunch today!

Came here last week during happy hour, they have decent chinese dishes for 3.75 a pop. It's no award winning cuisine, in fact you probably shouldn't eat it more than once a month, but considering we ate for 13 bucks for 2 of us, it's a great deal. 

I had spring rolls and chow mein with bean sprouts. The spring rolls were awesome, piping hot, crunchy on the outside and deliciously juicy on the inside. They gave me a huge heaping plate of chow mein, which turned out to be enough for lunch and to feed me again for dinner later. The chow mein was kinda greasy and bland, but it was perfect for my hungover self. ;D 

Overall, it was cheap, quick and dirty (not literally, at least i hope). The service was quick, the drinks and food are cheap, and it's decent chinese food.
It makes me feel home in Berkeley. I am from Guangzhou, somewhere near Hong Kong BTW. And the price there is really reasonable..~!

I came here for my little cousin's birthday party, right before the Cal vs. Stanford Woman's basketball game. I was told the restaurants name was Sun Hong Kong, so i was really confused to see pizza on the table. 

The food really wasn't that spectacular. I would say average to below average for Chinese food. I'm on a diet right now so I didn't eat the pizza but just by looking at it, it didn't look that fabulous either. So, really everything was below average, hence the two stars. 

The two good things about the place is 1. It's really close to Cal and an easy walk to the gym. 2. The prices looked pretty damn cheap. I don't know how much my meal personally cost but by the banners on the wall my bf and I noticed that Happy Hour is pretty damn cheap.

Talk about going to a place to be completely disappointed.

Sun Hong Kong. What I can possibly say. 

Well for college students on a budget, it's a great place (especially during Happy Hour when drinks are $1 and you can get a whole meal for less than $5). There's free wifi if you order food and they've got flatscreen TVs everywhere.

But as for the food and service, by far the worst I've ever experienced. And thats saying something. Let's talk about the food first.

Food - I've came into SHK many many times and each time i hope that the food gets better. But who am i kidding. They've got a knack at serving bad food. seriously. I ordered mongolian beef once and i couldn't tell if the meat was actually beef or not. I ordered schezuan beef another time and clearly, the only thing they wanted me to taste was hot sauce. I ordered this chicken noodle soup type dish and couldn't eat it after i saw a small strand of curly hair in it (=__=). the food here is decent but can also be severely diappointing (not to mention the many times my friends and I have found hair in our food).

Service - about the worst service you can get at a berkeley restaurant. The wait time is almost ridiculous and thats not because there may be many customers around. I see many of the staff here standing around and gossiping all the time. They're always speaking in chinese (i'm chinese btw and can understand everything they say) and they're either talking about someone's mother, family, or a customer being too skanky, stinky, or requesting too much of them. Well maybe if they didn't just stand around and gossip the entire time they might just accomplish something besides burning what little calories can be burned while standing. Not only that, the two women staffed here are by far the rudest and almost incompetent individuals alive. Literally. When they were my servers, they didn't ask my friends and i if we wanted water/drinks. we literally had to flag her down and request it from her. She then came and practically slammed the drinks down on the table. when we asked for more napkins (because she spilled some of the drinks nonetheless), she proceeded to gossiping about how we were useless college students who don't understand the hardships of working in a restaurant. But of course, she EXPECTED her 15% tip for the terrible service she gave us. 

Food here is cheap during happy hour. But other than that, i would much rather eat ANYWHERE else. If you have a huge group, they've got a lot of space so I guess thats an incentive to go. But like i said, decent food, terribly bad service.

Hong-Kong style tea-cafe type food such as crispy noodle and pork-chop over baked rice?  Check.

Budge meals under $3.00 during happy hours?  Check.

Clean, well-lighted place including a semi-open kitchen readily observable for customers to inspect for cleanliness?  Check.

Friendly, fast service?  Check. 

A variety of teas and other types of hand-made drinks to quench your thirst?  Check.

A very, very happy stomach that is waiting to come back again to try another one of the restaurant's two hundred menu items?  Check, and check for another two hundred times.

You pay for what you get. Don't expect some crazy good service here especially during the day. I like the lady who serves at night though, that's when I wouldn't complain about the 15% automatically added gratuity. They have deals throughout the day. Lunch special for $3.95 rice plates or with spaghetti. That is served like 12-3 or so. Best to try is the cream corn over rock cod over rice. Happy hour is from 3-6, with a variety of hong kong style food ranging from $2.75-3.75. Drinks are a buck only. I usually get a porridge, noodle soup, or fried rice. Their fried rice is worth the buck! Large portions and yummy 90% of the time. The food quality was horrible when i ate there after the big game. Dinner special is from 6-10, with Chinese and hk cafe style food. $4.95 comes with the entree and a milk tea or soda, so fairly similar to happy hour if you get a drink with your food. Milk tea, iced watermelon drink, iced strawberry drink are a buck throughout the day. So yeah, poor college student? This is your spot.

Yay! Sun Hong Kong is back!

As a student I lived off the plain porridge and fried bread and was so excited to go and have it again. It's just as good, but the dishes are even nicer! ;) Price is a little more than the $2.80 it used to be..... $3 for the porridge and $1.80 for the Fried Bread.... Not too bad considering it has been 10 years! 

It is a little weird in the bottom part of Kips... but still the ultimate comfort food for me!

Their happy hour food is a really good deal. You get a lot of beef chow fun for $4.10. The quality could be better, but for such low prices, I really can't complain. 

Their regular prices are ok, but not nearly as enticing.

Shitty food. 

Really shitty service. Like fucking diarrhea service. Got cussed out by a waitress for asking questions and asking for my bloody food to be cooked again.

This is my GO TO takeout restaurant.  I wouldn't eat in.  This is a typical hole in the wall Chinese restaurant with no ambience but it does have WIFI.  Just ask them to give you the WIFI code if you want to dine in with your laptop.

A restaurant by the same name and owners used to be on the corner of Shattuck & Addison but they lost their lease and now have relocated to Durant.  Their old location was open until 2 AM but his location closes at 10 PM.  The menu has changed also.  The old restaurant was more traditional Hong Kong style cuisine, had great table seating and used to be packed at all hours of the day or night.  This location and menu is geared for Cal students, has a mix of Chinese and American cuisine (burgers, pizzas & pasta) plus ice cream and gelato.

Bottomline, you can always get a meal here for $5 or less.  Restaurant tries to do too much so some dishes are winners while others are losers.  Don't expect great cusine especially since their target market now are Cal students, but if you give this restaurant a try, I bet you'll find some favorites too.

There is always a special happening.  They have lunch specials for $4 from Noon-3 PM, "Happy Hour specials" from 3 PM - 6 PM starting from $2.75 - $3.75 with $1 hot/cold drinks and dinner specials for about $5 starting at 6 PM. You never have to spend much here to get full and the food is tasty.

I have my favorites:
1.  Lunch special:  Black Bean squid over rice for $3.95
2.  Happy Hour specials:  Rock cod rice porridge or egg noodle with beef stew soup for $2.75 and chicken chow mein for $3.75
3.  Dinner special:  black pepper pork chops with veggies and rice or pasta plus milk, tea or soda for $4.95

They also have a  3-entrees plus soup special for $17.99 for those nights when you absolutely don't have the energy to cook for your family.

I'm always tempted by their $1 premium ice cream scoop as I'm walking out and on a hot day, their $1 ice cold watermelon drink is a must.

Here are dishes that are NOT my favorites so be forewarned:
1.  Chicken Wing appetizers--irregular pieces, not much flavor but during Happy Hour, you do get 8 pieces for $2.75.
2.  Mongolian beef or chicken over rice-sickeningly sweet--$3.75 @ happy hour
3.  Baked pork chops over pasta--they serve this awful canned spaghetti sauce over the pasta--$3.75 @ happy hour
4.  Chinese green with oyster sauce--just watery bok choy--$3.75 @ happy hour.

I think the primary virtue of this place is that I can order Mongolian beef over rice and a "small" plate of fries simultaneously if that's what I'm in the mood for. Much like the "small" plate of fries that is not in the least "small" and like the gigantic cavernous-like cafeteria space, the menu of this place is absolutely mammoth. They seem to sell pretty much most things, whether it's a glass of Horlick or a ham and egg sandwich (DO NOT recommend) or rice porridge/jook. 

This may come as a shock for you, but the quality of the food is not that amazing. Lotus House has better Mongolian beef for a couple dollars more. On that note, it was lucky that I wanted French fries that one time because the Mongolian beef is $4.95, and there's a minimum charge per person of $5. Crafty. 

Despite this lackluster review, I'm probably going to eat here again, hopefully between the hours of 3-6pm so I can get in on the happy hour pricing.

It is not the best Chinese food, but it gets the job done. If you are short on time, come to this place and you will be in and out in no time with a full stomach.

They have good specials on foods and drinks. Pretty much dirt cheap food.  None of their dishes standout, but I have not had a horrid dish in the half dozen times I have been here.

Service is faster than the Flash.

The decor is very cafeteria like, but it is clean and comfortable enough to finish your meal. The ambiance is blah. All it is a bunch of loud college kids surrounded by TV's.

If you come with the right mindset of it being just a quick, mediocre place then you will not come out disappointed.

I only go here for happy hours.
$2.75 for appetizers, $3.75 for entrees. 
It's cheap. I'm happy.
I usually go for the chicken wings and one of the baked dishes (I've tried BBQ pork and cod fish.... they're OK).
Also a good place if you have a large group. They have plenty of seatings.
Once we ordered food from here for a club meeting, too. They're okay as well. Good for the cheap price!

Reasonably priced dishes for the college crowd.  Lunch specials are likely to be the best deal in Berkeley.  IMHO, the owner could switch the ice cream bar up front to sell Asian style snacks and desserts instead to generate more revenue.

hk style milk tea = love it

By the end of my senior year I was coming here every day for a cheap meal.  Not because it was incredibly delicious, but it was good enough and cheap.  If you're really sheisty, go for the happy hour.  

What did I order all the time?  Don't even remember...some combination meal that came with a drink.  My friend though the baked seafood dish was okay

Honestly, most of the food is pretty terrible save a few items.  I endured the occasional meal here demanded of me by my friends who want to save a few bucks, but service generally sucks.  I've had my order forgotten twice, a waiter who really didn't want to get me a cup of water despite being asked several times, and even had a friend whose party was chased by an upset waiter with the nerve to demand that they leave more tip ( the short story was that they went for a quick bite, got ignored most of the time, spent an hour and a half because their entire table's orders were lost, then were left waiting for change when the bill came, so they finally just paid minimum and left ). Not somewhere I'd eat at just because I was in town.
Disappointed

Yeesh, me thinks this place is trying too hard.  Giant posters are posted on all the walls with random promotions and deals.  I swear, every time I take a peek inside, I see some new gaudy colored flyer advertising some new dish that's not even Chinese.  Nominally, this restaurant is chinese, but their American/Irish bar food selection is starting to grow much larger than the Chinese menu itself!

If you do eat here, order the traditional Chinese dishes.  Harder to mess up.  Also, only go during Happy Hour where you get your moneys worth.

I've tried the Beef Chow Fun during their happy hour deal. I was pretty tolerant with the mediocre quality of the chow fun (a little too oily for my taste) but I comfort myself knowing how little I paid for it.  Stay away from noodle soups; poor preparation and they skimp out on ingredients.

An OK cheap chinese on south side, the menu is gigantic including many non chinese things so really you could go there every day and have something new and comforting and relatively acceptable. It's also ridiculously cheap, especially happy hour, and is moderately filling. Even has good stuff like clay pots that you'd only find in more genuine chinese restaurants. An all around passable place for a student to go. And if you're not a student, you should know better. Tsk tsk.

ewww no. it's cheap, its greasy, you'll leave feeling GROSS. vietnam village offers better homecooked-tasting chinese food. or fork over a litlte more for quality tasting chinese food at great wall. there is also a place on north side..i forget what it's called...that is cheap and has good chinese food. something garden?

You don't go here 'cause it's fancycat chinese food.  The ambience is cheap and the theme is plastic.  The food will fill you, and will taste decent.

It will also probably cost next to nothing, which is why I used to come here so often, especially during happy hour.  This isn't the white man's happy hour either, no no this is the asian man's happy hour where food is cheap and satisfying.

So bring a friend, catch up, and don't break your wallet.

I love this place for the price, but I hate it for what it does to my stomach... I try hard to get the $1 pearl milk tea during happy hours whenever I can, but the last time I went, I had some stomachaches after. Also, their happy hour specials give me worse stomach problems... 

Putting my stomach's health aside, I do think their big rice plates are pretty good and filling. I got the curry rice plate, and it was only $4 and the portion was ginormous! I shared it with a friend and we were both really full. However, I just can't put its tendency to give me problems after, and I know I'm not the only one who has this problem. Nonetheless, if you're hungry and broke like me, and you just want some goddamn rice with a bunch of shit, SHK is the place to go

4 stars because the food is affordable, the menu has lots of options, there's happy hour prices and lunch specials, and their mango gelato is pretty good. Tastewise I've had better but can't complain when you're budget eating and their portions are generous and they get you outta there pretty fast for take out.
I LOVE their $1 Ice coffee!!! It's actually very good....and addictive!! :)

If you're looking for a cheap meal between 2 and 6pm on a weekday, you can't get much happier than Happy Hour at Sun Hong Kong with entrees ranging from 2.75-3.75 and drinks at $1.

That said, there are a couple things to watch out for (as there are with every cheap-o restaurant):

1. If you order tea, be prepared for blank looks even though it says "green tea" under the drink menu
2. the chow fun is not very tasty.  The beef is soft and tender, but tasteless.  Seems to be a common mistake of too much cornstarch or simply bad cooking
3. Do not order the red bean snow.  I know it sounds yummy, but do not start picturing fine, shaved ice and sweet red beans.  Instead, imagine chunky crushed ice mixed with cubed ice and freezer-burned-barely-an-excuse-for red beans.  Maybe that image will keep you from making the deadly mistake that we made. 

Avoid these pitfalls and hopefully you will enjoy your happy hour!

This place is JANKY AS HELL! First off the place looks like its ran by this family that serves chinese food, Italian food, gelato ice creams, and american/diner---ish foods. It looks dirty too from the outside and looks unorganized from the outside; I cant even explain it LOL

I had chowmein  which was oily and their spicy beef was a bit too salty. Their Tiramisu gelato didn't even taste like thick rich flavors; tasted like coffee ice cream -_-

I just don't understand this place! no wonder their deals are so damn cheap! its like roaches crawl the ground up. EWW

Will not come back

This is a review for the restaurant mainly, not the bar.

As an UCB student, this place is one of my favorite spot for Chinese food around campus. They have good Chinese (not American Chinese) food and decent pizza. For American food lovers, they also have omelet, risotto, pasta, soup, etc. And the Happy Hour (3-6pm) price? The BEST for poor college students. $3.50(?) for a dish that's enough to, well, get my stuffed, and $1.00 for a drink (non-alcoholic).

The staff here are pretty cool too. They may seem mean to some people, but they really don't mean to give that impression (and to be honest, they are nice comparing to a lot of Chinese restaurant staff). Betty (the slim taller woman) told me the other day that her and Helen (the shorter woman with short hair) are often misunderstood as rude when they talk to each other in Cantonese. Many people just assume that they are talking in a foreign language because they are criticizing. But the truth is, Betty needs to explain stuff to Helen in Cantonese so she can understand what's going on.

For the bar upstairs, I don't have much to comment about. I can only say that it's totally college style; it's not somewhere you'll want to go to if you are looking for a nice, upscale place. There are "interesting" drunk people and they are sometimes fun to watch.

CHEAP processed foods.  QUICK service.  LACKLUSTER traditional Chinese dishes.  Yup, it's one of those places.  You will definitely frequent this place if you're a poor Berkeley student.  If you don't fall into that category, there definitely isn't a reason for you to stop by.

Walking around Durant Ave and Telegraph in Berkeley leads to many choices for good food at low prices.  Sun Hong Kong is one that I stumbled into before the Marie Digby concert last month.  I was starving and the pictures of the rice plates posted on the window looked delicious.

This is one of those eateries that serve everything..  When I say everything, I mean, it's a Chinese owned restaurant that serves chinese food, but you can also order a burger, or pizza.  I ordered a beef+tofu rice plate for only $4.99.   My two buddies ordered a pizza, and won ton flat noodle soup respectively.  I wolfed down my rice plate before the pizza came.  The waitress apologized for not warning us that the pizza would be late, so she offered some fried calamari on the house.  My buddy declined and I was apalled.  He ended up eating only half the pizza and of course I took advantage of my recent spike in metabolism and ate the other half.  The waitress again, came by to apologize for the lateness and offered some ice cream.  This time, I spoke up and took the ice cream.

Other items on the menu include pearl tea/boba drinks.  I didn't get one.  For awhile during the concert, I felt ill but it went away quickly, so it was worth it.
Not cool...15% tip automatically added for non existing service and mediocre food.  The food was much better when the restaurant was still on Shattuck.

One of my favorite places to go because of HAPPY HOUR. Boba is only $1 and it is really good here (the boba is sweet and chewy). I am addicted to the Sweet and Sour Pork and it is only $3.75 during happy hour. 

The service is kinda bad. Some of the workers are rude, don't speak much English, and take a while to serve you. However, the value of the food makes up for it and still makes it one of my favorite places to go. Good for large groups.

Came here for something quick and cheap. Sun Hong Kong delivered on on both accounts. They're known for their cheaply priced Chinese food.

I ordered the Cal Special available from 6-10pm and got BBQ pork with vegetables, rice (or spaghetti), and Hong Kong milk tea (or soda) all for under $6!!!! It's definitely convenient that they accept credit cards since most of the Chinese restaurants will only accept cash.

The eating area is pretty basic. And they have an extensive menu with Chinese and American food (burgers, pizza). I always go for the specials which is always solid.

The Chinese food does not taste that great here, hence the cheap price. I like some of the food like fried rice and their appetizers - chicken wings, fried zucchini sticks, etc. My friend ordered beef stew, which was very hard to chew. I like the American food more here. The drinks are cheap but they put too much ice. I only come here only during happy hour or when I'm with a big group. The service is very poor. My friend accidentally spilled her drink, but the waiter didn't replace it and didn't really seem to care.

I only go there for happy hour because the prices for everything is so freaking cheap. 

They only get two starts from me because the food isn't that good at all (you pretty much get what you pay for).

This place has decent food, and the prices are great during Happy Hour! The chow fun, mongolian beef, and curry chicken over rice are pretty good dishes during Happy Hour. Also, the warm coke with lemon is good on a cold day! Service can be slow during the busy times but it's definitely worth the money! One of the owners, Betty is really nice. She gave me free ice cream for my graduation!
Salt and pepper chicken wings!

The only thing that makes this place more appealing than other Asian eateries around campus is its HAPPY HOUR specials. From 3-6pm all their drinks are $1 and their rice plates are like $3.75, which is pretty good considering how decently sized their portions are. 

The food isn't fabulous, but it's pretty edible especially if you come during happy hour b/c that time is (for me) late lunch time- meaning that by that time, I'm starving and will eat practically anything. 

The service here isn't very good. I always just go to the counter and stuff because they don't really proactively come over (but it's w/e). Another thing that isn't so good about this place is that my bf always gets a stomachache or some kind of digestion problem after he eats here. He hypothesizes that their dishes aren't cleaned very well because it's just so damn cheap. This never happens to me though, so maybe people with weaker stomachs shouldn't come?

Overall, just come here during happy hour-- probably not worth it otherwise. ALSO, happy hour = almost no customers = immediate food.

This review is for their HAPPY HOUR, which is the only reason I even step foot into this establishment.

ATMOSPHERE

Sun Hong Kong is pretty dingy... It's actually kind of dirty (I always see flies in the entrance). it's your typical low-end Chinese restaurant that's fast and cheap, which makes it a regular spot for broke college students. I only frequent this place when I want to grab a cheap and quick boba and some chicken wings with friends.

The bright side is that it's pretty big, which provides for ample seating so there's never a wait.

FOOD
1) The Hong Kong iced tea/coffee drink is delicious, but does anyone else think that it's weird that they use TINY boba straws?! They are seriously about 3 inches long...

2) The fried chicken wings are also a safe bet. It's enough to share if you're not TOO hungry and they are usually fried to perfection.

Cheap food near a college campus, what else can you expect?

Well, actually a lot! I love coming to Sun Hong Kong during its happy hour (3-6 everyday, besides Game Days). Here are a few times of significant notice:

- Fried chicken wings: 8 fried chicken wings for $2.75, where else can you find amazing price like that?! To add, they taste absolutely delicious! Mix some salt and pepper, which are on your table, and dip the wings in them: yum.

- Porridge: great for a cold day in Berkeley! Also $2.75. Not as great compared to the ones in Chinatown, but will do! They actually put a decent amount of preserved eggs and pork in the porridge.

- HK Styled Coffee and Tea: $1 for a sweet cold drink. You can't even get milk tea in Asian Ghetto at this price, and the coffee in it makes you work efficiently afterwards!

- Watermelon Drink: Also $1, but apparently it's seasonal. I heard it's even fresh made!

I don't go here except for happy hour nowadays, but it sure is great. The service may lag a bit, but you just have to be very direct with them and get used to serving yourself sometimes (with extra napkin and chopsticks). Perfect for a mid-day snack.

The food there is gross!!!  That's why it's so cheap.  You get what you pay for.

Their boba milky tea tastes like powder.  Their HK style iced coffee is not bad.

The atmosphere is not very welcoming.

The waiters are not very friendly.

The best hong-kong style restaurant near campus. The happy hour is perfect for a budget meal. My favorite part about it is the friendly fast service!!  Helen makes the best milk tea ever!! Also the fat guy seems a little cold at first, he's actually very sweet.  I am always so happy to go there. Everything there deserves five stars!

As a Chinese student at Cal, I have probably been to Sun Hong Kong for about 200 times!! 

If we are just talking about the food, I will give 2 stars cuz there are really not much good foods. Beef Fried Rice is one of the few that is good. 

However, as a poor student...this is an awesome place because it is ridiculously cheap!! i think the beef fired rice that i just mentioned is like 5 bucks or something...

One thing to mention is that even if you there by yourself, they will still charge you 18% tips automatically. Moreover, the tricky part is that if you pay by your credit card, it still have a space for you to write tips. So, make sure you don't double tips..

It's solid, it's cheap, it's filling...it's gotta be chinese food.

The best thing about Sun Hong Kong comes down to three things - variety, price, and real milk tea.  They have a slew of dining options ranging from chinese food to pizza to steak, and most of what I've had is pretty good and very generous.  The HK milk tea to me stands out here; it's not necessarily better than the delicious pre-mixed powder stuff, but it's different, and gives you a little bit more variety when you're looking to fill up ($1 happy hour milk tea sure doesn't hurt, either).

If you're willing to splurge a little, the honey walnut shrimp here is definitely better than the other places; you can tell the shrimp is freshly fried and delicious.  The "chef's special" curry is worth trying, but it took a while to come out when I ordered it.  As for other recommendations, I'll let you know; I'm on a mission to try everything on this ludicrously large menu.

The food is delicious and comes in huge portions! A great deal and nice to find a quality, sit-down Chinese restaurant so close to campus.

My main complaint with Sun Hong Kong is the service. I had to wait FOREVER to be served, and the waiters don't speak that great of English. When I received my check it had a few errors on it, and it took forever to resolve them.

Plus, I think there's a bit of a racist bias there. (I'm a white male.) I got there and was waiting around to be served, and about 5 minutes later a Chinese student walks in and a waiter immediately goes to his table. A similar pattern ran the entire meal; the waiters would constantly bypass me in favor of their Asian customers. Maybe I just had bad luck, but I honestly felt like I wasn't welcome there.

Additional problems: there is a mandatory 15% tip - outrageous for parties of less than 8. Especially considering the crap service I got, I did not like being forced to pay an extra dollar.

I also went using the Munch On Me promo (it's one of those deals web sites, where you buy a meal at a discounted price, and get a coupon code to use at the restaurant) but my waiter didn't understand even though I explained what was going on. I don't know whose end the issue was at, the web site's or the restaurant's, but either way, the waiters and staff should know when they're running a promotion! Or at least ask their supervisor who (hopefully) should know.

Still, really good food. If you don't mind waiting forever for service or grouchy waiters, it's worth putting up with lol.

You go to Kips if you want some cheap food. It's good, but not great. It's just a good place to get lots of people together and just have some food. They really have a variety in their menu from Chinese to American. It's quite interesting.

This time around I got something off the $4.95 dinner menu - Peking Style Shortribs. They were overly sweet and just okay. It's a great place to just watch some tv while hanging out with friends. We normally come here for gelato which is okay as well. I feel like this place is overall just okay. 

The milk tea there is pretty good so I always get that when I go to Sun Hong Kong.

After being a loyal customer for so long, I'm so fed up with how rude the servers are. The wait time is horrendous during peak hours. And now they started charging gratuity when I dine in...for one person.

One of my worst experiences I've had here was ordering one of their dishes with the tilapia. There was a stray bone in the fish that got stuck in my throat, and I had a really fun night after that...

CHEAP. like everyone has said. 3-6pm for the best deals.

personally, i think the milk tea is solid, iced coffee odd-tasting but got caffeine, the food... well.. i know my hk styled food and this food is def. got some good wok hei. too bad i dont eat meat... but the few times ive been here... it's decent and cheap :]

Their food was okay, but I definitely tasted much better food. First off, I ordered BBQ Beef with Scrambled Eggs Over Rice, and they got the wrong order. How does Sweet and Sour Pork sound like BBQ Beef? On top of that, I ordered a to-go box, and the cashier didn't even think of giving me a fork. I had to ask for one. Plus, the sweet and pork was not all that great. It really disappointed me because who can go wrong making sweet and sour pork?!

Now I'm going to review their gelato.  I had a massive craving for coconut ice cream but alas, was unable to find it after Amare, Moccacino, Carvel... etc.  So we ended up at Sun Hong Kong and I already knew I had to have the coconut gelato, but I tasted the blueberry too which was good!  But my heart was set.  Anyway the price is decent, 2.25 for a single cup (4 oz weighed to perfection).  

Also do not get the fried fish balls for happy hour appetizer.  You get 7 dinky fish balls and they don't even taste that great, for 2.75.  However the potstickers are very much worth it!  And the iced milk tea is pretty good.  Don't get the iced watermelon drink.  BTW they serve all their iced drinks with sugar and milk unless you tell them not to!  Until next time.

Ok, I only came to Berkeley due to a conference with UCSB.  Just letting you guys know, we have very little cuisine diversity at SB.  So my friend and I decided to wander the neighborhood a bit cuz we were hungry.  I recalled gettin a Singapore fried noodles and wonton soup.  The noodles were delicious and greasy.   The soup on the other hand, was definitely lacking flavor.  I did not enjoy the plain taste of it...and I LIKE PLAIN!  The noodles on the other hand were delicious.  Greasy and fresh.  I did not want to eat too much of it since it wasn't mine.  It may be because I was extremely hungover from partying when the conference almost ended last night, but it definitely helped me recover from a night of 4 Lokos and Vodka.

The only positive thing I can write about Sun Hong Kong is their happy hour. The food isn't exactly the best thing out there. But, if you're strapped for cash and want a medium-sized meal, then this is the place to go. Some of their baked dishes are pretty good, but the traditional Americanized Chinese type dishes are below the norm. Their milk teas have very little milk tea and definitely not worth that extra dollar. If you go, just get some of the baked dishes during happy hour, like the baked BBQ Pork, and I think it'll be satisfactory for what you have put in.

Cheap food, flatscreen with sports channel, and happy hour loaded with $1 drinks.  Awesome! 
Good for the price food. Can be so much better, but money is king in college life, cheaper the better.  
Service tends to be typical Chinese restaurant status, but it's all good.  You shouldn't expect much out of Chinese restaurant anyways.  
BUT! if you become a regular, the waiters will actually talk to you and it's pretty good.  
-1 star for not good food.

To be honest, I was surprised by this place. I expected tasteless subpar not enough soy sauce or msg Chinese food, yaknowwhaddaimean? However, to my delight, I found a pretty decent selection of CHEAP and fairly yummy food! I think I'm more smitten with the cheapness of happy hour though. See photos below for the most recent and relevant menus. 

While I've only tried one happy hour dish so far (Beef w/ black bean sauce over rice), I give this place 4 stars for its closeness to campus, CHEAP (can I emphasize this more?) prices and decent hours. Did I mention free wifi that I'll probably be stealing from now on?  I will be back to try the rest of the selection and their boba milk tea of course.

- Minus 1 star because they were still cooking their boba when I came in around noon and wouldn't be ready for another half hour.  Also because I'm a picky SoCal Asian girl who indulges in 626 Asian food so I know what's up and what's not. 

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/8Xq5VtwYjayKlxEY2PipQA?select=Ynnzt7eZJSdGIfKeG_AGjQ#Ynnzt7eZJSdGIfKeG_AGjQ

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/8Xq5VtwYjayKlxEY2PipQA?select=gXLC_UqWCcwSRHIrlBmn_Q#gXLC_UqWCcwSRHIrlBmn_Q

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/8Xq5VtwYjayKlxEY2PipQA?select=hjEXhYpvxhi_HxjKE5b3tA#hjEXhYpvxhi_HxjKE5b3tA
The worst customer services and bad food. I have to remember to not return again!

So dirty!  While having dinner, a guy from our next table jumps out of his chair to come over to us. He points his finger at my husband and warns him not to freak out. We are both scared by this "crazy" stranger.  It turns out my husband was accompanied by the biggest cockroach he or I have ever seen in our whole entire lives. It was as big, if not bigger, than those hissing cockroaches. Yuck. YUCK!!!!!

We were so traumatized that we dint remember if the food was good. Actually we are still trying to forget that we even went inside this place.

My initial impression of Berkeley after 4 years is that Chinese food in Berkeley, for the most part, especially compared to San Francisco, sucks. 

However, if you're willing to lower your standards, Sun Hong Kong is not bad. 

Now, what exactly do I mean by not bad?

Well, if you're willing to lower your standards of Chinese food to the Berkeley level, SHKR is more like a 7 out of 10. Their happy hour is awesomely cheap for the poor Cal student or college student in general and has large portions. Compared to Mandarin Gardens in the Asian Ghetto or for the more politically correct, the Durant Food Court, their BBQ fried rice is awesome and HUGE! One meal would satisfy at least 4 girls that eat baby size portions.

Furthermore, if you go between the hours of 3-6PM, your meal will be ridiculously cheap and you'll get a better deal than the days of being a freshie, swiping your card, and filling your to-go box such that it becomes a fat baby you're carrying. Plus, nothing can beat their $1 Asian drinks - boba, milk tea, red bean snow, etc...

How many sports bars can say that they serve decent Cantonese cuisine on the cheap? This casual and laid back sports bar utilizes its top floor to serve drinks and to show sporting events on TVs while the bottom floor is a well lit Chinese restaurant that serves decent Cantonese and Hong Kong cafe style dishes. My brother and I love to visit this place whenever there's an important Cal game to catch. Among the traditional Cantonese dishes, I particularly enjoy the chow fun, pan fried noodles, and shrimp with scrambled eggs over steamed rice. I'm also a big fan of cafe style baked fried rice as the seafood combination is one of their best dishes to check out. Service is attentive and on point especially when the owner is present. They also have a good selection of boba drinks but I often opt for the ones from Sweetheart on the other side of Telegraph Ave. Grading from the perspective of a sports bar, this is definitely a four star for serving above average bar food with a great price tag and outstanding service.

This place is definitely cheap, but you definitely get what you pay for.

Their happy hour dishes are quite cheap, probably 3-5 in range. I got the chow fun for $3.75 I believe, and it was edible to say the least, but my standards can get pretty low. The noodles were overcooked, very little veggies, and it was very salty. The amount of oil in the bottom was astronomical--there was probably a good tablespoon of oil left on the bottom of the container. 

Chow fun is oily by nature, but not justifiably THAT oily... I have heard their other dishes are a little better. The restaurant itself looks dirty, and the service is quite slow and non-existent for the most part. If you're starving and kips is the only place you can get to without fainting, then by all means go. I'd rather go to Smart Alec's and get about a pound of fries for $2.25 if I was hungry and cheap. As for me, I don't think I will ever go back to Sun Hong Kong.

Sun Hong Kong is our favorite restaurant whenever we are in Berkeley.  it is cheap and authentic Cantonese.  Lunch special features at least 10 rice plates at $3.95.  $1 for ice milk tea.  Real tea, not powder.
For dinner special, you get entree (chicken, beef, fish etc.) with veggie and steamed rice, plus ice milk tea, dine-in or to-go.
While it is for dinner, if you ask the lady owner, she'll let you have it for lunch too.  Service is good, but, yes, the cooking is a bit slow.  So, call in ahead if you know what you want to save time.
My favorite is the curry fish filet over steamed rice.  Big chunks of fresh fishes deep fried in a light batter and smothered in a mild curry sauce with pepper, potato, onion etc.  It worths every penny.  Will be back again.
3-6 p.m. happy hour is OK, but not great.  Wonder who was doing the cooking?  It does not taste as good.  Maybe just a bad day or we ordered the wrong stuff?

The food is very average, whether it's fried rice, noodle soup, or entree. But I'm giving it a 2star because it's much cheaper than some other Chinese restaurants(ex: lotus house, mandarin house) that charge much more for something that's just as average OR even worse (beware). Lastly, quality of service here is comparable to the food it serves.

I was at the restaurant&I ate 3 items dinner special....it was a HUGE plate of food!! It was VERY good, it was served by a nice lady who gave us some dessert&EXCELLENT service! People should really go to Sun Hong Kong at Kip's! The Happy Hour is so CHEAP...I can afford it even though i am still at school with a cheap job! I love it there....they should have more of these places&more of that nice lady!!They have alot of different food&specials like the steamed Sea bass  so yummy, that is one of my favorites! That is why i gave Sun Hong  Kong at Kip's a 5 Star!! Plus very good drinks!!(:

Food is not bad, especially during happy hour. However, service REALLY SUCKS. Owner gave me a nasty look when I asked for extra sauce. He didn't even offer a to-go cup when I asked. He said "go to the restaurant and pour it on your food yourself." So then I had to ask another server for a to-go cup. Who got me a cup without the cap. Then I had to ask for the cap. Basically, took me 5 minutes just to get some extra sauce. Not worth it. 

Other than that, food is pretty good for the price you pay. Just don't expect to get any sort of customer service. Not even a smile.

Come on now guys, this place is not that bad for food that's sooo cheap!! The food is not terrible tasting, it's OK. During finals week, I probably came here 2-3 times during happy hour. Get the rock cod porridge for only $3! It tastes pretty good to me! The other food like chow fun and chow mein aren't bad. The General Tsao's chicken was really good too (make your own rice at home and get it for to-go! Soooo worth it). It was a deal on munchonme for less than 4 bucks! Had a banquet here before and I've tried their vegetable dishes with meat.. not bad. A tad bit oily but it didn't taste bad. Their fried rice was a bit bland. They're food is a bit better than average for Chinese food that is really cheap. 

I've also tried their milk tea. It's not too bad... and I love milk tea. It's cheap during their happy hour too. Their grass jelly isn't bad either. I'd probably choose that over tapioca. 

My parents own a Chinese restaurant in SF so I'm a bit picky with my Chinese food. So far, this place is better than other ones down the block (won't say names..). Their service probably isn't the best (one of the servers looks kinda grumpy) but it's not terrible enough to get a bad review.

average chinese food, taste like the food from a chinese restaurant in a mall. big portions though and very cheap. for a starving college kid or anyone on a budget, i recommend it. For the rest of the world, steer clear. I gave it two stars because it does serve the purpose of cheap, large portioned chinese food in a college campus area, otherwise it would get one.

Good cheap food, large portions so I can pay $4 and still have some left for dinner! The seats/tables are Cal colors, so props to that. The mural in the back is a bit weird but still nice. 

This place lost a star because apparently the waitress only speaks Cantonese. She sees asian people and starts talking in Cantonese, and being Mandarin I had no idea what she was saying. Plus she got my friend's order wrong. Not sure why they have waiters that don't speak english.

When you get chilly, you might wrap up in a nice warm blanket.  When you want to breathe, you may elect to inhale oxgen.  When you want be disgusted by inedible food, you should visit Sun Hong Kong on Durant and Telegraph. 

A poem (sorta):

Food, advertisement goes.
Cheap prices, I agree.
Vermins, worms, and cockroaches - come get your share, unfit to be eaten.
Two-Dollar, Seventy-Five cents happy hour sign, oh the deceit.
Dollar milk tea, pour it down the drain.
Die away from me Sun Hong Kong Restaurant.
My ugly stick is too good for you.
Refund please.

Best Chinese restaurant around Berkeley campus hands down. Food is cheap but fresh, tasty, and in perfect portion. The place feels clean, simple, and organized. 

The lady serving tonight was very attentive. When I was done eating, she brought me a free scoop of mango ice cream! When was the last time you got served with free desert at a budget Chinese restaurant? Well, don't hold your breath because I might just be luckier than you is all :)

Lunched today at "The Kong." I had a diet coke and chicken curry rice plate for $6.55 +tip. It was pretty good, rice a little dried out, but still for the price, a winner.  I decided to look at other yelpers thoughts. I do agree, the servers are questionable, well, yeah, pretty bad and slow. You have to remember, it's a weird place to begin with. The landmark Kip's Bar with burgers and pizza with a Chinese restaurant below and some type of ice cream stand (looks dirty, too). While I do have fond memories of the old SHKg on Shattuck Ave., this store is no where even close. I guess my fellow yelpers are right. $8 for lunch, still not bad.

I guess their happy hour prices went up recently... I got take-out from Sun Hong Kong about a week ago the their happy hour dishes are now $4 each, and their happy hour drinks are $1.25. Still not bad.

Happy hour prices are effective from 3-6pm.

I got the BBQ pork fried rice and it was good. However, it was overly "diluted" with rice, so I was contemplating whether it was a good deal, even at $4. If you get it to go, they give it to you in a large take-out chinese-food-style container. This $4 I spent lasted me 1.5 meals (even if it was a bit too much rice, and not enough egg, bbq pork, onions, etc), so I was satisfied.

I also got the red bean snow for $1.25, which is basically 1/3 sweet boiled red beans, 1/3 shaved ice, and 1/3 sweet red bean broth (from the boiled red beans). Good when you crave something sweet, but not overly sweet.

Happy Hour: 3-6  All food on their special menu 1.95-3.75 
 -- Try the $1 watermelon or strawberry drink, they are surprisingly
     realistic
Special Lunch and dinner menus on the table: all under $5.75

The point: Check this place out.
Try: BBQ Pork Chow Mein
       Sweet & Sour Pork

Went here for the Moocho.com deal. After my meal, when I handed over the coupon, my waiter told me I should have specified the deal earlier, and mentioned something about a computer. In every other establishment that uses these deals, I've had no issues with the coupon being accepted at the end of the meal, so I was pretty confused. Finally, they told me I couldn't use the coupon because my total exceeded the limit by one dollar. I offered to pay the difference in cash but they refused. Again, I've dealt with the exact same issue in other restaurants and they have graciously agreed. I had to pay the whole amount and am still holding on to my deal coupon to use later.
The food itself was served in large quantities and seemed like pretty standard, white washed Chinese food. My friend really likes the sweet and spicy pork here. I wouldn't recommend the iced tea; it had a weird aftertaste. All in all, go here for the ridiculously cheap, generously portioned lunch specials, but don't have high expectations for the most part...

Dirt cheap chinese restaurant that offers American dishes as well. There are a good number of rice dishes that fall under $5 before tax and tip. Don't expect premium cuts of meat in your dishes. Drinks are very cheap and laden with sugar. 

Basically, you get what you pay for. This food fills you up without emptying your wallet. If you're gonna complain about the quality, go elsewhere.

*Ideal for college students on a budget

Two Words: HAPPY HOUR

(or DIRT CHEAP. haha)

I only come here for take out during Happy Hour to get some fried chicken wings ($2.75) and watermelon juice ($1.00).
The portions and prices actually beat those of Chinatown!
They have a pretty good and affordable selection available for Happy Hour from 3pm-6pm, but I can't comment on those items since I've been too afraid to try anything else. Plus, I only come here when I'm craving some cheap waaaaangs!

They only serve the wing part now, instead of the wing+drummette. (YAY!) And fry them to a delicious golden brown. However, they're unsalted/ unseasoned and occasionally slightly overcooked. :( 

Watermelon juice has been consistent and only a buck!!! Same with all the other drinks during Happy Hour. What more can you ask for?!

This place isn't the greatest restaurant in the world, however for a college town campus, it fits well.  They have great happy hour prices, which at this time and age is a genuine plus.  Their portions are very large, good enough to fill you up and take some home with you.  I personally don't go down and sit to eat, I prefer to take to-go orders.  The to-go orders can take a bit of time, so I would suggest that you phone in your order so that you don't have to wait.  You can't complain too much once you see their prices!  Just take it in slowly, it may be one of those places where you either love it or hate it.

I have become a regular over the past couple months.  I'm pregnant and began craving crispy pan-fried noodles.  I've been to four different places that had it on the menu and Sun Hong Kong's is by far the best!  Get the house special because it has a little bit of everything in it... the sauce makes the noddles in the center tasty, but it's the crispy outside that I really LOVE!

Another dish that my husband and I have become fond of is their salt and pepper squid.  Actually their salt and pepper anything is really good... loved the rock cod and the pork chops were good too.  The batter is perfect and the fixings on top (scallions and jalepenos, I think) are really yummy, too.

We've had the 3 item special a few times which also comes with soup.  I've enjoyed everything that I've ever ordered on that menu and I don't think I've ever ordered the same thing twice.  I've probably tried at least 20 different things on their menu.

We recently went during Happy Hour and it was pretty packed.  Super cheap and good portions.  Since my husband and I are no longer "starving college students", we both decided that going during Happy Hour is not a must and that we prefer ordering off the larger menu.  Still inexpensive compared to a lot of places.... and hearty portions.

I'll be kinda bummed once the baby arrives and I won't be making my weekly trip to dine-in.  But I do have a menu at home handy to call in an order and have the hubby pick it up if the cravings come back =)

I used to come here a lot when it was happy hour. The food isn't the best out there...but alright considering the price (~$5 a plate). 
*What I do love is the baked porkchop though...mm mm mmm.
*Getting bubble milk tea here during happy hour is a joke..they fill up the glass with SO much ice. I wonder how much milk tea is actually in there without the ice...1/5 the cup? Not cool. If you're really craving some milk tea I suggest going to Asian Ghetto while they're making the food. 

I think the owners are really nice people but the waiters are horrible. Especially this ONE waiter....if you've been here before and you've been served by him, I'm SURE you know who I'm talking about. He's incredibly rude. One time he was too busy watching some sports game instead of taking our order. Hellloooo don't come to our table and pretend you're working when you're not. Almost every time that I've been here I've encountered him and there's always something else I can nitpick on. Horrible customer service.

Nothing that special about the decor of this restaurant...but they have a huge area in the back for large parties.

I think I would have given this place 2 stars...but it's really a good deal during happy hour (again, not the milk tea though!)

I'm here probably three times a week during the school year. I'll admit, the food isn't the greatest Chinese food you'll ever have, but it's still pretty decent and a great value considering the prices, especially during happy hour! Between 3 and 6pm a lot of items on the menu are discounted. You can usually have a full meal for under five dollars during that time, and maybe between $8-10 outside of happy hour.

It's a great place for groups, there are TVs on the walls which you can watch various sports, and the service is (usually) good. To be fair though, it might just be because I come here so often that they started recognizing me, so I can't vouch for anyone else's experiences with their service. They usually don't mind if you hang out in there for hours either.

Yummy and greasy cheap Chinese food. I recommend going during happy hour (3-6pm). I usually get boba milk tea ($1) and dry fried beef chow fun ($3.75). I crave beef chow fun a lot and this place serves the cheapest one in Berkeley. Great for college students on a budget. They also have lunch and dinner specials that are pretty cheap as well. I notice there is a quality and service difference when I go with my friend who is a regular. Overall, I recommend this place as a fast and cheap way to satisfy Chinese food cravings. For quality and nice service, though, you should try another place, like Great China.
The chef has left, the owners are going to remodel the space and make it part of Kip's.

Cheap.  Just like every other review will mention about Sun Hong Kong.  But is it any good?  It really depends on what you order.  

Today I ordered from the Happy Hour menu.  Appetizers and entrees are either $2.75 or $3.75 and drinks are $1.00.  My friend and I ordered the fried chicken (wings and drumstricks), mongolian beef with rice, and dried fried beef with thick flat noodles.  The fried chicken was the best - it came fresh from the fryer.  The mongolian beef was the low point of the meal.  It was awkwardly paired with bamboo and the spiciness was near absent with the exception of red peppers.  As for the final dish, the amount of noodles was huge.  Definitely enough to serve 2 people as one order.  Again, the noodles had very little flavor.  

Among the other specials not mentioned by others are:
$17.99 for 3 dishes plus soup and rice.  For 3~4 people.  The dishes from this special are what you see at most other family Chinese restaurants.  The menu features more traditional Chinese beef, chicken, hot pot, and vegetables dishes.  

I'm giving the restaurant 3 stars:
1 - It's cheap. 
2 - The drinks aren't that bad.  I had the iced milk tea w/ coffee.  
3 - Menu is fairly diverse.  There's a lot of appetizers, main entrees, and drinks to choose from, whether its the happy hour menu or the dinner special.  

P.S. Don't order wonton soup with egg noodles.  I don't know what it is, but they don't taste like normal egg noodles.

Happy hour prices have risen! It's now $3/$4 for an entree or $1.25(+tax) for a drink.

But the beef stew with noodles ($3.30 after tax) is still excellent on a cold Bay Area summer evening.

Cheap food, nothing spectacular, and poor service. If you want to take your food to go, its a not too bad of a place to get food from. Generally its pretty cheap and you can get a meal and a drink for around $5. If you decide to dine-in, then you will be charge 15% tip for your meal, though the service hardly deserves it. Food usually comes slow or if you go in a large group, orders are forgotten. The drinks are decent, though they vary in quality from day-to-day; but for $1 how can you complain. Although they have happy hours, the lunch specials, and barrage of other specials all along the walls means you get a "deal" any time you go.

I actually visit this restaurant fairly often because there aren't many good Chinese food restaurants around.  

Pros: 
Service: Fast and nice service. They do customized dishes upon request. (ie. You can replace noodle soup with stir fried noodle with the same sides on menu). They seem to have hired some guy who speaks adequate amount of English. 
Convenient location: 1 block from UC campus.
Price: Their food is really a bargain and comes in huge portions; items for Happy Hours are unbelievably cheap. 

Cons: 
Dishes are either very good or very bad, depending on what you like. 

???:
 Selections: They have a very wide variety of selections and provide notes on the menu of their specialty. (I did not try the specialty items out because the one I saw was Ramen noodle...) I also notice that they have a "Chinese menu" and "American menu" starting from different sides of the menu booklet. The problem with such a huge menu is that you don't know which ones taste good until you order it. 

The reviews below are base on my personal opinion. I have lived in China before and am used to authentic Chinese food. I usually don't like most Chinese restaurants here, so I might judge dishes differently from what you might be looking for.

Above Average Dishes: 
Eggplant with Seafood Clay Pot: Yummy! There's actually no (or very little) seafood in the clay pot, but since I know the authentic one has no real seafood in this dish either, it doesn't really matter. The name comes from that the dish is made with fish sauce. For those who are particularly looking forward to the seafood? Order something else.
Boat porridge: Whoever like rice porridge would probably like this one. I recommend it.
Iced milk tea and Iced milk tea with coffee: I like them here more than other places in Berkeley. The portions of milk and tea are just right.

Average Dishes: 
Fried rice (For the price of $3.75 during Happy Hours, it is good enough).
Chicken in a clay pot: This one is acceptable and leans to the (slightly) salty side. It tastes good with rice. Huge portions, though. 

Below Average Dishes: 
Assorted vegetables stir fried: I guess they usually don't add salt to dishes unless the sauce they use is salty. Why? Salt is on the table.  
Sizzling Steak Cubes w/ Black Pepper: It is beef strips with green pepper and onion grilled on hot iron plate. It appeared so yummy until I ate it. If you are a fan of Korean BBQ beef like I do, then this is not the one you should go for.
Curry chicken rice plate: I like Thai curry, so that may be why I rate this one low because they use a different kind of curry.

I have never tried their American food such as pasta, pizza or burger because it is supposed to be a Chinese restaurant. 

Overall, a good place to hang out with a group; price is cheap; food is good if you know what to pick.

Entertainment Book Coupon: Buy One Get One (Up to $7, doesn't apply to lunch specials, happy hour, etc)

VALUE!!! Lunch specials are a whole menu of $4.25 items and seem pretty solid. Happy hour is 3-6PM and items are $3. We went in the afternoon and used our coupon, but we've also gone for happy hour and I'm sure I'll try their lunch specials sometime. 

I thought the deep fried pork with spicy salt was excellent regardless of price, and he packed our to go box so full he couldn't close it. We snacked on a few pieces on the way to the car just so we could close it (and because we were hungry). The chicken chow fun was not bad, and a good portion. During happy hour we ordered Wonton Mein and Pork Chop Ramen ($3 each) and were unimpressed. The soup was extremely bland, though the quality of the egg noodles and ramen was fine. The wontons and pork chops in the soup were both fairly good, but it's hard to really like soup noodles with bland broth. I won't be ordering any more soup noodles, but I look forward to trying everything else!

Okay, I gave this place 2 more chances and I can say I think they've improved since their earlier days last year.

The happy hour specials can't be beat - so much food for such a low price! BBQ Pork over rice is good (they really pack the rice in), chow mein, and chow fun are relatively good. The chow fun was super bland last year, but they've definitely improved it.

In terms of future health consequences, this is not a place to eat too often with its oiliness level, but for the days you need a quick dinner and your wallet is thin, this will be easier for you financially than going to Asian Ghetto!

Note to self: Don't get the grass jelly anymore...it comes in condensed milk. I'd love to try the watermelon slush though. Lemon tea looks good too. And my friends LOVE the red bean snow, but I'm not a big coconut fan.

I love Sun Hong Kong.  

I've been eating here since they had a location on Shattuck (where PiQ is now located) and I think I've had -- well, perhaps only 20% of what they have on the English language menu -- but it hasn't changed.  

Awesome dishes are the Hong Kong fried noodles (crispy) and I fell in love with beef with runny scrambled egg over ice here.  It seems like a lot of unhappy reviews come from people ordering the rock bottom cheapest dishes, but you can eat very well if you upgrade slightly, and get the 3 dishes for $19 or $20 special (I can't remember which it is).  

My main recommendation is: get Chinese food here.  Don't get bulgogi or other silly things!

This has become one of my favorite restaurants in Berkeley, so what's with the 3 stars?  The food's mediocre and tastes like something I can whip up.  Not to mention service is spotty.  The 3 stars are for cheap ass decent food, in large portions, at a convenient location. Like other cheap HK joints in Milpitas and Fremont, they use a Chef Boyardee-esque tomato sauce on their baked spaghetti/rice dishes.  I grew up on Chef Boyardee cans, so that's fine with me.

As an early bird eater, I always make happy hour.  For $2.75-4.75 (if I decide to drink milk tea with my entree) I can have dinner AND leftover lunch.  That's about $1.50-2.50 per meal!  Its less than cooking at home and great for those lazy days.  I highly recommended the baked dishes and beef fried rice, since they're more flavorful and hold up better as leftovers.  Definitely worth eating here if you're a leftover eater like me, and take advantage of happy hour.

I, as one who sometimes exchanges money for the service of having someone make food for them, reasonably expect some measure of quality in the food I am served. This holds regardless of the price. Just because food is cheap does not mean its taste should be little removed from cardboard, nor does it mean I cannot complain when the atmosphere is reminiscent of a dirty cafeteria. 
As for those who enjoy the taste of the food at Sun Hong Kong restaurant, I cannot imagine what they would consider unworthy of putting in their mouths. The french toast was nothing more than deep-fried white bread. The fried rice, albeit served in a huge pile, was unspectacular and disappointing, with only specks of bok choy, frozen peas and carrots, and thin strings of egg. The dumplings were so thick they had the consistency of thick buns, and were nearly hollow inside save an ungenerous spoonful of vegetable. 
If we were in a famine, I could hardly complain. The food we were served definitely offered us calories for sustenance, and none of it was so distasteful that swallowing it was impossible. But I demand a bit more when I trade my money for cooked food.

If you want lots of food for cheap, this is the place to go. Happy hour is from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. so be sure to go between these times to order off their dirt cheap menu. Drinks are like a dollar, and an entrée is ~$3.50. One thing to note is that they don't accept credit card unless your order is $7.

I usually get the curry beef or curry chicken over rice. The curry that they make is packaged, the beef and chicken taste pretty much the same, since they've suffered from so much freezer burn that the texture is mushy and indistinguishable. 

I wouldn't recommend this place unless you wanted to dine with somebody you dislike, or a huge group of guys who could care less about what they want to eat.

The milk tea with tapioca here is also not that great. They put MASSIVE amounts of corn syrup into the drinks, and I think after two or so, you'll have diabetes before the day's over.

This review is for their super cheap drinks. I heard the food here sucks so most likely I will never try it since there are a plethora of better options in Berkeley for cheap, delicious food. But the hong kong style milk tea for $1.35 (that's with tax) cannot be beat. Get it when the lady makes it because she puts less ice. Awesome tea at a super cheap price.

So today I go to SHK around at 4 pm to get the happy hour meals. I get my order to-go and it's all good. I always get them to-go because I can't finish the portions in one sitting or I take it and eat at home. But today I decided eat at SHK, and sit down in one of the tables near where they serve ice cream. So the dude comes over (seems like the owner) and tells me I can't eat on these tables, so I said, cool, I'll go inside and eat where everybody else eats. He tells me that I can't because I got it to-go. I tell him that I wouldn't have finished it even if I decided to eat in, and would have asked for a to-go box anyways. He again tells me no, and that I have to leave and I can't complain about it because I'm "in his property" and he wants me to leave with the to-go food. 

Remember guys, if you get food to-go, make sure you f***ing leave the restaurant.

Review at-a-glance:
- automatic 15% gratuity on the bill, no matter lunch or dinner, more than 4 people or not, for its crappy service
- no change unless you ask for it
- never order soup here
- food is never fresh here

I am sick of the food here. Shame on them. They even dare to put "Hong Kong" in their restaurant name. 

If there is 0 star rating, I will rate 0 rather than 1 star.
Happy hour is the only good part about this: $4 for a decent portion. Other than that, food is mediocre, service is terrible.

Good for super-cheap, I had a week or so where I practically lived off this stuff.  Basically, the secret is: from 3-6 they have a Happy Hour, meaning every dish on the Happy Hour menu (which is large) is either $2.75 or $3.75.  Basically, I've learned you should get one of two things:
1. BBQ Pork with Vegetable Chow Mein
2. Sweet and Sour Pork
Everything else is... not quite as good.  Also, WARNING: they have a lot of drink specials, do NOT get the drinks.  All of them are SUPER sugary to the point of undrinkableness. I mean, I have a huge sweet tooth and I almost puked.

you know a place is going downhill when they f**k up the jook (rice porridge). Seriously, how do you mess up rice porridge? It's just overcooked rice in a pot of water... I bought some to go and it was SOUR. What do they do? Re-serve the same rice porridge for a week? Cheap asians.. it takes like half a cup of uncooked rice to make a pot of rice porridge, they should have the courtesy to pour it out and remake it each day. GRRR. I dont know if I can trust their sanitation and quality control anymore.
And you know why the food is so cheap? Notice it is all tilapia/codfish/corn/cream/ramen/macaroni stuff... all this comes frozen, dried, or in a can.

Obviously the fellow yelpers that gave Sun Hong Kong 3 stars or less dont know what great Chinese food is all about. 
How can anyone compare panda express to anything? Especially with the one and only Sun Hong Kong. Thats basically like comparing shit to sugar. Thats disgusting  Someone needs to make an appointment with their local doctor or dentist and get their taste buds checked, cause their full of it.

Sun Hong Kong is my type of place. I admit, it is a bit confusing when entering the restaurant because there are 3 restaurants built in one. You got an ice cream parlor, Kips and Sun Hong Kong. SHK is in the back, so keep walking until the waiter says hello and seats you. The menu is pretty big, one side is for kips and the other is SHK. They have the family style meal which consist of 3 items and soup for 17.99. Great deal. They also have happy hour from 3-6 on weekdays, i believe. The prices here are real cheap just how I like it. I mainly go for the chow fun or pan fried chow mein. Beef and scramble eggs chow fun (runny style) and House special pan fried chow mein are the favorites here. The portions are Hefty and the customer service is real nice. I can tell the owner/ employees have experience in the restaurant game, cause they definitely know how to run it right here. Much props for that.

The food sometimes take a few minutes to come out. Its made to order, so its fresh and delicious. Its well worth those few minutes, so dont trip.

Basically, this isnt your same old "neighborhood Chinese food joint". Its Quality shit called Hong Kong Style. Get it straight, don't get it twisted. one thing i cant stand, is weak ass folks that eat shit all their lives and act like they know what they're talkin' about. 

Next visit, ill definitely try some new items. Might even stop by the happy hour special cause the prices are unbeatable.

I've probably had the worst food I've ever had in a long time here at Sun Hong Kong.  It was after a Cal game, and man, it was horrible.

When you look at the menu, you'll notice a large selection, but more like a WTF selection.  Uh, pizza next to won tons... that can't be right, can it?  Let me tell you it was wrong, dead wrong.

My party orders their food.  I got won ton soup, they got the pizza and some chow mein.  It was a recipe for disaster.

My soup came in and it was luke warm.  I like my food at least above room temperature, especially my soups.  It was so gross, I actually didn't finish it, and I was really hungry after all that cheering.  I tried some of the pizza, and it tasted like digiornos.  I guess its not delivery after all.

People rave about the happy hour's cheapness, but I haven't had a chance to try it yet.  But all I have to ask is, is it worth it?  Really is it worth it?

soup, 3 entrees, and a bucket of rice for around $20. 
The food is hearty and tastes pretty good and the portions are massive.
pretty good vanilla gelato :)

You can't resist the prices of this place between 3-6pm! $2.75 or 3.75 on a meal and $1 DRINKS!!!!! This place exudes college cheapness and succeeds at providing it.

Its odd at the amount of American-style food they have, and every time i've had it its been disappointing, as in recently:
Jessica T had the Baked Pork chop, expecting some of the homey-ness of this typical HK-western food fusion, instead got a friend pork chop covered in Ketchup...ewwww

But the beef stew and sweet and sour pork I got was pretty decent. But who cares for 2.75 and 3.75 respectively. The beef stew was tasty with tendon and brisket. And the pork was deeeeeep fried and saucy, and kind of typical panda-express style, but I can't complain at this price.

Also got grass jelly drink, pearl milk tea, ice lemon coke all for a dollar each!!!!! Can't complain about that

Simple rule, stay away from odd fusions/ western food (I've had the turkey burger and its cold, with lame condiments and rubbery), other than that you'll be happy with the Chinese food, especially at the happy hour prices!!

Best place for milk tea in Berkeley. 
It is $1.10 (happy hour pricing) and STRONG...not the cheap, powdery tea you get at Quickly with a poor milk to tea ratio of 4:1. I usually opt for the milk coffee & tea- the coffee gives you the extra caffeine boost and the combination of the two flavors is really nice. 

I have had their food on occasion...it's okay. The fried rice is a nice big portion but nothing special taste-wise. Don't choose the noodles...it's a hit or miss. I haven't had any of the meat dishes since I was a veg for quite some time but it is on my to do list to try the curry chicken lunch special. 

P.S. I like how they used to have clear glass panels looking into the kitchen then replaced them with fogged glass. Hmmm...what could be going on back there?

You get what you pay for.  

The happy hour prices are unheard of in Berkeley, since we don't have a lot of franchised restaurants that have happy hours for food.  Actually, the prices are unheard of everywhere: appetizers and entrees range from $2.75 to $3.75 and most drinks are $1.  

- BBQ Pork and Rice: my BF ordered this and hated it.  He said the meat was weird and he regretted his decision immediately after ordering but didn't want to change his order.  It came with a sauce that he threw on top of everything to try and make it edible but he just ended up eating what I ordered.  What do you expect for $3.75?
- Pork Baked Rice Dish: The first time I had this, it was much tastier.  Basically, they have rice that is slightly fried in a metal plate, they have random pieces of pork over it and it is covered with a tomato sauce and cheese (ew, I hate the cheese) and baked.  At most Hong Kong style restaurants, this is done pretty well.  Here, it is acceptable for what you pay for but don't base your opinion of baked rice dishes on this.
- Dried Beef Chow Fun: I really enjoyed this.  We got a decent sized plate of noodles for under $4 and they did not super skimp on the beef!  Some of the noodles were still stuck together, but that happens everywhere.  I will probably stick to this entree from now on.
- Chicken Wings:  They came out looking crispy and hot but you could tell the quality of meat was bad.  I bit into a chunk of fat and the wings were oddly shaped, with bones sticking out in random places and some were broken, leaving traces of blood marrow on the meat.  Not appetizing but we had to try $3 wings.
- Mongolian Beef with Rice: I just tried a bite and...is Mongolian beef supposed to be sweet?  There was a small kick of spicy at the end (not so much a "kick" as it was a slight tap) but not my cup of tea.
- HK Milk Iced Tea: Bleh.  I like my tea stronger and not as watered down.  Also, my cup was filled mostly with ice.  However, no regrets since it was only $1.  
- Lemon Honey Tea: all honey and no lemon or tea.  Undrinkable. 


Service was so-so.  The waiters there aren't rude but they aren't exactly friendly either.  The food comes fast so I'm fine with it.

Went during happy hour at 5:30 and ordered the beef chow fun, chicken chow mein, and baked pork chop w/ spaghetti.  Large portions of chow fun & chow mein for only $3.75 each.   Good authentic wok flavor according to the mother in law (who knows real Cantonese food.)
