Her only complaint is they don't use the thin egg noodles for the chow mein, they only serve it on the regular menu.  The baked dish came after we were almost finished eating the other 2 dishes, it was only ok, but how can you complain for $3.75?  Had the red bean ice drink for $1, not that great, but again, I couldn't make it at home for $1.  Friend had the watermelon drink which she said was tasted like real fruit.  

Overall a good value for the happy hour specails from 3-6 pm.  Very random assortment of chinese and American food.  Where else can you find a place that'll serve fried sea bass or crab legs w/ ginger & onion, with cheese pizza, ravioli and a tuna melt?    Not to mention they have $1 ice cream scoops?!?!?  I'll be back to explore the happy hour menu more fully...

Solid little place for a quick lunch.  Very typical menu - I even went with my chinese friend and she had no luck coaxing the secret menu out of them. Perhaps we were the dumb ones for assuming they'd have one.

I actually really like the rice porridge here, but it was my first expedition with it, and I am still learning what perfect rice porridge should taste like. I know Alex wants to kill me for saying this.

This place is oddly cheap and spacious, but my suspicions were unfounded when they brought the tasty food to me and my family very quickly. We got rice porridge, beef and "scrambled" egg over rice, beef chow he fun, and pan fried noodles. It was so good, and the waitress (manager?) was extremely nice! She gave us little cups of ice cream and made small talk about her kid. 

Oh and tea/coffee drinks for $1 from 3-6PM? My kind of happy hour. 

I'm not much for being a food snob. If it tastes decent and doesn't put a dent in my already-heavily-dented finances, I am happy. Sun Hong Kong wins in both categories.

Pretty cheap food, good for large crowds.

Service/Decor: Lots of tables, you can reserve the backroom if you're coming with a large party (I mean actually large, like 50 people). Servers are pretty cranky but food comes out pretty fast. 

Food: Food's cheap, but not very good. I usually just get whatever on the menu since I already assume I won't particularly like what I get, but I've gotten the mongolian beef, sweet and sour pork, curry chicken, and a few more. There's a special happy hour menu in which you get the meal and boba that I got with grass jelly, which is kind of nice. Apart from cheap food, there's really no appeal to this place.

I'm a huge fan of their milk tea, it truly has that Hong Kong style milk tea taste. It's super cheap too, $1.25. This may be the new place that I go to instead of Quickly for that milk tea fix.

I got a beef chow mein (the crunchy kind, you get a choice between that or thick noodles). It tasted great! The portion is really big I could barely even finish it. Keep in mind that I did not go during happy hour, I went on a Saturday night at around 9pm. The total came out to be $7.75 which is pretty good for a large meal and a milk tea. I'd say this is also pretty on par with Vietnamese Village in asian ghetto (of which I am also a fan of too).

Happy Hour is awesome here! From 3-6pm I think. The drinks are a $1 during that short time frame, but its to go only. The milk tea is pretty good but when I saw that they had grass jelly drinks I had to get one. I was pleasantly surprised at the amount of grass jelly, it was great the perfect way to cool off or just plain enjoy! Although in the last few times I have gone the man making the drinks didn't seem to know what he was doing and I didn't get nearly enough grass jelly. But all in all still good for the price and great for a starving college student on a budget!

I have been a regular customer here for the past three years, and cannot say enough good and bad things about this restaurant. I guess I will just list a few things...

PROS: Excellent food and value for the price. Lunch specials and Happy hour specials are only 3.95 per entree for a large meal, which is the best value you can get in Berkeley! The food is very good, and comparable to the other chinese restaurants nearby. And they are very generous in their servings. One of my favorite lunch specials is the chicken and soft tofu over rice. It is delicious!!
They have a very wide variety of foods in addition to chinese food, including pastas, pizzas, and burgers.

CONS: The customer service is just horrible. If you get takeout, make sure you call and order 15 minutes in advance before you pick up. Also, make it VERY clear what you want, and repeat it. I always make myself clear, yet the past THREE times, they screwed up my order. (I ask for chicken, and they give me beef...) They also did the same thing for my roommate, I feel like the employees have hearing problems.. Also, the chinese lady who works there to take orders is very, very rude. Makes me very, very angry.
The last time I went there, somehow my one order took them over half an hour to make, yet I was basically the only person in the restaurant..

I would definitely go there for the value and selection of food.

Go to Cal and want cheap Chinese food? Sun Hong Kong is the place to go. The price is very cheap, they have some set lunch and dinner for $4.95 plate + a soda or milk tea. I've been here twice and both times I was here I ordered the Sweet & Sour Cod and the Chicken W/ Onion. The sweet & sour cod was average because it was more flour than cod. The chicken w/ onions was kind of yucky because the sauce came in this snooty type of texture, really slimy but the chicken was a little crispy though. 

The service is not that friendly. Probably stressed a college student that works here. They pretty much just expect you to finish your meal and leave so they could clear up the tables for other people. The funny thing about the menu is that the first half of the menu is Chinese food and the second half is pasta, burgers and pizza. Also near the entrance of the store is an ice cream stand. It's like they started with an ice cream shop, changed their mind and wanted to go into Italian food then Chinese Ha-ha. 

The cool thing is they have open mic sometimes. Local talents come here during certain nights and do their thang. Parking isn't too bad sine there is a parking garage right across the street and the restaurant also validates. Street parking is very hard to find, especially around this busy area.

Sun Hong Kong has signs in front offering ice cream @1 a scoop, iced coffed @1,25, and hong kong milk tea @1.25

drink: hong kong milk tea
-first few sips okay. later sips just powdery tasting. 
-no one actually on duty, waiter was pulled to maked drink.

tea drips:
-doubt coffee would be any better.
-ice cream too iffy to even try.

I couldn't believe it when I found out they were opening up Sun Hong Kong again.  I remember the old Sun Hong Kong's pink decor, located on Shattuck, where the floors felt like an ice skating rink, and a diner's sleeves were bound to get yellow from reclining against the tabletops.  But lo, the NEW Sun Hong Kong has opened.  

I was dragged there by a group of my friends, "It'll be different!  It'll be great."  Of course, they had fuzzy warm memories of the old place, somehow forgetting that it was there on Shattuck that one of the guys had found a (what will go unnamed) body part of an (unidentifiable over the world wide web) animal in his house crispy noodles.  

BUT, I must say, I was rather surprised.  The place is clean, the kitchen is observable behind a glass window, and because it's new, the restaurant inspired some degree of confidence that was affirmed and encouraged by the food once it got to the tables.  

It's good.  My friends and I even got a discount and some gelato thrown in.  The backroom is large for big parties, the old Cal mural is still on the walls, and the service is so friendly (b/c, presumably, they're happy you're there) it can feel ingratiating.

A thumbs up here.  And I'm raising my glass to the hope that the old pink Sun Hong Kong of Shattuck from years past stays buried in our collective memory never to rise again.
it's CHEAP and you'll HATE it, but you'll also LOVE it, because it's so CHEAP.

The Yelp description for two stars is "Meh.  I've experienced better."  And I have.  In my own kitchen; with my own haphazard cooking.  This is not Chinese food.  It looks like it and might vaguely smell like it but that's where it ends.

Yes, I'd rather eat my own mystery concoctions because although they look questionable, they at least taste okay.  I'll admit the food here doesn't taste bad.  But it doesn't taste good.  Actually, it doesn't taste like anything.  Maybe it's a season-it-yourself kind of establishment.

I came here with a group and we all agreed that while portions were overly generous and prices were low, the food was not really worth it.  After all, if you're unwilling to eat the leftovers, does that make it good value?  I think not; and as a student, value means everything.

Service was spotty.  We asked for waters and they never came, so after our food came down we eventually managed to successfully wave down a server to ask for them.  Cups are not necessarily clean.

Not much to say about ambiance; typical student hang-out.  Clean.  Didn't check the bathroom.

Might have better luck with happy hour drinks.  But I'm definitely not in a rush to go back.

Lately the service has gotten worse and worse. If you have an hour for lunch, you won't have time to get in and out. Went there today, waited forty minutes for two lunch specials. Isn't the point of the lunch special, that it's ready to roll... that it comes out quickly, and is economical? Well, the price is right, but when you leave with an empty stomach forty minutes after you arrive, and rush back to work to try to get through the next six hours while you're starving, then the savings aren't worth it. Going to sneak out and get Subway to make it through the afternoon.

This is about the fifth time this has happened to me, here... though the other four times it was only HALF AN HOUR to wait and I could inhale my lunch and rush out with indigestion. Today the took bad service to the next level.

Although their Happy Hour prices are a steal, I never find myself eating here. I'm not sure why...

Their $1 watermelon or milk tea drinks are great and cheap on a hot day. My mother especially enjoys their Fish Balls or Pig Skin Curry and I have to agree. I usually order their Happy Hour chicken curry, which is delicious, spicy, and filling for about $4-5. 

I usually do takeout but I've found that they usually mess up my order when I try to order it over the phone. Sometimes I ask for the a la carte curry portion but they'll mistakenly mix it in with my rice and I'd have to wait around while they re-do it. 

Overall, an affordable and delicious Chinese restaurant in the Berkeley area. A much better one than Lotus House, in my opinion.

It was a cold summer day in Berkeley, and I was really craving some Bulgogi--my choice of comfort food. Espresso Experience was closed, however, so I wandered about Berkeley semi broken-hearted. 

I passed Kip's--"Grand Opening" said the banner. The new Gelato and Chinese food place had just opened a few days ago. After carefully studying the huge menu on the glass wall, I went inside. 

A waiter approached me: "Would you like to sit here? Or would you like to sit there?"

I sat down in the big big restaurant and ordered Mu-Shu Chicken. Biggest mistake of my life. I should have known better than to eat Chinese food at Kip's. What resulted was some sick sort of fusion food--the tortillas I received with my Mu-Shu Chicken were ACTUAL tortillas. Cut into fourths to equal 4 tortillas! Weirdest tasting Mu-Shu I've ever had. The tortillas were thick and very floury, and the ones on the bottom were kinda crispy too! First time I ever used a non-circular wrap for my Mu-Shu too, and I did not appreciate it. 

I hope they read this and fix those weird tortillas ASAP. The filling itself was okay...I have had better, let's just say...but at least I got my veggies today. (Wow, I 'm a poet and didn't even know it ) I give it two stars instead of one because the waiter was nice.

There are two reasons why I love Sun Hong Kong:

1. It's pretty cheap, especially for the lunch specials. For the price, the food is actually pretty good and comes in very large portions. A take-out lunch special would cost you under $5 and will leave you for enough food for at least half a dinner. 

2. They're the only restaurant I've ever been to that has cow tongue. That's right, friends, cow tongue. Most of you reading this will probably quiver a bit from disgust, but I really suggest you try it if you get the chance. It's one of the most tender and delicious meats I've tried, and a common tradition in my household. Sun Hong Kong's ox tongue is served in a curry sauce with green bell pepper and potatoes, along with a side of two scoops of rice. I believe this dish is only about $8, which is pretty good for the amount of food you're getting. 

The variety at Sun Hong Kong is pretty vast, and they are always more than happy to host student group dinners in their large dining area. Definitely one of my top choices for a quick bite!

Sure it's pretty cheap Chinese food for some Berkeley CAL students. Dinner meals for $5-6 with a choice of milk tea or soda. I ordered the grilled onion chicken and it was not that great. There was this snotty gluey sauce drowning my chicken. Pretty unappetizing. Don't think I'll come back here again. Try their other choices?? There's a mix of Chinese and American food in their menu. Don't quite appeal to me that this place offers anything that's worth trying for.

I think that Sun Hong Kong might be what heaven is like.  The menu is so tremendously and overwhelmingly comprehensive, that I can only compare it to what it must be like to stand in the presence of the divine.  It is, on its face, a Chinese restaurant, but it is so much more.  They even have Iced Ovaltine on the menu.  Ya, I don't want it.  BUT IT'S THERE, and somehow that comforts me.  

The menu is Chinese, it is American, and it is "American".  I have now eaten there twice and I will describe the dishes my friends and I have ordered on those two separate occasions....

- Mu Shu Vegetables ... tasty Chinese standard.  The veggies tasted slightly of mustard which was nice.
- Braised noodles with ginger ... very good, served with broth
- Spare ribs with 'orange zest' ... disgusting, tasted like donuts, apparently 'orange zest' meant orange flavored corn syrup ... i drowned it out with chili sauce but that only went so far
- Fried Oysters ... good, not everyone's favorite
- Curly Fries ... YES!!!!
- Szechuan Beef with Rice ... I didn't actually taste this but my friend seemed to think it was good
- Baked Ox Tongue with Spaghetti ... Thisssss was good ... not quite a standard American thing, but it was definitely more American than Chinese.  I am a fan of tongue, but it's definitely an odder menu item in the States.
- Oreo gelato and Raspberry gelato ... they gave us free samples and they were both quite tasty

Now, not everything was good, but what was good was REALLY good, and there was just SO MUCH to chose from.  They also have pizza and burgers and whatnot.

I have seen the future, and it is good.

Do NOT try the RANDOM ITEMS they have up posted on paper in the front.

Silly me I'm always sooooo curious about promotional/experimental menu items I just have to jump on it.

Baked Hawaiian Fried Rice - I thought this was pineapple fried rice, but it's a pizza over rice. As in, pineapple, ham, and CHEESE, over rice. Couldn't even finish it.

Half Kip's Fried Chicken with Fries - Waited 15 minutes for this, but it really was half a chicken. Unfortunately, it's too salty. Bahhhhh.

I dont think it's reasonable for people to give Sun HK such bad reviews when they go eat at their happy hour. You just cannot expect regular priced menu items quality food for $3 or even less! 

Anyways, I went to Sun HK for their porridge (take-out). I got a thousand year egg pork porridge and a chicken porridge. I did not go for the happy hour items, so the portions were huge (each porridge could serve around 4 bowls). They were definitely not stingy with the meat either! My chicken porridge was full of tender de-boned chicken. It was delicious!! Reminds me of the jook/congee my mom used to cook me back in Hong Kong!

I have to say after reading alot of fellow Yelpers reviews about this place, I came to the conclusion that they don't know what real good Hong Kong style Chinese food taste like. I'm not too big of a fan of any other Chinese food besides HKS, so I know how good HKS Chinese food taste like when i have it. And I have to say Sun Hong Kong has some great food.

I ordered the House Special Sun Hong Kong Crispy Pan fried chow mien noodles. It came with a combination of meats which included BBQ pork, chicken, beef, squid, shrimp and scallops. As for veggies it came with the normal baby bok choy and straw mushrooms and big black mushrooms. Everything was very tasty, the crispy noodles came out perfect. Very crispy on the outer edges, and very soggy in the middle just how i like it.

Service was on point, once you walk in you get seated and a lady brings out your water instantly. People are very nice here.

4 Stars for Sun Hong Kong Restaurant in Berkeley

This has quickly become my go-to spot for authentic, Cantonese style food in the Berkeley campus area. They have the expansive menu typical of most hong kong style bistros, including rice places, sizzling noodle entrees, noodle soups, sauteed/braised/fried array of seafood and meats, and even comfort foods such as baked plates and macaroni soup. My ultimate tests of a genuine Cantonese food spot is if they have chicken and salty fish fried rice, and how well they do their salt and pepper squid. How did they fare? DELISH!

$5 lunch specials, $6 dinner specials, and "happy hour" food specials. Don't expect a lot of ambience if you're eating in, but service is really fast and takeout is quite efficient.

The only thing that makes me sad is that they use ezdineinn.com for their delivery service, and the one time I got delivery, I was whacked with an $8 delivery fee.  WHACK!

soooooooo cheeeeeeep

On top of the happy hour specials, there are also:
Cal Specials
Anniversary Specials

Both of these special menus have the same number of entrees, same pricing, and same sides:

For $4.95 ($5.45 total after tax before tip), you get an entree
AND
a) rice
b) spaghetti
AND
c) soda
d) milk tea

That's a lot of combinations. You do the math.

We were headed for Thai Noodle 2 but the line was out the door, so we went down a couple blocks to this place.  There was only one group inside, which should have been a tip-off but we went for it anyway.

The food was perfectly acceptable; A-OK, as yelp likes to quantify the 3-star review.  I had the flat rice noodles which I found to be on the greasy side, however can't be too hard on them for that because I usually think that with most thai noodles.

The service was terrible.  The waiter didn't even take our order for a good 15 minutes.  We paid in cash and the tab sat on the edge of the table for at least 10 minutes while the servers walked back and forth; finally I had to get up and hand it to someone at the counter so we could get our change and leave.

Typically not very crowded at all, so this is my go-to Thai place. Everything's affordable and the service is quick.

Tried a lot of things here but here are the entrees that I recommend:
-Papaya salad: Order it Laos style, and spicy. I've ordered this extra spicy before and I literally almost cried. But it was so good, it was worth it hahaha!
-Pad Seew
-Pad Thai

^Can't go wrong with either. :)

From the outside, Racha Cafe seems like a hole in the wall kindda restaurant, but don't let that fool you.  The food here is really good.  I especially liked their Thai BBQ chicken w/ fried rice, and it's a really good value at $6.95.  The chicken is on the sweet side (it also comes with Thai sweet and hot sauce if you want it even sweeter), but I think that's why I like it.

The restaurnt is fairly large and well lit.  For larger groups, there is a large banquet type room in the back (which helps to reduce noises from the large crowds).

Overall, this is a great restaurant if you are looking for value and good food.

There's just something about the flavors in their dishes that I can't get over.  I've been to many Thai restaurants and theirs just tastes funny compared to others.  The first time I went, I ordered the pad thai.  It was too thick and too sugary & sour for my liking.  I also had the sweet rice and mango dessert, which wasn't very good.  For that, I'd go to Thai Temple on Sunday and get it to go.  Service is good - they let us pay separately instead of getting a single big check.  Also, there's a large room in the back suitable for large parties (~20-40).

racha = love.

in a sea of subpar asian cuisine, racha definitely rises above the rest (*cough* asian ghetto). it's inexpensive, the servings are always generous, the service is attentive and the food is fairly authentic. it definitely qualifies as a hole in the wall, but the food is good. 

i am ADDICTED to the fresh spring rolls. it's the one dish i consistently order. when first looking at reviews, i remember one yelper commenting about the "orgasmic" quality of the sauce. while the rolls themselves are pretty standard, she was right. the sauce is pretty damn magical. it's a bit on the sweet side, but far better than the standard plum sauce and sweet and source sauce that typically accompany spring rolls. 

the pad ka prow is great (pork sauteed with basil and peppers), as well as the pad thai. the papaya salad is also a nice treat that comes with a generous serving of dried shrimp. yumm.

the nice thing about racha is that they're open for lunch/dinner and offer take out as an option. no matter what, the service is always super fast!

Racha Cafe, you have taken over Thai Basil as my favorite place for Tom Kha! If you've read my other reviews for Thai restaurants, I always try to get the Tom Kha whenever I try a new place. It is what I standardize my experience by. If you don't screw it up, I am for sure coming back. Well, Racha, I will be back for more.

Their Tom Kha is surprisingly just that, Tom Kha [Gai?]. This basically means no chicken, which was very surprising. I'm sure you can ask for chicken, but I was too tired to. The soup posses the perfect combination of sweet and sour, and I could see the three proper ingredients (kafer lime, galanga, lemongrass) floating in the soup.

Only downside is that for $8, the bowl was way too small. I was still hungry for more in an hour or so, but by then it was too late. They might want to think about serving bigger portions for that price. Also the chicken thing kind of bothered me, but the fact that they executed the flavor of the soup itself flawlessly just might make up for it. 

Oh yea, I tried a bit of the Pad See Ew as well, which was awesome! At the end, we ordered fried bananas with lychee ice cream. The bananas themselves were pretty good; nothing too special. I've never had lychee ice cream before, and this was a good first time. Very flavorful! I wonder where they got it from...

We stopped in here while we were waiting for our clothes to dry at Bing Wong.

It was pretty darn good, I'd say perhaps better than Thai House down on Channing.

We got the crispy beef... which is was actually kinda weird. It was just beef deep fried by itself until it was turning to dust. The taste was reminiscent of Mexican tripas.

We also got a noodle dish. I can't remember it's name, but it wasn't Pad Thai or Pad See Ew. It was very good though.

Definitely going here again, but mainly out of convenience (location to laundry).

I've come here on several occasions.

Occasion #1
Came here after a football game [GO BEARS!], it was actually my first time coming here even though my roommate talks about coming here all the time.  The restaurant was suppose to close, but since there was so many customers coming in they decided to stay open for business. I ordered their Green Curry Special which had fish cakes, basil, eggplant + other misc. spices that I cant recall.  The fish cakes were delicious and fresh and the eggplant was miniature versions (very different from the regular ones I eat).  The green curry itself was so rich in flavor, hard to believe that they served it a la carte!  Service was slower than other days I've been here, but it was understandable since so many other people were there.

Unfortunately, there were these irrational people who were impatient and did not pay for their BEER.  It was like the scene of the restaurant.  They thought it was unreasonable that they waited so long for their food.

Occasion #2 + #3
One of my friends came up from San Diego (originally from SF) and we decided to go eat here.  I ordered something similar to Pad See Ew but with the silver noodles (FUN SEE/Chap Jae).  It was mediocre, but my other friend is a regular here and he got #62, Thai Fried Rice with Thai Roasted Chicken.  Seriously was the most DELICIOUSLY cooked chicken ever.  So the next time I came, I ordered it :D literally like drooling good!  Definitely worth trying!

why am i embarrassed to write this review? maybe because i would be admitting to eating food that is not exactly healthy. let me get over my pride for a moment. a friend caught me in a moment of weakness after the gym and asked if i would join her for thai. why yes, my post-workout-flat stomach needs a little puffing out. i've never noticed this place before even though i shop at buffalo across the street all the time. service was VERY friendly and quick. menu was extensive insofar as vegetarian options. i ordered #79 (tofu and vegetables in peanut sauce over rice, i can't remember the name, my eyes were looking at the food). it was very good. whatever my dining partner had was very good too.
so why only 3 stars? because i felt too guilty afterwards about how much food i ate (servings are large!). so really, 5 stars for the restaurant, and 3 stars for my lack of willpower.
i'll drink their peanut sauce, i'll drink it up.

Been there 3 times.

To die for.

Owners are nice, and service is good.

Everything is good.  Food comes out as it is prepared, so everything right out of the kitchen.

Not a lot of staff, so food can take a while if you have a large party.

Excellent value.
This place is hand's down the best in Berkeley. Good quality and delicious food. Portions are little small but hey quality over quantity right? EVERYTHING is good here!!!

Ehhh. I was really excited at first because one of my friends who has lived in Thailand before really likes this place and says it's authentic. My food WAS pretty good when I got it, and (possibly) even worth it's high price. But I took some home for leftovers, and the next day it was tasteless and a congealed mess. Maybe I should only judge the restaurant by it's food when it's fresh and just-served, but I just don't understand how food can go so bland and gross so quickly.

I gave this place 4 stars because it can be expensive for a college student's budget, but this is one of my favorite Thai places to go to! I like the decor of the place and it's very spacious!

Their pad see ew and curry dishes are all amazing. Even the red curry isn't too spicy. The flavor here is really good quality and the service is very quick; all of the plates are ready for you when you walk in and the waittresses are easy to flag down. I highly recommend this place for Thai food!

Yummy! 
Racha is a hole in the wall eatery and is usually busy with students in the area. I usually get take out because it is not the cleanest looking place, but the food is great!
I always get their Prad Prik Sod over fried rice and it is delicious. It is spicy and very flavorful, so if your into spicy...this is the dish!!!! The veggie egg rolls are also really good. The only reason I give it 4 out of 5 is because it is a little greasy. They also change the veggies included sometimes. I will sometimes get mushrooms instead of carrots and vice versa, they may have been low...who knows.

Great food and great service!!! I definitely recommend this restaurant!! I really like their Pad Thai! The inside of the restaurant is really really clean!! Im going back again! Its just a fantastic customer service!!! thats all I can say!!
boo, the  food here  has gone downhill:(

My first visit here was over the winter holidays; business seemed very slow since most students were gone on break.
I had a green curry dish that had eggplant listed as a main ingredient on the menu, one of the reasons I ordered it.
 I was disappointed with this dish for a few reasons, the first being that it contained a few thinly sliced pieces of eggplant-there was more broccoli in the dish than eggplant, and broccoli wasn't even listed in the dish on the menu.
Second, all of the vegetables were quite over-cooked and had a somewhat strange reheated or microwaved aftertaste.
Third, the curry sauce was thin, tasted watered down and was not at all spicy.
Resolving to give Racha another try since everyone has their off days, I went again this week and specifically asked what the spiciest curry dishes were-the waitress said the red curries, so I ordered a red vegetable curry dish, asked to have eggplant added to the dish & that I would pay extra for that.
Second time around, again another watery, poorly spiced curry sauce, 
3 thin, small, shriveled slices of eggplant in the dish and generally overcooked veggies with an unpleasant aftertaste resembling soup reheated from the day before.
I won't be eating here again soon.

Racha really blew my expectations away. The place seemed so small and the location was not exactly the most convenient either. I was a part of a committee dinner and had the largest party at the small restaurant. The servers were very quick in moving tables together for us, which was really good especially in the freezing cold weather this week has been yielding. Waiting was only a few minutes and not a problem. 

My only complaints are that it took a while to order and for the food to come to the table. The food was delicious!! (yes, with 2 exclamations) I had to try the pad kee mao since that is my signature Thai dish to try at every place. The food was literally fresh out of the kitchen and I mean HOT. It burned my mouth and my friends' mouths. I noticed only 2 waiters but they were able to run the place well. They placed 2-3 pitchers of water on the table for our convenience and that was excellent. One other plus was that they let us pay separately since it's always a horror when it comes time for the check. Definitely recommend over Berkeley Thai House and Thai Noodle.

There's so many Thai restaurants on north and west side of Berkeley but I heard a lot of people rave about this south side Thai place so I wanted to give it a try. However, I wasn't too satisfied with the food here.

I tried my usual Basil Fried Rice and Chicken Pad Kee Maw. The Basil Fried Rice lacked flavor & spice and was overall very disappointing, while the Pad Kee Maw was actually quite delicious as far as Thai noodles get. 

The ambiance was definitely not somewhere you would take someone on a first date, but the pricing and portions were quite generous. All in all, among the thousand other Thai restaurants in Berkeley, this place doesn't really stand out. Another easily avoidable Thai restaurant.

Racha's got your run-of-the-mill ginormous Thai menu. What sets 'em apart is the fast service and their willingness to appease me. They're always happy to change the order to how I like it, and they're one of few Thai restaurants that knows what a "jungle curry" is -- a red curry without the coconut milk, and super spicy.

The service is pretty fast and the portions are reasonably sized. You'll always leave Racha cafe feeling like you're in a good place -- and definitely not sick, like some other restaurants may make you.

OMG. I'm an official Thai food liker... My co-worker suggested this spot today for lunch. Three of us went over to Racha to order ala carte dishes.  They were ALL great. I don't even like curry, but the green curry with chicken is especially tasty. We will be eating here more often. It just sucks because we work on the Northside, and this spot is the Southside.

*Tip*
They deliver with a minimum purchase of $25

Thai Basil is for suckers.  Racha's Pad Kee Moa is the most interesting thing that will happen to your tongue since you lost your makeout virginity.  It will be difficult to quantify the novel qualia the tasty part of your brain will be newly privy to after a visit to this gem-uv-a-restaurant.  I'm considering writing a paper on how, in an indifferent universe devoid of transcendental meaning in which hedonism provides the only avenue to proximate meaning, green curry has replaced god as a motive for continued, yummy existence.

We enjoy Racha Cafe on our visits to Berkeley.  Friendly staff, good food with healthy portions, and good prices.  We especially enjoy their curry dishes.  A good sign is that it is usually filled with Asian students.  Also they seem enjoy a brisk takeout service.  

The last time we were there, seated next to us was a disheveled man off the streets, who was waiting for some takeout while swearing constantly in a loud voice.  Clearly a man with serious mental problems.  The staff was very kind in packing his food for him and not charging him, which probably would have caused an unpleasant scene.  We were happy that he quickly took the food and left the restaurant.
I don't even remember what I ordered. All I remember is my strong dislike for whatever I had. I really don't understand what's the rave about this place.

I have to say, this is definitely one of the BEST Thai Restaurant that I've been to. 

The first time I came here, the restaurant was pretty empty and I didn't expect much from here. However, after trying their food, I knew I would definitely come back here again! 

I can say that almost everything here is delicious! I tried the boat noodle soup and they gave a good portion and the noodles were very tasty. The second time I came here, I ordered the Pad See-Ew. Even though I wasn't that hungry, I finished the entire thing with great satisfaction. Also, I tried some of their BBQ chicken. It was very tender and tasty. I think I will get that next time. 

Here's what I've got to say about this place: 
- Big portion of food
- Great food
- Delicious food that will not disappoint you

This place is great! Definitely the best Thai food I've had that's within a few blocks of campus. 

My personal favorite is the Pad See Ew (extra spicy!). It's not dry at all and you can really taste all the flavors. Other plates that I really recommend are Red Curry Pumpkin, Pineapple Fried Rice, and BBQ Chicken over Fried Rice. Also, got the Silver Noodle Soup last time I came here: delicious! Very good for a cold Berkeley evening.

If you want awesome Thai food for a reasonable price, Racha Cafe is the place to go.

I drove down from Sonoma County to Berkeley Hats which is down the street from Racha. Since my bladder ain't what it used to be I need to find a restroom fast! I stopped in Racha ordered some tea so I could use the bathroom then decided to stay since it was dinner time.

We ordered the pad thai, the crispy pork and shrimp rolls. All of it was outstanding and the price was right! Plus their jasmine tea was also very good. So next time you're in berkeley and have a hankerin' for Thai, I say stop by and give 'em a try.

2 stars for the food and 4 stars for the ambience and service.  If you're a Cal student who lives within walking distance of Telegraph, Racha is a better option than Thai Noodle II, Thai House, or Thai Basil.

The last time I ate here, the tom yum was flavorful.  The green curry was flat (i.e. the oils from the curry paste were absent from the top layer).  And the Pad Thai was a little dry.
I've been here several times since my first review, and I've changed my mind.  It's good for an occasional lunch, but somehow always empty.

Racha's Cafe is deceptively good. Upon first glance, it looks like an unattractive Thai restaurant tucked away in the crevices of Berkeley, but upon eating the food, you start to wonder why more people do not come here.

I've tried some of their rice dishes, their Pad See Ew, and their soups...and I have to say - you must come here to eat great Thai food! The pricing is affordable, and for the food you are given, it is definitely worth it!

Thus, with all the elements combined, I can gladly say that Racha's is a place where one could go, without going broke, to enjoy well cooked Thai food with friends and family in a nicely, well-kept restaurant!

You can't go home again.

My friend and I were on our way to bongo burger but walked passed Racha and decided to eat there for nostaligia. We were undergrads in the 80's back in the days when students were proud of the radical politics of berkeley, back you know, when students protested against abominations committed by our government and well back  when Racha was really good.

It was edible and that fact that I was hungry was the extra seasoning the dish needed. It was pretty blah, which is not what I seek in Thai Food. I  had chicken basil noodles, often a spicy dish which it was not. My friend ordered his dish extra spicy and it was as bland as mine.

Oh well at least bongo burger hasn't changed.

Even after Thai Noodle ii went down in the fire, there were still quite a few Thai restaurants in Berkeley. This place deserves more credit for having a good mix between a nice atmosphere and delicious food with great portions. 

I got the Pineapple Fried Rice and was not disappointed. But really, it's hard to screw up fried rice. There was a good amount of food for one person and the ingredients were fresh!

A friend told me that you CAN in fact switch Thai Basil's pad see ew meat option for no extra cost. Just thought I would correct myself. 

Now I'm craving some Thai. :P

We were hungry and looking for something good and cheap. After searching on Yelp it was decided that Thai would be the cuisine we dine on. I have to say this place live up to the reviews it got. The food was delicious and reasonably priced. It was a bit hot as there didn't seem to be AC there but the food was worth it. Will definitely visit again or good cheap eats.

so far the only thai restaurant i've been to in Berkeley, but i just LOVE LOVE their veggie pad thai!!! omg and so worth it because the portion is huge which i can like eat over a span of 2 days if i saved it after haha.  ohh and for dessert, i used to order the fried banana with ice cream..but in my most recent visit i ordered it and it wasn't the same! :( sadly.  the banana tasted super strange.  but my fav dish from here is definitely the veggie pad thai.  pad thai is a must if you come here :)

chicken on fire

and 

peanut sauce curry (forgot what it's called)
REALLY GOOD!
good service

Definitely my favorite thai place in Berkeley. Delicious, flavorful, fresh food at a great price.

BEST PAD THAI EVERRR!!! It's not ketchupy like Thai Basil. I get it with chicken and it always lasts me 2 meals. I've probably ordered it a couple dozen times since being a student at Cal. I've also had the Pad Kee Mao (my 2nd favorite), Pad See Ew, Pineapple Fried Rice, Yellow Curry, Eggplant Chicken, and Chicken Satay,- all pretty good. I don't think I've ever ordered something from here that I didn't like. 

Huge noodle/fried rice portions, but smaller portions with stuff like curry. 

I always get such great service here; friendly, attentive waiters, our waters are kept full, and the food comes out relatively quickly. 

There's a room in the back if you have a really large group! 18% gratuity included on parties of 6 or more though :(

I came here with 2 others expecting to order Flaming Chicken, but unfortuntely I didn't see Flaming Chicken on the menu.  =(
So, we ordered the pineapple fried rice (which was pretty good), the pad see ew (which was delicious but sadly the amount they gave us was skimpy), and the black pepper chicken with garlic sauce a la carte (I don't think I'll ever order that again-- it was just chicken strips in sauce, wasn't very filling).
Inside, it's a pretty attractive restaurant in terms of appearance, but you could miss it while walking outside. The place is bigger than it appears from outside.
The service was alright-- there was only one waitress for the whole restaurant, and she was a bit... quiet so it was difficult to hear her at times. I ordered fried ice cream at the end of our meal, and we waited at least 5 minutes just for the waitress to come back and tell us they were out of fried ice cream. =(
I give the place 3 stars-- I rarely give restaurants 5, and 1 star off for not having fried ice cream and for making us wait 5 minutes before telling us they were out and for giving us a skimpy amount of pad see ew. Other than that, I really recommend the pad see ew.

this place was 2 blocks from my friend's house, filled with 6 boys, who are lazy and wont walk anywhere, but came here at least 3 days a week, partly b/c of the location, and partly b/c the food is so good
the ppl are nice and the service is good, only had one bad experience when my friend's order was forgotten about. 
the food is delicious and almost everything can be made vegetarian
my favorites: tom yum noodle soup, pad kea moa, pad kao kew wan (i dont think im spelling these right...) it is the green curry fried rice
my friends like the red curry, bbq chicken, bbq pork, pinapple fried rice, eggplant stuff
the pad thai isnt amazing though, so if you want noodles then id def recommend the pad kea moa
if you come for lunch they have lunch specials and if you order an entree it comes with a little cup of soup

I used to come here a lot, but  have stopped in recent years after one experience where they raised their prices and their portions got smaller.  Decided to try it again since it's been a while, and I don't know if I have a revisionist memory, but the portions looked decent again.  Prices aren't too bad given the economy and the rising prices all over the place, and the food was decent.  Wouldn't mind coming back here again...

I'm pretty shocked by the praise this restaurant has gotten below actually.  I have Thai food all the time, all over the country as well as in Thailand, and this is the first time I thoroughly did not enjoy a thai meal.  The chicken pad thai tasted terrible - it was sour and barely edible.  The pad sew ew and kra pow were acceptable.  Maybe I had really bad luck with the pad thai, but it tasted little better than Annie Chung's Instant Pad Thai mix.  Portions are decent and service is mediocre.  All in all a negative experience.  I think Thai Noodle on Shattuck is a much better choice.

My top craving when in Berkeley (close to Mario's) is this place!

YUMMMOOO

I have had a really difficult time finding a Thai place I like, until I found Racha... Oh sweet Jesus...I would make a special trip to Berkeley just for this food (alright, and see my friends too!).

Now I will say I think ownership has changed as those who have been going awhile say it used to be better, more consistent, but personally I have zero complaints.

I tend to get the spicy eggplant with tofu (although its really not spicy at all, so if you want it spicy, request extra spicy) and the vegetarian spring rolls--these are top picks among my friends that frequent there.

Great food for a fabulous price...if only I still lived in town!

Racha Cafe was one of my friend's fave places to catch up at for lunch. The restaurant is quiet, nicely decorated, and the staff are super nice. I typically used to get the yellow chicken curry, and my fave part was the little carrot flower they put on the serving of rice that comes with it. Their Thai Iced Teas were awesome too. Their prices are pretty reasonable too (about $10 pp or less)
I can't think of anything more to say about Thai restaurants, except that I love the food.   Wait, I thought of something else ....  aside from the food, the people who work there are SO NICE.
Ive had green curry, pad kee mow? (the spicier version of pad see ew), and fried rice. They were all pretty good! Not sure if it's my favorite thai place at berkeley but it's up there.

mm! try the red curry pumpkin with chicken (but not spicy)... although i couldnt find any pumpkin... and i was really looking forward to it! it doesnt look like a lot but will fill you up. attentive server. clean place. occasional singing from the hostess stand. $10 credit card minimum.

Racha is my favorite Thai restaurant in Berkeley.  I don't think they can be beat in terms of taste and price!

I can't help but get the PAD THAI every time.  It's so flavorful and large enough for two people to split (or one very hungry person).  Such a deal!  Lately, I've been branching out with my menu choices.  Tried the BBQ chicken.  It's very sweet and fall off the bone tender.  I love the side of fried rice too!

They have some very innovative house special items for about $10+/dish.  I was eying the duck with pineapple and lychee (i believe).  Just thinking about it makes me drool.

I'll be back, Racha.  I'll be back.

Came here for a wushu banquet.
we had a tray of whatever vegetarian dish i wanted ordered for our party since I was the only one with dietary restrictions. 
The green curry was okay. I wish it had more of a kick though..
Rice was pretty good- not broken at all.

YUM! I have been eating at several Berkeley thai restaurants since I moved to the East Bay and finally Racha Cafe has satisfied. Delicious red curries and panang. And their tom yum, while very spicy, is absolutely wonderful. It was just so yummy. Don't be fooled by the location/interior/exterior. This is legitimate thai with excellent spices. Just so yummy.

Definitely one of my top 3 favorite places to get thai food in Berkeley (and I've tried a bunch of places)! You can't go wrong with any of their noodle dishes if you are a noodle lover, and they give pretty big portions! I also really like their soups. I can't say much about their curries because I've only gotten curry once (I usually always get noodle dishes when I go to thai places) but their green curry is good. 

I've only come here for dinner but I heard they have lunch specials? In any case, dishes are definitely worth it for the price.

I love the food at Racha Cafe.  It tastes like what I believe to be authentic Thai cuisine, as it says on the sign outside.  The area is a little sketchy, being on Telegraph Ave and what not.  The only down side is that the service is really slow and they often mess up the order.

This place is underrated in my opinion. 

Yes, there are shady people lurking inside every once in a while (one time I experienced a shouting homeless lady with no pants..) but they won't do anything but give you a good story to tell later on. 

The menu at this place is HUGE and the food is cheap. Way better and more affordable than most places on Telegraph. Their rad na and yellow curry are excellent.
Prices are reasonable and the pad thai blows my mind. Yellow curry, tom yum soup, and a few other dishes are worth repeat visits.

I've been to this spot several times...and usually, I'm very happy with the food and the service. Thai food is kind of new to me, I usually stick to the safe dishes, which are Pad Thai , Pad Kee Mao and the Pinapple Fried Rice and Cashew Rice because I know what it is and I know I like it. I just can't get the damn noodles straight! I like the wide noodles, which I think, are the egg noodles. See, I'm still not sure. The Racha is usually great for any of those dishes...the noodles are delish, it's always spicy but no so much where I can't enjoy my food, the service is usually fast and friendly and not overbearing.  And even though I have a "but" coming... I'd still go there because I like their food most of the time. 

My sister and I went there yesterday, it was Sunday and the whole time we ate, we were the only ones there but this place is usually crowded, so that doesn't mean anything. I only mention it because if I would've been a first timer, I probably would've walked right out. Hello, empty restaurant, not a good sign, right? Anyway, I ordered the chicken satay because I recently discovered how freakin' delicious it is, and I wanted my sister to try it too. It's basically a thin slab of grilled, seasoned chicken breast served with an itty bitty cucumber salad and peanut sauce for dipping.  Racha did that very good 

After that our entrees arrived, my sis got the chicken pad kee mao and I got chicken pad thai... and this is where it started. Remember the whole noodle thing? Well, I didn't say I wanted the wide noodles, so I get these orange-y thin noodles (rice noodles?).  I figured, okay, my fault... so I try it, ew. It was salty and fried egg-y tasting, I so did not like it. That plus the orange, anorexic noodles, I decided, I was not going to eat that. So, I ask the waitress if I could get pad kee mao instead and she says, "but it all ready". No shit? I didn't realize. Is that why there's a plate in front of me? I said, ok... and kind of crossed my arms in my best impersonation of a tantrum, I'm not good at those. So I figure, my bad for not knowing how to ask for my damn noodles, it's not her fault and the effort was already put into making that plate. I get her attention and ask her to pack that hot eggy tasting mess to go (I did not say that, I do have some home training, hehe) and ordered me some pad kee mao as well, which was as always, delicious. 

So children, the lesson learned today, don't be afraid to ask questions about your food BEFORE you order it. You may all go out and play now. Thank you.

Food: ok
price: ok
service: ok
decor: nice

Nothing too special about this place. It's just your typical thai place in berkeley. Worth a try if you have some extra cash and don't mind eating mediocre food.

Yummy but  greasy.

As I ate my chicken with green beans sauteed in chili paste, a ring of oil out lined my lips. I really hate it when food does that. But this time, it was ok because the chicken was well done. Not too hard to chew or slightly under done. The curry was tangy but a certain flavor over powered it. I tried some of their silver noodle dish and again, another oily ring to the mouth. Yet again, I forgive it because it was that good.

The waitress was very courteous and did not stray to over or came over frequently.

As for prices, well one of the cheapest and tastiest Thai places. Will I come here again? Perhaps. To try out their fried rice dishes.

We ducked in here on a hot day because a big electric fan was blasting away in the seating area.  When we explained we're vegetarian, the staff was cooperative about substituting tofu for  meat in the Larb.  And the Larb was pretty good.  However, my husband's Tofu Salad was prepared with fish sauce, though the menu didn't mention this.  Most servers in Berkeley are on-the-ball about vegetarian/vegan issues and will warn us if we're ordering something off-limits, so the fish sauce was a shock and a disappointment.   When we sent it back, the server returned a little later with a vegan version that was just fine.  Fresh rolls were enjoyable but the little dish of sauce that accompanied them was a bit stingy.  More sauce, please!  My husband ordered a Thai Singha beer, which never arrived.   But the server was generous with the water pitcher.  So, overall, a mixed experience.

I used to live a block away from this place, and it was my go-to Thai restaurant.  Fair prices and everything I've tried has been solid, although sometimes quite oily (pad see ew).  

The service here has always been good for me.  Once, they even accommodated a group of ~20 (they have a room in back), and did a great job with only two waitstaff.

Racha is definitely my favorite place for Thai food! The ambience is deceptively dinky, but the quality and quantity of their dishes more than compensate for it. The service is really good too, you don't have to wait long for the food, which is a plus.

My favorite dish is the green curry fried rice with chicken, and I always ask for it to be extra spicy; it never disappoints. I'm a big fan of their spicy red chilli sauce, which is one of their condiments.. makes everything taste super good! Their Pad Thai is really good, and I like their yellow pumpkin curry with rice too. My only complaint is that their Thai iced tea tends to be too sweet so I never get it here.

If it seems kind of dumpy on the outside, you are not wrong.

The primary draw is that they are the only Thai restaurant on South Side that accepts credit cards. The food is below average, but cheap, quick, and good enough for a quick lunch or dinner. It is usually not crowded at all, which is great if you are looking for a place to come with a large group.

The service is quite gruff. I had to wave my hand many times before someone would come over to take our order or the check. Once when I was there they refused to move tables around to allow a lady in a wheelchair to maneuver to the table with her family, which is pretty unacceptable, as the tables are neither heavy nor bolted down.

Very poor experience. Would not recommend.

- The waitress was very unprofessional, wearing iPod earbuds the entire time. This is my main reason for giving 1 star. Not only this, but she butchered one order in my party and didn't act professionally when she was told they made the wrong dish. 
- The food is fairly expensive compared to other Thai restaurants. $7.95 for al la carte dishes (meaning you get no rice, but a tiny bit more of what you're ordering) considering the size of the dish.
- The restaurant's atmosphere is pretty bad: it's completely empty, and there's only two people working in the restaurant so service is slow
- In a party of 6 or more, get ready to get GOUGED by tax + tip.

Red Pumpkin Curry with Beef: you get three small penny size cuts of beef. A bit too oily too. They do not cook this fresh. You can tell because the pumpkin pulp breaks down into the curry if it sits around too long and this was definitely the case.
Pad Thai: Too soggy, not flavorful enough, and bean sprouts cooked in weren't cooked thoroughly
Pad See Ew: Too soggy and not flavorful enough
Fried Chicken over Fried Rice: Breading was soggy and flavorless. Rice was bland.
on the cheap, good thai, fast and easy to get in and out of there.  Great food.
I've had every thai place within 10 blocks of campus and this is the best by far.  I get the massaman curry usually.

I got the beef with broccoli on rice for dinner here once. It was just bad. Tiny portions. About 4 thin slices of beef in my whole dish. Drowned in oil. Bland flavor. There was nothing Thai about this dish.

My friend got the pad see ew, mostly noodles, too little meat from what I saw. 

All and all, I wouldn't come here again.

Being new to Thai food, I had only been to places like Thai Basil and Berkeley Thai House. When my friend brought me to Racha Cafe, I instantly became addicted to Thai food! Racha's chicken pad see ew is delicious! Many of my friends also really enjoyed their pad thai, pineapple fried rice, green curry, and other dishes. Overall, I haven't been to Racha with anyone who hasn't enjoyed their dish.

One thing, however, that wasn't so great was the service. Usually the service is fine and the people are generally friendly. However, when I went to Racha during graduation season in May, the waitress kept forgetting about our table. It wasn't so bad that I wouldn't come back though-- the pad see ew definitely makes it worth it. :)

Out of all the Thai places that I've tried at Berkeley, Racha is definitely my favorite! The flavors are way better than Thai Basal or Thai House. My favorite dish is probably the Pineapple Fried Rice.  The Pad Thai is my second favorite. The noodles aren't too wet or too dry, just perfect. The portions here are pretty good if you're planning to eat a dish by yourself. My friends and I decided to share 2 dishes last time and we devoured it within 5 minutes and had to order now. Lesson learned. 

Definitely get the Thai Tea while you're at it. You can tell that it's way better than thai tea at typical milk tea places around Berkeley! I will definitely try the desserts here next time (:

Solid Thai food that consistently tastes good and authentic. Great place to get take out.  Not very expensive and decent portions.  Also seems like a good place to meet a group of people.  Not fancy but cute enough on the inside. Like the name suggests, cafe ambiance.
Great Thai food, pretty reasonable prices for a pretty filling meal. I frequent this place; almost everything on the menu is pretty good. Pad see ew and pad kee mao are exceptional.

I don't understand the positive reviews for this place. If you like the careful balance and subtlety of good Thai cooking, you'll find this very heavy-handed. The service was marginal, even with just a few customers.  There are some very good Thai choices in Berkeley, but this isn't one of them.  I won't go back.

Me and a friend of mine had a late lunch at here this week. The service was especially fast because it was past rush hour and the server was nice. I'm a fan of thai food but my problem with a lot of thai places is that the beef is a extremely chewy and unpleasant. The texture of the meat in my dish was pretty great and my noodles and vegtables were delicious. Overall I was pleased with my dish and service.

Love this place! I place phone orders and pick up the food about once a week and eat in the restaurant every once in a while. My favorite Dishes are the Panang Curry (Chicken) and Pad Thai (w/e meat you like). I've just about tried everything on the menu. Their soups and appetizers are very well prepared as well. They can make the food pretty spicy if you so wish. Also love their Thai Iced Tea.

I have been coming here for about a year and a half.  I was so pleased to find a place that will make wonton soup without my allergens!  I really appreciate the staff's willingness to substitute so much and still make a great meal. 

The service is usually great, but I have been a few times when there was a completely different set of staff, the menu said "UC noodle cafe" in rainbow font, and when I ordered my regular substitution-riddled wonton soup, it appeared to be a totally different interpretation of wonton soup as it had been so many times before.   I stopped going so regularly after that, and I swear that the whole decor changed from one visit to the next!  I went a few weeks ago and got the bad cook, and then I went this past weekend and had a great meal!   

The moral of this review is that Racha's inconsistency is redeemed by it's (most of the time) deliciousness and its downhill proximity to my house.  Please let me know if you figure out the pattern/riddle of when is the best time to go!

I have never dined in here but done a couple of take outs and on the overall I am very happy with the food. Although this is not the best thai food I've tasted in the world it pretty much does the job and the best Thai food I've tasted in the United States.

Added:
So I ordered the papaya salad second time and I actually realized what was wrong in it. Although they say that it is authentic food , the papaya salad had only lime juice and not the fish sauce like it is actually supposed to. took out a star for not having the fish sauce since it is supposed to be authentic!

Racha among the many, many Thai restaurants in Berkeley stands out as my go-to Thai place. I've had the pad see ew, red pumpkin curry, and the red curry noodles. Most recently we came on a Friday night and the restaurant was super packed, but I was impressed that the service was still decent and did not slow down very much. Everything is pretty greasy, but that goes for all Thai restaurants around here. I don't know if it's the cuisine itself? From my observations, the pad thai is a bigger serving than the other noodles dishes, though all of them are more than filling. I like the curry dishes a lot, just because you can buffer some of the oil with plain rice. The curry noodles were pretty tasty because there are crispy noodles on top of the egg noodles in the soup. I'm sure I will come to Racha many more times in my college years.

Came here with a friend. I ordered the pad see-ew, she had the crab fried rice. I was surprised to see parts of crab in the dish! Claw and everything. Don't really see real seafood around this part of the town...anyway, my noodle dish wasn't too bad. It was definitely full of flavor. It had carrots though, something I'm not used to seeing in the dish. 

One thing about this place is quantity. Quality is just a meh...but I mean, if you're in the mood for Thai and all the other places are crowded/not your style, Racha has a nice dining room and isn't always swarming with people.

This place serves up some of the best Thai food I've had yet in the bay area (my other favorite being Ploy II on Haight in SF). Racha Cafe features a delicious and innovative menu, and makes me just a bit less sad about living 400 miles away from Hollywood's Thai Town.

The eggplant salad with minced chicken and shrimp is smokey and perfectly spiced. BBQ chicken (which the bf always gets) is just the right balance of salty and sweet, moisture and char. And my favorite - the steamed catfish with lemon sauce, is seriously cream-worthy. It's off the house special menu and perfect with a side of brown jasmine rice.

Service is decent, if not a bit absent-minded at times. This place might be a bit better for take-out.

Racha is a near favorite for me. I really like the Pad Kee Mao and Pad Thai here. The portions are also pretty big! However, I got a huge portion this one day I went.. and the next time I went, I didn't get as much. So I guess it depends on the cook. Anyway, the service is okay, that one waitress isn't super nice or anything. There's this one waiter that is really nice though, I don't see him all that often though. If you get to-go, be sure to call in 10-15 minutes before you pick up, otherwise you'd just be waiting around.
Extensive menu with decent flavor. Nice last minute choice if you are looking for some quick thai to put in your belly.

One of the better Thai food places in berkeley, and not too expensive to boot! Kind of far down telegraph but it's not too shady and the food is worth it. I don't go there regularly because it's still more expensive than Asian ghetto, but when looking for a sit down place this is one of the top choices.

Did you ever hear of mouth happiness? I first came here in the late 1980s. The quality, reasonable price, and deliciousness have not changed one bit, and they are gracious, wonderful servers. The red pumpkin curry, green beans with tofu, and green vegetable curry were equally tasty, with the plethura of sauce and savory-ness of the first and the dry paste-like texture and sweetness of the second, the third with sauce also, but with more of a lemon grass flavor. The rice was smooth, perfect. There are plenty of Thai places in the East Bay and San Francisco, and some compare with this, but Racha beats them with the prices! Wow.
Their shrimp fresh rolls (spring rolls) are sooooooo good. I get them all the time as an entre to go. Best in the east bay.

I've been eating at Racha for more than 5 years. The food used to be great but the new owners have changed the place so much that I haven't been back in almost a year. When I was a student I went there 2-3 a week because of the delicious food and cheap prices. Not anymore. All of my alum friends are sad that Racha is no longer good. I'd recommend Plearn on Shattuck instead.

Quaint Thai restaurant on telegraph in Berkeley. We went for lunch on a Friday and there were three other tables of people. We got seated quickly and the food came out pretty fast too.  
 We shared the chicken pad Thai and the red curry pumpkin with beef and a Thai iced tea. YUM! Pad Thai came out first then the curry. Pad  Thai had good quality meat, definitely not mystery meat like some Thai places we've been. Not too sweet or loaded with sauce. The curry had the perfect blend of curry, pumpkin and sweetness. Nice bug hunks of beef and pumpkin. Thai iced tea pretty darn good too. Total bill was $17 something. If your in a hurry you can be in and out within 30 mins ( just enough time for the metered parking right out front)

I tried this place one time, so it is based of my one experience there... I originally had planned on eating at the Japanese place a few steps down called norikinoko, but for some reason it was closed.  We had only tried three dishes including dessert; angel wings, pad see-ew,  and fried bananas.  The angel wings wasn't bad, a tad oily, and not much meat overcompensated with stuffing.  The pad see-ew was good and flavorful, but not overpowering.  We had ordered the chicken and it had a decent amount of chicken with it, but the wrong broccoli.  Traditionally it is supposed to come with the Chinese broccoli, but it had the regular what we think of broccoli broccoli...  Then we finished it off with the fried bananas which was not that bad.  We had asked it with coconut ice cream, but I dont think they gave us coconut ice cream... and if they did then it tastes just like vanila.

I really only came to Racha because I used to live right around the corner from here.

The Green curry with tofu was always my favorite.  Nothing really outstanding but plenty of vegetarian options and they can replace almost any dish with tofu.

The service isn't stellar and the atmosphere of the place is always mixed.  I've come into it most of the time bare empty with gives the establishment an eerie feel with its weird interior design of (I'm assuming) thai art that some what looks like out of a kama sutra book.  And then I've come into here when its packed which gives it more of a better feel.

Overall the place is alright but not memorable.

Ate here yesterday with some friends... I ususally always order Pad Thai when I go to a Thai place for the first time but this time I wanted to try something new so I ordered the Pad kee mao ... IT WAS REALLY BAD.. I'm really lenient with my food b/c I would basically eat anything and my taste buds have been deteriorating but the texture of the noodles was really slimy and gross. I like my flat noodles to be on the chewy side but this was just slimy and thin and greasy. I felt like gagging all night for hours after dinner. 

I hear their fried rice and curries are really good though so if I ever get dragged here again, I am definitely ordering one of those

Forget those Thai places at the Asian ghetto that claim to serve gourmet Thai cuisine, but end up serving food not worthy of your taste buds. Racha Cafe surprised me. The small restaurant looks a little shady on the outside, but inside it felt homey and cozy. The service was great! My water glass was always being refilled.
The food was so delicious. Every bite had a burst of flavor with the right spices. I enjoyed every bite. Try the duck fried rice, the yellow curry, and the pad see ew (you can't go wrong with this basic dish). The prices were a little more expensive than your usual Thai places. But the food was filling and so good.

It's an okay place to go to. 

Service is typically good and the waiters do make rounds often looking for empty water cups. 

Portions here seem to vary from dish to dish, or at least that's how I feel. I usually order the Pad Sea Ew and that definitely fills me up. It's also a pretty good dish with a good balance of flavor such that it's not too oily or bland. The curry dish I ordered the first time I went there, while it tasted alright, was a bit smaller than expected. 

Restaurant is a fairly spacious environment despite a small looking exterior. It's a good place to eat and talk (although I can't do this for some reason), and it can accommodate bigger groups although gratuity is included in the bill over a certain number. 

Between this place and Thai Basil, I'd definitely choose to go here instead.

Service is pretty slow. We were the only people without food and it still took days. But they have the best pad see ew. I literally go there just to eat that. They give you a lot and I never finish either.

The food here is pretty tasty! The restaurant itself isn't the prettiest, but the food makes up for it. I always order the green curry fried rice and order the curry to be spicy, and it is very yummy. I also like how they tell you on the receipt how much tip you should give. It helps out a lot when you don't want to do any calculations in your head.

For some reason I always have allergic reactions to the Thai food at Thai Basil on Durant. And since Thai Noodle is under construction this has been my new favorite Thai restaurant. I've tried three of their dishes: Chicken Green Curry with Rice, Green Curry Fried Rice and BBQ Chicken. The only one that I didn't like was the Green Curry Fried Rice because it had way too much basil and it was too spicy. 

The Chicken Green Curry was really nice and creamy. This curry was a lot better than the one I had at Chris Thai Food on Shattuck although I think they might have better Pad Thai. I live close by so I'll be sure to come back a couple more times.

Flavorless pad see ew. Okay thai iced tea. I've definitely had (much) better, but at least it's cheap and conveniently located. And they deliver, but it's tough to meet the $25 minimum; that's 4 dishes! Anyway, Berkeley has better places that aren't too far away... probably worth checking those out instead.

I would be giving the five starts but I got take out once from here and it wasn't up to par. Maybe the chef just had a bad day. Anyway I have had the Pad Thai and Fried Rice and BBQ and tasted some of my friends dishes and every time its always amazingly good. The prices are fair and the service is always friendly. I go out of my way to make trips to Berkeley just to eat here. Whenever someone comes into town and wants good Thai food I try to bring them here. Definitely worth your money.
One of my more favorite Thai restaurants in Berkeley.  I like their noodle dishes and their soups are pretty good too.  The service is nice and friendly, and the food is pretty quick.

I really like Racha, as the food here is pretty good and quick, and the staff is usually very friendly.

When I come here, I usually get the basil with ground chicken over rice.  It is quite good and convenient for those on the go, because it fits nicely (and cleanly) in a to-go box.  They also give you quite a bit of food.

All of the other dishes are pretty good, such as the stewed dishes (e.g., curry), and the various vegetable sautees.  They have this standard peanut sauce that I do not really like however, which is usually a little bit too sweet for me, and it tastes artificial.

You will have a hard time finding parking around here.  Do yourself a favor: park on Durant and walk over here.

Delicious and inexpensive food, both times I have been here.  The green curry with tofu was fantastic - perfectly balanced seasoning with a little heat, but not too hot.  Spring rolls are also very good.   Racha has an excellent selection for vegetarians and is located close to all the action on Telegraph.  Great place for an inexpensive bite in Berkeley!

Wow this place is really good! Pad see ew, pad mee kao, pad thai, red curry, and number 70 (I forget the name -- green beans, peppers, onions, basil) are all awesome. And the price: serving size ratio is great!

This is one of my favorite Thai places in Berkeley for a few reasons. The service is decent, the pricing fair, it has a nicer environment than some of the other Thai places in Berkeley, and of course, the food is yummy! 

My favorite is the Pad See Ew - I have yet to find another Thai place that makes it comparable to Racha Thai. So delicious! I would also recommend the red curry, pineapple fried rice, tom yum soup, and Pad Thai. All are delicious! Portions are pretty large, too. 

When I was going to Cal, my sorority held several dinner events here - their back room is nice for small banquets and even though the food is buffet style, it's still just as tasty. I hope that when my sorority holds the next Alumnae Luncheon, it will be held here so I can indulge in some good Thai food!

I've been here quite a few times and the food has been pretty good. The wait can be a quite a while though when there are people there. Don't be afraid of the exterior of this place because the interior is pretty warm.  I usually go with the Pad See Eew when I dine in. When I take food to go I go with the same or with Pad Kee Mao with a Red Curry and I make some rice at home. They often mess up your orders (give you different kind of meat that you ask for).. so make sure you have what you ordered. Check this place out if you're in the area but not a place to go out of your way for.

I was visiting Berkeley back in 03' and my cousin took me here for dinner.  Racha Cafe is the first place I tried Thai food BTW and that's when I fell in love.  Small but cosy and all the workers are friendly.

We started off with the Tom Ka Gai (coconut soup).  A perfect combination of salty n sweet.  Mmm.  The garlic pepper chicken is so mouth watering.  Spicy but just the right amount.  And last but not least, the pad thai was delish as well!  

If you're looking for some cheap but good thai food in Berkeley, you should definitely check Racha Cafe out.

One of the better Thai food place around Berkeley.  Slightly more expensive than either Thai Basil, Thai House, or Thai noodle.  Their food are all in the 9-12 dollars range, but they are absolutely delicious!  

I have had the Duck fried rice, which I highly recommend.  It's my go to dish if I don't feel like thinking of what to get.  Hmmm... Duck... I am drooling just thinking about it.  

The Pineapple fried rice is my second go to dish.  

Their noodle soup is not as good as Thai noodle, but their plates are def. better.  

They also have a back room which you can reserve for a group.  Last time we were there with 25 people and it can still fit more!

I went here with some coworkers one night, and overall this place was pretty enjoyable.  Everyone else really liked their dishes, but I found mine only so so.

I asked the waitress for my dish to be as spicy as they could make it, and she spent several minutes trying to convince me that I couldn't handle it.  After she finally relented and agreed to serve me my food at maximum spiciness, I was disappointed that my food was not, in fact, that spicy.  Since the dish I was having (something tofu centric) was otherwise pretty bland, I was disappointed with the food.

This was back a couple months ago when the store had different owners.  I have heard that the new owner's do not make very good food.  If you want Thai food and are near Telegraph, go to Thai Basil or Thai House instead.

Racha Cafe is definitely  better than Thai Basil in terms of quality.  How much better though? Only a little bit.

The curries are good as well as the noodle dishes.  My favorite is the Teaw Khak (sp?) which is the flat noodles with chicken and a ton of peanut sauce over it.  

The dessert is good as well.  Fried bananas and coconut ice cream? SO GOOD.

My favorite Thai restaurant in Berkeley thus far. This highlighter yellow building with its nondescript white sign is where I had my first great Thai dish as a freshman. 

Service: Every time I go, I am seated quickly, my order is taken promptly, and water is refilled periodically. Staff isn't particularly courteous, but definitely no complaints. 

Food: Large servings (I almost always have to take some food home) and delicious noodle dishes! My favorite is their Pad Kee Mao. Their Pad Thai is also far superior to Thai Basil's ridiculously sweet rendition. Sure, it's maybe a dollar or so pricier (if even that), but way worth it considering how much better Racha's dishes taste. Have yet to try their noodle soups though. 

Atmosphere: Great place to go to if you're looking for a nice sit-down restaurant that's not too expensive. Clean and well decorated. Not too busy, and nobody's hovering or waiting for you to finish your food so they can sit. Bathroom could be more aesthetically pleasing, but again, no complaints.

Edible, good service, but unbelievably dull.  I had the take out chicken satay (which was quite good) and the veggie pad thai.  In my opinion pad thai should be a staple of a thai restaurant.  This was just dull.  No spice, noddles all stuck together, soggy vegetables.  Really unimpressive.  Credit cards only for orders over $10.

Cheap and Tasty

Living for years in Berkeley, I've been to most of the restaurants in the vicinity of the campus. I'm tired of most of them and crave for variety, but I seldom go to any other thai places in Berkeley. I'd like to, but everytime I do I regret it. It's cheaper and much better food than Thai House, the portions are way bigger than Took Took, and I'm not going to mention Thai Basil. In Racha the portions are big, the food always tastes fresh (I tried everything on the menu, and liked most items, except for the duck), the service is pleasant, the wine is reasonably priced, and all that for the same price you'd pay at McThai places like Thai Basil. It's definitely a cheap eatery type of place, but out of the cheap eateries, it's the best in Berkeley

Racha's pad see ew is pretty good, I really like the portion size and the sweet sauce. Their fried rice is pretty serviceable too. I think their main dishes are a little too bland though, and could use more seasoning ie more salt. The service is nice though, and seating is not really a problem.
Very good food, and very clean place.  The service was quite prompt and friendly, and the prices are great.  Would definitely recommend.

FRIED CHICKEN OVER FRIED RICE= WINNER
THAI BOAT NOODLE= REALLY BEEFY WINNER
BBQ CHICKEN OVER FRIED RICE= MEGA WINNER
KAO MOO DANG= ADVENTUROUS WINNER
EVERYTHING ELSE= pretty decent. 
The waitresses suck until you become a regular.

I love this place. Decent prices, nice atmosphere, and they keep my water full without asking.
  One thing I love about Thai food is that I like most all of their condiments. Generally unless it is some yogurt based abomination, the sauces are tangy, spicy and delicious. With asian foods I enjoy making a meal of appetizers. Last night I got these little fried potato triangles wrapped in that eggroll type stuff served with a sweet-mild spicy sauce and cucumber salad. Let me dwell on the cucumber salad a moment. It is just wedges of cucumber, strands of red onion and carrot, in a syrup of water,vinegar,sugar and salt that is so simple, perfect and sublime that I want to bring it to the sasquatch and say "look, humans aren't all bad, we made this!" he would sip it, consider it a moment and his eyes would light up and give me a big thumbs up. After that he would freely move in and out of the human world and back to the woods, certain that there was at least some method to our madness.
  Anyway, I usually like to get this yummy ground chicken noodle dish with peppers and basil. I can always get satisfied with what I order and have a little bit for later. There is no wine list, but you can get a half liter of cheap wine for 6 bucks. Add a side of rice to an appetizer and my party is on motherfucker.
