   Nice restaurant for dates and shopping on Telegraph avenue.
I will see you there sometime.

This place is about average as far as Thai places go.  I've tried their noodle dishes, Pad Kee Mao, and Pad See ew, but they were okay, not spectacular.  I much prefer the Pad KeeMao at Plearn II down the street.  

Their noodle soups also left a little to be desired, with the Tom Yum being too watered down and not flavorful enough.  The curry noodle was super rich and not too bad, but needed some more noodles or some rice to go along with it.

The worst part was the insect infestation.  We were constantly swatting down these black flying insects.  They didn't look like mosquitoes, but when you squish them, and there were a lot to squish, a red bloodlike smear was left behind.  It wasn't just our table near the kitchen, but also others as well, as I could see patrons swatting the air.  Brrr, I get shivers just thinking about the experience.

Oh how I miss the special that gave you a free appetizer with select lunch entrees. ;( but I cant complain since the serving size is pretty big. I cant even finish Pad Ke Moa but I guess its a good thing because i can eat for breakfast the next day!.

I think this place has an identical (number for number) menu to thai noodle 2 down the street, but it's called racha instead of Thai Noodle III, I don't know why. Same thing except a little more on the 1980's restaraunt decor side.
Hands down the best Thai in the east bay. Not to mention the $8 per person ticket. Do yourself a favor and go Racha tonight!

This place was located a block away from my debaucherous Berkeley apartment so the roomies and I ordered our fair share of take out from here.  Mostly, I love the green curry fried rice, just the right amount amount of kick and great flavor.  It's even large enough to share with another person (but since it's just rice, plan on eating a bowl of cereal a few hours later).  I also liked their BBQ chicken and fried rice.  Sadly, their pad-see-ewe has been disappointing lately.  There's a sweetness to it that kind of freaks me out, so I've been sticking to the rice dishes.  Portions are bigger that way too (they skimp on the noodle dishes).  Generally, it takes 15 mins from call-in to pick up, so if you're looking for quick and easy this place hits the spot.

Pad Thai: nasty, lack of flavor
Pinapple Fried Rice: meh, thai noodle has better PFR
Pad Ke Mow: very good.
Pad see eew: really good

Good for large groups, they have a banquet room in the back.
I always loved the Pad See Ew here (without eggs), but most of my dining companions prefered other Thai places around Berkeley.

Most unsatisfying eating experience in... ever? Mostly I'll be whining about the service and portions, so I still give the place 2 stars because the food itself is pretty good.

Not trying to be dramatic but, I paid 8$ for a tiny tiny tiny plate of eggplant beef stir fry over rice that is only worth about 3$ max. When I got my plate, all my friends commented on how sad it looked. Portions here are ridiculously small its a total rip off (for the rice plates).

How ridiculous are the portions? One bowl of rice with probably two spoonfuls of the entree I ordered. My eggplant dish had three pieces of eggplant. Three. ??? But for some reason, my friends' whose orders were a dollar more expensive had about three times my portion of food.

.... what? I lost it when I saw my plate of food. The taste is fine, actually pretty good, but the feeling of being ripped off coupled with super slow service means that I don't think I'd dare to go back and try again for fear of being angered again. :(


Did I mention there is a 18% gratuity automatically included? I ate here during lunch, we had a party of 6.

I got dragged here enough in my college days to know that most of the dishes are a disappointment - especially those involving chicken (usually ground dark meat and not nice white meat chunks). This is the first place I ever had tom kha gai soup and it was pretty good, so that gives this place an extra star - all the way up to three.

The restaurant's atmosphere is as good as the food they serve. The fried calamari was OK, the batter didn't give it any special taste, it was too plain without the fish sauce. The Pineapple Fried Rice was too moist but all of the fundamental ingredients were there, the taste of the rice got too boring after eating it for a while. But desert was Mango with Sticky Rice; the sticky rice tasted really delicious, but as for the mango it was about sour. Evidently the food was good, not great.

not the best thai style rice, i ordered the pineapple fried rice and i was pretty disappointed, it was really bland and had no kick, no flavor!

my girlfriend tried the pad ke mao, and it was SO GOOD! If only their fried rice was good, this place would have been a definite four star if their fried rice was good because their portions are big, their prices are cheap and their noodles are soo good!

I was surprised at how good this place was despite the other reviews. Came here for a friend's birthday and ordered the red curry with pumpkin. The portion was just right for me, and the curry was pretty good for the price. The chicken was tender and the pumpkin was cooked just right. 

Since it was friend's birthday, they gave us a fried banana dessert...the thing was ridiculously good and the whole plate was devoured in minutes amongst a few people.

This place has got to be the best Thai food I've had in Berkeley! The portions are quite large (I've only finished everything off the plate once). Oh and they also have a call-in service where they'll have your food ready in 15 min. 

I usually get the Pad Kee Mow Chicken which is simply awesome.

Racha Cafe is by far my favorite Thai food restaurant. It hella beats Thai Basil and all the other Thai restaurant competitors.

The quantity and quality from this restaurant was appropriate for its price range. 

I recommend almost all the curry over rice.

I have been reading reviews on Thai places on Telegraph since I am within walking distance of several different restaurants. I chose Racha because of its reviews. It sounded like it was good food at a good price. I am a huge fan of Thai food so I was really excited. I ordered red curry and the fresh spring rolls. 

I got my food to go, so when I got home I opened it all up and took a look. There was a layer of red-ish grease on top of the curry. Nonetheless, I stirred it up and gave it a try with rice. It wasn't as spicy as I was told it was going to be (a little disappointing for a lover of foods that make you sweat and your nose run). Overall, I would say it was just ok. I have lived in Springfield, Missouri for the last three years, and I have had better red curry there...

The spring rolls were huge! The ingredients were fresh, but a little boring too. 

I might go back to this place (because its 100 yds away) but I might try some other places first.

My take-out default in Berkeley!

Don't settle for Thai Basil or Thai Noodle II just because they're closer to campus. The food, service, and decor at Racha are definitely worth the extra 5 min walk. 

I have so many fond memories of wandering into Racha on my way home from a long day and drinking hot tea while I wait for my order; or  running in the rain to pick up some pad kee mao before studying. Some days, I wouldn't be able to choose between a meat dish or noodles so I'd just get both... for myself! Don't judge me haha. 

Pad kee mao (winning), pad see ew, red curry with pumpkin or duck, green curry, tom yum-- all are sooo delicious!! But my favorite would have to be the pad kee mao. If you're feeling like a fatty, the curry with duck is pretty rich and on the heavier side :)

The only down side I can think of might be that they have a $10 minimum for cc. But most places on Telegraph have similar policies. 

I really miss Racha :(

This is definitely my favorite place for thai food in the area! Even though it is a little further than Thai House and Thai Basil, it's definitely worth it! I really enjoy their pad see ew, yellow curry, and eggplant dish. The price is about $8 per dish, which is only a bit more than the others, but it's a decent portion.

Taste: 3
Value: 4
Service: 4

Came here once for lunch and another time for a banquet. The food was okay, pretty typical Thai food. I've had some people hype this place, but it really isn't that special. It's pretty comparable to Thai House or Thai Noodle.
Great food, good portions, reasonable prices.

Oh how times have changed... I remember back when there was a dork named Bush in the White House, we were involved in a war in Iraq... oh wait. Umh...

The thing you need to know about Racha is that the original family who started the restaurant has sold it. I miss the days of the kitschy old look, but I do give serious credit to the new owners for sprucing up the place.

And, for the most part, they clearly kept the old recipes and that's worthy of note. I am deathly incompatible with seafood and it's nice to know that there is still at least one Thai restaurant in the world where I can get Pad Thai with chicken and without shrimp. Ask me about the day when I ordered Pad Thai at another Berkeley restaurant which shall remain nameless -- the thankfully out-of-business Plearn -- and the waitress smiled and said "no seafood in noodles, only shrimp." But I digress...

My only regret is this: any of you kids under 25 years of age probably never got the experience of the old Racha's "Minced Chicken with Basil Leaf" entree. The single best thing on Racha's old menu... and it looks like it's gone forever.

Maybe it's not the fault of the new owners. Maybe Suchada's old family recipe was just too precious to share. But trust me, until the day they can successfully imitate that one dish, this "new Racha" will never be a more-than-3-star experience.

To end on a positive note: their takeout order time-to-fill is consistently the shortest on record. This is very important to me, as I only visit them after getting my hair cut at Maxi just down the block. Kudos for speed and basic good Thai food at an OK price.

This is definitely one of the BEST Thai food places around Berkeley, at a very good price. GREAT FOOD for CHEAP.
I eat a lot of Thai food, and Racha is by far my favorite. I like the Pad kii mao, Pad see ew, Thai BBQ Chicken, and Pad kha praw. Each dish is only about $6-$7, and the portions are generous.  Racha is off the hook!

When I first went in college, I didn't like it. I thought it tasted awful and had a strong dislike. BUT, I've been back since then in the last couple months. It's alright if you don't mind all the buddhist idols and drawings staring at you throughout the restaurant, and don't mind the food. The food isn't great, but it's not bad neither. It's neither here nor there, and really isn't the point of coming to this restaurant. 

Kind of a strange review, I know. But the food wasn't anything to write home about. But I did have really nice company, received respectful and prompt service, and liked the atmosphere.

Their pad kea mow was pretty good! however, their fried rice was a bit too bland; they might have to modify their recipe a little. but definitely better than thai basil in general. Gotta say that I am satisfied w/ almost every visit.

I had two main dishes here along with an appetizer and the duck fried rice and noodle entree were nothing special.  There was barely any duck in the fried rice too.  But for the prices you pay, I guess you can't expect too much.  

It's a bit funny cuz a sign on the table says they will not serve water (for water conservation purposes) unless you request it, but first thing they do is bring us two glasses of water as we browse through the money.

I would definitely go back and order two servings of the angel wings (each serving has two wings).  They were deep fried with no bones and stuffed with some thin glass-type noodles inside.  Never tried anything like it before.  ANGEL WINGS, I'll come back for you again!!!

I always like this place! There's usually no line, and it's less known and feels more local. Most of the food is better quality than the other Thai food places around here, but sometimes the plates are smaller. But that's good anyways cause I'm getting chubby. BUT the fried bananas and ice  team dessert is GINORMOUS. It's a little exaggerated, but it's still a good size (that's what SHE said). Definitely go here and just order the dessert. Nom Nom.

I can't really remember what I ordered here because I was super hungover. What I can remember was that huge spoon they have attached to their bathroom key.

My friends and I ate family style and all I can remember was liking their fried rice that came with the chicken. My friend thought the fried rice wasn't very flavorful, but I thought it was pretty tasty.

Another friend of mine says this is her favoritest Thai food in Berekley area... so I guess I'll have to come back when I'm SOBER!

Jeff woke up early Monday morning. 7:30 to be exact because he had a 8 AM final. After the final, Jeff walked to pick up Celia and they strolled down the rainy path known as Dwight towards Racha Cafe. Celia had heard her floormates talking about it in the bathroom the night before, and decided to try it.

The two entered the Cafe, and immediately noticed the yummy, spicy air. Jeff enjoyed the dining area. 

Celia had a dilemma: pad see ew, or pad kee mao? She picked pad see ew, because her floormates had recommended it. It was a great choice! But there weren't that many vegetables-- in the end, it was all just noodles :( It was delicious though. Favourite pad kee mao she's ever had! Next time, she will order the pad kee mao, or the pineapple fried rice.

Jeff ordered the green curry with chicken. The green curry was a bit buttery, but had a very wholesome taste. It was very fresh and egg-y textured. Celia thinks there was an egg in it, but, in retrospect, that is probably not true. There was an egg in it. No there wasn't. / stream of consciousness.

Jeff definitely thought that this place was better for noodles, whereas Thai Noodle was better for curry, which is kind of ironic. Thai Basil is good at nothing. According to Jeff (Celia disagrees though). So. Racha was great. Would come back again. 

CAUTION:
When we left, Celia noticed a sample cup on the outside of the store. But actually, it was a religious offering of food with a stick of incense in it. Jeff was pleasantly surprised, because the offered food was the same thing that he ordered. So if you see a cup outside the store, it is probably not a sample cup.

My favorite Thai place in Berkeley!  And there are a lot of good Thai places in Berkeley, so that's saying something.  Service is always very good here and the prices are about right.  

My favorite dish is the red curry, they give you a lot of vegetables as well as your choice of meat!  Almost anything with duck is also pretty good, and you can definitely count on the popular dishes: pad Thai, pad kee mow, pineapple fried rice, etc to be savory and they are generous with their servings.  

Great for large and small groups!

Some of my Berkeley sisters took us here after a meeting. Normally I am not a big fan of Thai food, but I really liked this restaurant.

A couple of our girls went to the restaurant early to save spots for us. One thing I liked was how the waitress had everything set up- silverware, waters, and extra water.

When the waitress took my order (usually I am super indecisive) I asked her if she had a recommendation for the meat to put in my order-
I ordered number 44- and she quickly responded, "chicken,"  instead of asking me a whole bunch of questions before making a recommendation- which I liked. 

#44 had a good flavor with a kick to it (the chili). The flavors were yummy- not too over powering or too little. The portions were generous for a THai restaurant- I was expecting half of what I got.

When it came time to pay- I liked how you just go up to the waitress and tell them what you ordered and pay there- that way you dont have to calculate what you ordered and how much you need to pay towards the group bill. 

The one thing I didn't like, was how I think either they need to up date the prices, or let the customers know if they are paying with card and their amount is less than $10- they added the tip in. 

The prices said the noodles were suppose to be 6.99- with tax this would have been around 7.70-8.00 for the meal. When she told me my meal was $9 ( I think it was cuz she saw I was going to pay with a card?), I didnt think too much about it, but when I got home, I would have preferred her letting me know there is a 10 minimum- that way I would have tipped her the amount that adds up to 10 (if it would have been less than 15-20% I would have just given her 15-20% tip instead)



Overall I would come here again

My go-to thai place. Honestly, I prefer the flavor of Thai Basil in the ghetto, but this is the place for sit-down thai. The type of place you don't want to be rushed, and you sit down and have some quality time with friends and others.

Here are a few points:
1.) The green curry is yummy so I always come back for more.
2.) They have long tables, which is nice for when you're going somewhere with a group of 8
3.) They dont rush you at all. Which is a relief.
4.) My water glass is always full, which is a sign of great service.

Also, my friend tried the Chang beer here, and it was pretty damn tasty. First asian beer I've ever had thats actually had some taste.

I like Racha Cafe a lotttt better than Thai Basil! Why?? The service is great and the food is brought out quickly in generous portions & better quality! 

Chicken pad see ew is suuuper good! Just the right amount of flavor without being overly greasy like Thai Basil sometimes tends to be. Love it! 

Duck fried rice is sooo amazing!! Perfectly cooked fried rice with perfectly cooked duck (not too dry and very easy to eat)!

Pad thai is very delicious as well. Basically, I don't think you can go wrong ordering anything from Racha (: 

The service, as I mentioned before, is really good. The friendly waiters regularly checked up on us and refilled our waters without us asking (:

ALSO! Last time, they gave us some really good candy when they brought us the check.. and since we really liked it, they brought out more for us! yayy! (:

This is a fine Thai restaurant.  It's probably not the best Thai you'll ever have in your life but it certainly makes me happy.  I love that it is only two blocks away from my apartment so i can order some take out and pick it up and walk home.

Their Pad Thai is excellent. Plenty flavourful and well-balanced, it doesn't commit the sin, typically committed in Thai restaurants, of being cloyingly sweet. Instead, you get the right balance of salty, sweet and tart, and a little bit spicy, just as I like it. Portions are generous too, even for the meat: I have to take a box every time I go. The other Pad Thais I've had around Berkeley just don't compare.

I do remember, however, that there was one time the beef in my friend's Pad See Ew apparently tasted kind of weird and sour, so she didn't eat the meat. On the whole, though, with that lone exception, everyone's food's really good.

Service-wise, all the food comes about the same time, even for a group of ten, and they're willing to handle multiple credit cards on the bill, something I don't expect an Asian place to do.

Conveniently close, friendly staff, and good food at an affordable price. Their Pad Thai (beef), Hot and Sour soup, Silver Noodle soup, and curry are delicious. At an average price of $7 this place is definitely worth a try when craving Thai cuisine.

***Update 1/16/2007*** Racha recently undergone a renovation over the winter break and the new appearance (inside & outside) is a huge improvement to the dinning experience. Gone are the dark drab brownish color wall and replaced with bright vibrant color that is easy on the eyes. New Ikea style light fixture enhance the visibility factor when dining with friends and examining the delicious food. The facade also received a new coat of neon green/yellow to stand out from the brown wood-shingle that adorn the adjacent retail stores on that street.

A solid Thai restaurant that deserves 3.5 stars. This is my go-to thai place and food here is consistently satisfactory.

This is a well-rounded restaurant so you can't go wrong with any order! My favorite pad sea ew (pan fried flat noodles with meat and some vegetables) default order tastes good and oily, like all pad sea ews. Pad sea ew beef, chicken, and pork are all good, though I wish they have more vegetables in the dish. Portions here are huge, and I always have leftovers for another meal.

Red curry or green curry are also good choices, and pineapple fried rice=yum. Thai iced tea isn't really worth it if you are ordering to-go; they pour it into a cheap paper cup and you get less for your $2

NOTE: to-go orders are always burning HOT and placed in foil so you don't want to let the food sit for too long or it will steam cook itself to mushiness. That being said, food is always right off the stove and never cold, microwaved, or pre-cooked

Racha Cafe looks very unassuming for its obnoxious yellow paint exterior, but the interior is spiffy and well-furnished with sleek wooden chairs and a plethora of Thai deco. The feel is very exotic and Thai, though there is pop music playing softly in the background. Service is a bit on the slow side, and the lady in charge seems to be the only one who knows what is going on. 

WILL I come back: Yes
WHEN will I come back: When I crave thai; this is my defult and convenient Thai restaurant in Berkeley
WHAT will I do differently: Expand my horizons and try new dishes

Racha's is a step or two up from Thai Basil. Their food, service, and decor are all pretty good. The inside of the restaurant feels very welcoming and it's surprisingly really big as well (many people have banquets here). The servers are friendly and they often come around to refill cups. If you have a large group and want to split the bill, they'd be happy to accomodate. 

I usually get the tom kha (soup only) with a side of rice. Their Thai iced tea is also really good and it's cool how they let you mix the tea and milk together yourself instead of giving you something that they premade in batches.

Overall, I always enjoy my dining experiences here.

From a very loyal customer of two years. They can accept cash or card. Five stars because they have really big and yummy portions for the price! As a Berkeley student I used to cycle through their menu because they have a lot of good stuff: 

- The beef and Chinese broccoli (super rich in nutrient) over rice dish is a healthier alternative and reminds me of my mom's food. Pieces of cut beef are used, and the sauce is mostly soy sauce and not heavy. 

- Beef Pad Kee Mao is tasty and makes my taste buds very happy. It is a little spicy. Ground beef is used. 

- Tew Lord has shrimp and ground chicken over rice noodles, and the delicious sauce is served on the side you can pour in any amount of sauce to your heart's content. Mix the noodles up, and it tranforms to pure deliciousness! I pour in half but my friends pour the whole thing in. I usually ask for the dish to be less oily anyways, because even without the sauce, the ground chicken and shrimp somehow have a decent amount of oil. 

- Panang Curry. For those days when you want to soak the rice in curry goodness. You know. 

Their goes my four favorite dishes among a menu full of good dishes. 
Their Thai Tea is great! If you are picky about the unnecessary fat you can ask for more tea and less cream and it is still just as good!

All my friends love Racha Cafe, but I don't really know why. To me, the food is just all right and not worth the money. 

I've been here several times (because like I said, my friends love it), and I've had the Roasted Duck Salad, Duck Noodle Soup, Tom Yum Noodle Soup, and Pineapple Fried Rice. The duck here is pretty flavourful, but the salad and the noodles were bland. The Tom Yum tastes like water with some lime juice squeezed in, and it's probably the worst tom yum I've ever tasted. The Pineapple Fried Rice was pretty good, but the rice was mushy and too oily.

The seating area is pretty spacious and clean, and there's a back room for large groups or club events/celebrations. You can call in to place everyone's orders beforehand so you won't have to wait a ridiculously long time for your food.

Maybe I'm just ordering the wrong things, but I figure if I want curry or pad thai I can just go to Thai Basil. Until next time!

Service and environment is good.  It looks small on the outside, but the restaurant actually extends all the way in and can seat large groups.  The prices ares very reasonable, and the food generally tastes great.

Some traitional favorites include chicken green curry, pad thai, pad see-ew, and tom yum.  I can recommend all the above.  Portions are great for the price too.

Pretty solid Thai establishment. Its super spacious, so don't worry about a wait. If you ever need a place for a small gathering, birthday party or banquet: they can accommodate. 

Food-wise: noodle portions are good, and the taste is consistent 
Faves: Pad see ew, Pad kee mao, Pad thai

Soups: Tom yum, lemon grass 

Curry: portions are on the smaller side, especially if you order it with rice. I usually dont finish the curry but here, its no problem. 
Pumpkin red curry: delicious, and they give you a good portion of pumpkin. However, it was undercook when I ordered it. 
Yellow Curry: delicious, coconut milk and potato
Green Curry: Order it with chicken, cooked tenderly 

Cleaner than Thai noodle and definitely a good place to get your thai food fix in the area.
My favorite place to get Thai food in Berkeley. It's a bit overpriced for my standards, but it tastes exceptional and they give relatively large portions! I always get the pad se ewe shrimp.

My boyfriend LOVES this place so we come here all the time.
it's pretty much your average thai food. Dishes are about $8 and not very large. I find the curries too sweet, as well as some of the noodle dishes. I would recommend the appetizers with peanut dipping sauce...we had chicken satay. SO good. the eggplant (with other stuff) in a clay pot is also delicious.
The ambience is quite nice for a Berkeley restaurant. It's usually pretty empty and quiet, and the service is great.
Beware: If there are actually people here, expect to WAITWAITWAIT and starve for your food...

My friend suggested this place when I was in the mood for Thai since I suggested the regular Thai places we go to. I was pleasantly surprised by how clean it was. I heard they remodeled and you can tell. Very clean and modern looking with the new tables. A nice change for a Telegraph restaurant.

I ordered the bbq chicken over rice suggested by my friend. It was delicious! The sauce was perfect and the chicken was crispy on the outside and flaky on the inside. The portion was just right since the dishes over rice are for individual meals. My friend said that she ordered this once for lunch but it didn't have the same bbq sauce so come here for dinner and try it.

Prices are pretty cheap/decent for a sit down restaurant. I liked it just because it isn't obnoxiously loud. Only bad thing was there was only one guy working and he was slow at getting around to each table.

Easy. Cheap. (Bring an iPod)

I came to this neat spot further down on Telegraph with my Houston buddy, i gotta say, it is fairly well-priced for the amount of food, authenticity and general convenience. I got the papaya salad as a starter dish; it was both refreshing and quenching in all the right Thai flavors. 

You can get a Pad Thai, big enough for two hungry traverlers. 

The only thing, and I am clearly biased, is the music. It played none-stop trashy 90's pop crap. I wish it had some awesome Thai instrumental music. That's my two cents.

This place pretty much dominates the southside thai scene, especially after the demise of Thai Noodle. (RIP) I pretty much ate here every meal during the last finals week just so I could write a yelp review saying how I ate here every meal during the last finals week. Food is quickly prepared and pretty dericious, although there could be more vegetables in the pad see ew.

I came here with a group of people one night. Service was slow but there was a party of 20 or so, so understandable. 

During my past visits, I've had the:

Pad Thai - eh, nothing special. 
Pad Kee Maw - one of the better dishes
Pad See Ew - good because not oily like many other places make it
Green curry - sucked because it had more meat and veggies then curry. I guess I'm just not into Thai curry. 
Thai iced tea - pretty good. 

Overall, an ok experience but it's in general hard to find a good, authentic Thai restaurant in Berkeley.

I've come here twice and found it pretty decent. It may not have as much of a lunch-time crowd as Thai Basil or Tuk Tuk Thai, but as far as I know, Racha is slightly cheaper. The duck curry is highly recommended, though I have to admit that my idea of curry is more in line with the Indian type, and I found the curry here to be more like soup. There was also a fried pork entree; I don't remember the name, but it was at the right crunchiness, and my brother and I bickered over the last pieces.

Noodles were decent, especially if you get fried pork with it. They weren't as memorable as the curry entrees that I've tried, though. 

The environment might not be for everyone. There are some reviews here mentioning unfriendly staff. I've never had unfriendly staff ruining my experience, but they weren't really friendly either. And the place can be a bit empty at times, probably because it isn't as close to campus as the previously mentioned Thai places. Racha is more spacious, however.

Overall, if you're looking for good Thai curry and could care less about service, Racha is the place. For faster service and closeness to campus, Thai Basil is the better choice.

I thought my red curry tofu and fried prawns (sort of like veggie tempura w/ two little prawns) were spot on in flavor and packed with veggies. It was easy to accommodate a rando lunch for 20 here too, though the food came out at different times. It was really yummy though.

I've been here several times and it was actually the first restaurant that my sister took me to when I decided to go to UCB for school. Today, I came with a good friend to enjoy some Thai food and sit and chat.

Service/Decor: There are murals all over the walls, supposedly to give a more "Thai" feel to the place. The restaurant overall seems pretty clean. Extremely fast. There are chimes that jingle when you walk in that prompt the waiter to step in and seat you. He seemed nice, polite, and responsive.

Food:
The first time I came here and the few times I came back, I got the Pad Thai or Pad See Ew. It is definitely better than Thai Basil's, since Thai Basil's Pad Thai tastes like it was mixed in ketchup and oyster sauce. I usually add a good amount of peanuts that are available on the side and a small dollop of hot sauce. Their Pad Thai and Pad See Ew are definitely enjoyable.

Today, I ordered the Teaw Kak, which consisted of flat rice noodles, broccoli, pork (you have the choice of chicken, beef, tofu), and a VERY peculiar sweet peanut sauce. When it first came out I had absolutely no idea what to make of it. It wasn't pre-mixed and the sauce was just poured right on top of all the other ingredients. It looked like an even, brown sauce that reminded me of Japanese curry. My taste buds also had no idea what to make of it. I managed to finish it with a large amount of hot sauce. But yeah, don't order the Teaw Kak. Just don't.

We also got the fried banana with coconut ice cream. Delicious. The coconut ice cream had a lovely texture and complemented the fried banana very nicely. I don't even like coconut very much and I thought it was excellent.

Verdict: In my efforts to be adventurous, I failed and probably just chose the wrong dish. The other times that I've come here haven't failed me. I feel confident enough in this restaurant to suggest coming here with friends.

The food here is pretty good! One of the best Thai places in Berkeley, for sure. I definitely liked the pineapple fried rice and the curry fried rice. 

If only I were Thai...then I would be able to order all the other exotic things.

I was happy during my visit here. My friends ordered a lot so I got to taste a lot of different types of foods they offered. I can't say I loved the pad thai since I already have a place that I love love love their pad thai at, all I can say is that its satisfying.

One of my favorite places to get thai food.  They have long tables for big groups of people and they have waiter service, which is more rare in a college area like Racha is.  The food won't blow your head off, but the general ambiance, more than decent food, and reasonable prices will keep you coming back for more.  :)

Probably the second-best Thai food place I know of in the bay area, but don't take my word for it because I've only tried a handful.

Racha Cafe was actually the first Thai food place I liked... and coincidentally the first place that got me to like Thai food. Their green curry here is FANTASTIC. It is my absolute favorite dish, and I would recommend ordering pork with it. It's REALLY hard to make tender pork, but this place does it right!

Prices are reasonable (about the price Thai food usually is) and their dishes are all-around good.

I've been going here since I was in college (long time) but stopped after 2 incidents.

1. Having lunch with a friend (red curry) and a roach scampered across the wall.

2. Had dinner with another friend (I probably had the red curry again) and I'm guessing we shared a soup. She had the pork and spinach and threw up all the next day. Since she is a rampant carnivore she swore it was the spinach.

Even though I used to enjoy the curries, the fish cakes, the salads I go elsewhere these days.

By far the best Thai place near the UC Berkeley campus - affordable, affectionate, and all-around awesome (said with mouth agape). 

Service is always quick and friendly and what more can I say about the food?!?! Firstly, always end with the fried banana and ice cream; never a fail moment when you decide upon this - always such a great ending to a great meal. All the curries are rich and never dry or uninspired. Yellow Curry is always the safe choice. As for noodle, you can never go wrong! The soups are inexplicably flavorful and even though I like my food spicy, Racha always kicks it up a notch. I adore their rice dishes and it always fills us up with no such regret. Serving sizes are actually just about right and in terms of healthiness I (feel) like I can never go wrong with my curious appetite.

I guess what I want to say is that Racha holds a lot of great and enticing memories - whether it be the company, atmosphere, food or service - Racha was always the best place to go when we're in search for delicious realizations and appetite-quenching stress relief.

Racha makes (probably) the most flavorful Thai food I've tried so far in Berkeley. The dishes are reasonably large relative to the price of each dish. Although I was in a big group at the time I went, they managed to serve most of the people within 10-15 minutes. You might think the restaurant is small, but if you walk inside, it can accommodate two ~25 people tables.

Don't get their Tom Yum Noodle Soup... I've had it twice and I wanted to cry both times as I attempted to put craploads of hot sauce to make it more flavorful :(

Their other dishes are so good, but why must they do this to Tom Yum! :( Defeat...

This place is awesome. This is the best  Thai restaurant yet that I've been to in Berkeley. Their fried calamari has a thai kick to it, but just the right amount. The pad thai and yellow curry were delicious as well.

Drive across the bridge, there are better places in SF for Thai food. Don't come here expecting authentic Thai food. They have a very extensive menu with a lot of choices but the dishes were all lacking in flavor (e.g. tom yum soup) or they weren't cooked properly (e.g. bbq chicken which was way too sweet).

Oh Racha, how I love thee.

Too bad your new owners decided to get rid of any personality whatsoever on your interior.

But the food is the same, i suspect the same cooks are employed.  The lunch there is great, you get a little soup or salad and the price is cheaper.  The food is just as good as the likes of Thai House, but much less expensive.  Atmosphere leaves something to be desired.

I basically stick to the same items, and they're all good.  I'll name them in order of deliciousness:
1- eggplant with beef stir fry.  a little spicy and wonderful
2- Pad See Ew.  Thick, chewy noodles with meat of your choice and broccoli.  Yum
3- Yellow Curry with Chicken.  Always a sweet and mildly spicy treat.
4- Green Curry.  i just like it because it comes with eggplant.
5- Pad Thai.  Not that it's bad or anything, its just that after I discovered Pad See Ew, the Pad Thai just rarely makes the cut.

For those of you who live in Berkeley, you're probably familiar with the wide selection of Thai restaurants around the area. However amongst this myriad of options, Racha Cafe is my place to go for authentic, spicy Thai food. 

Like most thai restaurants in Berkeley, it's a small, family-owned establishment. So in a sense, most thai places here are pretty authentic. I like Racha because they use the freshest herbs and spices for each curry dish, instead of pre-packaged curry paste that other restaurants may use (not pointing fingers). To me, that speaks quality and care in their food. Furthermore, I appreciate that they do not overdress their noodle dishes with sauces. Noodles like Pad Kee Mao and especially Pad Thai are lightly sauteed in their spicy sauces, instead of swimming in sauce. Therefore, it tastes more refreshing.

I have ordered here many times in the past and am never disappointed with their dishes...always delicious, imo. Personally I recommend their green curries, pineapple fried rice, pad thai, pad see eew and pad kee mao. Please give it a try! I know that it looks dingy on the outside, but it is a gem when it comes to good, thai cuisine.

The yellow curry, pineapple fried rice, pad thai, thai iced tea... 

Everything was good. I have nothing to complain about, but I have nothing to rave about either. There are a jillion Thai restaurants in Berkeley so this review remains relatively boring.

+ close to bus stop
+ close to campus
+ uncrowded
+ clean
+ comfortable

They have Flaming Chicken.  

Seriously peoples...they light the entire bird on fire at your table!  

Yes, yes...it's dead already....jeez.

I wouldn't travel more than a couple blocks to come dine here. [Not implying this place is bad, it's not.  It is quite yummy.] 

Basically, I give it 4 Stars, because I live so close to this place.  It's convenient.  And I am a fan of convenience. 

Everything I have ordered here has been good. Last night I had the Pad Se Ew with Chicken and it was delicious. And I have left overs...Y-E-S!

The only complaint is that their mango sticky rice has too much coconut milk.

I dig this place.  However, one tip?  Order delivery or take-out.  The portions are insane and one dish can definitely be two meals.  I learned this by ordering through delivery sites like Seamless Web and Grubhub where they usually have $20 or $25 minimums.  It was worth it though because I'd order and have lunch and dinner for a couple of days.  Once time I ordered and the next day went on a road trip in an RV.  Having Thai leftovers on the road? Pretty awesome.

I'm partial to their drunken noodles, pad se ew.  Those are the wide noodles with meat and veggies.  They're my favorite.  I also like their yellow curry for the meat and potatoes.  They're always friendly and the food is always good.  It's also not too expensive, so it's one of my favorite local restaurants.

Its cheap, never a wait, the staff are very nice and the food is great!

I've been coming here with my girlfriend for the last 2 years and we've always been very happy with our meals.  Last night we got 3 dishes and drinks and the bill came out to just $30 and we had leftovers!

I almost feel bad reviewing Racha here because it should be kept the quasi-secret that it still is! Mmmmmmmmmm!

I was very pleased with my pineapple fried rice. 
I loved the yellow curry, the cashews, the raisins, the tomatoes, the pineapple, and the portion size. Sure they could've tossed in more pineapple or perhaps fresher pineapple, but for $6.95 it's understandable why they wouldn't. I know I couldn't make this dish myself, so I'm glad Racha Cafe is here to do it for me! It's not as good as some I've tried down in SoCal, but when you feel like pineapple fried rice I would definitely give Racha Cafe a go.

They also offer multiple other fried rice specials which all sound tempting (it was a toss b/t Pineapple fried rice and Duck fried rice, but JW got it to me before I could think twice!). They got you vegetarians and carnivores covered, all for decent prices.

I will say it's a little weird that each time I frequent this place it's empty..like completely empty. But that just means more attention from the server(s) I suppose. My party and I all received our dishes timely though not all at the same time.

I don't know if I'll return or plan on it...but if friends want to go somewhere close to campus and they feel like Asian, I'll suggest Racha and order some more fried rice. Yummm.

I'm sorry I hate thai food it all tastes the same to me. 

However, I think Racha Cafe is the most OK but I'm sorry I'm really not a Thai person.

I have tried a number of items on their menu and their curries are pretty good and their Pad Kee Moa is a good meal.

ENJOY!

Every Friday night a group of my friends and I like to go out to dinner after our weekly meditation sessions. As we were walking down the lovely streets of Berkeley on the hunt for a place to eat, a couple of the girls in our group started chanting "Racha! Racha! Racha!" There was really no point in arguing. Racha it was. We ended up in front of the Thai restaurant before we could even suggest another place. :)

The place definitely had its quirky Berkeley charm. The guy who seated us wore a big shirt that said "God Guns Disaster". Anyway our group consisted of... 13-16 people or so... and the host let us have our OWN room in the back with a huge, long table that stretched across. Immediately after seating they brought out glasses of water, silverware, and stood prepared to take our orders. We pretty much ordered everything on the vegetarian menu (we're all vegetarians), along with a some soups and a few thai iced teas here and there. 

Waiting for our food didn't take long. Everything came out at once, which was nice because everyone got to eat at the same time. Our food was delicious, simple, and very reasonably priced.

All in all, good times. Racha Racha Racha!

Great service, the food is delicious and come in very good sized portions, and the prices are more than reasonable. 

I would definitely recommend their green curry anything. It's pretty damn spicy, but the best kind of spicy. mmm nom nom nom

The spring rolls desperately needed the dipping sauce, as alone they were pretty tasteless.

3.5 Stars for tasty Thai Food.

I was having a major craving for Green curry. I don't get around to many Thai restaurants very much so, I was flying blind on which place to select in Berkeley since there are a bazillion of them scattered around.

I got Shrimp Green Curry and Pad Thai. They put plenty of shrimp in the curry and that was nice. They also add eggplant to the mix which gave it a trippy texture. I wish they served it with seitan, but they didn't. So, that sucked. So far, only place I've seen that does that is Your Place Thai on University, but they've started to suck for some reason so, I am boycotting that place.

The Pad Thai was pretty average and more greasy than I am used to, but it was good.

Not much more to say...it's a cool lil spot and it served its purpose.

I have a long history with this hole in the wall. The lighting is poor but it tends to get crowded with college students and people who work around the area. I've been coming here for lunch with my colleague and this time we both got the bbq chix with brown rice ($8 + change). While I thought the chicken was decent, I really enjoy the soft texture and taste of the brown rice. I'm not a big sauce fan but their sweet and sour sauce was better than many of the places I've visited. The previous times I've gotten their noodle soup and I thought that was just okay. Portions are modest, but it did a good job at filling me up. The server who works there is not always the most pleasant, but she is efficient and fast. I thought the food could be cheaper for something not as good as Siam Chan. 3 stars for being an adequate lunch spot.
dont hate. spam is delicious. the hawaiians eat it for thanksgiving

Bear Ramen is just a small, hole in the wall place, run primarily by a sweet little Korean woman and an assistant.  The gooksoo(noodles thicker than ramen, denser than udon)  is made fresh so the noodles are particularly good and the broth she uses is made from scratch.

Kim Chi Fried Noodle/Rice is probably the best dish on the menu. Incredibly addictive. The Champong (gooksoo noodles in broth with a variety of meat and vegetables) is also really good, however.

It's an ideal place for inexpensive, quick, casual meals. A quality place for poor, starving college students.

The food here is fresh and delicious.

Most importantly, the broth is delicious.  The noodles are made fresh all day long.  They are delicate and scrumptious.

The staff was friendly and welcoming.  As someone who often goes out to eat by himself, I often find that I get treated like I'm secondary to everything else the staff has going on with larger groups.  I did not feel that way at Bear's Ramen House.  Friendly conversation and a genuine smile came with my order.

Bear's Ramen House is a small, intimate little ramen house, authentic to the Korean style.

I will be going back next weekend.

If you ever eat here, you MUST try the kimchi fried rice. There ramen soups are pretty good too...although I know that I can easily make it at home now and put my own ingredients in it. The service here is great and fast since they're make your food right in front of you right after you order it. The place is a bit cramped up so if you choose to eat in groups, its better to eat outside. There is free water here, but the cups are so small..and the water wasn't cold..so I suggest buy a drink at the convenience store next to IB's.

There is an old lady who is really rude(uses INFORMAL Korean words to seemingly young Koreans), but rest of the workers are not.

well the biggest negative point of them is....FOODS ARE OVERPRICED.

This place goes into my fondest memory bank. Whether it was a cooler day at Berkeley or a nice sunny one, I never did NOT crave this place. Usually ordered rice cake and dumpling noodle soup. Although it wasn't on the meny wall, the patrons were always able to service made to order. And I loved it. And I loved that they eventually knew what I wanted. 

This place hit the spot in a way that no other spot did. Soup broth was always hot enough, tasty enough, and just the right amount of serving. I would come here atleast once a week or more just to find comfort in the broth and noodles. My home away from home. 

I remember the kindness of the owners, and recall when the wife was pregnant and still working... In such a small little hut, rain or shine, heat or cold, Bear Ramen was always around to serve.

Sometimes when I was in a hurry, I'd order the spicy kimchi spam fried rice, and that was on a class of it's own. I have yet to find a place that can make a fried rice of that calliber.

Until we meet again, I truly miss you ramen bear.
I had the beef ramen, which was flavorful and delicious.  I'd definitely go back again.

This place is cute. It's got the old country feel to it and it's pretty authentic I guess?

So why would I only give it a three? Because if I can make the same thing they make without costing me 6.50, you don't deserve my business.

So one day, I cooked Nong Shin instant noodle with Kimchi, some onion, bean sprout, egg and some fish cake and it tasted equally good. O, guess what? The whole thing only cost me $2.50 at most. What does this mean? OVER PRICED!

Oh yeah, fast food Korean style! The owners have switched 3-4 times but the quality of food has remained stable. The most current owner is a nice Korean lady who has been in the U.S. for a few years now.

+ Quick food, no matter what you order
+ Cleaner look than the previous owners
-  Don't order the veggie gyoza; too greasy and small portions
-  The free water here is kinda shady (out of a dirty ice cooler in a pint sized cup)

Final Call:
Southsiders with a ramen fix should find their way here.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Munchies:
1. Rice cake gook soo
     + Fresh rice cake and gook soo made on the spot
2. Kimchi fried rice
     + Tastes even better without the spam
3. What's up with the nasty complementary kimchi?

I've been coming here for a few years now, and I gotta say that this is probably the best ramen place in the east bay. Although the guys (and ladies) behind the counter have changed a few times over the years, the quality of their food has not changed one bit. 

The gooksoo, which is the ramen they make from scratch, is just the right consistency. The stock they serve it in tastes awesome, and isn't oversalted, which is what a lot of other places do. 

This place would be absolutely perfect if they got some more seats and started serving beer :)

So I felt like Ramen.  I know quality can be varied, but I'm flexible.  

This place serves INSTANT RAMEN NOODLES!  e.g. TOP RAMEN!  Give me a break.  for $6?  

I know this is a college town and there are lot of hungry students around.  But man, instant ramen noodles...shame on you!   

Irks me to no end that they use the word "Bear" in the name of the restaurant that serves such crap....

Go elsewhere.  Put this place out of business.  They don't deserve your money.

Does it taste good? Kind of...
Is it a rip off? YES!

The noodles are obviously pre-packaged instant noodles that will probably taste the same if not better if you bought it at an asian supermarket and cooked it yourself with the seasoning packet.

The kimchee fried rice is so simple to make... just watch them make it. You can definitely do that home with minimal ingredients or skill.

Bottom line: The food here tastes alright when you are on the run and craving for some korean-inspired dishes. But it is way overpriced for what it is. The next time I'm going to shell out over seven bucks for instant noodles, I might as well slap myself in the face and drive to ranch 99 for a 10 pack of shin-ramyun.

KIMCHI UDON SOUP WITH SHRIMP! KIMCHI FRIED RICE! I've died and gone to comfort-food HEAVEN!

Possibly under new management, don't let this spot in the college-kid-inundated "Asian Ghetto" fool you -- It's packed with flavor, charm, quality ingredients, and a beautiful, kind owner who'll make it JUST how you like it, and spice it to taste with a smile.

They're open late and in the best location near Telegraph to find parking.

I went here once and never went back.  This place is overpriced and not even mediocre (like the other restaurants in the asian ghetto).  If you are value minded, choose the thai place with their $4.50 lunch.  The noodles come from a package that looks like maruchan top ramen, the broth is not savory, and the appointments on the ramen aren't appetizing (chopped onions, fish cake, mushrooms).

Bottom-line: Don't bother eating here because the food is not good.  I prefer Gypsy cafe, Steve's Bar b q, the thai place (if im feeling cheap) or better yet, house of curries across the street.

With huge bowls of hot/spicy soup, pots of boiling water, one bustling chef, this cozy little nook is perfect on a winter day.  I've taken shelter in this steamy Ramen House many a time, and I have never been disappointed.  I recommend the Cal Gooksoo or the Champong Ramen.  Choose the ramen over the udon; it's nice and chewy.

One of the lesser populated eateries in the Asian Ghetto, it used to be one of my favorites.  I used to come here with a friend all the time for their curry rice.  The sauce was rich and tasty and the portion was very generous.  

I've also tried the kimchi fried rice and the curry ramen.  The kimchi fried rice was ok.  I'm not a huge kimchi fan so I don't think I can review it fairly but I found it to be too sour and too salty.  The curry ramen was good, but not good enough to get again.  The price of all the entrees is a little higher compared to the other restaurants in the area, but the cost seems justified when you see that it's just one little old Korean lady (who's very nice, btw) and sometimes another helper running the place.

I sort of stopped coming here after freshman year though because 1) I think they changed how they make the curry rice and 2) I discovered other eateries that became favorites for me.  Still, I do miss that curry and the quaint little ramen house.

A small and tiny place with delicious food and great prices. 
Kimchi fried rice w/ chicken ftmfw
mushroom chicken fried rice ftw
I love me sunny side up egg!

Kimchi Fried Rice is a winner. The owner of the shop is extremely nice (even giving me little dessert yogurt drinks when I came in late once, since I've been there enough for her to know me), as is her son.

Bear Ramen was kinda average. I think most of the Ramen is kind of average, though I haven't tried the Kimchi Ramen yet.
Black Bean Gook Soo looked great, wasn't all that great. Meat was sparse, and the radish was cut too thickly for my tastes.

That being said, since I almost always get the Kimchi Fried Rice, gonna go with a four. Without it, I'd probably rate it a 3. Then add one for the owner being awesome. Then possibly subtract one for one of the helpers always having a grumpy face :/

Seating a bit tiny, though you can always sit outside with the boombox guy in the background.
Their kitchen is small, but they have GREAT dishes. They know how to cook!

The Honest Truth: This place is pretty good.  Solid choice at Asian Ghetto.  The Kimchi fried rice is great.  Ironically the ramen isn't anything special.  I'd say the gooksoo is a better option.  The service is always good.

The Details:
I always enjoy coming to this place.  I always order the kimchi fried rice and I'm always satisfied.  However, there isn't much else I'll order.  The ramen isn't that great and I would rather make some instant noodles at home.  The Gooksoo is decent and the other thing I order is the spicy pork over rice.  The quality is typical Asian Ghetto quality, which isn't bad.  The price is around the same 6-7 dollar amount.  The workers are nice and they give you a fair amount of food.  Theres no place to eat inside, so get it to go and eat somewhere else!

You have to try their Kimchi Fried Rice with Spam!
You have to try their Kimchi Fried Noodle with Spam!

uh... just order something with the thumbs up next to it. lol my favorite Korean restaurant in Berkeley :)

How to make kimchi fried rice the ghetto way according to Lilly L. in only four easy steps!

1) Go to Korean market. 
2) Buy pork bulgogi.
3) Fry in pan with butter.   
4) Mix in rice, egg, maybe some MSG for real Asian authenticity and chemically-induced drowsiness?

I like this better. Makes me feel like a real cook :D. 

The rating is for the dish I had. The cute Korean cook/owner totally gets 5 stars for working so hard though!

I'm from Korea and there are a lot of places like this where they serve Korean noodles, fried rices, and other dishes

prolly the comparion is not fair, but everything's kinda pricy compared to similar restaurants back in korea
but i guess its reasonable for Berkeley

food is pretty good although i wish the portion is bigger since i eat a lot :p

and there are only about 6 seats so it is likely that you will have to sit outside.

I don't know how to make my own Ramen, so I think this place is a great.  Kim Chi (sp?) Ramen is my favorite.  Perfect comfort food, and they're fast and friendly.  Take out is a slight pain as you need to park - best to have one driver and one runner to pick up the food.  Pot stickers are decent too.

Definitely one of the better places in Asian Ghetto, their noodles are definitely one of the betters in the area. The woman who works here is pretty nice and is super beautiful and elegant for someone of her age. 

What I get here since I can't do spicy :(  :
Mushroom fried noodle - if you haven't tried this, get it! 
Mushroom fried rice

Extra noodles are only $1! :D

Notes: the noodles are hand pulled, so the quality can vary. Usually the noodles came out nice, decently thick, and chewy, but other times it can be suuuuper stretchy, sticks too much together, or a little on the thin side. Nevertheless, usually it pulls out to be SUPER good.

I give this place a four star because of their delicious food, price, and excellent customer service. Only had the kimchi fried rice (one of the best) and their ramen. The look of the ramen bowl is funny but I think it's cool. The broth was flavorful, but it needs more substance like corn and more meat! 

It's a small mom and pop show with very little sitting area, but a lot of seating outside. It's nice to eat outside and enjoy the atmosphere.

I've had the chicken ramen and it was honestly real ramen and not some instant noodle soup. I watched them make fresh pasta and make the soup from scratch with their spices and vegetables. Everything was so honest and fresh.

It's official - I'm addicted to the kimchi fried rice with spam. I ate it five times in the past week alone..At first I thought the spam made the dish too salty, but I tried it with tofu and couldn't taste anything. 

The prices aren't bad and the little Korean lady is adorable!

The noodles they use for the ramen here are the same exact noodles from the instant ramen packages.  Though the noodles are common, everything in the soup was excellent.  I had the "Beef Ramen" and the "Bear Special Ramen".  I can assure you that there are way better ramen places out ther.

One of the better korean restaurants in the Berkeley area. It's cash only, but definitely worth it! The first time I tried this place, I ended up coming back 3 more times in the same week. Get the kimchi fried noodles and kimchi fried rice. GO. NOW.
Kimchee Fried Noodles.  That is all.

I haven't been here in years, but it's not becuase it's not good.  I won't lie...there have been times I've been tempted to come back and get some of that kimchi fried rice!  I've heard the owners are have changed, but who cares if the food is just as good!  So many times I came here in my college days...and so many times, they didn't let me down one bit - such a better alternative to dorm food.  In fact, it probably helped make me what I am today....for better worse. =T
I tasted Kimchi fried rice there and it is really good. It is the first time I like something with Kimchi lol

Hands down best kimchee spam fried rice! And I always crave their kimchee rice cake ramen when I'm under the weather. I have been coming here for more than 12 years....and I'm definitely going to keep coming back for years to come. Love this place!!!!

Bear's Ramen House and I have a love/hate relationship.

I LOVE their kimchi fried rice with spam.
I LOVE their gooksu (when they don't run out).
I LOVE their prices.

I think they hate me, though, because I'm not Korean.  But I can live with that, I guess.
Kimchee Spam Fried Noodles!!!!!!

Noodles seem like they were from one of those packages from the grocery store. Broth really needed seasoning. But worst of all, the whole place and the food court it was in was one of the most filthy places I've ever seen.

The saving grace was the sweet smile from the gal who worked there.

Food not good!

KIMCHI FRIED RICE. One of my favorite dishes ever!!!

My typical order: Kimchi fried rice with spam, extra extra spicy with two eggs. (The extra egg is 50cents more but it is SO worth it.)

I usually call 10 minutes ahead to avoid waiting so long. I am so impatient when it comes to kimchi fried rice!!!!

Oh, and the mother and son who works here are always nice!
i always get the beef ramen because i figure this ramen must be healthier than that cup noodle ramen i would be getting from 99 ranch. it's not too expensive either and close to all the units.

love it
Spam and kimchi and rice together perfection
Curry ramen  yummy 
Homey and folksy 
one time I went there five drunk korean business men where singing a pop song and eating ramen very cool

Kimchi fried rice is really good here! However, I was very disappointed at how little spicy Korean rice cake I got in my order....that made me a little sad. It was delicious Korean rice cake...but...I seriously had like ten cakes in there. I don't know if she just hated me that day or what. 

Foods good, portion size that particular time I went was super bad...so I have some mixed feelings.
Get their kimchi spam fried rice or spicy rice cakes, you won't regret it.

Bear Ramen's food are really good, they don't suck. But it's not restaurant quality. Everything they make you can make at home. But that necessarily isn't a bad thing per say. I personally like homemade korean food, and they make everything homemade style. Their kimchi fried rice with spam is amazing, everyone comes here for that. 
It's not pricey either. If you want your homemade korean food fix, this is your spot. I came here yesterday to have lunch with my friend, the weather was hot and she felt like getting something cold, she ordered the nengmyun (cold noodle in soup). She was scared that it wasn't going to be great, because you can only get good nengmyun at certain restaurants that are known to make it good. But it ended up tasting better than she thought. I got the cheese ramen. I'm pretty sure my friend got sick of eating her nengmyun because she kept taking my ramen lol. The ramen soup isn't like the ones you would make at home, it's really good and more like broth. It costed around 6.50 which isn't too bad. 
You have the option of sitting outdoors or indoors. 

I think next time I'd stick with their kimchi spam fried rice. That's the one dish thats actually really worth it.

While Bear Ramen is overpriced for what it is, the food is delicious and the location is extremely convenient for Berkeley students. A nice big bowl of Rice Cake Ramen hits the spot on the cold, rainy days, and the Kimchi Fried Noodle is always a great dish. A personal favorite would also be Bulgogi Rice Cake Ramen, give it a try, it's not on the menu! The people who work there are always friendly, so chat them up!

the pictures of the food look good, but i can't get over the fact that the ramen is packaged as if you can purchase it from any korean grocery store and make it yourself at home. maybe i should get the kimchi fried rice next time... if there is one.

A small corner shop with a wonderfully kind owner, this is a convenient place to eat in Berkeley. The food here is humble and the ingredients are nothing special. But for college students or summer program students (as in my case last summer), it's a place of nostalgia where you can have some hearty and filling Korean comfort food.
kimchi fried rice!!! :D all my korean friends loooove it even though we could technically make it ourselves x]  the korean owner is soooo cute :)

I only come here for one thing... kimchi fried rice.

i live on this stuff. everytime i go to the asian ghetto, i come here 80% of the time for the kimchi fried rice. i always try to order something else, but in the end i tell the lady "kimchi fried rice w/ spam." even when i'm already super full, there's always room for this stuff!

i have recently tried the mushroom friend rice (only because my friend ordered it) and it is just as good.

food comes very fast too.

This place is just OKAY, especially when you're a hungry college student, but most of the time, I can't bring myself to come here unless forced. I've tried their kimchi fried rice, kimchi fried noodle, and mushroom fried noodle on multiple occasions, but this place is very inconsistent. One day, the kimchi fried noodles will be cooked perfectly and deliciously, and the next, oddly sweet yet at the same time, tasteless. I've had consistently better kimchi dishes elsewhere, so I will NOT be missing Bear Ramen when I graduate.

Can somebody please tell me where I can get a hefty serving of kimchi fried rice with spam & fried egg for $6 that is better than here? This would literally feed me for 3 meals... Actually, can someone just tell me where I can find this in the L.A. area??? If it wasn't for the cash factor (which annoyed me bc I never carry cash around) and the fact that I've never tried any other dish from here, I'd probably give it 5 stars.

i only come here for one thing. mushroom fried rice. 
tried their mushroom ramen the other day, not worth it. i could have made it myself. i feel like they just use those ramen packets -_____-
the owner is really nice though...she messed up on my order and redid it with a smile on her face =]

The owner there is super nice and friendly! The place is very small though, so you must get lucky to sit inside, or hunt for a seat outside in the court yard with the other bums and students, or you can take it to-go. The spam kimchi fried rice is the best with the fried egg on the top. They recently raised their prices but its still not that expensive. The noodle soups are pretty good too. If you can handle the spicy-ness of course.

My favorite place to eat at Asian Ghetto!!! I usually eat here when I'm pretty busy because the food comes out pretty quickly (except when it's packed on some nights). The Kimchi Fried Rice with Spam is the best!!! It's better than kimchi fried rice from any other place... it's better than my mom's (sorry mom). I don't know how they make it so tasty because it's so simple. I just wish they gave us more.
You should probably take it to go because there is not much space inside. They also don't take card here, so have cash ready.
3.5 stars

Yeah. So if you're in a mood for instant package ramen, this is the place. Quick, pretty inexpensive, fast. 

I don't know if you can tell from that but I wasn't too excited about their food. 

I think their saving grace is their kimchi fried rice (though I feel the portion size is pretty small for fried rice). It has a different flavor from any fried rice I've had before, has a nice little kick but still retains a little of the sweet taste from the kimchi. I don't think it makes much a difference what meat you get on top. 

Bottom line: if you're in the Asian ghetto, don't feel like waiting for Thai food or Gypsy's you can just grab the fried rice and go go go. 

OR you could just buy a few donuts and pig out as I have often done.

please note that this review is solely based on my experience with their KimChi Spam Rice. It's definitely, imo, the best item on their menu. Very filling and cooked perfectly. The rice was nicely separated and absorbed the flavors of the kimchi paste. It was great that the kimchi was cut into small bite sized pieces

The own lady and one helper are the sole operators of the store. I always am awed by how efficient they are because orders come out quickly. I have heard however that their ramen are not great, which makes me not understand the store's name if their ramen is just from instant ramen. 

So when you come, mainly try to kimchi spam fried rice. The mushroom one is good too

This very tiny hole in the wall makes very good ramens. I had the beef ramen and it was good, although I wished there were more food! The service was friendly, but the service wasnt fast. I came here on a thursday night and it was pretty busy. If you eat inside the place, goodluck because it is very tiny with limited seats and room. Also had the potstickers, which were awesome

Okay, maybe the food at Bear Ramen is not the greatest quality, but it's pretty delicious and Bear Ramen is my favorite place for comfort food (hello, kimchi fried rice with spam). It's also the only decent Korean place within walking distance of the UC Berkeley campus. 

The ramen is good, but I'm not enthused about spending $6 for ramen that has maybe one slice of meat, so I've stopped getting it. I love kimchi fried rice - spam and beef are both good. I kind of want to try the tofu one too (does anyone know if it's any good?). They also have surprisingly good fried potstickers. The lady (ahjuma??) is very nice too, and out of all the people who work there, makes the best fried rice and is the quickest.

I just wish they took credit card because there have been too many times that I couldn't buy Bear Ramen because I didn't have cash and no Chase ATM to run to. I don't recommend calling in your order ahead of time because in my experience they forget to turn their phone on quite often. And I wish they stayed open just a littlee bit later. !!!

This is seriously the worst noodle restaurant i've ever been. I ordered a "Kimchi Ramen." This is what they did: 1) took an instant ramen 2) boil it 3) add instant ramen seasoning 3) serve it in a bowl 4) put kimchi on top. All for $6. Wow!

#21 Kimchee GookSoo forever. Seriously, I've been coming here for 8 years and I always get the same thing. Their noodles are homemade meaning they are super fresh and have great chewy texture. The broth is spicy and a great cure for any ailment.  If you can snag a seat at the counter you're in heaven.

My favorite dish from this place is the Korean pancake. I usually ask for a vegetable pancake instead of kimchi or seafood since I'm a vegetarian and they're very willing to make it for me! :) The other dishes are alright, not the best I've had, and some are a bit overpriced. The place is open late, so I come at night if I'm craving a Korean snack.

get the kim chi fried noodle or the kim chi fried rice. SOSOOSOSOOO good!

ok, thinking about it is making me drool,MUST go there. the kim chi fried noodle is sooo bomb!

I used to come here a lot as a sophomore in college, but later just visited when I was craving their Kimchi Fried Noodle or Rice. The owner of the store is really nice and remembers you if you go a lot! Since I first came, she has hired a few more people. This is definitely one of the better places in Asian Ghetto. Besides the Kimchi Fried Rice with spam, I would recommend trying the Spicy Pork over rice too! The duk boki with ramen is good, but comes with maybe six pieces of rice cake max.
For those of you who like spicy stuff, their kimchi ramen with extra red chili powder can make even the most seasoned spicy food lover cry...tears of glory.
I ordered the potsticker ramen, it tasted ok, but come on it is only instant noodle. Even the curry are prepackaged curry. I won't be coming back again for something that I can make at home.

surrogate after-finals mother, 
kind, korean, cooking,
consoling with palettes 
of sauced carbohydrates 
and steaming meat broth

how did you know,
to put American cheese in my ramen?
A mother's intuition.

she hands me home 
in a plate of kimchi fried rice, 
supplicant cubes of spam,
smiling egg speckled with sesame,
lovingly?

"$7.95" 
I pay for my meal,
You are not my mother. 
But your meals taste so homey, 
(although a little greasy)
and all these asian youth, 
huddled hungrily about their steaming 
bowls of consolation 
look like me
The kimchi fried rice always made for a perfect dinner. Owners are super friendly and kind.

After a quick tour of UCB, my friend guided us over to Telegraph.  We walked around area and she mentioned a section called, "Asian Ghetto."  At first I couldn't stop laughing at the strange reference but she assured me that there's a lot of good places to eat in there.  So, we decided to check it out.  The small strip consists of various Asian foods as well as the random donut, Greek, & Italian restaurants.  The fact that all the selections looked like local mom & pop shops really hit home.  

While waiting for some friends to come meet up for dinner, I couldn't help but notice the pictures in front of Bear's Ramen House.  My friend told me that they're famous for their Kimchi Fried Rice.  Intrigued, my friends and I all ordered the fried rice (without the butter).  So good!!  The flavor was just right-not too salty, spicy, or oily (well, maybe just a tad).  If you're nostalgic for some home cooked food, come satisfy your tummy with this amazing goodness!  Plus, the friendly lady their smiles so much, it makes you feel like you're right in your own mama's kitchen (:

This place, as well as all the other eateries on Telegraph, makes me jealous that I didn't have all this accessible to me when I was in college :(

Sorry to spoil the party......but I had to try the place....given  my Cal alumni connection and the rave reviews, especially of the Kimchi Fried Rice with Spam dish.

Being of Asian extraction, and having traveled around the US and Asia sampling fare from China, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia, I have had some experience in gorging on some good grub.....and some of it dirt cheap.

Unfortunately.....this little hole-in-the-wall joint, unlike others of its ilk, didn't quite live up to its hype.

The "famous" fried rice dish was unexceptional.......underspiced, lumpy, and small portioned, both in size and ingredients (spam and kimchi).  The best thing was the properly prepared runny fried egg on top.

With tip, the dish ran me a quarter shy of $9......and left me hungry and disappointed, in search of more food.

Although I love supporting little mom-and-pop places, I cannot truthfully say that I will be back here again (granted that the older Korean lady/proprietor was not present on my visit).

For your hard-earned dollars.....I know you can do better.

Sorry......but our fellow Yelpers deserve candor and guidance!

Kimchi fried rice with tofu whenever I was hungry. 
Fishcake gooksoo when I wasn't feeling well. 
Doobukee because there wasn't another place in walking distance to get it.

Kimchi fried rice was ehh..ok, but the egg that came with it tasted like I could get food poisoning from it the next day. But their ramen is basically instant noodle cooked with some vegetables and egg, something I can prepare myself any time within like 5 minutes. Simply go elsewhere if you want something edible and with....more substance.

There's nothing like a steaming hot bowl of shrimp gooksoo noodle soup from Bear's Ramen House on a cold Berkeley day.  Bear's Ramen House is a tiny hole in the wall restaurant that is known for their ramen.  The soups are cheap and good and warm the soul like little else.

I heart my steaming hot noodle soups!  Nothing beats going here for a quick eat when Berkeley's horrible rainy cold weather ruins your mood to venture far away from campus for food.

Beware that since ramen bowls are quick and simple dishes, you get what you order, nothing more.  If you're a decent cook, you can definitely learn to cook them in the comfort of your own apartment, but if you're lazy or on a time crunch, this is the place to go.  Price is a little steep for ramen, but still pretty cheap.

I've tried many of their ramen bowls and they're overall pretty ok.  Haven't come across a ramen bowl that screams "must eat me" or "you will regret having me"

I've eaten here many times when I was in Berkeley. It was their kimchi fried rice and noodle dishes that kept me coming back again and again. I've tried these dishes with several different choices of meat and found beef and spam to work well with them. Though not as good as their fried rice and noodle dishes, their ramen tastes pretty good. In addition to their great food, there's a warm family atmosphere created by the presence of the cooks who are mostly part of the same family. I, like some other reviewers, find the Korean lady very nice and welcoming.

Not too shabby of a place to fulfill a craving for Korean food...

I was hungry and had run out of groceries to do any cooking in my apt so I decided to wander over to the Asian Plaza and see what was available for lunch. I checked out all the other fine establishments and settled on Bear's Ramen House since they had  Jjam Pong (spicy seafood soup) which I had been craving for the past few days. 

I walked in and placed my order for "dine-in" and sat down at the counter ready to eat. The cook took my order and then started preparing my food which only took minutes to prepare. Sweet.

Overall, my jjam pong wasn't the greatest, but it wasn't horrible. I really like the consistency of the noodles, but the broth which is what usually makes jjam pong so awesome to me was pretty watery and flavorless. It tasted like water mixed with that powder stuff from nong shim's spicy ramen. Ok...maybe not that bad, but still, it didn't quite hit the spot for me.

Overall, this place was a good find and I'll definitely be back to try some other dishes and satiate my desire for Korean food. I don't think I'll ever find any GREAT Korean food in the Bay Area though. Being from SoCal, I am spoiled with great and cheap Korean food. All is well though! There is plenty of other great find to try and discover in the Bay. =]

If it wasn't for Bear Ramen, I swear Asian Ghetto would suck even more than it does. 

My favorite dish is there the Kim Chi Fried Noodles w/ Shrimp (because I don't eat meat) but I'm  pretty sure it's more delicious with Spam!  I used to always order Kim Chi Fried Rice until my friend told me to try the noodles. Two words. LIFE. CHANGING. I can't go back to the rice again.  The noodles just soak in the kim chi flavor better than the rice. If you end up with leftovers, it's even better the next day! 

The only thing I wish that's better about this place is that he portion should be bigger. The portion are average but it's definitely not as filling if you're hungry. This place is definitely too small inside so I don't recommend that you should eat there. TAKE OUT IS THE WAY TO GO. The flavors also varies each time I buy it depending on who makes my food. If they're in a rush with a lot of people, they don't spend as much time frying the rice or noodles.

Seriously, I love this place. During lunch and dinner hours there will usually be a wait here because only the woman and maybe one other person will be working. That being said, I definitely do NOT mind waiting for a few extra minutes to get my Kimchi Fried Noodle. In college, my roommate and I would come here once every 1-2 weeks to get our fix of this dish and while we waited, we would cross over to Quickly's to get a drink to go with dinner (Me, a jasmine milk green tea, no pearls. Her, a regular pearl milk tea). Nothing beats this combo. 

After graduating, I realized that the thing I missed most about Berkeley was the Kimchi Fried Noodle at Bear Ramen. Honestly, it's the best thing ever and I literally feel myself craving for it at least once a week. The noodles are really "Q" (I'm not sure how to say this in English...) and the amount of kimchi plus the level of spice is just perfect for me.
