I usually get it with spam but you're free to substitute it with beef, chicken, or pork. 

The kimchi fried rice is amazing too but I personally like noodles better. Their ramen is pretty good too although the ramen noodles are closer to your typical cup noodle ramen (Korean style) not the Japanese style ramen. I really like their ddeokbokki (spicy Korean rice cakes) too but be prepared to take the heat (or ask her to use less spice). 

Also, don't plan on eating here. The place is insanely small and there are always students waiting for their food there. It's nicer to bring your food back to your dorm or apartment and eat while watching a good show. Best of all, if you don't finish your kimchi fried noodle, microwave it the next day and it's delicious all over again! Utter greatness. I miss this place so much.

This place is the hole in the wall restaurant, along with most other restaurants in Asian Ghetto (not PC, but that's what I call it).  Anyways, I come here for the kim chi fried rice, what they're most known for.  I had the ramen once, and it wasn't anything special.  I also recommend trying the kim chi fried squid over rice (kim chi oh-jin-oh bokum?).

The place is run by a nice Korean lady with whatever helper she has at the time.  She cooks the food as she receives the order, so it can take a while if they're a few people waiting in line.  Not a lot of seats inside, but you can also sit on the benches outside.

The prices are fair and the portions will leave you content.

Kimchee Fried Rice with spam and Kimchee Ramen. 
A cheap kimchee fix you can't argue with.
Prices are a bit much but the beef ramen is pretty decent (even if the ramen looks a bit "instant").

To all ramen gurus out there: don't get the ramen if you are craving japanese ramen. I love their kimchi fried rice and the kimchi fried noodles, but you know you gotta watch yourself when you like the rice better than the ramen at a place with "ramen" in its name. that's all i'm sayin. So its a great place to eat, except don't be midled by the name.

Got beef ramen from here and was very disappointed. I could make better ramen at home. I only give it 2 stars because the servers here were really nice. Other than that the quality of the food itself.. well lets just say I'd prefer to buy and make my own ramen. If college students don't have the time to cook, are lazy, and are craving ramen, I suppose this is a decent place to go to.
Rarely does the Korean in me crave Korean food, but when it does I always come here for hot noodle soup! I get either kimchi ramen or champong gooksoo. This place is my number one comfort food stop.

The food here is super delicious and I go so often that the lady knows exactly what I want! I get the kimchi fried rice with spam, and I also really like the ramen. It's a really small place, so if you go with a group, you should plan to get take-out.

At all hours of the day (and night), I could always rely on Kimchi Fried Rice for a solid dish. Toss in some spam and throw a fried egg on top and you have a winner. Prices are great for students (and non-students).

If you're at Asian Ghetto and can't figure where to go among the mass of stores, you can always count on this place for a great meal. 

5 stars

This was my favorite restaurant when I lived in Berkeley. 

I started out getting the Kimchee Spam Fried Rice (YUM!) but started getting the Kimchee Spam Fried Noodles (EVEN MORE YUM!) when it first became available.  

I went back last December to eat at Bear Ramen, and I must say that this place has gone progressively downhill. Dont get me wrong...it's still very good, but it used to be better.

I went in here to order kimchee ramen and I got some instant ramen noodles heated up in boiling water, with ramen, cut vegetables, and what looked like a big heaping scoop of msg or some kind of spices powder. I was thinking, I've never seen headaches measured out in tablespoons before. At least it was quick.

The location is super convenient for Berkeley students. It is in a small food mall with a bunch of Asian restaurants and a donut shop. The place has no table inside, just two counters with about 8 seats and you can watch the cooks prepare your food (that's a plus). The fried rice dishes looked good and the big udon pot looked ok. But instant ramen? No thanks. Wish I had known that before ordering.
I ordered the ramen with the potstickets...cept there were no potstickers when I got it. Boo. :(

Seriously small portions, very average taste and regular price? Not sure what all the hype is about. I had the kimchi fried rice and it didn't even fill half of the container! It looked like someone ate half of it. Really slow service, small portions, average taste, and average prices, definitely stay away!

this place probably serves the best korean food near campus. you can tell when there's a lot of koreans eating there and i happen to be one of them as i often eat there for a quick and cheap meal. i've noticed that most of the customers order the kimchi fried rice w/ spam and that was what i had my first time. however, i would like to ask you guys to please try other variations because they are even better!! i've tried kimchi fried rice w/ pork belly(much like bacon), squid, and shrimp and they were all so good. it costs less than a dollar more so give it a try. they also have other great korean dishes such as dumpling soup, dduk-gook, Cal gook-su, etc. so if you're not into spicy food, you have other options. the owner is very friendly and greets you with a smile so that's a plus.
studio nights, when i want to feel like i am at home-- kimchee fried rice, vegetable ramen or bear ramen will fixate the situation. thank you for being in the asian ghetto.

A fascinating experience, sort of like stepping off of the real world into the psychidelic Cal campus/Telegraph, only to step further into a rabbit hole that has the size/smell/look of a Japanese alcove.  Food is made to order, very reasonably priced, and quite fulfilling in a cold day.  Nothing fancy, but respectfully large menu.  The two ladies ran the tiny restaurant with military precision, with the fried rice stirred approximaely 20 times (I counted, could have find a reasonable average with standard deviation had I stayed longer).  I can see how many would become regulars, I would have.

"Kimchi fried noodles w/ spam (extra spicy please!)"

^ my typical order when I go in...once a week...

...need I say more?

Solely based on the Kimchi fried rice with spam I am giving this place a 3.5 and generously rounding up. I wish it had more green onion. I fried up two more eggs which helped round out the saltiness. I also added a generous dose of sriacha which it needed. With my enhancements, I would give it four stars as far as asian comfort food goes.

I love Bear's Ramen House for a variety of reasons: 

1) The food: delicious! A good variety of dishes--rice plates, fried rice, ramen noodles, ramen soup. Some of my favorites are easily the kim chi spam fried rice, kim chi ramen, curry ramen, and curry rice! 
2) The late hours: much like the rest of Asian ghetto, Bear's Ramen House is open pretty late if you're craving some warm noodle soup in the cold!
3) The atmosphere: I love that you can sit on the bar stools, watch your food being made, and eat it while it's still hot! The place is tiny, but oh so cozy.
4) The workers: the woman (owner?) is always very friendly and quick in getting your order made.

Korean Mama's as I like to call it.
The Korean mom who owns this place is so cute and nice I can't help it but fork over my 7.25$ for my plate of kimchi fried rice I could have made myself.

It might be a bit over priced, but on the days that I am craving Korean food, I like to come here. Though you don't get a super big portion, all the dishes there are quite excellent in taste. I've always liked all of their kimchi-fried-anything. Kimchi fried rice, kimchi fried noodle... mushroom fried rice...

The kimchi ramen is not worth the money though. They use instant ramen type noodles, and there's not even a lot of kimchi or vegetables in it. Can get it if you're desperately craving kimchi ramen but can't make it yourself.

Led on by all the hype behind the kimchi rice with spam, i decided to grab an order for lunch.  I've had better back in LA, but it wasn't bad.  The spam to rice ratio was good and the fried egg on top complimented the dish well.  However, I don't think it's worth $7.50.  On the bright side the cashier is nice and the food came out quickly.

kimchee fried rice w/ spam!!!!

mushroom fried rice!!!

I'm in heaven... they're just so yummy.

*reminiscing the good ol' berkeley days...*

Sooo good, especially after a bad day. I've only tried the ja ja noodles and kimchi fried rice with spam, so I have yet to try the soups and other things on the menu.

Bear's Ramen House pro's:
-hole in the wall restaurant with an authentic, homey feel
-really nice service
-deeelicious!!

So why did I only give it 4 stars?
- a little pricey (~$7 for rice/spam/kimchi)
- slow (they start cooking after you order)
I should've heeded the warnings of the reviews. This was not real ramen. It was noodles out of a bag and the broth was not flavorful. It only gets two stars for its convenient location.
This place has a nice homey feel and the owners are very friendly.  Come for the kim-chi fried rice with spam and two eggs which happens to be a staple for my college diet.  Ramen is just okay.

I like the availability of a quick bowl of ramen with lots of options, but why in the world would I pay someone 6$ to make it for me when that's probably all I'm eating at home anyway? The udon is more worthwhile but I always burn my tongue.
I came here for lunch and let me just say the spam kimchi fried rice (with an egg on top) is so delicious! (And this is coming from Korean so I know good SKFR when I taste it).

I used to love this place because of their kimchi friend rice. However the last time i went this Mexican lady cooked it and it was way too sweet and not enough salt and too much oil. They raised their price too so a fried rice is about $7 now, not really worth it.

I miss this Bear's ramens dearly after I left Berkeley...
awsome food (bear's special ramen, kimchi fried rice with spam (and that egg!), pineapple fried rice) for about $6.  The place is nice and cozy for a winter dinner study break.  I HAVE to come here everytime i visit berkeley!

Cheap pricing. I've only tried the ramen, which tasted like it came out of a package with meat thrown in it.  Very limited indoor seatings (maybe 2 by the cashier and 3 by the window). Self-served water by the door. Service wasn't that great, maybe because it was busy.

Next time, I'll try the highly recommended kimichi fried rice/noodles.

Love this place and try to hit it up anytime I am in Berkeley.  I first heard about it when a friend of a friend's boyfriend mentioned how much he loved their kimchi spam fried rice which is one of their most popular menu items.  I normally abhor spam but I do love me some kimchi so my interest was piqued.  I've tried it, it was delicious and I keep coming back for more - they are VERY generous with the portions, you definitely get your money's worth.  It's a pretty tiny place with room for maybe 5 at the front counter and 4 at the window but the service is quick and friendly.  They also have some interesting gook soos I'd like to try.  Great Korean comfort food at a great price.

Everyone suggests the kim chi fried rice here, and it did not disappoint. Ordered it to go on a sunny day and enjoyed it outdoors. Nothing quite like having the food warm your stomach while having the sun warm your skin.

We also got some fried noodle dish with mushroom, which was also delicious, albeit greasy.

I had the Mushroom Fried Noodle, which was REALLY good, but because there was so much flavor, it became really difficult to eat. I can imagine it would have been delicious as leftovers, but I was going to be out all day so I had to throw it all away. What a pity... The egg that came on my noodles was a little overcooked compared to everyone else's, so the consistency is a little off, but it's nothing major.

From what I've heard, even though this place is called "Bear's Ramen House," you should stay away from the ramen. Stick with the fried rice/noodle dishes and you'll have a yummy meal.

Ok so to be honest, I got ramen - the Bear's special or something like that - and didn't love it.  A lot of the dishes others were ordering looked better than what I got, so maybe I just got unlucky.

And the staff was so sweet and friendly, making sure everyone got what they wanted.  Note that you can call ahead orders and pick up so you don't have to wait.

I'll have to come back to try something different!

First off, yeah, there are better Korean restaurants out there. Get that out of the way. The place is not about "fine dining".  Think of Korean comfort food without the "uhhhhh, what is that? Am I supposed to eat it?" concerns.

What sets the horrendously-named "Bear's Ramen House" is that "ajima" (that's what she prefers to be called) runs a family-style noodle shop that specializes in a specific (but apparently growing) menu...noodles and fried rice dishes. I've always guessed that this is what an Asian roadside noodle stand must be like, all the way down to the seats that westerners can't possibly fit in (be prepared to bang your knees).

The gook soo (Yelp doesn't support Hangul) noodles are made fresh from scratch daily (not hand pulled, but cut...unfortunately, she doesn't make the noodles at ordering time any longer), the ingredients are basic and tasty, and the soups are quite good.

My personal favorites are the soo-jae-bi (su-jei-bi): hand-torn sheets of uncut gook soo pasta with a semi-mild clear vegetable soup, and the kimchee pancake. You'll probably prefer the fresh gook soo noodles over the standard ramen.

If you are a student going to the Asian Ghetto, buck the "Steve and Thai" late night trend and stop by ajima's place. Tell your friends that you'll be "over there". If you're a Cal fan (or otherwise frequent the south side), add ajima's place to the Top Dog/Gypsy/Bongo Burger/Naan-n-Curry rotation. If you're a "hipster", amaze your foodie friends with your diamond-in-the-rough find.  Don't go driving across the Bay Bridge to go there, but if you've already passed the "Entering Berkeley" warning signs and found parking, by all means try it out!

For you old-timers, this IS the original location of the various "Steve's Food Centers" (which eventually moved to the corner of the Asian Ghetto and became Mexi-rean). The "last Steve" converted it to a noodle stand. Ajima took it from there and ran with it.

3.5 stars. Went here for a late lunch. It's a cute small place with counter seats. I got the kimchi and rice cake ramen and the boy got the bears special ramen. Both were very tasty and the price was reasonable. The lady who works there is very cute and makes me want to take her home so she can cook for me. A lot of people seemed to have ordered the kimchi fried rice which I will have to try next time I go there but overall I was satisfied with my visit and if I happen to be in the area again I will definately hit this place up.

I've gotta say I love the lady who owns this shop. She has the biggest heart for all the kids who roll through. Don't judge when i say this, but she was like my surrogate Korean mama during my four years at UC Berkeley. Whenever i wanted some comfort food i would wander my way down Durant and she'd always offer a hot plate of home style korean food . There's a few other korean restaurants in Berkeley, but none as good as this one! If I find myself back in the Bay area I will definitely make it a point to visit and have a hot plate of kimchi fried rice!
This is how I am getting through graduate school.  3 words:  Homemade udon noodles.   This and lots and lots of coffee.

Sigh. This place used to be so good. Too bad it's going downhill with the quality of the food depending on who is cooking that day.

I always get the Kimchi Fried Rice w/ Spam. Either their portions are getting smaller or I'm just getting fatter and need more food because I can finish it and still want more after. After hearing several people tell me how good it was, I decided to spice up my order and get the Kimchi Fried Noodle instead. BAD DECISION. You would think it would taste the same as the rice version, right? WRONG. The sauce was completely different and the dish was SWEET. O____o Last time I listen to people. Psh.

Since this place is a "ramen house", I should probably come back and try their ramen one day.

AHHH BEAR RAMEN!  The best place to get ramen in Berkeley!

Not only is their ramen really good they also have a lot of other really yummy dishes.

At first impressions there isn't very many vegetarian options but you just need to talk to them and they can substitute items.

My favorite was the mushroom fried rice with the fried egg on top soooo good.  And the little Korean woman who works here is really cute.  

-1 star because the place is tiny and there is never room to sit inside and I never liked eating at the outside food court area.

Yum! I always get some form of ramen here and I love how:

A) It comes in its own "tupperware" container when you order to go
B) SO DELICIOUS
C) There is so much food that no matter how hungry I am, I cannot finish it all at once and always end up eating the remaining half for another meal
D) i see the same people working all the time (the korean lady who owns the place & the hispanic lady). they're always pretty friendly and they make my food fast!

Best kimchi spam fried rice in Berkeley!  You really can't go wrong ordering this, although they give WAY less than they used to.  Two years ago, I could make an order last two meals, and now it's barely enough for one.  Thank goodness I don't eat a lot, or I'd rate less. 

The kimchi's aged perfectly.  Honestly, it's not hard to make a decent plate of kimchi fried rice, but the difference between Bear Ramen and my kitchen is the kimchi.  Perfect crunch, perfect tang, perfect spice.  Makes the dish taste amaze.

The fried noodles are alright.  A little too heavy for me, and as others say, the quality's inconsistent.  Sometimes, it's Korean street food magic, and sometimes it's just a heaping dish of bland greasy carbs.  

And don't order the ramen.  Doesn't matter if the place has "ramen" in its name; just don't.  Go home, boil some canned chicken broth, toss in some veggies and fish cake and a block of packaged ramen, and top it off with a dash of msg and scallions.  Same exact thing, down to the brick of ramen.  So please do yourself a favor, and don't waste your precious monthly student allowance.

I'd avoid the place when it's crowded.  I'm pretty sure there's a negative correlation between the number of people in line and the quality and quantity of food per order.  Order take-out!  The seating inside's pretty dismal, but there's plenty of seating outside.  Also, they have complimentary roast rice tea, my fave(:

I've only tried the Kimchi Fried Rice with Spam and the Kimchi Ramen.
Both are pretty good. Friendly people that work here. The korean lady that works here is really nice. So were the 2 mexican ladies. Caught me off guard that there were 2 mexican ladies cooking the food while talking to each other in spanish and listening to salsa music. I thought I walked into the wrong restaurant for a minute.
Good food, decent price. I like the fact that they cook it right after you order instead of having a ready batch of noodles that have been sitting there all day.

Kimchi fried rice with Spam - 5 stars
Sujaebi - 2 stars
Lady in the back - 5 stars

Honestly, my fault for ordering something like Sujaebi at a place like that. Sujaebi is a soup made from seaweed and dried anchovy stock with lumps for flour mix. Almost like a Korean Gnocchi. The place was clearly a cheap fried rice and ramen kind of place and I was fool enough to order something that should only be ordered even at specialty places in LA's K-town with caution. 

I usually don't like Korean fried rice because... well, they use Korean rice and it's just too sticky for me when it comes to fried rice. It tends to come out greasy rather than soft and buttery like the way I like them. But Spam is a miracle meat that makes rice and kimchi come together like pb and j. Add an egg sunny side up and you got yourself a yolk covered treat of spicy, greasy, salty, and mellow all at the same time. There's also something that ruins kimchi fried rice, it's raw kimchi. The kimchi in fried rice should be fermented even longer than the kind you eat because the spices have to soak into the cabbage or else you'll get white cabbage in your rice. This place definitely uses aged kimchi but not so aged that it's sour. Good kimchi is hard to come by, so go here for real kimchi the way it should be. 

Also, I didn't have the ramen but I can tell just by looking at the kitchen that it'll be good because they prepare stock instead of using water. They know the secret to making Korean instant ramen taste like a real soup dish is a deeper stock and not just extra ingredients.

great for the price
huge portions
the lady is nice, very small place
im a vege, so i get the kimchi fried rice with tofu and extra kimchi
its like $7 and enough to feed you for 2 meals

never had the ramen though

I get the same thing every time I go here.  Kimchi fried rice w/ spam.  It's my absolute favorite dish on the menu.  The lady who runs the place is very nice, and I just love this little place.  I usually order to go and eat at outdoor tables.  The rice is so good, and I love kimchi.  Plus the fried egg on top is like the cherry on top of an ice cream sundae.  So perfect.  

Now that I think about it, I don't think I've ordered anything else except for the kimchi fried rice!  MMmm... my mouth is watering just thinkin' about it...!

Good soup, nice noodles, decent prices.  Very reminiscent of the low-rent ramen houses in old Tokyo.  I'd probably eat here for lunch a lot if I was local.

Side note, ordered the kimchi pancake and it never showed up.  Oh well.

cheap tasty korean food 

kimchee fried noodles with spam 
The noodles are machined pulled fresh which provides a very chewy but firm texture. The spiciness is just right not too hot not too bland. The sunny side fried egg adds an extra touch. 4/5

They only have 8 seats in the small room so getting to go is a better bet. All the dishes are under $9 and they also have self serve tea and water. I would come back just to try their other things or just get the kimchee noodles again.

PS ramen is packaged here so you can probably make it yourself at home. Get the rice or fried noodle instead.

GO BEARS!

Bear's Ramen has the most awesome spicy soup base and its cheap.  Come to think of it, I think most of its dishes tasted identical, yet I still come back for more.  Probably cuz most Ramen are Japanese styled and this is one of the few that is Korean styled.  

The place has limited seating so usually you have to sit outside and bring back the soup bowl after you are done.  On a cold day, the noodle soup warms you up almost instantaneously.  Too bad there isn't too much of a variety.

I'm not a big fan of the ramen here. And for a place that has it in the name, I expected a little bit more. And my dislike of kimchi pretty much disqualifies me from the highly praised kimchi fried rice, although their kimchi-free alternative wasn't terrible. But, I feel like I could get better fried rice at any of the other restaurants in the area too. I wanted to love you so much Bear's Ramen House, I loved the name, but there are just better options in close proximity.

Really cheap food - perfect for a poor student.

The best thing to order is the spam kimchi fried rice - if you're craving kimchi fried rice this is the place to go. It even comes with a sunny side up fried egg - ahhh everything I love about kimchi fried rice.

Ironically, I'd recommend staying away from the ramen. The broth isn't that tasty and the noodles are definitely packaged top ramen noodles - you can get that at home!

Seating is really limited both inside and out. If it's crowded, get it to go!

Yesterday was a pretty bad day, won't get into the specifics because we are talking food here but it was a real bad one.  Anyway, whenever I encounter a day like yesterday if I can I head on down to the Bear Ramen House and get some Curry GukSu Soup.  There isn't anything that can make me feel like I am being "held" like that soup...well I guess next to actually being held.  

This place is a hole in the wall, you can sit at the often crowded dingy counter and eat if you like or opt for the courtyard shared by neighboring restaurants...I usually schlep my soup home.  The broth is seasoned to perfection with just enough spice to pack a punch but not overpower the experience, the noodles are handmade and delicious.  The servings are huge and reasonably priced.

If you have a day that kicks you when your down, guaranteed, the Bear Ramen House will give you a nice warm hug.

So I had the curry ramen because my roommate was cooking curry in the apartment and it just smelled soooo gooood...

Bottom line: Bear Ramen's curry ramen stained my tongue, teeth, even toothbrush yellow.

Whitening strips! I need whitening strips!!!!!!!!!!!

...but it was pretty good though. very thick and probably very fattening... with only-god-knows-what kinda food coloring.

mushroom fried rice is pretty good too, but I could probably make it myself at home.

This place sucks asss... Don't go here.. they serve instant ramen.  

Hahah.. check out Lois S. review on this restaurant.  She said, they do not use msg but they use the instant powder soup from the ramen.  HELLO!!  that IS MSG..  Another reason why a lot of reviews are so misleading.. People don't know what they are talking about!!! Oh! the idiots you find on this site!

Quality and overall deliciousness has worsened in the past two years, preventing me from returning to Bear Ramen. If you have a sensitive stomach and fear food poisoning or salmonella, beware!

I used to come all the time for their kimchee fried noodle. However, the more I ate here the less I liked it; the noodles are more than chewy...they are gooey, and the sunny side up egg is undercooked and also soft and gooey. The taste of the food is okay (though the smell isn't appetizing) Their ramen is just soup plus packaged ramen, and the spam is from a can and too salty. The prices are cheap, most items are around $7

NOTE: This food is NOT good for curing hangovers. The pungent smell and gooeyness will make you sicker!
NOTE: If you have a low tolerance for food poisoning, food will make you sicker regardless of hangover or lack of hangover

Service is pretty slow since there are only two ladies working in the shop. Once I had to wait 20+ minutes because they ran out of noodles and had to stick new dough into the noodle-machine.  Said two ladies also handle cash register money (cash only!) while simultaneously handling food. The restaurant is cramped with very limited seating and isn't very clean at all. 

WILL I come back: Yes, but only once for old times sake
WHEN will I come back: Actually...no I wouldn't come back
WHY not: I don't want to risk getting food poisoning or salmonella

It was a rainy day and the second I walked in the Winter Sonata theme came on in the background.  No joke.  At that moment I knew what it felt like to be in a KDrama and be beautiful.

Also, the kimchi fried rice is delicious.

This is a very nice, tiny restaurant.  I come here all the time, usually settling on the mushroom fried rice.  Sometimes while I wait the owner gives me free gyoza.

Unfortunately, I can never go back to this restaurant...  I asked for her to make my food VERY MILD instead of HOT.  Through some miscommunication (she does not speak English very well) the owner got the idea that I am into spicy food and that she should make my food hellishly spicy.  I had to politely eat the food while holding back tears.  Now whenever I go in, she throws extra hot sauce on my food.

I really need to get someone to teach my how to say "Your food is delicious but the hot sauce is killing me!" in Korean.

Kimchi fried rice is good here but the service kind of sucks... :( I once ordered noodles and I realized last minute I forgot to ask for them to-go so I told her I wanted it to go (before she put my noodles in a bowl!) and she made this exasperated sound and gave me a look :( and I was like sorry Korean mama... also the noodle soups here are reallly bland and I asked to add fish cake once and the Mexican lady cooking gave me 1 piece....great.

OK, here's the incident that finally motivated me to register on Yelp:

Today I ordered the kimchi and SPAM fried rice to go. It sets you back $6.95 for a reasonable--but by no means large--portion of red-colored, greasy-with-chili-oil, fried rice that fills 75% of a plastic clamshell container. They top it off with a sunny-side-up egg. I'd ordered it twice before because it's nice and warm (they cook it fresh to order) and has a unique taste. It's a little too salty and greasy, and probably has lots of MSG for the umami flavor (not that there's anything wrong with that), and it's moister than I am accustomed to for fried rice, but it's not bad.

I am eating the fried rice in my room. I put another spoonful of rice in my mouth and... CRRRUNNCH. Yuck, it feels like I've just bitten an eggshell. I spit out what's in my mouth and dissect the unpleasant half-chewed bolus of rice, spam, and wilted pickled cabbage. And so what was the culprit? Not an eggshell. GRIT. No, I am not kidding. There were two hard, white-and-brown pebbles in my rice, like alluvium from a river, a little bit smaller than grains of rice. GRIT. IN MY FOOD. No, not stale rice, GRIT!

So I am never going back there again. (Automatic 1-star for grit. Would've given a 3 otherwise.) Oh, and like Karen says below, the value you're getting is pretty shaky for almost $7--mostly rice, one egg, a few chunks of SPAM, some kimchi.

I graduated in 2006, but everytime I go back to Berkeley, I HAVE to make a trip to Bear's to say hello to the owner and order the kimchi fried rice with spam. He even knows to make mine extra spicy, yum! I'm getting hungry just thinking about eating the runny egg yolk on top of the rice. The dish is big enough to serve two people or eat for two meals, for just $6. The jjeol myeon is tasty too, especially during the summer. I would not recommend getting the ramen here even though it is called a ramen house, but if you know what is good on the menu you can feed yourself for a day or two on the cheap.

I thought this was Japanese at first but then realized it was Korean after the language that they spoke.  Located in Berkeley's Asian Ghetto, this isn't the big GO-TO place.  I came here for dinner and the fish cake ramen was pretty good.  I would have given it a 4 star, but I told them no bean sprouts in my ramen!  Considering I was the only person there that ordered at that time and that they asked me if I wanted bean sprouts a second time, they couldn't even remember that I didn't want it at all.  -____- About $6 for a ramen dinner.  It was kind of a small portion so if you're hungry, you should go for something bigger!  I wasn't too hungry and the portion was just right.  It was a little bit spicy, too!

When this place first came out, I was really excited because I get to eat ramen. But that excitement only lasted for a while until the service got really bad. I always get ignored when I try to order. When I ordered fried rice with spam, what I got was fried rice without spam, and when I complain, the lady was fighting me that I said no spam. 

The ramen was okay because it's just instant ramen that I could get from the asian markets. The fried rices were good, as I remember. The seating is super duper tiny but whatever, you can sit outside if it's not raining.

Bear's Ramen House offers korean food at a cheap price. but you (almost) get what you paid for. only 2 benches for seating inside. common area outside has more seating.

menu: udon,  ramen, stir fry, and soups, rice cakes

eats: mushroom ramen(6.5)
-ramen still chewy, not totally cooked
-came with sliced mushrooms, seaweed, bean sprouts, slice of gluten, etc. 
-broth kind of tasty, had cooking wine, salt, pepper, msg, and a little chilie pepper.
1.5 stars saw a couple squirts from bottle, and a few pinches from condiment pans.

banchan:
-ramen is instant (jin ramyon)
-cooked to order on stove (open kitchen, kind of).
-learned how to cook ramen today, now i can do my own.
-for what one gets, fresh and all, seems overpriced.

I smh. For $7.50 at asian ghetto I expect a big portion but I was sadly disappointed. I was able to finish all of my Kim chi Fried rice and was still not full. It was yummy though but I wish I got a little more for what I paid for. 

My friend ordered the kim chi fried noodle which I would expect to taste the same as the kimchi fried rice... but it didnt. It was too sweet. o__O It was not good. 

The wait for your food is pretty long and it's usually always busy.

I absolutely love this place and the woman that owns it. Everytime we come in, she recognizes us and says hi. Being a fan of soups, I come here around every other day in the winters to order the gooksoo or ramen dishes. The kimchi fried rice is definitely one of the best dishes; I would eat it more often but I'm a real wimp with even mildly spicy food. The atmosphere here is great too, because it feels home-y and is a nice place to relax before heading off to study for a midterm.
I ordered chicken ramen to go... really quite disappointing. Not much to review - hot water on 3 tiny pieces of tough chicken and instant noodles with a few bland spices. For $6.50 it was poor value.

The ramen served here is from the 30cent packs you can get at the grocery store, Top Ramen style, no joke.

After realizing we'd have to stand in line for 30min for a piece of sushi at the Yelp event, Sunset Showdown or something (which sucked by the way), we drove to Berkeley for dinner. I'm pretty big on ramen and have tried all the major spots in SF and Peninsula, so naturally I got the kimchi ramen. Boy got the kimchi fried rice with spam. As I sat there, I literally watched as one of the ladies took a cube of dry ramen and put it in a pot of boiling water. Even the flavoring tasted like packaged ramen. At least they added some kimchi, bean sprouts and scallions? Buuut that does not make the $5.20 difference between what we paid and what I could have gotten at the store. The kimchi fried rice was aite but I've definitely had better. 

So...no thanks!

Compared to all the other Korean places in Berkeley, this place ranks close to the top. 

Granted, that's not saying much -_-;

The JA JA mein here is really good.  This was my 4th or 5th time eating this dish from array of places and so far this is the best one i've eaten.  We ordered 5 different dishes and everyone basically shared.  I basically caught multiple STDs and made out with all their boyfriends.  It was AWESOME!  The kimchi fried rice was the rave but I thought it was alright.  The fried rice needed some more fried.  It was too soggy for my taste.  I like it crispy almost like bi bim bap.  The kimchi pancake was also alright.  The star was obviously the ja ja mein and in second place was hand pull noddles in soup broth.  I am trying to think of the 5th dish but i dont remember.  It must have been that good.    I need to pick up my herpes prescription now.

Pretty good Korean restaurant to go to for a very cheap price. The Korean lady who owns this place is really friendly and engages with a lot of her customers while they're waiting for their food. 

I had their ddukbokki, which, IMO, isn't the best I had. (Go to Cafe Expresso for that!) I was really disappointed because everything else that I tried at Bear Ramen was good. Also tried their Curry Rice (yummmm) and Kimchi Fried Noodles (so goodddd). 

The downside: they only accept cash and the place is extremely tiny! It gets quite crowded sometimes.

Don't be fooled by the word "Ramen". It is not ramen, but rather, cup noodles with a tiny bit of shredded beef, bean sprouts and green onion.

Such noodle costs less than a dollar from the Asian supermarket. At this place, they put in some pathetic portion of meat and veggie, it suddenly costs $4. Enough said. 

Oh btw, they actually used the fatty part of bacon to fry stuff. When I looked at the way their food was prepared, I felt like eating here was so unhealthy that it was near suicidal.

I like this place. =) The owner is a really nice Korean lady and she's always there whenever I go. Makes you feel like you're getting good home-cooked Korean mom food. Except I don't even know her haha.

I've had the rice cake ramen soup, kimchi fried rice w/ spam, kimchi fried udon noodle w/ spam (same as kimchi fried rice, but with udon for another 50 cents or something), and some other dishes here. I haven't tried the bear ramen yet though. I think kimchi fried rice is probably their most popular dish. I like it, but definitely could not eat that too often haha.

I like the food here, but my only complaints are:
1. Slow - since she makes each dish as you order, it can be pretty slow getting your order even when it's not busy (I can't imagine what it's like when it IS busy). Sometimes she has an assistant so they can do several dishes at once, but yeah...this is not a place to go if you're really in a hurry.

2. Expensive - well, everything in Asian Ghetto is on the expensive side for the quality/quantity, in my opinion. But then again I might just be a really frugal Asian.

At Asian Ghetto, it's almost always either Thai Basil or Bear's Ramen House for me. =)

Instant Ramen + Egg + Green Onion = $7?!?!?!?!?!

For a "ramen" place, the quality of ramen sure is subpar.

I'm only giving three stars because some of the food
here, my friends swear, are good. But if it had to
come down to ramen only, I would only give this place
1.5 stars.

This review is only for their KIMCHI FRIED RICE.

THIS PLACE IS CASH ONLY!! (there's a BOA atm 1 minute away)

ATMOSPHERE
Located in the "Asian Ghetto," it's a tiny place with barely enough seating inside. However, you can always take your food outside to the benches/tables in the courtyard (although I strongly advise against this because the tables are eternally oily and gross. Stay inside if you can).

The cashier lady is Korean and speaks very little English, but strangely enough, the cooks are Mexican...

FOOD
Again, I only come here for the KIMCHI FRIED RICE, which is great 95% of the time. The other 5% it's a little burnt and when it's burnt I just can't eat more than 2 bites of it.

This place probably has the best kimchi fried rice in Berkeley and a lot of my Korean friends come here for other dishes as well considering there aren't many good Korean restaurants near campus.

The portions are big and you see them cook it right in front of you, so that's a plus. You can get the fried rice with either SPAM, CHICKEN, OR BEEF. I get beef because god knows what's in spam, but my friends always get it with spam.

TIP: Come with a KOREAN because you can get extra stuff, like extra sunny side up eggs with your fried rice.

I hate places like this and this place-. Why? 

I am on a recent Ramen fix---tried Santa Ramen in San Mateo finally, and while not perfect, it was damn near with Miso broth that has me chasing the dragon. 

So today I was dead set on Ramen from here, I tried Ryowa a few days ago and found it OK, nothing great, not terrible. 

Things started out nice, I found parking on Durant, on my way to the entry there was a semi-attractive female street type person sunbathing on the sidewalk in her bra-----

I walk in and there were several cues I should have walked out before ordering.....the lady/owner? was on the phone---while on the phone she was coughing, a lot. She finally ended her call and continued to cough up a lung. Rule one, don't go to work when you are a contagious disease  ready to spread. ---I looked up towards the ceiling and see 2 boxes of instant ramen,  product of Korea----I found it odd, were they props?, or does this place serve instant ramen?

I order Miso Tofu ramen with extra noodles  I like to watch "professionals" cook-----so I watch----lady takes out a pot smaller than I use at home, too small to make ramen and adds presumably stock?, maybe water?---she then gets some Miso paste adds to water/stock------then here is where my expectations sank----she goes and grabs two bricks of Top Ramen, freeze dried noodles----yup, the crap you used to get for 12 packs for $1. ---she adds them into the pot, then some misc vegetables------she scoops 6 powders and drops them into the pot. She drops in some tofu cubes. 

Done. ----I am not sure, but I would bet dollars to donuts, at least 4 out of the 6 of those powders are the seasoning packs which the store bought ramen came with.

I get handed my bowl of what I could have done at my own house with much more care, and for about 1/5 the $8 i was charged. 

Honestly, I hate so call restaurants who sell crap which they take no personal expertise to and charge people good money for. --I can drive to Koreana Market on Telegraph and 23rd and buy two packs of the same crap Bear Ramen uses and make it myself----Plus I would be making it in cleaner surroundings and not risking my health with a lady who is so sick she should be home resting in bed.

It is past 4 AM and I am dead-tired, but I have eaten and therefore must Yelp.

Today, I tried Bear Ramen due to my fondness for good noodles. I'd been advised, both by a real-life person I knew and by Yelpers that the Ramen is just instant noodles, so I heeded that warning. I do my research.

Instead, I ordered the Mushroom Fried Noodle. Why? Because most everything else was Kimchi this and Kimchi that and honestly, I don't even like Kimchi. I had stepped inside the restaurant to examine the menu and was too embarrassed to step out, as the owner had already acknowledged me.

Thus, I ordered the Mushroom Fried Noodles, hoping, and somewhat assuming, that there would be other things in it besides mushrooms. Wishful thinking, you can call it. Once upon a time, I learned that when you ASSUME, you make an ASS out of U and ME. 

So yes, I did make an ASS...out of ME at least. Okay, the noodles were good. The mushrooms were good. The sauce and the oil was good. The one egg on it was good. Was it $7 and finishable-in-one-meal-for-a-short-Asian-girl-who-wouldn't-mind-losing-10-pounds-good? Nope!

Call me demanding, but for $7 in the cheap-ass Asian ghetto, I expect something SOLID in my meal. Meat, please. Tofu. Give me protein! Besides a goddamn 20 cent egg! Even some freaking carrots or whatever.

Okay, it was my fault really. I got exactly what I asked for. Mushroom Fried Noodles. A substantial amount of noodles, lots of oil, and TONS of mushrooms. The same boring mushrooms...

Damn!!
Now this is real noodle!
O
M
G
!
!
This food is so Slamin Good!
I have been searching for that real Korean Noodle place....And yet it was hiding in a place I've walked by for a while. I was so shocked to find it and now find so many reviews. 
I love Korean food and Fish Cake (odeng) Ramen and a side of  rice cake with bean paste (DUK BOK KI) is at the top of my favorites list. 
Bears is a tiny place that can maybe seat 8-9 people inside. There are tables outside as well.
But the real draw to this place is the incredible food. Yes the food is a 10 on the yelp scale. I know, the yelp scale stops at five. Well lets times it by two and you get 10. It really was a surprise to find this bit of Seoul in Berkeley. The main cook is an incredibly sweet woman who puts so much love in each dish. 
You can't sit and chat for long in here because the line is out t the door. But go and eat and enjoy what is really a big gem in the Berkeley food experience.
Now that's what I'm talkin' about!
I dig it. The people there are so nice sort of motherly.  I like to go there alone for some good ramen. I am happy with everything I have had. It is a good hole in the wall.

satisfies that quick Korean ramen fix you have while traipsing around Berkeley. The owners have changed therefore the flavors have changed a little bit, but it's still decent. 

Tucked away in Foodcourtia I hit this spot up once in a while- I know Korean ramen is supposed to be spicy, but my tummy can't handle the spicy. I have asked them to not make it spicy at al, but somehow they usually manage to sneak a little of it in. Oh well!

I usually get their veggie tofu ramen and it's pretty good. Firm tofu, slices of zuchinni, carrots and some cabbage in the soup satisfies me on a cold night if I'm being lazy and don't want to cook. One night I was there eating at the counter and there must've been about 15 orders for kimchee fried rice, almost all with spam within a 45 miutes span. If only I can handle spicy food, I would be inclined to try it- guess y'all just have to tell me what it's like!

The only dish I have ever gotten here is the kimchi fried rice with spam, but it's delicious! For that alone, this place is worth a try. The portion sizes are also enormous -- good for 2 meal's worth (or one really huge meal if you're hungry...). I used to come here when I was in college to grab a quick lunch or dinner; most recently, I went back to Cal for a football game and picked up kimchi fried rice. It's still delicious! :)

-L.

My absolute FAVORITE place to get kimchi fried rice. I think that around 80% of my visits to Asian Ghetto end up taking me to Bear's Ramen because I just can't get enough of the rice. 

Can't say much about anything else because I've never actually tried any other dishes, but their ramen seems to be pretty popular as well. 

Cons: only takes cash. sometimes rice can be a little too oily.

I came here because my friends really hyped up the Kimchee fried rice with spam and egg. I really wanted to enjoy it. But the atmosphere just totally killed it for me. We sat outside in the square and there were pigeons everywhere... bugs flying and just plain unclean. So that was in my head... then i eat the rice and... i don't know... it really just didn't hit a spot. It seemed super oily, the Spam was a little gross, didnt seem like the typical SPAM brand spam, if that makes sense.... and the egg... more oil.

But i think it is just me. My brother was with us and he LOVED IT, ate the whole thing up. 

I will have to try this place again to make a final decision because i could have gone on an off day?

Good stuff! Located inside the asian ghetto. Came here after classes with a friend and we ended up choosing this place because she recommends the kim chi fried noodle. I ended up ordering the kim chi fried rice with chicken. 

Service was fast but the seating is very limited inside. We sat outside eating our warm food and hot tea on a foggy afternoon. Awesome ambiance. The fried rice was good. Not too spicy but just right. I tried a bit of my friends kim chi noodle with spam and I liked it more than my rice. I think they make the noodles themselves in their store and its really good! 

I'm totally getting spam instead of chicken next time. Screw trying to eat some lean protein.

This review is only for the kimchi fried rice with spam, and only made by the Korean lady :)

My version of comfort food.

What to get?

Kim Chee Fried Rice or Noodles. I'm more a noodle person myself, but a lot of people enjoy the rice dish.

There's spam in there! SPAM! What more could a college student ask for??

Satisfies the lunch time growling stomachs.

The very first Korean person I met was my best friend in college.  As we bonded over silly things on the same floor in Putnam Unit 1, she decided she would introduce me to Korean food at this place.  At the Asian ghetto.  This place probably contributed the other 5 pounds to my freshman 15.

Life changing experience.
Please just order the Kimchi Spam Fried Rice.  The first time I had this I thought to myself how weird, who the heck would ruin perfectly good fried rice by throwing in kimchi, spam, and 2 over easy eggs.  I was stupid.  IT WAS THE BEST COMBINATION EVER!!

Visit number 2: Sick as heck and wanted some soup.  For those of you who know Berkeley, not only do you have to deal with crazy bums on telegraph, rain, and the occasional creeper who follows you while you speed walk to the nearest brightly lit area, you'd know how freaking hard it is to get some good noodle soup.  Ramen here is great!  You have the sweet Korean lady boiling those noodles and you just feel as if chicken noodle soup would never compare.  Quite honestly it doesn't.  

Oh Fast as hell too!

This place is cheap and all the college students love it. 

The kimchi fried rice is by far the most interesting thing I've had from South Side Asian Ghetto. It comes with spam, a half cooked egg, and lots of kimchi flavored rice. 

When I'm not feeling the kimchi fried rice, I opt for the bear ramen special. The bowl it comes in is a little small, but it's packed with lots of veggies and chewy noodles, perfect for a student who doesn't eat their veggies.

4.5 stars actually, because I've only had bad service here once. I had ordered on the phone for kimchi fried rice, but when I arrived at Bear's Ramen, it turned out that she gave my order to someone else that also ordered kimchi fried rice, and then she ran out of rice! So instead of just coming in to grab my order, I had to wait an additional 20 minutes for her to ask another restaurant for some spare rice. Good thing I didn't have work or class, or else I would've been even more peeved.

Putting that aside... this is the only place I come to for my kimchi fried rice cravings. All the other korean places I've gotten kimchi fried rice at just doesn't do it for me. Everywhere else has vegetables in it like peas and carrots (which I HATE), but the kimchi fried rice here is simply that: kimchi and rice. It's simple, but it hits the spot for me.

I had a mad craving for some spicy kimchee fried rice this weekend, and my cousin raves about the fried rice here, so the bf and I decided it was worth trying. It's odd though, I lived in Berkeley for four years while I went to Cal, but never once ate here. 

The place was easy enough to find, although one could speak otherwise for the limited parking in Berkeley. The actual place (I am a bit hesitant to use the word "restaurant") was really small, with about eight spaces total to sit. Not that I wanted to sit inside because it was burning up. This is the Asian ghetto though, so what was I to expect? It was quite hot inside, so after placing our order, we stepped outside. The lady was really nice and greeted us as soon as we walked in. It didn't take too long to prepare our order, which was surprising considering the number of people in there. 

The fried rice itself was okay, it didn't live up to my expectations. I really enjoyed the egg on top, but spam and kimchee was lacking. The rice was a bit too mushy for my taste, and the entire thing was a little too salty. 

Great price for decent food, especially for broke college students. I don't fall under that category anymore, but I'll probably still come back to try other things off the menu.

i like ramen. 

and i like ramen from bear's noodle house. it kept me warm on winter (and summer nights) when nothing else sounded good. 

last night my bf tried to tempt me into ordering kimchi fried rice with spam, but... you know, i've never eaten spam. i don't think i'll start now, thank you. 

(and actually last night, i ended up going across the very crowded way for chinese food. but the bf's ramen was good, which i know from eating several large chopsticks full of it. yum.)

Not really worth the 7 dollars it costs, but a surefire way to satisfaction rests in the kim chi fried rice with spam.  The egg is cooked to perfection, the spam complements the flavors perfectly, and the texture of the rice is hard and not mushy or wet.  Perfect while sober or buzzed.  The owner and her son are really kind and friendly.  The portion is good to share with another.

I've only tried one item on their menu and I guess it was the wrong one. 

After seeing a friend eat their curry ramen, I decided to give it a go, since I love ramen and I love curry. I guess my initial thought was that it would be more of a noodle soup than just curry sauce over ramen. When I got my order, the sauce was extremely thick and the noodles were too overcooked and too soft to even pick up with chopsticks. The sauce did not even taste much like curry. I mostly tasted some sort of powder over mushy noodles.  

I've heard their kimchi fried rice is good but haven't tried it myself.

I really wasn't even hungry at all.  But because we were in Berkeley and because all of my friends have suggested that I try this place out, my boyfriend and I stopped by Bear's Ramen House last Friday night.

My boyfriend and I ordered a Spam Kimchi Fried Rice to share ($7.50 after tax).  Right after ordering, we saw the man begin to make it.  The place is quite small, with a couple of counters and about 10 seats total.  The guy working seemed to be friendly and my boyfriend described him as "chill."  Within minutes, our order was ready.

The rice was very flavorful and the portion size was plenty for the two of us.  Spam always goes perfectly in kimchi fried rice; but they also have chicken, beef, tofu, as options.  The fried egg on top was picture perfect, until we smashed the yolk with our chopsticks.  The yolk adds a nice creaminess and savoriness to the whole dish.  In fact, the egg was so good, half way through eating our fried rice, we asked the man for another egg ($0.50).  Delicious.  This place lived up to the hype.  I hope to come back!

My boyfriend's parents ordered tofu ramen which they really enjoyed, also.  

Notes:
-Free tea near the door.

I can't believe I haven't written a review for Bear's Ramen yet!

I LOVE their kim chi spam fried rice with 2 EGGS.  Emphasis on the TWO eggs.  This dish is comfort food to its best.  The portion is massive for to go.  I love the spiciness to it.  For $8, it is pricey after trying to make it at home.  

I've tried their ramen before but I prefer ordering the korean dishes here, such as the cold noodles or the cal gooksoo.  Next time I should try the kim chi noodles!

Service is quick. Perfect for a "to go" place. 

They got me to love this dish so much that I just started to make it on my own at home this past weekend!

I love their Kimchi Fried Noodle! It tastes really good. I think this is one of the better Korean food in Berkeley. I tried almost every Korean food in Berkeley, and this is one of the place that I will never get tired of. 
When I still live in Berkeley, I went to this place at least once a week, forgetting about my diet and everything. 

Now, when people asked me what did I miss from Berkeley, I will confidently say that I miss Kimchi Fred Noode from this place.

"Ramen House" is a bit misleading. This place serves up junky, comfort Korean food to its collegiate crowd. Can't go wrong, and nor can I knock it for delivering on face value. Our group decided to visit this place and try their kimchee fried noodles & ramen, and left satisfied. Fried noodles + kimchee + spam + fried egg = undeniable temptation.

Foodies will cringe: not the freshest, most intricate ingredients nor preparation ... but it doesn't claim to have this anyway! Nothing extraordinary worth a special trip or craving, but I know if I went to school here, I'd probably grab this stuff to go at least once a month!

Kim Chi Fried Rice with Spam.  Ain't nothin' like the real thing baby.  

This dish alone gives this place 5 stars as it goes down in my hall of fame of cheap, addictive all time plates.  I like to just sit down and eat it by myself cause I don't even want to TALK.  I just wanna savor the moment.

Ok, my beloved Bear's Ramen, I'm officially upgrading you. 

However I found a better bowl of ramen :(  I am however a devoted Bear's Ramen junkie.  

My devotion for Bear's Ramen is it's variety and price.  No other place has such a variety of Korean ramen.  I love it, and the price is just right!

Bear's may not have the best bowl of ramen, but it definitely have a ton of great ramen choices.

OOOOMG I do not know how to describe this kimchi fried rice with spam other than it is loaded with some type of foodcrack.

I have ordered this probably 50 times in my time at Cal and SF.  Every time I visit the east bay I fiend for it. Fiend.

I love me some homecooked Korean fried rice, but this just has a different twist to it. I wish I could pinpoint it more, but you just have to try it. Make sure you get the egg on top too!

Tip: call in and order before. There's basically nowhere to sit and this can be enjoyed in the container it comes in (maybe unlike the ramen).

Friends have ordered the dumpling ramen and kimchi fried noodle, but honestly, kimchi fried rice beats them all.

Bear's Ramen, you never disappoint! Of course I only come to you in response to kimchi fried rice cravings, but in addressing my needs, you do everything right. Drunk food, study food, a second lunch, it doesn't matter. Key features: globs of butter, diced spam, egg with runny yolk. Damn.

Wow thank you James H. for reminding me of this place.  This gem inside the asian ghetto should be familiar to just about every cal student for providing some of the best tasting homemade Korean food in all of southside, even all of Berkeley.  The Korean lady who I believe still owns and operates this small hole in the wall is so awesome and nice, I used to come here and bust out some of my mad korean skills and I'd be on her good side, and it helps to be on her good side haha.  

I used to always order either the Kimchi fried rice or my favorite dish, Kimchi sangyubsal bokkeum, which is like delicious pork cooked with red hot Kimchi all over rice.  It's a real piece of heaven and reminds me of my mama's cooking.
does it make me a groupie to also enjoy the kim-chi fried rice?

The kimchi fried rice with spam MUST have crack in it because it is really freakin good.  And no matter how many times I try, my attempts to make it at home have not come close at all.

Any of their ramens are good for your hungover days (Koreans know their hangover food), but on every other occasion just get the fried rice.

Ate here after moving my sister in to her dorm at Berkeley.  It's good - cramped seating area inside (two counter booths with stools, and lots of people piling in to order... hope a fire doesn't break out anytime soon or we'd all be screwed).  There's lots of seating outside though, so it's fine.

I ordered the kim chi ramen which was really delicious.  It was just the right amount of spicy and the kim chi was soo good.  I only wish the noodles were a little better.  They were instant noodle type ramen (she used a block of dried noodles), but the broth made up for it.  I should have gotten the udon instead, like my Dad did - those noodles were made fresh and looked par-fait.

All in all it was a satisfying meal and there are a lot of flavors to choose from.  I think my mom got the fish ball ramen and I love fish balls.  Unfortunately, I go to school in Chicago where the closest ramen they have is... still in California, so poor me I'll have to wait 'til winter break.  Lucky sister and her endless supply of Asian food...

I know the name of the place says "Ramen"...

but if I came here I would DEFINITELY get SPAM KIM CHI FRIED RICE.

mmMmmMmMmMmMm.

I wasn't a fan of the Mushroom Fried Noodle/Rice though a lot of other suggest that.  I didn't know there was a Kim Chi Fried Noodle but now I'm really excited to go try that too!!!!!!

I like. Very much.
Work many hours. Have many hours of school. Many hours of study.
Get tired. Must eat.
Very good gooksoo. Good ramen. Good kun mandu. Good pajun.
Nice lady feed me. It's good.
Me happy. Wallet happy.
Good. Me come back soon.

Easily favorite restaurant in Asian Ghetto. It's a REALLY small location and can sometimes get really crowded, but the freshly-made authentic Korean food here is amazing. Go with the kim chi fried rice with spam and share a seafood pancake if you're with a friend. There are other good things (try the kim chi fried noodles sometimes), but those are my favorite dishes and my mouth is watering now even I as I write about it.

Irene, the owner, and Angeles, one of the cooks are also really friendly and absolutely charming if you take the time to chat with them. I used to go shortly after the lunch rush to eat and watch Korean dramas with Irene. Love her!

Kimchee fried noodles with spam
 - amazingly fresh chewy udon-ish noodles with sweet gochuchang with a fried egg on top!  the egg is sunny side so when you mix it, the yolk bursts onto the noodles, creating a rich creamy texture. MMMMmmmm

Champong gooksoo 
- seafood noodle soup with fresh udon and spicy oil on top.  the broth was super savory and the best i've had in a while.  its even better than the casseroles at Toyose (SF).  it's packed with delicious seafood in almost every spoonful and the taste of the broth does not get old

don't get the beef ramen though, both the broth and the ramen are packaged.

beverages are self serve, cooks are super nice and legitamate mommys

i'll definetely come back to try the mushroom and kimchi fried rice everyone is raving about.

I LOVE THIS PLACE!

The owner is this cute lady that reminds me of MOM.  Aww!
It's amazing how many orders she can keep straight at ONE time.

Everyone get's Kim Chi Fried Rice. I recommend Mushroom Fried Noodle.  It's a hidden delight!

I love it so much! *heart*

Let's be judicious when rating a hole in the wall, Korean version of "fast food".  Of course it's not gourmet, the set up is slightly more sophisticated than your dorm room with a communal kitchen.  

Sometimes, home style basics cooked up by someone mom-esque can really hit the spot.  Little reminiscent of plate lunch shops in Hawai'i.  It's cash only, but there is a BofA around the corner.

I dived into my fish cake udon, and it was hearty and complete with a mini heap of fresh bean sprouts.  Loved the piping hot broth, that brought on a sweat and cooked the bean sprouts mildly.  My neighbor was killing his kimchi fried rice with an over-easy egg on top with his ear buds still in.  Solid, good, fast-food, Korean style.  Call ahead for to-go orders since it can get busy in a quickness.

Bear's Ramen House is a boonshik (kind of Korean street food) restaurant known not for their ramen but for their kimchi fried rice. And rightfully so, because it is sooooo good!  If you like spam (and you should), GO WITH SPAM.

I've also tried the ddukgook (rice cake soup) and the broth was delicious and savory.  I tried the labbokki (spicy rice cake) which I had seen before and wanted to try and I would've said it could've been cooked a little longer.. will try it again and see how it is.

I haven't tried their noodles yet because I always am tempted by the kimchi fried rice, but I hope to come back more often so that I try more dishes!

Some notes: Cash only, they cook to order so it might take a little bit of time, and it's the Asian ghetto so seating is sparse inside.  They also have barley tea (comforting and yummy!), but don't expect banchan because this is not that type of Korean place!

Wow! I haven't felt insulted like this in a while. The Mexican lady that works there has been working for over ten years. And maybe she has gotten too comfortable with her job. So, I ordered kimchi noodles, that is what i normally order and know the portion size. Anyways, after she finished and plated it. She took one third out and put it into another plate put rice on that plate and set it aside. Then she served me my plate with 1/3 missing and then had the gall to sit next to me and eat the rest of my dish. 

The food is pretty good here, though it is overpriced, but the service is subpar and plain rude.

Previous Review: 4 stars
"I have had good and bad meals coming here.
My last one was Kimchi Fried Noddles with spam. Which reminded my a lot of my ex girlfriend. 
The noodles were sweet, which was odd but worked quite well.
The food is over priced, but worth trying. 
But it seems to be really hot inside due to the bad ventilation.

I recommend staying  away from any dish that has curry in it."
Best gook soo ever.  Fresh noodle goodness

Before you see "ramen" in Berkeley and jump out of your chair, let's temper those expectations: this is no Tampopo's, no hand cut noodles or laborious, Cadillac of broths. The ramen begins wound tight and dry, wrapped in plastic. Aside from Kingpin Donuts, nothing in the Asian Ghetto is handmade. 

Being that it's Korean run, I'd skip their attempts at Japanese and stick to the kimchi dishes. The champong gives a spicy throat tickle, redolent with onions, heavy with noodles, the occasional tentacle of squid, a pair of shrimps, mushrooms and several requisite spinach leaves, soaking in red chili. Thumbs up! We didn't fare so well with the massive pile of curry, though. It was too humongous to tackle before turning into a cold and gelatinous pile. They need to ease up on the corn starch.

They also saran wrap their register and hover over you when they're trying to close up. It's got class.

Bear Ramen House makes me feel uber-Korean!  :)  I love the ramen and the fresh guksu and of course the kimchi fried rice w/ spam!  ooh, i get shivers just thinking about it!  If you sit at the counter to eat, you can also figure out some items on the secret menu!

:)

Literally a hole in a wall, but the food is great. The owner is super nice too! Personally love the kimchee fried rice and kimchee fried noodles. It is a little bit more on the pricey side, but they serve good portions.

Bear's Ramen House is one of the places I will miss after I officially graduate from Cal and move away. It is located right in Durant Square (or what students refer to as Asian Ghetto). I usually order the Mushroom Fried Noodle/Rice or the Kimchi Fried Noodle/Rice with Spam. I prefer the noodles over the rice though. Both come with an egg right on top and cost about $7-8. Eat it when it's fresh! Like Ava S. says, the quality of the food really depends on who is cooking that day. I am most satisfied with the food when the lady who owns the store is cooking. I think her son and a non-Asian woman is usually working the store now, but not always. The owner is seriously the nicest and sweetest lady ever! You can even CALL IN ahead of time to place your order if you're on the run.

If you want to dine-in, I must warn you that it is pretty small. I think there's only about 6-8 seats in there total, but you can always sit at the tables outside of the store. I would definitely NOT sit in there on a hot day. Complimentary water and CASH ONLY (but there's a Bank of America right around the corner if that helps).

4.5 stars, rounding up for sheer sentimentality. this was my go-to restaurant during my four years at berkeley. not only would i stop by and get my kimchi fried rice with spam, two eggs and extra kimchi 3-4 times a week but i would attempt to divide each meal into two by frying up a few eggs at home and separating it into two perfect portions. now if i'm ever across the bridge, i make it a point to stop by and pick up TWO orders from here (the more, the merrier!)

In college I worked part-time across the street from here and would religiously order the Kim Chi Fried Rice (or Noodle, depending on my mood) with tofu to go, much to my coworkers' chagrin.  I went there so much that the owner would periodically give me free bottles of the tiny sweet Korean milk drinks.  Words can't express how much I love Bear's Ramen House.  I once ate there twice in one day and ordered the same thing both times.  And that day happened to be my 22nd birthday.  It was awesome.

Bear Ramen House is A-OK in my book. Not exactly a standout restaurant, and perhaps a bit unforgettable compared to the ever-popular Thai Basil and Gypsy's.

Typically, I ordered the mushroom fried rice. It's my safe alternative to too-spicy Korean dishes and this dish is rather good! The downside is that you have to eat it pretty quickly, because it becomes really unappetizing when it's cold. BUT portions are pretty large and it comes with an egg! My favorite! :D

I have a feeling business would be a lot better if this place was named "Bear's Kimchi Fried Rice" instead of "Ramen" because everyone I know gets Kimchi fried rice with spam here. They have perfected the dish and you might not be able to find a better one in Berkeley. It is like a Korean mom cooking it for you at your dorm.

It starts with great rice, that's chewy but not overly sticky. Add in nicely chopped kimchi, cubes of spam and a sunny-side up egg with a runny yolk mixed in, you got yourself some comforting "Seoul" food. They serve a great cup of complimentary warm tea as well to go with it.

Ok, so if anyone gives this place less than a four star, I want to drop kick your face.  Also, it probably means you don't understand Korean food aka get outta here then.  

The food here is soooo good! I don't usually order the ramen because I have ramen at home but when I feel like I need a home style cooked meal from a motherly figure, I go here.  The owner is the sweetest woman in the freaking world!!! I want to adopt her as my second mother.  The kimchi fried rice or kimchi fried noodle is probably the most popular here for good reason.  It is really really good.  If I can't decide what to get, it's always a good safety.  I've also had the kal gook su and I didn't really have too much of expectations for it but it ended up being just like my moms!

The prices are pretty decent.  I think Berkeley people get so spoiled by the dirt cheap prices that when it's not cheaper than the cheapest they've had, then they automatically think it's expensive.  It's about average $6-8 an entree.  Oh, it's cash only btw.

I LOVE YOU MAMA BEAR!!! HEHE I'M ON MY WAY THERE RIGHT NOW!!

YUM!

I love fried rice. I love spam. I love curry.
This place has it all at a good price.

Kim chee fried rice w/ spam and curry ramen for grand total of $11
Can't beat that. 

nothing spectacular, but a very good cheap eats spot.

I heart kim chi fried rice! Curry gooksoo is soo yummy. and even the off-sounding cheese ramen is delicious too. besides the good homecooked flavors, I really like being able to sit at the tiny counter and watch as my food is made in front of my eyes. Great to see the gooksoo made fresh as well.

This is the place for LATE NIGHT Korean food cravings. I always order the Kimchi Fried Rice/Fried Noodle or the Dumpling Ramen with Spam... and it never fails me! 

Although they have been raising the prices on me each year, I always keep coming back! Quality food at any time of the day, what more can you ask for? 

Only downside is they have very limited (and uncomfortable seating), so take your food to-go and watch some TV at home :)

Today, I stopped by Bear Ramen for the first time since freshman year.  Brought back memories of getting fat all because of that damn food court. Anyway, I'm going home in a few days so I can stuff my face with all the Korean food I want, but I was craving kimchi fried rice so a trip to Bear Ramen was in order. 

I really think this is the only thing you should get here. True, I haven't tried every single thing on the menu, but something about the stacked boxes of Jin Ramen is questionable. Next time you're there, just look up and you'll see 'em. Just sayin', you can get a box of it at a Korean market for about $5. They better not be getting their ramen noodles from there...or maybe they are.

Their kimchi fried rice has improved. Sorta. When I had it freshman year, there was a load of oil that would just sit at the bottom. They don't seem to use as much now so that's good, but meh to the lack of Spam. C'mon, throw that stuff in there lady.

Okay, I give props to the lady for busting her ass cooking on her own, with the help of an assistant, but still. Lady needs to get off the phone with her friend when I'm standing there ready to order and when a pile of people shuffle in soon after. Hello?!?! I'm waving my hands in the air like I just don't care.

"Where are we eating today?", asked the best friend. 

I handed him a piece of paper. (http://static1.px.yelp.com/bphoto/ZGySgb8QKLXkHTl7tstCzA/l) (The bear is even holding a bowl of ramen! ^_^)

Unfortunately, the mushroom ramen I ordered was not quite as cute as my awesome drawing. Served with white onions, half a fish cake, seaweed, spinach, green onions, bean sprouts, and sliced mushrooms, (http://static2.px.yelp.com/bphoto/mSkSQgnGiPaMWSUPT2j5OA/l) the noodles were fondly reminiscent of the ramen noodles I ate from a bag as a college student.

The noodles were well cooked, and the broth was fairly tasty, but overall, the dish was mediocre, and my attention soon diverted to the pigeons swooping over my head in preparation to poop on me (my large head makes for an easy target!)

The bestie ordered the kimchi fried rice (http://static2.px.yelp.com/bphoto/w62OTTrkzy-4SVmnz7fatA/l), while our friend ordered the kimchi fried noodle (http://static3.px.yelp.com/bphoto/BFEn7l4opMgRDeZ6ak7rcQ/l), both which looked more appetizing than my boring dish. But after our meal, both fellows complained of a need to hibernate, as the pound of grease induced a major food coma. 

Perhaps next time, I'll draw a bear holding some fresh HOMEMADE ramen.

Yes, I think that shall work.

Bears ramen house is tucked away in the Asian food corner. The place is so tiny it can seat only a few on the counter, but people can also sit outside on the benches. The interior is very shabby, and its not the best looking place. However, it is situated in a very convenient location for Cal students, and its open until 11pm. 
The menu is very long, and of course they sell ramen and also a lot of other Korean dishes like the popular kimchi fried rice w/ spam and even noodle soups. Also note, she does not use msg, I talked to the lady and they use ramen soup powder and various other spices but not msg. Many people take the food to go, and she cooks fast and you can actually view the kitchen while you wait which is quite entertaining. 
Overall, not the best looking place, but obviously don't judge a book by its cover. Great Korean dishes to satisfy your Korean food cravings anytime.

So basically I was in a sorority in college.  Us girls before we got together for our meetings would grab some food and go on campus to discuss in great detail whatever it is that girls these days gossip about.

The "ghetto" was our go-to place of choice and for me, Bear's Ramen house is a big reason why.  Sure, some days I just gotta have me some Meesha's or a Combo Plate at Vietnam Village.  But the kimchee fried rice, mushroom fried rice, or gook soo from Bear's Ramen House always makes me happy and satisfied.  Esp in dreary weather, the hot soup and chewy noodles, or the nice fried egg on top of fried rice makes me happy to be alive.  There were numerous occasions when my friend who lived on Telegraph and I would just buy it to go then head back and munch away happily and have enough for dinner that night.  It's cheap, it's cash only, it's small, and it's good.  It's what Berkeley eats is all about.

*warning: don't get the ramen.  they dont use fresh noodles. they use the top ramen-esque ramen.  if u like that kinda stuff go for it but im all about the gook soo, fried rice, and dok buk gi.

note: this rating is for the previous owner.. 

i always felt at home, cuz the owners greeted me so happily, or mayhaps they remembered me... :) hmm yes.. i would like to think that... haha.. it's an uber small shop that seats maybe 7 ppl max at the counter..  make sure your turn radius is good, [ie, don't be lugging around giant backpacks and such], or you'll brush up against some sweaty ramen-eating folk.. or maybe you like that kinda thing...

my favorite: kimchee fried rice with spam .... and ... *drumroll please*.. an egg

totally hits the spot.. what spot? every friggin spot...

During those late nights in studio, the only thing I ever craved was their kimchi spam fried rice. I've tried the kimchi chicken fried rice and it just didnt quite hit the spot like the spam does. The spam adds a nice salty side to the dish. Their portions are huge but when I've been deprived of this dish, i can finish the whole thing. Lethal if you eat it after beat the clock, cuz you'll just clean off your plate. Its so good, I never tried anything else just because it would be one less time i can have the dish.

Just talking about this makes me want to make the drive just to get some of this.

Aside from this heaven sent dish, the owner is really nice. I think I've been there too many times if she recognizes me. She has also noticed when I look a little different (dyed hair, make up, etc) and she'll compliment. That makes me smile.

ORDER THEIR KIMCHI FRIED NOODLE WITH PORK! TRUST ME. If you don't like it, I'll buy you lunch somewhere else.

Berkeley has a very limited selection of Korean restaurants and please, STEVE'S KOREAN BBQ IS NOT KOREAN FOOD! Of all the dishes I've tried at Bear's, Steve, T-toust, and Koryo, Bear's has the best Korean dish. So save your time, money, and disappointment and go to Bear's Ramen House for their Kimchi Fried Noodle.

Good Food, Good Friends, ENJOY!

Despite it's English name, the ramen isn't the best thing on their menu (imo, of course). In Korean the name is Bear Boon-Shik which is a more general casual type of eatery vs. "Ramen House" 

Things I've tried:

Bear Special Ramen: ramen with chicken, mushrooms, and veggies like sprouts, zuchinni, onion, diakon. Noodles are made from instant bricks. Broth is a secret blend of mysterious powders from containers in the corner of the counter. From how my tongue felt, one of the white powders thrown in was MSG. 2 stars for the nice mix of toppings

Gook su's: same powdered broths as ramens but with fresher flour noodles. Bonus points for in-house made noodles. 3.5 stars

Kimchee Fried Rice w/ Spam: Probably my favorite dish here. Nice amount of heat. Tasty spam. Fried egg w/ runny yolk. 4- stars

Jja Jang Myun: Same fresh noodles as the gook su dishes. Sauce tasted a bit off and on the thin side. Didn't have much  meat like you find at other JJM specialty places (Yu yu, Koryo). The veggies in the sauce were total mush. Tasted like it'd been cooked days ago. 2 stars

You can't complain too much. It's a hole in the wall for college kids.

There is a good variety of ramen, gooksoo, udon, and rice meals. The curry rice is too bland and runny for my liking. The gooksoo udon and ramen are plain enough that I can make myself at home. I would suggest the Bear Ramen because it has the most substance in it. Good thing that meals here are pretty cheap, but prices do go up once in a while!

So, why the hype? It's all about the kimchi fried rice. You can either get spam kimchi fried rice or chicken kimchi fried rice. If you don't specify chicken, the default is spam. When I was vegetarian, I asked the lady to substitute in tofu instead. The fried rice is really spicy because of all the chili powder, but I've noticed that it is made a little differently now. The texture is not as smooth as before. It comes with an egg on top, but you can add a second one for 50 cents.
