That Korean lady is super nice and probably knew me by face because I frequented this place so often back then. She seemed very motherly. It was as if she was the mom of a friend. She does not always keep track of whether you paid or not, so I've seen people get away with taking their food and leaving or eating and leaving without paying. It's very informal so you go up to her when you want to order and you pay when you want to. She's very trusting. Bad thing is, prices have gone up and portions have gone down since then. One order of kimchi fried rice used to last me 1.5 meals.

cash only.

Slap my my Mama! Having just returned from the Seoul Mothership, kimchee fried rice w/Spam & two eggs is the ulltimate experience! Mama and son have their feng shui going on! I'm in tears. Agi yesunim gamsahabnida. And Go Bears!

the egg is back, baby. for a better part of the 80s/90s, eggs got this bad rap about being chock-full of cholesterol, and were shunned off menus and out of home kitchens. thankfully for oviphiles 'round the world, such as wylie dufresne and myself, eggs have been welcomed back with open arms. they are now placed, poached or fried, atop pasta, vegetables, fish, and anything else that chefs can think of. including one of my more humble favorites: kimchi fried rice. 

while the name of this place says ramen, cal students in the know will tell you that the choice option is the kimchi fried rice with spam. and being that it's been friggin' freezing around the bay area lately, i felt in need of a warm, hearty lunch, and if it comes with an egg on top, all the better! 

a good runny yolk is silky, sultry, velvety smooth; almost like sex personified in food (foodified?). there is perhaps nothing more luxurious than the yolk melting and oozing down over anything lucky enough to be in its way; it kind of reminds me of satin sheets. golden yellow satin sheets, flowing over a king-sized dinner plate. and is there anything more delicious than the spiciness of kimchi mixed with the chewy, filling fried rice, all doused in the creamy goodness of runny egg yolk?? methinks not. definitely one of my favorite dishes with an egg on top!
Service with a smile and they let you taste the beers before you buy. All of them are exquisite selections by an experienced beer master. Old Rasputin on tap, need I say more?

I like this place for the patio they have outside. It's really nice to sit there and enjoy the atmosphere on a warm summer night. Too bad they close the patio at 11 PM. 

They aren't that attentive when you're trying to order at the bar though. My friend had to wave them down to order a drink. 

It has pretty decent seating if you come with a larger group.

Beer was good and cheap! The giant pretzel was pretty good too! The outdoor seating area is super cute, although it looks like it's right outside of a dorm. Some other items on the menu caught my eye, but I'll have to be back to give this a full review.

Good lamb burger, great pot pie, and good selection of high quality beers.  Accommodations inside are extremely loud, but the courtyard is a civilized alternative.  The con is the price, not terribly reasonable.

Free House has a lot of potential as long as they get their taps and cocktails together. If they find their true direction, they could contribute a very unique and exciting venue to the Berkeley area. We'll see! Hopefully it won't turn into only a frat hang out or another Kip's.
Great selection of beer on tap, all of which are $5. Indoors has all this old, dark wood and there is a large outdoor patio in back.  Overall, a great space to meet up with friends.

This place's days are numbered. The only things it has going for it are the cool dark wood decor and central location. The food seemed to have a lot of potential at first glance. Good ingredients were listed...grass fed beef, Acme bread...the only problem is that they combine these ingredients to make terribly mediocre food.

Also, the service is really deficient. The first time I went for appetizers and drinks, the staff was very disorganized and different people kept coming over to us to see if we had ordered. Then they proceeded to give us the bill while we were eating. Not very polite.

The second time I went for lunch, they made a HUGE deal about letting us order a piece of bread alongside a salad and then gave us the bill again while we were still eating. It's a great location and venue, so it's really a shame that the restaurant is not as great.

Great location, good selection of beers and decent prices.  This fills a much-needed gap among campus bars, and has a beautiful upscale interior.  However, it suffers from growing pains and schizophrenia.  As a bar it's reasonable, and the dining experience outdoors is respectable.  The interior is too crowded and too noisy to serve as a restaurant.  Furthermore, after 4 visits I can safely say the service is consistently atrocious.  Sarcastic and disdainful staff, extremely slow, many confused orders, constantly out of stock.  Management needs to make things more efficient and systematic to improve the customer experience.

Overall Freehouse is a brilliant idea with poor execution, but I hope it improves.

Location wise it's convenient since it is right next to campus. Good place to grab a beer and catch up with a friend.  There are a lot of seating inside and outside and even a pool table which is cool. Since it was a Monday, there weren't that many people around so service was good (like it should be). Draft beer was $5 and they have some bottled beer for $4. I got the daily pot pie (steak today) and Velvet Merlin Oatmeal Stout. NOT BAD. The best part of a chicken pot pie though is the crust and they put it in a ramekin so no crust besides a top. My friend got the giant pretzel which was quite giant and came with cheese sauce and horseradish spread. Someone also ordered a chicken burger but it looked kind of dry. 

Tip: take pictures in the front outside! :) it's so pretty with all the flowers.
Bartender with the short hair is rude at best and a reason to never come back at worst. Made the night so unpleasant and inconvenient. I can't believe a person like this is hired at a nice bar.

I'm glad that this place is no longer Adagia, but I feel like it could have been better. The salmon sandwich was just okay -- you know like food that you eat because you bought it but don't particularly enjoy.

I like the atmosphere though, although it was super crowded on a Friday evening. The outside patio will be nice for summer days.

A good spot for cheap eats close to campus. Beers on offer are great, but the food leaves a little to be desired: soggy fries, burnt wings, tiny sandwiches and burgers. Not terrible but not fantastic either. I'll go back for the beer and location.

Great salads, ambience, and staff! I come here 3-5 times a week and I love the place. Some entrees are better than others. I would recommend the pretzel, ANY of their salads, black bean cakes, vegan chili, turkey burger, and their fries... oh they are so tempting. It may take awhile to get seated when it starts getting crowded but there are so many other times in the day when it is not too crowded and the service is super quick!

Steak frites was awesome, and so was the  black bean cakes. Plus all the those beers on tap, decorated by a beautiful bouquet of the finest top shelf liquors on the back drop. 
Truly a hidden gem in all of Berkeley

After a great start - delicious drinks and a perfect inexpensive menu -- it was all downhill in the food department -- mediocre to bad.   Unfortunately, here cheap prices mean bad cooking.  I'd add a few bucks to the offerings and hope for tastier food.  Despite the great location, we won't go again -- unless Yelpers tell us things have changed.

Karen in Oakland

Drinks menu great, food not so much.  Appalling pulled pork and slaw -- pork had weird back taste, truly vile, and slaw allegedly made from jicama was limp and utterly tasteless.  Complained and got hamburger instead.  Burger clearly inferior meat, had bled into bottom bun most disgustingly.  Yuck.  My co-diners were also unhappy with their food but not disgusted, as I was -- chicken salad, cassoulet, and steak frites all described as just barely OK.  These guys should limit menu to a very few items and do them exceedingly well, keep prices low.  My food was literally inedible.  A shame.

Food's decent, 1 or 2 items are superb, prices are fine by North Berkeley standards, perhaps a bit high considering it's next to the campus. Beer is excellent, haven't tried anything else. They have 2 TVs showing different channels, and the good sense to turn the sound off. Music was unobtrusive, but somebody's recently turned the volume up. Ambience is unbelievable.

Average to low quality food.  If you want something decent to eat, this is not the place.  The real failure here, however, is the abominable service.  Let me preface this next section by saying that the restaurant was not the least bit crowded or busy when I arrived.  So.... Last week I waited for about three minutes just to have someone acknowledge that I was waiting to be seated, and that was only to tell me someone would be "right with" me.  Several minutes later someone did finally arrive and I got seated.  Then another five minutes or so for the server to appear.  I ordered something to drink, although I was ready to order food, but that didn't seem to be on the servers list of important matters.  Off she went.  Ten minutes later, when the drink hadn't arrived it dawned on me that this was really a pattern of truly awful service (the worst in my experience I think).  So I stood up and walked out.  Then, at long last, I managed to get their attention.  Or at least they noticed the obvious.  "Are you leaving?"  Duh....  Not even an inquiry as to why that might be the case.  Perhaps they knew?

When this place was Adagia (and owned by the same man as Freehouse) the food was delicious and, putting it kindly, the service nowhere near the standard of the food.  But now the food has sunk to below average, and the service has plummeted proportionally.

There are many many other places around campus to eat.  Save yourself heartburn and annoyance and go anywhere else.

PS  This was my second experience in less than a week.  Although not as extreme as this one, the earlier was in the same league.  Two times is a pattern in my book.

I voted with my feet on this one.  Be warned!

This place is very cozy. This place has always been packed the two I have been here (probably more for the drinks than the food). Seating always seems to be limited.  For me, the food was mediocre. I had the salmon sandwich and my friend had the steak sandwich, which at $12 was a little pricey for sandwiches that was mostly bread and sauce. 

This place is only open for dinner and from Monday to Saturday only.

This place has very mediocre food, but a very cool atmosphere.

I guess that's why its so packed on weekend evenings.

I just wish the food had a little more flavor or creativity, then maybe I'd go there for more than just because its a cool looking venue near campus.

Can be really hard to find seating inside, but if the weather's nice the patio is a really cool spot.

The service is about what you can expect for the UC Berkeley campus area--which is to say not that great. Nobody's rude or anything, they're just not very attentive. The food selection has pretty typical American pub grub and the the drinks are limited but get the job done. It's a little bit pricey for what you're getting, but if you're a Cal student it's a really convenient and relatively nice place to meet up and grab a bite and/or drinks.

I am ever so conflicted about Freehouse.  The exterior is this gorgeous house on the edge of campus with a huge patio replete with wooden tables.  Yea, there is wood everywhere and it is oh so warm and sexy.  The bar is prominent in the dining room and big enough to accomodate sitting and standing patrons.  The actual dining room is a mess.  There are too many tables.  Someone wasn't counting right or wanted to squeeze a few more seats in at the expense of the comfort of the guests.  It just feels crowded and that's not an adjective I want around my person when I am eating.  But then there is the value!  Pints are five bucks and all the sandwiches range in price from 9 to 12 bucks.  The best part of this the size of the sammies and the fact that they come with a heaping pile of fresh cut fries and pickled veggies.  Ok, the picked veggies are this unthought out addition to the plate.  Broccoli, peppers, and something else?  I am not sure what the point was.  I dig the idea of some veggies on the plate, but pickled?  Maybe carrots would have been good?  The fries were beyond excellent.  The burger I got was a bit of a mess though.  Like the patty kept trying to make a getaway, which is illogical given it's size.  There was just a problem with the layout, maybe.  

So what's the final result?  I liked Freehouse, but I didn't like Freehouse.  I will chalk it up to growing pains.

Just what Berkeley doesn't need.  Another student hangout with no reservations.  Seems to me the owners should have concentrated on the food rather than "re tooling".
No longer an option before any of the Cal Performances events, I won't go here, so can't comment on the food.

There are other places to go for food.  This place was a bad choice.  The food was not impressive or even very good and expensive for what you got.    
  
I ordered a pulled pork sandwich which seemed to be missing the pulled pork.  It was a glob of super sweet orange flavored sauce.  Tasted like cheap Chinese food but lacked substance.  The fries were overcooked where they were no longer crispy but were like sticks that turn to dust in your mouth.  The coleslaw didn't have anything on it so it was just grated soggy cabbage and carrots, very bland.  They do not have anything on the menu that can accommodate any kind of food restrictions or allergies so probably not good for a group unless you know everyone can eat everything or you are only going for drinks (beer).

I guess if you are looking for a place close to campus to just get a beer and like a college, preppy crowd then you might like it.  But I recommend not eating here and I like good cocktails so I won't be going back here for drinks either.

Everything is just very normal.  I had the grass fed burger and it was fine but nothing stellar.  The chicken salad was pretty good.  The salmon pot pie tasted like chowder.  Mac & Cheese is bland - don't recommend it.  

Our server was excellent although it took us a while to get seated.  No one was there to seat us so we just sat at a table and I picked up a few menus for the table.  

I would definitely come back seeing as how its literally steps away from the law school but I don't think the food is anything to rave about.  Prices are pretty decent.  Everything is around $10-$12

I went here with coworkers. The food was okay. The atmosphere was fun. The beer selection was fine. I wouldn't have had any complaints...

But then they undercharged me on the bill. About $75 instead of $175, so pretty significant. After they ran my credit card, I looked at the amount for tipping purposes. Although I was in a hurry to leave, I did the honest thing and told them about the undercharge. They then made me wait for about 20 minutes while fixing the problem (which involved a swap with another's table's charge). They re-ran my card for the $175, apologized, and assured me that the $75 would be immediately refunded. Inconvenient, yes, but altogether not a big deal.

So...that was about three months ago...and they still haven't refunded the $75. I found this so annoying that I even wrote an email to the manager. No response....

Apparently, that's the price they charge for honesty these days. Do the right thing, and in reward you can wait 20 extra minutes, pay a $75 fee, and then waste your time writing emails and yelp rants...argh.

On that basis alone, I cannot recommend this restaurant to anyone.

Great place with great ambiance! Our server David was so much fun, attentive, and had a great personality. We started off outside by the fire but it got a bit chilly so we were moved indoors. The Grilled Chicken Sandwich was really good!

I'm down with FREEHOUSE
They have got an amazing Chef who previously worked at Monks Kettle(another 4-5 start restaurant/bar).
The food is a local/modern american style.
They will always have a few top notch beers, but if that's not what you're after no worries because they have got some great mixologists that can whip up a mighty fine cocktail.
This place has it all
-pool table
-huge outdoor seating area
-fireplace

A good place to catch a beer, while watching a game.
Food is ok, but if you're there after the sun goes down, the college crowd comes out, you feel really strange and old INSTANTLY, meanwhile pitying the bar tender for all the Cadillac Margaritas and Lemon Drops they'll have to make for the newly 21-ers.

All in all, not much to say about the place, and the drinks are on the pricey side.

TIP: As the weather warms up, enjoy the sunny, beautiful patio! It's clean and open until 11pm (with heat lamps, too). 

Technically, that's tip number four. Since the last time I've been here, a couple things have changed. 

The patio is awesome. There are still a few benches that can't be used yet, but it's really nice out there. The circular tables can be pulled apart and lengthened to accommodate larger parties. 

The service is still not as good as I think it can be. I understand that I was with a large group of rowdy students celebrating the end of a project, but considering the fact that they're located across the street from campus, wouldn't they kind of welcome these large groups? Instead, we get a waitress who doesn't seem like she really wants to serve us, forgets two drink orders, and tells me she doesn't think I ordered what I ordered... oh well. It all ended up okay though--no big issues. 

And stick to the beer (and admire their ever-expanding whiskey collection!). I got a nice glass of the Denogginizer from Drake's Brewing Co. in San Leandro. It's just one of the many IPAs they have on tap for $5. We ordered some fries, but it's really not worth the money.

This place is pretty chill.  Your standard American bar cuisine in a prime location.  Nice that they have a few things available on tap.  Its nice and spacious, so having friends is fine.  Outdoor seating with fire pits is available.  Pot pie was prime, as was the strawberry shortcake.  Decent bang for the buck, but if you're visiting parking can be a pain since it is right by campus.

I went to Free House prior to a concert at Zellerbach Hall....I will NEVER go back and it is not the food as i never had a chance to try the food. 

It is not clear you have to wait to be seated or seat yourself - turns out you grab a menu and seat yourself - this was not the problem. The problem was that after we sat down we were ignored - no sliverware no greeting no water - NO SERVICE AT ALL - this was after sitting at the table fro 15 minutes - we just left - DO NOT GO HERE AT ALL!

Pricey?  Maybe for a college kid.  However, there's an excellent selection of beers and the wings are to die for.  I haven't had bad service the 3 times I've been there.  I don't always require good service but when it's there, it's noticeable.

This is your place if you're looking for a business casual meeting place. The crowd seems to be of students from the law school and business school across the street. It's incredibly convienent if you want a watering hole near your work/school. What's also so grand about it is the woodsy interior, high ceilings, large tables. Although it's great for after work/school functions, it's also great for the mid-day read and write. There are great beers on tap, all of which are $5 per pint. Not all beers are created equal, so it's a great deal for ones like gift of the magi or the le merle saison. There's a full bar too and glasses of wine for $5. The fries are popular and it comes with three sauces. There's a ketchup, garlic aioli, and a curry aioli. That curry aioli is amazing. The food is not as well priced, but still reasonable. The pot pie looks especially small without a side of any sort.

OMG service is poor! I've been here 3 times now and every time service is really poor. Outdoor patio is nice (especially with the fire place), but by virtue of being outside the waiter never comes to you. Both times we sat outside, we'd have to send someone inside to grab the waiter, or we just went directly to the bar to order a drink.

Cocktails are expensive! Food looks good, but again expensive! I'm not a beer connoisseur so I won't comment on the beers besides that they aren't brewed in house. If I were to go to a beergarden in Berkeley, I say stick with Jupiter's. Better location, better service, and cheaper food and drinks!

Food here is.. OK and expensive. But I would come here again to just hang out and have a beer or two. 

To start off our dining experience, I ordered a belgian ale and my boyfriend ordered a stout ($5 pints). To accompany our drinks we ordered the special pizza of the day: BBQ chicken and a plate of clams. I was pretty disappointed in the clams as they were tiny and without much flavor. There wasn't enough sauce so that I could easily slurp up some good flavor with the clams. But I do have to say the clams were cleaned well. Not one bit of sand in my mouth and every time I eat clams, that's the one thing that bothers me the most. The BBQ chicken was the better half of our dinner. The crust was thin and crispy but doughy at the same time. It held a great texture against the tangy BBQ sauce. Our meal in total cost around $45 sans tax and tip, which I felt was expensive for the amount and quality of the food.

The interior of this place is what I would come here again for. I like that during the night hours, it's dim, resembling the interior of a cozy ski lodge. The couches around the fireplace add a nice touch to the ambience. The crowd is older, not so much young college kids but I like this scene better. No rowdiness going on here. The servers are friendly and check up on your frequent enough to get what you want.

Five stars for location
Five stars for gorgeous interiors
Five stars for beer prices
Five stars for peaceful atmosphere
Four stars for beer selection
Two stars for food prices
One star for food quality

I mean, really, if this place didn't serve food, I would seriously consider giving it five stars (alas, in part because all the other bars on the Southside suck so much). Short of giving up on food entirely, this place should either replace its chef, or revise its offerings entirely to simple inexpensive things.  The fries are already quite good: the rest of the menu, however, appears completely out of reach of the kitchen staff.

This is a very welcome addition to campus. Awesome space with good food and drinks - not much more you could want from a neighborhood hang out. Although its pretty freezing these days, I imagine that the outdoor area will be pretty sweet during the summer.

I highly recommend the turkey burger, and the beet salad was also pretty good. Food ranges from about $8-15 and is pretty standard Berkeley bar food (meaning way better than typical bar food - local ingredients, high quality, yada yada).

Well-played, Freehouse. I'm surprised no one thought of it sooner--a BAR ACROSS THE STREET FROM THE LAW SCHOOL. Location really is everything.

Credit for having a great beer selection.

Points off for:
-questionable cocktails
-bad house wine
-food with potential poorly executed
-but mostly for slipping in a few extra dollars on my cc bill

Wow.

It is still a hotel lobby but a hell of a lot more comfortable and a major upgrade from what is was before. Dark wood,  Fireplace, Couches, Really nice pool table and a lot of beer.  Food looked and smelled excellent but i didn't order food so i can't really speak to it.

They have an impressive tap list and a full bar as well. They had both beers one would expect as well as exciting things like Firestone Walker Velvet Merlin and Le Merle Saison and Lost Abbey Deliverance. Friendly staff as well. 

If i'm in Berkeley i will definitely visit again.
Now that Raleigh's burned down this is going to be my new spot. They have a great beer selection. I haven't tried their food yet but their overall customer service and vibe was great.

Ugh....this place is so bad! Will expand on this later. Do not go here though until they improve their food..
---

Edit: Ordered the
1. Mac n' Cheese: it was whatever - nothing particularly special and felt really heavy in my stomach.
2. Pork Chops: probably the only thing that was tasty on the menu! The meat is juicy and...that's all I really have to say about it.
3. Skirt Steak: SOOOO BAD. I asked for a rare/medium rare steak knowing that restaurants always cook it a little longer than you ask for, BUT THIS FOOL GIVES ME A WELL-DONE STEAK THAT IS BASICALLY BURNT. (Because they cook all their meat on a grill) Ugh, it was gross. I totally would've complained and let them know how bad it was if my super nice friend didn't want to cause any drama. 

Never coming here againnnnn shiet. The person below me who rated this place a 5 has either never tasted real food or is affiliated with the owner looool blech.

Thank goodness for Freehouse.  After spending my first few weeks in Berkeley fighting throes of undergraduate students to get a beer, I was pleased by the prompt service, booze selection and ambiance of Freehouse. 

Frankly, I certainly can't hate on a place that has a huge patio with heat lamps, fireplaces, comfy furniture, a nice beer selection and a SUPREME whiskey selection (ooh, lawwdy!). 

My boyfriend and I stumbled in for supper on a Wednesday and really enjoyed ourselves.  The service was good, drink selection was great, and our food was nice.  Granted, we had the pizza of the day and split a wedge salad which aren't terribly difficult dishes; I've never met a pizza I didn't like and I would consider drinking bleu cheese.  Still, we were pleased.

My only complaint is their very limited wine choices but seeing as cooler temperatures are on the way, I'll happily stick to beer and whiskey! 

Good on ya, Freehouse!

It's been awhile since I've Yelped and Free House was just the place to inspire me to start reviewing again. I never thought I'd have the opportunity to have the best pork chop ever until Chef Kevin emailed me to let me know his menu is up and running at Free House. I usually like to stick to my area of the Bay, but it's definitely worth a trip out to Berkeley to visit Free House. Ambience is great, Beer selection looks on point (couldn't try out any beers due to being preggers). But the FOOD, my oh my, that's where it's at. Started off with the pretzel, mac & cheese, and black bean cakes. All worth trying. Then it was on to the Pork Chop....let's just say it was heaven! The hubby had the cassoulet, he loved it as well. Our friend had the skirt steak and cleaned the plate off. Ended with dessert, strawberry shortcake and bread pudding. They definitely don't skimp on the portions. 

I will definitely be back! A special thank you to Chef Kevin for his hospitality!

I had an opportunity to see the bar, have some drinks, and try a lot of the food, and this place is going to revolutionize going out in Berkeley.

It has an awesome main room that might get a little crowded when full, but there's also a fireplace with some couches and lounging area for relaxing.

The food was very good.  I recommend getting several appetizers to share at a table (pretzel with dipping sauces, mac n cheese add some bacon, and cucumber salad were all fantastic), and then skipping right to a dessert of the peanut butter cookie, if you aren't hungry enough for a full meal.  The appetizer fries are very well seasoned.

There is also a nice courtyard which is protected so it wasn't too windy.  Space heaters make it quite nice even when it is a little cold.

It has very good music for people of a certain age group (mid 20's to mid 30's), good lighting, and an overall very pleasant atmosphere.  It isn't so loud that you can't have a conversation but also not too quiet.

This place has a great feel to it. It is definitely more upscale than all the bars in Berkeley yet still feels very cozy. I absolutely love the outside patio portion of it and really can't wait to eat out there during the day (but I went Saturday and it didn't open till 5). 
They have an insane selection of whiskey which isn't my drink of choice but I had some and it was reasonably priced ($6 for about 2.5 shots). The bar tenders and waiters are super friendly. Seeing that whiskey isn't my thing, the bartender was super helpful in helping me choose one. 

Now about the food- so good. We ordered the fries which came in a bucket and had chipotle ketchup, garlic aioli, and curry aioli as dipping sauces. Loved the first two, curry just isn't my thing either. This was about $6
Also tried the mussels which were delicious. The broth they come in was so good. The server brought us extra bread to dip it in. It also came with a side of fries too which was great for the leftover sauces. This appetizer was $12 which was well worth it since it came with about 20 mussels. 


I definitely see this becoming somewhere I will go whenever I want to get away from the younger crowds in Berkeley (not that I myself am older). But it's nice to pretend every now and then. I can picture it now-- me sipping on some whiskey next to the fire place, eating my mussels. Can't wait.

The chicken or pork banh mi sandwiches on toasted roll are so delicious, as is the pho.  I only wish they offered more veggie dishes, but for cheap eats on the Berkeley campus, this place can't be beat ~ excellent!

I would have given it 4 or even 5 stars, but...

I literally waited HALF AN HOUR for Vietnamese Iced Coffee. I placed my order at 3:19pm and was told by the person behind the counter that "it will take a while because we have to make it fresh". Fair enough. I've had Vietnamese coffee before and I knew the process of making the drip coffee takes a little longer than other coffee brewing methods.

I took my order of stewed beef with a hunk of bread, sat down and ate my food. I was hoping the coffee would be ready by the time I was done eating (by the latest). Not true. It wasn't until around 3:50pm that the coffee I ordered was ready. Seriously???? Every other time I've had drip coffee it took maybe 10 minutes at most, but HALF AN HOUR? Apparently, another unlucky person also ordered the same thing and I guess the employees didn't know that neither of us had been given the coffee...

Luckily I had a little bit of time to wait otherwise I would have asked for a refund. The owner (I believe) sort of realized I was waiting for a while and also included one egg roll when he gave me my coffee. This is just unacceptable. Maybe if they're able to find a way to speed things instead of making people wait half an hour for Vietnamese Iced Coffee that I'll consider writing another review.

On a more positive closing note, they do offer 20% off your entire order if you're a Berkeley student or staff member which is definitely nice. In addition, it is also helpful that they accept credit cards.

Fast and convenient, but not good.

Let's start with what's good. They give a 20% to Cal students! Their jasmine green milk tea is a winner. It smells so good and tastes just as it smells. It's not watered down like at other places. I have also heard that their pho is decent in comparison to other places around campus.

Onward to the bad. The Viet sandwiches here are NOT good. I tried it after my Viet friend told me that it was good, but I was disappointed. It was so sweet, and I had to drench it in sriracha. I decided to give this place another try when they had a munch on me deal for their shrimp and chicken salad. The salad was fresh, but there was something missing. The dressing that they put on it didn't complement the shrimp and chicken very well and I had to ask for extra to even taste it. It's so liquidy that all the dressing ends up going to the bottom. It doesn't stick to anything, so you end up with a pool of dressing when you finish eating the bare lettuce.

Sigh. I wish this place was better, so that I could fulfill my cravings for a legit Viet sandwich.

Stuff here is really cheap but I've found it to be extremely greasy. However, it definitely is a great choice if you want something really worth its price and quick. Lots of ready to take out pre-packed rice plates. Also, the lady who works here is really friendly.

I always get the rice plates with bbq/teriyaki chicken. Again, super oily but really flavorful. However, I tend to avoid he fish sauce as it's pretty darn strong and makes me smell like fish all day.

Just a tip, something that many people may not know: I used to come here during closing hours and everything is half off - $2.50 for a rice plate is a HUGE steal. So worth it!
The food isn't that bad. The only problem I have is how can you run out of nuoc nam in the middle of the day?! At least warn me before I ordered the Vermicelli noodles.

On my previous visit, I had complained about very greasy food, so I went back here today as they had a munchonme deal-- $2.95 for a shrimp & chicken salad. I was not impressed. 

The 'salad' consisted of bean sprouts, iceberg lettuce, pickled daikon and carrots, boiled chicken and shrimp. Portion size was fine for a three dollar meal... my problem with the dish was that it was so SOUR. I think the guy who prepared my salad had been soaking the shrimp in some brine, and adding this same brine to my salad. I also thought the salad would come with some nuoc mam as shown on the munch on me picture, but I guess not. 

I've given this place multiple tries. In fact, I had their grilled chicken banh mi the other day. They had toasted the bun with the pickled veggies inside, making them warm and disgusting. There was also no cilantro in my sandwich, too much mayo, and the chicken juices made the sandwich soggy. Still great customer service and the food tastes fresh... just not very delicious.

This place is great. I'm really glad we got some better food than the one we used to have last year. I've been to all three new stands and they are all really good at great prices. 

I've tried a couple of things a

I never did understand why Tacontento was so expensive.

I've tried to try the different foods that they have. DO not get the tacos! They are really bad. I had heard about Korean Tacos being really good in LA food trucks but not these. These were gross.

I've ate here like hmphhhh 5 times? My cravings for pho go crazy while I'm on campus. Coming from Oakland, where there are like hundreds of pho joints, I always give in to Saigon Eats even though it's not that good.

It's not authentic. Price is alright, $7 for a bowl? Not bad I suppose, compared to the other prices. It definitely gets you full.

Super greasy, they only give like 2 pieces of napkins. 

They say they have wonton pho but I don't see it...so I just ordered beef pho all the time. 

I recommend if you're super hungry and craving.

I tried the entree with two items and a side(teriyaki chicken, a tangy grilled chicken, and fried rice). Everything was just okay, but i did enjoy it and would probably go back if i wanted a good deal and some asian-like food. Although the rice was a bit oily, it was less oily than i would have expected and everything seemed fresh. It was a really good deal for a big plate of food for less than $5.

The staff were also really friendly and it definitely seems very clean. Don't come here expecting good authentic vietnamese food, but for a convenient meal and inexpensive meal, this is a pretty good choice.
Banh Mi's are tasty. Hands down. Finally something decent opened up in Lower Sproul. This accommodates for the loss of Tacotento!

When I went here I got one of the combo plates, which is like Panda express I guess, only worse. The chow mein was like the kind you buy in a packet and then stir with water on your stove, super soggy and not really good in any way. The orange (i think it was orange anyway, although you can substitute whatever saucy fried chinese adjective you like) chicken was about as bad as it could be, where the outside was mushy and the inside was crispy (its supposed to be the other way around!), think, soggy bread in neon orange corn syrup covering dried, hard, flavorless "meat" below. I also had eggplant chicken that I think they wanted to have a barbeque flavor but tried getting it with some sort of spary on barbeque flavoring that made it end up tasting like my old asian relatives smell, namely like mothballs, grease, and the looming prospect of death.

 All of the hot entree items looked artificial and soggy like they were prepared from the freezer section of trader joe's. The price isn't very good either, you could eat the same thing only better (dare I say it) at the chinese express place down the street for $5, whereas it costs about $6.50 here. One could only hope the pho and sandwiches here are better, but I have no reason to believe that they would be. 

With so many decent ethnic options near campus, and many other on campus dining options, there isn't really any reason why you should eat here.

I had the Pho today here and it was alright. I ordered chicken and they gave me beef, I guess they just get way to busy during lunch time to get the order rights but it was still alright. It didn't quite fill me up though, I was hungry again a couple of hours later. Maybe I'll get a sandwich next time, I heard they are good here.

Being a student at UC Berkeley, cuisine gets repetitive and old quickly. However, coming across this little hole in the wall restaurant really freshened up my daily lunches after class. Saigon Eats offers the convenience and friendliness to all students at an affordable price. You can get a large Vietnamese Sandwich for under $6, a flavorful meal that is hard to come by in an area surrounded by bland sandwiches (next door is Subway).
Along with the cheap price and friendly service, the food is very flavorful and diverse. It offers a Panda Express style assortment of Vietnamese dishes, you can choose a side of fried rice or garlic noodles (garlic noodles is bomb in my opinion), and entrees ranging from tropical chicken to vegetarian dishes (my favorite is the grilled pork, uber good and authentic). They also offer pho, vermicelli noodles, and Vietnamese tacos which I have yet to try. 
It is also conveniently located in Lower Sproul , and the wait for the food is very short, time efficient for busy students. Portions are very large as well, good bang for the buck.

ZOMG! I tried Banh Mi sandwich with for the first time last week upon the insistence of a friend, and it was so delicious! And with the student discount, the sandwich only cost $3.60! I got the pork sandwich and it was large. Beats any other hot sandwich in the area! I will be coming back again next week^.^~

I notice they also offer coupons on their website, for a free spring roll if you sign up for their newsletter. Ahh! ^.~^.^~

Pretty good food considering that this is a food truck. The food is super cheap and if you are in a rush and need to grab something to eat quickly, this is a good place to try. I had their Vietnamese combo sandwich and thought it was pretty good. I wished there were more veggies though. :\ The lady working the cash register and taking orders was super nice and gave me a small cup of free egg drop soup (delicious). Not sure if they had that on their menu but if they do I'll definitely buy some next time.

The pork is cripsy with a nice spice. I've only tried the sandwich with pork and am having difficulty branching out from there cause it's so good. Ask for some Sriracha if you like it even more spicy. Yes, the rumors of 20% student discount are true, hopefully not just temporary while they build a following. Really accommodating staff, also hope this doesn't change.

I used to hate the ASUC Food Court. With the mediocre exception of the sandwiches at Coffee Spot, there was nothing good down here. 

I ventured down here last week and discovered Saigon Eats, which serves my favourite sandwich of all time-- the banh mi! It's under four bucks (with the Cal discount, guys) for a plentiful amount of hot grilled pork, pickled carrots and daikon, jalapeno, and delicious crusty baguette (seriously, it's crusty and gets all over the place-- just don't think about it while you're chowing down). The servers are very friendly and I really hope they can make it work in this spot-- their prices are great, their food is delicious, and I hope they don't leave. It's also sort of funny to sit and eat a stellar banh mi while looking at the deserted new Subway right next to Saigon Eats.

A new restaurant on Lower Sproul! Maybe this will fire up the ASUC-owned restaurants. They also have a coalition with Munch On Me, which I'm guessing to be a newly launched deal website, and I was able to get a free thai ice tea voucher to use, which is what brought me here!

When I got there, it was about 1:50, and posted all over the counter was the fact that they're not accepting coupon until after 2:00pm. Since I wanted the thai ice tea, I was going to wait. 

I was a bit hungry, and decided to get their two-entree plate, with terriyaki chicken, and also broccoli and beef with fried rice. In retrospect, it's kind of weird that a Saigon (Vietnam) place would offer terriyaki and thai tea... 

For a total of $5, the price can't be beat. (It was only $6ish and they have 20% for students, which I really appreciate. I don't know how long that's going to last, though). The food is kind of greasy, and the broccoli felt way undercooked. It's a bit disappointing, actually. All in all, I felt that the rice plate at 99 Ranch is way better than this. Also, this is not self-serve, so your portions are determined by how generous your waitress is feeling (although it was pretty generous, actually). I didn't get to try the sandwiches that everyone talk about, so I guess I'll try that next time I stop by. With so many options, though, I wonder if I'll stop by Lower Sproul again without an incentive, for food.

The thai ice tea, on the other hand, is actually quite amazing! It's decent compared to some thai places around Berkeley. Definitely recommend for a quick drink.

The Short:
* Semblances of authentic Vietnamese food.
* Come for a bite if you're in a rush, or in dire need of Vietnamese food.

Located in Lower Sproul Plaza on the UC Berkeley Campus, this eatery was recently renovated early in 2011. With a new, more modern looking venue, the place looks appetizing. Unfortunately, the food can't match its appearance. I have had their Vietnamese sandwiches, Combination Pho, and Vietnamese Iced Coffee and all three left much to be desired.

Vietnamese Sandwich: It has the look and feel of your typical vWich with its toasty bread, parsley, jalapenos, and etc, but the meat really threw it off. I got the grilled pork, and the offbeat flavor left an unusual aftertaste. It was filling though.

Vietnamese Iced Coffee: It was nice to see that they make it with those old school drips and condensed milk, as expected. While it has the robust flavor you would expect, the texture of the coffee was not as smooth as I had hoped. But props to them for actually having it.

Combination Pho: It was interesting how they made it, but its understandable to have most of the items precooked and then dropped into hot broth to ensure that they are cooked. But this left the chicken overcooked and tough. There were some additions such as BBQ pork and wontons that gave it a more Chinese feel than your typical beef flank and rare steak that you'd find in a combination pho. Not exactly the best thing, but it was appetizing. The nicest part would be the broth, which was not drenched in oil or lacking flavor. Satisfying for sure though. 

Recommendations:
* Combination Pho (be sure to avoid ordering the Chicken Pho)

Pros:
+ Decent food on campus.
+ 20% discount for Berkeley students and faculty.
+ Clean venue.
+ Good variety of drinks and "quick eats" (pre-made Spring rolls, etc).
+ Takes credit card.

Cons:
- Not that authentic. You'd find better elsewhere.

Looking back, I see that I gave three stars to the Healthy Heavenly outfit that Saigon Eats replaced.  I argued that HH deserved a tad more than 2.5 stars and rounded up to three.

I feel the same way about Saigon Eats, which I regard as a tiny upgrade from their Healthy predecessor.  Unfortunately, the pho here is not worthy of a detour unless you happen to be standing on Bancroft Street with a slice of Blondie's pizza in the back of your mind.  I had the tofu pho, which set me back $5.65.  It was arguably A-OK but it's not likely to be an experience that I'll repeat soon.  The main result of today's lunch is that I'm now more motivated than ever to go down to the high-scoring pho places in Oakland that some of my yelp friends have been touting.

Out with the old and in the with new right? Healthy Heaven, a long time staple of the lower sproul plaza, closed down a year or two ago and now a new vietnamese "fast food" joint has opened up right next to the new Subway. 

Saigon Eats is quick, pick up food and go type of place. They have a nice stream-tray variety, where you can get rice or noodles with two entrees for $5.95. They also have banh mi's for $4.50, pho ($5.95), vermicelli cold plates ($5.95), salads, and spring rolls ($3.25). 

I tried out their stream tray food between classes, it wasn't too busy, cause it just opened and not a lot of people know about it. I got the pineapple fried rice, teriyaki chicken, and grilled pork. OMG GRILLED PORK GALORE! But seriously, that shit was good! It was juicy, had a lot of flavor, and was cooked well. The pineapple fried rice was mediocre and so was the teriyaki chicken. My girlfriend got the garlic noodles, fire-roasted chicken, and the lemongrass chicken. If you like Panda Express, you'll love this place. It's like a cheaper better version of Panda. The lemongrass chicken and the fire-grass chicken were both phenomenal. If you can't eat spicy food though, avoid the fire-roasted chicken. I really loved the garlic noodles too! 

Basically a cheap and better tasting Panda Express with some nice Vietnamese options. Fast, and UC Berkeley students get 20% off!

Pros:
- Great food!
- Try the grilled pork, garlic noodles, lemon grass chicken, and fire-roasted chicken
- UC Berkeley students get 20% off
- Fast Service
- They have Asian drinks!
- Accepts Credit Cards

Cons:
- Banh Mi's are expensive
- Spring Rolls are expensive

Here is their facebook page:
http://www.facebook.com/pages/Saigon-Eats-Berkeley/113853028677408

Meh, decent food for a good price.

Food: I'd recommend the sandwiches! They're always really tasty, and super cheap. You can't beat paying less than $3 for them. The entree meals, on the other hand, are really inconsistent. The first time I had it, the orange chicken was pretty amazing! The second time I went a few weeks later, they tasted totally different and soggy. It made me sad. Also...THE ASIAN WRAPS ARE DISGUSTING. I felt sick after eating it - the taste just isn't good at all. Spring rolls are good, but not as good as the place that was there before it. Haven't tried their pho.

Price: 20% off for Cal students/faculty...awesome.

Service: Fast and friendly. They are always nice and always quick.

If you're hungry, in a rush, on campus, and want Vietnamese food, go here (I guess that narrows a lot down for you, though).

I eat here ALOT! basically bc its on campus and sooo cheap, like most food places on campus, but its not the best viet place you'll find. STaff here is VERY friendly, the boss would make sure your soup is hot and to the best that it can be before serving you.

But even that, the pho is 5.50 for a reeeally small bowl that you can eat in 15 min. i mainly get there hot entree only less than 5$ except its ssoooo oily if you get the noodles, it was dripping in my bowl and then your mouth gets all oily so you can't eat it everyday cuz you get tired. But the good thing is that they do give you lettuce with it to partially balance it out.

THeir tacos are too shabby, but sometimes I get it cold and its not so great after a while. I got like 10 salads from munchonme for lunch. not so great, but its 3$ for lunch, sooo plain, everything taste like water lettuce, even the shrimp with no flavor and the dry chicken which also has no flavor. But either way is soo cheap and close I keep comin back.

Decent pricing for large amount of food. 20% for Cal students and staff. Got a hot entree combo with chow mein and 2 dishes: orange chicken and broccoli beef. Sadly their hot food feels cold. No flavor in chow mein so you would have to borrow your dishes to add flavor. The orange chicken had more flour than chicken, I don't recall biting into a piece of chicken larger than my pinky. Broccoli was undercooked and too salty. Beef was overbooked, some were burnt. I must say that this is one of the few times where I have to throw my food away.

TIP: You can get 1 FREE taco or 1 FREE Thai iced tea if you sign up on Munchonme.com!

TIP: Berkeley students get 20% off their entire bill!

After Berkeley got rid of the mom and pop shops down in Lower Sproul Plaza, I was hesitant to try any of the new eateries there, but since I had a coupon for a free taco, I was enticed to try it out.

ATMOSPHERE
This place gets extra points for convenience. It's literally right on campus so it's an easy go-to spot if you're short on time. They're open for dinner too, so you can snag a bite before a meeting.

Lower Sproul Plaza is like a food court, so the environment is very crowded and it's a free-for-all when it comes to seating. The upside is that you and your group of friends can eat different foods from different places and still sit together.

The workers at Saigon Eats are mostly students and they were very friendly. The booth itself is a lot cleaner than the old one and they seemed pretty tech savvy, what with them using iPads to take my order. The colors are bright and it helped make the food look tasty.

FOOD
There seem to be a lot of choices and I noticed them advertising their traditional Vietnamese dishes. You can order customized meals (imagine Panda Express), on-the-spot cooking, or grab and go sandwiches/spring rolls. Everything looked pretty good but I was only there for my taco.

The ASIAN TACO can be either chicken or pork; I chose pork. I thought it was going to be dinky, but to my surprised it was a HUGE taco. No joke, it was probably the biggest taco I've ever had. It reminded me a lot of a street taco, except bigger and overflowing with ingredients.

The pork was seasoned and flavored well, but there was too much sauce, making it an extremely messy dish. It was piled high with cilantro, bean sprouts, carrots, lettuce and tasty chili sauce. I give it another point for actually being SPICY!! I had to drink a lot of water! It was served in a paper dish like the ones normally used to serve an order of french fries. The taco normally costs $1.39ish, and if they're all that big then damn, what a steal!

Since the flavors and the portions were good, I would definitely come back in the future. Hooray, Saigon Eats, you have just garnered another loyal customer!

One word: gross.

Worst banh mi I've ever tasted in my entire life. That's saying a lot considering I grew up eating banh mi at least a few times a week. I couldn't even finish half of my sandwich because of how dry it was. What a shame because it also happened to be overpriced. If anyone charges you over $3 for banh mi, you're getting ripped off.

Oh yeah, their Vietnamese coffee was super diluted as well. You're supposed to feel as if you just chugged down 50 packets of sugar when you drink Vietnamese coffee.

I used to LOVE this place. Seriously, I thought this would be my go to place for Vietnamese food - not the Vietnamese take on Chinese take out  style of their combo plates, but the banh mi's and fresh chicken and shrimp salad with vietnamese dressing. 

But not anymore :( I tried out the place several times during the semester and it has gone DOWNHILL in food quality since the summer ended. The fall semester's food is not so great. Their garlic noodles are super oily and even oilier is their rice. How is that possible?! The orange chicken is like one nip of chicken surrounded by a huge HUGE mass of flour or whatever makes up the crunchy outer layer. And it didn't even taste like orange chicken o__O! Gurrll, I am not even exaggerating!

Their jasmine milk tea (used to be my favorite) is now tasting nothing like jasmine or milk or tea...I don't even knowww.

I'm utterly disappointed at how the food is turning out. It was my go-to place before for healthy eats. It doesn't even taste like vietnamese food anymore...whaththeheckkk?!!?

Has there been new management? I keep seeing new

I was craving a Thai ice tea for days. My co-worker told me that Saigon Eats has cheap Thai ice tea and urged my to get one so I caved in. 

It took a while to get the drink because the employees were occupied with refilling soups. One caveat: when the lady was filing my cup, she adds ice to the top of the cup rim! Ask for little ice. I opted for no ice which made my drink super sweet. For $2.20 (originally $2.50+tax) the drink was average. If I was at home in SF, I would have got TeaWay for $.02 cheaper and I get a stamp card. Anyway, the aftertaste was on the sweet end but typical. I'll be back to try the food next time.

Saigon Eats, you may just be that force that might make me start eating out on campus again. I was on the way home one day, when I bumped into a good friend I haven't seen in a while. He's related to the owner of Saigon Eats, and I just happened to have a Munch on Me coupon as well as an appetite, so I decided to give it a try. 

I got the Asian Taco, which came with a choice of pork or chicken (I got pork), the typical veggies, and some sauce. For a free meal, it was a pretty good deal! The pork seemed to be honey glazed, and they put A LOT of it in there, which was awesome. Very well prepared, not too sweet, and very tender. The veggies were all very fresh and so was the tortilla. A smart concept that usually costs only $2, but got me pretty full right away. I don't know what it was about it, but it was just so tasty and fresh.

Now I have to try out the rest of the menu and see if this 5 star review will be able to maintain itself. I definitely hope so!

I've gotten a bento box here once, some time ago, I think, so I can't vouch for the sushi or tempura (I generally don't like tempura), but I don't remember the bento being super awful or super delicious. For the prices, really, I've no complaints. As far as I'm concerned, Japanese restaurants are like steak houses. You really need quality ingredients to get quality sushi, and quality ingredients are going to be expensive. If you go to a cheap Japanese restaurant you can't have the same expectations. For high quality sushi, Kirala is the only place I've been to that is close to campus that serves really good sushi (and I'm almost certain I've been to them all), but be prepared to pay 2-5 times as much. You get what you pay for, and for the prices at Aki the food is totally reasonable. 

The reason I insist on 5 stars for this place is because on Wednesday nights this place serves authentic Taiwanese food that is absolutely delicious and super cheap. We ordered a WHOLE FISH and two ginormous taiwanese empanada things. They meal also came with a soup and rice, gratis. Everything they served us was delicious, and service was super speedy. The whole meal cost the two of us $13 total ($6.50 each!). I would have been content to pay twice as much. If you're in the area on a wednesday night, I cannot emphasize how highly I recommend this place. Ask for the Taiwanese menu and forego the sushi.

I haven't tried their sushi, because for some reason, I just don't trust for it to come from here. I had a couple of their cooked rice plates, and they were just okay.  The tonkatsu wasn't as crispy as I prefer, and the sauce just wasn't as tasty as others in the area.  =(

My gf and came here one weekend because, unfortunately, all the asian stores in the northside asian ghetto were closed except this one. (I don't why that was..)

I know my fish and I know when and where to get the best of fish;  My instincts told me not to order nigiris here but ......=(.... I did, and I regretted it.  Salmon was blah!!! It was gummy, smelled realllly fishy (fresh sashimi should have very little to no stinky fish odor).  STAY AWAY FROM THE RAW FISH HERE!

As for cooked entrees, we had the tonkatsu and salmon teriyaki.  Tonkatsu was great!  Served hot and crispy; not too oily at all.  However, slightly pricy for just fried pork over rice.  Salmon Teriyaki was pretty standard.  I had it as part of the bento box if I remember correctly so I'm not quite sure if it was worth the money.

So leeson learned, cooked entrees here are good, but stay away from the sashimi! Therefore 2 stars.
nice little tucked away restaraunt. on the northside of campus in restaraunt/cafe row. The tempura, rice, salad good. I loved the tea.  great for lunch.

Been here so many times ! The food is really good and the service is always great. I love their chicken tempura....it's mouth watering! It's my favorite...along with the tempura udon with the egg and veggies!

Okay, so this place isn't amazing.  But it's Japanese food, I'm Japanese, it makes me happy.  I've only gotten the tonkatsu don here (breaded and fried pork with eggs and onions over rice) which I can safely say is somewhat of a comfort food to me.  

Tip #1:  they only take credit/debit over $10.  I think last time they gave me this tiny little voucher--literally the size of a stamp--for the difference between my dish and $10.  Of course, I lost it before I even stepped out of the restaurant.  

Overall:  Decent, nothing amazing and not the best Japanese restaurant around, pretty cheap for a good amount.

Reasonable price
You get what you pay for
Pretty crowded with Berkeley students during the lunch hours

don't get noodles they suck
but their rice bowls are ok

This place is tiny, warm, and cozy. I don't care what people say, maybe the food isn't the best in the world, but its still -good-. You're getting a bento box with loads of japanese food for 8 bucks, what do you really expect? I think that for the price, this place goes above the bar. If you want to spend $30 for something mind-blowing, go to Yusan. But if you're in berkeley, have 8 bucks and want a warm japanese meal, go to Aki's.

I always get their teriyaki rice bowls here, and for ~$6 they are as good as it gets.  The meat and other ingredients always seems fresh and quality.  If you get a fish or salmon rice bowl, they use a fish batter that they make themselves.  They also make their own teriyaki sauce.

You gotta come here for lunch, yo!
We ordered the sushi bento box. I got the eel sushi. Pretty much everything was good--only thing I had an issue with was that they were pretty chincy with the ginger and wasabe, and they didn't give us our water until the end of the meal (?!?).
The bento box was about $9.00 for lunch.

So I had the fresh eel roll, and my friends had the chicken udon. The food was great, no complaints there... But, the service wasn't, so minus a star there, she forced us to sit outside, then just kind of slammed our check down before we even got like two bites of our meals, now THAT was kind of rude. Then later on, when we were halfway done, she GLARED at us... wth? So we paid and hightailed it out of there.

Also, I know, I know most food places aren't very sanitary... but we saw them drying their leeks out in the eating area, the outside eating area, so there were a bunch of flies humming all over it, and over the course of our meal, I saw them coming to take some leeks to use in dishes. So minus another star for that.

Add a really bland shrimp udon the other day, with at most 5 shrimps hiding under the noodle. Nothing to be really excited about. Even in this creepy northside "asian ghetto", there are better places to go.

I've gotten quality Japanese entrees at this place on a regular basis. As one of the plaza employees, I sample all of the other places' dishes and Aki has it down. People have mentioned that this place is a kind of a hole in the wall kind of restaurant but the entire plaza is built that way so ambience and setting shouldn't really be taken into consideration. All those yelpers that think this place is below par haven't taken into consideration the low price and location of this restaurant. Like some reviews have said, owning a sushi place is like owning a steak house. Ultimately, the quality of the entree is in the quality of the meat served. Aki offers decent prices for above average quality fish and entrees. Granted, compared to Kirala or other gourmet sushi houses, Aki pales in comparison. But if you're in the area and in the mood for Japanese, Aki's is the place to go. Noone on southside offers the same genre of food, and Mitch, the owner, himself is a kind and reasonable guy so if there's something wrong with your dish or you would like something more with your meal, he is more than willing to work with you. I highly recommend the service and food at this place, take it from a current plaza employee.

The North Side Ghetto's Japanese restaurant monopoly. When you're uphill on this quiet side and craving for Japanese food, this is the place to go.

I usually order their udon here since they fill me up for a decent price. I've tried their dumpling udon and chicken udon. They give you quite a lot of veggies. The soup is sweet and light. To me it's just right, it might be lacking taste for most. Their noodles were slightly flatter than the udon I would get from the store. Nonetheless, it tastes great. I ordered their Katsu Don today. It was alright, had better ones before. I liked Tako Sushi's donburi more. Tried their salmon sushi roll before. Too little fish and the sushi pieces didn't look too pro (rice was kinda falling apart).

The restaurant is small, so sit tight with your friends. Definitely not a place to go to when you're in a big group. Quick service but the lady never seems to smile at you.

Ahhh... the memories that come back with a hot chicken tempura donburi at Aki's.  I had forgotten about this dish, but used to eat it a lot while in Berkeley.  It was good years ago, and nothing has changed, which is both good and rare these days.  We also ordered the donkatsu donburi today too, and it was good.

It seems a little a bit generous to give a small hole-in-the-wall college eatery four stars, and mainly based on one dish, but I thought this one dish deserved the four stars.

Update:
I lowered it one star due to inconsistency in food preparation.  Sometimes the chicken tempura is really good and other times its burnt.
Cozy environment... the decor immitates a Japanese style home.

The food is quite good. The waiter who dresses G is the nicest guy ever and a really good waiter. I think the restaurant is family run.

And as I read in Jessica C.'s review "tempura chicken is to die for"

Place is cute, food is meh.  

Free green tea to start the meal, which is great on cold winter days. The rice bowls are probably the best deals, as they come with free Miso soup, and anything with teriyaki sauce on it is pretty decent.  The cooked fish can also be pretty good.  The sushi is HORRIBLE, and tastes like it was previously frozen.  The gyoza also tastes like it came out of a freezer bag, and I advise against ordering it.

I like Japanese food and really want this place to be better, but am usually left disappointed and a little hungry.  However, the food at least feels a little healthier than other Asian options on North Campus, and the little booths are cozy, so I will no doubt occasionally be drawn back in.

I came here once with some friends after a basketball game so we were all hungry and I'm sure that made the food taste better.  I don't even know what I had because my friend knew the people who worked there so they ordered for us and gave us some sort of discount on the food.  We ended up having something I would think is like chicken katsu.  

The reason I gave it four stars is the chicken was pretty good.  It had to do mostly with the breading.  It had this odd sweetness to it that most other chicken katsu or imitations of it I've had doesn't have.  The breading was light, yet you tasted it.   For that alone, I give it an extra star to four.  I would go back and order that if I knew what it's called!

I went here the first time here during their off-hours (around 5 PM for dinner) because I was finished with class early.

Even though I was sitting outside and there were flies trying to swarm my food, the service here is great and the food, soup, and tea were hot (and not lukewarm).
Yes, as far as I know it's still there. It's still good, still reasonably priced and still worth the walk up the hill.

Is it good _Japanese_ food? Hardly
Nonetheless, it's one of the places I like more in the Hearst food court. You get your food fairly quickly (unlike the vietnamese place). They have perhaps the best variety with udon, katsu, sukiyaki, donburi, tempura, etc. And most importantly, it's sufficiently good that I can enjoy the taste. 

Only in the Heart food court does this get 4 stars, but it makes me less depressed at the lack of decent lunchtime food options.

Run by Chinese people, not truly Japanese food... been there a few times to give it a chance... the chicken tempura is awesome.... not really Japanese, but damn good.

the BAD -- sukiyaki beef was TERRIBLE...

Oh -- no credit cards unless you charge $10. (It's illegal to have a minimum charge, by the way)

Very cramped, small space. Seats are hard wood, 90 degree upright

The free tea was a great way to start the meal. The free miso soup was cool too! The food was okay. The prices were okay.

The owner / worker reading the newspaper at the entrance farting while I was eating was not okay.

Hearing a *BRRRRAAPPPPPP* a few bites into your lunch is a really unappetizing way to start a meal. It would have been one thing if the flatulent emission had been short and sweet. No, it was long and drawn out. The guard at the door clearly knew what she was doing when she let out a second *tooooooooooot* a few minutes later. She was telling me to quickly finish my meal and get out. This was reinforced by the bill that quickly came to my table a few minutes later with a tootsie roll on it. A brown tootsie roll? REALLY?

Don't think of this as an authentic Japanese restaurant, because you're going to be disappointed. The tempura isn't done in the Japanese style, the sushi is crappy, the tea isn't barley tea, and the bento is overrated and too expensive for my taste. 

So why am I giving this place 4 stars? Because this place is run by a Taiwanese family, and their tempura is done in a delicious Taiwanese style that reminds me of Taipei, not Tokyo. Also, on Wednesday nights, they prepare Taiwanese comfort food, such as stir-fried vermicelli, ground pork rice, beef noodles, dumplings and buns, Taiwanese-style soups, and so much other Taiwanese authentic goodness that it blows all the other Taiwanese places in Berkeley out of the water. If you're a Berkeley student looking for good Taiwanese food, you cannot afford to miss this place on Wednesdays. Be sure to ask for their specials, because it changes every week. 

Also, the service here is easily the nicest on campus. The waitress will care for you and make sure you're doing okay, and sometimes offers extra soup if it looks like you're freezing on a cold winter night. 

So unless you're here for the chicken tempura donburi for lunch or the fish teriyaki rice for dinner, skip this place and come back on Wednesday nights. You won't regret it.
The cooked Japanese dishes here are not that good, but the sushi is actually quite bad.

Inside of a little chinatown, the place wasnt bad. Came here for lunch, and you would expect the speed of service to be faster, but it wasn't. The food wasnt bad though. Make sure you bring cash. Actually, just always have cash on you when you are in berkeley since many places only take cash

It is definetely the best Japanese-style Chinese food ive had.  It is certainly not authentic but it still tastes good.   I usually stick to the katsu-don or other rice bowls but my friends love the tempura.  It is cheap and looks clean, but I am still a little scared to try the sushi.

I don't normally yelp-- unless it's to defend small hole-in-the-walls like Aki. 

First of all, a lot of yelpers wrote bad reviews because they ordered raw fish. And I'm sure these yelp elites have "excellent palates" because they have tried $100 sashimi before. Come on--why would you even consider ordering raw fish at a place like this? No offense to Aki but clearly this place isn't for sushi. These yelpers are idiots-- once you step into Aki, you just know this place is known for dishes other than raw fish. Also, yeah this place isn't as clean as Chez Panisse, but come on-- this restaurant is so much cleaner than any restaurant in south/north ghetto. These yelp elite comments are ridiculous and so high maintenance. 

Please come here at least to try the CHICKEN TEMPURA DON ($6). I've attached a picture for your convenience: http://imgur.com/31wLz. This lightly breaded chicken is so moist and it is perfectly crispy. It comes on top of rice with a side of pickled/sour vegetables and miso soup. The only thing that can make this meal more satisfying is adding a Sapporo. 

And yes, this restaurant is owned by a Taiwanese couple. Omg how horrifying-- this place isn't owned by real japanese people?! Uhhhh every other Japanese restaurant in Berkeley is Korean-owned so don't get so don't get so dramatic.

Back in college I loved this place. I think I'd go twice a week after cs lecture. This is like the one place where I would not order sushi. And at Japanese places I always order sushi. 

Simply because their tempura chicken was to die for. It wasn't like classical tempura batter, but this bread crumb mixture. When it came out it was this brown orange hue, never super greasy, but piping hot dark meat chicken. This was such a tiny restaurant. My cs group would have meetings here all the time. Those were the good old days.

To do it right: $11

I've been wanted to write this review for days, but have been conflicted.  3 stars or 4?  I went again today to make up my mind: 4 stars, definitely.

The food here is OK.  The location is OK.  The seating is OK. The prices are OK.  The sushi here is--palatable, I guess.  Why four stars then?  Service!  I stopped by for an early dinner today with my friend, was promptly seated and looked at my menu.  I didn't feel like deciding, so I resolved to get whatever my friend got.  We ended up with a couple of orders of Yaki Udon.  It was surprisingly good, and I would recommend it (if your'e very hungry) after having had several things from the menu.  The Bentou is also pretty decent.

Anyway, like I said, the service is what did it here.  Our waitress was exceedingly patient and on point both bringing and taking dishes away.  The fourth star was secured, however, with the tea.  It just so happened that we emptied our teapot at the exact moment she brought the bill.  I raised the teapot lid as she came to pick up the bill with the money+tip already on it.  To my immense surprise, she came back with a fresh pot of tea, after we had already paid/tipped.  This was not only demonstrative of her awareness, but also her general attitude, seeing as how bringing us more tea wouldn't get us out of the restaurant faster or make the tip any bigger.  This may seem like a small gesture, but an excellent dining experience is at least 50% excellent service, and excellent service is demarcated from OK service by such seemingly small gestures.

Final say: Well played.  They earned that fourth star.

Still there? Located within a little open-air cove with tables surrounded by a number of small food shops off of Hearst, back in the college dizzay, I used to love going to this quaint little Northside japanese joint for a bento box.  Food is quite good and reasonably priced for the students.  That was then, though, and it may very well have gone downhill since or folded up completely.

Oh lord. It looked bad and it was. Much worse than I thought it would be. 

Food: I tried the sukiyaki bento (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/a4QUSAFVvTu7Gv0oegzbXQ?select=IaFpY8fM9dSYMYgEIFHB5w) and was disappointed in all categories. The contents of the bento were pretty sparse compared to what I've seen elsewhere. Couldn't they have put one more item in here, even if just a token addition, to make the box look fuller? I mean, when they say sukiyaki bento, they really mean just sukiyaki, some chicken, and the regular tempura rice combo. The rice occupied one of the squares rather than coming in a bowl so there went another opportunity for more variety. The chicken and tempura were okay to be honest, but the actual "sukiyaki" was just some bland stir fried beef with onions. The meal also came with some miso soup. I didn't feel like what I got was worth what I paid at all. 

Service: Mind-numbingly fast.

Atmosphere: I think the atmosphere of this food court severly damaged my appetite. It looks really dirty in the area with all the sun-faded pictures of food hanging from the windows and flies buzzing around. I probably would've felt much better about eating here if not for that. 

Synopsis: Not my cup of tea at all.

I would propose that this is the coziest restaurant on the northside of campus.  They have great miso soup, pot-stickers, and bento boxes for lunch.  If there is room, definitely sit inside - the atmosphere is too nice to pass up.

EWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW.

I can't just say "ew", I have to stress the "W". Think of W as an upside-down "M". So if something is "mMm good", then what is "wWw?" WoWoW bad. 

This place sucks. It is not cheap for what you order and to think they would have fresh fish in a perpetually empty restaurant on the far end of "Gourmet Ghetto" on top of a hill where only college students venture into is a ridiculous idea. I do not know why I didn't think of that before my roommate and I walked in one day to eat here. 

Place is old and reeks of it; menus are battered and stained with old food sauce/juice/WTFs?; waiter takes forever to place your order or deliver it or both; food is cold by the time it gets out.

I ordered the bento box and WOW what a terrible idea, there is literally 2 tiny pieces of chicken terriyaki, some limp iceberg lettuce, and a scoop of day-old rice.  

I won't come back.

the portion size is huge and it's cheap. they have a lot of varieties.but the food isn't that fresh. I've been there a lot and ordered many different dishes, and to be honest with you, I can't even recognize what kind of meat they are putting in there anymore. They just seem very old. but hey, with lots of MSG, and cornstarch, even stale meat taste alright.

When you want some good chinese food, this place is awesome. Well, the place is called Vietnam Village, but it basically serves what I know as chinese food. haha. The owner is super nice. The service is fast. The food is cheap BECAUSE the portions are HUGE. It's like 3 servings per.....serving! That's awesome.

Quality food, large portions, cheap prices, friendly service. This place is pretty great. Probably better for take out as seating is limited and cramped.

Their fish dishes are particularly good :)

The general environment of Asian ghetto may be little overwhelming but this place provides you with great food at a great price.

I tried several dishes and none of them has been disappointing yet.

My recommendation: Pho Noodle, probably the best pho you can get around the campus.
It's really good and especially good for the cold weather.

I also love the owner of this restaurant.  He's super friendly guy!!

Ack, I hate giving nice people low ratings but the food wasn't anything special. Their business model fits well with the DFC: pumping out quick food for large student population.

I ordered the fried chicken over pho...

+ Huge portions, cheap
-  Pho tasted 'fake,' out of a package
-  Chicken was overly fried...no tenderness

Final Call: 
Hey, I know what it felt like to be a poor college student so do what you gotta do.

The food here is good and cheap.  Their pho is pretty decent, but I usually get the scramble egg beef which I can't find anywhere else.  I've tried ordering it at other places, and what I get is literally, a scrambled egg over rice, but at VNV it's done right with the saucy scrambled egg with beef or shrimp.  But the real reason I came here was the owner at the counter.  She was super nice, always smiling and asking how school was going, how my gf was, offering me a seat even when I was getting food to go.  She just reminded me of my mom so I always came back.  It got to the point that when I didn't go there I'd feel guilty, having to sneak by trying not to make eye contact as I ninja'd my way into Steve's or Thai Basil.  Its sad though, that the last two times I've gone back, she was no longer there.  I miss my 2nd mommy.

People don't give this place enough credit but this is one of the best eateries in the ghetto. It is fast, delicious, good portion, great prices and friendly services. I've had many of their dishes which are all influences from Vietnam, Hong Kong and China. Even though there is a large selection, they do them all surprisingly well and efficiently.

It is a little ironic (given the name Vietnam village) that the Pho is the worst thing here relative to other dishes, although it is still not bad. The best would have to be the crispy noodles with bak choy and your choice of meat. Fish and corn rice and garlic spare ribs are also quite satisfying to the soul. People also find the special plate popular but that is more for cheap eats. The guy taking the order is fantastic and very nice to cutomers.

I don't know what people expect eating at a place called the asian ghetto, but this is the best it has to offer. 

This is college food, it has to be fast, easy, tasty, filling and most importantly cheap. Viet Nam Village -- check, check, check, check, and check. It pulls of Vietnamese (asian really) college food with flying colors. Its the cheapest of all the establishments. Very filling. The amount of variance in there menu is staggering for a lone cook and a friendly server. This is my most frequented restaurant in berkeley.

I recommend all the PHO (best in berkeley), the chow fun is tasty, the crispy noodles live up to their reputation, and the bok choy dishes are wonderful.

All in all 4 stars + 1 star for having tax included!

Maybe I've gotten pickier, or this place just isn't as good anymore. I've tried two or three of their rice plates and couldn't finish them - too nasty. The pho is still good as always (though how can you mess up MSG and noodles?) but nothing else is very palatable. Shame.
