Their food always makes me sleepy after I eat and I never finish all the rice. I like their combo plate and creamy corn sauce with fish but that's about it. I might get their pho if I'm feeling under the weather and don't want to go out too far but I've had way way way better pho.

Hungry and exhausted after apartment hunting with my housemate, we decided to go somewhere nearby for some food. My housemate was craving for some pho, so we ended up ordering here.

I ordered their curry chicken over rice, and my housemate ordered the beef pho. The waiter was really nice, but I felt uncomfortable when I was looking at the menu near the register. Maybe because it was during winter break, and nobody was around, but I remember feeling like the waiter didn't want us to leave (I mean, it's a business, who wouldn't want customers?)

Anyway, when we got our food, we were really disappointed. My curry was really thick. It seemed as though there were more starch added in to the sauce to give that consistency than curry.  It wasn't as flavorful. I've tried WAY better curry chicken over rice dishes before.

My housemate, who's been to Vietnam and eat Vietnamese food daily, did not like their pho. She said it was bland, but they did give her a lot of noodles that she didn't finish eating.

Overall, the quality of the food wasn't worth the price and I probably wouldn't go back there again. 2 stars for good service though.
I was not very happy with my meal here, but it is fast and inexpensive.  I think Petit Cheval, around the corner is better, but I suppose the tradeoff is that this place has a lot more variety.

Tried some new dishes:

Scrambled Eggs with Shrimp - Highly Recommended
BBQ Pork: Could be better seasoned, but recommended sort of
BBQ Pork and BBQ Chicken Combo Plate: the BBQ chicken is great, highly recommended
Beef Stew over Rice: Just like homemade, definitely recommended

When my wallet's empty, this is the place I go to until I can replenish. It's ridiculously cheap for how much food they give you - a full meal (maybe two meals, if you're not a big eater) for five to six bucks? How do you top that, especially during midterms/finals crunchtime? Two stars for the food, one more star for the price, and one extra star for the $1 AriZona iced teas (so I don't have to walk to Johnston's to get it).

Sure, the food's not the best, but they do have some half-decent dishes - the fish and creamed corn dish or the XO eggplant dish are two of my regulars. DO NOT COME HERE FOR THE PHO. Pho Hoa is a better alternative (not saying much, but if pho's what you're going for, then...you know). Considering it's a "Vietnamese" restaurant run by Chinese people, their Chinese dishes tend to be better.

Maybe I ordered the wrong thing, but when I got the vegetarian plate with mushrooms, bok choy, and tofu, the sauce that came with it made me feel kind of sick afterwards. From now on I'm sticking with Bear Ramen house.

Nestled in the far right corner of the Asian Food ghetto, Viet Nam village is a deal. Thier food is awesome, tasty, cheap and comes in more than enough proportions. I personally like the $3.50 shrimp or beef fresh rolls  with plum sauce. Ohhhh heaven for under $4. Nothing like it!
I ordered the beef ball pho here. The noodles and everything else was amazing! wasn't really a fan of the actual beef balls though, they were too rubbery...

#75 Shrimp with scrambled egg over rice is one of the best dishes they have in my experience. Good portion sizes and taste has always been consistent. The scrambled egg is a good consistency, not too runny and not too thick. They don't skimp on the number of shrimps either.

TL;DR; Try #75, the shrimp with scrambled egg over rice.

I like the guy working here. He's really nice and actually seems like he wants to make your food. Whatever it is it'll be at least decent to pretty good. Pho is not great but then again that's what westminster is for. yeah its more chinese/general asian than vietnamese food.

I dislike....muchly.
Owner is Chinese, not Vietnamese, so everything was of the wrong flavor than I expected, hah.
That aside though, in terms of pure taste....
Pho was...terrible...Watered down, flavored wrong, meat was of poor quality, and the vermicelli noodles were also of poor quality: almost rubbery in texture.
I tried to mask the horrible flavor of the meat and watered down soup using Hoison sauce...but that turned out to be watered down too?

Also got a chinese style stir fry vermicelli dish another time. Flavor was bland (not to mention kind of wrong. The abundance of celery made most of it taste like celery, go figure), and wrong ratio of ingredients (Way too many vegetables, not enough meat, with also nasty quality noodles.)

I felt kind of bad, since the owner pegged me as Chinese and we ended up chatting in Mandarin, and I ordered in Mandarin, and he was nice to me. But I really disliked what I ordered. Until I get dragged here by some friends who like the place, I really don't think I'll be coming back here for a third trial for another dish.

#74 Crispy noodle with Chicken is my favorite 
but there's so much here, with each bite you savor it
From the beef with eggplant to the chicken and baby corn
there's so many choices you'll be torn
So note this, you've been warned..

This is one of my favorite places at the ghetto.  There are so many choices, the food is tasty and the guy there is really nice.  This place is also the place to get a drink.  $1 Arizona drinks are awesome.    As for the food, I already mentioned it.  With any of the above with some vietnamese hot sauce and you're set.

I come here whenever I'm just hungry and need to get full, disregarding quality and just going for quantity. A college student needs to eat! Not to say this place isn't good, just that portions are huge and not bad. If you're expecting higher quality food at the Ghetto, go to Thai Basil or Gypsy's.

My favorite dishes are #74 (crispy noodle with chicken/beef/shrimp/tofu) and #77 (cream corn sauce with fish/chicken). 

I used to be a huge advocate of #67 (scrambled beef w/ raw egg), but that got me food poisoning, so beware of that dish.

Bring cash, or Bank of America and Wells Fargo are close by. The manager speaks Mandarin and Cantonese, and you can pay before or after getting the food. Sriracha sauces are watered down, which is a disappointment.
The pho was fantastic. Great portions and the broth was tasty.

I really like this place in the Asian Ghetto! The guy is really nice and always smiley. The pho is pretty good, but I ALWAYS get #74- Crispy noodle chicken. It's so amazing!! The sauce is so thick and it gets some of the noodles soggy while some are still crunchy and its just a delicious contrast! yummmmmmm everyone should get #74 at least once in their life.
Fantastic value with very generous portions and snappy service.  The Vietnamese Fried Chicken, Pan Fried Noodles, Shrimp with Scrambled Egg, and Sesame Chicken are all solid simple bets.

Can't expect too much quality out of the restaurants operating in the Asian ghetto. Came here a few times during my college days and then recently and I realized just how cheap food is (speaking about both quality and price). You definitely get what you pay for. 

Most entrees here can be summarized as: a few oz. of meat + generic sauce + a ton of rice = meal. 

Food here tastes pretty generic for the most part and is very forgettable. Popular items here are the crispy noodles and the beef w/ raw egg over rice, but as mentioned above, not particularly tasty, and on the high side for sodium.

The least well-known restaurant in the South Side Asian Ghetto is also by far the best restaurant in the South Side Asian Ghetto.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars, four stars.

My favorite dish by far was simple and perhaps a bit dangerous: Rice, ground beef in sauce, and a raw egg on top. Definitely something that normal people would be wary of ordering in a restaurant like this... but I am not normal.

One of the best decisions of my life was to order it, and order it multiple times. Mix it together, and you have a blend of savory goodness that unlocks Godmode. And I never got sick from it either.

The pho is also a favorite. A rich broth and beef meatballs, flank, tendon, tripe, brisket... "wow" is all I have to say.

Also, they have huge portions. Always a plus.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star, zero stars.

The small and cramped restaurant really can't help being small and cramped. It looks like it drew the short straw when selecting units in the Asian Ghetto "complex." However, it could help to clean up the place every now and then. The "Berkeley aura" only works when you are serving vegan food.

More a fan of this restaurant for their Chinese rice dishes than for anything else! I've tried their pho (not that great) and order beef chow fun once (okay, not spectacular) but the rice plates are the ones I keep coming back for.

I always get either:
- Scrambled egg with shrimp over rice: tried the same dish from other places, but I keep coming back here because it's good!
OR
- Seasonal vegetables with fish over rice: because I love fish and bok choy and when the two of them are together, even better!

Crispy noodle dishes are pretty good too!

Portions are huge and prices already include tax (and it's usually pretty even where the only change you need are quarters!)

This place is rather magical at satisfying cravings.

Maybe it's the extremely large number of items on its menu, but Vietnam Village manages to have a little something of whatever I crave.

Let's start from some of my and my friends' favorites (we eat here basically once a week without fail. We come here so much the owner memorized our orders and gave us mooncake during the moon festival. How cute!):

-Eggplant stir-fried with beef over rice

-beef stew over rice (this one is unique in that the beef is poured over a layer of semi-cooked lettuce leaves. Sounds weird, but oddly tickles my taste buds and makes me all giggly inside).

- bitter melon and egg over rice (if you don't like bitter, don't get this, duh)

-creamed corn/egg over fried fish (I stand by my theory that this dish was created on accident by someone cooking cream corn soup and frying fish at the same time when a fortuitous stumble led to the combining of the two. Grateful for that stumble, I am)

-any meat fried singapore noodles (I'm not sure what this is actually called, but it's stir-fried rice noodles with meat and assorted veggies)

-Pork ribs over rice (I think. It's basically sweet and sour pork)

Generally you can't go wrong with their dishes. You get big portions and quick service. They don't really skimp on the ingredients and everything tastes if not awesome then at least decent. With the exception of their pho, I've heard.
Am I the only person who can't stand the food here?  I've tried the food here multiple times and found the food to be quite bland.  Not too authentic either but hey, for the price, it fills you up.

Consistently good pho (hot steamy broth with thinly sliced meat). However, my favorite remains to be their scrambled egg/shrimp over rice. Sure, there's probably an unhealthy serving of MSG in it, but it's forgivable if you only allow yourself some asian ghetto a couple times during the school year.

I had only one plate from this place. It was something with a yellow-ish sauce and it was completely awful. The rice was bad and the sauce too much. I absolutely hated this dish with my entire being but ate it because I was too hungry to fight it. Because of this restaurant, I have very little faith in how good the Vietnamese restaurants are in the Berkeley area, with the exception of Bui.

I know that it's a cheap place to eat and that it's conveniently located in the Asian Ghetto, but come on! Yokohoma makes better food!

I don't go to Asian Ghetto (Durant Food Court) often, but when I do, this is always a safe bet. 

My favorite dish thus far: tomato & beef over rice. While my roommate and I were eating here, some people came in, looked at our food, and decided to order the same thing. hahaha, yeah it LOOKS good and it TASTES good too. 

I also like their scrambled egg & whatever meat over rice/noodles. 

Prices are reasonable, service is fast, and the owner guy is pretty nice.

food tastes homemade, comes out quickly, and the owner is very nice.

i recommend the bitter melon beef and the creamy corn with fish.

Vietnam Village service is pretty darn fast. Yes their pho isn't the best in the world, but it's their Chinese dishes that are so good (weird, huh?)

Their cream corn fish is hands down the best thing in the entire world. It's super cheap, super fast to make and so you're out the door in 10 minutes tops. Cream corn fish is basically amazing fluffy battered fried fish covered in this cream corn and egg mixture on top of rice. So amazing. I think they call it "creamy corn sauce fish" or something like that. You'll see the picture and know what it is.

The beef with egg on rice is also damn amazing. Seriously, you have to give their cream corn fish a try!

Somehow I got addicted to their creamy corn sauce+ fried pork chops over rice . Their Pho doens't taste too good and not worth $7. Try their Chow Fun and other rice plates. Hey if you are sensitive to MSG, don't go here because I can taste a lot of MSG added to my food.... but their food is better than Mandarin House on the opposite side.

Pros: 
Food amount
Better chinese food than Mandarin House
Quick service

Cons:
Small tables/seats in a small place
MSG ADDED!!!
Viet Pho (Noodle) is so so.

Got creamy corn sauce with fish fillet and rice. It was 7 bucks but you get a lot of food and its alright. The place is pretty janky looking, as the rest of the ghetto but the server was nice and attentive. 
I will come back to try other stuff. They do have all their dish pictures on the wall.

Honestly, this is the best Chinese restaurant I have been to near the Berkeley campus that isn't Great China. Yes, I say Chinese restaurant because the people in the back are speaking Cantonese. Their Vietnamese food is not the best, but their Chinese dishes are by far the best around the campus. You can't go wrong with the Tomato Beef, the Scrambled Beef with Egg, or the Fried Fish with Creamed Corn.

Strengths:
  -77 with fish filet (creamy corn fish)
  -74 with chicken (pan fried noodles)

Development areas:
  -All other dishes, especially their pho

How to get 5 stars:
  -Move out of the asian ghetto and stop serving pho

I don't think this place is good for pho, but their rice plates are off the hinges.  There is surprisingly a lot of variety in their menu and there's plenty of photographs of many of the dishes.  

Back in the day, all I ordered was the combo plate (brocolli, rice, pork chop, and chicken wings with special sauce). Ever since the owners changed, the sauce was never the same...but it's still good. My favorites: boneless fried chicken and also the lemongrass beef with rice rolls and imperial rolll. The roll might be a little thick and tough.  Almost everything is under $6.  

And the little man is so happy and friendly.
i really like their pho! and their sweet and sour chicken and tofu :D  they give you a lot for the price.. it can easily last 2 meals :)

Close to campus, entrees are around 7 dollars and filling! This isn't a bad choice if you're at Asian ghetto.  They have a variety of vietnamese and chinese foods.  

My favorite is definitely the creamy corn sauce with fish.  It's pretty tasty and fills you up nicely.  I haven't really tried many other things, but the owner is nice and the food generally doesn't take a long time to come out.  It is cash only, but they make the prices nice so that you just get quarters back  instead of having to deal with other change.  I enjoy coming here because its usually a less popular choice and the lines are shorter. Food is still good though!

Taste: 3
Value: 5
Service: 4

Cheap, mediocre Vietnamese food. I used to come here pretty often, but I haven't been back for two years. They have a lot of different dishes, which were all okay. I have not tried their pho, which apparently isn't so great.

Good asian food (apparently the other reviewers say its chinese and not vietnamese, I have no clue). It's not oily or greasy like other places in the asian ghetto while at the same time being that good combination of cheap and still satisfying. 

I personally liked the fried rice (combination shrimp+chicken is cheaper than any other place in the ghetto) and the scrambled egg with shrimp. I've tried to replicate their scrambled egg + shrimp combination but I wasn't able to. It was just hard, so they're doing something I can't at least.

Good service from the older gentleman who is always taking the orders. Food is cooked fast and it all tastes pretty dang good without being too oily. The good is actually chinese for the most part (except the pho) and is amazingly cheap (6 total for many of the entrees). Only downside is that they are cash only. I can't even count the number of times I wanted to ready here only to find that I didn't have any paper money on me...

I'm a Cal grad student and this is my default stop for a reliable meal of comfort food. I go there so often that the manager/owner/chef now recognizes me and knows exactly what I like to order. Prices are very reasonable, the people working there are friendly, and I've never had anything less than a satisfying, hot, delicious meal. I always leave full and happy. The shrimp with tofu and mixed vegetables is my usual - you won't be disappointed. Convenient location as well.

I'm Vietnamese, and this is this place has great Chinese food. I said thank you to the owner in Vietnamese, and he said "Thank you" (in English) back to me. Nice guy. 

So far, I've had the chicken with eggplant and X.O. sauce, chicken and shrimp fried rice, chicken with stir fried vegetables, lemon chicken, and beef with tomato and scrambled egg. The first three are very good, lots of food, decent tasting, and cheap price. The last two were very bad, which means I disagree with the majority of yelpers about the scrambled egg whatevers. It could be that I was expecting Vietnamese style eggs, and those were definitely not it.

The food gets out fast, and none of my orders have ever been mistakenly changed. So yay :D

I am a fan of this place, their Arizona iced tea's are actually $1! All of the prices are already including tax so it's easy to pay. This place is cash only so remember to bring cash.

This place has characteristically Chinese food rather than Vietnamese food, but the Chinese food is good. I usually get the beef chow mein and it's great! I've also had the pho before and honestly I don't think it's that bad, it's good for when you're craving pho. I'm not sure if I've ever had the best pho ever so I don't have anything to compare with I guess. The food comes out pretty quickly too! Definitely less than 10 minutes and it's out.

This place is to go when you miss the Chinese home cooking. =]

I ordered some pho here and I got watery broth with barely any meat....and egg noodles! I kid you not! They gave me pho with egg noodles instead of rice noodles! I felt like I was eating some genetic horror of a mix between pho and won ton soup. The broth seriously just tasted like it was from a can.

Yes, Yes, it's true....the owners are not Vietnamese.  They are Chinese, confirmed by the fact that the third time I went in, the owner (a short, bushy-eyebrowed, middle-aged 'uncle' type) asked me in Mandarin if I was Chinese.  

But let's get over that.  I really *heart* this place, and the bushy-browed uncle who owns it.  The food is solidly good and inexpensive (about 5-7 dollars...around 5.50 to 6.50 for most dishes), and there's quite a lot of variety.  Honestly,this may be a purely subjective thing, but I've lived in Berkeley for 5 years as a grad student, and for some reason, in the 5th year of being here, I've discovered this place and it has won my heart.  They also give really big portions, so one meal I buy there always ends up being dinner that night or lunch the next day as well.  And personally, I've always gotten good service everytime I've gone.  Although it's not like fast-food fast, I get the impression it's because they're validly busy or because they actually spend time on preparing the food (which hasn't disappointed yet), and the uncle always hands me my food with a toothy smile!

In short, I highly recommend, and even though I am usually a really big cheapskate, even when it comes to eating out at cheap Asian food joints, I will continue to patronise this place just because it makes me happy to give them business.

I like: the seafood pho soup (has veggies, fish balls, fish cake, and imitation crab); the scrambled eggs and chives (SO good) rice; the sweetcorn chicken soup rice (perfect for cold days also).

Also, stay away from Mandarin House, which is right across from it.  Now, THAT is overpriced crappy food served with sullen and deliberate slowness.  
 

 The noodle soups (pho) are inexpensive and perfect for rainy, cold days.  And
I had eggplant and beef for $7. It was pretty average, nothing really special to it. I thought they were really slow compared to other places near it and considering that there was no line.

BAD SERVICE!!

i ordered rice noodles with shrimp to-go. 
later when i unopened by to-go box i noticed that i only had two pieces of shrimp and the rest was chicken meat!! that's not what i ordered,woman!! if there was a shortage of shrimp they should have told me up front, not secretly replaced it with fat-laden chicken bits without my approval!

someday i'll give this place another chance since all my friends seem to love it here :P

A lot of my friends in Berkeley have shat all over Vietnamese food, and when I ask them where they've had it, they say Vietnam Village or Le Petite Cheval. I'm sorry, what? 

I just wanted some pho. And what I got was watery soup with grimy noodles and grimier meat. The other dishes didn't look like anything I've ever seen at actual Vietnamese places.

Which leads me to wonder--are any of the people who like this place Vietnamese?

What the hell? I know this site is somewhat new, but I can't believe all of the internet-using world slept on this one. Vietnam Village is Asian fusion in the true sense of the world. Make no mistake, this is no pretentious haute cuisine; it's a hole in the wall restaurant in a complex which is commonly referred to as the "Asian Ghetto." The only dish I've had (and recommend) is called simply "the combo plate" and I doubt I will ever have any other because it is the closest thing to the perfect $5 meal in existence. It consists of a fried pork chop, fried chicken wings, fried egg, broccoli and rice, with a meat-based sauce over everything. The chop has hints of cocoa, which sounds disgusting but is one the defining characteristics of the combo plate experience. If you arrive at lunch time, the eggs are cooked fresh, otherwise they are usually pre-fried, which can often be a bummer. The chop, wings and broccoli are all cooked to order.

I can't believe this, but I am actually giving this place a 4! woo hoo!

I love this place. It's owned by a Cantonese man serving "Vietnamese" cuisine. Whatever, I love the place for the price and it's amazing. 

I really like the crispy noodle or the pho. I mean, the pho isn't authentic or greatest thing ever, but it's still good enough for me. I mean, seriously, for about $5, you are getting some seriously good tasting food! I mean, who cares about MSG or health right?

Like many of the restaurants who employ a certain ethnic group to work in the kitchen, Vietnam Village is staffed by Chinese people who cook Chinese food, with the only Vietnamese item being their selection of pho. Food-to-dollar ratio is very high, unfortunately they only accept cash and their door is right next to the hallway of trash which stinks up the whole place. Sometimes I want to gag when I wait for my food. But hey, it's cheap and you get a lot of what you order.

Can't go wrong with their fried rice plates, but stay away from their salt/pepper fish.

THIS IS SOLELY FOR THEIR #67 ONLY.

My brother-in-law can never get enough of this dish (scrambled beef over rice with raw egg). I admit, it's pretty darn good. Be sure to mix the egg in right when you get it so that it can cook! The meat is tender and moist. It comes with so much too! Noms.

I'm pretty sure the owner knows my brother-in-law by now haha. He always orders in Chinese, which is a plus to the owner since he speaks Chinese. Although, I did have a bad encounter with him one time when he gave me attitude and refused to give me what I wanted. :[ Time has passed though and all has been forgiven.

4 stars because of flavor and value. (But there is probably a lot of MSG used, so don't go here if you're sensitive to that, so -1.) However, if you want dirty hole in the wall chinese food for cheap, this is your place. Scrambled eggs with shrimp, crispy noodles, or that one with meat and raw egg on top, forgot the name... but those three are pretty awesome! (But don't get the chicken on the crispy noodles, it doesn't look right...). This was my "go to" place when I went to berkeley. The owner is cantonese (interesting for a place named vietnam village) but he's really nice and makes pretty good food! However, it's not the traditional huge bowl of Pho vietnamese place, I'd go elsewhere for Pho. I used to play chinese chess with my friend outside his shop and he would come out and watch. Then when I made a bad move, he would sigh and go back inside.

If I'm not sure what I want on a long day, this is my #1 fallback.

It has huge portion sizes, cheap prices and some staple dishes that I never get sick of. If I want lots of good food I go with the eggplant beef over rice (I must have gotten this over 10 times last semester). If I want something less salty I go with the creamy corn sauce over fish. If I want something soupy they have a beef noodle soup that's basically pho but with some more chinese-style meats (I think). 

There were definitely some dishes that I tried out that didn't exactly tickle my taste buds, so I definitely recommend following these yelp reviews for dishes to get. (e.g. the tomato fried rice was way too sour for me.) And don't let one bad experience ruin the restaurant for you!

This is my favorite restaurant in the Asian Ghetto/Durant Ave. area. The food is good, the portions large, and the prices are low. Also the guy who works there is always friendly and greets you with a big smile. My favorite dish is the eggplant with XO sauce. If you like meat, the barbecue chicken or pork dishes are great too. Their pho is probably their weakest point, but everything else I've tried, I really liked.

WARNING VIETNAM VILLAGE IS STAFFED BY CHINESE/CANTONESE people. I read some of the 1 star reviews and the complaints seem to be centered about it. Although the name might be somewhat misleading, keep in mind that titles are not exactly truthful sometimes (Rubio's? Chipotle's? Panda Express?) 

Ok now that's out of the way maybe we can review the food. Despite the name, Vietnam Village actually has decent cheap Chinese food. The fried rice at Vietnam Village is pretty good, so are their crispy noodles. All of my Chinese friends seem to prefer eating at Vietnam village for its cheapness/quality, which I think is a testament to its decent food and price.

It's close to campus. If you're craving Asian, this might be one of the places you want to try.

Food: They've got a pretty large menu with all sorts of different things, like pho, crispy noodles with chicken/shrimp, fried rice, etc to satisfy most of your cravings. I'm not generally a fan of the food here, and I once got food poisoning from the creamy corn sauce with fried fish (or my body just decided to reject it). I'd probably go because of its close proximity to campus, but I'd rather go to Le Cheval for Chinese.

I have never tried their Vietnamese dishes... I'm all about their HK style cafe dishes:

- creamed corn with egg over fish and rice
- minced beef with egg over rice (I usually ask for the egg to be cooked medium...otherwise, the dish is done with a raw egg that slowly cooks through when you stir up the hot beefy mess)

So good.  No one does a better beefy rice.

This place is certainly the best restaurant in the southside ghetto. It is like quasi-chinesey-vietnamesy food. I have eaten here at least 30 times and love the food and service. I usually get the #70 with beef or shrimp. A #70 is a huge plate of pan fried rice noodles, veggies, and meat.  I top it off with some Sriracha to achieve noodle perfection.  The spring rolls are also really really good.

OMG CREAMY CORN SAUCE WITH FISH. How you have helped me get by those stressful college days when all I wanted to do was pig out... Portions are huge and I always make this into two meals. Tried the equivalent at sun hong kong = not even close! 

Don't try anything else! There were times when I wavered and got the beef chow fun or crispy noodles...sigh, waste of money! I come back to yooooou creamy corn sauce with fish ^^ 

Sucks cause it's cash only (like most places at ghetto) but the owner is really nice! always has a huge smile on his face :D Plus, the seating area is pretty clean!

I'm not giving it 4 stars because it's one of the best food you can get in Berkeley...but I am giving it 4 stars because this is a place I definitely think I'll be coming to. For over a year, I'd avoided all the Chinese restaurants int he Asian Ghetto and the immediate vicinity (Lotus House = NO). After all, Chinese fast food is often messed up. But after hearing that their chow fun is palatable, I decided to give them a chance. I plunked down $6 and was served a steaming plate of glistening beef chow fun. Upon my first bite, I knew it was worth the $6. It was good! The beef was tender and the flavor was good. There's a lot of bean sprouts so if you don't like those, don't get this. But, the chow fun here is MUCH BETTER THAN SUN HONG KONG down the street at  Kip's. NEVER GO THERE, their chow fun is not even close to even tasting good, much less authentic.

I'll definitely be trying other dishes here, if I can't wean myself off beef chow fun first...I consider this pretty good Chinese fast food.

Portions are very large (I should've made it into two meals, but greedy me stuffed down all of it at once and felt like exploding afterwards) and service is friendly and fast. I've seen that guy come outside and personally deliver people's food to them!

This is one of my favorite places to go because it's good Chinese food, which is rare to find in the bay area! I graduated in May but if I remember correctly, #74 (crispy noodle with chicken/beef/shrimp) and #77 (creamy corn sauce with fish) are really good. Service is pretty good too, the guy's really nice. It's cash only though.

The dishes here are worth the money because they serve a huge portion. For example, if you spent $7 on a dish, you can eat it for lunch and save it for dinner. That's a whole days worth of meals! The reason I give it 4 stars is because it's a bit too salty/greasy at times..but that's the price you pay for eating out! ha..

I wouldn't claim that the food here is authentic Chinese, but I'd say it's pretty close to the Chinese food I usually have (FYI, I lived in HK for 9 years).  It's probably the best option for Chinese food around the campus area (No, don't go to Sun HK, unless for their dirt-cheap daily specials).  Cheap prices and good portions, too.  Me and my friends regularly eat here back in my fresh and soph years -- it was almost like our canteen.  You have to know what to order though, as some of the more "authentic" items are either not on menu, or only posted on the wall.  Some of my favorites are bitter-melon with eggs and chicken,  creamy corn sauce with fish fillet, "gon chow ngau hor" (dry beef chow fun?) and beef and tomato with rice.  You can also ask them for "less oil", "less salt" when you order.

P.S. I usually don't bother reviewing restaurants because I don't like writing food reviews, but I couldn't resist leaving a review here this time after reading all the low-ratings.  People who are giving this restaurant a 1-star or 2-star rating after ordering simply a bowl of Pho have no idea what they are talking about, because this restaurant is not meant to be judged by its Vietnamese food.  I've had their Pho before as well, and I agree that it's lackluster, but you really shouldn't even be ordering Pho here in the first place, as they do a much better job at Chinese food!
This is definitely one of my more frequently visited places in the Asian Ghetto. I like their shrimp and egg over rice dish. I like to come here when I'm feeling nostalgic about Chinese food.

Ah, the good old days of eating like a college student at the Durant Food Court.  Happy to find that VNV is still around, though it has probably changed hands a few times since the '90's.  

Food is still pretty awesome and quite cheap.  I had the #64 combo plate, which comes with two pieces of fried pork chop, 3 chicken wings, 1 fried egg, broccoli and special sauce over rice, all for $5 including tax. The waitress/owner was also very friendly, taking care of all her customers with a smile on her face.  

Bottom line:  Good food, low prices...what more could you ask for?

Pho = lose-ville. You can get better tasting broth, pho, and beef at Le Cheval for a cheaper price.

However, a combo plate of MSG-fried porkchop, chicken wings, broccoli, an egg, and some bullshit brown sauce (mostly corn starch) for $5 is a steal if you're low on cash money.

I don't eat at this place anymore at all actually. If anything, I'd recommend their rice bowl plates. Fried fish + cream corn over rice is pretty solid and a huge portion. Beef & tomato over rice is good too. All of the food just tastes a little too bland for my liking. It's like eating water with texture unfortunately.

Decent food, huge portions, good price. I've found service to be a bit on the slow side, but maybe that's because I'm not Cantonese and I don't connect with the owner on that kind of deeper level. :( Today I had half an hour to eat and the food took about 25 mins. Scarfing down hot food in five minutes = not fun. Also, they don't take credit cards, which is kind of annoying.

Pho is almost a non-existing food genre in Berkeley. Well, good pho to be exact. Viet Nam Village does serve pho, but more on the normal beef ingredients noodles. Small portions for $8 bucks to be honest. This place is actually owned by Chinese, I trust their Chinese dishes more so for this reason. 

The dish my friends and I have gotten most is the sweet cream corn over rock cod filets over rice. They use a lot of corn starch to make the thick creamy texture. The sauce is mixed with eggs then poured over the lightly battered fish filets. It's delicious! For under $8, this plate is very filling, it could be sufficient for two meals. But keep in mind if you leave it for the next meal, the fish would be soggy.

Cash only like most of the Asian Ghetto places. Very nice owners, just mediocre Vietnamese food.

A few words about the place:
Located in Asian ghetto this 2-man show has been around a long time. Known as Viet-Nam Village, it really should be called China homestyle. My Chinese half finds the local style Chinese comfort foods that you can't find at most other restaurants. If you're looking for some of your mother's cooking, this is your place.

What I recommend:
I really prefer savory over sweet foods, but if I had to choose it would be the X.O. Eggplant Beef ($6.75) with rice or the Beef with scrambled egg ($6.75). Both fill you up and never let you down. Come in at any time, grab a seat, sip on some hot tea, and have your food in 10minutes or less. Other popular dishes are the sweet corn fish and the tomato beef egg. 

Bottom line:
Come in hungry leave happy for $7 or less. With no tax, no tip, and no non-sense, this is a regular spot for me. The ambiance is all you can expect of asian ghetto. Frankly sometimes it is hit or miss on dishes, but if you find a few favorites I'm sure that Vietnam village will make a fan out of you.

I've gone here over the years, sometimes out of fondness for the place, other times because I think the food is actually good for a student lunch or dinner. The restaurant has been passed down from generations to family friends, and I get to speak Cantonese with the cooks and owners.

I recommend any of the large plates of noodles (either rice or flour) and the Vietnamese cold dishes. They also have a curry tofu dish that costs under $5.

Be sure to ask for no msg; that might have induced Ashley L.'s sickness. (Though the soups are probably preprepared, in which case that's not an option.)

Vietnam Village...a place owned and operated by a chinese guy...where most items on the menu are Chinese rather than Vietnamese? SCHWAA?! haha

98% of the food here is mediocre, and doesn't taste "right"(relative to traditional viet or chinese food). Come here if you want to get your moneys worth with generous portion sizes; one dish should count as 2 healthily portioned meals. If you're in the asian ghetto, I'll assume you're a poor college student as well so this might be up your alley to try.

So you might be wondering why 4 stars right? I haven't said anything too great about it.  WELL...4 stars only because I am in LOVE with 2 dishes served here!!!  (It's enough to say "Yay! I'm a fan!". haha) 

1) Viet Beef Curry over rice (#68).  The beef curry is rich in flavor and spices.  I'm a huge fan of beef tendon; gummy and tasty.  One might think the meat in this dish is very high in fat, but it's common to mistake tendon for fat. (beware, there still is fat however!)

2) Crispy Noodle w/ chicken or veggie or shrimp.  Noodles are wet and soggy where it meets the sauce, just as how it should be. The dry portion of the noodle is fresh crispy  (rather than stale crispy at Lotus House bleh).  

Anecdote: I actually took my family here after my graduation commencement for lunch.  It was reallly awkward and embarassing to walk into asian ghetto with fancy dressed-up graduation attire but I had to because my grandma couldn't walk far and wanted decent asian food.  I walked into vietnam village and THEN, I saw two other graduates and their families eating there! haha  One had also ordered #68 and crispy noodle!  I was not alone! WA-hoo!

this restaurant was one of the worst decisions i made in my entire life... and i have made some pretty bad decisions before.

desperate for some pho after a long night, the bf and i decided to try viet nam village restaurant because it got the highest ratings among the pho restaurants in berkeley.

as soon as we entered the restaurant we noticed that there were 4 huge black flies hovering above our table, which was not exactly appetizing. we ordered our pho and one order of spring rolls. the pho came out first, which kind of upset me because i enjoy eating my spring rolls before my pho... it's just always like that..

anyways, the pho tasted horrible. it tasted like someone sprinkled msg in water and dumped in noodles. i had to pour tons of their watered down sriracha and hoison sauce to make the soup bearable.
the spring rolls were probably the most ridiculous spring rolls i have ever seen. they were as big as a burrito and they were so stuffed with rice noodles that it was really hard to even find the shrimp.

anyways, i would have given this place two stars, but throughout the entire day i felt like crap from eating here. no matter how much water i drank i felt like my insides were slowly drying up, probably from the msg in the pho

if possible, i would have given this place 0 stars, but i guess i'll just have to live with giving them one. i will NEVER come back here again, and recommend that no one else does as well.

"Late night dinner? No problem!" I feel like these words almost ALWAYS predict an impending trip to Asian ghetto...

This time, we dropped by Viet Nam Village. I had come here once before with my boyfriend a few months ago and I had some good memories of their pho, so I was all too eager to come back!

Unfortunately, however, I was sadly disappointed! This time, their pho (I ordered #2) was rather bland and tasteless. Only the meat itself was flavorful (and it was delicious, lemme tell you), but the soup and noodles could've been cooked in plain old water!

Since it's so freaking hard to find a good pho place in NorCal (I haven't succeeded yet!), I'm willing to give Viet Nam Village a second chance.... Crossing my fingers & hoping desperately that this was just a fluke!

:( sadness

I tried their pho, very disappointing.  Sad because I've had food from them before (several years ago) and it is usually decent.

BTW...this restaurant is owned and staffed by CHINESE people who lived in VIETNAM...

and this place only takes cash, but there's a BofA + Wells Fargo ATM walking distance.

Oh my gosh, I am devastated. This place uses MSG?! Asian Ghetto uses MSG?! *breaks down in tears*

Uhm, anyway, this place was my favorite place in Asian Ghetto for the longest time because there were so many different dishes I liked:

#77: Creamy corn sauce with fish fillets ... omg, to die for, just try it, I know it looks disgusting in the picture but just try it!

#56, I believe, is the curry with chicken, broccoli and tofu. It isn't bad, I get it when I feel guilty for not eating vegetables for a month.

#74 is the crispy noodle... that's always the bomb. Lasts 2 meals.

#73 is the wide noodle stuff, I got it once but it was like half cooking oil half noodle, so never again.

Combo plate is delicious and cheap, I really like it, it lets me imagine I am eating something close to a balanced meal.

WARNING though... as much as I love this place, I once drank water from their dispenser and felt something brush by my teeth, and I spit out the water, looked inside and saw 3 dead bugs in it... so uhm... yeah. Might just be a rare occasion, but I never drink their water when I'm there, that's all I'll say. Regardless of that, still 4 stars. That should say something about how much I like their food! Plus, the guy is really nice to me, and it seems he is nice to everyone... so that's my experience.

The menu is in English, so I wasn't 100% certain whether or not the dish I wanted was the dish I was seeing on there... so I attempted to order in Vietnamese. The guy scowled at me and asked me to repeat it. I did. He snorted and said "I don't speak Vietnamese" and then... just walked away from me.

Funny, I would have thought that perhaps he would have allowed me the opportunity to order in English before dismissing me. I waited about two minutes as he ignored me and waited on other customers before deciding that it was really not worth it. I left without ordering.

This place can bite me.

$4.75 Combo Plate.  Comes with pork chops, broccoli, and a fried egg.  SO GOOD.  SO SO GOOD.  And for less than $5. Hell yeah I'd tap that again...and again...and again.

The best place in Asian Ghetto if you ask me.  Their pan fried noodles are also surprisingly good...but not GREAT.  I'm telling you...COMBO PLATE.  Just do it.

Oh no...

This is the epitome of a poor student's dining. When you think of dirt poor college students who are subject to eating tasteless fast food because they cannot afford anything else, this is probably what I think of. Do yourself a favor and hop onto a bus with your bus pass and get yourself some real pho.

Everything else is alright, but would probably taste the same if you had made it yourself.

Looking at everyone else's reviews, I really wish I took advantage of their lunch menus! oh well... I mostly came here for snacks and drinks because the stuff here is way cheaper than the Walgreen's next door, and they have lots of selection even though it's a small store. It's so convenient because it's so close to campus and along the way home for most of us.  Great store! :)

A family owned and operated market that actually takes cards in Berkeley?! SOLD! The people are so nice and helpful, the prices are right, and they have just about anything you would need on a whim. I go here in between big grocery runs I take once a month. The deli is pretty solid as well. This is the kind of place that makes me love Berkeley.

The sandwiches are hit or miss, depending on who makes it and how they're feeling that day (the size varies as well as the quality). Sometimes it's great, and sometimes it's ... meh. I used to be a big fan of them but they've started to CHARGE EXTRA FOR CHEESE! They added tiny tiny print to their menu, so watch out for this. It was a good bit more for cheese and I was pissed when I realized it at the checkout.

The market itself is o.k. I believe the other reviews that have said the produce are on the older side. Most of the stuff seems like it's been on the shelves for awhile. I will say however, that there is a pretty amazing collection of sodas and juices here, so if you're into that this is definitely the place to go.

The service here can be kind of crappy. Sometimes they joke around with people who are regulars (or attractive, or cops), but I've also seem them start arguments with customers for no reason. I value service highly so this was a major turn off for me.

Summary:
- Prices comparable to Walgreens
- Sandwiches are decent but they started charging more for cheese = weak
- TONS of soft drinks
- People who work there can be dicks sometimes

Sam's has almost everything when it comes to breads and snacks and beverages.  Even my favorite Ritter's bars.  I live half a block away and it's such a relief to live near a quality market.  Still need to trek to Safeway or, better yet, Berkeley Bowl for all the fruits and the veggies.  And the prices are a little higher than average for some items, but if you live within walking distance, Sam's is totally worth it.

Stopped by Sam's right before a football game to grab a bite to eat. Everywhere else on Telegraph was pretty crowded but there was no line here, yay. We ordered the Famous Chicken Sandwich, which comes with your choice of a drink or a stamp on a stamp card. Interesting. They have one of the Coca Cola Freestyle machines here, which is pretty cool I guess. 

The sandwich was a pretty good size (and it was only $6!), the chicken was a bit dry but it wasn't that noticeable because of the sauce they put on the bread and the seasonings on the chicken.

THE TRUTH!!!!

ive been a customer since my Berkeley high days, frequenting Freds market on University. And since then i go in there for one thing and one thing only...the chicken sandwich. 

Im not a fan of grilled food,per se, but the onions, the bread, the meat, the lettuce, the mustard, its all a very tasty combination of warm goodness. I love it.

Everything in there is expensive so if you dont mind dropping $15.00 on that sandwhich (which is huge, btw) a bag of chips and a drink, then go for it. I go here seldomly bc its pricey and omg have you tried parking up there? Yikes!!!!!

Try their famous chicken sandwiches.  Sad thing is that you dont get to choose your bread like many sandwich places, you just get stuck with a french roll.

It's a bit spicy from the last time I had it.  Be prepared to have a drink ready!

I got a sausage breakfast burrito for lunch at $3.25 (it was to the right of where you order sandwiches). It was a little dry, but that's understandable as it was noon and it was probably made in the morning. The ingredients, which included potatoes, egg, and sausage, were good. There was a serious lack of vegetables, but for a breakfast burrito, that's acceptable.

The burrito was also large, especially considering the price. Overall, the breakfast burrito is not as tasty as the hot sandwiches are, but it's a better deal.
Tried the meatball sandwich today based on the Yelp reviews. It was tasty, great meatballs, tangy sauce....my only complaint is that they didn't toast it.

Philly cheese steak. Philly cheese steak. Philly cheese steak.

I was in town for the Treasure Island Music Festival, which turned out to be a weekend of complete mayhem for my friends and I. Anyway, after some questionable morning activity that sounds kind of like "shake and bake," we were very hungry. Very VERY hungry.

Our Berkelian host led us to this glorious place, where we proceeded to stare at the menu for what felt like an hour. It was probably more like five minutes, but that is still an abominable amount of time to be menu-staring.  In the end, we decided on philly cheese steaks.

Let me set the record. I abhor sandwiches containing cheez whiz. That stuff is like cheez jizz to me... not appealing. I prefer real cheese in my sandwiches. I distinctly remember talking to someone who appeared to be the manager or owner or something about the merits of real cheese in philly cheese steaks. Sorry, cheez whiz lovers. Oh... and he was really friendly :)

Back to the story. By the time we got our sandwiches and managed to walk to our other friend's place to chow down, we were freaking ravenous... but also considerably more sober.

And that sandwich... wow. I only ate half because I split with my boyfriend, but it was plenty, and it was delicious. Crusty bread, spread with just the right amount of mayo. Layer after layer of succulent steak. REAL cheese melted between meat and onions. (I think I blacked out so many times that weekend that I cannot recall if there were peppers in my sandwich... ) But trust me. I could never forget biting into that baby. It was bliss.

I cannot wait to go back. I never had a reason to visit my old friends attending Cal... but now that I know of this delightful sandwich, that may change. 

Sam's Market reunites long lost friends. What more can I say?

there's gotta be a reason why it's called Fred's Famous Chicken, it was delicious! Good amount of meat, great taste. The bread was kinda hard, but it was comparable to the crunch of a Vietnamese Banh Mi sandwich bread. Quality sandwich, cheap can and bottle drinks. Quick service.

Really convenient and close to campus if you need to pick something up.  I really like their huge drink selection and their staff is very friendly!  However, they don't have a huge inventory, mainly just basic grocery items.  I'm so glad this place moved in :)

Fred's Market is a block north of where I work, and I've going there for chicken rice plates for years.  Chicken dripping with sauce, lots of food, decent price.  Then Sam's opened up a block from my apartment, and now I rarely bike out to Safeway for groceries (I will hit the new Trader Joe's on the way back from work, though).  When I'm feeling lazy, I'll also grab one of their giant breakfast burritos.  The food is a bit pricey, but it's a prime spot on Telegraph half a block from campus, so there aren't many other places to get produce around here.

The produce isn't always the freshest, however.  It's a bit of a chicken and egg problem: the less people buy produce, the longer it sits on the shelf, and less people buy it because it isn't fresh.  The high turnover and refrigerated foods are fine, but I've had issues with onions, bell peppers, avocado, etc.  Come on, people?  If more people made dinner, we could all have fresh produce just blocks away!

I like this place. It is so convenient for the students, and quite frankly, they make really good sandwhiches. In a college town that highlights quiznos, subway, and Cheese 'n Stuff (the name pretty much explains the lack of creativity most prominent in the food) as there mainstay deli's, it was so refreshing when Sam's market opened. The sandwhiches are big, flavorful, and made pretty quick. Although sometimes the chicken is a little dry, and one time the bread tasted like a freezer, this place is great to snag a hot sandwhich in no time. Beware, no "five dollar footlongs"...Only seven dollar hoagies with more than one layer of meat...."eh hemmm Subway"

I got the famous chicken sandwich and that was really delicious and very filling. I also got the fried mushrooms with it because I was really hungry but I was displeased because they were uncooked in the middle and the sandwich is enough food anyways for no matter how hungry you are.

Awww I love Sam's market. I have been a daily, faithful customer for the past 3 years. This cute little store wins my respect because the workers here are sooo friendly, the prices are decent, and the location is especially convenient if you live right by campus! 
It fulfills mostly all my grocery needs and the wide variety of drinks is just lovely! I get my Aloe drinks from this store. 

Also, the price for food here is almost ALWAYS cheaper than any equal food item at the Walgreens store nearby.  I've noticed this after trying to buy the same items at both stores for the past few years... Walgreens' prices are inflated apparently. 

So if you want to buy food at walgreens, check Sam's market first, most likely it will be cheaper : )

This is EXACTLY what Berkeley needed, a CONVENIENT convenience store, campus-side.  Not like 7-11 convenient, like a supermarket hit by a shrink-ray convenient.  This place has so much stuff a dorm or apartment-dwelling student might need in a jam its amazing.  Their deli sandwiches are a tad expensive so I haven't gotten one yet, but I hear its good and pretty big.  They have a huge fridge with bottled drinks galore (no alcohol), and even a row with toiletries/cleaning.  Garlic stuffed spanish olives, varieties of cooking oil, chips, cinnamon sticks, semifreddi bread/donuts - the randomest things I wouldn't expect in such a small store.  They don't have a big variety of produce and the prices are kinda high, but its a small convenience store so I can't blame them - for what they have it looks decent most of the time.  They have a good dairy fridge - doesn't have everything but might have what you need if you're in a pinch.  Haven't figured out yet if they have a lunch meat deli, in addition to the sandwich bar.

Only quip is that their drink fridge isn't always cold.  Either they always load their drinks right before I take them or they're cutting back on electricity.  They don't have raw meat here - though I really don't expect that.  I'll go to safeway or the butchers across from it down college.  Otherwise this place is exactly what Berkeley needs.

THIS PLACE IS AWESOME.  I took off a star because some random things are super overpriced (cereal, almond butter).  But otherwise, perfect for all your eating needs.  Good breakfast burritos.  You will seriously be full all day.  The dudes that work there are crazy nice.

I bought a breakfast burrito here at 9 a.m., and it pretty much kept me full the entire day. Plus, it was pretty cheap and tasty from what I vaguely remember after I got out of my food coma induced nap.

Also they have a pretty nice selection of soft drinks, juices and even some produce in the back.  Pretty convenient location!

Sam's Market is the Telegraph version of Fred's which is on University Avenue. I went to Fred's for years when I worked across the street and got addicted to their delicious chicken sandwiches. The market itself is what you expect--a decent selection at reasonable prices. The have a nice selection of beer and sodas, chips and candy bars and most things you'd want from a convenience store. 

Now that Trader Joe's has opened up--Fred's Market is all but gone so the only place to get their chicken sandwiches is at Sam's Market on Telegraph. 

Sam's is a better version of Fred's. There's more room, which means more of everything and it's that much closer to the college for that crowd. 

The stand out is still those killer chicken sandwiches. The variable is the bread, which can vary from merely good to mind-blowing. When it's a good bread day you'll swear it's the greatest thing on earth.

Incredibly rude service and moldy food.
Never buying from here again.

I was so excited when this place opened up. This place is the closest super market-ish store around the campus area. I love their wide variety of drinks they have. I'm a total root beer whore and I'm slowly going through all the different brands they sell. I love their sandwiches and to go meals. The prices are really good for the portions they give you and plus you get a free drink! Can't complain about that :)

The cookies.  It's all about their cookies.  They make delicious, chewy chocolate chip cookies and there have been weeks in my life that I couldn't help but get one a day.  They $1.50 and amazing.

Their sandwiches are good, too.  I usually go with the meatball sub.  Delicious, very filling, and reasonably priced.  

The guys that work there are a lot of fun, too.  Always cheerful and have fun with their customers.

But remember: get one of the cookies.

Probably the best lunch counter in the campus area. Fred's Famous Chicken (with mayo, mustard, and provolone on the French bread) was an institution amongst my friends. The staff here are really friendly and love feeding people. 

Also noteworthy for the ample selection of sodas.

This place just opened up - I really like the selection that they have.  They have most everything you may need to cook simple meals, like spaghetti, soups, and ingredients for sandwiches and things.  It's clean and well stocked, unlike a lot of the little markets in the area, and it isn't incredibly crammed to the seams with stuff.  It is a great place for getting a few key ingredients without driving/walking to a larger supermarket.  I also feel that their prices are not crazy expensive, which is usually the case when you buy groceries at these little markets around campus.

Along with the weird bottled drinks (which I simply adore, and can't get anywhere else), they also sell Ritter Sport Choco-Duo chocolate. I haven't been able to find it in any other store in the area, so it's possible that they import it themselves. (The label is entirely in German.) This could be totally misguided, of course, but I think they actually do that with one of their other candy bars.

In any case, 4 stars for having an awesome selection!

Where would I be without Sam's? The great thing about this place is that you don't have to walk 20 minutes (if you live on campus) to the nearest grocery store, thus proving to your parents, in my case, that you're not refusing to eat again because the dining hall is still serving week-old noodles.
Sam's is located right on Telegraph by Walgreens, which makes shopping for most of us a 2-minute procedure. It's fast, the staff doesn't breathe down your neck like they often do at Walgreens - who has a poor supply of good snack foods in the first place - and they never attempt to BS you complete rearrangements of the grocery displays, which I appreciate.
Prices can be a little steep, but it's what you pay for living a bus ride away from Trader Joe's or Grocery Outlet. 
I've never tried the sandwich bar but I hear it's fine. Drink selection is great (my only qualm is that they don't have Jones sodas). Produce is so-so and expensive, but usually worth it. Bread is always the good kind, and they don't offer the crap kind of sourdough you get from Safeway, thank god. Meat and cheeses are in good selection, too.
The staff, again, is always great. The guy who works there (former ponytail man, for us regulars who still don't know his name) is hilarious and jokes with almost everyone at the counter.
I'll be coming here forever, or at least until our dining halls stop serving roadkill.

Sam's has everything it needs to be a super successful grocery store: great prepared food, ultra-convenient location, friendly staff and owners and a pretty good selection of stuff (especially their cold beverages). 

While I was at Cal, I probably went to Sam's every other day after it opened. After Sufficient Grounds closed, I was in need of a good sandwich place that was more than simply a cheap deli sandwich that I could put together myself in less than 5 minutes. I decided to give Sam's a shot and tried their Famous Chicken sandwich and was hooked. It's spicy, it's flavorful, it's hearty and filling and messy to the point where I have to use a fork and a wad of napkins. I've also had their hot pastrami, which is amazing as well as their egg salad, which is truly loaded with copious amounts of egg salad. Needless to say, Sam's became my place of choice when I wanted a sandwich. 

When I wasn't grabbing lunch at Sam's, I would stop by for an Arizona Green Tea and some snacks for a long study session at the library or to keep me awake in class, or I would grab some groceries to cook dinner with on the way back to my apt. 

Whatever it was, Sam's always had me covered.

Rating is for the burritos.  I ordered a chicken burrito.  It was, as promised, HUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUGE - among Sam's, Chipotle, Gordo's (super burrito), and La Burrita (super burrito), Sam's is the biggest. This is actually probably the best-deal burrito you can get - also, buy 9, get 1 free.

Sam's is heartier than Chipotle (no lettuce, boo), lighter than La Burrita (not as... saucey).  It has a nice mild kick to it as well.  The proportions and well-mixed-ness of the ingredients are very variable and depend on who makes the burrito.  The tortilla has grill marks on it, which is awesome.  And they grill your meat on the spot.

I've never bought food from here, and this review is strictly for the grocery stuff

For the most part, cheaper than Walgreens next door - for items that are also found at Walgreens
for items NOT at Walgreens - ex produce and fruit, etc... ridiculously expensive IMO
but it's sold in small quantity and right  at the core of campus southside traffic..

Not the most friendly staff/owner people there either ... 
but I go there for the random energy drinks,

I bought some fruit and a cheese steak sandwich the other day.  Man I really regret doing that.  Their oranges were not fresh at all.  In fact they were almost rotten.  I threw them away after I peeled them.  And how are you going to sell cheese steak sandwich and charge 75 cents for CHEESE?!? WTF?  The sandwich was mediocre at best.  Overall I don't see myself going there anytime soon, maybe never.

Part of my "Two Meals for $7 or Less Next to Campus" Category
Huge food for cheap!
I love their sandwiches, but you must order them on French Roll, because the quantity of ingredients is for some strange reason entirely proportionate to the size of bread you order the sandwich on. In other words, sliced rye = small sandwich, and french roll = huge sandwich, same price.
$5 gets you a gigantic cold sandwich, probably 2 or 3 times as much sandwich as you would get at Subway next door. That means 2 meals for $5. I call that a great deal. $6 for hot sandwiches, including the Chicken Shawarma Sandwich, a glory of cultural fusion. "I thought Shawarma's were wrapped in lavosh!" you say. But this is a special Shawarma/Sandwich hybrid with the fixins of a Shawarma on a French Roll (always French Roll, see above!!) and with a cheese of your choice.

Other bonuses:
 - tasty juices
 - groceries, across the street from campus
 - logs of goat cheese for under $6, a rare find. Combined with "everything" crackers this is an unstoppable combo of deliciousness.
 -Nice people, family-run and friendly.

This place has a pretty good selection of both deli food and groceries. Their sandwiches are especially delicious, and the portions are huge - they usually last me about two meals. You should also check out their drink selections, they have sodas and other drinks that I haven't seen for years!  The employees there are all very friendly, although sometimes when there are a lot of customers things will get a bit confusing when you're trying to order your food. I'm so happy this place finally opened though, it's so much better than waiting in line at the neighboring Walgreens for food that isn't nearly as good.

I love going to Sam's in the middle of the day to just grab a snack or meander through the food isles.  They have a wide range of snack foods, produce, frozen foods, ice cream, and ethnic foods for such a small store, so you never really know what you'll find there!  

Their sandwiches are great and really really cheap.  I would especially recommend their hot chicken sandwich or their hot pastrami sandwich.  The wait is normally a little bit longer than you might expect, so don't expect to get your order in two minutes.  Place your sandwich order first, go wander around to get your snacks and a drink, come back and pay for everything, and then your sandwich will probably be ready for pick-up.  Their fries are also delicious, and one order fills up an entire take-out box.

As people have mentioned, their cookies are absolutely amazing.  Crispy on the outside, chewy on the inside, and completely loaded with chocolate chunks.  If you haven't had it, try it, and if you have tried it, you're probably like me and stop by at least once a week just to pick one up.  Be prepared for the oil/butter to seep through the bag, though!  So make sure you get the wax paper sheets with your cookie.  Mmmm....

The people here are also so friendly and helpful.  So next time if you're just looking for milk, cookies, candy, chips, etc. that you might have gone into Walgreens for, duck into Sam's and support this great little store!

HUGE sandwiches. I've yet to finish one of these monstrosities in one sitting. Being a quickie-mart, everything else in this place is probably overpriced. Can't complain about the sandwiches though. It's kinda just a mess of meat, cheese, and sauce with slightly stale bread that's only chewable due to the first two. Tastes rather average, but there's so much of it...

I usually come here for the sandwiches. It's a decent size, I think about a foot long, and tastes pretty good too. Slowly working my way to that free sandwich...

Prices are kinda high, but after being forced to buy things on campus and at the Bear Market, everything else seems alright to me. They have a nice selection of drinks and the huge loafs of sourdough french bread they have are great too.

The Sandwiches totally rock and they're HUGE! Try Fred's Chicken. Six bucks and you'll be completely full. Full Deli and plates available.  No place to sit, but it's worth it.

Produce is cheap. It's convenient for students who don't have a car, who don't want to journey to safeway, and who don't want to pay $$$$ at andronico's.

Sam's Market is THE BEST. I would literally go in here at least once a day because they have EVERYTHING you need. 

There was a semester that I came in everyday during finals to get my daily dose of ONION RINGS. Mmm just thinking about them is making my mouth water. And their PHILLY CHEESESTEAK and HOT PASTRAMI sandwich yummmm. Plus, they have fresh produce, ingredients for baking, super cheap spices, my favorite ito en teas... really, everything you need. I almost forgot, BEER AND WINE TOO! What more can you ask for?? Ooh and cutting the egg cartons in half... genius!

Plus, the guys are super nice and friendly. I love to take my dog to Sam's, so whenever I didn't have her with me, Ramy would ask where she was :) Everybody who works there makes you feel really welcome. Such a cute, happy family. I love it!

Obviously they can't match some of the prices you might find at a supermarket, but you're supporting a local business :) and you can't beat the convenience of having a market across from campus. 

I miss Sam's Market!!

P.S. Someone wrote that their bread was moldy within a couple days. I experienced the same thing (I think because I bought the loaf on a rainy day). But I just brought it back in, explained the situation, and exchanged it for a new one with no problems :)
I haven't tried the deli here, but they have one of the biggest beverage selections in the area, and now they have a Coca-Cola freestyle! Orange Coke is good.

Relatively large sandwiches for 6$, the reuben had a very satisfying amount of meat on it, and the famous chicken was enormous and great. They have a good beer selection but you cant break six packs, which is kind of useless. A great oddball soda collection too.

The employees here are probably the most dramatic and stressful mini mart staff I've ever encountered, they always seem to be yelling at eachother or customers or getting heated up about something. You know, in the "ive had a hard life this business is my life now and Im running it how I want, service doesn't matter, life was hard in my country" kind of way. While I was there I'm pretty sure one of the staff yelled at another staff member to never serve one customer who was looking at yogurt for too long, I wish I were kidding. Also, never complain about the prices or you could get banned for life (I may be kidding about this, but I'm too scared to test it). 

If you don't mind that though, this place provides a third sandwich option in the area with a great selection and portioning that makes Toaster Oven across the street obsolete (since their sandwiches also cost a little more than subway but are substantially smaller). Needless to say, no one should ever have to go to the Subway on the corner. Also now that andronicos closed this is the only place on southside where you can buy mushrooms and occasionally kale. Which is pretty noteworthy. But they didn't have bay leaves. This disappointed me.

Great business near campus. Their deli sandwiches are the bomb! Both the Famous Chicken and Famous Steak hot sandwiches are awesome. My preference leans towards the steak.

They also have a pretty good selection of hard to find sodas in glass bottles. 

The guys who work here are great! They like getting to know their customers. Sam's market really cares about the students, their main customers, so I will continue to frequent this place despite the slight premium you may be paying. Honestly, the selection of sodas and quality makes it worth it.

I like this place caus they stock a ton of DRINKS on one side of the wall and a lot of produce/deli food too! And the guys working are pretty nice! 

Unfortunately, you have to buy at least $5 worth of stuff in order to use credit card.

I love to come here since it super close to campus. It is way closer than any other grocery store. The same people pretty much work there so they can recognize you if you are a regular. They don't have the best selection, but they do have all of the essentials.

I guess all the positive reviews are coming from people who went there for the sandwich shop, which seems okay.

All of the groceries here are nearly expired or already expired, and the shop its self is filthy and unorganized.

The workers are the worst part, they're extremely nice to regular customers, but they're unbelievably rude to new customers.  I came here after class to grab a drink, and I didn't have any cash on me.  When I got to register and handed the guy my card, he told me it was a $3 minimum.  I told him that merchants aren't allowed to impose a minimum for a Mastercard, if they accept the card, then they need to serve all Mastercard holders.  He immediately started yelling at me and said he's charged 50 cents for each credit transaction, so how about he just permanently refuses service to me instead.  He went from 0 to yelling and threatening me in 10 seconds, I was really surprised since he had been so nice to the regulars.  I told him refusing service to me because I was following the merchant agreement was also a violation of the merchant agreement, I didn't want there to be a problem over such a stupid thing.  He told me to go talk to the owner, who gave me a ridiculous excuse, saying that it's not a $3 charge to the Mastercard, it's a $3 purchase requirement to be allowed to use a credit card.  I was tired of being yelled at and lied to, so I just went next door to Walgreens and reported Sam's to Mastercard.

Stay away from this place, there are better places to get sandwiches around campus, and there are cheaper places to shop where you don't have to worry about a fridge full of expired milk and rotten eggs the day after you buy them.

I still remember when Sam's Market first opened its doors. I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw their products. I spent a good half hour just combing the aisles looking at all the things I hadn't seen for years, especially their wall of refrigerated drinks.

Their deli has expanded to offer hot sandwiches, burritos, whole roast chickens, and a giant fridge full of cheeses, sandwich meats, cakes, and cold dishes. They even have burgers now that come with fries. You can't go wrong with the chicken sandwich though. If you're up for a challenge, I recommend getting a burrito. If you think you've seen big, imagine a burrito with LaBurrita length and Chipotle girth. Sure, their meat and topping selection isn't as great as Chipotle, but for $5, you can get all the rice, meat, beans, salsa, and guac (actually it's more like avocado spread) you want.
I've never had the food here, but it is one of the few places with the MEXICAN glass bottle pure-cane sugar Cokes. Woohoo! Those things are so hard to find, and so good.

Sam's Market for me is about two things: hot sandwiches and soda selection.

Two things = TWO STARS
The sandwich is 6.99 for large portions of meat and a nice number of toppings, even though the bread is a little tough to chew through. I generally get the cheese steak because their sandwiches are a nice alternative to the not so Mexican burrito restaurant across the street. I still haven't tried Fred's Chicken yet, so update coming on that soon.

With the soda selection, it generally blows my mind when I get past the usual sodas you see at other markets. If you're a cream or orange soda fanatic, there's about six or seven types to try that may be on the bit pricier side but hey, curiousity killed my wallet (sigh, goodbye, Mr. Washingtons).

The other TWO STARS?
Their bleep bleep bleeping awesome service. Getting the sandwich/soda is half the battle. Paying for it is the other. Whether they're making fun of their cousins or lamenting why the 49ers kind of suck right now, they're really cool people. Their voices have inflections, they have emotions, they care about how your sandwich was from when you last came in... crap, Rami (sp?) went all Barney Stinson and started talking about Lebanese girls. I think the amount of laughter I get before I walk out the door helps me a bit more hungrier.

Nice people who serve nice food.

the produce here looks scary but the deli sandwiches are not bad. for about $4.99 you get about a 10 inch turkey sandwich with lettuce, tomato and onion (cheese is an extra $0.75). a bit overpriced, but its very convenient to the berkeley campus (corner of bancroft and telegraph). oh, theres a sign that says you get a free drink with any deli order. make sure to mention that and you, too, can get a free arizona pomegranate green tea.

Sam's has its flaws, that's for sure. It's not as expensive as Andronico's, but it still has some very expensive groceries. The milk they sell may be extremely close to its expiration date (or in one case, expired already).

However, their vegetables are great, the prices on milk, eggs, and veggies are fantastic, and the workers are fun people just to chat with. Location is great for running in and out, and I've bought more than one hangover cure there in a hurry.

Just watch expiration dates and avoid the very expensive products (chips, cereal, frozen goods).

The deli food is good, very large, lots of leftovers, but I mostly use Sam's as a place to make my own food.

I'm a student, obviously, and I work on campus nearby. I've always passed this place on my way to class, a quick trip to the pizza joints nearby, or a zip into Walgreens. It wasn't until today that I finally made my trip into Sam's and I'm glad that I did. 

This past week, I've noticed that a lot of my coworkers have been getting food on the breaks from Sam's. It started off with one or two of my coworkers coming back with great looking sandwiches. Interest soon aroused throughout the office and we all began to be fans of Sam's. The sandwiches are a hit with the office and although I didn't get one because I wasn't too hungry at the time, I did make a mental note to come back and definitely have a go. The sandwiches are a big hit because they are very filling and tasty. My coworkers were literally licking their fingertips so that must say something. For $6, a sandwich doesn't seem like too much of a setback given that I've sort of come to expect a sandwich or meal just to cost in that area. 

The sides are $3 and I love them. My coworkers have been coming back with onion rings and there was a fair amount; it was definitely worthwhile. Like I said earlier, I wasn't that hungry and I do love to eat hot and spicy food. I decided to give their hot fries a try. While the ordering process was a bit disorganized and the guy working the counter didn't interact with me at all after I said, "Spicy fries please," the food did please. What the guy at the deli lacked, the cashier definitely made up for. While I was waiting for my spicy fries, the cashier quickly chatted me up. We were talking about random going ons, what I study at Cal, the general area, and food. He said that the spicy fries would not leave me disappointed and we started talking about Man v. Food, which was definitely interesting, eventful, and pretty fun. My spicy fries were great by the way. They were homemade-cut potatoes. The spiciness was provided by a mix of a spicy red powder pepper and some smaller peppers similar to what you slap on a slice of pizza; he shook the container and although it didn't look pleasing, my taste buds did beg to differ. It was hot, spicy, and tasty! 

I did have a look at the groceries because it is convenient to have something so close by. We all know that it's a pain to go to Andronico's, Safeway, or Berkeley Bowl. We all know that Bear Market and all the other Cal quickie-marts are a rip, especially when you move out of the dorms and don't have meal points to spend recklessly. Sam's Market is actually competitively priced but I wouldn't buy my groceries here. I think the problem is that they're a mom and pop store and so they do just charge retail and can't give too many sales without getting kicked on the profits side like all the other large grocery chains can. It will be generally more expensive but not by too much. It's do-able but when I'm watching out for every buck, I will pass on buying some things here.

Sam's, you rock! I will give it five stars and I don't give out that rating a lot either.

I want to give you a 5 but I cant. This place is awesome...all except the produce which kinda sucks. I wanted to make a stirfry and it was a fail walking in there and seeing wilted veggies. They have AMAZING drink sections, the people that work there are WONDERFUL. I have been a faithful customer for 3 years...and they are always sooo nice...sorry for not giving you a 5...i just couldnt cause of the produce section...

5 Stars for THE BIGGEST burritos I have ever seen in my life. Their burritos put chipotle to shame, without any additional fees for guacamole or anything else. Oh and their meat is marinated really well; it is spicy and full of intense flavor. I do not know if their super burrito is on the menu, but if you ask for it, they will make it. WATCH them make it...it is really crazy how much they pack into one burrito. It lasts me two meals.

I created a yelp account just to spread the word. Buy their Super Burrito and you will be pleasantly surprised, like me!
