Much more extensive selection of groceries than the Walgreens next door.  Lots of tasty vegan snacks available here.  Their soda selection is also awesome!  They have both Mexican Coke AND Mexican Pepsi (made with real sugar instead of high-fructose corn syrup), plus a lot of other interesting glass bottle soda that you just don't see anywhere else.  Everything is reasonably priced and the cashiers are always friendly.

If you're a small girl like me, you will be full the ENTIRE DAY from eating a sandwich from Sam's. And if you're an average dude, or a fat meathead, maybe you can chow down at least another the same day. I swear today's epic four hour nap was a result of eating the Famous Fred's chicken sandwich. It was about time I tried something from the deli. It was tasty, portions extremely generous--loads of chicken hot off the grill, melted cheese, caramelized onions, the works.
 
I'm always in there anyway grabbing something quick from produce if I don't have time to go to an actual market or pacing the aisle of drinks. Glorious selection of drinks by the way. At least in my experience, I can only find Leninade in specialty stores. Plus, the people working behind the counter are always friendly and awesome, striking up convos here and there.

Groceries are all marked-up for their convenient next to campus factor.. but everything is also much closer to their expired/moldy date -- I bought a loaf of bread.. I found mold on it 3-5 days later... 

Won't be back for groceries.

The sandwiches are a decent price.  $4.99 for a cold one and $6.99 for a hot one.  The menu is real bare and the guy behind the deli counter (older gentleman) could use better customer service skills.  Speaks a bit harsh as if you should understand the menu within seconds of walking in there.  He tricks you into asking if you want cheese, which is extra, but is not mentioned on the menu.  

The sandwiches we had were pretty good, but the quality control could use some work.  We ordered 1 chicken sandwich and 2 roast beef.  The chicken was really good, but the 2 roast beef had different amounts of meat on the inside.  One sandwich was overflowing and the other one could barely cover the bread.  They also offer different types of bread, but will only give you the french roll for the hot sandwiches?  Something like the the other breads cannot handle it (I wish I could provide a better answer, but like I said earlier, I could not really understand this mario brothers looking character).  

A huge positive at this place is the customer service at the front of the grocery store.  Those two guys are hilarious and give off that local business feel.  Really personable and cool to talk to.  

I would go back here as the food is not pricey, its quick and pretty tasty.  They also have a pretty good selection of random snacks and produce in the back of the store.

Sandwiches here are awesomely delicious! My favorites are the Pastrami & Provolone and the Famous Chicken sandwiches! The portions are super generous and will definitely keep you full if you're looking for a sandwich meatier/more flavorful than Subway's and less expensive than Toaster Oven across the street. I've also occasionally gotten their breakfast burritos, which will definitely will keep you full for a long time if need be. There isn't much to the burritos usually other than a bunch of potatoes, eggs, shredded cheese, and your choice of meat, but it's decent. I'd recommend eating it relatively quickly too if you can because the burrito doesn't taste as good once it's more lukewarm.

While I usually come here for the sandwiches, the market's got a ton of grocery items including fresh fruits and veggies in the back of the store. There's also a pretty cool soda machine in the front that features a ton of soda flavors. 

The staff here is great and the family that runs the business is super friendly and welcoming! They always make sure that each and every customer is able to find what they need or if they had any trouble at all. Try their sandwiches!

So, my co-workers used to go to Fred's Market on University all the time, mainly for the chicken sandwiches.

I loved the sandwiches, but Fred's? Not so much. Maybe it was just University Ave. location or the fact that it was overrun by high school students much of the time, but it always seemed under-stocked and under-cleaned. I felt bad for the family that owned the place.

Enter: Sam's Market on Telegraph.

I go to Sam's all the time, because I love those chicken sandwiches, and I think the owners are great people. They have one of the best selections of off-brand sodas in Berkeley (Stewart's, Boylan's, Faygo, you name it) and they have a great selection of candy, to boot. (Man, I love Hi-Chew!) 

Seriously, the week would seem off if I didn't pay at least one visit to Sam's.

P.S. Dude who gets annoyed the guy at the counter tries chatting with you while you're listening to your iPod? Get a clue: Wearing an iPod when you're paying for something is just plain rude, and you're the one that's annoying.

"Like all burritos, when the burrito was made, it was inspected. If it had been sickly or mis-shapen, it would have been discarded. By the time it could stand, it was baptised in the fire of combat, taught never to retreat, never to surrender...Sam's, the effing biggest burrito Berkeley had ever known."

So, La Burrita burritos are sorta regular-sized with a more length than width. Chipotle burritos are like bricks - super fat and short.

Sam's is a combination of the two. IT'S A HUGE LONG BRICK OF A BURRITO AHHHHHHHH. I had always wondered how their burritos are since it's just a deli, but DAMN IT'S PRETTY GENEROUS. You can only get chicken (same as their chicken sandwich meat mmmm) or beef (I'll try this today), but you can get as much fixings as you want on it (cheese, beans, rice, salsa, guac, sour cream etc..

FOR $5.

This is the most incredible deal ever for value. Sure you don't have cilantro-rice, corn salsa, or chips, but this burrito itself is something else...You'll have to get it to believe me. I had it for the first meal of the day at 3pm, and I couldn't finish it....I'm quite an eater too.

It's not the super-best tasting thing ever, but I'll have it over La Burrita. If you're partial to Chipotle's taste, you might not enjoy it here, but for the value - it's hard to beat.

I'm pretty sure its a family-owned business because it's always the same guys and their father/mother at the register. They're so sweet! I'm giving Sam's 5 stars just because every time I come here the guy recognizes me and now knows my major and asks me about classes. They always try to strike up a conversation and ask about life. 

They have great sandwiches! Another thing is that there aren't really any close supermarkets around the immediate Berkeley campus area without having to go a little ways, but Sam's usually has the basics I need for baking or any other little get togethers.

They have drinks, spices, frozen foods, baked goods, etc that you can chooose from!

If you were to ever to go to Walgreens, try this place first.  They are extremely nice and honest.  I went in to buy ChapStick and the lady who owns the place actually told me the best thing to use is olive oil and not the products I am buying from them because it only makes my lips more dry.  The only downside to this place is the fact that they do not sale hard liquor.  Otherwise, best place ever for a night time beer run.

Previous posting for establishment so this review is about the grub I got today.

Hot Pastrami sammy on french roll (no onions, mayo and lettuce) totaling ~$7.

I'm pretty sure that it's not healthy but dang it's helllla good! José knows how to cook it right! 

+ Lotsa' meat, savory when hot
+ Tomatoes are NOT bland
+ Fresh french rolls
+ Takes less than 5 minutes (Dino works the register like a madman)
+ Frequent buyer's card (getting 7 stamps = free sammy OR plate)

Final Call:
This IS my sandwich of choice at Sam's. Friendly service + a buyer's card means I'll be eating a lottttta hot sammmies!

The bacon breakfast burritos are actually a good deal since they are only $3.99 and are probably 2000 calories. They are available until late afternoon.

Pretty decent place. It's a bit pricey for a corner store but the deli is good quality. I recommend the chicken shawarma sandwich.

The guy at the counter usually tries to chat with me or make jokes, which is kinda annoying since I'm usually listening to my ipod.

What a disappointment. I went there to grab a sandwich between classes and I cant believe how lame it is. 

There is tons of mayonnaise, one skimpy piece of wilted lettuce and a mushy piece of a tomato, not even a full slice covering less than a quarter of my sandwich. 
The turkey tastes like luchable meat from those poor quality prepackaged lucnhes in elementary school and I asked for pepperoncinis on the sandwich (since they only give you one on the side) and they give me two instead, on the side and not in the sandwich. 

I will never go back ot this place again, One of the most bland and disappointing sandwiches I've ever had.

The 1 star is for the cashiers who are very nice.

What a superb store.  Not only do they draw throngs of students lured in by the amazing-smelling chicken sandwiches (and full deli of falafel, piroshki, spanikopita, hummus, tabouli, grilled veg, meat salads), but for MY purposes they offer an astonishing selection of groceries --for great prices.  How do they do it??  I have even bought heads of romaine, celery, and fresh herbs here: not only are they priced as low as Berkeley Bowl, but they are huge and fresh too! None of this shady minimart produce, no no.

Their milk and eggs are also a staple for me, and you'll see in the fridge case as throughout the rest of the store that not only does Sam's stock everything you need,they stock it in at least two, often three, varieties: organic, non-organic, made-in-Mexico; or plain, lowfat, enriched; or vanilla, dragonfruit, goji berry...  Further, their odd little treats tucked around the store lend a treasure-trove feeling to the place. Ooh! Halva sticks -- never saw those before. Ahh! Lebanese cheese -- cooool.  Hey! Rose water, four kinds of tortilla chips, twenty-four kinds of hot sauce, twice as many organic chocolate bars....

Finally, the family that runs this place is utterly charming.  I love them.  They always greet with a smile, ask what I'm cooking with my motley assortment of groceries, check through customers efficiently. Sam's, I *heart* you.

Just to put this up front, I don't come here for the deli or prepared food. When Walgreen's lacks a food item, I come here. It's the best option seeing that Safeway and other larger supermarkets are much too far away. They have a good variety of goods, though priced higher than normal, as mentioned in reviews before me. However, when you're desperate to make soup on a chilly day or want a snack of pita bread and hummus, it's easy to come here since it's on the way for most who are unfortunate, like me, to live on Southside. As for the staff from the store, they need to learn to take a step back from chitchatting it up. Yes, it's nice that they're trying to get personal. But the creepy guys keep making comments about what I purchase. I don't need a commentary on a box of tea.

I can simply describe this place as a super amazing 7-11. The items like groceries and hygiene are a bit on the more expensive side, which is akin to a 7-11. There's nothing new or special about that.

But their deli counter is actually quite delicious and reasonably priced. Hot sandwiches are $6 with an extra 75 cents for cheese. I know that may sound pricey to some when Cheese n Stuff is right around the corner, but their bread is filling and the pastrami sandwich is always just the right temperature. You can also purchase schwarmas and various sides as well. You can watch them cook everything, even though ordering is a disorganized mess, and they are relatively quick getting everything back to you. Nothing is too unreasonably priced, they give sides in large quantities, and meals are filling.

I have to hand it to them: that's one aspect in which they totally beat out 7-11.

For a small, family-owned joint, Sam's Market has a FANTASTIC selection of items guaranteed to satisfy all of your last-minute grocery needs.  They carry just about any/every bottled/canned beverage I could possibly ever think to buy, and have supplied me with many a bottle of Perrier or Arizona Iced Tea before heading to the library for a study sesh.  Their produce selection is pretty limited, but they do carry most of the basics - I once was able to find all of the ingredients necessary for peach cobbler at Sam's.  Sam's also carries a huge variety of pretty obscure snack food items. (Digestive biscuits, anyone?) OH, and really quite an impressive selection of cup noodles-- after all, it is 30 yards away from the front of a university campus. 

Although I can't speak for the deli items, the packaged rotisserie chicken definitely did the job for this starving, newly-moved in college kid's first meal in her apartment! 

The staff is super friendly - my only criticism is that they dont accept plastic for charges of under $7.  it's pretty fair, just inconvenient for those of us who never carry around any cash :)  yay sam's!  shop here!

I LOVE YOU, SAM'S MARKET!  The hot sandwiches here are so amazing and the people that work here are so friendly.  

Once, I was ordering for a friend and I was reading the menu to her (she was on the phone with me) and I asked if she wanted a meatball sub.  The guy behind the sandwich counter looked me in the eye and then shook his head.  GOOD LOOKIN' OUT!  So instead, I got her the Phily cheesesteak and she LOVED it.  I usually get the chicken sandwich, which is a well seasoned shredded chicken on a french roll with your choice of cheese and lettuce plus tomato.  It comes with a spear of pickle on the side as well.

This place is so convenient, as it is very close to campus and you can get a yummy lunch here (without resorting to Subway sandwiches if you want a cheap sandwich) or pick up a few veggies that you don't want to trek all the way to Safeway for.  The prices are reasonable and even though the lines can be long at times, they always go pretty fast and the cashiers are always so nice and friendly you can't be grumpy with them.

DELI:

Grab extra napkins; you'll need them. That is, if you came for a sandwich. If you didn't come for a sandwich, stop and get a sandwich.

The sandwiches are big, and chicken is the mainstay. Whatever juices the meat is marinated will probably end up on your face, and the grilled onions -- oh man, I love grilled onions. Maybe you'll try some pastrami or a reuben once in a while, but you'll inevitably feel like you're being unfaithful. Even at around $7 with cheese, this is one of the better sandwich values around campus. (You get a pickle on the side!)

Also crucial is the sandwich stamp card; it's 10 stamps for one free sandwich, and you'll feel like a boss when you finally trade one in. (The card is also good on burgers and burritos; we'll get to those in a second.)

Major marks down for the grab-and-go breakfast burritos. These are very large and very dry. Avoid these.

Even marks for the regular burritos, which aren't exactly the best around. The steak is the thinly sliced sort that goes in sandwiches and I'm pretty sure it's straight hot sauce instead of salsa. Thing is, they're even BIGGER than the sandwiches. If you eat one for lunch, you probably won't need dinner. They're useful when you need a break from all the sandwiches you've bought. Former Cal DE Cameron Jordan once named the burrito as a favorite, and he stands at 6-foot-4, 283 pounds. (I'll assume he ate dinner after.) He's also about to picked in the first round of the NFL Draft.

Burgers are a great get as long as you're not too set on frills. They're fairly simple, but the beef patty is thick and the sesame seed buns bookend the whole thing nicely. Some fries come on the side too. (Sidenote: Spicy fries are good to get as a full side, as well as jalapeno poppers. The former works better if you're sharing.)

MARKET:

Solid enough, and convenient. It probably won't have everything you need or want, but it does in a pinch. The prices are fair for the most part, but you can always check the Walgreen's next door too if there's a significant difference.

It does carry a fantastic array of sodas and some harder to find candies/chocolates. Some homemade baklava and/or banana bread is usually tempting you as you check out. I have not tried these, but they do look appetizing.

I got fooled! Everybody mentioned in their reviews that the sandwiches were GINORMOUS. GINORMOUS they were NOT. One hot day, I was feeling hungry yet not hungry (my most hated feeling) and decided to *gasp* share a sandwich with someone else (I usually never share! DELICIOUS FOOD ALL MINE!). I heard their sandwiches here were BIG and I read on Yelp were BIG, so I figured in my not-so-hungry state, it would be enough.

FALSE. The sandwiches were only larger than average, not HUGE. Do not be deceived. Its smaller than Subway foot-long subs sold around the corner, which I can finish easy in one sitting.

The sandwich was only OK. The french bread tore up my mouth a bit because its was hard (thats what she said), although thats usually the case for me with any french bread. I would say I won't ever come back here, but ever since Sufficient Grounds closed, I'm a little short on sandwich choices. Maybe I'll try something that changes my mind here, who knows. I'm not betting on it though.

As a side note, they carry a bunch of other convenience store stuff too, as they are, well, a market after all. Never tried their produce/fruit stuff in the back, but they DO have a good selection of drinks (foreign drinks and even mexican coke I think).

*Note: may be a biased review since I was an employee

*Note 2: Christina B. mentioned the free drinks deal with the deli order. That was our beginning promotion because we had a lot, and I do mean A LOT, of cases of the plastic Arizona bottles. We pretty much just wanted to get rid of them, so that's why they came with the drinks. It's a nice promotion, but until we get a lot of cases for a really cheap price, I don't know when the next free drink will be.

*Note 3: We've had some people ask about all the deli charges. Basically it comes down to this: If it's a cold sandwich, it's just $4.99, no tax. If you order anything hot, we gotta tax it. The cheese, for 75 cents more, is not taxed. (They've been meaning to get a new deli sign and I keep telling them to make the cheese charge a little more prominent)

Pros:
- A great deli. If you get anything on a roll, it will definitely fill you very quickly. The chicken sandwich is a must. They even sell roasted chicken either by the whole or half and those are delicious too.
- An eclectic mix of drinks. I love the Looza nectar and the very random soda bottles.
- It sells produce that gets delivered M-F.
- It's very convenient for those who don't want to go far to Safeway and don't want to spend tons of money at Whole Foods, Andronico's, or Berkeley Bowl.
- One banana will not cost you 75 cents on your way to school or work in the morning.
- They are in the process of fixing the shawarma machine.
- There is a really cute cashier who works there and is very friendly. If you're short a penny or two, she will let you go. (I think this is where the biased part comes in. *ahem*)

Cons:
- Some of the items sell at retail price, not at a nice discounted price that you can find at the big companies like Walgreens or Safeway. The cereal boxes are at least $4.00 and as high at $6.00.
- Sandwich prices? Sure, $6.00 for a hot sandwich (not including tax) and the extra 75 cents for cheese may be a lot to some people, but take my word for it: order it on a roll (since the bread fills you up quickly) and you will see how much you can eat of that whole sandwich.
- No seating. For now anyway.

We're getting good business; people like our deli and they like our convenient location. We may be getting the liquor license at some point and I hear from those who shop at Fred's on University, they stock really fun and an eccentric mix of alcohol.

P.S. They are going to keep the Rexall sign as a part of history. The place that was there before Sam's actually wasn't even Rexall; it was called Blue Heaven. At and some point before that, there was a soda pop diner called Foley's... thus the name of the deli.

Ordering is a big disorganized, but Sam's Market has a cool variety of goodies: sandwiches, baked stuff, fruit snacks, fruit. All at reasonable prices.

I tried Sam's Famous Chicken...it wasn't amazing, but I can say that it was HUGE. About twice the size of what you'd get at Cheese n Stuff, Cafe Espresso...or for those who don't know Berkeley sandwiches, about twice the size of an In and Out Burger only with more meat. It consisted of bread, bbq chicken (I think), lettuce, choice of cheese, and a slice or two of tomatoes, for $6.  

I'm more about quality than quantity though.

The sandwiches are not THAT huge as everyone says they are. It is pretty damn big and I would not be able to eat it in one sitting, but I any growing boy can finish the thing. It is about the same size as a footlong sub. It is pretty damn cheap, I must say.
$5 cold cut sandwich
$6 hot sandwich
$3 sides

I got a pastrami sandwich and it was good, except they gave me cheddar instead of pepperjack, like I asked for. The french roll crust was too hard and chewy, so I'd have to try the sourdough next time. Actually, there are a lot of things that I'd have to go back and try like the schwarmas, burrito, and burger. We'll see!

When I was a kid, my aunt co-owned a convenience store in Glendale.  Always referred to as The Store, this place was a kind of mecca for me.  Originally, they made and delivered pizza, but even when they gave up the pizza part of their business, they still had Sam the deli man and a regular customer known as Lovely Bob.  Why Lovely Bob?  Well, he would come in to the store every day, and when my aunt would ask him how he was doing, he would reply, without fail, "Lovely."

But my favorite part of The Store was the cooler.  Remember when convenience stores had actual coolers?  These weren't loaded from the front; instead, the employees would stock cold drinks, dairy products, and the frozen foods from behind the wall.  Well, The Store had one of those coolers, and whenever I went there, my cousin and I would don these crazy wool-lined jackets and freeze our butts off as we restocked soda.  It was fun, and I secretly always hoped we would get locked into the cooler like Jack and Felipe got locked into the Jack's Bistro walk-in freezer on Three's Company.

Well, Sam's Market reminds me a lot of The Store.  It's not as expansive, but the employees are really friendly and helpful, and there's even a deli that makes sandwiches.  I don't know whether they have their own Lovely Bob, but they might.

$12 plate of fried fish, German pancakes, and a beer/cocktail.  Plus bread, butter, applesauce, and tartar sauce.  

Pretty delicious.  And we won the raffle!  Their chocolate chip cookies are amazing.  

There was live music which was also nice.  There was an accordian player.

I was invited to the SNMFF and requested ahead of time if tofu could be an option.  Hopes not up, just wanted to be supportive because I know Tim, one of the owners.  OMG!!!  I have never tasted fried tofu this great!  It was sooooo good and definitely a comfort food!  The bread almost didn't make it home...  (I arrived at 8:30 and they were closing shoppe).  I will definitely back next month!  My understanding is that they occur monthly.  Yummy!!!!

Holy Fish Fry! $10 gets you a plate with 2 large battered and fried fish fillets (w/tartar sauce), 2 potato pancakes (w/apple sauce), coleslaw, a drink and a raffle ticket. Additionally, you can buy some of the best carrot cake you have ever had for not much at all. Tonight they had a face painter for the kids, an accordion player and raffle prizes such as a bottle of wine or a "Fish Fry" tee shirt. Awesome atmosphere, great food. I'm hooked. Happens monthly on a Friday, check their website for details!

Stella Nonna did a tasting at Berkeley Rep which was very good, and I got a postcard that said they do a Milwaukee style fish fry in Berkeley! I had just come back from Wisconsin, and experienced a real fish fry and loved it. This is a tastier, more Bay Area version of a Milwaukee fish fry with quality fish (I wish it were all you can eat though like in the midwest!)

It is an outdoor gathering with tables with heaters, or you can sit inside this long tent thing with a long table. You pay $12 and you get 2 big pieces of very good fish, cole slaw, giant potato pancakes, homemade roll, and a Milwaukee style beverage. I was REALLY hoping they'd have Spotted Cow, but they only had Miller or PBR (also wine and sprite if you wanted). The service was [surprisingly] very fast. We thought that we were going to have trouble finding a seat, but people seemed to be getting in and out pretty fast so seating wasnt an issue for us (just 2 people). The groups of 3+ people seemed to have a little more trouble finding seating, but no one was waiting around that long. There was an accordion player there too, and lots of kids running around.

They only seem to do this once a month, and I'm already looking forward to going back, this time with more people in tow! Its a super casual laid back atmosphere with families, old friends, college kids, high schoolers, etc. Just a really nice place to just chill and eat good food. Can't wait until the weather gets warmer--I'll be here every month. Really glad I can have a "fish fry" experience without having to go all the way back to Wisconsin!

I have been here for brunch and for dinner; I prefer the dinner menu. The vegan charcuterie is always fantastic. The chef's imagination and inventiveness makes for food that is both exciting and satisfying.

All you need to know is spicy tomato pizza. I'm not even vegan in the slightest, but their use of capers, cashew puree, chili oil, and herbs is fantastic. I will get this every time.

Definitely Recommended.
Really delicious!
Tasty! We went there before a play at Berkeley Rep.  Delicious salads, and the pork chop was the bee's knees.

We were here for brunch today.  Much ado about not much, I'd say.  My egg sandwich,, with fancied-up name for hamburger bun and withered bacon, was quite bland, even though it includes cheddar cheese and about 4-5 leaves of micro arugula.  The eggs were cooked over well done.  My partner had had the Beluga Lentils that was also quite bland.  But she was more forgiving.  While I am all for seasonal and local, I am not sure my experience today would warrant another visit to this particular establishment.

I enjoyed coming here! We ordered the following:

- Grilled Squid
- Peppered Pizza
- Mushroom Stew
- Classic Burger w/fries

The grilled was chilled and delectable! I love love love LOVED it. Peppered pizza was amazing and so full of flavor, but the mushroom stew was disappointing as it lacked spice and flavor. The assortment of mushrooms was refreshing though, as well as the toasted bread served along with it. The burger was served medium-rare, just the way we like it! However, it was under salted and under spiced. The fries served along with it were quite tasty though! 

I accompanied my dinner with a square one vodka soda with splash of lime. While my companions opted for the complimentary bubbly or still water that the restaurant offered.

I ended the dinner with a nice cup of cappuccino instead of sweets... a sign that I'm getting older! Overall it was a lovely night, but I think that next time I will stick to the pizza or opt for the vegan plate as opposed to the mushroom stew.

I am in love with Gather so this review could be biased.

My fiance and I had reservations for 7:15 for the Magruder Ranch and Hodo Soy Beanery prix-fix menu, she had the vegan options and I had the meat, unfortunately we didn't share but it is okay because she is Vegan and I was satisfied with all the courses.

We both had the wine pairings as well which was a nice compliment to the food. We also sat at the bar which is fun getting to know your local bar tender, if you are into that sort of thing.

The 'head shoulders, knees and toes' was simply one of the best dishes I have ever had the luxury to eat and to lay my eyes upon, the presentation was beautifully arranged,the dish was something like a fried terrine the outside was light and crispy the inside was deliciously buttery and melt in your mouth saliva inducing flavors.

The Loin, Belly and Blood was also food of the gods, a slice of blood sausage, a nice piece of  belly which had a fatty layer, I love pork and this was a meal for the Pork Gods and Pork Lovers.

Oh how can I not forget the Lard ice cream it was infused or combined with some citrus notes so it was not so heavy, and was amazing with the pine nut tart.

If you have only been once to Gather I suggest you give it another try maybe on a week night if you have time, I will keep coming back for new and interesting food delights.

Very much enjoyed our brunch choice of a Pancetta Pizza with  egg, green garlic, spring onion tops, chili, and oregano.  Quite delicious and enough for two.   Went down well with my reasonably piced glass of Roederer Estate 'Brut.  Service and ambiance also a strength.  Would come often if I was lucky enough to live in Berkeley..

While it's true Gather not only accommodates vegetarians and vegans - they celebrate them - there is something here for everyone.

Some real stand outs include - raw local halibut mixed with minutina, grapefruit, radishes and hot green garlic oil, house-made meatballs served over creamy polenta, seared cod on a bed of artichoke fava bean puree, baby artichokes and wild mushrooms and a burger made with Prather Ranch beef. 

The only thing more appealing than the plating of their food is well, the plates themselves. Things look even tastier artfully arranged on this beautiful tableware. 

I love everything about Heath Ceramics - the color palette, the classic yet modern design and it's all still crafted in Sausalito as it has been since 1948. It even makes paying the check easier to swallow - no, not really. It just makes the presentation warmer - and that is how I would describe everything else at Gather - warmer.

Went here for Sunday lunch - table of 6 people. At first, I was extremely impressed with the service. We wanted to sit outside, but the only available table was in the full sun. We thought we'd give it a shot but realized pretty quickly it would be too hot. The hostess noticed right away and figured out how to configure some tables to get us in the shade. At that point the service had 5 stars.

So we sat with our menus and discussed the options and talked and talked and talked and....talked...and...umm, is there anyone here to check whether we're ready to order....and talked, and finally our waiter came. Probably 20 minutes in all with no one since the hostess coming by.

Since it was Sunday there were brunch-y options so our orders ranged from the french toast to a hamburger to the vegetarian market vegetable polenta/spicy lentil dish with the poached egg on top to pizzas. The drink order and the food order were taken at the same time....the drinks seemed to take forever, while the food seemed to be appropriately timed.

However, after the food came, that was the end of our server sightings....again....for what seemed forever. When he did come back, he brought the check. Weird. Because we wanted dessert. Although at this point I was truly hoping no one would order any because I just couldn't stand to think about the wait again. But fortunately the desserts came out in a timely manner, along with round 2 of the check.

Our server was completely friendly....that wasn't the issue. And when I left I looked around inside and outside and it sort of looked like although it wasn't terribly busy, he may have been the only full-fledged waiter! There were buspeople and hostesses but I truly didn't notice anyone else taking orders. I could be wrong though.

The food was fine. Nothing earth-shattering. The atmosphere was comfortable and inviting. But the additional 30-40 minutes we spent there unnecessarily prevents me from putting this at the top of my list to go back. Darn.
Even the decorative persimmon was delicious!

Fresh, high-quality ingredients, creative menu items, attentive service, and an all-around great dining experience on a busy Friday evening. 

My friend and I shared:
-Vegan "charcuterie" plate-- sampler style consisting of very creative concoctions featuring various veggies; (came with toasted, rustic slices of bread)
very tasteful, and a treat for those who love to try new foods.
-Squash blossom Pizza-- thin, crispy crust, thin layer of cheese and a few blossoms; really good and light.

I'm sort of stuck on Gather. It seemed half the things on the table were remarkable,  half of them weren't. The menu changes often, though, and if the opportunity came up to return, I gladly would.

Kale salad - amazing. 

Minestrone soup with an egg cracked into it - very good (see "Katie goes to LA and eats in Koreatown").

The vegan pizza was okay, sort of ruined by whatever fresh herbs they added, which just didn't jive well with the other flavors. But this could just be an installment of my own storied relationship with pizza, and a stubborn reluctance to let "California pizza" in.
Ridiculously overpriced for so-so dishes and tiny portions. I was underwhelmed. Obsequious service didn't make up for it.

Any place that charges $ 21.00 for the Smoked Artichoke "ENTREE"...that would not even fill a tablespoon, does not even deserve one star.  I was done with my "dinner" 30 seconds after it was placed before me.  Literally, no exaggeration here. My friend ordered the Vegan Charcuterie and was blesed with two tablespoons worth.  With our stomachs still grumbling with hunger pangs, we headed out the door and across the street to Saturn Cafe for vegan nachos and cupcakes, for way less than we paid for the artichoke entree alone.

We had a delicious meal at Gather. We were in a bit of a rush but they accommodated us and got us out with plenty of time to spare. The food was outstanding. I started with the calamari and had the squash "risotto" for my entree. My dining partner had a salad with some delicious giant radishes on it and had the burger for an entree. Not only was the food original and delicious, the portions were a perfect size so that having a starter and an entree didn't leave me feeling overstuffed. 
My only complaint was that we ordered wine and our appetizers came out before our wine. We told the food runner that we were still waiting for the wine and he brought it out immediately. It was frustrating because while we were waiting, we saw our server chatting with another employee not making an attempt at eye contact with any of her tables.
That said, we will happily go back (next time when we're not in a hurry!) and order the pizza because it looked fabulous!

Had a phenomenal meal at Gather on Thursday night. Each plate was a delicious work of art. So much care went into the presentation. The salmon starter was divine. Loved the lamb - melt-in-your mouth goodness. 
Our waiter was knowledgeable and attentive. The ladies at the desk were friendly and welcoming. 
Can't wait to go back!
EXCELLENT. This is the spot where we take our friends whenever they come into town. GREAT food--they are always mixing it up. And the ambiance is lovely.

I came here for lunch after my boyfriend's graduation. We were seated pretty quickly as I had made a reservation a day earlier.

Everyone shared different pizzas, and I had the grilled squid salad. Overall, the meal was kind of underwhelming, especially at the price that it was at. 

The salad was very tasty, but I would recommend ordering it as an appetizer (granted a pricey one for lunch). I left the restaurant still feeling a tad hungry. I don't think I would come back if I had the choice.

This place manages to calm, comfort, and cheer me up on the coldest of cold and grayest of grey days! Sho and I stopped by Gather for weekend brunch as the last stop of our weekend together, and it proved to be a comforting and delicious finish. 

We ordered the egg sandwich sans additions, the vegetable soup (broth infused with Shittake, asparagus, green peas, etc.) and the Floriani Red Flint polenta pancakes. The hot soup was soothing and rich for an overcast day, but the real deals were the main dishes. Both the egg sandwich and the pancakes are worth their $8-$11-ish cost, the sandwich especially! Never have I had pancakes so uniform and with such a strong (delicious) wheaty flavor. The sweet 
Sauvignon Blanc blueberry and ricotta toppings atop the pancakes painted a pretty picture and really helped to complemented the flavor of the wheat base. Yum! 

Best of all was the egg sandwich! Slices of bread toasted in olive oil + a sunny-side up egg + cheddar cheese + arugula? It touches one's inner desire for a spectrum of textures and savoriness. 

Gather definitely has one of the best brunches in the Bay Area and is among my personal favorites! The vibe is rustic yet modern, new-age with themes of reuse and tradition. The crowd is composed of the young and old, but everyone is really friendly and chill.

This restaurant is probably my favorite restaurant ever (if it's not, it's tied with Ubuntu).  They have redefined what pizza should be - delicious thin crust that's not burnt stiff, with a puffy bready edge, with a light touch on the sauce and cashew cheese and toppings.  Their vegan charcuterie is very innovative, complex and flavorful.  Some of their cocktails are very, very good.  (This is high praise coming from me.)

If I had only one meal left in my life, I would get all of the above, shared with good company, and oh, I'd die a happy, happy woman.

I really liked Gather. I came here on a Wednesday night for dinner, and it was packed. It is admittedly kind of a hipster place, but it doesn't come off as pretentious at all (which is a difficult feat!). 

The interior is beautiful -- it feels open and modern while simultaneously feeling comfortable and home-y. 

Service was friendly (this was probably why the restaurant didn't seem pretentious)! The price was relatively cheap, less than $20 per entree (another reason why this place felt accessible). The cocktail menu is really interesting!

Food was creative, tasty, and definitely worth its price. As many, many other reviews have mentioned, the Vegan "Charcuterie" is a must get. My co-diner had said that it had been better in previous instances (I guess they change it up somewhat often?), but I really, really liked it. It was gorgeous and colorful and had a wide range of flavors and textures. My entree was a little disappointing (special of the evening: goat meatballs) since the vegetables that accompanied it were a little bland. However, I do love goat and other game-y meats, and I love the fact that the restaurant served goat. I am fully willing to admit that my lack of love for the entree was because my stomach was twisted up in knots (definitely not the fault of the restaurant). 

In short, I'd definitely come again :)

A return visit highlighted Gather's flaws. The waitstaff is poorly trained, uneducated about the food they are serving, and altho well meaning, they are like most of Berkeley's restaurants: Amateur Hour. They can't pace a meal properly and at these prices, that's embarrassing.

The vegan charcuterie this time was not as creative or well executed. Okay, but not the stunning dish we had the first two times. Soup (pumpkin-tomato) was so-so - the ingredients got in the way of one another, instead of making a greater whole. 

T bone steak was huge but poorly conceived and executed, simply swimming in olive oil. Lamb ribs jerk style were tasty but it's a fatty cut. Vegetarian plate was astoundingly boring, as bad or worse as what Chez Panisse Cafe served us last year. 

The pizza, so great on our last visit, faltered like everything else. A little too salty on the sauce, and it needed more heat to be interesting. It ended up like a few ingredients taken at random and sprinkled atop the dough...nothing particularly imaginative or exciting.

Desserts are supersweet. If you like Cheesecake Factory, you'll love Gather's. Tea and coffee both showed Gather's consistently erratic execution.

Us? You'll find us at FIVE and Riva Cucina, or maybe at La Note or even Venezia. But not here, not again. Sloppiness should not be mistaken for casualness.

I have done Millennium many many times and always felt that their entrees never measured  up to their appetizers...not true at Gather where both are out of this world--always surprising, fresh and fabulous. Not inexpensive but you won't feel you're paying for posh--the value always shows up on the end of my fork.

I used to hate eggplants, but after Gather's eggplant sandwich (which I don't think they have anymore, sadly) for brunch, I've become a fan. It was a bit confusing when we were paying bills - it turned out that the waiter misunderstood our orders (which was soup+sandwich set, instead of whole soup and whole sandwich which was how the waiter served and billed us), but the waiter was real nice and apologized, and just  billed us for the soup+sandwich amount. We went back another day and had their pizza (which I can't remember), and it was good too! Looking forward to going back soon.

I love Gather. The food is innovative and you feel great eating it because it's healthy and they try to do local produce! Sure you don't get big portions, but it's not about eating a lot, it's about the flavor and where your food comes from. I also got a cocktail while I was there, the Bee Sting, and it was one of the best I ever had. It's a casual to nice setting with a nice ambiance. The only thing I didn't like about Gather was waiting so long to get seated! But that is easily avoided with a reservation, which we didn't have. I can't wait to go back again!
Great food and a great experience.  The food is fresh and locally sourced.  Atmosphere casual and relaxing.  We went here for a family celebration and were not dissapointed.

Probably my new favorite restaurant in Berkeley. We received a gift certificate for our wedding as a special date, and it was such a great treat! 

Ambience: Really great lighting, and a very pretty restaurant. I love the circular design. Even the menus look amazing!

Service: Our server was slightly awkward (but I can't judge...because I'm Queen Awkward) but he was thoughtful and prompt.

Food: We ate....

- Fried Green Beans with Bacon: Delicious flavor. Very savory - with a nice kick as well. I mean, bacon makes everything amazing right?

- Corn Pizza with Pancetta: I'm going to make a bold statement. This is my new favorite pizza. Over Cheeseboard, Zachary's, Little Star, etc. We ate the whole thing shamelessly. The crust is thin with air pockets of doughy goodness. Goat cheese, onions, and corn....oh! And potatoes! Plus, the pancetta! Delicious add-on.

- Roasted Strawberries: I would eat this every day. It's grown-up Strawberry Shortcake. 

We also each ordered two drinks (the Bee Sting is so refreshing...and intoxicating). All of that for under $100. We aren't ballers, but I would go back for a semi-special occasion.

My girlfriend took me here for my birthday as I had been wanting to go for awhile. Usually I am not for stories in Yelp reviews but the reason I mention this is that Gather is perfect for something like a romantic birthday dinner, the atmosphere is nice, pretty quiet, and intimate. We sat at the bar where you can watch the chef prepare food which was cool, we watched as he prepared several orders of the vegan "charcuterie" which looked really good. I am what is called a "flexitarian" (I eat meat sometimes and it must be sustainable, free range, etc.) and my girlfriend is a vegetarian. Gather caters to vegans (though there is only one option but I will note this comes in many forms), vegetarians, and carnivores. I ordered the burger with meat that is sourced from Prather ranch (which i looked up on-line and is all about sustainability) and Sierra Nevada cheddar, it was one of the best burgers I have ever had!! My girlfriend ordered the Baby Artichokes plate which was unbelievable!!! It had black chickpeas which I had never seen before and smoked potatoes, really really good, we both loved it. Not bad on price either for how good it is and how cool the environment is. It would be good to make a reservation as well, it gets busy, the first time we tried to come the wait was over an hour. Would definitely come back and recommend to others.

Woo Hoo.  Wonderful friendly hostess and waiters.  Fabulous fig pizza,
and incredible apple salad.  What a great meal in a great new restaurant.  I can't wait to go back and try everything on the menu!  I loved it.

I had one of the best burgers I've ever eaten at Gather.  We popped in there on a whim and they just happened to have a bacon and blue burger that day - fabulous!  Their housemade ginger soda is one of my favs.  The salads are on the fancy side, but I've liked every one I've tasted.  I'm a meat eater, and their meat dishes always sound too tempting for me to go veggie.  Read the menu carefully to prevent getting an unpleasant surprise when your order comes to the table.  The last time I was there, my companion thought he was getting something resembling a taco salad but it ended up being a vegan dish.

My FAVORITE place in all of the Bay Area!  I've gone about once a week on average since June.  I take all my friends, and even celebrating my birthday(!) there tomorrow!  I always get the vegan charchuterie, love the kombucha on tap, house sodas, and nonalchoholic beers.  Everything's well made, creative, thoughtful/ethical, and affordable.  Keep up the great work!

It feels good eating here, not only because your belly is full of yummy food, but because of their sustainable approach to eating out. 

The staff knows the menu and ingredients well and can inform you of the origin of everything on your plate. 

Unlike other pricey, fancy menus (cough, Benu), the proportions are generous and won't leave you going home hungry.

I've been to Gather a few times now.  Enough to have experienced its highs and lows.  The low notes are minor and brief such that Gather earns a solid 5 stars.  I'm proud to have Gather in Berkeley.  I love to take visitors to our town of weirdos, ex hippie hags and post adolescents to this place and watch them marvel at our Californianess while stuffing themselves with vegan charcuteries and pickled whatsitnots... My Midwestern hick friends will never be the same...  Gathers food is sumptuous and makes you feel good.  The cocktails are superb and the staff are plentiful and fun.

Went there for lunch and it was a lot better food.  I still don't really want to go back, but I know there are those that love this place.  It just doesn't do it for me.  Alas.  So why 4 stars?  Because it likely deserves them.

Gather exceeded expectations.  I particularly liked the tomato and cashew cheese pizza and the veg charcuterie.  The quinoa risotto was good.  The kale salad had a nice flavor and was cooked well but overly salted.  Bravo!  Especially for such a new restaurant.  The staff = polite and friendly.  The decor = fun.

I've been to gather many times and have never had anything less than an amazing experience.  Over time I figured out a winning system for ordering: the weirder something on the menu sounds, or the harder of a time I have wrapping my head around what the server is describing, the more amazing it will taste.  I've had so many bites of food there that have made me say, "I can't even understand what I'm eating right now, but I'm loving it".  To me, that's what distinguishes an incredible restaurant from the rest.

As another reviewer said arriving on a Saturday night without a reservation is a mistake. A party of four of us arrived at 6.50 and thought we got our name on a list...15 minutes later checked and it hadn't got registered in the system. We were told it'd be another 30minutes. We waited for another 1hr10mins to be told people had taken longer than expected to leave and it'd be another 20minutes. We left for  another restaurant very annoyed at being so mucked around.

Gather is an interesting place. I love how they have daily menus that change every season, giving a fresh look on the season's produce and what one can cook with them. I shared a Vegan Charcuterie and a black truffle pizza with a friend, and I applaud the flavors presented on the Charcuterie, as well as the taste of the pizza.

The pricing can be a bit high, but is decently worth it, as everything is really fresh and organic. I cannot make a recommendation on a specific order, as the menu changes, but if you have the chance the Vegan Charcuterie is a must, despite the absence of meat!

I am probably reiterating what everyone's been saying, but if you have a large group, you should definitely reserve a spot, as seating above 2 or 3 gets difficult fast! At least with a 2 or 3 party, you could sit at the bar of the "food" bar. The ambiance of the place is really nice, and going there for dinner, I enjoyed the semi-dark lighting with the homey wood furniture.

That place is really neat because it's different, well thought out and the menu features items you don't usually find everywhere. All sustainable from the tables to the building and the food of course. Original choice of seasonal vegetables.

Loved the pancetta and rucola pizza. The avocado and grapefruit with piment d'esplette salad. Not cheap

Do make a reservation otherwise you'll wait for your table for ever!!!

Gather is self-described as "the first restaurant/cafe/bar to bring affordable, sustainable, delicious food to downtown Berkeley three meals a day, seven days a week." 

So is Gather really a one-of-a-kind, restaurant that offers affordable, sustainable, and delicious food? Without a doubt. 

Let's start first with the menu- a melange of organic, local, sustainable, gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian plates. Needless to say, we took great delight in watching the finished works of art buzz past our table. With a recommendation from our waiter, we decided on the vegetable "charcuterie" plate which was artfully served on a wooden cutting board. Our waiter indicated that this was the most popular item on the menu, and rightfully so. Each of the five small vegetable salads were fresh, delicious and consumed in their entirety. As for the wine list, I was happy to see such a diverse selection of local, organic, and sustainable wines. Our waiter went the extra mile by enthusiastically explaining the difference between each of these classifications. 

The ambience rivaled the food. The artwork was creative. The staff was friendly. But best of all is the philosophy of the restaurant. The concept of local, sustainable, and organic food and wine is gaining momentum, especially in the Bay Area. It feels good to to support a restaurant like Gather, and in return, be given the gift of a wonderful dining experience.
decent service, decent food.  nothing gritty or interesting going on.

I love the pizza here, I would have never thought egg would have been good on pizza until I tried it!! The menu is always small since it's based on what they can get fresh, but the selection is always amazing and I usually find something I like!

We have eaten here several times since it opened and I got to say - every single adventure is a complete delight. The chef is so astoundingly creative and puts flavors together with such brilliance. The wait staff seem to love their job and talking about the food. They have so much integrity, getting their food from local sustainable, humanely practicing farms. The atmosphere has just as much integrity and is a fun environment, not too loud and not too fancy. My wife is a vegetarian and is so so picky about food and absolutley loves this place. We just ate here the other night and she exclaimed that it was perhaps the best meal she ever had. I am also a food snob and can't say enough good about this place. so so love it. you got to go

Please open from 230-5pm.  I missed you by half an hour and am currently across the street watching people get turned away because you  aren't open.  It's 324pm and the turn away count is up to seven.  I'm sure Saturn is greatful for the business, but please open from 3-5.
Came here for lunch with a friend. Loved the ambience and atmosphere! Server was helpful and friendly. Food was delicious! I definitely recommend Gather for lunch! Will try dinner another time!

Wow! My first time at a vegan/veggie restaurant and I was pleasantly surprised! Loved this place. 

We arrived at 4:45 right before the restaurant opened (@5pm) b/c we could not get a reservation on a Sat night. Now I know why..We were seated and greeted by a very happy, healthy staff...everyone was super friendly.  Our waiter was helpful and attentive to our needs. 

We started with cocktails. I ordered the Bitter Rose - it was okay...a bit strong for me, but good overall. For dinner, we started with the Vegan "charcuterie". It was pretty good...I had no idea what I was eating, but my mouth seemed to like it. We ordered the Delta asparagus & Spicy Tomato pizza. Asparagus: Just okay. Spicy Tomato pizza: YUM! Very flavorful, just the right amount of spice -- my most favorite dish of the night! We ordered a few more starters too, but I can't remember the names of the dishes :( 

Overall, we had a great experience here. Great service and good food. I will definitely come back again. This place has definitely opened my eyes to veggie/vegan food. I am a meat lover and the closest I get to vegan/veggie food is FRIED tofu. lol.

Unfortunately, it was very disappointing..

My daughter and I went there for Sunday lunch, expecting to wait a while. To our surprise, there was no wait. in fact, the place was half empty on beautiful sunny mid Sunday.

I had the special salmon dish. The fresh wild salmon was very good quality, but it wasn't prepared to the potential. The sauce the fish was in, was bland and nothing to scream about. My daughter's baked egg dish had a very similar sauce, too. They need to design each dish with its own special sauce and side dish.

We also shared French toast, but it was just all right. Nothing special. The fresh orange juice didn't taste like the one I make with my own orange from the backyard. Again, not enough flavor.

We watched many people stepping into the restaurant, checked the menu and left. It's too pricy for Berkeley casual crowd?

We will not go back again.

We went for brunch and mostly loved it. Creative and delicious food. Cute open interior. It would be a 5 star review if the wait staff could be bothered to be friendlier. We will give it another try for sure.

first, I love the ambiance of this place. seriously, it is upscale but indie, such a nice vibe. the water is served to you in a strauss milk glass bottle, very eco friendly and i like how they give you water so you don't have to constantly ask for refills. 

I got the vegan dish with the assortment of four different courses....kind of weird and unique. not what i was expecting...probably won't oder it again

my boyfriend got the carrot dish...it was good but too rich..he said he probably wouldn't order it again. for 45 dollars it was a bit of a bust, but the service was great and the ambiance made up.

maybe its just my personal taste, but gather wasn't for me.
the pizza did look delicious though and if i were to go back, that is what i would get.

After walking by this place countless times and finally getting the chance to try it, I AM NOT IMPRESSED.

The pizzas are a hit or miss. I like the thin crust, but they often burn the edges, making it unedible. The benedicts did not look appealing. My friends who got it were not satisfied. It was dark, almost black and filled with beans. O__o Weird. The mimosas are okay. The menu said that they made it with fresh squeezed orange juice, but I did NOT taste the freshness.

I don't mind paying a bit more for food, but this place did not deliver the quality I expected. Overall, I am quite disappointed.
Great tasting food, even for the vegetarian and vegan options. The food is filling, but not too heavy.

Goodness resides here.  Not much to add to all the other positive reviews, but here is my 2 cents anyway.
The vegan charcuterie was truly the highlight of the meal. Every day during my visit when dad asks me what I want to eat, my mind seems to turn to it but I don't want to disappoint dad by avoiding his cooking ;-o.
The Winter Kales Salad was also a winner. Wash it down with a Ginger beer and I'm a uber happy camper. 
The other plates were good but not as memorable. Just one note: the fries with the burger kinda sucked - cool temp and soggy did not measure up - sorry.
Gather charcuterie, you reside in my dreams until we meet again!

Gather had been on my short list of restaurants to try for awhile, so I was really looking forward to dining there.  We had a short wait at the bar before our table was ready and had a good conversation with the bar tender ("mixologist" now, right?) and he recommended a few cocktails that were interesting and tasty.  We then moved to our table and were scoping out what everyone around us was eating.  We really wanted to go the pizza and burger route, but we also wanted to get a sense of the the offering by ordering something across the menu - everything was interesting, but more interesting than delicious.  I found myself comparing Gather's version to other versions I have had and although Gather was good, it wasn't outstanding.  I will definitely try Gather again, but maybe for lunch or brunch - and if I do go for dinner, I think I will go the pizza route and see how they stand up.

Gluten Free people take note:  this place is amazing!  

As a strictly gluten free person with a child who is highly reactive to gluten, as well, we are very limited when it comes to places to eat out.  Other gluten free people will understand this.  Gather is a little piece of heaven for those with gluten free food restrictions! 

When we do find a place we can eat, it often offers things that are gluten-free-by-elimination (burger w/o the bun, no sauce or fries, veggies w/o the seasoning, etc.)... Not so with Gather!  Many of the items on the Regular menu are gluten free and they mark that right on it!  This means that the item was designed to be delicious and gluten free all at the same time, not GF if you take out all the flavorful things.  Items that can be made gluten free by request are also specially noted but they told me that these things cannot be guaranteed free from cross contact with gluten.  They actually went to the trouble of making me aware of this and noting this important difference on the menu!!!  When I asked about cross contact and kitchen practices they asked if we had celiac disease... they knew exactly what our needs are and took care of them without batting an eyelash, instructing us to simply notify our server that we were gluten free or had celiac disease and that our selections would be specially prepared to be safe for us.

To top it all off... Dessert!  Gluten free options went beyond the usual "raspberry or lemon sorbet" that one almost exclusively finds and delved into the uncharted territory of Gluten free chocolate hazelnut cake served with roasted date ice cream!  Our table ordered 4 different gluten free dessert options and enjoyed every one... not a sorbet among them (although they did have a tasty sounding stone-fruit sorbet on the menu).  

As if it couldn't get any better, they serve only in-season items and I believe they focus on organic as well, possibly local.  Not positive but I'm a big believer in "if it ain't tomato season, don't serve me an insipidly flavorless unripe monstrosity, I'll take my burger without, thankyouverymuch!".  

Pricy... yes.
Worth it for the gluten free eater or anyone who cares about quality ingredients: YES!
Staff: friendly, patient, helpful and knowledgeable

We will make the trek from San Jose to Gather, again.  It was a wonderful meal.

I have eaten here several times, and it's always great. Good service, pretty decor, relaxing dining room, great food. Some things we have ordered:

World's most amazing French Toast
Goat Cheese and Corn scramble
Vegan "Charcuterie" appetizer platter is so creative and delicious. 
Pizzas = perfect

Everything is good, but the vegan dishes are truly inspired, and they have lots of gluten free items. It's great to be able to go to dinner with my vegan friends and still have a  really good meal that can include a burger for me. Prices aren't cheap but the quality isn't either.

Not sure why everyone loves this restaurant so much.  I have been there a number of times and remain unimpressed beyond the charcuterie appetizer which is special.  It is expensive, many of the dishes are full of cheese or eggs, and I just can't get excited about the food tastes.

Came here with a few girlfriends on a Friday night. No reservations but we were able to snag a table pretty quickly. The space is open with some beautiful decor, a casual atmosphere but you could totally dress it up a bit too. 

We all loved the {PIZZA} It was the special for the day that had corn, pancetta and some amazingly fresh tasting heirloom tomatoes. Some of the other girls who were with me said it might have been their favorite pizza they've had in SF!

We also ordered the {VEGAN CHARCUTERIE} a plate they have been noted for, but I think it fell short of our expectations and while it wasn't bad it wasn't something we would order again.  Another one of my favorite dishes was the {GREEN BEANS} mixed with some bacon and it was wonderfully combined.

Tonight was my second or third time at Gather.  My buddy and I split  the Vegan Charcuterie, King Salmon, the Tar Tar, and the chocolate hazelnut cake.  The taste was pleasantly surprising on all counts.  

By the typical "American" serving size, I think the serving size at Gather are on the small side.  By Texan standards, they are tiny.  So I think that Gather is being courageous.  In this this time of "more is better" and so many overweight people walking around, the serving sizes were perfect.  I felt satisfied.  

I think with that food and four glasses of wine, the total was about $100.

So, just looking over my review list, it looks like I give out a lot of 5-star ratings but that's because I tend to review places I really like. I think they deserve the referral and the business - and it is no different with my review of Gather. I went here for dinner with my husband; his co-worker made the reservation. I admit I had reservations dining at a vegan and gluten-free restaurant (the images that came to mind were not pleasant - hay, anyone? =P), but after reading the Yelp reviews, I was encouraged. 

All the reviews about unique and surprising ingredients and the amazing flavors in the dishes are SPOT ON! It seems like Gather's menus change with what ingredients are available because the salad that we ordered is not listed on their website menu. I don't recall the name, but it was something-Turnip Tops with chicken liver. It was delicious and chock full of flavor.. I don't even know how to describe it. For our main dish, we had the cauliflower pizza (recommended by a fellow Yelper) and I'm still thinking about it - a week later. It was an exquisite thin-crust pizza; the crust was crispy (not soggy) and tasted of warm baked bread. For dessert, we had the apple crisp, which I thought was okay - it was too sweet for my taste but my husband thoroughly enjoyed it.

It was really busy when we went (dinner on Feb. 13). I don't know if it was just that night or not, but I would recommend reservations. We had wine with our dinner so I didn't order anything off the drinks list, although it did look interesting. I can't wait to go back!

I'm guilty for not ordering a vegetarian dish. I ended up getting the ham sandwich instead, but it certainly is not as bland as it sounds! It includes bacon, Wagon Wheel, lemon verbena-charred jalapeno aioli, pickle mustard, and Little Gems. It was so good! Don't let its small size deceive you! It goes well with jasmine milk tea and sparkling water. 

Venue: very earthy. Great for groups! The waiters were very accommodating as well. 

Location: accessible by Bart and bus.

I'll preface the review by saying that, though we had inexcusably bad service, the manager eventually noticed without our prompting and comped wine and part of the entrees. 

That said - our service was inexcusably bad. I have only once ever sent something back in a restaurant, and it was because of the hair in my food here. After that, it took our server close to an hour to bring out entrees; the couple next to us had finished dessert and paid by the time we finally got them.

The food itself was just OK - don't see what the raves are about. The beet salad I had was good, but the guinea hen entree (special) was underwhelming.

It was a third time at Gather and I'm amazed at how they manage to maintain the quality while keeping the menu constantly updated. 

I like how they have options for meat eaters and delicious vegetarian options as well. 

We had a table of 11 people so we could try just about everything on the menu. Everything was fantastic but here a few highlights. On the appetizers side the smoked mussels was a standout. Pizza wise, the kim chi pie was unique and to do for. I don't recall the name of the ice cream, but it was truly divine.

I can't wait to hit Gather again.

Met up here tonight with a few friends.  We were seated on the heated patio, which was very nice.  I rarely eat beef, choosing to be very particular about where it comes from, so I decided that this was a good place to get a hamburger as the beef is local and pastured (ask to see the source book!).  The burger was delicious, cooked perfectly medium rare.  The accoutrements were also very tasty, though the bun was somewhat plain.  The shoestring fries were very good, even if some of them were too short and seemed more like crumbs, and this is coming from a girl who prefers steak-cut fries.  My friends said their entrees were also delicious.  One thing that sort of irked us was that certain items are labeled as "gluten free upon request."  One of my friends doesn't eat gluten, and ordered the chicken which came with this label.  He asked how it was converted into gluten free, and the server said that the panzanella in the side was simply eliminated.  Not replaced with any other sort of carb, just left off.  But he requested fries instead and they were brought at no additional charge.  We shared the peach crisp for dessert and it was delicious!  I would definitely go back, I really want to try the eggplant lasagna, and the pizzas our neighbors were getting looked divine (and huge)!

So I've been to Gather more like 10 times now, but haven't written a review - shame on me!
I love this place! Not only because I know the products are mostly local, and organic, and of the best quality...I go back because the food is good, period.
I've tried a few different pizzas but my favorites are the Brunch Pizza (sooo good with that egg and caramelized onions), the Pancetta Pizza (again with those caramelized onions and the crispy pancetta). The crust is chewy and bubbled up from being in that hot oven, so good. You cannot go wrong with the pizza.
We've tried other things too..vegan charcuterie (pretty and interesting flavor combos!), the burger (perfect), french toast for breakfast (just delicious), beluga lentils with a poached egg on top (tasty and filling) and more...basically everything I've had there, I've liked.
I'd recommend this place to anyone, the health conscious, the vegetarian, the meat eating pizza lovers, basically everybody.
We will be back for sure, breakfast, lunch or dinner, all are good.

Mostly vegan and gluten free food... ehhhhh.

I'm not too much of a health freak, so the food here was kinda different from what I'm used to eating.  The boyfriend and I ordered the Sibley Pike's Peak squash tofu and a Nettle pizza to share.  The squash tofu dish was served cold, and the tofu was an orange-ish color. There was also some thinly sliced vegetables on the side, I think. The tofu was pretty good, but portion is just really tiny.  The pizza had German Butterball potatoes, goat cheese, rosemary, and leek (or so the menu says), but I don't think I really noticed the potatoes on it.  Still, the pizza was alright.

I don't think the place was all that great, but I'm glad I tried it because I've always walked by it and wondered how the food was. Probably..... won't come back though. :(

I had high expectations coming to this restaurant.  Right off the bat I found the menu limited for omnivores and quite abundant for those of the vegetarian persuasion.  Since I enjoy meat my selections were limited.  Both burrata and apple salad appetizers we had were pretty good.  The sausage pizza was the best I've had.  They make their own sausage which has a little more spice than usual but is still tolerable.   My main entree was the salmon which was perfect.  I really wanted a wider selection of meat entrees though.......and I didn't want to partake of the half chicken available.  The server was quite helpful.

They use good ingredients here.  Didn't think though it was representative of four stars though

3 1/2 stars..

I am ADDICTED to the Lacinato kale salad! I haven't seen any restaurants offering kale salads before and it is a dish I haven't tried making on my own. This is the only thing I get at this restaurant but the other items look great as well. I leave this place feeling like I've eaten something really healthy, as everything is organic and local. Can be crowded (& slow) at lunch so try to get there before noon or after 1:00 p.m.

The food here was exceptional!

Every dish was light and delicious. So many flavors and textures that were present in each bite.

There were 2 vegetarians, 1 vegan and 1 omnivore at this dinner.

We ordered:
-- Vegan "Charcuterie" -- Definitely recommend this. They give a piece of paper that describes each dish on there so you know what you are eating. Everything was so delicious and rich without being heavy.
-- Sheep's milk ricotta pizza -- This was also good and fresh. The ricotta cheese melts in your mouth.
-- Pumpkin soup -- I was told it was delicious. (vegetarians had this).
-- Cannelli Beans Black Trumpet Mushroom -- I was told this was amazing. (the vegan had this).
-- "Chicken Fried" Squash -- So amazing. I being the omnivore, read other reviews, and eyes set on this dish. Everyone that said this dish rocked was right on. I can't stop talking about how amazing this dish was. The fried squash with the mashed leeks (or whatever) and hen sauce was such a good mixture of texture and flavors. The fried part was lightly done. I was actually a little concerned that it was going to be heavy with it being fried and all. I am not a fan of fried foods, but this dish had a good amount of friedness which was easier to enjoy.

I would definitely come back here, and bring more friends to try the food.

Gather asked for help keeping their rating high so here I am because they have helped me so much
.
.
.
.
with one of the best hamburgers I have ever stuffed in my craw.

Seriously, I have dreams about the Gather burger.

I love this place. 

Everything else has been solid too. 

Gather's strength is letting the natural flavors of food come through the preparation. If your palate is accustomed to butter, cream, high heat and salt used by most restaurants, this is not the place for you -- but if you want to taste the essence of your pea shoots, come on in.

Gather is aptly named because it's the kind of place where the meal is the event, it has a bit of a European tenor in that regard -- service is luxurious and not rushed.

Finally, special shout out for the friendly, but not unctuous demeanor of the staff. One night in particular stands out  when four of the seven of us were late during prime time hours. There was no grief about seating an incomplete party, even before they realized we'd be ordering $100 worth of cocktails (which, also, are awesome).

Extra credit: the hostesses have great style. I've been known to rock more than one look cribbed from them.

I really enjoyed my experience here.

Went with two friends on a Friday night around 6 PM. Wait was 45 min so we went elsewhere until a table was ready. Thankfully we had friends to visit in the area so it wasn't too bad. 

I love the decor and the interior. We could've sat outside with no wait, but it was a little too cold out, and it didn't have the same vibe we were looking for. The inside is upscale but cozy at the same time. I thought putting the water in milk bottles was a nice touch and it's also nice that they don't charge extra for sparkling water. I ordered the kambucha and it was delicious. It's an acquired taste but I think it's great. 

Everything we ate was very fresh. Both pizzas I tried were great - the one garnished with olives was delicious and the tomato sauce was acidic and just fantastic. I loved the pizza dough too. I ordered the burger and it was cooked perfectly. The aioli on the burger was SO good and the onions and lettuce too. The salad that went with the meal was good -- the dressing a little too acidic and tart, though. The fries were great - perfect amount of crisp and once again, very fresh.

We split a blood orange sorbet for desert. I loved it. The piece of blood orange served with it topped it off. 

This is a great place to celebrate, definitely worth the price and the wait. I would suggest reservations on weekends, just to be safe.
About the Wine list at Gather...it could use some improvement in terms of adding organically grown wines to the list.

The food was really good, with some preparations that I've not seen before and I was rather impressed with the flavor combinations. The reservation was for 5:30, the restaurant was fairly empty yet we were seated next to an occupied table. I'm not particularly crazy about sitting next to the front door, especially in a empty restaurant (or when the windows & doors are open for the patchouli to waft in). The waitstaff were good - knowledgeable and communicative, not always immediately attentive, yet not painfully so. 
Overall a good experience, and I would definitely come back again.

I really wanted to like Gather as I have been hearing so many good things about it, see that its often packed when I drive by, and love the idea that they offer gourmet vegan and vegetarian food selections (but they also have sustainable meat options).  I went this past Saturday night with my wife and another couple that was visiting from out of town.  We had reservations at 9pm but arrived about 15 minutes early.  Fortunately, the host was able to seat us early although the table was not a good location (by the main entrance and I had my back to it (this kind of position makes me a bit unrelaxed).  The menu options looked pretty good, but the one thing I couldn't get over were the prices.  The price of everything seemed very high.  Having lived in SF for 5 years, I've been to a number of fine food establishments in SF that had equivalent food at prices which were considerably less.  

I ordered the Fontinella pizza which is basically like a Margherita pizza and it was $16.  Not overly expensive, but expensive for what it was.  When I lived in SF, I frequented a vegetarian restaurant called Source whose prices were much lower with more of a commitment to high quality ingredients and being strictly vegetarian.  I'm sure I'll hit up Gather again at some point (mostly because there isn't much as far as nice ambience restaurants in town for a vegetarian) but with the high prices I won't be a regular.

My experience with Gather so far is maddening, so it rates a 0.  They have the most retarded reservation system I have ever known...totally abusive.
I started on Thursday for a reservation for Sunday (Father's Day).  After 4 phone calls over 3 days, they tell me they will honor my date and time, but I have to call back EXACTLY  24 hours before the reservation in order to hold it.  So I was traveling and ended up calling late...so no reservation.  Are there any other hoops I can jump through for you.  It's now the night before Father's Day and no reservation.  I am invited to come put my name in and TRY for a table.  Sure I'm going to haul an old man down there to stand on the sidewalk and stand there for how long?
I don't think so!!

Almost didn't eat here.The menu on the window didn't look like anything special, but it was late and hubby and I were hungry and the place was packed.  What I want to know is this: How the hell did they get kale to taste that damn good? It's kale, for heaven's sake. And, what the hell is up with that gazpacho my husband ordere? I've never cared for gazpacho before. But Gather made it taste like something out of this world. I had the vegan appetizer. How was it? There are no words other than fantastic!  I'm determined to try everything on the menu. Service: excellent. Food: incredible.

Wonderful experience all the way around
great menu excellent service and presentation
nice to be able to please my dedicated veg husband who found so many good things on the menu he was delighted. We enjoyed our meal and returned again with friend who was blown away. Great place to enjoy meal anytime or special occasion. This makes the Brower Center complete. Bravo!

I wanted to love this place. Here is my debrief based on two visits:
+Great pizza. I especially liked it with a farm egg on top. 
+Pretty good kale salad and tofu skin special. 
+Lovely interior design. 
-Terrible service. The hostess was rude to us and our server was a straight a**hole during our meal. (One example: Rolled his eyes when I asked if the hot chocolate was milk chocolate or dark chocolate and snarkily responded "Yeah, there is milk in it so it's milk chocolate." Really? ) 
-Vegan charcuterie... while we were glad we ordered it because it was so interesting, it wasn't exactly tasty.

What a great new addition to Berkeley.  I've been three times now and each experience has great -- great food, great service, great atmosphere.  Our best experiences have been a casual meal at the bar.  The bartender was well-versed on the menu and full of opinions.  He steered us right with all his recommendations.  Loved the kale salad, pizza, hot toddy (thanks to the bartender for recommending this over a glass of wine when I was fighting a cold).  An excellent spot.  Keep up the good work.

Nit-Picking.  First a suggestion to diabetics (and others).  I asked for Splenda for  coffee, and was told, a bit uncomfortably, that many people ask for it and it continues to be  under discussion but for now it is not available because it is not natural. I was not offered sugar as a substitute so I'm not sure if that's available either.   They served me iced tea without a lemon (and no sweetener of any kind on the table). I was busy catching up with friends so I drank the iced tea without a sweetener (before I knew of the no-Splenda policy).
