Is there something I don't know about lemon that might make it unacceptable?   And there was no salt or pepper on the table.  There were four of us sharing two desserts.  The two desserts were put in the middle of the table for us to share but without separate plates for us and I didn't much like the idea of  double dipping into the desserts so I only had one bite of each.  So next time I'll be prepared with Splenda and perhaps lemon slices in my purse. I grew up in a family restaurant  where I learned that little things mean a lot to customers.

All that said I did like the burger and fries but the menu is not 50-50 so my choices were limited. My friends all liked their choices which included fig pizza and squid and the ambience was good and the whole place was very attractive.  Next time I'll try brunch.

I had high hopes for Gather. I like their look and feel, their menu sounds delicious and sustainable but the food is ok, the service is ok. I had dinner there and everything was ok. The vegan "chacuterie" was recommeded by our waiter and it was the best item we ordered but just ok.

If this is what it means to gather, then I think I'd rather hunt. 

(nyuk nyuk nyuk)

Ok, seriously though. We came here at 8 pm on a Tuesday night. The place was packed but luckily we were seated quickly. However, it took forever for our server to even notice us. We were starving and asked for some bread, and it took the waiter about 20 minutes to bring it to us. I later found out they charged us for the bread (what? who does that?). We ordered the wild arugula salad with strawberries (yummy), the duck sausage pizza (very very good) and the gnocchi (tasted kind of like it could have been a frozen entree from Trader Joe's). So I'd say overall the food was GOOD, not great, but the service left much to be desired. Also, not gonna lie, the place is a bit pretentious. It made me miss my regular restaurant of choice, Corso.

I've been here twice-once on a date with a vegan who said goodnight by giving me a high-five and once with my vegan mother before we went to Berkeley Rep to see a play.

The food both times was fantastic! If you think that vegan food is boring, than you need to try the vegan selections at Gather. Try the pizzas and the vegan charcuterie plate-but I'm sure everything is delicious.

They have a great alcohol selection too!

The one star down is because it got super super busy when I was there with my mom and our waitress disappeared for so long we had to hunt her down to pay the check so we could get to the theatre on time.

I'm always up for an artisanal, seasonal, localized, regional food experience, and have enjoyed such at several Bay Area restaurants. Gather had great potential on first sight: beautiful building, attractive, though uncomfortable, furnishings, open kitchen, great restrooms, and highly recommended by a friend. But even though I had looked at the menu on-line, the list itself that night seemed complicated to decipher. There were ingredients that made no sense to me (and I'm not averse to magical realism). Corn smut? Stinging nettles? Hedgehog? That's all fun, but if I have to ask the server what everything is, then it becomes no fun.

My friend had told me the Sole was fantastic, but it wasn't on the menu. So she asked if they had any left and the answer came back affirmative. My dum - I didn't ask how it was served (whole, head and all), or the price ($30!). It was smothered in delicious yardwaste - fennel, and some other thinly sliced vegetable. The server INSISTED on bringing it to the table whole, rather than deboning and de-heading first, so then I requested that they take him (the fish) back to the kitchen and return with the edible parts. Whole or dissected, it was just too much mess on the plate, and the sole was bland. With hope, comes disappointment.

My cocktail, though, a Moscow Mule was dee-licious. My companions reported that the hamburger was quite good, and the half a chicken was just chicken. If I go back, I will order the hamburger or the much touted Spicy Tomato Pizza, served at the table to our right. 

It was a Saturday night, so we came quite early, 5:00 and by 7:00 it was Packed! and Noisy! Not my idea of a good time. But hey, it all only came to $160  (note sarcasm) and included 3 lovely golden wheat beers.

Eureka! Cozy, scrumptious little vegan-friendly date spot! The food is fun, fancy, flavor-filled and has many secret prizes that will delight your pants off. Prepare to be seriously well-fed and pantsless.

YUM, YUM, YUM!!!!!  --is pretty much the only way to describe Gather. It's been on my "To Try" list ever since it was featured in Esquire magazine some years back and I finallllly was able to visit. The space is nicely decorated and welcoming and provides an open view into the kitchen (which is super clean, by the way). The ingredients are fresh and local which help make the genius menu taste great. 

We had the summer vegetable hash and the farm egg pizza - both amazing. The summer vegetable hash was complex yet simple in taste. The pizza just simply good. I would easily order both items again...except that I'd just love to try more of their menu items. The service was attentive and allowed for sharing of dishes. We not only enjoyed our food, but the housemade soda and fresh squeezed orange juice were delicious.

There are places you kind of just visit to try out - Gather is not one of those places. Gather is a place to revisit, many times over - for its delicious fare 
at affordable prices and casual ambiance.

Don't waste time by circling around the block to look for parking -- there is parking underneath the building with entry via Kittredge for less than $4 every two hours. Another plus? Reservations accepted via OpenTable. I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

The design is beautiful, but the food is still the best!  The chef is Sean Baker, who was sous chef at Millennium before cooking at Google and a few restos in Santa Cruz.

The ingredients are so simple but the combinations of flavors end up a delicious party in your mouth.  Woop!  Plenty for vegetarians or meat-lovers.

Favorite was the sardine 'bruschetta' where the sardines are definitely there, but perfectly balanced taste and texture-wise with the creamy base on the grilled bread, jalapeno mint puree and crispy fried brussels sprout leaves on top, and marinated egg yolk on the side that pops so you can smear each tasty bite in it.

Castelfranco salad w/ pistachios, mandarins, and grated aged jack(?) was amazing bitter, nutty, sweet, salty, crunchy.

Cinnamon-braised lamb small plate falls apart w/ a fork, and served w/ chicories, apples, and yogurt.

Vegan charcuterie platter was a big, filling plate, wow.  A vegetarian dish from heaven, altho being an omnivore, I would have liked to eat more of the other dishes vs all veggies, but it was still good and very unique.

Actually, our neighbor shared some pizza - awesome chewy crust. Romanesco, rapini, lemon and goat cheese.  Salty and satisfying for our 'dessert'.

Stopped by their food truck at Jack London, and thought it would be worth checking out the restaurant after encouragement by the wife.  Service was great, and the dishes are well thought out and creative.  I'm an idiot for not remembering the name of the strawberry dish (it's in the collection of photos here), but definitely give it a try.

I was disappointed with their carrot dish (again sorry I forgot the name), which when you consider the ingredients, is overpriced and not a great main plate.

Three of us split 2 main dishes, a salad, appetizer, and bottle of white.  Solid dining experience worthy of a return visit next time Berkeley is on the agenda.

Gather is a great addition to the Berkeley food scene. I have had lunch there several times and have never been disappointed. The kale with garlic and egg is great combined with pizza or a sandwich. The staff is knowledgable and almost everything is organic and fresh. Ths noise level is medium, so it's possible to have a lunch meeting, unlike other restaurants nearby that are just too loud for a meeting.

My daughter and I had dinner before a show at Berkeley Rep.  Snooty is a good description of the exchange on the phone, when I made a reservation..  I should have nixed it right there.  We started with the Vegan Charcuterie, tasty but would not order again.  Then a pasta special we wanted to share.  We were told it was a small portion, $13.00.  We paid a dollar for each tiny Lilly shaped pasta.  It was great but we felt taken.  Then came the pizza and a polenta vegetable dish.  Three tablespoons of polenta does not make an entree dish exceptable. This place is highly overrated and should you choose to go, you will be taken for the minuscule portions with high prices.

Just didn't feel it. I'm a meat eater, and I 'gather' that this place is geared toward vegetarians and vegans, but seriously, enough with the lemon and salt. There are more creative ways to make vegetables taste like an entire meal.

Any time I have guests in town I bring them here for dinner. The ingredients are everything at this place. Also... I love how they have Kombucha on tap!  It's one of those places you leave feeling a little healthier.

Gather- despite the crowds is one of my favorite local eateries, when you can score 2+ hrs for dinner and a movie.  I thought it a vegan veggie dining place however,
We shared their signature veggie platter- which was 5 star, and a Niman Ranch cheese burger, Yup range free, organic beef, which was also 5 star, and tasted like NO OTHER burger I have ever had in a resturant, the combo was fabulous, and dining at the counter watching the meals artistically & meticulously prepared was worth it.

Gather! A nice classy restaurant in West Berkeley. This is a nice place for a nice occasion. I've been here twice while I was in Berkeley and thought it was good, but it's pretty pricey.. so I'm not sure if I would come here that often.

Now onto the review! My first trip here was with my girlfriend on her birthday, we started off with a meatball appetizer, it cost almost 10 dollars, but we gave it a shot. So 20 mins later, the meatball starter came, and I was like T_____T Soooo small.. They were smaller than those gum balls you get in those quarter machines! And plus there were only like 5 meatballs.. 2 dollars for a meatball haha.. I was thinking..never again.. These must be some amazing meatballs in order to cost 2 dollars each.. The meatball themselves were pretty good in my opinion. My girlfriend thought it was good too, and she's a meatball person, so she can tell whether a meatball is good or not. I personally would not ever order it again..unless I was extremely rich.. but it was a nice.. 

Now onto our main entrees, we both ordered the Prather Ranch Burger, it comes with Sierra Nevada cheddar, aioli, and fries. We both cooked it medium, and it tasted really good. I like burgers especially when they juice comes gushing out of your mouth, which this burger totally does! The burger cost 15 bucks, but it was a much better deal compared to the meatballs.. but I would go back for their burger. Forgot to add, the fries were pretty good as well, not as good as the old burger king fries before they changed it.. but still good. 

Dinner (3.5/5)

My second trip was a weekend brunch with my girlfriend. We both wanted to try their French Toast, but only she ended up choosing the french toast, I got this corn pizza, which was delicious! It really reminds me of the Cheeseboard Corn Pizza..which is mouth watering AMAZING!! Go try it if you haven't. Yea anyways, the Corn pizza at Gather, was really good. It's not as oily as Cheeseboard, which is a good thing when you consider your health, but it taste just as good. It's different, but in a good way. The pizza bread part taste like naan!! I love naan, so that was a pleasure to find. I could just eat the pizza and then save the crust for later and dip it in some Paneer Tikki Masala from Mt. Everest Restaurant. My girlfriend's french toast was good as well. I didn't really like the prunes and grapes they put over it, but the bread with syrup was goood. Especially the bread. I believe they get their bread from Acme, which is delicious.

Brunch (4/5)
This is a long review..I'll wrap it up now. This is a pretty good place. It's definitely on the more expensive side, but I would try their pizzas and burgers. Definitely check this place out.

Roasted beet salad with chicken was a great lunch.
Service was better than last visit.

Gather is a good place for a special occasion. It is a bit expensive for a casual meal, and the menu is sometime esoteric. I have had breakfast there twice, and was glad I had a reservation because the place was packed. OTOH, I dropped by with a friend for a mid-week lunch a couple of weeks ago and we had no trouble finding a table outside. I suggest looking for slightly off hours if you don't have a reservation. I haven't tried it for dinner yet because it s pricey, but will probably book it the next time we want something special.

Burrata $12
Garghinelli $13
Herb Sausage $13
Sweet Potato Soup $8?
Vegan Charcuterie $16
Spicy Tomato Pizza $16
Hen of the Woods Pizza $17
Goat Milk Semifreddo $6.50
Chocolate Crema $9

We had a truly delicious meal here! Atmosphere was nice, cozy yet very spacious. Decor was modern, mostly filled with reclaimed wood and glass pieces. Noise level was medium, but then again, we weren't the most quiet party here!

Since there were too many things on the menu that we wanted to try, we just picked everything that sounded good. Because of the seasonal ingredients, the menu changes often, so check on the website to get an idea of what's currently being served and ask for the specials, should they not tell you.

All the dishes were distinctively flavourful, although they varied highly in sizes and portions (soup was very generous, white the garghinelli was much smaller). The pizzas are best shared by two people with the addition of an appetizer, as they were on the large side for a single person, but wouldn't be filing enough for two. Really enjoyed the Spicy
Tomato one, as it had a bite that would go away in seconds. 

What I really liked about Gather was the service.. it was just the right amount
of attentiveness without us feeling smothered. All wait staff was courteous and friendly.
Plates were changed seamlessly, water never ran out, and we never had to wait for anything.
I would definitely go back, and this is just based on my experience only. 
I'm not sure why there are people complaining about the hipster vibe, or its bland dishes,
but I had a really positive experience on all counts.

A bit absurd. Trying to be high-end cuisine. However, it was good. We all shared and had a good time. 

The Vegan Charcuterie was fun. The specials were all quite good. The veggie sides were excellent. 

The choc hazelnut cake was good. 

The creme caramel was not very good. Tasted too planty. Perhaps they were trying too hard. Definitely on the whole took themselves too seriously, but it was good. Service was fine.

We had dinner last night and the cherry gazpacho was one of the most delicious and most
creative things we've ever eaten! The pizza was great great great! The goat was fab fab fab fabulous!!!
The salmon was scrumptious! The vegan charcuterie was yummie as always! What wasn't good? 
That we were full and had to leave.... Love this restaurant!!!

My third trip to Gather. Second time for dinner. Good food. Questionable service.

Apologetically arrived 8 minutes late for our 6PM reservation. Parking sucks. Were given the option of outside or in. Though it was a nice evening, the patio lacked luster, so we both wanted in. There were a ton of empty 2-tops in/around the main part of the restaurant (it was early on a Sunday eve), but the host directed us to a table alongside a partial wall by the bar with a direct view into the wait station. I gestured toward the center of the restaurant and asked if we might be able to sit elsewhere. He obliged, but basically plopped the menus down on a table and walked away without a word. Maybe we were being punished for being late and then being "picky"? Shame on us! 

The sardine appetizer was yummy. We shared a Fontinella pizza with 2 farm eggs, which was also good - esp. the crust and the eggs on top - though we both ended up adding salt to bring out some flavor. We had three different cocktails. They were all pretty good. 

Service started out great and then diminished. Our server was a young, tall, curly-headed guy. Cheery, helpful, maintained steady eye-contact, steered us toward particular cocktails... brought things quickly, checked on us... but somewhere along the way we must have irritated him. That much was clear. Was it joking that we liked the "jam on toast" cocktail he recommended, but found it reminiscent of shower gel? Was it asking for salt? Maybe it was saying we'd take a look at the desserts although we probably wouldn't have anything more and wanted to sit a bit longer and chat. When he came back, maybe it was saying we hadn't yet taken a look. Regardless, the eye-contact was nil, the smiles were gone, and there was a general undertone of irritation. Check was put on the table without any personal acknowledgement... maybe a "thanks" under his breath after he'd already turned away. Basically, it seemed like he wanted us to get the hell out to free up the table unless we planned to order more (It was 7:30). Irritated or not, professional service doesn't show it. 

 ~$65 incl. tip. I'm not in a hurry to go back.
They've worked out the kinks. The restaurant is in full swing. The food is incredible. Something to please every diet. Including one helluva burger.
The mushroom pizza is to die for.  So freakin' good!  Really nice, friendly service.  Thumbs way up!

Went there on a Friday night.  Had open table reservations, but still had to wait 15 minutes.  Place is warm.  Inviting.  Great concept.  Great idealism.  Sad to say food is just so-so.  The four of us shared everything as follows.  The fried mushroom could have been fried cardboard.  They were so overfried as to be unable to taste any mushroom.  (This also pertains to the french fries too.)  The veg charcuterie was inventive, but pricey at little veggies for $14.  We had two pizzas both chewy and tasty.  The salad was crisp and plentiful.  Desserts were pretty average.  Overall a great place for beer salad and pizza.  The other stuff, eh.

Gather makes me want to eat more veggies. If you're a vegetarian or vegan, this place would be quite a treat. Gather takes pride in their greens and they also promote locally grown sources. With that, you're going to pay a bit more, but I think it's worth it. 

I went there for my girlfriend's birthday and I have been meaning to try it since I read about the restaurant from Esquire Magazine. They held chef Baker to be quite a rising star and Berkeley's next to my home town so I had to make a visit. Here's the thing though, finding parking in Berkeley is a big problem. You're safer taking BART or bus, but parking is just horrible at the evenings on weekends. Hopefully you reserved time for this. We didn't and circled around for quite a while. 

Gather is definitely a place where people, well, gather. It's a restaurant on the corner and attracts a lot of attention with its huge bay windows. Actually a few times we had visitors peering into our table (I'm glad I didn't have food in my mouth). They were friendly though. It's louder than the photos people post suggest, so be prepared for that kind of ambiance. People and music echo throughout, but it made it a bit festive though. 

We ordered three items between the two of us: the pickled strawberries, the pizza special, and the barbecue chicken. I also tried the ginger beer, which was the best I've had. The strawberries dish won the prize for appearances, but the thin-crusted pizza won it for taste. It was a medium sized pizza topped with asparagus, jalapenos, and corn. Somehow it was of perfect balance. Our final entree of BBQ chicken (young) and it didn't disappoint neither. It was juicy with a great seasoned skin. I was stuffed after the meal, but of course we ordered a dessert. We vouched for the kumquat tart. The ice-cream on the side refreshed us from the hearty meal. 

Almost five stars, but it's getting there.

Want to prove to your meat-loving friends that vegan food can be absolutely delicious - without leaving them feeling like something is missing with the dish? Try the vegan charcuterie. Hands down the best vegetarian or vegan dish I've ever had.

Took my vegetarian niece here for dinner,along with three carnivores.  Most of us ended up ordering vegetarian meals.  Not because that was the only choice, but because it looked so darn good!  We had two kinds of pizza, artichoke on black rice, and roasted chicken.  Everything tasted as good as it looked!

We also had an appetizer sampler on a wooden plank and it was exquisitely presented.  I didn't know half of what I was eating,but who cared?

We finished with a variety of desserts which were heartily sampled by everyone. 

The service was warm and friendly, with just the right amount of information about each dish.

I would definitely go back to this place, with or without my vegetarian niece!

I've been to Gather once for lunch and another time for the bar.  I can't recall the finer details but I do know I dig their laid back atmosphere, the earth-y decor.  As for the lunch experience, the server was super friendly, though very soft spoken.  Their food was excellent!   Overall a good place to dine.
Yum. The burger was one of the best we've had and the Fontinella pizza was also quite good. Service was friendly and attentive. If we lived closer we'd be regulars.

I keep trying to like Gather but it's harder and harder the more I go there... and recent meal there is my last.  The wait staff is smug and inept... reaching across customers constantly and not showing up for long periods of time.  The food is occasionally very good but at least half of it is very oily and lacking in flavor.  It's not inexpensive.  The most annoying quality is their refusal to reserve a table at a reasonable time for six people.... it's 5:15 or after 8:00.... and I find this greedy and rigid of them.
No more.

Had an excellent experience when trying this place for the first time a few nights ago for my wife's birthday. The staff were friendly, efficient but not all over us, and everything we ate was delicious. The atmosphere was very inviting too. 
The salad we shared was incredible, and I have to say the hamburger I had was one of the best ones in recent memories without a doubt. My wife had the gnocchi, which was also quite good but maybe not as amazing as the burger. 
Noticed some fantastic-looking pizzas being served too, which I will probably try next time. We will definitely be back!

2 years after opening and this place keeps getting better all the time. Had THE BEST BRUNCH yesterday . Wonderful, comforting winter food. Pork terrine with mustard sauce - beautiful presentation and light, non greasy  flavors. Poached Eggs with pork belly and potatoes with a slightly spicy seasoning was better than any Eggs Benedict I've ever had. 

For dessert- I know this sounds weird- we ordered Pancakes with persimmon, pomegranate and whipped ricotta cheese.It was a regular brunch item but sounded soooo good. Glad we did.  Incredibly rich without a s_load of sugar. 2 of us shared 
and could only eat half. Totally worth it.

great place. I love love the Vegan charcuterie. The place is very stylish.
It's not cheap so if you are trying to eat for cheap - probably not the place for you.

Unless you order one dish and a beer - but that could be kind of wasting the experience

My husband and I both loved this place. If you go there, you should request for Erich to be your server. He was awesome. He took the time to explain the menu and answer all of our questions, even though it looked like he was slammed with tables. The food was amazing. We got the burger, split pea soup, and duck sausage pizza. All of it was so flavorful. The only bad thing was the lights from the Cal football stadium that came on after 8 pm. They flooded the whole restaurant and many diners were complaining that the lights were shining right into their eyes. It was shining right into mine, but after awhile I didn't even notice since I had all of that yummy food to distract me. I think they need to invest in some shades or curtains. We will definitely be going back.

Went here last week as it's my fave place in Berkeley. We decided to go vegetarian based on the streak I've been on. 

We wanted to lighter meal and started with the charcuterie which I usually love but this time it was... interesting. And you know what that means when something is either good, bad, or "interesting." The combos of seasonal produce didn't "hit" the incredible way they sometimes do. My friend and I were both surprised.

The pizza was good with seasonal veggies but light on pizzaz; it was almost bland. I know it's (veggie) pizza but at Gather I expect more. I've had made-at-home home veggie pizza in a regular oven, and you can make it very tasty with all kinds of topings, so my expectations were set.

Pluses for Gather that are consistent: atmosphere and good service. The wait staff are always very nice yet not overly attentive. And this time there was no wait!!
Awesome Bee Sting cocktail. Yummy kale salad...Very fresh foods. Would definitely come back.
Very comfortable outdoor seating but the food disappoints. Wine and food selections both limited. The setting has a lot of potential but the restaurant needs to work on its food and menu.

I've been twice now and would definitely go back.  Our first visit we had the vegan charcuterie and the chanterelle pizza.  Good LORD the pizza was the best I've ever had.  Seriously amazing.  Great crust and the combination of ingredients was spot on.  
Second visit was not as impressive.  We ordered the squid appetizer, burrata, and collard pizza.  Still good, but nothing compared to the chanterelle pizza.  Too bad it's not always chanterelle season...

I love the food, it had smokey and spicy flavor. I ordered pizza, it was really yummy haven't tasted smokey spicy pizza. 
 This place is good for vegan and for Veggie lovers.

Because the menu changes frequently...you just never know what you're going to get.  I will say that we went the Friday after Thanksgiving and that menu was UH-MAY-ZING...best meal we've had all year...great, great place if you get a great menu spread.

Great place to "Gather', oops! :) Okay best pizza! I had the potatoe, fennel and goat cheese, wonderful. A thin pizza crust, airy with layers showing with the goat cheese and thin slices of potatoe and just about the right amont of sea salt.  I say it's better than that pizza place on Telegraph across from Walgreens, that Margarita pizza was just bought tomatoe sauce. Gather is truelly a delight for non meat eaters, I will be going  back, I hope they continue to keep me happy.....Wish they had pasta....

AMAZING. DELECTABLE. DELICIOUS!!!!! the most AMAZING food i have EVER tasted! They make vegetables taste better than ANYTHING i have ever tasted!! it is hands down my favorite restaurant ever. Romaine salad (seasonal) is my FAVORITE!! the roasted chicken is amazing to.

This is my new favorite place to meet folks for lunch or dinner.  As a vegetarian, with carnivore friends, I sincerely appreciate a restaurant that focuses on delicious, creative food for both .  I highly recommend that you give this place a try.

We had an outstanding meal here last night. We were in a group of five, and we had made a reservation, so although it was packed, they seated us immediately. And despite a long line of walk-ins waiting, they did not rush us through the meal, which was nice. The staff was terrific, very friendly and knowledgeable, but gave us plenty of room to enjoy the meal. Our waiter kindly told us that we were ordering too much (because we wanted to try everything), but we did it anyway. He was right, but it was worth it. Everything we ate was terrific, but particular kudos for the vegan charcuterie, the duck sausage pizza, and the marinated burrata. All of the presentations were lovely, and the ingredient combinations were creative and delicious. The wine list is nice, with a few unusual choices. The pisco sour was also outstanding. If they can maintain this food quality, it will be a favorite for us. Great place for people with dietary restrictions, as gluten-free or vegan dishes are clearly marked on the menu.

I am in love with the idea behind Gather. 
The support for the local farming community and the idea of sustainable food is clearly showcased by the whole Gather team. It is reflected in every piece of this restaurant, from the wooden and concrete modern interior by Nicole Sillapore (http://www.sillapere.com/)  to the menu items developed by Sean Baker and his team.
Everything here is executed with great care and a deep appreciation for food. 

So with that being said, you will definitely find some combination you are not very familiar with, but hey be adventurous. For example their breakfast/brunch menu is a bit out of the ordinary but their polenta with fresh vegetables as well as the brunch pizza was to die for!
As far as dinner goes, I really recommend the vegan charcuterie plate It's nothing you will find somewhere else), the pizzas and the burger. 

The flavor and presentation is great and good for the price but nothing which truly knocks me off my socks. Two thumbs up for gluten free bread on the menu though!!!!
Service is ok, a bit slow at times.

I'll come back and try some other menu items and hopefully I will be able to up my rating.

The ambience lighting and just overall look of the restaurant is great... our waiter had a lot of tables to tend but was definitely making her way towards our table as much as she could. The mussels and squid legs are so good all the food is locally produced so you can definitly count on freshness and our food came pretty quick after we had ordered .Overall the service was really good for a Friday night.

Eh.
My husband and I spent $92 on dinner for 2 the other night, which included 3 drinks, a pizza, and a main dish (beef shoulder), plus tip and tax.  In no way did I think this dinner was worth that much money.  My husband's cocktail was decisively not good...just kind of flat and bitter and unexciting.  The pizza was good, but pizza, especially at $16/small pie is pretty easy...oily bread, cheese and good things on top.  The beef was the biggest disappointment....dry, tough, nothin' special...which at $24, is an issue.  The atmosphere was okay, but trying a bit hard to be the hip Berkeley "you can't afford Chez Panisse" varietal. Eh.
decent

I went to Gather for lunch, and I am impressed.  In fact, I'm daydreaming about my next opportunity to go.  

First, the ambiance is warm and welcoming.  It is an open space and while it seats quite a few people, it never seemed too noisy to carry on my own conversation.  

Second, and most importantly, the menu.  It is well-balanced between vegetarian/vegan and meat options.  What's more, I feel happy and satisfied ordering vegetarian fare at a restaurant that serves meat that comes from local sustainable family farms.  Any restaurant that makes available the lengthy list of local and sustainable producers that provide the fruits, vegetables, land and sea animals, and dairy with additional links to those producers' websites gets my vote and my dollar.

Which brings me to the possible only downside to Gather.  It is pricey, and this may be a deterrent for some.  But,  I believe that with today's animal industry one votes with one's dollar.  I had the Kale salad with chopped egg for lunch, and it was delicious.  The portion was the perfect amount and I was happily sated.  The salad was $12 with an additional $2 added for a chopped egg.  This may seem like a lot, but you are most assuredly getting more bang for your buck.  Also,  I am willing (and able) to spend $2 for an egg from a hen that is treated humanely and is allowed to live a natural life instead of one in a wire cage without any access to fresh air, grass, exercise or sunshine.  I am also happy to give my money to local farmers who are attempting to do something different and radical (maybe not for Berkeley or California) and who charge more for their products instead of externalizing costs to the environment, communities and animals themselves.    

I would highly recommend Gather for brunch or lunch, and I have every intention of going for dinner sometime soon.

I have been to Gather 3 times already, and there is no question that it's awesome.
I build furniture, so I pay attention to little details in finish. This place cut no corners. Really, 5 stars for design.
The staff is very helpful and nice, and the dining experience is excellent.
The fig, egg pancetta pizza is phenomenal. Better dough the Delfina, which inaccurately is assumed to be the best pizza in the bay area.
Only two gripes:
- the food is def expensive, making it hard to come here often.
 - the menu, while elegant, thoughtful and local, seems to lack depth, as I always find myself going to the same items, and I am not too picky.
However I need to check them out for dinner, see how the menu varies. I will leave my 5th star for the dinner visit.
Great job guys!
LOVE this place- amazing soft atmosphere, great decor!  Awesome service.  Loved the vegetarian platter, chicken was fantastic.  Great place.  Will definitely return

hip looking place but  food was far too oily....not worth $19 a plate...
drinks were mediocre and expensive .
we might give it a second try ,  the pizza looked good on almost every table...

You know ... I really like Gather and eat here regularly with friends. The cocktails are very creative, the salads are delightful and the whole pizza/small plates thing is pulled off in a way that doesn't feel trendy.

My advise to you CARNIVORES is DON'T PANIC. On our last visit my friend raved about the half chicken and his GF had what looked to be a perfectly prepared chop (one of that evening's specials). I had sole with lentils. Spot on.

My only complaint is the acoustics; man does it get noisy when it's crowded.

Came here for a wonderful lunch with my mom and sister. We split the fig and pancetta pizza, crisp yet also chewy crust topped with arugala, the kale dish (which also includes roasted parsnips and carrots), and the heirloom tomato, burrata and sliced artichoke heart salad.

Six-year-old nephew had sides of scrambled eggs and bacon. He picked up the bacon and gulped it down with a glazed expression on his face and then proclaimed "This is so good."  He also had fresh squeezed orange juice. Lucky kid!  Even luckier for us, he only had a few sips and then we fell upon it.

Restaurant is sunny and spacious, with vegetables on display on the kitchen counter instead of cuts of meat or fresh fish. Heard more than one person in the bathroom raving about the pine and sage liquid handsoap. That kind of place, with that kind of customers.
Tasty, organic, hip, relatively new, very California place. Pricey, but it has to be if it's going to be "hip."

Okay--my expectations were high. Local, organic, great chef, the Gather buzz was that it hit all those notes we prize here in Berkeley. The squid salad reflected those qualities, but oh my goodness, at what price? Well, 12 bucks for 3 slices of baby squid, 9 small white beans, 7 peas and a few lettuce leaves. I am not one to count the food on my plate--this was actually a first for me--but I found the situation rather striking. I also had to find something to do at my luncheon date, because, although I am a slow eater, this teensy amount of food did not lend itself to a leisurely eating experience. I am not a huge eater, and I get the less-is-more idea, but in this case I think the ratio got a little skewed. A lunch salad should not feel like an appetizer at the dinky side of the spectrum--especially at 12 bucks. Maybe some bread would help? Tried to fill the remaining time by ordering a cafe au lait. Got the sort of bewildered look one would expect ordering an espresso drink in a rural diner. Tried to explain how to make this drink to our kind but not especially skillful server. The coffee in the cappuccino I got was distinctly sub-par (time to clean the machine?). Bottom line: if I want local, organic great chef as well as a decent lunch, I shall gather elsewhere,
**Umm--editing--why is my May review appearing with March reviews? Does Gather pay to have bad recent reviews bumped down?
Good, well prepared, innovative food.

I went on a friday night with three girlfriends, and we got seated very quickly! The decor is beautiful and the tables are spaced out nicely, so you feel like you have space. It was the perfect amount of "fancy" so that you could dress up or dress down and still feel like it was a special evening.

First and most importantly, the pizza was to die for! I had their special that day, something with corn and pancetta and heirloom tomatoes. The pizza was the perfect moistness without being watery, the flavors melded together beautifully, and the crust was fluffy, light, and chewy. Everything I could ever ask for in a pizza! I would come back again just for this.

The rest of the dishes:
-vegan charcuterie was novel and interesting, but I probably wouldn't get it again.
-green beans with bacon appetizer is very tasty
-the "lobster meatballs" were also very tasty, but an unexpected texture for "meatballs".

All in all, it is a great place for a classy dinner with friends or family.

I was so excited to go here, one because the owners have other great restaurants and two because they had so many delicious vegan friendly options on their web menus. But when I got to the restaurant, the menu hardly had any vegan options! So I had potatoes. It was unfortunate. If you have any dietary restrictions, I would go elsewhere like Fellini or Herbivore for brunch.

Based on reviews, I expected this place to be pretentious and have a long wait, but experienced neither. We couldn't make a reservation but walked in and were seated within about 10 minutes (on a Friday around 7:15). Service was solid, attentive, and helpful. Four of us shared two delicious pizzas (spicy tomato and summer squash) and a hearty kale salad, which was just the right amount of food. To me, the pizza crust tasted authentic italian-- perfect balance of doughy and crispy. Bottom line: yummy, filling, yet not overly heavy food, with a good ambiance.

There are many unique things about Gather, but my favorite is that you can have a vegan and carnivore eat side by side without attitude.  So much in the foodie world get pretentious and exclusive, but Gather is not like that.  The staff was accommodating with my endless questions and the food was just delicious.  Cocktails were well balanced, not too sweet, which I personally dislike.

Faves: Kale salad, rumble seat cocktail & pisco punch, vegan pizza and vegan plate.  

I like the source book they have and the staff seems to know a lot about the sourcing.  You can go there and just eat and not worry about any of it, or you can get really involved with the process.  It's up to you.

Parking can be challenging.  Take BART, walk or ride if you can instead.

This is one of my favorite restaurants and I come here every chance I get.  They have a great selection of cocktails, but I always get the Bee Sting - it's the perfect combination of lemon, honey, and mint.  My friend loves their Corpes Reviver II.  For an appetizer my friends and I like to split one of their pizzas, and they are always good. For the main course I am tempted to try on of the many options but I always end up getting their Ranch Burger.  It is one of the tastiest burgers I've ever had, and is what keeps me coming back to Gather.

Wonderful!

I'm always an organic/local/sustainable kind of gal, especially one who likes to try vegan/vegetarian options just to see how talented the chefs are at making those typically-flavor-limited options very colourful to the palate.

And they definitely succeeded!
 
My boyfriend and I had the vegan charcuterie, which was a lot of fun to see just how creative the chefs were, and was definitely a hit! One of the samples had an almost bacon-like taste to it, so we were very pleasantly surprised! 
We also had one pizza, which was also scrumptious, esp. since the crust was so mochi-squishy/puffy and oh-so-good...

The wine list was also impressive, since their selection is all from local (or, CA) vineyards.

We didn't stick around for dessert, but... the dessert menu looked awesome! Have to go back!

The bad:
My wife's burger not cooked to order- well done and she asked for medium rare.  The drip coffee was terrible.  Not everyone drinks lattes and cappuccinos. Unexpected in a great coffee city.  I think they slum with tulley's.  As advertised they are a bit pricy but that is to be expected due to location and the want to be affluent cliental. 

The good: 
I will say that the food was excellent.  Had the hedgehog eggs and they were great. Plain yet the spices and cheeses blended well together with the eggs.  The potatoes were seasoned well and complemented the eggs.   Don't ask for catchup, it's a tomato montage (salsa). Would have been  nice to have been offered preserves with the gluten free bread( which was pretty good).

Maybe this is the place that will break the downtown Berkeley curse on good restaurants (We will try FIVE this weekend).

I liked Gather. The feeling is very Euro modern, noisy, busy, aluminum, glass and exposed heating ducts. The food is equally organic, though more Local Bay Area chic than Euro.

The room buzz is fun, all ages: from CAL frosh on their first date (really) to wizened gray haired professorial types in deep discussion.

The food is good, but not quite the Gourmet Organic Veggie Crunchy Granola mecca that some describe. The basic problem seems to be trying to get too many different flavors on a single plate: The halibut small-plate, the rice pudding and especially the veggie charcuterie all suffer from this. No that the flavors, or the dish as a whole, are bad, just that less would have been more.

The meatballs were good, but not as good as at Marzano (on College Ave.) Oh yes, the toast was burnt and also suffered from some kind of flavored oil rub (Rosemary?) that tasted more like the ozone smell after an electrical fire.

Service: Pleasant, friendly, and not very good. Long delays between courses were clearly recognized by the staff, but an outright apology was never forthcoming.

On the whole, in spite of the negative sounding comments above, we liked the place and will go back - it is a positive addition to the campus area.

I haven't been this impressed with a menu in such a long time. So creative and delicious!!

The vegan Charcurterie blew my mind and tastebuds and left me immediately saying I NEED to come back for this all of the time. The ingredients were so creative and everything came together to form such amazing tastes. And for only 16$! Pizza was great too. 

I want to go back often and try everything on the menu.

Some of the most innovative food I've ever tasted and all sustainably sourced from local producers and purveyors. Very approachable for all palates and pocket books. You must try the Vegan Charcouterie Platter and the wood fire pizzas.

Delicious food, kid friendly, reasonable prices for a special meal.
Vegetarian entrees are unusual and delicious and the breakfast pizzas are a tasty treat.

We had a potato / leek / goat cheese pizza (the "Nettle")and a stuffed cabbage dish. I also enjoyed a tall glass of Imperial IPA. The flavors were fantastic with an atmosphere to match. And at least for the vegetarian dishes, the prices are reasonable for that special night out.

I haven't tried them all, but in my opinion, this restaurant easily places in the Berkeley top 5.

Pros: healthy, local, flavorful food with accommodating and friendly staff.

Cons: so expensive! I know you get what you pay for, but it's more of a special-occasion place. Also, it's noisy and you can get stuck next to a table-full of loud talkers and have them hijack your evening. 

The vegan charcuterie was really great. I didn't like the corn-tomato polenta, which is strange because tomatoes and polenta are among my favorite foods, but the mushrooms (Summer Mushroom Pate) were transcendent. 

I've been there twice and both times the salads were very good. This time, the "Summer Salad" was excellent, with a really lovely Cabernet-dill vinaigrette and very fresh foods. Also, I am always a sucker for a perfect tomato. 

I can also recommend the homemade Ginger Beer = light tasting, but with a great real-ginger flavor.

oh man this place is so good. i do not usually order burgers but someone at my table did and i ended up eating most of it. deeeeelish!

and the kale salad is amazing- it's good for you kale, and it's done with this cheese that you don't expect to find served with kale like dishes, and it helps make the whole thing super yummy.

for dessert the chocolate creme rocked my world (someone at my table loved the chai creme brulee but i was too busy with my chocolate scoop of love that i didn't care).

Came here for lunch a couple of weeks ago with a few girl friends to celebrate the ending of school & to catch up on life.

When I arrived, the hostess was very nice in telling me that she could not seat me until my party was all there.  The restaurant was pretty busy @ the time but there were plenty of tables available so I didn't understand the point of making me wait in a chair.  Once we got seated, the service was good but slow; from sitting down to receiving food, it took about 35 minutes.

The 3 of us shared a Spicy Tomato Pizza, a Local Lettuces, & a Grilled Squid.  The  pizza had a very thing crust which was nice but it had pockets of dough that were burnt which was bad.  The olives and capers were fine even though I am not a fan of them in general.  What I really disliked was how spicy the pizza was.  I can eat pretty spicy (think 2 rounds of Sriracha in a bowl of pho) but this was bordering on unpalatable.  The Local Lettuces was light & bright but the grapefruit peel made it a tad bit bitter.  The Grilled Squid was not really a salad @ all.  It was 3 pieces of lettuce, 4 small pieces of quid, a handful of beans, & a handful of peas.  The lemon ash on the plate looked & tasted like...well, ash.

My overall experience was made good by the company I was with.  If I did not have that...given the quality of the food, the prices, & the level of service, it was not worth it.

Gather managed to redeem themselves in our book.  Just well enough to give an additional star (2 1/5 may be more appropriate).  Good enough that we will return again.  It will take more to turn it to a go-to restaurant. The food, meat charcuterie platter, vegi charcuterie platter, 2 pizzas, chicken under brick and especially the cod were GREAT. For dessert we ordered one each of the vanilla, pecan, salted chocolate and tangelo ice cream, the citrus rice pudding and chai creme brulee.  All stellar! The chef also sent out a ginger rhubarb granita.  The service went much better than in the last reviewed visit. And we didn't call back to make a special reservation with management (they invited).  We didn't want special service to make our final review.  On this last visit (8:30 dinner for 4) there was only one hiccup due to our server entering one of the entrees with the appetizers.  Not good.  But he caught it and brought it to our attention and my husband misunderstood and thought server meant he fixed it.  But it came after our second appetizer and before our other main dishes.  So his pizza was cooled before our food came.  Everything else went well enough for us to return again.  Though we can just as well go to Cesar, Rivoli or Wood Tavern instead and trust we will receive good food and good service.

Had the stinging nettle pizza with smoked mozzarella, rapini, and olive caper sauce. It's a pretty good pizza. The toppings aren't anything extraordinary tasting even though it may sound like it. They could've just used spinach and they would've fooled me. The pizza is a bit strange because it's a thin pizza with a very thick puffy crust. So if you're a thin pizza guy but love crust, this is your pizza. Thin, thin, thin, then chewy thick crust.

Their menu is constantly changing based on seasonal ingredients, which is great if all their dishes are appealing, but I've been wanting to try this place for a while and their menu didn't interest me that much, until...

...I saw their green garlic potato pizza and kale salad. Boy am I glad I had the honor of tasting such goodness. 

In a month, their menu will probably change again, and will have items I am not that interested in. Hit and miss, but this time it was a hit!

We were pleasantly surprised by this new spot!  It is a great find for us (me the omnivore and hubby pescatarian).  There is plenty for us both to choose from!

We started out with the vegan charcuterie plate.  It was really delightful!  We will be back for that again for sure.  I had some pork over polenta.  The pork was tender and tasty, I ate every last bit of it!  The polenta wasn't my favorite, not bad, just not great.  My husband had the fish of the day and LOVED it!  I tried some and it really was outstanding.  We shared some french fries that were good, but way over salted.  Next time I'll ask them to go light on the salt.We finished dinner with the chai creme brulee.  YUM!!  If you come here, order it!

Our waitress was polite, but somewhat clueless when we asked questions.  I'm sure this will get sorted out after they've been open for a little longer.

We'll be back again for sure.

WOW! WOW! WOW! Stunning flavors, exceptional creativity! 
The vegan charcuterie platter is a must-order -- and mind you, I am not vegan...(usually I am a salami princess). But no, this is so creatively done and fresh on the tongue, not to mention deep and rich in beauty and color.
The chicken dish was to die for. I was moaning with each bite. 
 
Love this new innovative place, where everything is locally sourced, of the utmost quality and even the bench along the wall is made of recycled leather belts! The atmosphere is exquisite, with vine-y plants growing all around and canning jars filled with beautiful preserved foods decorate the shelves on the walls! 

Anytime we find the extra dime, we're dining here! I have declared it!

Imm no so impressed as everyone else here. My friend and I both ordered the special appetizer, something with duck. It looked fabulous and if I could have hung it on my wall it would have been worth $14. But the taste was bland.

The pizza was burnt when it arrived. They were kind enough to take it back and give us a new one which was really good. 

Then our salted caramel brownie and ice-cream tasted like salt. only salt. They were kind enough to take that off the check.

The reason I give this place 3 stars if because the service was good. The manager came over after the pizza was sent back and apologize. Made sure we got a good one. She also took the dessert off of our check. So I would give it another chance. I think the prices are high for what you get but the pizza was really good. It was the one with pancetta.
Fun place to take your family to for a small celebration.  Love their burger and side dishes.  Staff is extremely friendly.  With so many cool places in the BAY, this one is definitely a re-do.

Beautiful space, awesome philosophy...quintessential berkeley/organic/local etc.

I'm so glad I came here.  The cocktails are great, the vegan charcuterie plate is creative!  Although I did think many of the plate items were sweeter than savory.  Much of the menu is seasonal and changes daily...which keeps things fun, but makes my reviews of limited use.  I liked all the savory entrees though.  I think the pizza was actually one of my favs.  WIsh I tried a salad though.

As a carnivore, I was not sure how I would feel about a vegan type restaurant like Gather.  I must say I was thoroughly impressed with both the service and the menu in this great restaurant steps from the Berkeley campus.  We came for lunch.  Had a reservation but probably could have walked in as it was fairly open and spacious.  We started with the vegan pizza with cashew sauce.  It was great.  I recommend as an appetizer prior to the meal.  Then, I had to stay true to my meat eating heart and went with a ham and bacon sandwich.  Awesome w/ mustard dressing!  My wife had an egg sandwich and she loved it as well. Overall, food was tasty and not too hard on the wallet.  We would definitely come back and recommend to those who are looking to expand their horizoins with something new and fun.

Great food, great service and great atmosphere.

I had the vegan charcuterie and yellow tail to share with my boyfriend and it was amazing. We were so into the food that we decided to add another entree (a daily special, but I forgot the name), which was fantastic as well! The mixture of tastes in the vegan charcuterie was very interesting yet balanced. We saw the table next to us eating a pizza and it looked super tasty as well! I'm sure that I'll go back to try some more of their dishes!

My second visit to Gather...if only parking weren't such a pain, I'd be back there in a flash.  

At last, a restaurant that knows what to do with vegetables!  The vegan charcuterie was so good and so much fun.  

Had the hamburger...again.  Next time pizza for sure!
Healthy food. Good ambiance. Close to campus and Bart.

I really liked this unassuming celebrity restaurant.  It's a breath of fresh air from the similar "trendy" joints that plague Los Angeles.

What I most enjoyed about Gather is their actual use of fresh, seasonal ingredients.  It showed (visually AND on the palate).  So many places give lip service to "fresh, seasonal, blah, blah, blah" but you get the same arugula and baby veggies everyone else is serving up.  Gather, however, is the real deal.

I went with an adventurous group of people that don't mind playing Jewish Ping Pong (that's where everyone else reaches onto everyone else's plate) so I got to sample about 6 dishes.  My favorite was the raw, vegan "charcuterie" plate.  Each morsel was a symphony for the tastebuds and having not eaten anything that's walked the earth for two decades now, I was thrilled to enjoy charcuterie without the, well, charcuterie...

I broke my no bread diet to try the pizza.  It's definitely worth breaking a no flour diet for Gather's freshly made crusts...

All in, Gather lives up to it's reputation in stars...

This place is a-ok for me. I've always enjoyed the creative dishes they have here, but it's not anything that leaves me yearning to come back. Last night, I had the Monterey Bay squid with avocado, sesame, seaweed, and Fresno chili - really great. For the entree I had the Roasted Brassicas - Chanterelles, artichokes, Red Flint polenta, and hazelnut breadcrumbs. Perfection.

However, the house "on tap" wine is $9 a glass, and our total bill came to $90 without dessert. That's too pricey for my taste (and if the wine was priced at $7, we would have order more glasses of wine each).

This restaurant bills itself as one of those farm-to-table places, and I think they do a really great job on their dishes. Many people come here and split their pizzas, so it's got something for everyone. However, since opening a few years ago, the ambiance has lost a little of it's luster (the vine plants were looking very sad, as were the butternut squash and jarred veggies decor).

The staff were friendly after we warmed them up - I imagine they have to deal with a lot of rude patrons. Overall, this is a great place to try and determine for yourself if you'd like to come back. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu.

It was good. I can not complain. The service was great and the place looked great. We like to eat with friends and share so I will list what we all had. 
I thought the experience was a good one, and it was a fun place to hang out. I also felt good knowing that they care about the food they buy and where they get it from. 

Gin n root cocktail was refreshing but low on the buzz factor 
Cheese plate - kind of small, everything was underwhelming compared to say the cheese plate at Adhoc
Side of greens - okay 
Fries - also okay 
Polenta with olive oil - so good 
Bean ragu - okay, nothing spectacular, fennel was nice addition 
Baby chicken - cooked really well and tasted great 
Sword fish - Also fantastic 
Pork cheeks - I can't remember what kind but it was great, I wanted to give my bean dish back and have more of this one.  
Bacon apple tart - I love bacon, and it is great on dessert, but the tart was super dry 
Chai Crem Brulee - good, very good 
Earl grey something or other that was great 

All this for 159.00 (that includes a 20 percent tip)

It was very, very hard to get a reservation here but finally we made it!  We were seated right away and close to other tables, so close that I am sure they could hear our conversation.  The place is noisy.

Parking is very difficult.

The food was good.  The burrata appetizer was OK but the halibut was great and the spicy young chicken was very good as well.

The service was really bad, the waiter was never there and he had an attitude.

Expensive.

I liked Gather's emphasis on seasonal ingredients, the dishes were pretty, and the service was good. However, I was not as amazed as I expect to be for these prices. The portions on some dishes were fairly small and most things were nice, not fabulous. The pizza was definitely the best item we had and I'd recommend it. Dessert was the weakest point of the meal and really could be skipped. Finally, it was a bit louder in the space than I'd like in a fancy restaurant. 

Overall- had a good time, but, given all of the great food choices in the Bay Area, won't go back.

Food is pretty good, but menu in general is way overpriced for example $12 for romaine lettuce salad.  Reminds me of Plum in Oakland- showcase seasonal, local food and charge a lot for it  Service was lackluster, server never checked up on us to see if things were fine.  Good to try once.  There are just so many other better places to spend your hard earned dough.

I really wanted to like this place. And I applaud them for their innovative intention of serving mostly locally sourced, organic food. That said, their prices make it feel trendy and their portions are REALLY small - "squash and their blossoms" with one egg and a reduced sauce does not even come close to $22. 

I started by ordering an $11 glass of Pinot Noir, which was about 1/4 full. This really irritated me - because while the portions of food were ridiculously small, wine comes from a bottle and it costs them nothing (besides repeat business) to give a standard pour. I even ordered a second "glass", thinking that maybe it was the end of the bottle or something - only to realize that no, I would be paying $22 for a half glass of wine. 

My friend's eggplant dish was even smaller than my squash and their blossoms (read: its - there was no more than one squash on my plate), and we considered ordering bread to sop up the remaining drip of sauce on my enormous plate. 

Whatever innovative flavor and sourcing and presentation Gather is known for  was unfortunately lost on me, dwarfed by my irritation at leaving hungry, probably never to return. If I do, I'm bringing a flask and making sure I pre-eat.

Damn.  If all vegetarian/vegan food tasted like this, everyone would be a vegetarian.  We went at 6:45 on a busy Friday night, the place was packed, but the food and service were still flawless.  Even the cocktails are delicious to die for.  One friend got the Corpse Reviver, another got the Rhuby Cubed.  (Yes, I got to taste).  We ordered the vegan charcuterie, which changes seasonally, and comes with perfectly crisped bread (levain?)   We also got the avocado salad, the pizza with fingerling potatoes, goat cheese, leek and rosemary, and the roasted brassicas (chanterelles, artichokes, polenta, breadcrumbs, cauliflower).  Heavenly.  I enjoyed a visit to Ubuntu some months ago, was happy I'd gone for the experience, but probably wouldn't go back -- but I'd visit Gather again in an instant.  Even the deserts were amazing, such as the chocolate budino (yogurt ice cream, cherries, Sonoma salt).

With 717 reviews already posted, I really don't need to chime in, but I couldn't resist.  I was really stuffed after the dinner, because it was so good I couldn't put my fork down, but not unpleasantly full, trashed, bloated, you know.  Much as I love Pican, when you come out of there, your heart is pounding and you feel giddy from the slug of sugar, fat and alcohol coursing through your body.  This was different.  I was so full you could have cracked a tick on my stomach, as they say back in Texas, but never felt bad.

vegan charcuterie plate was divine.  It made me think it was created by forest fairies who went out into the prettiest and cleanest parts of the sierras and gathered herbs and mushrooms and seeds by a clear stream--the sheer number of different "local" and "wild" edibles on the plate was worth a botany lesson--taste delicious.  I'll be back. Service was lovely--my brother's baby artichokes could have been a trifle more tender but still this place for its creativity, flavor, and wonderful service gets 5 stars.  Love it! Love it. Our waiter from South Dakota was a real darling!

This is my Fiancee and I's go to classy restaurant for just about any happy occasion.  I love this place.  It's got a great ambiance and while I've not enjoyed every dish on their menu; I am constantly surprised by how much it changes and with what regularity I do enjoy their new experiments.  I love their cocktails, and their vegan dishes are, hands down, some of the best I've ever had.  The wait staff is always courteous, and professional.  

I'm even giving this place a 5 stars despite chipping my tooth on a hidden rock in my Quinoa because of the way the management handled it.  They couldn't have been nicer or more accommodating.  

My fiancee is a self-proclaimed carnivore, and usually only ever orders the burger which is consistently amazing, according to him. 
 
I recommend this place to anyone who's looking for a great date spot.
I can't stop daydreaming about Gather.

As a vegan with lots of meat-eating friends, I cherish Gather.  I'm always happy with the delicious vegan options, and the meat-eaters are always blown away by the fancy, local, sustainable meat options.

The menu changes with the seasons, so there's always something new to experience.  The chef often centers specials around a particular animal so that he can use all parts of it.

Not only is the food amazing, creative, and eco-conscious, the entire restaurant was built with green in mind, with benches upholstered with old belts, and a mural in the bar made from the packaging materials the chairs arrived in.

When the place is hopping, the wait can be long, but I always see this as a good thing because I want Gather to stick around.  The wait in the bar is usually shorter, and the bartenders are the best people in the world, so you have every reason to have your meal there.

The first thing out of my mouth after I tasted this little squid morsel in some kind of sauce was "Mother of God and all that is holy".  We dropped by on a whim for the prix fixe new years eve menu. We ordered one of each of the tastings, vegan and meaty, and nothing disappointed. The only regret was that no one warned us that the stuff under the oyster was salt and not shaved ice. I would not hesitate to go back and recommend it to all.

A friend and I went last night, having secured 6:30 reservations. We were seated quickly by some friendly ppl, handed menus, and our server showed up not too long after we sat down. The decor is great (nice lighting, love all the carved wood details, airy space, repurposed belts for bench covers) and the energy is good, too -- says a lot for this place that it was very busy on a Sunday night in Berkeley! 

We started with the vegan charcuterie, which was delicious. I also ordered a Bee Sting cocktail -- also delicious. We also ordered the "fried chicken" red kabocha with mashed root vegetables and gravy and the sheep milk ricotta pizza (with potato, leek, and nettles). YUM. The kabocha was obviously the more creative, but the pizza was damn good. 

We were SO full after the main plates, but we couldn't leave without trying dessert, so we shared a piece of Meyer lemon tart (awesome but the pith was still attached to the full slices of lemon) and tea and chai. 

I can't remember a more pleasant meal in a more pleasant space in a while. I will definitely be back! It's not the cheapest (we each spent $42+ tip for everything mentioned above), but it is so worth it.

Can I say expensive?  But the cocktails were great!  I had the No comparison and  Mirage.  Then I had a very tasty meal: mint cavatelli, vegan charcuterie , cuba fazoletti, pavlova.  The cuba fazoletti and pavlova were okay.

What a great place. Glad my mother and I decided to try out this new restaurant before attending a performance at UCB. and good we were there just early enough, because the reservation line stretched into the street. Fresh & modern, wonderful service, and of course, the food --- perfect in every way, but the desserts here deserve special mention because this part of the meal don't always take diabetics into consideration ..  but this kitchen does, and does so with fun and creativity. Don't skip it. A truly sweet deal!

SO DISAPPOINTED! $12 for THREE stalks of asparagus? Come on. I don't mind paying more for high quality, but I came out of this place feeling ripped off. 
The eggplant pizza was probably the worst pizza I've ever had, and for a place that supposedly looks out for vegetarians, beyond the charcuterie, (however you spell it...it was good) I was out of luck.
$140 for 4 people before tip sealed the deal. I won't be back.
So bummed! I really had high hopes and wanted to love this place!

My brother-in-law was attending a class at CAL so we invited him to dinner after hearing good reviews about this restaurant.

The restaurant is very modern looking and the kitchen is wide open for viewing.  Everything looked nice and clean.  My wife repored that they had Funnies in the restrooms, so that put a smile on her face.

I had a reservation at 5:45 incase things got busy, and they did, after we had been seated.  I told our server about the special needs of my wife, lots of water with no ice and he was able to accomodate our needs adequately.
He was polite and helpful.

My brother-in-law ordered the Saffron mushroom stew.  We all tried a little taste and exclaimed it as "good."  My wife had the Smoked potato mushroom pizza with cashew garlic puree, a vegan entree.  It was delicious and we all mentioned that we didn't even miss the cheese! I was very pleased with my Stuffed poblano pepper which was served in a bowl and spicy and flavorful.

Yes, it's expensive, but you get what you pay for, at least most of the time.  If you don't make a habit of going out every week, than I would say it's worth the splurge to support our local food producers and to eat food that was meticulously prepared.

I don't know why Yelp doesn't have a 'my favorite' bottom aside the rating...but if there was one, this restaurant would be on my top list.

Let me tell you this...I am a meat eater. I don't count my veggie / fruits serving. and needless to day...organic nor omvivore ain't my motto...

But every single thing on their menu and every bite I have, COMPLETELY MELT MY HEART.

The magic come when you can literally see the heart and soul behind each dish. The beauty of authenticity.... Nothing to hide. That's what I called real food.

Thank you for bringing that to my soul. If tomorrow is my last day on earth, I would come to order your cauliflower soup.

In a nut shell: beauitful environment with over priced BLEND tasting cafe food. 

Appetizer: Fried Cardoon ($9) very blend and Halibut Crudo ($8)  not bad. Well balanced. 

Main Course: Pig's parts pizza ($17). Was told the pig parts actually referred to sausages made from EVERYTHING of a pig!? ... sure...except only about 4 paper thin slices of the sausage were found on a overall extremely blend tasting pizza. Priced at $17, I thought it totally under delivered.

Desert: Chai Creme Brulee ($8) hit the spot.

Wine: a glass of Zin for $8 and Cab for $10.  

$79 bucks later, we (two of us) walked out of there feeling under satisfied. We support the restaurant's good intention to use local/organic ingredience, that's why we tried it out during its grand openning night. Would we go back? Not if the taste of the food is the same. Afterall, isn't the taste what people are paying for?

Loved the food, but the service was just a bit too casual.
Dinner was imaginative and delicious especially grilled calamari salad and corn and poblano chile pizza.  Absolutely recommend the food!
Wine list is expensive.
The service was super friendly but slow.  We were headed to a show so we were sensitive to the very long delay to order (even after mentioning our time frame to the waiter).  It was obvious that he had too many tables seated at the same time and was struggling.

It's the kind of place you go to so you can say you went to it.  There's lots of competition in Berkeley and this place really doesn't match up on food, quality, but it will survive because it is trendy.  The service is good.

Has a full bar, but you won't recognize any of the brands they sell, so don't count on your favorite beverage.

Burnt pizza and mostly weird concoctions that makes you think maybe the chef  is having a laugh.
Awesome service, fresh food, creative menu.  Highly recommended!

Local, simple, delicious...

The food here is very tasty.  It tastes very clean and very fresh.  I love the pizzas here.  But, as a warning, the corn pizza can be a little spicy.  The salads here are also excellent.  I particularly enjoyed the kale salad.

I would definitely have a cocktail again.  They mix savory and sweet elements and are innovative and refreshing.

The service here is adequate.  I have never had a bad experience, but it wasn't exactly attentive.  

It is a little on the pricey side, but considering the wonderfully sourced, unique, local ingredients, I definitely think it is worth it.

I have been here three times, and each time the items I selected were varied and delicious. 

I'm not a foodie, but I loved the interesting taste combinations and the visual beauty of the vegan charcuterie. It's been a little different every time, but always fantastic. 

Every salad I've tried has been great, and so too are the pizzas. The burger was great, but not particularly unusual. The best things to try here are definitely the unexpected taste combinations found in the charcuterie and salads. 

I just took my parents here. We shared everything, and they both loved the place even more than me!

A friend and I went there because of the gluten-free options.

We selected the pink pearl appetizer because we were really curious about the frozen cheddar (I mean, frozen cheddar cheese--how frequently do you see that on a menu?). It was amazing. Apple slices, two kinds of delicious sauces, and little pearls of frozen cheddar cheese that melted in our mouths. The cheddar seemed to have been whipped or processed prior to being frozen. Their form seemed possibly inspired by dippin' dots. Not much on the plate, but what there was was stellar.

I got the vegan charcuterie and my friend got the hamburger. Both also amazing.

I've only been here once, and it might be a little premature, but I really enjoyed my food. I went on Mother's Day with a friend, and the place was packed, but we were still seated right away. The waiters were attentive and it was worth the money, which wasn't as expensive as I expected. I recommend the egg sandwich, if you're there for brunch. And such great fresh orange juice!

Gather hit the spot on Friday night after a very long, intense day at work. The coctail list was fun and inventive. I settled on the Bee Sting. It tasted like a strong mojito. It was served in a martini glass which seemed overly fussy. I would have prefered a solid tumbler. 

We shared the little gem salad and duck sausage pizza. The salad was nice but not notable. The pizza, on the other hand, was fantastic. I've never called a pizza juicy before and never thought I'd want to, but I would describe it as juicy and savory. I think duck and duck fat is the new bacon. 

The service was friendly and efficient. Overall a lovely dining experience and I'll definitely be back.

I went in there an hour before closing so when I ordered their burger they didn't have any buns left, but I was so hungry at that point that I didn't care.
It was actually pretty good because they had the right combination of mushroom and cheese (I forget what cheese it was), though it could have been better with buns.

My girlfriend ordered the roasted chicken, which was pretty good but not spectacular. The marination wasn't something crazy but still good.

Service was good but the check was a little pricey for an average college student.

Now that Gather is open, I'm not disappointed.  We are vegetarians (Mostly vegan) and had plenty to eat.  We ate two salads (the fresh tasting radish salad and a kale salad), an appetizer (fried mushrooms with the most succulent sunchokes), a vegan pizza that was to die for (the crust was some of the best pizza crust i've had in the bay area) and a hazelnut with huckleberries and sorbet dessert.  Sauces and garnishes are out of this world good.  Even the water is amazing... I don't know what they do to the water to make it taste that good- I swear.  

They use the best ingredients and it makes a difference.  We ate a ton, and had dessert, coffee and a glass of wine and got out of there for $67.  You could get away with a stripped down (but delicious) meal for about $30 if you don't get apps, desserts or drinks.  I can't wait to go back.  I'm already thinking about what I'll order next time.

Even though we called a week in advance, we had to sit outside. I would recommend sitting outside because it's loud inside. There are heaters outside, so it wasn't cold. The food was great!!! The service was fabulous too!! My friends took me there for my birthday (big 5-0) and it was really special. We shared everything so that we could taste more items and the dessert was the only disappointment--it was too small. 

I'll be back ASAP!

Eaten here twice and left with the same feeling--okay food and not worth the high price. 

The atmosphere and look of the place are spot on. Modern and inviting. Unfortunately, seems like the owners are more focused on style than substance. The menu lacks dishes that really grabbed me. Food was only fine. Got the burger the first time and kim chee pizza the second. Both were tasted good not spectacular, but way greasy. 

Service was great on my first visit. On the second it seemed like we were a low priority at a table in the bar area and waitstaff were absentminded. No refill of our empty water bottle (I needed it after the jalapeños on the pizza!). Had to ask for plates for the pizza. Overall, the server was a step too slow.

With so many great places to get locally sourced seasonal food in Berkeley why spend so much on just okay food?

I've had two meals here.  The dinner was delicious and fresh.   We had  a number of beautifully presented, flavorful dishes ranging from an elaborate appetizer with pickled strawberries and sheep's milk yogurt (one of the best appetizers I've ever had at a restaurant) to a simple pizza.  The portions were a bit small, but very satisfying.  The free sparkling water is a nice touch, and the espresso from Thanksgiving Coffee is simply the best coffee I've ever had.

The brunch is also great, although the food was very, very rich!  I'd suggest getting some sweet and savory dishes and splitting them to avoid flavor overload.  If you're looking for the best of Berkeley, this should definitely be on your list.

Disappointing.

Had weekend brunch with my mom here and was anticipating a great meal based on hype and reviews.  

The first red flag was how empty the place was - it was a beautiful sunny Sunday afternoon and there was plenty of foot traffic outside, but the restaurant was only about 30% full.  We split 3 things for brunch: french toast, a house made sausage and baked egg dish, and a wild caught salmon special.  The french toast was just fine. It was drizzled with some sort of fruit reduction and sweet yogurt.  Nice texture, pretty satisfying, but nothing remarkable; it was just a decent french toast.  The sausage and egg dish had a lot of potential, but was probably the worst dish of the three.  The sausage was dry and chunky and stewed in a bland hodgepodge of vegetables.  Some of the vegetables were overcooked, some were undercooked, and had no flavor whatsoever.  I didn't know what I was eating.  To top it off, it was swimming in oil.  The salmon dish was also just mediocre.  It came with roasted vegetables (same as many of the vegetables in the sausage dish) and the piece of fish was rather small and ordinary.  That dish was $28, and I've had better salmon for half that price.  It wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't good; there was nothing defining about it.  

Don't get me wrong, the food wasn't awful.  But a restaurant with this much hype and self importance shouldn't be serving just mediocre food.  I didn't like the fact that the salmon and sausage dish featured the same vegetables - each dish on a menu should be constructed to stand on its own and have a unique flavor profile; using the same vegetables just shows that either they are lazy or unimaginative.

If my favorite restaurant, Camino, were to serve these dishes, I have no doubt that Camino would nail them.  It's the execution and thought behind the dishes that is lacking.  If you are looking for food prepared with seasonal and local ingredients and a restaurant that humbly takes pride in the simple elegance of food prepared right, skip Gather, go to Camino.

An excellent meal.

Yummy, well crafted cocktails, on the small side, but delicious.

Well paced, friendly, knowledgeable service.

The food was inventive, fresh and delicious. If you have time to sit, share and enjoy, Gather is a great place to do just that!

Gather is one of the great restaurants in the Bay area.  While it emphasizes fresh vegetables of all sorts, they can be ordered as part of a meat dish, on pizzas, or with other dairy products. They have a great variety of beveragaes.   The ambiance is wonderful, the long lines are now under control, and the service is fine.

Food was decent. 
The beer was good.

I have to say that our waiter was the best. On our opentable.com reservation comments I had mentioned some food allergies that were bad. Our waiter had written down all the ingredients so when the questions started he was right there with us guiding. The food was fabulous. You can feel the love of the food from the chef!

I really like the atmosphere here. I went here with a friend a couple of months ago for the first time and the staff was very friendly and the crowd was nice.
