It's the typical hipster berkeley crowd for sure. The wait times are ridic, so if you are in a hurry go somewhere else. It is however worth the wait, because I don't remember what we had but it was some soup and pizza and both dishes were delicious. They also have beautiful presentation. 

You should for sure try to make a reservation if possible, I work right across from here and they ALWAYS have lines for brunch and dinner. The prices are a little on the higher end but you know you're getting quality food and service.

I was treated to a wonderful lunch at Gather for my birthday and do not think I could have picked a more perfect place. The decor was elegantly natural and the fact that there is outside seating is a bonus (especially because it was an absolutely beautiful day outside!).

The liquid diet part of the meal consisted of kombucha and wine - perhaps not the perfect pairing but I had to try the kombucha (on tap!) and what's better than a nice glass of wine on a beautiful day with a fabulous meal? The kombucha was subtle in flavor - in a good way...it did not have an intense vinegar taste that some of the other ones that I have tried have had. 

The substantial (food) diet part of the meal was a shared kale salad and corn/pepper pizza. I was eyeing some other menu items but was told that I absolutely had to try the pizza - and I am certainly glad that I did. I'd describe the fantastic crust as akin to crispy naan. It was like a Neapolitan style crust in that it was thin as the base but the edge was light, fluffy and crisp on the outside. It also had an almost sweet taste to it - I'm pretty sure I would have been happy with a plate of crust. As a bonus - the toppings were unique and delicious. Perhaps a little greasy - but that didn't matter when the pizza was scattered with fresh corn and a slight spiciness that took it to a whole new level. The kale salad was good - I loved the addition of roasted carrots and a mild cheese. I'm not sure I would want an entire plate of this salad as I would possibly get bored of it - but it was still a tasty choice. 

I'm anxious to come back and try out a few more items - though I do have a feeling I'm going to want to keep going back to one of the pizzas - splitting, of course! They are a little large to have for a single serving. Best to have appetizers and then split a pizza.

I think this would be my strategy for both lunch and dinner - so I'm glad that the menu offerings are similar throughout the day!

INCREDIBLE food, very vegetarian-friendly.

featured ingredient of the day, featured farms, local & organic ingredients--a conscious-eater's heaven.

my cocktail was made with honey and was pretty good.

the 'charcuterie' sampler was memorable.

all light, yet filling.

one star off for TERRIBLE service; also, we had to wait 20 minutes past our reservation.

Super friendly staff put me at ease despite showing up directly from lab and rocking the "casual" look pretty hard.  I really like the layout which radiates out from the centrally located kitchen, and although a little loud at times, I never had trouble hearing my company.  Food was excellent, as would be expected here.  Little expensive for me typically, but great for a splurge.  My 5 star rating was sealed when someone in the kitchen noticed my hesitation on the pheasant leg and passed along the message through my waitress that gnawing on bones was encouraged by the chef.  They got their priorities right there.
nice place... lots of veg options... the food was good but not outstanding... service was great and ambiance quite good...

As with most restaurants in this genre, high expectations can skew impressions and give the feel of hit or miss with different dishes. That being said, when they hit (eg spicy tomato pizza), it's a home run! So keep an open mind, experiment, and give this place a few visits to find the dishes you love...there will be a few.

I love supporting the trend toward local and organic food.  Everything I had to eat there was delicious.  Polenta fried mushrooms appetizer satisfies the salty-crunchy cravings, and my cod dish was amazing.  I wished there were more vegetables served with my fish, as I like to eat something besides protein for dinner.  The burger was also really good.  
The tables are all made from reclaimed wood, and the benches are charmingly upholstered with repurposed leather belts.  
For a local, organic restaurant, the prices are really reasonable. 
I'll definitely go here again.
One of my favorite Berkeley restaurants.  I would choose it over most all SF restaurants.  I only eat veggies, and they have so many interesting veggies, with so much flavor!
still rocks!  food is always changing and so flavorful!

Well i had brunch here once. it seems the thing with this place is that they just used locally sourced items, is it good? It's fine nothing great. Will be back? Probably not, the food isn't worth the price tag. i'd rather eat across the street at Great China... 

But the decor is very modern and has a very hip feel to it. But all in all food ok, decor nice, overall experience just a 3.
fantastic. innovative. healthy but doesn't sacrifice taste and satisfaction !! not that cheap, however. more like $$ - $$$
Okay so If I could I would eat here every day. LOVE LOVE LOVE the Vegan Charcuterie platter. TO DIE FOR!

Delicious!!

A great date place - great service, yummy food.  I can't even remember everything we ate, but went because of all the great reviews from Yelpers and would definitely come back.

Thanks Yelp!

Overpriced beer served in a wine glass by a condescending bartender. Yeah, I know Belgian styles. Ive been to Belgium and they do not use wine glasses. Beer was served and we were pretty much ignored after that. 

Nice place however, food looked good. Maybe ill give it another shot some other time.
My favorite place for a tasty but healthy brunch. The food is terrific and they're always friendly.

I really want to love this place, Ive even gone back there 5 times, trying to have a good impression of it. my first trip there was OK... my partner's chicken wasn't impressive and our server seemed too happy-go-lucky - kind of out of touch with reality. I want someone to be real with me, not to baby me and treat me like a delicate "customer is always right" consumer. 

moving on... second visit was ok, still not super impressive.  I guess i really want this place to be a little more rootsy, perhaps give me a feel of the farm from where these fresh ingredients come from. I prefer the more rustic hip spots in brooklyn that effortlessly pull of that sought-after urban-farm rustic vibe, without sacrificing on presentation or quality. 

lastly... the reason that sparked my writing this review - my most recent visit on 7/7/10 was nice up until the dessert came. i had the chicory salad which was delicious, and everyone else was happy with their choices.  i was celebrating my birthday and we wanted a plate of cookies. we stopped a passing server to ask if it was possible to get a plate of chocolate chip cookies when she suggested that she could ask the chef to just cook up one big cookie. a fresh-baked cookie sounded divine, so we said yes. it took about 20 min, which we didn't mind, except for the fact that every few minutes our server visited to say it would only be another few minutes. the cookie came with candle and all, and it was the best tasting cookie ive ever had! it wasnt enormous, probably the size of 4 or 5 of their smaller cookies. the bill came (around $100) and we gave the server our credit card. when it came back it had an extra $6.50 added, which our server didn't offer to point out. we asked and he said "oh...oh ya... the chef said i should add another dessert charge" at which point we noticed that we were charged $13.00 for a cookie. that was the straw... 
we were eager to get out of there since we had already waited 20 minutes for our cookie and now felt cheated after they sneaked on an extra $6.50. 
We never asked for it in the first place... it was offered to us by a server (not our main server), and then we accepted it. It doesnt feel right.

anyway, i wont be going back unless someone treats me :)

I really enjoyed Gather.....fresh ingredients, good service and overall warm feeling.  We ate at the bar and the Bartenders were very attentive.  The grilled squid was fantastic and the chicory salad w/bacon was very tasty.
I'll definitely be back!

Tried brunch, ended up unsatisfied with my meal.  Ordered the 2 eggs and toast, I added a side of bacon ($9 total).  If you've every eaten breakfast in a restaurant before, and especially if you've eaten a $9 breakfast at any one of the terrific breakfast joints we have in the East Bay, you have certain expectations of what bacon and eggs and toast going to look like--this fell short of all of those.  Two small but acceptable slices of toasted levain bread, with a nicely poached, but completely unseasoned, egg sitting on each slice, and what appeared to be one sad little slice of dry bacon split between the two halves (that bacon slice was a $3 addition).  No butter, no jam, not even salt were available (were we supposed to make a special request for those? at brunch?).  So dry!  So dry!  So bland and dry!  

My husband's breakfast pizza (bacon, egg, onion) on the other hand was delicious, and a bargain (enough to share) at $15.  And the space is beautiful.  Hence three stars.

Another point, small but kind of important.  One of the things that makes me happy to order $10 cocktails is presentation -- interesting glass, thoughtful garnish, quality ice (there is such a thing!), or shaken and super-cold, a little froth on top.  But here my $10 brunch cocktail seemed sad because it was just dumped into the sort of cheap red wine glass you don't really see in restaurants anymore.  Made it less of a treat than it should have been.

My mate and I came here for brunch as I'd been following this restaurant from afar in San Francisco. After a happenstance coincidence we were actually in Berkeley (?) on an early-ish Sunday afternoon and I was not disappointed. The interior is gorgeous, we had a gorgeous host too that smiled warmly. Our server had impeccable timing and was nonchalant about it to boot! I tested her a bit by mentioning that I may want a cocktail with my amber wheat pancakes and she nailed it! I paired the perfect pancakes served with a dollop of ricotta, meyer lemon braised tiny oranges, itsy bitsy figs, orange zest and syrup with the Howler to drink. The Howler is my favorite cocktail now. I'm bummed I didn't see what was in it EXACTLY (it's not on their website and that's why I couldn't give this place a five) is disappointing to me. The cocktail in a vague description is a good representation of a margarita, however its made with vodka and is spiked with some jalapeno thing or another. At $11, I'm glad it's in Berkeley and not around the corner from me. I'm so happy that I read the write-up about Gather a while ago and followed them on twitter. If I hadn't seen a few of their great tips or new additions I probably wouldn't have made it there. Thanks!

This place has a food that tastes delicious!!! For small plates the lamb is delicious and very tasteful. For the large plates, the chicken has a lot of flavor. They have a choice of mineral water or still water and their home-made orange soda is good.

Fabulous local fare in an upscale Berkeley ambiance. The ginger soda is fantastic - very ginger-y! The portions are a little on the small side (especially the salads), but all reasonably priced. Extremely friendly service. We loved the baked eggs (who would've thought?).

I came here a few weeks ago with a last minute reservation on a thursday night around 8 PM. When we got there, the able wasn't ready so we were welcomed to the bar in the back by the host. +1 for tasty & creative drinks!

We were then seated in the dining room along the wall. It was slightly crowded but it was nice to see the room bustling. I ended up with the burger and fries and it was delish! the fries were really skinny...shoestrong style, with the right amount of salt & herb. i couldn't even finish the whole burger and had to box it up. we also had a salad to start and that was only mediocore. 

i'm giving it 3 stars because i was not very satisfied with the service. it was very hard to flag down our server and we were often waiting around--whether it involved getting him to take our order to getting him to bring our check. we had to ask other servers that were in the area to get our waiter for us. when the waiter did finally come to us, he was fine and friendly. I just wish he had taken the time to check in on us more frequently so we didn't have to look for him. but, i get it, it was busy...

Incredible food.  Sustainable, organic, locally-sourced ingredients.  Creative menu items and new flavors I've never had before.  Beautiful dish presentation.  Prompt, friendly, knowledgeable service.  Expensive, but appropriate for such a swanky place.  When I start making more money, I'll be returning.  Would definitely recommend for a nice date night.

I've been here twice with different groups each time. The first time I tried their foods was at a conference held in the same building. Fresh and simple dishes, that was all it needed to tell me that I should give the restaurant a try. I lived very close to Gather, but it still took me a while to actually dine there. Perhaps the ambiance of the place didn't seem to be a casual dining location for a typical college student. Even so, a lot of my friends think that it's too pricey and didn't want to join me.

My first experience was mediocre: great foods, but not so much for service. This was for a birthday dinner, with about 8 people. A lot of us just ordered their burger, since it was the cheapest entree item other than pizza. Not a bad choice at all. Their burgers were made just right, I remembered seeing pink juices when I bit into it. Their shoestring fries were crispy and goes well with their horseradish ketchup. I'm not a fan of ketchup, that's saying something. I didn't get to try their pizzas, my friends ordered their mussel pizza (this wasn't there when I went for the second time. Darn..) I didn't get to take a bite but I heard good things about it. Why did I say the service wasn't that great? Perhaps we were the wrong crowd in the restaurant, I remembered when our server asked if we wanted still or sparkling and we all wanted still, the server looks to the bar area and did a hand slicing neck motion. Yes, we cannot see what you just did there. I find that very rude indeed. This was about 2 years ago and I can still visualize this scene. 

Luckily my second experience was much more pleasant. First of all, I'm no longer on college budget, so I was able to try more of the other dishes. Secondly, it was only two of us dining this time. We were seated at the bar since there was a longer wait on tables. I don't mind it at all, I actually like the view of the kitchen. We were seated right in front of the two chefs preparing for appetizer dishes. I couldn't find the picture but their appetizers were presented in a delicate and colorful way. Definitely does its job as an appetizer.

The only thing is that their menu is so limited, only their pizza and their burger looked interesting. We ordered this hamachi appetizer, a pizza with pancetta (since they didn't have the mussels and I don't want to be vegetarian that night), a burger, and ended the night with a ginger sorbet. The hamachi was presented in a way such that you can have a number of beautiful pictures in all the angles possible. It had the pieces of hamachi with crispy seaweed and sprouts on top. Every bite brought out the sweetness of the fish, the saltiness of the seaweed, and then a neutral, clean taste of the sprouts. The pizza was fresh out of the oven, so expect it to taste even better than Cheeseboard. The crust was thin, so there isn't enough dough to overpower the ingredients on the pizza. This is not a dish to be finished by one person. I felt like I have stuffed myself when I tried to finish half. The pieces of pancetta was definitely the best part of it all. So for you vegetarians out there, you are missing out. The burger didn't have shoe string fries this time. Not as crispy but still pretty on par. I really enjoyed my sorbet at the end. It's very light and tingy, kinda cleans your mouth without leaving an "Oh I ate like a fat kid eating cake" feeling. Our server was much friendlier. First of all he didn't give us the neck cut when we wanted still water. Moreso, he is much more elaborate on describing each dish as he serves them. I do like to know what I put into my mouth and be able to enjoy it completely.

This place looks nice and has all the trappings of a good place. A nice space in a good location,  organic this and that, natural... But, the food is over-priced and not that good. The service is over-priced and not that good. And the whole experience is not worth it. Don't bother. If you do want to try it, get the pizza and bring your own wine.
Hit and miss with their selections but over all beautiful restaurant with gluten free options.

I've heard a lot about this place from veggie and non-veggie friends. On a Saturday afternoon we were in the area and decided to check it out. Although the menu had the little vegan icon identifying several dishes that could be veganized, many of them also were hot spicy...which I have no flexibility with. Perhaps I'm allergic but I have horrible coughing fits with the slightest chili flake in my dish.

So...I was feeling like their vegan friendliness was limited and acquiesced to a pizza that sounded rather dull -- smoked mushroom & potato with cashew puree. Thank goodness for the element of surprise! This pizza was so wonderful...even the dough was delightful. 

The ambiance is very comfy -- even the booth made out of old leather belts. It's hard to believe this place survives near a college campus; how many students can afford $19 pizza? But, as a bonus, you're offered a choice of still or gas water and it's free! ;-)

what a yummy restaurant! customer service was great, food was delicious, and atmosphere was warm. my girlfriends and i ordered the vegetarian charcuterie, lobster mushroom meatballs, and roasted chicken. the plating was beautiful for all three dishes. all the different flavors from each dish worked so well with each other. my favorite was the roasted chicken. sooo juicy and tender. this meal couldn't get any more "farm to table". amazing!

Who knew that a vegan charcuterie would be so good???? Who would have thought that anything gluten free anything would taste like any thing other than cardboard???  Gather is exactly what you might expect of a Berkeley restaurant--organic, not just vegetarian but vegan and gluten free options...it doesn't get much more crunchy granola Berkeley than that.  (And I mean that only in the nicest way.)

Every thing that I had was very good, the Bee Sting cocktail was especially tasty.  

The one con for me was the service.  My friend arrived a few minutes before me, beware of parking-it's a nightmare.  She got us on the list and when I got there we told the hostess that we would wait for our table in the bar area.  After about an hour we went to check on the table and the hostess told us that she'd given our table away because she couldn't find us.  It seems that she could have looked very hard and she certainly didn't call our name.  Once they were ready to seat us at a table they initially refused to transfer the tab.  

I will go back to Gather, the food was good and I am hoping that I just went on an off night.

Ingredients are the highlight here at Gather where the food philosophy is everything organic, fresh, and local... and yes, the distinctive taste follows through. The dishes are beautifully plated and full of novel flavors. The vegan "charcuterie" is an experience and similar to a mini tasting menu featuring four highlights of in-season ingredients, each with their own colors and complexities. Our other starters were likewise well executed: we had the kale salad, the king salmon crudo, and the sardines. For entrees, the brown teff panisse and the roasted chicken. For dessert, an almond teff cake.

A food dictionary here is a good idea and the stuff may surprise your perception of food all entirely. Gather reinvents what we take for granted. I wouldn't hesitate to bring a fellow food enthusiast here, someone who is looking for something new yet down-to-earth. Service is friendly and efficient.

My most interesting bite: In the vegan "charcuterie," Douglas Fir and Grains of Paradise give the blueberries, corn, smoked cashews, and pickled mushrooms an earthy and fragrantly delectable touch.
Just recommended this place to a friend.  It will be on the top of my list.

Always very pleased. The food, the service, the atmosphere, such a treat.
Catering to each patron's sensivities. Welcoming everyone.
Shall be back and back and back.

4 stars for food, 2 for service  We entered at 5:20 on a Sunday -- earlier they had refused our attempt to make a reservation for our small party saying we didn't need one. At the hostess station we were immediately told 'we can seat you but we need the table at 6:45'. So this was not a good start and given that the place was empty very off-putting. An hour and twenty minutes for dinner--we're off to the races.  We liked the sampler of vegetable appetizers. A good assortment and a creative and interesting layering of flavors but I wondered about how sanitary the wooden platter was as we had to scrape the surface to get the more liquid parts of the dips and sauces used that were just dumped on the flat surface when they should have been in tiny bowls.  A squash blossom appetizer was just two squash blossoms plus pieces of squash and a couple of onion rings. Competently deep fried and dusted with Parmesan the dish was tasty but if you call a dish squash blossoms that ought to comprise the majority of the ingredients.  These two first courses came out in rapid succession and our waitperson asked multiple times in a span of a few minutes how it was. Then we waited. And waited.  By the time our entrees came out it was 20 after 6. So 25 minutes left for eating a main course and, we'd hoped, to have dessert to celebrate a birthday. Not once after bringing the entrees did the server return to see if they were to our liking. 15 more minutes passed and someone came to take the plates. Awhile later she wandered back and offered to bring dessert menus. We looked but the thought of rushing through coffee and dessert while we overstayed our time slot put us off and we left. There is far too much good food in the east bay these days to put up with the way Gather treats its customers. 
We won't be back.

I have eaten at Gather 4 times now. I enjoy the interesting menus they put together and I appreciate the quality of ingredients they use. I've tried a sandwich, a couple pizzas, a vegetarian charcuterie plate, and a couple salads. The menu encourages you to try out of the box things like stinging nettle pizza(which is my favorite thing off their winter menu).

DELICIOUS and the ambiance is nice :)

I had the prather ranch burger and my friend had the barbecued young chicken (surprisingly huge portion!) Both were absolutely delicious and the chicken was succulent

Didn't wait long for our food, but we ate around 8:45.

I'll definitely come back to try their appetizers yumm

I've been to Gather now for brunch and dinner. I love their seasonal, locally sourced approach, modern yet warm decor and friendly, adept service.  The location just off Shattuck and University is great, outside patio, good parking yet near BART too.

Brunch was taken out in the lovely patio complete with an herb garden that grew more fragrant as the sun warmed the patio. Great meal options - Veg and Omnivore. Unable to choose, I had two dishes: Stone Fruit salad - delicate dressing, fresh produce and the Poached Egg with bacon-bean ragu - intense flavors, perfectly cooked eggs. Good strong coffee, too. 

Dinner had fun, classic cocktails (Corpse Reviver #2!!), a modest wine list and more lovely dishes of Veg or Omnivore. Nearly everybody around us had a wood-fired pizza and they smelled terrific, but we split the stunning & creative Veg Charcuterie platter (a savory blueberry sauce and pickled mushrooms?? Yes!) and the gazpacho. Not an ordinary gazpacho, mind you, but one made of roasted tomatoes with a dollop of strawberry granita - an astoundingly good combo of spicy and sweet, hot and cold.  The Prather Ranch burger was juicy and its french fries perfect. Also the heirloom carrot main dish was rich and hearty.  All dishes were very well executed. 

Dessert amazed - we had the burnt honey and green fennel seed ice cream but you must try the grilled strawberry dessert. It was complimented by smooth, mild goat cheese, cold olive oil ice cream and the most amazing, a delicate shortbread that hid a surprise of slivered almonds and sea salt!  The pastry chef is keeping that recipe to herself... Dang! 

Sean Baker proves to be an artist and Gather is a good substitute for the now defunct and dearly missed Ubuntu (Michelin star in Napa). Go and you'll find beautiful, creative veg dishes, savory meat dishes at a great value.  I'll definitely be back for more.
Very lovely place. Great atmosphere. Got the pizza and vegetable artisanal plate. Food was really good. Tried the Huerta Vida cocktail which had a smokyness to it.

Food: creative, fresh, flavorful. Love that their vegan/veggie dishes are very savory and I don't crave  meat. And I'm a beefaholic!

service: attentive and knowledgeable. Sometimes feels a bit college kiddish, with young staff, but overall professional.

Ambiance: tasteful and comfortable decor. Very smart design of space, no awkward tables.

My advice... Eat at the bar, good non-intrusive service. Food is a standout!

I love this place! It's usually bustling in here but it's pretty easy to seat a pair. I never thought I'd fall in love with vegan cuisine but here I am. I find myself returning for not only that but for their desserts. The honey pine nut tart was and still is the best dessert I've had in my life. I am a burger person but didn't like theirs all that much, but it doesn't bother me. Aaaand... one time the chicken was undercooked. But even so, I'm still raving. Every meal is beautifully presented. The waitstaff are extremely warm and attentive.

I was impressed by the use of local food sources. I was impressed with the presentation and the quality of the food. 

I was less impressed that the chef would not remove meat from half a pizza so that my mother and father could share (she is a vegetarian). I applaud the chefs choice not to alter a meal even slightly, It is only to be served the way he envisioned it, but I am surprised that the customer is not always right in a service based business.

Great food, Reasonable prices. A bit loud, but very comfortable environment. Staff were helpful explaining menu selection and great descriptions! Great organic cocktails with "new' tastes. Very worth the trip!

My fiancee and I were in the East Bay visiting a friend over the Memorial Day weekend and had napped in our hotel in Richmond until well after 9.  Not a lot of choices and another friend had mentioned Gather but had never been there herself.  So we hopped in the car and went.  Got there about 10 to 10 on Monday, Memorial Day.  They were happy to seat us.  The place was mostly empty at that hour so no wait.

I can't eat garlic, onions, leeks, shallots, and the entire family due to a sensitivity.  The waiter was helpful and suggested the burger and said that they'd put the tomato-shallot condiment on the side.

We ordered a lettuce salad to spilt which the waiter warned had some garlic or onions (he didn't say which) in the dressing.  A little in dressing is ok with me.  It seemed to have CHUNKS of onion or something in it.  Overall, I thought the salad was pretty good (picked out the chunks) but thought the dressing was a bit on the vinegary side.

To nit-pick, the waiter said that the burger was "medium rare" but it came slightly pink in the very middle and well done the rest.  That's medium, not medium rare.  Fine by me, actually, since I like it that way, but it just wasn't as the waiter said.

The burger itself was quite juicy, but without the tomato-shallot condiment, it was overall a tad dry.  Probably would have been perfect with the sauce and I don't fault them that I can't eat it.

The fries were the shoestring variety with quite a few overcooked.  And they had WAY too much salt on them.

My fiancee had they spicy tomato pizza.  I tried a bite and agree with her that it was REALLY good.  Quite a bit better than our local pizza places in LA.  The crust was really thin where it counted but the edges were thick and chewy - in a good way.

The lemon-lime soda was very good, but it came with the syrup on the bottom and soda water on top.  My first sip through the provided straw gave me a really strong, sweet taste.  After I mixed it up, it was really good and a nice touch over the typical cans and bottles.

We finished by sharing a pine nut tart with buttermilk ice cream.  The tart was very good, a lot like a pecan pie only more subtle and refined.  Not a huge fan of the buttermilk ice cream; it was incredible smooth and silky and very well executed, but the slight sour taste was just a little strange.  I think a more conventional vanilla bean or perhaps even a rose ice cream would have been better.

There were some misses... the fries were just bad with all that salt... but overall, it was a very good meal.

There are some things I found a little odd and/or annoying.  Probably differences in the Berkeley food culture versus that in LA.  For one thing, the menu is tiny.  There are a bunch of appetizers, but only 3 pizzas and 4 entrees.  Not a lot of options.  It just seemed weird that the wine list was far larger than the food menu.

I'm not sure why some restaurants have to use names to describe things that make it difficult to figure out what you're eating.  I've eaten at some very high end restaurants and high end, good ingredients, and good food do NOT have to feel pretentious.  Restaurants shouldn't make you feel like an idiot unless you're "in the scene" (and I'll bet most of those types of people are faking it).  I do actually speak French and the charcuterie is where we buy sliced cured meats and the like.

I'm glad we went, but if we lived here, I don't think I'd be a regular.

Growing pains certainly characterize many aspects of our evening at Gather, but what they lack in experience, this restaurant certainly more than makes up in ambiance, friendliness, and downright good food.

To start, we had a party of five that were seated comfortably along the recycled leather belt and wood barrel banquette. While we were waiting for the remainder of our party to arrive, (two of us had initially arrived), it took about 5 minutes before anyone came to attend our table in terms of water or drinks. Two additional members of our party arrived and were left wondering at the front of house where our table was, the front of house staff was attentive to those who were expressly seeking out their attention, but were less aware of those individuals who were apparently searching for a party - perhaps a problem of the glut of people that collects right at the entrance.

Water was served in reused milk glass jugs, either flat or sparkling, nothing pretentious and completely their own. Drinks were available in the form of a limited selection of wines by the glass or the bottle (those wines available by the glass were equally priced if not a better deal than the respective wine in a bottle - which was very confusing). The Gin-n-Root cocktail (gin, ginger syrup, lemon, and soda) was rather underwhelming with only scant hints of the root flavors - having just made a great batch of ginger syrup myself for cocktails. 

Our server was Kevin - extremely knowledgeable very friendly, and knew so much about the building, its origins, the food, and - well, everything we wanted to know, he knew about it. He was attentive, accommodated all of our requests (to the best of his ability), and overal heightened our experience immensely.

That being said, we were a bit disappointed as our first few plates came out that were delivered by the wait staff (and not our friendly Kevin), that they went without any explanation as to what we would find on our platters. The cheese plate was deliciously simple - although difficult to split among five people (extremely small portions), and each of their small plates/appetizer platters only come with three meager slices of bread/toast. The toast is amazing - but when you have a significant quantity of food (such as the absolutely amazing vegan "charcuterie", which also went unexplained for a good few minutes til we found Kevin again), and only three toast slices - that is a bit ridiculous. This was a struggle throughout the early portion of our dinner - as with five people looking to split things - more bread was a major issue. It ended up being suggested that we order a dish of their single-harvest olive oil (which was extremely aromatic) -- which came with a half-dozen slices of a lengthwise-sliced loaf of bread (a.k.a. three whole slices of bread). After much negotiation and learning that the three dollars we were paying was for the oil and not the bread - we doubled our bread-ings and left the proverbial card table on top.

That said, the food was absolutely delightful. The cheese plate was what one would expect to be on a cheese plate - fun types of (insert a cheese here), cheddar, brie, and and nettle gouda (which i was convinced tasted like a sage derby...), paired with a tiny mound of cranberry jelly, glazed pecans, a crabapple (we guessed, we never figured out officially), and some smashed dried apricots (again, a total guess here).

The vegetarian charcuterie was definitely a major highlight of the early portion of our dinner - "bacon" avocado with oyster mushrooms (we're not sure what the bacon part meant), beets with some intense south asian flavors (cardamom and cumin?), chicory rolls, a fennel salad, and roasted cauliflower with the creamy-goodness sauce... the drippings may have been the second wind of this dish - an absolutely reasonably priced at $14 for such an adventure. 

Our final app plate was the fried cardoons - which had the texture of fried okra, a similar taste to a very mild celery or even stringy zucchini (i speak in simple terms) - but the orangish spiced-almond sauce with the   scallion salsa was absolutely a wonderful accompaniment.

Next, we ordered a kale salad (which is blanched yet crisp and has great flavor - the marinated celery root looks like cubes of cheese but is tender and flavorful), split two pizzas. The "porky" pizza with guanciale has a permeating flavor of cured, salted pork & pork fat throughout every bite, and the crust is delightfully thin and flavorful - it brought the experience of pork on pizza to a different, level. The mushroom pizza was subtle - and the mushrooms were amazing, however, bits where one was left with neither mushroom nor other garnish, was merely a subtle mozzarella pizza where the oregano dominated the flavor of the bite.

We finished off our small-plate and pizza exploration with a selection of each of their sides - braised greens (i believe we had some chard), cream polenta, and fries. Fries - typical shoestri

Phenomenal!
As organic and fresh as it gets! Great service, great vibe, love the sunny patio. Also loved the chocolate pu-erh!  Didn't love the birthday cake cutting fee- never got why some eateries do this? Also, if you are dining with a big party (5+) call as far ahead as possible to secure a reservation. 
***Two snaps up...

I'll admit: the main reason I wanted to try this restaurant was the excellent rating that the Contra Costa times gave it because otherwise I wouldn't bother. C'mon, Berkeley, ANOTHER place touting free-range organic s...um-stuff?! (How "different" are you if everything's the friggin same?) 

But... my bf and I were pleasantly surprised...there's meat on the menu! (There is a God!!) So, of course, we ordered the meat platter..WOW and the pork... WOW again. Would've ordered the steak, but the tab was running a wee bit high by then--had to save room for dessert, which was phenomenal. 

And although the drinks could be a bit better and that you charge for bread(wtf)? This place is now a new favorite for me, I'll just swing by Acme for a baguette and bring it with me next time.

friday night - gather welcomes us to it's rustic-farmhouse-design-repurposed fixture-organic space, a full house, lively.

it's drawn-out dinner is intentional and thoroughly enjoyable.

sparkling wine to start, salads, pork cuts - samplings of deliciousness.
i got the angus burger. house-made sauces, bread.

everything here is sourced no further than a 30-mile radius. they don't even offer coke. which i kinda liked and yet found kinda annoying. but got over right away.

my plate slowly but surely emptied.
i saved a sliver of space for dessert = zucchini bread served with strawberries, blackberries and blueberries topped with a delicate, wafer-thin slice of candied zucchini.

reservations recommended.
casual attire.

be sure to check out the lighting fixtures (woven basketry) and the booth seat covers (old belts sewn together side on side).

fresh, clever.
really good.

LOVE IT, LOVE IT, LOVE IT
one of the best place to dine in....
the only issue is parking but who cares, a MUST go place

I eat here about 2-3 times a month since they've opened. LOVE IT LOVE IT LOVE IT. Had my birthday here, Will have my wedding here. Friend moved to town brought her in for the Vegan Charcutierie and she (a true southern belle) went hog wild all over it. When I told her it was vegan she was all like "No not this stuff holding up a crispy tofu skin." I said "yes that is deep fried tofu skin"and she said 'I want to have the chef's baby.' My future mom in law who is from Tampa loved the stuffed peppers and my best friend who regularly makes fun of berkeley vegans loves the Lipstick pepper pizza. I have hired Gather ( Back to Earth Catering) to cater a party for my office. 

My favorites: Artisinal Platter and I don't like sharing it at all. Any pizza with cashew cheese. most of the small plates and any time I can get the Braised Mushroom sandwich it makes me cry, swoon and curse like a mad woman. 

The service is hit or miss. I have found showing up 10 minutes before Lunch service is stopped can make the waiter resentful and I try not to do that anymore. Sometimes they are overwhelmed and in the weeds but as far as I am concerned the food more than makes up for it.

Gather is a wonderful restaurant to have in the neighborhood: excellent and very creative food. It is almost always possible to get a seat without a reservation even though it seems as though it is entirely packed each night. I have been here 4-5 times and I will defintely return, but they would be in running for one of my favorite restaurants if the service matched the quality of the food and drink. 

The wait staff is excellent - very nice and know their food well, but the restaurant seems incapable of controlling the timing of food delivery to the table. Every time I come here every dish shows up nearly simultaneously - hot and cold plates all at once and I feel forced to rush through a meal. For the price and quality I would much prefer to eat more slowly and enjoy the drinks with the meal. From a business perspective they might note this usually leads to higher drink sales.

This place has been open less than two weeks.  Only had drinks here, so I can't give it a full 5 stars.  Impressive looking menu.  A very Berkeley theme ... designed for Locovores, Glutin Free and Vegans.  Even the bar is organic based (no whiskey for this reason).  Great service at the bar.

I like Gather.  I like the idea of it slightly more than the execution. I don't like how noisy it is. I don't like the lighting.

The food is great but I think the prices are high relative to what you get. Many servings are surprisingly small plate-ish but priced like a full entre.

It all tastes great.

uhm....wow.

the interior is utterly home-y, earthy, and charming. 
the food speaks for itself. Ask your waiter if you have any questions on the ingredients on the menu, because there were at least 6 things I couldn't even pronounce on there, and had I not asked, I would have never known that you can make something so delicious with hay cream. yes....cream that comes from hay. Little gems of knowledge like this await you ask you inquire about obscure ingredients, it is really fun. 

The menu is different every few weeks (so unfortunately, you probably won't be able to have the amazing artichoke dish I had), but the concept behind this restaurant is so awesome. They basically go out to local farms and get whatever is cool, and they build a menu around what they've gathered during that period of time. Nothing goes to waste, as our waiter explained. They will find a way to use everything, new entrees and appetizers are being invented as you sit here and read this review, so go out there and try it before it disappears!

Small portions for everything but the pizza.  Two lady friends shared a birthday meal.  We explored the sample appetizer as recommended by the wait staff, only to find that there was only one serving of each sample.  It was pretty ridiculous.  She knew we were sharing?!?  We also had the pizza which was not bad, but ordered more salad because we were still hungry.  Pizza was decent, but definitely not crunchy on the bottom.  The tart dessert was good too, but unfortunately the wait staff forgot to bring a birthday candle for my friend.  

Also felt she was rushing us a bit, as she asked us what we wanted about five times instead of waiting for us to be ready.  Granted, it is a business and table turns are necessary, but there was nobody waiting at the door and there were some open tables.     

Still it is a nice place to dine, but slightly overpriced and small portions.

Wow this place is special.  This is my favorite restaurant.  I can come here and eat at Gather any day, any time.  I even love the name.  Food is sacred-it brings people together and we can gather to share in the experience!  Their food is so well prepared and thought out.  Every ingredient is paired perfectly with each other to make delicious dishes.   They have meat options, gluten free options, vegan options, all are delicious.  One can really taste the quality in all their ingredients.  Everything fresh, flavor at its peak, They make their own bread and pizza crusts and they are good.  This place is good.  Don't miss the kale salad with roasted carrot, pine nuts, and Fiscalini cheese.  You must try this place.  I love this place.

I had many preconceived notions about Gather, based on someone I knew who had to wait forty-five minutes to be served, its pricey menu, and the mixed review in the New York Times. I thought it'd be the kind of place that charged a lot for very little, but was pleasantly surprised by the gigantic portions, especially of the dynamic pizza.

I loved eating there. The inside had a very warm, friendly feeling. You can look and see the chefs making things (though my seat faced the window, so I didn't watch the chefs). My BF and I both started with salads--kale salad for me (I was wary because kale is one of my specialties), but their way of preparing it was fabulous. It was served with tiny slices of carrots, pine nuts, and some kind of shredded cheese that begins with F. There was some kind of dressing. Dunno what, but the blend of flavors was amazing. Also, the salad had such pretty colors. My BF's salad came with greens, ricotta, blood oranges, and some kind of delicious dressing. 

For our entrees we both chose pizza. His came with nettles, potatoes, goat cheese, and rosemary. Mine came with mozzarella, olive oil, and salt. Both the salads and pizzas were huge.  I am v. particular re pizza, and Gather's pizza hit the pizza spot! Thin crust with enough crisp and poofy dough and a bottom crust that holds the pizza toppings without being soggy. After years of trying to find perfect pizza in the Bay Area, I am happy to report that Gather's pies are among the best!

Finally, I would give Gather five stars, but we had to shout to be heard. I prefer a quieter dining experience.

Kale salad with chicken was amazing.  Service excellent at lunch time.  The quality of the food was top notch, locally sourced, etc.  We sat in the bar area, but did not have any drinks on our first visit.

I will definitely be back here to experience more of the menu and the good looking, $11 cocktail offerings.

FIve big shining Stars!  This is the top restaurants in Berkeley downtown.  Clean, environmental friendly restaurants with open kitchen where you can see the chiefs who are "loving caring" your food right from your table!

The foods are just excellent.  The pizza is amazing.  All dishes are created with fresh, in season, local ingredients.  Not to mention about the creative menus they have.  The menu changes a lot and it's just what top restaurants do.  To keep the regulars from not getting bored!

The brunch is wonderful too. They have a sunny outdoor patio.  In Berkeley, you will get the warm Sun without the fog!!!

Now, comes to pricing.  It's very good.  Most main courses are under $15 and it's enough food for the entire meal.  

This is a great place to eat and not having your money being robbed by the restaurants.  A place you must go when you are in Berkeley.

Really rustic decor and classy (although unassuming). Their dinner menu and drink menu was really mentally stimulating because it's so different than the run-of-the-mill menu; their claim to fame is from using local and sustainable recipes in all of their dishes and so it took a while to decipher the menu. I tried a Pilser beer which was light and refreshing. I ordered their barbecue chicken -- the chicken itself was awesome, but the side dish had too much of the beans it came with. But back to the chicken: the white meat of the chicken was the most tender and moist I've ever had of white meat. The Kale salad we ordered was superb. I've never had a salad quite like it because of the uniqueness of the greens they used.

New American cuisine but more vegetarian like vegan charcuterie blah blah blah

Interesting architectural touches seats are made of old belts blah blah blah

Rhubarb white teff chard creme blah blah blah

The company was good. The food was exactly what you expect at this price range in this style. Four stars instead of three because of the extra effort for vegetarian dishes. But the blah blah blah predictability makes me yearn for the shock of the new. AND I'M STILL HUNGRY.

Server: How are we doing today?
I'm thinking: Um, who the F is "we?"

...and it went down hill from there.

After the waiter repeatedly tried to sell us on the vegan charcuterie (and I really hate when waiters try to sell me things on the menu. I can see the freakin menu, I know what's on it, and I'll order whatever the hell I want to order), we decided on the kale salad, squash blossoms, and sausage pizza. We also each order a glass of wine. The waiter seemed thoroughly disappointed when I didn't order the vegan charcuterie.

A few minutes later, someone comes out with a glass of wine and tries to give it to my wife, but of course it's not what she ordered. A few minutes later, they bring her the correct wine.  Meanwhile, I still don't have my wine. A few minutes later, the kale salad comes out. A few minutes later, we're halfway through it, and I still don't have wine. I see the waiter and ask about it, and he mumbles something unintelligible about how the printer wasn't something something something.  We finish the salad, and my glass of wine finally comes.

The food: salty. The kale salad, all I tasted was salt and lemon. It was cold and slimy. The squash blossom was bland, and also seemed to have the same overly salty dressing as the kale salad. The pizza was decent, but i've had way better in the bay area, and way less than $18.50.

In the end, I do not plan on returning to Gather. Poor service, mediocre food, and outrageously expensive wine (only one red wine on the entire list was under $40. It was $39).

Their pizzas are good, I like the decor, outside seating is nice.  I also like to try things there and they are quite nice about letting me try things.  Portions and quality, however, do not justify their prices.  I have been there three times and have decided to move on.

At lunch recently, the pulled pork sandwich was average tasting, and not worth $11.  I probably would be ok paying $6 for it.  I also added the roasted market vegetables for $2.50, and was very disappointed.  It was mostly olive bits and whole beans (a few parsnips and pepper bits were there too).  I don't like olives, which is not their fault, but a plate of veggies should not be mostly brown beans, not especially flavorful either.

Dessert cookie plate was nice, portion-wise probably on par with other hifalutin restaurants, and the cookies tasted good.

Previously, at dinner, we ordered an appetizer sardine, and I was a bit surprised at the quantity of food that came - two small fishes for $9.

Stick with the pizza I suppose, it seems more on par with the price, although be sure you like their crust - it is thick and the actual cheesy/meat area of the pizza is fairly small as the crust takes up about 1.5" around the edges..

To sum it up - if you eat here, you are paying a decent chunk for the experience and some for the food, so be warned.

When Gather is on its game (which, inexplicably, it hasn't been for the last month or so -- my guess as to the reason for the recent less-than-positive reviews), it may well have the best food in the East Bay. (With all due bows to Chez Panisse, the food at Gather is more inventive, fresher, more contemporary, covering the full range from omnivore to vegan, with attention to gluten-free options too.)

The vegan charcuterie (served only at dinner) is usually quirky, delicious, inventive, and surprising. It's fun to sit next to someone who's never had it and is just astonished at the wooden board full of small delectable innovations. And though I'm vegan, most of my friends are omnivores, and I love that they can get a burger or chicken (I hear Gather does an excellent job with these), while I'm having an amazing plant-based entree. That way we're all happy.

So, why only four stars? It's hard to make everyone happy, and I want to acknowledge that, especially in a restaurant trying to serve so many different kinds of food. (It seems to me that the menu is too heavy to meat/cheese (but I see that some meat-eaters think too much is veg.)

Mostly, I wish that there were better lunch options for vegans, that the evening waiters didn't hover quite so much when you're nearing the end of your meal, and that the kitchen were less into exploring the possibilities of bitterness right now. What's up with the vegan lunch option (if you're not wanting pizza, and you do want some protein) being either salads of bitter greens (mostly designed to have cheese but you can have it left off) or a RADISH with cashew-ricotta? Now, Gather does dreamy things with cashews (their cashew-cream vegan pizzas are the best pizzas I've ever tasted), but a radish isn't lunch. It's conceptual art. 

Please, oh brilliant chefs of Gather, don't give me conceptual art instead of lunch. Use your gifts to marinate and bake some fabulous tofu and offer it as a salad add-on, the way you add chicken or fish. Or make some of those divine lentils and greens that you offer with weekend brunch. (Does divine lentils and greens sound like an oxymoron? You may have to try the Gather version to believe it.) 

If you did even this last couple of things, I predict that the dining room at lunch would start to be as crowded as the dining room at dinner. Because it's not that common to have places to lay aside the food wars and just all eat lovely sustainable food together. We really need you.

delicious, innovative, inspiring, arousing, but small expensive portions.

i didn't have any sort of alcohol (new years day fallout) but the in-house jasmine hibiscus soda was good times.

our server made it clear he was unimpressed by our group, but it was cool that he stuck around, and never disappeared otherwise, or anything like that.

a very cool, very friendly, very random lady brought us an extra dessert we never ordered, then said something like, "tee hee, then have one for the table!" then we were charged for it.

overall, good, but expensive for what was on the table.
go to this place immediately and often.  we are so lucky to have this gem!

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday earlier this year. Everything we ate was delicious, I wish I could have consumed more, and the service was excellent. I'm not into health food, or fads, i'm into just whatever tastes good, and gather is an wonderful place to go for happy hearts and happy stomachs!

Ate here with two friends and we ordered the burger, a salad and the pizza. All were very good.

Very nice, new restaurant with a good vibe at the bar.

Only downside is that parking can be bit of a hassle. As a tip, there's a lot a block away that charges a flat fee of $4 for weekday evenings.

Came here for a quasi-late night meal. We were pretty hungry, plus I've been wanting to come here for a while. Unfortunately, we were met by terrible service. We were seated at the bar, or at the *rails* to be specific. We sat there for 10-15 minutes and were ignored. When I motioned for the waiter at the bar, he walked over only to pick up the plate at a nearby table, and ignored us (couldn't even bother to tell us what's happening). When I walked up to the bar and told him we'd like to order food, he spitefully said that they don't serve food "at the rails" and immediately walked away. Then why did they put food menus down for us "at the rails?" The bar waiter didn't even tell me what I could do (like sit down here at the bar, or something), but just walked away. It was awkward and embarrassing, and there seemed nothing for us to do but leave. This was hopefully an isolated incident, but I don't think I'll ever come here again. We left and went to Gordos, where the service was much friendlier and we were treated like human beings.

Had brunch here with the girls a few months ago. Food was ok.  Service was ok.  I think we were expecting more vegan options.  It's a pretty space.  It's one of those places I wouldn't suggest, but I may tag along if someone else has a hankering for it.  Especially if they pay.

More like 3.5 stars - the food was pretty good, yes, but the service was slow and the atmosphere of the restaurant wasn't great and the food quality-to-price ratio was off. The large plates and the salads/starters really aren't that different in size. The vegan charcuterie was very interesting, and there's sure to be something for everyone on it. 
extra + : their bathrooms have far side comics!

Good food, friendly service, inviting atmosphere, and superb location.  On the positive: innovative flavor profiles, amazing cocktails (a superb sazerac), and relative affordability. On the flipside: slow food preparation and a very limited menu. All in all, I'd recommend it for anyone seeking local farming options without pressing schedules.

If I could give Gather a 3-plus, I'd do it.  Better than OK, but I cannot say I'm a fan yet.

Concept:  Love it.  The idea of locavore and sustainable eating is great.  Don't even mind the prices, as the food is supporting a local and sustainable economy (and probably costs what it should).

Food overall is uneven (some great, some feh!). Don't quite understand the hype over the pizza when there's such phenomenal pizza in the Bay Area. The dough typically is soggy for all but the outer edges (third pizza try).  Toppings are creative.

Enjoyed the creative drinks, too.  The greens are positively awful; no matter what leafy thing they serve, I found there were too many stems and the greens were always undercooked.  Salads are small and the menu seems swine-heavy to me.

Service:  Always friendly and kind and helpful. Never snooty.   One tiny complaint here:  some servers need to either bathe or get some more effective deodorant.  It's a little distracting when you're eating to have bad BO waft by as you take a bite of your food (has happened twice). 

Overall, it's good food and a good idea, too.  I'm a long way from "Blown Away," but I can understand why folks like it.  Perhaps they just need a little more time (and perhaps a teensy bit of soul --people, learn how to make greens, please).

Yummy food and great location if attending anything at the UC. All within easy walking. We enjoyed the romaine salad. The squid was the best I have had.....so good, we ordered seconds. Wine list decent and very affordable. The ambiance classy contemporary with a very warm flair. This place certainly far exceeds anything Olivento had/has to offer. Way better! Would definetly eat here again!

Walked into Gather, and it smelled aromatically fantastic! We ordered the Spicy Tomato pizza and the Smoked Artichoke entree. Both were excellent. When I first read the menu, the descriptions actually didn't sound too appealing. But I went with some review recommendations here and was quite pleased. There are a lot of ingredients in the dishes. To be honest, I don't even know what some of the stuff was on our plate but they work well together! 

Spicy tomato was awesome. Smoked artichoke entree was good, as was the accompanying farro/rice it sits on, but the two just didn't seem to mesh. I liked them better separately. Also, I just noticed that the menu has changed the farro/rice part, so it probably tastes different now. 

Dessert was the one disappointment. Had the warm parsnip cake and it was okay but nothing special. Not nearly as good as the pizza and entree. The one thing I regret not getting was the Vegan Charcuterie. Yes, everyone raved about it here, but we didn't get it. Then I saw another table order it and it looked fantastic. A large portion size, good for sharing. Next time...

Went for dinner with my husband and a friend who is vegetarian. I hear stories from her about Millennium all the time, and we wanted to branch out and try another place that had a heavy focus on vegetarian food. We got the veggie charcuterie to start, and my friend and I split the cauliflower soup, hoping for something amazing. The soup was just lacking in flavor after we've had some of the most amazing cauliflower soup at Laurus in Blackhawk (closed now *sigh*). The charcuterie was okay, but not amazing. My husband got the Prather Ranch burger with fries and my friend and I split the Stinging Nettle Pizza. My husband said the burger was good. I tried the fries and, I have to say, those were some of the best fries I've ever had. I think I liked them because they were on the salty side and I love salt. Pizza was good, I especially liked the blistered crust. Overall I just wasn't blown away. I was impressed by the dedication to the food and the fact that our server knew exactly what heirloom variety of broccoli flown in from France was in our appetizer. Gotta love that kind of passion. Only hiccup of the evening was our server put in the wrong pizza order. The manager just happened to bring our food to us and set down the pizza and said "Fontinella Pizza" and my friend and I both shouted out "No!". We told her we ordered the Stinging Nettle Pizza. She apologized and went to find out what the trouble was. She came back and apologized again and said that they were rushing our pizza for us and would take it off the bill. Then our server came over and apologized. It was the most gracious admission of error I've ever seen in my life and I totally appreciated it. They really deserve another star just for customer service.

One of the best restaurants in Berkeley, and for that matter in the Bay Area.  We tend to eat pescatarian, with a lot of veggies.  We want unique flavors, and really good plates.  Gather for dinner is great for that.  Whether sitting at the bar or at a table we haven't been disappointed with a dinner there.  Lunch...we were disappointed.  I was luke warm on their pizzas, and it was ok, but nothing special.  So you want to try interesting dishes it is great, of course it isn't huge portions, which won't go over well with some people but for us we like to enjoy the food and not feel overly stuffed when we leave.

Came here for lunch today. Ingredients are of good quality, but portions are rather small for the price. The place gets crowded very easily. Service is on the slow side, and it's even slower if you sit in the patio area. 

Pizza: Got the day's special, which had veal, mushrooms, and horseradish sauce. It was good, but $18 for a pizza that's only about 10" in diameter with 2" consisting of crust? Yeah, the crust was great, chewy and delicious, but $18 is pretty steep for such a small treat.

Kale salad: I never knew roasted heirloom carrots tasted like roasted potatoes. Not a bad thing, though. $10 for a large portion that wasn't exactly large. It probably cost them $2 to make that salad.

Desserts: (Got four of them, because we were hungry)
Cheesecake: If you expect a slice of thick, rich, dense cheesecake, you won't get that. This looks, feels, and tastes more like a  scoop of light cheesecake pudding/mousse. Covered in crushed pistachio "crust" with strawberries and raspberries, there is a hint of lemon flavor in there, and while it tastes good, it doesn't deliver the satisfaction that one usually gets when they have a nice, rich, indulgent cheesecake.

Bread Pudding: More like just a muffin coated in powdered sugar. Not bad, but not exactly extraordinary.

Ice cream: This is extraordinary. Flavors of the day (we got both) were vanilla and espresso. Both were heavenly. Vanilla is perfection, espresso was wonderfully flavorful and had great texture. Loved the ice creams. 

I was always curious about this place. I'm glad I came here today. Now I know there is no real need for me to come again. (I say this with no malice. It's just fact.)

Gather Restaurant is a perfect addition to the bay area, I just wish it was closer to where I live! It's so nice to see a restaurant where all of the food is perfectly seasoned and completely flavorful! Not too much salt, but not too little.

As a vegetarian it is rare that the food goes past "healthy" tasting, but at Gather every menu item was delightful, original and creative. 

We pretty much tried the whole menu and I couldn't find a single flaw... the desserts were incredible as well, especially the goat cheese panna cotta.

Keep up the good work!

We found Gather to be a mixed bag: We were excited to try the vegan charcuterie and although we loved some of the pieces, others were disappointing. The best part of the meal was the starters - everyone's dish was a winner from the cannellini bean soup to the kale salad to the gem salad. 

The real let down were the pizzas: they looked great, but weren't very memorable. The tomato piece was good, the summer squash barely had any squash and the Fontinella was a total bore.

Six of us went out to dinner - and all felt this place was better in concept that in execution.
Overrated! Food was bland. Service was good but wasn't worth the $100 spent.

ur.............down one star last Thursday I went.

We didn't know that on Thursday even if you show up at 5pm (when they first open), you'll need reservation otherwise your option is 'at the bar' or 'patio seating'.

Bartenders are very very very busy........so, we couldn't get his attention to order our drink and food until 30 minutes after. 

Food is still good, but right after our food came, the check also arrived, except it's actually not our bill....it's for the guy who's sitting on the other side of the bar.

Service is REALLY SLOW at the bar (side bar).
great atmosphere, delicious food and good service are the highlights of this restaurant. They have many clearly marked vegan options. It was delicious.

my boyfriend and i went here a few weeks ago and it was GREAT!! Service was good our server was very nice and helpful. My boyfriend had a glass of zinfandel an i had a bee sting which where both Great i loved my cocktail. To start we has the Brussels sprouts and the calamari. Both where great starters very flavorful and well seasoned.   Then my boyfriend had the special of lamb which came with tongue, liver, and kidneys. He LOVED it, I'm not a big fan of those parts of the lamb so i didn't try it. i had a Cesar salad with pears which was delicious. We both cleared out plates. We didnt have dessert but im sure it would have been great as well. Great food Great service!
Good food. Had their pizza and burger. Maybe a but pricey but nice to check out nonetheless.

Food is great, have never been disappointed.  Would have given it 5 stars but service a few times has been sketchy inlcuding an incident where the waitress argued with me after I politely reminded her that I was missing a burger.  "you didn't order one".  "no I think I did."  "NO - you didn't.  But I can put it in now".  ok.

This is my all time favorite restaurant in the East Bay! The food is always fresh, natural and delicious! If you haven't been there, try the tomato pizza and if you drink, a Bee Sting Cocktail. Fabulous place!

Had a wonderful experience eating here. Not sure why people were complaining that the service was terrible or the servers were unfriendly because our experience was extremely friendly staff, delicious food, and a perfect start to our evening.

We had tickets to a concert at the Greek Theatre, and wanted to have a nice, vegetarian meal beforehand. Given how Berkeley is, we were fortunate to have TWO veggie options right next door (Gather and Saturn Cafe). And from the descriptions I had planned on trying Gather first then using Saturn Cafe as a backup. 

Intuition proved right... there was a line out the door at Gather, and Saturn looked a little too informal for the mood. However, after waiting in line to which many people were being told it was a 45 minute wait, luck must have been on our side, because a very kind hostess ushered us into a private "reserved" 2-person table back near the bar. Joy!

The wait staff was very nice, suggested some incredible dishes to try (we even decided to go completely vegan for the meal, since it is so rare for us) and we walked out on-time for the concert and with bellies full of goodness.

My wife and I ordered the vegan charcuterie to start and the vegan tomato pizza (with cashew puree serving as a surprisingly good substitute for "cheese"). For drinks she had the Bee Sting, and I ordered the Smoking Gun. All of which are highly recommended by the staff, and now us as well.

In short, if you are in the area and want a nice, fancy (but not stuffy) pleasant evening to sample some delicious food, this is your place. And while they don't exclusively serve vegetarian/vegan food, I would highly recommend taking that route here. There is nothing better than vegetarian food done right.

Review is 2.5 stars.

I was both very impressed and very disappointed with this place.  For the price there are MANY other restaurants that can and will provide a better dining experience. 

 In some ways, this is exactly why people dislike restaurants with a message.  The message I got from Gather was "We have great products, but are still figuring out how to use them correctly", rather than what I assume was the intended message of local and sustainable ingredients used in a unique manner.

The oft mentioned vegan charcuterie plate definitely lives up to it's billing, and if this was the only dish I had tried, I would be raving about this place.  It is absolutely a must order if you go to this restaurant.

However, I was very very disappointed by the cocktails and main dishes.

The cocktail that my dining partner ordered was the "Summer Sandals" which was a sandalwood infused gin drink with basil and cucumber.  She asked if the drink had the flavor of gin as a main component as was assured that it did not taste strongly of gin.  After seeing her face after one sip, I correctly assumed that GIN was the dominant flavor.  

10 bucks down the drain. 

The dishes, which were both specials for the evening had great potential, but the sloppy execution and careless use of salt and spices ruined what could have been an excellent meal.

My dining partners dish, a sous vide lamb that was seared and placed atop a garbanzo bean ragout was wildly spiced and lacked any flavor focus.  The meat itself was excellent, but the flavors it was paired with were incongruous with the flavors of the lamb as well as with the other parts of the dish left on the plate.  This dish was 26 dollars.  It should have been about 19.

My dish, a porchetta made from wild boar, was so poorly made that I was actually upset the the chef served it to me. Porchetta, which I have had a number of times, is usually a fatty pork belly which usually contains a pork loin rolled with spices and herbs and is slowly cooked until the meat is melt-in-your-mouth goodness.

This dish on the other hand contained very little meat, was extremely overspiced and what meat was there was very tough.  The polenta that was served along side had great texture, but was also overspiced.

What a waste of one of my favorite types of meat.  It was also 29 dollars.  If it wasn't clear above, a total waste of 29 bucks.

The desserts were excellent however, with the peach cobbler especially refreshing.

Overall, 150 dollars with tip making this meal about 60 dollars higher than what it was worth. 

I wish I had ordered the burger.

We came for my close friends birthday brunch on a Sunday. We came at 2ish and they were rushing us to take our orders because the kitchen was closing. They came back and told us they only had one eggs Benedict left, so some people had to change their orders. 

I got fresh and ordered the Farm Egg pizza which had Bacon, caramelized onions, and herbs . I wish the bacon was more crispy. It was pretty much infused with the sauce so it was more on the limp side. Pretty good but I liked my friend's Magruder Ranch boar sausage which had Chilies, Fontinella, and oregano. However, my friend's crust was pretty burnt compared to mine.

 My friend also ordered mimosas. One glass for $10 is pretty ridiculous when there are places where it is $12 for bottomless mimosas. I thought the mimosa didn't have enough OJ. I also got the Kombucha Botanic which came in a small cup. SMH. I was not satisfied. I really appreciate that they provide their own made drinks but there was too much club soda. My friend liked it but I should have gotten the hibiscus/jasmine drink. I still think this place is average.

This is a very good restaurant with very good service.

I started with the lentil soup. Saying this was the low point of the meal is praising with faint damnation. It was actually quite decent and fresh-tasting but would have been better with a few dashes of pepper. Then again, maybe the issue was that I had it just after the ginger beer soda, which was tasty but had a strong taste.

2 of the 5 items on the vegan charcuterie were quite good -- although one of these had a few random bitter bites -- and the other 3 were omg good. 

the apple crisp dessert was omg good as well. I didn't expect the earl gray currants to work in that but work they did. every bite was a joy

service was efficient, not rushed, and friendly. not sure I saw acoustical tiles on the ceiling, but whatever they did the noise level is noticeably very reasonable here. thank you, gather!

I went to Gather because I received a gift card from work.  I went for a dinner with my husband and our 10 month old baby. I was pretty excited because it was our first evening outing, it was my birthday and I had read great things about the restaurant.
Parking was a bit difficult so I went in with the baby while my husband was looking for a place to park. As I sat down and sat the baby in the high chair the waiter asked me what I would like to order. I said I will order once my husband comes in, but would appreciate it if I could get some water. He brings the water and asks me if I want to order an apetizer. I repeat I want to wait and he gives me a strange look as if I offended him (rude!). When my husband arrived we ordered the food - their vegan plate that was recommended to us, the spicy tomato pizza and sea urchin. I wanted the grilled squid, but the waiter said if I like seafood I would love their house specialty - the sea urchin. 
While I was feeding the baby some baby food my husband explained to the waiter that it is my birthday and asked if they do something special for birthdays. The waiter replied to him "sure we do", but did not tell my husband what.
The vegan plate came pretty fast, and I thought it contained more sauces than anything else. I was not impressed that the waiter put the plate in front of the baby, and as he placed it she put her hand in it.
I mean, come on! I asked him to serve the food on our side so that the baby can nont reach it, well needles to say, he did not do it right even once. He even put the new cutlery (they collected our cuttelry with the vegan plate) in front of the baby and she picked up the knife immediately - I was really pissed off, but was trying to keep  my cool, so I do not ruin this very rare outing.  Out of the four things served on the vegan plate, each a bitefull, I liked two. I liked the raw aspect, and enjoyed feeling the taste of fresh food, but the serving was just too small. 
We waited for a very long time for the pizza to arrive. I work in event management so without trying I notice where things are and what goes on on the floor, and to my disbelief two tables adjacent to us, with couples seated half an hour after us, received their pizzas before us. When we were almost done with the pizza, the sea urchin arrived and that was the biggest dissappointment, it was a crusty slice of a baguette divided into three pieces with some pickled seafood (I imagine the seaurchin) and some sprouted wheat on top. I expected something grilled or similar to the squid, because that is how the waiter sold me on the sea urchin - if you love squid, you will love the sea urchin, however I did not see any similarity betweeen a meaty squid with the paste of sea urchin I was served.
Lastly my husband asked me to order a dessert so I could have my surprise. The waiter brought me the spicy carrot cake I ordered (did not feel the "spicy" in it). The cake serving was again very small. If you put your middle finger and index finger together you will get the size of the carrot cake, and they charged us $8.50 for it. There was a candle on the cake and the waiter just left it in front of me, no "happy birthday", nada. I ate the cake fast and left the last $ of the card as a tip as I am not planning to come back,

In summary, very bad service, we were ignored, and our baby was not safe. Food came out very slowly (on a Monday night!) and  even though the fresh ingredients filled our mouths with different tastes (nice, but not impressive), everything was just overpriced. I left the restaurant angry and disgusted with the way we were treated.

So much hype about this place - didn't really  live up to it.

Food was mediocre. The menu was limited. The waiter wasn't very helpful.

A good option if you're vegan. If you're not there's no reason to go here.

Just returned to Gather, for dinner this time, for my 30th birthday. Went with a few friends and had an AMAZING time. The food, drinks, service, and ambiance were all 5 stars. I finally got a chance to try the Vegan Charcuterie plate, and it definitely lives up to the hype. Makes you look at veggies in a totally different way. We also got the green garlic pizza, the young bbq chicken, and the baby artichokes. Fantastic! I got the Huerta Vida cocktail that has habanero oil in it. Delish! Can't wait to go back for another special occasion :)

Oh god, that mussel and bacon pizza---man I still daydream about it.  It was on soft and delicious crust with juicy little mussels and crispy bacon.  It also had a crisp garnish of seaweed on top.  It may not sound THAT good, but it WAS.  

We also ordered the Vegan appetizer plate (I can't spell that out, don't hate me).  It was fun to try and figure out the flavors and textures. It's also visually stunning!  The atmosphere is so beautifully decorated: lots of smooth wood and other natural-feeling decor!  A+ in that department.

Go here for a nice dinner with the folks or with friends before a show.  It's worth the money!

Met by pleasant lady who stated her outdoor seating was full. Finally apparently with deep regret she escorted us to the outside area which had plenty of open space.  Service mediocre to crummy food good of course at that price you can't miss reasonably decent.  If you've got money to burn and don't mind crummy service it's your place.

Gather is fantastic! Beautiful decor, chirpy service, great location. You feel kind of like you're in nature without the dirtiness. 

I first came here in Gather's earlier days for lunch. I remember loving our salad and sandwich but wishing I could have also tried the pizza. 

Recently came back for brunch. I was really sad that the current menu is not reflected on the website because I had pored over it and committed myself to getting something only to find that it was NOT offered anymore! Sadness...had to change my mind really quickly and just went for boring scrambled eggs on levain toast. It was fantastic because I decided to splurge and get the chile sausage side for $5 when my eggs and toast were only $6. We were curious how many sausages I'd get for that price, or how big the sausage would be. Turns out it was a dinky little thing with a side of greens. Anyway I ended up feeling very pleased with my meal, as the sausage was delicious and complemented the eggs + toast perfectly! Every bite was amazing - a little bit of toast, some scrambled eggs, a chunk of sausage, and fresh greens. Twas a great brunch.

My Americano was so-so. Their alcoholic beverages look delectable!! I'd go for that next time instead of caffeine. 

Overall I think Gather is probably a better place to go for dinner or a hearty lunch, just so you can get the pizza. I'm still determined to try it!

Having eaten at Gather on a number of occasions, I will note that the level of service I receive seems to vary greatly based on who I am dining with, our choice of attire, and time of day. I am tempted to knock this place down to three stars because I have had some awful experiences with service within the last four to five months.

However, the food is ridiculously good. If I could marry food, I would marry every one of the vegan "charcuterie" plates I have eaten. I am also in love with the tomato pizza.  I love how seasonal this place is and how they care for and highlight the ingredients.

So I can't hate on the place. Just don't expect the best service, and enjoy it if you get it!
