Food was really good but the service was pretty slow. Keep an eye on the clock because we were almost late to our show at the Berkeley Rep even though we were there early to have a leisurely dinner. Everyone was delicious.

Although our food was very tasty, and the hostess/bar staff were very kind, the food made me horribly sick.  The pizza we ordered tasted a bit funny but we ate it anyway.  I ate a little more for breakfast (it's pizza, after all) the next day.  I spent the next 3 days in bed with a stomach bug.  We noticed that the pizza leftovers smelled rancid and threw them away.

I wrote to the restaurant to let them know and their response was essentially, we're sorry but it wasn't us...no one else got sick.

with all due respect, Gather, when two people who hadn't seen each other in over 2 months get sick at precisely the same time after eating a meal at your restaurant, I suspect it is you...

I won't be going back anytime soon...
Meh..... food was unsatisfying. It tasted ok I guess. Fancy hippy food is what this restaurant serves in my opinion.

I was going to give this place 3 stars ... but then I decided to give it a 4th star for pure quirkiness. 'Cause I like quirkiness.

The dining room is a pretty funky place: all rustic wooden tables and chairs, simple shelves on the walls holding various jars of preserved vegetables, lighting fixtures hanging down from the ceiling on long cords (some of these lighting figures had "shades" that looked as if they were made from wire crab nets/traps), etc. The building that houses the restaurant has a dramatic curve where one would expect a corner, which gives the whole restaurant a neat, unusual feel. I think there's an additional dining room in the back, but I never went back there, so I don't know what it's like.

This certainly isn't somewhere I'd want to eat every day, because it's a bit strange, but I did enjoy it enough to want to go back sometime again.

We had heard that the signature menu choice of the restaurant was the "Artisanal Plate" of "vegan 'charcuterie,'" so we ordered that. It consisted of:

- tartar of tomato and corn, roasted tomato polenta
- eggplant "brandade," braised Jimmy Nardello peppers, saffron braised olives
- bruschetta, crispy tofu skin, avocado, tomato, smoked garlic "aioli"
- carpaccio of watermelon radish and turnip, horseradish salsa verde, grapes, grated almond
- summer mushroom pate, grilled nebrodini mushrooms

I particularly loved the tartar (I'm a big fan of corn), though I was surprised at how much I enjoyed the eggplant "brandade." I'm not usually a fan of eggplant, but that's because of the slimy texture. Since this was pureed, the sliminess was gone and all I got was the taste, which I liked. For our entrees, we both ordered pizzas, but neither of us could eat more than a couple slices, because the appetizer had been so substantial, so we had lots of leftovers for the next day's lunch. My pizza included the freshest, most flavorful basil leaves I've ever tasted. Incredible!

One thing I like about the menu here is that there are tons of tasty, interesting vegetarian options ... and yet there are good meat options, too. I was surprised to see a hamburger, for example, on the same menu with the "vegan charcuterie." I like restaurants that make it easy to eat out with friends of different tastes and diet limitations, so I appreciate the diversity.

My husband and I went here last night. We arrived at 7:30 and the place was absolutely packed on a Wednesday. (I guess Berkeley is recession-proof.) Luckily we had reservations and were seated right away. 

For as busy as the place was, the service was really good. The bussers, food expediter, and our server were all really attentive, friendly, fast, and efficient. Also, we really liked the ambiance. The only drawback is the tables are far too close to each other and you can hear your neighbors' conversations whether you want to or not. Unfortunately for us, we were seated next to a very demanding woman who spent the entire time pissing and moaning about EVERYTHING. So that kind of put a damper on our evening. 

The food was alright. We started with the vegan charcuterie, which we both thought was fabulous--very unique and innovative offerings. My husband had the kale pizza with chanterelle mushrooms, which was very tasty. I was a bit disappointed in my entree--the bean ragout. The crispy artichokes on top were amazing, but the ragout was pretty much what I make myself at home all of the time. I wish I had opted for the rock cod they were offering that night. The people next to us ordered it, and it looked delicious. 

We'll be back. This restaurant has a lot of potential.

An organic restaurant that supports local farmers!? Winner! I tried their Guanciale pizza and it was pretty good! I felt like I was having dinner and breakfast in 1 b/c of the eggs on the pizza. I tried their chocolate budino and chocolate triamble pumpkin tart. Both so delicious! The place is very cute & I'll definitely be coming back. Only downside is that parking is hard to find.

Was very excited to go and so were the the other couple.  

Environment very comfortable, warm and nice.  Able to talk at the table which was very nice now that we are getting up in years.

The vegan charcuterie was very good though for a party of four healthy and hungry eaters I think that the portions of each items could be increased...perhaps limit it by one and make the portions bigger since not everyone got to taste each item....trying to cut the beet ended up with that person picking it up whole.

Both guys enjoyed their plates - turnip thing and I can't even remember what my husband had, but he liked it.

I'm only writing about what wasn't good because that is important to readers and the restaurant.

Both salads were terrible.  I had the kale salad and my friend had the chicory.  Since I have know this woman for 20 years I felt comfortable saying: This is terrible to which she replied so is mine.   We both agreed it was due to the temperature.  It was like eating a bunch of soggy, wet and cold stuff. There was no flavor....all that you experienced was cold and wet.  Due to the temperature being too cold nothing tasted savory.  The fried capers were no where to be tasted and the cheese on both was very bland.  I cook with kale all the time and chop it in my salads, so I thought I was gonna get a delicious salad with "yum" tasting treats of fried capers and savory cheese and quality olive oil, but it was the worst tasting concoction of kale I have ever had.  Ditto on her salad.

My advice....get it out of the bins in the refrigerator....room temperature is the way to go with both of these salads.
The food made up for unexceptional service.  Very healthy/hippie-type food though, very "northwestern" cuisine, delicious to a native like myself ;)
Great location.  Limited menu.  Expectations were high.  Prefer Oliveto when coming to the East Bay.

I've eaten once at Gather.  We waited about 10mins before someone showed up with 2 glasses of complimentary champagne, apologizing for the long wait.  Moments later, a complimentary appetizer was placed in front of us.  We were amazed by the service.  I expect to wait at least 10mins at a crowded restaurant on a Friday night.  Food was great too.  Great concept, I hope more restaurants follow their lead.  I'll be back.

I feel like a failure for being unable to jump on the bandwagon but I've had breakfast once and dinner twice at Gather.  

Yes the vegan charcuterie plate is interesting to look at, and two of the four items were quite tasty, but everything else was just boring.  I don't want to have to eat here again.  I don't care how prestigious it may be to go here these days: Gather left me limp.  

I've ordered kombucha, granola and yogurt, an egg scramble, the charcuterie plate, a stuffed squash? Damned if I can remember, the dinner was so unmemorable. My brother got a hamburger, someone got a pizza...yeah.

This restaurant just popped up on me on day. Like wow a new restaurant and its nice and big. I looked up info on their website and became equally impressed. So yesterday after trying to fiqure out what I was going to eat Gather came to mind. For some reason I really wanted a good burger.

 Although I wanted to try many things on the menu I was solo and didn't want my eyes playing tricks on my stomach so I started with the sauted vegetable which was rabi ??? i think . It was good and stopped my hunger pangs but I found it slightly difficult to chew.

Main attraction was the burger juicy meaty gooy goodness its suggested to be served med-rare and I concur it was amazing it comes with a little arugula on the side which I put inside of the burger giving it even more kick the shoe string fries also helds it own not like other ff that once cooled down start to taste like cardboard they kept getting better...Everyone around me seemed pleased with there dishes  and experience overall.

My server was knowledgable and friendly. I will be back hopefully with someone else so I wont look like a pig...

What a gigantic disappointment!  My family went twice--the first time was superb.  We had the vegetarian appetizer, burger, another appetizer that I forget the name of but was battered and fried, a fish dish and lots of wine and local berry drinks.  After this experience, we were determined to return and make this a regular dinner place for us.  Life got in the way and it took us about six months to return in the spring. 

Every dish that we ordered was greasy and tasteless.  We again ordered the vegetarian appetizer, the burger and this time went with a spring pizza.  Each dish was literally dripping oil off of the plate--including the pizza and the burger!  

For a place to be considered good, I think they have to at least be consistent in the quality of their food.  Not to mention, if I am going to drop $100 on a meal for three, it had better be excellent, and at the least, palatable.

Truly disappointed and put off with this restaurant.  I applaud their philosophy, but find that presentation and trendiness do not make up for good tasting food.

I just can't see spending a bucket of money and not knowing if it will be good or bad.  Spend your money elsewhere.

I like Gather.  You can be a carnivore, like me, and eat vegetarian here.  And like it.  One of the most novel plates served here, or anywhere for that matter, is their vegetarian charcuterie.  Five or six small servings of vegetables served on a board.  It is perhaps inevitable that some of these would be more pleasing than others.  I have been here twice and loved two out of five, liked one of five, and two were just OK (to me).  

A main of tofu skin braciole  was composed of roasted winter vegetables, braised lentils, mushrooms, and chestnut-truffle vinaigrette.  It was nice enough although I thought that the braising made the lentils more mushy than I would have preferred.  

But overall I had a dinner that was strictly vegetarian and felt good about it.  From me that's high praise.

I recently returned to Gather for dinner, and want to update my review.  Gather is rather expensive, particularly considering the portion size.  We had the vegan charcuterie ($18) and a couple of the pizzas ($16-18).  Yes, they were overpriced; however, all of the items were very good.  In addition, locally-sourced, organic ingredients tend to be expensive.  Although Gather is an "omnivore" restaurant, their offerings are slanted towards the vegan/vegetarian, which is nice.  The vegan and gluten-free items are clearly noted on the menu as well.  If you don't focus too much on the price, and instead take solace in the fact that you can eat a meat-free meal made with top quality ingredients, you definitely will enjoy your meal.

overall, a great place to have a nice meal.

our table started off with the vegan charcuterie, the supposed "essence" of the place, and the pomegranate kambucha (describe dto us as fermented tea) to drink. the charcuterie was a nice introduction, and indeed, a nice display of the the chef's creative ingenuity. now that i've seen/had it once though, i do not feel the need to order it again. the kambucha also was adventurous, but again, did not fuel a re-order need. the other appetizers i sampled, kale salad and polenta friend mushrooms, neither intrigued nor blew away. needless to say, the meal at this point was pleasant, but not yet memorable.

then came the entree though: whole young chicken under a brick. just delicious. actually, my usual appetite would have been filled after the bevy of appetizers we ordered, but i surprised even myself and devoured this plate. roasted chicken so juicy i've never experienced before and i would come back to gather just for this.

for dessert, we went for variety and ordered one of each. the dessert chef was so cute. he was so appreciative of our large order, he sent out plates of fresh cookies, hot out of the oven for us. unfortunately, i have to be honest and say that although the desserts were good, the simple chocolate chip cookies were the best he did.

all in all, if i was the type to become a regular at a place, i would become one here just for that young chicken. the pizzas looked enticing too though... w ill have to try some the next time i'm here.

Overall, my wife and I were impressed with our experience here this past Saturday night.  There were some hits and some misses but the hits were amazing.

Let's start with the misses...

Yellowtail crudo - nori miso purée, chicharrones, radish, jalapenos, green almonds, chive blossoms (gf) - 
- I cannot recommend this dish, it just didn't do it for either of us...

Barbecued young chicken - dried fava bean, fennel, greens, olives (gf)
- I ate the whole thing, but the flavor profile didn't wow me on this one...mid west barbecue flavor meets mediterranean flavors...is what i took from it...it looked appetizing though...

Seared panisse - stinging nettles, braised Black, Trumpet mushrooms, San Joaquin Gold-pinenut salsa (gf)
- This dish was amazing...the truffle mushroom flavor with the parmesan cheese and the polenta like panisse was just awesome...

Spring vegetables - sea palm, sheep's milk ricotta, crispy black quinoa, horseradish (gf)
- This dish was the highlight of the meal...what a way to showcase local fresh produce...from crispy quinoa to horseradish sauce...the presentation was beautiful as well as the flavor.  This is how vegetables should be eaten...if you're not a fan a vegetables, this will change your mind.

i'm not a vegetarian by any means but my favorite dishes of the night were the vegetarian ones...

Gather is one of my favorite go-to places in the East Bay and I never get tired of it.

There is a genuine sense of cuisine.  Many places have good food, fresh ingredients, and so on, but the way it comes together is plain.  Nothing worth going out for.   At Gather, the whole is often greater than the sum of the parts - it's always interesting and at times sublime.  

I'm not vegan, but the ever-changing vegan charcuterie is a inventive delight.  The green garlic pizza was one of the best I've ever tried (though other pizzas on offer, while very good, aren't quite at that level).  I remember eating a young chicken once that was crispy outside, yet wonderfully moist inside.  

One of the top draws for me, pedestrian as it might seem, is the burger.  I had a theory for many years that a burger at a sit-down restaurant could never truly be great....no matter what the restaurant, it was always a variation on the same theme, and could never hold a candle to the classic likes of In n Out Burger.  Gather proved me wrong with an outstanding hamburger where everything clicks - the special home-made ketchup, the bun, the way the meat is cooked.  Yow.  A must try.

I find myself wishing some of the specials could become permanent fixtures...I remember eating some chilaquiles for brunch once and they were fantastic.  They avoided the typical tex-mex style pitfalls and offered something truly fresh.

The environment is also quite casual and pleasant.  Very enjoyable.

if i can describe gather in one word, it would be FRESH!!

the restaurant itself is very bright and welcoming and everyone who worked here was so nice, our waiter especially who you can tell is very passionate about the food. we went with two of his recommendations which i really enjoyed.

halibut tartare (special of the day) - it was with a pea puree and what our waiter called "uni butter" the halibut was extremely fresh! and you can tell (plus you see them) that all the sauces and puree were made to order. uni sauces were very light so that it doesn't over power the fish. my only complaint was that there was not enough!

spring vegetables - i love salads but i'm not one to order it often at a restaurant. we were going for two pizzas already so decided to order a salad as well to balance things out. this one was the other dish our waiter recommended. it was so fresh and delicious! definitely the most unique salad i've ever had. there was a mix of baby carrots, radish, peas, potatoes, and a different greens and flowers. it came with a light horseradish sauce, house made ricotta, and crispy quinoa. again, neither the sauce or ricotta was over powering.  a bite of the baby carrots with some ricotta over it topped with the crispy quinoa... loved the contrast of all the different textures.

spicy tomato pizza - i normally love meat on my pizza, but this one was my favorite of the two we got. you definitely need to like the taste of olives to like this pizza because that dominated the flavor of this pizza. the thin crust pizza was nice and crunchy, even though it did get soggy later

pork sausage pizza - i love sausages on my pizza! however as much as i like big pieces of what i like, i wish the lumps of sausages were smaller and more spread out on the pizza because other than a few bites of sausage, there wasn't much to the pizza. the chile salsa they put on it was good too.

overall it was a great dinner. i think the pizza were a little over-hyped for me but i would still say gather is definitely a must try place. food did not disappoint, great service, and there is even complimentary sparkling water! next time i think i want to try their lunch because it seems like there is more things i like there. menu does change often so make sure you check the online menu first and not drooling over a picture of something that's not there the day you go in :P

I've been waiting to try Gather for quite some time now and the reservations or wait time has always been too long! We swung by on cinco de mayo in hopes of getting a table and voila! They had an open table out on the patio for 4 of us. Even though Gather is known for it's vegan, gluten free, and healthy menu, we opted for the burger from Prather ranch. It was amazing. Next time we go, we want to try the pizza that has cashew butter substituted for cheese

This place is so BUSY. I went during lunch time and had their pizza which was SO good. However, service was kind of slow but the food made up for it. They have a unique interior and a nice bathroom. Haha random I know but I was so impressed by the bathroom LOL

I visited this restaurant with my boyfriend for his birthday and was pleasantly surprised,  We were both amazed that it was packed on a Monday night the week of Christmas.  I loved how it is located right on the corner and makes it every visible for passersby.  We had a great appetizer to start, the kale salad, it was so delicious and had so many great flavors in such a simple salad.  I had the red quinoa risotto and my boyfriend had the young chicken under a brick.  The risotto was great, very flavorful but the chicken was amazing.  I am a pesco-tarian, have been for about four years now, but will sometimes eat chicken.  It was so succulent and so moist that it didn't taste like other chicken I have had.  The waiter who served us was great and find this to be such a great find because it is organic and local, a huge plus.  I will make an effort to come out here again, maybe for their brunch in the near future.
trash!

If I were to take out of town guests to introduce fresh local produce based gourmet restaurant typical of berkeley, then this will be it. Not chez panisse as you have to plan too much in advance. Try their kale salad and the charcuterie as well as the squid, octopus special, if they have it. Also suggest the non alcoholic kamboocha which is like russian kvas except 0% alcohol.

I first tried some bites from Gather at a yelp event in Berkeley. the samples I had were tasty, so I made a mental note to check out the actual restaurant. it's been forever since the event, but paul and I finally got the chance to come out to Gather as part of my food and booze filled birthday weekend.

the interior of the restaurant is very cozy and warm. since we came on a weeknight there wasn't much of a wait. the one missing star is for the slightly limited menu. I understand it's Berkeley, so they cater to a vegetarian/vegan/crazy hippie crowd, but I was a little disappointed there wasn't a few more meat inclusive items on the menu.

we started with the toasted masa and burrata. I didn't care much for the burrata, but I think that's just a personal taste thing for me, Paul loved it. I thought the masa would come out like a polenta-type cake, with chorizo and corn and what not.. but it was a pasta! super surprising and VERY good. it had a distinct masa flavor and was balanced well with chorizo, corn, tomatoes, and sauce.

we also split the summer squash pizza and the burger, with all the fixings [heirloom tomato, lettuce, housemade pickles, bacon]. the burger is huge, juicy, tasty, and all around goodness. the real winner here is the pizza. oh my godddd, I didn't know something vegetarian could taste so freaking good. slices of summer squash, feta cheese, a nice tangy tomato sauce, and pesto. simple, but absolutely delicious. 

I would definitely come back for more pizza, and to try some more crazy Berkeley cuisine.
Some of the *best* pizza I've ever tasted, and the lattes are very good, too, and pretty!

So the host tells us that there is a 45 min wait for a regular table, but there are two seats at the counter. When we frown at the idea, he goes on to say that "it is like dinner and a show: you get to see the cooks work in the kitchen". So we reluctantly agree and he then proceeds to seat us at the counter... right in front of an industrial-size meat slicer, obstructing our view of anything else for the entire dinner. So whose idea of "dinner and show" is this? Maybe to Hannibal Lecter, but not to us.
Other than this appalling marketing stunt, the food was disappointing. The bread was forgettable. The salmon tartare was fresh but not mind-blowing, just OK. The green pizza was so greasy, it was inedible after two bites. And even though I don't mind spicy food, the BBQ chicken was way too spicy (as a reference point, I can eat the "spicy" curry at Japanese restaurants, which is pretty darn hot).
If I only ate with my eyes, they would get 5 stars: the presentation of all the dishes was fantastic. I'll give them that much. But it's just fairy dust. Overall, I will not come back.

Walk in at 1pm on saturday to, it will be a five minute wait.  My friend says this is very Berkeley, you wait while there are 10+ tables ready for you to be seated at.  The next person comes in and the host says 15 minute wait.

Sit down order pizza salad, crust is good so is the cilantro pesto. salad was ok to slightly overdressed stone fruit salad.  I probably would not go back especially since i only went with the 30% off blackboardeats.com deal.

I really do just love this place. It's easy to get something simple and delicious for a reasonable price, or go a little bit fancier and get a more expensive and extensive meal. I highly recommend this place to anybody looking for good food. If you appreciate food made with care, this place is for you. 

I also took photos: http://www.simoneanne.com/journal/2011/12/gather-restaurant-berkeley-california/

Second visit, same comments! Really good cocktails (although we were disappointed to learn that they don't do any bourbon drinks at all - goodbye Manhattan! - because they cannot source an organic bourbon), terrific ingredients in well-prepared dishes, and very good service. Too Berkeley for some, but I don't find their philosophy or their execution too precious. If you haven't been, check it out!

Perfect lighting, stunning food presentation, exquisite and unique flavors and incredible cocktails. Imbibed an eye-opening Corpse Reviver #2, savored the Kale salad and indulged in the most perfectly cooked squid (not a bit chewy!). Ended the meal with a decadent dried fig ice cream. In love.

I had lunch with a friend recently and was disappointed. The food wasn't bad, it just didn't live up to the hype. We shared the kale salad and it was WAY oversalted, which I mentioned to our server. The one I make at home is better. (And the Kale Salad at Yoshi's/Jack London Square is excellent!!) The carrot soup was good-but nothing special. We shared the stinging nettle pizza, and it was very good. The service was fine but the table arrangement at Gather is awkward. We sat at a table near the "inner circle" and the server had to reach over the railing, quite awkwardly, to give us our plates. Difficult for him and awkward, and not a very well thought out arrangement. The tables were too close together for him to easily reach us from the other side.
Gather is out of the way for me, I wouldn't go back.

Meh. I just don't really like the haute cuisine of the world. There are many flavors that I still dislike, and the upper eschelon of food usually has so much creativity that it ends up with something that I didn't want in my mouth. 

So, what to do? Vodka! Whiskey! I'll gladly cough up $10 for some creative top shelf libation, if we're already splurging on a once-a-season dinner. I got a moscow mule, of course with a modern twist and high end ingredients. Meh. Much better cocktails have been had. I can take a powerful ginger beer, like Reed's, and put a bit of vodka in it. That's all I tasted. After having floating dried cammomile flowers in LA and Old Ford's in Albany, this was a let down. 

The food wasn't very veggie friendly, eventhough Gather's premise is extremely green. Saving oil on transport is great! Saving land and water - well, this is more a comment on the customers than the restaurant, I suppose. It sure seemed like they were trying a lot harder with their pork and beef options than with their veggie stuffs. We had two great salads. I had an interesting pizza with charred chiles and corn. Drunk, very hungry, I ate. Not what I wanted, I made the best of it. The corn on the pizza was good. The crust and cheese were good enough. Meh. The salads were really great, but since J didn't want my chile laden pizza, she had to make do with those salads. Dessert? Meh. Pretty, fancy, but we should've skipped it. 

Didn't eat the sea food our guest ate. She said it was overpowered with picante heat though. Meh. 

 For $120 for 3 people, we expected much more quality. Service wasn't what you expect from a gourmet type of place. More like decent wait staff at any decent chain restaurant, with a healthy drizzle of the pretension that you can expect at a gourmet bistro. 

Worth a try. Maybe the meat makes it worth while. I love that they wear their locavore on their sleeves, but life's too short to return here.
Farm egg pizza is the best.  Wonderful lunch with outdoor seating.
Excellent service, timing and execution was perfect, small menu, the house vegan appetizer was amazing, the acid jazz on the stereo was annoying, none of the deserts blew my mind, truly great coffee.

This place is ridiculous. We went for brunch, which took over 45 minutes from order to table to arrive. This is odd, considering we both ordered salads and sides. Our second round of drinker arrived well into eating, and the waitress seemed distracted and a little tipsy herself. Do you want to spend $80 for poorly prepared brunch with awkward service? If so, Gather is just the place for you.

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday dinner last year. For drinks, I ordered the Bee Sting and my boyfriend had the Corpse Reviver #2. The drink were strong and delicious-- my highest praises to the bartender.  I would come just to go to the bar, and am often suggesting it to friends when they want to meet up for drinks. 

For the meal, I had Vegan Charcuterie and my boyfriend had the pizza (because he is not an adventurous eater). I loved the Vegan Charcuterie which was full of  amazing flavors and textures.  Loved the fact they have more than one vegetarian entree and the local-organic-sustainable vision for the restaurant, but wish they had a fish on the menu the night I went. My boyfriend's pizza was superb, prefect amount of char, and had an amazing bubbly, thick, soft crust. 

I can't wait to go back and try more things on the menu.
Also, can't wait to try brunch here!

Negatives: We had reservations and got there on perfect time (I was worried we were going to be late), but still had to wait 15 mins for a table. When they did seat us, it was at an out-of-the-way corner table behind a pillar. Nothing on the dessert menu that night looked particular memorable so we decided to go elsewhere for dessert.
Great food, very good staff, nice venue.  All good.
The service was good at first but a bit slow towards the end.  The pizza was good and the salad was fresh.  Its a great place for vegetarians or want to Be's like me!

I've eaten here many times because I live next door. Guests -- esp. from out of the area -- are always intrigued when they hear an award-winning restaurant is right downstairs.

The food is good, portions very small and prices high for what you get.  A salad can literally consist of four leaves of lettuce sprinkled with sprinkles of seaseed for seven or eight bucks -- it is artfully arranged so it looks like a full salad but it amounts to no more than a taste, a very few bites.  I have a hard time believing their profit margins are so tight that they couldn't put in, um, just a tad more lettuce?

And they are bad neighbors. Their employees sometimes drink after work - out in the patio, loud, drunk and noisy. People live here -- includings lots of kids. Nobody who lives next door to anywhere wants to listen to drunk waitstaff and cooks loudly partying to wind down after work.

Tonight, wed, May 23rd, a couple patrons with musical instruments went out into the darkened patio, which was not being used to serve food, and started jamming. The patio was not lit -- just musicians jamming randoly next to several six and eight story apartment buildings on warm evening with many windows open.  People matter, right? If it matteres how the animals served at the restaurant matter, shouldn't human neighbors matter too? Nice music, actually ...  . but a couple hundred residents were likely asleep at 11:30 pm on a weeknight with jobs and school in the morning. And it's warm these days so folks open their windows.

The musicians stopped as soon as I went down but I should not have had to get dressed, after their music awoke me, and then go down the block to ask them to stop. Why wouldn't Gather manage their space more professionally? The Gather staff knows they don't have a noise permit to play live music at 11:30 at night. Even with a noise permit, music adjacent to resident space legally is required to end at 10 p.m. -- unless they have a special occasion exception which they are only supposed to get a very few times a year.  Like I say, the musicians were polite and stopped but what the frak was wrong with Gather staff?  They never should have let it happen.

I called the cops, too, but this is not a top priority response -- Berkeley cops are more worried about Chief Meehan's son's iPhone than the Berkeley cops worry about tax paying residents trying tio sleep with illegal noise going on.

Good food. Lousy neighbors.

The Fried Green Beans were amazingly delicious and the pizza was super good too! I liked that they had both sparkling and "steel" water.

Their decorations were very unique and awesome, for instance, the overhead lamp had a wine bottle as a shade. 

I went here for my mom's birthday, so we brought a cake in. There was supposedly a $2.50/person plating fee, but they waved it because they didn't tell us. They also said that no outside food was allowed, which contradicts their plating fee.

Overall, the food was delicious and they handled the situation well. The waiter was very friendly, too!

I didn't yet have a go-to Cesar-style (informal, sharable plates, savory, open plan) spot in the BART neighborhood of the Gourmet Ghetto until I found Gather, which fills that role just fine, albeit it's no Cesar. My only complaint, sitting at the chef's counter, is that the cramped layout meant passersby smashed into our chairs every couple minutes.

My friend & I enjoyed this place. It had great ambiance, good healthy food that was well prepared, and wonderful staff.  The decor was simple, airy, and popped.  We especially liked the recycled belt booths. The host Yusuf made us feel welcomed and right at home.    Our carrot soup was creamy and had nice accents. The pizza was light and yet hearty.  Every plate we saw around us looked good too.  We will definitely come back here!
Nice ambiance, great natural wine on tap and enjoyed a great pizza...I think it was called the farm? It had egg, prosciutto and spice. Artichokes were bland.

I was really looking forward to trying this place after receiving several recommendations.  Unfortunately, I felt that the portions were way too small.  We got the vegan charcuterie which had unique flavors but just was not big enough for the price.  We also had a baby artichoke entree that was different then an average vegetable plate but again was not plentiful enough.  

The bread served with the entree was tasteless. Actually it almost tasted stale.  I was disappointed that bread was not given to us while waiting for our food but after trying it I was glad they hadn't.

For dessert we had chai tea with almond milk that was tasteless.  They use Pacific almond milk which has ingredients and a taste that I don't care for.  Making there own would have made all the difference.  If they had to use packaged almond milk, Trader Joe's is the best.  

Finally, we had a scoop of the cashew cinnamon ice cream which was to die for!  It was the best nut "ice cream" I have had anywhere.  It blew Cafe Gratitude's ice cream away.  

For Berkeley it is 4 stars but for San Francisco residents, 3 stars.

You know how you get that perfect bite with perfectly proportioned combination of tastes?  Well, I had that bite of Guanciale & carmelized onion pizza...and let it roll around in my mouth for awhile, savoring the marriage of the two.
The avocado salad was a nice presentation, and looked better than it tasted.  Our server recommended the Chocolate Pumpkin tart w/lemon Whipped cream.  It felt like too many flavors competing against each other.  I will go for the citrus cake next time.  Ambiance is very hip, and lots of natural light that enters through all of the windows that surround the restaurant.  Service felt very spotty, where we would have to wait a long time to get our coffee.

I was really excited to try this place.  I had heard the burger was amazing.  The burger was just ok.  The fries were also average and the salad it was served with was really salty and not very good at all.  My friends strawberry salad was also just average.  The service was pretty average, nothing bad nothing exceptional. Overall I thought the whole experience was pretty average right down to the decor.  I'd give it one more try. But I wouldn't go out of my way to eat there or to take anybody there. 

To be fair, I only had the burger and I tried my friends strawberry salad.   Maybe the other menus are stand-outs.

Maybe doesn't quite live up to the hype, but after eating there with a friend a couple of times, I have to say I found it consistently very good.  The soups we have tried were exceptional- flavorful, unusual, well-balanced.  The wood fired pizza was terrific.  Last time we had a salad with grilled squid and sous vide vegetables that was unique and delicious, and a pork sandwhich that was cooked over hay that was also incredible.  The one dish I was slightly disappointed by was a kale salad that lacked depth and punch.  Service is friendly if a little hyper, and I wish the tables were not so close together and the place wasn't quite so noisy.

AMBIANCE: I love it. A ton of windows and natural light. Lots of smooth wood & plants everywhere. Clean, too!

SERVICE: Good.

FOOD:
- Their pizza w/egg was delicious. (their pizzas are all thin crust) 
- Burger was great, too... but apparently not available for weekday lunches.
- The braised mushroom sandwich (weekday lunch) with cashew-pepper "cheese" was delicious.
- Pork sandwich was moist with a generous mound of pork.

My one criticism is that the menu is a bit limited - whenever I go, there are usually just 1-2 items that are calling out, "Order me!"  But the ones I've tried have really hit the spot.

The inventiveness of the dishes that come out of the kitchen were fantastic, and a major plus for vegetarians and vegans. I really appreciate the care that the chef puts into creating a menu with truly seasonal dishes. We shared the vegan charcuterie, spicy pumpkin soup, and chicken fried squash, all of which were delicious. I am sad to report that the service was poor and was at odds with the efforts of the kitchen. I will definitely be back for the food in hopes that they work out the kinks with the wait staff.

Day: Lazy Sunday brunch

Parking: Not bad. There were plenty within a few blocks away. 

Food: 
Country ham 
3 star - a bit disappointing when I was expecting a big sausage with nice flavors and egg. I got an over cooked greens and salty water-ly sauce. Hm...won't do that again. 

Knoll Farms fig Pizza
4 star - yum. Nice balance of pancetta and fig then tons of greens so you get a bitter taste. Nice crust. 

The Brunch Pizza 
4 star - simple. 

Roasted corn mushroom Pizza
3 star - so so. 

Service - great

Overall - Nice place to go for a lazy Sunday brunch.

This place was amazing! Being vegan, there aren't many places that give you the fine dinning feel and actually have such great food at a reasonable price.  Not all of their food is vegan either! They have totally perfected their craft.

Vegan or not, try the spicy tomato pizza and "misto fritto"!!!!!
Art on a plate. Local, organic, orgasm in my mouth. WOW. GO THERE. Nuff said.

I have been to Gather many many times and my love and admiration for the food and staff just keeps growing. The chef is so caring, creative and talented. His high standard is in everything - if you order a salad w/ fruit in it - the fruit is perfectly ripe!  Spice levels are perfect, textures are perfect, things are cooked properly, everything is pristine, fresh and flavorful. and i love that there are always great meat choices as well as vegan and vegetarian. i went with a large group recently - all with different food preferences and EVERYBODY was happy! I don't get why some reviews complain about staff. They are so knowledgeable, passionate about the food and super friendly and professional. I find the service great, no matter what day, or time we are there, whether we are at the counter, bar, table, or outside. 5 stars for both food and service!!!  I love Gather!!!!!!!!!!!

I wish that i had the same great Experience as most of the other reviewers. But that was not the case. the decor was  stiff and wanting, likewise the service. we were there for a small bite to eat, and drink a warm cup of tea. the weather was seriously cold on sat. the 9th of April, Stanford and cal track meet. Stanford Rules.... back to the review. after my wife and I and our friends placed the order, Tea ,Coffee and salad. I actully ordered a mix green with chicken. when the order arrived i noticed the salad had a few sprinkles of chicken. ok i thought being the Cool guy that i am, don't trip... so i asked the waiter or was it the busser, for Bread and oil. and guess what I received... toast. so i thought what a misunderstanding?  well, I flagged down the waiter or was it the.. no it was the waiter. and asked if i could get  fresh bread and not toast. Yes the waiter said , and off he went with the toast. i left the place to pay the meter.. which took about 10-15 min. back in the place  i noticed their was no bread. so you know what i did , Right.... i flagged ...you know the Rest! Long story short. I received my second plate of bread and it was seriously stale! There was no Misunderstanding.. the reason for the Toast.. too cheap to offer freshly baked Bread on a Daily basis! What a F&%*# Shame! I will never Return to Gather! By the way the second plate of  bread was placed in the Microwave.What a &%*.... you know the rest!

Great atmosphere and delicious food! I've tried two sandwiches (both vegan) here, the mushroom and the "B.L.T." I would completely recommend the mushroom burger to anyone! The mushrooms were marinated perfectly, and it was very yummy. The "B.L.T" was okay, but I wouldn't get it again. The "bacon" was crisped tofu sheets, and it wasn't nearly as flavorful. I also tasted their thinly cut fries and ketchup. The fries are salty (just how I like 'em) and scrumptious, while the ketchup is unique and so good you could eat it by itself.

This place gets a 2.5. Jose is a harsh critic. I wanted to give it a 3 but when you think that we went to Va Da Vi and spent about the same and portions were similar...well, Va Da Vi was a 5. 
Anyway, Gather's decor is warm. The staff is unpolished to say the least. Our server was friendly but unattentive and slow. 

The food...I appreciate their dedication to local, gluten-free, vegan.
We started with the vegan charcuterie- there were some great tastes. It made veggies interesting, especially for those who weren't interested before. 
Braised pork cheeks were a disappointment. I couldn't even tell that it was pork. The preparation and seasoning did nothing to bring out the pork flavor. The polenta was really creamy and I liked that as opposed to the usual dry stuff. 
Cinnamon braised lamb was also unremarkable. I love lamb and they did not know how to bring out its unique flavor. 
The best dish of the night was the tequila lime sorbet. It was good. 

If you are looking for veggies with an edge, give Gather a try. Don't eat any meat here as it doesn't seem to be something they're skilled in preparing. The table next to us was also unimpressed with the quinoa risotto.
Everything was great, including the service.  The kale salad was my absolute favorite!

i dove into what must be the best sandwich on earth....the braised mushrooms were so juicy i thought i was eating meat - the ciabatta came to my rescue, saving me from the embarrassment of dripping sauce down my face at 1pm...how ladylike :)  my inspiration level managed me room to include dessert - a few sweet strawberries with my creamy semifreddo - hm, how could i say no?

icing on their chocolate layer cake? core values being respect, honesty, transparency, comfort, and "always possible" 

next trip:  breakfast...with friends.

We tried out Gather for the first time about one month ago. We have thought about going here many times, but it always seems to be booked up, so I recommend reserving ahead. 

The ambiance has a pleasant high energy. The hum of the collective voices in the broad open space is loud but not overwhelming. Overall our meal was very tasty, even if I could not visualize what to expect from the menu description. 

As a vegetarian with a leaning toward vegan, I liked that the one vegetarian entree on the menu was vegan (seems typical that restaurants like this will have one token vege entree, which makes my decision making easy!). For a dinner like this, I was not worried too much about getting the right balance of food groups, but the vege options were surprising limited (a recent Sunset Mag article interviewed a Gather chef with expertise in vegan cooking). Then again, from my observations, there are far fewer vegetarians and vegans in Berkeley and SF area than one would expect.

Dessert was tasty, and the wines we had were great too.
Good vegetarian, though not as much variety as one would expect for Berkeley. Good quality. Slightly higher priced. Good service.

I went with friends to Gather last night--a much anticipated event. And I was not disappointed. The wait-staff was friendly, efficient, but relaxed. The food came in a timely manner and was absolutely fabulous. We started with the vegan charcuterie, a cutting board laden with interesting, flavorful tid-bits. Main course was chicken (organic), halibut-bacon pizza and various salads. All were seasoned just right.
The building itself is made from an "up-cycled" water tower, reclaimed wood, wine bottle lamps and the seat covers from used leather belts sewn together. 
Great atmosphere, great service and real food from Bay Area farms at a reasonable price.

Another great meal at Gather.  Two of us shared 2 salads to start: a kale salad with carrots, capers, pine nuts, and Fiscalini cheese, & an asparagus salad with black garlic and a duck egg.  They were delicious, though I wish the menu had said the kale salad was cooked.  I was expecting a raw kale salad.  

For entrees my wife had a special of halibut in brodo, almost a fish soup with a huge piece of halibut.  I had an appetizer dish they called yuba fazoletti, described as a tofu skin "pasta" stuffed with pork ragu & chard.  It was more like a fettuccine than a stuffed pasta, but was just as tasty as promised.  And though it was an appetizer it was plenty of food, especially after the salads.  

The wines were lovely and the service was responsive and friendly, though it took a while to get our entrees.  But we were there at peak time, before showtime at the nearby theaters.

My favorite Berkeley restaurant and one of my favorite Bay Area places. I nearly always order the beautifully-prepared vegan charcuterie as it changes every week or two. I highly recommend it for everyone & it's perfect for sharing between 2 people. Food is nicely presented and the ambiance is relaxing. Rarely does the volume in the place seem too loud, unlike many places. Servers are always knowledgeable about wines by the glass and are honest in their assessment of the dishes, which I value. Omnivores & vegetarians will enjoy it.

Back to Gather nearly 1 year later. My friend held a brunch here with girlfriends. At 10:30AM, there weren't a whole lot of people there. But the place quickly filled up by lunch time. I was surprised there was plenty of metered street parking on Allston.

Service was excellent and the food was great, but not perfect. I got the Acme French Toast, which was smothered in maple syrup and grilled nectarines. Hints of basil and spices enhanced every bite. Generous walnut halves graced the top. Food was nicely presented. Two minor gripes: I found 2 small bits of super tough dried fruit and they barely put any crème fraîche on the plate. If you like spiced cider and chai, you will like this dish. At $12 for 2 slices, it's not a bad deal.

Ambiance is awesome - modern rustic, earthy, artsy. Nice place to visit if you're in Berkeley.

Parking can be a little challenging, but we have been lucky so far.  There is a parking structure near the restaurant, but it gets full a lot.  On the weekends, I would recommend parking on the campus where its becomes open parking (please read the signs in case this has changed).

We always make reservations. The service here has always been very friendly.  We have never had to wait for seating.  Food comes fast!  A lot of the wait staff is easy on the eyes.A great selection of alcohol!

Even though this is not a cheap place by any means, it has been a real treat for our vegan and vegetarian friends.  Also for us non-vegetarians, there are some truly amazing specials and meals here (my partner had Rabbit 3 ways).  We love the vegan charcuterie.  

In my opinion, some of the meals here are hits and misses.  BUT we do always appreciate the clean taste and the creativity.

The pizza's are always great and a good bargain (2 can eat).  Also the Kale salad and some of the sides sport ample portions without breaking your wallet.  Some of the dishes can be more "micro" portioned in nature.

The desserts to me are always amazing.  You will always find something very creative and tasty.

You cannot go wrong here for a special dinner.

This place is so good, that I even liked their vegan dishes ;)

A great place, especially if you are having a mixture of vegetarians and carnivores in your group. A great burger + I enjoyed my wife's vegans dishes...

Make sure to reserve a table, this place is BUSY.

Yum, yum, yum!!

A friend had eaten here and was really disappointed, not because of anything the restaurant did, but because the menu at Gather just wasn't her thing. Having this in the back of my mind on my way to dinner, I was a little wary, but I had NO reason to be-- this place is incredible!!

The decor is great, the service is spectacular, and the food.... Oh, the food! Delicious! I am not a vegetarian, but I do love my veggies, and I was in heaven! Shaved melon with crispy pork belly-- YUM! Vegan Charcuterie--YUM! We had sooooo many dishes, and all were EXCELLENT, with the exception of the pizzas. Beautiful presentation, but the dough was sweet, and the toppings on the eggplant pizza were a little sweet, too, so the whole thing was --you guessed it-- sweet, and that's not what I was expecting. But, I'm eating the leftovers right now for lunch, so clearly it wasn't that bad. Dessert was amazing, too-- the special fruit desserts & the plum crostata with Pale Ale ice cream.... I wish I had those right now! The cocktails were delicious, and they have a really nice & accessible wine list. 

I can't wait to go back!

I am not ashamed to say that this visit was, hmmm, quite different than our previous one and that I may have been a bit too severe in my previous review. 

We recenlty visited Gather for lunch and had a very nice meal that included a unique and delicious salad and pizza that was politely fought over by we three.

And no unappetizing smells as we'd encountered previously. I always love adding new places to our repertoire rather than 'crossing them off of the list' so I am happy to report that we will be back!

Pizza, yum! Salad, yum! Wine, yum! Done!

Loved everything but especially the vegan platter, inventive and delicious. It's not often that you find a place that serves food that makes you so excited over vegetables. V enjoyable and will definitely be back!
Delightful and satisfying.

After the breakfast disaster I wrote about last weekend, I did want to give Gather another shot, because, like I said, I really wanted to love it. And, this time I did! :)

The occasion was a family celebration for my son's birthday. I was attending a meeting at the David Brower Center earlier that evening so we agreed on Gather. I was the first to arrive and found a seat in the bar while my peeps drifted in one-by-one. We ordered drinks (the drinks with house made Ginger Ale are delish) and just as the Birthday Boy and his Girlfriend arrived our table was ready and we were seated with our drinks (nice flow).

The Starters were many and VERY intriguing so we decided to order lots of them and get a Potato/Nettles/goat cheese pizza. Something we didn't order that sounded amazing was a Carrot/Nasturtium soup. Sounds like a great combination. 

The starters arrived in rapid succession which was great because we were sharing every plate. Everything was as tasty as it was inviting, beautifully presented, but the standout was the Vegan Charcuterie which sounds totally like a disconnect (charcuterie + vegan, huh?). 

It's gorgeous, very artfully plated on a ceramic footed sushi tray. One of the components was carrots and something about being soil-roasted or something along those lines. Never tasted anything like it. A true standout. Carrots with a very deep wonderful smokey flavor but still cold and crisp tender, some kinds of foam, other things that I can't even put my finger on. Comforting and palette-popping exciting at the same time. (wish I still had a menu in front of me so I could share the exact descriptions). ORDER IT!!!

We did the Blood Orange Salad. OMG., The Calamari with Corn Smut (didn't see anything that looked like smut, so will have to wikipedia corn smut), Lentils and something, also amazing. And the Pizza was wonderful.

Had to get some desserts to stick a birthday candle into. OMG, OMG. Best deserts ever! Blood orange sorbet was one, the little cake with so much chocolate, the lime panna cotta. If you don't go to Gather for dinner, PLEASE go for desert! Amazing.

The wait staff was great. Different servers brought different things to our table. Whether this is the custom or just happened, it was a lot of fun, getting different little descriptions from different servers. Fun.

Saw a lot of burgers coming out of the kitchen when we were at the bar, and next time, I'll definitely try one of those. 

So. looong story short, will have to check in on a brunch again and see if maybe the last brunch was just an off-day, will definitely go for lunch for a burger, and can't recommend dinner enough, especially desert. And many big plusses for ambiance.

It's kind of a bustling place, nicely lit, sustainable materials, and for as busy as it as, has no noise pollution. It's easy to have a conversation without the terrible din that you find in many large, busy  dining rooms. and still have the feeling of being somewhere hip, cool and busy. Maybe it's the sustainable materials used that are noise-absorbing and comforting.

Gather Your Peeps and go to Gather! We had a great time.

Such a good find! We passed this place on our way to our accommodations in the hills and I thought it looked interesting, so we ventured out late on a Saturday for some post-wedding noshing. Initially we just ordered two apps and the vegan charcuterie, but the appetizers appetized us so thoroughly that we had to try the special pizza (corn, Early Girl tomatoes and a few delicious peppers). 

If I lived in Berkley, this is where I'd be all. the. time. Drinks were delicious, draft selection was excellent, service was great (including from people who weren't our server), and above all the food was fantastic. It can be hard to find places that accommodate vegetarians (especially vegans) and meatovores equally well, but Gather rocks that like nobody's business.

I went to Gather when it first opened and it was wonderful. I went back another time and the food was awful. While presented beautifully and has a nice environment, it was greasy and didn't taste that great in general. I have heard that this is similar from some of my friends who have had similar experiences.
Great food politics and service, decent prices.  I've only been here once for brunch, had the Brunch Pizza, and licked my plate clean.  Yummy in my tummy.

Typical Berkeley style - nice decor, organic ingredients and many gluten free options.

I am a fan of their choice of tap or sparkling water -both free at your choice (yes, they use a soda machine to make the sparkling water).

Portions are considerably small and over priced, but hey, this is common nowadays.

Our waiter was very friendly but apparently new so not very familiar with the menu items when we had questions.

Other than that, we had a good experience.

Went last night. The place is pretty big, but was almost full when we walked in around 8:45, and was still maybe half-full when they locked the doors at 10.

Three menus: main, daily specials, and drinks. Here's a new one: "Ask to see our source book."

The vegan "charcuterie" (i.e., antipasto platter) was really good: eight items including salads, a crostino, a fritter, I forget what all. Everything was well seasoned. One saladish item was a bit overdressed. The spiel for the platter goes on and on. I'd say it would not be easily shareable by more than two people, a party of four should get two. Comes with a plate of grilled Acme levain.

Special pizza of the day ($16) was a bianca with Savoy cabbage and ... pancetta? guanciale? Great and new-to-me combination. Crust was OK, I'd have liked it slightly thinner and a darker bake. 12", eight slices, ample for two to share as a main course or 4-8 as an appetizer.

Got the greens ($5) with the pizza, escarole or something like that, tart and well seasoned.

Cheese plate ($10), two pieces each of three cheeses, nicely selected though a bit cold. Came with a few excellent spiced pecans, a dollop of spiced apple butter, what the waiter said was a spiced apple gumdrop but tasted more like persimmon, and a too-small piece of a great salty cheese cracker, plus a plate of Acme.

Service was kind of scattered, especially given the seemingly ample staff-to-customer ratio, e.g. we didn't get knives with the pizza or any utensils with the cheese plate. I'd upgrade to four stars if they get that together.

The all-California wine list is thoughtful but not to my non-mainstream taste. Only one of the wines sold by the glass (a pinot blanc) was my kind of thing.

I'll go back. Good addition to the downtown scene, especially with Downtown closed.

Five stars for food- it was really amazing... Everything was so delicious. As a veggie lover I really feel this place was spot on!

Two stars for service- we waited about 45 minutes between apps and entrees. I am not sure what happened or if our server forgot about us, but he rarely checked in with us and we felt he completely forgot about our entrees and pizza. It doesn't take 45 minutes to make pizza? After we got our entrees he decided to switch servers on us and we got amazing service. 

I rarely feel like bad service leaves such a disappointing feeling after a great meal, but I really feel something was wrong without an apology or a comp for even drinks or desert.

Nevertheless I will give Gather one more chance since the food was so excellent, it's a shame to punish the chefs for the poor service of one.

For the food.... The vegan charcuterie left me speechless. The strawberry and arugula salad was just perfection and the asparagus was amazing. Now for the pizza we finally got.. I love pizza...and the pizza here will leave you dreaming.... We didn't get to desert because it was sooo late by the time we finished our entrees....

I hope my review next time will be much better. I am really cheering for this place.. So I really hope they get their service improved fast!

This place was awful. I can't believe how horrible it was. The kale salad was decent. My colon needed that, I admit. But the 'special', which was a fish stew, was disgusting. The broth tasted like sea water flavored with a couple tomatoes, all of my mussels except one were unopened (i.e. BAD, and should NOT have been served), and the whole, unpeeled shrimp, with their antennae broken off and floating in the broth was completely unappetizing.  

Not to mention our waiter was horrible. He gave us attitude from the beginning ("Are you ready yet?") when we needed more time to look at the menu; he tried to take my boyfriend's plate away while he was in the bathroom, until I stopped him. He didn't mention or even ask about the fact that I hadn't touched my food, and he took my boyfriend's plate again later without asking, AS I WAS EATING FROM IT. Because I was still hungry, because you know, my food was shit. I understand that it's towards closing time, but we weren't the only ones left eating, and we paid to eat this food...

We got the chocolate hazelnut cake because we were still hungry. It was smaller than a baseball card, looked like someone had thrown up on it, and tasted of nothing. Not chocolate or hazelnut. Not even like vanilla....

I know I sound extremely bitter. And I am...this place charges enough that I expect polite service and edible food. Sorry if that makes me sound spoiled. I'm guessing from all these positive reviews that there are some menu choices that actually taste good. I guess if you have to go here, choose one of those? Definitely don't experiment.

I have been here twice and I absolutely love it! They always have the freshest food with the best service. They don't have a lot of options for hardcore meat eaters like me, but the veggie dishes they have are the best. I am usually not a big fan of just veggie dishes, but this place is the exception. Everything is always so good. i will definitely be back here again.

Amazing place.  Delicious food, fun and vibrant atmosphere, and smart and unpretentious staff.  Great prices too.

I took a large group of people there, including my mom from the midwest and my foodie friends.  Everyone found something to love-- my mom had a great burger cooked rare, while my vegan friend found her own culinary heaven.  You get the idea.  Sustainable food that doesn't take itself to seriously.

Only downside of Gather is that it's in Berkeley, and not SF where I live...

Tasty and creative Californian cuisine. 

I came here for a group dinner with people from work and the boss. The boss paid for dinner so my value judgment might be a bit biased.

They feature a select list of classic and original cocktail. 
I ordered the aviation made with gin, maraschino liqueur, and l crème de Violette. It was pretty tasty, but maybe a little on the small side.

To start we shared the Vegan "charcuterie" ($16) which features vegan dishes imitating and inspired by meat dishes. It included:
- Mushroom tartar, parsnip "lardo", roasted garlic
- Pear carpaccio, smoked persimmon celery root salsa
- Grilled watermelon radish "steak", leek "butter", horseradish salsa verde, wine grapes
- Oyster mushroom crudo, "tonnato" sauce, avocado, crispy sea palm
- Roasted carnival squash, sunchoke cashew bay leaf sauce, smoked maple 

All the components were flavorful, creative, and original. For only $16, it is a "must get" dish if you go to gather. Great for sharing. As an omnivore who loves eating meat dishes, I thoroughly enjoyed the dish. Great textures, flavors, and a very playful and surprising dish.

For the main course I shared three dishes with 3 other people. Specifically:
- Barbecued young chicken - farotto, turnips and tops, punterelle, cheese rind oil ($19.5)
- duo of lamb special with a whole rack of lamb and tenderloin (around $34)
-swordfish special (around $24)

The swordfish was well cooked. Crispy on one side side, tender on the inside. It was unfortunately a bit cold when brought to the table.
The lamb dish was surprisingly large. The whole rack was huge with a big bone, but unfortunately had mostly fat and not much meat.
The chicken was I believe almost a half-chicken. It was well cooked and juicy. The farotto (an italian grain ) was cooked like risotto, but sweeter was also tasty.

All portions were surprisingly large (a good thing!)  so I definitely recommend sharing so that you can try a few of them. They were all delicious, but the highlight of the night was the charcuterie.

Some people ordered the wild mushroom stew. Everyone was unfortunately disappointed with the dishes. It had too many beans and not enough mushrooms or flavor. 

For dessert I got sweet dessert wine and shared a cheesecake with berries. The cheesecake while tasty did not satisfy my cheesecake craving. It was pretty small, too fluffy, and the crust was nearly non existent. I wanted a nice slice of creamy cheesecake with a delicious crust. 

The restaurant has pretty rustic decor. All the dishes were well presented.  

The wait staff was friendly and professional. They were seamless and made great recommendations on dishes and portions when asked. 

Overall, it was a great experience. The only reason why I am not giving 5 stars is because not all the main courses delivered, but be sure to try the charcuterie and ask about the specials. Great for groups or a date!

Be sure to visit Gather at least one if you are in Berkeley. It is a great for vegetarians, vegans, and omnivores!.

I've been to Gather for breakfast and dinner, and they were both great experiences. Especially for breakfast, the pancakes and coffee were delicious. For dinner, I got a pizza and burger, which were also good. I like the customer service too. The waiters and waitresses are really nice. Another valuable quality of Gather is the interior design that sets a great environment to dine in.

Great food.  I was slightly let down by the cost of it but for the local sustainable hippy organic aspect i guess that's what you pay.  The atmosphere is great. The food was delicious and well balanced.  For a special occasion I'll go back again.  As a daily dinning experience, it's just a bit rich and a bit pricy.

Sustainable, organic, locally produced, delicious food.  What a find!  The service and presentation is wonderful.  Even the wine list is terrific.  Everything we ordered was absolutely scrumptious. We will definitely return.

I've heard good things about this restaurant from friends, and bad things. I've had a few salads that were good, but not excellent for their price. But what really makes me want to give it all five stars are their burgers and pizza (at least the vegan pizza with cashew cheese). Not bad for the price - $15 and can be split by two and utterly delicious. Though neither of us are vegan, we both agreed that it was the best pizza we had had. The pizza was thin, but had a fluffy outer crust. Best of both worlds.

I've also had their burger, which I highly recommend. Perfectly cooked with a delectable sauce. I highly recommend this restaurant and I will continue to come back and try their dishes!

Gather is now in my top 3 of favorites along with Cheeseboard and Gregoire. Like some other reviewers say, the menu doesn't make their food sound that exciting, but the photos really do them justice. 

I ate here on a brunch weekend and we ordered:

Prather Ranch Burger - We got it medium rare and it was perfection. The burger was juicy and full of flavors. The cheese was melted perfectly and the red onions added a bit of a crunch. 

The Burger Plate Cons: I'm not a fan of the side salad with olive oil. I kind of just feel like I'm eating oily leaves with no flavor. And their house ketchup tasted more like a slightly sweet spaghetti + salsa which wasn't what I was expecting.

Egg Pizza with Bacon, Caramelized Onion, and Oregano -  The perfect pizza! Almost better than Cheeseboard and as sacrilegious of a statement that is, it might be because I'm a meat lover and this pizza has tasty bacon. The egg also really complemented the pizza and made it more brunch appropriate. The other part that I really loved was the crust. They have billowy pockets of air which makes the inside of the crust so soft and tasty. As a kid, that was always my favorite part of the crust and Gather has really perfected it.

I love this place!

I didn't eat there but I'm doing the books and it was $42.  My wife and young daughter split a burger.  She said it was undercooked so she sent it back, after which they burned it to a crisp.  For $42.

Great dinner last night.  Had the green salad (big enough to split between the two of us), cauliflower soup, roasted artichokes (excellent), and a vegetarian mushroom dish (also excellent), great wine, and dessert (parsnip cake (!) and chocolate cake with salted vanilla ice cream.  It was pricey but worth it, especially for vegetarians who want to eat great food.

Phenomenal balance of flavors.
Loved the yellowtail crudo, the burrata and the squid. More creative and better executed than restaurants charging 3x the price.
Incredible!

PS: desert were a let down (we tried al three).

I eat everything. I am an opportunivore by trade;) Their vegan charcuterie was one of the most amazing dishes I've had in a LONG time. Amazingly complex and bright flavors, beautiful presentation, and uber fun to share. Pizza was excellent! We got a vegetarian one I think. We also had the BBQ young chicken and it was HUGE. They say it was "young" but it must have been a well-developed adolescent. We shared all the above between three of us.

My only negative about the place is the bar. My vodka martini sucked, and I love good martinis. The wine list for by-the-glass was so-so (I was looking at whites). However, the food was so incredible, and the drinks "good enough" that it was a great night out.

Great food! The service was ok. They had us waiting for our table when we had already made reservations in advance. The vegan charcuterie was too die for! So many rich flavors. My boyfriend loved the pork belly.
The pizza is excellent! The crust is perfect!

Welcome to the neighbourhood!  

Eaten here twice now.  very good pizza (in the style of chez/pizzaiolo, maybe not quite as good as those spots though).  other menu items range from off to excellent.  competent cocktail program (humo dulce... just the right amount of mezcal flavor... kudos)  and nice inexpensive wines by the glass.  

Fried mushrooms FAIL.  and that seems like a very hard thing to make not awesome.  I like sunchokes too but the texture here just didn't work.  too hard, crunchy.  Cardoons were similarly fried but markedly better.  
Charcuterie plate was good (raisins in wine garnish... or something like that on the side... delish)  but a bit heavy on headcheese-like things. more salumi or pate please.  
Halibut:  stingy portion.  also, menu should reflect that this is raw.  I love me some raw halibut, so fine, but, from how the menu is written there is no way to know that this is crudo.  not what I was expecting, and it was maybe an ounce of fish.  
Great kale salad.

We went there last week to celebrate a friend's birthday, and had a bad experience ever! 

I don't recommend this place to celebrate birthdays because they horribly charged $20 for cutting a cake. That's called a "cake-cutting" fee. Isn't it stupid? I've heard of fees for opening bottles of wines and separate plates but not cake cutting...... 

Also, the servant guy is not grateful..... He recommended appetizers for us, a party of 8, and said it's enough for everyone. When the appetizers came, we all thought that's only for a party of 2, at most. 
The most important thing is that, he was probably a good sales because he always stopped by our table, constantly, to ask us for more food and bottles, BUT, he charged wrong amounts to our credit cards and fixed them up, after he "double-checked" with us before he took our cards.......

Food wise, it is not too bad. For everything we ordered, we all think that the chicken was the best. The pork chop we ordered was way too salty... And other plates were not as good as other restaurants with same level of pricing.... so not recommended.......... don't think we will go again....

One of my friends recommended their burger to me and being a big burger fan, I definitely had to try it out. I was definitely not disappointed. They have an interesting menu. Everything is organic and a lot of the dishes were vegetarian or vegan. We got the 

Monterey Bay squid appetizer -- a very unique texture and taste. I'm not sure if it was cooked. it was definitely interesting. 

the burger -- it was a pretty decent. Since they're organic, they didn't have ketchup. I generally always eat my burgers with ketchup so I was a little sad =( but none the less, it was still a very good burger. 

sausage pizza -- I really liked their pizza. or at least the part with the sauce and the sausages. The crust was interesting. I think it definitely looked very interesting.

If you don't have a reservation (like us), don't worry. There were tons of tables available outside on the patio....in a nice half sun/shade mix. I had a hard time choosing between breakfast and lunch as we were there at noon on a Sunday. I ultimately went with lunch and ordered a delicious tuna salad. No to be missed. Fresh, not fishy, filling - what more do you need? I'm not giving Gather 5 stars because the salad could have been a little bigger and...my soy cappuccino tasted a little off...

LOVE GATHER!

Love them so much that I hired their sister company, Back to Earth to cater my wedding. It's that good.

Their menu changes by the season, so you'll never be bored. I really can't say enough good things about this place. Try to pizza, try the vegan "charcuterie" and if you're there for brunch, the breakfast pizza is a must!
Interesting and exciting food combinations. This is a place you will truly get to try something you have NEVER had before and LOVE it.

Took my girlfriend and her mom for birthday dinner.  Got a 220z ipa beer which was hella bitter, not my taste.  Had the burger and fries which was very good.  Girlfriend had the vegan charcutterie for dinner(not for appetizer)waiter said she may still be hungry but she was full, it was plenty of food.  She said it was the best vegan food she had in a long while and loved it.  Good food.

I've been waiting to try this place and finally today I did. One star off cause the salad girl was mixing the salad with her bare hands! Please use a glove or something....please. Haven't u heard of health department guidelines....

Now to my experience: at 11:30 weekday there was a line out the door! I was already excited. So we walked in got a table then ordered at the counter. Here is what we got:

1.Carrot saffron soup: heavenly! so heavenly that they ran out of it in 30 min and replaced it with chickpea soup. 
2.Romaine Salad mix: the dressing was utterly amazing. I always get dressing on the side since usually restaurants put so much dressing in salads that u hardly can taste the veggies. This time for some reason I forgot to mention it and I am glad I did. The amount of dressing was perfect. Well done! 
3.Asparagus pizza: one of the best pizza's I've tried. The crust is just something out of this world...yeah I think divine.  
4.Braised portabella mushroom sandwich: ok how do u guys make this? Soooooo delicious and tasty.....
5.Bread pudding for desert: this was probably the only average item I ate here, everything else was just excellent. The Crixa's bread-pudding is so much better. 

Overall I really liked this place. I must say it's a bit expensive but hay you are eating organic which is good for your body.

Many good noms, kombucha on tap, good (no, great) selection of vegan/vegetarian options without forgetting the carnivores, good selection of gluten free options, totally organic locavore awesome, nice decor, good service.  Downsides: it's like the trendiest place ever so we had to wait 45 minutes for a table, which I am not used to esp. in the east bay, and it's not super duper cheap.  Definitely get the vegan charcuterie as an appetizer.

We were very pleased to stumble on this restaurant.. It was a busy weekend night, but we got a table, ran into some old friends, and enjoyed the meal. I loved the focus on great vegetables, sustainable food and all of the staff. A nice dinner and I hope to repeat the experience.

Delicious, inventive and fun. 

Very Berkeley.

I'm a meat-eater, but couldn't resist the vegan charcuterie. The "goat cheese" was made with ground cashews ... mmmm. The whole concept was creative and playful, but it was tasty, too.

The burger was a big hit at our table, as was the panisse (a fried chickpea flour cake). 

Wonderful cocktails, impeccable service, comfortable atmosphere, and not nearly as pricey as I thought it would be (entrees in the teens). We're definitely going back.

Some friends and I came here for dinner for the first time this past weekend. The restaurant itself is beautiful, airy, yet intimate. The menu has a lot of interesting choices-many of which are gluten free or vegan. There were four of us in total and we just ordered several things and ate family-style (which I recommend). We tried the heirloom tomatoes, beef navel, and green beans to start- all were great but I especially enjoyed the green beans. Then we had the summer squash pizza (with crust to DIE FOR) and the lobster meatballs (meh...). For dessert we got the almond teff cake and apple crostata. Everything was ABSOLUTELY delicious- they even have house made sodas! My one complaint is that the servings are small for the price-so don't go if you're starving.

Not Super Spectacular, But Worth A Try

Not spectacular compared to other similar restaurants, but Gather holds its own. Gather is a place that emphasizes slow foods, local organic, etc. The place reminded us a lot of Founding Farmers in Washington DC. They even had the same pickled veggies décor. The restaurant is in a new building with an open kitchen area. There didn't appear to be a bar. The tables were crowded (difficult to squeeze in between tables for us and the waiter) and there was bench seating along the window line. This of course meant the waiter's butt was prominently displayed over your food as orders were taken at adjacent tables. 

We started with the vegan charcuterie (basically refers to preserved or cured meats). The vegan charcuterie is obviously free of meat, and presumably gout. There were a couple of items that were really good and imaginatively prepared including the bruschetta (w/ crispy tofu skin, avocado, tomato, smoked garlic "aioli") and the Carpaccio of watermelon radish and turnip, horseradish salsa verde, grapes, grated almond. The rest was just filler, but still good, in my opinion. I recommend getting this as a starter. 

We also had the Roasted mushroom, corn, braised leeks, habanero oil, thyme pizza. Of course this was really good because it was a pizza (hard to go wrong with pizza). The crust was very good--it seemed buttery, soft and chewy. A lot of people around us were ordering pizzas, and they all looked good.

We also had fish (halibut, I think), topped with some kind of salsa. It was good, but not super innovative. 

Finally, for dessert we had a "milkshake" that reminded me of a glass of ovaltine. What saved dessert were the two blackberry empanadas that came with the milkshake.

I've loved Gather on several visits over the past year+, there was always something completely unexpected (visually or flavor-wise), special, and delightful-except for this visit over the holiday weekend which was completely mundane and not very special. There were no dinner specials outside of one starter. The burger (normally outstanding) was salty and took a long time to arrive after the salad. The kale salad was mostly missing whatever tantalizing ingredient it has had on my last 4 visits, except for a few bites where it could be faintly detected. The kale pieces were huge and flopped all over the table when we tried to serve ourselves. The chicken didn't seem very interesting but then I'm not a fan of barbq sauce. The waitress also didn't seem very polished which was slightly off-putting.

Last year I would have given Gather 4.5 stars.

What's up with Gather?

I'll give Gather another chance for dinner, because I wasn't impressed with brunch. The ambiance is really nice, and the patio is fabulous. Service was pretty spotty, which was weird because it wasn't crowded at all. We went for really long periods of time without drinks, enough so that the three of us never all had a drink in hand at the same time to make a celebratory toast.
