The heirloom scramble was pretty good. For something called an heirloom scramble, though, it didn't have very many tomatoes. The burger was good, but really greasy and the two of us who had it felt a little sick afterward. The friend who had the french toast loved it.

The bloody marys have a very strong chipotle taste, the vodka pepper drinks were super yummy, and the sazerac was okay but super small. 

Definitely look forward to trying dinner. I hate to judge a place on brunch alone.

service was fantastic. went for brunch, got the burger, was pretty ok. company ordered the pizza, was fantastic! i loved the crust. the lemon lime soda was super tasty also. i would like to come back for dinner and try more!

The warm kale salad is reason enough to go back. It's perfectly cooked with pine nuts, fiscalini cheese and just the right amount of vinegar. The vegan charcuterie and prather ranch burger are also great. 

While the wait staff has always been friendly and knowledgable, the hosts seem to have a hard time organizing the room. Twice I've been told the wait would be about ten minutes and wound up waiting thirty minutes to an hour. Fortunately, the bar is lovely and I'm always glad to enjoy a glass of wine while I wait.

Everybody seems to be commenting on the "its vegan and for hippies!" notion...well, let me tell you, this restaurant is not vegan, and unless the hippies are shelling out $18 for a porky and delicious guanciale pizza, you won't find any of them either. In addition to the guanciale pizza we tried the basic mozzarella, sea salt and tomato sauce (which was so flavorful!). I had the kale salad and dare I say that it tasted a little too healthy?? It was a unique salad, but I probably would order any of the pizzas over the salad if I were to go again. I stole a bite from my moms fried egg sandwich and the bacon braised broccoli rabe is amazing! You get the bacon fat mixed with the egg yolk on a toasty piece of buttered bread and all is pretty much right in the world. Service was good, but a waiter was a little eccentric and a little to laid back, but I suppose it fits the restaurants targeted vibe. Sure there are vegan and gluten free options and I feel like as consumers we will be seeing more and more of that in restaurants, but there is also meaty goodness for those die hard carnivores out there.

What happened?  I probably wrote one of your first favorable reviews.  The food is still good, especially kale anything, soup and vegan charcuterie but the service--deplorable!  Really.  Would it kill anyone to check in once in awhile?  I was there on a Tuesday night, spent $130 for two people.  Felt like the servers were doing me a favor by bringing me the stalest of bread for sopping up the delicious charcuterie sauces.  Whatever complacency groove you've entered into based on being busy often, I recommend shifting to fixing your service.  On a Tuesday night, you were far from filled.  You could be busting out every single night if you could just train your wait staff.
First time at Gather: good food, but extremely poor service. Unattentive and slow staff.
Beautiful fun delicious and healthy

as a celiac it was nice that they understood no gluten and had tons of options for me. however, when i asked the bartender for a drink suggestion  she seemed annoyed, although finally with much arm twisting recommended the bee sting which was delicious although a bit pricey. then we ordered two waters and got one. finally seated, our waiter was really pushy! he recommended the vegan charcuterie which was delish and also pushed the special fish so hard we caved. but turns out, they ran out of it so he just brought us a different dish without even asking if we'd like to re-order! and it was not tasty! and he made us feel really awkward and in an attempt to make up for it made a huge show of bringing us free dessert...not going back for a while despite the celiac friendly nature which is a rarity.

Eugh,  Not good.  Just not good.  Maybe its me, maybe i just ordered the 'wrong' things on the menu, I don't know.  I had the vegan charcuterie platter and the carrot dish that came with a couple of fava beans, a tiny piece of dehydrated kale, and a pepper-onion saute.  Both dishes were a fail for me.  The charcuterie had about 6 different component and they all either fell flat or were plan gross. The only one i liked was a curry lentil dish and also the bread that came with the dish.  The carrot entree had this...smear? of grainy black stuff that reminded me of sandy tar, it was gross.  The carrots were also way too vinegary.  The pepper onion saute was good though. 
Based on my experience here, I would give it a 1 star rating, but I went here with a group of 7 people and they all enjoyed what they had.  The pizzas looked particularly tasty. So I'll give this place another shot...once i recover from this meal...

Revision to my review:  my review was based on the information provided to me by Gather employees at the time of my meal. They have since contacted me to inform me that they still offer table service for dinner and weekend brunch, but neither the bar tender, cashier, nor manager bothered to mention that to me when I expressed my disappointment to them. So I will probably go back to Gather for dinner or weekend brunch when they have table service; however, my review stands for their new lunch time weekday format...

Disperse! Disperse!

For those of you that have been to Gather before (I had been several times and enjoyed all experiences), I regret to inform you that as of Monday, April 5, Gather has decided to do away with table service.  Yep, you read right....now you get to stand in line for 15 minutes to order your $30 plus meal.  Such a shame.  If I want to take a number and grab a seat I will go next door to Cancuns for $10 from now on. 

Gather's menu provokes thought and bodes questions, when you're standing in line waiting to order your food, you don't have time to ask all of those questions...drinks?  The bar tender doesn't have a till, go stand in line for 15 minutes to get your drink and if you're ordering more than1 alcoholic beverage, you better make sure both people are in line, or the ever so friendly manager will come find that person to make sure.  Want a refill on your iced tea ?  Go stand in line for 15 minutes and pay for it....no free refills at Gather.

Shame on Gather. This was a great restaurant with delightful service people.  The food's still great, but this order at the counter and take a number format : 
1. Degrades your intelligent wait staff to cashier button pushing monkeys and reduces their income (Counter tips are never the same as table-service tips);
2.    Means people are going to order fewer drinks and less food if they have to stand in line every time they need something else (duh!);
3. and turns off those of us that used to enjoy Gather's ambience and professional servers.

Sure the foods still good, but I would rather walk down the street to 5, or Corso, or Cioccolata Di Vino and pay the same price, get food that's just as good and as sustainable, and have delightfull wait staff bring it to me. 

No more Gather for me unless they go back to table service.

I went to Gather for the first time a couple of weeks ago and it was a really good experience.  They have a good selection of vegetarian and vegan options as well as carnivorous options.  Their food is made from organic and local grown products.  The atmosphere is very comfortable and inviting.  The restaurant is conveniently located next to Cal so I'm assuming they have a huge amount of college student diners. 

Beware, dowtown Berkeley is notorious for limited parking options.  Gather was well worth the 5 time loop around the city blocks for a parking space.  I was not disappointed with the food, ambiance, and service.   I will be going back to this restaurant soon again!

I've been back to this place several times since my first review with groups & it seems they've worked out some of the service issues they had in the beginning. The food is pretty good, but I still think the place is a bit over-hyped. It's good & but it's not Chez Panisse. I also don't really love the whole "Hey Friends" talk from the waiter. How are we friends when neither of us know each other's names? Although calling me your friend is better than the total disdain I got the first time I came. Haven't seen the waiter or hostess I saw the first time I came on following visits, so maybe they got the boot ... Anyway the food and service are good & I love the wine on tap & complimentary sparkling water.

It was our first time at Gather but we had seen it being built from the ground up. I'm so glad we were able to finally visit!

Very good beer on tap AND I love that they used local ingredients. I will be coming here again!

Anything you get here is great, but I especially like the seasonal scrambles, service is wonderful and definitely ask to see the source book.
4 stars for the price; wish I could go here more often but we always spend lots of money here as the food is SO good!

Didn't quite understand the menu so I just ordered the porchetta sandwich , best sandwich I had!  My husband had the sausage sandwich, had a taste of it and it was very good as well!  Cousin had the farm egg pizza, it was good too!  It is a little pricey but well worth it!

The food at Gather is indeed good, but not great. The price reflects the quality of ingredients, but not the taste of the dish. I've had the spicy pulled pork sandwich and the sausage pizza. The meat in the sandwich was tasty, tender, and well cooked, but it was nothing fantastic. Although the pizza was good as well, it came with a lot of grease on it which I did not like.

This place is seriously work exploring, and worth the attention.  

Since there is no clear bible for sustainability, and so there are many creeds that the stunningly smart chef and kitchen at GATHER combine.  On the one hand, fantastic vegan plates with cashew and parsnip sauces that tantalize over watermelon radishes and fried tofu skin, or drizzled about elegant and sustainable leafy greens, with brave ventures into the 'whole animal' world.  In a restrained but nicely designed decor of recycled goods it is no surprise that sustainability is the ethos:  sure, you're sitting on benches made of recycled leather belts, so why not combine different notions of re-use.  But the neatest part of this hotspot seems to us to be how these credos of sustainability are combined:  there is even some harmony in having fatty pig's head meat works with low-cal vegetables, we discovered with surprise, and is even fun, as are the three or four vegan courses, including vegan pizza of caulifower and parsnip .  But you could easily do a fully carnivorous set of options.  And I loved that the head cheese (made by the restaurant's own kitchen) with the greens--even if we had to order more greens after this tasty appetizer special had been eaten save for two more strips of head cheese.  

Such warmly catholic sustainability--world ethos trumping food ethos; as it were, place trumping eating rules; credos reworked to fashion food design--works to amplify diversity among the dishes that Gather served.  As the short wine list might seem limited but seemed much more than satisfactory to us, the range of dishes was much much greater than we thought even after we looked at the menu.  And this serves to make eating out a lot of fun indeed, not to be missed.

So I'd strongly disagree that it is suited only to vegans; it is no spartan Moosewood-like dining experience.  Sure, they're not cooking more than they can serve, but there are rices worth unpacking in that menu.  Just start with the vegan charcuterie to get a sense of the breadth to be made in the vegan world, then look for the surprises. And make friends with your server if the menu seems foreign--they've got plenty to suggest.  Sure, if you want a steak frites there are other places to go.

Great service, even when they're about to close! The food is good, but expensive. I had the Prather Ranch Burger, which was very good. The fries were also tasty, but had way too much salt. I also had a Hibiscus-Jasmine soda, which was great as well. For dessert I had the chocolate hazelnut cake, which was good but all the  salt seemed to be concentrated in one part of the cake. Gross! 

The decor is nice. This is also one of those places that presents their food very nicely, which I am a sucker for even though it's not really needed. 

So in general, expensive, but probably worth it!

Really good dinner there last night. The only mix up was with bringing out food on time; the table of 6 that ordered after us got their food before us, but the server aknowleged the mix up, brought us some bread, apologized and then they comped us our dessert.
Vegan charcuterie: YUM, even my hubby the carnivore loved it. The only miss was the eggplant "brandade", which had a paste-like texture was sort of lacking in flavor. Everything else was very good.
I had the seared pork belly with some sort of beans and I needed to ask for salt for it: it was very good, but not stellar.
The stir fried green beans with chili sauce and cashews were delicious, but the beans themselves were OVERCOOKED!!
They are getting that 4th star for the following: focusing on local, organic and sustainable food; offering not only vegan AND meat dishes, but also gluten free options and the fact that they have a cute cocktail menu in addition to wine & beer.
Dessert was also very good: i loved seeing trifle on the menu and GF options there, too. AND good coffee. We'll be back.

I have been to Gather twice now and both times I had the most AMAZING pizza ever!!! It really rivals Pizzaiolo (Oakland), Delfina (San Fran), Pizzetta 211 (San Fran), A 16 (San Fran), etc. The ingredients are fresh and unique, the crust is thin and crisp - it's just delicious. This past time, I ventured to other parts of the menu and tried one of their vegetarian dishes. I'm not a veg, but I DID NOT miss the meat! My mother and I had an artichoke dish with fava beans, the featured ingredient of the week. Wow! I have never had such sweet, flavor-popping fava beans before in my life. Nice atmosphere, attentive servers, and fantastic food! Can't ask for much more!

hit-or-miss

I have had one of the best meals ever here and I have also had a nearly inedible dish. I must be due to the seasonable faire.

we caught lunch here and it was great. the vegan cheese has a great texture. I had the vegan pizza (im not a fan of olives, but this was great. would have been almost perfect with some cracked pepper. I found it a little salty) and the idiot i was with had some chicken sausage/egg/potato dish. we were both super pleased with what we ordered, had a great lunch and left happy. his "eggs were perfect" which is a huge compliment.

the decor is really adorable, effort went into it and it shows. the staff was attentive but not overbearing and as a whole was very delightful. 


I will be returning for a dinner in the near future.

I have to agree with some of the reviewers that this place IS a bit pretentious. I ordered some cruciferous vegetable soup which they have an uncommon name for which begs for an explantation from the server. When they tell you what it is, you feel a little stupid for asking. Having said that...the soup was absolutely fantastic. A little pricey for a bowl of soup with NO bread or crackers for $8.00 but it really was gastronomically satisfying. After the server took my order, I never saw him again...but no matter. The bartender, Ryan, was ever so polite and attentive, I never missed the other server. Also, another server/kitchen person came over to ask if I wanted anything else and again, was ever so attentive. I felt so welcomed by them. I then ordered the Semifreddo which is poached peaches with goat milk ice cream....DIVINE! Very satisfying meal, if you can call soup and dessert a meal! LOL! I would definitely go back for a proper dinner some time but would reserve this place for a special occasion rather than just getting something on the run. It is little on the pricey side, at least for me, to be going there casually.
As a vegetarian, I enjoyed eating there and my husband a meet eater also enjoyed it.  Interesting yet satisfying food, fair price, nice atmosphere.

I've eaten here three times in past six months and always had a delicious meal.  There is a "precious" quality to the menu and a bit of self-righteousness to the local sourcing canon, but the results are amazing.  The waitstaff is friendly and not at all pretentious.  They are very helpful with suggestions for pre-theatre meals and always suggest an appropriate amount of food for plate sharing.  Even so, once you have a glass of wine or two, this is an expensive restaurant for a quick meal, and isn't comfortable enough to make you want to linger.

i went there a day or too ago and it tasted really bad was exspensive and really cramped. u would think they would hire people who could speak proper english, we had a hosteses that i think was german or whatever and she was terrible ever time she came to the table there was a smell like of a wet dog or someone who hasent taken a shower. also you couldent understand what she was saying and took for ever to bring the water and food. i wouldent reccomend this place
Just go! Awesome everything and the Chef, Sean Baker, is VERY passionate about what he does and that is obvious in all the food.
My boyfriend is friends with the Chef here and said we HAD to try it. So happy we did, it was an amazing experience with such incredible, well-executed and delicious food!

October, 6 I was going to a  Madona concert with one of my girl friends and her husband recommended to eat at Gather. I ordered a lobster meat ball that was vegetarian. OMG, the food was excellent. I still have the taste of the food in my mouth from a week ago. The staff was friendly. The rstaurant twas packed though, but did not take long to serve us. The dessert was wonderfull!!!!

little gem salad - nuff said. i can't say enough praise about this delectable appetizer. it'll make you frown upon every other salad you come across...kind of. one downside is that i believe this salad is provided only on the lunch menu - but it's been a little bit since i've last been to gather so i could be wrong

their pizzas are really good too. when it comes out, you might question whether the dish will fill you up, but my friend and i shared a salad and pizza, and to be honest, it took some effort to finish it all.

other misc things -
it gets crowded during dinner, so you either need a reservation well in advance or you should be willing to be seated at the bar area. they have hooks underneath the bar table for the ladies' purses, but they're small so don't try to hang your coat there like i saw one woman do - pls, let's not get ridiculous.

you can order straight from the dinner menu at the bar area - the bartenders will serve you right then and there. speaking of bartenders, they're really friendly and provide great service and offer good drink suggestions, so props.

there is an outside seating area (with heated lamps) but i have yet to experience it.

one potential caveat - 
tables alongside the walls are closely packed together, so be prepared to get comfortable and inadvertently share conversation with your immediate neighbors. claustrophobes, beware.
fancy. foams. delicious. get to taste a bit of everything. bit too fancy for kids.

My husband and I have been wanting to try Gather for quite some time, and had heard a lot of good things about it, so with all the hype it was quite a disappointment to discover that Gather is, well, a disappointment.

First of all, I will say one good thing: the atmosphere is pleasant and the restaurant is attractive, which is what I noticed when I walked in - but unfortunately, it all went downhill from there. 

Our waiter was very pushy and I felt like he wanted to dictate to us what to eat. I enjoy having suggestions from a knowledgeable waiter, but this was a little too much - he recommended the vegan charcuterie, then asked us at least twice if we wanted to order it. When we declined and opted instead for a kale salad, squash blossoms, and a pizza, and specified that we wanted three courses in that order, he told us that the kale would be great with the pizza and we should have them together. Um...no thanks, we'll just have what we ordered.

We each ordered a glass of wine and it took at least 30 minutes for both of us to get the correct one - they brought me the wrong glass, then disappeared for 15 minutes. My husband didn't get his until we were already on our second course, and we didn't get any apology or acknowledgment of the mistake.

Onto the food. The kale salad was very salty. The squash blossoms were okay, but everyone is making squash blossoms these days so I think if you're going to do them you have to do something to set yourself apart. They were also quite salty (they seemed to have the same dressing as the kale salad) but otherwise lacking in flavor. The pizza was probably the best part of our meal, but that's only because there was nothing notably bad about it. It was fine. After that unimpressive start, we did not order dessert.

I like to eat out, and I like fresh, organic, local ingredients, and I live in Berkeley, so a certain level of pretension is sort of inevitable. I can deal with it, especially if the pretension is backed up by great food. That was not the case at Gather. High prices, pushy waiters, and mediocre food. No thanks. I think that Camino is going for a similar idea, but they do it much better.

The food here was absolutely wonderful. yummmmyyyy

I ordered the Burger and fries ( random for a nice place, I know). But really it was perfect. The meat was cooked exactly the way I wanted and the fries were SO good!! So good in fact that someone at our table ordered a side of them. My only complaint is that the options on the menu are very limited and if you're a meat eater you have like only 3 choices.  Also I did have to salt the Burger but I do love strong flavor. It was a really nice atmosphere and good food.

We went for a graduation dinner and it was perfect.

3.5 stars

This review is for breakfast. 

Their scramble was delicious including their potatoes. We also had the cornmeal pancakes- thing exciting about them. 

Coffee was good- so was their cappuccino. 

Service was ok, it's a hit or miss in this place with service. Last week we had the best waiter ever , Rafael, if you are reading this, you are AMAZING!!

As many others mentioned, the service here is lacking.  At lunch today we were one of two other parties on the patio.  We ordered soup and sandwiches and then watched the patio fill up with other diners.  All the orders for other diners who arrived well after us were coming out so finally I asked where our food was and the server seemed perplexed by this.  No apologies were offered.  How hard is it to bring out soup?

The bill was $20 per person with tip.  I'm all for quality ingredients and willing to pay extra for seasonal, organic food but the overall experience and taste has got to be worth it.

I'm surprised that the management hasn't addressed the poor service with all the reviews mentioning this issue.
1x Brunch, 1x Lunch, 1x Dinner.   Consistently great food.  Standout dessert -- some chocolate/alcohol dessert drink  -- so good!

I was fortunate enough to be treated to a business lunch here recently, and it was scrumptious!  

Some of the best pizza crust I've ever eaten, and I'm obsessed with all things bread, so I don't say this lightly.  Golden and crispy on the outside yet wonderfully chewy on the inside.

The burrata salad was superb: well-plated, flavors perfectly balanced, and the freshness of the ingredients just shone through.  

Service was attentive and friendly but not overly so, and the staff was  perfectly willing to handle some special requests from our party, and did so with ease.  

I wish I could come here more often, but my budget won't allow it.  Still, this is a great restaurant, and I'm very glad it's here.

This place has been over-reviewed already - but I had to write anyways.

There aren't many all-organic restaurants with reasonable prices and excellent food that I know.  The care put into the food and the restaurant itself was pretty amazing.  From the funiture made of salvaged wood to the funny food-related far side cartoons in the restrooms - a lot of thought went into this place.

I had to get on the band-wagon and order a vegan charcuterie plate like everyone at the surrounding tables were doing.  It was all that it was cracked up to be.  6 different veges dishes each with it's own distinctive sauce from what I remember:

- chickpea cakes on something like lemon sabayon
- beets (red & golden) with carrots and pistachio pesto 
- jerusalem artichoke with a meaty mushroom in an earthy brown sauce
- bok choy and peas on something like creme fresh
- abalone and oyster mushrooms on some tangy sauce

Another memorable thing was almond cake on meyer lemon curd for dessert.

I think this is a nouveau version of Chez Panisse or perhaps it's better.  There's no complicated souffle or squab on the menu but I like the concept of an organic place striving to keep food somewhat simple and affordable vs. fussy and expensive.

Fabulous, creative menu.  Perfect service.  Marvelous cocktail concoctions.  I seriously love this place.  We had a 9 PM reservation, but showed up at 7 and were seated by 7:10.   
We had the vegan pizza with capers and chili sauce as an appetizer--really fun flavors and delectable crust.  My bf had the burger which was wonderfully medium rare and came with the most perfect fries.   Other dishes ordered were the kale salad and the bibb lettuce salad--yum!

I found Gather's food to be absolutely delicious. For starter, my wife wanted to try the asparagus appetizer.... I dislike asparagus:-(... However, this dish was tasty.  This asparagus is picked daily each morning in Santa Cruz and brought to Gather each afternoon.  If my mom would have seen me eat that asparagus.  Wow!

The portions are quite small but the flavor is definitely delightful.  And for me it's always nice to venture out and try something new.  This place is not about huge portions or meat and although the prices may be high for some, the money is in the unique flavors.  The vegan "charcuterie" plate is like art and you've just got to try all the little delights of this dish.

Gather is in Berkeley which is the perfect spot for this kind of restaurant.  This is no place to take a country boy after a long day on the farm for a medium rare steak and baked potato, but it's a must try for exotic vegan dishes with a few "carnivore" options.

Order the vegan charcuterie. Very innovative, great flavors and interesting combinations of ingredients- worth the experience. Vegetarian mains also delicious. 
spicy tomato cashew pizza was decent, but a bit odd. Cocktails were good. 
Downside: For this price-point, except flawless service and clean facilities. Unfortunately both lacking.

Loved it! As soon as my friend and I sat down, we were asked if we would like complimentary sparkling water or flat water. We chose the sparkling water and it was delicious. I think they carbonated purified water. Loved the service, loved the food. I had pizza with halibut, potatoes, and capers (I think they were capers). Quiet enough to hear your dinner companion, but buzzing enough to feel the place is alive.  Food is eco-friendly. Will definitely go back!

Possibly one of the BEST burgers I've ever had. Nothing else seemed appetizing to me but that burger was legit.

Super packed; make reservations.

I've been here for dinner multiple times and never been dissapointed. Yesterday I went for brunch yesterday for the first time and it was amazing yet again. We shared the Rapini Mushroom Scramble and the Bacon and Egg Pizza. My mouth is literally watering thinking about it. 

I would eat here everday if my budget allowed it.
I love the way they create food with simple, local ingredients.

I came here on a Sunday night for dinner, and was pleasantly surprised by the quality/yumminess of the food. I ordered the kale/pinenut salad and spicy tomato pizza, both of which were original and flavorful. I especially enjoyed the kale salad dressing - it was tart and complimented the kale and pinenuts perfectly. 
I liked the "openness" of the floor plan, and the restaurant is designed so that you can see the chefs and entire kitchen area. 
Our server was very attentive, and the food arrived with impeccable timing.
Overall,  I had an excellent experience and look forward to going back.

This would be the perfect place to take a vegan or vegetarian friend. All their menu options are organic and sustainably grown; you really feel good about eating at this place. My friend and I came here for lunch and had the pizza and pasta with the pomegranate tea. I really enjoyed their house tea -- very refreshing and light. The pizza we shared was also very good especially for something with no meat! 

It's a huge place, so good for groups. Inside is woody and homey feeling. I would definitely come back here again.

Gather was almost too much delicious to handle. I shared my dishes with my party to make sure I was able to eat everything within my reach, and couldn't get enough of anything I got my hands on. We came for brunch and had iced tea and coffee to drink, both delicious and unique in their own special ways. The coffee was from Thanksgiving Coffee Company: fair trade, possibly organic, and absolutely fantastic; just how I like it. We enjoyed some veggie scramble with this toast that had a goat cream cheese-like topping that I wanted to scarf down but knew if I did I couldn't fit anything else into my fist-sized internal food storage unit. I had the mushroom pizza, which I liked but most of my attraction was to the crust so I'm excited to try a different pizza next time. We had the lentils side dish, a must for any bruncher. I also tried the beet salad, which had plenty of chicory and nuts to complement the late fall/early winter season. The server knew what was in just about every dish and knew exactly when we needed him and when we didn't. I can't wait to return to Gather for another fantastic experience.

WOW: Bloody Mary and Brunch Pizza

Really. Really. Good.

Just went again for dinner last night and had a great time!

The reason for 4 stars and not 5 are:
First batch of pisco sours were a little too limey.
There was a really long wait (20 mins) before ordering and getting any food - considering we were a 9pm reservation and the restaurant was emptying out I wasn't expecting this.
The vegan charcuterie had a hair in it - which came out mid bite. The reason they're not losing more stars for this is because when we made out server aware she handled it EXCELLENTLY.

So, for the food, the second vegan charcuterie we got was delicious! Black trumpet was our favourite, the cauliflower one was a close second. I really enjoyed the carrots but hubby didn't - he thought it was a little too bland, I like because of its naturalness. The citrus one was yum too.

We also split the herring appetizer; really huge portion and excellently cooked.

The pancetta pizza was also delicious. I love the little dough knots in the crust. Pizza really was flavorful. I don't typically order pizza when I'm out, I feel it's a dish that's hard to be wowed by, but this one wowed me.

Just had dinner at Gather with my family and had a GREAT experience!! I ordered the vegan spicy tomato pizza and it was so yummy! Even the meat-lovers at the table thought it was really good. We got the kale salad and the mixed greens salad and both were really tasty and good sized portions. The strawberry lemon sorbet we had for dessert was also delicious! Can't wait to go back soon!

The food at Gather all tastes delicious, but not quite delicious enough to fully justify the price.The Vegan charcuterie was about as confusing a plate as I have ever encountered, with something like six different combinations of items, none of them readily identifiable, or labeled in any significant way. The expensive carrot dish tasted amazing, but left me wanting more. The green garlic pizza was fantastic, the crust was thin and charred just the right amount, and the garlic had mellowed in the fire and merged with the cheese in a giant bout of deliciousness. 

I had a great time, but I spent more than I felt I should, and wasn't entirely satisfied when I left.

Delicious, fresh, local, sustainable, and did I mention delicious?

The housemade boar sausage was excellent.  The burger and fries stupendous.  And that is one hell of a ginger beer.

Well done, Ari & Eric.  This place is a winner.
First time here. Yay. It's nicely lit, live that we just walked in, got on the list and chilled at the bar while we waited. Food is simple, veggie heavy, interesting pizzas and yummy fish and foul.

Go for the drinks, eat if you're hungry.

I've been to Gather twice, and I really wanted to like it but came away underwhelmed with the food both times.  The drinks are a different story - tasty, strong, and well made.  
The first time I had the burger - the grill must have been too hot because I ordered it medium and it came to me blackened on the outside and a little underdone in the middle.  Though I will say that the fries and aioli were good.  
As that was the first month they were open, I decided to give them a second try this weekend.  I ordered a saffron mushroom stew, with came with a poached egg on top.  The stew was tasty and and the egg nicely done, but the mushrooms were rubbery which means they overcooked them.  Plus the italian butter beans, which the menu said the stew would contain, were completely missing.  Overall, it was fine, and I had no problem eating the entire dish, but given that it was the most expensive thing on the menu ($20 for stew!!!), I expect better.

Overall, given that you pay a premium to eat or drink at Gather, I feel that what you get needs to live up to that premium.  The drinks do the job, the food, not so much.

Pretty good stuff! I like the mix of hard-core vegan recipes (with lots of fake things like "ricotta" and "ice cream" in scare quotes) and absolutely meaty dishes. There's not a lot of in-between.

Everything was tasty, with pretty good value. Chicken-fried kabocha squash, ordered because it's a hilarious concept, was in fact hilarious, and tasty, on the plate although if they could find a way to make it crispy...

The sound track was pretty bad - like a baby boomer college reunion. I think I heard 'Brown-eyed Girl' and 'Do You Love Me (Now That I Can Dance)'. And sure, it's Berkeley, it's a boomer-heavy crowd, but it's also right on campus so there are younger people eating as well. Please improve this!

I love hearing prices with the specials (instead of having to ask, or guess, or be surprised later), and I love free in-house sparkling water. Defining vitellone as "pasture raised young cow" is a stretch. Again, I know it's Berkeley, but it's veal, and it's okay to eat it if it wasn't raised in torment (and it sounded really good, but we weren't feeling super meaty that night so I can't review it)

came here before a play at the rep

the star of dinner was definitely the nettle thin crust pizza, with and without pancetta
the lobster meatball tasted like falafel which i normally enjoy but i not in lobster form
the salmon crudo appetizer was tiny! but tasty. whereas the pork belly appetizer was huge and heavy - could have been an entree itself
Kale salad was good, not bitter
Sea bass special was a bit bland
If I was famous and could afford eating food like this at every meal, I would.

So many reviews, I'll keep it simple...

Pros: Bright, beautiful, and tasty food. A great option for a meal if you need to find a place that will satisfy a vegan, vegetarian, pescetarian, and gluten-free eater...also works for someone who eats everything and just like good food.  

Cons: Beautiful space with 3 distinct areas: outdoor patio, bar, and main dining room....but fairly noisy and crowded. Not a huge consideration since the food is good, but something to consider if you need a quieter place to eat depending on the occasion.

I would like to thank the evil genius behind the menu who decided to combine pizza with runny egg yolk. I wasn't huge on their popular sampler appetizer but their pizza and beer selections are superb.

Love, love, love this place!  We had the  vegan charcuterie, kale salad, and the mussel pizza.  All of it was super tasty and good sized portions.  I believe the beverage I had was a Bee Sting which had just the right amount of honey and booze.   I don't recall being shocked by the bill either.

Going back again soon even though it is quite out of the way for a SF person BARTing about.

Their food had the makings of excellence: emphasis on fresh ingredients, creative pairings.  However, the food was over-oiled and over-salted.  I found it unpleasant and needed a lot of water to get it down.  The food was tantalizingly close to 5 stars but ended up unpalatable because they overdid the oil and salt.  I couldn't manage to eat a full meal.  The dessert was likewise over-sweet.

Basically, I'd describe it as a bad version of the food served at Plant.  They're going for the same thing, but Gather drowns the food's flavor out.

My thought is that perhaps they are targeting a crowd that is unaccustomed to eating vegetarian food, so they overdo the oil/salt on the vegetarian food to appeal to people who otherwise would dislike the absence of meat.
Just barely 5 stars, but we did really love all of our dishes.  The wine was just OK.

A welcome addition to the Berkeley restaurant options. My husband and I enjoy coming here when we are going to Berkeley Rep. This is a "cool" but sophisticated option  and fun for us as we come from San Francisco to the theater.  
The food is excellent, really excellent. Vegan charcuterie is so creative, the table next to us got a pizza that looked delicious and they were very happy about it.  We have eaten here 3 times and have never been disappointed with anything we ordered. 
I agree with some of the other reviews that they are working out the kinks of the service (getting water to our table has been slow but that was it), we always come on the early side too --maybe don't visit at the most crowded times.
Looking forward to returning and trying more of the dishes.

Came here with my boyfriend and his mother when she was staying in the area. We sat, which started out being really nice, as I was directly under a heat lamp (I feel like a lizard, but I'm most cozy when I have some kind of heat source blasting me) and it was still light enough to see. We ordered a few different appetizers (a salad with roasted vegetables and creme fraiche) and a sausage, and for our entrees the two of them ordered a burger, and I went with half a roasted chicken. Our server seemed a little off - we speculated he was either very new, or just about to quit - just had a strange vibe about him that felt a little frantic, disorganized and awkward. I would feel him hovering over us and then he would place a fork down and just kind of scamper off. The creepiness of it may have been escalated by their biggest issue - as the sun set, it got DARK!!! There was very little (if any) outdoor lighting and it became increasingly difficult to see what we were eating. By the time they brought the salad (that arrived at the same time as our entrees - kind of a bummer and not very well thought out) I couldn't see anything and wouldn't be able to tell you what the hell was in the salad. It became more than an annoyance when I had to try and eat half a chicken in the dark and almost chocked on a bone. Every now and then someone in the building next door would turn a light on, which would help tremendously, but as soon as it would go off, we were stuck experiencing our meal minus one of our senses. 

The food was tasty, nothing blew my mind or was really worth making the trip over here again, but I liked what they were going for. I think once they work out the kinks in their service and overall experience, they'll be worth a second visit.

The waitress on this most recent visit was fantastic. She totally redeemed the last star that I needed to give this place. Everything here is absolutely excellent. The unique flavors just blow me away. It's definitely more pricey than your average joint. My girlfriend and I walked away spending $80 between the two of us and the portions are not large enough to take anything home. That won't stop me from coming here again... And again... and again. The menu constantly changes and it's very seasonal. Damn, how I wish I lived in the bay area again.

You wouldn't know it from my indulgent habits but I feel very strongly about eating healthy and organic. If you feel this way then Gather is the spot for you!

Gather is located in Berkeley right across from campus for those not in the "know" CAL Berkeley campus. It's a block or so up from Shattuck so it's close to the energy of the Ave yet far enough away from the bananas of it all and plenty of parking. 

I've yet to eat in the main dining room, and that could be because I don't like making reservations. I always gravitate to the back to sit and eat at the bar.  It feels alive with a low roar of energy back there like we have a private party going on. 

My server Carter was a cool guy, I wasn't the only one there but it seems like we were talking about everything.  So here's the great thing about Gather "guiltless eating". I ordered the Prather Ranch burger - (Sierra Nevada cheddar, aioli, caramelized shallot-tomato sauce, fries with bacon) And what I mean by guiltless is the meat is grass fed and treated humanely. Good for me, good for them.  

My dinner was delicious, the burger was juicy and the fresh flavors of the bacon with the cheese and the fresh bun exploded with flavor until the very last bite. 

Here's the bad thing about eating at Gather, after eating there you know what good, fresh, healthy organic food is supposed to taste like and then going somewhere else you can taste the difference.  

Great energy, lighting, people and location. I feel the price is reasonable for the taste and the way in which the food has been raised and prepared; not to mention the restaurants values and green footprint they are awarded for. 

I can't wait to return.
The vegan "charcuterie" is to die for.

Well, I have to say it is good, but no woww yeahhh greeeeaaatt, suuper duuper. Now if you expect woww... don't go. Because I sort of regretted the $160 I spent on this invitation for my family (we were 4) as I thought it would be something very special and it was just good.
I normally don't spend that much on going out for dinner so maybe my expectations about the food and staff were too high, but I wouldn#t go again.

What I love: the source book. The first and only restaurant I've had the pleasure of dining at where I know exactly who farmed which ingredients. As someone who both cares about the conditions of  work for each and all who make our meals possible, and who's needed to become ssuper mindful of the power of food as medicine as well as its potential to exacerbate chronic symptoms and dis-ease for our collective bodies, other beings and this earth, these lines of accountability and info sharing is so thoroughly appreciated and a breath of relief. 

Service always has been great, often excellent. I've been here for brunch a few times using a Chinook book coupon, and dinner several times for special occasions. On our last visit I reserved via OpenTable and included an accessibility request that they accommodated with grace and ease.

Accessbility-wise, as mentioned above, they've been super responsive even to a simple note in an online reservation system. It was clear that there was strong team communication to facilitate an easeful meal. The bathrooms are gendered and multople stalls. They might be one of a handful of restaurant bathrooms in the East Bay where I'm not immediately overpowered by exposure to chemical products and lingering fragrance. During the daytime, seating outdoors is great! And dogs are welcome on the patio.

Why not five stars: while I've always enjoyed my meals here, as have my companions, not each and every meal has been as memorable as those five-star dishes I still remember distinctly in taste, smell, texture, composition, and presentation.

Caveat one: we've only eaten here once.
Caveat two: I didn't pay for it.

Weekend night, packed to the rafters, we snagged a last-minute reservation. Although we had to wait a bit longer than our res time, the staff was exceptionally kind about it-- they brought bread for my hungry little nephew to snack on, and offered us water, and were overall apologetic and sweet. Our waiter was very good, attentive but non-intrusive (a tough balance).

Main event: the food was VERY good. I was prepared to roll my eyes at the whole Portlandia/hipster/blackened-soil-with-locally-sourced-foam business...except that it was DELICIOUS, and fun, and really a unique way of approaching and presenting the ingredients. We ate a lot, four entrees and several shared apps, plus desserts. Every dish had something I quite liked about it, and the desserts were surprisingly well-executed and tasty. Also: I was vegetarian for 21 years, but am making up for lost time these days by having meat with everything. Trust me, I have had enough vegan food. That said, the veggie dishes here were excellent and did not feel like an afterthought. Unfortunately I can't recall the wine, but I had something by the glass that was also quite good, a local red. I take my hat off to you, Gather, and apologize for pre-judging. One note, I guess-- I think it's pretty pricey but the atmosphere is more casual, loud, pizzeria vibe than maybe it should be, considering. Just a thought, but overall: great work.

Amazing, food and service. I am blown away by the use of vegetables and prices. I might go Vegan if all veggies tasted so wonderful. 

I have been there twice in one month. The cardoons are fried but not greasy and perfectly cooked. You have to try the vegen Charcuterie because it is a wonder, a selection of four amazing tastes. The amount of work that goes into this dish astounds me for its reasonable price. 
I could eat the kale salad anytime, it was mouthwatering. 
I've got so much respect for brassicas now that i've had them at Gather. How can a cauliflower taste so good. 
Dessert was amazing and we had to have two of the Frozen Pistachio nougat.

What gives this restaurant a wow factor is the attention to detail with the little dots of sauces to amplify the flavors of the stars. Go but you need a reservation.

One last thing I think the service is casual and attentive. The bus folks know their stuff and constantly on hand for any need.

The table we were supposed to sit it at took their sweet time with their dessert and coffee. So the hostess threw together a smaller but sufficient table for us instead. I love the recycled decor. Re-used wood tables, old wine bottle lamps, even leather belt upholstered booths! (not as kitchy looking than it sounds). We had three pizzas, a salad, and the Tofu skin Braciole. The braciole was my favorite item. The lentils were just delicious. The roasted mushroom and vegan pizzas were also very good. I can't wait to go back to try the much talked about Vegan "charcuterie"!

Great wine list and amazing cocktails. Of course, the best part of Gather is the food. The best vegan pizza I've every had! The use a cashew cream base with a spicy tomato sauce and olive tapenade! Wow!

This is a pretty quintessentially Berkeley place--hipster vibe, organic and locally sourced ingredients, and plenty of vegan options. I've been here four times and thoroughly enjoyed myself each time. 

1st visit: Ordered an arugula salad with plum, smoked ham, and molasses dressing, and had the bee sting cocktail (with notes of honey, lemon, and mint). Both were perfect.

2nd: Had their vegan platter, which seems to be a signature dish. I love meat and avoid vegetarian options assiduously, but I thought that Gather was the place to be adventurous. Was richly rewarded by taking this risk. The assortment of mushrooms and other unidentifiable vegetable items is selected and presented with care on a wooden tray.

3rd: Brunch, probably the least impressive meal I've had there, simply because it wasn't as filling. I had some type of walnut French toast that was delicious nevertheless.

4th: I had a perfectly cooked burger with an amber ale that the waitress recommended for me (and it was a spot-on rec). I tried my friend's pear cocktail which was extremely tasty--if nothing else, I'd go back to Gather to try the other cocktails. This time, what stood out to me was the service. A couple of people in our group didn't order food because they had already eaten, and the wait staff was completely cool with it. We then stayed for close to an hour after they had cleared our plates, during which time they were prompt about refilling our water, and they only asked us to leave when a large crowd of people had begun to amass at the front door, and then in the most courteous manner possible.

Pizza!  On a recent visit, I discovered Gather's pizza, which is maybe the best I've had in the bay area (that's right!).  Completely unexpected, we only ordered it because it looked like every other table had a pizza and the pizza looked good.  Well, it was GREAT!  We also ordered salads and entrees that were good, but really all I remember and all I want when I go back is the pizza.

Everything I tried was good - vegan charcuterie, dehydrated watermelon that looked like beef jerky, spicy oxtail gnocchi.
It felt a tad overpriced though. $16 for a small palmful of gnocchi appetizer? Outrageous.
The server seemed uninterested - I was trying to choose between a couple of things, and she didn't offer much in terms of describing the food. Surprising for a place that prides itself on their ingredients.
Lovely decor, tasty food. Chez Panisse Cafe prices, with less decadence.
Great place for vegans, and I would probably go back if I was on a cleanse and wanted to indulge.

I came here with my boyfriend back when they only served dinner. We conveniently made reservations on their website. The decor was aesthetically pleasing and the service was overall really great. 

We tried the meat plate for the appetizer. The plate had a nice selection and didn't have too little or too much. We ordered the Duck and the Young Chicken. Presentation was nice and the flavor of the chicken was to die for. The gentleman that sat right next to us also had the Young Chicken. It was funny because once he noticed that I had ordered the same thing, he kindly leaned towards our table and stated that it was the best he's ever had and that I would definitely enjoy every bite of it. And it seems he did, because by the time he left, all you saw were bones. Plus, he was right! I would love to order that dish again.

Wine list all highly priced. It was the first time in memory that we had wine by the glass because we refused to pay such an  inflated price for a botttle.  That being said, the chicken and the burger were excellent, the service was very good and the atmosphere was lively.

I have been back several time since my first review and unfortunately I have to scale it down. Although I love the concept of being local, organic, sustainable, etc. and enjoy the originality of the menu, I have had a few disappointments. First, I find the menu a little too encrypted and hard to decipher for the normal consumer. Most terms actually require that you either have some culinary knowledge or that you grab your dictionary for fear of being disappointed with what will show up on your plate. 
Also on my last visits, I found that the plates were fairly small, cooked vegetables too fatty, toasts over-burnt. I had braised beluga lentils on my last visit and the dish was way too oily, the brussels sprouts alienly named "brassicas" were actually fried, I could not stomach it. 
Proteins options are limited to eggs, it would be nice to have some poultry/fish too. I am gluten and dairy-free and there aren't that many options on the menu, especially when it come to desserts. 
I want to keep coming back, so please make the menu more reader-friendly, be lighter on the fats (including pancetta, bacon, etc), don't burn your foods, offer a couple of animal protein options, and be a little more generous. Thanks :)

Gather's innovative menu, excellent ingredients, and hip-but-casual environs makes this my default semi-nice dinner out in Berkeley. 

I've enjoyed everything I've tried here: their pizzas (both vegan and nonvegan) are piled with fresh and creative flavors. Their burger was juicy and tender, as promised. I ordered a daily special of cheese-stuffed sweet peppers that was mind-blowing. And the vegan charcuterie was fantastic. I actually felt like there were fewer vegan options than I expected given the hype - not a concern for me personally, but if you're considering this restaurant as a vegan, there may only be a few main items to choose from. However, they will be amazing, and I get the impression that many of the vegetarian dishes can be made vegan if you ask.

Gather's mixed drinks are strong, clever, and awesome; there is also housemade soda and local kombucha on tap. Amazing. Who does that? Oh, Gather does. 

They only reserve out half of their tables, leaving plenty of space for walk-ins. Gather is busy most evenings, but even on popular nights, I've never had to wait more than 30 minutes (a great time to flip through their Source Book, by the way). They're also open for lunch, which is less crowded, and the food is just as good.

The staff is... rather pretentious. The food is... rather pretentious. But it IS Berekeley, which I guess makes it acceptable.

The barbequed young chicken was delicious, the tempura asparagus was outstanding, but I did not care for the full belly potatoes. It left me wanting a little more texture.

I loved the seats against the wall (made of recycled belts). I'll give them three stars for being original ;).

Gather is that perfect kind of neighborhood restaurant that you wish you could patronize every night.  Hell, every morning and afternoon too.  As many before have said, the vegan charcuterie is fantastic.  But so are the daily specials (although they tend to run out of them way too quickly) and the regular menu.  I've had a lot of vegan pizza in my time and Gather's was by far the best I've had.  The cashew nut cheese tasted more like traditional mozzarella than I've had before - somehow they managed to really replicate the tanginess of mozzarella using cashew nuts.  The staff is fantastic and the atmosphere is beautiful. 

I also like that Gather keeps at least half of there tables open for non-reservations, but that they allow reservations, as well.  The best of both worlds.  

In a nutshell, Gather is fantastic.  Go there.

At Gather you will get sustainable ingredients, classy atmosphere and affordability all in one place. Well it may not be "affordability" of the starved-college-student variety, but it is affordable in the don't-have-to-throw-down-three-bills-for-a-salad-and-a-fist-sized-portion-of-meat variety.

5 stars for the vegan charcuterie.  I'm a huge fan of charcuterie plates in general.  Plus, my friend suggested it because she had tried it a few time before.  Always good, always different.

All the items were unique though my favorite was the watermelon done four ways; dried watermelon was even reminiscent of a sweet beef jerky!

The salad and pizza were just ok, hence the 3 stars.

Brunch on 2/13 @ 1p on a Sunday.  No reservations. After a 15 minute wait, we were seated at the bar. Despite my desire to try one of their pizzas (the people to our left and right ordered one and split between two people), we decided to order the following:

Winter root vegetable-Chanterelle hash (me) - $12
Spicy beluga lentil puree, comes with potatoes, a large slice of bread, "bearnaise", absolutely delicious, wished for more mushrooms & lentils.

Aleppo citrus sausage (J) - $13.50
tomato poached eggs, soft polenta, potatoes
J loved his dish. 

Side order of roasted fingerling potatoes & scallions $4

Coffee $2.25

Total w/ 20% tip = $41

Bathroom pristine.

The service was prompt and ambiance pleasant.

I only wish the server would have informed me that the winter root veggie dish comes with potatoes - I would have ordered a non-potatoes side dish.

Later, my intestines rebelled against the spices (though to me it didn't taste "spicy" compared to other food, like South Asian). 

I still want to return and try the pizza.

Gather is the quintessential California cuisine restaurant.  Everything from vegetables to meats and cheeses taste as if they were hand picked from the farmer's market down the street just earlier that morning.

I arrived for my 7:15 reservation with the gf half an hour early and were promptly seated (always love it when that happens).  She started with a glass of Tempranillo and I had one of the tequila cocktails recommended by our waitress.  I expect the food at a place like this to be top notch, but I certainly didn't expect the cocktail to be as amazing as it was.  Waitress described it as, "smoky and intense" and took the words right out of my mouth.

The gf and I began our meal with the Cherry Gazpacho.  I was both delicious and surprising.  It embodied the "comfort" of gazpacho while also having a nice zing to it provided by the sweetness of the cherries.  While I think it was a large portion of soup for two people (the dish starts to get less...awesome as you get towards the end), I am certainly not going to complain about large portions.

Next, we split the special pizza of the night which had sausage, carmelized onions, and a farm fresh eggs.  Part of me wants to dub it the, "breakfast pizza" but that probably would create the image that it wasn't delicious.  Sausage was perfectly cooked and just the right amount of spicy. The egg yolk provided a great compliment to the other flavors of the pizza. (I actually ate another slice that we had taken home just five minutes after we had gotten home after our meal :) )

We also split the Chicken which was described as, "juicy and balanced".  It was super flavorful and we stripped it down to the bone.  The Cornbread puree that comes with it was really the superstar of the dish and both the gf and I could have just eaten a bowl of that and called it a day.

We finished with the roasted strawberries (awesome and one of the more unique desserts I've tried) and the Peppermint Chocolate Ice Cream (fantastic, but just a bit rich.  We didn't even finish half of it).  All in all a great meal.

This is my current favorite restaurant.  I like that there is something for everyone on the vegan-omnivore spectrum.  I LOVE the spicy tomato pizza and thus have a hard time ordering other entrees.  The salads are all lovely but I carry a major torch for kale.

The dessert offerings for vegans have been just okay but I don't mind because Cinnaholic is only a few doors down.

The food at Gather was wonderful.  The vegan charcuterie had such an interesting and delicious exploration of tastes.  Two of us ate it slowly to savor every bite.  The bread (by request) helped us capture every morsel.  The olive oil that came with the bread was full of great flavor.  I had the eggplant entree and my friend had the roasted salmon special - both terrific.  We ended by sharing the Almond Teff cake, which was another combination of favors.  Corn and basil now seem like reasonable ingredients for a dessert.  I had a soy latte which was prepared beautifully.  I really appreciated that the soy milk was unsweetened, unlike many places that used overly sweetened vanilla soy milk.  

I wrestled with whether to give four or five stars.  I loved the meal and will definitely go back.  Our main server was friendly and did a nice job of letting us sit and talk without feeling rushed.  Other servers brought our food and they were indifferent at best.  One delivered the wrong dessert and it took a while for us to flag down our server to make the change.  She apologized and made the change quickly, so it was not a huge deal.
Overall, we enjoyed our experience at Gather.

it's SOOO good. i don't write reviews unless something's horrifyingly wrong or super wonderful. well, gather is SUPER WONDERFUL. 

vegan charcuterie. get it. no buts about it. you won't regret it. no, i'm not a vegan. yeah, it's really more like a salad medley, but the flavors will pop and surprise your palate. i'm still fantasizing the flavors in my mouth. 

service is great. they came and changed our plates and silverware after every dish.  

we also had the pork belly appetizer and the lamb pizza.  but as the menu changes often i won't go into detail since it might not be there when you go. just remember, the  MUST NOT MISS is the vegan charcuterie!
Open, rustic modern feel that I find relaxing. Ordered the half chicken and vegan charcuterie. Loved both.

Vegan charcuterie lives up to the hype -- delicious.  Was cool because we sat at the chef's counter, so we could see him making them all night.

Tofu pasta was TINY, but it was pretty good.  Very well balanced.

Squash salad was super fresh and flavorful.  Very simple but well put-together.  Plating was exquisite.

Cocktail (I forget what it was called -- something with gin and citrus in it) was very good also -- I asked for it less sweet, but it still came out very well balanced and refreshing.

Service was excellent.  I think the price range for this place is more $$$ than $$ for a full meal.  I want to go back to try their pizza!

Lovely place for Sunday brunch! Spacious with quick service.

Enjoyed my Roasted Chicken Beer Sausage with a Strawberry Fizz cocktail but wasn't impressed by the Acme Walnut French Toast. 

The people next to was were eating pizza and it looked so good that I would go back to try it!

Incredible culinary adventure! Very attentive to our gluten/grain-free needs, and they adapted my husband's chicken dish to include another side (after our waitress did a couple of consultations with the kitchen).

There are a lot of veg*n dishes on the menu, but don't let that stop you.. there are enough meaty options to choose from. We got both the vegan and meat chartucerie plates, a brussels sprouts appetizer, and split a chicken entree.

Exceptional food quality and presentation, and every bite was savoured!

The Vegan Charcuterie Plate at the next table looked amazing, unfortunately, that's not what we ordered.

The space is lovely, nothing like the usual generic restaurant decor, although the cool recycled leather-belt upholstery wasn't very pleasant to actually sit on. Don't be put off by the wall of sound that hits you when you walk in the door. Once seated, we were able to easily hear each other without yelling. 

We were seated instantly, and offered a choice of flat or sparkling water. It was nice that the server volunteered that the sparkling was no charge, without waiting to be asked. If he had been our server for the evening, maybe I would have added a star, but we never saw him again. The woman who appeared to take out drink orders was visibly annoyed that I only requested iced tea and my companion, water, even though she should have been able to see we were still reading the drinks list and clearly not ready. She also didn't bother to mention that the iced tea was a deep red, fruity herbal that was good, but not what would normally be expected when ordering simply "iced tea."  She brought the drinks back so quickly, we hadn't had time to decide on appetizers or salads, so we ordered only mains. I asked for bread, and was told there's a $1.50 charge because they "use a really fancy olive oil." Ok, so being charged for bread is a pet peeve, but I'd much prefer they simply state there's a charge, rather than try to sell it with some lame reason like that, especially since she couldn't even say the line with any believability. But, I was starving, so I ordered the bread. Pity it never came.

After a long, long wait during which our server never reappeared in our section, I managed to get her attention four tables away and TRIED to ask about the bread. She cut me off before I managed to say "bread" told me "it's being plated right now" and ran away. A different server appeared a minute later with our mains, tried to give them to the table to our left, asked if they were ours, and set them in front of us. A minute later, a different server tried to give us the drinks belonging the table on our right.

Given that the restaurant sells itself as the Berkeley locavore place, that they key their menu with locavore, vegan and gluten-free icons, and encourage you to view their source book, I found it odd that nothing on their menu was marked with that L. The burger and fries were nothing special. The burger tasted unseasoned and was done past the requested medium rare. The fries were fab when brought out, but quickly turned soggy. My gnocchi with mushroom and lentil ragout looked rich and wonderful, but was bland, tasting mostly of salt. No earthy mushroomy flavor. As for the gnocchi, the individual pieces were cut to random sizes, so about every fourth piece was light and soft. the rest were either small bits of watery goo or large, dry lumps. 

I wanted dessert, but the choices were odd. A cookie sampler with no description and a citrus rice pudding with a description that began with frozen yogurt. I wasn't really sure how those went together and didn't feel like asking. The chai was excellent. We asked for the check, asked to have the bread that never showed removed from that check, paid the new check and left.
Great food, great service - I have been back 3 times, and everytime it has been really fantastic.  Love that they support local growers/merchants.

We loved the vegan charcuterie, pizza and draft beer. We always look forward to eating here when we're in Berkeley. Kudos to Gather for giving credit to the farmers who supply their delicious produce, cheese, etc.

This place puts a Berkeley touch on fine dining. Slow food meets eco-consciousness. Kinda wish they had a dress code though - far too many people wearing birkenstocks and fleece jackets. Which is kinda Berkeley, I suppose.

Our appetizer, a deep-fried vegetable dish ("Fritto Misto") was tiny (it featured a roasted piece of lettuce) and definitely not worth the $12 bucks. At this point, I started to get nervous.

But was pleasantly surprised by a hardy grilled half chicken for my entree. I'm not sure what they did to the chicken, but it was very flavorful (perhaps a brine?) and the meat was moist. Well done.

Our dessert, a goatmilk semifreddo, was new to us and we both enjoyed it - the kind of dish you savor one bite at a time.

Re service, I'll just say that we waited too long for our entrees. That said, it was likely not the waiter's fault and I think the kitchen might not be as efficient as it could be.

We also waited for 15 minutes past our reservation which begs the question, why bother with reservations, especially in Berkeley.

Food: 5 stars
Service: 3 stars
Ambience: 4 stars

I'll start by saying that the food was fantastic and the presentation was beautiful. My girlfriend and I decided to split 4 small plates - halibut crudo, pork belly, wilted chicory salad, and the grilled squid. The halibut was extremely fresh tasting and delicate, with great presentation. The avocado was rich and delicious, but I thought the beet salsa was drowned out somewhat. The pork belly was great - the crispy, flavorful skin and fat overcame the somewhat dry center meat, and the squash and sauce was delicious and rich. The chicory salad was very tasty, but nothing special. The best dish by far was the grilled squid. The flavors in the dish were so perfectly balanced; it tasted clean and fresh but also rich at the same time. The squid was cooked perfectly - not rubbery at all - and the watermelon gazpacho was like nothing I'd ever tasted. I literally licked the plate clean.

Overall the food was colorful, fun, creative, and delicious, and the sustainable, locally farmed, etc. aspect of the restaurant is wonderfuly apparent in the food. 

I would say the ambience was very good. The restaurant is laid out nicely and has a great decor. I love that you can see into the kitchen. 

The service was neither bad nor good. Our experience at Gather started out a little shaky when we came in and there were easily 5 or 6 empty tables inside, in addition to 5 or 6 empty tables outside, and the hostess told us it would be a 45 minute wait for inside and a 20 minute wait for outside. She told us we could see if there was an open spot in the bar and that we could also wait for a spot at the counter. Given all the possible seating options, we figured it wouldn't be too long before something came available. Perplexed, but determined, we said okay and put our name down. We kept wondering about all the empty tables since none of them seemed to be filling, so we asked the hostess about it and she said that they were busier than anticipated for a Monday night and they didn't want to overload the servers. I understand the concept, but I still think it looks really bad to have a partially empty restaurant and tell a patron it's a 45 minute wait. Don't tell me I can't sit down and order drinks or have water just because you're trying to baby your servers. I'm sorry, but I have very little sympathy for servers. If you don't want to hustle, don't be a server. We ended up waiting about 20 minutes for an inside table. Not terrible. We sat down around 8pm and our server looked like she had been baby sitting a room full of screaming children all day. She wasn't rude or curt but she also wasn't sweet or enthusiastic. She struggled to remember the specials and, if it wasn't for the busboy and manager, would have seemed very inattentive. Bottom line - the service didn't sour our experience, but it also definitely did not enhance it. 

I will definitely be going back to Gather to try some of the other delicious sounding choices. Hopefully next time the number of patrons exactly matches their expectation for that day of the week.

I have to thank Gather for being a place that I could take my mother (vegan) and also having a menu with options that I could enjoy. I like the place itself and it is very spacious. The staff was friendly too. I thought the food was pretty good but I won't rush back to eat here again. The sea urchin appetizer was nothing to write home about and the items on the plate didn't really come together but the pizza was very good. I think my mom would have rated it higher because she really loved her Vegan Charcuterie.

Gather truly lives up to its name. On Oxford Street in downtown Berkeley right across the street from the UC Berkeley campus Gather was packed on the Wednesday evening my friends and I went. The food was solid, good portions, presented beautifully. We had started with the Fontinella Pizza and the Vegan Charcuterie, get the pizza skip the vegan dish. Then for the main course we had the burger and the roasted chicken. Get the chicken it was a good healthy portion, the burger wasn't very unique and left us wanting more. The dessert menu I also felt was lacking uniqueness and made us wanting more as well. The service was good, and ambiance as loud as it was from being so crowded was acceptable.  All in all a solid if not remarkable meal.

Out of four possible stars for the food: two stars.

I don't remember the names of the dishes we ordered (watch my credibility take a hit), so my disclaimer is that this rating is purely a product of the tastes of my friend and myself. 

I ordered the "Hedgehog Egg" dish (scrambled egg, potato, etc.) and my friend ordered something that was wrapped in bacon. I am sure I got the names completely wrong, but... far too oily. Far, far too oily. We wanted our food to gush with flavor, but my friend felt her dish gushed like Deepwater Horizon.

I can understand how Berkeley foodies will feel offended by this review, so I'll end by saying 1) This is our opinion. 2) I am more than willing to change my opinion, if I am ever back in town.

Out of one possible star for the ambiance: one star.

As a Berkeley restaurant in the style of Gourmet Ghetto, its clean and comfortable. The wrap around windows definitely make the restaurant feel more open. Unfortunately, the view was of the ugly side of Edwards Stadium. This I will NOT hold against Gather.

As for service, our waiter did not really do his job, but it wasn't really for the lack of trying, unless he had a novel means for skimming off the oil in our food.

I love the philosophy behind the restaurant, and the fact that they proudly display it inside the restaurant. Also, it is so cozy, intimate, and well-designed. What's not to love about the place?

My friend and I strolled in some time ago, and we were not disappointed. Disclaimer: Because they are always changing their menu, I feel like there are so many hit or miss opportunities, so it's easy to catch them on a not-so-great day. Nevertheless, the day we came was overall a hit.

We ordered the Mushroom Bruschetta to start, a Wild Boar Pizza, some Gnocchi dish, and Greg's Pisco Sour (egg white cocktail) and the Bee Sting (mint honey cocktail)? I'm not sure if they rotate their cocktails around. Of all the things we ordered, the Mushroom Bruschetta was by far, some of the BEST portabello mushroom I have ever tasted. They prepared the mushroom in this sauce, which apparently the waiter claimed was a "secret" house sauce. We managed to squeeze a few ingredients out of him. I made the mistake of asking him if there was beef broth in it. I mean it was an easy mistake, it tasted completely beef broth infused; he gave me this dirty look and said, "Beef broth?! This is VEGAN." Pretty damn impressive for a mushroom that tastes completely beefed up. Besides the secret sauce, the rest of the food was... acceptable, nothing too amazing or awful. I got the Bee Sting cocktail, which the waiter indicated was one of his favorite drinks, but I was not a fan. The Pisco Sour was good. Boar tastes like pepperoni, and Gnocchi always makes me feel like I'm eating carby barf pellets. 

Our check came out to around $80. It was tasty, and the place is absolutely beautiful. Do come if you get the chance; you can taste the freshness of the restaurant's ingredients out of the food, which is a fabulous experience.

My husband and I came here after hearing so much great stuff about it.  Although we were not blown away, we had a good time.  The food was good and the service was friendly, but when it got busy he had a hard time keeping up with his tables.  Which hey, I understand happens sometimes.  A pleasant enough time.

In one of the East Bay's greenest buildings I was always intrigued by the restaurant's architecture and warm atmosphere that always seemed to be oozing out curbside where people waited outside near the entrance.  When it first opened I thought it was just another overrated, foofy, Berkeley eatery, but it ended up becoming my favorite spot and a major staple in the local dining scene. 

Gather is the epitome of earthy, clean, mindful, Californian cuisine.  Lots of vegan, veggie, or raw options; high quality meats and a selection of organic wines and cocktails.  Last time I tried the very flavorful rabbit meatballs.  My absolute favorite is the fig and goat cheese pizza.  But unfortunately for me it's only available when figs are in season at the beginning of summer.  

The atmosphere is comfortable and natural.  I feel at home when I'm here. The seasonal menu is impressive and with lots of unique dishes there's always something new to try.

Gather serves organic, local food for the most part.  It combines eco-chic methods with upscale atmosphere and high prices.

Vegan options include the vegan charcuterie and a vegan pizza.  
The charcuterie is a bunch of little appetizers served on a wooden slab.  There's a mushroom pate that's very tasty when smeared on toasted  bread; olives mingled with roasted pepper; eggplant pate that tastes like dirt; and some paper-thin radish slices doused in olive oil.  (We couldn't help laughing about those radish slices; at that rate, Gather could serve an entire evening's crowd from one single radish!)  There's also a forgettable corn melange.  All in all, the charcuterie is overpriced for what you get, and a bit rich.

The vegan pizza is absolutely delicious.  Chopped mushrooms and herbs, smothered with a cashew "cheese" sauce, are served on a flexible thin crust.  It all tastes lovely...but is rich enough to cause gastric distress later.  

If you've been vegan for very long, you've probably encountered restaurants like Gather before.  The chefs are omnivores who try to make vegan food as rich and filling as meat.  What they don't get is that vegans have lower tolerances for rich food than omnivores, and would actually prefer less oil.  

Still, Gather isn't a bad choice if you want to dine with affluent omnivores.

This place is SUPER vegan friendly! They have many many vegan options and non-vegan ones as well. They also serve gluten- free dishes for those who are allergic to gluten. The nice thing about it is that they put clear symbols next to the dishes on their menu that comply with specific dietary restrictions some people might have. 

Came here a little bit before 5 pm for a table and there were already around ~5-6 people waiting outside! I was able to be seated immediately upon opening. The decor in here is sooo cute! Super cozy and classy at the same time. 

I ended up getting the vegan pizza made with cashew "cheeze". It had olives on it and a super super thin crust and let me say, it was AMAZING! Couldn't have picked a better vegan dish to order! I was debating between the pizza and the charcuterie but was in the mood for something warm as it was a cold day, maybe next time! My friend ordered a burger and said it was one of the best burgers he's ever had. 

So for all you vegans out there, don't be afraid to bring your non-vegan friends here as well! They'll definitely enjoy it as much as you do.

My best tip? Come here early if you want a spot to sit, it was PACKED by the time I left! Would definitely love to come here again to try other dishes on their menu, but it is a bit pricey.

I ate dinner here last weekend.  We sort of ended up here because we couldn't get a table at the first place we tried, and boy am I glad that happened.  This was, hands down, one of the most delicious and interesting meals of my life.  I'll break it down:

The ambiance:
Very chic and enjoyable.

The drinks:
The drink menu was so fun!  I tried the Huerta Vida.  Which was good, although tasted pretty heavily of Mezcal and I had trouble tasting the other ingredients.  But, still good :-)  And I am not much of a drinker, so my opinion here probably shouldn't count....

The food:
I had the vegan "charcuterie."  It was to die for.  So interesting and so GOOD!  Some of the best bites of food I have ever put in my mouth.  First of all, I am a vegetarian... so I REALLY appreciate the menu.  It was nice that the vegetarian/vegan food on the menu was well thought out, and care was taken to make an interesting and delicious dish.  So try this dish, you won't regret it.
