All in all, I will be going back :-)

Excellent in every way. I love that they serve you water in Straus Family Creamery jugs and that the booth seats are made with recycled belts. Sustainability is smartly laced in to its interior as well as its delicious fare. 

The vegan charcuterie (as I'm sure you'll read and hear about over and over, and for good reason) is a must. Each and every dish on the platter is absolutely mouth-watering and plated with such sophistication. I literally finished the entire platter myself and proceeded to wipe the plate clean with the complimentary bread it was that delicious.

And their pizza? I thought cheeseboard was the God of all pizzas, but they have a close competitor at Gather. The crust is insanely good. A perfect blend of crispy and chewy. My sister and I were in disbelief of a neighboring table, who left almost half a pizza's worth of uneaten pizza crusts and joked that we should've plopped our rears next to them without introduction and started helping ourselves to all that crusty goodness.

You can basically eat a meat (and dairy!) free meal here and either be enthralled and refreshed as a vegetarian or vegan, or surprisingly satisfied as a meat-eater, although I did have a meat dish (the crispy pork shoulder). And while it was on the salty side, it was melt-in-your-mouth and perfectly portioned, demonstrating Gather's prowess as a restaurant for all audiences.

The only disappointment I have experienced so far is the dessert. I had a plum tart with a beer ice cream. The ice cream was chalky and the pastry wasn't buttery or hot enough. A disappointing end to one of the tastiest meals I've had in a long time.

But really, the savory food is so blow you away good that it compensates for a mediocre dessert experience and still walks away with a five star rating.
far too foo foo for me.. i prefer saturn cafe across the street.

The food here is good, the service is so-so. They only get three stars because they, in my mind, are super hypocritical. "Local, organic, sustainable.. but most of our food is based on refined wheat flour that is not grown in California".

The Kale salad and the egg pizza are pretty amazing, though.

My friend and I went to Gather for brunch and came away with mixed reviews.  We were disappointed to find that by 1:00 they were out of the french toast.  We both ended up getting salads; mine was the green salad with blood orange, she ordered the kale salad, then we ate off of eachothers' plates.  Both were delicious and well balanced.  I was particularly impressed that the kale wasn't bitter in the slightest.  The woman next to us was raving about her soup and her pizza and everything coming out of the kitchen looked yummy.

Unfortunately I was disappointed in the cocktails.  I've been on the hunt for the perfect Bloody Mary and was quite turned off by the one at Gather. It was just too much.  With horseradish, thyme, basil, ginger, tamari, and jalapeno there was a cacophony of tastes which overpowered the tomato flavor.  My friend wasn't thrilled with her drink, The Hemingway Revolver, either.  It too offered strong taste up front but no depth.

Everything considered, the food, the cocktails, the vegan/vegetarian offering, the emphasis on organic, seasonal, all combined makes Gather a satisfying place to eat.  Just don't go there if you have your heart set on boozing it up at brunch.

Thought about giving this restaurant a 3-star review, but it certainly is not A-Ok; it's between 2 and 3 for me and my party.  Last night the kitchen was terrifically slow.  The waitress was fine but the food just wasn't coming out.  A hamburger took forever; the appetizers too.  These were quite simple items to prepare.  The appetizers were so small and so expensive it was a crime.  A pluot salad was only one piece of fruit cut into four.  The squid appetizer had about 5 tiny pieces.  All beautifully presented, but where's the beef?  We've gone there often, since the early days too, but if last night was the future I don't think we'll be going again.  Not helping was the noise level; I'd say about 4 bombs.

This is a place I really wanted to love. The philosophy is so close to mine, and if I were to open a restaurant I'd want it to be just about identical. I was overall disappointed due to high expectations but hope to return and enjoy better cuisine.

The bottom line was that for vegan/vegetarian, it just made me miss and crave Millennium. It felt dirty, like being with your SO and only thinking about your ex. Or something. Not that I've ever done that. ;]

A breakdown:

Design/environment/atmosphere, 5 stars. It's cozy without being too cozy and has a  lovely airiness built in through its rounded edge seating and high ceilings. The tables, which are probably reclaimed wood, were incredibly sexy softwood. I wanted one for my own home.

Cocktails, 1 star. Based on my one choice, the "out of the pod," I'd say boooooring! It's supposed to be made with lime, black pepper syrup, mint, and fresh-squeezed pea pod juice. I know a good cocktail is supposed to mix the flavors just right so that they don't really stand out on their own, but mine tasted like it was missing the pepper syrup and mint entirely. It was like gin and peas only. Bleh. Fro $10, I wasn't about to try a  second. Also my friend's $12 Humo Dolce was solidly unimpressive. 

Wine list, 5 stars. All biodynamic, organic, or sustainable from Cali. The albarino I had was solidly good, though I've enjoyed better from Spain.

Food, 2.5 stars. I had all veg/vegan entrees. They tried hard and put the right flavors together, but they fell short of expectations and just made me wish I were at Millennium instead. The least exciting was the vegan charcuterie, which would have been better had I made my own at home. The eggplant and tofu skin (wow, yum! reminiscent of 20+ years ago eating chicken and turkey skins) were memorable and great; everything else was completely forgettable and almost as bland as the grilled-to-hardness bread served with. The other starters we enjoyed were much better (marinated burrata, semolina-encrusted asparagus) but still made me ache for the flavors of Millennium--or even Gratitude, which overall is a bit better.

Service 3 stars. A for effort; he tried. A for eye candy. (I'd take him to go!) But timing and attentiveness were off, and the people next to us had a really hard time getting the correct check and payment taken. Perhaps there was simply overwhelm. I accidentally overtipped so perhaps he'll remember me with better service next time.

I'm going to go back and try a pizza or gnocchi. Perhaps a sea creature. I hope it redeems itself. My overall experience was that the cocktails made me crave Flora and the food made me crave Millennium. It's like being with your SO and thinking about your ex.

**UPDATE** I did go back and try a pizza and salad. I love nori, so I was expecting to like the gem lettuces and nori better, but it just missed the mark somehow. Delicious thin-crust pizza, but with so many delicious pizza options around (Paisan, Locanda, Gioia) it's not enough in itself to want to risk the more unpredictable food options and mediocre service.

Whenever we think of Gather we get hot between the legs.

Gather is the epitome of California dining.  We started coming here about 6 months ago.    This place is always crowded and for good reason. It is a great date spot

The ambiance is warm and inviting.  It has a nice view of an open kitchen. We love how you can look on the board and see all the local places that the meals are from. 

The pizzas are great.  Sauces are delicious and make you want to lick your plate. For the sake of other customers we just as the waiter/waitress for bread to soak all the deliciousness up. 

It is a place where you will eat something that you have never heard of because somehow they will make boar belly taste good and everything else.  The chicken dishes are to die for. Tender, juicy and well seasoned and seems to melt in the mouth.  They know how to combine different flavors and textures to make awesome dishes. A great value that feels like you are eating out at an expensive place for a really reasonable price.

Gather has won our hearts and we will keep coming back for more.  

GAAATTTHHHEEERRR.

Gather is one of those trendy organic restaurants that has good food, great presentation and ambiance, and slightly steep prices. Their commitment to organic/sustainable food sources seemed legit, and though the number of items on their menu that could be labeled truly "locavore" was limited, they were honest about the fact. The Vegan Charcuterie was very good, featuring an assortment of 5 or 6 tiny, artful piles of veggies, sauces, and even flowering herbs. The Chanterelle pizza, a special, blew us away. At $15, we were expecting great pizza and they did not disappoint. It was quite large, too. The mixed drinks looked amazing, but I did not try them. They have a good selection of beer and wine, and the staff are very courteous and fun (with the exception of one woman bartender whom I found to be a bit surly. Whatever, I don't know her life.)

One thing that really impressed me was the kindness of staff. A guy I was dining with had some questions about their definitions of local, sustainable, etc and asked the busboy (sorry if not PC, I don't know the appropriate term), who did not know the answer (and come on, that is so not his job). The guy was so polite, and later, returned with an answer on his way home for the night! It was just above-and-beyond. I will definitely return.

PS: Gather is a great addition to the UCB area. I love Asian, Mediterranean, and Indian cuisine...but ENOUGH already.

Okay, so I realize I am a picky, bitchy hard to please customer when it comes to food.  The fact that I have a sensitive stomach doesn't help matters either.  I went to Gather with a large(ish) group of friends (15 or 16 total people) and the manager came out to tell us (when we were only 12) that 12 is a HUGE number for them and we would have to order 'family style' or deal with having our meals brought out staggered.  Okay, not the worst thing in the world but none of us wanted to share our meals so the dealt with it the best they could.

On to the weekend brunch menu... it is B,O.R.I.N.G boring!  Very egg laden, not much variety and quite frankly I, still, can't figure out what the hell we were being charged for.  I ordered the "bowl" of fruit.  Translation: 4" square plate with the following paper thin slices: 4 small roundish pieces of grapefruit, 4 really small roundish pieces of dry flavorless navel orange, 4 teeny tiny rounds of kumquat, 4 really little wedges of kiwi and 1 strawberry quartered.  And the grand total?  $7.00!  WTF is all I have to say to that.  Actually that's not true: the coffee (they serve Thanksgiving, which I happen to LOVE) tasted old and a bit rancid and WAY too acidic.  Much like how coffee tastes when the coffee maker hasn't been cleaned properly or at all.  Way over priced, zero value vs. quality, really bad service, the manager needs to take a workshop and the overall menu desperately needs a facelift/organ transplant stat!

On the positive spectrum of things I like the recycled wine bottle light fixtures, the recycled belts they transformed into cushion on the bench and the reclaimed wood they used to make the tables.  GREAT way to repurpose things!  A+.  However, putting up to 20 frames of The Far Side comics in the actual bathroom stall was utterly DUMB.  Why would you encourage people to stay in the bathroom stall???  I could have stayed in there until I read every last frame however I was hissed at when I took too long.  Either line the hallway with the comics or put one or two of the 4 framed frames in the stall.  NOT over 20 for crying out loud!  Cute idea but failed on the execution.

The only way I would ever go back to Gather is if it were someone else picking up the check.  There are just way too many restaurants to try and Gather is one I would tell people to avoid unless it somehow made it on their list of places to check off.

Gather's name and locale just scream hippy shit. Their menu is completely local, organic, sustainable, etc. The menu contains numerous vegan and gluten-free options (a negative, in my opinion; where's the beef?).

Tangent: If you're not allergic to gluten, but still eating a gluten-free diet, then you're just a fucking moron. By voluntarily not eating gluten, you're just promoting further gluten intolerance among the general population. Way to go, douche!

Appetizers were dirty hippy style. We started with the vegan platter (my girlfriend sold me on it, and it looked beautiful) and the squid appetizer. The squid was great. It was like a squid and chorizo black-bean stew. Very tasty.

The vegan platter looked much better than it tasted. One of the items contained mushrooms and a creamy white sauce. I was blown-away by how creamy the sauce was, even though it contained no dairy. However, aside from that one item, everything else on the platter tasted, well... vegan (again, not a good thing).

The entrees are what really earned Gather it's 4-star rating. I ordered the duck breast. My girlfriend ordered the chicken. Both were cooked to perfection. The chicken was roasted nicely. The skin was crispy, the meat had flavor, and it wasn't dry. The duck breast was also fantastic. Again, the skin had a bit of crisp to it. Very well done.

The best thing about the entrees was the portion sizes. It was probably the largest amount of duck breast that I had ever been served in a restaurant. My girlfriend got half of a chicken on a plate. Nuff said.

Desserts were about as good as Chez Pannise, which means that they weren't very good. Our waiter recommended the parsnip cake. It tasted just like it sounded. Hippy shit to the max.

So go to Gather. Check it out. The hippy shit's flying all over the place here, but the entrees more than make up for it.

I admit that I wasn't too thrilled to dine at Gather for pretty much no reason at all.  There was a person that we used to know who used to work there and she WAS pretty lame, but as my friend pointed out, " she HAS been fired from some pretty nice places." Also, don't you just hate being in Berkeley? The panhandlers are just dirty bratty kids, ORGANIC is screamed from every window, and GEEZ, the sheer amount of Yoga studios with clever names makes me feel uncreative; Yoga Room, 4th Street Yoga, Berkeley Yoga center, how do they come up with those?

We were sat right away and made what we thought was a pretty sweet joke about how, "these tables look pretty good for being used, ha ha ha ha," only to read on the way back from the bathroom about how the tables were old gym bleachers! Touche, Gather!  They got us again with the water pitchers (Strauss Creamery containers) and we were sure that our server was wearing glasses that he fashioned from an antique kaleidoscope and old piano keys. I felt proud to be wearing the feather earrings that I got for my sister for Christmas, I mean, I'm ALREADY recycling them before I give them, not to mention that they fell off of a bird!

Yeah, the food was great, but what really impressed me was the menu copy.  Too many restaurants these days have menus that are in everyday english and then when you want to zap someone with a zinger on Words With Friends or "Check In and Tag Friends," on facebook, you look like an asshole for whipping out your iphone!  Not this place, they feature such gems as "Erba Stella," "Guanciale," and "Brassicas.! Everyone was like, "huh?" for a second and then we all grabbed our phones and checked in on facebook, so we had to find out that brassicas were just cabbage from our server, but the point is, that we didn't LOOK tacky and rude.  

I can't say enough times how yummy the food was. We gobbled it up too fast! 

I take one star away for not getting the comic in the bathroom about "Mary sitting down to have a little lamb for dinner," only because I usually get comics right away.  Well I guess that's not fair, because I also didn't understand any of the specials that our server told us about, so I guess I just have to get used to not getting stuff at Gather. ( Yes, we probably could have asked him what the hell he just said, but we preferred to burst out laughing after he walked away. )

Don't forget to save room for dessert and stop by the bar on your way out for a rousing game of Spot What IS NOT Organic.  (hint: they try to hide it!)

I went to Gather not expecting too much, thinking it would be just another foodie restaurant experience, kind of hoitie toitie and self important. But I was pleasantly surprised, the vibe there is laid back but happening, the space is inviting and well laid out. The decor is cool, the bar is beautiful and the tile behind the bar is amazing. Our meal was great. We had the vegan charcuterie (the best), fried cardoon fries, fish and a vegetable ragout. It was great to have so many vegetarian options (and not be stuck choosing the only veg option like at so many restaurants). We finished with the chai creme broulee which was totally heaven. Looking forward to going back.

agree with all the reviews about the space and setting being romantic, earthy, and tasteful. wood beans, dim hanging lights, wood boards for the check, big open kitchen surrounded by (fake?) hanging olive branches. bar tucked in the back to entertain yourself while waiting for a seat. i read mixed reviews when gather first opened and didn't expect it to be so packed. i was also fighting apprehensions that all the talk about "gluten free", "vegan" and "local" might be a little too much kumbaya for me. thankfully i never felt the urge to bust out in song (well, that one). this place is vegan, vegetarian, and meat lover friendly as there are options for all. we shared the "vegan charcuterie" (4 different veggies in 4 preparations) served with bread, then the kale caesar and pancetta, arugula and onion pizza. the first time i had ever seen kale in my life i was working at the undergrad dining hall, using kale as the decorating garnish under the meat plates at the deli counter. i had since categorized kale as bitter, tough and basically not a food group. this kale was delicious. then on to the pizza - superb thin crust, melt in your mouth, just the way i like it. this pizza sang to a different tune in my mouth - definitely not kumbaya. i will be back for brunch..
update - i've had the brunch. it's good. portions on the small side and not enough egg options for my liking (many "soft cooked eggs"). depends on what you're in the mood for of course..

The restaurant was filled on a Thursday night at 7 PM. 

 I liked the decor and overall atmosphere.  The noise level was a bit high but no worse than 95% of the other good restaurants, and we were able hear each other without shouting.  The server was knowledgeable and very pleasant.

Our dinner was excellent.  We all had the pan seared rock cod (Seared Fort Bragg rock cod - "Long Island Cheese" squash stemperata, pistachio pesto) that had a medley of very interesting flavors. The portion was ample, and the price reasonable ($19).   

We shared the fried cardoon (artichoke like vegetable stem)  with almond pepper sauce, grilled scallion salsa  and the Monterey Bay Squid with leek tomato ragout, cannellini beans, mint, lemon, housemade sausage. Both appetizers were unusual and delicious.

For dessert, we shared grapefruit and pecan flavored house made sorbets.  Again, surprise flavors that worked.

Including tax and tip,  with one glass of wine only, $40/person.  

I'll be back!

A group of friends and I just celebrated my 29th Birthday at Gather.  The warm, down-to-earth ambiance was the perfect backdrop for a beautiful, sustainably sourced meal.  Gather is unique in that it not only caters to vegan, vegetarian, and carnivores alike, but it delights all equally, which is very hard to come across!  Our group had 1 vegan, 2 vegetarians, and 2 ominvores, all of which are flexible (and vegetable loving) so we shared everything.

We started with the Vegan Charcuterie.  It was presented on a rustic wooden board.  Our favorite components were the baby fennel salad with smoked olives, kumquats, and avocado AND the grilled mushrooms with spring onion soubise, onion marmalata, and oregano.  The cocktails all sounded interesting but my girlfriend and I shared the "Bee Sting," with botanical infused vodka, lemon, ginger, honey, and mint.  And then we shared another.....

The Kale "Caesar" was dynamite!  We all vowed to attempt making it at home.  The lacinato leaves were tender, the roasted carrots carmelized, topped with crispy capers, crunchy breadcrumbs, and almond parmesan.  We ordered a second to share.  Definitely a crowd favorite!

For large plates we shared the Baby Artichokes with smoked fingerling potatoes, black chickpeas, young garlic-tahini vinaigrette, and zatar (similar to muhammara).  The seared panisse was another table fave: a seared chickpea cake served over stinging nettles, topped with braised mushrooms, pinenut salsa, a creamy sauce, and tiny cheese cubes.

My vegan BF got the Spicy Tomato pizza with capers, cashew garlic puree, herbs, and he added mushrooms.  It was really good, so good we didn't miss the cheese, but it was served burnt.  The crust was pretty burnt.  Not what I'd expect from a fine establishment for a $20 pizza.  

Our only other gripe was that the service was less than an exquisite pairing.  Our main server (her name was TJ) was knowlegable. friendly, and professional, however everyone else that came by our table to deliver food lacked finesse.  One lady gruffly came over, asked who had this_____? and set it down in front of the wrong person before we could answer, and promptly went back to the table she had been sitting with on the other side of the dining room.  STRANGE.  And she seemed to be the front-of-house manager of sorts. 

All in all we thoroughly enjoyed our experience at Gather.  So much attention to detail from the plating to the wall hangings (beautiful painting in the ladies room!).  The dining room tables and bar were lovingly crafted by Heritage Salvage in Petaluma, which is a salvage building supply yard and salvage boutique.  I love Gather's commitment to sustainablility,  approach to beautiful, elegant yet simple cuisine, and drive to serve all people with varying diets a fabulous meal.

I really liked this place.  Great atmosphere and service.  We got the Nettle Pizza which was fantastic, very flavorful with a wonderful crust.  Also got the burger which I was not all that impressed with, (I took a star away for the burger) but the fries and dipping sauce were good.  

 For dessert we got the Ginger frozen yogurt, no complaints...very good.

The service is phenomenal; my waitress really left a lasting impression on me without it looking contrived, totally natural.  I loved the Kale salad and would kill to find out what they use as a dressing.  Gave me a slight reincarnation experience which was pretty interesting.  Also, as a vegan and gluten free customer, I felt right at home with the menu.  I would compare this restaurant with a more formal version of Cafe Gratitude.   
Sat outside and felt really comfy under the heat lamps.  Really cool decor.  
It's pretty pricey though so make sure it's a special occasion if you go.

it's gonna be cool!  looks most beautiful, all glowing with lights.  should be open by 12/15....organic, bar, patio, pizza, local food

update:  two visits, "chef at work" producing excellent results.  we tried a lot of the dishes, and really enjoyed the food--from the soup, to the pizza, to the braised lamb, brick chicken, polenta with pork cheeks...
the space is gorgeous.  service still brand new but very kind.
good wine, have not tried a cocktail yet.
great overall place that I will return to.

The fours stars are based primarily on the delicious fig/pancetta/arugula pizza - the pizza was five star. Fantastic crust that was a bit thicker than I usually like but it was so tasty I didn't mind at all. The toppings were first rate (although I would have cubed the pancetta for best flavor distribution) and it was cooked perfectly.

Other stuff about the visit. Although the restaurant looked half empty at 5:30 we were offered a choice of eating at the bar or outside. Since it was chilly outside we were reticent but with their heat lamps it was actually pleasant. Service was good. 

The salads were fine but not as tasty as they sounded. The vegan "charcuterie" was disappointing.

The sardines sounded fabulous - will return to try those out.

I ate dinner here last night with my brother and it was phenomenal!   Looking over my menu, I had a lot of doubts, but when the food came, I was stunned at the flavors and composition.

I had the poached egg for a started and it was unlike anything I've ever eaten.  Beautiful flavor and very well balanced.  My brother had a cherry gazpacho that was quite unique and he nearly licked the bowl clean.   We split a pizza for our main.  it was tasty ... not terribly memorable.  Dessert was roasted strawberries with various accents, and it was a little difficult to "food" but otherwise terrific.    When I say difficult to food, I mean, it was hard to fork.    I think it might work better as a parfait or with a shortcake/biscuit instead of a sugar cookie.

Cocktails were beyond perfect.  neither too sweet nor too strong nor too sour....  just right and terribly creative.   I tried one recommended by our server - Strawberry something...   Did he recommend that because I was a girl?  I thought I might as well just try it, and I was so glad I did!   It was the best fruit-influenced cocktail I've had in ages!

Service was wonderful too.   We closed the place down and never once felt like we were getting the bum's rush.   And this is on a Monday!    We had an attentive server that was helpful with recommendations but not overbearing.   The meal was paced very well.

I'm looking forward to a return visit!   Unlike so many places in The City, Gather is unpretentious and friendly while offering phenomenal food and drink.

great new space in berkeley.  in the typical berkeley fashion, there is a plethora of veggie, vegan and gluten free dishes.  i liked the space.  it was airy and open and the place was full at 6 oclock which is always a good sign.  

the service was good.  we never had to wait long for anything and our waitress was nice and friendly.

food:

burger - nothing special.  kind of disappointment.  there was some aioli type sauce that didnt really do it for me.  it was good, but i would never order it again.  

forbidden black rice - my friend ordered this.  it was really tasty.  it had sea urchin in it, which i had never tried before, but i was pleasantly surprised.

jerusalem artichoke salad - awesome!  this dish saved this from a 3 star to 4 star experience.  my only qualm is that it was too small.  

i would definitely go back.  i felt it was a good value for what i got.  i really do not recommend the burger though....there are much better things to try here.  they really seem to rock the vegetarian dishes.

For my buddy and I to go twice in a week and have a near perfect dining experience both times, I could not pass up a Yelp review. I don't think I've ever been to a restaurant that pays so much attention to ambiance and what it's putting into it's customer's mouths. I must say, pretty much everything that was placed in front of me tasted like heaven. From the charcuterie, with it's amazing mix of flavors to the succulent one of a kind drinks, I was so impressed. This place is perfect for couples looking for a mixed, but balanced menu of vegan and meat dishes. I also think its pretty cool that places that are out to save the world by using all organic and locally grown products, keep popping up more often. A definite 5 stars for great servers & expos (who really know what they are doing), making kale taste SO good and teaching me a new word: bio-dynamic.

O Gather. So close to perfection, yet its best intentions can seem so...calculated? Is it possible to have a heart without a soul? Or is it a soul without a heart?

In every seeming aspect, Gather embodies the best of Berkeley, and more. The interior decor is well designed, and the photos by the restrooms show the original structures from where the tables, wood, and other parts of the restaurant came. I love the architectural display of the employee lockers. 

The food converted The Husband into conceding that a vegan offering can be imaginative and addicting -- enter the charcuterie. After appreciating the assortment of eggplant, a fried tofu concoction that mimics the taste of a BLT, etc., he made sure to order that the next time we visited. Also stunning in our visits: the fish of the day, the pizza (in one special, he agreed that the mushrooms actually outshone the short rib beef), that Niman Ranch burger.

With all the best intentions carried out about local, fresh, sustainable, and respecting the options of vegan, vegetarian, and omnivore cuisine, what could be wrong? The first impression -- i.e., the hosting staff. Michael Bauer of the San Francisco Chronicle (with whom I don't always agree) was on a radio interview, and pointed out how restaurants often staff their least experienced people in the front. I'm not sure if that's what Gather does, but there's definitely the attitude of, "I work here, I will act pleasant because I am hired to do so," but there isn't the sense of warmth or even empathy that you might get from, say, a mom-and-pop operation. 

Sometimes that attitude ripples through to the waitstaff, who again can seem very sweet, yet miss out on basic service: One time I was so thirsty but unable to catch my waitress' attention, and I actually stole leftover water from the vacated table next to me. The busboy happened to spot my move, and brought me a refill. (Maybe a sign that Gather should consider a service redundancy system.) 

Another visit: My sister-in-law got an less-than-best customer service when she tried to call in advance to make reservations for my birthday dinner. No more spaces, but she was assured she could do a walk-in for six people. She showed up at 6pm, fully prepared to wait 30 minutes to snag a table. The hostess told her the inside tables would take a few HOURS--despite a third of the restaurant being empty. Really? (It remained one-fourth empty for another hour plus--again, a systemic planning issue). Fine, she settled on an outdoor table in the very nice patio area, but as the evening quickly grew Bay Area chilly, two of the heating lamps went out and weren't relit. My 3 year old niece said. "I'm cold! We have to get the fireman!" We asked (politely of course), but the lamps must've gone out again, so we gave up. 

The food was excellent (not so much the desserts), the service was friendly enough, but again, a bit of heart was missing. No doubt, I'm coming back to a place that can convince my husband the carnivore to eat meat alternatives, but it'd be nice for Gather to tighten up its seating service. As for teaching heart, well, that can't really be done -- you just have to hire waitstaff who work because they love seeing how great cuisine can create a community, and care that a restaurant's greater survival depends upon them.

This is one of those places that I wanted to like. There are some good things about it - but too expensive to have this many minuses. The options of fizzy and still waters was a nice touch. I'm assuming that they make their water bubbly. 

First - the cocktails were awful - too sweet and too much going on that I couldn't appreciate what was in it. The tequila one - the mescal overpowered the rest of the drink - we didn't finish it. The Pisco sour wasn't a Pisco sour - should have called it a fizz something - cucumber fizz because that's what I could taste - cucumber vodka and sour mix - and that's not a good thing to say about a drink that has lime juice in it. All of the drinks were too sweet. I don't want an overly sweet drink before a meal. The next thing we noticed is that the wine list is more expensive than the food - what's up with that? We had two reds and one white (shared). The Sauvignon Blanc was awful, both reds were ok - but all of the wines were too sweet. Someone has a sweet pallet. The Poco a Poco Zin was the best and least expensive and opened up nicely during the meal. The pinot noir was "sweet" - tasted cooked to me. These were the ones you can order by the glass and probably "low end" on their list. 

The food; Sardines, fried mushrooms, vegan charcuterie plate, squid, burger, rock cod. The sardines were tasty but too much happening - I wanted to "know" that I was eating lovely fresh sardines. I didn't understand the point of the untoasted pine nuts on top as I couldn't taste them nor distinguish their texture with the fish and avocado coming through. 

The fried mushrooms tasted like fried things - not enough mushroom flavor - the vegan aoili was yummy and almost saved the dish. Why use oyster mushrooms for this treatment? Their flavor is too delicate. Kinda like fried crispy cardboard with aioli. 

The vegan charcuterie plate had some lovely touches but also a couple of duds. I love lentils and the the lentils were tasteless - we didn't finish them. The beets were the best - I love beets and these and the carrots were wonderful. The others were fine - roasted sun chokes and broccoli. The general presentation was odd - on a beautiful dark wooden board. If the wood was lighter one could see the food better. Each item was presented like sushi - cool!! a great idea. 

The braised squid was hands down the best thing we ordered. Tender and tasty. The croutons that came with the food were perfect with this dish. I would have this again. It's a small plate but I had it for my main course. It was satisfying.

The burger was fine - tasty organically raised beef but why put all of that junk on it to mask the beef flavor? The house made catsup's was quite good but let me do it please. The fries were awful - In and Out has much better fries. These were way overcooked and all you could taste was "fried" - no potato flavor at all. They got worse as they got cold - and they are cut thinly so they got cold fast. The salad that came with it was great!! I think that it was a type of pepper cress with a version of travisio - lovely. 

The rock cod was a bit over cooked, salty, and too busy with the flavors/ingredients. Individually the different sauces and purees were interesting - but together I got nothing much - underwhelmed -  this dish was the most expensive and we left most of it untouched. 

One wonderful thing I noticed as the evening got busier is that we could hear one another talk. How refreshing!! 

The dessert list did not inspire us - And we needed to be somewhere else so we didn't have any. 

I appreciate the locavore, organic, and vege/vegan perspective - but in general the food and drinks are over manipulated. Right now it feels like they don't let the products shine and they are reaching too hard to be creative. Complex can be good but it has to fit. 

The service was ok. When we wanted to know about ingredients in the drinks and food our waiter went and found the info. At one point another waiter came over and explained what was in the vegan charcuterie platter - very helpful as they use the words "butter" a lot when they aren't using animal's milk for butter or cheese). The waiter was pleasant and cheerful - just needs more seasoning. The pacing was great - he knew where we were with our meal. When we told him about the fries he wanted to know so he could tell the kitchen.

I think that this restaurant has potential but they need to have some non-sweet before dinner drinks and a reasonable and accessible wine list. Serious wine drinkers would be unhappy here - at least from what we had. They also must get serious with their creative food (and much of it is very creative) - so that these wonderful ingredients shine and not be masked by too many ingredients and they need to be a bit more careful on execution 

So they've been open for 3 weeks or so. I hope that they improve because I'd really like them to serve serious outstanding local organic f

I take all out of town visitors to Gather.  It is always a happy experience, with good food, ambiance and service.  My family has always had one restaurant where we feel happy and our spirits can be lifted just by going there to celebrate, get over a disappointment, or just feel like a familiar space.  Gather is one of those restaurants for us.  I appreciate that they have decorated with re-purposed materials and that the food sources are so transparent.  I used to take guests to Chez P, but now I skip that and go straight to Gather.  Breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner - all have been terrific!

We tried Gather for a nice date while my girlfriend was in town for the week.  Very glad that we had a reservation, we arrived at a packed restaurant at 7:00 on a Saturday night.  I was happy to see that it was crowded and doing well.  The super-local and fresh attitude at Gather is a little bit over the top for me, but I do appreciate the effort.  There were a decent number of choices on the menu in addition to two daily specials.  The wine list is small and the beer list could be much better, but I was able to get a nice IPA anyhow.  The food was delicious and of course very fresh.  I really enjoyed the burger with Sierra Nevada cheddar, aioli and caramelized shallot tomato sauce.  The atmosphere was loud but quite pleasant, and service was very good, with even the busers willing to help out with water refills (complimentary still or sparkling, which was also a nice touch).  I will be back for more.

Came here on NYE and had the pre-fixe vegan menu... my dining companions had a mix of the meat and vegan menus.  

Vegan Menu:
Beet salad
Foraged and sea vegetable melange
Smoked artichokes with black rice and cardoons
Chocolate mousse with citrus

(these titles really don't do much to describe the dishes or do them justice)

First - my meal was amazing.  Every single dish was just delicious, fresh, perfectly seasoned, creative - - I loved it!  The drinks were also great (one of my fave Moscow Mules I've ever had, probably due to their housemade ginger soda).  Service was courteous and prompt, but a bit lackluster.... with such complex dishes (everything had a title and subtitle about a paragraph long, but still managed to not list what was actually in the dish), we just wanted a little explanation of what was going on so we could enjoy it more.  Once we specifically asked for this, she readily complied.

Anyway, the only things I found off-putting were the meat main (rabbit?! I get that it's trendy now, but doesn't seem like that would resonate with a lot of people's interests...) and it was a bit pricey.  But that's probably to be expected for such high quality food and on a special occasion (food+2 drinks+tax = $250 for two people).

I definitely wanna go back and try the vegan charcuterie platter on a regular night.

I've been here about 5 times now and it is one of my favorite restaurants. It's the only place I know where I can go to dinner with vegan friends and everyone will be happy (vegas, vegetarians, lactards, carnivores, etc.). They have something for everyone and their menu changes regularly.

The pizzas are great and you can get an egg sunny-side-up in the middle. Also, the c-word (you'll see it in the review highlights) is tasty and is one of the best vegan things I've ever hard. Their vegan desserts are pretty good too.

I loved this place! I went here along with my husband randomly one night while looking for a spot to eat. I remembered hearing about this restaurant awhile back on check please bay area and wanted to go check it out. But with busy schedules I totally forgot about it till now. 

The inside of the resturant was really loud . There were a lot of people packed inside. (it was a Wednesday night) since my husband and I randomly walked in, we did not have a reservation . But lucklily the host placed us near the kitchen. Right in front where we would see the chefs in action. I actually didn't mind seeing how my food was prepared , instead of staring at at stranger next to me. 

We decided to get the ranch burger, guanicale , and the vegan charcuterie .

All of these items were to die for ! Everything was prepared with so much care and love! You can taste it  with every bite . 
Out of the whole meal I would have to say the best part was the vegan charcuterie . We actually did not initially order this because we didn't know what it was till we saw it come out to be served to someone else. I have never had total only vegan food before . I thought it was going to be not so great. But I was wrong.. Perfection .

I would definitely come back of the prices were not so up there.  But I may have to for that charcuterie !
Vegan Split Pea Soup and Vegan charcuterie were both AWESOME!  So was the service!

I've been here a couple of times and I love it. The menu is simple, there's vegan and gluten-free options along with meat and fish, some lovely cocktails and excellent wine. I love that everything's locally sourced and sustainably grown and harvested. And I love their creativity- last time my date and I had squid with watermelon to start and it was amazing.

I've never had an issue with a table. I've made reservations and I've happily sat at the bar. There's an outdoor area too that looks quite cute.

The venue itself is green and eco-friendly while still being hip enough to bring a first date. Not too romantic, so they won't think you're trying to move in, but not school-cafeteria-ish either- it's like a hipster bar, except with food and without PBR. It's not too loud, either, so you can hear each other talk. It seems like it's reasonably accessible if you have a disability, too.
I have never been disappointed by the vegan charcuterie or the pizzas. Often a place I bring out of town guests!

Gather has some things going for it. The fizzy drinks are terrific. They make their own ginger beer and have sparking water on tap. But the positives end there. The service at this place is ATROCIOUS.  I wonder if the staff has spent most the day smoking pot at the nearest pot dispensary. They move like tree sloths and seem completely disinterested in their customers. The last time I was there -- and it's the last time I'm ever going to be there -- was this week. It literally took 30 minutes for the staff to ladle out a bowl of soup and deliver bread. The place seems to have severe managerial problems -- at least during the day. No one seems accountable. No one takes ownership. No one has any energy. If the food were spectacular, I might be willing to endure this. But it ain't that great. With so many places to eat in Berkeley that offer attentive and respectful service, why would anyone gather here?

I went to Gather with a bunch of friends.  They weren't _my_ friends -- well, not until halfway through our drinks.  There were 11 of us and we were seated quickly (Friday night no less!)

My general review: The place had nice decor, service was friendly but clearly still new, the food ranged a lot but nothing was terrible, drink quality also ranged a lot, overall worth checking out.

Here's the details:

Stick to the cocktails on the menu for now.  It'll probably get better later, and be patient!  They take their time making those drinks for you.  They aren't mind blowing and the server might spill a bunch on their trays bringing it over -- but the Bee something or another was tasty.

Adaptability -- I asked for their chocolate stout with a scoop of their homemade salted milk chocolate (as a float) and they were really nice about making it up.  The drink was awesome -- their ice cream was really really good.

Appetizers & Side dishes: The kale salad was so good.  This was my favorite food of the night. Which I guess is a little sad about their other food, but the kale was delicious!  The fried mushrooms were good -- nothing surprising, but mushrooms are kind of like a good friend, consistent and reliable.  The greens they had as a side dish was chard.  It was underwhelming, not worth ordering for taste but ya know,  fiber is cool.  The polenta was liked by my new friends -- I however was not a fan.  

Main dishes: I ordered a special... pork with mashed potatoes and stuff.  It was good, felt healthy, but flavorwise didn't justify the price tag.  The organic-y localness might have, but it was just pork and potatoes.  The pizza looked and smelled amazing but I didn't try any.  There was a river fish (forget the name) that was boneriffic.  By that I mean it had lots of bone versus being boner inducing.  Pass on that.  Trust me.

Dessert: Did I mention the delicious chocolate ice cream?  I don't even like chocolate ice cream all that much.  There was a pecan dessert that 3 people ordered at the table and was nommed away pretty quickly.  Sounds like dessert was worth it.

Service: For the most part the service was good.  Our waiter was nice.  Cute too.  Only -- the entire time none of us saw him blink.  What would cause that?  Weird observations aside, sometimes things were a little slow and confusing but I think they just need more time to adjust.  

I know it sounded like I pigged out (ok, because I did) but I did try a lot of other people's food and I really had a wonderful evening.  I think it was over priced a bit, but you can make that call yourself.  I'm not dying to go back, but avoid going back either.

De-li-cious!

Yummy ricotta sandwich. I came two days in a row and got that as a half sandwich, half soup. The red bell pepper chutney, chicory (which is basically arugula), and sweet onion spread mixed together in the most charmingly yummy way. 

The butter that goes with the bread was excellent. I ended up eating all of the bread, mainly so I could have something on which to spread the butter. Very nice wait staff.

The dessert assortment was quite good. The dark chocolate truffle was everything a chocolate lover could want, in a truffle. Interesting quinoa mini muffins, yummy chocolate cookie, interesting date stuffed with fig. 

It was a rare treat, and while sure there's always pretension, actually it's really nice to eat carefully prepared, obviously cared-about culinary creations.

PS- the tofu skins in the BLT sandwich are really good. They are like potato chips, except tofu skins. They ought to package them in a bag and I'd happily crunch all the way out.

After hearing rave reviews from friends, I decided to try the Sunday brunch menu with my family and roommate. The place was relatively packed at 11:30 but we were quickly seated. We ordered: Acme Walnut French Toast (2), Spicy baluga lentil with poached egg, Prather Ranch Burger, and the Braised Mushroom Sandwich. The wait for the food was relatively long (might have been the big party that was seated right before us) but the great service kept our annoyance abated. 

The food was actually really tasty and it felt good to know all our food was sent from local farms. Just as the exit sign reads, I do plan to "Come Again" to "Gather" with friends. 

Spicy Baluga Lentils: recommend the poached egg
French Toast: A bit sweet...should order something savory and order just 1 serving of the toast. 
Prather Burger: Filling
Braised Mushroom Sandwich: Yummy.

Ever since Downtown closed, it has been tough finding a decent place to eat before Berkeley Rep, or PFA, or Zellerbach, or a movie on Shattuck: ta daaa, enters Gather! For my money, Gather is fine: it has counters where you can sit alone or talk close to your best friend, and tables if you prefer a noisier setting. On Superbowl day, I was with my pal Barb, and we picked the counter after our movie to catch up. Good choice: the bartender was super friendly, efficient and perfectly sophisticated. I LOVE that he immediately offered us tap water and gave it to us without ice WITHOUT my having to ask the "without ice please" !!! Bonus point for them already on that point! 
 Otherwise, the food was fine: Barb liked her potatoe pizza, and I liked the goat soup enough (I am not an expert on goat soup). I liked my small plate of tender cinnamon lamb with sweet yogurt a lot; tasty and the right size. We did not have time for dessert, so... I will have to go back!
 Ambiance wise, it looks less chic or fun than FIVE in the Shattuck Hotel, and more Berkeley/Birkenstock/MichaelPollanesque trendy -shall we say-. But we got great service: every one eager to help and polite, and we even even got greeted and thanked as we left the restaurant after our meal...which is so darn rare anywhere around this Bay!

I was looking for a different scene for dinner so I hopped on the BART and went over to Berkeley to see my buddy Martin. He mentioned that he and his wife had eaten a couple of time at Gather and both of them really seemed to like it. Since he is the type that usually NEVER recommends a restaurant I figured that this place must really be something. So we hoofed it over from the BART Station (very close by the way) so that I could try it out.

At first glance at the menu I was a little disappointed as the nothing seemed at all interesting and I had a split-second desire to go somewhere else but I stuck it out.

We ordered the Split-Pea Soup and Lamb Chop Starter Salad. The soup was amazing, especially with seemed to be a chile oil drizzle which gave it a kick. The salad was first rate EXCEPT what's the deal with the portion size. Don't get me wrong I understand that it was a starter but really? Would it have killed them to throw just a little more on the huge plate..or better yet make the plate smaller so I don't realize just how little I am getting. 

I digress. We also ordered the pancetta pizza. I thought the crust was right on target, not too thick and with a slightly buttery taste and a nice crispy finish. I would suggest putting just a pinch more sauce so that the toppings and crust don't overpower the fresh tomato taste of the sauce.

Finally, I although the Bee Sting was very very very good, again I have to complain about the portion size. It is not that I want to get drunk after one drink but for the price point of the drink I would like to think that it would be gone in three sips. When the Waiter bought me the drink I actually thought that the glass was one of those small plastic picnic wine glasses.

I would only recommend (strongly) that the owners try hard to get a little more of the middle of the spectrum between quality and quantity.

Gourmet food for a good price compared to nearby alternatives like Five and Chez Painsse.
The restaurant is usually packed on the weekends so make reservations in advance. 
I live next to this restaurant and I frequently swing by for their burger and a glass of wine after a long day.
I also recommend ordering an assortment of appetizers to get a taste of their flavorful dishes made with local ingredients.
Their menu changes seasonally but the food is always consistently good.
Highly recommended!

Bee Sting drink was great. Neither too sweet nor tart, a wonderful satisfying balance.
Vegan Charcuterie was flavorful, well presented, novel.
Our mains were good, not great: Nettle Pizza, and some Mushroom ragout (?). 
Brown Butter ice cream was great, and reasonably priced. 
Service was excellent.

Slow food (a good thing), just as advertised.  All the items our table had (6) were fresh and well prepared.  The kale salad and "little gems" salad were outstanding.  Wine list offered decent selection, but was not overwhelming.  Service was muted, knowledgeable.  The space was fine.

i went again for my friend's bday dinner and was again not very impressed with the food NOR the service.

I had called in earlier requesting the $20 dessert platter to surprise my friend, and the hostess took down my reservation info and said the chef would write her name on the platter, so I figured everything was good to go. However, after finishing our main courses, we were lingering for a bit too long, so I figured I needed to go ask the restaurant about our dessert platter. I pulled a waiter aside to tell him about my request, and then our waiter FINALLY pulled me aside to ask who the birthday girl was, and I was relieved because I thought they would finally serve the dessert platter. But after that, he came back to the table and asked what we wanted to eat for dessert, passed out dessert menus, and then told us that the dessert platter would be $7/person. I explained to him that we just wanted the original dessert platter that I had requested earlier and it just turned into an awkward situation because the birthdya girl was right there. Anyway, to sum it up, there service needs to be smoother and better coordinated. 

About the food we ate that night: we started off with the server-recommended vegan chacuterie (spelling?), which is supposed to highlight what the restaurant is trying to accomplish. There are 5, a bit more than bite-size portions, items that are placed together on a wooden board. While visually appealing, it lacked any real oomph, and later the birthday girl even said she was surprised that the server had said it was the restaurant's symbolic dish. Even though the server explained what each item was to us, I forget what was on our board, but either way, I felt like each item was pretty forgetable. I tasted a lot of hummus-tasting things, and tiny cut-up pieces of vegetables. The chacuterie was good, but not anything special.

For entree, I ordered the seared cod. I was served two tiny, 2" servings of mediocre seared cod. I could make this dish myself and it would probably (most likely) taste better than what I was served. The cod itself was bland, and the texture was lacking the tenderness I was expecting.

After eating here twice, I don't think I will be back again anytime in the near future. The food is tasty, but not worth the money I have to shell out for a meal here.

Oh, and not to completely bash the restaurant, before I forget, the restaurant does have some of the best tasting water I've ever had! I don't know if they have some special filtering process, but it tastes super fresh!

This is a weekend brunch review.

I splurged on Gather even though I really didn't think I had the money to eat so well. My friend and I split Full Belly Farm wheat pancakes with citrus marmalade and fennel pollen butter; I had the egg sandwich, and he had poached eggs on toast. We both added bacon, and I had a cup of tea. We split the bill down the middle and got out the door for about $18 a piece, which is really not bad for such an excellent meal.

The pancakes were absolutely delicious. The marmalade was too sweet for my friend and I thought the fennel pollen butter was so excellent that it deserved to be allowed to shine more, but the total experience was lovely. My companion's poached eggs were perfectly done and he enjoyed his illicit bacony treat (he's Muslim, I'm Jewishish) as much as I did mine. I only eat meat when I believe it's raised sustainably and humanely as possible, and I feel comfortable about this at Gather. The egg sandwich was absolutely delicious with just the right balance of smokey bacon, rich cheddar, killer eggs, and sharp arugula. My only point of dissatisfaction is that the (I think) French bread roll seemed too bulky and unremarkable for the overall deliciousness of the sandwich.

Service was standout, and the main reason this is a five star, not a four star rating. Our server had someone shadowing her who was presumably in training. Everyone from the hostess to each of the three servers who checked on us at various times was friendly, cheerful, and not at all stuffy. I enjoyed getting a mini-carafe of water (still or sparkling both free) for each of us, although that made it feel extremely weird when every time I lifted a hand someone was there to pour my glass for me, but the friendly and relaxed attitude of the staff put me at ease anyway. Two points stood out about the service--first, we were asked whether we wanted all the dishes at once or one at a time. Second, our server recognized, I presume based on the position of the remaining piece of pancake, that my friend was done with his but I wasn't, and she took the correct plate away. You can train for the first, but the second comes from hiring people who are just that on their toes. 

To the reviewer who asked "Isn't local and sustainable supposed to lower costs?" My answer is sadly no. Industrial food is cheap because government subsidies pay farmers to use fossil fuels to grow corn, soy, and other monocrops that they sell cheap to feedlots and process into the byproducts that are most of what we consume. Small scale, organic, local farmers produce food that is less costly in total--but it's more expensive for the consumer (or restaurant) because the government isn't shouldering some of the burden. With time and work, we can reform our food system so that sustainable, local, organic food is accessible to everyone--but at present I'm happy to pay extra when I can as an incentive to restaurants that take extra care with sourcing their ingredients.

I rarely eat out in Berkeley because the variety of options just doesn't compare to San Francisco. But a spot blocks from my house touting a sustainable, organic menu with great reviews in SF Weekly was too hard to resist. Yes, it's right across from the UC Berkeley basketball gym and you're surrounded by college dates and senior couples. But the space is big and great for groups. Parking is in abundance and they have a full bar.

Food was OK. I'm going to try the pizza next time since that was the popular item across tables. Fried green beans: of course YUM, spicy and delicious. Albacore tuna and crispy pork belly were good. Special fish of the day was small and the creamy sauce bland. I had the herb rubbed chicken and while tasty, doesn't compare to the one that I love at Marlowe.

The modern exterior is rather stark, but a step inside reveals a dining room full of warm woods and a cool vibe.  J enjoyed the warm burrata and a fall  salad, while I opted for the escarole lettuce (huge) and the prather ranch hamburger plate.  J devoured most of my fries, as I was completely satisfied by the cooked-to-order rare burger with all the trimmings.  The meat was of such high quality I would have been pleased to order it raw in the form of steak tartare. 
However, as a white wine drinker, I found the choices by the glass sadly lacking.  The house white, a Santa Barbara pinot grigio, was barely drinkable.  A second choice, a Chardonnay, was deemed dreadful and returned. The wait staff was quite willing to help me find an acceptable beverage and eventually presented an average  blended white to complete the meal.  It seems a shame that a good restaurant which prides itself on great, fresh food can't assemble a decent and affordable by-the-glass wine list for patrons who don't want to buy a bottle.

went for lunch.  one vegan item on the menu, a few others can be adapted.  2 vegan dessert options.  I had the roasted mushroom sandwich (yum!) & a small beet salad (emphasis on small).... and feeling decadent so I had a glass of wine.  went back for coffee & a cookie.  this set me back about $40.

woud like to check it out for dinner, it is good, but not sure it lives up to all the hype.

I absolutely love Gather! 

Our group of three arrived on a Saturday evening around 6pm and got seats at the bar, which were actually great because we could see the kitchen action as well as watch all of the amazing drinks be made. 

The place is lively, fun, chic, but very Berkeley. All of the farms where the ingredients they use that day are listed up on a big chalk board by the kitchen.

Try the Huerta Vida with apricot liquor and habanero oil or the Vodka Smash with cucumber and mint. So tasty and different. 

We had the vegan charcuterie plate, which was my favorite. You must get this! I'm not vegan and I still loved it. 

The pizza with any kind of cashew puree is phenomenal, as is the panna cotta if they have it. 

Note: I'm not a hippie, even though these dishes might make me sound like I am! Gather has the most inventive kitchen and makes simple ingredients taste AMAZING. 

I would also recommend taking family or friends from out of town here for a unique and fun Berkeley experience in dining.

I really love this place, and feel that it embodies everything that is so awesome about Berkeley. In a nutshell:

- Food is fresh and interesting, and I feel healthy whenever I eat there! (though I always eat a ton of their delicious bread and pizza so may be fooling myself..)
- Good drinks and happy hour special 
- Outdoor patio is perfect for a nice day
- Waiters are adorably hipstery
- In NYC or SF prices would be at least 30% more

I usually look forward to my weekly Gather "experience" ... yet today was a letdown. 

Over the past few months, I've consistently taken friends to Gather.  At first I was blown away with their decor and philosophy, but over the months I've noticed their quality and service going down. 

Today I went in for lunch. We ordered the Mushroom Pizza, French Toast, and some Mexican dish with cheese. But of course, it's Gather, so instead it is

Mushroom Pizza with braised leeks and thyme
Acme Bread French Toast with Sultranas and Blood Orange confit, 
Chicaquilles- with white beans...

The total price is $60. Our waitress, perhaps being Sunday, or having a great Saturday night, ruined my Gather experience. 

This review applies to lunch only. Perhaps my expectations are just getting higher, but yeah, Gather used to amaze me. Now I just regret coming here...

How many stars do you give a restaurant that you think has good food but bad service? Hard to say. The last time I went there, I didn't even GET to taste what I ordered, and it was their special, so I probably won't ever get to taste that even if I go back. The waiter just plain forgot to put in my order!! I wasn't about to wait another hour when the rest of us all already got our food and started eating already (We waited too long for the waiter to take our orders, waited too long for the food, waited too long when we asked for more bread, waited too long to get an answer about whether they can make a plain cheese pizza for the kids. . . . This restaurant has always been bad at customer service from the beginning. I thought at first it was because they were new. But they've got to get it together or they'll definitely lose customers. At check-in, half the tables were empty, but we still had to wait 20 minutes to be seated. . . That doesn't look good. I actually don't think their food is so good that it makes up for being treated like that. Part of the restaurant experience is being pampered, and you certainly DON'T get that at Gather.

I'm a fan of fresh, local, sustainably acquired and well cooked meal, and Gather is one of those establishments where I could find one. 

But let me tell ya, what I'm not a fan of is being lied to about the availability of tables. No, I am not Rihanna. I don't like the way my hunger pang hurts and no I don't love the way you lied to me, Gather hostesses... 

My apology for this ranting of a review but someone has to do it. 

So, we've been trying to secure one of your elusive tables for dinner on a Friday night for quite some times now and every time we called, your reservation hostess would readily reply as though she has memorized a script of, "I'm sorry, we're all booked but there are tables in the back patio for walk-ins. The wait could be up to 45 minutes." 

Well, we finally took a chance and do a walk-in for a dinner this passed Friday and we saw quite a few empty tables in the back patio. But nah, not a chance, both of the hostesses droned on with their script and told us that there would be a 45 minutes wait. They then directed us to wait at the bar area if we want to just grab something quick to eat while there. 

So to the bar we went and we managed to grab a small table and ordered our dinner. Since our table was right next to the glass window looking out to the patio with several empty tables, we were able to see that these tables were not even filled by any new patron for the whole duration while we waited, ordered and finished our dinner. This whole process was a total of 1.5 hours. What gives??

Ridiculous.  

Sure, your burger was juicy and delicious, but really, we're in Berkeley, why should one suffer so much pretension and seating snobbery??

Ok Gather, listen, I used to think you were a 5 star establishment but lately  you've been dropping the ball for me. I am vegan and really enjoyed the fact that Gather served fantastic veggie food but also served non-vegan food. Super easy place to take my family because their is something for everyone. Recently though, the vegan menu has decreased 10 fold. Last week I was so annoyed to see 1 appetizer that could be made vegan out of 10 or so apps. One? Really? There used to be at least four that were vegan or could be made vegan. All  I could get this last time was corn chowder broth, hold the cheese. How exciting. The same vegan pizza has been on there for months now. Try mixing it up! I don't know, maybe you decreased what you offer for vegetarians and vegans because the demand wasn't there. In Berkeley I doubt it though. Impress me again because I really want to keep being excited about your restaurant.

Gather?  More like Rather....

Came here on my birthday and had very high hopes for this place.

I heard it was highly vegetarian but looking at the menus, most of the appetizers were vegetarian/vegan but only 3 of the main entrees were vegetarian/vegan and they didn't sound that good.  One was a heirloom ragout and the other was a cauliflower something, which sounded more like a side dish than an entree.  There was 2 vegetarian pizzas, but I didn't come to Gather just to get pizza.

We started off with the Crispy Cardoons ($9) which apparently is like celery but (according to the waitress) tasted like artichoke hearts.  When they came out, they looked like deep fried zucchini which was presented over an "almond pepper sauce" but really looked like Trader Joes "Tomato Basil Hummus."  You really couldn't taste the "artichoke heart" flavor and mostly got the taste of the "hummus" 

I had the mushroom "cioppino" ($16)  When it came out, it had a very good presentation (see attached photo) but the taste wasn't that good.  The cioppino was sort of bland and didnt have much flavor.  The piece of bread that came with the entree tasted better than the cioppino.

The meat options sounded more tasty and eye catching than the veggie options.  My friend got the duck leg which sounded pretty good.

I have to give some extra stars for vegan/gluten free options with an emphasis on local/organic cooking, but I can't say that I was impressed.  Especially for a "green" place I was surprised that all the lighting was all incandescents and not LED or CFLs.

The food was okay but I think the thing that bothered me the most was the slow service.  After the bus boy brought us our water and we waited at least 10-15 minutes just to take our order.  Not to mention waiting for the check.

The layout for this place I think needs to be rethought, there is a LOT of seating for big parties but because there is so much seating, the bus boys and the waiters have a hard time walking around to other tables which I noticed slowed the service.  The walkways in between tables is only big enough for one person, so the flow of Gather is slightly slow.

Maybe we just came on an off night, but I'd like to give Gather still another chance in the future.

Highly suggest making reservations since this place gets really busy.

Gather fuses seasonal ingredients with great ambiance and clearly shows how much the owners care about sustainability. Located close to campus and BART, smack dab in the hub of eco-entrepreneurs at The David Brower Center, the restaurant is a fabulous addition to the relatively mediocre downtown restaurant scene of Berkeley. I can count 5 that are even worth mentioning (not including the Gourmet Ghetto).

While most target low-income college students, cheap food is cheap for a reason - it passes off the costs of agribusiness (chemicals, pesticides, and erosion), onto us in the form of medical bills. So I it's  refreshing to find a place with excellent meals sourced with concern for farmers and the environment that has such great prices. Restaurant eating in downtown doesn't get any better. 

(If you're a Midwesterner, don't miss their Winter Wonderland cocktail.)

THE BEST *FRESH* FOOD EVER

So you want an awesome setting, excellent dining, local food, fresh ingredients, and beyond amazing taste? Heck YES! The place? Gather at Gather.

The menu is tiny as they go by what is local and in season/fresh. What we had was beyond excellent. One thing to take note of--this is not where you go for the extremely hungry as the food is somewhat pricey and is fit for making one "just full".

Our Dinner Menu for 4 adults:
- [starter] Vegan Charcuterie: beets, fennel, asparagus, etc. 
  Doesn't sound appetizing? TRUST ME. Even my parents LOVED it. And they are picky eaters who dislike "meh" food. So yes, this was excellently seasoned, with four different "piles" of arrangements, each with an exquisitely different taste. It might be best not to try and understand each and every ingredient. Just dig in with the toasted bread and munch!

  P.S. I know it's delicious, but try to avoid licking the sauces.

- [main course 1] Pork Sausage Pizza
  It's super-thin crusted, but the pizza was perhaps the best ever pizza our family has tasted. It was again, perfectly seasoned. My parents are NOT pizza fans...yet they LOVED this. Again, they are perhaps the best critics. I mean, if you can win over some picky post-middle-age, Asian folks, you've got it down!

- [main course 2] Barbequed Young Chicken
  A bit on the spicy side, a perfectly cooked chicken comes with well-seasoned beans and cornbread. Might not be to everyone's liking but excellent nonetheless.


PROs:
- the afore-stated menu/recommendations
- fast service
- SPARKLING WATER (yeah, it's just carbonated, but cool nonetheless)
- the patio can still be warm and beautiful on a colder Spring night given that they turn on the outside heaters


CONs:
- parking sucks -- street only
- reservations are almost a must, though if you sit out on the patio, you're probably safe with going without a reservation
- not very filling
- somewhat expensive

OVERALL...A++ for an excellent meal, service, and setting. I would certainly suggest this for dates and small family/friends meals, but not so much for large groups.

I am surpised Gather only shows two $$ dollar signs because it's definitely more than $30/person if you eat like a normal person and have a drink/wine. In my experience, it was about $45/person and we ate pretty modestly. My favorite thing here is the Kale Caesar salad because it's really unique, tastes healthy and it's really yummy. I also loved the asparagus with the fried egg as an appetizer or side. We ordered the "special" lamb pizza which I thought was OK but a little dry. The burger was pretty solid. The pine nut desert was NOT good but I also can't stand when deserts aren't warm. The Zinfandel was surprisingly good because I don't normally like Zinfandel. Our waiter was really friendy and attentive and the atmosphere is cool.

Went to Gather last night for dinner with my girlfriend.   I had a gift certificate to use up and had been waiting for a special occasion to go to this restaurant for the first time. 
 
Started with cocktails at the bar -- they were good but not amazing -- still solid though.

Kale Salad is amazing! 
Pizza was good too - had the fontinella with pancetta = excellent

My girlfriend had the burger and said it was good but not great.  It needed mustard.

The strawberry ice cream had an odd texture - almost greasy.  It left a weird residue on the spoon and was oddly slimy.  I would not order it again.

My girlfriend had the Mutsu Crostada for dessert and said it was overly sweet.  She was bummed as the Mutsu flavor was overshadowed by all the sugar.  

The other piece is that the cloth napkins left white lint all over my girlfriends blue dress.  There was a ton of it all over her outfit at the end of the evening.  

So I have $25 left on my gift certificate to use at Gather.   I would go back for the Kale Salad and the Pizza.   Everything else was just okay.

Really this would be a 2.5 star if I had option.

After dragging a friend to a strange movie at the Shattuck, I knew how I could make it up to her - I'd take her to Gather! I'd gone there the week after it opened and shut down the place. Despite a waiter who was like an evangelical missionary for sustainability, the food and ambiance and conversation had been magical. This was not the case last Tuesday. We walked in to find the place packed; the 2 friendly hostesses suggested the counter -- great for watching the several 100 line cooks and pantry chefs cranking out planks of gorgeous vegan charcuterie. Seriously, I've never seen such a large (and heavily tattooed) brigade outside a hotel kitchen, and it didn't include the protein stations, which are inside! I remembered a fork-tender cinnamon-braised lamb and a complex, raw kale salad, with some sort of citrus marinade (Raw! Who knew?); our waitress said the new version, with cubed celery root, pignoli, and cheese was even better. Our one miss had been the special -- a sardine pizza, which we'd ordered simply because it sounded so hideous, we figured it had to be brilliant. No, it was as hideous as it sounds! Being a fan of both salty, oily fish and cheese, I'd quickly deconstructed the affront to God & Man, and enjoyed them separately. This night's special was also sardines, but chastened into a bruschetta topped with marinated egg yolk, striking the right note of weird yet not insane. While waiting, we enjoyed delicious hand-crafted cocktails, happy in the knowledge that gluten-free, vegan folks aren't doomed to a life of soy matés and kombucha. The sardines were nice, but the newly-bland kale was not in fact an improvement, and the lamb was simply an affront. Not only had the $11 portion been reduced to a knob the size of my (admittedly fat) cat's paw, but it wasn't even tender. My friend couldn't get over this. "That was ridiculous," she kept muttering. "They have the nerve to call that a portion?" When our fun but unreliable (in terms of advice and service) waitress returned, my friend complained, and bless her heart, the waitress claimed to have passed on the information to the chef. We shared the chai crème brulee, which is served not in a ramekin but atop a chocolate brownie thing that was a little too thick for the amount of crème, but yummy. Love the location and the idea, but for $37 a piece, it would've been nice not to have to stop off for a gyro on the way home! It felt like we were helping to keep a whole lot of folks in tattoo ink!

I finally tried it!

Gather rocks a really pretty and fitting decor (with lots of wood!), polished service, and a fully functioning cocktail menu.  Also, it's closer to work than my bus stop.  That's a solid start.

I really wanted to eat healthfully here, but fate worked against me.  I didn't want to take apart a chicken or order a $20 plate of carrots, so I thought about getting the special, which sounded delicious.  King salmon with pressed cucumber?  Yes, please.  However, given that it was an appetizer, and me a fattie, we were star-crossed.

I ordered the burger rare.  It was excellent and quite rare, but also $14.

Short of that fifth star:

-While the layout is sexy, I found the interior to be somewhat cramped.  I spent my meal with people brushing up against me, moving out of the way for servers with wine bottles, and dodging people looking for the bathrooms.

-I'll concede that I've only had a few things on the menu, but regarding the burger, I could've been 90% as happy at Barney's for 60% of the price.

Further study is definitely needed, but now that Gather has been added to my short list of nearby places to pop into with visitors, I'm sure I'll have the chance.

We had a great diner here on the 30th of December. Every item that we ordered was amazing. Our servers were amazing, and their recommendations were spot on.Though the Stinging Nettle pizza had been replaced by a Cauliflower and three cheese pizza, it was fantastic - especially as an appetizer for the four of us. The chanterelle mushroom dish was fantastic, and I'd love to know what the crispy fried garnish was on the top. The squash was amazing, and I would have loved to have more of it. Definite win on the desserts, too.

The only thing to mar the evening, and the singular reason for a 4-star, rather than a 5-star review was that a woman, who seemed to be managing the floor, came over while I was still drinking my coffee and two of our party had gotten up to use the facilities and told us that they "really needed the table." Having worked in retail and food service, I do understand the need for circulation, but none of us were dawdling. We had just had our dessert dishes cleared, and were waiting for those who needed to use the facilities before the long trek home. I still had half of a cup of coffee, and our check had just been returned after having our cards run. Yes, the restaurant was busy, but I felt that this was a bit rude. We were not taking overly long, and it was unnecessary.

hmmmm. Very, very good. The Vegan Charcuterie is out of this world, I had never had anything like that before and I was obsessed. The ginger beer was awesome as well. The burger could have had a softer bun but the meat was great and the fries were good too--the dipping sauce (kind of like a ketchup) was a nice touch. The gnocchi was was awesome too--very flavorful. Service was superb, and we will be back.

Gather Restaurant was WONDERFUL! The food was fantastic, the service was very good, and the two individuals at the host stand were the most friendly and welcoming people I have seen in a restaurant in a very long time. 

The Vegan Charcutterie was very interesting and I would recommend trying it. I sampled new things and new preparations. The fried mushrooms were excellent. The Salty Dog burger was one of the best burgers I have ever had. If there is one weak spot at Gather, for me, it was the dessert. I will definitely return to Gather, but I will most likely skip the dessert. We tried the double chocolate cake with pecan ice cream, warm apple tartlet with bacon, and the chai creme bruele. 

As a side note, my brother who is a vegan who cannot eat gluten is a HUGE pain to accommodate when we eat out - not at Gather! There were so many options for him here, he thought he had died and gone to heaven. They even made him a special vegan, gluten free dessert!

Sad.  I think they have grown too quickly and just can't keep up.  Sad.
Food was slow to arrive, not what it was described as and well, just so so for the money spent.

If someone treats, I will go again....hint, hint!  Otherwise, got other places to go....

Where to begin?  The cocktails (ordered before food) took so long to arrive that we were nearly done with our meal when we got them, and they were absurdly small for the price.  (The Hair of the Cat actually smells like wet dog fur, ew)  The salad didn't have the advertised ingredients.
