After we were seated, some awful band set up and played awful amplified music -- awfully, the singer couldn't carry a tune in a bucket.  We were on the opposite side of the restaurant from the band, and Had To Raise Our Voices A Bit To Carry On A Conversation.  (You had to walk through the band to get to the restrooms.)  The decor is hopelessly dull -- like if Ikea tried to do "edgy."  The food wasn't bad (hence 2 stars, not 1), but merely forgettable.  And to top it off, a patron was robbed out on the patio while we were there: police were called, and all that.  If not for the location, I doubt this place will last six months.  I put "not good for kids" because of slow service and uncomfortable furniture -- and did I mention the awful music?

Seated in the luminous, airy space of Gather, with the open, busy kitchen in the back and pleased diners all around, one cannot but feel good.  The short menu offers a fine selection of dishes for lunch - it is especially nice that all the sandwiches are offered as halves together with the soup of the day, allowing us to sample a rich and earthy red lentil soup with tomato and swirls of smoked olive oil - delightful.

My favorite dish was the grilled squid on goat milk yogurt (think Tzatziki).  The impeccably fresh and beautifully grilled Kalamarakia (to stay with Greek terminology), together with capers, and cucumber "noodles" made for delicious and compulsive eating.  Sandwiches were all good:  I tried the Smoked Tuscan Rose eggplant and the spicy chickpea with summer vegetables (great for vegetarians) and the albacore melt with potatoes and local cheddar - a treat.

The farm egg pizza was good, with its blistered and crackling thin crust, although I immediately regretted not ordering the pizza with guanciale and jalapeño - next time.

The reasons for four stars instead of five:  my little gems salad listed feta as one of the ingredients.  After searching high and low, I found five confetti-sized pieces of feta on the entire plate.  This is a joke!!!  I realized that feta is the last ingredient mentioned on the menu, so maybe that means it is the smallest ingredient, but come on!  I would have loved to taste the feta with the fine greens.  I mentioned this to the (very good) waiter, he only had a shrug for my complaint.

A second quibble is the misnamed "stone fruit" salad that one of my lunch companions ordered, expecting a salad of mostly fruit.  Wrong!  Under a mountain of arugula, there were some fine pieces of peach and other fruit but precious little given the name of the dish (Blossom Bluff stone fruit").  Here, arugula is the second last ingredient on the list, but, contrary to the feta, it played the lead role in the salad.

I finally got to try Gather last night. I have to say I agree with the raves for the kale. It had a terrific texture, and addtions like pickled onions, organic tomatoes and pine nuts were wonderfully flavorful accompaniments. I liked the vegetarian charcuterie, but I don't think it's the best thing ever. I will say it definitely had lots of interesting flavors and textures and is worth a try. I really like the pure flavors in my celery root tomato soup and grape sorbet. The complexity of the broth in my mushroom stew, was a lovely contrast.. Juice from several different mushrooms and a kiss of saffron gave the stew a rich, full, satisfying flavor. The poached farm egg served on top was so creamy, I thought it was cheese at first. Again, it was a wonderful mix of textures and flavors. My one regret was not trying the pizza. Folks at tables all around us were having it and each one looked really delicious, especially the crust. 

I enjoyed my aviation (with actual creme de violette!) and the other offerings on the cocktail menu sounded yummy. The service was good from beginning to end and I really liked the atmosphere. I just wish there were more offerings of wine by the glass. Only one pinot? I know Gather can do better than that. one word of advice, unless you live within walking distance, take BART to get there. You only have to walk one block. Parking is a bit of a nightmare. If you must have you car, give yourself some extra time. You want to be zen enough once there to truly enjoy your dining experience.

Okay food, very poor service, a loud and stressed-out atmosphere.

While Gather makes an admirable attempt at fine-dining for vegetarians, it could use a more balanced menu (if you're going to offer a hamburger, at least offer a few other non-meat mains).  Mixed quality: the squash ricotta starter was good, the tofu-skin pasta was pretty chewy and bad.

We would have more to report on but the waiter *forgot an entire course.*  That's right, skipped the soup and salad we ordered.  The service at this place is very stressed out and hectic, the environment is loud, and the staff clearly is not well-trained.  There are other East Bay options that are far better.

Seriously?  People give this place 4 stars?  Maybe I'm just not cool enough or Berkeley enough to appreciate it.  I went there for lunch, I thought the place was a little...prairie/church like, hard wood chairs and tables, a little sparse.  The service was unimpressive, the recommendation for the more "interesting" of the 2 salads I was choosing between was still only lettuce, add chicken and an ice tea - $20.  I am not a big person and I don't eat a ton but the portions were seriously small and the chicken looked rather unappetizing.  Luckily I read another review that said to ask for the bread, otherwise I would have had to go get lunch somewhere else as well that day.  Also, in addition to hardwood tables and chairs, trendy concrete floor.  Of course this translates to no sound absorption - very loud.  However, the flavor was good.  Bottom line, oh so many better dining choices.

Seven stars if it was possible in yelp. I love all the vegan items. The new eggplant dish and the egg and tomato dish are absolutely outstanding. The vegan charcuterie is "to die for" and I am not kidding. Service has professionalized quite a bit since my last review. Brunch is heaven too. You should try the beluga lentils with poached eggs and polenta and the french toast with yogurt. Everything here is a masterpiece. One single suggestion: Keep that kombucha available all the time.

My new favorite restaurant in the East Bay, yay!!! Excellent customer service, Excellent Food and Selection, Everything about this place is PERFECT, with probably the exception of parking, but who cares, we got lucky the night we went here and found VIP parking! Whoot whoot!

Had a fantastic dinner here on Monday night.  

DRINKS:  We arrived a little early for our reservation so we waited with beverages at the bar in the back.  Most of us opted for the Moscow Mules (which were delicious, and not too strong) but everyone seemed happy with their beverages.

FOOD:  Sitting at the bar gave us time to scrutinize the menu and figure out exactly what we wanted.  

Starters: vegan charcuterie (OMG, brilliant, best thing on the menu), kale salad (didn't taste bitter at all, very well seasoned), albacore tuna & crispy pork belly (didn't try but other people really enjoyed) and green beans (spicy!  delicious! love!).  All the small plates, btw, were sufficiently large to be used as an entree if you weren't super hungry.  

Pizzas:  get a bunch of NYers and ex-NYers together and what do you get?  Everyone orders the delicious looking pizza.  Across the table, we shared the Lipstick vegan (ordered by a vegetarian and one omnivore), corn/leek/mushroom, mussels w/ bacon and the kitchen even made a custom pizza to accommodate one of our food-allergic friends.  All equally excellent and delicious.  

We didn't opt for desert (too stuffed!) but I'm told the espresso was excellent as well.

SERVICE: We had a really disappointing experience at another restaurant the night before, so we were really impressed with gather.  As I mentioned we had to wait a little bit for our table.  We were a big party, so there was only one table in the house that could comfortably accommodate us.  When the table didn't become available when the hostess expected, she came back and explained to us.  A few minutes later, a patron sauntered over to the bar to let us know that she and her group had our table, and it was all ours.  We had a lovely conversation and she recommended some dishes.  

Our waitress was great.  She accommodated many special requests, frequently checked in on us and wished us a safe flight, remembering from earlier in the meal that we told her we had to fly the next morning. And this is on the last seating of the night.  We pretty much closed up the place but never felt rushed.  

ATMOSPHERE: while the menu may look "fancy", this place is decidedly casual. We were jeans as were the rest of the patrons (and not our nicest ones, either).  Just a great meal, made from great ingredients, without pretense.

To gauge my entire experience, this review started off with three stars and then went back up to four by the time our dinner was over.

We came here with a party of 10 for a friend's birthday. I called to make a reservation that morning and they said they could only seat big parties at 5:15 or 8:15. While I was a little surprised at this (maybe this is normal and I just don't have much experience making reservations at different kinds of restaurants) I decided to go ahead and try to make the 5:15 reservation anyway. The host on the other side of the phone asked me for my usual information and then for my credit card number. (Again, perhaps this is normal but for me it wasn't) When I asked why that would be necessary he explained that if anyone did not make it to the dinner tonight or did not change the reservation ahead of time by 2pm that day, $25 would be charged to my credit card for EACH person who did not make it. 

Really? Is that completely necessary? I understand you guys are a new restaurant in town and are trying to set the bar really high but is that really necessary? Needless to say, i was a bit taken aback and a tad annoyed so I decided not to make the reservation at all. (My spiteful side surfaces...)

So that night I go early and decide to see if our party of 10 can be seated anyway. The hostess said she would see what she could do and after about 25 minutes of waiting she was able to seat us after all.

Inside decor is very nice, our waiter appeared to look like a snob at first but ended up being very polite and fun. I had the burger which was very well prepared, cooked just to the medium I like my steaks in. The best part of this burger was the house-sauce which is their rendition of the ketchup we all know and love. It had just the right amount of kick and flavor that went perfectly with my burger and the crisp fries that came with it. The birthday girl had the vegan charcuterie which she said she really enjoyed. She ordered a tangerine cello which wasn't too good (her opinion)  

All in all,making reservations were hard but they will accommodate if they can. Keep in mind we did go on a weekday so it may have been easier to get seated without reservation.

Ate here whilst visiting from Portland, and loved it. One of the most beautiful, delicious meals of my life.  Eating the Charcuterie appetizer felt akin to destroying a work of art (but, oh, it tasted divine). 

Our food took a notably long time to emerge from the kitchen, and even though we didn't make mention of it, our server gave us dessert and a drink on the house to make up for it. All in all, it was everything a dining experience ought to be.

This place is always hopping, and now I know why.  It is pretty remarkable, for a number of reasons.  One theme truly pervades throughout the entire restaurant -- whether it's the decor, the drinks, or the food, this is a restaurant that is *supremely creative*.  Truth.  My "Mayan Calendar" cocktail had chocolate bitters and slices of kumquat in it -- it ended up tasting kind of like a Mexican hot chocolate, but on a tequila base.  Yummay.  It was all uphill from there.

The **vegan charcuterie** I knew was a must from the reviews.  Sure enough, this was probably everyone's favorite, because it offers a little taste of a few different things, and is SO artfully done.  Instead of boring you with what each of the four items on the charcuterie was, I'll just say it was beautifully arranged on a wooden tray, and our favorite was definitely the grilled beech and king trumpet mushrooms with spring onion soubise (yeah, I donno either), baby onion marmalade, wild oregano, and onion seeds.  It was amazing.  Multiple of the mini-dishes had an amazing creaminess to them, that we kept on forgetting it was vegan.  Ah man!!  I just realized, I could have eaten that "goat cheese"!  Sigh.

**Burrata** had tons of cauliflower, and was just...tasty soft cheesy goodness.  The **young carrots** I found to be pretty intense on the sweet carrot flavor, but it was just a wonderful big pile of 10 different things going on on a plate.  It was particularly gratifying to find the crispy fried parsley!

I loved the **baby artichokes** with fingerling potatoes, black chickpeas, and this delicious smokey red sauce.  Wowza.  We asked them for bread so we could get every last bit off the plate, and we are NOT ASHAMED.

It's a beautiful space, with a menu that while it includes meat is also vegan/vegetarian/gluten-free friendly.  Also, I just can't emphasize enough the physical beauty.  Each dish makes you want to take a photo of it, and the restaurant has beautiful wrap-around windows, vines, sustainable art... Quite an experience.  Wish it were cheaper. :(

This place has clearly developed quite a following already! My friend and I went for an early, casual Tuesday night dinner and the place was almost completely full, so I would suggest making reservations if you're planning a weekend dinner. I soon realized why this place has become popular. We both got the burger, which was incredibly juicy. They are at least on par with the burgers served at Triple Rock, which I have long considered to be the best in the area (the caveat being that the fries at Gather were not as good, and the price of the burger was considerably higher). I will certainly be going back to sample other items from the menu. 

Other selling points: I was impressed by the service - very courteous and efficient. The cocktails were pretty good (though the beer selection was a little limited). I can also bring vegetarian and vegan friends here as there is a fairly extensive range of options that are helpfully marked on the menu.

With the emphasis on seasonal and local food, I was expecting a delicious showing of vegetables and fruits, but the best plate was the Prather Ranch burger and fries.  The medium rare burger was perfectly cooked and the first bite was a juicy piece of heaven.  Prather meat was given justice. 

The dinner menu was a balanced mix of vegetarian and meat options.  Noteworthy was a farm egg pizza with green garlic and pancetta that revitalized my interest in an over saturated pizza market.  Although the halibut was a disappointment and suffered from overcooking, the mushroom dashi had a tasty inventiveness and the whipped tofu provided a warm, satisfying richness.

From the desert menu, the chocolate hazelnut cake was okay, but my fat tastebuds were craving more of the fig ice cream once it was gone. 

Monday night had around a 30 minute wait and food was a bit slow so, the appetizers and wine were a brilliant choice.  Overall the meal was relaxing and fulfilling, but with a 50/per person meal (appetizer, entree, desert), I expect every dish to be good; not brilliant, but good. The fact that the 14 dollar burger was the highlight was a letdown.

Came here one night after moving into the new apartment!

It was around 8:30pm and we didn't make any reservations, but thankfully, there was a table available for us. However, I think we just got lucky, because I know you usually have to have a reservation if you want to eat around 6pm--unless you're okay with waiting for a table. 

We ordered the Summer Sausage (fennel puree, smoked potato salsa), Summer Squash Pizza (Redwood Hill Farm goat cheese, pesto), and Kale Salad (roasted carrots, capers, pine nuts, Fiscalini cheese).

The Summer Sausage's fennel puree was really delicious as well. I enjoyed the combination, because the creamy puree really played well with the saltiness of the sausage. Not only did the flavors compliment each other well, but the textures were like fireworks in your mouth.

Even though the pizzas here are really thin, the Summer Squash pizza was very bold with flavor. The crust was beautiful as it puffed up from being baked. Nomnomnom.

The Kale Salad was small, but was very well balanced. I liked the vinaigrette it was served with, and I liked the texture contrast of having the roasted carrots and pine nuts in them. 

As for drinks, we had both the sparkling and non-sparkling water, a bee sting cocktail (Square One botanical, ginger, lemon, honey, mint), and an IPA. The waitress was very helpful in terms of recommending a good cocktail. The bee sting wasn't too sweet nor too overpowering with alcohol. It was very refreshing.

What makes Gather food so incredible is that the ingredients are from local producers and the owners value sustainability. Half of their menu is vegetarian/vegan and the other half is meat/fish. Their vision is directly reflected upon their food as well as their decor.

I love how the restaurant has an open kitchen lining the entire back of the place. It's always great to see your food being prepared fresh! I love the brick-burning pizza open that immediately catches your eye when you walk into Gather. The restrooms are also absolutely fantastic as well. 

If you don't know why I'm raving so much about Gather, well, then you should definitely go try out the restaurant! :)

I can't say enough about this place.

Vegan Charcuterie plate... delicious both times!  Most impressive was the mini BLT where the B was actually a piece of thinly sliced tofu which tasted amazingly like a pork rind.

The wild mushroom pizza was to die for.

I was too full for dessert.  I must go back!

Was finally able to make another visit to Gather in Berkeley, and once again the food was great but this time the service was much improved.  We got in early on a Saturday, sat at the bar immediately, and had some great cocktails and great food.  

Generally we find it more beneficial to order a larger numbers of smaller plates in this style of restaurant but we have had a mix of everything.  The latest visit included some of the following highlights:

The sardines with grilled calamari over avocado and pickled vegetables was out of this world, the highlight of our 3 restaurant tour that night.  The ink and chili oil really made it too.  

Pizza was quite filling, surprisingly so.  It was the special of the night with pancetta, fresh greens, and figs and could have used a bit of oil or something, but was still well accepted.  

Pork kidneys with lentils (another special) were ok at first, but as the dish got smaller and smaller, we liked it more and more until we basically licked the plate clean. 

The only complaint we have about Gather is that it is relatively expensive and there are other similar options in Berkeley and Oakland that come in a little cheaper for what we consider just as good.  However, since our favorite restaurant Cellar Door in Santa Cruz changed chefs, Gather is the closest food we can find to what that used to be.  Farm to table, excellent presentation, very fresh tastes.  

Definitely a restaurant I recommend for a Berkeley eating experience, but Oakland offers more/cheaper/better.

Very exotic menu items but I was in the mood for all American standards.  Burger ($14) was great.  Very good shoestring fries too.  Pizza was quite good.  

Maybe a little over priced but GREAT staff and fun environment.  Would return.

I've been wanting to go to Gather since it opened, but we've been saving it for a special occasion dinner. On saturday, though, we found ourselves in need of lunch in downtown berkeley with parents, and decided to give it a try. The first thing we noticed on walking in the door was that there were about a dozen people standing in the entry waiting, a dozen or so waitstaff towards the back busily avoiding eye contact with the line, and about twice that many empty tables. We decided this didn't bode well for the service inside, but waited anyway. 

We were seated outdoors, and while it took a long time for the waiter to make first contact or bring us water, the service turned out to be fine once things got going. I felt sorry for the table next to us though. They were a big-ish group, but not so big that there was a good reason for their dishes to come out in 3 sets spread over 15 minutes. 

My two companions had the burger, which was very tasty, and I had the baked ricotta sandwich. The sandwich was okay, but the cheese should have been more seasoned somehow. Also, the menu said it had treviso on it, which I found undetectable. Maybe it was inadvertently left off? I also had a ginger beer, which was really terrific. 

Atmosphere was generally pleasant. There was a pretty inoffensive musician playing outside, though a little loudly for my taste. I always feel bad for people who play gigs like lunch time at a restaurant, but I lost my sympathy for her when she WALKED AROUND WITH A TIP JAR. So gauche! What are you? A busker on a subway train? I just paid 12 for my sandwich, the restaurant can afford to throw you a few bucks!

All in all, the food was fine, the service was inconsistent, and I was somewhat disappointed. I still want to give dinner a try.

Wow, the split pea soup. 

Everything could be mended by this vegetarian masterpiece.

We need a place like Gather in DC right now.

We had an incredible meal here last night. I can't even remember all of the deliciousness. The menu had a great range of veggie and meat dishes, which was great as our friends included vegetarians, carnivores, and bacon-vores. LOVED the vegan "charcuterie," so many beautiful colors and interesting flavors! Fancy-mushroom pizza and gnocchi/dumpling special with tiny-lentil "Bolognaise" were also incredible. The Anderson Valley pinot recommended by the waiter was super-delicious. Desserts were good, although they were out of the chai creme brulee- sad. Honestly, I am a huge Millennium fan, but based on this meal, I might like Gather even better.  (It does have an advantage in that it serves real cheese and ice cream...mmm, real cheese and ice cream.)

The Michael Bauer review made it sound kind of in-your-face with its emphasis on local farms and sustainability, but I didn't find that at all. All of the information about the ingredients was provided, but the staff seems genuinely excited about it rather than being at all preachy. We have a lot of really awesome produce and wines in this area, why not celebrate them? 

PS- apparently they have lunch, and they're going to have brunch soon. NOM.

The two stars shown here are for the good things at Gather.

Great intention and some good food.

We went early 5:30 on a Saturday as we had our little girl with us but the place was swamped by 5:50.

The Good
-Vegetarian charcuterie was interesting and well executed.
-Regular charcuterie was also good but pretty standard, not even close to Wood Taverns or someplace like Perbacco.
-The Pink Lady pizza was very good IMHO and my toddler agreed.
-The Zinfandel we had which escaped my mind right now was very good, only one by the glass.

The Mediocre
-Kale Salad was fine, tasted like something we would make at home a little oily and the cheese was mediocre.
-Ok I know the tables are like recycled from a water tower or some such thing but wow my ass hurt after 90 minutes in those chairs. 

The Bad
- Service was slow; folks little tip folks people with kids are there to steal some time, not to linger.
-Our server seemed very inexperienced despite the hipster hat he was wearing. Lots of silly hats at this place
-Quinoa risotto dont call it risotto its not. I look forward to anyone doing something truly tasty with quinoa bleeech!

I dont know maybe it was the overly self conscious Berk-liness of the place and the crowd. 

Ill be back and I think it will be much better after they loosen up a bit and find the right groove.

Brunch review time!

Acme walnut French toast: DELICIOUS!  My bro and I split 1 piece since we had a pizza as well and it was gone in literally 60 seconds.  It's markedly different from the top Bostonian varieties I've had where they tend to use a cornflake crust for added crunch.  Instead, Gather excelled in selecting a combination of sauces and ingredients to provide a brilliantly complex party in your mouth.  The sweetness of the maple syrup and fruit compote...crunchiness of the walnuts...cinnamon spice from the bread...and tartness of the Straus yogurt all came together in perfect harmony =D  

The brunch pizza was a welcome change of pace as well with freshly cut bacon, eggs with yolks intact, and sweet caramelized onions.  The coffee, however, could use some work as it still had some sourness and excess acidity in the finish that I had to mask with extra milk.  

The prices are perfectly fine for the quality of the food and yay for complimentary sparkling water ^_^b

I was surprised how big this restaurant and its adjoining patio are. The decor is very industrial-chic, lots of metal, but with warm wood tables. It is a comfortable, light space, and not especially noisy, which I appreciate.

The four of us had lunch here and tried various sandwiches, all on fresh levain bread, grilled to a nice crisp--and all good. I also tried the soup of the day, three bean minestrone (vegan) and the roasted beet salad. The emphasis, of course is on local, sustainable foods. As a result, everything is fresh as can be. Service was refined and understated, but efficient. A good choice for parties with some carnivores and some vegetarians, as there are many options for each.

sorry Gather.
I love the decor. The waiter was fab - friendly, knowledgeable... but the food. What's up with the food? I ordered the crook neck squash entree. Turned out to be a pile of cooked vegetables with no relation to one another. The sum was not at all grater than the parts... possibly less because the entire thing was served in a pool of Worcestershire sauce. huh? 

how can this be the new foodie mecca? what did we miss?

friends had an okay buger (nothing special, not worth $18 with fries) and a fried egg on top of a tomato. 

we tried the famed vegan charcuterie. the eggplant bit with cashew cheese was very good. the tofu skin sandwich tasted like chicken skin - crispy salty. good. but the stewed vegetables were as appealing as the name.

good cocktails. like the pisco sours and cairo in flames was very good. 

overall dissapointing...

Saturday, 7:30PM. 
Waiter: Eric

Bad time to try this venue. It was jam packed and I didn't think they'd be able to handle the six of us without reservations. Hostess was able to seat us, albeit on the counter. 

Turns out that it was the best seat in the house! At least for us, because we wanted a peak at the preparations. 

Quickie:
+Great service: our waiter, Eric, made great recommendations and knew everything about the menu!
+Clean, upscale decor: the setup was like an IKEA times ten.
+Menu diversity: omnivore? Carnivore? Vegetarian? Vegan? There's something for everyone.
+Fresh, fresh, fresh ingredients with sustainable practices (YAYEAH!)

Final Call:
The food was delicious. Gather exuded an upscale feel sans the bourgie-ness. Eric, our waiter, was particularly enthusiastic and happy to be working that evening. 

Why, was he so excited? Verbatim: "...when you know the food is prepared fresh, meticulously and with pride, it's hard not to serve it with a smile." Nicely done Gather, keep up the good work!

**********
Stuffed my face in:

1. Vegan "charcuterie"
     +"Oysters in the half shell" was the best of the fab five but they 
     were all pretty dang good
2. Local halibut
     +People who don't eat raw anything won't like this but to the more 
     adventurous folks, this was firm meat that tasted like it came right 
     out of the ocean
3. Young chicken under a brick
     +Juicy meat, fried onion was a nice addition
4. Heirloom bean ragout
     +WOW, flavorful bean soup thick enough for bread-dipping
5. Mushroom "cioppino"
     ++Even those averse to fungus would be shocked at the potent 
     flavors of this savory broth - I can't believe this was freakin' vegan!
6. Sauteed greens
     +Kale and chard action with caramelized onion and cabernet 
     vinegar
7. Fresh milled creamy polenta
     +Despite its namesake, this dish was light and lived up to polenta 
     delissssshousnessss
8. Red velvet cake
     +Smooth cake outlined with white chocolate, very potent!
9. Chai creme brulee
     +Poached apple with some dark chocolate action - are you kidding 
     me!?

This place could turn me into a vegan which is saying a lot because I LOVE meat.

This really is a great place that caters to both carnivores and vegetarians.  Everyone wins.  Yeay.

Get a reservation early, you'll be happy you did!

As a student, I only came here because my best friend had a gift card. Ordered the vegetarian antipasti, a pizette, and roasted chicken.

Very homestyle food. Not screwed around with. On the antipasti plate, really liked all of the tomatoes, tasted like candy. You could really tell that all of the veggies were picked well and were in season. There were some thing I could have lived without on the platter though. I know it changes often, so I'm sure it can be up or down.

The pizette was so yummy! And the arugula on top really broke up the richness. But it was a cold fall day and the roast chicken reminded me of Mom's. And trust me, almost everything my mom makes you pee your pants.

Extremely happy with my visit with a group of friends. First off the interior is beautifully designed and has a welcoming layout. The atmosphere was definitely buzzing, but we had no problem hearing our own conversations at seating for 8. 

The Food here is wonderful. Full of flavor and in combinations that are very unique using ingredients both familiar and unfamiliar that kept everyone at the table saying the same thing after tasting "Ooh, that was good, what was that?" with responses of "I have no idea but pass it over here" or "Mmmmm". In any case, the menu is very vegetarian friendly though there is enough to satisfy the average carnivore as well. 

With our party of 8 we managed to widely sample the menu, including Halibut tartare, Compressed strawberries, Baby Artichoke Salad, Spring Vegetable Salad, Spring vegetable broth, Vegan "charcuterie", Spicy tomato Pizza, Barbecued young chicken, Prather Ranch burger, Braised Lamb Shoulder. EVERYTHING was good according to all diners, well sourced, executed and most important, TASTY. Favorites for me was definitely the BBQ Chicken (juicy and fall of the bone tender), Vegan charcuterie (amazing variety, unexpected, and very flavorful), and the Spicy tomato Pizza (light, wonderfully crispy crust, and had a good spicy bite). Oh, and I had the best Ginger Beer I've ever had. Light, refreshing and with a real spicy ginger kick like i've never had anywhere else before. Excellent. 

Service was great, the hostess was very accommodating to our group despite last minute changes to our party. Our server explained everything very well and kept all of our glasses refilled. Food came out promptly and for the price I thought everything was a great value. Gather is definitely a place to return to.

It's so Berkeley to know what farm everything comes from...laughing stock quail, and abigail farms chicken, and oh my god, have you watched that YouTube where Alice Waters poaches an egg over a roaring fire?  Anyway, I warned my colleague that this place was very Berkeley.  The food was generally quite tasty, although nothing was outstanding.  The chanterelle pizza was the highlight of the main meal.  Nice crispy crust with tasty mushrooms.

The fish special was generally good although a bit lukewarm.  The vegan charcuterie was very well-presented and tasty.  I had slightly higher expectations...I wanted something on the plate to blow me away, but alas it didn't.  Dessert was very tasty.  The citrus rice pudding was fantastic as was the house made ice creams. 

A solid 4 stars on the food.  Minus half a star for uneven service.  The waiter was nice enough, just spread a bit then, and the kitchen seemed utterly disorganized.   Plus a half star though for housemade sparkling water.  Everytime I get sparkling water, I find myself just a bit happier.

Update 11/18:
I've had many a good meal at Gather and sometimes a few great meals.  I come to this place often, but I have to say the one thing I find sorely lacking is consistency.  The food is always respectable and the service is adequate, but it can't just quite hit that 5-star level.  In my last 3 meals, I've been blown away once with my best meal in a long while, had a tasty but not perfect meal, and was sincerely disappointed with some pretty so-so dishes on my last visit.  Maybe this is the challenge of a restaurant that changes it's menu so often.  I've also found tremendous variability among the servers too...ranging from acceptable to outstanding. 

By the way, the swordfish is to die for.

I went here last week on a pseudo-date. Notwithstanding my own weird issues regarding the labeling of the excursion as "pseudo" rather than something more concrete (believe me, I could write PAGES about that), Gather was, if a bit on the expensive side, delicious!

Here's what we had:

Red Russian kale salad:
- roasted heirloom carrots, pine nuts, Fiscalini cheese (v*, gf)

Vegan "charcuterie" (this is a small appetizer plate):
- Roasted corn on the cob, leek "butter," Sigaretta Dolce chili
- Baby Yukon gold potatoes, celery, yellow romano beans, crispy capers, "tonnato" sauce
- Crispy Yuba (bacon tasting), lettuce, avocado, and tomato sandwich, smoked garlic mayonnaise
- Tuscan Rose eggplant, cashew "ricotta," "putanesca" sauce, fennel top pesto
- Seared summer vegetables, "ranch" (v, gf*)

Heirloom squashes Pizza: 
- squash blossoms, Sierra Nevada goat cheese, Fontinella, arugula pesto

The salad was good, although they piled it high with the shaved cheese and it looked a little unappetizing. After biting in, the carrots and the cooked kale (not entirely cold) with the cheese and dressing was delicious. The portion size was good.

The charcuterie was out of this world.  A couple of the offerings were either boring (veggies with vegan ranch? I can do that at home) or kind of not good (I would have passed on the potatoes) or kind of confusing (the corn was delicious, but I wasn't sure if I should eat the cob or just the corn off of the cob--very awkward and I'm still not sure even now). The "BLT" was DELISH and the eggplant was HEAVENLY.

The pizza was a bit crusty for my tastes, but it appears all of the pizzas they make have crusts similar. Other than that, it was good. Probably not worth the $18 we paid, but still really good flavors.

I guess I was most disappointed because this place serves meat. I thought, implicit in its name, it was at least vegetarian, if not vegan?

I would have given three stars, but our service was excellent and since it's brand new I feel its best for the restaurant to break itself in a little bit. But then, I'm optimistic that my pseudo-dates will turn into real ones, too.

Came here for a birthday dinner with friends on a Wednesday night, and it was still busy. It's good to make reservations.

Atmosphere: Pretty! Wooden chairs, tables, and a nice open area.

Food: Ordered the barbecued young chicken. The meat was flavorful and fell off the bone and the portion size was satisfying. My friends had the pizzas and burgers, and they all looked pretty damn good (and according to them, they were).

Drinks: Vodka Smash - yummmmmmmy. I love the zest of cucumber, and it wasn't too strong, but you could taste the alcohol

Dessert: Hazelnut Chocolate Cake, great balance of flavor between Hazelnut and Chocolate, and the ice cream made it even more delicious. I also got a free dessert for my birthday, which was niiiiiice.

Overall: Fresh food, good service, and worth a try.

Came here with a party of 8 without a reservation on a Saturday night = major mistake. This was was completely packed by the time we arrived there. I think we tried to make reservations earlier during the day, but all of the reservations were filled as well. 

I think the place is quite overrated. Let's just say my experience went from a 5 down to 4 upon arrival of the food and 3.5 when the bill came. 

The ambience and the atmosphere of the restaurant was definitely 5 stars. Walking into the restaurant, I can smell the aroma of good food. We got seated in the outdoor patio area, which was kind of nice, for some fresh air, light breeze (though it got quite cold later), and nice jazzy music. Our waiter was extremely nice, with a sense of humor. Instead of offering just regular water, they had sparking water as well. 

The menu was quite different from what I saw on the website. They had the evening special, which was the Halibut fish. But since it costs around $28, I figured it wouldn't be worth it. Instead, I shared a Duck sausage pizza, pork pizza, and burger with 2 others. The food took around 30 minutes to arrive. The duck sausage was quite interesting because they had a pouched egg in the center, which tasted quite good actually. However, I didn't quite like the crust because it was hard and some parts were burnt. The burger was delicious but tiny, the size of a small fist. I enjoyed the complementary thin crisp fries. Instead serving with ketchup, they had some organic kind of bbq sauce, which tasted pretty unique. 

Overall, the experience was unique and food was quite good, but paying $16 for 2 small slices of pizza and a third of a small burger was  not so worthwhile.

I'm an environmentalist health nut, and this place is just perfect for my taste...or any taste, really.

I like to go vegan whenever I can, and it was extremely easy here. The menus are very clearly marked with "V" for vegan, "GF" for gluten-free, and "L" for locavore. Unfortunately, I didn't find any "V, L" options besides the side of vegetables. A local-vegan dish would have been perfect. But what I did find was a bunch of satiating vegan dishes. I swear, they work magic back in that kitchen, because red quinoa does not normally taste so good!

I tried some non-vegan dishes too. The polenta was great, especially if you're really picky on texture. Since I came with my family, I also got a chance to try three desserts in one night! My brother ordered the goat cheese panna cotta, and mom got the dark chocolate crema. My favorite was my own dessert: chai creme brulee! It's light as a cloud, but the flavor is incredibly powerful. My second favorite was the dark chocolate crema. That thing is soo rich, so don't even think about melting it. Just let it sit on your tongue and let it work its magic. It comes with fresh whipped cream too, which is a fantastic touch. As for the panna cotta, I actually forgot what it tastes like (whoops!) but it wasn't bad either.

If you get a chance to yank your face from your dish, definitely check out the architecture. The interior is made from refashioned materials. You'll probably notice that the "pitcher" of water they keep at each table is actually a glass milk bottle. So cute! And the benches are especially cool - upholstered with used leather belts! Nothing like an upcycled seat to give your bum a guilt-free feeling.

Oh, and definitely try their sodas. They have a housemade seasonal soda (worth trying), and they serve Taylor's tonic chai cola. If you love chai, you'll love this cola. It's amazing, and the chai aftertaste doesn't go away for a full minute. Good news for someone like me =]

I had no problem with the service here. I've been to other restaurants where the waitors are actually kind of snobby, especially when you're unfamiliar with something. I definitely digged the lack of HOW-DARE-YOU-NOT-KNOW-PANNA-COTTA attitude.

But I'm not too crazy about the price. The bill came out to be like $124 for the three of us, not including our tip. And we ate everything! So if you're starving, don't come here. Save your Gather experience for special occasions, not for a quick bite to eat.

Wow. Wow....

This place is very special. I had read reviews, but hadn't gone until last weekend. It was totally worth the money, a real treat. The vegan charcuterie is so amazing-it's a little taste of some real yumminess. The fava beans were fresh and tasty. Those things are hard to cook, if you've ever tried. I give this 5 stars and 5 thumbs up!

So . . . I'm not a huge proponent of all this organic, local farm blahdy blah.  It's a nice idea, but is it just me . . it seems slightly . . pretentious.  Or contrived.  Or  . . . something else bad.

They claim that their menu is 50% vegetarian and 50% meat and fish, which I find difficult to believe under the laws of percentages.  Granted, they have a burger and pork belly on the menu, but it seemed like the majority of the dishes were comprised of a menagerie of vegetables.  Which is perfectly fine once in a while and if you're in the mood for a lighter meal.  

So why am I giving them four stars when I'm clearly annoyed by the foundational tenets of this restaurant?  Well, the vegan charcuterie and beefsteak and eggs (no meat . . .bah) were tasty and different.  And for once I left a restaurant not feeling as if I was going to die of a clogged artery from the amount of garbage I just consumed.

I've head "Gather? Pretty good!" and "Gather? Meh." from my friends and family.

After my visit, I lean more toward the pretty good side.  That vegan charcuterie plate was freakin' amazing.  I mean, that presentation takes a lot of thought, and it was tasty too (though I am an almost-vegetarian and have no issues with those sorts of things).

I also thought the pizzas were fun.  I recommend the cashew butter one if you don't mind a red sauce-less pizza that's sort of more like yummy bread with dip on it.

Prices are high due to the high-quality of ingredients and probably popularity.  I was there on a Monday night and it was pretty packed.  If you're not into the whole expensive for top ingredients/produce, don't go here.  I, thankfully, am NOT in that category.

I'd go back for lunch.

hell no! never ever again. made a reservation, confirmed the reservation, got there 10 mins before reservation,  BUT when we got there, the table is not even ready. they told us to wait a couple mins so we waited for 30 mins and never got a table so we decided to leave. im very very very very disappointed. 

i thought you make a reservation so you dont have to wait. i guess thats not the case for this restaurant.

Smoked Heirloom Eggplant Sandwich. With Avocados, Heirloom Tomatoes and Grilled Onions and a Side of Mixed Greens. This was pretty good. It was a very squishy sandwich though so I was glad I had a plate so I could fork and knife it. The flavors in the sandwich mixed well together and I loved their bread. The mixed greens were also delish, it had a light balsamic vinaigrette on it. The portions were pretty good too because I only ate half of the sandwich and took the rest to go (more about that later). Noms. 

Open-face Cannellini Bean Sandwich. With Lindencroft Summer Squash, Smoked Mozzarella, Opal Basil-Lemon Ash Pesto and Spicy Tomato Salsa. My friend ordered this but I ended up getting this in my to-go box. Fail on the server's part. But this sandwich was nommy as well. I'm not usually a fan of squash but this was yummy and the different textures of the starchy beans and more fibrous squash was delish. I also liked the smokey flavor the mozzarella added to the sandwich. The salsa, however, was not the least bit spicy. 

Note: Most of their sandwiches can be request to be vegan and gluten free. 

Food was good, but service wasn't that great. They weren't attentive and they mixed up our takeout boxes. Sure, I should have checked to make sure, but when you put a box in front of a person you expect it to be yours. Sadface. -1 star for that. 

See photos of food, http://potbellypanda.tumblr.com

First time here-  Very impressed  with the food . Ordered the Pork Belly,  Kale salad ,  Fontinella Pizza  and one of their specials - pork skin with kumquat , strawberries and kiwi.  The Pork belly ofcourse just melted in my mouth which was expected .. Very , very tasty and cooked perfectly. Pork skin with the different types of fruit was a good combination of salty, sweet, sour and citrusy flavors. The Kale salad was really good mixed with carrots and pine nuts. Great salad and perfect combination with both pork dishes ordered. The pizza was delish and added an egg for extra touch. For my drink I ordered the Oxford Street and it was delish.

I am taking off 2 stars for the service. Our waiter was BAD!   We had to call him several times to get bread ( which I mentioned twice), asked for fresh red pepper flakes which is TYPICALLY offered by all quality restaurants and good servers when pizza is ordered ( I had to ask him for that) and had to call him again after I asked for the Beer menu . Isn't it obvious that If I asked for a beer menu that I would like to order one? No need to call you again for the 4th time..

Quick tip- Ask for the levain bread if you want it and make sure your server hears you, so you don't have to ask twice.

Would like to recommend this to other ELITE YELP members however I am debating or holding back because of the BAD service.

I completely ADORE this place....so im one of the un-savvy locals who has never treaded to the opposite side of shattuck st in Berkelely. I mean theres so much there who would have thought theres even MORE on the other side??? lol

so  looking up a neutral place for my boyfriend and I to have dinner since im a vegan and hes not is not always an easy task and seldom has good results. I mean someones usually gotta compromise...but not here!!

First off The place is BEAUTIFUL but not uppity. Its perfect for a casual lunch, business meeting, or romantic date. The menu and decor are so versatile its crazy. You can get something fancy like the "Vegan Charcuterie" or an entire half chicken served on a platter (litterally) or something simple like a butternut squash pizza. Either way you your taste buds will be delighted by the freshest seasonal ingredients. no matter what you get it will be BOMB

It can be a bit pricey especially if youre like me and its your first time so you just want EVERYTHING! for dinner between me and my boyfriend we paid 73$ that included drinks appetizer and entrees. so its not craaazy but probably better for your wallet if you are disciplined enough to order one thing.

i definitely plan to come back here as soon as possible and explore the UC side of berkeley more often :)

My review for Gather is long overdue, but after yet again another run-in with their uber-pretentious staff, I figured it was time.   Now let me say that their food is delicious and if it weren't for there awesome breakfast pizza, I would have fired this place long ago.  Gather is pretty ridiculous and I am pretty certain they train their staff to be as pretentious as possible and give their customer a hard time about EVERYTHING.  Here are some examples:

-- I have been to Gather many times for brunch, and each time the restaurant is about 1/4-1/3 full....like, you will NOT be waiting in line for this place.  But each time I have been for brunch the conversation goes something like this.  Like really, this happens every time (and if you bring a stroller this is evening MORE of an issue)
    "Do you have a reservation"? (hipster host with mustache)
    "No." (me looking around at the empty restaurant)
    "Ugh....hhhmmmm....I just dunno if we can fit you in" (HHWM)
    "Really?  Looks like there is plenty of room" (me)
    "Make a reservation next time" (look of disgust from HHWM)  

--- If you ever ask the staff at Gather to substituent an ingredient or bring something on the side be prepared for them to give you big time attitude about it.  Here is how my conversation with the waiter went this past weekend at Gather:
     "Can I please get the bacon breakfast pizza but sub in sausage instead of bacon?" (me)
     "We dont do subs.  We like to make our food as it says in the menu.  Plus, our food is SO fresh that sometimes we dont have the ingredient. And we dont have usages today" (hipster waiter sighing audibly)
      " They do it for me all the time. So, do you not have the Sausage pizza that you have on the menu already?  Or do you not have sausage to add on a pizza like it says on the menu?" (me)
      "Uuuummmm...no we do have that." (Waiter truly shocked that I caught him in a lie)
      "OK, so since your food is so fresh I am assuming you dont have pre-made pizza.  I am sure you can sub in Sausage instead of bacon" (me)
      "Well, I will have to ask the chef" Waiter walks away annoyed and in a huff
      5 minutes later he returns and does not look at me in the eye.
      "The chef said no problem".  

This annoying attitude is something that I endure every time I come to this restaurant.  It would be much better dining experience if the staff would just relax and realize that there are a million establishments in the Bay Area that are just as good and fresh as Gather--so no need for the attitude.

Like lots of hippie high brow endeavours  the intention is great while the execution is weak. That describes our experience at Gather.

It's only been open a few weeks and there was a lot of hype about the place but it failed to live up to it.

It started when I made a reservation on line at 8:15 through open table. When we got there I was told the reservation system said the reservation was for 8:30. I have used the system for as long as it's existed and I know that the only people that can change the reservation are at the restaurant so I knew they were lying to me.

There were two hostess there at the front desk but mostly they just frowned and ignored people for most the night or talked to the staff. I think they are going for group serving which you get in fine dining places were everyone takes care of the tables and when it works makes for constant attentiveness but instead we just got a collection of servers and staff that couldn't tell us what we were eating, that asked if we had gotten food that had been served already and then at the end of our meal we couldn't get anyone's attention even though there were three people talking to each other. The staff seems very untrained and inexperienced. I really hope they work on it.

The space was weird too, for being all about homey hearty food, it was in a new construction building with no sound baffling. It was very hard to hear my dining companions and the layout was odd with servers either having to walk around a long railing or lean over it.

Now on to what's important the food.
The menu looks great, the description were interesting and it's good we read them well because our servers could tell us almost nothing about them.

There were three of us, one vegan, one vegetarian and one omnivore. We order the vegan charcuterie, the watermelon radish salad, the cardoons, Red quinoa risotto and the pork cheeks and finish it with the chai creme brulee.

The one consistent thing with all our dishes were that the portions were SMALL and considering the quinoa and pork cheeks were under Large plates, I can say they need to rename things.

The first dish out was the crispy cardoon even though we order the vegan charcuterie ten minutes before. A cardoon is just a cousin of the artichoke and it taste like one especially when it's fried just like an artichoke. It tasted just like the fried artichokes you get at fair food stands. It came on a tomato pesto sauce that was great.

Then the vegan "charcuterie" came. First of all why call it charcuterie? Charcuterie means deli so why not call it vegan deli platter? but I don't even think that would be right. What it actually seems to be is eight vegan spread. I asked the server to tell us what each was to which he replied "I don't really know, and then pointed to one and said that's mushroom something. The portions of each were tiny with two bites at the most. They were tasty but rather bland.

Then we got the watermelon radish salad which was larger than our so called "large plates". it was probably the best thing and a super easy dish to make.

The "large plates came out". The red quinoa risotto was small, tasty but small and I have no idea why they called it a risotto since there is no rice in it and there is nothing creamy about it. It did have a savory mushroom broth and flavour and was probably the best tasting thing we had. My pork cheeks were small too but very tender and moist, they were served on a lemon polenta that was better than the meat.

We were still all hungry after eating our meal so we ordered the chai creme brulee which was tiny! it was tiny tiny square of creme brulee with the tiniest segments of blood oranges and tiny pieces of pear. The brulee was not firm enough but the one bite each we had was tasty.

They make a big deal about using local produce but I've never heard of locally grown pears at this time of the year.

The bill came to 77 dollar, not cheap for the little morsel of rather bland food we received. Over the course of the meal we were served by eight different people, four of them who couldn't answer basic questions about the food. I understand they are recently open but staff should never say I don't know and leave it at that, they should go and find out the information.

I'm going back next week with another friend to see if the service will get better.

Stopped through Berkeley for a quick brunch. I hadn't visited the campus area since I graduated in 2004, so this was among the many newer nicer changes I noticed. This restaurant (along with the whole building) used to be a huge parking lot when I was in college. I heard from other diners that Gather just recently opened a little over a year ago.

We ordered their fresh local lettuce salad with two eggs, a side of bacon, and their scramble with the chorizo.  All the food tasted amazing. It's rare to find such a restaurant that offers decently-priced (at least for brunch) locally-sourced organic dishes!

I don't know why people were complaining about the size of the salads...both my husband and I thought they were HUGE. This is coming from me, a big eater (I finish 2/3 lb burgers at The Counter).

The eggs were probably the best eggs I've had at a restaurant, and they tasted and looked (deep yellow yolks) a lot like the pasture eggs I buy at home. I wouldn't be surprised if they actually were pasture eggs, but then that would be a pretty amazing thing for a restaurant to offer.

The bacon was perfectly cooked to a crispy-yet-still-chewy -- and nice and thick slices! Scramble and the side of potatoes were out of this world as well.

Service was a bit on the slow side, but still very friendly. The decor was so cute and "organic" looking. My husband even noticed that the seats were made from recycled leather belts haha -- how environmental =P The restaurant seems pretty roomy, and we noticed they also have patio space. When we went there as a nice mix between college students and a more mature/older crowd as well.

I had an amazing meal and hope to be able to try their dinner menu sometime!

I was skeptical about the prospects for a new restaurant in downtown Berkeley, but this is a winner.  I only tried a couple of things, the watermelon radish salad (delicious!) and the cod.  The devotion to quality ingredients, exuberant yet simple presentations, and creating a complimentary environment is obvious.  I really want to come back and try the rest of the menu, pizzas and all.  Could become addicting.

Gather can be a hit or a miss depending on where you are seated and depending on the season/menu choices. I've had prompt and attentive service, great meals and cocktails while other times we were sat in a corner, had mediocre food and mixed up orders.

The lack of consistency means it's only a 2 star as I'd rather go somewhere which is good (not great) consistently rather than experience such high's and lows as described above. 

My recommendations if you do go: 
check the menu before seating
don't get sat in the corner/get served by a bartender
verify portion/plate sizes so there are no surprises
consider reservations in advance as walk-in space will fill up early on

They change their menu often, but if you get lucky, the must haves are: shaved radish salad, seared cod & braised pork cheeks!! All mouth watering, really. 

I truly truly truly love this place!! Berkeley needed a place like this long time ago, and I am really glad we finally got :o) Kudos to Chez Panisse people who realized that most of us mortals like to eat well but cannot afford to frequent their North Berkeley establishment! Now we have a place that has that unbelievable Berkeley ambiance, all-natural organic menu and does not cost an arm and a leg!

So here's the story: went there on a Monday night with a few girlfriends to celebrate a Bday. First, we ordered a vegan charcuterie as an appetizer. I have no idea what was in there, but it was very delicious! Even if you're not a vegetarian (which we aren't), it is simply impossible not to enjoy the different palette of tastes that's on that plate! 
 
As second meals, I ordered a seared cod, girls ordered a potato pizza, housemade burger and some wild exotic salad (sorry don't remember the name!). My fish was unbelievably tender and went really well with the artichoke puree it was on! Same goes for the pizza and hamburger, but I only had one bite of each so won't really consider mine as an expert opinion.

Before I also tried their braised pork cheeks, and OMG I loved it! The polenta goes so well with pork and breadcrumbs, it creates an explosion of taste in your mouth! DO TRY!! Same goes for the shaved radish salad, albeit pork cheeks are a little heavier :o)

I wanted to like the place.  Berkeley needs more un-overrun-by-cheap-ass-college-students-places.  That being said, we are also very used to reasonable prices for decent cuisine.

I get that it's local, sustainable, organic, gluten-free, veg-friendly etc, but some items did seem on the pricey side.  Example: braised lamb appetizer.  $11 for a baby's fist of lamb.  Yes, it tasted fresh and tender, but really now.  It just looked sad.  They weren't kidding about the small plate thing.

On the other hand, $11 for the bay squid appetizer of more heft and heartier warmth seemed well worth it.  It was delicious and had just the right mix of flavors.

The three of us also ordered the charcuterie plate, chicken under a brick, and pork cheeks.  It seemed to be JUST enough food for us.  Charcuterie plate was to be expected, some items more delicious than others, a couple were too fatty to be enjoyable.  

Chicken under a brick was a decent-sized portion and the pork cheeks were on the slightly small side.  Both were...good.  But my meal companions were right.  Some of the dishes had TOO many flavors.  I get the idea of mixing unique flavors to create new flavors, but to be honest, it was kind of a flavor explosion in my mouth and not always in a good way.  So to be clear, it wasn't bad.  More like...not necessary.

I think it's worth a try, especially if you're one of the hardcore who buys Strauss milk every week or if your major is conservation resource studies or if you use Tom's toothpaste.  Otherwise, I doubt I'll go out of my way to return.  

Damage was $30/person with no alcohol and no desserts.

I was very excited to hear about the opening of Gather, since the downtown Berkeley area (I'm not talking the Gourmet Ghetto here, but further south) leaves a lot left to be desired in the restaurant department.  Sometimes I just want to go out and see...people my age (sorry undergrads).

Anyway, Gather has a really warm, inviting ambiance.  They don't over- or under-decorate, and I like the idea of their furniture being made from local (Sebastopol) wood.  Cool.  When I went in last Friday night, the place was bumping.  My group had to wait for a table, and opted to hit the bar for some drinks.  I was a *little* disappointed when I realized that they don't have a full liquor menu, but only a short list of rather frou-frou drinks.  I opted for the bee-sting: organic vodka, muddled ginger and mint, and agave nectar - shaken and served in a martini glass.  It was good, and POTENT.  However, I would like to see a more "general" drink menu other than these specialty drinks and beers.  Sometimes a girl just wants a regular martini!  But I did appreciate the bar service (it was excellent).

We got our table relatively quickly, and I was overall impressed by the waitstaff - very attentive and friendly.  I ordered a glass of the Santa Cruz Rose - very crisp and full-bodied.  For dinner, I ordered the roasted chanterelle pizza with leeks, thyme and mozzarella.  The crust was thin and perfectly crispy, and the flavors were excellent.  Others at the table ordered the Burger (very tasty, despite the price-tag), and the  heirloom bean ragout was very flavorful and spiced well.  Unfortunately, we were all too full to try dessert, but will definitely do so next time.

Yes, it's pricy, but I appreciate the locavore, sustainable, organic state of mind.  I didn't leave hungry, and thought the food was excellent.  I also enjoy the idea that I will be able to try something different next time, as the menu will change with the seasons.  It's the way I like to eat, but may not be for everyone.

I have gone to Gather about 5-6 times and until last night have had some really fantastic meals there. In the past both food quality and service have been excellent, but unfortunately the UNHOLY RUDENESS of the server we had last night has colored my entire experience with Gather and is now making me wonder if 1 star is too many for this joke of a resto. 

Here's what happened:
We waited 15 minutes for the waitress to come over, when we told her we were ready to order, she left and took another 10 minutes to come back. This was fine, we were relaxed, not in a hurry, and the place was about  full so we knew she had several tables to manage.  We waited another 10 minutes for her to bring the wine we ordered, then another 25 minutes  for apps to be served and then 45 minutes (after finishing apps) more for entrees to arrive, and then only 3 out of 4 plates were set with no explanation as to where the 4th entrée was.  After a few minutes we flagged her down and asked where the 4th plate was and she snapped "IT'S COMING RIGHT NOW OKAY???!!!WHY DON'T THE REST OF YOU JUST START!!!!"  

Super rude right? Well , still wanting to have a nice time and not ruin the night out we said nothing. (BIG MISTAKE)  Finally the 4th plate arrives and we can eat.  Everything tasted fine (although the BBQ chicken was kinda salty) but we were starving so again no complaints.  We eat, within a few minutes while my dad is still eating a buss boy tries to clear our plates, not very cool but we just wave him away and don't really say anything.  Everyone finishes... and then we sit there for another 35 minutes. The resto is now nearly empty, our waitress has maybe 2 other tables to deal with and we see her standing by the kitchen chatting to a coworker. I try to  politely make eye contact, wave her over to ask for the check.  10 more minutes pass and she finally comes over. We have now been at Gather for almost 3 hours. We just want to leave. The parents are getting super tired, we start chatting about yelp reviews etc. The waitress apparently overhearing comes over ( while I am talking) interrupts and says "I need to talk to you, tonight we were very busy, and yeah I took a little longer than usual..."

I looked up at her in shock, was this crazy b*tch actually getting bent out of shape because we were discussing yelp? Did she really just interrupt me?    I told her to just bring the check, we didn't need to have a conversation with her. She walks away and comes back with a dried-out skanky piece of cake and tries to put it on the table saying "this is a peace offering"  

I finally snapped and said " NO ONE CARES ABOUT YOUR STUPID CAKE, JUST BRING THE DAMN CHECK WHAT IS WRONG WITH YOU???"

She starts arguing with me. I tell I do not care about her or any of her issues we just want to leave and never return.  We go thru this for a few more minutes before she finally agrees to put the check down.   We leave , vow never to return, tell all of our friends that what once was a great restaurant is now ruined by rude, obnoxious and weirdly self important wait staff.

Alright, i'm gonna take a huge leap here and put my Yelp reputation on the line here. (Actually, this isn't that huge of a risk)- I'm declaring it now regardless, Gather is THE BEST restaurant in the East Bay. 

Oh yes, it's damn good.

Get the pizza, get the sandwich, get the soup, get it all.

If you've ever read my Yelp reviews before, you'll know there is one thing I often mention when giving a restaurant 4-5 stars. FLAVOR. Flavor flavor flavor means the world to me, and gather has a stranglehold on it. Gather has flavor owned like it's bitch. Gather takes flavor, wraps it up like a rubber band ball, and bounces it around the kitchen and onto your plate like a professional restaurant should. 

Oh Em Geez the flavor. 

The cauliflower pizza is insane. With broccoli and tomato, capers and cashews, a delicious mix of sauce and cheese with a splash of chili oil. The crust is super thin, with a puffy balled up edge- It's vegan gold, quite frankly. Oh, and the braised mushroom sandwich! Hello! This sandwich packs a flavor so outstanding you might literally have to order a second sandwich to go. 

Sit by the bar area if you want to watch the chefs work on your "organic, free range, etc etc" food! Yeah, this is one of those places too, so come get your 'Berkeley' on folks. This place is amazing, an instant favorite of mine- and I really can't think of a place in the East Bay that serves a more flavorful combination of dishes as Gather does. I 100% see a Michelen Star in their future, without a question.

Gather (verb) to bring close; to come together around a central point. 

Just the thought of the name of this great dining establishment is warm & inviting. It's perfect enough for a delicious brunch with a group of friends or colleagues in their outdoor patio equipped with heat lamps and spaciousness, & intimate enough to take a date to ravish in biodynamic wines & organic cocktails.

Gather supports local food producers & offers vegan or gluten free options on alot of their dishes upon request. Definitely something for everyone!

I flove their new Pig Leg Sandwich ($13) served with side baby greens. This sandwich actually replaced their popular pulled pork sandwich which I was dying to try, but ultimately didn't miss since I can say with much confidence that their pig leg sandwich is now my favorite sandwich in the East Bay! Simple, to the point & packs a punch. It sits on perfectly toasted ciabatta bread, served with shaved torpedo onions, crème fraiche mustard vinaigrette, & I believe cabbage? Soooooooo good I can't stop thinking about it! 

The Stinging Nettle Pizza ($18) served with smoked mozzarella & olive caper sauce was light yet satisfying. Capers can sometimes overpower a dish and add an element of over saltiness, but they were well balanced in the pizza. The crust, with perfect texture & added crisp, leaves you wanting a dip or olive oil to dip into.

The food came out very quickly within approximately 4-6 minutes from when we ordered. Their service was great & everything was almost perfect except that our waiter forgot our water and didn't get it to us until after our food was served. Other than that, a great way to spend an afternoon with people you love.

OOh, Gather.  So delicious, such a cornucopia of flavors, and there are good taste surprises around every corner of the menu.  The vegan charcuterie is always a good choice, and they definitely seem to realize that us veggies and vegans need our protein too - nuts, beans, mushrooms, and eggs are around every corner.

I've been twice, and loved it each time.  I like how specific the menu items are - this item is locally sourced, this is a "sunchoke" (which is?), that is a "winter citrus carpacchio."  (you can call me Vigo the Carpacchian if you like)  That specificity leads you to believe that they are constantly experimenting with flavors and picking just the right items to complement each other.  The results speak for themselves.

Beer selection and wine selection are equally good, and they stand up to and enhance the flavor of the food.

Sure, service is a little slow, but if you have time, it's definitely worth the trip.  If it's your first, it definitely won't be your last.

two weeks later and I already have to bump this place up to five stars!!  

Three reasons:

1) The Seared Panisse.  It sits huddled in the right corner of the menu, arranged with all the other larger plates. . .sort of a wallflower of a dish but. . .no, that stuff is THE BUSINESS!!!  It's similar to a soft polenta cake but it's made out of chick pea flour.  . .sure, that ain't sounding so sexy right now but trust me on this. . .it is AMAZING!!!  I had it on Thursday night and it's Sunday afternoon and all I want is a giant plate of that luscious little legume!  The set the night I ate it was nettles, black trumpet mushrooms and a delectable salsa made with tiny cubes of San Joaquin Gold - a gorgeous and sassy little raw milk cheese made by Fiscalini in Modesto . . .and pine nuts. . . a truly inspired combination that I cannot get off my mind.  

2) I have to rescind my dis on dessert. . . so the Mocha Flan was not my thing but the Meyer Lemon Semifreddo so IS my thing .. .SO GOOD!!!!!  Three of us shared it and I wanted it all to myself. . .

3) When I ate at Gather the first time I was with my family so I just really concentrated on the food, conversation and being with them. . the other night I was with some girlfriends and we noticed something that I missed on my first visit. . .Gather is a veritable buffet of handsome servers. . .. not only do you get top notch, delicious food but you get it served by serious HOTNESS!  Kudos to the GM. . .I don't know if it's simple serendipity. . .but yeah, eye candy abounds.  (sorry if I sound stupidly inappropriate or hella Sex in The City but hot is hot. . .)

it's like alice waters personally blessed this place and said go forth and feed people. there are a lot of small touches that convey their commitment to earth/food love, without getting overly hippie on you. 

the room is big and open and filled with natural light and wood tables and floors that look comfortably worn in. the huge wood-fired oven makes the airy space feel comfortable and cozy. above the open kitchen is a chalkboard detailing which farm their seasonal veggies are from. they have things on the menu like kale salad and cashew "cheese". they make their own sparkling water--of course they do. and what's even cuter is that they serve it in glass milk bottles. 

the food is simple and earth-driven--no bells and whistles, but they do know how to pair it all to get the most flavor out of their veggie influenced menu. the meat they serve is quality and sustainably raised. my sister had a shredded beef sandwich on thick crusty bread that was super flavorful and tender.

my mom and i shared the kale salad with pine nuts, roasted root veggies, and parmesan cheese. and the wild mushroom pizza. i love me some kale, and i was quite happy with the salad. altho i would have preferred it more room temp than cold, esp since they served it with the root veggies. the pizza was the just the way i like it, thin, crispy, with the perfect amount of doughy chew to the bubbled crust. and those mushrooms were full of wine-y, earthy flavor. 

the service is friendly and down-to-earth. i def want to head back for brunch or dinner. you walk out of here satisfied, but also feeling like you did something good for your body.

I had stared longingly into the windows of Gather for years, and just finally had my chance to sit amongst the cool kids eating vegetables on wooden boards. Swoon.

Apparently, you need reservations for 8pm on a Wednesday night because the place was positively packed. I scoped out peoples' plates while I waited for my table and decided I wanted the red soup with the grey foam on top. It turned out to be Pumpkin Habenero soup with Corn "Smut" (a fancy word for fungus). It was fantastic. Considering my love of mushrooms and stinky cheese, a little mold never hurts. 

My buddy had the Vegan Charcuterie, which would have made me very sad, but she loved it. It was a very small portion - just a few mounds of dressed-up veggie-matter with interesting sauces. I suppose this is a dish you admire for the sheer art and creativity of it. 

A few notables: it gets really loud in here. Also, the bar area is TINY with about 10 seats and a couple bar tables. I'm a bar-dweller, so this saddened me. 

Service was a bit frantic - our bread arrived with no butter or oil, our 2nd wine order was forgotten, and without a reservation we were treated as somewhat of a nuisance - BUT, I know Gather has potential, so I'll take this first encounter as a learning experience and come prepared next time. After all, it's where the cool kids are.

The words 'organic' and 'Berkeley' invoke images of fleece-decked, sandal-wearing, Prius-driving food Nazis looking to devour their next locally sourced, vegan, non-GMO meal.  inevitably they're wagging their fingers at you for not eating their way while eco-chic buzzwords like; grass-fed, local, organic, cage-free, sustainable, low carbon footprint, free range, and biodynamic fly around their dinner table with reckless abandon.

Say what you will about the whole 'farm to fork" fad happening in haute cuisine today, but the proponents do make a good point. Reduce the amount of greenhouse gasses, minimize the use of pesticides, and reform the way we house and process animals and eating becomes less costly on the environment and our bodies.

Gather does a great job with breaking down the stereotypes of pretentious eating while pleasing carnivores and vegetarians with their innovative use of local ingredients and tasty preparations. I don't think I've ever been to a restaurant that allowed vegetarians and meat-eaters to co-exist in a way that doesn't feel forced.

Astrid and I went to dinner at Gather with our friend Lisa Z. and started with the Vegan "Charcuterie" platter ($16) that was absolutely incredible! The flavors that the chefs coaxed out of completely vegan ingredients were mind blowing.  The seasonal selection included; a King Trumpet mushroom crudo and parsnip-pine nut sea palm risotto with crispy parsnips, a winter citrus carpaccio with shaved beets, olives and dill, braised endive with avocado, yuba, and smoked aioli on toasted bread and a roasted Carnival squash with sunchoke cashew bay leaf sauce and smoked maple all served on a cutting board with more toasted bread. I defy anyone who says they hate vegetables to find any fault with this plate.  It was magnificent!

We could have stopped there, but next up was the "Chicken fried" Kabocha Squash ($19) served over vegan mashed root veggies with braised collard greens. The flavors there were amazing too.  It was the perfect early-winter meal, hearty and filling, but light too.  Lisa Z. opted for the Prather Ranch burger ($14) cooked perfectly, covered in cheddar cheese and served with the nicest french fries I think I've ever tasted. The house made caramelized shallot tomato sauce to dip those beautiful fries in was divine as well.

The space is great with tables and counters made of reclaimed and salvaged wood, moody lighting and a bright lively kitchen. The bar where we sat was just as beautiful and featured some innovative cocktails.  While the other reviewers said the restaurant might be a bit tight, it lends itself well to the theme of 'gathering' to enjoy a meal with 150 of your closest friends.

But I keep going back to that Vegan "Charcuterie". I can't get it out of my head.  I think next time I'm ordering one to myself...and I ain't sharing.

I really enjoyed my dinner here. Gather certainly IS the place to gather, seeing as it was packed to the brim on an early Tuesday night. I really like the rotating menu, highlighting both seasonal and local goodness.

The staff was very sweet, attentive and knowledgeable. There is definitely something for everyone on this menu, from meat eaters to vegans, folks who seek gluten free fare or plain old vegetarians. 
We started with the polenta encrusted mushrooms with "ranch" sauce, not bad! A little chewy, but anything fried really can't be that bad ;-)

Next up was the vegan "charcuterie" plate -- which is quickly becoming their signature dish -- so I had to try it. We had an array of shaved beets, a wonderful smoked portobella mushroom crostini and a range of other veggies cooked in new and exciting ways (at least to me) that my date and I enjoyed sharing. It was a little party in our mouths, complete with dipping sauces.

For my meal, I had the mushroom pizza, nothing to rave about, but it was tasty. Thin crust, the chef is big on the burnt bubbles though, which wasn't a favorite of mine. Good wine menu, small bar to sit in while you wait and nice local beers to test out. Their cocktail menu looks interesting too, as I spied a few I wouldn't mind testing out.

Having just come from a road trip up the east coast from Florida,  I joked with the boy how we'd never find any cuisine like this where we just were driving through. It's "California cuisine" that fits the stereotype well, and I would bring any visitors here to try out the "locavore" scene. 

I'll definitely come back anyway to sit outside during warmer weather and for the change of menu in the seasons :)

I was meeting up for lunch with an elderly friend who is a fairly fussy eater - but was treating - and decided on Gather.  A little over my budget for general purposes, Gather turned out to have a somewhat limited lunch menu, but everything looked very tasty.  A few salads, a few sandwiches, and a few pizzas + one soup.  All house made organic beverages. 

 Unfortunately, for the purposes of a review, my friend ordered the same thing I did, the half-sandwich/soup combo.  The soup was a saffron chickpea concoction with olive oil drizzled on top.  Although the texture of chickpeas isn't always my favorite, the flavor of the soup was really very good.  I might have wished for a slightly more robust olive oil, but it lent a nice smoothness if not much flavor.  

The pulled pork sandwich on the other hand, was a little piece of heaven.  The pork was everything a slow-cooked pork should be, whether Mexican Carnitas, or Chinese pork shoulder.  It was as juicy as a gossip column, as tender as a mother's love, as sweet as baby kisses, and succulent in that way that only pork can be.  Not spicy or bbq-y, which may disappoint some, Just pure, unadulterated damn good pig meat.  (Apologies to my vegetarian friends, and to the piggies themselves.
