I do know that the pig is an intelligent and noble animal - why does he also have to taste so darn good.)

Service was just a little sketchy, but it was late lunch, so they were probably in recovery mode.  One orders at the counter and stuff is brought, but there should be utensils and napkins where they need to be, and if I've asked about one, you should probably be checking everything at that point. tsktsk.  Still I'd go back - you payin?

Things you should know before coming here:

*  Do not bring anyone here on a weekend night that wears a hearing aid or should wear a hearing aid.  The acoustics are bananas and while it didn't bother me, my mother complained about the noise level literally every five minutes throughout the meal, very annoying.

*  The portions are generally on the smaller side.  We LOVED the rice pudding, wish we had been given more than a tablespoon.


*  The fries are great, the polenta has a weird taste, the fried cardoons were bland and somewhat soggy and the polenta encrusted mushrooms would have tasted better if they were not cold.

*  It's a great place for grouchy toddlers because the staff likes them, the crowd doesn't care either way and its so loud that if by chance the kid let's out a blood curdling scream nobody will hear him...awesomeness

*  If you love fish, specifically seared cod order it here.  They cook it to the perfect consistency and the accompanying sauce and veggies are delish.

*  Militant Vegans should not be taken here.  My brother was less than pleased by the number of meat entrees versus Vegan/Vegetarian.  My husband, stepdaughter and I were thrilled, but he was not...which made for a tense dinner.  Note: if you do by accident end up here with a militant vegan, don't point out each meal option for them...they don't like that and may snap at you and possibly your mother loudly.

*  If you are roasted chicken fan but are often disappointed by the poor consistency and flavor offered in most establishments, order the chicken under a brick here.  Its moist, juicy and flavorful but not too salty.  The accompanying sauce and grains are sort of weird though.

*  It's easy to spend a lot of money here with small portion sizes, no bread unless requested and an ample beverage, appetizer and dessert list.  If you are broke go to Amanda's down the street.

*  Order the vegan Chocolate Cake, even if you are a heartless carnivore you will love this!!!
Been there twice and both times were just okay.  My salad was pretty good.  The pizza's come a bit charred and I'm not a huge fan of the egg on pizza.  It's just an egg folks~

With all the accolades here, I hardly to need to add another, but will just say that after deciding not to go to Gather right away precisely because of all the hype, I did go anyway last night, and was completely won over.

We had a reservation, arrived early and were seated early.  Service was flawless; our waiter sized us up accurately ("these two are settling in for the evening"), and then paced our meal perfectly. 

Other have described the food so well here that I won't even try; our four dishes were like nothing I have ever eaten, I felt completely transported, and I loved it.

Flawless food - absolutely flawless. Inventive, delicious, satisfying, and more.

Eat at the bar if you know what's good for you!

Gather, you schmancy huh?

Apparently this place is super hard to get a reservation on a Saturday morning? A friend and I came around 11:00AM, and it was half full. It definitely picked up though as we left!

We split the breakfast pizza (I think it was the egg) and the special of the day (sausage with fried egg). The titles are a lot more glamorous, and coming from LA, I appreciate the pizazz. Frankly, the food was delicious, and my friend enjoyed his cup of coffee. The pizza had a healthy helping of BACON! Nomage, because who doesn't love bacon?

Great service. They had still or sparkling water. QUITE fancy *pinky shoots out* 

I'd come back next time I'm in the area!

Gather has organically turned into my boyfriends and I's celebratory meal location. When we are wanting to toast our glasses we think, Pizza with egg...oh hell to the yeah! This place is a fine establishment with loads of interested dishes. In addition to their food, the decor is really beautiful and elegant in the no fuss Cali sorta way. Yes please.

WOAH! This may be the perfect restaurant. Rotating seasonal menu that always includes some version of incredible vegan charcuterie (beet tartar, carrot roasted in soil, miso-rosemary pinenuts), pizza (kimchi and prosciutto, garlic and nettle) and top-notch entrees to sate the carnivores among us (Prather Ranch burger, grilled chicken with lentils and braised greens). There will inevitably be ingredients you've never heard of, but that's part of the fun. Be sure to ask how big what you're getting is- some appetizers are frustratingly small and some entrees too big to finish.

"The Spicy Tomato is best vegan pizza ever... and easily one of the best pizza's ever."

FOOD: Delicious
AMBIANCE: Open, airy, friendly, serene
SERVICE: Incredibly friendly, totally helpful

The king likes pizza, and since going mostly vegan in the past 18 months, vegan pizza has been mostly a disappointment. Most vegan pizzas are either an afterthought, or a sort of special request. Gather went to the trouble of doing their research and coming up with something incredibly appealing. 

We also had the kale salad, which was also spectacular. 

They did mess our order up (forgot to veganize the kale salad) but they were so very nice and friendly about it, it didn't detract from the experience at all. 

Thank you, Gather, for doing your research and offering a superb dining experience for carnies, veggies and vegans alike.

In theory, I'm really glad this place exists. I'm completely on board with the local,  fresh,  organic, sustainable ethic that the restaurant has been designed around. I'm also a lifelong vegetarian, and while I've never had a problem eating out in the east bay, it's sometimes a relief to sit down with a menu that's been crafted with my dietary restrictions in mind. Finally, they serve cocktails, which is almost unheard of in my neighborhood, and it's a 10 minute walk from my house.

I went here on a Saturday evening a few months after it opened, and was completely disappointed.  Service, while kind, was slow and erratic, the food was bland and unmemorable, the drinks were weak, and the entire experience was completely overpriced. The atmosphere was similarly disappointing. It was clear that a great deal of attention had gone into designing the space, but that didn't translate into a better dining experience. It was crowded without being lively, didn't manage to be cozy or intimate. My girlfriend commented that the whole experience felt soulless, and I have to agree with her.

I've eaten here 5 times now and I've never been disappointed. 

I'm not a vegan, but I love their Vegan "charcuterie" and their kale caesar is as good as kale gets. 

In my opinion, this is the first vegetarian friendly restaurant Berkeley has had of this quality and I'm very appreciative.

I was taken here for an administrative assistant week lunch by a colleague, and oddly enough ended up ordering the egg sandwich with bacon. Most of their menu is vegan and/or gluten free, which I am not at all opposed to - takes me back to my vegetarian days. 

All of the ingredients are incredibly fresh. The yolk in my egg was that farm fresh bright yellow-orange that you see in really fresh eggs. The bacon was thick and tasty. It came with a nice little side salad.

The first thing I noticed when I walked in was the energy of the place. It's round in shape, with lots of windows that they had open to let the breeze come through. The furniture is all wood, and there are plants and vines hanging from the ceiling that somehow really add to the ambiance. I think my favorite part of the meal was the environment.

I'll definitely go back to try their pizza which was on everyone's table and looked amazing. The only thing that caught me off guard was how small the menu was. A couple salads, one soup, a couple sandwiches, and a few pizzas to choose from. But other than that, I'm excited to go back and try dinner.

We have tested this resturant last night. The location and decoration were very good but the quality of the food was not good at all. The soup was just water and the pizza also was smelly! I do not recommend this place. 

We came back home and had more dinner after paying 77$! (5 person)

Restroom was great specially the liquid soap! I loved the smell of the liquid soap.

On the other hand, the customer service was great too. I liked the behavior of the personnels.

Had the special t-bone with brisket and all sorts of goodness mixed in.  I made a reservation pretty late and we had no problem getting our table when we arrived.  The drinks were pretty good, and interesting getting drinks that came from sustainable sources.  The food came pretty slowly, the waiter did apologize and was very nice about it.  We weren't in a hurry so it was totally fine!

Great place, great food.

We had dinner there a couple months ago and I agree with most of the yelpers... The vegan charcuterie was sooo good! Everything on that platter had a burst of so many great flavors that's pretty indescribable.. from the beef tartare to the turnips... Yum! You'll just have to try it for yourself.

We also ordered the nettle pizza.. Omg, best goat cheese pizza ever!  I had never tried pizza with goat cheese prior to this visit, and now, everytime I make pizza.. I come up with my own concoction of leeks, red onions, homemade tomato sauce, pineapple sausage, and of course, goat cheese! Thank you, Gather.. for giving me a whole new perspective on pizza!

Anyhow, I knocked off 1 star because we made a reservation on open table and somehow the hostess couldn't find it.  We had to wait a few minutes but they were pretty nice about it.  This place is very 'green' and 'organic' which is great, but they will definitely tell you to put away your ipad if you bust it out in the restaurant!  

Oh yeah, and parking's a bitch! Arrive half and hour before your reservation to find parking or just use the public parking garage. Overall, great food! I will definitely go there again!

Let me qualify this by saying I've only been here once and was wildly impressed, but we only ordered three items so I don't feel I've sampled enough of their dishes to fairly render five stars.  But it's definitely a contendah.

We dropped in for lunch on a drizzly Saturday afternoon after becoming disillusioned with the menu at another establishment down the street.  I'd been meaning to come here so we walked the short two blocks and were lucky enough to score a table.

The restaurant itself is brand new and set up in a half-oval shape around the center focus: the kitchen.  It is attractively designed and decorated.  Booths and chairs are comfortable and there were several large groups there, including a few with kids. 

I had a tough time making up my mind what to get.  Everything sounded so good and inviting, healthy without being pretentious, inventive without being ridiculous. (I don't get why other people are hating on the fennel pollen butter, have they TRIED it?)  We decided against ordering brunch items, but I saw them passing by on other people's plates so I would like to come back here for brunch/breakfast sometime.

As in other instances, we order one salad, then two entrees with the intent of sharing them.  We settled on the roasted beet salad  to start, then chose the Prather Ranch burger and the roasted squash pizza.  I didn't pay much attention to the little (v) indicator next to the pizza indicating it was vegan.  So I was expecting cheese, etc.etc.  The whole nine yards.

The salad came and it was so incredibly fresh, the baby mustard greens peppery and crisp and perfectly dressed.  I love beets so I was picking those little puppies out and savoring each one.  Great way to start the meal.

Okay, so yeah, a burger is "just a burger".  No big deal, it's not as if we are talking about a Kobe filet mignon, right?  Wrong!  Damn, what a burger!  Everything about it was done the way I would want my perfect burger to be done.  Cooked perfectly, juicy and hot, just the right amount of cheese, bun fresh and gently crisped on the grill, generous helping of sinful shoestring fries and a small side salad of more arugula.  I inhaled my half way too fast and was sad when it was gone.  

But then, there was..... pizza.

I hadn't noticed it said on the menu that this pizza is vegan, which  means "no cheese", so of course I was expecting cheese.  The first bite I noticed that something was different because when I pulled away with my first mouthful I didn't get chased with big drippy cheese strings like I usually do.  The sage/cashew cream is the nectar of the gods!  This is no sub-par, fake "cheese substitute", this is way way WAY better than any real cow-juice cheese, could even hope to be, ever.  I never ever would have thought I would go into ecstasies over a vegan pizza, but that was the best goddamn pizza I've ever had, and I have eaten a lot of good pizza.  I was so pleasantly surprised, and it made me so very happy!

We were too full for dessert, and had half of the amazing pizza to take home for later... YAY!  Now I am left plotting and scheming on how I can get back there for more of that pizza.  Surely it couldn't be as good as my memory is making it out to be... right?  Next time I want to save room for one of those naughty-looking desserts too.  Pumpkin cheesecake with orange creme fraische?  Outta my way!

Well let me start out by saying I am a picky eater, however, I usually find something that will float my boat.  But I'd never go back here.  Their menu is pretty limited.  I'm a beef kinda girl and the only beef they had was a burger, so that's what I got.  A $14 burger add bacon for $3 - $17 burger.  IT was NOT great.  For $17 for a burger, I want FANTASTIC and it so wasn't.  The fries, however were pretty dang good!  Their menu is not simple.  There is a lot of extra stuff that I found some ingredient I didn't want to eat in each dish.  I like simple food done very well.  I just didn't find that here.  Oh well.
Ok. It's organic. We had the pumpkin soup, pizza with sheep cheese (?), and house burger.  Well, it's ok and nothing to write home about

I have been living in LA for a year now and this is one of the places that I still think about from when I lived in Berkeley.

This place is great. Go here. 

Order the vegan charcuterie, you won't be disappointed. The vibe is hipster/vegan/boho/organic. They are locally sourced, organically grown and just really delicious. The food is inventive and appeals to vegan/veg/omnivore alike. 

I have almost perfected the pisco sour cocktail at home but it still doesn't taste quite as good as the ones at Gather did. 

I hope to visit again soon and pray that it is as good as I remember.
Fresh ingredients, tasty food, nice, casual ambiance and great service.  What more can you ask for?  Would definitely go back again!
The food, cocktails, and service were all stellar.  I look forward to going back.  I have a friend who's as much of a foodie as I am so I can't wait to introduce him to this spot.

Whoa!!  I haven't reviewed anything on yelp in awhile but this was so darn good that I have to.

My girlfriend and I were really hungry and our original dinner plans didn't end up happening.  Sooo...... We had a last second starvathon snack at McDonald's.  Can I say that here?   Anyways, point is.... we weren't that hungry but we still wanted to go out.  Got there at about 9.  Got seated immediately at the counter, which was cool because i got to watch everyone cook and remember my old restaurant days.  Seems like they put a lot of love in what they do.  Service was good.  

Here's what we had.

Bee Sting- beautiful cocktail with honey and botanical liquor of some sort and other stuff.  Pretty kick ass.  Went well with the

Vegan charcuterie-  Man, this was awesome.  I am too lazy to put all the stuff we got but the last guy who reviewed here did it for me.  so check it.  I could eat this little set up everyday.  I do have to say, that i saw the regular charcuterie go out and my mouth was watering.  Beautiful piles of meat always turn me on.  Don't regret my decision on the vegan bit but next time we're going meaty.  

Chocolate torte with ?fleur de sel caramel?  cocoa nibs and lemon verbena ice cream - Awesome!  Just...... awesome.  I originally craved something a little more inventive but the waiter said this was good and he didn't lie.  

Girlfriend got a chai tea.  It was great.  

So..... next time i'm not going to have McDonalds beforehand and check out one of the most delicious looking pizzas i've ever seen.  

So, my final thoughts on Gather.....

I'm lovin' it.

Just FYI to everyone reading this - I tend to have an addictive personality. For food, that means once something piques my interest and excites my tastebuds, it occupies my thoughts and cravings for, well, Ever.

I am addicted to Gather. It occupies my thoughts, my cravings, my daydreams, my dreams, my inbetween dreams, my spacing out moments of absentmindedness and even when I'm showering and just thinking about how nice warm water feels, the thoughts turn to Gather, their delicious Pisco Sour drink, their pizzas (if they have it, try the mussel pizza because ohmygodthatissofrigginmothereffingooditsinsane), their delicious trifle dessert...

To be honest, I've never been less than satisfied at Gather and I've been there four times for dinner in the last three months. Perhaps the closest I've been to anything approaching disappointment is when trying their vegan charcuterie, but I think if I had still been a vegetarian when I tried it (and not been acclimated with pork... sweet, sweet, delicious pork! [which they do really well]) it would've been pretty damn satisfying.

The power of low to middling expectations.  This is how my friend described Gather to me, 'There probably won't be a lot of food, it's kinda expensive, and it's most likely going to be healthy food.'  Now, that doesn't sound too horrible, but it's not exactly what i would call a ringing endorsement. 

I'm glad she was mostly wrong.  Not only were we very very satisfied with the quality of the food, but the quantity as well was more than sufficient.  The prices were acceptable for such top shelf ingredients, and there's nothing wrong with clean eating when the food is this delicious.  

We partook in the albacore and squid as starters (mmmm~ seafoooood). With a soup and pork chop to follow.  Not one complaint did i have with the meal, and topping it off with cheesecake might have been the best decision of the entire night.  Now i just need for her to work on her descriptive skills and we're good to go.

It is hard to say meh in the same sentence as pork belly, but sometimes we have to fight on and take the harder path.  I say this because I ordered the pork belly hash (ironically named "summer vegetable hash") and my tongue was only mildly amused.  

First off, the price point is $15, so expectations are for a killer hash.  What arrives is a big pile of fresh corn, some Padron peppers (whole, tossed into the mess with stem and all) and 5 cubes of pork belly under two fried eggs, some vinegared greens and two toast points.   $15?  It was good, but nothing special and you are starting to get into an upper level brunch point at that pricing.  I liked (not loved) my food and my cohorts food was simply OK too.  

When we left, we walked away comparing Gather to other brunch options and found similar and better for probably less money at other local haunts (Venus, La Note, Sunny Side, the Vault, Bette's, etc). 

Looking at Gather's menu, I think the Pizza with egg shared between two people would get me to come back for a try (and would be a unique order and value too) but little else on the menu jumped out in that regard.  

The space is nice, the service was very good, but the odds I go back are very low; because Gather's menu is priced higher and yet not better than other local options.  Plus there isn't that unique item that only Gather can provide (maybe the pizza, which I did not yet sample).

I've been twice in the last month, and I have to say that the experiences were very different. On the first visit, we sat at a larger table for 6 or 7 and ordered all the pizzas on the menu, 2 appetizers , three desserts and some drinks. The drinks ranged from good to great, and all the food was excellent. 

The second visit, the menu items had changed, and the only item I ordered again was the burrata which was still good. However, the rest of the food and dessert was extremely inconsistent. The worst was the chocolate ravioli (there were 2 very flat three inchers on the plate) which had a weird rubbery texture. The blueberry cobbler was ok, it was like a corn bread pudding that was a little soggy on the bottom but nice a crispy on top. The beet fed oyster presentation made us laugh- pink tinted two oysters next to a swath of brown pate? It tasted good, but the two little oysters were kind of sad. The egg and pancetta pizza was too salty but the crust was fine, and the papperdelle texture wasn't bad for gluten free, but it was definitely made of tofu skins. That and the veggie risotto was a bit side-dishy for me. For almost 40 bucks a person (we ordered a drink each), i was disappointed. I don't mind a light dinner, but I do expect better consistency when paying good money. In addition I was the last to eat the last slice of pizza, and the busboy cleared everyone else's dishes when I ate. I was a little put out but didn't say anything. 

I might go again if I had vegan or gluten allergy/celiacs ppl in my party, but I would order very strategically.

Delicious, hearty vegetarian options (as well as meat), but the real star here is the dessert.  Each time I go, the desserts blow my mind.  The most memorable was a pine nut tart that was out of this world.  The apple crisp, the chocolate mousse-- and the vegan options are rich and scrumptious.  Whatever you do, don't say the words "What are your specials?" or time freezes and the chefs turn into zombies and will sacrifice at least three vegans.  Make sure to save room for dessert-- the best bet is to get a few apps and skip straight to the good stuff.

So, my boyfriend and I decided to come in on a Saturday night without a reservation. There were several hostesses at the front podium who were very confused about where to seat us. They could not provide an estimated wait time, and they didn't communicate with each other at any point to figure things out. They seemed really flustered, and we had the same question asked to us several times (how many? would you like to sit at the bar?) We were informed that an open table was being reserved for a 9:15pm reservation, but the reservation never showed up! We ended up getting seated at the bar.

Despite a rough start, I was eager to get ordering - it was already pretty late, and we were hungry. When my boyfriend tried to order ginger beer, they were out. Then, we tried to order a pomegranate drink and they were out of that too. Seemed like they didn't have too large of selection of drinks to begin with, and the drinks they did have were all out. 

Still, I give Gather four stars, because our appetizer blew me away. We ordered the mushroom bruschetta, and it was seriously damn good. The mushroom flavor was not as overpowering as I thought it would be. Everything about that dish was perfect! I also got the Gnocci, which was good, but bland. It tasted more like a vegetable stew, and I had expected something a little bit more flavorful. The gnocci pieces were too soft, and overall the dish could have been better. My boyfriend's burger on the other hand was so good! Perfectly cooked, very juicy, and well-garnished with bbq sauce and onion straws.

Overall - pros: incredible appetizer, good service & a cool waiter, and a delicious burger; cons: bad hosts, not so good gnocci, and limited drinks.

One of my aunts who is a vegetarian discovered Gather. So, to celebrate her birthday we went there brunch today. I made a reservation in advance for four people, but it turns out I made the reservation for the wrong day. I thought I had reserved brunch for 1:30pm today but my reservation was for 1:30pm yesterday. But, the maitre d's were great and honored my reservation although I was a day late! Anyway, I had the Farm Egg Pizza which was Delicious, which was topped with bacon, caramelized onions, and, oregano. The others in my party had the Hedgehog Scramble, Braised Belouga Lentils, Prather Ranch Burger, and the Fontilla Pizza. I tasted each and they were very tasty. For dessert the group shared a vegan chocolate chip Cookie and a lemon tart with huckleberries, Overall, I would highly recommend Gather if you have any vegetarian friends and your in the Berkeley area. I will definitely will be returning for lunch soon.
Great food, great place for a date

I had dinner there with two friends last night and we had a great time in this new restaurant.  The restaurant was crowded when we walked in around 8:15, but we had a beer as we waited about 10 minutes for a table to open up.  

Our group started out with an appetizer, House Cured Meats (Artisanal Platter) which was very, very good.  I ordered a Housemade Burger and was quite satisfied even though I thought the burger was a bit salty.  Overall, Gather is a great new restaurant in Berkeley which serves locally produced food along with organic ingredients.  Check it out, folks!

Had dinner last night and the food was really wonderful.  Delicious vegan and vegetarian options, everything super fresh and expertly prepared and so nice to finish it off with a little "boar pizza" when the veggies didn't totally hit the spot.  Also, the service was perfect.  

My only complaint is that the restaurant has a little bit of a cafeteria feel to it - very big and open and a bit too loud.  This would be fine except that the prices are a little more aligned with what should be a more intimate dining experience.  My company at dinner last night would probably disagree with this assessment, but hey - that's why they're opinions, right?

Thoroughly enjoyed my meal.

Don't bother looking for street parking - there's a parking garage below the building that costs $4 and your time is worth more than that.

*Unrelated bonus - got pulled over on the way home by a cute and friendly (and non-ticketing) Berkeley policeman cuz my lights weren't on... "Thank you officer!"

Tasty seasonal menu, good service, beautiful decor, and good company made my first visit to Gather a memorable one.  It was a little mini-reunion of sorts with my favorite gal pals in the bay, and this was our choice for dinner, as they were able to seat us without a reservation on a Saturday night within 30 minutes.

We first sat at the bar in the back of the restaurant, and had a nice little chit chat with the bartendress who went over the wine list with us.  I opted for the Donkey & Goat Four Thirteen red wine, which went well with the Prather Ranch Burger that I ended up choosing as my entree, once seated.  My burger was in one three-letter word - YUM.  My friend Anne, who also chose the burger, proclaimed it as the best burger she's ever had.  I wouldn't go that far, but I will say it was damned tasty.  Cooked to perfection -- Medium Rare -- and with really yummy ingredients, I practically licked my plate clean.  When it came to dessert, my group opted for a Blueberry Custard with pepper ice cream... who'd have thunk that pepper ice cream would be so damned good?  It was the perfect combo for the custard.  My cappuccino I ordered was also really lovely.

Service was friendly, casual, and attentive.  Our server, Chris, was very accommodating with my friend who was doing a gluten-free, vegan diet, offering up suggestions of what she could have, and how they could modify some menu items for her.  

Will definitely be coming back for more the next time I'm in NorCal.
The food and service are very very good. Been here twice: one for lunch and once for dinner.

tried this place for the first time last night, and was very pleased.  

we first ordered a salad called "little gem" and it was pretty good; there was supposed to be toasted nori in it, but they were hard to find, probably because they were cut into very small pieces.  but tasty nonetheless.  

the highlight were two things:

1) duck sausage pizza - very delicious, thin crust, puffy outter crust, cooked just right; whereas at most pizzerias the crust is thick and dense and fills you up, so you end up not eating it, the crust here was both dense and light and didn't fill you up.  there was a duck egg on it, right in the middle, the yolk nice and runny and so so savory.  each bite was like a little slice of heaven. 

2) blood orange sorbet - had this for desert, and boy, it was delish too.  was sweet and bitter, like a grapefruit, and tart too, and so cut the richness of the pizza perfectly.

the ambiance is cool, large open dining room, lots of wood furniture, kinda rustic, kinda chic.  gets a bit noisy, which is the only drawback.  seems like it's a hit with all of the berkeley foodies.

though i live in sf, i'll definitely come back and eat there again.

I took my parents here tonight.  Mom had the Pink Lady Apple Pizza special.  It was beautiful!  Dad had the burger and conversation stopped while he ate it (too good for words)  I had the bean ragout and it was also really wonderful.  The atmosphere was friendly and welcoming.

What I thought was great was that the portion sizes weren't enormous.  They were more towards what a NORMAL HUMAN should consume at a meal.  Quantity does not equal quality.  I'll be returning next time I'm in the bay.

This is a pretty amazing place.  The food is always good, as long as you are up for a bit of an adventure.  Do not take the menu literally - it might read "risotto" to describe the dish, but really, it is potato balls.  The dish is delicious, but no one would order potato balls with grilled veggies and dressing, so Summer "Risotto" it is. The vegan charcuterie is always fun to order.  Some are unbelievable good, others not, but it is still great to try new things.  Good appetizer for a group because everyone has different favorite.  The decor is cool, and the concept good.  Kicker cocktails too.  If you like them strong, try the Sazerac.  Sip, don't slurp.   Reservations are good, but you can get in if you go early or late.  You can also walk in and eat at the bar if seats are available.  Bar? Yes, there is a bar hidden in the back left corner.  Staff at door are friendly, as are most wait staff.  Bar staff can be abrupt, but warm up as you hang out.  Overall, a great place for something fresh and different.  If you are craving familiar and homey, not the place for you.

Went here for brunch with a group of friends. I had their spicy eggs and tried out my friend's brunch pizza. Both were good. HOwever, I did not like their bloody mary - maybe because it's vegan. Overall a nice dining experience. I really like their restaurant design and atmosphere.

I had wanted to eat here for a while and now I wont be back for a while.

1. The food is... okay. (too much hype -- unless I ordered the wrong thing) I have a few simple rules about any restaurant. Your restaurant is only as good as it's service, it's cocktails and hamburgers. (hamburgers and cocktails are important to me and they should be easy to knock out)

* Server was terrible
* Cocktails were kinda expensive.. but they were good.. I think? It took too long to get each one.. My girlfriend and I only had 2 drinks each but it felt like we waited 4 hours for each one.
* The hamburger was okay, not the greatest. I know, we should have ordered something else, something they are known for -- our bad. 

2. The SERVICE was AWFUL. I know times are tough -- I know tips are getting smaller when they should be getting larger therefore care is the first thing to go out the window. OUR server did not care and forgot she had us as a table. Biggest advice to service staff -- TRY TO CARE.

3. The hostess was the saving grace of this place -- she knew we weren't happy and kept trying to help us, she offered her condolences because they happen to be short staffed that night. I don't remember her name but she was great and deserves a raise.

I will be back at some point because everyone deserves a second chance -- I will make sure to ask my server what to order and leave it to their control.

See you soon.

You cannot believe how sublime this food is. Every dish I had for a three day visit to Berkeley was full of new flavors and combinations. I didnt want to eat anywhere else. Staff is smart and efficient. Prices are way below what the restaurant could charge for such quality. Gather is the best restaurant I've eaten at in the entire Pacific Northwest.

A change in scenery in laid back Berkeley:  sunny with blue skies, waves of young students with backpacks walking around, tall redwood trees.  And of course, Gather.

I had the great privilege of dining here with two dear friends recently.  The space is an unusual shape-sort of a half circle, with natural earth tones, medium wood tables and light airy metal light fixtures throughout.  Regular and sparkling waters are served in upcycled Strauss milk bottles and the servers are incredibly friendly, genuine and can offer great suggestions on portion size and favorite dishes.  We shared the gently sweet stone fruit green salad and a smoky and crispy pancetta pizza with a thin crust and two fried eggs on top.  Sheer heaven.

Our sweet tooths lead us to split a chocolate almond torte, gluten free, with a healthy dollop of whip cream and macerated strawberries.  

My kind friends let me take home the leftover pizza which I enjoyed for quick snack/lunch.  Memories flood back to a beautiful day spent with truly sweet and generous people.

Gather your dearest and closest family and friends and try.  You'll be pleased you did.  

PS Make reservations. It fills up quickly. A seasonal menu too.  Gather and nourish.

Uh!!! Where do I even begin?! AMAZING. Great atmosphere, vegan and gluten free options/availability listed right on the menu items. The drinks feel like they are healing elixirs. Super unique dishes (I couldn't tell you the names of the entrees, but my mouth waters to think about them again.) Take your date here, they will want to go home with you.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here for brunch on a weekend through a reservation on Yelp. This place is magical!

The layout of this restaurant is spacious and inviting. There are huge windows that let plentiful rays of sunshine dance all over your table, and the back section includes the kitchen decorated with a hanging ivy display. They have dim lamps that hang around the restaurant and add a down-to-earth feel to the place.

We were seated and served water from a glass jar! I really like little things like that hahaha. They gave us a printed menu specifically for brunch, and we happily placed our orders.

|| F O O D ||

ACME WALNUT FRENCH TOAST: Braised Bosc pears and Banana winter squash, maple walnut sauce, Straus yogurt [$12]
- The French toast was moist and sweet, akin to something angels probably eat for breakfast. I preferred my friend's toast to my pancakes because of the delicate balance of starch, sugar, butter, and cinnamon.
- The maple walnut sauce was beautiful! The walnuts were stewed to a slightly soft crunchiness, which added wonderful texture to the plate. The yogurt on the side was a great addition and dampened the sugary goodness of the sauce and fruits. Although I wish they could have swirled it into the sauce (not everyone would like that though).
- The pears and squash were brewed in some wonderful syrupy concoction, and the squash was a unique and delectable facet of the dish.

HARD RED WINTER WHEAT PANCAKES: Braised Fuyu persimmon, pomegranate, whipped Bellwether sheep ricotta [$11]
- Soft cloud-like pancakes drizzled in syrup and topped with a small mound of ricotta. Seriously, the ricotta made this dish a WINNER. It was spectacular amidst the fruits and syrup!
- I have never eaten anything but raw persimmon, so persimmon soaked in their magical syrup was pure magic. The persimmon was chewy and sweet, and the slight crunch from the pomegranate was brilliant! I wish they had given me more pomegranate though. At least it was ripe!

|| C L O S U R E ||

A delectable dining experience with quality food and quality service! A bit pricey for me, but I would return to try something new! And if you're here for brunch, I would highly recommend the French toast!

Gather was fantastic!!!! I can't wait to go back and eat amazing vegan/vegetarian prepared food.  It makes you wonder why you ever ate meat!  
I think Gather is significantly better than Millennium in SF.  If you haven't been I seriously recommended giving Gather a try!

Happen to be in Berkeley and saw this busy restaurant on a Thursday evening around 830pm.  Drove around the block several times and finally go a parking spot. Walked in but waiting list however we were offered 2 seats at the counter and we were sat immediately.
First glance at menu is it is pricey for a mid week and quick dinner.  Ended up with a Kale salad w/ toasted pine nuts and a nice vinegrette dressing-delish. The pizza was incredible!  Light crust and very flavorful cheese..best pizza outside of NY. The Niman ranch burger and fries were good. Watching the sous chefs prepare fresh salads in front of us with seasonally sourced greens were cool.  After the meal, we realized why the menu seemed a bit pricey but it was all worth it!  We would come back again.

Would definitely come back for the excellent ambiance (high end down to earthed ness) and great food - their Kale salad is super hearty and the farm egg pizza with bacon is pretty much to die for. For dessert, we got the ganache cupcake (there's a special name for it) which was good, paired with their coffee. BUT the service was subpar - our waiter was friendly enough, but seemed to be in a bit of a rush to get us out of there...but it was only one guy, so who knows. The hostess was super friendly as was the other waiter whom we bothered to take our picture. All in a all, a great place for a nicer lunch or dinner :).

Amazing Sunday Brunch !!
It was our first visit to Gather. We walked in a few minutes before 11AM without a reservation - no problem, no attitude.  The service was good not spectacular but certainly better than your average "college student waitperson" experience. But most importantly the food was amazing - the vegetarians were happy, (OMG the french toast was to die for)  the meat-eaters were happy (Sausage & eggs & toast & potatoes), the Pizza eaters were happy (maybe the best crust I've ever eaten) coffee drinkers were very very happy.  The portions were generous which is good because it's not cheap- but very worth every penny !!!

Gather is a restaurant that no doubt belongs in Berkeley, and only in the Bay Area.  Though the concept is awesome, I do not know if I would truly pick it for a prime dining experience.  It is nice and casual though, without any pretension.  It is also very affordable for fine grub.  I guess the best way to view it is "fit for foodies."

My overall impression was that the food was extremely well done, but it was nothing too out of the ordinary.  They definitely prepare vegetables in very unique fashion here.

I came mainly for one dish, the "vegan" charcuterie.  It was pretty much what you get at a raw eatery or Whole Food's "raw" section.  The platter was no doubt representative of hippie eating.  I also had the soup of the day.

The charcuterie tray: The citrus carpaccio was fresh and earthy with shaved beets, olives, and slivers of citrus fruits.  The roasted squash with cashew/bay leaf sauce and smoked maple was probably the best item, as it was hearty and slightly sweet.  The mushroom crudo and parsnip-pine nut risotto was a bit too complex with too much crunchy, softness, and nuttiness and too much of that raw flavor.  The braised endive with yuba and avocado on toast was savory, rich, and simple.  The worst of the spread was the chicory lettuce sausage; it was too pungent and soft.  All in all, the tray was an extremely creative spread of vegetables, and definitely is THE item to try here.

The pumpkin and chile soup was good and creamy, but it lacked a depth of flavor.  It had a nice punch from the chiles.

My dinner here was a great display of what vegetables can do, but I was not terribly impressed.  Nonetheless, the food was good, and the service was solid.  Gather is certainly a restaurant to check out in Berkeley.

I met N here for an early dinner before a night at Berkeley Rep.  The restaurant filled almost as soon as the doors opened.   While perusing the menu I enjoyed one of their signature organic cocktails.   I chose a tangy tart blend of Cucumber Vodka, Agave and lemon juices with egg whites and hibiscus powder of the top

We decided to share two small plates and one large plate.

Fresh anchovies (2) with aioli and topped with a crispy fried Brussels sprout; it was so good we decided if we not really full we would have another order at the end of our meal. Alas we were full and did not place a second order.

Next up was the fried mushrooms and pickled sun chokes with a citrus aioli; this dish was another winner.

We finished the up with a burger with Sierra Nevada cheese red onion and aioli. This was served with a thin crispy fries and a caramelized shallot-tomato sauce.  This was also good.  It would have been better with more of the sauce.

The three dishes were enough for us this time.  The small plates are just that and the large one was not that large I suspect that for many people the servings are really too small. This is an ideal location for vegans and carnivores to both enjoy a dinner together.

Parking is very difficult!

Gather is simply an amazing addition to the Bay Area food scene.  Walked in on the latish side on a Friday night and were gracefully seated at a nice 2 top close enough to the kitchen to see the action, but far enough away to enjoy conversation with an old friend who I shared many good years both growing up with and as a student at Cal many years ago.

So my friend isn't particularly big on beer and she said she might of had a little too much wine the night before, so we were more than excited by the fact that Gather has a full bar.  What is it about Berkeley restaurants that so few actually have a full bar.  Needless to say, Gather's well curated selection of spirits was great and their cocktail list was perfect too.  Just enough selection to provide variety, but not such a laundry list that you  lose your way trying to decide.  

Being late and not wanting to eat too much, we had the vegetarian charcuterie platter and the salad with the squid and spring vegetables.  Both dishes were exceptional.  Seasoning was perfect, culinary technique spotless, and the simplicity of the presentations was truly refreshing.  Bay Area food gets a pretty bad rap often for this style of food, (and it is often warranted due to poor execution) but I would put these dishes up against anything I've ever had in NYC or elsewhere.  On the Veg platter, the highlight was the cashew goat cheese with the salt roasted beets and braised pistachios. which was perfectly balanced and the vibrant fuchsia color emanating off of the plate from the  beets was like nothing I've ever seen.

I'm definitely going to go out of my way to head into Berkeley more often, as a combo day shopping at the Berkeley Bowl and a meal at gather can't really be topped culinary experience wise anywhere.

Gather was fantastic.

We went for a relatively early (7 pm) dinner on Saturday after Thanksgiving.  When we got there, it was hopping!  I worried about getting a table, but they were able to find a spot for the two of us.  Service++

The menu was small, but every item on was locally sourced and looked interesting.  I ordered a roasted vegetables dish (brocolli, artichokes, chanterelles) and my husband ordered one of the veggie pizzas.  The roasted vegetables were amazing, especially the romanesco brocolli - if you have kids who won't eat brocolli, try roasting it.  The pizza, I'm told, was "incredibly delicious".  It was also almost large enough for two, so if we go again (we live in South Bay) we'll share a pizza and appetizer instead.

Food, service, atmosphere, all were great.

I'm docking one star because I wanted to order a meat-and-veggies dish, but the meat ones looked pretty intensely meaty.  Also, a better description of menu items with uncommon terms in their names would be fantastic.  I ended up ordering a dish with Brassicas, and to ask the waitor what those were (they're brocolli).

I can empathize with other reviewers' comparisons of Gather to Chez Panisse Cafe. However the service is rough around the edges, and will need time to iron out. I don't want to spend too much time waxing the many little ways service was off, so let's talk about the food.

Gather isn't scared of vinegar in their dressings, and neither should you. The salads are amazing - wild arugula with strawberries and pecorino, and the most curious (and delicious) endive salad with crispy seaweed I've ever had. 

"Vegan charcuterie" shouldn't be something you ever order at a restaurant. However, Gather simply takes vegetables and makes them d-e-l-i-c-i-o-u-s by adding a magical combination of flavors, puts them in five small bunches on a board, and calls it "vegan charcuterie" on the menu. Don't worry, it's not vegetables trying to be meat substitutes -- it's just really good vegetables with gourmet flavors that make you savor the small bites, like good charcuterie.

I can't wait to come back here. Hopefully, the service will be better. I can list half a dozen awkward mistakes and flaws with service tonight, but I'd rather not. If the service at Gather can match the caliber of the food here, I hope Michael Bauer adds Gather to his list of the top 100 restaurants in the Bay Area.

I am a big fan of Gather's Food. I have been here many times before. Unfortunately, last time I came here, the service was very disappointing. It was surprising to me since I always had good service prior. It took approximately half an hour for our waiter to give us the dessert menu and the check even though he was going to tables near the area where we were seated. He was doing so well up until then. 

I am giving Gather 4 stars because they have the best Vegan / Vegetarian food around where I reside. They have something for everyone (Gluten Free / Vegan / Vegetarian / Carnivore). Their menu changes regularly and I love that because I get bored with things very easily.

Dinner - Must Try:

Vegan "Charcuterie" (the selection changes frequently): 
- Carrots Cooked in Hay, Sage Cream, Smoked Parsnip Lardo, & Currant Vinaigrette 
- Winter Citrus Carpaccio, Shaved Beets, Olives, & Dill 
- Braised Endive, Avocado, Yuba, Smoked Aioli, & Toasted Bread 
- Roasted Squash, Sunchoke Cashew, Bay Leaf Sauce, & Smoked Maple
....
- Salt Roasted Beets, Kombu-Braised Pistachios, Cashew Goat Cheese, & Saba
- Grilled Hen of the Woods, Spring Onion Soubise, Baby Onion Marmalata, Wild Oregano, & Onion Seed 
- Smoked Olives, Kumquats, Avocado, Baby Fennel, & Pepper Vinaigrette 
- Shiitakes, Pignolia, Asparagus, & Green Garlic
....
- Pulled Mushroom, Pistachio, Seaweeds, Olive, Charred Peanuts, Chili, & Cilantro
- Beet Blood Custard & Stems
- Mushroom, Potato, Porcini Butter, Cauliflower, Asparagus, & Dehydrated Onion
- Sprouted lentils, Vadouvan, & Curry Leaf

Compressed Strawberries - Pickled Green Strawberries, Goat Milk Yogurt, Sheep's sorrel, Dill-Pistachio Pesto, & Saba

Young Carrots - Black Trumpet Mushrooms, Hay-Carrot Top Pesto, Fava Beans, Dehydrated Kale, Charred Peel, & Espelette

Strawberry & Kumquat Salad - Arugula, Almonds, White Balsamic, & Vanilla Salt

Lamb Sausage Pizza - Spring Onion-Arbol Chile Salsa, Mint, & Pea Leaves

Duck Sausage Pizza

Pork Belly & Citrus Herb Salad

Sea Urchin


Desserts - Must Try:

Mocha Flan - Whiskey Currant Sauce & an Amaretti Cookie

Spiced Carrot Cake - Cashew Sour Cream Icing, Molasses Blood Orange Sauce, & Walnut Nougatine

Roasted White Chocolate Semifreddo - Strawberry Sauce & Cocoa Nib Caramel Corn

Pippin Apple Crisp, Cinnamon "Ice Cream", Earl Grey-Soaked Currants, Kamut, & Almond Streusel


The food does not disappoint.

Wow, so much better than I expected.  For some reason I thought this place was vegan only and was going with friends on a lark.  Turned out that they have a wide range of options, including fish and meat.  Many items are marked as either gluten free or vegan which I thought helpful--no need to wonder about some of the more complex dishes.

The dining room, open kitchen, and patio are all very beautiful.  Great staff and service.

We loved all of the food, this was absolutely my best restaurant meal in months.  The cost was a little higher than I expected, but not out of line with the quality of the food and overall experience.

The oft mentioned vegan platter was great, I recommend it as an app for sharing.  I wish I'd saved room for a salad, they had many interesting options.  Main courses samples: black cod, cheese burger, several pizzas.  All were really excellent, expecially the pizza.  They do something special with the edge of all their pizzas, making a nice ring of blisters (more delish than this sounds I promise).

Gather is flat out the best restaurant in the Bay. It's ridiculous to expect every single thing on the menu to ALWAYS be incredible. The sustainable concept of the restaurant is so F#&%ing important for our culture to embrace. 
PEOPLE NEED TO STOP EATING MEAT WITH HORMONES and stop supporting these filthy companies that produce it.
I love that I can go here and not be afraid of anything on the menu.
At Gather I can get a chicken and it is the correct size the animal should be. It's not this bloated water logged thing that most restaurants serve.
I am always curious to try every interesting and new thing here.
I guess I am really sick of paying high prices for food at fancy restaurants like Amber and Nopa knowing that the food actually isn't of quality.  Nopa has some organic and local things but not enough.
I am always thrilled to pay the price at Gather.. it is totally worth the money and it feels like you are contributing to a healthy world.
My husband and I drive her from SF at least once a week.
Please open one here in the city!!

I hate to give this place a less then a stellar rating but the service was so bad when I went there last Saturday night that I have to.

1 star for service 5 stars for food = 3 stars.

The food was amazing as usual.  I have been going here since they opened and the food has never disappointed.  
The pizzas are ultra thin and delicious.  The squid salad was great, squid not chewy at all & all the ingredients fresh.
The menu changes constantly - we had the garlic pizza and it was garlicky, not too greasy and thin thin crunchy crust.

The service:  our waiter was either a guy off the street pretending to be a waiter, or a waiter that was really high/hung over, or had just had a lobotomy.  i think he forgot to put our order in, and I didn't feel as though I could communicate with him b/c he would answer in a glazed eye/drone tone appeasement.  
After he realized that we were pissed off due to waiting for over an hour with nothing but appetizers and a no explanation "your food is on its way",  he lied and said he was done with his shift and introduced us to our new waiter. He did not leave as we saw him serving other tables.  I think he was so out of it maybe he didn't realize we would see him, only feet away? I don't know but this person needs to be fired IMHO.   

Our next waiter was a real waiter, not a stoner off the street pretending to be a waiter.  In general the service here is spotty and there is no excuse for it because I don't think Berkeley is a city lacking in experienced wait staff.

Bumping rating down from 5 stars to 4.

I came here twice while I was back home briefly in between work rotations - the first time was by myself http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=NvFMT6kSFO-5f2AZNiD05w, and the second time was two nights later with an old friend.

1. Vegan "charcuterie" 16 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=jKK3azhLMrwndCkNxbgrUw
- mushroom, corn, Purple Viking potatoes, 
porcini butter, dehydrated onion
- watermelon several ways, smoked olive, saba
- pulled mushroom, charred peanuts, pistachio,      
seaweeds
- stone fruit, walnut balsamic puree, chipotle cherry
condiment, Gem marigold
~Mediocre. The charcuterie I had was not the one above, but similar in a few ways. However, it was definitely not as good as the charcuterie I had at Gather previously. The components (mushroom, corn, and beets) were interesting, but they just didn't excel flavor-wise.

2. Pork pate, 28 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=S6fovjQb4Mj5je6UIxkH7A
~Subpar. Maybe I just don't like pate, but I didn't really like this special. Sprigs of green were too large to eat comfortably, couscous was mediocre, and the entire dish was too sour.

3. Full belly potatoes, 26 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=VToyxZ3vfrlh6E7f8ZERlQ
~Mediocre. Potatoes were good, but at the end of the day, it was still a dish of potatoes. I didn't care for the flowers and leaves.

Overall, 3 star dining experience, so I have to take the average and give it a 4. They still have nice water jugs though: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=25SaDYicEWBoDWiD3AA6Gw

This restaurant had so much hype coming with it, but I really do appreciate the sourcing sensibilities.

The "bee sting" cocktail was recommended to the wife, who wanted something "sweet". It turned out to be quite good. The kale salad was a huge mound of kale and unfortunately overly sour. The vegan charcuterie plate was pretty good, but not as amazing as the hype would have you believe. Service was a little odd but maybe they are still getting into the groove.

I'm not a restaurant reviewer but I decided to wait until I had eaten at Gather at least 3 x (I've been 4 x) before I wrote a review.  Simply put, this is the restaurant of my dreams.  Esthetically beautiful -I also love that most all of the materials are recycled (my fave are the kitchen tiles from Heath kilns) - the place is extremely warm and inviting inside and out.  The servers are efficient, knowledgeable and friendly. I am slowly making my way through the menu but my favorites so far are the kale salad, the red quinoa risotto, the garbanzo and calamari appetizer, the lamb appetizer, the cod, and the goat cheese panna cotta.  Everything tastes fresh and light -I have never felt uncomfortably full after eating there.  Any restaurant that grills Acme bread gets and extra star from me!  Still or sparkling water are complementary and the Anderson Valley Pinot I drank with the last meal, perfect. I have no problems with an all California wine list!  The diners all look very happy and  the place is buzzing with excitement.  It doesn't hurt that I often run into someone I know there,  And why not, it is an amazing place to "gather."  Can't wait for my next meal there, of course, I already have a reservation.

I ended up at Gather after driving around not being able to make a decision about where to go. My brother drove past and remembered he had read about it and thought it sounded like something I would really like. (He is a heavy meat-eater and oftentimes scoffs at healthy foods, but knows I am into that kind of thing.)

I didn't know what to expect going in, but I am so glad that we went there. It all sounded so good that my brother and I ended up ordering a bunch of things to share and we were not regretful. We enjoyed eating all of the interesting things included in the Vegan charcuterie he pizza and meatballs were incredible and even though we were so full, we could hardly stop eating. 

The service was excellent and the atmosphere in general is very warm and relaxing. The natural wood and design aesthetic make it a really pleasing place to sit and share a meal. I really like how it's focused on sustainability and locally grown ingredients that are in season (which is fortunately, in Northern California, a lot of things). The food was so fresh tasting and even though we ate a lot, it didn't feel like a typical food hangover after a heavy meal. 

Also had really amazing Moscow Muel's--I had never had one of those before and I was happy with the choice They were made with all organic ingredients, I think including organic vodka? Either way, it was quite delicious.



*We had a really late dinner on a Thursday night (and arrived without reservations), but it looked busy and as if it had been full all night up until that point. On major dinner nights, you might want to make a reso.

Had a great experience dining on the patio with friends. All around good service & good food.

I went simple, had the burger, and wasn't disappointed. The other dishes at my table were great. 

Great organic alcohol/drink options and the bar tenders knew their stuff.

okay, nothing's perfect, right?  & this is why this restaurant does not get the 5 stars...  actually... honestly... it's because they skimped on the wine!!  I mean, c'mon now, @ $ 9-11 a glass, the glass should be half full, not half empty...

but, hey, Jason, our server, was cute.  What a great smile & great attitude, especially when I asked to return my pizza (too much oil tapenade-- can't have it due to my restrictive medical diet).  However, in general, the food was absoultely fabulous.  And here, for further explanation, is Kim:

The combination of beans and greens in the salad were unusually delicious.  The mushroom sandwhich had a bbq sauce that made me feel that eating vegan is not that boring and the dessert cookies were spectacular, in fact it is hard to beleive that they were vegan.  The almond milk horchata was not very good.  The combination of citrus with almond milk left the drink tasting like sour milk.  The atmosphere had a comfortable sophistication and simplicity.  I appreciated the menu options being environmentally and health concious including the drink menu.

The bathrooms were clean & accessible.  The place was overall spacious enough for a wheelchair to get through.  

Gather does justice to its name because it is a place where vegans, vegetarians, and omnivores can all "gather" and share a meal together.  There are enough options for all to enjoy!

My friend and I were walking around in between classes and noticed this place for the first time, which was weird because it's in a very visible location across from campus, so we decided to try it (however if you're a college student just killing time in between classes, you might want to do that somewhere else because this could be a little pricey). The interior was pretty and the atmosphere was comfy. I got the burrata salad and it was so yum. The pesto was yum, the artichokes were yum, the crispy onions were an unexpected yum. The yummiest part was the dry farmed tomatoes; I had been wanting to get some before they go out of season, so I was excited to see them on the menu. I added chicken to my salad, but I got a good three pieces because they ran out. It's all good though, the salad was still lovely.
Currently one of my favorite restaurants. Get the Vegan "charcuterie". That's a direct order, foodie soldier.

It was a beautiful day in the neighborhood when we dropped by for brunch. We were happy to see there was absolutely no wait and the host (super friendly) must have seen us eyeing the available table outside because in no time that's where she was leading us to be seated. 

A cold, refreshing carafe of sparkling water was placed on our table and the fact that they offered sparkling was a pleasant surprise. I opted to order an iced tea. I heard great things about the pancetta pizza so both C and I shared one along with an order of the local lettuce salad which includes strawberries and pistachios throughout the salad. The flavors of the pizza (including the pancetta which I picked out and gave to C but was still able to taste hints of it) including the cheese and caramelized Lindencroft greens was wonderful. Along with the egg and the chili oil and thyme each slice was bursting with flavor. I was trying to avoid eating the crust but I couldn't help it and polished that off too in no time. 

No doubt will I be back. I was able to check out their dinner menu online and while they have similar items offered on the brunch menu there are a few of the large plates I am very curious to try.

I came here for my friend's birthday yesterday, and I was pretty excited. I LOVED the ambience and the hip vibe. They had good service too.

But I think the food was a little too hyped up. I went in wanting to try the Vegan Charcuterie after reading all the yelp reviews on it, but it was a little disappointing. I mean it was good, but I don't know if I would ever get it again. Maybe it's just me...but it definitely had an interesting taste.

I shared the burger with my friend, and that was pretty good. I just don't know if it's worth 14 bucks.

Overall, it's a really cool place. But I don't think I would "crave" any of the items on their menu.

SOmetimes sustainability and professionalism do not go hand in hand.
I ate at Gather last night and found the two cozy in a corner, smiling through the veneer of a figs and shittake.
I went there once before and thought it was good.
Last night made me glad it was a local option.
I will go back here instead of trying the litany of new underwhelming ghetto gougers.... 
Very Good food. Very good service.
Thanks for that.

Brunch with mom was delightful at Gather.  Next time I'm parking directly across the street, coin meter parking is far and 1 hour max, well I guess I got to work off some of that pizza I consumed!

I LOVED the polenta pancakes, we ate slowly and there was still a crispy edge to the cake.  The peaches braised in sauvignon blanc was a nice touch and the whipped ricotta was decadent.  Enjoyed the pizza, but I probably would skip the housemade sausage next time, it's pork, but it tasted really gamey.  Too salty for my palate also. The crust was chewy and puffy at the ends, deliciously satisfying.  

Tea selection: Numi bagged tea.

Neat: the bench seating is a compilation of leather belts and the wall is decorated with pickling jars.  

Will definitely be back for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

do you suck on salt for fun? then you might like Gather!
the saltiest meal i've ever eaten and i've once dropped brine into my soup on accident

i love the concept, but it's salty. like gross salty.

If you like spending a lot and getting small portions, this place is for you. Why oh why are places like these so in demand? All those catchy terms like local, organic, farm egg (like that makes it worth $2), vegan, blah, blah, blah. My entree was so small and since it featured artichoke, I expected an artichoke, not some emaciated thistle. and for $21?!? 

However, the drinks at the bar were superb. $10, which is what a cocktail seems to go for these days because the ingredients are so special and they are mixed by specialists who will provide a history for the bitters they are using....whatever.

I love Gather so much I ate there TWO days in a row for LUNCH and BRUNCH!! On Friday I had the ricotta sandwich with radicchio, sun dried tomato spread, and caramelized onions. Great balance of flavors I have to say: sourness from the spread, mild, soft texture from the ricotta and sweetness from the onions (love them!). I then had their chocolate cookie for dessert... I ate that cookie in less than 30 seconds: moist, chocolatey (of course) with occasional salty bites. I really think the salt and sweet combination bakers are doing these days is so unusual but so right. 

The next day I went in for brunch and ordered their signature dish: pork belly sandwich with a baked egg inside. This sandwich is to die for: delicious. I usually don't finish sandwiches because they are so large but I ended up devouring the pork belly. The meat is so soft and juicy, the yolk of the egg seeps into the bread and meat. The pickled cabbage balances out the bitterness of the egg yolk. The photos I posted  don't quite do them justice so I definitely recommend going to brunch at Gather trying either one of them (pork belly!!). 

If you guys are looking for a new and adventurous drink, order the Kombucha soda! Tangy and bubbly.

The large restaurant has such a nice all-American atmosphere. It's a great place to take a casual date to a nice dinner. My friend and I didn't have reservations and we walked in at 7pm on a Friday and waited about half an hour. Not bad. We ordered a spinach salad with chicken liver and other such unique organic ingredients and it was very good and a good portion for 2. We also ordered the sausage pizza which took a long time to come out. I think we waited at least 20 minutes after we finished our salad which came out rather quickly. When the pizza finally came out, we devoured it. It's about four slices per person and the bottom crust of the pizza is as thin as paper. However the sausages and everything made it so tasty that you forget about the lack of filling crusts. I guess it does attract your palate more to the actual sausage part of the pizza, which is good. 

I would definitely come back to try their other dishes. I love how their menu is very organic and sustainable! The restaurant found a perfect home and customer base in Berkeley.

Stopped for a post-Rep drink and nosh - tried the verbena gimlet served on the rocks. Great flavor combination. My friend had one of the beers on tap and loved it.

We got the vegan charcuterie plate, thinking we'd order more. This is one great platter of tastes! The mushroom pate, the eggplant "brandade", the sauteed peppers, watermelon radish "carpaccio, the tomato and corn relish - this was an incredible feast of flavors. 

We promised ourselves to come back for more, but it's really a great amount of food to have as a booze sponge. The service was really great, too - nice all around. Check it out.

This is definitely a Berkeley place (a bit pretentious, no?), but I enjoyed the food. It's a nice place if you're looking to eat out and get a bit more fancy treatment. 

I shared the Kale salad (pretty yum), and got the burger for dinner. The sauteed onion tomato sauce mixture instead of ketchup was delicious. The bun looked like it was made on location and the burger was actually made scrumptiously pink. (I hate overcooked beef). I had a very frothy pisco sour and some tasty plum sorbet for dessert. All in all a good meal.

The waitstaff could have been more attentive though. Our table water was often taken away and then forgotten about. The dudes who worked as hosts seemed to have two very large sticks shoved up their behinds. I got the once-over and then a stony look. I prompted the, "How are you tonight" and "We'll be two tonight" convos. They sat us at the dining counter in the back (no reservations) but that was fun to watch the kitchen and the charcuterie plates be prepared.  

My friend is vegetarian and gluten free, and this menu lived up to her expectations. All of the food is local and fresh and you could definitely taste the difference.

I will probably return again. I want to try the pureed soup.

The food was not good, for all of the pretense and egotism.  They serve animals on the menu that should not be considered food, even by carnivores.  I have to say I had high hopes for Gather, but after following their menu for a while, I was sorely disappointed.

I was very impressed with this place.  It is literally a stone's throw from campus, but this is not your typical restaurant geared towards students.  No Fat Slice or Cereal Bars here.  This place is a foodie mecca.  

The experience starts when you walk in the door.  Even on a foggy day the inside was bright and airy, with reclaimed wood furniture and and a smiling hostess.  We made reservations and were seated right away.  Looking at the menu, I admit I was a little skeptical.  Anyplace that has "vegan appeal" is a place I typically like to avoid. Veges can be pretentious and fiercely fundamentalist - kind of like the hezbollah of foodies.  This is not one of those places.  This place defines not being able to judge a book by it's cover.

We started with the turkey and fig pizza for an appetizer.  It was actually an entree size, but we all wanted it, and getting it as an app was the easiest way.  From the first bite to the last it was incredible.  The texture and flavors were like tiny flavor explosions with each bite.  Honestly though, the best part was the crust.  It tasted kind of like Acme's batard baguette, but softer on the inside with a great crispy crust.  I can only imagine how amazing breadsticks would be if they made them out of this dough.  

I got the sandwich special.  Thin sliced roast boar with a horseradish mayo on cibatta.  It was very good, though the mayo overwhelmed the sandwich a little bit.  I asked for mustard and that was exactly what it needed.  The mustard itself was very good, tangy with fruity notes.  Next time I'd have them skip the mayo and replace it for mustard.

My friend and girlfriend got the salads.  Presentation was great, though I didn't taste their dishes.  

The piece de la resistance, however, was clearly the dessert.  We shared a parfait type thing, one of the specials, with pecan cakes layered with marscapone, three types of grapes and grape jam.   We also got the ginger frozen yogurt.  I swear each bite opened up a new dimension of flavor in my mouth.  The ginger yogurt was topped with diced nectarines.  The flavors were layered so well on top of each other, sweet and spicy, with the different textures....incredible.  

I would definitely go back here.  It is a great brunch place for sure, and I imagine it would be a great date place as well.  Service was super friendly and fast, which is always an added bonus.  This is a place you can take your veggie or vegan friends and still have a great meal without feeling like a rabbit.  It was a little pricey for three people, even with only one of us getting an alcoholic beverage, but to be fair we did get a lot of food.  This place lets you taste with your eyes as well as with your taste buds.

This place is amazing.  I miss it to pieces (forced relocation to SoCal).  I love the ginger beer, the salad, the burger, the pizza, the veggie charcuterie platter, the soup, the latte, the kombucha on tap...you get the picture.  Also, the perfect interior for the perfect mission plan.  Definitely my go to lunch spot in Berk.  There was this one time we had a not so nice server (she forgot to tell us the specials, get us water, and ask about dessert); however, the kindness of her sexy coworker kind of made up for it...  Can't wait to eat here when I go back up to visit!

A group of us headed over to Berkeley last Friday to meet with some clients and we all loved this place! 

Place: nicely decorated, not too stuffy or overly done. I liked that there was a lot of natural lighting - large windows to let the sun in. Near Bart station. Clean and open - tables aren't too cramped. 

Food: yum. We told the manager to select some food for us since it was a large group. So we had: Heirloom Apple Salad, Kale salad and one more that I can't remember... Cherry tomato pizza, Sausage pizza and a Mushroom/Corn pizza. All of them were amazingly good! I usually don't eat pizza crusts but I did on these ones. 

Dessert: they made us a special something.. raspberry or something berry cobblerish cake that came with caramel and whipped cream on the side. It was heavenly! 

Great place to go for lunch and I hear happy hour is pretty good too.

The manager is SUPER SWEET and she checked in with us a few times during the lunch to make sure everything was ok.

Ladies and Gentlemen! Come hither! Gather around here for an experience you'll never forget! $10 per person, satisfaction guaranteed!

I followed the crowd, and sure enough, a magnificent experience, worth every penny and all the hype.

The wooden tables/chairs, warm friendly smiles of hostess/waiters/cooks (who are all incredibly bright and glowing and good-looking--I blame it on the food they eat...it should be a law that all Americans should eat what their eating, then we wouldn't have so many people with low self-esteem and high obesity rates...) and relaxing but classy aura of the restaurant all make Gather my favorite restaurant in Berkeley.

Service was slow but incredibly nice and gentle. I probably think it's "slow" because everywhere else, I feel like I'm rushed out of the store after our plates are taken away. Our waiter gave us ample time after we ate to sit back, digest, and chit chat despite there being other people waiting to be seated.

I love how water was served in Straus creamery bottles. I came home, got ride of our plastic water containers and drank iced tea out of our single Straus bottle. I guess this is the beginning step to becoming green.

Do yourself a favor and look at the menu before you go in. I'm not sure how often they change it, but today's lunch menu was the same as the one online. It took us a good 15 minutes to order still. With 3 meat-lovers and 1 vegetarian, we had to compromise and go with the wild mushroom pizza, pulled pork sandwich, and mushroom sandwich. We ordered the pizza first and it came out almost immediately. We each devoured our 2 slices. The chanterelles were cooked to perfection. All four of us are determined to go mushroom hunting. The sandwiches were amazing--the cream made everything that much more exciting. The cauliflower and side veggies---out of this world. In the end, 3 meat-lovers and 1 vegetarian turned into 4 leaf/fungi/green plant-life lovers. It was the perfect amount of food too. I wasn't overstuffed but wasn't hungry. I forgot what eating proper serving sizes feels like. But now I know, and it feels great.

It all came out to $10 each, not including tip. It's much more affordable than I imagined. 

Can you gather alone? No you can't. So come along with at least 3 others. This is the perfect place for a small group gathering.

I will be back again for the huckleberry pie and the burger, which I heard is ____________. (I'll come back and make sure it lives up to my expectations! Don't want to jinx it!)

Particularly for Berkeley, this was an outstanding meal. The atmosphere is pleasant, each dish is seasoned incredibly well, and the variety of options for vegetarians (and carnivores) is astounding. Our vegan relatives could not believe they had so many choices and that all of their dishes were not only veggie friendly but delicious. It was a really wonderful surprise to have such an exemplary meal so close to home. We will definitely be returning.

Really cute place. Came here with party of 4 for a birthday celebration. They let us bring our own cake (charges a few bucks for cutting/storage) and helped us bring it out.

Food menu sounds delicious (but the food is really nouveau so if you're into trying new taste combinations)!

Really recommend for a cute night :)

As a pescetarian, I was excited coming to Berkeley and seeing all the vegetarian options available. After browsing on yelp, the reviews for Gather really caught my eye. The restaurant had a lovely atmosphere--very energetic and modern. The place was absolutely packed, but we lucked out and were able to get a table on the heated outside patio. We ended up ordering one of the special--a piece of medium-well albacore with clams in a light tomato sauce, the highly praised vegan charcuterie, and the crispy pork belly. The albacore was perfectly cooked and the flavors were very well-balanced.The charcuterie lived up to its reputation; it was absolutely delish, especially the mushroom pate (although it was slightly overseasoned for my taste). But its a MUST if you plan to dine here. Everything was super fresh and very light, so we definitely had room for dessert. The waitress recommended the royal grape trifle, so we ended up ordering one to share along with a scoop of strawberry ricotta ice  cream. The trifle was wonderful--creamy, rich, and delicious, probably one of the best desserts i've ever had.   The ricotta ice cream, however, fell a little short. It was under-sweetened and icy (although the presentation was lovely). My parents complained that they were still hungry, although they did enjoy the food. True, the fare is quite light, but personally, i don't like being bloated after a meal anyway. It was a little pricey for the small quantity of each dish, but that's the price of good produce! I would love to come back here and try the pizza! It's a must if you're a fan of high-quality, fresh food.

On a Saturday night, Gather was the hippest place to be.  Nevermind, this place is ALWAYS packed (lunch, dinner, weekdays).  And I've always wondered why...

The food here is pretty spectacular.  I'm a fan of the "buy local" movement, but typically it's hard to figure out what the heck to do with these odd local ingredients.  

The chefs at Gather do a FINE job creating familiar flavors out of unfamiliar ingredients.  To summarize, don't be afraid to try everything. 

I ordered the...Vegan "charcuterie" ($16):  a fun collection of small vegetable items & bruschetta as carbs.  Super fun to eat - a flavor party in my mouth! Order it to impress everyone at your table. 

Also tried the:
1. Hedgehog Mushroom Pizza ($18):  great to share and large portions!
2. Prather Ranch burger ($13): comes medium rare and super juicy.  A surprisingly exceptional burger!
3. Barbecued young chicken ($19.50) - fall-off-the-bone , succulent, and seasoned well.  I recommend!

I have plenty of good things to say about Gather.  Filling portions, lovely ambiance, and a food philosophy to live by.

"Un repas sans pain, c'est comme..." Well, it's like dinner at Gather. I enjoyed the lamb meatballs, but really could have used a piece of crusty bread to make it a meal. 

Our server was annoyingly enthusiastic in that way that seems so prevalent in American restaurants, but she forgot to bring my glass of Tempranillo. I had to ask the host to fetch it, minutes after the entrees were served.

This restaurant has great variety if you have to satisfy any of those eating-out checklists: omnivore, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, local/organic/sustainable...

I've been for a few delicious lunches. You feel like you're eating fresh, healthy food that is still sophisticated. The staff is very friendly and responsive.

A few standout dishes: white bean soup, ricotta sandwich,  pear-pancetta-arugula pizza, pumpkin cheesecake

Gather has set the bar VERY high, leading the edge in the continuing trend of sustainable cuisine.  Amazing and impressive in so many ways, hard to know where to start.

The food is incredible, so many flavors, such variety.  The Vegan Charcouterie is the one dish not to miss.  It's ~ 5 different very small portions of appetizers, so unique you won't quite know how to describe them.  Constantly changing, we've ordered this all 4 times we've been to Gather, and it's blown us away every time.
