It's astonishing the range of rich delectable flavors and textures they can concoct all while keeping  this dish completely vegan.  They should write an entire cookbook just on the Vegan Charcouterie.

And of course, everything on the menu is organic, locally-sourced, seasonal produce, meats and fish.  Each night, they list the exact farms that their ingredients are from.


Portions are small, but perfectly so.  We left full and very fully satisfied, and without any leftovers.   The service is excellent.  The wait staff has a lot of info to remember about every ingredient in every dish, and they do a remarkable job being ready to tell you even more than you might have wanted to know.

Even more impressively, the entire restaurant's construction and design features reclaimed, recycled, and refurbished materials.  Even the artwork on the walls is made from shredding the packaging that their refurbished chairs were delivered in.

My only complaint is that it's a tad upscale and hence expensive.  We paid ~$45 per person, including drinks/desserts.  Oh, did I mention their drinks and desserts are INCREDIBLE.  Potent ginger-somethings, and a so-smooth and perfectly sweet Pisco sour.  And the varied desserts were exploding with flavors, even the fruits seemed unusually tasty.

We loved our dinner at Gather. Every little item in the vegan charcuterie was delightful; but the carpaccio of watermelon radish, turnip, horseradish salsa verde, grapes and grated almond was my favorite. The horseradish salsa verde was genius! We also had the albacore small plate with Romano beans, potatoes, frying peppers, etc. Loved that too. And the little mountain of kale buried under fluffy Fiscalini cheese was just divine; the kale had a hint of vinegar and the roasted root veggies added a bit of sweetness, while the herbs and fried capers provided welcome bitter and salty notes, rounded out by pine nuts. The Thai-oriented green beans were fabulous, they tasted like they were bathed in homemade Sriracha and Thai basil. And the local lettuces were hanging out with some roasted nectarine, which was an original and delicious treatment. For dessert we had fantastic zucchini and fig cake, and three local cheeses. 

This is exactly the kind of food I like to eat; light, fresh, with layers and layers of bright flavors. Inventive but not forced, erudite but not pretentious. It all feels born out of a love of ingredients. This must be how Greens restaurant felt back when it was cutting edge: an a-ha moment about not just vegetarian, but all food.

Service was impeccable too: we were seated quickly at the dining counter where we got to ogle the cute kitchen staff working their magic. Our server was perfect, every time we thought we might need something he showed up as if by magic. He was very attentive and knowledgeable but not the tiniest bit overbearing. I wish I had asked his name!

One thing for prospective diners: if you are the kind of person  who can't look at a menu with the word "vegan" on it without launching into a verbal assault on all vegans because you know this one vegan who is really annoying and blah blah blah, you know what: I've also met a meat eater once who was really fucking annoying. I'm over it though, and I let people order food without making it their problem. Shut up. Grow up. Bye bye.

I am so happy. It's like they saw me coming. 

I have to start out by saying that when you want a burger, it doesn't really matter what else is on the menu. My partner and I were almost committed to going to Barney's, but without much enthusiasm. We spotted Gather on Yelp and it looked like a lot of foodie fun so we swung by. 

There was a small crowd at the door already and they  were just about to open. We managed to get seated right away. 

First big star: choice of filtered or sparkling water. Sparkling! And served at just below room temperature. Perfect!

Decor is simple, but high quality and contemporary. Noise level was excellent for such a busy place. Great for conversation. 

Burgers on the menu! That made it easier, as the rest of the offerings sounded incredible. 

Burger was a modest size, nicely pink inside, high quality cheese, bitter greens, bun was soft but with a delicate crust, absolutely perfect. The generously portioned shoestring fries were fresh cut and served with a sweet/smokey shallot tomato sauce. Delightful!

Because the burger wasn't monstrous, we had room for dessert. I was so glad! Barney's always leaves you stuffed. The dessert menu was a delight just to read. Our waitress, who was sincere and enthusiastic as can be, recommended the special - Mexican chocolate with donuts made to order, filled with heavenly concoctions of orange, caramel and chili. 

OMG. 

My partner ordered the Pinot chocolate mousse, which we were told is made from a reduction of a full bottle of wine. So dark and rich! And served with home made nutter butters. I'm glad he likes to share!

It was a stellar quality meal, a real treat. We will definitely be back. The new year's eve dinner is beckoning.

Here's the deal.  I've been to Gather twice.  The first time, for brunch, it blew me away, and I couldn't stop speaking about it for weeks.  I had a pizza, something simple - lemon zest, green garlic, asparagus - it was absolutely incredible.  My friend's food - the portabella sandwich, was unreal as well.  We also had a bread pudding dessert and were in la-la land afterwards.  I'm getting excited just thinking about it.  

Given the amazing experience I had my first time, I went back recently with my parents who were in town for my graduation.  I took them there at 11:30am, just as the restaurant opened.  I did not expect to encounter what we found - it was not table-service at this point.  Instead, we had to line up with the crowd of others who had been waiting at the door to order our food at the counter.  The line curved throughout the entire right-hand side of the restaurant; but we didn't realize this would happen, so we had put our things down and sat in that section.  Bad move.  Soon enough, patrons were squeezing in behind us and things got very uncomfortable.  So we moved.  The next problem was that the coffee we ordered was waiting for us at the counter.  So, we had to fight the crowd to get the coffee, then fight the crowd again to get to the cream (which was spoiled, by the way), then fight the crowd again to get back to the table.  It just really wasn't the dining experience we were hoping for.  By the time we were settled with our coffee it had been at least 20 minutes and we were all feeling agitated.  The coffee had gotten cold.  Someone on staff corrected it by bringing us hot coffee and she also corrected the spoiled cream issue, but she didn't bring it to the table.  Instead I had to fight the crowd again to go retrieve it from across the restaurant.

Luckily, everything had calmed down by the time the food came, and we were all able to enjoy our meals, but I will say the the pizza I had this time (sausage pie with an egg) was not nearly as good as the one I had the first time.  This pie seemed heavier - meaning, weighed down by too many toppings, as it got soggy and the crust wasn't very crispy.  My parents seemed to enjoy their food and so that was good.  But I suspect the mad rush may have had an averse affect on the quality of the food that was coming out.

So would I go back to Gather?  Of course, yes I would.  But I would definitely avoid it around opening, and I would NEVER go back unless there is table service.

As a vegetarian I thought the food was going to be excellent after reading the reviews. However, I was extremely disapointed. I had the deep fried squash blossoms, which were terrible and the squash blossom pizza which was burned. I think they burn the pizzas on purpose but I thought it tasted horrible. They give you a 1/2 glass of wine for 10 bucks and the glass is not even big. Total rip and I'm never going back.

Damn, I am on a roll with the fine dining recently (sorry bank account)

Everything about Gather is great.  

Its a beautiful space-- open kitchen, cool light fixtures, ivy growing everywhere-- you feel like you're in a garden, but you're not because you're in the Bay Area and it'd be f*cking freezing if you were actually eating outside at night.  

The cocktails are great-- very fancy-schmancy (read: they take 15 minutes to prepare)-- I especially like the Brown Derby.  

The kale salad pretty much redefined kale for me.  Like, whoa, it can taste like this?  I may spend the rest of my life trying to replicate that salad.  Burger was cooked beautifully, fries were awesome and whatever that ketchup-carmelized onion thing comes with that dish, can you bottle that, please?  I was close to dipping my elbow and eating it, it was that good.  Service was fine, not overly gushy nice but sufficient.  

Clearly, a great place to bring vegans/vegetarians where you can still get an amazing meat dish-- like I said, everything they do is great.

Our weekend morning conversations usually go something like this...

MY BOYFRIEND: "Hungry?"

ME: "Hells yes."

MY BOYFRIEND: "Gather?"

ME: "You don't gotta ask me twice."

I'm serious. It's literally that simple a choice for us. Not a cheap brunch but a damn good one. And they know it. I absolutely love everything about this place. I find it funny that I've been here a dozen times for brunch but never for dinner. I think I'm subconsciously afraid that I might enjoy my dinner at Gather a little too much and our evening conversations will soon start to sound like our morning ones. 

One item we always always order is the is Spicy Pizza with capers, herbs, and cashew garlic puree. I didn't know it was possible to look like such a hog eating a vegan pizza. You're almost guaranteed a wet underwear. The Prather Ranch Burger is unreal with it's shallot-tomato sauce (their version of ketchup). The ambiance is so calm, relaxing, and inviting that it's no surprise the servers always seem so happy.

Everyone I've recommended Gather to has given it thumbs up, so try this place and if you don't like it you can bust my balls all you want. I'll be watching and waiting in the corner like a creeper ready to lick your grubby fingers.

pizza: HELL YEAH
vegan charcuterie: EH gimmicky.

Okay, what's with the four star review? I don't think I've ever repeated the sentence "This is the best ______ I've ever had" as much as I did during my amazing dinner tonight.

If you're vegetarian/vegan who's running out of ideas, you should really take a look at Gather's menu to get inspired. This place pulls off a tough feat--it makes eating your vegetables cool. It really got me interested in making my own versions of their plates at home. 

We split the Little Gems salad and the Spicy Tomato pizza. I don't think I've ever eaten a salad so ravenously. The Pt. Reyes blue cheese dressing was incredibly flavorful without being overpowering. It  complemented the bitterness of the radishes and the endives perfectly. I wanted to take a bath in the tomato sauce on the pizza. The crust manages to be soft, fluffy, crunchy, and thin all at once. I'm fairly sure that defies some rule of non-magical baking. 

We finished off this impeccable feast with the BEST chai latte in existence. The foam was smooth and the spices were combined phenomenally. Each sip was fully balanced with sweet and spicy notes. BEST, BEST, BEST.

The decor is worth mentioning, too. The soft lighting and the hanging ivy made me feel like I was walking into a rainforest. No manatee-patterned seats or robotic alligators here, though. It's "nice" without being too fancy. 

I'll be back to try their drinks and the vegan charcuterie plate next time.

Went here with some friends for dinner last week and we almost ordered everything on the menu except for the pizza and burgers.  There's something for everyone on the menu.  Great seBrlections as well.   Started of with a cheese plate. It was okay.  I was expecting a little more for the price we were paying.   We ordered all the sides, which were the fries, greens and the creamy polenta.  They were all decent.  Each of us ordered an entree and we decided to all share everything and eat family style.  I ordered the chicken under a brick, Kristi ordered the heirloom bean ragout, my other friends ordered the braised pork cheek over polenta and the swordfish with pistachio pesto.  Everything was great and tasty.  The chicken was very flavorful.  Afterwards we tried a bunch of desserts.  The chai crem brulee and the bacon apple tart, and a streusel with earl grey currants.  I looked around and everyone was ordering the hamburgers, which is what I'll try next time.   I got a kick out of the bathroom with all the far side comics posted on the wall.   Neat place.

Everything was super unique and tasty and flavorful. The vegan charcuterie was fantastic! Culinarily, Gather was a really fun and interesting experience from start to finish. I also enjoyed the service, and the general ambiance and atmosphere of the place -- relaxed, pleasant energy.

Now I understand why this place is so popular. It's well-deserved. Reservations are a good idea. I came here, without a reservation, with a party of 3 on a Friday just before 6pm (which I would say is relatively early), and we still had to wait half an hour.

Food Porn...
The overarching theme was food frustration. Enough of a taste that you want more but then it's gone because the portions are SO small. The few bites we each had for $100 for four people were tasty though. But for a $20 squash entree, I want to be pretty darn full...Why? Cuz I buy squash myself and I'm no ninny. I know I can get the best local summer squash for $3 a POUND. So when you serve me a quarter pound of it for $20, I feel insulted. Doesn't help matters that I'm Scottish. You hit me in the pride, man.
Otherwise, the selection is not great and we got the feeling the waiter was very eager to turn over the table. Not so leisurely.
We went home and ate snacks and a second dessert afterwards.
In a ditch effort for satisfaction, get pizza.
If you like to avoid being snuckered, go to Millenium in downtown San Francisco instead.

Gather is what Berkeley is all about. Fresh, local, organic ingredients for a reasonable price (at lunch, at least). We ordered a pizza and the kale salad (not too sour!), and had a couple glasses of the free fizzy water on tap.

Not everything I've eaten at Gather has been amazing, but it has been good and interesting. And you're not paying the kind of prices where you expect perfection. Portions are filling, and definitely healthy. You feel great after eating at Gather. Everything is sourced locally and sustainably to boot.

This is my favorite Berkeley restaurant -the place I take out-of-town visitors.

I came to Gather on a blind date a couple months ago. I thought the food was pretty good. Yes, you get a lot of market-fresh, environmentally conscious stuff on the menu. And yeah, the restaurant is pretty fancy. It's right on the corner, so if you come here for dinner,  you almost feel like you're in a dark greenhouse. I wonder if that factored into the design. It's a little cramped in there, but not overly so, and the waiters and stuff were pretty friendly.

We split a pizza. After having been to a couple of places that serve pizza on the menu...I'm kinda wondering why they do. I mean, it was good, but it certainly wasn't the star of the meal. I think the true secret to any good pizza is all in the dough. Sure the toppings were pretty good, but the dough was a little meh, a little too, well, doughy. Uninspired. Not enough char, not enough crunch. A bit too soft.

I do remember the vegan charcuterie as being of interest. It was cute collection of veggies and things, good for a date since it's all begging to be shared, but felt more like a curiosity or "something to try" versus something I'd want to go back for over and over again. 

If I ever do come back, I'd definitely want to give one of the large plates a go. But the next time I'll be back is really anybody's guess.

One of the best restaurants I've been to in awhile.  Gather was a wonder flip compared to most other restaurants.  Rather than focusing on mainly meats and offering a few vegetarian/vegan options, there were MANY vegan options and a few meat options still.   I'm not a hardcore vegan by any sense but I do appreciate all the options they provide here. 

I wanted to try everything on the menu so we ordered a lot.   We got the vegan charcuterie, kale "ceasar", burger, and pizza special.  Every item was delicious but the vegan charcuterie plate was #1 on my list.  The creative play in real thing was so interesting I wouldn't have minded eating the whole board to myself.  We were so full we didn't get to try any desserts but they looked great as well.

The cocktails were very tasty as well.  Both of ours were well made and did a great job to prime our appetite.  

The prices at Gather were very reasonable as well.  I think everything on the menu was under $20 so that was nice to see. I can't wait to head back and try other things.

Gather is an elegant restaurant across the street from the UC Berkeley campus that is committed to the local, organic, sustainable food movement. The menu offers to show you a Source Book so you can verify that your chicken is pasture-raised, your beef is grass fed, and your farmer is Joel Salatin. On the wall, they praise Michael Pollan's "In Defense of Food" as a must-read book.

Our party started with the vegan "charcuterie", a smorgasbord of beets, carrots, other greens, and grilled bread. My favorite part was the "cashew ricotta," which really did taste like its namesake.

For the entree, I had the "Young chicken under a brick." The drumsticks and body come topped with radishes. The chicken covers plenty of kamut doused in a fried onion vinaigrette. The juiciness of the protein made me want to force everyone to pasture raise their chicken. Furthermore, compared to other restaurants in this genre, e.g. Calafia Cafe in Palo Alto, I thought the portion size was very generous.

At this point of the meal, I was considering giving Gather five stars. Unfortunately, dessert came up a tad short. I had the vegan chocolate layer cake, which is served with a tiny scoop of ice cream on the side. The ice cream was crucial in preventing the cake from drying up my mouth. I also was able to sample the tequila lime sorbet, which had an odd texture. The best dessert I sampled was the grapefruit sorbet, which had a very nice, light taste to it.

Since Gather is committed to serving seasonal dishes, note that your experience could be vastly different from mine. The sample menus on the web site did not match what was served today. Gather was a wonderful food experience, and I'd definitely come here again.

I was fortunate enough to be invited to the opening night celebration at 'Gather'. In one word, unbelievable. The decor, the food, the people, everything is great. The highlight of my meal was the mashed potatoes, best i've ever eaten!

I was really not impressed with this place.  Went for breakfast and ordered the breakfast sandwich w/ bacon and it was $11.  After tax and tip it was $15 and the thing was 1) not that good at all 2) fairly small and came with NO side orders.  No potatoes, no salad, nothing 3) expensive and I left hungry.

The location is nice, and the restaurant is clean with a chic design.  The size of the portions and the pricing for breakfast were rediculous in my opinion.  The person I went with ordered the poached eggs and that dish was tiny too and over priced.
Fabulous restaurant.  Menu choices are always creative, intriguing, and delicious.  The artisanal vegan charcuterie plate is a must.

I feel bad giving Gather a three star rating. The food is very very good--I had the sausage pizza and my friend had the burger (yeah yeah, we go to an upscale place and still eat normal food) but the menu is incredibly short.
The cocktails are tiny. My friend ordered one and it was the size of two gulps. He sipped it to be refined but I knew what he was thinking: "mannn...I could probably drink a hundred of these in a minute. literally."

Also, earlier in the month, I wanted to have a large celebration here so I called several days ahead to make a reservation.
THEY DO NOT TAKE RESERVATIONS FOR PARTIES OVER EIGHT.
I exceeded that limit but they didn't call me back to tell me so. I eventually had to go over to the place two days before my party to talk to them about it, at which time the waitress told me the rule. I'm kind of confused as to why they didn't call me back to answer my message--I asked but she said I probably hadn't left my number, but I did--twice, clearly.

All in all Gather's got good food, a little pricey, and it's definitely worth the hour wait for a casual dinner. But for something planned with a lot of people...don't waste your time trying.

The vegan charcuterie.

My gawd, the vegan charcuterie. It was incredible. Not "incredible for vegan food," not "incredible but hey i never eat meat." Just incredible. Complex, generous, unforgettable.

I don't remember what else we had. But have I told you about the vegan charcuterie? 

No pressure, Gather, but you set the bar pretty high with that dish on my first visit...hope it stays that way!

good dinner option for meat eaters and vegetarians alike.  we came here for my dad's bday, and ordered a bunch of stuff to share.

we got the veg charcuterie platter, kale caesar, the young chicken and carrot entrees, and a special pizza of the day, which had pork belly, corn, jalapenos, and basil.  we asked them to put pork belly on one side only and had it veg on the other side.

everything was delicious, and the charcuterie platter was particularly inventive and beautiful.  the pizza was really good, and i loved the thin crust.

for dessert, we got a berry crisp w/ ice cream and an orange/fennel sorbet.  

a choice of complimentary sparkling water is a nice touch.

When my omnivorous sweetheart and I popped in for an early Sunday brunch, our hostess asked us if we'd been before - when we said we hadn't, she replied, "You're really going to enjoy this!" Such enthusiasm is super great, especially when not paired with a detailed lecture about why, exactly, we should. And she was right! We really did enjoy it.

The decor is phenomenal, a modern rustic wonderland with recycled wine bottle lighting and reclaimed wood. It's open and gorgeous. I would happily live there, if it was, you know, housing - and not so close to campus.

They make sure their menu is 50% vegetarian at all times, which is so, so  exciting to me. There are multiple vegan options, and the vegetarian options look easily veganizable! My omnivorous sweetheart is a beacon of fairness and won't even take me anywhere where I have one single option anymore, unless I am specifically in the mood for that one single thing.

I got an almond latte - fantastic that they offer almond milk in addition to soy milk - and the "Benedict" which was savory and satisfying.  The lentils were perfectly cooked, the spinach beautifully wilted. The flavors were rich in umami, which makes me sound like a snobby foodie but it was so tasty I don't care.

My sweetheart got the egg sandwich with bacon, and found it to be incredibly fresh, have the right proportion of arugula, a not-too-salty bacon and a perfectly cooked egg. The word "perfect" came up repeatedly!

I love that they are committed to local, safe, just and "beyond organic" food. They have a Source Book for their ingredients but I was too shy to ask for it on my first visit. Perhaps next time!

The only thing I didn't love about Gather was the price (minus 1 star).  This was honestly the best vegan food I have EVER had.  Will definitely go back.  As always, eat at the bar if you don't want to wait.

i took my wife to gather for our 83rd monthversary.  we went during lunch.  we brought our 5.5.month old son.  he loved how the restaurant was so bright with all the big windows and view of the busy berkeley street, right across the street from the campus.  i really liked gather, and it made me miss living in berkeley.  i wish they had a location in the south bay.

my wife ordered the kale salad with chicken, and i ordered the spicy young chicken.  both were _so_ good!  the spicy young chicken had such a nicely, browned, crispy skin.  it was well plated with dandelion greens and polenta.  the kale in the kale salad was more tender than kale i usually get.  the pine nutes and shredded cheese went very well with it.  i also ordered a glass of kombucha.  i wish i could get a big gulp of that stuff.  we also had a peach bread pudding dessert and decaf coffee.  all the food was great.

the service was also very attentive and polite.  they made it very easy to bring our baby to the dining table and enjoy our lunch as part of a totally fun day in berkeley.  i don't give out 5.star yelps to restaurants that often, but i'm totally giving gather all 5 stars.

This is very refreshing spot in the heart of downtown Berkeley. 
The food is organic and vegan by request. 
They have really cute names to title their food like "Little Gems" for salad and  " Farm Egg" for the pizza. 
The only reason why I don't give them 5 stars is because the wait time to deliver the food to your table needs improving. You cant really go there on your lunch break because you will be there for at least 1 1/2 hours.Other than that the food is delicious and worth it

We had a reservation so we walked right in past several groups waiting for tables and were seated immediately. I could not have been happier about the service. Our waitress was very familiar with the menu and answered all of our questions as we had never been here before.

We had a yellowtail crudo and roasted peppers as appitizers. The crudo was excellent but my wife and I split on the peppers. I loved how they were tart and charred and occasionally very spicy. She did not care for them as much but it worked out well as I got extra peppers!

We then tried the vegan charcuterie. This was the first time I ever ordered anything with the word "vegan" off a menu and thought there was a strong likelyhood of hitting In-and-Out on the way home. I was completely blown away with the excellent preparation of the vegetables and the sauces that accompanied them. My only complaint was that there were only four pieces of bread provided to finish off the sauces. I tried to use the "lick the finger" technique to finish off the last remnants of flavor from the plate but my wife put a stop without hesitation.

We will go back.

I've tried this place twice (lunch and dinner) and both times were consistently good.  I love their vegan charcuterie and pizzas, but their sandwiches are great too.  Though I'm not a vegan or vegetarian I appreciate the way they create complex flavors out of simple ingredients.  By the way, they do serve meat entrees/sandwiches as well.  I just have a hard time passing up their pizza.

Oh a whim, my friend Tory L. and I decided to come here for our monthly dinner. We always need a place to catch up at, and why not go somewhere both of us have yet to yelp at. 

We arrived at around 6pm and was informed that the dining room was full, but they had a private table in the bar area, which we were both fine with. Because we were sitting so far from the regular dining room, we had problems with service. We waited for about 20 minutes to get our water jar refilled and order our desserts. Other than that, service was pretty good. Perhaps since we arrived a bit earlier for dinner, it wasn't too bad in the dining room, but by the time we left, the dining room was full. 

We had each ordered an entree and shared a dessert.
I ordered the Barbecued Young Chicken on the suggestion of my friend Tiffany N who has been to Gather before. It was delicious. It just had me eating the entire time; I couldn't stop. The chicken was so moist and presentation was amazing. I did have some red spots in the my chicken next to the bones which I was a bit worried about. I brought it up with my server, but he said it was just something to do with the bone. Regardless, the chicken was delicious. 
Tory L. ordered the Marinated Tomales Bay Mussels Pizza. It was a bit burnt on the crust that was a bit awkward, but that was beautifully presented on a wooden cutting board and it was gorgeous. The bacon and mussels somehow went great together. Then again, bacon goes with EVERYTHING. The pizza was great as well. 
Together, we had the Scarlett Royal Grape Trifle. It was actually really delicious. Normally, I don't like grapes in my dessert, but it was really good. They had both red and green grapes sliced quite thinly. The cake portion was kind of on the dry side, but the whipped cream was delicious. The pine nut brittle was quite salty, but I found it a great contrast to everything sweet in the dessert. 

Overall, I would totally go back with a date or my best friend and just enjoy the food. They have some great sustainable and organic foods that is amazing. I love to support local businesses in any way that I can. I would suggest to make reservations through their website a couple days ahead of time or you can try your luck walking in. Delicious food, decent service, and gorgeous decor will mean that I'll come back and try something else.

Delightful.
Everything was fresh, delicious, and affordable.
I headed in for a birthday lunch yesterday and was incredibly pleased. We loved the pizza with the two fried eggs on top and we adored our salads and fresh organic sodas.
Nice big open space. Tastefully decorated. Delicious options for meat eaters like me and vegetarians like some of my pals. A place everyone can dig on.
Not much else to say...nice decorations, great food, friendly staff. Definitely check it out if you haven't.

I am such a sucker for local, organic, sustainably-sourced restaurants.  I have found a few that have lived up to my expectations - but this one fell far short.  Made a visit to Berkeley to visit an old friend, brought along a SF buddy.  When the subject of lunch rolled around, I had my heart set on trying Gather (a decision I now regret and feel guilty about, which led me to pay for lunch).

SERVICE: One gold star for the water boy.  He repeatedly brought us fresh, sparkling water - my glass was never dry.   He even brought some fresh lemon slices at my friend's request.  That was the highlight of the experience.  

Moving on, the old friend I picked up looked less than yuppified - but this is Berkeley, come on.  They stuck us in a shitty corner so as if to shield the older, wealthier patrons from his tattoos and plugs.  My other friend Kristen is of the type who "does not get sat in the corner," so she was already a little pissed.  

I ordered a $12 glass of chardonnay, I got a 1/4 of a glass of semi-decent chardonnay.  No one ever asked if I would like another after it was consumed in two sips.

Our server was competent, but never returned to ask if everything was okay (which it was not...see below).

FOOD: Everything on the menu sounded delicious, we couldn't decide.  Kristen and I decided to split the crispy chickpea sandwich and stone-fruit salad - with a side of "grilled chicken" ($3+).  The salad was fine, but nothing I couldn't make at home for a fraction of the price - plus the stone-fruit was still stone-hard and not ripe.  

The chickpea sandwich was not crispy, and I've had better veggie patties out of the freezer.  I took only a small bite and left it to Kristen.  The real kicker was the INEDIBLE pile of "CHICKEN," which was slapped on a separate side plate.  It was far from grilled, and tasted about 5 days old.  It had the consistency of the foster-farms pre-cooked packaged chicken you buy in a bad in the refrigerated section of Lucky's (except this one was all brown meat and cartilage).  I was trying to be nice, I sometimes have a penchant for being over-picky, but this time my dining guests were disgusted enough for me.  

If you're going to advertise an add-on "grilled chicken" on the menu, you had better make it edible.  The server cleared our plates, including the uneaten carcass swiftly and left the $45 BILL!  A small salad, a measly vegetarian sandwich, a sip of wine, and an inedible pile of old dead poultry.  Disappointing to say the least, I tipped like a decent human being - hoping the water boy would receive a bulk of the tip (it helped me sleep better).  

Knocked this one off the list of local, organic - and sustainably unpleasant experiences I hope I never have to repeat.  

Cudos on the decor - could have been a pleasant environment for a nice lunch.

Overrated. Went here on a Thursday night and it was packed. Despite having reservations, I had to wait 15 minutes for a table which was a bit annoying. Anyways, between my friend and I, we ordered a Mindful Meat pizza, a burger, and the half chicken. One thing to point out here, is that this place is super big on vegan and gluten free, and also, there menu is very, very limited. 4 pizzas to choose from + 4 different entrees options.

The pizza was very cheesey, lots of arugula, very little meat. $19. I've had better cheaper pizza at cheeseboard. 

The burger was small, and not seasoned well. The bread they used however was excellent. This and medium rare, was indeed medium rare. The fries are bad. Definitely on the overcooked. Fries off the dollar menu at McDonalds are better in my opinion. $14. 

Half chicken. Seemed more like 1/8 of a chicken. Really small portion, and not very flavorful. Definitely did not justify the price. $23

I wouldn't go on to recommend Gather for the cost, the quality, and the atmosphere (much too loud - seems like a grand Applebees more than anything).

For $71 after tax and tip, there are much better eats.

Can Gather open up another location in the south bay, please?  I just love how they use fresh ingredients from local farms.

Initially I was looking at the host weird when he brought us to a table for two when we have a 5.5 month old in the carseat.  I think he wasn't too sure how to handle an infant guest.  When that was resolved, I had a great time here.

I ordered the kale salad with grilled chicken, which rocked!  I didn't realize how good kale can be.  The dressing was more like marinade for the steamed kale.  The kale was tender!  The thinly grated cheese was the perfect compliment on the salad.  The salad also had these yellow roots, which I forgot to ask for the name.  The roots were SO tasty - mildly sweet almost like taro.

My husand had the spicy young chicken with verde polenta, which kicked @$$.  The skin was crispy with meat that was well marinated and seasoned.

The kombucha tasted fresh, light, and floral without being too alcoholic.  If I wasn't breastfeeding, I think I could've drank 2 glasses of this elixir!

The peach bread pudding was warm and comforting with a glass of fresh decaf coffee.  Yum!

I really liked the service.  Our server was polite and attentive.  I would definitely like to return again and try dinner perhaps.

On Sat nite we went here for a cool dinner. Didnt have much of a wait to get our table or our choice of sparkling or still water. BUT it took for ever for our food to come. Im not a 12 year old kid but I started playing with that pizza stand thing. I thought the pizza was a little small for the price but it was tasty and filling. I would come back here again. Id just expect a wait. 
Wait one more thing.. I think if the waiter dosent come with the check within 5 min after you tell him your finished your meal should be free Im just saying.

Pros:
This place is awesome.  This is the future of restaurants everywhere (hopefully), or at least in California: healthy (reflecting the latest research on health, not just an old vision of "iceberg lettuce and old tomato salad is healthy"), very tasty, delicious vegan options that are not just deep fried, and great/hip ambiance.  

***The vegan "charcuterie" plate is the standout, must have dish on the menu.  The kale salad (recommended to me by yelp) was also pretty good, and the honey pine nut pie with ice cream dessert was great.

Cons:
Pizza was underwhelming; the first pizza on the menu (tomato) had this creamy sauce all over that really killed the flavor.  Pizza especially has a high bar since it was one of the least healthy things on the menu, so I would expect super-tasty.  They would probably do better just to not have it on the menu at all as a distraction from all the other wonderful items we could have ordered.

Fun:
Here is the definition of charcuterie for your reading pleasure; I am much more happy with Gather's vegan take on the dish:

"Charcuterie (pronounced /rkutri/, /rkutri/; French: [akyti], from chair 'flesh' and cuit 'cooked') is the branch of cooking devoted to prepared meat products such as bacon, ham, sausage, terrines, galantines, pâtés, and confit, primarily from pork.[1] Charcuterie is part of the garde manger chef's repertoire. Originally intended as a way to preserve meats before the advent of refrigeration, they are prepared today for their flavors derived from the preservation processes.

I adore this restaurant. They have amazing food and even more amazing cocktails, and a wide selection of vegan appetizers, entrées and desserts. But more important than that, Gather stands for so many of the things I believe in: sustainability, compassionate food practices, the local food movement. They are doing so much good for the environment, and the food industry as a whole. I am continually impressed by their menu, their employees, and their overall attitude. I feel so lucky that this place is close to where I live! The menu is obviously seasonally influenced, so these dishes may no longer be available, but I particularly enjoyed the smoky borlotti beans starter, the vegetable pizza with cashew cream, and the masala infused cocktail. This restaurant is perfect for special occasions, as well as casual lunches or brunches, so go here as soon as possible You don't want to miss this place!

Plus:
Patio!
Greenery hanging from the ceiling.
Option of still or sparkling.
House-made sodas.
Locally sourced, super seasonal.
Brunch cocktails. I'm a sucker for places that dish it up before noon.

The Update:
Service was on the ball this go 'round.
Lemon-lime soda was refreshing and not overly sweet or tart.
Burger was solid throughout. Fries were improved, but no longer curly. Not sure the chutney works, but the effort is appreciated.
Cherry gazpacho (umeboshi plum, shiso, olive oil) - Impressive. Mature, balanced flavor combination and a gorgeous dish overall.
Egg, chard and corn scramble. Solid portion, lacked zing. Potato wedges beneath lacked character.

Verdict:
Fresh, locally sourced approach is good enough to lure me in, but will not be enough to keep me coming back.
$12 for the gazpacho seemed outright offensive. Upon seeing and tasting it, I took that thought back, but you have to make that decision to order a twelve dollar bowl of gazpacho first and it's a tough call.
Menu options for vegan, vegetarian and/or gluten-free folks makes ordering easy.
Brunch dishes are filling, but leave something to be desired.
Understanding the whole local/sustainable sourcing, I get what drives some of the cost, but $5 for a side of potatoes and some other menu items seemed outrageous to me. *shrug*

*Note* Online menu is CLOSE, but not exactly what they're serving. Additionally, expect the costs to be a smidge higher than the online menu as well.

I came here for my birthday dinner with my friend, and I was pretty disappointed. The atmosphere and service is nice, but I wasn't satisfied with my meal.

We asked the waiter what the most popular menu items were, and he said that the top two were the Vegan Charcuterie and the burger. We ordered both, and I expected both of them to be pretty good because I had heard nice reviews about the place. The Vegan Charcuterie was nothing like what I have had before. It was so out of the ordinary, and each of the four separate sections had such weird tastes that my friend and I couldn't even force ourselves to finish it. In my opinion, it was not worth the money--especially because of its super unique taste and small portion. The burger on the other hand was great. It was juicy, and the meat was gooooood! The fries that came on the side were too well done, so we weren't able to finish it. Btw, for the fries, you get some other sauce--not ketchup. I personally wouldn't get it again because I don't want to pay $14 for a burger.

Both tables next to us ordered the pizza, and it looked pretty good. If I ever decide to give this place another try, I will order a pizza. If the pizza isn't amazing, I probably wouldn't come back to this place unless someone begged me and offered to treat me out.

I think I'd be better off hunting.  I would give this place maybe 4 - 5 stars for concept, and maybe 2 for execution.  There was not a single part of my dining experience here which was NOT flawed.  While they make a good pitch to the Vegan and localvoire communities and feature fresh Kombucha on tap, their menu has many items which any self-respecting chef could make vegan which are NOT,  Seriously guys easy on the eggs.  When we had a very runny polenta type chowder they gave us FORKS!  We begged, waved and pleaded but no waiter was in sight to ask us if everything was allright.  I finally got up went to another table and stole their silverware.   Not cool.  With desert they were no better, giving us SPOONS for a LEATHERY vegan cupcake.  Furthermore they took an eternity to brink us a very CHALKY soy milk (seriously guys spend the extra 20 cents per bottle on the smooth stuff).  So so far we have really slow service.  Silverware-impaired staff and poor beverage selection, and while all of these are issues, there was still some redeeming quality to the food, so why 1 stars?
If you want to know what really cheesed me off, it's  pulling the # 1 foul in my restaurant book and taking it to a new level: We ordered our salad with extra cheese and paid extra for extra cheese.  When our salad arrived there was less than a thimbleful of cheese.  It is this failure to provide a satisfactory topping while charging substantially extra for said topping which moves them into their own category for SKIMPING ON THE SAUCE.

3-3.5 (ish) stars.  Not bad, but not quite 4 stars worthy.    I'm not particularly into health food, but I am very open to trying different types of menus, including vegan and vegetarian options.  Gather executes most of their dishes well, but for the price point and portion size, I didn't really love my meal enough to want to come back.

I recommend making a reservation, even for early weeknights as this place is quite popular.  Our server was nice, friendly, and helpful, though we did have to wait a bit to get our food.  Atmosphere is casual and fits in with most other restaurants on the Berkeley food scene.

We ordered the padrones, yuba "pappardelle" with smoked okara "bolognese", and the pancetta pizza.  I also got one of their specialty cocktails - don't think it's on the menu anymore, but it was fine.  Our favorite dish was probably the pappardelle - very creative use of ingredients and well-executed.  The padrones were also interesting - good, though I might want to try another appetizer next time.  I was looking forward to eating the pancetta pizza and it tasted good for the most part (how can you really go wrong with pancetta & egg on a pizza?), but the crust was burnt black.  We were starving, so we just dealt with it and didn't complain; however, I don't know why a chef would allow burnt pizza to even leave the kitchen...

Portions are not very large, so you'd have to spend quite a bit of money to really get full (I'd recommend getting a pizza if you're particularly hungry).  Overall, I enjoyed my meal well enough, but I simply wasn't wowed - especially given the price point.  Vegans, vegetarians, and health fanatics may enjoy Gather more, though I still don't think it's one of the best restaurants in this class.

Ask for the bread because it is delicious and so well-baked. Weird that the servers won't give you any unless you specifically mention it, though. Come to think of it, they kind of shoved my sister and I into a corner (when the restaurant was barely populated) and forgot about us until we flagged them down for water refills.

I had the porchetta sandwich, which tasted great but dripped a little too much grease for my taste. The oil would drop down my hands and collect into a little pool on my plate. Eek.

I thought Gather was a vegetarian/vegan restaraunt. Here's a tip: it's not! 

They have many dishes that are vegan/vegetarian and also gluten free, but they also have some very bizarre meat dishes. When I went one of the specials was a pigs head and the other was cow tongue. I was not expecting that. I was more than a wee bit intimidated by the menu, and the people I was with and I had to look up the majority of the ingredients listed. However, once we got our food, we didn't care what was in it because it was so good.

I got the baby artichokes and the other two I was with split a pizza and salad. The flavor was like nothing I've ever had, and I found myself moaning in pleasure with every bite. 

On another note, I tried to come here on a Tuesday night one week and without a reservation it would have been a 45 minute wait for 3 people at about 7:30. So, when I went to next week, same time, same number of people, we made a reservation. It turned out to not be too busy but I'm glad we were prepared anyway. Service was awesome.

The only reason I'm giving them 4 stars, instead of 5, is the menu. It was just really intimidating. I consider myself a risk taker and I like to try new things, but I prefer to have a general idea of what I'm ordering, and when I've never heard of 90% of the ingredients, I feel a little stupid and get a little scared.

I like the farm fresh hunter-gatherer theme, but the food just doesn't quite cut it.  We ate here before a football game, and maybe it's because we were in the football frame of mind, but the food is just too weird and over the top (and pricey).  Want some lentils with your polenta?  Pureed cashews on your pizza?  Broccoli rabe on your eggs?  Fennel pollen butter on your pancakes (what the heck is fennel pollen butter anyway?  And fennel + pancakes???)  True story.  It's all there.  You can't make up this stuff.  Well, I guess you can if you are Gather.

I had a lot of difficulty getting excited about any of the vegetarian options, so I ordered the bartlett pear pizza without the pancetta.  (I forgot to mention the pears on the pizza, but then that was mainstream compared to the rest of the menu).  I took one bite - and yuck - pancetta.  I thought maybe I could just pick it out, but it was loaded all over in the melted cheese.  The server took it back very apologetically and brought out another pizza sans pancetta by the time my dining companions were finishing up their food.  The pizza sans pancetta was just plain bland.  (Memo to file - Don't ask Gather change their meat dishes to vegetarian.)

Too bad it didn't work out for us.  The location is good, but we'll probably take a pass next time we're in the neighborhood.

It's a shame that, while Gather makes an attempt at making some decent vegan food, they are so filled with unearned self-importance that they end up treating customers who do not dress like filthy criminals (i.e. collegiate yup/academic filth) as second class citizens.

And that's FUCKING UNACCEPTABLE - do you hear me Gather?

I eat at Millennium several times every month and they manage to treat us with kindness and dignity each and every time. Is that really so fucking hard for you Gather?

We are polite people. We say 'please.' We say 'thank you.' When a waiter asks how we are, we ask how they are. Is it so fucking hard for you to be polite Gather? IT"S BASIC.

As other yelpers have reported, when we arrived *most* of the tables were empty and yet we were told we had to wait because we didn't have a reservation. No one came in, no one left...after 15 minutes we were seated at a table that had been empty all along.

Three parties arrived after us. All of them received their food before we were offered bread and water. 

We ordered, repeating our order twice because the waiter was too distracted. We made it abundantly clear that we're vegans.

About 10 minutes later we get some bread - with butter. Wow, way to be attentive to your customers Gather. "Oh right, you're vegan [sneer]..." Ask for olive oil, never get it. 

Two of the three parties that came in after us have finished their meals AND LEFT  when our food finally shows up.

And, surprise surprise, it isn't what we ordered. They bring us dishes full of meat and cheese, so we can't even just accept the mistake and just eat it.

The ONLY time the service was attentive AT ALL was when I finally asked that the remaining order be canceled and that we be brought our check. 30 seconds later we had our check.

Gather you could have saved us a great deal of time and frustration by simply explaining from the beginning - perhaps with a sign in your window or something - that anyone that doesn't fit your image of an "appropriate" diner will be treated horribly in order to assure that they will not return.

You can tell this restaurant has been built solely on marketing concepts ("vegan," "gluten-free," "local," "sustainable") and has absolutely no heart - the kind of thing you find when a restaurants owner's are actually interested in FOOD. Making money is awesome, but when you are a bunch of fake-ass scumbags, some of us are going to point it out.

In spite of some shortcomings, I really love this place. I've been here for lunch several times, and three dinners. The dinner we had last night was outstanding. The vegan charcuterie is always different, and each item is packed with flavor. Another crostini (or a second helping) might be useful, but they offer to bring some bread if you run out. I love vegetables, and clearly Sean Baker does too. My wife liked her cocktail, but it was a little too small. My Uberhoppy IPA was very good. 

The yellowtail crudo had two sauces, a cherry-mustard seed sauce and a pesto made with pistachios. Combined with the fish, the flavor is great, and the presentation is nice. 

The strawberry salad was not too inventive, but perfectly done. 

We had the carrot dish, with carrots cooked sous-vide with hay (I think he is paying homage to Daniel Patterson), this had a great flavor and texture profile. The extra touches like dehydrated kale elevate the dish, when combined with the other ingredients.

The chicken was good, the bbq sauce was a bit too spicy for my wife. I really liked the baked beans and cornbread croutons, reminding you that this is comfort food. 

The vegan carrot cake was interesting - my wife ordered it and thought it tasted too much like spice cake, but I think it was deconstructed with little carrot gelatins on the side to give the carrot flavor. 

I ordered the semifreddo, which was ok, I think I'm just not a fan. The caramel corn was a nice touch. 

We had great service, we had to change our reservation, but they were accommodating. I agree that the layout of the place is a bit odd, but I like the touches of the canned vegetables, fish net chandeliers, and leather belt couches.

I didn't even eat here. 

I do believe that the food here is probably 4 or 5 star quality, but I don't care if the food is good when the service is horrible--for me at least, dining is about the whole package--the food, the service, the ambiance. 

I politely asked for a table and was told it would be an hour wait. Fine, I would've waited and I understand that it was a busy night. Then, I saw some empty two seater tables and asked, mind you, very politely if they were reserved because I wouldn't have minded splitting up my party, since those tables were so close together anyways. Says the seater while rolling eyes: "Yes....of course they're reserved". RUDE. They better train their staff to be respectful to their customers. Why put them up front if they're unprofessional and unfriendly? I don't understand.

Guess everyone knows how great Gather is ... it is starting to be tough to get into.

Their food is pure goodness!

**NOT gluten-free friendly** 
(Must be able to order creatively to eat here.  The wait staff *will* accommodate you, however!)

This place is Bezrkeley-tastic!  Everything is locally grown, and the kitchen staff are very diligent about food allergies.  I let them know about my severe gluten allergy, and they tagged everything on our order so there would be little chance of cross-contamination.  They did it with a smile, even! I *really* appreciated it.

We started with an asparagus salad (yum!) and split pea soup, which I don't usually care for, but it was *excellent*.  I had a burger (with no bun, of course) that was *good*, if maybe a teeny on the salty side, but I think that might have come from the cheeze that was on top.

Also, my new favorite drink is the Moscow Mule, and I ordered 2 of them because the bar tender knew what he was doing.  I think it's the home-made ginger syrup that made the drink.  

If given the chance, I will *totally* come back!  Thanks again to the staff for being so quick, efficient, and accommodating to my food allergies!!

I am all for slow, local, sustainable, earth friendly foods, but this place left a seriously bitter taste in my mouth.  After spending a year in the PNW foraging for foods, I had high expectations only to be let down.  The decor is pretty neat with the recycled bottles, etc., but the food left me wanting.

I went with the BFF, his BFF from high school and her sweetheart.  My company was fabulous and lovely, the food not so much.  We had the 

kale salad
vegan charcuterie
pizza (I did not partake so I don't remember what it was)
stonefruit dessert

I also ordered one of the appetizers which was a boar cake (?) with an egg, and twelve other things (I am exaggerating).  

I will say one of the items on the vegan charcuterie plate did tickle my fancy with the delicious wild mushrooms, but other than that....

Everything else was so complicated with foams and other fanciness that maybe I am too pedestrian to appreciate, but I just want to eat good food.  That concept is fairly simple.  Gather just isn't.  This is probably a testament for my distaste for Berkeley in general, but I don't get Gather.

Was in Berkeley helping my daughter move from one apartment to another on Memorial Day.  Had seen a review about Gather a few weeks ago in the paper and thought to give it a try.  

Wonderful meal, beautifully presented.  

Though the restaurants was full and we did not have reservations, the hostess was very gracious and seated the 3 of us quickly.  The menus were well explained and several suggestions were appreciated.

I am a carnivore, but my daughter is vegetarian (maybe pescatarian as she will enjoy some fish - especially sushi).  The menu was very interesting and complete.  We tried 6 items to share and enjoyed them all.  

Crispy Pork Shoulder w/ manila clams (for me) was outstanding.   Seared Squid was delectable.  Turnip salad was great.  Vegan charcuterie was beautiful to look at and delicious to eat.  Probably my favorite was the Pizza with Olive Oil Poached Halibut Belly.  WOW!!!  Grilled Artichokes were perfectly presented.

All in all a fantastic meal at the end of a very tiring day.  

We will return.

PS - uploaded a few pics

I went to Gather with a friend a few weeks ago and had a wonderful time.

I am not a vegan by any stretch of the imagination, but I decided to go with a vegan meal because I felt like being healthy.  I had artichokes with forbidden rice and soybeans...I know it sounds drab but it was sooooo delicious.  My friend, who is a picky eater, got a pizza with pancetta and some kind of fancy cheese I forget the name of.  She loved it.

The decor is worth mentioning too, which I give an A+.

**And this place is great for people on a gluten free diet as their menu labels things that are GF.

I sat on this review for about a month, toggling between two and three stars, but the fact that I live a few blocks away and have had no desire to return here when famished even though it's the first suggested item that pops up on my mobile Yelp app is what sealed Gather's two star fate for me. 

I came here at 9pm on a Monday and the place was buzzing - clearly this is no longer a best kept secret. The menu is small yet enticing, though I'll admit disappointment in the few vegetarian items (I expected more of them). I settled on a dazzling pizza option of roasted cherry tomatoes, basil and smoked cheddar. I've never seen a pizza like this - the crust ends in a sort of nodini (bread knot: http://img116.imageshack.us/img116/5422/nodini3jh.jpg) twist and it's a heavenly pocket of dough. The pizza is big enough for two people and certainly priced accordingly ($17 is a bit much if you're dining alone).

The patronizing service is what will keep me from returning. My server  (contrary to the lovely seating hostess) was unwelcoming in a way that destroyed my first impression of Gather; I considered walking out before ordering my entree but I really was THAT hungry. You know when you feel out of place at a restaurant because of your attire, or the fact that you're dining alone, or aren't spending a fortune on drinks or appetizers? Yeah. A sort of "That's all you're ordering? I can't squeeze any more money out of you?" kinda tone that results in no tip and no repeat visits.

Really 2.5 stars, but I can't bring myself to round up and award the third one.

Took a friend here for his birthday dinner, and I have to say I was more than a bit disappointed considering what I've read here and heard from other friends.

Gather bills itself as "[a] place where you can find seasonal food, carefully sourced and thoughtfully prepared to appeal equally to vegetarians and omnivores". Well, I'm not vegetarian, but my friend was, and even I call BS when your menu purports to be 50% vegetarian, but most of the vegetarian options are under "small plates". In a place like Berkeley, offering vegetarians some appetizers and salads while paying lip service to them for entrees just doesn't cut it. 

We had crispy cardoons with an almond-tomato sauce and scallion salsa to start. The waitress, when asked what cardoons were, told us they were sort of like celery root but tasted closer to an artichoke heart, which I can't say I agree with. They didn't taste like much of anything, and sort of just served as a fried starch to put the sauce on. The sauce itself wasn't even that special; it just tasted like a hummus with tomatoes in it. Very one-note, which turned out to be the problem with my entree as well. 

I had an orange-olive braised duck leg, which came over some beans and tomatoes and stewed kale. The duck was cooked nicely enough and pretty much fell apart with a fork, but the flavors just weren't that deep. The sauce was rather acidic, being comprised of tomato and orange, and the kale was just kind of sad, like it had been thrown in as an afterthought. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't great. My vegetarian friend settled on a vegan mushroom "cioppino" because it seemed like the most interesting of the three(!) vegetarian entrees; he said it was pretty bland.

Okay, so the food was decent at best, but definitely nothing special. Why two stars? The service was abysmal. 

We arrived fifteen minutes ahead of our 7:00 reservation and patiently waited while they cleared up an entire section that had just been vacated by a party of sixteen; we were shown to our table after about ten minutes. No real problem there. Unfortunately, that was the best part of the service.

After sitting down, we were offered our choice of still or sparkling (filtered and carbonated in-house) water, and then waited for our waitress to show up. And waited. Ten to fifteen minutes later, she showed up. She was nice enough when she was at our table, but was kind of MIA most of the time. Wine showed up quickly enough, but I managed to kill half of my glass by the time our appetizer arrived, and no, I wasn't chugging it! The entrees took another ten or fifteen minutes after we _finished_ the appetizer; considering how long the appetizer took, this was patently ridiculous. Another ten-minute wait for the waitress after our plates were cleared... we were offered dessert but declined in favor of grabbing something sweet at another place rather than waiting another half hour. 

Gather is new in Berkeley, and seems to be having some growing pains. I want to give it another shot, but they need to work on both the food and the service before I do.

We stumbled on this place just by chance on a Monday night.  I was drawn in by the cool modern/rustic design and warm inviting lighting.  To my surprise, they were completely booked up for the night when we tried to get a table.  Since we weren't really in the mood to sit at the bar, we made the decision to eat elsewhere and head back here another night.  So the weekend rolls around and we find ourselves in the neighborhood again at the dinner hour.

Since we basically were there this time when they opened the doors for the evening at 5 p.m., we promptly got a nice table for the 3 of us.  Cocktails were all amazing.  I particularly recommend the Bee Sting which naturally has a honeyed taste.  As for entrees, the little lady got the Mushroom Stew and both my cousin and I each opted for the braised Pork Shoulder which was the daily special.  All of our dishes were excellent in flavor and preparation.  We all clearly shared this opinion, since not a speck of food was left on any of our plates.  For dessert, I tried the cheesecake.  This is no ordinary cheesecake...it's sprinkled with various bits of fruits & nuts that just make it absolutely tantalizing on the good old sweet tooth.

Overall, we highly enjoyed our initial dining experience at Gather.  Price is a little steep at about $50/person but you're definitely paying for quality here.  If you are a fan of Chez Panisse Cafe, I would say Gather will be right up your alley & well worth checking out.

We had foodie guests in town and made a reservation for 4, and were seated promptly. It all went downhill from there. 

After being ignored for 10 minutes with no water, our waitress appeared, described the specials, and then disappeared again. She reappeared and took our order. 

Someone else appeared with drinks and was confused about which drinks went where (setting the stage for a theme). 

None of our appetizers arrived, the waitress popped in, said she was confused about whether we wanted everything to arrive at once since some ordered salads, some small plates, some mains. Uh, we ordered appetizers for everyone! She went away, then as if on cue everything arrived: salads, small plates, appetizers and mains, carried by an army of people we'd never seen before, confused about who ordered what. 

The evening was iced when a cold mushroom salad appetizer arrived after we were done punishing ourselves, and was placed in front of one of our party. A comped dessert?

Our waitress dropped off some dessert menus, in passing and in silence. We never saw her again.

We ran for the door.

I can't remember what the food was like. I'd suggest sourcing some local wait staff. You could "repurpose" them from other locations.

Uninspired, get them in and get them out the door, sums it up for me.

If you're a vegetarian, you'll like the menu selections and the food. If you're looking for animal based faire, you might be disappointed, I certainly was. Not much on the menu interested me and I went for something that would be hard to dislike: Burger, fries and salad. Aioli on the bun was barley there. You would need a forensic expert to prove it's existence. Cheddar and grilled onions seemed to be rationed.

This experience wasn't awful, but it wasn't foodie either. If I had to choose the most memorable aspect it would be all the hard surfaces that bounced sound making it difficult to have a conversation without shouting. Concrete is cool, but so is some fabric either on the walls or ceiling to dampen the sound and make this just a little more intimate and friendly.

Solid 2 stars, nothing more and nothing less.

I finally had the opportunity to experience Gather last night for the first time. It was exquisite. The vegan charcuterie is an adventure all in itself! I'm the furthest thing from being vegan but this appetizer is not to be missed. I had the special seafood stew entree that was wonderfully complex, smokey and had spicy. Followed by a strawberry and vanilla semifreddo. Each dish was incredible. This is not simple and rustic.

The atmosphere is surprisingly comfortable, laid back and the details were well considered. Warm lighting, reclaimed wood/leather and a handsome style. 

I was concerned going in that I would be engulfed in sustainability, Berkeley eco-activism or guilt-ridden for enjoying pig parts. But it wasn't the case. The focus was the food, not the politics. In fact I didn't even hear the speech about where the veggies came from, or the family lineage of the shrimp. It's there if you ask. But after talking with the waiter about how the Habanero powder was crafted, you could safely assume that every detail about the joint contains a story of sustainability, health and most of all, taste.

I have to admit I was expecting this place to be exploding with hippie/vegan/overly politically correct nonsense and boy was I wrong! The whole staff was warm and professional...I will admit the service wasn't super polished with regard to timing and replacing silverware...but they were so friendly and eager I didn't mind. We ordered the vegan charcuterie - an idea that filled me with doubt and cynicism - and I must say it was exceptional! Super creative and inventive use of vegetables and sauces and a great presentation...

But what surprised and delighted me the most was the burger. This would be the last place on earth I would expect to find a great burger and when I say this was a great burger I mean great with a capital G. One of the best ever. The sauce! The meat! The caramelized onion! Hold me back!

Gather is still ironing out some kinks as a new restaurant but I recommend them without hesitation - great food, great prices, cool lights, and some of the warmest service I have ever come across. Success!!

this was my birthday restaurant. that's how much I love it here. And they have 3-4 kinds of Kombucha on tap!

Must try the vegan charcuterie and the pizzas are all to die for!

+ Very delicious dishes, especially the pizza and pancakes.
+ Unique cocktails made with some quality organic liquor.
+ Emphasis on sustainable, organic ingredients.

- Expensive, especially given the small portion sizes.
- Long wait for dinner foods (45+ minutes for dinner, party of 7)

The Short
4 stars. I'm a little generous here, but I am a fan of their food-- its well made. It makes me forget about the questionable value of the meal and long waits. I've eaten here 3 times, twice for dinner and once for brunch. Its been a good year since my meals there, but some things are unforgettable.

1) Prices are pretty steep given the portion sizes. 
Thankfully, the quality of the food is quite good. In particular, their Acme Walnut French Toast (cornflake crust, fruit compote, walnuts, cinnamon spice, and yogurt) was one hell of a french toast. My brother and I downed that in a jiffy.

2) Unique cocktails.
A lot of vodka-based cocktails used Square One organic vodka, which is one of my favorite vodkas. Their Bee Sting (Square One botanical, ginger, lemon, honey, mint) was a very enjoyable cocktail. I'd recommend it to those who love ginger. 

3) Fantastic pizza.
Their pizzas are hard to pass up. Their crusts are on the crunchier side, but the ingredients and varieties they have (breakfast and lunch) are exceptional.

If you had to choose between dinner or brunch, I'd definitely do brunch.

Recommendations:
Pizza
Cocktails

I think I would have given Gather a solid 4 starts if it weren't for the lackluster service.  I felt bad as it seemed like they were probably understaffed but it's Sunday and you have brunch, aren't brunches usually busy?

Gather wasn't particularly packed and there were several open tables.  Upon walking in with a party of 3 we were told there would be a bit of a wait.

Uh.  Ok.  Maybe there were large parties coming in to take the open tables we saw all over the restaurant.

Our hostess left, came back, offered us outdoor seating to which we were excited to say yes to, she left, came back and told us that the back patio was full and decided to sit us right near the host stand which was fine.

We sat and caught up.  We talked.  And we talked.  And we talked some more.  

15 minutes water arrived after we raised our hand to request it.

It was a lazy Sunday with no real rush to go anywhere so it wasn't a huge deal but there just seemed to be this weird laissez-faire thing going on with our table.  We had to flag someone down to take our order.

I like the space, the food was great and it made me want to come back for dinner and I'm hoping the service glitches were just because of the restaurant having an off day.

I always appreciate restaurants that call out what is vegan and what can be veganized.  My braised mushroom sandwich was really nice, the greens on the side were perfectly dressed and my side of potato scallion hash was absolutely delicious.  I added the roasted market veggies (+$2.50) to my dish which I don't think I'd do again as it was a scoop of carrots and random white beans and it was COLD.  When I think of roasted veggies, I think of something hot with some charred bits which I love.  (I HEART CHAR!)

I'll definitely come back for dinner and give Gather another shot but I hope the service is a bit more spot on next time.

about two months ago, i opened the door to my overly-excited boyfriend who said something like "gilly, there's a new restaurant opening up on oxford that looks so good". Now, coming from him this meant very little, considering his diet (when i'm not cooking) consists of pasta with Ragu brand sauce, microwave popcorn, and multiple snickers bars a day. 

after patiently waiting, looking at the sample menu, and drooling over the photos, we ate here last night for his birthday. 

started with the mixed lettuces with blood orange vinaigrette and pumpkin seeds - tasty; i love blood oranges and these were perfect ones; pumpkin seeds went well with it, but the salad was over-peppered. 

next we had the vegan charcuterie: 
- roasted beets with kumquats, chili, and fennel = perfect amount of sweetness, the beets were beautiful
- tomato porcini pate with grilled tardivo = smoky and DELICIOUS
- mandarin oranges with arugula, pistachios, and tarragon = good, but somewhat forgettable
- "potato salad" with red wine dijon sauce, capers, and oyster mushrooms = the first time i've ever liked potato salad
- parsnips with lemon, olive oil, and parsnip puree = love this as well
this all came with grilled bread, which we only ended up eating with the mushroom preparation. 
touching moment: while we were eating this platter of vegetables, rodrigo said to me: "this is one of the few times i've preferred quality to quantity". i nearly teared up at this, considering he's been known to casually eat a party-sized bag of doritos in ten minutes (no, really)

finally, we ordered the pizza with goat cheese, romanesco broccoli, lemon zest, and thyme. loved this also. the flavors were good and the crust was thin and crispy under the toppings and thick and fluffy on the edges. 

our waiter was great- friendly and knowledgeable about the food. 
from the moment we walked in, i felt like the service was a bit jumbled, but i'm not really one to downgrade restaurants for that, especially because i'm so awkward that i'm never really sure if it's my fault or their's :)

Okay, first of all...yikes. It feels kind of hurtful to give only 3 stars to such a classy looking restaurant, especially since this is my first ever review. But I'd have to say my overall experience was nothing very memorable.

A group of my friends and I came to celebrate a birthday. We didn't have reservations so waited for around 45 minutes (no blame there though-we should have expected the reservation policy on a Saturday night). The hostess was "nice" but that's about all I can say. Our actual dinner server was very friendly (not to mention cute..) and joked around with us a bit, bumping up my rating on this place a bit.

FOOD: My friends and I ordered the Duck Sausage Pizza, Pork Pizza, Mushroom Pizza, Ranch Burger, and Cauliflower soup to name a few. The ranch burger was flavorful,nice and juicy, but although I asked for "well done" I don't remember requesting "charred." 3.5 stars. The Pizzas were all pretty tasty ...I apologize for lack of other adjectives this is my first Yelp review. Again, the crust was more black than I had hoped for but it didn't seem to bother my friend. Fries were tasty upon arrival, but maybe the combination of the cold outdoor patio and skinny build of the fries, they starched  up quite quickly. Not too tasty, not really worth the money in my opinion. Nothing really saved the day except the good company and the elegant, classy ambiance of the restaurant which made it birthday-worthy.

woo! first yelp review!

Came back with my parents this time.

We ordered the charcuterie plate, and the Spicey Tomato Pizza.

The former was creative and pretty good, although smaller than I remember. A little pricey considering the small sizing.

But the Pizza was pretty big from what I last remembered, and the crust was oh-so-good. Soooooo good. And the sauces drizzled on top were amazing, along with the caper/olive tapenade. Very flavor intensive, while still remaining light.

Finally, we had the brown butter ice cream. Only $3 for a 3 scoopys! Surprised the deal! And it was veeeeery good. Not overly sweet, and the richness was tempered by something I can't quite tell...Very good.

Also, the ginger beer is good too! Didn't try any of the alcohol...(drank last nite, and its fucking finals week...) though.

Good when the parents come, since I don't have to foot the bill...

Server: "Does your food taste ok?"

We heard variations on this, throughout our meal.  Unfortunately, "ok" about sums up our lunch experience at Gather.  The components were beyond reproach, especially in the pizza crust, but the final presentation was seriously lacking in flavor composition and eye appeal.

The roasted beet salad was nearly bereft of beets, and arrived mysteriously hooded by an overly large, rather bitter, pale green lettuce leaf.  

The soup, while flavorful, was a monotone pastel puree; it could have used a sage leaf as a proverbial fig leaf for cover.

The tomato and cheese pizza presented another monotone pastel on a crust that was in need of more char.  

So, yes, everything tasted ok, and ditto Gather.  

We roamed down the street for the rest of our midday repast.

GATHER is a little gem that truly reflects the personality of Berkeley. It provides a dining experience like no other with its one-of-a-kind Vegan Charcuterie and fully organic menu that manages to appeal to both the meat-lover and the vegan&vegetarian PETA-enthusiast. The ingredients are as fresh as they claim - straight from local farmers, and are all sustainable. The waiters are also knowledgeable and extremely helpful. 

Although GATHER has a great concept and a lively atmosphere that really makes it a winning location within Berkeley, I can only give it 3-stars because the food was only OK and worthy of a one-time experience. 

We ordered the acclaimed vegan charcuterie and the flavors were crisp and very enjoyable to eat; but anything memorable?, meh. I also had the halibut crudo; it was very tasty but nothing extraordinary. Boyfriend ordered the daily special: spare rib pizza.. I found it too salty, but at least he liked it. GATHER definitely wins with freshest ingredients.. they just need to work on better preparing them.

I went to try Gather in Downtown Berkeley on Mon 1/24/11.  It's really close to Downtown Berkeley Bart - just walk South on Shattuck, up to Allston, then at the corner turn Right.  It's across from Saturn's Cafe.

I made reservations on OpenTable - No points given for this place, bummer.

Got Still tap water in a carafe.  Ask for Sparkling!! - the table that sat next to us asked & got it!  Bummed wasn't offered Sparkling water!

Menu is small.  We got to share:

Sheep's Milk Ricotta Pizza - $17.  It's a medium size pizza with 8 slices.  It has nettles, potato, leeks, rosemary.  I liked it, but my half I picked had burnt crust.

Barbecued Young Chicken $19 - flageolet beans, sausage, greens, turnip, almond-tomato pesto (gluten free).  I liked they cut up the chicken for us to share, it was juicy chicken - I was surprised.  I liked all the other stuff too.

$17 + $19 = $36 + $3.51 tax = $39.51 before tip & tax.  Credit cards taken.

Separate bathrooms on the Far Right past the curtains - Women's had 2 stalls & trough sinks, very powerful dryer.
 
I'd recommend it for a nice dinner in Downtown Berkeley.

The Vegans have done it again! The self-proclaimed carnivore beast was once again "WOW'ed" by the cooking skills of the Vegan people. I was eating their Spicy Tomato Pizza and was wondering why there was no cheese.  I thought the sauce was creme fraiche but it turns out to be cashew puree (this was when it dawned on me that some of their dishes are vegan).  The cashew puree was pretty delicious and it toned down the tartness of the pizza. The pizza sauce was a little bit too sour for my taste and it wasn't too spicy as I expected. I still thought this pizza was great and I will definitely order it again.

We also ordered the Fontinella (their cheese pizza) and we added pancetta. I wish they put more mozzarella on this because it definitely wasn't enough. Next time, I am ordering extra cheese. For both pizzas, I really liked the texture of the dough and the flavor of the crust was great. Usually when you eat leftover pizzas the next day, it tastes better.  Gather's pizza doesn't taste the same the next day and the crust became completely soggy overnight. I suggest finishing your pizza instead of taking leftovers home. 

Loverboy ordered the Prather Ranch Burger.  He ordered it medium rare but it came out to us medium well which was a bummer.  The burger was still a bit moist and it had great flavor. I really liked their fries.  They came out extra crispy which made me happy because I like mine almost to the point of burnt.  If you don't like your fries extra extra extra crispy, make sure you let them know to not overcook your fries.

The cocktails were pretty good.  The Rhuby Cubed and the Pisco Sour were really sweet so if you like your girly-girl drinks, you should try these out.  My favorite was the Bee Sting which I found quite refreshing.  Loverboy was amazed by their high tech paraphernalia that they use for carbonating some of the cocktails.

The service was cool.  The bartenders and servers were nice.  The staff were kind enough to call a cab for us at the end of our meal. Also be sure to make reservations.  We waited for over an hour because we didn't have reservations.  There is a patio outside where you can hang out and drink cocktails while you wait for your table.  However, the night when we went to Gather was cold and they didn't turn on the portable heaters.
