Thankfully I had a thick coat on so I didn't mind hanging outside and enjoying the crisp evening air.

High quality, organic, sustainably harvested goodness - this place epitomizes all that is good in Berkeley, and is where the hippies go to eat, once they grow up.

Short and sweet: Personally know the owners Eric and Ari. But that will not bias me, as I am true to the cause of objective food reviews.

Eric, hailing from NY, used to live in my apt building, and always turned me on to leftovers from his catering gigs. Ari and I both ended up in Berkeley, which is surprising, as we went to the same high school in Jersey. Like minds I guess. These guys started a business doing backpacking/yoga trips to Yosemite and the like, and also organic catering (not at the same time :-)). Kind of like two heads of the same beast, if you will. The opening of Gather is the end of a dream that I first heard about 7 years ago. Congrats, boys.

Food here is all organic, all locally farmed and harvested, and they will proudly tell you where every ingredient has come from. Pizzas are all great, the vegan folk will love the charcuterie platter, as well as other dishes, and you really can't go wrong ordering blindly off the menu. I went with a group of folks, and we just ordered a mess of stuff, and proceeded to eat and drink wine, enjoying the atmosphere, and the space, which for years used to house a parking lot  that many of us remember, often used when patroning Cancun right next door, Jupiter around the corner, or for taking in events at Cal.

Proud to say I too am a fan of this place, and look forward to returning for years to come. It's where the conscious-minded can eat worry free, and where the hippies can go and rejoice: high quality, veg friendly food that I'm sure has been endorsed by Alice Waters of Chez Panisse fame (creator of the locavore/California cuisine movement), and this place can suit all audiences: parents visiting their college kids at Cal, foodies looking for the best new place, and yes - the hippies of Berkeley, assuming they kept their day jobs.

And it being one of the hottest tickets in town, better make a reservation, especially on weekeneds, as this place can get packed.

Gather: perfectly...delectably...BERKELEY!
First impression: the bar was too busy to take our order before our table was available. Lasting impression: the ragout was fantastic and I left too full.

This place was phenomenal!  The food was fresh, well prepared, and super delicious.  Their wait staff was very kind and attentive.  We sat at the counter and had a great time watching the activity in the kitchen.

The menu (which rotates) has many options for vegetarians, vegans, and those on a gluten-free diet as well as serving the needs of the omnivores in your group.

Looking at the menu online I thought Gather looked a little upscale to be right across from the UC Berkeley campus, but when we arrived for brunch it seemed to make more sense with lots of kids dining with their parents. It's a large space with plenty of natural lighting from all the windows on this curved corner location where much of the interior is from reclaimed materials.

The menu has a good mix of vegetarian, seafood, and meat items including a Vegan "charcuterie". They do the whole locavore, organic, sustainable thing and unlike many places the phrase "whenever possible" does not make an appearance on their menu as a disclaimer.

I had the Summer Vegetable Hash ($15, Padron peppers, roasted corn, pork belly, fried eggs, potatoes, smoked butter, toast http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=2g1QnaAkCMhmirRN6NIlDQ). Overall, very good, but a couple of the potato wedges were hard / undercooked and not too many of the delicious pork belly chunks (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=ASJzhTuTp4JohaQq638txw). Watch out for the larger Padron peppers because the larger they get, the higher probability of getting a scorcher, and with Padrons it can be a bit of Russian Roulette! You can guess how I know ;-)

They g/f got the Braised Beluga Lentils with Soft-boiled egg ($9, Romano beans, Tuscan Rose eggplant, mint, soft polenta, smoked olive oil (v, gf) add soft boiled egg $2 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/BiZAzf2SAFCE0gJrX-PGFw?select=YrJ8L9fZcnyFwJtCjC4K7Q). Delicious, creamy polenta. The mint and olive oil added some interesting flavor notes. Nicely runny egg. Needed some toast ($1.50) to soak some of the runny yolk with.

Service was both scattered (the main waitress we had) and earnest (the trainee shadowing her around). We had to flag down other workers to get drink refills.

Michelin Bib Gourmand pick

Reserve early, folks!  Although the website says walk in welcome, the wait could be horrible.  I made reservation almost a week ago and I still got lousy hours like 8.45pm on a Saturday night.  

Voted as Esquire's 20 Best New Restaurants of 2010, this place has creative menu.  

We tried all small plates, sausage pizza and their Artisanal combination.  The small plates are:

1. Watermelon radish ravioli - Meyer lemon-cashew ricotta, puttanesca vinaigrette cress.
Beautifully plated but a bit too sour on the vinaigrette.

2. Crispy brussels sprouts - celery root, Point Reyes blue cheese, grilled bacon
Yum.  Could feel the grill heat and the crispness of the sprouts.

3. Halibut crudo - avocado, sinese pepper, Buddha's hand, Mendocino sea vegetables
Fresh fish and tasty avocado puree though not enough of it.

4.Seared squid - anchovy, romanesco broccoli, grilled baby escarole, chilis, capers, mint
A cent too strong on the lemon juice but overall creative and well blended.

5. Sausage pizza - pork belly, cayenne confit, Fortinella, oregano
I can't taste the pork belly but the sausage is well cooked but not dry.  The Oregano flavor is strong enough to stand out but hubby complained that there was not enough sausage on the pizza.

6. Artisanal Plate: Vegan Charcuterie
-Mushroom tartar
-Pear carpaccio, smoked persimmon celery root salsa
-Grilled watermelon radish steak, leek butter, horseradish salsa verde, pomegranate
-Oyster mushroom crudo, tonnato sauce, avocado, crisy sea palm
-Roasted carnival squash, sunchoke cashew bay leaf sauce, smoked maple
Served on a wooden panel.  Overall fresh ingredients and creative cooking, but the puree all seemed too limited consider they tasted so good.  The portions on each were very small and sometimes we missed tasting some of the ingredients.  

7. A glass of 09 Lodi Phoenix Ranch Cinsault
Delicious.  A bit thin on the body but still flavorful.

8. A glass of 09 Edna Valley Verdad Albarino
Smooth, flavorful but a bit young.  Medium body but with a lot of potential to age.

The service was attentative and the waiter knew the customers thinkings very well.

I came here for dinner because a friend recommended it to me and I think the food was pretty good but for the portion and price, I've got to dock it one star. 

Food: 
1) Kim Chee pizza: the best dish of the night! It was made with a fried egg on top with an oozing egg yolk and sprinkled with flavorful pork belly meat. Every bite had this spicy kick to it that was probably from the kim chi. I liked the idea of this Asian-American Fusion dish. Very inventive and tasty!
2) Marathon Broccoli pizza: A little overshadowed by the Kim Chee pizza, but this was the second best dish of the night. The broccoli was very well marinated with just the right about of cheese. It was just a little dry compared to the kim chee pizza so it just made it a little harder to swallow. 
3) Winter Chicories Salad: The plate was 3 times bigger than the portion of food. The cauliflower tasted really good but the rest of the leafy greens were ok. It was definitely too expensive for the amount of food that came. 

Service: 
Very friendly and welcoming! Pretty good service!

Ambiance: 
Very hip and happening place. Packed dining room with a very full bar too. It was a bit crowded and noisy so it was hard to have a convo going but it was a nice place to hang out and chill with some friends. The decor was very modern and hipster. 

Price: 
For the portion of food that you get, it's pretty expensive. Our meal came out to be $63 BEFORE tip and we only ordered three things. Be prepared to put a nice dent into your wallet if you eat here. 

Overall:
I guess I'm glad I got to try it but I don't think I can afford to eat here again...maybe when I actually start making some money I can afford to blow $63 on one meal...

THEE BEST SERVICE YOU CAN RECEIVE ON A JAM PACKED SATURDAY NIGHT EVER!!

Seriously, I walked in with my cousins to find out the wait would be about an hour (of course we called and tried to make a reservation, but they were booked) but we said no problem lets wait. As we sat and had small talk both the host and hostess walked over to us and said they could seat us at a table near the bar area (it had only been about 15 mins) the only down side was it was close to a door. Again not a problem for us ladies, give us a couple drinks and we will be warm, LoL.

So sure enough we get our lovely table and wanted to order everything. But instead settled for a nice glass of wine and a couple ginger sodas that were all so so yum. 

As for the food, we had a pizza and and a nice salad, both were so so so so good, not even good, they were superb. You can taste the freshness of all the ingrediants, and come to find out they actually buy some of their veggies right down the street at the Berkeley Farmers Market.

This place has fantastic service and is well worth a visit if you have never been. Great date night spot or even girls night. :D
Excellent food with a strong attention to fresh and locally sourced ingredients. Had the albacore sandwich - very nice. Coffee is fantastic. Bread pudding was just good.

I went here with katherine c. (her review is somewhere around here).

We got the Halibut Tartare, Spring Vegetable Salad, Spicy Tomato Pizza, and the Pork Sausage Pizza. 

I loved the Tartare and Salad as appetizers. They were light and refreshing. I felt soooo healthy eating these!

I was told by my boss who frequents this place that I should order the pizzas. They were both really good, but I liked the Spicy Tomato Pizza more. I'm a bit critical of pizza (I lived in Italy for a short period of time, so it's hard to compare), which is why I'm giving this place a 4 instead of a 5. 

Overall this place SCREAMS Berkeley! I liked the food and the service was great. I would come back here, but I don't craveeee it as I do with many other Berkeley restaurants.
This place is fantastic- nice ambience not too pretentious.  Great original drinks (had the bee sting).  Definitely get the charcuterie & pizza crust was amazing.

A nice place to indeed gather for family Sunday brunch....

Everybody's first time---Rick and Ann's, out... La Note, out.... how about Gather? oh my.... great unique things on the menu.

In was the brunch pizza. deelish! Esp that nice egg baked in there.
A chanterelle omelette with such delicate wonderful richness and depth was also tried. A locally souced organic burger and a highly priced halibut crudo ($$ but v fresh). And for dessert, you ask?  a not-so-great vegan chocolate something or other, and some homemade ice cream.

I felt the sweet department suffered a bit and though the ice cream flavors were original, we found it a bit too sweet and not creamy enough. 

The space itself is nice, decor could be bit warmer, but some nice touches (i.e. pickled jars) service being average and no real complaints. Brunch prices are around the mid $10's range....

complimentary carafes of sparkling water. Nice touch!

We came here for a birthday celebration with a party of 8, nothing grande by any means.

Pluses ~ interesting combos, creative dishes and all of the food was very fresh with beautiful presentation

Minuses ~ our server started off nice, although there was a bit of a snotty edge to her which came out full force later, the portions were actually insulting, our table joked about the dishes being samples of what was to come, we waited FOREVER for our starters, about 45 minutes from the time we ordered, then after we finished another 20  minutes passed, so we asked what was up ~ here's where she got snotty, and said with such attitude she was waiting for us to finish out starters ~ never was there any acknowledgement that the wait was ridiculous, and as so many other reviews stated, she really was quite absentee....in today's economic times, the cost of the tiny portions in this restaurant are verging on ridiculous, if not completely silly.  Fact of the matter is - they're making bank on you and me!  

I won't be returning ~ EVER!!!!!

What a wonderful restaurant! My parents came to visit so my husband and I decided to take them there since my mom has some dietary restrictions and my dad loves some good meat. My friends and I walk by here all the time and have tried to come a few times before but it's always packed...and now I know why. It's amazing!

I would highly recommend making reservations several days in advance using their website or OpenTable.com since tables fill up quickly. Their menu is 50% vegan, vegetarian, gluten free and 50% meat. Perfect combo for all of us attending dinner here!

From the host/ess to the server, the staff is very professional, outgoing, and friendly. They surely do know their wine, beer, and food menu and can make some great recommendations. Prices are appropriate, everything is local, fresh, and delicious. The plate presentation is gorgeous! If you have the option and the weather is nice, grab a table in their outside area!

I would highly recommend trying their summer squash pizza, steak, and french fries. All very good! We did have an issue with our pizza (the squash on it was old or not ripe enough, but it made our pizza the most bitter thing I've ever tasted, it was pretty bad, lol). My husband and I each had a bite of it and told our server who was wonderful about the situation. We weren't upset, it happens, but we wanted to eat the pizza since it looked amazing! She was really great and had it remade for us and took care of it. We did get it after everyone else at our table had begun eating, but no biggie...we devoured it once the new one came out. It was deletable! I highly recommend it! 

I'm excited to come back again. :) Thanks for the great food and service!

Wanted to find a brunch place after church today but didn't want to go anywhere with a wait. After a quick consultation of my Yelp iPhone app, I found this place and also found a note that it was the first weekend they were opening for brunch.  It could mean super packed or no-wait because  not that many people know about it as a brunch spot yet.  

We took the gamble and won.  No wait, we were seated right away.  Not sure how long that will last.

They squeezed us into this side table near the windows which felt a little too close to the table next to us (I felt like my butt was intruding into their space when I was sliding into my seat).  

I had the 1/2 Sandwich Cup of Soup option with the Roasted Porchetta Sandwich and the Chorizo Chili soup.  The sandwich was good but I was a little disappointed that the porchetta was cold.  Was it supposed to be cold?  The greens were really fresh.  The soup was wonderful -- just the right flavors, not too salty not too greasy.  The husband had the Ranch Burger which was simple but really delicious.  The skinny fries and the tangy sauce that it came with were also spot on.

The desserts were standout, we got the huckleberry bread pudding and the pistachio brittle biscotti ice cream thing.  The bread pudding was solid and warm from the oven but the pistachio brittle thing stole the show.  It came with fresh grapefruit and candied kumquats.  Such an interesting combination of flavors with the distinct taste of the pistachios.  It was delicious and memorable.  

Friendly and efficient service.  Not too pesky and not the most helpful but they are definitely available.

We will definitely be back to try the dinner menu.

I've been wanting to try this place for awhile now and finally convinced two friends to go with me last night.  My parents are always raving about it, and they raised me, so I figured I would probably like it too. Well, they were right! Here is what we had:

Seared Squid
Mushroom Bruschetta
Baby Turnip Salad
Charcuterie Plate
Sausage Pizza

Everything was amazing! I was full and I couldn't stop eating it was so good (one of my biggest problems).  All the dishes were tasty and seasoned correctly.  The charcuterie plate was probably my favorite, but the pizza and mushroom bruschetta were a close second. There was an egg on the pizza, which they do in France, and generally I find kind of weird, but on this pizza it was like delicious x delicous x delicious. (I liked it in case you can't tell).  I would definitely come back so I can have dessert which we were too full to order. :)

A farewell dinner to our fellow Berkelian friends who are leaving the country. What better to do than to "Gather!" and reminisce the good times while eating some amazing food.  

It's restaurants like this one that make this here Bay Area look good so darn good on the food map. Breakfast, lunch and dinner menus, all with unique mouth watering dishes: vegetarian, meatertarian, gluten free, veterinarian (who knows) they accommodate us all! You know the place is exquisite when you have to pop out the word exquisite, or look at words on the menu and go "oooh it has kishu mandarins? That's my cousin's name" or  "ooh mother loving Yukon gold potatoes in my dish bro.. just like my ride" or "forget a freak tonight, I got me some freekeh citrus in my chicken bro." 

Yes plates range in prices from expensive to "hmm remember we're still in a  recession." So if you're a hobo whose not just rocking the traditional Berkeley attire, this may not be your kinder meal. 

I had the Half chicken with the freeka-freeka freekeh citrus, and whatever other sorts of exquisite goodness to this entree that only stimulates that amygdala and heals all forms of psychological illnesses, such as Body Dysmophic Disorder and Dementia. Yes I am exaggerating, and I'm misinforming you with a bunch of clinical bull-shenanigans, but this was a damn good entree and I would highly recommend it! Little bit of tang to it, alittle bit of spice.. perfect.

I came, I ate and said my last goodbyes to my mates. May not be in Berkeley for a while, but when I'm back in hobo's paradise, I'll be sure to cop me a pancho and more importantly eat at Gather.

Gather is honestly a really great place to gather with friends, your significant other, family members, or anyone else you feel like sharing a nice meal with.  I went here with my boss to celebrate my ex-coworker's birthday.  The restaurant has a cozy feel to it.  There's a lot of wood and the hanging ceiling lights give off a warm glow.  The restaurant has a very welcoming atmosphere and the menu has lots of options for people with all sorts of diets as well.  Many of the items are gluten-free, vegetarian, and/or vegan.  Don't worry, there's meat available for all you meat lovers too.   

My party and I shared 3 pizzas and a kale salad.  In addition, we each ordered an alcoholic beverage.  The birthday celebrant and I got some fruity girly cocktails that were tasty (and strong) while my boss sipped on some red wine.  Everything here tasted good...even the kale salad.  It was my first time having kale and I've heard that it isn't always the most pleasant vegetable to eat.  At Gather though, the kale wasn't too tough.  It was cooked well and the salad was topped with carrots, pine nuts, cheese, and some other tasty ingredients.  The pizzas we got were cooked nicely and all had pretty good flavor.  The crusts were thin and crunchy.  My favorite pizza was the Corn Pizza but I think it would've been even more awesome if it had potatoes.  The Pancetta Pizza was a little spicy for me.  My least favorite was the Fontinella Pizza...it wasn't very exciting.  You can also add egg to your pizza for an extra charge - definitely trying that next time.  As for dessert, we didn't order any because we were so full.  We each ended up taking a to-go box of half a pizza! 

Service here was awesome too.  The waitress was very patient with my party whenever we said we needed more time to look at the menu. We were too busy talking and hadn't even glanced at the drink menu or regular menu each time the waitress came to take our orders.  Also, the restaurant didn't kick us out for staying and chatting so long past closing time.

Parking here is a pain so I'd recommend taking BART if possible.  The Downtown Berkeley BART station is so close to Gather!!  I love when public transportation is walking-distance to where I'm trying to go.

If you plan on eating at Gather, I'd highly recommend making a reservation at least a week in advance (especially if you're choosing to go on a popular night like Friday or Saturday).  It's a poppin' place and reservations fill up fast!  Also, keep in mind that in order to be seated, your whole party needs to be present.    

In conclusion, gather at Gather!! :)

Gather offers a refreshing alternative to traditional brunch. To me, their entrees are still comfort food with a modern flair.

From what I understand, their brunch menu alternates (as well as their dinner menu) and dishes use only the finest local, organic produce and ingredients. I was initially worried that they would be extremely expensive, however the price range was fair. Among 3 people, we shared 3 entrees for around $15pp and left satiated.

We ordered a pizza (pancetta, Bartlett pears, topped with aurgula), stewed lentils over polenta-altogether topped with a perfectly poached egg, stinging nettles egg scramble with goat cheese bruschetta. Everything was portioned very well. The pizza can be easily shared ~10 slices. 

See the pictures for entrees

I am probably not doing the dishes enough justice. Each dish was incredibly delicious. I can definitely tell that the chef put a lot of care and love in the food. and it wasn't messily created. 

I recommended sharing a pizza, they are extremely succulent. And some interesting dishes to share. Will definitely come back to savor their dinner service.

Service was nice, although we didn't get our water refill until the end our service because the waitress seemed to have forgotten. Other than that, they have complimentary sparking water, nice staff and a wonderfully classy atmosphere. I also appreciate their open kitchen and being able to watch the chefs play with the flames.

Gather is not a place known for its accessible real estate. Instead, it's bunched up underneath an apartment complex which may or may not be still under construction, a car wash/gas station abomination, and...nothing else (actually, across the street there's a huge concrete wall). So it's all the more noteworthy that the place is packed until closing.
 
     Upon entering, the first thing you notice is the laid back feel--clean and modern with wood cuts and faux-brass railing. The second thing you notice is the dress code. This consists, apparently, of black, V-neck shirts, sleeves bunched up (not rolled--that's too "square") to the elbow, paired with dark washed skinny jeans. My immediate impression was that the people here tried too hard to force the upscale/trendy/pedestrian slant. Listen, folks, you don't need to dress like a wannabe beatnik to be avant-garde-casual. Or maybe you do. Regardless, the bottom line is that all the servers look like douches.

     Aside from that, though, there's really nothing to complain about. The food is largely vegetarian, except, it seems, for one squid dish, one pizza, and a few main courses. Always. How odd. Also, their salad variations are abundant. Having tried much of their ever-changing menu, I have concluded that their pizzas are the thing to get. They're amazing. Thin and succulent in the interior with a disproportionately puffy and tender crust, this place is what cheeseboard *should* be. Great combinations of produce and, conditionally, meat (yeah fuck you cheeseboard) layered on a crust that doesn't have the mouthfeel of greasy glass. You think the corn pizza from the 'board is great? Try the corn, guanciale, and jalapeno pie here. Blows the former out of the water. The squid is good, too. Everything else is, well, passable but not mindblowing.

     And honestly, despite the clothing debacle, the entirety of the waiting staff is quite congenial if not straight up nice. Most recently, our waiter, assumedly because I wasn't sporting a suitcoat or a candy colored polo, refilled our bread basket without even asking, adding two extra loaves into the mix. I don't want to throw the term "soulmate" around flippantly, but...well, you know.

     This place rocks. Get the pizzas, which are well worth the price, given the execution. And be sure to look for the poorly shaved Asian guy with a buzz cut. He'll do you right with that bread. I'm tellin' you.

I think this place is decidedly overrated and perhaps slightly overpriced, but it is still quite inventive and a unique experience for out-of-town-guests which it earns it four stars from me.

The menu changes seasonally - a big "Berkeley" food trend that seems to have been adopted wholeheartedly by a number of other foodie cities - and prominently features those weird vegetables you didn't realize you could eat. (Picture kale, watermelon rind and all those types of squash that are hard to track down at the store.)

The ideal number to come here with is three people - enough that you can share dishes and try different things among friends, but few enough that everybody actually gets some of everything without feeling guilty about taking the "last bite." (We all know how that goes.)

One thing that is absolutely great about this place in restaurant selection is its ability to appeal to weird diets; if you have a friend that is vegan, gluten intolerant, lactose intolerant, etc. - and almost everyone does these days - this place has items on the menu that cater to all restriction sets without needing to get inventive yourself.

In any case Gather makes for a reliable choice if you're looking to show someone Berkeley in a food nutshell without spending Chez Panisse prices or having to adjust to all the compromises of going to Cheeseboard.

Came here for a later lunch on a Saturday. We were seated quickly and had drinks with a quickness. Ordered two salads and a pizza. 

The Kale salad was off the hook! We even ordered another one. 
The Beet salad wasn't to my liking it was bitter but a lot of people eating it seemed to like it so I'm thinking I just didn't like it. 
The pizza was sooooo goood! 
Yogurt Citrus Cake-amazing.
The drinks were Yummy. 

Overall this place was one point from beginning to end. 
I seriously can't wait to go back.

The ambience and service was great.  Im starting the organic dealio and wanted to go to a place that would fit with my diet.  This restaurant did the job for a nice dinner with the BF.  

Pros:
Everything tasted great!
Form of food was interesting
Servers were extremely attentive, friendly and on time
Was not crowded!
Street parking ok
Not too shabby :P

Cons:
Portions maybe small (except for pizza)
Very pricey
A little getting use to for the weird mushroom foam thing they had going on

By the sound of the review, I should be giving it 4 stars, but my overall feeling is that I wasn't that impressed with their menu.  I wish they had a little more to offer.   They had 10x more wine choices than food you can pair it with.

I had their vegan charcuterie, pork platter, and the farm egg pizza.  The charcuterie was interesting, like something very appropriate for cleansing the palette, not really appetizer like.  The Pork belly had great flavor and consistency, but it was like a baby's serving.  The farm egg pizza was really good.  It was very comparable to Delfina's in SF's Dolores Park district.  

I would come here again to try the other stuff, but it would have to be a really good occasion as to justify that dent in my wallet.

G ood for light bites; not for dinner appetites
A mbiance and service was wonderful
T he dishes were unique, but portions were really small
H ad the Vegan Charcuterie -- unique, but mostly uninspiring flavor
E xcellent Pancetta pizza -- wish the pie was larger
R ecommend the Kale Salad if you like pricy blandness

Hellooooo Berkeley.

Gather is cute, modern, and a good space.  It has the most Berkeley vibe without being holier than thou, or even being hipper than thou.  It is clean and organized without being pretentious, warm and inviting without being home-y.  The space is well set up, with tables everywhere without being crowded, and a cute pato for outdoor seating.

Papa and I came in for a Saturday lunch, which meant lunch for him, hangover food for me.  The Friday  night before was spent with me making mai tais and then immediately slamming them down. Yeah baby.

Anyways, we were sat immediately and were greeted fairly quickly. A cool bonus that sets this place apart is that they offer complimentary sparkling or still water that comes in glass milk bottles. That was kind of neat. It also reminded me  I hate sparkling water, but whatever. My bad.

Their menu seems to change because they don't have a solid menu, and there appears to be different ones for lunch and for dinner. From the lunch menu, I got the eggs over toast and a side of bacon.  Everything else sounded way too hard to process. Papa got a half soup and a pork belly sandwich. I know that would not have stuck well in me.

My eggs were done well, scrambled and not gross or overcooked and with a great pepper. The toast was the fat artisian bread that is difficult to eat, but delicious once you manage it.  The bacon was perfect, not overcooked and not oily.

Papa's soup came in a small coffee mug and his sandwich came hidden behind  a small mountain of organic field greens.

The menu has a good variety of vegan and non-vegan amenities, and also said that the plates were from Sausilito (um, I'm impressed).

It's just SO Berkeley, but in all the best ways possible.

It's really nice to find a restaurant that scores highly with both vegans and omnivores.  I loved it (despite having ridiculously high expectations because I love Millennium and the head chef used to work there) and my omnivorous dining companions also loved it.

Tips: if you order the kale salad do NOT eat it all. It's enormous and no human should should eat that much fiber. Also, don't skip dessert.

i usually do not give places 4 stars after a first visit, but I loved Gather.  It is a wonderful space - open, beautiful, comfortable and well appointed.  The food was delicious.  We split the little gem salad and eggplant pizza.  The salad was fresh, flavorful and I loved the use of nori.  The eggplant pizza with cashew creme was fabulous.  I did not miss cheese.  I was knocked out by the epert use of diverse flavors.  Lunch was  fantastic and I can not wait to try dinner.

"Local food" restaurants suck. While I like the "idea" of local foods, I find that local-food restaurants tend to serve really bland and boring dishes that make me wonder if "eating local" is synonymous with eating unseasoned, dry and boring preparations.

Indeed, didn't Columbus cross the ocean in search of spice? Surely all food in Europe in 1492 was local. And, of course, it sucked. Entire empires were built around sending ships across the globe in search of spices and seasonings to make European food palatable.

Fast forward to the present day. Local food is fashionable. We have access to spices from all over the world. But we willingly give them up in favor of some unrealistic notion that you can feed 7 billion people with organic wilted greens and pasture-raised beef.

There are a few vegan options on the menu here, but not as many as I expected. I ended up with a braised mushroom sandwich and a cup of soup ($11). The sandwich was passable, but nothing more. It consisted of marinated chunks of portobello mushrooms served in between two dry, excessively-large pieces of white flour baguette. Why no whole wheat? Why were the bread pieces so damn large, such that they drowned out the meager portion of mushrooms?

The bread was slathered with a cashew puree sauce which was pretty tasty, though. The sandwich didn't come together on a whole, however, and tasted like a to-go sandwich I could get at any simple deli.

The "soup" was a watery soy base with five or six pieces of chickpeas floating in it, alongside some green onions. Not very impressive or tasty.

One of my colleagues got the vegan pizza (which is made with a cashew "cheese"); this, too, was pretty bland, and the cashew sauce lacked any herbs or seasoning. It would have been better if Gather combined the cashews with tofu and herbs to make a kind of pate, instead of a "cheese" that looked and tasted like tahini (which is to say it barely had any taste).

The crust was overly thick as well. The only thing going for this pizza was the sauce, which popped with flavor.

For dessert I had the sole vegan dessert option, a chocolate chip cookie ($2.50). It was dry, mealy and over-baked. It came out crunchy and crystalline rather than soft.

The service was friendly but slow. We'd place a drink order and wait 10 minutes to receive it.

Gather is a disappointment. That said, this might be a decent place to take a mixed crowd, as it's upscale, has lots of space, and vegans can find something on the menu as can non-vegans.

I want to take back my negative comment about Gather.  Bite my tongue!  

We've since been back recently, and now that they've been around for a while, everything's changed. Gather is GREAT.  We came in for brunch with our 17-month twin boys and the service was great.  And they were SO sweet with our boys.  Although the brunch is more than you'd pay for your usual spot, the food was super delicious and relatively affordable (for two = $35 pre tax).  I truly LOVE Gather now, especially given how accommodating they were with our babies. We're always looking for family friendly places to eat brunch, and we're so pleased they didn't give us that "snooty-don't-bring-your-kids-here" look.  I'm a total fan and having my breakfast brunch there this week! 

I heart you, Gather!

This might be one of our new favorite special dinner spots. 
Just found out that the chef used to work at Millenium which is another favorite spot of ours, so it makes sense.

The idea is that that menu is local, seasonal, organic. 50% vegetarian options but they definitely serve meat. 

We really enjoyed the service, the food, and our overall experience here. We'll definitely be back. It's a block from the Downtown Berkeley Bart station and very close to the Berkeley Rep Theater.

As you walk up to Gather you will find the exterior very appealing. Looks warm, slick & inviting. Upon entering I immediately liked the ambiance. The pumpkins everywhere & big jars of spices gave the sleek space a hint of a rustic decor. 

Our server was a doll! She was informative, friendly & was gracious enough to split our bills individually (went with a group). The food itself was good. Not eyes roll to the back of my head but good. I had the mushroom scramble with goat cheese bruchetta & fingerling potatoes. The potatoes were pretty bangin! My friend order the brunch pizza. FYI: it is large & can be shared between 3 people. The Hemingway Revolver was my drink of choice & this I enjoyed. I felt the $10 price tag for the drink was a little steep. For 1 person brunch w/ cocktail (including tax & tip) was $30--not what I normally pay for brunch but a nice place nonetheless.

I'm a bit confused about how to rate Gather -- I love that when I need a break from the studenty-ness of Berkeley, it's calm, clean, and I get to feel all hip b/c I usually lower the average age in there by at least 10 years -- and I appreciate the freshness of the produce and overall look of the place, but sometimes my meals just aren't fabulous.

The menu rotates pretty frequently, and since we go fairly often, I've tried most veg options, a few of the pizzas, and a smattering of seafood selections they've offered since opening -- the kale salad remains one of my favorite salads of all time, and oh, the pizzas are pretty lovely -- but many of the veg selections are just "meh", and vegan charcuterie is nothing to write home about, regardless of whatever is on it -- the seafood tends to be solid every time, but the portions are occasionally smaller than I would like

Service is ranges from attentive to absent -- it's a mostly hipstery/pseudo hunky waiterstaff, all of whom are friendly but are clearly of the "I'm an artist, not really a waiter" variety. 

Din for two w/ glasses of wine and no dessert is usually $70ish?

Let's set the scene here. A brisk late Sunday morning in Berkeley.  Reservation? Check. Appetite? Double check. 

We were greeted and seated promptly, near the front of the house.  It was a great area, as the windows allowed for natural light to come through.  You have a selection of still or sparkling water.  As for the brunch menu, choose from pizzas, salads, scrambles, and pancakes.  We finally settled on:

Prather Ranch burger - cheddar, aioli, caramelized shallot-tomato sauce, fries.  Added heirloom tomato, bacon, Little Gems, housemade pickles
Farm egg Pizza - bacon, caramelized onions, herbs

You know you've ordered right when, a) the waitress says, "excellent!" as she's taking your order, and b) the surrounding tables ogle at your dishes (and no, that's not a euphemism). 

A quick look around and it truly seems like a place where people would *gather*. [Like what I did there?]  Families, old friends, new connections, all walks of life.  The hubby commented that this was a nice place and that we should take the rest of the family here.  Why yes, yes we should.

This place is stellar, thus, the 5 stars.  Our group of 4 had stumbled upon this restaurant while we were walking around after having been rejected at a Japanese restaurant nearby.  It was a game night (CAL won, Go Bears!), so all the restaurants were packed.  When I first looked it up on yelp, I saw it had high marks, and that it was "American" food.  When I think of American, I think, okay, your standard seafood fare with some noodles perhaps.  Thus, I came into this experience without any pre-conceived notion that this place was supposed to deliver awesomeness.  Boy did it deliver, and then took me to the market!

Fresh, organic, gastronomical.  Everything was presented well, smelled amazing, tasted delightfully complex.  Although it's a bit pricey, the quality of food is similar to Chez Panisse. so it's well-worth the trip.

Here's a breakdown of what we ordered:
Small Plates:
- Burrata with Linda's tomatoes: the burrata was so smooth, like brie, as expected, but the tomatoes were phenomenal.  I never knew tomatoes could be so full of flavor.
- (off the menu) Albacore in a salad of sorts (I forget the exact name): Small chunks of albacore were scattered within this salad that had super yummy corn and other delightful greens.

Artisanal Plate:
- The Vegan charcuterie: this is a MUST try for any visitor to this restaurant.  Absolutely blew me away.  It's hard to pick a favorite from this wooden plate between the "watermelon steak" paired with the smoked melon, or the eggplant with roasted garlic, to the tofu skins paired in the most perfect way with pepper cashew "cheese" and pickeld peppers.  The skins were so "rich" in flavor that it almost tasted dare I say, meaty!  

Pizzas:
- Marinated Tomales Bay mussels: Again, perfection in a pizza form.  Let's start with the crust.  It's semi-thin crust, but not paper thin like Delfina's pizzeria in SF.  Where there are "bubbles" near the crust, are actually pockets of doughy goodness.  Just the right amount of thinness and doughyness to give you a substantial-feeling pizza.  I think there was some yummy bacon on there too, but the mussels were the star of the show.  I've never had mussels on a pizza before, although I have had clams.  These mussels were so young, fresh, with a hint of saltiness from the bay.  I've had Tomales Bay's mussels raw before, and these were just as good, but cooked to perfection.

Large Plates:
- Barbecued young chicken: The chicken had just the right amount of tasty seasoning and was of coursed cooked to exactly the right amount of time.  It was juicy without being overwhelmingly oily, of which rotisserie chicken from Safeway can be at times.  

Dessert:
- A scoop of their house-made ice cream: chocolate with expresso: SUPER strong expresso flavor for those coffee lovers out there.  Came with a few cookies (chocolate-chip?) on top that were crispy and yummy of course.
- Scarlett Royal grape trifle: the waiter described it as a more upscale version of a fruit parfait.  He was spot on.  The combination of cashew cake, verbana marscarpone whip cream, pine nut brittle was joy in my mouth.  It had a savory taste near the bottom that mixed well with all the fluffy delight on top.  The pine nut brittle was so good.  I've never had a nut brittle other than peanut brittle, and this one, kicks its butt any day of the week.  I also like pine nuts, so I may be biased.


The waiter and hostess were super friendly.  We learned the watier had just come back from Italy, which somehow made the whole experience even more quaint and personal for some reason.  He was very helpful in recommending AMAZING dishes that they're known for, and referred to the chef by first name.  I don't know about these other low-starring reviews on here since they complain about stuff that they ordered while rejecting suggestions from the waiters.  Obviously, the waiters are going to recommend what the restaurant does best at.  It's like this cupcake place in SF...but that's another yelp review...

You must try their vegan charcuterie and mussels pizza, add it to your bucket list!

Yesterday marked my second time at Gather. I came here a over a year ago, not long after they first opened, and been dying to come back for the Farm Egg Pizza.  Although I'd love to give Gather a 5 star Yelp rating, checking in with the hostess is the ultimate reason I'm dropping a star.

I got here a little after 12:30pm yesterday.  My friend and I checked in with the hostess and she said it would be about a 10 minute wait.  Although there were several empty tables which seated 2-4 people, I was fine with that because I assumed they were for reservations.  As we waited, I watched how the hostess seemed to wander back and forth around the restaurant.  Two gentlemen checked in while we were waiting and mentioned they were pressed for time.  The hostess mentioned there were outdoor tables or the bar area they could seat and not wait, why weren't we given that option?  After seating them, I told her that if there was an open table outside, we would be fine to sitting there.  She said okay, but instead of seating us, she once again wandered back and forth around the restaurant.  We thought she would be seating us outside once she got back to the counter, instead she walked away and wandered again.  Five minutes later, she said she had an open table inside, but if we wanted a table outside, it would be another five minutes.  I said sitting inside was fine.  She walked us over to a table that was available the entire time, I see no reason why we were waiting in the first place.  

Note, Gather does occasionally change their menu, so items you've had before may no longer be on the menu.

FARM EGG PIZZA ($15 + $2 adding sausage) 
Yummy!!  I finally tried the farm egg pizza and LOVED it!!  The tomato sauce had a slight sweetness to it with bacon pieces, caramelized onions, and the sausage addition.  I probably wouldn't suggest adding sausage since it didn't seem like much was added.  On top was a runny egg that added a perfect complement to the pizza.  The crust was thin and crunchy, just the way I like it.  The crust edges were a bit burnt though, so I found myself attempting to pick off the burnt areas.  The pizza was a perfect size for both me and my friend to share.

SERVICE:
With the exception of the issue with the hostess, our waitress was great.  A couple minutes into being seated, we were asked if we wanted still or sparkling water.  She checked on us regularly and had a friendly attitude.

I was invited by a colleague to lunch. Great service. Uh, lack luster salads (small), not that inspiring pizza? Jupiter, don't you worry. Pricey for what you get. Salad, small pizza, ice tea (2) $24 +tip? She paid, however, too much for what we got. Still a nice serving crew. You should working at Chez Panisse.

Otherwise... Back to The Faculty Club or Top Dog or Arnell's. Don't expect me back.

We had a fantastic meal here Saturday night and it *would* have been really reasonably priced if we hadn't been such piggies. 

The Vegan Charcuterie is really something special. I am afraid of most items that are described as "vegan," but this was something else. The flavors were unusual in an exciting, delicious way - not unusual in a scary vegan way. 

Other favorite items: the polenta-encrusted mushrooms, Monterey Bay squid with black rice, and the mushroom pizza. 

Service was prompt and friendly. Wine list had a good assortment of wines and prices. Everything was divine. 

I can't wait to go back.

Gather the Girls
Gather the funds
Gather the appetites
Gather the fun!
Gather everyone!

This is a great place to do it. It's loud, it's crowded and the servers are...well...very Berkeley - but the food is tops.

Inspired flavors are infused into each seasonal pizza, like squash and zucchini with a bright tomato base. Or the pork jowell and corn pizza with jalapeno. The crust is truly unique with pinched off sections - not unlike a pie crust, so as to create a sort of string of beads-like appearance, giving you thin and crunchy right alongside bubbly and chewy. It's like two crusts in one.

Salads are fresh and vibrant with crisp greens, mine was topped with more zucchini and shaved parmesan. 

I took my favorite Blond Bombshell here for her birthday and brought my own dessert as a present, a little wary that we may be charged a fee, as we have been before at a place that shall not be named, but it certainly wasn't after the biggest planet in our universe just down the road a piece...but not only were we allowed to enjoy fully, the server was super great and brought us plates and everything.

The food is great, the atmosphere is alive and the service attentive and knowledgeable - which, let's face it, you're going to need with some of the ingredients on that menu...All in all, a great place to, well - Gather!

For a flickering moment, I enjoyed the company of The Luddite, who generously treated me to a provocative but amusing dinner at Gather.  

We began with the requisite vegan charcuterie, which certainly lived up to the buzz more than I ever could.  Whatever was unexpectedly lacking that evening was rectified with the amazing halibut crudo, with its bits of avocado, beet and cucumber in shimmering coriander oil.  Excellent!

We cheerfully elected to split two of the three specials that evening, a respectable seared sea bass and the lovely braised lamb.  Both were more than upright in execution, although not overly inventive.  But that's okay--sometimes people are slow to warm, and indeed I found myself later wishing for another tender bite that interesting night, which ultimately ended with a [peach] crumble.

I came to Gather for brunch around 11am today, Oct 23rd, famished after running a 10K race in Oakland. I attempted to order the Winter vegetable scramble with egg whites, only to be taken aback when the waitress told me that the chef wouldn't do it because he had no other use for the yolks and didn't want to waste any food.

I was too hungry to protest at the time, but - really? I consider his response arrogant, high-handed, and completely lacking in consideration for customers - not to mention surprisingly ignorant of the many uses of egg yolks, such as custard and ice cream. 

To add insult to injury, the eggs (yes, with yolks) were bland, overly greasy, and with barely a sprinkling of vegetables. This was my last visit to Gather. Luckily Saturn Cafe across the street is tastier yet cheaper, so, after I post this review, I will not have to think about Gather ever again.

Incidentally, what does the chef do with guests who don't finish their portions? Run after them with a knife and forcibly stuff the leftovers down their throat?

Only in Berkeley can you have the highest end decor, yet dine with people in sweats and flip flops.

Only in Berkeley does you server have such an intimate knowledge of every possible eating restriction that you are not quite sure what he just said.

Only in Berkley can you charge $16 for about $0.30 of veggies with some foam.  Is it worth it?  My tastebuds say "Yes!" my pocket book and rumblely tummy say "Not so much."   

Only in Berkeley will you wait 1 hour 15 minutes to get your hands on that $0.30 of veggies.


Only In Berkley do they butcher their own black pig/wild boar cross to make a perfectly done habanero sausage.


Overall I liked this place but felt a little over charged.   The only thing we ordered that could fill you up  was an artisan burger and home made fries with two homemade dips: caramelized onion and vaguely flavored aoli.  It was good, but nothing to write home about.

If you like a place where you can blend in with the woodwork and not be bothered by the servers, then Gather is the place for you. The service was lousy for a place that charges this much. This was one of the few times when I wished that the servers were more like the ones at Cafe Gratitude. I had to ask the bussers several times to get the server to come to our table.

The food is worth it if you order the unusual dishes that you can't get elsewhere. The albacore starter was decent. Everything worked well, the beans, the tuna, and the bitter greens. Nice stable dish.

The heirloom eggplant with beluga lentils was also pretty good. The fried garbanzo beans added a nice touch to the fire roasted green beans. This is not a dish you're going to be able to find elsewhere.

A lot of people were eating pizzas. We didn't order one, but they look very hearty and for the money are probably a good deal.

Since the service is so lackluster, I would never come here for the chicken, pork chop, burger, etc. In addition, I wasn't thrilled with the atmosphere. It's hard to hear yourself with the loud acoustics in the room. You practically have to shout to hear what the other person is saying. Also, while the decor looks warm and inviting at first, after awhile, it starts to look cold and trendy.

In short, if you want some interesting dishes like the ones we had, it might be worth putting up with the bad service. However, if you want to come here for dishes you can get at almost any other comparable place, you're wasting your time and money.

Oh, Berkeley, I feel like I hardly know you now? What happened to the grungy, dirty, bohemian, punkster that I knew when I was an undergrad? In the last few years, you've become this sleek, hipster, organically and environmentally conscientious debutante. 

I remember when Chez Panisse was our only choice if we wanted a nice dinner out (I know, I know, cry me a river that I lived down the street from Chez Panisse). So here is Gather. Gather is everything that is Berkeley and not Berkeley at the same time.

Gather is the result of the latest craze in organic, environmentally friendly, and locavore cuisine with a dash of molecular gastronomy. Although it's not a vegetarian/vegan restaurant, it might as well be as meat is a bit of an afterthought. Not a bad afterthought, oh, no as everything is exquisitely made, but it's simply not a focus. This is haute cuisine that happens to focus on vegetables.

We started off with yuba (tofu skin) pappardelle, roasted beets, and vegan "charcuterie." The pappardelle completely fooled us as they look exactly like pasta. It was absolutely delicious. No detail is left unturned as even the bread crumbs on the roasted beets were incredible. Long after the beets were eaten, we returned to the platter to pick up the little nibbles of bread crumbs. The vegan "charcuterie" was amazing. We happened to sit near the entrance and people gasped in amazement when they walked in when they saw our charcuterie. One girl exclaimed, "I don't know what it is, but that looks fantastic. I'm getting that!"

The charcuterie was an assortment of various little bites -- mushrooms, potatoes, sprouted lentils, etc, but they were carefully crafted into little works of art. I honestly wish that I had taken a picture, but we devoured it so quickly. No words can describe this. Honestly sprouted lentils don't sounds delicious, but they made it into like a pate and it was my favorite thing on the plate. Do make sure you order this when you come to gather.

For my entree, I ordered the PORK BELLY PIZZA. I know my pork loving friends are drooling over this. A thin crust pizza with a smear of tomato sauce, a bit of mozzarella, a generous layer of roasted corn kernels, a handful of sliced jalapenos, and cubes of pork belly dotting the pizza. Delicious! 

I was also a fan of their squash blossom pizza. They managed to not hide the delicate essence of the blossoms while cooking the pizza. I really miss squash blossoms. They're so abundant and easily found in CA, but rarely found in the restaurants of NY. Sad really.

A beautiful wide open space, with lots of wood in the interior. Berkeley has definitely grown up some.

What I liked:
The pisco sour was well made with a good foamy egg head.  The service was nice (even though he forgot to bring me bread).  I liked the kale salad and my pork chops were very tasty.  Despite Opentable saying they didn't have space, a phone call to them got me a reservation for my sister's birthday.  They returned with some very professional voicemails confirming the reservation.  

What I didn't like:
For the entire 2+ hour meal, watching the guy making desserts licking his fingers and garnishing the dessert plates and eating every other garnish / piece of fruit he was touching.  That's disgusting.  Despite it being a birthday, we opted out of dessert.

I could go on and on but this review is for one thing only, the "Vegan Charcuterie".. without a doubt one of the best combination's of vegetables I have ever eaten. The preparation is thoughtful and pure, smart and elegant. 
Charcuterie typically refers to different cured cuts of pork, so obviously this is only a fun play on words. "an assortment"..

There are so many different flavor profiles and textures on the board. and with all that is going on it somehow fit together. Trust me, it's extremely hard to walk that tight rope. Culinary magic or disaster.
here here are a few items I sampled;
 
-Fried tofu skin bruschetta, avocado, spicy baby fennel escabeche
-grilled chicory with white bean puree= bitter and creamy
-grilled asparagus with English shelling peas and spring garlic, "aioli"
-fava bean puree on toast= better than hummus by a long shot


In the meat world, here are some things that I would compare it to. and only as  measuring stick, NOT a replacement. Just to give you a sense of mouth feel and pleasure. 

#1 + yellow tail sashimi
super fresh sea urchin
butter poached scallops
duck confit
slow cooked pork belly
smoked short ribs

ok so you get the picture. the dish is ridiculously good. it's proof that you can skip meat and be extremely satisfied. as a card carrying meat eater this dish has my vote any day of the week!

Why didn't veggies taste like this when I was a kid? I'd sure have eaten a lot more of them for sure. My first revelation of this style of  creativity was when Jeremy Fox opened Ubuntu in Napa. I've since been chasing him around his various pop up gigs, Atelier Crenn, Saison, and soon Orson. I've now found a similar ethos in Sean Baker at Gather. I had heard good things about him but when John Mariani gave him kudos (as he did to Dominique Crenn of Atelier) I knew I had to try it. I dragged but finally made it. 

As a college student I walked by this corner of Allston and Oxford many a time but it'd been a while and the new fancy construction that has transformed the area was unrecognizable. The same thing was felt by my friend who spent the undergrad years walking by here as well. A much larger space that spreads a corner of the block and has a large patio to boot. Being a nice evening we ate outside and started off with a beer and a Moscow Mule from the interesting beverage program. After perusing the menu we went with:

-Salad of squid, its ink, roasted peppers, paprika
-Vegan charcuterie:
  grilled Japanese eggplant, Tuscan eggplant puree
  pulled mushroom bruschetta, vegetable slaw
  crispy tapioca, horseradish, avocado, tomato cucumber
  summer vegetables, tonnato sauce
-BBQ pork shoulder pizza, corn, basil, bacon, crème fraiche
-Toasted masa garginelli, chorizo, Poblanos, corn, cilantro, San Marzano
-Goat cheese semifreddo

Wow. Chef Baker has some mad skill. Getting the ingredients from our server on the tonnato sauce alone was impressive. Somehow the kitchen has managed to make a sauce traditionally made with tuna and anchovies into a meat free,super tasty likeness. It's genius I tell you. The combinations of seasoning, textures, and cooking techniques on everything was fantastic. Absolutely fantastic. 

Our server took good care of us and was affable yet soft spoken. Being outside on a temperate night was a treat though it seems there's great energy inside where you can look at the line through the semi open kitchen. As Berkeley's new food renaissance continues, the hits keep coming. I'm convinced this is worth seeking out if you love food and are visiting the east bay to do so.

If you've read a lot of my reviews, you will know that I am a recent convert to the church of Michael Pollan.  As much as I can, I try to make smart choices about the food that I consume, making sure they are locally sourced, vegetarian fed, antibiotic/hormone free, etc ... you get the deal.  Eating at Gather was no exception.  

Made reservations through OpenTable for Sunday brunch with a few friends.  They serve all your usual brunch fare but with a nice locally sourced twist.  I have to say - this was some of the best tasting food I've had in awhile.  The decor is tastefully done modern and deserves a mention.  The space is surprisingly large (but I guess that's because I'm so used to our size of a closet San Francisco restaurants - East Bay, you're awesome).  

Restaurants are worth 4 or 5 stars to me in all kinds of dimensions but if the only dimension that counted was food this would be deserving of all 5 stars I'm giving it.  Among the 3 of us, we shared the Kale "Caesar", a side of potatoes, and their Boar Sausage pizza.  The "caesar" here is not your typical caesar salad, it's really more interpretive (and therefore tastes nothing like it).  But I don't usually like Caesar salad and I loooved this.  The potatoes were great but let's face it - they're potatoes, who doesn't like them?  The boar sausage pizza was probably the highlight of the meal - not greasy or heavy like most pizzas leave me feeling.  All in all, this place makes tasty, "clean" food (a la Cafe Gratitude except with meat).  You'll leave feeling good about yourself and the world after eating here.  I would come back here in a heartbeat next time I'm in the East Bay.

If I didn't live on a budget I could give them 5 stars.

Was meeting an out-of-town friend for dinner and she suggested tjhis new place she heard about. Gather.  I peaked at their menu and saw they have vegan pizza and it was all I could think about so I ordered it.

I LOVE pizza.  Pizza has been one of my biggest regrets of having to go vegan-esque for health reasons.  Their vegan pizzas is AMAZING.  So it's $16 for a personal pizza.  It is practically the cheapest thing on the menu.  But the crust...so yummy crunchy on the outside and light and airy ont he inside and balled up like rolls surrounding the amazing veggies and cashew sauce.  The cashew sauce adds the creaminess missing from a cheese-less pizza so I didn't miss the cheese.  It was the best vegan pizza I have had.  

Fair warning, though, three of us dined, we had a total of 2 drinks and the bill was $100!  This is NOT economical eating.  It is a good shi-shi foodie destination as their food is art and they source local organic ingredients, but it is in berkeley so you can be sure the other guests will put on some sort of floor show for you.  We had a great children's b-day pasrty drama going on around us that was entertaining in so man y atypical ways for a kids party.  Don't worry, though, the kids were perfectly well behaved.

You must go to the bathroom.  It's a bit on the far side,.

Gather, you continue to impress this college kid conditioned-to-Asian Ghetto-takeout palate time and time again.. Kudos!  

I'm literally typing this with a big fat silly smile plastered across my face, despite the total approximately 15 hours of sleep I've gotten all week and the final exam that I quite possibly bombed today... because good dining experiences literally make me that happy. 

Almost everything about my end-of-semester celebratory meal tonight was immaculate.  

The wait time was reportedly an hour and fifteen minutes and we were seated promptly within nearly twenty.   

The food -a requisite order of the vegan charcuterie, seared squid and crispy brussels sprouts starters, a pork belly sausage pizza, and an excellent barbeque young chicken to share -- were all nothing short of spectacular.  (Only thing is I wasn't a huge fan of the brussels sprouts, which just seemed a little like burnt fried onions to me..)  How on earth does the chef do what it does with the charcuterie?  There's nothing like some delicious innovatively prepared vegetables to excite a group of hungry girls at dinnertime. 

Our server, Damon, was also extremely helpful, attentive, and attractive (don't be frontin' and pretend like that's not important sometimes, ladies!).  We had some wheat allergies in our group and Damon was more than happy to accommodate us by asking the chef to make some simple alterations to our dishes.  And because we were rushed out towards the end of our meal at 8:45 due to an incoming reserved party, he even prepared some to-go boxes of dessert cookies (and gluten-free goodies) for us!  Hats off, Damon -- you've got some serious boss status going for you! :)

Ambience, as always, was fantastically relaxing, and the service (!!!!) is just unparalleled at Gather. I am increasingly impressed each time I come here with how friendly and attentive, yet professional everyone who works at Gather seems to be.  

Thank you for the best end-of-semester meal I could have ever asked for, Gather!  I'm still smiling for real.  Seriously excited and still waiting to return here to try out your brunch dishes/mimosas.  Next time!

(P.S. shout out to the kick ass server who screwed up by giving us someone else's order of roasted squash pizza topped with a heap of delicious arugula... it was IMMENSELY enjoyed by our party, heh. The arugula topping works surprisingly well as what I thought was a good addition to the relatively neutral flavors in the pizza.  So thanks! haha :)

I have been following the opening of this restaurant for months and had extremely high expectations when I went to the pre-opening dinner.

In short, I was blown away.  The decor is fabulous, that is obvious.  It was the food that shocked me.  A meal at Gather is in line with the top gourmet, foodie restaurants in San Francisco.  The quality of the ingredients is top notch.  The flavor combinations are tantalizing.  The portion size is filling but small enough to leave you just wanting a little more.  The cocktails are perfectly balanced and not too sweet, they are dangerously good.

The one thing though that sets this restaurant apart from the rest is the price point and the casual atmosphere.  Where else can you get a culinary experience of this caliber and walk out satisfied for under $30?  

Well worth the trip.

The first impression is very pleasant right when you walk in the door. This is a beautiful restaurant! Lots of windows , light , and art throughout. I was there for brunch with my family. We met up at the bar as our group was meeting from a few distant places. We ordered drinks and then our table was ready so the drinks were brought to the table...no problem. We were offered two types of water- filtered and sparkling. I like that they left us a carafe of water for our party of five. We must have tried every drink on the brunch menu and several beers on tap. They have many interesting choices and every drink and brew was tasty,  The brunch menu has some innovative dishes. I ordered cannelini bean soup and a strawberry kumquat salad. Both were very delicious!  I want to try a pizza next time because everyone around us had one and they looked wonderful. My daughter had eggs benedict and braised lentils...delish!  I was pleasantly surprised with a birthday cake... it had chocolate and carmel..my 2 favorites! Very nice presentation on that as well. I love this place for creativity on the menu, efficient and friendly servers,  and the bright atmosphere. The open air kitchen had many busy but pleasant people working together to get the food out.

5 of us had a company lunch there last week: a manager's meeting. All five of us were impressed. They serve delicious food made from fresh seasonal ingredients, with a fabulous selection for carnivores and vegans alike. Think Portland young urban feel and Alice Waters etherial fare. From my pizza with the most fabulous pie crust, to the beet salad, to my husband's tuna sandwich, to the semifredde dessert with the crunchy things. I can't wait to go back!

My new favorite restaurant!!!  Today is a good day, not just because it's CNY but because I discovered this place.  

Had lunch here and I heard dinner is even better! is that even possible?

We Had:

CARROT COOKED IN HAY:  I don't know how many people will think this might sound appealing on the menu, i sure didn't but thought to give it a try anyway since it's different.  Boy was I glad!!  There's so many thoughts about this particular dish i don't now where to start and if I can ever even end.  So I won't say much more than to ABSOLUTELY TRY THIS ONE and end it here.

PORK BELLY SANDWICH:   they ran out of pork shoulder ... good because this one is fabulous!!!  I'm not a fan of pork belly or pork in general but this one sure makes me feel guilty of loving it since I want a pet pig.  As I was eating this sandwich, I didn't want the feeling to end, I even tried to order another one to-go but too bad they closed the kitchen.  I hope that the next time I'm here, they ran out of pork shoulder just so I can savor it all over again and make sure to order another one ahead to-go.

SHEEP'S MILK RICOTTA PIZZA:  very light and good.  Too bad the other two dish stole the show from this pizza.


I am absolutely coming back time and time and time again.

We got in late after seeing the Harlem Globetrotters and I was  famished... We got some deep fried veg, the mushroom bruschetta, and the potato salad.  Nothing was stunning, and walking out $60 lighter for three apps, a beer and a ginger ale, I was kinda bummed. 
I don't think that people should be jacked for local food- if it was brought in from GuanXi province personally in a handcuffed briefcase- ok - charge me for that. But this stuff is local and simple, right? 
I guess they gotta pay for that big new building somehow...

I was won over the minute we were presented with a jug of sparkling and flat water upon being seated-- I am such a sucker for free sparkling water! I ordered the walnut french toast which was out-of-the-park delicious. Everyone at our table loved their meal, including the three-year-old we brought along who sang with joy when he tasted this pancakes. Definitely make a reservation or you may be turned away, especially at peak hours (it happened to us the first time we tried to eat here).

Came in without a reservation around 6pm on Friday afternoon, and was directed to a communal table outside on the patio.  The day seemed warm enough to eat outside, so we went that route.  The patio was very nice and I really enjoyed the reclaimed wood tables.  Ordered a couple of drinks (Square One Cucumber vodka and soda for me, Gin-n-Root cocktail for my partner) and perused the menu.  Cocktails were good and we enjoyed while we decided between the vegan charcuterie and a pizza combo or a couple of the large plate traditional entrees.  Most of the pizza combinations sounded a bit off, and there didn't seem to be a standard tomato/basil or margarita option, so we opted for a burger and the seared chickpea cake.  Both were good, and when our server came to check on us we ordered a second drink.  

This is where things started to go a bit wrong. The next round of drinks took about 10 - 15 minutes to come out, which wasn't ideal since we had finished our entrees a while back.  A different server dropped off a dessert menu and we exacerbated our problem by ordering coffee to warm up as the sun was now starting to go down and the patio was getting quite cold.  We realized our mistake when the coffees took another *17* minutes to come out (not an exaggeration or estimate, I timed it!)  When the coffee finally arrived we asked our server for the check and booked it out of there.  

Bottom line, nice idea, comfortable decor, interesting and tasty food but very uneven service.  The restaurant was fairly full, but the wait for drinks was beyond acceptable.  I am not really sure what happened, but would not go back just for this reason.

I often imagine Vegan restaurants to some sort of cult followers worshiping the god of vegetables and trying to banish all meat eating evilness from the world. Excuse my silliness. In all honesty, I do enjoy good vegan food even though I can't quite agree with the ideals of vegans.

Here in Gather was where I had the first (but not the last) pure vegan dinner that rivals some hearty meaty meal. I did not feel unsatisfied in any way just because I was having pure vegetables. That alone, was amazing. Just try their Vegan Charcuterie and you will understand what I mean.

While Gather might not have converted my meat eating habits, I truly enjoyed my experience and it had introduced me to the wonderful world of vegan cooking. Working with limited ingredients was challenging but fun.

So, I ate at Gather last night, the first night they opened--and not a moment too soon! Between our table of 4, we tried 3 small plates, 4 big plates, 2 desserts, and 3 different cocktails. All of them were phenomenal. And I'm not just saying that--I'm way picky about food, and there wasn't a single dish I wished were even a little different.

For me, the standouts were the goat cheese panna cotta dessert (really unusual, light, not the kind of custardy dessert you usually get from panna cotta); the pork cheeks (sweet, succulent, perfectly textured and flavored); the burger.
Let me give the burger an extra moment here: it wasn't my burger, it was my friend's. Usually, I don't taste other people's burgers, because they're usually not that good, they're just reminiscent of what I want a burger to be like. But with this one, I eased into trying it by having some fries from his plate (always a good idea--these are fantastic fries!). Then, after a while, I had a bite of his burger. If that were a sexual innuendo, it would still be appropriate here--it's THAT good. You should have one. And give me a bite.
Veggies veggies veggies + cocktails.  What a great menu.

Looking for a nice, Vegan friendly restaurant in the East Bay to celebrate my sweetie's completion of her 30 day Vegan Challenge. I wanted something that would be impressive enough to make her want to continue on being Vegan as well show her that Vegans do it better. Gather comes highly recommended from other Vegan folks, as well as fellow Yelpers.

I made reservations for us but since we were dining with the old folks at 6pm it probably wasn't necessary. We felt a bit young for this crowd. Especially considering it's proximity to UC Berkeley. Then again, maybe the prices scare away the kids. Why would a kid take their date here when you can take them to a bar or to get pizza where the end result will be the same? A one-way ticket to Poundtown... 

Of course, me being a classy Gent, I can appreciate the gorgeous, rustic design of this place. There is plenty of window seating for couples but nothing really private. It's a lot more casual than I was expecting. This coming from a guy that thought Havana was a fancy place... http://www.yelp.com/biz/havana-walnut-creek The wait service is on top of their game here. Our carafe of water stayed full throughout our meal while there was a waiter almost constantly in the vicinity. There were even what seemed like three hosts greeting you at the front door.

Once we figured out how to work around the awkwardness of having to be seated across from each other, we were ready to order. There are not as many Vegan options on the menu as I was envisioning. We picked out what we thought looked like the best ones...

The Vegan Charcuterie is a must order. Whether you're Vegan or not. Four seasonally delicious small bites, spread out on a tray. Okay, make that three since the piece with the Trumpet Mushrooms was barely edible. Although since it's seasonal, it may not be on the menu when you go here, the Mushroom Tartare was my favorite out of the four dainty bites. 

The Summer Vegetables w/Avocado, Whipped Tofu, "Caviar", and Sea Palm Vinaigrette was my favorite dish of the meal. Too bad it's so small and pretty it vanished in no time. I think it was the Caviar type goo that added a touch of saltiness that went exquisitely with the Avocado. So good!

The Tomato Pizza with Capers, and Cashew Puree was a fantastic way to make a Vegan pizza without really trying to simulate cheese. There is just enough of the Cashew Puree to add flavor without globbing it on like it's Velveeta Cheese on your ballpark nachos. Although I'm not really a thin crust fan, it worked well in this case. The Chili Oil added a bit of a kick and lots of flavor.

Knowing that my girl needs her dessert fix, I was excited to order the Hazelnut Chocolate Cake for her and a Cappuccino to share. It wasn't a slice of cake as we were expecting, but rather a small hockey puck sized brownie that was all dolled up with drizzles and shavings galore. The hint of orange in the cake was what won me over. It went perfectly with that Cappuccino.

I think I could safely recommend this place to anyone looking to try out something different. They have a lil' something for everyone. They even let us lowly Vegans pretend that we're eating those small, yet artfully prepared dishes you normally see in fancy French restaurants. Heck, they even made a Vegan for life. I'm happy to affirm that my love's 30 day challenge has become permanent several months later, and is getting better and better with each passing day...

So, I was ready to hate Gather.  It has all the trappings of a restaurant I'd hate: their menu's obsessive orientation toward vegetarianism, their uniformly young staff, only organic mixers in the bar (OCD much?), and their apparent respect for that most nouveaux of food trends, the gluten free diner.  Pardon my tangent, but gluten free is just Atkins for hipsters.  Of the people you know who order gluten free, how many of them have had a biopsy to confirm celiac sprue?  Yeah, I thought so.  Right, so back to Gather.  In amongst all this new-food style there's a lot of substance -- a whole animal philosophy, a strong preference for local goods, and most importantly, really good food -- and I guess that's what got me through the door in the first place.  

And I'm glad I did.  I've had tons of food at Gather: pork belly sandwich, burgers, chickens, several salads, vegan charcuterie, quite a few drinks, soups, pizzas, several apps.  The worst thing I've had at Gather was still worth the money.  The best things I've had there are phenomenal.  Barbecue chicken is so moist within its crispy savory shell that it's almost hard to fathom.  Kale caesar exhibits a depth of flavor that's rare in vegan cooking.  Moist grass-fed burgers with Sierra Nevada cheddar and smokey caramelized shallot ketchup are a consistent winner.  Even the lowly mixed green salad becomes a work of nearly astounding passion, dotted with grapefruit peel prepared in a puree with saffron oil, with preserved fennel stocks and a little smashed olive tossed into the freshest, tenderest baby greens.  

I've been to a lot of high-end restaurants where the menu says 'organic,' but the ethos is far nearer to 'organic when it's convenient;'  Even if I find Gather's militant commitment to its philosophy off-putting, I have to respect the sheer totality of their execution.  

ps.  Don't listen to cynthia.  Browsing her other reviews, it appears that she's seldom found a fine-dining service that has met her expectations.  One bad service experience shouldn't overwrite an otherwise solid track-record of quality meals.

Ahhh, Gather. We first met at the Yelp Helps event right next door and you hold so much promise. 

Definitely a restaurant that characterizes Berkeley: Hip, sustainable, and, unfortunately, a bit overpriced. 

My former anatomy classmate treated me here on my suggestion last Wednesday (thanks so much, Yuri!) for the rides I gave to her back to Rockridge and depriving her of the pleasure of hour commute back on the bus. 

The "chicken fried" red kabocha squash. Kabocha in Japanese means pumpkin FYI. Quite tasty dish with kabocha quality found in Japanese restaurant. Itself is fried and no actual chicken were used for the actual dish (hence the quotations). Good but worth $19? 

My friend got pork pizza which consisted of sausage, pancetta, and braised pig skin, lard. The crust was very unique in that in look very much like the Cheesy Bite Pizza from Pizza Hut, only with no cheese in the actual crust and much better tasting. $18 is the tag for this piece of pie. PIzza is one of the most popular dishes here as I've seen at least 60% tables having at least one. 

In short, sustainable potential (yes, pun intended) and worth a second try!

My favorite Vegetarian is in town from New York so I decided that we should go to the very veggie friendly (and much hyped) Gather for dinner. As luck would have it, she got stuck at work and couldn't make it...would the two remaining meat eating dudes panic and chicken out? Nah, see, the beauty of Gather is that they have vegan and veggie dishes on the menu right next to meaty options.

I got there a little early and bellied up to the bar to wait for my friend. While there I imbibed a delicious Sidecar, had a taste of an Owen Roe Syrah (Ex Umbris) that I had never heard of before courtesy of the ever so sweet Michelle and met the infamous Bee-Rye himself. 

While service at the bar was fantastic, our waiter was kind of all over the map. He did offer great suggestions...when we could find him. He literally disappeared for 15-20 minutes a couple of times during service.

Between two of us we split the following: 
-Grilled squid: chickpea tahini puree, olive, corno di capro, parsley oil $12
