-Roasted young beets: horseradish-goat cheese cream, mustards, watermelon radish, Etude $12
-Pizza w/pulled pork, bacon, brussel sprouts, Burrata $19

The grilled squid was perfectly cooked and probably my favorite taste of the night. I absolutely loved the crust on the pizza but I'm about to utter words that you'll never, ever hear come out of my mouth again - it suffered from too much pork! The pulled pork flavor overwhelmed everything else on the pie and if you're going to add burrata to a pizza, you might as well be able to taste it. And the beets were fine but nothing special.

A solid four star experience. Prices seem a buck or two high across the board but I'm ok paying that for quality, local ingredients. Hopefully the next time my favorite Vegetarian is in town we'll be able to dine at Gather together....as long as she doesn't mind that I'm getting the burger!

What can I say about Gather that I am willing to type out painstakingly on a touchscreen? Quite a lot, actually. 

Happenstance.  

I was driving aimlessly around downtown Berkeley looking for a parking spot. Once I was parked, I crossed the street and looked for the first restaurant that appealed to me. Although I looked haggard and was weighted down by a huge backpack, they were quite friendly to me and offered me several seating choices. I asked the hostess to surprise me. She considerately seated me at the counter in front of the kitchen, where I had an excellent view of the cooking and plating process. 

Soon thereafter, the most gorgeous server came over and handed me a menu, then offered me the choice of distilled or sparkling water, contained in Strauss milk bottles. Quaint. 

The menu is small, but there are many choices for those who are eating vegan, gluten free, or want their meat. The menu is very clearly labeled, which I appreciate. 

When it came time to order, I went with the king salmon tartare and asked my server to pick my entree. He suggested the Magruder ranch pork loin and belly. 

The salmon tartare came out plates beautifully. I watched 3 people gathered around my plate in the kitchen just moments prior to its arrival to my table, so I got to see how carefully they presented and considered the placement of every little bit. Their attention to detail showed not only in its presentation, but in the intricate balance of favors. I eat a lot of sashimi and various forms of poke, carpaccio, tartare, etc., and I was pleasantly surprised at how well my appetizer came out. The fish was at the right temperature, not frozen, but not lukewarm. They delicately seasoned every bit that touched the plate, including the cucumber slices and tomatoes. The goat cheese and the fresh herbs and seasonings really complimented the salmon quite well. I believe that the attention to detail in this dish is what makes it better than normal. 

I was offered bread twice. The first was when my appetizer came out, and the second, when my entree was served. I declined on both instances, so I have no comment on the bread that other yelpers seem to feel strongly about. 

My pork came out after an appropriate digestive interlude and I dug right in. I'm normally not a fan of legumes, yet this dish was once again balanced thoughtfully. There was a nice salad of shell beans and sweet white corn with a few porcini mushrooms in the mix. I'm also quite particular about how I enjoy my pork, since I am in the habit of eating it Asian style, and I found that I enjoyed Gather's take on it. Although there was both pork loin and belly, the meat was quite rich and required the legumes for balance. I was impressed with how they made 2 pieces of meat and a scoop of beans look so elegant on a plate. 

As I was eating, I was watching their prep chef meticulously slice tiny tomatoes delicately with his big meaty hands. 

I also watched them prepare the vegan charcuterie and the sardines and it made me wish I could eat more. The visual aspects of their plating is attractive to the eye, complimenting their delicate ingredients. 

For dessert, I went with the sorbet. I believe it was plum and cardamom. 

The dinner crowd picked up while I was eating and gradually it got noisier and more crowded. The service was impeccable the entire night, and I never felt neglected. 

The food speaks for itself, but will set you back more than your usual dinner plans would. A 3 course meal with no drinks, tax and tip will rob your wallet of around 45-55 dollars per person, unless you are sharing one appetizer and one dessert course. 

It is also worth mentioning that their bathroom is currently broken, so you have to go on a crazy adventure that involves a maze and two different keys before you reach your destination. You have been warned.

Yelp Challenge 365 # 112/365

Busy place but they are timely. Kudos to the management and staff. Don't go there without a reserveration unless you're prepared to dine on the bar or infront along the chef's counter. Frankly, I would enjoy either the bar or the chef's counter but my host did the right thing getting a reservation. They were crowded. Each seat was taken from the time I got there to the time we left.

The menu was short and desireable. Wild boar meatball! Fritto Misto with mushroom! Magruder Roast Pork Terrine! Cauliflower Soup! Smoked Artichoke with black rice, pumpkin and a chestnut confit! 

Vegan Charcuterie- a 4 course combination: Black Trumpet with pnenuts, Carrot roasted in soil, Stinging nettles which is Martin's baby potatoes, goat cheese and leeks, Fontinella which is mozzarella and tomatoes laced with olive oil and sea salt.
I didn't have this but it looked good.

I'm a meat type person and the closest I got to was the Liberty Farms Duck prepared with hedgehog mushrooms, turnips and horseradish.

ALL local grown ingredients (not sure about the wild boar) but the vegetables were definitely just picked from the garden.

If not for the simple fact that I enjoy my meat more than veggies, I'd give this place 5 stars but ..... 

Service was absolutely wonderful and efficient and that in itself is a reason why I may go back again if the oppoortunity presents itself.

BTW, a block from the BART station so you could take the BART. Parking is a problem in that area as it is smack at the entrance to one of UC's finest!

The menu said "Roasted Sardines," so I of less-than-well-rounded palate, whose entire sardine dining experience to that point was strictly of the out-of-the-tin variety, selected that item. 

I did not have to hesitate and inquire further about the ingredients as I usually have to do.. (me being Celiac and intolerant of flour and other wheat gluten containing foodstuffs) because that menu item, along with many other items on the menu was helpfully labeled "gf" (gluten-free).  Love and kisses and big points from me for that.

Our waiter was very attentive, helpful, and knowledgeable. The sardines are fished from the waters off Monterrey, where they were historically fished in large numbers. They go on and off the restaurant's menu in accordance with the specie's endangered/not endangered status.. which changes frequently.. not so much because their absolute numbers are low .. but because, sardines being lower on the food chain, their numbers also have to be high enough to allow the bigger fish that prey on them to flourish ... complicated stuff.

Anyway, as he presented the plate, he cautioned me about being careful about the little bones.. Huh? I forked one and chewed with a certain amount of caution.. then shrugged and just chomped the whole guy down, tail, head, little bones and all.. I mean that's how you eat'em I think.. right? Before I dug into them.. I took a picture for your benefit.

Oh.. roasted sardines are quite tasty.. I think I'm gonna have to go to the cookbooks and look up how to do the roasting myself.. Either that or come back here when the little guys are off the endangered fish list and thus back on the Gather menu..

Gather needs no explanation. sat at the bar, noticed lots of new wave cocktails. skipped since it was early.

eats: prather ranch hamburger, medium rare (14)w/sierra nevada cheddar
-lots of crispy shoestring potatoes with mystery aioli 
-clump of spring mix lightly vinegaretted
-burger was reddish med rare, not much juice, probably low fat content.
-meat tender, not chewy
3.5 stars

drink: thanksgiving coffee(3.25)
-rich and bold, nice!

foodnotes:
-service very good
-burger not the star here, darn it!

Good concept!
Good location!
Good intention!
Good ingredients!
Good Green!!

It's not "vegetarian"!!  It's vegetarian "FRIENDLY", hippies!!!!

I was going to give it a 3-star when I was dining there w/Seb and RoMo.  But a week later, most of the meal was quite forgetful except the BAD part.

The waiter asked if we wanted still or sparkling water and explained that they filtered the water in-house.  Cool.  We said still.  He asked again to re-confirm before he walked away...  And what brought to the table was sparkling!!

Food tasted A-OK, really!
Braised Lamb was way too overpriced for 2 super mini medallion size!
Vegan Charcuterie was good but forgetful.
Regular Charcuterie was good, any salty pig bits are good!
Monterey Bay Squid was fine.
Fish was okay, my first bite (alone w/o sauces) reminded me of fillet-o-fish for some reason but then it was fine afterwards.
Seb's pizza was SAD!!!  It's a lot harder and chewy than we would like it to.  You can see the cut side of the dough was dense!  His jaws were sore towards his slice of it...

I'll let the dust settle for a loooong while before returning for another shot but till then, it's a solid 2 stars!  Price is not very friendly for a college town for local customers.  There are a lot better food around for a lot cheaper!  They better step it up a notch!  If I lived around there, I'd rather have pizzas at Jupiter or Lo Cocos.  It sure cannot be more than 3-star!!!  I wonder what do the ones who rated this place 5-star usually eats and what their standards are!!  Sheesh!!

Gather is kind of like "Babette's Feast" before the arrival of Babette.  They sure try hard, and everything they serve is local, organic and loved.  But there's something antiseptic and serious about the place -- there's no playfulness when you walk in.  Are the chairs too hard and straight?  The lights too bright?  It's hard to put a finger on what was wrong, but I didn't really have a good time.

My first course (a crab salad special) was excellent.  My second course, the special pork soup, was really "meh."  The pizzas that came to our table were vastly inferior to the high-scoring pizzas at places like Corso, Pizzaiolo and Marzano.  Frankly I'd rather have had a Jupiter's pizza.  The ginger Christmas ale from the Santa Cruz brewing company was over the top in the direction of awful.  Ice creams and sorbets at the end of the meal were good (winter squash ice cream: yes!).

The service was OK, but our server seemed to be constantly harried and out of breath.  When dishes came out, they were transported from the kitchen by a team of runners that didn't always include our server.  The geometry of the place is weird: the metal rail that cordons off the dining tables from the rest of the establishment sometimes made it hard for the staff to serve our dishes.  A staff member might be standing near some diners at your table but will then have to run around to the other side of the rail to serve those diners who are at the corner of the table nearest the rail.

This restaurant did look attractive from the outside, and it is conveniently located.  I hope that its level rises.  Babette: we need you!

After another year, another group of friends and I 'gathered' and enjoyed a lovely brunch. Gather has friendly and helpful staff ~ the handsome host opened the door welcoming us in, and wished us well on our way out (I didn't notice this the first time, but the sign as you're exiting says 'Come Again') - nice touch.

My friends and I split the buckwheat pancakes with sheep ricotta and Meyer lemon braised strawberries (it was overly sweet and a bit too mushy for my taste) and egg pizza with bacon, caramelized onions and oregano, which I absolutely LOVED! I also enjoyed the coffee, which was smooth and nicely paired with my brunch pizza.

I love the clean, natural ambiance, the open kitchen, the sustainable vibe. Good for the belly and soul.

PS: They have an outside patio, and for you Far Side fans, there are cartoons posted on the bathroom wall. Walking distance from Downtown Berkeley BART.

i'm a gal that likes her meat. a lot. bloody, juicy, medium-rare to rare meat. the less PC, the better. lamb, love it. veal, delicious. sorry PETA, meat is yummy, and i eat what tastes good. i tried to be vegetarian for a while because my best friend in high school was, but that lasted a solid three months before i started cheating. with bacon cheeseburgers. 

thusly, a place like gather, known for its vegetarian, nay, vegan fare, was somewhere i expected to enjoy more for say, their libations. however, gather is not at all what i expected - a polished 1-2 punch of cafeteria-style dining plus bar with a menu that includes minimal lentils and leans more towards fresh, seasonal dishes that most would call "california cuisine," and i call "just plain delicious." the vegan charcuterie platter lives up to its reputation as an artistic and appetizing sampling of vegetables, herbs, and nuts. while gather does have some vegan options that would scare a carnivore like myself ("cheese" made of cashews and leeks? no thanks), there is also homemade porchetta (pork wrapped in pork belly, 'nuff said). 

i may never be a convert to the vegetarian revolution (bacon is too damn yummy!), but i applaud gather for their inventive preparations and creative combinations of flavor, which ensured that i didn't miss the meat at all.

PS - the bar fully keeps up with the kitchen as far as imagination goes; my favorite concoction was the bee sting, a slurp-able combo of square one botanical, lemon, fresh mint, ginger, and honey syrup (but be wise; don't slurp and drive).

I can't believe it took me this long to try out Gather.

Thanks to a Daily Dishout coupon that Chuck L. had forwarded to me, the brunch pizza was on the house as long as we ordered some cocktails. No complaints there. We happily sipped our mimosas.

- Brunch pizza was super - eggs, great bacon, caramelized onions as toppings. The crust was perfect. 

- Beautiful and relaxing interior. You just breath a nice sigh of relief when you're here, so sit back and enjoy your food and company. 

- Incredibly warm and friendly staff. Our server was great, but the host was so sweet. I first called in to let her know that we were running a bit late for our reservation, and she said it was no problem. When we got there, she addressed me by my name and said it was really sweet of me to call in. Oh, AND she swooped in like a hawk when a homeless guy came into the restaurant to ask my friend for change as we were sitting right by the door. Not only did she make sure our service was uninterrupted, but was also all smiles to this homeless guy when she assisted him outside. 

I cannot wait to be back here for lunch/dinner one of these days.

I've been back to Gather a couple times since my last review - and was secretly hoping that they would have the fried maitake mushroom available last night when I popped in after a show at the Berkeley Rep.

Arriving just before 10, I was cheerfully greeted and directed to the bar in the back where the bartender was very friendly and helpful.  He let me taste some of the ingredients I had never seen in drinks before - a rhubarb liqueur and Rhuby Cubed - that rhubarb liqueur, rum, ruby red grapefruit, hopped grapefruit bitters.  It was light and refreshing, citrusy and exactly the kind of thing I would want to drink on a hot day.  I ended up selecting the "Bronze Resistance" which was absolutely delicious for me as a fennel fan - my friend got Corpse Reviver #2 which was really really good - I might get that next time.

Back in the days when I was still a vegetarian who occasionally ate seafood when dining out - I first encountered "Fritto Misto" while traveling in Italy - you get a giant pile of crispy golden fried seafood - usually more than you can eat before you get your entree.  I saw that there was a vegan fritto misto with oyster mushrooms - with some fond memories of both Italian fritto misto experiences and the fried oyster mushrooms at Millennium - I ordered.

While delicious, I have to say I was shocked that the price for 5 little pieces of fried mushrooom and squash was $12 - it should be more like $8.  The cauliflower-horseradish aoli was creamy and rich but lacked bite.  The fried bits were really crispy but the flavors didn't really come through - obviously, the onion ring was an onion - but the oyster mushrooms seemed to have lost their flavor, else I got a plate of fried squash bits only (which were like hush puppies).  I expected more mushroomy and sweet squash flavors - both seemed a bit lost to the batter.

Though I was tempted to order the vegan charcuterie, it looked like they changed the formula and I wasn't as excited about it as I had been about the smoked melon and the vegan sausage on the charcuterie the last several times I had been at Gather.  

Instead, I ordered the spicy tomato pizza.  Talk about Pizza-Gasm!  I recently experienced really awesome vegan pizza from Rotten City and then ordered one at home - which was satisfactory.  This pizza cost $9 less, was about the same size and was far superior (my friend agreed - having tried the RC pizza, too).

The crust was thin without being soggy and I like how the edges balloon up a bit in the oven, though they blackened a bit - the crust was crispy without being oily.  The sauce was absolutely delicious - very fresh tomato tasting, with the chile oil and chopped up capers/olives giving the whole pizza a bit of "arrabiata" taste to it - the only thing I might ask is for less cashew cream and more spice!

We also ordered the frites on the side - they were delicious with the outstanding house made catsup.

I am really happy that Gather's menu is changing and seasonal - and that they very clearly note vegan and gluten-free options.  That saves so much work for the wait staff and helps out customers a lot.  I hope to go back for the smoked artichoke entree before it goes off the menu!

Service was fantastic and dining in the bar area was actually quite nice and I think less noisy than the main dining room.

I'm just gonna go out and say it: I really really enjoyed my time over dinner at 'Gather'; no doubt in no small measures by the company (Hi Alice, Hi Kristy , Boo Christopher !), but also by the visually pleasing and palate-satiating plates of ambrosial delights.

On a different note, I wanted to complain and ask for "my cute waitress" as two of my dinner companions (I won't say which two) were busy ogling at the "cute waiter" (their words, most definitely NOT mine).

The Pizza with radicchio, already ordered by the hungry duo before I even made my appearance, was pretty good. It was thin crust, just the way I like it, and the vegetarian toppings were really good!

The Bay Area Squids were a pleasant surprise with the fava beans making for a very deserving complement. For lack of a better description, let me, in my own novel philistine ways, describe it as a gourmet turn on the bay area favorite --- calamari rings.

Next, the Potato Salad with artichoke hearts and mushrooms in blue-cheese dressing was unlike any I've had before. The three different textures and flavours played against each other beautifully. I would definitely recommend it in a heartbeat and would be having this again on my next visit.

My tummy and taste tentacles were clamouring for the cured-meats plate but alas, there was no space for it ! You can bet your last dollar that's what I'm going to have on my next visit !

My entree of choice was the "Young Chicken under a brick". The side, that I believe to be the hominy ragout was creamy with a smooth texture and accompanied the chicken very merrily indeedy. The leg meat was tender and succulent and even the usually dry breast meat (cue Chicken joke, please) was juicy and perfectly seasoned.

The other entrees I dug into a little was the gnocchi, and the shoestring (?) fries from the Prather Ranch Burger. The gnocchi was surprisingly light, and very tasty. It went well with the sauce and the green peas.

Lastly, I love love love the Pinot Grigio! But then I am a fan of sweet dessert wines (no matter the course I am indulging in) so it may not be for everyone. An aside: the Pinot Grigio I had at Becketts this weekend tasted weak and watered down; it simply did not measure up.

We skipped the dessert and hopped over to the Gelato place for my tryst with the coconut gelato --- bliss! And another Yelp review!

A contemporary version of Chez Panisse Cafe.  Most produce and meat are raised and farmed sustainably and organically in local farms.  

If you've lived in Berkeley you know the corner of Oxford and Allston is a cursed spot for restaurants.  It feels out of the way, stuck in between downtown Berkeley and the UC Berkeley campus.   But Gather seems to have a knack for gathering both food and foodies because it gets so crowded sometimes.

My friends and I shared the wild nettle pizza, potato salad, squid and beans, roasted young chicken, gnocchi, and one friend had burger and string fries.  Everything was good, but my favorite was the gnocchi with vegetable ragout.  The gnocchi was light and fluffy unlike many other versions I have had before.  The ragout sauce had the intense and concentrated tomato flavor with greens, peas, and baby artichokes.  The chicken was juicy and tender.

In addition we had an awesome server who made us feel welcome and was attentive despite the crazy Saturday night crowd.  The open space was a little hard to have conversations in, but it conjured the ambience of  free-flowing and organic energy.  We did not feel that we were there to critique our experience, but rather to gather, have good food, and enjoy each other's company.

Gorgeously casual interior, completely New American menu with vegan friendliness, cocktail forward bar with organic spirits and a spacious outdoor patio equipped with heat lamps? Count me in.

After tonight's visit to Gather, it's no surprise that this restaurant has received such high acclaim for its food and concept. While my group and I only sampled the pizzas, each one was as delicious as the last and for someone who detests cold pizza (just like I hate eggs or coffee gone cold), I found my last remaining slice to be totally toothsome. Shame on me for not getting to it until it lost to the powers of staying uneaten for so long. 

If organic, locally produced, outdoor seating, cocktails, vegan, or just delicious matches your search, look no further.

Out of town friends staying in Emeryville was just the excuse we needed to finally get over to Gather

Started w/ a California Pisco Sour - was an interesting take on a pisco sour - the paprika on the top gave it a weird savoriness & having just come back from Peru, I guess I was extra sensitive to anomalies

Burrata w/ Pumpkin - pretty tasty but have to say this was probably something we could have all shared....wasn't good enough that I wanted to hog the whole thing for myself.  The burrata wasn't very runny-creamy & there wasn't nearly enough pumpkin - added to the fact it was pretty bland, I was hoping for something really spiced well to complliment the already-bland burrata

Vegan Squash Risotto - corn & potatoes all diced up together & creamy like a risotto but w/out the rice - paired w/ chick peas, zucchini & cherry tomatoes.  It was good but Sis & I weren't blown away

Buddy got the Swordfish special & liked his dish a lot.  Said the fish was cooked perfectly tender & the accompanying veggies were fantastic

Dessert consisted of the Goat Milk Semi-Freddo w/ anise & poached Peach.  Sis said this tasted like vanilla ice cream & was hoping for a bit more goat milky richness

So overall, this was a great introduction to Gather & we'd def consider coming back. Totally kicking myself for not ordering the Vegan Charcuterie & their pizzas looked promising as well.....next time!

After 1 hour of trying to figure out what to wear and  1 hour of applying make-up (since I don't wear makeup)...darn it how does this eye shadow work?? HELP!!  

It was all worth it when I saw the love of my life get out of the car in his handsome grey button shirt.  I was like "DAMM I'm a lucky woman"!!  I know you know what I mean ladies...it's like everything is in slow motion.  As if you're watching a movie and you just stand there thinking is he really here for me?  The only thing missing was me tripping and the sudden ERRR!! Sound *stop of movie and rewind* haha

Anyways, I always wanted to go to Gather.  It was one of the restaurants I bookmarked right away when I turned Vegan.  Finally I get to try it out.  We were looking pretty hot.  As we walked inside, I was impressed by the décor.  The vines coming down near the kitchen.  As I started looking around, I noticed "Ummm I think we're overdressed".  I've noticed when your dressed up nice, a lot of people like to smile at you.  I thought that was nice or maybe they were thinking..."these idiots they didn't get the memo, jeans, shorts, t-shirts, tank tops are acceptable".

As we sit down and look at the menu.  I realized two things...One there's A LOT of old people here (Gray hair Grandma/ Grandpa type...odd  since UC Berkeley is just down the street...*scratching my head*) and Two this place is great for Carnivores.  So if you're a mix group, definitely check this place out.  They have something for everyone.  Regardless if your Vegan or not, mostly everyone orders the Vegan Charcuterie.  It's an item you have to at least try once.  The dish changes, so if you see it in a picture it doesn't necessarily mean it will be the same the next month.  The food is good; I wouldn't say it's great, I think it's a little pricey for the amount you get.  

We also ordered the vegan pizza and it was very tasty, it had a little kick to it. I saw a lot of people on yelp order the one with an egg.  I also noticed a lot of people at the establishment were ordering it too.  I think because it's the one item on the menu you get the most bang for your buck.  

If your a meat eater than you should have no problem.  The portions for "meat" is very large.  Which makes no sense to me since I thought veggies are cheaper than meat.  *shrugs shoulder*

"Dear Gather owner, why can't you pile the veggies for us Vegans and Vegetarians? We would greatly appreciate it...Sincerely, Rachel"

The seating here is very close to each other, but strangely enough we were able to have a conversation without having to raise our voice.  We enjoyed each other's company and no one tried to rush us.  This is the moment you just sit there have a cup of coffee and share a dessert and just bask in the each other's love.  

OK....I know enough Rachel...can you get anymore mushy.  Hey come on!!  Let me have my moment.  

Next stop Millennium...did you get that HONEY!! *hint hint*  LOL  *BIG GRIN*

FYI...
They close the doors after lunch to open up at 5pm for dinner.
Meter Parking available on the streets, free after 6pm
Parking Garage down the street
Very casual establishment.
Reservation suggested

Nothing fancy, modest little restaurant. The food was good for the price. The combo special was a good deal. I ordered the pad Thai though, it was ok. The flavor could have been a little bit more intense.

Their fried rice is superior than most other Thai places.

Let me be honest, though. Everything is over-priced.

You might think it is worth paying as long as it is good, but...

Come on. This place is next to Campus and most of their customers are poor students.

If you get a basil fried rice with extra rice, (which is not even much more rice than regular) 

the total is about $9.50 just for a fried rice plate.

Regular fried rice is also over $8.00...(At least a dollar or more
expensive than most other places)

I like that they use paper container for to-go unlike most other places.

It is sad that I usually go to Chiang Lai even though I like Jasmine's fried rice better.

my favorite place in northside in term of getting food. the buffet lunch is very good. 

if you get lucky, u'll get the server that does a REALLY good job. watching him filling my lunch order is very satisfying as he carefully fills my dishes into respected corners of the take out box, adds extra sauce from the dish on to my rice, and wipe off any sauce around the container that might make the food look messy. 

his action makes me respect my lunch.

but if u get unlucky, then u get good food that is slapped into a box. it happened to me today. sadness. it's just not the same when it is not handled with care.

It's a little overpriced for what you get.  It's not very fresh.  I agree with Josh K, the people who own and run this place are incredibly sweet.  I go here for the convenience (fast, close to campus) and the RED RICE.  Yeah, I get red or brown rice every time I want to justify a greasy thai meal.  It makes me feel like I'm making a healthy decision.

I eat at Jasmine Thai quite a bit. Their lunch buffet is always really good and their spring rolls rock the party. Folks from school meet there often. Good neighborhood vibe, and I've never been disappointed.

I'm quite frankly surprised at the negative reviews.  I think that the food is way better than the much praised Cha Am and much cheaper than many full service places.  The lunch buffet is good, cheap, plentiful, and fast (in and out in under 30 minutes).  For $6-$8 I really don't think you can expect better. 

I haven't ordered much from the full service menu but that too was fast and good.  I especially appreciate the fresh and perfectly cooked vegetables.  (And I love that they use real straw mushrooms rather than just tired-out-sliced- up regular ones.)  The pumpkin curry is particularly good.  Check it out.

Seeing as I work right next to the Euclid strip, I'm not left with a lot of exciting choices on my lunch break. For this Jasmine gets points just for being a non-sandwich place close by.

The food is neither remarkable nor cheap, and there's been chicken in my veggie plates more than once. The people behind the counter are friendly, though, and they've got some nice bottled drinks (yerba mate!) so I'm never really disappointed.

Taste: 3
Value: 3
Service: 4

I came here for their lunch special one time, and I was somewhat disappointed. Their food was okay, but the price was a tad higher than I would have liked, given the quality. Also, there's not much seating inside, and the hallway you order food in is very narrow. Also, the lines during lunch can be quite long. All in all, it was okay.

Finally, a place that has lasted longer than 6 months in that space on the northside. It is not a bad option for a quick meal. There are a few preset items you can quickly order for lunch. They also give you the option of black rice which is a good change of pace. The prices are reasonable, about $7 for a two-item lunch with rice. While the food is not exceptional, it is not too greasy and the spices are balanced. I like the pumpkin chicken and the green beans & tofu. 

Remember to bring some cash. They do not take credit cards, and they charge a small fee for using your debit/ATM card. There is a Bank of America ATM nearby on campus at the Terrace Cafe.

Although I liked the flavors, they give very little portions. My boyfriend and I were going to share the lunch special (3 items with rice for ~$9), but it was barely enough for one person. We had red rice with green curry, green beans with chili, and basil chicken. I liked the green curry the best, but again, it was a very small spoon of it.  

The actual restaurant was very small. I found myself very carefully navigating down the aisle so that I wouldn't accidentally hit the person at the next table as I was getting up. 

On the upside, it was fast. I don't think I'll go back.

The food at Jasmine Thai is definitely the best Thai food near the north side of the Berkeley campus--their lunch specials are very tasty (the Pad Thai and the green beans in particular), and their Pad Se Ew is great. You don't have to wait long for your food if you order at lunch, which is a great bonus for those of us who only have 30-minute lunch breaks.

The downside to Jasmine is that it simply doesn't have enough room. Waiting for your food can be quite an experience, as there is little room to stand or sit to wait and people are constantly squeezing by you to get to the tiny dining area. Finding a seat during lunchtime can be difficult to impossible, and sometimes your table can be intruded upon by people asking to share (I found this to be uncomfortable).

But the food is cheap, tasty, and fast--three things I value highly on my lunch break!

I've walked past this restaurant multiple times before but I never had a chance to take a look inside until today.

Jasmine Thai offers an assortment of standard Thai dishes and surprisingly, a selection of both vegetarian and vegan options. They also have specials posted outside the door and quite a bit of beverage options. Dishes are pretty cheap price-wise, although there are better Thai restaurants in the Berkeley area that charge at the same price.

I ordered the Beef Pad See-Ew and a Thai Iced Tea. The Pad See-Ew didn't appeal to me as anything out of the ordinary; if at all, a bit bland. The noodles were plain and didn't have as much flavor as I expected, and the beef was slightly overcooked. Regarding the Thai Iced Tea, it actually tasted pretty good. The drink was just right - not overly sweet and not too much tea flavor. There aren't many other places on the north side of campus where you can order Asian-style drinks, and if you're looking for something to quench your thirst, try here. The food is fine, but as I said before, you can find better quality Thai restaurants in the area charging the same dishes at the same price.

The restaurant usually isn't crowded, and almost every time I pass by the restaurant is empty. Even so, they cook their dishes quite fast, so if you need something quick or on the go you can always stop by here. Jasmine Thai also sells bottled beverages and pre-made buns - perfect if you want a quick snack.

The food is decent, but if you prefer a place to sit down and enjoy your dinner, try a different Thai restaurant.

I love Thai food, and this little hole-in-the-wall is as good as I've found in Berkeley - much better quality and taste than any of the bigger Thai restaurants on Shattuck (avoid Cha-am!). I would rather go to Jasmine Thai than any other place around, simply because nothing beats the flavor when Thai food is done right.

Organic thai ice tea with soy milk?? Yes! Vegan green curry with eggplant? My favorite. The pad thai is very good, too, very authentic, not sticky-sweet, actually the pad thai is the best that I've had anywhere. Very nice with a little key lime slice on the side. Vegetarian yellow curry with onions... mmmm..... and tofu with peanut sauce and a big helping of steamed spinach and broccoli.  Can you tell I'm a regular? I haven't tried any of their seafood or meat dishes, but those are available as well.

At Jasmine Thai the menu items are separated between meat, vegetarian, and vegan. All the vegetables are always very fresh and prepared well, steamed but not overcooked. Each meal comes with choice of white rice or red rice for 50 cents more. The red rice is amazing - hearty, nutritious, and very flavorful - I like the flavor better than brown rice.

I also love that there is filtered water, big plus. After you order you go and pick up your own flatware/chopsticks and water, and it always makes me happy to pour myself a glass of filtered water, as most restaurants serve their customers tap water. I can really taste the difference.

Prices are very reasonable. Two adult dinners and one thai iced tea to share rings in under $20. Lunch for one is around $6.

During the daytime hours, Jasmine Thai has a very fresh buffet where you can order one, two, or three items for a tiered price. At night you can order at the register from their menu, and your food will be served to you at your table. Or you can call in an order ahead of time (or order there to go). It's never taken more than ten minutes for my food - service is usually very prompt.

The atmosphere is not such for a hot date, unless you have a cool "Mr. Big showing Carrie the best Chinese food in the city" kind of affair. Not too many tables, mainly college kids ordering take-out and a few sitting and eating meals while they study.

Been her a few timed over the years.  It was around the corner from where I lived and the food and price is comparable to the other Thai place around the corner in the Asian Ghetto.

While the food isn't spectacular, they do have one item on their lunch menu that I always have to get when I'm here, and that is the son-in-law egg. It's basically fried hard boiled eggs with tofu and a tamarind sauce over rice.  If it wasn't for this dish, I'd be giving this place two stars.

When I'm here for dinner I usually opt for the BBQ chicken (it's not really BBQ chicken, they really should think of a different name for it, like Thai Chicken or something).  If you like rice, the upgrade to the sticky rice.  It's worth the extra money.

Bottom line, I'd would only go here if I was craving some Thai but was too lazy to walk down to Shattuck, where the better Thai restaurants are

WOW

Food so ridiculously terrible I am completely amazed that this place is still open.  This will be your cup of tea if you like food that looks and tastes like it was made yesterday and left out overnight.

I was embarrassed to be seen walking out of this place, disgusted at myself for even trying two bites of the crusty, atrocious noodles, and ultimately regretting that I didn't try to get my money back.

It's one thing to have a bad meal and decide you're not going back, but its another thing to have it be so bad that you have to go somewhere else to get food you can actually eat.

Go for lunch, their buffet is solid. I usually get "double basil" - basil eggplant tofu, and basil chicken, on red rice if I'm feeling rich. They have raised prices due to hard times and red rice, which used to be free, is now 50c extra.

I've never bothered to go for dinner and the style of the restaurant just does not fit with a sit down dinner place.

The people who run it are really nice though! It is a husband and wife (or at least a significant-other) team.

Among the many restaurants on Euclid and Hearst across the street from the North Side of the UC Berkeley Campus, this is a great place to eat.

They have several vegetarian and vegan options and they have separate menus for vegetarian and vegan meals (I love it when places do this).  

They have yellow, green, and red curries, which have various levels of spiciness.  I've only tried their vegan yellow curry tofu which is mild and tastes pretty good. Their vegan crunchy tofu is also quite good.  

The main reason I don't here more often than I do is their prices (Expect to pay between $7 and $8.50 for lunch)

This place is really close to where I work and has a pretty good selection of vegan items, which is why I'm willing to pay slightly more than I typically would to eat here.  But if you're not restricted to the North Side of campus, I'd suggest trying Thai Basil, which has slightly better quality food.
Good for fast thai food, although the prices are a little steep.  This is one of only a few decent restaurants that stays open into the evening and doesn't just serve the Cal lunch crowd.

This place gets the job done. 

Average food, average price, average service. The standout is definitely the chicken pumpkin curry. And unless you have tons of time to spare, don't order anything that isn't a special.

i just ate here for lunch. I had actually never been on the north side of campus, so I decided to walk up and check it out. There were a couple places to choose from--Hummingbird Cafe, Stuffed Inn, etc-- and I basically picked Jasmine Thai at random. 

It's a pretty small place, with most of the seating in the back of the restaurant. Nothing fancy at all, but I definitely didn't get a dirty or unclean vibe.

I ordered a Pad Thai with Prawns (I know, pretty unoriginal thing to order, but you might as well test the waters with the Thai staples first before getting into something more complex). I was expecting it to come from a hot plate given the price point (only around $7.50), but the lady actually took the time to make it fresh. And she took the extra 3 seconds to bring it out to where I was sitting, not just slap it up on the bar for me to pick it up.  

All in all, it was pretty delicious. I have a feeling this will be a definite regular lunch stop for me once school starts back up.
not the best, not the worst, typical thai resto in berkeley

I went there to lunch a couple of times and I felt in love in their red rice. They made the best rice I have had, and coming from a Thai, this is very rare. 

The entrees need a bit of variety though. I love their tofu n eggplants, son-in-law eggs, and tofu w/ string beans. I have never tried the curry because I dislike the way they put broccoli and carrots in curry. It's just not right for Thai curry. 

Pricewise, it is more expensive than other places in the area.

I would recommend  Jasmine Thai for lunch, as it's quick, inexpensive and tasty. On your left as you enter the door are about eight heated trays of various Thai dishes already prepared, from which you choose one, two or three items, rice included for about 6 to 9 dollars. A Thai couple seems to run the place, with the man doing the cooking. You pay her at the end of the "buffet" line and take one of about a dozen tables in the narrow but pleasant space. While it's not exactly a romantic place, it's relaxing and fun to talk with friends. About three quarters of the  tables were full around lunch time. I ordered all meatless dishes: eggplant, tofu green curry, and tofu yellow curry. The curries were great with fresh veggies added. I wasn't wild about the brown gravy that the eggplant was soaked in, but you may like it. If you enjoy a simple Thai lunch with the UC folks, it's worth a visit to see what you think.

If you find yourself on the northside of Berkeley, Jasmine is the best Thai food you will find. It has quite a good selection and almost everything I've had there was good. The staff is very friendly and the restaurant is clean. It can get a little busy sometimes, but thats true of any good food place.

I recommend the pumpkin curry and panang beef on red rice!
I go here for lunch.  6 selection of precooked trays for lunch hour combos.  It's fast and decent.  Bit pricey & some what small portion, but tasty.

Really yummy and really fast! For a quick lunch that is healthy, fresh and tasty, I'd recommend this place. The prices are a bit high (7-8 clams for lunch) but I feel that you get what you pay for. It's delicious and doesn't give you a grease-coma.

I've ordered the green curry with chicken and the yellow curry with chicken. PERFECT portion sizes. Not too much, not too little -- I always finish everything on my plate and feel perfectly full. They also provide red rice, which is extremely tasty and appears to be whole grain. The vegetables are fresh, and when you sit inside you can see down into the kitchen that prepares the food -- a very clean and cheery place!

Note: I would recommend dining in -- this ensures you get the fresh stuff. They have a little to-go area in the front, but I think those items are microwaved for speed. If you sit inside, the food comes out pretty quickly and it's really fresh.

The son-in-law eggs are their specialty, and that's lucky for me.  Hard-boiled eggs and tofu in a sweet sauce, perfect over some red rice.  You can also choose between various curries and pad thai for their excellent lunch special - one, two, or three items, plus rice, for under 10 bucks.  It's great!

Summary based on 1 lunch:
--My standard test lunch for dining solo of Tom Yum noodle soup wasn't that great.  It did have scallops, rarely seen, but no ground pork, no bean sprouts, no coriander. No discernible citrus.
--service just ok
--Restaurant was cold.  Waitress said there was no heat.
--Pricey.  Paid $11 with tip for what's usually around $9
--Parking limited without a UC parking pass.  If you have one there's a huge lot nearby.
--rest room was better than average
--ad supported free wifi didn't work out
--seating area not that large.  Probably not suitable for groups.

Occasionally I get obsessed with a certain meal and try to have it everywhere I go. Right now I am all about Tom Kha Gai, an amazing coconut milk soup with chicken and mushrooms, flavored with lemongrass, ginger, and galangal. So I had time to kill and thought I would try Jasmine Thai's version. It was... Not good. There wasn't a single piece of ginger, lemongrass, or galangal in the whole dish, so I'm guessing they used dried spices and probably a decent amount of sugar to (poorly) approximate the taste. The soup was really watery, not creamy-- the white color could have been achieved with cornstarch, not coconut milk, for all I can tell.  It also contained random things like baby corn and cherry tomatoes, and the chicken was dry. It is cheaper than Racha Cafe on Southside, but it's so bad that I'd much rather spend the extra money at Racha, which has the best Tom Kha Gai I've had so far. The only reason this got more than one star is that the lunch specials looked pretty good and others seemed to enjoy them, so I'm guessing it's just the soup that is utter crap.

Food and service is okay.  The place is small and tight.  I do believe their food has a more Asian taste than other Thai places, so if you want a more Asian Thai place, that would be the place to go.  To conclude, this place is okay, not a bad place to go for lunch if you are around the area, but otherwise, go somewhere else.

I could have sworn I wrote a scathing review about this place back in August after getting seriously ill from some food from here.  A group in our department had a Friday lunch catered by Jasmine Thai and while the food was tasty, I was laid up on the couch for half the weekend feeling like I had been shot with a tranquilizer dart.  NOT that I have first hand experience with that.  I'm usually just the one shooting the darts.  If by shooting the darts you mean making paper airplanes.

I guess in that food-poisioning-induced trance I forgot to spread the word.  Some sort of MSG mind trick, I suppose.

Many moons having passed since that incident, I decided to give their food another try yesterday.  It wasn't exactly worth the money for the hot lunch tray items, unless you think a giant pile of mostly rice is worth $6.  And, surprise surprise, I ended up with a terrible headache and felt like not-a-million-bucks the rest of the day.  Worst restaurant in the North Gate area by far.  Even La Burrita doesn't make me feel ill EVERY time I eat there.  As Meatloaf said, "two out of three ain't bad."

Pretty decent selection of precooked trays for daily lunch hour combos.  When I was on my vegetarian streak, this was the place to go because they have tasty veggie options.  My favorite is the eggplant tofu.  

Portion size is just enough to fill the average person and not put you over the top.  If you're looking for larger potion sizes, go to the Thai place in the northside asian ghetto (They too have a lunch combo special; about the same prices for more food, but slightly inferior in quality).

Sometimes there's a long line out the door during those peak lunch hours but it goes fairly fast.  Still definitely a quick eats kinda place: Thai on the go!

Nice place for lunch. 2 items deal is good - also superfast. For dinner, its  a bit pricey but arguably one of the few healthy food places on euclid. 

For six years, I have mostly ordered for take-out here but staff are quite friendly.  The place is small but usually quite. 

Comparing with all other places on Euclid, I give them credits for mainly two things: being superfast at lunch as well as serving reasonably okay thai food. They sure are priced a bit high.

My go-to place for Thai food during lunch. They have around 9 pre-made trays of food for lunch combos. Dishes start from $6 and go up depending on the number of entrees you choose. I also tried ordering off the dinner menu (during dinnertime) and much preferred the lunch entrees.

They handled my catering order for $450 worth of food very professionally. And gave me a free thai iced tea when I placed the order!
Good, quick take-out.  Buffets usually freak me out but this one doesn't.

They have the best coconut ice cream! I love getting their fried banana and coconut ice cream.

Other than that, pretty standard, but convenient if you're a vegetarian or a vegan (they have whole vegan selection).

It's not that great, it's not that cheap, but I like their Yellow Curry Tofu.

I'm not sure if I really want to review this place, or any place on or near the Euclid x Hearst, hence north gate of UC berkeley.
I ate here couple of times for lunch. Not bad compared to other food joints in the neighboorhood. I particularly like their thai iced tea. Not too sweet, just right.
Lunch combo is a bargain, and I like the fact they serve red rice, as well as white rice. 
Be aware, if you're not a big eater. One order of lunch combo will last until lunch the next day. Big portion.

Maybe it is better for lunch?

Went to Jasmine Thai with some friends for a late-night dinner.
I was starving and even then the food still seemed a bit disappointing. 

We ordered the crab meet noodles, the pad see ew noodles, and the eggplant tofu.

The crab noodles were one of the daily specials, and they were a decent dish. They had real crab meet and a tasty sweet house sauce. Unfortunately, the portion was not too big and they were devoured  quickly by the group. The egg plant tofu was also good. It was spicy and seasoned with Thai basil. 

The big disappointment was the pad see ew. The noodles were dry and mushy/ They were clearly not made fresh and just reheated from earlier in the day. Every Thai restaurant should always deliver on the stapes, and this dish was a huge miss.

The restaurant was empty, so service was fast. (Probably too fast because it resulted in reheated noodles) Maybe if you come by at lunch you will get fresh ones. 

There are only a couple of Thai places on northeast campus, so you might have to eat here to satisfy your craving. You might get a satisfying dish or you might get a dud.

Wanted: quality Thai food, minus the overdose of MSG/salt enough to put me in a coma.

I've been here three times for lunch, all for the quick lunch combo that comes with rice and 1-3 entrees.
First try: thought the eggplant tofu was delicious.  Portion was big enough to have leftovers for lunch the next day.  (Yea, I get full fast.)  I was young and naive...might have considered four stars.

Second try: had eggplant tofu with some other entree.  Again, enough for leftovers for next day's lunch.  Felt like a three-star place.

Third time's the charm? Methinks not.  Going after the lunch rush, I got a better flavor for the place.  I didn't get a very pleasant vibe from the staff - they even asked for my flimsy plastic fork back when I sat my to-go order down at a table.  This was just really odd.  I apparently ordered the bottom of the red rice barrel, and got a disproportionate amount of rice as compared to the eggplant tofu and chicken basil I ordered.  The chicken basil had an oddly off-putting aftertaste to it, and the chicken pieces looked like scraps.  There was a really weird drain a few feet from our table that spurted an extremely unappealing slosh of water every few minutes...gross.  I guess these are the details you don't notice when the place is packed and loud.
The last straw was when I had my leftovers for dinner today (stuck at work late), and I felt like I had eaten spoonfuls of salt.  About ten gallons of water later, I think two doses of Jasmine Thai is just too much for one day.

All this and my wallet was about ten bucks lighter...not worth the quality.  Next time I'll go for a healthier sandwich at Stuffed or the other asian offerings at the ghetto.

I have been to this place for dinner twice.  Both times have been pretty bad.  The first time I got take out and was disappointed with the price and quality of the food.  The second time, I made the mistake of dining in.

- The service is terrible.  They brought me my food to my table, but they did not bring water or silverware.  You are also expected to bus your own table.
- The food quality is low.  While not terrible, it is definitely cheap and mass produced.  They also give you very little.  I ordered the BBQ chicken and was served two thin slices of chicken on a plateful of rice.
- The price is not as cheap as you would expect.  For $8 or so I would expect some real service or some decent food or at least a reasonable volume.  This place gives you none of the above.

The one kid who was working at the registers was very nice so I feel guilty leaving this one star review, but a smile and small talk can't make up for the basics.

Solid place for thai lunch. They have a "buffet" where you can order one, two or three things and they put it on a good bed of rice. Very good selection of veggie options with lots of tofu. 

Weird layout and really loud. Hard to get a seat during the rush! 

Will be returning, but not too much:  this $6 meal is 3 soups at Stuffed Inn..

Wholly disappointing. I came here for lunch because Stuffed Inn had their usual ridiculously long line coming out of the building. The lunch specials are between $5.50 and $7 for rice and a choice of 1-3 entrees.

Food at Thai eateries usually have a rich flavor, but this place's green tofu curry and chicken basil was flavorless aside from the spiciness of the chili. It was just watery, spicy meat-and-veggies plopped atop soggy rice.

With competition like this, it's really no surprise that places like Stuffed Inn and even La Burrita can continue to attract large crowds during lunch hour on Northside.

1.75 stars.

So, I've been craving some Thai food ever since a colleague of mine brought some to a study session for the group.  She got it from Thai Noodle on Shattuck, and it was delicious.  However, since I was at the top of campus, I did not feel like walking all the way down to Thai noodle.  On top of that, I'm not really sure what the dishes were that she got.  Anyway, so I decided to try Jasmine Thai.

I ordered the Cashew Bean Curd dish.  It was pretty good/ok, about a 3 star dish.  I also got a Thai iced tea with organic soy milk, which was absolutely awesome.  However, while sitting down to eat I started looking over the reviews on Yelp for this place on my iphone.  I noticed one individual who commented that they had gotten food poisoning from here.  I didn't think anything of it.  Probably just an individual experience, and nothing to worry about, right?  Wrong!  I totally got sick a couple of hours after eating here.  My stomach was jacked up for a good two days.  

So, while the food was decent - it was definitely a solid 3 stars in the taste department- it's not cool to get sick after eating out somewhere, which is what knocks this review of Thai Jasmine down to 1.75 stars.   

The extra .75 is for the friendliness of the people working there.
All I can say is Pumpkin Curry! If you go for no other reason, it should be for the pumpkin curry, which is tasty and will warm you up on a cold rainy day.

I ate at Jasmine Thai at least twice a week for all of last semester and almost always from the ready-made food. I dug the red rice. I dug the not too spicy for my impossibly wussy taste buds yellow curry with tofu. I dug the friendly server and cashier. But why I am I writing a review now? Because my spring semester dining companion went to JT without me (how could you!?) and an employee said "How have you been? How is your friend? We have her sunglasses." It is now October. The last time I went there was MAY, freakin' 5 months ago. I had forgotten I  ever owned those sunglasses. Sure enough, I stopped by and they had my glasses up by the register (coated in 5 months of dust and cheap-food grease) but they were there none the less. Three stars for reliably decent food (ooo! try the black rice pudding for dessert! mmm...) but five stars and a round of applause for dedication to customer service and the best memory in the ENTIRE world. Maybe Thai food is the next gingko biloba.

A simple Thai lunch place close to the North Gate that serves tasty and fairly authentic meals for reasonable prices. Don't expect to be floored by the food, but don't expect your tummy to hurt after your meal either.  I  appreciate the fact that the people that work here are actually Thai  (I can hear them talking in the kitchen, and better yet understand!) as I've been to one too many restaurants where the language from the kitchen is not Thai. The place also has the aroma of a true Thai kitchen (like my momma's) and the decor includes a portrait of the revered king as well as the requisite Thai elevator, oops, I meant restaurant, music. I feel at home.

I've only been here once, and I don't think I'll be back again

The Pad Thai tasted like soy sauce noodles, and I had to try to take bites just to get it down.  The Thai tea was good, but how do you mess that up?

Honestly for that amount of money, I would have rather went to La Val's or something to get a few slices.

The entree menu is quite repetitive-I came here 3-4 times on random occasions and remembered seeing the same entrees every time.  I will let the statistics speak for itself.

The quality of the food was ok, but the tastes was not up to my Thai standard..i.e. the dishes definitely lack Thai characteristics.  For example, the level of the spiciness and the taste was way off and the texture of the curry was not quite right.  However, I had to admit that they had good brown rice.  Thai iced tea, bun, or anything else that was not entree were not great and tasted really bland.  Don't waste your money on it.

Jasmine makes it possible for me to wake up at 12:40, eat a filling and sufficiently exciting meal, and still make it to my 1 o'clock class.

For them, I'm going to create a new evaluative point for restaurants; let's call it factor C.  And we'll define this factor C thusly:

C=(goodness of food on a 1-10 scale) / [(divergence, in feet, from the route I would be walking if I didn't eat anything) x (time it takes, in seconds, to get and pay for food)] - (price of food in USD)

It so happens that Jasmine Thai has the highest factor C of any restaurant on earth.

Twice or thrice a week, I walk in and utter all of six words (seven if I'm very hungry)... Not one minute later, I'm crossing the street onto the UC campus while shoveling Panang beef into my mouth with a plastic fork.

I give them four stars and not five as a result of my best attempts to block out my bias.  Factor C aside, Jasmine is good but certainly not the best Thai around, and if I were to move neighborhoods or stop going to school here I would probably return only for sentimental reasons.  But for all those who lead UC-centered lives and live on Northside, this place gets an easy five stars.

*Recommended items: iced coffee; crab noodles, basil chicken

Very adequate food at a very reasonable price. The layout is very awkward, though. You queue, order and pay right by the door. This means that the people done with the queuing, ordering, paying and eating have to squeeze through in between the wall and the people still queuing, ordering and paying.

Northside Berkeley sucks ass for good food options, but Jasmine Thai is certainly an exception.

Nestled in a tiny slot on Euclid, Jasmine has managed to break the curse of that location by staying open for more than 6 months.  I noticed right away that unlike every other owner, they stopped using the front reheater and almost exclusively cooked everything to order.  The menu options offer a good variety of the usual Thai favorites (Pad Thai, Chicken Satay) and House Specials that often involve seafood.  The service is friendly, prompt, and (again, unlike previous owners) clean.

When considering the limited options available on that tiny strip of commerce, there's really only Bongo Burger, Top Dog, and Hummingbird Cafe to go with.  LaVal's used to be the best, but now it's either shit or god awful, depending on how little the server cares.  La Burrita serves the worst "mexican food" you'll ever eat in your life.  The weird Korean BBQ/Asian Vegitarian place is bland at best.  Around the block there's a food court that should be condemned (barring Top Dog) and the rest of the street is soup n' sandwich joints.

Jasmine is a gem amongst gravel.  I routinely order their Pad See Ew and Chicken in Garlic sauce with a side of eggrolls.  The eggrolls are absolutely fantastic - so much so I got a friend who hates eggrolls to dog mine once I forced them to try one (use the dipping sauce!)  Their prawns are shelled and picked so you can just eat them down.  You can get anything to go and they never forget to give you all you need (sauces, utensils, napkins, etc.).  Often I'll order on my way home and pick it up before I get there - that's a 15 minute walk, so we're talking fast cookin'.

If you're looking for a tasty bite to eat north of campus - GO HERE!  You won't be disappointed.

Not many places for good breakfast in the Berkeley area. This is my fall back hangover restaurant. Nothing beats sitting on their patio, drinking fresh squeezed OJ, having their fruit topped pancakse or their lunch menu after a night out. The prices are reasonable but they tend to be pretty busy on the weekends. Remember to go early otherwise, be prepared to wait in line with all the hung over people

Cafe Durant is a great place for brunch. The food is homey and filling, and the pancakes (all kinds, but my favorite is the banana chocolate) is SO FREAKING GOOD. The crepes and scrambled eggs/omelettes are good as well, and it's always nice to eat on the balcony/patio on a nice sunny, lazy Sunday.

I've only ever gone to this place for breakfast, so I can't say anything about lunch or dinner, but overall, I feel that this place wouldn't be my first pick. 

The breakfast combos/entrees are roughly $10, plus or minus $3. I always get the sundeck combos since they have variety, like eggs+ potatoes+ fruit, etc. But I've tried a good number, and it's pretty substandard.

Their french toast is more like plain dry toast, with powdered sugar on top. The omelets look like you could've made it better yourself, and a waste of my $10 bucks if you ask me. I might as well go ask a freshman to swipe me into Cafe 3, the dining common right down the street, which makes delicious, fresh, loaded omelets right in front of your eyes. The eggs benedict looks and tastes like a McMuffin. The crepes are dripping with oil (butter?), and kinda small. 

The Mexican food garners the two stars for this place, since number one, the horchata is DELICIOUS (just the right amount of cinnamon-y sweetness ^^ ), and number two, it has a self serve salsa bar. Those always get me. Yummy yummy fresh salsa. 

The burritos, enchiladas are alright, not great, and the beans and rice look like they're been scooped right out of a can, but still, I'd go for their Mexican food, than other "American" breakfast item. 

But their daily specials (i.e. Taco Tuesdays) and Happy Hour prices are ridiculously cheap, so I'll still come back to try those.

I tried this place after hearing some of my friends recommend it. God, I would not come here again. I ordered the steak burrito and it was really gross. They put guac and salsa all over my burrito, thus making eating it extremely hard and messy. The meat also tastes kind of weird - definitely not fresh. I kind of lost my appetite and took the other half home, and now it is all soggy.

This is the ultimate place for delicious food and hearty portions...it's great for breakfast/lunch/dinner/late dinner...whenever.  I've gone here for breakfast more than any other time I've been in Berkeley and every time, I have left full and happy.  If you are craving pancakes, crepes, french-fried potatoes, omelettes, breakfast burritos, and any other Mexican-style breakfast dishes, this places serves up the best and the presentation of their dishes is also definitely worth mentioning.  Come hungry and you will leave happy.

i love breakfast foods and i love cheap food. cafe durant is great - i got the sundeck combo and it made me pretty full. i don't really like their homefries very much, but that might have been because i was so excited to eat the rest of the meal. their fruit pancake is WONDERFUL. one of the best yet. their french toast is small but good. their omelettes are pretty good too. there's tons of veggies in it, tons of fruit in the pancake - i like how it doesn't feel like they are skimping. we sat outside, which was ok because it wasn't sunny, but i don't know what i would do if it were raining. it seems pretty crowded inside. the service is average. we bussed our own tables but i have seen people bus tables for you. everything on their menu looks really good. i kind of want to try it all

Come here for Taco Tuesdays ($1 chicken, beef, or veggie tacos) and happy hour ($5 all entrees plus $2 off a pitcher of beer)! The tacos themselves are tiny (much smaller than the $1 fish tacos you can get at Looney's) and do not have much toppings (ie veggies)... very expected for $1. I suggest getting their $5 entrees... split some nachos at your table and get a couple tacos each and it's worth it.

Great place (love the balcony) to chill with friends, grab a beer, share some nachos and eat some tacos!

For those of you at Cal in the 80's (and maybe before and after) this is the Manuel's successor.  Great for cheap beer.  Great happy hour.  Turns into a satellite frat house on a regular basis.  But dont' go there for the food, and especially not for breakfast.  Denver omelet and a cup of weak coffee for $10.01? At an "order at the counter" place?  At least the server didn't have the nerve to give me $9.99 change, and just handed me a $10.  Would have been one star if they had dumped a bunch of pennies on me.

Café Durant is my favorite place to eat in Berkeley.  It's not perfect, but it's my favorite.

There are so many options!  It takes me five minutes to decide.  Amazing sandwiches, great enchiladas, potato dishes, tempting crepes.  Hands down the best Mexican mocha around.

Sometimes I wish the food were warmer.  I've switched to La Burrita for my burritos and Smart Alec's for my salads, and sandwiches are always a tough call, but there's no place but Café Durant for a tostada.

My friends make fun of me for liking Café Durant so much, because, of course, it isn't quite as good as homemade Mexican food!

But under an umbrella on the deck or indoors, I like to eat here.  The tables aren't all clean, but I can find a nice spot, enjoy a conversation, study or watch tv by myself.  I can stay for hours.  It's pretty, calm and warm, and the light is just right.  The bathroom is swell.  Café Durant is like home away from home.
Chilaquiles!!!  Ghetto looking place but it's nice to sit outside on the upstairs patio.

Happy Hour is 3-7 on weekdays. All entrees are only $5!! I didn't find this place until my junior year, but it's definitely a cheap and convenient place to have group gatherings. They have giant TVs everywhere for easy sport viewing and cheap food to keep you satisfied. The cheap food isn't bad quality either as every item I've ordered from the menu has always satisfied me. (the standard burger, sandwich, burrito) I've almost always gotten full off one entree unless I was starving although that was extremely rare.

TL;DR; Great hangout for groups and super cheap food especially during happy hour. Go right before 7 on weekdays.

Sorry, I just don't see the appeal of over-priced, mediocre and (at times) stomach-pain-inducing Mexican food. 

Maybe Cafe Durant is okay for eating Wednesday night Wings but beyond that the appeal is zilch. 

If you do wind up going here, avoid getting a mimosa! It looks like a frothy mix of lemon tang and believe me you could do much better walking a little further to Henry's for a properly made drink.

Cafe Durant is a dive bar, sports bar, and cafe all in one. While a bit dingy and servers could be a little nicer, this is one of my favorite spots in Berkeley to pre-game, watch a game, and/or post-game!

They have a wide selection of bottled beers at a decent price, but come for the beers on tap during their happy hour. There isn't much to choose from by it's hard to say no to a pitcher of Blue Moon for about $7. Their margaritas are also pretty good (the kind that tastes good now, but will hit you hard later) - definitely get the strawberry!

As for the food, it's better than most places (on Durant). I'm a fan of their breakfast combos, Mexican breakfasts, and MIMOSAS. The nachos are also pretty good for sharing amongst friends. 

Watch a game, sit on the balcony, and enjoy!
Lovely outdoor deck, great service, and great food. I love their crepes, their breakfast combos, and mexican combos. It's a favorite of mine in Berkeley.
Great Mexican food, I love their enchiladas. The green salsa is super tasty. Big portions. The breakfast is a little pricey, but it tastes great! The chocolate chip pancakes are sooooo good!

Nice hidden place

had the cajun steak burrito

really filling but it wasnt of very high quality.

food also took forever

I really like this place for the large portions.  My bf always leaves here full and I guess the value is what brings me back here.  

Their sundeck specials are a great delicious deal, but I don't like the pancakes.  

Their burritos are huge and come with a lot of chips with unlimited salsas so that's why I think it's a steal.  You can totally fill up with that!  But the burritos aren't as good as Pancho's downstairs in Asian Ghetto in my opinion.  The flavors of the meat just aren't that clean and I feel way too heavy after I eat even 1/4 of the burrito.  

Good place for breakfast served all day!

Finally checked this place out after a year of wanting to go. Its kinda hard to find since you have to go inside and up the stairs to the left. It was Sunday night and it was pretty empty, maybe most people come here for breakfast.

I ordered the Green Chicken Enchilada Plate for $8. Really good, almost as good as the Mexican places in SoCal. Way better than La Burrita which is across the street. The food was warm. I would have liked a bit more rice but overall it was a good meal and two types of beans black and pinto which was unusual.

Also the self serve is a plus for me since I don't have to leave a tip and I get to get as much salsa or water as I want.

I'm having a hard time deciding whether I should write a single review with a mediocre rating or multiple reviews rating different aspects of the restaurant and their appropriate ratings. Oh well, read this list:

HAPPY HOUR SPECIALS? 5 STARS, especially for Berkeley. Cheap brewskies, food deals and an outdoor rooftop patio.

MEXICAN FOOD? 4 STARS. It's tastey. I know the legitimacy of "Mexican" style food is a very personal and touchy subject for people, but I'd eat it here again and again. Not super authentic or mind blowing, but decent with a decent amount of veggie options.

BREAKFAST? BOOOOOO. 1 STAR. Worst eggs florentine ever. I know, I know, it's my fault for ordering it at a place with happy hour and great mexican food, but still. If you can't do a good job, quit trying. The breakfast potatoes? Also piss poor. Somehow they're overly crisp, underly hot, and ugly.

I used to go here a lot when I was a starving student.  I remembered this being one of the best breakfast spots I've been to.  Now that I'm older and been to plenty more places, a lot of my fave college spots just don't hold up.  But this one does!

We wanted to go to the Crate & Barrel outlet in Berkeley, and since my football-mad hubby's would rather wake up early than miss the 49er game, we just decided to have breakfast there instead of dropping by in the afternoon.  He's also been craving strawberry crepes for a while, and after an unsuccessful attempt to go to IHOP (who knew they were so popular) last week, we actually decided to check this place out again.  We've been here numerous times while I was still in college and he was visiting for the weekend, but we haven't been here in at least 5 years!

I gotta say it's still the same divey-looking place, that serves both breakfast and mexican food(!) of all things.  And man, does the breakfast live up to my memories!  My buttermilk pancakes were perfectly cooked, with that very nice crisp edge that you only get if they're home made and from scratch.  Definitely blew McDonald's, Denny's, IHOP, and my own homemade pancakes out of the water.  The side of bacon I had was good, perfectly crisp...bacon always tastes good to me though!  Though I don't like fruit too much, my hubby's strawberry-banana crepes looked very tasty, and he enjoyed them a lot.  I think I wanna try some of their savory crepes next time (tomato and avocado!).  He also got a 2-egg breakfast that came w/ hash browns, toast, and sausage.  We got all this for under $20!  

We had a nice table outside where we can people watch and reminisce about when we were still in college.  Still the best breakfast I've ever had in the bay area!

I'm a regular here, and the workers are really friendly. For the most part, I like Cafe Durant. Most of the food is good, it's super cheap for the amount of food you get, and they have a good variety. I also like that they have TVs and always have soccer games playing. I had a lot of fun watching the world cup here. The only negatives I have are that sometimes I don't like the ingredients they use. The grilled cheese is made with regular, shredded cheddar and mozzarella. And the french toast is made with regular bread and tastes really bland. I wish they would use better ingredients, but it's not going to stop me from coming here. Overall, it's pretty good.

I wandered in here thinking it was a Mexican restaurant, but after looking it up on Yelp, I guess it's supposed to be good at serving everything.

I had a breakfast burrito with chorizo. It came with potatoes. Burnt potatoes. My sister had a breakfast burrito with chicken. It also came with potatoes. Burnt potatoes. The burritos themselves were nothing special and were topped with a scoop of guac and sour cream.

My sister wanted to sit outside to soak in the sun, but it was dirty, and the network of power-lines right outside ruined the outdoor mood. It was decent on the inside, though, with two flat screen TVs on opposite sides of the room.

food's pretty good considering the price.  lots of seating and the patio is really nice on warm days.  the freshly squeezed orange juice is pretty tasty and goes well with breakfast.  very affordable, pretty good taste, good atmosphere.

I had the eggs benedict.  It was overpriced, greasy and small.  It wreaked havoc on my digestion afterwards.  I can't speak for the other dishes but the one I had really did not encourage me to return.  I don't think it deserves to completely fail but there's definitely room to improve its pull for student customers.
I don't like their breakfast dishes. I ordered sundeck combo with pancakes, egg, and sausage....came out really bad. I couldn't believe I just paid for this meal...so disappointed.

The chilaquiles and machaca are a reliable breakfast and for a good price.  It is nice to sit on the patio and watch the passers by on their way to school while enjoying a breakfast that would be considered brunch if I hadn't just gotten up.

I've been here twice for brunch-type occasions.  

Pros: Nice vibe and environment.  Plenty of seating.  Good for groups. Food has generous portions.

Cons: Food isn't that great.  I had the Cajun omelette and it wasn't very good.  

I've heard that the sundeck combos are good and a lot of people come here for taco tuesdays.  However, I'm not a big fan of sweet breakfast foods so I enjoy omlettes and such.  But with my two experiences ordering omelettes, it tasted like something I could make at home and there wasn't anything special about it

Cafe durant's a great place to grab a cheap bite to eat, especially for all you poor Cal students.  They have a bunch of different happy hours that vary depending on the day of the week, but the 3-7pm weekday happy hour is always $5 for any entree, which is an incredibly cheap meal IMO.  The food is pretty good, nothing special, but a great value and usually pretty filling.
Recently I've only been here to get drinks, which has been great.  The deals make it very cheap, so keeping the pitchers flowing for a table full of people doesn't even cost much, though if you like beer you might be a bit disappointed by their selection (though Blue Moon's always a nice default).  
If you're going with a large group of friends you might wanna send a few people to go earlier and grab a table, especially if you want to sit inside.  There's usually always seating, but finding a table large enough to fit everyone inside can be tough, especially on weekend nights.  Speaking of which, it can get LOUD in here, so be prepared for that, especially when everyone's partying for the weekend, but if you go during lunch or non-peak hours you should be fine.  

A great place to grab drinks or a cheap meal and watch a game on TV (there're at least 3 or 4).

How have I not written a review for this place already?!?

I love this place! There are so many great memories here for me, so I am biased.  I think I would regularly give this place 4 stars, but it earns 5 for some great memories.

In sum:
- Great deals (cheap, tasty food is always a plus)
- Wide variety/selection
- Combos (Such as sundeck combos) available for people like me who want a little of everything
- Friendly service
- Delicious food
- Can be a fast meal (not waiter service) or you can spend a long time hanging out/talking there (some people come and go, and no one will bother you about it)
- Outside patio great when sunny/good weather
- Indoor seating available too
- Casual
- Accepts credit cards
- Convenient location for Cal students

Cafe Durant is a solid option that provides decent food at moderate to ridiculously cheap prices. Ridiculously cheap: Taco Tuesday's - $1 per small taco and $2 beers. They also have a "beat the clock" equivalent on Friday's for better prices than Bear's Lair. What's more, there is a balcony that overlooks the street as well as a huge indoors with big tables (good for bit parties). I give it four stars because if you limit your goings to Taco Tuesday or their version of beat the clock, you are bound to enjoy yourself & do well for very little cost. As for any other occasion -- ie, going out to lunch or dinner -- I'd put it at 3 stars.
Really cheap happy hour. How did I not know this before?? It's only $5 for everything on their menu! Go Monday thru Friday from 4-7pm!
