I'm writing this review now because I just discovered Taco Tuesdays..although I have been coming here for the past 4 years during college. $1, $2 beer. nom nom.. they always have such good deals!! their food is OKAY but the portions are big and I love sitting outside on a sunny day. I'll definitely come back for Taco Tuesday when I'm in Berkeley.

if i wasnt so ravishingly hungry, i would probably still be standing there right now reading the entire menu. i can see this being a really popular spot on weekends during the school year for a quick and cheap brunch stop. albeit slightly hard to find for first timers, the upstairs patio is great for observing the commotion of street-life below. 

i had a veggie breakfast burrito, which was ginormous, and definitely not the kind that is wrapped in aluminum that you can eat reasonably with two hands. no, imagine more of small child, or a normal person's limb on your plate. it was exactly the mexican savoriness i needed to start my day! if i lived nearby, i would be here weekly for a guilty indulgence.

Cafe Durant is most certainly, the shit. Every time my friends wanted to meet up for a quick brunch before class or to feel alive again after an epic night of drinking, we always ended up here. The prices are awesomely cheap, the food is so delicious and comforting, and the balcony view of Durant and Telegraph is fun. I love their combo plates -- you can get fruit salad, eggs, and pancakes all on one plate! Their sandwiches are so satisfying too -- I really like the salmon. And half of the menu is Mexican food, so with items like huevos rancheros and breakfast burritoes, you can't go wrong either way. Oh, and their coffee is the perfect amount of bitterness. Nothing like Starbucks that tends to burn the beans. BEST HANGOVER BREAKFAST EVER!

Taste: 3
Value: 3
Service: 3

Had lunch here a while back, and it wasn't anything special. The food was pretty mediocre college food, and I ended up having some plate of average Mexican food.

This place is alright, it's a little low-rent for my taste, but the chorizo omelet is good, and I had the enchiladas and margaritas once, and it was okay. I wouldn't run over, but the place isn't half bad.

The food is pretty tasty and Cafe Durant definitely became one of my favorite places to eat over my time at Berkeley. The Mexican food is pretty Americanized, but if you can get over that, it's not bad. Sometimes, they have a barbecoa plate as a special menu item, and it's BOMB.

If they don't have that, I usually get the steak fajitas or the Mexican combinations. I've also gotten breakfast combinations, which are pretty good, but not as tasty as their chilaquiles if you're looking for egg dishes.

This place gets five stars for the following reasons:

1. The Deck
The deck is amazing on sunny days. It's a great place from which to people watch when there are a lot of people out, like on gamedays.

2. Happy Hour
Five dollar pitchers! Beer pong tables!

3. Recent remodeling. 
The new tiles look nice. They made a nice new bathroom that connects to the dining room too (you used to have to go through the kitchen to a pretty sketchy looking bathroom). New HD TV's that you can request to be set to the game of your choice.

4. The Management
The people who run it are really nice and responsive.

$1 Tacos on Tuesday with a choice of Steak, Carnitas, Barbacoa, and Chicken.  The steak tacos are soooo good.  The carnitas are not bad either, but the barbacoa and chicken were a little dry.  But for $4 you can try them all for yourself!

I also had the shrimp fajita on a non-taco tuesday and it was pretty good too.  Overall 5 stars for the price and food.

Great little joint for Breakfast. Really inexpensive and pretty large portions. 

Gotta try the pancakes if you're there!

Taco Tuesday!!

$1 Tacos: Chicken, Steak, Barbacoa, Carnitas -   
- All the tacos were good and nearly legit taco-truck quality with plenty of flavors [spicy, salty, tangy, savory] and packed with onions and cilantro.  All the meats were juicy, and it is not the typical dry/grilled steak, or the boiled/pulled pork/chicken.  They might have stir-fried it with the sauce.

The best one hands down was the steak taco because of the sauce flavor, and it is cut like asian-style beef.   

Sit outside on the patio for a view [or to people watch =P]

Decent brunch place, especially for its proximity to campus. I got the Sundeck Breakfast Combo with French Toast, Veggies Omelet, fruit salad, & home fries. The home fries were a bit salty but pretty good (not soggy at all) and pretty comparable to the one at Ann's. I really loved the french toast - perfectly toasted and it stayed unsoggy and had the right amount of powdered sugar. The portion size is smaller than Ann's Kitchen but I think it tastes much better; plus the options for pancakes (lots of fruit pancakes) is better here.

One of my default places to go when I was a student. It had breakfast food AND Mexican food. Yummm!! I used to go an omelet of sorts along with an horchata and there aren't many places that give you that luxury.

I wish I it was open all day, but they close in the early afternoon. booo.

But, they're balcony is a great place to eat and people watch during good weather. 

4 stars!!!

Would definitely recommend this place. Most items are between $6-8, but the portion sizes are really big so it's definitely worth it. I've gotten a burger here and a turkey avocado sandwich, and they both came with really large servings of fries and left me feeling super full. 

Also, there's almost never that many people here so it's a nice place to catch up/have a nice conversation with friends (especially towards the side of the restaurant, where there are comfy sofas surrounding a coffee table). There's also an incredible variety of breakfast foods, Mexican food, desserts, beverages, and more. So overall, the food is okay, but the nice environment, fast service, and huge portion sizes definitely make this place worth a visit.

Great place for brunch after a night out. 

Get: salmon omelet (they don't skimp on the fish and the capers and feta cheese go perfectly together) or any of the sundeck combos if you want a mix of sweet and savory. I personally think their Mexican dishes/combos are alright...not the best but pretty decent given the price.

Happy Hour: how did I not come here for this earlier in the semester? M-F 3-7pm: $5 entrees and $2 beers. Came here on a Thursday with my fat sociology reader in hand and enjoyed a Corona and pale ale while I did some reading. When it's sunnier and warmer outside, I'll come back to do my finals studying! -- epitome of studying for last semester at Cal (plus there's free wi-fi!)

This hidden little place is alright for a relaxing breakfast.  If it didn't have the patio I doubt it would still be as many people's choice.  It's pretty cheap considering the portion sizes but I prefer places where I don't have to refill my own water.

Great breakfast cafe :) I had this ridiculously HUGE breakfast burrito which came with potatoes (a bit bland, but there's salt on the table so no problem) on the side. You definitely get your money's worth for your serving portion! 

I also like the interior. When you first walk in, the place may seem a bit tiny but you'll notice as you look for a table that the cafe actually expands as you go around the corner. Another (+) for their patio seating, but too bad I haven't been able to eat outside yet because it was raining the first time I came here :T

Definitely coming again!

I just love this place!  I go there all the time between classes because I know I can just sit for hours and do work, ordering eggs here or fruit there.  They have a great balcony for sunny days too!

Beware that they're not open for dinner!

What a nice place to just sit and enjoy the outside! The outside-roof-balcony thing really adds to it, it was my favorite part about this place! Although it would've been nice if I could see straight down from the railing instead of at a gutter. 

I tried their Chicken Guacamole sandwich, and it was very yummy and filling. Haven't had guacamole in a long time.... their prices are very reasonable too, around $6-$8. Huge variety, they had crepes and breakfast foods and other delicious-looking Mexican stuff. 

Very good experience for my first time, I'd never noticed this place before when walking by. I will come here a lot more in the future!
Good for brunch, or afternoon hangouts. Pre-veganism, I used to frequent this place with a friend for fruit pancakes and beer on weekday afternoons. Sit outside and love it.

I used to come here almost every wknd for brunch (using good life to berkeley coupons =P)

They give you big portions.  Fresh squeezed orange juice and horchata are my favorite drinks here.  Something about their huevos rancheros..it's jsut delicious.  Crepe/pancakes/french toast combo plates are also recommended for those with a sweet tooth.

This place is random. The menu is all over the place. Prices are good, the outdoor seating is nice. I will have to try them for breakfast as I wasn't too thrilled with lunch. But its a good place to go with a group of people since their menu has a variety of offerings.

Ah Cafe Durant, our typical sunday brunch place to eat, especially with a hangover from the night before.

The prices are really cheap and the food is pretty good.  Lots of vegetarian options.

I usually get the vegetarian breakfast buritto, but the crepes and pancakes are really good too.

If you are looking for good, cheap eats, Cafe Durant is the place to go.

Pretty decent breakfast grub for the telegraph ave area. We deifintely timed it well by arriving around 10am which seemed to be just before all of the undergrads wake up. After we ordered and I had realized that I forgot to get coffee the line was already snaking around the restaurant. The food was good enough for my picky taste buds. I had the french toast, he had some combo with a fruit filled pancake, a crepe, and a veggie scramble... all looked really good, I was just too full to bother tasting any of it. I love that they have fresh orange juice to order. We will definitely be back sometime soon.

Have been to this place on many occasions including to watch World Cup Final of 2010 (great choice btw). Place is great for breakfast, lunch or casual dinner. They have a pretty extensive menu with burgers, sandwiches, burritos, tacos, both American and Mexican breakfast, meat plates, and drinks as well. My favorites would have to be green enchiladas, wet burrito, breakfast plate D, crepes, and club sandwich. They have ample seating both inside and outside and there are several TV screens usually showing sports (soccer most of the time) - I believe you can even ask them to change to a certain channel (esp if it's for a game). The location is very convenient next to Asian Ghetto and in the heart of Berkeley Telegraph area. The workers are pretty nice and service is reasonably fast, prices are also typical of a similar place. Overall one of my favorite casual spots in Berkeley and if you enjoy watching a soccer game while eating this is a great spot. Highly recommended to those fond of casual Mexican/American dining.

Great place for poor students lol

Do not miss out on their wing Wednesday
Each wing is 45cents!!!

Their Taco Tuesday, thirsty Thursday seems pretty good too although I can't say much cuz i never tried this place on these days.

I'm not 21 yet so I haven't benefited much from their happy hours but I know many ppl go out their for chill drinking on weekdays

Food is pretty good with huge portion.  And they have multiple TVs so it's a great place to cheer for your team and they also have decent wifi too so u can see students trying to get their work done.

An enchilada plate (red cheese or green cheese) and a glass of horchata is $9 even. A glass of horchata is bigger than a glass of fruit juice. It's not very sweet either.

There is plenty of seating during a normal weekday lunch. The tables are big and there are a shitton of outlets, so it would make a good place to study.

I like the fake fireplace, but it's always on so it must waste a lot of electricity...

I love cafe Durant. Whenever I'm up at Berkeley we always end up here for Breakfast. They have a large selection of food including breakfasts, Mexican foods, burgers, sandwiches and the like. The place is always very iconic I've actually been here with a total of 4 different group of Berkeley and Non-Berkeley friends and they have all pointed to this place. So it just seems like a must if your around the Berkeley area.

The place is large, good selection of food with pictures, decent priced, large portions, parking in the structure, its right next to UC Berkeley, and has a nice patio area. For me this is a definite go if I'm in the area.

I am not a hipster- I swear!

But meh.  I've had better.

The place is nice and cozy.  They have a fake fireplace, the tables are neat, and the paint job is nice.  I haven't eaten on the patio, but I've seen torches turned on at night- pretty cool.

The food is pretty bland.  The club sandwiches aren't good, and I really don't like their spiced potatoes.  I have tried their banana, strawberry + nutella crepe, but it was too sweet to be enjoyable.  The Mexican food is a BIG no-no (but then again, almost all Mexican restaurants outside of Mexico are usually a disappointment).

Their hamburgers are good, though! Once in a while (like once every 1-3 months) I drop in for an avocado- bacon burger and for some Chocolate Abuelita.   That's it.

The best thing going for Caf Durant is its breathtaking view of the Telegraph area. Hopefully that will be enough to distract you from the terrible food. Most dishes--and there are a lot on the menu--will leave you reaching for the salt and pepper. I've always lived by the rule that if the menu is more than five pages long beware. There a lot of Mexican and American dishes to choose from so no one goes home hungry. In between bites of your meal, enjoy the music that pumps through the speakers and the cool Berkeley breeze. Saturday and Sunday mornings are the best time to visit Caf Durant when Telegraph is eerily calm.

Thee epitome of a hole in the wall restaurant. Loved their food, loved their prices, loved their location (near the UC campus) pretty amazing. Everything on their menu looks/sounds good. 

I was impressed by the assortment and selection of breakfast items.
I had the Sundeck Special C, wow! They can even accomadate requests for egg whites only. Their crepes were nothing special, but they were pretty good. I loved their pancakes, complete with bananas and chocolate chips baked into them, that was off the hook!

And you cannot beat the prices 6.75 for something of that magnitude, it was a lot of food, and best of all it was filling :)

Came here for the first time today. :D

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to dine in, so I wasn't able to experience the atmosphere of the place.

I ordered a Cabo Wabo Burrito in the spinach wrap, and it was pretty darn tasty. The potatoes and green beans were a nice surprise, and the mango salsa was absolutely DELISH. However, it wasn't put together too well and the rice/mangoes fell out as I was eating. :[
The order came with a side of chips... didn't get as many as I would have liked, but the price was good, so I mustn't complain.

I'm looking forward to trying their breakfast menu items in the near future. :]

I use to go here often back in college...I came back here for the first time in a long while...omg the service stinks!!! I ordered a side of onion rings... and it took 5 reminders to the waiter, walked up to the counter with the cashier telling me they ran out and the waiter was suppose to tell me... the waiter never bothered but kept ignoring me....and it took another 10 mins just for regular fries. who waits that long for just a side order??!

you would think with service like this they would offer you a free meal and return your money...they should either being getting new employees or better service.

This place is awesome!  You can always find a table, portions are huge, and they have a wide variety of breakfast items to choose from.  I usually share a fruit crepe and the eggs Benedict or the eggs Florentine with a friend.  Cafe Durant is close to campus, making it a convenient place to meet with friends for breakfast/brunch.

Prices are very low!
A good place for breakfast, I'll second the motion for the fruit filled pancakes.

Pass. I used to go here now and again, and came back recently to give it another shot. People working there are pretty unfriendly and the food (particularly breakfast) is slightly below mediocre. I had some really poorly cooked eggs, a couple of unpleasant pancakes, and a burned grilled cheese. Coffee is always burned. Yup, pass.

This is one of my favorite places to eat in Berkeley. It's a little pricey for what it is, but they do have fantastic sandwiches and really good breakfast options. I usually came here with my friends on lazy Sunday afternoons and I loved the outdoor seating area. 

Yeah the tables could use maybe a wipe down a little more often, but seriously, as long as you aren't a priss then you won't have a problem with bussing your own dishes or having the ambiance get in your way. It's on Telegraph and Durant, let's not pretend this is northern Shattuck where everything is more beautiful.

all their savory stuff is pretty greasy (but expected at a mexican diner). 
also i dont know what they did with my pancakes in the morning (i got the one with slices of strawberry inside) but it was so gross! cold and stale!!

I love getting breakfast/brunch here on the weekends! Portions are large but not so big that you feel like you need a nap right afterwards. I love their eggs benedict and french toast - not really Mexican, but it's very consistently yummy. I haven't tried any of the lunch (and now dinner) items, so I can't comment on those, but definitely go if you're looking for a relatively inexpensive, delicious breakfast!

I like to get breakfast here and eating on their sundeck is pretty nice on a warm sunny day. It's about one of the rare places around the southside of campus that you can get pancakes so that's a plus for me. I didn't really like how their syrup containers were open outside --saw a bee crawl around one -_- but I would still go here again

Like everyone else is saying, for the price, it's a solid place. You can't really complain about things like runny black beans and watery salsa when the portions are bigger than texas and you're a college student who likes to turn one meal into three. I'm gonna try their french toast, because they seem to be the talk of the town, but I ordered huevos rancheros and they were runny (but in a good way) and just totally satisfying. Just don't eat too fast. I'm throwing in an extra star because it's really quite pleasant if you sit outside on the patio/deck.

Our order sounded delicious - chilaquiles, home fries, mocha, and orange juice. It was not. The chilaquiles were a mess of cold eggs over soggy chips and the home fries were cold and not crispy at all. The atmosphere is kind of dive-bar ish and the outdoor umbrellas were falling on top of guests. I rarely regret a meal, but that was one of them.

YUMMY! Mexican food is the bomb! Actually, I came here for breakfast and got the veggie omelet. At 6.95 with lots of veggies and not a whole lot of oil, this is great. I would love to come back and try their mexican dishes. YUM YUM.

I don't know why I don't come here more often, they have some good deals. Taco Tuesdays for example: $1 tacos and $2 bottle coronas? count me in!

In addition, I think they have something similar to beat the clock (bear's lair) but better. From 5-6 pm = $5 pitcher, 6-7pm = $6 pitcher and so forth. I don't know their entire beer selection but that sounds good to me.

I've really only been here for breakfast and lunch, and I'm always happy that their salsas and jalapenos are stocked and that you get TWO different types of beans (for the entrees). At my most recent visit, I had flautas (YUM) but the chicken tasted kind of rubbery. That's why I can't give this place 5 stars. Everything else was pretty decent though. I now know to take advantage of their beer deals in addition to their beans and their breakfast plates...such as: banana pancakes, french toast, crepes... their selection is pretty amazing. Most plates come with home fries too, and those are cooked really well (i.e. soft on the inside, crispy on the outside :D)

FYI - It's located upstairs down a hall on durant ave. Nice deck for when it's warm and sunny outside.

Cafe Durant and a Bloody Mary are all you need to get rid of a nasty hangover. Their menu is 1/4 diner fare, 1/2 Mexican and 1/4 crepes. It is the only place I have ever been that has a combo plate with crepes, pancakes, an omelet and a fruit cup. Don't go to this place if you are a carb watcher/carb hater/complete idiot who still thinks a low carb diet will shrink off your freshman 15. 

The deck is big and wonderful when it is nice outside, but only if you can drag your ass there before 10am on weekends; after that the place is crawling with Cal students and becomes annoying, as most places that are crawling with Cal students tend to be. Oh, and they take credit cards.

Long story short, this place was designed with the poor hungover college kid in mind. I'm a poet and didn't know it. Word. Get the OJ -- it's fresh squeezed.

Stopped by to grab something to eat with the boyfriend before class. It serves basic american breakfasts, crepes, and a huge variety mexican food. I wasn't in the mood for mexican foods so I decided to go to with 2 eggs breakfast with bacon. Not very good.

Maybe it's because it's because it's a mexican place so so they specialize more in mexican foods, but is it unfair for me to expect them to at least cook the potatoes right? Everything came out semi warm. The toast, the eggs, the bacon, and lastly, the potatoes. And the potatoes were burn to a crisp. I mean, come one now. If they're burnt so badly, they HAD to of been heated up to the extreme, right?! Why is it that burnt potatoes aren't even hot?! The bacon also looked pretty old, like someone had fried it beforehand and then left it there to be microwaved and served whenever it got ordered. The toast wasn't even warm enough to melt whatever little amount of butter I tried to apply on it. Boyfriend got the eggs benedict breakfast and hated it too. But at least his eggs were hot.

Yuk! Yuk! Yuk!

Too salty and the beans were cold.  The day I went was cold and raining and the restaurant needed heat.  It was cold inside and then the food came and the beans and rice were cold, almost if they had just come from the refrigerator.  Terrible. Don't Go.

Went during happy hour (3-7) to get my $5 grub on. I got steak fajitas, my bf got a chile verde burrito, chips and salsa, a pitcher of beer, and horchata. The plus is that we got everything for about $20 and it looked pretty. The downside was that the food wasn't very good and made us feel bloated. Haha. The 2nd floor deck is super nice though. I would go there again, but maybe get breakfast because their Mexican food wasn't all that.

I feel like I have to give Cafe Durant more chance because they offer so much. This might turn into a disaster, though. 

TIP: Come hungry. You could technically order a Breakfast Combo and share, because each combo comes with four different items. 

Why might it become a disaster, you ask, if I give Cafe Durant more chances? Because if everything else turns out like my first experience, then I will have wasted a bit of cash. But you will read my warnings, and I will save YOU some cash. ...Anyway. 

My boyfriend and I came here for brunch on a sunny late August Sunday. Fairly standard setup to speed things up--order at the counter, take a number, sit down, get your own utensils and water cups. The food came quickly.  I ordered Breakfast Combo B.

It was a lot of food, but I wasn't satisfied. There just wasn't any flavor. The fruit combo pancake looked crazy--think ooey gooey banana slices, strawberry slices, and blueberries and their juices melded into a pancake--but tasted alright. The texture was off though, very rubbery. The french toast just tasted like fried bread, even with syrup and the powdered sugar sprinkled on top. The vegetable omelette was bland in taste, even with pepper sprinkled on it, and rubbery and tough in texture. The vegetables inside were okay. The fruit cup had strawberries, cantaloupe, honeydew--pretty standard. 

It was all just very... okay. Thoughts running through my head: "Alright. Cool. I'm eating a piece of this pancake... but I don't taste it. Okay, how about this omelette? Hard to chew and I don't really taste it. French toast... fried bread. Hmm."  

So why do I think I'll end up giving them more chances? It was decent for the price ($7). It's a good amount of food if you're really hungry. There are so many other things on the menu to try--maybe breakfast just isn't that good. They have what looks like a decent happy hour. But--and now you know why--it could end in disaster. Stay tuned.

i would like to go back just to sit on the sundeck. but for this visit, i just ordered the sundeck (A): eggs benedict, french toast, fruit salad, home fries. the eggs appeared to be on a small pancake rather than an english muffin and the home fries were probably the worst ive had. the french toast was alright and the fruit salad small but fresh. but for $7, its not a bad deal. try the mango juice, though, its amazing! 

its a hodge-podge kinda place. you can order a burrito or burger, crepes or fajitas, pancakes or enchiladas... beer or smoothies. its upstairs past the korean restaurant (and past a swarm of always-there flies) and has a sky light. yay for skylights! 

ps apparently cafe durant has $1 taco tuesdays, thirsty thursdays and tgi friday $3 margaritas! they are also avid cal fans. go bears!

Large menu + good prices + good view + best bathroom in Berkeley + possibility of eating Mexican food and breakfast and hamburger at same time + pretty big portions = added to our starting rotation of berkeley restaurants.

Although after a while you kind of realize that all the food sort of has the same mediocre/stale/bland quality to it.

This place has the best daily deals around. Happy hour all entrees are 5$, and beer is 2$, before 7. Amazing.

I generally like Cafe Durant alright, but after eating lunch there the other day (I had chicken enchiladas) I endured a night of rather unpleasant stomach issues. I've been food poisoned before, and it wasn't like that, but something in the food made my stomach and bowels rather vengeful. I eat Mexican food all the time and don't have any problems with it.  I would have given Cafe Durant 3-4 stars, but questionable quasi-food poisoning knocks that down to a sub-par score for sure.  If I was positive I had been food poisoned by them I would obviously give them a 1.  So I've definitely had good meals and great fresh squeezed OJ here in the past, but I'm afraid to go back and have another "special" following night.
Nothing fancy, but good when I'm randomly craving breakfast food and am in the campus area.  I usually default to one of the breakfast combos, and it does the trick.

The food here was just ok, wasn't amazing or anything. But they are now open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner now!

But the only reason why'd I would come here again is for the view. The spectacular view on the 2nd floor outside let's you see quite a bit of a city view.

New discovery as a senior at Cal. This place ain't half bad to study at! IF and this is a big if, you come on a weekday early to lunchtime-ish. Breakfast foods, big tables, beer, and free wi-fi! Perfect combination for a study session. Minus the beer. Replace with a new drink I invented today that I dubbed Mexican Horchata Cold Chocolate. It requires a half drunk Horchata and Mexican Hot Chocolate, put it together and voilà! New drink. If you do not like cinnamon, do not try this. It's like a drink version of the cinnamon challenge. Except do-able and delicious. I'm pretty sure this is the first Mexican Hot Chocolate that I've tried that is authentic because I saw the blended bits in the drink, and from the limited knowledge I have from my friend, making of this drink involves blending...with a blender.  

Tried the Sundeck Combo with Chocolate Chip Banana Pancake, fruit salad, strawberry and banana crepe, and veggie omelet. A lot of food! I thought everything was very yummy and liked the fact that I could use the fruit from the salad on my crepe. It did get kinda sweet but I snuck a couple of savory and deliciously filling bites from the breakfast burrito. That thing is monstrous burrito with lotsa fillings, generously topped with salsa, guac, and sour cream. Don't think I could ever tackle that on my own, but it was SO GOOD. Bf was full from this meal the whole day. 

Don't think that I would make this my regular studying spot, but will come here time strategically and when I'm craving breakfast. Who knew my hangover spot could also be an occasional studying spot. :)

This is a great cafe to eat anything from Mexican food to
breakfast food to American food.  Recently me and some 
pals were watching soccer on TV.  The vibe is great inside
when there is a crowd.  I've ate at this
joint a couple of times, there enchiladas are superb, as are 
their burritos!  Plenty huge portions
Outside it can get hot on the roof but it is scenic and they do have
tables with umbrellas.  I've ate at this
joint a couple of times, there enchiladas are superb, as are 
their breakfast burritos!   And there fajitas as to die for.
I think I am also madly in love with their desert crepes. 
They are mouth watering yummy!  I'll have one anytime of the day.

Quick service, generous portions, great price (especially the Sundeck portions), and open at 7:30am every day of the week!

Unfortunately, the quality and taste isn't the best...I mean, definitely okay but nothing to rave about. 

I usually get the Sundeck Combo B but opted for the Californian omelet last weekend. It barely had any flavor! The egg looked and tasted fried and I was deeply disappointed by the 3 slivers of avocado hangin' out inside. 

The home fries were similarly listless and tasteless. I strangely enjoyed the toast though. Perfect texture and crunchiness.

BUT it's $5 per entree at happy hour and for THAT price, I'd go back.

This is a great place that is kind of hidden. I didn't realize it was there until one of my buddies showed me where it was. But the enchiladas here are awesome. Didn't agree with my stomach too well but it was worth it. Will be back to try some other dishes soon.

I've eaten here twice.  I like sitting on the balcony looking over the street.  The food is fine, the pricing is fine, the wait time is fine - but it's just that.  It's not going to blow you away, but shouldn't be a big disappointment either.  I'm not in a hurry to go back, but I wouldn't object to it if the proposition came up.

Great college town food.

Decent food. Ridiculously cheap prices. If I had gone to UC Berkeley, this place would have been on my standby list. Cheap prices for decent food (quality & taste) and good portions.  They seem to be known for their pancakes and they appear to be quite tasty.  You'll leave satisfied, maybe not wow'ed, but satisfied and not feeling like you got ripped off or like you need to eat something else.

Reasonable place for breakfast. Hueva a la Mexicana were solid and Eggs Florentine were impressive, though the egg was fried instead of poached. You get free coffee with a student ID. You have to get our own water, napkins, and utensils and I think you have to bus yourself (well, we did). Right in the 3 star range.
food was okay. food is cheap. they have a variety of food. it was a nice sunny day and i sat outside so that felt nice. i didn't really think it was anything special tho.. =P

this place was okay, fine, they were on the good side of okay.

first of all, the outdoor patio, although a nice idea in theory, is kinda run down, dirty, and dingy

I have only been here for breakfast, and I ordered the sundeck D combo, which consisted of a strawberry crepe, a veggie omelet, and a chocolate-banana pancake. 
here's the breakdown:
- the crepe was good, i'd say it was the best part of the meal, but this is probably because it's hard to make a crepe taste bad, i mean it's fried batter, strawberries, and whipped cream
- the veggie omelet was on the small side, and it was kinda bland. i mean i liked the veggies it had in it, but it was just lacking flavor somehow. i'm not quite sure why..... also, this was the first thing on the plate that i ate, because i like my omelets hot, so i literally ate it the second the server put my plate down, but it wasn't even that hott. it wasn't really even that warm, so that was dissappointing.
- the pancake was just totally average, it just tasted like warm, sweet bread with bananas and chocolate mixed in. it wasn't bad, but it definitely wasn't anything special.
- latte, definitely not worth it. the latte was served lukewarm, which i was not happy about, and the coffee was not especially tasty or strong

so overall, this place was pretty mediocre
the prices are pretty cheap though so i guess they have that going for them

also, I have never had the mexican food from here, but I've heard that it's good, so maybe i just didn't try the right thing
it's worth a shot to try the mexican food i guess, but whenever I'm near this place i always opt for asian ghetto instead, it's just better

Cafe Durant is a really solid selection if you order at the right times.  I try to take advantage of their happy hour deals, when all entrees are 5 bucks.  My favorite is the Don Diablo burrito, which, for 5 bucks, blows la burrita and panchos out of the water.  They also have a decent salsa bar on the side should you choose to dine in.  The menu is extensive and diverse, so if you're the type that likes to mix it up, this is the place for you.  It always boggles my mind how many upperclassmen have failed to try this place, despite the fact that it's situated at the heart of the berkeley food scene.  My only supposition would be that people are just too lazy to walk up the flight of stairs -.-  Still, for the thrifty college student I highly recommend this place.  If you have the chance, try to take advantage of their daily deals -- mostly notably "taco tuesday's" or "wing wednesday."  I've tried wing wednesday (45 cents/wing) and i must say that the wings were much better than I expected -- well sauced and of respectable size.

Awesome and underrated place for brunch or Mexican food! 

The stairs up to Cafe Durant are kind of hidden and always overlooked because people go to Asian Ghetto by default. However, I love Cafe Durant! They have really good brunch plates, with pancakes, omelettes, crepes, and a fruit bowl, all for around $7 :) Great pick-me-up in the morning.

The Mexican food here is slightly above average, but when you take price into consideration, it's definitely worth it. I once got a burrito and chips and a taco salad for $8. The burrito was really big, too!

I definitely recommend this place for group brunches or lunches. Go on a nice day so you can sit on the patio outside!

it gets 2 star for the upstairs view..and yes u see some interesting stuff happening on the streets of berkeley. 

The food is gross, i am big on quality deli meat, i was excited for my fabulous turkey club and when i get it its freakin OSCAR MYER MEAT! nasty. If i wanted cheap processed turkey i would have just gone to the golden bear. I got nasty wonder bread, oscar myer turkey crap, ice burg lettuce and flavor less tomatoes.  and it wasn't that cheap, i mean i get some quality sanwiches at Cafe Milano (which is closer to campus may i add) AND i get a freakin salad on the side.

This place sux, i hate it because they fooled me into thinking the sandwich in the picture was the one they actually serve. On the other hand i hear the breakfast is good i am not that fond of checking it out...i have my own breakfast place that claims my arteries. That place u may ask is the one and only Anne's Kitchen. duh.

The only thing I'd ever gotten here was the Huevos Rancheros but that is because it is so damn good. It comes with eggs with salsa on top, beans, and rice, with a side of tortillas. I usually mix it all together and scoop it up with a piece of tortilla but I guess you could eat it separately. Also, their horchata has just the right amount of cinnamon.

There is a nice patio area with shade which lets you forget for a while that you are eating on Durant Ave. Maybe you are vacationing in a Mexican villa next to the ocean. Maybe. Prices are reasonable for brunch, and the portions are so large that it's worth it.

I love this place. Their balcony, the cheap beer, the yummy $1 tacos on Tuesdays, and occasionally their wings too. oh and their nachos with steak!!

Since discovering their amazing happy hour each day, I have been a huge fan of this place. On a nice day, their patio is amazing. Their food is pretty good especially their nachos and I really enjoy their tacos.

Complaints:
-get more flavors of wings on wednesdays!! 45cents is good but i dont wanna eat only buffalo wings
-the tables can get pretty dirty especially when people dont clean up after themselves so maybe they need more workers
-the service isnt good -- theyre actually kinda rude

I come here for cheap beer and pretty yummy food.

i've began to really like this place. i've had the mexican breakfasts both times that i went and i liked it quite a bit. the atmosphere is great and the place is very cozy and cute. the portion is more than enough and kept me hungry well pass a second meal. the people there are quite professional and nice. the only thing i find weird sometimes is the cheese in the tortillas... i don't like that too much.

I'm pretty surprised this place gets four and five star reviews, but I figure it's because it is being compared to places like Steve's Korean BBQ and Mandarin House in the Asian Ghetto...

I had the Cajun omelette and a cup of coffee, with a strawberry and nutella crepe. The food was alright in the sense that it tasted fine... but I think anyone who can cook could make the same thing or better with ingredients at home. The omelette was a bit oily with some spicy sausage and jalapeños, nothing special. The crepe was a crepe. Again nothing really great about it, but not bad per se... 

What gets this a 2 instead of a three is the coffee. This was coffee-machine flavored tea, if anything. Any human who has ever made coffee before should know that coffee is not supposed to be that clear, even if they didn't taste it first. It was honestly terrible, even at 8am when I was in dire need for a cup... I couldn't finish and I gave up. 

I guess it would be an acceptable place to go if you a) don't like to go to the grocery store, b) really don't like cooking in the morning and c) have no other options. But I think for most people, that's not the case.

If you need a hearty breakfast, Cafe Durant is a pretty good and convenient place to get it. I got strawberry pancakes, short stack. Not the BEST pancakes I've ever had, but they were well made. There's a lot of variety here. Prices are a little on the higher side, in my opinion...
Good place to get some beer with friends. Great rooftop outdoor seating, but other that it's nothing special

List: Berkeley's Cheapest Eats

OK, so you can't eat here for under five dollars.  But, I still think it's Berkeley's best value for brunch.  For about $7 you can get a big plate of any number of breakfast items (steak and eggs, waffles, crepes, whatever) and a coffee.  Their roof-top patio is the best place on Telegraph Ave. to find yourself on a sunny Sunday morning.  Of course everyone else in Berkeley has the same idea, so show up early if you don't want to wait for a table.  Four out of five past due notices from Sallie Mae.
Happy hour from 3-7 from Monday to Friday?! I'm there! The food is delicious and you get good-sized portions. There's also lots of tables and always places to sit.

This place is great for brunch, and gets really busy on Sundays especially. It's located in the upstairs part of a Korean restaurant; not sure if that restaurant changed, but it's next to Lotus House and near Asian Ghetto.

The restaurant has a very homey and cultural decor. There are television sets showing Animal Planet or something, and there's a patio for those who want to bask in the sun and observe students and homeless people wandering about. The best dishes are the Sundeck Combos and the Mexican combos. The food is very filling!! Their horchata's really sweet, but the food comes to you very quickly.

Frequented this place all the time while I was at Cal. 

Super cheap, filling breakfast. Best thing is you can customize/mix and match side dishes and they don't mind.

I like coming here after a night out but the prices are a tad high for berkeley students and the portions are not as large as I'd hope for. Still delicious and I hear the happy hour deals are great (although I haven't been yet). I like this place for the most part and continue coming back.

I always used to come to this place last year to treat myself after a gruelingly early Thursday 8 AM UGBA discussion.  I love sitting outside on the sunny upstairs patio, lingering over delicious chocolate chip pancakes while ponderously filling in the Daily Cal crossword.  If you're a Cal student, there's a student specials board with discounted prices.  Always a plus in my book.

I went again this weekend with a group of friends from out of town, and tried the Enchilada plate.  It came with two cheese enchiladas, one in red sauce and one in green sauce, plus your usual bean/rice/lettuce sides, for less than $5.  Decent price, amazing enchiladas.  I'm still craving those enchiladas days later -- I tried some at Wahoo's today and they just didn't live up to the perfection of Cafe Durant's.

Conclusion: "Yay! I'm a fan."  This is a great little place, yet sadly unknown to many passersby who frequent this area of Durant.

I eat here for the novelty, not for the food. Club sandwich is decent, though I wish it came with real fries as opposed to potatoes. Seems like their sides are just based on potatoes, toast, or an assortment of beans. The $3 cup of mango juice that costs $5/gallon at Costco? nothx.

I used to come here only for lunch to share some nachos or munch on a burrito while I pretended to read for my afternoon classes. Now I actually do my reading and come here more often!

The food is pretty decent and they have gotten a lot better about coming and getting your food since I used to come here as a freshman. They must have hired new (and more!) people in the three years that I have been here. I was here at this year's Cinco De Mayo where the place was packed and they had four people scouring the dining hall making sure no dining numbers were still waiting so they've definitely gotten a lot better then they used to be! 

I would recommend their breakfast burritos, although their home fries kind of suck. They're just seasoned potatoes and not "real" home fries like I've had at diners. The nachos are pretty good (and definitely sharable) and I love their happy hour specials of $5 entrees and $2 beers. A word of advice on the beers though: they only have PBR and Bud Light (or Miller Light) on draft. If you can handle that, come here for their beat the clock knock-off on Fridays: $5 pitchers at 5 pm, $6 at 6 pm, etc. If you want to come here for Coronas, make sure you come during TACO TUESDAYS $2 Coronas and $1 tacos that's what's up! Margarita-wise, do not get the pina coloda. It's seriously a pina coloda flavored margarita not a pina coloda! 

Seriously, just come straight up for the specials. Taco Tuesdays rock. Happy Hours are great. And Wing Wednesdays with 45 cent wings are decent too and with their patio and some couches in the middle of the dining room, the place is actually decent to hang around with friends and chat it up! This place is cheap-ass student approved!
I like this place. Good food better prices

Not a bad place for brunch! I headed here with my cousin around 2 on a Tuesday, so there was absolutely no one there. We sat outside and relaxed under the sun, and had a nice view of meter maids patrolling the street below and gangster wannabes walking around with fitted caps and popped collars. A full Berkeley experience!

I ordered a chorizo breakfast burrito that was served like an enchilada, which was kind of weird. It was smothered in sour cream (gross) and guacamole (not bad). Not the best breakfast burrito I've had, but it was huge and very filling, and the crisped potato cubes on the side were delicious! A hearty breakfast (er...lunch), very reasonably priced, and a cool place to chill.

The food is so-so, but the location is pretty good.  You can sit outside, on the rooftop and overlook Durant, watching the crazy people screaming or the hungover freshman wandering down the street.  I usually just go with the usual combo of bacon, eggs, and toast and they don't mess it up, so I can't complain.

I wasn't expecting very much from Cafe Durant but I got a steak breakfast burrito and I pleasantly surprised by the taste and size of the burrito. It was friggin HUGE!! The side of home style potatoes was unexpected but downright tasty. They get a bonus point for the sheer size of their menu - there's tons of breakfast and lunch options to choose from.

First things first, there are a LOT of things on the menu. Every time I come, I am simply overwhelmed by the number of choices. Ever heard the expression, "jack of all trades, master of nothing"? That pretty much describes the food at Cafe Durant. I've never been blown away by the food here, and most of it is pretty forgettable. Mexican dishes usually come with rice and soupy and oversalted beans, and are generally overcooked and fairly dry. The omelets are also nothing to write home about. You do get a LOT food, but I'm not really sure if you'd actually want to eat all of it.

It's recently been renovated, and the new TVs are pretty nice. I've heard good things about Taco Tuesdays - cheap food and cheap booze make a combination that's pretty hard to screw up.

Came here with a large group of friends after a long Saturday. They primarily serve Mexican and American food but also enable you to bring food from the other nearby places. This is part of their open seating / cafeteria-like policy. You order separately (like a Pluto's or Sonoma Chicken Coop) and get an order number so they can deliver your food. It was very convenient for us, but unfortunately the convenience ended there.

After all ordering, we sat at our big table and waited. They had some TVs on and we chatted up, anticipating a separate wait time for each of our dishes. But then the wait got longer. And longer. And no one approached us if our food was coming. We had to ask them.

Theoretically the first person who ordered their food should get their food first (unless the dish takes longer to make). Well that didn't happen for all of us. Some of my friends who ordered in the front of the line got their food LAST. After a 40-PLUS MINUTE WAIT!

One of my friends ordered Onion Rings. She waited and asked several times. They told her it was coming. Then after the 40-plus minute wait, she went up to the counter and asked where her Onion Rings were. They told her they ran out. After 40 minutes of telling her they would come out! ARE YOU KIDDING?! She decided to change her order to regular fries and got no refund or discount for it. Seriously?! This just tells me that they are disorganized, unprofessional and uncaring. She was nice about it and let it slide.

I ordered the Avocado Cheeseburger. The burger was decent. However, the side order of fries...was insufficient. They gave me like 10...individual fries. Seriously?! I thought maybe it was just my plate, but when my other friends got their burger they received the same amount. You might as well say a side order of very little fries.

I also ordered a Peach Smoothie. I was hoping the smoothie would bring a nice relaxing finish to my meal. It didn't. It came out after I was done with my burger. Thanks waiter. Someone ordered me a beer (which came BEFORE my smoothie) so at least I had something to wash the burger down with. When I finally received my smoothie, I instantly regretted it. I was already full and the smoothie looked diluted and icy. In fact, it didn't even look like a smoothie, more like a Slurpee from 7-11. Except it was bland. Since it took so long and tasted so icy and bland, I wouldn't be surprised if they just melt flavored popsicles in the back for their so called "smoothies".

This place is horrendous.

I just ordered hot wings from this place and they were pretty unimpressive. I really don't know how to describe them. They weren't completely horrible and inedible. They certainly weren't stellar. They also weren't Okay. They were...indescribable...but not in a good way. 

Other than the fact that they were a little dry, I don't really know what was wrong with these wings...I just know that nothing was right with them... I certainly won't be back to order them again.

Breakfast burrito? More like I am angry at you and throwing s**t in a box and then going to sling over the counter at you.

To Quote Yelp: Eek! Methinks not.

I only come here for Taco Tuesday and it's probably the best time to eat here! Tacos are literally $1 (seriously, what can you get for a dollar?) and even though they're small, they're pretty good. Pitchers are also $8 (for Lagunitas, at least).

If it's your first time going, it might be hard to find. You need to walk up some sketchy stairs to get there because it's on the second floor so look out for signs from the street! This is definitely an undergrad spot on Tuesdays so it can get really crowded and really loud. Still fun and worth going!

The sundeck special B was amazing!! The pancakes and crepes were soooo good! The huevos rancheros were bad! The eggs runny and the beans and rice didn't have much flavor. We ordered an extra side of bacon and chicken and both were really good. The lime margarita tasted like water and the strawberry margarita tasted like cough syrup! Yuck!! The chips and guacamole were good. The sundeck seating area was charming.

The breakfast burrito...the strawberry+nutella crepes...my favorite!!! Not too expensive ... 

It takes about 10-15 minutes to get your food, even if it's not busy...but I've never had a bad meal here.

Been here once and will never come back again.  First off the cashier was a total B****.  She was rushing us to order and giving us an attitude when we had questions about some of the ingredients (my friend is allergic to several things).  The food is kind of pricey and take forever to come out (there was only one other table in the restaurant).  I ordered crepes and it had some kind of after taste of garlic! I'm not even kidding, all my friends tried a bite and they all said it tasted like raw garlic fell in the batter or something.  I left hungry and will never come back.

Sunday, 11:00AM. 

Neophytes to the Durant Food Court will guess this joint offering only good Mexican food. Locals know that it's solid for brunch too, especially after a late night of partying.

It's tucked upstairs next to the DFC. The canorous, Latin tunes will lure you in. Bright, colorful wall menus will tease your eyes. 

Some notables:
+Sports on the big screens (usually soccer)
+Sweet view from the balcony to enjoy the weather and check out Durant's strip

Grubbed on:
1. Red enchilada
     +Lotsa' cheese on top and filling
2. Veggie omelet 
     - tomatoes were dry

And then...?
Thankfully, I didn't need a hangover subterfuge to enjoy brunch here. Bring the crew and grab a quick meal on the balcony.

I wish I could love this place more. I haven't tried anything other than their wings, and they have so much flavor to them! For $0.45/wing for happy hour (Wednesdays) you can't beat the value. However there are inconsistencies in the quality of the wing (quantity of meat per wing, tenderness of meat). As much as I try to not come here, I find myself wanting to come back precisely for their wings. I do want to give them credit for knowing the way to appeal to the college crowd with their happy hour selection. 

Wing flavors: limon, BBQ, hot

I like spiciness, and the hot wings are sufficiently hot. The BBQ wings are often slathered in BBQ sauce, and that's awesome. The limon wings could use some more kick and more flavor, but definitely try them out as well.
Great omelets and margaritas! I love that place. If you ask for a strong margarita, they make a strong margarita :)

Been flashing back to my college years, since a former roommate from those days was living back in Berkeley for about a year. The few times I visited her there (she has now moved to a friend's place in SF for a few weeks before leaving for a journo gig in Nepal - crazy woman!) we visited spots from the olden times.

Cafe Durant is one of them. We never lived far from this place during school years and sometimes we stopped in for a tasty cheap breakfast, whether at breakfast time or not.

Their menu is huge, with burgers, breakfast, and Mexican food. The atmosphere, as others have noted, starts out bad at the entrance, but once you climb the stairs and order your food, the patio is quite nice on sunny mornings/afternoons.

On my latest visit I had fish tacos... which were edible but nothing to write home about. I still think their breakfast items are the best things to have and should have stuck with that.

I was a little disappointed today with Cafe Durant. I usually like their other food plates but I had their chorizo con huevos plate today and it was a little bland. I had to add Tapatio sauce for it to taste better. I was also not a fan of their use of the microwave to heat up tortillas and beans, but maybe that was because I was probably one of their first customers in the morning.

Decent fish tacos, and one of the few places near campus that serves taco salads. 
Go during happy hour. The only time the food is worth the money.

How have I not reviewed this place yet? I've been getting cheap Mexican food here since before college. It's a cool location looking over Durant and Telegraph, especially when they light the torches on the balcony at night. As always, I can't order anything other than burritos when they are available on a menu. The don diablo burrito is yummy, with really flavorful steak and shrimp in generous portions. All the burritos come wet style, too, for the sauce-lovers out there. The super nachos are tasty too, and definitely more than enough for a filling meal.

In my indulgence of 21+ privileges, I came for the happy hour for the first time last Friday. I've never seen the place so packed! Despite the noise and commotion, the servers remained friendly and attentive. One iffy thing in retrospect was the pricing: I thought that a pitcher of beer was $6 after 6pm and my burrito was no more than $7 (in fact, I thought entrees are supposed to be only $5 during happy hour), but somehow the two together came out to ~$16. My friend and I didn't question it at the time, but we should have. Nevertheless, I'm sure I'll be back in the future, among other cheap Mexican places in the area, when I need my regular burrito fix.
This place is delicious. The authenticity of the food is unmatched and their Huevos Rancheros are to die for. Their homemade horchatas bring back memories of my time in Guadalajara. Two thumbs up!

i love breakfast, and i really hated this place. i came here expecting pretty decent food and the place is on durant, aka, asian ghetto. i really thought the food was horrible. decent view from the upstairs balcony, but i really hated the food. bleh

HAPPY HOUR. TACO TUESDAY.

Cafe Durant is my go to place to pre-game for BTC. $5 entrees during happy hour and $8/$10 pitchers all day, every day. Not too shabby. The breakfast foods aren't too bad either.

Cafe Durant is a bit pricier than the other alternatives along Durant Avenue. Nonetheless, I think it provides a solid brunch on the weekends or on the weekdays if you and a couple friends don't have morning classes.

I'd definitely come here again for brunch if I were in town. The french toast is quite memorable and the pancakes can compete with just about any other pancake in the area. Check it out!

Breakfast here is great. Cheap, fast, and tasty. Definitely appreciate that the homefries are fresh and tasty rather than coming out of a freezer bag, and my eggs benedict tasted good even though the eggs were fried instead of poached. 

Definitely would be great hangover food, and makes a good quick and inexpensive alternate to doing brunch at one of the Shattuck standbys.
Flavors do not flow with the portions served. Nice atmosphere. Wouldn't come back...

12/16/2006 
for the price, not a bad place to get breakfast. good benedicts, bad pancakes..but again, can't really complain. having said that, they could really do a better job with the bacon since it's such an essential part of a good breakfast dish. i've been here twice, probably wouldn't go back anytime soon unless i'm really pressed for time.

Whenever I come here, its normally for breakfast/brunch. The food here is pretty good in general and there is nowhere else in Berkeley that serves the same selection of food quite the same as Cafe Durant. I usually make a point of getting the fresh squeezed OJ here from their on-site juicing machine they have. Beware though, several times i've gotten the Sundeck Combos here thinking they taste delicious at the start but overwhelmed by the sweetness by the end. The other plates are great though, and don't suffer from the same drawbacks.

The sundeck seating area is pretty good too. I can always use more sun.

Pretty good food for a reasonable price with the best and fanciest coffee in Cal, I recommend it except for the bitch of a waitress and her daughter that work there.  They seriously need to learn how to smile and stop being such rude ass faces

I was very fond of this place when I was a student at Cal ... a young, impressionable, poor 17 year old.  I'm bling now and the Cafe seems to have lost some of it's luster.  

Came here for brunch after practice.  I forgot that it was a Mexican place. The boy ordered 3 egg breakfast with corned beef hash and I got the salmon omelet.  I ended up eating all my toast and only half my omelet.  The side of bacon was fully consumed though.  Free wifi (that's an upgrade!) and lots of flat panel TVs.  I didn't sit outside since I'd had enough of being cold and outside already that day.

The food was average ... but cheap.  And while people watching is fun, listening to awkward kids half my age gets irritating - FAST.  The nostalgia has faded.

So I went back here and had a Mexican Combo, which ended up being a variation of all the same dish. Fackkkkk.

Chicken Burrito: rice, beans, chicken
Chicken Tostada: rice, beans, chicken, some leafs of lettuce, chips
Chicken Quesadilla: chicken + cheese
Chips and Salsa

As you can see, it's not very.... varied. Luckily there's a salsa bar there now so I had to mix and match my sauces to taste anything different from all of them. I should have gotten the pancakes.

Cafe Durant has a soft spot in my heart, though not necessarily in my stomach.  It reminds me of my college years, when I used to visit at least once a week for no other reason than this place was kind to my negative bank account.  In a way, it's good that my review is coming long after my college and law school days, so my nostalgia wont cloud my judgment (not too much at least).

On the plus side, the location, prices, and overall atmosphere were delightful.  I love sitting in the outdoor patio on a sunny day surrounded by liberal Berkeley-heads like me.  They have an extensive selection of breakfast, sandwiches, and mexican food.  I can't say much about the quality, however.  Breakfast is more like a slight upgrade of Denny's.

I ordered the club sandwich and it took seriously forever to come, but it was definitely worth the wait. It cut into four parts and each part was the size of my fist! It was so freaking good too. The bacon inside the sandwich was so orgasmic and crispy, i thought i died from bacon euphoria.

A lot of ppl get their breakfast/mexican dishes, which are also pretty good, you see the club sandwich is GREAT

Oh mannn.  If I still lived near this place, I would be here all the time.  It is so damn cheap, with just the right portions for someone who needs savory and sweet dishes.  I usually get half of an eggs benedict with one choco chip pancake.  This is the only place that does a benedict combo with pancake or french toast!!!  All brunch places should do this.  Why don't they!?  Now I have to order a whole benedict and whole pancake item like a fatty and box up the rest to go.

I like sitting out on the deck.  It doesn't get much more chill than a wknd brunch on Cafe Durant's deck, watching people below.  I think the three star ratings should really be four... people aren't thinking about how cheap this place is.  To be fair, they don't make a real benedict; their egg is fried not poached.  For the price, though, who cares?  It's still an egg.

Okay, so, I don't exactly have high standards for food. Usually, I can just eat anything and be a-okay with it. Since I've gone to UC Santa Cruz, I've been complaining and crying about how freaking ridiculously terrible the food is. Not once have I ever thought in my entire life, that there could be food that actually sucks more than dorm food, and then I came upon this "cafe". I ordered the Sundeck Combo E which was supposed to come with some sort of pancake, eggs, sausage or bacon, and some potatoes. I ordered the WHITE chocolate chip pancake, scrambled eggs, and sausage. My pancakes weren't white chocolate, in fact, there was NO chocolate. I guess in this ghetto looking cafe where the stairs are about to collapse, they don't have chocolate chip. Not only that, but in the picture, they have a nice little bowl for a little ball of butter, but this time, they just found a stick of butter that looked like it was picked off the side of the street and threw it with my pancakes. The scrambled eggs were just trashy, tasted like they came from a cardboard box. The potatoes just sucked. The sausage was oily, but okay. Overall, this place sucked. The architecture was interesting, definitely unique, but it wasn't very attractive. I wouldn't recommend going here anytime soon.

Everything on the menu *sounds* really really good, but it's hit or miss.  I think the egg breakfast dishes were my favorite... I'd avoid the regular Mexican food (like the flautas & tacos).  Crepes are okay too, but not as good as Crepes-a-go-go.  Sandwiches are huge portions & a little bland.  Prices are very reasonable and there's a lot of seating, which is nice.  Overall, a decent, cheap sit-down place for breakfast or lunch.  I guess I'd describe it as a Mexican Denny's...

One of the hidden beauties of Cafe Durant is actually happy hour.  One day, Beat the Clock was ridiculously full, so we headed to Cafe Durant & ordered a few pitchers of beer.  They also serve regular & strawberry margaritas - it was cheap and pretty good.  I don't think they're equipped to handle a lot of people at once, since they tapped out of beer that day... nonetheless, it's a fun & cheap alternative to Bear's Lair.  The balcony is especially nice on a sunny day.
Food ok, very bad service and rude people.

Maybe I'm not a fan of breakfast food, but I think I can make everything they sell here at my apt.  However, I do really like their breakfast crepes (the sweet one with banana, strawberry, and nutella), and their mexican lunch/dinner dishes.  The best part of cafe durant is HAPPY HOUR.  On the days where beat the clock at Bear's Lair is just too crowded, just come over the Cafe Durant and get your $4 pitchers...or was it $5?  Either way, GREAT price for beer.

You want fast and cheap mexican food? Come here. I came here on taco tuesday and ate 10 tacos. They were fantastic and not your average taco bell hard shell type. Beer is also cheap, but my complaint is the service is pretty rude though, but they are fast.

I'm really a big fan of cafe durant. Many a sunday morning i will come in here with a friend and enjoy their 2-egg plates and a huge glass of homemade horchata. The plate comes with 2 eggs, toast, whatever meat you like, and potatoes. The eggs are perfect, the potatoes are delicious! And this is the only place i know that has corned beef hash (which i love!).

Their whole wheat pancakes are not good, though. i don't know why i thought it'd be a good idea to try a healthy, easy to get wrong breakfast option when they have delicious alternatives.

I definitely consider this place a super chill and fun place to meet up with friends over a few drinks and some cheap and decent eats. Cafe Durant has a ton of space for people to mingle (with both an outdoor patio and indoor seating) with quite a few TVs for people to watch games on. 

One of the best parts about this place is that they have great deals for Happy Hour (basically every day) and their regularly priced food options are already pretty reasonable! The food isn't amazing, but with a cheap beer and some good friends, this place does the job just fine.

Basically if you're starving or need to grab a bite to eat and don't want to wait out in the cold down in the Asian Ghetto, this place works just fine! But yes, Happy Hour here! Good and cheap (and there's a good variety of options)!

Delicious brunch food. LARGE servings, though expensive. I've always gotten the Sundeck combos, which I think offer the best deal. They also have a stamp card, and have a discount listed on the Cal Press Card some years.

Pros:
You can elect to sit out on the patio area, which overlooks Durant street OR you can sit inside and watch TV
You can have as much water as you want to drink, since they just have these water pitchers out for you to take to your table

Cons:
The restaurant people are scary and get annoyed easily if you aren't ordering quickly and intelligently
The servings in the Sundeck combos are growing smaller
You have to bus your dishes (okay, maybe not a NEGATIVE per say, but I still don't really like having to do this at a restaurant)

Cafe Durant is my favorite breakfast spot  in Berkeley. The food is good and the prices are great. There is a nice outside seating area that overhangs Durant St., where a lot of people get work done or browse the internet on the cafe's free high speed wifi over lunch or breakfast. I highly recommend you check it out.

this place has good breakfast items, and the shrimp and steak tacos are awesome because they actually put slices of avocados on them which is a really nice touch.  my old high school classmate owns this joint which makes it even better.  both the american and mexican foods are consistent across the menu.  there's alot of choices to eat downstairs, but why eat downstairs when u could eat in the upstairs balcony with heatlamps?  

tip: no waiters really, just a cafeteria style ordering kinda deal, nonetheless very efficient

Where else can you find a place that specializes in Breakfast, American food, and Mexican food?  Cafe Durant of course!  I love sitting on the balcony on a sunny day with just a view of the buildings and not the dirty streets below haha.  

I tried the steak and eggs here and it was NOT good.  The steak was cooked with onions, as it said on the menu, but the menu did not say there would be some weird red sauce that it is smothered in.  It was gross and kind of hard to eat, but if you like that kind of sauce, it's actually a really good deal because it comes with rice and beans and corn tortillas.  My friend and I gave the guacamole and chips a try, since it was so cheap, but the guacamole tasted like there was too much lime in it.  Not good.  My friends both got breakfast dishes (I don't believe in eating breakfast foods until it is dark) and kept on raving about the good ass pancakes.  They said they were light and fluffy and amazing and then talked about them all day; I guess I should try them when school starts again.  There is a salsa bar, which was nice because it salvaged the chips we got with the disgusting guacamole.  

The menu is very extensive and everything is really cheap, so I will definitely come back to try more items.

I like a lot of things about this place. The out side deck is great on a sunny day, you feel like you are out in So America .,,,, or so I would think   , Ive never been there.

The food is good and even though their prices went up a little , their quantity stayed the same and the quality is good too. If its cold out, you can sit near the fire place and warm up. The coffee is good and they have a nice selection of teas if thats your thing.

You can get a nice Macho Buritto for only $4.50. Thats enough to fill you up if you feel like a buritto in the morning. If your pocket lets you, I would recommend the green cheese enchilada plate. Its $5.75 but worth it. They also have fresh orange juice! Their horchata is not bad either.

Great place to go out on Sunday morning, just be sure to get there early, they are a popular place for the students to go.

Hole in the wall.... Wait more like hole in the attic. 

Look carefully or you'll miss it. Once you discover it, your weekend brunches will not be the same. This place is a great place to study, congregate, loiter, etc. The patio deck creates a very relaxing atmosphere. I love hearing the old traditional Mexican songs playing in the background.

Food is pretty decent. I love the chilaquiles and the yummy sides that ususally come with the entrees: either pinto and black beans, rice, home fries and/or tortillas. The portions are good for the price; most entrees are about $5-$7. Fruit pancakes especially tasty. I recently had a burrito and was not impressed, but that's one miss out of a bunch of hits.

Place looks a bit beat-up (germphobes beware) but overall it's a great little place.

I have never been here before even though I had been living in South Berkeley for over a year.  Mostly it's because I couldn't find the entrance.

The place is sort of dim & feels kinda greasy (think oily smudges on the glass table tops).

The food is fine.  I would advise against the orange juice because it was about 3 fl. oz. for $3.  You can get a lot of oranges & therefore juice for that price.

The price are slightly high for the mediocre quality of the food served ($7.25 for overcooked chicken in overdone, over'salted eggs).

Everyone has those days where they want some greasy comfort food.  If you find yourself having that kid of a day & you happen to be in South Berkeley, then Cafe Durant might just be your stop.

One of my favorite places to take visitors of Berkeley.  I love sitting on the deck on a nice day and eating either some really good breakfast, or some really good Mexican food for a nice brunch.  I know the owner has changed, but hopefully nothing will change.  Great place.

Food: 
-strawberry and nutella crepes: I really think they use the same batter from the pancakes for their crepes...but they just make the crepes thinner. They drench their "crepe" in syrup, which made it unbearably sweet and way too soggy. Worse crepe ever!  

-sundeck breakfast: It came with two chocolate/banana pancakes, a veggie omelet, strawberry crepe,  and a fruit salad. The two pancakes were pretty good. The omelet wasn't bad either. The fruit salad was gross because the fruits tasted really old. The crepe again was soggy and WAY TOO SWEET. 

-berry smoothie: tasted more like sorbet. Too icy and not enough of the creamy, smooth texture smoothies are suppose to be like. 

Price: $6.95 for both the entrees. Not that cheap for the quality of the food and definitely not worth it. 

Service: you bus yourself 

Ambiance: Flies everywhere. The table was sticky. It just seemed very dirty all around. I was afraid to eat the salsa from the salsa bar. I really had this bad feeling that I was going to get food poisoning from here! It did have this nice fireplace there, but the overall feeling I got from the place was run down and dirty. 

Overall: Not a great experience. Not going to come back. For this price, there are other places that offer a solid meal. And you won't be eating in fear that you are going to get sick afterwards!

I live in the Telegraph Ave. area and it's hard to find a place with good all-day breakfast around here. The omelets are AMAZING! I recommend the veggie omelet...of course. Pretty much everything comes with these delicious home fries, which are super flavorful and go well with everything. The Mexican is pretty good too...they have HUGE portions...I can never finish it all. One of the best parts about it though is the great view from the sundeck. In the spring and summer the patio is the best place to be!

The paradox of Cafe Durant is that it's neither a cafe nor is it on Durant. (Ok ok.. I kid. It is on Durant.. sorta.)

If you're a poor college student but you feel like having a decent brunch, Cafe Durant is a good option to have. This place is bizarre is that you can order anything from enchiladas to strawberry-banana crepes to a burger. These chefs know no-boundaries.

They have a pretty sweet deck which is perfect to eat on when the weather is nice. 

Also, it's nearly impossible to find. You have to go into a small alleyway where you half-expect to find a group of crack addicts.

I think one of the primary draws to this place for me is that I feel completely comfortable showing up on Sunday around noon, wearing an oversized Cal hoodie and pajama pants with monkeys on them. Because, let's be honest, Cafe Durant isn't really the classiest establishment. 

It has a decently wide selection of breakfast items, combo plates, and drinks at a reasonable price. The portions are just right, and you get to enjoy them on a lovely outdoor patio, where you have a wonderful view of campus-area Berkeley landmarks like House of Curries and that sad, empty complex that used to house La Val's. After you consume your food (while avoiding the somewhat sketchy looking bits of fruit that come on the plate), you take the rickety staircase down and start dealing with that enormous pile of Sunday homework.

2.7/5 it is what it is.

if you're not a first year and can ask your legs to take you beyond the campus perimeter, then there is a world of great food awaiting you. but for every other occasion, i guess this is what people put up with. 

it's whatevs, really.
This place is horrendous. It only gets 2 stars for sheer convenience. Two food poisonings and it isn't even all that cheap. Ick.

This place confuses me. Crepes, breakfasts, late-night, Mexican, burgers, and shakes. I don't know how to define that theme... but I like it.

Not super-slammed at lunchtime. Reasonable prices. My burrito was big and fat and when I said extra spicy they gave it to me with both barrels. I'm diggin' it. Especially the outdoor patio.

i had brunch out on the deck one early afternoon last summer, and it was a great way to start off a lazy saturday, soaking in the rays.  the food was very mediocre and the place is pretty dirty, but it's cheap, and the proximity to telegraph etc is pretty convenient.

OH I love this place. My cousin took me here and it was delicious. I don't even remember what I ordered but I know I ate the whole thing. Prices are reasonable. I just feel like I'm going to fall either going up or down the stairs when I use them.

I don't know what's up with all these snobs coming on this page complaining about the smallest details of their meal. I for one loved my 5 dollar enchilada plate (in green chile). Speaking from a Mexican-American standpoints, these enchiladas are the best one I've had on South Side so far. Then again I may be biased considering the price. 

The place is really comfortable, across from my table are four other students laughing their butts off and continuously ordering cheap pitchers of beer. There's internet, there's three TV's with different games on. Pretty cool tunes, too. 

I'm wondering to my self why I never came here to eat in the past. After a long day in school, go after 3pm for their $5 entrees. You won't regret it. Or you can keep going to the same old places you go eat to. 

I give this place . . . . two . . . thumbs up!

I've only come for the super cheap beer.  It's cheaper than beat the clock but not as crowded, a little less watered down and you actually get a nice place to sit most of the time.  And what other place in Berkeley beats $2 coronas?  

Have not tried the food, but I'd like to.

"Happy Hour! Mon - Fri $5 Entrees 3pm - 6pm 
All entrees included except for combos

Taco Tuesday - $1 Tacos 5pm - 10pm
Chicken | Steak | Carnitas | Barbacoa | Veggie

Wing it Wednesday - 45¢ Wings 5pm - 10pm

Thirsty Thursday - $2 Beers $3 Margaritas 5pm - 10pm

TGI Friday Pitchers! - Countdown 5pm - 8pm
$5 @ 5pm | $6 @ 6pm | $7 @ 7pm | $8 @ 8pm"

Yup. What more could you ask for?

SUCKS!

Overly priced tacos were disgusting. I seriously didn't know what I was eating. Not coming here for Mexican cuisine again.

Jeez louise.

P.S.: If "The Client is #1" you would acknowledge my existence at the counter instead of looking at me like some fucking retard. Learn how to talk, assface.

Man I HATE Cafe Durant for posting that they open at 7:30am when they clearly DO NOT! RAGE RAGE RAGE!!!!!

Anyways... I ordered the Don Burrito today here and it was good as usual. However! Instead of small shrimps, they used full size ones. Gasp! Looks like they're stepping it up! The Don Burrito for $7 and change is definitely very filling and I highly recommend it. The steak inside is GOOD.

My friend gave me a bit of his Pesto Chicken crepe and it was pretty good. I would've liked it more if the pesto flavor was stronger but the chicken was tender so no complaints there.

Would come again, but NOT at 7:30am -_-

Cafe Durant doesn't have the best food, but I do like the place itself. It has a patio where you can sit and eat while observing the hustle and bustle of Berkeley. It has all kinds of food, and the portions are filling - they're not HUGE, but they're definitely good enough for the prices they charge. My friend recommended their crepes, and although I've heard a lot of people that like their sweet crepes, I think they're average... not the greatest or anything. The potatoes that they serve with their savory crepes tasted kind of weird too. But I do like their selections under the Breakfast section.

Popular place for breakfast. The ambiance is cozy - a deck, self-serve water and condiments, lots of paintings and colorful tiles. They play spanish music all day - one of the small handful of words I know is "corazon", which I hear a lot when I come here - so romantic...

Food is cheap and tasty - the breakfast food outshines the rest. I had a phenomenal veggie omelet here. The pancakes come with super sweet toppings - strawberry, white chocolate, bananas... I like the sundeck combo's a lot, but, looking around, people order all kinds of things on the menu.

Oooo a rooftop cafe!

My first impression when I came in was like... whoa, it feels like Mexico! Hola amigos! Friendly people. The food was good, but the most appealing aspect is the rooftop deck.
