It's a great view and a nice escape from the chaos on Telegraph/Durant. Sorry Hector, I had to dock 1 star... it's kinda ghetto up in there.

Tips: Can't find it? It's upstairs. Look for coupons passed out on the street.

Unfortunately this is another one of those  "approved" places that our group goes to for lunch. So sometimes I get stuck eating here.  The burritos are terrible and greasy.  Its like a taco bell burrito covered in red sketchy sauce. It has the same old shitty nor cal steamed tortilla (why is there a phobia of grilling tortillas up here?). The enchilada thing was less offensive but it was far from good.  If i get sucked into coming to this place again, I will follow the lead of two of my coworkers who only get burgers and breakfast. I give Durant three stars for the cool patio and two anti-stars for the food.

I love this place for the White Chocolate and Strawberry pancakes ($5!! $2 extra for Bacon) while the husband opts for Sundeck special. This is the best spot on a warm sunny morning to absorb some Vitamin D on the outdoor deck.  I must say I am continually thrown off by the entrance and atmosphere of this place - as it looks like shit and I am thrown off by walking past the sketchy chinese places leading up to the Cafe. Past the exterior, this place is a gem.  Granted I have only had the pancakes - why stray from a sure thing!?

The only bad part about this place is how long it takes you to decide what to order. With prices made for students, and a menu a mile long, Cafe Durant is the perfect college town establishment. The ambiance might be grungy, but the breakfast burrito kept me going back every Sunday morning when I lived in Berkeley - and it keeps me coming back even now that I live on the East Coast!

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Berkeley. Don't judge.

It's cheap, fresh, and really tasty. I love the chimichangas and fresh squeezsed OJ and deluxe combo D with the chocolate banana pancakes and the perfect little omelette and a strawberry banana crepe and a fruit salad. oh baby baby, how can you not just start salivating copious copious amounts of saliva? You can also get a margarita or pina colada in a cute little ceramic pot for only 5 bucks! There's a lovely patio that you can sit out on too. I can't think of anything else they could add to make the place better. The location is also a little secret because you have to go up these shady stairs, but that just makes it seem like even more of a treasure! i *heart* you cafe durant have my babies.

The pictures on the wall coming into this place do not do the food justice...  it is killer.  Cafe Durant also has fresh squeezed orange juice at a good price, and a worm sunny patio with lots of tables.

Diner food on southside, hmmm, where to go? There are basically 2 options, here and Ann's. I like Durant Cafe more, it tends to be less greasy. 

It is an okay breakfast place, friendly, relatively quick service. The coffee tends to be fresh, although sometimes it's not. I too like the sundeck combos, but they lack flavor. The homefries could be larger cut and be moister. The pancakes lack any flavor beside the skillet grease. Overall, the mexican breakfasts taste better and fresher. 

I also enjoy sitting on the deck, and I love the cumbia music they play.

Okay, so my friend dragged me to Cafe Durant because he has something against La Burrita (yes, I gave them 4 stars too). I'd been twice before, but only for breakfast, which is mediocre but fairly priced.

The mexican food is pretty good! I'll give them that, with all the authority I have as a half-mexican (hah). I ordered the steak tacos, my friend ordered his usual wet burrito.

We went outside on the patio, and it was a beautiful day! If the weather's good, sit outside because it's great; it may even be why I gave them an extra star!

The presentation of the food is great. Worth the extra dollar I would've saved going to the place across the street. My tacos were BIG and bulging with meat and toppings, with some chips and guacamole on the side. The only thing I was missing was some authentic spicy salsa. But what can I say... some like it hot.

So to all you gringos, come give it a try!

Brunch and mexican food! What a funny sounding combo. They have good combos that come with a good serving of food. Happy hour also has great deals. Try the orange juice if you come for brunch! They squeeze it fresh and it tastes delicious.

Great place to watch games with friends on their tv (place extends to an outside deck and further back into the room)

I'm updating my first review (worst review).

1) They give you SO. MUCH. FOOD. --cheap too!
2) The place is cutesy but it's SO hot...
3) The service is ehhh
4) They have 3 TVs. They don't need 3 TVs.

hmmm... that's all! Aite then lates! :b

I remember going to this cafe with two good friends for a carb filled breakfast, which was delightful.  It's your basic cafe with many combo platters and deals to choose from.  It's very college oriented in the sense that there's a 'Breakfast Club Card' you can use and many students getting their last minute studying done or finishing up that paper.  

A combo minus one star.  Minus half a star for being across the bridge from me (living in SF - boo!) and minus another half for the lack of decent parking.  However, if you're doing a bit of shopping, you will definitely get some energy from the food offered at this establishment.

not fusion food...just a confusion of different breakfast/cafe offerings. decent, affordable offerings. sort of creative - i had white chocolate strawberry pancakes. they also have crepes. and nachos.

I come here for the $5 entrees happy hour (M-F 5-7p). I usually get a burrito. The burrito is pretty large and it comes with chips. They put guacamole and sour cream on the burrito.

The place has TVs so if you want to eat and watch a sports game, this is a good place to go. Or if you want to eat and chill out on the balcony if the weather is nice, that's an option too.

I don't know what these bad reviews are for! 

The french toast here is awesome and the home fries are my fave ever of any place. The fruit pancakes are also fluffy and delish. 

And for those that can't get their own water/utensils/condiments...this is a casual, cheap but good eats, college student kind of place. Go elsewhere for your pampering!

Food's pretty good, the coffee decent (however, a bit overpriced).  My main complaint is the upstairs area which feels like you're in a back alley of North Philadelphia.  The place is not super clean but the crowd is always interesting...if you can score one of the three tables in the front winidow you can just enjoy the world passing by and people watch to your heart's content.

Cafe Durant is one of those places you go to because you love it inside of you. This is one of the best brunch places to go to in Berkeley because their menu is so huge and you get so much food for what you pay. They have a whole outside patio with umbrellas which are always cute to sit under while you eat, and their breakfast specials that come with eggs, crepes, hashbrowns and sausages will fill up anyone!! Great spot to go on a slow morning/afternoon after a night out, but don't expect the food to be spectacular. It is just a little cafe in berkeley that students love for the value and convenience.

its a bit tucked away, so not the easiest place to find, but definitely worth the visit.

its got a large 2nd floor patio with a view of the uc-berkeley/telegraph area, and the inside is large and spacious and well-lit.

food was good, and service was fast. i got a mushroom burger (i think) which was definitely bigger than your run-of-the-mill fast food fare. the fries were good too.

pretty much everytime i've come, there's been a sizable line - its definitely worth the wait and you can't complain about the prices.

I've been here multiple times and today will probably be the last. I've never had a problem with Cafe Durant until today. Today is the first Cal football game of the season and we were hoping to catch the game here and have a nice bite. When we first get to the register, there is chaos already. Another patron comes up and demands for a refund because his friend who ordered his food 30 minutes prior to him received their food and he is still waiting. Should have taken that as a sign to leave already. But the place was pretty empty so I thought it would be nice to be able to sit and watch the game. But I also should have taken that as a sign to leave.

We ask the lady at the register if they were going to broadcast the Cal game later. She replies "No." Then, quickly mutters "Yes, yes.." Well, okay if you say Yes, then I'll stay and order my food. Well, 12pm comes by and the channel on the TVs are still on ESPN, not PAC-12. We ask the server if they're going to broadcast it. She replies, "do you know the channel?" Well no, we didn't.. but she mentioned they have Direct TV. So with a quick internet search we realize Direct TV does not have the PAC-12 network. I sit there grumpily eating my lunch. What kind of restaurant in the heart of bear territory doesn't have the PAC-12 network?? And to lie to us about it saying that they'd show it just so they'd have our service? Unacceptable.

Good riddance Cafe Durant. We're done.

My first date with my boyfriend was here at Cafe Durant.  Today we relived out one year anniversary by going back.  We forgot how yummy it was here.  The menu kept making us change our minds while we were in this long line.  As we got closer to the register, we caved into the best deal on the menu, their sundeck combos.  You get for options for just $6.95!  We have only ate out on the deck, because you can get fresh air and look around at the city.  Next time I'm going to get their Mexican food, should be good.

Hmm, 3.5 stars.  4* for the food, -0.5* for the cost.

This place used to be super-cheap when I was at Cal in the late 90s.  I think it used to be about $3-$3.50 for crepes.  Agree with the other person's nostalgia, haha.  That's why I came back here a few weeks ago.

DAMN the crepes are good.  I believe they're filled with liquid crack.

YUMMMM!  So bummed I found out about this place so late in the game.  It's like a little hidden gem amidst nasty Berkeley food.  Ok, ok, it's not the BEST breakfast---but a breakfast you want to cook at home, but are too lazy to do so.  It's a yummy mixture of a  bunch of stuff you want but don't have time to cook.  Good food. YUMMMM.

OH, and totally affordable!!!

I haven't been here in a while, so I thought I'd give it another go while on southside on a monday morning. I used to be a fan of the sundeck combos (but usually its during hangover mode), now coming here for a regular lunch was eh.....nothing special. 
Got the huevos rancheros, which turned out to be just some eggs and beans with rice. Whatever happened to the tasty red ranchero sauce that makes those huevos OH so good! 

So its a little sad to see such a simple, yet great mexican breakfast dish turned into something boring! And $2.50 for a small orange juice WHAAA??? wayyy to expensive. Maybe you should just reserve this place for hungover and too lazy to reach Venus or La Note!

okay, the lack of stars is not for the food, do not get it wrong. the food is actually quite delicious, which redeemed itself one star higher than what i wanted to rate. 

i went in with a friend after receiving a flyer on the street for one of their breakfast specials, and decided to order otherwise, ordering the chicken burritos, which i specifically asked for no sour cream, and with black beans. the price written on the board was 5.50$, but the guy then proceeds to charge me 6.50$ per burrito, plus tax (~14). puzzled, i ask him, "um, did the black beans magically add a dollar to each burrito or something?" he then looks at me equally puzzled, and then says "oh, 5.95, board." he then asks me for 13$. 

i then look at him even more quizzically, and point at the board, and ask him "isn't the chicken burrito 5.50$?" he says "oh, board wrong, should be 5.95, 12 dollars." i hand him twelve dollars more confused than pissed off, until i calculated that 5.50 x2 plus tax only 11.96. bastard stole 4 cents, without asking if i wanted to give it to them. 

on top of that, both of our burritos had sour cream, cheese, and pinto beans. what a bunch of jerks.

This place panders to everyone and of course pleases no one. It's like meeting one of those dudes who agrees with everything you say. At first you take a liking to him and think that you are that special and interesting, only to realize he does that to everyone and there is not an ounce of sincerity or authenticity to be had. 

Well, save the time on this one and skip the introduction all together.

it's sunday.  i have woken up quite late but have no fear!  brunch is here!  gleefully clutching the address of the new to me cafe durant, i wait for the bus.  each minute that i wait for the bus is another minute my anticipation mounts.  not even the bus lurching into action as i deposited all my laundry booty into the money eater making me trip all the way back to my seat next to a very stinky person could sway me (metaphorically; literally it did thus) from reaching my destination in good spirits!

i reach my destination.  i follow the arrows.  i arrive at: a cash register?  a man takes my order quickly and disappears just the same after thrusting a pokey numbered thing at my partner.  coffee?  oh coooooffeeee?  i look around.  i see the serve yourself water.  i see the salsa bar.  i see the coffee fixins.  i get it!  you get it!  but i didn't think it appropriate to step behind the counter to give myself some coffee!  upon return, the curt fellow gives me a cup.  it is tepid, but it is coffee, and i nurse it back to health with a healthy dose of sugar and cream.

perched on the lanai in a spot closest to the edge, i think, this might not be over yet.  the weather is on my side, i have what i think is the best seat in the house, and it looks like the pancakes come with chocolate chips by default! alas, forty-five minutes later, another crappy cup of coffee later (and i mean really crappy, i have a special place in my heart for crappy coffee and this was worse than that), three parties who came AFTER me getting their food BEFORE me later.  the food arrives.  i immediate jab my pointer finger into the middle of my pancakes.  COLD.  i put my pointer finger in the scrambled egg.  COLD.  i point my pointiest of pointy fingers at the... turkey?  is that even turkey?!?!

maybe i ordered the wrong things.  maybe they made me extra special pancakes and i waited just for them because cold pancakes are special.  but i have never before in my life felt like throwing an adult temper tantrum.  you know what i am talking about?  the kind your dad has thrown after receiving his food and the froth that lands on the face of the server, who has nothing to do with said plated crap but must endure the rant, is so embarrassing that all you can do is wish you had more tinkerbell peelable nail polish to pick at?

i really, really wanted to.  and if the person i love most in the world hadn't been sitting across from me, i may have.

I've only been here for breakfast. For years it was one of my favorite breakfast places near campus.  Well designed and diverse combo plates are surprisingly cheap, including items like crepes, pancakes, french toast, roasted potatoes, fruit salads, etc..  The joint is well hidden up a flight of stairs but worth the searching.  Plus, on nice days one can sit outside on the balcony.  They also serve traditional diner fare like burgers as well as Mexican food, neither of which I've tried.

In the middle of Berkeley's Asian ghetto, up a flight of stairs past a dim sum place, is the Cal kid - laden rooftop haven that is Cafe Durant; a place where you can choose from a huge menu of breakfast, lunch, and dinner dishes, as well as Mexican food, all while admiring sweeping views of Berkeley campus housing, and the north Oakland hills in the distance. 

Cafe Durant is quite a unique place. where you get in a line to order, and they bring your food to you. Service is often quite slow, to be honest, so don't come here if you're in a hurry. 

They have a beer pong table sometimes, and there are often bros in there, being bros, but that's just part of the whole thing, and they never really get that rowdy. They also have super cheap pitchers, if you go during happy hour. The have TVs so you can watch baseball, and a random cast iron stove in the corner. 

Their sandwiches are bomb, and their mole burritos are, as well. You may have to wait a little while, but for a nice, cheap meal, it's worth it. They also let you bring in (non alcoholic, I think) beverages from other places, so you can get boba down the street, and eat it with your bomb - ass brunch.

Also, the tiki torches and rooftop seating at night? Love!

TACO TUESDAY!!!

What more do I have to say? Actually, a lot.

1. Taco Tuesday is fantastic! $1 tacos? YES!
Cafe Durant has a good selection of meats which include steak, chicken, carnitas, ground beef, this one that's slow cooked beef that I seriously can't remember the name of, and my all time favorite--CHILE VERDE!
I recommend you get here early because it gets packs. Cal students hangout here all night and continue to get pitchers of beer. The line does get long so just order as much as you think you can eat to avoid the line.

2. Margaritas!
I believe they're $4.75? A little more than $5 when you add the tax.
Mango, Strawberry, Lime and Peach is what's one their menu I believe.
I just wish they sold them in pitchers like Chevy's. Then my days as a Cal student would have been complete!

3. Breakfast
So many breakfast options. Personally, I just get chilaquiles (skip the sour cream because it's a lot). 

4. The A, B, C, D, combos
What is great is that you can get Mexican or American breakfast. It's a win win situation if you want both. For example, go on Wing Wednesday ($0.45 each!) and then order a combo with it. 
The combos have these options: tostada, burrito, taquitos, quesadilla, and enchilada ( I think). It's a huge meal for under $7. Eat half before your meeting or dance practice then save the rest for later! Trust, you'll finish it all.

5. Location & Ambiance
It's close to campus and they don't care it you're loud. It's always loud except for in the mornings.
I'd have meetings here with folks and it worked out great because there's lots of seating. The outdoor and indoor options are really nice on sunny days or rare hot Berkeley nights (or just when you drink lots of beer for your alcohol jacket).

Now I'm not giving it 4 stars for just the food. Most of the food is pretty standard, it's not over the top. But, I love the tacos.
Sometimes you need loud places that can hold a lot of people, namely college students.
I like the tiki torches and umbrellas. It's comfortable to me.

One more think. there is only ONE (1) bathroom so beware if you're out for a night on the town. Just run to campus. It's not too far!

The menu nearly gave me an anxiety attack.....breakfast, lunch, dinner, all of the above?  

So, I went for the breakfast which was decent; nothing to write home about but it worked.  The real happiness came from the AMAZING margarita....it was really good and tasted pretty authentic. 

I loved the patio..I couldnt imagine NOT eating on the patio!  The place looks pretty shabby but the prices are reasonable so "it's a give n take."

I'd go back...

This place looks like it should be terrible. It's located up some worn concrete stairs and decorated with fake vines. But the breakfasts, oh the breakfasts. Their white chocolate pancakes were my favorite breakfast near campus, and I reserved them for special occasions. They also come in crepe form.

Get something with crepes. One of the five "value breakfasts" or whatever they're called has many different items. You can get a huge, delicious breakfast for like $6, and even though the orange juice is $3, get it; you won't be sorry. The outdoor 2nd story patio is awesome.
Cafe Durant is a great place to start your morning off right-- with a good breakfast and a nice, tall glass of freshly squeezed orange juice. Their fruit pancakes are superb!

breakfast, lunch, or breakfast for lunch,
and you can sit outside overlooking Durant st., very relaxing in good weather.
good food, good prices.

Hands down my favorite breakfast spot in the East Bay.  Everything here is great, and the combination meals allow you to have a little bit of it all--pancakes, crepes, fresh fruit, omelettes, you name it.  Top it off with fresh-squeezed OJ or a smoothie and take it outside to eat on the deck.  As much as I love living in SF, there are certain things about East Bay living that I really do miss, and this is one of them.

The food just wasn't good. I love the patio, though, and the cashier guy was friendly and accommodating! My chicken fajita caesar salad with a diet coke wasn't worth the almost $9 I paid for it. It was as if the iceberg lettuce was washed (yay!) but never rinsed (boo!) so the salad was afloat. The dressing didn't taste anything like a caesar, though the ocean below certainly didn't help. I might go back, just to sit out in the sunshine on a nice day, but ti's definitely not my first choice in Berkeley cuisine. Cafe Durant is perhaps a jack of all trades, master of none.

Cafe Durant is starting to become my go-to place for breakfast food. Their bacon is delicious and I'm a pretty huge fan of their Three Egg Breakfast!

Today, though, they drop down to 3.5 stars in my book. There wasn't very much business (or very many people), but I still found myself waiting for nearly 10 minutes in front of an empty cash register! Several times, different waiters passed by me on their way to and from the kitchen, but not a single person stopped to ask if I had been helped yet. Terrible service!

I must say that this place has the quirkiest decorations and a huge menu you can pick from ranging from breakfast to deserts... can't expect any more from a place in Berkeley. haha

I thought the service was good and the workers were nice. Self-serve for water and condiments. I got the Diablo Burrito (?). I think that's what it was called. I just know that it was REALLY REALLY freakin' spicy! and then I found out the English translation was devil or hell burrito... something like that. Let's just say my mouth was on fire! But a good kind of "on fire".

Good size portions, reasonable prices, friendly service, I'll consider coming back whenever I'm in town. :)

Horchata! Beans! Crepes! Enchiladas! Enormous pancakes! Eggs! Potatoes!

I am ALWAYS a happy panda when I come here. They have great variety and their prices are unbeatable. You can get 2 huge pancakes, potatoes, and eggs for $6.95. I enjoy their Mexican breakfasts a lot (even if it is a bit more on the Tex-Mex side). Plus, the deck seating is fabulous. What better way to spend a sunny, Saturday morning in Berkeley? 

Post-meal I usually realize I ate too much and go into a food coma. Then I don't get any homework done until late that night. BUT SO WORTH IT!

This is a great little breakfast joint with a real Berkeley college-town feel.  They have the best most amazing mixed fruit pancakes I've ever tried and a great sundeck to enjoy them on.  A wide variety of choices including breakfast, sandwiches and mexican.  Really reasonable prices, partly because it is quasi-self-serve, where you walk up to the counter to order, seat yourself, and then they bring it to you.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here to do some interview prep over lunch. You walk up the flight of stairs and turn right to place your order. To the left is the dining area, with a good number of tables and good light from the plexiglass doors. Food is ready in 7 minutes or so, and everything else is self-serve.

|| F O O D ||

DON DIABLO BURRITO: steak, shrimp, onions, Don Diablo sauce, with rice, beans, cheese, guacamole, and sour cream [$6.95]
- Comes with a complementary side of nacho chips! You can ladle some salsa from their small salsa bar.
- The steak and shrimp are yummy and tender, although the rice and beans were much more plentiful. The shrimp is quite delectable, though.
- The Don Diablo sauce is SPICY. To the point it made me tear up. Sniff sniff ;___;
- The guac, sour cream, Don Diablo sauce, and cheese are drizzled on top of the burrito, not inside the burrito. I would have liked the guac inside, but then they would have had to give me more than the little mound on top. Oh mann, that Don Diablo sauce was so taste-bud-inflaming Q__Q

SUPER NACHOS: nachos with melted cheese, fresh salsa, jalapenos, black & pinto beans, drizzles of sour scream, and a dollop of guac [$6.50]
- A large portion that looked tasty! And my friend confirmed that they were c:
- Not too much cheese, which was a bummer. But there was a good balance of the other toppings, so s'okay.

|| C L O S U R E ||

Decent food at decent prices, but there are better places that offer better food. Like the Stuffed Inn omgoodness. But if you want space and time (DIMENSIONS), they have their outdoor patio and late night hours. They also have happy hour and other specials (http://www.cafedurant.com/offers.html), so I could be persuaded to come here again for those reasons only.

I loved going to this place in the weekend mornings when I was in college.  It was always busy, but it was usually worth the wait.  They had great breakfast combos that I never seemed to get tired of.  You know it's good when you still come back to the places after you've graduated from college and now live more than 10 miles away.

Great place to grab a large and yummy brunch! The menu is huge and full of both Mexican and American style breakfast and lunch options. I stared at the pictures for several minutes, trying to decide what to get: And omelet or a crepe? A quesadilla or a sandwich? Prices are around $7 and everything is self-serve--water, napkins, utensils, etc.

Finally, I settled on the Club Sandwich, and my Brunch Buddy got a Sundeck Combination (omelet, crepe, and pancakes?) I got a lot of food--the Club Sandwich came with home fries on the side. It was quite yummy, much to say...turkey (or ham?), bacon, lettuce, cucumber, sprouts, and tomatoes between wheat bread. I had to take it apart though--it was too fat to fit in my mouth. We ate on the cute sun deck.

I will probably be back at some point, once I get my hands on the Berkeley Coupon book, which apparently has Buy 1 get 1 free Coupons for Cafe Durant.

Happy hour is excellent.

Pitchers of PBR and Coor's Light are $5 at 5, and any entree is $5 (sadly, these are considered good prices for Berkeley). I recommend the suicide pitcher, which is half PBR and half Coor's Light.

If you order pitchers, they only give you 1 cup per ID, but children can obviously use self-serve water cups.

Sometimes they have beer pong, which along with the light beer gives this restaurant the potential to become its own frat.

Superior to BTC if you want to hear anything your friend is saying, but sometimes I don't.

Hangover, meet your kryptonite (and on the cheap, too!).

Also: the $5 shakes?  COMPLETELY worth $5.  (Yeah, I had a Pulp Fiction moment the first time I ordered one.)

Why is there cheddar cheese in my enchilada? 
I really don't get it.
The enchilada gravy was sort of flavourful, however.
I did eat it but then again, I did have the munchies.

Cafe Zeb is good enough if you don't want to walk down to Telegraph area etc. But, at one point when I ate here, I found something in my food -- still not quite sure what it was. It was really nasty and I refused to eat the rest of my meal. I guess I really should have brought it to someone's attention...

There's a new and improved Zeb in town thanks to the recent completion of the Boalt School facelift + construction project. Their menu looks great on paper, though I am forlorn about the departure of the southwest chicken salad with the tortilla strips. 

The flank steak sandwich sounded really appealing, but the way that it sat on the sourdough bread was not. The caesar salad was okay. There are a number of other items that I'd go back and order though, so this review is in pending status until further notice.

I enjoyed my meal at Cafe Zeb today! Some of the menu items are pretty pricy, but I thought my turkey&avocado sandwich + mixed greens meal was pretty cheap at about $6-$7. It filled me up and it was really tasty.

My boyfriend got the Californian sandwich without realizing it didn't have meat in it. We're both carnivores so we thought it'd be disappointing, but it was actually really tasty! They were generous with the avocado so it was pretty delicious.

I have meal points so this won't be my go-to spot on campus, but it's a nice change from Ramona's&GBC. I definitely want to come back to try the Nicoise salad because that looked delicious.

I have only tried the Chipotle, Mediterranean, and Asian Chicken salads. They were all pretty decent, but I still think almost $7 was on the high side for a salad. My favorite is the Asian Chicken salad because of the dressing and crunchy noodles tossed in. Otherwise, the Chipotle and Mediterranean salads seemed more generic. 

The BBQ chipotle quesadilla was also pretty decent--filled with lots of cheese and had a side of green salad. 

I'll return to this cafe due to its proximity to work and when I'm too rushed to go home and make lunch.

I love to study at Cafe Zeb! Their menu is a little pricey, however this place don't mind if you bring your own food or drinks! If the cafe gets too crowded, you can always go downstairs and study at their library. Law library is directly underneath the Cafe. They do impose restricted hours for undergraduate access!

I'd say this is the best on-campus cafe. Definitely better than GBC, Ramona's, Pat Brown's, or the Haas Cafe. They mostly have Sandwiches and daily soup, but they have a wide variety of sandwiches. I like their Chicken Schnitzel sandwich, although when I had it again yesterday the Schnitzel was mushier than I would've liked it. Their price is okay, considering the sandwiches are quite big and it comes with a side salad. But if you get the Soup+Sandwich combo, the sandwich is quite small. As for their soups, their Cream of Broccoli soup was awesome, but their Clam Chowder was too diluted. I like the place because it's comfy, new (and thus clean), and close to the upper campus (so I don't have to go down towards Telegraph or asian ghetto to get food). You can also sit outside when the weather's good, and I've also seen people sit at the big stairs when it's sunny and warm. oh and, I absolutely LOVE their Freshly squeezed lemonade - just about the right soure-ness!

I mean really, what do you expect from on-campus food? 

Zeb's salads are huge and delicious. I recommend the southwest. Their sandwiches have sprouts and fresh produce--what more can you ask for? I recommend the Californian and the Chicken. Great, healthy, quick, and inexpensive lunch.

Yes, there is a line at lunchtime. That's because people get out of class and want food at lunchtime. But wait a few minutes, and especially for the price, you won't be dissatisfied.

The only positive thing about this cafe is the location.  It's convenient if you're at the law school and don't want to leave the building.  If that's the case, I recommend that you get something prepackaged.  My experiences include 1) a bagel that tasted like mold, 2) coffee so disgusting that I had to throw it out (and I have a high tolerance for mediocre coffee, 3) the most repulsive chicken sandwich I have ever had - brown, strong-tasting chicken, covered in a pinkish dressing that looked and tasted equally foul.  

Why do I keep coming back?  I was hoping for improvement, and I see so many people eating there, that I couldn't imagine it could be this bad.  I strongly recommend taking the 2 minute hike up the hill to the International cafe instead.  They have better food, prices, music and nicer staff.

I just had to downgrade the star rating when I remembered that they charge you extra for decaf coffee and for skim milk. Wha? Those items shouldn't be costing them any more so why are they charging a dime more for each. Very annoying.

Bleh.  Zeb doesn't actually cook anything on the premises.  They heat food and assemble sandwiches and salads.  The food is fine if you're hungry and don't have time to walk across the street to I-House.  My favs are the BBQ chicken quesadillas and the chinese chicken salad.

Service is hit or miss here.  The menu hasn't changed in years and they don't do a very good job of managing the long line that piles up during lunchtime.
Good quality coffee, unfriendly staff.

Best cafe ON CAMPUS for sure. I'm happy we have a decent place to eat around Southeast corner of campus.
I've had the veggie California sandwich, grilled turkey sandwich, they 're both really good. And roasted chicken sandwich is divine!! 
A little expensive, but I'm sure I will still visit really often.

Did not answer their phone. Their phone line gives that ghetto modem sound. I am a hasty college student who needs to save time by calling restaurants in advance so I don't have to wait for them to make the food. So I don't care how good the food is; this is unacceptable. 

I have also never been to this restaurant.
it's like the max and the peach pit for boalties. damnit. i'm outing myself.

Love their White Mocha, which is basically the Bianca Mocha at Strada. Love their two seating areas--especially the one on the West side since it's basically a giant study spot with bar stools along the windows, booths and cushy seating. AND HUGE TABLES. 

They have pretty quick service and it's just a lovely place because the windows are huge and you can enjoy the sun. Also, they take that new Cafe card that Strada, Fifo and FSM take. Woohoo!

TIP: 
-Load $20 onto the Cafe card right now and you get a $5 reload coupon!

I haven't tried anything else on the menu but the one item that I have tried makes this place the #1 cafe in Boalt Hall (doesn't matter that its the only one).  

The California Veggie Sandwich!!!  It's a must have with the whole wheat bread.  They put in ample amounts of avocado, sprouts, tomatoes, lettuce, pickled onions (makes it infinitely better), and top it off w/ a chipotle mayo.  I could literally eat this sandwich every single day until I graduate and not get sick of it.  It's also great because they have cups and water available so you can serve yourself endless cups of water (it's important to stay hydrated).

The few times that I've been here I have been pretty excited about my order and then when I get my order and it ends up being something else. How does a turkey sandwich with pesto on a focaccia roll turn into a turkey sandwich with yellow mustard on sliced wheat bread? How does a BBQ chicken quesadilla with a green salad turn into BBQ chicken quesadilla with a caesar salad (very strange combination btw).  Strangely, even though the place is owned by the same people as Strada, the coffee is much more mediocre. Nice study area and patio, though.

This was one of my favorite spots on UC Berkeley campus.  I love their turkey panini with lots of avocado!  And they open quite early everyday, so every time when I had class at 8, I always ran into Cafe Zeb and grabbed a cup of coffee before class.  The staff there are very friendly and you always can see lots of students hanging out, at outside patio tables.  Definitely a good place for lunch.

Awesome place (often overlooked) because it's in the Boalt school on the bottom floor. Great food - definitely beats Haas cafe or any of the dorm cafes.

The food is awesome, would recommend the warm sandwiches. Service isn't THAT fast but it's not slow either. Awesome seating with glass doors (so you can really enjoy it on a sunny day, sitting indoor with a good book and some coffee)

Also the sofa seating and chair seating have outlets! They sure know the way to a student's heart...

So it's finally back up again after the fire! It's not necessarily the best Thai place in Berkeley, but I like the nice restaurant feel you can get here close the main campus area. It is hard to find a nice indoor sitting restaurant that doesn't feel too fast-food-like close by. 

Service is warm and friendly and very attentive. The food is pretty good too. Their Thai Kea Mao with beef was pretty good the other day, though once they gave me a young coconut that was too fresh and tasted sour. Otherwise, if you're looking for a nice place to eat nearby, I definitely recommend it.

I hate missing FtR's.  I had boatloads and bucketloads of grading to do, but there was an FtR to be had, and I didn't have it.  Maybe that's why I regret everything.*

Anyway, the portions are large.  The pad see ew with tofu is A-OK.  Not terribly amazing, but not bad either.  And they don't use fish oil!  Yea.  They have a spicy-looking powder/concoction that's not actually spicy.  It feels spicy, but it doesn't taste spicy.  That doesn't make sense, but it does.  Kind of like this entire review/my life/2002.

Remember 2002?  Wow.  It felt so much more modern than 2003 for some reason.  Kind of like how I used to be a fat skinny person but now I'm a skinny fat person.

*I don't really regret everything.  Just most things.  I'm a dweller par excellence.  Not quite a navel-gazer, but definitely a ruminator.

Things I like:

i. Good internet.
ii. Amazing blueberry danish! yum!!!
iii. Food is ok and varies. Comes out fairly quickly. 
iv. People behind the counter tend to be nice. 
v. Great place to study (if you can get a table). 
vi. They gave a tv on in a news channel. Great way to keep the students up to date with current affairs. 
vii. Newspapers headlines from all over the world outside!! Love it!! 

Things I don't like:
i. They have no idea how to make a latte. Seriously, ugh. 
ii. Coffee is either a hit or a miss. No consistency. 
iii. Only small or large size drinks, which means I either finish it on three sips, or end up just throwing away the remainder of my drink because I can never finish it in my one hour break. 
iv. Always too crowded. But that happens on almost every coffee shop in our around campus. 
v. I know it's a busy place and you have a line all the way to Moffit library, but please wait for the customer in front of me to move out of the way before you start taking my order. I do not like to scream my order to you across three other people who are just putting their change away. Rude.
Good place to remind yourself that you're in a different income bracket than the majority of your fellow students. Just gape open-mouthed at the prices for a while and then go home to your ramen.

5 stars for free coffee!

If you bring your own cup they will fill it up for free, only during a different 1 hour period every day though. 

I just throw my mug in my bag in the morning and check in every so often.

No complaints.

Although this cafe has a great location, I find its coffee to be aggressive and not very complex.  Accordingly, I never order naked espressos or even macchiatos from these guys.  In fact, I generally stay away!

However, I was here yesterday after lunch at a friend's suggestion.  I ordered a cappucino, and my friend had a latte.  The milk really saved the day.  Sitting out on the terrace in the sun, we were both very happy with our drinks -- and with the FSM Cafe.

My primary purpose in sitting @ FSM was to meet students I tutored.  It's a convenient place to meet on campus.  There are several tables inside and free WIFI.  Outside, there are longer benches and tables which work very well for meeting bigger groups.  Free Speech serves hot and cold food.  I've tried their salad, soup and sandwiches and there's nothing to write home about.  The salad tend to be fairly small.  The soup is almost always bland and the sandwiches are edible.  I did like some of their desserts.  The raspberry cheesecake in particular is quite good.  Their coffee cake and almond croissant are also good.

FSM has a few selection of food which I think the students can appreciate if they're studying @ Moffitt and are looking for the closest place to eat during breaks.  I'm not sure the prices are reasonable, however.  One needs to only walk across Sproul to find cafes that have better prepared salads and sandwiches at much affordable prices.

I am constantly disappointed by FSM. Sure, it's nice that it's open as late as the library, and it is close to many classes on campus, but it still manages to let me down. It is next to impossible finding a seat inside during the day, or even outside on warm days. The prices are high (which is expected I suppose, due to it's awesome location), and the food and drinks are average. If you come earlier in the morning, I have on multiple occasions been sold yesterday's stale croissants. All in all, I'd rather hike up to Yali's, or even better, somewhere off-campus.
Bleh. Moca bianca = good.

The Free Speech Movement Cafe has Mario Savio's immortal words etched in metal that you can read while waiting in line:

"To me, freedom of speech is something that represents the very dignity of what a human being is. ... It is the thing that marks us as just below the angels."

That being said, FSM is the second-best cafe in Berkeley to engage in that practice known as "eye-f*cking."

Any student who has ever sat in a cafe to study during midterms has done it.  You're sitting at a table, enjoying your hot grilled chicken panini and fresh green salad, allowing your Americano to cool, when you see an attractive person sitting across the way from you.  S/he is typing away at a laptop, but every so often--so you think--s/he looks up and gazes intently into your eyes.  Maybe s/he is looking THROUGH you to the grayscale images of the Free Speech Movement behind you; maybe the person is simply seeking the camaraderie of another weary, exam-riddled soul.  But you know better.  S/he wants you.  You then allow yourself for the next twenty minutes to highlight the same tired line of Samuel Huntington while eye-f*cking that person.

I've heard this practice referred to in a number of different ways.  For instance, for those inclined towards religion there is "eye-hand-holding" (which sounds gross, actually).  For those pursuing MRS degrees there is "eye-marrying."  I prefer the anonymity and ever-so-titillating term mentioned in the paragraph above.

This all being said, FSM is a great place to study and hang out.  It's right in the middle of campus, so it's convenient for mid-day snacks or meetings.  It tends to get very crowded and very hot.  Expect to share your table, unless you do what I sometimes did: turn your table so that it is lengthwise against you.  Then spread out pens, books, and notepads over the entire expanse.  This will give you a little bit of privacy!

And the sandwiches, entrees, and soups are delicious and reasonably priced.  Just be sure not to make a habit of it, as $7 or $8 for a sandwich and coffee every day tends to add up quickly!

this cafe in the middle of uc berkeley is a nice spot to grab lunch or coffee. they have good panini sandwiches and salads to choose from. the coffee is drinkable, but not good. it's definitely convenient if you find yourself on campus although when classes are in session, the line can be rather long and tables are difficult to come by. 

the tables and walls are covered with newspaper clippings and histories of the movement that made berkeley famous, so you can grab a lunch here and learn something too!

lastly, it tends to be a bit expensive...the speech might be free, but the food and drink's definitely are not.
nice coffeshop. Lot's of students with their laptops. Good coffee and nice big patio! The staff is friendly. I really liked the atmosphere.

I'm really suprised at everyone's raving reviews of this place and Strada. If these places are the best of Berkeley, I pity you people. I guess I may just brew it at home for two more years...

The coffee here is also boring, and you pretty much have to order coffee because any iced drink is tasteless. 

If I'm having my joe to stay, I'll come here because its pretty spacious out on the patio. If you're getting coffee to go, I think the GBC has better coffee options...

I like this place a lot. The drinks, the wraps, the desserts. It's a really good place to go for a non-study study session with friends, but the problem is that it's always packed. Always. I have rarely been able to get a seat inside, or even one outside sometimes. But if you can find a place, hunker down and stake your claim.

The walls by the register have art about and inspired by the Berkeley Free Speech Movement, and it's nice to read little tidbits of speeches and pictures of significant moments from Berkeley's history. All around, a great place to soak up Berkeley culture.
I like that it's open so late. The food doesn't taste the best; however, the selection of pastries is awesome. Their coffees are above average too.

Ordered a simple black coffee but it turned out to be disappointingly weak and lacking in aroma. Also ordered a bagel. $3.25 in total for both coffee and bagel. Bad experience! 

I compared this with my experience in Tully's (on Shattuck Ave), which offers a "coffee and bagel combo" for a cheaper price and better quality. At Tully's, the coffee was fairly good, and at least they toast your bagel and spread cream cheese for you. Not here. 

Also, it's crowded and NOT a good place to study. If you want to study, there are many quieter cafes around campus that might be more conducive and have better ambience. If you want to chill, hang out, meet friends, read your favorite book... Don't come here either. There're quite a few charming cafes around this area (Caffe Strada, for one, and my favorite - Sack's Coffee on College Ave). 

Sorry, but FSM cafe gets only 1 star from me, despite its grand name and historical significance.

I am grateful that I have FSM so close to me. The food and drinks are okay, but it is really the wifi and studious atmosphere that I come for. 

Whenever I need to study I am never torn about going to either a noisy caf where I can get drinks and nourishment or a quiet library where I feel too alone. Personally, I have trouble studying by myself in places that are too quiet. I need some sort of soft background noise to quiet my mind and keep me focused.

FSM has the awesome mixture and caf convenience and library studiousness.

My only compaint is that there are not enough outlets and indoor seating, but that usually doesn't stop me from coming.

Every time I come here I rant about how overpriced the food is but end up getting it anyway, since it's right next to Moffitt (obviously this is how they get away with their prices).

I definitely wouldn't recommend the coffee, but the white chocolate mocha seems to be a big hit among students (it's decent, very sweet). As for food, I like their chicken quesadillas and Chinese Chicken or Cobb salad. And of course, I highly recommend the pastries! The apple cloud, strawberry cheesecake, pumpkin tart (Thanksgiving season!), coffee cake, etc. 

Of course the best thing about FSM is that its hours coincide with Moffitt's - perfect for 24 hour library hours during finals. 

As for seats, ask to share! No one ever stays long to study here anyway.

The food here is actually pretty good. Here are the things I like
-cake-like cookies
-Mediterranean Salad
-Coffee, Chocolate & Almond Croissant
-Tuna salad wasn't bad, needs more of the tuna salad
-Soup. Soup is the best thing here or anywhere.  They give you bread. And I love to soak it in the soup and just eat it. It nearly killed me when I saw my clam chowder had actual pieces of clam in it.

The bad
-No credit or debit card. That is just extremely primitive and annoying.
-This cashier on the weekend never smiles.  She said hi to one of the people in line in the worst way possible. Monotonic yet somehow very aggressive. This takes two stars away.  Its just very unpleasant! I just want to leave tip for the other cashiers out of spite for her. a faint smile at least?
-Caesar salad.  Just don't.

Just the name alone and what it stands for merits a food rating....but I also happened to frequent this place a lot as its attached to the main library. The drinks here are only decent and a little on the weak side I found. I think they call it a spider bite here, a coffee with added espresso shot...well I normally got that with added Irish Cream flavoring and added creamer just to reach my caffeine threshold, especially during midterms/finals! (there's better oncampus coffee at that little stand at the bottom inside atrium thing of the chemistry building!)This place is a fairly good place to study but only on a good weather day and only outside. Its VERY noisy inside!! Which i guess makes it a good place to enjoy coffee and chat with friends.....of course only if you're lucky enough to find a seat. Being the central coffee joint in a bustling University...this place is usually jam packed. I ate here a few times for convenience....and I don't know why I did actually....the food over at Bear's Lair is much much better!

This place is CASH/CAL1CARD FRIENDLY ONLY. if you only have a credit card, you can buy a giftcard though. 

I come here when I have twenty minutes to eat and want something warm and soupy. They have two daily soups, although I've seen days where they only had one by lunch. The soups tend to be something of the curry lentil/california minestrone/chicken and vegetables variety. Not very creative, but good. If you ask for to-go, they give you a cup that looks exactly like the ones at GBC or Q2. If you ask for here, they give it to you in this glass bowl that seems a little bigger - not THAT much bigger, though. They also give you one or two slices of nice, soft bread... mmm, the best part! (:  For a little over $3, I'd say, not bad, not bad. 

I've also tried the Californian sandwich on focaccia bread. It tasted fine, but the proportions were definitely smaller than I had imagined for the price. They give you a salad with it too, which makes for pretty presentation, but the salad was limp and there was wayyy too much oil. I've seen their salads, too, and I guess I must be spoiled by Intermezzo or something, but they're definitely small comparatively as well. 

Indoor eating is REALLY LIMITED, mostly because there are a lot of people who just buy a coffee (or nothing), and sit there and study. Personally, I prefer to study at the library, which is only a few steps away... but outside seating is plentiful, if the weather is nice. I wouldn't go here with groups.

I love this cafe for it's spacious outdoor seating (plus outdoor outlets!) and cheap coffee. It's my go-to study spot on nice days that I want to spend outside but can't because I have to study like a good Cal student. So I make the best of both worlds and study outside under the comfort of the awnings. The only downside, though, is that the place is usually PACKED with students. It's difficult to find a good seat unless you're hounding like a vulture and swoop in as soon as you see someone starting to pack up.

There's this girl who works at the register who either doesn't enjoy her job too much or doesn't care about the customers at all. She speaks in a very robotic way when she talks to you and tells you your total before taking your money and sending you on your way. I understand that it gets busy and you can get tired, but at least try to smile and make the customer feel welcome for buying something.

The coffee is okay -- nothing too special about it, but at just under $2 for a large cup, it fuels me through most of my mornings.

Expect to stand in a line that's just too long before ordering. Expect to wait 15 minutes if you've ordered food. Expect to never find any indoor seating because the people sitting at the tables are actually furniture. Expect to go outside and freeze your ass off when you have to settle for a table in the shade because this is Berkeley. Expect to come back because there's not that many over par patios at campus.

expensive, cash only, kinda slow
the food is alright, the coffee is alright
they do have fresh fruit: apples and banana for 75cents, i usually would grab one while i was studying
the atmosphere is good though. there is an indoor area as well as a large outdoor patio. nice for reading, grab lunch w/ a friend, meet up a study group. had some good times here during my college years at Cal. *sigh, the memories

The best soups ever !!! I usually go there when I am alone for lunch and it feels like such an urban place both inside and outside. I love the pictures and the tables they have inside, each of them carrying a bit of history from the free speech movement at Berkeley. And outside when you sit facing south, you get a wonderful view of trees on the lawn and on your right biosciences bulding stands very aesthetically. Coming back to food: my favorite soup is the Italian Wedding Soup, followed by Chicken Gumbo. Always homemade soups, very fast service...Don't be scared with the line, it moves really fast. Also, their pecan swirls are very crispy, love it, especially with a cup of latte, which is always perfectly made...Currently, my favorite on campus lunch place!

Nice atmosphere. They offer sandwiches, grilled paninis, salads, coffees, and various baked goods. They also have biscotti. The only thing I've tried is their sandwiches: turkey on wheat and tuna on foccacia. If you ever order a sandwich here, definitely order it with foccacia. Still, I wouldn't recommend this place for sandwiches. The sandwiches are a bit overpriced for their size--small.

It's just convenient caus it's in the center of campus and easy to go in and grab food, but:

a) it's expensive
b) there are usually long lines at food-eating times
c) there will never be seats because all the studious berkeley students hog them to study

Food is okay.

FSM! Definitely a great place to study. 

Environment: There is a really nice feel to FSM because everyone is studying, and it (hopefully) motivates you to study too. It's usually not too loud, only a nice background noise that you get in cafes. However, this place is usually packed, and it's hard to find a spot inside unless you come early in the morning and stay throughout the day, which happens a lot during finals week. Oh, and I love that it's open 24 hours a day during dead week (for Cal students!). But, there's plenty of seating outdoors, which is nice on a sunny day. They have sort of a sun roof outside, so there can still be shade if it gets too hot, and there are lights outside at night as well. 

Drinks&Food: I personally love FSM coffee. It's a little small, but I think you get a discount if you get refills. Also, they offer honey instead of sugar, which is great. Their mocha is great too because it's not too sweet. They have huge salads and decent-tasting sandwiches. My favorite is the chiptote chicken Quesadilla.

Prices: I think FSM could be considered a bit pricey, and they only take cash or cal debit. A Mocha is $2-3, and a meal is about $6-8, depending what you get, but they have pretty good quality, and I think it's worth it. 

Service: Workers are pretty fast, and they don't really care if you just go there to study and not buy anything.

The same owners run Cafe Zeb in Boalt, Caffe Strada, and Adagio restaurant. Quite the family business!

Stars only for the Italian soda:

My cousin got me hooked on Italian sodas so I wanted to try their kiwi one. But they had no kiwi syrup! Booooo. I went with my usual drink (pomegranate soda) and I was pleasantly surprised that their club soda is soooo much more sparkling/carbonated compared to Cafe Zeb's. I got a gift card from work so I'll probably max it out on Italian sodas...or maybe a BBQ chicken quesadilla.
Very crowded but I'm still a fan of this place.

It's in the library, and near the academic building in which I live.

My hand to God sometimes I go there just because sometimes I need someone to call me "senorita" or "sweetie". 

Decent espresso drinks, heinously overpriced (but tasty) food. So really based on the above it's more a sad affirmation of grad student life than anything, but that's not their fault.

This is a very good cafe with convenient location, alright coffee and pastries, good food in a jam, wifi, some indoor seating, and lots of outdoor seating when the weather is nice. The morning buns and almond croissants are really good here. Outside there are well-lit stands with local and international newspapers in large print, updated daily. It is also nicely located in Moffitt Library with easy main stacks access.

unfair to say, but it is the best cafe ON campus - though strada and milano beat it by far

Evan's Thoughts

Because this place is called the "Free Speech Movement Cafe" I would assume it means I can say anything I want about it.  Well...I choose to say this: it was good!

I ordered the turkey/avocado panini, with chips and a peach Italian soda.  It was delicious!  I felt very chic chewing my panini, looking at the quotes of Mario Savio, and watching the energy bar fluctuate showing us how many kilowatts of power were being used.

My one comment is expense:  $10.50 for a sandwich, chips, and drink?  I'll be coming back here every once in a while, but on a college student budget it would be difficult to frequent this cafe.  If you're looking for a rare treat, or a small bite, look no further.

I would come here for the proactive studying ambiance, but not necessarily for the food.

The sandwiches and salads here are so-so; not bad, but I've definitely had better. I tried the turkey panini sandwich which was toasty and had turkey, avocado, pesto, and tomatoes. For $6.25 I expected larger portions and a better side salad, but it was still good. 

NOTE: Cash or cal 1 debit card
NOTE: Bus your own tables!

The atmosphere of Free Speech Movement Cafe is wonderful and perfect for studying or group projects. There are several outlets and lots of indoor and outdoor tables and seating. The place is buzzing with activity and is geared towards student use as it is at a super convenient location on the UC Berkeley campus. The cafe is decorated with Civil Rights Movement wall images, and there is a cool little energy bar at the center of the cafe to show the kilowatt usage in the cafe. TV at the back plays news updates.

Cleanliness could be a little better. The staff doesn't have time to clean tables between customers, so I found some crumbs and a penny on my seat.

WILL I come back: Yes, but for the environment, not for the food
WHEN will I come back: When I need to meet for a group project
WHAT will I do differently: go with coffee, not food

had the soup and salad combo. the house salad was extremely average. the soup - chicken tortilla -  was not pleasant. it was somewhat lukewarm, chicken tasted like fake meat, and the corn not blended with the rest of the flavors in the soup.

FSM is known around campus for being the place where it's nearly impossible to find a table inside. It's true. I've gotten a table there way too few times in my 2 years of being a regular, and each time I've rejoiced quietly and made plans to somehow never leave that spot.

Other than the impossible indoor seating, I actually love going to FSM. Their food is delicious, I've never experienced anything other than very pleasant service, and the location is the most convenient on campus.  The prices are high, though, which is why I set aside a certain amount of money per month on my Cal1 Debit card and just use it there. If it runs out, then I know I've gone to FSM too much and I should probably stay away from those bacon-filled cobb salads and yummy white mochas anyway. 

Tip from a regular: when you're feeling depressed about an upcoming midterm (or if you just got one back and want to drown your sorrows), get a bundt cake. They're all delicious, but I'd say the chocolate one just adds that extra dose of comfort :)

This place is about convenience (if you can get a seat) and good Californian sandwiches, which are, admittedly, overpriced. The coffee is pretty bad. The staff are loud and can be kind of rude. I do like the atmosphere, though, and it gets 3 stars just because the location can't be beat.

I usually come here for the paninis and their chinese chicken salad which are consistently good. They have a pretty good pastry section if you're looking for something sweet. This isn't my go-to coffee place but it's conveniently located on campus so I end up getting coffee from here. It's a nice place to hang out with your friends otherwise.

Okay, so this place is amazing when it comes to final, midterms, or taking a break from the library. 

I really like the paninis cause they always taste good. But the vinaigrette dressing can be a bit acidic at times but it's still good nevertheless.

Their black bottom muffin, biscotti, and espresso brownie bar are my stable.

The only reason why I took away 1 star is because the Italian soda is not that great and it's always crowded with a bijillion people during normal school year.

I used to go to the FSM quite a bit as a student because the atmosphere is unbelievably serene by Berkeley standards. And wouldn't you know it, I got a job downtown Berkeley. So, I'm back! 

I typically just get a bowl of soup, which is a bout 4 bucks. They have two different soups ever day. You never know kind of soup it is going to be, but you can always guarantee it'll be very good. 

Besides the soup, their antipasto salad is a favorite of mine.

This place is almost always busy. I love this place. It's always a great place to pick up some food or get some studying or people watching in.

They have some great food here. The paninis are great here, but I love the salads and quesadillas are amazing. My favorites are the Caesar Salad with Chicken and the Southwestern quesadilla. 

The espresso brownie is amazing here! The chocolate cake is good too. I enjoy chocolate so everything that is everything chocolate is good. 

FSM is a great spot to eat, drink, and "study"...more so than that...people watch!

It is ALWAYS difficult finding a seat inside the FSM, but outside is very spacious. The pastries and drinks are pretty good. Really enjoyed their apple cloud and iced chai latte. I got to use my Cal1 Card (even though I wish meal points could be used here). The location is really convenient to meet with fellow students, study, and grab some coffee. :)

Downsides: The coffee is mediocre, the vulture-like waiting on the limited amount of tables can be vicious, the bathroom might be sprayed with urine by some douche who used it beforehand (maybe this just happened to me) and conversations of the people sitting nearby can be incredibly distracting. 

But overall, the FSM is a cool cafe. Good place to meet up with classmates and study with friends (central location) and their food is delicious (especially the Californian sandwich w/ focaccia bread). 

A definite Berkeley-must.

oh FSM with their dim ass lighting, yet somehow even during non-midterm/finals season hordes of college students sit and study/read/youtube.  the outdoor seating is okay, although Berkeley is pretty chilly most days to actually enjoy the outdoor seating.  i always go for the quick, and overpriced costco croissants.  recently i discovered the chocolate cake which is actually pretty heavenly. seriously it's like putting a chocolate cloud in your mouth.

This is a pretty awesome place to eat while studying or also just pick up coffee or a wrap really fast. The only downside is that this place is almost always really packed, especially the inside seating. Also, the line gets really long during the day time. The prices are also a little expensive for not all that great food.
Love the outdoor patio.

FSM Cafe has always been a perfect place for studying and grabbing a quick bite! The fact that it's open late (2 AM) and has both outdoor and indoor seating means it's perfect for any occasion at basically any time of the day! As one can imagine, being so close to campus means that everyone is here in between classes getting a snack or a fast meal aka lines can seriously suck during the lunch hour. The food and drinks usually do come out pretty quickly though (less than 10 minutes), which makes up for the long lines.

I'd recommend the Cobb Salad or the Chicken Pesto Wrap here! Those are my main go-to food items here - the salad portion is pretty generous and the wrap is tasty and already ready-made! The drinks here are also really good especially the mocha - the coffee used here is also fair trade, which is always a plus. Warning: cash only.

Outlets will be hard to find here generally speaking so don't expect to find one that easily. You should probably be enjoying your company and/or textbook anyways I suppose...Oh and a side-note, there's a bathroom around the corner from the cafe, which is pretty nasty. My suggestion: go to the bathroom directly across from the cafe through the door leading to the second floor so that you don't have to deal with waiting in line to use the bathroom, which already doesn't smell too welcoming in the first place. Other than that...FSM Cafe is a great place to study at in my book!

I LOVE FSM! Not only is it conveniently located on campus, it has a soothing, quaint ambiance and good food/ drinks! Definitely one of my favorite study spots but you have to get here early in order to find a table. I like their coffees and iced teas, and generally end up ordering food here- the BBQ chicken quesadillas are really good, fresh, and filling, and their chocolate cake makes me feel better after a brain frying study session at Moffitt. I like how they have yogurts, fresh fruit, and fruit juices- helps me pick healthy snacks while I'm cramming for a big midterm.

The only complaints I have about this place are that they don't accept credit cards and that it gets really busy during mealtimes. Plan ahead!
it's fine. its not terribly pricey and everything is OK but nothing is really remarkable. it saves you from walking 10 minutes to anything else.

I worked on campus post-graduation for a couple of years and FSM cafe was really close to my lab so I would often get a sandwich here if I didn't have time to go off campus for lunch. I liked the turkey sandwiches (add bacon of course!) and occasionally had a decent cup of soup here (except I was not a fan of the Italian wedding soup - weird unidentifiable meatballs in it that were grey and strange.) compared to the other on campus cafes this one is much better in my opinion. also they have my favorite chips - the kettle brand (honey mustard & thai spice rule!) If you have more time hit up a better nearby cafe like Yali's!
Not terribly bad. I love their food! It's delicious, but their drinks are only okay. Try the danish, blueberry! It's dabomb!

I don't think I would have survived college without FSM. 
Find yourself falling asleep in the library at 1AM? No problem, head next door to FSM and grab a cup of tea or coffee. 
They also have some decent pastries to satisfy your late night sweet tooth (I recommend the apple cloud or black bottom muffin). 
Their coffee isn't great, but it isn't terrible. Their tea selection is pretty decent. The best part is how convenient it is and how late it is open. 

If quiet libraries aren't your scene it also provides a really nice atmosphere to study in. I love and miss this cafe dearly.

For me, this is one of those places I'm not a huge fan of but am a regular out of convenience.  

It annoys the hell out of me that they (sometimes) charge me an extra 50 cents just to lighten my tea with soy milk...most places only add this charge when you're actually making an espresso drink with soy.  I know its just 50 cents, but its still annoying, considering how little I actually use, and how much tea I drink.  Actually they don't serve tea that well at all...for some reason there's this one guy who pours soy milk directly into hot water (which by now isn't hot enough to even brew tea), which is filled like 2 inches below the rim of the cup and hands me a tea bag...uh, thanks? 

Also, the constant yelling of numbers for orders of food gets really annoying.  I'm not saying I know of a better system, but its still annoying.  There are tables with access to outlets for laptops, but they're usually always taken and well coveted.  Finding an indoor seat is often rare.  Again, annoying,.

Still I go here all the time because its conveniently located, and I still have this romantic notion of havng a bite to eat while doing homework and not being too far away from class.  Yet I always feel a little aggrivated when I leave.  That usually depends on what homework I do in there, as there are some subjects that you just can't study while someone is yelling "Fifty-three! Fifty-three!"

I will say this.  They handle the volume of people coming through very efficiently. Also, food doesn't take that long.   At peak times, there is a tremendously long line and the workers are incredible at going through it quickly.

As of now, my favorite coffee place in Berkeley!  A pretty high compliment when you consider the competition of places like Philz and Peet's.  I usually only order their coffee (soy latte = amazing), but I've had their food a couple times and it's equally delish.  Also, its location on campus is perfect because it's in the middle of everything:  near my classes, right next to the library, near food.  

My only complaint is that it gets ridiculously crowded at times.  If you want to study here (it's a really nice place to study, if you don't mind louder places), you'll probably need to head outside because the tables on the inside are normally full.  Also, barely any outlets. 

Tip #1:  Kind of unrelated, but it's extremely difficult to sneak coffee/food into the library.  It needs to be completely hidden. Just a warning, because they've definitely made me chug a full cup of coffee before letting me through... 

Overall:  YUMMY COFFEE, close to lots of stuff, crowded but worth it.

somehow i always found myself here my last semester at cal. 

the coffee &espresso drinks are crap. their sandwiches looked delectable, but too pricey for the size... yet i always came back.

it must be the environment.. i always found that i could concentrate best here. of all places. really. for non-final times, make sure to stake out a table before 10am. by an outlet. yeah. bring snacks. yes. i said it.
Got the Mediterranean salad and I'm pretty sure all the ingredients had passed their prime except the lettuce.  The feta and artichoke hearts tasted rotten.  Yuck.

Favorite place to study on campus. I love the outside terrace! You get to see lovely squirrels occasionally being fed (or sometimes stealing!) and being adorable !
I absolutely love the atmosphere. I never understood how this place was more quiet than the library. (Its the only place on Earth you have to be quiet, come on people. Come on.) 
Now, its not deathly quiet. There's casual conversations, but you can totally study here. I am sad on the days that it is cold, well both sad and happy. I'm sad that I have to sit in the cold, but I am happy that no one else does! They all crowd inside... I personally don't like the inside..

Its cool. Just me and the squirrels will enjoy the whole terrace then :)

Their cobb salad is delicious. But I didn't pay for it, so what can I say. That's probably why it was good.

this place charges .85 for a cup of hot water--even if its your own cup!  Kind of reminds me of the behavior of the UC Regents.  I like the patio when its nice out.  It is also open till 1am but super crowded.

This cafe is also a walk-in exhibit.  While the free speech images and Mario Savio quotes plastered all over the walls and tables are pretty amazing, they have this even cooler interactive exhibit.  Check out the energy consumption meter at FSM (http://www.macetech.com/blog/node/91).  You can see all the details of how much power is being used throughout the cafe, including what you are using from your laptop.

Oh!  The ICED White Chocolate Mocha!

I am quite positive that this place is run by the same people that run Cafe Strada across from campus. How the two differ is beyond amazing to me. What I love is that they accept the Cal 1 debit card so my dad can still pay for my late night study sessions when I have a group project. MAJOR PLUS!

Besides from that, I love that it's always full of people studying and doing everything and anything. The seats outside where you can just relax on a cool nice day and eat a slice of cheesecake with a strawberry on time? Fantastic! People watching because you are taking the fiftieth study break? Yess!!

The coffee could be a little bit better so stick to the espresso-based drinks, seriously. I am a big fan of their Americanos (espresso and hot water) and just snacking on their pastries. The only thing that I hate is that they are just horrid at managing their lines. I used to work at Starbucks back in the day and we expedited people through by taking their orders in line so we can have their drinks done when they pay. Why can't this place do the same if you know your store is busy, especially during certain hours? Additionally, I look at the people that grab the food and damn, they look really good but I am just too broke to pay for those salads and sandwiches. They look amazing but why must you break the bank?! :(

This dump deserves at least three dollar signs if only because a fucking hardboiled egg costs 75 cents.  Thats also pretty much the only thing worth getting here unless you want to pay 10 bucks for a warm Cobb salad in too much dressing.  The coffee SUCKS, the prices SUCK, but the selection, especially for late-night studying rounds, oh yeah IT FUCKING SUCKS.  "Hmm, shall I have the defrosted cheesecake or a bag of chips with my muddy "fair-trade" cup of coffee? They both sound soo refreshing at 2 am. Brain-food, really."

Okay so there is one thing about this place that keeps it from earning the monostar. On any given night, should you be lucky enough to actually find a seat, sit back, put your studying aside, and prepare to witness an endless influx of the HOTTEST Persian girls you never knew went to this school. Why do hot Persian girls love this place so much? I'll never know. But God bless America, Free Speech has em hooked.

The coffee is god-awful terrible, the food ok but way overpriced, and at least 50% of the time your order will get messed up.

So why 3 stars? Best place to study/do work on campus that isn't the library. When it isn't super crowded. Make sure you come with your laptop at 100% battery life, because fighting for an outlet can be brutal.
The food and coffee here is nice. And there are plenty of seating. Kind of pricey though and very very busy.

This is a great spot to grab lunch from on campus. It's pretty busy in the day time on weekdays. Sometimes, you'll have to wait 15 minutes for food , but if you go on the weekend or late at night, the wait is very tolerable. The coffee here is okay. I always grab a mocha or a hot chocolate. The food is pretty good. The paninis are the best! Soup is delicious too! I was not too impressed with the main entree salads however. I don't get sandwiches too often, but when I do, it's pretty good. My fav order is a ham panini.

The atmosphere's nice. Lots of college kids. However, the place is just so darn packed with indoor seating that I mostly get take out.

You'd better arrive early if you want to seat and it's not school break, but the staff is super friendly, the expresso is good, and generally speaking, the food is good for a cafeteria. Not the cheapest place on campus, but I could spend hours working there. Except a little noisy, I'd say if you can't focus that well, take earplugs or music.

During midterms and finals seasons, I spend a lot of time studying at Moffitt and Doe, so I occasionally drop by FSM for a quick bite to eat. It's almost impossible to find a seat inside since those tables are always in high demand, but if it's a nice day, I don't mind sitting outside (although there are only a few outlets). I usually order the California sandwich on foccacia (cucumber, tomato, avocado, onions, greens, and some zesty mayo), which comes with a side salad if you eat in but not if you take it to go. The sandwich is delicious and the sauce is good (this is coming from someone who doesn't even like mayo). However, they tend to put too much dressing on the salad most of the time. I've literally had my salad drowning in dressing before, so I just tried to scrape as much as I could off...

There's nothing too special about their coffee, but I do like their chai latte since the spices are yummy. If you're feeling something sweet, get the apple cloud!! It's kind of a hybrid between an apple pie pastry and cheesecake! It's pretty dense, so it'd be perfect if you shared with someone, but I have been known to finish the whole thing myself before!

TIP: Try to avoid coming during the lunch rush since the line can extend from the counter to the Moffitt lobby desk..eek! Also, $5 minimum for card!

Every time you come you have a term paper or a midterm and you're desperately looking for a place to sit, no seating is to be found. You're forced to join the mass of people hovering in the corner waiting for a seat. Experiencing this one too many times forces me to bump down my review a couple notches.

I absolutely love the food here, though. Skip the overrated grilled paninis and stick with the normal sandwiches. The foccacia that they use is delicious. The cobb salad, loaded with fresh greens and actual roast chicken that they shred themselves, is also one of my favorite go-tos. If only they took credit...

I work near here, so I have tried many things....

1) Cobb salad is good, lots of good stuff in it.  Ask for extra dressing on the side though, because one time I barely got any vinagrette dressing, so my salad was bland is unsatisfying.  It comes with lots of goodies in it, including avocado and bacon!

2) Do NOT get the caprese panini unless you want the most bland panini EVER.  It has mozzerella cheese, tomato, and pesto sauce.  Essentially the only thing you'll taste is the cheese, at best.  0 stars.

3) Their deli sandwiches are good.  I've had the honey ham sandwich numerous times, and only once did I not enjoy it because they gave me stale bread.  Otherwise, it is usually a satisfying meal. 3 stars.

4) The quesadillas are good, but they get soggy FAST if you do take-out.  Try to eat these on site.

5) The turkey & mango wrap is good, and is easy to eat on-the-go.  When it's not mango season though, the mango might be a bit sour and not very soft.

6) The lowfat cranberry pumpkin muffin is pretty good, once you get used to the texture.  It's a bit more dense than your typical muffin.  Good flavor though.  4 stars.

7) The apple cloud is good, just don't get an end piece and you'll be fine.

8) The espresso brownie is DEEElicious! 5 stars.

9) The blackbottom muffin is said to be really good, according to my boss... although I haven't tried it myself.  Per his review, 4.5 stars.

10) Apple juice and orange juice are good.  Apple is more of a cider.  The orange juice can be sour, if it's not orange season.  They do not have cranberry juice, other than the fizzy kind in a bottle.

11) Their espresso drinks are always made right for me. 5 stars
