The food at FSM is absolutely delicious. I've tried just about all their vegetarian options, all of which were reasonably priced and delicious. Their veggie sandwich with the pickled onions is to die for and was a weekly treat for me in between my two toughest/longest classes. It made my 10 hour class day manageable and almost...dare I say it....worth it? 

-1 star for the seating. Finding seating inside is nearly impossible, but if you can deal with the sun/wind/rain/heck, all the natural elements outside then there's usually room. It's more likely that the weather elements will disappear before they make any huge changes to this building, but it wouldn't be so terrible for them to convert some of the outdoor space into more indoor seating. 

They say they only take cash---under $10. It's a well kept secret but you can use a credit card if you buy a gift card or if your order is over $10!

Organic & tasty food, reasonable prices, great location, quick service...I'm a fan!
The name always cracks me up.  I can't really say much about the food, never had it.  I have enjoyed two italian sodas from this cafe and like others have said, it's convenient.

Very disappointed that there were not any hippies, but instead were just a bunch of wannabe hipsters and college students at The Free Speech Movement. The coffee was great (Winning, anyone?) but the muffins left me wanting to take part in a movement of a different kind.
FSM can get really crowded but they make pretty good tuna melts.

Customer service :)

I was having a pretty off morning and decided to grab a hazelnut iced coffee only to be disappointed. I bought a regular iced coffee also to see if it was just the syrup I didn't like. However, I was unsatisfied. 
When I went back to complain, the barista asked no questions and offered either my money back or an iced americano. I took the americano; good decision.

Great customer service is always awesome. Finding a table to study at FSM... not so much. But by far, my favorite place to study on/around campus.

Lemon poppyseed cake. YUM. Chicken tortilla soup. YUM. Sandwiches. YUM! Great place to eat and study.

I wish I were a Berkeley undergrad still =(. Go BEARS!

This place is good for the quick late night omg! i'm fucked espresso shot taken right after you woke up in the library 2 hrs before closing time. 

they also have espresso brownies.

and red bull.

I've only been here for coffee related beverages because: a) the actual food is way too expensive, especially for a place that serves mostly college students, b) there's never anywhere to sit, especially if it's cold or rainy, c) the line is typically very long, especially around lunch time or during finals, which is when I'd probably want to go here in the first place. 

The Coffee Spot on Lower Sproul is a better alternative, and is far less expensive, although they're open less.

3 stars for food. The food is pretty bland, I would recommend walking the 5 minutes to Bancroft or Hearst. 

5 stars for location - so convenient!! Especially during finals...

FSM is great for the quick Red Bull/ coffee/ chocolate chip cookies run...
It is also a great place to meet someone to quickly go over some work.

Used to visit this cafe at least once a week while studying at Cal.  I loved the outdoor patio, lattes, salads and focaccia sandwiches.  My order was always ready quickly and made correctly!  The location on campus is what really makes it...so central.

I really like studying here, esp. if I get a seat on the left side against the wall. Those are my fav. Their coffee is good and lighting is good, it's not too loud but it's not so quiet that you can hear people's every movement. The bad thing here is that it is always crowded, so I always have to be QUICK about running to open seats once they free up. 

I haven't tried their food here yet because it's kind of pricey, but I can TELL they are really good, esp. their salads! I'll try one soon, I will. 

I wish I'd come here more often though--but I'm just too lazy to walk from my apartment to come here to study most of the time. You may see my roommate here though, like EVERYDAY :D She's a die-hard true FSM go-er.
Come here, grab a coffee, and plan an intifada or discuss which tree on campus is the best one to take up residence in.

From Sun-Thu, this place is open as late as the adjoining library -- 2am. Which is nice, since you can grab that last cup of coffee before you head home and finish that last page of your term paper that you oh god make this end already i don't care about what plato and caesar have to say help me

Anyway, the drinks and food are actually reasonably priced for a cafe. Their sandwiches and salads are decent, and they're usually prepped quickly. The problem, however, is the crowd. Jesus, the crowds. A parade of students, faculty, and staff results in ridiculous lines during lunch hour. Good luck finding a place to sit indoors during the afternoon/evening hours. The lack of seating bothers me, since the cafe only opened a few years ago. Couldn't they have anticipated the popularity of the place? It's difficult to get a decent-sized study group organized here because the seating is so awkward (individual chairs placed around very small tables).

The outdoor seating isn't too bad, but beware of the student groups who gather here AND TALK VERY LOUDLY JUST BECAUSE THEY CAN.

FSM is a partial reason to how I turned into a better student hahah mainly it helped drag my butt over to the moffit library to study. Especially during 24 hr library i had comfort knowing if my stomach was growling at 2am and needed a quick fix, i could pop downstairs for a chai latte or espresso brownie. I also like just sitting there in a place surrounded with bustling people who are equally stressed out about their stuff.It just motivates one to study more in the frenzy. With my music on and a room filled with people i can be in the zone to tackle w/e I need to. 

Its hard to get seats ( the wall ones with the outlests)there during midterms and finals weeks but its doable but one just have to be a little bit more diligent and motivated to get one and be patient enough to wait for it too. Either you wake up really early and get there around 7:30amish or hoards of ppl leave there around dinner time too around 5:30pm. 

Food and Drinks wise i've tried an extensive bit. I'll list a few consistent Favorites:
Drinks:
Soy Latte- its really frothy and creamy and comes in a tall "venti" sized glass.

Chai Latte- i used to not like chai tea because the spices were too overpowering for me but this changed my opinon of it. I'm not one to change my opinion so quickly either.

Italian Soda- I really like mixing Strawberry and Pomegranate. The sweetness of the strawberry is balanced with the tartness of the pomegranate. A wedge of lemon is given with the drink. It's perfect for a hot summer's day.

Apple Juice- Their fresh squeezed apple juice is just so refreshing. Its a bit expensive but worth a try if you want something just wholesome 100% organic i guess haha. 

Food:
I love their Salads and Panini Sandwiches 

1) Cobb Salad- This salad is HUGEEEE. If i wasn't gonna eat anything else for the day this is sufficent to keep me full for the whole day. It is delicious and nutritious!!! It has all the carbs,veggies,protien you need in one! As a person that used to not like blue cheese this salad has made me a fan of it. The crumbled bitsof it in the salad add a hit of nuttiness to the overall taste of things. It also comes with a strip of foccacia bread. I highly recommend it no one ever has been disappointed by it. 

2) Chicken Caesar Salad- The sheer amount of chicken that comes with this salad is already worth the price but i love it for the creamy dressing and the really fresh romaine heart lettuce as well. 

3) Caprese panini- Simple fresh ingredients are the best for sandwiches. Fresh mozzarella cheese slab with tomato,basil drizzled in balsamic vinegar and pressed hot.  

Other honorable mentions are the roast beef panini and the BBQ chicken quesadillas (this one takes a bit longer to make).

Desserts; i'm a dessert junkie and FSM desserts fufill my sweet tooth.
1) My favorite is the Carrot Cake. The cream cheese frosting isn't overpowering in sweetness but compliments the cake really well. The cake itself is very moist.
2) Strawberry Cheesecake- The cheesecake is done right, firm and not runny. It's pretty solid and a treat to have especially right after acing a midterm. 

Other noteworthy ones are the  espresso brownie,chocolate cake, blueberry muffin and the apple cloud. 

I will for sure come back and visit it in my grad school years as it has served me so wonderfully in my undergrad days :).

There's nothing particularly great about any of the food or coffees served here. I've had the paninis and sandwiches offered and both times was pretty disappointed. 

However, it's on campus and convenient. Those are the only two reasons I would ever eat at Free Speech; but it's still over-priced (almost $15 for a sandwich and a coffee) and pretty bland. 

You're better off just eating at People's Cafe or the Yali's Cafe on campus

And they only take Cash :/

FSM is basically where all CAL students will frequent often at some point in their time on campus. During the school year, it's nearly impossible to find a table inside. When you do find one, you basically don't leave until you absolutely must. 

The outdoor seating is nice during the summer, but the concrete benches are so uncomfortable. During the fall and winter, it's freezing, but when there's no seating inside you suck it up and go outside. They should consider installing heating lamps. 

The sandwiches are expensive, but I do enjoy their turkey panini with avocado, tomatoes, mozzarella on foccacia. The salad that accompanies the sandwich is sort of blah. 

The only drinks I've ordered here are chai lattes and mochas. It was here that I discovered the greatness of the chai latte; so GOOD!

One drawback is they don't take credit card, although I think they just started to take cal1 points? Also the workers there sometimes carry a "I don't give a damn" attitude; I don't blame them though, college students can be annoying.

I have many fond memories studying at FSM for bio, physics during the summer, and with random groups. The pictures of the free speech movement lining the walls of the cafe are awesome! 

Go Bears!

Quality: Organic/fair trade coffee. My favorite. :) The salads and quesadillas aren't worth it, so I wouldn't suggest eating dinner here unless you absolutely have to (staying in late to study)

Venue: To stay true to its name, there's a lot of references to the free speech movement + other related politics. Just yesterday, they had a segment on the arab spring which looked pretty cool. 

Amenities: Bathrooms are disgusting. However, the outdoor seating (with SOME outlets) make up for it. 

Accessibility: Right in the heart of campus. Walkable distance. 

Nearby: VLSB, East Asian Library, Moffitt Library

Hopes: A bit loud, especially when you need to study. Other than that it's pretty good.

Tip: This place gets PACKED during finals. You're pretty much out of luck if you don't reserve a seat by the time it opens. It closes when Moffitt closes. Cash/Cal1Card only!
Wi-fi for students only.

Will I come back? Yes! (if there's room)

I've been going to Cal for two years and I've never sat down at FSM to study until this summer. During the school year, this place is always packed with PEOPLE. Not like you can't get enough of that at Berkeley already. 

During the summer, it's a little more mellow, so it's not as crowded. 
- Coffee: I love their coffee!! 
- Mocha Bianca: almost as good as the one from Strada. 
- Latte: Vanilla = extra 50 cents, nonfat milk = extra 10 cents, total = $3.85 = too expensive for just a latte
- Pastry: their pastry is alright
- Food: I tried their Californian Deli Sandwich and it was really good. 

Good place to study because they have nice seating area, but I doubt I'll be able to study here during the semester. Outdoor is nice for light reading/meeting.

Best bet of finding a seat would be ten minutes before any hour - aka when people are heading out to class or else the chances of finding a seat are super slim.
The atmosphere is basically just Berkeley students. A lot of meet ups/ casual office hours are held here so if you wanted a quiet cafe to study... Not the place sorry! 

Food wise they are like the rest of the campus restaurants - overpriced. However I think their soup and salad combo is pretty good and the coffee ain't half bad! The salads tends to be drenched  in dressing though. The expresso brownie is fabulous.

the californian sandwich is delicious. also try their cobb salad. this place is always crowded and has a nice outdoor patio. overpriced, cash only, nice outdoor area. 

fantastic hot white mocha... even better when they actually use the soy milk that you paid the extra 65 cents for.

One of the best salads around campus, now that Cafe Intermetzo is gone. I love their Asian Chicken Salad. Its nice and crunchy. Their roasted chicken is delicious and so is the ginger/Asian-tasting dressing. The only negative is that its too crowded and the only place to find a place to sit is outside and its always really cold outside, especially during dead week. I'm not big on coffee so I can't opine on that but it seems popular.

Got a bran muffin for ~$2 for a pre-meeting snack in Moffitt. As said in previous reviews, FSM is over-priced, but they survive despite what they charge because of their prime location for catching students with severe mid-study session cravings. Seating is rather hard to come by, and the squirrels out on the deck are way too comfortable around people--warning: they will climb right up to your face! Previously, I've gotten their chicken sandwich, which comes with salad. Satisfying meal, but by no means extraordinary. Lines get long, though they have quick service.

I think my reviews are probably positively biased just because I am always super hungry, especially when I resort to on-campus locations.

I recommend the salads (especially the mediterranean vegetarian salad and the blue cheese/bacon/egg salad), the soups are decent, the veggie and chicken quesadillas are good, and the chai latte is superb. The best deal is to split one of their huge ass salads with a friend.

Ditto what everyone else said about price being meh and convenience great. Its a great place to study--too bad you have to wait forever for a seat inside no matter what time it is because tables for two are almost always occupied by one person. 

They accept Cal 1 card.

This is my favorite spot on campus!! I come here all the time, whether for studying or just a break in between classes. The food here is a bit pricy, but it's worth it and they're all organic. Do try their Californian sandwich, it's sooo goooddd. They got lots of tasty pastries (I think they got them from Cafe Strada), including apple clouds, banana cream pie, blueberry danish, and chocolate chip cookies. The coffee/tea drinks are very decent as well. I can't imagine my life in Berkeley without FSM, not joking. plus, all the people here are very friendly. LOVE this place!!!

Amazing panini. Soft, luscious focaccia that felt like it was at risk of breaking off into chunks, but stayed strong in supporting the roast beef, cheese, and vegetables inside. Toasted not lightly, but not obnoxiously crunchy...it all melted in my mouth.

Also:
-Very convenient location.
-Location inside library means that the rest of your day is more likely to be productive.
-Food isn't overly filling, which means you actually can think.
-Seating is doable if you're alone and you aren't too shy to ask someone to share their table.
-I feel bad for the cafe because of the people who sit on their laptops for 8 hours occupying a table without buying anything.
-Outside is not great but not terrible.
-I happen to like the mini salad that comes with the sandwiches!
-I also happen to like their black coffee.
-Sandwiches are $6.50 and they don't take any CC :( :( :(
so far, the best chinese chicken salad that i've ate. i love their dressing for this salad. i'm not a huge salad fan but i would go here to eat this salad whenever i was near the library!

Taste: 3
Value: 3
Service: 3

I've been here 2-3 times in the past few years to grab some quick food. The roasted turkey panini is quite good, as is the Californian sandwich. However, the prices are a bit high, and you're going to have a hell of a time trying to find a seat in here. The bathrooms are also pretty bad, and there's only one stall each for men or women with a significant line for both.

Relatively cheap and convenient for students taking a break from the studying at the library. 
I think it's a genius idea that they should have at every library. 
I mean, it only makes sense to have some caffeine next to a library where you need it. It's so convenient. 

UCLA should take note. At UCLA, (although i love the school) you have to walk down the hill to Kerkoff to get coffee which isn't that bad but then it's the middle of the night and it's hella dark you might trip and fall and break your face on the stairs (not that it's happened to me). And i don't think it's open until 2 am. It closes at like 11 even though the library is open 24 hours. 

But the Free Speech movement is open until 2 am just like the library. 
They are always packed though even though there is a lot of outdoor seating. Probably gets too cold for all the starving students. 

I suggest that they give away free pastries to the students that are there till late night. Like 1 am when they are closing anyways. It'll go a long way to help with their PR. Oh wait, it's the UC system. They're probably raising prices on the donuts as I write this. $10 for a bagel anyone?

The Free Speech Movement Cafe is exactly what most coffee shops attempt to emulate. They have a social and dynamic atmosphere complemented by that San Franciscan modern aura that keeps people working on their homework for hours at a time. 

Their selection of foods is a bit limited but the quality compensates. The coffee's great, the seating is comfortable and there's a plethora of plug outlets. 

The people are often easy to approach, so you can take a break between chapters and get to know someone that's interesting. It's a fantastic way to get work done without unproductive interruptions. Great for students and faculty!

This place is always busy. Either that, or I've never been here when it wasn't (and I go a good amount throughout the week).

Food: Their sandwiches are really yummy. I usually get the Turkey or the Roast Beef Panini. It's one of those sandwiches that makes you sad once you finish it because you wish there was more. The salad that comes with it it also pretty yummy, especially if you like vinaigrette. 

Try the Espresso Brownie - it's a little piece of coffee/chocolate heaven.

Drinks: I only get Soy Chai...which is kind of inconsistent. Sometimes it's really flavorful, and other times it's watered down. I guess it depends on who makes it.

Service: The people at the cash register are usually friendly.

Overall: I'm going to be frequenting this place more in the next few weeks while I pull my hair out writing this huge research paper. FSM is satisfying and the food/drinks are worth what you pay.

Since it's right by mainstacks a lot of people come here to study which is understandable but unfortunately that means it's really hard to find a seat inside. Finding one along the walls with an outlet is just downright impossible. It also tends to get really loud when the place is full as well, which isn't really conducive to studying. They are open whenever Moffit is though which is really convenient.

FSM drinks in general are decent, their coffees are good but nothing exceptional, they get the job done as far as caffeination goes. As for their food, their paninis are pretty decent and come with a small salad on the side. Their actual salads are good as well and for a salad, the portions are pretty large. They also have a good selection of tasty pastries. 
FSM is a little pricey in general but probably worth it given that it's probably one of the more decent places to get food/drinks on campus. They also finally started accepting debit/credit cards for purchases over $5 if I remember correctly. 

My main gripe with FSM is their service - it's really hit-or-miss depending on who happens to be working at the time. I've encountered polite, friendly, and efficient workers, but I've also experienced rude and incompetent workers as well.

The paninis are SO good, but soso overpriced. The salads are also decent, but overpriced. 

The only deal here is really the convenience of the coffee and location... It's always always packed, but if you wait long enough, there's always someone leaving within 10 min. ++ there is outdoor seating! (WATCH OUT THOUGH, CAL STUDENTS CAN TRY TO BE SLY AND STEAL YOUR SEAT IF YOU'RE NOT WATCHING CAREFULLY :)!!!) 

The lines get super long, especially on the hour. But service is normally really fast. If you want to avoid the lines, come at an odd time (around one-quarter before or after the hour!)

Hours are convenient for students as it opens the same time as Moffitt Library... 

And the place has outdoor seating. I love going here! :]

Do you know how freaking lucky you guys are to have this place? It's incredible. Right there in the center of campus, a capacious place to drink high quality espresso and lunch on tasty sandwiches. The interior is lovely, and on most days you can sit outside with the gorgeous views of San Francisco and the west campus. Ten stars!

You'll need to vulture for a seat, especially if you want an outlet.

The menu is fantastic! I highly recommend the mocha bianca. The soups are great - especially the aztec chicken and chicken tortilla. 
Salads are huuuge! but I do recommend getting the dressing on the side though.

It's always pretty crowded in there....

but when I have some extra cash on me, and I come out of the library, FSM is always a nice reward.

I love their mochas. Not too sweet, not too bitter.

Their sandwiches are pretty good; most things on the menu are healthy!

The almond croissants are great too... 

Don't knock it 'til you try it!

I'm a senior at Berkeley and I still don't know how to get a seat inside the FSM.  I've never been too impressed with their drinks.  The food looks good but everything is overpriced so I've never bothered to try.  And if I can't get a seat inside, I just don't know the point in coming here.  Two good things: 1) I don't know if they still are, but during finals week when the library is open 24 hours so is this place.  2) I do enjoy their Italian soda selection, although you can get them cheaper at a lot of places close by.

Best banana nut muffins on campus. Pretty sure they get it from the same distributor as Strada. Once in a blue moon I will dream about this muffin that always managed to make me happy in between classes on particularly dreary days. 

Yeah the lines are long, yeah it's crowded, yeah the coffee is kind of expensive and mediocre-tasting at best, but when you're trekking up the slopes, in dire need of a caffeine fix, FSM can be your best friend if you let it. 

I remember being enchanted by the apple cloud. It's deceptively cute with an adorable name, but all it really is is a cold pastry with cream cheese and some apple slices.  Expensive and not that good. I'm telling you... banana nut muffin ftw.

OVERPRICED AND UNFRIENDLY CAFE OFFERS LITTLE MORE THAN CONVENIENCE

FSM is a place that should have two separate review pages, one for males an one for females.

As far as I know, at least the food is the same for both sexes.  That is, from time to time when I've had a sip or a bite of a female friend's order, it's been just as unexceptional as mine.  The sandwiches aren't bad per se; they just don't contain any ingredients that aren't in my fridge right now.

As I sat there just now, eating a bowl of flavorful [hence two stars instead of one] but solid-deprived soup, I thought about all the nasty things I would say in my review.  On my way back downstairs to write it, I ran into a girl I know.  I made a comment about seeing her there a lot.  "I love this place!" she said (without a hint of sarcasm).

That's because you have breasts.  The young men behind the counter smile at you and treat you like an old friend.  They remember what you like, they ask how your finals are going, they tell you they like that thing in your hair.

When I order something, I get a very different reception.  The message they try to send is "Hey, man, I'm not into guys or anything, but I'll serve you because it's my job."

Once when I ate there, I asked for a ham panino without cheese.  In a few minutes, the guy called my number, and I took my sandwich from the counter.  Guess what was in it.

I order things without cheese all the time, and I've had all kinds of restaurants screw it up.  It's a little mistake that I easily forgive, because I'm so used to it.  Hell, I bet it even happens to female customers sometimes.  But then:

I politely reminded the guy that I had asked for no cheese.
His eyebrows dropped.  "That is not what you told me."
I insisted, still nicely, that it was what I had told him.
"Well I'll make it again," he said, "but that is not what you told me."

Let's just say for one minute that I really did forget to say no cheese.  Let's say that even though I have to utter those two words at about half of the meals I ever eat, I forgot to say them just this once.
What greater good does it serve, Mr. Barista/ToasterOperator, for you to tell me that I didn't say "no cheese"?  Your ego?  Or maybe it's constructive criticism; you're trying to teach me how to order better next time.  Thank you so much. 
I love this place!

You seriously have to constantly be on the look-out if you want a seat inside FSM during its peak hours. The cafe is always poppin'! 

FSM offers great menu choices for a decent price, considering how convenient its location is. It sits right next to the Moffitt Library and is also open for the same amount of hours! It's hard to find good quality food during the later hours. 

I feel like you can't go wrong with any of the menu choices! They have a variety of paninis, salads, sandwiches, coffees (that everyone sneaks into the library), desserts, and fruit! Everyone who works there is pretty nice as well!

I give FSM 0 stars for: the college students who stay there the whole day when theres limited indoor seating, for having crappy coffee, and for overpriced quesadillas. But considering that I'm a student, and that I don''t feel guilty for using their space without buying anything, FSM gets 3 stars.

I get all misty thinking about FSM.  I seriously do.  Appreciate it while you're there, kiddies, you will miss it when you're gone.

My main study buddy and I used to be here 'till close on many a night-- Reading Milton, discussing Derrida and dissemination, cramming for tests, and writing essays.  I always grabbed my morning coffee here on the way to Wheeler.  Sometimes I had their soup for lunch.

I was even at FSM the night the votes were counted in the '04 presidential election.  And I was there the following morning, watching CNN with a hundred fellow students, tears in our eyes as we realized Bush would assume a second term despite all of our phone-banking and meek contributions.

If you haven't read the Mario Savio quote on the wall-- Do.  In fact, rent the documentary on Berkeley in the 60's so that you can fully appreciate your school's role in the movement this place is named after.   

And don't complain about always being here to study.  That's the point.  It's why you're in Berkeley.  Love it or don't, but life will never be like this again.

I loved studying in the FSM at Berkeley.  Although the prices are a tad high to eat there all the time, the prices for coffee and drinks are decent and they make it rather well, too.  

It's a nightmare trying to find a place to sit so unless you go really early (sometimes there's a line waiting outside the door already) or really late, you're gonna have to breathe down the back of someone who's already sitting down, hope you make them uncomfortable enough to leave, and grab their table.  Otherwise, esp during finals time, you're gonna have to be REALLY lucky to get a table. 

That said, their salads are great, sandwiches are alright, and pastries are sometimes okay and sometimes not.  Skip the overpriced juices and just go for the coffee.  No time limit, so linger there all you want.  But watch out cuz if I want a table I'll breathe down your back.

FSM Cafe makes it possible to enter the library in the morning, eat muffin/coffee, study, eat delicious sandwich for lunch, study, eat dinner (maybe salad or quesadilla with a red bull), and then study and get a late night snack and more caffeine without ever having to leave the cozy environs of the library. Not that I've ever done that. But I like that you could if you needed to.

Everything I have had here is delicious, but on a student's budget, it isn't affordable. If your a student looking for affordable and good in this area of campus it is best to head up Euclid for more options on a budget.

I love free speech movement cafe!
First, their Cobb salad is really good. I also like their turkey breast panini. It's the main library cafe, so it's a campus cafe. But, compared to most campus cafes, this place is upscale. Honestly, the salads are better than some restaurants nearby on Euclid.
I also like the fact that they know this is a study place and play FM102.1, the classical music station. It's very relaxing when trying to write a 20 page molecular and cell biology term paper.
Thirdly, in the same vein of studying mentality, they have Jolt soda and diet coke and all sorts of fun treats.
Fourth, they  have hard boiled eggs for we south beach freaks.
Fifth, the have CNN on TV playing softly so one can distract yourself with information that is useful.
Sixth, they have air-bears wireless that usually has a strong signal.
Seventh, the new outdoor patio is really really great, now when we get that warmish drizzle, we can sit outdoors and be covered.
Eighth, it's IN THE LIBRARY, once you are done you can go downstairs to the computer lab or into the bowels of the stacks to study.
Ninth, it's a central location so your study group mates will meet you there. You will run into people there. And I have spied some very cute people. If you sit along the back wall, it's a perfect cute people peeking perch.
Enjoy Free Speech Movement cafe, the school down south should be so lucky! 
Go Bears!

Highlights:
Turkey Panini
Chicken Quesadilla
Watch the news while you wait for your order
Friendly staff

I went on a Friday during lunch time. I recommend going when the students are off as it is too crowded and MUCH TOO slow otherwise. I waited nearly half an hour for my salad to go.
I have tried all their salads and nothing else. Their salads are marvelous. I can get whatever I want on the side and they are filling. I recommend trying all their salads and you will surely find a favorite.
The decor is nice. I always read the excerpt of the Mario Savio speech on the wall. It has become one of my favorites.
The menu us full of ingredients that are support sustainable agriculture, and are local and organic when they can (so they say).

FSM Cafe brings back somewhat traumatic memories.  I discovered this cafe after graduating from law chool, and while studying for the CA bar exam.  To get away from all the freaks at the law school, I'd go study at the undergrad library.  For lunch, I'd go to FSM Cafe.  I would meet my lil' bro there, who was two years out of Cal and studying for his 1st year Medical Boards.  We'd meet for lunch and eat our food silently.  FSM Cafe's food is nothing to speak of.  Bland sandwiches, salads, and other desserts made by some vendor and sold to you by college students.  But I think the decor/theme is pretty neat.  Cool posters on the wall depicting the women's rights movement, civil rights movement, and the free speech movement, etc. Anyway, back to the traumatic.  We'd eat our food, outside, on these hard ass cement seats, quietly.  I contemplated how it would feel to fail the bar exam.  The bro contemplated how how it would feel to fail the medical boards.  We both passed.  But it felt miserable that summer of '03.

Fast forward 4 years later...the H and I returned to FSM when we took a walk through campus one night, and it sure was hoppin'.  We came right around finals and the students were typing away on their laptops, freakin' out about this or that.  All I could think was, "Wow, I sure am glad I'm done with all of that!"  Anyway, if you want to be at the center of student central, FSM is it.  It's not quiet enough to actually do hard core studying, but it's a nice place to take a break and observe a bunch of people try to study.

Among one of my many trips to Berkeley, I thought I'd jot down some thoughts as an outsider.

The cafe appears to be a good pit stop or studying lounge for most students. I found myself having some coffee with some friends and enjoying a quiet day on campus. The coffee was average, but fresh, and I couldn't find anything wrong with it. The workers seemed relatively happy, and the place wasn't too packed. I would recommend coming here if you needed to make a quick stop on campus, but it wasn't the best place for a beverage or snack in the city.

So. Good. This is my favorite panini place that I can think of. Delicious turkey panini and fresh side salad to go with it. Seating is not so great, and prices are a little high, but damn, it's good... possibly good enough to go back after graduating........
"ok un co-fee para llevar. $1.10, senorita"

GOOD FOOD! Honestly, I don't come here for the coffee or ambiance...I just love the food here! Try the mediterranean salad...to die for! Lemon/oil dressing. Tried to make it at home...didn't taste anything like it.

Coffee: not the best I've tasted, but then again, I view coffee as more of a caffeine delivery system as opposed to something to savor, so in that regard their coffee does the job. And it's cheaper than starbux =)

Food: pretty good, a little on the small side and pricey.

Location: this is where it shines. In my opinion, it's central location right on campus, and next door to the library, makes this cafe. Great place to meet with groups (especially at those outdoor stone tables), great place to cram for that final while saving precious minutes that would have been lost if you went to cafe on Durant or Bancroft. Plus, you stand a good chance of bumping into some old friends you haven't seen since freshman year there, due to the sheer volume.

I love this place. Not the best coffee, not the cheapest or best food, but I have fond , fond memories of studying here with buddies late into the night.

The salads here are pretty good as are the drinks. The coffee is surprisingly good and it's not a bad place to pick up some orange juice to go. Good luck finding a seat inside. They are most likely filled up by students cramming for their next midterm and whatnot. More annoying are graduate student instructors that schedule their office hours in here. That is just ridiculous to suggest, but it happens. Good luck trying to talk over everyone else's voices in here. There are tons of tables outdoors, but you'll be in hard find of outlets if you want to get anything done on your laptop. There really is no reason to come here unless you are a student or faculty of the university, but no, this place does not take meal points.

it gets way too crowded in here to study, but the food is decently good. 

Turkey and Roast Beef Sandwiches are great and served on (I think) acme foccacia... and if not thats what it comes really close to.

If you want your classmates to hate you, take their Banana Cream Pie to eat during lecture like I always did! works.

I'm sad that this place doesn't accept meal points.

But I'm happy it accepts Cal-1 debit card!

That being said, I love coming here to study :).

When I want to protest something on sproul on a cold day  I  hit the fsm for a hot cup of soup first.  Inspirational pictures of Mario, good cheap soups, and a supply of potential sign holders.  Just another way uc berkeley helps me stick it to the man.

I don't even know where to begin listing the craptascular issues with this place. Maybe the beginning is a good place to start:

(1) It is rather difficult to get a seat at a table indoors, particularly the nice, squishy seats that run along the wall. Not everyday is an outdoor seating day

(2) The cashiers are kinda rude. Perhaps not rude to me so much...someone suggested they're nicer to females. But they're pretty goddamn rude sometimes. One time I was studying there and one dude came around sweeping. Nothing was under my seat but he just HAD to have the broom knock into my seat repeatedly. Another time one of the workers was bothering a student about moving a table to a place it normally doesn't go, but instead of the worker putting the table back where it should be, he moved it around somehow and the table ended up where the student put it in the first place...???

(3) The workers shout out people's order numbers in a very obnoxious way. I've been to my share of restaurants...that degree of shouting is really unnecessary. I bring headphones just to drown them out.

(4) The food is too expensive for what it is. I've never understood why that line is so long. I seriously take the time to walk to the Bear's Lair because I can get anything the FSM has cheaper over there. Thank you Cheese 'n' Stuff and Heavenly Healthy Foods.

(5) I've never been to a restaurant that charges you EXTRA if you eat on a plate. How can their food be so expensive then they're charging 20 cents to wash the plate? They could have at least hidden the charge so I wouldn't feel snubbed. I'll have mine on the wax paper thank you!

(6) The only TV in there is on CNN 24/7. Umm cuz that's "the best news" on TV. There's no sound anyway, they should continue on their thrifty track and get rid of the TV altogether. I don't wanna hear about Jane Fonda's sex life at 50 on Larry King Live when we're in a war.

The only reason why I gave them an extra star is because I LOVE the carrot cake. They lose points for sloppily dumping it into a paper bag, causing the frosting to stick to the wax paper in a most unsavory fashion. It's called a TO GO BOX!

Dear woman at the cash register who made fun of me in Spanish with two other co-workers in front of my face,

Today was the worst day of my back-to-back finals schedule. The stress of it caused four large angry canker sores in my mouth, and I had medication on the suckers to numb the pain. Unfortunately, said medication also made me look like I had been gnawing on a glue stick. I get it. I spoke funny. I had weird gelatinous things in my mouth. I also asked if you had ran out of sandwiches yet (which is not so outlandish if you've ever tried getting one at Micro-Yali's in VLSB after 2 pm and ended up with the crappy breakfast burrito) but to you, was apparently equivalent to asking if the library had books or if Britney's boobs were fake. I must have looked to you like some greasy, dark-eyed, gummy-mouthed street urchin asking if there was still soup left in the pot at the soup kitchen. Understandable.

But that gives you no right to immediately turn to your co-worker in the middle of the transaction and start gesturing at me and pointing and laughing. Moreover, you then made the effort to go to your other co-worker and proceeded to do the same, all while glancing over at me and giggling. It doesn't take a linguist to interpret what's going on there. It would also be nice for you to give me my receipt so I can leave the counter before you start your SNL skit.

It makes me so sad because FSM had a special place in my heart. It's fueled me through many desperate, late-night study sessions with its overpriced but addictive pastries and surprisingly well-made lattes. Some of my most treasured memories happened within its very doors. But to be pointed to and laughed at when I wasn't even standing 2 feet from you right before my last final as a senior was a terrible way to remember one of my favorite study places at Cal.

Please treat your customers with kindness. It really goes a long way.

If I must state my occupation, I will of course go on to say that I am a college administrator.  I work in college administration at UC Berkeley.  I am one of many.  I push papers and pay grad students and talk a lot about academic disciplines that I don't personally study.  It actually can be kind of fun, if you don't let yourself be crushed by the bureaucracy and/or your filing cabinets.

Anyway - my office is housed in the University library, which is majestic and beautiful with views of Berkeley and the Bay and the GG Bridge.  Not too shabby.  Also, this places me within close proximity of the Free Speech Movement Cafe, a place of coffee and food and students and really nice people behind the counter.

Yes, it is expensive.  But you know what?  It's in the dead center of campus (for which rent must be rather steep) and everything there is actually GOOD.  Some of the other campus places run by the dining services are expensive and the drinks/food are unexciting at best.  

At FSM, the coffee is fresh, strong, and HOT (try the Spider - house coffee with an espresso shot.  That'll put hair on your chest), and the food is well-made and tasty.  My favorites: the hot turkey panini with avocado and pesto and the cobb salad with fresh greens and lots of hearty cobb-y toppings.  Yummmm.  I don't go everyday, because that wouldn't be the most cost-efficient way of doing things, but on days when I value convenience for lunch and/or my morning coffee at home just doesn't cut it, FSM always satisfies.

I was here early in the morning.  It was like McDonald's sponsoring a third world country in there.  It felt like a Starbucks trying to pull off.. well, just about ANY cause.  It felt like the Inferno.  Everyone was flying around and didn't want to make any relationships.  I didn't find our little corner to be particularly warm or cozy or conducive to conversation or ANYTHING.  Gut this place.  Put couches in here.  Some fucking megaphones.  And let her rip!  Free speech, man, what a bitch.  ON TOP OF THAT.  Don't fucking call THAT cappuccino.  Nop.  Sorry, dudes.  NOT A MOTHER FUCKING CAPPUCCINO.  Call me a snob.  Maybe I am.  But you gotto get THAT drink another name.  If it's not a fucking cappuccino, why call it that?  I pray.

Dear God, please give free speech another chance.  

Maybe I'll go back for a sandwich, which I hear are good.  

SIDENOTE:  A cafe serving this shit ass "cappuccino" should ALWAYS, I mean ALWAYS (and I hope the law would back me up on this one) have a bathroom within running distance available to it's customers.  If you're here before 9 when the library opens...  Wear Diapers, the moffitt bathroom here doesn't open until nine!

One star for bringing me closer to GOD.

Caution to those that plan on studying at FSM. If you want a prime seat (anything close to a power outlet) you must stake out a seat in the morning, or pray someone leaves. 

The cafe is opened late (2am), and its always a great place to take a break from studying in the library. Why i like this place so much? There is always traffic. When you are miserable, tired, sick of studying, its good to see others in your same situation, suffer together! 

Coffee-wise, i dont think its that strong (caffeine wise). The house coffee is dark but doesnt really taste that good. I usually get their orange juice instead, its pretty fresh.

I have been to FSM a few times in my studies at Cal, usually late at night and usually with study groups. I mostly get food (some of their soups are okay and their asian chicken salad is decent) but i rarely get their coffee. When I do, the situation looks something like this:

First visit:
Me: 'I'll have a nonfat cappuccino please."
J: "I'll have a nonfat latte."
*drinks*
Me: "These drinks taste terrible. Let's never get them again."
J: "Agreed."

Second visit:
J: "I'll have a cafe au lait"
Me: "I'll have a nonfat latte"
J: "Steph, what are you doing?"
Me: "Well, the cappuccinos are bad. Maybe this will be better" *drinks and makes an unhappy face*
J: "Steph, all the espresso drinks are bad. The plain coffee is passable I suppose... hence the cafe au lait"
Me: "Right... remind me never do this again."

Third Visit:
Me: "I'll have a nonfat cappuccino."
J: *looks at me incredulously*
Me: "FUCK!"

... God knows which visit...
Me: "I'll have a mineral water and cobb salad!"
J: "Yay! You're learning!"

Yeah... the coffee is shit. But when you need a boost past midnight, it's just the place. Better than that, they now take meal points for those of you still in the dorms (and even though the food is bad, it's about a million times better than dorm food)

Most recent visit to FSM:
J: "I'll have a cafe au lait please."
Me: "I'll have a nonfat cappuccino"
J: *laughs hysterically*
Me: "What's so funny?"
J: "It took you nearly two years to learn this and what do you order?"
Me: "crap..." *facepalm*

Old habits die hard I suppose...
buying a sandwich here is like slitting your wrists, pouring lemon juice into the open wound, and sprinkling cayenne pepper over it to ease the burn.

Free Speech is not generally a good place to get laptop work done because the ratio of indoor tables to Berkeley students is ridiculously small and the sun is too bright outdoors. Also, you need to be able to get on the Berkeley network to use wireless, I think, so if you aren't a university affiliate it's no good. 

The food and coffee are both reasonably good and reasonably priced, although I have learned two important facts about the prepackaged sandwiches that are ubiquitous on Berkeley campus:

1) Roasted vegetables = zucchini
2) Yellow tofu != eggs

One day over the summer (fewer students!), I did manage to get a table inside. I guarded it with my life for hours and hours until I was so hungry and so cold and so ... um ... needing-to-use-the-restroom? ... that I finally had to vacate. I pulled out my cell phone to check the time, used the facilities, hurried down to BART, tried to find my cell phone, and discovered that it wasn't in the usual spot in my bag. 

I suddenly had that terrible sinking feeling you can only have when you realize something that is basically an extension of your brain, like your computer or cell phone or hippocampus, has been lost or destroyed forever. I had left my cell phone in the bathroom.

My brain: YOU HAVE TO GET IT BACK
Me (to brain): It's probably gone.
My brain: WHY WOULD ANYONE TAKE A CELL PHONE THEY ALL HAVE CELL PHONES ALREADY
Me (to brain): Hmm.
My brain: WE HAVE TO AT LEAST TRY
Me (to brain): So we'll go back, and look in the bathroom, but it probably won't be there, so then what?
My brain: MAYBE SOMEONE TURNED IT IN
Me (to brain): And then we're going to go up to the guy at the cafe and be like Hi uh okay so I'm retarded and left my phone in the bathroom don't ask questions but did anyone like uh find it?
My brain: EXACTLY
Me (to brain): What if he thinks I was using the vibrate function of my phone for unspeakable purposes?
My brain: EW NO ONE DOES THAT EW 
Me (to brain): Okay well what if he thinks I was calling someone in the bathroom, that is also weird.
My brain: IT DOESNT MATTER WHAT HE THINKS IF IT GETS THE PHONE BACK MUST GET PHONE AT ALL COSTS EVEN DEATH SHUT UP AND GO NOW

As it turned out, though, all the worrying about how awkward it would be to try to explain that I had left a phone in a bathroom was for naught because it was still on top of the toilet paper dispenser. 

Thus, at least one of two things is true:

1) Berkeley students are not thieves or
2) Things left in bathrooms are too potentially gross to steal.

I haven't tried this experiment somewhere other than Berkeley to see which is the case, but maybe someday.

FSM has some crazy history that I really should know more about, being a bear, but since my knowledge is spotty I refer you to: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Speech_Movement.

So let me stick to what I do know: pastries. The pastries here are GOOD, and not unreasonably priced, about $2 each. 

Some of the yummies I've had here: Chocolate cake, raspberry cheesecake, pumpkin cheesecake, almond croissant, and more. I've been eating this stuff since Freshman year so there's quite a few I'm leaving off, though I do have a penchant for the cheesecakes and chocolate cake. 

Basically, the pastries are way better than what you could get at the GBC or DCs or the Bear's Lair food court, and what better way is there to get through a class than by eating something yummy for the tummy?

I also like the actual Cafe. Cool decor, internet (but of course), and nice, chill atmosphere. Only bad part is the sometimes *insane* lines between classes.

Thumbs up for FSM!

I have to go to the bathroom.  Bad.  Really bad.  If I get up, I'll never get my seat back.  Maybe the feeling will subside...

With a raging case of undiagnosed ADD or maybe even ADHD, I love FSM.  It's always crowded and there's always something to distract me while studying.  I can even eat here alone and not feel awkward: plenty of people around to look at, the tables are decorated with newspapers from the '60s, and the CNN effect is always steadily going strong in the background.  Magic.  Good luck finding a seat, though.  I used to cut out of class early in order to find one.  And once you do find one, don't even think of getting up until you know you're ready to leave.  If you're having trouble, try sharing a table with someone and not so subtly edging them out.  The more books you have, the better.  

Best quality food on campus, but you will pay for it.  Go for the soup/salad combo.  It's probably the best bang for the buck  and the soups are really good.  Sometimes they accidentally give you a bowl instead of a cup -- score!

Minus one star for not taking credit or ATM cards and only cash or Cal1.

Good coffee, delicious pumpkin bread and cinnamon rolls! I can't wait to try their other baked goods and breakfasts. I love that their coffee is organic-and kept properly in airpots, not slowly turning stale and burnt on the old glass carafe-on-the-warmer deal that so many cafes around here seem to rely on. 
The atmosphere is very casual with self-bussing of tables appreciated, seating in the upper balcony overlooking the main floor seating and counter area, plus a small amount of outdoor sidewalk seating outside the front door.
Also, every server/counter person I've met seems to go out of their way to be personable and just generally nice.
A great local spot for affordable coffee and breakfast.

I had a muffin here without any drinks, and it was quite dry.  I really like how spacious it is and it's pretty quiet.  Plus they're open later than peet's, so if you want to grab some coffee at like 9, this is a perfect place to go to.

This is a writer's cafe. Pay your dues by ordering a coffee--triple iced espresso followed by some half and half at the station--then take a seat and write. You may be joined by any number of characters who may find their way into your novel. Or may just pee their pants at your table. [To be fair, I think the guy had already done that by the time he sat down.]

One of the best writers cafes in Berkeley.

5/4 Update: Why do I go back? Breakfast last week took 25 minutes. Really. It's not a fancy place either.


I wanted to give this a 3.5

As the previous reviewer said, this is sort of the 'waffle house' of Berkeley. It's a bit ghetto, and a bit of a homeless hang-out, but I have to say that their Breakfast Sandwich is the best deal in town. It's $2.50, and has more eggs and toast then their $5 - two eggs and toast. Go figure.

The coffee is good. Be warned it takes about 10 minutes to get your food. 5 minutes for the cook to realize you are waiting and 5 minutes to make.

So supposedly this is where the cafe latte was invented so of course I wanted to try it. What they gave me instead, however, was a large coffee. Uh, no. I was too lazy to care though so I just drank it. My friend actually got his order right so I got to try it. It was decent I guess but not anything special. I got the tuna sandwich as well, and it came with a salad. They definitely did not skimp on the tuna, but that didn't really make up for the fact that it tasted pretty ordinary. There was nothing particularly great about the sandwich or the salad so the meal was relatively unmemorable.

This place is dingy, bordering on filthy, the service is awful, and the food is mediocre at best. It is however dirt cheap, and a great place to nurse a hangover over strong coffee and greasy food. 

Plus, they invented the Latte, or so they claim...

I've had some of the best mochas here, one of the worst veggie paninis -- nearly gagged on it in all its squishy sticky sweetness and spice -- and the service is usually quite slow, but the price is right and I'm trying to be patient.  On one late afternoon, I got the most blatantly rude sass from someone who obviously doesn't want to work there, as if I offended him by asking a question and then trying to order something from the menu.  Gee, I'm sorry answering a question is exasperating for you, and that you don't have the ingredients to make what's on your menu.  I'll bring 'em myself next time.  

Maybe he'd just had a long day.

If the coffee drinks weren't so good....

I liked this place.  Definitely had a Berkeley feel to it.

I read this was a tourist place for inventing the latte.  As a former barista, I had to visit.  And of course, I tried a latte.

The latte tasted like any other latte.  Steamed milk and espresso.

I think the guy behind the counter was a little stoned.  I think that added to the Berkeley feel.  :-)

Nice coffee shop ambiance.  Definitely felt like a place you could take someone and have an uninhibited, thoughtful and intelligent conversation.

There's an upstairs with seating that overlooks the lower floor.  I always like that.  It's ideal for people watching.

This place boasts that it is the Birth Place of the Cafe Latte. So I thought Hey Now I am going to give their latte a whirl. I did and I was unimpressed. The latte was drab, the scenery was dark and dingy the people behind the counter are kinda snooty . I did not even like their banana nut muffin :(  The only and I mean only saving grace was that the  latte art ( a leaf ) was wonderfully crafted.

Went into this place after passing it way too many times, and before reading any yelp reviews. It was about 9:30 a.m., and class was canceled. That means breakfast is in session.
First thing I noticed: everything seemed VERY cheap. Egg plate with home fries and toast? 3.50. I don't know about you, but that surprised me. The rest of the menu seemed quite well-priced as well.

Got a coffee and the starter breakfast plate. Both were tasty.

As far as the environment, I liked it. It was relatively empty, peaceful, and just very relaxed.

Of course, after reading the other reviews I realize I'll have to come back at another time. Now that I think about it, I saw the hipsters trickling in as I was leaving.....

But if you want to stop somewhere in the morning and don't want to spend much, this is a great spot.

-Good hours & location
-plenty of tables to sit and study at
-large food menu

I might go back, but I've been a few times and gotten a Cafe Mocha both times, which I probably wouldn't get from them again. They put way too much mocha powder in it, so it's all grainy and sludgy. Plus, all their drinks have two espresso shots, which is good if you like strong coffee, but if you don't, it sucks. I haven't tried asking for one, but I'm guessing with one it would be the same price. I might update later if I have a better experience. This review sort of gives them the benefit of the doubt.

One of my favorite places, ever. Wonderfully located on Telegraph Avenue, across the street from Moe's Books and Shakespeare & Co., The Mediterraneum is a hotbed of cafe literatti in the grandest tradition. Any time of day or night, you will find it packed with students and writers, many of international reputation, talking of books and politics. But there is no snobbery here: there are homeless folk as well, wandering in off the streets of Berkeley. Everybody is treated as a welcome guest. Although the place is large (two stories), the service is personal and attentive and the staff always makes me feel as though they are welcoming me to their home. These folk also care about food and coffee. (They invented the Caffe Latte.) Coffee is always prepared with care. Food is basic, fairly priced, and prepared with care. Salads are fresh, omelettes are perfectly cooked, pancakes are delicious, potatoes are exceptional, nothing on themenu is over $7.00.

They are proud of their literary history about which you can learn from articles and photographs posted on the walls.

A Great Place!!!

Coffee: These are some of the few people that actually know how to steam a good latte. As a barista for 3 years, I've come to be picky about my espresso drinks, but the staff here always get it right, and are really friendly.

Food: Food here is delicious and decently priced. Breakfast is super cheap! I'm never going to Ann's kitchen again (Not true, I probably will end up at Ann's) with this right across the street. Pancakes are a dollar. Starter plate was $4 I think (eggs, toast, etc).

Also, a nice place to study with just the right amount of background noise.

Free Wi-fi too? Yeeuuupp. 4 stars.

Will forever be a fan of this place. Great espressos, lattes, veggie burritos, and my favorite, the veggie omelet with avocado. The only knock I have is the lack of tables. I often fear standing with my omelet and having no place to sit--inside or out front--but it hasn't happened yet!

I decided to give this place a try.  I got an omelet and was surprised that I also got some potatoes and what appeared to be some toast.  The "toast" was just warm, but not very toast like.  The portion was pretty good.  The price wasn't too bad.  I like the fact that they use loose tea leaves and the tea was quite good.  The service isn't the greatest.  The place was kind of dirty too.  I'm not too sure if I would come back here.
breakfast burrito is cheap and very good!

Coffee is real good and sandwiches are surprisingly decent. The service here is very mediocre, once I had to wait 10 mins for a toasted bagel. There are always some pretty loud and obnoxious people hanging out inside and outside that make studying here difficult. Come by for a nice strong coffee but don't expect much more

Cafe Mocha is pretty good. Cafe latte, not so much. Oatmeal raisin cookie was lacking in oatmeal and texture. 

Sit upstairs if you're going to study. Service not the best but bearable.

Everyday for about 9 months I would wake up, either hungover or still drunk, and stumble my way up Durant to Telegraph Avenue. Telegraph offers many distractions from my thoughts and woes, with pizza, burgers, beer, clothes, frozen yogurt, beer, or smoke shops as potential outlets.  Everyday, without questioning, I would pass these places and a myriad of spangers and tourists with the thought that something more glorious was on the horizon.

My mouth would begin to water as I imagined what waited for me between Haste and Dwight.  I would rustle through my pockets, weeding out the bottle caps from the coins and unfolding the beer-soaked dollar bills to determine the amount of Caffe Med's delicious elixir that I could consume.  Most days I would have to sacrifice my obsession with crossword puzzles and forgo purchasing the always-hilarious SF Chronicle to make sure that I had the option of consuming the most ounces of the Med's SUPERB iced coffee.

If Moses was alive today, he would have made sure that the Med's iced coffee were included in most, if not all of the commandments.  In fact, he would climb atop Mt. Rushmore, as he did so gloriously 60 years ago, and denounce God, naming Caffe Med's iced coffee as the supreme chancellor of awesome.

If you're really feeling like a pro, add some of Caffe Med's endless supply of free honey and a splash of brown sugar to complete the experience.

Putting aside the iced coffee, the Med has quite a bit more to offer.  I know that you are all thinking drugs, and you're right, but it goes even beyond that.  If you know anything about the Med, you know that those who live, and I mean LIVE there, are the craziest monstertruckers this side of anywhere.  Crazy, though, is always construed as frightening.  The Med's crazy is only entertaining.  Furthermore, the people who are hired to serve these crazies are even more entertaining, as someone who has the patience to listen to a very drunk homeless man tell you that your wife will leave you for a black man is not only filled with very entertaining stories, but will also let you crash on their couch, spray paint obscenities on the windows of the Telegraph tourist traps, and stay up drinking with you until 7 in the morning when you all walk up to the Med and do it all over again.

I would say that those who go to Peet's or Starbucks or whatever other coffee shop should come to the Med, but I don't want to hear you request a 117 degree soy half-caf latte and a salad with light dressing and then complain about how Derek in human resources can really be a pain in your neck.  I want you to stay in your plain, delusional world and think that you're happy.  What I want, though, is some in-your-face iced coffee and a chair outside so that I can waste away my day and walk home knowing that I have been fortunate enough to stumble upon possibly the coolest coffee shop on this planet.

Caffe Med was my second home during college and I credit that to their house coffee. There exist a plethora of coffee shops speckling the campus/Telegraph area but none with a comparable cup o' joe. No sugar or cream necessary; it is brewed often and is consistently delicious. 

They also carry a great selection of specialty teas; the tea pot service is perfect to share with a friend. I found myself studying at Caffe Med for more hours that I had at my apartment or on campus.  They have wi-fi and a lot of seating, and the old staff was always very friendly.  The breakfast burrito, salads, sandwiches (grilled cheese!) never disappoint as an affordable boost of energy in the middle of a long haul of studying.

This is the place I spent most of my time at during my visit to the Bay. They claim to have originated the cafe latte and I wouldn't put it past them -- it's delicious! it's all I have there hah. Should probably try some of their other stuff, too.

It's a nice, casual place, nothing fancy at all, but the bartenders/servers are super nice and friendly, and there is a wide diversity within the clientele. While that might be off-putting to some, I enjoyed it. Even the homeless people who'd come in weren't really a nuisance or anything. They only problem I had with the place was the bathroom. While in theory it's locked and you need to get a key, anyone and everyone can just take the key and go at it. My worst experience was someone apparently puking inside (which is what I could discern from the noise). That's really why it's a 3, otherwise it'd have been a 4 for sure.

Cute place. They claim to be the home of the original latte - the latte is quite decent, though I'm not sure I believe the claim. The pesto panini was good. The pesto is made from scratch on premises - we had to wait a bit while they made it.

Walking into Cafe Med, you sense a extensive history.  Aldous Huxley used to hang out at this Cafe during his time in Berkeley. In addition, a scene from the "Graduate," with Dustin Hoffman was shot in the front window. This place is definitely a staple of the Free Speech Culture in Bezerkeley. The Cafe is often filled with old hippies, young hipsters, and the occasional tarrot card reader. The discussions and conversations I've heard in this place are priceless and unrivaled. 

Cafe Med has tasty coffee, a huge selection of teas, nice pastries, and a full breakfast, dinner, and lunch menu. It's inexpensive, and everything is pretty good. 

Downsides: the Cafe has a small number of outlets, so if you have a computer, I wouldn't suggest it. In addition, the culture of Cafe Med is very tolerable of vagrants and vagabonds who stroll into the place. Rarely is someone asked to leave. This sucks when your trying to write an essay and someone keeps bothering you for change. In addition, there have been numerous thefts of personal belongings, so take things with you if you use the bathroom. 

Also great hours: they are open til 12 at night!

Get tea service, another good place to study for students. 
The selection of tea can meet anybodies expectations.

I work at Nomad Cafe and I've been to just about every cafe in the area, as I'm also a student, and this place is BOMB.  I don't feel I'm betraying my beloved Nomad, as it's about 2 miles away, but for me:  Near the BerkLand border, go to Nomad, near campus, go to Mediterraneum.

although I guess it just depends what you're looking for.  I'd love if they had a couch or two, and I happen to like that it doesn't look all glittery clean, as long as they wash the cups, and as far as I can tell, they do.  I also don't mind the crazies and eccentrics that wander through.  They won't hurt you, and they make Telegraph pretty much the only interesting thing in Berkeley.  

So here's why the 5 stars.  Most importantly, they consistently make the best drinks in Berkeley.  Espresso; delicious.  Coffee; delicious.  Foam; perfect every time.  Even a rosetta depending on the barista.  It's also remarkably cheap.  The food is not gourmet or knock your socks off, but it, also, is cheap and consistently good.  Also, there's sooo much room!  And I hate cramming myself into a cafe to sit, so this gives it a lot of points.  There's free wi-fi, unless I've been stealing someone else's.  
I also love that there are always enough people actually conversing with one another to make some pleasant white noise, rather than just the clicking of laptop keys so typical of most near-campus places.
The two times I've been here the workers have been really rude  and unhelpful. Their coffee is mediocre at best and the only good thing is that they open late!

Great espresso drinks! Cheap filling meals! I literally don't know how they serve breakfast so inexpensively but they do fill up your plate for under 5 dollars. This used to be our go-to Sat and Sun morning hangout when we lived in Montclair. Yeah driving to Berkeley was a pleasure when we had Med coffee waiting for us. Now that we live in the City it took us a few months to find a coffee spot that cared about making great mochas and lattes as much as Cafe Med. (Simple Pleasures in the Richmond Dist.)

This has become my hang-out of choice. Why? Well, because 1) It stays open until midnight! I am definitely a night person so I go here to get my work done. 2) I am not a big fan of coffee but I really do enjoy their Cafe Mocha. It really hits the spot. 3) Great location on Upper Telegraph by the University and my house!

The food at Mediterraneum is pretty good, especially for the price! I like that this place also has history...it's been here since the '60's I believe and you can tell it has served many a straggler. While this is awesome, it is also part of the reason I don't give the place 5 stars since I feel like it has a little too much grime to it sometimes.

I write this from their upstairs area right now and am very pleased to be present while someone is playing wonderful live music on the piano.

I walked into this place for a pick me up experiment.  I asked the two baristas, a girl and a guy (whom both were positive and humourous) to make me a nice experiment.  We decided on a simple vanilla soy latte with a mocha drizzle.  Best coffee I ever tasted, perfectly layered with good amount of foam, YUM.  I had to borrow money so I could tip them.

I also like that they offer ceramic or paper cup for my own hippie environmental way.  

I haven't had the food, but the display looked very clean and presented nicely.

Overall a relaxed environment, might I add that the homeless floaters adds an interesting extra ambiance to it all. ;0)

The birthplace of the caffe latte, Caffe Med is a good place to frequent if you want some good, relatively cheap caffeine while soaking in the Berkeley atmosphere. Their lattes aren't the best I've ever had, but they're pretty good. I wouldn't recommend their iced teas, though; I've tried them twice, and once it was just ice water (almost tasteless) and the next time it was super sweet. It's nice to just get a pot of tea here (works out cheap) and sit and get my reading done.  

I like going here because it's near my apartment. However, the service is frustratingly slow and their internet isn't always reliable. The place has a definite Berkeley vibe to it, and is rich with history and culture, but I've grown tired of the eccentric people who frequent this cafe. It's good, cheap, and has convenient timings, but it's not my favorite Berkeley cafe.

Their chai latte is pretty good. :)
It was a bit noisy and crowded when i came in one morning, but service was still pretty fast.

Good squating location for laptop doers. There were plugs everywhere, wireless access never lost connection, and nice atmosphere. 

I would have liked so more comfortable chairs since I planned on doing hours work there, but that's not to say they were uncomfortable, very pleasing actually. 

There's also a "read a book.... leave a book" shelve, nice! 

I had a soy white mocha, perfectly served. :) The food looked delicious as well, next time I'll have breakfast..... stay tuned!

I came here with a friend. We ordered two small Chai lattes with a shot of espresso each. The barista makes the 'dirty' chais and then she says "oh shoot. we're only supposed to make sizes medium or large of this dirty chai. is that okay?"

Is it okay for...?? you to remake our drinks? for you to charge us for medium chai lattes? She thought the latter.... we were charged $10.50 for our mediocre drinks. These cups are SMALL by the way. I would have rated higher if the atmosphere was better but this cafe is dingy, dirty and full of smelly people. I would not recommend this place at all, and will probably not return unless I'm feeling extremely frivolous and/or risk my health.

The upstairs portion of this local spot is where it's at. Surrounded by books with a "read a book, leave a book"  policy. I sat back in the corner and was shocked to see a hidden office and storage area packed behind an orange bookcase (you can see the lock if you look closely)

It's a pretty busy cafe, but the only spot on the entire street where I felt like I wasn't being crowded or rushed. The cafe claims that the latte was created here first in the 1950's, but I am yet to find actual proof of this. 

I had an iced Vanilla Bean latte and found a standard latte. The espresso was very strong in taste. Service was kind, but pretty difficult to understand because of language barriers. Eager to try a hot latte and see if their art can cut it.

Bad experience here but it seemed to be because the manager on staff was a little out of it... I know, it's Berkeley; I should expect this.

The Bad: They forgot my order, the lemonade was incredibly pulpy and sour, and the mango smoothie had chunks in it.

The Good: The employees were really friendly and their almond croissant is glorious.. it just melts in your mouth. 

I will definitely go back for their almond croissant and try a latte.. They claim to have invented it. Although from the other reviews it sounds like a mocha is the way to go...


Also: They have a "share a book, take a book" bookshelf upstairs, which I found incredibly cute..

As stated in other reviews. This place is the birth of cafe latte. I've had it about a year ago. It was good from my memory. I'm going to get it the next time I go. Yes, the location might be slightly less than ideal since there is a slightly a larger population of hobos outside on Telegraph, but there are definitely a LOT of pros for this place. 

Price is pretty darn decent.
Giant Cookies- $1.00
Intense 4 layer Chocolate cake: $3.50
Pot of tea: $3.00- can refill up to 5 pots *I love loose tea leaves*
Sandwiches are less than $5

Nice and chill service

Live music on the piano.

Open til 12 AM!

Surprisingly, even though it is midterm season, this cafe was not jammed packed with student&their books like Cafe Strata or Milano. It was a relaxing and chill atmosphere to hang out with friends or study. 

One inconvenience was that there is no outlets on the lower floor. I peeked upstairs for future reference and there were outlets upstairs for long cafe nights. Also, the internet wasn't the best- but that might be good on days I need to study. Nonetheless, I shall be back for another study adventure!

We were killing some time before heading to the Oakland airport after a wine tasting trip in Sonoma and decided to stop in Berkley. My dad went to UC Berkley (back in the 70s I think) and suggested this place, where he said he always used to study (and complain about the corporations, maann). He said it was where the latte was invented-- so I got one and it was delicious. Breakfast was great. My dad said it hasn't changed much. The pictures hanging on the wall were pretty cool, and I thought the service was friendly. A cool end to our trip.

My favorite coffee shop in berkeley, it is kinda crusty, bums outside, burntout hippies discussing the undeserved prestige of Harvard while they drink the last sip from the coffee they ordered 2 hours ago. I think the bums keep some of the more annoying college kids away, so they actually do at least one thing! The tables and the ceiling are almost certainly the originals from the 1950s.
Great espresso, crappy drip coffee (dont get drip coffee here). I dont know how someone wouldnt like their mocha, I think it is great. Their cappuccino has not much in the way of foam, relative to other spots, but it is way good. Their food is cheap, and for the price, surprisingly good. 3$ for a stack of good french toast! If I have the choice I go here,

Every time I got out of class and my girlfriend got off of work for lunch we would head down Caffe Mediterraneum and order the strongest cup of coffee Berkeley has to offer. The people here are so nice that there have been days when we have been late for class/work b/c of us enjoying the company of other patrons and employees.
All about the Cubano!

it's dirty, and the bathroom can get outta hand - i feel lucky to be a guy in that respect.  still there's a soft spot in my heart for cm, which now forms "the triangle": cm, moe's and amoeba records.  "triangle" now instead of the "square" becuz cody's is gone... :(

yeah, it's fulla berkeley crazies, but they're harmless.  just laugh at 'em.  free wifi, unlike peete's, which has attitude and makes you log in every hour so you have to get a new code, etc.

food's just ok - 2.5.  all in all, a classic berkeley hangout.

Damn good lattes, caps and espresso.  

The best, and depending on the barista, dare I say, better than Peet's Coffee.  

The older gentleman with the gray hair, is the best.  Make sure he makes your drink for you.

This is a great place to study and read. There are always enough seats for everyone and the staff are very friendly. And the most attracting feature of caffe mediterraneum is that it has a fairly long history and it's on telegraph ave which is what Berkeley is about: the homeless, the musicians and the poets. 

The coffee is pretty strong. I had a regular house coffee and it was one of the strongest regular coffee i've ever had. 

The downside is that you can find local poets trying to sell their books in the cafe, which depends on whether you like it or not. :)
this place feels like bum central. cheap and dirty except tea was like twice as much as at starbuck's or peet's.

Nice space, and perfect lighting to study, read, etc. Mediterraneum has good chai and they were nice enough to suggest I try honey over regular sugar. 

When using the bathroom, I found the light was out. Fortunately there is a window and it was still light out. 

Despite the toilet being for customers only, a homeless guy found ways to continue using it without the key (waiting for people to come out). He also kept going up and down the stairs. Also, a bunch gathered on the 2nd floor (where I was) and hung out, constantly using the bathroom. 

If the bathroom light had worked and if there weren't as many homeless people inside, I'd give Mediterraneum Cafe 4 stars (not 5, because of the neighborhood).
Five stars for the good, cheap coffee, and for being one of the only places that was open near my friend's apartment. I didn't know this place was legendary. Allen Ginsberg? Howl? Epic.

I have been here many times and enjoy their food, but I cannot respect them as a business. I understand that it is standard practice to have places not allow outside food (which that ticks me off already) but I was told to either buy something or I couldn't stay there. For a cafe, I just see it as downright rude and completely arrogant, I don't care how good the food is, they don't have the respect for their patrons unless they pay every time. If you don't give them money, you're unwelcome. It's good food with a very greedy and disrespectful staff.

As a Yelper who values service as much as the food, I would give it 1 star (I actually wouldn't mind seeing it closed down) but I respect it for having a Berkeley ambiance to it and of course, making history with the famous latte.

'The Med' is is open from 7:00am to midnight so it is there pretty much when you are..

The staff is generally welcoming and the large tables have enough space around  them to crowd some chairs around them to accommodate a gathering. The wireless signal is strong. And the Med offers food and desserts in addition to a full range of coffee drinks, teas, and Italian sodas.

Best mochas in the world. Ever. Strong and delicious. With a pretty fig leaf if you get the right barista :-)

Brewed coffee is delicious too - always well-balanced and interesting.

Pancakes are remarkably round and fluffy, and omelettes are good - I used to live on them when I was a student because of the price and amount of food.

Too bad I live on the other side of town now and we only make it over for breakfast on the weekends sometimes, but oh man, I miss those mochas and that insanely cheery red-haired guy in the mornings :-)

It must have its pros and cons.  
Pros can't be the food though.  I had the nEopolitan panini.  mediocrity.  I'm not hostile to this place except that I feel like I wasted one of the meals of the rest of my life there.

Everyone's upstairs with their internet connections.

My relationship as a customer with the Med has been like that of someone trying to hold onto a crappy boyfriend who just keeps effin' up after lots of second chances. I've given this place so many tries strictly because I really like the friendly, often quirky staff and the menu is cheap, but here are the things I am really not into:
