1. The coffees are VERY hit or miss. One day you get a spectacular cappuccino and other next you're wondering if the barista was trying their very best to mess up your hot chocolate?? I was a barista for 2 years, I don't buy that "it was the soy milk" excuse. come on...

2. The veggie burrito is not really vegetarian. I discovered this when one of the staff members mentioned that the rice is made with chicken stock. I was pretty pissed since I ate it damn near 3 times a week without eggs and cheese, doused with Cholula sauce because it was so bland. I later tried to calmly talk to the management about it but got an awful response from the bitchy cook.

3. The crust kids that hang out in front. 'Nuff said.

It's over, Caffe Med. It's not me, it's you.

The ambiance is something like a 1950's ballroom meets a bustling diner. I love the upper level and overlooking the hustle of the day from up above. With two levels, there's quite a bit more space to stretch out and certainly enough tables for everyone to have a seat. There are lots of outlets as well (thankful sighs emit). 

As for the coffee, I am a mocha fiend and they are certainly up to par. Although not as rich and sweet as most establishments, the cafe mochas stand on their own for style and flair with an indulgent caffeinated delight (Be prepared for a whipped cream avalanche is you ask for it).

I have also had a pleasant experience with Caffe Mediterraneum's famous Caffe Latte which was a lush as any caffeine or coffee-goer could ask for. Props as well to the beautiful foam art on every order.

My only qualm is, as a known drinker of only "hot" coffee, the scorching heat of the day can make the inside of the establishment a bit sweltering. Thankfully, the second floor seems to have a considerable breeze which makes drinking hot beverages in the summertime far more manageable.

Let's face it, this is the place where the latte was invited. Nuff said!  I'm not really into writing fragments. Alas I must. Like I stated in another check-in at this place this, The Med has some of the best Espresso on the west coast.  Though I can't understand how this place has rated 3.5 stars with 87 samples. I can only think that the ambiance has not helped matters. Though I wouldn't change this place. If you are somebody who likes the coffee and ding this place because of the decorum well I suggest you go down to Urth Cafe in Beverly hills and enjoy yourself there.

What abhorrent service.  We sat and watched our friend's food sit getting cold while they prepared everyone's orders. Then they unapologeticly gave him cold food. When the last thing to go on an orders plate is bacon and someone is standing there waiting for their order, don't make two bacon burritos for the people who ordered after them. This place has really gone down hill.

It's funny, but I've never been to this cafe during my 4.5 years of schooling at UC Berkeley. So when I re-visited my stomping grounds, I was excited to experience my dining at this location.

Food is very good, organic and fresh. The place have that cultural ambiance that's a perfect place for studying, catching up, or having a quiet meal. I love how they have an upstairs offering as well. Clean for the most part. 

The staff could be a bit friendlier. I thought they were a bit grumpy and not friendly at all. Made me feel uncomfortable which is bad because you want folks to feel welcome especially in a mom and pop cafe. But I'll give them the benefit of the doubt because they could be having a bad day.

Probably come back here, and it would be because of the food.

It's unfortunate that the biggest, most conveniently located cafe in Berkeley has such greasy food, incompetent employees, and a guaranteed stock of crazies from Telegraph. Whenever I'm in there I want to take a sponge to all surfaces. I'll admit I dig their mochas and I applaud the free wifi, but the bad experiences outweigh the good. Blah.

I feel like I've swallowed the idea that this place has "charm." I'm always looking for it, but I can't find it. 

Pros:
The espresso is great, the wifi is fast and stable, I kind of like the way it looks, and it's a cool place to go check out your new purchases after you've visited Moe's across the street. I really liked coming here by myself on the (rare) mornings that I woke up too early and snacking on their $3.50 eggs, potatoes, and toast breakfast.

Cons: 
The bathroom is disgusting.
The people: as a student, I want to be around other students when I'm working at a coffee shop. There's a large diversity of people here, including a good chunk of loud crazy people. The environment doesn't feel very intellectual, and it's actually kind of depressing--like it's stuck in a degenerate version of Berkeley's past.

I lived a block from here for 3 years, but tried my best to avoid it as much as possible. Not because it's that horrible, but because there are so many other great places to study and drink coffee that have much better ambiance. Now, the coffee here is very good, though I'm not sure if I totally believe their whole "birthplace of the caffe latte" thing. I feel like the caffe latte is a simple enough drink to be invented at tons of places. They do serve the best one that I've ever had, though. 

But the ambiance here is not that great. Though the waiters are pretty friendly, about half of the tables are set out in the middle of the room and there's an echo, which doesn't seem very cozy to me. There are always a bunch of hobos outside the door that hit on me (and I'm sure they do it to a lot of girls) and I do NOT appreciate it. During finals I came here to study, and the waiters or whoever let some of them in where they proceeded to have a concert, completely screwing over my studying. I have never been back after that.

I love cafe med. Since the day I came to Berkeley, this was one of my favorite spots. But today I learned that they co-sponsor the anti-homeless ordinance in the city (http://berkeleycivilsidewalks.com/supporters/), which is a huge disappointment for me. This place prides itself for its connection to the civil rights movement and the black panthers. Unfortunately, it looks like it has changed since then. 

 I decided to join the boycott against businesses that sponsor the anti-homeless bill, which is so disgustingly called "Berkeley Civil Sidewalks" - as if homeless people are not civil. Cafe Med's management should think whether they're the ones who are not civil. How shameful.

cheap consistent food. really nice baristas. AWESOME TEA!!! 
i agree with another review on here, if youre near oakland then go to cafe nomad and if youre near campus go to the med!

This place is a Berkeley institution and certainly has a lot of interesting history but from a pure coffee and food experience, it's only ok. The coffee is alright. If you like sweet drinks and feel like splurging, the iced white chocolate mocha is pretty decadent. The omelettes are typical diner-style omelettes, nothing much to write home about. 

If you want to come here to study there are a few outlets upstairs but they're not always available so be wary!

I've walked by this cafe about a million times and never went in.  But I needed some after-dinner tea and Peet's was closed, so in I went.  And it turns out that this place has a pretty nice loose leaf tea selection.  And the barista was really knowledgeable about the different teas and gave friendly advice on how long to steep each variety of tea.  I had no idea this place cared so much about tea!

Very well lit, free wifi, not nearly as crowded as Milano or Strada in the evenings, and has talented and friendly staff.  I can't believe it took me this long to "discover" this spot.  I'll be back for espresso soon.

I've been  meaning to try out this place for a while and finally got the opportunity to when Ann's Kitchen was mysteriously closed this morning. I was pleased with the prices since they were lower than Ann's, but I would soon be wishing I was at Ann's. Whatever this place is known for, the food definitely isn't it.

I ordered a simple breakfast of eggs, sausage, homefries and toast. They were out of homefries but if I had the chance to try them I'm sure the most they would have been would be at best mediocre just like the rest of the meal. The one exception and the worst part of the meal were the eggs. I ordered sunny side up, the easiest egg dish to make, and it was ... way overcooked. The edges were pleasantly crunch and the egg yolk had solidified to a tasteless powdery block of blech. 

I'll probably be back to try out this amazing coffee everyone raves about when I need a caffeine hit, but next time I'm getting breakfast won't be here.
Pretty good panini.  Prices are great.  I think the foaccia was a bit stale though.

OK, so the environment's not that killer, but there is something endearing about the black and white checkered tile floor.  The clientele's not that upscale, but if you want shi-shi, go get shi-shi! (chi-chi?  sheeshy?  Sheesh!)

But as far as "don't wear your nicest", as another review suggested, &$%*! it!  Wear whatever the heck you want, always!  Wear it and declare it!  I admit I'm probably a little out of place with my heels and business garb, but I like to stand out.  But that's just me.  And sure, I do my best not to make eye contact with the other patrons, lest they harass me while I'm trying to work.  "Hey pretty lady, I'd love to have you in my art sometime.  Can I draw you?"  Nice guy, but no free modeling here, and kindly leave me alone!

But I like this place.  They know how to treat coffee.  A self-professed coffee-snob and former barista, I can appreciate that they tamp and swirl the milk pitcher.  It makes nice percussion, too.  Tamp, swirl.  Tamp tamp tamp, swirl.  And almost all of the baristas can make the little rosetta leaf designs.  I really like the barista with the green hair and many piercings.  And the graying red-haired guy.  Both incredibly sweet humans.

Great chai, too. Divine chai, aptly named.  

Oh yeah, they invented the latte here, too, but the cappuccinos are so good I've never even gotten to a latte.  You can read the blurb they have about it on the wall above the register.

I've been to Med so many times and had amazing coffee here, but apparently coffee is all you need to know about to work here. I ordered an iced loose leaf tea- which in their credit they don't usually do... but I think logic could at least assist one in this process. One might figure, steep tea- pour over ice, yes! But for some reason the barista thought it was the best idea to just put the tea bag in the cup, put some ice in it, and fill it with cold water. Sure, you can cold brew coffee or tea, but it's a long process. 
Making matters worse, he then proceeded to stick his fingers into the cup to pull the tea bag to the surface of the ice. I've been sitting next to it for about 10 minutes and have only been able to bring myself to take one sip.
Although this experience is the only one of its kind I've had... I will be seriously hesitant to order from this barista again.
Best latte I've ever had. My mother owns a cafe. Craig is so nice and so active in the community. It's difficult not to support this place. If you're in Berkeley, you should definitely try it.

In love.

With cheap food. (2.95 for a bomb hot and melty egg sandwich, with your choice of cheese, bread, and meat if you eat meat. I don't, and opted for monterey jack and rye bread with the eggs... SO DELICIOUS. My boyfriend was laughing at me across the table as I devoured my sandwich with a look of intense pleasure on my face.)

With ambiance. (There's no shortage of conversation fodder in this place, namely in the shape of photographs on the wall from back in the day when Berkeley was a whole lot more interesting... naked hippies and dancing in the streets and whatnot.)

With the abundance of plugs. (Not sure about downstairs, but upstairs is definitely accommodating for students who need to park their butts and laptops for a while and get something done)

With fresh squeezed orange juice! (I love sitting upstairs and watching the barista slice open oranges to be made into the freshest juice ever!)

With their hours of operation (Open early, close late.)

What's not to love?

The Goods:
+friendly, helpful staff
+excellent coffee beans for the purchasing (Barefoot, et al.)
+decent lattes
+across the street from a fantastic bookstore

The Not As Goods:
-insipid drip coffee
-mediocre pastries
-tiny, wobbly tables
-aseptic, "study hall" vibe

The Take Away:
A good place to peek into your new book over a latte or to refuel your coffee bean supply; not the coziest cafe to park for extended cafe lounging.
Great coffee. Like the giant coffee mugs. Like the available tables outside.

I work down the street at the Center for Independent Living, so I've tried the full range of breakfasts offered in the area: Ann's Kitchen, Bongo Burger, etc. Honestly, you get the best bang for your buck here. I always get the same thing - Med Omelet with Wheat toast. It's fantastic! Kalamata   Olives, Spinach and Feta cheese, homefries and toast to boot, all for under $5. I'm not a coffee drinker so I can't vouch for anything other than the food.
Great space and darn good latte.

Meh. It was O.K. Had much better breakfast foods in other restaurants in the area. Apparently it was where the latte was invented, but I'm not the biggest fan of coffee, so I'll only be commenting on food-related subjects.

Decor and Service: The biggest thing that stood out to me were the tables. And I mean that literally. The tables on the first floor were absolutely ginormous and pretty tasteless. They could do better. Service-wise, they seemed pretty nice. They have a system in which they shout out the order when they are done cooking it and customers have to come pick it up. I was talking with my friend and since I didn't hear them shout our order, I have no idea how long that plate was sitting there. At least it was still warm.

Food: My friend and I both got the denver omelette, which consisted of ham, bell pepper, and tomato, and it's served with a piece of buttered toast and home fries. The toast tasted fine, it was toasted with butter, but the home fries were a little disappointing. The flavors were uneven and some pieces of potato were more undercooked than others. I felt that the parsley taste was overpowering and would've preferred them a bit crispier. The omelette itself was very basic, and I think they actually used sandwich ham inside of the omelette. The proportion of egg to filling was a bit large, as well.

Verdict: Probably not a place I'd come back to, except to try their latte that I have yet to taste. Breakfast-food-wise, you're definitely better off at Ann's kitchen.

As with other Telegraph businesses, Caffe Med has large portions of decent food at cheap prices. And that's a recipe for success in a college town. The more eccentric patrons add to the lively and raucous atmosphere, and you definitely have to raise your voice to have a conversation, but it's a fun, casual setting to enjoy a meal. I got the tuna sandwich for ~$4.50. Maybe it was just because I was a first-timer, but my friends and I were not sure when our food came out because the shouting from the kitchen is not really audible from the dining area. You just have keep an eye out and recognize your order, I guess. As for the food: I appreciated that the hearty wheat bread was toasted. Interestingly, the tuna had corn in the mix, too. I'm not a big salad person, but the vinaigrette dressing that came with the side salad had a good sweetness to it and made eating leaves nicer. One of my friends got a breakfast burrito that looked really awesome, so that's a priority next time I come. I might replicate the idea of an egg sandwich in a tortilla myself in the meantime. Saw board games on the piano against the wall--bonus points!

My ideal espresso bar, with genuine Berkeley ambiance, ample seating, good coffee drinks, decent prices (although lattes are a bit pricey), cheap cookies, etc etc. Haven't tried the food though, but that doesn't mean it can't be my current favorite place. Plus they're open til midnight, which I don't think any other coffee bar would have the gall to do.

It was okay. 

I tried the chai latte for ~$3. I brought my laptop with the intentions of organizing my calendar and classes. I like that there's free wifi and lots of space. 

However, there are definitely some interesting characters who go there. The smell of foccacia was delicious, but then someone would walk by, and I would get a whiff of less than cleanly hygiene. 

Also, I didn't notice until I was picking up my backpack to leave, but the floors were really dirty. Maybe I just went on a bad day?

My friend and i stopped here because they had outside seating.  It was great for people watching... you see it all from crazies to UCB kids to homeless and wannabe homeless (you know those young people who sit on the sidewalk and do nothing but go home to their parent's house at night)

The bathroom was terrible and disgusting so try to hold it!

The guy who helped me get a drink was really nice and friendly, the guy who told me where the bathroom key made me feel like i was wasting his time as he stood there doing nothing.

Summary: great for people watching bad for peeing

Not gonna lie.  I came here just to steal their internet.  Purchased a cheap drink and loitered around for a while.  hehe. I'm bad.  I discreetly looked around at the food other customers were chowing down and it looked pretty good..

Still, it wasn't very crowded and had that nice laid back cafe feel.  I'd definitely recommend if you don't want your soul to rot at main stacks.

Hey people, if you're looking for a "nice" cafe this isn't it, look for something more anticeptic--those kind of places are only too easy to find.

The Med is a hallowed haunt, perfect for writing, thinking, talking, and some good, heimishly-prepared eats at a reasonable price (the huevos rancheros are a personal favorite). It's within spitting distance (so to speak) of Mo's Bookstore, best bookstore East of the Bay: paradise!

The old Cafe Picaro on 16th in the Mission (before it morphed into a tapas place) was in the same niche as today's Med. Dingy comes with the territory. If you're put off by the vibe, move on to Pete's and be happy, rookies. For everybody else...well, there's always the bathroom at Mo's across the street!

The bathroom is dirty and sometimes has syringes in the trash. Most often people are asleep in the upstairs area. Intelectuals adorn berets, greasy hair, and books by Keets. I love it

Everything changes but the Med has always stayed the same.

Really cool barista behind the counter.

Love the spacious seating upstairs overlooking the railing.

Good peanut butter cookies.

But the depth charge (2 espresso shots + drip coffee) totally kicked my ass.  Man, I thought I had a tolerance, but apparently I'm still a java lightweight!
The tea here is so hot, I wonder if the water is radioactive. Great people watching...

This place has truly fallen apart. Living in Oakland it takes a lot for me to come all the way out to Berkeley just to get something to eat, but I had some faith in this Caffe from my first visit a year ago.

Things have changed..

I stood in line for almost 15 minutes just to order my food. A kid who looked like he was still in high school didn't even know how to work the register.. k whatever.. big deal..

But it didn't stop there. It took the two chefs (calling them chefs is a stretch considering one looked like a crusty punk from people's park and the other looked like she was still in high school) about 25 minutes to make me my "Med Special" which isn't all that special (three eggs, sausage, and hash browns). Hash browns were nearly freezing.

To put the icing on the cake, they completely forgot about my friends order. When my friend asked for his money back the owner rudely slammed his money on the table and said to "GET OUT!"

This place is a joke.. Just because some hipster authors wrote some lame books here doesn't mean it deserves your time or money!!

Absolutely no outlets on the first floor. Don't even bother looking. But all the individual tables on the second floor are TINY. So between power outlets or table space, you can only choose one. Bathroom could be cleaner. Heck, the whole place could be cleaner. But okay, enough complaining.

Good selection of teas. Got a pot of one of their rare teas (milk oolong) for $4, and it was very good, tasted great after multiple steepings.

Coffee is good. And they supposedly invented the latte??

From the assortment of peoples in front of the cafe I am sure you can tell that they get a lot of interesting characters... Once when I was studying, a man at the table next to me started talking to me and sort of addressed me on-and-off for the next 15 minutes. Actually, he was quite interesting, and I didn't feel at all harassed, but basically my advice is not to come here if you are trying to get some hardcore studying done--you never know what's going to happen here. Light reading or non-urgent work is recommended; midterm cramming is probably best done elsewhere.

All in all, a nice cafe with a lot of history. Read their little blurb next to the window about a scene in The Graduate being filmed at Cafe Med and you will feel like a special, hip little snowflake.
$2 Short stacks! $3 Tall stacks! My egg was done perfectly.  My meal was excellent, unfortunately my coffee was super watery.  All the employees were really nice.

This place is really cute and a nice environment to sit over a pot of tea or a nice latte and catch up with friends, study, read a good book, etc. Their teas are loose leaf, nice quality teas, not the tazo or stash bagged teas I kept coming across whilst in search of a great little cafe to grab a tea. I was surprised that I couldn't find some great organic tea options in the area... but, I probably just don't know the secret spots. 

The staff was helpful and the man gave me tips on brewing times, etc. It was kind of noisy and a bit dirty in terms of used dishes lying around, but I can see the appeal for students trying to get some studying done. Free wi-fi. A couple of outdoor tables, but they were full.

Tired from walking up and down University and Telegraph, my boyfriend suggested resting for a bit.  I agreed, and we started looking for a coffee shop of some kind.  We saw this place, and he just looked at me.  "Perfect," I said, and we walked into the seemingly small hang out.  That was deceiving!  This place is huge!!  Two floors of sitting area?!  Free wi-fi?!  Open late?!  Why can't there be a place like that near where I live?!  Oh, yeah- because it sucks down here.

Anyway, I got a chai latte (sweetened, as recommended by the friendly guy behind the counter) and the man got a lemonade.  The cost was pretty much par for the course for a chai, but the lemonade was something like $2.50 for a small- and they mean SMALL.  It was gone in 5 gulps.  

Two stars were subtracted for the miniature lemonade serving and the place wasn't really that clean.  Plus a smelly homeless guy was sitting in there talking to himself.  As entertaining as it was, I'm not so into that at a coffee shop.  But maybe I'm just a bitch.

Cafe Med--also fondly known as 'Homeless Cafe'--is my favorite cafe in Berkeley.  I drink A LOT of coffee and definitely know that when I enjoy it, it's good stuff.  Cafe Med has the most delicious and strong coffee available.  I live in Oakland now, and though it isn't that far away, I always make the trip to study at Cafe Med.  Even though sometimes the bums and grunge kids can be annoying, I really think they contribute to the unique experience at Cafe Med.  I love that it gets a little loud in the evenings because I need noise to concentrate.  Cafe Med also has really excellent huevos rancheros---they are a must have.  Their other food is not that great, but I come here for the coffee, the great owners and staff, the crazies and their hours--they are open from 7 am - 12 am!
Authentic Italian coffee (very good espresso)! Free WiFi. Good spot to sit outside and what the Berkeley life on the sidewalk.

I've been going here for 4 years..so this review is a long time waiting. 

Their breakfast is pretty great..their drink serving needs work though. Every time I have gotten a drink either "for here" or "to go", it manages to spill or I get burnt. I think they over pour, don't use big enough cups, and do not give cup holders upon receiving coffee. Their coffee jacks me up like no other though. 

The bathrooms are seriously gross. Homeless people galore. 

I have a spendgo account, and the guy keeps telling me to go online and redeem it..but spendgo says to activate the redemption upon purchase....anyways. 

The lady who makes the food is a total jerk..just saying. I asked her for to-go ketchup packets and she said, "we don't have any". Then I asked her what I should do, and she says, "there are little containers to get it to go"...why couldn't you just tell me that in the first place as opposed to making me ask you..common sense, FAIL! 

The flow of ordering is confusing. I feel like when I walk in, i'm immediately cramped for space, even if there is 2 people ahead of me. When ordering, I just kinda linger awkwardly waiting for my drink as opposed to being told what to do ("go sit, i'll call you"; "please wait over here").

All in all, solid 3 stars. Food is pretty good (they have vegan cookies!), and drinks are good. Service, flow, and maintenance needs some work though. 

P.S make sure you specify, if a vegetarian ordering with a meat eater, you want your food on a seperate plate. The evil lady placed bacon ontop of my pancakes then accused me of stealing food because I asked her to remake them, even after offering to pay for it AGAIN.

I came here to hang out, and by the time I left, I was a little charmed by the place. Its a straight up breakfast/lunch/cafe all mixed into one. It has actual menus to choose from but the atmosphere is very cozy and inviting, like what a cafe should feel like. I ordered just the starter for breakfast (2 eggs, onions & potatoes, 2 slices of bread) and it was pretty good for $3. They just recently begin to serve this Vietnamese Coffee drink, and I would advise not getting it. They are still experimenting with it in my opinion, just a tad too sweet and uses a lot of condense whole milk. 

I had fun hanging out there and I like their not-too-expensive breakfast/lunch menu. I now have a new place I wouldn't mind coming back to for hanging out, doing studies, or eating. And that is something rare nowadays.

..Though parking is a b**** in that area. Just saying.

Wonderful place to chill and people watch. Very distinctively Berkeley. Very Telegraph. I can't imagine a Telegraph Ave without The Med. Hippies, weirdos, radical self-proclaimed anarchists, sketchy, funny-looking folks, Cal students and homeless floaters rub shoulders outside this café. Inside, it's warm and cozy, with a diverse but low-keyed patrons, reading, chatting or typing away on their keyboards. It's comfy upstairs. Big Plus for Me: Good loose leaf tea selection, including Asian tea leaves. Liberal, relaxed vibes all throughout. I walked in on the day of Berkeley World Music Festival and heard real good psychodelic live music played by a guitarist who shook his head like mad while playing his amazing songs. Lovely! Come here, read a book, drink their famous latte or get a cuppa tea... Keep this café alive. I don't need another clean but characterless Starbucks or even Peets here. Keep Berkeley's indie spirit alive!

Good spot for wifi, tea and coffee.  So far I haven't tried the food but I did like their smoothie. Kindda drab environment.  They have a second level towards the back of the (large) unit where most of the laptop totting crowd is based. Good office away from office (OAFO) spot.  Plus they stay open late.  

PS: This place has so much potential.  Just add some nice furniture, better lighting, plants and perhaps flat panel TV
PPS.  Want to use the bathroom?  The key to the bathroom is keychained to a medium size metal pitcher.  I had one lady waiting in line commenting on the (tantalizing? nah..) possibility of peeing in the keychained pitcher

Meh. Couldn't have said it better myself. I was initially intrigued by this place when I walked in, and, in fact, the reason I decided to have a sit here instead of at another coffee shop was for its neat atmosphere. The people watching is great if you are like me and are strangely fascinated by deranged or otherwise dysfunctional folks, creating disruptions of any magnitude. If this is the intellectual community the Med claims to foster, it's there alright.

I don't usually assume coffee shops will let me sit with my dog, but I asked anyway. When they said no, I tied him up outside, and came back to order something to drink. It was only after I had paid for my drink and settled down with my things that I was informed rather rudely that I couldn't have the dog outside, not within 200 feet of the entrance. Or, anyway, this was their spin on things. Well, I have news for you, homie:

According to the CA State Health Department, "any open air dining area that is not COMPLETELY enclosed (that means no birds, no insects, etc) is not considered a "food facility" and is not required to comply with code 114045 which specifically bans dogs (with the exception of working dogs) from food facilities."

But it was pretty smart of you to let me put down all my things and get comfortable, so that you could seal the purchase before completely deterring me from ever giving you my business again.

And in all honesty, if you are that concerned with health and sanitation, I would recommend you look at some of the reviews on the dirtiness of your establishment, because they speak VOLUMES of truth. I'm not all that bothered by it personally, but if we're going to be consistent here...

Overall, I like that it's crazy and dirty. But I don't like being conned. Learn some manners.

Oh Cafe Med, what did I ever do to deserve you?
If there was such thing as a "dive cafe", you would be the queen of queens in that category.
I love this place.
If you're tired of cramped, boring and dull places like Starbucks, Pete's or Tully's come here.

The Good: Cheap food (grilled cheese sandwich w/swiss and home fries are my favorite!) cheap coffee, wonderful staff (if you don't smile, don't expect one back) great wi-fi connection and a place to study even when I don't buy anything, and you can call in orders too!

The Bad: People watchers (I myself rather do something worthy of watching than sit there and wait for something interesting to happen), pretentious customers and I wish they were open longer (although they stay open the latest of all the cafe's around)

This place is amazeballs!

I'll go here if I need caffeine right after hitting Moe's, but that's about it. The menu is more extensive in some ways than most cafes (I think they do smoothies and milkshakes). Ambiance here is deadly -- despite the huge space, it's dingy in a way that makes it feel cramped.

UPDATE: I've had second thoughts about this cafe and raised my rating from two stars to three. Why?

The staff is friendly and the upstairs section has outlets and is spacious, so I can work or talk with friends without feeling cramped. It's not like Milano or Brewed Awakenings, where the tables are crammed together.

really full of fun people, a bit different from the rest of the coffee places in berkeley, service is good, one of the guys kinda looks like the man from that mythbusters show, he rocks the berret

the coffee is good, if you like sweet stuff you should try the vanilla chai latte. im a fan of the mocha, the fresh oj is great, you see them throw the oranges into the sqeezer thing when you order it. the food is pretty good too. the hot drinks are served in these big round mugs, they make me feel like im at home.

though its not the calmest or the cleanest cafe, its got free wifi and is open pretty late. oh yeah, they have huge cookies

I work from coffee shops a lot.  It is hard to find really awesome places to camp out with a laptop for 9 hours and get stuff done.  I spend a lot of time going to places, not having anywhere to plug my shit in, having a hard time finding a place where I can sit and not feel cramped, dealing with sketchy "free" wifi, or having to watch some stupid ass advertisement every hour to keep the intertubes flowing.  I also don't like when people look over my shoulder, or the barista stares me down for not buying enough coffee refills. 

The Med Cafe is definitely the best place in the eastbay I've found to work.  Ive been coming to med several times a week for over a month now.  sometimes for as much as 12 hours in a sitting.  Sometimes I drink a cup of hot tea for $1.50 and sit here for 12 hours.  Sometimes I stay all day and eat breakfast lunch and dinner here and buy 19 cups of coffee.  No matter where I sit, how long I'm here for or how much I buy (or don't buy) everyone is super nice. 

Here are as many reasons as I can think of off the top of my head which contribute to my 5 star ranking of this place.  

-Free internet that doesn't suck.
-Lots of tables, and on the second level, there are lots of power outlets.  I have never had a problem finding somewhere to sit where I can plug all my electro-crap in.
-Cheapish and goodish coffee and tea.  ($1.50)
-They have rad mango/green iced tea
-All of the food is pretty good and cheap.  Omelettes, sandwiches.  All like 5 bucks.  The sandwiches come with a salad.  The food gets brought to your table fast...maybe 10 minutes.
-They have tobasco sauce (a must for omelettes)
-You can stay here as long as you want and not have to feel compelled to buy more than 1 cup of coffee, although I usually do.
-They keep the bathroom very clean.
-Lots of secluded-ish tables
-Some of the tables are lower than the average table - which gives you perfect wrist positioning to type on a laptop for a long time and not have your tunnels get all carpled and your fingers go numb.
-Open windows in the back on the second level for fresh air
-There are usually at least 4 entertaining weirdos here.  (not the type that come over and bother you though.)
-Did I mention the green/mango iced tea yet? mmmmm.

Here are a few cons, however they have not managed to taint the 5* rating.
-THEY DONT HAVE BEER!!??!!! (this almost made a dent in the rating)
-One time I got a piece of chocolate cake, and it was a little crusty, but I have had it since then and it was good.  I guess just don't get the cake at 11 at night because its probably been out all day.
-Sometimes there are smelly people here.  Sometimes they sit near you.  Whenever this has happened to me, there have been plenty of stink-free people to sit next to in other parts of the cafe.

MOST IMPORTANTLY!!!! - The convenience store down the block (walk out the door of med, turn left, go 1.5 blocks) closes at exactly midnight.  Make sure to leave MED a few minutes before they boot you out at 12 so you can buy beer before the place closes.  The dudes who work there are cool but will bust your balls if you buy Colt 45 and Doritos.

I lived in Berkeley thirtysomething years ago, and the Med is where my friends and I spent a couple of hours nearly every evening.  I loved the place.  My travels over the past few months have been taking me across the Bay to Berkeley again, and I'm delighted to find that the Med is still there--and hasn't changed much, other than the addition of wi-fi and the removal of ashtrays.  It ain't fancy, but they make a hell of a cappuccino.  Give it a try.

It's definitely a little rough around the edges, but the Med is a unique cafe that exemplifies a certain side of Berkeley, and for that matter, Telegraph. The crowd can be a bit scruffy at times, especially later at night, but I've never encountered any problems. I find the Med to be a comfortable place to set up my laptop and get some work done. There seems to be less empty distractions here than at a Starbucks-type place, and thus I often find myself getting into the zone and being able to study uninterrupted for an hour or two. The more I visit, the more the Med grows on me.
Hands down the best place to be hungover.

Back in high school, I used to come here every day. I thought this place was "electic" and "authentic" and was full of "vibrant atmosphere." I thought this place was Berkeley at its finest. 

Much later in life, I began to realize that "eclectic", "authentic" and "vibrant atmosphere" are just synonyms for "urine stench", "lunatics with Tourette's Syndrome" and "too dirty even for rats and cockroaches." However, the fact that this place is emblematic of everything that is Berkeley still rings true. 

That being said, I'm pretty sure there's still some of my old punk band's stickers stuck to the wall in the bathroom somewhere. Sigh, memories.......

I'm not sure whether to be happy [for myself] or sad [for the owners], but this place is definitely an overlooked gem in terms of espresso around campus.

To think people even consider drinking anything less diluted than a latte at any number of the conveniently located coffee shops (milano, strada, brewed awakening, etc. etc., etc.) makes me cringe, especially when something like this exists. I know of no other place in walking distance that actually has employees who both know how to use an espresso machine, and actually seem to care about the art they are creating. 

They preheat their cups with hot water before pulling shots, tamp the grounds correctly [and by hand] in the portafilter, are aware of how long they are pulling the shot, are skilled at creating the perfect micro-foam in one-person servings, and will actually make beautiful rosettas in your cappuccino. All other shops in the area use disgustingly over-roasted greasy charcoal black beans which some people might think is 'strong' coffee, but is simply burnt. Caffe Med not only uses properly roasted fresh beans, but they make their drinks with Organic Clover Stornetta milk (which I'm pretty sure they modestly refrain from advertising).

They have a sign claiming to have invented the Caffe Latte 30-40 years ago; whether this is true or not is most likely disputed, but if there's one place around campus that could have, it'd be here.

I haven't had enough of their food or pastries to make a conclusive judgement, but personally, I come to coffee shops for their espresso and their amiable atmosphere, and this place has the best of both. I totally agree with Chris M., who importantly has experience working at a cafe, that this place is BOMB.

Yes, there are the handful of regular eccentrics, but what would Berkeley be without them? The free and fast wifi, lots of space, nice upper seating, and knowledgeable staff easily make up for any gripes you might have.

this is one of these places that definitely deserve more attention as well. though it's a bit hipster-ish and there are random people that come in and out and the bathroom is a bit ghetto, their drinks here are quality drinks. i have to rave about their tea selection just because I am a big fan of tea. they have a wide variety of tea from ooloong to indian black tea. i got the pu-er tea, which is my favorite tea and the quality here is definitely very good. it's a super good deal too. you pay $3 and you get a pot of tea and i literally refilled it 4 times. 

this is definitely a good place to do some light catching up/studying.

I don't come here for the food and drinks, admittedly. While I was a Cal student, and especially during my senior year (because I lived five minutes away), I came here often for the WiFi and the occasional Italian soda or café latte, and many of my friends also met here for hanging out or doing homework. 

The drinks are decent, though the service could use some work. Once a clerk forgot my soda, another time a different clerk asked me if I wanted sugar in my latte, and even though I said yes, my drink was sugarless. However, this is purportedly the birthplace of the café latté, and they make it well. The sandwiches and salads are also good; I never had any problems with them, though really, how can anyone mess up a salad?

As mentioned before, I came often for the WiFi. It's free, a rarity when most other shops require a purchase. It's up against Café Strada for best ample seating, though because Med has most of its tables indoors, it quickly becomes crowded on rainy days. That leads to another problem: there's no air-conditioning. There's just basic window-opening for ventilation, and on hot days, it can get pretty humid inside. But the lighting's good; it beats Café Milano in that area.

Overall, it's a decent place, nice for studying and hanging out with friends, as well as being a historic place in Berkeley. There's Moe's across the street to boot if you want to grab a book to read, too.

This is one of those sad Berkeley places that has a Past, and that seems to have never got past that Past, giving it a pathetically anachronistic or tired air nowadays. As someone else says, the aging regulars here do a good job of either scaring away or repelling the younger (student) set (which admittedly might be an advantage to some).

It's often difficult to sit in peace here -- there always seems to be some damaged hippy or aging unreconstructed Boomer talking at the top of his or her voice about the Past here as though it were of interest to everyone, when in fact it's usually just toe-curlingly embarassing stuff. Urgh. And it always feels gloomy inside, even on a sunny Saturday morning.

Having said all that, the coffee can be quite good, it's usually not too hard to find a large table, the staff are friendly, and the food won't kill you. And it's near Moe's...

Very cool this coffeehouse has such a history behind it, being one of the oldest, if not the oldest coffeehouse on the West Coast. I have been visiting here on and off for nearly the past ten years, and have seen the place get a lift, some good much needed maintenance of the restroom and building in general.

Earlier this afternoon I had a cubano--it's like a rather strong espresso with caramelized sugar. Such rich flavors, ever pleasant even through the slight bitterness of the espresso-sugar mix. My friend had a mocha, which he described as "very chocolatey." Good to last drop, so I heard ;-).

I'm so glad an institution like Mediterraneum still graces Berkeley--nice to make a visit every so often.

I wrote this cafe off years ago when I walked in and there were bloody tissues strewn across a table.

Times have changed.

No, the Med is not prim and clean. There's still suspect characters both in and out. But I just had a delicious hot apple cider, there's free wifi, the place has a new-ish paint job in parts, and the guy at the counter was far friendly than I've experienced before. Hell, even the bathroom was a lot better than I'd feared.

Besides, you could hang out here all day and the worst thing that will happen is that someone will spange you. That, or mistake you for Dustin Hoffman.

The Med is a piece of Berkeley history - for better and for worse.  Yes, expect some filthy conditions and some wack-a-doodle-doos who frequent (and a few who work at) the joint.  Meanwhile, the caffeine rush from the espresso based beverages will see you thru another day.

A good place to chill with a book or people watch.

Not my favorite and Definitely not elegant - but you gotta check out Cafe Med at least once or twice while in Bi-zarre-keley.

When I'm itching for a good cup of coffee or a comforting place to study, I always find myself at Caffe Med. I first discovered this cafe on a cold, dark night with my boyfriend. He was looking for a strong cup of joe, I was looking for some dessert to calm my sugar withdrawals. Although I was wary of the colorful clientele in front of Caffe Med, I decided that my dessert needs were much stronger. My boyfriend ordered the house gourmet coffee while I got a slice of pumpkin cheesecake. And from that moment on, my relationship with Caffe Med began. 

I fell in love with its inviting atmosphere, the vibrant characters who occupied Caffe Med everyday, and of course, the coffee! I was never too fond of coffee until I had Caffe Med's caffe mocha. Although a tad expensive, their caffe mocha is worth its price with its a rich blend of chocolate, complemented by two generous shots of espresso. I never have to add any fixings to my caffe mocha because it is perfect just the way it is. Don't tamper with perfection!

Although I personally do not like the taste of the caffe latte (because it is not sweet enough for my tastes!), I would recommend coffee lovers to give it a try, seeing as how Caffe Med is the birthplace of the caffe latte. Another coffee concoction I recommend? Try the Berliner! I'm even drinking it as I yelp :) The Berliner is comprised of 2 scoops of vanilla ice cream with a cup of the house gourmet coffee, topped with a generous cloud of whipped cream and flurries of chocolate powder. A delicious, cold coffee treat for anytime of the day and anytime in the year.

The food is good, but doesn't measure up to their coffee. Their sandwiches are nothing too extraordinary. One thing I would recommend on their food menu are their hearty breakfast burritos! Their breakfast burritos are huge, large enough to prevent me from eating until dinner time (side note: I eat A LOT for a girl, trust me). I always get the Denver breakfast burrito, which has a generous serving of eggs, ham, black beans, rice, onions, bell peppers, and cheese wrapped in a warm tortilla. Yum!

Caffe Med is a nice, comfortable place to study, especially on the second floor. There are outlets everywhere on the top floor and free wi-fi to boot. Some people may not appreciate the homeless people or those who appear "different", but I personally like it because it makes Caffe Med, well, Caffe Med. 

I wouldn't change a thing.

If you shower twice daily, look well kept, or godforbid DON'T care about violation of Right to Privacy, this is not a place for you!

Mediterraneum is an important insitution on Telegraph Ave, or at least what Telegraph used to stand for. All the old radical intellectuals, and hippies and passer-by anarchists congregate in and around here to, well, be radical. Unfortunately Berkeley has long stopped being the cradle of rebellion, so mostly all these guys accomplish is scaring off freshmen UCB students to the other side of the street. 

The coffee and pastries are like the ones you can get at any 24-hr doughnut shop, and I've never stayed long enough to try the food.

Valuable as a kind of time capsule of American liberalism. If you have time, chat with one of the scarf-wrapped men who look like they are in a perpetual existential crisis- you will be surprised how many interesting things they have to say!  You might even be tempted to google Camus or Cocteau when you get home.

I frequent this cafe on a weekly basis because it's so close to where I live now and because it's open until midnight everyday... a caffeine-dependent student's dream. :P

I haven't had too many food dishes, but I fell in love with their turkey sandwich. It's so cheap too! Basically everything on their menu is sold for a pretty decent price. Their cookies are only a dollar; hence, I ALWAYS get the almond cookie. Not overly sweet, which is exactly how I like it. Plus, it's really big, so it always leaves me satisfied (yes, inappropriate jokes are popping into my head at this moment...).

I'm not much for sugar-y and milk-y espresso drinks, so I haven't tried their famed caffe lattes yet... I swear I will next time! I always get their tea service. $3 might be pricey for some, but there are free hot water refills, so you can definitely get your money's worth.

Service has always been really good. The people who work there are very very nice, and you can tell that they have the best intentions for their businesses. Makes me warm and fuzzy inside. Hehehe.

My major gripe about Caffe Med is its overall ambiance. There are times when everything's nice and calm with the background chatter lowered to a slight buzz. However, there are some, errr, eccentric people who frequent this place. They usually don't bother the patrons, but there are some who are quite rude. There was one time when a fight erupted on the second floor, with yelling and everything! It really disrupted the mood, and I left not too long after.

tl;dr: I really like this place, with the exception of some of its guests. 
3.5/5

The hey day of this place passed decades ago but the disheveled burnouts and hippies still keep the seats warm, heads buried in laptops and e.e. cummings. The food doesn't keep them coming back, but the colorful cast of characters and potent brews seem to still deliver a kick. I suppose an institution is nothing without its coat of grime. And its a good reminder to the Cal passersby of Berkeley's radically liberal roots. Props to these folks for keeping the spirit alive.

The best thing in the former left-wing radical glory that was Berkeley.  

It does look run down; but really, that's a plus in my book because I feel comfortable here, not like I'm in some upscale dining room.  The cappuccinos are by far the best I've had in Berkeley (good coffee in the Bay Area usually ends up with me going into the city), the food is cheap and honestly good.  The food isn't gourmet, but like something your grandmother who wasn't big on presentation, but heavy on butter and giving you a good meal would cook you.  And again, let me emphasize: cheap.  A lot of food for under 5 bucks.

The wireless works and it's free (unlike Milano, which obviously likes taking money from Cal undergrads with daddy's credit card).

It's never too packed, and not deserted.  It's a good work environment.  

Legend also has it that this was where Alan Ginsburg put 'Howl' to paper.  It's always good to support your local old school bohemian haunts, and it's even better when they are worth the money you pay.

I've said it thrice, quarice, and pentice (haha): the Bay Area is a liberal person's dream come true when it comes to creative little hole-in-the-walls to consume at. This place is no different.

Sure, you're on the edge of a very touristy, student-ridden Telegraph district, but this place does combine history, comfort and the avant-garde into one little dumpling. It's open til midnight daily. Killer.

It also claims itself, despite the emergence of Starbucks in Seattle, to be the placential origins of the Caffe Latte in 1953.

Optimal opportunities to people-watch from a second floor sequestration (where all the wall outlets can be found, chicken-poxed by people's laptop plugs).

Probably one of the richest mochas I've ever had in recent history. It tasted like a chocolate cake suspended 30% in the solid state, 70% in the liquid state (that's a good thing).

Love it.
My opinion has been lowered a tad by the realization that there seem to be no outlets on the ground floor. Boo.

I'm not a coffee drinker, unless its foo foo 8,000 calorie frozen coffee drinks. So the fact that I not only tasted, but actually enjoyed my girlfriend's Iced Cafe Americano, and even considered ordering one for myself (then actually did on my next visit) speaks very highly of this place's cup of joe. The key is the liquified simple syrup compund, which makes sweetening cold beverages that much easier. Since I prefer iced coffee, why not?

The breakfast burritos would be good if this restaurant were located on just about any other street, but rank right in the middle of the crowded Telegraph Ave. Breakfast Burrito consortium. In general, the food is fairly average, though the service is much faster than one would anticipate.

the berkeley cafe saga continues. this is a place that i had walked by, and shuddered, for years when i would visit berkeley. there's usually this fustercluck of guys in front who look like shit and are probably talking politics or the time ginsberg tried to pick up on them. inside its dingy with depressing flourescent lights. 

well i'm doing this berkeley cafe tour - so i finally went in. the help was very friendly. the latte was weak. there are no visible plugs on the ground floor so i ventured up the steps....

and hung out there very happily for hours reading my book and using my laptop. free wifi - yes. huge bonus points - open till midnight!!!

and i read on a sign that christmas eve they were giving out free cups of coffee. how cool is that?

i was introduced to caffe mediterranean by a fellow merritt student during my jr. college days. he was a persian foreign student who was vehemently anti-shah (of iran). he'd always refer to him as  the "f.... shah" . he worked part time here and we engaged in all kinds of social and political discusions here. this was the late 60's.

robert introduced me to lattes here. this caffe claims to have created the latte in the 1950's. it wasn't till way later i became a fan of lattes.

i still drive by here quite often but seldom stop since parking is hard to find.  just by happenstance i remembered robert the other day. i hope he is doing well wherever he is and was able to return to his homeland.

As a Berkeley institution, Cafe Med has most of what you could ever want. The espresso is strong, the upstairs seating is wonderfully cozy, Ginsberg wrote part of "Howl" in this location, and it can be seen in The Graduate.

I went in there and ordered a Caffe Latte because the sign on the wall proclaimed that they had invented the Latte in this location in the 1950s for individuals who requested extra milk to combat the strength of their Italian espressos. Though I am usually a cappuccino drinker, I had to try the latte, especially if that's what made them famous.

The espresso is very strong and the milk is steamed just right. Not too much foam, and absolutely the perfect temperature when served. The inside is a little grungy, but that's okay. It's the perfect place to stop with a newly found, used treasure from Moes across the street. It's great for people watching, and the upstairs area always has ample seating.

It's not my favorite coffee shop in Berkeley or elsewhere. For that, I don't even have to leave my block, but it's wonderful if you're in the area and don't mind a few dusty tables and slightly slow staff.

+espressos
+caffe latte
+mochas

While they claim to have invented the caffe latte, they have not perfected it. Do get it while you're here, but don't expect it to be mindblowing. I would suggest seats upstairs to observe all that goes on in here and the seclusion is good for if you're actually trying to get some reading done too.

Ligaya T. and Stephanie W. have already written every single word exactly what I wanted to write and I cannot put this place in better words than theirs.

A place that is not for the faint of heart. This is a favorite place for homeless and crazy people to hang out. I've seen a guy spin himself for a solid five minutes next to my table. I've seen a poor girl get interrogated because a guy was convinced that she was secretly a psychic medium. Best of all, I saw a guy literally facing the wall and talking to it. Some might find this disturbing, but it is this insanity that makes me come back again and again. There is never a dull moment!

Coffee is okay. Wireless is free and so is the entertainment.

I grew up in Alabama. I went to Waffle House religiously. I love sketchy breakfast places.

That being said, I stumbled upon this place after being in Berkeley for only a few weeks. I was looking for free wi-fi at the time and couldn't find any on Telegraph.

I then started making a habit of buying coffee and breakfast here. 

What kills me is that I started getting addicted to the "Med" on my own, and THEN I find out it has some kind of past associated with a certain 70s film and a certain poet and a certain clientele of hippies. 

Why does this bother me? Well, because I thought, in my egocentric universe, that I had discovered it first.  And I had loved it first.  Damn you, Beat poet people.

And you know, now that I am going to a place with that kind of history, I feel like those people that Danny Hoch whines about, you know, the people who are trying to be "hip" by trying to be poor. 

Yes, there are days when I avoid eye contact with some of the men in there. There have been days when I have worried about the staff's safety when they engage in talk with strangers who look like they're ready to pull a gun on those of us who are on our laptops instead of on a guitar or writing in a journal.  But that's beside the point.

I love reading there, and I love that they take the time to squeeze oranges to make juice for me. I love the coffee with the perfect amount of steamed milk, and I love the Roma platter with French toast, eggs, and bacon.

It's my new Waffle House. I don't care that people think it's dirty or that the tables have specks of unknown material clinging to them from an earlier era.  So does the Cafe du Monde in the French Quarter of New Orleans. 

It kills me how many "liberals" like to critique a place for not being as clean as their maid keeps their own home. Ah, the irony.

The sad part is that this coffeehouse has history and potential on its side, but fails.  I remember 15 years ago liking this place for providing cafe au lait for the price of a regular coffee, back when I was a college student and that kind of bargain was a big deal to me.  

But having been back recently, it looks like they have not cleaned the place since I was there a decade-and-a-half ago.  The bathroom is "interesting" in that the graffiti has piled up so much over the years that not a square inch of unadulterated wall space survives.  Of course, you would only find that out if you were brave enough to ascend the rickety staircase to the dark and gloomy balcony where the bathroom awaits.  The balcony is the most like a back alley I have ever seen in a space that was actually inside.

The coffeehouse is a good place to go to study semifunctional mental illness, if you are ready to hold one or more very unusual conversations with the other customers.

I hope one day someone buys this place, gives it a good cleaning and a fresh coat of paint, and draws back the old crowd of intellectuals, poets and artists that once frequented it.  In the right hands, I think this coffeehouse could be great, but today it is just depressing and miserable.

Not as good as Barefoot Coffee Roasters (I was told that the baristas here were trained under them, btw), but the taste just isn't the same.  I like the layout of the place.  I like that I was approached by a dude to test out some new strain of weed.  I like the crowd of hippies and hobos lounging around too.  It give me a feeling of home.

One of my first jobs was at the Med, in Berkeley. They didn't train me at all, just set me to making coffee drinks and working the cash register. 

Not surprisingly, I was fired after my first shift, and they refused to pay me. I have espresso-making anxiety to this day. 

Saw a very elderly Julia Vinograd wandering Berkeley the other day, she used to hawk her poetry booklets at the Med...brought back memories. There was a point back in the 60's-70's when the Med was one of the few places to drink capuccino in California. The movie "the Graduate" has a scene at the Med. 

Lately it is looking a little sad, like so much of Berkeley.

Great sushi.. They have good baked rolls.. but The service is horrible.. Use to go here all the time until they treated us like we didnt pay or something. Waitress and waiters are a$$e$. other then that just dont dine in. order togo

This is the cheapest place around to get nigiri sushi. 
Highlights:
- Green Salmon nigiri
- White Tuna nigiri 
- Seared Tuna nigir 

I only really get the sushi from the half price menu (as I am a destitute student like everyone else) so I can't testify as to the other stuff on the menu. Admittedly, this is not Tsukiji, Tokyo or Kirrala but I am forgiving if the sushi is forgiving on the wallet.

yummmmmmmmy! always get energy roll. I think that's the best thing on their menu.  other things are pretty good too, and I usually like getting a seaweed salad to start off while i wait for the sushi.  Service is usually friendly, and sometimes they get pretty busy, but most of the time it's pretty ok.  They do have like a 50% off menu, but the other stuff is SO good that I usually would rather pay more for some good good sushi :)

First and foremost there is truly an amazing selection of sushi from sashimi to tempura to baked sushi BUT the best part is that the PRICE completely affordable!!!! :) The staff was helpful and attentive on refilling our drinks. I will definitely come back if I'm ever around the area.

This place was pretty good. 

Food-wise, very good. 

I came here for a farewell dinner (friend is leaving country) and was looking forward to having some sushi again! It's definitely casual, but not really a hole-in-the-wall place I don't think. They're busy, that's for sure. 

On that note, the service isn't terribly good, it's just alright. 

Okay now let's go on to the food (what actually matters right?). Here is what we ordered:
- Yummy Crispy (appetizer): crispy fried wonton skin with spicy tuna and tomatoes medley thing. VERY GOOD! My friend sure knows what's good
- Sashimi salad: it was spicy! But so good. I actually don't normally like to eat sashimi but this was SO tender and SO flavorful ... it was great!
- Mexican roll: I love spicy and crunchy!
- Shrimp tempura roll: Great balancing roll for the meal. and the tempura was delicious (and I'm usually not fond of tempura either!)!!!! 

All in all, price was okay/reasonable. Cheaper than Sushi House in Alameda, but rolls aren't as decadent/stuffed as the ones in Sushi House. Still, very good and very fresh. I would come back happily for this food!

before you read on, you should know there are at least 2 categories of sushi places.  the real fish places where you go for the nigiri and sashimi and try all of the specials of raw fish on offer, and where uni is sweet and sublime, and anything cooked is off limits, unless you can get them to fry the amaebi heads. i'm thinking uzen in rockridge, oyaji in outer richmond, or koo in the inner sunset, or ebisu in the inner sunset but only on a good night.  yum.   then there are the cheaper places you go just for rolls, perhaps someone in your group wants tempura, or unagi, or terriyaki, for shame, but at places in this category you avoid even the thought of ordering the nigiri or sashimi.  these places are cheap, usually run by koreans, and perfectly adequate for your spicy tuna fix, and whatever place-specific crazy ass rolls they offer, actually there is usually  a roll at a place like this actually called "crazy" this or some other.  think manpuku in elmwood for a good example, or domo in the hayes valley, and for a gross one to avoid there is  tako sushi on telegraph.   I guess there is a third kind, which would be any chinese or other run sushi place or anything that says buffet in the name.  those you should avoid at all costs.  

So CU fusion squarely falls into the second category.  And in that category this place gets all 5 stars.  clean, korean owned and operated. and seriously people, don't be turned off from a good thing by the 1/2 off sign.  I don't know if these people are from the east coast, because for some reason, there is 1/2 price sushi perpetually advertised in places all over the upper east and west side of manhattan.  i don't get it. and it doesn't make sense. but really, it doesn't matter.  actually, there was a bookstore on shattuck near the bart station called 50% off books or something like that, which may or may not still be in business, so maybe they got it from them.  but in any case whoever's complaining about the 50% off thing just really needs to focus here.   you get fresh-frozen-fish here (most likely none of it is fresh fresh but the more you know the more you realize this is perfectly reasonable for a place like this.)  

Also if like me you're instantly turned off by anything "fusion", don't be.  this place avoids the gimicky wasabi balsamic reduction nonsense and offers perfectly acceptable dishes with good flavor.   I have even actually tried a few pieces of nigiri here and was pleasantly surprised.  I would try it again, if i can ever stop ordering the spicy tuna bowl, which I can't.  (think nuvo- hwe dup bap for $8.95!!)   I had walked by this place many many times (it's on the trail to bart from campus) but was always turned off by the 'fusion' thing.  But really, you should fear not, and sneer not, give this place a shot.  

My adviser first told me about this place and we've been going here for lunch ever since.  went here again today and food is consistent. You never have to wait too long for a table even at the lunch rush.  The items, and especially the lunch specials "red" "orange" etc.  are set slightly pricier than some of the other sushi options around campus, but damn worth the extra couple of bucks.

no AMEX, which sucks.

I had a birthday dinner here with some of my close friends and All i have to say is that I was blown away on how good their food was for being such a hole in the wall. All we ordered was rolls and rolls of sushi but over all the price wasn't too bad. unlike some other sushi house. Quality was to be expected on the price range per roll. But what got me going was the 50% off sushi they had. That was ridiculously awesome! 
Fresh Fish was really fresh haha Didn't smell old haha just saying.
The waitress was very helpful she kept on coming by occasionally asking if everything is alright and if we needed anything else. Its surprising how packed the area can become during dinner time. 
The only negative thing I'd have to say is that Finding parking is a pain especially in Berkeley, Other than that I was really full and enjoyed every bit of sushi.

I would definitely recommend this place for a quick bite to eat. but avoid going during peak hours lunch or dinner.

I'm just not feeling the sushi that comes out of this place. I've been here multiple times, but this review is strictly for my latest visit.

This place is good for groups if you arrive early and snatch a table. We all got different dishes, and all of them seemed small for the amount that we were paying.

The Tiger Roll was good, but I could not taste the salmon or eel unless I ate them by the slice. Even then, I could barely taste the salmon. I recall that I've had a better experience here before, so I won't hold it against them too heavily.

This is a small, hole-in-the wall, place which is great if you want to eat alot of sushi.
The decor is japanese fusion, which reminds me of a modern-esque decorating style.
But the sushi can be bought in bulk, which makes me very excited.
Whenever I am in Berkeley, I stop in and wind up taking home 11 pieces or so, after righteously stuffing my face, of course.

The Black Dragon Roll is a personal favorite.

Not that it's gross or anything, but with the dirt cheap Tako Sushi even closer to where I live, offering the same quality of freshness and service, I don't think I'll ever come here again. 
 
 Again, it's not bad food. Or bad sashimi/sushi. SS got the chirashi bowl, and he said it was pretty fresh. I got the Lion King roll, which was a tiny 8 pieces, given that it was 9 bucks. 

  Service was a little slow. I mean, we did come at 4, when there was only 3 other parties in the restaurant, with 3 idly waiting waitresses, so it should have been like BAM BAM BAM. But alas, not all restaurant people think like I do. 

  Conclusion: If I were about to faint from starvation and I was in front of C U Sushi, I would get it again. Otherwise, there's waaaay better sushi places to spend your $30 bucks. 

But if you have no choice, go ahead and order the tofu steak appetizer. It's like agedashi tofu, but bigger pieces. Only four, however. Actually, that's probably a terrible deal. Over a buck a piece! Oh well. It was the only thing I actually liked and would maybe maybe maybe eat again.

It was a movie date night & we had only an hour to eat.  Therefore, we turned again to out go-to place.

The Nigiri pieces were somewhat backwards.  The fish was not as fresh as usual but the rice was sticking together much better.  On top of nigiri, we also had 2 appetizers.  The Ika calamari tempura was light, crispy, & not too oily.  Be aware though, the actual pieces of calamari were a lot smaller than they look on presentation.  The Baked green mussels were disappointing.  Neither of us could really taste anything other than the sauce which was SO oily & sweet.  It was so bad that I had to pour the sauce onto the plate before I could eat it.

The mussels?  Never again.  But C U Sushi? We'll be back. Oh & we got some $1 coupons too...that always makes things better.

Ive eaten her three times. Once a friend brought me here also its down the street from where I work. I gotta say its never disappointment when I come here. I think that there 50% off is a little misleading as it seems like every roll that is 50% off has a slightly higher price tag then I would expect. I ate here with my 8 year old and her with her mini appetite and affliction for California rolls and me with my average appetite spent over $30. That is a typical bill at any sushi restaurant that doesnt boast 50%. That being said the rolls have been consistently good. The menu has a variety or basic and fancy american rolls as well as noodles. I always feel a bit rushed when I come her but I think the staff is trying to accommodate the flow of traffic.
Would come back again. No matter how hard I try the lore of 50% still fools me.

It was getting late tonight and we needed to find a place to eat before heading home after a movie. 
The 50% off sign should've been a sign...

Ok, some of the stuff is ok, but I'd think hard before I go back again.  

1.  The rolls (we got yellow tail, shitake, krab, california, dragon, veggie, and a couple more) were made with waay too much rice.   This was a huge turn off because I didn't come in to get 90% full on rice, I came in for 50% off sushi!  :-p

2.  Their veggie roll had lettuce in it.  LETTUCE!  what the...  maybe this is where the "fusion" part came in.

3.  The picture menu is helpful, but only up to a point.  I could've sworn the vegetarian tempura roll showed that it had krab.

4.  The crab was fake Krab and they mayo'ed it. 

What was good, what did I like?  
Their miso soup was very nice.  
The shitake in the shitake roll was nicely marinated.  
The spicy tuna roll was good.

With many many sushi spots in Berkeley around campus, this is one I continue to frequent. My future brother-in-law turned me on to this joint and I can never repay him adequately. In such a busy area, I still get parking easily, I get seated quickly, and I'm always overly-satisfied in sushi heaven. The fish is fresh and it's super affordable. LOVE LOVE LOVE!

4 stars on convenience, price, consistency, and quality.

This place is sooo close to campus (on the West side), and it always satisfies my sushi needs while I'm on the run. While I won't say it's the BEST sushi I've ever had (I have yet to try what the yelp consensus considers to be the best), the sushi here is nonetheless always fresh and not expensive.  

This place never disappointed my expectations for a delicious, healthy, quick meal in Berkeley (whereas other local Berkeley restaurants tend to be quick, but gross.... ahem.. a la Top Dog & La Burrita)

Best place to get sushi in downtown Bezerkeley w/o breaking your wallet.

I can get completely full on sushi for about $20.

Not sure why it says "Fusion" in the name, everything on the menu is what you'd find in a standard Japanese place.

I like this place because you can get a pretty good salad there.  Spicy Tuna Salad (with organic lettuce) and the Seaweed salads are the best, and well under $10.  A lot of the menu items including the Sushi are deep fried, but you can pretty much get around that by ordering raw sushi, salads, soups or a teriyaki item.  I did have the teriyaki chicken before, but the chicken was a bit dry, bland and not "grilled"--it tasted baked instead.   Everything else is pretty good.  The wait staff is very friendly, and remember what I like--they know my voice even when I call in and thats not very often.

Good for the prices that starving UCB students can afford (50% menu yay!), but not the best place to come for quality sushi. Service also needs improvement...
I usually come here and get the Sashimi Salad ($8.95) if I don't want food that is heavy.

aah CU Sushi, a.k.a. 1/2 price sushi to Mr. Gin. (no that's his name, I don't befriend bottles of alcohol). Anyway, when I actually lived in Berkeley, I never came here. And then I moved out of Berkeley and realized what I was missing!

This is a good, affordable sushi place. I'm going to say it doesn't have the, how you say, prestige of Kirala...but it beats going to something like Tako Sushi. Good portions, tasty, and good service.

I even get a new $2 off coupon when I use my old coupon, it's like a revolving door of coupons

I used to go to this place because Nigiri was always on sale and sushi is not that expansive, but I wouldn't go to this place ever!! We were two, and many table was empty. The waitress guided us to the table next to the restroom, so I asked her to change the table since there are many empty tables but she said"NO". We left the place not eating anything there!! Service is HORRIBLE!!

Good sushi, good prices, nothing too amazing...

chickent teryaki rolls and california rolls are really good

the service is a little crappy when they get busy

I ordered the Spicy Salmon Bowl. Warning! - The tomatoes in the salmon bowl can be quite deceptive! Initially I thought I got a huge portion of salmon sashimi, but a lot of it turned out to be just diced tomatoes camouflaged in...disappointing. With that being said, the portion of sashimi was decent, but not great. The spicy mayo sauce had good flavor and the sashimi was of acceptable quality. Prices are fairly affordable. Overall, a good meal but I'm not really too excited to come back.

Three friends and I popped in for a Saturday night dinner. There was only one table open inside, which was lucky because I was not about sit outdoors when I seriously need to thaw from a cold and drizzly Bay Area afternoon. A packed restaurant is always promising, so I opened the menu eagerly and became unsurprisingly overwhelmed and indecisive about the many choices of sushi rolls and other entrees.
With help from one of the servers who recommended a number of popular picks from each of their three categories of fresh fish, tempura, and baked rolls--only slightly narrowing it down--we settled on a spider roll, a spicy salmon roll, and the Lion King roll.

The spider roll came out first. It's relatively large in width and sadly crumbled before I could complete the dip-in-soy-sauce-and-deliver-to-mouth move. We weren't even sure what the tempura-d meat was, as it tasted just like fried breading. All in all, tasty but not amazing. Next, we got the spicy salmon roll, my favorite by far! I really liked popping an entire piece in my mouth at a time and tasting seasoned fish, avocado, rice, and seaweed all at once. The flavors melded together so well and the salmon tasted super rich and buttery, in the good way. The Lion King roll came out last. It included baked salmon, the warmness of which was a good way to end the meal. It, like the entire meal, was quite tasty, but still could not surpass the spicy salmon roll in my eyes.

The servers were very attentive and handled the busyness with skill. Now I know of a good go-to sushi place near me, and will probably be back to chow in the future.

After moving back home from being away for four years I was missing my Eugene sushi spot. To my pleasant surprise I found a Berkeley equivalent. CU has a delicious Orgasm Salad that never fails to impress me. The variety of rolls make each visit new and exciting and with out a doubt and I always leave satisfied. The few times I've eaten there have consistently been delicious. The ambiance and snug seating isn't ideal but the sushi makes it worth it. I highly recommend the Lion King and Heart Attack rolls.
Okay sushi; definitely good for the price, but WTF they gave me tuna instead of salmon I swear...either that or that was the leanest, firmest, and reddest salmon I have ever eaten before.
The rolls here are pretty good and very cheap.

Don't be deterred by their 1/2 Price Sushi advertisements -- this place makes GREAT sushi and is definitely the best bang for your buck in off-campus dining.   I love stopping by here on my way home after a day at work on campus and am always greeted with a smile, prompt service, and (if coming in for dinner) a free bowl of edamame with every meal.

Typically I order their nigiri and have always been really happy with their salmon and yellowtail.  The meat is always fresh, their wasabe is well blended, and the rice is perfectly done.  Even better was the time I found a tough spot in my yellowtail and they gave me an extra two pieces for free!  What service!

Six pieces of nigiri and one of their excellent "Green Monster Rolls" (shrimp tempura roll with avocado on top) runs me just about $18.00.  With tip I'm spending a little over $20.  So if you've got Andrew Jackson in your pocket and you're looking for a great way to spend it on a healthy, delicious sushi meal, stop by CU Sushi and enjoy yourself.

And as they say, C U Soon at C U Sushi!

A very conveniently located spot (not that it really mattered to me as I discovered this place after finishing undergrad lol) with good sushi at decent prices.  The rolls are nicely presented and tasty, but I gotta default to Ernie F. for recs on specific ones as it's been a while since I've eaten here.  Thankfully, my memory isn't good enough to recall any obnoxious music to go along with the food XD
The pace is brisk. It was a busy tuesday night and our order came out in 2 minutes. Not a place to relax, but a very good place to eat.
Good food. A little pricey. Otherwise good atmosphere

They used to have 50% off the paper sushi menu that they give you to mark up. I stopped by the other day and was disappointed to find that they don't offer that deal anymore; only Nigiri.

Other than that, the sushi is of OK quality.

I had to go to Berkeley for some errands on Sunday and was looking for a cheap place for lunch near campus (and near BART as a plus).  CU is located on Center Street where there are several other restaurants.  There appears to be high turnover along this street since most of the places there had changed about 2-3 times since I went to Cal 7 years years ago.  Anyhow, the restaurant appeared to be fairly busy, which was a good sign.  I liked how they have outdoor tables (in the shade).  I always thought this row was a great location for restaurants since it's walkable from campus, along the way from BART to campus, and located right downtown.  But the restaurant biz is tough, I agree.

We walked in and sat ourselves at a table next to the window.  The inside had a modern look to it and was airy and clean.  The waitresses were Japanese and friendly.  The menu is pretty extensive and full of colorful pictures.  Lots and lots of pictures.  It was hard deciding what to order because there were so many choices.
