CU also has a special list of sushi that is 50% off.  Judging by the previous reviews, it looks like the 50% sale happens all the time and isn't really a "sale."  There's a minimum of 2 orders per person if you order off the list so you can't just get 1-2 orders as an add on if you are with someone else.

We decided to get 4 orders of sushi and 2 entrees - yes, I am a big eater.  I picked the unagi and avocado (this might be one of the few places that doesn't call it the rock and roll), California roll, scallop roll, and spicy tuna roll.  Each order came with 6 pieces and it was cheap.  Around $3 or less per order.  Taste-wise, they were ok.  The tuna roll had a generous portion of tuna which was nice.  Scallop roll was probably the worse of the three, but probably because it had a very mild taste to it.  The California roll tasted great - flavorful without being overly mayonnaise-y.  Unagi and avocado roll was my favorite, but then again, it always.  You really can't beat the price for a whole platter of sushi for around $10. 

For the entrees, we got the mushroom stir-fry ($8.95) and yaki udon with beef ($8.95).  Portions were decent, but I hated the sauce.  Unfortunately, both dishes had the same sauce, too!  The mushroom dish came with huge chunks of mushroom and veggies with a side of rice.  The yaki udon dish had lots of beef in it.  This place is not stingy with the ingredients, but I just didn't like the sauce...it was sort of a starchy tomato-y sweet and sour sauce.  

Overall, this is just a cheap place to come have American-ized sushi.  Looking around, a lot of people seemed to be ordering some sort of fried sushi roll.  Maybe I should have tried that.  Anyhow,  the food is fresh enough and service is good, but don't expect to be blown away.

The guy working was really sweet & the service very good here.  Just the quality of food is really lacking.  The sushi was suuuuuuper cheap, but it was kind of like Costco sushi... okay, better, but it verged between Costco and Tako sushi.  I probably won't be back.

There are a lot of roll choices here and all for reasonable prices.  My natural inclination is to order spicy rolls and both the 911 and the spicy tuna rolls were good, but not particularly spicy.  The nigiri sushi (hamachi, surf clam, tuna, salmon, tai, salmon) were adequate, and the fish wasn't bad nor was it outstanding.  This is a good place to satiate a sushi craving.

My boyfriend and I love this place. It is a small sushi joint with no more than 15 tables inside and  a few tables  outside. Service is always fast and friendly and the sushi is cheap and good quality. We have been here numerous times and definitely not even a quarter done with trying different items on their menu. 

There are two menus at CU. There is a list of 50% off sushi which includes a variety of nigiris and also simple maki rolls such as california rolls, salmon, avocado, shrimp and etc. It's great marketing because everyone comes in thinking OMG 50% So cheap! However, it's not really 50% because it is priced at what its worth, a little on the cheaper side but i definitely wouldn't order it if it was full price. 50% menu prices ranges from 3-5 dollars depending what you get. 

The other menu they have is extensive. It was like 6 pages of special rolls, combination boxes, noodles, some korean entree and etc. All of the items are pictured so this place is great for people trying sushi for the first time. Some of the things that i esepcially liked were the special california, the volcano, the spicy salmon, yaki udon and etc. Complimentary edamame too!! Yummmmm.

Always a great experience here! Definitely give it a try if you are in the area. :)

3.85 stars?

CU Sushi is by far one of my favorite sushi spots around campus. Good, quick service. Decent price, especially with their 50% off rolls. And always filling. It not your traditional sushi, they do warn you its fusion, but the fish/quality is not bad.

I usually get their sushi combo specials,with the Calamari Tempura Roll specifically. Its the most filling and never a disappointment. Its huge and tends to fall apart, but it always gets the job done!
 
A few of my favorites though,
Orgasm Salad - a for sure pleaser.
Heart Attack Roll - good amount of spice and gotta love all the crunch.
Palm Spring Roll - similar to getting Chirashi, but just a bit nicer: less rice, more bite?

3.5 stars for the cute modern decor.  This is a solid sushi place if you're on the west side of campus near shattuck.  Definitely better than the sushi house at the asian ghetto, tako sushi on telegraph, and joshuya's on dwight.

They have this 50% off thing if you order 2 orders of sushi or more per person for lunch and 3 orders per person for dinner...I don't think I've ever really taken advantage of it...because their rolls just look so much tastier and more interesting.

I've had their yummy crispy appetizer, which is tuna and some sauce on wonton skin, and it's pretty good.  The hot night roll (shrimp tempura, spicy tuna, onion), the baby lobster roll (california roll with baby lobster on top (freakin huge), and poke salad, which were all surprisingly good.

Definitely a lot better than anything they have near southside.  Prices are reasonable, and the portions are generous.

Pretty good lunch deals and service. I got the rainbow roll that comes with soup and something else.  I ordered without the miso because I don't like it. It's not the most fantastic sushi ever, but it's pretty good and it's priced well so I went for it and I was not disappointed.

Like the sushi rolls, but the other items on the menu aren't that great.
That said, whenever we feel like sushi rolls, this is the place we go to first.

I am no Chef Ramsay, but If I were, I would totally be in love with this place.  I have been to a number of sushi places, but C U Sushi seems to have the freshest and tastiest dishes.  Every time I attend C U Sushi, I can not leave without having the Monkey Ball... A must have when you visit.

CHEAP AND FRESH SUSHI!!!  $50 to feed 3 of us (we had about 15 different items which included rolls, nigiri, maki).  Everything was soooo fresh, presentation was beautiful and service was quick.  I love pretty looking sushi!

Pretty small sushi restaurant near campus. Clean looking, so that's a plus. It does get pretty crowded, so avoid dinner rush times if you want a seat :P 

I personally don't eat sushi, so my rating is based more on their non-sushi options. (However, my bf really likes their sushi, so I guess sushi lovers would enjoy this place more than I do) I've tried their Yaki Udon and Rice Bowls, both of which are kind of mediocre. There's nothing spectacular. 
However, I have to say i LOVE their sesame dressing on the salads. It's sooo good I even bought some home. I even came back the second time to buy more, but they skimped out on filling my container all the way, so I was a little irked :P 

The service overall is nice. Sometimes when it's too busy , you have a hard time getting their attention. They expect you to make a minimum purchase or so of like $7? I think that's unfair! 

Anyways, I only go here for the salad dressing now. Or if the bf wants to go.
Great food, very tasty, cheap!

This is my go to sushi place for lunch while I'm on campus. If you come in before 11:30 and after 1:00 you won't have to wait for any open tables as the place does get really busy during lunch. What I like is that the sushi is cheap compared to other sushi places and the food itself is good. The service is also wonderful - they are really attentive and very polite. 

My favorite part of this place is their cuckoo clock - it doesn't match the rest of the decor but it's a really nice clock. Look above the register if you haven't noticed it yet.
Not bad at all. The half price sushi is great. The service was good as well.
Tried the Baby Lobster Roll, filled with flavor and freshness for $13. This has to be a top sushi restaurant in Berkeley.Good Eats!

Is it really 50% off if it's ALWAYS 50% off? My answer? I dont care. It gets me every single time. "sweet, the sushi is 50% off. I'm getting a lot" 

They play random techno music in here at times but the food is not bad. The rolls have a good amount of fish and for the most part, it seems rather fresh to me. It's fast and hits the spot when I want sushi for less.

Their other non-sushi dishes are not so great. I had their yakisoba the other day to switch things up and what was given to me was a plate of noodles and meat in what seemed like a mix of sweet and sour sauce and soy sauce....Not a fan at all. I ended up ordering the usual sushi dishes and taking the noodles home to mix in more udon noodles. 

I say, stick to the sushi and rolls. I've heard about this orgasm salad but i just feel silly ordering it....it's like going to a bar and ordering a Cosmopolitan or a Prickly Pear. Nothing wrong with it, but it just feels weird.

It doesn't get better than half price sushi! It's like happy hour for sushi! I love the Soy Bean Paper Roll --deep fried unagi, tobiko, avocado wrapped in soy paper, too bad it's not in their half price menu.

Damn, where do I start. I have been a semi-regular at this establishment for quite some time but today's service was horrid and their overall quality was completely unacceptable. During lunch, I ordered a spicy sashimi salad while my friends had a typical set of varied rolls. I am not the type or complain out loud when it comes down to waiting around for my meal but 30 minutes after all my friends got their orders, I still had an empty plate in front of me.

I asked the waiter several times about my salad and they repeatedly replied with," its coming right out." I even noticed other patrons that ordered similar dishes in which they received on time. I got so hungry to the point where I had to leech off my friends' plates and the overall quality of the sashimi was just par and not worthwhile to give another try.

Too bad C U. You were good once.

3 words: spicy tuna salad.....omg, with or without rice you will love it. It is chunks of perfectly spicy tuna mixed with crisp, delish tomatoes over a bed of salad or salad and rice. Gotta love the no-carb option...is that even cool anymore?? 

4 stars b/c: 
super, duper affordable (1/2 off special everyone else mentioned). 
super duper fast 
they don't bother you if you linger around chatting after your done with your food even though they are a fast, cheap restaurant.

I think I've lowered my standards for sushi a lot after moving from SF to Berkeley. Berkeley knows Thai and Indian, SF knows sushi and Mexican. End of story. 

As for this place, pluses are that it's fast for take out and prices are cheap. Minus is that it's not very good sushi. It's not bad per se. But not very good. California roll, salmon roll, and some others are ok. The only one I'd steer clear of is spicy tuna.

We were starving after getting off to a late start and having a long commute to get to Berkeley. I appreciated the diversity of food selections on this particular strip. 

The restaurant was small and cozy. There was one employee seating customers, taking their orders, and delivering their food and drinks. And because it was lunchtime, the place was quickly filling up. Service was quite slow. It took awhile for the guy to take our order and deliver our drinks, but i almost couldn't blame him because he was the only one. He looked stressed.

They offered 50% off their nigiri. I ended up settling for a combo set which included a calamari roll and your choice of a Cali roll or spicy tuna roll. The calamari roll was good and the Cali roll was just okay.

Overall, okay lunch experience.

This is one of my favorite sushi restaurants in Berkeley!

Compared to Manpuku and Tako Sushi, the prices may be a bit more expensive, but I think the quality of the sushi and even size of the sushi is much better. They also have really good specials where you can essentially get 2 rolls for around $10! Service is great and I am a sucker for presentation - they plate the sushi so beautifully. I got one of the Orange Specials, which was a spicy tuna roll and a salmon tempura roll. The salmon tempura roll was pretty huge (in diameter) and even came with a size of some veggie tempura. Super cute. Each meal comes with a miso soup. 

My friends got the dinner bento boxes, which looked delicious as well! They were huge.

This is Morla's favorite Sushi in the area, and I tend to agree.

Fast, fresh, and a deep menu - casual but not chintzy, convenient but not gimmicky. Great for lunch or a relaxed dinner.  I actually had the curry udon noodles, and I was really happy with it.

UC Berkeley is busy and bustling, but head up Center after a days work or BART trip and relax at CU fusion. It's yummy enough to remember, and cost effective enough for multiple trips.  

Thumbs up.

Me and my friend have been here once (on separate occasions) and we have both gotten horrible horrible food poisoning resulting in vomiting out of mouth and nose. Oddly, we both got a fried roll and both of us got really sick. 

I usually have a stomach of steel and I can eat anything without any problems but... it must not be a coincidence if two people get food poisoning (after having been there ONCE) ordering a similar roll. So... perhaps maybe not get a fried roll if you want to eat here... 

me? NEVER again.

4 stars for food quality. I have never experienced bad sushi here, or even mediocre. It has always been very fresh with great texture. the nigiri is great, and the specialty rolls are delicious, and not too too much sauce, mayo, etc. the portions aren't skimpy either.

5 stars for service. The ladies are always on spot, friendly, kind, and quick!

5 stars for price. Collegiate wallet friendly for sushi.

I can only put my cents in about the nigiri, but every time I go, it's consistently great. They have a 50% off sushi menu, which means you get most fish (tuna, salmon, yellow tail) for about $1.80-$2.25 range. Service is great and you get free edmame and tea. What else do you need? I'm here every week!

Update (11/24): Since this summer, the prices have been slightly raised and the quality has gone slightly down (the tuna is strange sometimes, same with the yellow tail). It's still my choice for affordable sushi in Berkeley.

I love this place. Whenever I'm looking for a place to eat in Berkeley we always try to think of other places but somehow always end up here. I'm on Weight Watchers and I love coming here to treat myself...especially since sushi fits is very plan friendly. Half off nigiri all day every day...who can deny that? The Berkeley Roll, the H.O.T. Roll and the Tofu Steak are my three favorite menu items. Trust me, try this place and you won't be disappointed. Psst, the Walnut Creek location is also amazing.

I would say that this place is more like a 3.5, but I'll round down because We were seated right next to the door, and every time someone opened the door, I got a huge blast of cold air on one side :(
Anyway, on to the review.  For a party of 4, we ordered a bunch of salmon and tuna Nigiri, a super california roll, 49 roll, nabeyaki udon, chicken bento and salmon bento.
The Nigiri was realllly good, the fish was fresh and the texture was delightful.  It was also 50% off, which made it a good deal.
The rolls were ok, the super california roll was a California roll with some sashimi stuffed inside it as well.  It could be a bit big to pop the whole thing inside your mouth...  The 49 roll was interesting, because it was a California roll topped with salmon sashimi and very thin lemon slices.  I didn't care for the lemon slice, but overall it was ok.
The nabeyaki udon was pretty standard, tenpura shrimp and squash, mushrooms, onion, poached egg, seaweed... It was good. Not amazing.
The chicken teriyaki box came with salad, tenpura medley, and gyoza.  The chicken was pretty salty, and the tenpura wasn't especially crunchy, but overall decent.
The salmon box came with the same extras as the chicken box.  The salmon steak came just rolled, with no sauce.  The salmon was well cooked, but wished there was a sauce to go with it!
Overall, the food was average, but  I think the prices make this place worth another visit.  We paid under $100 for all that food, Which is a victory for us, since we usually spend over $100 at Japanese restaurants for dinner.

I was so hungry when I went there and I didn't even find the sushi there appealing. There was only me in the restaurant but they were still soooooo slow!! I felt that the sushi weren't fresh any more. Even if the sushi was 50% off, I didn't feel so good.

C U Sushi is good. The half price nigiri and roll all day long make the price really reasonable. It would be really hard to find the same quality sushi with lower price than CU. 

The worst part of the restaurant is that parking is really hard to find since it is right next to UC Berkeley.

This is my favorite sushi restaurant in Berkeley. My boyfriend and I come here almost every weekend. The sushi is not as cheap as Tako Sushi on Telegraph Ave, but it is definitely not expensive. The restaurant is always crowded every time I went there. 

One thing we order every time is the sashimi salad. The quality of the fish is really good. The salad tastes very refreshing. My favorite roll is the Tiger roll. We never tried the bento or noodles here, so I don't know if they are good as well.

Definitely recommend this place!

This is my FAVORITE sushi place near the Berkeley campus ever since I discovered it during my first year here. 

Prices used to be much cheaper with their 50% off rolls but during the past year, the prices have gone up. 

My all time favorite roll is the [Baked Salmon].  It's similar to Lion King but I just somehow don't like the LK roll as much.  The Baked Salmon melts in your mouth (drooling now -_-) 

I've been there too many times to recall individual visits.  A few things I recommend: 

[Tofu Steak] - as boring as it might sound to some people, it's SOOOO good. 
[Dynamite] - baked cheesy seafood combo goodness.
[Spicy Tuna] - loved the level of the spiciness. 
[Unagi avocado roll] 1/2 off !! 

Can't recall the different rolls that I liked, but DO TRY ALL OF THEM!

The service has generally been very good.  

Definitely recommend this :)

In my opinion, there are not many places in Berkeley to get quality sushi.  Even after numerous meals at C-U Sushi, I still cannot say I'm a fan.

Every time I grab sushi and/or japanese food, it's usually because I'm craving it, instead of thai, american, italian, etc...

My typical order at C-U Sushi is the Red Special with the Rainbow Roll.  I'm a big fan of sashimi, and C-U Sushi's fish is only okay.  Once again, I only come here when I'm craving sashimi, and C-U Sushi can satisfy my craving, only satisfactorily.  

The last two times I've been here, I got mild cases of food poisoning?  Maybe it wasn't "poisoning", but I didn't feel great afterwards.  I hope that their hygiene regimen hasn't gone downhill.

Yum, C U Sushi! I always come here multiple times with my friend over the course of summer. They have outdoor seating, which is great for warm, sunny days. The service is not too bad and the waitresses and waiters are very friendly. Sometimes it gets pretty packed in here, especially during lunch hours.  Two things I always order is the lion king roll and the eel roll, which is a special combination--- it comes with a warm bowl of miso soup and three different pieces of nigiri for a great price. I also love the fact that they have a 50% off menu! I always get the california rolls to come with it as well. My only cons is that the food takes a bit too long to come and the rolls fall apart quite easily. Other than that, I totally recommend this place!

The fish always tasted fresh at this place and it is much better than more expensive places around Berkeley.

With 50% off, it is one of the cheapest sushi place too.

Keep on going back because every time we try another one to see if there is anything better, we can't.

If you have a taste for some good, cheap sushi - this is the place to go. They have a half price sushi menu which is pretty extensive. I usually go for the Sashimi salad, Gyoza and a couple picks off the 1/2 priced menu. 

The restaurant itself is cute and on the smaller side. Since it's in such close proximity to the university, parking is always horrific. The background music is also kind of interesting - it's a mix of hip hop/pop...pretty random for a sushi restaurant. Overall I like CU. It's not the best sushi I've ever had but definitely good and worth the price.
I only come here for the Japanese seafood salad. The sushi rolls are okay, taste the same as Sushi House (Asian Ghetto).
Customer service pretty bad here. Foods are over-priced.

Great prices for all you broke college students that are craving sushi that isn't completely as bad as that place in Asian Ghetto.

Sushi is not the best (not the freshest I've tried) but they have great deals that come with rolls, sushi, miso soup, and tempura fro around 8-11 bucks. Rolls are a dollar or two cheaper than Joshu-ya on Dwight too. I tried the tempura green tea ice cream. 5 bucks but they give you two HUGE scoops of ice cream and the serving is pretty. My sushi craving was satisfied for the time being  :)

For the money, this place is great! The rolls can be a bit wee messy and they fall apart easily, but service is prompt (most of the times) and the bill never makes you frown.

During the nice weather months, it is great 'cause you can sit outside, and if you are a retired raver, or just a techno-lover, you will love this place... I am half expecting the server to bring us miso soup, sashimi and glow sticks to go with the music, he, he...

I think this place is between a 3 and 4. The sushi is pretty decent  to good. It's a little deceiving with their 1/2 off sushi because it doesn't include the special rolls. But i think their service is fairly good and sushi quality is pretty good too. The only thing is the place is very crammed. 

What I recommend: 
- Heart Attack (spicy)
- Rainbow
- Unagi

What I will try: 
- Orgasm salad (always wanted to try it to see how good it is).
This place is GREAT!!  I work close by and I love the 50% lunch prices they have.  The sushi is great and the variety is vast.  I give this place a great score and will keep coming back.

If you want great sushi rolls this is the place to go. Always consistent and always so good. The owner and the servers are incredibly nice. I'm always happy with the service here. 

I get the Crab Salad and Baby Lobster Roll ... if you want to try something different and incredibly yummy go for The Baby Lobster. Every time we order that, more than half of the people we sit next to always asks us what it is. Its California Roll on the bottom bottom with Baby Lobster, Mushroom, Onion, masago and then this creamy cheesy yummy goodness on top. Its the only way I can describe it. Its sooooo good mmMmmm!

Always loved coming here as an undergrad because it's cheap sushi and a gajillion times better than Tako Sushi in Southside Berkeley.  Their half off sushi rolls are such a steal!! I like this place because they wrap their sushi very nicely and their rice is the right consistency (not soggy not too undercooked).  I also love their udon and salads.  Their udon is better than Alameda Sushi House's instant udon.  They are always really friendly.  It's a bit small but I'd like to think of it as cozy.  There's always a fight for that prime spot for parking, but it's Downtown Berkeley and pedestrians rule the streets.

I very much enjoyed the sushi, and I'm kinda picky about it. The fish was fresh, the rolls were good, and the service was great. The place is pretty small, but there was a guy running around filling water and watching for anyone needing him. The wasabi was just the right amount of spicy, and I like that they don't have dyed ginger (bright pink). I've been looking for a sushi place here for a year, and I've found it.

I come here all the time for sushi- its my go to place! Take out is the way to go as it is usually crowded and the service can be a little slow. But nonetheless, the food always tastes fresh! Their big special rolls are only $9.99 for soup, tempura, CA/spicy tuna roll, and a fancy roll (may I suggest Orange Special #3).

Bottom line- I like this place! Its easy going, affordable, and delicious.

Cute, small place--very clean and service is good. Now that I'm vegan there's little I can eat here, but I still really like their tempura and tempura rolls, and anything with avocado--very fresh veggies, crispy, light tempura, and the prices aren't bad.

I love this place, I've been here like 4 times.

Before living in Berkeley, my friends and I use to drive to Berkeley just for C U Sushi.

The baby lobster roll is a MUST!!!

I've been here so many times in the last year. Man do they serve a lot of good food, let alone very good portions. 

 The last time I did go, it seems as if our blundering economic dilemma of high price has reached our sushi spot. In the form of smaller portions. 

I still like it though, good people, servers, food, tea, prompt service. 

Their Great, I would recommend this place to anyone who wants to try something new and isn't afraid to try Japanese food.

So go, try it.

Not necessarily not fresh but not necessarily fresh either. There isn't too much fish taste, but I like chewing on the texture of fish, so I come here because it is cheap.

Music:
Not that I do not enjoy hip hop, but it can get really annoying when they play it sort of louder than comfortable on a sunny afternoon. Some soft rock seems more suitable. 

Service:
Not bad, not excellent. Regular. They do serve your food pretty quickly.

So-so/Not-so-good Eats
- Bento box: It is a 2-star but its not overpriced. So whatever. The beef bento is not your typical beef teriyaki and not in a good way. Don't recommend getting it.

Don't Eats:
- Do not get the House Salad. Seriously, you will make a better salad at home. The dressing is nothing spectacular, very regular thick, sweet sauce with two slices of tomatoes. This salad is neither Japanese, American, or anything of any culture.

Other than that, feel free to try anything. All the simple fish rolls and fish in general are pretty bland but that wasabi and soy sauce helps a lot!

This place is really something. I went in expecting the usual fare...mediocre sushi in college territory. But boy was I wrong. I had the sake nigiri, super white tuna nigiri, california roll, special spicy salmon roll, and a few others. Everything was delicious. The fish was fresh and literally melted in my mouth. To top it all off, this place is super affordable! This will be my default go to spot for nigiri.

More like 3.5 stars.  This is a great place to go if you're looking for a place near campus to get some sushi with a group of friends.  Prices are very affordable and the food is pretty good.

They have a good selection of "cooked" sushi rolls here if you have friends who just can't do the real thing.  And for those of you who like real sushi, the quality here is better than any of the other sushi choices near downtown.

It's also got a prime location if you like to people watch as there is a lot of foot traffic on Center Street.  Service can be lacking though as it can get crowded.  They really should just hire more servers during busy times.

I ordered a tiger roll and I loved it, felt orgasm in my mouth.
the waiters/waitress were very kind and friendly.
I also ordered a yaki udon/chkn damn it was hella good.
cheap and good quality sushi. 
I'm coming back to this place again!!!!!
Good good sushi.:) love the fact that they are opened late on Sunday's:)

Cant beat the 1/2 off menu
Although as a broke college student I was mad when I had to order TWO just to get the 1/2 price! :O
But the sushi was good, fresh and made quickly
This is also where I go to get my green tea Ice cream fix even though it is pricey its all about location location.
Of course I'll be back

Love, love, love this place! I've been here tons of times (at least 20?) and each time the sushi is great. I usually go for the basic rolls (California, spicy tuna, etc.) and my bill is around 6-8 bucks. So cheap! I love its proximity to campus.

As for prices/quality, I find it comparable to Manpuku on College (I do like C U Sushi more because it has a cleanlier vibe). Tako Sushi just feels (and tastes) dirty, and Joshuya is way too overpriced. C U is the way to go. 

Some dishes I like are the yummy crispy appetizer (crunchy wonton skin topped with tuna/tomato), all of their salads, the seafood pasta, and of course, the rolls.

not bad at all for being on the strip from the bart station to cal.  i've seen many a restaurant fold on this stretch.  i came here with a friend at the beginning of summer.  the first thing the waitress said was "are you here for summer school?"  i was so flattered, but my friend was annoyed.  anyway, the edamame was nice and salty and i enjoyed the fried scallop roll.  good price too.

We came here for a late Sunday lunch. I ordered the spicy tuna dish with two mounds of rice. The spicy tuna cubes were mixed with tomato cubes to form an interesting mix. I would probably order this dish again but it is not spectacular in my humble opinion. We also ordered the steak tofu appetizer. The tofu seemed to be boiled then fried and seared to give it a fairly "meaty" taste. It was drizzled with a not too sweet soy based coating. I would definitely order this again. 
The other dish we ordered was the avocado tempura roll combo which was above average. We had to remind the waitress to bring the included miso soup. She was dingy but bless her heart I could tell she was trying.
I would like to come back and try some of their other rolls

2 words: food poisoning.

I had some kind of salmon roll that had raw and cooked fish, agedashi tofu, and a dragon or caterpillar roll, and it tasted okay... until it came back up. I had never truly experienced food poisoning until I ate here, and it was painful. Oh so painful.

I am usually willing to give places a second try, because the first time could have been a fluke, but the food here isn't worth it. Not when there are so many other options for sushi in the area.

I've eaten here a couple time already and have been satisfied with it.

Things I  like:
Fresh fish. The Super White Tuna is butter in my mouth. Hamachi, yum. Pretty much all the sushi is pretty good.

Things I don't like:
I don't know if anyone realizes, but the sauce that they use on their appetizers is the same for ALL the appetizers. Seriously! Tofu steak, Monkey balls, all the same sauce. Teriyaki? After a while, they both taste like the same thing.
Beef Curry Udon. Egh. (I make better beef curry.) It was a good size portion though.
Why don't they have REAL (asian style) soup spoons? Kinda hard to eat udon with a western spoon.
Service was good and the food came out in good time with good presentation.
Nice paintings and interior design.
Prices are great for the sushi, but not on the other stuff. A bit too high for that place.

I'll admit it: I really wanted to go to TGI Sushi's, but to my dismay, it's closed on Sundays. Then we just couldn't figure out where else to go for sushi, and we somehow found ourselves at CU Japanese Fusion Sushi. 

The food was pretty good. Their menus have pictures of virtually everything you can order, give or take a few of the typical things you'd normally order at a Japanese restaurant. I know I have a bad habit of ordering too much when going out for sushi (because I get greedy), so I limited myself to three rolls: 

1) Tuna roll: They were less than medium sized, but still pretty tasty. Tuna was nice and fresh.
2) Shrimp Killer: It had shrimp tempura inside, topped with shrimp. Also, note the cool name, which made me want to have it even more. It tasted good.
3) Tiger Roll: another roll with tempura inside, topped with eel, salmon, and a spicy sauce. Nice flavor. 

I went to this place with the folks, and they ended up ordering some tuna sashimi. They did this thing where they gave you some regular, nicely cut pieces, and then some big thin pieces (but more than enough AND it was still good). Another thing they ordered was the salmon steak entree ... I was picturing something spectacular, but it looked like some pretty small steaks served with miso soup, all on a whole lot of lettuce for the 12 dollar price. 

As for the service, the waitress was really nice and actually came around a couple of times to check on us, take away empty plates, and fill us up on more tea. It was pretty packed, so I guess this place is popular for the people who live around the area. 

Although I did enjoy what I ate, the reason that I gave the place three stars is because I didn't think they had too much variety in their sushi roll choices. A lot of it is some kind of fish on top of a California Roll, or some kind of deep fried California Roll. This is not the place if you're too big on CR's. And it absolutely drove me nuts that any roll that had tuna in it was only spicy tuna. I was looking for more of a fresh fish variety, but they had a lot of things that were baked, deep fried, or included cream cheese (*shudder*) and crab (*double shudder!*). You're better off waiting for TGI Sushi's to to open the next day (or not), but I suppose since it's called "Japanese Fusion" I should have expected all the crazy rolls that I didn't want to try.

Decent sushi for decent prices. I haven't tried much except for their nigiri and maki rolls, but so far so good. Their salads are a good size and very tasty with lots of ingredients. My boyfriend and I come here all of the time when we are walking from the Bart station. It's the perfect place to stop for a quick sushi bite.
for the price, the sushi is deeelish.  my sister and i always get the half price sushi so good :)  the tempura udon was pretty good as well... and the edamame!

This is without a doubt my favorite sushi restaurant around the Berkeley campus. Having said that, there isn't a lot of great Japanese restaurants within walkable distance. Don't go out of your way to come here. But if you're around Downtown Berkeley and would like to have some sushi, this is the place to go. What you can get here is fresh sashimi and Japanese entrées that will at least temporarily satisfy your cravings for sushi, hence the 4/5 stars. 

Whats keep me coming back here, though, is their awesome 50% off deal for selected hand rolls and nigiris. We're talking about $2-$4 full sized six piece rolls. They've figured out what students want: cheap and decent sized entrée that still taste good and fresh. Just a note though, special rolls do not fall under this 50% off menu (e.g. Lion King, Rainbow Roll, Ninja Roll...etc). And you have to order at least 2 orders from this menu for the deal to apply. But even doing that, you're only talking about $8 max for two full sized rolls.  

For two people, I usually order the following from the 50% off menu:

Salmon Skin Roll
Spicy Tuna Roll
Unagi-Avocado Roll

These are simple rolls, but they're prepared well in the sense that I can taste the freshness of the rice and materials put into making it. Try it and you'll know what I'm talking about. But if you're looking for something more than just hand rolls, they got that as well. There are two entrées I would recommend:

Orgasmic Salad and Seafood Pasta

Both dishes are priced around the $8-$10 dollar range. While they are expensive, they give you A LOT of seafood. Orgasmic salad (I know it sounds weird) is basically a combination of a insane amount of tuna sashimi, seaweed salad, onions, pieces of octopus, and lettuce. Once again, I emphasize that they give you A LOT of sashimi. So if you're into eating raw fish, then make sure to get this. The seafood pasta is just the pasta version of the salad. They add udon into the mixture. The sauce they put on it is tangy, sweet, and light, which doesn't overpower the raw fish in there. 

I always leave having to pay around $15 dollars per person though. At least I leave extremely full with some food to take home. Let this place quench your thirst for sushi!

Most of the time the service is very good - on a couple occasion it was a bit slow. The appetizers and sushi are very yummy.  Excellent sushi menu selection. 

My reason for the three stars rating - each entree we have ordered wasn't as yummy as the sushi.  Altho' we tried the tempura the other day and it was very good not oily or greasy.

I'm gonna give 2/5, my husband gives 3.  

Aww what happened, CU Sushi?  I used to love this place.  Tasty rolls, good service, affordable.

I went there for lunch today, even waited in front of their door for 10 minutes before they opened at 1130.  We weren't the only ones.  Two other parties were waiting too.

We got two Red specials which came with miso soup, 3 pieces or nigiri, and a choice of one of their special rolls.  For the special rolls we got the rainbowand spicy tuna tataki rolls.  We also got the hamachi roll and unagi roll from the 50% off menu.  Total price was $29 b4 tax/tip

The miso soup was a little on the salty side but fine.  I  can get over that.
The rainbow and spicy tuna tataki were pretty good
The salmon nigiri looked a little ... slicker than what I'm used too?  Had a funny feeling about that one.  My hungry stomach told my brain to be quiet and I tossed that puppy in my mouth anyway. 

My main issue is that after the meal I had strong icky yucky fishy aftertaste.  I'm guessing the fish was just not fresh?  I mean c'mon that's just gross.  First time in my sushi roll eating life I felt this way afterwards.

=*(  sadness.  Probably won't be back again.

Oh yeah  My husband had no major issues.

50% of maki and nigiri! Yum. 

I wasn't expecting that much when we came here for dinner. We ordered a bunch of nigiri and a couple of the maki rolls (salmon skin roll and unagi and avocado roll) off the 50% menu. 

The sushi came out relatively fast and neatly presented. The rolls were simple, but tasted good. The pieces of fish on the nigiri were generous and tasted fresh. 

Sushi dinner for two cost about $35 dollars.
I love coming here... They have a big variety of rolls. Spicy Tuna Tempura Roll  super Yummy =).

this place has gone wayyyy downhill since i first came 4 years ago with my dad during the big game. since everybody and their mom was either at the game or at a sports bar somewhere cheering on cal, the food was great! tasty, fresh, and under $30 for 2 ppl for lunch set, sashimi salad, and piping hot udon noodles. can't go wrong there. 

fast forward to 2010, and either my taste buds have become more sophisticated or this place has just deteriorated. i think it's the latter. it must be the economy or something, because even the salad lettuce they use is just crap green leaves, not the fancy schmancy organic salad mix that they used to have. i used to love getting their sashimi salad! bits of sashimi, salad mix, imitation crab meat, and avocado slices. YUM. now there's barely anything and the quality's definitely gone down the drain. their sushi is below par and looks like it's overstayed its welcome. 

btw i think the 50% off is just a marketing gimmick, the "discounted" prices seem to be the market rate to comparable japanese restaurants. 

cu sushi, what happened???

Ambiance: 4 stars
Food: 4 stars
Service: 4 stars

Well, I will not lie, this is a pretty good place to get sushi in the Berkeley area. It is not the freshest ever, but it is pretty good, especially for the price! Happy Hour (half-off) prices are valid all-day on nigiri -- the only thing I have eaten here. The service here is also very fast, they do not ignore customers and it is definitely easy to just have a quick meal here. I really have no complaints about my experiences here. It is conveniently located next to the Cal campus and not too far from the BART station. Not sure what else will beat this in the area.

Ultimate Salmon Roll is all you need.
tempura salmon on the inside, raw salmon on the outside. HEAVENLY.
chicken curry tasted watered down.
Very affordable and very fast sushi. I will definitely be back

OMGGGGGGG, me and my husband took a lot of medicine to prevent food poisoning or some other possible digestion issues. He ordered Rainbow and I ordered Philadelphia roll. The rolls weren't fresh and tasty at all. We were very disappointed by this place and the quality of the food. 
I'm not that picky in food, but common- there were little brown spots on avocado in my rolls - it means it was spoiled. All the raw fish was stiff. 
I can't believe they use this type of quality products.
MY FAVORITE SUSHI SPOT. The Berkeley Roll is my favorite. The Shrimp Killer is also very delicious. The Orgasm Salad to die for.

GREAT place if you're looking to satisfy a sudden onset sushi craving and happen to be in downtown Berkeley.  To be honest, I am rather orthodox with my orders and have largely stuck to the rolls (unagi, yellow tail, salmon) when visiting CU, but they have always been fresh, tasty, and exactly simple sushi rolls should be.  That said, the strength of CU is the service and the price.  If you're in a hurry, you can expect to get in and out within 15 minutes provided you don't visit between 12pm and 1pm when the UC Berkeley crowd hits.  As importantly, you can do so for under $8 if you're eating all by your lonely.  If you're in the market for an upscale sushi experience, this is probably not the place for you.  But if you want a quick bite to eat and have a penchant for fresh fish, CU is beckoning.

I like the "Heart Attack".  The price is reasonable, the wait is sometimes long, but the sushi is quite good.  

It's definitely better than Tako Sushi on Telegraph and Joshuya's.

The location is nice, too - right by downtown Berkeley and very close to BART.

I suppose I could begin and end my review by simply stating that CU has good sushi, prices and service. Then again, that would be boring. 

I went here the other day with a group of friends. We had just spent the day in the city and were hungry for sushi. Luckily, the lone Golden Bear in our group suggested that we head on over to CU. 

CU is exactly what you might expect of a college town sushi restaurant. It is relatively small and the layout can only be described as efficient. However all that is unimportant when compared to the quality and prices of the food. I know other people have mentioned it but the 50% off menu is pretty awesome. Seriously, where I come from, discounted sushi normally yields a trip to the emergency room with food poisoning. 

I ordered the spicy tuna tempura roll and some vegetable tempura (mmmm... fried things) and was very pleased with both. The tempura was made to order (a fact I learned the hard way when I bit into a piece of broccoli and almost gave myself third degree burns) and the tuna roll was very good as well (the fish was fresh and not overpowered by the sauce). My friends all enjoyed their food as well and the bill for four of us only came to $60 (before tip). 

In conclusion: CU Japanese Fusion is a great place for good, relatively inexpensive sushi. Also, the service was very friendly and efficient too.
really good sushi with a very fair price

I just  stop by this Japaness Restuarant to get dinner, because my wife and children are so hungry. 

First look - very moden and simple design, nice Chandelier, very clean,  and around 25 ~ 30 tables ,  they wore all yellow T shirts  looks nice.

Second Menu -  we ordered palm spring roll, shrimp killer, sushi,  and udon.   Their price are very reasonable but awsome deco dish, and taste was like A++ .  and very Nice service, no rush , we really enjoyed that dinner .

Third  check out -  We were surpised, this is opening event season now  , and they gave us 50% off  from their price,  My wife and I we looked at each other and laughed,  how could we expect this .  .. 

Yes, I definately enjoyed this, good to review them here.
Please visit them they are now  opening season..

Oh by the way I found they are Walnut Creek , new opening , not Berkley.

I have been in a long search for the best sushi place and so far this is the place I've found to be just that. Also mainly because of the PRICE. For their discount sushi rolls, they're still really good. One time me and the bf got TWENTY FOUR sushi pieces for only 14$. you seriously cannot beat that anywhere else. And also their speciality sushi rolls are super yummy. i love the calamari roll! omgosh and you have to try their orgasm salad, yes dont let the name scare you haha. its DELISH. has seaweed, house sauce, mixed greens, & seared tuna! sooo good, & fills you up! Hm, would've given 5 stars only if they had MORE seating, but i dont mind waiting for a table.

def come here also if you want really good, welcoming, & fast service. CU is thee best.

Came here for take out with my boyfriend.

Pros: 
-got our food to go and it was ready very quickly, which was good because we were in a rush
-got a lot of bang for our buck - rolls were a decent size, and no roll we bought was more than $3.95. 
-pretty tasty - I really liked the avocado and cucumber roll. 

Cons:
-although we got take out, I was there long enough to decide that I did not like the service at this place. Lady who helped us was not friendly or informative - for example, it's one of those 'check the box next to the roll you want on a slip' kind of ordering schemes, but the waitress handed us the slip with no pen and didn't explain what to do - I guess it should've seemed obvious but we thought it was just a menu. Perhaps just a miscommunication, but then when we handed her our slip she just had a bad attitude - not like, oh yeah sure i'll ring you up, but more like, "ugh, I do not want to be here." 

Conclusion: If you're working or at class in a nearby building and need decent, cheap sushi fast, then try this place. If you have a bit more time, I suggest going to Sushi Ko - prices are comparable and the service is *much* better.

I went here for the first time at the suggestion of my date.  Having just moved to the area, I was pleasantly surprised to open the menu to so many amazing options.  

In contrast to Mori Y. I LOVE spicy sushi especially when it has extra hot sauces on top, sometimes of the creamy variety.  They have a lot of really great combos for people who like spicy sushi as well as the spicy tempura combo. My date got the Orgasm salad which looked good.  We also got free edamame, and I ordered a roll of their 50% off menu which was a great way to fill up.  

I will definitely be back here to try more of their great combinations.

The shitake mushroom special is pretty good, just a little too salty. It made me thirsty all night. We also got a vegetable tempura roll and a vegetable roll, both decent. The miso soup was also way salty, and the edamame way overcooked. Still, we had a decent meal for a very decent price, about $26 for all that.

All these veggies must've been my detoxing for the dry and overcooked teriyaki burger I had this weekend...

I typically don't pick favorites. I can't even settle on a favorite color, so don't take me lightly when I say that CU is my favorite go-to restaurant for sushi. It's not only affordable (with a 50% off menu), but the food is scrumptious and the fish is fresh and delicious every time I go, early or late in the day. (I always order the yellow tail scallion roll, it's amazing!) 

The portions are also appropriate for what you pay for. Some of their rolls are huge and easily fall apart, but with practice the skill to eat neatly can be acquired (if my whiteboy bf can do it, then so can you)! And if you like to get your bang for your buck, I'd suggest one of their specials, definitely worthwhile. The restaurant itself is small and can get crowded during peak hours, but it's cozy and they have great service. They also have some outdoor seating, but since it's on Center St., right above the BART station, there's always a lot of foot traffic passing by. Don't get me wrong though, it's a great place to go if you're meeting a friend, parents, co-worker, or even a date since the setting is small and intimate.

My favorite dishes include: yellow tail scallion roll, salmon roll, spicy tuna roll (all three are on the 50% off menu and less than $4), spider roll, sashimi salad, tempura green tea ice cream 

PS if you go for dinner you get a free side of Edame, yum!

Good food for decent prices.  There are many varieties of sushi rolls, hot entrees, and salads.  The combination of ingredients in the salads are very creative and unconventional, but the soy sauce-like dressing has always disappointed me -- it's runny and overwhelms the delicate ingredients with saltiness; they should really switch over to some type of thicker sesame or ginger dressing.  The rolls are delicious and filling.  I recently had the tempura scallop roll and loved it.  Great bang for the buck.  Unpretentious service.

Great Prices! 50% off sushi when you order more than 2 x pieces. How cool is that? 

Not cool at all, really. In the end you are paying 1/2 the price for 1/4 of the quality of any random run of the mill sushi spot. Not only was the fish borderline unacceptable, but they were very clumsily made and fell apart. 

Don't sell yr dignity for their 50% off discount. If I'm every led to this place again, I'll definitely avoid the sushi.

I do have to give them props on the visual presentation of their food. Unlike the actual taste of their food, everything was tastefully crafted. It's nice to see a fast-casual place put some effort into catering to the second-most neglected sense in the act of eating.

Being a broke college student paying for my own education i enjoy cheap good eats! C U sushi is a cute and trendy sushi place. I of course ordered off the 50% off menu, i know its all a ploy , but it was cheap. I ordered the salmon roll and the unagi and avocado roll. Both were good and fairly priced, something like  $3 each, 6 pieces.

The prices are fairly moderate. The menu literally has endless selections. Having too many things to choose from should never be a bad thing but it certainly gave me a hard time picking what to eat.

The 5-piece nigiri special I ordered came with a California roll and miso soup. The fish on the nigiri is exceptionally fresh. I definitely recommend their sushi.

I still like coming here for lunch, but the last two times, my order has been messed up.  I like to order the lunch bento box, which includes shrimp and vegi tempura.  I specifically told the servers the last two times I was there that I do not eat shrimp, and that I wanted only vegi tempura.  Both times, I watched the servers write down my order, and both times I got shrimp tempura. After I pointed out the mistake, they refused to give me more vegi pieces, but were happy to take away my shrimp.  If they mess up my order, they should at least replace the food they mess up.

Such a great place for sushi lover. Especially for its low price on those sushi rolls. I can't believe I finished consuming 30 pieces of sushi in a meal. LoL~

Great for those UCB students study aroundby, its low price just doesn't match its great sushi quality.

I didn't expect much but the returning experience is exceptional. Definitely I will go there again soon.

The only bad thing around this area: parking.

I don't get to come here too often since I'm seldom in downtown Berkeley. Each time I've been is because a friend to go along for a Cal men's basketball game (it's my chance to show some Golden Bear alumni spirit), and we would eat here before or after. The sushi is quite good especially considering the price.  I definitely go more often given the chance.
Nothing memorable, sushi is sushi.
They have very creative sushi here. I had their 911 sushi and it was pretty good and spicy too. I mostly just ordered because it had avocado in it. The sushi didn't take that much to be made either.

Really nice sushi place ! Polite people and food is excellent, however, you easily order more than you can eat :)
Stick to the classic sushi - their American-deep-fry-things are... not for me :)

Had the Unagi Bowl.  It was pretty good, probably some of the better Japanese food within walking distance of the UC Berkeley campus.  The place was nicely appointed with CA Fusion restaurant type decor.  The only drawback is that it might be 20% too expensive, as the Unagi Bowl cost $10.
The sushi here was fabulous when I went here for lunch!  HUGE portions.  The 1/2 price was the best part.   I will come here again next time I am in town!

This is really my new favorite place to go when I am at school. I usually spend at least an hour here, savoring my food slowly (so I can fit more in my stomach) while reading, people watching and sipping on green tea. The service is really good and fast, the 1/2 off list is really a bargain and you can order nigiri/sashimi/maki individually. I like to pick and choose from that list on some days and on others I get the specials.
OMG, the specials. They are really fabulous. They have everything I would want (except for the seaweed salad which I order anyway but it's a hefty amount at 3.50). Check this: the specials I refer to are 9.95 and they include miso, a small selection of tempura veggies, 3 pieces of nigiri ~or~ spicy tuna/cali roll and your choice from about 6 different fancy rolls. I was there today and left so satisfied.
O, and the bathroom is spacious and clean too with agreeable soap.
The bathroom kinda puts me over the top and makes me wonder why I don't give them a 5...

I have such mixed feelings about C U Sushi. 

On one hand, I love their spicy tuna bowl. It's all sorts of yummy goodness for around $8. What a steal. The banana tempura ice cream dish also makes for a very satisfying dish.

On the other hand, I hate the service in this place. The waiters take forever to take your order and to collect the bill. The tea cups also sometimes taste of bleach. Not good. Oh, and how about that table for two, strategically placed right in front of the bathroom in the corner? Yeah.

So, three stars for the food...and minus two I guess for the mediocre service.

a-ok standard for sushi that is: well-priced, convenient to campus, made of good-quality ingredients.  the staff are friendly.  it's reasonable sushi, not special, not great, definitely fine for a near-campus solution to a sushi need.

best sushi in berkeley for the price i paid!
i mean it when i say it's the perfect place to eat a casual lunch with a friend; the atmosphere is cheery and bright while the service is great.

CU Sushi is becoming another one of my company's favorite. Not to mention my co-worker that's Japanese even stamps his seal of approval :).

So my co-workers and I recently decided to venture further out for our lunch breaks and we happen to come across CU Sushi. Strange name for a Japanese restaurant (I think - only because I'm Japanese myself), but obviously the name didn't stop us from having lunch.

So, what's my favorite you ask?

I actually became very fond of the 'Spicy Tuna Bowl'. Turns out this is my co-workers favorite too :). It comes in a rather biiiiiig bowl w/ a decent amount of tuna slices. It's pretty filling for lunch. . .yet my co-workers and I still dare to order from the 50% off sushi menu :p. 

They also have other entrees from udon, donburi's (rice bowls), lunch boxes (which I thought was just okay), and a big selection of sushi rolls to choose from, which looked really good. I might have to try some of those the next time I'm there :D.

CU again CU Sushi :).

The old man and I just ate there for the first time tonight.  It is definitely one of those "you get what you pay for" places.  The 50% off sushi is probably because it's not fresh and not thoughtfully prepared.  The menu was several pages long with lots of impressive looking pictures of specialty sushi rolls.  Way too many options on the menu...  We placed our order for seaweed salad, edamame, spicy tuna hand roll, salmon skin hand roll, Mexican roll, salmon nigiri and hamachi nigiri and they turned it around in less than 10 minutes.  Hmm...sushi might as well have been a microwaveable food at this place.  The spicy tuna was orange in color and very questionable...  The edamame overcooked.  The Mexican roll was avalanched with panko shavings.

They do seem to get quite a crowd (which is why we took a chance and tried it) and our poor waitress looked stressed.  There was a "Help Wanted" sign out front, so they are clearly short staffed. 

We decided it is one step above Party Sushi, only because the restaurant was clean and the sushi rice wasn't warm.  Head over to Joshu-ya on Dwight/Telegraph or spend the extra money and eat at Kirala/Kirala 2.

I was so looking forward to having sushi and they totally botched my order.  They need someone there who can speak and understand English taking the orders.  My dinner was ruined by their incompetence.

Definitely one of my favorite sushi joints in Berkeley! Beats Tako by a mile. Reasonably priced, fast service, and free edamame! The Orgasm Salad--a spring mix with seaweed, topped with seared tuna lathered in their special house dressing is the perfect melody of flavors and textures in your mouth. And yes, it really is orgasmic!!! The Baked Salmon Roll is also a nice treat for your taste buds! 

CU Sushi, C U soon!

I have been here a couple times, both for take out and dine in.  I think their sushi is good... mine has always been fresh.  

I was pleased to see Monkey Balls (fried mushrooms with crab meat)  on the menu!  They are sooo good!  Not  many places I have been to have them.  I liked theirs because they were smaller and easier to eat.

The prices are great, especially for the poor college students.  They have some specials.  I think it was the Yellow special, were you get a roll, 3 pieces of fish, vegetable tempura and miso soup for 10.95!  I think that was the best 'meal deal'.

THeir service is ok... Like others have said, they are slow.  I had to ask for tea refills after my cup was dry for awhile. 

Also, the environment is not the best for a date, or even a quiet dinner.  It is in the middle of a bunch of other restaurants, so people are always walking by.

I would definitely recommend this place for someone who want good sushi at a fair price!

Not a fan of the fish here.   Everything is super cheap, but the quality is really sub-par.  All of the fish tasted the same, like nothing!   Tasted like old watery fish, thawed and sitting for some time.  The hot dishes are also disappointing.  A friend ordered teriyaki and it was, frankly, gross -- dry and tough, and in little chunks like kung pao chicken, with an off-flavor.  Another friend ordered the Monkey Balls --some sort of deep fried roll concoction -- and those were passable.  Can't go wrong with deep fried, I suppose.
  
This might be a fine place for UC dormrats who don't drive and need a cheap little place for a fillup or a cozy cute spot for a dinner date, but if you're looking for good sushi and remarkable food, no.
  
BUT, the service here is friendly, you get a hot towel before dinner, and the restroom is very clean.
I mean, it's 50% off all the time, so it's actually pretty good considering....  You get what you pay for, and actually a bit more.

MMMM I ate here for my lunch break with a friend & was pleasantly surprised by the price. The rolls were ginormous & the 1/2 price menu was perfect  for my budget. I can't really afford to go out to eat too often but I can here. The quality was great & again the sushi was exceptional. The service was great too, fast & friendly : ) I highly recommend them for sushi if you are in the neighborhood

Came here for dinner on a Friday around 5:30.  All of the tables outside were full, but plenty of seating inside.  Ordered some udon curry, and a ton of nigiri and rolls.  Everything came out super quick, it reminded me of going to a Vietnamese place, ordering your pho, and getting it handed to you within seconds of placing your order.  

The waiters were quick to refill my water, and since we got our food so fast it was nice to be able to pick and choose on what to eat, instead of some places that give you one or two things at a time and by the time you get the last dish you kind of wished you still had a piece of the first roll to compare it to.

I wish I lived in this area, I'd eat here more often if I did.

I visited CU more frequently during the summer, when their business was slow and I've been getting a good quality food.

However, a few times I came back with my friends the quality of fish we got seemed worse than before. 

Too bad, I used to like their spicy albacore...
50% off is a very good deal, specially like the white tuna sushi, but they don't have toro and uni is not available all the time. And green tea ice cream is out when I visited at a Sunday night.

Great sushi, the atmosphere is lacking. 

I love the dragon roll, ultimate salmon roll, heart attack, etc. etc. I've never had a bad experience with their rolls. Yum! :D

It's pretty cold, the place isn't very cute, and in general I don't like hanging out there. But the food is good and the prices are good, too. 

I've been here multiple times and I always come back.

3.5 stars.  I again recently and the rolls weren't as great.  The caterpillar roll was filled with 98% crab with just a sliver of unagi.  Trying to be cheap, I don't know, but it's pretty hard to mess up a caterpillar roll.  I will continue to come here, mostly because other sushi restaurants I have been to in the area aren't as good.

I go to this place at least once a week even though I live a half hour walk away!
50% sushi (reasonable nigiri), huge selection of rolls, delicious and large portions of udon and curry, large lunch boxes, all kinds of beer, clean and classy, friendly service, great dessert!

It's not cheap, nor is it expensive. It is not the best sushi but I would say it is significantly better than average... and it's open late (until 10PM?)

I've been to CU a lot since it's been open. 

It's meticulously clean and the service is consistently good. 

Their dishes are especially creative by combining Japanese cuisine with more everyday flavors to bring out something that is delightfully good. 

My new fave is the orgasm salad. It has seared tuna and seaweed salad covered in a wonderful dressing. I would also recommend the Japanese pasta salad. It's a great and surprising fusion! It's a mixture of fresh greens, sashimi, and udon noodles!

I've been here twice for dinner and both times, the food was excellent!  I mean, 1/2 off sushi.  Where else can you find that?!  

The food is quick and the service staff is friendly, but the service might be a bit sluggish at times (such as water refills) when they're super busy.  Nevertheless, I still absolutely enjoy dining here. 

The outside patio seating is excellent for a warm summer night (rare in Berkeley).

Good place when you are craving weird "fusion" rolls that the better sushi restaurants refuse to make. You can get a lot of rolls for $15 dollars. No-frills, not the best fish but it's fresh, and I end up going here every 4-6 weeks. 3 stars for food, 4 stars for value and because when I am craving it, it always delivers.

edit: meh, i've been here a couple times and though it's always what I expect I give it three stars. my rolls fell apart last time i got take-out.

I have been trying to find a good sushi restaurant in Berkeley for awhile and this one had good prices and a lot of options.  I went with my boyfriend and we each got one of the meals that come with a roll and miso soup. The miso soup was pretty good and i really enjoyed my roll.  We were still a little hungry so we ordered another roll and walked away paying around $30 which isnt too bad for a sushi dinner. I would go back again.

- I will never order anything outside of the 50% menu because it's not really worth it.
- They don't skimp on ingredients 

Although the quality isn't that good... the price makes it the ideal place to go to when you want a cheap but decent sushi-fit.

I wasn't expecting such a nice experience here.  But they did a fairly good job. The price was reasonable compared to other restaurants along Center street.  They have some nice Americanized sushi ideas.  The large windows and cute Japanese decoration add some class to the ambience.  The waiter there was friendly.
  
This was our first time here.  We had Salmon sashimi and mini lobster dish with California roll.  I loved how they fried the lobster with mushroom.  The sauce was divine.  Their sashimi was cut into thick piece, which would be nicer if they were thinner.  But they were fresh and creamy. 

Their dishes were filling.  We were all really full in the end.  Lunch for two only cost $30 including tax and grat.

I will definitely come back.

Decent sushi for a reasonable price.  Who can say no to that?  The sign outside advertises, sushi, 50% off!  But the sign is always there.  Which begs the question - if you write the "original price," put a line through it, replace it with a number that is half as big as the original, and always charge the "sale" price . . . is it actually 50% off?

there are 14 duo tables inside the restaurants and a couple outside the restaurant. place cooled by overheading propellar fans. blackish decor cool and modern.  pretty quick service. by single server. rainbow roll came out within a minute. probably was either premade or was sitting around. nigiri came out in 10 minutes

entrees: nigiri: seared tuna (2.48) salmon (2.48) super white tuna (2.48) hamichi (2.75) special 1/2 if ordering more than 2 nigiri  rolls: rainbow (9.95)

rating: 3 1/2 stars  for value for what i ordered.

pros
-fish on nigiri pretty fresh but not the freshest i've tasted. good value.
-small amount of rice with nigiri
-checklist given to order from and server reconfirmed order.

cons
-fish on rainbow roll very thin and not so fresh. fish bland.
-rice in some instance not so soft.
-parking not good.
-rolls don't seem to be of extreme value. just market valued to overvalued.

server reminded me of someone in a korean tv drama but i couldn't remember which one.

Well, well, well... this place does the work. They have so many varieties, I had a difficult time focusing my eyes on a certain entree. Weird names too,, Heart Attack, Tiger Roll, lol what? But yes, definitely a recommendation if you enjoy eating Sushi. Don't get the New York Beef Steak or whatever it's called though, that thing is mean.

my favorite sushi restaurant in berkeley! it's a little out of the way on west side and definitely not as convenient as good ol' tako, but the quality is miles better. my usual order here is the red special with the spicy tuna tataki roll. fresh and cool with just the right kick of spicy. i've also tried the baby lobster roll, which was good, but too rich after a few bites and i was forced to take the rest home. i also really like the spicy tuna salad. basically, i'm a fan of anything spicy tuna haha 

the restaurant itself is pretty small so if you have a large group you may have to wait a while.

The portions were just right after I finished a McDonald's Premium Burger (mushroom&Swiss) an hr earlier. I ordered a salmon collar, which was real tasty - fatty the way I like it, and topped with the sweet teriyaki sauce. good stuff. 

Waitress was really friendly and gave me my hot water like I requested. +1 for accommodating my old-woman tendencies

I'm not gonna try and not go overboard but here it goes. In all honesty, poor service ruins my meal, and I think everyone can relate.

The place looked pleasant and clean and I was expecting quality service from a staf that only had 2 other customers at the time I was there (3:20-ish). 

I was handed the menu and the waitress returned to the register and talked amongst her co workers 2 or 3 others who had nothing to do. Now I understand its somewhat of a college town and a lot of business are run by kids/young adults, and lord knows I was one of them to talk with co workers during a slow point in the day but the lack of acknowedgment from the staff was really upsetting. 

*I had to walk up to the 3 wait staff members, interrupt their conversation (which they gave me a an off-put look) and give them my sushi order and told them I was in a rush. Whatever. I can deal with that.

*The waitress then came to my table and gave me a cup of ice. Okay? I guess water is introduced to the ice when my meal comes? Whatever I can wait for water. I AM kinda thirsty but I'm willing to wait.

*I receive my food but still no water. Okay I'm a little annoyed cause YES I am thirsty and it is my firm belief that water should be served WITH the menu. I look back and all the wait staff are in the kitchen talking and laughing. I'm really upset.

*Started eating/waiting for the waitstaff to come out but NO, they are STILL in the kitchen laughing and talking. I'm really thirsty from the soy sauce, and aggravated that I'm getting terrible service.

*I had to walk up to the register and wait for someone in the kitchen to notice me. "Oh more water?" No, you didn't give me water at all.

*I'm over half way through my meal before she comes out with the water. Sorry lady, but your customer service skills are absolutely terrible, and if I had no time constraints, I would have definitly wanted to speak to a manager. Service like that would/SHOULD get you fired. 

Thanks, but thats the last dime that restaurant is gonna get out of me and/or any of my friends unless I get a full refund and/or an apology from the owner (which in all honesty, I would prefer the latter).

My experience today at this restaurant INSPIRED me to really get back into YELPing.
I would go back.  I thought it was affordable and decent, although the service was a bit slow at lunch.

Great bang for the buck if you want Japanese food in Berkeley. 

I personally had the spicy tuna salad bowl and it was bomb! I could barely finish it, which I was really surprised with because Japanese restaurants usually give really small portions. 

Our friends had the rolls and they looked pretty good too, but I guess I have to come back for those. 

Solid place for Japanese. Relatively Cheap. Would come again.

5.20.2009

I wouldn't order sushi from here because it's a rip off (some, not all to be fair). They have a 50% off select sushi menu on the weekends, but what they really do is have the price be double the market price then cross it out and put a 50% discount on it, which is to say that it's the market price after the discount.

Additionally, while I was paying, I saw a tray of what looks like CA rolls sitting in the kitchen. Why was it pre-prepared? The rice would dry out.

I was disappointed with the grilled chicken with watered down curry alongside dried rice. The chicken was grilled in a massive batch then used for whatever was ordered. Teriyaki Chicken please. Sure no problem; let me spoon some teriyaki sauce on. I was surprised to see mushrooms in the curry along with the usual onions and pickled daikon. In my take out container, the curry was separated from the rice by foil which I found different since most places let the curry run into the rice.

I thought I overpaid for what I got.

Mediocre sushi. 

They have this marketing tactic, a menu with 50% off their rolls. The menu never changes. It reminds me of when you walk through Chinatown and every single stall has a SALE sign, every day, forever. It doesn't sell to me. 

The sushi rolls aren't bad, but I prefer Manpuku anyday.

Once I ordered the eel over rice and it didn't came until everyone (6 of us) was done with their dishes. To top it off, the eel was rubbery and disgusting. Nevertheless, I never came back.

I took my close friend Oz for her birthday, here because she only raves about it. We came for a monday lunch, and wow it was crowded. There was a slight wait for most, but we got right in. We ordered the california special with the spicy tuna. I also asked for the chicken with curry (damn no chicken katsu, my fave). Both were really good! We did order that half off deal they have at lunch but they never came. But since the other 2 plates were so good, they did me a favor, I could barely finish the curry rice because I was so full. If ur a single guy, its a great please find that book reading, quiet single girl out there, the place was jammed with them. Price was median range for sushi if not a lil lower. The service and food came out fast. Give it a try, might meet a girl or boy and get a great meal also. Thanks Oz!
Not bad. Came here a few times with friends and each time came away satisfied. Not the best sushi in the world, but it does get the job done.

Had lunch here the other day and I was quite impress with the experience. Having occupied the former Q-Cup Boba cafe, CU offered a unique food option to an rising popular 3rd food corridor in Berkeley (Telegraph/Durant and Shattuck/Vine being the other). Being that CU is a 'fusion' place, the decor is modern and the background music is techno (the audio level does not require ppl to shout to carry a conversation, but is enough make you wanna to whip out the glow stick and go wild if you choose).

For those who also eat with their eyes, the menu is well illustrated of the items they serve. And by-gosh the food they bring out looks exactly what is depicted. The 50% off sushi section is an affordable way to sample different items without braking the bank.

I ordered a Nabeyaki Udon and a Crab Roll. The roll was average but my Udon was excellent. The bater they used for the shrimp tempura made me recall fond memories of the noodle dishes I hard in Japan; in other words it was GOOD! I will definitely come here again for any tempura cravings.

Best Tasting and most affordable sushi house in the Bay! Recommend the baked salmon roll, baked green mussels, yellow-tail collar (when in stock) and both dragon and catterpillar rolls!!! Good service, even better prices, all cooked/made to order!!!!
Had the udon, lots of it and pretty good.

I've had a few rolls here. My favorite is anything with unagi and unagi sauce slathered all over :-P.   The tempura ice cream here is also really yummy!  

The entrees on the other hand are alright (like the Chicken bowl).  The udon is a sort of small, but it's not bad either.  If you're coming here, I recommend sticking wit the rolls!

I really like this place alot! The prices are good and I don't think that similar priced sushi restaurants offer the same quality. I live in Oakland but always make the drive to come have dinner or lunch. It's become a go to comfort place for my and my bff when we haven't seen each other in a while. 

Things that I always tend to get are: the baked green mussels, raw oysters, spicy tuna bowl, 911 roll,.. basically anything with spicy tuna. Love the tofu steak as well.

Even though I eat here quite a bit, my rating is based on selection for gluten-free eating and consistency of service around understanding my requests that the staff double check that everything I order is free of soy sauce, breading/tempura, egg, and mayonnaise. I do not always feel like the waiter or waitress actually heard or understood my request and I have had to either give up food to my dining partner or send things back several times. That happens less and less as I get used to the menu.

I have always enjoyed the food I can eat here and at a good price, but the selection is limited based on how much teriyaki and soy sauce (both of which have wheat) is poured on top of the rolls as well as how many rolls use tempura. 

I am unclear about if the tempura is wheat-free or not, because I can't have the egg used in it. Because the spicy tuna, salmon, etc is all mixed with mayonnaise, which has egg, another big portion of the menu is off limits too. 

I can get the Philly roll as part of the special and I recently found out that the Alaska roll is actually a chunk of crab, (rather than mixed with mayonnaise,) but other than that and a one or two other rolls, I stick to the nagiri and sashimi, which is always tasty and fresh.

a lot of creative sushi choices

gf and i got the Box A special, it consists of miso soup, salad, rice, gyoza, tempura, and your choice of beef, chicken teriyaki all for just $7.99...the preparation of the beef and chicken teriyaki isn't that great, it seems like a lot because of the way they cut up the food meh...

besides that great price for a lot of food, service was actually better than other sushi spots i've been too, very polite staff...

I've gone to this place twice now, initially at the recommendation of a friend.

The first time was with a medium sized party (6 people), and we ordered a fair amount of rolls, sushi, beer and sake.  The service was good, and they accommodated our party outside. We had a number of unique and specialty rolls. I enjoyed the spicer ones.  I don't recall the price, but I didn't feel robbed.

The second time was just my boyfriend & I.  The service was quick, but not overly friendly.  We got sashmi (HUGE portion), sushi and two rolls.  The price was ~$30.  The only disappointment was asking for cucumber Maki rolls.  We wanted cucumber wrapped in rice wrapped in seaweed.  Small rolls, usually come 6 at a time. Palate cleanser.  What we got was flipped such that it was a LOT of rice around seaweed around cucumber and a huge amount of cucumber.  It was far too filling and not really on the menu.

My husband and I love this place. We go at least once a week. We love sushi and we still haven't found another place that has a decent sushi for the same price.
We order always the same things, but we have tried a good part of the menu. Our favorites are  the eel special roll and the green monster roll. The also have some simpler rolls that are always half price. The teriyaki bowls are also good.
Service is always really friendly and the food comes really fast.

i like how cori put it - "cheap and decent." that's CU in a nutshell. beware that portions are large here. whenever i've ordered an appetizer and entree, i have to take some home. but i love the green monster roll and the spicy tuna and scallop roll. the yummy crispy is pretty good - their version of tuna tartare - but for some culinary reason i don't understand, they've added chopped tomatoes. don't ask me how tomatoes and fresh tuna with japanese spices go together. my friend liz v. loves their spicy tuna bowl, which i suspect is similar to the yummy crispy, but in bowl format. i go to CU for lunch when i'm in the mood for sushi and don't want to pay a lot. they have nice outdoor tables where you can people-watch. the sushi is respectable and won't break your bank.

Excellent little sushi place in Downtown Berkeley - cheap for students, without too much of a dropoff in quality. Most of the rolls are 50% off these days - specials, and the bowls of Udon are really high quality, much better than what you find in the Asian food court off Durant. Definitely worth the trek to that side of campus.

The sushi here isn't bad, but it's not fantastic either, hence the 3 stars. The half priced sushi is great! Well, for the price it was pretty good. The half prices apply to the more "simpler" rolls, like California roll, and spicy tuna. The prices for the more elaborate rolls were about the same prices you'd find at other sushi places. If you like spiciness, definitely try the Heart Attack! I also liked the Spicy Tuna Tempura Roll.
