This place is an okay place for groups, but I wouldn't suggest going with more than 5-6 people. I believe we had a group of 10-11 and we had to sit outside, good thing it wasn't a chilly night! Definitely stop by here if you're in Berkeley and craving sushi. I must try other places in the area, but I would choose to go here again if I didn't have time to locate another place to try. 

The service was friendly and nice. They were willing to rearrange their chairs and tables to accommodate our large group. And they even split the bill, so we didn't have to go through the hassle of figuring out how much each person owed. Which is nice, because it can be a pain to figure out, especially for such a big group. Saved us a lot of time!

After a terrible first experience I gave this place a second change, since it was right by my apartment. Boy did I regret it...The sushi is so sloppily put together it just falls apart and on top of it they got my order wrong. I guess when you order to go they really don't care what your meal tastes like since they include gianormous pieces of sushi that couldn't possibly fit into one person's mouth. I was severely disgusted and haven't eaten sushi since because of this place. If you like special rolls, don't eat here, no matter how tempting the pricing is. I honestly don't know why people eat here.

Its been up and down for me at CU. The price isnt bad. But some days ive had great sushi, others days it has been terrible. I love the orgasm salad, but at least once or twice the fish used has just been awful. Like it was left over. But i always go back because its close to where i live and i love sushi. Overall a good experience. Friendly service, clean.

The plainer sushi here, both the nigiri ( raw fish on top of rice) and maki (what you usually think of when someone says sushi), always seems to be half off. This putts the maki (I got a California roll, a Salmon roll, and a Scallop roll) at $3.25 a roll. It's not the best sushi ever, but for the price, it's pretty good. I found the Salmon and Scallop rolls a bit bland compared to the California roll, even with a decent amount of wasabi and soy sauce added to them.

The entree dishes, which have either rice or noodles as their base, are about $10, I think, and are pretty good. I remember getting the salmon dish and finding it flavorful enough, and it also came with a generous amount of salad so I found it to be enough food.

The miso soup, which costs $1.50 if you get it on its own (it comes with the entrees automatically), is decent.

Service here is attentive and professional, too.

Just to note: in the berkeley campus area, there arent that many options for good sushi. So yeah, it's not as good as lets say, GetA or Ichiro in Oakland but for the Berkeley student, this place isn't too bad. I actually like it better than Joshuya and definitely better than Tako.

The half priced rolls are really generous. Our table got the california roll, salmon roll, and salmon skin roll. The salmon roll was really generous with the salmon and the salmon skin roll was really big for what you pay (less than $4)

We also got:
- the spicy tuna bowl which was HUGE. Someone could have ordered that alone and would have been full and still take some leftovers home. 
-yaki udon plate with chicken which was pretty good but a little bit too saucy for my taste. I would have liked it a little more pan fried since the sauce was just really overpowering. i still liked it but maybe if I shared it like an appetizer instead of eating as a main course.  

Overall I was happy with the portions and the way the waiter showed a meal plan that ended up saving us a few dollars. 

I'll come back again. I mean, I'll CU there... heh heh ...

Delicious, inexpensive, and conveniently located near my office building in downtown Berkeley. What more could I ask for?

Worth the trip.

Without CU Susi Berkeley just wouldn't be Berkeley.  Whenever I crave some good inexpensive sushi or just can't figure out what to eat I turn to CU and they never disappoint.  Their baby lobster roll is decadent and oh so rich and tasty, and all the half price 'normal' rolls are a great yummy deal.  I keep on coming back!

Although they have cheap sushi here (50% off), I got one of the special rolls. YUMMY! The free edamame dish they give is a plus, too. This place has nice outdoor seating and is very student friendly..for a group or for one.

Seriously the best sushi place in the East Bay. Great sushi at affordable prices. It's like that place where you can go to lunch alone and feel great because you didn't spend too much money.

I took my college's Gay-Straight Alliance there and everyone had a great time.

Tasty sushi at a very affordable price.  This was my first time out to CU Japanese Fusion (aka CU Sushi).  The wait staff was amicable and prompt.  The sushi was very good and was at great prices too.  Their prices are comparable to Tako Sushi up on telegraph, but I think I'd give CU more praise as their facilities seemed cleaner, less cramped and the food is a tad better as well.

The yellowtail with scallions is delicious.  I also had the salmon roll and scallop roll.  The spicy tuna is good.  The california roll is okay, but I recommend something other than that one if you want to step outside the box.  You've come for sushi, not pre-cooked fake crab and cucumber and avacado.  Jeez.

If I ever want cheap sushi I'll be coming here.
Price, price, price...  The quality is alright, given the low price.  It's the cheapest place for Sushi that I can think of.  The soy bean is so good!

I love eating here!! My favorite thing to order is the orgasm salad!  The salad comes with a FRESH spring mix and many delicious pieces of sashimi!  I have no idea what the dressing is, but it's very light and fresh.  At times, however, it does tread on the oily side.  And, I also LOVE their playlist...the music is soothing and not too loud.  

The only sad part about this place is that they do not make lion king roll, which is probably my favorite roll.  Other than that, 5 stars!

I've always loved CU Sushi when I was a student at Cal, so when my fellow alumni and I came back for a Berkeley food tour, we absolutely needed to come back.

Now why the 3 stars? It's definitely not due to price or quality, because both are excellent (I can't get enough of their sashimi salad!); but due to their $7 minimum per person to dine there. I never had a problem with this when I was a student, and I'm relatively sure I've eaten there without hitting that minimum. This time, when my friends and I came here just to get a little snack of a few rolls and a sashimi salad, we were told about this rule. I wouldn't have a problem with this rule if the restaurant was busy, but there were only a few other tables seated with people. It could also be considered a good thing that we didn't hit the minimum because it speaks to how cheap the food costs. We decided to still get the food to-go because we do like their food, but it was still a bit of a downer for the day. The take home: the food is pretty good quality and definitely worth the price, but make sure you're going to be eating at least $7 worth of food each, which could be a whole lot of food since some rolls are less than $4.

This place is definitely on the low end of sushi places in Berkeley.   I frequent it because it is relatively cheap and the closest to work.  

The food is okay.  Decent but never great.  The 50% off rolls aren't a bad deal, but their gyoza is very disappointing.  Also, the fish:rice ratio in their rolls is pretty low as well.

The service is unattentive and sporadically poor.  I usually order take-out here, and there have been many times where they have forgotten to include part of my order and still charged me for it.  Usually it is just the miso soup, but one time they forgot to give me a whole salmon skin roll!  You have to be attentive dining in as well, because they have also forgotten to bring appetizers (usually the miso soup) and put it on the bill anyway.

The final nail in the coffin for me was finding out that a friend of mine got some rather bad food poisoning from here.  After hearing that, I'll walk the extra few blocks to Sushi Ko on Shattuck.

I always come here because of their 50% off all rolls deal! I've actually never ordered anything else besides their rolls. 

If you share with friends, it can fill you up! Each person has to order at least 2 rolls. And you guys can share everything.

Probably one of the best Japanese restaurants near the campus

I only get sushi here so i can't really comment on other menus but their rolls are great and reasonably priced

Each role ranges from $6 to $10 and I usually get two rolls which is enough to fill me up.

The restaurant is pretty small (can hold about 25 customers) so occasionally you might have to wait outside but the waiting is worth it.

They claim some of nigiri are 50% off but I think they are always 50% off so I wouldn't jump to get those nigiris

My cousin brought this back to her place for dinner.....and it was so good!

We had the cream cheese shrimp tempura, potstickers, edamame ( I didn't get to try that), CA roll, veggie tempura and this spicy tuna roll.  OH SO GREAT!

We only got 2 chopsticks and food for like 8 people so that sucked.

I went back in person this past weekend and had the Chicken Udon....I personally didn't like the seaweed so i plucked that out (funny I love eating sushi but no likey the seaweed in my soup) and added some ginger.  BOMB!

I also had a Killer Shrimp roll (shrimp inside and outside) SOO GOOD. Mmm i wish I could have some right now!

I'm a fan!

So I was just there earlier, and the food wasn't very good this time. The first time I went there with my sister the food was SUPER Good. This time the food tasted bland and yucky. I order my usual Miso Soup and for some odd reason it was SUPER salty. *Yuck*. I also ordered the fresh half shell oysters and it made me throw up. So as of now I'm a little iffy about returning. Maybe because it was 8pm, but that isn't an excuse to make me nasty food. They don't close until 10:30!! Maybe that is why they had so many rolls for 50% off, because their food sort of sucks, so that's their way to pull in the customers again. Sadly, they don't understand that, it they want to keep the customers, they need to make good food. 

I would say, go at your own risk. I feel like sh*** right now.
Like others have said it is not the best sushi but it is pretty good and a lot cheaper than most places.  They don't mind our kids and they are super friendly.
Best place for legit sushi on a budget. Love their specials and green tea tempura fried ice cream

Very respectable Sushi at great prices. My Berkeley friends were saying that the prices here are perpetually listed as "50% off" which is funny. Would recommend this as a good local go-to sushi spot that knows how to do the sushi roll!
CU Sushi is a great place to eat if you want quick service and fresh sushi! The employees there are so friendly and I love the outside area they have! I highly suggest this place.

Walked by on a visit to Berkeley.  Sat outdoors and had a very enjoyable meal.  It is an informal and cheerful place.  The food was pretty good and the price very reasonable.  A pleasant all-around experience between BART and campus.

First of all, I don't consider myself to be very food critical; if it tastes half decent, I usually won't complain. Ok, onto my story...

I was in Berkeley to pick something up and my girlfriend was hungry so we yelped the local sushi joints. C U Sushi was just around the corner so to save a drive, we walked right over and were seated immediately. Water took forever to get, isn't that the first thing that should be given to the customer? Ok, the water wasn't a huge deal, but after we finished looking at our menus, we had to wait a while before the waiter came back, even though the place was half empty. 

The food:
The tuna tasted funny, had sort of a metallic taste to it. The yellowtail was acceptable, but not the freshest tasting. The caviar was nasty, it was very sweet which tasted odd because i've never experienced that before at any sushi restaurant. The sushi rice on the nigiri didn't even stick together well, it fell apart when I touched it. Spider roll was okay, definitely tasted utterly average. the only noteworthy thing about this roll was that they gave huge pieces of soft-shell crab.

Overall, the prices were very reasonable, but you are basically getting what you pay for, cheap prices, cheap food. I have had better sushi at Safeway. Not a place that I would find myself eating at again any time soon.

Good enough.

Pre-cut sushi, but the prices are very reasonable, service was fantastic, and I've never seen a place put out food so fast. Good location near the campus.

We tried a platter of nigiri - including crazy generous ikura nigiri and very well priced uni.

If they only had Tofu Steak I'd eat here just for that! Nice, super clean environment, excellent customer service, fast, and all around great food! Only minus (and this is super picky, maybe), they don't use real crab. Otherwise, I love it!

This place is great and affordable.  I went with a party of 8, and while they don't take reservations, they were ready to accommodate our large group and were very friendly.  After taking our order, the food came out promptly.  We ordered a number of sushi rolls and udon.  While the portions were fairly small for the rolls, they were filling.  I would recommend the salmon rolls.  Per person was ~$10, a great price for a nice, sitdown meal.

Good, relatively inexpensive sushi. The quality might not be the best in town, but the flaw is more than compensated by prices (also quality is still pretty good).

 I would go back, especially if I can make it a little earlier than closing time. My main issue with this place in fact was that they were starting cleaning the place before closing and everything smelled like bleach, which made a bit more difficult enjoying the fish.....

If you're in the neighborhood and in the mood for sushi, and you don't want to drop more than $10 or so, you can do pretty well at this spot.

The sushi is decent, and the half-price sushi is a good bargain.

Service was ok -- not amazing, but definitely not bad. Depending on where you sit and how busy the place is, you may be waiting a while for your tea/bill/whatever.

The ambiance is a bit institutional, but for the price, this place is good for a quick bite. Definitely recommended for takeout; definitely NOT recommended for a relaxing dinner or date. Too small for a group.

This is the first Sushi place I've tried in Berkeley. I really liked it. I took advantage of their specials and got a roll and with three nigiri on the side. It's a great idea for a special, if you like nigiri. The fish was fresh, and my total bill was $16, which isn't bad for sushi. It is pretty small and crowded, but if you can find a seat, I highly recommend it. Bonus points for location, a great people watching area right next to the college.

Grabbed some dinner here tonight.  I'm not sure why they've called themselves a fusion restaurant.  The stuff on the menu is pretty straightforward Japanese food (Sushi, sashimi, speciality rolls, udon, rice plates, etc.).

We ordered an assortment of nigiri, rolls and a cold tofu appetizer.  Big thumbs up on the Unagi (warm, not too sweet and tender) and the Albacore (melt in your mouth).  Everything was delicious.  The rolls could have been packed a little more tightly. They fell apart too easily during the transfer from serving platter to soy/wasabi to mouth.

The space is small and cute.  There are tables inside to seat about ~50.  Tthey have 4 tables set up outside so you can take advantage of the delightful East Bay weather.  It's a nice and clean Japanese joint that rests comfortably in between expensive Kirala and questionably-cheap Party Sushi.  This place just opened in the past few weeks, so I think it'll get even better once it finds its groove.

The biggest surprise was the warm cloth provided to clean your hands with pre-meal.  The server brings a shallow dish with what looks like two medium-sized marshmallows on it.  I thought to myself, "Wow, what a nice little amuse bouche!"  Then, hot water is poured over them and VOILA! They expanded all sproingy-spring-crazy!

The high rating is only because this is one of the better sushi restaurants in the immediate campus area. The fish is fresh, the portions are fair and the prices are reasonable. Trust me, as a sashimi lover this place is a million times better than Tako Sushi on Telegraph and has better prices and portions than Joshu-ya. 

I'm not particularly fond of actual sushi rolls (y'know the ones with sauces and fancy names) so I can only vouch for the sashimi. I would also recommend their tempura udon and their chicken teriyaki - both are great!

Seriously, come here for the sashimi. It's better quality than Tako or Manpuku.

This is without a doubt the BEST sushi place in the East Bay. The ingredients are always FRESH. 

I highly recommend the baby lobster roll. YUMMY!!!!!!

Like many of the Japanese restaurants around here, this place is owned by Korean people. That's not to say the food is bad - it's good, and it's affordable, especially with the budget of a college student. Their crunchy rolls are nice, and the portions are pretty good too. But if you're looking for 'authentic' (and i mean AUTHENTIC) Japanese food, this isn't the place. Let's say it's a good Korean/American interpretation of Japanese cuisine. Though that said, they've recently opened another place in Walnut Creek - so that must mean people like it! :)

This place was okay. It wasn't out of the park or behind the dumpster throwing bad. It was literally average. I met up with one of my fellow sushi fanatic to try C U Sushi on Center. We both got the I think red special combo that came with 3 pieces of sashimi, miso, and a choice of sushi roll. I got the eel special roll and she got the rainbow roll and we shared half/half. It was just decent I really have nothing much to review :/ There was free edamame though! I can't comment on the freshness of the ingredients because it really did not tip one end to the other. I would say if you craved sushi, was close by, and have never tried this place to give it a go. Or else..skip.

I frequent CU Sushi a lot. I have regularly had good service and the food has always been good. 

I enjoy getting the Orange Specials (a tempura roll, choice of CA roll or Salmon roll, miso soup, and a little bit of tempura), it is very filling. 

I also like their Nabeyaki Udon on cold days, truly hits the spot. 

This restaurant can get busy, which is when I think service lacks. When it doesn't have a waitlist, the service is very good. 

My only complaint is that it is slightly expensive. I know of cheaper sushi places that are just as good, if not better.

Visitng from L.A., my friends took me to this place. Their dragon roll was delicious. Cucumber and CA rolls average, tempura above average. Not a bad place. What shocked me was their "orgasm salad". What people will do for shock value these days. BTW, I asked one of their servers, if this place is Korean-owned, answer is yes. Does this mean anything? Not really, as long as you enjoy their food. There's actually a lot of such restaurants around.

my rolls fell apart...which was kinda disheartening.  the beer was cool though (begins with a 'K').  staff is fairly nice.

the crunch scallop rolls are kinda bland...

The sushi was so cheap! My coworkers and I went over for lunch and ordered 6 rolls and the bill came out to be 7 bucks each! The sushi wasn't the best I've ever had, but definitely filled me up to satisfaction for lunch. They also have outside seating, which is a big plus in the nice Berkeley weather.

Like most people these days... "I heart SUSHI". But by no means am I an expert, I am just a HUGE fan and wish I could experience (& afford) more its deliciousness.  

CU Sushi is the place I go to when I want to stuff my face and not worry TOO much about price. Although I warn you, it IS pricey.. but not as pricey as other sushi places. If you want chheeaaappp sushi in Berkeley.. .look up 'Party Sushi' but I warn of the freshness of that place. Anyways, I like CU Sushi because the environment is relatively lax, service is decent, and the sushi is tasty! I am a big fan of unagi-anything and I think the unagi here is great. It's very rich and is very sweet. 

If you are new to sushi this is a good place because of the 1/2 price specials on simple sushi rolls. This way you can try different/new types of fish meats without burning a hole in your wallet. Experiment!! 

all the standard rolls (dragon, catepillar, ,etc etc) are delicious too. By no means are they the best but it definitely satisfies my sushi cravings (which are many and frequent). SOme of their rolls are difficult to eat because they are sliced so thinly that they fall apart for people who haven't used chopsticks all their lives.

I find CU Sushi to be "cute" and a standard for any sushi loving student. good for up to a medium sized bunch of friends (5-6 people) because this place is small, and therefore might be hard to find a table large enough within a reasonable waiting time. 

and please.. don't go for the california roll. i know it's a standard and tasty but there is so much more out there.
The sushi rolls are fresh. Uncomplicated and delicious. What more can a girl ask for!

Pretty good and not too pricy. Close walk from campus and BART so it's very convient to get to. 

I ordered the lion king roll and although it looked like a small portion, it is pretty filling given that I wasn't as hungry. It was pretty delicious. 

The place itself is pretty small so I can't imagine a large group of people coming here.

Would love to come back and try their other rolls :)

My favorite sushi joint in Berkeley.  The food is amazing, the prices are reasonable, and the waiters are very friendly. You should definitely try their sashimi salads -- the best I've had. Even better topped with udon noodles. Their teriyaki chicken is awesome too. For dessert, I definitely recommend their yummy green tea tempura ice cream.

Went here a few weeks ago and ended up hitting the sauce a little too hard that night that I forgot to write a review. Good thing the restaurant gave us coupons for $2 off our next visit bc when I found them in my wallet I remembered that not only did I like this place it was cheap!!!

So three of us ladies ate here and my ladies like to eat so we ordered:

Red Special with a Hot Night Roll and it comes with 3 pieces of sushi (Tuna, Salmon, Albacore) and miso soup.

Tuna Maki
Albacore Nigiri
Salmon Nigiri
2 more miso soups
one more speciality roll that I can not remember the name, but it had eel sauce and crunchies
2 large Sapporo
1 large Sake

Split three ways we paid about $15 a piece, super duper cheap! The sushi was yummy and I left full and tispy. I will def. return.

I go here a lot. Good sushi for pretty rootin' tootin' good prices. 
On west side of campus, its the sushi spot for sure. 
Outdoor seating on the sidewalk always makes for a great lunch or dinner too. 
Whenever friends come into town, I take them to CU!

Meh. That is my response to this place. It gets the job done and is ok. Their half of thing is kinda stupid cause 6 pieces of sushi, ex: california roll is generally about 3ish dollars. They say it is supposed to be $6 and they give u half off...stupid. Service is good...just kinda like whatever with this place

Got the "Orgasm Salad (or whatever it's called)" and it definitely did not live up to its name.  The lettuce leaves were soggy and the seared tuna was not fresh and tasted as if it was microwaved (I ended up picking at one piece and leaving the rest).  The only good parts of the salad was the marinated seaweed on top and the dressing.  I did try one of my friend's spicy tuna rolls and it tasted much better than my tuna so maybe their rolls are better.

The service was also inattentive and not friendly.  I had to ask the waiter to come and bring us water.  Bottom line, I'm pretty disinclined to come back and give it another try especially with so many other sushi options in the area that I know are solid.

I probably would've rated higher if yesterday's service wasn't so bad. And it really is too bad because their sushi was good for the price. Although I will be kind of a bitch and call them out on their "50% off" menu. Two pieces of salmon nigiri does not cost 5.95. You just don't see that anywhere else. So I guess taking 50% off 5.95 would make the two pieces of nigiri  3 bucks. Meh. Sounds like regular pricing to me. 

But anyway, my friends and I went to this place for sushi. The four of us all took our orders, in which the three of us received our rolls promptly. My other friend ordered a salad. She got excited for a sec when she saw the waiter walking out of the kitchen with a salad that looked very similar to her's, but was saddened when the salad went to the people sitting outside, who actually arrived later than we had. So we're like okay, maybe it'll just take a few more minutes. Ten minutes pass, she asks if her order is coming out, she's told that it's on its way. She asks a second time some time later, and again, she's told that it'll be out in a minute. 
I had a salmon roll, which was okay, and a few other nigiri rolls. 40 minutes go by, I'm actually kinda full at this point, and some of us are actually asking for a box to go. I looked at my friend's plate and realize she still has not gotten her food yet! Now I am usually very understanding when it comes to small discrepancies in service because I also used to be a server, but this is totally unacceptable. Food takes a little long to come out, sure...but COME ON, we're all done with our food here and her food still hasn't come out! I didn't think she wanted to let our server know that she wanted to cancel her order so I got up and told him. He tells me the salad is literally almost done, but come on, everyone's ready to go, she's not going to sit there and eat her salad by herself. 

Poor girl, she had to sit through an entire 40 minutes watching us eat, and then having to run to 7-11 for a hot dog afterward because she was starving so much! That's fucked up, man!

I don't know what happened, it's a salad. How do you screw that up?
We were given three $2 vouchers, but it's not likely we'll be returning...*sigh

We went to C U Sushi for lunch and it was really great.  

The edamame was served piping hot and really yummy.

My favorite was the Stacy Roll which had some spicy tuna on top with some Korean gochujang (spicy pepper paste).  The Green Monster was really good too with a shrimp tempura and avocados.  Someone in our group ordered the California Tempura Roll and it was my least favorite.  It was a deep fried California roll and it was just okay.  Plain California rolls were perfectly good...  no need to deep fry it!

The tempura udon only had 2 pieces of tempura in it - shrimp and kabocha squash.   It was on top of the udon so if you don't want these to get soggy, ask for the tempura on the side.

Service was good.  They were busy but handled the customers well.

Definitely will come back here when I'm in the area!

delicious sushi and its 50% off (but im not sure for how long). try the vegetable tempura. 

the chopsticks say, "CU soon" which i think is absolutely endearing.

Excellent Sesame salad dressing. The rolls had kind of a laid back attitude about them -- the nori was kind of all over the place and they were loosely put together. That's okay though; it made me feel like it was okay that i'd been wearing the same shirt for two days.

simple. fast. cheap. no, not previous men in my life - CU Sushi. Sometimes, all I want is a cucumber and avocado hand-roll or some inari, then I wanna leave and not feel bloated. I did just that for dinner tonight. Great rice, not too sweet. I loved my cucumber salad. The edamame was way over-cooked and mushy, but I LOVE the water-activated expanding towelette, very cool.
The tables were nice and clean and the bathroom was well-maintained. Great place for a quick meal and great service.

The Short:
My typical stop during my hectic days at UC Berkeley. Conveniently located near the Center St. Starbucks and the Bioscience-end of campus, C U Sushi offers quick eats that can be affordable (50% nigiri/maki menu). My only gripe would be the loud pop/electronic music they play; it makes eating for long periods of time a little bit unpleasant.
 
Recommendations:
- Vegetable Tempura Udon (ask for tempura on the side)
- Unagi-avocado Roll (6 pieces, $3.75)
- Yellowtail-scallion Roll (6 pieces, $3.75)

Pros:
+ 50% Nigiri/Maki menu
+ Friendly service that checks how you are doing frequently.
+ Entrees have a well-done fusion flavor.

Cons:
- Unpleasant soundtracks at an obnoxious level. (The worst was the trance-mix of Christmas classics during my most recent visit)

CU Sushi to me is like Howard Marshall is to Anna Nicole.  May not look like a whole lot on the outside but treats you to a damn fine time. Keeping in mind that it bills itself as a fusion restaurant, their food is good (esp spicy tuna rolls and tempura ice cream), and when you factor in how cheap their 50% rolls are, its practically like they're giving you inheritance/sex money.  

 If you call in your orders (like my house was doing on a bi-weekly basis), you can pick up in under 15 minutes. 

Especially in a college town where students like their things cheap and easy, its basically the ideal restaurant.  And for those of you who enjoy a little class with your classes, the eat-in atmosphere is cute and cozy.

I love sushi, but not when its grainy and falls apart in my mouth... gross. I guess there's a reason for them offering rolls half off. I tried this place about a month ago, then today for brunch. I figured they were having a bad day, every business has those ever now and again. This time I did not order a single item from the discount menu and the same result. 

I am use to freshness and quality, the location I usually patron is nothing but sensational. My favorite sushi spot has constant business, but so does this place or at least it seems. Maybe they do not buy fresh, I'm not sure but I do know I will not be returning.

I have eaten a lot of sushi...just not from a lot of different places.
From the handful of sushi places I've eaten this place is the best by far. To me it tastes extremely fresh and well put together. It's also really cheap!
I've had to pay three times more for sushi that wasn't half as good. 

I'm not proclaiming this place to be the best sushi in the world or anything, but to me it's really good.  
It's close by. It's tasty. The service is always spot on. 
Good stuff.

Cheap sushi and rolls and surprisingly, delicious.  I tried one of their unagi rolls and thought it was great. I am a fan of unagi rolls, but most places mess it up with too much sauce, but this place did it right.  Tuna and california roll were also good.  I wouldn't try the chicken bowl or beef bowl, too much teriyaki sauce.  Service was little slow, but overall they were very accommodating and friendly.

Recommended.

Bon Appetit

Probably a 3.5 now since they don't offer as many roll discounts as they did before, but every time I come here, I leave satisfied. So my 4 stars still stand. Would still recommend this place to others, just not as enthusiastically as I might once have. 

I just came here a few hours ago. Ordered the salmon tempura roll (I recommend!) and the tempura udon, with the tempura on the side. They failed with the tempura on the side today, but the waiter remembered just as he put the udon down. He looked terribly apologetic and offered to fix it immediately, but it really wasn't that big of deal and he was super nice about it. 

CU Sushi has my favorite texture of udon noodles--super chewy yumminess of just the right thickness. My mom says the broth is pretty bland, but if its just about their noodles, this place has gotten it down. 

Love the tea, as always. 
Dinner comes with edamame!

I usually rate restaurants based off of their food, service generally doesn't play a major role in my ratings.  However, my last visit at CU Sushi ended up in pure frustration.  My biggest complaint is this new $10 minimum for credit and debit cards (which is posted towards the back of the store near the kitchen so if you eat outside you don't even see it).  I understand what they are trying to do and why, but a $10 minimum at lunch time with half off rolls and lunch rates forces you to buy more food or drink then you need or want.  My bill came to $9.73, I was 27 cents away from hitting the $10 mark and the server actually had the nerve to tell me that next time I have to spend at least $10!  If you restaurant can't afford the fees for credit and debit use, then become cash only or just raise all you prices, don't single out those who use credit or debit.  I personally think this is greed and has nothing to do with the owner being able to afford the fees, with Cal, Shattuck ave and Berkeley Community College next door the restaurant it is always busy.  Finally, tell you servers that they should wash their hands after they clean tables and pick up dirty plates, before they deliver the food to new patrons or hire a busser!

The servers are complete space cadets but the food is pretty good. The Chicken Udon was filling and the broth was good although I was hoping for more vegetables.  The unagi nigiri was fresh and the monkey balls were apparently delicious. Not a bad place to grab a quick and casual lunch or dinner by campus.
Cheap sushi located near the UC Berkeley campus. Can be busy during the lunch hour, it is a smaller place. My standard is the California Roll, which is just ok here.

This sushi restaurant is very close to campus. Prices are decent for college students. They have a 50% off menu on nigiri, basic maki, and sashimi. Three different sushi specials with miso soup, a fancy roll of your choice, and nigiri for about $11. 

The quality is pretty consistent. Raw fishes are pretty fresh, I don't have a bad stomach ache after like I would at Tako. Sizes are ok. I usually order sake, tai, hamachi, and shiro maguro. Sometimes I'll order uni and amaebi. Sake nigiri are at good value. Don't ever get green salmon nigiri though. It's just a slice of avocado slapped onto the salmon and you pay like 50 cents extra for that. Uni and amaebi are kind of small in my opinion. Amaebi orders do come with fried lobster heads, so it's not a bad deal I guess. I'm just not a fan of chewing that. Their sushi rice is ok at times, when the whole piece stays together and not fall apart when I dip it into my soy sauce. Sometimes the rice is too vinegary and took the spotlight of the fish topping. Star off for that

I've tried their nabeyaki udon and their tempura udon. I don't really get why I'm paying an extra dollar for a hot stone bowl. I swear I get like the same ingredients in my udon soup! Curry udon with chicken is pretty good too, if you like non soupy noodles. 

Service is ok. Sometimes they get so busy that I feel like I'm being ignored. Or I'm being rushed. Like many other restaurants in Berkeley, they do have a minimum on credit cards, $8 minimum.

3 stars for average. If I can do half stars, C U is more like 3.5, better than average. Good deals. Close to campus. I come often mainly for convenience and cravings. College budget, can't pay for fancy stuff.

I don't really know why I'm even giving them two stars. 
The food was eh -- my roll was drenched in sauce (as are most of the rolls, it seems) and it just tasted fake.  The nigiri I got (yellow tail / hamachi) was very rubbery and fishy tasting, I couldn't even eat both pieces.  And the service was awful.

My boyfriend and I came here for the half off sushi deals, but it was pretty basic, so we ended up going with their $11 plate specials--miso, a gourmet-ish roll, and sashimi. 

The sushi was really good, but the service was pretty terrible. We had to get up to ask for more water and the bill. Our water didn't come until the food did, and it didn't seem especially busy. We didn't come with huge expectations, so it really wasn't a big deal, but this place is VERY casual, so don't bring huge expectations, and you'll love it!

I dropped a Hamilton for a spicy tuna salad bowl thing.

I CU and your game, Japanese Fusion restaurant.  You try to use your "half-off" wordplay to suggest that your sushi is a really good deal when, as a point of fact, it really just costs what it should.  Well, you've never crossed vowels with me before, and I'm quite PUNishing when it comes to linguistic challenges, so please lay down your "half-off" declarations.

Anyway, my lunch was fine, if a little bit over-priced.  I like to come here when I come to campus from Center St. by foot on a weekend, or occasionally just to change up my "meh" sushi routine.  However, other than that, it's just as forgettable as any other sushi place in Berkeley whose name I can't currently recall.

You can walk-in and order things to go.  It takes about ten minutes.  That's a little bit cool for a minute.

Good selection of inexpensive, decent sushi. They have 50% off nigiri and another menu selection of small-ish, simple rolls (6 pieces) for $3-$4 which is good if you wanna get full quickly for cheap. The last time I was there, we got the crab, salmon, spicy tuna, scallop and yellowtail rolls. We also got 2 maki rolls - the philadelphia and ultimate salmon and together everything was $46.. not bad at all! The ultimate salmon is probably my new favorite roll - baked salmon on the inside, fresh salmon on the outside. It was huge and delicious!

Service is spotty, but I think it's because they don't have enough servers during rush hour. I had one bad experience in which we had a party of 4, which is difficult because most of their tables are for 2. Instead of seating the party of 2 that came after us at a table against the wall, they were seated adjacent to another table for 2 that was about to leave. We asked the server if they could be seated at a corner table for 2 so that we could push the other tables together to seat 4, but he refused, which was annoying. Luckily, the party of 2 voluntarily relocated themselves to the corner table so we could push the other tables together and be seated FINALLY (after +30 min wait). It was sad that their guests had more sense than their servers though.

This place is A-Ok for sure.

Another great cheap sushi option, plus it's on a really cute street and you can sit outside on a nice day. If you are in a hurry, they seem to turn over tables really fast. 

My favorite role is the spicy salmon special role, it's like 8 bucks and filled with salmon and avocado on the inside and out, and has about eight pieces. Another good deal and you only need one to fill you up. Their hot sake isn't as cheap as Itchiban though...so if I feel like having a drink, I head over there ($3for a large sake vs. $6 for a large at CU).

This is not a great place to go if you are a sushi purist.  But if you like to try new things, CU Sushi has a very good and interesting assortment of rolls to try.  The service there is excellent, and the sushi is delicious.
this is my favorite sushi place near campus.  i've tried tako and joshuya and the place in asian ghetto, and  CU is better in both price, atmosphere and most importantly, quality!

My first bad review.

I pop into this place for lunch, mostly.  And, I went in recently for a takeout order of udon noodles just before the lunch rush. 

It was incredibly cold out (by Berkeley standards), so instead of waiting for my order outside, which I gather is their preference,  I took a seat in the corner and waited for my udon. I mean, I paid for my food AND tipped. I don't see why they couldn't just let me rest for a moment while I waited for my noodles. But, alas, they made me move. 

I was flabbergasted. "These seats are for people dining in" Wow! I just tipped you. 

I complained to the poor kid, who obviously didn't have the discretion to exercise  judgement, but it was such a classless move. I acquiesced without much protest, and they moved me near the bathroom to wait for my food. 

In the kid's defense, he did apologize and the place DID fill up as I was leaving, but it was just a bad call. I feel the service there is too boorish in general. 

They are not a 2-star establishment, but they deserve to have their aggregate rating impacted. After all, there were other seats in the place and my udon noodles do not take that long to prepare, so there was no real opportunity cost. 

Bottom line: No one likes getting the bum's rush. 

I tipped you on a to-go order, don't rouse me from my seat. I don't need that.

I love more traditional rolls, and considering all the more traditional sushi is 1/2 off here, I'm in heaven!!!  The more inventive rolls are super as well, and the lunch combos give you the right amount of sushi for the right price!! I make it here at least three times a month.  The only down-side is the restaurant itself is surrounded by like 5 other restaurants (if not more) and I think it gets lost in the commotion.  I didn't know this place existed until my husband took me there, and it never seems too crowded.  Anyway, great food, great price, and something for everyone!

I love CU!

I usually don't go for quantity over quality, but I've made an exception for CU since the quality is still pretty good. I've been here at least a dozen times.

When I first tried sushi, I would only go for the special rolls. After converting to raw fish, it's hard for me to go back. That said, it's nice to have a sushi restaurant with a bunch of cheap and fresh regular rolls (they're usually half off). My usual order is the Orgasm Salad (becomes less awkward every subsequent time you order it) with a salmon roll on the side. I've tried some of their cooked rolls and I think I like the Lion King best out of them all. They seem to have pretty good deals on their specials, but I've never tried them.

Some of my friends are pretty cheap, so it's always been hard for me to find a good place for us to go to for a low price. I brought a group of them here a few days ago and they all seemed to enjoy their food without complaining about the price.

Why not the five stars? The sushi is good, but not amazing. I also don't like how we have to specifically ask for tea with our water. The tables are pretty small, so sometimes they have to play Tetris with my plates, combine my dishes in front of me, or even ask if they can move me after I've been situated. Lastly, they tend to bring out one dish early on and wait a while to bring out your next plate (ex. the appetizers may come out halfway through your entree).

For a place I've passed for the past two years on my way home from work with genuine curiosity because of the amount of people eating here, the sushi was just ok. Maybe I'm just spoiled by all the really good sushi places in the bay.. The rice was too crumbly and the Unagi roll that I ordered had cold unagi on top. Wouldn't return if I had the choice to. Feel kinda bad for giving them such a low rating because they've got friendly staff but I'm not gonna fake the funk.

I have actually been to this place many times, since it's really close to BART, the bus stop mecca, and campus. And for being a frequent patron, i say it's okay.

The service is pretty good - they're nice and try to be quick with serving your food. The same people are usually there and i think they don't have the capacity to be rude, so expect good service.

As for the food itself, I'm not a giant fan of fusion. I like tasting authenticity, but with sushi I don't mind trying something new. Their menu has some out of the box rolls and some standards of a sushi restaurant. Most are usually drawn to the cheaper nigiris and such, but I like trying full on rolls. And here is the main compliant i have with this place...

The rolls are too big. 

Not like too long, but too big - too much girth. hehe...girth. anyway, I usually order the spider roll, and taste-wise it's fine, but when i pick up a piece its pretty huge. I believe they expect you to eat each piece in two bites, but the roll isn't rolled up tightly enough which results in just a big fat mess. Or, a deconstructed sushi (top chef anyone?), which I don't think was intended.

If you're very savvy with chopsticks, maybe you can cope. I'd give it 3.5 stars if i could, but yelp laws say i cannot.

3 stars!!!

Great place to drop by and try.  If you don't like the quality of the nigiri there's probably nothing we can do to change your mind...but to me I think that it's perfectly fine!  In fact, for the price I think it's great!  I uploaded a pic of the nigiri menu and everything else can be seen here -- http://cusushi.com/

The price isn't necessarily THAAAT cheap because they probably increase some of the prices before giving that amazing 50% off :)  My favorite nigiri there (in order) is the White Tuna, Seared Albacore, Tuna, and Salmon.  The seared tuna is so-so.  

Some other items to try are the yakitori udon (dry) and the baby-lobster roll (I don't know what meat it really is...but it's a bad dish.  Make sure to share it with some others tho because it's pretty rich.  The normal udon (in soup) isn't good though because it's too sweet.

I wouldn't mind stopping by once in a while :)

I eat her a lot (and am a generous tipper), but the other day I just wanted a snack (tofu steak and rice) and I got a stern lecture from the waitress that "she would let it go this time" but I needed to spend more money to eat there in the future.  The place was almost empty as it was about 4 pm so I don't know what the big deal was.  It also seems like there is a big turn around in serving staff, so no one knows you when you walk in.  I'll think again before going alone or bringing guests.  I felt very uncomfortable with the whole experience.

Today was my last day in the Bay Area before going to college, so I went with my boyfriend to get some good Bay Area sushi. (Socal sushi has nothing on ours. Just saying.)

We walked in and were greeted by a pretty young-looking waitress. She directed us to our table and left a pencil and a sheet of paper with the 50%-off sushi. Being cheap college kids we checked it out, but it turns out only the "plain" rolls (California, Philly, etc.) were the ones eligible for the discount. Boo. We didn't know that we were supposed to write our orders on it, but the girl was nice about it, haha.

I ended up ordering the Berkeley Roll: cream cheese, avocado, crab and fresh fish, all deep fried. He ordered the spicy salmon roll (fresh salmon, avocado and spicy salmon on top) and the salmon sashimi. He really likes his salmon, apparently.

His salmon sashimi came in and I tried it. It tasted pretty fresh, I liked it. This is coming from someone who doesn't really like sashimi. His spicy salmon roll came in after. Didn't try it but he seemed to like it.

My Berkeley Roll was amazing. There were only about five pieces but they were humongous--it was difficult to pick them up, and while eating it sometimes fell apart. It was pretty good though.

I'm not sure why there are reviews complaining about the service, I had a pretty good experience here. Our waitress was really nice and the rest of the staff were good with keeping our drinks filled/taking our plates. They asked before they took them away, and when we were paying for our meal the chick asked if we wanted coupons. :)

$30 for sashimi and two special rolls. Not bad. Coming back!

Perfect for my sushi craving, affordable, good, and quick. We pick up sushi there all the time. The teriyaki bowls are good with large portions, the miso soup is excellent (for my taste, people have different preferences on how they like their miso). I usually always get a caterpillar roll or dragon roll and it's always delicious. The waitresses are nice, the atmosphere is nice, though they do play an odd variety of music, pop and then randomly country? 

The restaurant is a little small though because it's usually pretty crowded, and they definitely need to get gift certificates. Overall, good sushi for a good price, definitely cheaper then Joshuya's.

You're not supposed to judge a book by its cover, but I was bad.  I'd already judged CU by the time we were seated with our menus, menus screaming with obnoxious "trendy!" font in "fun!", "bold!", "exciting!" colors and sprinkled with some even trendier!! weirdo rolls.  The word "Fusion" also set off warning bells in my head.  Yuh-oh, I told myself, here we go again to another mediocre Americanized sushi place.

So I tried to salvage the situation by staying faaaar away from rolls and ordered the vegetable tempura udon.

Hooooooooooooooooooooooooo--OOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO OOOOOOOO--ly.  No doubt the reaction was in part from my judgy-judge low expectations, but that $7 bowl of udon was frikkin AMAZING.  The broth was light yet flavorful enough to counter the thick noodles, which were slightly translucent on the outermost layer and had a powerful, addictive chew unlike any other udon I've had.  Tempura batter was spot-on (and they accidentally gave me a shrimp, HEE I WIN!)  

Halfway through the deceptively-shaped bowl, I declared myself full.  And then proceeded to inhale udon until there was nothing left.

I do humbly apologize for being so judgy.  I'd go back in a heartbeat!  :)

c u at CU!

Ok, that was lame. But this place surely isn't. This place is priced like any other sushi place we're used to, but in my opinion they put more thought and preparation into their dishes than others. I had the baked salmon roll with cream cheese wrapped in the sushi. I used to hate having cream cheese in rolls because they are just too overpowering in taste. At C U, the grilled roll softens the smaller than usual chunk of cream cheese a bit, so when you bite into it (or stuff your face like I do), the cream cheese spreads around and blends with the rest of the ingredients surprisingly well. The rich cream cheese is like the cherry on top; it completes the baked salmon roll in a way by adding an extra layer of flavor. 

I also tried the Curry udon with chicken. Man did it smell DELICIOUS. Udon was nicely done: cooked all the way through but chewy and not soggy. Curry smell made me drool like crazy. Their chicken was interesting: most teriyaki-type chicken meat tend to be really soft and "tender", almost to the point of making you wonder, "So... did this chicken get no exercise?" CU's chicken was tender, soft but not too soft. When you bit into it, you still feel the strips of muscle we're suppose to be eating. It tasted much more natural and organic. Not to mention there were a lot of it.

The environment is very lively, filled with tons of college students. Their servers are nice and work very quickly to get you what you need, without appearing like they're rushing you out of the place.

Baby lobster roll!!! California roll covered with baby lobster, mushrooms, onions, and a bunch of other stuff and baked... definitely my favorite thing from CU Sushi, but I guess I haven't tried too many things because I just order the baby lobster roll every time :) 

I think the prices have gone up slightly (I think the paper menu used to be 50% off but now only nigiri is discounted) but either way, it's still the best sushi place near campus.

it's cheap for japanese. it's filling. it's near campus. 

i was pretty disappointed by the quality of the food after hearing so many good things about it. the rolls leave you desiring something more. and the fried calamari leaves your mouth with an old oil taste. 

i think their best dishes here are the salads, like the sashimi salad...good flavor and portion size. but it's a salad. i don't just go out to a restaurant because i'm craving a salad. that's just ridiculous.

50% off select rolls and nigiri. What's not to love about that? It's not really the best quality sashimi, but for 50% off, it'll do. I ordered spicy tuna roll, yellow tail, and salmon. The yellow tail was a little bit fishy, but it might be because we were there right before they were closing. (but still, that's no excuse). Their wasabi was not very spicy at all, I had to use a lot of it to get a slight taste of spice. I'm still giving a 3 star because their 50% off deal can't be beat, and their menu selection is huge. I'll have to come back and try their different rolls.

My math buddy and I always came here before buckling down and doing our problem sets. 

We've only been here for the rolls, and why wouldn't we? It's cheap and delicious, and better than Tako or Joshuya's. We would usually had 3 rolls each (each roll about $3-4 each) that filled us up quite nicely. The salmon skin rolls are really good!

My only problem is that this place is tiny. To the point where it seems like I always elbow the person next to me who's at a different table. We've also had to wait for almost 30 minutes once, and there is absolutely no AT&T cell phone reception at all here.

Their Orgasm Salad is friggin' bomb!  The salmon doesn't smell fishy and that's how I know it's fresh.  Lay those pieces all over the veggies, seaweed, and sauce to make the best seafood salad I've ever had in Berkeley.  If healthy, filling, and delicious are qualities that you look for in a salad, then try this.  

The portion is likable to Intermezzo's Chef's Salad.  (Okay... maybe not, but it comes close!)


Everything else here is decent.  But the only thing that wows me is the salad.

CU sounds shady--half priced sushi...really?...really? But no, really, it is actually great!  The food comes out unbelievably fast, the service is on point and the food is quite good.  This place is a great spot to get sushi AND get full without breaking the bank.  Again, the orgasm salad SOUNDS shady...but it is actually one of my favorite dishes there.  Delicious, fast, friendly.  Who could want more?

You know you need to judge a restaurant by only its food when you see their cash register screen flash "SMILE!" signals when it's on idle. The waiter/waitress here are rude. If I had to give them stars based on service, it would be less than one star! But I have to say the 50% off rolls are worth the agonizing wait. This is a typical college spot, so don't come here on a first date or try to impress someone with the Berkeley vibe. It ain't all that cool. 

Try the yellowtail roll (6 pcs) for $3.25 and the shiitake roll (6 pcs of mushroom). The spicy tuna roll (6 pcs) for $3.25 is also satisfying. I really can't complain when I can buy 4 rolls for $15, but it's simply just a quick mediocre sushi fix.

I can't believe I haven't Yelped about this place yet.  They've been so good to me, and they deserve more respect than that.  I've been to this place since it opened, and I can't say enough good things about it.  First and foremost, it's very reasonably priced, which can't be said about many sushi places irrespective of the quality of their sushi.  While this is not the MOST AMAZING sushi I've ever had, it's a place that I love to come and grab a lunch or dinner.  I burned myself out on it for awhile, but now am glad to be back.  The service is truly great and the atmosphere is relaxed except for the techno or Kelly Clarkson playing over the sound system.  Portions are large, and it's a great value for food and ambiance.

This is definitely one of my favorite sushi places in Berkeley. Their fish is fresh(Mmmmmm sake sashimi) and prices are fair. They sometimes give you coupons off your next meal. I've never trouble with their service.
We ordered the Hawaiian something with seared Albacore. yums!
The scallop roll was okay, but it one of those cheap ones, so that's probably why.  Will definitely keep coming back.

the fish is nice and fresh. the spicy tuna isn't alarmingly soft and mushy like the other sushi places around cal. i had a plate of maguro sashimi and it a half hour of proverbial gastronomical heeeyyy-ven!
they also serve edamame to get us started. we spent almost 40 dollars and they gave us $4 in gift certificates - very sweet of them
i highly recommend the spicy tuna and scallop roll. caterpillar roll was pretty standard. the udon is okay - too salty for my taste.

Cheap and decent. Can't beat the 50% sushi special. We stopped in for a snack and ordered some edamame, inari, avocado & cucumber roll, and a shiitake mushroom roll. Our bill was only $14 including drinks! The sushi was good, the cucumber was thinly chopped and delicious. I prefer when the rolls are inside-out so I was glad these rolls had the rice on the outside. 
I've had better sushi but not for that price.

the sushi was ok... 
the rolls are as usual, kinda pricey and not all that authentic, but the stuff that are on for 1/2 off right now are pretty good. all in all the fish was fresh. there's nothing more scary than warm fish...

i've been there a few times already. you gotta get a good waitress btw. the first time we went, we all noticed that this one waitress was talking shit about us. hope you don't get the bitchy one!

The first thing you'll notice is a 1/2 Off deal advertised on a sandwich board outside the door-- sounds good, but it's not quite a 'deal' when its prices are printed permanently on the menu. It's still a fair price to pay for decent fish, though, and mine seemed fresh and clean. The miso soup and edamame were both too salty for my taste, but a good Rainbow Roll makes those complaints minor. The service was fast, which I appreciated, but the atmosphere was bland, similar to the other quick and student-oriented places on the block.

*NOTE: This review is only for the udon

I was craving udon the other day and decided to check CU out since the prices seemed really reasonable and they offer take out.  I ordered tempura udon to go ($7 after tax) and it was ready in less than ten minutes and they give you legit containers for the soup!  I rushed back to the office only to be very very disappointed.  I got two pieces of tempura - one shrimp and one squash - uh, I've never been to a place that skimped so much.  The udon itself was a good texture but I'm not a fan of the broth at all - and they put WAY too much white onion in it.  It was like 5 pieces of onion per noodle. YUCK.

I definately won't be coming back for the udon but I'll give their sushi a shot.  Will update...
So I had to make an update. I love calling in my order and picking it up. They are very attentive in answering the phone during the busy lunch hour, and they have never made me wait!

Originally I would've given this place 4 stars but after a return trip, they've been demoted!

First time I came I thought this place was pretty decent -- good food, okay price for Japanese food. I typically order their orange special which is $10.50 for some specialty roll + california roll or spicy tuna roll (I would get the shrimp tempura roll and it came with a significant portion of tempura vegetables and shrimp on the side). Their baked salmon roll was also really good. The first 3 times I came it was always huge portions for the price and good quality. 

However, when I came back here yesterday their price went up and they now charge more for spicy tuna instead of the california roll with the Orange Special. Not to mention, they now give less tempura with your rolls. I was quite disappointed. I also ordered the spicy tuna tempura roll thinking that it would be spicy tuna with tempura bits on top (that's what it looks like in the picture) but my roll was completely deep fried, the tuna was 100% cooked and not even spicy. Can I just say I was thoroughly disappointed. 

3 stars for price (I'd say just mosey over to Sushi Ko if you want rolls), 3 stars for quality. I ordered to-go so I can't comment on the service, but their seemed to be 2 waiters for the entire restaurant, and they seemed flustered / unable to keep up.

Meh. Eh. You can definitely find better sushi restaurants in Berkeley. I came here with a group of about 5 on a Sunday afternoon at about 2 pm. 

First off, apparently you're supposed to be given free Edamame before you order? My group didn't. 

The waiters were extremely unprofessional. They were probably college students (which is fine), but they didn't make much of an effort to see if we were satisfied with our food. Our orders came out in long increments. A group of 3 got their sushi rolls at least 10 minutes before the other group got their rolls - and this is after we already waited about 30 minutes for our rolls.

I ordered the Power Roll, which is pretty similar to the Dragon Roll. For about $10.50, I got about 5 small pieces of sushi that definitely did not fill me up. The sushi was poorly rolled, so it was falling apart immediately after I picked it up with my chopsticks. 

Totally overpriced and not worth it. I'd rather go to Joshu-ya and pay a dollar or two more. 

I went to McDonald's afterwards to satisfy my appetite.

It's a sushi joint near a college campus with so-so prices. You can pretty much imagine that the taste will be so-so as well. Ordered the scallop nigiri and the udon bowl that starts with an "n". (comes with a tempura'ed squash slice and one shrimp.) nothing exceptional and the broth was kind of bland. all in all, not bad, but not great. would still come back here cuz it's relatively fast and cheap.

Cheap, fast, fresh, and delicious! My only complaint is that the place is really small, which makes it hard if you want to go with a group of friends. Your rolls are ready within 10 minutes of ordering. I strongly recommend the Mexican Roll. Just to give you warning, it's spicy!

Note: I don't eat seafood so this will be just for their udon.

I came here a while ago with a friend and got their chicken udon. I had THE best udon in LA Little Tokyo last summer, and have been on a quest to find one that comes even close to that deliciousness. C U Sushi has come the closest so far.

The udon I'm pretty sure is prepackaged, but it was cooked perfectly. Not too soggy and just chewy enough. The broth was really good though. Although not on par with Little Tokyo (obviously), it was still really hearty and delicious. All the veggies and such they add are pretty standard. But I'd go back again just to taste that broth. Yum.

I also came here last night and got the curry chicken udon. I was debating between that and curry chicken rice, but decided I wanted udon. I probably should've just gone with regular udon instead. The curry didn't really taste like anything. I expected it to taste at least somewhat curry-ey. But it tasted really bland, even though it was dark brown. So I was confused. Definitely won't be getting curry udon here ever again.

The place is really small, and crammed with a lot of tables, so it can get kind of noisy and bothersome at times. But the servers are rather attentive so it's okay.

If I ever come back, I'll be having the chicken udon.

My baby LOVES this place!!!  I thought the salmon sashimi was really good:  7 pieces for $8.95.  The miso soup and the seaweed salad are pretty good too.  The only downsides are that I'm pretty sure they use imitation crab meat and it's so loud I can't hear my BF tell me all about his day.  Stats Rules!!!

P.S.  You made my baby smell like tempura!

Whenever I'm in the area, I always drop by C U Sushi. This place is hard to find parking and is small, but they serve their food so fast that the turnovers are very quick. Their quality of food is pretty good so I'm not sure how they make their food so fast! They always have a list of sushi that is 50% (but they are very plain rolls) that is worth it if you like simple rolls. This place isn't THAT cheap except for that 50% list. The prices are pretty normal.

They start you off with some edamame and main dishes come with miso soup. Both are good quality.

Things I've tried:
1) Looking at yelp, I tried the Orgasm salad. Not really as good as people say. I mean, the seared tuna is decent (4 pieces) which is served on a bed of lettuce. The house sauce is good too but they put a little too much that day. The seaweed salad they put on top is my favorite! One piece of avocado too. It just didn't strike me as something special aka ORGASMIC...especially just using regular romaine lettuce.

2) Dynamite!: THIS IS MY FAVORITE DISH!! It's a baked dish of baby scallops, masago, onions, and mushrooms. The sauce they use is DELICIOUS!! It's savory and sweet! It's great to pour over rice. I don't know why it's just so delicious....

3) Unagi bowl: NEVER GET THIS! So not worth it! You get only 4 pieces of sliced unagi over a bed of rice seasoned with seaweed, 5 little pieces of broccoli and some pickled radish and ginger. UHHH..for $9?! Heck no...

4) Udon with chicken: Ehh, I don't think their hot plates are their specialty. It's just normal..nothing too good.

5) Baked salmon (kind of like Lion King): Pretty good! Very tasty

6) Their rolls in general are pretty good and they have some special ones like the Berkeley Roll that people like.

Overall, a good place to enjoy. The service is good in that they do things quickly.

I will C U LATER C U Sushi!!

This place is actually worth about three and a half stars, but today I am rounding down (unfortunately). 

Like most of the reviews stated on this page, if you're ever craving for sushi, this is probably the quickest and cheapest way for you to have your sushi. Another good thing about this place is, it is never crowded, you can go in at any hour of the day(when they are opened of course) and you will almost be guaranteed to find a place to sit.

Rating...?
This place did not receive five stars not due to the fact  that the sushi here is terrible,but it just isn't comparable to others that I've had. Sushi is sushi is sushi, it is hard to make bad sushi, just as it is hard to make really awesome sushi! If you are living on a college budget, as I suspect you do, as this place is right next to a (expensive) learning institution.

Stopped in here just before the Yelp sponsored Passing Strange show at the Berkeley Rep.  I was able to order, eat and pay all in 20 minutes flat!  Great service and the sushi was fine (philadephia roll, unagi nigiri).  I also got miso and free edamame.  It was perfect and healthier than eating a hot dog, like my friends did next door.  I'll be stopping here again when I'm heading to the rep!

A few days ago we were in Berkeley and decided we were hungry, but what to eat?  I mean, come on, it's not there aren't many choices!

We finally decided we would narrow it down to one block of Center Street, but even then it was a tough choice.  

We opted for C U Sushi, and ended up being quite happy with our choice.  One of our group was REALLY hungry and got an order of tempura as an appetizer; it was good, but tempura is tempura, it's either really greasy or it's good, never spectacular.
BTW, did you know that tempura isn't traditionally Japanese?  The Portugese introduced it to them in the sixteenth century.

I digress...

We ordered the Spicy Tuna Tataki Roll and Hot Night Roll specials, plus a Tiger Roll and a Teriyaki Chicken plate.  The fish was all very fresh and just about melted on your tongue.  The Tiger and Hot Night rolls were actually very similar, one with tuna and one with salmon.  All three were good and we couldn't decide on a favorite.

I usually prefer simple sushi and sushimi to fancy fru-fru sushi with sauces squirted on top, but I have to say this might have changed my mnd.

We were full but decided to split a Banana Tempura Ice Cream to end the meal.  It's a good thing we didn't order three of them because we were just expecting a scoop of ice cream.  It was a huge scoop of ice cream with four tempura banana pieces and a drizzle of chocolate sauce.  Mmmmm

Our only complaint was that our food didn't come at the same time.  Between the first and last dish, is was probably 5 minutes, which seemed really long considering there were only three other goups there at the time (about 4pm).  What would the wait have been like if it was full at lunch or dinner?

The staff was very helpful and friendly, and kept a watch on us without being pushy.

All in all, I think we'll be back the next time we're in the area.

I almost didn't recognize it because of the new green awning.  How.  Thoughtful.  

One lunchday, during bar prep.  Christina found herself in need of something.  Was it company?  Was it a sympathetic shoulder?  Was it escape from the confines of her Barbri prison?  Certainly, the siren call of greasy, comforting, fry-a-lator foods beckoned from the recesses of the dark matter floating in the universe, sending out transmission of tightly hugged arteries.  But who was there to receive the transmission?  

It was nearly raining when Christina crossed the threshold of this establishment.  Water was offered.  A bento box was selected.  It had choices.  Similar at face value to the multiple choice, Christina blundered this choice too.  It was the first time she picked the spicy chicken bento with rice, salad, 1 gyoza, tempura and fruit.  The magic of the multiverse continues, there is a way to screw up "chicken" by making it "spicy."  

The tempura was decent enough.  Not as good as Anzu.  Oh Anzu.  You are like a belly button ring that has suddenly fallen off after a rough hike up the mountains and a terrible mudslide down the ravine.  Missed, remembered, regretted, but I'd do it again in a heartbeat.  

Here, Christina has given up on the sushi for the time being.  With the notable exception of Uni and Amaebi (and then, only when there is money to burn), the sushi here is pretty indecent.  The prospect of return rests in the hands of Uni.  But for all other sushi needs, the belly button ring prevails.

**I don't have a belly button piercing.  I merely enjoy writing about them.

I love their teriyaki bowls and wakame salad :) I've tried some of their half-off deals (they have 50% some really basic maki/california rolls), but they didn't strike me as amazing. The service is typically very fast and friendly, and your food order is usually done in about 10-15 minutes. I'm not a regular dining-in customer here, but their takeout service is always reliable!

I've also seen my friends order their regular-priced rolls, which they said were decent but a little undersized. Just something to keep in mind! :)
Tons of sushi for $15-20 ??? Where do I have to sign? Yay! Very nice place.

Sometimes this place has the 1/2 off special on sushi rolls and that's the BEST time to go! Otherwise, it's just too expensive and not all that awesome! I know..I know...I'm totally blinded by how cheap the sushi is when it's on sale, but I can't help confounding the two factors. Cheaper food = Tastes better b/c expectation of the food decreases. It's a simple equation I'm sure everyone can relate to!

I love CU Sushi! The staff is warm and inviting. The food is always fresh and yummy. Another great place for work lunch.

My personal favorites: Orgasm Salad, need I say more? The dressing is incredible on the salad and they should box this stuff and sell it as retail.
I also love the gyoza- which I have no idea how to pronounce.
The lunch box is also good and the prices are reasonable. They are always busy with a line at lunch time so I suggest going around 2pm for faster service and wait time.
Ohh and for some reason, we get gift certificates for this place once a year which is very much appreciated and comes in handy since we frequent the joint so often.

So, I wish I could go to Berkeley. Not because I want to be  smart and blablabla, but because there are  soooooooo many good places to eat. C U Sushi is affordable and tasty. The only good sushi in Davis is owned by a mean Asian lady who shouts insults at me when I try to eat. Read my review on Zen Toro if you want to learn more.

Why, yes. I am shamelessly trying to gain more site views. What of it? Okay, i'll move on.

The Rolls:
Lion King Roll : Very yummy baked roll. Perfect temperature, and just enough cream cheese.
Spicy Tuna and scallop roll: The fish was fresh, the spicy tuna was spot on and the scallops added a nice touch.

Honestly, all the rolls on their menu sound and look great! A couple next to me ordered the Power roll and it looked amazing. I think I'll order that next.

Good food and service? Yes pleasee. C U soon! ( Sorry for the corniness, I am writing this very late at night)

I usually get the sushi combo specials here, particularly the yellow and red specials. The calamari tempura roll is a must-try; although it might be loosely rolled to some people, I didn't mind since it's all going into my mouth anyways. I still need to try the hot dishes like the udon and the bowls, but a friend who went along said his tempura udon was decent, not extraordinary.

As many other reviewers can attest, the 50%-off menu is a steal. Granted, you need to order at least 2 dishes from that menu, per person, to get the deal, but since I usually order 2 at a time anyways, it's no big deal. The different varieties they have on the menu will keep you coming back to try them all (or get them all at once, your choice). And better do so. The sushi here may not be super-awesome-blow-your-mind, but for the price, they are simply delicious.

Service is smooth. Never had a hitch in service. The waiters are polite and friendly.

Better come early for lunch or dinner, though, if you want a space. The restaurant has maybe less than ten small indoor tables, with a couple outside.

The fish is good and fresh but I am not very impressed at all with their udon. It was totally not authentic tasting and it was just wrong in terms of the ingredients included and the flavor. I'd come back for the sushi only.
Relatively good sushi. For $10 you can get miso soup, tempura and one of their special roles. The miso soup was extremely salty but the rest was decent.

I would give this place about 3.7 stars, because of the following:

1 - Best sushi within walking distance of campus
2 - Good variety in the menu
3 - Good service for the most part
4 - And most of all, cheap prices!!

I've been here about five times now, and my experience varies. I have way more good experiences here than bad, but when it's bad.. oh, it's bad. On bad days, every piece of sushi falls apart in my little soy sauce dish. And sometimes the service is downright unmentionable. Sometimes, the servers linger in the kitchen, talking to other employees, and they don't pay any attention to the customers. There was also one time that we ordered the Baby Lobster Roll (SOO GOOD), but it came like 10 minutes after we had finished everything else! If you already know you want a baked roll, I would suggest asking them to put the order in for it first, before you even decide what else you want. 

Overall though, the fish is usually fresh, and the decor inside the restaurant is very nice. It always feel clean, and I love that sometimes they give complementary things, like moist towelettes (the ones that look like little marshmallows and expand when they pour water on top) and edamame. They refill water quickly, which is important for my camel of a boyfriend... and it's not usually very crowded. At least not when I go, which is usually later at around 8:30pm or 9pm. Prices are reasonable, not too expensive but definitely not cheap. If you are looking to save some money, the "to-go" menu is 50% off always. And you can order off of it even if you're eating in the restaurant. Pretty sweeeet.

I have been here multiple times with friends, and must say that I am always shocked by the bill, it is so very affordable.  The half-priced menu is great.  The food is average, but even when crowded, the staff is attentive.

It's been a while since I've written an review. Usually when I do, it's because there's something extraordinary about a place that piques my interest enough to write about.

Anyways, let's get down to business. I went here tonight with two friends. The highlight of my meal was the edamame. 

First, let's talk service. We waited for a good five minutes while there was an empty table inside. When we were finally seated, it took the waiter another 10 minutes to acknowledge us and take our order. Granted the place was a bit packed, but any good waiter knows how to scan the tables and look for eye contact for a customer. I ordered the "Shitake mushroom special". Our plates came out at 3 different times! Amazing. There's nothing I love more at a restaurant than to wait and watch my food get cold until everyone gets served. When the last plate was finally brought out (10 minutes after we received the first plate), we ate.

Second, let's talk food. Ever seeing that South Park episode "City Sushi"? Yea, that's a pun on "Shitty Sushi". If I had to pick one word to describe my meal, it would be "shitty". My $9.95 Shitty-take mushroom special was marinated in a familiar sauce. I almost didn't believe my taste buds when I realized the main two ingredients in the sauce was ketchup and Sriracha. Really? Did your kitchen run out of oyster sauce and teriyaki sauce? 

TL;DR: Shitty sushi. Shitty service.

The owner tried to tell me I didn't see what I saw, what a jerk, proof this is not a place I want to ever go again. I watched the ENTIRE EVENT. BE A MAN AND APOLOGIZE FOR THE INAPPROPRIATE ACTIONS OF YOUR EMPLOYEES.
 


HI. This is the owner of the C U SUSHI. Between kenny L. and Heather L.

Thanks for the review but there is some incorrect information such as jail etc. Both side decided to not make a sue. please help our business from wrong info. if possible please put down your review. we will appreciate.

This review is not incorrect I WAS THERE and watched with my own eyes. Your employee was cuffed and taken to jail for assault, I watched the police take him away, and the young man was taken from the scene in an ambulance. Your employees assaulted that young man and chased him DOWN THE STREET AFTER THEY TRIED TO TRAP HIM FROM LEAVING YOUR RESTAURANT! I WAS THERE AND SAW IT ALL I WILL NOT CHANGE THIS REVIEW.

I like this place. I find that I am not the best person to review sushi restaurants considering I am allergic to fish. However, I do enjoy a good veggie sushi roll. 

Nonetheless: 
CU is one of those places that you go back to because of a combination of reasons. The food is good, the service is great and to the point, and their combos make ordering easy. Most importantly, as many times as we have been there, we have not had a bad experience. So...track record, check!

I enjoy the veggie tempura roll (on the orange special). A nice change from the avocucumber roll at most places.

My inly complaint is that they do not have containers for soup take out. But i am just trying to be nit picky.

Had a quick, cheap, and relatively tasty lunch here. The service was very friendly and prompt. Their menu features a gazillion different types of rolls and good lunch specials. Unfortunately,  my shrimp tempura roll was impossible to eat. It was loosely rolled and much wider than a typical roll. It was difficult to pick up with chopsticks and even harder to actually eat. I felt so self-conscious about shoving a hockey puck sized thing into my mouth I attempted to bite it in half, which of course didn't work. It was awkward.

UPDATE: 
Tuna: 5 stars
Service: 0 stars for takeout, 2 for in house eating
