I still love the salad. What I don't love is the punk ass people working in this place. First of all, when a customer comes in at 11:28 don't refuse to help her because it isn't 11:30 yet and if you are going to do that, than keep the damn door closed! 

Second, lets try not acting like you don't see people who come in to pick up their take out just because you don't think you are going to get a tip.

 I think they are pissed because student's don't give good tips. WELL here is a tip-- if people ARE considering giving you a gratuity they probably won't if you are an ass! 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
As a Berkeley resident, alum and wife of a current Grad student, I spend a lot of time looking for food around center street. One Sunday, when almost nothing else was open, I stopped into this place. Now, I as assuming it would be lackluster like the take out sushi 2 doors down closer to the BART. BOY was I wrong. First of all, it was real plates, a big drink and a sidewalk seat. Then came the 4 stars.... Spicy Tuna Salad!!!!!!!!!!! It was delish and only $8.95. 

Every once in a while you stumble onto a "hole in the wall" which unexpectedly surprises you and becomes something you pine for.... need I say Spicy Tuna?

Just as this place led me to give up plastic box sushi, one day, when I have an actual job and can afford omakase regularly, I will abandon CU. Until then, the not-really-50% off menu (it's about 40% cheaper than Kirala) will be my regular sushi choice: I like it much better than the "creative" main menu. I usually pay a bit over ten bucks, including tip, for a light meal of a couple of orders of nigiri (try the scallop) and a maki roll (salmon skin), attractively arranged on the plate. All freshish, if not "I just got this maguro from the Sea of Japan via teleport" fresh. I'll enjoy it while I can, until somebody takes me to Sebo.

For the longest time I thought that this place was just called "50% off" because their biggest sign just said that...
I had some great sushi here for lunch.  And it is very reasonably priced.  Both a friend and I ate here for 15 bucks.  And we got a lot of food.  My friend's salad had way too much dressing and my terriyaki bowl could have had more veggies like broccoli and carrots.  But, all in all, it was good.

My peeps and I have a moniker for this place: B12.

Why?

Because B12 corresponds to CU's Baby Lobster Roll aka The Best Thing Ever.

I generally try to avoid Asian fusion places, but I've been coming here since its Grand Opening back when I was an undergraduate and broke.  The fish isn't the freshest and I recommend avoiding the Crazy Monkey Roll or whatever it's called, but you can't beat sushi and sashimi that's 50% off, friendly service, or their fabulous B12.  Both the salmon kama and hamachi kama are incredible (but it's rare that they will have either) and their tempura and nabeyaki udon are all pretty good too.  Not to mention the sleek decor and cool soysauce bottles!

CU there!

I've been here a couple of times and found the sushi to be tasty and the service to be friendly and attentive.

My favorites include the Seaweed Salad, the Energy Roll, and the Yellowtail (Hamachi)/Scallion roll. Their nigiri sushi is also pretty good, served with enough wasabi sandwiched between the fish and rice to give you a nice horseradish headrush.

Nom nom nom nom nom!!! 
Sushi!!!
Nom nom nom!!! 

So, we're talking about a little hole-in-the-wall sort of place, no great frills, no sushi bar, no high-end fussy bits. Just a really cute place that has really good sushi. AND a really good price. Especially if you stick with the "half-off" basic menu.

I've never had better unagi btw. :)

You know the old adage: "quick, cheap, good -- pick two?" WELL, this place breaks that. The sushi came out in no time flat, I got a huge roll and 4 pieces of nigiri and tea for under $15, and it was mighty tasty.

5 stars!! Will so go here again!!!

See you, CU.

Maki rolls and nigiri are 50% off but it's not worth it to get the rolls unless your the type that like your sushi plain like California roll. We ordered the orgasmic salad which looked good in pictures but didn't taste so good. It was basically 4 large pieces of seared tuna with leafy greens and a shit load of dressing.  It was over dressed and I didn't like it. 

What saved the day were the monkey balls. I don't think anything deep fried can go wrong. Crispy golden balls stuffed with mushroom and tempura glazed with teriyaki sauce on top.

Everything we ordered came out within minutes. There are some ninja sushi rollers and chefs in the kitchen. Too bad the food is bleh.

Eaten here way too many times, but never knew the name. We know it as 50% off sushi. That's right. 50% off. Not on certain days. Not at happy hour. All day, every day. Basic rolls and nigiri only though. It's a pretty good deal. No one's been sick... yet. 

The fish is ok, not the freshest slab that you can find, but it'll do. The preparation isn't great, rolls often have way too much rice. But then again, it's 50% so do you really expect it to look that nice? 

What exactly is the fusion part? The orgasm salad???

Came here after returning something at the Buffalo Exchange heard this place had 1/2 off sushi so decided to give it a try since my sister LOVES sushi.

Place is very small and is located on a really cute street with a bunch of neighboring small shops and restaurants. They have a pretty extensive menu with a bunch of different rolls that are price from $6-$9. But of course my sis and I opted for 50% sushi. 

The 50% sushi consisted mainly nigiri and your basic maki rolls (6 pieces). We ordered tons of nigiri:- (4)Salmon, Tuna, White Tuna, Scallop. One Hamchi Roll and (2) Scallop Roll. Total bill was $30. The quality of the fish was really good I was very impressed considering the price for the nigiris. I really enjoyed their Salmon and Scallop Nigiri. Make sure to ask for a side of spicy mayo if you order the scallop nirgiri or roll you won't regret it. Reason why I didn't give it four stars is because I didn't like how their sushi rice tasted. I like it with a little more rice vinegar and stickier.

Overall good place to come if you have cravings for Nigiri and basic rolls. Also another thing is they don't put a lot of rice with the Nigiri so its great for those who likes more fish and less rice!

I would not call this place super-cheap. It is reasonably priced, but their appetizers are very costly.
Their food was very fun (hence the "fusion" in their title). Their menu was full of rolls and they had great lunch specials. Their presentation is very good for eat-in orders. I rarely eat in. I prefer take-out. I call ahead and by the time I get there, my order is ready and my bill is error-free. I have tried many rolls and other dishes. There is not one that I did not like. My only problem was there were so many choices, it was hard to concentrate on just one when I was hungry. The tan curry was good. Their "half price" nigiri was fresh. I always get a few of those.
Their service was good.
Their location is very convenient to BART and the UCB campus, so it is a quick walk to satisfaction. I will be going there often while I am too busy to grocery shop.

I've been going here ever since they first opened and I go there so often now that I startled a waiter when I recognized he no longer had braces. There's a reason why I keep coming back.  Whether I'm having dinner with friends or grabbing something to go, I always get prompt service and the waiters are always kind when called upon. 

Though their rolls might upset people who want "authentic" sushi, their fusion rolls are fun to try out and have yet to disappoint me. At dinner time, I love it when they place these little pellets in dishes and pour a little hot water on them - they swell up into instant hand towels, how cute! They give a lot of food for a relatively lower price than many other places which is nice for college students who are tight on cash. However, it's a smaller place, so if you have a large group, it can be a bit of a wait.

I go here alot. It's a convenient, cheap place to either sit and chill or grab and go. 

Their rolls/nigiri always fall apart (always, lol) but are still yummy. Their nabeyaki udon is amazing on a chilly day. 

They give you $1 coupons if you ask!

Yes.
It's true.  All these years I've been going around the block but today was the first time I ever had an orgasm...

...salad. That's what it's called. Seared tuna with avocado with a few lightly marinated veggies on beautiful, crisp mixed greens- thank god I asked for the overly creamy dressing on the side because - forgive me, but that nasty mess would have been a serious downer if it were sliming up my pretty crisp greens.  (Frankly the name "orgasm" is a little bit of an overstatement. I hate to think of 18 yr old college freshmen eating one and wondering "ls that all there is?") But it's a good salad all-in-all.

What I love about CU's menu is the variety of dishes that feature sashimi - so many places give you just one sashimi appetizer option or maybe a chirashi bowl.  CU has lots of different salads and bowls that feature different sashimi with interesting ingredients to accompany. 

Oh - and I LOVE getting there just before noon so I can watch the little fan dancers on the so-hideous-it's-beautiful cuckoo clock do their little thing.

Had a nice, late, outdoor lunch here recently, and I was pleasantly surprised at the creativity and quality of this place.  What we have here is a student friendly eatery, that could stand on its own against much more expensive places.

I tend to be a purist when it comes to sushi, and 'modern' sushi just irks me most of the time; something about spicy and/or creamy sushi just makes me cringe.  However, CU sushi really captured my heart (via my stomach and taste buds of course).  They offer a lot of wonderfully creative rolls, without going too overboard in trying to cater to an Americanized palate; what you get is a delightful selection of Korean and Japanese inspired flavors.  More importantly, they do have all the basics on their menu, and they do them very well.

First of all, I loved the presentation.  Each order is plated meticulously with lots of care and personal attention.  You see this throughout the restaurant in terms of decor and cleanliness too; the owner has that desire for obsessive-compulsive order that is the hallmark of a good Japanese restaurant.  The dish arrives at your table, and the first thing you'll say is either "cute" or "pretty."

Even better is CU's flavor.  Their sushi rice has the perfect seasoning (not too sweet or too vinegary) and texture (firm and holds together, but not sticky).  The fish in their nigiri and sashimi is fresh and very tasty.  The rolls are what are cool about this place though.  The large selection of tempura rolls, baked rolls and other creative delights are a lot of fun.  I was surprised to find my shitake tempura roll came with extra shitake tempura on the side.  The tofu steak is also very good here, crispy and crunchy fried, yet not greasy, it is light and clean tasting.  The unagi is amazing here as well, and the sauce is perfect ... just perfect (they use it on most of the fried items as well).

All in all, a solid 4 stars based on flavor, price, presentation, sidewalk cafe seating near UC, being half a block from BART, and the 'kawai' factor.  CU makes a solid addition to the Center Street line of cheap eats for lunch, and makes a seamless conversion to a dinner spot in downtown Berkeley as well.

UPDATE: 8/1/06  REALLY GOOD UDON!  Well, perhaps just 'good' udon, but that means a lot in the crappy-udon-verse that is the bay area!  Cheap, and a large bowl too (~$5.95).

There is a dearth of good sushi places in Berkeley.  Although CU Sushi is by no means the best sushi place, I come back again and again, because it is the best sushi place within walking distance that is also a good value!  After multiple visits here, I've settled into a routine of getting one of their combos -- Hot Night roll, which is spicy and delicious, along with their miso soup/salad and a few pieces of nigiri -- all for $11.95.

Should you travel to try it?  No.  But if you're nearby and you want sushi, this is a decent option.

I love this place! Maybe it's who I always go with :P but really, this place is great!

I'm surprised at the low reviews of this place but I think it's my favorite place to get nigiri (since it's cheap and good!). All their nigiri is about $2.50/2 pieces so it's a pretty good deal! I recommend trying the seared albacore and super white tuna. The salmon, tuna, and hamachi are pretty good too. I tried their scallop roll (raw) and that tasted pretty good too! Everything tastes fresh and it's melt in your mouth good. MmMm. 

As for appetizer, definitely try the "Yummy Crispy". It's a lot bigger than you think and the sauce is grrreatt! 

What really makes this place great also is their service. They are sooo nice and friendly. We always get free edamame and they even gave us free nigiri last time! How awesome right!?

My niece's 14th birthday (YIKES!) so we decided to hit up Berkeley for an adventure. As per her request we were on the hunt for a nice Italian joint for a fine birthday dinner. Seeing all the restaurants on this block we decide to take a gander. As soon as we walk past the place there was no where else we were going. I think she was attracted to all the people and noise coming out of the place. Turned out to be a pretty solid choice. 

The prices are ridiculous, in a good way. Their 50% menu is just that, tons of options for $2-3 sashimi and a nice selection of hand rolls for $4-6, had 3 hand rolls an order of Unagi, Maguro and Hamachi. We also got a Rainbow Roll and a Spider Roll with 3 sodas for around $55. The prices match the quality but it was absolutely perfect for a teenager and her kid brother. 

They were kind enough to bring out some delicious green tea ice-cream on the house for the young lady's birthday.

Great if you're on a budget and need a sushi fix.

Dropping into Berkeley to have lunch with a friend (see zipper guy) we happened upon C U on our way to Tako. There was a line out the door, but it was windy and adding that to our laziness meant that within about ten minutes we had a table.

I must say they served us the best sushi I've had in a long time. Tokyo Lobby good *Crosses self* My Spider Roll was amazing, the avocado roll was yummy and I always love it when the miso has huge chunks of seaweed in it. This plus the palm size cups of tea equals a happy Megan.

The service itself was steller, they kept our teas filled and our food coming and the shop was warm and cozy.

5 Stars the whole way.

This was stop #1 on the (sushi) bar crawl to say farewell to a friend moving out of the area. The rolls in particular are very good, as were the Monkey Balls and Creamy Shrimp Tempura appetizers. The miso is pretty salty, as are the warm edamame, but both are tasty. Service is fair, and the space is a little cramped, but the quality and price basically make up for it. Being only a block from UCB and Berkeley BART is another big plus.

The sushi here is of mediocre quality. The fusion is nothing eyeopening or mindblowing, but the food is pretty good still. I am consoled by the fact that the rolls here are cheap!

I have no food allergies, yet I managed to break out in small hives after eating dinner here once! It was especially terrible since I was going to a concert right after! Ever since then, I've been afraid to come back. Perhaps I'll come up with the courage to one of these days.

This tiny place goes through a nice stampeding by college students everyday during lunch hours. I sneaked in for an early dinner to get the gist of the phenomenon and the experience did not disappoint.  My spicy tuna tataki roll (8.95) had decent spicy tuna in the middle and a generous portion of tuna tataki with a mix of scallions and onions on top. To my surprise, all of their nigiris are half price all day long, so my order of green salmon (2.63), spicy albacore (2.25), and ikura (3.95) came in large pairs with the salmon layered with a thick piece of avocado being the most tasteful. 

There were no traces of fusion cuisine but instead the menu was dominated by sushi rolls with remnants bento and appetizer items. The smallish dining area did not deter this place from having a nice ambiance of using red, pale wasabi green, and dark brown as thematic colors to correlate with the food. Although the cuts of the fish were generous, it was nonetheless grade B quality and not the freshest. Service was slow but attentive. I will give it 3 stars for having an exciting menu, nice large quantity, and for making sushi affordable and accessible to the masses.

I stop by here every so often, and it's always solid.  If it's nice outside you can sit outdoors at one of the little tables and enjoy being outside.  On a colder day, you can perch in the window and watch the flow of people down Center Street.  Very basic, yet cute inside, and always clean.

We usually get a few different rolls, the spicy tuna, crab, and cucumber rolls are all good and no mayo like some spots around town.  (I don't really get why places do that.)   Sashimi is also nice (try the hamachi and super-white tuna) and generously sized.  The menu has a funny conceit of listing all the prices as "half price," but either way it's a great bargain.  Hot sake is yum and super cheap, perfect with a nice frosty Asahi.  

Service is efficient and nice and location is right near BART - definitely my go-to sushi spot on the way home from campus!

This place was cute, and pretty good for the price.  I think that if you tried enough different things you'd eventually identify what to order.  Of the things we ordered, the squid and spicy tuna were both good.  The miso soup was also pretty good.

Aside from that, the service was pretty mediocre.  My water never got refilled and we only got our edamame after begging for it at the end of our meal.

I'd go here again if other people wanted to and maybe for the half-price menu.  Still, it's not my first choice for sushi.

I can't use chopsticks. I've tried. Really. But, you know, I didn't start eating sushi until I was in college, and it was hard enough just getting over the idea of ingesting raw fish. 

Now, of course, I don't know what my life would be without sushi. I crave it. I "heart" it, if you will. But I eat it with my hands like a silly clueless white person. Many people have tried to teach me to use these handy chopsticks - to no avail. 

Most of the time, I get takeout from CU Sushi, which means I can bring the tasty sushi back to my office and eat freely with my hands without fear of judgment from all the normal, chopstick-using people. When I dine in, I simply grin and bear it - i.e, stuff my face without care. Because really, the sushi is worth it, and they have a bunch of creative dishes, pretty decent lunch specials and daily 50% off specials on select rolls. 

Try the "ultimate salmon roll," if you dare.

This location seems to have a revolving door policy with restaurants changing at a depressing and predictable interval. I hope Celia's fares better. The food, Quesadilla with Carne Asada was excellent, the chips hot, and the salsa tasty. It's a nice quiet place to sit down which this street as lacking. I'll definitely try to come back.

Had a chicken enchilada and the wet pollo asada burrito. The complimentary chips and salsa were delicious. Food was tasteful, burrito was HUGE! Took the food to go, the way they wrapped everything was very nice. Not the cheapest place, not the priciest. Not the best Mexican food I've ever had, but over it was good.

Celia's-- me and my friends are regulars. We've been joking that they're going to have to give us our own private table.
Anyways, this place is a good sit down Mexican joint. It is best to come at lunch when they have lunch specials that will run you about $8. Dinner will be a bit more, about $10 for the meal. A little spendy compared to other northside restaurants, but that's the price you pay for sit-down service and good food.
They'll bring you free chips and salsa and refill the chips. If you like, ask them to bring out their hot salsa or their green salsa.
The Fajita Burrito is fantastic, as is the chimichanga. And if you're in the mood grab a pitcher of margaritas -- one of those will get 4 of you a little buzzed or 2 of you on your a**es.

I don't hate it, but I definitely don't love it. The quality of tortillas is lame, the mole is not flavorful, and the fajitas are just a little too bland and spice-less. The margaritas aren't made with tequila (they're made with agave wine), so don't expect to get drunk on a Wednesday (believe me, I've already tried). If you want better Mexican food, I'll gladly make it for you.

There are 2 Mexican options if you are dining along this block of Euclid: Celia's and La Burrita. Celia's is more of a sit-down place that offers more typical Mexican restaurant fare. They offer you chips and fresh salsa as a free appetizer. Most of the entrees and burrito offerings are nothing to write home about. Pretty average. Décor is better than La Burrita across the street, but doesn't make up for the increase in prices to eat here. I'd give Celia's a solid 3/5.

I had a wet chicken burrito here, and I was pretty satisfied. It lasted me two meals and tasted pretty good. I wouldn't go too far out of my way to go here, but anyone from Berkeley knows that good Mexican food is hard to come by. This place will do. I wish I had tried the sangria, but it's worth checking out sometime when you're in the neighborhood.
Loved the food and the friendly service. We have been looking for a good Mexican place in Berkeley and have finally found one that we want to come back to repeatedly.

This restaurant keeps us coming back. 5 stars for the service.. We always know what we are going to get with the service and never had one slight disappointment. 
The food, is delicious and generous. Cheesy, but I'm not complaining about that. Shredded beef, perfection. My 3 year old daughter orders 3 things off the menu and eats it all. I have never seen her eat so much. My wife orders the vegetarian tostada, she says it is ok, but I know she loves those slices of fresh avocado on her plate. The prices are right too. We always stay below budget on eating out.

I've been coming here for years & hands down my most favorite Mexican Restaurant. Fiancé & I are regulars here since their location was still right off the exit of University Ave near the Sake Factory. I always get the same thing which is the Ceviche & Chicken Enchiladas. I remember the first time ordering their Fried Ice Cream, I died & gone to heaven or should I say I had a foodgasm. One of the best shizz I consumed. Sangria here is legit too. Affordable prices for bomb ass food. Not a college student but this place moved to a perfect spot by UC Berkeley where college students on a top ramen diet can afford to eat here. Love this place!

The food here is a-okay.  It's a good value for your money-- as in, it's a HUGE amount of food. The guacamole is bland- so be warned.  But the mango agua fresca is great.  We're vegetarian, and I definitely feel like they could have seasoned the veggies in the burrito a lot more.  But it wasn't bad.  And the beans and rice were good.  It's a lot of heavy food, but it's an Americanized-Mexican restaurant, so that's par for the course.

My girl and I moved to Berserkeley on New Year's and were stoked at what we thought was going to be a smorgasbord of Tex-Mex restaurants (it is, after all, California) but hadn't quite landed on anything that great in our four months (not that we'd been trying especially hard). Then we spied Celia's and gave it a go.  
Service was excellent, prompt and accurate.  Prices are quite reasonable and everything was delish.  I was especially impressed with the salsa: homemade and not watery.  
I would recommend for a third or fourth date (when you don't mind getting sloshy with your beau, also enjoy some intimate seating options toward the back) or a larger group.  Nice location, too.

Celia's offers a great variety of dishes to order and they have some awesome specials like the fiesta time which is an awesome deal that resembles tapas bars where you can order drinks and they come with free appetizers. 

Anyway, I had to get a California burrito because I've only had it once and it was in San Diego so it had pretty tough competition. The burrito was pretty good but it's a little pricey, although in return you get huge portions along with a constant refill of great chips and salsa. The staff were really friendly and funny so this place definitely gets a thumbs up from me. 

This was my first time there and I left satisfied. I'll definitely be going to Celia's again in the future.

Most of the entrees seems a bit pricey, but the vegetarian burrito is a pretty good deal for about $7. Definitely a big fan of the salsa here which kind of tastes like a combination of salsa and marinara sauce which makes it so damn good. My friend and I finished about 3 bowls of salsa, and I was surprised didn't place us on their watch list or something. Overall, a nice sit down Mexican place on Northside.

Decent, yet pricey Mexican food offered at a sit-down venue. 

If I could, I would give it a 2.5.
There are too main differences between Celia's and the other more casual Mexican food restaurants in Berkeley:
-Larger menu with more elaborate dishes
-Wait Service and less casual atmosphere

The food is not bad, but you shouldn't come to Celia's for a burrito. You can get a cheaper and probably better burrito across the street at La Burrita. 

The first time I went to Celia's I tried the Chile Verde that was listed under the house specialties. It was pretty tasty and had just the right amount of spice to it. The second time I got a 3 combo plate with tacos, stuffed chile, and a tamale. The tacos and the chile were fine, but the tamale was dry, hard, and simply inedible. I am not going to be extra harsh on Celia's about this as I have yet to have a good tamale in any restaurant in the US. 

The dinner plates range from $11-15. Service was always attentive.

Come to Celia's for a group dinner if you want a sit down meal. If you want a burrito, just go to La Burrita across the street.

Pros:
*friendly service
*chips and SALSA

Cons:
*food is too salty

I like it here. It's a little pricey though. One time I came here and ordered a quesadilla with a side of rice and beans... my bill was over 15 bucks! Not cool for a "quick lunch catch up with a friend" lol. But the food here is pretty good and authentic-tasting! Would have been 4, but 3 stars for the pricey-ness.. Nice to have have by campus though.

The first thing you must know about Celia's is that they do not serve real Mexican food. This means there's no grease, no extensive amounts of onions and cilantro, and the salsa comes from a jar in Safeway. TexMex it is not. Ceclia's far superior than Chevy's or Applebee's. The ingredients are fresh and everything is marinated to perfection. 

My boyfriend and I shared a large combination: chicken enchilada, ground beef taco, and pork tamale, rice, and beans. Too much food for us two! I think it could have been enough for 2.5 or even 3 people. The tamale was okay, but I think the taco and enchilada were much better. The enchilada came with a red sauce that seemed to have came out of a jar but it was actually a lot more flavorful than I imagined. The beans were delicious! It's hard to find good refried beans so I was pretty pleased. Cheddar cheese is sprinkled on everything, which isnt really Mexican food but more TexMex.

Chips and salsa are free here and served at the beginning of the meal while you look over the menu. When the food arrive, they bring out the corn tortillas and butter. The tortillas are amazing! Def. homemade.

Parking can be a bit difficult since it's so close to campus and involves hill parking so good luck, yelpers! 

I came here with a www.restaurant.com coupon...so $35 worth of food for four people ended up to be $19. YAY! It's like eating Mexican food in LA! I wish I can give this place more stars, but the facade of being Mexican and the slow service brought this place down to three.

I was excited that there is a Celia's on this side of the bay. Cute little street it's on. Never too crowded. Celia's is not the BEST place, but I've grown up with it since I was little and love it!!!! Yummy beans by the way.

Very good food and not very expensive! Just went here for the first time. The service is impeccable. We pretty much had two waiters on us the entire time.  Ask for their hot salsas when they bring you the chips, they usually serve it with the mild salsa. I ordered the enchilada and my girlfriend ordered the chicken burrito. Both were GREAT. I woud definitely come here again. Also
HAPPY HOUR 330-530 on weekdays with free appetizers. Would go here just because of that. I definitely want to go back  to try their Chimichanga,
The tortilla soup was very interesting as well. Do not hesitate to try this place next time you're wandering north of campus.

Celia's is a nice little Mexican restaurant that replaced a long line of not-that-great places on the north side.  They have complimentary salsa and chips, which are excellent.  I've never been dissatisfied with the meals I have ordered there, and am really happy about this north side addition.

There are more than enough places around Berkeley to pick yourself up a gut-busting, tasty burrito on the cheap.  That's not why you go to Celia's.  It's an unassuming, sit-down restaurant to eat something kind of like "real" Mexican food and have a pitcher of beer among friends and/or coworkers.  

If you stick to the basics, the prices aren't too bad (paid $6.95 for a fairly large polla asada burrito).  Taste was moist and flavorful.  I should mention that it was easier to eat the burrito with fork and knife than holding it with two hands.  And I was fairly pleased with their store bought salsa and enchilada sauce.  I'm a big fan of places that serve chips and salsa when you sit down and are thinking about what to order.  Pitcher of draft beer runs $15 and was good for about 4-5 pints.

We sat in a booth in the back where it's a little more dim and isolated if you're into that.  You can easily carry on a conversation without straining too hard to hear each other speak.  There's also a good amount of seating by the large window in front which brings in some natural lighting.  Service was pretty friendly and frequent enough without being intrusive.  

Probably won't make my regular rotation as it can get more expensive in a hurry, but wouldn't mind coming back for the occasional meal here and there.

This could be my new neighborhood...well maybe. 
Actually, my boyfriend works in the neighborhood so as I was picking him up from work one weekend evening we decided to eat dinner nearby.  
If It's the chain restaurant from the ones I've been to on the Peninsula I wasn't going to have high expectations.  It was just ok, as I expected.  
There were mainly college students, but it wasn't super crowded.  I ordered a standard 2 enchilada dinner plate and it was just fine.  Service was pretty prompt and food came out fast.
The owner messaged me to inform me of new (lower priced) menus, and other kitchen improvements. Bump up a star for now, until I get a chance to try again

I am incredibly excited about this restaurant. I am particularly excited for the exact reason that others have dismissed this restaurant as not appropriate for the fast food berkeley crowd. I desperately want a place I can sit with my friends, eat some snacks, and suck down some tasty cocktails - all this without trekking to shattuck or south side. This is potentially it! I had lunch there the other day to celebrate a friend's birthday and we were all really happy with our food. Yes, it's a bit expensive given the other options of the area, but its nice to have this option sometimes. Today I'm meeting a friend for happy hour, and I 'll report back on our experience.

Celia's is your basic Mexican comfort food joint.  Not authentic, not fancy, but the food is plentiful and good.  The service is sweet natured and the selection of beers is decent.  Good for satisfying your hunger at odd hours.

Just had their chicken enchilada and it was delicious!  This place is no-frills homemade Californian-Mexican food at its best.  I'm sick of paying $10 for two tiny gourmet taco truck goat cheese and pulled pork creations.  Sometimes you just want an enchilada.

Nothing trendy or innovative, but just plain good. The salsa is delicious and the enchilada sauce was just right.  Also, really friendly, speedy service.  

A little on the pricey side overall, but the small combos are a good deal.

Highly Recommend!  The food was awesome, and the margaritas were just as good!  It was my first time, and I had a $25 giftcard from Restaurant.com.  

The service was very good, and he was the only one.  We didn't have to wait long for our meal, and the margaritas came out quick too!  My husband and I really enjoyed ourselves, and will be back FOR SURE! 

Oh and they provide chips and salsa!  Which is a must at a mexican restaurant!

I use Celia's to cater group lunches.  I like to order large pans of beans, rice, meat, salad, etc. so that people can assemble their own plates of food.  This is particularly great if your group has a large number of vegetarians (their beans and rice are vegetarian).  

I also go to Celia's to eat on my own sometimes...they have a vegetarian menu that I like.  They also let you sub in black beans and corn tortillas which makes me happy.  :)

Had the shrimp burrito and it was A-OK.  The only issue was that the shrimp was overcooked and not very tender.  The atmosphere is good for large dinners and margaritas with a group of your college chum.
I went here a while ago so I dont remember any specifics. It's probably better than anything Mexican on southside, but not as good as things farther out or in oakland. sit down, which is nice.
their crab enchilada is great! i really liked their salsa too. service was good when they're not busy. didn't like the chicken chimichanga i got tho, so that knocks off a star. overall lovely.
My husband and I have been coning to Celias for 30 years! Service is fast, food is HOT, and most importantly good! The wait staff are always polite and engaging! Good margaritas too!!!!

My second trip here has done anything but lower my review, but I did make two slightly sketch observations about Celia's: 

My friend and I came in during happy hour 3:30-6:30pm and got margaritas. They are $6, a large portion, and super sweet! However, single drinks during happy hour are supposed to come with a free appetizer i.e. mini tacos, nachos, etc. and our waiter did not even mention that to us. Holding out, much? Fortunately, both my friend and I wanted to get full entrees anyways and we are also both extremely passive people so we didn't say anything, but we decided that it was not very honest that they didn't even offer the freebies. Perhaps they thought they successfully took advantage of us...but we're on to you!

Second, they don't card. 

As for the food, this time my pollo Mexican-style entree completely outshined the burrito I got last time. It has made me believe that restaurant "specialties" are really titled that for a reason, and not just randomly priced higher. The giant plate of rice, refried beans, cole slaw, with an additional tray of chicken sauteed with bell peppers and onions on top came out so hot--not spicy, but temperature-wise--that I could not touch the plate and I slightly burned my tongue on the first bite. But that didn't stop me from devouring it. I'm not quite sure I'll be back now that we have no more coupons to use, but Celia's has certainly increased my appreciation for non-burrito Mexican food.

chips and salsa was good.  portions of the food was big.  the happy hour menu looked like a really good deal (i think it was a free personal appetizer for every alcohol drink?).  service was a tad slow.  but their dessert was my favorite part!  i forgot what it was called but it's pieces of fried churros or something drizzled with honey and comes with a side of ice cream.  make sure you get an extra scoop of ice cream if you're sharing.  

overall - i'd most likely check out my local La Penca Azul the next time I'm in the mood for mexican.

Decent Mexican place, a lot better than La Burrita and a bit better than Mario's. For sure not a grab-a-burrito and run type of place. Love the colorful decor, not so much a fan of the prices. One of the better Mexican places in Berkeley, but by no means great.

What a shame that the historic location has closed. But at least the bar no longer need to compete with the drunk Irish at Brennans. I used to love going to the Celia's at the bottom of University. Having parties upstairs was the best.

The new location near campus is convenient, noticeably quicker, and the food is just as gourmet. I miss the house signature margarita mix that was on tap (literally a plumbing tap that came out of the wall behind the bar). 

My recommendation: try the carne asada tacos. You won't be disappointed.

When you live in the Fruitvale and end up at Celia's in Berkeley to have dinner with friends, there is only one word that appropriately sums up the whole experience.

"Meh."

It'd probably be two stars, if it hadn't been for the fabulous ladies I was dining with!  Food was EXPENSIVE, service was slow despite the fact that no one was in there at 5:30 on a Wednesday, and if I weren't in a lovely mood right now.  I'm feeling generous.  So Celia's, you take that extra star, you hold it to your heart, and you cherish it.  'Cause if I ever come back... watch out for my review update.

The friendly and attentive service almost bumped Celia's up to 2 stars, but the food was so terrible that I really couldn't justify it. My mole-covered enchiladas consisted of two tiny tortillas filled with dry bits of chicken and drenched with the blandest mole I have ever encountered. The tasteless brown goop to one side (beans, I hope) was covered with a congealed mass of artificially-coloured, radioactive-orange cheese. On the opposite bank of my mole puddle was a pile of overly-vinegary coleslaw. Not counting the beer, this was the best part of the meal.

The price for this plateful of mediocrity? $13.95. If you want bad Mexican food, save yourself some money and head to La Burrita instead.

My first experience here was decent. The tacos were pretty good and would agree with other yelpers in that aspect. 

The chile relleno are not bad they are disgusting. The mole had a good base, but what makes a mole, mole is the 30 or so other spices that have to be added. And those were lacking...so disappointing...

Its not overly expensive for a nice mexican restaurant, except its not that nice and the food not that good.

I like Celia's mostly for their wet burritos. I agree with other reviewers that they are on the pricier side, but the portions are huge! I always walk out of Celia's either with leftovers or feeling way too full. But I consider it a good thing!

Before your meal comes, they serve chips and salsa. Unlike Mario's La Fiesta, their salsa is not too spicy, and their chips are usually fresh. Service is great - someone always comes around to refill the chips or salsa. One time, four of us had seriously like 5 rounds of chips and salsa while waiting for a friend to join us. Celia's staff was so nice about it too!

Every time I come to Celia's, it's to get a burrito. The times when I've gotten just a regular burritos (without the enchilada sauce), I've been less than satisfied. So, minus one star for that. But the sauce makes the burrito so much better. Also, I love it when they line a glass of horchata with cinnamon sugar.

Overall, I give them four stars, because I think I get my money's worth here. Thanks, Celia!
I love Celia's. The owner and staff are extremely nice, and the food is excellent.

cute place close to campus.

Both ordered the taco salad. We've had better. Everything was kind of bland, and the taco shell was just ok. Nothing totally jumped out about this place. If I came back, I would try something else off their menu.

Jeff saw this restaurant with Esther on Cal day and hurriedly took a picture of it to show me. We waited a few months before we finally tried it. 

It is a really cutely decorated restaurant, with multi-coloured chairs and a cute cactus logo. The owners/casher was super friendly, and seated us quickly (because there was only one other person). 

We ordered just two tacos, because we weren't super hungry, expecting it to come with huge amounts of side-dishes, since it WAS $13 with tax and tip. But the portions were measly. The beans and rice were really good, but MSG-ish. Overall-- the food was decent, but it really wasn't worth it. I could have bought colourful Sony earphones from the Cal student store or 13 medium-quality pens!

We have given it two stars, because it shares my name. It lost all the other stars because it was overpriced. Paying almost $7 a taco is NOT our cup of pinata.

But CAL STUDENTS! There is a coupon in your planner! We discovered it afterwards, so... make sure you use it.
Good service, quick response on the order, food was average quality and a bit over priced.

I begrudgingly came here because my buddy loves this place and was in from out of town. I can't for the life of me figure out WHY! I love Mexican food but theirs is just not that good. It reminds me of strip mall Mexican restaurants in middle america. 

I ordered a carnitas burrito and margarita. The fried pork was dry and bland and the rest of the burrito was mostly rice. The margarita was weak and they use commercial sweet and sour. 

Its right off campus and maybe they run happy hour specials (20$ for a pitcher of bad drinks is not a deal) but I won't be going back.

Went to the new location after a million yrs of having eaten at the original place. (Maybe a tad exageration) Ordered the same mole enchilada dish I remeber enjoying but this time seemed a tad saltier. Are my taste buds changing or did the gloomy day , surrounding homeless peeps , and dirty storefronts affect the taste of my food? Not to mention we were the only ones there the whole time on a mid Saturday. I was a little disappointed with the old tasting "grilled" not grilled chicken in my kids quesadilla. I love the side cabbage dish but not sure if that's enough for me to go back unless I was in the area.

I just had tortilla soup.... The soup was decent, but the server took 20 minutes to realize I was alive. Then after he gave me the check it took another 20 minutes for him to come get it from me. I ate solo so I think that may be why. But very frustrating!

Went here during happy hour specials and it was a little slow. There was one other table at the time.  During the summer, I imagine they really miss the Berkeley students. 

My daughter enjoyed the black beans as she rolled them up in a tortilla and added some onions and tomatoes.

All in all it is not fancy but it is festive in Celia's. It is a good value.

No thanks. Visited this place Thursday 16th before a CAL Men's Basketball game. Only a few tables occupying the place and experienced horrible service. We interacted with our waiter 3 times. 1. For drink and food order, 2. us complaining about our missing dip 3. My party inrritated trying to get the attention of our waiter to acknowledge we had been done with our food (approx 15 mintues) and were wanting to get out of there. No refills or anything. Not going back there. 

Party of 4. All said their food was just so-so. I got the sizzling suprema fajitas (Beef, Chicken, Prawns) and the only thing Suprema about it was it's smoke'n sizzling action as it was brought to our table. The Prawns (shrimp, lol) didn't taste fresh at all, no RED bell pepper, four slivers of GREEN bell pepper (on heat for too long) and heaps of over cooked onion. I DO NOT plan on going back.
Picadillo (shredded beef) tostada salad is the jam.   Beans, crunchy tostada shell, picadillo, tons of melted cheese, a mound of lettuce, tomato and avacado plus red enchilada sauce.  THE JAM!

I've actually been to Celia's before they introduced their California Burrito, and I got a rather sub par wet chicken burrito. BF's vegetarian burrito was nothing I've ever tasted before, but actually REALLY GOOD. Nicely seasoned spuds and everything. Even though it's pricier Mexican food than I'm used to, Celia's (like most mexican places, I think) gives you HUGE proportions and decent, prompt service. 

That being said, this review is mostly about their CALIFORNIA BURRITO. And I have to say, it's not bad. The flour tortilla could be chewier and thinner, the burrito more packed, the cheese more melted, the fries crisper, but then, it HAS been 8 months since I've had a Cali Burrito from San Diego, and well, absence always makes the heart grow fonder. 

The only real problems I had were the carne asada, which was quite tough and stringy, and salsa, which I don't like in my burritos and specifically requested them to leave out, but I guess they didn't understand/forgot. 

In any case, it hit the spot. I'd definitely go back for it, even if it was just okay.

I was expecting something great from the newest restaurant in the cursed building that once held Asiana Garden.

Unfortunately, it's just not that great.

It is a proper sit down place which is a little jarring amidst the self-serve atmosphere of Euclid Ave. Of course, their main competitor is La Burrita Northside, and it doesn't exactly take a master chef to beat 'em. But they can't. They are not much better. While they are generous with chips and salsa, so is La Burrita. Celia's has a better menu selection by far but perhaps I just got the wrong thing because I just wasn't impressed.

Celia's could really steal the show if they improved their dishes and blew La Burrita out of the water. But right now they're far from that.

Taste: 3
Value: 2
Service: 4

Came here for lunch today, and got the carna asade lunch special with beans and rice, along with corn tortillas and an orange juice. It was okay, but it wasn't what I would call "good." Tropicana orange juice would have tasted better. Also, they apparently do not have to-go boxes, so I was forced to take my leftovers on a paper plate covered by some aluminum foil.

I have been going to Celia's for years.  First at the old location at the foot of University Avenue and the new location on Euclid near campus.  I usually go for lunch while working in Berkeley. They have a great lunch menu - very inexpensive and fast, efficient service.  Their cole slaw is fantastic and comes with just about every combination plate.  Their to go service is fantastic - it's fast and comes with all the items you would get if you were eating in house.  

But try it yourselves - I will keep going back again and again.

I have been a Celia's customer since I was 16 years of age. It was one of my mothers favorite restaurants. My very first margarita was enjoyed with my mother at this restaurant - old location.

Fast forward  location has changed but the staff hasn't. I love this place - On tap Margaritas and an awesome selection of options if you like seafood.
My favorite dishes are crab enchiladas and the crab nachos. 
This is great food and fun with my family. 
Whenever I am there I feel close to my Mother in heaven.

So this is the brand new location for this restaurant, and it could not have been a worse experience for me.  I order a burrito with guacamole and sour cream, should be a no brainer right?  First off, the bill comes out to $12! $12 for a burrito! are they kidding me?  Secondly when I get it, neither the sour cream nor the guacamole are inside the burrito, they just gave me two sides.   What am i going to do with two sides and nothing to eat them with? So i have to dismantle my burrito and put it myself in some sort of "build your own burrito kit."  Thirdly, why open up a sit down mexican restaurant next to Cal when 75% of your business is probably going to be students grabbing a burrito and heading back to campus?  Hopefully this is just growing pains and they can turn this spot around because La Burrita sucks too.

From someone who has eaten at Celia's since 1990 when the original location was on the pre-yuppy 4th street Berkeley, I can say that this recently remodeled, clean and authentic looks has not given up anything!
The food is prepared in a traditional authentic way so that everything on the menu is full of flavor. 
My favorite: the chicken enchiladas. With the best enchilada sauce it's a must try!

A recommended must try!

Yelp cracks me up.

I mean, seriously, guys? Complaining about $10-$12 for a full meal? If you can't afford to eat more than a cheap and greasy slice of pizza, don't go out of your budget then blame the restaurant. Besides, complaining about how much something cost when you knew the price going in--especially when it's not even particularly expensive--is just plain tacky.

Trust me, I've been there with the ramen and the greasy pizza and the quarter-counting. I'm not speaking as a snobbish rich girl. I just don't get knowing the price of something and paying it willingly--it's not like you don't have choices--then whining about being ripped off. Especially when it's still inexpensive compared to a lot of other places. 

Ok, my review. The fajita quesadilla is absolutely to die for. I pretty much order this every time then try samples of what everyone else is having, and so far, it's all been good. The tortilla soup is particularly memorable. I also had one of their giant burritos once, and enjoyed it (though I couldn't finish the whole thing).

Definitely one of my top three Mexican places in the East Bay.

I visited Celia's the other day for the first time.  I was there in time for happy hour, so the place was fairly full and there was a steady stream of people coming for take out the whole time I was there.  I was seated promptly and the service was consistent and attentive.

I like that during happy hour you get a free mini appetizer.  The margarita was very good and strong for me (but I'm a light weight, so it's hard to judge).  I got the Celia's Super special which is like a four item combo.  It was reasonably priced considering that it was only a few dollars more than a two item combo and I took the rest home with me for lunch the next day.  The food was great, excellent salsa, chile rellano, and rice. I couldn't really tell the difference between their enchilada and their burrito, but as they were both delicious, I don't think this is a big deal.

All in all, after spending a year on the east coast, Celia's you were my Mexican food, "Welcome Home!".  And a tasty welcome it was.

Food is bland, but not terrible--everything could have used more salt and spicy sauce. Chips were stale and lacking salt when we went. But the veggie chimichunga and burrito were fine, and everyone's portions were enormous. If you are hungry in the neighborhood and need food, there you go.

The biggest disappointment was the margaritas--they might have been missing the tequilla. Also, why have salted rims if they are served with straws? Mystery.

I've been to Celia's twice and enjoyed it both times. It's excellent if you're in the mood for Mexican but would also enjoy a pleasant sit-down. Prices are totally manageable and the food is quite tasty -- I had an enchilada and a tamale. The beans and rice were definitely above average, especially for Berkeley, which has a surprising lack of quality Mexican. Jealous of Northside: they get Celia's and we get Chipotle.

Delicious!

I came here for lunch with a CampusCred deal ($6 for $12 of credit at Celia's) and it was definitely worth it. My favorite is the Wet Burrito, which is HUGE and definitely lasts me 2 meals, even though it is like $9. 

Service is amazing, lunch is pretty quiet because not many people are up at northside, and they have some great chips and salsa. This is a great place for groups because it's very spacious. I would definitely come here again (especially with another CampusCred deal)!

It's hard to find good Mexican food in Berkeley, especially when you've been spoiled by SoCal like I have. While purists should probably stick to the Mission, Celia's definitely satisfies.

Excellent, speedy service, all the tasty standards that you've come to love and a few that you haven't heard of yet if you're feeling adventurous.

Celia would make an awesome mom.

My boyfriend and I spent a beautiful MLK day afternoon enjoying their happy hour, which can be enjoyed by others M-F from 3:30 till' 5:30. If you order a pitcher of beer (~$15) or a pitcher of margaritas (~$20), they'll give you a giant appetizer platter complete with nachos, chimichangitas, and quesadilla. With a glass of beer or margarita, they'll give you two fresh taquitos (little tacos, not the fried roll kind). So you're basically ordering drinks, but getting dinner, and the price reflects only one half of what you'd otherwise pay. 

And if Celia were my mom, I'd want our waiter to be my dad. He told us that making the margaritas was his favorite part of his job. That's the kind of role model we could all use.

This restaurant seems out of place on Northside because it is significantly more expensive than all the nearby restaurants. When you first enter, there is the option of ordering-to-go, otherwise you are promptly seated for dine-in. 

Complimentary chips and salsa come with every table. I ordered the sizzling fajitas supremas, which serves 2 people who aren't starving. Comes with beef, chicken, and prawns; onions, and bell pepper while the rice and beans come on a separate plate. The tortillas come in a container that keeps the tortillas from cooling too quickly; every place should have these! 

The total bill would have been close to $20 including tax, but thanks to Campus Cred's deal it was closer to $13. I'd recommend the sizzling fajitas supremas because it tastes way better than anything La Burrita has to offer.

Celia's just opened on the east side of Euclid, a few feet up from the corner of Hearst.  This is a location that has housed many a restaurant over the years.  None has been good; at least one was Mexican (c. 1996).

The new restaurant opened a few days ago, and it was packed today for lunch.  I asked the host whether they are related to the Celia's on Fourth Street.  The answer surprised me: they *are* the Celia's on Fourth Street.  More precisely, they got kicked out of their building, which is now a big hole in the ground, and they moved up to campus.

To me, Celia's represents the "old style" of Americanized Mexican food.  I think that I went once about 30 years ago and decided never to return.  But how can I resist a new place at the edge of campus?  So there I was today for lunch; there we were, in fact.

The set-up is that of a traditional restaurant with table service.  You get seated by the host, order from a waiter, and get served by the waiter.  This makes things potentially slower than at Nefeli, say; Nefeli is a place where you order at the counter and then sit down and wait for your plate to be delivered.  In fact, our waiter came over quite soon after we sat down, and our orders were delivered about 10 minutes after they were taken.  I had a fish burrito; my friend had a vegetarian burrito.  Both of us had the same reaction, which is essentially "meh!"

I don't expect to be back any time soon.  There's better food to be had in the neighborhood and on campus.  On the other hand, one never knows.  As I said in reviewing another restaurant, I won't resist all that strongly if friends want to drag me in for another go.
had the fish tacos, which were just fine, but the sangria was sub-par. the fruit had a weird smell to it.
Outstanding service, generous pitcher-sizes, homemade flan, and an unbeatable happy hour.  The only thing that could make it better for me is live mariachi! One of the best kept secrets in Berkeley!

Celia's in Berkley is a dream come true.

This isn't any cheap imitator Mexican restaurant. This is the real deal folks.

I've been going to Celia's all over the Bay Area and Celia's on Euclid has it all!

A tantalizing assortment of salsa to go along with the free chips.

A stunning menu including every traditional Mexican platter your little heart desires.

I don't drink often folks, but when I do, I prefer XX. . .AND THEY GOT IT ON TAP. . .You know I "tap" that

Great after class, in between, class, during class, or for a date with a pretty young thing or even with your Mom. . .Celia's is classy enough like a tuxedo shirt, yadig?

Plus they cater. . .Efficient and affordable.

WAIT! This is the ONLY place in Berkley with the So Cal burrito!

So if this isn't enough to convince you that Celia's of Berkley is legit, go test for yourself.

Philthy over n' out

Tried Celia's for the first time recently and liked it quite a bit. Good food, friendly service and great atmosphere. I'm not sure I get the comments about the prices: I felt like I got more than my money's worth here, and then some.

WOW. this place is for people who like their food to lack flavor. My boyfriend and I had lunch here. I like salsa with tomato chunks and this salsa was just soupy with a whole lotta cilantro. The chips were whatever. I ordered steak/chicken fajitas. They came out sizzling and i was ready to dig in.... FAIL the meat had no seasoning or flavor. So i thought, Okay I can work around that ill just add a ton of rice and beans on the tortilla and drench the meat with this soupy salsa. FAIL THE tortillas were so hard they were cracking. The rice was so bland ( and i love rice) My bf had enchiladas and these were probably okay just because they were covered in sauce. BIG WASTE OF MONEY

I went here for lunch one day while working on the campus. Keep in mind I was just looking for a quick burrito to take back to work to eat.

First off, it cost WAAY too much for a regular burrito. I just got the house burrito with quite regular ingredients and the burrito was just normal, nothing special. This cost me about $9.50.

I don't think I will be going back here when I can get an even better burrito from La Burrito for $5.99

Celia's is like a dream come true for the Berkeley resident.  A full service Mexican restaurant (not a taqueria), Celias offers a comfortable and friendly environment to eat large portions of delicious Mexican eats.  Tacos, Tamales, Chimichangas, Enchiladas, and your friendly burrito are all available, ala carte or in combination dinners.  The portions are generous and the hosts are friendly and attentive.  If you're looking for take-out, they are fast and prepare full plates packaged to go (paper plates and aluminum-wrapped to keep 'em hot!)

NOTE: I strongly recommend the ground beef tacos.  They're delicious and don't have "mystery meat" as filler - no sir, good bits of real beef.

Another reviewer compared this place with the rat-infested shithole that is La Burrita, to which I can only say - if you're interested in Uncle Ben's rice, Salsa you could squeeze-spray on, boiled meat, industrial grade beans and chips, and sitting on the can afterwards regretting it, well, you're welcome to it.

Me, I'll be across the street chomping down Celia's delicious eats.
I went here this afternoon with my boyfriend. Fantastic service, very large portions, and great burritos. Their pineapple agua frescas was delicious. :) Awesome atmosphere as well.

Celia's mexican restaurant is my favorite on a cold day in Berkeley! They have great chips and salsa, which always accompanies my DELICIOUS margeritas as i wait for my food to come. The food is fast, warm, and flavorful. The prices are good for how much FOOD you get. I don't think I have every completely finished a meal, but it makes amazing lunch the next day too. Overall, the waitstaff is extremely nice and they remember you, which makes my experience there always comforting and satisfying. I just can't go anywhere else now, because all the sit down mexican places in berkeley or in the bay area just don't compare.

You can get much better Mexican for a fraction of the cost, I had a mediocre burrito that came out to ~$9.  Instead, I could have applied that $9 much more wisely, to 2 much better burritos at a place like Gordo's, or maybe to 12-month CD (with the interest paid in burritos).  In any event, I don't think I'll be investing my money in Celia's again anytime soon.  

ps: If you're going to get a pitcher of sangria, ask for it without ice, otherwise they'll pack that thing full of the frozen stuff like like it was a sno-cone.

All my classes are on the north side of campus, therefore, lunch at Celia's happens.  Quite honestly, it wouldn't have to.  The food across the street is just as good, but cheaper.  The only reason they get away with charging so much, is that they have a large space to serve indoors.

Happy to say that upon my return, the service was at 100%. We were seated, had ordered, and were served in under 20 minutes. Food is still homey calie-tex-mex wonderful, and their margaritas are still the best. I'm a regular once again.

HORRIBLE food. HORRIBLE service. HORRIBLE prices (excusable had the food been better... but it wasn't)

Like many other UC students, I had excitedly purchased a CampusCred deal ($6 for $12) and was eager to try a new Mexican place around the area. I'm a long-time fan of Mexican food and have tried places ranging from Cancun to the taco truck at the Ashby flea market, so you can understand my disappointment when I found my food so unappetizing here that I couldn't even finish it. 

My friend and I had come here for dinner at around 6. We were quickly seated and given a menu and chips with salsa (so far so good). However, when it came to ordering, it was difficult to flag down a waiter and even after we told someone we were ready to order, had to wait another 10min. Later on, our waiter had to come back and ask for my order again since he had forgotten what it was.

We ordered the Nachos appetizer, a Chicken House burrito, and a Shrimp burrito. 

Nachos: the Nachos weren't bad, but not great either. The upside was that they were covered in nicely melted cheese (who doesn't love cheese?). However, they could have used a bit more toppings. There were barely any tomato and avocado chunks and I didn't see any onion pieces. I found them a bit bland, but I like heavily flavored things so I drenched them in salsa.

Shrimp Burrito: They should rename this the BEAN burrito. There were hardly any shrimp in here and FILLED with pinto beans. Like the Nachos, I found it extremely bland and had to once again drench it in salsa. Also, I cannot emphasize just how disgusting their tortillas are. Both my friend and I were a bit taken aback by its bland taste (It's a bit hard to describe, but imagine eating an uncooked wheat tortilla from Safeway). 
*Note: I had over half of my burrito left which I brought home and gave to another of my housemates. She also noted that the tortilla was horrible in comparison to that of Pauncho's or Chipotle. 

Chicken Burrito: My friend thought the chicken tasted and felt a lot like canned Tuna. I thought hers actually tasted a lot better than mine considering how it wasn't drowned in beans. She was a bit upset by the minuscule amount of guacamole they put in it (add-on). Like the nachos, there were only a few small avocado chunks dispersed throughout the burrito. Lastly, the sour-cream wasn't well spread out and heavily concentrated at one end of her burrito so when she cut into it, a giant blob of it spilled out. She ended up scooping it out and then just applying it to her burrito as she ate it.

**Note: One thing I have to give them is that their burritos are HUGE...

Perhaps it was the day or what we ordered, but I found this place very unsatisfactory and will probably never come here again. Although generally a good deal, I wouldn't have bought the CampusCred knowing what I do now about this place. For those of you reading this review, I hope you have a much better experience. :)

Our family has been coming to Celia's (of Berkeley) for over 18 years now, and it is easily our go-to restaurant. We've grown to adore the people that work there, the ambiance (even though they changed locations!), the food, and the Celia's food coma.

We typically order the cheese enchilada dinner plate -- very cheesy enchiladas with a side of rice, beans and coleslaw, ceviche tostada (omg yum), or chimichangas. Reasonable pricing and fast service! The chips and salsa are also very fly - chips can be stale at times, but we are usually so busy inhaling the salsa that we don't mind it! And holy crap - order the decadent, sugary cinnamony sopapillas if you can still handle it.  Service is sometime sub par, but it's all gravy because in general, this place just makes you feel good. :)

I always order the #4 combo plate.  I never stray from the combo platters, because they never do me wrong!  I could live on Celia's tacos and enchiladas for every meal of the day.  I've noticed most of the negative reviews are for the prices, understandable considering its next to UC, but it's not pretending to be a cheap taco-stand restaurant.  This is family style, sit-down mexican food at its best, and I wouldn't want it any other way.

Portions are HUGE! I took a picture of the plate vs. my hand...wow! The actual food was okay, but considering that it's in Berkeley and that it's really reasonably priced (about $12-15 for a plate) it's pretty good. 

My favorite is the fried ice cream. Definitely save room for that! MmmMmMMmmmm I am hungry just thinking about that stuff

I'm from so cal so I have higher standards for mexican food, so take my review with a grain of salt. It was not too impressive and I really didn't think that they gave THAT big of a portion. I do have a BIG appetite though, so maybe you should take that with a grain of salt too. Overall, I don't really recommend making a special trip to this place. Any normal burrito place would do and it would be cheaper. 

VERY NICE SERVICE THOUGH :)

First, this is not MEXICAN food but IMITATION. 

Be aware of Mexican Restaurants where the only people who eat there are not Latinos or people who cannot distinguish the real from Celia's type. 

My friend was very eager to go because she got a coupon. That should have been the sign (a bad one). A good restaurant is not going to give you coupons. If the food is good, people return and recommend it.

I'm vegetarian and my only few choices were "vegetarian" fajitas, chile relleno or tostada de aguacate. I asked what was on the fajitas, the waiter said potatoes, carrots and the rest (onions, tomatoes and peppers). Sorry, but not even my pet would eat something like that.

I order the avocado tostada which came with an oily, half-fried smelly tortilla (perhaps very old palm oil), a layer of fried cheese, a layer of avocado, some lettuces... I COULDN'T BELIEVE that cooks could get so creative and come up with something so disgusting. 

The chile relleno was a layer of cheese, a layer of pepper and fried egg, topped with canned salsa. You'll never find something like that in a Mexican restaurant in Mexico or in the U.S. if the restaurant is owned by a first-generation owner. 

Celia's is worst than Taco Bell. IT IS THE CHEESE AND TORTILLA restaurant and a real offense to Mexican food. I couldn't even stand the smell inside. I'd recommend you El Colibri in San Francisco -a gourmet Mexican bistro and 5-starts restaurant.

I came here again to try it again (and because I work so close to here). I did enjoy the carnitas! It was really good - disclaimer: I'm not a pork connoisseur by any means, but I didn't think it was too bland. It was soft but still had a bit of crispiness on the exterior. Just the right amount of flavor (non-spicy flavor), but I did add lime and salt.

I asked for the hottest sauce they had. Someone brought out this red paste-like which looks a lot more intimidating than it actually is. It's bright red but I really had to pour it on to taste anything.

Anyhow, the carnitas plate was really good and hearty for $11 + extra for tortillas, I think. I wouldn't expect anything to be spicy though. To be fair, I would really recommend this place to anyone who DISLIKES spicy food. For anyone who enjoys a bit of kick and heat in their food,  don't expect it here.

I'll have to agree that the decor is fun and colorful! I highly enjoyed trying to decipher the names on the back of the chairs.

I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at Celia's. We were greeted promptly, and in all actuality I had no idea it was a sit down restaraunt. Most places are casual fast food with diner style seating, but my experience was great! Everything was splendid, the deals, and the portion sizes!

The waiter was very friendly and attentive to us, never missing a beat! Service was A+++ and the food tasted absolutely great. La Burrita and Gordowhatever have nothing on this place!!

Great value, even better tasting food. I'm a fiend for chips and salsa, and their salsa is among some of the best I've ever tasted, and I taste a lot of salsa. Great robust and spicy, thick and hearty salsas, my mouth is seriously watering as I think about it.

I ordered the Chilé Colorado Expresso Burrito, included rice,beans,cheese,smothered in red sauce (wet :P) and topped with salsa.

GOOD GOD this burrito is like 12" long. It's awesome to get for lunch, and save half for dinner later on. That's like $5 a meal for lunch and dinner each!

One thing I have to note, if you are wondering if this place is a good place to eat, they have AWESOME happy hour deals. I only WISH I saw the happy hour menu before I ordered the burrito. Free food with the purchase of alcohol! Woo! -- Buy a pitcher and get the 6 soft taco, "Taco Tray". I think I'm going to buy this next time.

Thank you for such an amazing dining experience!

As of recently they have a new white rice with no meat stock in it, this is awesome. They also have a spicy green salsa that is much better when combined with their very mild red salsa. Service was excellent this time!!
Definitely more impressed than previously.

Disappointed.  I've had MUCH better Mexican food off of a taco truck.  Cam with my bf and we ordered two platters:

Camerones Rancheros - tasted like frozen shrimp (unseasoned) thrown together with some peppers and canned tomato sauce.
Cancun seafood platter - So full of cheese and sauce I couldn't even taste any seafood.

Wait staff was nice but overly worked.  

Utterly puzzled.  Will stick with the Taco Trucks.

I am ashamed to say that I actually ate here 3 times.  I don't know why.  I really want all that money back.  Celia's is one of the most expensive dining options around the Berkeley campus (excluding downtown), but definitely not one of the best.

Esp for dinner.  Do not go for dinner.  A meal is at least $12 or 13, which is ridiculous.

I won't say that the meals here are bad.  I even liked the burrito with a spicy red sauce, but I just like mexican food in general, and I would likely have been just as happy with the same thing at la burrita right across the street.  And i would have spent a lot less...

Stepping a few tree widths away from the frantic Northgate, just up Euclid, you will find yourself in Celia's colorful Tex-Mex restaurant. After living in Houston for the past 4 years, naturally I was ecstatic that a decent restaurant showed up on this busy student intersection. Today I sampled their first dish.  

During a research lunch meeting, chips and salsa provided the snacking atmosphere. Their lunch menu looked very reasonable. All under $10 for a main dish served with rice and beans. Vegetarians, be ware! Their rice is made with chicken stock. 

Today I had the Chimichanga Rice and Beans combo. Although the chicken is made from thighs or breasts, it was well flavored. The guacamole is creamy, wishing it was a bit more limey. 
I especially liked the decoration and the personalized cute chairs, they made lunch a break from the blend white. 

plus, they have horchatta.

I may be especially partial to Celia's because she saved my life.

ok, not really, but after arriving at Bakesale Betty's half an hour after closing, I was left hungry and hopeless.

I just wanted to go home.

Celia's is a block from my apartment, and I thought, maybe this will fill the hole left in my heart.


 Oh Celia, you seated me quickly. You're decor is a little loud for my tastes (think bright blue walls), but you provide me limitless chips, and even compliment me and my partner on our chip scarfing abilities. Yes, you are expensive, but you are tasty and your food could run laps around a La Burrita meal. 

Our food came hot and gooey. Only complaints I had was that the chicken taco I had was so juicy that is compromised the structural integrity of my taco, thus causing a taco break down. However, I was able to salvage the situation by using the complimentary tortilla chips and creating makeshift nachos. 


all in all, a decent sit down Mexican food restaurant, with slightly elevated prices, really friendly service and really tasty melon margaritas.
(which make all the day's disappointments seem miles away)


PS: I really enjoyed their horchata :)

No, thanks!

Sub-par food (so unmemorable that I can't even recall what I had), indifferent service, a creepy manager, and just an overall awkward atmosphere. One star for decent prices and one star for interesting chairs.

It's so "meh" that I got bored just reviewing it.

Finally getting a chance to update my review!  My prayers have been answered!!! 

Celia's now has a FULL BAR!!! Dropped by one afternoon for lunch like normal, but this time added a shot of Tequila to my lunch (shhhhh don't tell...it was one of those days!)  Well one shot turned in to two shots, turned in to three...(then I realized I had to go back to work).  

Can't wait to stop by after work for happy hour to try one (or five) of their many Tequila options!  

Like usual, great atmosphere, convenient location for campus and always fairly priced!

Your average tex/mex-ish mexican food ala Chevy's. I am told this place is also a tiny chain. But i have to say, i have eaten here four times in the last six months and it isn't just because of its proximity to my home. The food is good and filling. This is not a gourmet spot for foodie snobs, but a fill you up, enjoy it going down, take a nap afterwards place for everyone else.

What attracted me to this place wasn't necessarily that they served Mexican food or because it was the only table-service dining restaurant on Euclid; Instead, It was actually the brightly colored chairs!!  I loved how each of the chairs look like they're handpainted by kids with their names on the back.  Very vibrant in colors.  I don't think it makes the restaurant look gaudy; it gives it character.  I love weird eccentric stuff and I dig it.

I had the Carne Asada burrito for (~$10) and mannn was it huge!  Picture two normal burritos put together, but squished so that it's short and wide.  I had to eat it with a fork and knife. Meat was pretty juicy.  Other ingredients were standard: rice bean cheese.  The portion size well justified the price, but the burrito wasn't necessarily the best of burritos.  I'd rather go elsewhere for a standard sized burrito that tastes amazing then settle for a large mediocre one.

I just returned yesterday.  And again, a solid performance.  Sure, it's not super cheap for students (we split an entree and bought two drinks--came out to $20 or so), but honestly, it's nice to have a sit-down joint on Euclid Avenue.  The service was also very good.  They kept on checking in on us, getting us more chips, salsa, etc.  I'd give it a thumbs up, for sure.

Came here with my roommate tonight to use a $30 gift certificate. Since it expires today, we decided to splurge.

I ordered the Cuban Platter, which consists of shrimp, chicken, crab and mushrooms in a spicy wine sauce, covered with cheese and served with rice. The dish came out in probably one of the biggest plates I've ever eaten out of. However, I really feel like they're just trying to make you feel like you got your money's worth, because half of the plate was pretty much unoccupied. 

Everything was cooked well, but I just feel like the whole dish was lacking a lot of flavor. Instead of the extravagant wine sauce, it pretty much felt like I was given simple pasta sauce. The spiciness had a strange taste to it as well, just like the hot salsa provided at the start. For such a large portion, the amount of rice could've been bigger, and is it really necessary to charge an extra $1 for beans?

Overall, it was an alright meal considering it was free. I don't think I would pay $15 for such a poorly prepared dish again, but at least now I know.

I'm not sure why so many people are against Celia's.  I lived two blocks away from this place for a year, which meant I came here fairly often.  It's definitely not the fanciest restaurant by any means, but it's charming.  I'm especially a fan of the wooden chairs with names hand painted on.  I've always been able to find a seat here, regardless of the time of day.  They were also able to accommodate 30+ people for a group lunch with short notice.

When you first arrive, you are given complimentary chips and salsa, which are fantastic.  I recommended asking for the spicy salsa if you like heat, since it's great (and much more flavorful than the mild one in my opinion).  The staff gives free refills of both the chips and salsa, so go nuts!

I highly recommend you come here for the happy hour.  If you order one drink, you get a complimentary appetizer.  If you order multiple drinks (or a pitcher of margarita's), you get a complimentary appetizer platter with nachos, chimichanga's, and a small quesadilla.  

My favorite meal here, by far, was the taco salad with shredded beef and spicy salsa for dressing.  It comes in a huge taco bowl, and is everything you could ever want in a taco salad.  It's so bad for you, but so, so good.

Where this place shines is with their deep fried ice cream.  They unfortunately don't always have this in stock since they only make so many a day. It's a huge scoop of ice cream covered in a thick layer of cake, deep fried and covered in whipped cream and chocolate (or caramel, or both!) sauce.  It's absolutely delicious.  I recommend sharing, since it's very big.

I don't live in Berkeley anymore, but the fact that I miss this place should tell you how good it is.

For those of you who study my reviews diligently and have figured out how I choose what to review and when (there really is a pattern, but because of concerns about terrorism, I can't explain exactly what it is), I may switch it up a little bit in the near future.  Don't worry; I'm not trying to mess with you.  I really do appreciate your readership and fandom, but Berkeley and specifically many things Shattuck are about to get some serious John S.-review-writing bumps.  Hopefully.  This has nothing to do with Celia's, but you don't really read the disclaimers when they're at the end of reviews, do you?  I didn't think so.

Celia's.  That wonderful little unassuming place north of campus.
