I also ordered half of a turkey and pesto sandwich, which wasn't bad. The pesto really saved it from being ordinary. The sandwich saved this place from being a 2-star place.

Given all the other dining choices within a quarter mile, though, I have no reason to return here.

My coworkers and I were craving soup one day and decided to trek up to the other side of campus to go to SF Soup Co.  Who can resist a place that offers 10-15 different soups DAILY???

I decided to try a regular clam chowder ($5.30) with a wheat roll.  The portions are really decent for the price.  The clam chowder was pretty thick and creamy - the downer for me was that occasionally I'd bite into a not-so-tasty clam that left this gross aftertaste in my mouth.  Won't be ordering that one again.  I hear the Mexican Chicken Tortilla soup is good...

There are negative two tables inside so don't expect to be eating in.  

I also am not a big fan of pre-made sandwiches.  Yes, they're good for convenience and people who really need to eat on the go - but I like to see my sandwich made fresh.

Prices are reasonable, especially for students.  My sister told me that there's usually someone out on the sidewalk handing out coupons but I didn't see anyone that day, rats!

Will I be back?  Probably to try a different soup (with no seafood in it).

Picked up a freshly-made chef's salad here on my way to a lazy, sun-soaked afternoon in the sunshine at the Berkeley Marina.
Highly recommended way to spend your day.

All the soups of your liking all in one place? 
Why have I never been here before?

My co-worker had a Groupon for SF Soup Company and she really wanted to use it. Today was the ideal day since it was freezing and raining out. I have been fighting off a cold for weeks and have become addicted to soups, so this was the perfect fit.

The location is right on Bancoft so be prepared to see a mixture of UCB students and tourists checking out all the great cafes, stores, boutiques, bookstores, etc.

We scored a great parking spot right our front and must of got there right before there lunch rush, because there was no line. As we gazed the menu and took in the mouth-watering smells...the sweet attentive staff asked if we wanted to sample anything...

We  immediately said Yes as we were so indecisive since there are soooo many soups to chose from. 

                               You name it- they got it!  

The sample size is pretty generous.. I could imagine starving students going ridiculous by sampling each soup and not needing to actually pay for anything. 

A staff member suggested  getting 2 kinds since we couldn't decide on one. So I got the Tortilla Soup and the Turkey Chilli! Each soup comes with a large piece of bread or a roll. 

As you slide down to the cashier area there are also pre-made sandwiches, salads or you can customize a salad and beverages to chose from.  An assortment of condiments, napkins, to-go bags, and spoons of course.

Moments later there was a line out the door. We were so excited that we were able to get here when we did!!

The woman who worked the cashier was as stale as day old bread. She lacked personality and really made our great experience questionable.
I felt like she was the Soup Nazi, like the episode from Seinfeld.. she was very rude and not warm. 

There isn't anywhere to sit and my co-worker knew this ahead of time, so we took our hot soups to go and headed back to the office.

When we opened our bag of goodies... it was definitely worth the drive and the wait as we savored the warm flavorful hearty goodness!

I loved each soup equally and can not wait to go back!

Beware SF Soup Company, you are going to start seeing a lot of me!

"Well, I know you cannot tow my car with me in it".

Is the statement I heard from a middle-aged women stomping to her car on Bancroft as the traffic cop obviously caught her in some big trouble, they don't just tow your car for nothing.

The SFSC occupies a spot next to the line out the door smoothie shop. Even though there were a few people in line before me, it went very quickly. I ordered their clam chowder in a bread bowl (yes, the only full fat, non vegetarian, vegan, or low salt option) and a corn chowder for the hubby. I told them I was driving them back home for supper so they wrapped them in cellophane for me and bagged them up along with the spinach salad I bought with a gift card from their PR guy (Thanks Tom).

Walking back to my car, middle-aged lady is still in her car, the traffic cop has blocked her in and I can't help but chuckle. Returning to my car, the attendant could not give me change for a tenner so he gave me parking for free. Only in Berkeley could all of this happen in less than a city block.

When I got home, the soups were still warm and we ate them without having to heat them up. My clam chowder was mmm mmm good and I thought hubby was going to lick his bowl clean.

Great place for soup. Great place for bread bowls. Be careful where you park.

The lunch menu is amazing! You get so much food for your money. Both times I went, I had the peppered fish filet. The portion of fish was a lot compared to the rice. This is nice because other places just put a big chunk of rice on your plate with little food. The eggroll was average but it was a nice combo addition.  My friend also had the spicy shrimp dish and it was delicious! I will definitely try that next time. 

I love how they give you soup. This place is the go-to place for lunch if you don't feel like spending a lot of money in Berkeley. The food is really good for around $7! (: 

I went with a group of about 13 people overall and they owner and waitress was nice enough to accomodate everyone and got the food out fast enough for everyone to enjoy their food!
Pretty decent Chinese food! Bad customer service though.

Pretty good place to grab some Chinese food. It's what you would expect from South Berkeley; affordable, large portions catered to a predominantly college population. I have no qualms about it. I prefer eating here to any of the other comparable places in the Asian Ghetto (sans Berkeley Thai House because the owner is so friendly and jovial all the time!)

Good quantity of food, tastes all right, friendly service.

love love LOVE this place! I was looking for somewhere to eat and found this place on yelp and was impressed by the great reviews :) I decided to check it out, and I am happy to say that I loved dinner yesterday so much that I have since then already recommended this place to 4 friends. When I walked in I was greeted by the friendly staff and then escorted to my seat. I immediately noticed how clean the restaurant was, and although the outside looks drab and unappealing- the inside felt very classy but casual. A nice change for a college student on a budget. The menu had plenty of options that would seem to suit anyone looking for a great meal- and the best part is that they are pretty cheap but great quality. Even the portion size was generous. I ordered the Kung Pao chicken and I loved every bite. The flavor was phenomenal, and the texture was very pleasing. The vegetables were not under or over cooked, and the rice I ordered along side it as not mushy or not too dry. It was very nice. I have been to the other chinese places in Berkeley and after dining there- decided not to return. However this place is a gem! Please come and try Happy Valley, the food is great, the staff is friendly, the ambiance is refreshing, and the quality is superb. Definitely returning soon!

We were searching for a good chinese spot one night and this place came up in the yelp search. We were finding that it was really hard to find a good, cheap, cantonese style chinese joint in our area and stumbled upon this place. We were seated right away and noticed on the menu that they had salted fish clay pot and salted fish fried rice. Definite plus! There were too many other things we wanted to try so we opted for one salted fish dish (the clay pot), the salt/pepper fried fish appetizer (very good), and the dry fried green beans. The green beans could have been a little bit drier...they were still a little wetter than I was expecting them to be. But overall everything came out in a timely manner and in good portions. The decor is clean and casual and is big enough for larger groups. The price is very reasonable, as well. Parking wasn't too hard...it's street only but we managed to find a spot pretty fast on a Friday night. We'll be back to try the salted fish fried rice along with their other dishes.

This is one of the few times i write about a Chinese restaurant, it's simply because my standard for chinese food is so high that i dont bother to try much Chinese restaurants. 

But i've found myself came here three time already in the past months or so. I ordered honey walnut prawn the first time i was here, it was disappointing because the portion was small and it was overly too much mayo and the taste didn't really blend that well. The second time i went there, i got a dish of fried rice, the portion was really good and i was surprised at how much material they put in there for a cheap price. So i decided to go back a few weeks ago and ordered a simple Beef Chow Fun. I was watching the chef the whole time, and it was like a show. He made sure he went hard on the fire, heavy on the seasoning, and the noodle was not soaky like Sun Hong Kong's and not too dry like mandarin house's. I swear, he's probably a cook from China. 

I just wanted to write a review of them, so you know that there IS another Chinese restaurant choice around Berkeley, with a comparably better cook (:

THIS place is SOOO good!

Came with a friend and I ordered the Kung Pao Chicken wings, with Fried Rice and my friend ordered the Roast Duck. Let me tell you, the Roast duck is really good. It's not too fatty and bony, and it's almost just like the ones they sell in Chinatown in SF or in the Sunset. It's THAT good. The Kung Pao chicken was perfectly crispy on the outside and a tidbit spicy (so i picked out the jalapeno pieces), and there was just enough sauce for my rice. 
The restaurant was really clean and service was great. Right when i came in, they gave us a pot of hot tea and asked if we wanted water. They were very attentive and very nice. Got fortune cookies too :]

Their lunch deals are great, and take-out seemed super fast. 

DEFINITELY COMING BACK HERE AGAIN. Best Chinese Food in Berkeley, Asian ghetto doesn't compare.

This place has the best Chinese food I've had since coming to Cal (excluding my trips to Chinatown. Trust me. This gal knows her chinese food.)

Granted, it'd not as legit as say... actual food from china, but Happy Valley has asian ghetto owned.

The prices aren't bad, either. I paid roughly $7 for a fish fillet and green bean dish with 2 scoops of rice, and a "salad" (more on that later). Had I not taken togo, my order would've came with soup.

The rice was well cooked; not mushy, not too "chunky," and not "broken" (as chinese people say). The food wasn't greasy. The fish was suave.

The food is enough to last me for 1.5-2 meals. 

1 star dock off because the salad was a disappointment. I even asked what it was like. The server responded "like a regular salad with vegetables and asian dressing?" It was lettuce. ALL lettuce. (I make salads for the Food Collective. This "salad" broke my heart.)

btw, service was awesome :)

I got the General Tso Chicken lunch special with rice and an egg roll for about $7. The portion was big, I ate about 3/4 and took the rest home. It's a pretty cheap lunch, but the quality wasnt great. They give you complimentary egg drop soup..it was so thick, kinda unappetizing. The General Tso chicken has a really nice sauce that was ginger-y and sweet, but the pieces of chicken was mostly batter for a lot of the pieces. Egg roll was average, not that great either.

My friend got the kung pao chicken and he thought it was pretty decent although a little too much sauce.

Everyone says the food here is really good, so maybe I had to try something else. The black bean stir fried udon looks pretty good.

This place is by far the best Chinese food in the area. (The others suck--too fried, greasy, etc.) I have already been here twice and will go back many more times. I ordered the crispy ginger chicken for take-out tonight. It was great and even better than I remembered from the first time, especially for the price. (I've only had better at gourmet, very expensive restaurants.) Their take-out is very efficient and prompt! The first time I was here I ate in the restaurant, and the service was very accommodating and helpful. It is nice to be served at a table for the same price as other places that just call a number and you have to bus your own table. I highly recommend this establishment!

the other day my friend told me about this new chinese place that's been getting rave reviews on Yelp.  Turns out he was talking about this place and I remember having tried this place a while back when it first opened.  It's pretty shocking to me that its 4.5 stars on yelp -- I was pretty inclined to play villain and bump it down a bit by rating it a three... but I don't really have enough of a reason to.  As I recall, I ordered a fried rice to go when I went here and the cashier/server was very kind and polite.  The food was a little on the cheaper end and they made it pretty quickly (five minutes or so).  I have no complaints.  The restaurant itself looks pretty decent too -- clean & probably suitable for a nice lunch conversation.

oh, the fried rice wasn't remarkable, but then again I've never been a fan of fried rice in general .. so taken by those standards it was solid.

As good as it gets for Berkeley, at least!  This place is totally solid.  We had the twice-cooked pork, garlic chicken, and mongolian beef.  It's clear from the careful selection of vegetables for each stir fry combination, and the thoughtful choice of sauces as well, that someone in the kitchen clearly gives a damn.  I love it.  We saw what looked like really great salt and pepper pork chops going to an adjacent table- will definitely get those next time.  Please go eat here so I can keep having awesome Chinese restaurant near my house.

Nice to finally have a go-to Chinese place on south-side.  

We ordered Kung Pao Chicken and Beef Stew Claypot.  Both were really delicious.  The vegetables in my dish, the Kung Pao, were fresh, the chicken was good quality, and the dish wasn't greasy at all.  We also left with two containers of leftovers because the portions were so generous--always a plus!

Service was fast and friendly--found out the new owner is also the chef, something nice to support!

Wow, this place is really good. Surprisingly so. 

From the front it looks like your typical greasy Chinese place catering to students. Not so! 

I got the lunch special which starting with a delicious, filling soup (purred carrot I think?) It was creamy and thick, so much better than the throw-away soup most lunch specials start with. 

My main was just as good, crispy ginger chicken, which was perfectly breaded, crunchy, but not too much breading. You could taste the chicken, which isn't always the case with these fried dishes. The lunch menu was cheap ($6.50 with tax) and a big portion. I made two meals of it. There were plenty of more authentic dishes to chose from. In fact, I picked the only classic American-chinese dish on the menu, because I was in the mood for comfort food. Next time I will definitely be more adventurous.
Rude staff. Period. The food is far below par. I just can't find any place good to eat around Berkeley for under $10.00.
Great Restaurant! I go here for lunch all the time and I'm always happy with my meal and the service.

I'd been looking for a place with good Chinese food, and I'm sososo glad I came across Happy Valley. It's well-within my meager college budget, but is still a clean, classy sit-down place. My friends and I got wonton soup, chow mein, kung pao tofu, garlic chicken, and chicken with broccoli. Everything was 100% delicious. Particularly fond of their tofu. Omnomnomnom. The thing that I really loved about this place was the service. Our waitress was very upbeat, accommodating, and friendly. We'll be back!

I found a place to eat at where it's less crowded and cheap! ~$ 7-10 per plate for Lunch and dinner! And best of all its probable to take home another meal from your leftovers.

Wonton Noodle Soup- Real shrimp and none of that fatty pork filling in wontons! Soup is not oily, a few broccolis here and there, definitely perfect for dieters lol

Beef Chow Fun- Yes a little on the oily side, but it definitely tastes better than any Durant food court chow fun :)

Mongolian Beef- Lots of beef, sliced peppers, and onions.

Tea served free with every meal, can't get better than that. I'd prefer eating here than at Durant food court.

Solid Chinese food, reasonably priced, and nice dining area! I've been here a couple times, and each time the food has been decent but not amazing. Most recently, I got the HK style House special chow mein because I was craving some crispy pan-fried noodles. The noodles didn't disappoint, but the the meat in the dish did. The beef and chicken were very rubbery/tasteless, and the sauce was very starchy.... My bf got the Shanghai style sticky rice noodles, which were much more flavorful. (And this dish is also more unique) So I think the dishes here are a hit or miss.

Nevertheless, the place seems to be pretty popular among students, and I had no complaints about the service.

Food isn't too bad taste-wise, but it's not some quality dish that will blow your mind. Portions are just enough to get you full. It's probably better than most of the "Chinese" food restaurants around Berkeley, so it's not a bad place to choose to eat. 

There are many options for lunch specials here too and prices (in general) are standard ~6-8 maybe 9 for most dishes.

Took 50 minutes to get the food and it didn't come out all at once. 

Not good enough to come back, but they don't seem to be hurting for business. 

Say NO to the Mongolian Beef. It's cheap rubbery meat. The Crispy Ginger Chicken was good.
Best Chinese I've had in a while. Service is great, portions are large and entrees are reasonably priced. Id highly recommend coming here. Sweet and sour chicken and fried rice are excellent.

Food here is okay and it is a nice alternative to people who live on southside and are too lazy to trek to Lotus House.

I came here with friends and got the dinner special (supposedly same as the lunch special but $1 extra). It cost me about $7 to get the kung pao chicken (spicy but not enough flavor - tasted like it was just seasoned with salt), which came with rice and a sweet taro porridge for dessert. I was disappointed not to get a salad, so I think I would consider coming back here for a lunch special.
great service! delicious food! nice place to have group dinners or parties!

We had salt and pepper fish filet lunch special and chicken chow mein.  The chow mein was excellent and I really liked them because they were thick and chewy.  The fish was great, it was fried with salt and pepper and jalapenos.  Salt and pepper fish filet is one of my favorite dishes and so I always look for it on the menu at every restaurant I go to, and this was one of the best kinds I've ever had.

Happy Valley is pretty decent. The food tastes a lot better than a lot of other Chinese joints in Berkeley and it's pretty cheap as well. My boyfriend is very picky when it comes to Chinese food (he was raised in Taiwan all his life) and even he approved of it. It's a step up from Asian Ghetto in terms of food and decor but costs about the same.

I come here for lunch with my co-workers  at least once a week.   I've tried over half the lunch menu and have not been disappointed.  The food is very tasty and comes in large portions.  I've abandoned all my other local Chinese food places to eat here.

Happy Valley is an okay Chinese restaurant, but given what Chinese food options we have in Berkeley, it's the best we got. I normally go for the lunch specials and have ordered only a few dishes so far. The Basil Eggplant Chicken seems to be the best so far. Tomato beef is something that isn't really appetizing, nor the beef stew or sweet and sour pork. I had a Wonton Noodle Soup the other day that is good when you're kind of sick, but otherwise quite bland in flavor. Service can be so and so, depending on how packed the place is. It seems understaffed at times and food came out at a slower rate.

Great food.  Ordered the salted fish and chicken fried rice, garlic chicken, and beef chow fun.  Asked the server for extra noodles in the chow fun and the serving size was huge and they didn't charge me any extra.  My buddy said it was some of the best Chinese food that he ever ate.  I always order the chow fun at Chinese Restaurants and this was one of the tastiest.  Salted fish chicken fried rice was exactly what it was suppose to taste like.  Only wish this restaurant was closer to my house as I was working in the area away from home.  Prices are real reasonable, food was great, what's not to like.

I was ecstatic to find out that a quality Chinese restaurant was finally opening up near the Berkeley campus. This place is more of a Hong Kong style Chinese place. At times they seem a bit understaffed but the waiter/waitress is very friendly and gets you seated with a drink and soup as soon as you get in. So far I have only tried the lunch specials here, but if you eat there, they give you free soup and tea with your meal. The soup is actually pretty good unlike free soup at other places. I have had hot and sour soup and cream of broccoli soup here. The lunch specials consist of your entree of choice, two mounds of rice,  and a salad/eggroll, all of which fills a 12" plate. This is also one of the few places in Berkeley that serves roast duck! I have yet to try anything that I did not enjoy. This is the place to go if you want a good (and filling) meal for a good price!

The owners of Milanese Cafe decided that they couldn't compete with Ann's kitchen across the street and decided to turn their restaurant to a Chinese fast food. Not a bad idea, especially for a college town like Berkeley where kids want quantity for their buck.

I came here at lunch time on a Sunday and the place was pretty empty, largely cause everyone had already gone home for summer. The main gripes I had with Milanese Cafe was that the food came too slow, and the waitress messed up my order 4 times before it came ( 1 hour to get an omelette ), and this no longer is the case with Happy Valley. It does puzzle me how they'll manage a full restaurant as there is only one chef in the kitchen...

The food here is typical Chinese fast food. Two mounds of rice, with your choice of heavily sauced stir fry meat. For $6, it's pretty dang cheap. Not the most tasty, but nobody's expecting that for $6.

Tips: dishes feel heavy in MSG, and don't order the shrimp. They do not taste fresh.

Delicious chinese restaurant located below my apartment. What are the chances? 

Their beef chow fun is really delicious. I actually ask them to make the dishes with less oil and surprisingly it comes out with.. less oil! I've tried their combination chow mein and beef chow fun and both were very delicious. It may be due to the fact that I have not eaten fatty foods in months, but hey... tastes good to me! 

Their hong kong style chow mein is also very good. Consistently fresh and yummy ingredients. Their general chicken is also a hit (we ask for no ginger). Their kung pao chicken has an adequate amount of chicken and good ratio with the veggies. Very good!!

I am very happy they are open and I hope that these reviews helps them gain more customers! I would hate to see a new business go out just because this place isn't smack in the middle of telegraph near campus. Their chinese dishes are hella yummy and authentic. Try this place out!

Was a bit turned off at first when I saw a picture of "Strawberry Pork Chops" posted on their window. That brought to mind Panda Express, orange-sesame chicken chop suey egg foo young---fake Chinese food to swindle ignorant Westerners.

The Singapore rice noodle I had was actually not bad. The curry powder was fragrant; the noodles were well-cooked and not too oily, and the vegetables were fresh. Portions are not insanely huge, but enough to fill you up. The chefs working in the kitchen, chatting away in Cantonese, gave a sort of Hong Kong style cafe feel. They should offer Hong Kong style "silk stocking" milk tea.

Berkeley has always been lacking in good Chinese restaurants but I'm happy to have found Happy Valley, which ties with Vietnam Village as my favorite Chinese places. When I first tried the duck noodle soup I was disappointed because the duck had no duck flavor (which is probably not their fault since they buy out), but I've tried it again many times since and am very pleased with it. Happy Valley is Hong Kong style food with some Asian fusion choices like the sirloin steak udon noodles, courtesy of their creative chefs. 

Some of my favorites have been the black bean sauce fish, hainan Chicken rice (really yummy rice!), scrambled egg & shrimp over flat noodles, HK style pan fried noodles (either with shrimp, fish or beef), and the ordinary meat/veggie combo rice (just choose a meat and say you want a seasonal veggie with it). My favorite thing about Happy Valley is their rice, because it's not too sticky nor is it loose individual grains. 

You can also order things off the menu if you ask for it. I speak cantonese so one day I asked for milk tea and they mentioned that they had taro tapioca dessert soup and tofu-fa (a tofu dessert) too. The taro tapioca was really good and tasted like the one I eat at home; the taro was not mushy and had a good starchiness and it was not too sweet. Milk tea was also not bad. 

Definitely give the traditional Chinese foods a try here and don't be discouraged because there are few people seated inside at certain times of the day. They also have WiFi, just ask for the password.
still questioning why sweet and sour pork has the taste/scent of strawberry syrup.

Only go when they have corn soup! Call first, if they do, totally worth going just for that. Otherwise, the food is okay, the service is better than most Chinese restaurants, vegetarian friendly, that is why they get 4 stars

SO GOOD. 
And this is a lot to say coming from a girl from the SGV area filled with Chinese food options. I guess maybe I missed authentic food and the rest of Asian Ghetto just did not measure up.
I went with a friend during lunchtime for their lunch special. I got the Basil Eggplant Chicken with salad and soup. Delicious! This wasn't like those Americanized Chinese dishes, which I totally appreciate...Sorry Panda Express lovers. Anyways, friend got the salted chicken I think? I didn't try it but he cleaned the plate so I assume it was pretty good. 
I went after worked out so I wasn't really down to eat super greasy Chinese food. However, I still ordered the dish because I had been wanting to try out this place for a while. I ate as much as I could and really enjoyed it. The Asian hostess saw that I barely ate and asked if I didn't like it. I felt so bad!! I really liked it and when I brought it home my roommate ate it all...wiped it clean. 
This place is good for lunch specials and overall Chinese food for Berkeley. I will be back!!!

Place was the epitome of fresh, excellent Chinese food. Portions were generous , and very fairly priced. Myself and a friend enjoyed the chicken chow mein, with salt & pepper pork chops. Haven't had Chinese food this good since I moved here from NY 2 years ago

I came here for lunch with my boyfriend. We saw it and thought it looked like a new, better than average Chinese place, especially for the Berkeley campus area. 

We got the Beef Chow Fun and Kung Pao Chicken lunch specials. The Kung Pao Chicken special came with soup (corn and tofu soup), choice of egg roll or salad, and rice for 5.50. It's a pretty fair price for Berkeley, considering most places range 7-8 dollars per dish. The soup was pretty good and the egg roll was evenly fried and fresh, though there wasn't any sweet and sour sauce with it. 

The Kung Pao Chicken had lots of peanuts and was saucy which I liked. The chicken tasted good but seemed like there was less compared to the beef in the chow fun. A good plus is that there were two servings of rice given, I hate when Chinese places only serve one small serving of rice and expect an extra order for more money.
My boyfriend's Beef Chow Fun looked good and he said it was decent and nicely portioned in regards to beef, sprouts, and noodles.


There's complimentary tea, but it wasn't very strong. Better than getting charged though. The place was clean and inviting and the service was good though we were the only table there. It looked like the place is family run but I could be wrong! 

Since there's not there many good Chinese places on Southside Berkeley, I recommend people to try this place out if you want Chinese. This place is much better than the Chinese places on Durant/Asian Ghetto and worth the walk over. There are lots of Lunch Specials to choose from too, good for cheap students.

I am actually surprised that this place is that good. From looking at the pictures on the outside and the generic menu that they have inside probably doesn't do it justice.  
It's a little bit further than the regular food haunts 
I do recommend their specials board when you go walk into the place. 

I had the Sirloin steak Udon priced at $7.95. It came in huge portion size that was enough to take home for another meal. This was delicious. Steak was so tender and the sauce that they mixed the udon noodles with was so good It was a bit tangy and complimented the steak very well. Highly recommend it although this dish is more japanese fusion than chinese.

Also since its hot out try the fresh squeezed watermelon juice that's $1.95 that comes in a large venti cup. It's super refreshing! 

Service was really quick!

 They serve you complimentary hot and sour soup as well. 

I will be coming back to try more of their dishes and hopefully it will still be good!
Really nice people, excellent service. As a chinese, I have to say that their food is really good. I'd highly recommend their Mandarin Chicken Wings, taste absolutely amazing!

The lunch special (dish+rice+soup+salad/spring roll = a lot of food!) is offered on weekends! ASK AND YOU SHALL RECEIVE.

The food here is NOT BAD. For some odd reason it's really hard to trust the UC Berkeley Chinese restaurants. I don't know! But this place gets better and better with each visit.

They have round tables now a more realistic Chinese meal experience, and the largest table can fit about 8-9 people.

We came on a weekend for lunch and there weren't many guests. Ordered the spicy basil chicken and was quite impressed. The portions were quite generous when you get the lunch special. They also allowed us to have separate checks, which is extremely uncommon nowadays.

When they first opened, but probably would have given them three stars, but now that they've been established for a bit, I think that a solid 4 stars is a pretty accurate rating.

The Chinese food they serve is pretty good! Not amazing, because I've certainly had better, but in comparison to the other Chinese food restaurants in the local area, pretty darn good. Less fast food oriented, and more traditional that most other places. Not only that, they don't just stick to their menu items; they have a billboard with new dishes that they offer, including Shanghai rice cakes and Hainanese Chicken Rice.

Which brings me to the main reason that I finally decided to write a review. I grew up eating Hainese Chicken Rice from a restaurant in SoCal that specialized in making that dish - so I'd like to think that I know the difference between good and bad HCR. I ordered it today when I walked in on a whim, because I wanted to see if it was good or not. After all, it's not like I've seen any other restaurants in Berkeley offer the same dish. I had low expectations, because I've never been able to find a decent HCR dish anywhere since, but to my surprise, it was actually not too bad! It was actual Asian-style chicken with chicken flavored rice, and even came with a grated ginger and scallion dipping oil. The rice a bit less flavorful than I would have liked, but it will do. Sadly, the dish didn't come with the traditional chili sauce that is usually served with it ): ): 

But other than that, I've also tried their Wonton Noodle Soup, their Salted Fish fried rice, and their Beef Chow Fun. Not bad - big portions and I have no complaints. Only other thing I don't like is that I wish their menu was in both Chinese and English. Sometimes I can't tell if the dish that I'm looking for is the one that is described in English on the menu.

But other than that, when it comes to getting Chinese food within walking distance of the campus area, I'd prefer coming here over anywhere else

Cheap Chinese food! Something surprisingly hard to find in Berkeley... With its large Chinese population at UC Berkeley. 

If you're Chinese and are searching for that cheap, go to restaurant, wait no longer! Happy Valley is the restaurant to go. It located on the corner of Dwight and telegraph and has replaced cafe Milanese which was an awful Italian restaurant..

I walked by last week to book a reservation for Racha Cafe and saw this new Chinese restaurant called Happy Valley. I was a little skeptical cause of its name, but I decided to search it up on yelp.com and reviews were pretty good, I made sure the good reviews were from Chinese people though, which there were a few good  ones. 

I gave it a shot and went in to look at there menu. They have a huge menu, I felt like I wanted to try everything! There was walnut shrimp, eggplant chicken, hot and sour soup, kung pao chicken, beef chow fun and more! O was stressing over what to choose! O ended up going for my favorite food.. Basil eggplant chicken! I love Chinese eggplant anything. 

I got it to go and then met up with my girlfriend to eat. She went to Le cheval and we both just ate there.

I opened up my food and it smelled amazing! There was a egg roll included which was a plus. It wasn't as good as the eggrolls as the ones at Northern California Pre-Pharmacy Symposium or NCPPS, but it still not bad. My mouth was watering as I begin to  dig in. Bite by bite, I began to devour that eggplant! It is Hans down the best eggplant I've had in Berkeley. I've had eggplant from Mandarin House, Lotus House and Thai Basil in Asian Ghetto but nothing can compare. Sometimes the eggplant doesn't have any flavor other times its not cooked to the right softness, but at Happy Valley, it was just perfectly made. Yum! Yum! However the eggplant was quite oily, so towards the end it felt a little disgusting but none the less I still finished it cause it was that good! I will try something different next time I go.

I suggest ya'll go check it out cause there aren't any other affordable Chinese Restaurants around UC Berkeley!! Happy Berkeley Valley!

I really enjoyed their food.

I ordered the Chicken Kung Pao Chicken lunch special with an egg roll and steamed rice. I hate mushy rice that sticks together, I've seen a lot of that at other Chinese places. This one was very well cooked. The best part was that the chicken was not overly greasy. It was somewhat spicy so I took out some of the hot pepper pieces. The egg roll was ok. Did't have any problems with it but it wasn't spectacular. 

They have pretty good lunch deals similar prices to what you would find across the street at Pene Pasta. Most meals are less than $7 with taxes included. The service was great, the food came out very fast and the cashier was very polite. 

Around the area I think there are three other Chinese restaurants, the cheap take out place on Channing(?) across from Unit 3, I think its called Chinese Express and the two place at Asian Ghetto. This one is the best out of the three.

Came in with a large group of 13 people, but I was disappointed that there were no circular tables like at traditional chinese restaurants. Also the menu's are all in english, although I guess I'm not surprised. This place is still a great destination for chinese food on southside. 

Ordered a bunch of dishes:
Westlake beef soup - not too peppery, lots of flavor, highly recommended
Honey walnut prawn - portions smaller, tasted fine
Beef with broccoli - decent ratio of beef to broccoli
Cashew chicken - average
Twice cooked pork - too starchy, better off getting something normal
Dried fried string beans - good vegetable dish, can't go wrong
Mixed seafood with tofu - delicious seafood, squid, shrimp, and tofu, recommended

Rice is charged by the bowl which is frustrating for those rice lovers; however, we managed to negotiate for a large bowl of rice.

I'll be back to try out the lunch special everyone raves about.

Really nice people. I'm writing this review from inside the restaurant. 

I never write reviews about the product -- I usually know what I'm getting when I walk in. Service is everything. 

First time I came in months ago, great service, huge portions (they let me substitute chow fun instead of rice for the lunch special for free). Second time I came in, they charged me 50 cents for the substitution, even bigger portion than the first time. Third time, it was really busy. The server was over loaded, and we ended up waiting a long time before they took our order. My husband was upset, but since they were so great before, we tried them again since, and service was fine.

They were great again tonight. 

I walked in and ordered, and pulled out my computer as I waited. The server came over and handed me a piece of paper with the wireless password on it just because he saw me pull out my computer. Didn't have to ask. 

I came here this evening because I locked myself out of my apartment and needed dinner and a place to wait for a while. They are letting me sit here even though I finished eating ages ago. Food was good as usual. I ate quickly, but they are still refilling my water and checking on my tea even after I paid. At this point, they could ignore me, but they aren't. 

I didn't tell them I locked myself out; they're just this nice. 

They got a big tip for being great and making my hectic day a little more peaceful.
Reasonably priced Chinese food that actually tastes good! And the lunch special is great, soup, spring roll and entree with rice. And they take credit card. I'm sold.

Nice, clean environment and pretty decent food- the closest you can get to Southern Californian Asian in Berkeley.

The waiters are incredibly attentive, and their lunch specials are a sure thing for any starving Cal student.

Their fried rice and chow mein portions are huge, and the mushu pork/beef w/ Chinese pancakes is their signature dish. Make sure to grab it at least once here!

All in all, a clean, fast restaurant that doesn't load up your food with heavy sauces or MSG like some of the other restaurants in Berkeley, and where customer service is pretty good too.

I've heard a lot of good things about this place, but was kind of disappointed. I got the  chicken chow mein and the beef stew and wonton noodle soup. It wasn't really seasoned enough, sadly. The staff was nice though and speak Cantonese and English.

NO MANDARIN GARDEN, I REFUSE! I'm coming here!

There are a lot of times when I'm craving Chinese food, and I had to resort to places like Mandarin Garden, which isn't good. When Happy Valley was opened, I was skeptical of the quality of the food due to its plain exterior. One day, I gave it a try and it was bomb. The crispy ginger chicken - title says it all. The chicken has a good crisp to it and they use fresh ginger!!! I love their Kung Pao Chicken, though I could use a little less veggies. Overall, get the lunch combo when you can - so much food! You get a side of rice, meat entree, egg roll, and egg drop soup for a really great deal ($5.95 at the least). It get super expensive at dinner time though :(

Service: it depends on the crowd. However, your meals come out pretty quickly and they never fail to get your orders wrong. The older server tends to rush things and she COULD things put more gently on the table - but I usually don't care when I am starving.

The portions were good size and the food could have been decent... except my taste buds were shot and my stomach was killing me from the bleach they used to mop the floors when we first sat down. Then they did it again while we were eating. ...And my cousins chicken was almost all batter?

Awesome, cheap Chinese-American food! Great for late-night takeout. 

First off, THE RICE. Typically at these types of restaurants, the long-grain rice is dry, crumbly, and inedible. But Happy Valley's rice is fragrant and has just the right amount of stickiness for long-grain rice. I could eat bowls and bowls of it alone.

The fish fillet with black bean sauce was delicious -- fish was delicate and well-cooked, and the vegetables were tasty as well. My friend had the  ginger crispy chicken, which was tangy and zesty. Both dishes came with HUGE portions, but were easily downed because they weren't heavy or overladen with MSG and other seasonings. 

I'm definitely coming again!

Happy Valley truly made me happy today (:

I kind of really dislike all the chinese food restaurants in Berkeley because honestly, they all taste pretty gross. Whenever anyone asked me what I wanted to eat, I would say, "Anything but Chinese or Korean."

That is why I was skeptical when my friends told me that this place was bomb. But now I belieeevveee!

I went today (Sunday) at 12:30 pm. The restaurant is very clean and spacious, unlike most of what you see in south-side Berkeley. They give you tea right away when you sit down and it's free! The tea had a deep brown color to it, but it kinda tasted like tap water plus a little bit of tea flavor ): 

The waitress was super nice and helpful. Although the lunch specials (entree+salad or egg roll+hot and spicy soup+rice) say Monday-Friday, 11-3pm, she said we could still order off of it. I'm not sure if this is what they'll keep on doing or whether it's just for now.

I got the Hot and Spicy Eggplant (~$6), which was so good! I loved it. And it was a huge plate so I ended up only finishing the eggplant and salad. Left some of the soup and rice behind. My friend got Chicken Chow Mein (~6) and it was huge. SO HUGE. Like you could eat yourself full and take home lunch for tomorrow. 

The bill came out to $13 and change since my friend ordered a drink. Left a generous tip and came out very happy (:

Come here! It's not a very far walk from Asian Ghetto...and the food is definitely more yummy and clean-tasting.

Want to eat at Panda Express in the East Bay without driving to El Cerrito?  Well, you could come to Happy Valley.  In addition to having a superior name, they have similar prices ($6-$8 lunch specials), larger portions, and somewhat better food than everyone's favorite two-tone bear named chain.

However, as I recall, the service was rather slow, which I suppose could have easily just been the day.  Either way, it's worth a shot.

Excited there was a new chinese restaurant, seeing that the only other place I can think of is Mandarin House in the Asian Ghetto which is super gross and Great China which is in downtown, busy and kind of expensive. Definitely keep going back. The service is great- they're super nice! It gets a bit pricey for dinner but tastes good! :) 
Hope it sticks around!!

I've been here a couple times with my BF and ordered:
1. Peking pork chop- not what I was expecting. Not the super red sauce and thick but more thin and a lighter sauce. It was still good but I really want to find a place that serves the first one up here

2. Mandarin angel wings- chicken wings, pretty good. Be careful there were a few tiny specs of extreme spicy peppers in there but generally not spicy at all. They were pretty good but I wasn't super a fan of the flavor. Not fantastic but not horrible. Would order again if I was feeling for chicken wings. 

3. Roasted Duck Noodle Soup- I got this to go and it was HUGE! I mean they packed in a whole bunch of noodles and lots of duck! The duck wasn't super meaty but it was good and had enough. This is definitely not a soup you should eat by yourself like I was trying to. Definitely share this one! I felt it was more like the type of soup you're supposed to share at the beginning of the meal. Also note to self, don't spill on yourself because it kind of has a strong smell and I spilt all over my pants at work.... wasn't too great :( Would definitely get this again.... as long as someone else shares with me! :)

4. Honey Walnut Shrimp- who doesn't like honey walnut shrimp? It was a bit on the skimpier serving size but they charge a few dollars less that most places. I think that is why there's less in there than you would expect. They were good though, tasted like what I expected. Still a bit too expensive for what it is but if you're craving it, it's good. Can't really share- good for one person. Two people if you've order lots of other things and aren't going to eat this as your main.

5. Hong Kong Style Beef Chow Mein- I thought "Hong Kong" style meant the skinny crispy noodles but it wasn't exactly what I wanted. It was a bit too crunchy for my liking and even when I tried to mix it all together to make it softer, it was a bit too hard :( Would NOT order this one again.

6. Wor Wonton Soup- I looked up the difference between "Wor wonton" and "wonton" the "wor" is like a "supreme" with extra stuff in it. Lots of wontons in the soup and they were pretty good-fillings were not skimpy; I was actually eating a wonton! (Unlike lots of places where they're really small and nothing inside) There were other things in the soup, lots of veggies and shrimp. Definitely can feed at least 3 people with this. (with seconds)

Contrary to a lot of other reviews of this place.. I actually don't like the food here that much. I agree that it is a step up from Lotus House, but I would definitely prefer to go elsewhere for my food. 

But the two times I've been here, I've had a singaporean noodle dish, and a lunch special (with roast duck). Both portions were huge, and they give generous amounts of noodle or rice with whatever you order. The Singaporean noodle dish had lots of eggs and pepper and random vegetables inside, and the roast duck was very fatty. 

Overall, it's a good place to go if you want to eat a lot and don't really care about what you eat. 

Also, they give great fortune cookies here! Great messages + sweeter tasting than normal ones.

Nice, clean Chinese restaurant with some interesting new dishes in addition to traditional ones.

I came here for lunch and had the basil eggplant chicken lunch special and it was really good!  It was quite spicy and actually had a lot of basil, unlike most restaurants that are skimpy on spices.  It came with a soup and a salad, and my leftovers were enough for dinner the next day (and it was still good)

I would prefer to have another soup besides the sweet and sour soup though, just because that's what they always have at Chinese restaurants and I've gotten sick of it since I was a kid.  Something like the tofu or corn with egg white soup would be better, at least in my opinion.

Service was nice: the lady was very friendly.  The setting was nice and spacious.

Overall I think this is the best Chinese food in Southside.  (besides when my mom brings me food)

Best lunch special I have ever encountered.  It's not because they give you a ton of food, which they do, but more because the quality of the ingredients is top notch.  Real piece of chicken in sizable denominations decorated my plate along with huge spears of eggplant.  If only I were not leaving Berkeley!  This food is almost good enough to make me rethink my move.  Well, almost.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here for a dinner reunion with an old friend. I was surprised to find that this restaurant had replaced the Italian place, but hey, I'm a fan of Chinese food.

There was plenty of seating at 7:15 PM, so we were seated quickly and handed our menus and a pot of tea. The food is decently priced for dinner (it's not THAT cheap, with entrees around $7 - 9). My friend and I decided to family-style our meal with two entrees and a serving of rice.

Our bill was $17.43 (or somewhere around there), and we left $20. At $10 a person, it was a decent meal. Also, they bring you fortune cookies with your bill, which was an added bonus for me. My fortune had something to do with moderation...very profound...

|| F O O D ||

CHICKEN WITH SALTED FISH AND TOFU CLAY POT: stringy chunks of dark meat chicken with blocks of hard tofu and fish, topped with green onions [$8.50]
- There was fish in here? I didn't even notice haha. The chicken was pretty good though, although they cut the chicken into weird long chunks. I think it's chicken thigh.
- This dish was pretty salty, especially in comparison to the noodle soup. Perhaps they meant to say "chicken with salt and tofu," not chicken and salted fish :P
- Tofu was amazing. I love tofu.

ROAST DUCK NOODLE / FUN NOODLE SOUP (no joke, that is what it says on the menu): roast duck, broccoli, vermicelli noodles, broth, green onions [$6.95]
- They give you lots of roast duck pieces! They're pretty fatty though.
- The broth is unsalted and un-MSGed. Good good.
- They could have used better noodles in my opinion. The vermicelli was too tough.
- Broccoli! Awesome addition!

|| C L O S U R E ||

Good food, good (but not extraordinary) prices, and fortune cookies. I would highly recommend the roast duck noodle soup, as it is filling for a very good price--and there's roast duck! Would return if I'm craving Chinese food and don't have patience to wait to go home...or maybe for their lunch specials.

Responding to a quick tip from Yelper, Tammy S., my boss and I strolled over the Happy Valley. 

We were greeted by a friendly young man and seated near the window to be entertained by the street folk that hang out at Dwight Way and Telegraph Ave (which is OK). The store is nice and clean, unlike what you find in the Asian (Food) Ghetto on Durant St.

My boss opted for the Kung Pao Rice Plate and I, like Tammy S., ordered the Roast Duck Plate. Most excellent choices that left each platter clean. The bill $15 and some change!

It is several blocks from campus, however, after the meal, we did need to take a walk!

The Honest Truth: They give you free tea! And its a good place to have a sit down lunch or dinner.  They're food is decent, but I don't know why most of my friends are raving about it.  I would say that both price and quality are equivalent to Lotus House or any other standardly okay chinese place in Berkeley.

The Details:
I came here for lunch with my friend.  It was decently priced and they had lunch specials (always a plus!).  I ordered the crispy ginger chicken (lunch special) and my friend got the Roast duck noodle soup.  The lunch special wasn't bad.  The soup was eggdrop soup with corn in it.  It tasted like a standard lunch special soup and mine had a clump of corn starch in it.  They also give you a typical lunch special salad (the lettuce was a little large).  The chicken was good.  It was a little saucier than I would have liked but it had good ginger flavor and it was nice to eat.  Towards the end I got a little tired of it though.  The roast duck noodle soup was good.  The soup was clean and simple, but nothing amazing.  They give you a lot of roast duck, which is good.  The noodles were mushy and were overly soft.  Overall, I like the environment and theres plenty of seating.  I'll have to give it another try, but for now, its just another decent place to eat in Berkeley.

Heck to the yeah! Finally! A good chinese place to go for lunch. I had the duck over rice plate lunch, and it comes with steamed broccoli, an egg roll, and hot and sour soup (they even gave me a duck leg!).

Nothing fancy, but considering what you get in the Durant Square chain of bad food, this place rocks and satisfied my roast duck craving. It's on the corner of Dwight and Telegraph that used to be a skate shop, I think (or maybe it's next to it), so it's a bit of a walk further down Telegraph than I'd like to go, but for the price and quality, I will be back many more times.

This is definitely not the best Chinese restaurant ever. But most certainly, this is the best Chinese restaurant in Berkeley. After eating the dog food they call Chinese food at the Asian ghetto, you begin to appreciate Chinese food that is even just slightly tasty and authentic. Happy Valley is actually pretty good, not just some "ak-gwai-loh" (fool white man) Chinese food. It's funny as hell how asian people call fake chinese food "ak-gwai-loh" chinese food lololol. Anyway, this place is cheap as shit. Literally. It's as cheap as literal shit, and tastes like the SHIT!!!!!!!! The service is also bomb dot com. The 2 waiters there were SUPER courteous, some of the nicest people I've met in my life. All-in-all, it was a great experience and Berkeley definitely needs a decent Chinese restaurant. I went with a friend, got the westlake beef soup, salt and pepper pork chops, salty fish chicken eggplant clay pot, 2 rices, and it was still only $26 bucks, $30 out the door after tip. Darn good deal if you ask me.

I'm pretty glad that there's a new Chinese restaurant in these parts. While it's perfectly fine to do take-out, this isn't one of those joints with food laid out in bins. This is a true sit-down place with noodle entrees and dishes to share family-style. Unfortunately, I didn't think the portions were that big, especially for the price. I had the Peking Pork and the Kung Pao Beef, both of which are a complete mystery to me. The Peking Pork came in huge pieces and was well-coated, which was good. The Kung Pao Beef was very wet and soft. The couple of meat dishes put me at $16.80 and the same would've costed no more than $10 at a fast-food joint. At least the service is fast and friendly. At least the restaurant is clean and as new as it was left by the previous restaurant.

Finally got to grab lunch here after hearing so much about it!

This is really a grab-n-go place because theres no seating inside. I got the Venetian with penne and bolognese & sausage. I see everyone's complaints that they had to wait so long for their food but I think I only waited about 5 minutes for my food. The food came out really hot and fresh. The sauce was really tangy and bit spicy and was super good. My biggest disappointment is the pasta, because i really dislike pasta that isnt al dente, and this was a little overcooked for my taste.

It was $4.95 with tax already and it was a good portion. I'm definitely coming up to try their pesto chicken pasta!

Pasta? IN A BOX!?

I really do hope this Italian establishment grows to be a quick and easy place for people (especially students!) to come and pay $5 for a good portion of food! 

After walking into what seemed to be a quiet, overlooked grab-and-go eatery, I glanced over their menu displays and decided to order the Venetian (Italian sausage and bolognese sauce). What can I say? it was good pasta at the right price - no complaints here! Also, everything is cooked fresh! Unfortunately, there is only one stove, so I can see how too many orders and no time to spare would frustrate costumers :/ 

Pasta-In-A-Box is still in it's beta phase, so it goes without saying that time is needed for this place to really feel established and ready to take on the hungry crowd of Cal students. After all was said and ordered, I was proud to walk up and down Telegraph with my conveniently packaged pasta in a box!

I decided to try this out today with my boyfriend as we were looking for a quick and cheap meal since the streets were pretty crowded today due to an event on campus.

We both ordered separate boxes of penne pasta with pesto sauce and a drink totaling to about $8 (really cheap for a meal for two).

Service was a bit slow and the place itself felt a bit dark and depressing. There wasn't any place to sit and enjoy the meal so we had to find a spot on campus to go and eat. The menus are also in an awkward location so they are far from the sight of the cash register.

I would return here again as I feel they might need some time to settle in and gain some customers. I'd recommend they brighten the place up a bit and try offering a special to get students to try it out more.

Decided to stop by because they currently have a promotion for any size fountain drink 99cents! To my surprise, this place was fantastic!!! I ordered penne pasta with alfredo sauce and it was only $3.60 for a good portion! It was absolutely delicious not bland what so ever! It did have a lot of spices and garlic but it had a good flavor! They have other pasta selections for the same price, and if you want specialty pastas with meat in them they are $4.95. If you pay with a card they charge you an extra 40 cents

My new obsession. 
I'm a total pasta fanatic and this place is now at the top of my list! 
It is SO cheap, has huge portions, and is delicious. 
I got the #2 with tri color pasta, and it was amazing and only $4.95. I've had my eye on the store as I walk to campus every day and I finally went yesterday after it's opening last week. 
The owner is so sweet and you can see he really wants to please his customers!

See you again today, Pasta in a Box!

LOVE THE CACCIATORE (don't know if that's right, but it's the one with salmon). Don't know if I was supposed to order where I walked in (where the different types of pasta are displayed) or where the cash register is (near the end of the walkway), but I just ordered at the cash register. The chef greets everyone once he sees them, so bonus points for his politeness. Four different types of pasta (I got the tri-colored; no complaints, but I haven't tried any of the others), and you can either pick your own ingredients (about $3-5) or pick one of the specialty pastas (e.g. the cacciatore, which cost $4.95 exactly). I probably waited about five minutes for my pasta. Only one person was cooking and one was at the cash register (helped with the pastas once he wasn't busy) at first, but they were pretty efficient I think. Definitely coming back for my next pasta craving.

3.5 STARS

My first time going to Pasta-In-A-Box! While I wasn't particularly blown away by the place, it wasn't too bad either!

Mostly, I agree with everyone else- Pasta-In-A-Box is a ridiculously affordable alternative to Gypsy's & Pasta Bene. The pasta itself isn't bad at all and is less than $5. Plus, I'm a huge sucker for places with cheap drinks and, well, a giant soda for $1? Count me in!

The one thing I really think could be improved about this place is that it's so tucked in. Seriously, my friend & I walked down Telegraph specifically looking for this place & we almost missed it! ):

That being said, I give props, because Pasta-In-A-Box is so new. And I love that it's already catering to the takeout lifestyle of most Berkeley students. For your debut- not bad!
Cheap, delicious pasta. Lot of variety of pastas to choose from here. Only wish they would churn out their pastas faster.

I REALLY REALLY wanted to love this place. It's on my way home from school, the prices are student budget-friendly, and I love pasta. Unfortunately (probably because they're still working out the kinks of being new) my experience was less than stellar.

As the name suggests, they serve pasta in a box, similar to a Chinese take-out box. In addition to their pastas, their menu has a selection of salads and sandwiches, with very reasonable prices across the board (only about $4 for plain pasta and sauce and around $6 for the specialty pastas and salads). I ordered one of their specialty pastas with salmon and a side salad and the total came out to about $8. The food was good and the owner was very friendly, but it just took waaay too long. With only a single person preparing food, it took me upwards of 20 minutes to get to the front of the line (with just 1 person in front of me) and have my food ready to go. Furthermore, service was awkward as the cashier fumbled around trying to fit the salad box into a small paper bag. For a carry-out place like this, I want to be in and out quickly and smoothly and for now Pasta-In-A-Box doesn't check that box for me.

I'll probably give it another shot in a month or two to see if they've been able to work out the kinks because I did enjoy the food and really do think they have potential.

This little place just opened up two weeks ago, so it looks like they're ironing out a few kinks with regards to service, payment by card, etc. All that aside, they've got a pretty comprehensive menu of pastas (with your choice of spaghetti, penne, little squiggly things, among others) at 4.95 a box, including tax. We got #3 (Alfredo sauce with chicken, olives, mushroom) and #6 (red sauce with caramelized onion, sausage) and both were delicious. Great prices, great portions -- I'll probably be coming here over Gypsy's. :D

I read in the Daily Cal that this pasta place just opened, so I decided to check it out. The presentation on the outside isn't that great. If I wasn't looking for it, I would've easily walked past it. This place is obviously still getting used to being in business. The cashier seemed really nervous and based on the lack of pasta choices in comparison to what they offer, it seemed like they had a busier than anticipated day and were under staffed. 

With all that being said, I think this might turn into one of the regular places I eat at. The pasta is well cooked and very reasonably priced. I paid $4.95 for a box of pasta that I ended up having to share with my boyfriend. The owner is also really sweet. He came over from Paris and believes pasta should be affordable and convenient. The owner also told me that they open til 10, which is nice if you want something quick to eat late at night. I can't wait to see how the restaurant blooms once they get more settled and accustomed to being in business.

This place just opened last week! And it's already becoming a favorite at work for Italian take out for lunch hour! I met the owner, and he is such a sweetheart! He told me he learned his culinary skills from Le Cordon Bleu in Paris. And you can tell from his food that he is a PRO! he cooks with great passion which makes his food more delicious! 

So far I have had the Chicken Alfredo   and some of the specialty pasta which were all scrumptious. If you are looking for a light lunch, I recommend one of their salads. All their ingredients are fresh and their dressings are made from scratch. Next time Im in I will order a sandwhich because I hear they are yummy. Their portions are really good and at a steal! their pasta box's range from $3.95 to $6 for a specialty pasta. 

Please be paitent everyone because they just opened, I know they are working on hiring more people and having a sit down area for people to eat. The food is worth the wait! I know once they are settled in with the right staff and a dining area, PASTA IN A BOX WILL BE A SUCCESS!

Ciao! Amid  io amo il vostro cibo!

This place is awful. I'm huge into Pho and was so stoked when this place FINALLY opened across the street from my work. Huge disappointment. I can't even get into how bummed out my meal here made me... but I'll go ahead and save you the awful meal and let you know I'm never going here again. What a joke.

I'm from LA, and back at home Pho is not only incredibly cheap, but can be found anywhere. Eating it almost every week sometimes, I was a bit distraught to find out that Pho in Berkeley was extremely hard to find. Sure there are the fast, dirty, and cheap ones, but those aren't that. 

When I first went to Pho K&K, it was okay at best. It was more pricey than Pho back at home, and the broth was not at good. However, seeing that I am a Berkeley student without a car, this Pho place was the only nearby one worth eating at, so I ended up going back again and again. After the third time, I was hooked. I grew used to the taste, and the broth is actually very clean and light. The vegetables are nice and fresh, and the service is wonderful. The place as a whole is clean, including the restrooms. 

If you tried this place and were not fond of it, try it again at least a second time. Number 8 is extremely good, with the meatballs being very rich and flavorful.

I really love this place. They have good Pho, and I know some people think 'how can you have bad Pho?" but yup, you can (Casino 580 restaurant!). i go here a lot, i love the chicken Pho, and highly recommend the fresh spring rolls. All their dishes are pretty good, there's always space. it's continually busy but not too busy and the waiters and waitress are always nice.

This place is only two stars at best and this is because I was hungry. After moving to the west coast, this was my first pho. Maybe it was the expectation, but I didn't get any satisfaction from it. It was MSGlicious. The waiter also seemed pretty rude. He asked us again what we were ordering like he was questioning our decision.

Also they are a little more expensive than pho I've had elsewhere.

Ok.. so I'm being nice and giving this place 2 stars. 

My boyfriend and I decided to pay this place a visit because it was close by and my normal pho place, Little Saigon, was closed on Sunday. I ordered a flank and steak pho and my boyfriend ordered a sauteed pork and rice dish. My pho was fairly pricey ($6.75) for the size and the broth was not good. To be honest the broth lacked flavor. Also my meat was not good. They pieces were chewy, flavorless, even and required me to add pepper. I even found a large artery tube shaped piece and fatty tripe-like piece floating inside the bowl, which were just ewwww :( My boyfriend said that his pork was ok but his rice tasted stale and not fresh. 

But.... the decor and staff were nice & they played old 90s pop classics, which are pluses but I definitely won't be coming back.

I came here while on a diet and ate their vegetarian clay pot dish and it was delicious. I hope to try their meat dishes and Pho, which look pretty tasty. 

I really liked their service and it's located just a block south of Dwight on Telegraph in Berkeley where there's not a whole lot of traffic, so it's a got a very cozy atmosphere. 

I can't believe I've never heard of this place before. Southside Berkeley restaurants really don't get much recognition.

Pretty good food and reasonably priced. 

Ironically, their best food isn't their pho. I would recommend trying the other noodles not listed under Pho because those are more flavorful. The pho here is only mediocre because the broth lacking in flavor compared to many pho restaurants in Oakland. I wish there were more bean sprouts and basil leaves in the sides they give you with your pho. I also noticed that they give you a bit less meat in your pho compared to other places. The size of the bowl they give you would be considered a size medium at some places.

I would also recommend trying the spring rolls they serve because they come with a great sauce! 

Would have given this place four stars based on the other dishes but considering the fact that they have "Pho" in the name and I don't actually like their pho... this has to be 3 stars.

A small humble pho place that serves the decent beef pho. It was nice of them to still serve my friend and I when we walked in the restaurant a little before 9 PM (closing time). Super fast service - we got our pho in about 5 minutes! I ordered the rare beef and brisket pho, which was pretty good for $6.75. The soup was nice and aromatic, and they don't skimp on the noodles or meat. Come here if you just want some stomach-warming Vietnamese noodle soup.

When on/near Telegraph you could do worse than K&K. Several visits have shown that this place does a good job with prices that even a student could love. 
Pho Ga is simple, warming and restorative chicken noodle soup.  Bun thit nuong cha gio is fresh and tasty, combining rice noodles, grilled pork, crispy egg roll and assorted fresh veg moistened by fish sauce. Bun Bo Hue is a hearty soup, beefy and red with chili oil, (though not too hot) chunky beef brisket, bits of wiggly tendon and thick rice noodles, dressed up with raw cabbage, sprouts,jalapeno slices and lime wedge. 
The only dud so far was the wonton soup - so salty.

We go to Pho K & K at least once a week. The soup is nice and hot and the food is yummy. I wish they did not skimp on the beansprout and basil. We also have to ask for another plate of it since they only give us one to share.

Quality: Okay so their pho isn't THAT great, BUT pho is still pho! It's becomes heaven during a hangover. Trust me.

Venue: What's with the LONG hallway to get to the bathroom? Overall, nothing special.

Accessibility: On Telegraph, so take the 1.

Service: It's okay... nothing special. 

Nearby: Peets Coffee, Pasta Bene

Tip: You can ask for meat on the side!

Will I come back? Yes, most likely when I'm hungover though.

All I ever order from a pho place is rare steak pho because I can cook fresh meat to my heart's content. I have been here many times. This are what you would expect from a pho place. Mouth-watering thin rice noodles in MSG-rich broth with sauces and fresh condiments on the side. Decent. Good price. Need I say more?

LARGE Pho portions served with hot flavorful broth. They add thinly sliced meat immediately before serving so that you can watch your meat cook in the broth--that way the meat remains tender and flavorful. I ordered the vegetarian one with tofu. Although there was no meat, I enjoyed it because the broth was delicious.

Smaller portions than all the other viet places in the area, the taste is just average, places like camile's, anh hong, and le cheval have much better place at the same price.

but honestly, the restaurant is very clean, the service is good, and the food selection is authentic, so it's an alright place, but if you're looking for best viet food you've ever eaten, this is not the place for you, also if you're a big eater or you're very hungry, you might want to dabble on some finger foods prior to

Somehow, this place confuses me, but I'm cutting it major slack because it just opened.

So I'm not really a pho before, simply because I no longer eat beef. So instead I got the BBQ pork noodle plate (the one with fish sauce?). For me, it was already. Definitely had an overload of veggies, which was what I needed given my recent meat binge. D on the other hand got a beef and onion rice plate, which he enjoyed. He said the sauce they provided was good (lime & pepper?).

However, the plates didn't really have anything special, and the noodles were too dry due to not enough fish sauce. The waiters were a bit confused, as they tried to take our order twice ... as well as almost brought us an extra cup.

Likewise, it also had a "People on Yelp Love Us" and I'm pretty sure it just opened. Just say.

Btws, cash only.

Sadly, the only thing I'm happy about is the ambiance and how cute everything looks. Then again, they just remodeled. If it wasn't looking nice, fail.

I'd have to give this place 3 stars. It's not a great pho place, but it's not bad either. I've been to this place enough times to know that the food is decent, and that their service is ok. I'm a little annoyed that their vermicelli uses the wrong noodles, but it makes do with the taste. Being that it's the only pho place on the Southside of Berkeley, it pulls its own weight.

I've been here a handful of times. Only thing I've ever ordered is the rare steak pho.
Since everyone seems to care about the broth I'll let you know hte broth is decent.. not overly sweet, salty, or greasy.  I usually douse it with cock sauce anyways, so it passes my test. 

At 7 bucks a bowl (one size) it's moderately priced, I just wished they offered larger servings because even with extra noodles, I find myself a little hungry after a bowl.  They'd completely win me over if they'd offer a larger size.

Broth, meat, noodles, size, etc... everything is pretty unremarkable as far as pho goes.  That said, even unremarkable pho is pretty awesome as far as food goes! Given that there is really no competition in Berkeley (besides maybe Anh Hong on University), Pho K+K will continue to have my business.

I was going to give Pho K & K a chance because it's really close to my apartment. I had some reservations because of some of the bad reviews but I was going to give them the benefit of the doubt.

I went with my boyfriend and family and we all ordered pho. There were only about 10 options which was surprising. They were all 6.75 and the dac biet was 7.75. I wanted tendon and brisket but that wasn't a choice. I ended up getting the tendon only pho and hoped for the best. The service wasn't that great but it wasn't too bad. It seemed like the waitress was rushing us a bit though.

But the worst thing was that I got two eyelashes in my soup! They couldn't  have been mine. I didn't want to complain so I just took them out... :( It would have been okay if the broth was good but it tasted like they just instant beef bouillon cubes. There wasn't enough noodles and the portions were small. I think it was filling enough but compared to other pho restaurants (especially ones in Oakland), it is considered a small.

The restaurant was really nice and clean but other than that, I don't think I would go again. The portions and flavors weren't great for the price.

I got #19, which is vermicelli with a pork skewer, two egg rolls, and shredded veggies. 

Pros: 
- The egg rolls were pretty good, and I like how they gave 2 egg rolls instead of just one (like other places). 

- The grilled pork was also pretty good - had that slight burnt/grilled taste that I like. 

Cons: 
- The nuoc mam (the side of fish sauce this dish traditionally comes with) was really light - it barely tasted like anything!! And it didn't even come with shredded carrots like it's supposed to! When I order this dish, I normally pour the whole thing on top of my noodles, so obviously the nuoc mam is going to be essential for me. So to my dismay, it just felt like I was eating plain noodles. 

- Half my bowl was the shredded veggies and the other half was noodles. If they change the portions such that there's more noodle:veggies ratio, then maybe I would've been a little more satisfied (although this doesn't change the fact that their nuoc mam still sucks).
Best Pho I have had! I've been to more than 10 pho spots from Washington state down to Cali and this is the best. Decent price but GREAT food!

First time here and I was seriously craving some pho!! Came here with a group of 6 around 7pm and the restaurant was really busy already but luckily we got the last table! I ordered the regular pho with rare steak and beef flank. The portions here are decent and since its only $7.24 (with taxes included) im not complaining. The noodles were good, but a little overcooked. The broth was pretty standard but it had a good flavor. The only thing is I wish they'd give more meat cuz it really didnt seem like that much. The service here was average since it was so hectic and there was like one lady working the cash register, serving the food, and taking the orders(?). Havnt really been to other pho places in Berkeley so cant really compare but this satisfied my craving :)

I've been a big adventurer of Pho restaurants for about 6 or 7 years now and by this time, I know what I expect of a Vietnamese Pho restaurant.I usually go to these places on cold days, when I'm feeling sick and/or hungover.Believe me the right Pho place can really cure your symptoms, but this place i don't feel did that for me.
In a nutshell here's my experience: 
1)The egg rolls were only 2 per order and was NOT served with lettuce or mint leaves and only a very little bit of fish sauce (which sucks to be lacking when grubbing on egg rolls).
2)Their Pho Ga (my fav) and all types of Pho had waaay too much ginger in it and had to be disguised in order for me to even enjoy it.Ginger should be optional and in a little tray on the side.The sides that came with the Pho were small portions as well...not cool.I need plenty Cilantro and limes.
3)No sweet chili paste was to be found...only cock sauce.You cant have one and not the other.Especially in a Vietnamese place.
4) And last, they do not make shakes...at all.I love to get a strawberry shake with black pearls every now and then after my meal and well this place just doesn't do it.
All in all I left there full, but not satisfied.I do not recommend this place to Pho veterans.I think they half-assed this place to assimilate to the college kids in the area as businesses tend to do in college towns.  -PunkluvsPho

Was just there today with my boyfriend. We had the spring rolls to start off. Totally not work it. $3.50 for two very small fried spring rolls. Wasn't even that tasty. 

We both had the pho with everything. It was ok, the soup was kind of cold when it got to us though. The meat was extremely tough. 

I feel really bad for them. There was a couple people there when we were seated but all finished fairly quickly. By the time our food came, we were the only two patrons left. The staff had nothing to do expect walk around awkwardly filling up soy sauce bottles and watching us eat. Ever have someone just watch you eat your food? It was extremely uncomfortable.
Best veggie pho I've had!

The fried spring rolls had a really nice and light crunch to them.  They were good, though a little too sweet.  But good god...the amount of msg in the pho put me in some kind of a shock.  I'm as chemically dependent as the next alcoholic, but there's enough msg in their pho to turn any mouth into the sahara.  The pho broth had a surprising amount of star anise that almost bordered on unpleasant.
Reasonably priced pho but not the best. I didn't finish the rest of bowl because I was uninterested. The broth was more herby and not the delicious kind of broth I was looking for.

Its really clean and the decor is class. Its a new place, but it doesn't have the run down look of many pho place is see. The smell is strong and exactly what one would ecpect from a real pho house. The music is very appropriate for the college scene. But, and a big but it is, the pho is bland and not authentic.

As most yelpers have mentioned, this place doesn't have the best pho. The same can be said with plenty of other places, but their pho is definitely tasty. It was almost $8 for the special pho. The broth was not as beefy tasting as I would have liked, but portions were huge and service was really nice.

Got the pho with all the different cuts. It's not some mindblowingly tasty pho nor do they give you loads of protein, but portions (including broth and noodles) are definitely enough to fill me up. The broth isn't overly oily, so that's a good thing. They could do with giving a little more bean sprouts, but oh well. 

Coming here on cold nights is definitely nice as its location is somewhat convenient. Waitresses are fairly attentive. I have yet to seen this place get overly packed, but I have passed it once or twice and seen all the seats taken. Yet I don't think that should be a worry if you're thinking about trying/going.
