There are better places to go to if you're just visiting, but if you're here on Southside for a while, this place can be nice for those weird, miserable Springs.

Pho K & K, pretty good, so far my number two pho place. I've been there quite a few times.

For appetizers, you can't go wrong with either of their fresh spring rolls, very tasty.  The fried rolls are ok, but lacking; and for two people you better order two plates or fresh spring rolls as well.

The pho here is good, the broth is rich of beef bones, just the way you want it.  I tried mine with the meat balls a couple of times; I'm just not a fan of the meat balls, I usually get the combo without tendon at every pho house I go to.

About the restaurant itself: it's very casual, like a Vietnamese dinner almost.  The ladies that serve there are always friendly.  Its full of Cal students like myself, which can be kind of obnoxious; e.g. one time when I was there with my girlfriend the kids walk in and sit next to us and one of them it ranting aloud about how he "guesses" he always been against abortions because he's a "true Christian".  Very inappropriate to be shouting at a restaurant huh, but that college students for you, no shame or public consideration.

In conclusion, the friendliness of the ladies running Pho K& K: ****.  The fresh spring rolls: ****.  The fried spring rolls: **.  The Pho itself: ***.  Its good place to go on a rainy day if you are nearby, but not what I would call a date place.

Sorry, not to rant, but I'm from San Diego and when you go to little Saigon in the University area (east of the 15 around El Cajon Blvd), or Clairemont, and you are the only non-Vietnamese person out of 40 people (unless you are Vietnamese) in a pho house, when you order the fried roll they are ALWAYS served with mint and lettuce.  You take the leaves of mint and lettuce and wrap them around your fried rolls, and it makes everything so much more delicious.  It's the perfect contrast of fried and fresh, it truly is just wonderful.  But so far of all the pho houses I've been to in the Bay Area, no one serves their fried rolls with mint and lettuce.  People need to start demanding it; you all are missing out on the sensation.

Better than the place on Shattuck. Better than drunken Pho delivery at 3 a.m., but have had better. If you like a lot of star anise than you will dig the broth. A great middle of the week roomie excursion. The bums that are shunned by the other bums on Telegraph find their way down there, and they may try to fight your roommate in front of this place. So beware the young lookin punk in the red bandana.

[3.5]

I had the #19, which is basically the only type of "vermicelli" they have except for the fact that they didn't actually use vermicelli noodles.  This is probably the only big concern I had about what I ate because the rice noodles that came with it (usually for soup) didn't work very well texture wise.  They also lacked in having different versions of the dish and just had about 4 different types of noodles under "noodles".  Aside from the noodles, I did like how the bbq pork was skewered and how there was a lot of chopped cucumbers and mint.  Their egg rolls were also not bad at all - I might consider getting them as an appetizer if only they had some chili located somewhere on the table.  Boyfriend didn't like the #18 very much - I think it was also very different from what it usually is supposed to taste like.  Not horrible or anything, just different.  

Since they just opened, one thing I would advise them to do is put some curtains in because the sun was just blazing through the window and it was hard to see across the table.  Also, I just wanted to comment on the super long hallway they seem to have - it's just so .. long.  The music they were playing was nice, but then again that's because I can listen to 96.5 without complaints.  

All in all, I probably wouldn't come back too soon into the future.  I'll probably wait awhile for them to get accustomed to things and settled in.  They have the potential to be a good pho place but only time will tell.  The people working there are very nice however so that's a good sign!

The first time I tried Pho K&K was when they first opened and I ordered a rice plate with beef. I came with a handful of friends and we all tried different dishes from the menu. Some pho, spring rolls, veggies, and the rice plates. They were really busy that day and be that as it may they weren't overwhelmed or anything.

The service speed was moderate and the food was okay. Location-wise, I really like it - instead of having empty spaces where creepers congregate.

The next time I tried Pho K&K would be a few days ago. I had the Pho combo and it was high-end pricey compared to Le Cheval's but it was good nonetheless. It was much more empty this time - I was the only one ordering around noon on a Wednesday and there were family members there chatting and kids running around with their Nintendo-3DS. It was cute and they were very friendly and respectful. I could have stayed and enjoyed my Pho but I wanted to try separating the food and add my own rice and condiments ... like ketchup from home.

Overall I'm enjoying their kindness, really spacious and clean venue. I've just had better, especially in Sacramento

After the unfortuante close down of Pho Hua, I have been looking for the next restaurant that'd give me that cheap pho quick-fix in the UC Berkeley area. (Pho Me Now excluded b/c delivery takes time) 
When this place finally opened, I could not wait to try it out!
So I walked into this new establishment approximately an hour ago from now, the decor was all right, which is alarming because everybody knows the shadier the place, the better the food. But I was determined to have my pho fix, so it didn't matter. The place was relatively small and empty with a maximum occupancy of 49 but only two tables were being occupied. Their menu is also relatively small with only 27 items, drinks excluded. There was only 3-4 choices of pho with no addition choice of extra large bowl of some sort. But I was okay with that too, because they could totally be going the quality over quantity route.  
I ordered the pho with three choices of meat, and I chose two things of rare beef and a thing of well done steak. As I waited for my food, one of the waiting staffs brought out a complimentary appetizer -one free egg roll and picked carrots, cabbage, and daikon. The egg roll was freshly fried, but with the lack of dipping sauce it was mediocre. As for the pickled vegetables, let's just say they should have started pickling earlier, the seasonings have not married together, and were not ready to be served at a restaurant. 

When my pho came out, I was immediately thrown into a vertigo of confusion. First of all, the tiny tray of fresh herbs consisted of a slice of lime, some bean sprouts, one pepper and ONE stem of basil. And then it got even worse when I looked at my bowl of pho. There was no rare beef, no steak, but a couple shredded pieces of beef. Nevertheless, I calmly made a couple eye contacts on top of hand waves to call the waiter over and asked about my pho. Even though English was not his forte, I eventually got him to take the bowl back into the kitchen. 

Ten minutes later, a new bowl came out, and here we go again -VERTIGO! Another extra effort to get the waiter's attention later, I finally got to that I ordered two things of RARE beef, which has little resemblance of the unevenly slices of meat in my bowl. (see picture) He nodded and walked into the kitchen without my bowl this time. And I sat there and stared at those inconsistently cut beef like in awe. 
Minutes after, other waiter came out and said that this bowl of oddly shaped meat is what I ordered. When I tried to explain to him that, despite the sizes and shape, every single piece in this bowl looked exactly the same and there's nothing rare about them. He responded that the rare beef is 50% cooked and finishes the rest of its cooking in the piping hot broth. So I got  tired of wasting my  precious final studying, so I just told him that this is not what I am used and gave up being a "difficult" customer, and just asked him for more herbs because I used most of them on the last bowl of shredded confusion. He picked up the plate and left. 

After getting my  herbs  (three stems of basils this time but with no apparent addition of bean sprouts), I finally got to start eating. The noodle itself was overcooked and lost the basic tenderness that even the old Pho Hoa which was ran by Chinese people could put out. The new bowl of WTF-ness had nine slices of beef which each came in unique shape and form, but managed to taste exactly the SAME -  overly thick, well done, but relatively tender. The broth was all right, typical pho broth that's a tiny bit better than the broth made from a package. It had  a tad bit less MSG and grease, but nothing to write home about. Oh! Did I mention my cute little lunch date Mr. Green Fly? He was quite a friendly one! 

Service wise, this place needs a lot of work and re-organization. People, that don't seem to be like part of the staff (e.g. young girl in UGGs & six year old boy) were coming in and out of the kitchen side door. I guess their big kitchen also doubles as a play room?
There were two waiters with very little coordination between the two and the kitchen, because refilling water and attending to customers was slow. New customers walking into the front of the house had to constantly wait awkwardly for someone to come out and seat them. The waiters clearly did not know what eye contacts with customers means. As I was read  to pay my bill and GTFO, they took a long time (w/ an almost empty restaurant) to tell me that their credit card machine is out of order, so it was now cash only. Luckily, I happened to carry some cash, or else I would have to call someone to bring me lunch money like a sad loser kid in elementary school. They could have told me earlier.
In the end, the bowl of WTF that is pho costs $6.75, I paid a little more than $8 with tax and tip. I gave them 15% tip because they have just opened and it's understandable that they don't have the smoothest operation yet. 
But seriously, Pho K&K, get it together!

I tried this place despite the less than stellar reviews because I so badly wanted them to be wrong so there could be a good pho place in Berkeley, but unfortunately, this place is pretty meh. 

The bowls of pho are on the small side, and the broth is salty and flavorless.  They are definitely stingy with their sprouts (just one plate to share between 3 people).

K&K is more of a 2.5 though because the restaurant is really clean, well-lit and neat.  Plus, as so many other reviewers have already noted,  the service is speedy and attentive.

This place is great! 
I'm pretty picky when it comes to Vietnamese food--it's hard to substitute for what you can get at home! But I ordered the Papaya Salad and the fresh Vietnamese Springrolls --and they were delicious! The sauces were perfect!

My friend ordered their special for the day which happened to be Banh Xeo (Vietnamese Crepes) and it was so delicious that he didn't even bother sharing with me!

All the dishes came in perfect portion sizes so that we were both thoroughly full! The service was friendly! 

If you're looking for good, traditional Vietnamese food--not wanting those crazy fusion stuff for today--I'd definitely recommend Pho K&K!

p.s. Try their fried bananas and ice cream, too. Perfect dessert.
A place for  convienience not a place to seek out. Portions are small for a pho place. We came here hungry. We left hungry. Can't say that about most pho places. Service is fast, place is clean

Pretty surpised to see the average reviews..I love this place. I am not a huge fan of Pho unless I'm sick, but I love the clay pot rice bowls! They are very filling and have lots of flavor. I love how the rice gets a bit brown and crunchy on the sides of the pot! I have been back 3 times since I tried it! I live about 45 min away, I wish it was closer! Also, give the coffee a try! They serve it so fresh!

Came here for an early afternoon lunch. The service is blazing fast, and the place is very nice and well priced. I'm used to east coast Vietnamese food, so how they make food here is very different. I had the rice and grilled chicken, and there was so much food I couldn't finish, and I eat a lot. I wouldn't say the food was too tasty, as the last time I came here, I felt the same way, so 6 months later, nothing has changed. Still, a nice place to go for some non-orthodox Vietnamese food.

I've eaten at a LOT of pho places in my life.  There's been times when I would eat it for lunch then dinner for several days.  And i think i've tried just about every pho place in SF/Eastbay area.  

This place is decent.  Clean comes to mind.  

Not your typical ghetto hood pho place.  

Sprouts, basil, jalapenos, and lime seemed fresh but don't give you a lot like the typical places.  

No choice on sizes of bowls.  

The broth was decent.  Not watery but not richly flavored either.  

However the noodles were perfect but the broth to noodles ratio was low so better eat fast or you won't have much soup left before you finish your noodles.

The meats were good.  Rare steak was thin, tender, and fresh.  Flank was ... well, flanky (chewy & crunchy).  Not my favorite of the meats but when I'm at a pho place for the first time, I like to try the combo with everything to gauge the quality of the place.

The tripe was thinly sliced so not over powering like some places where you feel as though you're chewing on a clump of rubber bands.  

The brisket was tender and tasty but was a bit fatty.  Some people like it that way so not necessarily a bad thing.  

I also tried their sausage spring roll.  Had a nice fresh crunch to it though I think they could have been more creative with the meat.  I did like their plum sauce (?) dipping sauce.  

Would I come again?  Yeah i would if I was in the area and didn't have time to go to Oakland to grab a genuine bowl of pho.

I was wary to try this place after other reviewers mentioned that the pho was bland and unreasonably priced. I tried the pho here for the first time and ordered the chicken pho. The broth for the pho was just right and not salty. Overall, I thought it was a filling meal and well-priced. My only gripe was that they gave very little bean sprouts and herbs. I will definitely be coming back for pho again, since the flavors are just right for my tastes.

I didn't have the pho, so no comment there. But I love #19 (not sure what it's called). It's cold rice noodles with shredded lettuce, carrots, bean sprouts, cucumber, and mint leaves topped with Vietnamese egg rolls and a pork skewer. The mint leaves totally make the dish. Oh, and the fish sauce. Best food for lunch ever.

Their pho isn't bad, to say the least. It's probably one of the better and more convenient pho places around the Berkeley campus, so that's definitely a plus. But I don't really go out of my way to eat at this place. The place is pretty clean too! 

I don't really like their beef pho, but their pho ga is pretty light and is probably my favorite dish here. They use white meat for their, and the strips of chicken have a nice consistency. I also like their bun bo hue - from the times I've ordered it - the broth hasn't been too overpowering. Also - they have a rice dish in a clay pot which is very good, albeit the portion is very small. Small portions seem to be a commonality throughout the menu, but it's not too expensive and I'd rather have food that has been prepared cleanly with smaller portions than possibly dirty food. 

I really like their three bean drink as well - I think it's under desserts. I can't seem to remember the name of it - but it's pretty good. 

Overall, Pho K&K is definitely the best pho that I've had in Berkeley. The cleanliness of the restaurant is probably the most appealing factor to me.

Their menu isnt very impressive, there should be size options, and if it cost 2$ less I'd probably eat there every week. You can get many more varieties of asian noodle soups across the street at Racha and Thai Noodle.

Being a typical Vietnamese who ate Pho all her life, I did not get Pho when I came here. Instead, I got the Com Tam (rice plate). First of all, I was fairly disappointed in the menu and how limited it was. I was used to a wide variety of vermicelli and rice plates but I guess not here. I got Grilled Shrimp with a fried egg for my food. Overall, the food was average. Nothing special about the grilled shrimp. I expected them to have the signature Crab/Shrimp cake that goes with every typical rice plates but they didn't have that at all on the menu.  

My friend ordered Pho & Bun Bo Hue.  Because I don't eat meat, I didn't get to try it. However, the soup for the Bun Bo Bue looked very clear and I can tell that there was a lack of that spicy kick. Both the soup dish also looked very plain. There wasn't a lot of meat in it . I heard that the Vegetarian Pho is pretty good so maybe I'll try it if I ever decide to come back again.  

Overall, the service saved this place from 2 stars. They were very nice!   Maybe because I am very picky with my Vietnamese food but this place is just too average. It is good enough for Berkeley though since there are no better Pho places in Southside. Until I find a real authentic Vietnamese restaurant in Berkeley, I'll just save my cravings when I go home to my mother's home cooked Pho.

*The only thing I truly liked here was the Thai Tea! :D
I love this place!! I only ever get the rare beef pho. Very clean, fast, friendly, and fresh.. I've been there many times always perfect!!
Based on Berkeley standards, for which there is no comparable Pho alternatives, KK deserves a 5-star rating.  The Pho is good and does the job.

So, how should I even start this post.

I have not even tried their Pho yet. 
People might say, "why are you reviewing this then?"
My answer would be, "I sat there for 10 minutes waiting for the waiter to come by; however, instead of serving my friend and I, the waiter decided to serve a group of girls who came in to the restaurant after us."

You know what?
I might NOT know about the food that they serve; however, I do KNOW that their waiters did not get the proper training on how to serve.

Conclusion:  I will not even consider trying this restaurant, and I will definitely not recommend it to my friends.

I'm a fan of this place, mostly for its location as there isn't another pho place on southside.  The restaurant is clean, the staff friendly.  I've never actually eaten here, I always get takeout, and the soup is packaged very well. Nothing more disappointing than going home to find that your pho is all over the bag, and that there's some in the car too.  

I'm a big fan of the spring rolls, the peanut sauce that comes with them is fantastic and just creamy enough without looking like it's old or expired. 

Pretty big portions, good broth (the most important signature of any pho), not too salty.  Nothing special, but sometimes that's a good thing.

Well, well, well, what do we have here?  A good place for pho if ou're in the Cal Berkeley area and spent all day walking around shopping or just touring what a cute college town looks like.  Or...are just freakin' sick and the only cure is more cowbell, I mean Pho.   Any real asian-american restaurant does not charge for a pot of hot tea.  So I dub K and K officially asian-american restaurant.  The pho bowls are reasonably priced and the music is super pop and fun but now too loud.  

It never seems too crowded and its pretty nice and clean.  They do take card and they do have those tiny cute little bowls to dip the meat in when you know you just want more rooster sauce with your soup.  They only give you one lime though so if you're a lime junkie, ask for two.  

And always...always...always ask for a pot of hot tea.  ITS FREE! ORDER THE HOT TEA! ITS FREE!! WOO HOO!

I dropped by Pho K&K today with my girlfriend before I needed to make a long drive over to San Jose. She was worried I'd eat too much pho before I drove but I shrugged it off, claiming that "Pho K&K doesn't give that much food anyway..."

Fortunately/Unfortunately this wasn't the case this time! I ordered the special and I'm pretty sure they increased their portion sizes to be more like normal pho places! This made me pretty happy and is why they have at least 3 stars in my eyes.

The soup is pretty dark and slightly more savory/salty than other ones. The noodles aren't left in the soup long enough, I think since they were a little bit tough. I don't think Pho K&K is too generous with the meat, but I really liked the tendons along with the other pieces. Overall the meats aren't the best but good enough!

One thing we noticed was that the cups are pretty cool! They definitely spent some time making sure the ambiance was good and even though its a pho place it has a classy cup for sodas and the water cups have a pretty unique design. 

Overall not bad...not amazing but it has become a solid place to grab pho if need be!
The broth was delicious but the serving size of the pho was quite small for a Vietnamese restaurant. They could be more generous on the meat, too.
bland broth, noodles were fine - not mushy as people claim. definitely the best out of berkeley pho though! people need to stop being picky though, it IS berkeley.

I waited a couple of months before they opened this place since most places around Berkeley weren't that good (disclaimer: I'm from SoCal). And it's literally one block away from my apartment. The food is decent, definitely more tasteful than most Vietnamese places I've been to around Berkeley. The service is great, even though they're often short on staff. 

Hope they will stay around.

I had lunch there today, and it was about my fifth time there.  I had the pho (#8) and it was fine, along with a Vietnamese Iced Coffee (yum) and a fresh lemonade.  The service was helpful and friendly, and there are nice watercolors on the walls.  

This place is on Telegraph, just across from Moe's and just a few blocks south of the campus.  It's great for medium quality pho.  The place is clean.

First of all they messed up on my order. The broth was bland and the meat was wayyyy overcooked, it was chewy and thick. The price of this place was about $1 more than the really good Pho places in Oakland, not worth it. Definitely will not be coming here again

After a night out, waking up dehydrated and slightly groggy left my friends and I craving for some noodle soup. Pho K & K came to the rescue with a big delicious bowl of msg filled goodness with noodles and thinly sliced rare meat! 

The only complaint I have with their pho is that they do not give enough meat. They skimped on the meat as other pho restaurants usually give much more for the price. But overall, I was satisfied with the flavorful broth, soft noodles and yummy basil. This review is only for the pho though--my friend got egg rolls and they didn't look too impressive. If you're craving for some soup on a cold day in Berkeley, give Pho K & K a try!
Good value and some great fresh items on the menu. Try the papaya salad and the fresh pork rolls.

I've walked by this place so many times living around the corner from it. The Pho was alright, nothing to brag about. The service was shitty. We ne'er got our water cups refilled and she never came by to see if we needed anything. Service is half the visit. I won't come back here

woke up this morning (hehe 2pm) and craved pho, heard that there's a new place around so decided to give it a try.

the interior decor was pretty nice, which i guess should not be surprising considering that it IS a new place and they DID just open.  the purple ceiling tiles and other miscellaneous decoration choices around the place made it look more like a thai restaurant than a pho house though.

my boyfriend and i both ordered pho dac biets, which includes all the different cow parts.  the plate of nasties (beansprouts, lime, and other green grass ma-jiggers) that usually comes with pho was surprisingly small, but considering that i'm not a fan of putting a forest in my soup it wasn't a biggie for me.  i would say the pho itself was pretty fair, but for some reason my stomach failed to agree and proceeded to protest violently for the next 3 hours, eventually compromising only after some hot chocolate and a slice of west coast pizza.  maybe the broth was too oily?  i have no clue.

i wouldn't say service was terrible since the waiters were pretty friendly, but it for sure reeked of "inexperience".  i guess with time and more costumers that would change, but for now it shall remain a point of concern.

points to consider:
play some music.  i don't like controlling my voice just because i could hear my echo.
less lemon in the water.  if i really can't stand your iced tap water than i'll ask for some lemons
include pictures in the menu.
provide sizing options and perhaps add more rice plates to the menu
fix the credit card machine

hopefully they'll improve soon and learn to actually run a restaurant

I love this place. The spring rolls are wonderfully crunchy, and the pho is comforting and just what I want when I'm craving it. The service has always been good, and it's been by far the best pho place I've experienced in Berkeley. 

I haven't tried any of the other dishes, but the pho has always been good. I haven't had a problem here like I've had at other places where they cook the noodles wrong and they're all just a massive clump of stuck-together noodles.

It's a great place, and I'm sorry more people aren't there whenever I go!

Not bad - I went with the beef balls.  Standard for a pho place - pretty much what I would expect for a pho place near the college campus.  But the value was really good - it was maybe a little bit cheaper than other pho places that I've seen.

Eh. I havent had a really good bowl of pho in so long, I wonder if I even like pho anymore. Sighs.

Anyways, I ordered the combination pho that had everything in it. it was like $7.50+. So I had high expectations. I did appreciate that the fat wasnt ridiculous (I wanted to take it out but my friend wanted it so I just put it in his bowl). But there was barely any tripe; I had to really look for it. The actual broth was strong with star of anise but I felt like it needed more beef flavor and wasnt too impressed. 

We also ordered shrimp spring rolls. Pretty good but there were only two regular sized spring rolls cut in half....

The staff is really nice and were pretty good about keeping our water filled. They joked around with us and were always smiling. One of the waiters spilled my water though but accidents happen. Three waiters then proceeded to ask if we were ok and made sure the mess was cleaned up asap. 

I probably wont get their pho anymore but I might come back to try their rice dishes since it's so close to campus.

We went to this restaurant with a group of 8 people. Some of our friends were late, so we just sat at our table and talked for about a half an hour. The wait staff was very welcoming and continued to check in on us and re-fill our waters. I, personally, had my water filled up 10 times during dinner. I did not have to ask to have it filled up at all. They did so anytime it was close to being empty. It was a nice touch. The restaurant was well lit and inviting. The staff had smiles on their faces and were very nice. One of our friends was Vietnamese, so we attempted to say thank you and other things in Vietnamese. The staff got a kick out of it and attempted to help us. 

The food was very delicious. I had a chicken dish that was well seasoned and delicious. A couple of my friends had a type of Pho. They all enjoyed their dishes as well.

It was well priced and a nice experience overall. I will return to get some more Vietnamese food very soon.

As mentioned by the other reviewers, this place is really clean. Attentive staff, clean atmosphere, decent taste. Only comment, I would have preferred lime over lemon but not a big deal. Basically if you're craving pho, it gets the job done.

My friend and I tried this place today. The service was great! Friendly, fast, and very accomodating with a couple of requests my friend made with her dish. We shared the goi cuon (spring rolls)- delicious and well priced ($4 for two rolls). We each had pho and the portions were generous. We both thought it was very tasty. We'll be back!

Great atmosphere. Crowded for a Sunday night dinner. Bathroom is super clean. Pho comes out extremely fast. 

I ordered the rare beef and tendon. Staff is great! Rare beef and tendon pho wasn't on the menu but they allowed me to have it at no extra charge so yay! Glad that they were friendly and adaptable. Soup was the best part! If I could give it a 4.5 stars , I would. 

The only bad part was that took them awhile to see that I wanted to pay the bill and there wasn't anything super special about the pho.

I heard this place was supposed to be pretty authentic, but it falls short in my opinion. The broth has a flavor to it that I've never tasted in any other restaurant. Maybe this is someone's idea of authentic? 

I normally get pho dac biet (pho with everything) wherever I go so that's what I had. Can't really say much else for this place.... the restaurant is clean, the chopsticks and small dipping bowls were clean... I'm just really picky about the quality of my pho.

I wish that this restaurant got more credit that it does. Their pho is pretty good and really cheap. If you're a Berkeley resident/student, you need to understand that the quality of food near campus is fairly low. 

Therefore, ADJUST YOUR STANDARDS ACCORDINGLY. I'm tired of reading reviews for the restaurant beating the crap out of them about how this and that sucks. It's BERKELEY, you're not going to find gourmet fine-dining restaurant to bring a date to propose to. 

Going back to the food, Pho K&K is pretty good. I've had pho in almost every city that I've visited or passed through and I'd eat Pho K&K. They have pretty decent broth and their meats are okay. My only complaint is their tendon is overcooked and too gooey but other than that I like their other cuts.

Give this place a try despite the low overall score.

I wrote this review in part because I thought the existing reviews were a bit harsh. It seems as if many people consider themselves "Pho experts" and have rigid expectations about exactly how Pho should be served. I think this place is worth a visit, if you live in Berkeley. Nonetheless, Pho K&K probably should listen to some of the feedback, since apparently meeting expectations is important. 

I've eaten Pho at many of the awesome places in Little Saigon in Garden Grove and Westminster, CA, when I lived there. I have also eaten it at places that are less good at it, including Brentwood, San Diego and Boston (e.g. Pho Pasteur) and have a pretty good idea of what the standard is and also what good Pho tastes like. I thought Pho K&K was not as good as Little Saigon, but as good as or better than the other places. 

As far as I know, this is the best Pho you can get south of Berkeley.  I believe that Pho Me Now, which is much higher rated currently, is basically inedible. As such, I think that people should be careful about reviewing Pho K&K negatively, since as far as I can tell, this one of the better restaurants on Telegraph.

A few notes from previous reviews:

- The service sounds like it's gotten a lot better after their first three weeks of business.

- Currently, when you order the rare meat, they put it in before they serve it. My guess is this is a conservative strategy to try to avoid putting off people who are less comfortable with raw meat. If you would like the meat raw, so you can cook it yourself, *just ask for it on the side*. One of my friends requested this, and it was fine.

- The Pho comes with a generous assortment of noodles. I did not notice a lack of meat. The fixings could have been a little more generous, but there was enough. How much basil and sprouts do you really want in your Pho anyways? I actually would prefer it if they offered a small size, as the standard bowl is a bit more than I like to eat.

- In terms of the cà phê sa á (vietnamese iced coffee), if you watch, you can see them making it, they do not use a mix. Probably, if you asked, they would bring you the apparatus and have you make it. Next time, I will ask them to go a little lighter on the condensed milk, as I prefer it strong.

- The desserts were quite delicious, although you have to eat around the ice.

- I also liked that it was quite clean, unlike most Pho places.

I certainly don't claim to be a Pho expert.  

But I like this place. The vegetarian pho is always super hot and yummy.  the staff is so friendly it will knock your socks off.  

And its walkable from my house... always a plus!

I came here for dinner and ordered #9 (pho with beef). Food, service, and everything else was decent. Nothing was amazing enough to make this place stand out. Oh, I did have to wait for my beef and noodles to "cook" in my bowl because the beef came out very red and the noodles weren't as soft.

I feel bad doing this review because the owners are VERY nice people, but I have to be honest - it's best for their business (hopefully they'll use these reviews to improve the quality of their food) so here goes...

Despite reading the low reviews, I decided to try the place out for myself. First things first, I love love love that this place is clean - not many pho places are. As for the actual pho, reviewers are right. The meat was really tough and not thinly sliced (this goes for the flank and the rare steak). Also, the broth could definitely use a little more flavor. Unless they improve their meat, I probably won't be back.

Came by for some pho, but I ended up ordering the cubed steak.  Taste-wise, I was pretty satisfied with the meal.  It came with that lemony salt and pepper sauce that I used very liberally and the steak itself was delicious.  On the other hand, there just wasn't that much of it.  The plate was split at about 2/3 (or more) of rice and the rest a mixture of the cubed steak and other filler (mushrooms, onions, etc.).  I really wish there had been more meat, but I guess for 7.50 it wasn't too bad.  
The meal definitely tasted great, but the service could've been a bit better.  After we were seated, I guess the server forgot that we weren't part of the group next to us (since the tables are sort of connected) and took a while before she realized we hadn't ordered yet.  Not really a big problem though, and probably more of an honest mistake.

Wish their portions were a bit larger (at least of meat) but otherwise a tasty and fairly quick meal.

I've never been able to find any good pho places around Berkeley & I guess my search continues...

Pho K&K is decently near campus, however, and the pho is pretty cheap. Unfortunately, the food reflects the price and the pho is simply average/mediocre. I'll admit the setting is a lot classier than I expected, so this might be a good place to take someone on a date if you don't want to spend too much.

Otherwise, Pho K&K is a decent pho place, but it's not the best.

I've definitely had better.

Note: I'm not a super big lover of pho, so I would prefer to go to those places with big bowls for cheap prices, because pho is just noodles and meat to me. I end up putting lots of sauce in the soup anyways. 

That being said, if you are like me, then this place is not worth going to. The serving sizes are relatively small, making it a tiny bit pricey for the amount you're given. When I went, service was also a bit slow (as far as refilling our tables' waters go).

Today was my second time here and it was significantly better than the first time. The first time i went, I was craving pho and their pho deeply disappointed me. It's expensive (~$7 when in SoCal I can get pho for ~$5). They give a puny amount of bean sprouts and the broth is bland.

Thus, this time around I decided to get something else. The first picture I saw on the Yelp page for this restaurant had this bowl with noodles, veggies, egg roll, fish sauce, and bbq meat on a skewer. It looked so good so I decided to order it. My Viet friend helped me figure out what it was (name was hecka long so i don't remember but it was #19). MAN IT WAS SOOOO GOOD. Definitely redeemed the place, though I still can't give more than 3 stars to a place called "Pho K&K" but has mediocre pho.

Nice and clean restaurant with lots of seating. Service was nothing extraordinary, but not bad either.

TIPS:
1) Order #19!
2) Don't get the pho if you're looking for the pho that your mom makes or the pho that you can get in Little Saigon in OC
3) If you do get the pho, ask for extra bean sprouts. Seriously.

I'm actually a fan of this place, for several reasons.  But first, let me say that I'm not very picky when it comes to pho.  When I want pho, just about anything satisfies my craving.  

First of all, their service is extremely quick.  It's easy to pay and divide up the bill if you're in large groups (just walk up to the register and tell them what you ordered).  Not too expensive, close location, and the hot-spot for hangover food.  

Tip #1: If you're feeling extra hungry, ask for extra noodles!  It's FREE. 

Overall:  Might not be the best, but it has quick service, easy paying, nice location, and free noodles.  Win.

Having only recently discovered pho, I was really excited that this place opened up a block from my apt.  Not being a student nor enjoying bums constantly asking for change, I don't like to venture too far up telegraph.  I'm happy this place opened too because it removed most of the people that were staying below it's massive overhang.  

That aside, the prices were decent, service was very inexperienced (i was served a glass of ice for my beer... then they whisked that away and gave me a warm empty glass instead.  I'd hate to see them try to manage a busy restaurant),  the broth and noodles were delicious.  I got the #8, there wasn't much tripe or tendon, the beef was good and included meatballs.  My fiance got a vegetarian dish (which makes me happy that they have them since she's a vegetarian) with fried tofu.  She liked it.

I will definitely be going there again.

Honestly, this is most authentic and best pho restaurant in Berkeley. Seriously, our only other options would be "Saigon Eats", "Pho me now", or "Vietnam Village" in Asian Ghetto... not to knock these other restaurants, but they're all pretty much "fast-food" variations of pho!

K&K workers are super sweet and attentive. The restaurant itself is clean and bright. I've had pho and bun bo hue here a few times, and granted, it doesn't taste like my mom's cooking, but it's probably the best I can do without leaving Berkeley!

Most likely I give it a 4, but seeing that the average was 2 1/2 ratings, I thought I might bump it up alittle, since it is one of the best places to get pho in Berkeley, even though it may not be comparable to oakland, but in my opinion, some of oakland's best are now lacking, and this place is a decent pho place to eat.

Still a bit pricy for me, 7.75 for combo pho in just one size. But when I came in here, the place smelled delicious, like a pho restaurant, like I was in a big bowl of pho. The place can't get any cleaner, especially since it just opened, and everything is absolutely new and spotless, especially if you look at the spoons and sauce bowl, it gleams of cleanliness.

I came here with my boyfriend and when he got his bowl he instantly complimented it on its smell and taste. My bowl came out pretty quickly, and it was boiling hot! which I really love. It stayed hot until i finished it, which is a plus. The plate of vegetables were of smaller size than the average pho restaurant, but who cares? how many ppl actually eat more than a stick of basil and all that bean sprouts anyways? I usually feel bad for throwing them away, but in this case, there's not much to do so. and if you wanted more, just ask. The bean sprouts that I had were amazingly fresh and crunchy.

The rare beef was still red when it got to my table, which is good. The meat on the other hand was very tough, making it very difficult for me to chew. But that was the only problem I could find. The meat was not amazing, but definitely edible. The broth was delicious. And I'm vietnamese, we know how to judge our pho, not this over the top perfectionist that everyone expects. Its pho, a bowl of water, noodles and meat in berkeley, not in some fancy pancy hotel in paris.

The workers here were also amazingly kind. They always greeted me with this huge smile, the hugest I've seen in any waiter give me, and everytime too, from taking my order, to giving my food, refilling my water, and giving me the bill. And for those who think that Pho Me Now is better, you must not be vietnamese, that thing is inedible pho, I would call it double imitation pho bc even the broth just  tastes horendous.

Seeing as though I did come here a bit after they opened, they improve pretty quickly and people should give this place a try, w.o. coming in and expecting the best of Vietnam in their bowl. One of the closest places to get pho in berkeley.
Good cheap tasty

I gave it five stars when maybe it deserves four, but other people rated it way too low.  I have to agree with Michael T. on almost everything, especially about this being one of the very few places to get pho in south Berkeley.  Yes, there are some good places in Oakland, but Cal students will not be venturing there on a regular basis.  I really hope this place stays open because their pho is really good.  Yeah, the spring rolls might not be worth it, but I go here for their specialty: pho!

If you like Pho Me Now then I have a few things to say to you:

1)You're crazy.
2)You're drunk.
3)You should definitely like Pho K&K cause it is way better.

I agree with the post Hannah W. posted below. 
It is probably one of the best pho restaurants near campus right now based on tastiness and cost.
The beef pho is great- they provide a lot of meat (brisket, rare steak, etc.) and the meat is not too dry. The broth is delicious. The spring rolls are also fresh.
What to avoid:
The chicken pho- the broth has a sour, bitter taste. 
The OJ- artificial and very sugary. I had to ask the servers to dilute the OJ b/c it was so sweet.

I've been wanting good pho since I moved to Berkeley 6 months ago and I think we've tried every place in a ten mile radius at this point.  Most pho we've had here is really just 'good enough'.
Finally we popped into Pho K&K and found what we were looking for; good broth.  It's really the broth that makes the pho.
Beyond the broth, the meat was perfectly prepared and the noodles had great consistency.
As a big plus, the service is quick and friendly and it is one of the cleanest restaurants in all of Berkeley.
We will definitely be going back.

Mediocre pho - not bad but not great. It is a bit pricey; I ordered pho with just noodle and broth (no meat) and it was $5.50, and my can of Sprite was $1.50.

The workers were friendly though.

There is awesome pho in Oakland and not much can compare to those around West Oakland.
However, this place is decent, and for one of the few pho restaurants in the Berkeley campus area, this is probably the best one. 
Compared to other pho I've eaten, the texture of the noodles was not as good as it can be, but at least it wasn't strands of flour. 
I got the #8 and I usually get #8, cause that's just the benchmark pho bowl. You judge pho by the special. And boy, was the broth was awesome. Awesome meaning tons of MSG. I know it's bad but it still tastes soooo goooood. 

The place is quaint. Service is alright, they watch you drink your water, and once you're done there's another full cup for ya.
Could do with more meat in the pho. For the price they don't give jack. Got one slice of beef. Don't bother asking them for more ingredients unless you're willing to pay an extra dollar for nothing.

Reason for 3 stars:
Would give 2 stars based solely on the pho quality and price and size. But taking into account location location location, it's pretty good to have a nice pho place near campus

Pho Ga is my big comfort food when I have a cold...heck, anytime.  I was excited to see this place open up near me, I can even walk to it (I was driving by when I saw it tonight).  

The broth was delicious and is always the key to a good Pho. It was on the salty side but not too much, just borderline. The chicken tasted fresh and was shredded and a very good amount of it was provided.  The fresh herbs and sprouts were great, I wish I had gotten a little bit more of them however.  (thats my only complaint).

As others have said, its VERY clean, easy and friendly to eat at. I went there alone tonight actually and it wasn't awkward at all thankfully.  I will be back many more times!

Good location and the mandatory Sunday lunch to cure any hangover. There's a lot of variety and the prices aren't bad. I always order Pho (the one with all the different types of meat..). There isn't really much service at Pho restaurants - but I come for the cheap and OK pho. It hits the spot and it has a convenient location, what more could I ask for?

I think that it's not the best pho place ever, but it's really not the worst either. Although I read my friend's review of the place, I know that I needed to try it for myself. 

So it's not perfect, but it's decent. Nice broth for the sick person - which I am for now. There was a decent amount of meat, but broth was kind of bland. I had to add the hosin sauce which I normally do anyways. The bean sprouts looked sad so I didn't add any of those in, but I normally do because they're nice and crisp to contrast the different textures.

It is a bit pricey - $7.75 for a medium size of pho? There is only one size as well so for those people with bigger stomaches they can't really get more, unless they buy a whole other bowl. 

Perhaps they've gotten better since reading comments on yelp. They also apparently closed down for a week or so in the beginning of January to remodel? Perhaps, they made some other changes as well. 

Not too bad, I'll be back whenever I'm sick and need a nice bowl of pho.

Can't speak much on the pho since I got a tofu salad (stellar!) but the tab came out to $31 for our party of 4 voracious eaters. 

Luckily, we beat up the lunch-time crowd and got our food minutes after we ordered. (A group of 17 walked in 10 minutes after we sat down).

From sticking my nose in other people's business, I noticed that the pho was rather lacking in meat/the good stuff. Despite the unfavorable ratio of noodles:broth:good stuff, I'd still come back.

Really good pho - both the chicken and vegetarian.  Best Pho in Berkeley, in my opinion.  Their clay pots are the best I've had in the bay area... period.  The staff is friendly and attentive, the place is clean, and to go is pretty quick.  I eat here every week (just about), and I love it.

Pros: Very clean and pretty little place. Really sweet-natured and attentive servers. Clean bathrooms (Haha it says a lot, ok?) Reasonable prices 

Cons: Pho broth started ok but after a while starts to taste bitter and weird and left my mouth really dry. Meat is kinda chewy.

This place could have been SO AWESOME. A pho place so close to campus is one of those "of course!" ideas like Cream that has everything going for it if well-executed, and yet it doesn't quite work. We got the pho with everything, which only had slightly more meat than the pho with a fraction of everything? The spring rolls were pretty standard, but the pork one had sausages wrapped inside, rather than ground pork, which was surprising but not unpleasant. 

Overall, I'd come here again if I was in the mood for pho but was too lazy to drive/ too cheap to order from pho me now

P.S the KK stands for the names of the owner's sons cuteee :)
I've had better Pho and noodles, but it's good for not being in Oakland. Great location and service. Overall very satisfying.

The Pho here was PhoK&King awful! 

My experience here started off bad - the wait staff stared at me blankly, I ask to be seated, couple of seconds of vacant staring from said wait staff, and then realization dawns. I'm shown a table. 

I order a bowl of Pho with rare thinly sliced steak, brisket, beef balls. Soon, a plate of sad looking basil, limp bean sprouts, and a forlorn slice of lime are deposited before me. And what is that I see garnishing the sprouts? A long strand of beautiful hair! I point at hair..the plate is whisked off and replaced with a less hirsute version; a sheepish apology is attempted.

Then comes the final disappointment - the meal itself. The broth was a sad excuse for a Pho broth, a homeopathic dilution of the essence of a Pho broth. And in this sea of failure were found floating two thick, chewy slices of steak that showed no visible signs of rareness, one cleaved beef ball, one thick, gristly brisket slice with plasticky looking fat hanging on, and a copious amount of noodle. I squeezed the lime, dropped some sprouts, shredded some basil and dug in. I manage to gulp down most of the meat, slurped some broth and left the vast amount of noodle untouched. I fled! 

I don't think there's anything redeeming about this place. It opened recently; I suspect it will close shortly, unless a miracle happens.

Okay, I would normally give this place 3 stars. BUT.... here's how it goes.

My friend and I were about to eat at Norikonoko Japanese Restaurant across the street but found out it was closed. We were hungry already and saw Pho and decided to eat there instead. So we ate here by default haha.

A combo was about $7.25 and the other pho bowls were about $6.75. But they were HUGE!!! Holy crap. I only ate half! The broth and pho itself was good, the shrimp spring rolls we had were alright. 

SINCE the bowl was so humongo and I didn't finish everything, I had to get a take out box. Grabbed that gigantic bowl, was pouring it only the plastic cup, and then it accidentally slipped my hands and landed on the other plate of bean sprouts and broke it into 4 different pieces :( I felt so bad and embarrassed that I offered to pay for the plate lol. But they were really nice about it and said "it was just an accident" and they smiled.  They even joked around and said "maybe it's just an old plate!" to make me feel better. What awesome service!!

Food was decent, portion was good, service excellent.  Because I accidentally broke a plate and they were so nice about it, I'm giving them 5 stars lol. Sorry Pho K & K for making you -1 plate but thank you for being so nice about my clumsiness! :)

Finally, some decent pho within walking distance of the UC campus.

The space is small but clean. It looks very plain from the outside and even more plain on the inside.  It goes to show that this place is for eating not for entertaining.

In the $8 beef combination pho, there's plenty of rare beef,  well done beef and a couple of beef balls. I liked the clean tasting beef broth, not greasy at all.  They give you plenty of basil, sprouts, peppers and lemon.  Thankfully, they don't skimp on these favorites! It could use more tendon and tripe though.  

It's $6.75 or 7.75 for a medium sized bowl of pho. It's a smaller serving than other pho places in the greater East Bay but it's made well enough to come back often.  Best part yet is that they accept credit cards!

I'm gonna have to agree with most of the previous reviews and say that this place definitely has a lot to learn about customer service and making pho. Being a new business, I hope they improve down the road, but for now it's just not that great.

I came in with two of my roommates to see if what everyone's been writing is really true. Since Pho K&K is practically down the road from us, it was worth trying it. Their decor and friendliness is surprisingly exemplary for a pho establishment. Everything else, however, is just not up to par. 

It was just the three of us in the whole establishment, yet they somehow managed to screw up orders. We all got the #8 combination (one with everything, one with no flank and no meatballs, and one with no meatballs and steak on the side). Somehow, they only managed to get the one with everything right, and screwed up the other two orders. It's really not that hard considering there was no one else there. 

Once I got my $8 bowl, I stared at it for a while and thought "where's my meat?" I think they try to pass it off as a large bowl, allowing them to charge so much. However, I only saw one small piece of each kind of meat in my bowl. ONE PIECE!!! I'm sorry but I need more meat to fill me up (that's what she said?). If that wasn't enough, it didn't even taste that great. The broth was pretty good, and plenty of noodles, but just not enough meat for the price. 

Let's hope the owners read these reviews and implement some changes, or else I won't be back. Surprisingly, I saw a "People love us on Yelp" sticker on the window. Suspicious much?

Coming from Seattle, where Pho is just as available as Starbucks, I needed to get my pho fix since I just recently moved here and have had trouble finding some places that serve it...until now!  

Since I recently moved here, I decided to go out for some pho since it's been way too long since I've had some. Came here since it's somewhat close to home and seems legit. Came in for lunch and was pleased that they had a variety of items on their menu aside from pho. Their pho options are great, however it would be nice if they had several sizes since my hubby wanted more and I wanted a little less. We both had the veggie pho and the broth and vegetables were well cooked and tasty. We thoroughly enjoyed it. We did hope that they would have meatballs like some other places we have enjoyed pho, but they sadly did not. 

Prices are appropriate for this area, staff is efficient, pho is tasty, and the place is clean. I really like that they are located right on Telegraph and it's easy to get to. I foresee coming back again sometime soon :)

ps- the places I frequented back in Seattle that served pho gave out complimentary cream puffs with pho orders. Cream puffs should be the standard everywhere, lol...hint hint ;)

They speak Vietnamese! I can order in Vietnamese! The service is fine. They responded well to our requests (i.e. more lemons) and responded promptly. 

Got the Bun Bo Hue and it had a decent amount of meat in it, which is good. Tastes nothing special...and it wasn't very spicy as Bun Bo Hue is supposed to be.

To be honest, I probably won't come back. It's not that the food is bad, it's just....nothing special. It is just A-OK. I'd rather go to Oakland for Bun Bo Hue. My friends ordered Pho and weren't happy with the portions nor the flavor. Not authentic enough, I guess. For Pho, my place would still be Saigon Restaurant II in Richmond (99 Ranch plaza) or Kang Nam Pho down Telegraph.

They take credit cards without a fee. That's always good.

It pains me to say this, but I had the worst bon bo hue today. The broth was not the bright red I was looking forward to, but a murkey yellow, almost like diluted curry. There was no chili oil or anything. In fact, the broth looked powdery and starchy. Color aside, it was the cuts of meat that really pushed it for me. There was no congealed blood and no cha lua. The steak and brisket was cut way, way too thick and sinewy. The tendon was a huge monster of a chunk. I've never seen a hunk of tendon cut like that served in a noodle soup and it would be more appropriate to use that piece to boil broth. Plus, there wasn't even that much meat at all. The plus side is that they do give you shredded cabbage and mint instead of trying to pass off basil and bean sprouts like some places. The lesson of this is to never get the bon bo hue here again. Just stick with the pho, bon, or rice plates. 

Prices are decent. The Vietnamese coffee is only served iced and there is more ice than there is coffee, though it was still good. They do not drip it in front of you, which makes me think that they just make a large drip batch in a coffee maker in the kitchen. It was only $2.

Though as much as I'll complain, I do see myself becoming a regular here, attracted by the good smell and because it's so close. I need a pho fix somehow or at least to satisfy until I get myself to a better pho place. 

cash only

As has been mentioned, this is a super clean Vietnamese restaurant. I think I was the first customer of the day at 11:20 or so. Every sriracha bottle was topped off and all of the green caps were perfectly clean with no dried sauce on the tip. The hoisin sauce bottles were similarly immaculate.

I ordered an iced coffee ($2.75), cha gio (Imperial Rolls, $3.50), and Pho Dac Biet (special combo, $7.75) with no cilantro and the rare steak on the side. In addition to the beef pho they also have, Pho Ga, Bun Bo Hue, a Bun dish, Hu Tieu, and several rice plates.

Review summary: Decent flavors. Small portions. Not enough meat in the pho.

Long version:

Reading the history of reviews, it appears they've stepped things up since their first month of operation.

I was happy to see that, unlike an earlier review, they bring out the brewing coffee to hypnotically drip in front of you (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fcdjnsgO8Z5LthXUx3y-lA?select=kKejul7ImD74Vg9VpFZpOA). I was worried about how fast it was dripping making the coffee weak (sometimes can take the entire meal) as it finished about 2 minutes after arrival, but the coffee had a nice strong flavor to it.

The Cha Gio are two smallish rolls with some pickled radish, carrots, and cabbage (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fcdjnsgO8Z5LthXUx3y-lA?select=PWYmCo0gXcIBQ6JRivdIfA) with a thick dipping sauce. I prefer a thinner Nuoc Cham. These tasted OK, but seemed a bit over priced.

The pho came in a medium sized bowl with a plate of fresh condiments (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fcdjnsgO8Z5LthXUx3y-lA?select=POnktJw5LCvwbNX9ISg3ow). 7 decent sized pieces of rare steak came with some fresh green and white onions (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/fcdjnsgO8Z5LthXUx3y-lA?select=GnYYK572VIrKm265XhbPiQ).

The broth was pretty good. Clear. Beefy with some nice spices. My mouth was getting a little dry so looks like some MSG. The noodles were overcooked and in a slightly harder to unravel than average clump in the bottom of the bowl.

In contrast to the decent amount of rare steak, the meats in the bowl (flank, brisket, tendon, tripe, beef balls) were in short supply. Half way through the bowl, I had no meat left other than a few rare steak pieces, but still plenty of noodles and broth. Unlike other reviewers, I found the meats to be tender and flavorful. Just not enough.

Pho K & K has the makings of some solid food. Just need to step it up a notch.

I came in here on opening day, and let me just say I am so glad they opened! 

Ambiance: 
The place is bright and clean, and very pleasant inside. Also it smelled good.

Food:
Note* It's not primarily a vegetarian restaurant, but they do have veg options. 
As a vegan I was thrilled with the substantial veg menu. They use vegetable broth in the vegetarian pho (with tofu!), which is awesome! That's all I had and it was great!

I will definitely be back to try more!

Their menu definitely allows for variety, but the pictures don't help. They make their food look unappealing and less appetizing than it sounds. Why are they offering Chinese-inspired rice and noodle dishes? It's just spaghetti. I'd stick with their burgers and sandwiches, like their cheesesteak. Full of flavor and good to the last bite. Fries can be a bit oversalted, but those little shoestrings are great.

I'm one of the people John's taken to experience the cheesesteak here, and I have to agree, it's fantastic.  But, it's true that if someone other than the head woman (elderly asian woman) makes it, it's only ok.  See John D's review for exhaustive details.

Decent burger and much much cheaper than Bongo Burger.
Satisfies of my occasional lunch burger craving.
I wish they had good heinz ketchup.
The lady there is nice.

I don't like the food here. I keep coming back because I have a strong aversion to hot dogs and it's the only other place open on the weekends, but I almost always regret it.

They're fries and burgers don't have any salt. That really bugs me. I had one of their cheesesteak sandwiches and I nearly got sick. Their Hawaiian chicken katsu (they call it pacific islander chicken) probably was the best thing there, but it was a little too oily for my taste. - 4 stars

Their shakes were good though. +1 star.

Taste: 2
Value: 3
Service: 4

This review is for a visit about two and a half years ago, back when they first opened. The place was pretty empty, and I walked in here since I thought I'd try it out. The lady at the counter was very friendly. I believe I ordered a chicken broccoli pasta dish, but unfortunately the lady told me that they were out of pasta and broccoli. Instead, she offered to make me something else.

About 5-10 minutes later, I was presented with some spaghetti noodles and some cooked chicken on top. It was pretty unappetizing, and I definitely could have done a better myself. She then claimed that the dish was an experiment, the first time she tried making it, and asked me how it was. To be nice, I said it was good. 

I'd give this place 1 star, but at least the lady was nice. However, their burgers (or at least the cheesesteak) seems pretty good, so I'll definitely order that if I come again.

Burgers are ok...here.  They're a tad bit cheaper here than at Bongo Burger down the street because they're a tad bit more bland (the patty, that is).  There's a tray full of condiments in seemingly unmarked random bottles/containers (looks unappetizing).  Burgers are forgettable but when you need to eat, the portion size can fill you.

The strawberry milkshake was undrinkable.  Don't believe their picture of it; it looked really good on a hot day.  I give them props for fresh ingredients (milk, a box of fresh strawberries, and ice) but when it came down to blending it together, the proportions were all wrong.  Tasted like watered down icy milk with a splash of strawberry. It was however the first time the young girl made this drink though? She kept asking her mom(?) who was busy at the time on how to make it.

This place used to be a lot better. I was gone for a few years and it wasn't the same after I got back. I used to like their lunch specials, but they just aren't that great anymore. Kind of mushy or salty. I think the quality of produce they use in their dishes has gone downhill.

Always get the grilled chicken sandwich meal here. Little Mom &...well its always the same older Asian lady (at least every time I've been) working there.  Cool little place, decent food, makes me feel comfortable.

The lady at the front was nice enough, but the food I had was bleh.  

I got the grilled chicken on rice with BBQ sauce.  It was bland and just not appetizing at all.  I wanted to go here because I thought I would definitely be getting food big enough for a couple of meals for less than $10.  It was big enough sure, but ugh.  I did not look forward to eating it again.  ~$5.75

The fries here are good though.  They were crispy and not burnt, which is enough to satisfy me.  I suppose they could add a bit more salt.  ~$2

If I ever come back, I think I'll try the cheese steak sandwich and order the fries again.  I'll update my review accordingly.
I've never tried their burgers.  I'm somewhat a fan of their chicken fried rice, although it usually is overwhelmingly salty.
Had a cheeseburger here that was so downright disgusting, I won't even think of giving this place a second chance. Plenty of better options on northside.

Alright, so maybe the execution is not so hot.

But the ideals behind Peppermint Grill make me all giddy inside.  That somebody actually had the balls to open a place like this gives me new hope for the human race.

I guess the best way to describe their culinary tradition is Hawaiian Hapa, but I have a feeling they don't even know what that is.  The resemblance is probably accidental, more likely the result of Asians from Asia trying to make Western food in the West but not quite sure whose palate they're trying to please.

Examples?  Well, "fish burgers"... which are not quite as weird if you consider that they're made of salmon... but I think it's adorable that they chose that name over "salmon burger."  The really eccentric items, though - the things that make Peppermint Grill Peppermint Grill - are not the sandwiches but the fixed plates.  Take the "crispy pork": something sort of resembling carnitas, except battered and deep-fried, on a bed of white rice, and of course topped with a fried egg.

Thing is... Peppermint Grill's food is a lot better when you're reading or writing about it than when you're seeing or eating it.  That fried egg will be overcooked, that batter will be oily and will only loosely hold onto the meat, and its porky inside will include bones.  Plus their fries might as well be microwaved potato chips.

But between five-star theory and two-star practice, mediated by very low prices, I think three stars is a fair assessment.

I wouldn't really come here again. Nothing stands out. The burger is kinda weird tasting and the fries aren't very good. I paid ~$6.50 for a burger, fries and a small drink. Service wasn't bad.

Situated in Northside Asian Ghetto, you won't have a very "clean" feel. It makes it rather uncomfortable eating. They leave the condiments sitting out, including the ranch. I don't think ranch is supposed to sit outside at room temperature....

I came up to Berkeley to have lunch with a friend who's doing an internship. He wanted to go the Hearst area, and since I'm not very familiar with the Berkeley location he picked this place.

I walked in and was bombarded with a bunch of options for my food. My friend ordered a double cheeseburger with fries and a drink, which set him back about $10. I ordered soda and the grilled garlic chicken, which comes with rice, egg, soup and salad, which set me back around $7. No idea why my meal with more food costs more than a burger and fries, but that's alright. You pour your own soda, which I like.

My soup was OK, but it wasn't very flavorful. They use Japanese-style salad dressing in their salad, which was a plus. The egg was a bit overcooked. The rice was a nice consistency, and the grilled garlic chicken was really good. My friend's burger was huge, and he said he enjoyed it, so I'll take his word for it.

The lady who works there is this sweet Asian lady who talked to us about how hot the weather is (it was 80+ degrees). Very nice.

I wouldn't go out of my way to go back here, but if I'm in the area and I want a cheap eat I wouldn't mind coming back.

The cheesesteak at the Peppermint Grill is possibly the best sandwich on the planet.  You have to get it from the head woman, though, because the other employees just don't make it like she does.  

Why so good?  The core of the sandwich is spot on: tasty mid-grade steak is smothered in cheese and garnished with grilled onions.  But, where other cheesesteak places stop, Peppermint just gets started.  The bun is thoroughly buttered before it's toasted on the grill (same grill that cooks the burgers and such, so it's extra flavorful).  Lettuce and tomato are provided as well.  

Then come the sauces.  There's really good BBQ sauce and thousand island on the tables there.  I use both in ridiculous quantities until my sandwich is overflowing with flavor.  The result is just awesome.  I'm not alone on this one; I've brought a handful of others to partake of the cheesesteak, and none have left disappointed (except when the young dude makes them sometimes).  Peppermint Grill 4 eva.  Peace.
the only thing seriously attractive about this restaurant is the cute name.
It wasnt that great. It was too salty and it was on the slightly expensive side.

mehh

the price is too expensive for what they give. 
just normal cheese sandwich.
but i like their drink and customer service and the layout of the place

I believe the melt is a relatively recent addition to berkeley! I got the classic and they added tomato and bacon for free. I love grilled cheese!! I wish they would put something other than chips as the side though seems kinda cheap. The restaurant is new and white and has a clean feel so I really like the environment.

Pricey for a grilled cheese.
Free bacon is nice.
Solid soda (made with real sugar instead of high-fructose corn-syrup).
But still, pricey.

For those of you who are native to the Pasadena/Los Angeles area, The Melt is a much more modern version of Mix n' Munch (http://www.yelp.com/biz/mix-n-munch-south-pasadena#hrid:kmKuoAr9RS-4_rjKun8vlA/src:self). And for those of you who are new to both establishments, you're in for a treat!

The Melt serves delicious, customizable grilled cheeses that are made to order until late at night. Every order comes with a side of kettle chips and you can add bacon to your melt (at no extra charge, score)! A single order is a big enough portion for a filling meal, but it's slightly on the expensive side.

I personally love the Egg in a Hole for breakfast and the Mission for lunch/dinner. Thinking about The Melt makes me miss Berkeley.. )':

Pros:
* Ambiance. The place is modern, clean, and welcoming. The use of plasma screen televisions are key in making this feel like a cool place to eat.
*Free Drinks w/ College ID: They have a soda machine that dispenses old fashion soda. 
* Location: Located right on Telegraph and Channing. Not too far from Campus, and close to student housing.

Cons:
* Price: I cant seem to justify $5 for a grilled cheese sandwich. Especially when Gordo's is RIGHT next door and I can MUCH more food for the same price. 

* Food: I guess this ties in with price, You're getting a grilled cheese sandwich. Maybe if you're a picky eat its fine, but I enjoy food diversity and flavor. The melt lacks this. The soup also isnt very impressive, and the chips are fairly greasy.  Also, for $5 I can get good cheese and Acme bread from Berkeley Bowl, and make a whole slew of grilled cheeses are home.

The food is good, but not work the price. I wont be coming back.

I went here a few days ago while visiting UCB, and oh my, I had no idea a grilled cheese sandwich could actually taste this good. I came here pretty early in the day (around noon), so there wasn't much of a line. The tables were all taken, so I went back to campus to enjoy my grilled cheese.

I got "The Mission" melt, which is a Jalapeno Jack cheese on sourdough bread. I'm one for spicy food, so I really enjoyed this. The bread is definitely heavily oiled/buttered, but that's probably why it tastes so good. There is a decent amount of cheese, but not overpoweringly so.

It was a bit pricey (about $6 for one melt), and about $9 for the combo including soup. The service is pretty quick, and as a person with an inconveniently long name, I appreciate that they call you by your initials when your food is ready.

This place is amazing. The food is great quality and very tasty. I am very impressed with the jalepeno pepper jack melt. I didn't think that any sandwich could top that, but then I stopped in for their weekly special, the jalepeno pepper popper sandwich. I couldn't believe how tasty it was. It has cheddar cheese with jalepenos and a delicious creamy layer of cream cheese. The sandwich was so warm and the texture was perfectly crisp but soft. Besides the sandwich, the restaurant looks great inside, with the white subway tile and sleek metal barstools. To top it off, the melt's soda fountain serves Boylans soda, which is usually 2 dollars a glass bottle in the store. Way better than coke or Pepsi! This place has class. And the servers are super friendly. Even tho it's a little loud, what do you expect, it's not a cafe. Don't listen to the other people on here who complain about the prices. It's the experience that matters, and this place is a great addition to telegraph. Definitely a must see.

Meh. 
I looooove me some grilled cheese, but forreal $9 for a grilled cheese meal? Puh-lease, I can make myself a heartier one at home for less than two bucks. This place is definitely overpriced and overrated.
I like that they give you free bacon and tomatoes though, and they do have some interesting flavors. It's actually pretty tasty, but I can't justify the price for the quality and quantity of the meal.
I'll indulge in this once in awhile because I live in the dorms and I don't have a kitchen available, but this is definitely out of my poor college student budget.

I ordered The Classic Combo and it was mediocre at best. The significant portion of positive reviews are from the period of free giveaway. At the $9 price tag, the portion was extremely small. 

The only positive aspect is the superior customer service and the "high-tech" atmosphere. 

Personally, I would not eat here again.

This particular branch has been open for not too long (maybe ~1 week?), and I was told that there are 3 other restaurants in San Francisco, and one other in Stanford.  Had the chance to stop by to try this pace with a friend.  This time I ordered the weekly special, which consisted of a "Grilled Mac and Cheese sandwich and tomato soup w/chips".  These are my impressions after my initial visit:

Pros:
-Love grilled cheese sandwiches!  I admit I like having cheese on lots of my food...but there's nothing like a delicious grilled cheese sandwich.  My grilled mac and cheese sandwich was good.  The tomato soup is a good companion with the grilled cheese.
-The decor is fun and dare I say, hipster.  (There was a fixie bike outside on offer as a prize...)  The inside is nice and bright with a variety of seating.  If rating just the ambience, definitely at least a 4.  Very appealing and attractive.

Cons:
-Getting a grilled cheese here...is not cheap.  Dare I say, overpriced?  Getting a combo gets you: a grilled cheese sandwich, couple handfuls of chips, and a small bowl of tomato soup.  Cost?  ...$9.  Now...in S.F. that might be cheap (I'm not too familiar with SF food, but every time I've gone, food is expensive.)  But in Berkeley?  You can get much more food that is more filling, larger quantity, and dare I say, better tasting for less.  However...if you're a CAL student, you do get a free drink: choices are fountain drinks, bottled drinks, and canned IZZE sodas.
-Food is...good, but not great.  I didn't pay attention how the grilled cheese sandwiches were cooked, but the bread was a bit oily.  The texture was good, but I'm not a huge fan of oily bread with grilled cheese.  Tomato soup is...just tomato soup.  It complements the grilled cheese well, but by itself, tastes like just an average soup.

I'm curious to see how this place does in a few months time...I'll be willing to come back here if I didn't want to eat a lot of other food Berkeley has to offer, since it's quite expensive.  Best of luck to The Melt.

I'm going to guess that the "not enough food for the cost" folks are starving students, 'cause I thought it was plenty! It's certainly enough calories! I took home the second half of my sandwich!  The black bean soup was very filling and tastey! Also my sandwich was good! nice and spicy with the cream cheese / jalapeno combo! the bread was greasy, but of course - as one would expect in a grilled cheese.

It was a pleasant surprise that the combo came with a giant pickle and some 'tater chips (as though you needed to add more grease to this meal)... I was bummed there wasn't more things to add to the sandwich like spinach or avocado or more bread choices; but generally a positive experience

Yuuuum!!! A fun gourmet grilled cheese place. A lot of ppl are complaining about the price and while it is a tad high ($8.50 for a soup and sandwich combo) it is very filling, high quality, and environmentally friendly. The price does not exceed the quality of the food. Plus, Cal students get a free drink with their ID. That being said, everything about The Melt's business model/advertising is genius, as are their tasty soup and sandwich pairings. They also have awesome breakfast sandwiches. I highly recommend!!

The Melt is good in a junk food sense.
Don't go expecting a gourmet sandwich because it's not.
Melt is pricey.

Tips:

If you order online you can pull up the QR code on your smartphone and The Melt has a scanner for you to check-in for your order to start cooking. You get to skip the line!

--------------------------------------------------

So it's about $4.89 for just a sandwich and around $9 for a sandwich and soup combo.

Italian Job - My favorite so far at The Melt. This sandwich is grilled on top of a special garlic bread which tastes amazing! I highly recommend getting this sandwich.

The Mission - A sandwich with pepperjack cheese and personally I was a bit disappointed with this sandwich. It's too spicy for my taste because I don't take spicy foods very well.

Sweet Corn soup - Very sweet and delicious.

Taste: 4 Stars (not much of a grill cheese expert, but I like their bread & cheese! You don't get that yucky taste from paninis that are drenched in non-stick spray)

Portion & Price: 1 Star ($10 for a combo is way too expensive... especially when the portion is so small! Although their ingredients are probably top notch, the price is still too much for college students...)

Overall: 3 Stars... Would have been a 2 stars, but I give them props for using good ingredients & trying to be green. However, the price is still too much just for a small grill cheese, small soup, some potato chips, and a drink.

Came here for the free sandwich+soup combo that they were handing out a few weeks ago and got the Asiago combo, which contained brie cheese (mmm!!). This place definitely is filled with comfort food, but I really have to wonder how they can justify the high price. I know that it's brie, and it's accompanied by delicious mushroom soup, but a $9 for a grilled cheese sandwich and a small cup of soup is crazy expensive.

However, the technology (for lack of a better word) they use inside the restaurant is quite innovative relative to Berkeley standards. You can order in advance and Berkeley students get a free drink with their student ID!

On another note, I really like how they got into the Berkeley community through their participation at Caltopia and how they gave away free sandwiches.

I have not been to the restaurant on Telegraph. But they were raffling off a cool bike at Caltopia today, though, and I entered to win and stood in a long line for quarter-sized pieces of grilled cheese sandwiches:  I scooped up two flavors and wanted to try all three that they presented but I felt guilty. The kids moving the sandwiches didn't care. I should have taken more after the long line.

My two samples were very, very good. I can't make that same sandwich: they must use good grease and a fast, hot grilling technique. It was very tasty.

Eight bucks for bread and cheese and labor and marketing and rent?  In 2012? That's about what things cost. Doesn't it cost that much to buy a meal at McDonald's and more at Chipotle?

They are selling comfort food to college kids. 
And, price aside, the sandwiches were really good. But, then again, I did not pay and I never would.
