A grilled brie would cost me at least three or four bucks in ingredients cause I would only buy very good bread, grill in good butter and buy very good cheese. Is that what Melt does? At this Caltopia booth, no info:  just kids working very hard to keep up with the endless line.

I bet they do very well.

I believe economic research demonstrates that out of all categories of society, college students as a class have more disposable income than almost any other social category. They typically don't have any debt service, live in dorms or shared housing that is lower than working folks pay and parents still supporting them.

I know it is the tradition for all students to gripe about being poor and I know the economy has bitten into college kids' lifestyles -- just like almost everyone's lifestyles -- but I am confident kids will have money to buy yummy comfort food like these sandwiches.

5$ for a grilled cheese sandwich.....The restaurant itself is nice and the staff was friendly......but all they have are grilled cheese sandwich, no different from what you and I can make at home for 5$

They were giving out FREE food Thurs 8/23/12 until the food runs out on or before Midnight.  Stood in line for 1hr, we are crazy!  

When got a sample of the Mushroom soup while in line.  Good it was free, just ok tasting.  We got to try The Mission Combo, no meat given.  It came with a grilled cheese sandwich, pickle, chips, & soup (Sweet Corn Tortilla), plus a cup to help our self to a drink I picked Boylan Rootbeer.

CAL Marching Band came up & played for us.  That was nice.

So this place was great for a late night nosh after a show at the Greek Theater, but I seriously doubt I would return...I had the Classic Combo - it was cheesy, but the bread really isn't grilled well....it's too doughy, and everything is way to salty. Also the price of the food for what you get is just not worth it.
Definitely on okay choice if you just want a cheesy sleazy snack...middle of the road choice.

Fighting World Hunger..one small grilled cheese sandwich at a time?


Mind you..I understand this is a business that needs to be profitable so they can accomplish thier goal of helping to feed the needy, but you have the needy right outside your door.... so start there. 

I am a fan of most foods filled with cheese, so I was convinced by a line of people this would be worth the wait. Well, needless to say I was BAMBOOZLED..but I am glad I wasn't the only one. I had a Classic Combo, tastey, yet slightly missing the mark. Besides..you can really make it at home for less than nine dollors.

Overall nice set up, good service and cause, but I think one time is good enough.

Meh.

I was excited about this place and thought it was promising, but it unfortunately didn't live up to the hype. I got the Mission Combo (Jalapeño Pepper Jack on Sourdough & Sweet Corn Tortilla Soup) for $8.75. It's a bit pricey for what it actually is. The little cup of soup is $3.95 alone, and it's not even good. It tasted like pureed baby food with a mushy/grainy texture. Bleh. I didn't even finish it. The sandwich was okay, but it could have used some more cheese. It wasn't oozing the gooey goodness that I was craving, but the flavors were decent. Each sandwich comes with Kettle brand chips and a pickle spear.

However, I did enjoy the atmosphere. The decor is bright and pleasing to the eye. They have a screen that shows you all the upcoming orders so that you can see if they are working on your order and what place you are in. They also have the option to order your meal online, allowing you to skip the line when you get there by scanning the QR code you are given. Very techy but cool. Someone from the marketing team came over to our table to gauge our opinions on the price and the product, which showed me that the company actually cared about the satisfaction of their customers and their overall experience while dining. 

P.S. They add bacon and/or tomatoes onto your sandwich for FREE and give Cal students a FREE drink with the purchase of a combo.

Ordered The Mission combo ($8.75) today for lunch. The Mission is jalapeno pepper jack cheese on sour dough bread. The soup included is the sweet corn tortilla. To be honest, the sandwich was way too basic and ordinary. The soup tastes better than the sandwich. The pickle just didn't fit with the sandwich so I just dipped it in the soup.

For $8.75, the price is way too high. Ordering online doesn't really help with the wait. There were at least 20 people staffed today for opening but it was so slow. It's not like Chipotle where you can just go in and out in a few minutes. I waited for a good ten minutes for my combo even after scanning the QR code at the counter. I don't anticipate long lines here for what it's worth. Sadly, an acquaintance who knows the owner of the chain highly recommended The Melt to me but after trying it today, wouldn't recommend it right off the bat.

The Melt has scheduled giveaways but i missed them. menu has 5 staple sammies. sammie (4.95), soup (3.95), combo (8.95+). 

eats: italian job, sammie, fontina & provolone(4.95)
-interesting taste of cheese, garlic bread greasy
-1/2 spear pickle crunchy, not sour
-potato chips semithicked, way too salty


crumbs:
-mechanized system, humans friendly, courteous, efficient.
-soup made by machines as is sammie.....
-little parking available
-some inside seating available
--is the competition toast? very efficient dispensing of food.
-value resides in the eyes of the beholder.

--General
They were giving away free combo meals for their opening promotion, and I went twice (I'm sorry, hehe). It's very close to campus and conveniently located, and the atmosphere is very modern, young, and cute. There is seating inside, but not too much especially for groups. Try to have somewhere else to eat the sandwich or hope you get lucky (grassy areas on campus is a good idea and close by!)

--Food
Their combo is $9 for a grilled cheese sandwich, a soup, chips, and a pickle, all conveniently packaged into a nice little to-go box. A grilled cheese by itself is $5 and a soup is $4, if you get them singly.

I personally love the portions for the combo, its just the perfect amount of food for me to be satisfied/full without bursting like typical American portions. I do know that a lot of my friends eat more than me, so you may have a different opinion.

The grilled cheeses are delicious! Probably the best grilled cheeses I've had; I've tried The Classic with the Two Tomato Basil Soup, and The Mission Job with the Corn Tortilla Soup. Both were great, but I'd recommend the Classic over the Mission Job. Their tomato soup is amazing (I don't usually like tomato soup), and their chips are quality chips.

I realize this place is a bit pricey for what you get, but I'd recommend trying it at least once!

This is a brand new store. They were offering people
 free food until closing time. So I jump into their line of people and waited for a free meal.

Why did their grilled cheese sandwich was better than mine. And, how is it that their tomato soup is good to the to the last slurp.

This was the best tasting meal I've had all week.

BASIC grilled cheese sandwiches. That's basically what you're paying $7-9 for. 

I ordered the Parisian (Brie with honey apple on Country French). It comes with some potato chips and a half-sliced pickle. I thought the apple pieces gave it a nice little hint of sweetness...but still nothing special. 

I was a little iffy about the price before I decided to order, but I thought "What the hell...these must be some damn good grilled cheese sandwiches if they're going to be this expensive." 

But nope! That def wasn't the case...

I assume if you're a grilled cheese fanatic, you'd love this place. But I'm not....so this is why I sum up my experience as "meh"

Dude... nine bucks for a underwhelming, and more importantly, tiny grilled cheese sandwich in a college town filled with starving students and homeless Phish-heads with dogs to feed?  Okay, College Ave. I'd understand, but Telegraph?  Really?  Yeah yeah, the line's out the door right now -- perhaps the fact they're giving away FREE grilled cheese sandwiches may have everything to do with that.  LMAO.  

Epic fail.

During move-in weekend every time I passed by The Melt the line was out the door. After I finally got my things settled in and had some free time I decided to give this place a try. I chatted a bit with the manager and found out that the restaurant is only a few days old! You can certainly tell it's new by the perky attitudes of the employees and super cleanliness of the place. The atmosphere of the restaurant immediately reminded me of Burger Lounge in San Diego. The combination of orange and white colors, the sustainable eating utensils and packaging, and the the simple menu all were a friendly welcome. 

Now onto the food. I tried the weekly special which was the pizza melt sandwich. They layer pepperoni, fontina and provolone cheese, and pizza sauce between slices of garlic bread. You can also add bacon or tomato for free which I think is pretty awesome. The combo comes with a side of soup (with this sandwich, tomato basil), some chips, a pickle and a drink. Cal students get the drink for free with your Cal1 card! 

The sandwich itself was pretty tasty. Nothing spectacular. The soup, however, was really good. As good, if not better, than the sandwich. And not being a fan of tomato soup to begin with that's saying a lot. It was rich, creamy, and really flavorful. Dip the sandwich into the soup. DO IT. 

Overall the food is a bit pricey, so I'll deem The Melt an occassional visit kinda place.

Came on a Friday around lunchtime, and boy was it crowded! Luckily, I was able to order online so I could avoid the line; all I had to do was go scan my QR code receipt at the front to input my order. I didn't have to wait long, it probably only took a total of 5 minutes after I had placed my order for them to make it!

I got the Parisian combo: Brie and Apple honey grilled cheese with wild mushroom soup, which comes with some chips and a pickle. The soup was pretty tasty, although the color was a grayish-brown and not very appetizing looking. The grilled cheese, on the other hand, looked pretty impressive! The bread was a seasoned french roll, and I got a free bacon add-on! However, the combo of the Brie with Apple Honey didn't work for me: The honey overpowered the cheese, and my sandwich just tasted sweet... If I come back, I'll definitely be trying a different sandwich!

Overall, I was very impressed with the efficiency of the restaurant and their menu options, but not so impressed with the Parisian combo I chose (but the other combos look like they could be much tastier). Also, at $9 per combo, it's pretty pricy for a grilled cheese sandwich and soup. I'll probably come back to try other combos, but it's not exactly a go-to place for me.

either,

peel my cheese 
from filmy plastic squares.
square it down with two bleach-white 
wonder slices- 

or, 

carve me a wedge of something french and erudite 
stucco it between the bread of artisans   
and elevate my brow. 

but, 

do not ask me to dwell 
in this liminal sandwich. 
to revel in it's half-baked
aspirations towards gastronomy. 

this sandwich, 
--"baguette" giving like a colombo roll, 
bacon steamed and waxy, 
waning in a stingy stratum of 
baby brie, (so fetal in flavor)--  
is a charlatan! 

And I cannot pay $8.00 
to indulge you and your ketchup soup's 
delusions, 
poser sandwich. 

But I like your staff and you have very clean bathrooms.

Mushroom burger or Turkey burger for me whenever I come here. Both of them taste ...standard. No extraordinary ingredients or anything. I think of this place as the equivalent of the bigger fast food chains if there were any in Berkeley (excluding Mickey Ds). 

I mean I guess, between McDs and here, I'd go here, but that's not exactly a tough choice, quality and location-wise. The buns are kinda nice--a little crisp and not all soggy and soft. Not much more to say. Cashier/Service was quick and nice. Place is pretty clean. This location doesn't have that much seating and its windows are so big, I almost stepped through the frame of one once because I thought it was the door.

I like this place but they often mess up my food. Almost every time I have to wait for it to be remade... Today I'm in a rush and I had to wait over 20 mins because they acted like it was my fault. Everyone else after me got served before I did. Horrible customer service. I don't think I'll be back here anytime soon.
Very yummy, non-greasy, reasonably priced burgers await.

I have always walked by Bongo Burger and have always heard a lot about it but I had never once gone in and ate any food. It wasn't until last night that my friends stormed into my room happy that finals were over that we decided to get some late dinner at Bongo Burger.

I wasn't too hungry and so I had the large hummus with two pita. The order came to a little more than $4 after tax and I had to take home some of the hummus, sweet! I love hummus and Mediterranean food and so I was kind of suspicious of a burger joint offering hummus. I didn't know that they were Persian and I certainly didn't expect the great hummus! 

Their burgers were pretty sweet (I took a bite out of my friends' burgers) and the crinkle-cut fries are simple but a classic. You could never get enough! 

While it was a bit expensive than what a burger usually is, their hummus and sides are pretty reasonably priced. I'll have to come back and try the Persian burger or maybe the mushroom burger. I do love my mushrooms (they're my favorite fungus)!

I had never heard of a Persian burger, but this joint has some of the best burgers ever! I was very impressed by the taste. I don't even remember what burger I ordered, but it was really good. The hummus was amazing too.

There was a period of time in my life where I was going to Bongo Burger every other day. If I had not recently become more concerned with my health, I would probably still be going there as frequently as I did in the past. 

First off, I just want to say that the meals are definitely filling and worth the $7-9 price. I've had 3 of their burgers: the Persian Burger, the Black Bean Burger, and the Cheeseburger. The Black Bean Burger is by far my least favorite. It tastes like crappy Mexican food mushed up into patty form which is placed in the middle of two pieces of bread. GROSS. The Persian Burger is pretty freaking good, however, my heart is devoted to the Cheeseburger (literally). I can't pinpoint why it tastes so good, but it is very satisfying (maybe it's the Niman Ranch beef). The thick, crisp cut fries are always the right extent of crispiness and are perfected by adding ranch (which is not really ranch but some ranch like sauce. It's the best fake ranch like sauce I've ever had)

The cartoonish semi-nude picks on the wall also definitely add to the meal.
SUPER fast service; DELICIOUS food.  Prices are reasonable and very affordable.  I love the option of a half burger on a french baguette  - AWESOME.

I decided to check this place out after reading the reviews. I have to admit it didn't disappoint. The Persian burger is served with lamb meat, lettuce, tomato, mayo, served on a roll. If you add the onion rings and a drink, it will cost you around 10 bucks. Now, considering that the portions are huge and definitely tasty, it's a pretty good place to go. If you are looking for some gourmet burgers that have expensive herbs and spices, this isn't the place for you. I'm only talking to those that want some cheap eats and huge portions...good food that's it. What else could you want from a burger joint.

I LOVE BONGO BURGER! Whenever I'd walk down from the UCB campus and take the BART home for either lunch or dinner, I'd contemplate about pigging out at this delicious joint.

The burgers are AMAZING. They (and the fries) are made on-order so everything is fresh and hot when you pick up your order. The buns are toasted to give you that extra bready crisp when you sink your teeth into burger heaven. The meat is the perfect blend of salty, beefy, chewy, soft, and anything else the meat should be on a burger. I love the dressing they use on their burgers to lightly add taste to their shredded lettuce and veggies.

I LOVE these fries. Sometimes I go to this place just for the fries. They are shaped in the crinkle style and perfectly salted. Crispy, crunchy, juicy, moist... yum. The combo meals come with a drink too so you'd get a filling lunch or dinner for just $8 (including tax).

I wish I had a Bongo Burger near where I live now that I've graduated from Berkeley.

This place is a solid 3 stars, maybe approaching 4, but I'm only giving them 3 since everything is good, but I'm not sure it's I ever particularly crave it.  I always think my meal was pretty good when I go, but that's sorta the limit of my enthusiasm, "pretty good."

Bonuses are that they have some middle-eastern fare in addition to the regular burgers.  This is something you can't get most places.  Stuff like falafel or lamb burger or something.  That and they serve the burgers on something besides Wonder Bread-type buns.  The burgers didn't seem horribly greasy or anything.  Good, but I came for the burger not as much for middle eastern options.

On the bad side, the location is small and usually pretty cramped if you go when people are there.  I guess you could walk over to People's Park and eat with homeless people or something if you can't deal with the claustrophobic crowding.  It's pretty tiny to eat there.  Oh, yeah, I seem to remember some attitude sometimes, but it's been a while.

I do like the burgers slightly above average.  It's pretty much one of the better cheap-ish burger places near campus, except for Smart Alec's which is a thinner and completely different kind of burger (with baked fries).  Or Oscars which is a grease-slathered cheapo drive in-type Americana burger (good in a sorta trashily delicious way).  Or the overpriced "gourmet" burgers at someplace like Barneys.

Who knew there were so many varieties of burgers within a reasonably close distance to campus?

Anyway, decent burger for a sorta healthier fast-food, but not trashy kinda burger with middle eastern options if you want them.  Less obnoxiously hippy-tarian-seeming and faux-healthy than Smart Alec's (just saying, even though Smart Alec's is about as ok). Somehow I can't elevate it to four stars, though, since it's just not stand out better than anything else to me.  I like it but rarely feel the urge to eat here in any addictive way..
two words.. Persian Sandwich

When did this place get so expensive? The food is pretty good (esp the mushroom burger), but you can get a sandwich at Gregoire for the same price as some here. For the price of pretty good you can get 'actually good' food elsewhere.

Ah Bongo Burger. So consistent. So wonderful.

I may dream about their onion rings.

They put grilled onions on their burgers!

I've heard their breakfast food and falafel is pretty good too.

Can bongo burger do anything wrong? I don't know.

I LOVE bongo burger!  Not only for its convenience and proximity to campus, but its delicious mushroom burger!! Def recommend getting that if you're okay with the shrooms :)  Also, I really love the fries here, they remind me of mcdonald fries, just without the sogginess.  I always ask for ranch to dip the fries in, and I love it!

Great great great onion rings! Had to start off saying that. The turkey burger I had was a good solid tasty burger (though I was highly upset to learn they didn't have pickles, as no burger, sandwich or the like is quite the same without them). Kudos for the delicious, buttery, flaky bun; it made the burger.  Not the best burger I've ever had, but a solid find ... I wouldn't mind coming again

Keeping rating at 3 stars.

I came here a few weeks ago and tried their persian burger since I've only had it once before. It definitely failed to meet my expectations. The meat was okay, but the sandwich was just very plain. It's definitely not worth the $7-8.
Berkeley is too fast food deprived. Come on, burgers that come from a long plastic sleeve of frozen costco patties aren't that great. They're not even good.
Best place in Berkeley for a good burger.  I've only tried a couple of the burgers and the steak sandwich - - all good.  Call ahead and order to save some time.

I have been craving a turkey burger from Bongo Burger for weeks. I have an extremely sensitive stomach and I didn't get weird after eating here, which is rare for a fast food restaurant. This is because the burgers here are fresh and not super greasy. Amazing. Check it out if you are in the area and are craving a burger. Can't wait to eat there again!

Mmmmmm. I love Bongo Burger. It's my favorite burger place in Berkeley.
I usually get the hamburger combo. The hamburger bun is crisp on the outside and soft on the inside. The beef is nicely cooked and all the fillings match up nicely. It does drip a bit but it doesn't get too messy. However, the best thing about bongo burger is the FRIES. The crinkle-cut is pretty unique. They are crispy and nicely salted. It's not oily at all. Even after they've gone cold, they've still got that crunch. So delicious. I would go back just to get the fries. The food is five stars. Nom nom nom.

As for the restaurant itself, there's ample seating and I've never had trouble finding a space to sit. The service is nice and quick. The location can lead to some interesting characters but the restaurant workers are pretty good at solving issues.

I am a vegetarian and I love to eat here.  Usually I get the falaffel and it is delicious!  When I was broke and driving home I would often stop here and get some dinner.  This place is inexpensive.  I love it.  They need more of these everywhere.  The food is fresh.  I probably ate there 50 times, and never a bad experience.  A great place when you want to get full and not spend much.

This place is the definition of a greasy spoon.  I ordered a cheeseburger meal and was satisfied, but it didn't blow my burger mind or anything.  My companion got a turkey burger and was left asking "where's the beef" (translation: less than impressed).  You have to go behind the counter to use the bathroom, which I would rate 1 star (tiny, dirty, walk past the kitchen crew preparing raw meat, etc.).

Overall, I'd say it's a decent place to get a cheap, quick greasy fix.  Burger connoisseurs should go elsewhere.

Blast to the past!! We used to eat these when we lived in Berkeley, and this week end we took our youngest son to his dorm, and we had Bongo Burgers.... As tasty as we remember it!!
I guess good things don't need to change!
persian burger so good!!! thats it

Nice little place to grab some great old fashion burgers and crinkle fries. The burgers are pretty big.  Location is descent with little shops around it. Neighborhood is a little ruff after dark. All in all, great food at a good price. Worth the stop.

The burgers are above average. The prices are a little steep however. 

Persian Burger is AMAZING and you must try it. Perks to this place are they have a nice seating area and the environment is warm and welcoming. They give you ranch and ketchup to dip your burgers and fries in so that is nice. The fries are average usually, and sometimes not freshly made.

Overall: Great burgers, but pricey for college students. Might as well go all in and try the Persian Burger!

I went here after a few cold beverages at Raleighs. Because I thought the wings were a joke, I was still hungry and didn't want to drive all over Berkeley. 
 I've learned never to watch anyone cook my food, so I ordered my double burger combo and sat.  I wish I would have eating there, but my potty was calling me at home, so I had to take it to go. Even ten minutes after I got it, it was hot and tasty.  
 Next time I'll eat there. The fries were good, as well as the Baklava. Service was fine too.

I am by no means a burger fan. Honestly, the only ones I'll really consider eating are Wendy's. But Bongo Burger is my exception. The best burger-and-fries joint I have ever stepped foot in. Service is good (though the guys behind the counter tend to eye me more often than not). Prices are fair. Seating is always available. Yum!
bongo burger...not bad ...but not the best.  If I am in the neighborhood, I'll stop by.

After I tried their delicious Eggplant Plate, that's all I ever get when I come here. The perfect combination of veggies + swiss cheese + hummus that you can scoop up in one delicious bite with pita bread, yum!
I'm not really a burger kinda guy, but dam bongos makes some dam good burgers. The bread was of the hook. I like this place a lot.

A coworker had recommended Bongo Burger to a group of us and so we all adventured over to Bongo Burger for some lunch.  After an adventure through Telegraph to find the restaurant, we ordered and got our food.  

I ordered a bacon burger with fries. The burger included a thin pattie cooked well done on a toasted sesame bun filled with the standard condiments in it.  The fries were swiggly fries that were slightly crunchy, but mostly soft.  In general, I was not too wowed by the meal.  I really didn't like the amount of sesame that was on the bun (a few flakes I can deal with, an entire bun with toasted sesame?  not so much) and the meat didn't have much flavor.  I only a few of my french fries but I couldn't have cared much for them.  They weren't seasoned nor did they hold that crunch french fry texture.

My coworkers weren't too equally impressed by their burgers, though my friend's chicken sandwich looked a lot more appetizing and fulfilling than our burgers did...

i only tried the all american burger, which had a nice toasted bun with cheese, medium well done patty, lettuce and tomato. it was quite delicious, esp the way that toasted the bun!! i wish the meat could be a little hotter since i like hot cold, but over all, pretty good food. it was $4.95 for the burger, didn't come with fries or drink. nice hanging out location for students. would i go again? i think so!

The black bean burger is so good!

It's a real no-frills place with good burgers.  My husband got the falafel, and he thought it was just ok, but I loved my [black bean] burger and my sister really enjoyed her bacon burger.  The fries are pretty standard, and there are fountain drinks, fresh orange juice, and different teas.

I'd pair up the burgers with a nicer bun, though.

great muncy food. i have been  literally eating here all my life so i may be a little bias (also i am Persian and my weakness is lamb ) if you are a lamb fan get the Persian burger, if your not a big eater you may even have enough for another meal( this burger is not small )

Went here with a friend after a long bike ride through the Oakland Hills...man did this place hit the spot.

I ordered the persian burger, a delightfully satisfying blend of lamb and beef in a delicious baked roll.  Also ordered the side Mediterranean salad which was a great compliment to the burger.  Add a small drink and french fries for a total $12 and this place just rocked!

bongo burger s on point. it's one of the few establishments in the telegraph area i haven't grown weary of. admittedly, it's because i try not to come here too much lest i begin looking like i weigh like i come here too much. 

but i am a bit of a burger nerd. and i can spot a quality burger from 45 ketchup packets away. yeah. i measured. 

their burgers are really good. i only wish they'd use bacon that was less chewy. the bacon they use tastes alright but it sticks in my teeth. 

my favorite item here is the turkey burger. and everyone should try the persian joint. 

crinkle fries are the thizzness. 

and that's pretty much it. 

oh and the workers are always cool as penguin pussy.

I had their mushroom burger and loved it! It gets everywhere, so I had to eat a lot of it with a fork, but so worth it! For people who like real, somewhat greasy burgers, this is your best bet. (For a delicious burger sans grease, try Smart Alec's up the street.) Every time I pass by there it's pretty crowded, so if you come in a group, have a friend snag a table before it's snatched up.
Awesome persian burger, pretty good regular burger, and fast.  A little on the pricey side for fast food, but its worth every penny.

I Would come here and order the mushroom burger meal and every time I would visit, I was always satisfied. The burgers here are absolutely juicy!  Plain and Simple!  I wish there was a Bongo Burger in SD because if there was, I would definitely be there all the time. ):
Seems more like a thin restaurant burger than a fast food burger. It's large but thin and not spectacular. It's good but not spectacular to recommend.

so, after going back here a couple more times i'm upgrading these dudes to a solid 5. the burger and sandwiches are consistently delicious. they cook everything to order and put care into the preparation, which is unusual at this price range. usually for 3-6 bucks you'll get a heat lamp burger. the crispy bun is what really wins me over i think. something about a toasted burger bun paired with a juicy (medium rare on request) hamburger patty is just the bees knees. also the turkey burger is one of the best i've ever had. all of this is enough for me to look past the backward drink refill policy. plus i usually just pickup a 40oz on the way home anyway.
Their Persian burger was great

The vegetarian bean burger was fantastic!  The fries were crinkle cut, which always makes me happy.  The woman behind the counter was nice enough and the burgers came out quickly.

They charged for refills, which made me a little sad since I love refills.  Even if you only get one.  Just one refill would have helped this place boost itself in my rating.  So if you aren't a soda fan, this place might be burger heaven on earth for you

Pretty good burger - but, if you are hooked on this place, take a little visit to the restroom -         G R O S S.  I WILL NEVER GO AGAIN.  This is the same restroom the staff uses and it is not habitable.  Repeat - inhabitable - should not pass any inspection in my estimation.  Who cares about the food - get a quick peek in here and you'll not care any longer!  Note to any wheelchair visitor - there is NO WAY you would ever be able to use this restroom.  I don't know how the City of Berkeley and their ADA requirements allow this.

OMG! I am crazy for their dolmas! They are homemade and cost 50 cents each. Also the burgers. I so love the Persian Burger, so big I save half for lunch the next day. It is lamb on super fresh roll. Black Bean Burger is flavorful, moist, so heathy I get the fries too.

Bongo Burger is one of those places you go to when you're really hungry and just really want a burger and fries. They have other stuff too, of which I've only tried the lamb sandwich, which was delicious.

Recently they changed their buns so it's kinda hit and miss with those. They are either too big and crispy or flaky and hard. Every now and then you'll get one that is perfect-soft on the inside and slightly crisp on the outside. Fabulous. 

I don't know what the poster below me is talking about with the meat being "too red" since they seem to cook their meat medium well to well. I've never had a red burger from there-seems like you can't really cook ground meat like that. 

Anyway, the service is fine-to be expected from a fast food place. They are a bit standoffish, which honestly works in my favor because I can't stand overly friendly staff. Yes, you have to get your fat, lazy ass up to get forks and ketchup and salt and other things you might need. This is a three-steps up from McDonald's fast food place, not Harris'.

the persian burger may be the most flavorful i've ever had.  the taste of lamb and swiss cheese will be permanently ingrained in my taste buds' memory.  although, my only complaint has to be too much bread and not enough meat.  but it's a minor transgression for the best...

Bongos is really a three-point-five tops, but Yelp doesn't allow half points, and I'm feeling generous tonight.  The falafel is very good, the fries are too, but the burger ... well, it's my fault for noticing only midway through my dried-out husk of a dead-cow that the "Best of the Bay" signs they so proudly display are all from about eight years ago.  I think my burger dated from the same era.  Making the whole thing even less palatable was the cranky woman who took our order.  The cooks all looked like they were having fun anyway, but the woman -- presumably part owner, at least -- was sour and unpleasant to us and them alike.  Yikes.

Hands down, my FAVORITE place to get a burger in Berkeley. It's consistent, it's decently priced, it's fast, it's Niman Ranch meat, it's crispy CRINKLE CUT FRIES WITH THINNED OUT RANCH and it's CRISPY BUNZZZ!!! Yes, warm crispy toasty sesame seeded buns, where else does this exist no where that's why Bongo Burger get's a five. Try it they way I like it: hold the mustard and raw onions and you got gold baby.

Oh, and their Mediterranean stuff is pretty tasty too.

I've come here a few times. Everytime has been very good. The Persian Burger is good lamb. Not greasy at all like some lamb can be. It's funny, I'm Persian and realized today that I was the only person in the place who gets the regular cheese burger which I love. The fries are simple, crinkle cut fries, but man are they tasty. Nice and crispy. Good food for sure.

as i watch them make my food, i am amazed at how efficient they are. they understand teamwork and they get really close to the grill. that's crazy. they are dedicated and i appreciate it.

and the food's good.

I was sold with the Persian burger. Lamb in a burger...?! I ordered the combo number 7 that comes with zigzag fries and a drink for 9.50ish. I was starving when I got my food. The edges of my burger were sort of dry, but by the time I took a couple bites I was pretty satisfied. I think if I had Tzatziki sauce with me I would have plopped it right on. 

I think Bongo is a place everyone in Berkeley likes to recommend for burgers but it's different than those tiny fast food places. I've tried Barney's down on Shattuck and these two are similar in the taste of the patty (a little more charred) but Bongo has a slightly better taste (Barney's has too many flavors)

I should also mention that the first time I tried this place I was really craving In-N-Out but friends recommended Bongo Burger to satisfy my craving. If you're looking for in-n-out, Bongo isn't really what you're looking for!

Also, they have fresh squeezed orange and carrot juice! :)

I just had the experience of eating a Bongo Burger yesterday, while on my trip to San Francisco.  My cousin recommended this place to me and my friend, saying that his was the place that he went to whenever he got hungry and was too lazy to walk all over the place.  

When we got there, instead of ordering a traditional burger, I ended up ordering their... HUMMUS sandwich!!!  I am a sucker for Hummus and I always make sure to get a side of hummus whenever it's available, but I thought maybe this will taste good.  And it was, until about halfway through.  Let this be a lesson to everyone, there CAN be too much of a good thing.  The sandwich was very large for the price I paid and it was stuffed with Hummus, Lettuce, Onions and Tomatoes.  It was delicious from the first bite but Hummus has a very distinct taste that needs to countered with something else or else you'll get sick and tired of it. 

Needless to say, that was the only thing I ordered and fries wouldn't have helped since they have such a neutral taste.  I ended up finishing the burger but I will make sure NEVER again to order a pure hummus sandwich.

My friend got a more traditional affair with a Bacon Cheeseburger which filled him up quite well, maybe next time I'm in the area, I'll make sure to eat a normal sandwich.  The service was good and the food came out extremely quick.

OMFG this is what a burger is suppose to taste like.  Fries are fair.  Been here after getting the munchies from toking with friends and had to have something better than that nasty fast food crap.  This place makes them all shameful.  Burgers are made to order.  menu is limited but choices are good.  I always leave satisfied.

They make a damn fine burger here, flat but with a large surface area. Tasty, especially with bacon, very satisfying overall. Fries are good, I only wish you got more of them. One problem, however, is that everything costs about $2.00 more than I'd like. For about the same price you can get a bigger, Flame Gourmet burger on college. Still good though.

Great burgers, reasonable prices. Most surprisingly of all, however, is the quality of their Persian food; I'm a fan of Persian food in general, and for such a reasonable price from a restaurant that doesn't strive to be fancy, they churn out some decent Persian grub here.

Maybe the best and most reasonably priced burger place in Berkeley.Their fries are quality ones, though sometimes a little undercooked(usually they're perfect).Burgers of course are good but my fvoirte is their steak sandwiches.SO awesome.And one of the other awesome things about Bongo Burger?They're not cash only!!So many places in this area are cash-only and it's a pain in the ass but Bongo Burger knows what's up.

Bongo burger has been a staple for me for the last year and a half.  They have a lot of vegetarian options and have some of the best fries you can get in Berkeley.

Aside from their burgers their falafel is actually really good too, but unfortunatley there are no combos (with fries and a drink) that come with the falafel.

Great food, decent price (~$10/meal), yum.
A+ burgers,  A+ fries (esspecially when made extra crispy),  Beautiful chicken and falafel plates, all at a great price!  I love this place!

Bongo Burger is one of my favorite businesses in Berkeley.

You get a quality burger for a great price. Toasted bun, Niman Ranch meat, grated lettuce, tomato, etc. And the fries are delicious.

They also do a few things a little bit differently, not that you're getting an unusual burger experience or anything. They butter the buns, and provide ranch alongside the ketchup. It's good.

A hamburger and fries is less than 7 bucks. The lady who works at the dwight location is gorgeous and regal. And there are several locations very close to the Berkeley campus. If you're a student and you've been in the library studying for hours and you stumble out into the dying light wondering how far your plummeting blood sugar is going to get you - know that there is Bongo Burger - right outside North gate on Euclid, on Southside on Dwight and Telegraph, and out of West Gate on Center.

Bottom line: burgers are delicious, economically priced, consistently good, and available from multiple locations close to campus.

Really Yummy burgers. Definitely would come back here, definitely would walk the 4 blocks from campus to get here if I'm looking for a good burger. I've  only have tried the American burger here.

Only real downside is that the place is small and usually crowded, and its a little more expensive than some other places.

The description below is right on. So when I went to Bongo Burger, I heard about this fake meat burger. I didn't try it because I don't like them no matter what, so I actually don't remember what I had, but I remember that it really didn't seem all that worth it to me. Even the fries left a lot to be desired. Anyway, why 4 stars? it's close to where my friends live and really, it's not all that bad. They could do with some specials or something like that. Competition my friends!

I'm a big fan of burgers - restaurant burgers, fast food burgers and everything in between. Bongo Burger here is about as forgettable as any burger can be. There's absolutely nothing outstanding about it.

The burgers are generally dry and virtually inedible without a soda. They're not very generous with the meat either, although the service itself is quite good.

Yelp defines the 2-star rating as "Meh, I've experienced better" so that's what I'm going with. You can get a much better meal elsewhere in the area for the same amount of money.

NOTE: My college roommate LOVED Bongo Burger and ate it almost every other day. I'm not sure why, but I suppose it does work for some people.

Oh Bongo Burger! How I dream of you from across the pond. 

And all your Persian burger deliciousness. 

*Sigh*

Way back to mid 90's, I was so impressed how juicy this burger was.  Still it is quite a good one as a fast food.  
Personal note: when I was eating on 8/7 Friday...around 5 pm, a girl was sitting by herself at outside table, eating some sushi box form other place.  She was really cute....really.
I love this place. I always get mushroom burger with fries and ranch on the side. tastes awesome.

This place is a sleeper! The Persian burger is bomb! The fries are really good too. Nice and crispy!

You kinda have to look around for this place cuz its not right in your face and the store front isnt too impressive... but the food is really good and its pretty fast. Would come here again.

That's one tasty black bean burger.

Fries are only ok; I'd recommend the onion rings.

I used to live only two blocks away from Bongo Burger and eat at this joint for their amazing food all the time. It is a comfortable little restaurant with delicious food at a very affordable price.

As the name suggests, they serve a variety of burgers here. Mushroom burger and bacon burger are always delicious and Bongo's versions are to die for. The burgers are made fresh and the portion is generous. Other than burgers, they serve some Mediterranean plates and sandwiches. They are healthy alternatives which are delicious at the same time.
Been going here since 1984. I have tried several persian burgers elsewhere. THIS IS THE BEST! The yoghurt soda is great too!

So all I wanted was a good burger. So my buddy puts that request into his cell phone and it leads us to Bongo Burger. It doesn't look impressive but what burger joints really do? So we both just order a regular hamberger and it was amazing. Both of us where shocked at how good it was. Would I go back....yes. Would I bring friends.....yes.
Interesting twist of burgers.  The lamb burger is my fav.  A little on the expensive side.  Love the shorcut I take through People's Park to get there.  Oh the character's I've seen there!

So their burgers are good.  Service is good.  Place is clean.  But, OMG their fries are amazing!!!  Their fries are like my favorite Mexican fast food place, Del Taco's, but OMG their fires are 10X more amazing!  I also love the fact that they are not cheap about giving away free sauces ( most restaurants these days charge for everything).  I am a fan, I want to go back.  Highly recommend for a great lunch with friends.

Whenever I want a burger in Berkeley I lean towards Barneys - I like their curly fries.  Finally, this past weekend my boyfriend and I went to Bongo Burger for lunch.  There was a short line that moved quickly and the lady at the counter took our order. One bacon burger, one mushroom burger and two fries.

The burger was pretty good and you could taste the chargrilled-ness of the grill which was yummy. The bun was also really good. It looked too thick, but it was light and squishy yet held up to the burger patty and toppings. 

The big disappointment for me was the fries. The portion size of crinkle cut fries was generous, but they weren't fried very well. I could also see that they had the fries sitting under a heating lamp, which resulted in not so crispy fries =(

Overall, it was a good experience...the price is right and it's close to home, I just wish they would improve their fries!

i don't usually like burgers but this place is GOOD! even their turkey burger was tender and juicy (for a turkey burger). everything is always made hot and fresh with quality ingredients. i also really enjoyed the mediterranean plate and eggplant plates.

I survived on bongo burger while i was an undergrad at berkeley. I won't say how long ago that was, but the breafast was 99 cents and a 1/2 falafel was less than $2 and  was a complete meal.

Recently I had the occasion to enjoy a falafel there again and it was delicious and still cheap and filling. i have not had their breakfast special in recent history but it was great for a dollar  i think it will have to be better for $3.00

I had a craving for a good burger and fries, so decided to check out Bongo Burgers since I figured if your name has the word "burger" in it that it must be good.  Surprisingly there menu had an array of different types of dishes and there burger selection was very minimal.  I ordered the # 1 combo which was the Mushroom swiss burger, fries and a small drink.   I actually really liked the bun they used on the burger as it was perfectly toasted on the grill.  They had the right amount of mushroom and gave a good portion of fries.  

My gf wanted a side of onion rings so we ordered that and have to say there onion rings was really REALLY good.   The lady taking our order was not very friendly but at least she took our order correctly.  

One thing I liked a lot about this place was the fact that they had a bottle of ranch laying out on the counter which you can use as much as you want.  Most places will charge you for a side of ranch but being a guy who eats ranch with everything, this was a major plus.  Only gave 3 stars b/c there was nothing really special about this place and we've has better burgers elsewhere.
I love to order their MUSHROOM burger, so juicy, especially with their special sauce. I always order more than 1 burger to satisfy my needs. YUM

Holy Cow - this place rocks.  The burgers are on my top-ten EVER.  I've even had the falafel sandwich, and it rocked, too.  I'm kind of glad that it's not in the City - otherwise I'd be here every day.

I used to live right down the street from Bongo Burger, so it became a convenient place to get a great burger.

I've actually never had a hamburger at Bongo Burger because I only happened to go there during my "no red meat" phase (I eat red meat now). Fortunately, this allowed me to stumble upon the wonders of their Turkey Burger. Now I haven't had many turkey burgers in my life, but this is probably the best one I have ever had. It's juiciness and flavor rivals that of a medium rare beef burger.

The bun is also different than most traditional buns and has a thicker and chewier consistency to it, which can cause some bites to be a bit too bready. I'm also not a big fan of shredded lettuce as it gets soggy really easily, but Bongo Burger somehow manages to make it work out. The crinkle cut fries are also a classic and consistently crispy and crunchy. (Unintentional alliteration).

Love Bongo Burger!  It's well-priced and their burgers are large as well.  I would definitely advise the french fries as well--after all, what are burgers without french fries?!  I think my biggest compliment for the burgers here are that they are perfectly proportioned.  Exactly the right amount of bun to offset the juicy burger, just the right sauce to balance the bun, and not too much tomato to overpower the other flavors.  GETTING HUNGRY RIGHT NOW WRITING ABOUT THIS.  

Tip #1:  Sriracha sauce + ketchup + ranch + french fry = ?????? Try it and see!  (I go with half and half ketchup/ranch with a dab of sriracha, but mix it to your own spicy tolerance).  

Overall: Top burger place in the Berkeley campus area!  Actually, possibly the only one... But still.  It's yummy.

How can you ever go wrong with a good burger? I always end up getting either the cheeseburger or double hamburger combo, but they have a lot of other choices (sandwiches, hummus, and breakfast?!) on their menu.

The burger patty is always juicy and well-cooked, and the fries are a big bunch of zigzaggedy goodness. The portions are pretty big for me, and just right for most guys. 

I like Bongo Burger because it doesn't feel too greasy, and it's about 5 minutes away from where I live. It's affordable and fast, and it's an easy hangout spot to grab a quick bite with friends.
Persian Burger. Best burger in the world. Yum.

My rating is based on value for your buck, not great food quality.    Don't get me wrong, the breakfasts are  good, especially for the price (three bucks!).    You won't find a better deal in Berkeley - even at McDonald's.

Update:     About 12 years after my last visit here, I found a spruced up atmosphere, and higher prices of course (but you can still get two eggs and hash browns for $2.95).    I also ordered, for the first time, something other than breakfast -- a mushroom and cheeseburger, which was delicious, for  $5.15.
I ordered the Lamb burger and what I got looked more like a hero sandwich. The lamb meat was good and the fries were okay. The small drink is a joke.

Had the Persian Burger today--it's huge size definitely makes for a filling meal at ~$7, but taste-wise it is an a-okay sandwich. I was starving though, so I ate it all happily.

In the past, I've had one of their mediterranean plates, in which everything was pretty tasty except the falafels, which were too hard and a bit overcooked. In general, Bongo Burger is a standard spot to get a no-fuss meal.

I came here with my family for breakfast, and the parking is easy during the morning and we parked right in front of the establishment. 

I had their Persian Sandwich and it's incredible. The taste of lamb is perfect with the tomato and the bun. 

My family members enjoyed their meals as well, I would call this joint a winner.

I went to Berkeley/lived here for 5-6 years, and I finally tried Bongo Burger. I don't really have any idea why I hadn't tried it before, as I love burgers and I had heard this place was decent and priced pretty cheaply.

I'd have to say the burger I got was overcooked and the meat patty is very thin, but it was still pretty tasty. I just got a regular hamburger, though I hear their alternatives are quite good. I was pretty surprised by the menu, as it had a good selection of vegetarian items (as if I'd ever order one) and stuff like falafels and pita wraps. It's definitely not a IB Hoagie's style menu. The fries were quite enjoyable as well, though they don't have a good ranch here, probably something out of the bottle, so I had to settle with regular ketchup.

Considering how much I like hamburgers, I should have come here before when I was a student, but maybe it was better I didn't since I probably would have gotten it almost every day. :P

Great burgers right near campus. My fav is the mushroom burger with swiss. I skip the fries to be a little bit good. They actually will cook your Niman Ranch Burger medium rare. I wish there were a bit more elbow room and more small tables. 

Yummy!

I am particularly fond of the persian burger and the half falafel. My family eats here wehn I am too tired to cook and the price is right. The Telegraph area store is next to a bookstore so you can browse as you wait for your take out order.
The burgers are fresh and delicious. The chicken sandwich was ok...the falafels are also very good. Their french fries are always a hit.

Mmmm, delicious.  The Persian burger was amazing.  The lamb was spiced and cooked up just right.  My only complaint was that there wasn't enough!

One thing that stood out to me was their crinkle-cut fries.  Usually I detest those abominations, the soggy and bland abominations gracing the halls of public school cafeterias everywhere.  But they were fried up perfectly and completely shattered my perception of crinkle-cuts.  Those bags of frozen fries in the freezer aisle will probably still make me want to gag, but I will know that somewhere out there, crinkle-cuts are being well defended.

Yep, it's a college burger joint.  Nothing fancy but the burger was decent and the server offered to wrap mine in lettuce since I can't eat bread.  Good prices, very low-key with pleasant staff.  It is not a place I'll be craving in the future, but if I'm in the area and I want a burger, Bongo Burger will do the trick.
This restaurant offers great quality food at a low price!

This place is kinda weird. I think I didn't order the right thing.
I got a regular burger which was fine. Nothing special. I like the toasted all sesame seed bun. It gave the bun this weird chewy toast consistency that was actually kinda good!
If I return I will go for the 'foot long' looking lamb burger.
I really liked this place! The burger and food was yummy - not anything super special, but delicious anyways. The people working were SUPER friendly though.

So I came here on the suggestion of my friend with high expectations and found that the food at this place was below average. The location is great, but if it weren't so close to campus this place would struggle.

bongo has something for everyone. salads, lamb, beef, fries, and so on. it is great. I was recently in Minneapolis at the good earth restaurant (why isn't there one in Berkeley?!) and the waitress found out I was from Berkeley and asked about Bongo burger because she used to live here and loves it so. Come on people it has to be good.

My boyfriend and I decided to make a trip to Berkeley today, so I came onto yelp to find a decent place to grab a bite to eat. 

I came across Bongo Burgers and saw the reviews and decided it would be a good place to try.

I ordered the Persian burger, and he ordered the Bacon burger. The Persian burger was decent. The meat was moist. The fries were what I can make at home, but would probably taste better at home. 

A bit pricey for a burger, small drink, and fries. I rather have spent my 17 dollars at In n Out.

Both the falafel and the persian burger are great.  Fresh squeezed carrot juice is delicious (if you swing that way).  Breakfast isn't bad either for cheap eggs and toast.

Odd recognition - I've easily gone there 100 times in my life, and I've never ordered the regular burger.

Northside location is equally good.

And a note to Grey H.  Your 8/15 post was completely nostalgic.  When I was 16 (and could eat like 8,000 calories a day) an appetizer at Top Dog followed by main course at Bongo Burgers (with a concluding stroll to Vivoli's at Trumpetvine for dessert) was a frequent fave.

TEAM MUSHROOM BURGER. Big, juicy, messy, delicious goodness.  My man, on the other hand, is a bit jealous cuz he got the persian burger (based on all the good reviews), and regretted it the moment he laid eyes on my beauty. The persian burger wasn't bad,  but it doesn't compare to the classic mushroom burger. I will definitely be going back for more. Oh, and the fries were good and crispy. It wasn't dry like I thought it would be. Good job, Bongo!

My (and many other college students') quest to find the perfect burger has led me to Bongo, a popular joint next to UC Berkeley. Though not as affordable as other Berkeley restaurants, the simple and filling burgers are worth the price tag 

The burgers come with a 1/3 lb patty. I ordered the bacon burger with cheese. I found the patties to be a little dry, which was why I was thankful for the juicy bacon. Unlike the usual grilled slices we are all accustomed to, Bongo's uses English-styled bacon, similar to a thinly sliced layer of ham. Complementing the burger is are the burger sauces (the name escapes me...), and the basics of lettuce and tomatoes.

A combo is the way to go, which is generally a burger with fries and a drink. The fries and drinks are both small sizes. The fries are very basic, crinkle cut, so be sure to load up on sauces or salt. A combo will cost around 7-8 dollars, which isn't exactly ideal for the college student's budget. But the burger packs a punch in both quality and quantity, so it's definitely worth the price.

And like most of the restaurants in Berkeley, plenty of vegan and vegetarian orders are available. Also, the Persian burger and the falafels are very popular.

Seating is limited at Bongo, so this is an ideal place to order to-go, for in between classes or whenever you're around the area.

They have a couple of good menu items here: The Salmon or Persian Plate is nice and filling and you don't get as full as when you get a combo with fries. Surprisingly inexpensive. There aren't many places that serve grilled sea food around telegraph so this plate is extra special. The persian burger was a-ok, nothing too praise-worthy, at least not for the extra price. You should try it at least once though since you don't see many lamb burger places around. The turkey burgers are also good, as well as the regular beef burgers. The fries are some of the best also, always nice and crispy.

get No.2 [Bacon Burger + fries + drink]
get the Eggplant Sandwich, if you are an eggplant lover like me. 

The Eggplant is a bit expensives for a sandwich, but it's big enough to split between two girls. 

Never opt out of the burger combinations. These fries are golden. Buns are superb.
THE best burger place in Berkeley. Doesn't make you feel fatty afterwards either. 

They also have a bathroom.

we found this place while circling the neighborhood for parking..and i am so glad we did! after walking the streets, we conjured up a huge appetite!

its  a small little place, up the street from upperplayground and they have all kinds of burgers/sandwiches/juices here.  they have persian burgers (not sure whats in it), turkey burgers, black bean burgers, kababs, carrot juice (lol), falafels, and other kinds of food. i got the cheeseburger because i wasnt too sure how everything else tasted.. each burger came with a small side of fries and a small drink for about 8 bucks

wow! very impressive! the bun was something that i never had before! it was a sesame seed bun, toasted and it was delish! the hamburger patty was humongous too! everything was sooooo good! 

if your ever on the other end of telegraph, this place is a must! but they have 2 other locations near campus for your convenience!

I come here. A lot. Maybe more often than my arteries can handle. But, for a good reason: the food is simple, but solid.

I can't really say it's the best burger I've had, perhaps it's one of the better ones you can get in Berkeley for lunch. Nothing too fancy about the burger either, sesame seed bun, patty, lettuce, tomato, ketchup/mustard. But, I think what may put it over the top is how they toast the bread. It puts a nice crunch to the burger. I'm not even sure if that's a legitimate reason to speak well of their burger, but it certainly caught my attention the first time I bit into the burger, as shards of hardened bread dough sprinkled upon my tray.

The crinkle-cut fries are, for God knows what reason, AMAZING. Actually, it's probably because it's fried in heart-attack-inducing oil for awhile. But it is definitely a crucial part of my order every time I visit this place. Their ranch is unusually good too. I'm usually not a big fan of ranch, but their ranch, which probably isn't anything particular, is served cold and just compliments the salty crunch of the fries.

I'd say the item I order the most often is their breakfast special. Most people don't even bother ordering it because they wouldn't think much of breakfast at a burger place. But, let me just say, for about four bucks, you can have yourself two generous eggs prepared anyway you like it, soft, fall-apart-in-your-mouth homefries, and four slices of toast. You really can't go wrong with breakfast, especially for four bucks. 

Probably biases my review that I live literally seconds away from this place, but I love Bongo Burger!

Good lamb and solid burgers. 

This was my first restaurant visit in Berkeley when I arrived at college 20 years ago and I have been going back since.

Pros:
* Good lamb
* Luleh Kebab, which is a ground lamb patty in a 1/2 pita with lettuce is great but not a big value.  So when it college I couldn't afford it often.
* Fries that are crispy.
* Good burger
* Chicken sandwitch, but get it with hummos because it's kinda dry without it.
* Lite eaters will go there with you because they have all those dolma, tebuleh, salmon kind of options.

Cons:
* Breakfast potatoes are never crispy, they are kinda steamy and sometimes even crunchy and that is disturbing.
* Random use of cucumber, sometimes it's in falafel, sometimes it's not.  I hate cucumber, and 1/5 of the time they sneak it in.

Mmmmmm! I broke my Bongo Burger Boycott (okay it wasn't much of a boycott but I like the alliteration) after about a year, and I was very pleasantly surprised. My cheeseburger was totally yummy and enormous, with good quality beef and cheese. I also loved the shredded lettuce, the sesame bun that was toasted to crunchy perfection, and the crinkle cut fries. Burgers at Barney's and elsewhere might be more satisfying, but this will do when I can't be bothered to walk beyond a 2-block radius of my apartment...which is more often than not.
Tastiest burger I've had in Berkeley.  Different.  Not nearly as fast as Smart Alec's, but with a superior and more unique flavor.  Nice locations, but not so great seating.  Definitely to go.

Can you Believe The First Time I ate Lamb Was Here???!!! Weird Right Lol ......Well I use to Date an Afghan sooooooo we use to Love to come here and Have their PERSIAN BURGERS....... and Oh My is it YuMmY!!! you have to try One!!! I love this place its nice and Clean and the Prices Aren't bad at All .... So if ever your Around telegraph doin some shopping or what not come here to Eat YumMy Burgers!
I guess I was expecting a little more.  I can honestly not say there is anything special about their burgers.  Are they good, yeah, are they worthy of any rating above "A-OK", ummm, don't think so.

I checked this place out on the recommendations from some people in SF.  I figured if they are driving from the city all the way to Btown just for a burger... its gotta be good... 

It was OK..

I got the mushroom burger combo.  It was a good average burger.  Not bad, but nothing special.  I should have tried something different that they don't have everywhere (Persian burger or steak sandwich) but oh well..  

If I'm in the area and craving a burger I would go back.
Though I have not been there for seriously 7 years (dates me), their cheap breakfast is for the ages.  The only thing that would motivate me to get up before noon while I was in school.

Sweat beads erupted from Celia's forehead. The sun's heavy rays hit Jeff's face as he and John carried a sofa up to the third floor. 

After a morning of tiring manual labor, Celia's apartment finally had a nice sofa bed! Accompanied by Judy, Celia and Jeff walked down Dwight in search of food. Bongo Burger!!!

Bongo Burger makes delicious burgers to order. The ingredients are fresh and very high quality. Jeff ordered the mushroom burger and Celia ordered the regular cheeseburger. Both were delightfully surprised by how filling the burgers were. Jeff believes it is because of their denser, more bread-like bun. 

When Celia passes by Bongo Burger now, she always looks longingly at the menu before Jeff pulls her away.

To Celia and Jeff, Bongo Burger is the In-n-out of Berkeley!
It's a solid burger and fries. They need BBQ sauce and other condiments. The atmosphere is just blah. Prices are decent. Not memorable, but I would go every 7 weeks or something, if I'm in the hood.

This place is made of win. I used live less than a minute's walk away and ate here all the time. Everything on the menu is delicious (except for maybe the salmon... but I don't like salmon). My favorite combo was the half persian burger on peta bread + fries + fresh squeezed OJ. The quality is also very consistent, once in a while they give you kinda soggy fries towards the end of the night but it's still not that bad. Bongo definitely tops the list of the best fast food places around campus. Yeah, I'd take it over Gregoire any day.

The Persian Burger: Lamb, tomatoes, and lettuce on flaky french bread. 

For me, the Persian Burger is the thing to order at Bongo Burger. 

Even though sometimes it seems like a hit-or-miss sort of deal, Bongo Burger is definitely worth trying!

Let me just say this joint ROCKS

Combo no.4 is the best thing ever, period, the fatty burger, the perfectly fried fries and a small coke. 1000 cals with pounds of saturated fat, yummy

4 years ago when i was still a Cal student,  I was a regular and one night at around 8, I walked in for a combo no.4.  The Iranian lady ( kinda milf type) was shaken, I was like, what the heck? Then I turned around, two bullet holes on the window.  Some Oaktown dude shot at the joint just 3 minutes ago!  I asked myself, what would Chairman Mao do? Then I decided to just calm the fuck down, order a combo no.4, sit down and help the good folks pass the hard time. 5 minutes later, all the relatives came, it's quite a warm thing to see...

falafel plate, Persian burger are also very good like other folks said.. BTW, what's in the white sauce? it's magic
The place is always very crowded and full of university students. They have one of the bet falafel sandwiches I have ever had!!!  The lamb burger is also really good. Make sure you check it out.

mmm. so delicious. i finally got around to trying bongo and was impressed. the cheeseburger was cooked perfectly and i randomly got free french fries. good price and fast service. ive yet to try their breakfast but i hear its delish.
as far as i am concerned the best burger in the bay area,and i know a good burger.i have been going there for the past 4 years.and will continue going therefor many more years.
Food was good. The lamb burger was phenomenal and delicious. The cashier didn't look too happy to be here.

I went here with a friend a few days ago and got the falafel plate, which was delicious and cheap. My friend got the lamb burger, i think it's called the Persian burger, and he loved his as well. Their french fries were delicious too - perfect crispiness! No complaints here!

Bongo burger definitely makes really great burgers and I am always satisfied when I come here. There are some burger places in the bay that I prefer more, but bongo burger never lets me down (especially when they have free ranch dressing just sitting out in a squirt bottle for your fries)
Great lamb burgers (beef available as well), middle-eastern sandwiches, tabuli (heavy on the parsley), fresh orange juice. They need to open one in Santa Cruz too!

The first time I heard about this place, my first response,"Bongo? Sounds kinda lame." After eating at this place, I was quite wrong. This burger joint knows how to make a pretty good burger. I got the bacon cheeseburger meal (fries and small soda) which was all awesomely delicious. This place definitely ranks itself at the top of my burger places list.

Just want to say that I love this place sooooo much!!! The best Turkey burgers ever. I even love the black bean burgers... It's a cute little spot to go to while out shopping with friends. I prefer the one on Telegraph Ave verses the one by the U.C Berkeley campus. However, don't go here on a busy Saturday, parking is horrible! It's defiantly a place that I like to go to when I'm off during the day, enjoying  the weather. 

Your friend,

OB
I ordered the Persian Burger combo and it was insanely delicious. It's like a foot long so I was only able to eat half of it alongside the crispy fries. I would definitely come here more often.

Probably my favorite burger place in Berkeley. 

Best bites: (1) Mushroom Burger (2) Persian Burger (3) Bacon Cheeseburger (4) Fries with RANCH.

I eat fries with ranch. And of all the burger joints I've been to (which is a lot -- burgers are my favorite food), Bongo's ranch lands at the top. It's insanely good. My friend Glen suggested dipping fries into their ranch mixed with ketchup and pepper, which sounds horrendous but is actually delicious.

As for their burgers, toasted sesame buns, charred juicy beef patties that are packed with flavor (and decent cuts of beef too, not excessively fatty), sweet grilled onions, tons of lettuce and tomato, and an assortment of condiments to choose from.

Baklava isn't so good though, OVERWHELMINGLY sweet.
I live down the street.  I come here often.  The turkey burger is really good!  It is what it is and I appreciate that.

The Persian burger is definitely a step up from their hamburgers. The Persian burger still suffers from the ridiculously thin pattie, but it is hella long. It is almost like a footlong sandwich. The sauce that they put on it is also fantastic. The second time getting their fries, they're greatttttttttt, like frosted flakes! +1 star for good persian burger and fries.

Yummy, there burgers are DELISH and fresh! And for the money, its well worth it. Try their bean burger or the mushroom one. So good. I had their falafel one and it was ok - I just stay clear off that!

Always a great place to grab a burger.

Combo #2. Bacon Burger.  Love it.  Near campus this is the place to go.

All in all a tasty burger.

Get the Persian Burger.  It's a sub sandwich sized burger made with seasoned lamb in lieu of beef.  It is quite unique and tasty.  Although probably the best non-gourmet burgers in Berkeley, you pay for that distinction as the meal combos (with small drinks and fries) come in just shy of $10.

As a whole, I was disappointed. I expected burgers, lots and lots of burgers. And sure, there were of course lots and lots of burgers. BUT. The whole attempting to be Mediterranean thing, completely unnecessary. To give it a shot, out of curiosity, I ordered a Shish Kabob Sandwich and a dolma. The dolma was barely an inch long, and tasted NOTHING like real, authentic dolma. I don't even want to know what was in there. The Shish Kabob Sandwich was basically grilled beef in bread with lettuce, tomatoes, and mayonnaise. I'm not saying it wasn't delicious, it was, it was a delicious sandwich indeed. But a delicious grilled beef sandwich, NOT a Shish Kabob Sandwich. They could have at least wrapped it in lavash, or pita bread, to make it look slightly more convincing. 

Anyway, my only problem with Bongo Burger is its fail attempt at being something it clearly is not. I would appreciate a little more effort. Otherwise, it's fast and it's food. Their bread tastes great. But everything is overpriced. My 75 cent excuse for a dolma, especially. I wouldn't even eat whatever that was if someone paid me 75 cents. My suggestion: Knock a few dollars off everything on the menu, and stick to burgers. Just burgers. Three stars for that delicious grilled beef sandwich. Good luck to you, Bongo Burger.

I really don't like this place at all. They have  a poor attitude and their burgers don't taste any different from what I can make at home. Next off, their fries are super salty and they don't have the greatest variety to choose from.

Like how they have a tv in there, in addition their breakfast isn't too bad. You can get eggs , toast and a side for less than $2.50.

I
LOVE
THEIR
FRIES.

I would sell my soul for a lifelong supply of their fries, with a tub of ranch. They look so simple, these wavy well-done fries. But something about their crunchy sturdy outer shell yet soft interior make me feel like I'm eating Satan's trap and I'm actually secretly being led to hell... Why are they so good??

Their burgers are all good, partly because of the meat, but mainly because of their bread. Their buns aren't like the soft buns that break easily (that you'd buy from safeway or other grocery stores) but instead are like actual bread. They're toasted, of course, and don't fall apart when you bite it, but instead are a bit chewy. My favorite here is the Persian Burger. A long patty, shredded lettuce, tomatoes, and ranch sauce are put in between a foot long piece of toasted French bread. Sounds so simple, but so satisfying. I really recommend eating their fries/burgers with their ranch sauce. 

Burgers here are affordable, and aren't as greasy as most burgers are. For 9$ I can buy a Persian burger, fries, and a small drink and I can never finish. Definitely a good deal for your buck, not to mention it's super close to the UC Berkeley campus.

A few words to think about....

Persian Burger.

Fries.

You will come back.

I've been getting turkey burgers at Bongo Burger for eight years now (omg I think I'm getting old) and they've consistently delivered. This is not your gourmet-type hamburger spot so don't come here with those expectations. On the other hand, it's medium quality yummy burgers with average toppings at a good price. For those who don't eat beef, you know how difficult it can be to get a good burger. Put this one on the list!

I'm not really a burger fan, but these were tasty.

Had a bite of the falafel sandwich (really good) and the Persian sandwich. The whole Persian burger is only appropriate if you're starving, otherwise the half Persian burger was plenty for me.

Still haven't tired sunrise deli, so I'll have to compare their falafel sandwiches. But for a HUGE juicy burger, come here.

I've been coming here since the late 80's when I was in college and always ordered the full falafel plate freaking loved it better than anything I had in Amsterdam which has some pretty good falafel joints but I had a hankering and stopped in last Saturday, something was off. The patties were kinda dry, they didn't have that cuminy, spicy, garlicy goodness that I love about falafel, frankly they were tasteless. The tahini sauce tasted like thinned out ranch dressing, I couldn't find anything remotely tasting of sesame and lemon. Not only that they raised the prices by about a buck. Until this visit I always found their falafel so satisfying not anymore. I think I'll try my hand at making my own.

I had the mediterranean plate with falafel, hummus, etc.  Actually I think I had to order the hummus separately.  You can end up paying a lot for lunch/dinner here, but the food is pretty good.  I have pretty high hummus standards, and while it wasn't the best, it was acceptable.  The portions are quite large and you will leave full.  This location is a little small and can get crowded depending on the time of day.

I just finished eating my turkey burger from here and I'm totally satisfied!..I got a big turkey burger w/ fries and small soda for 7 bucks!! I also added a baklava which was good because it had pistachio...the place it's not really big but it's a nice place to stay and enjoy your food and the service wasn't bad. I'm ready to try the Persian burger next time.Oh by the way they also have some Mediterranean items like hummus and falafel !

This place does everything on their menu right.

The turkey burger has a healthy feel while still being satisfying.

The bacon cheeseburger is a calorie splurge no doubt, but ohhh is it worth it (don't eat this every day though)

The falafel is okay, nothing spectacular unfortunately, but considering the strength of their other offerings I don't fault them too much because some times you just want a filling meal without killing bambi or her friends, that is when the full falafel comes in.  

The breakfast special used to be the deal of the century but since has crept up in price.  Still though two eggs toast and some tasty potatoes for around $4 is not too shabby at all.

Finally the Persian burger, quite delish, with nice peppery grilled flavor with just enough lather of mayo on a french roll.  Wonderful!

we went after bikram got the Persian Burger with crinkle fries and Whole Falaffel, and baklava.

Overall:  Delicious as everyone stated!  Service was good.

Persian people know how to make a burger, cause Bongo Burger is BOMB. I have two burger places that I go to in Berkeley, one of them is Smart Alec's and the other is Bongo Burger. 

Hands down, Bongo Burger beats up Smart Alec in the taste arena. I usually get the Bacon cheese burger or the Persian burger. Both are unique and pack plenty of flavor. The burgers are juicy and when mixed in with their diced lettuce and tomatoes, is even better. The bun is unique too, and they always cook the bun a little, making it extra delicious. 

TIP: Get the ranch sauce and add it to your burger. You won't regret it. Hell, fill two containers of it. 

The atmosphere is cool too; good amount of seating and a nice big tv. Perfect to watch a game for a short time while you enjoy your meal. 

It's a little pricey though  - $9 for a whole meal. But the burger is pretty big, so it'll probably fill you up. Anyways if you're looking for a good burger, look no further, go get your Bongo on.

not bad. might give this place another visit whenever i feel like it (which would probably be years from now, or never.)
nothing i'd go out of my way for since it's a bitch to find parking sometimes.

The burgers are delicious and huge! My friend and I both ordered the bacon cheeseburger combos and we were so stuffed after just eating our burgers that we couldn't even look at the fries afterwards. Seriously, we ate a late lunch/early dinner at around 4 and weren't hungry the rest of the night. Pretty good deal for only about $8 per person!

The burgers are good here, but for me, just not as good as the one on northside, the buns are not as fresh and toasty tasting. The fries are still delicious here, I always order the bacon burger, but I try to eat at northside as much as possible.

I had a very juicy standard burger with onion rings the first time I came here. I was surprised how inexpensive the burger was ($4.75 I think?).

I was very unhappy when I finished my meal and almost wanted to order another one. I'll be looking forward to going back to this place considering how just the REGULAR burger tasted that good.
For years I have ordered the Persian Burger when visiting Berkeley, ground seasoned lamb patty on a long toasted bun and have never been unhappy. Don't know where else to find this but it is YUMMY!!!
Solid standard burger place.

Bongo burger--tasty burgers. I was confused as to why a burger place sells baklava, but let's not focus on that detail. I love their bacon cheeseburger. Nice pieces of bacon, lettuce is shredded really finely, with a toasty sesame bun to boot. If you're hungry, don't opt for the onion rings! They only gave me 5-6 pieces... I mean come on, if you're going to charge me almost $2 more for it than fries, at least don't be stingy about it!

Anyways, their burgers makes up for everything else. It has a nice char on it that smart alec's burgers just don't have, and they use Niman Ranch beef.
I go here whenever I want to binge eat on juicy burgers and fries. Their grilled onions are so good! I also ordered breakfast here at one point and got their omelette, which wasn't too bad.

Best burger place close to campus! I LOVE their sesame buns, and I'm not a huge meat-lover so their thin patties are just right for my taste! I always get their mushroom burger, which is just a regular burger with mushroom and swiss cheese, but the bacon burger is really good as well! (How can bacon not be delicious?) Their prices are very reasonable, and they even have dine-in space.  There usually isn't too long of a wait either, although you can also call in your order. Plus points for using Niman ranch beef!
The Persian burger is top notch, but that doesn't make the normal beef burgers any better. I am a ranch guy and they serve a nice mild ranch.

had the full falafel sandwich. loved it. the 4 falafel balls were deep fried but had no signs of greasiness.
