one star reduction cause the menu said it had their famous tahini sauce, but later found out they do not put it in for you, there is a bottle of tahini at the pick-up counter, which did me no good once I left.

What a surprise, when we were just looking for burgers and fries, (and had walked out of Top Dog, next door because they don't do fries...) to find a Mediterranean restaurant in disguise. The tabbouleh salad was very good, as were the burgers and fries. On the tabbouleh salad spectrum, theirs was heavy on cucumber, light on bulgar. I think they use vinegar rather than lemon juice, but it was tasty and perfect for a sunny lunch side dish.

Somebody here knows how to cook and prepare traditional middle eastern foods. 

I'll be back.

Great spin on hamburgers! I love their Persian Burger. It's in a long roll with a thin pattie of lamb. It's flavorful, moist, and delicious! Their fries are excellent, as well as their mushroom burger. Everything is great here.
I only been here once, but my experience with this place is pretty awesome. I had a falafel. Very tasty and you get the bang for the buck.
Everytime I come here, I get the Persian burger.  Large portion and tastes great!

The burgers here are very forgettable. Nothing special about them...at all. They're your standard frozen quarter pounder you can find at Costco in a 60 pack. The only thing that's a *little* different is that they offer a turkey burger, which from my experience, is pretty good. Props. For about $4 a burger, this is cheaper than most burger places I'd say, but the fries that they offer (sold separately) are like their beef patties: frozen and completely standard. Nothing special about them at all. I feel like Bongo Burger was a restaurant started from a Costco shopper who had too much leftovers in their freezer rather than a burger joint. 

I'd come here if I wanted a cheap burger, but if a McDonalds were closer, I'd probably go into that instead.
Not very impressed

This is a Berkeley staple. Add extra tabasco and white sauce to the burgers. This is why Berkeley is better than Harvard. Lived near both schools for a long time and there is no place near Harvard that comes close to a decent, casual joint like this. Proof that Bostonians don't intuitively know how to eat.

My favorite food in the whole world is a burger. Any kind of burger, as long as it has meat (chicken, beef, and fish), fresh vegetables (tomatoes, iceberg lettuce, red onions, and condiments (ketchup, mayo, mustard, American/Cheddar/Swiss cheese). If you know me, you know I love burgers. And I am pretty excited to write my first review on a local Berkeley's own Bongo Burger.

 Bongo Burger has a unique approach to the way it makes it burgers. The bread's texture is different for some reason- in a good way though. The meat is good- Niman Ranch Ground Beef (so it's really tasty and healthy), vegetables are fresh, and the fries crispy as ever. I've had the American cheeseburger, with fries and small drink combo. Enjoyable meal, but for me it was pricey- it was about $10 dollars! 

The menu is pretty cool too. Not only do they offer different kinds of burgers- Persian burger, but they also offer a variety of options- from breakfast, to vegan and vegetarian options, to main plates. I have yet to try these other plates, but will update this review if I do. 

I plan to continue eating here, but sparingly- when I have money and when I am in the mood for Bongo Burger. Other than that, probably not as much.

Pretty good burgers, but kinda expensive. Sorry, I'm used to combo meals at In-N-Out (:

I got the mushroom burger which was really good. So big, though! And their zigzag cut fries are yummy, too.

The cashier was not that nice..she did not look like she was having a good day.
Great burgers! Not much to say after that than nom nom nom...

Let's first start out with me saying I HATE BURGERS, HATE EM! I grew up on rice and a side of meat, never putting bread and a slab of hamburger together. The boyfriend took me here on one of those "I'll make my girlfriend pissed off days by taking her to a food place she hates" but jokes on him, the burger here was so yummy! I may go back to putting beef in my mouth...(yes i went there)

The cheeseburger I had was fresh and didn't make me feel fat after eating it. Tasty!

This is easily my favorite place to get a burger.

My roommate and I have a tradition of coming here to celebrate birthdays, end of midterms, etc. I've successfully converted her into loving black bean burgers and i absolutely adore their fries dipped in ranch/ketchup/Sriracha.
It's a small place so we always take it to go and deal with the pouring rain as we trek back to our apartment, but the food manages to still stay hot. :)

Worth a try, i promise

I LOVE Bongo Burger- and not just because I'm Persian. 

Although I do enjoy the 'Persian Burger', I generally get the mushroom burger. As someone wrote a few posts down- those mushrooms are seriously marinated with crack and with a hint of more crack. 

Back to the Persian- A whole entire Persian Burger is sooo huge, that I've only finished it once (when I was REALLY stoned). The half burger is more than enough when complimented by fries. I personally don't even think it requires an acquired taste to appreciate, just know that its lamb (and so it tastes different than normal burgers because of the meat). 

Their fries are okay. And overall, I love the quality of their meat (Niman)

What I REALLY love is their Ranch. Yes, oh yes. This is such a huge plus that comes from such a minor detail. They not only make their own ranch (thus ensuring freshness) but its absolutely delicious and doesn't even get close to the "salad-y" types of ranch. It's pure ranch made for burgers and fries. mmmmm

I think it's the best burger on the Southside of campus, easily edging out I.B Hoagies, Smart Alec's, Julie's and probably only rivaled by Blake's (which is sit-down status).
Their Turkey Burger is delish. I love the crinkle cut fries...It reminds me of when my mother tried to cook once when I was little, but these didn't light the kitchen on fire only my taste buds.

Oh Bongo Burger.... how I love thee. I OMFG love the bacon burger. I cannot express in words my love for their bacon burger. But this was back in something like 2003ish. I see a review somewhere about little bacon. I remember there being lots of bacon. That was the best part of the burger.... *drools over keyboard*

the best thing about bongo burger is the mushroom sandwich. i think they soak those mushrooms in crack somewhere in the back, then put them on a toasted bun with cheese & lettuce & tomatoes (if you don't think tomatoes are gross) & condiments for you to eat. i eat one, and immediately want five more. 

man, oh man alive, those crack mushrooms are really good.

I love love love love love love love love Bongo Burger... I wish I could give them a 5, but I am not a very big fan of the male owner. I hate onions, and one time I ordered the same, the number 2 (bacon cheese burger) with no onions and no tomatoes, and I guess they made a mistake and put onions on it. I usually hate taking food back, but I felt so comfortable since I always went to bongo burger ever since I went to high school. Well, the owner guy basically made a huge deal and said it was not onions that it was lettuce and did not want to take my order back, so I kind of got pissed and showed him. Anyways, he was not too happy with taking it back but did anyways. 

Overall, everyone there is nice and I love the burgers and especially the fries. When I meet someone, I always tell them how delicious their burgers are and they end up loving it too! One of my favorite places ever!

Yum yum yums! Deliciousness in my tums!

Bongo burger is delicious, and I'm salivating just thinking about my next burger. I usually get the Black Bean burger or the Persian Sandwich, simply because I no longer eat beef. Both are delicious, and as well as all the beef ones (well, the ones that I tried before I gave up beef.). However, at this point, I almost religiously always get the Persian Sandwich. Can't really go wrong with lamb.

But honestly, it's not the sandwiches that captivate me. It's the fries. I know wavy fries are one of the lowest on the fry scale (with criss-cut/waffle fries at the very top), but for some reason, Bongo makes wavy fries like no other. They're perfect, and everything wavy fries should be. Not to mention that they offer a ranch dipping sauce, which is better than crack cocaine (it's a metaphor! i honestly wouldn't know). I usually need about 3.5 portions of ranch, 2 for my sandwich, and 1.5 for my fries. *licks lips*

Bongo makes me happy. I mean, I think I prefer the Northside and Westside stores over the Southside one (Southside wins only due to proximity). It's location next to People's Park has made it an interesting journey on several occasions. However, one of the conviences of the Southside location, it offers a huge table. Good for groups of 6!
My favorite non-slider burger in Berkeley. The thought of the mushroom burger gets my heart racing, and not just because of what it does to my arteries. :/

hella guud! whenever i'm too lazy to "cook" (which is about 95% of the time) and i'm in search of something just damn delicious and down the street (from oakland to berkeley that is) i find myself at bongo burger. the order is quick--no need to think--just get up to the register and say "persian burger." it's lucky number 7 on the combo menu and it's damn good. within just a few minutes i'm chowing down on my foot long lamb burger and crinkle cuts fries. I douse my meal in the white sauce; a lot of people call it "ranch" but that's blasphemous. it's SO much better than ranch. with in a few i'm full off of lamby-ness (baah! so sad!)

I save half for now and half for later. and it's so good that i plan out when i'll eat the next half. and am i crazy or do i wash down my burger with RC cola? perhaps. anyway, the place is spick and span and always serves up quality eats in fast food-like speed. 

the only thing i hate about the place is how cold it gets from stupid customers walking in an letting the door fly open. "geez man i'm freezing over here!" it messes up the persian burger-ness. parking sucks everywhere in berkeley so go after traffic and you'll have plenty of time, cuz they're one of the few telegraph eateries that actually have reasonable hours.

My favorite burger joint in Berkeley, hands down!!

ATMOSPHERE
I love the large glass windows and the ample seating! It never feels cramped in there and I especially love stealing the large table right next to the cashier-- gives my friends and me enough room to thoroughly enjoy our meals.

The owners and workers are Persian and they have this "cool air" to them. You can tell they live another life beyond the restaurant, but they're still really friendly. I always ask them to cut the burger in half for me and they always oblige! 

FOOD
Combo #3 (Cheeseburger, fries, and a small drink) is the only thing I order here and I have yet to be disappointed.

The quality of their ingredients rivals In-n-Out and there isn't one thing I dislike about their burgers.

The sesame seed bun is toasted to perfection, and the veggies are fresh and crisp. The lettuce isn't a whole leaf; instead, it's cut into skinny strips, which are so good. The patty is made with high quality beef and it's succulent and juicy. 

My favorite thing at Bongo Burger has to be the old school crinkle fries. THEY ARE ALWAYS AMAZING. The texture and consistency cannot be beat. They are always made-to-order so you can expect a tray of piping hot and crispy french fries when the worker calls your number. I've definitely found myself wandering in just to buy an order of fries...

Pros:
The Persian burger plate (no bun/ carbs) is awesome! Great flavor and solid price. 

Cons:
The ambiance is a little more of a takeout place even though they have a few tables to sit on. Works well for students I'm sure. 

Fun:
I drank a 50/50 fresh "squeezed" carrot and orange juice blend (can you squeeze a carrot?)--that was interesting. Not to mention if you can't find fun on nearby Telegraph Ave then you're in the wrong place.

I've walked by this place so many times over the past 15 years, that I finally decided to try it. And I was a bit disappointed. The people there seem friendly and the prices are decent for what you get. I was enjoying my burger until I saw that they don't prepare them there. They just come out of a bag. I'm not sure how they have won best burger in Berkeley when they don't even make the patties! I understand why I just kept walking all these years.

Living literally only two streets up from Bongo has made it my burger go-to for the last couple of years. If you are looking for a meal that is economical, filling, and most importantly, delicious, I highly recommend you give these guys a shot.

My top two favorites:
1. Hamburger Meal - Keeps it simple, but a damn good burger and those crinkly fries (always hot and fresh) are the perfect side dish.

2. Black Bean Burger Meal - Coming from a vegetarian family, I usually like to try vegetarian burger options if they are available since most restaurant veggie burgers easily fall flat. Bongo definitely has an above average black bean burger and it serves as a great replacement for those days where a hamburger might just be a bit too heavy.

SIDE NOTE: It one day dawned upon me to squirt a little bit of their Sriracha sauce into my obligatory Bongo ranch cup. The mixture was easily my most life changing experience. Trust me, if you get on your Sriracha-ranch game at Bongo, there is no way whatever else you order can go wrong.

Minus 1 star because I am not a fan of the no-refill drink situation, it's a small cup of soda (with a lot of ice) for the amount of food to be consumed.

Bottom Line: Worth trying if you're in the area and you are more than likely to leave satisfied!

I LOVE burgers & it makes me sad this is the only decent burger place within walking distance in South Berkeley. 
(Triple Rock & Barney's burgers = AMAZING) 

3 stars for food. The burgers are inconsistent & there is little bacon on the bacon cheeseburger. The quality has gone down since I've been at Cal. The fries are also average. 

2 stars for the cold service. I order here a good amount & each time I'm greeted with rudeness. The cooks seem friendly though.

If you live in Berkeley, you should be forced to try Bongo at least once.  They have some of the dankest burgers.  While most people will compare this place to Barney's and criticize Bongo to serve smaller portions, I really do prefer the taste of Bongo's burgers.  The patty is always cooked very consistently and is pink in the middle.  It has a nice smokey flavor to it.  I always either get the mushroom or bacon addon, both of which add tremendous flavor to the burger.  It is topped with fresh lettuce, tomato, and spread.  One of my favorite parts of their burger is the bun.  Their buns are lightly toasted and are extremely fluffy.  They feel great when you bite into it; you'll know what i'm talking about when you try it.  The staff is always friendly, and they get orders out FAST.  I live right by this place so I've had this on multiple occasions, and the service and consitency of taste really impressed me.

PROTIP:  Their fries have the zig zag texture, meaning they are fried more evenly and taste great with their house made ranch sauce.

i love you i love you i love you. First of all, i love berkeley, second of all, i loooove bongo burger. i've only tried south campus, not the others, but i have history here. i basically used to live up in berkeley (was there 4 days out of the week, then was at Cal for a bit), and i would go here almost every day. I got to know the ladies that ran the place, super nice, and persian obvi ;) so they loved me. my usual was the bacon cheeseburger with onion rings...the onion rings are HUGE..some of the best i've had. and the ranch..omg the ranch...buttermilk ranch!! ahhh! so good. the persian burger is so good too! second favorite thing on the menu to my bacon cheeseburger ;) i have been here so many times and i will keep coming back

We came here just for the persian burger combos and that's what we got. I thought it would be a persian spiced regular round burger but I was so wrong. It's like a 1.5 foot long nice, toasty, yet soft, hoagie like bun with a flat, large piece of perfectly seasoned beef kabob with even sumac spice, with tomatoes, diced onions, lettuce, and some olive oil or some kind of light seasoning on it. I kind of wished we had shared one since it was huge, but I I figured I don't come up to Berkeley often so I should just eat my heart out. Paired with the hot, fresh from the fryer french fries and my drink, all for $9, this was an awesome dinner. 

I would think everything here is good, too, but since there are Persians running the place, I'll stick to the persian burger. The order came out very prompt and the staff were all very nice and friendly.

One of the few reasons I go here is because they accept credit cards, and most other burger places nearby do not. Other than that, they're burgers are okay, and the fries are decent.

That being said, I still like the taste of the food, especially the bacon burger. It's only a short walk away from Unit 2, so I can run down, come back, and still have time to study for finals.

For a fast food joint, Bongo Burger is pretty good. It's simple and good, but probably not a place you want to visit TOO often due to health reasons. Good fast food can't be good for your health, right?

I liked:
*An 'American Grill' with a Persian twist = options include lamb, falafels, etc...
*Place is clean, has a TV, and plenty of seats
*Food comes out quick n' fresh
*CHEAP and decent quality (especially breakfast)

Blah:
*The main cashiers come across rude and not really happy with their jobs
*They charge for minor changes to the orders - don't be bilks to people who frequently visit!

Final Call:
*It's a good place to visit if you're on this side of Berkeley and need a quick meal with limited funds. It's not good enough to visit more than one or two times a month though, there are healthier and better alternatives.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Munched on...
*Turkey burger
     -Juicy and yummy
*Falafel plate
     -I've had better
*Fries
     -Nice n' greasy

Bongo Burger is a very good solid burger. It's none of that health conscious crap they serve at Smart Alec's or ridiculously over-priced gourmet stuff they serve at Flame. 

When you come to Bongo Burger you have to know what to order. What I always get from Bongo when I come here is the Mushroom Burger. The combination of sauteed mushrooms and the veggie toppings is sublime. 

Recommendation:
Mushroom Burger Combo + Baklava. 

Good Food, Good Friends, ENJOY!

I went here for the first time on Saturday after the gym, and I came back on Sunday (again, after the gym).  This should speak volumes to the simple perfection of an uncomplicated and uncompromising Bongo burger.

I was comforted by the "We use Niman Ranch" sign and surprised by the quality of the bun.

I look forward to returning for the Persian Burger and the Mushroom burger.

A large group of about 11 of us went here for lunch about a month ago and though we all had pretty standard orders, we were glad to find that there were no mistakes made on any of our orders.

We originally had a little problem finding seating outside but after a couple of parties left we put together two or three tables and brought chairs from the inside to seat all of us.

All of our food was good, but not great. The food was filling but it seemed to lack some flavor especially the persian plate. It was really just the burger minus the bun. The fries tasted like school cafeteria fries, which some people like but I don't care for.

The food is good and filling, I just wish it had more flavor.

so this isn't your authentic persian style restaurant if your thinking that, The workers seem to not be of persian decent which was the case with previous workers. The persian burger is good, very good infact, i enjoyed it, they use high quality condiments and meat on their burgers and you can watch them make it as well. I would give them 4 stars but they messed up my order and the workers are hard to communicate with.
Love it!
Good Persian burger.

Ok so like, it was Good Friday and me and my amigos were lookin for some fine cuisine. We were high out of our minds when we stumbled upon Bongo Burger. We decided to let our mouths taste some of their goods. I ordered the Persian Burger because I haven't had lamb in years. The burger came out looking like a long sandwich which freaked me out at first, but it tasted like the lamb of Christ. The bread was a little too toasty for my liking and the fries are the shriveled looking ones (still pretty tasty). I like how they have ranch available to squirt in a small sized cup to use as a dipper. Overall this place satisfied my hunger, but there are a butt load of better burger joints out there.

Mushroom burger. MMMMM so juicy. This is my go to order when I come here. I get the combo so I can get some fries too. The fries are zig zag cut. 

Since the mushroom burger is so juicy.... it gets kinda messy so I find it odd and a little annoying that they dont have napkins available to grab yourself. You have to go and ask them for some and they give you like two. -_____(") my messy eating needs more than two please!

Not particularly memorable. Never tried any of their burgers, but I do love their (don't hate me all you foodies) falafels. Falafels + ranch = bliss in this sort-of-southern-gal's mouth that goes straight to the heart. :)
I have been here many times and usually have shish kebab sandwich. The taste of food is great. Nice staff. The only con is the environment. It is not very clean.

I always come here after school, (easier to cook food at home and impossible when you have homework!  unless you have someone who cooks for you )

Food is so delicious, If you are new I recommend you go for Shish Kebob or Persian Kebob. 

The bad thing about this store is that between 12-1 it is very crowded and sometimes you need to wait 15-20 minutes to get your food.

Prices are moderate, quality of the sandwiches and stuffing are very good.

I have been going to Bongo's for over 25 years never had an bad burger or Persian burger love the Persian. Back in the day after they opened other locations we would do "the walk" and have burgers in all three stores! Great stuff if you don't Ike these burgers you don't like burgers!

5 bucks for a burger that's like a billion others but with A RUBBER TIRE FOR A BUN!!!

if nothing else, i can use it for a spare when i get a flat...

my hunt for the great bay burger continues...

5-Line-5-Star Review

1: Great Ingredients

2: Great Prices

3: Great Spot

4: 5 Stars

Bongo serves burgers, breakfast (til 11am), and Mediterranean food such as falafel, hummus, etc.--a good place to go if you're a vegetarian with a carnivore in tow.  Their burgers, beef or turkey, are charbroiled and the buns are toasted well; not the best burger in town, but it still hits the spot.  They also serve the "Persian" burger:  lamb patties with the usual burger fixins and a squeeze of tahini on a long hoagie-like roll.  It's fantastic!  If you're craving Mediterranean, they have falafel sandwiches and various Med plate options including one that comes with falafel, hummus, tabouleh, dolmas, a slice of stinky feta, and pita--all this food for around $7!  They also serve cheap breakfast (it used to be $1.99, but it might have gone up thanks to the recession) early in the day, but that's not a highlight of Bongo aside from the price.  Everything is very affordable here, including the fresh-squeezed orange juice.  There are some tables indoors and two tables on the sidewalk if you want to observe the Telegraph Avenue characters.  They also have a location in Northside as well as downtown Berkeley on Center Street.

Not a place I like too much. The burgers are okay when you try them the first time, but it gets tiresome pretty fast. It just seems to lack a burger's substance. As a result, I tend to go for their so called persian burgers for a change.

 If you like the burgers here, you're a burger newb. N00b I TELL YOU!!!

This burger does the job. I usually get the turkey burger, place the fries inside, and pour some greek sauce on top of the fries and veggies. It's nothing fancy, but the burger always holds together. So many of them fall apart. It's a clean burger experience. When I lived in the Bay Area, everyone loved Barney's, but their burgers fall apart. Great place to go if you're craving a burger and are hungover. 

I'm not totally sure why I'm writing a review of Bongo Burger, which I haven't eaten in ten years ago, but I'm in South America right now and am craving random food from my homeland, mostly ethnic. I find the food in Santiago disappointing. If you're in the University neighborhood, and you're hungry, go to Bongo Burger!!

YES. I am so excited to write a review for Bongo Burger. I'm sure everyone has given this place well deserved 4-5 stars, but I will reiterate what has most likely been said and say that I LOVE BONGO BURGER. Not only because it's down the street from my house, not because it's near school, but because the meat is so delicious. Their burgers are so good. The bread is thick and perfect with the meat and all their lettuce and onions. It's a place that will always satisfy my burger craving (which I admit occurs quite too often). I do not need to continue raving about bongo burger. Crack of the burgers. End of story.

Why is this place so expensive?  For the price they charge and the amount of food they give you is not really worth it.

They only have one vegetarian burger, the black bean burger, which is like $7 for the combo.  The burger is tiny and not that great.  I thought the crinkle cut fries were better than the burger.  You also get a soda with the combo but its more like a small size.

I've had the falafel here which wasn't that bad and a little more reasonably priced.

I have to say my favorite is the really cheap breakfast they have which is like 2 eggs and toast for only $2.

I also don't understand the decor here, they have a painting of a chef holding a naked pink woman and another man from afar staring at them.  WTH is that?

In the end, the bongo burger has me left with this place not feeling very special or memorable.

What a ripoff!

I went to go get a cheeseburger to go, took it home, opened it up, and there was NO CHEESE.  I couldn't taste any cheese, and I couldn't see any cheese.  So I call them up and the lady talks to the cook and she says "No, he put the cheese on, you just can't see it".

Hold on right here.  Can't see the cheese? WTF? Is this invisible cheese? Disappearing cheese? Yeah right, lady.

So I say "NO, I can't see ANY cheese, and I can't TASTE the cheese, and I have it right in front of me".  And she tells me "No, he put it on, we know, it's there you just can't see it."

So I'm just ready to blow at this woman, because I already paid for an overpriced cheeseburger and now I'm told they only serve invisible cheese?  I say goodnight and hang up, and I will never ever go to Bongo Burger again, it was a mistake going there this time.

What rude people, I hope no one ever buys from this overpriced no cheese place ever again.

After that horrid experience with Smart Alec's, I was reluctant to try another burger joint within nuking distance of the UC Campus area.

OK, let me just state for the record that BONGO BURGER ROCKS.

First of all, the lady behind the counter (owner?) is really nice--she didn't even get mad when I broke the Tabasco bottle by accident (Sorry, I'm such a Klutz!)

Anyway, I tried the TURKEY BURGER ($4.50) and was glad that I didn't order fries, because this burger was gi-normous!  The turkey patty was about 6.5 oz (1/3 pound), with lots of leaf lettuce & tomato and a very high quality bun.  

In my lifetime, I've had few turkey burgers of this quality or taste, and the other folks in my party were really satisfied with their cow burgers & fries.

This is one of the rare times I've gone to a restaurant and said: this is just a really well made (*insert food item*). Well..at Bongo Burger, they know how make a fucking well made burger. DAMN. Although Bongo Burger isn't anything special, their attention to detail just makes a great burger.

I got the CheeseBurger with swish cheese and a fries and coke. Initial thoughts:

-Fries weren't salted enough and I had to add a good amount to get the right taste. WHATS UP WITH UNSALTED FRIES?!?! It's not really being that much more healthy. ARGH.

-Soda cup  was pretty small and they charge for refills

-AMAZING BURGER. Focusing in on the main course, I realized this was going to be a great meal. All the ingredients, the burger bun, the shredded lettuce, the tomatoes, the patty: all could have been bought at your nearest grocery store. However, at Bongo Burger, they serve these ingredients together just the way you want them...so delicious. The buns were perfectly toasted and the patty, although not thick, was plenty juicy. The shredded lettuce was nice especially since the burger is pretty big in size. This sitting in a bed of melted swiss cheese just hit the spot.

Finally Verdict?!

Come here and get blown away by how awesome a simply well prepared burger can be.

The burgers are flavorful. And they have those neat crinkly fries you had when you were in elementary school. But the burgers are almost too flavorful, overpoweringly so. 

If you just want a burger though, I would suggest going here. It's still pretty good.

Maybe I was just really hungry.. But after Hitting Top Dog, my friend and I came here for meal #2 (this is within 15 minutes).  We ordered the Mushroom burger combo and split it.  And even with diminishing marginal utility, the flavor just kept getting better.  The mushrooms were marinated to perfection, so juicy.  As was the burger patty itself.  As I bit into the burger, the juice came out of both the mushroom and burger patty, melding together to make this heavenly melody (like in the beginning of simpsons)  Almost as good as Kobe :)  They use beef from a specific farm?  I still must try the Mediterranean food, since it keeps getting such good reviews for it.  This place is definitely a must try, and at a very legit price.  Try it Out!

Synopsis:
I've only had the burgers to go and they were really good. The fries came in a nice portion too.

The Scene:
Bongo Burger is a nice place, very quaint. It's interesting to see elements of middle eastern cuisine tied in with american staples like burgers. In terms of looks, there isn't much to report other than the fact that there isn't too much seating area. It was nice, however, to know that if you are having take out, you can get ketchup and ranch (as much as you want).

The Food:
The burgers were delicious. The beef was well spiced and cooked to perfection. The shredded lettuce and tomatoes added a nice touch. Fries were just okay, but if paired with a burger, who really cares?

The Best Part:
The Burgers

Ahhh if they had a location in LA, I'd frequently visit this place! The ground lamb patty is a healthy and DELICIOUS alternative to beef! UCB students, consider yourselves fortunate to have this place in close proximity

Maybe I'm sentimental but I have wonderful memories of eating at Bongo Burger before and after shows at the Greek theater. The falafel isn't the best that I've had, hell I make a better falafel, but the persian burger is quite nice and the whole setting is pleasant and easy on the wallet. They do some fresh carrot and orange juices which are very nice. Their fries suck so don't even bother with that, stick to the falafel and persian burger and you can't go wrong.

For some students, bongo burgers can be a bit more on the pricier end compared to the massive amount of food that you can get for like $6 at Steve's Korean BBQ at the Asian Ghetto a block away.

There burgers are very juicy and fat!  Order any style you want.. and if you are in the additional mood to eat mediterranean items, then that is also available to order.  I haven't tried any of their mediterranean items though, only their burgers and fries.

Nice crunchy fries and fulfilling burgers that will make you stuffed for hours.

Make sure to Ask for plenty of ranch sauce at the front!!!!!!  :)

Fairly tasty burger, though thinner patty  than I expected given the height of the final product. The fries were ok but nothing special. Definitely gets credit for lots of veggie options and Persian flair - hummus, tabouleh, and lamb burgers are all available. If I'm nearby again, I'd give the lamb burger a shot. 

TRIVIA: Bongo drums are especially popular in Cuban music and have Spanish origin. The larger of the pair is called the "hembra" (female) drum while the smaller is the "macho" (male drum.

Bongo Burger gets the award for the cheapest breakfast around, and I have taken advantage of this many times. But the fact that they (1) don't serve bacon, (2) their "sausage" is a hot dog, and (3) everything is served on a paper plate with plastic utensils, makes Bongo a pretty bad choice for breakfast unless you simply need fuel.

Burgers for lunch are much better, particularly the Persian lamb burger, although the burger prices have gone up recently and it seems a little steep for what you get.

MmmMmmMmMmMmmmMmMMMMMMmmmmm

Came here today for lunch again. YUM just yum. Mushroom burger = best by far. Tried the spicy chicken sandwich (not bad, but sort of dry)

Sauces are the best. I love mixing their sauces. My suggestion is that they pre-mix the sauces and call them..."RANCHUP" or "KETCHRANCH" yummy for burgers, fries, & everything.

I've been a HUGE fan of Bongo Burger ever since my very first burger here! From previous experience, I ABSOLUTELY recommend the mushroom burger. It's perfectly savory, not too dry (like many burger places), and completely filling! Plus, the fries are ridiculously addictive.

Yesterday, I got the All American Burger which was all right. It's your typical burger with patty, cheese, lettuce, etc., but without the mushrooms, it just wasn't the same.

Bottom line: Bongo Burger is completely worth your money, and a great casual eat-out spot. The prices aren't too bad and everything is delicious!

This place is very solid. Great tasting burger with Niman Ranch Beef, grilled onions and well-mixed toppings and sauces. The burger was also made very well, something lacking at most burger places. The fries were also very good. A burger and fries for ~$6 isn't the cheapest you could find, but you're definitely getting your money's worth here.

The service wasn't exactly cordial, but at a burger place, I don't expect much as long as the food is good and served fast. A great place for students and other residents looking for a great burger near campus.

Wow I saw my boy Steven Lee review this place.  Now I gotta write one too.  I lived about 5 minutes walking from this place for 2 years.  My roommate and I would literally eat here at least 3 times a week.  Their burgers are delicious and filling.  If you can wake up in time, as most college students cant, check out their breakfast.  YUM.  

A burger + fries + drink will cost you about $10.  Not too bad.  Give it a shot!

Let me begin by saying, get a combo.  

So, the plan was to eat at In n' Out but we were in Emeryville... and had developed a serious case of lazy.  Then, came Trueburger in Oakland but they were closed on Labor Day.  And then came Rocky's... but we'd tried it before and wanted something new.  A quick hop onto my Yelp mobile app and search for "burgers" near Berkeley led us to Bongo Burger (comes up as the first restaurant!)  It's a total mom n' pop shop with plenty of neighborhood street parking.  

Throughout my search, all I saw was "Persian Burger" and "so juicy" and "white sauce."  We got a combo Persian ($8.something) with a mushroom burger ($7.95) and an extra side of fries (cause one isn't enough!  Getting a combo next time...$2.14 after tax)  For someone who doesn't like lamb, this burger was pretty bombastic.  Can definitely tell it's lamb but the flavors all work together really well.  The mushroom burger was chunky, juicy and very filling.  I thought it had plenty of mushrooms and was deliciously melted with cheese.  

The white sauce looks like ranch dressing but is faaar from it.  It has a subtle mediterranean-y/yogurt-y flavor that really enhances the taste of the meat (and fries).  OHH the fries... crunchy, crispy, wholesome deliciousness.  Fill a condiment container with ketchup and pour some tabasco and pepper in it.   MMMmmmMMMm, classic dip...  

My allegiance goes to Bongo.  Touche.

With our sudden craving for a burger, my boyfriend and I decided to go to Bongo Burger to satisfy our hunger. I was expecting a burger that would do just that but I ended up becoming a little disappointed. 

I ordered the mushroom burger, which was a Niman Ranch beef patty topped with sauteed mushrooms, Swiss cheese, lettuce, grilled onions, tomatoes, mayonnaise, mustard, and ketchup with a side of french fries. My boyfriend ordered the mushroom burger as well with a side of onion rings.

Here's where my 3-star rating comes from. My boyfriend and I noticed that the onion rings were frozen in a name-brand box, not the freshly- made kind I was expecting. To make things worse, they charged us $2.75 for 7 [previously frozen] small onion rings. The crinkle-cut fries were good, definitely better than the onion rings. They were crunchy and piping hot, just the way I like them. The burger was okay, nothing too extraordinary. The patty was pretty thin and a little burnt, not the juicy patty I was hoping for. There was too much mayonnaise, which kept flowing from the sides of my burger. My boyfriend's burger patty kept slipping out of the buns because of the overabundance of mayonnaise in his. The lettuce and Swiss cheese were good, but who can mess up on that? I loved the grilled onions though, which was definitely an incentive for me to finish my mushroom burger. 

Overall, it was okay...but the next time I am craving for a  good burger, I will look elsewhere.

I wonder where that could be...

Monday nov 17 08

Location is bright and open. I enjoyed how the front windows open like doors to give you fresh air and so you don't choke on cooking fumes. Also you don't wanna leave smelling like cooked beef patties or the usual berkeley stinkies you find around there.I ordered a Persian Burger (lamb) and also a steak burger.No, not just for me my cousin was there so we split them to try each.
The bread is nice and toasty to my liking but the insides were not packed with enough meat. I esp. hate it when you get a bite of just bread, lettuce, and well nothing else. If I wanted 20% of my burger to be vegan I would have ordered that. Strech the meat to the ends of the bun, or better yet, have the meat sticking out the side!! For how thin the meat patty was, you would expect it to reach both ends of the bun!

I started off eating the steak sandwich, the steak needs to be marinated in something, it was bland but somehow enjoyable. Fresh and neatly packed but I feel like I am spending 2-3 bux more than what I feel this grub should cost. I still give them 4 stars because when I ate the lamb burger it had flavor. Not the overwhelming  lamb flavor, I'm sure they use a little lemon juice in this.

Crinkle Cut French Fries are cooked just right. No complaints here or raves.

Overall I enjoyed my trip here, Parking wasn't too hard to find and only half a block away. The spot is what I liked, The seating wasn't cramped and the open airy feeling was good because I tend to overheat easily, I think I need more exercise to burn all this food off, ok it's winter, I could use the extra insulation, I'll wait till march!

Bongo Burger is freaking delicious! Definitely one of my favorite burger places in Berkeley. (Just for reference, I only have 2 favorite burger places in Berkeley...) Anyways, My favorite is the Turkey Burger! It's healthy? (that's what it says on the menu!) I think Bongo Burger tastes different from other burger places because their bread is different! (&& I freaking LOVE their bread.) The burgers are very filling & cheap so if you are ever in Berkeley, try Bongo Burger! =)

I used to live two blocks from here when I was a Berkeley student, and I used to come by all the time to get their $3 breakfast. I have no idea if they still offer this, but I LOVED it. Eggs, toast, potatoes - so good for a starving college student.

I also loved the burgers and fries here, I still dream of this place. If only this existed near me now!

I came here on the suggestion of my friend, who likes to eat out a lot. I wanted to try a place with an awesome mushroom burger. I love mushrooms so much you have no idea. This is a small place, but it works for them. They've added a Persian flavor do some of their dishes. I haven't tried them though. 

I just ordered a mushroom burger. The patty was very flavorful. My only complaint is there wasn't enough mushrooms! Also, I really liked their fries. I think they're using Oreda fries, which I find funny.

Persian Burger.. You were quite tasty. Even though you were put together like a sandwich, the lamb meat made it up to me. The chopped up lettuce, tomato, and some mayo did add some nice touch. I like the idea of being able to choose from a french bread bun or pita to wrap you up... or if I want you whole or half. And you do go quite nicely with the crispy crinkle fries. But I do wish you were a bit meatier because that would had been more savory. 

Bongo Burger.. You're a good spot for a quick bite to eat. My friend seems to really like your mushroom burger since he ordered one to nom in the restaurant, and the other for to-go. That must say something about your burgers. Plus, I thought the portion size was good for it's price, and there's a pretty good assortment of food in your menu. And your service was not bad, but it was a bit too obvious on how much nicer you became after getting tipped in the tip jar.

Since I am from way out of town, I believe my first time meal here would be my last one as well.

Want a really good burger and really good fries for cheap? Come to Bongo Burger!! Seriously, the food here is high quality and very tasty and a meal is under $10. Unfortunately, you're compromising ambiance for price. This place is located right next to People's Park so may get someone ask, "Are you enjoying your burger cause I've been starving my whole life," then guilt you into buying them lunch. 

Still, I love Bongo Burger and usually get either the black bean burger or turkey burger with fries, then load up on sriracha and ranch.

They also have a really neat painting of a woman cheating on her (I assume) husband with the cook.
mmmmmmmmmmmmm eggplant mmmmmm no 7. mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm thats all.

i had the hummus combo. 
the falafel was incredible and the hummus was better than average. 
for the price, it's amazing.

My husband had been eating at Bongo Burger for years and always told me about how great it was, but I don't spend too much time in Berkeley. When I finally got around to trying them out, I realized I was missing out on a gem. 
The food is consistently high quality (they use Niman Ranch beef). My fave is the shish kebob sandwich - a huge french roll with sliced up steak, onions & tomato. simple but delish. They also make the best falafels and hummus I've had anywhere.
We now make the drive to Berkeley just to get Bongo Burger!

I'm not sure why I like this place so much. There really isn't anything that amazing about it. Everything is fairly average. However, for some reason I end up eating here almost every time I'm on telegraph, and I'm always extremely satisfies afterward. It's like they put nicatine in their patties. I always get the Cheeseburger combo, which is a pretty sweet deal for 7.50ish. I think what sets this place apart is their clean, cool atmosphere, their kinda large patties, and their quality buns. What ever it is, I'm down with it.

Hmmmm... people seem to like this place. Well, I went there once, and had a different experience. 

I was starving, and had a 30 minute ride back to the city ahead of me, so popped into Bongo and had a Burger.  I thought it tasted ok, but not great. Then I hopped on  BART, and before I'd even reach MacArthur, I knew something was wrong. 

So wrong, in fact, that as I sat there in a cold sweat, zooming past West Oakland, I was forced to strategize for what I hoped would not happen before I reached my safe, clean bathroom, and I decided that in the event of an under-the-Bay-Bongo-Burger emergency, I would fake a seizure. 

Luckily, it did not *quite* come to that. But it would take a lot to get me to go back there again.

Mmm...Best burgers in Berkeley.

This place is tasty, fresh and reasonably priced, I just wish they would come to SF!
Go for the fullsize lamb sandwich, add a couple falafel, and top with extra tahini,  the northside and southside location make it a great pre-drink spot if you're looking for some cheap mediterranean

Can't believe I forgot to review this joint.  My friends and I used to come here at LEAST every other week for our burger fix back when we were undergrads.  Let's face it, decent burger joints are hard to find within walking distance of the southside of campus, and though this place doesn't exactly hit the spot, it comes pretty damn close.  Their burgers taste pretty amazing and it's huge, and their crinkled fries are just right.  I think the secret is in their Niman ranch sauce or whatever they use.  I'm a real sucker for ranch so you apply that goodness on the burger and fries and all of a sudden I'm a fan. 

Only problem was the steep prices, sure their portions are heavy but expect to shell out around 9-10 for a combo meal, and though it might be worth it, I"m willing to bet that most of the customers here are money starved college students and I'd say that's a bit on the steep end for us back then.

soooooooo im pretty sure that bongo burger's persian burger is one of the most delicious things i have put in my mouth. that little lamby was so tender and flavorful and a very filling. I also sampled the bacon burger which was average at best. 

I also thoroughly enjoyed the krinkle fries that came with the meal.

This review is for the Persian burger ONLY, which I love and would eat every time I come to Berkeley if I didn't want to try other restaurants in Berkeley. Bongo Burger advertises using Niman Ranch Ground Beef, and the Persian burger beef does not disappoint. It is flavorful and cooked perfectly medium rare and paired with a roll. The biggest plus is the size of the burger; definitely enough for a hungry boy like me. 

What I recommend: Persian Burger

After my first try at Bongo a few years ago, I totally forgot the existence of this amazing burger place. Recently my roommate reignited my interest in oily American foods, so I dropped by this place for the mushroom burger combo (#1). The buns were slightly burnt and crunchy and there weren't as many grilled mushrooms as I thought, but the flavor of a good burger was definitely present. I had a nostalgic moment of being a freshman - totally entertaining!

Come here for a hearty and aromatic burger and fries!

This place has the best onion rings I've ever had! They're done in big, thick slices, and so have more of an onion taste than the rings at most burger places. They're amazing!

I like the variety of different stuff on their menu here, especially as it's all quite cheap. I particularly like their black bean burger (pleasantly spicy, with a sorta odd texture that isn't bad but takes a bit to get used to), their turkey burgers (which are made with some kind of seasoning that makes the patty simply delicious), their new special spicy chicken sandwich (it's a seasoned ground chicken patty, not too spicy, but very tasty), and their shishkebob sandwich (very good quality beef, seasoned with what they call "soma," which should perhaps be sprinkled on all food for the rest of time, as it is so tasty). I've also been known to order the Mediterranean Plate pretty often (falafel, pita, hummus, dolmas, tabouli, and a big wedge of feta cheese), and I appreciate that there are some distinctly non-burger options at such a distinctly burger-ish place.

They have a number of plates and specials (sandwich, fries, drink), and they are totally flexible about substitutions: you can get onion rings instead of fries, get a different size drink, etc. They adjust the price slightly, and you still end up with a nice discount.

The dining room is very small and often quite crowded during the school semester, but I still find it quite pleasant when I can get a table. One entire wall is made of windows looking out onto a fairly quiet side street, and the large windows slide open, so that you can get a very nice breeze sitting there in the summer.

Persian burger and fries gets me every single time.

Fast, doesn't-feel-like-it's-going-to-clog-your-arteries, easy food.

Eat it. =)

The burgers are good but breakfast is unbeatable! Two eggs any style with yummy potatoes (I add their bomb ranch) and toast for $3. Ate at the Southside location practically every other day. A Berkeley favorite.

This Bongo burger gets a star lower than the Bongo burger on center namely because of service/location.

Personally, eating right near People's park and telegraph? Call me snobby but let's be honest here people, it's not very pleasant eating outside the restaurant. 

Burgers are about the same as its University Ave. and Euclid St. counterparts - standard sized burger, but nothing too crazy. I really felt like the bun didn't get that nice golden crispy look = disappointed kelly D:

If you're in a hurry for a decent burger + fries, hit up bongo burger. If you're in the mood for a better burger... Well. It's berkeley. What do you expect?? 

Only 2 nomstars!

Restaurant area and service: small but clean. Cooked up the food quickly.  Cashier was nice.

Persian Burger plus mushrooms: It had a flavorful but thin lamburger patty housed in a long bun.  I can't even call it a burger because it looks like a sub or hoagie. I paid them to add mushrooms but I feel like they didn't put much of it at all.  The sandwich tastes great with the sriracha and ranch that they have available at the counter.

Bacon Cheeseburger: The hamburger patty was really thin and slightly dry.  You can barely taste the beef.  The patty looks like one of those frozen prepackaged patties you buy from Safeway. I suggest making the patties thicker so that the burgers are juicier.

Fries: Nothing fancy. They look and taste like the crinkly Ore Ida fries you can buy from Safeway.  

Bottom line: I am not really sure what the fuss is about this burger joint. I was really disappointed because based on Yelp reviews, I was expecting my tastebuds and belly to be blown away.
I went to Cal from 1988 to 1992.  I have not had a sandwich or burger since, better than the Persian Burger.  Go Bears!  Go Bongo Burger!

I've heard good things about Bongo Burger so Sunday morning I decided to try it out.

The service was AWFUL! My friend and I tried to order 1 breakfast special (3 eggs, toast & jelly, hash browns) and 1 turkey burger combo (fries and soda), from the unfriendly and intimidating cashier. But they were out of potatoes so we were told our only option was fries. We asked if there were other options, the cashier told us no! 

Minutes after ordering we realize that: 1. You may substitute tabouleh or another side for fries in any order for $1 extra. 2. Fountain soda is not the only drink available, they also have fresh-squeezed orange and carrot juice. Why did the cashier not tell us this? 

The girl who ordered after us asked for a carrot juice and the cashier gave her a withering glance which seemed to say, "do I really have to turn on the carrot juicer today?". Not friendly.

Upon receiving our food, there were no forks and no jelly and no knives. Had to go back to the counter twice to get items which ought to have been served with the food! At least the server was apologetic...

The burger was very delicious and had a good amount of toppings. The eggs and fries and toast were hot, greasy, and yummy as expected.

But the service is enough to convince me not to come back.
The Dwight Bongo is my favorite Bongo Burger, and the one with the most bongo memories.  Everything on the menu is tasty, but I'll keep coming back for the turkey burger and swiss.

Yum + Cheap ($7.80 for burger/fries/soda) = Excellent

Only in glorious Berkeley do you find a cute little burger joint that accommodates vegans and vegetarians, too... ah, I love California.

While I stumbled in for real burger on my way to somewhere else, I couldn't help but notice the wonderful (and healthy) menu --- full of fun stuff like falafel, tebouleh, etc. 

The cashier was so darned friendly and so were the young guys cooking up the goods. Good vibes all around. Cute little stop-in joint, no doubt.

So here I am at a fancy hotel one day attending a sleepy cocktail fundraiser and in the midst of wolfing down lamb chops, I start chatting with one of the friendly servers. Turns out he is Persian and noticing how I am annihilating the meat in my hands, points out that he is a foodie too. So we hit it off well.

I ask him what his favorite Persian food joint is in the area, and expect him to mention one of the more traditional joints. He says "Bongo Burger." I say "Bongo Burger???" He confirms "Bongo Burger." And then throws in "Try the Persian burger there." And then he draws out a slow whistle.

Not one to let a good recommendation go - especially one backed by a slow whistle, I end up at the lively Bongo Burger the same week and order said Persian burger. Holy sideburns of the Shah! Why didn't anyone think of this before? A very, very tasty and perfectly grilled chailo kebab with all the works in a bun? It is, simply put, "khailee khoob".

Thank you anonymous Persian server.

I've only had one thing here before--the lamb sandwich and I'm a HUGE fan of lamb SO I WAS ECSTATIC!! The taste is not super amazing, but for some reason I'm very intrigued by it. But like I said, I just really love the taste of lamb. Definitely an interesting sandwich that all lamb lovers should try.

I really like this place, mostly because there aren't that many burger joints here. I ordered a Persian burger combo, which came out to be less than $10, and enjoyed the hell out of that lamb sandwich. The fries were zigzag shaped and fried to a crispy delight and the burger was everything done right to a lamb kabob. 

Cheap, fast service, delicious kabob, credit card okay? Yeah, FIVE FUCKING STARS FOR YOU, BONGO BURGER.

It's another perfectly good Bongo Burger! Conveniently located next to Shakespeare and Co.! A great way to spend 2 hours on a rainy afternoon like today.

Is it just me, or are the fries better here than at their Euclid Ave. location?

Gave this place another try and, this time, I did not let me diet hold me back.  I got a burger (don't remember the name on the menu, but it's just a regular burger) and fries.  The fries are delicious as I remember them being the first time, but the sandwich I got before was what kept me from rating this place higher last time.  When I first took my burger out of my to go bag, I already knew I would have to update my review.

The burger is massive.  The bun is a perfectly round and golden masterpiece.... if you're thinking something dirty, it's not my fault!

The patty itself is juicy and delicious.  The toppings are again the downfall of this burger - shredded lettuce, a few slices of tomato and a blander than mayo yogurt sauce.  Still, I can tolerate this much better with the moist, flavorful patty.

Too bad I ate this the week I was graduating... otherwise I would have been a frequent customer of Bongo Burger.  Good I thing have friends to visit in Berkeley :D

Good food reasonably priced.
Great breakfast specials.
I enjoyed the Mediterranean dolmas, hummus and falafel.
The sandwiches are good and tasty.
Overall a good experience.
Small place with outside seating.

I would classify this place as an above average typical campus restaurant. The seating is limited, the location is convenient, the staff and service are OK. The selection is kind of limited, but I think this is the only place i've seen that serves a "Persian Burger" or a "Black bean burger". 

I love the mushroom burger here. I don't know what kind of sauce they use, but it is delicious. The bread they use for the burger too is also pretty tasty. They also serve a selection of sandwiches, which are also pretty good as well. I used to think the price here was expensive, but I have come to terms that it really is pretty average around the area. 

If you need a burger and don't have the time to get to Barneys, this is the place to go.
4 stars for the yummiest black bean veggie burger!!!

I was craving for a burger really bad tonight when I decided to try some place new. I always passed by Bongo Burger and after some research on Yelp, I decided to try it out. I was in a mood for lots of meat, so I ordered the Bacon Burger and its best friend, a side of french fries, to go. 

When I ate the burger, I found the meat to be a little too red for my taste but the parts that were a little more cooked tasted fine to me. The bacon was a little thick and not as crispy as I would've liked, but it was the buns that killed it for me. The buns were so incredible tough and chewy that it felt like I was gnawing on leather. Every bite was a battle and I came out the loser - the burger totally fell apart. I eventually ditched the top bun and sloppily ate my way through the rest. The fries were crispy, but they didn't knock my socks off.

Even though I was expecting more, maybe I'll give the much talked about Persian Burger a shot, but I'll be passing on their beef burgers.

I never ate here as a Cal student so I'm glad I finally tried it, especially after a massive burger craving. Loved that this place has ample seating (for a spot near campus). I got the #7 combo which is a Persian burger  that's made with lamb, fries and a small soda for about $8. My friend and I also shared a mushroom burger. 

I thought my combo was a bit expensive so was pleasantly surprised when I got the order because it is quite big! My friend and I could have shared just shared a combo and that would have been enough. I wouldn't really call the Persian a burger since it looks like a subway foot long. The lamb was thin and tasty enough but I definitely liked my half of the mushroom burger better. It was a sizable burger, juicy and flavorful. The crinkle cut fries were piping hot. 

They also have falafal plates, fresh juices and baklava! But no refills on the sodas. There are better lamb burgers out there but the beef burgers here can definitely stand their own!

When I was a poor student in the early 80s, I lived on top of Bongo Burgers and tried everything they had.  The same Middle Eastern guy has been running it for the last 25 years.  I've eaten a lot of Kip burgers and Top Dogs, but these guys are tops.  They were voted best burgers in Berkeley.  They are now a Berkeley Institution.  But better than their burgers are their Persian burgers.  Even the owner says the Persian burgers, made with lamb, are the best.  My favorite is the half Persian burger on Pita bread ($3.95).  I haven't figured out what the white secret sauce is.  The only reason why I pit-stop from time to time in Berkeley is for their half Persian Burgers (once called the Lulah Kabob), French fries, and root beer.  Then top that off with a Baklava.  This is the best lunch ever and totally worth the detour to the corner of Dwight and Telegraph Ave.

This review is a shout out to my lovely Norwegian friends who introduced me to this place. Imagine this, having them repeatedly telling me, "what?! you've never had Bongo Burger", in their slightly accented English, then going on to chant "Bongo Burger is the best burger in Berkeley", "Bongo bongo...". You see why I had to give this place a try? so I did.

I tried the mushroom burger, which was really fresh and tasty. The mushrooms were nicely sauteed. As I was munching happily on my burger, it bought back memories of when my -ahem- lovely friends tricked me into almost believing that Norwegians were so health conscious they'd banned McDonalds in Norway. GRRRR but definitely good memories.

So Kenneth, Michael, Havard & Matthias you all were right. This is definitely a solid burger place.

On our Saturday Random Eats, BF @JaRue2011 & I flipped through my Yelp bookmarks to find ourselves making a lunch drive to Bongo Burger in Berkeley, CA (courtesy Yelper Peter J) http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=R9En8v3vSH1uYj_Zmzpj6g

LOCATION:  Located on Dwight Way  just a few meters East of Telegraph Ave; you can't miss it. Parking on the street (good luck) or garage parking options in vicinity. Lots of other neighbor restaurants & dives in area; lots of foot traffic from local Cal Bear students & others like BF & myself just out for a foodie adventure.

RESTAURANT: Small space, but table seating is not truly arm to arm. Most ppl who dine to eat, do just that & then they're out; else folks take it go. With small space, patrons come w/ the hawk eye of seating availability & the fast pace stretch to grab the seating before it gets taken. It's not combative tho, everyone seems to know you either find space inside, find space on outside tables, or stand out on the sidewalk & eat. Armless wood chairs, simple wood tables 2-seater or 4-seater inside, & few outdoor patio seating on sidewalk. Courteous patrons after dinning inside/outside & bring their empty tray inside & dispose of trash.

CUST SVC: Friendly, helpful, & fast. Arrived on a Saturday late afternoon, about 3rd-4th person in line, grabbed indoor 2-seater table (think we lucked out honestly), & waited like 5-7min for our # to be called for pick-up. Being our 1st visit here, cashier was friendly & helpful for questions ...like "What's in the Perisan Burger?" Their condiment bar options are kept well full for their many Bongo Burger eaters.

EATS: All around hot fries & flavorful burgers served! Almost a bonus when a joint grills your buns, & they do here. BF absolutely loved the condiment options available with Ranch, Sriracha Hot Sauce, etc.

BF-J with his Persian Lamb Burger http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=xxOBYkHeSyyZSqLozCinBw
** $6.50 Persian Burger almost length of serving tray http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=F1RG82mIU9zGqltx3pKjPA
** Few bites into Persian Burger http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=VKHP6X67J8DlZomBg0aHkA
...Ingredients all fresh, toasty bun, enjoyed the shredded lettuce, & flavorful. BF's only "wish" would be for a thicker pattie; he felt there was more bread ratio than meat.

Me with my Mushroom Burger http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=9d55sdKJSjNASTIvKSzwUA
** $7.95 Mushroom Burger Combo http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=1p5rpJI1ElEQLHhoExI3VA
** Few bites into Mushroom Burger http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=GKqcDaP4YkCnJLUh4j1dsg
...Toasty bun, fresh vegs, a good tasting pattie. Combo comes with small fries & fountain drink prepped from behind cashier counter; not sure if free re-fills.  

OVERALL: Final tab for our "Yelp flipped coin decision" to Bongos came to $17.84 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/G3d-xJF_Rt-P_za2eZ1q-Q?select=Ja4IMy2HBaCaOld78LjbYw It was a good foodie adventure that we both enjoyed.

Hmmm... don't know why I haven't review this yet! Aside from the classic burger, I recommend the persian burger and steak sandwich. I don't think the vegan plates are that great, but do go for the vegetarian plates. I've never been here for breakfast, but I would for an omelette. While it is expensive, you do get a lot for your money.

Yesterday:
1 bongo salad + 
1 mushroom burger combo + 
1 cheeseburger combo = 
$21 for 3 people with small appetites

I pine for cheeseburgers about once a week and it's been my dedicated duty to scour any and every city I'm in for the very best. Since moving to the Bay Area, I've tried a handful and on my list of bookmarked spots to check out, Bongo Burger proved to be good, not mind-blowing, but decent. I'm sensing that the Persian burger is clearly the standout option. Alas I'm not the biggest lamb fan.

Unlike In N Out, Shake Shack, and Five Guys style burgers, these burger patties are super thin and suuuper wide. Holding all the condiments and toppings together is a pair of fully seeded sesame seed buns. In my perfect burger world, the bun is either a potato roll or a sesame bun, but never should they be wider than my hand with extended and parted fingers. It strays too far from my ideal beef to topping to bread ratio.

Fries were crinkled and over greased, so nothing to note there. How does this compare? Pretty average I'm sorry to say.

Meh, should have spent my money on something else for lunch while I was in Berkeley. I was craving sushi during the time. That little alley plaza has a bunch of good cheap food, and this sushi joint doesn't really belong in there. It was completely empty with no customers, which should have been a huge red flag. The inside felt like a sauna, it was so hot. Probably not good for preparing sushi -_-

Their rolls were overpriced for their quality and presentation. Not sure how fresh the fish tasted... oh well. Well at least they take credit cards, I suppose.

It seems that some of these people have mistakenly posted Alameda Sushi House's review here... there's no receptionist, there's no seating or waiter service really...

I always get the crunchy roll, because it's cooked and I don't raw stuff. So someone tell me how I got food poisoning from this sushi? Obviously some ghetto factors here, and cleanliness issues. I've eaten here perhaps 3 times, and gotten sick once, so I guess it might have been a rare occasion.

Not just that though, I ordered my roll to go, and I was standing around waiting for 20 minutes or so, and the guy at the register (I believe he owns the place too! Shame on him...) is just chatting in Korean with his buddy, and I'm standing there, right in front, waiting for my food (in the meantime, my boyfriend's already ordered Thai Basil and received his food and been waiting with me for 10 minutes)... and the guy doesn't ask me what I'm waiting for, he doesn't check on my order. It was only when the 2 chefs were basically standing around doing nothing, that I realized that either my order was forgotten or it wasn't made or already made...

The owner didn't seem to care that I was standing there waiting for something that wasn't coming, so I approached him and asked, and my roll had been sitting in a box next to him for who knows how long, and he didn't bother figuring out why it was there and what I was waiting for. WTF?

Not going back here. Sorry. Go to Joshuya's on Dwight and Telegraph instead, or go to the REAL Sushi House in Alameda.

Though the sushi are pretty good they are a tad overpriced for their flavor. I must say, I ordered one of their specials that came with California rolls, Gyoza and Teriyaki Chicken and was utterly disappointed. The Teriyaki Chicken had the funkiest spoiled taste. After that incident I never returned even for sushi. I have become a  Tako guy and is staying that way

I purchased an A's roll here before, and it was ok - hard to screw that one up.

Today, however, was an entirely different experience. It was the only place on the way to my house (and Nude Sushi does not deliver on Sundays), I was starving, and mistakenly assumed I would receive a decent meal. I usually order nigiri (mackerel and unagi) and edamame. I asked for it to go, which was probably a bad idea to begin with.

On my way home, I kept smelling a fishy stench. Only when I got home I realized it was my dinner. The unagi was ok, but the mackerel - I did not dare to eat it. The skin was still on it, which I have never seen before, and when I attempted to peel it back, I realized it was impossible, since the fish slices were paper-thin.

I left edamame for last, and at this point it was supposed to be my only salvation. Yuck! First, it came in a small plastic container, but there were exactly 16 edamame pods in it - barely to cover the bottom of the box. And second, it was so overcooked and mushy, I had to give up on most of it.

So here I am, $12 later, still starving, and having a bad feeling that this experience might be accompanied by a food poisoning later.

In short, it was absolutely horrific. And for the price I paid, I could have gotten a satisfying meal anywhere else. So no matter how badly I want sushi next time, if the Berkeley Sushi House is the only place available, I'd rather starve.

Let's have a sit-down sushi restaurant in the size of a dorm room!!! really, it's that small and I would never want to eat there unless maybe it were summer, christmas, thanksgiving... any time when school isn't in session. 

The food isn't bad for cheap, fast sushi... i suppose. I really like the spicy tuna roll which I get to-go (and I usually have to wait like 10 minutes for it, but at least I get to see them make it to order) and they have some hot tea for you to sip on while you wait. I've tried a few other things on the menu but, I really wouldn't recommend it unless you're just looking for an alternative to all the fried rices and egg rolls and heavy pastas and slabs of meat that you normally find at asian ghetto. 

The 'finding nemo' roll picture on the outside (don't know if it's still there), is it... an advertisement? to be funny? it's like a cartoon picture of nemo, cut up in a roll, and SMILING?!?!  highly, HIGHLY disturbing.

It's overpriced.  This place basically gets by because people are too lazy to go elsewhere.  I'm not a very picky eater, and it'll take a lot for me to feel cheated after eating somewhere, but at sushi house I've felt cheated more than a couple times.  

Lunch is probably the only time I'd go here, and even then, you could find something better for cheaper, literally 10 feet away.

I've gone here a couple times and this was the first time I got a bento box which cost me $10 so I was hoping to get a good amount of food. I got the bento box with salmon teriyaki and California rolls. You get rice, salad, and a couple slices of oranges with it.

First of all take a look at your middle finger. You may as well eat that because the piece of salmon you're getting with this bento box is probably the same size if not smaller. It was literally two bites of salmon. For the price I paid this is a horrible portion to be getting. The salmon Teriyaki didn't taste that spectacular either I got like a tablespoon of Teriyaki sauce.

You get the regular order of 6 California rolls and they're not bad so I wasn't too upset about that. Next time you come here don't go for the bento box if you don't want to get ripped off.

The sushi here is really average, meant for college kids I guess.  My friend wanted a bento box and out of obligation (not really hehe)  I ordered two rolls.  They have a $10 card minimum which kind of pissed me off because I actually only wanted to munch on one roll.  I forgot what the name of the rolls were but they were there was a huge rice to fish ratio .. never a good thing.  It was good for what it's worth I suppose and the prices for each roll are somewhat cheaper than what you'd usually expect.  But still, it's hard to justify paying 11 dollars for something that doesn't wow me.

I had the biggest sushi craving ever and decided to try out this place because it's one of the only sushi places in the area that is open on Sundays.

I ordered three rolls to bring to work and share with my co-workers.  However, the rolls are tiny compared to any other sushi house.  I spent way too much money for the rolls to be tiny.  The prices seemed average but I expected more for what I paid.

I waited 10 minutes just to order from the Asian man who was working, he didn't even raise a head or hand to note that I was there or any greeting at all to notify me that he'd be with me when he was able.

The sushi wasn't that great, I've had better and fresher.

This location does accept credit/debit cards but with a $.50 fee nicely posted at the register.

Overall, I'd go some where else for your sushi fix unless you just so happen to have a craving on a Sunday.

My teenage son wanted to come here because he had eaten at the sister restaurant in Alameda.  His mother is Japanese so he should have know better, but I came anyway.  Bad choice.  The place was empty.  They didn't have uni, amaebi, or toro, my favorites.  That's 3 strikes right off the bat.  I ate the soba with shrimp where they added a sweet sauce - terrible.  And the hamachi was not very fresh.  
When my son gave me the address, I suspected that it would not be good because being next to campus, most fast food places are not particularly good.  They are designed to be fast, inexpensive, and good enough to get a student by until the next meal. I should know, I was a Cal student back in the day.
So I would say if you appreciate good Japanese food and have been to Japan - don't waste your time or money.
Their rolls are good but I don't like waiting for a long time during peak business times.

I can honestly say that the Berkeley Sushi house far outranks the original Alameda sushi house, from my experience....

+ The rolls are bigger, FRESHER, and just plain better.

+  The lady who works the cash register is really nice.

+  My roommate is on a mission to eat every single roll there, and as a result is getting a roll named after her when she finishes the list (i swear!)

+ they are CONSISTENT with their sushi quality!

- The music SUCKS

- limited seating, but its the asian ghetto...what do you expect?

Pretty okay. Not as good as the Sushi House in Alameda. I believe I had a samurai or island roll. Berkeley special is definitely worth it. You're better off making the trek to Kai's or Sushi House in Alameda
Love their California and California Deluxe Rolls! Pretty inexpensive, too.

Sushi here really isn't that good. To much rice and not enough fish and crab. 

Their 6$ Berkeley Special is actually pretty good though. It includes chicken, rice, California roll, and salad for a low price.

Very pricey for low quality sushi. The fish and unagi were not fresh. The sushi was just plan not good. Avoid!

Pros:
- NONE

Cons:
- Pricey
- Not Fresh
- Bad Tasting Sushi

I just came back and let me say, BEST SUSHI I EVER HAD! My friend and I stuffed ourselves with their A's rolls and California Deluxe rolls. THEY TASTED AMAZING and for about 6 pieces of each assortment the total (15.33$)  was worth every bite!

Good: Food, Service, Atmosphere, Location, Prices.
You're crazy if you pass this place up!

They take cash, debit, credit cards and didn't seem to ask for any ID...

This place is bad. Came here for lunch one day, and I had to wait over 25 minutes for my food. And when the food finally arrived, it was tiny portions. Never coming back here again, nor suggest it to anyone to go here at all. Avoid if you can.

Like mentioned by Yan N. many of these reviews are incorrect because they are reviewing the wrong sushi house.   Many are referring to the Sushi House in Alameda (which i highly recommend). 

1. this sushi house is not located in front of any water or beach.
2. no patio....
------thast Alameda.


This place is okay...but a bit overpriced.  Don'x expect a lot.. the rolls are decent but not fantastic.  There also pretty small as well.  The environment isn't the best for dine it  but its really a place meant for Cal students to grab a quick bite of sushi.  IF you're desperate and in the area, you'll like it or otherwise id take the effort to venture out towards Alameda or SF.  Overall........................3.8

hubby and i came here for lunch before heading out to scharffen berger.. the restaurant itself is very nice.. next to the water, huge windows, and a great view.. 

we arrived there right before the peak of the lunch hour, so we got the last inside (non patio) table...and we were seated right away.. 

i don't have much to say about this place...except that the only thing they really have going for them is the location because of the view..

service - crappy... my sushi bar food came 15-20 minutes before my bf's bento.. when it was obvious i ordered the sushi for MYSELF, and not a SHARED thing.. knowing that, they shouldve waited to make my food so that it came out around the same time...5 mins is alright, but to have my food just sit there for 15-20 minutes is NOT okay.. when the bf asked about his food...the only thing the waiter said was "it kitchen food, take longer you know" umm not even a sorry? our drinks were NEVER refilled. our waiter did not check up on us once after giving us our food.

food - average tasting japanese food...big portions.. rolls are humungous.. each roll is approx 6-8 peices and is so big it wont fit in your mouth.. i did like how his bento came with a wedge of honeydew melon though, better than the usual crappy orange..

don't think i'd come back...such a shame.. it should be turned into a nice classy restaurant with views like that!

NEVER GOING BACK AGAIN!- Worst place for anyone vegetaran.

I ordered a veggie bento box, and I saw her use the same knife for cutting my tofu as she used to cut chicken and pork. Additionally, when I went to sit down and eat my veggie tempura, I took a bite and noticed it was SHRIMP! I went to complain,and the owner said to just take the shrimp out, and be thankful that I got free shrimp for the price of veggie tempura. UH! HELL NO! They also use the same oil, and cook in the same pans. NEVER GOING HERE AGAIN. POOR sanitation

It would have been a 3 to 4 star review last year, but I never got around to it. This year, I finally went back last week for dinner. Basically, the rolls that actually taste good (or okay good) were expensive for a restaurant in the Ghetto. And the rolls that are not expensive only sound good on paper and tastes very mediocre. Their pricing strategy (which was to significantly increase prices in the past year) isn't that smart.

I love the food in Berkeley - you find so many delicious and filling goodies for low prices! With Japanese food being one of my top cuisines, I do have to say that my experiences with Sushi House has been pretty much disappointing.

Customer Service: Normally, small little family-run restaurants are the best at customer service because they genuinely care about their patrons. Every time I've been at Sushi House, the oldish man seemed to mug me a lot. Not a welcoming environment at all - it's not like I'm wearing a Stanford shirt (god forbid).

Food: The portions are fairly small and not really filling. One of my favourite sushi rolls, the Lion King, is one of my favourite rolls - baked salmon atop California Rolls with sauce. Normally delicious and massive! At Sushi House, it's fairly measly and doesn't tame my hunger even a tiny bit. I end up with enough room in my stomach to order another main course.
