At Sushi House, the salmon wasn't that fresh either and was fairly sloppily made. Disappointing is the right word for it.

---

In terms of delicious Japanese food, you can find it elsewhere in Berkeley. There are plenty of other locations that offer tasty treats.

I'm a major sushi critic, the others are just on crack or something. This place is bomb, I love their samurai especially! I've tried all places in san jose, san francisco (yes SF) and there is nothing better that compares to this. so far I've tried 13 specials out of their menu and I haven't been dissappointed once. This is a good deal for their prices, some other places charge up the arse because of their service, area, seating, experience. Sure, this place doesnt have any of those to be on their good side, but fact is the sushi kicks ass.

Today for lunch I decided to check out my old "favorite" sushi place, Japanese Snacks, located in the food ghetto on Durant. I say "favorite" in quotes, because it was the place I always went to when I was living in the dorms. It was their sushi that got me to like sushi in the first place, but oddly enough it's not great sushi. So I have other more real Favorite sushi places now, but I kept going there for many years, because it was close and convenient and decent. A year or so ago, I switched and started going to Tako Sushi. Why? I'm not sure. Tako Sushi is about a block closer to where I work, and I am a lazy-ass. Though I think that mainly the switch happened because Japanese Snacks didn't have a salmon/avocado roll on the menu, and the one time I tried to order it, the language barrier was enough to make it a pain in the ass. And then it wasn't all that good.

But after a really bad experience at Tako Sushi, I decided to give Japanese Snacks another shot. As I approached the restaurant, I noticed that things were a bit different. The sign now said Berkeley Sushi House, and the interior had been remodelled. The previously somewhat jank but homey little Mom & Pop Japanese restaurant was now slickified. Gone was the familiar face of the older woman who'd been serving me sushi since I was 18. In her place was a larger crew of much younger cooks. I was wary, but then I saw the menu. YES! It was greatly expanded, and closely mimicked that of Sushi House in Alameda. I LOVE Sushi House. I was also happy to see that they hadn't increased their prices.

I ordered an Oregon Roll--yep, now they have a salmon/avocado roll on the menu--and miso soup to go. I sat at the bar and watched one of the chefs preparing the sushi. I saw him cutting slices of delicious-looking salmon, then I saw him roll up some shrimp tempura, and when he pulled out the lemon slices I realized he was creating my favorite: the Island Roll. SCORE. He didn't make my sushi; that was done by the other chef, who he seemed to be training. I got my food and walked back to my office, delighted that I seem to have stumbled upon a good sushi restaurant that's only a couple of blocks away!

After all that buildup, the food was unfortunately a bit disappointing. The miso soup was okay, but kind of bland. I tried not to stress about that, though, as I remember in the old days of Japanese Snacks, there would occasionally be bland miso soup. It doesn't mean it'll be like that every day. They still didn't give me enough soy sauce (I need two packets, not one!) and the wasabi was still not hot enough (problems that the old restaurant had). The roll I'd ordered came with only 6 pieces, not 8 like it used to, and it didn't look as super-scrumptious as I'd hoped. The avocado was a little brown, and the salmon wasn't very generous. But it looked like salmon, not mysterious red mush (ughh, Tako Sushi), so that was a major plus. It tasted okay, but not great. Nothing to write home about. I was annoyed because it seemed like the chef-in-training who'd made mine didn't know how to properly cut the salmon. There were still white connecty tough bits in it, which could have easily been removed and greatly improved my sushi experience.

In the end, though, it was still far far better than the alternatives in the area. I'll definitely be going back and trying some of the different rolls on the menu. The fish in the sushi bar display case all looked good, and the rolls made by the chef who knew what he was doing looked very tasty. I just hope it's better next time!

Edit, 12/3/07: I've gone back to this place a couple more times and each time it's relatively disappointing. The rolls range from "blah" to "not so good" and their miso soup still sucks. I generally don't go there.

On a sushi scale of 1-10, I rate Berkeley Sushi House about a 3.5.

Some of the better sushi in the area though that isn't saying much. I came here because I am a big fan of the Alameda Sushi house. It is a hole in the wall in Durant Food Court and the setting isn't spectacular or inviting. First timers may be confused that you need to order and pay first at the counter. I was hoping for the delicious baked rolls that the Alameda brand has and they had them in the beginning but now it seems they are slowly taking things off the menu as they take too long to prepare(the first time I went I waited about 20 minutes for one roll). 

Also vegetarians watch out- make sure they don't add tobiko on the top of your roll as they did to the veggie dragon roll me and my boyfriend ordered(though I think they will no longer do this). Overall the price is the same as the Alameda Brand but not as well made.

I'd go back every now and then but it won't be one of my most frequented restaurants ever
Not that worthy.

Located conveniently on Durant Street in the "Asian Ghetto".. haha i love that term the asian ghetto.. i guess the Berkeley Sushi can be considered as a ghetto restaurant. This place reminds of small dirty restaurants in Hong Kong, but the thing is that i remembered about the small dirty restaurants in HK being good and flavorful. The Sushi house has fish that has been frozen for who knows how long! It tasted like the freezer burn! I hate that taste. But seriously what can you expect from a place like this.THE ASIAN GHETTO! The Ton Katsu Don was um..... WHERE IS THE DAMN CHICKEN? It was all rice and vegetables.. and it was very sweet for some reason. Gross. The only thing worth getting here is the Baked Scallop roll and the crunchy california roll. Just stick to those two items and your stomach will be fine!

If you're feeling like sushi in Berkeley, i'd definitely try to avoid this place!  Though this does share the same name as the Alameda Sushi House, the quality of sushi here is a large step down with about the same prices!

Just in general, the fish here is not very fresh at all, if you plan on ordering any rolls with actual raw fish in it, you will be disappointed.  It may not be prevalent in the more sauce covered rolls i.e. the titanic roll, but with other rolls where sauce isn't so prevalent, i.e. alaskan roll or other maki with tuna, salmon or eel, the fish will just leave a bad taste in your mouth. 

I was lucky to be wary of the fish there and not order any nigiri. 

I haven't checked out this place in a long time, I tend to ignore it right away walking into asian ghetto, but their deep fried and regular california roll is fine i guess, just maki rolls outside of raw fish will keep you safe, and from what I remember, the berkeley student special is OK for its value compared to everything else on the menu.  

If you're really really in the mood for sushi and have walking as your only means of transportation, i'd just walk a little down telegraph and hit up Tako, for just decent, nothing too special, rolls.

The food is marginally better than Nanayiro and Joshu-Ya, but you do trade that little bit of quality for a whole lot of ambience. It is nice, however, to have a sushi option in the ghetto, even if it isn't open as late as some others are. 

As good as Sushi House is for staying on that line of mediocrity and fighting to veer away from the horrendous, I have noticed one atrocity being committed on a consistent, if not daily, basis: sticky, goopy, flavorless rice-- a phenomenon to which I've assigned the name "church rice." It's the oddest mix of paradoxes for how rice is supposed to turn out: it is overcooked and mushy but falls apart in a roll. One would think that such tacky, sticky rice would at least do a decent job of staying put once molded.

I love hating on my own ethnic group just as much as anyone, but I'm not quick to put down an establishment just because it's a Japanese joint being run by Koreans (sure, statistics seem to indicate that if it's not Japanese-run, it won't be great, but there is the power of the benefit of the doubt). But I cannot forgive a Korean who does THAT to my precious rice.

It's still better than some other Japanese places, as far as rolls go; you shouldn't rule it out completely unless you're an orniphobe by day and hobo-phobe by night.

Surprisingly expensive for this part of town, being in a college cheap eats area.  The sushi is reasonably good, but you can get the same quality at a lower price elsewhere.

the BAD - -- ordered a katsu don... these guys canNOT make it right... who puts tomatos, bell peppers, cucumbers, and yakisoba sauce in katsu don?!!?!?!

I tried their Oregon roll and Alaskan roll, both under $5.  The rice was a little bland. I want to complain that the pieces (six of each in either roll) were cut too thick.  But that actually just means more food for my dollar, so I'll leave it at that.  And while we're on the topic of portion size, the chunks (yes, chunks) of salmon we're *huge*.  I'll probably keep going to Tako Sushi for dinner, but for a quick lunch bite, Sushi House might become my regular spot when I'm craving a quick bite.

A fellow Chuck runs Sushi House. He actually owned Bear Ramen and decided to try his hand at a Japanese restaurant. Him and his wife run the business and seem to enjoy it. 

+ Variety of sushi
+ Nice staff
-  Quality not commensurate with price
-  Hygiene needs wrk
-  Crammed space, bad layout of space

Munchies:
1. Lion King Roll
     + Sauce is nice drizzle on heated scallops

Final Call:
When you're a poor college student, you don't have a lottta options for good sushi.

Edible, but overpriced.  

We all know that those Big Macs and Whoppers you get never look anything like the ones pictured in the print ads or in commercials.
What a dumbass I was for thinking that this place might be any different.  Unlike in the pictures, the cuts of sashimi were basically paper-thin, and far from fresh.  (Do they freeze and then thaw them?  Sure seems like it)  
I think it's reasonable to say that if they cut their prices by 50%, it would be borderline acceptable.  But I feel ripped off, and there's nothing that pisses me off more than getting ripped off.  To top things off, I was on my way to the always dependable Steve's BBQ, but got duped by 

1) those pictures on the wall
and 
2) the name "Sushi House", which I mistakenly assumed would make this place comparable to Sushi House in Alameda.

What I want to know is: where did they take those picture-perfect snapshots of scrumptious morsels of fish and masterfully-wrapped sushi rolls?  I want to eat there.

Have a sushi craving? Hold out! Go get Thai instead.

-2 stars for food's quality (rice was hard, rice's seasoning was overwhelming and avocados were brown going on black)
-1 star for price (price is the same as a regular sushi restaurant; food court prices ought to be cheaper)
+1 star for nice staff

What HAPPENED to the portion sizes?! Everything is smaller and more expensive! I mean, this place has 'a-okay' sushi with caveats. First, the Berkeley special, which consists of rice, gyoza, sushi, your choice of meat, and a salad is $6.95, the portion size is ridiculously small. It tastes pretty okay, although I would be weary of getting their beef because I'm pretty sure last time I got that it was slightly raw on the inside because the center of the meat was cold and still chewy. Definitely not the way beef should be. You'd have to order another side dish (ranging from another 5-10 bucks) just to fill you up. And plus, they have a minimum charge of $10 if you want to use your credit/debit card. You can find better sushi in Berkeley.

3.5

I find this to be a little out of place.  My friend and I walked in expecting to be seated and provided with menus, but it took us a couple of minutes to discover that the menu was on the wall.  The pics of the rolls are helpful, but the other random magazine clippings below were distracting.  We were excited to try Toro, until we were denied to order it because it's a "special order".

It took a while to finally get our order, especially for a small restaurant like this.  Most of the food was pretty good, but the Lion King Roll kept falling apart. It's similar to the baked salmon roll at Nanayiro...but it doesn't come close to Dynamite at Koryo Sushi.

This Japanese Restaurant Impresses me by the fact that it serves mainly Students who constantly eat on the Go but still serve good quality Japanes Food! their Water Polo Roll is Simply My Favorite, Along with the Tempura Udon. It's a quick and easy place to eat Good Japanese Food.

Pros: - Easily the best sushi on the south side of campus (better than Tako obviously, better than Joshu-Ya's, better than that one place on Channing and Shattuck, etc.)
- The cashier lady is really nice, and frequently gives out free food to guests
- Hella conveniently located

Cons: - The space is really cramped (but what do you expect)
- A little pricey for me

I go here every once in a while and always like the food - I almost always get some combination of lion king roll, webster roll, and caterpillar roll. I would go a lot more if they cut the prices.

Well, I was hoping this would be the same as sushi house in Alameda, but was woefully disapointed.  The menu is more limited that the Alameda joint, and more expensive to boot, which is a shame since usually the durant food ghetto is a good place to get cheap eats.  However the worst part is the portions were tiny.  The C.F. roll and the spicy tuna rolls were depressingly lacking in substance.  $12 for two rolls that could hardly feed a child.  Sad.

Top that off with slow slow service and not much seating and I would have given it a 1 star, however the crunchy monkey that other people were getting looked like it was a decent amount of food for $6.50, so if one must have to eat at this overpriced weak sequel to the original sushi house then I'd sugest trying that first.

Eat at your own risk to your wallet.

Berkeley special. It's a go-to for me when I study--for finals, for the bar, whatever--and am looking for a quick meal that isn't single item/one-dimensional. You get chicken teriyaki, California rolls, gyoza, salad, rice, and some orange slices. Not the most compelling combination, and a little bit rice-heavy, but does the job when you're not looking for something fancy. Haven't had the chance to try the rolls except for the V8 (decent), but the pictures on the wall make most of them look pretty appetizing.

The sushi is pretty overpriced for the quality that you get. The only perk is the berkeley special which is 6.95 for chicken teriyaki, gyoza, california rolls, steamed rice and an orange.

The service isn't that great either...the cashier was half reading a book once when taking my order. Also it takes them a while to prepare everything

It's a shame tako isn't open sundays..

Few years ago I went there once as the name "sushi house", I would give them 3 stars.  

This second time I went there because the Steve Korean food was closed, it's getting worst, only 2 stars. 

Nothing much.

Love this place. The owners are super nice and the food is consistently good. Plus I usually score a free roll when I go there. My faves so far are the Cf roll, Titanic roll, and the Lambada roll. And the spicy tuna is actually really spicy! Definitely one of the better sushi places around Berkeley. Don't let the fact that it's in the Asian Ghetto fool ya. It's better quality and the prices reflect that quality. And it's probably the only place in the Asian ghetto that wont give you a bad shit the next day.  This place rocks.

worst bento box ever.....for both quality (bad sashimi) and quantity (small portion).

It was not even cheap; I can't believe that I gave tips....no service.

This place USED to be good. 

I liked their sushi roll, back in the days, when the sushi was decent and the rolls were well-made. However, the last time I went to visit, the rolls were a lot smaller and it tasted like those that came in the box. With the same amount of money, it'd be more well-spent getting 50 pieces from nude sushi or tako.

bento boxes are tasty and almost enough to feed two people (at a hefty $14 price tag). sashimi is fresh, thank goodness. maki rolls are big! - i have to psyche myself out before each bite. my favorite is the cherry blossom roll.
yaki udon's are pretty good. donburi's are lackluster.

the best place in southside for japanese food (beats tako and joshuya, not better than cu fusion), but be prepared to take a hit in your wallet.

2.5 stars? It's really not THAT bad...

Service: 3
Taste: 4
Quality: 3
Variety: 4
Price: $7-10
Recommend to a friend: Depends on what they're looking for...

Sushi House has been my friend since freshman year, although I definitely went a lot more when I lived in the dorms than I do now. The prices are pretty standard -- it's going to be pretty pricey because it is, in fact, sushi.

My friend always gets the Berkeley Special. It's chicken teriyaki, 4 Cali roll pieces, some gyoza (fried dumplings), cabbage salad, rice, and orange slices. I'd say it's a pretty good deal for 7 bucks. I either get the special or the Lambada roll. I used to get it so often that "lambada" is a recurring word that's thrown around when I'm with friends. It's a roll that incorporates some of my favorite things in sushi rolls: spicy tuna, salmon, avocado, and tobiko (yes, fish eggs). It's pretty delicious.

The quality isn't the BEST, but it's a lot better than Tako, imo. I'd rather pay a little more and get Sushi House than Tako... I haven't tried any sashimi here, and I'd probably say that it won't be the best place for it. They have no reason to invest in prime fish since few college kids will order it.

Otherwise, the people who run the place are nice and have been there for years (at least 4, since that's how long I've been in Berkeley). Keep in mind that there is a $10 minimum for credit card usage. But when I only have my card and am under by a dollar, I'll just grab a soda and swipe away.

Their rolls are amazing. I can't ever go in without ordering the Lion King roll, which is the best I've ever had. The sushi is pretty expensive but is pretty high quality. I feel bad to come here too often, because of the price. But when I went home for summer, I found myself missing this place. The seating is a little cramped but servable.

The Berkeley Student Special (~$7) is a decent deal. Nice if you just want a little bit of everything. Overall taste of everything isn't that great though. It has: 
-Chicken teriyaki: not that great, but will satisfy if you're craving some meat in your meal.
-Salad: The dressing is sweet if I recall correctly, but the salad leave are not that fresh
-Gyoza: Pretty small, decent when warm
-California roll: Tend to be skimpy/uneven on the avocado, but pretty good. Rolls are slightly sweet. 
-Rice: Pretty good

The tea is /delicious/

Most of the rolls are good:
-Island roll is excellent (fresh salmon with a thin slice of lemon, shrimp tempura, crab, cucumber, avocado)
-Super california roll! California roll with unagi on top :)

Usually I get the Student Special + Super california roll. It totals out to be pretty expensive ($14) for college food, especially when Gypsy's is nearby and you can get a huge Calzone for like $6 (and other places like Blondie's or Subway are just around the corner). This combo usually lasts me for lunch and dinner, and perhaps a little more the next day.

I'm not understanding the low rating... because for it being in the Asian Ghetto, I was pleasantly surprised by their sushi! It took me the longest time to order because I was really hungry so the sushi all looked sooo good- they have pictures of pretty much all their sushi taped on their window which really helps the choosing process. 

Friends and I ordered the Berkeley special, the Lion King, and some other sushi and I thought they were great! Please try the Lion King next time- its baked sushi so its soft and the sauce is nice and warm.. yum. 
 
The wait wasn't long (considering there was only one guy working there) and he brought them outside for us. And come on guys, this is the Asian Ghetto.. don't be rating it like a real sushi restaurant.

One of the worst places I've been to in Berkeley, and that's saying a lot. 

The prepared food was not fresh at all--the fried pot sticker was basically all skin a pinch of meat (AND it was stale). Also, I was supposed to get two, but the owner said that he ran out and was preparing a new one momentarily. I never got it.

Sushi-wise, it's pretty bad. I would rather go to Tako Sushi for the price of the low quality food they offer here.

Don't waste your money here.

I think I've been to this place once or twice.  Once because I was curious.  The second time because one of my friends suggested it.

I got a monkey roll or something of that sort, and perhaps the baked scallop roll once too.  Nothing too memorable.  There's free green tea.  But this place is overpriced for the Asian Ghetto.  

There are better sushi places if you venture out into the Rockridge area.

Oh yea, they aren't that nice, and there's like a $12 or $15 minimum for credit cards.  Lame.

I prefer Tako sushi to this place, and I don't think I'll ever eat at Tako sushi again.

This is more like a 2.5 stars.

I had their Berkeley special for $7.
Granted it's cheap, the quality doesn't even make it worth it.

The only thing tasty about it were the 4 small pieces of sushi I got with it. The potstickers (gyoza) were so deep-fried dry that I could definitely cook it better myself.

For $10 a roll, the sushi rolls are overpriced and quality is mediocre. However, with that being said, the Lion King Roll is probably the only rose in this sushi garden full of prickly thorns.

Why the one star? A few years ago I came here to buy a couple baked rolls to go. They quickly packed up my number, called my exact check, and sent me off after grabbing my receipt. After a long uphill walk back home to my apartment near the Clark Kerr dorm area, I sat down gleefully in front of the TV to relax. When I opened up the bag, I was quite surprised. Alas, there were not two rolls, but just one. I looked all everywhere inside the brown paper bag, which took me about one second, before I realized they had screwed up terribly.

Despite my efforts to retrieve my lost $10, I was never compensated. Without my receipt, I was up the creek without a paddle. Dear Sushi House, here are the other four stars. **** you.

Mexican cooks.. you know this place is not gonna be good. Sushi House specialty rolls are all bland and their spicy tuna is one of the worst I've ever had.. idk how you can mess up spicy tuna; its one of the easiest to make taste good, right?.. you don't have to worry about the fish quality as much as a normal tuna roll since you can always mask it with the spiciness.. instead we have tuna and jalepenoes?? idk... but it was the worse spicy tuna i'd ever had. They do have their berkeley special for $6.95.. but its not really worth the poor execution. 

Sushi House does have a trustworthy Negihama roll which keeps me coming back for my quick sushi fix and keeps me a happy camper.

The owner is a nice guy... noticed my motorcycle helmet and proceeded to give me his life story growing up and riding a motorcycle.  The whole time I was eating he told me about his accident and even cared to tell me "youre a handsome guy" there was this real handsome Asian actor and he had a motorcycle accident... he wasn't so handsome after that.  

The sushi was not as fresh, and the rolls tasted... tasteless, ok maybe not totally tasteless but I've had better at cheaper and crummy sushi places.  Some of the rice was hard in my rolls, but maybe they just gave me the tail end of it since I came late in the evening? Still no excuse.

WARNING: This place is capitalizing off of the Sushi House in Alameda. Their name used to be Berkeley Sushi House on Yelp, but obviously they've changed it in order to try and get their customers. The pictures are also NOT the same as the food you will get.

The food here is TERRIBLE. I've been to the Sushi House in Alameda many times and it's GREAT! This place is small, dirty, smells bad, and is run by one guy who is the cashier / chef / everything else. He obviously does not wash his hands between taking money and cooking the food. The customer service is non-existent.

The food is very badly made and sauce is smeared on the food to make it taste better. Amazingly enough, the sauce is ALSO BAD! It wouldn't be that bad if the average price of the food was cheap, however they have like 2 cheap items and the other items are way more expensive then the other restaurants in the "ghetto".

Finally, they use a outdoor garden water faucet / spigot for the plastic drinking water container... what else more do I need to say?

Oyako-don and a spicy tuna roll ran me $13.

After mistakenly leaving work to grab food without checking Yelp, I walked into Sushi House.  There were three things I noticed when I walked in: every wall was a different color, the couple standing next to me was not embarrassed to be macking in the awkwardly quiet shop, and M. C. Hammer's "Can't Touch This" was playing on a stereo above the run-down drink refrigerator in the corner.  If only I had listened to the prophet Hammer.

I'll kill the suspense right here: the food is bad.  Even for bad food it's bad.  The bad spicy tuna rolls across the street at Minami are actually better AND cheaper.  Well, at least you can't screw up oyako-don.  Oh wait, if you reheat the rice in a microwave (wtf?), make a runny scramble of eggs instead of frying them, and add an inordinate amount of lotus root for no reason, you can actually fuck up oyako-don something fierce.  My tummy is not pleased.

On the upside, the guy behind the counter was really nice and super quick about making the food.  I also appreciate that he started making everything when I asked for it, which is kinda necessary given what I ordered, but still encouraging.

It makes me feel almost bad for him to write such a negative review, but the fact remains that throwing out all of the food in the restaurant, hiring a line cook and finding a guy to hit the suppliers markets to get some good ingredients are all fully necessary.

Quite.
Over.
Rated.

I used to go here a lot with the old Chinese owners.. (back in 2005-2006...) but after the new owner took over the place, they jacked up the price while the quality/taste of the food went down. THis place is definitely the most expensive in the Asian Ghetto (when it is supposed to be ghetto... )
and their food isn't that good. If you are willing to walk a bit, I'd go to Joshuya's on Dwight/Telegraph or even better, CU Sushi on Center/Oxford
The cashier/owner guy is very rude and unpleasant as well... I really think he should mind his own business and not take it upon himself to lecture students who are their to just get a quick, cheap food.
Their service was bad, food took FOREVER to come, and then they are expensive too. WHen I asked if and when my food was coming after like 30 min of waiting, the cashier/owner guy took it up on himself to lecture me about proper manners in a restaurant... Maybe he forgot. His place was in Asian Ghetto. GHETTO. People expect their food out in 5-10 min. 15 max. (food ended up taking another 15 minutes to come out)

I would NEVER go back here again unless they brought back down the prices or/and do some major improvements to their food


Really, if I could give negative stars, this is one of the VERY few places I've ever been to in my life that SHOULD get negative stars

Some rolls here such as the Island roll are really great.  Quality and freshness of the fish are also a lot better than some other sushi restaurants, such as Tako Sushi.  However, like a previous poster said, it really feels strange paying a lot of money for sushi while all the nearby restaurants have meals for $5-10.

I've been here for its grand opening during my 2nd year at Cal and once a year thereafter to test out the quality of their sushi.  This place started out "ok" but gone downhill.

Reason being...
1) Yummy picture does not imply yummy taste. Don't be deceived!
2) Daily Special is a good deal for volume and variety, but NOT quality.
3) Typical fusion rolls are reasonably priced but overpriced in terms of quality.
4) Service/Hygiene..some of them don't wash their hands when handling money and food..wtf
5) Hard rice on CA rolls and am I really eating crab meat?.. First of all, it's really hard to mess up sushi rice; either the rice isn't fresh (meaning CA rolls were premade) or they just simply don't know how to cook rice.  Second, crab meat resembled those dried up prepackage CA rolls served by Cal Dining.
6) The Sushi Chef (I shouldn't even call him that) did not know much about the fish that he was cutting and preparing..wtf

I will not go again unless they make some MAJOR improvements

I totally got shocked today by a restaurant owner.  When I asked him a ginger, he graped it by his finger that he gave me a change just before I asked.  So so so gross!!  I think they should have a better service.

worst Scallop roll ever- seriously it was a mound of rice with minimal scallop inside. very dry. Allaround terrible. I didn't even finish my sushi and that says a lot considering how much I love sushi.

The last time I ate here was almost 3 years ago and it was worse than I remember it. I ordered a cherry blossom roll which did not meet my expectations. The picture of the cherry blossom roll on the menu was wrapped in tuna whereas the real thing had one small morsel of tuna on top. Talk about false advertising. The rice was kind of hard and the fish was not fresh. I felt ripped off having paid over $10 for the roll when it was not of good quality nor was it filling. I left feeling hungry and craving more food. I could have eaten a burrito from Chipotle and felt fine. 

Overall, I was disappointed. I do not recommend this place at all. This is probably one of the worst sushi places near campus. Even Tako Sushi is better. At least their prices are cheaper. 

For better sushi places near campus, I would suggest Anzu on Shattuck and Haste or CU Sushi on Center near Oxford.

I am a sushi lover at heart so this place is somewhat of an oasis for me in Berkeley. The rolls are quite affordable ($5 for smaller ones - $10 for delicious deep fried tempura rolls). My favorites are the Island and Webster (anything with tempura on it). 

3 stars since I think the quality is not as great as the original Sushi House in Alameda but what can you do?

This place is absolute crap. I guess I can't expect much from a cramped place in the Ghetto, but wow and yuck. First of all, do NOT be deceived by the pretty photographs of perfect-looking, mouth-watering sushi rolls plastered in the inside of the restaurant for you to get a "sense" of what to order. I ordered the Rainbow Roll, which is idiotic on my part because how could I expect this tiny place to top California rolls with any kind of fresh fish. A lot of places use imitation crab, but I have no idea what they used. It tasted really dry, and worse, the rice was just mush. My roll basically fell apart. The worst part was the fish, which tasted like it was thawed out for a long time. Gross. Even the tamago piece was tasteless.

Another time I ordered the spicy tuna rolls thinking they'd be the typical ones I imagined at other sushi places. Wrong. It's basically tuna and a little bit of Korean hot pepper paste added and wrapped. It was way too spicy for me because of that. I think they took it a little too literally...

I would rather go for Berkeley Bowl's packaged sushi rolls.

Are you a student? or a roaming passerby?? Are you checking out this so-called "Sushi House" on your iphone or blackberry or droid ?? And you wanna know is it worth it?? Then you better get this warning my asian food lova brotha from anotha nice nice homey motha...

STOP. Do not come here for sushi or rolls or whatever.. if you are Japanese.. you will throw up.. if you are asian.. you will say WTF motha.. if you are a white man.. you will say "my hottie hottie asian girlfriend cooks better than this.." and if you black.. i dont know what you will say..

seriously.. are these the same owners of the Sushi House over in Oakland??  Dont dare call this place Sushi House if you cant hang like the LEGENDARY sushi house over in oakland with 1K reviews..

why do people go here..??
Prices are super high for what they give you..
Rolls SukorZ.. Hella Small.. (not what she said..)
Rolls are bland and do not taste good at all..
Service is whatevers..

so go to Tako sushi man.. they know how to give you food that is properly priced for what you get.. nasty food for nasty cheap prices..

I can tell you what I got.. but why bother? i gave you the jist above.. dont come here unless Tako is closed and you are a desperate motha brotha..

Continuing on the I-have-a-narrow-world-view-because-I-am-a-college-student theme, I came here, to Sushi House. Why?

We were close by and my favorite relative felt like sushi, out of all the choices in this college town area. So Yelp found this the closest nearby. 

It's in that tiny food mall on Durant, just above Telegraph. It's sort of like a suburban shopping mall food court, but the urban version that is open with small eateries. All the businesses have changed hands multiple times since I was student.

Sushi House is a made-for-students type of place. Although there is a small sushi bar that seats maybe 5 people, nobody sits there to eat. 90% of the orders are to go. In fact, when you order, both the Chef (who appears Korean) and the new Latin cashier, both ask, "to go?" like they would prefer that. 

There are pictures on the wall, that's how you order. Then when it is ready, you get your own chopsticks, grab a napkin, and walk your food to where you're sitting. It is sort of like Korean Sushi meets Chipotle, but slower and not as clean. Reasonable, but not cheap. 

We had 1 order of California roll (standard 6 pieces)l, 1 Chirashi, 1 Arizona Tea bottle, and 1 canned orange soda. The cost?

$26!

Not exactly student budget saver prices. The Chirashi was just random little bits of fish thrown on rice. 

The sushi here is not good, and it is not really sushi. A lot of junked up jive-ass rolls,  which probably many students who don't know better, actually like and think is good sushi. They are confusing other Japanese dishes like Teriyaki Chicken with similarly dressed Sushi. A lot of sesame seeds, teriyaki sauce, secret thousand island sauce, etc, etc. Everything but good fish, good sushi rice, and good spirit to make them with pride. 

The Chirashi did come with a salad, and a bowl of miso soup, so it was enough food, but not good food. The donburi is cheap, only $6.95, but is served in smaller bowls than you would normally get. 

I don't blame the owner, he is trying to scratch out a living in a tough economy, with often a lot of skittish and cheap students as customers.
So he has dumbed down his offerings to match the main customer base, who is looking for quick, cheap food on the way to or from campus. 

And if Students here, even though they are bright and attending the #1 public university in the country, perhaps the world, think this is good sushi, well, they are still living in that college student bubble.

"Bushi House" as i like to call it for it's location, not anything else (you sickos!), is decent.  The place is tiny being located in the Asian ghetto, but has enough wall space to display it's menu with pictures at least 10 times over. Ordered three simple rolls, salad and miso soup, which amassed to over $20, which i thought was a bit on the high end for a place as such (nanayiro and manpuku seem slightly less), and the portions were on the small side. Although it's open 'till 1am this week b/c of finals, which is a definite plus, but not sure what the normal hours are.

I was visiting a friend in Berkeley and we were both craving sushi. We were looking for a specific place but we got a little lost so we just went to the Asian Ghetto.

Walked in and the place was empty, except for one other customer. Ordered the Anna Roll, $10. Meh, I thought that'd be OK since that's pretty standard for a special roll. The sushi was alright but definitely overpriced for its quality. Place was kinda run down, customer service was very hands-off.

I had really low expectations and went here just because I wanted to check it out and see for myself. I was pleasantly surprised. The Berkeley Special was reasonably priced, the flavors were all pretty good, and the service was solid. For a little food-courty place, they really do a nice job.

This place is a decent lunch spot. Conveniently located near UCB,  and definitely caters to the college crowd. 

Decent lunch special.

Will I go back? Probably not, but I'd recommend it if you want a cheap Japanese lunch.

3.5

I'm giving this place a 4 star because thats what it used to be back when I first started coming here. But in reality, its more like a 3-3.5 because this place is starting to drop off in quality. I guess you got to blame it on the popularity on of this place. It seems like everybody goes here now. The lines are insanely long, like Cheesecake factory status. A few years back, sushi here seemed really good, but the quality of everything seems to have gone down the drain. I mean, its still good, it'll still satisfy most people, but either things just got worse or my taste for sushi has gotten too sophisticated because I'm just not as impressed when I eat here. Bummer...

The gist...

High points: The sushi is okay. They have all the favorites including every roll that has to be topped with every piece of crap in the kitchen. Seriously, sometimes the rolls look like Yogurtland yogurt thats been smothered with every single topping in the house. 

Low points: Quality? Where is the love, Sushi House? Where is the love?

Sushi House : real sushi :: Lee's sandwiches : Vietnamese banh mi.

When you see Latino employee's cranking out the sushi in the back, that's when you realize that this is not authentic sushi made by trained chefs.

That's why I never buy any rolls because the price is the same/close to REAL sushi restaurants, ones where there are waiters serving you drinks instead of a dirty water dispenser tucked away in the corner.

If you want your money's worth, get the Berkeley special, which is basically a bento box on a dish (or plastic container for take-out) for $6.99! Or you could go down the street to Tako Sushi for $1.85 California Rolls.

For sushi found in the Berkeley Telegraph area this place is it. I'm not too sure if it's owned by the same people of Sushi House in Alameda. Because they basically stole the same menu, same rolls, ingredients, taste, and presentation. Ha, but I'm not complaining! I love those rolls. 

They have daily specials which I think is a steal for a meal that is around 7 bucks.

Service was a bit slow after taking the order. It shouldn't take too long to make rolls, but once you eat it you forget about the wait. The place is really small but it's Asian Ghetto (Durant Square) so you can't expect much.

Island roll, Samurai, Lion King, Bay scallop. The only thing that made me upset was that they put soy sauce in a styrofoam bowl for my to-go order like the ones that miso soup is served in. And they only filled it up quarter of the way. No wonder we're all going to die from global warming. Just get some soy sauce packets and then you can save the world! Coincidental Heroes implication? I think not.

--------
Update 3/10
I've been here a few more times since my last review. I heard through the grapevine that it's the same owner as Bear Ramen House. Today's service was friendly. We got nigiri complements from the chef. Could it have been because it was a group of girls? Or because we were Korean? Or maybe because he's just....yea I won't finish that thought. 

They don't serve soy sauce in styrofoam anymore for take out. I'm thinking that night when I did have take out it must have been a fluke or something.  

My friend put it this way. It's the best deal because it's Sushi House type rolls without having to tip and to drive.

I go here practically every day.  It really is one of the best sushi restaurants in Berkeley.  I am really confused about the location though.  It is kind of surreal spending $15-$30 on high quality sushi in the middle of the Asian ghetto, where a $7 or $8 meal is the norm.

The fish is extremely fresh and it is very well prepared.  I usually just get the nigiri dinner and it consistently is near perfection.  Their rolls are very good, and so are their donburis and gyoza.  It is hard to find really good sushi in Berkeley and sushi house truly is one of the best.

The only problem is that they can be a little slow which is unusual for the Asian ghetto, but that is just the nature of a high quality restaurant though.  If you want fast food, go to one of its cheapo neighbors.  I usually order to-go, then get some tapioca milk tea and finish it while they are making it.

The owner is super nice and she always gives me free stuff.  I take a lot of people here and she is really nice to them too.  It is really worth your while to become a regular here.  I love restaurants that actually pay attention to their customers and make an effort to get to know them.  If I could give this restaurant more than five stars, I would.
Ate here today and found the sushi really really good. Very fresh... Tempura udon is so-so but it did cure my hang over. =)

I don't think this place is all that bad.  Their rolls are actually pretty decent, perhaps a little overpriced.  The Bento box is actually a good deal for lunch, and it's pretty good.  It comes with salad, dumplings (these are really crispy and good), some california rolls, chicken teriyaki, and some rice.  I honestly like the food, but the three stars are for the extremely slow service.  I think this place tastes cleaner than Thai Basil, Steve's Korean BBQ, and Gypsy's.

So I came here about a week ago, and it was definitely my worst sushi house experience ever. 

We go there around 7:30, and the receptionist said that we would have to wait 30 minutes.  After about 45 minutes, we started asking her when we could be seated, and she kept telling us "5 more minutes" (this happened probably like 7-8 times).  In the end, we waited over an hour.  Not only did we not get seated in a timely manner, the receptionists were very impolite.  They didn't apologize or smile or anything while we were waiting and dying of hunger. When we finally sat down, my lion king roll's salmon was overcooked and dry. 

So, this trip to sushi house was very disappointing, bad service + bad food. Normally they're better but this last visit was just ridiculous.

If you're going to eat here, make sure you bring at least $11-20 per person if you want your belly filled well. Plus they have a $15 dollar minimum for credit cards, which sucks big time because most rolls are about $9, $4 for hand rolls. For that price range you obviously COULD eat at a nicer sit down restaurants with menus and waitresses that take your order, and the surrounding restaurants are way cheaper, but in terms of food quality... I don't think you're going to find more delicious or fresh food anywhere near the area. The sushi is absolutely positively amazing! It is straight up bomb with a cherry on top. The portions are pretty big for what is typically served in a sushi restaurant. If you're not sure what to order, try: Spicy scallop hand roll, Lion King (a california roll wrapped in salmon baked and glazed with a sweet rich house sauce)-pure orgasmic heaven!!, Island Roll, Webster Roll and Samurai roll, you can't go wrong. I only give 4 stars because I always leave this place with a small dent in my wallet

tip: the owner is Korean, if you're friendly and you speak to the cashier in Korean, you will probably get free miso soup.

Located in the Asian ghetto, so none of that romantic upscale feel. BUT it's yummy =] 
Lots of choices, including vegetarian rolls and bentos that I want to try, though I'm not a vegetarian. Reasonably priced, at about $6-10 a roll. I ordered a Vegetable Dragon Roll ($6), with deep fried eggplant and asparagus, and avocado. I asked them for cucumber instead of avocado and they asked me if I wanted tamago in there too! Wonderful =]

college cafeteria sushi.  i give them props for having an incredible selection in terms of rolls, but wow the rice was just either old or undercooked - you know, when its hard and chewy . . .

if you're in a need for sushi in berkeley, this fits the bill.  here for a cal game, had some gypsies, but wanted a sushi roll.  i've been a few times before, went inside, saw the pics on the wall, got hungrier and hungrier . . . ate a roll.  and felt very underwhelmed.  enough that i may go back, but i probably wont unless i just can't live without sushi before a game . . . it wasn't bad, it just wasn't certainly up to par.  on the plus side, it's cheap, so this is clearly an example of the adage your mom used to yell at you - "you get what you pay for"

I think I will call 2/3/2009 as the one of the crappiest culinary days of my life. It began at lunch with a crappy meal at Kai's in Oakland. Then a crappy pasta dish at Gypsy, then here at Sushi House. 

Ok, this place is in a mini-mall which caters to mostly UCB students. So college student should equal cheap/affordable, right? My problem with this place is that the prices are no different than you would find in a nicer established 'real' Japanese place, (ie not in a mini-mall and bigger than 300 ft). The owner was nice, contrary to what others have experienced.

I ordered 2 Makis. my tab was $10.87. Not cheap, the same price they charge pretty much at any Japanese restaurant.  Yes, it did take over 10 mins to get my rolls.

The worst part was the acutal food. The rice really did not seem like Sushi rice. If it was, it was a very light version, ie, almost tasted like plain white rice, perhaps it does dual duty for their entrees?

the portion of fish was small. My Negihama was almost just like a rice roll as I could not taste the hamachi. 

They also provide the cheapest Soy Sauce around, the stuff which is served in cheap Chinese take out. 

I guess my beef is that if you are in a student served cheapo mini-mall, make the food affordable to students, meaning, drop it down a notch on pricing vs place which my parents would eat at. if you are not going to do that, then provide the quality of food that one would expect from that pricing....it seems like Sushi House wants it both ways.

PS--on a side note, I did see some Tempura when I was there which really looked good, the batter with all the crispy texture on the outside...I may be forced to try it.

Ew. This place has HORRIBLE overpriced sushi. I'm disgusted. I will never go here again. You can get the exact same sushi rolls at Tako's sushi half a block away for cheaper and much better quality. If their quality is going to be so low, they may as well make their sushi cheaper than their competitor. Seriously, it boggles my mind.

I am confused about how to rate this place.  On the one hand, the guy who takes your order is horribly rude, the food takes forever (once I waited 30 minutes for my 2 rolls), it is often crowded and sometimes smells bad.  On the other hand, I've never had roll sushi like this in my life.  Well, maybe, but certainly not for the price.  The Water Polo, Hero, and Crunch Monkey are my favorites.  Get all 3 for under $25!

If you're looking for traditional sushi, this isn't the place.  Do they even have sashimi on the menu?  I didn't look.  You won't miss it with the rolls being as good as they are, but if that's what you're craving you won't find it here.

One more star because where else can you eat sushi and then go next door and get a fresh doughnut for dessert?
an unimaginitive and overpriced clone of your typical japanese restraunt. Quality is up to par though.

I like this place.. I don't see why people complain so much.. It's close to the campus, the rolls are a great size and the few times I've been here, I've had no issues.. I like the veggie roll and the lombada which is spicy with salmon.. Both are huge and it was only 16.00..it's nothing fancy- but it takes care of the sushi fix. I'm a fan.. :)

So the business model of having non-Asians running Asian restaurant continues at the Asian Ghetto which is quite effective and efficient for owners. Whether there is a lost in quality is debatable but I don't think the sushi here taste like anything near Sushi House. The hot food is pretty comparable but something about the sushi and sashimi is a tad off. Maybe it's not the chefs but the quality of fish? Maybe it's the bums and overfilled trash cans stinking up the flavor? Maybe the blend of smells from Italian, Mexican, Thai, Korean, Chinese food, and donuts is confusing the appetite? Regardless of the reason, the sushi is good but not spectacular like Sushi House. The Special is cheap but the rest of the menu has normal prices. Easy quick sushi fix for students is the only motivation to eat here.

So craving sushi
Unsure what to get
Sushi for under $10?
How come so cheap?
I got: California Delux ($4.95)

How come the rice is so hard?
Oh, asian ghetto-ness
U get what u pay for
Seriously only $4.95?
Eh... o.O

2 to 3 stars (maybe 2.5)... This place needs major improvement. It's tiny and cramped inside. Though the sushi is cheap here, it wasn't super fantastic in taste. Most rolls are around $5. I couldn't believe mine was only $4.95. I was expecting to pay $10! For six pieces, I was still hungry and wanting another roll... haha I couldn't believe how hard the rice was. I've never had such hard rice in my sushi. That was the most disappointing part. I guess if you are desperate for sushi and want something cheap (quality and price) then come here. But don't expect much.

There's never a line here. And that's because it's pretty gross.

But I found myself coming here on a Sunday because Tako Sushi was closed, and I was really craving some sushi. 

The sashimi wasn't as fresh as I would've liked, but they packed my Chirashi ($13.99) with a lot of it. I also ordered a California Deluxe for $4.95.

So my 1 star wasn't enough to show you I'm not a fan?  Actually, the star is for me because I returned.  Sadly.

I enjoy their Alameda counterpart, so I thought I'd give the one in the asian ghetto a chance.  Most Japanese restaurants can get away with $17 for a mouth watering plate of fresh sashimi, but not for this hole.  

What I ordered: Salmon sashimi dinner

What I got: Overpriced frozen salmon over shredded daikon.  Their menu says all dinners include rice and salad, right right?  I had to prod the old man to include salad, AND he forgot the rice.  Moron.

I broke my cardinal rule of returning to bad eateries when I went back for a second round of disappointment.  This time, the salmon was mushy,  and my dinner came with soup but still no rice.  And yes, I had to request salad again!  

How does the saying go?  First time, shame on you. Second time, harakiri me?  

Sushi from the ghetto?!  Think about it.  It's disgusting, and so is this place.

What can I say?

If you like rolls, you'll like it here. Sushi house is great for rolls, I would take my friends here for their quantity AND quality of rolls. But that's pretty much it. 

As for myself, I would go somewhere else for traditional sashimi or nigiri. 

It seems Korean run (I'd rather eat sushi from a trained Japanese chef) and the wait is terrible, close to, or probably even worse than Kirala in Berkeley. 

The place is huge though, so it is great for big groups, if you can get in. On the down side, it can get quite crowded and noisy, but not in a good way.

all rolls look the same
not that cheap for what you get
long wait, big pieces

top pick: island roll

Having been to many sushi restaurants, this place is actually not as bad as others make it seem. I always order the lion king here, and it's just as good as the Sushi House in Alameda, or Rays Sushi in Hayward. Maybe it's the setting of the place that puts people off, but honestly you can't expect amazing sushi in this area. This place definitely beats Tako Sushi on Telegraph, so why all the hate? If you want awesome amazing sushi go to gourmet ghetto, at Kirala, not Asian ghetto.

So my sushi style is this: I want to put as much in a roll as possible. Shrimp tempura, avocado, tuna, salmon, eel, cream cheese, scallions, tobiko, special sauces, EVERYTHING. I bet if you could put doughnuts and pizza in a roll, I would order it. So, when I think of sushi, I think of this place because I can get anything under the sun wrapped up in a roll. 

Now, I've noticed a lot of reviews have mentioned the Lion King roll. I agree that this roll is not very good, so I understand if that's one of the only things you've tried, you'd be disappointed. I think I've tried 1/2 of them, and my favorites are the anna, island, water polo, and caterpillar. You will not be disappointed if you order any of these. 

It's true that you can wait awhile for your orders, but this place is small, the rolls are complicated, and it gets busy, so that's totally normal. If there is a line to the door before you order, then obviously you're not going to get your food in 5 minutes. I think it is worth the wait, and certainly better than any other sushi in the area. 

I can't give it 5 stars because well, I've been to Japan and really there isn't much comparing. But 4 stars because it keeps me coming back!
completely awful. they try to hide the shitty quality of their fish by drowning the rolls in thick sauces. it gave me a terrible stomachache afterwards.

Out of all the places to eat in the "Asian Ghetto", I'm not sure exactly why I chose this one. When the cashier is Korean and the 2 chefs in the back are Hispanic, I should know sushi isn't really sushi anymore.

With that being said, I played it safe and ordered the Oyako Donburi & Cali Rolls. I figured it's extremely hard to mess up a Cali roll...but they still somehow managed. The crabmeat they used tasted like it was dipped in a bucket of honey and butter (that's seriously the best way I can describe it). There was barely any avocado and the rice was hard. Again I say, how do you mess up a Cali roll!?!!

The Oyako Donburi wasn't that great either. The sauce was extremely salty and again, hard rice. My friends ordered the Anna roll & Samurai roll which weren't half bad, except they were drenched in sauce. I had a difficult time deciding which roll on the menu would be tasty, but i seemed like they all carried the same ingredients, so it came down to a matter of how much I wanted to pay for my meal. What a waste of $10 for everything.

Don't mistaken this place for the Sushi House in Alameda. No relation whatsoever!!

Living on Durant, it's hard to find a decent sushi place without having to walk further out of my way. I live close by to the Sushi House but was always wary. C'mon - we're talking Asian Ghetto. After reading the Yelp reviews, I decided to get over my fear of being food poisoned and tried this place out. 

I don't know if I was taking crazy pills or if the people who wrote glowing reviews were, but I had some of THE worst sushi in my life, but that's just the half of it. It took me FORTY MINUTES TO GET MY LION KING ROLL (baked salmon). I came around 3:00 pm, mind you, and it was definitely not packed at all. I'm a patient enough person, but after 20 minutes, I asked if I was getting my roll anytime soon. The cashier then tells me they burnt my roll and were making me another one. 20 minutes later, I finally get the roll. I don't even know why I didn't demand my money back. Perhaps it was the fact that I was desperate for sushi and my stomach was eating itself. 

I got back to my apartment and was ready to dig in when I saw the most disgusting sight in my life. The roll was wrapped almost 3 times over with just rice alone, a little bit of imitation crab (there was so little of it, I don't know if I just imagined it being there) and the smallest pieces of salmon on top. The rice was overpoweringly sweet and after two bites, I chucked it. Rude service, bad food, and overpriced. On the plus side, I didn't get food poisoned.

Cafe 3 (or Cafe Tre, as I like to say) used to be the bomb diggity when I first lived in the dorms but sadly, quality has dramatically decreased over the years.

When I went in today with my stomach literally rumbling, I expected palatable food. But apparently that was too high an expectation.

I got the omelette from the omelette bar with everything except cheese. It was basically ham, onions, and bell peppers when it used to include spinach and mushrooms. Anyway, it didn't taste like anything and made me wonder if it was made from real eggs or from the generic liquid mix. 

There was nothing else appetizing so I followed my flavorless omelette with a salad and grapefruit. 

You can't muck up fresh ingredients but when the best part of a meal is baby carrots + peanut butter, especially at an all-you-can-eat establishment, there's a problem. 

Sure, the glitzy decor is fancy and all, but I'd rather have better food than wall panels that change colors ever 2 seconds.

ewwww, just gross and disgusting and bad.
 the food lacks flavor, and is monotonous, and sickening. most of the vegetarian or vegan options are terrible and gross and over-salted and lack any other flavor. the "celebration roast" is especially terrible. 
I guess they should get some points for having an all organic salad bar and organic milk, but the salad bar doesn't have much variety and the dressings are bad. the desserts are okay, sometimes, they're really the only thing i can eat with getting totally sick.

ewww, i can't even think about this place anymore.
i'm gonna go throw up now

They have pretty good breakfast, which I usually came here for.  They mostly have Asian food but the variety isn't very great however.  Really hit or miss.  Also, limited hours and not open everyday of the week for dinner.  At least that was the deal when I last went a couple years back.

Quality only a notch above crossroads in the Asian food section, the rest is arguably worse. Its smaller selection is also a downside. Only good to go to if you a) live in unit 3, b)don't like the crossroads menu one day, c)crossroads is too crowded, d)you want to watch ESPN while you eat. Actually the decor is the best part about Cafe 3, with several different festive sections to liven things up, and a lot of TVs to use.

Café Tré, as my floor mates used to call it, seemed better than Crossroads at first.  I'm talking decor, food, flat screen tv, etc.  But after a whole semester eating lunch there with my friends because it was convenient, I was convinced that Crossroads was actually better than Café Tré.  When it comes to lunch, Crossroads isn't actually that bad.  But for Café Tré, there's always brunch.  Which means that their main entree is usually something involving eggs or macaroni and cheese.  You get sick of it very quickly and I normally mix in salad just so I don't feel sick afterward.  Also, if you don't grab a piece of fruit or dessert before 7pm, don't even think about it because there won't be any left except for some gritty red Washington apples.  Waffles and omelets are the only plus.  BTW, the omelet bar did not arrive till spring 2009.  Finally, the design of the tray kitchen area is very poor.  I've been to Crossroads more times than Café Tré, but I've witnessed many tray accidents at the latter.  In fact, I've done it three times there and I'm not that clumsy!  There you have it, Café Tré.

This DC is well liked by students, but the sushi is really abysmal and the place feels very cramped.  When I'm here, I feel like I'm in the snack bar of a hovercraft that's about to cross the Channel.  There are relatively few food stations -- limited choice and long lines.  I'd much rather go to Foothill, Crossroads or Clark Kerr.

The reopening of Cafe 3 was something needed for all the people in Unit 3.  The inside is amazing with a sleek look and all new everything. There are some noticeably great things about Cafe 3.  Omelet bar is the best creation ever.  The make your own waffle is also amazing.  Pizza is also not bad.  The big screen is nice for not having to talk to people.  Now the bad... terrible sushi and blue plate 80 percent of the time.  Salad is okay with some ingredients missing from time to time.  Pho station is just kind of weird tasting.  Also non and low fat milk seems to run out every time I go there, which is characteristic of all the dining halls though.  Not bad... just not good.

Ok, I know everyone must think I'm INSANE for giving Cafe 3 FOUR stars......but here's the reason why.......READ ON!! 

Food: 
BUFFET style so it's different every night but here's what I had tonight--
-Chicken enchilada casserole: The chicken was soo good and super tender!! The baked cheese on top was crispy and chewy! Just enough sauce in between all the layers! It was super YUMMY! I had like 5 helpings! I would have had more, but for some reason it wasn't self serve and someone had to keep serving me and I was afraid she would recognize me cause I kept going back for more, so I stopped getting more helpings......

-Penne Pasta  with Garbanzo Bean curry sauce thing?: I'm kinda biased because I LOVE penne pasta so that was automatically like YUM! The Garbanzo Bean curry sauce thing was pretty good. I like saucy things so that was just like a big sloppy goo of goodness! 

-Salad Bar: Had a wide variety of veggies and so many toppings! It was almost like a mini souplantation! Everything seemed very fresh and healthy and tasted really good too! I was especially into the onion, cilantro, cherry tomato, corn salsa that you can top your salad off with! That was super TASTY! And then there's a variety of dressings like "tomato basil" that were unique and added an extra kick of flavor to your salad! Not to mention there were some sunflower seeds and pumpkin seeds that you can also add to make it extra special! Totally digging it!

-Soups: 
--Spicy Lemon Thai soup and Italian Wedding Soup: Neither of which were very good...have to say, they were down right sub par from what I was expecting. Looks can be so deceiving.....that's all I've got to say....

-seaweed salad: So this is normally pretty expensive, so when I saw that they had this, I went crazy and downed this stuff like there's no tomorrow..only to find that it  was a bit too salty. I bet they did that on purpose so there's only a limited amount of this stuff anyone can eat before they go into a hypertensive shock from an over consumption of salt!! 

-shrimp fried rice: honestly, sounds better than it tastes. Rice too soggy, shrimp not fresh/big enough. Relatively bland tasting, not all it's cracked up to be. 

-drinks: wide selection, but i'm not a big drink person. The only thing that caught my eye was organic soymilk and lemonade...everything else sounded like sugar + water to me (aka: sodas and juices). 

-desserts: brownies, cakes and froyo, oh my! I LOVE brownies! YUMMY! The blueberry cake looked good, didn't try it. The FROYO (only vanilla and chocolate flavor) was ok for being all you can eat froyo! There's only like three toppings: wannabe granola (which I really think was some variation of Kashi cereal), crumbled oreos (my favorite!!!), and sugared up cherries. I honestly don't like vanilla and chocolate flavored "soft served ice cream" froyo that much but since it was all you can eat......it made up for it!

Overall: So after having been to crossroads and now eating here, I really feel like Cafe 3 is just a toned down, miniaturized version of Crossroads. Obviously, not as much variety but who said a ton of variety is a good thing? I mean, when you go to Berkeley Bowl and you look at the overwhelming mounds of 30+ varieties of apples they've got in stalk don't you just drop your jaw and think: "dude, where do I start???" I don't know about you, but when there's a surplus of variety, I always end up making the wrong decision because my brain is so overwhelmed I don't even know what to look at or what to choose. So think of Crossroads as "overwhelming" and Cafe 3 as "manageable options". Don't get me wrong, variety is a good thing, but not in SURPLUS. 
Due to less variety, Cafe 3 has less traffic so it's a more intimate dining environment. It gives you a more cozy feel. Nice place to sit down with a pal and just chat all night and keep indulging in their endless supply of food! That's exactly what I did! Ok, enough about food...let's move on.....

Ambiance:
So I really wanted to give a positive review on the ambiance here because I felt like half of my positive dining experience there tonight was due to the ambiance!! I really liked how it was decorated. Some areas has cute little booths for two people (which is what I sat in), some stools with high tables (to make it look like a dinner), and some cushioned benches. There were TV's and quirky/modern designs on the furniture. It was really unique and unlike any dining hall I've been to or seen. At crossroads I really felt like it was so mainstream and high efficiency factory like dining hall. But Cafe 3 really has a homey feeling to it and it's quieter so you can carry on a conversation without shouting! :)

Price: ~$8 for and endless supply of food.....how do I get in on this?!?!?! I honestly feel like I ate $50+ of food and paying only $8 for it made me realize: "So this is why our school is on a budget crisis and they are spiking our tuition! I get it now!" 

Service: you bus yoursel

By the end of two years of mealpoint based subsistence, Cafe 3 was one of the only dining halls I would go to. They may not have as many stations as Crossroads does, but it doesn't really matter when half the stations at Crossroads are inedible. Its menu has an Asian slant (oh god that was not supposed to be a racist pun) on most days of the week and it tastes reasonably good. The sushi is not terribly great nor terribly awful -- what are you expecting anyway? It's an ~$8 buffet. 

Caveats:
-If you like the dessert they are serving that day, get it immediately. Don't wait until the end of your meal because it will not be there. 
-If you're in any way tall or even normal-sized, snag one of the few tables that have real chairs. Seriously, some of those low couches and chairs and tables remind me of the children's section at Ikea.

For the quality of their baked goods, I feel like they're a bit pricey. The staff didn't really seem to know what they were doing. The barista was slow and a bit clumsy. The only thing good about this place is that it's open late for a nighttime snack that isn't too overbearing or greasy.

I might be a little spoiled, because I've spent enough time in Taiwan to know what actual pastries should taste like. I AM glad this kind of place exists; given how many Asians are at Berkeley, I'm surprised it's taken so long. But when I look at the pastries, none of them actually look appetizing to me. They're lesser versions of what you'd normally get at a bakery and at a higher than average price. The only things I would trust getting are the Sogo goods, because Sogo is DECENT. There's not much variety, and what they do have isn't all that appealing.

Cute little store!  The "buy four get one free" macaron deal (at Ucafe, macarons are effectively $1 each) is fun, since at other bakeries macarons are over $1.75 each. A good introduction to the macaron trend!

My friends and I got the lime, mango, coconut-rum, blueberry, and strawberry macarons. The buttercream filling was the best part, and the blueberry and coconut-rum fillings were the best out of those five.

* disclaimer: didn't try their baked goods yet - only macarons*

So, I should have known to not get macarons from an Asian bakery. 
I looked at the six or seven flavours - each flavour unmistakably uneven and lumpy (first sign to stray away from macarons), however, I decided to give them a try. 
After a "buy four get one free" promotion (5 macarons for $5) I ended up with coconut rum, passionfruit poppy, strawberry, vanilla and mango. 
Upon taking my first bite of the cheerfully colorful coconut rum macaroon (lavender with blue specks and a lime green buttercream filling) I knew that I was in for a less than kind taste/texture combo. 

Let's break down each flavour ( I only tried a 1/4 or less of the macaron)
1) Coconut Rum
Flavor: unbearably sweet with a slight hint of coconut and a weird aftertaste.
Texture: crumbly, dry, and semi-stale.
Overall: not impressed, decided to move on to other flavors.
2) Passionfruit and Poppy 
Flavor: Interesting, the buttercream was by far the highlight of this macaron with a fun and tart passionfruit aroma. 
Texture: crumbly, possibly due to being over refrigerated and dried out. 
Overall: The execution of this one was horrible, the buttercream was globbed in the middle resembling a spere rather than an even "patty". In hindsight, this was probably the best one (seems very sad now). 
3)Strawberry
Flavor: artificial food color and artificial flavouring anyone?
Overall: GROSS
4) Vanilla
Flavor: decent vanilla taste.
Texture: brittle, and almost "sand-like".
Overall: better flavor of the bunch, crappy execution.
5) Mango 
Flavor: weird sensation, HORRID aftertaste. It's been 10 minutes since i took a bite of one and rinsed my mouth out yet I can still taste the bitter, semi-salty, aftertaste. I'm imagining this is what decomposing mango would taste like if someone tried to preserve it in formaldehyde for a dissection. 
Overall: gross, gross, gross. I hate being critical of the places I review but this was not just inedible, it was borderline poisonous. 

OVERALL: I'm really disappointed in this experience. I'll probably return to UCafe to try one of their asian buns but definitely will not get their macarons ever again. Whoever doesn't believe me I still have 3/4 of each macaron sitting on my table awaiting to meet my garbage bin.

Good to have at least one Asian bakery near campus. But this one is just ok. The storefront is cute. The display of food is tidy and accessible (so instead of troubling someone to get you a loaf behind him or her, you can actually look closely at the goodies and decide what you want.) But the service was just sad. The girl did not pay attention to what I said (and she didn't seem to be paying attention to anything else.) I requested the red velvet mini pound cake but got a chocolate one. And before I asked to separate the buns into two paper bags, she tried to violently squeeze in four naked buns of different flavors and the pound cake in a tiny paper bag! Ugh! Who wants a deformed savory bun (the hot dog and green onion one) with the smell of taro or red bean? She just didn't think!!

Not bad! UCafe is a cute little Asian bakery near campus. They have a great selection of Sogo bread, which I basically grew up on. Mmmm coconut custard bread! UCafe brings me a little taste of home whenever I miss the abundance of Asian goodies in Cupertino. Their macarons are decent, but I think the cream filling is a bit heavy. Disclaimer: I always compare macarons to the ones from La Duree, so perhaps it is difficult for any bakery to match that. They have a pretty good selection of macaron flavors, from lime to coconut rum. I am excited to try their freshly baked buns and pastries too! 

I tried their milk tea once, too. I don't have too much to say about that, so it was okay.

In terms of ambience, UCafe is really cute. I love walking around and staring at all the baked goods!

I have tried:
- Hot dog and green onion bun (3.5/5)
- Pineapple and porksung bread (4/5)
- A few other sweet buns (idk I eat at Asian bakeries often so I don't recall the exact ones) (4/5)

Pros:
- Good, convenient location
- Open late! 
- Decent variety
- Also serves Asian drinks, sandwiches and other deserts like macarons (the macarons aren't as good as they should be)
- Always has samples out on the counter
- Super cute interior :)

Cons:
- Doesn't accept credit cards (since 1 week ago, not sure about now)
- I wish they opened early in the morning though because I want buns for breakfast! They typically don't open until 11AM or later.
- Pricyyyy (compared to other Asian bakeries)
- One table w/ 2 seats to constitute as the seating area

I'm really curious to see what the Sheng Kee bakery on Telegraph will bring to Berkeley.

Bottom line: If you're craving Asian pastries and don't have time to hit up 99 Ranch or Chinatown, then stop by here. Otherwise, I wouldn't bother wasting my money here by coming too often. A bun here and a bun there really starts to add up!

The atmosphere is very nice and the workers there are extremely kind and welcoming.  The food is fairly reasonable considering that it's located in a college town and extremely close to campus.  I wouldn't expect the prices to be as cheap as Chinatown just like many other places located a block away from Berkeley.  It's a nice place to get some sweets if you're craving any.

For Berkeley, this place is decent (although that may be subject to change when Sheng-Kee Bakery opens up on Telegraph).

By Bay Area standards, this place pales in comparison to many others. If you're willing to take the trip to Oakland or SF Chinatown then I'd recommend it if you're seeking more authentic Asian bakeries.

That's not to say that this place is terrible for what it offers, in fact they have a decent selection that cycles frequently from the many times that I have stopped by. I've only gotten a few things from here (mocha sponge cake and pineapple bun with red bean) and they've been alright. I've also picked up bahn mi from here for a very cheap $3.25 for a whole sandwich, which tastes good for its price but you can only get one kind.

I've also been given a cake from here (tiramisu) which was pretty good but unfortunately the cakes are pretty small for the price that they are charging (between $16-25 from what I've seen lately).

The service is also a bit slow but on the plus side they are open pretty late (2AM over the weekend) so if you need something cheap then I'd recommend it.

Ucafe is a pretty small space devoted almost entirely to displaying baked, wrapped chinese buns, cookies, macaroons. (ala sogo, sheng kee, et al). store is really lite up, this creates an happy buying environment, i presume.

behind the counter are other drink/food options:
-milk tea
-slushies
-smoothies
-banh mi
-iced/hot coffee

drink: coffee: peerless, 1.50
-several blends offered, was just poured one, 
-smooth brew, no harshnessk,
eats:  banh mi sandwich (1.95)either 1/2 or 1/3, not sure
-premade, referigerated, meat combo with veggie.
-tasted ok.
-good for eskimos

crumbs:
-service quick,
-day old pastries available, @.95
-no seating at all

Nice display and decoration of the place. However, they need to work on their baking skills. I tried the almond twist and the pumpkin bread loaf. The almond twist was very hard and it was no freshly baked. The pumpkin bread did not taste like pumpkin at all. I guess once you tried a good chinese bakery such as Shengkee in Richmond, you have a much finer taste of how fresh tasty baked goods are and the things in UCafe are not. It looks good but it ain't good.

i tried the mini green tea red bean pound cake, which was obviously not made on premises (pre-packed in plastic) and the Portuguese egg tart. both were pretty good, but definitely not anywhere close to chinatown prices. i do like that they have trays/tongs that you can use to pick things out.

YESSSSSSS. FINALLY SOME NICE NEW FOOD PLACES TO LIVEN UP TELEGRAPH AREA. 

UCafe is a nice asian-style bakery (think 85C in socal) with colorful interior, tongs for picking up bread, and trays for piling on the baked goods. 

Egg bread tastes like regular white bread, but fluffier and pretty yummy.  I thought it was a little on the pricy side, with a half loaf going for $3.95
Some of the other choices they have include thick toast, taro, redbean, green tea, hot dog, egg tarts, etc. NOT BAD!
Today was their opening day so there was still some setting up going on , but it looks like it'll be a nice place to purchase bread and such. 

In addition to the baked goods and desserts, they also have a lot of colorful macarons on display. Flavors: passion fruit, salted caramel, earl grey... aahhh drool drool. 

Saw some nice tea lattes and drinks on the menu ; will definitely give those a try soon (:

THEY HAVE BIRTHDAY CAKES!

Before UCafe popped up there was nowhere within walking distance of UC Berkeley where you could get a birthday cake for a surprise party or just cause you're craving cake. The closest would be Whole Foods on Telegraph or Safeway on College, and it's always a burden having to go so far to get the cake. 

But no more! I got an 8" mango cake for $24.95 (no tax!) and it wasn't too shabby. There were layers of mango (jelly?) and cake so it was more than your average fruit cake. Definitely a bit more expensive than usual birthday cakes - Whole Foods has amazing cakes for around $20 - but you pay for the convenience.

There definitely aren't many Asian bakeries around Berkeley (closest is probably Oakland Chinatown), so it's nice that some are finally beginning to open around campus! The bright, pink and green interior is really cute and inviting, plus the circular paper lampshades hanging from the ceiling add a stylish touch. They have a selection of pastries, buns, and loaves of bread from Sogo Bakery that are self-serve and also have cakes and macarons that you can order. One thing I noticed is that the macarons looked a little sloppily made and uneven, but maybe they will improve on that over time when they become more established. The frosting on the cupcakes also looked too rainbow colored, so it didn't seem too appealing to me. Most of the cakes, however, looked promising.

What I ordered:
- Mini Tiramisu Cake ($4): http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ucafe-berkeley?select=i8IHUKqEA3QFBm4hkkVRnQ#O6i_QzsVcJ-NnOxFLSoV4g

The cake looks pretty fancy with chocolate shavings and a strawberry on top, but I was sad when I opened the box and found that the strawberry had fallen off in transit :( It was pretty yummy and moist, but nothing extraordinarily special about it. Good choice though and I might come back and try something else another time!

TIPS: No photography allowed! They also have individually packed $0.95 day-old pastries, but I'm not sure how they taste..

I had my reservations, but gave this place a try. It's kind of nice to have an Asian bakery around. It's something I missed and there isn't anything close to it around these parts. They have a wide selection of buns, some on the smaller side and most of a usual size. The coconut cream bun was soft and perfect, but gets stale quickly so eat it immediately after purchase.
