There are also hot dog and green onion buns, which is a favorite of mine. There's also a tuna bun that I've never had before, but liked. They also have minced meat puff pastry pies, which I like. They also have those cake rolls. I bet they'll also have lots of people buying their full sized cakes for birthday occasions. There are only a few, but they look presentable and are a decent price if you live nearby and don't want to make the trek elsewhere. They have smaller cakes and some cake slices too at reasonable prices of $2 to $4. I was also surprised to find that they have macarons. They're $1.25. They're a reasonable size, but light and hollow. I'm not sure what the drinks are like here, but they serve Peerless Coffee. Also, staff needs to be more careful when handling the goods. One of my buns was dropped onto the counter when being rung up, but I took it anyway because it would be a shame for it to be thrown away.

I'm not sure how well this place will do once Sheng Kee opens up on Telegraph.

Seriously unimpressed by this place.

Coming back from Oakland Chinatown, their Chinese buns seem pricey (~$1.50/bun? vs like 60 cents) in comparison. Plus some of them just look odd; I mean, their croissants are seriously flat. However, I gave in and bought a few today, and now I'm convinced I will not be back. 

Their hot dog & green onion bun was a little too salty for my taste. Overall, it was alright, but their ham & corn bun was realllllllllyyyyy gross. I hate wasting food, but I ended up throwing away more than half of it, since I couldn't bring myself to eat it. The filling is this weird ham, corn & sour cream(?) mixture. It just tasted like dairy, and a lot of the corn kernels were dry. 

I also tried their mini tiramisu cake, which is so pretty looking! However, it's pretty standard, and even though it's small, I'd recommend splitting it with a friend.

The people here are so nice. But the food.... Nope.

Well, it's ABOUT time!

With its never-ending abundance of Thai, Indian, and various ethnic foods, Berkeley has always lacked an asian bakery. Where is the happiness when your closest sweet, fluffy bun is all the way in Richmond?! But never fear, my dears! UCafe is here!

Let's start by being superficial. UCafe has some of the cutest interior decor I've seen. The bright colors and simple, cheerful vibe remind me of Yogurtland. The perfect place for a delicious pick-me-up!

So far, I've tried the cream cheese bun, the coconut cream bun, red bean toast, and hot dog bun (?). Out of the first three, my favorite is the red bean toast, because it's really the sweetest. Unlike typical Asian bakeries, in which the bun itself is sweet, UCafe's buns rely more upon the sweet toppics & fillings. That being said, the hot dog bun was cooked to savory perfection!

While I'd love to give UCafe a 4, I'm going to have to be satisfied with a 3. Cute decor and great job of filling a long-empty niche, BUT the buns aren't up to my standards just yet and they're also on the price-y end! Hoping that Sheng Kee Bakery (whenever that opens) will finally be able to fill in for my bun cravings but until then, UCafe, here I come!

This small cafe new to the UC Berkeley area is definitely unique to the area. This place is like  a small Asian bakery which doesn't start showing up until you hit the Oakland area. I think it was a good idea that UCafe decided to open up now before the Fall semester starts to get more students to go. There is going to be a new Sheng Kee Bakery on Telegraph really soon so UCafe is going to have a hell of a competition to combat.

UCafe has all kinds of different pastries like Russian bread, Japanese milk bread, Portuguese egg tart, and even pineapple bun! Each pastry runs from $2-$4 and they have loaves of special breads for about $5-$6. The prices are pretty good and walking around the bakery you find yourself spending a lot more than you expected. Everything just looks so good in the display!

Raisin Custard Bread: This is a good choice for any bread lovers. The bread is slightly sweet which is a good choice for someone who doesn't have that large of a sweet tooth.
Cream Cheese Roll: This roll was pretty good. Definitely the best roll for any cream cheese lovers out there. There is a good chunk of sweet cream cheese in the center of the roll.

No reports of "the runs" from our group so far (see Pookieiam k.'s review), so no complaints.  I had the red curry chicken which was tasty, but a little runny...I guess that qualifies this yelp as a report on the "runs".  Hopefully just the curry stays runny.

A good balance of tomatoes, peppers, and chicken...with a little iceberg lettuce salad.  All for under $8.00 with complimentary hot thai tea.  Service was good and quick.
Mediocre Thai food.  Nothing special to report here.
I used to think this place was great, acomodating of groups and very reasonably priced. However, I've gotten the runs the last two times I went, so no more.

This place is a high 3 stars during lunch, simply because the eggplant tofu is so quick and always quite tasty.  There was a time when I would have given this place four stars... I used to order the crispy fish special for dinner and just go crazy trying to eat this 16 inch wide platter of fried fish, but at the end of the day I decided it wasn't actually that good.  

Really, though, if you're in a hurry and want eggplant, this is a great place.
Lunch special: blah!

A source for Thai convenient to the north side of campus.  Two stars because I never find myself going here unless someone else suggests it first.  There are many better Thai restaurants in Berkeley.  (I hope this is a fair assessment, as I've only tried their lunch combos, not had anything special made to order.)

I only had the lunch combo once, and it is NOT the greatest. Yes I'm cheap so I tried it, there. BUT I would only get the pad thai or pad see ew since you can't go wrong! A thai tea and beef pad see ew for $7 is definately not bad. However, get here before lines show up since the place seats like 15!

Every time I eat here I have a different opinion about this place. Most of the people that will serve you here are very friendly, but some of them seem completely unable to do their job. You can order something precooked and be out of there in no time. Or you can order the duck which always comes out great. Some of their precooked items are actually fairly decent too. The weirdest thing here is that if you take the precooked pad-thai, you'll get exactly one shrimp. One.

This place is pretty small and easy to miss, but it's portions are enough to be shared with one other person. I had korean shaved ice, which was full of all kinds of fruits like bananas, strawberries, pineapples, etc. It's really nice on a warm/hot day. Not only does it look colorful and appealing to the eye, but it tastes good too! They used to talk about eating 5 servings of fruits and veggies a day, but with this, you probably get 5 different fruits in one bowl, so you'll have plenty of good nutrients in your body!

I can't speak for the rest of the menu, but their bulgogi sandwiches get 5 stars from me!  It is also nice that for Cal students, Airbears is accessible here, and many of the tables are next to outlets if you need to plug in :)
This place is all about the bulgogi beef sandwich.  It's good, reasonably priced, and very accessible.
I've eaten everywhere there is to eat in Berkeley, but the bulgogi sandwiches from Espresso Experience are what I miss the most.

Really cute place to eat! I had never known about it before. I got the bulgogi sandwich - it was really delicious but I'm not sure if it was worth the money? I think this is one of the only places that's super close to campus that has REALLY GOOD shaved ice :)

Took a break between paper writing to get some lunch with my roommate.

Atmosphere: There are a good number of seats. When I walk by on the way to class it's always busy around lunch time, but I went today for lunch around12pm and it was nearly empty.

Food: Bulgogi sandwich is pretty yummy! The meat is well-flavored, and the bread has just the right amount of toastyness (toastiness?) to it. It's about $6, and the portion is pretty accurate for the price (it's pretty filling). I remember having it about two years ago and not thinking it was that great, but when I had it today I enjoyed it.

I ordered a Green Tea Latte with soy as well, and I couldn't really taste the green tea, which was a bummer. That and my sandwich cost around $9ish.

Service: The lady at the counter is super nice and friendly.

I'll probably go again to try their other sandwiches - they have a lot to choose from!
come here for the shaved ice, bulgogi (SO GOOD) sandwich, and spicy chicken sandwich...you won't regret it!

I use to come here when I was an undergrad living in the studios above yogurt park. Great place to study, electrical outlets present, within range of airbears, and the food they serve here is pretty good.

I loved getting the spicy chicken sandwhich. It was made fresh and had a nice vinegar taste to it (so it's really more like mild vinegar chicken but whateva its good!). The shaved ice here is also incredible. It's nicely arranged when it comes to you, and you don't feel too guilty eating it - afterall it's just water, fruit, and some sugar syrup. Well actually it does have condensed milk in it, but it's probably not as bad as an ice cream...I think...well regardless its good! 

I love the location as well since its right across from campus. I will say that it would get 3 stars if you're not a berkeley student tho since it doesn't have its own wifi and just assumes their customers will use airbears instead. This makes studying here pointless if you're not a student. However, check it out if you're still a student.

I LOVE their Bulgogi sandwiches. I always try to finagle a trip out to Berkeley when I need my fix. The sandwiches are always toasted just right and always hit the spot. They've remodeled in the last year or so, so it's even more cozy.

Side note that the owner admitted the "Teriyaki Sub Sandwich" and "Bulgogi Sandwich" are actually the same since some people didn't know what "bulgogi" was. Weirdness. You'd think of anyplace, people in Berkeley would know the difference. Oh well. Still a good sandwich!

Despite the name of the place, I do not come here for coffee (which I personally do not think is that great). The food is great. Again, Berkeley lacks on good korean food but their bulgogi sandwiches are the best!
turkey sandwich is alright, nothing special. they charge for debit use and do not accept c/c. friendly staff.

I love this place because it never gets too crowded and you can actually study in there and catch up with friends! It's also owned by a really kind Korean family (I'm pretty sure they love Jesus, which I also love).

+ Bulgogi sandwich - yes it really is good. If you're looking for quantity over quality though, just go to Subway or something because this is definitely on the pricier side for a sandwich (and a poor college student). Definitely try at least once.

+ Spicy Tuna sandwich - okay I must be the only person who gets this more frequently than the bulgogi sandwich but I just love it! They really lather on the tuna but it's not the mayo-ey type of tuna--it's more spicy than mayo-ey.

+ Bulgogi salad - don't let the word salad deceive you because it's literally just a bed of rice with romaine lettuce and bulgogi and some yummy spicy sweet sauce. t's more of a rice bowl than salad. I split it with a friend -- huge portions! It's no culinary breakthrough but I really like it! 

+ Pat bing soo - let's just say that socal does it WAY better. It's the only place in Berkeley that has it though but it's really disappointing if you've been to Socal Korean shaved ice places :( I feel like it only had mochi, fruit, ice and ice cream....oh well.

Bottom line: I like coming to this place to chill and eat. Never tried to study in here but it seems very doable! Also never tried their drinks, but do check this place out!

I got the spicy Korean rice cakes here...it was...alright.  I've definitely had better and more authentic Korean rice cake. I was slightly disappointed! 

Not too sure how the other food is, but I heard the bulgogi sandwiches aren't too shabby!

I came here for lunch with a friend. I ordered the bulgogi sandwich, about which I'd heard so much. It was okay. A good portion for the price, but the bread got soggy (from what?) and I could see white chunks of fat on the meat which made me a little eh. I think the sandwich could benefit from more solid vegetables. It was nice that they toasted the bread though.

My friend got the dukbokki, which was very spicy (good) but overpoweringly sweet. She also ordered the steamed pork dumplings, which I recognized to be the pork pot stickers from Trader Joe's.

However, the owners were very nice (could have been helped by Korean-speaking Korean friend) and they serve filtered water, not plain tap water! I readily drink tap water, but sometimes restaurant tap water tastes a little like disinfectant.

As for the cafe portion, it's a great place to study because it's so light-filled and you can take breaks watching people walking down Bancroft, but I didn't see a bathroom, which would limit how long you could park your butt there.  Also the surfaces (floor, furniture, walls) are hard and reflective of sound.

Yes, the bulgogi sandwich is delish! Also had an iced mocha bianca today that was pretty good. Like everyone else has said, the Korean lady is super nice. 

Just eat your bulgogi sandwich soon because it gets soggy fast!

Visited on Wednesday around 6p, ordered a Bulgogi sandwich. Cost: $5.20, tax included.

Pros:
-Tasty bulgogi sandwich. Bread was crispy, tasted fresh
-The bulgogi meat was similarly fresh-tasting, juicy, tender, and quite delicious.
-Satisfying portion. Half of the sandwich (it came cut in half) would be a rather light, but tasty lunch. Both halves made for a great filling dinner, without the point of becoming heartburn. to the guy above who got the $9 portion instead, I have no clue how you ate that thing.
-Great location for students or those tied to public transportation. Directly across the street from the south side of the Cal campus, and a few major AC Transit bus lines: the 1, 51, 52L, F, 7, etc. Parking is decidedly less convenient but there is a short-term garage a block away on Durant.
-Restaurant was unusually clean for southside Berkeley with attractive furniture, lighting, etc.
-Free water seems to come from an outside source (a Sparkletts-like machine) instead of the tap. I realize this is a strange personal preference but years of drinking bottled water has trained me to hate the taste of tap water.
-Friendly staff.

Cons:
-Does not accept ANY credit cards. $0.50 charge for debit cards. If they took American Express, I would probably go twice a week for lunch (hint hint). Minus one star.
-The lady behind the counter failed to ask whether I wanted mayo on the sandwich (I didn't), and it dripped over my hands. They didn't have a restroom on site, which kind of ruined my original plan of reading at the table after my sandwich. To her credit, she tried to open up the restroom around the corner of the restaurant in a nearby alley, but couldn't get it unlocked :(

This place is known for their bulgogi sandwich, and I don't know why. I found the sandwich to be too sweet and not satisfying. I've tried to get myself to like it on multiple occasions and each time, I am disappointed.

I also tried their shaved ice recently because it was a rare hot day in Berkeley. BIG MISTAKE. (see my picture) it had so much random stuff in there that it was disgusting and not the refreshing ice I was looking for. In fact, my favorite part of the dessert was actually the ICE. From what I remember, there was condensed milk, vanilla ice cream, bananas, strawberries, kiwi, pineapples, mochi, chocolate syrup. Talk about an overload of sugar.

I will never be back.
i didn't find anything special with their bulgogi sandwich. maybe because i am korean and so accustomed to the taste of bulgogi. but i can see how others might like it.

Little hidden jewel across from campus :)

1) Innovative food.  Spicy rice cake with mozzarella cheese? Bulgogi sandwich? Yeah. AND... they're actually all REALLY GOOD. I know... Not an acquired taste either.   They also have the best takeout ware I've seen in Berkeley.  Unlike other places that use cheap clear plastic boxes that melt when your food inside is too hot, Cafe Espresso Experience has really high quality plastic ware for takeout.  

2) Cute and quiet atmosphere. 

3) Nice Korean couple/service. 

But the one-star off comes from the price range.  The spicy rice cake is $8+.. You can buy a whole bag of rice cakes for like $3.. 

The green tea latte is also made differently from the ones you get at Starbucks.  Cafe Espresso Experience mixes Tazo Green Tea with soy milk to get its own unique taste.  It's really good also.  But all green tea lattes are overpriced. 

Did anyone also notice they don't have a kitchen?  So everything we eat is basically pre-cooked and heated using their microwave.

i came here all the time while i was at cal. their sandwiches are perfectly toasted and yummy, though a little on the small side portion wise. try the bulgogi sandwich for sure! they also have good pahtbingsoo (shaved ice) for a hot summer day :) every person i bring here falls in love with the sandwiches. i miss this place!

It is what it is.  Their spicy tuna is decent, but nothing else has ever caught my eye...well...other than the paht-bing-soo, which seems waaaaaay overpriced to me.  It'd be nice if they came in mini sizes that were more affordable.
Really yummy sandwiches and came here every Friday with my roommate for their Patbingsu!

Although I'm Korean-American, I never tasted a bulgogi sandwich before so when I heard there's a place that sells it right across campus, I knew I had to try it. 

Mmmmmmm, first bite was delicious. In fact every bite just tasted like the first. I also had their ddukbokki and patbingsoo and both were also sooo good. Definitely a nice place to grab lunch with a friend in between classes!

My friend took me here for my birthday lunch; it's a really chill environment and I now understand why I always see students studying in here. 

Prior to this day I had been told by others that they have the best bulgogi sandwiches. After 4 years at Cal and having walked by this place an infinite amount of times, I can now too say that they have the best bulgogi sandwiches. But wait, what am I comparing them to? Have I ever even had a bulgogi sandwich elsewhere? No, no I have not. But I am confident enough to go out on a limb and say they do have the best bulgogi sandwiches. 

The BEST part about this sandwich is.....the BREAD. Oh. My. Goodness. So soft yet crunchy, delicate yet firm, tasty yet not overpowering...MMM. it seriously put the icing on the cake....the bread on the sandwich...whatever.

The bulgogi was perfectly sweet, savory, and simply delicious. The tomato and shredded lettuce complimented the meat perfectly. 

I did add a little sriracha on the sandwich but even by itself it is delish!!

Satisfying bulgogi sandwich and friendly service. .

I had walked by this place a few times and their comfort korean food items have always piqued my interest. I was hungry after working out and decided to give their "must try" bulgogi sandwich a shot.  

The bread was nicely tasted and the sandwich nicely assembled. The chopped jalapenos on the side were appreciated. Nothing mind-blowing, but just what I needed. They have both regular and large size options, but I was not sure 

Service was extremely friendly and warm. They unfortunately do not take credit cards though. They also serve a variety of coffee and tea drinks as well as Italian sodas.  

I will have to come back for their highly recommended cheese spicy rice cakes someday.
I go here because the menu and prices are reasonable, its convenient, the wait is minimal, and the lady owner is so sweet.  I feel like whatever I order is made with tender loving care.

Don't mean to be a spoil sport but when I saw this in the top five in the Best of Berkeley list, I had to complain.  No way it is in the top 15 best places to eat in Berkeley.  

If you're a vegetarian, this is not a great choice for you.  They have hot-dog-topping-style veggies: my veggie sandwich tasted like a McDonald's salad on bread with Italian salad dressing.  Does that sound exciting?  Considering that the sandwiches are smallish and not that filling, they are rather pricey.  The ambiance is a bit clinical: clean, but without personality or style.  

However, the staff are really nice and it is always refreshing to see a clean, well-lit, non-seedy looking cafe in Berkeley.  I would bump up the rating if they had better veggie sandwiches.

Everyone says to try the Bulgogi sandwich so I did. It was pretty good. $5.20 for a small (about 8") sandwich? It's definitely worth walking the extra block past Subway. Besides, sandwiches are better toasted.
I have been craving one of their bul ko gi sandwiches for hella days, but they are closed on the weekend and close at like 5 on the weekdays, WTH?

The best, filling sandwiches.  I love the veggie sandwich, a salad on sweet bread, even with cucumber slices -- and I hate cucumber!  Prices are good compared to other places.  It's a quiet and comfortable shop.  And you can watch your food be carefully prepared, too!

This place has become one of my favorite places to stop by, get food (snack) and study.

My review has changed based on the preparation of the food and the bulgogi sandwich.However, the staff are super nice and the cafe is very close to campus which makes it convenient.

Good food, great customer service, and quiet atmosphere! What more could you ask for?

If you're looking for a quick bite to eat that won't hurt your wallet and leave you happy this is the place to go! I have tried a few sandwiches here(pastrami, bulgogee aka korean beef, and spicy tuna) and they are amazing. The spicy tuna and bulgogee sandwiches are a must try! 

If you are looking for something warm and hot on the cold days, dukbogee aka cheesy rice cakes are your answer. The rice cakes melt in your mouth and the melted cheese is a good contrast to the spiciness.

On hot days, papingsoo aka korean shaved ice is an absolute no brainer. The korean shaved ice is packed with varieties of fruit and red bean. It will really cool you down and is not intended for 1 person, I learned this lesson the hard way thinking I could finish one on my own. But boy was I happy!

The quality of the food is great but I think the Korean couple that runs the place are amazing. You can tell the owners really care about their customers. They really put the extra care into the food and it shows. If you are looking for something simple and quick, or just looking to get together with friends and catch up this is the place! I highly recommend this place to my friends and look forward to my next visit!

Very unique food. I've never had spicy noodle rice cake before. I fell in love with it. It was like eating spicy mochi. The spicy was very new to me. It was different from any spicy I've ever experienced before. It was sweet and spicy at the same time, but unique as well. The noodles were good too.

I have heard good things about their bolgogi sandwiches so I finally tried it yesterday. I cant say I agree with the past reviews about how good the bolgogi sandwich. There wasn't any jalepenos like the review said (maybe because I had to ask for it and didn't know). I felt like the sandwich itself was sweet. The bread was good at least. So all I can say is EH. The café is pretty big, that can fit like 30+ people and some of the salads look interesting. If I come back, I wont get the bolgogi sandwich or the Hawaiian bolgogi at that, since it'll probably be even sweeter!
What's that you say?  A beef bulgogi sandwich?  Tender meat? On fluffy crunchy bread you say?  Why are we still having this conversation?

I'm a big cafe hopper, and I absolutely love this place for its nice calming atmosphere and its well-priced drinks. Most importantly though, I enjoy eating here for its sandwiches and have been coming here for the past few years as an undergraduate student.

It's a great place to bring your friends-- especially those who are interested in trying something different like the famous bulgogi (Korean bbq) sandwiches, or the Korean snack-like dishes: spicy-rice cakes or the sashimi over rice dish.

My personal favorites (in addition to the bulgogi sandwich): Egg salad sandwich & the Pastrami sandwich. All of them served on delicious toasted bread!

I could be wrong, but  I feel like the bulgogi sandwich used to taste a little better. In any event, it's still a very good sandwich at a reasonable price. The owner is very nice and this place is worth coming to for a quick bite.

Monday, 1:00PM. 

A coffee house with a Korean cuisine twist? Sweet! 

They accept debit but not credit cards. Technically no free wi-fi, but registered users can use AirBears provided by campus.

Did ya notice?
+Many outlets, along eastern wall (take a hint Café Milano!)
+Large cups for water

Grubbed on:
1. Veggie sandwich (large): cucumber, avocado, onion, lettuce, tomato, mozzarella 
     +Toasted wheat roll is a nice contrast to the cold ingredients

And then?
$10 for a large sandwich wasn't enough, was still hungry afterward. Decent place to make a quick stop prior to class or a Cal event.

I have been to this place twice in the last two years. mostly because I try to eat at home. BUT I really like their ddokbokki (spicy rice cakes) and the patpingsu (shaved ice) I am from L.A and my expectations for korean food, and in particular these two dishes is kinda high. Its really good stuff though, it definitely hit the spot today when i went with my friend. The atmosphere is really nice and relaxing and the lady who works there is really sweet and welcoming.

I tried their spicy rice cakes and bulgogi sandwich. I seem to always come back for the bulgogi sandwich though.

Something about the combination of sweet barbecue beef and crunchy french bread (maybe coupled with its incredibly short walk from campus) tempts me into going back. The sweet bulgogi meat is tender and juicy on a bed of shredded lettuce and tomatoes. When you bite into a bulgogi sandwich, you first get the chewy and crunchy bread that cushions the soft and warm meat, soaking up some of the meat juices. The lettuce is there to refresh your taste buds, in case you grow tired of meat or bulgogi's rather strong sweetness. A bulgogi sandwich, however odd it might sound, is honestly almost like a fancier and more exotic version of a burger.

The place is clean and relatively fast in serving. Plenty of seats to dine in, but they tend to fill up fast.

MMMMM I finally got to go try their bulgogi sandwich, as recommended by one of my friends and it was absolutely delicious!! Soooo good. They had a good balance of meat, cheese and veggies. Although, I don't think you can ever go wrong with more meat in a sandwich. ;D It's just extra yummyness on top of already MMM MMM goodness.

I also took the time to notice that they have sushi for sale on the menu too, and some korean shaved ice dessert. Must go back again soon to try them! :)

I've been a fan of the bulgogi sandwich since I first had it in 2000.  The owners have been super classy ever since, and continue to provide quality service and food.  Their spicy tuna rolls are good too, and have a good amount of tuna - more than at most restaurants.  I haven't had much  else here because I always get the bulgogi sandwich - you just have to try it.

It seems as though they changed the recipe, however.  Back in the day, they used to include julienned carrots, which gave the sandwich a crunchy texture as well as sweetness to complement the beef.  Still an outstanding sandwich, though, especially with jalapenos.

It's a great place to study and read, as it gets a lot of sunlight.  Not sure if they still have them, but the sliding glass doors by the tables at the front were also a nice touch.

WOW. The bulgogi sandwich - I knew it'd be good, but I didn't realize it would be a combination of like every awesome taste/texture ever. Crunchy - toasted bread. Juicy - tomatoes. Crispy - lettuce. Meat - bulgogi. It was also sweet and tangy and I was very surprised. And only $5.50!!! Amazing. Too bad they only open on weekdays and it's cash only. 

Also took off a star because a fly landed in my water and they ran out of water. :(

Just tried the sandwiches and they are quite tasty.
I would recommended the Hawaiian bulgogi or the buffalo chicken sandwich.

They are not the most filling sandwiches and they are kind of expensive at $6 for a 6 in and $10-11 for a footlong.
Its worth a go.

Bobby Abreu. Bulgogi. 

Those are 2 words that when someone says them, I think they just threw up a little. 

That being said, this place has an awesome bulgogi (excuse me) sandwich. Very good. Warm ,soft bread, a good amount of meat, lettuce, tomato...yum.

It's takes a bit for them to prepare the sandwich, but that's cool. I tried their Hawaiian bulgogi, but I won't get that again. The difference: Add pineapple and an offensive amount of shredded cheese, nix the lettuce. 

Stick with the regular bulgogi (sorry) sandwich.

it's a breezy socal night... 2am, i'd say.  my girls and i have a hankerin for some comfort food, slash insanity.  

let's drive to berkeley for some bulgogi sandwiches.

there's nothing like toasty warm baguette hugging pieces of home-marinated bulgogi embedded in melting swiss and veggies at 10 in the morning, after a 6 hour drive.  and the friendly service and reasonable prices don't kill you either.
Just go for the bulgogi sandwich, which was delicious, and the friendly service. But don't plan to stay... it smells kinda funny, poor ventilation I think.

This is one of my favorite places for an afternoon snack and definitely a place i will miss after leaving Berkeley.

Staple foodings include:
-bulgogi sandwich
-hwae dup bab
-Korean shaved ice
-green tea latte (love it)
-cheesy rice cake (yum for the colder days)

Its good to go with friends or by yourself. Most visits I usually run into 2 or 3 groups of friends during my long lazy hours spent here. Its generally quiet and the cute Korean couple that run it are always sweet and friendly. Even if I'm not hungry, I often get to-go sandwiches and bring them home for later. 

Try it! You won't regret it.

This place is great for a laid back feel. I recommend their bulgogi sandwiches, chibokgi (cheesy spicy rice cake) and their shaved ice for dessert! 

The bulgogi sandwich is a nice fusion American-Korean sandwich with the korean marinated beef inside it. It has a good balance of sweet, tangy, and saltiness. Quite yummy with jalapenos! The cheesy spicy rice cake has a fusion-ness to it as well with the cheese on top of the traditional ddukbogi (spicy rice cake). Obviously if you're lactose intolerant, I wouldn't recommend it but you should try it if you can take some lactose at small doses haha. Love eating the cheese with the dduck (rice cake) and pulling on the cheese. It's a fun experience to try and eat it! Also, their shaved ice was surprisingly pleasant. I personally like my shaved ice with lots of fruits so that was a minus for me but the strawberry syrup made it more pleasant and the ice wasn't too chunky either.

I love the open decor of the place, with wide windows that let lots of sunlight come in. Definitely recommend coming here for a quick eat with your friends or for a delightful eating experience.

One of my favorite sandwich places in Berkeley. Started coming here when I was still going to school across the street and I still head out here for lunch every once in a while. The chicken teriyaki sandwiches are still my favorite. It's because of this place that I have a higher standard for sub sandwiches (always need to be toasted) and I now need to have jalapenos with them. Their subs are a good portion - everyone who's gone here for the first time is always surprised by how much you get. I love how the sandwiches are toasted perfectly. Bulgogi and beef teriyaki sandwiches are both also very tasty. It just depends on what I feel like eating that day...

I wasn't expecting much... but I was rather impressed with my bulgogi sandwich. Good luck trying to find parking around here... it's right smack dab in front of the college, so you are better off walking.

This place exceeded my expectations!
I tend to avoid Korean places around campus because the food usually sucks and tastes nasty, and I prefer my own Korean cooking to whatever junk they sell near campus. (Seriously.... what a disgrace to Korean cuisine...)

I think I can safely say that Espresso Experience is the most legit Korean place I've tried near campus (even though it's fusion). I got what they're famous for: bulgogi sandwich.
Dang. It was pretty good. The bread was toasted to a very delightful texture that I completely did not expect. Mmm. The bread.... really wasn't expecting it to be that good.

Shaved ice was big (we shared it with 6 people). And slow. Like an elephant.

Overall, food here is very good, but it takes quite a while to come out. I kinda want to try their other food. 

FYI: Cash or Debit Card (processing fee applies) only. No credit cards.



---- Update!! (11/10/2010)

I had the spicy rice cakes w/ cheese (cheese ddukbokki, a.k.a. chibokki) today! It's $1.45 more to add cheese to the ddukbokki and I think I know the reason why - they use the entire $1.45 bag of mozzarella cheese to smother your food in! Ah hahaha! I really didn't expect so much cheese - I shared my stupendous wealth by giving half my cheese to a friend who got the regular (cheese-less) ddukbokki, and it was still more than enough. At least we know they ain't skimpin' on the cheese!! I enjoyed every gooey, warm, stringy mouthful... =)

BTW, their spicy tuna sandwich and hwe-dup-bab (huge sashimi bowl with rice and veggies) are also really good. Actually, I don't think you can really go wrong with this place.... I like!! =)

I had spicy noodle rice cake and bulgogi sandwich. 
The sandwich is really good, especially the bread! It was crunchy and the taste is just right.
The rice cake was decent, and it was very spicy.

I've been eating their bulgogi sandwich for about 15 years now and I still love it.  I particularly like how they toast the bread for you and adding jalapenos in it. 

The issues I have with this place is 1) first of all, parking (but that's the same as every other place in Berkeley and no fault of theirs) and 2) price.  I love the bulgogi sandwich but $6 for a small one is just too much! It's just a bun, some meat, lettuce, tomato, and slices of jalapenos on the side.  I guess the price hasn't deterred me from eating there all these many years, but it does make me hesitate at times.  If it were cheaper, think I would go there even more often.  

As for everything else, I only find it so-so.  Nothing else particularly stands out.

This cafe is so great! :D 
It's run by this (married?) couple and it's a great place to get Korean food. ^___^ 
The Bulgogi sandwiches are BOMB (for a low price), and the spicy rice cakes make me want to go to Korea again. :O
In the summer, order the shaved ice! It's like heaven. In your mouth.
I miss you bulgogi sandwich...so toasty and flavorful...a sweet memory of my Berkeley days.

I used to come here all the time during undergrad years.  I STILL have cravings for the bulgogi sandwiches... with jalapenos. yummy.

Does anyone know their hours?  I'm trying to come back but can't during M-F lunch time.  Every time I call the number it goes straight to voice mail.
"Their sandwiches restore my faith in humanity."

CAFE ESPRESSO is probably one of my favorite places to have lunch dates! It is a cutesy place with yummy food! yummy Korean food! =)

Usually I am VERY picky with my ddukbbokee BUT Cafe Espresso DID NOT disappoint me! YAY! It was very yummy! =)

I LOVE LOVE LOVE Bulgogi! I LOVE LOVE LOVE bread! put those two things together & add on some sauce here & there = BULGOGI SANDWICH! nom nom nom! I never had anything like it. Have you heard of it? Anyways... TRY IT! I usually get the regular Bulgogi or the Hawaiian Bulgogi Sandwich =)

HMM... one more thing!... I LOVE their shaved ice! It's so cute & yummy of course! It's not year round so when it's summer/spring... TRY IT! =)

The service = awesome! The lady knows me.. LOL she knows I don't like tomatoes in my Bulgogi sandwich && that I don't want jalapenos. ^^

Keep in mind: the place has weird times... sometimes it closes @5 or later... that is the only flaw.

Taste: 2
Value: 4
Service: 3

I came here because of the good Yelp reviews, but the bulgogi sandwich I ordered came out soggy. Not sure what the hype is all about, but it was definitely not worth the high yelp rating.

This review is based on food. Particularly, their spicy rice cake.
I was absolutely horrified - HORRIFIED when I saw how they cook their food. 
You don't microwave liquidy food in microwave, in a disposable clear plastic container. I was afraid that I would be eating spicy rice cake sauce + molten plastic - There actually were holes on the container, because of this thoughtless microwaving. 
Judging by their carelessness and absolute no regard for the health of the person who'll be eating the food, I've made the decision to never to return to this place. I know that cheap price means cheap food, but I don't want to be paying to feed myself carcinogens

toasted bread, bulgogi, mayo, lettuce, and some other stuff  =  glorious euphoria unequaled by any other sandwich experience, ever. 

people, this is good stuff.

EE is a pretty good sandwich place.  Their bulgogi sandwich, if anything, is unique, and I love eating it with the jalepenos they give with it.  They do have off-days, when it doesn't taste as good, so if you had a bad experience, I wouldn't completely write this one off.  Their coffee is usually pretty good too.  I think I've had the cafe latte and the cafe mocha, and I remember both of those being pretty good--not too strong and not too sweet.  The patbingsoo I'm actually not that fond of.  I actually found it rather bland and the ice was really chunky.  The owners are really nice.

The Korean lady here is a bit awkward. The other reviewers said that she was really friendly, and I guess she is, but when I asked what was good, what was popular, she had really vague, disinterested answers. 
-_____-
It tastes good though. The bulgogi burger is a bit over-hyped. It's good, but I've had better. =P
I tried the spicy tuna roll (there's two kinds, raw or cooked; I tried the cooked) and the chibbokki (I think the translation is the spicy rice cake with cheese) which is basically ddukbokki poured into a platter with white cheese spread over it and baked till its in melted perfection. yummm so good! The portions for the roll were big, too, and together (not the bulgogi burger) was about $14, if I remember correctly. 
The only thing that really sucks here is that they don't take credit card and they charge a fifty cent service fee for debit cards (but the lady didn't tell me beforehand, I found out in the receipt. Actually, it posted on the counter's surface, but honestly, who reads that?)
Overall, it's not really "authentic Korean food" since the taste/style has been altered to conform to other non-Korean tastebuds, but I'll definitely come again :D

It's so hard to find a good coffee shop/cafe in Berkeley that's quiet, not crowded, and friendly. Thankfully, this place totally fits the bill. The family that runs this place is so kind. Plus, the food is delicious!

If you must eat, definitely opt for the bulgogi sandwich. The meat is so flavorful and the sandwich just plain works! If you like it spicy, ask for extra jalapenos! Another thing I love is the spicy rice cakes. So delicious!

The drinks are okay. It's not the greatest, but the food more than makes up for it:)

Good lord, I'm obsessed with their bulgogi sandwich. The idea of putting Korean beef into a perfectly toasted sandwich -- totally brilliant. The owners of the place also seem extremely nice, which is why I'm able to forgive the fact that a fair amount of time passes between when I order a sandwich and when I'm finally able to take a huge, delicious bite. 

Really not much else to say, considering I've never tried any of their other menu items (and why would I do such a thing?) The place is clean and bright for studying, it probably gets AirBears, silly $0.50 charge for credit/atm card...but really, who cares about these details. Bulgogi sandwich = everything. More people need to know about this place!

This is one of those stores that I've always passed by but never entered and, to this day, I do not know why I didn't. I finally came at the recommendation of my friend and I must say, I was not disappointed in the least.

The bulgogi sandwich has been heralded here on Yelp and the masses were certainly not wrong. Freshly made with just the right amount of the other ingredients (lettuce, mayo, etc.), each bite was a sumptuous tidbit of Korean heaven in my mouth. The balance of the sweetness and saltiness was just perfect and I wanted more even after my last bite.

Since it was a cold, rainy day today, I decided to get their spicy rice cakes too. If you like spicy, you'll love the rice cakes. The spicy pain in my mouth was worth every bite. Served with tian bu la (I don't know the English translation...so here's a link http://edu.ocac.gov.tw/culture/chinese/cultureenglish/Cuisine/Ecuisine0504_11.htm) and a hardboiled egg, the amount was served was generous and I was stuffed by the time I took the last bite.

An added bonus to the great food is the owners are both really nice! Friendly and smiling throughout the whole transaction =]

In short, this is a great mom and pop restaurant that you should definitely swing by to try! I'll definitely swing by more often now for the bulgogi sandwich xD

Truth be told, Berkel Berkel a few blocks down Telegraph does better bulgogi, but not in convenient sandwich form. Esp Exp's is kinda like a Subway sandwich, except with surprisingly decent bread. Given that it's reheated, the bulgogi is about as good as it can be.

LOVELOVELOVE their bulgogi sandwiches!!!!

I usually get either the regular bulgogi sandwich or the hawaiian bulgogi sandwich. The regular bulgogi sandwich has lettuce, tomatoes, mayo, and some bombbb korean marinated beef, while the hawaiian bulgogi sandwich has pineapples, onions, cheese, and of course bulgogi as well! Both cost $5.95, which is pretty reasonable for the size of the sandwiches (:

Also, if you don't want something in your sandwich or if you want to add something, just let them know - they'll gladly change it up for you! Last time I got a hawaiian bulgogi and I asked them to add lettuce, and they willingly agreed (: 

The bulgogi sandwich is one of the top things I crave when I'm in socal during my breaks.. so that says a lot!! (:

I've also tried their korean shaved ice, which has (on top of the shaved ice) strawberries, pineapples, bananas, red bean, colorful mochi, and a scoop of ice cream, with the whole thing lightly drizzled with chocolate syrup. It's a good amount to share with about 3 people (: 

The service is good, the workers are friendly, and the cafe itself is very clean and has plenty of seating! (: Definitely a must-try in Berkeley!

3.5 STARS 

I don't like to order the same thing from the same place more than twice, but every once of in awhile, I come here to satisfy my bulgogi sandwich craving. 

Being a big fan of Korean food (especially Korean MEAT), I have had better bulgogi. Their bulgogi are not made from the best quality of meat, not marinated in the best of sauce, and etc, but it hits the spot in terms of consistency. I think that's the beauty of Cafe Espresso Experience's infamous bulgogi sandwich. In my opinion, it's just a simple sandwich played well. It's got the lovely  freshly toasted bread, crisp shredded lettuce, thinly sliced tomato, right amount of mayo, and a relatively generous amount of bulgogi that's not too dry, too saucy, too salty, or too bland. All the elements just work well together. It's not spectacular or out of this world, but hey, if a poor college girl needs her above-average sandwich and cheap bulgogi fix in Berkeley, THIS IS THE PLACE. (Well, okay, I can also suck it up make some on my own, but sleeping always sound like the better choice) It is on the small side in terms of size if you compare it to your five dollar foot long Subway or chubby Chipotle burrito down the block, but it usually fills me up to a comfortable point. 

I've also tried the spicy rice cake. Well, same with the bulgogi sandwich, it's pretty good, not fantastic, but it hits the satisfactory mark for me. Though I do feel they could put more things in there asides from the sad onion slices and two pieces of thin fishcake. Not extremely spicy, but definitely stay away from it if spicy food is not your thing. 

As for drinks and desserts, the coffee is meh. I have had better and I have had worse. I'd only order it if you're desperate for caffeine. The shaved ice is also on the meh side. It's pretty and decorated with many fruits and a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top, but the shaved ice itself is way too rough and hard and I am not a fan of the artificially colored sugar syrup and the lack of condensed milk. I only had it because my friend bought it for me. 

Overall Cafe Espresso Experience is definitely up to par. Though not quite a solid winner, but it gets the job done when you're in the mood for what it has to offer.

They take ATM, but there is a fee.

My #1 rule for eating out in Berkeley: EXPLORE! Never eat at the same place twice in a semester.  That's how I came across this cafe and its amazing BULGOGI sandwich!

I came in the store after a long tennis match and I told the sweet Korean lady "Hit me up with your best sandwich yo!" and she's all like "Bulgogi fosho!"  Conversation went down like that more or less.  

I had NO IDEA what a bulgogi sandwich even was (I think it's Korean BBQ beef or something), but man, if you want a juicy beefy sandwich on a sub roll, you must check this place out.  I lived at Unit 3 for a year and I walked past this place a MILLION times but didn't discover it until senior year.  wtf?  Don't make the same mistake as me.  Get off your lazy butts and try this place out!

I think this place is a little bit over-hyped. No offense or anything, but I didn't think their Bulgogi Sandwich was THAT amazing like what everyone else has been saying. 

Came here for lunch and ordered what everyone else recommended - The Bulgogi Sandwich. The regular sized sandwich is about $5.50 and large is twice the price, around $10, which I think is kind of ridiculous. So my order took about 15 minutes... I honestly don't think it takes that long to make a sandwich. 

It was way smaller than I expected and I felt like I didn't eat anything afterwards, and the taste was so-so/mediocore. Nothing amazing. Overall, I'd rather go for bibimbap from Toust or even Chipotle would at least fill me up. 

Bottom line: I certainly didn't find this a fulfilling experience.

This was my spot for lazy/gluttonous afternoons with my Korean girlfriends in Sophomore year. We had a reunion here today, and I realized how much I love this place. It's rare to find a place that takes me back to the days in Korea. I've even brought my cousins from Korea here, and they even thought it was good Korean food. 

Favorites:
Cheese Spicy Rice Cake: The regular one is awesome with rice cake, veggies, and an egg covered in sweetly spicy sauce. But when you add the cheese into the mix...it is magical. It is COVERED by mozzarella cheese and melted in the oven. SO GOOD. If you are a cheese lover like myself- try this! Tip: Buy dumplings and use it to dip it into the left over sauce/cheese.

Sashimi Spicy Rice Bowl: HUGE bowl. Lots of veggies and a decent amount of sashimi. You can add your own spicy sauce to accommodate your spicy taste buds. 

Shaved Ice: Huge..we were 3 girls and we had a lot left over. Imagine copious amounts of shaved ice, drizzled condensed milk, sweet red sauce. Garnished with bananas, pinapples, kiwis, strawberries, mochi, and red beans. Top it all off with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Heavenly on an unusually sunny Feb day in the bay. 

There is also drinks, sandwiches, and CA rolls offered here, but the food listed above are a MUST TRY'S at the place. The Korean lady at the counter is just really friendly and sweet. She greets everyone as if she was like an aunt. It gets a tadddd bit loud at the cafe due to the Korean population (like myself) the cafe attracts, but I've studied here before and it was ok. Just bring earphones. :)

Two words: Bulgogi Sandwich.

Yes, I'd hate to repeat what all the other reviews have said but a simply truth cannot be denied. You come here for the Bulgogi Sandwich. The beef is tasty, the bread is toasted, there's a decent amount of veggies inside so you're not just eating beef between bread and eaten with pickled jalapenos that add a nice zing to the flavors in your mouth.

I really miss this place and have never found a similar substitute for it. The place seemed to be family owned and the owner and her daughter (?) are really nice people. 

I have no idea how anything tastes here (including their coffee since they are a cafe after all) because it was love at first taste with the bulgogi sandwich. Back when I was there, the price was decent.

The sandwiches are filling and great quality. I've tried most sandwiches, and I'd have to say the best ones are the bulgogi, the crab salad, and teriyaki beef or chicken sandwiches. The coffees are pricey but good quality. It's at a convenient location and there's plenty of seating but I heard the prices have gone up lately.. so sad.

been coming here since i first went to berkeley, um, years ago. you have to try the bulgogi sandwich- best ever. in fact, the ONLY place i know that serves it. now if only they open longer hours on the weekend...it's anti non students--i can't catch them on weekdays!

This is one of my favorite places to eat on the Berkeley campus!

Their selection is primarily limited to Korean BBQ sandwiches, and a few other Korean dishes, but it's soooo worth it.  The meat is tender and flavorful, the jalapenos (optional) add a nice spicy kick, the bread is toasted but soft, mmm...

Plus the owners are so cute and super nice!  I came here one Valentine's Day with my boyfriend, and since we were regulars and it was raining so hard outside, they gave us free hot tea to warm up with.

Ooooh, and their shaved ice is DEFINITELY worth a try, though you should probably bring someone along to help you finish it.  It's a veritable mountain of delicious fruit, fine ice chips, condensed milk, and red bean.  YUM.

It was ridiculously scorching today so I decided to come here for some Korean shaved ice that a friend recommended I get!!

SUCH A RELIEF. I don't know if people have tried Guppys in socal but this place is comparable, but much more authentic. A small size can easily feed 2-3 people (about half the size of a Guppys small though). It comes with ice cream, red bean, jelly, syrup, mochi, and some other toppings I can't seem to remember. I believe it cost 6-7 dollars. Well worth it if you split with a friend.

We all know Berkeley is usually cold, but this is a great escape for those random hot days global warming is bringing around!

Came for a quick lunch after hearing all the compliments from fellow yelpers. It sure didn't disappoint me. The bulgogi sandwich was great and the owner was very nice. Good price, wi-fi, clean interior, great food, and what else.... I'll leave it there. Will surely go back soon.

Love their bulgogi sandwiches! The portions don't look that big, but the price is fair and the sandwiches are pretty filling. And it's pretty unique for the Berkeley area. They also serve some other Korean-inspired dishes, as well as regular sandwiches as well. 

The staff is also super nice, and there's always seating available.

After always walking by Cafe Espresso and hearing so much about it, I had to eventually try it out. I consider it a hidden gem amongst the more popular Korean options on South Side, although it's always pretty packed. 

I ordered the Crab Sandwich, which is the first thing that popped out to me after the Bulgogi Sandwich. I'll save that one for next time though ;-)

The Crab Sandwich was really delicious! There was a good amount of fresh crab, as well as a pile of lettuce, tomatoes, and onions. The bread was toasted to perfection, and the whole dish was just very well prepared for something so simple.

I also got a chance to try the rice cakes covered with cheese, which was pretty good as well. I don't know if I would consider Cafe Espresso absolutely amazing, but it's definitely up there. For $5, I was pretty full for the rest of the day, and I will definitely come back.

I came here a while ago, but I just now remembered to yelp it. Awesome place to get a great Bulgogi sandwich. There isn't much meat, but its all about the flavor! Sweet BBQ'ed beef on a great roll. The bread perfectly complements the rest of the sandwich.
My only problem is that its far from where I usually am. Its not really Cafe Espresso's fault, so I cant take off a star for that, but if more of my classes were closer to the southwest side of campus I would come here a whole lot more often. Maybe its time for a change of major to get closer to these sandwiches!

This place is so cute! 

The food is good, the prices are cheap, the atmosphere is warm. What more can I ask for?

Also, I'm not a fan of green tea, but I tried a green tea drink here that was amazing!

The only thing I have ever ordered from this place is the Crab Salad Sandwich. And there's a reason for that! It's really delicious and has just the right amount of toasty-ness in the bread. There are times when I'm craving that sandwich and have to go out of my way just to get it.

The service is great. The woman that is usually at the cash register seems pretty sweet and always has a smile on her face. And even on a bad day, I can't help but smile back.

I sometimes go there to study because it's a cute little cafe. Sometimes they open up their very large windows and bring in a nice breeze. So it's a good way to study "outdoors" without actually having to be outdoors!

This place has a nice atmosphere, plenty of light. 

I really like the ahjumma who works there because she is really pretty and nice. She speaks to you in korean if you speak to her in korean. She usually welcomes people in korean. 

My favorites from this place is 

1) Spicy Rice Cakes with melted cheese 
2) Bulgogi sandwich

I haven't tried much else on their menus, but so far I like what I have tried. I usually order to go from here because it's convenient to just bring home. I don't really feel the need to sit and eat there unless I'm meeting up with someone. 

I have yet to try their shaved ice which looks good from pictures, but it is seasonal. Overall I like this place and will be going there from time to time if I feel like dukbokki  =)

I've only had their popular items here which are the bulgogi sandwich and the spicy rice cakes. I like spicy rice cakes, but I didn't like it here that much. It rice cakes were a little too hard. I attribute my dislike mostly to the sauce because it was too starchy and gloopy, if there is such a thing. On top of that, there was just way too much of it. As for the bulgogi sandwich, I can find no fault with that except that it does take them a while to make. It's not as quick as you think, but it's a great portable lunch item. Overall, the staff here are nice, but the food can take a while. There's a huge lunch rush and you can get no work done, much less have a conversation. Otherwise, other times of the day are fairly quiet and you can take advantage of the free wifi.

I never heard of a bulgogi sandwich before, and I was inrigued. I ordered the small which was about $5.00 and it was plenty big to fill me up (and I'm the guy who's never ordered the 6" at Subway, always go for the 12". 
Really nice flavor, unique yet familiar. I'll definitely be back.

I'm not sure I would have gone to this place if my curiosity had not been piqued by the rave reviews of this "bulgogi" business.   For that reason alone, I had been meaning to go here for a while.   I finally dove in today, and I am psyched about it.   Thank you, fellow yelpers, for introducing me to my new favorite easy campus lunch stop.   I usually have trouble finding food I really like around campus.   I will have trouble no more.

Here's the run-down
First impressions:  the cafe was totally clean and friendly.   And by friendly I mean both the service AND the customers were very pleasant to be around.   The cashier asked how I was doing (standard) but in a very genuine way and with a huge smile on his face (not so standard).   
Ordering:   Ordered the regular bulgogi (sans mayo) for $4.80.   Please note, I never eat beef.  I don't particularly like it, I never want it, I don't see the point.  I ordered it here because I felt I owed it to yelp to try this famed bulgogi sandwich.  It took a little longer than I expected for it to be ready but there were a lot of orders in front of me and the cute lady behind the counter was making each item fresh and with care.
Taste:   holy crap.    The first bite was amazing, mind you, but I swear it got better with each bite.   I lost myself in this simple little sandwich.   It didn't LOOK like a sandwich I would normally eat--shredded lettuce, toasted white bread roll, and, again, beef--but after trying it, I'm pretty sure this will be a lunchtime staple for me.   The bread was the perfect texture (not what I would expect from an everyday white bread roll!), the meat was perfectly thin and had great texture, the lettuce was crispy juicy good, the tomatoes weren't the mushy flavorless slices of crap you'll find at Subway, but fairly flavorful and juicy (good considering this is not their season).   The beef has a slight sweet flavor which is clear in each bite but not overpowering (THANK YOU.  No bigger turn-off than over-sweetened, drowning-in-sauce teriyaki items).    


I adored the food and the atmosphere.   I will definitely be back.   Bonus: I don't have to feel guilty for spending  all of my money.   Delectable but simple sandwich for less than five bucks?   Yes.
The bulgogi sandwiches are great, but too small.  It would be a 5 if I wasn't still slightly hungry afterwards.

EDIT (1/14/10):  ** They have raised their prices so now the regular order of a bulgogi sandwich is $5.95.  I've eaten at Espresso Experience for the last two years and the quality seems to have gone down while the prices have risen.  The bulgogi sandwich I had today barely had any meat in in.  While the bread is still nice and crispy,  the sandwich itself lacked it's old flavor and it didn't wow me as usual.  I probably won't be coming back anymore, the sandwich just isn't worth $6 when there are few ingredients and the meat is scant.    

The famous bulgogi sandwich is so good and cheap!  A regular order is only $4.80!  ** They have raised their prices so now the regular order is $5.95. ** The bread is also very crispy and just the right texture.  They serve coffee drinks and sushi here as well.  I have never tried the sushi but I've seen some very happy customers dig into them, the rolls look delicious.  Now they offer shaved ice and it is heavenly!  Bananas, strawberries, mango, grapes kiwi, mochi, red bean, cereal, and a scoop of ice cream  = very yummy!  The only negative would be that service is kind of slow, but then again that means they take their time with each order!  I got the shaved ice to go and it came in a HUGE container.  Totally awesome.  The owners are so so nice too.  I will be back for the sandwich though!

I forgot to write a review of this place.
Now 3 months later here it is.
Right across from UCB campus.
Bulgogi Sandwich!
Order of california rolls.
Mom and Pop's Joint.
Simple and Sweet spot to drop by for lunch but parking might be hard if you're not paitent.

I always hear about this elusive "perfect bite," never knowing what that means. I've had really good food before and I've definitely had food that's blown me away, but I never really understood the meaning of the perfect bite until I came to Cafe Espresso Experience.

The perfect bite is three words: "Spicy Tuna Sandwich." There is nothing more satisfying, more simple, and more delicious. The tuna fish salad is mixed with spicy sriracha-mayonnaise. The kick of the spicyness, the meatiness of the tuna, the crunchy onions, the refreshing lettuce, and the toasted bread all combine together to make the perfect sandwich. Yum!

The dokbokki is also good, but I usually only come here because I'm craving the spicy tuna. I also love this place because it's rarely ever super crowded and if you sit by the windows, you can use the Airbears internet, so it's a good place to study as well!

BULGOGI SANDWICH FOR THE WIN!!  Definitely get it and try it.  Sweet korean bbq style marinated meat in a toast roll with lots of lettuce.  It comes with jalepenos and although a little spicy, adds that extra kick to make the sandwich a perfect 10.  I've found a decent substitute in socal near Ontario but it will never compare to the original I've had here.

Regular is two halves and large is 3 I believe!

Tips:

The spicy rice cakes are SPICY, be warned.

-------------------------------------------

This small little cafe owned by a Korean couple is super cute with good food. I've gotten the spicy rice cakes and the spicy noodle rice cake. (The spicy noodle rice cakes have a majority of noodles so if you want rice-cakes definitely get the other dish because the proportion of noodle to rice cake is definitely not equal in the second dish.) It really is the spiciest thing I have ever eaten in my life. I was in pain. T_T Definitely not a good dish for weaklings like me that can't take spicy too well.

The bulgogi sandwich is SOO GOOD. The meat is so sweet and tender it goes GREAT as a sandwich. The bulgogi salad is also a great choice as well! It's kind of like a small bibimbap with a leafy salad, rice, and bulgogi. These 2 dishes are quite similar so they're good substitutes for each other if you really want some bulgogi.

The coffee on the other hand isn't the greatest, but that's okay because I don't really come here for the coffee anyways. I'd suggest to come here for food rather than coffee. There are a lot of other places to get coffee from that I believe are better choices.

Came here a couple days ago hoping to get some shaved ice. I've read on Yelp and heard that the shaved ice here is really good. Unfortunately they don't serve it during the winter months, and the lady said the machine would be available in March. Womp womp.

Anyway, the large bulgogi sandwich is really two sandwiches (four halves), so if you're going with someone you should order the large, otherwise go for the small if you're going solo. The bread was toasted and crispy, the meat was juicy and succulent, but I'm not sure if it was worth the money. A large runs about 11.50ish while a small is $6.

Don't get the Italian soda; $2-3 for syrup + club soda is a ripoff. 

Make sure to bring cash. They don't take credit cards, and if you're going to be using a debit card they'll charge an extra 50 cents. Luckily Wells Fargo and Bank of America are close by.

Overall, Cafe Espresso is a good place to study, and is yet another place to have coffee or drinks for Cal students.  I'll be coming back for the shaved ice when it's available!
This spot is popular for their bulgogi sandwich.  but..!  I wanted give mega big ups to the macchiato!  not too sweet, not too plain. def. better than franchise version!

AHH Cafe Espresso is probably my favorite places in Berkeley. They have awesome bulgogi sandwiches, dukkbokkgi (spicy rice cake) and dumplings (mandoo).

I want to give it five stars, but I hate their random hours. They don't serve dinner, and they're closed on the weekends (I believe). There were a lot of instances where me and my friends walked up to the cafe, only to find that it was closed. I wish they had a more concrete schedule.

But they have the tastiest food, in my opinion. I love their sandwiches (bulgogi, Hawaiian bulgogi, sometimes spicy chicken) for the taste and  the price ($5-6 for a regular size), I love the dukkbokkgi even more ($6-7). The rice cakes are perfectly chewy, and the spicy sauce is JUST right (it tastes like the dukkbokkgi from Korea).

A lot of non-Korean people don't know about this place (which is sad), but Cafe Espresso has some BOMB food. TRY IT!

Came here tonight for dinner and the location is really convenient since it's right across the street from campus! I had never really noticed it before, but I'm glad that friends recommended it. The Korean woman working the counter was very friendly and helpful!

What I ordered:
- Vegetarian spicy rice cake (dokbokki) ($6.25): http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/gYbX_IfkzWme4ItyXb_lgw?select=Yn8jvkbGnwiTy02j-Cf_TA#wkUyjkXMQLqTRJBrC9NTPA

I'd had dokbokki before at O.B. Chicken and I didn't remember the dish being that spicy, so I thought I could handle the one from Cafe Espresso Experience no problem. I generally enjoy spicy food as long as it's not crazily overboard and would rate my spiciness tolerance as pretty decent, but I surrendered to this dokbokki. The food came out hot, which coupled with the spiciness of the sauce, made it pretty hard to eat and I could only take half bites at a time. I probably would've needed 5 glasses of water to finish the whole thing, but I got pretty full by the time I had eaten 2/3 of the plate. The sauce and the dish itself was good though, but I just had to eat slowly. It also comes with a boiled egg on top which is nice! Next time, I'll probably try the dokbokki with cheese to balance out the spiciness a little!

It's all about the Bulgogi Sandwich.

Don't be a fool and order a generic turkey sandwich. Get the mighty Bulgogi Sandwich. There's no other choice. It's a little overpriced, but totally worth it. I used to motivate myself to go to the RSF by letting myself have one afterwards. So awesome. Now I'm crazy ripped. Aw yea! Just kidding. But seriously the Espresso Experience is one of my top ten fondest college memories.

Tips: Hurry! This family owned shop closes down for summer vacation.

Clean, usually can find a seat, can get Airbears, really sweet owners!  

The only available bathroom requires walking all the way around Musical Offering and behind the building... just hold it and go across the street to Eshelman Hall.  

Their coffee is decent - definitely a safe place to grab coffee in between classes.  Specifically I am talking about the soy latte.  

As for the food, I think the original concept of the Bulgolgi sandwich was super exciting to me!  I'm not sure if the novelty has worn off, but it didn't seem to be as good the last time I had it.  At 5.50 for a regular size, the price is not bad.  It's definitely still yummy, but it's not as good as it used to be.

The spicy rice cakes are pretty good too.  I think they are 6.50.  I love how hot it is, but it's a little too sweet for my taste.  However I don't think the sweetness is out of the ordinary.  I like sharing a plate of the rice cakes and sharing a bulgogi sandwich for a satisfying meal on a cold day :)

The bulgogi sandwiches are delicious, though it is true there isn't a whole lot of beef (but health-wise, we could probably do with less red meat). 

But really, the lady is so warm and friendly! She always remembers that I like jalapenos on the side :).  The cafe is such a nice little nook with chaotic Telegraph a turn away that I really recommend this place very much! Ever since my boyfriend introduced me to the sandwich, I'm allll about it.

Update 1/08: I went today for lunch (DELISH) and my bulgogi sandwich had the perfect amount of beef in it! SWEEET.

I had an English GSI who had a thing for this establishment because Michel Focault supposedly frequented the coffee joint during his Berkeley escapades of the '60s. Well, I no longer come here due to its Foucaultian history, but rather for their sumptuous eats.

While they may be called ESPRESSO Experience and have a full coffee bar complete with affordable lattes and teas, their main selling point must be their sandwiches, which are perfect for a light lunch that won't give you a severe food coma in lecture afterwards. I especially recommend the chicken terryaki. The price of the regular size (below $5) is very reasonable. Highly recommend that you try it, they're very addictive.

The cafe itself is owned by a Korean family that's really friendly and almost kow-tow when serving you...kinda weird but nice that they appreciate your business. They just opened a few weeks ago after a renovation and I like the new, more sophisticated atmosphere. Though it's not crowded at all during the summer, it does get busy during lunchtime throughout the academic year with students opting for the signature bulgogi eats.

Oh Espresso, Espresso!
Let down your hair!
I crave the secret of bulgogi
Please share!

That's what I'd say if I knew how to cook, anyway. Since I can't cook, I eat out, then I Yelp. My first bulgogi experience was about a year ago, and let me just say.... roast beef has never been the same. The bulgogi has a slightly sweet flavor and is full of warm juices and tender goodness. The bread is crusty and fresh, and the mix of sliced carrots and some pickled veggies makes a refreshing contrast to the warm meat. I also love how they give you all the sliced jalapenos your tongue could ever take. For less than $6, you can easily fill your tummy with 6'' of  yummy! And for $9, it's twice the yummy, but if you're by yourself it would probably leave an ache in your tummy.

The food at Espresso Experience is great, and the owners are hospitable beyond belief. I was meeting some friends all day there, and they did not mind at all while I surfed their free WiFi for 6+ hours on a rainy day. I only ordered a chai latte during that time and had water from their cooler for the rest of the day, but they did not mind me sitting there at all! Some other cafe owners might get antsy, but they welcomed me back with smiles over the next few days and c'mon, who wouldn't give them business after that?

Don't be fooled by that generic (and kinda lame) shop name, this place is one of the hidden gems of Cal!  First of all, this place is technically a cafe, but I have never had coffee here, and they aren't known for their coffee either.  What they are known for are their bulgogi sammich!  In case you didn't know, bulgogi is Korean marinaded thin sliced beef.  The bread is nicely toasted and the beef is sweet and delicious!  Perfect for lunch and it's only 5.50!  Even though this sammich is definitely drool-worthy, my favorite dish from this place is their dukboki!  But I guess I'm a bit bias because dukboki is one of my FAVORITE FOOD OF ALL TIME!

In my dorm days, I would often get dukboki from Bear Ramen House.  And although BRH remains my favorite spot at Asian Ghetto, CEE makes a better portioned, spicier, and more delicious dukboki.  Chewy rice cakes, fish cakes, and a boiled egg smothered in a hot chili paste (or as I call it, red Korean sauce).  Get 5 bottles of water ready because your whole pie-hole will be burning!!! (but in a good way)

This place is seems to be family owned and operated, and they are always extreme nice.  Korean old little ladies (or ajummas) are always adorable. This place always make me happy for supporting the mom-and-pop stores.

Just get the bulgogi sandwich.  

May have had a coffee drink at one time.  Nothing spectacular, nothing terrible.  Better off going the stone's throw to Musical Offering if you want a caffeinated drink.

But seriously.  The bulgogi sandwich is delicious and always freshly made.  And I think it's made with love.  That Korean lady is super nice and friendly and always smiles at you.  Maybe it's not made with love.  Maybe it's the hopes and dreams of a united Korea.

More Berkeley kids need to know about this place to support this unknown cafe. Their bulgogi sandwich is just THAT good. Cult following right here for this thing. It's strange how I've never heard of such a concoction in my life until coming to Cal. There's jalapenos in the sandwich which gives it a kick. It's a hot sandwich with a toasted bread. The perfect bread for this sandwich! Haven't tried anything else and I don't think I want to. Hm, maybe I'll get one tomorrow! :)

They serve other hot sandwiches as well. Coffee, tea, pastries, etc. Try this place out!

One day I walked into Espresso Experience after having heard loads of good things about the bulgogi sandwich. Perfect, I cried, it holds the two culinary entities that I love the most: Korean barbecue and bread-and-cheese. Completely expecting to be floored by this marriage and having seen other customers each with two large-ish halves which I misinterpreted to be the large, I decided to order one, myself. While simultaneously wondering how Espresso Experience could charge almost five dollars for a measly half-sandwich.

Five minutes later at my little table, out come four halves of this bulgogi-bread wonder. I can feel people doing double-takes, politely trying not to look but flabbergasted at the piles of meat and carbs presented in front of lil' ol' me. A lightbulb-d'oh experience that still leaves four halves of a sandwich waiting to be consumed.

So, to my (and, I'm sure, now your) horror. I ate it. All. In that one sitting. Before rolling off to work across the street and then falling asleep in my chair at the office sometime later. There was something irresistible about this melding of East and West, but I soon discovered that though it was in part the bread, it was mostly the concept that was so alluring.

Soft, spongy, crunchy-on-the-outside grilled bun and choice of (what I think might be--has to be) provolone (could've been white American, fine) aside, this sandwich was poorly executed. I saw the beef being cooked on one of those portable griddles, slices stacked atop one another in large piles, which will lead to no browning whatsoever. The meat will just boil in the marinade, which at EE is bland, unpleasantly sour, and too black peppery. The beef is the star of this sandwich, and should shine like one! How about some char-broiling or something to get a little caramelization on these bad boys. Plus, the meat is of low quality; too much fat and gristle stays on the pieces. Traditionally, bulgogi (not galbi) does leave a little room for fat and the like, as it is prepared with less pricey cuts, but this was a bit much. I know my eating the equivalent of two sandwiches had a lot to do with it, but it was also the beef that left me feeling nauseated. Additionally, something was off about the shredded lettuce.

I'm in love with the idea of this sandwich, but not so much the item itself at Espresso Experience. I will definitely not be shelling out nine-plus dollars next time, and I'm very reluctant to try it with even 4.60. However, the location is convenient if you're around campus and they make a pretty good cappuccino. 

I'm actually fantasizing about the perfect homemade bulgogi sandwich, this time using marinated short ribs, which I happen to have in my freezer. I would chop it up like cheesesteak, sprinkle some fresh black pepper on it, lay a piece of provolone on top, stick it in the salamander until the cheese melts, and top it off with shredded lettuce (maybe blended with a little cabbage), tomatoes, and thinly-sliced, white balsamic-pickled onions and jalepeno. I just have to find some quality bread on which to smear some mayo and I'm good to go.

I'll have a steak sandwich and a . . . steak sandwich.

Soft toasted roll. Shredded lettuce. Tomato. Mayo . . . hey, is there any Bulgogi (Korean bbq'd beef) in here? Overall the bulgogi sandwich was tasty, but ultimately the smallish size and skimpy meat portion left me unfulfilled. 

By the time I thought about ordering something else a mob of 15 Korean college kids had descended on the place. I ended up grabbing a falafel sandwich at Sunrise, next door.

Food:  A-
Value:  A
Service:  B-
Decor:  Americana style cafe
Rate of Return:  Often
Best Time To Go:  anytime they're open

BULGOGI in a SANDWICH ... who would have thunk it.  It's super affordable and worth a few trips a week for a college student.  But it's definitely a must try for anyone living in or visiting the bay area.

For the first three years at Cal, I thought this place was a cafe catered to Asian people. I mean, it is, but it turns out that in Korea, cafes serve drinks AND food, unlike most cafes that specialize in drinks.

I first chanced upon this place when my friend ordered their rice cake dish. She invited me to try some, reassuring me that she had asked them not to add in anything spicy so that I could eat it. I was hesitant at first, mainly because I was sick that day, but after eating a few bites of the ricecake-egg-cabbage-pork dish, I couldn't stop eating. And what do you know, after a few minutes, I had eaten half of her food. Oops @__@

When we went back to lab, she also recommended their bulgolgi sandwich. I put it in my bucketlist, and the following semester, I whisked another friend there on a Thursday noon. Both of us ordered their bulgolgi sandwiches (total was around $14). 

After 15 minutes, our sandwiches were ready. Jalapenos and salt/pepper can be requested. We picked up our sandwiches from the counter and proceeded to satiate our appetites. The beef is well marinated, and the lettuce, tomatoes, and delicious mysterious sauce are wonderful complements. The bread is crunchy, and the serving size is just right! I seemed to enjoy my sandwich more than my friend did, but I still have to say that overall, the sandwich tasted like a superb Subway sandwich, Asianized. It was good, but not outstanding.

The cafe is right across from campus, has a good number of small tables, gets good light, and is a self-busing system. And cash only!

I used to work next door to this place, and it was a serious challenge to keep myself from grabbing a sandwich here every day. I always get the pastrami sandwich, and it's awesome!

I can't put my finger on what makes the sandwiches so great. They seem pretty mediocre on first glance... just bread and meat and iceberg lettuce... but for some reason they turn out delicious! I think it could be the bread? Whatever it is, it keeps me coming back.

The pictures of the Korean dishes look really appetizing as well, but I've never been able to work up the nerve to order any of them. I've also been meaning to try the shaved ice. It looks perfect! But, so far, I've always stuck to the sandwiches.

The woman who always takes my order (one of the owners, I assume?) is always really friendly. When I worked next door, she would remember me and remember my order, and I'm a sucker for that stuff!! =)

To Stephanie L:
You might want to do a bit more research before bashing a traditional Korean dessert that is rarely available in Berkeley.
