I don't know, maybe the fact that the cafe is owned/operated by a Korean couple, the fact that they offer Korean BBQ as a sandwich meat, AND the picture of the papingsoo (shaved ice) WITH Korean letters next to it (which is clearly visible on the store window) doesn't give a hint that it's going to be WAY DIFFERENT than your typical 10-cent Torani shot mixed into a bowl of crushed ice. Your review seems a bit too provincial for someone who's "been around the world."

Anyways, after that wall of ownage text aside, the sandwiches from this place is totally worth it. For any sandwich, there's 3 elements which attribute to its kickass-ness. 1) meat, 2) bread, 3) sauce. I've had the Bulgolgi as well as the spicy chicken sandwich, and they were easily some of the better sandwiches I've had at Berkeley. 

The owner is a nice old Korean lady (I have a penchant for nice old Korean owners), who I guess owns the place with her husband. The interior of the cafe is nice and cool; the building and lack of side windows provide an excellent shady location which is a perfect getaway from the ass-kicking heat that's been making Berkeley a literal living hell (during finals week too).

So in conclusion, don't come here if you're looking for a normal shaved ice flavored with cheap shots of artificial syrup; DO come here if you're looking for an ass-kicking sandwich (jalapenos included) that actually fills you up.

The bulgogi sandwich at Espresso Experience is an instiution. It was my post-finals celebration dish back in my college days. Even when my brothers went to Cal in the late 90's, they raved about the bulgogi sandwich. And I really think this place is one of the main reasons I eat all my sandwiches with japapenos now. Toasted roll with shredded lettuce...yeee boy

 I don't think I have ever come here for coffee, and I'm not even really sure why this place is called Espresso Experience when everybody knows what the real draw is...

The espresso isn't much of an experience - I tried it. It tastes kind of like coffee.

The bulgogi beef sandwich or the teriyaki chicken sandwich, however, are quite delicious. Imagine a Korean cheese steak and you're getting close.

They just remodeled and it looks nicer but has lost a little soul in the process. Still, cheap and delicious.
The best sandwich ever!  You'd think that in LA's K-town I'd come across a place that sells bulgogi sandwiches but no... I have to go back to Berkeley to get my fix!

My first Bulgogi Sandwich...and it was YUMMY.
Hot tasty beef, mayo (a yummy sort, i usually hate mayo), lettuce, and tomatoes sandwiched in a white deli roll. 

Other stuff here:
-Chicken Teriyaki Sandwich: Yummy! Lighter tasting than the Bulgogi. The chicken is very fresh and tender.
-Edamame: 1.25 a box! Yay!
-Potato Salad: Similarly cheap. Not bad, great portions.
-Shaved Ice: Pass on this one. It was heaping, but the quality was so-so. Not enough Adzuki beans or other toppings, and NO CONDENSED MILK. Craziness. Also, the Ice was very hard. It needed to be chipped off. Unsatisfactory.

I rediscovered this place after my first visit last year (my friend studying for a year here from Korea took me here)...and I remembered why I liked it. Bulgogi sandwich = HEAVEN. Not just the meat, but even the bread is really nicely toasted (not too crunchy, not drenched).  Now I go here at least once a week. I used to always forget it was there...because when I think of "fast food" in Berkeley, I usually think Asian Ghetto. But I'd almost rather go here now! My favorite cafe in Berkeley, hands down.

Another thing I tried recently...the ddeokbokki (the spicy rice cake). SO delicious. You'd better have desensitized taste buds though because it'll leave your mouth on fire for 10-15 minutes after...I was seriously crying by the time I got to my last bite. But it was worth every moment of pain. And also the 10 cups of water I had which caused me to have to use the restroom every 10 min after I left. :P I'll put up a picture of this tantalizing goodness!

Oh how I would have given this place 5 stars because nothing was wrong with it.  The place was clean, access to air bears, bulgogi sandwiches (gosh I love the toasted bread here) 

So I am in trying to get my usual order and ask for the bulgogi sandwich (2 to be exact) with no mayo on either one.  Needless to say, she put mayo on each one and realized she wasn't supposed to afterward.  Instead of doing what most places would do and either 

A. move the stuff to a new bun
B. make a new sandwich all together

her eyes light up and she makes the "oh no" face and proceeds to wipe off the mayo with a napkin. Lucky for her we didn't ask for no mayo for allergen reasons as there was still hints of mayo left that my friend and I were exposed toooo argggggggg! Lucky for her I let it slide that day =p

I love this place!!!! Can't believe I didn't discover it until a friend brought me here sophomore year!

This is my favorite place for dokbokki! I usually go for the dokbokki with cheese(!) since I am major weaksauce with spicy food. The cheese kind of balances out the spiciness of the sauce, but even without it, the dish isn't as spicy as other places. 

Their bulgogi sandwiches are also really good! But, I didn't really like their shaved ice. It was just okay, and it comes with these really weird gummy candies.

The people working here are always really nice! I like coming here to study during the day, since you can access Airbears, and there are a lot of outlets along the walls. They do close kind of early though (8p?).

We'd go here just for the yummy bulgogi sandwiches, with carrot sticks and jalapenos on the side, this boy and I.

We'd go for the coffee and tea drinks, this boy and I, now my boyfriend.

We'd go to snag a seat by the big windows that fold out, this boy and I, now my fiance.

We miss this place, this boy and I, now my husband.

We have had nothing but a love affair with Espresso Experience.

Last time I had a bulgogi sandwich or burger was at a McDonald's in Korea some odd years ago. You think it would be so tasty, right? Just because it's from the motherland doesn't mean anything, homie. I don't know how bulgogi can be...so square and thick, but it sure as hell was and coated in too sweet of a sauce. Well, it's McDonald's after all. But I digress.

Bulgogi should be shredded meat and should carry a balance between slightly sweet and savory pretty well. I had Espresso Experience's bulgogi sandwich today, and it hit the spot, especially after a squash match. Yes! I defeat the purpose of working out by gorging immediately after. Who's with me?

Anyway, the bread was perfectly toasted. The bulgogi itself was good except I wish they had added a little more to the sandwich. But overall, with the jalapenos to kick up the spiciness, I was very content. I also got to score some points by conversing with the kind ahjuma (lady) who actually knew what the hell squash was. Hey, I gotta brush up on my Korean. I'll be sure to come here more often for lunch.

Oh, how I miss the bulgogi sandwich.  $5 for a mouthwatering mound of sweet Korean barbequed beef on a crunchy roll.  Sweet baby Jesus I just had Christmas dinner but I want this now.  It's a little on the small side, but what it lacks in size it makes up for in taste.  I came to this place to study in my college days and they were always nice to me, probably because they knew me and I gave them a decent amount of business by bringing dozens of friends here throughout the years.

I went back a few months ago and it looks like they've got new ownership, but I think they've carried on the same tradition of great customer service and good quality food.

Who's coming with me next time?

Cute little cafe! The bulgogi sandwich was better than I expected, because honestly "bulgogi" sounds like it's gonna taste like feces or worse. Rest assured, you're in for a great lunch. The cafe is cute and in a convenient location and the sandwich is less than $5. As others, I really liked the bread. No complaints, give this place a try!

Oh man these bulgogi sandwiches are so good that i want these things in my mouth at all times.

So here's the bulgogi-sandwich-eating-experience breakdown:
-first bite:  toasted bread, bite of lettuce and tomato, hint of the bulgogi that's about to amaze you, thinking "man I hope this sandwich is worth the hype"
-second bite:  "ok this is good, but I'm not sure if it's as amazing as yelp says"
-third to almost last bite: start to take bigger bites, eat a little faster than normal, stop talking to anyone because that means bulgogi is not in your mouth
-last bite:  "oh crap there's no more sandwich" and commence to order another sandwich

I'm serious.  Every single time I get this sandwich, I go through each and every one of these steps.  Especially the last one.  I can't think of how many times I ordered another sandwich simply because I didn't want to ever stop eating it.

Thai Basil was my enjoyable sustenance through my freshmen year at Cal. I must admit, that I probably ate at Thai Basil several times each week with my friends. Given Cal Dining's atrocious food, I relied on Thai Basil to keep me alive through the course of the semester. Heck, my friends even hassled me quite often about my desire to eat at this restaurant.

However good the food at Thai Basil may be, I've decided that upon entering my second year at Berkeley, I must end this love-hate relationship with the most popular Thai restaurant conveniently located in the colloquial "Asian Ghetto."

My go to dishes at Thai Basil are/were the basil eggplant chicken, with a fried egg on top. My friend Matt and I would literally order this for a month straight. I also like their Pad Thai - it's not like most pad thais in the Bay Area, but if I'm eat here, I'm probably going to order this. It's not as sweet as most pad thai's, which I like. Also, their combination basil fried rice is good, but I recommend that you only order it when they're not busy! And this brings me to my next point: the service/timeliness of receiving my food.

I normally order my food to-go, and I do realize that Thai Basil is one of the most popular restaurants in Berkeley, but I've had to wait too long (time which could have been used studying!) and have had too many orders mixed up/messed up. It can be frustrating when the food comes out literally 40 minutes after you order. 

If I want Thai Basil, I'll be sure to come here at the waning hours of the night, or mid-afternoon, when they're not as busy. The food's good, but it just can be a headache when I'm waiting an absurdly long time for the food...

If you're in berkeley and in the mood for Thai this is where I would go in addition to Berkeley Thai House. I love their basil chicken dish and pineapple curry with white rice, it's delicious! They complete and cook orders really fast however there are times when this place is too crowded. I usually call ahead to order so I can just skip the wait. The prices are reasonable which is expected as they are so close to a UCB college campus so they cater more to the students. An entree with soda is about $7.50 (tax included). Overall, I come back and have a meal here at least once a month for over a year now.

I love Thai Basil. I can definitely assure you that they have the best Thai food in Berkeley. Also, the food is fairly cheap for students. Usually 6-8 dollars for an order and the portion is really big.  But during lunch or dinner time, the waiting can be really long. So definitely call ahead time if you know what you want. During school year, they have this lunch special thing. Basically, they have 4 items as lunch special every day. You can pick 3 of them. The lunch specially portion is usually bigger than the regular order, but for the same price. Definitely worth it.

It has been nearly two years since I left Berkeley, but nearly every time I'm in town I still come here for an easy meal.

For one thing, it's cheap. You'll get a very full meal for under $8. You'll save even more if you go for the lunch specials during the weekdays, but you won't be getting any less in portion.

It's really a great thing for college students who want to spend a few bucks for a very flavorful meal. My favorites are the Basil Chili Chicken (#4 on the menu, I believe) and the Pepper Garlic Steak.

The Thai Iced Tea here is not to shabby either.

The reason I'm only giving it three stars is because the quality of the food has also gone down over the years. Lunch specials were fine when I was a student, but for some reason they now taste like leftovers that weren't microwaved properly. It may just be me.

Some of the dishes are also rather salty, and the wait can be a little annoying during peak hours.

It's still a good place to visit if you go to school around here; heck, I'm sure I'll be back again some day.

I suppose the best thing about this place is its location.  It's close to other eateries and to campus.  The food is decent thai food.  downside is that you come out smelling like food - never a good thing in my book.  there are better thai places around campus (for the same price) - but for lazybums like me, the ghetto is the way to go.

I still have not found a pad Thai that I love more than Thai Basil's, I think its  something about their sauce.  

Its great for a quick meal to go, or to eat in the restaurant while sipping on some of their free tea.

Full disclosure, I am writing this review based on my experiences as a student at Cal.  I believe a lot of my love is out of nostalgia but I still enjoy going, even when I visit.  

For the price I think its great Thai food.

Tip - Call your orders in ahead of time! Simply calling in and getting your order in as you walk there from your house/apartment/dorm/people's park cuts down on the inevitably long wait you normally face. 

My favorite is the Pineapple Curry Chicken - the perfect combo of sweet and spicy with a healthy serving of white rice to pour it all over. Every time I order it I say i'm gonna save half for later, and every time without fail I find myself polish off every grain of rice.

Very average Thai food but they have a lot of options. I would recommend the pad see ew / pad kee mao over the pad thai. The pad thai noodles are  tough. The thai iced tea is good here. The panang curry isn't bad either. Expected bill is $7-$8.

Widely popular with UCB students so don't come here if you're looking to get away from the younger crowd.

I seriously have not written a review for this place yet?? 4 years later, here it is..I love this place. Wanna get stuffed on less than $8...go here. they have vegetarian options..SCORE! You order at the front, pay cash only, grab some free tea (i mix it with water cause the tea is super hot and will melt the plastic cup)...and wait for your order number! I'm a fan! The -1 star is because when they get swamped, it can take up to 40 minutes to get your food and the lunch "3 items" taste like a day old...otherwise, I'm a total fan!

Thai Basil is probably the best overall spot for Thai food in Berkeley. During my four years there, I've had a lot of Thai food from all around Berkeley. A lot of my friends always like to meet up here for dinner because we know how epic the Thai food here is. 

I like Thai basil because the prices are fair (on the lower side), the food is delicious and flavorful, and the Thai Tea here is also pretty awesome. 

I like the pad thai here a lot. It has a delicate mixture of flavor, texture, and moistness. I have experienced wet, sloppy and disgusting pad thai that makes you feel like having the runs. There ain't none of that here. It's always made to perfection.

In conclusion, I venture out to try new places a lot and somehow always find myself back at the origin of my Thai food pleasure- Thai Basil! It's like the Beatles... no matter how much you like these new pop songs, those will get old, and you will always go back to the Beatles.

I know the daughter of the owner of this place.  For the amount of food, I miss this place since the price is right.  It's always packed so you know that it's good or at least decent enough!  I always got the pad thai J...no clue why it's a J since it's the vegetarian version of the pad thai.  They also ask you if you want Egg or No Egg..and the lady there's cute when she says the order.  Good place to get cheap food.  Just don't get anything with peanut sauce...it's literally peanut butter melted *yuck*
the vegetarian pad see ew (w/egg) here is my favorite thai dish ANYWHERE. that it comes from a little mom-n-pop getup makes it even better!
Pepper garlic chicken!

For the last four years of my life, Thai Basil has deserved 4 stars. But I just went back for the last time and found out that they've downgraded the quality of ... just about everything.

The pad thai sauce is redder and tastes crappier than the old orange-colored stuff. Even the questionable meat got more questionable. The yellow chicken curry has also been watered down, and (maybe it's just me) now you get more carrots and potatoes than chicken. I am really disappointed because this was the best place in the Asian Ghetto hands down.

What's the point of the huge portions (yeah, I made two meals out of my $8 fried rice) if you can't wrap your mind around finishing the second half?

At least the pineapple fried rice is still decent.

This place is great! I especially love the peppers they have for customers to self serve (so crunchy and delicious, yumyum) -- the main reason I come here. Good Thai food (affordable/cheap).

I'd say the peppers are what make the food here go from "decent" to "great." Would buy the peppers alone if they sold them to customers.

I have tried many of their items from eggplant curry, pra rama, pad-sew, to pad mein (spell check) and all their dishes are flavorful. I have had better thai ice tea, but in terms of the food items, it's really flavorful.

If you don't mind the long line and wait, then by all means! Price is ok, considering it's in Berkeley. The only thing I didn't like is that they don't serve the crushed peanuts in a cup as they do for the spices. Other Thai restaurants do this, so I felt it was cheap.

The Thai BBQ with fried rice is where it's at. Haven't really tried their other meals, because I still haven't gotten tired of the #2 combo. It's just so damn good.

Oh, and by the way, they don't accept credit cards--only cash, so make sure sure you're carrying at least $10 when you walk in, or you're going to regret walking back out.

This is my top place for Thai food in Berkeley, it's much better than Thai Noodle in my perspective.  The classic Pad Thai is tasty, so as other Thai dishes served with steamed rice.

One thing that's not so good about this place is the environment.  It's located in one of the food courts around the campus area, which makes it noisy and hot.  It could be a very good choice if you just want to grab lunch quickly though.

Love this place. This place is cheap, quick, and easy to get to.  I always ended up eating here when I visit Berkeley friends or go thrift shopping. My friends and I usually order 4 dishes and split the remainder as we usually cannot make up our minds on what we want to eat. Definitely a hole in the wall kinda ambiance, but that does not mean they are lacking in flavor. The pineapple fried rice, thai fried rice, pad kea mow, pad thai, pad see ew, tom yum soup are all great, but the best dish here has to be the fried red sauce fish (not sure what the correct name is, will update this review) the sauce is tender, sweet, and spicy. I have dreams about this sauce!

This rule applies to most restaurants at the Asian Ghetto. Asian Ghetto= cheap, greasey, not that great food; with Thai Basil as one of the few exceptions (along with D'Yar). They actually make some pretty delicious pad thai and curry here that isn't too greasey. I recommend eating at the restaurant if you can rather than getting your food to go because I noticed that you get significantly less food. Sometimes the line is really long at lunch time and the food can take a really long time. If you're in a rush to go back to class or something, Thai Basil might not be a good idea because its so popular..

Out of the all places in the "asian ghetto" this is probably the best and the long lines and ridiculous wait times say it all.  It is fairly inexpensive and the food is always hot, never sits around (unless you get the lunch specials because all that shit is premade)

Their hot thai tea is pretty good and its free.  Seating is typical for a Berkeley place, pretty small but enough to accommodate a good amount of people.  I used to come here all the time and if I were still going to Cal, i'd probably go here still, love itttt.  Doesn't deserve a 4 star rating though.

Pros:
-Great for Vegetarians
-HUGE Menu Variety
-Good Price
-Authentic

Cons:
-Cash Only
-Lack of Seating
-Poor Service
-Long Wait time
-Crowded
-Smelly
-If you're allergic to seafood, dont eat here. Pans get reused, and sanitiaton is a bit of a flag.

Overall I LOVE Thai Basil!

yummm! i ordered pad thai and liked it, but not loved it.


over time, the flavor was too overpowering and couldn't stand to eat the rest.

but it was very fresh and temperature-hot!

A good regular place to have lunch or pick up dinner.  Their Pad Thai is the Pad Thai my boyfriend judges all other Pad Thais against.  It's not dirt cheap, but it's not overly pricey.  They have an extensive menu and you don't have to wait long to get our food.  And it's close, and always open.  Good Thai for white-people-students  who may not have the highest standards.  : )

Only came by to order the Tom Kha Gai because it was 12AM and I was still cold from the Ice Cream from Cream.

A little lemony and tiny for $5. Definitely nothing I would be tempted to get again. Also they don't serve Papaya Salad... Not a great way to find out. Open really late hours though so that is nice.

When the boyfriend asked to have Steve's BBQ again (read my review), I passed & went next door for some Thai since he won't eat it with me.

I ordered my usual - Pad Kee Mow with chicken.  The portion is pretty big but there is plenty of chicken so it's not just a plate of noodles with a couple pieces of meat on top like I've had @ other places.  What I like most about the dish though, is the good amount of spice.  I've had Pad Kee Mows @ other places before & none of them have been spicy; & it is supposed to be spicy!  So thank you, Thai Basil, for doing it right.

Every time I've been here it's been busy.  Even still, service is usually pretty quick & I think that it is even quicker if you get your order to-go.  This place is definitely much less glamorous than som other Thai restaurants in the nearby area.  But if you don't care about that stuff, then you should give this little hole-in-the-wall a try.

The food is over-seasoned - usually too much pepper and too much salt. That would normally lend itself to maybe two or three stars, but what really dropped it down to one star was that the cashier purposely overcharged me for adding extra noodles. The register read $9.25, and the cashier told me it was $10 when I stood there waiting for my change.

Thai Basil is one of my go-to places in the Asian Ghetto (the others being Bear Ramen and Viet Nam Village). The service is a bit hit-or-miss probably due to its popularity, but the food is pretty consistently decent. Value-wise, you don't get as much food for what you pay as you do at the other places in Asian Ghetto.

The specials here tend to be pretty good. My favorite dish here is still the Pad See-Ew.
Love this place! I highly recommend  their Thai BBQ & fried rice. Prices are very affordable and portions are huge. Also, great location for UC berkeley students!

Cheap, convenient Thai food.  It's definitely the best Thai food around for the cheapskates like myself, and it's one of my favorites in the Durant food court.

I've probably had a half-dozen other dishes here, but Basil Fried Rice is my regular.  Very flavorful and a generous quantity.  I've ordered it countless times and enjoyed it immensely every time.

Their pad see ew is pretty good, and you get a decent portion compared to other places that charge about $2 more, but for significantly less. 

Close to school!

I LOVED this place when I was in college. Super cheap Thai food that is pretty tasty.  I loved how they have the menu on the wall with pictures to help you decide.  Honestly, its not that great of quality, but when you are broke in college, quality isn't exactly your first concern.  I loved getting togo from here on my way home from class. Their pad thai was my favorite :)

The best Pad See Ew I've ever had. For that alone, I come back over and over again. I haven't experienced long waits for take out food like others have mentioned and I've been a frequent patron since 2007. So there are no complaints from me in that department. My only complaint is that their servings are getting smaller and smaller.

 I order pad see ew most times I come here but once in awhile I like to venture out and try different things. Here's my recap of other dishes:

1. Pra Rama Chicken- YUM! better than tuktuk's pra rama chicken.
2. Pad Thai- I've had better and elsewhere. When I had this, I was disappointed and wished I ordered Pad See Ew.
3. Yellow Curry- Good. not the best I've ever had but it will suffice if you're craving curry.
4. Garlic Pepper Chicken- Hit and Miss.. sometimes the chicken is too dry or too salty.
5. Tom Yum Gai- Mediocre/ Good, If you feel like soup on a cold day. Don't expect too much because it's not exceptional. More mediocre than good.

Overall, if you're going to come here, try out the Pad See Ew and Pra Rama chicken. They're the most solid dishes here.

THEY ONLY TAKE CASH!  

That would be my number one tip about Thai Basil.  Luckily, BoA and Wells Fargo are both right down the street if you need to withdraw.  Food-wise, it's delicious, well-priced, and large servings.  I always get the pad-se-ew (sorry for the atrocious spelling) or the fried rice. 

Overall:  good food! It's probably not the healthiest, but still delish.  Downsides: CASH CASH CASH (I always forget that) and they take a painfully long time to give you your food.  That being said, I think it's worth it.  But if you're famished, you're better off going somewhere else with faster service.

Oh man, Thai Basil has some bomb food.

The food always tastes great, and the price is set right for any college student, which means its right for the working class too. Everything I've ordered here has been pretty good, except one thing: the tom yum. I wasn't pleased with their soup at all, but everything else is right on.

good service + good food + good price = good times.

The pad see ew here is very good. I also like getting the curry chicken and the pineapple curry. The prices have gone up over the years, which sucks :(  

Also, the wait time is long and it gets so crowded in here but that's because the dishes here are all very yummy, and in reasonable portions! You also get free tea and water. I recommend this place for all students because it's so close to campus and it's very convenient to where everyone needs to go!

I think one of the biggest reasons why I'm against this place is their service. They servers/owners are VERY RUDE! Not only do they literally throw your food on the counter if you dare ask for a napkin or a fork they give it to you with such a horrible attitude. 
The quality of the food goes up and down. Sometimes it's great and sometimes its not. The last time I went I got PAD See EW which is one of there most popular dishes and one dish I get almost every single time i come. This time it was horrible. It tasted weird....as if they mixed some other spices in it or cooked it in a unwashed pan(from another dish). Anyway I tried to bring it back and they yelled at me saying that that was what I ordered. It was not until my much braver sister went up there once again to demand that they make me another one did they take my order back. The looks they were giving me were scary!

I prefer Racha's cafe on telegraph! The prices are similar and the service is much better. Also the dishes seem like someone put more time into them! Definitely compare and see for yourself! 

However...at the end of the day I've had thai basi many many many times. It is definitely not the worst place you could go. I just am now appalled by it because of my previous experience. Dont think i'll be coming back for a while. Good luck!

Came here again the other day. Service was just as slow. Friend ordered the yellow curry I believe, and I had the Thai noodle soup. He liked his curry. My noodle soup on the other hand had WAYYYY too much flavor. It was like you're slurping on a mouth full of spices. YUCK. I had my friend try it also, and he didn't like it either.

Um yeah, next time I think I'm going to stick to Thai foods that I know and have eaten before. XD

this place is GREAT for their BASIL FRIED RICE...or their 2 or 3 item lunch special - which usually includes pad thai

- 1 star cuz the prices have risen since my freshmen year (more than a 10 percent increase BOO)

They have the best Pad Kee Mow I've ever eaten. The rest of their food is average. But, I will say it one more time because it deserves recognition for people whole like spicey noodles like myself: Best Pad Kee Mow ever...

Out of all the places I go to in the Asian Ghetto, I always end up here. This place is definitely great Thai food on the cheap for those late nights wandering around Berkeley with the wallet of a college student. Plus, I was drawn to the "People Love Us on Yelp" sticker. That's always a nice thing to see.

I'm a fan of Thai food and although this is not the best Thai food you will ever have, it is pretty good for the price you're paying. The place is small and on busy days or nights, you'll have trouble finding a seat in there. The service is okay. They definitely give off that "I'm just here to take your order and give it to you" kind of attitude. No time for small talk. Well, that's alright. I'm just here to eat. I usually order pad see ew or pad thai, which I highly recommend. It's safe to say that dish is the clear favorite for everyone.

So if you're having a Thai food craving and need your fix, you should stop over here. Nothing says happy like a college student with a full stomach.

Food is good.  This place made me fall in love with Thai food.  Quite possibly the most overpriced food in the Asian Ghetto--every other place is about $5, and this place is like $7 (huge difference for brokeass college students).  Always got the eggplant when I did go here.  Berkeley has plenty of Thai places.  If you have a car, make the drive to Tuk Tuk Thai on Shattuck.

Very traditional Thai flavors in decent portions at an acceptable price.  This place screams mediocre at me, but maybe its because I'm spoiled by all the good thai food in southern cali.  Sure they are great at cooking it, but the food here seems rather inconsistent from time to time.  Some days my pad thai will arrive perfectly cooked, while other days it tastes overdone and dry.  For a little more money, I would definitely recommend Racha Thai on Telegraph.
This place is extremely reliable and cheap.  I love their garlic dishes.  It's no Chez Panisse, but if you want cheap, relatively fast, and tasty Thai food, this is your place.

Thai basil is my favorite place to get pad see ew (~$7). I've tried it at other thai places in the area - tuk tuk thai, berkeley thai house, cha am - but I can't get enough of their pad see ew at Thai Basil.

All of the other food is alright, it's pretty greasy and unhealthy for you in general, but if you don't care and are looking for a fast and moderately priced thai restaurant, go here.

Definitely one of my most-visited places during my freshman year at Berkeley. I think eating here a lot played a small part in me gaining my freshman 10. I usually got Pad Thai, but then a friend of mine introduced me to Pad-See-Ew, and I've been stuck on that ever since. I'm definitely not a vegetable type of person, so I normally order Pad-See-Ew with no broccoli. Prices are a bit steep for the portions that they give you, but I've been very satisfied every time I eat here. Definitely a must-try if you're ever in Berkeley.

If you live in the dorms on southside, thai basil is a godsend for oily thai food. I loved it. Prices were a lot lower back in the day, but yeah... 

Whenever I met up with friends at the asian ghetto and we'd all disperse to buy our meals, I always found myself siding with thai basil. It's just so easy to eat and way, way flavorful. I tried too many dishes to remember, but I do remember liking everything. So, you're pretty safe with every dish.

Decent thai tea. Lots of employees are teo-chew (YAY). Kind of a long wait if you go during rush hours, which is really annoying if you're a really hungry and cranky college student.

Cheap Thai food.  It's quick and the lunch special--3 assortments of dishes for lunch (out of 4 that they have prepared) is a really good deal, especially if you're in a hurry because since it's pre-prepared, all you have to do is tell them which ones you want.  If you go for dinner, I've heard that the combination fried rice is really good, and pineapple fried rice is really good too.  The pad thai always tastes ketchup-y to me, but it's decent, and their garlic basil eggplant (or something like that) is really good.

Overall, not too bad. Again, this is coming from someone who is not that crazy about Thai food. However, I have to admit their TOM YUM KHA soup is pretty good. I'm certainly not a regular at Thai Basil, but when I do come here I usually only eat one dish.

I have tried their lunch specials where you get to choose I think it was 2 or 3 different items plus rice and they were all pretty mediocre. To be frank, if you want a combo rice plate China Express is a much better and cheaper choice.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
TOM YUM KHA

Good friends, good food, ENJOY!

I come here constantly for Pad Thai! Just be sure that you (and your friends) have cash on hand; I've spotted people on more than one occasion.

The lines do get long occasionally, but I think it's worth the wait. Haven't gotten any "bad thai" yet!
I love love love their food here.  The prices are great too.  I recommend the #4 which is Chicken with bell peppers and onions sauteed with chili garlic sauce.  YUMMMY!!!

This place has THE BEST Pad See Ew (sp?), hands down. However, the serving size has gotten smaller over the past few semesters, therefore it loses one star in our rating. 

But nevertheless, the food is just way too good--and it is definitely worth the wait. But then again, we have only tried the Pad See Ew and Pad Thai. (For those of you in Vallejo: It's even better than Cha-am.)

Happy Eatings!

I am a fourth year at UC Berkeley and have been coming here even before then, but my last visit will definitely be my LAST visit. I came here before because it is very close by to campus and the food is pretty decent but good customer service is very important to me---and this is NOT the place to find it. 

Sunday evening, I ordered the pad thai dish for sit in and when I got my dish I noticed a strand of hair INSIDE of my noodles. It had to be PULLED out, which definitely meant that it wasn't mine. None the less, I was not trying to be rude or difficult. I understand that these things are inevitable since I myself used to work at a restaurant setting. I only asked to have my dish remade. When I told one of the male chefs that I found a strand hair in my dish, he took the dish back but didn't say anything to me. They remade the dish, and I went to the counter to pick it up. Then the lady that gave it to me gave me a dirty look and pointed at me, and said "That was YOUR hair!" Mind  you, my hair was tied up and I noticed the strand in my dish right when I sat down. She made a very big deal out of something very minor. I did not eat the pad thai. I left with no refund because I was very upset.

BAD SERVICE should never be tolerated. I will not come back.

This is one of my favorite places for Thai that's fast food. It's cooked to order so there's a bit of a wait, and they're usually always busy, too. If you get the special combo plate, you get to pick 3 of the 4 or 5 items and I don't recommend this. I like variety but I appreciate freshness and quality first so I usually get my usual which is the chicken pad-see-ew, yellow curry (comes with rice) or the pepper chicken. All of the items are DELICIOUS!!

decent thai food. there are plenty of other places with better pad thai so i wouldn't recommend it here. the basil tofu is nice.  
but it's not worth the long wait during lunchtime.

the upside is they don't require $10 minimum order for credit card payments.

I'm not a student at Berkeley, but years ago when I visited Berkeley to see if I wanted to go to this school, I won't lie: I almost chose to go to Berkeley over UCLA just for this place.

The first thing I tried here was the Pad Thai, and to this day, I've never found a Thai food place that does Pad Thai the way that I like it except Thai Basil. It's not the healthiest, but when you want that quick Thai fix, nothing hits the spot more than this place. I've tried a few other dishes here, but I'd have to say that my absolute favorite is the Pad Thai.

The food is super cheap, and a super short walk for students and visitors of the Berkeley campus. I tried finding parking near the Asian Ghetto, but I found that it's much easier to just walk there.

I'm a Southern California resident, but I find myself craving Thai Basil all the time. Every time I visit Berkeley, which is about a 2-3 times a year, I always make sure to stop by Thai Basil to get my fix.

If you see a long line, don't go. I love this place, the Pad Thais is delicious, the Chicken Chow Fun is delicious. Everything there tastes good. If there's a line though, expect them to get your order and wait a loooong time. It could be 10 minutes, I've waited up to 45 minutes, and it can get even longer.

But it is delicious, it is cheap, and it's worth it if you have something to do while waiting.

I've eaten at so many Thai restaurants in Berkeley, and honestly Thai Basil is still the best. The quality hasn't changed since I was a first year at Cal, but the prices are a bit higher now. 

My go to dishes are Pad See Ew, yellow curry, and pineapple fried rice. I pretty much order one of these whenever I go to a Thai restaurant and Thai Basil is the place that cooks it the most flavorful and most consistently.

The wait is ridiculously long now (20 min +), so avoid this place if you're looking for a quick bite.

Really folks! the Thai food is basic, nothing special. I suggest you read the other reviews more closely, as some folks are clearly clueless about Thai food. One guy wrote it was the "Best Thai food in Berkeley" which is, well, absurd. There is excellent Thai food in Berkeley and this place is does not have it. Plates average $8.00, add brown rice $1.50 and tip and well it's "inexpensive" but ah not worth the "lower" cost. And DO NOT bring a date here, but you probably knew that already. For clueless UCB kids maybe this place works, can't figure it but...

Thai Basil, you're getting demoted to two stars for cash only, because seriously, fuck that.  The only reason I put up with your bitchy staff and mediocre food is because you're convenient, and now that you've made yourselves MUCH less convenient I've got yet another reason to take my business elsewhere.

Nice item, does what it says.  Got the BBQ pork rice plate.  Good portion and price is right at $7.25 with tax.  I would have liked to have a little garnishment of some kind, like shredded carrot, bit of lettuce, or some cucumber as I am accustomed to, but even without it, it's a fine dish and were I in this area more often, this establishment would make it into my normal rounds.

I understand the reasons for coming here during late night affairs in college. It gets old fast though...

+Quick food
- Pad thai, noodles, and other rice dishes are way too oily n' greasy
- Place is not well kept

Final Call:
Those into Americanized Thai will enjoy the grub here.

--------------------

Munched on:
1. Pineapple fried rice
     -  Not enough pineapple, overkill on grease
2. Pad Thai (veggie and chicken)
     -  What happened to the veggies and chicken??

3.5 stars

we stumbled upon this place. the pad thai was super. the prices were just right, similar to the other joints in durant square. we missed the lunch special cuz it was cal's spring break; 3 or 4 items for $4.60.

can't wait to go back to try the other dishes.

3.5 stars

Good portions for your money but not the best Thai food I've had. Gets pretty warm and toasty in there, with all the people. I came in around lunchtime on a regular weekday. I got the spicy pad see ew and it was the perfect spiciness.

One of the better places in Asian ghetto in terms of food quality. The service is slow, and they always seem to argue with each other, but the entrees are well made compared to its neighbors in the area. I like the yellow curry and the basil chicken fried rice (the latter's portion is huge).

The first time I had Thai Basil was when I was a sophomore in high school. I had their Pad Thai and liked it a lot. This place is very convenient if you live on Southside, like I do. You can always count on going in for a quick meal. I have to agree with other Yelp reviewers; rush hour can be very annoying since the lines are long and the wait can be cumbersome. I remember waiting once for about 30 minutes before getting my food. 

Nowadays, the prices are higher, the portions are smaller, and the quality of food seems to be going downhill. Back about 3 years ago, it used to be better. It just seems like a fast-food joint now. Don't get me wrong, you can still get good quality Thai food here, but if you're in the Berkeley area, there are definitely other places worth trying. 

Personal favorite dishes include: Pad Thai (of course), Pad Kee Mao, and Satay chicken (just don't get this particular dish to-go because the peanut sauce can be quite messy). I've never had their Thai Tea before but I heard it's okay, not too amazing or anything.

Some popular dishes: Pad See Ew, Pad Thai, Pineapple Fried Rice, Combination Fried Rice, Pineapple Curry Chicken, and Basil Chili Chicken. But they also have this numberless dish called Pra Rad Prik which consists of fried fish with a delicious sauce over it, served with rice. Would recommend trying it. 

One of the yummier restaurants in Asian Ghetto, but just mediocre for Thai food. It sucks because they're cash only now, and the wait for food tests your patience when hungry.

I came here quite a bit my freshman year but didn't return until yesterday.  Now I realize why.  The food here just doesn't compare to the other Thai restaurants in the area.  If you go to West side or walk down a bit more on Telegraph, you'll experience better Thai food. 

I ordered the veggie pad thai; and it was burned.  =T Maybe this was a one time thing, but they should have at least made me a new batch when tofu and vegetable pieces were 3/4 covered in charcoal.  Not coming back here again...

Cheap, decent portions, but slow service

I usually go for spicy eggplant chicken or pad see-ew, but their noodles smell like urine... it's really strange.

My very first Pad Thai. A mentor took me and my sister here to try it and we loved it. Since then, whenever I am on telegraph and craved Thai, I would go here. No other Pad Thai that I had ever tried tasted was \ as good as this one. The Pad Se Ew is also the thing to order; there is just more flavor in these dishes here than anywhere else.
Services: You get into a line, order your food, hold on to a ticket, wait for them to call your number and pick  it up at the left side of the cashier. 

They take only cash (bummer huh)  but they do have an atm machine inside(which I think going to the bank would save you some money!). They also offer free hot thai tea to eat with your food.

Space wise: Not the biggest. very crowded usually and packed. 
However, I don't mind  the space if I can get the best Pad Thai in the Bay Area!

My favorite here is the chicken and eggplant in the garlic chili sauce.  They serve the eggplant the way I like it, soft enough to fall apart.  I also come in to get my Thai iced tea fix.  I may be a bit biased because it's only a couple doors from my apartment (sheesh, half the staff lives in my apartment), and my club likes to take over a few tables late at night after practice.  Good food, good price.

this is based on memory but the pad thai, pad see ew, pineapple fried rice, and basil fried rice were all pretty bomb. the wait is long, but i was usually here with friends so it didn't matter all that much.
i waited 20 minutes and find EGGSHELLS in my pad see ew?! ridiculous.

how can i say no to cheap thai food across the street from campus? 

i've been here plenty of times but never felt the need to yelp about it. but then thai basil was put to the test ......and they passed! 

noon rush hour, super hungry, credit card machine breaks down, no cash. =(

i sadly walked my brink of starvation stomach to BOA to get some cash, and while i was contemplating just going to another restaurant that ACCEPTED my plastic, i opted to still go to thai basil because when my heart (or rather my stomach) is set on something, it's set. 

i waited in the line that stretched outside the door (AGAIN) impatiently and as i got to the front and the cashier gave me my change, i looked at her and asked her if the credit card machine was fixed. she immediately apologized, switched out my number and gave me a lower one and said that my food would be right up which made me extremely happy!

LUNCH SPECIAL... $5.75 with up to 3 items!!!! while the items you can choose from are fixed it's still an extraordinary deal!

I come here every single time I go to Berkeley. Their Pad Kee Mow is to die for. I've tried other dishes here and they're not so great. If it weren't for the Pad Kee Mow, I'd probably stay away from here. The portion is a little small, but I'm kind of a big eater, so don't be too worried about it. Overall a good place to come for a cheap thai dinner that will leave your tastes buds somewhat satisfied.

Mmmm! I love their pad mod kaew, extra spicy! Absolutely delish.

it's a large portion, and for $7.50, it's not that bad of a deal.

The only downside, however, was that this place only takes cash. Boo. I'll still give it five stars.
My favorite restaurant in the Ghetto food court when I used to go to Cal!  Everything on the menu is nice and spicy!

Everything I order here fills me up and is delicious to the point of me wanting to give the old people who run the joint a hug. Curry = bomb. Chicken = savory. Tofu = like eggs but better! Eggs = like eggs but better too. 

ONE ISSUE.... CASH ONRY! Darn you... oh well, guess I have to jog to the ATM and spend an extra $3 to pull out a $twenty. On a serious point..., you gotta love Berkeley

I like Thai Basil although I seem to forget about it a lot. It is good for those random Thai food cravings, especially if you're looking for something quick and cheap. Had it tonight and got the pad thai and combo fried rice. It is good but I can't say it's the best Thai I have ever had. They have good portions and the price is definitely worth it!

I was craving Thai in the Asian Ghetto and I finally decide to give Thai Basil a try. I figured, I had basically tried everything else in the Asian Ghetto, why not get some Thai here?

I ended up getting the spicy basil chicken with rice. While I do prefer a lot more spice and a lot more basil, it was still pretty good. It didn't hit the wallet too bad so I really couldn't complain. Thai Basil is pretty cheap in the first place and what I ordered happened to be one of the cheapest on the menu. The food came quickly, there was plenty of space to sit (a rarity in this place), and the food was really good. 

How can I complain?

Have I really never reviewed Thai Basil?  What's wrong with me!  

So, Thai Basil has done a serious about face since the first time I went.  Four years ago a trip to Thai Basil was akin to a voyage into your local dive bar only with really tasty food.  The menu was sort of haphazardly thrown on the wall and the whole place felt trashily cozy, if perhaps a little unsanitary.

The new and improved Thai Basil is just what I would hope for in an upgrade: fresh new digs, but the same old tasty (if greasy) food.  Now Thai Basil is the pride of the "Asian Ghetto" (I know, sounds kind of racist to me too.)  

Don't leave without trying the cashew nut chicken.  I'm hungry just thinking about it.  I love this place and will continue to eat here so long as my arteries will allow it.  

Oh, and they definitely DO accept credit cards and always have.  I don't know why so many people voted that they didn't.

My friends and I rolled here for a quick bite before heading to the city.  Durant food court is convenient and the variety of food works out well if you have a group of folks.  It offers not only a variety of food, but such a assortment of smells:delicious food, bad homeless people stench and trash if you're lucky enough to get a table outside.

Thai Basil has ample indoor seating.  I got the BBQ pork over a generous tray of rice.  They were stingy with the sweet and sour dipping sauce though.  Having spent the prior 3 hours in a vegan zone, the meat hit the spot.  It's cool (and somewhat depressing) to visit these old stomping grounds when my metabolism was so much faster and my wallet so much thinner.
An hour and about 6 cups of water later, my mouth still feels dry and stale from all the MSG in my pad thai.

OBSESSION! OMG they definitely have my favorite basil tofu ever! the food is made so quickly and tastes amazing...and it's all for such cheap prices. i don't go to Berkeley very often, but when I do it seems that this is the only place I end up eating each time.

My Go-To place in the Asian ghetto when I want a good, quality-consistent meal thats not super expensive. 

I really recommend their Combination Fried Rice and their Pad See Ew, as well as their Basil chicken. However, their Pad Thai is a bit on the dry side. Lunch specials that I've tried are usually hit or miss, so I tend to always get the same things.

This place usually has good business, and they provide free tea/water. A good place for students getting takeout or enjoying a quick meal, but not very good atmosphere.

Long wait, but pretty good thai. The pineapple curry is AMAZING - definitely recommend getting that. It's sweet but somehow spicy and fruity, all together! the ginger chicken isn't half bad either, but nothing phenomenal. For the prices, it's a good deal on thai food. the wait can be excruciating, so be prepared.

Im not always crazy about Thai food but this place was very good.  It can get a little crowded inside but the cheap food is worth the wait.  The menu is set up with pictures so those people unfamiliar with Thai food can pick and choose quickly.  Careful of the lunch rush here as a line can form out the door quickly.  This place has won numerous awards in Berkeley for their outstanding food.  Check them out in the Food Court and enjoy!

Yeah, I'd say the rating distribution for this one is pretty much on the dot.

The food is good, but you could find better Thai at other places around Berkeley. The wait can be pretty bad, even if you beat peak hours. The portions can be somewhat small if you come around lunch. 

But like I said, the food is good. I've tried the pad thai, pad see ew, pad kee mow, pineapple fried rice, and the basil chili chicken. All of them were good, particularly the pad kee mow.

For me, a bit pricey for lunch (ranges b/t $7-$15), but definitely a good plate of yummy goodness. I got their green curry chicken, but next time I am going to try the pineapple curry. 

* Random blurb *

I was light weight disappointed that I called my order in ahead of time (about 15 mins), but by the time I got to Thai Basil to pick up my food they said they never got my phone order!! LOL. It's all good though. The wait wasn't that long.

To Hubert H.

I'm a friend with the owner and her family and trust me, the owner did NOT want to increase the price. Her family members had to force her to increase the prices due to the increase in rent and overhead costs aka inflation, i mean why don't candy bars cost a nickel anymore?  You do realize that Berkeley is not the cheapest area for both those costs right? The palette of the undergrad population is vast and unbiased, so i believe that the reason why they're so busy all the time is because their food is really that good. I've been eating there for the past four years and have tried other Thai places. Thai Basil is hands down the best quality and the best prices for what you pay, sure, it has increased like documented, but the reasons are understandable and their profit margins aren't that great and they decide to keep their margins low in order to help out the student populace. Additionally, they remodeled their restaurant to make a more pleasing atmosphere to eat in, in my opinion, the best found in the ghetto. Also, I don't know if you carry a salt shaker with you or something and accidentally spilled it all in your food while at Thai Basil, because I know for a fact that they do not use salt in any dish except for the fried rice and curries.

I normally get the Pad Kee Mao here, and it's not too bad. I think it could be a little more flavorful though. This is one of the more popular places in Asian Ghetto, so around dinner time it can get crowded. They typically take around 5 minutes to make your order, so when it's crowded at dinner time, the wait time extends.

pad thai, pad see ew, & eggplant chicken is so freaking good. honestly nothing else matters here except these three dishes. dont get tofu with these dishes though, the tofu tastes liek its been washed with water and some pinesol.

I came here during UCB's move-in day.  I ordered the pad thai to-go.  Normally Thai Food and my stomach don't go well together because I feel like Thai food in general is REALLY oily.  After I ate the pad thai from here, I felt okay.  My stomach didn't hurt for the first time ever!  The portion was really really big! (Well, to me because I'm a pretty small person)  I almost considered giving the rest of my pad thai to a homeless guy that was around there!  The price was okay; $7.75 I think for the pad thai, no drinks.  I accompanied my pad thai with some Quickly's milk tea, which is a couple doors down in Berkeley's Asian ghetto.  It was really busy though, and I waited at least 15 minutes until I got my food.  Worth a try!  AND it's apparently the BEST Thai food in Berk!

The food here was pretty awesome, but the atmosphere was just "eh..." 

It's bordered on telegraph.  Of course, that means an abundance of homeless and trashy people.  The interior is OK, but nothing fancy.

This place is my boyfriend and I's go-to spot for late night Thai food. Nestled in the Asian Ghetto, there are various restaurants open late at night, along with this establishment. It is a simple restaurant with a to-go/fast-food type feel, however there are places to sit.

We've been here twice already and both times I've ordered the Pad Thai. It is delicious for what it is and for being available late at night. My boyfriend ordered the Thai Noodle Boat soup (I think that's what it was called) the first time and he hated it. I tasted it myself and it wasn't too bad.

I would definitely recommend this place to those who are late night eaters.
seafood basil is the sh*t! we  come here when its late @ night and we get  hungry. hits the spot!

Food is just OKAY, not anything to write home about.  The UC Berkeley students who live close by in the dormitories, will love this place, because its way better than the crap being served in the Dining Commons.  Here in Sacramento when you pay these prices, you get served at your table by a waiter, and the portions are much bigger.

Very good Thai food and close to campus (good for the college student).

My favorites include:

Pad Thai
Chicken Pad Prik King
Pineapple Curry

Thai Basil, you probably contributed to 10 pounds of my freshman 15.  I remember the days when you were a run down place.  You closed for about 3 months and made me really sad, only to open looking so spankin' new.  I love what you have done to the place and I hope you will still be standing when I return with my own lil bears to watch a Cal game.  Located in the Asian ghetto, oh excuse me the "Durant Square", probably one of the best Thai places I've had hands down.  

Things I've ordered that I love: Pad See Ew, Pad Ke Mao ?, Rad Nar, Pineapple Fried Rice.  Each plate is like $7.  It's so cheap and sooooo good.  I miss you sweet Thai lady who screams out the numbers.  I would not suggest the lunch menus, given that you probably get more variety and a slightly better deal, I'd spend the extra dollar or two to get some entrees.  

Oh and drench everything in that hot sauce.

I would say that Thai Basil is more a "3.5" star restaurant, but oh well... The food is alright, but nevertheless plentiful, for a low price! Try the Tom Kha noodle soup or Pad Kee Mao with chicken/beef!

Thai Basil = good food + cheap prices + long wait.  My first exploits into Thai food came here my freshmen year at Cal.  The food was good and cheap, but I always wondered why it took them like 30 - 45 minutes to get the food out.  That was the only thing that kept me from going back more often, and instead choosing one of the other dining establishments of the asian ghetto.  Although the long wait allows plenty of time to get boba somewhere or to pick up lunch/dinner for later/next day at either Steve's BBQ or Gypsy's.  

3.5 stars rounded up to 4 for the college memories.
cheapest and best.

I used to eat here a lot because of the inexpensive prices and large portions but had to stop because their food is SO greasy! I am a big Thai food fan and would much prefer to pay a buck or two extra to get a delicious meal at Thai Delight. I'll leave it for the students to enjoy.
This place is really awesome, i usually only stick to a few things i know such as Pepper Garlic Chicken and Chicken Satay. you cant go wrong with those!!!

I really think the bad outweighs the good when it comes to Thai Basil.  I know it's a perennial "Best of Berkeley" and the front window is flooded with Yelp stickers, but hear me out.

Good: Flavored fried rices (Basil, Pineapple, Curry) are very unique and filling.  Also, I'm not usually a fan of pad thai but this place really pulls it off pretty well.  Finally, the thai iced tea might be the best in berkeley.

Bad: Service.  If they forget something, good luck trying to communicate to people with broken english in a noisy atmosphere.  I remember I ordered a lunch special with eggplant tofu and cashew nut chicken.  They gave me eggplant tofu and yellow curry for some reason.  After about 5 minutes of deliberation, they TOOK OFF THE EGGPLANT TOFU and replaced it with cashew nut chicken.  Frustrated, I just left and vowed not to come back.

Worst:  The pad-see-ew, my favorite classic thai dish, is absolutely terrible here.  What's with the bean sprouts?  The flimsy, stuck-together noodles that don't absorb the sauce?  Where the hell is all this grease coming from?  IMHO, you can't have a good thai restaurant without good pad-see-ew.

The thai food in Berkeley isn't leaps and bounds above other places, but I'd say there's a pretty high standard.  I recommend trying everywhere out for yourself and I think you'd agree that Thai Basil isn't as good as it's raved about.

During my four years as a Berkeley student, I loyally ordered the infamous chicken pad see-ew whenever life got too busy. So damn good. The trick is to call in and order your meal 20 minutes prior to picking it up to avoid the wait. A year or so ago, along with other Berkeley restaurants, they changed to cash only. I will forever remember the glory of the chicken pad see-ew.

Taste: 4
Value: 5
Service: 3

Decent Thai food for pretty cheap. I used to come here pretty often my freshman year, but I haven't gone back anytime recently. Definitely one of the better places in the Asian ghetto.

CASH ONLY. As a general rule, try to have at least $10 in your pocket when walking around Berkeley; cash-only and credit/debit price minimums abound here.  You can thank me later(:

Generally reliable Thai food.  Somewhat hyper-savory, a little greasy, and a lot of things are really just different names for basically the same thing (all the chicken stir-fry dishes), but it's consistent and student-budget appropriate.  I've tried at least half the menu here, and I've never left dissatisfied.  Not sure what's so special about the Pad See Ew - the noodles aren't always fresh, sometimes it's a little charred, and the broccoli can be bitter from having been frozen - but it's honestly my favorite place to get Pad Thai.  I don't know why, but I haven't found a place whose Pad Thai I like better.  My other go-to dishes: Pineapple Fried Rice, Basil Eggplant Chicken, Thai Noodle Soup, Pineapple Curry, and my all-time favorite, Pad Pong Prawns - - TRY THIS DISH!!  The curried egg and prawns on top of rice is soo delish^^  The noodle soups can be hit-or-miss at times; sometimes there's too much soup and sometimes there's too much noodles.  Also, Thai Basil has something of a love affair with tomatoes.  Everything from Pad Thai to curries to Tom Yum and Tom Kha (it's supposed to be white) soups are tinged red-orange from their not-so-secret secret ingredient.  I happen to like tomatoes, so I'm a happy camper, but if you don't, pick your dishes with care.  

Like many places in Asian ghetto, I'm positive they've reduced their portion sizes over the years.  Lunch special is pretty cheap (rice and 2-3 items for ~$6), but the dish options are cooked in bulk and the quality is mediocre.  Thai ice tea is a lot of bang for your buck, but it's also extremely mediocre.  Complimentary hot thai tea in the back; get a cup from front at the cash register.  As with other popular Asian Ghetto restaurants, the wait at peak hours can take foreverrrr.  If you're really hungry or just impatient, you have the option of calling in before.  And don't forget: cash only cash only cash only!

The food is quite greasy...but it's delicious.  The portion is generous as well.  

The Pad Thai isn't that great. Instead, I recommend getting the Pad Kee Mow or Pad See Ew (excuse the spelling if it's totally off).  The combination basil fried rice is also really good!

Pad Se Ew.  And Pepper Garlic Tofu.

Great tasting food.  Really oily but hey you dont really go here for healthy food.

4 stars because theres usualy not enough seating and you usually have to enjoy their great food to go.

There are much better Thai places around Berkeley to eat at.  I guess this place gets alot of its business due to convenience located in the high traffic area of the Asian Ghetto.  I still eat here due to that reason, but I stick with what I know- the Pad Se Ew.

3.5 stars
**YELP please change your rating system so we can give partial stars**

This was a frequent dining spot for me in Berkeley. I only order their pepper garlic chicken. Its that good that I wouldn't want to try anything else. Service can be a bit slow at times compared to the other places in the Asian ghetto.

Greasy thai cuisine pretty much sums up Thai Basil. The food is good and the price is arguably right (except for $8 dishes of fried rice). Classics like pad thai and pad see ew are crowdpleasers, and the wait is usually okay despite busy lunch and dinner hours. They accept credit cards and phone orders, so that's a big extra in my book.

I only recently tried Thai Basil for the first time and am now incorporating it into my regular lunch rotation.  What I have ordered off the menu has been flavorful and fresh, and the lunch special - while obviously less fresh - allows you to try a variety of things and is a pretty good deal as well. 

I'll admit that 4 stars is a rating that may be partially inflated as a result of comparing Thai Basil to other places in the Telegraph corridor, many of which I can hardly tolerate anymore.  But I think that's fair; why compare it to the best sit-down Thai places?  If you're near UC Berkeley's campus, want Thai food, and like the idea of sitting outside to eat it, this is the place.

Yay for Thai Basil!  They have a wide, wide selection of Thai food, and is pretty large yet cozy inside.  They serve hot tea, which is always a plus in my book.

I would avoid the appetizer spring rolls - definitely a menu item that is not worth your money.
Thai food is great but lines can get very overwhelming and long. Damn Uc students lol j/p over all I give it a 9 out of 10

Ok first thing... This place is for a quick grab. Nothing fancy at all. It's more like pay first and wait for ur food at a window. The bathroom is pretty ghetto, u need to give them your Id so they give you this key and u walk into an alley thing to go to the bathroom lol.

Ok Im giving it a 5 star bc regardless of how ghetto this place looks, their food is cheap and legit. Cooked by real Thai fellas. Their pad Thai, is by far one of the best pad Thai I ever had. Taste even better than a lot of fancy Thai restaurants. If ur in the area and looking for a quick grab, this is the place. O ya I forgot their Thai tea is legit. 1.50 can't beat that.

It's $7 total for a big a$$ meal that you can split between two, or get leftovers that last well. Although the portions have been getting smaller lately :( They also have free tea :)

Their pineapple curry chicken, thom kha soup, and this spicy green bean dish with chicken that I forget the name of are my favorites. I love that they have pics of the food on the menu.

On the other hand, their chicken is terrible quality, and the people are somewhat rude. The wait is not 30 minutes though; look inside, if there's five people in line you'll have a 15 min wait for your food, if there's more and you're in a rush, don't go.

To the haters: this is the best of Asian Ghetto, it's not a 5 star restaurant, it's a good deal.

BBQ pork.  Pad thai with chicken.  Basil fried rice chicken.  Shared between two people (with about half left to take home for seconds).  Heaven.

Do you occasionally have to wait too long?  Yes.  Are they completely unwilling to give you one or two extra large plates?  Yes.  In fact, it'd probably be easier to get them to give you a kidney.

But the food?  Incredible.  The best thai food I've ever had.  Better than every place in Berkeley.  Every place in SF.  And, oh yeah, everywhere in Thailand.

I am really appalled that this place has 3 and a half stars.  Three years ago I was introduced to the heavenly goodness that is Thai food.  

And then I met Thai Basil.

Since then I have tried countless Thai places (I'm not kidding, like 50) and no place compares to this one.  The food is amazing and the price is ridiculously cheap.  Also, I've read some reviews that say that the pad thai is "so-so."  HA!  Who do you think you are?  Better yet, where have you been eating?  The Pad Thai, Basil Fried Rice Chicken and BBQ Pork (moo yang) are the best!!!

I really want to like this place... especially since it's so well-loved by many college students in the area. I really have to disagree - their food is greasy and it always leaves me feeling funny afterwards. I had the yellow curry and the fried rice and both are just not up to par with what Thai food should taste like. I will continue going to San Francisco for some real Thai food... until Berkeley comes up with something better.
Service is slow and the lady at the counter isnt very nice.

I've been to Thai Basil a few times and I'm not a fan of the customer service and general environment, but I'm giving this place 3 stars because the food is O.K.. So far I've gotten Pad Thai, Pumpkin Curry (during Thanksgiving, I believe), Eggplant Chicken, and Red Curry. They have good portions, but there's definitely MSG in their foods, which is a major turn off. You'll feel thirsty for hours afterward.

One of the few places here that takes credit card. That in itself is enough to keep me coming. I would say their best dish is either the pad see ew or the basil chili chicken. The former is delicious flat noodles with chicken and broccoli, with a sauce that's more sweet than savory. Chicken tends to be a little dry though. The latter is pure delicious on a cold day - just the right amount of heat while being a little sweet. Maybe I have a sweet tooth. Either way, this place is good times. 

Long waits are only a problem if you come during a normal lunch hour. During the school year, it will be empty at 11:59 and packed at 12:05 as everyone gets out of class. Time it like a starcraft pro.
Best Thai in Berkeley. Found this gem by mistake. Def going back next time we are in town.

Love this place!  Its cheap and its super delicious.  When I go back to the bay area to visit I manage to find my way over here for a random lunch and nothing has changed since i lived nearby.  Its still wonderful!

This is my favorite place in "Asian Ghetto," hands down.  There are numerous other Thai places around the UC Berkeley area but this one is my go-to place for quick, cheap Thai food without sacrificing quality.  

I've tried a variety of dishes there, but the ones I tend to get the most are the Tom-Kha Noodle Soup and the Eggplant Basil Chicken.  I also sometimes like to get the Rad-na noodles or Red Curry.  Most dishes cost around $6.50 plus tax.  You can also substitute different meats for no extra cost unless you want shrimp.  Not only is the food good, but the service is also generally fast.  I usually don't have to wait more than 10 minutes to get my order.  Waiting isn't a big deal anyway since you can walk over to Quickly/Sweethearts to pick up a boba while you wait.  

In addition, they take credit card!  This may seem like no big deal elsewhere, but most places in Asian Ghetto are cash only or charge extra for credit.  To-go orders are very nicely packaged (especially in terms of the noodle soup entrees) and the staff is very friendly for people who don't speak English that well.  The location is great - 1.5 blocks from the UC Berkeley campus and close to the Unit dorms.  I don't go to UC Berkeley anymore, but next time I visit I will make sure to come back here!

UPDATE 12/09/11: Knocked off a star because they don't take credit card anymore! :[

As a broke college student, I was excited to find the "Asian Ghetto". The prices at Thai Basil were reasonable and the food was good. I always got the Pad Thai so am not the biggest expert when it comes to other dishes. I highly recommend trying this place out when you are having a craving for some thai food!  The place is small but her is plenty of seating outside to people watch on a nice day!

This is a fairly tasty Thai place in the Asian Ghetto. But as a Berkeley student, I'm starting to get sick and tired of this food court. 

However, sometimes service can be a little slow, and sometimes I'm skeptical at how clean they are in their kitchen. :/

I love this place. I went here probably once a week during college, and never tired of it. To be clear, this is cheap thai food and it tastes like cheap food. That being said, it is really delicious, flavorful, hit-the-spot, cheap thai food. I love their panang curry and pad see ew, but really everything is pretty good, and the portions are HUGE. I even took my parents (nothing else was open) and they liked it too. 

Only two minor gripes (which are not bad enough to ever deter me from going): cash only and food can take a while to come out. 

Finally, the place has no ambiance, but if you're looking for good take-out thai, this is the place.

Thanks Yelp sticker for not steering me wrong!! We wondered upon Thai Basil Cuisine and got just what we had hoped for tasty food that was filling. For two meals and drinks we ended up with a $20+ bill which seemed a little high but we could have easily had lunch the next day had we been willing to carry it home on the shuttle. We had a decent wait since the place was packed with local college kids but I did not experience any of the rudeness that the previous Yelpers mentioned when placing my order.

This place is HELLA good! 

They have a million different dishes and lots of vegetarian options. The pad thai and cashew tofu are AWESOME! 
It's also very affordable with good portions.

If you don't like this place it's probably because you don't have a tongue.

Delicious, greasy, cheap, filling. 4 magical words that, when used in combination, mandated a place to be visited weekly as a starving college student. The pad see ew here is really great and the I liked the fried rice dishes as well. For really refined curries and entrees, fancy dates and such, there are other places in Berkeley to go to (Thai House). But for an everyday eat, this is a mainstay. I hope this place never changes.

This place (my favorite-est in asian ghetto) has the best pineapple fried rice I've ever tasted. It's... I just can't describe the yummyness, you'll just have to try it yourself!
Downside is that it might be a tad expensive given there is no waiter service.

I've been to Thai Basil three times, and each time has been underwhelming to bad.

This time I ordered the Pad Kee Moa.  The dish was almost flavorless.  Making the dish somewhat appetizing required extensive use of chili sauce, but this could not salvage it.  My meal became the effective equivalent of plain noodles and Sriracha, a meal I could make at home for less than a dollar (though, of course, I never would).

The broccoli, bell pepper, and onions were not merely semi-cooked, which would be acceptable for a stir-fried dish, but raw.  This would be somewhat understandable if I had gone during one of Thai Basil's daunting rush hours, but there was only one girl eating in the restaurant when I ordered.  This Pad Kee Moa was a creation of the chef's undivided attention.

Thai is my favorite type of cuisine, but if I had first eaten it at Thai Basil I might have been reluctant to ever try it again.   The best Thai restaurant I've ever eaten at is in Berkeley, and just a few blocks down Telegraph.  If you dislike Thai food because of Thai Basil, give Racha Cafe on Dwight and Telegraph a try.  And if you actually like Thai Basil, you deserve something better.  The chef at Racha actually seems to give attention to the food, and the flavors of the dishes are beyond my ability to describe, so I won't try.

It's incomprehensible to me that Thai Basil has found such a niche with the student community that it's consistently considered a good restaurant, let alone the "Best Thai Food in Berkeley" as several plaques proclaim.

This is pretty much my favorite thai place that i've tried in Berkeley in the past few months. 
I love:
Pra rama chicken
Veggie  and non veg Pad Thai
Spicy thai basil catfish (fave)
chicken skewers
Probably my favourite place in the Asian Ghetto, I loved the green curry with chicken, and usually got an iced to with it, loved it, kept going back again and again.

people claim this place is inexpensive, but I beg a differ. It seems like a lot of money to pay for greasy chinese-style thai food. I'm always asked my opinion on this place when people find out I'm Thai. But I say nay to thai basil. I suppose people need their pad thai fix, and rich Cal students don't care about buying overpriced fast food.

I used to go to Thai Basil all the time my freshman year at Cal just for the Pad Thai.  It was reasonably priced and I thought it was pretty dang good; of course, I never had Pad Thai elsewhere to which I could compare it but I didn't care.

I went to eat there with my family last summer after we finished showing my grandmother around campus.  She was visiting us from another country and she was tired, so we didn't want to go very far for food (rice, in particular).  I suggested Thai Basil-- good Pad Thai, bound to have rice, less than a five-minute walk from campus.  It seemed perfect....It wasn't.  After patiently waiting in the slow-moving line for about ten minutes, it was finally my turn to order.  I ordered for my family and then remembered that I still needed to order rice.  I didn't know they had multiple sizes, so when the lady at the register asked me what size I wanted, I asked her (politely, I might add) how big the sizes were because I didn't want to get too much and waste it.  She rolled her eyes, dramatically threw her arms down to her sides and sighed before she walked over to where their rice containers were.  Initially, I felt bad and thought I should have just said medium to be safe.  When she came back, however, and shoved each container in my face while rudely telling me each size as if I were a small child, I didn't feel bad at all.  I just said I didn't want any of them, paid for the food I already ordered, and left.  

I haven't gone back since, especially after satisfying my Pad Thai urges elsewhere.  Compared to other places around Berkeley that are just as convenient to eat at, Thai Basil is mediocre.  Mediocre food + terrible service = no thank you.

Expensive, long lines, and a lady who's so rude you want to strangle her with a rice noodle...but the food is good. I've heard from thai people at Cal that the quality isn't that authentic but I grew up eating American style thai food - give me my pad thai with a bag's worth of C&H please! 
They could definitely give you more per plate tho I feel like. Additionally, they don't keep fresh limes in stock and use limeade instead. I recommend their Basil fried rice, pad thai, pas see ew and pad kee mao.
I like this place. Cheap, good and fast!

Besides Gypsy's, it's the only other place most people walk into after circling the Asian Ghetto seven times.

pad see ew is literally, pad see EWW, but I guess the pepper garlic chicken is OKAYYY...I'd rather have it actually taste like garlic and walk around with canttalktoyou breath than to have it drenched in grease though... I guess that's what the cucumber slices are for.

Their curries are also coated with a layer of floating oil on top...just imagine that layer solidified under your skin, okay?! Toxic FAT. Your body is a temple (Thai temple if you wish), don't soil it.

Don't know why it's so good nor why it is one of my favorite Thai places, but it is.  This small "hole in the wall" place by UC Berkeley is a must for me.  The only thing I ever get from here is their Pad See Ew- which may be the best I've ever had.  

It is a tiny place and you wouldn't expect such goodness to come from such a place, but oh my yum- it's so good!  I've never been disappointed here.

Not my favorite in the "Asian ghetto" on Durant, but a lot of people I know really like it. The pad-thai is good, but I'm always lured into the other restaurants which just seem more attractive for some reason.  But the eggplant is Soo good.

4 stars for their Garlic Pepper Chicken (45a), lol, that's all I ever got here, don't know why I didn't branch out more. They heap on plenty of MSG that is tough to see, but it sure tastes great later.

-1 star for taking a long time, longer than they should. It's up to a 30-minute wait at some times.

Good price, but as one yelper also wrote, I got the wrong order, but decided not to complain mainly because I wasn't going to be coming back again.
