We were looking for Bear Ramen, but it happened to be closed on this particular Sunday, so we ended up at the Thai restaurant.  We saw a lot of people in and out and thought the food must be good.  It was okay, but  there are probably better places in the area with a more friendlier cashier.

The food here is SO bomb...but it's an oily deliciousness as opposed to a healthy deliciousness. Nonetheless it is undoubtedly my favorite restaurant in Asian Ghetto. 

Also, you can order your food by phone and it'll be ready for pick up in approx 15 minutes. 

Minus one star for only accepting cash.

If you're a first timer here, you can't go wrong with Pad Kee Mow or Pad See Ew!

Been coming here since over 2 years ago. Perfect restaurant for poor starving students. For $7, I can get a very filling and delicious meal the likes of Basil/Curry Fried Rice Chicken or Basil Eggplant Chicken. No need to pay tips even if you eat here because you pay at order time.

Call in to order if you intend to come during peak hours, so that you can bypass the line.

Despite the hoards of college kids you have to make your way through, I always love coming to Thai Basil for my thai food fix.... even 3 years after I graduated.

Combination basil fried rice: BEST fried rice everrrr. Top it off with a little bit of chili sauce, the best. Has seafood, all meats, peppers and onions with the hint of thai basil.... makes me salivate just thinking about it.

Pad see ew: 2nd dish I usually order, sometimes the quality varies depending on how busy they are but generally a decent pad see ew, and I'm never realyl disappointed with this.

Chicken and Eggplant basil: I love eggplant and its texture, so if you're not normally a fan of eggplant well then, I feel bad for you. This dish is kind of oily but so so good still. Eggplant can be a little soft but on a good day it is PERfect. 

Parking is always a b*tch, so just plan to park far and walk it, or circle around for days, esp if you are coming during some kind of Cal event.

Good cheap Thai food.  I'm a fan of the peanut chicken here. Although, it takes a while to get your food when it's busy and the people at the register are rude, but whatever it's inexpensive and relatively good.

I've been going to Thai Basil for years. I don't know why I haven't written a review yet. 

Their pad ke mow and pepper garlic chicken is some of the best I've ever had. 

The only downside is that the prices are about $2 high per entree for Berkeley campus food. 

Love this place though.

Pros:
Decent thai food

Cons:
relatively expensive (7~8$) for the amount of food they serve
expect to wait 10+ mins for your food in rush hour.

Hands down, my favorite place in Berkeley!  Great Thai food, big portions, cheap prices - this place is a winner.  I have eaten here so many times while I was a student at Berkeley and keep coming back even now when I crave Thai food.  All of my friends love this place too and I've never met a Berkeley student who hasn't eaten here :)

My favorite dish is the basil eggplant chicken, although I've never tried a bad dish here.  

The atmosphere is not the greatest, it's a very casual place, but the food is great and you can always do take out.

This place is like a guilty pleasure. And it is not without due reason. 
Open late. Fast service. And good food. What's not to like?

The fried rice is pretty bomb. But a tad heavy on the basil side.

I usually get the pad see ew and its on general pretty good, though its not as consistant as i would like, sometimes ending up a little greasy

Located in Durant Food court, formerly known as asian ghetto, its a pretty good location.

There is also a lot of seating inside. Its a pretty chill place...you can study, watch a few games, i don't think its ever a packed house, most people just grab the food and bounce

A little Thai place tucked into that plaza of Asian places on Durant near Telegraph. 

Food: Pretty much your standard issue Thai food. Nothing life changing or out there, but tasty, and the portions are large. A great place to come if you're hungry and you want something flavorful. 

Their lunch special is also a great deal, where you get to choose two dishes from a rotating set of three (say, pad thai, pineapple chicken curry and cashew tofu) for about five dollars. 

Service: Pretty standard. They take your order, the food comes, you eat it. It does tend to get a bit crowded during the lunch rush hour from about 11:30 to 1 though. 

Overall: There's nothing particularly memorable about this place (I had to think a little before I remembered the actual name... normally I just refer to it as "that Thai place in the Asian place"), but you always need those places you can drop in and have a quick, cheap, satisfying lunch.  Gets extra credit for being a hop, skip and a jump from South Hall.

A great place for cheap and very good Thai food. Its located right near CAL and shopping corners on Telegraph and Durant. Its surrounded by other food joints but i always prefer Thai Basil. The menu is pretty big with pretty good options. One thing is the appetizers, i don't recommend them. They're not worth your money.

Yum!

Evan's Thoughts

Thai food lovers unite!

Centrally located for the UC Berkeley student, this Thai place is exceptional.  I know my Thai food and this place knew exactly what they were doing.  

I usually get pad thai (a personal favorite) but I decided to get the chicken kar parma (spelling?) instead.  It is an extremely good chicken dish, with white rice and a lovely peanut sauce.

One of the best parts of the whole experience...$8 for dinner!  This is the place to go for the Berkeley student on a budget, looking for amazing thai food.

Happy Eating!

Every time I go to Asian ghetto people are always flocking over to Thai Basil. I'm not the biggest fan of Thai food, but I do enjoy eating what is popular so I gave it a shot. It was so whatever and "Meh. I've experienced better." It was so spot on 2 stars it's not even funny.

I'm not just being biased against Thai food, but I give it 2 stars knowing it's Thai food that I typically don't like. The food takes a long time and the lady at the register is just straight up rude. If good service is important to you, then you definitely won't find that here.

For college students Asian ghetto is a great location and it does have a nice flat screen TV if you enjoy watching something while eating. I suggest phoning in if you just want the food, which is not bad, I suppose. But remember to BRING CASH!

the Great,
GumZ
Yum! Cute little place to fix your Thai craving!

Ask any Berkeley student what food they miss most, and Thai Basil is guaranteed to be in the top 5. This place has it all.

Open past midnight? Yes.
Vegetarian Selections? Yes.
Spicy? Yes
Cheap? Yes

If you want a serious kick order any of the dishes "5 star spicy". I particularly enjoy the tofu panang curry, the pad thai, the basil chicken, the pineapple fried rice, the green bean tofu, the ... There is probably nothing bad on this menu.

To top it all off they have complimentary hot steeped tea to drown out the spice when it becomes too much to take.

The only con is that they accept cash only, but there is a convenient BofA ATM about 50 feet down the street.

PRO TIP
---------------------
Call in your order and it will be ready when you arrive. Otherwise be prepared for a 10-15 minute wait even during slow times.
i had the pineapple fried rice. quite ordinary, but kind of oily.

Excellent Thai food - I recently went for a visit after graduating and leaving Berkeley for a few years. It is still very much the same taste as before. It is a shame that they no longer accept credit cards. We had pineapple fried rice and garlic chicken. Good stuff. The food is slightly slow but worth the wait.
One of my favorite Thai restaurants. Really good pad-see-eew...i just always wish there were more of it. Also good comfort food. Good panang and yellow curries, too. I try to eat here once a week.
Cheap, convenient, tasty, well-spiced, and good-sized menu and portions.  It's always a good go-to when you need a quick meal with great flavors.

This is my most-frequented restaurant in Berkeley. The food is cheap and tasty. I love the Pad Thai and the Spicy Basil Chicken is awesome. Spicy enough to get your nose running but not so spicy that you burst into flames before the meal is over. Delicious, cheap, and my favorite part of the "Asian Ghetto"!

Great food. I am personally a fan of the Chili Chicken. Great price for the portion. However, they did get my order wrong a couple of times but were kind enough to change it. Wouldn't advise going at peak hours (i.e. lunch and dinner).
delicious pad see ew

Good place for Thai to-go. 
Cheap, fast and tasty.
I never have to wait more than 10' for the food.
Really big portion for the price.

Dude, Thai Basil is pretty good! I had low expectations for this place when the bf first took me here, but after coming here a good 4-5 times, I have not been disappointed!

I recommend the Pad Thai (generic I know, but hey it's good) and the curries. The Basil chicken is also great. The reason why I especially love the Pad Thai here is because they have tofu, prawns, AND chicken all together! At all the other Thai restaurants I've been to you usually only have one choice to choose from.

The prices are really reasonable too! Perfect for a college student's budget ;). The only downside is the long lines and wait time so go early to avoid the crowds!

I love this place... it's super greasy and pretty cheap, and delicious!!! I've only tried a handful of things on the menu because once I find dishes I like, it's difficult for me to branch out to try others. I get cravings for their Pad Kee Mao, Basil Fried Rice, and (occasionally) their Eggplant Tofu. It's basically my comfort food whenever I crave something greasy and satisfying.

Better and cheaper than most Thai places here in Berkeley. I usually get the Pad Thai, Pineapple Fried Rice, or the lunch special here.

The Pad Thai is always very flavorful and not bland at all like other places, the portion that you get is quite large, and the bean sprouts are cooked in. What isn't so great about the Pad Thai is that sometimes your order comes out a bit too soggy and every single time, the shrimps (count them: two) are overcooked to death. I also wish that they could have crushed peanuts available at the table when you eat in. Peanuts are always a huge plus with any Thai dish. 

The lunch special that they have is pretty special. Two or three items plus rice for $5.75 (tax included). Compared to other places like Le Chevals, you get a ton of rice here. For the two or three items that you can choose, you choose from the ones that they decide to make that day, which always includes Pad Thai, and sometimes curry, garlic chicken, or other stuff I've yet to have. 

Though they have three people in the back cooking, on a busy day, your order can take up to 20 minutes or so.
Baby, I want you, all night, every night. Me and you, it'll be okay, lights off or on, it's okay, whatever you like. It's okay. Whatever you like, just me and you pad-see-ew, me and you.

The kitchen works like a machine.  You can see everything the cooks are doing (which i always appreciate).  I honestly think they're all related because it seems they're always yelling at each other; doesn't matter - the food comes fast, consistent, and perfectly spicy.  Not the best Thai food, but for the price and speediness, I'm back every two weeks :)

All I've got to say is "SPICY CATFISH WITH EGGPLANT" All time favorite. Got my daughter and Hubby hooked on it. Been to many great thai places but this is the only one where I can remember the address? lolz :) There coconut curry soups are great, eggplant basil chicken is delicious too. It takes a minute to get your food to go since it is cooked to order. You want to go when the students aren't  there for lunch.

There is a place next to it my hubbie used to love called Steve's bbq which looks HELLA dirty but he's now a fan of thai basil.

#1. Two years in Berkeley, and I've never stopped by.  It's kind of embarrassing, especially when I live on the south side of campus.  So I decided to pay you a visit.

What do you get with chicken, shrimp, crushed peanuts, and thin flat noodles?  Amazing pad thai.  The lady at the counter wasn't the nicest person, but I can take affordable comfort food over a little frustration any day.  I dropped by your place the next day to get the combination fried rice.  I eat a lot, but one order can last two meals for me!  That makes $4+/meal.  Not bad at all.  I would recommend you to go a little easy on the MSG.  The food was authentic and delicious, but I had to chug a water bottle to quench my thirst!  Nevertheless, you are now officially my go-to place in Asian Ghetto.  Sorry, neighbors, I made a new friend down the block.

They give you enormous portions for cheap prices and the food isn't bad. It's also not particularly special, but if you're a poor hungry college student and you need a quick and satisfying bite to eat before you head back to the library, this is probably right up your alley. In fact I think this entire alley (a.k.a the asian ghetto) is right up you ralley. 

If you're a grad student at UC Berkeley, be prepared to feel very old, the entire area is basically a freshman hangout.

A Berkeley classic. I would call this place the crown jewel of the UC Berkeley food ghetto. The food is cheap but still really good. I'm not a fan of curries but I have friends who are and they like them here. I like the ginger chicken and beef broccoli myself. The food does take kinda long to prepare, but on sunny days you can sit and eat outside. 

This place is as much Berkeley as Sather Gate.

I love everything here!!!! So goooood. Too bad the quality goes down a bit during peak times (lunch, dinner) but otherwise it's SO good!

Dishes to get:
-pad kee moa - ONLY GET THIS HERE and no where else in Berkeley!
-pad thai
-pad see ew is good too
-pineapple fried rice

Great food, decent price. Seating area is kinda small. The only reason I gave them 4 stars? One time they took 53 minutes to make my food (ok, I approximated)...  FIFTY THREE!!! What were they thinking? Though this has only happened once, it was enough for me to take off a star...

Keep in mind that the place only takes Cash.

The Pad Thai here is the only dish I order whenever I come to the Thai Basil. It's a pretty big portion for about 7-8 dollars, but I say it's worth it. It's big enough to share with 2 people and can satisfy your stomach for a couple of hours. Plus the pad thai is filled with lots of spices which adds an extra kick to it.

- This place is usually opened late which is great for people who crave midnight snacks. Just be careful if you ever decide to come here at night because their might be a few homeless people lingering around trying to mob you. The last time I came here, a homeless man talked to me and my friends for about ten minutes explaining to us that UC Berkeley was corrupted. So just be aware of your surroundings the next time you decide to pay a visit.

Tofu curry fanatic seeks feel-good Thai.

The fact that this place is constantly packed speaks for itself: it's a hit!  The flavors and portions are great (I approximate  I got 36 cubic inches of beautifully-made white rice with my order of yellow curry.)  Curiously enough, there was no tofu in my TOFU yellow curry.  The veggie chunks are too big to soak up all the curry flavor.  

Veggie spring rolls are Chinese-esque, and its companion peanut sauce was not that great.  I'd pass on this next time.

For the price, it was a nice meal.  The excess of flies don't exactly add to the ambiance.  At least a couple of people had their orders butchered, which you want to AVOID because the language barrier will just worsen the situation.  Check your stuff before leaving.

oh god do i miss this place.

thai basil was my go to food when i was heading home from campus.  the pad see ew is the best i've ever had, and the pineapple rice is perfect.

the wait is usually super long, and good luck finding a table, but it'll be well worth it.

Come here if you like to eat grease and msg. I'll admit that while you're eating it's like a drug - hits the spot on a cold day, on one of those lazy days you don't feel like cooking - but you pay for it about an hour and a half later when it seems as though you could drink Lake Eerie and still be thirsty. For your health, I don't recommend it.

What the heck are they putting in the sauce for the Basil Eggplant Chicken?!?  It is sooo addicting!  They also have one of the best Thai Iced Teas I've ever tasted too.  I think I ate this meal every week, if not ever other week, while I was at Berkeley.  I don't have the cravings any more but maybe that's a good thing since I'm about 400 miles away!
Good food.  Good price.  Ok sizes. Takes a while.

This place is conveniently located in a food court near the UC Berkeley campus of Telegraph Ave.  My spicy basil red curry cat fish was definitely mouthwatering down to the last bite (even in its pool of grease), and I left feeling satiated from my hunger.   However, my cousin and I both felt the dehydrating effects of MSG as our afternoon of shopping progressed on Telegraph Ave.  

Never mind the cafeteria style interior, and cash only policy.  It's quite appropriate for a hole-in-the wall college kid food joint, but MSG just rubs me the wrong way.  -no can do...

I've come here twice and each time I get a stomach ache afterwards.  I'm always craving red thai curry so that's what I got both times (first time red curry+pumpkin; 2nd time red curry + chicken) and seriously my stomach is KICKING afterwards.  

But something tells me I'll probably continue to come here just because its so close to campus.  I never learn...

This place is terrible.  It is the only Thai place located inside Asian ghetto, and their pineapple fried rice is decent.  However, the service is terrible.  Twice I got literally yelled at/scolded.  Once because I didn't bus my dishes to the right location, the second time because I asked for chopsticks with my to go order.  I came here again post graduation after a Cal football game and got the special, and the noodles were dry and the food all in all tasted old, like they prepared all the food at the butt crack of dawn and didn't replenish it as the day went on.
We had the Pad Thai. It was OK. Pineapple fried rice was very good. This curry with rice was also very good too.

Not the best thai place, but given the price, this is one place I have to swing by every few times I'm in Berkeley.  The service isn't particularly fast, but the food is certainly quite good (most of the time), and there's something soothing about being able to watch them make your food.

My personal favorites are the Pad See-Ew and Pad Kee-Mow (spelling may be terribly off, I'm afraid), as well as anything they make involving Basil.  Overall, pricing is good, food is good (if somewhat oily), and the servers haven't messed up my order before, which is already a good sign.

The only real downside is that sometimes the service takes...a bit long, but given the long lines, it's a forgivable offense.

I used to go there quite often because a few of my friends like this place, but honestly, I never really liked the food very much. It is greasy and some dishes just are really not tasty at all, e.g. their Pad Thai. The staff is also not the most friendly, like when you ask for a box for you food they don't even reply or look at you.

As far as I can tell, the food served up at Thai Basil is pretty typical fast food Asian. Different from fast food Chinese, but not miles different.

That said, the food is good. Solid Asian food, sure to please most at the typical $5 to $6 price tag. And you get a lot for your money as well. Mountain of rice, plus whatever you decide to get 
(the seafood curry is pretty good if you're willing to splurge). The wait is usually 10 to 20 minutes, not too bad, but not good if you're in a hurry.

Small picky point: sometimes the curries are a tad too sweet. "Sweet?!?!?!?!?!" I hear you cry? Yes. Almost syrupy sometimes, but a forgivable offense, considering the price and overall quality.

Overall, a great place for cheap, solid Asian food.

While Thai Basil isn't great Thai food, it's a good deal for the price, and probably your best bet in the Asian Ghet-- er, 'Durant Food Court'. While your food will take longer to arrive than at neighboring joints, it also tastes significantly better (no Mandarin House or Vietnam Village for me).

I recommend the Pad Thai, the Garlic Pepper Chicken, and the Satay. The "yellow curry" isn't bad either.

CASH ONLY 

This isn't just another place named Thai Basil. Situated in a corner of the "Asian Ghetto" this place has some really cheap Thai food. They actually have a pretty big menu for such a small place. 

As for the food, you get what you pay for. You get a decent amount of food but it is very salty and oily. I ordered some Tom Yum soup because it's my favorite and I wasn't feeling really hungry. It was pretty oily but the soup was overall good. Also, the portion is much bigger than a restaurant portion, so it ended up being pretty filling. Also, they don't skimp on the chicken or vegetables in the soup. 

The bathroom... you're almost better off peeing your pants...almost. They also hold your phone hostage while you're in the bathroom. 

They also have a lot of vegetarian food, as Thai places normally have a big selection of vegetarian food.

My friend recommended this place to me a couple years ago when we were hungry after a club meeting. On his recommendation, I had the pepper garlic chicken, which was an excellent dish. Then I tried the pad thai and fell in love with it ever since. I also had some leftover fried rice of some sort that another friend left in my fridge, and heck, that was good too. I really don't see how you could go wrong with this place, and I've even seen the pad thai brought to an end-of-year class potluck.

This place gets five stars as far as the food is concerned and the only reason I am giving it 4 stars is because the people working there are just generally in a pissed off mood all the time. When the lady calls your number, she gives you about 1 second to get up there before she starts calling the number out repeatedly like you are moving far to slow. Not only that, but they just never seem to be in a good mood. I mean I have been there a good 10 times and they are always in the same mood. But, aside from that, seriously the food is delicious! Especially the BBQ pork dish and the Pad Thai. Both are amazing and the only reason I don't get Pad Thai every time, is because it is a little overwhelming at times. If you haven't been yet, and you like some good Thai food or are even looking for the closest place that has some good chinese food, this place comes close.

The best fried rice EVER!  I ordered combination fried rice every time.  Other dishes I tried are grilled pork, basil chicken, rad na noodle, pepper garlic chicken, curry shrimps.  All SOOOO GOOD. They used to accept credit card, but no longer.  I understand it completely.  I own my own business, and credit card companies charge a lot of fee...   And for the person who got their soup order in separate containers, you probably asked for to-go.  If they put broth in the noodle, the noodle will become mushy and absorb most of the broth after 10 minutes.  That's the reason why they have to separate the ingredients.

Location..yeah it's not that great.  Homeless hanging out outside, but if you can find a table inside, then it's fine  Otherwise, take it to go.

Price: cheap, large portion.

Overall: cheap, good food. What can I say...

Along with Intermezzo, this is my favorite place around Cal! The Basil Eggplant Chicken is great, and the prices are pretty reasonable. Watch out though, some stuff on the menu isn't all that good. And the tea sucks.
d

I love this place. Coming here after game days can be a complete cluster fuck as Jason j. said but, on the weekdays after a long day of work, this place is hard to beat. 
The Thai Ice Tea is good, the pineapple fried rice is great and the pineapple curry is amazing. 
I'm not a foodie elitist and have a pretty lenient palette but regardless I know that I love this place and so will you foos. paece.

Lots of students but the food is great.  I would give it five stars except a) they insist on making everything fresh; for many people I know that's a plus, but for me, I just like having things fast.  You'll wait 5-10 minutes.  and b) If you order a drink they have to prepare behind the counter, they WILL forget when they serve the food, and you have to remind them.  But the food is great.

My second favorite spot after Gypsy's in the Asian Ghetto. You gotta love the authentic grandma's in the back cooking with masks over their mouthes. The food's alright, nothing special, but it definitely is a good place to get some spicy food in the Berkeley area. The basil fried rice is one of my favorites on their menu, along with garlic pepper chicken.

This place is a little bit more pricier than the other spots in the Ghetto, and they usually take a little longer to get your food to you. If you want a better dining experience (sit down, no blums loitering, etc.), I'd recommend just going down the block to Thai House.

I love Thai Basil. It's not expensive, the portions are big and, most importantly, it's really delicious! The vegetables are never soggy and everything is freshly made. I definitely recommend the Pad See Ew or Pad Prik King or the wontons...or anything really! 

They do take cash only, so make sure you stop by the ATM on the way there.

This place is a hair off the beaten path. It is hidden in the back of this deep covered area surrounded by other small restaurants. Judging by the 7 placards on the wall they have earned many awards and have been established here for over 10yrs. 
I had the Tom-kha noodle soup with chicken. I was very pleased with this dish. Even though it was a coconut milk based dish it wasn't too over powering or too rich which i liked. The portion size was just right. Not too much to where you felt stuffed after being done and not too little to where you are still a bit hungry. Overall it was delicious good food at a great price!

An added bonus to being right down the street from Cal is that this place has free wi-fi and water!! I'm actually doing the review in the restaurant!! Cool huh?! Plenty of seating too.

I wish I can give this 3.5 stars... 

What else can I say? This is definitely my go-to Thai food place in Berkeley. I love thai food and I've hit up a lot of the thai places around Berkeley, and though I do enjoy most of them, this place is still my go-to place. I don't even think it's necessarily the best food, but it's solid, fairly cheap, and located in AG so it's my natural choice. 

Their food is good and really satisfies a craving. Their curries are pretty good too, but their pad thai is definitely the best on their menu. I don't know why people would get the fried rice there because you can get that for a few dollars cheaper and better at the Bear Ramen House next door. 9/10 times i've been here, I've ordered the pad thai and I've never been disappointed. 

As a cheap college student, I wouldn't call this place cheap, but it's decently priced, especially for thai food in the area. I always think pad thai would only be around 6 dollars, but it always ends up at almost 8 with tax. Also. the wait is long so you should order first, light up, and then come back for the food. 

However, if you're looking for a good sit down thai place similar in quality and price, you should also hit up Berkeley Thai House. Honestly, I think all thai food is good so I might have lower standards but both these places are pretty good. I usually only order pad thai but I've had the curry at both places and it's pretty good. the only difference is that thai basil is better for take-out i think. I've only dined at thai basil once and I think they give you more when you order it to go. 

But yes, if you get the woman cashier, she's not a nice woman at all. the man is definitely nicer. in the end though, service doesn't matter as much as the food, and this place is a solid 3.5

This might be a bit of a shocker for some people but after living in Berkeley for 4 years and becoming addicted to Thai food I really have NOT been able to find a place that can match Thai Basil's Pad Kee Mao! I have tried everything from hip places in San Francisco (Osha Thai) to expensive 5 star restaurants in San Diego to similar hole-in-the-walls in Sacramento but I really cannot get my hands on a more delicious Pad Kee Mao (and trust me I have TRIED). For $7.65 this place is UNBEATABLE! Props to mom and pop for maintaining such a delicious restaurant to serve the severely beaten and often hungry students of UC Berkeley!!

Now that I have graduated from Cal, Every time I go to the Bay Area or pass anywhere remotely close to Berkeley, I have to stop buy and get 4 orders of Pad Kee Mao for my entire family (who also vouches for their amazingness). My only wish is that they can deliver 90 miles to Sacramento :(

I love order pad kie mauw and their curry is tasty. This is the best place to go if you're hungry and craving cheap asian food. Try to order on the phone prior arrival so you don't have to wait in line. During finals week or dead week, this place may not be the best place to go since it'll be crowded and you may ended up have to wait in line for almost an hour.

Cheap and good Thai food :) I really like this place, whenever i go to Asian ghetto i always go to Thai Basil to get food. 

Everything I've tried from them has been good.

I really enjoy this place.  Whenever I want some Thai, I usually like to come here.  The only reason I'm giving this place 3 instead of 5 stars is because the quality of the food seems to have changed in the past year, so some of the dishes I usually order aren't the same and not necessarily for the better.  But it's a great place to eat and the portions are pretty good for the price.
Been here twice and my general fear of Asian food has been alleviated. Very hearty meals with a sizeable portion of rice.

Situated within the "Asian Ghetto," I thought at first that the kind of food would be of similar mediocre quality to the restaurants nearby.  However, I was wrong to think so.  It has some tasty Pad Thai, and has a good assortments of ingredients to complement the seasoning.  I have also ordered pineapple fried rice and curry, which were both pretty tasty as well.

Although the food gets 4 star, the rest of the place is lackluster.  The lines are long, and there isn't much room for sitting.  Furthermore, regardless of dining in or not, the food is served in a to-go container.  Lastly, the workers are always in the same foul mood and quick to call your name and move to the next person.

Yes Thai Basil, yes. Not ashamed to say this was my favorite place in all of Asian Ghetto. Their food has consistently been the most delicious and flavorful out of all the places, which try to mask their averageness with cheap prices, oversized portions, or lots of unnecessary sauce. Thai Basil just gives you what you want, the way you like it.

There have been many nights when I bring back a bag of Thai Basil food and it's fantastic when I get it home and dig in. There is little wait for your food aside from the long lines of students who might be in front of you, but again, long lines are usually a good sign people. If you're willing to wait during the busy periods, you won't be disappointed.

Everything is good. Everything is (relatively) cheap. Dinner for $6.50? And a filling one at that? I approve.

Try Basil Chili Chicken, Pad See-Ew (spelling?), and pineapple curry chicken if you like it sweet-ish. Thai iced tea is just OK.

Fast, Affordable, and Delicious! 
What more can I say? This place does not disappoint! Their pad thai and basil/curry fried rice is simply scrumptious, and great portion! 
They do get pretty busy and packed very quickly, due to their small place. I recommend taking it to go, other than that, give this place a try!

It's not a bad place to go for a quick eat, because it's so close to the university and they have cheap ($5-$7) dishes. But I wish they would have bigger portions -- I never feel full after eating at that place. I can get bigger volume from Steve's BBQ right next door (at around the same price), or from Naan 'n Curry down the street (for about $3 more).

Woooh! The best and most easily accessible Thai food in the UC Berkeley campus! They have the usual array of Thai dishes. It is reasonably priced and made well. The portions are typical of things from the Durant Food Court, very standard. The only downside to Thai Basil is the wait times. It can range from 10-30 minutes. Besides the waiting, the food is great, the prices are cheap, and the taste is there! Definitely recommend it! As for what to get, it's really up to you. There are a ton of choices and everything that I have tried (which is a lot of things!) is delicious! For spicy food lovers, I would go with the Basil Chili Chicken. If you're in an adventerous mood, try the pineapple fried rice, it's a nice blend of the flavor of pineapple, the fried taste of the rice, and the grilled chicken meat!

4 star pad thai!!! Great for students on a budget or a quick weekday take away meal to eat at home in front of the TV.

If you ask for the food spicy... be prepared.  I loved the spicy version of their food but it can be a little overwhelming if you don't enjoy the sweet burn.

So tasty.
It's cheap for a reason...

Returned here one night after 11 years since graduating from Cal. Still the same crowd and menu. It's good Thai food if you're in the are. I got the basil chicken eggplant..kinda salty but not as spicy as it looked.

One of my preferred stops in the "Asian Ghetto".

They are open relatively late and accept credit card, which is always great when you're on a food run with friends. Like most places in the food court, you get generous portions at a reasonable price, though don't expect anything gastronomically exciting.

I like the Pad See Ew and Basil Chicken most, though I like most of their other dishes as well. Their Tom Yum wasn't very appetizing though, and I think their meat is on the cheap side, but it gets the job done.

I've been here twice and it's one of my favorite places to eat when I'm on the south side of the UC Berkeley Campus.

It's a pretty small place and there's usually quite a few people in there (which is a good sign), but I've never had to wait too long for my food.  And if the seats inside are all taken, there's several tables and benches outside.

The first time I came here, I had the vegetarian pad thai, which was quite tasty.  With all the Thai places in Berkeley, I'm sure there's places that make it better, but I didn't have any complaints.  

The second time I came here, I had the vegetarian thai basil eggplant, which was delicious.  I highly recommend this dish. And it's a very large serving, so if you're not too hungry, you'll likely have leftovers to take home with you. 

I definitely recommend trying this place.

Definitely my favorite place to eat in Durant Square.  I personally think it's on the pricey end for a college student, but you definitely get what you pay for - a tasty and good-sized meal.  I often get Pad See Ew or Pad Thai, and I'm satisfied every time!

Absolutely love it! I come here many times during the semester. The food's always nice and hot when you get it and the food prep time is short. Great portions for cheap!
 I really suggest the vegetarian curries...the ones marked with a pepper are actually spicy! (I have a high tolerance for spiciness) You can't go wrong choosing a curry. All are delicious.
Great Berkeley staple. Probably had Thai Basil every week or every other week as an undergrad at Cal. I am a fan.

RELIABLE LATE-NIGHT THAI FOOD

I stop by here occasionally when I am craving late-night Thai food.  I usually get my food to go because the small dining room is crowded, noisy, and bright.

Pad Thai
Tonight, I ordered the pad thai and I thought it was very respectable.  A little stingy with the shrimp and chicken but it was not too sweet and had a little kick to it because I asked them to make it spicy.

They make the food to order so you may have a short wait.

I come here sometimes, and I usually have something concerning pineapple. Like pineapple fried rice, or pineapple curry, because the reason I ever feel like Thai is because I want Asian food that is sweet and  spiced right. Food is pretty good, atmosphere is kinda cheap and grimy, but its all students anyhow so what can you say? Food is made kind of slow, but its all made up for in the food.  And when you look at a restaurant, looks mean little compared to food. So the food is good and cheap and definitely makes Thai Basil a good place to spend a late night dinner. Their order over the phone thing doesn't work out quite well since its pretty loud there, so you'll want to order in person.

Probably my favorite place in Asian Ghetto!  I hit up this place regularly - in between classes, on my way home from work, or delivered straight to my door through CampusMunch.com (sooo convenient during finals).

Prices are not bad & the food is veryyy good - I've never been disappointed.  Dining in is nice because of the complimentary hot tea.  Bonus: the food still tastes good 15-20 minutes later when you get it for take-out.

I have tried a good portion of the menu & my favorite things to order are still the chicken pad thai & tom kha.  Everything else I tried (all the curries, fried rice, wonton things, etc.) was good too - just only so much room in my stomach for yummy Thai food! 

My only complaint would be it's a bit of a wait for your food, but that's only cuz they make it on the spot for you.  Overall, definitely a place to check out if you are in Berkeley!

Not my favorite Thai place in Berkeley, but it's close and convenient. Actually, scratch that. Wait times here are RIDIC. It usually takes ~30minutes to get your food, and by that point, the hunger pangs have disappeared and you're irritable and moody. I would take the advice of other Yelpers and call in your order, if you plan to go here.

Newbie? You can't go wrong with the Pad Thai. I love my food spicy so I drown it in sriracha hot sauce and it tastes DELICIOUS. I like some of the chicken and rice combos too.

In the heart of the Asian Ghetto, I was so glad I was introduced to this Thai food haven! My friend from the area recommended the Pad Thai so I was all over it. For only $7, I say that the dish is a steal! The Pad Thai was de-lish! It consists of shrimp, chicken, tofu, cilantro, and my favorite, crunchy delight, peanuts! The portion was huge, but it was so good, I forced myself to eat it all. My only qualm about the place is that the service is not the best. I mean I guess they can afford to be a little hostile because there is always a mob of customers. *Please be nicer to your customers when they ask for more jalepenos. Thanks! :)

Overall, the food was delicious, the complimentary Thai tea made my meal that much better, and you just cannot beat the price!

Ordered the pad thai- a dish that often never fails me. I was surprised by the amount of food I got; for a little over $6 at lunchtime, it's hard to top this. Washed it down with an ice cold can of Coke. My lunch date got the red curry, which was also delish, albeit a smaller portion.

I really, really like Thai Basil. I have always left satisfied. The price is more than reasonable and the food is OH SO GOOD. For around $6, I got a huge portion of tofu pad see-ew that I ended up taking home because they gave me so much! I definitely recommend this place for college students and people who just like to get what they pay for.

Weak, weak, weak. Oversalted, and they raised their prices about 4 years ago without upping their food quality. The abundance of rice given has been well documented, in lieu of quality goodies. I don't know how all the Berkeley undergrads are duped into thinking that this is good food. If you order without salt, it will be tasty enough... perhaps the only recommendation I can give if you must eat here.

When I was living overseas, I would get serious cravings for Thai Basil's pad thai. I really like this place. Sure, there are tons of other thai options in the east bay, but this place is inexpensive, tasty and convenient. The portions are big enough to keep you supplied for two meals, in my opinion. You can watch them make your food if you feel liek standing at the counter.
I wish it wasn't in the asian ghetto, though. Make sure you pee before you go. the bathroom is next to the dumpster and it REEKS.

this place is good, it's always busy with students during lunch and dinner time
but it's definitely worth of wait :D
I'm not a big fan of going to Asian Ghetto to eat, but if I do go, then this
is the only place that I go to.

My rule of thumb is if there's a long wait, it's gotta be aMAZing.  Thai Basil however is an exception; it's only got decent food

During peak hours, Thai Basil always has a longest line in asian ghetto This is a very popular place to eat, but the quality of the food is not justified by the long wait.  I suggest beating the rush or eating late at this place to save yourself time that can be better spent elsewhere.

My personal favorite here is Pad See Ew Chicken.  For those who don't know what it is, it's kinda like chow fun.  Slightly greasy but still enjoyable.   Sometimes I'm still left hungry after eating it.  Suggestions for other popular dishes are Pad Thai and Pineapple Fried Rice.

I absolutely looooove Thai Basil. Usually whenever I visit my friends that are in Berkeley and we're broke I would choose to go here. Their basil chicken is amazing, and the Pad See Ew is the best I've ever had (although the broccoli is a bit hard, but I don't mind). It's cheap and the service is fast.

I walked here with a couple friends from class a few days ago. We only had a hour lunch break (errr... actually more like 50 min because our professor went overtime). It really isn't enough time to sit down and enjoy lunch. We were looking for something quick and tasty that would be affordable for struggling college students. Luckily the friends I was with are Cal students throughout the normal school year, they suggested this place located in the "asian ghetto".

The place is no frills thai food and you can easily tell that they cater to students. I asked the lady behind the cash register how long it would take to get Chicken Pad See Ewe and she said it would only take 5 minutes. Normally when people say 5 minutes they mean 10, but when Thai Basil says 5 minutes they mean it! The food came out speedy and hot. The pan fried flat noodles were yummy and had a nice gummy texture to them. Could've used more chicken & veggies though!

This place is good for lunch but for about a dollar or two more (per dish) you could probably eat at a full service sit down Thai restaurant. If you're just looking for a place to grab a quick bite then this is good! Another downfall is they only accept cash. Ugh...

They give a generous portion of pad thai, and it is full of flavor. 
Check it out.
Great food at a reasonable price . Keep in mind this place is cash only and everything is self serve.

I came here after reading some of the good reviews on Yelp. I have to say, I was slightly disappointed. The pad thai was pretty bland and there was too much sauce. The chicken was the driest I've ever had, and the only redeeming part was the shrimp and tofu. Maybe next time I will try the  pad see ew, which a lot of yelpers say is the best dish here. But I probably won't come back unless I'm really really hungry. Also, the lady who gave me my food and took my receipt seemed grumpy and moody. Her attitude was just awful, and that's why I docked off another star.

Portions are resonable for the price. The food is acceptable, not exceptional. The pineapple fried rice has a curry taste (but tastes good overall), and the garlic pepper chicken is a little dry (has sauce but the chicken itself is dry). The cashew tofu is good, but if you don't like a sweet taste, it's not for you. They allow a selection of 'mild', 'medium' or 'hot'  for the spicy dishes. Food is cooked on the spot and although freshly cooked, this requires a wait, depending on how  many people are in front of you.

Pretty good--probably the best place in the ghetto, if that's worth anything. I'm on Northside and don't make it here much anymore...I went the other day, and the pineapple fried rice, pad thai and curry were/are still good, but it seems a little pricey for the quality/portion size now. Oh, well. I'll probably be back now and then.

Best Chicken Basil I've ever had.
I'm sold.

'Nuff said.

The food was good, the portions were good, the Thai tea was very plentiful, and it was open pretty late night. So why is this place getting only 1 star? Because of the trip to the bathroom a short while after eating here...

I brought my friend here tonight and we waited THIRTY-FIVE minutes for our food! TOTES RIDIC!! I don't think I've ever waited for that long at Thai Basil ever...it's usually at most 15 minutes... food wasn't worth the wait. Didn't know if they were killing the chicken as we were ordering or what, but we got so restless just waiting for the food. It wasn't bad though. Good sized portions, but way too salty.

I have tried more than half of the dishes available for Vegetarians here; Vegetarian Pad Thai, Vegetarian Pad See Ew, Vegetarian Mad Kee Mau, Basil Eggplant Tofu, Pepper Garlic Tofu, Basil Thai Fried Rice, Vegetarian Yellow Curry, Basil Tofu, and maybe two other dishes I forgot the name of  ...

EVERYTHING HAS SATISFIED MY TASTE BUDS EVERYTIMEEE.
AND IT'S PRETTY CHEAP.
AND IT'S A GOOD PORTION.
AND IT'S CLOSE TO BERKELEY CAMPUS.

I guess the only downer would be the employees/owners; because they work practically everyday of the week, their stress levels are high and they become short tempered or annoyed with the customers every now and then ...

Thai Basil was one of my favorite places to eat when I was an undergrad at Berkeley. Relative to the places nearby, you get a lot of bang for your buck here. The food is inexpensive and the portions are always very generous. They have a lot of options to the menu, and the food is friggin tastyyyyy. I admit though that the food does tend to be a little greasy, and sometimes they skimp on the meat parts or vegetables. However, I think giving this place anything lower than three or four stars it totally uncalled for. It's not lie that the food is delicious even though it's not the highest quality. Besides, what are you expecting for $5 to $8? If you want real thai food, go to Thai House around the corner, but if you want a quick, cheap, good meal, thai basil is great. It is what it is.

If you're craving thai food, but don't want to try something too terrifyingly new, Thai Basil is perfect. The food is unchallenging but tasty, and the portions are generous. The major problems are the lack of seating and a cashier that doesn't have a sense of urgency even when there are 20 hungry students waiting in line.

This review is long overdue since I have been coming here since 2007!!! I think that was before I even had a yelp account!

I love this place because it is cheap in terms of cost, but not in terms of quality!

this is my FAVORITE PAD THAI in the bay area... and trust me, I've tried a lot!  I also like making it a bit spicy by asking them!  Its great!

The fact that it's near Cal helps because it's good food at a great price.  I don't know why they stopped accepting debit cards, but always bring some cash!  After, check out king pin for dessert, or of course, CREAM.  I'm glad I work in Berkeley so that I can always get my fix!

Best Thai food I have tried.  Their Pad See Eew chicken is delicious and their cashew nut chicken is just as good.  They are always busy during dinner and lunch times, but it is worth the wait....most of the time.

Sometimes, it doesn't come out as good.  I  haven't been able to figure out which one of the cooks isn't as good.  I've narrowed it down to the tall skinny guy or the lady that usually serves. 

Even though their food is great, their service is HORRIBLE.  They have no customer service whatsoever.  The lady will yell at you if you even hesitate for a second, 1 SECOND, when it is your turn to order.  Sometimes there is no line and she still says "  If you not ready, why you in line?!"  I have seen her yell at many customers because they are not ready or because they use the numbers they put on their plates to order instead of the name.  She says, " I don't know the numbers!  Tell me the name!"

I can go on...

But the food is GOOD!  haha.  

My advice, look at what you want first, then order and pay. Don't expect them to call out orders in order.  And enjoy.  (and if you don't look like you can use chopsticks, you automatically only get a fork. I have sat there and watched!  haha. )

I've been here several times and somehow it still hasn't grown on me. I still haven't found a favorite dish here yet, I just think the food is ok. I've definitely been to other better Thai places. The only good thing is that this place is closer than other places.

This is probably my favorite place to go in the Asian ghetto, but that isn't saying much.  I've had several things here in the past- pad thai, pad see ew, pineapple fried rice...  and this past visit I had the combination fried rice.  The portion sizes are good for their price, but it seems to me as if the quality is hit or miss.  Sometimes it's decent, sometimes so-so, etc.  This past time my fried rice was quite greasy and didn't want to finish it.  Three stars based on decent food in the past.  As I like to say, you get what you pay for, so don't expect too much!
Great Pad See Ew! Decent service. The venue itself is a little depressing, but it's worth the take out. Slightly overpriced.

Discovered this place late in my college career at Cal, but it is definitely one of my favorites!  I always get the same thing - Vegetarian Pad Kee Mao with no egg - and they have never messed up my order.  The food is hot, delicious, and cheap!  The line can get long if you come at peak hours and the tables inside aren't always the cleanest, but I don't care at all because the food is that good!  I always enjoy coming back here to eat while visiting friends still in school.

Thai Basil is far and away the best option in the asian ghetto, and the line out the door reinforces that fact. Most people circle the ghetto a few times before coming back to Thai Basil. Theres just something about it thats both delicious and comforting.

The garlic pepper chicken, as others have already pointed out, is where its at. I really really wish I went to Berkeley, just for Top Dog and Thai Basil. But I digress...

Besides, any restaurant in a location far and wide described as the 'asian ghetto' has to be some level of awesome. On top of that, this is the BEST food in said ghetto, so thats even more bonus points.

So there was a little sign on the front of this hole in the wall that said 'People Love us on Yelp!' so it sort of begs for a review. Cheap eats, but not too amazing Thai food. The pad thai was excessively greasy and sticky, and absolutely demanded that I buy a sweet drink to wash it down. The meal took awhile to prepare- around twenty minutes, and they screwed up my friends order and had to redo it. So, maybe the best thai place to eat at on telegraph, but that's not saying much..

TIP: Come here if you want relatively fast (if the line is short), relatively cheap (better deals elsewhere though), relatively delicious (lots of salt and grease) Thai food--basically as a last resort. 

Do yourself a favor and Yelp the other Thai places around in the area unless you want a plate of grease and MSG. Granted, it will be a heaping, steaming, filling plate of grease and MSG, but do you really want to eat it all and then fall into a deep food coma afterwards? Works in a pinch (especially if you have self-control and divide your meal into small portions so you can save it for later meals) but there's much, much better Thai food nearby. 

(I do think you should try this place at least once though, especially if you're just discovering Berkeley or if you're a freshman at Cal. You will be addicted for a few months, or a school year. But then you'll realize that better tasting Thai food exists..!)

Located in the Asian restaurant Ghetto near the Berkeley campus, this place is always bustling with customers, especially when the school is in session. It is a good place for take-out order.  There are also some tables where you can sit.  I love their pineapple fried rice and tofu with cashew.

Thai Basil lacks in efficiency, but you don't really go here expecting much. When I go to the Asian Ghetto aka Durant Food Court, Thai Basil is normally one of my top choices. It's not saying much, as joints here are just meh, but Thai Basil gives cheap fix for students.

Pad See Ew cannot go wrong.

It doesn't take card and the portions tend to be on the slightly smaller side when in comparison to other thai places. Still, the food was pretty solid and the staff there are typically very friendly to me which goes a long way in my book!

Pretty greasy, but their pad see ew is really tasty.  Better than some of the more expensive places in the area.  It's good if you want fast food thai.  Their curry is generally not that great though in my experience.
Not the best Thai food ever but I had a yummy eggplant dish. It feels really cluttered and hot in there, but it is in a college town so whatevs.

Their food is too fast, too standard, and a little Americanized: a lot of oil and MSG. I've only been here once and I don't remember what I ordered (I think the tofu eggplant dish). It came with the standard side of rice and the usual sweet and sour sauce found on many Asian dishes in the Asian Ghetto. Sure, food is cheap, but service was okay and the place is a bit dirty and crowded. When the lady called out my order number and I went to get my order, she wouldn't give me my dish since I wasn't the one who ordered it (my friend ordered it for me), which got me pretty ticked off and gave me an unpleasant first impression of the place. Other than that, I love how they give free tea.

I've had consistently good food from Thai Basil.  I have really only had the pad thai and pad see eaw, but both are good enough to keep me coming back.  The pad thai isn't very spicy, but I'm sure you could ask for it like that or add something to it.  I'm not a huge fan of the atmosphere, but it is quick and easy to get the food to go.  Most dishes are $5-$6, so it is also very affordable.  Great place to go if you want Thai but without having to pay extra to eat at a sit down place.

Like the food here a lot. Pad Thai is my favorite in the whole bay area since i judge every Thai restaurant on their Pad Thai. Other winners include Basil Eggplant Chicken, Pad Kee Mao, and the Combination Fried Rice. Any of these are tasty and you can't go wrong.

The unfortunate thing is the rush during dinner. I waited one time for 30 min for my food and all the people in my party have finished eating.

It's a small place, so prepare to take it to go if it ever gets crowded. I've only came here twice, but never had trouble grabbing a seat. I had the Pad See-ew Chicken and Garlic Chicken, which didn't disappoint my taste buds.

Nothing fantastic about this place really.

I have been coming here for almost 10 years now and have finally been able to resist getting one of my favorites and try a new dish.  Since I was in the mood for soup, I got the tom yum noodle soup, which I can happily add to my list of dishes I have tried and liked at Thai Basil.  The pad see ew is still the best around and is what I get from here 95% of the time.

Well, given the area - Asian ghetto near UC Campus - it's a pretty decent spot. 
It actually is one of my favourites for lunch near campus - although the average quality of spots around campus is pretty low...

I always take the Basil Eggplant Chicken, which is also supposed to be the dish which earned them a couple of awards- don't ask me which kind of awards though... I like the sweet-sour sauce in which eggplants and chicken are marinated. Also, I think this is a really good combination with their steam rice. 

My friend usually gets the Basil Chicken, which is basically the same as above without eggplants and with a different sauce - that too seems to be pretty yummy. 

Given the low price, it's definitely a decent spot where to have a quick lunch.

Delicious food, good service, good price. 
Personally, I don't like the seating though.

I'm slightly hesitant to give Thai Basil 4 stars.  I will explain this later in the review.

Thai Basil is my favorite Thai restaurant in Berkeley.  Perhaps it's because it was the first one I went to upon arriving here, but I've always had good experiences here.  Other Thai restaurants may be better, but most are generally inaccessible for students (particularly if you live on southside, because many good thai restaurants are on northside).  

My recommended item?  #23, Pad Kee Mow!  (I think that's how you spell it??)  Came here again with a friend and it tasted great!  I love the wide, flat rice noodles and the texture is chewy and the noodles separate easily (a must have for good flat noodle dishes).  I've had other items here and there around their menu (i.e. lunch special [2-3 items w/rice for $5.75?), some noodle soups, etc...) and I haven't been disappointed.

But as I mentioned earlier, why am I hesitant to give 4 stars?  First, I feel like the food is getting more oily with each successive time I eat their food.  Second, the service seems to be getting slower and slower...Last, Thai Basil is now CASH ONLY.  I found that out today, but luckily had just enough cash to pay.  

Let's hope Thai Basil improves their speed and possibly go back to accepting credit cards.

Now that I have been a student here for a couple  I will say that no place that I have been in Berkeley beats Thai Basil if you are looking for some good food that will also fill you up for cheap. Its not *amazing* but after a long day of classes/studying its pretty damn close =]

It's nice that you can see the chefs make your meal on the spot. This place is always super busy, so expect to wait at least twenty minutes. I ordered the pad thai before, but it wasn't too memorable. The second time, I ordered the green curry with pork which came with A LOT OF RICE. Like, enough rice for the dinner and the next morning. The curry itself was tasty and fragrant, and not too spicy (I chose mild). I have to admit, it was a bit on the greasy side because the curry sauce had a layer of oil on top the next day. 


Oh, and free thai tea! Doesn't come with milk but you can add sugar. It smells so wonderful.

Their food is pretty tasty but haven't been here as much since they've raised prices. Would not eat in there since it gets pretty crowded and I never liked eating in the ghetto in the first place. I like their pad see ew and eggplant dishes. Those are worth coming back for.

It's decent for Asian Ghetto quality. I had the green curry chicken today, and I thought the curry was well spiced--good fragrance, right amount of hotness, and a bit sweet from the coconut and basil. Portions are very generous.

Well first, the cashier hung up on me when I tried to order takeout.  Okay but I really want some pineapple fried rice so I called back.  Twenty minutes later, I get canned pineapple and some sketchy shrimp mixed with rice that's undercooked.  It was so bad I had to throw most of it away.

Aww...why is everyone so mean to Thai Basil?

They make a great Pad Kee Mao here. All the spicy dishes here are great.

Good portions for a great price.

Most of the employees are unfriendly, rude, hasty, and impatient (especially the old hag at the counter). The food is good, and by good I mean it is cooked in such a way that it -resembles- authentic Thai food that you can only find in San Francisco, but doesn't truly reach authentic (you can taste the MSG). 

Thai Food Quality: Reaches near-authenticity but fails to commercialization of its flavors (MSG, added sweetening)
Price: Moderate; Leaves you feeling whether or not you should have spent those $8 dollars somewhere else (somewhere better?)
Environment: sucks
Service: Rude

If you don't mind the artificial flavor enhancing, then this is the place for you.
Yummy Pad Thai for about $7. The portions are fair, the food is delicious, and the service is fast enough. Thank you. Exactly what I want from a Thai restaurant!

Best Pad Thai ive had in CALIFORNIA!!! 
this includes price, portion, and taste!!! 

mmm mm not sure why other thai places make their pad thai so gummy!
blah.

Anyway, five stars for the Pad Thai alone. I have ordered this every time for 236282362846 times! :)
This is best Thai restaurant around.  Our favorites are Pad See Ew, Basil chicken. This place is awesome.

I went here a decent amount when I was a freshman living on southside. I have tried the pad thai, fried rice, and pad see ew. I like the beef pad see ew with veggies (broccoli) the best. The beef can be a little tough to chew sometimes and I don't like how much oil is used. The flavor is good but I would get stomachaches afterward a lot. Also,the wait can be pretty annoying sometimes-lasting up to about 20 minutes. Still a fan though. The price is good for the amount you get.

My god, the pad thai here is sooo good.  I used to dutifully go here for dinner nearly every night, and nearly every night, I almost always got the pad thai, and it was usually the highlight of my day.  Even now, sitting in LA, I still crave it and will always make sure to stop by to get me some pad thai.  The portions are generous and it's cheap, particularly for pad thai.

Went here on a Monday evening at around 8 pm and there was still a line, so I can't imagine what it would be like around a more traditional dining time. Regardless, it only took us around 5 minutes to get our food and the pad thai was pretty decent -- not the best i've had in berkeley, but not the worst. the outside sitting area was pretty busy, but we waited for around a few minutes and a couple of tables opened up. overall a decent place. probably the best part about this thai place is its location. 

cash only

in the asian ghetto; open late. 

try: thai basil rice dish is good, but a bit spicy. 

i wouldnt get the pad thai (and i loooove the stuff). the combination fried rice is pretty good and very filling. its got peas, carrots, a little (like 2 small pieces) beef and chicken. oh... it comes with some odd white, gelatinous mini-pineapple shaped thing. ewwwuhhh. 

and after i was done with my meal (and delicious pomegranate honest tea), this old thai woman comes up to me and asks for my receipt and tells me that i didnt pay for the freekin drink, as if its my fault she didnt ring it up. so she stands there til i hand over my credit card for the additional $1.75 to be charged.
The tom kha gai soup is about the best thing you'll find to cure a hangover. And it's good for sober days too!
I love this place. After several years I recently discovered the Korean BBQ pork, which is my new favorite.
The Pad Thai was delicious!

Pepper Garlic chicken is the diggidy-dank.

Only time I've eaten in the restaurant I made the dumb mistake of sitting under a fan...I was eating satay sticks and halfway through my meal all the sauces had cooled off and start coagulating...wack, but my own fault.

Services is butt slow but the food is good.  I once had to hop behind the counter to void a credit card transaction they had screwed up.  Absolutely ridiculous that I had better knowledge of their credit card machine than they did...but absolutely hillarious

My first meal in Berkeley was at Thai Basil, and I liked it from the start. The food is very tasty and the workers are very nice. The food usually takes awhile (mostly because the place is so popular) but it's worth the wait! I love any of their dishes with eggplant, as well as the Pineapple Fried Rice.

The pad thai was very good.
The only problem was the small space filled with lots of people.
A good place for take outs! =D

Came here with a friend because we had been craving Thai and it was one of the only places open at the time (around 9:30pm on a Sunday night).  We got Pad Prik King, a somewhat spicy curry with chicken and green beans.  It was very tasty, however it was some of the oiliest Thai food I've ever seen.  It's also cash only, which is a big detractor for a grad student like me who never has cash.  I'd come here again, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

Their Pepper Garlic Chicken is really addicting, not sure exactly what they put in there, but my guess is a powdered sugar.  Some of the other dishes are ok, but the Pepper Garlic Chicken is the bread and butter.

Side note:  

Berkeley's a minefield of delicious restaurants that will please anyone's tastes.  Thai Basil lies in the heart of what is known to be the "Asian Ghetto" (just a small alley lined with restaurants).  The alley has a few benches placed for outside dining and can appear to be pretty dirty, but it's a popular spot for students.  Affordable dining right off campus on durant.

Don't come here all the time. It's so greasy, you'll regret it once the euphoria has worn off, but when you're sitting infront of a huge plate of pad thai or pad see ew, you'll forget all about MSG warnings and potential heart failure. If you want Thai in Berkeley, this is the place to be.

Great value late-night food.

Near UC (and King Pin donuts.)

Everything I've ever tried here has been reliable enjoyable Thai food. Not a gourmet explosion of joy in every bite, but definitely a good value for the price.

Very noisy, young crowded. Be warned. Not good for crowds cause there is usually one there already.

This place has 4yelp stickers, so I assumed they'd be pretty good, and I was craving Pad Thai so it was PERFECT. I got the Pad Thai, medium hot, to-go. It seemed kind of dry to me. I will always love Jasmine Thai's Pad Thai (in San Jose). 

I also had some of the Pineapple Fried Rice, which was ok. It seemed hella damp/wet compared to my Pad Thai :(

My friend ordered Tom Yum Noodle Soup, but they accidentally gave him Thai Noodle Soup. Apparently, it was really bad for him.

Pricing was pretty decent for the portion.
This is easily my favorite pad see-ew chicken!  Not the nicest people, but you usually get food to-go anyways.

I was never a big fan of Thai food and I was constantly baffled by people's reactions to the mediocre cuisine until I experienced Thai Basil.

It's located in the heart of UCB's campus so it is very very affordable. My favorite (and the ONLY dish I ever order) is the basil eggplant chicken.  It is the perfect concoction of sweet and salty goodness.  The basil sauce is so scrumptious that you can't help but devour all of the white jasmine rice that's served with it.  The sauce saturates the eggplant completely and soaks in all the flavor.  I always save some for my last bite.  

My bf was the one who introduced me to this delicious gem.  I think the only comparable place would be Osha Thai. 

Sometimes I excuse myself and say that I'm just wayy too tired to cook just we can go to Thai Basil for some hearty good Thai food.  Just thinking about it makes my mouth water!

This place was horrible, the service wasn't the issue but the food was not at all anything you could call "Thai." I got the vege pad thai and it tasted like BBQ! It was so surprising, I was more excited to get a slurpee at 7-11 than eat the rest of the dish..
pad see ew was bland...dont think they live up to all the hype.()_)

I admit that I have only tried the Pad Thai, but I have also had authentic Thai food and it definitely does not do justice to the the amazing tradition of complex and skillfully balanced flavors in Thai cuisine. It was too sweet and I think it needed a little more tamarind...

Tried this place yesterday. It was 4 or 5pm but the restaurant had a long line of hungry people.

The food is reasonably priced and there are many vegetarian options (basically whatever meat can be replaced by tofu, so you get tofu green/yellow/red curry, pad thai with tofu etc). 

I ended up having the mixed vegetable with basil stir fry. It was okay - a bit salty but generally yummy.  Given it's cheap and conveniently located on campus, I will go back.

Pretty good food if you're up for the wait and a certain distinct heavy/oily feel to their dishes. My favorites: basil eggplant tofu or chicken and pad see ew.. The pad thai doesn't taste like traditional pad thai, but it's still good. In general, a good choice if you're nearby and don't have cash (they accept credit cards).

I am bias toward this place just due to my college memories here.  Nonetheless, it is still one of the better Thai place in the area, especially with its pricing.  It tasted just as good as other places that charge almost double as here.  Not to mention its fast.

I usually order the ginger chicken or pad thai, and claim a table and just chat away with my buddies for hours.  There is nobody that would rush you out or even care how long you been at the same tables.  As long as you bus yourself by the time you leave.

I did try their sister store in dublin, which taste as good but has a higher seat turn over rate especially at lunch.  Guess I shouldn't just try to claim a seat in a restaurant for the sake of chatting forever anymore.

Thai Basil is my favorite place to eat in the Durant Food Court (hey, that's its name, yo!).  It is a little disappointingly slow, but it'll serve you the same dishes you expect, and you will like it! :)

The noodle dishes are delicious, and if you get a curry dish, it will come with a nice serving of curry and a ton of rice.  They don't skimp!

This is definitely one of the most popular restaurants on Southside, and it's easy to see why.  If you have more mobility/time to go further afield, you'll find better food, but in student territory, Thai Basil is king.

Btw, there are plenty of delicious vegetarian options here.  All the eggplant dishes are A++.

This review is based on the Pad Thai. Like someone else has said, a thai restuarant should only be as good as the Pad Thai. 

This dish was pretty gross. I was looking forward to some Thai food and I was near the Asian Ghetto, so why not? What's up with the flavor? I can't even describe it. The Pad Thai I normally order from other places didn't taste like this. The awful flavor was so strong that I only had 2 bites. I'd rather go next door and get the Chinese food instead. The portions were also small as hell. NO thanks.
No one can make pad prik king like this place!!! great food large portions

they only take cash, and it's a bit pricey, but still it's a decent place.
I recommend thai basil chili chicken.

I've DEFINITELY experienced better. 

Even though it was late night, they gave us a really meager portion of Ginger chicken. $7 down the drain for a whole lotta rice. Thai House on Channing has always taken the win over Thai Basil for pretty much everything (besides being a later night option).
I like their Basil Fried Rice. One of the cheap and delicious places in Durant square.

Thai Basil is one of two safe choices in the Asian Ghetto, the other being Gypsy's. The reviews here say that prices have gone up and quality down recently, but I haven't come enough to tell the difference in either.

I ordered #6, the Cashew Nut Chicken, for lunch on a Sunday. It costed $6.50, and came with steamed rice. There were onions and carrots mixed in with the cashew nuts and chicken.  Portions were satisfactory, and the taste was good, although the amount of flavor in the different ingredients was uneven. It also wasn't healthy, but I didn't feel that bad because I didn't eat a lot of the oily-looking sauce.

The service people don't speak the best English, but they are nice. Food does take a little while to come out, though. I waited about 10 minutes with there not being a huge line when I ordered.

There are about ten tables inside the restaurant, each seating about four, but you can eat at the wooden tables outside. Be warned that, at least on the weekends, there is usually water on the table benches at lunchtime that you will need to wipe off with napkins if you don't want your pants to get soaked.

My go-to place for Thai whenever I'm in Berkeley's Asian Ghetto. A friend took me here a few years ago and I've been a fan since. I usually go for the Pad Thai or Pad See Ew and it's not bad (not the best I've had but not the worst either) and I usually get it to-go. My most recent visit, I ate in with some friends; the space was small and it was rather dark inside, even during the day.

Oh and this place is cash only!

I think this might be one of the cheapest places to get Thai in Berkeley.  I've never tried the lunch special, but they look like a good deal.  all of the other entrees are very reasonably priced and they give good portions.  Also a plus: they take card.

The pad see ew and yellow curry are quite good.  It's also nice to see a place that doesn't charge you for the rice separately. I mean honestly, am I going to eat curry without rice?!  Their pad thai was a bit off for me.  Lacking in flavor and a bit... dry if that makes any sense?  

One downside is that it takes quite a while to get your food, even when the place is relatively empty.  It can be a half hour wait during peak hours.  I only recommend going when you're not in a hurry.
Honestly, if you're just craving some cheap thai food that is not lacking the flavors and grease. This is the place to go!
I found a piece of glass in my food. Enough said.

As a transferring Cal student, I like to check out the eateries in the area to prepare myself for school.  Me and my cousin came here since she was craving Thai food at the time.  This place is hidden in the back of Durant square.

We ordered some safe bets with Pad Thai and fried Gyoza.  Both of them were tasty but nothing really that sets it apart from the rest of the Thai places I've eaten at.  Perhaps I have to try something else to see if anything perks my taste buds.

I'm only giving them three stars instead of 4 because now they only accept cash.  Are you kidding me!!!  I rather would have had them slightly raise the prices than to not accept credit!  Well, guess more business for Berkeley Thai House, especially with Thai Noodle II having to close down because of the fire...

Price and quality are decent. The wait can take a while depending on time of day. Portions are generous. Stand by the pick up section in order to hear them call your number. 

It would help if you came with a group so you can score tables and seats. They use a lot of oil so if you are not a fan of greasy goodness, refrain.

I usually get the basil fried rice with chicken. Very flavorful. Plenty of chicken. Ample amount of vegetables. Could have more rice though.

Great food, great people behind the counter, and free tea!! try their coconut soup! i thought i wouldn't like it cuz coconut in soup doesnt sound tasty, but that soup really hit the spot! pad see ew is bomb and their basil chili chicken is cracken too!!
i dont understand why i always order pad thai from here even though i know it tastes like ketchup. it gets me every single time.

(+):
- Their pad see ew is pretty good. Came here often for dinner. 
- Prices are decent

(-):
- Don't come here if you're super hungry. Takes forever to get your food. They definitely do not do first-come, first-serve system...

(- - - - - - - -):
- Found pubic hair in my pad see ew. Never came back again.

It's okay... I had a really bad impression last time with their lunch special--basically leftovers from the night before. Pad Thai noodles were all soggy, the chicken was dry, grease started coagulating at the bottom of the container... gross stuff...

This time, they improved a little. At least the green curry and cashew chicken was pre-made on the same day, yet I don't understand why that lady at the cashier had to be so mean.. raised her voice and yelled at me with saliva shooting at my face: "so you want num-ba won and two no fore YES? NUM-BA WAT? OK! two and fore! Now pay."

Simply put: the food is cheap.  There is really nothing special about the place except it closes late and it is in the Asian Cuisine area in UC Berkeley.  The food is exactly what you would expect from a cheap thai place.  They are semi-helpful with dietary needs.  Just because I gave it three stars does not mean I would not go back to enjoy a cheap and simple thai meal.  I would recommend this place.

The food I had here last night was a lot like me after 4 hours at Bears Lair:
a hot vegeterian mess that was way too sauced for it's own good.

I rarely eat curry, but it was midnight over Christmas Break and everything was closed...I got the curry with prawns, then added catfish. OMG it was awesome! I later went to Thai House on Shattuck was nothing in comparison: watery and diluted. Eckk!

Sounds interesting and so I decide to try it out. It's in the durant/telegraph quadrant of UCB.  (Bermuda triangle?) Small place in strip mall type building with tons of other restaurants from Italian to Mediterranean. I ordered Basil Sauteed Veggies combo (#44d) at the suggestion of the counter lady. This is mixed vegs and tofu sauteed in bell peppers, onions, basil in chilli garlic sauce.  Food was satisfactory and I would have given it 3 stars but...and here the list of negatives:

No menu... Only what's on the wall
No credit card. period. 
I ordered to stay.  They gave me to go. Wtf. 
(And it wasn't as if she didn't understand English)

Final nail to the coffin.  I'm just about to finish my meal and a man walks into the restaurant with half eaten sandwich. Talks to the counter lady and then proceeds with a small plastic fork to remove hot peppers from the spices tray (the marinated ones) and decks his half-eaten sandwich with hot peppers.  This guy looks semi-homeless.  The fact that the fork touches peppers to half-eaten-sandwich makes my stomach turn.

I was here with my cousin who goes to Cal Berkeley. we were pretty hungry, and with thai being my favorite food, i decided to give this place a shot. i decided to try a foolproof dish: pad thai. The food itself was pretty good. there was a good amount, enough to fill a hungry teenager. but the flavor was lacking. by the time i was almost done, everything sorta tasted the same. the chicken was fine, as was the shrimp, but it could definitely use more sauce.

THE SERVICE IS ATROCIOUS. but i mean, thats typical of any asian owned restaurant. :P (im not being racist, im chinese myself). the price for the pad thai was 6.61, and so i thought 7 bucks would be enough. i ordered in a cherful voice, and then the lady stuck out her hand without telling me how much it was with tax. i gave her the 7 which she took, and then she stuck out her hand again and rudely gestured for the extra 25 cents that i was lacking. i was confused for a moment because she never even said how much the total was, but then i looked at the register and fumbled through my wallet for another dollar. she then took it, looking a bit annoyed, and then gave me my receipt.
