(side note: DO NOT LOSE YOUR RECEIPT. you need it to pick up your food.) so yeah, i got my receipt, and then waited something like 15 minutes for my food. that part was fine since i was with friends, but just a heads up on busy days.

overall, the food was pretty good, but the service was bad. if you have a thick skin, you'll have no issues getting some decent chow. and if you dont like it, there are 7 other types of food in the pavaliion ranging from italian to vietnamese.

Mmm, you can smell the delicoiousness outside the doorway, almost so thick it covers the lingering piss smell that reeks around the Ghetts. The food is delicious, as the portions are generous, meanwhile the flavors are abundant and salty. Dishes usually range between 6-10 dollars, which is about normal for places around this area. They do have complimentary water, that you fill up yourself. As you walk in, the noise level is almost at an unthinkable level, since there's so many college kids. The interior is messy, but clean enough to pass inspection and eat in. On the right wall as you walk in, is a full blown menu along with some pictures and prices, as well as descriptions, to let you know what trouble your tummy is about to get into! It serves most thai foods. The noodles, the rice plates, the specials you name it. The line moves are a sluggish pace, since the cashier is this asian lady, who is straight up rude and just sits in her chair. The wait depends on the people, so I suggest you come along with a friend just to kill time since the wait can get up to about 30 mins if you're unlucky. But you know the food is fresh because you can see them cooking it behind those murky glass shields over the counter and your food does arrive piping hot. 

I suggest to order the Pad Kee Mow with chicken and the grilled pork with rice! Both are nomnomnom goodness! Street parking on the streets, but for the most part college students come here, so its best to walk or public transit.

Thai basil is great! The food is tasty and the portions are huge. I really love the pineapple fried rice. It comes with huge chunks of pineapple, cashews and raisins. Their pad see ew and pad thai are also excellent. I've been told that the food here is not authentic Thai food, but I love it, regardless. 

The one dish I would not recommend is their rad na. It's supposed to be a noodle dish with gravy but I found the gravy to be really diluted and just kind of gross tasting. 

Also, I admit that the old guy who works as the cashier is slightly hostile. Service is not their strong point. 

Overall, it is the best restaurant in the Asian Ghetto though.

Decided to go to the Asian Ghetto for some lunch, and stumbled into Thai Basil. Definite plus that the menu is on the wall, is huge, and has pictures of everything. Ordered the Combo Garlic Pepper, which consists of sautéed chicken, beef, pork and seafood, with mushrooms and onions in garlic chili sauce. The assortment of seafood is a bit strange, but nothing tasted out of place. The beef and pork were especially yummy, and the rice hit the spot when mixed with the sauce. Overall, average meal at three stars. Worth a try, but definitely not a regular.

I came to Berkeley from a super small town with no ethnic food and where I was a part of the 1% asian population in my school. 

Ironically, my white floormate from San Diego took me here and introduced me to the wonderful world of Thai food. 

One bite of the pad thai and I seriously fell in love. This is a college kid's dream...huge portions, cheap and delicious. 

I always get their pad thai, but their pad see ew and eggplant dishes are pretty yummy! 

I also love their green peppers!!!

Obviously the pad see ew and pad kee mao are delicious - they're freakin' oily, caramelized noodles.

I like this place because the noodles stay relatively whole and the chicken pieces are pretty big (instead of near-ground chicken at some other places). The meat is really dry though.

Their portion sizes have definitely been shrinking and their prices have been increasing. When I order late-night greasy food I don't want the portion size to be sufficient - I want it to be FOOD COMA sized.

TIPS
1. Call in your order so you don't have to awkwardly wait. It does take a while for them to cook.
2. When ordering, ask for less oil. They listen.
3. At home, add extra broccoli to your pad see ew to reduce oiliness, saltiness, and most importantly, guilt!

Probably been there 4-5 times over the course of three years.

The food is like... okay.. but it's not like I am going to miss it or anything. They are pretty stingy for the amount of food they serve for the price. 

I was gonna give this place a 3, but the angry cashier lady makes me reconsider. She always yell out something in Thai to her workers and she always give u the death glare if you hand her a creditcard or debit card. I am sorry alright? Sometimes I am out of cash and I apologize if you are reading this review. See! DO I NEED TO FEEL BAD ABOUT SPENDING MONEY AT YOUR EATERY? That's abnormal!

Nestled in the very back corner of the Asian Ghetto (yes I can call it the ghetto because I'm Asian damnit, none of this Gourmet Ghetto or Durant Food Court nonsense), one would expect a hidden treasure of Thai Cuisine.

Instead, sheer gravity of mediocrity falls upon patrons, crushing one's spine more severely than all those Chem 3A books in your backpack during finals season.  Yeah, the pineapple fried rice is good, the pad thai is satisfactory, but they really need to stop watering down the curry.  You can't cut corners on curry, fricking pour in that coconut milk and make heart clench in high cholesterol pleasure.

The service is probably the most sub-par.  Sometimes they just don't understand special orders like "Please don't make this spicy" or "Hi I am severely allergic to _____, please do not include it in my dish so I can eat my meal without going into anaphylactic shock."

Recent e.g.

Trang (My friend): Not spicy. Ok?
Cashier: Ok! (Scribbles down EXTREMELY HOT on receipt)
Trang: Wait wait wait! This not spicy right?
Cashier: Oh yes!
(Order comes out completely speckled with chiles)

TL;DR: Cheap Thai food for under $10, but you really get what you pay for, and arguably less.  Be prepared to bring your own Epi-pen or spend a few secondss picking out unwanted ingredients before eating.

I've been here a few times and came here last week after a 3 year hiatus. The food is good and affordable and serves good portions. This place can get a little crowded because your near campus. 

This place is a little small and you can over hear peoples conversions whether you like it or not. For instance, when I went last week, there were a group of girls talking about farting in front of their boyfriends. I wasn't trying to listen, but they were sharing a tiny table and sitting so close that it was unavoidable. It was difficult to keep a straight face and was laughing in my mind hysterically as I ate my noodles. I guess that's what they mean by girl talk, eh?

Hands down, my favorite place to eat in Berkeley. When I was a Cal Student Orientation counselor, I think I'd come here like 3 times a week. In fact, I just took a trip to Thailand, and even though Thai food in Thailand was cheaper, due to my American-accustomed taste, I couldn't wait to have myself some Pad See Ew Chicken when I returned to Berkeley afterwards. There's just something about it that I'm addicted to...it might be the loads of oil in there or the salty/sweet taste of the pad see ew noodles...but I must have eaten that dish like 50 times as a student at Cal.
  I should also add, that my fave combo is Pad See Ew Chicken and Snapple Apple. One of the only places I know in Berkeley that has the addicting drink that is Snapple Apple! Haha. Good stuff.
  The only other things I've had at Thai Basil are Pad Thai and Yellow Curry Chicken, which are both tasty as well, and I would recommend them.  Something to note is that since mid-May, they are now CASH ONLY! No more cards for Thai Basil :P

The moment you walk into this place, a million MSG molecules adhere to your face and start activating NMDA receptors, cascading through the rest of your body and convincing your hands to fork over six, seven dollars for food that is 40% simple carbohydrates, 40% soybean oil making its way towards the trans state, and 20% sodium - with 50/50 chloride and glutamate as counterions. 

The food here makes John Basedow cry, and every time I see one of you freshman hotties parading in here my heart cracks a little at the thought of the imminent loss of a pair of good, sturdy thighs. How else will you run from your boyfriend over to my humble haven at northside?

My lovely boyfriend is Thai so I'm picky about my Thai food. First off, the portions aren't really "asian portions" where they can feed a party of 2 and a half. Located in the heart of the Asian Ghetto, it's like walking down the dirty streets of China. Trash overflowing with no recycling bin.

The order took a very long time :( Upside is that there's hot thai tea while you wait :)

My cousin took me here when I came up to visit NorCal. I ordered the Chicken Curry, and they got the right amount of spiciness that I like! It definitelyyyyy HIT THE SPOT. I was freezing my little socal-ass off up there! It was ridiculously cheap, too. Very reminiscent of Thai Spice back in Irvine, CA. I would definitely come back if I'm ever chillin' in Berkeley.

Thai Basil, why are you always so packed!  My Freshman year, I basically lived at the Asian Ghetto when I wasn't burning my meal points and Thai Basil was amazing to me.  I always got the grilled pork, which is a lot like its Vietnamese counterpart.  It does come with a sweet thai chili sauce and a side of rice; I usually ask for a side of steamed broccoli and even though it's barely cooked and still super crunchy, they never roll their eyes or charge me extra for it!  It makes me feel healthier, too.  

The pad thai here is good, definitely better than the Thai place at the Gourmet Ghetto (I got prawnS with it and they gave me TWO prawns.  One less and they would have had to call it PAD THAI WITH PRAWN).  Anyways, I've had the basil chicken which was way too spicy for me and made me feel like I was going to get sick because the "chicken" was in super tiny grounded pieces, making me believe it was just leftover parts.  

The people that own the place won't go out of their way to be friendly.  It used to make me nervous that they wore face masks in the kitchen, but I guess if I were inhaling smoke fumes all day I would do that too.

Whenever I'm in Berkeley or north Oakland and feel like eating Thai I go here. My aunt is Thai and I've had home-cooked Thai. This may not be as good but it's close enough. Having a separate vegetarian menu also gets an extra star from me. 

Thai iced tea is ridiculously orange but tastes good. Never had an order malfunction. Although one time when I ordered the catfish I was severely disappointed but a time before that it was fine. I seriously go here all the time! 

Being in the Asian food court helps in case someone I'm with doesn't want Thai. Very well priced for poor bastards like myself. Right by telegraph and the Bank of America is on the same street.
Really great, cheap, fast hole in the wall Thai restaurant in the Asian ghetto. I love the Spicy basil chicken. Haven't tried much else b/c I haven't had the desire to.
The Thai food is mediocre at best, the portions do not justify the price, and the line is not justifiable either! Where is justice!!! Dam Durant food court makes mediocre food seem heavenly

You know those times when you just crave something? When something just comes over you? When you want Thai Basil, you have to get Thai Basil. Nothing will hit the spot like Thai Basil. 

I've been coming to thai basil all 4 years of my undergrad and my feelings toward it has not changed. Relatively cheap, great tasting, and pretty decent portion sizes. How can you go wrong?

I would say that this is a decent thai restaurant located in Berkeley. I recommend their pad see ew chicken, basil chili chicken, and thai beef and chicken. But their pad thai is pretty bland with little flavor. Their food comes out pretty decently, and is pretty enjoyable. However they no longer take credit card anymore so you have to bring cash.

Best part is when you are screamed at like a criminal for asking if your order is ready after 20 minutes. 
The popularity of this place amongst Cal students is enough to make you feel like maybe you didn't get into that good of a university in the first place... Come on Cal Students you are supposed to be smarter than this!!!
Huge long lines, slow service, rude employees scream at you over crackling
microphones, flies buzzing at your face, cash only.... THEN you FINALLY
get your food and it is oozing with high fructose corn syrup and MSG. Berkeley students must crave MSG and abuse. There is almost no space to
stand and wait for your order, so don't count on this place changing
anything theyre doing anytime soon.
I can't imagine a worse eating experience unless you actually got food
poisoning. Although, with that much MSG and high fructose corn syrup, the
term "food poisoning" might abstractly apply. I thought I must have
ordered a bad menu selection because how does this place stay so busy?
Went back and realized that Berkeley stereotypes about healthy eating are
just that- stereotypes. Berkeley students wake up and smell the MSG!!!

No one can beat the price for the amount of food and even decent quality that Thai Basil gives their customers. Back when I wasn't a vegetarian, I regularly craved the basil chili chicken. The tofu pad Thai, however, was less than satisfactory. First off, there were about two pieces of tofu on the whole plate. Also, most of the noodles were drowned in peanut sauce.
The absolute best place to go after a Cal football or basketball game!  We order one set of dishes to eat there, and another to take home to Pleasanton to eat the next day.  It's the best!
Great, fast, cheap thai food...works well if you're in a hurry and not in the mood for a sit down restaurant.

The first time I tried Thai Basil's pad thai as a freshman, I thought it tasted amazing! Like, even better than the pad thai at any of the other Thai establishments near campus. But recently, the pad thai just hasn't been as good as how i remembered. Maybe it's a decline in quality, or maybe it's because my taste buds have matured, but the pad thai just seems to taste less flavorful. The chicken can also be dry at times. Nevertheless, I still come whenever I have a craving for Thai food because it's the closest place to my apt. 

I also like their pad see ew, but their portions seem to be smaller than the pad thai...

And expect a longer wait for your food than the other Asian Ghetto establishments. Sometimes I even phone in my order beforehand to avoid the line.

THANK THE BERKELEY GODS FOR THAI BASIL! 
Whoooooooo! This is definitely as good as it gets! So darn good, I'm afraid it has become a serious addiction. I might have to start my own Thai Basil Rehab...

At this point, you may be thinking, "what is so good about this place?"
Well, once you get past it's location which is in the furthest end of the "Asian Ghetto," as us Berkeley students like to call it, you face a delicious dish made in Thai Berkeley heaven. Not only are the prices great ($4-7) but the portions are HUGE! You can easily share a dish with a friend. I personally don't like to share my Thai Basil. It's just too good, I'll take as much as I can get. 
The place is pretty small so you may have to sit out in the cold and eat your food. If this is the case, get ***** spicy (five stars spicy level). That'll warm you right up. They only take cash, so make sure you make a pit stop at the ATM before arriving. Another perk about Thai Basil is that they are open until 12:30am. SCORE! I'm always up studying late, and who doesn't get the munchies after a long study session, right? 
Honestly, I am a big Thai food fan and I've tried many Thai restaurant but I can't get past the price, quantity, spice, and deliciousness of this place. My favorite dishes are the Tom Kah, which is perfect for those cold nights, and the Pad Thai, perfect any day at any time. The noodles are cooked to perfection and since I'm a big fan of spicy, I always ask for ***** 

Really, this is one of the best restaurants in Berkeley. BY FAR! Try it and enjoy! :)
Extremely good, extremely spicy (especially if you order it Thai hot). This is the best Thai restaurant in Berkeley, believe it or not!
The most expensive counter-ordering Thai eatery in the vicinity of Berkeley but also one of the better Thai restaurants.  I like their garlic pepper chicken.

I always tell myself that I'll try all the different Thai places around Berkeley (since there are SO MANY), but I usually end up at Thai Basil because it's at such a convenient location. They now are cash only which is sometimes annoying but the BoA ATM machine is 30 seconds away, so it's not too bad. 
Their foods have so much flavor (& is also very greasy), whether it's the noodles like Pad Thai or Pad See Ew or the rice places like the Cashew Chicken or Basil Chicken, and it never fails to give me food coma after. Frankly, the food is nothing really special. It's decent and fills you up but it's not anything to really "wow" over.
I especially like their lunch specials where you can choose 2-3 items from the choices for a pretty decent price. & I also love the hot thai tea that they have. Mmmmm.
Downside: the wait is always SUPER long.

The first item I ever ordered here (probably over a year ago) was their Pad Thai, and I wasn't very impressed so I never came back... until recently, when a friend of mine let me try some green curry that he bought here. I'm so glad he did!

Since then (this was a few weeks ago) I've been back at least 3 times each week, and everything I've tried has been delicious! My favorite is the Pad Prik King chicken or the green curry. 

Huge servings, good price (most items are between $5 and $8), fairly quick, really tasty. 

The only downside is that they're cash only.

Greasy fried goodness?! You got it!

Although the noodles tend to be a little too greasy the sauce they are in is absolutely delicious. 

Tends to get rather crowded at around 7pm but the line moves pretty fast and they are pretty efficient at pumping out orders. 

The menu is very vast (maybe a little too vast) but the prices of this place are perfect for the college location.

Tasty Thai at a reasonable cost - it's a hole in the wall but what you lose in ambience you save in the cost of the tip. 

Basil Chili Chicken = WIN (fried egg optional)
Pad Thai & Pad See Ew are also very good
and..Pepper Garlic chicken/beef/tofu  

Definitely call ahead for take-out, they get busy during peak hours

It was late... nothing else open so why  not? all these awards from years ago are misleading.

My first Thai experience in Berkeley was not a great one.

Chicken Satay =  unflavorful, dry, rubbery.
Pad Thai = unflavorful, dry, clumped up.

one bite of each and then handed it over to a few homeless people.

A friend and I were visiting SF/Berkeley, and we walked into this place to grab some dinner. It wasn't all that busy, but ~15 mins after we got in line, the place became PACKED. I guess the place was popular and we didn't even know it.

I don't even remember the name of what I ordered (I wasn't exactly in the right state of mind, haha), but it was a noodles + seafood dish. It was quite good, there was enough seafood to keep me happy. Mine was one of the more expensive dishes on the menu, probably because of the seafood. Sad, but what can you do when you don't eat meat (the meat dishes were much cheaper).

The food was good, but it was much too crowded and hectic for my taste. There were no seats left empty, my friend and I were sharing a 6 seat table with 4 other people that we didn't know. (I don't really care, but the table was cramped!) The entire restaurant was packed, and it took me 5 mins to walk 5 feet and navigate my way to the hot sauce/water. Twice. :(

Ok, the fried rice is not bad, but this owner lady always gives me trouble. 

I once ordered beef fried rice with extra rice expecting to pay about

a dollar extra at the most. I gave her my card and it was $10.50!

beef fried rice ($7.00) + extra rice = $10.50?

I asked her why and she said, it's one order + half order which is $3.50

I was like WFT?? The thing is she did not even tell me what the

total was and just swiped my card and ripped me off that way.


Another thing. They left a big giant piece of spice in my fried rice plate and I did not know what it was and I almost threw up.

I still think the regular fried rice without a big giant spice in it is decent,
but I just cannot give this place more than one star.

Tips:

Cash only

-----------------------------------------------------

I really like the pad thai from Thai Basil which is more on the sweeter side of pad thai. They give you pretty good portions as well. I got a Yellow Chicken Curry today for $7.25 and the curry tasted good. The curry is the typical Thai curry that's sweet and not thick. The rice was a bit undercooked because it wasn't soft enough for my taste, but rice can be eaten at any consistency.

Personally I like Racha and Berkeley Thai House a bit better than Thai Basil, but it's still a staple in "Asian Ghetto". It's great for a quick bite to eat.

Good, cheap and fast. 

The best of the student take-out places and you won't feel like you just ate a meal only the metabolism of a nineteen year old could handle.

Pretty good food. And cheap. It's hard to understand the cashier when it's the older man or lady working, and the lady is usually pretty rude. Oh well. I love my Vegetarian Pad See-Ew. Hate anything with  meat in this place. Had it, and never will again. Cheap low quality "meat," but I guess that's expected. But yea...vegetarian pad see-ew. yum.
Good, inexpensive, no frills thai. And the menu is huge....literally. It takes up a whole wall. I'm a huge panang curry fan and they do it well. And of course they have really good thai iced tea.

I actually used to like this place.  It's convenient, and a lot of my friends like it, so I ate here. 

The guy who takes your order isn't very nice, so don't ask him any questions.  I've had the pad thai and the pad see ew (sp?) here.  Both okay.  Then I discovered the basil chicken fried rice.  It's not basil chicken, it's basically chicken fried rice with basil, and it's spicy, and it's good.  

Once, however, I got take-out a night before a midterm or a final and I got super sick after eating my thai basil.  Seriously, I woke up in the middle of the night and puked my guts out.  I thought I was going to die, my stomach hurt so much.  From the looks of it, I didn't digest the food.  And this was food I ate hours ago.  I think I only had a little of it too, since I normally don't eat too much when I'm stressed

Too greasy for my liking.

Anyway, because of that experience, I will never ever eat here again.  It's like one of the aversive reaction effects.  If you do however, decide to eat here, I recommend the basil chicken fried rice.

I don't think they accept credit cards, but maybe they do now?  Oh yea, it's normally really busy and crowded, esp. during peak hours, and it takes forever to get your food.  So be prepared to wait a bit.

I used to like Thai Basil a lot, but I just grew tired of their food after a while because everything seems so greasy and full of MSG.  The prices are reasonable, as are the portions, and the service is good enough.  I also appreciate that they have a good amount of vegetarian options, although I dunno if they use fish sauce or not.

Anyways, the food here always just leaves a greasy film in my mouth from all of the oil and MSG.  I think the MSG also gives me a little bit of a headache afterwards.  There is better Thai food out there.

I have frequented many Thai restaurants over the years, and comparing those to Thai Basil, I have but three words: greasy greasy greasy.

I will concede that many of their dishes are certainly flavorful and evoke many classic Thai flavors such as the sweet, sour, spicy in their Tom Yum Goong or the alluring wok-flavor in their Fried Rice. However, I do feel that many of their dishes could get by with a lot less oil. Plus, the food they serve for their lunch special is sub-par compared to their other a la carte items (Lunch special items are pre-cooked and spooned onto plates when ordered). Having two contrasting sets of dishes in this light shows inconsistency in my book.

Their Basil Eggplant Tofu is my favorite thing here. Big portions and the price is very reasonable, especially for the college student's budget. I love this place

TIP: They recently went to cash only.
cheap, consistent, centrally located by campus. many great vegetarian options. i crave basil eggplant tofu every single day

OK Thai fast food. I like to get the garlic chicken or the weekday lunch combo specials. The free Thai tea makes me feel all warm inside too on a freakin cold Berkeley day. The food is made quick and the people making the food are very clean about it since the women hold back their hair w/ scarves and also wear masks over their nose and mouth like a sergeon.
this place gets an F for service though. The service at the cashier is very rude. also, the prices here are the most expensive in Asian ghetto for the price. Its a good place though for your Thai food fix but if you have the time to walk go to University Ave. and check out Lucky House.

I can't believe this place only has 3.5 stars! Super cheap, delicious Thai food! Love their Pad See Euw and Spicy Seafood Stir-fry(?) Yeah...don't remember the name of the dish. It was super tasty though. We asked for the food nice and spicy, and damn, it was hot. Like deliciously masochistic-ly hot. Yum.

The food does take a little while, and the place can get pretty busy. The food's worth it though! Especially with their prices.

P.S. Cash only.

Value-wise I think Thai Basil gets 3 stars since sometimes they give you nice big portions (e.g. Pad Thai) and sometimes you can still see the bottom of your take-out tray (e.g. Pad See-Ew).  That being said I'm giving Thai Basil 4 stars just for being in a convenient place near campus; in addition, over the past almost-three-years that I've been at Cal their food has been pretty consistent quality-wise.  I like the pad-see-ew best; their pad thai is alright but there are some other places that do it better.  The Kao Moo Dang is like a Chinese-style BBQ pork on rice, but not even a really good BBQ pork...so I've only had that once.

I agree with previous reviewers....despite the rise in prices the food is still pretty dependable!  I'll be back.

Craving some good Thai food around my area and haven't really been able to fine one. Sad. 

But, when I think of good, cheap Thai food, I can't forget Thai Basil when I was at CAL. I loved this place. It's cheap, walking distance (for me), and really freak'n good. Their pad-see-ew, pad thai and combination fried rice were delicious. I remembering ordering the combination fried rice a lot because I could never get enough of it. When it's fresh and super hot, mmmmmm yummy! So flavorful. It is a cash only place, and it's not the cleanest place, but hey, it's inside the "Asian Ghetto" in a college town, so you kind of figured. =P Don't get me wrong, because I get food at the asian ghetto a lot, but you should come to expect what kind of place you are eating at. Either way, 4 stars for the delicious food. 

Now if I can only find Thai food that is just as good, and at just as good of a price around here.....

1. Pad See Ew
2. Pad Thai
3. Pineapple Fried Rice

This is basically what I go to Thai Basil for. Soo goodddd!! I hear the BBQ chicken is pretty good too but I've never tried it! You get good portions for the relatively cheap price you pay! I've never really eaten Thai food before college.. but now I love it! (:

The only downside is the slow service.. even though it doesn't seem like they're slow.. they are... they take a good amount of time to get the food out to you. I usually wait around a good 15-20 minutes for my food. As annoying as it is, I guess it's worth the wait if my cravings are satisfied in the end!

Otherwise, this is one of the better Thai restaurants in Berkeley and it's conveniently located super close to campus, but if I had to choose, I'd go to Racha Cafe down on Telegraph Ave for better quality Thai food & a lotttt better service. That's just me though!~

This is ok food but certainly not the best in Berkeley. Most dishes are a bit too oily for my tastes so I usually go with the fried rice. There isn't much space and the food is a bit pricey.  I like Thai House better when on the southside.

My girlfriend and I are surprised by the low ratings of this place on Yelp. She started attending UC Berkeley recently and we've been visiting different eateries and Thai Basil is by far our favorite. The best dish we've gotten so far is the Curry Vegetable Fried Rice (I'm a vegetarian; she's not, but she likes the dish tremendously, as well). A big plus is that unlike most other Thai places, this place is very cheap for Thai food. Most dishes range between $5.50 and $6.25 or so, and even dishes loaded with seafood aren't much more expensive.

One of my favorite places to go to at Asian Ghetto!

Waiting for your food takes a ridiculous long time though...and I have no idea why. I was waiting for almost 20 minutes for my meal and there was only like 1 person ahead of me. 

Other than that, the food is pretty cheap and the portion usually lasts me two meals. I recommend the pad thai or green curry!

Really good Thai food for the price.  The combination fried rice is amazing.  The pad prik king is really good, and the pad-see-eew is not bad either.  The owners are nice, and my mom accidently reunited with an elementary school friend she knew back in Thailand.  Weird.

I come here for one thing, and one thing only: Combo Pad Thai. Never had such amazing Pad Thai for the price its worth. The Pad Thai comes with shrimp, chicken and tofu with no extra charge! 

nom nom nom. All in my tummy!

What can i say abt thai basil....words cant do justice for this place, its the BEST thai food you would ever eat in your life!!!

From college days to now, only one place which really knows how to hit the spot is Thai Basil. Try Basil Tofu!!! Its a total hole in the wall with the cheapest thai food ever but dont let the price fool you...the sevice is crappy but the food makes up for everthing!! They are open until midnight and worth to drive to berkeley (or even fly to bay area) to eat Basil Tofu!! lol..Yummy!!!!

This place has terrible service. The bitter old boss lady always gives me an attitude. She is very impatient and scolds/yells at customers. This place is a joke.

Their food is only average. Definitely not worth the bad customer service. 

I would rate this place a 0 star if I could. I would not recommend this place to anyone, the terrible customer service might ruin your day.

I LOVE THIS PLACE. Everything is so delicious and affordable. Plus the owners are very nice and always remember me. I've had the yellow curry, pineapple fried rice, combo fried rice, satay chicken, and pad thai and I have loved every dish. Can't wait to try more.

I'm surprised that this place fell under four stars!

It seems like nobody on campus has anything bad to say about the food here. However I do agree that it does not have greatservice and you usually have to wait a good minute for your food. (but it's because it's so busy!)

The curry here is very good, and the pad-se-ew chicken is amazing! The basil fried rice chicken is also very good. But in my opinion, stay away from the pad thai. It tastes really cheap cafeteria food for some reason and it might be the reason that it fell under four stars!

Okay - so it is the best Thai food I have found in Berkeley, CA and it is cash only and a big student draw as it is in the food court.   So I am not saying do not go - however I am saying take the food to go.  It is a good value for the quality. 

The owners and staff have all their focus on the kitchen which makes for consistently good food - however they really need to pay attention to what is happening in the dining room also.  Maybe they can buy some cameras or mirrors or just darn start to pay attention. 

Today -  there was a TV Show called the 1000 ways to DIE blasting loud in the small dining room - which was all blood and gore on the TV.  This was not exactly appetizing to eat a nice relaxing lunch to.  A great contrast to the floating lotus flowers at the order station.   Three people went to the front and asked to change the channel on the TV and the lady never did a thing to change the channel and just ignored the complaints.  If she does not understand she should try to get someone else that does or investigate.   A couple people left and I changed seats so I did not have to watch.

However - then a homeless man with some definite mental health issues came into the restaurant.  He went straight to the busser station in the main restaurant as if he knew exactly where to go.  He cleaned off a plate at the busser station with a used fork and started digging through all the left-over waste - in front of all the people dining.  He then prepared himself a meal out of the garbage and sat himself down at a nice table in the main dining room and ate his meal in the middle of the restaurant.
  Many staff saw him and did nothing to interrupt him.   

The man then went table to table asking for food in a very aggressive way and psychotic way.   He yelled some obscenities at the customers for not giving him their food and then hit the condiment station where he decided to suck down the soy sauce and thai condiments like a baby bottle.  Mouth to bottle and drank it all down like a refreshment.  The buss boy  finally asked him what he was doing after 40 minute roller coaster and the guy left.   He did not remove the soy sauce bottle - until I said that it was not sanitary to leave it there. 

I think people should feel safe in a restaurant and their managers need to make sure that the ambiance is as important as the food.   They should be a bit more protective and be aware of who comes in and out the door.  You could tell the homeless man does this all the time - he knew exactly where to go and what to do.   We all can practice compassion for the less fortunate.   However - at the same time if we are paying to sit at a table and dine on a nice meal then we should not be screamed at for not giving someone else our thai soup.  I would have much preferred that the owners just give the man a meal then have him eat out of their garbage in the main dining room.  It was just wrong.

Oh, how nice it would be if the old man simply said "thank you" or didn't snatch the cash from my hand 1/1000 second after ordering. 

S-L-O-W service. Great food.

Not one of the best Thai in a city full of Thai Restaurants but it has a few things going for it.  It's super cheap, no tipping needed, it's relatively fast and the food is delicious.  The pepper garlic tofu is great with a spicy sweet sauce.  The pad thai is good too although sometimes they burn the noodles.  The fried rices are the best deal with lots of food for around $5-7.

Good food, horrible customer service.
I saw the worst thing at this restaurant today.
----------------------------------------
Young lady asked for lunch special that was posted/ advertised outside the restaurant. It was a tofu option.
Lady taking her order gave her chicken instead.
Young lady came back and told older lady that she could not eat chicken, and that she wanted the tofu that was advertised outside.
Older lady got angry and went outside to show the young lady that it was really  CHICKEN and NOT TOFU. 
But when Older lady read the sign posted outside her restaurant, it read LUNCH SPECIAL: TOFU.
Older lady then went back inside, grabben piece of paper, wrote CHICKEN on it, and covered the TOFU part in front of the young lady.
Young lady had to take the chicken after arguing.
This place does not pride itself on customer service.

If you are willing to put up with this kind of attitude from the employees/owners for the good food.........YOUVE been warned.

Meh, it's alright. I got the ol pad thai. It was nothing to write home about. The service was terrible. The old asian ladies were talking about me in chinese  because I asked to switch from to-go to for here twice, and didn't think I could understand them.  It's not like it was any trouble for them since I was still waiting for my food. . didn't have to be so rude.

They don't accept credit cards anymore. Such a drag. Guess they want students to carry cash around.. which some would consider dangerous in Berkeley at night.

Not to mention, their food is ceasing to impress. Still good for the Asian Ghetto though.

i really just don't get the hype around this place.  i'm a die hard pad thai, panang, and green curry person, and all three counts, thai basil is *awful*.  the pad thai is just completely bland  and the green curry (despite my asking them to make it *super* spicy was just tatsteless.  the panang chicken was just okay.  moreover, for being such a ghetto ramshackle spot, it's not even all that cheap...

We stupidly chose Thai Basil on our way to see Portishead at the Greek. Seriously one of the worst meals EVER!

The soup we had was served in the most inefficient way with the veggies and noodles in a box and the broth in a container. How are we supposed to combine this without a bowl? 

We were served chicken in an order instead of tofu, and when my friend brought the entree up to the kitchen to complain, the staff acted like she was lying to get a free entree!! We didn't care about getting it free, we just wanted it meatless! SO RUDE, really. 

None of us finished our meals, what a waste. With all the thai food options in Berkeley, there is just no excuse to eat here.

I'm not an expert on Thai cuisine, but this place hits the spot. If you're not on a diet, I would suggest to eat at this place everyday for a week. It will be the best week of your life to that point. If you begin to have visions, don't worry, this is normal. Maybe pick up a Thai ice-tea to cleanse your palette. 
Go during the summer. Less students...less students is key to your success!

"NO PAD THAI FOR YOU!"

Man, we were in town for Cal day and want to Thai Basil for some lunch.  Staff was very rude.  You would think they would be happy that they are busy.  

Anyway, I ordered Pad-Sew with chicken and Pineapple Fried Rice, first to eat there but my son was tired and fussy so we asked to have it to go...WOW, the lady behind the counter looked like she would stab us with the kitchen knife, even though we told her our son needed to go home.  We didn't want everyone to hear a screaming, whining child.  If it was not an open kitchen I almost bet she would have spit in our food.  Rude service.

The food was mediocre at best.  The Pad Sew tasted like they pour a cup of sugar in it, way too sweet.  The Pineapple fried rice had nuts in it when I told them no nuts.  So important safety tip - Don't take anyone allergic to nuts here, they don't take special request very well.  Price was not cheap either for Berkeley.

I would never go back due to just rude service and mediocre food.
The pineapple chicken curry was unbelievably spicy and had wonderful flavor. Unfortunately to eat it I had to pick around all the sub-sub par chicken that littered the rice dish like minefields.

I don't understand the hype.
Most of the food is drenched in MSG
and the pad Thai is RIDICULOUSLY sweet
(it's unpalatable). 

Personally, I think the price here is too high
for the quality of food they serve. The service
isn't exactly renown here either. And yet, this place
is always packing customers. What gives?

I absolutely hate the service for this place whenever I pass by it i give a huge glare at the staff. Both of my encounters for this place was horrible.

I went here on a busy Sunday. it was so packed everyone was sweaty and seats were nowhere to be found. I ordered a soup because I was feeling a bit sick and I wanted something water-y. I was too short to reach the counter where they call your number and serve you food so the man push it a little further. Since he was in a rush, he pushed so far that the soup fell and spilled all over my hand. My hand was automatically on fire, and burned so bad i had to go to the hospital. It was a second degree burn, and as of today I still have that burn. 

The second time I went was when they started printing out the new receipts for their customers, this lady was having a hard time using it so it took forever for here to get my order. After that she did not give me a receipt, I didn't know that i was suppose to get one either. So i waited forever! When i asked her where is my food it has been more than 45 min! And then she said where is your receipt. I said she didn't give me one and said she doesn't remember putting my order in, and i should get out of the store! 

EUGH. this place makes me angry!

My love for Thai Basil only grew stronger over the five years I lived in Berkeley. Now even though I'm not within walking distance of this dive, I still dream about the amazingness of the basil eggplant tofu dish ordered thai hot (of course). Consistency and fresh ingredients were the name of the game when it came to this dish. It never failed to disappoint; it was always incredibly hearty and reasonably priced. 
If you are trying to find something to complain about, you could try and point to the wait - depending on the time of day you visit, you could expect to wait 10-20 minutes after ordering your food. BUT, the only reason you are waiting is because their food isn't ready made. You order and only then do they start to cook.  A freshly made meal is what you get --so really who can complain about a 10 minute wait?
Finally, the grandma-esque lady behind the counter totally reminds me of my great-aunt (seriously sweetest old lady with the kindest face!)
I normally like this place but they're slipping- they're not running lunch specials anymore and today I got the shrimp pad thai and was given only two shrimp.  That's pretty lame.

Good Thai food for o.k. prices. More expensive than Viet Nam Village, but also takes CREDIT. Plenty of VEGGIE options, and lots of great curries. 

Sometimes the time it takes to make it can be a bit longer than you'd hope (~10-15 min) so keep that in mind. Call in ahead of time if you're in a rush, use 1-800-GOOG-411, Yelp App, or (510) 548-6692.

Highly recommend: Pineapple chicken curry. It's heavenly.

Protip: Come in weekdays at lunch and get the lunch special!! 5.75 for lots of pad Thai and choice of 2-3 items (out of a list of 3), usually 2 chicken and 1 vegetarian choices. It's premade so not super fresh, but it's FAST, CHEAP, and still tasty.

also I saw the old guy who sometimes works cashier (probably 70 years old and doesn't speak very much English) doing linear algebra. BEAST.

i have to give it up for this place,  They do make great Thai basil anything.  When I worked in Berkeley I try to stop by to pick up some of my favorite seafood Thai basil.  Pretty bold taste and a kick in the mouth if you like seafood.  This place i would most def recommend for lunch..

We had an adventure to Berkeley and after shopping wanted to eat. My sister Yelped 'THAI' and low and behold we found thai basil. 

I liked the food and it was greatly priced. The only downfall is the lack of seating and the I wish that there was a bathroom or a huge bottle of hand sanitizer to clean your hands! 

Otherwise, a great place and will definitely be back. 

I would love to try the pumpkin curry next!

This place is located in my favorite eating area when visiting UC Berkeley, what the locals call "Asian Ghetto." It's not a luxurious eating experience by any means, but the atmosphere is fun and relaxed. There are a modest number of tables inside the restaurant, as well as the tables outside that are for all of the surrounding eateries. 

While I go out for the atmosphere, my boy is a stickler about quality of food, which is why he took me here. The Tom Yum Soup is spicy and tangy, perfect for the freezing cold, rainy weather that we were enjoying this past February weekend. He got a chicken dish and a noodle dish.. either Pad See-ew or Pad Thai, I can't remember which, but both were delicious!

The best part-- it's amazingly cheap for the portion size. My huge bowl of soup was only $5. To college students like us, there's nothing like cheap, good food =]

Why this little hole in the wall deserves my 5 stars (6 if I could give it) is very simple:  life before Thai Basil was a time with no Thai food in my life.

the food is good, excellent for the price and if it wasn't for this place, I may not like Thai food at all today.  

You will have to wait for your food - it usually takes a while for it to cook, but you can watch your food get prepared and cooked right in front of you and soak in all those mm-good college vibes (or go next door to get some milk tea).  most of their stuff is good, but I have a really hard time not getting the pad thai (memories, ah memories) whenever I'm in the area these days.

i used to eat here often, mainly because i didn't know what else was available within a 3 block radius of my home. anyway, the meat here is god-awful, it baaaaaarely surpases the meat they serve in the dorms, which is Grade D (aka: Prison grade.) the food is always oily, and they skimp on ingredients - a good summary of the dishes is: rice, chili oil, soy sauce, msg.
the pad thai is really awful too - pad thai is supposed to be refreshing, sweet and sour, with a little kick. it tasted more like a katsudon than pad thai, in an gross way.

but they are open after 11, and always reliable. so. yeah.  -____-

This is my favorite spot to eat in the Asian Ghetto-- the food is always excellent and super cheap. I usually get the basil eggplant chicken (sooooo goood, the perfect amount of spicy), but I've also been satisfied with their fried rice, pad thai, and cashew chicken.

I'm also a fan of their lunch special-- you can choose 2-3 items from their daily listings of four dishes and it's only $5.75! So cheap, and the portions are really big-- whenever I go to Thai Basil I usually share with my friend Cecilia or I end up taking at least half of it to eat later for a second meal! :)

The wait is kind of long, especially during lunchtime and dinnertime rush hours, but if you go at a time when it's not so busy and hectic it's definitely worth your time.

Thai Basil and Lucky House Thai

Two best thai places in Berkeley.  I've been to 12 others.  nuff said.

Let me just start my review by saying that I like Thai food. A lot. In fact, it is my favorite kind of food in the whole world.  I have eaten at a lot of Thai restaurants, and this one is no more than mediocre.

But Thai Basil has a lot of redeeming qualities. It is very cheap, especially if you get the lunch special.  It is also food that you can order to go. Who wouldn't want takeout Thai food?  Best of all, the food is loaded with MSG and sugar and other things that make is very, very delicious (and very, very unhealthy).  When I am craving cheap Thai food, this is always where I go.

Some of the dishes are also genuinely great.  I am especially partial to the Basil Tofu or Basil Eggplant Tofu.  Do not get the curry dishes, they aren't that good.

One more tip: if you like spicy food like I do, ask for the spiciness as a number of stars, not as "Medium" or "Very Spicy".  When you order it a particular spiciness, they put down a number of stars on your order to indicate that.  If you explicitly ask for four stars spiciness (normally higher than they would actually write down for me, even if I explicitly requested it extra spicy), the person at the register will know what you mean and the food will taste a lot better.

For the amount of food you get, this place has good value.  I've tried a lot of the places in the Asian Food Ghetto and this one is pretty tasty.  I was surprised by the amount of time needed to wait for my order though, however, I guess it's a plus that they apparently make each dish to order. I ordered one of their chicken dishes with chili and basil.  It was tasty but a bit oily.  If you're looking for a good variety of choices, come here!

Basil eggplant chicken is boss. After ordering this once my freshman year I seriously cannot order anything else. It's probably pretty nutritionally bad for me (especially since I'm a nutritional science major), but damn it's too good! I recently just discovered they serve brown rice which brings this review to 5 stars (although they charge $1.50, which is a little steep). Ive never found a basil eggplant chicken with so much flavor. The slightly sweet but spicy combination is mouthwateringly addictive.

The Honest Truth: This is a mid-tier thai restaurant in Berkeley.  There are definitely worst places and there are definitely better places.  But it's conveniently located in asian ghetto and also one of the better places in asian ghetto.  The food is on the greasy side.  They always take a really long time to cook your food with or without a line.  And cash only! Basil chili chicken is my go to.


The Details:  This used to be my favorite place to eat in Berkeley for my first two years in college. It has dropped significantly since then due to the fact that my roommates have cars and we are not limited by distance as well as the fact that they are now cash only.  Since my freshman year, their wait time has also significantly increased.  When there is a line, you can wait up to 45 minutes for your food and even when there is no line, you have to wait 15 minutes.  But since freshman year, their food has stayed the same.  It's still on the greasy side and it still tastes good.  It also still makes your burps smell nasty.  For thai food to go, this is definitely my first choice because of its convenient location, but given the choice to sit down, it would be my third or fourth option.  Overall, the quality of thai basil has not deteriorated over my four years in college (which is good news), the bad news is that other things have... So if you're willing to wait a while, and have cash on you, and you don't care about the greasiness or smelliness of your burps, thai basil is a solid choice.
i like getting their food to go when i'm too lazy to cook. Pretty good

This place is awesome - you know why?  'Cause they use great ingredients and aren't afraid to use a little oil and onion...mmm....their pineapple fried rice is amazing as are all of their tofu dishes.

I could eat here every day of my silly life. 

Favorites:
Tom Kha Soup (if you haven't had this, you'll thank me)
Pad Thai
Regular fried rice
LUNCH SPECIALS!

While I do think their chicken is alwwwwways over-salted and not the best quality, I do believe they have the best pad thai in Berkeley which is definitely a comfort food for me. Their bottle of fish sauce with thai chilis is great...I can't eat a meal without it sitting at my table. And their Thai Ice Tea is consistently good. 

While the old uncle working the cash register will stare at you like you're the dumbest person alive and then yell at you when you try to use your credit card for anything less than $5, just deal. The food is worth it. And you can't beat the lunch special...sooo much food....soooo much salt....nom nom. Must limit my intake here before I start getting high blood pressure.

I cannot stand this place.  The food here isn't even close to tasting authentic or good.  I don't understand why so many people like it.  Every time I've gone there, I've asked for nam plaa on the side (nam plaa is fish sauce that is used in Thai food to salt/flavor most dishes), but they say that they don't have it.  A Thai restaurant that doesn't have nam plaa?  What, do they cook with soy sauce (contrary to popular belief, soy sauce is not Thai, but it is used in some dishes that have more of a Chinese origin) instead?  That was the first hint at inauthenticity.  Then I tried their food, and I was even more disappointed than I had anticipated.  Their food is flavorless and overhyped.  If you're looking for authentic and delicious Thai food, don't come here.  This place is not worth it.

While this place is CRAWLING with "under-rats," it's quick and cheap Thai food as Thai food goes. A good varied selection of the usuals on the menu. Pleasantly healthy sized portions so if you're a "hungry man super size me" eater, go somewhere else to gorge yourself.

But they do have the second best pad see ew in the Bay Area. Thai Noodle being the first.

It's a shame because I think the quality of the food has been going on a downward spiral since I came to Cal.

I always get the Pad See Ew which is my absolute favorite. Sometimes I change it up a bit with the lunch special that comes with Pad Thai and 2-3 other dishes I can't seem to remember the name of. 

The Pad Thai has become seemingly drier and less tasty than I remember a year ago. Also the prices have gone up a bit and it takes them ages to prepare the food.

My girlfriend and I work at Unit 3 so we often go to Thai Basil on our breaks, and in the past, the portions have been fairly sizable. We haven't eaten there in a while, but today we decided to go there to share an order because we're trying to save money. To our dismay, our order of Basil Chili Chicken was noticeably smaller than usual. I won't hold this against them, because the food is still great. but personally I'd prefer a slight price raise over a portion deduction.

I've come here a few times, and I've tried their pad thai at least 3 times.  I think 3 tries is plenty; I am convinced that they don't cook it in the traditional way, or at least not in the way I grew up eating it. The owners/cooks might be from a different region of Thailand, so they cook it their way ---- too sweet, if you ask me.

Their mango and sticky rice is good though.
Their basil fried rice with added spicyness was one of my staple foods when attending school in btown.  Actually, I'd always order it before going out and getting craazzyy.  I'd highly recommend it.

I was sick and this place cured me of my stuffy nose, sore throat, watery eyes, sneezing, stuffy head, and minor coughs. Sounds like a Nyquil advertisement right? Well you're close but it's actually Thai Basil in Berkeley. After literally minutes of being lost on what to order in this courtyard of restaurants, I had chosen Thai Basil because of the long lines and numerous awards slathered on their window front.

Upon entering, the ordering process was togo style and I was enthusiastic about that because my food would arrive much quicker. Their menu is posted next to the line in huge lettering. My watery eyes grew large as they read each and every dish offered. Most dishes were below 7 bucks, a total winner for a college student. In addition, they had numerous vegan options for my 2 friends who happen to be vegan. 

I had settled upon the Penang curry and you cannot go wrong with curry. Last time I had curry was in Southern California and I experienced food poisoning for days. Well, first thing I noticed when I got my OJ and food, portions are huge! Dude, I can feed someone else with this. Instead of foam boxes, we have see-through plastic boxes which are a tad bit more environmentally friendly. 

Don't we love the word green? I like saving green, the kind in my wallet. Thai Basil in fact did that and the curry, a solid A. The curry was made fresh and it was piping hot. The steam coming from both the rice and curry literally fogged my camera lens like the Golden Gate's fog. The food cleared my sinuses with spiciness and permeated my taste buds with immense flavor as well. A total winner tucked away in this small courtyard. All its awards on the window, I agree.

I don't claim to be an authority on Thai food (or any other type of food for that matter), but I can say that the things they make here do taste quite good.

Out of all the places in Asian Ghetto, this place is the one i go to the most, despite the long waits. 

The Yellow Curry is really good, and the Pad Thai is alright.  And it is far better than that other thai place at the northside asian ghetto.  They give you a fair amount of food for the prices (which are deceptive, cuz they're all weird values like 6.21(actually 6.75) and 5.98 (actually 6.50), which has me thinking that they tend to round up for tax...) 

Anyways, if you wanna wait less, call them...they start making ur stuff just as if you'd ordered it in person.

After eating the Pad Kee Mao last night I realized that I had to update my review to 5 stars. 

My friends are always telling me how critical and judgmental I am when it comes with my food. I don't really realize it but I understand and likewise blame my growing up around the restaurant industry (especially my Dad). 

No, the food wasn't suddenly mind blowing last night. It was really good, the way it's been as long as I can recall. But it's more so that I realized that I couldn't count the number of times I've gone back to Thai Basil time after time for the Pad See Ew and/or Pad Kee Mao. And for me, that should automatically mean a 5-star yelp review.

So here you go. 
Keep up the good work.

from my first year in college where i had to portion one dish into two meals till now where i can eat a whole pad see ew and get a thai iced tea =P, this place has been absolutely awesome. i can't think of another place that serves amazing pad see ew and thai iced tea. it's also interesting to see that the same ppl that have worked there and the changes it has gone through throughout the years. i absolutely adore this place! 

minda heart thai basil/azn ghetto

ok...so i gave it a second chance and i love it. i have no idea what was wrong with my food the first time around but its actually REALLY good. 5 stars good. i had the same stuff the second time around it was very delicious, i will be returning!

I've ate at some expensive Thai places which came highly recommended by friends and the food at Thai Basil blows all of them away. And then there is the price...You can get any dish you want for around $7.50, but be sure to bring cash (no cards allowed).

Been here twice. I like how it doesn't have any minimum charge on credit card or actutally takes it. I heard lots of good things about the Pad Thai. It does taste really different from others, more darker and drier but really great flavor. I also ordered the Thai Noodle Soup, the soup is so dark it's kind of disturbing for me .. but it was GOod enough. At times, the flavor got a bit too much for me, even when I put hot sauce I couldn't taste much of my hot sauce. But it's worth trying because it tastes exactly like the average Thai Noodle Soup, not no Vietnamese pho. So far, the courses are fulll of flavor. It's a really laid back place, you don't get any servers or anythingg and all my courses were on average $6 and you don't have to tip, so it's great for a poor college student.

Accepts credit cards! YAY!!!!!!  Besides that, the thai food is good if you've never had Thai food before... but in comparison with Thai Noodle II, or some other Thai restaurants in SF, the food here is way too greasy!!! And after you try them all after 4 years of undergrad...they all begin to taste similar... but I guess you can't go wrong with the basil chicken. That was my fav

I love TB so much.  I rolled up to this place at all times and always satiate my craving for Thai throughout my college experience. 

I've had their Panang Curry, Yellow Curry, Pad Kee Mao, Basil Eggplant Tofu, but near the end of my college experience, just kept ordering the standard Pad Thai.

My qualms about this place are that it takes FOR EFFIN EVER to get your food.  I would go with my friends to Asian Ghetto and we'd all order at different places at the same time only for me to get my food 15 minutes after everyone else.  Also, I like paying by CC everywhere I go which is against anything and everything Berkeley's cash economy believes in.

I think you'll find better quality Thai food at other places, but Thai Basil is good because you get a hefty portion of decent food for a reasonable price.

I always choose between the following (from my fav to almost fav):
- Pad see ew
- Combination fried rice (really good if you ask for it extra spicy!)
- Pepper garlic chicken
- Pineapple fried rice

I've literally been going to this place for 20 years, and the food remains as delicious now as it was when I was at Cal. The Tom Kha Soup, you'll find none better outside of Bangkok. Creamy as hell, and a flavor that makes you feel like it was simmered for days. The Thai Fried Wontons are to die for, and the flavor on their Basil Chili Beef has kept me coming back for 2 decades: deep, rich, flavors of beef, peppers, onions, and spices. Tucked in a nook foodies might ignore, Thai Basil is NOT to be missed!

Coming from San Francisco, it's pretty special for me to say that this is a very good Thai restaurant.  The food is just plain awesome with strong flavors and very quick service.  Coming for a pleasing atmosphere or helpful cashier is not what you come to a take-out restaurant like this.  I've tried about 10 dishes and all are excellent.

Been here twice.
Most items on the menu are about $6. Portions really aren't terribly generous. Today I ordered the Pad Se Ew with Chicken...I was disappointed by the small amount of broccoli. Would rather go to Lucky House for this dish, but it was still good.
Another downside is that this place is really popular--not good if you're impatient like me.

What's awesome about this place is the location, and the variety.  Most of their dishes are very good, and of course this is wonderfully convenient and cheap.  My favorite dishes are the pad thai, pad see euw, basil eggplant chicken (surprisingly very good), pineapple fried rice, and garlic chicken.

THAI BASIL
I love Thai food. The spices, the presentation, the iced tea. Thai food is excellent, exotic, and simply delicious. My favorite Thai restaurant is in Davis, where they had bottomless iced tea. My favorite one in the Bay Area thus far is Krung Thai near Valley Fair. Surprisingly, my experience with Thai restaurants has been limited in San Francisco. Thai Basil has excellent sea bass. The meat was succulent and the taste was absolutely delicious! Suffice to say, the atmosphere was nice as always with excellent service. We also ordered the papaya salad, roti bread, crispy catfish, and chicken/basil dishes. If you like spicy, this is the place to go! Great place to dine on good Thai food, although sometimes, the music can be a bit too loud. There is also a full bar there; great mojito!

Dirt CHEAP thai food. :)

I fell in love with this place when I first tried the pepper garlic chicken. So juicy and flavorful. I don't think I've ever tasted anything like it! I remember I'd come here frequently when I wanted some quick thai food to be made. I was always satisfied every freaking time. 

Oh, how I miss the days when I could randomly come here ):

Okay thai food...i like thai noodle on telegraph better.

I don't understand why everyone is willing to stand in line for so long

i usually get the thai basil beef, pad see ew

Good portions for a decent price.

BUT since being spoiled by legit Thai food (I have thai friends), I'm starting to not dig this place anymore. The food is so greasy!

Thai Basil is probably my favorite Thai restaurant in Berkeley. BUT, I have to give it three stars because the service and quickness of the cooks are TERRIBLE. 

Seriously, this restaurant is the slowest one in Asian ghetto. I usually have to wait AT LEAST 20 minutes for my food...and for a thai food restaurant in the ghetto, that is ridiculous. There's always a long line of people waiting to order, and an even longer line of people waiting to get their numbers called for food.

I don't know what takes them so long...maybe they have to man-up on staff? But seriously... 20-30 minute wait for Asian ghetto food is problematic.

Despite the horrible service and wait, I still like Thai Basil. In my opinion, they make the BEST PAD SEE-EW EVER! I've tried some bomb thai food in socal, but I think Thai Basil's Pad See-ew is seriously a party in my mouth. I have random nights where I crave their Pad see-ew...yum.

Bottom line: they have good food, if you pick the right dishes. Just go at a time so you can avoid the hoards of fellow students.

Big portions and fair prices. I always get the basil eggplant chicken, which is around $7.50 and fills up a standard size to go container. Rice to eggplant ratio is a little high, but I like rice I don't complain. Other recommendations: pineapple fried rice, pad see ew, and pad kee mao. I think the noodles are too greasy, but they're well liked.

The Thai Basil Eggplant is wonderful and comes with plentiful rice!  In fact, I have not found my Thai Basil Eggplant replacement in San Francisco yet. 'Tis a shame.

When will my cravings subside?  It has been so many years!  This place makes me want to go back to college again.

That, my friends, is how you know it is true love.

(Disclosure: My love is only strong and true for the Thai Basil Eggplant.  I'm not a big fan of their other Thai dishes.)

College would not have been the same without Thai Basil.  I fell in love with Thai food when I first came to town so I went back this past weekend to relive my college years.

The #5, extra spicy: Basil eggplant chicken never fails. A friend's friend put it once: "they must put crack in this stuff." As soon as the first bite hit my tongue, I had flashbacks of all the late night study sprees, fraternity hazing events, the drugs (the illicit kinds), the music (the fast kinds), the alcohol (the tequila kinds), the parties (the good kinds) ...

I never wanted to relive my high school years, but I'll never pass up a chance to recollect an experience I had in college.  I'll come back here whenever I want to remember the good times and Thai Basil helps to solicit them from the deep regions of my polka-dotted memory.
#23 the Pad See Ewe. Enough said. It's so delicious and I love spicy foods so this place adds a little spice into my life :D

pad see ew is pretty good
but man, you'll remember one thing, you stood
a loooooooong time, 
if there are more than 4 in the line.

Place is a decent Thai place, food is good, prices are slightly high, but the wait.....oh, the wait can kill you.  If there's not that many people (like 2 or 3) then you should be good, but if there are more, whew!  I've seen friends wait like 30 minutes on a busy night.  Their food is cooked to order, but the wait might not be worth it.  

Gotta admit though, food is tasty.  I like it on the salty and saucy side though.

Part of the good ol' Asian Ghetto in Berkeley, a local favorite for late night eats and when too much brain power has been drained from hitting the books. 

If you like Thai food, this place is pretty good. They're a little too salty and saucy, but if you like your food that way, you'll like it here. Prices are a little higher than the rest of the place, but I find Thai food is usually like that. This place isn't nearly as fast as the other restaurants in the Ghetto.

I love eating here. 
Its cheap.
Its fast.
Its delightful.
I used to work a few blocks away and I would go to Thai Basil multiple times a week. 
My favorite dish is Pad See Ew.
I like that you can have it with no meat, and no eggs.
And it takes them no time at all to make.
I always recommend this place to all my friends.
I love their pad see ew!!!! Nom nom nom. I was hooked on it and wanted it everyday.

Cheap, delicious and convenient- this is definitely a STAPLE of my food life at Cal. My personal favorites are the Pad See Ew Chicken--safe, but yummy-- and the Combination Fried Rice-- SOOO good!

Definitely one of those Berkeley must-eats-- just remember to bring cash!

Closest thing to Asian comfort food in Berkeley.  It always hits the spot.  Food is full of flavor and cooked quickly in a wok.  While I stick to either the Pad See Ew or the Beef Fried Rice, others have told me that their curries are good as well.  It brings a touch of class to the food district known as the "Asian Ghetto".

Can't really complain. Inexpensive and delicious. Their pad see ew is amazing, and whatever my friends get is always well-received. Their spring rolls come with a wonderfully sweet (albeit heavily artificial) sauce. Unlike some reviewers here, I've never had them get my order wrong. The solution to this problem -- not guaranteed to be foolproof -- is to give them both the number AND the name of the dish so they'll have two chances to get it right. Easy enough. As for the wait, it's not impossible by any means (ten to fifteen minutes), but you might want to call ahead if you can.

You know that "delicious and comforting" feel about their food? It's called MSG, and lots of it. I saw them haul in a fifty-pound bag of the stuff and considered whether or not I should continue eating there. There was really no choice though; the MSG was too irresistible to quit. Like me, you'll keep coming back for more.

I've tried quite a few items on the menu and I think the only one that I probably would complain about is the pineapple fried rice. I didnt care for it since there were so many other good options for the same price. 

Pad see ew- I literally crave for this sometimes but I always finish it and want more. I'm satisfied but I wish I could food coma from it. haha.
Thai Basil chicken- Its one of the most popular dishes for a reason. I also ask for fried egg to put on top of my rice. :)
Pad Thai- its good but nothing special. I feel like you get more pad thai than pad see ew though so I guess that's a plus.
Combination Fried Rice- I used to get but the last time I got it, it was really oily so I stopped getting it. 
Sukiyaki- Its a bit sweet for my taste but on those cold berkeley days, this can really hit the spot. 
Any of the curries- I like thai curry so I guess I'm a little biased but the portions used to be SO big but now when I see people get the curry, its gotten so small. 
chicken skewers with peanut sauce- not reallly worth the price. I was hungry still after. 
bbq pork: pretty good but I'd still go for the noodles or basil chicken. 
Thai tea- noms. 


Besides the food, the location is really good since it's so close to campus and boba tea :)

Good cheap food. We ordered a ton of stuff. Red curry chicken, fried wontons, egg rolls, combination fried rice, chicken fried rice and some kind of peanut sauce chicken.  We ordered 4 drinks along with out meal and it was only $55!!!!!!!!  That was two appetizers and four main dishes along with drinks. Super cheap.

The only reason I didn't give this place five stars is cause of the disgusting bathroom I had to use. Another big disappointment was that this place is self served and you also have to clean up after yourself. No bueno on that note.

In the beginning I didn't like this place, but I finally found 1 dish that i like.  I always came back for it, but that's all.  The service is ok and the dining area is a bit dirty/sticky.  But just take it to-go and you won't have an issue.

i only order pepper garlic chicken over rice.. sooooooo good... 5 stars for that one dish? i just can't bring myself to do that..  but it is damn tasty forreal...  

they remodeled about 2 years ago now.. looks the same to me.. 

pepper garlic chicken... my tastebuds yearn for thee...

Cheap and fresh food!

Though the food takes a little more time than the other places in the Asian Ghetto, it is worth it. 

The basil eggplant chicken goes well with rice. Then again, most Thai dishes requires eating rice to aid the oily entrée to go down. 

The only reasons I knocked two stars off of my overall experience is (1) the staff is a bit rude, (2) there were not any pickled jalapeños and (3) most importantly, BASIL eggplant chicken lacked basil. 

But on a side note, if you love spicy, try the crushed dried red peppers. Ingesting a small amount creates a battlefield of spice in your mouth.

Since I actually know the people who own this place... how can I not 5-star it? =P No, just kidding, I really do like this place... I know it's in Asian Ghetto and everything, but it is the best pad see-ew I can find anywhere! And I have Thai restaurants up and down University Ave that are within walking distance of my place, including @Siam, Palm's Thai Dining, Bangkok Thai Restaurant, Plearn, and so on.

I love their pad see-ew. I love their pad thai too. And their thai iced tea. But honestly, besides that, I don't really try other dishes. I just come here for the pad see-ew. I dislike coming out smelling like Thai Basil though, so I try to take it to go when I can.

This review is only for two items - pad thai & pad see ew. I have only ever ordered those two items off the menu. Pretty greasy/not super healthy but OH SO DELICIOUS! They give you a good portion (depending on the time you arrive, if it's busy time they tend to split your portion with someone else)

Cash only is a big bummer since they used to take credit. Order takes an EXTREMELY LONG TIME so I'd recommend calling ahead!

The best place to go to inside the Durant Food Court (aka the Asian Ghetto).  For decent thai food that's easily accessible for students, this is the place to go. I'm a regular on getting basil chicken fried rice, and it's freaking delicious!  Whenever I want a homey, asian, rice dish, this is the place to go.  

The only bad thing is that it's super popular, and so lines and wait times can get hecka long.  TIP: Call in ahead and order, so you can just pay up when you get there and pick up immediately! saves a buttload of time.  

Also don't buy arizona here! get them at the vietnamee place right across, or the liquor store right outside the ghetto!

P.S. This place is way better than Thai House.

My friend who attends berkeley brought me to this place when I first visited.  
I'm an absolute fan of their chicken eggplant riceplate.  Super saucy, super tasty!! Big portions and cheap!!

After eating at this place, it made me want to go to cal, lol.  but too bad so sad, not smart enough -_-

Too bad she's graduating, now I won't have an excuse to come to this place to eat.  And on my last visit, they had some plumbing issue so they were closed. UGHHHHH so sad

practically the only thing in the "asian ghetto" worth eating.  i always get beef sa-tay (not on the menu).  their stir fried noodle dishes are decent as well.  they have cleaned up their decor/furniture, too.

it's okay Thai food, and really close to campus.  their bbq chicken and satay are both safe bets.  pad see ew is also decent.  don't go for anything too fancy or you'll be disappointed.  I used to like their pineapple fried rice a lot but I discovered that it can get quite old fast.  decent prices....hard to find a seat!

3 is pretty good for a place that is surrounded by homeless ppl and trash, so dont judge by the stars. 

Thai Basil is the second place that I went out to eat to while I was still a doe eyed freshmen girl with pigtails (jk no pigtails). Yes the place is gross, the ground leading up to the place is full of gravel, dirt, crack, pot, urine, ...., gross but once you get there, u can imagine that everything outside doesnt exist. The food is very satisfying, huge portions of carbs (rice, noodles) and a good ration of protein (fish or chicken whatever).

It's definitely the favorite and the lines can be long at odd times of the day but the food comes out relatively fast. Don't worry about what to order from their long list of menu, there are generally three different tastes category either sweet basil ish or slightly saltier sweet basil ish or curry. It just comes in different names or with different types of f meat, so a lot of things taste the same. I also like it that they have chili stuff lying around because I love spicy food, if it's empty, i'm probably the one who took it all on.

They redid their interior maybe a year ago so it's better than before but  dont take anyone here for a romantic date unless you really like getting kicked in the ass.

Oh also, they close around 11 or so, earlier than other gourmet ghettos so probably can't go here when you get the munchies, their neon sign is off when they're closed.

I LOVE CHEAP, GREASY THAI FOOD! DELICIOUS!!

My favorite dish here will forever and ever be the spicy eggplant chicken.  Perfectly sweet, salty, with a hint of chili (oil) that makes this dish the BEST dish ever!  I've tried other Thai restaurants' eggplant chicken, and no other place compares to good old Thai Basil.  If you like eggplant, this is **THE DISH** to order.

I've had the pleasure of trying a few other dishes, such as their curries and their eggrolls, which aren't very impressive or tasty.  I tend to stick with their eggplant chicken (per above) and their noodle dishes (pad see ew, pad kee mao, and pad thai).  I find that these dishes are their signature, hallmark dishes.  I'd stick with these and definitely recommend these dishes hands down. 

A few changes since my last review (came here three times since my last review) -- they don't accept credit card anymore.  There was a period of time when they did, then they didn't, then they did, and now they don't again.  So, bring cash!

Thai Basil still gets 5 stars in my books since their signature dishes are consistently excellent, cooked well, and never disappoint.  While there are a few dishes that were not to my liking, this doesn't take away from any stars since Thai Basil is cheap, great quality & quantity, and spicy and greasy - just the way Thai food should be. 

Every time I'm in Berkeley, I have to come here to order something at Thai Basil.  I don't think I can live without it.

Cheapity cheapity. For about $7.50 you can get a generous serving of whatever your heart desires. The only downside is that everything is super greasy! Food comes out lightening fast and the seating is a free for all, serve yourself. One of my faves in the "Asian Ghetto food court".

total cluster f**k after game days.  it takes some 30 minutes to get your food.  seriously people whats going on?

needless to say, i love the spicy eggplant and chicken, and will continue to order it.  sure it's not the greatest, but its been a reliable joint for over 10 years.

I definitely wouldn't call Thai Basil the "finest" Thai restaurant in the East Bay, but I would hazzard to call it the best.  During my one semester at UC Berkeley I ate here probably four times a week.  I would not recommend the noodle dishes or fried rice unless that's really all you're into; it's the stir fry that rules here.  For me, Thai Basil is great due to the terrific Thai triumvirate of the dishes Tofu Prik King with string beans, and Eggplant Basil with Tofu, along with free (at this price!) hot tea.  The sauces are rich, sweet, salty, and greasy, so if you're looking for haute Thai cuisine with delicate flavors, you should probably go somewhere much more expensive.  But for what it is and at this price point, Thai Basil is the best.

Whenever I'm in Berkeley and I have a spare hour and half I go here. You really need patience to eat  here especially during the school year.
