Basically it's guaranteed that your wait is gonna be around 30 minutes long even for just Pad Thai and on top of that this place is cramped there isn't enough seating for all the people who want to eat here. And when you do get a seat (lucky) you can care less about personal space cause theres gonna be tons of people up in your cooch sitting wayy to close. The food itself is either a hit or miss, I've had some delicious dishes on the other hand I've had some friends who think otherwise.

Basic thai dishes here
Always order pad thai #21
Size is quite large
Inexpensive
Long lines and wait

Ordered the pad thai ($7.25 included tax) and waited a really long time for my order. I noticed they're always super busy and can be rude to non-asian people. Not cool. But cheap $ and greasy food will last for 2 to 3 meals (CeCe size portions)! haha 

There are soooo many eateries in that mini plaza!!! Thai, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Middle Eastern, Italian, massive size donuts, etc.!! I wanted to try everything!!

One of the finest Thai restaurants in the East Bay; they recently completed an overhaul of their location sporting newly painted walls, an updated counter and relatively comfortable seating as well as new lighting.  Yes, that is right; you no longer have to sit and eat under the horrible glow of flourescent lighting.  But you dont come to Thai Basil for the atmosphere.  You come for the inexpensive food cooked rather quickly and consumed while mingling and staring at the hordes of Berkeley students that pack this and eight other asian restaurants off Durant Ave.  During lunch they have a special for under six dollars that offers soup or spring roll and a main dish.  Their vegetable fried rice does not ever dissapoint, this after nearly fifteen consecutive attempts at eating this dish.  The sweet and sour tofu is a delight for vegetarians; but in essence, there is no shortage of decent options making the Thai Basil a great spot for a quick fix of Thai food.  It will please the group and your stomach while not putting a hole in your college-sized budget.  Just be sure to not look right into the eyes of the meth-addicted rail kids that perch on the street corner begging the youth for spare coins. Ahh, it is all part of the Telegraph Ave. experience.

Call me biased being a Cal grad, but this is still my favorite Thai restaurant.  I say that even after having been to Thailand.. and even with a Thai restaurant on every half block around me in SF.  

They took my pad sew ew virginity and no other place has been the same.  Unlike your typical stir-fry, their noodles come out a bit charred.. I love that smoky peppery taste and have yet to find another place that does it the same way.

They also stripped me of my pad thai innocence and again, I have yet to find another one that hits the spot.  Their flavors are just a bit richer than any other Thai restaurant I've been to.. leaving an everlasting stamp on my heart.  And who doesn't miss the ~$7 dinners of our college years?

Thai basil for dinner.. paired with a Sweetheart's boba.. with a stop at King Ping Donuts for dessert.  THAT'S HOW IT'S DONE!

Thai Basil was my first introduction to Thai food... Back when I was a student, Thai Basil was my spot.  Eggplant Basil Chicken, Garlic Pepper Chicken, and the Basil Fried Rice (w/ extra cilantro and basil).  **drool**    I'm going to knock them down a star for rising prices, watered down chili paste, and those tiny ass drinking cups!

This is the "go-to" spot for Cal students when they are craving asian food. This place is cheap, tasty, and is one of the reasons why the asian ghetto has such great reputation. All dishes range from $5-$8

The "chefs" at this place are actually Moms and Grandmas. Do not underestimate them, in fact, I'm sure they can make better food than pricey/overrated fancy thai restaurants! 

Recommendations: 
1) Pineapple Fried Rice: because the wok is super heated (I'm sure with the help of LOTS of oil) the fried rice is cooked just right. Each grain is separated and is seasoned with yellow curry powder. This plate paired with pineapples, peanuts, cashew nuts, and shrimp is the perfect combination for "pineapple fried rice". Extra ratings for this dish because they don't put raisins in there! I know some thai places will do that in their pineapple fried rice. 
2) Pepper Garlic Pork: tasty tasty tasty. Great marination. The pork is shredded into pieces and is grilled. It's purely heaven when paired with steam rice. The rich marination balanced with close to tasteless white rice is a great intervention. 
3) Beef, and Broccoli Pad See Ew: this is a rice noodle. The pan fried noodles are similar to the chinese "ho fun". The noodles are well flavored with soy sauce and sugar. (yeah sugar, sounds weird but it's really good!) This is definitely a must try if you are craving noodles. 
4) Yello Curry: can't go wrong with coconut milk tasting curry. If you are a thai place and you screw this up then you don't deserve to stay in business! 

Lastly, to honor broke students around the area, they have this daily lunch special. You get to pick (i think) 3 items for like a little over $5. Great choice if you want to be spontaneous and feel like  trying a little of everything!

It's one of several restaurant in the Asian Ghetto / Durant Food Court that actually has seating. While it's good for a quick bite admist hardcore studying, it's not good for those who think they can bring their notebooks and cram while waiting for their order. The noise level here is usually pretty loud.

Friends used to complain that the size to price ratio here is not big enough compared to other places in the ghetto, but all the other places are slowly raising their prices and decreasing portions anyway.

Favorite: pineapple fried rice. the pineapple they use is really firm, which makes me believe that they use fresh pineapples, but they probably don't, in which case, does a good job of fooling me.

The chicken is not recommended here.

Nothing has made me realize how far I've fallen in life than this excuse for food.

Four years ago, I was a reasonably well paid consultant. I traveled the world, eating the best food I could find. Life was good.

Now, I'm a grad student, and this sketchy alley reeks of low expectations. I couldn't finish my meal. I don't know what I should have expected, but it was terrible. I just wasn't hungry enough to swallow more than five or six bites of it. Maybe when I was a young and tired undergrad, maybe. But like Plato's cave, there's just no going back to some things.

Minus 2 for being gross, and minus another 2 for making me feel terrible about myself.

I walk in and order my food to go and wait like 20 minutes. It finally comes out and is not what I ordered so the people who make the food tell me to go pay the difference to the cashier and they'll give me what I really ordered. I go up to the lady and tell her I ordered X and she yells "No, you didn't!" and argues with me. TIME FUCKING OUT.
#1- I AM THE FUCKING CUSTOMER AND THUS ALWAYS RIGHT.
#2- I FUCKING SPEAK ENGLISH AND YOU DON'T SO I'M PRETTY SURE I KNOW WHAT I FUCKING ORDERED.
I was so pissed at her audacity I walked away and told the food people to give me the wrong order because their cashier was a bitch. They were very apologetic.
Oh, and the food sucked.
The cashier bitch is a bitch. (She's the old hag with ugly big eyeglasses who barely speaks English.)

TIP FOR RESTAURANTS RUN BY IMMIGRANTS: YOUR BEST ENGLISH SPEAKER SHOULD BE YOUR CASHIER.

Bottom line: don't come here unless you're a)starving, b) fluent in Thai, or c) both.

This is one of my favorite thai place to eat but I would never go here unless I was around. It's full of college students and homeless people. Eating outside makes you feel a little iffy because of all the homeless people walking around digging through trash for left overs. If you eat inside then it's fine. The food is great!

The Pad ke mao is good and the pad se ew is good too. Everythign I've had there is good. The Basil fried rice... mmmmm

Thai Basil is really well-priced for their delicious Thai food!  Serving sizes are also pretty big.  I've always had left-overs.  It's probably one of my favorites in Asian Ghetto.  They have all the typical dishes you would expect at a Thai restaurant.  I'm a huge fan of their pad thai which has a different kind of sauce than the pad thai I order at most thai restaurants but is really good nevertheless.  My roommate, one of the most pickiest eaters I know, only goes here to get fried rice.  The one downside is that sometimes the wait can be ridiculously long due to its popularity.  Not such a good option when you're in a hurry.  But if you have time, the food is worth the wait.  You get it immediately after it's cooked so it's always nice and hot.  It's especially good if you're a fan of strong and heavy flavor.  Probably not so great, though, if you're trying to be healthy.

nestled deep in the back of Asian Ghetto lies a fried rice wonder land known as Thai Basil. its neon-lighted sign and scent of MSG reels in Cal students like a moth to the flame.

i know there are complaints about the old hag manning the register. don't mind her, just pay the lady and chuckle at her ancient garb. and i know the old guy can be a bastard, but just remember that he has to have hot oil splashed on him from an old rusty wok for 12 hours a day.

all that aside this place does wonders for starving college students. the thai basil fried rice is a must and would be recommended for newbies. or you can step it up a notch and try the curry panang, or my favorite, pineapple fried rice. most dishes, seafood excluded, cost around $6-8. a fair price for a mound of fried rice, or a moderate plate of noodles.

i know they grease that wok like a holiday ham, and yes, indigestion is quick to follow, but in all my travels to Berkeley i have not found a more suitable place to chow down at after midnight.

let me make this short and sweet so you can quit reading this and you can get your ass over there to try it!!!!

BEST PAD THAI EVER. EVER. (They have plenty of awards to back this up, plus me and all my friends who eat pad thai on the reg in and all around the bay area agree---their pad thai is SOOO GOOD). It's cheap, slightly sweet, has all the right flavors--basically perfect.

My two other top favorite dishes are the  pineapple fried rice and ***THE PINEAPPLE CURRY CHICKEN***.  Even if you are not an avid curry-lover, or have never tried it before--this dish is the best place to start! I've already converted some of my friends who said they'd NEVER eat curry, and they all say this dish is delicious! It's spicy (from the jalapeno and spices), doesn't have too strong a curry flavor, is complimented by the sweet pineapple chunks and the sauce goes perfect over their fluffy white rice.... YUM-O!!! 

(ughhhh, I just made myself hungry writing about it!!)

I've been a big fan of Thai Basil for many years.  I have always gotten the same dish--Pad Kee Mow with tofu (#42).  It's f'ing good. Seriously.  I just got some today.  They make it nice and spicy if you tell them to.  I haven't really tried anything else. I don't think there is any need.  The wait can be long sometimes if you go during lunch hour.

I think it's about time that I write a review for Thai Basil. I've been coming here for the past 3 years, and after visiting all the Thai places in Berkeley, they definitely top my list. Asian ghetto wouldn't be the same without Thai Basil. My top favorites (in no particular order):

- Combination Fried Rice
- Yellow Curry Noodle
- Tom Kha Gai
- Kao Moo Dang
- Cashew Nut Chicken
- Yellow Curry Chicken

... and so much more! They're pretty decently priced, although they tend to round up their prices when you order. For example, $7.56 will really end up costing you $8. When you think about tax thought, I guess you're actually saving money. 

I seriously have to salute the employees that work here. All day long on their feet in a crowded kitchen, providing hungry impatient college students with really good Thai food, and they're still there. These guys are really amazing. Some might complain how long it takes to get your order, but Thai food takes a while to make, especially if you want it done right.

As much as I love Stanford, the food there is bland and overpriced and all in all, kinda sucks.  

After moving some of my stuff to Berkeley, I stopped by the infamous Asian ghetto to try some of their food and decided on Thai Basil.  Synopsis: Somewhat fast, pretty cheap, and comes out piping hot and delicious!  I'm gonna like food at Berkeley...

When I first came to Berkeley as a 17-year-old freshman, I was quite misguided. I thought that to get to campus, I was supposed to walk south on College. I thought that a boy kissing me meant that he must really, really like me. And I also thought that the Asian Ghetto was exciting and full of delicious places to eat. 

Three and a half years later, I've managed to realize that none of the above is true. However, the one place I still come to in the Asian Ghetto/Durant Food Court is Thai Basil. It always promises heaping portions of satisfying, slightly greasy food at a reasonable price. When I do get lunch take out, I always opt for the lunch special -- $5.75 for 2 or 3 items (see photo: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/h11Hr07ffM-dn-rico0_fA?select=oRZrMoluXTQ6r2PFd5Eu_g). At dinner, I almost invariably get the pad see ew. 

The wait here can get pretty ridiculously long, so I'd suggest that you program their number into your phone to call ahead.

Thai Basil is a Berkeley student standby. It can't be considered the best Thai food (because anything that's a standby can't be the best) but it works to satisfy the asian food craving. Most of the time I order 2 only the Basil Eggplant tofu or the Pad Kee Mao. Both are served in huge portions and the rice is never overcooked or too wet. The eggplant is by far my favorite dish served at the restaurant, but it can be a bit too greasy most of the time.

I went in for lunch the other day and had the lunch special, which consisted of rice and a choice of two items. I got the cashew chicken and the basil tofu though I have learned now that the majority of their meat dishes are usually overcooked and I would do better not to order the chicken in the future.

The flavors are a bit too muddled and not distinctly Thai like I would hope. Even so, it serves well as a quick bit to eat in the middle of the day.

o thai basil.. you have fed me well throughout my college years.. o i miss you so!

I came back here for dinner with a friend yesterday night. and the pad see ew was delicious!! I've mainly ordered their Pad See ew here thats why I had to come back to have a reminiscing moment with my favorite!  I loved how thick the noodles were with full of shrimps.. Too bad they only gave me 3 broccolis......!  On the side, I had my favorite thai drink of Thai Iced Tea.  Nice, sweet, and milky! just like how i like it.. Good amount also!!  If you ask them for less ice though, they will charge you an extra 25-50 cents....

Quick and fast for students!  I am all for it!  Good selections against the wall with few pictures!  The lady at the front is very nice and understanding.  Good amount of seats inside Thai Basil.. No AC though! but good luck finding spots in the middle of asian ghetto amongst all the students!!!!!!

This is some of the better food in this food court. What struck me most about this place is their rice. Very aromatic rice. I think they might actually use basmati rice, instead of the typical Californian calrose variety. The interior is recently renewed, and much cleaner than before.

Mmmm, I always love binging on food after a night of binging on alcohol.

My shrimp fried rice was pretty good- it hit the spot, but was nothing exceptional. However, my friend's garlic eggplant dish was amazing. Makes me wish I had ordered it as well!

To the douchebag who told us to quiet down because he was "trying to have a conversation"...hello, it's midnight and you're in a college town! Besides, your date didn't seem to be too into you. Hah!

Pad kee mao: $7.25

Who doesn't enjoy the occasional round of "Try to blend in with the undergrads?"  It's one of my favorite games.

I returned to Thai Basil for lunch today after a fairly awful experience with their curry a fairly long time ago, and I'm glad I gave it another shake.  In the South Asian Ghetto, lunch is always a process of eliminating the worst options and then seeing what's left.  Then you deliberate for five more minutes with your friends until you just say, "Eff it, let's just go there."  I'm happy to add Thai Basil as another tummy friendly option to the deciding process.

There are no frills here: they make your food (in about five minutes), you eat it (it tastes like Thai food), and you leave (once you're done eating; the order is crucial).  The food's pretty good and the prices are reasonable.  Additionally, I'm intrigued by their $5-6 lunch special where you pick items from the board.

Please note, however, that I will still never order their curry again *shudders*.

Super Affordable.  Great Taste.  Convenient Location!

Every student at Cal should try Thai Basil.   Okay, when the boss lady argues with her husband (?), it gets pretty scary.  But who cares?  The food is so good and cheap.

I can't give a fair review of the restaurant because the only dish I get from there over the past 5 years is Basil Fried Rice w/ Chicken.
But as other reviewers have pointed out, everything else seems to be great too!


Try it once and you'll fall in love with it.   I've personally converted a lot of my friends.

5 Stars for the great quality yet low price.

I would pick this place over a lot of other gourmet Thai restaurants in a heart beat.

MUST TRY!

so, admittedly, i'm the leftover queen.
i'll eat mine.
i'll eat yours.
i'll eat your friends' who are sitting at the other end of the table (who i haven't met yet) that are giving me the stink eye b/c i'm already eyeing their half eaten entrees.

am i ashamed?
of course not.
i WOULD be ashamed of myself if i threw away food that people would kill for on the other side of the world.

thai basil conversation:
me:  can i have a box please?
female cook behind the counter:  do you want one or two?
me:  one, please.
(cook hands a box to me.  i turn around, take five steps, turn back around, realizing that my spicy basil catfish w/rice (which wasn't spicy and was average tasting) will require a second box...)
me:  actually, can i have another one, please?
cook (scowling):  i asked you if you wanted two, and you said no!!

yeowch.

...the trials and tribulations of the leftover queen...

I love this place! They are open late and conveniently located in the Asian food Ghetto. Their food is cooked fresh and authentically, and the flavors are always bodacious. 

I also love the totally gangster Asian lady that works here. I often come here drunk on obnoxiousness and she never ceases to amaze me when she puts me in my place. Cue scene:

Me: AYAYYAYYAYAYYAYAAYYAYAYAYAY!!!! *playing with the toothpick dispenser"
Friend: YAY TOOTHPICKS! YAY! YAY! YAY!
Me: YAYY! *making more toothpicks pop up*
Asian Lady behind the register: ENOUGH! *mean look*
Me: *stunned into stopping* Oh sorry! Sorry! *stuffing toothpicks back in the dispenser.
Asian Lady: YOU DON'T PUT BACK! *sticking out her tongue*
Me and friend: Okay...*backs away and is shamed into silence for 30 seconds"
Me and friend: YAYAYAYAYAYYAYAYAYAYAYAYAYAYAYYAYAY!
Asian Lady: SHHH!
Me and friend: *quiets down*

As I said. Hella gangasta.

My favorite entree here is the garlic basil eggplant. I get tofu when no one wants to eat my chicken, or I'll get chicken if someone wants to eat the chicken. I'm here for the eggplant :)

I've been here several times for what else, but of course, for boba tea. 

Tiny space, dirty counters and mediocre drinks.

But their deep fried snacks are good, it's only because the germs are deep fried as well, so you won't get food poisoning.

Quickly is my favorite place to get milk tea out of all of the boba places in Berkeley.  The tea is very strong and flavorful and it's super cheap.  I like how they don't put a lot of ice in their tea so it doesn't get watery if you take your time.

I am a fan of boba and I have tried boba in other places too. I used to get it from Tapioca Express in Union City a lot and they have the best so far. About a year ago, I found this place on Durant @ Berkeley. They have very good boba and I would give them 4 stars on the alone. They are the cheapest $1.64 [5 stars] among all the places that I've been to and provided with the quality that we are talking about. With no doubt this place is very small, it can fit 3 or 4 people to wait in line.  Cleanliness is really an issue for them though and I would say if they can provide straws in clear plastic wraps would really be better.

So, I was a faithful customer of this place for about one year, then i discovered sweethearts next door. They are cheaper, and better. I went to get a boba today, but sweethearts was closed, so I went to quickly. It was 40 cents more expensive, the boba was NOT cooked at all, and the drink had an ant in it...GROSSSS....I threw it out after 3 sips...what a waste of $2.18....never again...

Bleh.

What did you do to my boba? What have I done to deserve it?
dirty.
The milk tea is pretty standard for a Quickly. A large milk tea with pearls is a little over $2. Cheap and fast, perfect for a student rushing between classes.

This Quickly is just as good as any other Quickly.  The store is very small but the service is quick.  They don't have shaved ice here but their tea selection is pretty much the same.  Their lichi rose tea is sooo goood! 

If I lived in the neighborhood, I'd be stopping by more often to grab a tea!

It's okay, nothing too special, nothing bad.

Customer service is hit-or-miss, depending on who's there.

Only place I've found that makes decent Taro Milk Tea though; nearby boba shops don't really compare. Usually really fast service; there are some long lines sometimes though.

This is one of the worst boba drink places I've ever been to in my life.
I've been a fan of boba drinks for 10+ years (and have drank just waaaay to much boba...)
and this place really is at the bottom of my choices for my tapioca savoring adventure.
 
Their tapioca tastes gross, sometimes. At rare occasions, it has been good but i'd rather not take the chance and go elsewhere
Their teas are OK. but the snow bubbles were horrible. THey charge all that money to make it smoothie but when the product comes out, it looks all melted and doesn't really resemble a smoothie. 

There's Sweetheart's cafe right next door. I'd rather go there than quickly any day.

My friend worked here for a while, so I came to visit him...

I got a free boba. ehhh it's ok. I like the plaza that this is in tho...
you can get your fast cheap asian food.

"THE ASIAN GHETTO" they call it.

Quickly's my go-to place for boba.

Service: I always found the cashiers at the front to be really nice and fast.

Food: Popcorn chicken, in my opinion, is better at Sweetheart, but boba is definitely better here. Their milk tea is not too sweet and their boba is chewy to the right texture. I don't even like boba all that much and I come here anyway. Good for a quick drink.

Before, I never really had a reason as to why I always went to Sweetheart instead. Now I do. I'm pretty convinced the cups are bigger over there, and the employees are nicer and faster. Oh, and not complete idiots.

The guy that gave me coffee with pearls at Quickly was the worst!

a) He didn't put the cap on tightly, so a little spilled out and scalded my hand
b) He gave me the wrong amount of change
c) He charged me for pearls after I ordered them, but didn't give them to me. I would have caught the mistake then and there but the coffee was practically boiling still and I couldn't check.

I was angriest about the last one! Never again!

Wednesday, 5:00PM.

An extempore run for boba led me to the Quickly's here in the DFC. Their interpretation of tapioca is aberrant from what it's supposed to be!

+Quick service
+Cheeeeap
- "Stale" boba
- Lack of soy, low-fat milk as options

And then...?
Moccachino's closed? Long lines at Sweetheart Cafe? Super tight budget? Fine, Quickly's in DFC it is.

How fast can they get food and drinks to their customers... QUICKLY?  I think NOT!

I really want to like this hole in the wall in Durant Square (and don't you dare call this place the Asian GHETTO)! Why has the name of this place been racialized?! YUCK.  

The one only think I like about this place: It does the trick when I am craving fried fish balls (once in a very blue moon).

But eh, overall... the service is mediocre, drinks are just okay.  There are way too many boba places in Berkeley... this place is not tops.

If you want a "run of the mill" Quickly's, here you go. Not too much to impress customers here, as I really wanted to write something to give the locals a reason to go here instead of another place for desserts. 

This Quickly's is small, fast, yet something's lacking (perhaps a few seats more seats). Their selection is the same as others, though none of my companions were too impressed with this one.

Nothing really wrong with this place, though its not the only dessert specialty in the area, not by a long shot.

My usual: Green tea - DOUBLE rainbow jelly. 

$1.74. I hope this never changes!
Decently cheap and okay boba... nothing more, nothing less...

I know it's a bit of an unfair gripe to apply to Quickly here but is it really that hard Berkeley stores and restaurants to accept credit cards? I hate that I have been turned away so many times (and have missed out on really good places as a result) because I simply don't carry cash around anymore. That being said, you have to be weary that this place is cash-only, which is a bit annoying in my mind. 

Quickly in the Asian Ghetto is just a hole in the wall, which means you're in and you're out, or so you'd think. My feeling is that this place could use another staffer or so and close later. The line is almost always out the door, which means that there are only four or five people in line. Once in though, it's actually decent. It's pretty sweet that you can have a mix of different things to put into your milk tea besides the standard big ol' balls of boba like jelly or tiny boba. I would also have to say that their food is definitely a lot better than Sweetheart's, albeit you'll get a bit less. 

Sweetheart's just steals up all the customers because there is a greater food option at Sweetheart's for nearly the same price and they stay open so late. Also, the appearance of a long line because of their small store size is also a bit intimidating if you're trying to just grab a boba and go. But hello, know your customer demographics! You're right by a college town catering to poor college students! Stay open longer and hire another person so it doesn't seem like you guys have a humungo line all the time!

this place sucks. only one person works there and she does the cashier, making the food, and making the drinks.

fried chicken- it sucks. it really sucks. they make fried chicken but dont put the hot seasoning on it, you have to do it urself. and they dont put in those tiny green leaves used for seasoning, which i love! 

in socal quickly, boba already comes with the drink but here it isnt. idk why.

well anyways dont get the drinks anyways, it aint good.

I don't really know why this place gets such a bad rap.  You can't really compare discount boba places to cafes like Tapioca Express.  The price difference is significant, as is the quality, but you get a pretty good return for your money at Quickly.  The tea is some of the best as far as cheap tea goes - better than Sweethearts' and Moccacino's in my opinion.  Some days are better than others, but it tends to go that way with these kinds of places.

I think this is the only place in Berkeley with mini boba (maybe Tapioca Express has them, I can't be sure), and it's much better than their regular boba.  Their regular-sized boba tends to be too hard.  

The reason this place gets 3 instead of 4 stars is because, in comparison with other Quicklys, this place is not so great.  The tea is more expensive, not as good and there's no seating, as compared to other Quickly establishments.  This isn't exactly a problem when you're looking to get your tea fast and bounce, but it's difficult to justify a higher price when you have fewer amenities.

Despite all this, Quickly is still my place for super fast, super cheap boba.  I go more often than I'm comfortable admitting :P

Not much to say, except this is the place I go when I crave bubble tea. There is nothing more satisfying than an almond milk tea or a taro milk tea from here. Super cheap, very fast, and consistently good.

Whenever I pass by, I get a "passion-fruit snow".  It is always good and unlike other places, it doesn't quickly lose its flavor and leave you with ice water at the bottom.  Don't get their food though...  That looks pretty gross.

Lately I have been getting their Thai Iced Tea.  It is decent, but it is much different from what you get at Thai restaurants, or the pinnacle of Thai iced tea: the Thai Buddhist temple.  It just is not as good, unfortunately.

The line sometimes reaches out the door and there is usually only one person working so things can get backed up if there are many people ordering. Items are a bit on the pricey side for what you're getting, but I guess that's the luxury of drinking blended beverages. The creamer used in their milk tea makes it a bit too sweet, but it gets the job done if you're craving a fix.

This is one of the tapioca places that I go. The place is very small, I would say only barely 5 customers can wait in line. But it's ok. If you get the food there, you can sit outside the benches in the common area. I have never tried their food here though coz my favorite is still tapioca milk tea and it's only $1.96. But I still would like to see them put out more napkins and have the individual wrapped straw.
Boba is cheap, but doesn't taste that great. Rainbow cafe is better.

I like the black sesame milk drink here...but everything else is typical of the Quickly chain. A good selection of boba replacements.

Probably the tiniest boba shop in the area too.
I loved this place cause it was a great fast stop between classes!

Downside: as part of the Durant Food Court ("Asian Ghetto"), you can't expect Quickly's to have the most sterile environment. The place is small and you usually feel cramped when there's a line. 

Upside: most of the time, there is/are 1-2 people working on the orders and service is usually fast. I always order their green milk tea (sometimes with, sometimes without boba) and it's consistently good. Compared to Sweethearts, the milk teas at Quickly's are more milky.

I come for the cheap boba and popcorn chicken. Nom nom!

But what I really love about this place is the variety in types of boba you can get--I love getting the small tapioca! To be honest, it seems on the same level as Sweetheart or Moccacino. I prefer Mocaccino for their bento deal and Sweetheart for its quicker efficiency when there isn't a long line.

it's hard for me to pick between quickly's and sweetheart cafe.  Milk tea's here are less sweet than those at Sweetheart and the workers here are definitely much more affable.  I once came here around noon and somehow they were out of boba. what the heck!?

Ordered a drink.

10 seconds later the cashier handed it to me.



I suppose that's why they're named Quickly's?
Just so so. The milk tea is too plain.

$2.16 jasmine green milk tea, half boba, half lychee jelly. 

My friend tried to order this somewhere else and was charged for the half half option so yay for berkeley's Quickly's for being nice ;)

I dont know what people are complaining about the service. I find it the service pretty fast and my only complaint is that the waiting space is a little small. If anything, I feel like the service at sweetheart is worse because some workers there are so grumpy! 

I've never tried any other flavors here so this is just based on the jasmine green milk tea which is my favorite :) I actually dont even go to Sweet hearts anymore.

I used to like Sweetheart Cafe more than Quickly's, but when I found out that Sweetheart's uses powder instead of milk tea and Quickly's doesn't, I quickly switched over ;).

$2.16 for a jasmine green milk tea with pearls. I like their variety of jellies and pearls - I like to get 1/2 small pearls with 1/2 lychee jelly. Mixing half and half of different pearls/jellies is free of charge!

Definitely not the best milk tea ever, but it works quite well for Berkeley.

I'm usually not one to support chain restaurants but quickly is so cheap and fast that it's hard not to like their drinks.  The people working aren't too cheerful but aren't mean like at sweethearts.  The boba is usually just the right consistency with a chewey but not gooey consistency (like at sweethearts).  With most of my drink orders, I never go over 2 bucks and it takes less than 20 seconds to be sucking boba up a big straw (sweethearts takes about 3 minutes minimum).

I don't care for milk tea/boba, and even if I had tried theirs, I wouldn't know where it would fall on the scale of amazing to terrible. 

So whence the five stars?

Their potstickers! I'm sure that these grease/oil-ridden potstickers rank pretty high on the list of my worst vices, but they're so delicious. For $2.99, I get a fantastic snack that always seems to hit the spot. I've recently been diversifying and gave their mini corndogs a try as well -- tasty. I guess one of these days I'll give their milk tea a try, too...

The drinks I think is not as good as other Quickly! I've have much better Quickly.
The service was not very good.
Small and cramped space. Uncooked boba. There was a special though so I scooped up my jasmine green tea for less than $2.

I like the location because the plaza seems to have every type of food imaginable. It's cash only so make sure you have them dolla billz

Selections are vast, but was missing aloe as an optional topping... I like that they have two types of boba (small and large) and it's cheap. I would say it was an average experience.

This is the smallest Quickly's I've ever seen.  There's no seating area, just standing room to wait for your order.  After eating at Steve's Bar-B-Que before a Cal football game, we came across this Quickly's.  We wanted some tapioca and it was cheap (they still had the 1.49 Jasmine Milk Tea with tapioca special at that time).  It satisfied our tapioca craving.

I'm giving it 3 stars 'cause the prices and speed cannot be beat. By the time I'm finished paying, my drink is already ready. The drinks themselves are mediocre. I usually get the jasmine milk green or the normal milk tea (no boba. Got over the whole boba craze years ago) depending on my mood. It tastes alright. Bubble milk tea is bolder, the jasmine milk green more subtle. But the milk green does leave this weird filmy feel in my mouth. I can't really describe it. It's just this weird feeling. I think it's funny when the workers mix the milk tea in that huge pot thing. It's like a small Asian girl using this huge mixer tool to mix up the drink in this ginormous pot. Kinda looks like she's using one of those drill machines (can't think of the name) to bore a hole in the ground.

This Quicklys was a let down - while I understand that different boba places make their bobas differently, the boba at this place is almost inedible! (The milk tea is alright).

For the food, it's a lot of money for not a lot of (low quality) food.

I'm surprised at how this place is still in business when the Sweetheart's around the corner is a gazillion times better and cheaper.

This quickly consists of many sinks and a table behind the counter. promo items are covers the walls and windows.

sampling: jasmine tea (1.29+tax)
-how can they charge tax when it's obviously to go?
-not much tea flavor, tasted slightly sweet.
-passed on pearls and milk option.

tea drips:
-courteous fast service. probably disappointed on no upgrades.
-few seats to sit in.

UGH. I hate this place. I guesssss it's all right if you want boba for less than a dollar but I always feel cheated out of my money and mad whenever I come here. 

Some of the horrible things that have happened whenever I decide to give this place a try (because it's so cheap) or because someone else wants to come here (also probably cuz it's so cheap):
-boba being stuck together so you can't get it out of the damn straw, you literally have to blow the boba back into your cup *ewwwwwwwwwww* and then try to avoid that boba cluster until you're finished with your drink
-on hot days, they NEVER put enough ice and you're left with lukewarm milk tea or jasmine green tea
-hot drinks are SCALDING so be careful. can't sip for a while. if you try it on a cold berkeley winter day, you'll know how hard it is to resist trying to drink it... but beware, you're gonna get burned!! 
-misunderstanding of my order... UGH. has happened at least 2x. both ended up with me going 'never mind never mind, it's ok' just so i can get out of the claustrophobic little space
-their drinks just always taste bad. i have never been to a place with gross thai iced tea as bad as quickly's. out of alllllll businesses that leave berkeley, why can't this one disappear?! 
-long wait times for crappy, sticky, hard, clumped boba 

i hate this place.

Fast service even with only one employee working. Unfortunately really small so... If it's packed, it'll take awhile till you get your drink! 

Boba was a little too squishy for my taste. Otherwise, it was satisfactory.

Berkeley boba in general is CRAP. Quickly's isn't an exception with its pre-made powdered drinks and hard boba. I would suggest just getting regular tea w/ NO milk or boba. I guess their chicken isn't bad if you want a quick and relatively cheap lunch.

Quickly's ridiculously cheap jasmine milk tea kept me coming here a few times a month for the sugar boost I needed to make it through my accounting lectures.  Too bad the all of the other Quicklys charge more for the same drink.

$1.95 for a milk tea with pearls. That is tears of joy to my eyes coming from Austin, where boba with pearls at the minimum is $3.75. Service was fast today and the lady was nice. Like other places in the ghetto it seems to be cash only.

The tea was pretty decent, though I've had better. My boba was a bit too soft, but at $1.95 at more or less equivalent quality to what I'm used to, that's pretty awesome by my standards. Though I give this place a 3, as I'm sure in the area, there must be better.

I prefer Quickly, over all its neighboring joints, for a decent, strong servings of pearl milk tea. Their teas are always strong, fresh and never disappoint me. Pearls, however, are a little lackluster in terms of texture; they can be a bit harder than other places like sweethearts. But I still prefer their pearls because they are not sweetened. 

I like the fact they have a wide selection of pearls, jellies, grains to add to your drinks. Personally, I prefer their lychee jellies and barley in mine. I recently became addicted to Jasmine Green Tea (w/o milk) with Barley, after a friend of mine recommended it to me. I can't go back!! It is a little unusual but I think the combination is delicious, especially the paired with the creamy barley flakes. It's also probably a lot healthier than the jellies and pearls.

Their food/snacks are not up to par with their drinks though. I find their popcorn chicken to be more like strips of chicken, chewy and thick; and the calamari popcorns are overprices. However, I have wanted to try their french toast strips for awhile...so we'll see. 

Overall, this is my go-to place for asian drinks and be adventurous with your drinks!

I grew up in an Asian neighborhood so I do not ever ever expect any sort of courtesy or politeness from a boba joint. However, this place took rudeness to another level. In addition, the place is a dump and it's dirty as hell. O, have you have noticed the owner of the store is too cheap for air-con so I feel like I am in a sauna whenever I go in to place an order for my drink?

Onto the drink. It's like powder flavors with water and corn syrup. Straight up nasty crap! The boba/pearl, mega ew.

I only went there once and it was enough for a lifetime. I don't care how long time line is at Lotus House, I am going there for their delicious boba.

Whaaaa? 2.5 STARS? Seriously yelpers? 

It was a cold, rainy day when boyfriend and I stopped here to grab something hot before heading to the Spice of Life festival. It was a bit empty but at least it was warmer than outside. The guy who made our drink was extremely nice when we ordered our hot milk tea with boba. He asked if we would be alright waiting 2-3 minutes for our drink. I was thinking, "Uh ok..." but he made it right away. The bathroom was clean, typical for any Quickly. 

As for the drink. Man oh man. I would come here everyday if I could. It was piping hot and delicious. I don't know what they put in that, but it was soooooo good. The boba was delicious too. Although, I do wish there was a bit more boba in the drink I am satisfied! 

5 stars from me! woot!
cheap and good. try their fried squid and thai tea

Got the red bean slush today and thought it was pretty good. A bit pricey for sure at $3.25 but I guess it's to be expected if you're not in Taiwan. 

Service was definitely slow with only a single person working at the store, but I got my drink in less than 10 min so I was happy enough

contrary to most people,( I see people with boba from sweethearts more than quickly) I like this place the most.
I'm particular about the milk tea as well as boba, and I think Quickly has the best balance. I would like to place Sweetheart's boba into the tea, but Quickly's boba is normally just a good and more chewy and not sweet ( I don't like it sweet, which is what most places have...)

2.18.08: MUSHY PEARL ALERT, MINUS 1 STAR!

the pearls are nice and chewy and there are always 99 cent specials =]
the jasmine milk green special is absolutely perfect. not too sweet, not too watery...
the taro is pretty good too.
service is usually lightning fast. nowhere to sit though.

The service is quick and the location is high traffic, but the drinks here just don't quite cut it. 

Both the milk tea with tapioca and taro with egg pudding we picked up most recently tasted watered down. I guess this could be considered a good thing cause there's way too much sugar to begin with, but it didn't quite satisfy a boba craving and now I'll just have to go get another elsewhere, soon.

This place is decent, there are better boba places.

I'm not a student of Cal but I certainly come by often, over my spring and summer breaks to visit my friends who are students or supporters of this area. I have not tried the specials, but they seem pretty reasonable seeing as boba (or pearl as it is referred to in other places) are steep in prices (talk about inflation).

Well in anycase, this is one of the many places to get your fill in the infamous "Asian Ghetto of Berkeley."

Cheers with a Thai Tea on hand, nontheless!

Their Boba is OK ... but they are out of supply, or some other lame excuse for a lot of the menu. 
The staff there are some of the most unfriendly boba beings that I've seen even compared to others - and most other boba places are ran by Asian people who don't really give rat's a$$ about customer service. 
Judging for the boba alone, I'd give 3 or maybe 4 stars... 
but service takes one star away, 
and their frequent lame excuses for 'out of stock' or 'kitchen's closed' etc takes another star off

cheap yes, but the product isnt that good
id rather go to sweethearts round the corner
also, quickly raised prices, def not worth it

While I lived in Fremont, everyone went to Tapioca Express instead of Quickly's because everyone we knew worked at TapEx. After moving to Berkeley, I found that nobody goes to Tapioca Express and that Quickly's contender is with Sweethart. Here's the thing. This Berkeley branch of Quickly's is better than the Berkeley branch of Sweetheart in quality, but not in price. Both are pretty damn cheap for drinks, but a few cents matters a lot to college students.

Other than coffee, tea, tapioca, slushies, and other drinks... They sell little snacks like fried cheese sticks and fried baby octopus too.

I think only a maximum of 5 people standing can fit in the area in front of the counter. This is seriously a grab and go place, unlike other Quickly cafes where you can sit and hang out.

I hate this place. Their boba tastes bad, their drinks are powdery and bad. Sure, they might have some of the cheapest boba drinks in town, but that doesn't mean it won't cost you. Spend that ~70 cents toward much better boba at any of the other places on the same block.

Relatively speaking, Quickly's is my favorite boba spot compared to Sweetheart and Mocaccino Cafe. Then again, I do think that I have to give Sweetheart another try because I judged it since I didn't get any special impression the first time I tried its boba (hot taro milk tea w/pearls). Mocaccino flat-out disappointed me with its super-sweet rose milk tea (but I will be going back to try the bento boxes) that I had to toss after sipping through half of it - and that was only so that I could get the pearls. The milk tea was terrible, in my opinion. 

My default boba drink is almond milk tea w/pearls. I've also tried the peach snow and hot regular milk tea, both with large pearls. Now I realize that I need to get a bit more adventurous because so far, Quickly's hasn't let me down. The peach snow is super delicious and the milk teas perfectly sweet and milky. The pearls aren't anything incredible, just average. Good enough for me at least. I think I'll start doing more interesting mixes, like jasmine milk tea and small pearls or mango snow and mango star jelly. I would appreciate if anyone out there had any cool mix suggestions! 

For me personally, the popcorn chicken was okay... but I prefer Cha for Tea's crispy chicken. Unfortunately, Cha for Tea seems to only be in Southern California (where I'm from) and not up here. The popcorn chicken was oily and made me feel way more unhealthy than I wanted to feel; gripping a plastic boba cup alone can be shameful sometimes. Only sometimes, though. Maybe I need to try popcorn chicken with milk tea. The saltiness did make me crave a complementary sweet beverage, but I don't think I'll be trying it out anytime soon... I couldn't finish the chicken. However, many people seem to love the popcorn chicken so don't let my first-time experience prevent you, fellow reader [who might not have tried the popcorn chicken], from giving it a shot. 

Overall, I'm decently content with Quickly's. Out of all my experiences with this place, I've only had one drink that I didn't really like one specific evening: almond milk tea because it had several tiny, weird powdery chunks in it. Kind of ruined the drink for me... but I still finished it HAHA.

I went here with my roommate last month and they ran out of boba. I'll repeat that. They said, "we don't have any boba." How can a boba tea place run out of boba? That's like Mrs. Field's saying, "we ran out of cookies" or Macy's putting up a sign with the words, "we ran out of clothes." My roommate was upset, but I wasn't, since I'm not a fan of boba anyways and just got their "Bubble" Milk Tea for 59 cents. If anyone else here does that, note how the surly cashier girl sours up when you say you want JUST that and nothing else.

The line gets pretty long during dinner hours, but there's a plasma TV there that shows a video of a guy buying a drink for his ladyfriend, but forgets the bouquet of flowers, which the Quickly girl runs after him for. I can recite this from memory because the video just keeps looping again and again and again and again and again while you wait. Pretty entertaining after awhile actually. Watch it, buy the 59 cent tea, and you've got a steal.

It's only a few minutes away from campus, so it's pretty convenient. Good for a cheap boba fix (if you're boring like me and only ever get their jasmine or plain milk tea, both of which cost at least a dollar less than the other flavors). 

Rush hours are usually around lunch and dinner. The wait can get pretty long around then, but they're right there if you're really jonesin' for a boba to go with your Asian Ghetto meal. And college students can be pretty patient when they're too lazy to walk the few steps over to Sweetheart's (right next to the Asian Ghetto entrance).
If you're running a boba place you probably shouldn't run out of tapioca pearls of any kind. Sure, I had the small pearls because I really wanted pearls, but I still wasn't happy.

I love Quickly and I've been to other locations, and it's been good. No worries, just basic quick fast food and decent boba tea. So today I got a taro smoothie and the boba was somehow scalded... it tasted like burned marshmallows, really foul actually. I've probably had boba 100 times in my life and never experienced anything like that. It seems like a fluke, so I'll likely give them another chance... but... uck. I would have returned it but was a block away and in a hurry before I bit into one. Nasty.

Sure, to satisfy that unquenchable need for boba I'll come here, but it's far from the best. I had the traditional milk tea boba. Nothing notable about the boba, except that they didn't have mini boba :( and the milk tea's flavor was nowhere near as strong or tasty as it needs to be.

This place is alright nothing special. You pretty much pay for what you get. The price is cheap about $2...tapioca is very sparse!

I tried the popcorn chicken and about 75% of the chicken was raw on the inside, which was seriously irritating because by the time I figured out that the chicken was raw I was already back on campus and did not have time to go back or find other food. 

Lesson learned don't go to a boba shop for fried food :(

Yes, this place isn't as great as other boba places in Berkeley, but it's not terrible either.

They have baby boba!! and prices are cheap for your standard drink.

I really like the popcorn chicken here though. Always juicy and crispy.. their other snacks aren't as awesome though.

When I first moved to the Berkeley area, milk tea was only FIFTY CENTS here.  Because of this, I turned my nose to the slightly disgusting interior of this literal HOLE IN THE WALL branch of quicklys. But over the few years I've lived here, the milk tea has gone up to roughly $1 but I'm still slightly grossed out by the store. I guess doubling the price of milk tea wasn't enough to renovate the store into a more sanitary condition. 

Milk tea is standard. 
Popcorn chicken is good. 
Store looks dirty. 
Cash Only.

I have to say that this place is absolutely DISGUSTING. 
The store is not even store; it's the size of a closet or storage room. And to make matters even worse, the sanitation standards are sub par with spiderwebs lining the corners of the wall.  

Aesthetics aside, the line is ridiculous considering there is only one person working there at a time.  The limited service available is terrible.  I came with my parents on Cal Day and the 3 of us all ordered different drinks.  The result was 3 of the same drink.  If the employee was going to give us the exact same order, I would expect my drinks to come out faster but the wait was unreasonably long given that all she had to do was duplicate one order thrice.  

Fine, price was reasonable but so are all the other Quickly's in the Bay Area and at least there's good quality and service at other places.

As disappointed and disgusted as I am with this pearl tea place, it's the only one I know of in Berkeley so far so I'll either have to deal with it or  abstain from my PMTs for the next 4 years. =[

I didn't mind this Quickly.  I just didn't like the fact that it was so small.  No where to sit and enjoy my drink.  But service was really fast.  I didn't feel that it was very dirty like other Yelpers.  Berkeley in general is a very organic town and not upscale like the city.  So I'm confused by other reviews.  Anyways, my drink was good came out to $2.18 for a regular taro milk tea with boba.

Damn, this Quicklys sucks! I felt so bad for the sole girl who was working. Seems like she just couldn't do anything right! She was working on a second batch of some sort of fried snacks for these guys cuz the first one sucked! After handing the second batch to them, the guy goes up to her and says "yea, I'm leaving but next time leave it in longer!" haha..sucks for her. Then we got our drinks, two almond milk teas with boba (my fav) but after the first sip..SO BAD! No ice in the drink and it was barely cold. You can taste the powder mix, the boba was too sticky, it was just a total mess. I didn't think milk tea could be bad but this was very bad. I would never come back here again..what a waste of my money! I could've used that for Tapioca Express or a much better Quicklys..or perhaps froyo from Yogurt Harmony on Shattuck!

Cheap boba, but I'm not thrilled with the quality of the boba.  Most of the time, the boba is too tough; sometimes the boba is better but it's still not throughly chewy to the center.

I actually like coming here for the crispy chicken instead of boba (yep, one of my guilty pleasures)  They used to give you only a couple small pieces in a small bag but now, they fry larger pieces and use a slightly larger bag.  I like to double coat my chicken with the spicy powder condiment to get it UBER spicy (the spicier it is, the less my gf will want to eat my food teehee!)

Anyways, yea come for a quick boba fix but don't expect greatness

The girl who works there isn't that friendly. I enjoyed my drink but for future reference all advertisement is for no boba only. Tacked on almost a dollar for boba. 

Really tiny space. It got crowded with only me and another customer waiting for our drinks.

This is my GO-TO boba shop. I've had four years of boba tasting and this place is consistent, which is one of the main reasons why i choose this place over Sweethearts. 

I'll pay the extra 25 cent! Just judging on plain milk tea, or plain jasmine tea or what ever the general public orders, their milk tea is delicious. 

Definitely take a walk on the wild side and order your drinks with Jellies! Lychee is a good one. 

Complaint: SMALLEST SPACE EVER. I find myself in this narrow corner or outside. 

Service is good too, I don't get much judgmental looks--especially when they've seen me 3 days in a row

Aside from horrible service, the lack of sanitation, and stacked upon supplies in the middle of the establishment, this place has the second best place I've had peach green tea.

And why were the lights off when we went in? The folks working there were more interested in playing with their PSPs than helping out.

It is great to come in here and get a milk-tea while I am waiting for my food at thai basil or vietnam village. The workers are always friendly and service is hella fast. The tea is powdered but good for the price. The boba are average but acceptable. The squid is good too.

Fried mini octopus.  If that doesn't do it for you straight away, no amount of booty-licious, bible-thumping, banana-peeling excitement will get you aroused.

It has boba, little snacky things asian style like fried fish balls, fried popcorn chicken, things that normal asian teens take for granted in their country but can go terribly wrong when in the hands of americans.  

Everything is take out, there is no seating.  

The minute you order, this really really FOBy guy fires up the fryalator and dumps an order of mini octopus to be fried.  The batter is amazing.  And the spicy powder that they have to sprinkle on top of the order is amazingly flavorful.  You are required to eat it with long skewers that act like a one pronged fork.  It was good.  I burnt the roof of my mouth chewing.  And you know what?  I'll do it again.  

This from the girl who just yesterday, swore off seafood for fear of water pollution and high cholesterol.  I'm going to enjoy every moment of this artery clogging death.  As long as I can have my fried mini octopus.  Next time, I'm all about the fried chicken.  I needs me some fried chicks.
I don't care if the tapioca drinks here cost a penny, this is the worst crap I have ever had.  How does this place even survive with Sweetheart's right next door?  A true and utter travesty.

I also like the half-half option (I get half boba half pudding). This place isn't the cleanest but it's average for an asian food store. I really like the drinks here; the milk teas are strong in flavor and it's a good deal.

This was the place that first introduced me to boba and milk tea, and I love their selection of different bobas and jellies and puddings that you can add in, definitely a perk of coming to quickly.  I also love their popcorn chicken because they add basil and some pepper into it...so bomb!  Especially if you add some additional red cayenne pepper, or the other pepper powder to make it spicier and more flavored.  Their taro milk tea is better than any other taro milk tea in the area!

So, back when i was going to HS in SF, i would always go to the Quckly on Clement for a watermelon slush with large tapioca.  It was good, damn good, and expensive too (that quickly covered up all of the original prices and added a dollar to everything). It was worth it tho.  

So, i go here and get a watermelon slush with large tapioca (because, henceforth, all quickly shall be judged by this standard), and i can honestly say, i was surprised at its suckyness...

First of all, there were large chunks of ice in it (nothing like the nice smooth consistency of the SF one), and it was almost brown because they there was so much liquid from the tapioca that it obscured the watermelonness...

I think I frequent this boba shop so often that almost all the employees recognize me now.. I always order the usual - on a cold day, I'd get a hot bubble milk tea with large tapioca, and on a hot day - bubble milk tea with large tapioca. 

Yeah, I know, I'm boring for always ordering the same menu items. But I think this might originate from my fear or trying anything new and always liking familiar things (but why would I like to try new restaurants then?) 

Their popcorn chicken is almost always delicious, and the boba is cheap and quick and it always hits the spot. The employees are MUCH NICER THAN SWEETHEART'S EMPLOYEES. I almost never have a problem with having drinks taste too diluted or sweet.

I love boba and Quickly's is my go-to place when I'm around the UC Campus!

Uh...gross.  This one by far was the wosre one I have ever been to.  And it looks gross inside...flies flying all over the place.  What the heck... =x  Drink nuthin to rave about...and no boba available.  Boo on you guys!
Can get busy at times because there is only one worker. Their drinks seem powdery to me but maybe it just me and the drink was too sweet for me.

I ordered a Taro Milk Tea here with QQ pearls (QQ pearls remind me of home....and Verde!) came out to be $2.18 which is pretty cheap in my opinion. And the service was fast. Because I was the only person in line. LOL

+ 1 star: wide variety of flavors to choose from
+ 1 star: cheap specials [prices range from .59-.99 - costs extra with boba]


- 1 star: slow service. sometimes theirs only one person taking orders and making drinks and the line is out the door
- 1 star: very small. get your drink and go kind of place. no chairs inside.
- 1 star: lacks cleanliness

----

5 stars: i am a loyal customer and cannot live without this place/restaurant!

4 stars: consistently great food. a place i would definitely frequent if i dont already.

3 stars: good food. id come back for more if a particular craving for something specific they offer hit me. 

2 stars: for the sheer reason of convenience and semi mediocre food [but convenience being the majority of reason] id come back.

1 star: id never be caught dead in the place ever ever again.

I always stop by this place when I visit Cal for work. I love the prices.... basic drinks always seem to be on special for $1.50 or so, and the variety. You can have pretty much any flavor or add-ins (jelly, boba, pudding, barley) your heart desires. Sure, it's TINY, almost a literal hole in the wall, and not the BEST boba ever, but I love the variety and prices. Definitely worth stopping by!

Customer service is at the bottom of their priority.
To be frank, they were rude.  Here is a story:

I order my drink and the cashier looks at me with the eyes of the devil that said, "WHAT DO YOU WANT?!"  I ordered a drink and handed them my money.  I feel like being unfriendly is a prerequisite to work at Quickly, that and speaking Taiwanese.  

I stepped outside with my drink and shook it to mix the pearls.  The cup slipped out of my hands and exploded on the ground, to the amusement of my friends and strangers around me.  I picked up my damaged plastic cup and walked back into the store with a sad expression on my face... before I can say anything the cashier shouted, "NO REFUNDS!" 

Thanks for the sympathy.  I know it was my fault, but the cashier was excessively harsh.  I don't care that your drinks are 47cents, my heart was crushed and you were so rude.  

Never again.

Quickly as a whole is like Chinese Starbucks taking over all the boba nai cha places.  But I've been gracious here: their milk tea isn't bad, neither is their popcorn chicken.  But this particular location, especially right next to campus has TERRIBLE service.  This is a very small Quickly, more like a stand with a bit of standing room.

First, their huge screen blasting Mando-pop is right behind the counter, above the head of whoever's manning the counter.  It's so freaking loud that the girl misheard my order.  I wanted "popcorn chicken."  She thought I said "poppers."  She took the poppers (already pre-made) and heated them up.  I looked at it, and said "This isn't what I ordered.  She wouldn't exchange it for my popcorn chicken, even though ALL SHE DID WAS HEAT UP THE POPPERS.  Fine, so I thought, maybe I'll try them.  I'm not one of those customers who makes a big deal out of every little thing.  I decided (bad decision) not to make a fuss or ask for the manager.  So I asked her what was in them.  SHE DIDN'T FREAKING KNOW.  It's a given that if you work at Quickly, you should know all about the drinks and snacks you sell, or rather, heat up.  I wanted to see the manager, but decided to give the dubious looking "poppers" a try.

Poppers?  They're not on the menu any more.  Want to know why? They're PICKLES AND CHEESE fried together in batter. Disgusting.

The one star is for the juice specials of the day, and the popcorn chicken that'll work in a fix.  But there are so many other places that have better popcorn chicken: Old Teahouse (which is gone now), Sweetheart Cafe, even Tapioca Express.

I stopped going here because the texture of the tapioca in their milk tea is not unlike that of little rocks.

Sweetheart Cafe is ten seconds away. Save yourself the walk into this one.

As much as people bad mouths this place, really....for less than a buck you get any standard milk tea boba.  Where else do you get that?  I really miss this place since I always just get the milk tea with no boba and it was less than 70 cents.  *sigh*

*edit 03/31/07*
I went here yesterday and it was like someone slapped me in the face.  I arrived in Berkeley hoping to finally get boba.  *note* I have been craving boba for 2 days before now and first I substituted it for Coldstone since San Ramon has no great boba place and I just couldn't have mediocre boba.  Then I went to Green Tea Cafe in Walnut Creek and they just closed so they had no boba left. Well at Quickly I was jumping up and down.  I went in, I said can I get a Jasmine Milk Green Tea.  I payed my $1.08...wait...that's more than it was before....and finally got my drink and it was sooooo not Jasmine Milk Green Tea.  It was normal milk tea and...*gasp* NO BOBA.  I was walking and drinking it since I ordered it anyways, but I was so disheartened that I 1/4 into the drink i couldn't do it anymore.  It was like a pity drink to the milk tea.  I ended up throwing it away cause I just was that disappointed.  Quickly...was quick....quick to fail.

Asian (presumably Chinese) guy is on his way to meet a cute Asian girl (presumably Chinese as well). Who is also presumably his girlfriend. Presumably. He buys flowers for her. But he is late! OH NOES. What will he do?! Buy boba at Quickly's of course! Meanwhile, we are treated to a shot of the girl, standing alone in a busy area, staring at who-knows-what in the sky and waiting for her boyfriend (again, presumably). Cut back to the guy. Who has left his flowers on the countertop at Quicklys! NIUUUUUUUU! The guy meets the girl and gives her the drink while acting all apologetic. But it isn't enough! *GASP* In comes the worker at Quicklys to save the day! HOORAY! Now freshly armed with the flowers, he gives it to the girl who now is full of joy and fuzziness. Crisis averted. PHEW. Good work, soldier.

Dangerously cheesy commercial that once was looped endlessly on the TV at the front door of Quickly's aside, I would say after my entire undergraduate experience at Berkeley, Quickly does boba the worst. The boba is almost always too hard in the center and the milk tea tastes like over creamed sugar water. Do not want. I don't know how the girl in the commercial was so happy. What was the guy THINKING?! He could of gone to Sweethearts next door! I would be pretty pissed if I was that girl. Hmph.

The place itself is tiny and has barely enough space to squeeze in, get your order in, and get your drink. Which I don't suggest you doing. Spend a little more and go to Sweethearts right around the corner. Please. For the both of us. And for the dude doomed to his fate of forgetting his flowers and getting subpar boba over and over again. He needs as much help as he can get.

Most people that come to Asian ghetto for boba fall into two camps: the Quickly die-hards and the Sweetheart lovers. What can I say? I'm definitely the latter.

Between the two stores, both Quickly & Sweetheart have similar speediness; I've been to both a few times and never really noticed much difference in terms of how quickly (haha, get it?) you receive your drink.

Quickly is smaller than Sweetheart, so it might be better for a pick-up-and-go trip. I also feel that Quickly has a wider selection of drink options (but correct me if I'm wrong) and I give them points for their super cute mechanical cat tip machine!

However, based on my experience today, I think I'm heading back to Sweetheart. Don't get me wrong- the service at both places is stellar. But the drinks...?

At Quickly, the drinks are less sweet. I ordered the Green Apple Green Tea today and was SUPER disappointed! It was very sour and bitter and had a very artificial-infused kind of taste. Not good at all! ):

Tiny? Dirty? Stuffy? Mmm, reminds me of Taiwan.

Actually, it's not as dirty as most reviewers say it is. Or maybe it's because I don't pay much attention/give a crap. The service is pretty quick. Order a boba tea, and three minutes later, boom! there's your cup. The boba tea needs work - boba were either gooey, falling apart or stiff. I usually go to Sweetheart Café for better quality drinks.

Don't count on lingering inside the place - it's obviously not made for sit-ins. It's second only to the City's Café Dolci for the "smallest cafe/fast food place" award.

Alright, I admit, I gave this place an extra star because they make fried octopus well, and is the only place that has it. Prices has gone up since I first came to Berkeley however. At the time of writing, the octopus goes for $4.95, which is the same price as a bento box at Café Moccacino. Go figure.

The boba specials are neck-to-neck with Sweetheart's deals. But Sweetheart's drinks are better, so... sorry Quickly. If it weren't for your crunchy yummy octopus, I would have never thought of you.

I have no idea why this place is called Quickly because the service is ridiculously slow. Also, seeing as this place is a chain, I sincerely hope that the other branches pay more attention to sanitation. 

Food: This milk tea and snack shop has some major cleanliness issues, but at least the food tastes good. The almond and peach milk teas were both delicious (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/H7K1YI4ECl8oIY3Zt8qEsg?select=kVqLFumeWRtxyKIUsyZUAg). I didn't really think they were watered down at all, but I was also ridiculously thirsty at the time. I also had some of the fried octopus (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/H7K1YI4ECl8oIY3Zt8qEsg?select=z1llwA319VMmcD5Fv8yxRQ). It was crunchy, but a little overfried. You can sprinkle a bunch of spicy seasoning over the snacks if you need an extra kick, but be forewarned. The containers holding the spices look like they've been dropped in a toilet. 

Atmosphere: This place is absolutely disgusting. First off, the area customers can occupy is only about 4 x 3 feet. Is that even legal??? The counter is gross as is the kitchen which would have been completely visible from the register if not for the dim lighting. Moreover, the seating area outside in the Asian ghetto is freaking nasty. I was constantly batting away flies and had to watch where I was sitting because of all the bird crap on the table. 

Service: Though we had a large party, I don't think this justified the long wait time for our drinks. The octopus came much later, but at least we were warned about that. 

Synopsis: I'd probably never again buy boba here and consume it in the vicinity of the restaurant. Ignorance is bliss in this case...

1 point deduction for the line always being long. 
Food is good, boba is chewy and the drink taste like heaven!

Zero, zip, nada for Quickly.  It is the worst boba place ever.  
*My "avocado snow" should have been named just "snow."  No avocado taste AT ALL.  It was all ice.  You know it's bad when you burp, and there is no avocado aftertaste.  OHHH...it was hella expensive too, $3.99 not including tax.
*My sister got a taro boba.  It was cheap, 99cents, so she can't complain.  But, when she finished her drink, there was a big chuck of jelly, about 1in.x1in. left uncut in her drink.
*My poor cousin got a durian (yup, we are so damn Vietnamese).  It was also $3.99.  Tasteless just like mine.  In fact, she said "they should call this place 'quicky' cuz they barely put anything in their drinks, just like a 'quicky'...haha...get it?!" Okay, it was a lame joke, but really, it was really really bad.  
In summary, we, Vietnamese know our durian and avocado drinks, so just trust us, they are REALLY BAD here.  Take your money to that other place near the donut place.

What?! I can't give no stars?!  Okay, I guess I have to give it one star, but just because I was so lucky to find parking on the first try.

wow. please avoid this place.

it's that damn sign that says $0.59 milk tea - it draws you in! but don't get fooled, it's 59 cents for a reason.  you get your choice of either milk tea or green tea. HELL-UV watered down, both kinds.

i was desparate for boba and was wandering by the asian ghetto so i decided to go for it - such a big mistake.  first of all, is it just me or does it always seem like there's only one person working there? and that they look completely miserable?  i ordered a "green tea milk tea" but ended up getting a green tea and a milk tea. so then i walk out with one drink in either hand thinking, what am i gonna do about this.....

i tried the milk tea first, so watered down! i ended up needing the regular green tea to get the gross taste of the milk tea out of my mouth.

don't be fooled!

Scenario: Freshman comes to Cal. Freshman has no Asian friends back home and has never tried boba. Freshman decides to go out with his new dorm friends and experience milk tea. Freshman goes to Sweetheart's and Quickly and discovers the magic wonders of boba.

Well, that was pretty much all the white people I met in the dorms 3 years ago. Thankfully, Quickly has always been there to fulfill their boba cravings, as well as mine. 

After Verde in Cupertino an Mountain View, I think this Quickly's is probably my favorite boba place in the Bay Area. They have a massive variety of flavors, and my favorite ones are nowhere to be found at Sweethearts. Passion fruit milk tea is mindblowing, and their variety of boba, jellies, or any other non liquid addition to your milk tea is pretty vast.

Sure it's more cramped than Wheeler auditorium during a 600 person lecture, but what would making it bigger achieve? You walk in, get your boba, and you leave. It's that simple. 

Thank you, Quickly's for being able to fulfill my boba urges during my most urgent times. Sure your service sucks, but like I said, it's just milk tea.

Two words: utter crap. I've never been a fan of these cheap boba chains that serve powdered drinks. Today, after a good long 3 hrs of suffering in lectures, I was craving boba and traversed to this dear convenient Quickly to satisfy my needs. Having had a horrible experience at Sweethearts with their Strawberry Milk Tea, I thought that Quickly was the lesser evil. 

I was wrong. I ordered the Strawberry Milk Tea and it tasted like sh*t. I can describe the bastardization of this drink as either tasting like old chocolate and strawberry jam or strawberry jelly along with wood from a popsicle stick. Needless to say it was gross. The worker at Quickly probably just squirt in a pump of disgusting strawberry jam in a mix of tea and milk. The lack of boba artistry was apparent. I expect Strawberry Milk Tea to taste like a creamy strawberry Calpico. This was not the case, and in fact, I did throw away my drink and my poor meager Berkeley dollars. Never again. 

It's called Asian ghetto for a reason. I'd rather save my bucks for Alhambra's Cha for Tea which actually takes the time to craft mouthwatering drinks supplemented by sweet, chewy boba.

02.15.11

It's cheap.
It's quick.
She's efficient.
Gets the job done.

Crappiest Mexican Food I have ever had.

Im from socal, and there is some realy good mexican food as well as some bad joint. But Taqueria is terrible.
best mexican restaurant in the uc berekeley campus area. my favorite dishes are the taco salad and the veggie burrito.. plus they are cheap! :)

Where can a girl get some melted nacho cheese!? Its not that hard to make, and its dirt cheap so why isnt it anywhere to be found near campus!? Sigh.

It was stuffed pretty well.... i GUESS. But "melted cheese" aka shredded cheese that they put in the microwave that wasnt really melted ANYWAYS, just doesnt cut it for me. Also came with salsa, olives, sour cream, and I paid for extra guac for a total of 5.70ish. 

EH.

They CLOSED.
But, it was a Great place, friendly service. Big plate of nachos with beans, cheese, and salsa for about $4. I'm sure everything else is good, relatively cheaper than other places, very convenient. Too bad they're going to be gone next semester because the ASUC wants more money.

This place makes consistently good veggie burritos and vegetarian tacos. I'm actually always surprised how good it tastes for the type of place it is. Yes, it's fast food--but it's not a chain, and it's on campus, which gets a little boost to the rating. The staff are also very friendly, and they manage to chat/joke with regulars and serve food realllly quickly at the same time. Recommended if you want a little Mexican between classes.

Someone in my study group brought a burrito and a horchata drink from here yesterday, and I suddenly craved some good Mexican food. So, after group, I walked the ten feet from the SLC to Taqueria El Tacontento and took tried to buy some time to survey their menu by hiding behind the fat pole in front of the counter.  I was able to look at it for a good five seconds before the guy at the register finished helping out the customer in front of me and started to smile at me, ready to take my order.  I laughed awkwardly and tried to look at the menu a little longer so that I could make an informed decision (first impressions do matter, after all).  He just smiled and laughed at me while I stood there awkwardly trying to figure out what I wanted to get.  He was pretty cool about it-- maybe because there were no other customers there at the time, but cool nonetheless.  Fifty years later, I settled on a special plate because I really wanted some of the Mexican rice.  I got steak (SO GOOD) and an extra side of rice instead of beans since I'm not a big fan of the latter (he didn't look at me like I was weird/picky like other Mexican food places I've been to, haha).  He added some potatoes, a salad with pico de gallo, and three corn tortillas; I added a medium "orchata" and paid only about $8.50.  The "orchata" was really good, not too sweet and not too cinnamon-y.  Definitely planning to go here again.  I hope the ASUC decides to let them sign the contract after all.  :-(
Average, forgettable burrito.  Nice people though?

I love this place. The food is pretty good for the price you pay, and it's the closest "Mexican" restaurant/fast food place around Berkeley where you can get pretty authentic mexican food

I love getting the tortas and the burritos. Although it's kind of a assembly line format, I love how each bite of my burrito I can taste the sauce of the carne and they overload my burrito. In addition, the service is great. They love speaking spanish to you and the cashier is hilarious. Plus, agua fresca de toda lo que quiera. 
Downside: they dont' sell Gorditas :(

DELICIOUS!! Obviously if you come here, you're not expecting 5-star Mexican food; you're looking for something convenient (on campus) and good....Well you've found it! 

It saves so much time during M/T or Finals weeks when you want to study on campus and don't want to have to pay $15 for a bland coffee and sandwich at FreeSpeech

It's cheap! It's on campus so super convenient! They take debit card! AND their breakfast burritos are delicious! I've never had their meat, so I can't vouch for it; but their vegetarian burritos and CORN QUESADILLAS are sooo good! Salsa is also great!

Taqueria El Tacontento is cheap, yes, and it's on the Berkeley campus. That's about the beginning and the end of it. I don't know why all of these undergraduates are salivating so hard about it. The ingredients are prison-and-high-school industrial-grade quality--soggy overcooked veggies, not-too-appetizing tortillas and tacos, flavorless beans, etc. I eat there because it's cheap and I'm happy with that, but let's not get carried away.

This is like the Panda Express of Mexican food, but it definitely does the trick.  I'm a fan of the "Super Nachos" (oh yeah, very authentic sounding) as well as the numerous agua frescas.  Do you guys ever get hungry while you are writing your Yelp reviews?  I just got hungry.  Anyhow, a bit more info:

When it's open:

Expect the taqueria to be closed any time the UC Berkeley campus would be closed, such as on weekends and major holidays. 

Where to find it:
