I should mention that this place is on the UC Berkeley campus, but is open to the public.  It is not visible from the street, so look for The Bears Lair (pub) on Bancroft Ave. and behind it are take-out restaurants including El Tacontento.

Simply put, yumlicious and cheaplicious. I always have the veggie burrito, either super ($5.99, I think) or regular ($3.75), and it's one of the best I've had. This place doesn't bore me with only bean 'n' cheese veggie options, like some places--they offer sauteed veggies (usually zucchini, carrots, corn) or potatoes. I've been told their meat burritos are good, too. The main difference between a good burrito and a bad one in my book? Distinct flavors. I like that at Tacontento you can taste each individual ingredient, including the salsa... mmm.

I regret not trying this earlier! After urgings of a second friend, I finally got my ass to the on campus food court for some potato-filled Mexican food. I am a big fan of potatoes. 

The menu was really difficult to read, but there were Breakfast items, Nachos, Tacos, Burritos, Quesadillas, and Agua Frescas at least. I ordered what was labeled as the "Flour Chesse Quesadilla" (but I said "cheese" instead) as opposed to the "Corn Quesadilla." They used one tortilla with cheese, scooped on some potatoes and salsa, and then wrapped it up like a burrito.

Never had a quesadilla that way, but it was SO GOOD. Satisfying, juicy, and cheesy...and a great deal at $3. I do wish they had the option of meat--I'll have to investigate next time. My friend told me that afterwards I'd feel like I was going to have a heart attack, but honestly I felt pretty healthy. How bad can a tortilla, some cheese, some potatoes, and a bit of tomatoes be for me? 

I also tried an Agua Fresca for the first time. They had six flavors of fresh juice, including strawberry, watermelon, lemon, and cantaloupe. I got the cantaloupe ($1.25/small) and it was quite good after some ice melted and it got less sweet. I loved the bits of cantaloupe pulp, although the guy next to me in class looked at me like I was retarded ("Are you okay?" he asked) when I almost dropped the cup on myself while stubbornly attempting to suck up the pulp. 

Very much recommended for starving students!

I love the taco salad, super nachos, and super burritos! Their steak pieces are huuge! I'm more of a chicken/turkey type person but here, OH MAN... I indulge in their steak! I'm also a fan of their agua frescas, especially watermelon and mango mixed together or strawberry and watermelon!

These guys make the best tacos. This is the only place I've found where the tacos come "regular" style with rice, beans, meat, salsa, hot sauce, and chips. I get the regular steak taco with guacamole, and sometimes a special aqua fresca that's a blend of all the best flavors. SO CHEAP, so yummy, so friendly, so don't let panda express kick these guys out.

The calorie/$ ratio is quite high, and the lunch that I had yesterday was quite tasty.  I ordered the chile verde enchiladas after a long consultation with one of the guys behind the counter and was grateful for the advice.  The meal that I ate reminded me of the kind of Mexican food that used to be served around town before the foodies got involved and made everything more sophisticated and healthy.  Maybe we should bring back Casa de Eva now that Zax and Maritime and come and gone from their Telegraph location!

I had to eat here quite a bit one summer out of convenience and necessity. The taco salad is pretty good, but not much else. The horchata tastes too powdery. Like most other places, they melt your cheese with the microwave instead of baking it, but it's worse that they microwave it in a styrofoam box!! After I saw them doing that to my enchilada once, I got the taco salad from thereon out.

OH MY. Two of my friends and I would meet here at least once a week for every week the last year I attended school here. It's pretty much amazing. Well, I only get two things, but they are both AMAZING:

- steak breakfast burrito - best I have found ANYWHERE
- grilled chicken quesadilla - muy delicioso!

I tell everyone about this place because it's surprising--especially being on campus--and it's a must-try.

This place was quite terrible. Even though it may seem unfair to judge it this way since it is not korean food to begin with, the dishes are far from decent flavor-wise, although they do have large portions, the extra dollar above average (other places in the area) kind of make up for that. The bbq chicken was unpleasantly dry and actually tasted a bitter, they should try not to overcook it every single time - it was like chewing on hard pieces of pebbles.
 The beef plate was ok but the veggie portion was pretty horrid as well(kinda like fast food style) but could definitely get worse..like thai basil's never-properly-cooked broccoli. I would most likely never come back unless friends absolutely insist on eating here for whatever reason, even though half of the restaurants in asian ghetto are about just as bad if not worse.
This spot is pretty damn good, my sis and I used to eat here like 10 years ago... gotta say it's pretty damn good still. My fav is the bbq chicken with rice! Delish

If you ever attended UCB, you'll know about Steve's.  Not the best Korean BBQ but good for a student's budget, especially their bimbimbop.  Good portions.  If you eat in and run out of rice or side dishes, just ask for more.  Make sure you slather their homemade hot sauce over your dish.  M M good.
Eh.  You can do better.  You deserve better.

This place is great when you're hungry, craving korean food and on a budget. They serve up some up hefty portions of decent food for pretty cheap. Don't expect super high quality though and you won't be dissappointed. The service is limited to just the counter, but the guys that work there and the owner are super nice.

I'm not a big fan of Asian food, I must say. Whenever my friends and I go to the Asian Ghetto, they often go to Steve's while I go to Gypsy's for some Italian. I finally tried Steve's and broke my Italian at the Asian Ghetto habit. 

The food is great. I loved that there was plenty and free tea to drink, although I don't do hot tea. I love that it was quick and the portions are pretty good. Keeping in line with the spirit of the Asian Ghetto, it was more cheap food for good prices which I can definitely appreciate. I had their chicken and I love it. My friends always get it and so I had the same and was definitely not dissatisfied. There was a lot of rice, some noodles, and some kim chi so there was definitely a lot of food. 

I'm surprised that the all-Latin or Mexican staff can cook some good Korean food. They rock!
the only thing that's really korean about this place is steve, but it's cheap and pretty satisfying.

I stopped by Steve's because I needed a snack before a dinner a friend and I were going to. You know how it is. You know you're going to dinner, but you also know your friends who might be late and therefore would prolong the starvation stage. So we were in Berk and decided to buy a kalbi plate to go. It's good if you're hungry and the perfect place, because you're definitely getting your money's worth (about $8) with bean sprouts, kimchi and enough rice and kalbi for two people. Not the best flavor in the world, but if I were in college, I definitely would hit up Steve's for a quick take out.

whenever i have meat cravings, i come to this place. 
this is my favorite korean bbq place near the uc campus area. 
i loooove their side kimchi (because they've sweetened it) and bean sprouts.

we stopped in during lunch on Sunday.  I got the chicken and the wife got a dish with noodles also.  Each comes with Kim Chi, rice and some sprouts.  It was all very good,  The whole plate cost 6.99.  My kid ate that rice and chicken up.  I would recommend this place to anyone.

the beef shortribs are terrible. they have an aftertaste that is reminiscent of bad breath. the kimchi and bean sprouts are also pretty bad. however the bbq pork is ALOT better and pretty good. plus big portions

Come on. If you call yourself Steve's KOREAN Bar-B-Que, show me the Koreans. SHOW ME THE KOREANS. This place should be called Steve's Mexican Bar-B-Que because I have yet to see a Korean work at that restaurant. 

Cashier: Mexican. Cooks: Mexican. Bussers: Mexican. Food: Not very good Korean.

I'm sorry but if you're going to call yourself Steve's Korean BBQ at least have a Korean sitting in the back yeah?

Please don't take offense to my comments but all I'm trying to say is that if you go to a restaurant called Luigi's Ristorante and you see a bunch of Chinese guys running the place how authentic or good do you think the food could possibly be?

Yeah, thought so.

Aside from being really cheap, I'll pass on Steve's 

ENJOY.

I ate at Steve's BBQ weekly from 1992 to 1996

Unlike some of the youngins here, I have actually met "Steve" of Steve's  BBQ.  When I started at Cal in 1992, I discovered Steves, which operated in a much smaller space in the Durant Food Court.  I would chat with Steve during my meals and he'd always give me extra kimchi and top up my bori-cha (Korean barley tea).

I'd usually get the #1 Bul-gogi but sometimes would go for the Kal-bi or the Yakitori #5.

Been going to this place since I was a boy.  For 7 bucks they really hook you up with a lot of meat.  My only complaint is that it isn't open till 2am like top dog across the street from it.  If you want fast and cheap Korean food, this is the place.....it's sooo good I would live in North Korea for a year if someone told me I had to to eat this.

Obviously, this isn't real Korean BBQ. I heard people critiquing Steve's for that...no shizz! I'm sure Steve isn't trying to play the image either.

The most "Korean" thing about Steve's is the kimchi. It's spicy and tangy the way it's supposed to be. I'm actually surprised that Steve's of all places in Berkeley has my favorite kimchi. 

+ Quick food, bbq the way you like it
-  Hygiene is an issue here; not so clean kitchen and seating area

Munchies:
1. BBQ Chicken
     + If you dig kimchi, you can sub your bean sprouts for more kimchi
     + Hot off the grill, it's yummy
2. Spicy Vegetables
     + Veggies are spiced to a good level, sauce covers the rice

Final Call:
If I were to visit the Durant Food Court again, it'd probably be only for Steve's.

I love this place!! I would come here every time I came to berkeley. Its actually the only place I go to in the asian ghetto. The short ribs are the best here and the prices are affordable. The quantity of food they give you is amazing and the venue is pretty spacious so you would never have to worry about finding a table.

They are serving GREASY AND NOT-SPICY version of Korean food.
Good mix of american and Korean, but I prefer eating the authentic Korean food because I am a Korean.
Ehhh...their short ribs were all fat and lacked a certain flavor.
This isn't so much "Korean food" as "fuckload of grilled meat with rice and inedible kimchee". Good value for money...and that's about it. The #1 would last me two meals when I was a student.

We end up going to Steve's a couple of times every couple of years.  Objectively, I should probably give it two stars, but hey, I go back there, don't I?

I usually order the bibimbap or the grilled chicken.  Prices are fair, especially for the portions.  They give you a lot of food, although a lot amount of the quantity is rice.  Spices and sauces a generous enough to last the whole dish, and the sides of sprouts and kimchi are ok-ish.  I guess I just like that this place has absolutely no pretensions.  You pay, they cook, you eat.  

Interiors are pretty much from the discount section at home depot.  The best things about the atmosphere  are the bbq smoke (if you're in, you're in), and the constant stream of students who make it lively.

On the down side, my biggest complaint is that they could do a much better job keeping the customer area clean, with not too much effort.  How hard would it be to have someone wipe down the tables with a hot rag every ten minutes or so?

We will be back, but not  too often.

I still haven't reviewed a bunch of Berkeley eats/places but this was on my GOTTA REVIEW list. 

I LOVE THIS PLACE but minus one star for getting more and more expensive! I remember when a bunch of the plates used be $5.49 or something. The short ribs and bbq pork are the best! I've also tried the bibimbap and MMM SO GOOD!

I'm not really a fan of kimchi (I know sad) so I tell them "No Kimchi" and they pile on tons more of those sprouts. MMM MMM! I wish they'd start serving some brown rice though because they put A LOT of white rice. You get a great ratio of meat:rice, if not more meat than rice, which is good.

I love the #4

The rising cost of beer kind of sucks.
Terrible.  Hardly any meat, too many vegetables, and no flavor.  Just disgusting and stay away.

Ok, this very modest place is located in the Asian Ghetto section of Berkeley. Its food on the cheap since its near the Cal campus. I didn't excpect real authentic food as I didn't see any Korean people in the kitchen cooking the food. I guess Steve had the day off.  

Ordered a bi bim bap with chicken for $6.99. The flavor was ok and the chicken was very well seasoned. It was actually much better than I excpected. Your order comes with a free side of kimchee. I found the kimchee to be a bit soggy and it must have been sitting a while because it was already turning limp and sour. But it was free so I can't complain, I suppose.

My boyfriend and I came here on a Friday evening hella hungry! We heard the portions were big and that we weren't gonna be able to finish them..yea right! I got the bbq pork with veggies and my boo got the shortribs! It was a pretty solid meal..I mean you really can't go wrong with bbq. Nothing too too special about this place, just a good place to eat hella meat and rice. I'd definitely come back but not until I tackle all of the other amazing looking places in the Asian Ghetto. Damn, for this square alone, I wish I went to UC Berkeley! Argh..I want an Asian Ghetto in Santa Cruz, I think it'd do well!

the food here is very tasty. i recommend the spicy pork and bbq beef short ribs. this isn't your traditional korean restaurant where you have 1-2 main dishes and like 9/10 small dishes of pickled radishes or kimichi. most dishes come with rice, kimchi, and sprouts. 

the prices are reasonable. cheap in fact. this is my favorite korean spot. i haven't found a place yet that beats their spicy pork.

If you need a Korean BBQ fixing and you're nearby the UCB campus, this is the place.  They offer you a giant plate of various grilled meats on rice served with a side of Kim Chi and some type of fermented bean spouts.  I think the BBQ is very good, sometimes a little fatty but everyone knows the fat's the good part!  

I've never tried their other items such as the bul go gi cause I'm weak when it comes to the spice.  I heard it's good.  One thing they could improve on is to give a little more rice.  There's a lot of meat, but not much rice.  The rice is cheaper than the meat.  Take out a couple pieces of meat, throw in more rice, and no one would even notice.  

I do find it funny like another reviewer how it's all Latinos working the kitchen and they can say Bul Go Gi para llevar!
Oh Steve's, the multicultural korean bbq. The only real choice to make is whether to get the beef or the ribs, because everything else doesn't even matter.
Parking can be difficult at times around this area. I usually order #1 or 2 on the menu. They also have a tasty vegi plate.

I'm going to rate this by the college student's perspective, not by the rest of the free world's.

Steve's is one of the few places in the "Asian Ghetto" that accepts credit cards, so that's always a plus if you just came up from class and don't want to walk to your ATM. The menu is pretty simple and has everything you'd expect. The food isn't all that bad; it certainly fulfills the most important requirement for college students: the most food for the least money. You'll leave with a full stomach and content taste buds.

good korean fast food.  so what if latinos cook the food..95%of CA restaurants have Latino cooks or short order cooks assisting the chef even at top restaurants in San Francisco.  Korean fast food is not rocket science.  For seven bucks, who needs to pay 2O usd...at other places for one item
I miss this place.  Steve is my homie.

For the past year I been going to this place about once every other week. I looooovveeee the bbq short ribs they got going on here! It been kinda pricey (close to 10 bucks) and the ribs got way too much fat on it, and sometime they will give me too much ribs to eat (not that I am complaining, but too much fat can give people high cholesterol). Food is simply delicious, it's bbq, what else do I want. I haven't tried  other dishes they got here, but whenever I crave short ribs I just go here!
i really like the bbq chicken :)  they give you sooo much food !

Steve's is awesome for those of us who crave home korean food, and will take anything that tastes slightly korean.  Steve's is also awesome because it's close to campus and relatively cheap.  Steve's is particularly awesome because you can ask for "a dollar extra meat" and they almost double the amount of meat that they give you.  I think you can ask for "two dollar extra meat" but i've never tried it... I don't even know how much meat that would be.

I'd recommend No. 2 the bbq pork, or the bi bim bap.  Both of these seem the most authentically korean to me.  No 3 short ribs (galbi) is also okay, but I usually find that there's not enough meat, or it's too fatty to be appetizing

The two reasons why this place deserves way less stars than I gave it are 1. the kimchi (it's not kimchi) and 2. The No 1, bbq beef (bul go gi).  They cut the meat in the wrong direction with the grain instead of against the grain so it's tough and almost not edible.  but then occasionally, as soon as you get used to the idea of having to tear to meat with your chopsticks and your teeth with force, you get the one piece that was cut correctly.  yeah. not good.
The dishes have no taste whatsoever. I only like the large quantity I get.

Steve's has always been best place I know to get generous portions of Korean BBQ at a relatively cheap price. Their meat is tasty enough but I wish they would carry a few more of the side condiments like the pickled radish or those crunchy wood fish.

I got #11, barbecue beef with vegetables (onions, broccoli, and carrots, mostly). This comes with rice, bean sprouts, and kimchi on the side. It cost $8.22 (including tax). Portions were large, but the food was bland and the ingredients didn't mesh. The kimchi was OK, definitely not too spicy for most people, while the bean sprouts weren't tasty but were still edible.

Service was quick but professional.

Even in the asian ghetto, you have better options than this.

came here after sf kollaboration! so this is a late post.

i just got something light, i think it was the chicken or pork rice plate. i had some fatty pieces, but the meat in general was tasty. we came at a late hour and it was still open. the price was okay, could be cheaper for what they offer you, but i'm glad my cal friends brought me here.

I used to eat at Steve's every week. Oh the memories of dirty gross liberal Berkeley... Hahaha spent a summer living off the "beef noodles" which was really bits of marinated beef and jap chae over rice. No I know. Although my little brother (who'll eat anything, like typical brothers do) hated it for some reason. "Rice and noodles together?!?" Yeah get over it. It's not weird. It's GOOD. So four stars for that fabulous dish, followed by a maple bar at King Pin. WHAT. I'm viciously against the no-carb trend. Besides, stupid Cal has so many hills I walked it off by the time I made it up to my physics class.

This place is obviously not that authentic but they have huge portions and are cheaper than pretty much every other Korean place nearby. I pretty much always get the Korean BBQ (short ribs, or galbi) because the price is so cheap there with an ample amount of meat. I've had friends and family get other stuff on the menu before and from what I can gather, you should just go for the BBQ.

What? Steve's Mexican BBQ?  No thank you. 

Overcooked/charred pieces of meat and the kimchi SUCKS big time.  Their bibimbap was one of the worst things i've ever had at berkeley and i think it made me sick.  Also got into a fight with a then-bf here because the food took so long and we both got annoyed so this place must really hate me.  

But I guess two stars for their ginormous portions and okay dumplings.

My all time campus fave.  When I was a student I was here all the time.  I love the option of sitting outside on the patio shared with the other little eateries.  Great budgetable student plates.  No it's not your finest korean dinner style stop but heck the price is great, they give you a great amount of food and it's quick.  The quality isn't #1 and it also isn't the worse you'll have.  Bi Bim Bop (w/beef) without the sprouts please!

Dude, it might not be high cuisine, but if you have $7 to spend and want a really filling meal with some kick, Steve's is the place to go.  Granted, the decor isn't great and some say it's not real Korean (I'm not Korean nor have I been there) but if you want a giant plate of meat, rice, and tasty bean sprout salad this is your place.  Great to sit and grade papers while munching on your lunch, just try to get a table.  It can be kind of packed during lunch hour.

Priced average with a generous serving of kimchee, sprouts, meat and rice.

My sis and I shared the short rib plate. DELICIOUS. I did happen to bite and spit out a piece of meat that was still partially frozen BUT life's not perfect. The meat was cooked perfectly. Tender and full of that korean bbq flavor. So a eensy bit of frozen meat won't kill me ( I spit it out anyways)

Sprouts delicious and kimchee, IDK because I don't care for the stuff. 

I'd love to come again next time I visit the sis at Cal. Nom nom.

The Short:
Not authentic Korean at all, unless you count Korean food as grilling meat with random marinades and serving it with poorly made kimchi. The only plus side to Steve's BBQ is their portion sizes. I'd only go here to get full off of meat and rice, but don't expect the biggest bang for you buck. Great for any Berkeley students who are looking for a lot of food to get that Freshman 15 ;)


Recommendations:
- Can't think of any.

Pros:
+ Good portions. Lots of meat and rice.

Cons:
- Not authentic Korean food.
- Prices are not too fantastic.

This place is great!  This is a very casual, cheap, good-for-students, type of place in Durant Square.  The orders have huge portions, and delicious taste.  Try the beef short ribs, and you'll know what I'm talking about.

Definitely not good for dates, or formal dinner, this is more like a mom-and-pops place, cheap and tasty =)

Taking one star away simply for its lack of ambience.
Good for hungry students. The spicy pork is my favorite. The spicy sauce is so good! Huge portions allow you to share =)

Not the most authentic...if at all. Korean food cooked by non-Koreans. Maybe the cooks specialized in Korean food....Yeaabuddy. 

Located in the Asian Ghetto, it's one of my go-to places if I just need something meaty and filling. Meat portions are typically plentiful and come with some bean sprouts and kim chi and a good amount of rice. I say typically because there's always those occasional times when I take the box out of the bag and see a scant amount of meat and I get a little bit sad. 

Prices have risen a little bit the past few years I've been here, and now it's about the standard 7-8 bucks. But at least you'll be full of good ol' protein.

I love Steve's. Of course, my review is based on when I was at Cal which was only about a year ago but I've gone back back there occasionally when I'm in the area. Their food is at a reasonable price for college students and you definitely get enough food for the price you pay. If you want to eat healthy, don't come here though. Like the name says, it's mostly bbq food so expect lots of carcinogens, oil, and all that yummy goodness entering your body. If that's not an issue though, I'd personally get the bbq chicken with glass noodles over rice. I've heard from other people that the price has gone up, so I'm not sure if it's still worth the price. If you go to Cal, you should probably at least try this place once before you graduate (or even come after becoming an alumni).

Korean food served in Spanish.

It always makes me smile for many reasons- but reasons aside I truly enjoy the food they serve. My order- Numero uno para llevar. (Number one to go) It's Korean Beef BBQ. The food is made to order, the portions are always generous, BBQ Beef with steamed rice, kimchi and bean sprouts. It's enough to fill a big eater like myself, though you can always NOW and LATER eating half now and saving some for later. It's good cold or reheated.

Steve's is a college students best friend. it's budget friendly and the location is between school and the dorms.

There is just one thing I wished to change about this place- They aren't open very late. Food like this would definitely hit the spot for those study breaks, late night cravings and post party munchies... 

Until next time

cheers!

i do love me some steve's.  cheap, quick and authentic flavors.  yes, their kimchee and side dishes are not great but not gross, but the bbq is good and authentic, trust me.  it's cheap, college food so don't expect any frills.  my bf and i have been going here for years now and have never had a bad experience.

Came here again... with my friend and since we were both hungry... we grubbed. She had BBQ chicken and I had the usual, BBQ beef. 

Food plate came out fast... we came, we ate, we conquered. 

Life is good...

I only ever really crave this place if I want cheap no-quality meat... and lots of it. Definitely not authentic Korean BBQ. 

So is it edible? Of course. However, I'd go maybe go just a few times a year at that.

Best yakidory; bit of heavy use of vinegar and pepper; however, I still love 'em.  Also, the Americanized Korean style hot sauce is great.   For UCB students, it's the best choice for Korean/Asian food.
Good food, been here a few times...

Steve's has been a part of my undergraduate career. As a freshman in Architecture studio, all of us would get the Korean BBQ and vent at the world. Fast forward 4 1/2 years we still go twice a year to reminisce the splendid food.

Though it was cheaper back then, this place brings back great flavors, smiles, and service. The guys are always kind and drama-free and they do their work to the best of their ability and I appreciate that.

Everything here is quite awesome - I was always satisfied by their meat with vegi dishes, the bean sprout and kim chi they put in every dish is always delicious and never over bearing or anything.

This place is the one-stop Korean cuisine if you're near campus and DFC is the only choice you feel comfortable with.

Had an order of Bi Bimbap (~$7): rice & raw vegetables (lettuce, carrot, cucumber, radish, and zucchini) topped with egg and Kimchi. Food was delicious, staff was quick, and the ambiance is like an oasis (metaphorically, not literally).

NOTE: The egg is prepared on a grill which is used for other orders as well; one could ask for the egg to be withheld were it to be a concern.

If you're craving quick korean bbq, Steve's is your place. Although I think the shortribs (galbi) are good, my sister and I normally order the bulgolgi because there are no bones so it's faster and easier to eat. Nothing extra fancy or gourmet, just a good place to grab some quick food with generous servings.

Word to the wise: 
1. Avoid lines and phone your to go order in.
2. It's easier to get exactly what you want when the Mexicans who normally cook are working the register instead of the Korean owners. They'll let you do things like extra sprouts or kimchi.

umm, value for money, big time. i work on "the Ave," so i find myself here pretty frequently.

OK, it barely qualifies as Korean bbq. but it''s far from bad and the prices are cheap. one time i went there and "Steve" was working. i ordered "Kalbi," and he just looked at me funny. so i said "#4," and that he seemed to understand. the Bulgogi, #1, is mediocre. the Deaji Bulgogi, #3 (i think, spicy pork), is pretty good. as is the Kalbi, #4. their veggie/meat combos are decent too, and marginally lighter than the giant plates o' rice & meat that are the backbone of the menu.

i go here not for quality, but for quantity and value. kinda grimy and greasy inside. food is hardly spectacular, but gets the job done better than some of the more expensive places i've been too. also, as an aside, seems to really do the job on those days i come into work hungover and only copious amounts of greasy meat will make me feel human again.

Not too good BBQ, but it's super close to campus. 

Love their #2 BBQ pork, you can ask for extra kimchi !!

Steve's Korean BBQ was a Cal staple for me. I don't make it back there very often. However, after visiting a couple days, I can say that not much has changed since my undergrad days. In fact, I think I recognized at least two of the people working there.

Most of the other reviews have it covered but I'll add my spin. 

Good: The portions are huge. When you are hungry, this is the place to go. They don't skimp on anything. They don't start cooking until you order. The food is served quickly. About a 5-10 minute wait.

Bad: The restaurant is always cold and you won't get that authentic feeling. Like everyone says, most of the folks that work there are Mexican and speak Spanish. 

With that, the food is good. If you are on a super budget, get the chicken over rice. It's decent. However, their best dish by far is the short rib. Get it and enjoy. It is excellent.

Parking is tight in the area so plan ahead.

No matter how much I think I'm going to order something besides the bbq short ribs, I always end up getting the short ribs!  They are so deliciously amazing in their messy goodness.  
You will not go hungry eating at Steve's.  The portions are rather incredible, many people pack the leftovers up in a to go box.  

I'll admit, I was a bit skeptical with the name "Steve's Korean Bar-B-Q".  But then on the suggestion of a friend whom I trusted, I gave it a go.  
I have actually tried all of the bbq options, pork, chicken and beef and none of them come close to the short ribs.  They are so good.  
Their spicy sauce is amazing and the kimchi (sp?) that comes with the bbq combo plate accommodates the rice and meat well.  

I have never had a problem getting a seat here.  It is reasonably clean by multi-ethnic grotto standards (that's what my friends and I call that food court!) and despite non-Koreans working behind the counter, the food is consistently solid and satisfying.
I'm not sure this is a great place for vegetarian options but fortunately there are many choices for non-meat eaters in the vicinity.  

I have eaten at most of the places in the grotto and I consistently return to Steve's.  Occasionally I'll make the mistake and think I want some chow mein.  I always end up regretting it because it's never as good as the short ribs at Steve's!!

This place isn't too bad. The first time I came here, it really messed up my stomach and I didn't plan on going back, but I gave it another shot the other day and it was much better. It is worth a shot if you get sick of going to Thai Basil. Probably wont happen for me, Thai Basil is the way to go in the Asian Ghetto, that and Gypsies.

Steve's has been a local, near-campus go-to staple throughout the semester. We always get the 32, with no egg, as we're on a special (read, *weird,* diet) and the price is great for what you get, the food is decent (fresh veggis, rice, no MSG) and the kim chi is yummy and abundant. Never felt sick after eating here, which is a huge boon for near-campus, CHEAP dining. Oh, and the staff is super-friendly.
The BBQ Short Rib plate is all ya need when you got that crave!  Nuff said.  Walk up to the fridge, grab a cold drink, order at the counter, have a seat.  And don't forget the hot sauce!

Several of my friends have gotten sick from eating the barbecue from Steve's.  It's the kind of place that you might like if you prefer quantity over quality - and there's nothing wrong with that!  But if it's just gonna make you sick then the large portions are sort of pointless.  I usually get the tofu soup from there, and I have to say, Berkel Berkel's is definitely better.  You can hardly taste anything even after you ask them to make it spicy.

I hate giving negative reviews, but i also want to be helpful for those who curious about this place.

I had Spicy Beef Soup and my wife had Bibimbap with chicken.

My soup was just okay at best. It smelled a bit like ramen, although it didn't taste anything like it. The soup was spicy but it didn't taste all that Korean. The soup just wasn't very flavorful. There was plenty of meat in the soup but it wasn't very high quality. I felt like I was just having hot spicy soup with no real flavor. 

The kimchi was really bad. Actually, let me rephrase that-- what you get is FAKE KIMCHI. They use the wrong cabbage so the texture is super gross and the taste is awful. You would have to pay me to eat it.

My wife's bibimbap wasn't great either. They gave her a lot of chicken, but they were burnt, too hard to chew, and super greasy. 

This place is NOT an authentic Korean BBQ restaurant. THe bulgogi looked a little better, but even that's cooked incorrectly. Real bulgogi is supposed to be cooked on a grill. 

Needless to say, I will not be going back to this place. I am sure its employees won't disagree too much with this review. I saw one of the cooks having lunch--- it was a wrap from a place down the block.

I give it two stars because they've been good to me in the past, but I don't even know what happened today.

I ordered veggie bi bim bop.  I knew it wasn't going to come in the stone pot, but I expected it would be...warm.  It was just a lot of cold vegetables on top of cold, clumpy rice.  I ended up buying a second dinner elsewhere... The half uncooked egg just sat there and the part of the egg white that wasn't cooked remained clear because there wasn't anything remotely hot anywhere around it to cook it.

I've enjoyed just the barbeque chicken here before, so I suppose I would suggest the bbq dishes, but I don't think I feel like going back at this point...

Korean? I don't think I've ever seen a Korean employee here.

Tons of meat with rice. No veggie. A full double meal for me. Loved this place when I was still in school.

I considered this fine dining when I was a college student.  Yes, the servers are Mexican, but who cares!  They really hook you up here with rice and meat.  This is one of my all time favorite spots in Berkeley for cheap eats.
good priced and fast service!! the clear noodles with bulgogi is good!!!

Food isnt spectacular but it outshines most places in the asian ghetto.  I always get the Short Ribs and on some occasions the BBQ chicken.  SIde of Kimchi and bean Sprouts are not good at all so you should just swap it out for extra rice.  If you were thinking of the tofu soup, it is not a good idea.  It is very watered down and lacks flavor and quality. 

Minus what they specialize in, which is the BBQ, everything else is below average.  BUT like I said earlier, it does outshine the other places in the asian ghetto

Everyone is complaining about the kimchi...i'm more about the meat.

This place is getting expensive (and they're starting to skimp on the meat)!  I remember my freshman year it was at least two dollars cheaper, but I guess everything is going up now (looks down the street at the strikers).

I like the spicy pork and even the chicken over the veggies is good.  Also, i forgot what it's called something with meat, veggies, and the glass noodles...really good, you get rice and noodles!  I don't really like the short ribs and i only see korean people actually ordering the soup dishes.  If you smile really big and ask nicely, sometimes they'll put an egg on top for free = ) (haha i'm assuming it's only for the girls)  overally, good bbq for college students

i graduated and moved to san francisco, and the other day, i came back to steve's, and man, did i miss steve's.  what's up with all these people saying you have to lower your expectation?  what's wrong with a pile of tasty tasty meat???

number 17 with beef is bomb, yo.  that's the dish you should stick with.

i wish i could give 7 stars or something.

If youre looking for good korean bbq, I'd recommend you go down telegraph more into oakland in the korean area there.  Steve's provides just the simple standard of what korean bbq is.  

The meat quality isnt the best, but it'll get by if you simply just want something a little reminiscent of korean bbq, since asian ghetto covers the other countries of asia =P  Personally, i hit this place up after a workout at the RSF for some quick protein, because they do give you alot of meat for sure, compared to all the other places in the area.

The kimchi is not too good or fresh tasting either...but youll most likely get pretty filled with everything else and wont have to resort to picking at the kimchi post-meal =P

Evan's Thoughts

All I be seein' is Korean!  For the past several days, I have been having a craving for any type of food from the continent of Asia.  And this place served me well.

Great food, good location, and not too pricey ($7.50 for the BBQ Pork).

My one bone to pick is that the pork was a little fatty.  I was easily able to pull it off though, but still.  You might say I have OCD but I actually have OLGP (On the Lookout for Good Pork).  And despite the occasional fat, this hit the spot.

My advice Berkeley student or resident, if you're in the business for good Korean BBQ I would definitely stop by.

I use to love this place 5 years ago but now the service is not good.  It should be Korean bbq but when I go there there, no body looks korean in that place.  I would say, this is South American BBQ place not Korean place.  I don't know why the owner give it to them...  They need to manage properly for this place for the cleanliness, service and food quality.  I doubted the cleanliness of the way the cook.

Their prices rose since the last time I've been there..  The food is good, and the portions are large.  It's great to share a dish with someone at times when you cannot finish it all by yourself, making it under 4 dollars a person.  

It isn't really authentic korean bbq, but oh well

korean bbq is always sooo expensive, but steve's is definitely a good deal.

i normally get the short ribs but i have definitely tried the chicken and it's pretty good. my only problem with the short ribs is there tends to be a lot of fat on them which doesn't taste so great.

otherwise, the service is fast and the jap chae is always good. whenever i go to berkeley, i always stop by to get a quick meal at steve's and save the rest for a late night snack later on.

this is really a 3.8
two meals in one... two meals in one.

about this place. Its funny I always feel like my last time eating Steve's was better then before. Its like I'm chasing that first Steve experience, and keep going back.
If i only went once i would have given it a 5

I love just drenching the boneless chicken in soy sauce and then getting after.
Great greasy hang over food, always does the trick.
just not all that specail to go above 3
actualy 3.5

two meals in one... two meals in one

Steve's BBQ is probably the best place aside from Thai Basil in the Asian Ghetto, although it is kinda EXTREMELY oily.

However, its pretty cheap and they give you ALOT. The store is bigger than most of the restaurants in this area, so its nice to sit down and enjoy your meal.

Their charbroiled meat is pretty good, as well as their grilled chicken with veggies, but their bi bim bap is not authentic at all - its not in a hot clay bowl thing and THATS NOT RIGHT! lol...at least in my book. Free tea and water - pretty standard for restaurants in the area.

Overall, good for students who want a filling and savory and cheap meal.

Cheap Korean BBQ fix on southside.  Steve's isn't really anything to get excited about, but it is perfect when you and your buddies are absolutely starving.  The shop, like the rest of Durant square, is kind of sketchy, but damn the food fills you up on a budget.  The marinade and the rice are spot on, but the cuts of meat they choose are low on quality and fatty.  Kimchi and beansprouts abound, but no suitable banchan that you would expect from a full service Korean restaurant.  Still, for cheap, filling, fastfood BBQ Steve's is a sure bet.

I went there on a Tuesday night during the summer.  The service was quick and the beef bibimbap was really good.  

The next week I went there on a Friday night.  The service was, again, quick.  However, at least 1/4 of the veggies in the chicken bibimbap were frozen!  The chicken is also dark meat.  I was sad.

I love meat and I love Steve's Korean BBQ.  If you decide to go here order the short ribs and make sure you get some sauce and you will not be dissapointed.  I went here all the time when I was an undergrad and even though I may die of a heart attack because of it, let me tell you it was definitely worth it.

Steve's has large portions and great food! They offer very quick service with great quality food. This is the kind of food that you will crave from time to time and you can get it in no time. BBQ Beef is my all time favorite and recommend anyone to try it but you can't go wrong with anything in their menu for only about $8!
I always have the short ribs or bbq beef.  Its really good, but the only reason it gets 4 stars is because its somewhat overpriced.  The kimchi is nothing special, but their meat is where it is at.

I've been here a couple times, but I've only ever gotten the soft tofu soup. Lots of food, but it's not THE Korean place for me. I've seen my friends get the BBQ beef though - wow there is a TON of meat. When a friend from another college was visiting, he mentioned how typically he has to ration his meat so that he doesn't run out of it before he finishes the rice, but for Steve's, he had to ration his RICE.
This place is great. The BBQ chicken and beef are pretty good and the quantity is stellar. Just NEVER forget to get spicy sauce with your order.

On a too-lazy-to-cook night, we strolled into college town for some cheap grub. The food itself deserves three stars since it's nothing authentic tasting, but a great value for the equivalent of two meals. From the many times I've been here, the bbq beef is pretty much the only thing I order. For ~$6, you get a huge portion of beef, rice, pickled cabbage w/cucumbers and bean sprouts. Don't be fooled to think this is even close to authentic Korean bbq or kim-chi. Stay away from the boneless bbq chicken. It looks like it's pre-cooked before it's thrown on the grill and some pieces came out black and burnt. 

Satisfied and happy with another leftover meal in hand, I was ready to leave UNTIL...I nearly stepped on a DARK GRAY RODENT camouflaged into the rubber mat at the doorway nibbling on leftover scraps!! As cute as the teeny weeny mouse was, my stomach did churn one too many times.

I love this place. It always brings back memories of my roommate and I rushing to Asian ghetto an hour and a half before Lost started to get our dinners. I know it's not authentic Korean food (in fact, I have never seen an Asian person working here in my 4 years), but I don't care. 

The greasy kalbi will forever have me smitten and my arteries clogged.

If you just want lots of food for a cheap price and fast, Steve's BBQ is perfect! You don't find a lot of places that do KBBQ to-go, Steve's BBQ has always been a favorite of mine. The meat's perfectly marinated, but the chicken can be kinda dry. Just kind of sucks finding parking, but that's just how it is when you're near Telegraph.
Unbelievable great good. The spices they use are just amazing. Try the chicken. The first place i go when i'm in town.

You can't really call this authentic Korean food. The kimchi here is made of cheap cabbage, not napa cabbage. The bean sprout salad tastes...really funky. I would say that the bbq here is okay, but in my opinion, it's like what you get at a Korean church picnic...just mediocre in taste. The kimchi stew here is okay, but you can totally taste the MSG. I gave it 3 stars because I'm a starving student at Cal, and we need cheap food like this around our campus! (Because our dining commons are just...ugh)

This might not be the best but what draws me is consistency. Not much has changed for the past 8 years, you get exactly what you expect.

Recently I've turned pseudo vegetarian, my favorite includes seafood tofu, bibimbap and the glass noodle dish.

My wife and I are both Bears and she loves this place. I think it is just okay. 

The meat is often overcooked and the kimchi is too Americanized. 

The best thing about Steves though is the quantity of food and the bang for the buck.  Great place to get enough food for dinner and lunch the next day.
Nice food.

Perfect for a quick chow-down. Order, pay, gobble, gobble, run.

Note: You will get your daily intake of sodium and then some. Drink plenty of liquids lest yer internal organs turn to dust. 

I had heaping fatty BBQ pork (bul go ki) over a sizeable mound of sticky rice. Kimchee, and sprouts. Normally I would clean the plate, but something about the kimchee caused me to leave a lot of it behind.
Spicier than most places that cater to the bland. 

Interior is pretty ugly and there is a thin layer of grime covering most surfaces. At least our table was clean. There may have been a civilization of microbes living on there, but it LOOKED clean.

If you can't find the bathroom, it's hidden behind that bulletin board thing on wheels.

The bibimbap is passable, the barbecue items are...really bad cooked meat.

I bet the recipe sheet that Steve passes on to every new cook/employee reads something like this:

1) Buy chicken from Costco.
2) Put on grill.
3) Put chicken on pre-made rice after 20 minutes.
4) Serve with soy sauce.
5) Actually, f*ck that. Make those college punks get their own soy sauce.

It's a lot of food for the price, but it's about 80% white rice. Bad white rice at that.

There really isn't good korean food in Berkeley.  However, if you're having a craving and don't have a lot of time, then this was the place to go.  Not too expensive and give decent portions.  There were always a bunch of mexicans doing the grilling and cooking and the manager (steve?) behind the register.

Anytime I want to gorge myself with piles of meat with tons of rice and sprouts (I dislike kimchi), I just go straight to this restaurant. It's definitely a very blah interior, but that's not really what people come here for. I actually only get either one of two dishes: BBQ Beef (classic) or BBQ chicken. And I never get tired of it! I also think it's adorable that they always play mariachi or something or other music every time I go there.
I got the Bi Bim Bap, which wasn't that great because it was pretty bland, no matter how much spicy sauce I put in it. The rice did not taste very good either.

this place is ok. wasn't what i expected. told by some friend that they have great korean bbq so i gave it a shot found out it was run by some mexican so i knew it wasnt going to be up to par. rice on my bi bim bap was barely warm when it was served to me. the short ribs was full of fat then meat. only great thing is that the portion size was huge, but what am i going to do if the food isnt any good.

I don't really understand how this place can even advertise itself as Korean.  Maybe the fact that it serves rice?  Regardless, if you're looking to chow down on huge portions or bbq with great prices, look no further.  This was one of my favorite places during my college years, simply because it was cheap, effective at filling me up, and not terribly unhealthy.  They offer different types of bbq including beef, chicken, mixed, etc.  Its always cooked well, never overdone, and they prep it at lightspeed in case you're rushing off to class.  If only I could solve the mystery as to why its advertised as Korean.

I generally am not a fan of the asian ghetto, but Steve delivers.
A plate costs about $7 and comes with A LOT of meat and is pretty quick.

Broke Student Tip: Order a plate, eat half the meat with all the rice... Save the rest of the meat for a second meal when you make rice @ home.

Before a Cal football game, my husband and I came here to eat.  Their serving size is huge so we split a plate of BBQ beef, rice, and kimchi.  We were full.  It's very reasonably priced for the amount of food you get.  The meat was tasty.  We were satisfied and if I'm ever in the area I'd come back.

Come hungry!

A mountain of meat.
A mountain of rice.
Very bodybuilder friendly! 
Everything tastes fresh and not too greasy.  The free tea and water are also a nice touch.  DOn't forget the red sauce!

Kimchee yummy, sprout salad delish.

It aint the ritz, but dont come to the ghetto for fancy food.   Rivaled only by meesha's in the "durant food court."

NOOOOOOOOO! NOT good at all.

I've tried the meats, soups, and other stuff they have here and I can definitely say this place values quantity over quality. I don't even know if there is any quality at all because every time I give this place another chance I end up throwing most of my food away.

People give this place a good rating because they give you a lot of meat, but the quality of the meat is grade D to F meat. The meat is sometimes crappy, full of fat, and with strangely "un-meaty" like texture that you wonder "is this really beef?". By crappy I mean tasteless and bland sometimes such that you're just chewing on a big ol' piece of meat with no flavor. What's the point of getting all this meat when it tastes bad and you end up chucking it away?

Also, the "Korean" chefs at this place don't take much care into preparing your food, it's pretty much like an assembly line. Who am I kidding, no one here deserves the title of chef. Anyways, one guy gets the meat out that was prepared already, slaps it on the grill and cooks it. They use the exact same grill every single time and clean it with a scraper which does almost nothing to past bits of food already solidified into the grill. I can't prove it, but there is a difference between food cooked with care and love and your fast food "pump and dump".

So honestly?

Lowest grade meat possible... it's a meat hell.

BBQ Short Ribs w Japchae over Rice. A lot of food for those who are hungry.

Bang for your buck for Korean food.

For those of you looking for authentic Korean food, venture elsewhere.

when i attended my cousin's college graduation last month, only then did it dawn on me that it's been 10 friggin' years since i've graduated from cal...*gasp* oh the memories...including late night runs to durant square for some of steve's short ribs!  luckily, i "have" to go back to cal every now and then for work (it's a tough job, but someone's gotta do it) and the last time i went, i made a nostalgic return to steve's...to find not one asian working in the kitchen?! (was i that drunk in college that i never noticed? j/k) decor seemed a bit different (okay, i swear it was in a different location in durant square) but the ribs were still good...even after a car ride home across the bridge.

Best mexican food i've ever had. :p

Only gets 4 stars though because of the price.
A lot of the other restaurants in the area are a lot cheaper and give you more variety of food to choose from.

Great value, decent food but meat quality is so-so. Deserves 5 stars for price (one 6$ plate will fill two large people) and for having perfect, hard to find korean rice (sticky and rounded but not as glutenous as japanese rice) but I have to downgrade to 3 because of ingrediant quality.

Sometimes this place is the only reason I head into Berkeley.  The portions are generous and the price is affordable.  The only reason for 4 stars is because of the atmosphere and the long lines. Absolutely the best place to get some cheap and delicious food. Whatever you get, add an egg to it!!!

The grilled shrimp with vegetables was alright! Can't really mess up an easy dish. As for the Spicy Beef Soup, it must have been great because the two girls that went with me completely finished it, with smiles! How often do you see skinny asian girls finish their meal. WOW, this place is a must ! Price isn't that bad either at under ten dollars a person! 

They should change the soundtrack though...How bout some genuine korean tunes instead of the mexican radio!!!! !@#$%^

Pretty average Korean BBQ.  The food is by no means bad but there's nothing really about it that makes me want to return very often.  I've never really felt that their meat was very good.  They do however give you a TON of food so, considering the makeup of their customer base (i.e. mostly college students), this place is more than adequate.  They also give you a generous pile of kimchi with whatever you order.

There's always been seating when I've gone and you get your massive portion of food very fast.  It's not my favorite restaurant in the Asian ghetto but it's not so bad now and then.

This is the place to go if you're cheap (on a student budget), are a healthy eater and like ample portions!  I'll go here several times in a month and always get the same bbq chicken plate.  The whole plate is covered in chicken and you get two kim chi side dishes along with a mountain of rice.  I can't put it any simpler than if you like lots of chicken for 7 bucks, this is your restaurant.  They should name it lots of meat for 7 bucks.

i went here on my trip to the northern cali...
u have to rate this pl for what it is.
cheap/fast/huge plates of semi- (or not-even-semi) korean food.
can't come here expecting good quality/authenic korean food.
just like u wouldn't order steak from carrows and expect morton-quality.

anyways...their flavor of meat/veggies is still yummy and that red sauce...YUM

I've read the reviews that say this is cheap, inauthentic Korean food, but what else do you think you're getting into at the Asian Ghetto (is it still called that?). If you want real Korean food, go to Korea town or... Korea. 

I love Steve's for the same reason I like that one Chinese restaurant that probably pumps their DELICIOUS food with MSG (allegedly- covering my legal bases here), and Tako Sushi- it's fast fare that is probably bad for you but hits that sweet spot on a rainy day or during the stress of finals weeks.

Their Spicy Chicken plate is amazing, I always get lots of the condiments. The portions are heavenly and I am always full after. The price is pretty stellar too, generally everything is under $10. They're also really fast so it's perfect for the post-study group walk by, etc.

Subpar food, not authentic korean whatsoever. Hefty portions though and average price. If you're looking for real korean food, go elsewhere. Scratch that, if you're looking for any food, go elsewhere. The only saving grace is that they have very quick service.

Pros:
- Quick Service
- Good Portions

Cons:
- Subpar Food
- Not Authentic
- Not Cheap

Steves is great. You get a lot of food for your money. To specify: a lot of good food for your money. My personal favorite is the bbq chicken over rice. The short ribs are good but I personally prefer no bones in these kinds of meals. Best Korean BBQ in Berkeley.
I love Steve's.  They give you enough food for 2 meals and make it fresh.  Sure, there is not a lot of ambiance, but the food quality & amount per $ is great!.

Not the best judge of Korean food but this place definitely was not too special. The food was fine, but could not really enjoy my food with the rude and annoyingly loud group next to us. I would rather pay more and go to a nicer place.
the number 31 with beef is the BEST !!! have been getting it for years !!! love it! and the kimchee is outstanding !  wish i were in Berkeley now !! (live in SF)

I used to come here when I was still in college. As other reviews said big protion, good price and quick. Do not come here if you expect good korean food. Here is a place for students. That's why now  I thougt the food is not as delicious as before, lol. I like their bbq beef ribs, spicy beef soup. Yes, I will still back sometimes.

This is the first place I ate at the day I moved into Cal (Unit 1 whoooooooo) because I was craving some Korean BBQ. Maybe I was too excited and expected too much for my first meal at Cal, but I was super disappointed because the kalbi (short ribs) didn't even taste like Korean kalbi. It wasn't marinated well so the flavor was whatever. I didn't get much meat--mostly bones--so I had a lot of leftover rice. I would not come back here for Korean BBQ. A pro about this place is the large servings... but what good do large servings have if the food doesn't taste good...
All of the bar-b-que is really good, so don't worry about which one to choose.  I usually crave the spicy pork, so MmmM.

All I gotta say is that I can't get enough of Steve's Meat!

The #4 is SOOOO good, I can't get enough of it. It really doesn't taste much different from "real" Korean Kal-Bi, so fill up here. If you were to go to those "authentic" korean restraunts, you'll probably get a quarter of the meat for double the price, and it won't taste that much better.

Just stay away from the soups and stick to Steve's Meats!

ps The rating does NOT reflect the environment of the restraunt (Mexican music in a Korean BBQ never made sense to me). I also must state that them giving free cold AND warm tea may not seem like much, but try to get that other places in the "Asian Ghetto"!
They have a ton of different meat dishes. Korean style BBQ. It gets the job done for sure. Plus, good serving sizes and you get kimchi & bean sprouts. :)

Ok...I'm updating my review for Steve's BBQ.  My homegirl got mad at me because I gave Steve's BBQ 4 stars.  Her parents own this joint, so she's making change my rating to five stars.  LOL!   I thought 4 stars was pretty money!   But, the food here is pretty dang good though!  The best place for quick on the dime Korean BBQ.  Get the BBQ chicken!!!!  Woohoo! As good as it gets!

I went here with a fellow training class classmate who was a former UCAL Berkley student and is Korean. He said he used to eat here all the time while in school.

Like others mention, the portions are huge! I mean, you'll probably gain a pound from eating all of it. Some complain about the taste, but I thought the stuff was very good. It might not be authentic Korean, but it is good enough to try at least once.

The first and last time I was here was a little less than a year ago.  Some friends and I went here for some food and there was a mouse.  It freaked us all out.  I gave this place 2 stars only because of the delicious smell.  But I'm hoping they really do not have any more rodents and maybe I'll actually give this place another try.
Love the grilled beef and grilled chicken with veggies!! Perfectly sized portions!! Enjoy the simple and casual atmosphere.  Can't complain about free Tea = D
YUM! I loveeee their bbq! sooo yummy! My must have every time I come to eat :)

YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. NOT KOREAN FOOD! Its like the chefs were given a menu and made the dishes their own. Ummmm I ordered the kimchee and tofu soup...took it home....not expecting a ton of pork bits to be floating in it. Threw it all awayyy!!!!!!!! Disappointing ...... to say the least!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

kimchee tofu soup with meat bits????? ...usually just kimchee soup over rice...the way we make it at home...growing up...ummmm and in korea. Well not here. Never going back. waste of money.

Oh yea if your looking for a korean place with an authentic korean setting also....not the place...unless you want to hear the chefs choice of music while your eating...which lets just say....sux!

The first time I went to Steve's BBQ was July 2010. I ordered the Beef Bibimbap to go and I was impressed. For $7, I had enough food for two meals and I was a happy camper. The beef was not overcooked, the veggies were fresh, but the kimchi was a bit sour...

Anyways, I went again today to get the same thing and although I wouldn't say I hated my food, it felt like a downgrade. Perhaps it was because I went after the noon rush, the rice was a bit mushy and the veggies didn't seem as good. 

For all those people that say there are no koreans working here, I found a little korean lady today working the cashier, haha. She tried to shoo me out when I tried to enter again to eat my to go food though. That was not cool, although we resolved the matter.
I can't remember exactly what I ordered, but it was a big mound of yummy food that included marinated beef and an egg. I'm not on telegraph that often, but could see myself coming back to this spot.

Do not come to Steve's Korean BBQ looking for authentic korean cuisine or bbq for that matter. Do come for flavorful, large-portioned, korean-tasting food. I've had their tofu soups and Bi-bim-bap. Both are a great for college students because they're large and great for sharing/splitting over multiple meals. Although not authentic, it still tastes ok.

I lived on Steve's in college. Waaaaaay back when Steve was still cooking, it was in the old small space next door, and before the whole food court started being called the Asian ghetto. 

I went back recently and it's still cheap, but I ain't in college no' mo' 

Oh yeah, #2 for me.

Let's get to the basics.  

Quality:  It's not bad at all.   I'm not sure what people's expectations are.  It's not authentic Korean BBQ, but its good none the less.

Price: The price has gone up since renovation, but it's still not bad.  I believe it's like $7.50 now for a plate.

Atmosphere: The area is called the Asian Ghetto and there's an apparent reason for this.  It's not bad at all. 

Overall: If you're looking for a quick place with a rice plate.  This is it.  The Asian Ghetto and its restaurants cater toward students who usually are in between classes, meeting, and busy doing something else.

Down hill slide...or very bad day?   When spending over $7 for lunch, I want some flavor AND a desire to finish (or want to take home) the entire plate...even the hot sauce did not cut it (or make it better).

Quanity or quality does not make for a good lunch.  Nuh said.

So I told my roommate that I was going to the Asian ghetto tonight, and she says, "NOOOOO!!! It's not AUTHENTIC!" and...you know, you just don't go to the Asian ghetto, or somewhere called Steve's Bar-B-Que, and you definitely do not hear music in Spanish at a Korean restaurant and expect authenticity...

But hey, if you're not expecting authenticity and just want good cheap greasy salty short ribs, then this is the place!

For someone who is hungry, this place is great.  For that they always give you tons of rice, and a good amount of chicken.  However, the chicken are usually fairly dry, and I had to add a lot of the spicy sauce to make it edible.  I do love the spicy sauce here though, enough to come in to ask for the sauce even though I order my food elsewhere in the FOB square.

Then again, the place was here for more than 10 years, they must be doing something right.  At the same time, I did sorta figure out their cooking style, which is pretty easy.  Charbroil the chicken put on rice and serve with a side of spicy sauce (which I finally figure out where to buy them, the korean market down on telegraph)  Thus, I am only giving them a lower rating for that I can make it myself and I don't like to go to restaurants to eat stuff that I can make in my kitchen easily.

Obviously, you would never confuse Steve's Korean BBQ with true Korean BBQ (not like you would come here with that expectation anyways...unless you are really deluded).  BUT, you will be hard pressed to find a better value for pretty decent Korean food than Steve's!  

Spicy pork was my slayed meat of choice, but the whole menu is pretty decent, though the chicken is sometimes a little on the dry side (I've had worse though).  Even if you aren't overly impressed with the flavor, you certainly can't argue with the generous servings they give you - talk about getting full on a budget!  Throw on the hot sauce and we're talking an oh-so-filling dining experience fast and cheap!  Just the way your kinky side likes it...

Oh Steve's BBQ...you are one of the biggest things I miss about Berkeley!

i love this place. =)

i miss berkeley.

*sigh*
Not gourmet Korean BBQ, but for the amount of food you get for the price, it's 5 stars.

Yeah, "Steve's Mexican BBQ"...that's what she said. KIDDING.

ANYWAY, the portions are monstrous. I could raise a baby tiger with Steve's BBQ if I wanted to. I always order the beef or chicken bibimbap to-go, eat 1/3 of it before I go up two pant sizes, and then dump the leftovers in a pan to make kimchi fried rice that'll easily last me another two meals.

Don't get the barbecue chicken or beef, just get the bibimbap. They're essentially the same thing, same $7ish, but the bibimbap comes with more sides+a fried egg.

p.s. Since the bibimbap's $7.06, if you hand them $10 or $20 dollar bills, they'll give you exact change (including the 94 cents); if you hand them $8, they'll just take $7 :)

One of my favorite places to eat in Berkeley!  During my poor college days, I didn't have too much money to splurge on eating out, but man, do you get your money's worth here.  For about 6 bucks, I would get a large mound of beef short rib, and an even larger mound of rice (I skipped the veggies and kimchee since I was a carnivore at the time), enough to easily last me for 2 meals.  

My then-boyfriend (now hubby) went to Davis, but whenever he visited me in Berkeley (duh, nothing to do in Davis), he always wanted to go here more than any other place in the Telegraph area.  Though we are no longer starving students, we still try to stop by here whenever we're in the Berkeley area.  

I've been to lots of korean places since (especially working in Santa Clara near the "Korean stretch" of El Camino), I still consider this one of the best places (and best values!) for Korean BBQ in the bay area.
Not real korean food. It's greasy. Fatty meats. Don't get the tofu soup.

I just ate here tonight after being hungover all day and only having eaten toast. It was late, around 9:30pm so I knew most of my options for good food were limited.

I needed carbs and meat. This is essentially what Steve's is. But it's amazing. There's a lot to be said for the huge portions, but the tastiness of the meat was what stood out for me. I had the chicken plate. It made me wish I'd discovered this place sooner. 

It's great for those who are seriously hungry but don't want to break the bank. I guess it's not authentic or anything but it tastes amazing so I'm really not going to complain

Love it, cant eat it enough...

Yeah yeah, the kim chi sucks and the sauce on the meat is heavy... but it tastes soooo good.  I get the #2- Pork bbq every time I'm by the campus at meal time.
Didn't taste much like Korean BBQ. Tastes more like sweet carne asada. It's a fast food place so I can't complain but it was still pricey. The portions are huge I'll give them that.

Cheap, quick, big-portioned Korean food.  It's really poor-quality, honestly, but it's cheap and quick and they give you a lot.  I really don't care for this place, but a lot of guys seem to like eating here.

Great for hungry students. Portions are big (lasts 3 meals). I usually get their chicken bibimbap, which is pretty good. The rice, meat and hot sauce from steve's is really yummy, however, the vegetables are bland, and the kimchi tastes a bit off. I like my kimchi tasting a bit different. Their's tastes a bit too fishy for my liking. 

There isn't that much to dislike about steve's. especially if you are hungry and need food. The people who work there are nice. It is great for indecisive people as well, considering their menu only has about 9 dishes to choose from.

FOOD:  They give you a good amount of food and they make it right in front of you.  I would definitely recommend the BBQ Pork.  Their pickled bean sprouts are yummy.

SERVICE:  Quick and cheap.

AMBIANCE:  It's kinda like a hole in the wall.

Yelp mispelled the name of this place.  It's Esteban's Korean-Style Bar-B-Que.  It is the least authentic korean food place I have ever seen and I'm not sure there was a time in it's history that a korean person touched the grill.

That said, this place rocks for college food.  $8 for enough food for 2-3 meals?  Hell yes.  The rice is usually soggy, the tea is watered down, and the meat is delicious.  It's all marinated before you get to try it and they just fry it up right before they give it to you.  The rest of it is just standard assorted veggies, bean sprouts, etc etc.  It's one of the places I blame for making me fat =[

The food is damn cheap and comes in large portions, but other than there's really no appeal here. The bi bim bap is served in a plastic kid's bowl instead of a hot stone bowl and the kim chi is fresh from the freezers Costco. The meat is a little rough, but at least they give you a lot of it. And who the hell is Steve?

Much like any other venue in the asian ghetto, unless you're a freshman at UC Berkeley, be prepared to feel really old.

Steve's ain't authentic but it sure does get the job done. Hands down the greatest thing my ex girlfriend introduced to me.  Everytime I order a plate I'll think of you!  RIP

Dont forget to give your loose change to the bums on the corner!  They need it more than you!

Huge, huge, huge, HUGE portions of food. A little pricier than other places in the Asian Ghetto. Meat quality is a little questionable (at least the chicken). I like the bean sprouts, the kim-chee not so much. If you're hungry as hell this is the place to go (especially after a gameday...go bears!!)

Steve's isn't a fancy place by any stretch of the imagination, nor would it suit your need for authentic Korean cuisine. When I'm in the neighborhood, it is one of the first places I'll consider when looking for a place to eat. You can't go wrong with the spicy pork or the short ribs. I mean if you're looking for chigae or pan-chan, you can head south on Telegraph for more authentic fare.
Meat so chewy your face will be sore for hours afterwards.  I still have a headache.

This isn't any place to die for, but there have been at least two times that I've been hungry to eat here (specifically here), and because of that, it's A-OK. The meat isn't particularly great, but for some reason, the beef + rice + bean sprouts always get me. I guess I have a sweet spot for their bean spouts. =\

Many of my East Bay friends love this little joint for cheap, filling meat.
Being a vegetarian who eats fish but doesn't like shellfish, that leaves me with three menu options:

The Bi Bim Bap- not enough rice and the fried egg was really cold!
The Tofu Stir-Fry- Yummy, but the Tofu has a funky texture.
The Veggie Noodles- Delicious!

The verdict?  Go to Steve's if you love meat, or if your friends do and you are veggie- get the noodles!

A bonus is the donut shop on the way out...I hear they will bake you a fresh tray of doughnut holes and sell the entire thing to you in 7minutes for $30 (that's 15 dozen holes!)

sorry to the owners but change your employees i just ate here i spent over 9.00 and was served flavorless very F**** grease  beef it was really bad never coming back here....I got so excited when i saw it was finished because i love korean food ... the worst meal ever u guys suck so bad

and the kimche sucked too

I've been coming here for 12+ years now, and I always leave satisfied.  The #5 BBQ Chicken comes in generous portions for a student-friendly price, and is quite tasty with their hot sauce.  The other grilled items are great too.  

I know the cooks are Mexican, but I used to regularly see Korean Steve and his Korean wife, Mrs. Steve, there as well.  Not the last few visits though.

You might not get 9 different side dishes like at some nicer Korean restaurants, but Steve's gets 4 stars for tastiness and value.

Orale vato... Velcome to la best Mex..I mean... Korean BBQ place in the Durant Food Court.

This is the trustworthy house of meat, in a sense that when you make your order you know you would be satisfied (if you are a meat lover of course) and taken care of for several meals. It looks like they took two handfuls of meat and slapped in on your plate along with two handfuls of perfectly cooked rice that you can feel steaming in yo face. 

Some places (I'm talking to you UCB Chipotle) can be stingy if you want a hardy helping of meat. These guys run a meaty fiesta down here. 

MEAT MEAT and MORE MEAT is what you can expect from this establishment. Not to mention, this place reminds me of my childhood when I used to live in the sunny streets of East LA...

The only thing missing is Bulgogi Tacos...

I'll still come here regularly, but...

I went today and got my normal special (see previous review.) Unfortunately, the boss lady was there so I took the kimchi instead of switching it for noodles.

I went outside to eat with my girlfriend. I notice that the kimchi's kind of sour, kind of weirder than it usually is. My girlfriend was in south korea for awhile, so I ask her about it... and meanwhile, this fruit fly lands on my kimchi.

"Go away, fly!" It doesn't move.
"hey! this fucker is persistent!" I poke it with my fork and it just kind of rolls over...

because it's DEAD.

That's right ladies and gentlemen, the fly lands on my kimchi and DIES. I'm not sure that this is how one lives the kimchi dream.

If you are a big meat eater you will love this place. I'm a normal American girl who tends to eat abnormally large portions of food, but at Steve's you just can't eat it all in one serving. When I was a broke college student, I would buy the Bar-b-que beef and have two big meals over 2 days ^_^. The quality has suffered a bit, but it still hits the spot and really fills you up. Plus, its open pretty late and takes card, a rarity in Berkeley. 

Its also a great first-Im kinda broke and don't really like the person-date lol, because its cheap, but when you eat in you get nice plates and tea.

Cheap Korean BBQ. My friends seem to think this place is magical, but I do not see it.

I find the food to be simply okay. It isn't too expensive though, which is a good.

With Top Dog across the street, I question why most don't simply go there.

I LOVE this place...

I'm a BERKELEY grad and I had to go to Steve's at least once a week or once every two weeks.

It's marinated barbecue beef/chicken, or pork in LARGE quantities over rice w/a touch of vegetables and a very watered down version of kimchi that tastes more like sweet/sour radish.

The food's like 6-7 bucks but feeds enough for some to last 2 meals.  For people like me..it did not...it would last one meal =)

It's located in a food court in Berkeley that houses cheap ethnic food over every nationality.  The rest of them seem very manufactured and synthetic tasting.

On the contrary, at Steves, you get pretty good fast food style korean food w/that grilled charcoal flavor.  The grilled chicken to me has the best flavor and best bang for the buck.   

It's always tough for me to roll through Durant avenue, and have to decide between Steve's Korean BBQ, Top DOG, and the now defunct..LaVAL's pizza(the best pizza in the east bay bar-none..too bad no one will be able to realize that anymore).   Sometimes I would get ALL THREE at once!  THOSE WERE THE DAYS! and DAZE....(the food coma that ensued after).

Steve's has price, quantity, flavor, bbq, and satisfaction.

If you go there, hit me up, and I'll meet cha there!  I need my Steve's fix!

NOTE:  YOu know you've gone to Berkeley too long when the homeless panhandlers who hang around Durant Square start to know you on a first name basis.   

When I was walking to Steve's w/this korean girl that I was dating who swore to me that she wanted to become a doctor SOLEY to help people in 3rd world countries...(Doesn't this sound like the worst kind of pageant answer???.couldn't POSSIBLY be for the MONEY, Notoriety, etc...THE.SAD thing is..she really thought she meant it).

Here's how you can give miss pageant answerer rose colored glass looker, a dose of reality...

While walking to Steve's..introduce yourself to Randy/Joe...the homeless guys and have them come over and give you a high five or hug (don't worry..they're pretty clean) and look at the look of horror on the face of the suburban overachiever azn girl w/3rd world pseudo-aspirations.  

She looked at me like "um...do you KNOW him?" (w/this look look of valley girl elitism).  

"yes..I know him.   By the way..you were saying about your charitable work in 3rd world countries?"   

haha...gets them everytime.

You want Korean but your friend wants Mexican?  How about Korean food cooked by Mexicans?  Steve's BBQ!

Some people complain that this place is nasty because it doesn't taste like real Korean food.  It may not be authentic but a mound of extra fatty marinated short ribs over rice next to a few bean sprouts can only be a good thing.  Yes, it's not "real" korean food.  Yes, the kalbi seems to be extra fatty (lower quality).  Yes, the bean sprouts and kimchi suck.  Does that mean I should stop coming here?  By no means.

It's one of the pricier places at the Ghetto but they give you a lot of food.  The beef short ribs, spicy pork, bbq chicken are all pretty decent and come in mediocre quality and large quantities.  Some people like the bibibop but I haven't tried it.  I have to admit that I do feel kinda of gross after eating here.  Definitely not good for your health.  Bring some floss.

Steve, Steve, your skin is dark
much more than any Kim or Park
But it's OK if your cooks aren't Asian
because on the outside I'm Korean, but inside Caucasian

OK, here's the deal, the kimchee is lacking, and the sprouts are "eh", but the meat over rice is tasty and they give you a lot!  My favorite is the Spicy Pork (#2), had the regular beef (#1) but found it lacking taste.  This place is one of those places where they may not be good at a lot of things, but the one or two things they have are solid.  

PS: they give you extra spicy sauce (koju jang...I'm sort of Korean OK!) and so mix that in and you got yourself a winner whether it's meat plate #1 or #2 :)

First off, if you're coming to this place expecting authentic Korean cuisine, don't.  Come to this place if you want carne asada + pseudo-kimchi in massive (and tasty) portions.  There's a reason I call this place Steve's Mexican BBQ.

This was pretty much my go-to spot when I was a student at Cal.  Cheap - check.  Quick - check.  Filling - check.

I've really only cared about trying two dishes here: the BBQ beef and the BBQ chicken.  Both get the job done and are usually made well.  Douse the dish in their not-hot (but delicious) sauce, mix it all together, do a little dance, and you're set.

This place is also great if you're in a hurry.  It takes about 5 minutes to have your meal in-hand after ordering, and you can pretty much watch them make your food the whole time.
