Having witnessed several of my meals being made, I can happily say that microwaving meat is not a critical step in the cooking process.  I am a simple man with simple tastes ... so thumbs up for that.

Oh, I almost awarded this place an extra star for the simple fact that the Korean cashier relays the order to the Mexican cooks in Spanish.  God, that's impressive.

"NUMERO UNO, NO KIMCHI!"

I'm surprised this place is getting some decent reviews as it was one of my least favorite spots in Durant Square.  The kimchee was pretty nasty to the point of erasing any good that could come from the rest of the food.

Pull the rip cord.

Mandarin House is right there.  Turn away from the darkness, walk towards Mandarin House.

A lunch entree and a bottle of water cost me about $10.  Portion size is decent, but don't expect authentic Korean food... if you couldn't already tell by the name.  (My coworker brought me here, otherwise I never would have tried it.) Staff is definitely not Korean here.

No traditional pan-chan --- the little appetizer dishes --- here.  Kim chee is not spicy at all.  With your entree you get a little bit of kim chee and a pan-chan-like salad made of bean sprouts and sliced cucumbers.  I'm used to getting my meat separated from the rice, but they MIX it all together here, which I found a bit odd.  

But then again, a Korean place called Steve's is odd as it is! Again, food is edible but if you're looking for real Korean food, this isn't it.

After an excruciating long day of working and STARVING in my research lab,  I like to let loose and splurge on a hefty meaty plate.  I go to Steve's!!

Don't expect to get your daily serving of veggies here cause it's non-existent!  (Even If it's a dish with veggies, there aren't much veggies)  I typically stay away from the BBQ plates (even though the store is called BBQ).  The meat in those plates are usually dry and charred.  

I'd go with the grilled meat plates with noodles.  Grilled meat is always nice and juicy.  I'm a big noodle fan.  I admit it's a little weird to have the noodle served on top of rice, but it's necessary.  The noodle and meat can get salty so the rice is the neutral supplement.  Also, the portion size is monstrous!!  Can easily be 2 meals, possibly 3 healthily portioned meals.

This is definitely my favorite place in the Asian Ghetto. I don't care what people say about the Mexicans working there. I went to a Korean place on Telegraph (Berkel Berkel) that was actually run by a Korean man and the food was terrible.

I usually order #11, the Grilled Beef with Veggies. It's $8.11 with tax and easily serves as two meals.

Well let me begin by saying that this is my first review!!! I was contemplating on which restaurant to choose for my first review...and i decided on Steve's..it really got me into Asian food..so why not.. 

The story begins back on a breezy late Saturday afternoon in 2001, a newbie, young freshman at CAL enjoying frat parties during the first week of school. Me and my high school homie decided to crash this Korean frat to try some Korean BBQ. After freeloading, i became a big fan of short ribs and BBQ beef...so we drink a whole lot and i wake up in some homie's dorm, the next morning... so then i have a choice, eat some raggedy ass dorm food or prowl around telegraph and venture out into something new, and different. 

So now the homies and I start walking down telegraph, we decide to make a left on Durant because some of them wanted top dog. Halfway down the block we come across a small, pigeon infested village of several small Asian restaurants. So we decide to check it out. Once the pigeons cleared away as we walked through the village, near the end of the village, I see the sign...Steve's Korean BBQ. So we decide to check it out. I noticed the Hispanic cooks with loud ranchero music behind the counter, How bad could it be? I decided to order the BBQ beef, it was $7 with a 32 oz drink, well within my college budget. So i get my food, right, it smells so good, a bed of white rice with a mountain of perfectly seasoned beef, with a little kimchi and bean sprouts...i had picked a bad time to learn how to use chop sticks...I threw away the chopsticks and chomped my way through the mountain of food with a fork..I love to eat...and i eat at least 3 times a day...well not with Steve's, one meal is perfect for the rest of the day..I was going to Steve's every single weekend.. 

Now I'm an LA person so every time i go to SF or somewhere in the bay area...i have to stop at Steve's...and they still have the same Hispanic cooks!!! 

its great, its cheap, its a lot of food, its simple, an easy 4.5/5 stars

I think this is more of a 3.5 star place, but I'm rounding up because of the large portions.

I almost always get the short ribs which comes out to $9 and change. They give you SO MUCH ribs, it's amazing. It comes with rice (obviously), kimchi and bean sprouts as well. There is  complimentary self serve hot tea and water too. 

I've also tried the beef plate and chicken plate. The beef is okay...portions are large, but it was a little dry. Nothing flavorful or its taste has nothing worth  mentioning. I won't get it again. The chicken was pretty good. If I feel like eating a (little) more healthy, I'd probably get chicken over short ribs.

Overall, this is my go-to place for when I want to eat MEAT. Short ribs, especially.

TIP: (relatively) clean bathroom here for customers!

I used to love Steve's as cheap and filling comfort food, but the quality has gone so downhill that I can't bring myself to go anymore (...and yet I still do, every few months or so when I've managed to forget how little I enjoyed it the last time). It was a good go-to place for me when all I wanted in the world was an enormous quantity of white rice and barbecue chicken, with some beansprouts on the side. However, my chicken has been pink the in the middle the last few times I've gone. Chicken is not supposed to be cooked to medium. People don't ask for chicken to be medium. It's wrong and it's scary. As for the quality of the meat, it was never fantastic but good enough. With the amount they gave you, there were bound to be a few bad pieces but more good than bad. I feel like the ratio has been shifting, and I've stopped coming.

Hungry for meat? This is my default stop for a good meaty meal. I get the #4 short ribs and it never fails to satisfy my craving. I rarely try the other options on the menu because this is my favorite meal in all of the Asian restaurants in the Durant Food Court. Friends of mine have tried the others and have never been disappointed.

Service is quick and efficient, they cook it right when you order. Sometimes there's a line but it's always well worth it. Lots of tables to dine in.

If you don't like the sides (beans or kimchee) you can ask them to hold it and replace it with more plain rice instead.
Huge servings.  And I mean huge.  But that's the only thing going for it.  Last time I was there involved bland meats and overcooked vegetables
Nothing special and the prices are a little bit more expensive than other places at Asian Ghetto. The portions are big, but I thought the meat was pretty bland and overcooked.

I was NOT impressed with this place! I ordered the kimchi chigae, and what I got tasted like watered down kimchi, which was then heated up. Not good AT ALL. From what I ordered, the food didn't seem to be KOREAN so it was kind of weird. However, the place has great location in the Asian Ghetto, and if you're not looking for Korean, but you're looking for FOOD, then it's AAIIIGHHT.

Oh, Steve's Mexican BBQ

Their portions are huge for a decent price, but I wish they'd get some real kimchi and toss the bland bean sprouts for some japchae. Maybe they need a real Korean working there to tell them their banchan isn't authentic?

I don't see what all the hubbub is about. This is sub par Korean BBQ, and on top of that, there isn't a Korean in sight. I don't think I've ever even seen "Steve" at this place, and based on that alone, if I had never eaten here before, it would probably deter me.

I have eaten here once or twice, but it was nothing to brag about. Typical run-of-the-mill Korean BBQ, no zing, nothing to run home and tell my friends about. In the "Asian Ghetto", there are far more promising restaurants.

Haven't quite figured out who Steve is, but there isn't anything special about this place. Overpriced dishes of meat, rice, and assorted vegetables sums up what you get from this place. The homemade hot sauce has a slight tinge of alcohol that I can't quite narrow down, but it could just be vinegar.

If you're in the mood for large amounts of grilled meat atop a bed of rice and a bean sprout salad with kimchi on the side, pay Steve's a visit.

It's a tad pricer than other places in the Asian Ghetto, but this place is your place if you want serious big bang for you buck in terms of a high food to price ratio. One order can easily be two meals. While it's not top notch quality or even that authentic, it's still tasty and filling. Everything tastes better with the spicy sauce too. The place is pretty big and spacious for a fast food joint, but you can definitely see the marks of age. Another good thing is that it's open late and one of the last places to close down in the area.

I am a vegetarian, so if you are a meat lover read this review with a bit of skepticism.

Steve's Bar-B-Que is not very great.  The food is mediocre, at best.  And they don't even make a pretense of being a Korean restaurant -- I don't think that a single employee is even Asian.

That said, I know a few Koreans who like to eat here, and the food isn't that bad... but if you are craving Asian ghetto food, go to Thai Basil next door.

Yes, it's not high-quality food, nor very healthy, but it's very very filling.  In other words, food for college students.  I personally liked their BBQ Short Ribs.  It's a little on the expensive side compared to the rest of the menu though.

You can substitute out the kimchee if you don't like it.  Free self-serve diluted tea and water is available as well.

If you are starving and like BBQ Beef, ribs, or chicken, this is the place for you. 

Don't try their soup, they are not worth it and taste below average.

Pros:
a big plate of BBQ beef/ribs/chicken and rice/ kimchi for $7-$8, Enough to make 2 averge females full. 
Quick.
Kimchi is alright.

Cons:
Sometimes the beef is not tender enough maybe overcook?
It gets really crowded on a school day during lunch time

The place, first of all, is not pleasant at all. They do try to make it look "oriental" by putting some random korean cultural decoration, but clearly, it doesn't cut. 

When you look in to a korean restaurant, one thing that you have too look first, "banchan". Which is the small varieties of side dishes that comes out with main dish. Their Kimchi is horrible. They don't use Asian winter cabbage, rather they use any store bought american cabbage that doesn't compliment a method that kimchi is made. Furthermore their marinade for the kimchi is poorly made, in return, you get bad kimchi. 

Also their main chef, or should i say pretend cook, is non korean person, who is not familiar with traditional korean cooking method and spices.

In simple words, if you are korean, don't go (haha, get it?)

If you don't care about the taste or the origin of the cuisine and just wanna get full off of EXTREME PROTEIN heavy dish, maybe this restaurant is for you.

Like the reviewer Michael T. said, the place is not cheap. But if you just want meat that tastes mediocre and is in disguise as a Korean cuisine, go ahead! Enjoy!

4/5 #yes.

guilty pleasure. this is like going to bed without brushing your teeth - it's not good for you, but my goodness sometimes it happens.

ps. be a boss and mix up soy sauce and vinegar in their little to-go cups.

Love it. My boyfriend and I took me here when we first started dating and it is still our spot 2 years later. We typically get the chicken and bbq pork then go to town. The hot sauce is soooo tasty, too.
Ugh ... this place is not real Korean BBQ. They should really call this place "Steve's cheap meat and rice" ... go to Gonmaru north side.

"Steve" needs to expand his business. One of the better Korean BBQ joints I've been to besides Yummy's, Tasty's & Dong Yang, which are all in Honolulu. Besides the taste, they serve it in "Hawaiian fashion" and pile generous portions onto your plate. The Kimchee is good enough and service is friendly. I'm just trying to figure out how "Esteban" learned how to cook Korean food... lol

Probably the best short ribs around if you don't care about your health.  When I was a kid this place was fantastic but now that I'm all grown up and know better, the amount of fat on the ribs is kind of off-putting.  Decent sized portions though, so if you're hungry and looking for some fast and tasty Korean BBQ, I'd definitely recommend Steve's!
tons of food, decently cooked, and very cheap, but the pickled vegetables and kimchi are kind of rancid tasting. it's not really the kind of korean food i was expecting.

Even though Steve's is really not considered authentic Korean bbq it still has a place in my heart. you either hate it or love it. i like it b/c the portions are huge and the price is sooo cheap for korean bbq. also, i order a spicy beef soup (yuk-gae-jang) which steve actually makes himself in a shady place in the back of the restauarant. for some reason though, i like the way he makes it better than more expensive korean restaurants. the service is also fast.
the decor  isnt all that great but it is just a place to grab a good hot meal and then quickly leave for class. 
the bad thing is that i hate their kimchi. that kimchi is not korean, i do not know wut the hell it is. also, the gochu-jjang sauce is not exactly what i know is gochu-jjang sauce. otherwise, if youre on the college student budget then i recommend steve's.

Ahh Steve's, how I love the heaping piles of BBQ beef and incredibly quick service...

Definitely a frequent visitor to Steve's when I want a simple all-meat-no-veggie to-go meal. I've been known to get the #1 whenever I have BBQ beef cravings at Cal.  It's simple, has tons of meat and rice, is under $10, and there's a bit of bean sprouts and kimchi as well.

When I'm feeling like I do need veggies but still want some beef, I go with the bi bim bap, which is usually a huge portion of food (kimchi, spinach, sprouts, egg, etc) but very good when hot. That one can usually last a couple meals, which is great for the college budget.

Dang!  As crazy cheap and good as I remember it.  I used to eat at Steve's when I was a poor college student and now that I'm all-growns-up, I still get my Korean on as an old dude among kids at the Food Court.  This place is actually a 3.5 stars.

Food = 4.  The kalbi is awesome, the bi-bim-bap too.  You can get either for about $8.00 and you leave very full and satisfied.  The food could be spicier but they have bottles of spicy sauce available (which isn't the same as if the food had been cooked with spices).  

Service = 2.  You order at the counter and the cooks turn the food out quick-style.  Even when the place is busy, you get your food within a  few minutes.

Atmosphere = 2.  Remember folks, this place is in the Durant Food Court.  Steve's is probably the cleanest joint in the entire place but still not immaculate.  You don't go to Steve for ambiance.

If I weren't Korean and knew what Korean food truly tasted like, I might give this a 4.  It is tasty, and the portions are HUGE, but I just can't shake my innate Korean-ness.  Still, two solid meals on $6 can't be beat.  The kimchee is like orange non-spicy barely-pickled cabbage, which is a total turnoff for me.

Eww. I should of known from the name I was not going to be satisfied with this place. Steve's Korean BBQ? More like Steve's yucky food in a box. I ordered veggie bi bim bap. Now how in the hell can you mess up rice, veggies, and an egg? Well, it's possible. Rice was cold, hot sauce was bland, and the veggies seemed a couple of days old.

Upside. It was insanely cheap. $5.00. Will probably not go back though, as I type this, I'm developing a bad food related headache.
cheap korean eats for students on a budget....if anything, it'll get the job done.

Man, there's something so addictive about that red sauce. Every time I eat here, I just spray that shit all over my food like there's no tomorrow. Just hosing the meat down like I'm the mayor of Red Sauce Town. You smell what the Rock is cooking?

But no, the food is great. One plate can seriously feed like two mouths. And it's quality BBQ too! If you order the short rib combo plate, be prepared to use up a environmentally-dangerous quantity of napkins.

Seriously, you'll be hacking rain forests down like a Republican with the amount of napkins you'll need.

It's that much food.

But all in all, I love Steve's although he's never around no more. Where did he go? It's always the two goofy Mexican guys. Those guys crack me up. They're always playing Mexican music which is funny because it's a Korean restaurant.

But who's complaining? Good food, good people, gotta love this place.

What to know:

-It's obviously not authentic Korean BBQ (duh)
-That having been said, don't expect much.
-The portions are big
-The prices aren't necessarily cheap
-But again, the portions are big
-Sometimes the rice is too mushy
-Meat and rice = what's not to like?
-Meat and rice = needs variety


If you like lots of grilled, half-assed-marinated-but-still-decently-tasting meat and large scoops of rice, Steve's is your place. I'll come here once every blue moon, but it is definitely not a place worth frequenting more than once every couple of months.

My freshman year a korean friend of mine said that Steve's isn't "real korean bbq."  Well of course he's right - the place is staffed entirely by mexicans - but does it matter?  

The place doesn't make the cut for reasons other than authenticity; a restaurant doesn't need to be authentic, it just has to taste good, damn it.  The only good thing here is the "bulgogi" - and I use that term loosely, they just call it "BBQ Beef" - and the mysterious chili-paste that they put in ketchup containers.   Use it liberally; it's not very spicy but it sure is yummy.  

The rest has been pretty sub-par in terms of flavor and price.  The kalbi is pretty ridiculous; the smallest meat to bone ratio I've ever seen, I know any of my korean friends would be outraged.  The bibimbap is cold and bland, and the spicy pork stimulates your bowels more than it does your palette.  The worst part is just pure variety; I think there is barely 20 or so dishes on their entire menu, with only a few of them being passable.  

If you're looking for a good korean fix, Toust in rape alley (or whatever that's called...Sather lane?) and Koryo on telegraph are better bets.

I wish I could give them 1.5 stars, because the volume of food is good, but the value isn't worth 2 stars in my book.  I've gone here, probably 5 times, while I was a student and have never really been happy with their food.  Granted Korean BBQ, if you do it the right way, will be pricey, but this place is funky, even for the Asian Ghetto. 

The meat is really dry and tastes unmarinated (translation: overcooked). Slap in some supremely sour kimchee and bean-sprout namuru.  Also, stuff yourself with boatloads of rice and you've got a meal there.  The volume is great for what you pay, especially in the Berkeley area.  I never finished my food and you'll probably have left-overs to leave for the local dwellers.

Aside from the poor taste in food, what repeatedly turned me off was the staff.  When I went in the summer, there was a shirtless hairy-chested man grilling my food. He also served the rice on my plate and handled my cash.  Happened twice while I attended summer school and that was the end of me going there.  Imagine if this store was in a place where it actually got hot during summer: game over.

ughhhhhhhhh....

So my buddy takes me here and I figure ill settle for something not so unhealthy.  That would leave me to ordering "grilled" chicken and rice with veggies.  Why is it when I get the  plate full of rice topped with meat sparingly is it drenched in oil?  on a whats supposed to be grilled dish.  If I wanted chicken and rice soup with the oil as a broth I would make it myself.

Is it my palate or the fact that Steve is not physically there anymore? Everyone has a go-to place where no one particularly loves. It's like having a security blanket for my palate where the most perverse form of nostalgia and ceaseless craving erupts mysteriously unexplained. Somehow Steve's is that place for me whenever I'm away from the Bay Area. 

First and foremost, I dream about the rich sticky steamed rice smothered by charred chicken pieces with brunt fat trimmings to give off a low down dirty smoky carcinogenic flavar. It is this place where I would take a bite of that soggy lifeless kimchi so I can relearn the fact that it's the nastiest thang e-v-e-r. I also can't say enough about the bulgogi that didn't seem to have a hint of marinate or a plate of kalbi that has more bones than substance. How about the semi-sweet pickled bean sprouts that is boring tasteless to a fault but also something I always wished to have more of. Go figure.

Steve's is a big contradiction for my palate and the perpetual mystique despite the dingy straight laced ambiance. Somehow this rosy, overly romanticized urge wilted during my latest chicken plate. It was just not the same anymore as the security blanket didn't seem as wholesome and comforting as the previous finger sucking endeavors. Maybe something else has finally taken its place but the lack of a better taste can also give anyone a cool-off awakening. Can't completely let go, 3 stars for the latest experience. Eventually I will return and hopefully the magical spark will reappear, somehow.

This review is based on experiences 7-8 years old. I looooooooooved Steve's BBQ in undergrad.  Huge portions at a relatively decent price and it was Korean BBQ!  My favorite at the time was the spicy pork and I also really liked their pickled bean sprouts.  I remember trying other things there (the BBQ chicken is okay), but all that I can remember now is their spicy pork.  I've moved on to bbq'ed spareribs as a preference now, but I'll always appreciate Steve's relative cheapness and its kindness to my wallet and tummy.

This place is not very authentic but it serves a good portion. Meat is overcooked and just wasn't hearty enough to satisfy my korean carving. 

I wish I can write a better review. I have been here twice and it's been consistent of 3 stars.

Don't come here much anymore but once in awhile I have a craving and come here to get some spicy pork bbq over rice. It always brings me back to my college days when I was so poor having Steve's was a luxury. 

I even love their sides of kimchee and Korean spiced bean sprouts. They give you pretty large portions but I am usually still hungry when I finish. That's no fault to them, it's because I'm huge. 

I finally met the owner several years after I graduated college because he and his family went to the same church I attend. I was like, "What the hell, your dad owns Steve's BBQ!!!!! Hook it up girl!"

$1 to double the amount of korean bbq on your plate bought me in but after this, all I know is Steve sure ain't Korean. 

The food definitely didn't taste korean. The bulgogi wasn't that flavorful, a bit bland honestly. The sides were meh and the meat was meh. It was just a lot of it, which I guess in a college town is all that matters. They were nice enough to let us move the chairs around to outside.

I hear all the places in Asian Ghetto are about equal but at the price point it sure doesn't feel very asian or very ghetto. I've had cheaper in Austin for better taste, asian food wise.

Big portions, tastes okay, and a good deal...
Got the bi bim bap with beef and it was SO MUCH FOOD! Definitely something to eat as a starving student. The food isn't authentic Korean food, but it's doable.

They were also pretty quick with cooking the food. Don't know how clean the place is though... it looked a little run down.

To be honest, overall this place deserves 3 stars. But because of it's Grilled Noodles (w/ beef or chicken), it get's 4 stars. 

Do not get anything else but this entree at this restaurant in the Ghetto. It comes w/ kimchee, rice, and chow mein like noodles with your choice of meat... aboslutely delicious! Add some of that hot sauce on, and you're set!

spicy pork please! the flavor on the pork is really special, once you taste it your going to crave it. But be for warned, if you get the chicken or the beef that flavor won't be there. five stars for the pork (even if their is some connective tissue, easy to pick out.) Other meats are just average in my opinion, except the always delicious spareribs.

Cheap and they have hot tea for free!
Affordable and they definitely give you a big portion. Always crave their bbq, #1 or #2

cheap good korean food which is hard to come by (why aren't there any korean restaurants to fill the void between the cheap ones and the expensive ones?).  The BBQ pork is my favorite.  They should really do something new with all the space they have though.  Could be a lot more comfortable.
omygod, super duper fatty meat. :X

I forgot how cheap you can eat at a students' joint. 

Huge Bibimbap for $ 7 ... would have been great if it was warmer.

When I was 18, this was the ONLY place to eat at Berkeley other than Top Dog.

When I was 21, this was the ONLY place to eat at Berkeley other than Top Dog.

When I was 25, Steve's was still pretty good but I've been spoiled by the finest KBBQ spots in Los Angeles

When I was 30, maybe I didn't care as much as I did before but I thought Steve's BBQ downgraded quite a bit, the quality of their meat was not as good as I remember.

Now, I only go there if Top Dog is closed or the line is 38 people deep, and Top Dog is never closed.

Granted I am fully aware that this is not authentic Korean grub but since I was introduced to it by my best friend Mikey who is Korean it should at the very least get a yelp. I honestly have cravings for Steve's and when I do get a chance to have it I am more than happy. The short ribs plate is the kind of thing I lust over at odd hours of the night. I realize that next to the great cuisine of Mrs. Um this is nothing but after some beers on a weekend night...spot on.

Fast, cheap and satisfying Korean BBQ. I always ask for my food to go (even if I eat it there) because the portions are so huge. I love the bibimbap. The kim chee is okay, not as good as other places, but really what can you expect for a high volume, inexpensive Korean place geared towards students?

If you are a stickler for authentic Korean BBQ this is not the place for you, but if you're a poor college student looking for an extremely filling meal for under $10, this is the place to go. Whether you get the beef, pork, or chicken you will get a mountain of meat, rice, kimchi, and bean sprouts. My favorite is the #2, spicy pork. They also serve up your meal quickly, so this is a good place for people in a rush. This is definitely one of my go-to's in Berkeley, but not necessarily because of the quality but because of the quantity.

When we crave Korean BBQ and in the Berkeley area visiting my parents or hanging out in the area, this is where we go.  It's definitely an older location that has been there for years on end and of course places like this could use a little remodeling and could use a little more cleaning.  Although, I doubt that a remodel would ever happen.  However, their food never fails!  You barely ever see the manager of the place here.  What you will see is a bunch of Mexicans who will cook up your Korean BBQ for ya and a whole lotta college students chillen in this small place and "the village."  You will find that Steve's Korean is smack dab in the middle of a village of other food choices such as Vietnamese, Thai, etc.  

My favorite here would be the bbq beef platter either for there or to go.  I always ask for extra bean sprouts and kimchi and they hook it up like nobody's business.  I've always tried their grilled noodle dish, which is quite delish as well.  Their Kalbi dish is bomb too, but be sure to have floss with you because that stuff will for sure get all up in your teeth.  

Prices are legit and the amount of food is perfect!  For $8-9 bucks per plate, I can't complain.  Of course I love the location even more because I can go next door to Sweetheart Cafe and pick up a boba drink to enjoy with my plate from here.  I gotta say, get your grub on!!!

One of my favorite places in the UC Berkeley area!  I've only gotten the #1 from here, and I've never had a reason to switch.  It's delicious, gives you a ton of meat and lots of rice (a savior for a rice-deprived dorm student like me), and is close to campus.  They give you your food really fast, too. 

Overall:  YUMMY.  You get the bang for your buck! ...Hm, maybe that's not the right saying..... Anyways, basically if you like marinated meat and lots of rice, this is the place to go.

Although I graduated in 2005, when I visit Berkeley (usually twice a year), I make sure to check into Steve's BBQ for some short ribs! They're not overly marinated so the meat flavor goes though, and you get a pound or so of meat for $8! Are you kidding me? 

I wish there was a Steve's BBQ in Palo Alto, so that I could go there everyday. 

I think when I was actually at Berkeley, I didn't realize how good of a deal this place was... I mean in San Jose, you get similar quality of meat, over marinated (too salty, can't taste meat, etc) for quadruple the price (for the same amount).... Enjoy this awesome food!

I don't care if it isn't really authentic Korean.  I don't even care that most of the cooks are not even from the right hemisphere.  All I know is that for $6 I am going to get a huge plate full of delicious meat, and I love it.

I've come to Steve's BBQ a lot...and I have no complaints. 

The staff are friendly and the service is quick. Most of the time I get the BBQ short ribs...yum! The pork is pretty good as well. 

I didn't give it 5 stars because sometimes the short ribs were more fatty than meat and/or the other dishes were good, but not as yummy.. 

Another great thing is that they take credit cards :)

I do not understand all the hype about this place...seriously, the food is not that delicious. While portions are quite large, the meat quality is lacking and often overcooked and oversauced (yes, it's not a word, I am literate, this is Yelp, get over it). The portion-to-money ratio plus the fact that the food is palatable gives it three stars, but I'd much rather trot over to Berkel Berkel for their slightly smaller, slightly cheaper, but much tastier offerings.

It's pretty hard to find decent korean food here at berkeley, and while steve's probably lacks the authenticity/home-cooking that some might look for, it gets the job done for me simply by virtue of the portion sizes offered.   The plates are HUGE.  I personally don't care that I've never seen a single korean behind the counter.  The mexican workers are friendly and they awesome short ribs -- and even if you don't think the short ribs they'll undoubtedly satiate your hunger.  

Steve's takes card, making it one of the more convenient places to grab a bite within asian ghetto if you're out of cash.  It's a tad expensive though, about 7-9 dollars for a meal.

Came here for the first time finally!  FYI, I am in my 4th year at UCB, but I NEVER went to Steve's.  Reason?  The pictures they post outside of their food are...not appetizing.  I think they at least retake their pictures to make it more enticing...

Anyways, finally went with a friend because I was craving korean short ribs.  Definitely got my fix, but only in terms of quantity.  It is a LOT OF FOOD.  But it's not cheap for korean short ribs (ALMOST $10!!!).  Plus, the sides are only kimchi and a mediocre bean sprout "salad".  The short rib was okay, not that flavorful but I was happy it wasn't overdone.

I'll probably not come back...next time I have my Korean fix, I'll try elsewhere.

My kimchi was soggy and had zero crispness last Friday night... wtf?! But my kalbi was the bomb, like usual!

Not Steve's fault but kick all them stinky hippie bums outta the asian ghetto entrance... It's like walking through an invisible musty curtain of funky BO. Isn't there a tree to live in or something you have to handcuff yourself to in protest? GTF outta here!

Pretty good for the price. The portions are huge!! 
My friends and I came there for dinner and it was hellaa filling. There were three of us, and we couldn't even finish 2 plates. 
The meat was yummy, and the kim-chi wasn't so spicy (which I personally liked!) .
The person who took our order was nice too, so there's nothing to complain about. 
Although, their interior could use a little bit of an update - but then again, it IS in the asian ghetto ..

I'm sure the history channel will help substantiate my hypothesis within the year, but to give you a teaser, I have some preliminary evidence that God made Adam and then Steve's Korean Barbecue immediately afterwards. 

Why? Let's first take a look at the food. Each meat plate packs about 100 grams of protein, 150 of carbs, and some double digits of fats - the perfect macronutrient composition for the developing stud. This place is practically a scientifically-engineered pimp factory. There is no doubt that Steve's is the premier case study for the nutritional sciences department and thus heavily subsidized, all the better for our manly needs.

Second, any frequent eater will notice that patrons here are consistently 90% male. Is this bad news? No! Brothers, how else can we consume our fortified meal with complete concentration and diligence? All that perfume, female aroma, and exposed thigh would simply trick us into satiety and lead to muscular atrophy, no different from the excessive partnered cardio we receive in 'exclusive relationships', a devious trick invented to deplete us of the energy and charisma necessary to conquer further damsels. 

So, let us rejoice in this fraternal haven that is Steve's, and hopefully, in our festivities, we won't develop a preference for male company during it all.

If you like meat and lots of it, you should try this place out. The short rib plate gives you a generous amount of  ribs along with rice, kimchi, and sprouts. Oy! I could've eaten myself into a food coma, but I was good about it. And the line for the register built up right after my friends and I placed our orders. No worries though, because they were up in only a few minutes. The prices have gone up slightly, but portion size makes up for it. Will I try to come back here? Most definitely.

Steve's is an absolute staple anytime I'm around the UC Berkeley campus. A visit to the neighborhood is never complete without getting my fix in from the Asian ghetto. How could you complain when a meal is hot, fresh, and about $8! You just can't! Making it even more mind boggling is the fact that the place is run completely by the most proficient Korean-cooking Mexican crew to ever live on this Earth. I'm a fan of #31, Beef Bebimbap and I normally don't look at any other items. The bulgogi beef is always flavorful and is super delicious with the spinach, sprouts, carrots, radish and of course, the creme de la creme, the FRIED EGG! Over the years, I have grown to love Steve's and I've always come back to get my quickstyle bebimbap fix.

Dude, I love beef. I really do. So when you can get kai be served hot on a plate of rice and with those Korean style bean sprouts relatively late at night... then... I love that place as well. 

And it's where I had my first MTV reality show person sighting. I saw Yes sitting on a stool waiting for his food to go.

STEVE'S MEXICAN BBQ.  hahaha...that's what u'd guess the place would be called if u looked inside and saw the very non korean chefs.  i haven't been here all too often but it's definitely worth a try.  it's one of the famous berkeley landmarks and it's been here for a long time.  

def get a meat dish.  don't come here for the soup.  the bi bim bop looks not bad either.  finish the night with some boba from a couple doors down.

I'm going to skip right to the food part of this review, so all I have to say about the restaurant itself is that it is in the Durant Food Court (AKA Asian Ghetto) so restaurant itself can be best described as functional. Not super clean, not disgusting either. Take from it what you will.

This place can be viewed in one of two ways. From a Korean like me, I would say its an embarrassment to the Korean BBQ name. I'm sure the point has already been belabored here over and over, but I feel obligated to repeat again that Steve's really isn't true Korean BBQ. The food initially starts off actually tasting pretty good, but about 1/2 through it, the ratio of fat to meat really starts making the whole deal taste nasty. This is especially true of the short rib Kalbi dish. The kimchi is made of low quality cabbage and tastes like over-vinegared nonsense. The bean sprouts are pretty good though. I've tried all the BBQ meat dishes, and nothing really saves the day. I haven't been convinced or motivated to try the rest of the menu (soups and other rice dishes), so I can't comment on those, although from the reviews already here, I see that I'm not missing much.

However, you can judge this place through a more general lens as well. Although the food's quality is kind of suspect, the do give a TON of it. Throughout my entire undergrad career at Berkeley, I would say that this is one of the places that is among the top of giving you the most MASS of food per DOLLAR. Given that the food actually does somehow pass as edible and is quite filling (AND will most likely leave you leftovers for another meal) this is the only mitigating plus Steve's possesses.

I would recommend this place for the starving college student who can't be choosy about how to fill his hungry stomach. Or for the undiscerning person who just wants to get full. Otherwise, if you can afford to make a choice, I would stay far away. Its a shame that there aren't any other Korean BBQ places close to the Berkeley campus that are good alternatives.
This place rocks. Huge plate of Korean grilled beef or chicken with excellent kim-chi, marinated sprouts, and rice for hella cheep. One of the food treasures of the Telegraph area.
My boyfriend forced me to come again...and it was actually good this time! The meat was nicely cooked and flavorful. Apparently, the secret is to tell the cook not to burn the meat. Who knew?

awesome BBQ. I can't say that I know authentic Korean BBQ but this place is great nonetheless.This place is a meat lover's heaven, the portions are absolutely massive, and well worth your money. I usually order the BBQ Beef with Veggies, its about 6.75 and comes with kimchee and a yummy side of sprout salad. A bit on the greasy side but who the hell goes to a BBQ joint expecting to eat healthy anyway?

honestly not the best, or should i say, not at all traditional bbq. 
BUT, it does get the job done when i am hungry after a work out and need protein. 

I always go with the chicken and 2 eggs. 

in and out within 10 minutes and for under 9 dollars

Very filling portions, albeit with average-quality meat. A meal runs you $6-$7. Don't try the soups unless you're with a friend - you'll never finish it, it's pretty dull, and it feels like a side order. Also, their hot sauce isn't that great. More sweet than spicy.

Come here for a quick, cheap Korean food while listening to Mexican music.

So I've heard jokes like this is like Steve's Mexican BBQ rather than Steve's Korean BBQ, and only tried this place last year. Surprisingly, it's not so bad. I love their Dak-gu-i (BBQ chicken, I think) - not because it's like a korean dish, but more because it reminded me of Shaslik, a dish I had in Kazakhstan. For those who know what that is, seriously, it's SUPER similar. Also, they make Cabbage Kimchi that's different from the usual Kimchi (which is made from Napa Cabbage). Some might not like it because it taste different, but I've had those kind of things when I was a kid, so it actually gave me nostalgia. Weird, I know. 
Anyway, they give a lot of rice, and even though sometimes they burn the chicken a little too much, it's a place I'd go when I'm really hungry and I want korean food, fast. They're usually not that packed, so your order comes out pretty soon.

Gosh, its been awhile since I've have a Steve's number one combo... with their homemade sweet chili sauce. Its not the best Korean food in the world but it sure tasted good when I was a "starving" student. I'd go back just for the heck of it... for old times sake!

We actually walked into the little restaurant area there to go to the Ramen place next door, but saw the Korean BBQ and that sounded better so we walked in. I ordered the chicken soup with side of rice, with a moderate spiciness.

SO GOOD. I was pleasantly surprised and they were not cheap on the chicken and fresh veggies thrown into the mix. 

I would definitely go back sometime, but if you are going you have to know it is kind of a whole in the wall kind of place. You are going for a lunch type divey- korean bbq, not a fancy date kind of place.

The Berkeley alumnus in me still has cravings for cheap, good Korean food from Steve's. Get it to go if you're not super hungry because portions are huge. If you ask nicely, they'll sell you a little tray of japche too!

My trip to the Asian Ghetto begins here. I will forget the previous attempts in the past.   I introduced my coworker to this place. I had the bbq squid. It was good as I had them make it with no oil. So plus to that.  The squid was tender and easy to chew.  The minus would be for the bean sprouts and kim chee.  The bean sprouts was flavorless and the kim chee was not spicy.  A good cheap Korean place to go to when near the campus and does beat Sorabol in Emeryville. Only because they have the bbq squid, sorry my good ole stand by. But if you want good Korean food, head down to Koreatown in Oakland.

best hole-in-the-wall korean bbq place!! it's cheap and they give huge portions!! the food got me through my marathon studying sessions. one bbq order would last me for two days.

bbq pork is the best! nommmmmmmmmmmmmnomnom *drooooool

I used to live in the dorms down the street from the Asian Ghetto.  Steve's is one of my all time favs for cheap eats in the Bay Area.  Love the large portions, cheap price, fast service, and free hot tea.

YEEEE.  Need a meat fixing?  COME HERE!  The portions are HUGE, and I always have meat and rice left over!  The short ribs are delicious (for a college student), although they could be a little more lean/less fatty, but their chicken fried noodle with veggies is another of my favorites!
this place is only intended for college students who need an alternative to dc food.

This is not authentic Korean food.  Just to get that out of the way...

That being said, I love this place.  I used to go here all the time when I was in college.  It certainly contributed to my Freshman 15 (or 50, but who's counting?).

Now that I've moved back to the area, I come here every now and then for the great food.  While it's not authentic, it's still quite good.  I always get the short ribs as I think that's the best.  It's fatty, greasy, and really hits the spot.  Try a fried egg or if you're especially hungry go for the extra meat.

Steve's is worth the trek all the way over to the "asian food ghetto" (aka Durant square) in Berkeley. I love the kal-bi (short ribs), no kimchee extra sprouts. They give GENEROUS portions for a reasonable price.

Steve's is alright.  If you're scouting for some muscle-building PROTEIN, then come here because the meat is cheap and tastes like average Korean BBQ.

I recommend the glass noodles w/veggies and choice of meat.  You definitely get a variety of flavors and a heaping portion. Overall, the meat isn't tough, but not melty tender either.  Like everyone else said, the kimchee is blegh.  :[

TIP:  Request EXTRA MEAT with your meal.  Only $1 extra!!  You won't be disappointed.
This Korean fast food spot is one of the better spots in the AzN ghetto. It's as simple as BBQ beef, rice, kimchee and bean sprouts.

I've been coming here since I was a little boy, since my family friend owned the restaurant a few doors down. 

Great food for under $10. The serving sizes are huge and I eat a lot! I recommend the Bim Bim Bong, with BBQ beef in it.
Food is always great and fairly priced!

Yes it's not an authentic Korean restaurant...

but who cares?

the food it's still delicious and i'm always amazed by its incredibly quick service.
the portion is always good as well

it is open till late so it's great place to fulfill your late night munches :D

When I lived in Berkeley & when I used to not want to cook, the other half would more-than-often suggest we get Korean food.  After successfully fielding his requests several times, I gave in.

I got a Bibimbap with chicken which came in a hug portion.  Everything was cooked nicely except for the fried egg.  It was slightly overcooked so the yolk didn't break, run, & coat the rice.  I also didn't  are for the particular kimchi that the restaurant uses.  The boyfriend ordered a BBQ beef which had less food than  my bibimbap & the beef was a little bit overcooked.

On a separate occasion - I didn't give in, I got myself Thai - the boyfriend got himself BBQ short ribs.  While there was a lot of meant, they were really really fatty.

For the times that we've been, Steve's has only minimally disappointed.  While it probably does not serve anywhere near the best Korean food, I am going to miss having it so close by.

I like to think of Steve's "Mexican Korean" BBQ as the greatest simple food you can find around Berkeley. There really isn't nothing to it. Just cook some rice, grill some chicken, add bean sprouts with kimchi, and there's your typical Steve's take out. 

However, there is something so good about all this that I just can't put my finger on. The meat is always really delicious and cooked with a lot of flavor. Rice is just rice, but Steve's does it right, unlike Mandarin House next door.

Steve's has been there for me through thick and thin, rain or sunshine, drunk or sober. If you're not quite sober and they're still open, it's the perfect fix if you don't feel like going to Top Dog. 

There's not much else I can say about Steve's. You just have to go there and experience the flavor of Mexican Korean BBQ for yourself.

I'm glad this place is still around.

I dropped by Durant Square last week to grab a bite of nostalgia from my old stomping grounds. Among poor college students, it was widely known that Steve's served the most bang for the buck. All orders come with a pound of rice and sides of kim chi and sprouts. One meal can easily stretch to two, unless you're a fat guy. My favorite was the BBQ chicken, but the spicy pork was a close runner up. I should mention that this food isn't super authentic, especially since it's not really Steve's BBQ -- more like Steve's Amigo's BBQ. But that doesn't even matter, because if you're eating here, you're probably not Mr./Mrs. Zagat -- you're just a hungry student in need of sustenance. Anyway, I ordered the classic BBQ chicken -- same recipe, same satisfaction.

Tips: They host one of the few bathrooms in the square.

Steve's Barbecue is as far away from good Korean food as it gets. 
Out of all the restaurants in the Asian ghetto , Steve's would probably be my least favorite after Panchos. 
I have been there a couple of times and tried almost every item on their barbecue menu. The portions are huge which seems to be the only thing going for Steve's. The service wasn't exactly top notch either. What put me off the most was the bland tasteless texture of the meat which seemed to be undercooked as well. 
The kimchi that came along on the side felt as if it had been taken straight out of the fridge. It felt stale and bland. 
-1 star for bad tasting food. 
-1 star for overpricing bad food
-1 star for lack of authenticity ( if you want to open a Korean barbecue place make sure that it serves real Korean food and not generic tasteless food) 
+1 star for large servings

If this place were called Steve's Mexican Bbq, I'd probably give them 4 stars. But the misnomer and lack of marginally authentic korean food forces me to dole out a measly 3. 

The galbi's greasy and probably contains more trans-saturated fat than my grandparents were rationed in an entire month during the Cultural Revolution. Not to mention the fatty ribs give me the worst stomach pains and watery diarrhea. 

I regret going there during that 30 mins of PAIN on the toilet, but I'll still find myself at Steve's in the span of another 2 weeks. If you ever find yourself lost amist the students of Cal and the homeless of Telegraph, be sure to stop by Steve's for 30 minutes of greasy goodness. Just be prepared to find a bathroom two hours later.

The only reason why I go to the asian ghetto... and I still do.  When I end up going to Newman Hall's 10pm'er, I make sure I pass by this joint for some good old BBQ beef or chicken.  

Some things never change...

it's not the food. it's the memory embedded in each piece of overcooked bulgogi; the memory of my early college days when steve's was the only source to remind me i was a carnivore. i become so nostalgic that i forget what im shoving in my mouth. history lives on. so as the sour cabbage and saggy bean sprouts. 

boy, am i getting old.

I used to eat at Steve's quite a bit when I was going to Cal, and always liked it. They give you a TON of food for pretty cheap, and IMO it's pretty tasty. Admittedly, I know nothing when it comes to "authenticity" of Korean BBQ, or how this place stacks up. All I know is that I like it and I'm giving them 4 stars. 

Like I said, I used to eat here a lot when going to school, but that was eons ago. I finally got to eat here again after witnessing a demoralizing defeat of the Golden Bears at the hands of the Oregon ducks. I got BBQ chicken which comes with (a lot) of rice as well as sprouts and kimchi. I think the only other thing I've had here besides this is the BBQ beef, which comes the exact same way as the chicken.  What can I say...the meat is tender and there's a lot of it, which is good. 

As far as the restaurant itself, who cares what it's like? It's in the ghetto food court so what do you expect (for those not familiar with the Berkeley's ghetto food court aka Asian ghetto, the fact that the work "ghetto" is in the title should tell you what it's like)? They're pretty quick with orders, and if you're planning on eating there, and don't want to eat outside they actually have quite a bit of seating compared to other places in the food court. 

I'm a fan of Steve's BBQ!

This place = Godly.

I think for a stretch of 2 weeks during my 2nd year at Cal, I ate here at least once a day every day for lunch or dinner (or both).  This place is the reason why I don't fit in 32 jeans anymore.  The taste is just okay, typical low-mid grade meat, but dude the QUANTITY.  I mean, I really shouldn't be coming to a joint like this when I have no portion control, but dude these guys will put heaps and heaps of meat onto your plate or take out box.  I know the owner (Steve obviously) pretty well so he'd always wave at me and give me extra food, but I don't know anymore.

You can't go wrong with any of the dishes here, even the grilled chicken is fantastic.  The wonton soup is quite legit as well and so is the bibimbap.  Really, just go and try this place out if you haven't already.  And if you're a student who hasn't tried them yet, shame on you.

I totally remember the first time I came here. My boyfriend (now hubby) took me there 10 years ago. I remember telling him I wanted to eat at a sit-down restaurant.  This was his idea of a sit-down restaurant, a place where you could sit down AFTER you order your food at the counter.  I was super mad at him..but the tasty food made it hard for me to stay mad at him for long.

Ok, enough background information...The food is delicious. I always order the kalbi (short ribs) and substitute the glass noodles for the rice.  The portion size for me is perfect, I usually have enough left over for the next day.

I didn't get into Berkeley so I have to settle for wannabe status. But on the days when I am on campus for meetings, I imagine myself as a happy undergrad or MBA student sitting down to Steve's more than once every couple months and cramming loads of flame grilled Korean bbq down my throat with block of rice and a quarter pound of kimchee.

The first time I came here I was hungry and my mentees suggested coming here. The food was cheap and I reminisced of college life where food is cheap and your metabolism and activity are high enough to ward off even the most obscenely unhealthy food's impact on your gut.

Ever since I have been hooked. I usually just get the beef over rice (occasionally mixed with veggies) and it's a satisfying, if belly busting, delight. The flavor is seared into the meat and actually stays if you choose to refrigerate the meat. The kimchee is not spicy, but crisp and contains a wickedly tasty flavor that complements the meat and rice.

All for like $6 or $7. Hot tea and iced water on the side is available. And the staff while not overtly friendly makes your food quick. Parking is, as you'd expect, horrible. You're lucky if you find something on Durant, otherwise there is a garage down the block.

Long live Asian ghetto and Steve's!

Whatever this place lacks in authenticity, it makes up in the amount of food... like, RIDICULOUS piles of meat!!!

I wish they'd stop trying to force bad kimchi on me. Although I am ashamed to say that I love their kong na mul, it's so delicious to me, hahahah... I know it is sad, don't hate on me. I actually ask for no kimchi and when I do that, they give me double scoop of kong na mul and I eat every single bit of it!

Great place for hungry college kids. Cheap food if you're not a big eater and you can save half of it for a future meal. Don't overstuff yourself. The spicy BBQ pork is darn good. =)

Good stuff!  Part of the Ghetto Gourmet (or whatever that area in Berkeley is called with all the cheap eats places).  Portions are large, tasty (almost too tasty...what do they put in their food?!?!), and if you're looking for anything more, you'd probably give it two stars or less.  You get what you pay for, and if you're looking for 5 star dinning in a place called the Ghetto Gourmet (again, or whatever), you're missing out on the point.  Stop being a food snob and just try the darn place...you won't be disappointed!

If you're confused on what to get, just stick with the Kal Bi and you can't go wrong!

Happy Eating!

Another Berkeley Student Staple...
I can't comment on how authentic it is or whatnot, but I do know it is what every college man needs, some MEAT and some RICE and HOT SAUCE. This was the best cheapest meal you could find in Berkeley, keep you full for hours or until you got the munchies again and make the trek back to the asian ghetto LOL.

Not much else to say about Steve's, it is what it is and it is Awesome!

MY GO-TO DISH: BBQ Chicken or Beef Spicy, do they even have anything else???

Went here at like 9 and it was pretty dead

damm the bbq beef here is good and totally worth the price

bbq short ribs are also really good

if youre looking for a good korean restaurant you with huge serving sizes definitely come here

Steve's is where I go to really grub. It usually takes me two sittings to get through one to go box of bbq pork, which consequently gave my dog one shining opportunity to knock the food off the table and devour the second half of my meal within the five minutes I was out of the room. Believe me or not, he has really discerning taste and never ran into a room faster than when I got Steve's. Studmuffin (boyfriend, not dog) prefers the bbq beef. $6.29 for each. Also, pass on the kimchi for extra rice.

Leave it to a Korean restaurant to say "to hell with it" and serve meat and spices in the in-your-face manner that only they could.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: two stars.

My friend and I frequented Steve's all the time for our BBQ meat fixation. Steve's offers a huge plate of rice, topped off with a huge amount of really well done BBQ chicken or beef. Get it spicy though, because otherwise there is no flavor. 

Besides the meat, there is not much flavor to speak of. Yeah, there is kimchi, but since you listened to me and got the spicy beef or chicken, it doesn't give any new flavor. The rice is white rice, so expect a surface for your meat and nothing more.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: one star.

Some people have a problem with having to walk up to pick up your food or having to walk to get anything else, such as tea or utensils. I know South Side kids are ridiculously lazy, but come on. Big ******** deal.

Best bang for your buck for the Telegraph area. For $9 you'll get meat, meat and more meat. I come here if and only if I have a high craving for meat. 

If you want quality, go to Oakland or San Jose. If you're looking for large portions of meh Korean food, this is the place to go. 

Credit cards are accepted! For some reason this place is one of the emptiest restaurants in the Ghetto.

No, it's not "authentic" -- but as long as it tastes good, I'll keep coming back. I believe that this establishment gives you the most food for your $ in the UC campus area (please correct me if I am mistaken), and the time between ordering and receiving your food is literally like a minute. 

Pretty much every time I decide to eat in, I do not finish my meal. I pick up a plastic container to pack up my leftovers, and one of the employees behind the counter will walk out and hand me a bag unprompted. It's a simple gesture, but I definitely wouldn't come to expect that anywhere in the Asian Ghetto. 

Minus a star since the quality of food might be sketch, but for the price, I honestly do not mind. (I don't mean sketch as in it will make you sick--but I have received some gristly, fatty pieces of meat.) 

Bonus -- Being able to share one $9 plate of food between a girl and a guy and having us both walk out full is a rare occurrence.

Have you ever slept with someone, perhaps they barely qualified, you might not know them that well, nothing spectacular, nothing special, but nothing terribly wrong either... and you haven't got anything better going on right now... so you went again... that's Steve's BBQ in a nutshell.

For $9, you can get a large plate of beef short ribs.  You will definitely be full of meat after you come here.  That sounds dirty.  It isn't the best.  The kimchi is really underwhelming.  Not spicy or salty enough.  But, the turnover is high.  And the food is fresh (but, not the best quality).  It is not exactly the cleanest place.  The best part is the outdoor seating.  With all the other restaurants sharing outdoor seating, you and your friends can get whatever you want and sit together.  It is kinda like the UC Berkeley equivalent of the food court at the mall with the following notable differences  (1) lots of college students, (2) cheap food, (3) all the food is Asian, (4) it is dirty, (5) people smoking marijuana all over the place and (6) homeless people.  Actually, this should be a required stop on parent's weekend.  So, they can see what kind of education they are getting for their precious child.  

Child:  Mom and Dad, college is great.  I am learning a whole lot
Homeless Man:  Are you going to finish that?  Can you spare some change?
Father:  I am trying to have a conversation with my daughter.
Friend at other table: Hey, do you want to hit this?
Father: we are sending you to UCLA
Child:  but at least I am filled with lots of meat...

Hunger is the best sauce.

And Steve's got a lot of sauce for you!  Poor quality meat. Dirty. But since they give you portions and it's cheap, students love this place.  

Music to a starving budget concious student's ears...but hell to anyone that has a tongue or a stomach.  It's a testament that if you are hungry you will eat anything.  Stop by next door to Thai Basil instead.

Yes their prices have been going up bit by bit for the past couple of years, but when the other places in the Asian Ghetto are cutting back on their portions, Steve's doesn't. When I came here 3 years ago as a first year, I thought the prices were a bit high, but still worth it for a good portion of bbq meat. However, back then the other places around weren't stingy either. So I had options.

I hadn't been back to Steve's since that first year, and I really don't know why. Thai Basil for sure started giving less food, and I could actually finish it without being substantially full. Came back to Steve's and was impressed that prices still haven't yet hit the $9 mark, and yet their portions are the same. Super filling. I think I used to eat a whole dish by myself (oh yay freshman 15). But getting a boyfriend means being able to split everything, even the calories! We came in and got the bbq beef. I never liked their kimchi though, just theirs because I like other restaurants'. Not a fan of bean sprouts so that was part of my boyfriend's half. The meat was tender and juicy, just the way I like it. They also gave a good amount of rice and was very prompt with the order. 

So basically, if you're really hungry and in the Ghetto, go to Steve's, it'll get the job done. Otherwise if you're looking to spend a little less and not starving for food, you can go elsewhere.

Anybody who really knows me, knows that I could Steve's every day for a month if I really wanted to. I have been going here for the past 12 years, ever since a good friend of mine took me there. Of course it isn't ver authentic and the guys who work there are brown, ( which I love more than anything) however the food is aweseome and comes out the same way everytime. I am a carnivore and I love meat ( no hetero).  How could I not love going to Steve's. I could however do without  all the non ethnics around though being loud and annoying. That's why I find myself calling in ahead of time so it's ready by the time that I get there. I would also wish that people would stop referring to the food court as the "asian ghetto" because they do in fact have italian, mexican, and greek food as well.

What inspired me to walk into this restaurant was looking at the plate portions and the fact that it was a K-BBQ place but in hindsight I lightly regret choosing this place to eat lunch.

Everything about this place seemed like your typical hole-in-the-wall restaurant (cheap, not a lot of people, slightly dirty) but I had high hopes when I saw that this place had BBQ chicken; I love anything BBQ and chicken is awesome too so by instinct I had to choose it. But reflecting back on the meal, it makes me regret choosing this place. 

The meal was satisfactory for me except for one thing. The chicken was dry, charred, and almost tasteless. After the first bite, I immediately regretted choosing the dish. I had to drench my entire plate with the red sauce to try and salvage my meal and make the dish more tasteful but, truth be told, any sauce should never overpower the meat's flavor; it's only meant to compliment it. Unfortunately, I had to pour the sauce on. Heavily. Otherwise I think I would've given up and not have finished my meal. I'm not usually a picky person when it comes to eating, but burned and tasteless chicken is definitely not what I expect when I think of K-BBQ chicken.

I used to really like this place. They give you HUGE portions of meat for a good price. I always ordered the beef short ribs, and I always had enough left over to save for another meal.

However, the quality has been lacking in the recent year or so. The meat is fattier than before. And the rice has become merely "edible" (sometimes I wonder if I should just make my own).

typical asian ghetto... overpriced and overrated.

sorry steve, but your food made me sick.

they didn't have kimchi fried rice so i opted for the spicy chicken and vegetables hoping that it would be similar to gomnaru which is amazing but a bit out of the way.

instead, i got a mix of chicken and vegetables loaded with grease that resembled japanese teppanyaki rather than korean food.  

i'm definitely sticking to gomnaru whenever i need a spicy chicken and kimchi fried rice fix

Not the best Korean food you can find in the Bay Area or even Berkeley for that matter, but they are catered to serve the college kids in the area so what can you expect?

The obvious choices to get if you're looking for some good bar-b-que for a very affordable price with generous portions would have to be any of the protein dishes such as the chicken, spicy pork and of course short ribs.  However, I must say for those who don't know what's up....my personal favorite dish has got to be the short rib beef soup (getting it spicy is a MUST and they will ask you first when you order).  It's very filling, very tasty and you can't even order this particular soup (spicy that is) at any normal Korean restaurant which is why I love it there so much.  The spicy flavor just makes it taste so much different from all the rest that I've tried anywhere else.  Trust me folks, I am Korean and if you're in the mood for a great tasting soup after a night of hard drinking or when you just feel like something hearty and warm on a cold day or after snowboarding etc, then this is the meal to have.  

Oh and one more thing...don't forget to do it the Korean way and drop you rice right in the bowl of soup (although the whole bowl is not necessary) and you'll be good to go!!

Say what you will about how unauthentic Steve's Korean Bar-B-Que is... but let's be honest, most college kids are looking to spend less money on food and more on booze. With that said, Steve's is a great option- the portions are huge (enough to make-up two meals), which was perfect for a poor college student like myself. My top favorites include the Bar-B-Que Beef Short Ribs and Yu Ke Jang (Spicy Beef Soup)... the Kimchee and sprouts were so-so, but hey, we've already discussed its lack of authenticity. Unless you're a stickler when it comes to Korean food, I'd say this is a great spot.

oh please...this is steve's BBQ!  this isn't gourmet korean food.  if you want "real" korean food go to koryo or a place like that.

this is a plastic to-go container filled with big scoops of rice topped with lots of meat with some sprouts and american cabbage kimchi on the side...and it's freaking AWESOME!  

i remember back in the day when steve's was in the middle location with only the bar, my friends and i would sit at that bar because the owner would give us more rice.  sure, it's a lot of food but when i was in college, i ate like an elephant...i would ration though short ribs and fill up my stomach with rice...and the owner would just give me more scoops of rice...lol!  heck, i probably used my broken korean to talk him into giving me some extra scoops of meat back then too... 

i've had meals at some of the best restaurants in the world but whenever i head back to Cal to watch them beat up on stanfurd in the big game (or get blown out like last year)...i still walk over to steve's bbq after the game and i love it!

stop expecting steve's bbq to be something it's not.  it's good, cheap, nostalgic, soul food for korean people...food.

Not even close to being Korean food. In my 3 years at Cal, I don't think I have ever seen a Korean working there, nor has my bibimbap or bulgogi or anything Korean even tasted anything like authentic Korean food.

But, on the upside, you get a good serving for your bbq food, and it's pretty decent food. I usually get the short ribs, but I also only come here when I'm feeling for some oily meat. Your meat orders always come with a side of bean sprouts and kimchi (which you can substitute in kimchi for an extra side of bean sprouts and vice versa). 

Eh, I would shy away if you're looking for Korean bbq. But, if you're a meaty kind of person... this place is for you!

This place isn't somewhere you go for great Korean food by any means. It's trashy, it's cheap, it's filling, and it's consistent.

And I love it. I go here every time I'm in the area. It was one of my comfort foods when I went to Cal and it makes me happy every time I can get my hands on it.

The portions are monstrous. You get a giant pile of meat on a giant pile of rice with two small piles of kim chee and bean sprouts. Okay, the kim chee and bean sprouts aren't great, but I've had worse.

I always get the BBQ pork. The flavor is actually really fantastic. The pork isn't always super tender and can have some connective tissue or chunks of fat at times. But it's not hard to pick it out.

If you go to Cal then you already know about the Asian ghetto and have probably at least seen this place in the back. If it's late and you're really hungry then you can't do much better than Steve's. I know I'll come here every time I'm back for a bit of super filling and tasty nostalgia.

Please forgive the Cal alumni who have stated the following sentiment:  "How can it be Korean BBQ when I have never seen a Korean behind the counter, etc, etc,"  or any variation.  Clearly, they are ignorant and racist.  For if their statement contained any bit of truth, then no French restaurant in America can really be called French because behind the counters are non-French cooks from South America and from other poorer nations like the Philippines.

I can attest that there have been Koreans behind the counter.  That is because I've been eating at this place since 1986 when they occupied the middle section of Durant Square and they only had 8 seats at the bar.  The current location used to be a Mexican restaurant.  (Sidenote:  Berkeley alum Class 1990, Ph.D. 1997)

Now, some Koreans have mentioned that this is not true Korean food.  I would point out that for a non-Korean like me, this is likely the first introduction to Korean food one can have.  And, it is absolutely the best way to be introduced what with the plethora of meats such as beef, chicken, pork and the RIBS!  

Twenty years later from starting my gastronomic journey, I still go back to Steve's BBQ even though I know of more authentic Korean restaurants.  Why?  Because there is a chemical reaction that happens when chicken or any meat for that matter is grilled to perfection over fire.  In every meal, it happens here.  If you are under 30 years old, order the beef ribs to your heart's delight.  If you are older, content yourself with the BBQ chicken and savor your increased life expectancy.  

As for authenticity based on spices, traditional methods of preparation and technique, one can classify Steve's BBQ as Korean-American.  The serving of meat and rice are Texan in size.  The efficiency of cooking is New York.  The taste is Californian.  And of course, the labor is provided by the poverty from South America.  

Steve's created a wonderful restaurant built on hard work and perspiration.  I remember the days when the server, the cook, the cashier were most likely his family.  Now that they have succeeded, why should  I not appreciate the fact that capitalism works.  The restaurant is successful enough that he can share his bounty and hire other people, no matter their race.

There was a short time where my friends and I came here once a month on a religious pilgrimage. We didn't come here because we like Korean BBQ. We came here because we like Steve's BBQ. Please don't mark it off stars because it isn't real Korean BBQ - because you'll eat it. You'll eat it and you'll love it.

Steve's Korean is some of the best food you can get at the infamous Asian Ghetto. You don't expect much from places in this location but they get it done with their solid offering of grilled meats. Very limited selection compared to your typical Korean restaurant but at least they churn out quality selections at a very affordable price. Just got to make your way pass the mob of college students armed with their boba and dollar noddles and the lurking bums and looking for more change than Obama

Tips:

$7-8 for a BBQ meat dish comes with bean sprouts, kimchi, and white rice.

I wouldn't dub Steve's as a very authentic Korean food place.

--------------------------------------------------

I really like Steve's because they always give you a HEAPING portion of meat on top of your rice. Honestly I think the portion size could feed 2 people, they just give you that much. I always get the BBQ chicken and it's super awesome I highly recommend getting that meat combo.

If you don't like bean sprouts like me, or you really love kimchi, you can ask for no bean sprouts and they'll double up the amount of kimchi they give you. Steve's is definitely the place to go if you're really hungry and you're just craving some meat and rice. (The good stuff)

The bibimbap is great as well! Sure it's not the most authentic Korean food, but it's still good to eat!

One of the high points of the Asian ghetto.

It has everything a restaurant that resides in the ghetto needs: late hours, cheap prices, and huge portions.  But it tops most of the other restaurants on in the ghetto for two reasons: 
1.  70% of my plate is meat and that makes me happy
2.  Only 30% is not meat!

Although most people go for the BBQ beef and short ribs, I usually get the BBQ chicken.  It is perfectly seared, has a great smokey taste, and is usually at least 2 breast-sizes worth of white meat.  I like getting the spicy red sauce (comes out of a dispenser next to the hot tea and water dispensers) and pouring it all over the rice/chicken plate before indulging.

I also really love their Tofu soups, especially with seafood.  I am a fan of the seafood hodgepodge that many restaurants just throw into dishes in order to add a dollar to the price.  I mean, I think I can identify most things in the soup, but who needs to when it's so delicious?

We interrupt your current television fetish of trying to watch the entire Battlestar Galactica series before Bar review starts on May 23rd with this important review.  Yelp just won't let you forget that you've marked this business as "to review" and is giving you more attention than an efficient prostituted from the continent.  

Sunday mid-day, Cal was graduating, students were fleeing, graduates were tottering around in unaccustomed heels that they thought looked "smart" "sexy" and "unique."  There is nothing more cringe-worthy than watching a relatively pretty girl in full regalia wearing cheap shoes that she is so proud of, wobbling at the ankle every step she takes and threatening to tip her over onto her pretty face or shatter her femur in 3 places.  I have a huge pet peeve about people who cannot walk in high heels yet insist on wearing them.  

I came by Steve's because I was craving Ramen and I couldn't find any that fit the bill.  After a delicious meal at Oyaji in SF on Friday for $8.50, my standards for mediocre ramen have changed.  I want it damn sexy and damn tasty, AND be less than $8.50.  

The prices in Steve's were closing in on the $10 limit.  My order of short ribs came out to be around $9 after tax.  The grill-manipulator dug his tongs deep into a bucket of marinating meat and retrieved a portion worthy of applause.  Was all that mine?  My greedy little mind went to work calculating the value-price ratio.  I was accustomed to and expecting 3 strips.

It was served on top of a mountain of rice, on a petal-pink plastic plate.  The plastic plate was the size of obese America in the 1990s, portion distortion separators filled with bean sprout salad and kimchee.    The bone-in bits were well caramelized and a bit chewy in parts.  But, here's my secret confession: I like gristly meat sometimes.  Especially if I get to rip it off the bone with my teeth.  It satisfies some primal hunting urge that bubbles up deep within my subconscious and causes me to lick the flavors off my fingertips the way the witches in MacBeth savor the eye of newt.  

After I was done gorging myself on the slightly charred pile of meat and rice, I got a plastic to-go container and packed the rest to go home.  One serving here is enough to feed a family of 3.  After eating half of everything on the plate, the remaining only just fit in the large to-go container.  

It gives you an atomic bang for your starving student buck

Six dollars will get you a heavy plate of rice covered with a generous portion of grilled meat along with a side of bean sprouts and kimchi. Pro tip: Swap the kimchi out for a double portion of sprouts (the kimchi sucks), and stop by the sauce dispenser at the utensil stand to get a couple shots of Steve's delicious red chili sauce. 

The food isn't authentic Korean, but you'll get over it pretty quickly because, let's face it, any kind of grilled marinated meat is still damn tasty. 

I usually order the chicken, but the bulgogi and spicy pork are also good. The sprouts aren't the sesame oil kind you're probably used to--they have a unique vinegar flavor that I love. Portions are large enough to feed two, but a hungry guy can easily kill a plate on his own.     

The tables are fine for a quick meal, but it's easy to see why most students order entrees to go.

Steve's is actually more of a three- or four-star place, but I bumped it up to five for nostalgia's sake and to help balance out the haters. I've been out of school for a few years now, but I still find time to visit every couple of months.

This place is the Sorabol or Hahn's Hibachi of the Asian Ghetto. Cheap, big servings, and somewhat tasty. BUT sketchy kimchi, not the best quality meat (really fatty), and over sauced.  Not super authentic Korean BBQ. 

If you're in need of calories, but short on cash, come here. If you want authentic Korean BBQ take a drive down Telegraph into Oaktown.

Cheap college eats scale: 3+ stars
Korean for Korean's scale: 1-2 stars

When I first moved to the Bay Area, I was fresh out of living 4 years in the middle of rural New Hampshire. There were like two Chinese restaurants (hello, Panda House!), one Thai restaurant, and one Indian restaurant in town. And since I didn't have a car, that was all the exposure to Asian food I had (other than during Thanksgiving and Christmas.. yum, turkey and kimchi).

At the time I was kickin it real big in Mountain View, another mecca of Korean food. Ok, that time there really was a Korean restaurant on Castro St. (which was later replaced by a Mexican restaurant and which I now think is the Chinese restaurant Ki-Rin), but there really was very little Korean food and furthermore, there were no websites like this which would tell me where the heck to go. And I was jonesin for some duiji bulgogi (spicy pork bbq) action.

So I went to Berkeley. I figured, hey, there must be lots of Korean kids there, so I should be able to find some Korean food. And I was right... kinda. 45 minutes drive later, I pulled into town and illegally parked in one of the UC lots and walked back down to.. yeah, you guessed it, the Durant food court. 

To my ethnic-food deprived eyes the food court was a paradise of food options - they had ramen, cheese steaks, pasta, korean bbq, chinese,  sushi and more all in the same cramped area.
