Sure there were overflowing trash cans and dirty stone tables covered with fly infested refuse but hey, it's no Hanover NH.

I saw some kids digging into plastic containers full of rice and what vaguely resembled bulgogi and kimchi. "Where'd you get that?" I asked hungrily. They gestured towards the back. I started smelling the greasy smoke about 10 feet later. I ducked in and saw a huge line and possibly one of the scariest looking grill surfaces ever. Actually it's only in my 20/20 hindsight that it looks scary; at the time it looked like heaven.

I ordered the duiji bulgogi, which took me about 10 minutes to get. It mostly tasted like... the grill it was cooked on. The kimchi.. I don't even know what it was. I think it was made from regular cabbage and not napa cabbage (i.e. the kind of kimchi you get from some Chinese places) and was lukewarm and sour (probably from being stored right next to the grill). I grabbed a ketchup bottle full of kochujang (the Korean hot sauce - how appropriate they put it in the ketchup bottle) and squirted it on. Weak sauce.

Still, even this smoky memory evokes a fond response in me. This is the kind of place I would go to once every 10 years as a kind of pilgrimage to remind me of my roots and how far I've come. Which reminds me, my 10 year anniversary in the Bay Area is coming up next year... anyone want some ghetto korean bbq? 

I can only imagine how much scarier the grill has gotten in the last 9 years...

FIVE STARS. 

(cuz if i don't my mom will kill me...my mama's best friend's childhood friend runs this joint)

On par with what you'd expect from student budget food, Steve's is A-OK. 

The portions are pretty decent, but the food itself lacks any significant flavor. The crowds of students that flood this place speak for itself though, as Steve's sure is popular. For around $8 I feel like there are much better deals within the Asian Ghetto area itself, especially if you're looking for an Asian inspired meal.

I seriously can't believe there are so many reviews for this place. 

Steve's is not great by any means, though if you want some kalbi or daeji bulgogi, you don't have many other options in the area. It's cheap. It's sketchy. There are meat and eggs sitting out. The place is kind of dirty and grimy. You will walk away with the standard korean bbq smell. It comes with rice. It will also come with the worst kimchee I've ever tasted. No spice to it. Very soggy. 

Yet I still come back and haven't been sick yet!

I've never met Steve's of Steve's BBQ but if I did, I'd like to shake his hand and thank him for feeding me during my 4 year stint at Cal. 

Sure it's not "real" Korean food, sure "real" Koreans don't cook it, but it tastes delicious and you can't go wrong with the ENORMOUS portions they give you. 

My personal favorite here is the Bibimbap. It is STACKED to the brim with vegetables and meat and will feed you for the entire day (granted you don't stuff your face to begin with). 

So if you're hungry and not looking to spend too much on food, come through to Steve's. You'll leave the restaurant full, I guarantee it.

OK so I'm not going to try to say this is a 5-star place but I feel like averaging 2.5 stars is super low and I'm going to try to compensate for reviews that  I don't agree with.  My friend and I got the chateaubrian steak and the fondue ticines.  The fondue ticines was definitely the better one but both were pretty good.  Service was perfect i'd say...the guy was really nice and very attentive.  I suppose what could allow me to truly rate this as a 5 star experience is the fact that I had a restaurant.com coupon and my friend I ate for just around $11 each!! And we were totally stuffed.  Definitely give this place a chance.

similar to what others have mentioned, food is ehh-ok but it's definitely a fun/interesting experience especially with a group of friends. 

food: we got the mexican fondue package with cheese, tortilla chips, potatoes and they give you bread. we also ordered side of veggies and shrimp. the cheese was really good and it def goes well with the veggies. potatoes were esp well cooked. the bread was good with the cheese but i felt overall, it was poor quality bread that has been sitting for a few days. didn't taste fresh. there were def a lot left over of the bread and chips. 
chocolate fondue - chocolate was good and it goes well with fruits and marshmallows. 

service was a bit slow bc there are only 2 ppl working. 

overall, it's fun with friends but it's a bit pricey so i'd recommend getting the restaurant.com coupon if u wanna come here. otherwise, it's better to just get a fondue set urself and try with friends.

i went to fondue Fred's for a girl friends birthday there was 25 of us. the setting is very cute almost like ur eating in a ally not a restaurant, however our dinning experience was horrible it was over priced for what we got. the waiter maybe came to the table 2 times. didn't seem to forget about us, but just flat out ignored us. refills for get a bout it! the food was not fulfilling at all and very hard to share with a large group. there are set menus for large groups witch is very help full however the price quoted was not the price charged. not even close!the tip was included in the bill, but they did not give prompt service and did not deserve a tip at all. to top it off after spending like 45 dollers a person on a veggies, bread, and a pot of stew with a few chunks of meat in it...we stoped at jack in the box on the way home!maybe a group of 4 would be better but i wont be going back to try and find out!
So gross, never again.  Maybe their desserts aren't  bad, I wouldn't know, I was terrified to order any after terrible food we had for dinner.  This place gives fondue a bad name.

I was completely amazed by this place, honestly. It was really good and for the price, you really can't beat it. We tried two cheese and the steak as well as some chocolate and all of it was amazing. If you are looking for velvetta style cheese, this is it not for you. If you love cheese and chocolate I highly recommend this over Melting Pot any day. But hey, if you are the kind of person the craves the high end experience, this is not for you. If you want a fun night out with friends and even the kids this is the right place for you.

It was my birthday so I decided to celebrate with 20 of my closest friends at Fondue Fred. Granted, the service was a little lacking but it was forgiveable considering the size of our party.

After realizing that our group was serious about getting our money's worth, they were pretty consistent about bringing out our grub and libations. We opted for the party package at $26, which gets you salad, all-you-can eat of 5 fondue's (they brought an additional one which was just meh. stick with cheese only), bread, veggies, potatoes, a chocolate fondue with strawberries and marshmallows and wine. 

Not the most stellar fondue, but it's probably the best for the cost. Also, great for accomodating large groups. We had a great time! 3.5
I've been going to Fondue Fred for over 20 years & absolutely adore their food. It's a great spot for largish parties as well as intimate dinners. The atmosphere is casual & relaxed.

Cheese, meat, fresh fruit, chocolate, wine - what's not to love? Just went for a birthday party and highly recommend the "party rate" which includes plenty to satiate your friends' dipping and drinking desires. We seemed to agree that the Gouda fondue was the best. Just be sure to save room for the chocolate! The outdoor seating is the best, especially when it's summer. The staff were very friendly, though we seemed to go through the wine faster than they could refill it.
Very friendly and a very fun venue for our 11 year old daughter's birthday party!!

EIW I can't believe I haven't yelped this yet. My friends and I were really excited to go there and try it, but it was soooo disappointing.  Not even the chocolate fondue was that good...and how can you go wrong with chocolate?  

I get that the idea of cheese fondue is to make use of stale bread, and they really take it to heart. It was the most disgusting, stale bread I've ever had. I wouldn't even feed it to the ducks at Lake Merritt, it was that bad.

It seems cheaper than most places, but you get what you pay for. For real fondue, go to La Fondue in Saratoga instead.  I don't like the chain Melting Pot much more, but even that is better than Fred's.

THIS IS NOT FONDUE!!!  We made the mistake of not checking out Yelp! prior to stumbling in to this lousy excuse for a fondue restaurant.  Guess it serves us right.  The last fondue place we enjoyed was The Melting Pot and when you've had real fondue cooked at your table, it's kind of a joke to even try this place.  Crunchy water salad (aka iceburg lettuce salad mix with little purple bits of cabbage and carrot mixed right from a bag) with an indistinguishable vinaigrette was followed by an "Asiago cheese" fondue (hard to call it that) melted with some wine, too hot, broken and separated, accompanied by a bunch of cubes of bread.  If we hadn't been really hungry, we would have left it.  The biggest let down was the "Chateaubriand" fondue (again, hard to call it fondue).  This was much more like Beef Bourguignonne with one mushroom (and I mean one cap and one stem), a pot of tasty brown gravy and some chunks of last night's steak leftovers.  The best part about this whole meal was the GIANT Hefeweizen the kind gentleman that ran the place brought me, twice.  I can't say it was the worst place I've ever been, but I can definitely say it was the biggest $50 let down I've had since I moved to the Bay Area over 2 years ago.  Really nice guy, I mean I hate to rag on it b/c he was so nice, but if he was really nice he would serve FONDUE!!  Maybe he should change the place to "Melted Mel's Cheese Shop & Braise 'em Bob's BBQ." Then I would have known what I was in for from the beginning.

Tucked away in a little, old, and slightly grungy courtyard on Telegraph ave near Cal is this quaint little fondu restaurant.  I am sure, years ago when fondu was the latest and greatest, this place used to be filled to the brim nightly.  However last night it was empty, and we were able to be seated immediately, given we were the only ones in the place!

I believe for the most part, I bought service last night.  The fondu was ok.  I came with a small group and we got one Gouda and one Cinnamon Swiss fondu.  The Gouda was really good and went well with a glass of their house Merlot!  The Gouda fondu has a nice buttery-nutty flavor, although the texture was a little disturbing.  It was a little grainy and chunky, and I couldn't figure out if that was from the calcium deposits in Gouda cheese, or something else...?  The Swiss fondu was utterly unbearable, but then, i'm really not a fan of Swiss cheese (since I think it has no flavor and a horribly thick, stringy texture) so i'm not exactly an impartial judge on the topic.  The server was beyond helpful and accommodating and appeasing, and apologize profusely when we complained about the Swiss Fondu, and immediately took it off our check, so five stars to him!

The chocolate fondu was amazing, but really, how can one screw up chocolate?!  I do wish there was a little bit more of a variety of fruit to dip or more strawberries- either way.

It wasn't such a horrible experience that I wouldn't come back to fill my fondu need, but I certainly will look for better alternatives, which I have been told can be found in both San Rafael and San Francisco.

I have been coming here for years and love this place and the owner. They served us all the food, wine and brew that we could down in a sitting. Great place for a party, just call and let them know ahead of time or there could be a bit of a wait(the place is pretty popular on the weekends) Great for the kids

Service at this place is horrible.  Sure the waiter/owner(?) was friendly enough when he showed us to our table, but then we hardly saw him the rest of the night.  It was like pulling teeth trying to get our orders taken and to get the check.  By the end of the night we had spent a good THREE HOURS sitting in this place and there were only a few other tables there so it's not like they were too busy!  

We mostly came here to try the chocolate fondue, so I was looking forward to enjoying that after having the savory fondues we had for dinner (which were mediocre).  But after waiting for what felt like an hour for the chocolate fondue to arrive, we were so sick of waiting in this place that my boyfriend actually got up to look for the only waiter in this place and CANCEL OUR CHOCOLATE FONDUE ORDER.  We had rather cancel our only reason for coming to this place in the first place just to GTFO of there.

Never again.  Avoid this place.

Service was HELLA slow. I remember coming in with eight of my friends and we were seated immediately and everything but we waited a good 30-40 min for our food to come. Don't leave hungry college students hungry! We ordered Cheddar and Gouda fondue, a plate of fresh apples, a plate of shrimp and vegetables, potatoes, their tortellini cheese pasta, and a chocolate fondue to top it off. The Cheddar had a little too much wine for my taste but my friends enjoyed it. I did like the smoky gouda with the nice array of vegetables and shrimp. The tortellini was also very good. My favorite part of the meal was the chocolate fondue! I loved dipping the marshmallows and strawberries and bananas. And I had fun roasting my marshmallows. But I agree with the other yelpers - its better to make your own fondue! The place has a nice ambience and its really cute - kind of tucked away for the faux Swiss experience. I'm giving it two stars because of the long wait and the $10 minimum per person. And the fact you really can buy all of this food at Berkeley Bowl/Trader Joes/Safeway.

Came with a party of five. Had  the party combo of 5 different fondues. I recommend  the steak and 5 cheese. And then the chocolate for dessert. I believe the fondue is all you can eat so you really don't need to order much. It's a small place and we went on a Thursday night and our service was great. I will totally go again but not order as much.

Really cozy

Owner is extremely nice and generous. You can ask for seconds and even thirds for bread.

There is a minumum per person though

I had the steak and chicken pots

If you are even remotely interested in fondue or trying out something a little different (if you aren't then why are you here?)...  then you need to try out Fondue Fred.  Eating in the middle of the courtyard area is an interesting experience in itself.  The owners are super friendly and the food is generally great.  Here is the main selling point: if you get a group of 6 or more to go, then it is $20/each for all you can eat fondue (except for the chocolate fondue, i believe) AND all you can drink wine.  Granted, they aren't cracking $100 bottles and i am pretty sure that they wine comes out  of a bladder, but for that price, you can have one hell of an experience!

I have to say I'm really shocked at the amount of bad reviews for this place!  My friends and I had a totally different dining experience than most of these folks. 

Anyways - we went to Fondue Fred for my birthday - my friends chose the restaurant and none of us had been there, so we were looking forward to trying it.  We had excellent service from the start - the waiter went out of his way to accommodate us with extra chairs, and asked if we had more guests coming and needed another table.  Once we got settled in, we selected 3 cheese fondues for 7 of us - PLENTY of food.    We ordered the garlic, five cheese and fiesta fondues and an order of fresh vegetables.  The cheese was definitely high quality cheese, and well flavored.  Fresh, toasted bread, seasoned potatoes and crunchy fresh vegetables were the perfect dippers.  There were still left-overs at the end of the meal - and trust me - we can all eat!  
The waiter was extremely attentive - and even offered a pitcher of soda rather than individual sodas for our table. He brought us new plates after our salad course and also a set of fresh fondue forks and plates for our dessert course. They even brought out a piece of cheesecake and sang happy birthday to me. 
The chocolate fondue was excellent - and I used to work for a chocolate factory - so trust me when I say that.  A huge plate of fresh fruits and marshmallows were brought out, and the waiter even left two of the sternos burning so that we could toast our marshmallows.  
All in all - a great social dining experience and great food!

Who doesn't love fondue?  It's fun to eat and tasty as well.  The indoor courtyard setting is cool enough, and when added to a pot of bubbling cheese it adds up to a night of endless fun and excitment.

although i have never had fondue before this place was good. the place was all and cozy  but it was really cold in the restaurant. my bf and i ordered Salami Parmesan fondue and the steak. although it was good the steak was kinda like  a stew. it was good non the less. they fondue was good it came with potato and good french bread. we also got the mushrooms.
My personal  favorite jumping-off point for Girls' Night Out.  I've enjoyed the meal every time I've gone.  Wine, chocolate, cheese, and lots of fun.  What else could girls ask for?

Ok, I totally enjoy Fondue Fred's. I first came here in college, but still come back when I want some great fondue. It's very cozy and reminds me a bit of a cabin, which I like. I usually have always had the same server who is friendly, nice and attentive. The food is great--very generous portions initially, and you can ask for more if needed. The price is also pretty reasonable for fondue and it would be a great place for groups as well. 3 cheers for Fondue Fred's!

Came here on friday and had the gouda cheese fondue and the chocolate fondue. The cheese fondue was good as was the bread. The potatoes had far too much paprika and were overcooked but cold. Also cold was the restaurant! My friend and I had to put our jackets back on because it was just as cold in the restaurant as it was outside!
The chocolate fondue was ok. The fruit was great, but the marshmallows were stale.

Overall the food was ok but I can't say that I was terribly impressed by the ambience or wowed enough by the food to actually care to go back.

I have reservations about recommending this place. On one hand,  the twinkling courtyard, festoooned with Christmas lights and heat lamps. On the other hand, the blah factor: there is NO way they are using real Gruyere, most of the cheeses taste cheap/the same, and the raw vegetables are strictly Costco variety. Still, the all-you-can-eat option includes limitless carafes of cheap red and white wine. So... if you don't mind an almost guaranteed hangover the next day, go for it. It all depends on your priorities. 
The two times I've gone here with friends, we had fun - with one MAJOR caveat. The rage-aholic guy who runs the place. The first time I went, he shamelessly came on to my brother's girlfriend ("Ohhh... you have beautiful eyebrows... tell me, are you Persian? Ohhh... "), and the last time, he practically threw my (sick) brother out for showing up late and declining to eat ("Oh, so you are not eating?! Just going to drink, eh? So, you are feeling sick, heh? And you will not eat?!!"). It took us a minute to realize that the reason we were being harrassed was that the dude thought my brother was going to scam a meal without paying the $25 all-you-can-eat-and-drink fee. Totally insulting and unacceptable.
(FYI the place is owned by the same folks who run Chester's at Cedar and Vine. That establishment is very well-run and the food is terrific. But then, I have never seen psycho-dude there.)

This place is definitely a solid 3.  Nothing wrong with the place, but I don't think that a pot of cheese and bread is worth making everyone order $10 per person at the table........ I dunno that's just me.

I would go here again if it was with a large group I guess and we wanted to socialize.  The fiesta fondue was my favorite.  Bell peppers, mushrooms and melted cheese.  AND you got tortilla chips to scoop up the delicious melty cheese.  I love love love!   I don't even remember the rest!   

hm.... Maybe I will go back with my friends soon.  I love melted cheese..

This place is okay if you manage your expectations.  (Or if you don't have any, I suppose).  My very first fondue restaurant experience was La Fondue in Saratoga... followed up by the Melting Pot (in Larkspur).  So coming to Fondue Fred's after those two experiences was a huge disappointment.  But this place is also about 1/2 of the cost.

As others have mentioned the service is extremely slow.  It is one guy managing the entire restaurant.  On average, it takes about 2 hours to get  through a meal here (including salad, cheese + dessert fondue)  The salad sucks (but are you really coming here for salad anyway???).  The cheese is okay, but not high quality.  Out of three cheese options, I thought all but the garlic were kind of bland.  You only get bread and potato's with your meal, but you can pay extra for more options (apples, shrimp - all pricey in my opinion.  $5 for apples, REALLY?!?).  The chocolate fondue is very good, but the dippers suck.  You get a ton of melon, with some marshmallows and very minimal amounts of strawberries and banana's (which come on, that's what you want to put your chocolate on!)  Despite the bread continually being refilled, we ran out of dessert dippers and got cut off.  No refills on melon or marshmallows, people!

The best part about this place is the price tag... $28 per person (and I was full but not overly stuffed).  Fondue Fred's is good enough in a pinch, but I'd much rather just make the drive to the Melting Pot for quality fondue with excellent service.
Fondue Fred's fondue is pretty good. Fondue Fred's employees - not so pretty good. In fact, they were down-right somber.
I hear a lot of people talk down on this place, but I love it. I love the Swiss dude and his dry sence of humor, I like the wine and I love the fondu! I will come back!

I like this place. It doesn't knock your socks off but it's great for large groups. They get  the fourth star for their all you can eat special of under 30 bucks. Pay for your bill at The Melting Pot once and you'll know what I mean.

   I've had a few get togethers here. It's a great setting for a large group and the more people you have the more fondue you get to try. I like to dip the mixed veggies, potatoes, and apples more than the bread. The ultimate dessert is the chocolate fondue; especially when you toast your marshmallow in the burner and then dunk it in the chocolate ;)

This is a great place to drink and eat, in the entertaining evening sense.  Yes it's boxed wine and yes it's not the best fondue to write home about.  But it's good enough and the decor is chill and relaxed.  But the bottom line is eating cheese and bread and getting drunk for $26 with friends is always a winner in my book.

It was our first visit to Fondue Fred's, and a Restaurant.com certificate made it a reasonably priced meal.  The owner was very friendly and joked with all, but seemed to be handling a lot of early Saturday night responsibilities and we did not see him much after he brought our wine and salads.  My daughter loved her melon salad with two giant marshmallows, but we did not feel the same about our small side salads.  We ordered the Cinque Formaggio cheese fondue, Chateaubrian steak cheese-less fondue and a side of shrimp and veggies.  I really don't understand the complaints about a $10/person minimum.  This is a small restaurant, and they can not afford to have tables taken up with four college students sharing one pot of fondue.  If you don't want to spend $10 on dinner out, stick to the dollar menu at fast food chains or try Sweet Tomatoes.  We enjoyed the cheese fondue, and the french bread and roasted red potatoes with it were a tasty dip, but we were very glad to have ordered the veggies to give us some non-starch variety (would skip the shrimp next time).   We expected the cheese-less fondue to be us cooking the meat in oil, as we done at other fondue restaurants, but it was a ready to eat stew of steak and mushrooms with a few veggies dropped on top.  It had a nice flavor, but really could have been any inexpensive cut of stew meat in this preparation.  We had a half carafe of house Cabernet, as the branded wine bottles seemed to be marked up 3x-4x store retail.  Our expectations for it were low, but we hoped for a Cab with a little bite to cut through the cheese.  It was a very soft and generic red wine, so maybe a better option is to bring a bottle and pay the $10 corkage.  We did not have time for dessert, and were sorry to miss out on chocolate fondue.  My daughter enjoyed the fondue experience, and so did we.  Yes, you can easily do this at home, but if you have plans to be out in the Berkeley area with friends and are looking for a fun, social dining experience, grab a Restaurant.com certificate and give Fred's a try.

This place was good for groups and I rather liked the all you can eat /all you can drink wine special. I noticed they filled us up on bread pretty quickly. All in all it was just okay but for 15 it was probably more accommodating than other restaurants would be.

I'm in Berkeley visiting my boyfriend and his best friend has wanted to go to fondue for awhile.  I intentionally, did not go to the melting pot in Pasadena when the BF visited me so that we could all do fondue together here at Fondue Freds.
We gather together our group of 6 planning to have the all you can drink wine.  I called to find out how it works, how late they are open and if we need a reservation.  They are open 'til 10:00  it's Thursday, the earliest we can get everyone together is 9:00 (I know, not the best way to take advantage of all you can drink but it's what works for everyone).  I ask if we need a reservation, the guy on the phone says no but since there's 6 of us and we're coming so late, he takes down my name and number and asks me to call if there's a change of plans.  
Me and my 5 friends arrive at 9:00 and this place is totally closed, shut down with no sign of life.  Seriously, that sucks, that's no way to run a business stay open during your posted hours.  Oh and you could've called me since you obviously had a change of plans.
Absolutely love this place for so many reasons, atmosphere, food and cheep for all you get. It's a wonderful place to celebrate special occasions, birthdays or just because.

We had a fantastic experience here! We were a large group of about 20 people including children. I loved their Parmesan fondue and Asiago fondue. I also tried the traditional fondue, that has a lighter, less interesting flavor but was good for children, as the owner suggested. The fondues came with bread, veggies, and perfectly cooked potatoes. I am not into chocolate fondue but their chocolate fondue was also really delicious and came with fruit and marshmallows. 

Compared to other fondue restaurants I tried, in the U.S. and in Europe, this is one of the best. The menu is very creative and has a lot of options. The athmosphere is cozy, the price more than reasonable and the service was great. I read in other reviews that it is cold there but we ate outside under the heating lamps and the temperature was fine.

O.k. so my friend had a coupon to this place so we decided to try it. We loved the look of the "outside patio area" if that's what you want to call it. Unfortunately we were stuck inside where it looks like it was decorated with 70's thrift store crap. O.k. so on to the food. Not bad, but I thought when you do fondue you cook it yourself at the table. I thought the original cheese fondue was really really good. The dessert fondue was good too. It's worth going their once just for a fun experience.

My 1st time here was good and the place felt like a great place to drink some beer. So i order the, "Huge" $8 glass of beer(samuel adams)  it was huge! But I wouldn't come here again because one fondue is $16 and it is just a bowl of potato with a basket of bread plus the cheese fondue or whatever fondue you order. The chocolate fondue was just a plate of marshmallow,melon,strawberries,pineapple, and plus the chocolate  for $18 and there's nothing fancy about it. They just throw it on a plate like all the other reviewer said! It's tastes good, but it's like something you can make at home. Well, all fondue is $16-$18. That is just not worth it, but it is a good experience for first timers or for their beer.

( I used restaurant.com gift certificate and got $25 off my bill.)

We had a lovely anniversary dinner last night at Fondue Fred.  I'm surprised by the other comments, but like all places/people in the service industry, sometimes even restaurants have off-days.  

We ordered Fondue Ticines (#9) which came with salad, potatoes and bread.  We added a side of veggies.  Sure, the salad was garden variety but what do you expect from a $17 fondue for two?  The portions of bread and potatoes were gigantic - could have easily fed 3-4 with one order.  We barely got through half of our entree fondue because we wanted to save room for dessert.  The chocolate fondue was equally as delicious.  We could tell the chocolate was of good quality - it tasted rich and dark, not like some cheap brand of milk chocolate.  With 1 glass of wine, 1 soda, 1 entree and 1 dessert fondue (which left us bursting at the seams), we were out the door for about $50.  That's pretty good!

The service was just fine.  Our waiter was friendly and checked on us often.  When he went on break, the restaurant owner took over our table and was equally as friendly and attentive.  

We will definitely return to Fondue Fred!

I could just say it's ok, this is the first time trying fondue
We ordered the classic fondue. It's fun, but the cheese here is not creamy enough, the bread is good.  
We didn't order the chocolate fondue, but it looks really nice

For a first time fonduer, I thought it was pretty good. Who can complain about fatty, gooey, goodness on a stick, right?

My favorite cheese fondue was the gouda.  Not sharp, but mild in flavor. The Cinque Fromage was ok, but I preferred the gouda. Also had a meatball fondue, which was just like meatballs simmering in tomato, wine sauce. All you needed was pasta and you had a hearty spaghetti. My suggestion is that you dip your bread into your cheese, then skewer a meatball and eat it together. Tastes like a pizza. 

The dessert fondue was ok. It was chocoate fondue with a serving of fruit and marshmellows. Oh and if you go to their website, print out the coupon and you get it for free if you order 3 entree fondues.  Be sure to print it out. I saved a image of it on my phone and gave it to the server. She let it slide, but she said they are getting strict and that you need to have a print out of the coupon.

The food is amazing. The cheese fondue is great, and there is enough to share with a few people. The chocolate fondue is great, and seems like it would be fun to share among friends and family. I love cheese and chocolate, which both makes me bias and also picky,  but I can honestly say both were fantastic. Also the garlic bread is very fresh!
The ambiance is cute and cozy, and the owner is very nice. 
Truly an enjoyable food experience.

Do not, I repeat, DO NOT go to Fondue Freds.  I heart fondue including The Melting Pot and was excited when I got a Restaurant.com certificate worth $25 for only 2 bucks.  

After a less than stellar cheese fondue with stale bread sliced so big I couldn't easily fit peices in my mouth, boiled potatoes and raw veggies (my bad for ordering raw veggies with cheese foudue I guess) I was hoping for a kick butt chocolate ending.  Nope, just regular old chocolate melted in a pot.  A few strawberries (YUM!) were accompanied by pineapple (yes), apples (ok) and canteloupe and honeydew melon (come on, these fruits do not accompany chocolate well and I know they are cheap plate fillers).  

The only upside was that we got to roast our marshmellows over an open steno.  

Price: (with two alc. beverages) $58 AFTER $25 coupon.  Rip off.  

PS Service was also pretty scarce.

Wanted to check this out after watching a show on Food Network about fondue.  This is a cute little place and I can see how it can be fun if you and a bunch of girlfriends got together here, like the large party of loud women that were dining there while we were there.  They were so loud that we couldn't hear each other.

The fondue was okay, a little bit too much on the liquid side, but maybe that's how fondue is supposed to be?  I imagined having ribbons of cheese after you dip the bread and swirl the cheese around it (like what we saw on Food Network).  We had the garlic fondue, which was a bit bitter (burnt garlic?) and the gouda fondue.  I recommend the latter.  I like my cheese strong, so I'll have to try the blue cheese fondue next time.  It's fun for little kids as they can roast marshmallows right from the table and dip it in the chocolate fondue.  

I will try this place again, but this time I'll bring all of my loud girlfriends.....ha!

We spent the night here as a family and it was so much fun!!  I can't really imagine being a consistent customer here because it is:

1.  probably not worth the busride from Alameda
2.  a very heavy meal 
3.  pretty expensive considering what comes out 

The food is good, it's just priced like a gourmet meal when it doesn't really taste that way.  Dude, though, the service was great.  Don't get me wrong.  We thoroughly enjoyed every goddamn minute we spent in here (the outdoor mall seating was actually suprisingly pleasant and the family style service was perfect for the occasion!!).  

If you haven't been to Fondue, this may be a great place to start.  Consider it like Fondue 101.  After one visit, consider yourself a graduate.  Now you can go on to greener and stinkier melting pots in the greater bay area...

Next time, I'll bring a date and order less to save room for dessert...

Me and my husband had our wedding reception at Fondue Fred 4 years ago. It is a perfect place to have a small celebration. I love fondue and they offer many different kind, like garlic, champagne, Parmesan etc. and their service is excellent. We always go back there to celebrate our wedding anniversary and our birthdays. And we usually get free wine!
I would highly recommend this place to anyone!

Well I love fondue. All fondue. So it should come as no surprise that I loved this fondue. 

That said, something about this place seemed cheap. The bread was not that good, the cheeses were probably fresh out of Costco and I'm pretty sure the 1/2 carafe of Cabernet we ordered was Two Buck Chuck from Trader Joes.

As for the service, maybe the owners read some of the scathing reviews here and changed their attitude, or maybe they just decided to be nice 'cuz it was Valentine's day, but we had a lovely waiter and no bad things to say about that.

Oh, and if you go there, be aware it's RIGHT next to the Berkeley campus and you will be surrounded by college kids. Nothing wrong with that, just an FYI.

BTW, be sure to go to the bathroom and ask for the big red ladle that has the key on it. Hillarious!

The delicious and smooth semi-sweet chocolate fondue with marshmallows and fruits made up for the rest of the experience.

EXTREMELY slow service. Took us 45 minutes to get our food, and the rest of the dinner went equally slowly, despite the fact that we were one of 3 parties in the whole restaurant. Cheese was a bit gritty, but the overall flavor was pleasant and mild (for the Garlic and Fiesta fondues). The Chicken Tortellini fondue was was savory and tasty (wine and butter sauce), but the chicken itself was dry and difficult to chew. The bread for dipping would have been better toasted and warm, but the vegetables were good (had to pay extra for them).

Overall, it's a decent first-time experience if you've never had fondue, but I wouldn't return over and over again.

It was my floormate's birthday and the owner was very nice to us, but honestly - the quality of this place wasn't that great.  The bread, for one: it was like large hunks of Safeway baguette that had been left in the bag for two days, and the crust was all wimpy.  This isn't really acceptable when there's such a live bread scene in this area.  I'm a super bread-snob, so this was especially disappointing.  Dipping it into the fondue pushed it into palatability, and well - white bread that you don't want to eat on its own is pretty bad.  And the "cheese fondue" was more of a salty cream fondue than a cheese fondue (skimping on the cheese?).

 And then the $10/person part was pretty lame, too.  Really sorry, nice-owner-guy :/.

It is always a pleasure to dine at Fondue Fred.  The people are very nice and the fondue is good. Tonight, there were 8 of us and the service was great, the food was great, and most of all, the wine carafes were never empty!

I had my first fondue experience ever at Fred's.  The food was pretty good, the gouda is DELICIOUS! The chocolate fondue with the fruit and marsh mellows was my absolute favorite. HOWEVER, the service SUCKED...we were at the restaurant for over 2 hours total. Most of that time was waiting for our food...if you're looking for a fast place to eat, don't go here. Also, make sure to check that your plates are clean. Luckily I checked mine before eating and it had a large amount of dust/dirt on it....

I went here once with some people and I ordered this chicken dish which had mushrooms and vegetables in it and was more like a soup. It was really tasty. The other people ordered different cheese fondues and they really liked it but I thought it tasted a little bitter or something. I must say that they give you huge servings; we were not able to finish everything. I was a little put off by how dirty the wine glasses, cups and silverware were. I had scrape food particles out of my cup. And the chairs were really uncomfortable. My boyfriend switched with me because I felt like I was falling out of my chair. I think the floor was also slanted where we were too. And they could definitely make the tables bigger. It was kind of crammed with 3 pots on burners on the table. We had a restaurant.com gift certificate and even with that this place seemed a little expensive. It is kind of cool and was a fun experience and the food and wine was good, but they need to fix their dishwasher or something because that was kinda gross.

Super delicious! The staff was very friendly and laid back.  I went with my three kids and they were very friendly to them and welcoming! I thoroughly enjoyed myself. I recommend it and will go again! Especially with the restaurant.com gift certificate!

We had the quince fromaggio and the Parmesan classic! We ordered a side of mushrooms and shrimp.  Then we had the chocolate fondue dessert.  We were all stuffed and very pleased!

After getting disappointed with melting pot, we'd stopped going for fondue completely. Until we discovered Fondue Fred. Setting is interesting, with lots of college kids hanging around. They have a nice outdoor seating. We tried cheese fondue, which was ok. But the chocolate fondue was amazing, lots of fruits.

The first place I ever had fondue...  It was pretty good, and I was on a date with my girlfriend there.  The location and all was only subpar, though, and the only difference between most dishes (it wasn't this way at The Melting Pot) was what could get dipped.

Nice enough place, but The Melting Pot kicks its ass.

I really like Fondue Fred's. Is it the best fondue ever? Maybe not but it's good.  The staff is friendly, the atmosphere is fun, and it's great for groups. I have gone as a party of 2 and as a party of more than 6. 

Most recently I went with myself and one other person:
We shared the Chili Pepper Fondue and add a side of mushrooms. It is plenty of food( as the fondue comes with red potatoes and bread).  I have never had a problem with the freshness of vegetables, and  this time the mushrooms were bright white. That came to $27.15  with tip, that's a pretty good meal for 2 and not really too expensive.  I have to say though we are very portion minded people, most restaurants give way too much ( 2-3x what you should eat) so I'm much happier with restaurants that give more real portion sizes like Fondue Fred's, one pot is plenty to share for 2. 

The group parties of 6 of more are always fun you get 5 of the basic fondue's to try, chocolate fondue and unlimited wine for I think $26 a person, and they never make you rush or kick you out.  The parties I have been too everyone drinks more than $26 in wine a person, so it's a great deal.  I've never had a problem with my reservations and I've made them on a few different occasions. 

Usually you can find a coupon on their website for a party of 5 or under too.  

This is someplace I keep going back too, but when I want something a little better quality ( and pricier) I go to the Melting Pot in Larkspur.

3.5 stars
3 of us got there around 5:30. There were about 4 other tables occupied. Sat ourselves in the 'courtyard' area. Ordered meatball, 5 cheese, shrimp and veggies & garlic bread. 
Got the salad right away (that comes with order, along with red potatoes).
The salad & potatoes were fine. Really enjoyed the 5-cheese. 
The meatballs were good and hot. Unsure of what were supposed to do with the veggies because they were all raw. Waiter took them and brought back steamed. Which tasted good. Had a lot of garlic bread leftover. 
Overall, enjoyed the meal, although if we go again, will probably forgo the shrimp and veggies & garlic bread. 
There was only 1 waiter, but the service was not slow. 
We skipped the dessert and went to C.R.E.A.M. instead ;)
With the $25 coupon, we each paid $15, with drinks, tax & tip.

You know, for what you get and what you pay, it's really a decent place! The other fondue places are just a bit much, you know? Cost, amount of food... K and I just wanted the cheese fondue and of course, chocolate fondue to top us off. 

Had the Gouda fondue and the chocolate fondue for dessert. Both were pretty good. Loved how dessert comes w/ an extra flame for *roasting* marshmallows. 

Only drawback of the place that I have found so far, and I've been dining occasionally at Fred's for years, is that it's usually cold in there. I gotta remember next time to bring a sweater.

BLAHH my Boyfriend sam and i went here last night because i had a restaurant's gift card. got here.. had to order 50$ to get 25 off so we ordered two cheeses and garlic bread and chocolate the cheeses came 45 min down the road.. it was really good the first few bites. i suppose because we were so hungry... they gave us stale bread and blan potatoes. that's it?? after we couldn't take anymore. i asked our waiter whom was the only onoe working there if we could get our chocolate because we needed to be some wear.. which he looked like he totally understood until a half hour later the coco late came out and we were presented with a plate of sliced bananas strawberry's and red apples... oh and four marsh mellows. SAM took the first bite as i was trying to roast my mellow over a candle... he had a very odd look on his face and promptly requested that i try it because it had a familiar taste.... could it be???? HERSHEY SYRUP!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! warmed of course but defiantly not decadent.... as he brought the tab it was 45$ he hadded on 18% gratuity.. anyway... gross place never coming back i loooovvveee the melting pot go there. all the people on here that say its good....have no taste buds and low standers.

Its hard not to like melted cheese, and the fondues themselves are very good. I wish the peripherals were better - fresher more interesting dippables, salad with real dressing, etc. Basically its a good casual place, and I would rather they take it to a higher level.

I was certainly disappointed at Fondue Fred. The only thing preventing me from giving it just one star was the funny and polite waiter/cook?/owner? who seemed to be doing everything. The fondue was just not good, I can't say it any other way. We wanted to try a lot so we tried three cheese fondues and a few meat ones. None of them I found appealing, and I actually just ate bread for part of the meal without fondue. Really bad, especially for Berkeley. I suppose if you were a college student at Cal your opinion might be a bit higher, especially since I noted the alcohol selection was extremely cheap - which may bump my rating up higher if I go back and get wasted for very little money.

I would probably give this place 2 stars if I've actually experienced better but since it was my first Swiss fondue experience I can't say that I have. Fondue Fred does not have great fondue though. It was actually quite mediocre for what it was. Our meal started with a complimentary small salad and it came with a tangy dressing that I did not like. We ordered a chateaubrian steak $16, a garlic fondue $16, and a chocolate fondue $14. I think I enjoyed the flavor of the steak fondue the most. The garlic fondue I thought was good when you first bite into it but after you swallow you're left with a wine aftertaste. Some people may like that but I definitely did not. These two fondues came with bread and potatoes. The potatoes I liked but the bread was soft and of low-quality. I saw a yelper here say that they offer nacho chips too. How come we weren't offered any? I liked the chocolate fondue the least. It came with a platter with sliced fruits (apples, bananas, strawberries, cantaloupe, and honey dew) and marshmallows. I found the chocolate too be too bitter and I did not find most of the fruit to go well with the chocolate. What I did find nice was that they had a portable heater running right behind my chair which helped keep us warmer on a cold day. We used a $25 restaurant.com coupon which helped with the meal. I know there are better places for fondue like at the La Fondue or Melting Pot. You'll be paying more for it but not too much more I guess cuz Fondue Fred was not cheap either. The reality of it is that you can easily do fondue at home for way cheaper. I think I may want to do that instead and it would probably taste better too.
Food isn't tasty. Service is spotty. Only reason this gets a 2 star and not a 1 is because it's kind of an experience. On top of that, it isn't a cheap outing either.

If you're looking for something different and have a appetite for some good fondue. Then Fondue Fred's is the place. Its located in on Telegraph in berkeley right across from the Buffallo Exchange. 

The food is REALLY GOOD.... the different chesses, meatballs, sauces, foundue dippings you can imagine. The chocolate fondue
at the end of the meal with strawberrys, marshmellows, is the bomb!
$20 a person to drink all the wine you want! Check this place out! :)

What an embarrassment.

I knew not to expect too much from this place after having read other reviews on here, but I was still itching with curiosity after I came out of eating a somewhat mediocre fill of Ethiopian food just next door. Mulling over a pot of melted cheese sounded like a really good idea to me at the time, especially since it was so cold. Honestly, none of the customers at the time (2 families, a group of about 10 college kids, and a handful of couples inside) looked very happy and I was tempted to ask them if their food reflected their sour expressions. 

I got the $25 off coupon from restaurant.com (recommended by other Yelpers), and it made the experience a bit easier to swallow. (Click http://www.fonduefred.com/menu.html for the list of prices). I've never had fondue before so maybe this might not be a fair review, but I know my food, and everyone who knows me knows I know my food. So in a way, it should be a somewhat-fair review x")

My party of four ordered the classic fondue ($16) and the fiesta cheese fondue ($17). I think I could have made a better classic fondue AND a better fiesta fondue in my own kitchen despite the fact that I was a fondue virgin. The classic cheese fondue was a little gritty, with a hint of bitterness (as if the wine:cheese ratio was off). Fiesta fondue was better but only because we had the disappointing classic cheese fondue to compare it to. We asked for vegetables ($6 for a plate of broccoli, zucchini, cauliflower, carrots, and maybe bell peppers) because I was sick of eating a meal of only carbs and fat. Although the veggies made the meal better, it also made it worse. I stabbed my piece of cauliflower and when I held it up to my face, I SAW TINY SPIDERS AND GNATS SMASHED INTO THE CREVICES. I didn't tell anyone at my table because I didn't want to ruin their already-sorry meal as well. (I tried to take pictures of the insect confetti, but my camera wouldn't focus properly XP)

We all unanimously agreed that the fondues were blah. Really blah. And not worth it. 

We then proceded to dessert fondue ($14) in hopes that it would taste better (I mean, how can you go wrong with melted chocolate?). Our lukewarm chocolate fondue came with a plate of deliciously refreshing Costco fruit salad and a few Jet-Puffed jumbo regular and strawberry-flavored(?) marshmallows. I loved the fruit the most. Costco never disappoints. ^^ The chocolate was a bitter/dark chocolate (not milk) which I thought was pretty smart if you're looking for a more adult palate to satisfy.

Service was okay - not as bad as people said. You could tell that the man meant well and he joked with us, too. He was nice and attentive, and although he wasn't the fastest server, I doubt it was because he was lazy or grumpy. A for effort. :) As I mentioned earlier, our party unanimously agreed that we didn't like the place, and when it came for our server to pick up our check, he asked us, "So, will you be coming back again?" 

I'll leave you fellow Yelpers to answer that question. As for me, I didn't want to disappoint the poor man, so I just shrugged, grinned, and told him, "Maybe!!" as I winced inside thinking about the cheese-covered congregation of spiders and gnats that could have entered my belly that night.

I've never had fondue, and I have to say that my experience here leads me to think I I just don't like fondue!

We ordered 3 dishes and still was not filling. 

I don't like paying $50+ and still leaving hungry!

people always say this place is too pricey for what you get. well...it is. but if you want local fondue, where the hell else are you going to get it? wait...i can answer that: it's pretty easy to make this kind of stuff at home. so my rec is to go with a discount coupon and you'll feel pretty good about it.

Food: 2/5
Service: 3/5
Atmosphere: 4/5
Value: 2/5
Total = 2.75/5

What a disappointment. After reading the reviews, my girlfriend and I didn't have high expectations. And yet, what a disappointment. 

The fondue is of very mediocre quality. Bad quality cheese, with a weird powdery texture..... yuk. The potatoes don't have much taste, some are undercooked. The bread is OK. The wine wasn't so bad for the price. $60 total for 2 was WAY over priced what it is.

Service is good, nothing special but the waiter was friendly. The atmosphere is the highlight of this place. Cute wooden European decoration, it feels like you're eating outside even though you're indoor. Minus 1 star for the horrible slow and pseudo-romantic piano music.

We were checking the place out to maybe have a friend's birthday party there. Now we know we won't...

Fondue? Fondon't. From the name, this joint sounds like a cheap imitation of that famous French cuisine, and that's what it is. Way overpriced--$17 for a pot of fondue that tasted like it was made with swiss cheese from Safeway. And the bread they gave us to dip with? Tasted like cheap white bread from Safeway.

I'm used to fondue restaurants where they give you raw meat that you cook yourself by dipping it in the soup. Here, they basically just gave us a bowl of chicken soup. This was nowhere near as good as other fondue I've had. And the kicker was that when we asked "Fred" (I assume that's who it was ) if he could wrap up two of our fondues, he said, "Uh, do you want it in two separate boxes, or is one okay?" Are you serious? You're pressuring us to mix our two dishes together, just so you can save one box? Sounds like Fred might be in some fon-ancial trouble.

I really hate having to give this place 2 stars but really it's all I can muster. 
I went here a while back and ... we also did the whole group all you can swallow disaster. 
The fondue was runny, the service was just plain weird. The people seemed nice enough... honestly I really wish this place was better than it is.
Please owners of Fundu Fred... get it together. You have a great concept and a good location .... just please get it all worked out.

I don't think I'd ever go back ... and after going to La Fundue in Saratoga... I think I am ruined for all other fondue spots. Damn you La Fondue you WHORE!

I'll keep it short. The food is mediocre. Fondue tastes like cheese from a can, bread is cold and stale, and meatballs taste like Chef Boyardee. 

Dessert Fondue was good and the fruits they served were decent. Wine was also good given the price. 

However service was slow and unresponsive. I had to get up a few times to call the waiter over to get service. Unacceptable. Steer clear, so many other choices in Berkeley to go to then this dump.

My family wanted a fondue meal, so we decided to drive out to Berkeley to use a Restaurants.com gift card. We made a reservation since we had a large group, and were seated immediately which was a plus. 

We decided to order off the party menu (groups of 5 or more) that has unlimited fondue for a set price per person.  We were told that the gift certificate could not be used for the party menu, but after talking to the waiter (who appeared to be the owner),  he said he would help us out and took our gift card. 

It took an hour and a half to get our first 5 pots of cheese and meat. The food was ok; the meat is not your typical fondue - its like a pre cooked stew but no spoon or anything to serve it with.  There also was not enough bread and stuff to dip in the cheese. We finished and asked for one more pot of cheese since we were paying for unlimited refills.  

After an hour of waiting for our second pot of cheese, a member of our party went up to find the waiter who had been actively avoiding our table (he came to our table to take our order,  deliver the first pot of food and once more after we had been done for awhile.  He never asked to see if we were doing ok or anything).  The waiter said the cook was working on our order and that the kitchen had been slammed.  Almost all of the tables were open,  and when our party member looked back at the kitchen there was only one guy who was cooking and eating while he was making our food.  The food came out in another 20 minutes (an hour and 20 minutes total)  and was lukewarm and had absolutely NOTHING to dip in it. He brought the chocolate at the same time, which was not great (we ended up going to CREAM down the street for dessert which was great and very inexpensive). 

When we finally got our bill,  he had charged us full price and an 18% tip.  We tried to talk to him, but he kept our gift card and didn't give us any discount. In the end we gave up since we are never coming back to use the gift card even if he gave it back. Terrible experience, but luckily the company was great!

I've always wanted to try this place, and since I had a restaurant.com coupon, I figured that even if it blows, at least I didn't pay full price.

It definetely blew.  The server was attentive when we first got there, but as soon as he came by with a pitcher of water with no glasses, it pretty much went down hill from there.  We had to flag the server down each time we needed something.  There was this super large party (20 people probably) at the table next to us, but I don't think that's any excuse to neglect your other customers.  Especially when catering to large parties seem to be part of their business.  Hire more help is my tip.

We ordered the 5 cheese fondue, and the steak fondue.  It was mediocre at best.  The steak fondue just tasted like watered down soup.  I wanted to add salt and pepper.  The 5 cheese fondue was really thick and tasted so stronly of wine that I had to stop eating it.  And this is coming from a cheese addict.  It broke my heart that I couldn't continue eating the cheese.  There was just something lacking in the dish...ah yes, the taste of cheese.  I swear, I thought I was just eating chunks of solidified wine.

We asked for the food to go, and the server only packed the fondue dishes.  He did not bother packing up the side dish we ordered, or the bread and potatoes that it comes with.  We had to ask for everything to be packed up, which I think is ridiculous.

Since we had a coupon, the server took the liberty of including the suggested tip amount, which he calculated post-tax, and which I don't think he deserved.  

I really wanted to like this place, as I love cheese!  I might give this place another try...maybe the 5 cheese fondue is supposed to have a strong wine taste??  I guess we shall find out...

So - I've seen this place almost every time I have visited Berkeley and I have always wanted to try it.  Something about the courtyard setting and the social aspect of fondue was most appealing.  Today, we spontaneously decidied to go to Berkeley for some shopping and people watching.  My friends were gracious enough to go eat at the place I suggested.  Thus, we found ourselves seated at Fondue Fred, a cozy little restaurant tucked a little ways back from Telegraph in that cute little courtyard.  I found the owner (who waited on us and prepared our food) to be most pleasant.  She was more than accomodating and we thought the food was just fine for what it is.  It was reasonably priced and fun to eat with friends.  It's definately not "gourmet" or "noveau" but come on - it's on Telegraph and it's fondue with all you can drink wine for the college crowd.  Who cares - we had a great time and enjoyed the food which is all that matters.  To top off the experience she brought us complimentary cheese cake which was outstanding!  I read the other reviews only after visiting.  Other YELPers seem to have been a little harsh here.

If you come here expecting a fancy spancy fondue restaurant, you will be disappointed. This is not a fancy place, but it is a fun experience and would be great with a group of friends. Also, make sure you get a coupon from restaurant.com! 

The regular cheese fondues are okay. To be honest, I had a hard time telling the difference between the gouda and the cheddar. I highly recommend the Mexican fiesta fondue. Not only does it come with the potatoes and bread like the other cheese fondues, but it also includes tortilla chips. Getting a plate of veggies is also a good idea. 

You don't want to miss the chocolate fondue. It comes with both fruit and marshmallows. Yum. 2 fondues for 2 people is plenty of food with leftovers to take home! It's pretty hard to reheat the fondues properly though. 

For drinks, don't bother ordering wine at the restaurant. Who knows what the house red/white is. Bring your own wine and pay the corkage fee. If you order 2 fondues and pay the corkage fee, it's works out perfectly for the restaurant.com coupon. 

If you can, try to get one of the courtyard tables near a heat lamp. The interior space is kinda dark and sometimes a bit dingy. It's not bad for a low key date night though.

Service can be a bit slow if they are crowded, but the owner (I assume he is Fred) is very friendly and kinda quirky. One time, he took a great interest in the wine we brought for the meal and offered to waive the corkage fee if we let him taste it. It was a Spanish red (Tempranillo), and Fred declared it was very tasty and a good match for fondue. Woohoo, no corkage fee!

It's definitely not quality, but it's fun. When I need "fun" I go to Fondue Fred's with a group of friends. If I want quality, I go to the Melting Pot or La Fondue with my husband. 

They use iceburg lettuce for their salads. You don't cook any of your own food like traditional fondue (which could be a pro or a con, depending on how you look at it). I always leave feeling stuffed off of all the cheap bread and moderate cheese.

Thankfully, their prices aren't too outrageous. And if you go with a group, they have a special price so you get drinks, etc included. This is definitely a "group" type of place!

Service is "ok". Not great. I think the waiter/owner was drunk the time we were there. Not sloppy drunk, but just very "happy". ha! We were entertained, but it didn't make for a fast dinner. He was pleased to serve, though, which was nice.

Their chocolate fondue is simple, but yummy. So yummy, you may need 2 to fill your group's craving!
Blah everything (decor,fondue,bread,) and the service really sucks!

Came here with a bunch a friends for dinner on a Friday night. It wasn't crowded, as I would have expected.  They have indoor and outdoor seating.  

For our party of four we ordered the Cinque Formaggio, Gouda, and Meatball Fondue. The Cinque Formaggio is a mix of mozzarella, provolone, romano and guyere cheese. From the cheese fondues, I liked this one over the Gouda, as it was more flavorful.  The meatball fondue was also good. Lots of meatballs in a wine sauce. Very savory in taste and went well if the cinque formaggio, if you added both together.    

For dessert we had the chocolate fondue.   That was the least impressive fondue, as the chocolate was not what I expected. I was expecting a thicker, richer, and sweeter sauce. What came out in the fondue pot was literally Hershey's chocolate sauce, just heated.   It came with a mix plate of marshmallows and fruit (banana, strawberry, honey dew melon, and pineapple. I thought the pineapple didn't work well with chocolate, as it was too acidic.

Service was slow, as it was only 1 person serving the entire restaurant. I think she was the owner. Very nice and friendly, but after more guest came to the restaurant, it took longer for things to come.  

Overall it was fun night and the food was affordable compared to other bay area fondue restaurants.  For Berkeley, this place fits the demographics.

Not worth the money AT ALL.

My husband and I went to Fondue Freds in January 2009 for a friend's birthday party. We were very disappointed in the food we received for $30 per person.

What were my main complaints?
- When asked about the salad dressing and food allergies, the response was simply, "Don't eat it". No attempt at all to find out what was in the salad dressing.
- The veggies served with the cheese fondue were all just thrown on a plate in a heap. No attempt at all to have a nice looking platter of veggies. Also, the veggies just had that "not fresh" look about them. You know, a little brown around the edges and a little wilted.
- Same thing as above with the fruit served with the chocolate fondue.

For $30/ person we received:
- salad (I don't know how it tasted because I was told not to eat it)
- cheese fondue (Okay, the cheese fondue was actually pretty good. But I have made similar at home- not that hard.)
- bread squares for dipping
- potatoes for dipping
- gross plate of veggies (described above)
- a few different meat dishes that did not taste good to me
- cheesecake (not the best, but I am very picky about cheesecake, I'll admit)

My table also ordered some chocolate fondue, and I have to admit, I was so disgusted by the looks of the fruit plate that I didn't even try it. So it could have been good, I don't know.

My recommendation: save the $30pp you would spend at Fondue Freds. Buy a fondue pot. Look online for some cheese fondue recipes (not hard, usually just cheese, wine and some spices). Buy the supplies you need at the grocery store, and have a fondue party at home! I can guarantee it will cost less and taste better.

I've been here a few times now over the last year and I love this place for groups. They have a deal for 6 or more people that includes all you can eat fondue and all you can drink wine and unlimited dipping items like bread and veggies.

Last time we went, we were 1 person short of the 6 people required for the group rate, but the lady was nice enough to let us 5 split the cost of the other dinner and we were able to get the unlimited wine etc.... Totally worth an extra $6-7 per person... She even threw in a free chocolate fondue at the end since there were only 5 of us.

If anyone knows of a supposedly better fondue spot in the east bay let me know and I'll check it out. Till then I can deal with slightly limp veggies and half stale white bread I guess.

The food took at least 40 minutes to come out after we first ordered. It wasn't that great. I blame it on the bread, which should have been toasted  to make it taste better. THe chocolate fondue was great though.

I haven't had any better Fondue in the Bay Area (my mom's being the exception), so I'd recommend this as a place to try!  The atmosphere of the restaurant is pretty nice, with it's location among the other stores in this kind of courtyard.  The sodas are provided in these gigantic jars, which is pretty nifty.  And of course, the dessert fondue is delicious!

So I just wanted to start this review by saying that I am not realy a cheese person (as I ordered the steak dish in wine type sauce), but I have an open mind and will try about almost anything and will usually really like the food.  Unfortunately, my first time experience here was not too impressive. 

We had the classic fondue and a steak fondue dish, with a side of fresh mushrooms.  The classic fondue was actually quite good upon the first 2 or 3 dips (with bread and our other sides).  But for some weird reason, the wine taste in it started to become noticeable.  After about the 6th piece of our side with it, it tasted just like dipping your sides in thick creamy wine (what happened to the cheeeese?!).  Needless to say, we had A LOT left of this dish which we packed to go.

The steak dish... eh tasted like a mediocre steak stew that was actualy a little bland.  The mushrooms were really good, but then again, its hard to mess up mushrooms in any type of dish (I heart shrooms :p).  Far from impressed.

Service was... ok...  our server forgot to give us cups for our pitcher of water, and he rarely ever came to check up on us.  It actually seemed like he neglected us (maybe b/c we had a restaurant.com coupon and we weren't white?) .  yeah, service was horrible.  I think he only came to check up on us once and the rest of the time he had to be flagged.

Price wise, this place totally isn't worth it.  It was about 16 bucks for our entrees each, and a side of mushrooms were about 6 bucks (wtf?! they were just fresh mushrooms cut into pieces you could have bought from a regular grocery store).   My suggestion, bring your own mushrooms and bread and just order the entrees.  The thing that really erks me is if you are going to charge so much for your dishes, you gotta have at least attentive service.

Ah yes, and the thing that took away the final star (to become 1 star for my review), upon asking for our items to go, our waiter only packed the two entrees.  I literally had to ask him to pack our bread, our potatoes, and side of mushrooms (which we paid 6 bucks for!).  I'm sorry, but don't waste food, i dont care how prestigious you think your restaurant is, but it is really just a shame to throw away perfectly fresh and edible food...!

oh yeah, our waiter had the audacity to write down the suggested tip, which was fine since we used a restaurant.com deal, BUT he wrote down a POST TAX tip, which i personally didn't think he deserved even a 15% tip pre tax seeing how we were neglected most of the time.  Alas, being the nice guy i am, i gave in to his post tax tip.  

yes, i may try this place again, but only if the g/f wants to give it another shot.  who knows, maybe we just ordered dishes that we just didn't like... I guess we'll just have to wait and see...

If you really want good fondue and can tell the difference, go somewhere else and pay half again as much for a great meal. If you want a fun, congenial shared meal with friends where you're not rushed and can play with your mostly okay food, this is the place.

The service is friendly, albeit pretty slow. One person for the whole restaurant and I kind of wonder if he doesn't make the food too. So this isn't a place for a quick bite and you may wait awhile to see your food and then your check.

The salad is beyond abysmal. Iceberg lettuce and shredded carrots that have seen better days. Give it a miss. The fondue (we had the basic traditional) was grainy as though water had been added rather than wine. It was thick enough with decent, though rather salty flavor. It's best quality was quantity - I'm guessing they cater to the hungry kids university crowd where more is always better.  Two of us with the basic and a plate of veggies couldn't finish everything. It was enough, especially if you get dessert, to feed 3 or 4 average eaters. 

The bread was terrible - stale and not a particularly nice texture even when fresh. They gave us a lot of it. But we decided, if we ever come here again, we'll bring our own bread as it would be worth an extra few bucks for fresh, crusty good bread. My dining companion lived in Switzerland for awhile and commented that the bread was no worse than that in the average Italian Swiss restaurant, though appalling by French Swiss standards. So I think it depends on your own standards and taste.

We enjoyed the chocolate fondue, even though we were already pretty full. The fruit wasn't super impressive. Melon doesn't make a good dip and there was too much of that and not enough strawberries. But the chocolate was as good as any I've had in higher end places. It could have used a shot of kir, but it was rich and smooth and plentiful, certainly not the Hershey's syrup someone complained of. There were marshmallows too. I don't know if it was on purpose, but the waiter left an extra burner lit on out table and we had fun roasting out marshmallows over the flame before dipping them. My review got an entire extra star for that bit of unexpected whimsy!

So, it's a nice place to come and spend an evening with friends if you aren't picky and are hungry. The decor does look like a little place in Europe that's been around 50 years. They were wonderfully accommodating to a huge party of students having a celebration and I could see that the kids were having a super time. It was very cheerful. That's probably the nicest thing about this place: it's cheerful, friendly and easy-going, the food is edible, not great, the wine is okay, not special and, if you've never had excellent fondue, you'll be content. Fine dining, however, its not.

This review is based on my memory from being here a while ago.  But, much of what I remember is being disappointed.
I love fondue.  If you don't already know, I love cheese.  I couldn't wait to come here when my friend said she planned a group outing.  We did the all you can eat thing for the group.  First of all, the service was the slowest I think I've ever encountered in a restaurant.  It literally took almost an hour for them to bring us the first pot of fondue.  When they did bring it out, there was hardly any in the pot, so we would need more within minutes, and then have to wait forever for another pot of cheesiness.  We also had the oil fondue if I remember, but I don't recall being impressed.
At the conclusion of the meal, it took another 45 minutes just to get someone to clear the table and bring the check.  By that point, I was about to tear my hair out.  
This place is just not worth it.

Go to Berkeley Bowl, grab your favorite cheese and chocolate, and invest in your own fondue pot.  Trust me.  You'll get a lot more out of it than going to Fondue Fred.  I won't say that this place is bad, but it's simply not worth it for the quality of food and price.  I mean, $10/person minimum purchase?   Spare me!

I wasn't holding very high standards to begin with after reading all of the reviews.  We ordered:

1)  Gouda fondue (Dutch Smoked Gouda and imported Swiss cheeses) - $17 - nothing special about this dish at all, sorry.  And I love Gouda.  Cheese fondues came with nacho chips, bread bites, and boiled potatoes.

2)  Fiesta cheese fondue (Cheddar, Gruyere, Mexican spices, mushroom, tomato, green onion, Tortilla chip) - $17 - I preferred the fiesta cheese over the gouda.  It was supposed to have more of a spicy kick, but it just did not make it.

3)  Chocolate fondue (with marshmallows, strawberry and banana slices, cantaloupe, honeydew, apples) - $14 - This was my favorite part of the meal because I could roast marshmallows over a flame.  I learned from the little kids at the other table that they catch on fire and that's pretty cool! You can't do that at The Melting Pot.  :P  The fruit assortment was odd though.  Who dips cantaloupe?  I prefer the cheesecake bites and graham cracker dipper assortment with Melting Pot's chocolate fondue. 

My friends and I played with our food...but that's the best part about fondue , right?  If you're looking for a going out Fondue experience, I suggest that you go to The Melting Pot:  better ambiance, better dippers and fondue, and roughly the same price!

Also, BYOB bring your own bread.  Bread is the best for cheese dippin' .  Not potatoes.

I am a fan of fondue so I was really excited to come here. I didn't hear AMAZING reviews about this place, but I came anyway because I thought that my love for fondue was all that mattered... 

My friend and I came around 8pm, and we got seated right away because there was only one other group in the restaurant (probably why service was so fast). For gourmet fondue, we got Cinque Formaggio (Mozzarella, Provolone, Romano and Guyere), and for dessert, we got Chocolate Fondue. 

Salad: I did not enjoy it. I could have easily put that salad together in a second. It consisted of repacked things (lettuce, red cabbage, and carrots)... and it wasn't even fresh. 

Cheese fondue: Other fondue places I've been to had more food items to dip in our fondue (such as meat), but this place gives you just potatoes and bread... which was pretty disappointing. The cheese wasn't that great quality. It was like as if it was watered down? Something was just off. We got pretty full fast because of the bread, so we didn't have much room left for dessert.

Chocolate fondue: It comes with milk chocolate (in the pot), strawberries, marshmellows, pineapples, apples, and cantaloupe. I ate all the bananas, strawberries, and pineapples heheh. 


Total: ~$38 with tip (btw, this place requires a minimum of $10/person)
Not worth it in my opinion. I would rather spend over $100 at La Fondue for legit fondue.

Just got back from a casual night out with four of my friends, armed as we were with a $25 restaurant.com coupon (like another savvy reviewer)

Between the five of us, after the 25 buck reduction, the bill came out to about 44 dollars, or a little less than 9 dollars/person. Thoroughly worth it for two cheese fondues, a side of raw vegetables, and a dessert (in addition to the salads, potato chunks, and endless baskets of bread bits to dip). We were all stuffed!

So what did we actually order...?
(3/5 of the party members are vegetarian, so no meat fondues for us...)

1. "Classic Chive"--didn't like it, though other members of my party enjoyed it very much paired with the bread chunks. ($16)

2. "Fiesta"--yummy! cheesy, nacho-like goodness with mushrooms, jalapenos, and delicious spices. Came with tortilla chips, though a little stale

3. Vegetables: a heaping plate of various sliced veggie chunks, including zucchini, carrots, cauliflower, bell pepper, broccoli, etc... One order was quite enough between the five of us, when the bread and potatoes and chips and such were also taken into account.

3. For dessert: chocolate fondue. Highlight of the meal!! Came with strawberry and regular white marshmallows AND fresh cantaloupe, strawberries, pineapple, honeydew, and sliced bananas. Now, I'm not saying the fruit was of the veeerry best quality, but once you smother that stuff in chocolate, even the least ripe chunk of pineapple seems divine.

Seems like a pretty decent place, right? So why only 3 stars?

For starters, I'm a little torn about the service. The guy who was serving us seemed nice enough, but his humor was a little strange, and made us feel a little awkward at the beginning of the meal.

At this point I should probably interject with a disclaimer: this was my very first time having fondue, so maybe the strange taste of the chive-cheese fondue is just an acquired taste. But until I have had the chance to go back again and build up my tolerance, I'll have to stick to the more mainstream (i.e. not "Classic" fondues)... and leave the rating as is.

On another note, the salad served at the beginning was interesting, but the dressing was really too sour.

As for ambiance: the inside reminded me of a ski lodge--true to fondue's Swiss origins? not sure. It was kind of cute and cozy, I guess... The place was fairly empty (only two other parties there tonight), but I suppose that's to be expected for a Tuesday night in a college town.

All in all, a good dinner for 9 bucks a person, but not so much for 14 bucks a person (without the coupon!).

"Its amazing what you can find at the dollar store," said the owner.

The place -Mediocre at best.

I've been there with a group and if you're talking and laughing so much that you don't notice how gross your food is or how absolutely atrocious the wine is (like Franzia sounds pretty good in comparison), then its decent.

A group of 4, and you start noticing how bad it is. You need a minimum of 6 for the group discount - and like the other reviews say...don't expect good food. The outside seating is lovely but everything else is bland. 

I think twice in a lifetime is more than enough for me. 

The owner just bought Chester's Bayview Cafe on Vine (between walnut and shattuck) - I'm waiting to see the decline.

I feel Like this place is probably hit or miss and I've just been lucky enough to get hits both times I've been. I'll let you in on my formula for success.

~First things first, invite 5 people besides yourself, but don't invite whiny people, cheapskates, picky and/or non-adventurous eaters, or sloppy drunks. 

~Second, if you and your party like wine, try Party Rate #1 {$26.00 per person (plus they included 18% gratuity when our bill came). Unlimited salad, freshly-cut vegetables, red potatoes and French baguette. Five fondue selections and Chocolate fondue for dessert. PLUS Unlimited Burgundy, Rose and Chablis Wine} You can drink enough wine to justify the price. 

~Third, ENJOY!

I recommend getting the cheese fondue as opposed to the cheese-less because first of all it's frickin fondue and thats pretty much synonymous with cheese and second, the cheese-less kind is the equivalent of soup or marinara sauce depending on which you choose. Also, every ten minutes or so have everyone pick up a pot and move to the next burner so you can get the full rotation of fondue flavors!
