Ya know what? The fondue may not be the best quality, but my friends and I had a good time and all 6 of us left happy and full!

bad food bad service. don't do it. 
the salad is awful, fondues are pretty bad, barely edible, service is appalling and owner/manager very unfriendly. We had a large group, did not get enough food/wine and it was pretty expensive. we paid a lot more than the $20 another review was charged. 
The only redeeming point was the chocolate fondue. 
Give it a miss... very disappointing

I had an event for nearly 100 people at Fondue Fred and had a great experience!  The owners were extremely accommodating to my group's needs and made the whole process personal and fun.

There were about 3 very long tables set up in the courtyard and we took up the entire inside of the restaurant as well.  Wine was waiting for us as we arrived and the fondue came out about 10 minutes after everyone was seated and settled.  Our group felt very comfortable and welcomed at the restaurant, as they let us wander around, take pictures, and have a great time while enjoying wine and decent fondue.

Overall we had an extremely positive experience.  I would recommend Fondue Fred for any group!

I once visited this joint with a bunch of friends when I was a student @ Cal. That was a LONG time ago. The memories are fading... but I remember enjoying the food, sucking down plenty of wine (which flowed freely -- all you can drink! hmm... maybe that is why the memory is so hazy), and having a great time. Highly recommended for groups!

I'm not coming back here again. $19 for a buffet type meal may sound like a good idea, but not when the buffet consists of:

mediocre bread
redundant sauces that are essentially identical
vegetables that i can get from any supermarket veggie platter
and lastly, bad bad bad house wine (which is pretty much expected for $19 per, eh?)

but still, bad food. sadface.

Service was a bit slow ... and our small party of 4 (half of which was missing in the beginning) was easy to miss.  But we ordered the Parmesan (with salami) fondue and a 5 cheese fondue.  Both were very good - but the Parmesan was preferred by all.

The extra veggies for $6 offered some variety ... but it's the bulk stuff that comes straight out of a bag so don't expect super fresh vegetables.  Definitely save room for the chocolate fondue though, that's a winner.

Ever heard of don't play with your food? Well, you kind of have to here. That's the whole fondue experience. It was my first time and was a decent experience but not super awesome. 

The service was slow but wasn't bad, maybe because we were the first customer? We asked the server what he recommended, so we got just that because we really didn't know how things worked. The dishes came with nacho chips, bread bites, and potatoes. We ordered:

Fiesta Fondue (Cheddar, Gruyere, Mexican spices, mushroom, tomato, green onion)
- I really like this one. But it's like paying triple price for spicy nachos. I guess you have to pay the price for playing with your food. 

Chateaubrian steak (Tender steak with broccoli in wine sauce)
- I didn't like this dish. It tasted like another beef stew with some wine sauce. It's so not worth the price and I wouldn't get it unless it comes with rice.

We also ordered a whole bottle of wine. For $28, the wine wasn't good. The $2 wine from Trader's Joe is way better. We manage to finish it because we didn't want it to go to waste.

I felt like it wasn't a full meal and more like an appetizer with chips, bread and cheese.  We were still hungry, so we ordered dessert.

Chocolate fondue (Mixed fruits and marshmallows)
- The best. I had fun playing with it and burning the marshmallows then dipped it in the chocolate.

We were finally full with all the carbs and sugar we ate. It was a decent experience but I wouldn't go there for dinner. I would only go there for an appetizer or dessert place. The service was really slow but server was polite to us so it's ok. I had time to play with my food.

In our case, the $25 off coupon from restaurant.com did not help. It forces us to eat more than $35 and automatically forced to give 18% tip even if it's a crappy service. The worse is that, they do 18% after tax. It wasn't worth it for us because most of that $25 was the 18% tip total. So yeah, just keep that in mind.

This is the best fondue restaurant in the bay area. Yeah I have been to The Melting Pot (one of the worst dining experiences in my life: I mean when I order truffle fondue DO NOT BRING ME AN ATOMIZER AND GIVE ME 1 MEASLY SPRITZ)- sorry sorry still get a little heated about that, and I have tried the Matterhorn in S.F. (yeah it's good but it would be nice to have money left over for other food for the month!).

Fondue Fred's is cozy, affordable and extremely friendly. The staff remembers you and I have a party of 5, and we always leave stuffed and happy. Actually it's almost like a cheese high! The bread is always toasted and lovely, the fondue always fresh ( the classic, garlic, and cinque frommaggio are all to die for). My family loves cheese and if you have the taste for it, you can taste the gruyere, swiss, and the delicious kirsch, all things that make classic fondue what it is!

I have been going here for years and honestly, yelping always slips my mind (I swear Favorite Indian Food- you're next). But I am sitting here with a silly cheese grin and a full belly and I have to give credit where credit is due. 

Needless to say- I will be back!

Go here for the social experience, not the food!  If you come with this expectation, you will have a great time.

I've been here for massive bday parties (parties of 40-50 ppl) where we had the all-you-can-eat-and-drink deal.  It was amazing how they were able to seat all of us together at an EXTREMELY LONG table.  They placed 5 tables end to end.  The unlimited wine deal was PERFECT for the occasion; Let loose, unwind, and chat with all your friends.  But watch yourself! At the first sign of unpleasant behavior, they will stop serving the wine for everyone!  Don't be the partypooper.

So how is the food and wine?  
Salad is a sour, watery mess.  
Potatoes lacked seasoning and were served cold.  
Bread was stale.  
Veggies for dipping were pretty good and fresh. 
Fondue had good consistency for dipping and many flavors to choose from.
Wine was not great at all (but most college kids just drink to get drunk...)

Overall, not a satisfying meal.  For such parties, the food's primary purpose is to assist your alcohol intake.  With all you can drink, you definitely need the food!!
Ate here almost two years ago, most of us got sick afterwards. Never returned. Never will.

I read the reviews and went anyway, because I was meeting some friends I don't get to see very often, and I would have gone to Chez Cat Food. Maybe if we had, the food would have been better. The bread was stale, the "salad" was soaked in "dressing." I had some serious doubts about whether the cheese was being recycled into different pots. Don't get me started on the wine. 

Now, the chocolate fondue? That's a different story. Strawberry marshmallows and fresh fruit! Bring it on!

really?  fondue?  is that what we're calling that?  reeeeally?

if you are any sort of fondue connoisseur, as it clearly states on my resume, you should skip over fred's.  it's simply just not good fondue.  maybe it's because they're churning out enough in the kitchen to keep up with the all-you-can-eat special.  and there's probably a reason said special comes with bottomless wine. 

sorry, fred.

If you come here with a group of friends, we're talking 6 or more, then you'll have a great time.   Lower... I mean, really...lower your culinary expectations.   This ain't gonna be gourmet fondue, but it'll be fondue, and it'll be lots of it, and you won't care because you'll be drinking lots of bad wine alongside it.

If you're on a date, then stay the hell away from this place... Go to the Matterhorn (http://www.yelp.com/biz/av8vitp4twNYvUi4Ox0pGw) across the bridge for some quality fondue and genuine swiss wines in the heart of SF.

However... you got a group of people, and you want a fondue fix, with all kinds of different fondue styles, including chocolate fondue for dessert?   Fondue Fred's the place to be!   I think you and your friends make or break the Fondue Fred experience.   If you're in the mood to just have fun, go.  If you want epicurean delight, stay away... very far away!

Yes, I am going to give Fondue Fred's five stars.  I have eaten here  a few times every year for the past two years, so maybe five times total.  I have always enjoyed the location and the food.  I don't drink wine so I can not say anything about it.  However the fondues are very good.  The  chateaubriand fondue is excellent and is made with rfeal filet mignon.  Not some inferior cut paraded as Chateaubriand.  As for everything tasteing the same, It all depends on what fondues you order.  For instance never order a Appanzeller and a cheddar fondue together.  They have such a simular taste, unless you are a Gourmand,  it may be hard to tell much difference.  Now for the comment about the bread being stale.  Personally I always thought fondue was to be served with crusty bread that has sat out a bit.  I really  wouldn't want soft fresh bread for fondue. So I would say that their crusty bread is just right.  And now for the statement about not being hot enough to cook vegetables.  Those little gel burners or one of the best ways to heat fondue.  You just have to adjust them to the right flame height.  We have had no problem getting our fondue to bubble it was so hot.  So whatever the hate for fondue fred's comes from, don't listen to it.  The place is very nice and comfortable and the fondue is great.

yep 3 stars... this is definitely not your high end restaurant experience... but for the price, YES!   Very low key, almost TOO casual environment.  I'd expect a bit more class/elegance cause the whole concept of fondue just brings to mind fancy, exquisite, European, hoity toity - ness.  Not the case at Fondue Fred.  Fondue Fred hits the spot without all of the pretentiousness and high prices.

The owner (I think he is the owner) was quite pleasant, goofy, a bit slow taking our order, but charming none-the-less.  

I was a Fondue virgin until last night!  WOW.  Orgasmic indeed.  

Seriously how can you go wrong with melted cheddar or melted 5 cheese fondue.  The 5 cheese fondue had provolone, asiago, parmesan and I can't remember the other two.  We also ordered sliced apples and sliced mushrooms and it included potatoes, bread and salad.  I could not stop dipping my bread in the decadent cheeses.  Oh.  My. GOD!  YUM.  I want to go back right now.

We had a gift certificate (www.restaurant.com) for $25 off and we each ended up paying $20/person!!!  That included stuffing ourselves with salad, bread, fondue, etc + 1 glass of wine a person.  Talk about a bargain!!  I will be back and I can't wait!

My husband and I decided to try out this place because we got a coupon off restaurant.com. After getting excited to have fondue after such a long time, I got really worried after seeing some bad reviews. BUT, all went well. 

With a $6 pitcher of diet coke on its way, we ordered the $16 classic fondue (delicious, nice texture, nice heat) which came with a salad for both of us. Sure the salad was like the pre-bagged (lettuce, carrot, red cabbage) but it tasted good, was fresh, crunchy and the dressing wasn't as bad as people say. I liked it! It was sorta like a citrus vinaigrette. I thought the seasoning in the dressing was flavorful, not sour.

To go along with the potatoes (well-cooked, slightly seasoned) and baguette (not amazing, but abundant, fresh and great for dipping) we ordered some shrimp and veggies for $8 to dip as well. Once again, it was pre-bagged sorta thing, but it was all fresh enough, crunchy and good for dipping. My favorite was the broccoli and cauliflower.  Next time, i'd be very content sticking with just the bread and potatoes though. 

Even with my husband, who's a very heavy dipper, we were stuffed with some cheese left. I would have finished the deliciousness but I wanted to save room for dessert which came highly recommended from others on here. 

We ended the meal with a $16 chocolate fondue. It was nice and rich, great heat and texture. It came with a large variety of fruit (including strawberries, pineapple, melons, apple) but the best was the marshmallows, which he brought another heat-source over to roast the marshmallows first before dipping them, which was a great magic touch to make it perfect.  We had a ton of leftover and the waiter/cook/probable owner OFFERED to box up the fruit for us. I didn't think of asking, so I thought this was a nice touch.

Yes, the place was empty besides 2 others that came in near the end of our meal.  Yes, the decor is cheesy and the ceilings are a little low. Who cares? With all this food, soda, tax and generous tip, this was was about $45 (minus a $25 coupon). 

I would for sure go back. The waiter even asked us if it was our first time there and joked that we'll never be back. I told him we would and I genuinely mean it.

Excellent place for a big group reunion or for groups of 4 or more. If you have less than that it becomes a bit pricey without a lot of people to share with. 

We ordered the Asiago Cheese, Garlic Cheese and the Chicken Soup-y type Fondue. If you are going for two I would definitely recommend Asiago and Chicken-Soup-y: Chicken Soup-y gives you bang for the buck with the extra chicken, broccoli and cauliflower bits in it that you can then dip in the other cheese fondues! Asiago...the first time we came here and asked the waiter what he recommended he said that Asians generally like the Asiago. No hate - I appreciate the honesty and, quite frankly, he was right.

Tip: go to the website and print out the coupon for a free chocolate fondue with a purchase of 3 other fondues!!

As far as fondue goes, Fondue Fred's is not all that great. However, that being said, we went here for my birthday. Just me and 5 girlfriends for the all you can eat/drink price. I figured, hey, if people are going to go out for my birthday, I might as pick someplace that is somewhat affordable. At first they tried to sit us outside under a heater (in the middle of feburary) but us whiney girls made sure we were moved inside. Its old and drab and a little on the small side.  The wine is cheap. Probably that stuff you buy in the wicker lined bottle.

The waiter/owner was very helpful, but his jokes were a little annoying.

Oh,  yes, the potatoes lacked seasoning and needed to be served hot, not cold. The salad was a watery mess and the fondue was boring ( only one we all liked was the Garlic Cheese). The cheesecake was surprising good. The best part of the evening was the social aspect that Fondue lends to. . .so I guess I got my money's worth - cheap wine and gabbing girlfriends is always fun no matter where you are. If you want excellent fondue go to the Melting Pot or La Fondue.

Can't beat melted cheese. I did not get sick as reported by most other reviewers.

'Fred' is quite charming. He kinda looks like Peter Sellers.

3.5 stars (i like to round up) for a cute and cozy place in berkeley. we ordered the classic cheese fondue, which came with a big basket of bread cubes (slightly dried out, but personally i think it's a better vehicle for the cheese that way), a platter of raw veggies, and a bowl of cooked potato cubes. i thought the cheese fondue could have been thicker and little more flavorful, but it was decent.

dessert fondue was chocolate with a plate of assorted fruit (strawberries, bananas, cantaloupe, pineapple, apples) and pink and white marshmallows. they also provided a separate burner for us to toast the marshmallows, which was a cool touch.

prices are okay. definitely cheaper than the melting pot, or la fondue.

as for service, the owner was very nice, but one of the employees took away our cheese fondue after asking if we were done (we said "no"). oh well, we were ALMOST done...

This was my first time to Fondue Fred.  My friends and I were celebrating a birthday so it was great fun with everyone.

We didn't get any of the party specials - just ordered different fondues to try which were:

Classic chive
Garlic
Parmesan
Blue Cheese
Apple Cinnamon
Chicken
Steak

The fondues I liked were garlic, parmesan, blue cheese and apple cinnamon.  The apple cinnamon isn't anything special; it just has some cinnamon sprinkled on top and the apples have cinnamon sprinkled on top.  The apples are not in the fondue, they come on the side for dipping.  I think you'd be better off just ordering some of the cheese fondues and get the side of apples.  

We also ordered two large dishes of the vegetables.  The vegetables are raw - you get strips of green bell pepper, white mushrooms, carrots, celery pieces, broccoli and cauliflower.  Don't expect to cook them in the fondue/broth.  I don't particularly like my vegetables raw, except the carrots and celery.

The bread is plain inexpensive pre-made french bread.  Good for dunking and gnoshing.  The "red potatoes" seemed like plain potatoes sprinkled with paprika.  They were good because they were already cooked.  The salad was okay.  The dressing seemed unique.  Perhaps the swiss equivalent to french salad dressing

For dessert we shared three chocolate fondues.  This was my favorite of the night.  The dessert portion of the menu could use some expansion.  Fondue is fairly versatile when it comes to dessert.  The chocolate fondue includes a plate of marshmallows, strawberries, cantolope and honey dew melon, pineapple and apple.  The marshmallows, strawberries, and apple were my favorites.  The chocolate was very tasty too.

Fondue fred gets only three stars because the cheese isn't anything special.  I think with some better quality cheeses, the dishes would improve significantly.  My water had strange particulates at the bottom of my glass.

This restaurant is very good for groups as you can try many different dishes and have a nice time with friends.  I wouldn't take anyone special here on a date though.  There are better places.

this place was awful! i went for my birthday with 25 people.we could barely get the guy to come over twice the whole meal.and he was rude.anytime we tried to order we had to get up and go find a waiter.I think velveeta cheese probably tastes better!next time ill spend a little more and go to a better place like the melting pot!

While the food here is not worth its price, the experience certainly is. It's not every day that you have Swiss fondue and this place delivers that experience. The service was good and the decor was kitschy cute. Between four people, we had two fondues: chateaubrian steak and asiago. We were served large plates of veggies and bread for dipping into the fondue. There seemed to be unlimited bread cubes. Quantity didn't seem like much, but those bread cubes actually filled us up.

I went to a birthday party that had 25+ in attendance, so I was impressed that we were well-fed (albeit slowly), and most importantly, well-stocked with wine!  I absolutely loved the meatballs, that was the star dish of the night!  Other than that, I couldn't tell the difference between the fondues, and it was hard for the vegetarians because some fondues had meat in it.  Even though reservations were made, the owner was the only one there so we had to wait a while for more fondue.  But regardless, its a great place for lots of friends if you don't mind dinner stretched out for 3 hours, and it has amazingly cozy, very cute ambiance.  It's awesome fun equation time! Sticks + cheese n' bread (times 30 people) + copious amounts of red wine = SUPER FRICKIN' FUN! 3 1/2 stars in my eyes

Came here with fellow Yelper Kathleen W. and a couple of other friends for a Friday evening dinner. Having never tried fondue before, I had high hopes. Then I read the Yelp reviews the night before and started to get a bit weary. One of the food mottoes I live by is "if I can make it myself, I'm most likely not going to go out to eat it." I would say this place falls right under that category. Like Kathleen said, go buy your own cheese and chocolate, melt it, bake some bread and potatoes, and there's your fondue for a heck of a lot cheaper than here. 

We ordered the Fiesta Fondue (Cheddar, Gruyere, Mexican spices, mushroom, tomato, green onion, Tortilla chip), Gouda Fondue (self explanatory), and Chocolate Fondue. Quite honestly, you could barely tell the two cheese fondues apart and both were not that great. They tasted a bit stale and got pretty bland by the end of the night. I've gotta say the roasted potatoes they give you with the dishes are pretty tasty especially with fondue, but that's probably one of the best parts of the whole process. The chocolate fondue comes with a whole bunch of fruit and marshmallows, and was all very plain and simple.

The price just kills it all, but with a Restaurant.com coupon, it's probably not too bad. The $10 a person minimum just ruins it, especially considering the fact that you're not really even eating a whole meal, but just bread and cheese. Thanks to Kathleen W, who graciously brought her own heap of baguettes, we never ran out of bread to dip with, which would have been a very likely situation if she didn't. The best part of the whole experience was playing with the food, which is a good break for any stressed college student. Other than that, there's nothing special to this place. The decor wasn't too bad though.

I love this place. Whenever my family has a special occasion, we jump in the van and head for fondue. The fondue is simply the best in the area. How can you not have a good time with laughing conversations with family and friends over bubbling cheese pots (and meatball pots, seriously, try the meatball pot!) As much as I love the food, and I really really love the food, the service has me coming back just as much. The owner lady feels like my middle eastern mom that wants me to eat more bread and potatoes. She also wants to send me home with my empty coke bottle filled with her mustard salad dressing that I can't get enough of, true story. I love this place, and if you love fondue, you really need to give it a try.

FOOD:
1.) Choc fondue = mmm it was simple but sufficient.

SERVICE:
Kind of a communication barrier, and we came towards the closing time, felt like we were rushed because of that.

ATMOSPHERE:
The restaurant was inside a courtyard, had a feel of being outdoor, yet indoor, Christmas lights were strung above giving a very Italian feel (how in Magginno's or Macaroni Grill)

ALTERNATIVES:
La Fondue, Saratoga

Couldn't believe how empty this place is on a Friday Night, but I guess it is because it is a hidden jem of Berkeley.

The food is delicous, great price for fondue.  Recommend the Chatuebrian Steak Fondue.

The service was lacking and the food was mediocre.  We went with a large party (6 adults, 2 kids), the server seemed very confused about our large party and said he needed time to put the table together (even though there were very few people at the restaurant).  After waiting for a few minutes, we were seated or rather crammed into two small tables.  We added another one later so that we could all fit.  

It took him forever to finally bring water and a salad to start.  He only brought one pitcher of water and a small salad but indicated he would bring more.  After about 10 minutes, I finally got up and asked for more water because we had already gone through our one pitcher, at which point he told me that I needed to be more patient.    

We ordered our food, which was a confusing ordeal but somehow we were surprised that he managed to get the order correct.   After eating our overpriced cheese, veggies and bread, we were about to leave when the server brought over a chocolate fondue indicating it was on the house.  We thought ok, well this makes up for the earlier problems, unfortunately, not the case as when we checked our bill we were charged for it.  In the interest of wanting to leave, we went ahead and paid for it.  

Bottom line: slow service, mediocre food, expensive

Pretty good, but i have had better for the price i had to pay!

I love cheese and this hits the spot but all they give you is bread to dip, considering there should be a variety of foods to choose from like, apples or veges, and maybe some more potatoes. The chocolate fondue was okay but again lacked in variety of dippers. If you want some really good fondue experience try The Melting POt and get Big Night Out. you get a little bit of everything and will be there eating for about three hours!
oh btw, the waiter/owner dude at Fondue Freds was kinda creepy

Our waiter forgot about us....many times.
Our food was scary....the cheese fondue was definitely low quality and bland and came with bread close to stale.  They had to re-light our fire several times as well.
The chocolate fondue was low grade dark chocolate, nothing special, and it came with more stale bread, VERY few strawberries, and mostly apples.
For all this, it was FAR too expensive.

My first fondue experience was here. I thought it was pretty good. Our heat source wasn't really keeping our cheese warm though. Other than that it was decent. Plus its fun dipping stuff in cheese and eating it, ya know? LOVE the outdoor seating. Fun and romantical in once.
It's a perfect group dining activity....fondue and wine...who can pass that up?  it's not expensive, and fancy as melting pot, but it works for that down-to-earth kickit spot

Its THE BESTEST fondue place in the world!! I have been going to this place for last 7 years and there has never been a single time i have been disappointed. Service is amazing, the best service ever!! SAL is the MAN! This is not one of those upscale fondue places but its a cozy place with a lot of character which has food to die for!! My favorites are fondue Ticines and Fondue Fiesta and complete your meal w/ heavenly chocolate fondue!!! I am craving the food as I write....must dine place!!!! Food is amazingly delicious and great price. I love cheese and I can't get enough of it, its such a cute lil place to have a long conversation, good laugh and enjoy the food w/ nice champagne or a bottle of wine:) Perfect for any occasion...date or birthdays or just a casual dinner with friends..I know I am sounding like their marketing rep but trust me you gotta check this place out!!

Adam and I did an early VD here tonight. (Valentine's Day, you sickos.) 

Ordered the Ticinas fondue (veggies) and the Chateaubriand. I think the novelty outstrips the quality of the food; the bread is a bit stale and the potatoes served on the side would be better pre-warmed. 

Service is friendly if not overly attentive. Surroundings are nice. 

The upshot: Everything's better when you're in love. But Fondue Fred is pricey, so only three stars for y'all.

Me to waiter: "I don't know what to order, which do you like best?"
Waiter: "I don't like cheese"

We should have heeded this as a warning and left. I'm not sure how you mess up melted cheese, but it was grainy without a single pleasant thing to dip in it.

This place was not impressive at all.  We had the gouda cheese fondue, which was alright, and then we had the chateaubrian steak, which was blehhhh. I really wanted to like it, but I just wasn't a fan.  The best thing about our meal was basically the chocolate fondue, which was awesome with the fresh fruit and marshmallows, but I kinda wish they had a bigger selection of fondues to choose from.  I think they only had one option of chocolate fondue, but I prefer the places where you can choose special chocolate or different flavors or something.  

Oh, and the service was not up to par, as our server was not very pleasant and not very helpful in helping us figure out some of the items on their menu.  Maybe he didn't understand English too well, but that's no excuse. 

Also, i hate how the restaurant doesn't have a restroom so you have to take their dirty key to the outside restroom that is basically like a little hole in the wall. Soooo super dirty too. Sigh. 

I'm just gonna stick with Melting Pot or La Fondue for now..

I came here with four other people for my birthday and had an awesome time.   We ordered the Classical Fondue, the Quince Formaggio Fondue and the Chocolate Fondue. The Quince Formaggio was my favorite. We also had a side of veggies. The Chocolate Fondue came with a large plate of strawberries, melon, pineapple, bananas and marshmallows. IT WAS AMAZING!! Everyone LOVED it.  We wished we ordered two. It was my first time having fondue and it was everything I wanted to be. I like the laid back vibe of the place too.

I came to Fondue Fred's to celebrate one of my Fiance's friend's birthday.  Considering that it's called "Fondue" Fred's it should come as no surprised they serve Fondue here.  Fondue Fred's can be hard to find as they are located off of Telegraph in a building that contains several other businesses and they are toward the back right hand corner.

Fondue Fred's is a small place inside and seating is a bit cramped.  They do have "outdoor" seating in the courtyard and it is heated by heat lamps if you want a little bit more room.  We were shown our spot inside and given our menus.  They have about 20 different selections of fondues from your classic cheese, to garlic, apple, feta, asiago, blue cheese, and a couple meat type of fondue.  For the most part, most of their fondues is about $15 - $16 and comes with salad, potatoes, and bread.  For vegetarians out there they have several veggie friendly options.

They also offer party rates for 6 or more people and have the basic fondue items for $20 or the one that includes most of their specialty fondue for $23 (+17% tip).  Both of those deals include all the house wine you can drink and cheese cake and it is "all you can eat".

We decided to get the $23 deal and got the Garlic, Parmesan, Blue Cheese, Asiago, Steak, and Chicken Fondue.  We put in our order and after a short while got 2 big bowls of salad.  The salad was your typical Costco mix iceberg salad with (IMO) too much italian dressing.  We did run out of salad (I got salad scraps) but we got the waiter and he did come back about 10 minutes later with a new salad bowl.

They started to bring the dishes of potatoes, veggies, and bread, and lit the burners for the fondue.  Up first was the Parmesan, Garlic, Asiago, and Steak.  At this point the table was super crowded with food and we barely had room to move.  The potatoes were just regular boiled potatoes with a light dash of spices on it and the veggie plate was your standard Costco veggie plate.  We dug into the fondue and overall it was ok.  The Parmesan was disappointing as the swiss cheese of overwhelmed any parmesan taste.  The Garlic was very very strong, and I like garlic.  It was something you would get at the Gilroy Garlic Festival it was that strong.  The Asiago was probably the best one of the night.  It was a nice blend of flavors.  The steak one I'm mixed on.  The steak was not real "fondue" or even a hot pot.  It was more like they brought out a pot of strew and you just choose the meat/veggie you wanted and ate it off the skewer.  Most places you cook the meat, here at Fondue Fred's, you're served it already cooked in a stew.  Taste wise, it was ok, best way to describe it, it reminded me of pot roast.  After several glasses of wine and dipping, we were able to get the Chicken and Blue Cheese.  The Chicken was again served in a "stew" and already cooked.  It was a bit chewy too and no where as good as the steak.  The Blue Cheese like the garlic was overwhelmingly strong.  All of the pots had plenty of food in it and 1 pot should be more than enough for most people.

After we finished the Fondue we kind of sat there for a while.  Probably like 15 minutes+ when we got the cheese cake.  This is your basic no-bake sheet cheese cake and with some chocolate chips sprinkled on top and it tasted exactly how I described it.

After we ate our cheesecake, again sat there waiting for the bill.  During these break several of us used this time to go to the bathroom.  It's outside in the courtyard and you have to get a key to use it.

Overall we wrapped things up and paid our bill (also they don't do split Credit Card Charges, so if going in a big group, bring cash).  As to the rating, the fondue was ok.  Nothing special and nothing really stood out.  The service here was a miss.  Not much attention done and we were left waiting for periods of 10+ minute hoping to get notice or refills either on pitchers of water, wine, or even to get a can of coke or two.  The decore is nice, but it's so cramped in there.  But I have to admit, the party price of $23 is a damn good deal.  So overall this Fondue Fred's is more like a 2.5 star place, but there just isn't that extra something to get them the average mark in my book, so alas, 2.5 stars from me but a 2 Rating from Yelp.

I hadn't been to this place in 25 years and will probably wait that long before I step foot inside this depressing place again.  I was with great people and didn't have to pay, which makes all the more crappy that i hated this place.  Owner is an ass - he made weird jokes, was unfriendly and refused to get bread for all the kids with us before the meals arrived.  "No.  There will be too much food.  Don't fill your kids up with bread," he boldly stated before turning around and walking away.  The cheese (3 different varieties) had little flavor (where was the white wine, fresh cheese, herbs, one expectsf from fondue?).  The bread was lousy, the veggies limp, the potatoes overcooked and soggy, the salad freezing cold, bland veggies and overdressed with a salty bottled dressing, and the meat in the beef fondue were like cubes of Now n' Laters without the sweet fruity taste.  Chewy!
The atmosphere sucked: uncomfortable chairs and drafty and bad music.  The only thing that was decent was the chocolate fondue although cantaloupe and honey dew are bad fruit choices for dipping in chocolate.  

Fondue is not high on my list of foods to seek out in the Bay Area, but if you have the urge find somewhere else to dip your thing.
Had a fun Ladies' Nite there this past weekend.  The staff were attentive & even played our personal CDs!  My personal faves were the APPENZELLER & the FIESTA foundue.

If You want to have a PARTY... and don't want the Hassle.... This is the Place! Had My 30th B-Day here... And am Planning My 40th Here too! Always a Good Time..... Great for Large groups or Small ones... Or You can Just do a Chocolate Fondue! I cannot TELL You how many Parties I have been to Here! Great for Proms too.... Something to remember.... And the Ambiance is really Cool... it is inside a Neat old Building with Skylights and Plants and Cobblestones...... And if YOu book a Group... You pretty Much can Take over the Patio....... Can't say enough Good about it!

It gets an extra star b/c its ALL fondue and that's awesome. Was a casual , wonderful experience. We got the Fondue-teccine and it was very yummy. You get a house salad, bread and potatoes with the order too.

I absolutely hate to give bad reviews, but I had such a horrible experience, I want to make sure others do not go there.  I went there with 5 of my best gal pals for a birthday dinner. The food was horrible, all the cheese fondues tasted the same, the salad was dripping in oily dressing and the white wine (in a carafe) tasted as if they diluted it with water.  STAY AWAY from this place!
It's like, offer people unlimited food, and they'll eat anything.  I'm waiting for "Poison Pam" to open next door.  That will be one for the sociology majors to deconstruct.
I like the festive decor of the brick building in which the restaurant finds itself, but the food and service are both just OK.

I never really liked fondue until I had it at Fondue Fred.  Then again, I was pretty sheltered until I came to Berkeley.

The owner is great, and both times I've been there (once in a large group, once with my GF) he's been super friendly.  There is a group discount if there are 6 or more, and boy can the wine flow.

There are many different kinds of fondue and the recommendations we were given both times were spot on.  It's tucked away on Telegraph (if that's possible) and you can either eat inside where it's very dim or out in the courtyard which is great on a cool summer night with friends.

For fondue, it's not that expensive.  I haven't really found a better place in the Bay Area after 13 years.  Writing this review makes me want to go again.

Great atmosphere, nice owners, large portions, good selection of choices, decent prices: just don't expect gourmet. 

Now, this doesn't mean that it isn't tasty when you've been jonesing for hot melted cheese and lots of it, it's just not going to inspire any symphanies. Great for large groups!

Worst. Service. EVER. Food is decent but not worth the trip because of way the waiters and owner treat their guests. I think there were maybe three groups at the place when we went and it took us half an hour to get drinks and even longer to get an order in.

I've known about this place for close to 15 years, but never ventured to try it for various reasons (lactose intolerant mate, vegan mate, you name it!). Finally, the opportunity to finally break my Fondue Fred's cherry arose- FAMILY NIGHT! 

A little background. Family night usually consists of good friends, cigarettes, lots of alcohol, food thrown in, and cop/investigative TV shows. Lacking the TV aspect since my apt layout is too small for more than two people, and with the promise of unlimited cheese fondue, beer and/or wine, Fondue Fred was a pretty easy no-brainer.

We decided to get the party set B, which allowed us as much of any 6 fondues (even the not so cheesy, meaty ones) that we could eat, unlimited beer and wine, and cheesecake. 

Sadly, none of the cheese fondues we chose (garlic, blue, cheddar and appenzeller) were distinguishing, apart from a slight zestier flavor from one to the next but really lacking any specific taste to them at all. If they eased up on the flour base and used better quality cheeses like someone else mentioned, it would be a drastic improvement. Good cheese has so much better flavor.

I was unimpressed by the volume of food that was given to us because I'll gladly pay for additional servings if the food is good. This was not the case and I think they relied on the "quantity vs. quality"  aspect with certain eaters. The bread, which was dry on the cut edges as if it was prepped but not covered, tasted like Safeway baguettes. (as a hostess for clubs years ago I remember using those on our hors deveures trays when I wasn't able to make it to La Farine in time. Tasteless unless you're drunk and needing something to sop up alcohol.) 

The dessert- I wish we got chocolate fondue instead of cheesecake. My bro said "I can make better cheesecake than this", and I agree, even though he's got more of a savory tooth than a sweet one. Their cheesecake didn't taste much like cream cheese- it had some other sort of strange flavor to it. Not to put them down, but I think the cheesecake I've gotten at Jack in the Box when I ate fast food actually tasted better. 

 My 2 cents is it's a good place for groups but not if you're expecting good quality. Service was also a little on the odd side with our server disappearing for extended periods of time when we asked for beverages 10 minutes ago, albeit he was technically the only server. When we asked the woman that brought us our bread about the beer, she commented she didn't serve the beer. HUH? 

In all, everything was pretty unremarkable and I don't think I would pay $33 per person for that meal again.  My friends and I had fun hanging out eating and drinking, and they didn't seem to mind the food at all so that was a saving grace.

This was a first for my whole party...none of us had ever been to a fondue restaraunt before. We didn't really know what or how to order. The waiter seemed more interested in our names than offering any advice. We explained numerous times that it was our first time and asked for suggestions. We got  salads(with tons of black pepper), 3 pots of cheese and 3 LOAVES of bread. We thought we'd try the different flavored cheeses and didn't really think about the other 3 of  4 squares, meat, veggie, dessert. Well, we crammed as much down as we could...a $60 bill and no way to put the cheese in a doggie bag, will do that to you!  We left feeling bloated and sluggish. For being such good sports we took the kids to Burger King afterward, as they didn't really fill up. My daughter and godson quipped, "Hey what'd you have for dinner? Cheese, cheese and more cheese!"

My wonderful BF took me here last night as a belated V-day celebration dinner and I have to say I was really disappointed.  Now I need to clarify, I certainly wasn't disappointed in him planning an evening out, and as far as BF's go Chris is Boss!  But...Fondue Fred's is lacking in many things.  

First of all, we are kinda Fondue freaks!  Not only have we been to all the fondue places that we know of in the bay area, we also make fondue at home for friends and when we just feel like eating some cheese.  Fondue Fred's is nothing like La Fondue or even a chain fondue place like Melting Pot.  

The restaurant was staffed by what seemed a family, and some illegals who spoke ZERO english...as in not even enough to understand my request for more water.  Secondly, the fondue only comes with Bread, unless you pay extra to get mushrooms, veggies and or apples.  EXTRA for stuff to dip besides just crusty bread...to me that is LAME with a capital L!  

The fondue pots are not electric, so the cheese ends up gelatinous and then what's the point of even eating it.  They have these cheesy little flames underneath the pots, and no fancy cheese mixes at all.  I will say that the Asiago cheese fondue was yummy...but once again it didn't stay hot and liquid but became more of a goo.  

The waitress had family come in, and basically sat down and had dinner with them while leaving all of us paying customers with no server whatsoever!  We decided not to even have dessert, because we didn't want to get up and get it ourselves. 

If you are looking for good fondue, please don't waste your money here, go to Melting Pot, or the Fondue place in SF, and if you want TOP OF THE LINE fondue head down to La Fondue in Saratoga.

To be honest, I'm not a huge fan of cheese so this is going to be biased. I'm actually lactose intolerant. Harhar :o)

This was my first taste of cheese fondues though and it was definitely interesting. Not really my cup of tea though....too....much.....cheese. But I did get to try the dessert fondue also. You can't really mess up a dessert fondue though so I can't really rave about it, but it was still good!

The plus side is that this fondue place is a few minutes from my dorm because the nearest fondue place in my hometown is prob a 30 min drive. Gotta love Berkeleyy

Went here last month, and then yesterday I said "Hmmm  I could F up some Fondue.... we should do that."
The BFer reminded me that I'd spoken those same words just a few days previous....thus and therefore apparently, I am a melty cheese junky.

It's true that I've had 'better' fondue.
Like at The Left Bank- a blue/brie/goat combo that mmmm blows my mind consistently and every time.
But Fondue Fred's has the absurd courtyard for indoor/outdoor dining, a bathroom key on a bike lock chain, and that sweet sour salty mustardy dressing for the complimentary salads. How can you pass that up?
The fact that 'Fred' is part of the name of the place warms my little heart too- forcing me to think of movies like Drop Dead Fred, or of anything with little and adorable Fred Savage. Mmm I love the name Fred!! So eat here with your cheese lovin friends who have a sense of humor and have a good time- it's cheese for chrissake!

We all know that fondue is not something you can have everyday.  It's just too messy and crazy.  I recently went here for a friend's b-day.  It was  an enjoyable dining experience, but anything involving this group of girls would have been fun!

The guy who took our order kept sniffing me....that was interesting. We followed his suggestions and had plenty of food for the 5 of us.  My only complaint was that I wanted more marshmallows to go with the chocolate at the end....by the time someone came around my desire to eat bad things had passed, and I didn't want more marshmallows.

Yuck, I can't believe this place is still in business.  We went here for a birthday dinner and other than the company our experience was just terrible.  Not tasty at all (and I'm a cheese lover), expensive, and the help was surly at best.

The owner is friendly.. VERY friendly.. okay, TOO friendly. He treated my husband like a pimp to us 3 fine ladies, which meant extra attentive service, but the leering got old quickly.
The food is OK. The selection of items to dip could be more diverse, but with the prices you pay here, I think it's appropriate. I'd go just for the dessert fondue, which was the best thing we had, but still not fabulous.

My friends and I had never eaten fondue before - aside from our own melting of  Velveeta cheese - so we decided to try it out for real.

We ordered a pretty simple type of fondue, and we couldn't even go through with eating more than a few bites of it! The taste and texture were horrible! We just ended up asking the waitress to take away the cheese and we feasted on their very yummy chocolate fondue with fruit. 

Even though the cheese was very unappetizing, the chocolate fondue was great. I recommend it for an after dinner dessert place, unless you're into the whole plaster-tasting, too much wine and hardly any cheese type of fondue.

If I could give this negative stars I would.  This is hands down the worst food I've ever paid someone to serve me.  I rank it even lower than McDonald's or a microwaved burrito from the gas station. (OK so I've never actually consumed a microwave burrito from a gas station, but you get the idea.)

In both taste and appearance, their so-called "fondue" more closely resembled wallpaper paste than cheese.  We ordered the party menu, which included all the wilted-iceberg-lettuce-with-mouth-puckering-acidic-dressing-salad you can eat, all the cheap white, red, and rose wine you can pour into the plant next to you, and all the bland vegetables and white bread you need to dip into your bottomless pots of flavorless potato-starch and/or flour-based goop they sell as "fondue".  

This would have cost us a mere $23.00 per person (BTW-the prices on the restaurant's website are out of date) plus a presumptuous gratuity is automatically included, but hoping to redeem the evening, we actually opted to pay more (Party Rate #2) in order to try the "deluxe" fondues.  That cost us an extra 2 or 3 bucks per person plus the addition to the gratuity (17% or 18%).

I will say this about Fondue Fred--they were consistent.  Their service was as bad as their food.  I can not stress enough how disgusting this place is.
This place was disappointing. Stale chips, stale bread, mediocre cheese that gives you the runs--and a tad on the overpriced side. Blah.

I love fondue and this place has some good ones. However, the bread was stale and dried out when I tried it.  In my opinion, the vehicle used for dipping makes the fondue experience.  If the bread is stale, the strawberries or apples too tart, the sausage fatty etc., then the whole experience is tainted.  I was really disappointed.

The nostalgia factor was high, but Fondue Fred didn't measure up. There were 11 of us, we ordered the special: all-you-can-eat fondue, salad and cheesecake, and all you can drink of their crappy house wine. It cost $24 a person, even though their website lists it as $20. When we asked about the discrepancy we were basically told "tough luck".

And what do you get for 24 bucks? 4 pots of fondue, although it was more like 3 since the cheddar one was so revolting nobody could actually eat it. You also don't get to pick the fondue out yourself, they just bring whatever they feel like. We got 2 little carafes of wine, some bread, one plate of veggies, one plate of taters and salad with too much dressing. The yucky salad was the only thing they granted us a refill on. Dessert was a little piece of cheesecake with chocolate chips sprinkled over it.

We also got ignored, a lot. Had to beg and plead and ask 5 or 6 times for more wine and water. By the time they brought it we were ready to leave. There was a huge party outside (40 or so college kids) but that's no excuse the truly crappy service. The woman who cleared the plates before bringing dessert yelled at us for not keeping our forks. Someone asked if she could just bring us new ones and she snapped "now I'll have to wash them"!

Stay at home, make your own fondue, Fred has jumped the shark.

every time i fondued my stale bread into the cheese i was a bit surprised at its bold, nutty flavor. it obviously won me over, though. came with over-dressed salad and the wine was sweet. i couldnt get enough of it. cant wait to go back for smores :)

How is this place still in business?? My only guess is because its Berkeley's only attempt at a fondue restaurant. too bad its waaay overpriced and really low quality food. For some reason I have gotten suckered into coming here twice and I regret each visit with a vengeance.

You can pick a variety of cheese dips, which is decent, I guess. The standard meal just comes with cut up bread and poorly cooked, soggy, sliced potatoes. Your appetizer is "salad": White (not even green) iceberg lettuce, some shredded carrots and bland Italian dressing. You will look down at your meal and realize you're paying a lot for extremely low quality ingredients. 

Cause we're poor we decided to get a carafe of "house wine" instead of a name brand bottle. I guess the house this stuff came out of was that of Carlo Rossi. Mind you, there's a place and time for our good friend Carlo, but that place is a dorm room and that time is freshman year when you're bribing someone's older sibling with a fist full of $8. Carlo doesn't belong on the table of those of legal drinking age nor should he cost $20! I downed that swill cause I was celebrating after a final and all it did was get me in a lot of trouble and cause a mean hangover the next day.

The only reason I'm giving Fondue Fred any stars is the outdoor ambiance and the dessert. If you're gonna go here, bring a date for dessert only and sit outside. The patio is a cute and intimate little cove. The dessert is a big pot of melted chocolate and plate full of diced fruit and pink marshmallows! Very cute.

Do not come here for a full meal. If you want a good fondue experience do yourself a favor and make a trip into the city or jump into your time machine and go back to your grandparent's dinner party in 1974.

I haved mixed feelings after reading the other Yelp reviews about this place.  I have truly enjoyed coming to Fondue Fred's everytime I've been here.  I have been coming here for many years.  

Perfect location, good prices, tasty food (maybe not authentic, but tasty), and personal service.    No complaints from me.

When I walked in with my group of ten (we had a reservation for 6pm which I had called to confirm earlier in the day) we were ignored for at least ten minutes. Finally I proactively tracked someone down and then the owner of the restaurant went on to tell me that my reservation was for 5 o'clock. Um, no. 6 o'clock. I argued, he pretty much ignored me and reluctantly seated us. Strangely, from then on, the service was GREAT! Especially for such a large group. I had never eaten fondue before so I'm not sure where it ranks on the fondue scale but I'd go back. The meatball fondue was good as was the chateaubriand (sp?), even though I wouldn't really call it chateaubriand. The cheese was good and appropriately unhealthy tasting. The chicken fondue was quite bland; if you get it, get some cheese at the same time! The cheesecake was on the house and it could've been better, but can you really complain about free cheesecake? I'm giving the owner the strong benefit of the doubt because he did an impressive one eighty but if he was ever rude again, I'd never return. 

We got the group deal, with wine, and I think it was a good deal. We definitely had fun!

Fondue Fred is a great idea - but HORRIBLE execution. Not sure what was worse, the food or the service.

We made reservations a month in advance & went as a party of 6. When we arrived, the owner/host said we had no reservations. Well, I had personally made the reservations - and he went so far as to imply that I was lying.

We were seated, and after 2 hours we left hungry and angry. For a bunch of money, you can expect:

- REALLY poor service
- a bowl of stale bread
- a watery plate of bagged salad
- some greasy gross goo that should worry you to eat

We had stupidly ordered a fondue with shrimp & actually SAW the in the kitchen (which is right there) pull out a giant costco sized bag of frozen shrimp & hack at it with an ice pick. Seriously folks, it doesn't get any worse than this.

At this point, we paid in full before we received that shrimp course & headed to Chow in Lafayette for a fabulous late night dinner. We laughed for a long time. I can't believe this dive is still in business.

Horrible, rude service from the staff and the owner. The owner is such a @$%&**!! I do not recommend this place for groups. Actually, I don't recommend this place to anyone. The owner humiliated me on my birthday in front of my friends and ruined everyone's evening. If you like to be treated with disrespect and being overcharged, Fondue Fred is your ideal oasis. I will never in my life return to this dump!!!

I had dinner here on Saturday, 1/23/10 as part of a large group (34). We were seated outside at a very long table in the covered Courtyard,  good thing they had heat lamps. After some deliberation beforehand, we had decided to go for Prix Fixe option, ($33 including tax & tip)where you can have as much as you like of any 6 of the dozen fondues, along with as much house wine (Burgundy, Chablis and Rosé) as you like.  We had the extra-cost Chocolate Fondue thrown in for free.

Service was indifferent, at best. The meal started with a bowl of ready-made salad, the boring-kind you buy at bulk stores. Then the servers plopped down "Caquelots" (enamelled cast iron bowls) of whatever fondue they felt like, (although we had requested from a list) lit the warmers, and scurried off. You had to grab the servers' attention and ask them to bring you more fondues as they were not volunteering to do so, nor asking if we wanted more wine or fondues (it was as much of both as you liked), much less asking us how our dinner was. Looks like they have a "Don't ask, don't offer" policy. 

The "Chateaubriand," "Coq au Fondue" (Chicken) and Meatball "Fondues" were AWFUL, despite the descriptions, as were strange concoctions, which they attempt to pass off as "Fondue" because it was neither Bourguinonne (hot oil) or Hot-Pot style, (Broth), where you dip your raw ingredients to cook in. Instead these like an already pre-cooked casseroles. For example, the "Meatball Fondue" was just some meatballs in a tomato (spaghetti?) sauce. The "Chateaubriand Fondue" was some steak slivers swimming in some oily liquid with some mushrooms. The only fondues worthy of the name were the "Classic" and the "Appenzeller." Even then, it tasted like they use a lot of plain, white cheddar cheese. For dunking, we got chunks of plain bread, (certainly not baguettes, as their website claims) tasteless chunks of baked potatoes and a tray of sliced veggies. 

Chocolate Fondue was decent, with slices of apple, bananas, pineapple and marshmallows, but on the other hand, how difficult it is to make a chocolate fondue? "We use only the Finest imported Swiss Cheeses"? Methinks NOT! Pleeze! If you want REAL and tasty fondues, go elsewhere.  

The Owner's wife (Laleh) sorely needs some lessons in Customer Service. She was very rude towards our organizer, when the latter requested knives, and anyways, none were ever brought out. Seems like this lady has an aversion to washing cutlery, as per other reviews here. Towards the end of the meal, a couple of us ordered coffee, and she seemed irritated at this request and in a loud voice demanded: "YOU WILL HAVE TO PAY EXTRA FOR IT!!!""  We sure DID, because we had 10 (TEN) coffees tacked on to our bill, when this was NOT at all the case! The least she could have done was to politely say: "Sir, with pleasure, but this is not included." or even better, offered coffee to us for FREE.  After all, we dropped over $1,200 at her establishment, and am sure she loves the money that large groups like ours leave behind.

To add insult to injury, she made sure that everybody got  handed fliers about their Valentine's Day Dinner, and a second one  promoting their other restaurant, some Tapas place they own in Berkeley. Needless to say, none of us were interested in returning or in patronizing any of their other establishments, given the abysmal level of customer service.

Am not being harsh, just relating the facts of my experience, after all, a fondue is an experience, not just some melted cheese in a pot. I know profit margins are very slim in the restaurant business, but now, more than ever, this is no excuse for unfriendly, shoddy customer service and mediocre food. Even good, highly-rated restaurants, sadly come and go,

If you happen to be a large group, and decide to eat here, despite the warnings of this and other reviews (anybody who gives this place 5-stars must be the owners or doesn't know what fondues are), be deadly accurate and document the number of guests, because we were overcharged for a non-existant additional guest. The unfriendly lady owner insisted that we were 35 when in reality, we were 34. Needless to say, we will NEVER patronize this place ever again!

To sum up, if you happen to be in the area, are hungry for some mediocre, at best, fondue, and are not very particular about the quality of food and service, you could consider dining here. Larger groups, stay away!

I went here for my birthday party. We had a blast. All you can eat and drink of specified items. Make sure everyone has the same type of diet. If you get twelve or more people in your group you get a free shirt (plain grey...). 
  I feel that if you give them notice of how big your party is , you have a better time. Be prepared to convince them though, they get parties of 20 where 7 people show up. I told them 15 to 20 and 27 people showed up. He needed help. We did get a bonus meatball dish not included in our package though! Deeee-licious!
   Chill area, not too many bums around. We smoked a couple of joints around the corner during our three hours there with no fuss. Also, if you have a big party, they let you bring YOUR music to play. I want to try it for a sweet date sometime.
   Parties be warned! Beware friends that show up and say they are not going to eat but just hang out. They lie. The staff takes a head count of whoever is partaking and you will be in an uncomfortable position when the bill comes. A standard rationale is that two friends come and one says they are not eating. In their mind, it is probably like this: " We are not that hungry, so we will pay for one person, and both of us eat and it will equal one hungry person." Not true. They take a head count so be prepared, and HAVE FUN

I was a little hesitant to come here after reading all the other reviews.  But I was anxious because I have never been to a fondue restaurant before.  I've had fondue in the privacy of my own home prior to coming here, but that isn't a true fondue experience because burnt chocolate and solidified cheese doesn't quite count. 

A group of 9 of us came here for dinner and shared two cheese, two meat and two chocolate fondues, each paying $15 including tax/tips, and we were all stuffed.   I wasn't quite fond of the asiago cheese fondue, as it was so strong and pungent. I liked the meat fondues, especially the steak, but if I had to choose between cheese or meat, I'd go with the cheese.  Served with plenty of bread and potatoes for the meat and cheese fondues, and plenty of fruits/marshmellows for the chocolate one. 

Overall, 3 stars at the most.

Fondue Fred is not fancy schmancy fondue.  Oh noes.  This is the kind of fondue place where they really should serve tall boys and 40s.  For reals.

Nonetheless I came here for dinner not too long ago and had a very nice and funny time.  The cheese fondues all looked and tasted somewhat the same with just a little difference between them.  The only one that stood out to me was the spicy fondue and the garlicy one.  The meat and chicken fondues were just like eating campbell's thick and chunky soup.  The veggies that you got to dip in your fondue pots didn't look like the freshest in the world.  It wouldn't have surprised me if they came straight out of a veggie bag bought at Food Maxx or something.

Things I liked about this place were that the dude didn't bat an eye when I ordered a pitcher of Red Hook and asked him to keep the glass because I was drinking straight from the pitcher.  He actually liked it and called me *Beer Guy* all night.  Another big plus was the UNLIMITED CHEESECAKE!!!  I ate so much cheesecake it was ridiculous.

Y'all know what happends when you mix beer and cheesecake?  Yeah, talk about sonic boom when I got home.  I have no one to blame but myself though.  This place definitely has it's place in the fondue world and being located so close to UC Berkeley it's target audience is not the ascot wearing crowd...unless we are talking about douchebag hipsters.

*I forgot to mention that if you get the chocolate fondue ask them to give you all PINK marshmallows!

I am a huge cheese fan, HUGE, so I love fondue. If I didn't care about my health at all, I would totally eat it every day and be a happy camper. 

Fondue Fred's is my go-to fondue place because I like Berkeley and it's the closest fondue restaurant to where I live. I came here tonight and was very impressed again. The service was decent, but the fondue was outstanding. We had the garlic fondue which was amazing, and the beef cheese-less fondue (I think it was #17). It comes in a crock-pot type thing and was like a beef stew with mushrooms. It was SO HOT thought, so it made it a little difficult to eat. The garlic fondue was also really, really hot, which led to us experimenting with the burners (you can turn them up or down). Luckily we didn't burn the place down. 

We stuffed ourselves silly but couldn't resist having the chocolate fondue for dessert. It was SOOOOO good. Oh my gosh. It came with marshmellows (which I like burned, like you can do at a campfire), strawberrys, cantaloupe, honeydew, and apples.  The prices are reasonable, and most of the choices are between $14-18 I think. Our server, which might have been the owner, forgot to bring my coke, but I think it was meant to be, because this way I only had water so I could intake more fondue...and the more cheese the better!

The whole idea of fondue and dipping things in cheese and sauces is mouth watering, so I really wanted to try out a Fondue place. I purchased a restaurant.com gift certificate and decided to give Fondue Fred a chance with a couple friends. 

When I got there, I did not know what to expect. This place has been around for over 50 years. The place is small and located in a mall that looks like an old Disneyland Village with lots of different shops. We arrived at Fondue Fred and felt the place was in dire need of a makeover. That aside, we decided to go for it and order up a couple pots of fondue and such and a pitcher of Hefeweizen. 

The place really is a great place for groups because of the way the meals are set up. You pick your fondue, it comes with a standard green salad, lots of diced fresh sourdough and roasted red potatoes. The waitress/ owner suggested that we order a cheese fondue in addition to our meat selections. Each pot was around $16-17.

We chose the: 
* Beef Burgundy Fondue: Not actually cheese at all, but stewed chunks of steak in a gravy with mushrooms and they put raw broccoli on top that cooks as you eat the fondue. 
* Parmesan Fondue: Cheesy Cheesy! Seriously when dipping the cheese did not stop. Topped with a couple slices of pepperoni and mushrooms. This was great dipping for everything. 
* Beef Meatball Marinara: OMG, these were so good. Nuff said. 

Then the dipping began. It was easy to want to EVERYTHING. Go ahead and dip the beef in the cheese, then the marinara. The meatballs in the cheese and the bread and potatoes in everything. It was a dipping fest and even after we were full, we were still dipping. 

It was a lot of food, but we all really liked it and left feeling very satisfied and glad we tried a new fondue place.

Delicious.

I understand what one of the yelpers said about the service not quite matching the warm decor.

I asked for two entrees. 

Fezenjoon -waiter asked if I wanted chicken or meatballs.  I asked for meatballs.  Waiter confirmed I did not want the chicken, but the meatballs instead.  However, I got chicken.  And it was dry...

I also got the lamb.  Yes, it WAS delicious.  Somehow, I am a fan of raisins and sultanas with meat.  :)  I'm also a fan of when touching the meat, that it practically falls off the bone.

Lots of rice.  Did I say lots of rice?  I sure got lots of rice.  lol.

The faloudeh, that was awesome.  They serviced it with a slice of Meyer lemon.  

I'll be back for the koubideh, if I can round up another person to go with me.

we just happened in, for lunch, and had a delicious meal.

they serve flatbread with onions spiced with sumac in lieu of bread--it was fantastic!  we ordered the yogurt with garlic and the roasted eggplant as appetizers--and would highly recommend both.

the mediterrean salad was substantial and delicious.  the lentil soup only slighlty dissappointing--not quite flavorful enough (but perhaps all the yogurt and garlic had dulled my ability to discern flavors).

Attentive service and very nice atmosphere.

Looking forward to going back.
Only 3.5 stars!? Are you kidding? Apparently Non- Persians are wasting their time rating this place. This place is AWESOME! Nuf said! Don't skip the deserts!

I've been raised with Persian food all my life and have given a try to many restaurants in southern and northern CA. 

One that sticks out for being probably one of the worse is Alborz in Berkeley. Typical Persian restaurants should be packed on a Saturday at about 1pm. When I drove from Marin to meet my parents halfway (they came from Walnut Creek) I asked them to meet at Alborz since its convenient. Well we met there and my folks ordered the Alborz for two and I ordered the soltani. The rice looked and tasted like as if it was made 5 days before and they just reheated the dish in the microwave. The barg was hard as a car tire and the koobideh was terrible as well. Long story short, the food gave the three of us the runs for 1.5 days and I can truly say that the experience was awful. Now I like giving the restaurants the benefit of the doubt, so I was brave enough to go back and get a stew dish, khoreshteh ghaimeh and it was very mooshy and water down. 

By the way, the Walnut Creek Alborz is no better and I think one or both of them will be closing soon. 

Its too bad, cause we need more good Persian restaurants like Sahalizaar in Belmont out in the bay area.

Wow! I've known about this restaurant in Berkeley for a while and finally decided to give it a try. But before I dropped in I just wanted to make sure they had one or two of my favorite Persian dishes so I called and asked about the menu. The guy answered something like this: Kibeetigeu thabatiki thsbee elp u? Now he was speaking in english, okay? Do you understand what he said? NO! I didn't think so. I didn't understand him either- he's just a cocky twirp! The guy, sounded like between 25-45 yrs old, and had a Persian accent. He was cocky & rude- he was a very polite asshole if you know what I mean. He obviously never had anyone teach him how to answer the phone professionally- nice, clear, business name, your name,etc. No! For him it's all just a blur- blablablablabalbla- bla- elp-U? Very rude!  I'll never even end up trying this place out!!! My questions were very simple for anyone who knows Persian dishes. I just wanted to know a couple things about the food before I order but this guy was making it very difficult. His answers were not answers. He was short and really gave me misinfo, so I asked if there was anyone there who knows the menu well enough to answer my questions & he just said no. What a prick!! He was just lying. His whole demeanor was cocky, and short the whole conversation! Trust me, don't eat here! If they're like that on the phone there's a lot behind the scene you don't know about!! The food is probably just as crappy as their attitude!
The food was not the best persian food i have had. The rice seemed old and dry, but not too bad, just a little pricey.

Overpriced for the quality of food.  I shared the combo appetizer, a couple kebabs, and a couple lamb dishes.  Don't bother ordering the lamb with white beans, but the lamb with eggplant was probably the best thing we had.  The flavor was good, but I've had much better lamb.  The chicken kebab was dry, the kofta kebab was tastier but nothing great.  I can't say i really liked anything from the appetizer plate.

Very delicious Persian food! The lamb skewers are awesome - very flavorful! We ordered grilled chicken and lamb skewers and our dishes came with plenty of rice and grilled tomato on the side. Great service. I ordered the yogurt drink but it was kind of salty for my taste.. Otherwise, this is a good place to try good quality Persian food, especially if you like kabobs and grilled meat!

First time having Persian food at a restaurant and WOW.  The pomegranate chicken with saffron rice is something special.  
It's a nice restaurant, and thus pricey for everyday dining, but I would definitely come back.

A mixed experience: good wine, bad salad (too much dressing & had to ask for the Kalamata olives which were missing), good lamb shank (very tender) & rice, terrible ice cream (bits of ice inside), lackadaisical service, rather grubby interior. Persian food can be terrific, but this wasn't worth it--won't be back.

A friend took me here last week as a birthday celebration.  It was unplanned and we stumbled onto it before a show.  I'm glad we stumbled!  The food was delicious with a capital D.  The Dolmeh was the best I've every had and half chicken was incredible.  It came out in a savory thick soupy sauce that was so flavorful with the tender chicken and Persian rice.  I will take my parents here when they visit this spring and surely many other times, too.

Came here for a get together with old friends at around 7:30. Waddled out of the restaurant at 11 PM, well past their listed closing time...So nice that they waited on turning the light off on us until then. :) I had been passing this restaurant daily ignorant of the decadent foods that resided inside. C for Classy. Dimmed lighting and all that jazz. Apparently the kitchen is run mostly by a Persian grandmother, so big shoutout to her. 

Part of my awesome experience here was that I had the luck of being with a group who were very familiar with Persian food, The person who took the lead on ordering even spoke Farsi. Such a beautiful language! The server was super nice and accommodating. He brought out samples of red wine. Decided on a bottle of Cabernet. Went nicely with the meal. 

THE FEAST! Did this family style. HELL YEH

I love complimentary food! Twist on bread&butter. There was a Paired with onions and butter! They also brought out delicious yogurt and tomato/cucumber dishes. We went through 3 baskets full of bread. :)

2 orders of beef and lamb kabobs, which came out with a grilled tomato. Both were good but I preferred lamb because it was just SO tender. It came out on the bone and it was just perfectly cooked! 

Lamb and eggplant stew. SO GOOD. Probably my favorite dish because the flavors of the stew which had mini grapes in them just infused into the whole lamb shank. The meat literally fell off the bone. LAMB GALORE! My favorite meat.

For the rice, we got saffron rice apparently because this type of rice pairs really nicely with lamb. This was a HUGE heap of rice. I must have gotten 3-4 servings. Addicting and went well with the entrees.

Dessert: Baklava. My Persian and Afghan friends, the best baklava they have ever tasted. A lot of baklava apparently gets really dry because some places use walnuts. This restaurant uses pistachios and hits the perfect balance of soft and flaky. It's a pretty decent size, too! We also tried a dessert with what I can best be described as balls of donut. I think they said something about spun sugar? I wish I remembered the name of these dishes but we just had way too many dishes. This paired perfectly with our mint soaked teas. With actual mint leaves inside the tea, it reminded me of a tea version of mojitos. We got free refills, too! :) You can hold a piece of sugar in your mouth and drink the tea and feel the sugar disentegrate and fuse deliciously with the tea. YUM. Perfect end to the meal. 

Dishes were on the pricey side, but it was worth it because of the quantity. We had the honor of having former runner-up for Mr. Lebanon help out a little with the tab even though he only got a glass of white wine, so the price wasn't to harsh on our wallet. $31 for all that food is a steallll. I think this place would be cool to come to with a big group again or a date. Maybe split a plate. Nonetheless, I shall be back for some more Baklava and lamb!

Went in for a quick lunch before a movie.  The service was super fast and the food was amazing.  

I had beef meatballs in a pomegranate sauce over safron rice, and it was absolutely amazing!  My friends had the chicken and beef koobideh, which went great when dipped in the pomegranate sauce.  For appetizers, we had this thick, creamy hummus and a minty onion dipping sauce.  

I'll definitely be going again!

I took my best friend here for her birthday. I tried the a lamb shank & eggplant sauce with some basmati rice. It was very delicious. The lamb was cooked beautifully, and the meat practically fell off when I touched it with my fork. The eggplant and sauce was also with not too much tomato but a perfect blend of spices. 

I paid about $15 for the dish, which I find is pretty darn reasonable considering the ambiance of this place is pretty high class, and least to say my friend and I really enjoyed the food. Parking is hard though, which is normal around Berkeley but probably the only reason I would probably not drive all the way back here to eat again. 

I loved the food, just hated the parking problem and it's not a place to go if you are in a hurry since the service isn't super fast.

Not the correct proportions!!! Ok, I might be a more carnivore than an omnivore and would like to have enough good meat on my plate at the same time with veggies and rice. We were there for a lunch and got the special of the day "Lamb stew". It tasted good but the lamb amount was 1/3 of what it should have had been and also half of that was fat. I get excited to go to kebab/middle eastern/mediterranean places but get really disappointed when I see the unfairness done in these places for some great dishes. It is way overpriced for the huge pile of rice you have to eat to fill yourself. Not going back there...

Food was excellent!  Grilled chicken and ground chicken kabobs were very tasty!  The salad and rice were plentiful.  They make sure you leave stuffed!

Try the ice cream!  It is a must have.  The ice cream is curned in rose water and has a distinctive taste to it.  Once you take a few spoon fulls you will be in love!
This place is absolutely delicious!!

I can't testify to the authenticity of the food vis a vis being Persian. All I know is that this is my new favorite Berkeley restaurant. The service was very very good (a little leisurely for our theatre going needs, but it was fine). We were given the option of replacing half or all of the rice in our entrees with salad. The salad alone was fantastic - fresh and beautiful, not overdressed. Four of us shared the combo appetizer platter, I had a cup of the Asah Reshteh (soup - VERY filling) and the Cornish Hen kabob. Tender and large portions. One friend had the salmon kabob, another the Baked chicken with fantastic saffron rice mixed with nuts, orange peel, and more. We had to try the Faloodeh (frozen sweet rose water with rice noodles) - light and refreshing. One reviewer said they thought it was fancy - wow, must be a student. It's a very nice atmosphere, but I wouldn't say fancy. And the prices are great for what you get.  I can't wait to go back!

This was the first time my BF and I ever tried Persian cuisine. We wanted to try something different; we often eat a variety of Asian cuisines, Mexican, Spanish, French, Californian, Greek, etc. Recently, we've been exploring Middle Eastern cuisines and have discovered a world of spices, herbs, and sauces that are entirely foreign to our tongues, in a good way. 
Alborz was our first attempt at Persian food. I suppose it would have been more helpful if we had a friend or someone who could have advised us on the popular and common dishes. Our server, upon our request, did recommend some items and showed us the way to eat what was brought to our table. His recommendation was a kebobs plate, which I thought was the safest and least effort recommendation. Before I could object, my BF said okay we'll have that. Err. There were 3 types of meat for about $33: chicken, beef, and a ground lamb patty. I thought it was expensive for the plate. I also only really appreciated the chicken. The beef wasn't good and I'm just not a lamb patty person. As for appetizer, we were recommended the combination plate with herbs, cheese, yogurt, nuts, and several other items that I can't name. The rice wrapped leaves and the dark green spongy slice that somewhat resembled a quiche was yummy. Overall, I thought we had a good meal but I've discovered I don't like the yogurt, which appears to be an integral part of persian cuisine. However, I do think there are many dishes that I would enjoy, only if someone would explain it all to me. Hehehe...
As for the rest. the server was nice but did not appear enthusiastic about helping us out. The prices seemed high but the rest. did have a nice atmosphere.

Alborz is where I go when I want yummy Persian food. The koobideh and chicken kabobs are so savory  and tendor and the portions are generous.  It's a little pricey, so I do a lot of take-out orders so that I don't get carried away with ordering appetizers.  I can bring an order home and have it for dinner and save the extra to enjoy again for lunch the next day!

Alborz is the place I come to when I want excellent Persian food .

This place has excellent kabobs and the portions are huge.  I always end up taking some back home for lunch the next day.  Food prices are around the 10-15 dollar range but with that price you get excellent dishes, good waiters, a nice and clean restaurant plus endless yogurt with lavash (Persian bread).
