If you are ever in the University area of Berkley I would recommend trying Alborz if you want to eat some authentic Persian food

4.8.2009

I was confused when I received my very heavy bag of take out because I had only ordered one entrée. When I started to unpack the tower of containers I was absolutely lost. I got slightly toasted pieces of lavash wrapped in plastic, what seemed to be tomato/vegetable soup, and half a raw onion. I, then, was hoping there was an instruction sheet, but no such luck. Was that tomato liquid a soup or a dip for the lavash? What was I suppose to do with half a raw onion? Put it in the tomato liquid, entrée, lavash? Was it placed in my bag by mistake? Help please.

When I saw the Shirin Polo, I thought it looked absolutely gorgeous. It was a striking yellow from the saffron, orange from the orange zest, gold from the golden raisins, green from the pistachios, white from slivered almonds. It looked like a breathtaking sunrise to what will be a warm sunny day with a slight breeze. 

The flavors of the dish could be balanced better. The rice mixture had a very fragrant flavor from the saffron and orange zest, which was almost like eating perfume. Both the pistachio and almond were overshadowed by the fragrances, so all it did to the dish was add another layer of texture in addition to the softness from the basmati itself and the chewiness from the golden raisins and the zest. As for the chicken, it was seasoned well and both the breast and leg weren't dry.

Very good  Persian cuisine.  Having said that I must admit I do not venture out too far and typically stick with the saffron rice, beef kabobs.  Very nice service, friendly wait staff I will return once again for sure

All 3 stars are for the Khoresht Bodemjan, or lamb with eggplant. And maybe a fraction of a star for their super decked-out bathroom. But 0 stars for service.

Two of my friends and I decide to come here for dinner. I had come from proctoring a midterm, so all of us still had our backpacks (my friends graciously waited for me so we could catch a 9 PM dinner :3). We got to Alborz at around 9:30, which I admit is late but is still before their closing hours.

However. The entire time we were looking at the menu, the female owner kept giving us glances and telling our server that the kitchen was closing soon. As a dutiful Yelper, I already had an idea of what to order, but I didn't appreciate her 'tude.

I think our server was deaf, except for taking orders. After he brought us our appetizer, sangak with raw onions (aka pita with cilantro-sumac-onions and butter pats) and filled our water, he completely ignored additional requests for water refills. Or our check, which totaled to $38 (not bad for 2 entrees feeding 3 hungry college students). We had to ask the irritated owner for that.

Now. On to the food.

We ordered the CHICKEN KOOBIDEH, $14.95, which came with two long strips of very yellow chicken kebab, a serving of saffron rice, and a stewed whole tomato. The chicken kebab had the texture of a fish ball used for hot pot. The portion was decent, but the taste was meh.

The glorious KHORESHT BODEMHAN, $15.95, was stewed lamb with a sliver of eggplant and a stewed whole tomato. omgoodness the lamb was so tender and succulent!!! PURE BLISS. The eggplant was really good too! I really wish they gave us more than one slice of eggplant. And the sauce was great drizzled on top of the rice from the chicken koobideh dish. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Super fancy bathroom. Discriminating staff (just like my beef with Kingston 11--you operate one block from a college campus, so expect to get some casually dressed college kids as your customers...OR NOT).

It was my first time getting Middle Eastern food and it was delish! The service was prompt but a bit serious for my taste. However, it was super classy.. which is NOT the case in the general Berkeley campus area so it was a nice change of pace.

Taste: 3
Value: 2
Service: 4

I came here once with a group of friends for someone's birthday, most of whom I didn't know, about 1-2 years ago. From what I remember, the food was definitely unique and an experience, but I didn't think it was that good. The food was unique, but none of it really stood out. Also, it is quite expensive, so keep that in mind. Definitely not worth the price.

IMHO, this place has some dishes which are amazing, but also a couple popular one's that miss the spot. Stick to the recommended dishes and you can't go wrong. If the prices were better I'd have given them 5 stars, because you can't expect every dish to be great.

My Recommendations:


APPETIZERS

-Tahdig (with choice of stew Ghormeh Sabzi or Fesenjan)
-Mast o Khiyar OR Mast Musir (Two delicious yogurt dishes)


MEAT SKEWERS (w/Rice or Salad)

-Shishlik (lambchops, this is delicious. but I don't think many people try it)

-Kubideh (ground beef kabob)

-Joojej Kaboab on the bone (Chicken Kabob, the one on bone is really good, the chicken breast one is a bit dry)


STEWS

-Fesenjan (pomegranate stew with chicken and rice)

-Ghormeh Sabzi (stew of greens with lima beens and lamb/beef)


To Avoid:

- Gheymeh 
- Joojeh Kabob without bone (a bit dry)
- Barg (Filet beef, is also bit dry)

On a recent visit to Alborz we had hummus, dolmas and various kebabs.  My kebab was lamb tenderloin which was good, but was a lot of food, and was served with a ridiculously large amount of rice.  Our server brought the sumac (spice) to the table and gave us instructions on how to use it - maybe he's been reading Yelp!  My husband had the filet mignon/ground beef combo which I tasted and was also pretty good.  Alborz definiteley seemed like a place for carnivores, so vegetarians beware.

At the time being, this one of the better Persian restaurants in Berkeley that I've tried.  Still does not compare to some of the places that I go to in the South Bay, but it does satisfy my kabob cravings.

The dish I normally get would be the chicken kabob (i.e. joojeh) plate.  The kabob is properly spiced and is quite tender, the rice there has always been fluffy and the meal is accompanied by lavish bread.  I've also tried the salmon here before and while it was good, it did have a slight fishy taste to it that I was able to get over by squirting some lemon in it.  

The meal could be considered a bit pricy, but for standard Persian fare, it's the right price.  The service is a bit slow and the servers are a bit reserved, but not awful.

Big portions. Attentive Staff. Nice ambiance. It's a gem. Not many Persian restaurants in the East Bay. 
I've eaten here twice in the past two weeks!

The Ground Beef Kabob with rice and a side of Torshi Leetah (yogurt with shallot dip) was Excellent. The free pita bread they give you before the meal wasn't too good, but who cares.

Highly recommend this place. Best Persian food in the East Bay (significantly better than I Squared in Rockridge)

So I came here with my muffin Sarvi! It was a random outing to the city of many eats and just walking! Fun stuff right? LOL So I got the beef and chicken kabobs, rice and veggies and lemme tell you!! THAT is smacking.... yogurt with the red powder stuff!!! O- YAAAA!!! GET IT IN THERE.. ALL NICE AND DEEP LIKE!! hahahah (movie quote) The atmosphere is lovely and pleasant! The servers are very kind and motherly! LOVE IT!

Sarvi got the lamb and rice and cucumber salad. I tasted it too!! That was good!!! SOOO when I come back to Berkeley! This will be another one of my many eats!! ME LIKES!!

I love coming here, but had forgotten how huge the portions were. I ordered a chicken kabob dish that came with two skewers and a huge amount of rice. I had enough to take home; incidentally, I didn't finish dinner so that I could leave room for dessert--the iced noodle rose water dish. The only thing that bothered me about the meal is that in the not so recent past the restaurant used to include a small dish of yogurt with the lavash. This time around it was lavash and raw onions only. The yogurt helps to take the edge off the onions.

Just okay. Kabul had set my standards high for middle eastern food. 

The rice was bland. I had to salt it several times! The food was over priced for the quality. The chicken was moist, but also lacked flavor.  

The server wasn't very friendly.
Tasty but pricey for the portion and decent quality.

Finally had a chance to go back here sans... Anyway, since my uncle hasn't tried Persian food--this was the perfect opportunity to do so since bro and I were craving it for awhile now.

We got here and there weren't that many people dining on a Saturday night. Recession. We got seated right away by our usual server. 

Menu design changed (yes I noticed stuff like that...) and believe me ... I actually complemented the typography used - it was very clean and elegant.

Anyway... all 3 of us ordered koobideh, wine glasses for bro and I and beer for my uncle.

Food came out pretty quick... the grubbed came faster =)

Overall, food still consistent as well as service. Uncle was happy and so are we...

Alborz is the best Persian food in the bay area.  As a Persian, you should trust me.  

My mom's Persian food is a 6, Persian food in Los Angeles is a 5.5, but for the Bay...this is as good as it gets.

Get some kabob...you'll like it.
Yum. How do they make that rice? Seriously? A classy restaurant, not to fancy, but don't walk in with sweatpants on. Great service and really great food - fresh - that is filling. Nice.

Ended up here after wandering around in the rain on Saturday night without reservations, following the Arab Film Fest (yes, I'm aware of the irony). The large, warm room and immediate seating fit the bill. My Arab dinner companions were delighted with the Persian noodle soup (dill?), combination platter (huge - it's a meal, not an appetizer!) and Mediterranean salad (greens, kalamata olives, feta, red onion, beets, pomegranate vinaigrette). Given all the lamb and saffron options, I had a hard time deciding and finally settled on the kabob of Cornish hen brushed with lime & saffron and a side of saffron rice with orange peel, pistachios and golden raisins. My plate arrived, as huge and golden as the sun. Who knew a little game hen had so many pieces on her? The meat was tender and well-grilled, the rice aromatic and light as air. The only minuses: the dirty sheepskin on the chair in the Ladies Room, a tiny cockroach on our table, the weak Turkish coffee.

a review for alborz is long overdue.  

i've come to this place many, many times.  lunchtime during the summers, dinners before class, and nighttime chomp and gabs with my BF and my BFFs.  

i started off with the only thing i knew on the menu - the koobideh.  uhhh...delicious!!!  then i became more adventurous under the guidance of my close persian friend.  i dabbled in fesenjoon over tah dig.  on another occassion we did the lambshank.  DELICIOUS.  the falloodeh is off the hook for dessert.  rosewater sorbet-like with rice noodles soaked in fresh lemon juice.  CRAZY DELICIOUS.

the service is always fast and i'm never left waiting for anything for too long.  the ambiance here is way better than the alborz in the city.  and, parking is never a hassle.

i haven't been here since february.  i think it's high time i paid them another visit...

Was introduced to this restaurant by my ex., and was pleasantly surprised  to find a decent Persian restaurant in my own back yard. 

Lunch prices are decent. So far I have only tried their kabobs, and they are excellent. 

I am not Persian, and I would have to recommend to all those who are not to definitely give this exquisite cuisine a try. Once you have it though, I think you will  become a regular!

Are you kidding me? This place is a joke.

Four friends and I just went to Alborz because we craved Persian food. After sitting down, it took 30 minutes for someone to come check on us. 30 minutes later, the burnt food came... Being hungry, we shoved what we could down and tried to leave. Of course, we had to wait another 30 minutes for someone to come with the check. 

When we saw the check, our meal for FIVE people cost almost $20 more than it should have.. Why? They charged us a 17% gratuity. We checked the menu and it explicitly said "17% for party of SIX and over." Being poor college students, we asked why we were charged the mandatory gratuity, even though the menu EXPLICITLY said otherwise. Apparently, a restaurant can charge whatever they want to whoever they want... Sounds like a bunch of BS to me.

Service was horrible. Meal was expensive and burnt... Not recommended.

I Love this place. I've never had Persian food before and I am now a major fan!! They make a walnut pomegranate chicken that is to die for. The safron rice is incredible! The lady that served us was very kind and attentive. I'll definately go back with another date. =D

We were here for a late lunch on Wednesday. House flat bread served with butter...kinda weird...should be served with hummus.  We ordered the special kabob plate for two ($32.95); lamb and filet mignon kabob. We asked to be served family style. Large platter of meat, four roasted roma tomatoes (no salad) and we each had a full plate of fluffy basmati rice.  Meat was tendered and cooked perfectly. Not overly spiced, you can really taste the meat....nice and clean tasting. Lamb was our favorite, didn't care for the filet mignon.  Should had ordered a salad and maybe the yogurt dip to go with the meat.

Friend ordered the yogurt soda.....expected it to be sweet, like a soda....we were in for a surprise as it was not sweet.....more sour to me.  Turkish coffee was muddy halfway through the tiny little cup.

Service was good, not excellent. Decor was nice enough for a birthday celebration.  No parking lot, city parking near the restaurant (meter machine does not take bills, bring coins or use credit card).  Across the street from the UC Berkeley campus.

Food is good! I'm not a big meat lover, but the chicken, ground beef, and fillet mignon that we got was SOOOO GOOD!!! If it wasn't so expensive, I would have ordered more food! 

The waiter was super nice, that's always a plus! But don't be fooled! This is NOT a TWO DOLLAR SIGN RESTAURANT!!! Try more like THREE DOLLAR SIGNS!!!

Yet another Persian food review from an Iranian dude. This place was freakin awesome. I judge Persian food based on family cooking that I have had. This place is very good. We went with 5 people so I tried everyones stuff so I could make a fair review. Everything I had was very good. We got bread with free Must-o-Khiar (yogurt with cucumber) with onions on the side (amazing). We ordered some eggplant (I can't remember the name now) and it was amazing also. My fiance who doesn't like eggplant at all loved it.

I had Gormeh Zabzi and it was wonderful. I tried Joojeh Kabob (chicken), and Soltani ( mix of barg  and chelo kabab). This place did everything very well  and even the tea was good. The only thing is I like to try the Persian Ice cream (rose flavored with pistacio) but I was way too full to try it. 

All in all the place is a little pricey but worth every damn penny of it. Amazing place.

My parents and I had the Joogeh Kabob, Lamb Kabob, and Shish Kabob with Basmati rice, hummus, and Lavash bread. It was delicious. I love scooping the hummus with a piece of bread grilled tomato, onion, and chicken, beef or lamb. The staff was friendly enough and the atmosphere in the restaurant was pleasant and clean. Definitely a spot I would consider for a date night ( :
If its JuJu Kabob or Ghormeh Sabzi...its almost as good as a home cooked meal...and with out the over protective Persian parents.

Food was tasty although all with big helpings of rice; only later we learned that we could have half rice and half salad. The service (starting with the reservation) was indifferent, not unpleasant and efficient but "I could not care less" attitude.  Ambiance/decor is very pleasant and prices are quite reasonable.

Food was tasty--the eggplant dip and the minced chicken kabobs.  Rice was lovely and fluffy (but charging extra for the barberries seems a tad mercenary).

Probably won't go back though because of the reviews about people getting sick and then looking on the public health site for Berkeley restaurants and seeing some major hygienic infractions at Alborz

Even when restaurant is slow and empty, waitstaff is not inclined to come over, fill water glasses and the like..

Alborz, clean up your act so that I can come back, okay?

Schmanks!

what a surprise!! FEMALE CHEF********** :))))))))))
kashk was bomb. aash was dead on. and the bademjoon was so so so delicious, very unique tasting, unlike home--which was a nice change. good service and moderately priced. check it out!

Tried this place out early on a Friday evening, about 5:30.  The server was very nice, and answered all of our questions about the flavors of the various entrees.  

For appetizers, we had hummus (needs bread), sabzi (very good, weird, a big portion), and lamb tongue.  As a mostly-vegetarian, I'm pretty grossed out by the tongue of anything, but my boyfriend, the food curmudgeon, absolutely loved it.  He mentioned several times how much he wanted the recipe for the yellow broth it was served in.

For entrees, two of us had the fesenjoon, a walnut and pomegranate stew, which was amazing - sweet, slightly sour, SO satisfying.  Laura B. mentions it below as well.  I'm forgetting the name of the other entree, but it had beef, eggplant and lima beans, and was apparently delicious.

We had baklava for dessert, which is homemade.  It was warm, and the flavor was perfect, but I'm used to baklava being more crispy.  

Note:  Beer is served in these tall narrow glasses - we knocked ours over really easily, broke glasses, spilled beer...sad.  They need some better glasses....=)

I took my co-workers to Alborz for their first Persian meal.  Our server was very nice and helpful and everyone enjoyed their meal.  This is a great place to try new flavors and the prices are very reasonable.  Definitely recommended if you are in the mood for something a little different.

Delish Persian Food, a bit pricey, but totally worth it!  I love the Ghormeh Sabzi, Koobideh and chicken skewers. 
My sister-in law and my niece eat here when they are in town, joining them is always a pleasure.  

I've taken a coworker for lunch and he enjoyed the lamb dish. 

I'd bring others with me in a heartbeat.

Waitress said only reservations were allowed inside but I witnessed multiple parties walk in without reservations (only if there was someone in the party that was non-Asian). Then when I went to go to the restroom one of the cooks stopped me and wouldn't let me go. When another party that was all Asian came, they were not allowed to sit inside either. I thought the civil rights movement already happened. I suppose we're still fighting on. 

Food wasn't great either. I feel insulted and will never come back.
Because of this place, I love Koubideh and Tah Dig. The saffron rice is pretty good too. It just seems pricier than what I would expect.  For the rest of the night, I kept burping Koubideh.

I like this place. It looks classy and more expensive than it actually is. My favorite thing when I go there is the Shishlik? (Did I spell it right?)  Tasty beyond belief. Another one is the salmon, OMG always cooked right.  I like to get my entrees with half rice half salad.  It's too much rice otherwise. They have good pomegranate martinis. The Persian ice cream is obligatory for me.  I guess my only complaint is the Doukh?  the yogurt drink disappoints me. I like it with sparking soda, and often the drink is flat and the pieces of mint are humongous.

The food here was pretty good came here once. Parking is kind of a pain but its not that bad. The only thing I did not like is that I had to wait about 10 minutes just to get somebody to get me a water and a menu.

Great Persian food and great service. I love the lamb koobideh and the saffron rice is very unique and a new treat for most people that I know.

The prices are on par with fine sit-down dining.

I know Persian cooking and I love this place.

Came here for Persian new year with the family and to my dismay they were out of ghormeh-sabzi and chocolate cake  - two vital items on their menu, which is rather disappointing. As a persian I recommend this place, but not for other persians since the taste of their kebobs is not as authentic as any other persian restaurant in the bay area. Also, their service was rather disappointing since they took their time to arrive with the appetizers and dinners - despite seeing the plates of our food being ready in the kitchen. It is too white-washed and fits perfectly with the UC Berkeley environment. This is NOT the place to go if you want to impress your Persian relatives!

I learned during this dinner that Fesenjan is like crack cocaine to the BF, who enjoys food, but is not one to rave about a dish.  Well, he wouldn't shut up during our pre-movie dinner here.  We had sort of stumbled upon it, and as we wanted to have something ethnic that's not available in Tahoe, Alborz fit the bill.  While service was a bit stilted - the young Persian waitress would not talk to me, only to the MAN - the food came quickly and was filling.   I ordered a few different dishes that I wasn't able to pronounce, and really enjoyed the Reshtah soup (with whey), though am not a fan of herb salads that include large chunks of raw onion.  Color me unadventurous there.

Not being from Berkeley, I'm not sure how it compares to other restaurants, or other Persian restaurants in the Bay Area, but this mountain bumpkin found it more than satisfactory.
we enjoy good lamb very much and it is hard to find but alborz fits the bill!

I stumbled across this place with my Persian father who has extremely high standards for kabobs and my girlfriend. I had dined at the Alborz in San Francisco, and didn't care for their food too much. I hoped that this would be better and voila! It was for the most part. It's hard to find a Persian restaurant that serves fresh made bread. With that being said, this bread was cold and almost stale. Yuck.

My father ordered the lamb chops, which I found were incredibly tender and DELICIOUS. I ordered the classic Koobideh which was fairly good. Unfortunately, my dad disagreed. He insisted that it was dry and overcooked. My girlfriend ordered the prawn kabob which was decent. The actual prawns were a good size just a bit overcooked.

Although, my kabob was a tad dry I would come back. I know they all have their days and overall I enjoyed the experience. This one is MUCH better than the one in San Francisco, that's for absolute sure!

This restaurant is amazing.  Everything is good as well as unique.  It seems that Berkeley doesn't have any food that isn't out of the norm and this is no exception.  I'm not sure about the other dishes but the kabobs are simple and delicious and that's a definite plus.  The rice is great and the food is very filling.  I'm not a cultural cuisine aficionado by any means but I highly recommend this place!

Alborz is good, but definitely not great. I ended up getting the Koobideh which is a ground beef skewer. The meat was cooked really well and the portions were also large. My first couple of bites tasted amazing, however, by the end of my meal, I was sick of tasting the same exact thing. My meal came with basmati rice and a pretty gross grilled tomato. I feel as though if the tomato would have been better grilled, the meal would have tasted much better because I could have accompanied it when needed.

One of my friends ordered the Chicken Koobideh and the meat was also well cooked. It was very juicy and not chewy at all. My other friend ordered the Mahi Kabob, but did not like it because it tasted like unseasoned fish. 

Additionally, I give customer service a 1.5. We had to wait an absurdly long time to order our food and the only time our waiter checked in with us after was to refill out water cups.

I've gone to Alborz for at least a decade. It used to be my second favorite Persian restaurant in Berkeley, but then Papa's cuisine closed its doors and we started going to the more westernized Alborz. The food is good, and decidedly less greasy and aggressively-seasoned than most Persian restaurants (which is a good thing in my book). And Alborz has a nice, if somewhat dated, look. Service can be a little slow and difficult, as this isn't a family-run-and-super-attentive kind of restaurant, like so many other Persian restaurants, but just a typical California restaurant that happens to serve Persian food. So if you are expecting the owner to chat with you in Farsi and recommend whatever dish has been the most splendidly-prepared that day by his brother-in-law, this probably isn't the restaurant for you. But if you are looking o get some kebab or Khoresht without the chit-chat, Alborz will suit you well.

I am a really big fan of this place - it is a nice, clean sit down place that is good between friends, good for the family, good for work buddies. I first went here for a staff appreciation dinner with my co-workers a few years back, and just kept going. I even took my parents. The kabbobeh is delicious, but my personal favorite is the  fesenjoon. They actually have a really great selection of vegetarian food. Overall, all of the food is delicious, and it's not like it's that easy to find a Persian place to begin with, right? Price is moderate - hey, you get what you pay for!

The food here tastes really delicious, but it's overpriced. 

The atmosphere is kind of fancy. 

But any of the kabobs are really good.

Service is friendly.

Basically just minus one star for the price.

The place looks good and I have always wanted to try Persian food. I asked for the lamb that costs $19.95, so I thought it would be amazing.  As a matter of fact, it was. The lamb was perfectly done and tasted amazing. But the portion was so small I could finish it with 3 bites!!! And then they serve a lot of rice that tastes like nothing. So...completely unworthy. I am not coming back.

Lackluster taste for overly priced dishes! Definitely authentic Persian food though, but the portions were pretty small and it really lacked any memorable tastes. It tastes just like D'yars actually, maybe even a little less tastey. I ordered the Shish Kabob and it was one large kabob over rice with a roasted tomato on the side. The tomato was pretty gross and the kebob was good, but I was still hungry afterwards, enough so that I picked up a topdog (three doors down) on my way back home.

Pros:
- Fancy atmosphere
- Authentic
- Variety of Persian Dishes

Cons:
- Slow Service
- Over priced
- Not Very Tastey Food

I went here last night as Plan B as Plan A was Cheese Board and it was closed on Monday - stupid Mondays. So I have to admit, I was expecting virtually nothing from Alborz, but was pleasantly surprised. We ate fairly early (around 6pm) so service wasn't an issue for us at all because we were practically the only ones in there. It was about 8,000 freaking degrees outside last night (which I absolutely love) so we sat outside, drank a few glasses of wine and had some pretty decent food. 

I'm not overly familiar with Persian cuisine so I'm probably not the best judge, but I liked my meal and would go back again. Fairly standard dish - chicken kebab with saffron rice with pistachios, almonds, raisins, and orange peel. The yogurt dip and lavash bread that they bring you at the beginning is tasty too, although we couldn't figure out what to do with the raw yellow onions they serve with it. I mean, I KNOW what to do...you EAT them...but WHY? They're raw onions. 

Anyway, like I said, I'm no persian cuisine expert, but I like Alborz...good food, good service, clean restaurant, close to BART...

This is a traditional Persian restaurant with delicious traditional food. It has all the basics and a great restaurant for the daring person whom wishes to expand their horizons. I am an Iranian and truly enjoyed the food which we had. 

Apps: salad shirazi= diced salad (below average)
Bademjoon=eggplant(amazing)
Tadeek and ghormesabzi=crunchy rice and herb/bean stew(good)

Main course: I had the Soltani (amazing). This is a steak skewer(barg) with a ground beef skewer(kubideh). The barg was smokey and tender while the kubideh was moist and juicy. 

The wife had the joogeh kabob (chicken kabob) which also was excellent. 

The nuance was great with sliding doors and Berkeley right outside. 

The only gripe I have are the bugs right outside. Some of these get into the restaurant. Store owner needs to buy a Blower which attaches to the top of the door and blows air every time you open the door in order to prevent  the bugs from coming in.

Highly recommended

Good Kabobs! Great Persian cuisine. Service is kind, attentive, and fast. Try the Koobedieh or Jooghe Chicken with a side of the garlic yogurt. After your meal you MUST get a Persian tea, not only is it good, but it helps with the digestion of your meal.

The food was fantastic!!! The rices were amazing! My mother and I  ordered the Alborz kebab sampler, and the meats were delicious!!!  the fillet mignon kebab was sooo good!! The saffron ice cream was also really good. I will mos def come back because the food was totally worth the long ride and the traffic jams we get stuck in coming from SF to Berkley!

Despite being Armenian, I don't think I've ever had Persian food before. My one complaint is that I felt the kebobs I got were a little "soggy" -- that is, they must have been cooked with a lot of water that didn't get fully grilled. Armenian kebabs are usually MUCH more charbroiled.

But they had freaking sumac, right on the table! And jajough (yogurt with mint)! And lavash bread! The price was good, the service was fast, the ambiance is great, and the staff is nice.

I've had Persian food while in college in SoCal and have always enjoyed it...After having eaten at Alborz, I am now a true fan.

Alborz has a nice ambiance and is located in my friends building in Berkeley.  The yogurt, grilled meats and other dishes are made with high quality meats and produce.  This is an authentic place and a fun place for those seeking middle eastern food that is not falafel or gyros...
Good food, with a wide variety of authentic Persian dishes. The service is friendly and the restaurant looks nice.

OUTSTANDING

We've been here more times than I can count and have always had a completely wonderful experience. The ambiance is understated low key elegance in a causal sort of way and the food matches. High quality, authentic Persian dishes at a reasonable price. Another plus are the staff - very attentive and gracious. I've brought many a friend here - they thank me for introducing them to this terrific find and keep returning themselves.
pricey, but good, hot, persian food. now only if my man's would come like this
Pricey but really good food. It's very quiet inside but very nice and elegant.

I agree that its weird that they served lavash with butter instead of hummus, but nevertheless it was fresh and tasty. 

The pomegranate chicken was amazing!! SO flavorful and tender. And the fahoodeh was delicious- i still can't stop thinking about it (it's shaved rose water ice with frozen thin tiny noodles that give a slight crunch)
yay for khoobideh! such amazing food, i highly recommend the khoodbideh...the soltani is good but the khoobideh is better. plates of shirazi and mast a little small...

Alborz is the best choice for Kabob's in the East Bay. I've been to them all and trust me I know. They don't call me the Kabob King of Cali for nothing! LOL

Their rice is always consistent, consistently great! All of their meats are fresh and I have NEVER had a bad meal here before. The food also comes out really quickly.

I would highly recommend Alborz to anyone who is looking for a great meal.

I will mention that parking can be a bit of a pain and watch out for those Meter Maid's they don't play around. Make sure you but extra money in the meter because an expensive parking ticket can easily be avoided by putting an extra $0.25 in the machine.

I love me some Persian food. There is clearly a lack of Persian cuisine options in the east bay, but Alborz delivers quality and value in their authentic dishes. Their kebabs are pretty tasty, but if you're feeling a little more adventurous, I'd recommend any one of the rice (i.e. "pollo") dishes and/or the Gourme Sabzi. Mmmmm.

Made a reservation for 15 about 2 days in advance. The manager guaranteed they would have one big table for us. We arrive about 5 minutes late, and when we get there, there is literally not even one table open. I talk to the manager, and she said that we came late so she gave our tables away. But there was no way because all the tables were filled and they were eating so it didnt look as though they had just been seated. The manager finally apologizes and says she lost my phone number and ended up giving away my tables. okay.....she promised to give us free champagne and appetizers so we decided to wait. 30 minutes later, we get seated at the most cramped table right beside the door where nobody could get by. She gave us two appetizer platters, and a free bottle of champagne. The whole time she apologized.

I ordered the lamb koobideh plate -- this gives the place 4 stars. For only about $14, it had two long skewers of meat and a pretty big portion of rice. 

All my friends enjoyed their food as well which is why im giving this place 4 stars. Their service was honestly horrible (other than the manager) but their food is good. And the fact they blamed the mess up with the reservation on me, and then later admitted it was their fault...it was kind of annoying. But she did make it up with the free stuff. I also got a free slice of baklava for my birthday dessert.

I'd come here again..but definitely not with a big party.

To start with they don't have any vegetarian options, except stew of veggie which is not good at all. I have eaten Persian food a lot and I know they have so many vegetarian dishes. The service is good though (that's why I am giving it 2 stars). The food you get for your money is not worth and not enough either. I'll accept small portion for a quality but Alborz doesn't have either.

Thank you for finally having a good Persian restaurant in the area that is worth every bite. I come up here every year to visit with friends, shopping and good food. And never have we been able to find good Persian restaurant, comparable to the ones I love here in L.A. 

I have to say that I was little skeptical but it was worth every dollar. I absolutely had to try their pomegranate drink which is made from barley ( i can't remember the name) It was FANTASTIC!! I got wasted on one drink alone and it was the perfect balance of sweetness and alcohol. I ordered the ground chicken kabob and my friend ordered the koobideh kabob. Both were delicious, moist and not overcooked. The rice was nice and fluffy and the tomato was roasted to perfection. We also order the Shiraz salad which is cucumbers, tomatoes, onions and parsley in lemon/oil dressing which - hello I loved. 

Every bite was delicious and I wish I could have eaten it all, because it is large portion. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking great Persian food because it is hard to find restaurant like this in this area. 

Thanks to fellow yelper Reza K. for recommending this spot. This is a gem in Berkeley.

The food here is always great. It tastes amazing and the food is clean, as in not old/greasy. I've never had issues with the service. I don't eat rice so the always substitute the rice with a salad free of charge.

This is a nice, clean and comfortable place. I went there for dinner last night and I got  a chicken kebab (actually the plate was served with 2 kebabs) with rice and I also got the free bread with must-o-khiar  which its similar to tzatziki. My chicken was so tasty...and tender...and juicy...and I just loved it!!! The rice was OK but I've tried better oh and I also asked for the yogurt soda so good  .The service was good and the prices are reasonable.
I'm sure I'm gonna go back and give a try to some other items in the menu so this is just a temporary rating...We'll see!!

I recently visited Alborz on Halloween.  In truth, as a passerby, I was drawn to the large portioned, colorful, tasty-looking food that current patrons were eating outside.  After continuing to walk around the neighborhood, my guest and I eventually made our way back to Alborz.

Alright, so the decor was very dark, but in a romantic type of way. There was a beautiful large window as the store front, which brought in great light and allowed for people watching!  The greeter, whom I think might have been the owner was very pleasant and accommodating.  I ordered the chicken kabob thing with rice, while my guest ordered the filet mignon equivalent. My food was good, the chicken was a bit on the burnt side, but that could have just been a mistake. The dish also came with a fire-roasted tomato, which sounds much better than it tastes. What I received was a burnt, seriously burnt, mushy Roma tomato. Suffice to say, I left that lovely little feature on my plate.   I tasted the filet mignon, which was juicy but a bit tasteless. My friend ate it all though, so I guess it was good enough. Overall, it was a nice restaurant and a pleasant experience. I didn't give the whole five stars because 1. There was dirt on the plates and I had dirty cutlery (a HUGE pet-peeve of mine)  2. My dish was rather burnt. But I'd be willing to give it another shot- maybe.

i excpected more for an ( upscale ) persian place like this too bad i m from the middle east and i know whats the difference between good and ok wantta be good food , it was just plain under seasoned i would consider giving it another chance maybe for lunch not dinner but i ve had  much better persian food

Came here for a friend's birthday. Other than the fact that they managed to omit my friend's reservation (which was quite large), I felt that the food was pretty good. They even threw in a couple of appetizers & drinks because of the mistake - which was a nice way of reconciling the unnecessary wait. 

Aside from the appetizers, the lamb shank & eggplant stew was really good, and portions were more than generous. For a college student, the food might be out of the price range ordinarily, but Alborz is a great place to have a nice dinner with good company (a date, family, close friends, on business, etc), and the portions certainly don't disappoint. 

Ambiance was nice, too. Overall, aside from the mix up, the food was pretty good. I'll be returning with family or for special occasions when I'm feeling too lazy to go into SF to have a nicer dinner.

I've eaten a lot of Kabob in my time, and a lot of forgetable Kabob at that. But let me tell you; Alborz is no exception. It's not bad, but certanly not good either. The oddest thing about this place is that they ask you how you want your Barg cooked, which is as everybody knows, a stupid question. There's only one way to cook it, and if you are getting it bloody then you've missed the point. The biggest draw to this place is that's the only formal style Kabob Resteraunt in the East Bay this side of the Caldecott.

I took my mom out here this past weekend because she had the random hankering for Persian food, and I was pleasantly surprised with Alborz. The restaurant was nicely decorated with mellow, dark, candlelit undertones and the waitstaff were quick and friendly. We ordered a delicious eggplant appetizer dip that was even better when eaten with the yogurt sauce and paprika spice mixture at the table. The kebabs were all you could hope for when it comes to meat on a stick; tender, juicy, savory morsels that satisfied the hunger. I ordered the fesenjoon which is a pomegranate walnut stew. I was quite pleased with the rich, tangy flavor and even more pleased when I ate it with the fluffy basmati rice. Alborz is definitely a nice trip to the Middle East all in the comforts of the East Bay. I'll be back again.

To get fed: $17

Looking for a place close to UCB where the entire waitstaff looks like they have a hint of organized crime about them? Well my friend, you've just arrived! Seriously though, while slightly shady, they were all very nice and pretty helpful.

Alborz does Persian food, but that's a generalization of the point: they make fesenjoon.  And I love me some good fesenjoon.  The dish is conceptually perfect, as it contains chicken, pomegranate, and walnuts, a trinity of deliciousness.  The one I ate here was not particularly fantastic tasting, but oddly satisfying.  I can't describe it any better than that.

The decor inside is pretty run of the mill as far as Persian restaurants go, but the seating is endearingly worn down.  I was here with a fairly large group (12+), and the service handled our several tables efficiently.

My big complaint here is the price point.  I understand charging 20+ for kebabs and the like, that makes sense.  However, $14 for fesenjoon is kinda like charging $12 for a bowl of chicken soup.  Basmati was included and pretty good though.

Summary: Comfortable (s)eating.  25% price reduction = 4 stars.

The service is impersonal and cold for a restaurant that seems to have a warm atmosphere. In retrospect, the Chicken Koobideh tastes like any other that I've had at other restaurants.

Also, our waiter charged an extra 2% gratuity charge (17% total) for a party of 5 when the menu explicitly stated that the extra added gratuity applied to parties of 6 or more. Even after confronting him about this discrepancy, the waiter said our using an extra table warranted this. ...seriously? We should've asked to see the restaurant manager.

Ok, it's a little pricey. The thing is that I continually forget exactly how expensive it is between visits and I think that is a very good sign (because I'm fairly cheap). 

Their fesenjoon with chicken is AMAZING. I also think that despite how noisy it can be, it has a great atmosphere. Everyone seems to be having a good time probably because the food is so good. I also think the service is above average. 

I honestly can't comment too much about the remainder of the menu because I always order the fesenjoon, but friends have said that their lamb is "quite nice" (a true Aussie compliment). 

Well worth any difficulties getting/parking here.

Meanies! The food was OK but the service was absolutely atrocious. The waiters did not offer to refill our cups of water once and charged gratuity for a group of 5 when the menu clearly stated that gratuity is charged to groups of 6 or more. His excuse was "We had to use another [small, 2-person] table." Not cool. I would not recommend this place for potential costumers.

It gets a star because the service was pretty good.  

\I went with work folks for lunch and all of the kebab plates were between $10-$15.  All you get is a big plate of rice -- big whoop it's basmati -- and one teeny tiny skewer of whatever meat you pick.  So let's see, $1 dollar worth of meat and 50 cents worth of rice...  Oh and don't forget the grilled tomato they toss onto the plate.  

Never going back again, it's a total rip off.

I had a good experience at this Alborz as well as the one in San Francisco. I enjoyed my joujeh with bone with a persian (saffron) ice cream. Parking is easy nearby as there is a Bank of America parking lot right across the street that charges a $5 flat fee when not during bank hours. It is a good place to eat, then take a short walk to the movie theaters nearby.

Merci, Alborz, for a wonderful celebratory dinner with my family. We brought my dad here for his birthday, and we were all treated so well. Alborz seems to be getter better and better, and what better way to show your Baba some love other than to take him to a beautiful restaurant with open windows and the subtle aroma of saffron?

Alborz has a very nice wine list so those of us who were drinking ordered some glasses, and then we went on to our meal:

Sumac onions - delicious with butter on lavash, or included in a mini lavash wrap as below.

Sabzi paneer - a platter of fresh herbs, soaked walnuts, and a little bit of feta cheese. Wrap all these in your lavash bread and enjoy. 

Mast-o-musir - yogurt with shallots, a very thick and savory dip. I recommend this.

Mirza ghassemi - a tasty egg, tomato, and eggplant dish, which is another good filling for your mini lavash wrap. I usually prefer Kashke Bademjahn, my personal favorite, but mirza ghassemi is good, too.

Koobideh kabob - mouthwatering beef kabobs done just right.  I really enjoyed these, but just so you know, my dad told me the secret to ordering at a Persian restaurant "is to order the barg...that's Persian steak."  ;)  Perhaps next time. 

Jujeh kabob - we ordered these "ba ostokhan," with the bones in, because I think that keeps them juicier. These were delicious and the lemon marinade came right through. 

The rice and grilled tomato that came with the kabobs were done to perfection. For dessert, they brought out a pie slice of baklava, which I hadn't seen before, with a little birthday candle for Baba. All at the table agreed that this was the best baklava we had ever tasted.

Alborz provides good food and Persian hospitality, just the way it should be. We had a fantastic time, and can't wait to go back!

Note: parking is difficult in this area, but there is a lot across the street (I think for $1 for 25 minutes). If you don't mind a very short walk, you could take BART, too.

I've eaten at the Alborz location in the city quite a few times; though this location is owned by the same people, it just seems to be lacking a certain something that the San Fran location has. However, it delivers with quality food and good service--prices, of course, are a bit steep, but show me a nice Persian restaurant without high prices.

Do you ever have a place that you walk by all the time, literally hundreds of times, but never go in?  Well, that was this restaurant situated conveniently between BART and Berkeley campus.  Finally, my friend Jonathan and I popped in for an early dinner and actually had a really tasty meal.

I had a great chicken koobideh kabob (saffron chicken) with saffron rice...do you sense a theme?  Of course, one can never get too much saffron.  The chicken was moist, delicious, tender (this sounds like chicken porn).  Jonathan's lamb was maybe even better.  I wouldn't have minded some veggies thrown in the mix though.  

One big plus was the wine by the glass.  It was actually a generous pour.  I hate the restaurants that think a bottle of wine equates to 15 glasses.  A little odd is the flat bread and butter they serve as a starter.  Maybe with some hummus instead.  All in all it was pleasant, although I can't really give them any points for value.

What is an "Alborz" anyway?  Well, if you google, it looks like the name of lots and lots of Persian restaurants.  Now if you google even more you discover it's a mountain range in northern Iran.  And now you can try to impress your server when you come.

I think that you should trust my reviews of Persian restaurants for the simple fact that I am half Persian.  The half of me that's Persian will understand how to fully appreciate the food and menu, because we cook it at home, and I've had many a meal Iranian-style, including several locations in Iran.  The American half of me will be able to explain it to you as someone who has also grown up eating Spaghettio's and Cup 'O' Noodles.

Anyways, back to the review . . . 

I stumbled upon Alborz Restaurant this summer, and I've eaten here a few times since, because it was the only Persian place I've come across in Berkeley so far.  I think this is definitely a typical Iranian establishment in America, with most people coming here to order the koobideh (beef kabob) they've heard about.  I think the menu has a nice selection of varying kabobs and stews, which most people look over too quickly.  If I had to give some advice to someone not familiar with the menu, I would recommend ordering one kabob plate, and one stew to try, which all go great poured over rice.  

The times I've come here, I've been pleased with the service, the food and the tea, which are really the crucial parts of any dining experience as far as I'm concerned.  It's all pretty good, but it didn't blow me away.  My friends were all very happy, and so I considered it a success coming here . . . but I've had better joojeh kabob in a restaurant.  Also, I wanted more rice.  But maybe that's just me.  

However, you will see me frequenting this place, because I'm a slave to the food I've grown up with.  And they do a pretty good job.

A little pricey, but Persian food is my absolute favorite . Maybe I have some hidden heritage here, because this food is just so homey to me. I know how to make a few of the stews and the fabulous rice, so I feel I'm a good judge of the quality and flavor. 

They are pretty good at our take out orders, mixing it up familiy style when the order is large. Which, I'll be honest, is whenever I order there. They have only shorted a small item us once out of may 20 times we have ordered. They are pretty far from us and yet I will shlep it there because the food is awesome! 

Love the Gormeh Sabzi (green aromatic veggies, kidney beans, and meat stew over rice), chicken Barg (pounded, skewered, grilled, saffron chicken breast), saffron rice, any of the rices really (particularly with currants, cause I'm just like that) any mast, but particularly mast o'moussir (yogurt with shallots). Hubby loves their cinnaminy Ghemeh Bademjoon (tomato and yellow split pea stew with meat and eggplant, which you can get without the eggplant) which I add lemon juice to at home to give it a little kick. The Kashk Bademjoon appetizer (eggplant, yogurt, mint, garlic, heaven - I'm pretty sure its all in there). 

Service is always lovely, even when they are crowded. I might go tomorrow for my birthday. . .

At first it's hard to eat here because it seems like a kabob place i went to in DC, except with tablecloths, and I couldn't stomach the prices.

BF and I had just spent 4 hours in the library and our eyes were dry and tired and we were HUNGRY. 

Then we ordered and food came out. This was WAY ahead of any kabob place. I highly recommend the roasted eggplant (Kashk Bedemjah) the flavor was AMAZING and unique and trust me, I eat a lot of eggplant. I had a perfect Koobideh (ground beef kabob) which was perfectly cooked, still juicy, well spiced. The BF had Fesenjoon with Chicken. It's ilke a stewed chicken in this tart-sweet-nutty sauce. You can taste the walnuts and the astringency from the pomegranate. He loved it, I agreed it was really good but a little too sweet for me to eat the whole thing. Finished the meal with some perfect Persian tea.

I am persian and unlike my real life friend Darin E. i think Alborz is a great Persian Restaraunt.. in fact, i think its the best one i have been to and my family and i go there at least twice a month... everyone we bring to it enjoys their food as well.  

I do agree that the service will probably not be the greatest if you have no one that speaks Farsi, but it wont be rude either.. just not great.

but the food....ahh the food is marvelous as well as is the Basmati Rice.

I recommend getting 

Koobideh which is two skewers of ground beef and rice and is usually the cheapest thing on the menu, but i always get it cause its just the best.
Soltanni (one filet mignon, one beef); Barg (steak), Juje (chicken) are also very good.

The appetizer platter is awesome and a great intro into a lot of little things us persians eat, but definitely split it with several people, because when your food comes.. it WILL be a lot of meat and rice.. and a wonderfully bbqed tomato to boot.

I highly recommend checking this place out if you have never had persian food and want something "authentic".... walk in and i guarantee you will see a persian at nearly every table.. which is always a good sign.

I really REALLY like this place. The food is awesome and since I only come here with a certain family I ALWAYS have a good time. I can't pronounce anything on the menu but I've loved everything I've had. So far Joojeh Soltani is my favorite. The koobideh was really flavorful and perfectly cooked, moist and delicious. But the standout star in Joojeh Soltani is the chicken. It is some of the best chicken I have ever had in a restaurant.   I do sometimes feel a little self conscious since I'm probably the whitest person in the entire restaurant and I tend to butcher the language while trying to order but It's more my own issue. The staff is pleasant and accommodating and the restaurant is clean and has a great atmosphere. 

Oh but FYI... Don't try and cheat on the parking in the across the street lot. They'll get ya.

al boring. Maybe that is just how persion food is in general but I really thought there could have been alot more done here. I ordered the lamb skewers. The meat was chewy, and just not all that good, and the only other thing it came with was rice and a plain whole grilled tomato. Maybe it is better at dinner but I will never know.

As a Persian/Iranian-American myself, I have to say their food was pretty tasty. Took a girl on a date there; we shared an appetizer and an entree, which was more than enough, but for the price they charge, I deem it to be fair.

But, I was not too big of a fan of their tadigh (crunchy rice). It wasn't as crunchy as I would hope for it to be, or maybe my mom does a better job.

When I walked in, the Persian lady at the front immediately recognized I was a fellow Persian (and on a date), so she did everything to tend to us and make it as great of an experience as possible. For this, I truly applaud Alborz for great service; I was truly satisfied.

I've never had Persian food so I was pleasantly surprised by the experience. Had to ask for help with the bread, onions, and yogurt that came to our table as a starter. Got a lovely thin sliced filet mignon with buttery rice, and a black charred object that turned out to be a delicious, roasted tomato. The Turkish coffee was strong and sweet, with a powdery finish. I'd love to come back for lunch specials, as the dinner menu is slightly more expensive than I'd like.

I know that there are no other Iranian options near by (particularly since Papa's closed), but I refuse to settle for the mediocre, over-priced food at Alborz.  

The kabobs are okay (I introduced my friend to joojeh kabob here and she still goes with regularity despite the fact that I don't), but I truly think the markups are outrageous (and this is probably because of the lack of competition more than anything).  $15 for Joojeh Kabob? $22 for Soltani?  Almost $5 for Torshi?  Really?  None of the khoreshts can hold a candle to my moms cooking -- though I will say I enjoy how you can get tah dig smothered in your choice of them.  I was really excited when I saw that Berkeley was getting some Iranian flavor, but I can't say that Alborz has lived up to my expectations.

Not suitable for vegetarians, but that's more the cuisine than this particular restaurant.  In case someone is still not hip to the raw onion, all you need to do is take a piece of lavash, spread some butter on it, and roll a small piece of onion in the middle.  It has a nice crunch and a surprising sweetness -- give it a shot.  Adding some sabzi to the middle or dunking the whole thing in yogurt are optional variations : )

Madre and I wanted a Mediterranean-y din, so I Yelped and found Alborz, which is close to my apt and seemed to fit the bill.  The restaurant is nicer than its surroundings prepared me for --not the deli style med fare that most of the places in Berk seem to be.  

We were seated immediately--the place was only 3/4 full on a Friday night at 7:45, and although it took our waiter a while to come greet us (well, maybe only 5-7 min, but when you think about it, that's actually a long time for the "hi, how are you" part of the meal to get going), once he acknowledged us he was quite friendly, verging on adorable.  

We started w/ the shirazi salad (really more like a cup of chopping cukes and tomatoes in a lemon/spice/olive oil dressing) and a Greek salad.  Both could have been a smigden bigger, but were yummy.  We then went for the hummus (excellent--thick, plentiful, lemony) and the roasted eggplant dip--not anything like babaganoush (sp?)--but lovely.  A bit sweeter, drizzled w/ "whey" and sprinkled w/ walnuts.  We split a salmon kebab which came w/ green bells, onions, and enough rice to feed all of a small country.  Fish was a smidge dry but warm and filling--rice was spiced w/ dill and limas.  Glad they added some interest to it.

Oh, and they give you wonderful lavash and yogurt dip to start.  Yum. 

It was a bit spendy for what it was (I think 60 for the 2 of us before t and t, and w/ no drinks), but it was calm, and Sar Sar was footing the bill, so it didn't really fuss me. 

Overall, the food was certainly solid, perhaps a B+, and while I'm probably no expert on Persian specifically, I know some good hummy when I taste it. 

Oh, important--if you're going w/ vegetarians, they have a few dishes but not nearly as many as one might expect from a med place--probably 5-6 total.

Some of the best Persian food in the Bay Area. 5 stars!

One tip: I usually order "Soltani" kabob at Persian restaurants, which is a combination one skewer each of Koobideh (ground beef kabob) and Barg ("filet mignon" kabob).  The Barg here is not very impressive, although usually at other places it is the better.  Save yourself 50% and just order Koobideh--they will give you two full skewers for half the price of Soltani.

Nine of us came here for dinner, and nine of us left, more or less intact.  The location is a plus.  Prices are reasonable and quantities are large.  The food was a real "meh" for me despite my good attitude.  (Our group included a Persian woman who claimed that the place was really excellent.)  You get a large number of chunks of grilled meat, a huge mound of rice with some spices in it and a small green salad if you agree to have your mound of rice made somewhat smaller.  You'd be better off elsewhere.

We ordered two red wines: the Ravenswood Lodi zinfandel ($28) and somebody's Lodi Sierra Foothills "shriaz" ($32).  The zin was marginally better than the shiraz, but I don't plan on drinking either again.  The menu price of the Ravenswood was about double the standard retail price.

Meat on a stick. 
Anything on a stick, for that matter. 
It's hard to go wrong. 

Ground up, well... that's another story. Take hot dogs for example. I have close friends that no thanks to Pee Wee Herman and his hot dog tree to this day still have phobias. How I would get them to try the deliciously juicy beef and chicken kobiddehs here, I do not know. But I can confidently say that if you're a believer in meat consumption, this is the supreme form of its ground up existence. Imagine a burger flattened, flame-licked and thrown over a spit. Pair it with a splash of fresh lemon, grilled whole tomato, and fragrant rice and you'll begin to understand the most basic yet gastronomically delightful staple of Persian cuisine.

"Why three stars, Ligaya?", you may ask. And to this I scratch my chin and pull on its hairs and say in a feeble voice that I've had better. That the eggplant dip though bathed in green olive oil tasted like it was made days ago, and that the dolmas though warm lacked a zest of herbs. And that in ordering the paneer sabzi what I got was literally a plate of fresh basil, cilantro and mint, slices of cucumber and tomato, yogurt sauce and a chunk of feta. A little creativity, please. 

A little wine to soothe the disappointment never hurts, right? Alas. Our cab as suggested by the waiter was as one-dimensional as the man himself. thought I'm not holding that against them. White tableclothes and all, I expect a level of reservedness though the fork and the knife had erroneously switched places with the spoon. Is that a Persian custom?

In conclusion: a fair option for a tasty meal but for the pennies and ambiance there are finer plates a-calling.

I ate my first Persian meal at this restaurant, and I really enjoyed it. It has a fancy ambiance, but a meal is affordable. I ordered the chicken and beef kebab plate, which has one chicken kebab and one beef kebab. It was served with rice and a deliciously roasted tomato. It tastes best with some yogurt sauce and lemon squeezed over the top. So good!

Also, a must is their ice cream. It tastes like it is rose-flavored, and has small sugar crystals mixed in. It's a great end to the meal.

Yummy!!!!!!!!!!!! Server has a lot of smile and friendly :) 
I love the Lamb dishes and portion is perfect! We had 7 people, 3 of us ordered lamb dishes and it taste so good. We did not like the beef kabob that much. 
Just don't ever order the Yogurt drink in this place..its like sour cream/ ranch mix with club soda... LOL~

Let me start by saying that I used to love to go to this restaurant, the food was mostly great, a few misses over the years, but everyone has a bad day or two.  

HOWEVER- I had the most unfortunate dining experience here at lunch a few months ago.  It keeps eating at me and I need to vent.....my husband has been seriously ill over the last 9 months and the first place he wanted to go when he had regained his strength was Alborz...we took my mother in law who has been our angel!  I ordered Shirin Polo, which is my fav dish there....when the busser delivered my food he handed me an unlined shallow soup bowl with scorching hot broth (and chicken) in it that was almost overflowing.  He had it an an angle so when i touched the bowl it scorched my hand which by reflex i pulled away, he then proceeded to dump about half of the SCORCHING HOT broth on my LAP! It was so hot i yelped and jumped out of my seat.  The busser brought me a bag of ice for my lap and said i'm sorry.  NO ONE ELSE CAME OVER.  My waiter just stood there and looked at me talking to the other waiter.  The woman chef stared at me from across the room but no one said a word.  When I finally flagged the waiter over to ask him for more broth, he rolled his eyes (serious attitude) and took my bowl with out saying a word.  When it was time for our check he just plopped it down on the table...we mentioned that it might be a nice gesture on their part to comp my meal since they seriously burned me.....you know what the waiter said ....."well, she spilled it on herself!!!!!!"  He grabbed the check out of my husbands hands -comped the item and again said nothing.

Even if I had dumped the whole thing on myself (which i SO did not) human nature says to go and ask if you can help someone in pain...I was a food server on and off for 15 years, and you NEVER serve a shallow bowl of soup or any hot liquid without a plate liner.

It took 3 days for my legs and hand to feel better.

I guess things might have been different if the owner was there, but perception is reality! So Sad.

Stumbled unto this place when we realized it's neighbor restaurant, Raphael, was closed.  We loved the feel of the place -- classy but not overly -- well lit, clean.  We weren't disappointed.  This was our first time trying Persian cuisine and it is excellent!  The chicken and filet kabobs were TENDER and tasty.  Rice was plentiful and tasty.  Staff helpful and professional.  We'll definitely go back to try the many other menu items that we couldn't try our first time!

I really must commend this place for their amazing service. 

 I was disappointed to see that they did not have albaloo polo on the menu.  I resigned myself to ordering something else when, as the waiter was walking away to place our order, I blurted out "Do you know if you'll have albaloo polo on your menu anytime soon?"  I was shocked at my rudeness, but he was seemed surprised that this little asian girl knew what that was (Dude, I spent five years at UCLA- walk five minutes down Westwood Blvd and you're in Little Persia).    He cocked his head to the side and, in a thoughtful voice, said "I think we can do that, yes."  Ten minutes later, I had an awesome plate of cherried rice in front of me.  YES!  I know where I'm going next time I crave polo.

I was SO not crazy about this place.  I think it's because I have been spoiled by authentic Persian and Middle Eastern food straight from the home kitchen.  But as ethnic food restaurants go, this one will do just fine if you don't know any better.  We went about a month ago, so the memory is slightly faded, but I'll share what I can.  Starting with the hummus, unfortunately it was salty, too salty - and our waiter agreed and removed it from the bill.  Thank you, waiter.  I remember having some sort of tadeek dish, which arrived at our table barely at room temp, and inclued beef, of which I specifically requested none.  The dish was taken away, beef removed, then returned to us.  The waiter explained that the remainder of the dish would be replaced.  So they brought out more of the same OK dish.  My cousin and I both ordered the salmon kabobs for our entree.  I was satisfied enough with that, but I don't think she was.  The waiter, who was incredibly friendly btw, talked us into ordering a special dessert that he thought was the best thing since packaged lavash.  Neither of us agreed with his taste buds on that, and I think it too was removed from the bill.  The best thing about this place for us was the service, very, very, very friendly.  Would I go back... probably not.  But that's because I have access to the real thing.  If u don't, u might really enjoy this place.

Pretty good food.  The prices are very reasonable, and nice ambiance.  Great place for lunch!  I had one of the stew, and it was decent.  My friend had the sweeter one, and it was a little too sweet for me, but it's more of a personal preference, since everyone else loved it.  We had the combo appetizer and everything on it was yummy! The meat dishes were good as well, not too dry.

My first experience with Persian was not so great (it was bland city) but I really liked this place.  It was a bit pricey (just missed the lunch specials) but they give you HUGE portions.  I had the cornish hen which was grilled to a crispy perfection and my boyfriend had the lamb kabobs - both were quite flavorful. The dolmas are also quite good.  Not a high recommend, but worth checking out if you happen to be in the area.
You got to try Abgoosht there, the best meal ever

There aren't many nice, white table-clothed, good Persian restaurants like this around Downtown Berkeley/ UC Campus area so I'm not surprised that Alborz gets busy at night. 

Before your meal they bring you flat bread that you can eat with yogurt and raw onions or just butter if you prefer. Persian food can be a bit on the dry side compared to Indian food and I wanted something a little saucy to go with my rice so I ordered the Fesenjoon with Chicken (roasted ground walnut cooked in pomegranate sauce). Our cool, super nice waiter said it was a good choice. He was definitely right. Mmm..rich, a bit tart, sweet, moist tender chicken... I was diggin this dish, but be careful not to overload the rice with the pomegranate sauce or it might be a little on the strong side.

My bf orderd the Chicken Koobideh (two skewers of ground chicken breast seasoned with saffron, and onion). It's a massive platter and he ate the whole thing. I don't blame him because the chicken skewers were damn good. So juicy and cooked jsut right. Everything's better with butter. I think I'll order that next time.

We're not drinkers so the total bill was $38 (including tip) which isn't bad at all. Good food, friendly service, and great company make for a happy belly and an awesome night.

I'd never had Persian food before but I was anxious to try it.  The "appetizers" (hot flatbread, onion, yogurt sauce, butter, and some sort of dark brown spice) should have come with instructions, or at least the server should have suggested what we were to do with them.  Apparently the bread and yogurt sauce is for whatever, the butter is for the rice that comes with your entree, and I still have no idea what the spice is for.  For the entree, I got the Shirin Polo with Chicken Kabob and the platters came out with massive portions.  One big skewer of chicken marinated with lemon (yum!) and a heap of saffron rice with almonds, pistachios, raisins, and orange peel.  It was like candy.  So sweet!  The candied orange peel was a little unnerving to some people in my party, but I really liked it.  

We had a HUGE party, so it's understandable that service was shaky because it appeared that our waiter was serving the whole restaurant as well as us.  But, we got to taste everyone else's food!  The various types of "Barg" were not only fun to say, but also delicious.  Someone had a roasted walnutty stew that tasted like raspberry-infused chocolate.  I don't know how that happened, but it was good.  Like I said, portions were huge so we all left very satisfied.  Totals came out to about $20 per person, decent for the food and dealing with our large party.

Just help me out with the appetizers!

Alborz is the place I come to when I want excellent Persian food (outside of my dad's side of the family).

This place has excellent kabobs and the portions are huge.  I always end up taking some back home for lunch the next day.  Food prices are around the 10-15 dollar range but with that price you get excellent dishes, good waiters, a nice and clean restaurant plus endless yogurt with lavash (Persian bread).

If you are ever in the University area of Berkley I would recommend trying Alborz if you want to eat some authentic Persian food.

Decent Persian place.  Nice wine list, good atmosphere.  If the weather cooperates you might consider sitting outside although this is highly dependent on the amount of street people and teenagers running around.  Inside is a nice option too.  Service was attentive that night without being clingy.  I will echo the sentiment raised by another though that they suddenly appeared with a bunch of stuff that I wasn't sure where to put it.  Did the cucumber dip go with the onions, the flatbread, or where?  On the other hand, I say screw convention and had fun figuring out where I wanted to put these things.

Ok the food.  Rice, and tons of it.  Fortunately I love it and it was prepared well.  Mine had onions and orange slices and nuts in it along with chicken on the side in oil (although too much oil for my taste) that fell off the bone.  I don't remember the name but it was one of the new non-kabobs on the menu in the specials.  My friend had the joojeh kabob and her chicken was marvelous.  I'll get that next time.  Oh, and you must stay for Baklava, not overpoweringly sweet but just right in it's flaky texture.  Mmmmmmm ....

If you haven't had Persian food then you don't know what you're missing, and this is a great place to get your feet wet or continue your Persian exploration. 

The food here is very good. The koobideh (my go to, 2 skewers of minced meet made with some delicious spices, and a side of saffron rice) is always delicious. It's usually perfectly cooked and very juicy. At times it's a bit overcooked on the ends but it's still great. The joojeh (chicken skewers marinated in great spices with a side of saffron rice) is also delicious and a great choice. You can't really go wrong no matter what you order but these are my two favorite. 

The dessert is also great. My favorite is the bastani (rose water ice cream, it tastes like eating what a rose smells like). This is great choice. If you're on a date I suggest getting this. It's a perfect size to share especially after the vast quantity of food that you probably just ate. 

The service is great and pretty quick. It's also priced pretty similarly to most persian places. 

The parking here isn't great though. There is a lot across the street but it costs $5 as a flat rate. And the street parking is nearly impossible to find. 

This is definitely a great spot to try out.

Delicious food..  ghormeh sabzi i would happily bring the persian side of my family to..mmmmm keep up the good work!  ps: i asked for the ghormeh sabzi on tah dig (which is pretty much crispy, almost burned rice, purposely burned, that is..) and they happily obliged..but they did the kind that incorporates bread. that was fine.

This is my second favorite persian restaurant,.
It is very hard to find a really good authentic Kabob experience in the Bay Area that does all the other Main dishes and side dishes on the same level, too.
I have had the both Chicken and Lamb Kabobs, they were prepared very well, succulent and flavorful- not overcooked and bland, like so many I have tried at other restaurants.
The saffron rice is perfect in its consistency and flavoring, as well.
For me,the most important part of the persian experience is a seemingly strange mixture of ingredients that I learned years ago from my Iranian friends, but makes all the difference in eating traditionally.
When ordering your main dish, make sure you also get "mustomosir", a yogurt based preparation, and plenty of raw onions and roasted tomatoes.
When your entree arrives,( for me, i always order the Chicken Kabob)
mix the yogurt, roasted tomatoes and raw onions all together with the saffron rice, and take alternating bites of the grilled meat. OMG!!
Unbelievable flavors !! I hate roasted tomatoes and raw onions on their own, but this mixture of flavors is synergistic, and ungodly in its sinfulness.
This mixture alone is what makes me crave good persian food.
Ambience is very nice here, but not too stuffy, you can dress casual.
Parking is a difficult pain !!  especially at peak times.Be prepared to shell out some extra cash  at one of the lots.
Service was excellent, and food arrived fast, even on a Saturday night.
Recommended. Portions are HUGE, always have to take half home, don't understand other reviews saying opposite, maybe they have bigger appetites ?? It is expensive though, bring your plastic if your'e not carrying that much cash.

[pronounced] Alburz; is a mountain range in Northern Iran.

I am not Persian, but I love me some Persian food!

I have been to this fancy classy Persian restaurant a dozen times with my close co-worker. We usually go here when we want to be super indulgent. On my first experience I was quite impressed since I have been able to have authentic Persian food from actual friends and family members. I could tell the place would be good when I noticed a lot of Iranians there.

The food is prepared right and so delicious. It was such a royal treat! And when I'm really in the mood for it, this is the only place I will go to

The space is quite small however to use of mirrors throughout give it a larger appearance. The décor, lighting and genuine hospitality of the wait staff make a quite comfortable fine-dining experience

Start your lunch off right with their Hummus and Yogurt Salad- a mix of home-made hummus, yogurt, cucumber, tomatoes and spices topped with feta cheese, served together with their version of complimentary warm pita bread.It sounds simple- but it will blow you away.

Moving on to the main course the kabob is a must, a Soltani combination will allow you to experience both the koobideh (ground beef) kabob as well as the barg (sliced beef fillet). We usually split dishes..she will order a skewer of chicken, I will order koobideh and we share since they give such generous portions. The jasmine rice is perfect!  Very fluffy, airy and seasoned with such exotic flavors. It is presented very elegantly too because some of the rice on the bottom is white and on the top it is yellow because the use saffron seeds.  {side note} Saffron flower seeds are very expensive, not the herb the actual saffron flower seeds. 
There is a also a small bowl on each table with a baby spoon to add additional salt-like seasonings to your liking.

Wash everything down with a glass of aromatic Persian tea and you'll be raving for weeks about one of the greatest dining experiences in Downtown Berkeley.

Upfront:  Great service, wonderful food, and ambiance to match - Alborz does more right than most, and comes up with a big win in the Kabob game.  4.9 stars...

Standouts:  Service was great - and from the moment we sat down, water and lavash was instantaneous.  Our apps (a thick n delicious Persian noodle stew and a salad) were delivered so quickly that we barely had time to blink.  We also ordered hot tea in response to the early autumn night chill, and it was soothing and elegant - with a hint of rose water.

Meat:

Yes.

Freakin' awesome kabobs that were succulent, hefty and satisfying.  My wife and I ordered the "for two" kabob plate of filet mignon, chicken, and spiced ground beef - and it was all expertly prepared.  Yay meat!

In The End:  Go for lunch or dinner - well worth it, convenient, and bound to produce smiles.  We'll be going back for sure.

3.5 stars! We were promptly seated and got complimentary lavash bread with an all onion spiced salad and butter.  I wasn't really into the onion side, as raw onions have a very strong flavor and are difficult to eat, even with the lavash.  We ordered the Soltani (ground beef and filet mignon skewer) and the Chicken Kebob in the house specials section (with byrani rice specially mixed with orange rinds, pistachios, almonds, and raisins) - waiter recommended.  The chicken was delicious and tender! I usually really dislike chicken, but this one was nicely marinated and tasty!  Even better with the lemon! The rice contained wayyy too many citrus rinds though, and they were thickly cut -- not my preference at all.  The ground beef was also tender, a little on the salty side though.  The filet mignon was good too! Overall, my chicken was the favorite though which was ironic given I usually am not a fan of chicken since it is usually too dry.  The waiter recommended us to get half rice/half salad, instead the full portion of rice they offer you, and it was a really good idea! They do give you a whole lot of rice!  The salad was mixed greens, with a oil and vinegar like dressing.  Not bad!

Our waiter dissapeared on us, and some one new came out to help us.  Overall, service was a little slow for us.  The meal was pretty good though and the dining atmosphere is nice, simple, and classy!

Whole family got a food poisoning after dining there.  It was not the first time I have been there and I love Persian food. Yet the last dining experience really put a black eye on their reputation.  Their stews were tasty but deadly. Everybody was sick and in and out of bathroom for a couple of days.  I read other reviews and am glad for people who had good time there. On my end, it was the last time I was anywhere near the place.

Really, really, really good.

Got the combo shishkabob of chicken and beef. A TON of food. 

The rice is just perfect. If you like Persian, you'll like this place a lot.

Pros:
Close to Berkeley theatres and hot spots
Good for early dinner
Nice fresh tasting ingredients
Good service
Very clean and pleasant ambiance 
A nice night out for those of moderate means

Cons:
A little pricey for what ya get
Along those lines - they might consider lowering the enormous quantity of rice and putting in a nice salad, which would make the meal a little more budget friendly and nutritionally balanced.

So overall I like it. I just think it's a little on the expensive side.

Food was delish, but service was mediocre.
