I wasn't greeted - it's a small independent place with what I assume was the owner and one cook/sandwich maker, who were casually talking.  I scan the wall for Falafel and locate two items of interest: a super falafel and a regular falafel sandwich.  Given this is lunch, I didn't want to spend a whole lot so I decided on a regular.  I walked up to the counter, but the lady didn't acknowledge me, continuing to talk for a good half a minute as I stood there half-awkwardly.  She finally said "hi" and I ordered, paid, and got my change - still somewhat awkwardly - I couldn't really understand why but it didn't seem like a friendly place - even la burrita workers are at least slightly friendly regardless if they're on a slow morning or pumping out burritos to a hungry crowd of drunk college students at 2am.

The falafel sandwich came fast - it was prefried and I suppose just sitting in a warmer; I was slightly disheartened at this, but whatever.  I took my order to go and walked back on campus, unwrapped one of the two half pitas and took a bite of the colorful composition.  Extra crispy, warm, delicious.  Each falafel was nicely crisped on the outside with a deep golden brown color, encasing a rich green center with texture that wasn't blended to hell and back.  Add the default topping and conveyed in a standard pita and ... heck that doesn't matter - good falafel can make anything taste good.  I was overjoyed.  Mouth so satisfied that I didn't even notice the protest forming at Telegraph.  It wasn't until I plowed through both halves that I felt anything else but happiness.  That last bite was followed by a tinge of sadness - a sadness that grew exponentially.  I finally found good falafel - Norcal, Socal, wherever, I have looked for good falafel and I finally found it - and I will be leaving in two weeks.

The best I can do is write this review and convince at least one other falafel lover to try it early on before a situation like mine arises.  In two weeks I'll be back to finding good falafel - I'll have to call up my friend and ask his mother to make me some more.

The falafels at Sunshine Deli are perfect - golden brown, good-sized and well-done. Mmmmm...I used to buy 3 or 4 and eat them out of the paper bag.  The falafel plate, which comes with hummus, tabbouli, dolmas, and picked radishes, is also delicious or if you need something more portable, the wraps are great. I don't eat meat, so I've never tried the shawarmas, but meat-eating companions have attested to their tastiness.  

This is an ideal lunch place, centrally located on Bancroft, right across Eschelman Hall. Get your falafel plate, wrap, or paper sack to go, sit on the benches in Lower Sproul, and watch people practice the Soulja Boy dance. Good times.

I haven't been back to this place in a while, but by god, I hope it still stands. Before Sunshine Deli, this used to be a boba spot. Oh, the fickle palates of the Cal populace.

4.5
love it, wish it had more flavor though. like offering tahini sauce.

I've tried the super falafel and lamb shawarma. The burrito-sized super falafel was excellent. Lamb shawarma was good too, but not as good Truly Mediterranean's in SF. You can get Airbears here, and I think they have their own wifi too. I'll definately be back for the super falafel.

Lamb shawarma time (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/J27yz2L8PoubYmfi_DWrSA?select=YnNCrPsT_s70anPdynkl5A) I always forget that this comes in a pita and only their Falafel Deluxe comes standard in lavash. DOH!

Tip: Lettuce in a hot sandwich get's wilty . . . I just don't get the appeal. You can sub it out for delicious pickled cabbage which maintains it crunch under pressure (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/J27yz2L8PoubYmfi_DWrSA?select=MojM73a_w5FPN6PlbOpagg). You're welcome! :)

There's a sign outside that says "best falafel in Berkeley". I'm still new to the whole falafel, thing so I can't say just right now that that statement is true.

However, it was pretty tasty. I could't believe for $5.48 I got 2 half pitas stuffed with goodness.(see picture) Hummus, falafel, lettuce, tomato and sauce(not sure what it was, and doesn't matter, cause it was good).

Ok so after eating the first half, (when I got back to the car...what??) I was full. But I couldn't help but think when was I gonna eat the second half. Well as soon as I got back to my side of town, I started to go in on the second half. It was just as good as the first...got down to the bottom, I just picked out the remaining falafel and just ate it, them by itself was very flavorful and had a little spice to it too! 
Now I'm thinking to myself, when you go back next time just get an order of falafel...did I just say that???

Maybe they do have the best falafel in Berkeley????

If I were remotely vegetarian I would eat at Sunrise all the time and would easily give them four stars.  But I'm a kebab and shawarma kind of guy, and they just don't cut it as a kebab and shawarma kind of place.  

There's a certain flavor-infused fatty juiciness that's tragically missing from all Berkeley middle eastern meats.  The Persian restaurants in the East Bay (e.g. Alborz, Pomegranate) don't seem to have the same problem, so you might try their kebabs to get an idea of this quality I'm looking for.  But as for shawarma, you're kind of screwed around here unless the one-note, dried up local equivalent is all you've ever known.

Still, as disappointed as I have been by this shredded chicken and lamb jerky that Sunrise Deli dares to serve me, I have to say they are the best middle eastern in Berkeley.  That's not saying much, but it does mean that I always turn to them when I have certain cravings.  They definitely have me covered when I want falafel, and  their hummous is particularly good.  Importantly, Sunrise is generous about putting hummous in their sandwiches, which surprisingly many restaurants here neglect to do.

The Super Falafel is my favorite item as it is a sandwich that includes fried eggplant and potato - in my view staples that are too hard to find in the Bay Area.

I always end up getting the falafel pita - don't recall ever trying anything else. The falafels are quite spicy with a recognisable chickpea taste, though they could be crunchier. Other fillings are good, especially the tahini. The pita is wholly generic. Overall, not as good as Holy Land's but better than all others I've tried.

NB: Karl, my olive connoisseur officemate, think the complimentary olives here are outstanding.

(See pic)

Sunrise Deli in Sunset.

Instead of eating at one of the Asian eateries, I found this clean, neat, bright red and yellow deco place that just stands out like a bright kid standing there quietly, waiting to be discovered.

I had the chicken kabab platter that came with 2 sides (I picked dolmas and tabouli) with pickled turnips, olives and stripped onions.

The food is very fresh as you can see them keep on making tabouli and bringing it out from the kitchen while people stream in and out of the place. The chicken is perfectly seasoned and not overwhelm your taste bud. The olives are subtle and did not take over the main plate. Dolmas are perfectly firm with the perfect scent of grape leaves.

Now the bonus part is the Turkish coffee that is served in a lovely demitasse cup! While it did not have foam on top, and that I already had a cup of Blue Bottle and a cup of Henry's (House of Coffee) cap earlier, which was totally over my regular daily consumption, this just made it as a high note of the day. The undercurrent of cardamom danced around the coffee, leaving my lips happy with the ginger feel. The coffee itself was on the lighter side.

The service is very friendly but also quiet-- no crazy music or TV like many other eateries, my absolute like.

While some places might have screaming good food, Sunrise has this surprisingly refreshing, crisp, pick-me-up sensation! Definitely feel like sunrise after the meal.

Truly amazing falafel, but bring some Altoids because they are potently garlicky (but oh-so-good). Occasionally they get a bit busy and rush the falafels, so go when they have time to make them fresh and hot. The basic falafel is all I ever get - no need to mess with perfection - it is huge and a real bargain.

To avoid the lunch rush, come before 12:00 on MWF, or before 12:30 on TuTh (this is how the UC Berkeley scheduling works).

Sunrise Deli can be easy to miss since it's pretty small and not around the Asian Ghetto area that a lot of students go to, but it's a good place for solid falafel. There's only a few tables though since space is limited, but they also have some counter seats along the window.

What I ordered:
Super Falafel ($6.25): Hummus, Eggplant, Potatoes, Lettuce, Tomatoes, Tahini Sauce, served in lavish bread http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sunrise-deli-berkeley?select=zwDNag0zdtNDz7seNd4U-g#zwDNag0zdtNDz7seNd4U-g

The wrap came split in half and the inclusion of potatoes in a falafel wrap was intriguing, which is why I decided to get the super falafel. The wrap was stuffed full and everything tasted yummy and went together nicely. The falafel was cooked nicely and slightly crunchy. I'm not sure if it's just me, but falafel always tastes pretty much the same to me and I don't think I've ever had bad falafel really. This is why it gets old sometimes and I only eat it every once in awhile. Portion size is big and I was super full after eating the whole thing!

I came here because I was craving falafel and hummus, so I went on yelp and this place popped up. I never really noticed this place even though I past by it soooo many times while going to school.

I ordered the Regular Falafel which had falafel(obviously), hummus, lettuce, tomatoes, tahini sauce in a pita bread. It was pretty good, I LOVED the falafels, they were so crispy and flavorful. I am a bit confused as to where all the hummus went though... or maybe i was the hummus and tahini sauce got mixed together and I couldnt find it. I tasted a little bit of hummus, but couldn't really find that hummus texture.

Still, it is a $4.99 is a very good price for a falafel sandwich and I am stuffed. I just wish it had more hummus.

Ordered the falafel sandwich two weeks ago. 

The good:
- Nicely portioned
- Good accompaniment of tomato & fixins -- what I want & expect 
- thin pita bread

The bad:
- Falafel a little mealy and very oily -- definitely not cooked in hot enough oil

The ugly:
- Server went back & forth from working register & taking money to handling & prepping food. Without washing his hands. 

Patrons seemed to enjoy their meals, but don't think I'll be back unless some hygiene 101 is incorporated ...

There usedtabe......outdoor falafel stands in Berkeley..............The best was run by Israelis, it was at the corner of Shattuck and  Center.  Falafels belong outdoors.. but that's a whole  other life, I guess.
Sunrise 
was wise            to open up a neareastern Deli  near  UCB.
It is very popular,
 sure it IS small, and no ATMOSPHERE, 

 but doesn't that make it more authentic? 
(not really a question)
I know I can't finish one of their sandwiches, so I  to go.

Then when I'm on the bus going home, everybody can have a whiff of
some foreign land.............

I've had the veggie plate from here in the past, which comes with hummus, baba ganoush, tabbouleh, falafel, dolmas and a few other things. It's quite filling and is always prepared quickly at a reasonable price. The inside is small, so plan of taking it to go, but everything is fast and the people are friendly.

The falafel and dolmas are some of the best I've had in the east bay. The hummus was not as good as other places, but the warm pita bread and the side of cucumbers and so many other  flavors totally made up for it.

This afternoon, I got a half dozen falafel and a half pint of tabbouleh. The total was $4.25 and it was quite a lot for a small snack. The falafel were fried perfectly, just like I remembered and the man behind the counter stuffed as much tabbouleh as possible into my to go container. It was super dense and super filling at lunch. I would have liked it if they drained the falafel a bit more, but I was in a rush so I suppose that's okay. Comes with a side of the great yogurt sauce.

Nice place for a full meal or a quick snack. Reasonable, close to everything, and with pretty extensive hours as well.

What this place lacks in atmosphere, it more than makes up for in taste.  It really is the best falafel in town.  It may even be better than Mamoun's in the Village.  They also have a location in the city which I have yet to try: http://www.yelp.com/biz/e02eHaL0toY64Tzodnx8_Q
I got a mango sago and it was a little bland and lacking true mango flavor. Oh well, can't complain too much when putting price and location into consideration.

the people that work there are SO SO nice. they try to provide the quickest service even if it's just boba. the best part is they offer drinks that are ~60 cents. for a poor college student, that's awesome. the burgers there are good too. they even have burger meals... and the boba... the best i ever had.
I love you even though you're average because it only takes whatever change I have at the bottom of my purse to get a pearl tea fix. Thanks!

Used to be my favorite boba place before I was introduced to Moccacino Cafe. The strawberry milk tea is sometimes too powdery, but other times, it's delicious. I suppose it's a gamble whenever I order it. The popcorn chicken is also pretty good, although the wait for it is extremely ridiculous. I was almost late to work because they took over 20 minutes to make popcorn chicken. Ridiculous! It's an okay place, but I definitely prefer other boba places to Sweethearts now.

The first time I came here it was good. Nothing great.

The second time I came here- my drink tasted like soy sauce.

As a Berkeley student, I loved coming to this shop. I always came for the Taiwanese style milk tea, and sometimes I ordered the food (burgers, fries, what have you). I also liked looking at the desserts they have in their display case, usually some variation of an Asian mochi treat.

If there was one of these closer to where I lived, I'd go all the time!

This is ONLY for the Mint Chocolate Chip Milkshake!!! Get it. Nuff said. So freaking good. I know I know, getting a milkshake at a Boba place is kinda random, but omg, yummy its amazing. Plus they are open pretty darn late, which is great.

(On second thought, boba rocks too (more like a 4 star)...esp the Jasmine green tea.)

Sweetheart cafe is probably one of the best multi-stored tapioca drink places I know. I'm not sure if they are franchised or not, but all I can say is that if I'm in the mood for a tapioca drink and I'm near one of these I'll get me one. The snacks that they have are truly amazing, my mouth salivates when I'm in the mood for crispy chicken, mmmMmm good.

I am giving them a 2 because of the bad service. However, this is decent boba for the price (which has been going up every year). My worst experience here was getting something I did not order and then I realized I was overcharged for what I ordered. I imagine this occurred because the girl taking my order was on the phone and yelling at others who work at the cafe all at the same time. After she screwed up our order she was yelled at by one of the workers there (family run place?). All they did was to replace our order with what we actually ordered but did not refund us for the extra money they charged. We left as we were fed up with the service and now I only go there once in a while (I used to go almost every night my freshmen year).

PS They say they open at 11 (or 11:30 am) but they never are, so never expect to get boba there at that time. One time I went at about 11-11:30 and they were supposed to be open but the guy inside just waved me and my friend away. The service here is crap. So if you want decent service and some to reply "thank you" go somewhere else the extra dollars are worth it.
it's overrated.. disgusting food. okay.. cheap boba

I've been to other boba places, and this is the original and still the best. Just writing the review reminds me it's been a while and makes me want Thai milk tea with tapioca NOW.

I've never eaten the food, but the candy they sell by the register is fun to try.

I've been going to Sweetheart Cafe for years now, and I must confess it isn't the best. I will testify that they make some really good drinks, and have some good food, but the service here is lousy as can be.

I do have to say though, that I'm not sure what Karen W is experiencing. I've never been here and been served nesquick. How do I know? I almost every time go in and get soy strawberry w/ pearls, and although they aren't fresh strawberries, they're real- really frozen. None the less, I find that my drinks are always very tasty.

The owner guy is really nice. Unlike other boba joints in the vicinity that shall not be named.

Cheap boba specials, strawberry / taro / jasmine green are all great choices.

Pearls/tapioca are soft and chewy. Perfectly cooked. Huge plus.

I've never had a burger here and never intend to. But I will always come here for milk tea. Thank you Sweetheart Cafe.

I've loved the cheap boba made out of powder for so long... but 99 cents? Come on. The one in Oakland is still at 59 cents, and it tastes better too. I can't believe the Berkeley Sweethearts has a higher rating than the Oakland one, but maybe that's cuz I've never been to the Oakland one personally.

It's a great place to be for cheap boba, open til 1 or 2am for wonderful night owl students, in a convenient location. However, their boba drinks are inconsistent from day to day, and their service isn't even trying. It's like we're begging them to give us boba-- okay, yeah, I guess we kinda are. They know they don't need to put in any friendly effort to keep business going, and so they don't.

So even though I've been a regular at Sweethearts, and I love that bubble milk tea... 3 stars for their service and crowded environment. And please, could we close the door just a bit when it's like a hurricane?

Yes, it's cheap. Yes, they have super-cheap deals. Yes, the boba is tasty here. But seriously, the rudeness is off-putting and it makes me uncomfortable to purchase drinks here. I really liked this place during the summer, when I first arrived, because I didn't know better, but since then I've been to places that have treated me like a customer and not a nuisance...that's kind of important when you run a business, I would think. It's a shame, but with so many other milk tea places around campus it's not much of a loss to my daily schedule.
Came here late night for bubble tea and popcorn chicken. The one-two combination brought me back. And it was so cheap. Definitely recommended if you're visiting or living in the area!

Still a great place after the college years have long been gone! This is probably the best bubble tea place to grab the perfect tapioca pearls in Berkeley and surrounding areas. 

The bubble tea is a great value. $3.58 got me two. While it seemed sweeter than before, it is a great deal for an excellent and well made drink. 

There wasn't a line either. Generally speaking, this place is pretty quick on getting your drinks out.

Cash only.

Dude, this place is good! Too bad it's all the way in Berkeley! But on the cup it did say there was a location in SF....anyways, I got the strawberry slush with boba. And when I got my order I noticed they put lychee in it by accident? I'm so glad they did cuz it was bomb!

The only thing I ever get from here is the $1.55 Bubble Milk Tea with Boba, which is awesome! The tea isn't too heavy, and the boba is just the right texture, a little soft and a bit firm. It's also really convenient that they stay open til' pretty late. Best boba I've ever had.
The only thing that sucks are the people who work here, who seem to hate their job. It's also a pretty small cafe, and is always packed. 
This place is way better than Quickly! Haha.

Update: Jacked up prices AGAIN, now bubble milk tea no pearls is $1.29.

For real good milk tea visit Pacific East Mall in Richmond and go to J&S Coffee and Tea

I think everyone else is right. The balls are sugary sweet- yum!  But for the past few times I've been there, I've noticed that the drinks (especially the $1.19 bubble milk tea) is really really really watered down - nasty! 

For a cheap cold drink on a hot day, come here. :)

Even though I walked right passed it, I didn't even know this place existed until we saw other people with boba drinks & asked where they got them from. It's located right outside that little alley of food, but I guess nothing caught my eye. 

I ordered a regular milk tea with lychee jelly. You can't go wrong with a milk tea. It wasn't the best boba drink I've ever had, but it definitely satisfied my craving :) 

+1 star for their quick service. 

I've heard great things about their Cookies & Creme. I think I need to try that if I'm ever back at Sweetheart Cafe.

Okay jasmine green tea on a hot summer day. 

Pros: near campus, cheap, fast service

Cons: taste like powder + water, service attitude 

Eh, can't complain since it is quite popular and convenient

I like the pearls here. They are sweet and tasty! 

However, I don't really like their actual drink. It's either too milky or too watery. But I do like to come here for their cheaper drinks such as pearl milk tea or milk green tea. The more expensive things aren't worth it because you can get tastier ones elsewhere. 

Also, this place is kind of old and dirty....so I wouldn't trust the candy they sell at the front, or the ice cream. Just stick with the classic common drinks to be safe!

Omg, there is no good milk tea or boba in Berkeley. The boba everywhere is always rubbery or stale, and the milk tea is always watered down. However, I give Sweetheart's 3 stars, because they have the best Taro Milk Tea that I have tried. It's not too sweet, and usually not too watered down. The service is very fast - there's usually no wait at all. Boba is very inexpensive but filling! AND, Sweethearts is open later than any other boba place.

The down sides... People there aren't ever that friendly. It's cash only, which I know is easier for businesses, but sometimes I really don't have cash!
Pretty cheap boba. I like my boba chewy. Sweetheart has some pretty chewy boba with "alright" tasting bubble milk tea. Definitely needed my boba fix, and I got it for less than 2 bucks.

Boba is always good although one time I got some shoddy tapioca pearls. 
Pretty expensive compared to most boba places I've been (~$3-4).
I am a lover of boba so I love stopping by this place for a delicious treat.

I've tried Chrysanthemum (really good), Regular Boba (always a fan), Roasted Boba (also good), Taiwan style (too creamy, not a fan), Honey Aloe Green (not with milk, pretty good), Coconut (very sweet), and Almond (ehh, it's okay).

Sweetheart Cafe certainly does not have the best boba in Berkeley but it is certainly the cheapest. 1.79 for a Jasmine Green Tea, Jasmine Green Milk Tea, or Milk Tea with pearls is a great deal and the drinks are decent but pretty inconsistent. Sometimes my Green Tea is perfectly sweetened and delicious and other times it is about as flavorful as a glass of water. I think it is worth the gamble but don't expect the best-tasting milk tea of your life. You get what you pay for!
Sweetheart Cafe has cheap boba. I guess it's okay... It doesn't compare to the boba places in rowland but when I crave boba (rarely, especially in Berkeley), I like Sweetheart over other places. :)

"MMmmmm tentacles....," as my friend Helen says when we go here

I like the fried squid here. It's really greasy and tentacl-y but it's so good and cruncy. I usually get icked out when I eat a whole body of mollusk like thing but for some reason, the dangling tentacles don't bother me that much here.

It's pretty peppery and you can add more spices to make it extra delicious. It's not gourmet calamari but it's a very decent to-go snack. It might look like a battered clump o sea creature but it's good. Just don't look at it.

Drinks are good - better than Quicky's and TapEx.

Food - not so much. Fried squid is extremely greasy.

Service is terrible and everyone is constantly screaming in Cantonese. This place actually reminds me of Chinatown. Except that it's in the middle of Berkeley. I just suck it up and get my drink, because this is the only decent milk tea place in Berkeley. SIGH.

Pretty much the best boba AND the best popcorn chicken I've ever had. The boba is always soft and chewy, and I LOVE how you can pour seasoning onto your chicken on your own! Boba is pretty cheap and they make it SUPER fast. The chicken is actually expensiveish, and it takes them literally 5 minutes to make it. 

The only other real downside is that if you want your boba with hot milk tea, they will charge extra. Also that they don't know what "boba" is, so you have to order "Bubble Milk Tea with Pearls." And that 90% of the time that I've ordered the boba+chicken combo, they give me like, the Taiwanese version of boba or something, where the milk tea is VERY orangish in color. I'm not sure how to convey that I just want the normal boba, but the orange one still tastes normal so I'm okay with it for now.
Cheap bubble tea and Taiwanese street food. What else can a starving student ask for? Neither are great quality but the price can't be beat.

We were trying to find boba in the area and my friend found this place on yelp. The reviews were fairly good but to my dissappointment, it wasn't as good as what the reviews said. The milk tea tastes watered down and the popcorn chicken is really bland. The only good thing about this place is the boba. I have to say, the boba is really good. Probably some of the best boba I've had. I really wished their milk tea complemented it. Because of the boba, this place gets three stars from me.
Sorry Sweetheart: the one star is for the extra dollar you charged just to heat up my iced milked tea (even though I had requested it hot the first time around).

Take note: I'm not a boba fan, but I have it every once in a blue moon. 

With that said, I didn't expect this place to taste amazing, and I was right- nothing extraordinary. Not bad, not good. Just your typical boba.

Upside: For all you boba fans, this place is open pretty late.

SMH. I feel like the quality of this place has gone down over the years. Maybe its just me. 
In high school my friends and I would drive all the way from Richmond to get Sweethearts, and now I only come here for their Pepper Squid when my sister is in town. 

The pepper squid and the popcorn chicken come in a brown paper bag with herbs which are quite yummy. :) if you mix it with the right amount of salt/pepper and chili powder MMMMMM. The portion is also really generous and can be shared with others. 

The milk teas are whatever and anything else is not worth what they charge. 

the service needs some improvement. This one time, I asked for more sticks for my pepper squid and the young worker almost stabbed me with one when he shoved it into my bag. WELL THEN MISTER. SOMEONE DOESNT LIKE THEIR JOB. Dont need to take it out on me! 

also, i find it weird that they call it bubble milk tea and then ask me if I want boba in it.....whats the bubble then -___(")

i added one more start from my last review 
the taro milk tea that i got today-was actually not THAT watery, finally.
if only their drinks were somewhat more consistent..
sometimes im like "wow it tastes like milk tea!" and other times im like "i should have just bought some quickly's instead..."

another reason i added a star is because i have to admit, their boba is sweet. its actually sweettttt! yay!! not many places have that, so i guess the boba SOMEWHAT makes up for the watery drink.
Really good. Fresh fruits, good tea, delicious boba. Puts all the other boba shops to shame.

been here twice. great pricing on specials. i was so excited when i got the lychee milk tea and there were actual lychees in the bottom of the cup!!

a little ghetto but it's ok.... this place is legit. with good mousse cake.

I used to get shaved ice and boba from sweetheart when I was living in Unit 3 down the street and it was such a good place. A one stop shop for all kinds of savory and sweet treats. But now the place is a bit run-down. The boba is still decent but I couldn't get any shaved ice because the machine was broken! Please get a new machine and rectify this!

Good place to pick up boba when you're in Berkeley around the campus or on Telegraph. 

The boba is good, nothing amazing, but inexpensive. 

Just remember to bring some cash

Not as dirt cheap as it once was, but still a pretty good deal.  I miss the days when this place was a dollar for milk tea with boba.  Now it's a little over $1.50 I believe -- not a huge price jump, but significant for a boba-addict like myself.  Besides, it was so nice when I could pay for my drink with my pocket change.

The pearls themselves are consistently good in quality - just chewy enough, just soft enough and a little sweet.  I've never had a problem with quality of boba at Sweethearts, unlike many of the boba places in Berkeley.  I'm a big fan of the lichi jelly as well.

The tea is another story - sometimes it's watered down, sometimes it's not sweet enough.  Sometimes, though, it's just right.  It's not exactly mind blowing, but quite good for the price.  

I don't get anything off their regular menu, only their discounted drinks menu, which includes Taro, Strawberry (not sure if they include this anymore...), Jasmine, and Boba tea.  The Taro is a little too sweet for my taste, but is very popular.  The strawberry milk tea is nothing special.  The Jasmine (no milk) is good for days when I feel guilty about drinking too much milk tea.  The Jasmine MILK tea though is pretty awful, in my opinion.  Every time I've gotten it it's been watered down and flavorless. 

As far as food goes, they've got a bunch of overpriced candy and some hot treats as well.  The pop-corn chicken is what you would expect for pop-corn chicken - fried, oily and delicious.

If you want cheap, reliable, boba, this is the place to hit up.  They're open ridiculously late, too, which is another bonus.   They don't have a lot of seating inside, but that's usually not a problem for boba.

P.S. - Don't touch any of the cakes in the deli cabinet - that stuff has been sitting there for months.  Trust me, I go at least once a week.

the ROASTED MILK TEA is sooooooooo good !!!! the best ever...
jasmine milk tea.. not too good..
almond milk tea.. OK lah..

I live in Emeryville, but when I want a milk tea after 9pm, when the places near my home close, I will get in the car, and drive through the 2983578457943 traffic lights to get to Sweetheart Cafe.  

This is where I go to satisfy my sweet and savory cravings.  The milk tea flavor choices are endless, but in addition to that, their tapioca pearls are the sweetest and chewiest that I've had in the area.  A tasty milk tea, paired with a bland tapioca pearl is not a good combination for me, but Sweetheart makes sure that no one ever experiences that at their shop.  Perhaps they soak the pearls in honey, or in sugar water, but whatever the case, I hope they don't change their method.  Boy oh boy, if I've gone through the trouble of driving over there and battling other drivers for parking, you better believe that I'm going to get my salty fix on as well.  The curly fries, when fresh out of the fryer, are amazing.  I'm a guy that likes to keep up appearances, but I throw those standards aside when I go to Sweetheart, and am caught with milk tea droplets on my clothes, curly fries crumbs on my shirt, and greasy fingers.  

It's a good thing I didn't go to Cal, because I'd be handing in papers with milk tea stains, and greasy finger prints all the time!
They usually have friendly service. Except they didn't accept my nickels and sell me the boba because "we have too many nickels". It is still legal tender. Horrible service.

4 1/2 stars

Hands down, best boba ever. Since I came to Berkeley, I have had so many cups of Sweetheart's boba. The standard milk tea (off the $0.69 special menu) is nothing special, but it's the actual boba pearls themselves that are the highlight - sweet and chewy (i think they cook and soak  the pearls in a sugar syrup), they've never been anything less than perfectly done (and like I said, I've had many a cup of boba here). I'm fond of their taro tea (i think the richness appeals to me), their many fruit-flavored teas (lycee and mango are good), their weekly special ($2 + tax), and their hot tea (try it, the pearls have a whole new texture). They have only 1 type of pudding though, so I go to Quickly's next door for my milk tea with honeydew pudding (so good).

They're open til 2am, which is probably one of the only places opened that late. I have had many great late night conversations at Sweetheart's, cradling a cup of milk tea, sitting at their little tables. The memories alone give them a high rating.

1/2 star off for the inconsistent customer service. Some people working there are just not nice.

I only frequent this place while accompanying someone else who has the late night urge to have boba milk tea.  

From having a sample sip from most of the drinks my friends buy, I can safely say, Stay away from the boba!  Even though the boba here has a better consistency than Quickly's, it still is not good enough for enjoyment.  They're not throughly gummy =( 

Experimenting with the different milk tea flavors offered is pretty fun though.  I enjoy ones with lychee and mango.  Some are made from real fruits but I have my suspicion that the vast  majority of flavors are syrup based (kitchen is in the back and you can't see them prepare it...shaddyyy)

Side note: why do they sell burgers? just why?

Yeah.....uh-huh....good.

Still working on tasting every single one of the drinks on that expansive list. I am up for the challenge SC!!

Although I love Berkeley, I do not love the boba milk tea its stores produce.  The boba itself was pretty good, chewy and sweet, but the milk tea was no bueno. It tastes too artificial to my liking.  3/4 way through I had to give it away. =(

I was surprised to see nite crawler eggs hanging on their candy aisle. The last time I saw those was at a gas station on the 5 freeway. I was tempted to buy them, but since the lady behind the counter was busy with another customer I decided to forgo the gummy treat.

Nice place for boba/pmt - much better than some other places in Berkeley (e.g. there is one on Durant that is cheaper but way worse). I always get the basic #1 or #2 - they're the cheapest and fulfill those boba longings, but there are lots of other options. Good stuff.
You cant go wrong with Sweet Heart Cafe, family owned and their boba is fresh. Open late

I would probably give this place 4 stars had they not increased their prices... but I'd have to say best boba near southside 

they could probably improve on organizing their menu... it's chaotic looking for a drink, then looking at the sticker system to see which color/star it pertains to just to find out how much the drink is... and all the while wondering how the heck did they categorize it all... it's not alphabetical.... or by the type of tapioca... ugh.   

always check the specials board that's by their door... one week, they had the mocha freeze (one of my favorites) as their special!!! ^.^ needless to say, i was out of cash that week (it's cash only).

they also have decent burgers (picture is of a carl's jr. ad) and dreyer's ice cream (unexpected) and curly fries and popcorn chicken. i'm not a fan of the squid, but i do like that they put more basil in their popcorn chicken than other places. =) they also have mochi and other japanese treats... and if you're craving them enough to spend what they charge for it, at least it's nearby :P

love the boba consistency, not too hard, squishy and soft, sweet... it's worth the 600+ calories!

I love this place but the prices are basically the same as nearby Quickly's. $1.49 for a bubble tea with bubbles is alright though. I love how sweet and gummy their bubbles are though.

It's a favorite of mine when I'm walking to class and sometimes I just have a craving for some bubble tea or if I'm on my way back to my room and feel like drinking something sweet while I read.

This place pales in comparison to other places i've tried, but considering prices and milk-tea boba ratio, this place is pretty good. The boba is small, but sweet and chewy, so that sorta makes up for the watery milk tea. And its also a bit cheaper than quickly's. I've the the burgers here once...and it was very ordinary. so i guess you should stick w/ their boba.

Thumbs up to them for actually replacing the worn-out chairs.

BUT BIG thumbs down for them for jacking up the prices of their milk tea by 30 cents. Prices are now $1.29 + 50 cents for upgrades...BOOO

Out of all the other boba places around the Berkeley campus, I only buy boba drinks here.

I do consider myself somewhat of a connoisseur, with Chinese blood running through my veins and having visited Taiwan, arguably the birthplace of boba (or "bubble tea," or "tapioca") drinks. I have tasted amazing boba, and though no American boba shop can touch Taiwan, this place is still head and shoulders above most.

The boba (little spherical black tapioca balls) itself are only OK, but the overall drinks are quite good. There is none of the powdery texture that you see/feel from the crappier boba shops (like Quickley's and Moccachino Cafe, two nearby shops. Gross). They also sell the usual fried toothpick-based foods (calamari, spicy popcorn chicken, etc.)

You will also find the largest variety on any boba menu anywhere, and each drink is genuinely different. Many are the traditional tea and milk tea variety, but others are various juices and exotic fruits. I consider myself an explorer, and unfortunately not all are good...definitely, definitely do not get the "Lemon Coke with Boba." Exploring is not supposed to be easy, but the reward can be great. My personal favorites are lychee, mixed pudding, and grass jelly. 

Despite all the good that can be found here, I feel like many reviewers rate Berkeley boba places based on the weekly drink specials, which do not do Sweetheart's justice. Normal prices are a tad more expensive ($3-5), but it's worth it to truly enjoy what this place has to offer. Go here. Now.

Appendix: I was curious for many years why this thoroughly Asian boba shop also offered Edy's ice cream and hamburgers. I finally tried both once. Mediocre.
Just a place near work that satisfy the craving of boba. Pretty cheap. Not fancy at all. Cash only, so be prepared.

The prices went a little bit up this semester, but I must say i LOVE this place. Their boba is always great and tastes a little bit sweet. Sugary drinks taste great and there's so much variety - always something new to try.

Melon Milk is great. In the summer I love Watermelon Freeze Boba. Their bubble milk tea is a great quick grab too. 

Late at night, if you're hungry their burgers and fries aren't bad at all :)

Less than $2 for a "bubble milk tea w/pearl", so what do you expect for the price?  Well...apparently "bubble milk tea" is different than "tapioca milk tea".  Who knew?

I only come here when I'm craving boba...unfortunately Berkeley doesn't have a stop for good boba (in my opinion).  But if you're craving boba, how can you not resist getting a $2 boba?

In the past, I had a "pepper chicken" phase for awhile too...their chicken is not good.  FYI.

I used to like this place a lot.. I'd always get the regular black milk tea or the jasmine milk tea with tapioca & it was pretty good! But then the last few times I went I felt like the quality of the boba became progressively worse :( 

The last time came here I was realllyyyyy craving boba.. and then when I got it, the milk tea barely had any flavor to it & tapioca was ridiculously hard and so hard to chew.. made me so sad... :(

And their service isn't even that great either - last time my friend accidently spilled her drink right after she bought it & they wouldn't even make another one for her! Umm excuuuse me are you kidding me right now?!?? Almost all other places would've replaced it for free if that ever happened. 

THE VERDICT: Go to Moccacino Cafe down on Bancroft for their 2 for $3 special and their consistent & better quality! (:
All the boba of a boba place, plus cheeseburgers that echo those of Oscars. Sweetheart succeeds in what it sets out to do, so five stars to them.
Decent milk tea and fat portions of popcorn chicken.

Worst thai tea ever. Apparently they think thai tea means milk tea. 0 stars.

Seriously, order a "Thai Ice Tea" and they will give you "Boba Milk Tea". They really think that's what Thai Tea tastes like.

This place has always been one of my favorite boba spots. The one in china town Oakland, isn't very good anymore. I would really recommend the peach slushy with pearls or without. If you get the peach slushy without pearls try it with some lychee jelly. Also their green milk tea is good if you want to try a new milk tea flavor that isn't over powering. If your in a coffee mood try the hazelnut mocha freeze with whip. The only reason why i didn't give it 5 stars is bc parking is a major B*TCH

God, I can't get enough of these tapioca drinks!  I've been coming here for years.  This is the only place I EVER get tapioca drinks from!  My favs are honeydew, piña colada, coconut milk, watermelon and mango milk.  Most of the time (for the fruity drink), you can taste the fresh fruit, sometimes it's a little artificial.  Either way, still delish!  The tapioca balls are soooooo yummy and chewy.  I think that's what I crave the most!  Prices vary around $2.75 - $4.25 for drinks. 

I want to try some of their fried food bc I always see ppl with their brown oil-stained bags of goodies, but I usually come here AFTER dinner as a treat. 

If I'm on a sweet binge, I go next door to get some donut holes, which are also absolutely my fav donut holes ever!
I'm still not a boba fan, but if i'm going to get some, this is the place I go.

Tried this place for the second time after a horrible experience with the passive-aggressive cashier, just to give it another chance and my stomach hurts. Whatever is in their milk teas (powders who-knows-what) needs to be examined. Im getting heartburn...like, seriously? To top it she is as rude as ever-news flash: WHEN YOURE CHARGING 4$ FOR HEARBURN AND A STOMACH ACHE YOU NOT GIVE AN ATTITUDE TO YOUR CUSTOMER!!!!

I'm from the South Bay, where there are a gazillion pearl milk tea places so personally I think Sweetheart drinks are just okay, teas are not strong flavored. I can tell that they use powdered tea instead of the real stuff...and their pearls are often too sweet for my liking. For some reason, the people at the register always seem a little cranky and come off a bit rude. But I guess it's cause they are always busy and service may be hard to keep up. 

However 5 stars for staying open late to feed hungry, stressed college kids and because they have the best taiwanese popcorn chicken in Berkeley. It's always nice and moist, compared to those at Quickly's ad Tapioca Express. Lastly, 2 stars for their drinks.
Avocado boba = big yum! Nice and cooling after an especially spicy meal. Other favorites include sago and coconut milk, as well as taro boba.

This is one of the cheapest places in Berkeley to get your boba fix.  They have an extensive selection of drinks.  Their boba balls are chewy and uniquely sweet but not overly.

With such price though, it's not surprising that their standard milk tea drinks (like bubble milk tea) taste somewhat diluted and lack a strong essence of tea.

Besides bubble milk tea, for about the same cheap price, I usually get green tea with lychee jelly.  There's a stronger tea taste with a bitterness that is perfectly complemented by the sweetness of the lychee.

They also offer various asian confections and deep-fried goodies.

Honestly, I'm not the most experienced with boba drinks :( but I'm getting there! Although the taste isn't the greatest (diluted??), the location and price won me over on day 1. They have increased their prices by a quarter or two over the past couple of years, but I still love getting a regular milk tea boba after a tough day or long day or great day.... yup, there's always a reason to get boba.

I used to come here with a co-worker late at night to catch up on our lives, since we would work together once a month. It was conveninient place to meet up since it opens til late.... I hated the popcorn chicken, too greasy and a little tasteless. They have separate condiments in little shakers which I guess is nice.... but I refuse to get popcorn chicken from here again. 

All that being said, I prefer going to Moccacino!! Pair your boba up with some popcorn chicken (sooo good!) and you'll be in heaven!

Nothing special about their tapioca drinks.  I usually get the coffee milk tea which is good.  

It's all about their popcorn chicken!  Unlike Quickly and other similar places, you don't really need to put any additional salt and pepper.  They already have it fried in the batter for you.  Plus, they put in a lot of basil that accentuates the flavors.

These tea's are tasty, but on the expensive side ($3-4). To make up for it, they have the best special that I've found so far (on southside at least)--large tapioca Taro or Strawberry Milk Tea for $2.05.

I love all the Sweethearts in all the location but this particular one is close to school.  Although the inside is cramped and dark the tapioca drinks totally make up for it. I always get the cookies n' cream mocha freeze. This is my favorite drink. The pearls are just the right amount of sweetness and chewiness, and they are never cheap w/ the amount of pearls like tap-x. I tried the avocado shake at another place and it tasted like  pure saturated fat but i tried it when it was a monthly special here, and it was delicious!

K, I like this place. It is better than other boba place in berkeley, and the prices are decent...slightly overpriced for certain drinks, but great for the jasmine green milk tea ($1.79). This is all I get from there...I got a slushy once and it came out to 5 dollars...me think not! So, good for a caffeine fix and yummy...oh yeah, the service is quick and great!

Have you ever seen their huge "DELICIOUS BUNS. HERALD OF LIFE" posters? I'm always so amused by those. I thought they would be stale and boring but the PORK BUNS (3 for $1.25) was some of the best comfort food I had gotten in the last week. Warm those little things up and it makes for a great snack or appetizer. I can't give Sweetheart too much credit though since they buy them from a bakery in Oakland Chinatown.

Also, I don't regularly buy boba, but when I do, I get the LYCHEE SLUSH.

Last year this was my go-to place for Taro Milk Tea. I recently started going to Quickly's though, and realized that Sweetheart's Taro Milk Tea is cheaper but also diluted. I'll only go to Sweetheart now if it's late at night and/or I'm broke.
Green tea slushy and Mango/ Passionfruit slushy are the best ! Alos tasty curly fires!

THEY STOLE MY MONEY! LITERALLY!!
so I went in one night and was getting a bubble milk tea for $1.79. I put a dollar down on the counter and while I was pulling out the 79 cents, the cashier took my dollar off the counter. When I put down the rest of the money, she said I still owed her $1. I insisted that I had already given her the dollar but she kept saying she "didn't see it" and that I "still owed her". She then proceeded to stare blankly at me. I didn't know how to tell her that I SAW HER SWIPE MY DOLLAR FROM THE COUNTER without outright accusing her. When she took it, I didn't think she was TRYING to steal from me. I thought she was just holding onto my dollar and waiting for me to get the rest of the $ from my wallet. I was absolutely appalled. I don't think I will go here anymore. I prefer Double Rainbow Cafe on Bancroft (they have a 2 for $3 deal with better flavors). DON'T SUPPORT MONEY HUNGRY THIEVES!!!!

The first time I ordered a boba drink from the cutely decorated Sweetheart Cafe, I thought I had found my favorite boba place in Berkeley. The drink (black boba tea) was a perfect companion on a hot day walking along Telegraph Ave. The second time I returned to Sweetheart Cafe, however, my drink was too sweet and the tapioca balls were not cooked thoroughly. I gave the cafe a third chance, but found my drink to be less than desirable again. A hit-and-miss place for boba. I recommend trying The Old Teahouse (located about 10 ft. away)-- similar price range as Sweetheart, but more consistent quality drinks.

Very good chocolate milkshakes with pearls here (my favorite) and of course the usual pearl tea (tapicoa) drinks.  Sometimes the service is a little slow, especially if there are a lot of people in line.  Very small space, so only a couple of seats inside.  More of a take out place!

I like their Jasmine Green Tea Boba w/o ice nor boba pearls. This place isn't bad, especially for the price. Their flavors are nice and strong. Their popcorn chicken is pretty good, but oh-so-unhealthy. Small shop and sometimes gets crowded, but it hasn't been too much of a problem at odd hours (between or right after classes), but definitely could get very busy during the evenings.
Always love their classic milktea with large tapica. They're somewhat chewier than other tapioca places.

I love the milkshakes.  It's like ice cream put in a blender with a splash of milk.

The pearls are the best I've had around campus.  I never get milk teas.

The curly fries are super tasty.

The service is lacking.  They're rude and act like you shouldn't be there.  One time the girl didn't give me my change (I would have given you a tip if you didn't take my change).

Yes, the space is small, but the boba is done right. 

My favorite is the green tea boba (they raised the price) =(

 No artificial milk crap in my green tea. 

The service is good and fast. My order is always correct. 

4 stars for extra boba. =)
Best boba in berkeley in my opinion. Super cheap and quick. They always have deals going on which make it even cheaper. I like their mango stars the best. It goes great with the strawberry milk tea.

It's my brother's place for boba in Berkeley. He got a milk tea but I don't know the exact name; all I know is it tasted a bit different. They are really quick with making your drinks and actually speak Cantonese. They also have small snacks and BBQ pork buns though I'm not sure how good they are. The prices are decent. Overall decent place to get your Asian drink fix in the Berkeley area.
They make their pearls soft and chewy, unlike Quickleys and their milk tea is pretty flavorful. When I'm feeling generous to myself, I get the strawberry banana smoothie with pearl. Yum!

The boba was.. interesting, to put it in a nice way. If you chewed on the tapioca and burped, it tasted like popcorn chicken. i do not know why and dont want to.

The milk tea was a bit watery and lacking in punch. Just wasn't as satisfying as boba milk tea should be, but was drinkable.

My new spot for milk tea. It has a certain taste to it that makes it oh so delicious. Sweethearts also has the cheapest milk tea available in the ghetto, with pearls or an upgrade to large being an extra 50 cents.

The popcorn chicken isn't bad either, deep fried and served with basil leaves.

$1.55 for a jasmine green milk tea with pearls...not bad at all! The milk tea itself had a pretty strong tea taste which I like, but I didn't really think it was sweet enough. The pearls were cooked just right, not mushy but not hard that it hurts your jaw to chew it. I have yet to try the snacks here, but it looks like they have a pretty good selection!

By far some of the best boba milk tea I've ever had. The pearls were very fresh, not liquidy or hard like some places can be. But as other reviewers have said the seating is pretty limited, but the drink quality is top notch.

I ordered their coconut milk with sago once and it was really good! It wasn't overwhelmingly sweet and the consistency was nice. Unfortunately, I ordered the almond milk tea with pearls today and it was terrible. It was really watered down and the almond flavor left a weird after taste in my mouth. Also, I'm not sure why it was a tawny orange-brown color...most of the almond milks I have had are white.

"Meh, I've experience better" is how Yelp defines the 2-star rating. That's exactly what it is.

The portions of the boba are relatively small given the competitors in the area. The prices aren't any cheaper than, say, Quickly just a couple doors down. The milk tea has always tasted like it has been diluted to me. I can't imagine this being ANYBODY's choice for boba (or PMT to the NorCal kids). But it is, and I'll never understand why.

Drunken night and we wanted some heart clogging snacky food, so we came here for fries. My sober friend thought they were way salty and looked at us in disgust as the rest of us devoured them like a pack of hyenas. Damn they were good. Perfect for our numbed up tastebuds. 

I have come here for milk tea on other occasions though and I've never gotten one I really enjoyed. It's weird tasting...like watered down overly sweet milk tea.

Perhaps all the bad things everyone else says are true. 4 stars because I had my first boba drink here and now I'm hooked* , the blended coconut milk with boba tastes like an orgasm but sweeter, and my best girl Morgan and I always go get them at Sweethearts when she's in town. No one makes is better. At least that I've tried... yet.


* I bought my first bobas from the store yesterday and am planning on cooking them and making my own drink tonight!

Ah Sweetheart Cafe. I've trekked out to the South side of campus so many times to fulfill boba cravings. 

I remember freshman year of college, my roommate used to bring coins to pay for her drink because it was $1.17 back then. The cashier eventually stopped counting the coins, and muttered profanities in Cantonese under her breath whenever my roommate showed up with the coins. Random, I know, haha. 

Anyways, the boba here is always so fresh tasting. I've been to a few other places--the worst being the boba shop on Shattuck--Lollicup is it? I usually order the Jasmine green tea with boba--no milk. It's very refreshing, and usually always hits the spot.

I'll miss paying under $2 for a boba drink when I move further away from the campus. I really will.

Okay. So there are like five other places next door that serve tapioca/boba/whatever the fuck you wanna call it. All of them have better service. Frankly, all of the boba in the telegraph area are similarly priced, so don't waste your time going here!

This has always been our favorite boba joint during college. Nowadays I get to visit it only once in a while if I am near campus. I also introduced my friends to this place and they all loved their boba and wanted more. Yes the prices are a little more expensive than Quicklys around the corner, but their boba definite taste better. My favorite is the Taiwanese green milk tea with pearls. The Lychee milk tea is also very yummy and comes with both pearls and lychee jellies, yum! I also love their fried squid. Definitely try this place if you have boba cravings.

Doesn't beat Pacific East Mall's J & S Coffee & Tea House, but still great. I LOVE LOVE LOVE their Banana Lover smoothie (WITH PEARL). It is great.

One thing I don't like, cash only. But it is Asian Ghetto, so it's understandable. But still, I have a card, I NEVER have cash, so yeah.

Also, one of the people at the registers (a girl) has an obnoxiously rude attitude that most Cantonese women have when they're aggravated, but there's this thing called CUSTOMER SERVICE and it's what keeps me and other people coming back.

A-OK, but needs customer service training.

Oh, and the burgers are excellent.
High marks for the Boba which is a delightful treat.

I've been in berkeley for over two years and I just love this place! I've tried so many boba places but Sweatheart is my favorite. It's a little pricier than other places nearby but i feel the quality is so much better! My favorite is the passionfruit or mango slush. The boba are super fresh and squishy (not hard like other places). Wish that it wasn't cash only, but can't complain about the drinks!

one of the best boba places in norcal!
i love the mango milk with boba

Try #22 the Vanilla green tea with pearl.  They do have the best boba that I've ever tried (yes there is bad boba...one that's hard in the middle and not squishy enough).  And trust me, I've tried a lot of Boba in my day.  They also have some good hangover food ie fries, burgers, chicken tenders.

Hands down the best tapioca I've ever had. The pearls are always soft and chewy. The quality is reliable. 

The people working there typically feels like there are other places they rather be but that's true for almost every tapioca place I've ever been. It comes with the territory. The drinks are good and that's good enough for me.

Price and boba balls

Super cheap and great for college students who need that caffeine or just sugar rush during those laggy days

Yummmm, flavored sweet and chewy boba balls. Awesome texture.

Well, I'm not entirely sure WHY so many people recommend going to Sweethearts for boba on campus....because in my opinion, it's not that great....

Located right at the entrance of Asian Ghetto on Durant, it's a pretty convenient spot to meet up with friends.

Yes, boba tea is pretty cheap and whatnot, but every time I go there to order, the cashiers are always so grumpy or mildly rude. They give you the impression as if they don't even want to be there...which starts making me not what to be there either, haha.

There's nothing special or great about their boba. About 30% of the time I get boba there, it's warm. And as any boba-drinker out there, you all know that warm boba milk tea tastes kind of strange.

Anyways, there are better boba places around campus! Sorry, Sweethearts, but you break my boba-loving heart.

Five stars for some of the best pearls I've tasted in the Bay Area.  They're soft, chewy, and they're not too sweet.  Plus, at $1.50 for a green tea with pearls, it's a steal.  I'd definitely come here more often... if I lived in Berkeley and not San Jose.  :-P

I've been frequenting this place for quite a while now to satisfy my boba craves at 1AM or just to quench my thirst. Place is usually open and I haven't been finding any random hairs in my boba so I guess this place deserves an upgrade. But I've come here countless times just to walk back in the bitter cold because I tend to forget that they still don't accept card...

I used to come here for really one item - their fries. Man, when it's 12am/1am, and you need something greasy and hot for cheap, Sweetheart's is the place to go for a cheap bite. It's basically a Quickly's, but not as Asian-fied. The fries are always hot, cheap, and greasy, almost like a bad porno, except delicious.

I'm not a connoisseur of pearl drinks and such, but I stopped here last week for a cheap drink and got the bubble milk tea for 99 cents. It was incredibly good. They have so many different drinks on the menu that I wish I'd discovered this place earlier. So check it out some time, right outside the Durant Food Court ("Asian" Ghetto).
No more hot grass jelly?!  One star GONE!!!

Was there today and had their COMBO D (fried squid w/milk pearl tea) and the bubbletea was alright and their fried squid...hmmmm...how should I say this, I went straight to the bathroom shortly after :(  Partially was either too much batter or barely any batter and either too salty or no taste. Worst part, they didn't even have "HOT SAUCE"!!!

I've been coming to Sweethearts since my sister went to Cal. Going on 8 year strong! I can't believe I'm doing a review now, but I'm encouraged to write amount the change in quality =(

I would give their boba a 3.5 star. I always love a deal $1.79 for Jasmine Milk Tea. The tea is never watered down and it's not filled with excess ice (I don't feel ripped off lol).

I remember always coming here for boba and popcorn chicken with my sister, but lately when I've been coming here for that sweet memory the chicken isn't as delicious as before. I would give it a 1.5 star. Before Sweetheart's popcorn chicken had a wonderful mixture of herbs in the popcorn chicken. I can still remember the taste of basil and other herbs tossed with the chicken. Now, they seem to have conformed to Quickly's popcorn chicken... salted fried chicken, not that wonderful. So maybe if the owner reads this review PLEASE consider putting a little more love in the recipe like you guys did a few years ago, it would really make me order the popcorn chicken again.

My boyfriend and I went here because we were craving boba big time and we saw a ton of Berkeley students going here.

I ordered a standard green milk tea with boba and he got an almond milk tea with boba. The both milk teas were fine (although the almond taste was a bit too strong and artificial for me) but there was something really off about the boba. I couldn't put a finger on exactly what it was but there was something wrong with the texture of it and after a while, it got kind of gross. I don't think I'd come here again unless it was really convenient to do so.

I have nothing against their boba or their food.  First of all, I don't drink boba.  I came here for popcorn chicken after boba cafe closed down.  

I know it's not really their fault since the Sweetheart Cafe is located in the asian ghetto, and most places in Berkeley are probably not quite up to code.  But once, I saw a couple of rats (small rats, but rats nonethless), crawl across the floor and even over an unsuspecting girl's foot.  Needless to say, it was definitely enough for me to vow NEVER EVER to go back there again.

best boba i've had!  for those who don't know who boba is (i sure didn't before i moved to cali), it's a drink with large mushy tapioca pearls (also called pearl tea or bubble tea).  sweetheart has a great selection of juices, smoothies, teas, and milk teas.  just beware the fresh young coconut juice flavor.  the coconut is *not* fresh!  it's definitely out of a can and has a weird flavor accompanied by a metallic tang.  somehow, that bizarre taste combined with the boba made me feel like i was drinking clotted blood.  it was gross...steer clear of the coconut juice.  (the coconut milk tea is fine though).
Best Boba in Berkeley. a must when visiting the Telegraph area. this place is too good!

Probably one of the saddest moments of my time at Berkeley was when I came down to Sweethearts with just my 99 cents in change and discovered I couldn't get my bubble milk tea with no tapioca.  =(

But Sweethearts is still my favorite place to get my plain ol regular milk tea because, in my opinion, it tastes the best compared to Quickly and Lotus House.  Also, since I normally only order the plain milk tea, it comes out lightning fast.

The only downside of my Sweethearts trip is that it now costs $1.29, but it's still definitely worth it .
love the taiwan style bubble milk tea with pearls.  I haven't had any bubble milk tea that tastes better than at this place.  The snacks are yummy too.

"I WANT SOME BALLS!!!!!!" We only come here for the drinks, never the food (I don't think I can trust the food). They only accept cash - BOO! I hate only cash-taking places. The cashier doesn't speak English so speak clearly. If you decide that you'll be coming here often, then ask them for a stamp card so that you can get a free drink once the card is full (I think ten stamps are required for a free drink). 

Ever since my bestfriends and I first discovered tapioca pearl milk tea drinks, we've been hooked! We call them "balls," and this place has the most perfect balls, ever - soft, slightly sweet, chewy, and fresh tasting! Yes!! A lot of people give us crazy and disgusted looks whenever we publicly announce our love for balls lol -- "Let's go grab some balls!" "I miss balls" "Balls are soooo good!!" -- The jokes and our love for balls will continue forever and ever... I love getting the usual "Pearl Milk Tea," and sometimes I mix things up by getting the "Thai Iced Tea with Pearls." I don't like ordering any other mixed drinks because sometimes they're made too sweet, and it tastes funky or artificial. Smoothies make the balls hard. I recommend getting regular teas or something light like taro. If you want something really refreshing on a summer day, I'd suggest you get the honeydew melon tea with pearls; it's really light and not too sweet at all. I really cannot get enough of these balls.

First I was already disappointed that they didn't have Peach Green Milk Tea. Then I get really disappointed when I order a Jasmine Milk Tea but somehow my drink is super watery and diluted. not cool. :(

i've been craving a milkshake for weeks now. no joke. 

me and a friend were on a last minute food run before a night out in the city and she decided to stop by I.B.'s for some chili cheese fries, and i realized i could probably get a milkshake at sweetheart. didn't see any milkshakes on the menu so i settled for a coconut smoothie.

while they were in the process of making my smoothie i realized the sign on the wall that said "milkshakes". son of a bitch!! it's too late now. all good though because that coconut smoothie was on HIT! 

the only thing that irked me out was that when i walked in, i went up to the counter and the guy was on his cellphone. he looked at me. i looked at him. he continued to talk. if i did this at my job i would be fired in a heartbeat.

Oh my beloved Sweetheart Cafe, if only I could give you 5 stars.

I've gotten pretty much all of my friends addicted to the milk tea with boba here which is tasty and cheap.

The only problem I have happens every so often and every time it happens I am severely disappointed.

I come here fairly often, and 1 out of say every 3 or 4 times I order here this happens:

I order a milk tea with boba. Everything seems to be fine until I receive my order and or check my receipt. Instead of a delicious milk tea, I end up with some dark orange thai-tasting monstrosity D: AND I was charged extra for getting what I did not want.

Because this happens repeatedly to me and is by no means an isolated incident, here are some tips to keep this from happening to you.

1. Articulate as well as you can that you would like a "MILK TEA" don't even say with boba, because they will always ask you if you want it and when they do you can reply, "Yes". I find this is the best way to keep the cashier from getting confused and putting your order down as something else. 
2. As Tip #1 has been known to fail me from time to time, pay attention to how much you are being charged. If they ask you for any more than $2, you are being charged for something that is not a regular milk tea with boba (which runs at $1.79)

As a broke college student I appreciate their cheap drinks and relatively fast service, which is why I wish they would re-name their teas or get better cashiers or something that would stop this from happening.

As for those people complaining about the milk tea being diluted, I suggest ordering yours without ice. This will keep it from getting watered down.

My Taiwanese jasmine green tea was realllllly milky, and my friend's bubble milk tea was revolting. Mine at least was edible and drinkable, with the jasmine flavor coming out very strongly (overpowers the tea taste), good sweetness level, but the boba was slightly hard to chew and stiff....so I would most likely not come here again. This might have to do with us stopping by kind of late (11:30pm-ish)...but that shouldn't really be an excuse.

Personal experience- went to topdog but didnt get a drink but only had a bucks and some change in my pocket. walked across the street to sweetheart's and noticed what?! 1.29 for just milk tea?! and 1.79 with boba?! LOL I was set after that. NUFF SAID haha.

one thing though the cashier seemed like she didn't want to touch anyone which she didn't even have to  -__- leaving my change on the counter when you can just drop the coins in my hands with out touching me? I don't know maybe shes stuck up or very unsociable, either way that effected my rating but its A-OK in my books

Well...I was a boba virgin. Always afraid of the consistency of balls. And then, I went to Sweetheart, and it changed everything for me. 

I regularly order a variety of the fruit freezes here with extra pearls. They never go wrong for me. They are always sweet and go above and beyond to make the drinks to my liking. I even have a frequent buyer card. 

No Flavor? You must be kidding me! You're ordering the wrong thing then! Go by me...the connoisseur of boba.
Yum! That was the first word out of my mouth after trying a milk tea boba my brother brought home. When I found it out was only 69cents, I was even more impressed!

Best Boba (Tapioca Milk Tea) in Berkeley as well as one of its extremely rare establishments that sells real ice cream and not that frozen yogurt stuff.  They sell Dreyer's Ice Cream and also very good milkshakes.

My default boba place because
a. they cook the tapioca just right. not that undercooked hard shit in the middle (like quickly's next door) or too mush gushy. JUST RIGHT.
b. they're open until 2 a.m., so as long as i can haul ass over there before then, i'm good.
c. they sell hella tasty popcorn chicken, though i feel like any other non-boba on their menu (e.g. the burgers?) would just be too sketch to try out.
d. rotating daily specials!

i just wish they had more seating (not so close to the door), so it'd almost be like a cafe where you can study.

Here's the rundown:
Their boba is pretty cheap. 
There's always a line but it moves fast. 
Cash only.

I really wanted to like this place, but have never been more disappointed by a bubble tea café. Maybe it was a poor choice of flavors, but the durian shake was so bad (weird smoky flavor) that we had to throw it out, and the mango was also uninspiring, with a strange artificial aftertaste. The pearls were too sticky-sweet for my taste. The décor leaves much to be desired too, though it seems most people grab drinks to go. Having just gone to Asha Tea House the day before, and spent less ($3.75 on a drink instead of $4), I can't imagine ever coming back to Sweetheart Café's uninspiring environment and overpriced, poor-quality drinks.

So outta all the boba places that they have around durant food court area, I'd say that I like Sweetheart Cafe the most. Really lax service, and cheap milk tea which is usually what I go for anyways when I have a few extra dollars in my wallet, since they do cash only. Overall great! But also pretty small and gets kinda. Crowded at night.

Don't be frightened by the dirty, over-packed store with an angry-looking lady behind the register. And don't fall for the sketchy hamburgers this store claims to sell. This place is just like a Halloween haunted house: you must endure the torture to get your treat.

The only thing I've tried here was the milk tea with boba. That's the ONLY thing I get when I'm trying out a new boba place. Wow. The milk tea tastes like the ones I had when I was a kid ... when my Japanese exchange student brought me bottles of milk tea.

So, I would say this is good in my book. Once I move here, and try some of their other drinks (and if I like them), there is a possibility that this will be my boba place.

This place always seems a little grungy to me, but it's inexpensive boba that is open late at night and is therefore popular with the student population. I had their regular pearl milk tea today for $1.79 I believe--it's really sweet, which makes me suspect that they add sugar. Mochaccino will always be my favorite boba place in Berkeley, but Sweetheart is in a prime location to get tons of foot traffic and I'm sure they will continue to thrive if their prices stay cheap.

The only place that serves deep fried black peppered baby squids (you know, the whole squid with the curly little legs).  Everywhere I've looked, they only have squid balls or calamari type squid. I like them whole!

Though they don't get that 5th star because the jasmine green milk tea that I bought had a few stray tea leaves in there... though I appreciate the authentic tea, I make the same kind at home - that's why I pay you the extra $2.50, make sure its strained!

Love the bubble milk tea and the fried pepper squid. Totally addictive. Price is cheap for the bubble milk tea. The place is very small, so you cant really sit there and hang out with friends. They serve popcorn chicken, hamburgers, ice cream and other stuff as well. It closes pretty late which is good (sometimes closes earlier than they should). Given the wrong order a few times as well ==''

When I'm in the area,  I stop by Sweetheart Cafe first before walking over to Top Dog. I'll order the Coconut Milk Tapioca drink. It's coconut juice blended together with ice milk...comes out almost creamy. This girl i use to date introduced this drink to me about 6 years ago and its still the only drink I would get...yes it's that good! mmmmm 

I noticed that they're serving hamburgers which was odd....doubt I'll ever try though.

Needed a boba fix before touring the campus of UC Berkeley with my cousin who goes there. Stopped by here. Really small place. Everything is posted up on poster paper on the walls. Prices are decent and selection is pretty big. Lots of random specials on drinks. 

I got a strawberry milk tea. It was alright. Tasted kind of weird to me. I traded with my boyfriend who got a green tea I think. Pretty standard green tea drink. My sister got a lemon honey tea with aloe. That one was actually pretty good 

And I don't know if it was just that day but they had full size samples of their buns. They were pretty good. They had hot dog bun, pineapple bun and some other bun.

Overall, I would come here to get another boba fix, but not one of my favorites because I like the ones where you can hang out in.
the tapioca pearls are cooked perfectly every time. The pearls have the right chewy cosistency.

I always come here to get boba with a friend. They have a lot of varieties. It's a little overwhelming sometimes. I usually just stick to two flavors. They are really fast about it too. You just pay for your boba, and it's ready for you in 1-2 minutes.
Went to Berkeley over the weekend for a tournament, and had milk tea 5 times. and its HELLA cheap, $2.29 for a large milk tea with boba? Hell yea.

The battle between Sweethearts and Quicklys rages on. Unfortunately, I'm sticking with Quicklys.

Service: The cashier at the front is rude. She yells at you for your order even when there's no one else waiting in line. 

Food: I found popcorn chicken here to be a bit better than Quicklys. It's a little more moist (or oily, I suppose), and it has never been dry. I would definitely prefer the boba at Quickly, though. Both their tea and boba are too sweet for my liking, and sometimes it even tastes a little powdered. I haven't tried many of the specialty drinks, but hey, college budget.

Pity, I didn't want to side with the chain, but for boba, I'm going with Quickly.

Had a Jasmine milk tea w/ pearls.  Pearls were really good.

under $1.50 CHEAP.

I went yesterday for a strawberry milk tea and an ovaltine slush boba.

$5.98 for 2 including the $1.45 special

Pearls are good.

Ovaltine could have been mixed more. 

Satisfied my boba craving but not very memorable.

One of the few places with sago. 

The only tapioca place I got when I'm in Berkeley.

Other people have talked about it and it's true:  MUSHY BALLS SUCK.  Sweetheart is really imbalanced and for some reason can be perfect sometimes, and horrible other times.  Quickly's is far more consistent and cheaper.  The people working there seem to look down upon everyone going to their store for some odd reason.  

To their credit, they are open fairly late when everyone else is slow which is good for those late-night boba runs.  Also the little snacks are quite good.  Still, for a drink shop it leaves a lot to be desired in the drink department,

I've never liked boba much but that was because I hadn't tried it from Sweetheart's. My roomie now (floormate then) took me here and I refuse boba from any other place. 

Firstly, it's really inexpensive. Secondly, the taste of the milk tea and the boba are yummy. I've had some of the slushies which were a bit too filling for me. The milk teas were a much better fit. I like strawberry milk tea the best and boy do I gulp that thing down. The boba is sweet and chewy which I really like. 

My heart belongs to Sweetheart's!

I LOVE PASSION FRUIT GREEN TEA!!! this place is bomb... i love bubble tea and i can honestly say that this is the BEST bubble tea in the bay!!!!


YAY SWEETHEART CAFE!!
We were close by and had to stop. I had my usual  litchi green milk tea with boba. Cool little spot!

It was 11pm, I was at a cafe in Berkeley getting some work done, and then just out of the blue, the manager kicked my bf and I out because they were closing.

So... having the munchies and craving tapioca drinks, we checked if Quickly or Tapioca Express were open at this hour only to discover that they close pretty damn early! It's Berkeley, a college town!!!! Why would you guys close at 9 and 10pm in the first place?!!! :( But anyways, we Yelped some places that served tapioca drinks and Sweetheart Cafe came up as one of the first few results! 

When we got to the cafe, we noticed a lot of people hanging out near the entry way, so I was thinking it was going to be packed with 40 or more people. Turns out it's more of an "order-and-get-the-hell-out" type of cafe since the space surrounding the cashier was occupied by huge boxes and only as much as 8 people could wait inside for their orders. I got a little claustrophobic once I put in my order, so I decided to wait outside until everyone else left.

Fifteen minutes later, I receive my order: a green apple slushy with tapioca AND lychee cubes, popcorn chicken and fried fish balls. I've never had a green apple slushy before, nor have I had lychee cubes added into a tapioca drink, but it tasted great! The lychee acted as a sweetening balance to the sour taste of the green apple juice. I wouldn't have enjoyed the drink as much without the lychee. The crispy popcorn chicken tastes exactly as it's made by Quickly, Tapioca Express and Lollicup (ironically), but the fried fish balls were damp and bland. It could use some salt and pepper, but then again, maybe I should have ordered the curry fish balls instead.

Not sure if I'll be coming back here in the future since I rarely spend time in Berkeley, but since the cafe sits next to a very attracting food plaza with nearly every ethnic food you can think of, I just might think about getting a tapioca drink from Sweetheart Cafe before leaving.

Sweetheart has locations in Oakland Chinatown, this location in Berkeley, and in McCarthy Ranch (Milpitas).  They are very consistent in the flavor of their drinks and the same drink will taste the same at a different location.  

My personal favorites are Mango Milk, Jackfruit Smoothie, and Taro and Coconut Milk.  Each drink is about $4, and they are definitely better than Quickly inside of Durant Square.
