Tip 'o the day:  Ask for a stamp card.  Buy 10 drinks, get one free!
Cheap boba. Like $1.25 for a regular...yea that's all that matters. awesome

Dang, I haven't been here since college.  When a boba craving hits, it hits.

I had a lychee green milk tea with boba and it hit the spot.  Yummy, chewy tapioca! Definite plus for having actual lychee fruit chunks. Too bad some of them were too big and didn't make it through the straw, sad day. 

Student friendly prices and speedy service.

Cheap boba! Get the jasmine green milk tea; it's under 2 bucks with pearls.

It's one of the better boba place close to campus, but I've had better boba elsewhere. 

I wouldn't buy the candy or the cake/mochi things in the display, cause I feel like they've been there forever. 

I would also refrain myself from ordering anything other than the simple tea bobas (bubble tea, jasmine green tea, jasmine green milk tea). The fruit and the "hamburger" ingredients are probably not the freshest, and the popcorn chicken is a giant oily mess.

However, now they sell pineapple buns and pork buns (a couple of bucks for a pack of three, I think). Haven't tried them yet, but they seem to restock everyday. 


Cash only, like everything else in asian ghetto (or DFC, so all you politically correct people out there).

This place is conveniently located in berkeley's notorious "Asian Ghetto." I always stumble into here on my way back to my apartment on a hot day. Their boba is pretty standard; average prices. 

I always get the strawberry milk tea for 2 bucks. My favorite drink from here is the strawberry peach smoothie w/ boba. A little pricy at over 4 bucks, but it's delicious! Don't get the strawberry banana  one though...no flavor :(

When visiting Berkeley last summer, I suddenly felt the overpowering need for boba tea.  And there this place was, like a miraculous apparition from the heavens!

Alas, had it only been a mirage, and not a real place existing in the real world.  This is the first place from which I've had tapioca tea so disgusting that I had to throw it out.  I ordered taro milk tea with boba - usually a pretty foolproof choice.  Wrong!  It tasted like aspartame with artificial grape flavoring plus a hint of potato.  My companion had something else, I think a Thai tea, and it was slightly less murderously offensive, but nothing I would call tasty.  I wouldn't come back here unless I was actually in a desert and dying of dehydration.

This place deserves 5 stars because it is SO GOOD! The prices are good, the people are nice, and it is in a really great location. I come here all the time, it is the perfect place to de-stress after a class or too much homework!

I've had a lot of almond boba tea's but the ones at Sweetheart cafe rule all the others. They have a huge selection of different teas to choose from if you're not into almond, and all the ones i've tried are amazing. Their green tea milkshakes are to die for! Oh and you must order their popcorn chicken. It's little fried chicken pieces with basil. It's given to you in little bag with a pokey skewer stick so you can stab it and not get your hands greasy. We call it stabby chicken. Although most boba places serve this stabby chicken, Sweetheart Cafe has the best by far! I used to be secretly in love with this one guy who worked there but he totally had a girlfriend. Psh Whatever. haha.

Gone are the days of boba for 70 cents. Which is really what they should be charging, as it only consists of some powder mixed in as a drink. 

It's better than Quickly's though.

I am definitely not impressed.  The drinks should not even be worth a dollar because it is so watered down.

I have gone to over at least fifteen different pearl/boba drink stores (and no, they were not all the typical Tapioca Express or Quickly's), and this place falls under one of the worst I've been to. I know I sound harsh, but hey, I guess I'm just crazy about my green milk teas.

The pearls have a weird chewiness to it.  It's not a bad thing, but I don't like it either.  I don't know.  Nothing is too unique about the store; I didn't find the aura to be much to my liking either. Maybe the pink color threw me off a bit.

BTW, I got a bit irritated (even though I probably won't come back again) when I found out that they do not stamp the frequent buyer's card if your item is under $2.50.  It's understandable, but irritating at the same time.

The only reason why this place gets one star is because I can't give it zero.

They didn't have the passion fruit so I ordered the lychee. It seemed like the flavor was thrown is an afterthought. And their boba is weirdly soft, I didn't like it. I like a little chew to my bubbles.

it's not the best milk tea or boba i've had, but this is in comparison to Taiwan and how it should be done. nothing too exciting about the drink or the boba, but I do think it's the best around, especially for the price. personal favorites if I'm feeling cheap is to just get a bubble milk tea or the special of the day (changes once a month or something) or if I'm willing to spend a little more, the green tea smoothie hits it home  for me.

During my CalSol (student orientation), I tried my first Berkeley boba here. I got a regular milk tea, and I couldn't even finish it because it tasted so gross. It was too watered down, and the pearls were hard so they were only good for shooting out the straw.
 If you have no other place to go, I guess you can come here for one of the fruit drinks...

I come here for the taro with coconut milk and sago!! 
I'm a bit bored with pearl milk tea because 1. it's everywhere, 2. it's overdone, 3. I am an elitist. Snob effect!

That being said, if I'm going to fill up on a 500 calorie drink, I would much rather go with something a little more fresh, like the taro with coconut milk and sago.

Their other stuff is okay, I guess. Their pepper chicken/calamari can be good, but can be overly breaded. Their oreo smoothie is like drinking sand though.

You can't really go wrong with bubble milk tea, but like I've said, you should all be more adventurous than that!
*********************************************
edited 5/13

I'm taking off a star because some new, overweight girl who works there messed up my order and refused to give me a small straw. I practically had to crawl over the counter and get it myself. Geez.

Boba is one of my loves. I can't stay away. I'm Taiwanese and I've been addicted from a young age.

Sweethearts is my favorite place in the East Bay to get boba. They have the most consistently QQ boba of any other place that I've been to. Not saying it's always perfectly QQ, but generally more often than not, it's pretty good. 

Typical orders:
- Bubble Milk Tea with Boba ($1.55)
- Jasmine Green Milk Tea with Boba ($1.55)
- Crispy Popcorn Chicken ($3.95)

If you want the they have a few drinks on the $0.99 list. If you add boba they come out to $1.55. Be warned though, if you order Boba Milk Tea it's kind of like Thai Iced Tea. If you want Black Milk Tea, get the Boba Milk Tea. The popcorn chicken here is always good. The chicken is pretty much always juicy and tender.

Sweethearts has the best boba for the best price. That's all.

I love a good boba joint, and have been on a hunt to find a place I can come to regularly and Sweetheart Cafe is not it, unfortunately. 

My friend told me that it is a fairly inexpensive boba place a lot of college kids come to, so I decided to try it out. The first thing I noticed was that there was a special: Bubble Milk Tea, Green Milk Tea, and Jasmine Green Milk Tea for $1.29 each. It was a deal I could not pass so I decided to try the Jasmine Green MIlk Tea. It seriously came out in 1 minute, which made me a little suspicious, but it's all good. (The place itself feels a bit grimy, but its in the Asian Ghetto.. it figures!) It looked unusually artificial, but it tasted pretty decent, nothing spectacular. The one thing that stood out was the boba, which was surprisingly sweet. Usually boba is bland and chewy, but these were sweet and chewy! 

I left not blown away, but not disappointed either. Try it out if you are desperate for some boba!

One word: Cheap Boba!

Ok fine that was two words. But you get the point! You can come in here and get a milk tea for the price of $1.25 + $1.75. That my friends is cheap boba, and you'd be hard  pressed to find cheaper.  

Of course the milk tea here isn't of the highest quality but that's expected of the price. You can pay $3+ for higher end milk tea, but that's getting up there in the price range. 

In my years at Cal, I've made many a late night trip here to grab a snack/drink and hang out with friends.  Perfect late night stop for the poor students we all are and were.

Their boba balls sometimes stick together and come out in clumps, had it happen to me a few times. The price is also higher than that of Cafe Moccacino on Bancroft. Service is.. a bit aloof and cold. 

One time late at night I went to get some boba with my friends cause we were craving boba. Unfortunately, I dropped my boba drink outside on the cement ground, and the drink ended up cracking in 2 with the boba balls going everywhere. 

I was pretty sad because I was looking forward to drinking the boba, so I went back in the store to ask them if they could give me another drink (no charge). The girl at the front stared at me emotionless (as I've mentioned before.. she's a bit cold) as I explained to her that I dropped the drink. She went to ask the guy in the back if they could give me another drink. Girl comes back and tells me, "We can only give you another drink if you dropped the drink IN THE STORE." So, I informed her that I dropped the drink right outside the store, but she was firm with her statement. I stood there thinking about if I should just buy another drink when another lady appears from the back (owner?), and she asks me what happened, I tell her and what do you know -- She gives me the boba drink no charge. Thank you!!! Would've given the place 2 stars without the nice owner :)

not as good as their milpitas counterpart!  

tiny cafe which consists of maybe 2 tables and a huge counter taking up most of the cafe. they sell ice cream, make smoothies, and have a small variety of snacks.
chinese college students work here... they're okay....

they have cheap drinks like $1.50 for jasmine milk tea, etc
my drink tasted fine

i've had better--- bottomline : for the real Sweetheart Cafe experience, Go To Milpitas Sweetheart Cafe !! located in chinese side McCarthy Ranch

hands down best boba balls in the bay area! very QQ. my girlfriends and i love this place. we make up excuses just to detour by this place. 

i esp love their fruit milk series. they use REAL fruit, no fake flavor stuff. best is hot taro milk. mmmm...

don't forget to get stamps for your stamp card!

Their roasted milk tea is a godsend! Finally, a milk tea I can actually enjoy without having to drive over to Oakland or Richmond. Nothing else I've had here has been good enough to bring me back--until one day, desperate for boba, I dropped in and tried their new special. Seriously, get the roasted milk tea. It's the only thing that's good.

Excellent popcorn chicken. It might be a little on the saltier side for some people but as a person who loves all things sodium, it was just right for me. Fresh, piping hot, and not too covered with batter like some other tapioca places, the popcorn chicken here in Sweetheart Cafe has effortlessly won first place in my heart. They also have a $5 combo that includes popcorn chicken with the boba drink (a good deal, considering the chicken is normally $3.99 by itself), and the bag is big enough to share with a friend. Beware - they only accept cash!

I get the mango slush with tapioca balls.
Solid bubble tea for $4. 

Warning: Make sure you ask for ONLY tapioca because otherwise they add these weird colorful gummy squares that are not very tasty.

I go here all the time. It has quick service and is fairly cheap. Cash only. The boba and drinks I would give maybe three stars at most for, since sometimes they can be pretty watery or have strange texture. The location and times, however, are great, and they have a huge menu, so you'll usually be able to find what you're looking for.

Seriously, the service here has gone down by A LOT since the last time I've been here. RUDE staff who just grabs your money from out of your hands. Doesn't even bother to greet you, or say "your welcome" when they're being thanked. Charges me for boba when I said NO BOBA and then when the drink comes out, it has NO BOBA. Wooow.

I've always came here because I honestly like the taste of their taro milk tea better than Quickly's, but with such rude service, I can take my business elsewhere. $2 gone won't matter much to them anyways!
I definitely like the milk tea here. It's sweeter and flavorful. It's way cheaper than most places too. Though the Taiwanese milk tea doesn't taste special.

After being warned numerous times by my friends about the poor quality, I decided to give Sweetheart a try and I was pleasantly surprised to find that the boba here is actually soft and chewy! The tea itself wasn't exceptional, but it had definitely exceeded my expectations. The price is also very good for the college student :)

First place I had boba in the US, and a fine measuring stick for average boba in that it's a good balance between price, size, choices, and taste.  There's better, and there's worse around (and in Berkeley, there's a lot of other choices)

UGH.  I'm sorry, but I HATE the boba from this place.  Born and raised in SF so I'm pampered by GOOD boba and this place does not cut it.  I'd rather go to Quickly's around the corner.  Even my boyfriend who is from SF, but goes to Berkeley and frequents this place admits that when he comes home he wants "real boba."

Usually my reviews are much longer, but all I can say is.  The boba is undercooked -- TOO chewy.  TOO much ice!  Milk tea is mehhh below average for sure -- tastes watered down or maybe thats the excessive ice melting?  Service is slow.

Really, if you want REAL boba, BART over to SF and make a trip to Irving.

Well, well, well... Sweetheart has impressed me on the second try. First time I was here, I tried the hot taro milk tea with boba, and it didn't taste like anything too spectacular. However, I don't like hot boba anyways. The second time around, I saw the cheap price of a bubble milk tea w/peals for $1.79 and went in. Took a long trek uphill in the heat to get home, and by the time I arrived in my apartment, I was sweating and looking oh so forward to that bubble milk tea. One sip and I was smitten. Cold, refreshing, not disgustingly over-sweetened, and pearls just the way I like them: chewy and not too mushy. 

Mind you, this is coming from someone who swore that out of the close Boba Trio - Moccacino Cafe, Quickly's, and Sweetheart Cafe - Quickly's was her go-to place for boba. However, now I'm not quite so sure... Uh oh, Quickly's, you have competition in my book. I'm going to keep switching back and forth between the two to decide what's really my favorite place. I'll still say Quickly's for now out of loyalty, but Sweetheart just might be able to nab my heart. 

Wow, I'm almost done with this drink and I started writing this review about 3-5 minutes go. Either Sweetheart is good, or the heat is making cold things taste better. Or both!

So, here is my two bit.

I used to adore this place because milk tea + boba = 1.09. Then it went up to 1.19. All the sudden, it went up to .99 for tea and .50 for boba. WHAT THE HELL!

With this price, I am definitely going to Lotus House for their much better tasting tea and much better boba. Honestly, this place was only bearable when the price was low. I used to make Sweetheart my default and Lotus House as my secondary luxury boba. But now, with the price hike, I suggest everyone migrate to Lotus House. Lotus House actually mixes the tea in front of you and it's not as sweet.

Overall, I really hate the Cantonese speaking douchebag who keeps on yelling at his workers. This is another tragedy of understanding Cantonese. I hate it when I go to a restaurant and the workers think that you don't understand what they are saying, therefore, giving them the right to say whatever they want. Douche!

I was considering a one star, but their salty chicken is actually pretty good and they have spices by the exit that allows you to control the spice level of your chicken. That's the only other redeeming quality.

Thanks for making my Mocha Snow Bubble with extra tap, just right, every time I come here!  

I love that this place is right next door to Steve's Korean BBQ.  Come for some Korean BBQ and pick up a Mocha snow bubble before or after dinner, love it!  It gets packed sometimes with all the college students waiting in line, but to me, it's worth it.

My default choice: strawberry milk tea with pearl. I used to love how before, whenever I would order any milk tea with pearl it would only cost $1.50 exactly. Now that they've upped the price, I'm not frequenting here as much, thus the 3 stars. 

I hear they make a mean delicious burger (but I have yet to try). I love their fried squid and chicken poppers, especially after a drunken escapade.

3 Words: REALLY GOOD BOBA. yeah i said, BOBA and not TAPIOCA...

Their POPCORN CHICKEN & FRIED SQUID IS ALSO GOOD.

They're opened late which is a bonus: 1 am on Thurs and 2 am on Fri - Sat =)

Personal favorite is the Jasmine Green Milk Tea with Boba no or little ice :)

I don't really get the asian snacks/junk food there cuz it seems like it just sits on the shelf haha

Can't lie that I've been here many a late night....

Even with the price hike a couple cents, I still manage to come back here from time to time for my fix of random flavor tea (no boba plz).

I make an effort to experiment their special flavor blends, but the most recent one "Pomegranate Green Tea" is just syrup + green tea = Jolly Rancher Tea. BLARGH.

More interesting ones have been Avocado Lychee (intriguing flavor even if it did look like grass + dirt) and Papaya Mango Milk.

My friends and I have a running joke about the burger meals and picture they have there. We're still wondering if the burger actually would be as tasty as the picture looks, or if they have someone go out the back-door and drive somewhere to get it from Carls Jr. (it looks like a six dollar burger stock photo) and come back really quick....

It's hard to say how I feel exactly about Sweetheart Cafe. My female friends are craving this every time someone mentions boba, milk tea, asian ghetto, kevin durant, or bob. But I can't say I have those same girl sweets cravings.

My girlfriend is obsessed with their Milk Tea Boba and I definitely love getting a little sip from her drink. But I'm not sure I would purchase my own. Maybe its because I prefer a coffee or a yogurt as my snack, but in comparison to other Boba places I have tried in southern california I would say it's a little above par. Within Berkeley I would definitely have to say its the best boba place, which is why it is always pretty popping. 

Swing by and definitely try it for yourself. It's also open late and has random munchies. A pretty wide selection for you. Overall, sweetheart cafe is pretty not bad.

the Great,
GumZ
i crave popcorn chicken every weekend

I love this place!  My taste buds still have yet to come across any taste short of delicious at this spot.  Sweetheart Cafe offers a wide variety of tapioca drinks.  Pretty much whatever flavor you crave, they offer.  The food they serve here is also very good.  Their popcorn chicken comes second to none, and their burgers are also surprisingly tasty.  I have never had problems with the service here, so that is definitely a big plus.  This really has no relevance, but there is also some eyecandy to look at sometimes...if you come while school is in session.  Anyway...whenever you are in Berkeley and have a craving for boba, I suggest you pass by this spot.

Meh. 

Let me let you in on a secret, I UNDERSTAND CANTONESE. So, don't try to pull a fast one on me. Service is pretty bad. I swear they just slam your charge onto the counter and walk away. Not even a 'what can i get you' but a 'NEXT!' 

Their milk tea is watered down. Also, they skimp on the boba. 

Pro: Their tapioca is good in comparison to other places, they open late, its spacious inside, reminds me of Asia.

Re-visited Berkeley to grab some milk tea,
Kathleen wanted Sun Hong Kong, but Sweethearts for me!
Ordered the usual, Taro Milk Tea to go,
Grabbed the purple straw - matching, I know.
Took a sip, knowing Sweethearts couldn't be beat,
Looked up at my friends and exclaimed, "This is too sweet!"
Kathleen gave me a face and said, "Told you so,"
Then reached for my milk tea to give it a go
We agreed that the boba, though, was just right
So it wasn't a total milk tea fail that night
Sweethearts, I ask, please lower the azucar
Cuz right now in my book, you are only 2 star   : /

Statistics show that the Earth's surface is approximately 71% covered by water, with only 3% of it being freshwater; the human body is composed of up to 60% water, with the brain being 70% water; and a watermelon is astoundingly made up of 92% water.  Olympic swimming events draw audiences with an irresistible magnetism; amusement park water rides are often the most satisfying on scorching summer days; and a skillfully-aimed water balloon produces indescribable elation.  Despite the prevalence of water across the world and the numerous joys it produces, its overwhelming concentration in a milk tea drink is undesirable.

Sweetheart Cafe's original milk tea with tapioca is so watered down and flavorfully weak that a 90 year old man can convincingly beat it in an arm-wrestling contest.  The initial sips produce nostalgic memories of tasting muddied water after being tackled during a rainy day football game.  Subsequent attempts at downing the drink invoke heart-wrenching feelings of betrayal in being cheated of $2.75, and prompt a litany of better uses of the money to race through the mind.  

I had never thrown away such a high percentage of unfinished milk tea, but a higher percentage of water had never invaded my milk tea.

No, no, no, no, no, no, no, NOOOOO.

I do NOT want that plastic wrap over my #72 Cookies & Cream w/ Boba! I want the DOME-SHAPED lid plus WHIPPED CREAM that you used to give me before!

We had such a good 3 year old relationship, what happened to ya? After all the tender loving care I gave, all the money I spent on you, all the time and trouble I went through to visit you - after all of that, you're going cheap on me and skimping out on the whipped cream now?

Sweetheart, I know the economy is harsh, but love should surpass the boundaries of money. I'm sorry, it's over. I'm moving on to your brother in Chinatown - he can give me what I need, even during bad times.

The first boba place I ever visited.  For six boba-only months of my college life, things would never be the same.

I'm all boba-d out, and it's Sweetheart Cafe's fault.

My boyfriend says balls don't belong in a drink.  He might be right.
Hands down best boba in Berkeley. The tapioca balls have the perfect amount of give and the correct sugar content. Also try their pepper crispy squids! Delish!

Was wandering around Berkeley and found this place for a bubble tea and chicken nugget fix. Had a black milk tea and the nuggets were fine, but over-seasoned. The wait was a long time (I know, they have to fry up the nuggets), but I wasn't too impressed with the quality. It's average.

I would've originally given Sweetheart Cafe 3.5 stars because they're a pretty standard boba place, order your drink, pay and get a yummy treat after. Minus a star for cash only and minus another half star for the wait.. but I give Sweetheart two stars today because after they got my order wrong, a cold almond milk tea instead of a hot one, they proceeded to fix the problem by pouring the cold drink into a hot drink cup, scooping the ice out and then heating it up. I ended up with a hot almond flavored water drink. 

I'd come back if it was one of my last resorts to fix a hot milk tea craving. I need to find myself another cafe/tea house with hot milk tea as good as sweethearts, minus the horrible service.

Sweetheart CAFE is my college sweet heart crush! 

If you're in the area and looking for a quick, tasty and cheap snack, I totally suggest this place! If you've never tried 'Bubble tea' type drinks, this is a great place to try one.

Check out this wikipedia link:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubble_tea


The real reason why i go here is not just for the Bubble Tea, but for the   
late night SNACKS!!!

If your have a flexible and open palette, you have to try the SALT & PEPPER SQUID!!! extremely tasty and crispy! They fry it for you on the spot and serve it in a brown paper bag with only a stick to poke it out. 

Street Cart style experience in Berkeley without the cart. LOL

Another snack sensation you have to try is the 'Fried POPCORN Chicken' 

If you're not sure what kinda of Bubble Tea to get when you're here, you can try my default: "Milk Tea with Pearl"

Ok, this is getting me hungry! I think I'll go there TONIGHT! lol

Can't beat the price. 
Thai tea all the way.
Stay away from taro.

This boba cafe never disappoints. I've gone here numerous times and their boba drinks are always really tasty. See, the trick is making the consistency and texture of the tapioca (boba) balls good. You don't want it to be too chewy/hard and you don't want it to be too soft. And trust me, I've had it both ways and it really ruins the drink. But this place nails it, every time! 

Even something that sounds really gross (i.e. cookies and cream boba) is surprisingly good. My fave is the regular milk tea boba. Yummy! The passionfruit smoothie boba is also a must-try.

The drinks are good, but not rich enough. The food is not bad. They serve burgers and fries. They sell Asian snacks at the counter, but at expensive prices. If I'm having a good day, I like to celebrate with a scoop of green tea ice cream.

Service is fast. They have weekly specials on drinks. The cheapest drinks here are cheaper than the cheapest drinks at Quickly's, but Quickly's taste better. This store isn't as good as the one in San Francisco. The facility is a little dirty from all the foot traffic. There are a few small tables and 3 window seats.

sweethearts is always packed with students getting a quick refreshment/meal.  Service is normally rude, but understandable for the low prices and efficient delivery.  You order your drink, and it takes less than 2 minutes between the time you pay and the time you receive your drink to pop the fatty straw into the boba lid.  PERFECT.

I always forget about this location, but something about Top Dog and boba gets me drooling.

I love how this place is open until midnight to cater to the college crowd, and regardless of their location, their recipe stays exactly the same and always tastes good!  Their mango milk is the perfect consistency for me, not too sweet and always icy cold.

One of my favorite boba shops in the whole Bay... Sweetheart Cafe is a must stop whenever I'm in Berkeley.  I usually park right by this place, so it's usually one of the first stops I visit.  They have tons of flavors to choose from, and they even sell burgers and ice cream.  I get the same drink every time:  Passion fruit slushie with boba.  I don't remember the last time I ordered another flavor.

The popcorn chicken is damn good, too.  I love this place!

Great Pearl Milk Tea here that has a unique flavor setting it apart from most other places I've tried.  Doesn't quite match up to that of Ten Ren in Richmond, but the tea and boba are very consistently good.
I love coming to this place. Whenever I'm in Berkeley in the telegraph region, I come here for $2.28 large bubble teas. Best deal I've ever seen in the States! They're fast too.

My favorite place of all times in Berkeley. Located in the "Asian ghetto" and open late!

Service: 
This is were the minus star comes in. Their service is decent, but would it kill you to put a smile on your face once in a while?

Drinks:
I love all their milk teas with tapioca. I like the way they make their tapioca as well. It's soft and chewy, but not too chewy. (that's the key to good boba!) And they are relatively cheap. 

Overall:
I would definitely recommend this place!
99 cent milk tea! you can't beat that! boba bumps it up to a buck 55. This is the best place to get your milk tea fix in asian ghetto.

milk tea had a weird aftertaste and they couldnt get my order right the first few times. it's just.. iced milk tea??

i direct you to mochaccino just on the other side of the street down Bancroft....

If you like tapioca drinks, I highly recommend the Sweetheart Cafe.  On top of their being a wide variety of drinks to choose from, they are all very tasty.  They also have quite a few locations (Berkeley, Oakland, Milpitas and there are more).  My favorite is the White Chocolate Mocha.

This place is great! I used to come here all the time after a long lecture and order a plain milk tea w/ tapioca. I'm giving this place 5 stars b/c it's full of great memories and makes my drinks way faster than Tapioca express ever had.

SO..I wsa there with my brother while my parents and sister have their dramatic fight. I was looking at the menu and wondered WHY some of the drinks were 99cents 85 cents and $2..I bought my brother the strawberry milk tea. It tasted more like milk than strawberries which was a disappointment to me -_-;; but oh well...still drank it XD they sold Japanese snacks, american soda, water and that mushi cheesecake. If you want to try that mushi cake, I very highly recommed you not to eat it cause it reeks :[ very tiny store too and I like it..

I consider myself a chicken strip Connoisseur  of sorts.

I was told Sweethearts had the best around.

LIES.

so gross. 

Maybe their pearl tea is good. Avoid the chicken if you can glean any respect for yourself. Asian ghetto, you usually delight. Not this time. Just ghetto.

mushy balls anyone? hahaha

besides the mushy bobas this place has, it was ... just alright. It wasn't that crowded so they were able to pump out drinks pretty fast.  I ordered the cappuccino freeze w/ pearl and it tasted a bit watered down... perhaps more ice than it should have had? They do offer quite a selection though.  They have lots of little Asian goodies, ice cream, burgers, popcorn chicken, and misc other tidbits.  It is also open till about 1-2ish in the morning so that's a plus for all the late night prowlers. They had some mini food posters on the wall which were not really appealing. I think based on the posters I would not order the food that was portrayed in them haha.

Maybe I'm just picky, but I'm not a big fan of their milk tea because you can tell it's made from powder. I have to give them some points because I do like their snacks. If you're looking for a quick drink that's cheap ($1.29 for a regular milk tea), Sweetheart's will definitely satisfy that craving.

BUT...I'm willing to put in another dollar or so for a drink that's not made with powder. I was quite disappointed with their strawberry milk tea...I could taste the graininess from the powder. 

However, they have really friendly service and they are very quick to deliver food and drinks in a timely manner. I like how they're open late at night too!

If a boba shop's drinks are cheaper, does that mean you should be more foregiving if it's not as good as the more expensive places?  I don't think so.  I've been here about 5 times and IMO, the tea is average, the milk is average, and they use too much granulated sugar or something like that.  With the amount of ice they put in, on a hot summer day, your drink will become even more watery.  

Now, I want to let you know that my standards for milk tea tapioca are quite high.  This place just doesn't compare to, let's say Wonderful Foods in SF.  Oh and it would be nice if the people who work there could smile once in a while.

i've given chances to all the other boba places on durant, and sweetheart's still wins after 3 years of trial. the boba at old teahouse is consistently bad. the boba at quickly is only good if it's small (harder to tell how bad it is). the boba at mandarin house is hit-or-miss. boba at sweetheart's is almost always appropriately chewy, sweet, and plentiful. you can ask for less boba, and sometimes they replace the loss with jelly. the fruit drinks are also made with fresh fruit. anyway, this is the best my socal taste buds have tasted in norcal.

Sweethearts is one of the worst boba places I've ever been to and  I will never get boba from here ever again. The milk tea they serve is watered down and diluted. The actual tapioca were ok, they weren't the best tapioca I ate, but they were decent. Go to moccacino cafe on bancroft instead. They have 2 for $3 for not only milk tea with tapioca, but also thai milk tea with boba! Also The milk tea doesn't taste watered down like the ones sweetheart serves.

Not one of my favorite places to go for tapioca drinks, but it will have to do while I'm at school. 

I always get the Jasmine Green Tea here, but only because it is slightly less watered down than Quickly's just a few feet away. Downside is that they don't have small pearls, and I believe that their green tea is a few cents more expensive than Quickly's. Popcorn chicken is good, but sometimes it will be extremely greasy to the point of absolute disgust. Not much seating here, sometimes people don't know how to get out of the way, but eh. Whatever.

The tea used to be more like sugar water than tea and now I hear it's too watery, but Sweetheart consistently makes the best pearls.  They're soft, which makes them easy to chew and swallow, and I swear, they're infused with sugar or magic or something.  At other tea places chewing pearls can be a chore, but at Sweetheart, each pearl is a perfectly cooked snack.  I always swing by for a pearl milk tea whenever I'm in Berkeley just to taste those pearls again.

There's not much else to like here.  The burgers and desserts are pretty bad.  The ice cream and shakes aren't that good a deal.  There's hardly any inside seating.

The pearls keep me coming back though.

Go here for the drinks, not the service. I usually like this place because it's super fobby, you're guaranteed a boba drink reminiscent of Taiwan and it's close to Steve's Korean BBQ which I like. In the years I've been going there, a guy named Raymond but whom I call "Eva" because that was the name on the receipts he'd hand me, always helped me. Nice guy and fast, too. Anyway, I go there yesterday after having place an order at Steve's and order what I always order - a jasmine green ice tea, but this time I got it with sago. So she's like, "You don't want milk?" and I said no milk. And she says, "Who orders it without milk?" And I think, wtf is your problem, I can order it however I want. So my friend is sitting there and sees them whip up a slushy green drink. You know, those kinds that are like moss green and look super gross and are made from powder. So I look on my receipt and lo and behold, it says I ordered a slushy. 

I go up to the counter and tell the older, manager-looking man at the counter now and I ask him nicely that I just wanted to make sure that I wasn't getting a slushy, I just wanted a green tea cold. He was like, oh okay, and said that if you order ice, it means slushy. I was like, okay, whatever. So I bust out the Chinese and say I didn't want a bing sah, just bing kwai. So he was fine and he actually gave me money back. So they make my drink, while the biatch in the back is muttering about how I didn't order it right, and I'm thinking that she probably should've been listening to my order instead of criticizing it. 

So 2-stars since I don't feel I need a cashier at a boba shop judging my orders, but I've had great experiences there before and they addressed my concern. That biatch needs to leave. I didn't get her name, but she has long, straight hair and talks on her cell phone instead of taking your order. And her cell phone has like a million charms hanging off of it. I'm not against fobs as I feel I'm one myself, being MIT, but I'm just against rude cashiers.

I am a HUGE fan of Sweetheart Cafe!  This place is awesome!  Where else can you get a boba for less than two bucks?!  I usually get the green tea or the green milk tea with boba.  The drink is refreshing and the boba is the perfect texture and tastes like it's been soaked in honey.  I always find myself at Sweetheart when I am up on Telegraph avenue.

WOW SO CHEAP!!!

Not my fav milk tea but it will do. Sadly situated in the Asian Ghetto, this place is quite far from my sister's place in Downtown Berkley. But possibly if I follow her to class next time I visit, I can detour here. 

I would love to try like 5 different drinks next time since it's so cheap. 

Hole in the wall, super asian tea place with cheap prices. I'm sold. Bubble tea is wayyy to expensive nowadays.

My favorite boba place in Berkeley! Really cheap and really good! Some people say their milk tea is water downed and really sweet...but I guess that's the way I like it. I don't know why but I really like the taste of their bubble milk tea and it's only $1.79!

Very cheap and fast service, but the quality of the milk tea and pearls is pretty bad. You get what you pay for. Bubble milk tea and jasmine green milk tea are $1.29 with no tapioca, and $1.79 with tapioca (for the small size). 

Beware: Sweetheart uses powder for these two drinks, not real milk tea, resulting in a powdery flavor. Service, while fast, is generally pretty unfriendly.

Tip: If you want regular bubble milk tea, you have to ask for BUBBLE milk tea. If you ask for PEARL milk tea, they WILL give you a more expensive Thai milk tea. And it's not good at all. I made this mistake a few times when I first came here, and left very confused.

I direct you to Quickly's (inside the same square) or Moccaccino Cafe (on Bancroft).
The original boba hot spot of the UC Berkeley campus.  Quickly's and Old Tea House aren't even comparable.  The snacks are yummy too- curly fries and popcorn chicken are my picks.

All I've had here is the bubble milk tea because everything else is like 3 times more expensive and honestly, at 1.79 a pop, why would i get anything else?  Anyways my rating is solely based on their cheap bubble teas, which, if you're an avid boba fanatic like myself, won't wow you.  However, you won't be disappointed either.  Quick service and the boba itself has this peculiar, candy-like taste to it which I enjoy but could very easily ruin the beverage for others.  

Cash only. :(

Originally, I gave them 5 stars for having Taro milk tea for under a dollar...BUT i walked in there today and they increased it to a wallet devouring $1.45. 

Not only is $1.45 more expensive, but it's also a very inconvenient amount to pay for a drink.  Paying 2 dollars will result in you getting at best 3 (2 quarters and a nickel for you philosophy majors) coins back...how inconvenient =( . 

I've recently seen a lot more people walking around with Quickly drinks and now I know why.

I came back here for their milk coffee boba, which I absolutely enjoyed.

They had different workers compared to my previous visits. They were nice and efficient.

Boba was perfect. Not too soft and not too chewy.

Pooh says "I'm so rumbly in my tumbly, time for something sweet"
This happens to me too, but it is always in the middle of the night and I want something crazy like an strawberry Julius or a unsweetened lemon tea or some type of crazy jelly. Sweetheart takes the cake because they have more options than Quickly and they are open late unlike Moccacino. 

I must tell you that I always try something different and sit there while they make it thinking "that was so stupid, i know i won't like this" and they always prove me wrong. whether I want a major sweet fix or "less sugar" as they have taught me to order, I am always delighted. now i will admit the boba itself stinks but everything else makes it worth it.

I got a strawberry milk tea boba here. It was a little too sweet for my taste, but really fresh boba. I didn't taste the tea in the milk tea. It just tasted like strawberry milk to me. Fast and nice service though. Just not a big fan of the "weak" drinks here.

Oh my gah... how does this place have this many stars. My friend and I walked down here at the beginning of the semester on a Sunday afternoon. What a mistake that was. We both ordered the same thing.. a regular pearl milk tea.. but hers was $1.20 more expensive than mine...?? 

We obligatorily finished, and 2 hours later we both had agonizing stomach aches. Worst food -er- boba poisoning of my life.... lucky for her, she felt better the next day. But me? I wish. Spent more time in the bathroom than in my actual room that night, and I had to skip class for 4 days.

This place completely ruined pearl tea for me, and I'm still scared to drink it even at the places back home in Cupertino where it's actually clean.

boba is pretty not bad... i mean, it's cheap and fast... and it is located in Berkeley... what more can I expect?

on the other hand, the delicious popcorn chicken + deep fried octopus takes way too long to cook. I once waited 30 minutes for it. sorry, i can deep fry a whole farm of chickens by the time you finish making some simple popcorn chicken.

Boba: prices went up! decreasing supply, increased demand :(?
Popcorn chicken: CANCER IN A BAG.

Every piece I popped into my mouth was another offense committed against my body.

Afterwards, I went to Peet's to buy a box of green tea to detoxify.

(but I still come here anyway to get my boba fix before every all-nighter.)

Delicious!  I came here for a boba fix after ramen house and was surprised that they lowered the prices.  Back in the day, boba was expensive here and I would get my 99cent boba at Quickley's.  When I came back here, I got a green tea w/boba + milk tea w/boba for $3.  Dude, most places ONE boba is $3 and I swear that Sweetheart (all of them: Berkeley, Milpitas, San Francisco) are all of higher quality and better tasting boba than anywhere else.

Their balls taste really sweet - in fact, this is the only tapioca place I know that has balls THIS sweet. Some of you may like that...but I prefer my balls to have only a slight hint of sweetness. 

In terms of the actual drink itself, their pearl milk tea can sometimes taste really sweet as well, or watered down as hell - it's a hit or miss. If you want authentic black milk tea, I think they charge you $1-1.50 extra.

After you order, you normally get your drinks super quickly.

As an Arizonan that likes to claim "I'm a Boba Freak" Id like to introduce you to the MOST AMAZING & Flavorful Boba I've EVER had! On a recent trip to California I had the chance to try a few places from San Diego up to San Fran. #1 is Sweetheart Cafe, EASILY! 
I only got the Raspberry Smoothie with Boba but the Boba itself had... depth, a flavor profile like no other boba I've ever had, perfectly made, perfect in EVERY WAY! See I told you I was a Boba Freak! LOL 
Go here... Get the Boba... You won't be disappointed.... Trust me, "The Boba Freak" from Arizona! 
Damn it... Now I want one!

If this was a battle between Quickly and Sweetheart for the title of better boba shop in the Durant Food Court, then Sweetheart would win--but only by a margin. 

Price: Sweetheart was always my default place to go because their prices on a regular bubble milk tea (no pearl) was only $0.99 before they raised the price to match Quickly. So now I have to dig for extra spare change to go along with my dollar. 

Jasmine Green Milk Tea: I usually get this one. I wish their green tea to milk ratio was larger, because I can barely taste the tea sometimes. Ask for little or no ice if you do not want your drink to be watered down in the next twenty minutes (unless you're a fast drinker). 

Tapioca: small, chewy, sweet. More pleasant to chew on compared to Quickly.

Popcorn chicken: My favorite late-night snack! Tossed in salt, pepper, and maybe MSG (haha), it is always freshly made and hot. I try to share with a friend because eating one bag would be too heavy on my stomach. I don't get it too often because it is slightly pricey for me as a snack (I think it's like $4?).

Service: I believe this shop is run by a Cantonese male. The entire staff is Chinese (probably most are Cantonese). They are quick and to the point about your order, so there is usually no "Hello, how are you today" and small chit-chat....which sometimes makes the people seem cold. They tend to warm up to people more if you speak Canto to them. 

Wait Time: Milk teas usually come out pretty quickly. But I have had more than a couple instances where I felt like I was waiting close to 10 minutes for a simple drink. Place tends to get crowded in the evening during peak dinner time.

I'll agree with some of my fellow Yelpers here and vouch for the superiority of Sweetheart over the nearby Quickly. The tapioca here is just about the perfect consistency. 

The milk teas are nothing special, but good for a cheap tapioca fix. I'm a huge fan of the coconut milk ice with tapioca. I don't know much about the food. I'm a tapioca-tea-only kind of guy here.

The service is as fast as it can be with 9-10 UC undergrads crowding the counter almost consistently. Could be made faster if this cash-only establishment made their prices more change-friendly and predictable (including tax in the price list might help). The cumulative slow-down stemming from the cashier counting out the change from the commonly proffered $5 or $20 for a $1.62 boba (listed as $1.50 or whatever) might be ok in a place that doesn't see as much business, but it's less than inefficient when it has to take place nonstop....and it's a pain for us customers who have to shovel a bunch of useless change into our already burdened pockets. I just want a boba, not a quarter pound of coins.

I used to get a bubble milk tea with pearls from here after every time I played tennis at Channing. It was practically every 3 days or so. It used to be really appealing. The specials outside advertised the bubble milk tea for 99 cents without pearls. If you wanted to add pearls (who doesn't?) it comes out to $1.55. I guess coming from SoCal where boba is 4 dollars, it seemed like a steal. Plus tennis was tiring so anything tasted good.

However, just had one today and the pearls seemed to spit out this chalky flavor once you bite into it. The milk tea was just okay. They also raised the price. So now it's a random $1.79 for a regular bubble milk tea with pearls. Definitely not coming back unless I'm desperate.

While hanging out in Berkeley one fine Sunday afternoon i had a sudden craving for a Jasmine Milk Tea boba. As sweet as he is, the bf looked up boba places in the area. The first one we went to was closed early (what the heck, this is Berkeley everything should stay open late on a Sunday). So he went back to looking up another boba place in the general area, which lead us to coming to this small cafe about a block and a half away.

Walking into the cafe you realize wow, this is small. Only a couple of stools facing Durant Ave, which made it for some interesting people watching (the bum and his "lady friends" were the most interesting to watch by far). 

The menu is pretty large for a boba cafe, they served teas,smoothies,coffee,fresh fruit,sago,slushy and dessert drinks and taiwan style shaved ice. Their food menu was much more then just popcorn chicken and egg rolls. They also served onion rings,chicken wings,curry fish and squid balls, curley and french fries, and cheeseburgers.

Everything on the menu is pretty cheap at this place. My milk tea was $1.29 and there was no tax (awesome).  The drink was a prefect size, and wasnt heavy tasting. The boba had a sweet taste, normally im use to the bland tasting boba.  

Service was fast, keep in mind that its cash only!!

Oh my goodness. Why did I come back? Why?!!

Oh yeah...maybe because Sweetheart is the only tapioca place open late in Berkeley. Sucks for me.

So I thought I was smart this time. I ordered a drink WITHOUT tapioca. I ordered a FRESH FRUIT drink--Strawberry Milk. To make absolute damn sure it was fresh, I asked the girl at the register. "Is it made with real strawberries?"

"Yes," she replied sullenly.

So I got my fresh fruit strawberry milk drink for $2.75. Then I stood around and waited in the little shop full of my fellow Asian Americans. I stared at the menu and noticed something suspicious. Under the Fresh Fruit Drinks category, they had longan juice, guava juice, sesame milk, almond milk, carrot juice...okay, let's point out the obvious. Sesame seeds are not fruit. Neither are almonds and carrots. And where would they get fresh longan or guava? This is not Taiwan!

Sure enough, my suspicions were confirmed. I received a slushy which was quite obviously artificial strawberry milk (nesquik perhaps?) blended with ice. I am 99% sure there was not a single strawberry in there. I mean, strawberries have seeds...and they taste like strawberries...

Damn them. I was too tired to complain and decided just to take out my steam by writing this review. Justice is served.

Honestly the best Boba I have had. And I live in San Francisco. Whenever I frequent Berkeley, I make sure to pass by this place! I have a frequent buyer card and I have filled it up. Again, and I don't even live here!

Only downfall? I have noticed the cafe to be closed at random times even when it was supposed to be open without notice!! And I came all that way!

i first had boba circa 1990 or so when sweetheart cafe opened up their first location in oakland's chinatown neighborhood.  it was a typical thing to do pre-chinese school (yes, i endured 8 hours of school from 8-3 and then another 4-5 hours of chinese school) or post-chinese school.  i have always appreciated their iced milk tea and popcorn chicken.  as more of these "tapioca/boba" type establishments started to pop up and become trendy in the late 90's and early 2000's, and i've tried most of them, i still feel like sweetheart cafe has remained one of the best.  they use real ingredients to make their milk tea (and that makes a huge difference as opposed to the powdered junk).  if i'm not in the city getting my fix for milk tea at WONDERFUL FOODS, SWEETHEART CAFE is where i'll go for boba in the east bay.  it's somewhere around $1.50 for some iced milk tea which definitely isn't bad.  they're popcorn chicken and strawberry banana smoothies are also very very good.  the three of these combined come out to about $11 total.  not bad for a small snack and some drinks for 2.  i really like the older gentleman that works here.  he's always so happy and smiling when and if he's taking our order.  the other people are usually relatively polite too.

i'm glad you're still around sweetheart cafe.  you bring shame to those wannabe boba places (even with their trendy decor and fancy big screens).

Scouring Shattuck, one weeknight, 
It seemed as there were none in sight.
Though it was shit, and now I'm far,
Sometimes I think of UCR.
Where bubble tea, I oft enjoyed,
'Cause I was rich, and unemployed.
Bubble tea across from bubble tea,
All open late, just right for me.
Now Berkeley, though I love you so,
There's no late night place I can go,
To satisfy this need? I can't!
Until I wandered up Durant.
There surely was a magic town,
For there, my boba, I had found. 
Small shopping alley, tucked away,
I came upon this sweetheart cafe.
Inside was simple, small, and cheery,
Although the staff seemed kind of weary.
I understand, 'cause it was late, 
With tea in hand, I could not hate.
The price? Not bad, the tea, real good,
I made it last, long as I could. 
As each pearl burst, inside my mouth,
I thought about my days down south.
I thought, "Why do I miss them so?"
But this shit's better, so let's go.
popcorn chicken -- then go around the corner to get your fresh kingpin donut -- ah the life of late night college eating.  at least i get it a little late in life now.

WTF??   I want a boba, but you can hold the atitude' FOB boy.
Got me P.O.'ed when you LOL and talked shit in Cantonese.
No worries though, you got F'd up teeth and bad skin you A-HOLE
My other Asian A.B.C's ain't so rude, so eat my A.S.S and get my order beotch.

Seriously, the staff here makes mainland Chinese seem like pleasant well adjusted people.....quite a feat considering. I don't get angry easily but I was ready to punch some bad-breath MO-FOS out. 

They still have the best boba around. so I added a star. Try going to the other one in Oakland Chinatown, the lady there is sightly nicer.

Sweetheart Cafe has the usual boba drinks and they serve hamburgers, etc. store is really small. 1/2 the front is used for storage....so not much room to sit down at if at all.

sampling: jasmine tea, (1.29) no tax
-has some jasmine tea flavoring and a  tenny bit sweeter than quickly's..


tea drips:
-service courteous and fast

I love that this place is open so late (except now during winter break). Their drinks are consistently good, and their actual tapioca is my favorite in all of Berkeley (though I have a sweet tooth so this means their drinks and tapioca are on the sweeter side). 

They have quick service for drinks but expect to wait if you order food.

Wasn't really the best boba I've ever had, but for it's price it's definitely not bad at all! There was a sign that advertised pearl milk tea for $1.59?!!! WHAT IN THE WORLD?!?! That's like Asia-cheap status. I got the lychee smoothie with pearl for about 3 bucks and it came with lychee jelly as a bonus and it tasted just fine. It was nice that Sweetheart Cafe was open pretty late when I came (around 10pm) because  tons of Berkeley students crave late night snacks. The only downsides I'd give would be that the place is a little dark and cramped and especially in the hobo-filled area, I'd recommend quickly buying your drink and going somewhere more well-litted (or your dorm) to enjoy your drink.

Great Boba!

Order the Durian Pearl Smoothie!
i used to go here ALL the time late night with one of my best friends.. we always get the same thing.. their popcorn chicken is the best thing there.

RUDE OWNERS!

So I was in Berkely, so I had to stop by and grab a tapioca drink. It was around 11:30 in the morning, and The Sweetheart Cafe had their sign on the window, saying it opened at 11:00 a.m. Ok. . . . It was 11:30 so I tried opening the door. . . . It was locked. They have a little window right next to the door, and it was wide opened, so I peeped my head in and looked if anyone was inside. There were no customers, just a man doing something with his back turned to me. "Hi! Are you open?" I asked. I got the RUDEST RESPONSE. "NOOO NOOOO!" screamed the owner. He didn't even turn around to look at me. He waved his hand like he wanted me to go away! I left. That owner is not a "SWEETHEART".  Instead of saying, "Sorry, not open yet", he yelled at me: "NO!"  I will not be going there anymore, since It seems that they don't like their customers. They should change their name to "SOURHEART CAFE" instead.

I've found myself here many a time now ever since Quickly decided to raise their prices. And they do have better popcorn chicken! 

Full menus, great meal combos, and good priced syrupy drinks!

they use dryers ice cream for the milkshakes, and they are very well made. good fries as well.
I don't get anything else there, but my friends like the burgers.
its open late, but I always go for lunch.
I would say its the best place to get a high quality milkshake in the east bay, and it is quick.
I have been going there for years, and it is always good.

I went here way too many times. Yes, I'm guilty of being in the "Boba rocks!" crowd while everyone else wonders what's so good about it. And Sweetheart Café makes their boba drinks well.

It has the cheapest price for certain boba drinks. While Moccacino comes close in price, it's a buy-one-get-one-free offer, so I would have to grab a friend along. The regular and jasmine milk teas are made just right: not too sweet, and they actually taste like tea (unlike Quickly which tastes like coffee :/). The boba is chewy, not slimy, and is just sweet enough. I once had the lychee drink, and while that took a while to make and costs more ($2.50 if I remember correctly), the fact that it contained real lychees made up for the wait.

I never had any of the food entreés, except the fried squid, and that was a mistake. The squids weren't cooked all the way, so they filled my mouth with slimy, soggy grossness. Only Tapioca Express' version trumped in being undercooked.

The café itself is a bit dark inside. It's like they're trying to conserve energy and use natural sunlight instead. Not a big issue if you're in and out fast, and the service is pretty quick.

I highly recommend this place over Tapioca Express and Quickly. And don't forget to try the lychee boba - no tea, just lychee fruit and juice.

After having Top Dog, I make sure to order calamari and and milk tea!  Yessss--I am a fatty and I try to spoil myself while I'm in town because I love the fried squid at this place and you can't complain about the price!  It gets very crowded here but the service is fast.

It's been a few years since I've been back at Berkeley, but I whenever I get around to it, I always make sure to stop by this place. I absolutely love their mocha freeze with pearl. Their tapioca has the best consistency--just the right blend of soft and chewy. Both the drink and food menus have grown considerably, which goes to show how long it's been since my last visit. They even have drinks with sago in them now. That's a first! Next time I shall see how their chicken compares to TapEx.

They sell a bunch of different drinks, but I usually get their bubble milk tea or jasmine milk tea. They have a deal where you can get generic milk teas for only $1.29! (Plus 50 cents for boba) I also like their green apple slushy, and it comes with lychee jelly! 
Their boba is pretty consistent, and slightly sweet, which my sweet tooth is definitely a fan of. And they make your orders really quick!
Just order the pineapple royal slush or the 99 cents milk tea.  Otherwise eat a double cheeseburger.

Their roasted milk tea with tapioca is pretty good!

They have deals on their basic tea flavor drinks, such as black, jasmine, taro milk tea and etc.

I like how they are open till late.  They probably know college kids want to grab some tapioca drinks during the late night hours!

Sweetheart has such an extensive menu that I'm not sure I would ever get through it all. I usually get either the regular milk tea or roasted milk tea with boba (~$2) since they're cheaper, but sometimes when I feel like splurging, I choose a slushy or frozen drink since they can get to be ~$4. I like that the roasted milk tea isn't as sweet and it tastes especially yummy served hot when the weather is cold. There can sometimes be a line late at night, but it moves decently fast since they're pretty efficient at making drinks. 

Some of my favorites:
- Roasted milk tea
- Green tea slushy
- Passion fruit green tea

They also sell candy which seems a bit overpriced to me and food, but I've never tried any of the burgers and other regular food items they serve. The popcorn chicken is supposed to be good though!

Ahhh, Sweetheart... Also located in Asian Ghetto, Sweetheart's is about the same as Quickly, except that their boba's sweeter! I would totally encourage you to check out some of the yummy snacks they have their- I just tried the fish balls today and oh my goodness, they are DELICIOUS!

Open late, yeah!

Sweetheart is pretty much my go-to boba spot, even though I live closer to Tapioca Express. Major pro: if your friends don't like boba, there is /everything else/ to choose from. They can get frozen yogurt, donuts, or a full dinner!

I've really only tried Sweetheart's slushies and milk teas, so I can't speak on their ice cream, but I'd like to try it, too. They also have a nice little assortment of Asian snacks and candies, and those can be hard to find in this area. They're a little expensive, though, so be careful!

The drinks are reasonably priced and pretty tasty. It's fun to head over to Durant late at night and fill up on random desserts and boba! (God, I can't wait for the semester to be over so I can do just that, guilt-free.)

I've already graduated from Berkeley for a few years now but whenever I go back I always try to visit Sweetheart's. Can't say anything about their milk tea since I usually resort to my default....

Papaya milk shake with extra boba. OMFG SOOO GOOD!!!!! 

They use real papaya since sometimes I'm thrown into a state of depression when they say "sorry, no more papaya today..." O_o The boba balls are also the perfect amount of chewiness and sweetness. AND they don't charge extra if you ask for more boba (unlike other places) =) 

They also have a HUGE list of types of drinks they make. I've only tried a few, but really...I'm only reviewing their papaya milk.
best balls ever -- cooked and sweetened to perfection. they have a nice variety of flavors, all made with the fresh stuff (none of the powdered crap). and the popcorn chicken... mmm.

I forgot what time it was, but I came here after the freshman homecoming dance at the beginning of the year and it was about to close..but the nice man still let us buy drinks because we were very thirsty :) I ordered a pina colada snowbubble that just tasted like sugar water, but I was thirsty at the time so I was satisifed.

the sweetheart will have a special place in my heart.  they took my pearl tea virginity from me!  my gay boyfriend took me here one day, and i've been going here now for about six years.  really fuity, really refreshing, and alot of flavor.  extra pearls makes it even more yummy!
I like this place more than the quickly's around the corner. I order the popcorn chicken once and it was extremely greasy and nasty although my gf says all the other times she ordered it was perfect.

Typical cheap, fast, dirty campus food service. Within the set of its peers, it does alright. Make sure to come here with the right expectations.

DO get the boba here over Quickly's next door. I don't know why, but I really don't like Quickly's. Their boba tastes like they dump a buttload of sugar when mixing every drink. Sweetheart's isn't much better, but it IS better. And thats all that matters when making the decision of which bad boba place in the south-side campus area to visit.

Don't get the burgers here. They're small, expensive, and not tasty enough to warrant buying.

Also the jasmine green milk tea is probably the best thing I had here. Also, if you're having trouble ordering, just say the name of the base drink you want (example: jasmine green milk tea) and THEN add "with boba/tapioca/pearls. Avoids some confusion, as their stuff is named weirdly here.

Wait, I haven't reviewed this place yet?!?!

I think Sweetheart's has the best jasmine green tea for the price around. Beats Mocaccino's on the other side of the block. 

Never tried any of their snacks, but I find it really weird that they serve burgers....haha.

I Heart Fresh Boba

I Heart Green Tea Ice Cream Milk Shake with Boba

I Heart  Salt and Pepper Squid

I Heart  Curry Fish Balls

This place is __________  (enter any extremely positive adjective here).

I had finished my Top Dog hotlink and nfactorial was done with her Fat Pizza slice, and it was now time to move our snack train to Sweetheart Cafe! I hadn't had bubble tea in a long while, and D had given some pretty high praise to this place, so my expectations were set pretty high. I wasn't very adventuresome and only got the milk tea boba. The tapioca was good and the drink satisfying, but not memorable. I'll come here again, although I'll probably give the bubble teas from other nearby establishments a try first.

Came here with my best friend(months ago hahha), she was telling me how her and her brother came here one time and I just came and tagged along.

It was a bit hard to find parking, surprising because it was past 11pm and we had to park behind some buildings a block away from this spot. It's really cramped inside, we could barely go through all the people just standing in there. She got her drink probably 5 minutes or a little more, but it was sort of quick. We weren't paying much attention, we were looking inside the place, checking out the drawings and their menu. 

It's basically a Quickley's to me. Pretty decent looking place, I'd like to try some of their stuff next time I'm around :)

Cheap and convenient but very mediocre. Though debatable, I think the Quickly in Ghetto is much better especially if you like your tea with grass jelly.

If you want better quality frozen drinks, Moccacino on Bancroft is your best bet.

The chicken here comes out oily and in huge, awkward chunks. Oftentimes, I found pieces that were not cooked through all the way. Salmonella is dangerous, man!

What a ripoff. Drinks are now priced up to $4.30. Most of the drinks are overpriced and definitely not worth it. At least the service was somewhat decent probably because there weren't any other groups around. Save your money and go get some Jamba Juice where you actually get some fruit and nutrition in your drink for about the same price instead of just sugar and starch.

Wednesday, 12:30AM. 
Cash only. 

Lots has changed since visiting during college:
- Poor customer service
- Can't combine stamps on cards

And then...?
Based on an employee's description, we ordered one of their drinks. It was an incorrect description - which is normally fine, but he failed to inform us prior to making it. Continuing the bad customer service, he expected us to just take the drink without reconciling his mistakes. Bummer!

...Kind of the worst bubble milk tea ever. Yeah, it's cheap but even Quicklys can make milk tea taste like milk tea. But this place.. it just tasted like the leftover liquid from boiling boba and some milky water. No tea taste at all. I drank a few sips and tried really hard to like it but ended up throwing it away. Where they running out of milk tea since it was late night and decided to water mine down with water? If so, not cool. 

I wouldn't get boba here. I don't understand why everyone else would. If it's late night, you're probably better off grabbing donuts and coffee next door (it smelled amaaazing).

This is the routine: Top Dog and then boba. Never fails to satisfy my belly and my calorie count. 

Minus one star cause the guy got my order wrong once. When did "mango milk tea" become "coconut milk tea"?

Regardless, it was delicious. So plus 4 for the drinks and snack options.

I have a love-hate relationship with Sweetheart Cafe. I love their bubble milk tea with pearls (for only $1.55!) and their delicious popcorn chicken. But I hate the rude cashiers and the poor customer service (I'm not sure the people working there have even heard of the concept of the customer is always right). However, I keep coming back for more because in my opinion they make the best milk teas, and the quick service means I can be in and out in no time.

Being an old timer who was at Berkeley BEFORE any boba places opened (Fun Fact #1: Mandarin House was the first to have boba on Southside.), I've tried them all and watched many a boba places set up and close shop.  (Fun Fact #2: Lotus House used to be Old Tea House - same as the Davis one and a hippie coffee shop before that.)

Sweetheart's always has a certain college nostalgia.  We always get boba there whenever we're back in Berkeley.   Yes, there are better ones in S.F., but they can't replace the memories that come rushing back.  Many used frequent buyer stamp cards are a testament to that.  (Fun Fact #3:  Doing the math, one stamp card is ~$30 spent @ ~$3 per drink.  Boba will make you broke.)

Boba is sweetened - an acquired, addictive taste that makes boba from other places taste bland in comparison.  Taiwan-style milk tea is the drink for the more tea flavor, although there's a unique taste that some might not like.  The cheap drink specials are nice when on a budget, but they're pre-made and powdery.

The usual fried chicken and squid are always delicious with peppery goodness.  The packaged fobby snacks on display are overpriced, but in a bind, I've given in.  Burger and fries are also available (which my friend loves better than any others on Southside), but usually a drink and a snack is good enough, and food can be had elsewhere.  (Fun Fact #4:  Boba is good with everything except drinking.  ^_^)

Disgusting!! Bought the Red Bean Milk drink for $2.50 and all I could taste was the large amount of corn syrup that they put into the drink. The drink had the *slightest* hint of red bean flavor (clearly artificial), and was so sweet I think I now have diabetes. Would not recommend. 

Other notes: not that I would come here again, but expect long waits past 9pm when large groups of Berkeley kids like to frequent this place.

hmmmmm

the boba is still really good...

but...

the boba takes too long

there is no candy store like the one in oakland

the dude behind the counter is hard of hearing.

i'll still go here, but...

hmmmmmmm

: I

I think my obsession with boba is a little unhealthy sometimes. This place fulfills my cravings and is cheap. 

$1.79 for a bubble milk tea with tapioca. I literally come here like 4+ times a week sadly. 

I keep telling myself I will try something new but why change what I already like so much :)

Stereotypically, college students stay up late & eat at all odd hours of the day. Unfortunately, most restaurants around Berkeley that are of the yummier variety close earlier in the night.

Sweetheart's hours are great. It's location on Durant Avenue in so-called "Asian Ghetto" is pretty convenient for Berkeley's dorm residents and apartment dwellers. Even if you live farther, if you're looking for FOOD, GREASE (the good kind?), and LIFE, you can generally find it at Ghetto or across the street at Top Dog or La Burrita.

Also, it is undeniable that Sweetheart uses way more NATURAL ingredients than a place like Quickly does. It isn't worth it to skimp quality for speed. Sweetheart keeps it real.

Yes, their menu can be confusing and repetitive. Yes, they don't offer some of the things ON their menu. But it is an OBVIOUS good choice for a place to hang out with friends or on the solo whether you'd like to sit down and chat or pass on through.

[P.S. Their shaved ice isn't half bad if you're tired of boba or don't like tapioca.]

I probably am one step closer to diabetes because of this place.  It does not help that this place is conveniently located on Durant on the way home/to class.  

Love:  Fast, cheap, reliably good.  I always either get the Bubble Milk tea or the Jasmine Green Milk tea which last I checked, were the cheapest items.

Complaints:  The ever increasing price.  Since I've been in college, the price keeps going up every year.  Yeah, the economy is terrible, but it is so disheartening to roll up on a hot August day for back to school and not have enough change to buy my Boba  (I carry cash...never.)
Boba is the bomb at this spot. It's in the mecca of berkeley's international food court. It's cheap and the service is fast. Raspberry Smoothie is one of the best.

Sweetheart is my favorite boba place ever. You get the best bubble milk tea for the price, $1.79

Whenever I go back home for socal I try a lot different places for boba, and nothing compares to the quality and affordability of sweetheart's. For example, Koreatown boba just tastes like trash compared to anywhere in Berkeley. The menu is pretty basic (or rather, i don't order anything else except bubble milk tea or green tea with lychee), but the tapioca balls are perfectly done!

I always seem to crave this place...I love their long hours too :)

It's really cheap and it tastes like it too.

One of my favorite boba flavors for a long time used to be taro and at sweethearts it always tastes really watery than flavorful.  Even their other flavors like regular milk tea and strawberry milk tea was not great at all. I suggest going to Mocaccino or Quickly's instead if you want better tasting boba.

Had the special under a buck, Strawberry milk tea with no pearl balls. Afterwards, I found out why it was under a buck, not much flavor to it. Pretty water down. Maybe the other stuff is good, but my drink suxed. Might come back and try something else and give it another review.

This use to be one of my favorite places to get boba because they were cheap, but over the last 2 years, they've gone up in prices and its pretty much the same as everywhere else now. Their milk tea is ok but the pearls have too much of a pasty taste in it. Quite disgusting actually. In my opinion the quality and service of sweetheart has gone down since 2008 when I first tried it..I use to get boba from here 2-3 and maybe 4 times a day..but not anymore. 

Haven't been here in a while and probably won't go back. I rather drive 30 minutes to get some decent boba than save $0.30 and get disappointed.

I stepped up to the cash register and ordered the jasmine milk tea.
The girl at the register asked, "The cheaper one, or the more expensive one?"
I was confused, "Um, what's the difference?"
To which she replied, "The cheaper one is more watered down."
Ohhh. Seeing that I was running low on cash, I ordered the cheaper one. Yes, very watered down. I guess that's the catch with the cheaper drink specials.

I used to come here all the time with my UC Berkeley buddies. I came back a few days ago for the first time in two years and was glad to see that nothing has changed. Well, thats not entirely true; the prices have gone up but you could say that about almost any bar/restaurant/cafe these days.
Rude servers who will argue with you about what you ordered.  They do not understand English, messed up my order, and would not redo it.  Horrible customer service.

I don't know why people complain about the boba or the freshness of their drinks for Sweetheart Cafe. You get what you expect - I order the bubble milk tea for less than $2. It comes out super quick and it tastes great. Their boba is pretty fresh in comparison to other places. I am a San Leandro/Hayward gal (originally) and have been to all the famous Tapioca Express locations in the tri-city and would say that I actually find Sweetheart Cafe better, only because their Bubble Milk tea tastes unique to all other milk teas I have tried. 

The reason why this joint wins my heart is because of their extremely late business hours. It is totally worth employing people past midnight when I see hella college kids grabbing their drinks here around 1AM. 

Thanks for being open late, Sweetheart Cafe! I'm glad you're nearby, but still a nice five minute jog... makes me feel less guilty when consuming you on a once-a-week-basis.

Good selection of boba + slushies + food +etc, but the milk tea just isn't as good as Mochaccino Cafe on Bancroft... the milk tea is too diluted here and tastes extremely watery, especially when the ice melts.  Maybe the slushy drinks are better, but I've tried the honeydew one and I'd just put it at mediocre.

They have fried snacks, candies, ice cream, and of course, milk tea.  Sweetheart Cafe doesn't have the best milk tea I've ever had- but what they have going for them is that it is cheap, very quick, and tastes pretty decent.  

My boyfriend and I got a large milk tea with boba added for $2.29 (to share).  Literally 15 seconds after paying for our milk tea, it was ready- sitting right in front of us.  I can't really complain about that.  The flavor is pretty subtle, not overly sweet.  The boba was chewy and there was a decent amount (but not an overwhelming amount either).

I can't really say much about any of the other drinks or food, because I've only ordered milk tea here.  But it's pretty good to me.  

Notes:
-The place is pretty small; but they do have a couple of small tables inside.  Most people just grab food/drink to-go.

Sweetheart's is a quaint little shop that serves some wonderful boba. It's by far my favorite boba shop in Berkeley and very reasonably priced. Whenever I need a little pick-me-up after a failed exam or a long day, I make a pit stop at Sweetheart's on the trip home. I always order the bubble milk tea (I'm so boring, aren't I?), which cheers me up a bit. The mango slushy with rainbow jelly is also quite delicious on a hot summer day, which is the ultimate drink to cool me down. I've gone here so much during my four years at Cal that I probably drank 300 drinks easily. Now that I just graduated, this will definitely be a place I will miss. 

PS: My girlfriend forced me to write this review.

I believe I had my first boba drink at this Sweetheart Cafe. I was one angsty  teen at the time and was visiting my sister who was attending CAL. When she introduced me to boba, my mind was blown. What was this drink that had weird little balls in it!? We can drink AND eat!? MAGIC! This was light years ahead of anything that existed in my hometown in Oregon. 

I continued to go here often over the years when I visited her and then eventually when I lived in Berkeley myself. I've tinkered around with their menu, from their slushies to their sago, and eventually expanding over to their food menu (famous popcorn chicken!).

After returning this weekend, I couldn't help but notice the decline in quality. The man behind the counter was as friendly and the lack of decor remained the same. I ordered my standard Bubble Mlik Tea with Lychee Jelly and got my sister a Taiwanese Style Milk Tea. 

Once we popped our straws it, we noted that it tasted really watered down. To make things worse, once the ice started to melt, the drink was barely tolerable. 

C'mon, don't hurt me like that, Sweetheart! Don't make me go to Quickly's!

I loved Sweetheart Cafe even before attending Cal and it's no different now that I have graduated. I was in the area and went back last Saturday with a friend to grab a quick bubble milk tea. Yes, the prices have gone up by like 50 cents but I don't care because the tapioca balls here are sweet! So many places serve boba with regular, flavorless tapioca and I get sick of just chewing on what tastes like nothing. Here, I always finish every single tapioca ball (up to 15 calorie for each one). Yea..I looked it up and I still think it's worth it! 

The regular milk teas are comparable to the mega franchise Quickly's located just a few steps away but the fruit smoothies and drinks are WAY better (not to mention also that Quickly's service can be sketchy). Their fruit drinks CLEARLY taste like it's been made with plain sugary syrup but Sweetheart Cafe's is always made with the real thing. I love their avocado w/boba drink and got it like everyday when it was their monthly special. It sounds weird but you have to try it! 

The food is also done very well, from the fried squid to their popcorn chicken, which is my favorite out of all boba places. It always comes to you fresh, PIPING HOT, crispy and with lots of basil for added flavor. They serve several hamburger meals that come with fries for those not looking for something too exotic to snack on. They're surprisingly delicious coming from a little boba cafe.
