I've gone to a lot of boba places in the US and Asia but I always go back to my sweetheart. :) Corny but true!

It was a sunny day and we were in the neighborhood so and I had a boba craving. It was unusally empty for being so close to the campus. But then again, it was a sunday afternoon....so maybe people aren't out? Anyways, I got a coconut milk tea - can't really go wrong with getting something staple. It was delicious. We also got a green tea smoothie - which wasn't so good at all. It tasted really powdery and it was usually really green. Just because it is green tea, dosn't mean that its GREEN. Aren't smoothies supposed to made out of ice cream or yogurt and not powder and ice??

What weirds me out is that this location like their other locations is small. But at least when I go to the SF location (or actually any boba location), I can actually see them making it. But after I ordered my drinks, two people disappear into the back room and a few mins later, the drinks come out. So no, I don't actually know what was in the green tea smoothie - it could have been green food coloring and tea flavoring mixed with ice for all I know. It didn't taste very good. At least the coconut milk tea was decent  and the boba balls were chewy so that made up for it.

This place used to be 4 stars in my mind due to their prices. 99 cents for a taro milk tea and 59 cents for regular milk tea or green tea. Yes, these were worthwhile prices for the well cooked tapioca pearls, quick service and decent tea.

But then they raised their prices. I think it's 99 cents for a regular milk tea (50 cents extra for pearls) and 1.49 for taro or green tea. That meant it was now $2 for sub-par tea (taro tea is WAY too sweet). I liked Sweetheart when the prices were still cheap. They're still some of the cheapest teas around and they totally kick Quickly to the curb, but they're not nearly as great as before when they once had reasonable prices.

Their curly fries fill my drunk grease cravings though, which is great. Can't say anything about the chicken strips. I do not like that they try to sell you overpriced candy when you just want to go in for a drink.

They're still three stars due to the fact that they're cheaper than most places though.

I've been here twice and both times the people behind the counter were EXTREMELY rude to me. Someone should teach these workers some customer service skills. ): rude

The milk tea here was decent, but does not compare to other milk tea that I have had in the past. The Jasmine Green Milk Tea was good, and not very sweet if that's the type of milk tea you're going for. The bubble milk tea was pretty good too, and a little sweeter than the jasmine green milk tea.

I was confused though, because the first time I went the bf and I ordered pearl milk tea and jasmine green milk tea, and the pmt was 1.29.. and when the guy handed it to us he called it bubble milk tea. The second time i ordered two pearl milk teas and the total came out to $5.30, and the pearl milk tea was different from the bubble tea that we got before. (The pearl milk tea from the second day was much too sweet)

So my question is: what's the difference between pearl milk tea and bubble milk tea, because I had always thought that they were the same thing.

Sweet!
What a treat!
Even better than Moccacino Cafe
Expect a line of Cal students here
The Jasmine Green Tea is only $.99!!

They have really sweet balls. I think they soak it in sugar or something. The iced boba is really good, not like other places that don't mix the powder in very well so that you're choking on it. 

But if you still hadn't had enough with their boba, you can order their popcorn chicken, too. 

For full out food coma - I'd do this - order a boba and the popcorn chicken, get a hot dog from Top Dog (across the street), and then have a doughnut from King Pin (next door to Sweetheart's). Omg, I used to drive up to campus just for this late at night with my friends.

Oh no!!! You jacked up my $0.99 bubble milk tea special that I adored so much over the years!!!  Ladies and gentlemen, it is now for $1.29 .

It's ok. I still give you 4 stars since I am still a fan of your absolutely light and refreshing milk tea!

*ring* *ring* *ring*
Me:  Hello?
Leetle Cousin:  Hey Eddo, it's me!
Me:  Oh hey!  How are you?  How are you enjoying Berkeley?
Leetle Cousin:  It's good!  I got homesick my first week though.
Me:  Really?  Why?
LC:  I just kind of missed San Diego.
Me:  Did you miss your parents?
LC:  No, it's just that none of my friends who are going to UCLA or UCI have started school yet.
Me:  Ah, but you like Berkeley now?
LC:  Yeah, I like how it's kind of weird.  And really different from San Diego.  And how everyone here is smart.
Me:  Yeah, that's pretty much why everyone likes it.
LC:  Yeah, so.....
Me:  ???
LC:  Um.....
Me:  ???
LC:  Can you buy me alcohol?
Me:  [Sigh]..... sure.
LC:  Oh my god!  Thank you so much!
Me:  You have to buy me boba though.
LC:  Okay!  From where?
Me:  Sweetheart Cafe.  It's the most consistent and the best boba place in Berkeley.  And none of that pre-made crap that Quickly sells.
LC:  Is that the one next to the Asian Ghetto?
Me:  Yeah.  Get me popcorn chicken too.  They make it really good,  with the fried basil and the spices.  And they use dark meat too.
LC:  Okay!
Me:  You're WELCOME.
LC:  Thank you, Eddo!

I tried to buy her the shit I drank in college - Winner's Cup (sweet as mother's milk) or Pavlova.  But at the end of the day, I couldn't bring myself to actually purchase a plastic jug of vodka.  That bitch got Hangar One.  I am the best older cousin ever.  And she *better* be the most popular girl in her dorm.

Wanted to order milk tea for a wedding
Guy heard the order and seemed to be dreading
Wasn't that nice
But gave us a price
And off to buy containers at Target we were heading!

No large containers to hold the tea
And soon we thought, how can this be?
Called them and said
Maybe cups instead?
He said they could and with boba separately!

Two days later, came back for pickup
No drinks ready, what's the mixup?
Talked it out
Ended the drought
And walked out with boxes and no further hiccup!

Driving and parking are truly horrendous
The crowds of Cal Bears so very tremendous
But I was blessed
'Cause I'm the best
So carrying the tea was easy -- stupendous!

It was my first time in Berkeley and I wanted Boba, bad! So my friend took me to this place. $1.99 for a Taro Milk Tea WITH Boba?! WHAT?! Where has this been all my life?! That is SUCH a steal! Their roasted milk tea with boba is delish!

Cash only doe.

Either this place has lost some grounds or my palate has gotten more sophisticated since it first opened. My fresh taro boba ($3.95) still has the same thick smoothie consistency but it was a downer to experience a fainted taro taste and a set of boba that no longer has its magic touch. Maybe it is time to try their other flavors but it's hard to get excited when their menu hasn't grown from its inception. Quickly losing its go-to status, 3 stars for the underwhelming experience.

[Fighting off tears] I want my old Sweetheart back!

Update:  A return visit for a dinner buffet requires an update and severe downgrading of my rating.  The place was BAD, and not just bad in the sense of "oh, that wasn't very tasty" but horrific in the sense of "shouldn't the health department shut them down".  One dish was so burned that it literally looked like black char in the bottom of the pan.  I sampled nearly everything else in a futile attempt to find something good.  Most dishes were watery, bland, and/or had food that was the wrong texture (dry meat, too-crunchy garbanzo beans).  Even the naan was bad.  Perhaps they cook once per day and if you go at lunchtime the food is still reasonably fresh but by dinner time it is disgusting.  I would have fared much better picking up a frozen Indian entree and pre-made naan at Trader Joe's.    

Original review:
Went to the lunch buffet a bit late in the afternoon so I was hesitant what the quality and selection would be but pleasantly surprised to see that all the items seemed well-stocked and reasonably fresh.  The taste of the food varied from OK to good, so it didn't amaze me but it's definitely a place I'd visit again.
This place blew me away by how great the food is for a buffet, and also the atmosphere was great. Chicken masala, naan, salad, and veggies were awesome!!!

There are so many Indian restaurants here in Berkeley and I must say it is best in all. The food is very well cooked, fresh and price is damn cheap. I do not know how they make money.

Their service is excellent. There is this girl who entertains all the people and never fail short in anyone's expectations. I have been this place 4-5 times so far and never been disappointed. I do not like too much spicy food and they have everything very well cooked and less spicy.  Over all 5 star and must place to eat if you like Indian food.

Don't go to this place. This place is only second in terms of bad food and service to a Chinese place I went when I was in London.
Water down food, not fresh, salad is old...bread was old...service ..bleah...she doesn't care about you. She either reads or is on cellular phone. 
One star because of decor with the big elephant on the wall...

I thought this place was really good.We went before a Cal Basketball game around 6pm.Everything was delicious. The Tandoori Chicken was not dry. they even had a great beer on tap for not too much. White table clothes make it a nice experience. I think this used to be a place that served great Duck Tacos.
It's always nice, friendly service. The naan is soo fresh. This place is amazing.

I came here for lunch on a rainy day with a friend today, hoping to get some great indian food and buffet. For $8 a person, I definitely don't think it ended up being worth it. The only reason I did not give this place less than 2 stars is because our server was very kind and attentive.

Although it looks great from outside the window - clean setting, a wide variety of things to choose from - the food was really not great at all, especially compared to a lunch I could get at Indian Flavors Express, which has less variety but is also equally close to campus. 

Almost all the dishes were pretty bad...it also didn't help that they were cold. I was excited at seeing rice pilaf, but it turns out that was also cold and the rice was very dry and hard, probably from being out for too long. 

I don't think I would ever come back, based on this experience.

A small, but well positioned Indian place that can't be more than a year or two old.  Love the Vegetable Korma, but they never sell it!  Every time I go, I miss it on the buffet.  Apparently, they've nixed the menu option and it's only the buffet??  I may be wrong, but that's what the ever-pleasant waitress told me.  Too bad I keep missing that Korma.  The sauce is so incredible, I'd swim in a vat of it if they'd let me.

Punjabi by Nature offers a wide range of mediocre cuisine at rather cheap prices. 
Their Chicken Vindaloo and rice pudding were outstanding, very well spiced and quite tasty. The Naan was plentiful and warm as well. However, their Chicken Tikka Masala, Tandoori Chicken and Chickpeas were definitely not warmed well enough, and lacked any distinctive flavor.

Service was pleasant, my water glass was refilled often and my plates were cleared in a timely fashion.

The definition of "Meh".

Excellent price for what you get. The place isn't that big and thus there's not that much variety, but I think what the people put out here is pretty good for the money you pay. For about $8, you get your buffet, and you also get a soft drink and naan, both with unlimited free refills. Unlike most places, the naan is fresh! Love it! Even if you get a refill of naan once, you get your money's worth from the meal.

Some of the chicken in various dishes is somewhat dry, but I can easily overlook this by grabbing any of the curries that they have in the warmer. The curries are flavorful and you can actually distinguish them from one another. Props to them~ The staff is pretty nice and the place is surprisingly empty. I'm a fan of this place, but a 5 star place in my book has to have AYCE meats besides chicken ;)

This is  a good buffet and the value is great, about 9 bucks for all you can eat lunch. This is roughly what you would pay for a so called 5 dollar lunch, once you add the tax and beverage.

The tandoori chicken is flavorful and juicy, fresh veggies and curried veggies are put out periodically. The naan is hot and fresh. The only thing that was a bit annoying is that they were slow in replenishing the tandoori chicken when it ran out.
This shouldn't happen at a lunch buffet, and the restaurant was definitely not crowded, there were only about 4 or 5 customers at the time.

Best to come at the beginning of lunch hour.


Ok- I'm revising my rating down to 3 stars because we just went there yesterday and they seem to deliberately stall on bringing the tandoori chicken when it runs out. I waited 20 minutes after the waitress said it would be out "in a minute".  
With a dozen customers in the restaurant in 25-30 minutes,  each paid at least 8 bucks, it's clear they could bring enough chicken and still make a profit!!!

Definitely  check to see if there is chicken before paying for the buffet, unless you don't  eat meat, or you have  time for a long leisurely lunch.

Perhaps other reviewers have not had decent Indian food or perhaps I caught PbN on an off day but this was some of the worst I've had. 

Not only were all of the dishes bland, most of them didn't even look appealing. The worst offender was the Chicken Curry, which only had a few pieces of chicken to start and at one point one of the cooks seemed to have come in and dumped some old pieces of Tandoori Chicken into the sauce. 

I'd much rather have 4 decent dishes to choose from than a dozen revolting ones. The best thing I had here was the naan, but that's not enough to save this place from a 1-star. I realize this is cheap, college-student priced fare, not cuisine, but we're still talking $8 for a meal that I regret.

Watery curry and restaurant smelling like clorox? Not impressed. 

My friend and I came here right when they opened for lunch and was displeased to find them still cleaning dirty tables from the night before, mopping the floor with strong smelling detergent and an empty buffet table. After waiting for them to do everything they *should have* done before their opening time, my friend and I sat down inside. 

My first plate consisted of a simple salad with the yogurt dressing, tandoori chicken and 2 types of curry. The tandoori chicken was actually pretty good until i bit further into my drumstick and found that it was still bloody inside. I also tried the eggplant curry and some vegetable curry which I found to be sour, watery and luke warm.

I decided to try some different curries in hopes that they wouldn't be disgustingly watery. Nope, the consistencies of the other curries were just the same. My friend and I flagged down the waitress and told her about the curries, she explained that the curries were just put out and needed time to heat up etc. Shouldn't the curries be warm since you just opened for lunch aka you should have just cooked the curry not too long ago? This just means that the curries were most likely leftover from the day before.

The naan brought to our table was delicious but I would never come back for another meal. There are many better Indian restaurants in the Bay Area such as Amber India in Mountain View.

The main selling point of this restaurant is their relatively cheap food/drink.  They offer an $8 all you can eat buffet (w/ naan by request) and $8 pitchers of beer.  The food is not good but, if you're thirsty, it is a good deal..

Surprisingly satisfying. At 7.99 all day it's a full dollar cheaper than Naan and Curry's buffet, but with more variety. You get freshly made Naan when you eat here too, instead of the stuff that's been sitting there a while. The meat dishes were surprisingly tender and moist, and the spice and flavor were certainly there. I was happy with this all you can eat experience.

A solid two and a half stars

Plus one star for being a cheap buffet

Minus one star for having three or so pretty-much-identical veggie options

Plus one star for fresh, hot naan

Minus one star for all of the food tasting pretty much the same

Plus one star for not-overcooked chicken tikka masala

Minus one star for overcooked chicken curry

Plus one star for having lots of pakoras

Minus one star for the pakora batter in the middle of the pakora being raw

Plus one star for an enormous ganesh on the wall

Minus one star for being the only Indian place in Berkeley that doesn't give you chai.


Would I eat here again? If I'm on the west side of campus with absolutely no time and a hankering for Indian ... maybe, but probably not.

Pretty good. I went to prospect the Graduate School of Ed at CAL and was jonesing for some good cheap indian food afterwards. I was actually surprised how little there was to offer. I saw about 3 buffets, and this was the only one not empty. And it was the cheapest so I had to give it a go. The food was pretty good...tandoori chicken had good flavor, chicken tikka masala had great sauce and the aloo -eggplant/potato thing was good too. Naan was average- I have had better for sure but it was abundant and warm and I got more without having to ask. If I was ever in Berkeley again, and wanting of some Indian food, I would come back. But buffet's are usu a waste on me, since I can't eat a whole lot. I would give 3.5 stars if I could :)
The buffet is so good! The service is exceptional! I can't wait to eat there again.
$8 all you can eat including naan & pop!! Yes, pop, I'm from the Midwest. My only complaint is that I can't eat more rice pudding in one sitting.
i heart this place! very convenient, comfortable whether you're alone or with a friend, good service. and great nan.

3 stars for the food, one star for having $2 anchor steam.  

The selection is not as good as other places such as India Palace, but the quality is decent for what you pay, and in fact they have some very good vegetarian dishes.  They had a eggplant curry and green squash curry that were quite good.  I'd say for the price it's probably the 2nd best indian buffet in town, just behind India Palace.
Its a small but has good stuff...

Some guys and I dropped by for the lunch buffet.  I don't have high standards for Indian buffets, but Punjabi by Nature came up well short.  The curry offerings are limited and the tandoori chicken was extremely bland, not to mention unusually dry.  The waitress was nice, but needed to be called upon for service.  The silver lining?  It's clean?

Still, 7 dollars isn't too bad if you're dying of hunger.

2.5 stars.

BF and I headed over here around 5:45 yesterday. We had both loved Dollar Curry House, but were intrigued by an $8 buffet. 

We actually live right smack dab in the middle of Berkeley's version of "Little India," and have many options around us in terms of Indian Food Buffets. Of them all, by far my favorite is Priya's, but it's also a couple dollars more expensive and nowhere near campus.

This buffet was OK. I definitely wasn't concerned about sanitary conditions or getting sick by eating bad food. While we were there, the cooks came out and refreshed almost everything on the buffet. The first dish of food I got was a little older. The rice was almost crunchy and the veggie fritters were kind of soggy/warm, like they'd been sitting out for an hour. The raita was totally empty.

My second plate was much better, and very fresh. The vegetarian options are decent, although on the spicier side (I'm pretty sensitive to spice). I guess my big issue was with the naan-- they gave us each one quarter piece, and didn't appear to offer more. Unlike other buffets, naan was brought to the table, rather than kept on the buffet bar. We asked for them to refill the raita and they finally changed it twenty minutes after we asked them to-- well after we needed it.

Also a bit disappointing was the lack of bussing of our old plates, which took up a substantial amount of room on our little table.

Definitely OK. I'm not sure I'll come here again. We'll see.

So I gave this place a second try and had the buffet. I honestly don't know why people eat here, my only explanation is that "average Americans" must not like flavor in their food. Seriously. It's bland, undersalted, the chicken was dry, the naan was laughable. There's a lot of other Indian in Berkeley, so I can't imagine why people would go here. It's cheap and close to campus, but that's about it.

A surprising new welcome to Oxford, mysteriously taking the place of that god-awful Dollar Curry, caught my eye as I wearily walked home from class a couple of weeks ago. The HUGE posters, as well as the poor man wearing an ad poster dancing around stupidly, advertised a buffet lunch for $7.99 + tax or buffet dinner for $10.99 + tax. "$10.99? Really? That's kinda pricey." But wait! What's this? Under the huge price number is written in slightly smaller text, "Naan bread and drink included." Holy Mary Joseph, it's on like Donkey Kong.

I ventured inside to a mostly empty restaurant (this was at like 4pm though) and the waitress immediately welcomed me with a warm smile. I sat down and indicated that I wanted the buffet dinner. I ordered my Diet Coke and got up to look at the buffet selection.

For a $10.99 buffet dinner, the selection is really quite impressive. Rice, papadum, salad, and all the usual dressings (chutney, raita, etc.) - staple fare, to be sure, although papadum was new to me. Then I looked at the dishes and immediately my eyes fell to the chicken tikka masala. I know, I know, but shut up, it's Britain's REAL national dish, okay? The dish selection was pretty good too - tandoori chicken, chicken tikka masala, daal, lamb korma, two different kinds of pakora, aloo, and a few other dishes I failed to try. Overall, all the dishes were quite tasty, at least for the price I was paying. I could certainly find better, but this was really a deal. (Plus, I was about to pass out from having not eaten all day.) Punjabi by Nature has a real a la carte menu too, but unfortunately, I don't think they're going to make much money off of that, since the buffet seems to be their major selling point.

Now, you notice that, despite all the praise I have heaped upon this place, that the Holy Grail of Yelp reviews, that ever-coveted Fifth Star, is missing. It's because of the rice - they failed to change out their rice often enough, and therefore when I went for seconds, much of the rice had become really hard kernels, making the rice inedible. If not for the fact that I had some pretty darn good naan to make up for it, I would've knocked them another star.

Also, for some really great unknown reason, the waitress gave me 1) a discounted price, only charging for lunch when it clearly should have been dinner, and 2) all the naan and soft drinks I wanted. I'm not sure what their normal policy regarding the naan and soft drinks are, but I'll be damned if you can find a better deal near campus.

I'm not into buffets; however our friend recently had the buffet and loved it. We always order off the menu. This place is our current favorite spot. The food is really done with care. The flavors are complex and balanced. When you order something "medium spicy" it is just that. Spicy enough to leave a pleasant reminder in your mouth of the delicious thing that has just been there. I also love all the little extras like grilled veggies and which ever little side dish they have. I've gotten some nice lentil curry and I've also gotten some chana masala. Plus the little dob of chutney rounds it out nicely. It's ridiculously reasonably priced and the service and atmosphere are great. We sometimes get Punjabi By Nature to go and they take the same care there.

At $8, the buffet is a real deal! Best Naan I've ever had--they bring it hot and fresh to your table. It tastes buttery and rich. I wish they would refresh it without your asking, and when you've asked, it takes a while before it's back. Otherwise, best Chicken Masala I've ever had. All the other offerings were superb as well! I really enjoyed the Matter Paneer in particular. An overall delicious experience!
Great food and an amazing value!!!  Love the lunch buffet.

This was some of the worst Indian food I have ever eaten, I ate their lunch buffet.. Gah, bland, cold, and had none of the life and flavor I associate with  indian food. All the vegetarian options tasted exactly the same, and the food felt old and sad. I would never eat here again. I had a stomach ache for about 2 hours afterwards....

I was on a quest to eat at every Indian restaurant in Berkeley and this place was definitely the bottom of the barrel. I went for the lunch buffet. I scoped it out first and thought the selection looked fine. However, the food tasted horrible. All of the vegetarian curries were bland and mostly just tasted like tomato paste and potatoes. I didn't eat the meat dishes but they looked like they might have been better. The naan and rice were fine. The rice pudding was disgusting- it was sour. Being the cheap person that I am, I usually try to go to a buffet mid afternoon and eat enough to fill me up for the rest of the day. But I could not force myself to eat a second helping of anything here. There's plenty of other Indian restaurants on University for the same price but much tastier.

There is a change in management. The chef used to cook really good Indian food. I usually come here for lunch, but ever since that new chef came, everything is bland. 
Chicken Tikka Masala was too watery and it seems that they recycled that "red"-colored chicken into Tikka Masala. There were way too many options, but low in quality. 

I would go back if they improve their food quality. Weirdly, they added asian / chinese food on the buffet tray.

you know what? this is $8 indian food including naan and drinks. you serve yourself, but a very busy waiter takes plates and keeps your glass full.

I don't think you can go to a strip mall nail salon and expect a Swedish massage next to a waterfall.  So, i'm not really sure what people expect when they see "7.99 all you can eat buffet." but here's what I expect:

1. clean place to eat
2. more food than I want to eat
3. decent quality food

This is what I get:

1.great tikka masala, and a drink and some good naan
2. super clean
3. a good variety of Indian food that is actually quite tasty

Thus, this place has met and exceeded my expectations and is deserving of 5 stars.

Uh, i had high expectation for this place especially with the positive reviews here. First all, the selection was really poor, and what they had tasted subpar at best. The tandoori chicken i had was very tough, dry, and chewy. The rice i had was wet and gloppy (i think they might have mixed coconut milk at the very end). It came to my serving dish as one big glop. The potato curry (Aloo Mater, i think) quite watery and did not have enough spices. Sure, price is cheap, but is it worth it? Me definitely think not.

1 star for being a 7.99 cheap buffet. 
1 star for being next to the famed cinnaholic. 

Rude waiter, on her personal cell while we were in there. Asked if she could get me a cup of ice and and she put up her hand to shush me and continued talked. Then came over like I had inconvenienced her. 
Rice pudding, horrible! Their sad attempt at kheer. Most dishes watered down and gross. Rice was old and crunchy from being left out. 
Only saving grace was the chicken curry today. 
Went there because we wanted something before our fantastic cinnamon rolls from cinnaholic! 
They need Indian chefs, having Mexican chefs that don't speak much English, can't make cooking Indian food too easy.

My fave place for curry! Always cheap and the Naan is always freshly hot . The waitress there (always the same girl) is super attentive and polite. The fruits were surprisingly good as well, but my fave there was Chicken TIkka! Nothing there is spicy, so I recommend this for curry newbies like me :)
On second thought, relative to many Indian restaurants I've eaten at, this not a good experience overall, at all.

Not very crowded at lunch time and I can see why. The setting is nice enough; it is obviously converted from a one-time sushi bar. The food is only OK. As mentioned in other reviews, the only meat option is chicken and many of the rather watery veggie curries were something with potatoes, not appetizing enough to even try. The Tandoori was passing good, but undercooked(!). I won't be back, given so many options in the neighborhood.

Burning food on the buffet table.  (-1 star)
Chinese/thai food on the buffet table (-1 star)
More chinese/thai food than indian (-1 star)
Barely warm naan (-1 star)

I really liked this place, but their buffet had obviously been out since the beginning of the day.  All the meat was dried out and inedible.  The usual options (chicken tikka masala) were out or missing.

A lot of the food felt like they had just put water on top of it periodically through the day to keep it from drying out...
Buffet style Indian food for $8!! Chicken Tika Masala was creamy w/ very tender pieces of chicken. Service was great. Rice pudding was too!

Wonderful lunch - calm oasis with simple decor and pleasant staff.  Yes, as reported, the naan is warm, chewy and tasty.  Love it!  Ummm...plenty of potatoes to suit my taste!  I had lentils, veggies, chicken, all very good and spiced perfectly! Friend enjoyed bbq chicken a couple times over! Meeting there at 1:10 pm allowed me to find a parking place...a block away.  Not bad.
The buffet is very average. The spinach was salty, the two meat dishes were curries that looked soaked in fat, and my salad had a piece of chicken in it! However, the naan was really fresh and soft.

this place has gone through its phases. When i first tried it first it was an awesome all you can eat place that was perfect for to go when your at work. Then it turned into a $1 menu, which was okay. Then it tried being a higher end place and failed. Now it's at this middle ground between all you can eat and menu options. The food is good and not too spicy. They have good veggie options and they're always nice. I think it's exactly what someone on a budget would want, if they like indian food.

this is by far and away the worst indian food that i've ever eaten in my entire life.  it's obvious that the spinach and vegetables on the buffet come from frozen packages since they were all extremely bland and watery.  in addition, a lot of the dishes were incorrectly labeled (for example, lobia AKA black eyed beans was labeled as rajma AKA red kidney beans).  the aaloo mattar (potatoes and peas) had no potatoes but a few other random vegetables like broccoli and carrots.  i was totally astounded since broccoli is an ingredient that is not traditionally found in indian cooking.

the only way i can imagine people liking this place is if they don't mind cheap, horrible food or have no idea what good indian food tastes like.  the 5 star ratings boggle my mind.

Nothing about the lunch buffet met my expectations.

The food and variety were disappointing. It was under spiced, overcooked (even for a buffet), and left me feeling very unfulfilled. The service was also lackluster since the waitress did not buss dirty dishes off of our table. Overall, this place was disappointing and not worth the value of what I paid. 

I will not be going back and do not recommend this place.

The price for the buffet is decent. I got to taste various Indian dishes for $8. The fresh naan is a plus. I wish that the girl gave me more naan during each trip because it is a hassle to keep asking her to bring me more. The food is hot and the quality is good. For anyone who thinks that the dishes are "watery," just stir and fish out all the ingredients.

I totally did not know about the free drinks. I wish the girl who served me told me about the drinks and the naan. In fact, I wouldn't even have known about the naan refills if I hadn't read about it on yelp in advance. The service can be improved.

Price is unbeatable but the quality of the food horrible. The tandoori chicken was ok but the chicken in the tikka masala tasted old. The saag wasn't creamy the way I like it, but my son liked it. We went at 4pm on a Saturday and they had 2 chicken dishes plus the tandoori chicken and the rest were vegetarian..not really typical ones either..they had a squash, two mixed veggies, a bell pepper and potatoes one, and a few others. I didn't really like any of the dishes. The tikka masala tasted very ketchup-y. No pakoras or appetizers. And no drinks included in the buffet like other yelpers said there was. 
I guess if I was a student at UCB that I may eat here, but otherwise , never again.

Went there on a friday night with hubby. I am not a big Indian food fan but he likes it a lot, so we agreed on a buffet, so that I could maybe discover new dishes that I'd like. Everyone seemed to say that Punjabi was the best quality/price ratio. Hubby called the restaurant to ask if they had korma (my fave) on the buffet tonight, just to make sure I'll eat at least one thing that I like, and the lady on the phone said "yes, vegetable korma, of course". So I was like LET'S GO ! 
We arrived around 7pm. No one in the restaurant. I didn't let that discourage me. The very nice and smiling hostess seats us and we say we want the buffet. And we go for our plate. Huge disappointment : no korma !!! I almost wanted to tell our only service staff member that we were told on the phone that it will be there. But really, it would not have brought it back to me so I didn't say anything. I'm thinking now that I should have, just to let them know to be more careful about what they say. Anyway ... 
the buffet selection was not grandiose, as I expected. Only 3 meat entrees : tandoori chicken, tikka masala chicken, and curry chicken. You'd better like chicken let me tell you ! The vegetarian dishes were not too appealing. And no samosas or any appetizers except for a salad of lettuce and red onions. For dessert there was cantaloupe. 
We both take the tikka masala and the curry. Both of their sauces were SO runny. And I really had to fish for tiny bits and pieces of chicken in the tikka pot. Flavorwise, I actually, to my surprise, liked both. Hubby as well. But they really need to work on making it less runny because that really takes the dish down. One of their plus point was definitely  the naan. It was piping hot, fluffy, soft, had a buttery taste... really delicious. The other plus is the hostess/waitress, being smiling and fast at bringing drinks, naan and cleaning up our table. 
$20 for both. That's fairly cheap. But because of the "korma incident", the selection and the runny sauces, I am still not sure we will come back.

I love the $7.99 buffet!  All you can eat Indian food that includes naan and soda.  Some of the vegetarian items could use a little more flavor, but the meat items are usually great.  There is even unlimited tandoori chicken.  Beer prices are great $2/$3 for good beer on tap and $6 for a pitcher.

Good value - all you can eat lunch for $7.99 with drink. Service is good. Food is just average. Several of the dishes are bland and need additional spices. Naan bread brought to the table by waiter is not hot, and tastes a bit old. Salad is OK, selection of sauces is limited, only about 3. Several vegetarian dishes, but all are just average tasting. Rice (plain white) with peas is good and served (kept) warm.

For $8.69 (including tax) you get some of the best Indian food I've had in the bay area. There were TONS of options (chicken tikka masala, chicken korma, chili chicken, chicken vindaloo, some pork dish, tons of vegetables dishes, chicken pakora, potato pakora, and even two Napalese dishes and a thai dish!). Delicious! Only wish they gave you a little more naan with your order.

this is a really good deal and really good indian food, esp the chicken masala. the buffet is $7.99 and comes with the best naan ive ever had plus fountain soda. they even have fruit (cantaloupe and watermelon). dont forget to look up or you will miss the beautiful, colorful ceiling decorations.
Very poor buffet. some of the food was downright nasty. would never go again.
Last few visits have been disappointing

All you can eat for 7.99$. You get what you paid for. Weak curry and bland tandoori chicken. The only reason I would actually go back is if I was at the starbucks next door studying all day and didn't want to lose my seat. The na'an was freshly baked and that's the only redeeming quality. One of those places where you wouldn't go unless you were sick of everything else nearby.

Cheap lunch buffet, nice enough staff.  Owned by the Khana Peena folks, who know Indian buffet.  Nice to give them some business.  Good for large groups (20 or so).  Not super crowded so room to talk.  Bring your own energy, tho (we did, it worked out great).

I didn't realize anyone could talk so loudly without being drunk, but I never saw the women near us imbibe more than ice water! Although there are several beers on tap. Still, it didn't ruin an otherwise pleasant and affordable dining experience. 

$7.99 - ALL YOU CAN EAT

Solid three stars for a pleasant lunch spot (or early dinner*), extra star for the sweet & attentive waitress who waited on us Tuesday. *Plan for the fact that items will be under hot lamps and kept warm for hours on end. Admittedly we aren't very experienced in Indian food, so the place is good for the novice eater as well. A basket of fresh, warm bread was immediately brought to our table with just the right amount of charcoal toast to it. 

Indian food can seem similar upon first glance, but the proof is in the pudding, or in this case...curry. An excellent place for vegetarians, many curries focus on one note or melody of vegetables; I realize that's economical as well as kind to animals. However, there are different qualities to the vegetable dishes upon taste: 

- Zucchini was extra spicy and had nice texture in the mouth
- Eggplant (Aloo baingan) spent time absorbing & contributing to their sauce
- Chickpeas had one of my favorite sauce tastes.
- Creamy mixed vegetables (including broccoli) were tasty in yellow curry
- Mixed veg in red curry had potatoes & carrots tasting like pot roast
- Crispy, caraway papadan (WANTED TO TAKE SOME HOME!)
- Mint, Tamarind, and Yogurt sauces
- Basmati Rice

The sauces also frequently went well together!

Punjabi by Nature only offers chicken as a meat dish, but the three varieties were tender, plentiful, and delicious (see photos). As stated in other reviews, the Masala has a savory depth amid the cream sauce and was as juicy as the Chicken Curry (my favorite). My friend thoroughly enjoyed the Tandoori and we both marveled in our first time adding tangy, tamarind sauce to the dish (so good)! 

Cons were that my orange wedges had a taste like alcohol, like they'd sat too long at the bottom of their container. However, my companions wedges were resting atop those and were fine. The salad could've been fresher, but was still edible. And there was only one dessert -- rice pudding -- but we were too full to really consume a sweet, still we managed a taste and found it good (with perhaps an under note of rose water).

I tried very hard to respect their "Don't waste food policy" and gladly would've brought home the bit that remained on my plate, but alas wasn't able to finish every last bite. We left stuffed and content to our next engagement.

There are nice, large windows and it's a pleasant spot to absorb a little sunlight, get away from some of the bustle near BART, with room to seat larger parties amid stylish indoor decorations of traditional Indian Gods.

I think it's pretty awesome to find an Indian restaurant that does a buffet for dinner.  The selection was good and food was excellent.  I also really like the decor and ambiance of the place and the service was great.

Buffet, cheap Indian food usually spells disaster, but surprisingly not for Punjabi By Nature.

First of all, for a buffet they are VERY attentive (un-necessarily so), which is great. 

The price is DIRRRTY cheap, but the food is surprisingly good. Trust me I'm Indian and am really critical of all Indian food. But how could you really complain at this price, and the food being decently authentic Punjabi food. You can complain how shitty it is, but if this place can make me think of home, then its done its job WELL!!

I went here on a cold rainy day and pigged out. It made me homey and happy. The MASSIVE overlooking Ganesh is a little creepy, plus I really don't like my gods being used in massive restaurant decoration =(

The dishes available are simply and has nothing wrong with it. Its decently flavorful and you can't complain when they give you a drink and even dessert too!

Try this place if you're lookin for cheap dirrrrty but homey-ish Indian food. Don't go expecting more, otherwise you should be asking you're Indian friend's mother to cook you food (and don't look for places like Himalayas to fill that craving)

I'm a fan, but only on occasion.  So long as you understand that there's not that much variety here, you'll be very satisfied.

So like most people have said, this is a great and inexpensive buffet.  They're offerings are really good, but they don't change them that often, so you'll want to only visit occasionally.

Other good things:
~Great decoration featuring a really big diety, nice tables/chairs, and goooood tunes.  Mostly I've heard actual classical Indian music, rather than Indian pop.  Nothing wrong with the latter, but I'm a big fan of the traditional stuff, particularly while eating
~Good happy hour deals on beers, etc., that make this great for stuffing your face after work and getting a little tipsy.

Take home message: this is slightly quantity over quality, but really nails the combo of inexpensive and plentiful while tasty.  Drinks are a good bonus.

This place loses a star in my heart because of the numerous Indian restaurants I've eaten at...and since it was buffet style for dinner...the quality of the food wasn't as good. I find that it is impossible to cook good Indian food if you are cooking large pots of it at a time, and then serving it to the masses in a buffet line.

The food itself was not too bad, although I regrettably ventured into the Chicken Tandoori, which was the driest chicken that I had ever had...Indian food or other types! Their saving grace is the price for the buffet: $7.99, and that their Chicken Tikka Masala was pretty good.

I love that they deliver and that is why I gave em a shot.
everything was pretty good.... but not the chicken Tikka masala...the only thing I could taste was the heavy cream and the Ghee. Its one of my favs but next time I eat here I will pass it by.
and the mangos in the chutney were really tough

I went back for lunch and was less impressed. There seems to be a Berkeley Indian restaurant curse that they are wonderful in the first week and then go quickly downhill - why? This time I got the lunch buffet (not offered the first time I came in), and while I love the variety, the tastiness of my first visit just wasn't there. I would still come back, and still go to town on the buffet, but it doesn't have the initial "wow" factor.

Had their buffet for the second time today, and it was just as good as the first time I had it last year.  The chicken tikka masala, which is my general favorite with Indian food, was a little runny and not as flavorful as I like it, but still enjoyable.  The chicken curry, potato & cauliflower curry (something ghobi, I forgot the name), and salad were all plenty tasty.  The naan was fresh and tasty, though a bit on the crisp and thin side for my tastes (a little bit fluffier and it would have been absolutely perfect).  Not the best Indian food I've had by any means, but good enough that I'll be back eventually, especially with that price tag.

I came to this restaurant for a quick bite after being stuck at UC Berkeley a little too late. Based on the 4-star rating, I expected the food to be better. That said, it was more than fine, the location was convenient, the staff was friendly, and if you're hungry enough to take advantage of the buffet the price of 7.99 is pretty great. And as someone who loves naan, I appreciate that they make it fresh for each guest.

Decent for an all-you-can-eat.  The price was about $8~9 dollars for one person (including tip).

[ATMOSPHERE]  Nice wooden tables with white linen covers.  The place gave a vibe of cleaniness, which is always good for a buffet.  

[DINING]  They have a large buffet cart on one side of the wall.  Basically you just get a plate and take whatever you want.  I had the chicken curry and the chicken tiki masala.  This was pretty good, basically tasted the same as in other Indian places, but all you can eat!  The fried vegetables were extremely hard and probably left out for a while.  They had long rice and it was a bit hard and tasted old.  The rice pudding tasted like they just used the same rice to make it.

[SERVICE]  The waitress was polite and quite.  She promptly gave us water and naan.  Although I wish she would have refilled our naan.

[OVERALL]  The food wasn't that great, but I guess that's what you get for going to a buffet.  Decent food for a decent price.

My girl and I went tonight before she attended a lecture at Cal.  I found out at last minute that it was buffet style as I was checking the address on here.

When we first got the buffet peninsula, we didn't see any naan.  We were slightly disappointed and filled up our plates with mango chutney, rice, spinach, etc.  We were happily surprised when we sat down to our table with two glasses of water and a basket full of steamy naan!

Overall for $7.99 pre-tax & tip is a great value for the taste, quality, and assortment of the food available and soda.  It would get five stars from me if there were more veggie items, less meat and optional add-on soda, but I understand that their market is pretty much dialed to the "starving" college student.

Downsides:
- if you aren't a soda drinker like myself, you still have to pay for the included soda.
- bike parking is lacking.  one bike loop and one sign within 3 businesses.  if you sit outside you can keep an eye on your sweet ride all kitted up with the nicest parts

Congratulations, Punjabi By Nature, you have served me the most horrible meal I have ever eaten in the Bay Area.

One star because the waitress was not rude.

I had the dinner buffet. My bf and I stopped in to take a look and for some reason, we thought it would be ok. Don't ask me why, I guess I thought the food looked passable upon first glance. The pappadum looked ok. The restaurant was crowded with people. Good sign? Or just in a location next to campus?

It started to go downhill when I started to get the food. Usually, it's pretty warm or steamy if your hand is near the entrees at the buffet.. Hrm... Not even lukewarm. That must mean this pappadum is stale. Well, it was. Moving on-- let's try some meat, some veggie dishes, and something that looked like soup with was called "eggplant curry." Hint: it's not soup. The rice was hard. Gnarly business. 

Sitting down, the waitress brought us naan-- undercooked, chewy, dry, flavorless naan. It was not translucent because of delicious butter or even grease, it was just dough that was not ready to come out of the oven. I couldn't bring myself to let her know, I didn't think there would be anything that could be done. I didn't think this would be a new complaint to anyone there anyway.

Everything was so watery, and the chicken tikka masala looked like they poured bleach in it! Why was this sauce so white? And the chicken was so tough!

 I saw other Nepalese dishes and found it seems to just be an excuse to just make something burned looking and watery. 

There was a potato dish with, again, a watery discharge, faintly flavored with tomato  It had the unexpected addition of --- pickled bamboo shoots? Whaaaaa?

I knew I was having a terrible meal but decided to revel in it! "Go for the gold," I told myself.  I decided to try the rice pudding. Wow, it was--- medicinal.

One plate was all I could stomach and I had to gtfo.

Oddly, I saw more people coming in as my bf and I were leaving, and I wanted to warn them to stay away! We should have! I feel bad for them. It was awful!

Ergh, my stomach is not thanking me... And it's already been a couple hours. With so many Indian places in Berkeley, just skip this one. You can get so, so much better for just a dollar or two more.

MOE: There are so many great Indian restaurants in Berkeley, it's such a shame we wasted our time and money on this place. 
PENNY: Agreed. The dishes were bland, semi-warm, and overly creamy. Adding fat to the dish isn't going to make it more delicious. It just made it difficult to eat, and I felt awful afterwards. 
MOE: I'd classify it as Indian food for white people. 
PENNY: That's about the worst thing you can say about an ethnic food, and I agree. 
MOE: I found bones in my chicken tikka masala, and the chicken itself tasted foul. 
PENNY: What about the atmosphere? 
MOE: I didn't like having to squeeze through the dining space. That place is tiny, and has too many tables. See, this is what Breads of India does so very right, among other things. That place is tiny, and there aren't tons of tables, but I guess if you're going to sell cheap, bland food to a bunch of undergrads who don't know better, you might as well pack them in. 
PENNY: Oh, and what was with the Thai dishes in the buffet? That's never a good sign. 
MOE: Quantity over quality, clearly. And if you can't do Indian food correctly, don't just try your hand at Thai. 
PENNY: So what's the verdict on Punjabi By Nature?
MOE: Penny, I might not be down with Other People's Punjabi.

Mehhh. I don't know about this place.  I was kind of excited to try it because of all the good reviews, one of them being my friends that I always enjoy eating with and have pretty similar tastes in.  

The only good thing about this place was that the na'an was fresh and I guess because I love watermelon and I ate a shit ton of them there.  

Every single curry that was there was wayyyyyy too watery for anyone's good.  I had to put rice under them just so it wouldn't spread and mix.  If I didn't, I'd probably have to put only one curry on one plate.  The flavors were so so as well.  The spinach one was missing something because normally it's my faveeee but I had one bite of it and just stopped.  

The chicken was pretty dry and flavorless as well.  I just took the drumsticks and dunked pieces of the chicken in curry.  

One star for the price, one star for the naan but I'll probably not go there again unless it's the only thing open. Now I'm on my way to kick my friend in the face for believing his review.

All-You-Can-Eat Indian Curry and Naan???
heeeeellllll yeeeaaahhhhh X)*********

I think "Yay! I'm a fan!" puts it perfectly. Hungry? Eat here. Short on time? Eat here. Don't feel like cooking tonight? Eat here. Feelin' cheap? Eat here. Craving good tikka masala and yummy, soft, warm, fresh naan? Eat here. (Actually, all their curries are good. Ha!) Wanna eat till your insides explode, without paying exorbitant prices for doing so? (Maybe this last one just applies to me..) Eat here. X)

mmm... yummy Indian curry buffet... this is my lazy restaurant. And I love it X)

I now see that I may be kicking a dead horse by offering another one star review. On the other hand, this place continues to be in business, so this flavorless, runny bag of meat is somehow still galloping. 

I don't understand it. Is Berkeley so unconditionally loving and supportive of a people as to overlook Tikka Masala that somehow tastes like airplane chicken alfredo, sourdough-like naan, and a variety of different-colored, equally-bland veggie swamps posing as curries?

Some have made a fair argument that $8+tax is a great value for unlimited amounts of anything edible, and once my taste buds indicated I was eating for quantity rather than quality, I switched to sport mode and attempted to take them for all they're worth. Now I'm paying the price with an upset stomach and a sad resignation that I will never, ever find good Indian in Berkeley. Since I work here and Indian cuisine is my favorite, Punjabi by Nature has brought me that much closer to suicide.

One star for clean paper tablecloths, freshly and unnecessarily torn as you dine.
FABULOUS EVERYTHING: quality, quantity, price, seating, hospitality. Two of us ate lunch for just over $20. My friend Kevin N would probably like it.

Taste: 4
Value: 4
Service: 4

Came here with a friend for dinner and got a couple different dishes. Overall, the food was pretty good, and we didn't have any big problems. Service was good as well. Definitely would drop by in the future, possibly to try out their lunch buffet since that seems to be pretty popular based on the Yelp reviews.

Ranking of Indian food in Berkeley:
1. Indian Flavors Express
2. Punjabi by Nature
3. Royal Indian Cuisine
4. Tandoor Kitchen
5. House of Curries
6. Naan N Curry

Like most of the reviewers, I think the buffet is an awesome deal. Service is good and the place is really clean. The naan and papadum are fresh.

Loved the chicken masala, especially since I was turned off by the salty curries from House of Curries the night before. The chicken was tender and the sauce was creamy. 

One of the reviewers was right: the food will put you to sleep--at least that's what it did to me.

I'm coming back!!!

I've lived near punjabi by nature for a while and I never took the time to try it out but I'm glad I finally did.

The first time I went here I figured they could justify such a cheap price for the buffet by charging for the naan. I was wrong, the naan is free unless you get the specialty naan, then it's a couple of bucks extra. 

The food here is pretty decent, not the best indian food but it's way decent for the price. I'm a huge fan of the zucchini and, of course, the tiki masala.  

The food's a little hit or miss with the rice sometimes being overcooked, but overall, it's a way decent meal for the price.

My friends and I stopped by this place yesterday while taking a break from the Olympics frenzy. At first glance, it doesn't seem like the place to go to, due to the lack of customers (at the time). The $7.99 buffet deal seemed too good to be true. But since we were all starving and didn't want to stray too far from our apartment, we gave it a shot. To make this review concise, here are some quick things to consider about this place before you decide to take that $7.99 chance.

Pros:
- Chicken tikki masala. Wow. Sweet & creamy goodness. Get it. A LOT OF IT.
- Naan is usually served hot, fresh, and as much as you want. If it's not there though, ask the waitress/waiter.
- For a buffet, much of the food was quite decent. I could actually taste some quality in a dish.

Cons:
- Not the greatest service. The waitress, after seating us, wasn't prone to helping us out unless we prodded her consistently.
- I noticed that the salad, fruit and some of the curries weren't very fresh. Somewhat old actually. We ate around 7:30ish (which is late), but still. Just a warning.
- DON'T expect a lot of variety in these dishes. There weren't a lot of choices; at most, there were 7. A few were empty throughout the night, despite the waitress saying "they were working on it."

Overall, it filled my stomach well. It isn't a bad restaurant to go to for some near-broke college students that are completely devoid of food. But, it isn't a place I would want to go to again. One-time experience is more than enough. 

Fun fact: Although they do play Punjabi music, it's funny that the workers in the back are blasting out Latin music, muffling out the Punjabi environment lol.

When I saw the signs on the street pointing to this place, I was expecting the typical joint needing lots of street signage to coerce people in the door. I was pleasantly surprised when I followed those signs in to an upscale vibe of a place that was bright and clean, as opposed to the stained carpeted barely clean, type of place that you find all over University Ave. and Sacramento St. Well, the food was the clincher for my 5 stars. I came in at 2pm and had just come from an AMAZING free lecture by the fabulous Amy Goodman at UC Berkeley, happened to be arranged by student Sarah Porter, thank you Sarah P.!. So, I just wanted a snack. Opting for a la carte instead of the tempting buffet at only $7.99, I ordered a simple samosa and chai. Both were fresh, light, crisp, and really quite good. It definitely whetted my appetite for trying more of this place when I'm in my typical craving for indian food state of mind, which hits me about once a month. Punjabi--I'll be back, with family in tow. Loved my first experience here!

This is an amazing place to go to when you are extremely hungry and just want some nice hot food. 

Not all the dishes are absolutely amazing, but the ones that are are definitely enough to fill you up. I definitely recommend the Tikka Masala as it has a much more savory (and less sweet) taste than that of other South Asian restaurants in Berkeley. They also have fresh-made naan, nice and hot, served to your table when requested. Everything else is up to your taste, so there were definitely dishes I wasn't fond of but overall the experience is great every time I go.

Though not the best Indian food I've had by any means, their offerings are still pretty solid and at $7.99 for the lunch/dinner buffet it's an awesome deal.

Chicken Tikka Masala - not bad, decent flavor.
Aloo Bhurtha - meh, overly grainy texture and a bit bland.
Vegetable Korma - very good!  easily the best of the selection of curries.
Chicken Tandoori - didn't get a chance to try it, but my friend said it was mad dry @_@
Naan - only okay, it was more on the thin and crispy side and I much prefer mine thick and fluffy.

The buffet also includes your choice of soda with free refills, not to mention a good variety of dipping sauces.

Sweet people. Good location. I wish the food was better! I think that a new cook would transform this place into a gem... like Uddipi Palace is (spelling?). 
Unfortunately I have to report sour yogurt, funky tasting saag, and bland masalas. The chicken tikka masala was the saving grace of my meal, not due to the chicken (dry) but the yummy creaminess of the sauce.
A message to the owners: work on improving flavor and quality of food and I would be a big supporter! There is nothing like good Punjabi food and it would be a joy to have you be it :)

The food here is pretty good, especially their naan.  They have expanded their food options at the buffet.  Back in the day they used to include a drink with their buffet for no extra charge, which they no longer do.  The service is mediocre.  Still a pretty good price for the dinner buffet, $7.99.

Yes, this place has a bad name. Previously heralded as "Dollar Indian Cuisine", Punjabi By Nature has, in the past 8 months, transformed twice: first they were an everything-is-a-dollar-including-the-beers wunderland, with great music and a giant Ganesh. They said they were closing due to bad business, but hell, I woulfd have given them a loan.

During their "Dark Period", they because a sit-in indian food place with an attitude and an expensive menu. Neither did this business model work for them.

Now, they seem to have settled on the happy medium of a well-priced all-u-can-eat buffet. 

Get whatever you want as long as it is this:
2x pieces veggie pakora
3x pieces succulent Tandoori chicken drumstick
1.5x mini-bowl chicken tikka masala sauce (no chicken cubes)
1x free naan (ask)
Dunk all of the above in the tikka masala sauce

Also I suggest you call ahead as they sometimes have weird hours.

My first Indian restaurant that I've eaten in and Punjabi did not disappoint me! 

The restaurant itself is super small, and their buffet cart is kinda dinky but their curry is so yum, especially their Chicken Tikka Masala. Their other curries are really good, too. Some have stronger spices than others so it depends on your sense of taste, but I don't mind spices so they all tasted really good to me (especially chicken tikka masala!) 

Their naan differs. Sometimes the back will be burnt. Other times, it's perfectly made to a soft, buttery bite. It's good dipped in chicken tikka masala! 

Nice interior, average waitress, and great curry.

This is by far the worst Indian buffet I've ever eaten - every dish in the buffet tasted off. The chicken tikka masala was bland and oh yah: why do they have random Chinese and Thai dishes at an Indian restaurant?? All of their curries had way too much butter/cream and not enough spices and had the same clumpy coagulated texture to it. The palak paneer  was mysteriously sour which made me feel like it went bad. All the Chinese dishes all had this blackish color to it so I didn't try them but I know they're not supposed to look like that. You can tell all the food had been out for a while because of the thin layer of film on the top.  I left very unsatisfied. 

I give it 1 star because the nan was good.

They must put crack rocks in their food cause I dream about their curries errrday.

One bite and I'm like, "hip hop hooooraayyy!"

Way better and cheaper than Naan 'n Curry, and nicer atmosphere too. Definitely worth a second visit. The veggie korma was good and so was the chicken tikka masala. The aloo palak was also yummy, and the naan was hot and fresh. Awesome!

guys... I have no idea why this restaurant is rated a 4. if there was a -1 rating i would give that.

I have been to quite a couple of Indian restaurants.. and this one is BY FAR the WORST. 8 bucks buffet lunch is comparable to most indian restaurants as almost all serve a less than 10 dollar buffet for lunch.

The food is just so bland and ewww.. and i live right beside it.. its always empty. i think all the people who commented haven't taste real authentic good indian food. if you believe its high rating on yelp. go ahead see for yourself, but be ready to get disappointed.

3.5 Stars.

Pros - Very cheap $7.99 includes fountain soda refills & freshly made Naan. The decor is nicer than what you would expect for the price they charge.(BTW... look straight up at the ceiling for a pleasant surprise) Their food is tasty enough for me. My favorite dish was Chicken Tikka Marsala. I liked how they labelled each item.

Cons-  Barely enough variety but acceptable for $8. Some yelpers commented that their sauces are watery.(they mean thin consistency vs thick but not diluted or weak in flavor) I like thick curry sauce to pour over my rice.BTW their rice is like dorm rice.edible after you drown it with sauce.  Their Tandoori Chicken was OK. I expected it to have more flavor & alittle more spicy kick to it but it satisfied my craving for meat. It irritated me that the staff was very slow to replenish the Tandoori Chicken. I watched them restock the other items but it took them a longer time to bring out more Chicken. It took them so long that I had to ask them if they were working on it.They said they were aware but it still took them a long time even after I spoke up. I think they need to monitor the food more closely & cook more food before it runs out.( especially the Tandoori Chicken).

I plan to come back once in awhile but the low variety & slow restocking made a negative impression on me.

These folks *totally* "get it."

Been here a few times now, and they've all been terrific.  Lunch/Dinner buffets are less than $10/person *and* include your beverage and naan. SCORE!

As mentioned in previous reviews, the buffet does not have endless variety, but what they do provide is tastey and plentiful.  Chicken tikka masala has been there everytime, however surprisingly saag paneer was not-and the time it was out, the cheese wasn't so great.  That aside, I think this place takes the #1 award for most tender chicken in tikka masala-it absolutely falls apart on the fork-unlike some places which tend to have dry chicken drowining in sauce.

Other curries and korma have been in rotation on my trips there, each has been very well spiced and flavored.  The naan was a little oily on my first trip, but has proven to be fluffy and fresh on the most recent trip.

All in all, this is turning out to be one of our new places in Berkeley to hit up Indian food. Sorry Biryani House-but this buffet just has it goin' on!

I was sort of shocked when I saw that this place had four prior reviews with five stars out of five. I was thinking a three or four star rating, at best.

The decor is nice and the service was excellent. But the food was really nothing special. Don't get me wrong. Nothing was bad. The naan was standard fare but a bit dry. The tandoori chicken was flavorful but not the juiciest I've had. The chicken tikka masala was acceptible. But nothing "shined" at all on the lunch buffet, and being the first ones in the door and finding it in pristine condition, that was as good as it gets. 

For $7.99 including drink and naan it's a great deal, don't get me wrong. But finding better (albeing pricier) Indian food isn't that hard in Berkeley.

Would have liked to experience this place, however they were not open even 10 minutes after they were supposed to open. The man inside rudely told me "If you want to eat you have to wait". He even pointed at me as he talked and spoke in a high pitched voice. What the heck? Like I'm a child? No thanks buddy, especially because you should have been open 10 minutes ago and I dont have that much time in between lectures.

don't do this to yourself. a block and a half away is "india palace restaurant." the price may be a bit steeper (by like a fucking dollar or two), but the selection over there is tastier and the food tastes more fresh.

the only dishes i legitimately enjoyed here were the chunks of watermelon and the green salad - and ironically, those are the two dishes that don't require much preparation.

We were in Berkeley on Election night wandering around looking for a new Indian restaurant to try. Once we pushed through the enormous crowd of people clustered at Ben & Jerry's for their free ice cream, we found Punjabi by Nature. The seating is in a room with a very high ceiling hung with colorful swathes of cloth. A huge bas-relief Ganesh adorns one wall. The dinner plates came with rice, vegetable, and nan as well as the ordered entrée. I ordered saag paneer my boyfriend ordered a lamb dish, we both ordered nan, since we didn't know that nan comes with the dinner. I got the gobi (cauliflower) nan which was ok, and he got the lamb nan which was good and very flavorful. The dinner portions were generous, and both of our entrées tasted excellent. Service was good and efficient.

$7.99 Indian dinner buffet includes naan and soda. Same price for lunch. It's a great deal. I'm sure there's off days, but it's been fine when I've gone. 

Best is the chicken masala, and there's usually about 6 different options, evenly split between vegetarian and meat.

Service is actually better than some sit-down restaurants I've been to. And they have beer on tap. Not sure what it is, but it was pretty cheap at $3 a pint and $8 a pitcher.

The lunch buffet wasn't the worst meal that I've ever had, but who has heard of Indian lunch buffet without good vegetarian options?

There were two or three "different" veg-friendly dishes.  Potatoes in a red not-that-flavorful sauce, and potatoes in a red not-that-flavorful sauce with some green peppers in it.  No sauce variation, so spinach, no cheese.  If I had to sum it up in a word: Boring, and if I had two, I'd add: Bland.

I love Indian food, and Indian buffets are usually my favorite.  Still on the search for something good in the Easy Bay.

Punjabi By Nature was the perfect pre and post Cal football game location. All I really need to say is... good food, good people, good location, && GREAT $1 beer deal on game days! 

PS. Very underrated by the regular Cal drinkers.. lots of room for my rowdy Gaucho crew.

Overall, pretty decent. First of all, you can't beat the price. I'm a great fan of Chicken Tikka Masala and this place has the stuff in a deep tray, ALWAYS. They also have a variety of veggie curries and sometimes lamb. Their naan is pretty good as well, and there's rice in the buffet if you prefer to mop up your masala with rice. OH and tandoori chicken! Nothing to write to anyone but Yelp about, but it's decent and it's also a staple.

It's always half empty, and it's true, the waitress, cook, owner all seem just a little bit awkward, but not enough that you'd feel awkward eating in there. The tables can be a little cramped, and I don't think anyone uses a new plate when they get seconds. Still, nobody's dipping their fingers in the sauce, so I wouldn't be too worried. 

To sum up: good for a quick, cheap, and filling Indian fix.

P.S. Open from 11:30 AM to 9:30 PM, one flat price of $7.99, naan and soda included.

Wow... This has quickly become one of my favorite restaurants in the East Bay. 

It is a wonderful place. Best Indian food I've had in a long, long time. In fact, their delicious chicken korma is the best I've ever had. Exquisite. And so is everything else. The saag is tasty. The samosas just right. And they absolutely bend over backwards in their service. They even remember my previous orders. Just can't say enough good things about their food or the restaurant itself. 

The interior is lovely and elegant, and the prices are terrific for the amount of food you get, not to mention the quality. I highly recommend it for everyone. 

And get there while you can. They're new, having only been open about 2 months, but once others find out about them, I expect they'll be regularly packed. Though no matter how packed they get, I can safely say I plan to be a regular customer from now on.

Okay. it's cheap.
But their cabbage was DISGUSTING!!!
everything else was just okay.

First I have to say: I agree with the 4 star rating of this place.

Second I have to say: Affordable, good Indian buffet!?!? Woohoo!

Yumtastic Indian food, beautiful / mildly classy interior look & feel, pleasant Indian music playing in the background, excellent service, and an outstanding price.

The reason I give 4 stars instead of 5 is because they don't include mattar paneer, vegetable biryani, OR samosas in the buffet (ever) and these are three of my fav Indian dishes...

Still, I'm definitely a fan and will recommend as well as return to PBN in the near future!

The food was excellent! The atmosphere was lovely considering how cheap the meal was! All of these things will keep me coming back. But...The service was lacking. I just came in today with my boyfriend for the first time. We were originally going to go to Saturn, but decided to give this place a try instead. The girl at the counter seemed as though she didn't give a shit, and had a slightly demeaning tone. I had to get up and remind them of our naan as no mention of bringing it to the table was mentioned, and I had to get our own water and refills, because even though it's wasn't even busy and the girl was just sitting there, she couldn't manage to see that we may need some refills. If they don't want to have to serve at all then why don't they just keep the water in a fridge like they do at naan and curry?

With all the Indian places around here, this is possibly one of the worst. How can EVERY Indian restaurant get 4 stars? Do people know what good / bad Indian food is?

It used to be Khana Peena, which was ok, then it was Dollar Curry, which was kinda ok, and now it's Punjabi.... which is pretty bad. The CTM is not real CTM, i dunno what it is... and here's the most interesting part:

Lunch Buffet is $7.99, posted right there on a sign. I had no time, so had to get it to go. I filled up a tiny, mini plastic container with some rice and chicken, and the woman rang me up for $10. $10?! It says $7.99! "It costs more if you take it go...." even if you get less food. I almost walked out without paying.

Come on, are times that hard that restaurants have to tack on $2  here and there and stiff their customers? That just isn't right.

Forget Naan n' Curry, come to this place.  It offers more bang for the buck.  The buffet is only 7.99, with endless naan, so you really can't go wrong for the price.  

I can recommend the indian salad, the seasoned rice, the naan, the BBQ redened chicken drumsticks, and especially the chicken tiki masala.  A single plate of the mentioned food above would easily run 8-9 bucks at another Indian joint, so why not get here and get it endless?

Parking really sucks (street parking only).  Sometimes, the service is lacking too because there is only one waitress for the entire restaurant.  While the food is not spectacular, its been consistent for the times I've eaten here.  

PROTIP:  Take the 1R and it stops right by this place.  The rice pudding is good too!

Yesss they are all you can eat at 7.99 both lunch and dinner!(probably, the most impt reason for their ratings!)

 The other important consideration would be the location. Right on oxford street.

Hubby and me walked in for dinner yesterday, and were impressed by the spread and the large Ganesha mural. What we were not impressed by was the quality of the spread.

 Spinach and garbanzo, Broccoli masala, Vegetarian kurma, Rajma, Fresh beans in masala and Dal makhani. All these curries will get 2-3 on 5, mainly because the base sauce for many of them was the same and really not exciting from a mix of flavors perspective.

The naans will get a 4.5 from us. They were made fresh and were crispy and soft. 

The rice was nothing to talk about, and the rice pudding was blah!

Didn't try the salads/raitha or the non vegetarian dishes.

May go back here coz it's cheap and serves Indian!

What a crazy deal. $7.99 for unlimited food, diet coke, and Naan. Whoa. The CTM was yum. The pakoras were amazing - very besan-y. The service was attentive. The naan was ghee-y. I just was so impressed. I will be a frequenter.

I went there today with a friend to try out their lunch buffet. I've got to say, for $7.99, it was totally worth the money. There wasn't much variety, but the selection was pretty good. 

What I had: 
- Chicken Tikka Masala: It was pretty good, compared to the other ones that I've had. 
- Veggie Lamb Masala: It was alright. I didn't quite like the lamb. 
- Chicken Tandoori: It was a bite dry. 
- Rice pudding: I really enjoyed the rice pudding. It was spiced the right amount. 

The lunch buffet came with FREE NAAN and soft drinks! I really liked the naan because it was soft. 

Overall, I think for $7.99, it was definitely worth a try. The food was pretty good and there's a variety of vegetarian and meat dishes. I definitely loved the naan. The restaurant décor was also very relaxing. My friend and I sat by the window, which was a pretty good location. The service was nice and there isn't much of a wait. 

Bottom line: I definitely recommend this place. It's worth a try for cheap and all you can eat Indian food.

Buffet for $7.99. Must try, if you are looking for a good indian buffet.
Need I say more. It blows Naan N Curry out of the water. Thats not saying much because naan N Curry is probably the most disgusting indian restaurant in all of berkeley.

They also have fresh naan, made to order, unlike NNC which has them sitting out and getting stale.

What do you do when a bridal shower is going on at the house you live in? You go eat at a buffet! But, what cuisine you say? Today's choice, Indian. 

$7.99 gets you a buffet at lunch (and I think the same price for dinner). This includes a drink and naan. The food was all good. They don't have a lot of variety, but it's plenty. Chicken Tikka Masala, saag, aloo gobi, a lamb one, chicken tandoori, one with mushroom, and one with long green beans. 

I was plenty full. I still haven't had dinner today. Anyway, might try this out again. I was happy.

the best indian food in the east bay!

beautiful food!
beautiful service
beautiful presentation

I love going here- I've been here 3 times and every time has been superb! And the prices are SOOOOOO good!

I never met a buffet I didn't like.  well, ok, so some hometown buffets are downright disgusting, but as far as indian goes, i loooove me my indian buffets.  

now typically the indian buffet only comes out at lunch, but punjabi by nature is filling that night time buffet void in my life by offering buffets for every meal.  

ok, so it's not the biggest spread i've seen at a buffet, but they've got the staples.  And sure, it's not the most delicious indian food i've ever had, but it's still pretty tasty and a buffet, and I wanted to go back time and time again, and the meats were plentiful and the sauces thick and delicious.  totally not the worst indian buffet i've had, in fact, pretty darn good.  did i mention that it's the cheapest indian dinner i've had in a long time/ever?  

mmm, punjabi, i'd almost move to berkeley just for your unlimited indian food access all night long.

I love me some Indian Food and this place is great if your are in the mood for authentic Cheap Indian Cuisine.

I have gone here twice with a co-worker and there $7.99 buffet is as good as it gets. The wait staff is very accomdating and friendly. There selection in the buffet is plentiful. The place is quaint and perfect to go solo.

Look people, you have to judge the food in the category it is in as well as the location. As far as cheap Indian buffets are concerned, Punjabi by Nature is a win! BTW this is my first Yelp review, so sorry in advance if it rants!

Price/Value:

Their buffet is only $8 (at time of writing), which is a great value considering that competing India Princess, Viceroy, and Pasand will all cost you $10+ per person for one Naan and one curry dish. The closest you'll come to price is Biryani House, which still runs you $8 for one naan and one dish. Oh and did I mention a free refillable soda is also included in the price? Viceroy's buffet is the same price (no Soda) as Punjabi, BUT, read below...

The Taste:

Keep in mind this is coming from a native of India who has eaten at every single Indian restaurant in Berkeley at least 3 times each. Not only is this the best cheap Indian buffet in Berkeley, it has some of the best overall food as well (see rankings below).

-The naan is some of the best you can get in Berkeley, soft and chewy/ crisp ratio nailed to perfection. 

*CRITICSMS*:

-The food tastes great..when it's warm. Which is not very often. You have to have your timing right so you don't get there at an off hour when nothing fresh is coming out. Otherwise, the quality of the food quickly deteriorates to be far worse than many of the restaurants I've ranked below. So it's really a hit or miss depending on freshness/warmth of food. I don't know why for the life of them why they don't keep the food warm!

-The food will put you to sleep. Out of the Indian food in Berkeley, this is probably some of the most heavy in terms of you feeling groggy/ lethargic afterwards. My reccomendation: Don't eat too much of the cream-based dishes, that's usually the culprit.
