- NO variation in selection. I've been here a lot, and the dishes are almost always the same, save perhaps one dish which I don't bother touching most of the time anyways. So you can get bored of these place real fast, even if though the food is good. 

Service:
Pretty good in my opinion. The Nepali waitress usually there is very nice and greets you with a smile every time; the owners do not when they are managing but the service is still there. When my favorite dish was gone at 9pm, I requested more even though the place was deserted, and the waitress happily ordered more to be made from the kitchen. That's great customer service and a win in my book. Oh and your water glass is always full, what more can you ask from a buffet with no tip? 

This is how I'd rank the taste of North Indian Restaurants in Berkeley (this takes into account everything, naan quality and consistency, curries, etc.) The list is not exhaustive yet, as this is my first review.

Now I know a lot of you are going to disagree, but keep in mind this is coming from someone who is a native Indian. I'm sure for non-Indians many of these restaurants seemingly serve "great" Indian food.

**I will keep updating this ranking list **

Updated 6/24/2010

1) Flavors of India / Kabab and Karahi (tie)
2) Himalaya
3) Urbann Turbann ($5 Cholay wrap: best value for your money, period).
4) Punjabi By Nature
5) Chaat Cafe
6) Priya
7) Viks (yeah, I know I'm going to get a lot of flak for this one, but it's true folks, severely overrated due to bandwagoning)

8) Breads of India (OK, but overpriced)
9) Biryani House
10) Khana Peena (the one on Solano, a little better than the other one)
11) Pasand (OK, but severely overpriced)
12) House of Curries (College)
13)  Kabana (Great food loses massive points for racially based treatment of customers)
14) Tandoor Kitchen
15) Khana Peena (the one on Shattuck, absolute trash, avoid) 
16) Indus Valley Restaurant (literally serves frozen vegetable curries)

**Now if I called Khana Peena Shattuck trash, then you can imagine how the following are...yeah...these don't deserve to even be ranked**

House of Curries (Durant)
Naan N Curry

$7.99 ALL YOU CAN EAT + FREE DRINK (INCLUDES NAAN!) Must I say more?

If you have had Indian food around Berkeley, you know it can get pretty pricey. WHY?? It's just naan and curry! Seriously, stop wasting your money because this is the best value for very good quality food. 

Chicken Tiki Masala is an always good staple and everything is bottomless! So come hungry and leave happy.

Good Food, Good Friends, ENJOY!

Small spot with 8-9 tables. $7.99 AYCE buffet which includes fresh baked naan & soft drink with refills of both. Extra fresh naan doesn't seem too common at most buffets. 

Average sized spread with 8 hot dishes. Today was 5 veggie curries, 2 chicken curries, and tandoori chicken. Also rice, salad, and papadams as well as melon and rice pudding for dessert. Four sauces like raita, tamarind, and that green minty sauce are available.

Good overall. Nothing stood out as great or bad. The tandoori chicken was moist which is better than most buffets, but pretty bland flavorwise. It tasted better shredded into the chicken tikka masala.

Good place for starving students and the value concious to fill up.

Side Note: Cool elephant thing on the wall above the buffet and be sure look up and check out the fabric covered ceiling.

(probably a stick of butter in each order, but soooo glorious, even if guilty fat/carb-fest)

my end of semester treat to myself, after all finals: chicken pesto pasta. *deep sigh* ... honestly, all their stuff is big and heavy enough to split too.... also tried this as a calzone, and that totally knocked me out; will stick with lighter pasta!

note: you'd better like garlic! it comes ON the bread! yummy & roasty

beware: if you get something to go, don't tip the box...you'll get oily!

This place rocks.  Ive been here many times and its always that damn good.  Its cheap, delicious and filling.  Its just like how mama makes it, except my mom doesnt make italian food.  But if she did, i would imagine it would be like gypsy's.   I always go for the chicken con pesto pasta  and gypsy's chicken.  Calzones are good too, but not my thing.  Only bad thing?  Gets crowded, dirty tables and my fork was sticky.  But its all good, just ask for a new one!

After a  late night out with my girls we ended up here. Near the UC campus, they stay open late so this was the perfect spot to go to. Mouth-watering Italian food for a cheap price! Try it out if youre in the area!

Calzones and shrimp alfredo pasta is pretty good for the price. It's borderline fast food, but you definately get a decent meal for the price you pay. Worth making a trip over for lunch or dinner if you like Italian food! :)

This has to be one of my top three favorite italian restaurants. I recommend the crazy Alfredo, the shrimp Alfredo or any of their calzones! Their garlic bread is different but still so good. It's fresh bread with a slab of garlic halfway melted on it (atleast when they give it to me!) oh & friendly staff too!

Spagetti and meatballs are delish!

This place is a go-to when im in the area. Ive never been at a time when theres no line and its a little crazy but well worth it!

CHICKEN GNOCCHI...mmmmm
Okay okay... I am definitely a gnocchi fan and they have some good gnocchi here. Not the best in the world, but darn good and for the price, you can't beat it. Plus its actually amazing how Gypsy's has created a legit place thats basically a fast food italian. It is quick for pasta considering they make everything fresh and their pizzas and calzones are always right out of the oven. Another plus is that you will literally see so many people you know walking there, in there, or around there... nice place to stop and people watch :)

Very worth the price! The pasta is a little better than average and the calzones are huge and delicious, but sometimes a little too cheesy. If you're feeling ravenous, Gypsy's will definitely be able to fix that.

One thing I miss about living on Telegraph, besides of course being kept up all night by the obnoxious drunkards smoking outside of Blakes, is Gypsy's. 

Located in the Asian Ghetto across from King Pin Donuts, Gypsy's is a modest takeout joint where you get quality Italian food QUICK and for a reasonable price. It's almost always crowded but it's not impossible to find a table if you don't wanna do takeout. You order, get a number, wait, and enjoy. 

Although the menu has a lot to offer, I always get the same thing: ravioli alfredo with chicken breast. =P** All pastas come with a piece of garlic bread, but not your typical garlic bread. No, this one is a piece of bread lightly toasted with a clove of sauteed garlic rubbed all over its surface and then stuck right in the middle. It's yummy but not the salty, oily, buttery thing you might be thinking of.

I always say I'll order something different "next time." If I do, I'll write another review. In the mean time, take yo ass to Gypsy's and try SOMETHING. You'll like it!

my office is right across the street from this place,so naturally i come here from time to time. The food is good, the price is great. The quality of the pasta is not always perfect, but for less then $ 7, well, what can i say! 

I don't like sitting there though, i don't like the atmosphere.. and the number-yelling..

I used to frequent this a lot more during my freshman year, but there's definitely a reason why I stopped coming back.

Major issue I have with this place is that they ALWAYS overcook their shrimp. In anything I order (that ha shrimp in it) it's always dry and tough instead of crisp and juicy like it's supposed to be. Gross.

Also, too many items on the menu are cream-based, making for a very "heavy" meal (because it's already carb-heavy). I always intentionally order items that don't have cream in it because of that, but my selection is actually quite limited because of it.

Customer service is terrible. No apology or explanation if there is an excessive wait in line. Today the cash register was broken, and it was holding up the line and making it difficult for credit/debit card customers to pay. An explanation or at least a "sorry about that"/ "thanks for waiting" would have been appreciated. Plus, their food isn't all that cheap for what you're getting, and if you're paying by card, it's more expensive.

That said, I'm pretty sure their loss of a loyal customer isn't that big of a deal. They're in a prime location and are open late. Usually busting with activity during peak meal hours.

I guess you could call this Italian food.  Greasy pasta piled on greasy sauce with greasy bread and chunk of greasy garlic with butter.  That about describes every non-salad dish I've ever had at Gypsy's.  Then you leave feeling like you've got a brick in your stomach.  

Buuuuutttt, the flavors of some of these dishes are pretty good.  The Crazy Alfredo is tasty and so are the calzones.  It's gotten pricier over the years and it doesn't seem as much of a value as when I was an undergrad in 05.  But it's good drunk late night food.

Oh how I miss this place! In my 4.5 years spent at CAL I came here about 100 times, it was even the first place I ate here when I came to orientation. I've ordered almost everything on the menu. Now that I am back in LA I can't find another place that makes quick and cheap italtian food so Gypsies kinda offers a rare service. My favorites were the chicken piccata, chicken pomodora, gypsy chicken, and chicken pesto.

You'll want to be a student at Berkeley just so you can eat here every day. The best gnocci in the world, the WORLD... So good that you don't mind that there's no parking and nowhere to sit. Chicken and Gnocci with the bread and smushed garlic on top. mmmm, OK, I'm leaving my house now to get some.. Mmmmm...

This place doesn't look very fancy but for some reason it's always packed.  It must be the food!  The kitchen staff shovels out pasta dishes like a mini factory and the wait time is pretty reasonable for pasta.  I almost always order the "Gypsies Chicken" and they give a good amount of chicken... (if you read my other reviews you'll notice a similar theme involving chicken quantity)... hehe I love my chicken.  I always gaze at the other items on the menu but in the end I'll just order the "gypsies chicken" just because I know it's THAT good and that I'll still be satisfied even though I get it all the time.  It's cheap too... around 7 bucks.

Heard about this place from sales lady at Best Buy.  Yeah....

We can't remember the last time we spent this little money for dinner.  Food is average, but defintiely a great value for the $7.99 price (entre + salad + soda).  big portion too!  Wow.

I think this is a pefect placce for takeout.

College students eat your heart out!

It's Italian cuisine that's part of the asian ghetto straight in the heart of Cal eatery world . Nothing beats cheap filling pasta when you are a starving, pockets almost empty student.

I'll admit I haven't been back in years since my life has moved on to adult slavery, but Gypsy's brings back nothing but good memories. If it wasn't the calzone I was ordering I would typically get Chicken parmigiano, pollo gorgonzola or Gypysy's chicken. 

The reason I put it at 3 stars is because it can be incredibly cheesy and a bit too greasy and made more for iron stomachs, which I do indeed have. 

It's a no frills place so don't come here for ambience, but if you want to dine with students in the hustle and bustle of Caltopia, this is your spot.

Love their special: House Salad with choice of dressing + ANY MENU ITEM + drink = $8 and some change !

Big portions. Always more than enough so I end up having to take the leftovers for home. Although there's a $0.50 refill and the staff doesn't always smile....it's no big deal. The food is great & I'd come back again.

The pasta was flavorful enough, not al dente and served with weak bread, but for less than $6 bucks it was a pretty good deal. The salad with caesar dressing was OK as well. The atmosphere inside is just so so, but seemingly clean. You order at the counter and sit down until they call your number to pick up your own food. So there's not much service, but it's cheap fast food and a grade above the chain fast food restaurants. This food is probably on par with Olive Garden, though I haven't been there in over a decade.

The food here is so good. The portions are huge and every dish is only $5-$7.50! I love the chicken alfredo, linguine with clams, and futti de mare. I always get the pasta but they also have calzones, pizza, salads, and sandwiches.

They're not real gypsies, but it still tastes really good. Haven't eaten anything, but it all tastes good and takes a few minutes to cook. Vent your calzones with a fork though or you're in for a mouth burning.

Cafe Intermezzo may have the longest line outside its doors during the day, but Gypsy's is where its at after the sun goes down. The pastas and calzones are by no means authentic, but they are hella delicious. Gypsy's cooks up every kind of pasta combination imaginable and if it isn't on the menu, just ask -- they may make a custom dish for you. The menu also features an impressive number of vegetarian dishes and gourmet personal pizzas.

The dining area is small and often crowded, so getting your dish to go may be the best option. Listen up for your number or your food may sit on the counter for a while. Lastly, beware of hovering flies, especially during the summer.

Some of the stuff is amazing.
Chicken Picatta, Linguinis are generally good, alfredos pretty decent. The garlic bread they serve is a hit or miss; I've taken to scraping off the garlic since it adds nothing to the bread, and if it's cold and mushy, actually makes it worse.
Ravioli is average.

Never tried Calzone or Pizza (not a big fan of either usually).
I always get their combo for the salad, which is just romaine lettuce, tomatoes, and dressing, but a sizeable portion for a small price increase (plus a small drink.)
Gets kind of crowded. Usually crowded. With good reason too :P

Overall a 5 if you pick the right plates, depending on your taste preferences.
wish i could give 6 stars for their gnocchi and garlic bread. this is in the asian ghetto of berkeley, but the taste is second to none. i miss this place.

i've tried many dishes here and came to the conclusion that the only pasta ill get here from now on is the pesto chicken one. their cesar chicken salad here comes in huge proportions. you could share the salad between 2 people while still paying around $6. Their calzones are huge as well but be patient with ordering that cus it takes a while to bake. That lasted my bf 2 meals, but I could usually finish their pastas in a meal. All their items are very cheap for italian food ranging around $6 or $7. would highly recommend this place to someone who wants good food and is on a budget.

Gypsy's is my new found love!

Italian food has always been my favorite, so imagine my excitement finding a really good italian food place that is not only fast but extremely inexpensive! My boyfriend and I are always in Berkeley wandering and eating, but instead of our usual stop at Top Dog we decided to try this place out since he's always heard a lot of good reviews on it. 

My mouth started watering the moment I walked through the door and saw all the yummies that everyone was eating. We were even more amazed at the prices! Most of the pasta dishes range from $6-$7 and you can add a pretty big salad and drink for about $2.  The portions are huge, enough to satisfy the both of us with the salad, but being the little fatties we are, we like to order 2 dishes to try new menu items and to have some left overs.

So the first pasta dish we had was the Crazy Alfredo which is linguine in Alfredo sauce with mushrooms, sausages, chicken, and red bell peppers.  It quickly became a favorite until we had the Pesto Chicken pasta which quickly replaced the Crazy Alfredo as our numero uno.   will admit that the pastas are a bit rich and can make you feel a bit heavy after, but it's well worth it, and nothing a quick gym session won't fix. We've also tried the calzones after drooling over seeing everyone else's come out.  I prefer the pasta better.  The calzones are really HUGE, and when you cut into it the juices start flowing out of it. I, myself, am not really a pizza person so I stick to the pasta. 

We're always trying to fit a quick trip to Gypsy's into our schedules, and it's awesome cuz you can just phone in your order and make a quick pick up. Or stop by the many tapioca drink places nearby for a $1 drink while you wait! Overall, it's definitely worth a visit. =)

I come here for lunch often. Great location near campus at only $8 a plate. Godfather's favorite is a regular order :) Gets a bit heavy, so not something to get often but all in all a great place. They have a really efficient system of getting food to you quick though. Loses a star for presentation of the restaurant and not using compostable take-out boxes. This place needs to go green! Especially in the heart of Berkeley.

this place is awesome, the food here is cheap and fast and hella good. its par to pasta p's except its cheaper faster but you dont get free bread.  probably the sickest thing about Gypsy's is that its open til 12. kinda weird that its in the epicenter of all the asian hangout with all the asian restaurants surrounding it. good fettuccine and tomato pastas and theyre calzones are huge. its usually full inside but theres seating outside if you dont mind the bums staring at you while you eat

I know it's sad to use a $6 student eatery in the "asian ghetto" as a pasta standard but I freaking love this place. It is much better than pricier local places like Macaroni Grill, Giovanni's, Filippo's, and Pasta Pomodoro. Don't come here to reminisce vacation in Italy or expect refined Italian but for cheap and yummy basic pasta it's still my favorite. I miss you Gypsy's.

*oops i made the mistake of eating here in a recent visit. not as good as i remembered since living in sf has made me a foodie. its ok, i still love u and wont dock the rating.
Calzones are dank as in da bomb

i love gypsys! everything is good here. my fav. is the godfather's favorite! 
its really cheap + delicious! and they close @ 12! one of the best spots in berkeley!

My friend and I were camping at a local park in Berkley and it's 10p[m and haven't had dinner yet. I turned on my handy dandy Yelp and located this place within the mile! Lucky for us, this establishment is open til midnight! Woot woot! I sent my guy off to get us some food and in a blink of an eye, he brings back linguini and clams with shrimp. If we wanted the whole shebang, it came with mussels, clams, shrimp, calamari, etc. On top of that, we get to chose red or white sauce. Our to go box also came with garlic bread.

Quite possibly the best "Italian" place in the Bay Area.

5 stars for:

Portions........huge!

Taste.........delicious, hearty, and rich.

Price......$7 for any menu item with a salad, bread, and drink....WOW!!!!

Speed......usually about 10 minutes from order to eating.

Location.......close to Telegraph and the weekend vendors, and right across from Kingpin Donuts......the desert after the meal and the BEST donuts in the world.

My Favorites:  Pollo Con Pesto (I ask for mushrooms on mine)
                         Godfather's Favorite

If you are looking for an "authentic" Italian place with waiters and a wine list, you'll have to keep looking.

If you want a quick bite to eat that is convenient, reasonably priced, and DELICIOUS, then Gypsy is the place for you.

Seriously......stop at Kingpin Donuts afterward.  AWESOME chocolate buttermilk bars!!!!!

This was way better than I expected it to be. Basically it was a huge portion of delicious pasta. I made a bad call and ate everything on the plate, but it didn't feel like I had eaten a rock afterward. I felt all right. A little too full, but not sick. It wasn't a greaseball. 

Over all, it's an amazing deal. I paid $7-8 for a meal that easily tasted like $12-15.

This place gets good reviews because it's mostly college students that patronize it.  Those in the know, who have experienced many different Italian restaurants will think it's just OK.  The price is really cheap and it's definitely a good value but go elsewhere if you only care about taste.
My favorite place!! Love the gnocchi and godfather's favorite and the shrimp alfredo! Great quality for the price!!! :)

dude.  i LOVE places like this.  semi crowded.  Not too clean, but not dirty by any means...   6 dudes in a tiny kitchen, slavin' away, bustin' their @sses to get you your food.  and it's DELICIOUS.  this is gypsies.  If you want a nice gourmet italian meal of elegance, this ain't the place.  If you want some down and dirty italian food, Gypsys' got what you're looking for.

Great pasta and at a very affordable price!

I was amazed when I walked in to see that the price for a plate of pasta was only around $7/8 bucks?!

That is unheard of! 

Pastas were very flavorful and they put a good amount of meat in there too! I kept finding more and more pieces of chicken in there!

Great Italian food for a great price.

I got the linguini with chicken and peppers which was delicious.  A favorite of mine, this is the place to go for some excellent well priced Italian food.

And if you are a student, this is a must go.  It would be great for friends, groups, or for a date.

If you appreciate quality Italian food and are in the UC Berkeley area, andare!

Gypsy's has huge portions for the amount of money you pay.  That's what drew me there initially.  Good eats + cheap prices = me as a repeat customer.  They do simple pasta dishes and calzones well, and their salads aren't too shabby.  Gypsy's doesn't shaft you on meat and sauce on any of its dishes.  My personal favs are the linguini frutti di mare, Gypsy's chicken and pesto pasta.  The garlic bread is fantastic yet simple, just a couple of cloves of buttery soft roasted garlic and some EVOO make for crunchy garlicy goodness.  Coming from Gilroy, I know a thing or two about garlic, and they do it right.

One of the longtime staples of any Golden Bear. The restaurant is constantly packed - usually students - but the service is quick and not personal because they're trying to get the food out as fast as possible. 

The prices are decent. The portions are large enough to be considered a meal. If you're really daring, you can always order one of the massive calzones - these orders take a bit longer. I'll definitely be eating here more over the years as a student.

Vegetarian pasta dishes -- Funghi and Fettuccine Alfredo -- are pretty good. Although I'm a huge meat fan, I really enjoyed their vegetarian pasta dishes. These dishes (in my opinion) trumped their meat plates. 3 stars because only a few dishes are good/decent and not majority. Still, if you're craving italian and pasta, this might be a good go to spot.

Me and my lady have been going to Gypsys for years and all i can say is they have really good food for a very reasonable price! The servings are huge and worth the money. The shrimp fettucine, chicken pesto calzone, and  chicken/peperoni/ calzone are our favorites. FYI it gets pretty packed in there, so dont expect dining in if you dont know how to swoop on a table!

Located in Berkeley's "Ghetto food court", Gypsy's is a favorite amongst Berkeley students, especially undergrads, due to its convenient, fast food style, entree variety and above average quality relative to cost. 

(Scales are 1-5, same as Yelp ratings)

Atmosphere: 2

The place gets very busy during lunch and dinner on most days, especially on weekends. If you want to eat in, try doing it before or around 6 pm for dinner and before 12 or after 1:30'ish for lunch. Otherwise, prepare for a long line (which, to their credit, goes fast) and difficult to find seating. This is not a great sit down restaurant. It caters to college students who come in, talk loud, answer their cell phones in a obnoxious and pretentious manner and eat fast. The cooks call out your number and you pick it up and bring it to your table. You dont bus your own dishes, as someone typically comes out every so often to clean up tables. There is seating outside (available to all Ghetto food court restaurants)., but the tables are usually dirty.  I normally avoid eating in (and this is true for all the restaurants in the food court). Take out and eat at Sproul. At least you can people watch there without feeling cramped.

Service: 3.5

The service is relatively quick. They dont go out of their way to serve you, but there are no real problems with the service. The guy taking orders is difficult to understand at times. When you eat in, you pick up the food from the counter. And sometimes they take a tad too long to bus dishes and clean the tables. They also close late for those who need a late dinner.

Food: 4

I've tasted only 3-4 entrees, but plan on trying out a few others in the future. I really like their Godfather's favorite dish (penne pasta with thick white cream sauce). Their other pasta dishes are fine. The dishes are filling, come with bread and are big in quantity. I tried their calzones once and did not find it especially appealing. I would say the quantity and quality are a notch above something like pasta pomodoro but lower than a nice dine in Italian restaurant you would fine in North Beach.

Cost: 4

Can't complain about the cost. It is relatively cheap for good quantity and quality. The restaurant caters to college students, so the cost of a decent size meal matches the budget of its regular customers.

Pros: Cheap but good quantity and quality. Closes late.

Cons: Dont come here for the dining experience. Long lines, loud students and limited seating makes this place more of a take out type restaurant. 

Best Entree: Godfather's Favorite.
Worst Entree: Calzone


Sample Size: I have eaten here over a dozen times.

Come fall when I'm at UC Berkeley, Gypsy's will be in my belly every Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Good.

Oh but I do have a problem with the drink system. Dishes usually run at around $6-7 and for $8.99 you can add a salad and a drink, but your drink is dinky (I'm talking the volume of maybe four dixie cups) and you have to pay 50 cents for each additional refill. But other than that, no complaints.

I am totally fine with eating at greasy spoons, I love paying under $10 for a meal, and I frequent University-area eateries whenever I'm in Berkeley.  

This place sucks, though.

The older man at the register is on auto-pilot and seems a little hard of hearing (not a good combo if you want your order correct), the food is really sub-par and the students here are super annoying. My lasagna was terrible & greasy, my sister's eggplant parm plate looked very gross and my other sister's chicken cesar salad was lame (the chicken was "real" and cooked in front of us, but STILL unappetizing nonetheless).  

I did like the hispanic guys cooking and would have tipped them separately if I could.

Now that La Fiesta is closed (my previous go-to place), I'll stick with Top Dog or La Burrita.  If all the other places on the block are closed, and I'm extremely stoned, I miiiiight return, but this is highly unlikely.

I love this place. Great food, cheap price, nice atmosphere. For the cheap college student, nothing beats this place. I always order the Fettuccine Alfredo with no mushrooms, and I'm never disappointed. I love the fresh cheese grated on top. I'm not a fan of the bread with the garlic on top, but other than that, the food is awesome. The portions are huge, and I love how its made fresh to order. Although its a little loud most of the time, most places are in berkeley, so i don't mind.
Authentic Italian food for an unbeatable price...you need to try the combo Calzone and the Mediterranean Pasta!

Gypsy's is Famous for it's Cheap Good Quality Italian Food, I brought an Italian friend that says it's Just like the Real thing in Italy! It's the almost the same as Trattoria La Sicilian, But Cheaper! When I walk by, it's always crowded, no matter what the time. (what does that tell you?)

The greatest pastas in the Bay Area period! 
The guy at the register is very impatient but friendly after all. The food is incredibly good and the prices are incredibly low!
Highly recommended :)

I love that chicken pesto calzone like theres no tomorrow. My eyes used to light up like a kids on Christmas when it was on the table, looking all glorious.

But lately, it's been coming out super cold in the middle. So disappointing. And the last time, they put it back in the oven and forgot about it; then gave it back to me looking like a burnt football.

Sucks :(

Usually, this place is good. The past 4 times, though, not so much. Heat my calzone thoroughly damnit, is it that hard?!

After seeing the raving reviews, I decided to give this place a whirl on a beautiful weekday after selling my clothes down the street.  I ordered the Chicken Pesto and added a salad and drink.  Any menu item with salad and a drink is only $7.99.  I have never been to a quick, fast, cheap Italian restaurant where fancy tablecloths and tipping was not involved.  This is it!! The food was great, a little more pesto then what I am use to, but the taste was awesome and came with a slice of garlic bread.  

The salad was your standard green and i got Cesar Dressing.  

Only con was 0.50 for refills on fountain drinks, which would be okay provided if the drink was a decent size.  The drink was smaller then my hand!!! 

Staff was friendly and made for a pleasurable experience.

Gypsy's is a college student's dream come true.

Their food is delicious, but what makes it even more appealing are the large portions and great prices.  Every time I eat there, I get the combo which is any dish, a small salad, and a small drink for just a little bit more money.  To say this is a steal would be an understatement.  For a small girl like me, the "small" salad is perfect for a light lunch.  Then I can just get the main dish to go and eat that for dinner: two meals for the price of one! 

I have yet to try a calzone, but I hear those are definitely worth trying.  If I lived closer to the Asian Ghetto (say, in the Units) I'd definitely be there every week to escape the boring food at the Dining Commons.

Almost everything on the menu is less than $7 but the food is delicious and they give you a lot of it. They serve up the dishes quite quickly for the large number of customers they receive. You can't go wrong with any of their Alfredo dishes. Definitely recommended if you like a nice, affordable meal that fills you up.

Great Food for what you pay for.  Good atmosphere.
I don't like their Cal Zones.  
Personal favorites:  Pomodoro, fungi, I don't remember the name of this last one but it has salmon in it.

Gypsies is actually very good Italian food for being run by Mexicans in the "Asian Ghetto" so near UC Berkeley.  The prices are very good and the food is excellent and come out in good portions.  I stopped here on many occassions between classses to get a chicken salad or Victor's Spaghetti for lunch.  The Calzones are quite good, quite big, and quite popular.  Its all good.

I would say that this is more like school/hospital cafeteria imitation Italian food than actual Italian. 

I got the Gyspsy's chicken - the "alfredo sauce" was more of a garlic goo with a lot of oil and butter. I couldn't even finish my plate. Once I got past the initial ackward taste, I just couldn't get past the pool of oil and salty-garlicky-goo sauce at the bottom my dish. The color was off too - normally alfredo sauce is a cream color, this was kinda biege/green. I couldn't shake the feeling that something was wrong it. It was just all around not quite right. 

No thanks.

Great place for fresh great pasta at a reasonable price.  Where else can you get Italian pasta for $6.00 that tastes this good?!

Try the Penne Gargonzola or the Godfathers Favorite if you like creamy dishes.  I don't recommend their red sauce dishes, but do like their Calzones (They are huge).

My absolute favorite Italian place in Berkeley. Maybe it's because I started eating there when I was in college, but I love this place. It has excellent prices. Also, it has amazing food. Everything I, or anyone I've eaten with, has gotten has been delicious. And they are very good about making the order exactly as you want it (meaning holding some items), even if it is a bit strange. My absolute favorite dish is the Crazy Alfredo. Each dish also comes with a slice of toasted bread with garlic on it. It does take a little while for orders to come up, but it is worth the wait. Although I am a bit bummed they started charging extra for credit card transactions, I will still keep going, because the employees are so nice and the food is so great!

So the last few times i've been here, i've been ordering the Chicken Ceasar Salad with Jumbo Shrimp (sometimes without shrimp) but boy do they fill up your to go box or give you the proportions you want. The downside, not enough dressing. Makes the salad sort of dry most of the time. 

The other thing is, I realized how small of a proportion the pasta servings are. Sure I know pasta is filling, but when they give so little for $8, its depressing to look at. 

I'd come back occasionally for the salad though. Only when i am feeling healthy after the gym .
Delicious chicken alfredo! All pasta dishes are truly scrumptious. Garlic bread (with actual garlic chunks) makes a great side. Convenient location and decent service.

Gypsy is a nice little restaurant with quick service and a surprisingly varied menu. I had the chicken gnocchi for lunch and it was superb. The sauce was creamy, well-seasoned and thick, the gnocchi was tender and chewy and the chicken was perfectly cooked. Nothing fancy here, just good Italian food made by Italians. What more do you want?

This is probably the cheapest Italian food you'll ever eat. The catch? It kinda tastes like the cheapest Italian food you'll ever eat.

It's great every once in a while for an easy meal loaded with carbs and butter. Don't get me wrong, the Godfather's Favorite is definitely within my top 20 favorite dishes in Berkeley. However, most of the entrees here are so unhealthy that you feel like Gypsy's invented the Freshman 15 in Berkeley.

The prices are not the lowest in the surrounding area, so there are much better options. The Italian place across the street even offers better value. However, this is one of the few places in the "Asian Ghetto" that takes credit/debit cards. That will come in handy at some point.

The wait is typically pretty long, so you might find yourself waiting here with a backpack on and an empty stomach for quite some time.

The prices were low and the portions were big.  This is a good place to go for lunch or dinner when you are visiting Berkeley.  Good if you like roasted garlc...they spread it right on to the garlic bread.  

The pizza and calzone were fair to good.  The dough was a little bland.  It's not as good as Zachary's but for the price, it's a good value.

I wouldn't say the best Italian food in the world, but relatively good for the price. Sometimes a little greasy, but that's what you should probably expect from an intalian take out place open practically whenever you want.

I love how this place is soo convenient for students! They are open late nights and serve pretty damn good Italiano food. The pastas are actually cooked from scratch and I have seen the cooks do their thing. They are actually using legit ingredients for their sauces and pastas. They are not stingy with their pastas and they serve garlic break which is a basic bread slice with a moist garlic rub on top. The pastas are good here and I dont care! The place itself as well as the seats, etc. are janky and they need to do something about their soda fountain bar because the counter is sticky as hell. Oh and the owner on the register is hella niiice! he has great patience for people late at night.

If you're looking for the classic college town restaurant - cheap eats and large, filling portions - Gypsy's is pretty much it for the Italian variety of food.

They have a decent variety of pasta dishes, and absolutely humongous calzones. Most of the dishes are heavy on the sauce - very filling food that'll last you for a good while. The dishes are mostly well-cooked as well - even if the flavor is somewhat masked over by the sauce, the pasta is cooked right and the meats are pretty savory (sometimes heavy on the oil). Definitely not overcooked or rubbery like some of the other Berkeley places that sell Italian food.

The one knock on their food (aside from not being suited for lighter eaters who can't handle lots of sauce/oil), is their "garlic bread". Just a plain piece of a roll, but with this scoop of gross garlic paste slapped on top.

YUM......... omg it's 2:40 am and I could really go for a CALZONE right now, the food was great, and prices are fair as well. The wait was a bit long, but hey if that means fresher and cooked on the spot then who cares? :) Definitely want to go back again!

"Meh... I've experienced better" seems to fit, so two stars seems more appropriate but the food itself was average, so I hate to give it such a low rating.  I ordered a hawaiian pizza with no cheese the crust was thick and the ingredients just okay.  They did say that the dough was dairy free though, a nice bonus.  I didn't like the Taco Bell-like atmosphere and the visible kitchen from the cash register.  But I guess I didn't know that the closer you get to campus the more okay it is to have this kind of environment as long as you have decent food.  Next time I think I'll spend another $3 and get a real sit down meal at a place with good atmosphere if I am looking for just a so-so dairy-free pizza while having lunch with friends.

Gypsy's is a decent italian place, i'd say the main appeal is the price and the portion size.
Their pasta dishes are okay, for pasta dishes. They taste good because the sauces are normally creamy and the portions are huge, and everything comes with garlic bread. although the garlic bread is really just plain white bread with a dallop of garlic sauce. 
Their calzones are huge, and they taste okay, and they are really fresh, you see them making them. the calzones are pretty average, but they're huge, so that's the main appeal.
the salads are okay, i mean they're nothing special, but they're good and fresh and have good dressing. 
Gypsy's looks a little bit dingy, and the food is just okay, nothing extra special; I've had much better italian food in the area, and it wasn't super pricey. I'd say gypsy's is just always crowded because it's so close to the dorms, and it is so cheap and serves up such large portions. The pasta's don't taste that special, honestly, some of the sauces taste like they could be out of a can/jar, i'm not saying they are, but they don't taste like anything special.

Gypsy's is good if you want fast cheap italian food, or you want somewhere cheap to go with friends.

A warning though, at busy times (like dinner time any day) the indoor seating tends to get really full.

Fast Italian food. Huge portions. Cheap. 

Gypsy's isn't your typical romantic Italian date spot. It's a great place for groups - there's seating both indoors and outdoors. It's also a great place for busy people who want decent, hearty Italian food that is quickly made to order and is affordable. I can easily order one of their pasta entrees and save half for another meal - the portions are THAT big. Plus, I love their toasted bread with the smeared garlic.
Best calzone pizza, great chicken pasta, what to say, an all timer for lunch!!!

so yummy! but so unhealthy that i don't think it's practical... 
pools of oil kind of ruin the dining experience T____T

This is one of the place that i have to visit during my berkeley trip.

The dishes are so goooooooooooooooooooooooooooood!!!!!!!!!!

price is just right and the portion is very big
Had my first calzone from this place. Not bad. Not as mind blowing either. But it's cheap, so can't complain.

Oh yum. What a great place to get pasta, salad, pizza, calzones, anything really. No air conditioning, so be prepared. I'd recommend paying in cash, although I believe they do take credit cards. Also, the atmosphere can't be beat! Lots of high-ons engrossed in the melting cheese of their calzones.

I have been going to gypsies for over 12 years now. Even now that I am no longer in the Berkeley area, I will drive a good 45mins -1 hour just for their Gnocchi in white sauce (usually it is with a cream sauce). I have eaten gnocchi at home, fancy restaurants and even in Venice when I visited and I can honestly say they serve the best ever! I can't really comment on the other food since I am a creature of habit and eat the same thing but every time I take someone there, they love it too. Delish!
Tastier than, say, Pasta Pomodoro. You get a huge bowl of pasta for under $7.

Okay.. This place has not only won the heart of me and my husband but also Our Three friends, My brother, and My father. They all live out of town and tell me all the time how they wish they had a place like Gypsy's around!

If you call to order, and the guy at the other end hangs up on you right after you tell him what you want, don't worry; it's their policy to ignore time-consuming activities such as politeness.

Other than that, for about 6 bucks you good Italian food; the various chicken pastas are probably your best bet, but if you're hungry - and have time to wait - order one of their calzones.

The food is inexpensive and that's what i like, cheap eats. The spaghetti is very flavorful and done to perfection (I am not an expert in this field of determining Italian food but I like what I like).  The house salad was pretty good even though it was kinda boring but it was good.The only down side to this place is no free refills on soda. When I finished my food, I didn't know if I should bus my own plate or just leave it and they would do it for me.

Pros
-Delicious pastas, pizzas, calzones, and gnocchi 
-Indoor seating that, although a bit tight, can accommodate medium groups perfectly
-Relatively fast
-Cheap
-Did I mention that some of the pasta I had from here was way better than $20 plates from "downtown" Italian places
-The bread with the roasted garlic is sooooooo good.


Cons
-A little on the messy side
-The calzones take a while but, hey, at least you know they are made just for you and don't sit under a heating lamp
good food, and great prices.

Great, authentic, Italian food for as cheap as it gets. This is a whole in the wall place, but the food is quality. We ordered a calzone combo with salad and a soda for only $8.95. The calzone was as big as a football! It was so good and filled two of us for the entire day! 
The pastas looked delicious and the salad was fresh. Definitely going back here soon.

Decent cheap italian place in the south asian ghetto. Everything here is ok, it's by no means a bad place but it's not particular great. Basically, I would go if somebody wanted to but I don't seek it out when I visit the southside asian ghetto. It's just not that great italian. 

Best thing I would get here are the calzones, beware they take a while though.

So far I've tried the Lasagna, Crazy Alfredo, and the combo calzone. And all of it is very good. This place is always somewhat busy, and the portions are very generous. One of my favorite places by Cal campus. A must go if your in the area.

Oh Gypsies! You're so lucky to be the most convenient pasta place for Berkeley students to dine in. But alas, your food is too rich! I'm not a health nut, but seriously lay off the pints of cream! Food averages $6-7, while the calzone is a little bit more. The calzone is a little deceiving though... it might seem huge, but in reality, it's about 50% air. It's still quite filling either way.

One more problem... my friends and I have found hair in our food during more than one occasion. We should have learned the first time around right? Overall food is acceptable if you want to try the hairy roulette of luck.

It's been well over a year since I ate at Gypsy's, reason being was last time the food was mediocre and the plates were cracked and old.  Add to that the fact that there are other good pasta stops (i.e. Pasta Bene and Milanesse Cafe), I found no reason to go back.

Fast forward to the present.  Today I happened to be near the Asian Ghetto, and since I had had Thai food two nights ago, I found myself craving for some pasta.  Well behold, I was actually quite satisfied this time!  I ordered the special: ANY menu item, a healthy-portioned salad, and a fountain drink all for $7.99!  Consider that most items range from $6.49-$7.49 alone, add a salad that's worth at least $1.50-$2.00, and a drink...how can a college student say no??  And when I say any menu item, I mean ANY ITEM (if you know Gypsy's calzones, think of the amount of food you could potentially get for $7.99!)

Anyways, this time I ordered the Pollo Con Pesto.  I quite liked the pesto flavor, though the chicken was okay (Gypsy's chicken is always overcooked, maybe to ensure safe food?).  The salad was crisp and refreshing, a simple medley of lettuce, cucumbers, tomatoes, and dressing.  

From past experiences, I've had better luck with seafood pastas at Gypsy's, but from this most recent experience, I can see myself coming back to Gypsy's for a quick, fast pasta fix.

I really have never understood why people think this place is soo good. Yeah its cheap, but they basically use canned sauces. The food is bland and not good at all. They just put a ton of butter and cream in everything and say its delicious.

hands down one of my favorite spots for italian. no frills, just good food, a big portion with garlic bread with a roasted garlic spread on top. go for the bronx tale or crazy alfredo if you're a big meat eater, which i am. and it's dirt cheap! oh how i miss good cheap berkeley food.

I haven't tried everything here, but their chicken/pollo calzone is to die for.  Literally.  Their linguine with clams (in the white butter sauce) is also amazingly good.  Mmmmmm.  They're open late and the food is cheap.  You can't go wrong.

I ordered the frutti di mare with white sauce, and it was really good! I couldn't finish it because the portion was huge, especially for the price (it was $8.15). It was pretty creamy, but not ridiculously drowned in cream sauce. Lots of noodles and seafood (calamari, shrimp, clams, etc.). The food came pretty quickly, but it is not table service. You get a slip with a number, and you go up and get your food. 

Where you get water/drinks is crowded and a little claustrophobic. The restaurant itself got crowded very quickly, so we were lucky we found a table inside. There are quite a few tables indoors, but you can get a table outside as well.
I tried their lasagna today. It was okay. I had to add hot sauce to kick it up a notch. The portion was super huge though, I couldn't even finish it.

Gypsy? Yes, please! My Cal-Bear cousin took us here this weekend and I was very impressed with the large portion, cheap price, and scrumptious flavor of the food here. Had a taste of The Godfather Special which was probably the best white-sauce pasta I've ever had. I'm not a big white sauce fan so that's saying a lot! I ordered the funghi which consisted of a variety of mushrooms, linguine and smoked mozarrella. How's that for unique? The smoked mozarrella overpowered all other flavors which was I absolutely loved! For $7, you can even share a plate with your significant other which I most definitely did!

I actually eat at Gypsy's all the time; not because it's all that, but because it's really one of the only Italian places close to campus on south side.  That and it's super convenient.  I used to get pasta dishes all the time, because honestly that's all I really want out of an Italian place: good pasta.  And it was alright.  Nothing special, but reasonably satisfying for someone like me who finds himself craving Italian on a regular basis.  But I don't know if they've downsized their portions or something but I don't find any of the pasta dishes filling any more.  I've moved on to calzones, which they do a better job with anyway.

Good, not great.  Portions are too small, but I guess that's what you're paying for.

The dishes are very affordable for Italian food.  My sister and I ordered pesto pasta, which was full of flavor, but I wish there were few more strips of chicken.  The bread topped with roasted garlic was good, but it would have been better if it was fully toasted.

Yum, yum, YUM! My first experience at Gypsy's was two years ago when I was craving Italian food and a friend said that I just HAD to try Gypsy's -- and, my god, it was one of the best decisions I've ever made. I've been going back ever since!

My favorite dish is the Godfather's Favorite: chock full of flavor with chicken, Parmigiano cheese, egg (in the sauce, not fried with the pasta), and the salty taste of pancetta makes this pasta absolutely perfect. You won't regret eating this.

A close second is the Crazy Alfredo: chicken, sausage, roasted red peppers, and red wine in an alfredo sauce. The taste of the red wine really comes out and is just delicious.

Gypsy's is located in the "Asian Ghetto", so don't expect a fancy gourmet Italian restaurant setting. Just expect tasty Italian food that will leave you licking the plate and craving more.

Also, a word of advice: they do accept credit card, but they've recently implemented a policy where they will charge an extra fee for credit card purchases, so I suggest bringing cash.

I've been here a couple times, and every time, I've ordered the salad. And no, it's not a dainty little salad. It's in a bowl far larger than my head, filled with so many vegetable goodies. The line is always long, and seating is cramped, but you don't come here for the ambiance. You come here for the tasty, filling food, and you leave satisfied.

First, the owner/cashier is the same one from when I was a student! How's that for consistency! The food is Italian fast food, but for $8 combo, it's still a good deal. Godfather's Favorite is still as I remember it. Delicious and coma inducing.

first and foremost. I heart greasy Italian food. 
second, i love a place that gives you a big lump of garlic on their bread, its like they know me.
This is a quality college food stop that is always pretty busy.
Which is my only knock (but they can't help it) some times its kinda a long wait for the food

ou, and they should serve vino

still a winner though

Chicken Parmesan. mmm

This place is wonderful! They have the best italian food I have had in a while and it is very cheap! They make it extremely quick and there is a deal that comes with a drink and side salad. You definitively get your moneys worth here! The only thing i wish is that they could do something about the angry bums outside scaring people. It is also a little chilly inside at night as they seem to keep the door open but TIP THE STAFF they work very hard and bust out quick delicious italian cuisine in just minutes for your enjoyment despite how busy it is!

ive always loved the chicken pesto, crazy alfredo, or the godfather's favorite.  

it's nothing incredible, but i would say it's better than your average college italian restaurant.  i do like the garlic bread, and they have never been sheisty about the portions.  solid italian food, generally you get your food fast, and always brings a smile to your face.

It's definitely not 5-star by any means.  It's just good food for a decent price.  Two plates cost us about 14 dollars.  And the portions were huge.  
A little greasy, but at least its not olive garden.

This is probably one of my favorite restaurants in all of Berkeley.

Even though it's hard to understand them through their Italian accent (I think?), they make every item on their menu with perfection. And all of the pastas come with a delicious slice of bread.

The price for a meal is around $7, but it is really worth every dollar. And they just got their seats and tables refurnished. :)

I try not to eat here so often...but its so convenient and delicious. I usually get the Crazy alfredo or the godfather special. The portions are great and you can even order your food to go by phone to avoid waiting.
    I eat at gypsies about once a week. They already know what im gonna have before i order, and i appreciate their friendliness despite how busy and crazy it can get.
     It gets 4 stars because its not everything a restaurant could be. ie, no restrooms or places to wash your hands, however The food is great and its a popular spot.

If you want cheap good italian fast food, this is the place. I ordered the lasagna my first time there and was hooked. I visit this place at least a couple times a month. I have yet to be disappointed by any of their menu items. 4 stars for me!

Please don't expect gourmet from a restaurant inside Asian Ghetto (or Durant Food Court, for all you PC people). But still, it's the closest Italian place around campus, so it's a good lunch place.

Don't get the ravioli. It's like, straight from the freezer, like the premade kind you get at Costco. Waste of my moola. 

But stars for cheap prices (everything's under 10 bucks), and they don't skimp at all on the seafood. I really like Godfather's Favorite ^^

But beware the GIANT CHEESE SLUG, aka the calzone. It is oozing out cheese the minute you cut into that monster, and it drips buckets of oil. Seriously. That thing gave me a ginormous stomach ache. It's totally delicious when you eat it, though, and then it stealthily attacks once you're back home, about to start your homework. Sadness. 

Don't go for the pizzas, their cheese sucks too. No one really gets the sandwiches, so I don't either, lol. 

But every pasta entry comes with free garlic bread, and it's delicious. And you can get the meal special that comes with an entree, salad, and soda. SO CHEAP I LOVE IT :D

I ordered the godfather's favorite, the crazy alfredo and chicken gnocchi. I liked the first two - the gnocchi, not so much. 

The food was really cheesy. I wasn't a huge fan of the salads but that's probably just because I don't consider vegetables real food. 

Cheap and decent. I recommend Gypsy's.

Get the calzone or nothing else.  On the past three occasions when I ordered pasta, I was left feeling disappointed.  I just don't taste the sauce in their pasta, only olive oil.  If you really want to eat some good pasta, either make it yourself, or spend $15-$20 at a real Italian restaurant.  In fact, I prefer Milanese Cafe to this place.  

In a nutshell, come to Gypsy's for their CALZONES!

I love Gypsy's. I come here every time I'm visiting friends in Berkeley. The calzones hit the spot ...the saucy and cheezy mix of marinara/ricotta/motz never fails. I also get (can't remember the name) the penne with marinara, meatballs, and italian sausage. Can't be beat for cheap dining and huge portions.

It is good italian cheap food on the corner of the asian ghetto.  Mostly a student hang out.  Very big portions and yet their are big windows of floor to ceiling glass and you look over the grimy neighborhood and homeless people outside the restaurant digging through the garbage for something to eat.  It sort of makes gluttony impossible.  So if you want to be reminded socially why to remain on a diet - dine here.
This is a good, cheap restaurant.  They give you a ton of food, and it is surprisingly decent.  I usually get a calzone, but I like their chicken dishes too.

From the cheap college student perspective, Gypsy's serves it's purpose. This is not delicate Italian cuisine, but hearty, creamy, get-the-most-calories-for-the-least-dollars food. I like the calzones. Huge! And exciting because they come in delightful pink pastry boxes. The restaurant gets packed at meal times. Apparently they have the touchdown discounts on Mondays now, so I imagine that even more students are clamoring for carbs. The only negative thing I remember is waiting quite some time for a calzone to-go one night. My club has used their catering service, and they got our order wrong by giving us less vegetarian pastas than ordered, but we definitely had sufficient food for an inexpensive price.

Cheap heaping portions of pasta! Open late too. I really like this place. I'm an Italian ex NY'er and do occasionally need a late night pasta fix. I've probably eaten here a hundred times over the years.

If you want something yummy and don't regard your cardiovascular system as important, I recommend  the Godfather Favorite. The $1.99 side salad is huge and probably the only healthy thing served here. My only minor negative comment is that the bread could be better ... but then again, I'm getting 2.5 lbs of food for under $10. 

It's not fine dining, but why should it be?  Make that a hundred and one times ... I'm off for a Gypsy's run!

Food is very good for a place on campus. only complaint was a called them up the man was so rude. Wasnt listening to me and just had such a bad attitude. i was trying to organize food for 30 people so thats about 200+ bucks worth of business and he was still obnoxious and rude after all and when i was askig questions he was having none of it so i gave up and i will have to go in there coz i cudnt get anything out of him. il probably go elsewhere though after all that

Most, if not all of the food is about 5.99 a plate. They have a wide variety of Italian food to choose from. They do not discriminate against your meat preferences, because they also have a good amount of choices for you chicken, beef, vegetarian lovers. The portions are huge, so if you are a light eater, I highly suggest you share. 

I ordered this dish that looked like a giant hot pocket, but with a lot of cheese inside. I forget the name of it (what's new, right? hehe) but it was pretty good and fulfilling. I just didn't like all of the cheese that they stuffed in there, which made it really hard to eat sometimes. Aside from the overstuffed cheese, little sliced up meat balls, and a few mushrooms, I really liked the bread. It was delicious. I loved how crispy and non greasy it was. I also liked how the upper layer of the bread was not smeared with cheese like the bottom layer was. 

Overall I liked this place. I loved how it is located near campus, so you get to meet a lot of local Berkeley students. The restaurant itself is small and kind of cramped. But it is a place for college student, so you can't except much more than a box. 

I would most definitely come again because I love pasta and good cheap food. Although I thought service was crap, so I give a boo hiss hiss to the service. 

They close at 12am, I am not sure if it is everyday, but I know for sure it's during the weekend. So it is a good place to eat with your homies for a late dinner.

Yes, the sign outside states that this restaurant is top-rated! However, I think not.
My family and I came by after a Cal tour, and my aunt and I both got some of their pasta. A day after (while I was at Stanford for another tour) I started throwing up, and so did she. We narrowed it down to this restaurant's food because we were the only ones in the family who ate that food, and we were the only ones who were sick days after.
The sad part about this entire experience was that we actually enjoyed the pasta! It was very well cooked and tasted great, so the after-effects were just a huge surprise. Being sick my last day in the Bay was also a huge disappointment! I came to do college tours and visit family, since I live in Jersey, so it's not like I can see everyone whenever I want!
Anyway, maybe it was just an off day for the restaurant (as I see it is rated four stars here on Yelp), but I'm never coming back.

LOVE LOVE LOVE! This place is the best! Great prices and creamy pasta with generous portions. The garlic bread on the side is delicious too. The little piece of garlic they put on it just melts on the bread when you're spreading it. My boyfriend goes for the godfather's favorite and I go for the chicken and broccoli. You can't beat the price for good pasta! After eating here, Olive Garden has no match! This pasta is even better than the expensive restaurants by any fisherman's wharfs I've been to. Everytime I pass by Berkeley on my way into or out of the city and I have time, I always come here!

Gypsy's is definitely one of my favorite places to eat in Berkeley, and I almost always get the same thing. At the beginning, I always got the clam sauce linguine, but I quickly moved onto the pollo con pesto dish. What I like about Gypsy's is they pretty much let you choose any sauce and any pasta, they just don't outright say you can. They mix the pasta right behind the counter, so it's really easy to see when your order will be up. The pollo con pesto is supposed come with linguine, but I always substitute penne because it's my favorite, and oh so good with the pesto. They also give you fresh garlic bread with pieces of fresh garlic on top, mMmm. I wish there was a place like Gypsy's near me, any takeout pasta place that's this good and this decently priced would be amazing. Love it!

Victor's spaghetti is near godly. And I always follow up my pasta with some San Pellegrino, because sparkling fruit juices are the best. Unfortunately, the other pastas are good, but not great, and calzones are nothing new. Haven't tried pizzas and sandwiches, but might give it a spin later on. Atmosphere is like one of those old diners, but Italian-American style. Pretty loud and kind of hectic. Asian ghetto really isn't my thing, but I'd have to say that Gypsy's is definitely the crowning glory of it. Which is kind of disappointing.

Awesome food. The portions are also huge and the prices are great especially their new deal for a pasta, salad, and drink for only 7.99. My parents constantly crave gypsy's and we go every time they're in town.

Great pasta, calzones and pizzas. I've tried the pesto chicken pizza and calzone and they were both excellent. I use to come here all the time when I went to Cal. I still make the trip once in awhile, it's just such a great deal for your money.
I love their garlic bread, since there's an actual clove of roasted garlic on top! My favorite pasta is the shrimp linguine, it comes with mushroom in a yummy garlic wine cream sauce. The calzones here are HUGE and it comes out fresh from the oven.
It's as good as it gets for under 10 bucks =)

Pros: Delicious, quick, easy and cheap. 

Cons: Too many people and not enough room. Not enough busboys clearing plates. 

Definitely a college eatery. Wish I could go there when no one is around to actually enjoy myself and not get bumped in the back by the person sitting behind me.

Get the Pomodoro! Fresh, tomatoey, basil-y, cheesy goodness!!!!
My boyfriend got the Crazy Alfredo and it was rich and creamy! delicious sausage, peppers and chicken. 
Both dishes are equally delicious!
We will come back, but probably order the food to go.

This place is just simply rich. Located in the "asian ghetto", I love coming to this place for a post workout meal. I usually get the pollo con pesto, but sometimes indulge in the godfather's favorite. The pricing is relatively decent for such good quality food. Parking could be a pain in the butt since it's so close to the cal campus, but the food is definitely worth it.

Gypsy's is good if you want a quick fix for dinner and don't want something too high-end or expensive. All the times I've gone here I got the fettucini with broccoli. It was okay-that's all. Nothing amazing but I just wanted something fast and filling anyways. I disliked their bread though. The service is fast, price is good, and food is decent. Not really a super high quality restaurant but that is generally the case with restaurants in the Durant Food Court. Portions are large and I've heard the calzones are great. Next time, I'll try one!
When I'm hungry, I get one of their calzones.  Tasty, filling, good price.

This is seriously the first Italian restaurant I've been to with no waiter service (i.e. my first visit to a trattoria.)

Ordered the Chicken Parmigiano which included spaghetti and bread garnished with a clove of garlic. The chicken was okay; I was kind of looking for more. The spaghetti was a little greasy and definitely out-portioned the chicken. The cheese was a strong mozzarella and distracted from the taste of the meat. The sauce used in this dish was lacking in spice.

I like how they serve their bread, but I think a prepared garlic butter would have had a better finish; nonetheless, the garlic clove made for an interesting after taste.

Maybe I'm not used to this type of restaurant. For now, I'll leave it with two stars and I'll try it again later.

Honestly, five stars doesnt do this place justice and this is coming from one of the most pickiest eaters in the world. Everything here is made from scratch and is authentic. There prices are really cheap too, I would highly recommend people to get the chicken sandwhich if there ballin on a budget its only 5.50 and will mos def fill your stomach up. The best thing to do is order over the phone, make sure you speak clearly otherwise they will get your order wrong.
Great italian food on the cheap + on the go.
I miss the Godfather special! AH! must have!

my first time here, and i'll stick to brevity for reasons that will be revealed.

the staff, ambiance, service, taste and yes, even presentation were all exquisite in ratio to the price paid.

after checking reviews on yelp, i stumbled in..the durant entrance is PULL not push (or was that the other way around..no it was definitely pull to go in and push to get out)..and after a short wait, my pasta was ready. not wanting to disturb the other patrons with my dining demeanor i brought it back home.


by consistent habit, i'm a slow, meticulous eater, but with the appetite i had going in fueled by the taste of what was in front of me, i just could not stop.

it's a good thing i bought enough for a second meal later, but it's not so good that the supply was available.

result: a carbonara combo (which was added on after the initial transaction with no problem) destroyed, with only a few forkfuls of a godfather's favorite, a cup of ice with residual barqs and a quarter can of aranciata for tomorrow. i honestly should not try to move for another ten to thirty minutes.

wow how did you ever escape me all these years, Gypsy's?

bottomline: taste to price ratio and/or quantity to price ratio, both in favor of the formers.

A decent place to go to for Italian food near campus.  The portion sizes are okay, but the dishes tend to be a bit heavy with their oil and sodium level.  Also, there are some exaggerations by other yelpers in saying that the Calzones can feed up to four.  If you're like me - a normal college guy who exercises an average amount, one calzone = one person.

just mehh.....

I am in the middle of my chicken parm sandwich. It was very cheap, coming in at 5.45 I think, but I can taste that the sandwich coasts less. The sauce is bad quality and tastes like canned ragu. Not so good, but fulfilled my need for a chicken parm sub.....Id get it again in a pinch, but think that ill find a cafe makes a better chic parm

This fast food eatery was yummy!  This is my first time here, and for a fast food type restaurant, it is very good and quick.  My friend and I got here before the student lunch rush hour; so we had no problems finding a table to sit after ordering.  I hear lines get super long during lunch rush hour, but they're fast with their numbering system and calling your order number over the intercom.  The staff was super friendly and was patient with me since I never been  here before.  The price was at a very affordable $7-$8.  There is a great variety of pasta to choose from.  Unfortunately, I don't remember the name of the plate I ordered, but it had chicken and spinach.  The sauce really impressed and the chicken was tender and not dry.  If you want super fast Italian food served in a friendly atmosphere all for an affordable price, Gypsy's is the place to go.

This place isn't unique, but it's great if you're craving pasta and just want a cheaper, quick bite to eat.  Located in the "Asian Ghetto" of Berkeley, I highly recommend the Godfather's Favorite, which is basically just chicken alfredo with some garlic bread.  My friends have also ordered the calzones before, which were ginormous, but they didn't seem to taste all that great.  The place as a whole isn't very clean, but based on where it's located, 'nuff said.  I suggest ordering the food to go, especially if you live on campus or nearby.  I visited Berkeley a lot in college and always liked this place because it was open late, so you could make late night food runs there.  Although I like fancy schmancy restaurants, this place is comforting to me, probably because of all the carbs...mmm, carbs!

This place is about one step up from Fazoli's (this reference may not help if you are a California native).  Definitely not bad for the price.  I would like to try the pizza here- my pasta dish (the funghi) was OK but lacking in the funghi department.  The garlic bread was only intriguing because of the roasted garlic- the bread was really quite atrociously white and soggy.  In fact I must say I not-so-secretly like Fazoli's garlic bread better.   But this place did satisfy the I-want-pasta-fast requirement from my husband AND the I-don't-feel-like-cooking requirement from me.

I have been going to this place on and off for the past three years. In general, it is tastly, quick, and the portions are big. 
Although this is true, I got really sick after eating there today. I think either the food was bad or they didnt wash their hands. The place doesnt look too sanitary either.

Cheap and Delicious Italian food? I thought I was dreaming *v*...seriously, I wish I go to UCBerkeley so that I can come here everyday...
okay, so yesterday I went to Berkeley to travel with my friend from Hong Kong, we were starving when we arrived Berkeley, so I yelped and found this place, I thought it would cost at least $13 for a plate, but no, it costs only $6-8 for a plate and for that price, you get a big portion too! OMG, I couldn't believe my eyes, Its so goood...

There were flies in the place, but I don't care, just don't look at them and look at your plate!!!Oh, and they charge you more if you pay card, so bring cash.

I mean it's asian ghetto food. You can't expect five stars.  Food is decent for the price and portions are generous.  I think their salads are pretty decent.  I've heard their calzones are really good, but I've always been too reluctant to try cuz I always go hungry and I'm not willing to wait that long.  Plus the calzones look too big for me to finish.  It's ok for a quick meal, or if you're craving Italian food and need to stay close to school, but if you have the time, it's much more worth it to go to trattoria sicilliano on college.

Cheap price, reasonably good food.  So worth it.  313 reviews and still have 4 star average means something.  Best food at Durant Food Court!  Get their deal of entree+salad+soda for 8.99$ sooo good!  Yum!

After studying in Italy, my pasta radar goes crazy when I see "Trattoria." Noticed this place while enjoying a donut across the street, and came back for dinner. 

It is not the romantic, Lady and the Tramp-style Italian restaurant, but more cafeteria style. If that is what it takes to keep the prices low (low for Berkeley standards!), fine with me! The area seemed clean, the radio was playing Christmas music, and there was pretty quick service.

Extensive menu for venue of its kind, and the $2 green side salad was as big as my entree'. I had gorgonzola penne which was rich and creamy, with tomatoes and spinach. Yummy! My boyfriend had a meatball calzone, which was "sizable, delicious, and employed a multitude of textures." And whatever the textures comment means, it was a good thing.

I cannot wait to visit again! Although it is not like the classic Roman trattoria that holds a special place in my heart, it is definitely on my radar. 

I would actually rate it a 4.5, but we can't half-it.

It's not the most authentic Italian place, but the portions are decent and you might even end up taking some home. It's a good place to sit with friends for a meal between classes. I had the chicken alfredo and it was good. They charge for refills, which I think is a little cheap, but whatever.

Not anything special, but decent Italian food if you are craving fast Italian food. I usually go here when I am really lazy to cook, or want something cheap because their food is quite cheap for the quality of the food. 

I usually get Godfather's Favorite or the Pomorodo with chicken. 

It is definitely better that Pasta Pomorodo. And Cheaper!

I try to avoid coming here unless my friends are adamant about their cravings for greasy Italian food because their food just doesn't tend to sit well on my stomach. Considering that I cook my own Italian food often and it tastes great WITHOUT tons of garlic, salt, and butter, I get terrible headaches and grogginess with Gypsy's. 

You do get a LOT of food with Gypsy's and if you're watching your portions, you can definitely split an entree with a friend or save the rest for leftovers, though they taste rather gross the next day. The biggest meals are definitely the Calzones, which take 15-20 minutes to cook, but actually taste pretty decent and aren't as loaded with all of the salt and fat (not as much at least).

Most of their pastas are so-so, though I favor the Godfather's Favorite for the creamy, savory sauce, even though it kills me from the inside. I haven't tried their pizzas or salads, though nothing really compels me to try them. If you're a student, this might be a fair enough deal to merit eating at every once in a while, but note the glob of butter they put into every pan and ask your heart if that's worth working off every day at the RSF for.

I like this place generally because they serve good food for the price. But I'm giving only 3 stars because I found a strand of "hair" in the pasta I bought today. Yes, hair. I was eating Got father's favorite when I found a fine brownish hair (1 inch long) in it today. Yuck.

Wow, considering the price and location, this place was really good. I got the chicken pesto pasta accidentally instead of the calzone but it was so yummy that I did not regret my mistake. Disgustingly packed with people but worth it.

This place is alright.  From the selection in Berkeley, this definitely is up there as far as the Italian food goes.  But then again, "as far as the Italian food goes" in around campus, well that's not very far.

Essentially this place sells decent Italian food that will satisfy your palate if this is indeed what you're craving.  But in my opinion, some of the dishes from this place are a bit too salty without much taste...
Cheap "Italian" food.  I like the bread they give with each entree.  Not much to say since I'll probably say the same as everyone else.  Just be wary of the homeless.

Compared to the other places in the area, this place most certainly equals good eats for college students. The portions have shrunk a little over the years, but they're still pretty generous. 

The people that work there are friendly, nice, and cool. F/N/C, what else can you ask for?

You know the place is good when just thinking of their food at certain times of the week makes your mouth water, and this place certainly fits that criteria. 

There are many dishes that are good and they'll let you adjust some of the ingredients to taste. Try everything, even the gnocchi and you're sure to find something to come back for... 

Lastly, the 50 cent refill policy? Worse than 50-cent's first video game (I would assume since I never actually bothered to play it). 

Fountain drinks for a fee, at least they have water for free.

I must admit that in the beginning I didn't really like this place.  But I guess it was what I ordered.  But when I got the gypsy's chicken and added broccoli that definitely changed my mind.

This is a great place for pasta and salads.  Although it gets very busy, it is definitely worth it.

The one star is gone since there are only certain things on the menu that I enjoy.

I haven't had Gypsy's in a while so I have been having a strong craving for it.  YUMM!!!!

Three stars is not a diss; it means that this is a staple of the UC Berkeley student's diet. 

A cultural anomaly set in the "Asian Food Ghetto" on the edge of campus, Gypsy's represents one of the only few places in the greater Berkeley area that even serves cuisine by the name "Italian." Truthfully, it's practically just as good as most places around the city, too. I really mean that.

It's quick, and about 7 buckaroos. Oddly, there are usually seats available because most people probably take theirs home in a huge, clear, plastic container to get down with it in the privacy and comfort of their apartments and dorm rooms. 

Aside from the times it kind of smells like puke in here (and who knows why), let it rip. The carbonara was always my go-to dish. I recall that the garlic bread was usually variant in quality, but isn't that the nature of bread itself? What else...they're heavy on the cream and light on the tomatoes here, and a lot of dorky couples frequent the place (really?), along with jocks (duh).

Whatever happens, just remember that an overdose of powdered parm can fix just about anything...when you're still twenty, you lucky kids.

Yay! Love this place! They are open late. They accept cash and credit card. (credit cards they charge a little extra though). Their portions are huge! And their quick! Super close to Cal, so after class I would just hop on over. 

Service:
It's a order and sit down place. All the guys working there pretty friendly. I never had a problem with it. 

Food:
The food is awesome for the price. 
Alfredo Fettuccine with mushroom - Loved it. The pasta was al dente, which I loved because most "fast" place always over cook the pasta. 
Cannoli - Yummy. It fixes my sugar craving. 
Calzone - Super huge! But it's worth it! It can actually be split into two. To share or to have for lunch and dinner! Good bread:toppings ratio =)

Overall:
I would definitely recommend this place.

Really crowded durin meal times

pretty long wait for a calzone in my opinion...

maybe ill try the pasta next time because i heard that's pretty good

The line gets a bit hectic and there is limited space in there. So if you like your space then this place isn't for you. This isn't a dine in place where they come and serve you the food. It's more like a fast food joint where they call your number and you come and pick it up. So the service is like a fast food restaurant, but the quality of the food is like a dine-in restaurant.

I had the crazy alfredo combo which comes with a big salad and coke. The crazy alfredo was delicious. The pasta was cooked perfectly and the sauce was abundant and flavorful. The bread that comes with it is delish too. It was the probably the cheapest Italian food I had ever purchased. All of this was less than $10! 

 If you are on a budget, come here to make your tummy happy. 
So basically it's cheap, great portions, and delicious! =)
