This place is always packed. It's more like a fast food pasta, order the food, find your own seat (or you can sit outside in the ally) and eat. (of course, clean up your tray when you are done). I come here every time I'm craving for pasta.

Price: 5 stars -   I always order the combo (salad, pasta and a drink for $9?? not remember but really cheap)
Taste: ~ 4 stars - 
pasta always come with garlic bread  and it's pretty tasty - 3.5 stars
Pasta is tasty...we have tried different one and none of them really fail so far - 4 stars. I personally love the meat ball with penne....add a bit chili pepper if you can eat spicy...and it just taste like penne arrabiata.. my favorite!!! 

This place'; pasta tastes much better than lots of fancy Italian restaurant. If you want something quick and love pasta ....absolutely recommend.
I would come back on the late nite!

i love gypsy's. ever since I bought my first pollo con pesto back in 1999, i have gone to gypsy's every time i visit berkeley. it's cheap, the portions are great, and it's fast. what more could you ask for?

Cheap, fast, convenient, and delicious enough. I had the carbonara and my friends had the pesto chicken fettuccine and the "bronx tail". The sauces were all heavy and creamy and the prices were great.

Great place to grab a quick bite, service is fast, and the system is quick and simple.

[edit] So I've just tried the Pesto Calzone, how oily is it you ask? Well, it is so oily, that the oil seeped through the pink take-out cardboard box AND the first 10 pages of the New Yorker that I put the box on top of. When I touched the cover of the magazine, the color went onto my finger. 

Now, how GOOD is it you ask? So damn good that I don't mind messing up my New Yorker, or the kitchen counter top I was eating it on :). [/edit]

Maybe my review is biased because I went here for a quick pick-me-up 10 minutes after I was checked out from nearby Alta Bates for a syncope episode, but I thought the carbonara was the bomb! 

And what? Only $7 for a plate that I stretched out to 2 and a half meals? I'm a small girl and pasta fills me up FAST. Me likey.

Good place for students, pretty cheap with big portions. The garlic bread is rather odd. Gnocchi is just OK but the Calzones are huge AND delicious. Always crowded and the lines are somewhat long so get their early.
I came to this place based SOLELY on photos, and man oh man I fell in love. Great price, fresh food, friendly staff, 50 cent refills, this is a foodie's heaven.

Good, affordable italian food.  I've always liked the Godfather, but you better plan a workout the next morning.  Cream sauce with bacon and other good bits, heavy but good.  Calzones are good too.  It's a Berkeley staple.

Pros: Absolutely delicious food. Proper dinner portions. Variety of dishes. Meal prices are proper. 

Cons: Promises a set price if you get a soda and salad with your meal, delivers a different price. Soda is overpriced and you have to pay for a refill. This point just annoys me because the food is decently priced, and soda costs almost nothing to the restaurant, yet they're gouging with the drink. Why? Let me have a refill. 

 I've eaten here maybe 10 times now. The atmosphere isn't the best for a "quiet evening" rather it's more a socializing spot I almost always end up talking to someone.

The food here is really cheap and huge, but other than that.... I'd tried it three times (fair enough right?), the pasta is oily, really creamy, but not much flavor at all. The side garlic bread is ok. Their calzone is much better, yet it's SUPER oily!!! once I cut it open I can see all the oil flowing out... I guess for a hungry student with a tight budget, this is the place, but I would not go there anymore...

Came here during an MUN conference about 3 months ago. Many of my friends had pastas and said it was good. I for one had the chicken and spinach calzone. It was bomb!!! In my opinion it was a larger and more tastier Hot Pocket. lol!!!

A must go!!!=)
I had the calzone here, which was pretty decent. Cheap, large portions, greasy... what more could a college student want?
Any of their pasta is good and the garlic bread is pretty special.
Reasonable price with fantastic food

I used to eat here occasionally simply because it was the only cheap quick place right near campus when I was sick of Thai Basil. I would have rated it "meh" 2 stars back then, the food is not that great its just a bunch of pasta for real cheap because pasta is cheap.

Then one time I bought it and it smelt like PUKE and tasted nearly as bad. I felt sick to my stomach, showed it to my boyfriend and he agreed that it smelt like puke and tasted disgusting. I have never eaten there since and everytime I walk by I am sick to my stomach.

Wow, this place is good. Walk in, order what you want, pick it up in about 5 minutes. Eat here or take it Togo, which ever you want. It's cheap, fast, and best of all good. No matter what you order, it seems to be good!!

I can't vouch for it's authenticity, but I just know it's fantastic pasta for a great price. I've been to far more expensive places, but still find myself preferring Gypsy's pasta dishes.

Service is of the lunch-counter variety with order numbers being called out, which is fine by me. As chaotic as the kitchen looks, they've never messed up my order or skipped me on accident.

The only minor quibble I'd have about the place is the lighting. Seems like the food's good enough that it deserves something better than the same generic fluorescent ceiling lights that you'd find in a classroom on campus.

I had the meatball sandwich for lunch. My first warning was no peppers/pepperoncini . How can I consume a meatball sandwich without peppers? How can a restaurant serve a meatball sandwich without peppers? They obviously aren't taking it seriously.

The bread was fine, the sauce was fine. My problem was with the meatballs. Rubbery and not meaty and not so flavorful. Too much breading and not enough ground pork or spices in the mixture. 

I'll go back once to try a pasta dish but I recommend that you avoid any dish with meatballs.

On an on-going quest for great italian food in east bay, we stumbled accross this place. Since, we've been back several times with the same deliciously brilliant experience. GIANT portions at very, very reasonable prices. The calzone can easily fill two people, & I believe the cost is somewhere between $6-8 dollars. I've had a few of the pastas, all delicious and reasonable - they even come with a large slice of garlic toast. There is an alright selection of beverages as well. The staff is friendly enough, and hey - you've got the best donut place of all right next door!

Drawbacks, parking in this area is difficult & they always keep the place 10 degrees colder than outside. Still, easily a 5-star, one dollar sign joint.

Foods pretty good....seriously good prices
Chicken pesto calzone ( I added mushrooms) was the size of my frikin head! It was pretty good...a little too much ricotta in ,ine though...it was splurging out of each bite
Crazy alfredo-pretty good...
We both got the combos for it...add salad (which the skimped on the dressing) and drink
Service wasn't that great..I got togo but he definitely wasn't friendly at all..when I called or came in..

Their calzones are gigantic, food-coma inducing masses of carbs and butter and deliciousness... one of these could easily last you two-three meals.

Aside from the calzones I only remember getting the Bronx's Tale (I may have forgotten the name...) Yum! Overall the food is decent, though with so much butter how could you go wrong?

Definitely a favorite of all students here. If you're looking for delicious food and a reasonable price, come here. Just watch yourself when you head over there because there might be a long line, and it takes time to make good pasta. So be willing to wait if the situation calls for it.
The portions are awesome relative to the price, except the angel hair pasta dishes can be a little unsatisfying since they don't fill you up that much. 
The alfredo pastas here is amazing. 
And the calzones are so big they alone can cause a food coma. 
I think the best pasta 'ive had is the godfather's favorite.

How can you NOT give a 5 star rating for Gypsy's on Durant?!

REMEMBER, this is a fast food italian "joint" but with great taste.  It's cheap, filling (typically take some home), and very good.  You will typically wait for about 5-10 mins for the food and many of the items on the menu are very good.

I always get the Godfather and the Bronx Tale and the Calzone's are pretty darn good as well.  The only bad thing is after years of going here (pre-college through post), I cannot find a bathroom to wash my hands!  Oh, ask for an extra slice of garlic bread, it's worth it.
my berkeley buddies took me there and i loved the food tremendously. i recommend eating outside.

Gypsy's is definitely one of the better restaurants of Asian Ghetto, and even takes card.  I would have to give 3.5 stars for the food, but .5 extra star for the convenience of the place.  It's definitely mentioning the convenience of this place and here's why:

For any Berkeley student, Asian Ghetto is something of a social hub, it's like the go to place for after events with clubs, between classes, a pre meal to the night, or even a post meal to end the night.  

The food isn't particularly great at Asian Ghetto, ESPECIALLY if you don't have cash, youre limited to panchos, steves BBQ, mandarin garden, sushi house and the gyros place no one really goes to.  These places list above...arent too good of a choice for their respective ethnic food, (iono about the gyros place tho, since ive never been =P).  

But Gypsys serves as a save haven for those who don't have cash, which for some reason college kids dont like to carry around!  

The pasta is pretty decent and reasonably priced, but you do have to get over the fact of all the greasiness with pastas with creamier sauces.  I would recommend the Gypsy's Chicken for any first timers, it's the pretty safe dish to go. The more tomato based sauces are definitely not as heavy (less grease), if you're looking for a lighter pasta.   

Their calzones are also pretty good!  They're also pretty huge and worth the price.  These come with a good amount of cheese, and a lot of grease...but the meat to cheese ratio is a little low.  I usually go for the pesto and the sicillian.  The calzones do take a little while to cook, so one thing you can do is call in about 15 minutes ahead of time to get your order in, and it'll be about ready by the time you get there =P

And bread fans, you can order extra garlic bread for a quarter each, I always get at least one extra one  :)

HUGE servings of fantastic, hot, flavorful pasta. Very fast service (though even so they get very crowded with undergrads at lunch time) and the cooks are willing to customize a little; if you're jonesing for a pink sauce or something, just ask.

Perfect "I had a bad morning, I'm going to indulge in some comfort food" choice, particularly if you go a little before or after the main rush.
Not bad for the Southside food ghetto. It's open late, and the pastas are cheap and filling.

Last night a friend and I were craving for a good calzone. Since we were so hungry and we were by "Gypsy's Trattoria Italiano" we decided to try it. The place was so crowded and noisy we have to wait to get the a table.We asked for the calzone SICILIA for just $5.69 and the calzone COMBO for $6.29 which was yummy!. we also got the chichen piccata and it was also great it was really tasty and good seasoned. This is not a fancy place I think next time I'll call ahead for take out because it was a long waiting and for the service it's not bad but nothing exciting so my  3 stars are just for the food but definitely I'm coming back because the food it's tasty and cheap It's just a deal!!

For years I passed by this place on my way to the stadium for practice, and for years I would drool over their calzones! I never had the guts to try one until my last year at Berkeley...let me tell you...it is DELICIOUS and A LOT of food. I wish I had gotten it earlier but I always resorted to pasta after a night out. 

Keep in mind this is located right at the front of the "asian ghetto" so it is not the cleanest, well decorated, or the most "first" date worthy place (unless both of you are broke college students)...Go here you won't regret it (at least I didn't).

There are some times I just crave some cheap give-me-a-tummy-ache mediocre pasta, and when that happens, I come to Gypsy's. I really do like the food, though we've all had better pasta, pizza and salads, and in fact, could probably make it better. However, nothing beats warm creamy pasta and bread with a whole clove of garlic at 11 at night. Pasta and cream sauce is one of my comfort foods, so sometimes I don't want my comfort food at a fancy Italian restaurant at a fancy restaurant price. I want it cheap, late at night, and guaranteed to make my dairy intolerance act up.

Cheap, dirty Italian food that is perfect for a cash-strapped, hungry student on the go.  Compared to a "fine-dining" Italian restaurant, they are obviously not very good, but you get what you expect! Don't go here expecting good service or great food. My only complaint is the calzones are often cold in the center.

Gypsy's was my favorite restaurant during undergrad....you gotta go for the cream sauces. The tortellini gorgonzola is *****!! I got other things that were good but once I got that I stopped getting other things. Good gnocchi and calzones. It's cheap, fast, easy to sneak free fountain soda in the water cups, and the semi-cranky guy who I can only assume is the owner has been there every single time I've gone. It's no hot date spot but if you're sick of dorm food it's a lifesaver. I'd suggest avoiding ordering food to go because I did once and my hot pasta melted right through the plastic box.

These guys are rude. I will never eat here. I was in the middle of ordering over the phone. At the end I changed the first thing I ordered  and the guy got attitude with me telling me it was already being made. Well now my already being made food will sit there cause I ordered from somewhere else. Learn some manners.

So. I really come here for one thing. And one thing only.
The godfather's favorite.

There is nothing that needs to be said about it. And when you try it, you'll understand why.

Once I got a combo calzone. I was also speechless.

Been coming here forever. besides the God Fathers Favorite, and the Gypsy Chicken the best thing on the menu at the moment is the Caesar Chicken salad with Jumbo shrimp added. Its the best healthy plate they have in my book. 

Be smart and call it in before you head there so you don't have to wait forever

I've heard a lot of this place even before I went to Cal. I've never been able to go until tonight and boy was I definitely glad that I had Gypsy's instead of Cal's Late Night. 

I got chicken with pesto; it was fantastic except for the oil -- there was a lot of it. In the box, it greased up the bag and some of the napkins. Despite that, it was still pretty good though. I don't see myself eating there because it's really awkward. You have people with their iPods with a book in front of them (it is Cal after all), people begging for money and staring at you enviously (again it's Berkeley), and you're all cramped up against other people. You should definitely come here (and get it to go) for a late night Italian craving; it's awesome when everything is under $7 not counting the tax.

Good price and Food Taste great.

Pasta and Calzone was tasteful. Good menu list.

All I have to say here is Lemon Chicken Salad and Lasagne.  You can finish your meal off with a Honey Dew bubble tea at the chinese restaurant 2 doors down.

Cheap and good. 

If you're on Telegraph and Durant.


Then go.
I love this place! Best gnocchi in town!! They also give you amazing bread with real roasted garlic on it...so good! They say they only take cash but they have a debit machine I have used it!

OMG!!!!! The pesto calzone was so huge I shared it with a friend but so delicious I wish I had been selfish and ate the whole thing. The calzones are like football size or bigger (no joke) perfect amount of pesto and cheese.

the ambiance was cute and quiet. great place to go with friends or family. Im deffinately taking my BF there for a calzone. He will have a foodgasm for sure. The calzone was about $6 and was ENORMOUS!!!! 

I want one right now!!!

and the server dudes were pretty awesome!!

Cheap Italian food that comes out quickly. My friend suggested the restaurant as a good place to eat lunch. I ordered the seafood pasta in a marinara sauce. Eh, the seafood was overcooked. The marina sauce overpowered the pasta. 

I didn't like the food too much. However if you need to get away from dining common grub, then you can come here to eat. I like how the portions are generous, plus you get a piece of garlic bread!

Excellent place for a tasty platter at great price.  I am a huge fan of their calzones, and i love their pasta dishes.  You can ask for almost anything on your calzone or pasta.  I usually get the pollo calzone and add pineapple, and when I get a pasta dish I add eggplant.  What makes this place so great is how inexpensive it is.  6-8 bucks for a great plate of food that will leave you satisfied.

When you're in the mood for greasy, filling Italian food, Gypsy's doesn't disappoint! 

I love their Carbonara! But it's super cheesy/heavy, so go there with an appetite! And their pizzas are yummy as well! (But take longer due to the bake time) 
They also have good standard salads if you don't feel like overloading on carbs/cream, but they give you a lot of dressing. I personally am not a huge fan of the calzones. The huge size is definitely impressive (but keep in mind a lot of it's air), and they're fun to eat, but taste-wise I wasn't that impressed.

Conveniently located, and the price point is perfect for college students!

I think that maybe the most popular off-campus eatery (at least off of Telegraph) deserves an honest write-up, and I have to say that Gypsy's is probably so well-regarded because of the lack of accessible Italian food in the area, and not because the food is really that good (as far as Italian food goes, at least). Gypsy's is surrounded by hot dogs & hamburgers, mediocre Mexican, and terrible Chinese & Southeast Asian places. 

Waking up every day knowing you are going to eat in a dining common two or three times before you go to sleep that night is a frightening prospect, and I can see why people flock to Gypsy's. It's cheap, the portions are huge, and it's really pretty satisfying. But really, it is pretty half-assed as far as Italian goes. The pasta is often greasy and usually cooked way beyond al dente (they have it pre-cooked in a plastic container and they throw it back in the water when you order it), and the pizza isn't much better than delivery. Still, given your options as a student, Gypsy's is a good choice.

5 stars, why?  Simple.  It's open late, it's cheap and their pasta is a little better than above average.  The food isn't exactly 5 star quality, but for the price you pay, it certainly is.  It's a great alternative to the "food" they serve in the dorms.

Gypsy's is one of the reasons why I miss Berkeley so much.  Where else can you find pasta this good for this cheap?  Sometimes when I'm daydreaming at work my mouth starts to drool because I start thinking about the godfather's special.  Then my heart starts racing because it gets scared when it hears I want the godfather's.  Yes, they do in fact toss in at least half a stick of butter for every dish, I've seen them do it...but, if you're eating here, you (most likely) still have a metabolism that can fend off this minor inconvenience.  Do yourself a favor and eat here as often as possible because I guarantee that you will miss it when you finally have to grow up and leave Berk.

I consider this the best pasta place in Berkeley.  It is close to the UC campus and can get quite crowded but their food has never disappointed me.  My usual is fettuccini alfredo which comes with mushrooms and sometimes I'll add some meatballs which come chopped up as well.  Every pasta dish comes with bread with real cloves of roasted garlic which is yummy.  Their calzones are huge (so huge that when you get it to go they have to put it in one of those pink boxes that are made for a dozen donuts).  I've only tried their pizza once and it was good but I prefer their pasta or calzones.  They also make your order quickly so that the most I've waited was about 15 minutes when the line was nearly out the door.  Parking in the area can be sparse but so is the case for pretty much everywhere in Berkeley.  The prices aren't too bad either since their main target are college kids ($7-12 if my memory is correct).

I've been coming to this place since for roughly 11 years. I haven't been back in probably 2-3, but decided on a whim tonight to get the best $6 pasta in the bay area. Guy still remembered me and joked about how he will be there for the rest of his life. 

If you've been here before you know what it is; You're sad when they're out of bread, and you've tried something from every corner of the menu. If you haven't been here before, feel free and try something off every corner of the menu. Hella sure I saw Opio from Souls of Mischief tonight too (and you know he did it right and got a donut across the way while waiting for his pasta [see my review of Kingpin for more info]). Five stars for cheap, delicious Italian food. Because cheap, delicious, and Italian are not words that are juxtaposed often enough.
We come here for the delicious Fruiti de Mari (seafood pasta with shrimp, mussel, clams and calamari).  Big portions for a small price.

The food here is amazing. If I am in Berkley I try to come here for lunch. 

It is the only place where you can get Italian food at a cheap price. Not to mention it tastes great.

The fettuccine pesto is amazing. A must try.

If you like large quantities of butter, you'll love Gypsy's! There is at least one whole stick of butter in each creamy sauce dish. I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw them preparing their alfredo or gnocchi. Top it off with the heavy cream itself and you have the perfect recipe for feeling like crap for the remainder of the day. I was curious about their salads so I ordered a chicken caesar salad only to watch them warm up the chicken with half a stick of butter too! I wouldn't be surprised if they made their own dressing with...can you guess? BUTTER. Sure, everyone says their food is delicious, which it is. But as long as you don't think about what you're eating, you'll have a great experience. I recommend their calzones. While they take a little extra time, it's definitely worth the wait.
best italian you can get for the price and the portions are very filling. i usually dont try anything new but when i do im always satified.

This is an awesome hole in the wall spot perfect for students as far as pricing. The food is great; from pasta dishes to pizza or even your salad, you will get nothing but the best tasting , greasy food here.My favorite dish is the Chicken Gnoccho. With alfredo sauce, chicken and gnoccho pasta, it also comes with a side of french bread and garlic. If you're looking to sit down for a quick bite to eat this is the place. It also is conveniently located near telegraph ave so you can soak up your surroundings right after you eat. Only turn off is  that it looks like a fastfood joint.

Um... what? I always prided myself on being a cheap date, because I could eat anything and it'll all taste the same to me. That is, until I came here.

I REALLY don't know why there's so much hype for this place. Maybe because it was cheap ($7.50?) Two stars for the cheap price.

I had the Chicken Gnocchi. Hard and dry - I had to dip it into the sauce to eat it, which I'm sure was store-bought. The pasta, unlike the pasta that I had from an earlier Italian restaurant in SFO, was too thick and starchy. The bread had some weird garlic paste on it that left an unpleasant aftertaste in my mouth. My friend ordered the spaghetti and meatballs - she was better than me. She at least finished the pasta, but said that the meatballs tasted weird and weren't even warm enough. 

Did we just have an unpleasant experience? Maybe. Maybe I just need to try it once more, but as for now... Gypsy's Trattoria ItaliaNO.

After graduation, Gypsy's pasta is what I missed most in Berkeley. And this statement is also true to many of my friends, so we decided to go and had lunch there. It was so comforting and nostalgic.

Like many good eats in Berkeley,  it is cheap. You could see the kitchen and see how they prepared it. They put wine in the sauce, and probably that's why their food smelled so good. I ordered Chicken Gnocchi, which was the best gnocchi I've ever had. Not a lot of people like gnocchi, but it is my favorite dish there. They also have a pasta in red sauce, with salmon and capers. That is my other favorite. Oh yes, their roasted garlic toast that comes with every dish.

I love restaurant that you can just pick any thing off the menu randomly and they still came out delicious. That is exactly what Gypsy's is. I am missing it already.

The food is definitely heavy and unhealthy, but very delicious. The restaurant gives you a very generous amount of food, and you always leave full and happy. The price is also very, very good for the amount of tasty food that they give you. I always try to go to Gypsy's when I'm in the area.

Love the 2 dollar side salad that comes with a dish! Not a fantastic salad, but pretty big and filling especially if you're sharing the dish with a friend. 

Anything not tomato-based is done strictly Paula Deen style:  all butter all the time. Chicken parmesean is pretty good, the chicken tends to get a little soggy though because it's absolutely covered with melted cheese. 

Again, if you're going to get the calzone, which I highly recommend, but don't want to wait around awkwardly standing next to the drink machine, just call ahead and pick it up. Chances are you'll wait around a few minutes anyway.

Extra star for convenience sake! 

If you're in the Asian Ghetto, this is a pretty safe bet. Avoid it during peak dinner/lunch hours as the line can get pretty fatty.

I wonder how many hours the owner works there, I see him everytime in his knitted sweater and glasses despite how stuffy and hot it gets in the back kitchen. The man must have no sweat glands.

Love their specials. Accepts credit.

Large portions, served with bread and garlic. Don't order when it's busy--long wait and the quality of the food could be bad (not flavorful and overcooked pasta).

Get the godfather's favorite, it's good.  A bunch of goodies packed into a togo plastic package.  It's different in a good way.  Apparently recommended by many Berkeley students.  It's hard to explain besides that it's loaded with fatty goodness, a variety of meats and italian bacon?, and a big piece of garlic bread.  If you're on a diet, I'd probably stay away from this one, cause you'll probably get hooked.  It's a little on the oily side too, as expected.

Funny thing was that the cashier asked if we wanted more bread.  Lol?  Free shit?  Hell yea we'll take some.

This is THE BEST italian takeout place in the bay. I love the Calzones, but the Gypsy's Chicken and the Linguine Clams are my favorites. They're also really cheap AND open late. So what more could you ask for? If you're in Berkeley, do NOT miss out on this place!

Mmm...cheap pasta.  
Times are hard.  Gypsy's answered the call.

Really great Italian food served!  Can't wait to try more new dishes but the classics always hit home for me at a good price.  If you haven't been to Gypsy's and go to Cal, GO!   After reading this and the list of usuals, go to Gypsy's...It is good for your soul. :))  

Usuals:

~ Pollo con Pesto
~ Lemon Chicken Salad w/ Italian Dressing
~ Linguini with Clams and red sauce. (they also have white sauce, too)
~ Gnocchi with gorgonzola sauce and chicken (my bf's usual but I always nibble on his first, then my plate. haha)

the best place in Berkeley period.
I could not have survived in berkeley without this place.
I would strangle the last of endangered pandas to eat Gypsy's food.

LOVE the Gypsy's Chicken, along with their side of garlic bread. Their other plates are yummy too.



All I gotta say is BOMB.

One word: CALZONE

I love getting the Sicilia Calzone when I go to Gypsy's. Not only is it the biggest Calzone I have ever seen, but it is quite tasty (I can finish one in about 5-ish minutes...). Not to mention, if you get it to go, everyone will think you are carrying a dozen donuts or a cake, since they come in those boxes!

Their dishes are cheap compared to many other Italian food places around the area, and you get good portions for the price. They also accept credit cards and have good priced combos. I've had some of their other plates like lasagna and fettucine alfredo, and they are quite delicious and rich if you like that taste.
The portions for the pasta here is pretty good. Got one of their alfredo sauce pastas and it was wayy too much sauce. Actually made me sick after eating a few bites.
This place deserves a 5 star.  If you don't give it a 5 star, you sir (maam) are a food snob.  Is that possible?  As I have been told and repeatedly reminded by my family that I am the food snob!
Fettucini Alfredo is soooooooo grub!  Words cant even describe.  Hella good, cheap eats.

Sure, they can cook pasta.  Yet what use is pasta when the pasta sauce is thin and wrong?  I've never had a pasta sauce here that felt like it did what it was meant to do.  And the garlic tastes merely like toasted bread, nothing more.  I never understood why this joint was usually filled until I realized that at the time it was the only Italian restaurant anywhere near campus.

Cheap plates & generous portions! 
The combination calzones & fruti di mari was delicious! 
Great flavors, plenty of seafood in the fruti di mari for $8!!
The only reason people eat here is because there are no good, cheap pasta options nearby.  If you are a lazy, broke, college student craving pasta, then maybe go here; otherwise, definitely skip it.

PESTO CALZONE IS THE BEST!!!!!!!! 
I haven't had any other item here, but based on the pesto calzone 5 stars!!!!! It's that flippin good!!!!!!!!!

A good number of people I talk to think that eating at the Asian Ghetto is, let's say, undesirable, to put it nicely.  But I don't know what they are talking about.  Gypsy's is a great place to eat, and one that I frequent when going to the Asian Ghetto, or whenever I'm in Berkeley now that I've graduated.  It's a pretty good price - could get lunch or dinner cheaper at some places, but I think it's pretty good amount for the price.  I recommend one of the calzone, one of the sandwiches, or the GodFather's Favorite.

The Honest Truth:
Quantities are good.  Calzones are pretty big! Godfather's favorite is my favorite.  it's a little on the heavier side (lots of cream and butter).  One of the few places that accepts credit card (slightly more expensive).  Good to cater as well.  Solid Asian ghetto option.

The Details:
This was the first place that I ate at in Berkeley and it was delicious.  Part of the deliciousness was due to the allure of coming to Berkeley, but in my four years here, it is still a good go to option in the Asian ghetto area.  Whenever I have a friend or new freshman that is coming to Berkeley, I will take them here and they always seem to like it.  Most of their food is pretty good.  I'm usually full and satisfied after eating it.  Their dishes tend to be really heavy so eat it while its hot or else it'll solidify and become unappetizing.  When I'm hungry, I get the calzones.  They're BIG although they seem to have gotten a little smaller in the past couple years.  But I've never been hungry after eating one of those.  Service is usually pretty fast, although the calzones can take a little longer.  A couple times, I've also catered from here for club banquets.  The prices are reasonable and its worked out well every time (plenty of leftovers).  Gypsy's is a staple of Berkeley and its continued to keep up its quality for the most part over my four years here.

When I used to live in Berkeley I would eat here at least once a week. I love pastas! They have unique dishes as well as traditional ones. Their prices are great. You can get a delicious pasta for less than seven dollars. You will not find that somewhere else. I recommend to try all their menu. I haven't had a dish I did not like. Now that I left Berkeley I still go back and have gypsy's if i'm the mood for Italian. It is a small restaurant so sometimes it gets packed and you may have trouble finding seating. But it's worth it because their dishes are tasty!

Not really a fan of Gypsy's. I find that their pastas are usually over cooked and the sauces aren't that tasty. I've personally made some better Italian dishes in my own home.

On top of that, pizza is pizza and this is something Gypsy's doesn't do well. If you're going to use the excuse that its a quick place for college kids to eat, then you could easily head down the block and be smack dab in the middle of two other pizza places where you can grab a slice that tastes better for much cheaper.

If you're looking for a quick, cheap meal that doesn't excite your taste buds, then sure, Gypsy's is for you. Then again, why do that when for an extra couple bucks you could get a much better Italian meal at your local Olive Garden? Catch my drift?

This is...hands down...the greatest restaurant ever.  I graduated from Cal a year ago and I still think about this place on almost a daily basis.

Anyone giving this place a lower rating than a 5 should be taken out back (of where, I don't know) and shot.

Everything is good, but the Godfather's Favorite is other-worldly!

so good! their alfredo was amazing!
they give great amount, and it doesn't take too long for them to cook the food. 
it's self service.

Gypsy's... The only reason why I like this place is because its pretty cheap and Borat is a big fan of gypsies. I guess it's cool because you can get a pasta, drink, and a salad for $8. However, this stuff is heavy and it makes you feel heavy. I usually eat whatever and would be able to go to the gym and play just fine... But if I'm going to eat Gypsy's, I very much expect my day to end with Gypsy's. (With some time on the toilet)

The food is just like any other pasta except covered in cancer and death and these cheap-os don't even offer free refills. So that can definitely ruin the restaurant experience. But if you want to eat Gypsy's just so you can appreciate Milanese Caffe go and give this an eat. Then be prepared to walk a couple extra blocks to eat even more delicious pasta.

Calzones pretty fun, cool, and big. Eat it!

the Great,
GumZ
Cheap, and REALLY good Frutti di Mare. The calzone and some pesto dish my friends got didn't seem that great though.

I have a love/hate relationship with Gypsy's. I have yet to find a pasta dish I am crazy about. And I love Italian food. But I am also picky.. you can ask my friends.. they think I am an alien. I dislike Alfredo and pesto sauces so it isn't their fault at all. I blame my mother and her crappy cooking from the packet for that. Sorry Mum. The calzones are really good or crappy depending on the day. I've had ones where I ate it all in one serving just wanting more because it was so good, and others where it was super runny and messy and non-edible. But for the price and the hours.. I would definitely suggest Gypsy's.

Cheap, decent and quick, not much more you can ask for at college and that price. I usually got the spaghetti with a side of garlic bread, the portions are pretty large, I don't remember finishing up except once or twice, definitely one of the better places in the Asian Ghetto, my other favorite is Thai Basil.

The food here is surprisingly good. You can't tell by the way it looks, and the long line just might indicate that college students can't afford to eat anything else, but that's not the case.

Large portions, and really good tasting pasta. I've had like 4 different dishes, and they were all really good. Add to that the low price of about $6 - $8 for a plate, (which beats paying $17 - $19 at some trendy little Italian place), and it makes this place a winner
Some of the best Italiano food I have ever eaten moto bene

Gypsy's gets 3 stars for me because everything that I used to order, I coulda make at home but I was to lazy to do so. The prices however, are good to me... I've never left paying over 7 dollars, unless I was treating. It does get ridiculously crowded at certain times though.

NOTE... if Berkeley is having a home track meet or a meet in the area, you will see ALL of the track athletes there filling up on those cheap carbs.

Not a bad place for lunch. Came here and got the chicken option. They give you plenty of food for the price, and its pretty fast. If you want to sit inside, the seating will be limited, as many individuals take up 4 seats by themselves.

1 word. calzone. 

I don't like their cream-based pasta sauces (which is about half their menu) where the pasta is stuck together with glops of cream, butter, and cheese, and I don't think much about their seafood dishes. I do, however, love their calzones (as big as a small child). The crust is chewy and slightly sweet, the filling (i usually get chicken) is plentiful and tasty - lots of cheese, meat, sauce, and onions. It takes 15-20 minutes to bake, so I call ahead as I'm heading over there and the golden-brown, shiny-topped calzone is ready for me when I arrive. I can't help but sigh with pleasure whenever I crack into my calzone - gooey mozzarella, warm tomato sauce....hmm... Did I mention it will easily feed 2 people and cost under $6? 

their chicken masala is pretty good as well, and my friend is in love with the chicken piccata. I've heard good things about their pizza as well, so maybe next time I'll get that....or not - the calzone will always be calling.
Great place to come if you're drunk, hungover, or depressed about schoolwork and want to kill yourself with cheese. Standard Berkeley campus fare: cheap, fast, HUGE, and satisfying.

From the outside Gypsy's never appealed to me, but I went one day for a work thing. We were a large party, but they were really fast in gettin gour food out to us. I'm not a fan of the whole line-up-to-order-then-go-pick-up-your-food scene, but a lot of places near UCB are like that, so whatcha gonna do?
The chicken gnocchi is okay. I usually have to trek over to Giovanni's for some, but the dish at Gypsy's is not bad.
Italian food on campus! Tastes so good! And great prices! ; ))  the only bad thing: sometimes the guy who rings me up has an attitude.

I was really debating whether or not to eat here but I'm glad I did.  Ended up ordering a godfather's special with a salad and beverage.  For just over 8 bucks it's a deal I can't really complain about.  The pasta was great, although I didn't find the portion size to be as big as everyone says it is.  The caesar salad complimented the pasta very well.  I think I'll try one of their pizzas next time!

Great menu with a wide variety of foods. Their calzones look humongous but it's mainly air inside - not that that's a bad thing. It's still more than enough to fill you. Most of their dishes are pretty heavy and filling. Their garlic bread is great because they actually give you real garlic to spread. It somehow feels more authentic. I've tried and liked their spaghetti with meatballs and lasagna. LOVE lasagna. their salad is ok but why buy salad when there are so many other things to get! Prices are cheap, considering the portions are so large and the taste is great. Although it seems like it would be hard to get seating, the workers clean tables amazingly fast. I like their large glasses for water because you don't have to get up and refill them too often. It's kind of awkward to stand around waiting for your order because it's pretty cramped but what else can you do.

I've been here a few times over the past... 10 years. hahahah jk, maybe like 5-6 years.
i only get the pasta... and most of the time its been quick, easy and affordable. The last time i went, I had the God Father's Favorite... OH EM GEE. pancetta... drooooooool. it was very yummy.. very high in calorie and fat lol and probably sodium! but it's not something you should have every single day anyways.

It's a pretty simple process. You go to the front to order, grab a table and claim your territory, then grab your food when your number is called, then DIG IN! 

The dishes range from  7~10 bucks. The portions are generous. It's made to order. there are alot of varieties.

you can get a "combo deal" which means adding soda and salad. It's not too bad of a deal if you want to get your veggie fix and carbonation rush. lol

It's usually pretty packed here, but it looked like most people got food to go.

Only thing I hate is the parking, it's crazy trying to find it around this area!! takes foreverrrr!!
Also, i think they charge you like 50 cents when you use your credit/debit card.. so bring cash!!

Overall, this is my go to alternative is I just don't feel like having Pasta Bene...I will be back Gypsy!! =]
The food is really greasy but if you're looking for a carb bomb this is the place to go. The service is relatively quick and it is the only place to get Italian food on telegraph.

I love Italian food. I love cheap, good tasting Italian food. Hence, I LOVE GYPSY'S. Honestly, italian places are not cheap. They're always higher end sit ins, and it doesn't taste all that great. Gypsy's does it right. Generous portions for a cheap price!!!!

The Crazy alfredo is awesome. Chicken, sausage, red bell peppers in a cream sauce?

And their calzones?!! It's as big as the big girl's face who's eating one next to me. It's HUGE! Nice, warm, crispy on the outside, soft and chewy on the inside bread, loaded with melted cheese, and tomato sauce?! 

BOOM BAM.

Definately college-oriented. I'll write a quick review her and mention that the Calzones, which I used to love and which many reviewers rave about, are much much smaller now and the same 7 bucks. I had it for lunch earlier and vowed not to order that again. In contrast, their meatball sandwich is still big, filling, and fattening.

RIP large Calzone.

This is a cozy little Italian place near the UC Berkeley campus. I've heard much hype about here while I visited Berkeley so I made sure to eat here for lunch before I left. Their menu had some pretty standard pastas, but they were well known for their football sized calzones. My friends said the calzones were pretty good, but I was in the mood for pasta instead. I ordered the special of the day, which was tomato cream pasta with scallops and shrimp.

The workers there were very nice and polite while I figured out what to order. Food came out pretty quickly, which was a plus. When I dug in though, I found that the pasta's shrimp and scallops were rubbery and tough :( I was quite sad because... they were supposed to be the highlight of the dish! But I could barely even chew the scallops let alone swallow it. Sadly, the shrimps were the same and I had to leave them behind in the plate. The pasta itself was very filling and well seasoned. It's just such a pity that the scallops and shrimp were too tough to eat.

But having a cheap Italian restaurant near campus means a cheap and filling lunch at your disposal! Cal kids, you are lucky.

yeah, Gypsy's pasta is better than Pasta Pomodoro, Macaroni Grill, and other so-called pasta places. 

so many good choices, and so many of them are SO GOOD
as much as i love Pasta Pomodoro, i think most of the things on their menu sucks. but at Gypsy's, i am rarely disapointed with their creations. and their the specials always kick-butt. 

their quality is worth way more than they are charging. 

the only thing i did not like was the fruiti de mare--even though it was packed with seafood, as it should, every time i (or friends) try it, the sauce is watery. (maybe because of the way they cook the seafood? i dunno...)

one warning, you will not like Gypsy's pizzas/calzones or the cream/white sauces if you do not like cheese
cheese is greasy, and they are not skimpy on the cheese
thus, Gypsy's food would be greasy (duh!)

hope to see u in the Asian Getto!

A college student's dream dining spot....yeah the cashier could be a bit friendlier and there is a short wait, but the prices and consistent quality make up for it...where else can you get a $2 salad, $6 pasta dish and bubble tea next door if you still have room afterwards?
Along with La Burrita and IB's, gypsy's completes the holy trinity of Durant Avenue inexpensive student eating. For the price point, Gypsy's cannot be beat.

Get the gypsy's chicken. Get the gypsy's chicken. Get the gypsy's chicken. 

I'm totally biased on my review as I was once a berkeley student, but I'm assuming most of the readers for this restaurant are, so why not? The gypsy's chicken...is...special. Creamy and fatty? Yes. Guaranteed to put you well on your way to the dreaded freshman fifteen? OH yeah! (follow it up with a milk tea from sweetheart's right next door and you're already ahead of the pack)  Not for everyone but eventually will be if you eat it enough? Hell yes. 

That creamy, succulent taste...I definitely would not review it now since I graduated over 3 years ago.... had it not been for the fact that I was recently able to visit again...and experience another penne of heaven. I was seriously tempted to buy another and take it back home to our hotel in SF. 

Objectively though, the garlic bread is made with real garlic roasted on top, the food is fatty and delicious, and the gypsy's chicken isn't for everyone (esp the health conscious).  I don't like how they have an obnoxious sign in front of their soda fountain that says "Refills 50 cents" in sharpee...talk about being cheap! (at least get a typed sign) I don't believe I have ever gotten any kind of drink there.

everytime i come here i leave very full. even though it's in something we call "asian ghetto", the food is pretty good. the pasta is always smothered in pasta sauce (which i personally like) and the serving size is just enough. the place is cute and the service is good too. the garlic bread, however, is sometimes sketchy because it's just a piece of brown garlic smacked on top of bread. i've only had chicken and seafood (shrimp and clam). shrimp and clam are good but the chicken, i wouldn't get again (personally). the food is prety fairly priced but the 50cent for refill of soda?! what's that about?

One of my favorite restaurants in Berkeley.  Great prices. Great portions. Great food.  The Calzones, pizza, and pasta are all good.  My favorite is the meatball calzone... put some siracha on there and its simply superb =D

Crazy Alfredo is to die for! You can actually taste the red wine with the bell peppers! I would love to try some other plates on their menu but I'm afraid it won't be good! Next thing on my list shall be the eggplant sandwich! $7.99 for any meal w/ SALAD & DRINK?! Heaven!

* Don't try their seafood menu if you're really a big fan like me! I was very disappointed when I ordered Frutti De Mare. It's expensive & not worth it.

Best Italian Restaurant in Berkeley, the awards don't lie! I am a regular customer and feel privileged to live so close, extremely cheap for the quality and portions, any menu item + salad + drink only $7.99!!  Gypsy's is definitely my favorite place to eat in Berkeley, could eat here everyday and not get tired of the food! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

This place is pretty cheap for what it's worth. I came here a couple days ago and ordered the Gypsy Chicken. It was pretty good but I'm sure I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have it to go. When I went, it was during one of the heat wave days, and boy was it HOT inside. But anyway, that's besides the point. The gypsy chicken cost about $7 for a fair large portion. I don't remember what my boyfriend ordered but there was angel hair pasta with marinara sauce and some seafood. This was pretty darn tasty. All in all it cost about $16 for both of us. Will definitely come again if I come by Berkeley.

Definitely get more bang for your buck here. 

Parking Garage down the street = no problems here!

I got lucky and came in before the big lunch rush- this place is usually busy so i'm guessing it would be smart to just call in an order and pick up. 

I ordered the God Father's Favorite, which was soo good for $8. The portion was big, and it came with a side of garlic bread (literally, bread with a clove of garlic in the center) Delicious! The side salad is HUGE also, it was like a full meal. 

The eggplant sandwich in marinara is delicious also, lots of flavor. If you like garlic like i like garlic, you'l love it. 

Next time i want to try the calzones, which are as big as my face! 

Gypsy's is worth trying! :)

If you're ever shopping in the telegraph area and in need of a pasta fix, this is the place to go.  Its part of a small food court area, you can't miss it. Because its located so close to CAL, its patrons are usually students, making the prices affordable.  The most expensive item is $7. It can get super busy at times, the cashier can be somewhat rushed but the food is totally worth it and comes reasonably fast.  Sometimes there is no seating inside.  If its not too cold, there is ample seating on the outside area.  The portions here are very generous and the ingredients are fresh.  Every pasta dish comes with bread and a homemade roasted garlic paste on top of it.  I personally love the garlic bread because I love garlic.  But others find the garlic taste a little overwhelming.

YUM! I went to this place for the first time last night and got a Pesto Calzone (Chicken, Mozzerella, Ricotta, & Pesto) and it was delicious!  The chicken was a little dry and it wasn't overflowing with it - but the "healthy" amount of cheese in the calzone made up for it.  My boyfriend got the sausage calzone and that was pretty yummy, too (I had a bite -- the sauce was just a little sweet though).  The total came to $13.03 for two big calzones -- not too shabby! And they're open late which is cool too -- we went there around 11 pm and it was pretty busy.  Oh, and their water didn't taste dirty -- which is a plus for me, especially compared to other places around Berkeley.

In essence, this place is great for a carb-loading for cheap and at later hours. One pasta entree gives you quite a bit of food for about $6.

I like the Godfather's Favorite, which is basically chicken carbonara. I've also tried the meatball calzone, which was super disappointing. True, it was bigger than my head, but it had way too much cheese (saying a lot, since I adore cheese,) and wasn't very flavorful.

And yes, the garlic bread is delicious. Roasted garlic cloves smeared over bread..om nom nom.
Nice food.
Cheap, lots of food, and delicious! The perfect college eatery.

In short, best bang for the buck type spot. Street parking sucks so definetly hit the parking garage a short block away

had the carbonara, noodles were aldente, sauce was rich and creamy and not runny, binded well with the noodles, pancetta was cooked just right in my opionion had the outter edges crisped up but the center at just well, flavor wise was also good, that pasta water had to be salted because the sauce was past bland this---much, which is good

big ups-

-alot of foot traffic which means your food will most likely be cooked fresh
-good view of the kitchen so you know their hustlin back there
-for the amount of ppl passing thru, service provided with experience

big down-

-place is packed around 5pm
-garlic bread needs help, lacked the flavor, crust, the big ass piece of garlic in the middle didn't help

yeah, I would come back

Been here three times now and have enjoyed my food each time! I ordered the shrimp alfredo twice and also the shrimp scampi. The shrimp alfredo was really creamy and flavorful and the shrimp scampi had an awesome lemon sauce with capers! Definitely would recommend for anyone who's looking for a cheap, quick eat that's good

Gypsies is the only reason why I come to Berkeley.

Olive Garden, Pasta Pomodoro cant beat Gypsies' pasta. And for $6.89, you cant beat that. Huge portions, hot and right out of the pan. You just cant beat it. 

Parking can be a little hectic and the restroom is no where to be found. But thats okay. 

I recommend ANYTHING on the menu.

Last, I wish there was a dish with chicken and shrimp alfredo or whatever with penne. That would be a killer. Or maybe I'm not looking at the menu long enough because craving for pasta clutters the mind?
Usually a line but it moves quickly. The cheese ravioli and crazy alfredo are my absolute favorites. You definitely can't beat the prices and you will not go home hungry!
Cute little place with great pasta & salads. Great prices for large portions!I will definitately be a regular here whenever in berkeley :)

This is probably one of the cheapest not-pizza-only Italian place you will find.  Ever.  

Therefore, given this price range, I'd say their food is pretty amazing.  I always get the crazy alfredo, or the gnocchi one (forgot what it's called), but find other items on the menu not as great.

As good as their food is, you can taste the death in every bite you take.  They put a huge amount of cream, butter, or sauce in general into every single dish.  It gets a bit greasy and unpleasant after a few tries.

Their service isn't exactly the good either.  Also, they started charging for using credit cards.  This charge has gone from a one time transaction charge to a per-item cost increment, meaning you're paying twice for the transaction cost if you buy two items.  BUT THEN AGAIN, this whole thing is illegal so...

We went here on a Sunday morning at 1030AM because the Philly Cheesesteak shop didn't open till noon and we were on our way to the city.

-1 Star for charging $0.50 for refills.  Hmmm, water, thanks.

Quick and friendly service.  All our dishes were sit down restaurant quality, huge and CHEAP.  They have so many selections.  I got a chicken, mushroom and onion calzone.  There was a lot of cheese which made me happy.

My fave dish out of all four we ordered was the chicken and broccoli pasta.  It was light and perfect.  The sauce was very flavorful too.

One friend said the lasagna had too much ricotta.  

My friend described it perfectly, "When we were in college and wanted to eat out for a nice dinner, this is where we went."

So everyone!!! I loove Gypsy's it's the best really. You get a nice size plate of food at a geat price, being that I just don't have money to burn on crap food thats small!! The men that work there always provide EXCELLENT CUSTOMER SERVICE!! Which is my ultimate thing being that I'm a custmer service girl. All around if you want fast affordable, hot, large varity of meals.......Gypsy's Trattoria Itallano.

Calzones? Pasta? Pizzza? Cheap prices? A block away from campus? Grrrrrrrrrrrahhh!!

This place has been an all-time favorite for years. The Gypsy's chicken is superb, and the calzones - especially the ham and the sausage - are filling and well done. Service is quick. Staff is not the friendliest, but the important thing is they get your orders right and move the food along. Can be hard to find a table during peak hours with all of the Cal students, but there is always outside tables or can just take it to go and walk yourself back to campus in less than 2 min. Is a great break from studying, and nice to visit during the weekend before football games.

Overall: One of the best deals near UC Berkeley campus and delicious Italian food that keeps you coming back again and again.

CALZONES.

It's under $7, and bigger than your head. And if you take it to go, you get a nice donut box to transport your calzone in.

I always thought the name "calzone" was so representative of UC Berkeley aka Cal. Not that they meant to do it that way, but it's cool anyway.

Pretty impressive selections.
Massive portions to fill any hungry college student!
A lot of cheese and its located nearby other great shops.
Watch your tongue though, stuff comes out piping hot. For serious.

Its not surprising why this place has garnered a good bit of critical acclaim from the community.

Everything is reasonably priced.

4.0/5.0

Awesome Italian....keeps you coming back for more....Resonable prices and wonderful food...Lot's of choices too!!

They make you feel like one of the Family........

Easy to find and parking is moderate

as seen in my reviews, I love a cheap, convenient, low-key place which serves a fair portioned meal which can also hold its own with the bigger more expensive boys.

I had gone to Gypsy's many many years ago but never really ate there on a critical basis....you know, one of those times where you are hungry and need to eat something.

Well, I was hungry last night and I am now in my Yelper review stage. 

The place is always packed to the gills. Yes, it serves the UCB students so it has to be inexpensive.

I ordered the Fruiti De Mare @ $7.49 which is pretty reasonable. here is where the problem starts. ....i am on a 2009 kick where I am testing my own homemade pasta red sauce along with other restuarant sauces,...I am really taking the time to find a good sauce and what goes into a good sauce.

Problem 1: Gypsy's sauce is just average, really not much different or better or worse than a jarred sauce. With the seafood in the dish, the dish still was a bit bland, sour, not sweet. 

Problem 2: the pasta is cheap. it really didn't taste like an Italian pasta. Could have been a macaroni pasta.  the problem was it was overcooked and turned into a generic glob of starch.

As seen in the all the prior reviews, this place is liked by many. Who am I to argue, but I would venture to guess most of the reviews were from people like me during my visit many many years ago. .....If you really take a few extra steps, you would find that for the same price, Pasta Pomodoro, Little Henry's, or even Bodega Pasta in the Public Market have a much better product with far more superior sauce.

Oh my goodness, Gypsy's!

My ex-boyfriend and I used to drive from Belmont to Berkeley on a regular basis for this addictive, affordable, fast-Italian-food!

Mmmm I have tried their salads (fresh!), pasta and meatballs (mystery meat..but bomb meal), fettucine (rich!), and calzones (perfect and HUGE) and I would have to say A+.

The only reason they get a 4 is because it isn't super, duper sanity (although it IS berkeley we're talking about), they use mystery ingredients in the meatballs, and it gets crazy busy.

It's not the best or healthiest style of italian food, but when you factor in the price, it somehow tastes amazing. This is probably the best value in all of Berkeley, and really the only place to get half-decent italian food anywhere within walking distance of the UC Berkeley campus.

My absolute favorite is the Godfather's Favorite. It's an alfredo-style penne with pancetta and chicken, and while it tastes like it is going to clog my arteries, I get it basically every time.

As a "healthier" alternative, I sometimes get the Lemon Chicken Salad. It's basically a caesar-style salad with chunks of chicken. It's quite delicious, but it's certainly not actually healthy.

And finally, I used to always get their spaghetti with meatballs. Their spaghetti is fine, but the meatballs are a little gigantic and bland. It's filling though, which for 6ish dollars is not a bad deal.

Oh, and I love their garlic bread.

Looking for delish empty carbs? Gypsy's is the place to go! My favorite dish is their Chicken Pesto pasta... just thinking about it makes me hungry haha. It's really unhealthy though, swimming around in a lot of olive oil, and it's not something everyone can handle.

Overall, a good place to grab some good Italian food. Their portions are enormous, and I love their bread with garlic. It gets packed and the food takes a while, so be prepared for a wait!

Pretty good selection of Italian food - pastas, calzones, salads, etc, for about $6 to 7. They give really big portions, and if you order pasta, it always comes with a slab of bread with (literal) garlic on it. The store people aren't openly friendly (lots of smiling/small talk), but they're polite. Good amount of seating! You pretty much order at the counter and seat yourself.

I really want to give it 5 stars, but I just can't. It is what it is.

However, the value is absolutely incredible. Absolutely enormous portions/calzones for 7 bucks. I know plenty of places w/ much more expensive calzones where you get far less. Great place to grab a quick bite before the Greek Theatre.

I used to go here a lot to fulfill my italian food cravings as a student. I always got the pesto calzone. delicioso!!

But i recently went back and ordered a fish dish, but i felt like the fish i was eating was not fresh and i couldnt finish it. so watch out.

For nostalgia purposes, I couldnt be too mean. But hopefully that last time was just a fluke.

3 stars!!

Probably the cheapest Italian food place I ever had.  Being the only non-asian restaurant in durant ghetto, it holds its own against all those cheap asian restaurants in the same square.  It had the same qualities as the other restaurants in the area, cheap, large portions, and packed with taste.  Exactly what every college students wants!

I especially like the garlic bread that comes with the pasta, they use actual garlic.  Stay with the Pasta though, cuz the calzone weren't that impressive.  And remember to add the salad for only $1.99 more.

I know its not the most authentic italian place, but being half the price as most other places, I am willing to let that slide.  Besides, just cuz its not authentic doesn't means its not good.

oh carbonara,
how i love you. but bring cash--
extra charge for cards!
Sure this place is cheap, but the food just isn't good.
Cheap&&&YUMMY!(: (: Loud. /: Crowded! );
Not a bad place to stop by and pick up a bite. They have a large selection of foods and it all seems to be pretty good. The calzones are especially good.

Pretty much where I go when I have those carb cravings and want some delicious, unhealthy, Italian food. I used to be addicted to the Pollo con Pesto but I've moved on to their Chicken Gnocci.
I came here every week with my roommate to get pizza over the summer (they make it pretty similar to the real Italian pizza in Naples in my opinion) but I've had it a few times recently and it's just not as good as it was then. Maybe they changed ingredients? :[

Pizzas suck

Pastas are great for the price 

Calzones are boring

Sandwiches are good.

I had the godfathers favorite. It was preeeetty tasty. Definitely needed to add red peppers for that extra kick tho. This place was super busy, then it died and picked up again 10 minutes later. People were literally jumping in seats as SOON as a person was done eating. I suggest you do the same if you want a table. Anyways, only thing I didn't care for so much was the garlic bread that everyone raves about for some reason. They use roasted garlic and that's it. It gave me a headache when I bit into it. Way too strong for my taste. All in all, the place was pretty decent for the price I paid.

Menu item + salad + soda = $7.99 
Can't say more than this, besides being a super inexpensive place for dinner in the Asian Ghetto. I have been here a handful of times and every plate has been a consistent OKAY. Last night we ordered the Pizza paradiso combo and the Godfather's favorite combo. Both were very filling and the total was less than 20 bucks, for some hungry college students this is a STEAL.

The pizza paradiso is a 10 inch pizza with sausage, pepperoni, onions, bell peppers and olives. The godfather's favorite is penne pasta with chicken and pancetta in a cream sauce. It wasn't the best for my waistline, but definitely worth the price. All in all, I was already full once I was done with my salad so the entree was a great meal for later. This place is open late and gets super crowded once school starts. Luckily, I went during summer so I was able to find a seat, but usually you have to stalk for one. The only thing I don't like is the fact that you have to pay for refills at the soda machine which was .50 cents. Not a big deal, but for such a crowded place it seems like such an inconvenience to wait in line for a dumb refill. Anyway, be sure to get your dinner here and then walk right across for some late night donuts!!

I've been in Berkeley for how many years now (closer to half a decade than to 0 by now) and had never gone to Gypsy's until this February.  Wha???

People always talked about it but for some reason I was always more called to the Pad Thai from Thai Basil, or the Cantonese food at Vietnam Village (?)

The frutti di mare is the thing to get in my opinion.  It's always hot, nice big portion (I'm in grad school, this matters), and lots of nice yummy clams and mussels and shrimp.  I suspect they might all be from frozen, but it tastes so good!

I haven't had the calzones because I'm not a big fan of large pieces of bread (although their garlic bread is pretty good), and the lasagna is filling but heavy on cheese and oil.  Also the meat filling was ..different.  Couldn't quite put my finger on how...maybe it's pork?  Or just more ground up than I've had it before.

Next time I'll try the pesto chicken, but probably my favourite will always be the frutti di mare.  Sorry lasagna, Old Spaghetti Factory wins that round :(

This is the only good pasta place at a college student's budget near campus.

The food isn't that great but it fills you up and sometimes that all you want as a college student.

I usually get the Godfather's Favorite but you can't really go bad with any of them, but don't expect anything spectacular.

Gypsys! The staple Italian restaurant of UC Berkeley. 

The restaurant is always busy, but you can usually get a table inside. It can get pretty loud inside, so you might want to sit outside anyways.

My personal favorite dish is the Pollo Con Pesto, or Pesto Chicken pasta. Also, the Bronx Tale, Godfather's Favorite, and Fettucini with Clams is pretty good. The clams are the canned kind, but for some reason i like it haha. 

Also, the garlic bread is EXCELLENT! SUPER TASTY!

Located almost right across UC Berkeley's Unit 3, Gypsy's was  so convenient, so good, and such a bargain, we went two nights in a row.  When I think about the size and quality of Gypsy's "side salad," it puts some of our local eateries in Hawaii to shame.  Two people can share one side salad. (Yeah, Hawaii costs a lot,  but so does California.)  The pastas were delicately seasoned and al dente as it should be.  Thank goodness, The Sherbert suggested that we buy calzones to take on the plane ride home.  Gypsy's was nice enough to give us a bunch of foiI to wrap the calzones tightly.  I swear the other passengers were salivating as we ate our calzones with cabernet on the flight.  Sure beat the airline's unappetizing dry turkey sandwich!

I love Gypsy's... When I used to go to Cal, this was like my favorite place to go. It's super cheap and they have the best, best, best chicken pesto pasta ever. I would seriously go back to Northern CA just to eat there... mmm. so worth it. The seafood pasta dish is also a favorite of mine :). For the locals, call ahead if you're ordering to go! I used to get out of class, place my order, and then it would be ready by the time I got there.

OMG, the BEST pasta I have ever had. Just kidding. Because I had a calzone. 

My sister and I shared a chicken pesto calzone. It was HUGE and it cost about 6 bucks. It was loaded with mozzarella and ricotta cheese. I almost choked on the cheese because there was so much of it. I'm not complaining though because I love cheese! It was absolutely delicious! I can't remember the last time I truly enjoyed a meal from a restaurant. Next time I go to Berkeley to visit people at school, I am stopping by this place again!

They also have like, 6 or 7 "Best of the Bay" awards so I guess my review is pointless. Oh well.

They weren't kidding when they voted Gypsy's Best of Berkeley in Italian food for about 10 consecutive years, it is just that good! Not only are the prices extremely reasonable for the broke college student like myself, but they also give hearty portions that will surely hit the spot. Only negative comment I would give about this place is the small location, and since it's fairly popular, the place is almost always crowded. However, don't let that stop you from getting a good meal.

I always order the Godfather. For $6.99, it is absolutely delish.

I have frequented Gypsy's many times over the past 5 years. Unfortunately, I have only ordered the Crazy Alfredo... every single time. I need to get out of my comfort zone and try the Calzone and other pasta dishes. Still, Crazy Alfredo is consistently delicious and decently priced!

Gypsy's is still the same old cheap yet good pasta venue. I've tried quite a few dishes now, but the ones I remember are the calzone and Godfather's favorite. The calzones are huge, but if you open them, they're full of air...Not my favorite. I think I did find a favorite dish here which is the Godfather's Favorite. Probably because its one of the few pasta dishes with panchetta (love the stuff). I do wish they were a bit more lenient with the panchetta but I guess the greasiness would be overpowering and they're doing a favor for my arteries. Also very crowded during meal times so expect to wait, eat outside, or to-go. You can also give a call and pre-order so you can go in about 10 minutes to pick up your order. Very convenient. They also added a charge for plastic. I'd say at least 3/4ths of the Berkeley community (students and whatnot) use credit cards more than cash and Gypsy's decides to add a fee for plastic. Brilliant...
Gypsys is bomb! Their pesto chicken pasta is always on point! I love their food, never had anything bad the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is bc the parking sucks.

I came here with my friends because he really likes this place. I stared at the menu for a good ten minutes before ordering because I was being picky, I didn't want heavy sauces and craved shrimp.

I ended up ordering the Mediterranean which was angel hair pasta with sun-dried tomatoes and king shrimp. The pasta itself was alright, it wasn't cooked al dente and was a bit soggy but since I was really hungry, I didn't really mind much. Since this dish doesn't have a sauce, the general flavor comes from these chunks of sundried tomatoes which were overwhelmingly sour and salty. I had to carefully pick out the right ratio of tomato to pasta with my fork in order to avoid bites of blandness and weird sour-saltiness. The shrimp really bothered me because they didn't remove the tail shell. I guess I'm spoiled by completely deshelled seafood. The dish came with bread. I had to stare and pick at it for a while to figure out that tiny pile of off-colored slimy stuff was supposed to be garlic. It tasted pretty good if you can get past the visual of it.

My friends ordered the carbonara and a penne dish. I guess they had better luck with theirs because they were heavy cream dishes. I later found out that most of the favorites are sauce-heavy and the lighter dishes are always so-so.

I'd definitely come back next time to pick one of their better options, but be warned that if you're looking to have a lighter meal, your dish will err more to the unsatisfactory side.

This place is like having olive garden to go and cheaper! Pretty much anything on the menu is amazing.  My usual is the chicken pesto and I really don't like getting pesto anywhere else, it just can't compare.
Love this place. Call your order in if you don't want to wait. First come first serve so don't complain about the seating. Thats all.

I will keep this short and sweet. This place is awesome if you are looking for cheap Italian cuisine and good conversation with a few friends. The food is delicious and very filling. Also, the location is very convenient if you are on campus or in the UC campus area. The only caveat is that the food does take a while to be prepared but what can we expect from an Italian food joint?

4/5 because of good food, large portions, moderate pricing and friendly staff. If you are willing to wait 15-20 minutes for food, then by all means come here and enjoy!

My homegirl suggested that we go here before we started drinking one night. It is a small place in a food court down the street from the cal campus, and it could be a little tough finding a table if it's busy but the food is good. I've had the crazy alfredo, lasagna, and some pizza though I don't remember which one due to alcohol killing my memory of that time. The crazy alfredo is my favorite so far, but the menu has a lot of choices and there are other things I want to try there. I like the place and would recommend it for something fast and good.

Great cheap, Italian food.  Best in Berkeley by far.  I miss this place so much after moving away.

The pastas and calzones are tasty.  The garlic bread that comes with most food items isn't very good.  In fact, the garlic on top of the bread is especially lame.  The pizzas are terrible.  Minus one star for bad pizza tacky garlic bread.  However, if you enjoy huge servings of cheap pasta and calzones, then this is the place for you.

It's alright. I've ate here about three times since I've been going to UCB.

Nothing to go crazy about.

Garlic bread is GOOD though.

I really like their salads 

note: everything is pretty heavy
the godfather is alright
i really like the gnocchi
the calzone always look so delicious when other people are eating them, but every time i've gotten it, it's only okay (don't get chicken...dry)

Gypsy's Trattoria Italiano is located within Asian Ghetto by UC Berkeley, so it's very convenient if you're looking for a quick bite. This place is constantly full of customers (mainly college students), so there might be a short wait during rushes.

I recommend the calzones and pasta plates. However, beware of their sauces! They're pretty rich, so be ready to food coma after eating here.

They also offer any entree, salad, and soda for $7.99. Good deal!!

Fruit de mare is my favorite.  I know my italian friends says real italian food is so much better, but I'm asian and I love this pace! the garlic bread is yummy.  I like that hustling busting type place.  Staff pretty much just do their, not really conversating much.  But then again it is just a whole in wall, but great food.  parking sucks!

Their calzones are HUGE & pretty cheap, but know that they take a bit longer than the pasta dishes (the cashier will warn you about this when you place your order). Oh, & did I mention that they're super tasty? The pastas are pretty tasty, too, but I'm stuck on the meaty calzones -- mmm, toasty crust, gooey cheese, tart tomato sauce, & chewy meat. Yum.

My friends and I were able to share 2 dishes not completely stuffed, but def. satisfied. 

Hmm...it's not the best Italian restaurant in Berkeley (still have to find it!) but it's still pretty tasty. You get a nice portion for what you pay.
I think the reason why I'm giving it 4 stars is because it was my first sit-in restaurant at Berkeley and I found it to be really pleasant- the taste, that is. It tends to get pretty crowded and the tables are close to the standing customers waiting in line so they're always looking at the food you ordered, which can get pretty annoying, esp. if you're trying to eat!

My Favorite place to grab some pasta. Im a sauce guy. If you like some pasta with ur sauce Gypsy's is your place. 
The times I've been there it was very busy so i might not be a bad idea to get your meal in a to go box and sit outside.

Decent Italian food at decent prices.. my favorite is the tri-color tortellini with shrimp.   I'm not sure if they still have it but that dish was pretty creamy and tasty from what I remember.   The staff is quick and efficient so if you're looking for a quick italian meal then gypsy's is a good bet.

I came here again last Friday, and as always, it was super packed. 

I just wanted to update my review because I had two different dishes. I had the Godfather's favorite and a combo calzone. The Godfather's favorite was yummy, but slightly bland. Way too much cream and not enough kick. I had to add salt and peppers to add the kick. I would order it again, except I'd get it with linguine or something different next time. The thickness and texture of the penne just didn't go well with the sauce.

The combo calzone I would never order again. Way too much cheese and not enough salt. It takes SUPER long to bake and that's really irritating when you're hungry. I just did not enjoy it at all. Every bite was just cheese, cheese, cheese. I barely tasted any sauce or any of the goodies inside.

I tried the calzone here with a salad and it was good and the portions were generous. The food comes out promptly making it ideal for a quick lunch. The atmostphere is college town. I look forward to coming back to try other items at this joint.

I absolutely love this place! Every dish I've tried is pretty much amazing. My favorites are the Funghi (vegetarian) and the Godfather's Favorite (penne with chicken, bacon, cream, and egg). The calzones take longer but are definitely worth the wait. Gypsy's is cheap, quick, and extremely popular =)

The only complaint I have (and thus the reason I gave this place a 4 instead of a 5) is the garlic bread, which is pretty much a piece of bread with a hunk of roasted garlic on top. Some people like it, but I can't stand it and usually give it to a friend who can.

one time my friends drove from all the way from fremont ONLY to get gypsy's. nothing else.

the godfathers pasta is my absolute favorite. the portions are very filling and i love how they give garlic bread with their dishes. mmm mmm mmm...PLUS the prices are so cheap! 

gotta go back this summer!
greasy food, quick and easy, not too bad. go here if you're craving cheap italian.

I came here on a Tuesday, 2pm in the summer with a friend, and we both ordered calzones since my friend is such a huge fan of them and since I've never had one before.
I ordered the primavera calzone, which I believe has vegetables, tomato sauce, and cheese. It was alright, nothing spectacular, and not as good as I expected it to be since my friend was always telling me about how great he thought they were, "rolls eyes". But then again, he usually got the meaty calzones, and I got the vegetarian one...
It was fun to eat, though. =D

On my 21st birthday I cornered the owner as he was relaxing in KingPin Donuts at about 1:30am.  This was the drunkest I had ever been in my entire life (and forever after I'm sure).  Mind you, I'm not a mean drunk.  I'm actually a lot a fun but I was pretty sloppy and likely not making sense.

I came into Gypsys the next day and hoped he'd forgotten...but he didnt.  He was however, really cool about it and told me I wasn't that bad to deal with.  I guess it didn't hurt that I was eating there quite regularly at the time.

But anyways...that was a bad tangent...onto the review.
