This portions are filling and it has great selection: lots of different dishes to pick from.  My favorties include: Godfather's Favorite, Bronx Tale and the Chicken/Broccoli pizza.  Don't expect the best quality though, some dishes can get greasy as all hell (Pollo con Pesto for example).  But if you're starvin, go get your grub on.  

Oh and lest I forget, call ahead for Pizza and calzone. The lines can get ridiculous sometimes.

I love this place but I'm hardly ever in Berkeley but when I am in the neighborhood, I LOVE eating their Shrimp Alfredo! There's baby shrimp in there which aren't that small, I'd say they're about 1/2 the size of a tiger prawn. The meal is hearty, fresh, piping hot and oh-so-yum! I've also had their calzones (I don't remember which one) and it's also delicious! Warning: The calzones take a long while to bake since everything is made fresh! They're usually always busy and their prices have increased a bit (approximately 50 cents) but it's still less than $10 and is totally filling.

I like the mediterranean pasta.

The calzones have way too much cheese though.

You can call me bias, you can call me a bear lover but I LOVE GYPSY!!! 
Although I graduated from CAL about 4 years ago, I always try my best to make a trip out to Berkeley, especially Gypsy to grab some pasta. 

My favorites are God Father's Fav, Pollo con Pesto and if you want something a little more healthier, the Chicken Salad with Caesar dressing. I miss all the yummy food around Berkeley. 

The portions size on everything is pretty good. I normally share with my bf when we order something different.

OMG, I love this place and could not believe this was my first time. A chicken pesto entree for less than $7 AND delicious?!?! Dear lord. One downside to this place is that it's super crowded but there's very good reason!! So if you're looking for a bang for your buck while keeping great quality, search no more! If you're lucky you can find a table (it's self seating, most people take orders to go and eat outside at the patios). They also have AWESOME hard to find sodas in their fridge. :)

Their food is fantastic, their staff is nice, and the location is great (full of happy college students). I can't wait to come back here again!!!

Really great prices for the quality and quantity of food you get.

My favorite is the Pollo con Pesto, it's just really good comfort food. If you're a pesto lover, you'll approve. Recently went on a cloudy day for lunch and it was perfect. Their portions are huge so I always have some left over to take home.

Their pizzas are also good but I think pasta is the way to go at Gypsy's.

To get food, order, wait for your number to be called, and grab a table! A single order of pizza and pasta without drinks or anything comes out to around $7.50.

Ahh YES! Good old Gypsy's... If you went to Berkeley, there is NO way you didn't eat here. It' in the Asian Ghetto and definitely one of the BEST in the ghetto. Everything here is pretty delicious and it is all made to order fresh! 

I have to thank my Freshman roommate, who I refer to as Gramps (he was a senior, but lived in the dorms and we became great friends) Anyways, I have to thank him for making me try the Pesto Calzone!!! OMG I have tried and tried to find another place that has something similar to this piece of pesto perfection and I have failed miserably! We would mash on one of these at least once a week. Quick Tip: Call ahead because the Calzones take about 20 minutes. 

This place is always packed, but the lines move fast! It's funny to watch 
how baked all the chefs are too, you know what I am talking about! 

MY GO-TO DISH: Pesto Calzone, Crazy Alfredo and Chicken Gnocchi.

Went here for lunch with my brother and my boyfriend. My brother told me that he really loves their pasta here since he has been here a couple of times. We went around a time where it wasn't as packed and also our food came out at a decent amount of time.

I order the Frutti Di Mare which was a seafood pasta dish and it was delicious. My boyfriend and my brother both ordered the Gypsy's Chicken and they enjoyed that as well. 

Definitely recommend this place if you are craving for Italian food in the Berkeley area!

If you've never had a Gypsy's calzone then... you've probably never been to Berkeley.  It's hard to justify coming to this restaurant and NOT getting a calzone.  For seven dollars, you get a meal fit for two.  It's like a giant pillow of perfectly fluffy bread stuffed with cheese, sauce and meat.  I'm partial to the Sicilian and Italian sausage ones.  I frequently come here with a friend to split one.

The lasagna is heavenly too.  Very meaty and cheesy.  This place has perfected their marinara sauce as well.  Maybe it's not authentic, but it's not as if I can tell the difference and it's delicious anyhow.

The only drawback of this place is that the pasta dishes are hit and miss.  I used to like the Pollo Con Pesto but have come to dislike the texture of the pasta - a little too dense to me.  Also, the sauce on it is kind of gross as it starts to cool down.  

The Alfredo Ravioli is great but makes me feel like my cholesterol levels have jumped 50 points (not necessarily a bad thing...).  My friend swears by the Godfather's Favorite.  They do a good job with their gnocchi too - light and fluffy.

There's not a huge amount of seating so at peak hours (dinner time) you may have to wait around a bit for a table.  That shouldn't stop you from going though.

I come here at least once a week and order the same thing everytime: Gypsy's Chicken, sub penne for the fettichini.  YUMMMM-O.  The garlic bread has a real piece of crushed roasted garlic on it... i love spreading the clove all over the bread and dowsing it with parmesean. MMmmM.

The place is always packed with students, but the food comes out in a timely manner.

The only downside:  the workers, although very friendly, watch you from behind the kitchen while you consume.  I don't really care, but I could see how some people could get freaked out.

Gypsy's is excellent.  Tremendous pasta, very affordable.  I would eat there every day if carbs were the new protein.  Don't go here if you hate fresh bread with fresh roasted garlic that comes with every dish.

Might I recommend:
Godfather's favorite
Chicken Piccata 
Bronx Tale
great pizza and awesome pasta and salad for very little money. Wife said the cannoli was delicious. Open late (a relief for those of us used to places closing at 10pm).

Gypsy's is a good place to eat when you have absolutely no qualms about your health...and I mean that in the best way possible.

The Italian food is buttery and rich and the portion sizes are very generous. It was a guilty pleasure of mine in college, but I haven't been back since my metabolism isn't Gypsy's capable anymore! The staff is nice and the food is quickly prepared and served. A good place to try if you want something that won't leave you wanting more at the end of your meal.
When I crave pasta and want it to-go...i go here.  Good bread and good pasta no matter what you get. Not the best, but enough to satisfy a craving
Favorite FAST italian food.

I am going to preface this review by saying that I am not a college student in Berkeley. I think this is a local favorite, and I admit that my perspective as a traveler passing through might be a little different.

The food was decent. I actually was impressed with the quality of the ingredients that were used in my pizza. But there was something sweet (maybe the cheddar) that tasted off, and the oregano was a little over-done in the sauce. But it was much better than I would have expected in a place decorated like this.

The atmosphere is casual, kind of like a diner where you'd just stop in to eat something fast, and I think that is pretty much what this place is to the student crowd here. The prices are low, consistent with this type of place. 

Overall, the food is a step above what you'd think of given the atmosphere and the prices, but that doesn't change what it is.

Gypsy's is the best place in the Durant Food Court, aka. "Asian Ghetto". Quite ironic I guess. For the price, you really can't lose. Most of the entrees are around $7, and you get large portions. I never feel hungry leaving this place, unless i get take out (something I do frequently), but you get the idea. All the pasta dishes are quite good and come with some tasty garlic bread. It is literally garlic on bread, awesome. The Tortellini Georgio (not entirely sure of the name) is my favorite dish thus far from what I've tried. It is basically tri-colored tortellini served with a thick alfredo-like sauce and baby shrimp. Good stuff. 5 stars indeed for the tasty and cheap!

Where else am I going to get cheap Italian in the Southside area? That isn't super suspicious anyway. Gypsy's fulfills that need which is why it's such a popular spot with the students and myself. If you need pasta, it's here, but I think their ridiculous values come in the huge calzones. Pretty large for a great price.

Yep, it gets busy, but busyness is always a good sign when it comes to cheap eats.

If you went to CAL, you should know how wonderful this place is. Voted #1 numerous times, their awards speak for themselves. Go with the godfather- Crispy chopped bacon + al dente pasta + great sauce + tons of flavor= happy college student or just happy patron. All this for under $8? Great deal and great flavor!
Pretty good for the price, very cheap!! Ordered 1 pizza, 1 pasta shared between the two, 2 sodas, it came out $18.75. Very hard to beat this price.

The best things here are the CALZONES.  They are ginormous and filled with gooey cheese, along with whatever other filling you may order.  I think I've tried most of the calzones and there is not one that I did not like.  I usually can eat only half and save the other half for another meal.  It's also cheap here!  But it's a really popular place, so it is usually really packed.

Best italian place in berkeley/oakland hands down. wing the menu, it doesn't matter you'll like what you randomly picked. their garlic bread is actually garlic on bread. its awesome sh!t. all at a cheap price too! the only thing that could improve is the atmosphere and actual parking.

I've been going here since I was a freshman in college in 2003! This place has always been 5 stars to me and continues to be. I've only ever gotten two things on the menu....calzones and chicken gnocchi! I have never been disappointed. Gypsies is cheap and stays so consistently over the years. You can get a great Italian meal for 2 for 16 buck, that would normally cost 40 bucks somewhere else....and it's much better!!! 

It's fast, you order at the counter and grab a seat. The place is always hoppin and open late. It can get loud but it's a fun college environment.

Great food, good prices and they are supper fast! However I feel like some of the workers are sleazy. I always order an extra bread when I go and always fork out the 40 something cents since I believe its worth it; and theyve always been nice about it and nice to me. However when I came in with my boyfriend they
 wouldnt let me buy an extra bread (they said they didn't do that) and then wouldnt let me order no mushrooms on my dish. Now I come by myself and they let me order whatever I want. It kind of killed a good date spot though..

I wasn't really expecting anything spectacular from this place... but I was just so hungry & I didn't wanna look further for a place to eat. The $7.99 combo (anything on the menu + a salad (pretty big) & drink) definitely enticed me. It's a GREAT deal! 

It definitely exceeded my expectations! I got a seafood pasta with scallops & jumbo shrimp ... & they definitely didn't skimp on the seafood. Loved it.

I had an average experience here. The lasagna was 3 stars worthy. Service was nonexistent. I liked how I could see some of the chefs prepare the pasta dishes in the kitchen. My greatest complaint would be how nasty the left over lasagna tasted. I'm eating it right now. :(

Everything seems to be so good when I order a new dish. They have a lot of selections from pasta, pizza, calzones and let's just say they basically got everything. I'm sure you'll love it! 

There is nothing I can think of that I didn't like about this place except the size of the spot. It may be small but there's also outside setting with other restaurant. It's like a mini mall but who cares, the food is good!

Prices are average. Not too expensive. It ranges from $6-12.

Tried the pesto calzone.  Absolutely delicious.  Always come here for there calzones.  Very down-to-earth setting.  Pricing is fair.  Very fast service.  Very pleased customer.

To get a true sense of campus life, come here to eat.  All UC Berkeley students drop by this place at least once in their lives.  Good food.

So I've been here twice. I shared a gigantic veggie calzone and a HUGE greek salad. They were both only $6 and soo tasty. I love Berkeley for the quality of the food and the price. It can't be beat. 

Today I had the greek salad all to myself. RIDICULOUS. It could easily be split with two people but I ate almost all of it myself. YUM. for 4.56? Ridiculous.

Great place to go on a budget !! this place is just... MMM !! if you crave italian, GO HERE ! pastas only about 7 or 8 bucks a plate and its a great portion for one person ! you get full and you save money !

I am a fan of this place, and yes, I come here for the calzones! I used to bring all my friends that visited me to Berkeley here and they like it. It i conveniently located in the Asian Ghetto, a block from the southside part of campus.
The calzone is big enough to satisfy your hunger, so you might want to share it with someone else. The pasta dishes are huge as well. 
It is also pretty cheap. I don't think there are other Italian places nearby that serve the same quality with a lower price.

This has recently become one of my favorite places to go in Berkeley. Their calzones are stupid delicious! I have only been once so I need to go again soon and try more of their dishes. GO NOW!!! It is so good

The portions are ideal size for any Italian restaurant but there is a huge plus compare to the other restaurant, its almost half the price u would pay at another Italian restaurant. customer service is fast and friendly.
Damn!! me and my friends go here all the time. If you're looking for some good ass Italian food like CALZONE  this place is awesome it open late and its hella cheap for good Italian food.

Pasta if phenomenal. The price is dirt-cheap. They have 2 prices (cash and credit): .50 cent difference.  Refills are .50 cents. Pasta comes with garlic bread (baked whole garlic). Also had the margarita pizza which was nothing to be favored.

Pretty good Italian restaurant. Great location, good prices (less than $8), and pretty good hours (open later than some of the family owned places on South Side). 

The calzones are excellent! They have both veggie and meat. The pastas and pizzas are only so-so, but I haven't tried all of them. Out of the pastas gnocchi (some potato pasta) is a pretty good one (you can also order marinara instead of the normal sauce to go with the gnocchi), but the calzones are generally considered to be better.

Protip: The extra 50 cents or so for the combo calzone vs. a chicken or steak one is worth it. I can't put my finger on it, but having a combination of meat versus just one kind makes it that much better.

Protip 2: Calzones take a long time to make (~10-15 minutes), so you should definitely call in beforehand.

Protip 3: The older guy with glasses and a mustache who owns the places is actually pretty funny. If you go in late at night (right before closing) and it's not too busy he sometimes talks to customers and is entertaining and funny.

This is my MUST STOP BY place in Berkeley when I go out there with my boyfriend. We LOVE LOVE LOVE Gypsy's Chicken. I've tried a few other dishes here, but when I tried their gypsy's Chicken...I fell in love. My boyfriend eventually started eating it too after trying mine. I've brought a few friends here, and they too love the dish.

I wish San Francisco had a place like Gypsy's! A friend brought me here after rock climbing, swearing that the combination of price and quality was unbeatable. We both had Gypsy's Chicken by his recommendation. Penne, cream sauce, mushroom, garlic and chicken. Amazing! The garlic bread was awesome, too - actual roasted garlic on bread. 

I'll be coming back to Gypsy's anytime I'm in Berkeley!

When I think about what I miss about my time at UCB, Gypsy's ALWAYS comes to mind. I LOVED the gypsy's chicken! It was so much food I always ate half and kept the other half for my next meal.  I've heard the prices have gone up since my time there, but it was really cheap when I was there.

Totally love this place. I come here every time I crave simple italian or just visiting my sister at Berkeley. I'm a simple person and a creature of habit and this place sure hits the spot. I usually get Gypsy's Chicken. Its creamy and delicious. An absolute fave that my boyfriend and I order every time. The price range is decent. About 7 dollars a plate.

They have pizza, pasta, salad, calzones. Located near campus! After a good meal, you can walk a couple feet away to grab dessert at the donut shop or quench your thirst with some bubble tea.
Amazingly consistent, solid Italian food.  Great pastas and sauces...and tons of it.  The portions are huge and the prices are always right.  Love this place for a dependably good meal.

I love Gypsy's!  Everytime I'm up here in Berkeley, I always want to stop by here!

I love their pastas because they always seem to fill me up and they're good the next day.  My friend always comes here for their calzones, but i never realized how HUGE they were until he showed me.  Even the box it came in was fit for a cake or something.  

This is the kind of place that gives you a generous amount of food for what you pay.  Just a block away from UC Berkeley and near many other restaurants.  Can get crowded at times, but it's worth the wait.

Gypsy's is pretty decent when it comes to quick and cheap pasta.  I had the carbonara without the bacon.  I know...I know...what's carbonara without the bacon, but I don't eat pork so the creamy sauce, egg, and cheese made me happy.  BF had the chicken Marsala, which was good.  The chicken was very moist and tender and the flavor of the sauce was perfect; not too salty and not under flavored.  I had to take away two stars only because when we walked in there were plenty of empty tables.  The only thing was that none of the tables were cleaned after each patron.  I actually had to clear my own table, which was pretty disgusting.  I understand the place gets pretty busy, but it's totally unacceptable when tables aren't cleared right away.  This definitely doesn't affect another trip to Gypsy's.  I'd probably just take it to go next time.

So yum in so many ways.  I can't help but order cream dishes each time I come.  The red sauce is super tasty but I love what is done here with cream and butter.  If you're still hungry you may get a donut right outside in the next biz across the dining patio.  So yum.

Every time we go to the "South side" for lunch, I become even more mad that my building is closer to the "North side", where there is essentially nothing but sandwich shops.  Since I'm carb loading, I've been trying to eat more pasta.  Tried La Val's on the North side last week and was unimpressed.  Labmate said there was a good Italian place in the Asian food court.

Gypsy's is excellent!  I ordered the capriccioso, which was penne with spinach, red peppers, garlic, tomato sauce and cream, for $6.51.  Really good portion and tasted delicious.  Comes with a side of garlic bread.  And this is real garlic bread, as in bread with roasted garlic spread on top.  Yummy.  I asked for a cup of water, and was given a glass.  The other food my friends ordered also looked and tasted good.

The inside seating was full and it was kind of stuffy, so our group opted to sit outside.  The outside seating is just ridiculous.  There are plenty of tables, but the benches are situated so that you can only use two sides of the table, a long and a short side.  If there were chairs, problem would be solved, but there weren't any.  

Summary: Good food, quick, inexpensive = Thumbs up!

No other place serves cheap, delicious pasta like this.  IT'S SO CHEAP.  I still haven't made my way to Cafe Vivoli in SF, apparently the Gypsy's of SF.  

Godfather's Favorite ftw!  Frutti di mare (request white sauce instead of red) is also amazing.

I'm slowly starting to like Gypsy's now. The first time I had it and I especially hated the crazy Alfredo. (I still don't really recommend getting the Crazy Alfredo) I've tried the shrimp tortellini which is very good. The Grandfather's Favorite is alright, personally I think it's a bit overwhelming with all of the meat but some people really love their meat so this dish could be perfect for those people.

I also really like the calzone's because it gives me my carb fix. I'd recommend getting the calzone only if you LOVE cheese because it is stuffed with a lot of cheese. I personally like the pesto calzone a lot though the ricotto cheese can be a bit too much after eating over half of the calzone. I'd recommend sharing the calzone with someone else.

Such a great bargain for Italian food in middle of Berkeley campus.
Portions are enormous and prices are under $10.
They got pasta, ravioli and these football-size cal zones.

This place is always packed with CAL students so sometimes it's kind of hard to find a table. 

tip: Go eat a donut from King Pin's donuts across the alley from them afterwards.
best feeling ever.

There's a reason this stuff is good...with all that cream and butter what could go wrong? In the end its cheap college food that makes the Freshman 15 last all four years of college!

Its got a fast turnover rate, making the food fresh regardless of their frozen meat. There's a simple formula of sauce (tomato, pesto, or alfredo ie. CREAM) + pasta + meat + some kind of veggies or none at all. This is just generally hearty college italian-style food.

And if you're in for the big time, eat one of their liver sized calzones. You'll be surprised you can finish it. It takes a little longer, but the greasy gooey-ness is oh so satisfying.  But don't expect anything worth calling Italian. 
This place is Cal's favorite Italian, but it doesn't mean that Cal students have a refined palate. But it does satisfy that craving for college-style food at college-style prices!

So if you're a poor college student, or even a college-grad looking for nostalgic shit college food, this is really all you have to choose from in Berkeley.
Oh and call in the order when there's a long line, even from right outside the store!

This has got to be one of the best deals in the entire bay area.  Thanks to the yelpers on the penne gorgonzola tip... I've decided to go veg for the next month and this didn't leave me feeling like I missed out on anything.  Awesome dish!  Yes, heavy and creamy and rich, but oh, so worth it!  I get the small salad (not so small, but only 1.99), and then have two meals for one low price!  I ordered the Frutti Del Mar for hubby and an extra order for the kids so I don't have to cook dinner tonight.  I think most places would laugh at you if you told them that you wanted shrimp, mussels and calamari on your pasta and oh, by the way, you want it for under $8!

I haven't had the same experience with a rude cashier.  The man standing there both times is a middle aged mexican man and he turns people around quickly, but I don't think of it as rude... just efficient.  I had a large order (13 items) to take back to the office and he insisted that one of his guys help me to the car.  I told him it was no problem, I could make two trips, but he wouldn't hear of it.  I got both a 'thank you' and 'have a nice day' from both him and the guy who helped me carry my stuff.

It's a bit of a trek from Emeryville, but as long as I get there a few minutes before noon, I'm golden!

oh, gypsy's, how i love thee. basically, cheap eats in the UC Berkeley campus area that offers fast and affordable food. italian is my favorite, and honestly, i would choose gypsy's any day over some stuffy over-priced restaurant in SF. the calzones are pretty amazing, just take awhile to pop out. today i tried the crazy alfredo, and at first i wasn't too fond of it, but it grew on me. this place is heaven. ahhhh i love gypsy's! by the way, every single dish is literally under $7 and the portions are HUGE!

For cheap, tasty, fast Italian, this place rocks. Made the mistake of phoning in a takeout order of 2 Godfather's Favorites on a Saturday night. The guy on the phone didn't ask for my name, give me an order number, or anything. He just hung up. After walking into the place I learned why. It was a cluster- you-know-what of Cal students with a huge line ( which moves way faster than it looks). My bad. Next time I will just go directly there to order it and take it out. After finally tracking an employee down, he went in the back and retrieved the bag it had probably been sitting in for 10 minutes. Took it home and gorged...no worries, still piping hot and a cheesy, orgasmic, bed of wonderfulness. Dirt cheap, too! While waiting on the food, saw another customer eating the lasagna which looked amazing...that's next on my list.

This place is not a full service restaurant. It's one of those places where you order at the counter, pay and then wait for your number to be called to pickup your food. They do serve the food on real plates and silverware. The food is amazing though. The price is extremely reasonable. We paid $25 for 2 plates of pastas and a pizza. Ok then, here's the low down on the food we had.

Linguini Carbonara - it was amazing. They load it with lots of pancetta.
Linguini with Clams and Cream sauce - I've never had it with cream sauce. They give you lots of chopped clams and chopped garlic. It was delicious. 
Pizza - we had the Caprese. The toppings were great and fresh. The thin crust had really good flavor but the center got really soggy due to the juices from the fresh tomatoes. I hate soggy crust.

The pasta dishes came with a piece of roasted garlic toast, omg, it was so good.

I love this place! It's not pricey and they give you so much food! The food is always really hot and they give you garlic bread (with actual garlic on it!) which is delicious. The serving sizes are huge! I usually end up taking half of it home and it still tastes delicious the next day. 
I have had the lasagna, gnocchi and chicken and broccoli which have all been amazing (the lasagna was especially amazing!
The staff is pretty indifferent but they are so busy that it doesn't even really matter. There is usually a lot of people but it is still a pretty nice atmosphere to dine in.

Great Location 
Good Prices 
Pasta is great 
Calzones need work- kinda blah 
Quick and Filling

One of two of the best Italian places in Berkeley.

Warning:  lots of very immature, very clueless, very rude and sometimes stinky smelling students swarm this area.

Gypsy's is a great place for pasta, calzones, pizza and sandwiches close to the campus. They have a pretty broad menu for those that love variety. I used to try their different calzones (~$6), and the serving sizes are huge, aka lunch, dinner, and breakfast the next morning.

so delicious!

-Pesto chicken--yumyum and oily.
-Pasta special with eggplant, chicken, and marinara sauce: good!
-Vegetarian marinara pasta stuff: Full of veggies but bland! passss.
-Victor's spaghetti--Beef, onion, tomatoes, and marinara sauce: yum!
Ate there with a friend a few years ago - there was a moth in her salad. No joke - a moth. Enough said.
Calzones are awesome and quite filling. Large varied menu leaves tons left to be tried. Good stuff.

i try not to  yelp a place until i've been there a couple of times . i think its unfair to judge an  establishment after just one visit. with that said...

if i just said the word " gypsys ' on a random night, all the folks that i kick it with would be juiced because this place is just that awesome. 

the SERVICE is great considering how busy they are all the time.

the PRICE is just right for any budget. 7 dollars would get you a hearty italian dish. 6 dollars would get you a giant calzone. 5 dollars a bomb ass meat ball sub. 4 dollars, well i dont know a salad?

the ATMOSPHERE is nice. inside -  its a little small but has that cozy feeling. outside - its walking distance from UC berkeley so after your meal, you can just stroll down telegraph and soak in the culture of the city.

the FOOD is delicious. youre paying fast food price for restaurant quality food. honestly i think its better than some restaurants i been to. if you dont know what to order just close your eyes and point at the menu youd probably enjoy the outcome. the only thing i would not recommend is the lasagna, i didnt like it but then again im not a big fan of lasagna in general so yeah.

i hope this review helped .

This place is the bomb. Went here with a couple of friend. First off this is how Pasta should be priced. For goodness sake why go to olive garden and pay 15 bucks when you can pay 6.50!!!!!! I got the godfather but tried my buddys pesto. From now on Im gettin pesto but the godfather was great as well. Btw incredibly fast service, and the calzones are HUGE. This is now my DEFAULT italian place.

I wasn't even hungry at first, but my friend and these two girls dragged me here and just ordered a bunch of shit and made me try it. 

It turned out to be pretty great. The dishes are prepared very traditionally and also well presented.  I tried the chicken 
fettuccini  with pesto and it was terrific. I also tried the rigatoni with meat sauce and shreaded chicken. It was excellent although the meat sauce had some weird yellow cheese in it that didn't go well with it. That and the garlic bread  having giant chunks of wet garlic on it were the only 2 bad things about this place.

Over all i'd say this place is A OK especially if you are into traditional itialian cuisine.
Best sang good greasy Italian food EVER!!!!!

Gypsy's is a good destination if you're looking for tasty but cheap italian food. I highly recommend the Crazy Alfredo. It's one of the best items on their menu. It's often crowded, but they have extra seating outside.

Clam linguine in white sauce.  It's awesome, and creamy.  And it taste like goodness.

The wait for your food is pretty long, but only because there is a constant flow of people ordering.  Just know that you'll be the last one out if your buddies are ordering elsewhere in the Asian Ghetto.

Oh, their garlic bread is SO good.  It's real garlic that you mush and spread onto your bread, so it taste homemade and fabulous.
Godfather's favorite. My favorite. Can't get over their garlic bread either, absolutely delicious AND with real garlic puree. Definitely recommended for all pasta lovers.
i love this place!  Pollo con pesto everytime!  Never disappoints!  Fast, cheap and YUMMY!

Okay, honestly, I can do the same things they do just standing there look at the cooks.

So what do they do? A couple cloves of garlic, some heavy cream, some meat, and add some heavy cream. Two minutes later, voila! enjoy your meal and $7 forever in the abyss of regret. 

I guess it's okay for college budget, but wouldn't hurt to use a little bit of spice yea? But I guess a dash of something here and there would have doubled the price.

I been at Cal for 3 years and I only been there twice, excluding the times other people ordered for me.

Cheap Italian food, and for the price it's really quite good. I got their number in my phone and often order stuff to pick-up. They also have calzones and pizzas which are both really good. Great place to go for college students.

Yum! I go here all the time for their lasagna! I always say I want to try something new, but I just can't get away from the lasagna - great Italian foods at GREAT prices! Stuck in a little college town next to UC Berkeley, of course the prices would have to match for broke college students, perfect for meeee! Only inconvenience is that it's really smallllll but other than that - it's delicious, so worth it!

Cheap Italian food easily accessible for college student is a pretty accurate description of Gypsy's.

When I come here, I usually get the calzone that they offer. They're priced around $6.25 or so, so cost is about average compared to other places in the Asian Ghetto. The calzone is huge! It's literally like the size of a football cut vertically. My only complaint about it is that it takes too long to cook once you've ordered it, and also that if you get the pesto and chicken calzone, the pesto's green oil just seeps out, making the calzone unappetizing and the chicken is quite dry. I've ordered most of their calzones at least once and always, it's filled with enough cheese to clog your arteries. 

I've tried the gnocci here once, but they give you such a tiny portion of it and drench it in so much white sauce, it's not something I would get again. 

Not the most healthy place to eat, especially the white sauce pastas, but worth trying out if you haven't had it before and want to have the whole Asian Ghetto experience.

I have had quite a lot of Italian food but when i had the Crazy Alfredo i was blown away and this place instantly got a place in my mind and i will remember this place on my yearly  trip to Berkley. The price is great and its ready pretty fast. I came in while I was with a group and we were running on a pretty late schedule and we had to catch BART, I came in and ordered and i had my food ready in time with everyone else without having to sacrifice taste. This place has: good food, great atmosphere, amazing service, and just something about the place that separates it from the rest

Gypsy's Gypsy's Gypsy's.

First off, I've only ordered the Pollo con Pesto, since I am a super duper Pesto fan and that's all I want whenever I am in "Durant Food Court" (Asian Ghetto).

The bread...eh. I could do better myself (no seriously try my garlic bread) their little garlic slice isn't even tasteful. Sorta kills the bread for me.

The pasta is amazing. It's never been over/under cooked but I do have to complain about the creaminess. At times there is wayyyyy too much creaminess and it just becomes a HEAVY meal for me.

The chicken is sometimes dry, but usually really good in the Pollo con Pesto plate.

I recommend Gypsy's, but be wary of your diet, as Christine C.'s interview says, your arteries will suffer.

I was much conflicted in writing this review. I like the place although.. I really cannot stand the abhorring odor/stench that attacks your olfactory system upon stepping into the college-student ridden little restaurant. Nonetheless, they do hold certain appeals.  So, here's a list of what I think are the: most "bang for your buck" dishes,some suggestions as well as general dislikes about the place. 

Best dishes:
Primavera Calzone, Greek Salad (or any other salad on the menu), Lasagna, Fetuccine con Pesto. 

Dislikes: They need to clean up the place! Although they do have a solid consumer population, and cleaning up after college students who probably couldn't change their own diapers isn't easy, it is not excuse to have that kind of smell invade whoever walks through/past the door. 

General suggestions: If you're looking to go there, be sure to evade times such as 1-3, and 5-7, where the mob just over-runs the place.

Cheapest best pasta I've ever had...  I tried the Godfather's favorite and was very satisfied.  I even had to wait until I was back in San Francisco to try it.  For the price, you'd have a hard time finding better.  Want to come back... because portions are also more reasonable than you think.
I love this place!  Cheap, quick food with huge portions, plus it's delicious.  I'm craving it right now!
Love this place. Has some of the best pasta for a reasonable price.

Charges 50 cents for credit card purchases.

Huge portions, always filling. Pretty good food, pretty good deals. Pastas are very creamy, sometimes too creamy. 

Get the Godfather's Favorite or the Crazy Alfredo! Or just about anything else if you can't decide.

Also, the calzone's are huge. Huge. Like bigger than your face huge. And it looks like they come in those pink boxes used in Chinatown for cakes xD

maybe a 5th star if the seating situation was better.  the pasta i got was pretty delicious.  i can't recall the name of it but it was penne marinara with a hint of creme, with mushrooms, spinach, garlic, and olives, i believe.  fairly generous portions.  i tried a few bites of a friends' veggie pizza (with BROCCOLI !!!) and it was awesome.

best pasta: Godfather's favorite...
If you happen to like something Don Vito approves of, the NY Mafia might just spare you.

...but you might die later on from high cholesterol and heart disease. just FYI.

Not very refined food, to be sure, but if you need some basic hunks of meatballs and a boatload of pasta in a hurry and/or late at night, it doesn't get any better in the entire city of Berkeley. The food is good quality and ample, but the place lacks any sort of cozy atmosphere. Yet, I give it 5 stars for saving me from passing out on a street after a long set of classes.

Over the course of my life, my internal ranking of Gypsies has gone from 5-stars (as an underclassmen at Berkeley) down to 4 stars and now even probably a 2 or 3 star place, but I'll average it out. I like how it's quick and pretty cheap. The gnocchi marinara is a good dish, and, like all of their pasta dishes, comes with a piece of warm garlic bread.

The pasta Cappriciosa (I believe it's called that) is also very good.

I saw Carmelo Anthony eating here once. Pretty random, but I guess he had just gone to a Cal game while the Nuggets were in town.

The calzones are enormous and the salads are actually pretty good too.

I honestly don't know why I'm reviewing a place that has this many reviews and great rating because obviously it's known to be good....but here's my two cents.

Order your food before you go if you don't have a lot of time.
Order a calazone and put yourself into a food coma you won't regret.
Laugh at everyone who thinks you just came to class with a pink box full of donuts, when in reality it's your personal ticket to food paradise with a layover in food coma-ville.

Cheap and a lot of food. I got the eggplant sandwich for like, 5 bucks? and it was huge. The bread is good quality, the eggplant is drowning in batter and cheese as you would expect, and they throw on a ton of roasted garlic if you ask for it, which is probably the best thing about this restaurant. You should definitely get the side salad (it's pretty big) in order to add some vegetables to the artery-clogging food here.

I really don't know why I'm writing this. If you're a student at Cal, you have eaten here. Otherwise, you are probably dead inside.

It's good when you're hungover from gameday and it's cold, and it's good when you're depressed from being in the library for 8 hours. If I'm trying to be healthier, I get the shrimp on angel hair or pomodoro. If I'm feeling straight up terrible, godfather's favorite cures all. Just go to the gym a little extra next time.

Pasta tastes good and is cheap but may give you a stomach ache if you haven't built up your tolerance to grease. Most people are obsessed with this place during freshman year and then reach a point where they never want it again in life. Restaurant always smells vaguely like homeless. Ah, memories.

I ordered the carbonara with extra parmesan and added sausage, and I also ordered a side salad (with yummy caesar dressing) and a soda.
IT WAS SOOO GOOD. And cheap too! My order came to around $10, which is pretty decent giving the fact that Gypsy's portions are really generous.
I actually had to take some to go.

The only complaint I have was that the carbonara was a teeny bit dry (I don't know what's up with me and thinking that my food is dry, lol.)

My friend who was with me ordered the combo calzone, and he thought that the calzone was ok, but that the sausage and sicilia calzones are way better.

All in all, Gypsy's is a great place, and it's definitely worth your money.
their spaghetti and meatballs is so disgusting. the pasta is overcooked and bland. the meatballs are literally blocks of rectangular meat and taste like cat.

This italian restaurant is different from one I have ever been to. First off it smells like Cheese the moment you enter. Kinda sickening and kinda not. I like cheese, but when it's too cheesy I feel like I want to barf. Don't worry I didn't barf. 

Anyway this italian restaurant is like fast food, but the quality is plated restaurant style. You order, take your number, wait for them to call your number, and then you EAT! I had the Pollo Con Pesto Pasta and my boyfriend had the Gypsy's Chicken Pasta. Big portions! If I had known that from the beginning, I probably would have shared a dish instead of getting my own. The bread that came with the pasta wasn't that great, but the pasta itself was so damn good! The only thing that was making me hesitant about eating the pasta, was that it was so filling! I felt so heavy with every bite I was taking. After eating half of my meal I felt like a ginormous whale!!! The pesto pasta I had was very cheesy and had lots of pesto sauce (i think it was dripping in oil too). The pasta noodle was yums! The Gypsy's Chicken Pasta looked too creamy. I don't really like creamy stuff. Overall this place serves really heavy food!! Be ready to get food coma after!

I paid $15 for both of us, so like $7.50 per dish? SUPER CHEAP! Especially for Italian food. Open late and a great place for college students on a low budget.

If you've ever seen the episode of "Sex and the City" where Carrie wonders why Big keeps taking her to that shameful Chinese hole, you will understand how I feel about Gypsy's. No, I do not bring my ugly dates to this Mecca of cheap college dining; Gypsy's IS my dirty little late-night secret. Every now and then I will make the trek in the cold, dark night of Berkeley to make sweet, sweet love to a tub of pasta or a calzone the size of a small child. Gypsy's and I have a mutual understanding: I know that I am getting more than what I'm paying for in the way of quantity but should not ask for a whole lot of quality, and Gypsy's knows that I will not be spending the night.

We're also not exclusive, but when I go back, Gypsy's gives me the same love that it did the last time I stopped by. We engage in a tableside romp that is both rough yet tender. The tender part being that the pasta tends to be slightly past the ideal point of al dente, and the rough being that every time a plate is presented before me, I attack it with more gusto than I ever knew myself capable of.

Overcooked pasta aside, the dishes are delicious, and they come with a slice of slightly-toasted bread studded with jewel-like cloves of roasted garlic. You can taste that nothing is homemade, but that's fine. Gypsy's never pretends to be what it isn't, and I've found such authenticity harbored through its maintenance of artificiality one of its more charming traits over my two-year affair. Among my favorites are the Crazy Alfredo, a dish that gels a trifecta of meats (chicken, meatballs, and sausage) with a red wine cream sauce; the Cappriciosa, which couples the sweetness of roasted red peppers with the acidity of a marinara made rich with a dollop of cream; the Funghi, a mushroom dish that packs a punch with the rich headiness of smoked mozzarella; and, of course, their many calzones, which are loaded with tons of cheese and tomato paste (or pesto). The calzones take around twenty minutes to bake, and some people just don't have the patience nor the ingenuity to wait for such delightful confections. I have the latter. I (albeit pathetically) call them up right before I'm to make my journey over; that way, it's practically ready for me when I walk in the door! I love the shiny, brown top that I like to crack like a creme brulee.

The couple of items that I did not much care for at Gypsy's both involved whole chicken breast (in most chicken dishes, they will cut it up for you in thin strips): the chicken piccata and the chicken marsala. Both are pretty delicate dishes, so perhaps it's best to save them for when you're going to a grown-up, chi-chi, jacket-required, no-quickie-in-the-bathroom (we-actually-have-a-bathroom)-policy type of place. At Gypsy's, if you are really looking to nurse your hankering for either dish, expect a thin filet of breast that lingers on the dry side and an alarming absence of much flavor. The sauces didn't do much for me; in the end, the dishes ended up just tasting like... chicken. And who wants that at Gypsy's?

Those are just two items on the menu, out of probably around sixty. Just as long as one lets go of any expectations of staggering cleanliness, creativity, and class, one should find Gypsy's to be the little one-night stand that could, night after night. Really, what do people expect from an Italian restaurant in the section dubbed Asian Ghetto? Ditch the credit card and grab a handful of dollar bills on your way to Gypsy's. It's guaranteed to be at least cleaner than what else you might use those bills on.

I didn't like this place the first time I tried it.
I didn't like this place the second time I tried it.
I didn't like this place the third time I tried it.
I didn't like this place the fourth time I tried it.

You're probably wondering why I keep trying it then. I wonder that too. For some reason I always think this place will be better if I order something else, but it never is. 
I just don't understand why everyone loves this place. I can only guess it's because of it's proximity to campus, or that it's better than the other restaurants in Asian Ghetto.

The pasta here is oily, greasy, and heavy. The feeling I get after eating here is gross, it's like I drank a bowl of msg or something.

So I was reading about this place on yelp all day and finally at lunch went to go eat. I had the calzone primavera. It was good. $6 for a great size personal calzone. I was definitely pleased.

Bad note, which I do understand that it happens, I found an olive pit in the calzone. It was a surprise and I almost lost my teeth.

A lot of the pasta dishes are very heavy and greasy... After eating here, I get a complimentary lip gloss because of all the oil from the pasta. I've tried a lot of different pastas here, and I think the one that is the least heavy is the Pomodoro. It's plain, but it's delicious, and it doesn't make me feel like dying afterwards. Great garlic bread! If you take it to go, eat your garlic bread before it gets soggy in the to go box :(. Calzones are also HUGE. I would probably gain two pounds if I finished one by myself.

Convenient location. Nice prices and serving sizes. Difficult to find seating inside for big groups.

QUICK STORY: I brought my friend, who was a prospective student, to Gypsy's. He was in the process of eating his pasta when a homeless man came up to our table, grabbed his plate, and walked off to a corner to eat it... A worker noticed this and took the plate right away, but this angered the homeless man who threw his fork at the worker and yelled something O_O. Yeah. Great welcoming experience for my friend. He's still came to Cal for college though!
Do you like butter? Because there is roughly an entire stick of it in each one of the orders here.

If you're looking for ambience, keep walking.  It's Berkeley.  Like, practically on campus, Berkeley.  Like, I'm going to kill these packs of students if they don't walk across the street so I can find a damn parking place, Berkeley.  But it's cheap and quick and surprisingly good.  And you get a lot of good for the price.  Try the carbonara.  The students are even kinda cute (in a non-creepy way) when you're not starving and/or pissed as hell from driving around for 8 hours (or 20 minutes) looking for parking.

Yeah..it's good...but I feel like every time I order something with the cream sauce, it's the same taste.  They're obviously using the same sauces for their pastas. 

It's definitely worth it in terms of size and fulfillment, but if you're looking for a healthy meal, look elsewhere.  The chicken salads are pretty worth it - they give a good portion.

I went back to Gypsy's after trying Pasta Bene and I realized how poor it was in comparison. The food at Pasta Bene is so much better than Gyspy's and the prices are the same! The wait time at Gyspy's is almost 30mins guaranteed while it's only 10 mins max at Pasta Bene. Gyspy's definitely has become the perpetual second choice for Italian food after Pasta Bene. Even the selection is smaller at Gyspy's.

I gotta say, this place is a great combination making this a solid 4+star place. First of all the value. The prices are great. $20 can feed two people very well. 
Second the quantity. They give you a lot of food for the few bucks you spend there. For instance, I got a Combo Calzone and spent under $7. According to their signs you can get a salad and soda added on to any plate for a total of $8.99. NOW THAT'S A DEAL!!!! 
Third and most importantly, is the quality. It was quite busy when I went so I waited a few minutes, but it was because you can see,every place is made to order, not because they were falling behind..... IT'S ALL FRESH!!! So the quality is amazing!! I will be going back to this place many more times, that's for sure.

Gypsy's is among the elite of Berkeley Southside cheap eats.  If you can stand the long line during the peak dining hours you will be rewarded with a plate of satisfying carbs that will fill you up and not empty your wallet. 

The food isn't authentic, nor does it try to be.  They serve up good dishes of pastas with nice sauces, huge calzones, and tasty thin crust pizzas.

In my college days I was a fan of the pesto calzones, the chicken gnocci, and the tri-color tortellini (I'm sure there's another name for this dish, but I don't remember it).  I celebrated finishing finals here one semester, and after 22 hours without sleep, it was still a satisfying meal ;)

The pasta here is soooooooo good! I love the pesto, yum! The pizza is good too, although the pizza takes quite a bit longer to be served than the pasta dishes. You get a good amount of great tasting food for a reasonable price.

Good, cheap Italian food in Berkeley's beloved Durant Food Ghetto (there are plenty of other names for the area as well), where usually the Asian choices get all the attention.  I've had a number of things on the menu, and I've liked them all.  I'm especially a fan of Gypsy's Chicken pasta, Gnocchi, Tortellini with baby shrimp, and the pesto pasta.  The pastas are all served with very garlicky bread -- basically a piece of bread with a clove or two of roasted garlic on it -- and the portions are very good.  The pasta dishes are all only $6-$7 each.  Their calzones are also very good, and HUGE!!!  

On a bad note, I've heard that the pizza is just average, and I would probably recommend going to Fat Slice or Blondie's if you're in a pizza mood.

Hole in the wall Italian place, it's no Pasta Pomodoro or Caffe Del Stelle but it gets the job done. I ordered the Chicken Parmigano, and it was pretty good for what it is, if not cooked in butter and with a ton of cheese baked on it. But for $8 with a side salad and a soda, it's not a bad deal. 

Strangely enough, it's in a food court by Cal that is mostly Asian dominated. It's a nice contrast.

this place is awesome! i can't say that it's RIDICULOUSLY good or anything, but the food is VERY delicious for the price, it's around 6 - 8 dollars and they give you very big portions, you will for sure be satiated after a meal from this place

Want to know where to get great Italian food for cheap. The Asian ghetto of course! Where else would you go, little Italy? Nah.

Going to school and being poor makes it hard to find and eat decent Italian food. This food is priced well for what it is, which is cheap Italian food.

I have had almost everything on the menu and there is nothing horrible and nothing exceptional. As yelp describes my three star selection, this place is A-OK indeed. That is all. Move along.
Located by the entrance to the Asian Ghetto, this place serves various pasta plates topped with chicken, seafood, or beef. Cheap ($6-$7), tasty, and their cream sauces are quite filling.

Sooooo many fond college memories at Gypsy's ...
Too bad my liking for the food here has faded over the years. 

Gypsy's is most Berkeley students go-to place for lunch, dinner, and of course late-night dinner since it's basically always open. This place is usually packed, but service is fast and they accept credit cards (a huge plus now that the rest of Ghetto is cash only). 

The calzone here is HUGE and pretty good. They take a lil longer to make but definitely worth an order at least once during your college career. I get the combo, with EVERYTHING in it! As for the pastas, I would say that Godfather's Favorite was once my favorite too. 

Personally, I think the food here has gotten oilier over the years and is too heavy on the cream and butter. I always food-coma after a meal here and it's sadly not one of those happy, blissful food comas.

Italian Fast Food! That alone deserves big juicy red ones!

Their menu is so extensive and filled with a lovely array of options. It's almost aggravating to just choose one! The service is quick as a bunny, and the food.. OH... MYGOD! I honestly would prefer Gypsy's food over Olive Garden or any other high-priced, sit-down Italian restaurant. They offer enormous portions for half the price. They don't skimp out on the flavors AND cheeeeese! Gypsy's is awesome, CHEAP, and so worth a try =)

Gypsy's really is "A-OK." Not bad, but not the best. But not at all bad.
It's a staple for UC Berkeley students mostly because it's convenienty located in the Asian Ghetto right across campus. I doubt most people come here because they think the food is actually of superb quality. Gypsy's is like a nice, reliable buddy that you take for granted and don't really hang out with too much (and don't make an effort to change that fact), but you know will always be there when you need someone quick and dependable (or when no one else will play with you). I mean that in the best way possible.

Their calzone is hands down the best thing on their menu. Calzones take a little longer to make, but it is huge, piping hot, and pretty darn good. And it's chock full of yummy stuff (definition of "yummy stuff" depends on which calzone you order XP). Also, f you order your calzone to go, they will give it to you in a large pink pastry box, so from the outside, it looks like you're eating cake for lunch. Hahaha. That's awesome. X)

Yay! A sit down italian place! And you don't have to leave a tip!

I love Gypsy's because it's not trying to be anything that it isn't. They know they're in a completely different realm than the pasta at say... Cheesecake Factory, but they're damn good at serving up some great pasta for some poor and hungry college students. 

You can't really go wrong with anything on the menu. I really like the Gypsy's Chicken, so that's usually what I get when I go, but I've sampled other things on the menu and they're all pretty tasty. 

If you're looking to get your food quickly (and looking to not have to vulture for a table), I'd suggest coming for lunch; it's crazy in there at dinner time.

Gypsy's!!!! Ahhhhh. I freaking LOVE this place. My favorite I-just-want-freaking-good-food-and-the-ambiance-doesnt-matter Italian restaurant in California, hands down. You can get a delicious meal for $10 here, and not only be full from it but have your taste buds singing to the heavens about it! 

First of all, WORD OF ADVICE: BRING CASH!
They do add an additional charge (about $1) for ordering with credit card. (Merchants get charged for credit card transactions per transaction, so it makes sense.) 

Now, you want recommendations? I highly recommend the Crazy Alfredo or the Godfather. Both are VERY delicious. Personally I prefer the Crazy Alfredo a little bit more, but they both really hit the spot. 

I know this place doesn't look fancy, and it's located right in the heart of what the locals call "Asian Ghetto" (there are a lot of ghetto looking asian restaurants around this area), but this place is really the best bank for your buck Italian food in the area.

Definitely worth the drive here.

Hearty, cheesy, warm, and carbalicious are the four most important adjectives I'd use to describe Gypsy's. 

Every dish I've ever had here has fulfilled my yen for hearty/cheesy/warm/carb goodness. My personal favorites are: Pollo (chicken) con pesto, chicken piccata, Godfather's favorite (this is the ultimate!), meatball sandwich, eggplant sandwich (yummy marinara sauce,) and any/all of the calzones. The garlic bread (with a chunk of warm, soft garlic) seals the deal!

I have delighted twice now in Gypsy's delectable Eggplant Parm sandwich.  It's big, hot, and oozing.  And less than 6 dollars.  Or maybe a little change added on for tax.  

It is not the quickest of meals, but it is priced quite right.  The calzones look massive and the next time I go I will be trying one of these bad boys.

HUGE pesto chicken calzone for less than $7. I could only eat half, so I saved the rest for later. Perfect place for a poor hungry college student. 

Just to keep in mind.. If you're in a hurry, the calzones take a bit longer than the other restaurants in the courtyard since they have to bake it. Mine probably took about 15 minutes.

So I used to like Gypsy's because it was quick, relatively cheap, and garlicky and right smack in the middle of Durant Ave. conveniently known as the Asian Ghetto.  Then I got sick once after I ate here.  Which is okay because I self-admittedly have a weak stomach and lactose intolerance + cream sauce doesnt work well.

But then they tried to steal my cell phone those bastards and I never went back.  Story: left my cell phone on the table one day after I ate here and went back literally 5 minutes later to find it gone.  Asked the cashier 3 times and each time he told me no one had found it.  Went back, desperate, the fourth time and the bus boy told me it was in the cashier's drawer.  Confronted him about it and he reluctantly gave it back. NO APOLOGIES.  SHADY.

But if you must go, try the Godfather's Favorite, it's greasy creamy goodness on a plate for $6.  Berkeley college food doesn't get much better than this.  Calzones are good too but they take forever.

I've come here a few times, and I gotta say, this place is delicious and very good.

Every time I've come, I get Gypsy's Chicken. I like how you get a lot of food for a good price, and all the menu items average to about $7-8 dollars.
I like their bread because they use roasted garlic that is very fresh and it goes very good with the pasta. They do orders very fast, so you'll have your food relatively quick and enjoy it even quicker. =]

Gypsy's very popular, which means the place is usually really crowded, and there isn't much seating inside the restaurant or outside because it's in the Asian ghetto which is also usually crowded.

If you don't mind waiting inside a loud, crowded restaurant for some quality italian food for a reasonable price, this is the definitely the place for you.

C'mon UCB students! You clearly haven't ever had real Italian food (I'm not talking about yuppy stuff either.). Where are all the Italian people in the bay area? Oh yeah, in San Francisco.

How could you give this place more than 3 stars? The food here blows.

MONSTRO servings, very rich and filling meals (you won't find any watery linguini here).  They take cards, which is exceptional in Berkeley, and they serve calzones that are bigger than my head.

Garlic bread is a piece of sourdough (I think) with cooked garlic perched on top of it.  Yum-may.

Costs are reasonable.

Wash your glasses before you use them, though.  They're known to be iffy.  Also, Gypsy's can get seriously crowded.

Definitely a good place to go for hungry college students.

Their calzones are huge and filling. When I say filling, I mean FILLING. I shared a pesto calzone with a friend and when we cut it in half, green oil just started leaking out of that thing like no tomorrow. It was still delicious though (just forgot about calories/oil/sat. fat intake and such).

Their pasta is also pretty rich and flavorful. I had the....something with sausage. 

Overall, I pretty good place for college students to grab some grub. Just watch out for the oil/cream/cheese-induced coma afterwards.

Here's a bet: of all the places in the world where the menu is on a wall and has two columns of prices, one for those paying with cash and one for those paying with card, you can't get Italian appreciably better than from here.

Gypsys gets a lot of good reviews, but I think its a little skewed.  It really depends on what you're ordering.

The pasta dishes are ok.  Too oily for my preference.  You can feel the fat you're eating every time you order a pasta meal, especially the ones with Alfredo.  It's basically white sauces with pools of oil and grease in it.  I usually feel pretty queasy after wards.

The salads are also only so so.  I've rarely ever seen anyone eat them.  This place is always crowded too, so be prepared to deal with so so service and antsy people.  There's no other good Italian place on the south side, other than pizza.


Their Cal Zones are legit though.  Real legit.  Best Calzone I've ever had, and it's really hard to find a good Calzone.  Just order it.  Words do not do it justice.

Gypsys gets a lot of praise from current students, and its well deserved.  They treat Cal students pretty well.  But when you graduate and your an alumni, you find that you like it so much simply because it brings up good memories.  The food itself is okay.

Except the Calzones.  Did I mention they're legit?

Gypsy's is reasonably priced, filling, yummy, and carbilicious - its sure to make your tummy feel warm and happy. I've left Gypsy's with a smile on my face every single time. Their calzones are huge and you can easily share (unless you're feeling greedy) and their servings are enough to feed two people or for two servings (lunch & dinner if you're low on $). My favorite is the Pollo Con Pesto. Yay pesto! I love how they serve their garlic bread with oven baked garlic pieces. Mmmm. The only thing that bothers me is the long line and crowded restaurant but waiting is never a huge problem. They try to get order ready as fast as they can! I know I will enjoy going to Gypsy's for tasty Italian food throughout my years in college!

I forgot to mention on a previous review that although the prices here are very cheap the kitchen cooks and busboys are ALL ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS FROM MEXICO! With so many Americans out of work you would think that they would hire some. But then again, the owner would not be able to exploit the workers for cheap pay.

Gypsy's is a well-oiled machine, in every sense.

You can just tell.  The guy at the register is in the Zone, permanently.  Their pasta dishes are wonderfully creamy.  They know how to garnish the cheese jusssst right so that it remains suspended in gooey melted phase, somewhere between solid and string.  Perfect.

Unfortunately, not so perfect are the calzones, which are certainly big enough (but still no match for the Great Joe!) but lack that same meltiness that the pasta possesses; in fact, the 'zones have a nasty habit of being merely lukewarm in the middle.  The personal pizzas, on the other hand, are delectable and are very well-portioned as well.  

Will Gypsy's make you fall whimsically in love like dogs in a Disney movie?  Not quite.  Will Gypsy's simply fill you up right with fattening and famous food?  Oh yes.

Gypsy's has the best pasta I have ever had in my entire life.

I'm going to start this off by saying that I am REALLY picky about my pasta.  My parents both went to college in Italy so I grew up eating Italian food all the time and have been to some of the "best" Italian places in the Bay Area.  I've also been to Italy.

Having said that, no pasta I've ever had matches the perfection that is Gypsy's.  I have had the shrimp alfredo, the godfather's favorite, the pesto, and the carbonara.  They are all amazing.  They're cooked perfectly and they taste like pasta is SUPPOSED to taste.  

I go out of my way to return to Gypsy's since I graduated from Cal.  No place will ever compare.  It might be worth a move back to Berkeley someday.

Carbonara: In the first few bites, the cream is pleasantly thick and creamy, but the after taste is unpleasant and CLOYING. 

Pesto Chicken Pasta: Pesto sauce is way too creamy and too rich on the whole. The sauce is too thick. Not refreshing. The chicken: Totally flavorless and tasted plastic. 

Okay, this is not a fine dining restaurant. So don't expect a sophisticated tasting and dining experience. But even so, the price is ridiculous for the quality of food you get. I'd rather go to Thai Basil or that Chinese restaurant next door if I were to fork out the same amount of $.

I end up going to Gypsy's whenever I want to feel insanely satiated/bloated - usually, after a long week of tough classes or work. The first time I went to Gypsy's, I didn't think that the portions were that large. The quantity provided in the dishes looked rather standard for Italian fare, and even with the garlic bread, I didn't think I would be so full. The penne proved me wrong.

 I ordered a penne gorgonzola to go, and decided to eat it in my dorm room while watching Dexter. My first impressions of the pasta were fairly good. Good gorgonzola flavor; sauce was slightly too rich, but it was tasty enough; pasta was cooked well; garlic bread was...interesting (never had a whole garlic clove on my bread before). 

 And then, halfway through the pasta, it hit me: I didn't want to eat anymore. The problem was, my stomach felt full, but my hunger pangs were still not satisfied. It felt like the pasta was sticking to the walls of my stomach, refusing to let peristalsis move it to free up some room. But I wanted to eat more, so I brazenly consumed more and more of that gut-sticking pasta. My memory seems to have failed me, since I can't remember what happened after. Probably went into severe food coma and fell asleep. 

 My lesson was learned: if you eat Gypsy's, stop before you get that feeling in your stomach. Even for me, a college male who eats a fair amount, one order should probably be enough for a meal and a half, if not more. 

 On the taste of the food - it ranges from slightly unpleasant to decent, but never fantastic. I've had the penne gorgonzola, carbonara, funghi (my favorite), gnocchi (not good - too sticky), and a few others that weren't too memorable. The sauces are usually a super-heavy cream sauce, or a red sauce that's supposed to be made of tomatoes. The meat is usually a little tough or too fatty, both of which probably contribute to the filling factor. 

 Go to Gypsy's for the price, the portions, and the proximity. If none of those are too much of a concern, you're definitely better off going somewhere else.

Great food!
The gypsy chicken is awesome!

We chowed down here after a day as tourists hanging out in Berkeley. We were 50-somethings with two teens in tow. I imagine that the reviews here would likely divide by age; anyone 21 or younger, this place is a dream -- a cheap pasta feedathon and place to see your friends. Anyone older, it's a raucous, rushed, thrown-together approximation of food, mystery water glasses and napkins, and no bathroom -- or at least no bathroom they will let you use, even when you try to reason with them, even when it's pouring buckets of rain outside, and even when you, as instructed, march down to the lady at the Chinese restaurant at the end of the alley and ask for the key, which, naturally, this being the hard-as-nails Bay Area, she will refuse to give you. 

Summing up: your kid will enjoy the place on a visit or if they go to Berkeley. From the rest of us: screw you, Gypsy's.

OH GOD, SO GOOD!! Everything I have ordered here has always been good. The prices are decent, the portions are good, and the pasta is QUALITY for what you are paying. I think my favorite would be the pollo gorgonzola (I LOVE CHEESE) and the pesto penne. I also like how they give you a piece of bread with garlic on it...delicious! If you need Italian close to the Berkeley campus, this is the place to go!

What is not to like about this place. Me and my friends loved going here because the $5-$6 dishes gave you decent portions with good taste. This is prolly one of the few places I actually miss about Btown...

BIGGGG, delicious portions at VERY affordable prices! Plus, service is fast and friendly. What more can you ask for???

It's definitely a tasty carbo-loading stop!

I love Gypsy's! I went here twice this past week. I have to limit my amount of visits though because this stuff definitely isn't low carb.

Godfather's Favorite and Gypsy's Chicken are two very tasty dishes. They are somewhat similar except one has pancetta and egg while the other has mushrooms and garlic. The sauce, chicken, and penne pasta seem to be the same in both dishes. It's a safe bet to go with a creamy white sauce. I tried the red sauce on my friend's gnocchi dish and the tomato flavor was too powerful. After mixing some of her red sauce with my white sauce it mellowed out the tanginess. 

The bread alone deserves it's own little section. Roasted garlic cloves nestled on a a chunk of sourdough bread. So yummy, so garlic-y, and so bad for your breath.

Unfortunately this place is cash only and tax isn't added on the menu prices. I only had $8 the first time I went here, which meant I couldn't order the special (any pasta + a fountain drink + side salad for 7.99). Instead I ordered just the pasta which cost me 6.99 (before tax). On my second visit I was able to get the combo, but then felt like it wasn't really necessary to get a giant bowl of just okay salad with my pasta.

They're somewhat quick! I normally receive my order within 10 minutes of ordering it. This is a good place for lunch if you're craving Italian and don't want to dish out lots of money at a fancy sit down restaurant.

I love the food here.... cheese ravioli was YUMMY and I really liked the cesar salad.

Pros:
Price (Geared toward the college crowd)
Location (Pretty central w/ a small parking lot acroos the street)
Speed (Even thought it is busy almost ALL of the time you don't have to wait long)

Cons:
Atmosphere (College students, rushed and loud)
Cleanliness (How clean is this place? Your guess is as good as mine.)
Service (NOT a sit-down type of place)
Health-kick (on a diet?.. keep moving!) 

All in all if you are out in the Berkeley area and feel like some good, greasy Italian food you have come to the right place. If you are on a romantic first date try Trattoria La Siciliana on College Ave. 

TIP:
Order your food to go. 
Eat somewhere else so that you can enjoy the food and your company.

The food is fast, cheap and good, but not amazing. It definitely satisfied my craving for Italian food without paying the usual $20-30 per meal. We ordered a beef calzone and lasagna for only $13 and we didn't even finish the food!

Yes, the food is greasy and may cause indigestion, but the price is just too good to pass up for all that  gooey madness!

Definitely the #1 spot in the Ghetto. I've gone to school / worked at Berkeley for around 7 years now and can consistently rely on this place for a good hearty (and unhealthy) meal. I've had everything on their menu except the salads, so can speak on everything there. 

The pastas are pretty damn good; I'd say better than a Pasta Pomodoro type place, and for the price, you're getting a real deal. Gypsy's Chicken, Carbonara (which is surprisingly hard to find on any menu), Chicken Marsala are my usual favorites. The calzones are humungous and are really filling. It's not all bread and there's a lot of content in there. I'd recommend pesto and combo. Get some ranch on the side and you're set. They take about 5-10 minutes longer than the pasta orders, so maybe give them a call ahead and get them cooking it in advance. The sandwiches aren't my favorite, but they suffice. It's really sloppy, so watch out if you've got a white shirt on. The pizzas aren't that bad too, but my alliance for pizza's with Cheeseboard or Zachary's in Berkeley. 

Overall, their menu's pretty greasy and fatty. You're not gonna see any light stuff on there. It gets crowded during lunch, but the rotation's pretty fast so give it a try even at its busiest time.

The "Italian" food I've hated because it's highly overrated.

The "Crazy Alfredo" is pathetic and quite far from authentic.

The calzones are rather enormous for me, who eats small portions

The pizza I ordered looked like a pile of barf and grease, because of its hodgepodge of toppings and cubes of cheese. Since I'm lactose intolerant, I only ate part of it, then offered the rest of the pie to a bum, though I'm not sure if he even ate some...

It's an insult to even equate this with Italian, just cuz they put a piece of "garlic bread" on the side don't mean it's happenin'

And I don't care how cheap it is, the servers are whack and the food tastes like shit...ake mushrooms from hell ; )

Gypsy's, the wannabe Trattoria, freakin sucks, Mona Lisa in North Beach is a better place to spend your bucks.

If you're a sensitive nelly with a weak stomach and a hunger for paying steep prices for Italian food, this is not the place for you! 

Gypsy's is the perfect place for a quick bite at a reasonable cost. Typically when you crave Italian cuisine you expect to break the bank but that is not the case with Gypsy's. 

We purchased a plate of lasagna and a calzone for only 13 dollars and some odd cents. I don't know about you but I would never expect to pay ONLY 13 dollars for two plates of Italian food. 

The calzone was big but not hefty. I expected to have to flex a little muscle when I picked up this bad boy but unfortunately my 6 inch biceps had little to no trouble carrying out the calzone. Now some of you may ask, why the hell does weight matter? Well for those people that have a big appetites, weight matters!!! It may be healthier to eat less but guess what, I am craving Italian food! I've thrown the idea of 'healthy' out the window! 

The calzone had a good balance of cheese, tomato sauce and steak. It was tasty but not overwhelmingly flavorful. It lacked salt and various other spices. I like my food to have a kick and this barely had a weak slap at most. 

The lasagna was tasty but I only got a few bites since my sweet GF continuously stabbed me with her fork every time I reached for some. I can only say that for 6 dollars or so, it wasn't bad. 

Yes, the food is greasy and far from 5 star cuisine but when you're on a budget and want to satisfy a big appetite, you cannot go wrong with Gypsy's.

Terrible, terrible, TERRIBLE.  

Unless you are very drunk or a semi-retarded college freshman who's too busy to cook and too broke to afford a good meal, DO NOT EAT HERE.  Even if you're stoned it's a bad idea -- this is the shittiest "Italian" food I've ever had.  I don't mind greasy food and I don't mind cheap food, but I mind this.  

My sister (a Berkeley student) recommended this place to me and my husband as a good late-night place to eat.  It smelled like garlic when we walked in, so thought it might be decent and flavorful.  It is neither.  The pasta is overcooked to a degree which I have never seen in a restaurant.  I mean, really, guys?  You can't cook pasta according to the directions on the bag?  The garlic bread is soggy and limp with a giant clump of mushy, disgusting looking garlic on top.  The pizza is disgusting but, sadly, is the best dish we got.  The ravioli alfredo is dry and may be by Chef Boyardee.  

Unless you think that going gaga over bad food is "hip", don't believe the hype -- this place is crap.

Taste: 3
Value: 4
Service: 3

I always get either the combination calzone or Godfather's favorite. The food is so-so, and the prices are pretty cheap. I don't come here very often anymore, especially since there are better places in Southside.

I've been familiar with this place ever since my sisters went to Berkeley, so it's strange that today was my first time actually ordering there! My sisters got a greek salad and fungi pasta while I got a meatball marinara sandwich. I tried all three and they were so delicious! Not only that, but while I was waiting for the order, my eyes couldn't stop wandering over everyone else's orders. There were so many different pastas I saw that I wanted to order more! The prices are so reasonable and it makes me want to go back to try all the items on the menu =)

This place is a bit pricey and food takes a while to come out, especially the calzones. I've tried the pesto calzone and most of their chicken pastas. I do not recommend the gnocchi because it was kind of dry, but I recommend the Crazy Alfredo, Gypsy's Chicken, and Pollo con Pesto dishes. The food is amazing but it's just expensive for a college student's budget.

The combo calzone is sooooo good and huge! Definitely enough for two people to share. I also really like the pesto pastas and the crazy alfredo (the portions are pretty big as well). The sandwiches are okay... I would stick with the pastas and calzones though. I also wouldn't recommend the ravioli...you only get like 10 pieces and I finished everything in less than 5 minutes! (usually the pasta is enough for two meals for me).

Very convenient (accepts card unlike so many other places at Asian Ghetto) and cheap for us college students!

For a college town where "posh" will not get any customers and where everyone is concerned about CHEAP and AWESOMENESS..

Gypsy's..seriously. no joke for the Italian Stallion choice..
Its not a nice date nite place, but its not supposed to be..
Fast food Italian.

Im glad this place has an average score of a solid 4 stars with 300+ review to back it up.. because it AT LEAST deserves that from the PRICE/FOOD/YUMMIE ratio at a college town..

wassup with all these low scores?

Disclaimer: Yes its crazy unhealthy.. but so is everything Italian that tastes good.. cmon.. and the food does not suck at all.. I read some things about grease.. how other places dont use that much oil or no butter.. dude.. this place makes you full for $10.. cmon..

they also give you TONS OF FOOD..

The Godfather Special - OMGAH..
Calzone - Straight up Cow Utter..ya. that Big.. looks like a tumor on yo plate..
Funghi Plate - full of mushrooms, linguine and smoked mozarrella

Ya. Heart Attack till you possibly Yak attack.. but its so yummie in my tummie..

people still go to McDonalds to order Muffin Tops Super Sized and Butt Sloppies to go..cuz its good and yummie for $1.. But I give McDs a negative (-)10000 stars.. cuz their food is made from tampons..

cheap college italian food next to berkeley...it's good.  I had the Godfather's favorite.  I loved the garlic bread and for what i'm paying, it's a good italian pasta dish.  Great portions and opens late...what can you ask for in a college town?

But let me just say: I've never had so much sodium in my pasta...they put more than your typical chain restaurants.
