My lips are already thick and I swear, I woke up this morning with the thickest lips I've ever had in my life.  My lips were hurting because it was stretched beyond what my fat lips are capable of handling.  I looked like a platypus.  

I've never had sore lips from going to bed after eating a dish.  Gypsy, calm down a bit!  and no, it's not from kissing.....i wish.

I give it 4-star for the price of it! They are so fast and the portions are very generous. 
I  always get the "Godfather's Favorite," which has penne, chicken, carbonara, in a creamy-ish sauce. It always tastes the same, never fails! However, I would like to say, that they may not be the cleanest kitchen ever. The person taking the money, should definitely wash his hands before touching the food. I think I saw it once or twice, that he didn't wash and was handling the garlic bread. 

In reality, I would give this place a 3.5, due to the sanitary reasons.

This place is hands-down the best place to eat near the Berkeley Campus. 

Their Calzones are amazing, and the Godfather's Favorite is to DIE FOR! + their salad, soda deal is good too. 

Definitely a place to try if you're visiting Berkeley! :)

Good pasta for a good price. I didn't completely fall in love like other people when I tried it, but its a lot better than many other places.

Pasta is always cooked just right and the sauce is thick, just the way I like it.  There are some places that give you a lot of sauce, which can overwhelm the pasta, but this place gives you just the perfect amount. There is also always a lot of meat and vegetables (if you ordered a dish with those items), and it is very well worth your money. Definitely will come back.

Had one of the specials -- shrimp, scallops w/ tomato cream sauce...really good :)  went around 11:45 and they were still open! 

a hint for late-night eaters: closes down exactly at 12am even if the door's open.

Ordered the Chicken and Broccoli tonight for $7.50

This was on the healthier side, meaning no sauce drenching pasta. But I thought it was a bit plain.  Chicken was a bit dry but if you let it sit still in the oils in your to go box, it will do the trick! Sounds gross but it works!

This was an average dish. Nothing too special... Maybe I should of stuck with the one I always order, The Godfather.

as far as cheap eats goes, gypsy's is definitely a dependable, to-go place. most items are generally quite good, though tomato based sauces tend to be a tiny bit bland. drown your pity in the fake parmesan cheese and red pepper flakes, provided on every table. 

extremely cheap pizza and calzones as well, all freshly baked, and good enough to make you think twice about eating at blondies or fat slice. 

i myself make frutti di mare a regular meal whenever here, the chicken dishes tend to use dry chicken meat, but the pesto and cream sauces are very rich and very good indeed. 

i'm on a diet though, i miss it all ;*[

Other than Sorrento, this is the only place in Berkeley you can get pasta and leave paying less than $8 a person. It helps that you order at the counter and don't have to tip. Another good thing: it's open super late.

The bad: the food is only okay. Every entree comes with a piece of bread with a few roasted garlic cloves which sounds better than it actually is.

I have to say that this is one of my most frequent stops when I'm in Berkeley.  The one thing that I always order is the Linguine Clams.  It's incredibly creamy, full of little clams with bursts of intense flavor, and the sauce is just dreamy all together.

I've also tried the Calzones and I was really impressed --it's enormous and stuffed with gooey cheese goodness along with whatever your heart's desire. 

The prices are very reasonable and outstanding.  Their portions are very generous and the food is extremely hearty and filling.   

I used to not like Italian food at all until I tried out Gypsy's.  I've been enlightened since then.  

I do have to say that sometimes their dishes can be a hit or miss.  It does really depend on how crowded and full they are.  It's usually occupied by college students throughout the day and night.  Sometimes there can be a huge long line with about 15 people ahead of you or there can be no line at all.  It does vary.  

If it's a full house, the tables can be a bit troublesome.  When I know it's full, I tend to take my order to go. 

The parking here is difficult, especially on the weekend.  I usually park up about two blocks near the hotel nearby, but since everything is in walking distance anyway, it's not much of a pain to park a bit further.

Cheap student priced 
Huge Portions
Legit Italian food

Recommend:

1) Fettucine Alfredo- A little rich on the sauce but  still delicious
2) Pollo Pesto- for the pesto lover like myself

WOW! 
5 dollar pasta dish still exists!
I can't believe that food here tastes even good.

Great for a quick and cheap late night meal, large servings and rich sauces. The kinda place that will satisfy any Italian food craving. The owner is very efficient with orders (kinda reminiscent of the soup Nazi but definitely not as mean!)

But whenever I eat here I prefer to do take out because this place is always crawling with undergrads in their PJ bottoms. Oye.

In the interest of full disclosure I will admit that I haven't been to Gypsy's in about a year.  This isn't, however, because my tastes have refined to the point that I no longer crave their sub-par greasy Italian fare.  No, it is because I have taken a vow to never set foot in this less-than-fine establishment again, nor give the owner another cent of my money.

I had been going to Gypsy's for about 4 years prior to our bitter split.  Increasingly I noticed that the food was getting worse, while the service was becoming almost intolerable.  Still, on a student's budget, and with few options within walking distance of the bars open late enough, I continued to come in for favorites like the pollo gorgonzola and sausage calzone.  I also have always appreciated that they have a side salad option with entrees for less than two bucks.  

But every time I made it to the cash register, I would ask my self, why?  Why am I putting up with this snotty person, who will barely look at me while I am ordering?  Is he even writing down what I am saying?  Obviously not, because those people ordered long after I did, and they got their food first.  WHERE IS MY SALAD?!?!?!  And how much is this frustration worth?  Average pizza?  Bready calzones?  Limp noodles?

My last night with Gypsy's was a total disaster.  Like they somehow knew we were on the verge of breakup, Gypsy's ignored me, got my order wrong, and then flung it at me (upside down!) with an air of disgust and no hint of apology.  Right then I decided to take a stand.  No more Gypsy's.  Not ever again.

No. Just, no. Way too heavy on the flavors, and the amount of cream they use is criminal

Take lukewarm noodles, meat, and butter, and smack yourself in the face with them. Then have a friend kick you repeatedly in the gut. It'll feel about the same as having a meal at Gypsy's.

Which one of these is not like the other? In the midst of the Durant Food Court (aka DFC, 'Asian Ghetto'), this fast food Italian joint provides a nice option for those who aren't into East Asian grub. It also closes at MIDNIGHT, which is freakin' awesome (dang you Berkeley ordinance). 

+ Food comes out in a hurry (except the calzone, but it's their best item)
-  Ingredients are not fresh, does a damage to my tummy every time!
-  Place is not well kept, it's really messy
-  Kitchen maintenance is one of those things you ignore so you can eat here

Final Call:
I've only been here when it's pushing midnight and out of other options.

********************

Munchies:
1. Funghi
     + Sauce is good, mushroom gives it a good chunkiness
     -  Use REAL cheese, please!
2. Calzones (all of 'em)
     + Making it fresh locks in the juices and flavors
     -  Gotta wait an extra 15+, depending on crowd
3. Garlic bread
     -  What's up with the yucky spread?

This will make the Sicilian side of my family cry, but the Gypsy's's, much like The Olive Garden, is... *wait for it* my secret pleasure. 

Wait!!! Before you begin casting stones, hear me out!!! I know, I know. How can you call this Italian food? What a disgrace!

So to compromise, I will describe Gypsy's as Italian AMERICAN restaurant. When said like that, it makes it almost... forgivable, doesn't it?

Anyway, this is one place in the Durant Square (more endearingly known as the "Asian Ghetto") that I secretly like. Never have I been able to say it aloud for the harsh lashing of tongues from my peers and colleagues, but here I am in all of my shameful glory. Naked and vulnerable I am, at the mercy of fellow Yelpers who WILL look kindly on my review and AGREE with me!!!

Yes, the pasta is kind of on the oily side. Yes, the garlic bread is half-heart-felt (just kind of tossed in there). Yes, the crust on their pizza kind of looks like a play-doh puddy dough, but WHO CARES???

It is DARN GOOD!!! At a really decent price too! I love almost everything this place has to offer and I stick by my words, no matter who says what and what gets thrown at me (I prefer words over any physical, tactile objects, thankyouverymuch). 

Italian food snobs and you foodies, before you judge, just try the place. THEN judge. Mind you that this is not fine dining, this is not authentic Italian food and that this is kind of sort of the fast food American version of Italian food. So when expecting this, the experience can be just... sinfully heavenly.

I've definitely had better Italian food. I love their calzone and vegetarian pizza. 

But try to avoid this place for your own health.

recommend the chicken and vegetarian dishes. calzones are pretty good too. beef pastas are hit or miss (mostly misses). seafood pastas, special pies, and sandwiches are abysmal. 

I've been eating the same thing here for 4 years - lemon chicken salad, extra lemon, no dressing.

The Funghi is my all-time favorite (smoked mozzarella & mushrooms galore); Gypsy's Chicken is also really good. Good prices for great food! Was a staple in college and I always stop by for a meal when I'm in Berkeley.

Um..ok, how did this place win "Best of Berkeley" for best Italian Food? I thought about this and I should have known...whatever is cheap and convenient for college kids is what will win--it doesn't even have to be good. I ordered a calzone and spaghetti and meatballs and it wasn't bad, but it wasn't delicious either. The homemade meatballs did not taste fresh. Definitely not good enough to win a title.
5 stars enough said :)

For a little hole in the wall, this place rocked! It's a good place to go to for some late-night grub. I've tried both the calzone and linguine with clams - both were exceptional. Portions were great. As someone mentioned, the place is small. Seating is limited. I'd love to try out more stuff since the menu seemed pretty extensive. Prices were very good. Definitely going back.

4.5 stars! where else can you get an Italian meal that comes with salad and a drink for just $8?! GYPSY'S!! seriously, i can't even find that in davis. Gypsy's is right next to UC Berkeley and it is such a great location for students who are eating under a budget! i kinda wish davis had a Gypsy's!

WHY the 4.5 stars and not the full 5 stars?! well, they charge 50 cents for a refill and the cup is a small size. =/ 

so you can get ANY item on the menu for $8 and it comes with a salad and a small fountain drink.  i got the Linguine Clams w/ Tomato Sauce $6.69.  it also comes in cream too.  i have to say that the portion was HUGE! it comes with garlic bread and baked with real garlic on the top.  my other 2 friends ordered the $8 meal and they couldn't finish either.  and my other 2 friends who shared the $8 meal couldn't finish their plate either! of coursee, i finished the salad, and the linguine clams!! it was DELICIOUS!! ahaha

so the Linguine Clams with tomato sauce was DELICIOUS!! it had a wine taste to it, which it should have.  there were lots of clams in the dish and very saucey too.  

the garlic bread was also DELICIOUS!! baked with REAL garlic. yum yum 

the salad comes in in either italian, ranch or caesar dressing.

the only downside is the 50cent charge on refill =/

the decor is small. at first i thought it was an asian fast food restaurant, since my friend who brought us there kept saying that we were going to the 'asian ghetto' o_O it is pretty clean there. they are very prompt at cleaning the tables right after the customers leave. 

i can't wait to come back here the next time i visit berkeley!
i got a 10" caprese pizza.. awesome! *drooooooooool*

Awesome: Cheap. Huge. Delicious. 

The pictures say it all. And yes, it is as delicious as it looks.

a wee bit expensive for asian ghetto-ness standards (but hey it's italian).. but the godfather's favorite is just.. orgasmic. straightforward and fast service, tasty and satisfying portions. i love gypsy's!

I think the asian ghetto is defined by two infamous restaurant s--- one being Thai Basil and the other Gypsy's. (Though, the term "asian ghetto" doesn't exactly fit well with italian cuisine...)

Gypsy's surpasses the quality of many fancy italian restaurants I've been to. I think good food should not be limited to their location and decor. 

My recommendations: 
Godfather's Special, Crazy Alfredo, Shrimp Tortellini, and the Calzones. The pastas are rich in BUTTER which is probably why it is sooo darn good. I've actually stood there secretly and watch the guys cook my pasta. I swear they used like 1/3 of a stick of butter for each serving. That description is not meant to discourage you from coming to this place because ALL pasta dishes require that much oil! Anyways, the sauce is rich in cream and it's definitely possesses a unique "gypsy's"  taste that is hard to find elsewhere. 

If you wanna be a bigger fatty, walk across to king pin donut and get some donut holes for dessert! ;)

2 or 3 years ago, this used to be my favorite place to go whenever I crave Italian food. I love their bronx tail, I never really tried other dishes. Anyway, overtime the price have gone up slightly; the food doesn't taste as good, and the garlic bread is just not fresh. And what sup with the dude at the cash register providing service and doesn't look like he want to be there?

The food here is delicious, fast (for the most part), and cheap! I love the Gypsy's Chicken! But everything on the menu is really good. Each dish comes with bread with roasted garlic. The pasta dishes range from $6-8.

Also, the calzones are AMAZING and big, but do take a little bit longer since they have to bake it fresh when you order. It is worth the wait though! The combo is always a good choice. Not a bad deal for only $6-7!

They also have a combo deal now with a pasta dish, salad and drink for $7.99. Haven't tried it yet since I usually don't want salad when I come here, but it seems like a good deal. They also accept credit cards which is very convenient especially since I don't usually carry cash with me.

Gypsy's is popular, but even with ample seating, it is sometimes difficult to find a table inside during lunch or dinner. You can't really go wrong with anything on the menu!

Ah Gypsy's, every southsider's favorite Mexican-run Italian restaurant.  The pasta is just absolute creamy fattening comfort food, and their calzones are enormous.  I think I'd gain 10 pounds a month if I ate there everyday and I'd get an aneurysm pretty soon too.  But oh so delicious.
i'd choose gypsy's over pasta pomodora or the old spaghetti factory anyday!

Mmmm Calzone.  I miss you so.  I started salivating the other day when my friend talked about getting a calzone at Gypsy's since we were in Berkeley the other day.  I was bummed that I had to go to Zachary's that night.  Don't get me wrong.  Zachary's is awesome, but the pizza's so expensive.  I just remember the days when I would order a calzone and it came out it the pink donut boxes that a dozen usually come in and realized that the calzone was taking up that space.  *drool*.  I will eat you again one day.  I promise!

Once in a while, something comes along that makes me think, "Gosh, I wish I were a student again."  But then I looked at the greasy pimply faced varsity athlete sitting at the table across from where I was sitting and reality sets in.  I couldn't even understand the things that he was saying, and I don't *think* it was an accent.  But the girl he was talking to was so into the conversation, SO into it.  

The food here has gigantic portions and thus I understand why it is so crowded here.  Really, would you rather have a paltry serving of sushi, some overly sweet BBQ, Chinese food *again*, donuts for dinner, or a not too bad italian meal that could easily stretch in to 2 meals?  If I were a student again, that's the kind of thinking that would rule my decisions.

The Funghi Pasta was rich and delicious.  But the smoked moz cheese on top was a little too rich.  The sauce was delicious and not too buttery.  The calzones were the size of my head.  I am not fond of the way italian sausages are seasoned.  Unless it on pizza and then it's not considered italian sausage.  But the calzone had enough cheese to drown a puppy.  It was stuffed with cheese, sauce, sausage, mushrooms.  Overwhelming.  

Next time I might try their pesto.  I saw many people ordering it.  

It sure is crowded.  And there are some homeless people that talk to plants right outside.  But now that the weather is better, there is seating in the courtyard that is not entirely unpleasant.
i ordered a calzone that was massive but harder than richard simmon's knob. honorable mention for quick late-night stops, say no to first dates here

Pesto chicken fettuccine was my favorite dish from here. For some reason i liked the way they made their pesto sauce and i've never had pesto quite like it ever since. Their cal zone are huge and very filling!

Hell yea. =) That's really all I need to say, but for the sake of information and the Internet, I'll go on. Godfather's Favorite is delicious, calzones are gigantic and steamy hot, and it's just pretty darn good food over all.

Sure, it might not be under $7 like most Berkeley food is, but it's still hecka good. Watch out for the lids on the pepper and cheese, cuz sometimes they aren't screwed tight and well, it isn't pretty.

I almost took off a star for the damn long wait that seems to be inevitable at Gypsy's from 11am to 10pm, but eh, the wait's worth it. It's not like they are slow, they are just way too popular. I can't bear to penalize them for being loved.

I'm still hungover so I'll make this short.

Over-rated. I ordered a "margarita pizza" expecting a topping of cheese, tomatoes, and basil. What do I get? A soggy, oily $6 mess of a  cheese pizza (mozzarella and CHEDDAR no less). 

Calzones are huge, but a light on the filling and again with the soggyness. 

The pasta's look promising, but didn't get to try one. 

There's tons of great places right next door so I suggest hitting those up if you want to get your money's worth. Blondie's down the street for pizza, falafel / gyros next door, cheap Thai around the corner, Top Dog.... Go anywhere else but here unless you have a raging hard-on for Americanized-Italian fast food.

DELIZIOSO! & cheap! ooh, & i love the pile of cheese melting slowly away on top.... this is such an amazing place for a fast, hearty, filling meal, that's worth your buck!

Such a fun, busy location next to Cal. GREAT value for your money. i want to try ALL the pasta dishes! new college goers, with deals like these, beware of the infamous freshmen 15! ;)

The great thing about Gypsy's is the large portions.

This, however, is also the bad thing. The food is decent, pasta is usually cooked just right, etc., but every time I come here, I never want to come again. There's just something about stuffing yourself with so much carbs and sauce that makes you never want to return. I'm the type of person who eats in moderation, and I just found everything way too overwhelming.

Still, come here if you have someone to share with.

Solid, reliable, massive amounts of food, cheap. If you're a Cal student, this place is probably your second home. I'll gladly tag along with friends when they get the craving for Gypsy's: the food is always decent and the price is always right. Everyone likes the calzones here, but I'll typically order pasta so I can get my grub on faster.

The parking situation in this entire area keeps me from visiting here frequently or by myself.  Plus, I can make the majority of this food in my kitchen (the same quality in less time than it takes to drive there and back). If you're already in the area and want some cheap Italian, Gypsy's is your destination. The food is good and cheap, but just not good enough to get this Yelper off his lazy butt and moving towards downtown.

Every time I go to Berkeley, I insist that I go eat here!  What's great about this place is that it's cheap and delicious!  With every meal you order, you'll find a splendid garlic bread that is to die for placed at the side.  I absolutely love ordering the Chicken Gnocci (or however you spell it)!  

But if you don't plan on packing on a few extra pounds, make going to this restaurant a "once a month" occasion.

Decently priced for a huge bowl of pasta with bread. I always either get the capriccioca or the chicken and broccoli pasta. My boyfriend used to get the Godfather special and I'd wonder how many animals had to die to make that thing. Anyways this is the best cheap pasta you will probably ever come across. I come back again and again.

Gypsy's is my to go place if I'm ever visiting UCB. the portions are big and it's cheap. The menu is a bit limited-but who needs a ton of choices? the one downside is that there is no air conditioning so it can get really hot and muggy inside during the summer- but in that case i'd just to go it!
I love this place! It used to be my favorite when I went up to Berkeley to visit my ex. My favorite was the Gnocci con Pollo (I think that is what it is called). Reletively cheap as well.

Definitely really good for a cheap Italian place. I tastes a little bit of all the plates my friend and myelf got. 1 Paradiso Pizza, 1 Ravioli Bolognese, 1 Gypsy Chicken, 1 Veggie Ravioli...and a couple of others. They were all something I would like to order again. It's probably hard to get something here not worth your money.

This is the perfect example of a place that the students can walk to and, so, doesn't have to be very good. I was a lot disappointed with the dishes we got here. I must say I didn't get the cream sauce that everyone loves, but the other stuff was a little canned-- not authentic. I guess since I am blessed with a car I would prefer pasta pomodoro or even Macaroni grill!

I effing love this place.  Everytime I go to San Francisco I always have an urge to come here.  Why?  Because its friggin cheap , good, and has huge portions.  People will say "oh this is not as good as such and such place" but come on!  It's only like 8 bucks a plate average.  If you want to sit down at a nice place and have the ambiance for the 15-25 dollar a plate you are paying then yeah go for it.  Just don't bitch and moan about how this place is not good compared to that place please.  Nowhere have I found a place that will plate you up all these different dishes for the price.

No one does what Gypsy's does so I have to bump them up from a 4 star to 5 star.  I mean, really?  Do people want to talk down about this place and compare it to another restaurant that is twice as expensive?  Don't be stupid, eat here and enjoy it.
Affordable Italian "fast food" that even a student can afford to eat here every day... Gypsy's will always hold a special place in my heart even after my days as a Cal student. hmmm....

This little hole in the wall place has probably the best tasting italian food i have ever tasted, and the best part is, its all under 9 dollars a plate, whether you get a pasta plate, calzone, personal pizza with any type of meat its all around the same price. 

one of the favorites is the "Chicken Pesto Calzone", their pesto sauce is good with anything on the menu. a few other favorites are the "Bronx tale" (which consist of meatballs and italian sausage) and the "Pesto con Pollo"

only downside is the location, since its in the heart of berkeley  and off telegraph its packed with students everywhere and you can expect to park a couple blocks away if you're not lucky, but its all worth it.

Everything here is GOOD.  Now that I'm back in the LA suburbs, I miss all the good cheap hole-in-the-wall restaurants.  Nowhere here can I get a $7 italian meal that is fantastically tasty and enough for two people.  Take advantage of the fact that Gypsy's is there and so cheap.  Finding good cheap Italian food that doesn't consist of just lasagna, pizza, and calzones is rare.
Carbonara and Gypsy's chicken with Nang. They're food was tasty and made me full right away since their portions are quite big! I don't really like to waste but I was so full. I enjoyed their food =)

Well, I suppose it's the only Italian place close to campus. I felt the need to review it after a particularly dissatisfying experience.

Service: Pretty slow, you order and pick up your food at the cashier. They take a pretty long time making your food, especially if you order a calzone.

Food: All the menu items are alright. The calzone is really large, and depending on what you get in the filling, can make or break it. I usually get the pesto one, which has chicken, ricotta, and mozarella inside of it. For pasta, the godfather's favorite isn't bad. In my most recent experience, I got the fettucine al salmon, which was also just alright, but incredibly salty.

Basically, all the food items just don't give any of that wow factor, and they taste like they've been cheapened by heavy cream and fatty oils. All of them also taste pretty salty. Come here only if you're craving Italian badly.
Got to get their pesto chicken and calzone ... parking here is a huge issue ( right by the campus)...if parking wasn't an issue it'll easily be a 5 star..

My two staples: chicken fettuccine and pesto/ricotta calzone. 

This is Italian fare for il populo (the people)!

You can get most entrees for about $7.

Good luck trying to find a place to sit inside or outside in the courtyard during lunchtime or dinner time. 

Anytime I pay more than $2- for italian food I compare it to the well-priced food at Gypsy's and think about how I'm getting ripped off.

My go-to place for cheap, good italian food! It's right near campus and it's a pretty good portion for the price of 6 or 7 bucks. 

They have pizza, calzones, salads, and different pastas. EVERYTHING feels like it's filled with oil and cream so you feel like a oily lard after, but it's still tasty. Each pasta comes with garlic bread with real garlic on top.....everyone I know smears it but I'm not that big of a fan so I usually toss the garlic aside.

The calzones are humongous. If you've never been here, you'll have to order it to experience it yourself. True, the majority of it is the air bubble, but despite that it's filled with a bunch of toppings. I've only had it once but honestly it wasn't THAT great..People always rave about it to me but there was a bad ratio of toppings and cheese. Plus, it looks so big I'm always reluctant in ordering it.

I think overall, Gypsy's is a good Italian place because it's at such a near location to where I'm always at.

mmm CARBS. Gypsy's serves cheap, good Italian food.
Gypsy's makes everything to order and is super consistent. Plus, their food is reasonably priced and fills you up. Thus they win the hearts of Berkeley's hungry college students. Plus they have their nice and toasty garlic bread, with fresh cloves of oven baked garlic!

NOTE: Gypsy's has great yummy Calzone that can easily be made into two meals! If you know which one you want, call your order in ahead of time since Calzones take twice as long.

Gypsy's Chicken! Pollo Con Pesto! Their pasta has never failed me (but then again, I usually order the same thing). Whenever my boyfriend visits from out of town, THIS is where he wants to go. Each. Time. But I don't complain. My brother said this one dish called...linguine something wasn't so great, but someone else who had their lasagna said it's GREAT. Their calzones are decent, too! I ABSOLUTELY love their pizza - it's fresh, light (I ordered one with broccoli, and replaced chicken with mushrooms), and NOT greasy. The prices are fantastic. There's usually a long line, but the wait is really not bad. Plus, they're open til super late (midnight), so you have a wide window to fulfill that Gypsy's craving ;)

Synopsis:
The place is cramped, the food is good for the price, but I would stick to the pasta dishes that don't have marinara (it's a bit acidic to my taste)

The Scene:
Gypsy's isn't authentic or high class by any means. It's an order at the counter and seat yourself type of place that is usually swarming with college students. It usually takes the bus boys a while to clear tables so more often than not you have to sit with someone else's mess for a while before it's cleared off. Nonetheless, the place isn't messy. Just be careful to not get your head taken out by an overeager college student with an unwieldy backpack. 

The Food:
The food is descent, I've definitely had better, but at this price, you can't really complain. The pasta is good. The gnocchi especially. The calzones, not so much. They tend to be oversized and especially dry. I had the pesto calzone and began to get really bored with it half-way through. The chicken gnocchi on the other hand, is delicious. I would avoid the tortellini with garlic - they go a bit overboard and I ended up with a headache after I ordered that.

The Best Part:
The price.

Hehehe. Love Gypsy's. I love it dearly. I don't care if it's authentic or not, this place is delicious and it's bad cause whenever I want pasta I come to Gypsy's, when I should be trying new places.

7 bucks here can buy you a delicious meal, and trust me, it's definitely worth it. The pesto linguini is one of my person favorites, but you cannot go wrong with the Gypsy's Chicken or Crazy Alfredo. The Gnocchi is also delicious, and I swear to you, my mouth is watering as I type this.

Best meal would definitely be Gypsy's and milk tea from Sweethearts. With those two, we can just call it a night.
Overcooked pasta...
i think i could cook better italian in grade school, but at least it's cheap and open late...

DELICIOUS and CHEAP--probably not the healthiest, but who cares?
hahahha

I love, love Gypsy's Chicken and Godfather's favorite.

Their calzones are reallly good time.

I want SOME NOW!!!

Tip: Buy Gypsy's chicken, wait for it to cool, and store in the fridge--eat it the next day or two..it tastes so much better for some odd reason!

Would you down a gallon of heavy cream straight from the dairy aisle at your local grocery store? Would you have someone hand you your bread after they count the endless dollar bills that have passed the hands of all who live in berkeley.. I mean all. Do you like having the random hair be nicely mixed in with your food? If so, Gypsys is your place!!! :)

I've been here a few times, all the time forgiving and forgetting bc its so popular and chalk off my experiences to one a million. Nope. Still heavy cream with some garlic tossed in, add a couple pieces of nastily cooked chicken, and insta pasta -- presto, the basis of most meals at Gypsys. I paid for extra bread, which was handed to me by the cashier with his hands, after he had counted the money from the cash register. And to leave a lasting impression, this last time there was a nice little hair swimming in all that heavy cream. 

YUCK, YUCK and YUCK (translation: EFFING DISGUSTING). I'm sorry us students are subjected to such crap called "italian" and wish there was a better more convenient option. 

Oh and the best of berkeley shit all over -- yeah, its been a few years since they won it, should tell you something. Craving cheap italian.. safeway... frozen food section .. Bertolli's. Try it.

For value and quality this place tops my place among all Italian restaurants I've been to.  Back in the day when I would visit Berk. I would always want to hit up this spot.  When I moved to Socal I would ask my little bro to FedEx me some Gypsy's and anytime he wanted me to come up to visit all he needed to say was Gypsy's and I would book my flight the following night.  This place is nothing fancy, but it hits the spot and lets you have enough to treat all your friends for boba tea!  I miss you Gypsy's!

Garlic is my friend.  For those seeking late night eats, this is a great find.  Bear in mind, when I say late night, it's hard to find a hot cooked meal after 9:30 PM on a week day.  It's definitely crowded at times, but the items are fresh and made to order.

this place is good until you realize that it's not the only italian restaurant in the world.

that changes things.

sometimes salty and often bland.

Second-best food in the inaccurately named Asian Ghetto - and fewer flies than Thai Basil. Usually get one of the chicken pastas (the calzone is better but I don't have the patience to wait that long). Pasta is too saucy, but at least the sauce has some taste. Sure, there are ten million better places, but there are twenty million worse places.

The best Italian food in Berkeley, hands down. Godfather's favorite has saved the day of a starving child as he walks down the streets of Berkeley in the Asian ghetto, not knowing what to eat. Then a shine of precedent light hits his eyes and he looks into Gypsys's and orders the Godfather's favorite. Best decision, ever.

Although a lot of their other pastas are good as well, like Crazy Alfredo, I forget the names..etc etc. Godfather's favorite is a personal favorite. I highly recommend it. Because, after all, there is no harm in trying some amazing Italian food..is there?

-----Visits
Many.

-----Service
One of the worst places service-wise. The main manager guy who works at the cashier is very grumpy and tries to rush you out of the way or off the phone when you call in. I would say he is misunderstood, but we did overhear/witness him getting into an argument with a black customer who claimed he had called him a "n*gger," so there are no redeeming qualities here. :\ The cooks and workers are very nice, however!

-----Food
Really nice selection of vegetarian dishes. Any white/creamy/cheesy sauce dishes are extremely rich, so be prepared. The pesto is also heavy. I am not fond of the tomato-type sauces here, though, which taste a bit *gasp* out of the can. I usually get the ravioli marinara, which is a good balance of ricotta and a nice thick marinara sauce. The penne gargonzola (we get it with angelhair) is also something to look for. The calzones are as big as your head but they are delicious and could easily feed two---just be prepared for the extra long wait while they bake!

-----Prices
Pretty damn reasonable. You get a good-sized meal for about $6 here. The drinks in the cases are pretty overpriced but there's always free ice water---in a real glass! We opt for boba from next door.

-----Atmosphere
Can be hard to find a table during peak times (12pm and 6pm) but the interior is pretty nice for being a restaurant in Asian Ghetto. Everything is pretty clean, too, and it doesn't get too noisy even though everything's in one room. It's also really easy to call in and get stuff to go, though.

Cheap, delicious, stick of butter in every cream sauce dish, I am utterly sold. My favorite has to be the Victor's Spaghetti. I find it impossible to get sick of this thing - was having it once a week at one point. There's usually a long line around popular lunch/dinner times but I don't even care, it smells delicious in here. $7 for all that goodness (plates are like twice the size of your head) is hard to argue with.

Mmm I do agree with everyone that this place is delicious.  Tried the Godfather's favorite and it did not disappoint.  It had pieces of chicken, pancetta (which is similar to bacon), egg and parmigiano cheese mixed together with penne noodles.  My friend got the Chicken Parmigiano which was pretty good too, marina sauce and mozzarella cheese with chicken and spaghetti.  (I liked mine better tho hehe)

Most of the pasta dishes were about $7, comes with a piece of garlic bread so it's a good deal. 

Their calzones are HUGE!! I'm 4'11 and my friend was like "whoa, those are like almost half your size" lol. and they're about $6! Well worth the money, I should try those next time haha.  There's also pizza, salad, and sandwichies all reasonably priced.  Definitely coming back when I come back to Berkeley. It's a must try!

Looking for cheap, quick and delicious Italian food?  Come to Gypsy's in the Asian Ghetto.  

First off, the calzones.  They. are.  HUGE.  Imagine a football inside one of those pink pastry boxes filled with meat and cheese and then imagine it some more, because you'll probably be eating it as leftovers the next day.  They do take around half an hour or so to cook, but so would ordering a pizza or baking one yourself.  It's worth the wait.  

Second, the pasta.  Each pasta dish comes with a slice of bread with roasted garlic.  The garlic is so soft you can just smear it on like a spread...IT'S AMAZING.  Every pasta dish I've had, although oily at times, has been amazing (minus the gnocchi, but I'm just not a fan of potato pasta, sorry!).  The chicken pesto is so creamy and they are very generous with the sauce and chicken.  I also love the victor's spaghetti, which is made with red peppers and strips of beef; it is slightly sweet and always delicious.  The menu has a lot to choose from, so give it a try!  I once got some seafood linguine with capers and was starting to resent my decision after I ordered but when it came, everything was so delicious, even the mussels.  The pasta is usually $7-$8, and the seafood ones are a dollar or so more.  You can also add a salad for a few more bucks. 

The place is always packed but the servers and people working in the kitchen are nice.  On a crazy day, just get to-go if you can't find any seats.
Always have to stop here for a calzone when I visit Berkeley! It has a college atmosphere, which I like.  Calzones are huge and delish! Really nothing to be disappointed by.

Pasta, the ultimate fallback food, plus the convenience of a 2 minute walk from campus? I'm sold!

I've only had a few dishes at Gypsy's, but it remains my go-to for late-night dinners, or when I'm feeling much too lazy to cook anything. Suggestion? Try the Gamberi! It's this savory shrimp-filled dish that will have you coming back for more.

Bringing back some good memories...

We were on our way to an APHiO retreat  and stopped by here for a quick bite!

OH how I love Berkeley!

Anyways, had the Crazy Alfredo, which was suppose to be incredible according to a brother. I have had better. There wasnt enough sauce on it! A lot of the flavoring came from the sausage and roasted red peppers, which was pretty good! I have to say this is not your usual chicken alfredo pasta. 

Dude, their calzones were the size of my head!! 
Tried the Meatball Calzone and it was flavorful! Had plenty of filling inside! Also had the Pesto one and tasted mediocre to me! Quite a bit of oil from the pesto flowing out as my fellow brother cut it open, but it's normal! 

Busy on a Friday night! People were coming in and out of there. The people traffic was flowing pretty well though! 

I do want to give Gypsy's another shot....hopefully soon!

Gypsy's is pretty good Italian food for it's $6-7 price. In my hometown these dishes would be at least $10+. Everything is suuupper creamy/heavy though so you'll definitely be in a food coma afterwards. I like that they give you a piece of complimentary bread but I hate that garlic crap they put on top (because I'm a vampire harhar) AND you don't have to pay tip because you clean up after yourself so that's another plus hehehe. The portions aren't huge but are definitely filling. 

The calzones however are HUGE (bigger than your face) but I actually ate an entire calzone in one sitting, but I'm just a fat ass. The calzones aren't thaaat good though..I think they bake it for too long because the crust gets kind of old. I've only had calzones from 2 places before but I prefer the ones at Claim Jumpers.

I'm a fan. I've always heard great things about Gypsy's from friends of mine who are Cal alum. Gypsy's is found in the Asian Ghetto which is a bit of a misnomer at this point considering the diversity of food that can be found there.

I ordered the Chicken Marsala with linguine. It came with a thinly pounded chicken breast that was sauteed to perfection. It was smothered in thinly sliced mushrooms that were doused in Marsala wine. There was just enough sauce to make sure that the noodles were covered. And of course, it came with a slice of the famous Gypsy's garlic bread. The bread is nothing special, but the roasted garlic on top makes all the difference. So good! I only intended to have half the dish, and keep the rest for later, but it was all so tasty I couldn't stop myself from finishing the whole plate. 

Next time, I definitely want to try the Gypsy's Chicken, though maybe without the extra Parmigiano cheese. Not a fan of too much cheese so I commiserate with Katrina T.'s review below. And the Chicken with Broccoli sounds kind of tasty too, again without the cheese though.

Prices are super reasonable, and of course you just can't beat the $7.99 special with a pasta dish, salad, and soda.

The only gripe that I have with Gypsy's is the lack of water from the soda dispenser. Basically, if you want water, you have to buy the bottled kind. This doesn't seem so environmentally friendly, especially considering that this is Berkeley!

Gypsy's is really hit or miss for me. Their pizzas are really good, based on the few times I've had them. Their Calzones, especially the pesto, are delicious, and huge to boot.

Their pasta, however, is very inconsistent. I remember really loving their gnocchi, but the last time I went it was completely bland. I also had their chicken parmesan recently, and the chicken tasted like week old leftovers that had just been microwaved. It was very rubbery and it tasted that way, too.

When Gypsy's is good, it's good. But sometimes their pasta leaves a lot to be desired.

The Durant Court is really hit or miss, but this place has always been good.  Their calzones are huge and the sauces taste homemade.  Not like the chain stores which taste a bit watered down.  Oh, and I highly recommend the Pollo con Pesto.  They are open pretty late and on holidays.

Even though they can get kind of busy and a bit hard to converse over the noise, I would come here for a quick bite before pulling an all nighter in Moffitt.

cheapest good italian food! went here a lot wit friends..portion is big and pasta dish comes wit garlic bread. service is great and food comes right away ..da best thing is dat everything is under $7.

I was reluctantly dragged to Gypsy's Trattoria several years back and had the distinct fear that I was walking into some Post-Apocalyptic underground food scavenger's market. 

This is perhaps more to the credit of the entire foodcourt's atmosphere and only minimally the fault of Gypsy's - I now tell myself - but the fear set in all the same. 

Those who appeared most like regulars of the outdoor patio, were participating in some sort of scavenger hunt where they needed change to complete their final challenge. I knew they weren't homeless because they all appeared to have nicer shoes than me and proceeded, between inquiries, to check their cell phone text messages. I checked my pockets, with no intention of obliging, and insisted that I did not, in fact, have any change. And wished the young Kerouac good luck. 

Gypsy's iteslf is perhaps the cleanest of the foodcourt joints with clean wooden tables, and a bar-height counter overlooking the street. I was taken aback by the line of burners with several dozen skillets being handled by a single line-cook behind the register. He tossed one after the next with mundane precision and I was certain that whatever mechanical technique this fellow had acquired would result in the absolute lowest quality of grub. 

Surprised I was. Though the pizza came hours after the first pasta dishes, it was crisp, fresh and had the aroma of leavened bread and tomato and cheese caramelization. The table next to us had a calzone, which made my mouth water ever after I was absolutely full. The thin crust, the melted cheese, the basil, all distinct. And here I was, thoroughly convinced that pizzas can only be toasted into a cracker under dry heat conveyor style oven. No, this was really fresh. 

The pasta dishes came out within minutes of order. These were the very same pasta dishes I observed the not-an-ounce-Italian cook skillfully throwing around. 

Who are you guys kidding? Is this going to be Ragu with precooked pasta? Classico on special occasions? What the hell can I even expect from this? What I got was a pleasant surprise. 

Look, I'm a pasta purist, and I've had some bad, bad pasta. But this, this wasn't bad. 6 bucks and four and a half minutes later and i get something that beats half of the so called high end Italian joints in the city. What kind of pot-laced air are they pumping in here anyway? I haven't had these kinds of munchies for years. Could i even trust my palate? Best to eat outside. 

I took a seat outside on one of the benches, and politely replied "No I don't have any change!" 

Damn this still tastes good. Not great, not perfect, but damn good and well worth it. 

I decide immediately not to admit to anybody that I did, in fact, appreciate a 7 dollar pizza and a 6 dollar seafood pasta and made my way home quickly with my head dropped in humility. 

I proceeded to visit Gypsy's weekly and to learn whatever I could from their line cooks of efficiency and food consistency at light-speed. 

As far as I am concerned, Gypsy's is like a true Mystery Spot. A place where illusion doesn't cover up a cheap product but where the laws of physics (or restauromics) seem to not work. Food is prepared way too fast, way too cheaply and way too fresh and delicious. 

And the pizza? Well this is one damn solid pie -  an' I give 'a you a black eye if you 'a say anythin' othawise? Capisce? Cooks and restaurant owners have much to learn from this place.

What more you could ask for in Italian food under $8? The prices are phenomenal, the food delicious, the portions huge, and the service quick (even when they're busy, which they usually are, but even so, the service is quicker than seems humanly possible). I don't know why there's so much negativity about the mass quantities of cream and butter they use. Does this actually come as a surprise? It's fucking ALFREDO, of course it's not healthy! I concur that you shouldn't come here if you're counting calories, but not for the same reason. Even if you save most of your dish I promise you'll be eating those leftovers within hours of putting them in the fridge. Too...good...must...devour...

My mom and I favor the fettucine alfredo with shrimp, and my boyfriend raves about the Bronx Tale. They also have great side salads for cheap. The caesar dressing doesn't particularly taste like caesar, but it's unique and very good. Can't complain! One note: if you're not getting take-out, don't go during peak hours. If you do, bring brass knuckles. You'll need them to fight to the death for a table.

Pros:
- Large portions (I kind of hate the size of their plates though.)
- Convenient location
- Stays open late

Cons:
- Too much sauce/oil (My salad is always soaked with dressing.)

Service isn't the most friendliest, but I understand that they're always busy. One worker was nice enough to show me how the water machine worked without me asking for help.

I think the reason why this place is so overhyped is because it's one of the better places to eat at Asian Ghetto. But that's pretty much it. If you were to compare it to other Italian places in Berkeley, it would fall short.

Bottom line: I'll eat there if everyone else I'm with wants to eat there, but otherwise I'm not interested. I wish Pasta Bene was closer to campus!

This is as cheap as Italian gets and with generous portions, it is a good place for a guy to bring his unsuspecting date and indulge in creamy penne goodness while the female species looks on in horror. 

Unfortunately, that was just a story out of my imaginary life, because a sober observation reveals that Berkeley girls like this place, too. 

The general taste is surprisingly mild - even the marinara is relatively unsalty. Everything is over-oiled and over-creamed though. I find myself wiping down little strands of pasta on the edge of the plate every time to dry them off of their saturated fat bath. The pasta is also a far cry from 'al dente', just in case chewiness is your style.

This is a good venue to bring new visitors to in order to wean off a gourmet lifestyle and get accustomed to Berkeley ghetto goodness. Better yet, bring that date here, and if she seems to enjoy it, you can forget ever having to bring her to college avenue or the gourmet ghetto to eat. Cash saved!

I LOVE PASTA, so when I told my friends that I would kill for some Fettuccine Alfredo, they immediately told me I needed to try some of Gypsy's in Berkeley. We drove 30 minutes there, and I had the Seafood Alfredo. IT WAS AMAZING. It's no wonder it's been rated the best Italian restaurant in Berkeley for several consecutive years now! The portions are pretty big and at such a cheap price; you definitely get your money's worth! 

The place isn't fancy or anything, and it can get pretty crowded around lunchtime, but it's definitely quality food you can't complain about! It's one of my favorite restaurants!

NO FEAR:  I didn't really care to try GYPSY'S  till later in my college career.  I think the name just spooked me out, and I thought it was going to be too expensive for my college blood.  Boy was I wrong...

ITALIAN JOB:  This place does Italian food in a way that you don't find too often elsewhere.  They make it fast (for Italian food) and they're cheap (for Italian food).  I wish there were more places like this... it's just CONVENIENT.

PESTO ADDICTION:  My addiction to pesto began here.  I always get the Pesto Chicken Pasta or the Pesto Calzone.  It's not the healthiest thing in the world, as you'll see the pesto becomes mutagen neon green with all the oils, but MAN is it good.  The pesto calzone reminds me of a Mario Bro.'s turtle shell cooked and oozing with green pesto and cheese.  mMMmmmmmm.

The food here is soooo good and cheap... but it is ridiculously crowded and small... so most of the time I take my food back home to eat.

I LOVE the pesto chicken pasta that they have here, it is delicious and i love pesto. The calzones are also amazing... it is HUGEEEE (at least in my eyes) and still very cheap. But it takes a while to make... it is soo worth the wait though. 

The only thing I don't really like is that the pasta is really really really oily... normally i hate really oily stuff, but for some reason it still taste really good. but it is definitely not healthy....

Gypsy's offers quick, tasty, and reasonably priced Italian food. They are very efficient and ultra consistent in their dishes. The meals are VERY heavy, so don't come here expecting a light refreshing dish. Their Pollo Con Pesto might put you on the couch for the night! (as it does to me) I like this dish, along with the Pollo Gorgonzola, which is a sort of vodka sauce with gorgonzola tortolini. This is a great place to come if you've just gotten out of a football game and are looking to soak up some of that booze. If you want a REAL duzzie, grab Gypsys and then go across the way to KINGPIN donuts! You can do this combo for under $10 bucks! ENJOY

I haven't eaten at Gypsies in a few months, primarily because the meals are so heavy. That is why I give them 3 stars. I think they could try to offer some of their traditional dishes in a fresher and lighter format. catch up with the times, Gypsys! 

oh another trick, if there is a long line, CALL IN YOUR ORDER. Wait five minutes and then walk up to the cashier and it will be ready! Don't abuse this, but it comes in handy once in a great while.

You can't go wrong with any of the dishes here. In fact, the most negative, if you can even call it that, part of the experience is deciding what to order.

The first time I came here was with the bf who ordered Victor's Spaghetti. I had no idea that spaghetti could be so delicious!

I got the Combo Calzone and although was disappointed that most of the innards was air...still was more than satisfied with all the gooey, cheesy contents. 

I also suggested Gypsy's when some friends from LA came up and their food not only impressed them, but way surpassed their tastebuds' expectations.

I LOVE THIS PLACE! The food is sooo delicious and cheap. Large portions too. My favorites are the calzone and the pasta con pesto. Great quality and inexpensive. Kinda pisses me off when I go to other Italian places and eat pasta that isn't as good and are pricier. Def one of my favorite spots in Berkeley!

This place has been consistently good. The service is always quite quick (minor wait, but they cook it when you order it...so it's a good thing). There is plenty of seating especially outside. 

Caveats-
Your paying for college food... expect it 
At night the bums come out lurking outside for food...DO NOT LEAVE YOUR FOOD UNATTENDED

I can't believe I haven't written a review for this place yet! One of my absolute favorite places to eat in Berkeley! Gypsy's is the best! Great Italian food, giant portions, great prices!

After I graduated from Cal, there were just a few things I really missed. Gypsy's was one of those things. 

This isn't a first date place by any means - it's located in "Asian Ghetto" for one thing, and two, they use a TON of garlic. so yea, don't try this for a first date...or maybe not for any of your first 5 dates. haha. 
It's definitely a hole in the wall, but the food is great. Pretty much everything on the menu is filled with some kind of combination of cheese, cream, garlic, and butter - that pretty much says best food ever to me. My favorite dish is the Pollo Gorgonzola tortellini. It's 3 colored Gorgonzola tortellini with chicken sitting in tons of a garlic, creamy, cheesy sauce. SO DELICIOUS! Plus a piece of very garlicky bread! Yum yum.

The only thing I would say to skip here are the calzones - they are gigantic, but compared to everything else on the menu, there are just so many better, more flavorful options.

Mmm..now I'm craving Gypsy's...time to make a trip to Berkeley!

Let me just start off that my belly has expanded from this eating out experience. It is a great place for a reasonably priced Italian meal. A bunch of us from work were all in the mood for Italian and were told about this place. It was busy, yet it was a steady stream of people eating inside and out as well as take-out. The portions are  substantial and it does not hit the wallet too hard. I got the chicken pesto and it had the right mix of ingredients and yes the hidden secret of BUTTER! Each meal came with a piece of bread that had a little garlic piece on it for you to spread out...Yum! If you are in the mood, then go for it. The only down side is the guy who takes the order, he definitely does not get the Mr. Personality award! However, the service was quick!

I am not kidding when I say that me and my roommate use to come to gypsys everyday. and sometimes, even twice a day. Gypsys is just so good and it has so many varieties that it makes it really hard to choose anything else. 

We liked to mix and match our pasta with different sauces, but we steer clear of any red sauce and The Mideterrianianninan. Feta Cheese and Tomato dishes just don't cut it. Our ALL STAR dishes are 

Linguine Clams - CREAM SAUCE
Frutti D'Mare - CREAM SAUCE
Shrimp Alla Primivera- PESTO
Pollo Con Pesto
Crazy Alfredo

Gypsys has really been a home to us. Thanks to this place, I can now wisely point out the difference between 'angel hair' and 'linguine' in a cocktail party. Their relentless use of grease, butter and lard gives their pasta a rich and exuberant taste that keeps pulling us back. They have succeeded in engineering a perfect combination of pasta and sauce, where every strand of pasta is bursting with an explosion of flavor. Props to Pasta Bene for doing sort of the same thing with a cleaner environment, but in terms of taste, Pasta Bene just isn't heavy enough.

Why the 4 stars instead of a heavenly 5? Health concerns, my friend. As a wise person once said, 'a moment on my lips, forever on my hips'. I now only limit myself to one Gypsys every 2 weeks. I know that makes me sound like a bitch, but the wait only makes that PESTO-DRENCHED plate of pasta all the more seductive 14 days later.

Take a bite of that Godfather's Favorite.  You feel that sharp pang in your chest as the blood vessels constrict tightly near your heart?  With each pulse forcibly pushing the mud that is now your blood after that piece of linguica?  Do you hear your heart begin to race (THUMP THUMP THUMP OHGAWDITHURTS) as it struggles courageously to overcome the thick walls of plaque crystallizing in every artery, depriving your tissues of sweet sweet oxygen?  SUDDENLY the clog of butter in your veins breaks and blood flows freely once again.  A small cough escapes your lips. You smile and dip your fork into the sea of pasta for another bite, washing it down with a piece of delicious garlic-smeared bread.

This is pretty much what Gypsy's is about.  Damn good food that will make you hate yourself so good as you eat every artery-clogging bite.  I recommend the Godfather's Favorite, Chicken Parmesan, or Chicken Gnocchi, sh*t is so clutch.  Calzones' are a favorite here too, but take really really long to bake.  Surprisingly I have never eaten a single pizza from here in the 5 years I've been in Berkeley, but I'm sure I'm not missing out on much.

TL;DR:  This stuff will kill you with obesity and diabetes, but in a strangely ecstatically good way.

It's the only place I would dine at "Asian Ghetto" primarily because the food is cheap and delicious.  The portions are great and the service is good.  However, the food can be inconsistent at times in terms of quality and taste.  Also, the food takes awhile but it's worth the wait and it's understandable because the place seems busy all the time.  Sometimes they overcook the meat but I am not a fan of meat anyway so don't take my word for it.  The Crazy Pasta and Fettuccine Alfredo are my favorites.  I would highly recommend the Calzone as well.

This is a good place to fatten up a manatee.  If you want a dense, hearty meal then definitely hit this place up.  I thought the pasta was ok but it was the sauces that made the difference.  This place is usually packed with students but if you have a manatee then you can use her fat ass to bump people off a table.  I wouldn't say this is the best quality of food but its worth trying out.

I could summarize this review in one short sentence: I WANT GARLIC BREAD.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: four stars.

My friends and I consistently ordered their calzones, but I would always get pasta when I was by myself. I loved their linguine and clams and their shrimp primavera. Gypsy's is the closest I have seen to true Italian food in America.

And as for the garlic bread... they give you entire cloves of roasted garlic. You can spread it on the bread for amazing garlic bread, or you can do what I did and just pop the garlic into your mouth. Thanks to Gypsy's for taking the time to roast the garlic, because those cloves have so much hidden flavor that can only come from roasting.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: zero stars.

The wait is often unbearable, especially when you are talking about a restaurant packed with hungry college kids.

Gypsy's, you were the restaurant I ate at when I first stepped foot into Cal.  You haven't changed since.  Here's to us babe!

What I would order here:
Godfather's Favorite ($7) (Order me!!!)
Pollo con Pesto ($7)
Crazy Alfredo ($7)
Gypsy's Chicken ($7)

Orders all come with a slice of garlic bread.  Portions are large and they do not skimp on the meat.  If you pay $8 total for your entire pasta meal, you will get an additional decent sized salad and a small fountain drink (all for an extra dollar).  No need to tip!

Miss you!  Visit soon, I promise.

Love,
Fei xx

An honest-to-goodness 3 Star performance with 4 Star pricing, I must say.

I was amazed at their prices.  Even though I was told that they were more popular for their calzones than anything else, I decided to go for their Shrimp Alfredo.  The Alfredo sauce was a bit on the bland side, but the baby shrimp was rather impressive.  The portions of baby shrimp, and the whole dish, for that matter, was generous.  Served with a slice of bread with a whole garlic clove on top at a price of $6.79... I'd call that a steal!

Their Carbonara was a pretty serious contender in the flavor category.  The smoky essence from the bacon accompanying the cream sauce over a bed of spaghetti made for a good mixture of flavor.  Of the two pasta dishes, the Carbonara was clearly the winner.

The two Calzones my friends ordered seemed to be even more impressive than our pasta dishes: HUGE, lots of goodies inside, and priced similar to our pasta dishes.  I'm definitely gonna get me a Calzone the next time I'm in town!

3.5 Stars to mix between flavor and pricing... I'm going to round up to a 4.  I'll be back!

One of my preferred places to eat at near campus when bumming around south side and craving a calzone. It sort of resembles a deflated football on a plate, and like a dirigible, tends to be filled with a lot of hot air. But then there's all that sauce and veggies and/or meat that lines the bottom of it and occasionally makes it into your mouth with some skillful usage of the knife and fork.

Or you could just manhandle the beast and eat it like a hotpocket. Not recommended unless you're about to do laundry.

Since I work in TV sports production, I've ended up working a good amount of Cal football and basketball games over the past few years. Whenever I work a game at Cal, Gypsy's is one of the places that myself and the other crew members tend to frequent for our lunch breaks. I'm a big pasta fan, and there's no shortage of good pasta dishes at Gypsy's. When I was there this past Saturday, I ordered a "Bronx Tale", since it was one of the menu items I had always wanted to try in the past, but had never gotten around to actually ordering. If you're a pasta fan too, I would recommend the "Bronx Tale". I'd also recommend their calzones...they're freaking huge, but well worth the effort to scarf down. To tell the truth, I'd recommend a lot of other dishes here too...I just can't remember the names of everything I've had here in the past. 

If there is one knock against Gypsy's, it's that it can get really crowded in there sometimes and seating isn't always guaranteed, but it all depends on what time of the day you're in there.

A staple of any berkeley student's (past or present) diet.  I can't say how long Gypsy's has been right there, front and center of the 'asian ghetto', all i know is that i'm glad it's always been there for me.

The food here is simple, quickly prepared, cost effective and with enough variety to satisfy anyone who isn't a snob about their food.  Let's be honest here people, if you're coming to the asian ghetto looking for world class cuisine, then clearly someone has led you astray at some point.  But if you're looking for good hearty food that doesn't strain your wallet, then choosing gypsy's might be the smartest decision you make all day.

From my own experience, the calzone's are really the only thing that takes some time to prepare, other than that.. the lines move quickly and the food comes out even quicker.  Godfather's Favorite with pink sauce (combo of the red and white sauce) is the go to move for me.  Give it a try and hey.. if you don't love it, it cost you less than 10 bucks.  There are worst travesties in the world.

I ordered a Sicilian calzone. That thing was HUGE and cheap. I felt overwhelmed when I first saw it thinking I won't be able to eat half of it. There was a little too much mozzarella. I think I was getting full off the cheese. Maybe I shouldve shared my calzone. The bread part of it was good though. 

If you want some cheap eats near the campus, come and check this place out. They have other things than calzones.
yummy!  i always ordered a pasta dish, loved their garlic bread, hated the workers for being unfriendly, and loved that it was open late.  definitely my go to spot after studying!
Five stars for Gypsy's for being open until midnight and serving up pretty OK pasta for $5.

I was not expecting to find anything anywhere near decent at this little place next to the asian restaurants. However, I was truly mistaken. My chicken pesto pasta was delicious and it also came with some bread/roasted garlic. It was enough for my lunch and a night-time snack. My friend got a massive calzone and I got my pasta for under $13. That's a deal you just can't beat.

My favorite food is Italian, and having been in the restaurant business serving Italian for more than 3 years, Gypsy's is definitely not the best Italian I've tasted.  And that's because they're very inexpensive.  

My problems with Gypsy's are that firstly, their dishes take FOREVER (every time I've been there, it invariably takes 15-45 minutes for my food to arrive, seriously 45 minutes one time).  Secondly, their pasta dishes are super runny and finally, their garlic bread is pretty much bland, plus the garlic spread on top of it does nothing to enhance the taste.

And their pizza is not tasty - go to Blondie's on Telegraph for their whole wheat veggie slice with organic veggies instead.

Cheap decent Italian food.

Pizzas, cal zones, and pastas all have similar prices, which i love.
The pasta tastes good too. I usually get the Godfather's favorite or the carbonara. I tried the pesto pizza, but it was a little dry for me-id like it with more pesto sauce.

However, i have gotten short black hair in my food twice. It was always the time whenever i got my pasta to-go. I would go home, open the container, and see a piece of hair in the sauce.

Besides that, i do recommend this place if you're hungry!

I've been trying to remember where I used to eat out  when I was at Cal.  Pretty much every place that Tintin has suggested, I don't recognize.  Well, except for Fat Slice and Intermezzo.  I thought about it for a while and I realized that because I was broke, or maybe because I preferred to spend my money on clothes, I usually ate at home.  When I go eat in Berkeley now and see the prices, I think I was just extra cheap.

Gypsy's is cheap (everthing is less than $10)and delicious.  I've had several of the chicken and pasta dishes as well as salads and nothing has disappointed, except for the salad dressings.  I'm pretty sure they use Wish Bone or something like that  but everything else has been fresh and well seasoned without being overly salty.  

It's right by campus, full of students that make me feel old and has no ambiance to speak of but if you're looking for a quick and filling meal, I recommend it.

Taste of food = 4 stars - 1 star for absolutely cold food = 3 stars

I'm a fan because it's relatively cheap for lots of food, and good food at that.

I didn't end up eating my food there, I took it home because it was ridiculously cold though. Hence the 3 stars instead of 4.

I got the lasagna, and it was cold all the way through.I ended taking it home and reheating it. It tasted delicious, wish my lasagna could come out as good.

If you are looking for a heart attack, look no further. Eating at Gypsy's is a cheap, sick, guilty pleasure.

I remember the first time I ever had Gypsy's, I made the mistake having a calzone all to myself. Ever since that experience, I have never eaten a calzone alone again. The thing is huge and oozes of sauce. It's a monster. The grossest looking one is probably the pesto one because all the oil floats to the top so when you slice it open, all the oil pours out first... yet it's my favorite one!

favorites:
pesto calzone
greek salad

honorable mention:
linguine pesto
linguine with clams

To do it right: $8

Since I moved here, Gypsy's has been nestled firmly in my heart and stomach--both literally and figuratively.  I stick strictly to the pasta menu here, and have had nearly all of them.  They are consistently good, very filling, different from each other and calorically obscene, which I consider a plus.

Top three picks: 
1. Crazy Alfredo: standard Fettuccine Alfredo with a love tap in the sauce, chicken, and Italian sausage--good if you're feeling particularly gluttonous
2. Chicken Gnocchi: surprisingly good, not too starchy gnocchi with chicken in a heavy cream sauce--more subtle flavors; potatoes are filling
3. Pollo Gorgonzola: lots of gorgonzola stuffed into tortellini and served w/ chicken in a tomato cream sauce, which they call a "pink" sauce--not for the lactose disinclined

Pretty hard to go wrong here.

Prices are a bit high, but so are the portions.  Additionally, this place gets more crowded than a Talk thread with "penis" in the title during lunchtime on weekdays.

Final say: You need to go at least once, but probably won't stop there.

Best dish by far is the chicken gnocchi!! Their meat balls aren't great so I would avoid the spaghetti w/meat balls and the meatball subs. Also, if you're ordering take-out, ask them to double the containers. Unfortunately, the containers they use are VERY cheap and more often than not end up cracking and/or leaking.
Other than that - service is super fast and portion sizes are more than generous.

This place has HUGE calzones.  I was pretty shocked when my cousin came back to our table with his.  They also have tasty, rich pastas.  At their cheap prices, you really wouldn't expect the pasta dishes to be so yummy.  I don't know about the pizzas, sandwiches or salads, but the calzones and pastas are DELISH.  You order at the front, take a seat, and your food comes out in a flash.  Well, if you get the calzone it'll take a bit longer.  It's fattening, but you know that.  You don't go for pasta, pizza, or calzones when you're on a diet.

Affordable, delicious, and fast.  Works for me!

mosdef 5 stars for the price.

it's cheap, they take credit cards, it's quick, it's pretty good, and the portions are generous. what more do you want?

Was in Berkeley over the weekend for the West Coast A Capella Showcase. With time to kill, we went ahead and got some dinner first. It's been three years since I've lived in Berkeley, so nostalgia hit and I instantly wanted Gypsy's. Everything still looked the same, but maybe the kids suddenly looked younger to me. 

I was happy that the prices haven't fluctuated too badly over the years. The prices were fair and luckily, the portions were very generous. I didn't even need to look at the board as I ordered the Ravioli Alfredo out of instinct. White cheesy goodness! The others ordered the Ravioli Bolognese and the Godfather's Favorite.

Once we got our food, and I was relieved that it still tasted so good after all this time. My ravioli was smothered in alfredo sauce that I watched them make on the fly in the pan, and they've perfected it. I even grew to love the bread with hunks of garlic on top. See, Gypsy's, I've matured!  As for the other's, they had no complaints. The meat sauce for the Ravioli Bolognese was great I was told. We barely spoke as we polished off our plates.

Calzones were always pretty darn delicious here and could be split between two easily. I saw a couple bring theirs out to the table and I'm happy to report that they're still huge as ever.

I'm glad that some places can remain unchanged over time and maintain their awesomeness.  I still dock you one star for questionable cleanliness in the kitchen and the mess at the seating area, but I turn a blind eye. That's love.

This place is good, but it's just so creamy/buttery. It really overwhelms the pasta. I'd recommend Pasta Bene (a ways down Telegraph but price-wise in the same range as Gypsy's)

I definitely can't eat here too often because the food is way too unhealthy. The load you up with cheese/carbs and it's so creamy that you can't really taste anything but the cheese...I'd recommend going with lighter non-cream based pastas here!

The other day I was hanging out in Berkeley, which rarely ever happens. My BFF, who regularly visits Berkeley, met up with me and told me I had to try Gypsy's.

"It's my favorite," he said. "I come here just to eat at Gypsy's."

He told me that it's inexpensive Italian food. And this homeboy is pretty stringent on his money, so I was curious as to how cheap (and maybe gross) this food was going to be.

Boy, was I stoked to find a wide selection of comfort food: pasta dishes, calzones, salad, and sandwiches for a super-affordable prices. Great vegetarian selection as well.

Being the lover of all things cheesy, creamy, and carbolicious, I ordered the penne pasta with Gorgonzola, spinach, fresh tomatoes and requested mushrooms as well for about $7.

The dish was just as I imagined and exactly what I needed. They also included toast with a clove of roasted garlic. I finished the plate in one sitting, but if I hadn't had such a huge appetite that day, the dish could've lasted two meals.

Gypsy's is a no-fuss eatery that serves restaurant food without waiters, formal vibe, and hefty tab. It's a great place to grab a meal (not just a bite) for less than what it would cost to get a good sandwich in San Francisco.

It's not the greatest or the highest quality of foods, but it gets the job done, is reasonably priced, and is open super late.  

My recommendation is to try the calzones which are super huge, tasty, and cheap. For the same sized calzone at eXtreme Pizza you are looking at paying 3x the price of a calzone from Gypsy's and I would even venture to say that it tastes about the same if not a little better. Did I mention they are open late?

What can I say? Living next to Gypsy's has endeared this place to my heart.

I usually order the Crazy Alfredo, which is not too heavy on the Alfredo sauce on just right on the portion. It comes with a piece of garlic bread that is pretty good. The chicken pesto pasta here is also quite delicious if not a bit oily.

The calzones here although fairly large in size are less filling than their pizza cousins. 

There is nothing I dislike more than overpriced and Gypsy's is everything but that. It is also located in the heart of the south side of the beautiful an gorgeous California Berkeley campus.

I don't understand. I know lots of people that love this place but I've never had anything that good here. I've tried and tried to like gypsy's but no luck..

Things I've ordered and not enjoyed:
gnocci - really really disappointing. The pasta itself was overly salty and the sauce was way too oily

lasagna - super greasy and mostly just ground beef..not enough pasta to sauce ratio

chicken pesto calzone - it's literally just chicken, a fistful of cheese and pesto in a fat bread taco..I realize this sounds really good..but it wasn't. It was also leaking oil.

salmon fettucine - little flakes of salmon on a bed of pasta with way too rich fettucine sauce


It's not even THAT cheap for being in the asian ghetto.

Gypsys, you're making me fat
clogging my arteries with cheese and bacon
Why is your food so tasty, what's up with that?
It's always the godfather's favorite that I'm taken

Tasty food, not for those who can't take lactose
not to be mistaken for galactose
Just kidding, couldn't find anything to rhyme
Will try harder next time

Godfather's favorite and Crazy Alfredo, these are both my favorites.  But be careful, eat too much and it'll kill ya.  The food is tasty, the garlic olive oil bread they come with is always good.  But this place uses heavy whipping cream by the vat so be careful.  This is a favorite at the Asian Ghetto, I highly recommend it.

I had a dream about Gypsy's Chicken last week, so this week (my Spring break)  I flew from Phoenix to Oakland, and requested my boyfriend to take me to Gypsy's.

I ordered Gypsy's Chicken and it was still delicious like in my undergrad memories. The mushrooms were yummy just like they always were. Only downside is that I think their portions decreased by A LOT. I noticed a Pepe's Pizza & Pasta buffet across the street and was thinking maybe that's what attributed to Gypsy's scanty portions. I say you should give more food, so that students would pay a little more for extra food to take home.

I used to always get the Mediterranean or Chicken Alfredo. Both of those are delicious. The garlic bread is so yummy. I can eat that all the time for real. Man, I miss Berkeley!

This is some of the most delicious down-home Italian I have ever had. Seriously - what a delicious dive in the Berkeley Asian ghetto of all places. I had the pollo gorgonzola tortellini meal deal. I was so impressed with EVERYTHING - from the pasta/sauce - scrumdillyumptious, the garlic bread with roasted garlic smeared on it, and the generously portioned side salad. If you're a local, and you are looking for yumminess, you should go!

If you watch them cook your hearty-tasty meals, you'll know why it's so tasty.

The answer is: BUTTER.

Anything NOT tomato sauce based (pesto - only green with a small amount of pesto if you notice, alfredo, creme sauce, etc etc) uses a quarter, if not a half, stick of butter. CHOO CHOO. NEXT STOP, MY THIGHS!

Plus, this doesn't count the half-and-half they add later. CCCCOMBO.

All I'm saying is people should beware if they eat something cream-based here on a daily basis. The food ain't shabby. I mean, why does it win BEST ITALIAN on Daily Cal from year to year? Maybe because it's the ONLY Italian restaurant in the area. Seriously, there's no one else to nominate unless you count Sun Hong Kong's Over 9000 Menu offering of spaghetti and macaroni as a contender.

Oh well, I got over their salads, pasta, and pizza real quick and have resulted to a Calzone-only diet here.

Yummy, affordable Italian take-out food right next to the UC campus. Win!

Gypsy's is a staple for Cal students. If you are in the Berkeley area, I definitely recommend stopping by Gypsy's for lunch, dinner, late night munchies, whatever.  They have an extensive menu and everything is pretty good.  I usually get pasta, but the calzones are good too (MASSIVE and take about 15 min to cook after you order).

You get a bang for your buck, food is nom nom, service is relatively fast.  It might not be worth taking a BART ride over solely for the purpose of eating here, but you should definitely try Gypsy's if you're close by and looking for a quick bite.

Really great food for the return on the stomach AND wallet! My friend had a pesto calzone that he deemed fit to feed an entire family. I had a dish of penne pasta with tomato and spinach all in a cream sauce--it might also feed a family (maybe half of my family, given we are big eaters LOL).
