Plus, with the pasta dishes, they do give a nice crusty piece of bread with roasted garlic smeared on top. Not only are the servings generous, they're so bargain priced--about $6 for each of our dishes. Not a full service place; you pick up your order when your number's called, but not unusual in a college town. Why I haven't eaten here more in the past, I'm not sure, but I know I'll be back in time!

Yes, if you're a poor college student and need to eat decent food to survive, eating at Gypsys will do you good. HOWEVER, if you're the least bit health conscious , this is NOT the place for you!

Many of the pasta dishes that I have seen and/or eaten (and I've seen many) contain an excessive amount of grease/oil/butter.  Calzones, when cut open in the cardboard take-out boxes, will ooze out ounces of grease and render the grease-soaked box useless.  Especially the pesto calzone...Bleh.  Jennifer W. states it quite succinctly: eating here is a "cheap, sick, quilty pleasure."  Food is decent; Splurge if you will, but pay the price in life expectancy.

Side note: Back in the day, I always preferred to eat at the Ma n Pop owned Linguini place across the street (lobby of the hotel) since their pasta dishes were much simpler, less greasy and more flavorful.  Now, it's replaced by house of curries =( sad-sies
Food Poisoning.  When I was living in shared housing.  Not fun.  I will spare you the gruesome details, but I haven't been back since.

During my first trip to Berkley we happen to be walking around the "Asian Ghetto," and decided to give Gypsy's a chance. The place was definitely crowded, so has to be good, right? The line to order was a little crazy and long, and finding a table was also another mission as well.

I ordered the meal special which was a dinner item of your choice with a salad and drink.  I was in the mood for pizza so I ordered the Hawaiian pizza with ham and pineapple. The pizza and salad portions are huge! so very filling and with plenty leftover for later. The salad was actually good, I thought the lettuce would be brown and dry for some reason, but no it was very good. Also, came with cucumbers and way too much ranch dressing, but still not bad.

The pizza was very good, but huge! The ham and pineapple were very juicy and tasty, and most importantly not burnt. The dough and/or crust was also very good, also not dry or burnt. The pizza was also very cheesy, yummmm!!! Cheese is very important to me, I love cheese, lol.  

I definitely could've just ordered 1 pizza and shared with a friend instead of all of us ordering separate meals. Portions are very huge here, but really cheap so definitely worth it if you want something quick and cheap to eat. Like I said before though, the seating area is a little small and packed, so I would recommend eating outside or taking it to  go if you're in the area.

If I were ever to move away from Berkeley, my last meal in town would be here at Gypsy's. Dear Gypsy's, you are my first love in Berkeley, from the moment I tasted your Godfather's favorite during my first visit to Cal when I was shadowing my best friend from high school. I can't thank her enough for introducing us! Since then, Gypsy's, you've been there for me for many memorable occasions - curing DC food poisoning with your Chicken Marsala, mending a roomie's broken heart over Victor's Spaghetti, celebrating the last CS final ever with a round of Frutti Di Mare, inhaling Funghi pasta after a particularly long and hard dance rehearsal, sharing my hopes and dreams and a plate of Crazy Alfredo with my boyfriend, and many more times.

This place has such a delicious variety of unforgettable pasta dishes, is always crowded with pasta lovers, always very very fast, and extremely affordable and actually under-priced - ideal for all starving students and (ahem) young professionals. Their special of late is any menu item, a garden salad, and a soda drink for $7.99 (a bit more for some seafood dish) and makes a perfect meal for yourself or to share.

The secret to their cooking may be big quarts of cream and mounds of roasted garlic that they add liberally to nearly every dish which always results in unforgettable aromas and delicious creamy sauces that satisfies every food craving in your bones.

Sometimes they're so busy, they run out of garlic bread. Sometimes the chicken is too dry. Sometimes their calzones are cold in the middle. Sometimes there's a strange blizzard cold draft coming from one corner of the room. But I still heart you, Gypsy's, and hope you will always be here for me wherever I may go in life.

Drove from SF to eat their pasta and was not disappointed. Agreed there are other Italian places around, but hang on..this cheap? Nah... Tried their ravioli and it was smothered with cheese (and more cheese) and a cheese lover like me could know no bounds of happiness when I savoured this.

Come here for a quick and cheap Italian fix.

Gypsy's is one of my favorite Italian restaurants in the bay area. I like they way they cook the pasta, the prices are affordable, it's cooked and given promptly to you, and it's tasty tasty tasty!

I usually get the mediterranean with penne noodles, and alfredo sauce. I like the garlic on their bread, and I wish I could have a big bowl of it. If I'm with friends, I steal their garlic when they aren't looking :D 

I've tried a lot of the other items on their menu as well, and I like the green salad that you can get as a side along with your order. The downside is that they don't sell it a la carte, and you have to buy some food to go with it. I've also tried their calzone once, and it wasn't baked for long enough and the middle was still raw, and after sending it back to be baked, it was still uncooked in a few parts, which was disappointing. Their lasagna is good, but nothing too special, and I usually go for my favorite. The Gypsy's chicken is really good as well, the chicken is cooked tenderly, and there are some mushrooms that go well with the sauce.

My complaints about Gypsys are few and are mostly things they can't control. Their food is a bit on the heavy side, if I take home my leftovers, I can tell how much grease was in my food and it tastes bad cold so I have to heat it up. They could really use a bigger location as it gets packed during lunch and dinner. They should also consider expanding to San Jose, so I don't have to drive 50 something minutes for a good pasta craving. Also the parking is horrible around that area of Berkeley, and there are a lot of homeless people hanging around the restaurant and they hit you up for money and leftovers before and after you go in, and they will come in and take any food that is unattended at the table, so keep an eye out for that.

Besides that, it's an awesome place for cheap food. I've had 'expensive' Italian food and pasta, but none of it has been as good as Gypsy's in my opinion. Every time I'm up in the area, I make sure to stop by and grab a bite to eat.

Headed over here after a disappointing trip to Berkeley for Off The Grid. 

Everything looked so good and what made it even better is "any menu item + salad + soda" for $7.99. SWEEEEEET! The salad comes in a giant bowl! The lasagna was so big, I shared with the boyfriend AND had lunch the next day!

Cheap eats for poor college students!

The service here is absolute crap.  There seems to be just one main cashier during all the years that I've dined here.  From the time I started school in Berkeley, to the time I eventually graduated in San Francisco and beyond, same douche-y cashier.  If it weren't for the out-of-this-world food, the service alone would warrant one star.  However, after taking into consideration the quality and taste of the food, its operating hours, and the price, which would alone warrant five stars, I'll average it to four stars.

Seriously though, dude, it doesn't hurt to smile or say "hi", "bye", "thank you" or "you're welcome" once in a while.

Onto the food:

Salad: Drowning in dressing, but it does make me feel better about all the other carbs that I'm about to inhale.

Pizza: Umm... why order pizza _here_ when there's Blondies, Fat Slice, LaVal's, Cheeseboard and Zachary's, etc. so close in proximity?

Calzone: Bigger than the size of my head, but mostly filled with air.  Can probably comfortably and reasonably feed two, maybe even three, people, but tiny little gluttonous me can eat the whole thing by myself!

Pasta: Along with the calzone, the pasta is the crowning glory of Gypsy's.  Every pasta dish that I've ever ordered here has been incredible.  The pasta always seems to be cooked just right and the sauces well-seasoned.  Comes with a slice of french bread topped with a whole yummy, roasted garlic clove to lap up the sauce in.  MMMM!  My favorites are penne con pesto, and penne gorgonzola.  You can never go wrong.

I'll also give them props for occasionally paying a homeless person to sort out their recycling in the walkway inbetween the kitchen and the dining room, you know, stimulating the local economy and giving back to the poor.

All in all, I would definitely recommend this place, despite the occasional line, crass cashier and crude environment.  Where else can you get delicious, delicious Italian food without breaking bank at 11 PM?

Damn I love this place! I regret not going to Cal just because of Gypsy's but on the other hand I can't imagine my waist size if I did attend Cal. I'd eat here every day and you would probably have to roll me to class. 

If your looking for a high end Italian restaurant, this isn't the place to go. But if your looking for good, cheap food then you should definitely swing by. I can say confidently that everything on the menu is delicious. It's either drenched in cream, garlic, butter or cheese, how can you go wrong with any of those? 

My favorite would be the clam linguine, sausage and mushroom pizza and the pollo con pesto. Delicious. Oh and my girlfriend Inha, swears by the frutti de mare. So if your ever in the area, give it a try. 

Note: Not a date friendly place. They give you a piece of garlic bread with chunks of garlic on it... If you like your date and have hopes of a second date, spare them of the garlic breath and take em some where else...

What I like about this Top Dog is that there's hardly ever anyone there, except for at lunch times and on weekends, which means for a quick fix of  what is the best sausage and buns in the Bay Area (I just read that sentence again to myself and somehow it doesn't sound right).  Also, while you're waiting you can wander around and read the yellowing political cartoons and posters plastered around the story in an ever so conspiracy theoristesque fashion.

They have an awesome potato salad and cookies and other non-hotdog stuff here too.

yummy hot dogs for $3-$4!  Can't beat that!  The bun is a toasted french roll too, which is much better than the cheapy bun you usually get at other hot dog stands.  I wish they had toppings like grilled onions or cheese though.
I could spend hours reading the plenitude of libertarian sayings, articles, and cartoons posted on the walls.  As for the food, it's (just) sausages.  If that's what you want, they can be good.

Relatively convenient place for UC Berkeley students living on the north side of campus. Like with every Top Dog location, you're pretty much guaranteed some juicy and tasty hot dogs.

I wouldn't recommend their chili, though. Too much beans and very little heat.

For some reason this top dog isn't as good as the one on the south side of berkeley campus.  And it closes relatively early, maybe they think engineers doesn't need to search for food late at night.  

Nonetheless, i cannot figure out why the southside top dog taste better, seeing they are suppose to have the same supplier and has the same training to cook the sausages.  The price is $3 which is relatively pricey for how much you get.

Thus, I rather go to costco for the sausage and grill them myself as oppose to eat at this top dogs.

Great hot dogs.  3 bucks for one hot dog is a tad expensive but the quality is worth it.  I usually end up getting 2 hot dogs, the frankfurter.  And RC fucking Cola is the shit.  I hate soda and even I think this shit is so good.

Back in my lazy No'Side days, this was MY Top Dog. (Hm, I was lazier, ate more crap, and claimed to have my own Top Dog, but was also somehow skinnier than I am now that I [sometimes] go to the gym and sort of [sometimes, kinda] watch what I eat?? Damn age!) 

It's the mellowest, with the best seating options. That little food court it's in is hella cute, but most of the food there is mediocre, so the Dog is a good default.

There's a lot of crazy political stuff around, and the buns are just a bit dry, but we walked in a minute past eight, and the guy still served us (after informing us they were closed). I got a german frankfurter, the person I was with got a regular top dog and a sausage of some kind.  they were pretty good.  I would have rated this place a three but they get a bonus star for staying open for us.
The best hot dogs in the east bay.

Top Dog is awesome! The dogs are fat and juicy and the buns are warm and soft. I tried their kielbasa and it was nicely spiced and yumm-o!

I gave it 4 stars because the place isn't the most sanitary looking. But hey, it's meant for busy college students who are looking for a quick bite. If you can ignore the flies sitting on the sauerkraut and onions, then this place is a great snack shack for you!

I've always felt the staff was really unfriendly even when I'm being extra polite to them. Maybe it's supposed to be part of the charm or something. I've tried the Top Dog-didn't think it was anything special (tasted like a Costco one to me) and the Chicken Apple Sausage which I love!!! I like how the bread isn't too toasted but the sausages are always a bit too burnt for my liking. But, what do I know? I like my hot dogs boiled...Also, I really dislike how they only take cash under a certain amount but that isn't much different from the majority of places here in Berk. Maybe I'm not a proper connoisseur of sausages but I really think this place gets too much hype. I do enjoy the decor and sometimes rude customers who get whipped into shape by the employees though.

Never had the hot dogs here but I am assuming they are as good as the Top Dog's on Durant. I just came here to buy a bag of ice, because they sell them here for $1. It was a pretty good bargain. They aren't open too late during summer though.

Top dog how I loveth thee( for 30 years)! From the crunch of the dog, to those awesome sesame rolls, to the hot russian mustard, the killer sauer kraut. I loveth thee greatly.

Your bird dog also rocks my world. Sitting on the deck on a day like today with the sun out and people walking by...nothing could be finer.

Thanks TD!
Somehow this one just isn't as cool as the other Top Dogs.  Something about it makes it just a great hot dog, not a Top Dog.  Its still great, just not supreme.

Best sausage place evaaaaaaaa!!! Had every hot dog there at least once save the vegetarian one. Only thing I dont like is the bread... It is not soft at all. Although it is good for holdin the relish.
I've been going to this place since I was a kid and love it!  Great dogs at great prices.  Try the bratwurst with saurkraut!  Tops!
Awesome Top Dog. The bread was toasted to perfection and you gotta try the Hot Russian mustard - but beware it's hot hot hot!!!
Good dogs, but not great. Casper's is much better, IMO. Top Dog's potato salad is quite good though.

this is the same chain as the durant one.  same review.  hard to mess this kinda thing up.

if you want a hot dog, come here.  the end.

ok i'll say more.  the selection is huge.  the sausages and hot dogs are good.  and i love the selection of mustards.

it's hot dogs plain and simple.

there's a different vibe at dog north. it's alot more mellow. i remember when it was the training ground(my observation) for dog south. you can go in there and rap w/the guy or girl working the grill, drink your apple juice and eat your dogs. everything's the same as dog south. just an old top dog helpin' out students and locals forever...
Freshly grilled sausages in a crispy bun. Try their apple juice too. Cash only.

Top Dog's a Berkeley institution:
- Very flavorful hot dogs.  I'm not into straight beef so my favorites are the Bockwurst, Hot Link, Bird Dog, and Smoked Chicken Apple.  But your mileage may vary.
- Free onions and sauerkraut toppings to trick out your dog.
- Toasted bun.
- Easy to carry so you can eat while you walk.
- Old school soda fountain served in small paper cups... I feel like I'm in the 60s.
- Libertarian sayings plastered all over the interior.
- This one's conveniently located right near Soda Hall if you're a CS nerd.

Maybe not the best value-for-money, but you owe yourself at least one visit if you've never been.
Love this place...dont love the fact that Julie had to move away and no longer works here.  no more shitty (but free) coffee to bring up to GSPP.

I grew up in Chicago, so I'm big on hot dogs. My boyfriend had been raving about Top Dog literally for weeks before we made it there... and I'm giving it a fourth star mostly because he loves it. Service was quick, the dog was good, but I wasn't overwhelmed. I still miss my Vienna Beef dogs on poppy seed buns from back home, but this is about as close as California gets.
Yummy top dog. Low key and fast!

This place is a Berkeley icon, if u go to school here you must go. The price is a little high but the taste makes up for it. I usually get the calabrese, a spicy Italian sausage that is so amazing. Get crowded whn the bars get out but thank god its open. GO HERE

Go for the Veggie!!!! Go for the Veggie!!!! A $3 lunch that can't be beat. This is my favorite location since I've never seen busy. If you are a mayo crazed just ask for it, they have it behind the counter. 
remember: CASH ONLY

I love the idea of this place, but for some reason, i just wasn't impressed the two times i went. I ordered the german and the calabrese and while i preferred the calabrese, i didn't think it was worth the price. Both seemed underflavored and both the sausages and the bread were dry making it difficult to eat. I like that they heat their sausages on a flat top, they have a variety of sausages, and they use pretty good quality ingredients, but i'm happy with a simple $2 polish or hot dog from costco. Their hot dogs may be boiled and often overly salty, but it's good enough for someone simple like me.

Tried this place out when I started out my undergrad since it seemed to be a popular Berkeley spot. 

There's definitely a good variety of hot dogs and sausages but... overall seemed a bit pricey for what it is. Still worth checking out though.
Love it.  All the dogs are good but the Top Dog is the Top Dog.  This particular shop has abit more room to sit at the counter.  You will love it.

YUUUUUM!  My friend lived in the apt complex next to this location so every night after having fun in the city, we stopped by to get our favs.  My favorite is the Bratwurst..oh so yum.  I think my friend's favorite is the German Frankfurter but whatever, my selection is better keke*  Anyway, try this place if you are hungry in UC Berkley area....you won't regret it.

*Hotdog = YUM
*Service = good
*Location = I think this location is not as nice as the other ones but I still like it.

Oh yeah, on my last day at Berkley, I stopped by to get 3 bratwursts for my 6 hours trip back to L.A..
Good hot dog...simple yet delicious.  My favorite...hot link!

There is a Top Dog just like like this one, a few blocks away on durant... why isn't this one as cool? I think its because its all new and stuff. I don't really go for that in a ghetto hot dog eatery. Oh well, at least the hot dogs taste the same.
Friendly service.  Hot links are spicy and good.
Love this location. Love the hot dogs.

My parents were in Berkeley some 30+ years ago, and when I was growing up we'd often go to Berkeley and wind up at Top Dog. I think this was part of their plan to brainwash me into going to Berkeley, or maybe they just missed Top Dog. 

In any case, I wound up going to Berkeley and got a CS degree fueled by Top Dog (and Bongo Burger), so it worked. And now I miss them both. :(

A hot, bockwurst and kielbasa.  Always good sausages.  Small place with a few stools and two tables outside. One-man operation.  No parking lot, good luck on finding a spot on the street that is close by.  OK service, the usual nonsense, order taking person on the grill.   A real hole-in-the-wall place.  No dollar menu here, it has gotten a bit pricey over the years.    They serve RC Cola, no Coke or Pepsi.  You order, wait a few minutes, dogs and buns are grilled, you get them plain and apply your own condiments.

I used to run here from El Cerrito during high school on cross country "training runs". One day, I came back and prices were a quarter more. However, I'll still pay for the kiel's here. My favorite spots to eat on this side of campus.

This place is just OK. When I went my first time it was good.. when I went back and ordered the LINGUIÇA.... I couldn't even finish it because it was SOOOOOOOOOO freaking DRY!. Any drier and it was like eating jerky. The relish and ketchup helped, but man.. blehhhhh. If I go back there again, I'll definitely order something different.

As hot dog places go, pretty awesome.  They have a very wide selection, and almost all of them are great.  I used to eat here seriously four times a week, since it was right next to Soda Hall.

However remember- it just serves hot dogs.  Which is great if you are young and getting lots of exercise, but all that fat and meat does catch up with you.  Just a warning there.

Top Dog is also a "only in Berkeley" type of thing, because it's run by Libertarians.  This means there are ranty diatribes all over the walls about how the government is trying to oppress you by making you pay for roads and the fire department.  And how global warming is a myth being used to silence Freedom Lovers.  So that is a bit obnoxious.

I'm not sure but I think the dude working the counter is "leasing" the entire business while he's there, in keeping with the Libertarian principles of the place.  Whatever the reason, he has a bit of flexibility; you can cut deals with him for buying dogs in quantity.

Top Dog is my favorite hot dog source in the Bay Area, and this location is one of my two favorite Top Dog locations (the other being the one on Durant).

Beef, pork, veal (!) dogs, and even a good vegetarian dog (this coming from a meat eater). They know their stuff, and they care about their dogs.

Get a Top, add hot mustard, relish, ketchup, and saurkraut and enter dog nirvana.

This is another place that I've finally been to, thanks to my job on campus. I would definitely go back. I had the German Frankfurter, it was god damn delicious on that French roll. My co-workers made me get a second, so I picked the Kielbalsa but I just couldn't finish it and even from the first bite it was too much. The woman behind the counter was the right mix of friendly and efficient.

This location is a short walk from my lab and I find myself coming back here quite often. For $4.75, you get your choice of a dog, chips and drink. Can't beat that! The hot dogs are well done and very flavorful. There is plenty to look at and read all along the walls in here. They are very anti-authority but the reads are hilarious and a good time killer while waiting for your order. 

Definitely recommend this place and I'll be going here all summer long!

I like Top Dog in general, but I had a very bad experience at the Northside Top Dog ("Top Dog 2"?). Two years ago, after I ordered, the woman behind the counter started whipping up a special egg concoction for her friend (right next to my sizzling frankfurter).

The next day I had two finals and horrible food poisoning. I had to rush out of my first final, and as for my second final, I just didn't go.

I haven't been back to "Top Dog 2," but 2 stars for a finals week I'll never forget!

Im more of a fan of a the steamed hot dog and bun (Kasper's style hotdog) but the Top Dog is definitely a suitable substitute.  The grilled style hotdog with the grilled bun is delicious!  The bun is crispy on the outside and soft and warm on the inside.  The dog itself has a lot of flavor and has a good "snap" when you bite into it.  

I came to this little hold in the wall joint on a Sunday and it was dead.  I was the only person there and enjoyed a nice convo with the person working.  It was like I was at a bar chopp'n it up with a bartender.  Over all, great hot dog at a decent price ($3.00 a dog).  Definitely plan on coming back!
The dude who works at this Top Dog is kind of weird.  He looks like Jesus.  When I went there he was watching this weird Fantasia thing.  I think he was stoned. 'Nuff said.
Although the dogs are nearly $3, they are very tasty and if you are yearning for hotdogs, definately come here! I don't think they're open as late as the one on Durant...

Oh man I love this place.  I've been going here for years and I'm not tired of it.  I'm not much of a meat eater anymore but I will banish my obsessive health habits and throw down to eat some red meat and nitrates...hmmmmm ok they have a pretty good veggie dog too but the hotlink is to die for.  Plus it has all sorts of anarchist/libertarian literature to read and be amused by, which was so typical of the  Berkeley I grew up knowing.  Oh yeah and on a nice day you can sit out on the deck, eat and soak up some east bay sun got to get it while I can cuz we aint be gotten none over here in foggy SF.
Best Hot Dogs in the Bay Area!
My dad used to always take us here when we were kids after piano competitions. Back when he went to college, it only cost $1. Now prices have gone up, and I don't think hot dogs are worth the price.

though not the original top dog location, this place isn't that busy to me grab a kielbasa, polish, top dog or whatever.

i catch dogs for the nostalgia.

I don't get the hype, but it's just average size, average taste sausage in a bun.

Shop: disgusting and dirty... looks like nobody's ever wiped anything here in a few years!

And at $3, it's not even that cheap!!  I can get twice the size @ Costco for half the price.

All the sauerkraut, mustard, unions, and other fine condiments you want are provided for you. I usually get the Kielbasa and load it up with as much spicy mustard and sauerkraut I can fit in/on the thing.

I really don't think Top Dog is worth it for the price. Three dollars is just a little too much. I've kinda stopped going here after that realization.

I actually really like this place, service is pretty chill if you're a regular or know what you want right away.  I haven't been disappointed with Top Dog, you get a little better than what you pay for it.  I do, however, really like all the libertarian propaganda (i mean, information).  Always an interesting read while you wait for your dog.

I'm an absolute fan of Top Dog!

I always get lemon chicken with lots of sauerkraut, onions, and ketchup. Most of the dogs are $3 and you can add a small drink and a chip for extra $1.75. 

The dogs are super tasty and rolls are very crunchy.

It's open till 2am during the weekdays and 3am during the weekend so great place to fulfill your late night munchies.

Many friends of mine complain about this place being dirty and ghetto, but it's Berkeley. You can't really expect quality here :(
This is a classic when we go to Berkeley, it's simplicity of ingredients and complexity of flavors make it a "must have". Perfect portions, better price.

My favorite dog in Berkeley.  They will treat you nicer here than they do in the top dog on durant, and the libertarian propaganda is better here.  Be sure to try the calabrese (pronounced cala-breezy).

Sausages, sauerkraut and mustard: the requirements for an awesome hot dog.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: three stars.

Tog Dog's appeal is not so much in the preparation of the food as it is in the ingredients used. The rolls are not tasteless Wonderbread rolls, and the sausages are not your usual beef franks.

Just a sampling of the selection: Calabrese, Kielbasa, Bratwurst and Chicken & Apple.

The kicker is the vat of sauerkraut. It is not a hot dog without it.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: one star.

There is a huge difference between the Northside Top Dog and the Southside Top Dog. There are by far fewer people that visit TD2, so the wait is not nearly as unbearable and the cooks are far friendlier. We even knew each other on first name basis.
Such yummy goodness.  A brat fresh off the grill, heaping serving of kraut, warm bun ... slobber.

Who cares about a hot dog, it's just a sausage on a bum with some mustard/onion/cabbage thrown in. It's the free speech, baby! I absolutely love and agree with most of the wall posts in this joint. Mao should be real proud of this place.

I don't eat these thing anymore.  You know.....cholesterol.
So now that I'll live forever, I question whether longevity is worth it.
I miss top dog.
same libertarian dog, shorter lines.  I dig it
Delicious, delicious $3 kielbasa sausage in a toasted sesame seed bun. Can't beat that!

Okay...so I've only been here once but based off of the service and what I did have here, I have to give it 5 stars. The person working there was super nice and patient and gave me a rundown of all the hot dogs they have, describing the tastes. Since it was my first time ever going to a Top Dog, he also gave me a free hot dog sample to try! One of my food obsessions happens to be hot dogs as well and these hot dogs are off-the-charts good - juicy, flavorful, and best of all, the wonderful snap of a perfectly grilled hot dog. I couldn't ask for more in a hot dog. The regular top dog hot dog is perfect - exactly what you would expect from a hot dog! The calabrese is delicious too, but is more sausage-y and spicier; the flavor is intensely good. For me though, I have developed a bit of a sweet tooth, which really only applies to savory foods actually lol. So two of the other hot dogs really hit that sweet spot - the lemon chicken and smoked chicken apple. The lemon chicken is just perfection...no words could describe the happiness I felt biting into it; for me, it was miles above the rest of the flavors I tried. The chicken apple...while I didn't quite get the apple chunks, had a great chickeny taste with a slight hint of sweetness, although I actually found the lemon chicken to be a bit sweeter than the chicken apple! I will definitely be back to try more of their selection, but the lemon chicken and original top dog hot dog keep on calling to me.

Taste: 3
Value: 2
Service: 3

I came here a few weeks ago since I wanted something relatively small for dinner. Since I've tried the lemon chicken and chicken apple sausages (both of which are pretty good), I decided to go with the bird dog this time since it had cilantro and bell pepper, both of which I like. The dog was ready within a couple minutes, and I put on some relish/onions/ketchup. 

The hot dog itself was pretty good, but not "really good," hence the 3-star rating. I actually couldn't really taste the bell pepper either. I still stand by the fact that these hot dogs are not worth $3 each.

FYI, none of the Top Dogs have much seating. They all have bar-like seating with about 4-5 seats. There usually aren't more than that many people at any given time anyway, so you'll probably be able to find a seat.

The Top Dog on the south side of campus is definitely better.

I just wanted a quick bite to eat for lunch and I noticed that the service wasn't as fast and my lemon chicken was way burnt on a few parts. I think Top Dog in general is really good. This particular Top Dog was aaaiiite.

After many years away, the first place I went to eat  was Top Dog.  The Lemon Chicken and Hot Links were as good as I remembered.  Damn it, I'm getting hungry for them as I type this review.

These are gourmet hot dogs.  Seriously.  All the hot dog varieties are excellent and customizable with a variety of fixings, including four kinds of mustard,  to satisfy any palate.

Top dog is a fun place. I usually get only two kinds of hot dogs, the lemon chicken and the hot link. I've been going here over the years and meeting the different people serving the food. I always found their service style to be neat and engaging(and competent, evidenced when football games are held here)

Since their chip and drink selection is lacking, I would advise just walking across and buying it from the convenient store. Chips and a drink makes the meal feel so much more complete. I can't even explain it. If you eat there lunchtime, you should go chill outside with your fellow engineering/CS classmates. They need your attention. (Especially if you are female)
Really good dogs.  When I worked at Cal I would get two for lunch.  The lemon chicken is tasty, so you can get that one if you are trying to be "good."

Hot dog joint lives up to name!

Pros: Great dogs, and the staff ooze some sort of enigmatic cool.

Cons: Limited seating space, but a little bit more then the Durant location

The skinny: Four words, and folks who have eaten there will agree: "Best hot dog, ever!"

I took a visiting friend here and she ordered the Louisiana Hotlink.  As we were eating our topdogs, I noticed that her eyes were tearing up.  The sausage was way too spicy for her.  She said that the only reason she ordered it was because the cashier caught her off guard and it was the first thing that she saw on the menu.  The cashier coerced her into eating this sausage.

She will probably need a lot of therapy for this one.

There are three kinds of hot dog joints in the world:

1) Nathan's (one kind of frank, few toppings)
2) Spike's (one kind of frank, 1 billion different toppings)
3) Top Dog (13 kinds of dogs, a few toppings)

The hot link is to die for, and it will kill you.  If they served any kind of freshly fried potato it'd be knocked up to a five.

It was good enough for me to come back.  Got the chicken apple sausage twice over the weekend and it was sufficient as a quick snack.  Not overly amazing or anything, but decent (I agree with the guy who prefers less burnt stuff on them).

Kids who work there are pretty stoned and oblivious.  Latex gloves or more frequent hand washing would be good.

Though I love all the top dog locations in Berkeley (they even have one in San Jose now!), Top Dog 2 will always be near and dear to my heart do to its proximity to Soda and Cory Halls (CS/EE buildings).  This place has provided sustenance after long long hours of slaving away on projects, and always brings a smile to my face after being frustrated by difficult problems and tough professors.

My favorite is the chicken apple sausage, butterfly cut so I get nice grill marks all over.  Bread is nice and fresh and toasty.  Mmmmm.  I can recreate the flavors by stopping by the top dog in SJ near my work, but I will never forget the memories of bliss going here for a quick respite before I spend the rest of the night in Soda Hall.

I was utterly disappointed by this place.  This joint has been around for such a long time.  I remember having it once a long time ago (pre yelp days) and it was okay.  I went back this Saturday b/c we wanted to try out some places in the East Bay.  Also b/c the week before, we had tried Underdog and we really wanted to compare.  Underdog wins hands down.  The dog here is way too salty.  You don't taste the meat in it.  I've always eaten anything covered in ketchup, but this time, i felt like tossing the entire thing away.  but I finished it anway, b/c of the ketchup.

The condiments aren't great and the buns are just bulk, but the non-chicken sausages are excellent, and that's what matters, right? Well, only up to a point. Despite the limited lunch options on the north side of campus, I still only come here once a month or so - enjoy it, but then don't want to have another one any time soon. I think it's because the saltiness and slight chemicalliness necessary in a top-notch dog deter me: I don't have the same problem with the not-as-good Miller franks at Oscar's on Shattuck. So I'm punishing Top Dog for being too good, which is very unlibertarian and absolutely justifiable.

(The figurative) you have got to be joking that this is 4 stars.

Ate there today.  Ordered a Chili Cheese Dog.
The hotdog itself - just the meat part - was good.

The cheese was almost non-existent, but here's the big WTF!

WTF was that chili?  It was the singularly most vile-tasting chili I've ever eaten.  Worse than any unsalted non-fat vegan chili you can imagine.
It was as if one boiled up some chili beans and mixed them up with some horrible chunks of tomatoes and water.
Zero flavor.
Disgusting.
I tell ya, I am no chili snob.  I can eat any of the above - no salt, vegan, and no fat.  But that stuff  was not chili in any sense of the imagination.

Wife and son thought the exact same thing.

And the soda selection...  RC what???  It tasted like rubber.

Anyhow, I got far better food at the food truck near the student store.

Yuck!

Five stars for the memories. This Top Dog location has been around at least 25 years that I know of. 

I'm going to use first names here only; we did illicit stuff. Would the statute of limitations have run out on drug offenses from so many years ago? Would my employers care now about my youthful indescretion?

We went to this Hearst St. Top Dog because our good buddy, Sam, slung hot dogs there. Sam was famous at Berkeley High for taking small amounts of LSD every day for a year. His personality never recovered, but he was good at making those dogs (he's a research scientist today). 

Anyway, the afternoon in question, my first love, Justin, and I bought some hash off Sam, and smoked it on the patio at the Hearst St. Top Dog.  Being the innocent kid that I was at 16, the THC hit me pretty hard, and I couldn't ride my bike back down Hearst (it's steep). Justin had to basically carry me and my bike home. A few more experiences like this later, and I had completely given up on drugs and alcohol at the tender age of 17.

Ah, a childhood in Berkeley!

#810

Omigod this place is freaking amazing. They toast the buns. They have amazing sausages. They have amazing greasy food to hit the spot.

I consistently order the Calabrese. MMMMMMMmmmmmmm!!!

I dream of the days when my company catered with Top Dog. I dream about wonderful wonderful sausages cooked perfectly. *droool*

Why do holes in the wall become legendary?  Because they serve great products, sometimes virtually unchanged, at extremely fair prices, for DECADES!   

That's right, I'm so old (please don't fill in the blank) .... I've visited this Top Dog for decades back to my UC undergrad days, and it has always, ALWAYS been one of the best dogs anywhere.  The dogs at this northside location are the same as south side, btw, but more relaxed, no one will bother you.

To me, the perfectly spicy and juicy hot link is king.  But they have many other delights including the fennely calabrese, the luxurious brat, the german garlic and many more.  I highly recommend you starve yourself before going so you can each try at least two different dogs... one does not do justice to the experience, and at $3 a dog, you can splurge.  (the dogs will keep for later, but seriously, just go for it!)

I've always liked the libertarian flair here, they even have a well-worn book on the counter of the collected sayings of Mises the great Austrian school economist.  But I digress.... you can select and apply if not slather several mustards (no stinkin' catsup here!), fresh diced onion, sauerkraut and pickle relish.  The seeded bun is toasted (natch) and has just the right balance of substance, crispness and spongyness to soak up the dietetically abominable but palate lovable sausage, ah, essences.   

The grillmistress or grillmeister may be a bit high. So what.  No booze and you may not find a nearby seat. So what.  Cross the street onto campus and find a bench and then try to defend your dog from the squirrels.

FWIW, the sausages come from Schwarz Sausage in the Mission... sadly, they only sell wholesale. So go to Top Dog.  Indulge.  Repeat.

Somehow feels smaller than Top Dog (1) but it's really the same size. What you'd expect, good hotdog, good service, just that sometimes it gets crowded during passing periods because it's where a lot of engineers eat (since it's on Northside) I was only there for a section and got hungry. Not bad!

Summary: This review has my original thoughts, a message I received  from an angry man, and my response to his virtual attack.  
The main point is that due to my own experience, there is a high chance that I'll get a BURNED hot dog if I go here.


Top dog has always had a lot of hype.  I've been living near campus for a few years now and the hype has always been the same, and so have my experiences with it.  I'm a health freak so I hardly ever eat hot dogs.  The few times that I've had Top Dog was due to Peer pressure or for stress release.  Right when you order you'll notice that there are just a whole bunch of dogs sitting on the cold part of the grill.  While I'm deciding the workers give off a vibe of impatience as if I'm supposed to be an expert on their variety of sausages.  Anyways right when I order the cook moves a hot dog from the cold part to the hot part of the grill.  I'm assuming that the dogs have been pre-cooked and this process is merely to heat up the dogs for eating.  However they burn them every single time i've been there, which is probably 5 or 6 times over the years.  It's almost like they purposely systematically burn one side, then flip it over and burn the opposite side and then hide the charred sides of the dog by enveloping it in a cheap bun.  

I personally do not like eating Burnt Hot dogs.  two stars.

EDIT: here's a message that I received from an angry kitchen employee from a different restaurant, along with my response.

"Kitchen Employee"
((((I work in a kitchen and just wanted to let you know some things you seem un-aware of.....
   The part of the grill your calling "cold" is in fact over 150f.
   Not all dogs are "pre-cooked"
    If they are pre cooked it was pressure cooked to treat the meat, not grilled to expand it or give flavor
    the "burn" you refer to is the grease from the dog and other dogs before it adding flavor (some dogs carmalize due to sugars, others just grease.)
    You obivsuly know nothing of breads.....
    To some-up your tastes seem like that of a 4 year olds, and not someone who needs to be going around writeing un-informed yelp reviews))))))


"And here is my response to the self righteous defender of burned food"
I'm not going to argue with you about kitchen etiquette or processes because I'm probably wrong.

However I agree with you that even a four year old can tell when food is burned. Let me put it this way for you. That "black stuff" coating the food? It doesn't taste good to me and Oh it causes cancer.

Do I care why that "black stuff" is all over my dog because of caramelized sugar nonsense? Rhetorical question, no.

In addition to the fact that yelp reviewers require NO credentials, my review was VERY well informed and the truth remains that a LARGE MAJORITY of customers at this establishment will actually get "burned" hot dogs. If people believe the burned black cancer causing stuff all over their food is caramelized sugar then they are still free to go try it.

I Stand by my review.

The hot link is the star of my world. Greasy porkaliciousness wrapped in the soft, but not too soft, sesame seed bun. I cant visit berkeley without grabbing a dog and i suggest you do too. I tried the linguisa but still prefer the hot link. Wish they had grilled onions on the side

One of my friends has a great story about how he was locked in here way back in the day during some of the riots. Can you imagine 7 hours inside Top Dog? At least you have something tasty to eat! Always a reliable frankfurter regular stop walking up Hearst on the way to a show at the Greek Theater.
Great dogs so conveniently close to the co-op.

loving the top dogs selection! I had their  kielbasa and it was pretty good. Definitely worthy of 3 stars! if their kielbasa was only 3 stars, why did i give them 4 stars on my yelp review? well, the additional star is courtesy of University of Cal @ Berkeley school of education! The school hosted some sort of gathering in front of Pat Brown's cafe and Top Dog cater the event! I scored a free top dog! was it worth the additional star, probably not, but since i am in such a giving mood, why not?

Having grown up in Berkeley, the one on Durant has many great memories, but I like the location ,convenience and speed with which you are served at Hearst.  The quality is high, the condiments are kept tidy.  They have several kinds of mustard, one of which was labeled "Milde", to which we always added a "w" at the end as a joke.
Only one downside: occasionally they hire some loudmouth as a cook who loves the sound of his own voice and makes you listen to his inane comments while you wait for your dog. Otherwise, love them dogs!

Came here with some co-workers after an event at the Berkeley campus.  This was my first time at a Top Dog... and after hearing about it, I felt I needed to give it a whirl.

My dogs of choice:
Top Dog Frankfurter - Standard dog... juicy, flavorful, love the bread... loaded it with ketchup and mustard after the first bite.

German Frankfurter - Definitely tasted the HINT of garlic... but I like me a garlic KICK.  Loaded this guy up with mustard and ketchup ftw.  

Hot Link - There was a claim that this was supposed to be super hot... so I tried it.  I found out that they had a hot sauce to add as well, so I tried that as well.  Admittedly, this sucker had KICK.  Very good.  It needed nothing else but the dog and sauce.  (folks, I think we have a winner here).

I have to say, the prices are somewhat steep for what you get.  I'm glad I ended up getting the Hot Link because it sorta saved the experience for me.  The Hot Link came way after the fact too.. after I'd finished both my other dogs.  

The cashier / dog maker was very nice and enjoyed watching us all chow down.  If not for the nice person behind the counter and Hot Link, this would've definitely only been a 3 Star joint..

Where else can you have a hot link, kielbasa, bockwurst, bratwurst, or just regular hot dog grilled to perfection on a toasted sesame bread?  I can either go to Top Dog or do it myself with the help of my beat-up weber grill in my own backyard.  

For me hot dog is best with sauerkraut and mustard (any mustard).  Everything else is optional.  Thankfully they provide plenty of sauerkraut, as well as ketchup, relish, onion and choices of mustard.

This top dog is nested in small food court along with a few other joints.  Unlike the legendary Top Dog on the south side of UC campus that hardly has any place to sit (http://www.yelp.com/biz/top-dog-berkeley),  here you can easily find a seating outside to relax and enjoy your warm hot dog.

The only downside is while they kept increasing the price over the years, the sausages seem to get smaller and smaller (minus 1 star) compared to when I was a regular during my college years.

Irene S. used to work at this top dog & if we promised to clean the grill & mop the floor for her while she sat outside on the deck & smoked she'd give us free top dogs.   I used to live off this stuff.

I'd have given 5 stars if she just gave them to us without having to do manual labor.  It's not like they were HER top dogs.

When you have a craving for meat, you should go here. The dogs are pretty tasty. My ultimate favorite is the lemon chicken one. However, I still don't like the idea that the dogs have already been grilled and are just reheated when you order them. I also want to complain about the shortness of the dogs. It definitely makes you want to buy more. The toasted hot dog bread is a nice touch.

Let me start by listing my attributes that make me a superior hot dog connoisseur:

1. I  own two weener dogs
2. I was a hot dog for halloween
3. Sometimes I wear my hot dog costume to Cal Football Games
4. 3 years of experience tailgating A's games, mostly grilling bratwurst
5. 2+ years experience crawdad fishing with hot dogs, circa 1985-'87


That being said, this is my favorite location of the Top Dog joints. The others have great dogs, but this place is a little more low key and has more seating area. My favorite part about it is the outdoor seating that is elevated and overlooks Hearst.

The dogs are great, the attitude is easy going and friendly, and there is an ample supply of condiments, including warm Sauer Kraut. Beware of the Hot Russian Mustard, I severely underestimated its strength last week and almost had to throw up.

Yummmmmm........

My fav Top Dog location!  It's near my Alma Mater (PSR), not grungy like the cross-campus location, and thier dogs are just as good as every other Top Dog!

My favs are Lemon Chicken and Polish!

You can also buy them & the buns in bulk and BBQ them yourself!  

When I crave a Top Dog- this is the location my tatse buds lead me to!

UUUUUUMMMMMM!!!

I dream about Top Dog.

That 1st bite... crunchy bun, hot grilled dog, mustard.

But the anticipation of the 1st bite is a good moment too-- there's nothing like it.

After a couple days in SF we decided to skip going to the new Academy of Science museum, and instead go over to the EastBay-- which by comparison sounded like it would be quieter, calmer, more attuned to what we needed. And it was that, plus a beautiful autumn day..So what did we need 1st ??-- TOP DOG!  

The Northside location is my all time favorite one... it's just got that perfect funky ambiance... step in, tell the cook what dog you want & just savor the moment.   I love reading all the handwritten ' thoughts for the day' postings on the wall... my favorite being " there's always free cheese in a mousetrap.'  Then sit & watch the scene across from Cal-- ah, brings back good memories. 

But the memory of the 1st Top Dog on Durant is of my then- boyfriend,  who after a date would drop me at the dorm, and I found out later would THEN go to Top Dog!! before he went home.   Another Top Dog memory is of living in a brown shingle apt. house on Ridge road and taking a short cut thru a vacant lot to cross Hearst to the campus!  Shortly after that year, guess what went in there? Our T.D. !  Hate to say how many years ago that was, but it's still a fun memory. 

So we each had 2 dogs today-- i can never stop ordering the Kielbasa-- and with a full, happy tummy, hit the road to head north to home. And very content to have this little dream come true.

julia l. is trying to claim this top dog for her own, but i'm going to have to set the record straight.

top dog two was MY top dog.

as a freshman, living in the dorms up the hill, this was where i procured my first during-college employment. at the time, i was the only girl in the top dog stable, making me something of a novelty. (boobies? yes, please, i'll take three hot dogs kthx!) i worked a few nights a week, grilling dogs, watching tv, drinking hot chocolate, taking A LOT of cigarette breaks (this was back in the cigarette-sellin' days of the dog) and manipulating my friends into helping me clean up. (i may have given away some free top dogs.)

i had some really awesome regular customers.

there was the dude who came in every tuesday to watch buffy with me and jen e. the gawking construction worker who was always too shy to actually speak to me. the old man who came in & ordered apple juice, drank it down, burped, and ordered a refill.

occasionally, i would be forced to work a shift at the southside dog and would always hate it. who were all these customers? why was everyone so drunk? why couldn't i just sit on a stool and read? i'd always be so happy to go to work at number two after one of those shifts, appreciating immensely how closing at ten meant you really limited the number of drunks you'd have to serve in a given night.

one time, i found a tiny glass pipe & some grass hidden under the counter. this, obviously, belonged to someone who worked with me. i claimed it, & to this day i own it. a reminder of the old days, really.

another time, the ONLY time in my life i've ever had a uti, i tried to call in sick to a shift only to be strong-armed into coming in. i can't recall too many details, only that this was probably THE WORST DAY OF MY LIFE. 

sweet, sweet memories.

& proof, total proof, that this top dog was mine.

This is a 3.5 in my book - the burger is too small given the price - actually like their fries better than burger.  I had the mushroom burger - while I enjoyed it - it was not memorable and it was definitely on the smallish side - In-n-out is same size at 1/2 the price.  

I guess if it is open (and nothing comparative was) and you are on campus it might be better than the burgers on campus but while I admire successful small business where I see owner behind the stand grinding it out to make business a success - the line can be very slow if more than a half dozen people (the cooking area is absurdly tiny - we beat a crowd of a dozen by less than minute and the difference in time would have been at least 30 minutes) - 

So even though 3 stars I would return if my son said he wanted to go but wouldn't be in my rotation if I was going to college for the next four years (as my son will be)
used to go here for lunch a couple of times a month .  burgers are good, fries are good. waiting can be a pain sometimes especially  if  you only get a 30 minute lunch.falafel plates were tasty.

Great place, good service.  First thing I tried was their half falafel. The portion was just right for lunch. The falafel was moist and delicious, it came in pita bread . Really enjoyed it.  Next time got half Persian burger. The portion size was good and the price was fantastic.  

I hear Persian burger is a Berkeley "institution".

No. 3 Cheeseburger (no tomato, no lettuce) meal with fries and double-dip ranch-ketchup. MMMM. 

Fulfilling and convenient meal for that hour-and-a-half break between awkwardly-timed midday classes.

My husband and I like the onion rings here, and the black bean burger is very good, too. The coffee has been good, but no free refills. Service can be slow and occasionally unpleasant. Lots of newspapers by the door to browse while you wait/eat.
i've never had anything else here except the persian burger...which is frickin delicious

Of the burger places i've tried in Berkeley, this is my favorite. They use quality Niman Ranch beef, frozen, but you can still tell the difference. I usually get the cheeseburger and fries or onion rings or both if i'm sharing with someone. The fries and onion rings are always crisp and perfect while the burger also has good flavor. The one thing i don't like is that they use thick roll-like buns here which they toast and i prefer soft buns with my burgers so everything doesn't get squished out as i'm eating. The persian burger is also really good and probably my new favorite since they use a softer baguette for this one. 

The burgers will definitely fill you up and it's a good price for a great quality burger.

This place does everything on their menu right.

The turkey burger has a healthy feel while still being satisfying.

The bacon cheeseburger is a calorie splurge no doubt, but ohhh is it worth it (don't eat this every day though)

The falafel is okay, nothing spectacular unfortunately, but considering the strength of their other offerings I don't fault them too much because some times you just want a filling meal without killing bambi or her friends, that is when the full falafel comes in.  

The breakfast special used to be the deal of the century but since has crept up in price.  Still though two eggs toast and some tasty potatoes for around $4 is not too shabby at all.

Finally the Persian burger, quite delish, with nice peppery grilled flavor with just enough lather of mayo on a french roll.  Wonderful!

I would give this place 2.5 stars if it was available, but since I feel like most folks have overrated this place, I'm going to stick with 2.  Also the "Meh, I've experienced better" description that goes along with 2 stars is about how I feel about this place.

No free refills on soda?  What the hell?  $1.30 for a small soda with no free refills at a burger place is just not right, especially since it would probably cost about a quarter to give you two refills.  

The burger I had was good (mushroom cheese) but the slice of cheese was not thick and didn't even cover the whole surface area of the burger. STOP SKIMPING!  The bun is also way too big.  Eating just the bun is a mini meal in itself.  I found the price point to be a little high (I think it was a little over $8 for the combo (mushroom cheese burger, small soda and fries)).  

I'm not a big fan of crinkle cut fries, but I may be the outsider on that one b/c all of the people I was with love crinkle cut fries.

The service was terrible and the cashier made it seem like she was doing me a favor just by being there.  This was a weekend day a few weeks ago.  She was rude and had an attitude.  While waiting for my meal and drinking my non-free refill small soda, I decided I was going to need another beverage of some sort.  I asked for a cup of water and the cashier looked at me for a second and said, "didn't you get a soda?"  I was already sick of the poor service, so I simply gave her a stone face and answered "yes."  I guess she thought that if I had a soda, there was no conceivable reason why I might want a cup of water....  She begrudgingly gave me a cup of water.

There is ketchup and Ranch dressing on the counter, but one thing was missing, sauce cups.  When I got my food, I realized why, there was one sauce cup placed on my tray.  I guess they want to limit the sauce that you can get.  I'm glad they don't do this at any other burger place I've been to, if you just take Berkeley Burger places, none of them come across this stingy, Barneys, Oscars, Nations, All Fast Food Places etc.

I read another review that said that the bacon isn't pork?  I'm glad I didn't order a bacon burger, but that just seems suspect to me.  I've heard of turkey bacon, but it is always called turkey bacon so there is no confusion.  

If I'm going to spend this kind of money, I would much rather go to Barney's.  The burgers are better, the service is friendlier, the indgrediants are better etc.  Nations doesn't have all the options, but I would go for Nation's over this place.  Free soda refills, all the sauce you can eat and an overall good burger.

One more thing before I step off the soapbox, it was freezing inside.  It was a cold say to begin with, but it was even colder inside.  I guess everyone in the kitchen wanted to make sure they were not warm, who cares about the customers anyway.  An overhaul in customer service and a few minor changes and this place would be a lot better.  Hopefully the owners will read this and make the improvements.  It would cost them a new cashier and a few cents in water, soda, and sauce.

The Black Bean Burger at Bongo Burger is out of this world. I can't remember the first time I had it, but the patty has actual whole black beans in it, and the entire burger--though it somehow takes 20 minutes to cook and assemble--is a true treat. Plus, it is a tried and true hangover cure, which has saved me on multiple occasions.

The fries are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, and the falafel is extremely tasty--and they do not use hydrogenated oils. The prices are not that bad, though still a little much for me to spend on lunch, so I don't end up going very often.


The big reason I don't end up going very often, though, is that the location on Euclid has HUGE LINES at lunchtime, every day, without fail. And even if they didn't, which happens if you get there early enough, it somehow takes them 20-25 minutes to get everything made and assembled anyway. If I get there at noon, I can expect to leave with my food to run back up the hill to my office AFTER 12:30, and I only get a 30 minute lunch break. I haven't been back here in months because I can no longer take liberties with said break, and it really is a sad thing.
plainnnnn blahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh  fries are ok its hard to mess up anything fried :)

I really like their burgers, especially the bacon one that I always get, and their fries are freshly fried to order. And you have to get the white sauce to dip the fries in, they are soooo wonderful. The buns are also toasty and delicious, it'll really fill you up, for about 9 dollars for the meal. The burgers are quite large and decent portions for a burger, not dry at all but not entirely juicy-but still quite good.

I also tried the persion burger, but its more like a sandwich and it's not one of my favorites because it just doesn't seem to fill me up as much.
The food is good but the service is awful. I rather have less tasty food to see that cashier lady. I won't go there again.

The standard Niman ranch beef burger ($4.25) or turkey burger ($4.50) are solid choices and never disappointed me. I just got bored of their food because nothing really set them apart in taste (seasoning is standard), but they did their stuff consistently.

Burgers are solid, but I found their other Middle Eastern offerings quite lacking. Pretty cheap prices for a decent burger if you're in the mood for it, but it's nothing awesome. Meh, I've moved on.

Great spin on hamburgers! I love their Persian Burger. It's in a long roll with a thin pattie of lamb. It's flavorful, moist, and delicious! Their fries are excellent, as well as their mushroom burger. Everything is great here.
i really like food here.  better than any regular hamburger.  i like the northside bongo burger better than the southside one.

Get the Persian Burger.  It's a sub sandwich sized burger made with seasoned lamb in lieu of beef.  It is quite unique and tasty.  Although probably the best non-gourmet burgers in Berkeley, you pay for that distinction as the meal combos (with small drinks and fries) come in just shy of $10.
Chicken Sandwich - add the Sumac --- OFF THE HOOK!!! Great quality, a little expensive, but you get whaht you pay fro in the end.  Everything is grileld to order - no heat lamps for thier burgers!

When I lived on northside I ate here often. Pretty good burgers, the turkey burger is definitely one of the better turkey burgers i have ever had (tasty seasonings). However I once made the mistake (early in my patronage of bongo burger when i was living near telegraph) to order a burger with bacon on it. HUGE MISTAKE. No pork here folks and what the hell is beef bacon anyways? Its just not right is what it is. So dont do it. They shouldn't confuse us bacon lovers like that, its just mean. 

Breakfast deals are pretty reasonable here too, although only had the egg plates a couple of times and one time it was pretty oily. 

the fries rule though!

O man I love this place!!  My best friend and I were slaving away on the streets on Berkeley and came across Bongo Burger.  Since we were both starving, we went inside.  I am so glad that we did!  I ordered the hummus/veggie plate, so delicious! Big portions too! Come to Orange County please...:]

Taste: 4
Value: 3
Service: 3

Like my review for their Southside location, I think their sandwiches are pretty good, but definitely overpriced. I've only been to the Northside location two times.

I live in So-cal and whenever I'm up in bay area I come out to Bongo Burger, Persian Burger is the best.. tastes, smells and looks just like the burgers we eat back in motherland. and ppl that work here are very friendly and awesome.
A completely competent burger.

The persian burger is great. Most of their food here is actually great. I know I tried their steak sandwich and remember thinking it was a little skimpy but all in all...great place for a untradiational burger/sandwich.

Quality Burgers and quality ingredients on the burgers.


Tastes Amazing:
Buns
Burgers
Sauce
Tomatoes
Lettuce
etc.

Completely fresh and incredible.

The straight up All-American Burger will cost you $5.00 and it will more than fill you up.

Completely worth it.

Onion Rings: sum of the better ones around oddly enough...NOT 2much batter(sum cornmeal mixed in?...yum)...good amount of onion...

Fries: as a prev yelper stated-as bad as cafeteria...yp

burgers: avg-better many other places( if distance not an issue, these are ok)...make SURE u specify med rare/med, otherwise a cinder

Lamb Burger: meh...no flavor

Veg Plate: avg +...ask for X-tra pita

Service: tends 2get a bad rap...never had a prob...

seems popular for a bargain breakfast ala Nations.

This place is good for quick, tasty burgers and sandwiches. Usually get the Persian burger, and though it's really delicious, I still didn't feel like I was getting the best bang for my buck. Otherwise, if you want to treat yourself, do stop by Bongo Burger and grab a bite! There's a quite a line during lunch hour by the way...

Every once in a while, a girl just wants some french fres (okay, maybe every few days).  When that craving hits, I run to Bongo Burger for consistently crispy, salty, fully calorie-laden fried potato goodness.  The persian burger, which is lamb, is a nice departure from your typical burger, and the black bean burger is another interesting alternative - a little spicy, not as beany as you might expect, but all in all a good vegetarian option.  And my favorite part?  They big squirt bottle of ranch sauce at the counter.  Make yourself some russian dressing for those fries and you won't regret it.

Satisfying casual burgers perfect for a quick meal during a work break. 

I have been to this Bongo Burger location quite a few times because it is so close to work. The burgers at Bongo are similar to a fast-food burger, but made fresh with better ingredients. 

You order food at the counter and can decide to dine-in or have your food to-go. Bongo Burger can get quite busy during the noon rush and getting your food will take forever so avoid coming here if it is packed. 

The regular burgers are all pretty good, but I prefer the Persian burger. It is a large lamb patty sandwiched in French bread. Bongo burger is not super cheap, but you can get a meal with fries and a drink for $10. I did venture off the burgers once and ordered the falafel sandwich. While it was certainly the best falafel I have ever had, I thought it was good alternative if you are looking to get something vegetarian or just in the mood for something different. 

Despite being a little slow and not super cheap, I have yet to be let down by Bongo Burger.
Our new favorite burger place. I like how the burgers are big, but not thick - that way you can eat them without all the toppings falling out. Price is good too - $4.50 for a regular burger.

Normally I am vehnemently against all vegetarian items. It just doesn't sit well with my stomach and causes me to be both hungry later as well as a grumpier person all together. Except when I have had the portabello mushroom burger here. It's delicious, filling and tastes like meat.

I had the mushroom burger.  My daughter had a plain burger.

Burger:  3 stars--a well done piece of beef that turned into a hockey puck.  The toppings and the bun were fine--the burger ruined it.

Fries:  4 stars. Really good--crispy and served fresh.

Service:  3 stars.  The woman at the counter offered to cut my daughter's burger in half.  We asked for water--they use an old coffee pot filled with water as their pitcher--ick.

Not sure we would come back--but am curious about their Mediterranean fare.
Yuck!!!! How does a thin little patty ever qualify as a good burger?
Good turkey burgers, but I would avoid the falafel.

I just love this burger joint ever since my UCB student days...greasy take-out bag and all.

I've almost tried the entire menu.  I still go with my "first love" and that is the Number 7 (Persian Burger).

Juicy...mouth-watering...satisfying...this is what you want in your BURGER!

Prices are reasonable too.  The south-side campus location is also good too, but I prefer the north-side location.

Bongo is my kind of fast food.  Breakfast from Bongo is the way to start the day--particularly if the day follows an endless evening.  The 2 eggs any way with homefries and toast (sausage is extra) is nice and greasy, the perfect compliment to any hangover.  And the mornings tend to be pretty quiet, so it's a nice place to sit and eat and read the paper.  Burgers are also quite tasty--I love the black bean burger and the turkey burger.  The fries and the onion rings are fabulous (one of the cooks seems to follow the "I shall serve no fries before their time" rule), piping hot and slightly salted.  I tried the falafel plate for the first time tonight (falafel, tabouleh, salad and pita bread) and it was very tasty and filling.  And I felt healthy after eating it!  Well, kind of.  If I wasn't so full.

Soo good. The fries are exceptional, the burgers are good (mushroom burger all the way across the sky!!) and the service is fast. A bit pricey (burger + fries is 8 and change) but good enough that I still go there semi-regularly.

I like their mushroom burger and their lamb burger (I forgot the name). And trust me, I NEVER eat lamb--I just don't like the taste and smell of it. But this one was really good because it didn't taste or smell like the traditional lamb lol. 

I'm usually not a big sandwich/burger joint fan, but this place is pretty good! And I really think northside and southside one is about the same.
Had an order of the #9 combo deal (~$8): black bean burger (w/lettuce, tomato, & mayonnaise), fries, and soda. Food was delicious, staff was wonderful, and the ambiance was laid-back.
Friendly staff. Food tastes awesome. I love their fries it's so good
good persian burger

I went to Bongo Burger for the first time yesterday.  I wish I had knew about it when I was a student.  I ordered a Turkey Burger and I loved the toasted bun.  It tasted light, but also flavorful.  

I was impressed by the diversity of the menu, with items like the Persian burger, Baklavah, and crimped fries. I can't wait to go back and try the other stuff on the menu!

Other pluses:
1. the meat is Niman Ranch, more sustainably raised
2. the lady at the cash register was very friendly and made me feel at home

I love this place for the chicken plate.  The chix is always juicy and tasty, and goes great w/the salad and pita bread it comes with.  Plus the best part is the fresh fries.  

Good thing I don't live too close to this place, or I might get a heart attack soon from the fries...  

PS - Don't try to go to this location at Noon.  It's always packed w/a line out the door.  Try earlier or later.

I've been eating at Bongo's on and off for the last 40 years starting with binges of 2 or 3 Persian burgers after high school back in the 70's when the only location they had was on Durant that was 1/2 the size it is today. I tend to frequent the north-side location now as it's easier to park here than at the other 2 locations. I live about 3 hours away now, but we make a point of still coming here to indulge in their Persian burgers and bongo salads. Occasionally get a baklava as a treat for desert. All I can say is that if this place has been in business for 40 years they must be doing something right.
Aw yes, when you have the craving for a hearty burger with french fries.  Can also satisfy falafel cravings.

This place is definitely my guilty pleasure. My normal routine is order a burger meal (#2 - bacon burger - or #7 - turkey burger) to go, sneak it back to my room, and it in solitude. Everyone I know makes fun of me for eating at this place.

Sure, all their food is just reheated frozen patties and mediocre buns. But who said that's a bad thing? Their persian food isn't bad, and they definitely are one of the best restaurants on Euclid.

I'm not really sure what they serve is from Niman Ranch. The burgers definitely aren't - I totally have the same frozen patties at the house I live in, and those things are cheap franken meat. Maybe the all-beef bacon?

Overall, not a bad place. Greasy, cheap, and fast.

The best dish at this restaurant is not on the menu!
Get the bongo salad with chicken on top, it's very healthy, very low carb and tastes amazing! Most of the employees know me and know my invented dish, but just explain you want the grilled chicken on top and they'll know what you mean.

Mmmmm.... Mushroom Burger. The way those mushrooms just kiss that swiss cheese, while the cheese simultaneously embraces the warm bun, which envelops the meat. It's a complete orgy in the mouth. Save your money and don't buy the fries or drink. JUST GET THE BURGER.

I'm not sure what all the hype is about. So what if they serve breakfast items in addition to burgers? This isn't McDonalds. The burgers aren't anything to celebrate about. I'd rather just eat elsewhere and go to In-n-Out on the weekends. The price is a bit high for the quality, but it was good to try.

I don't exactly have happy college memories. But I do of Bongo Burger. Persian Burger, I miss you so. No matter where I go, the memory of a cheap yet immensely satisfying meal and that strange white sauce that goes awesome with fries will stay with me.

To the people who always get a turkey sandwich here: You are not asking for the optimum taste of the place, so don't complain about the food. 

Get persian sandwich in pita bread: It is ground lamb slices grilled and seasoned perfectly! Mixed with tomato slices, lettuce and the hummus sauce.

Get eggplant plate: Deep fried soft eggplant slices topped with a diced tomato/pepper sauce and melted cheese. I think melted cheese part is to look appealing for the american customers with traditional taste, I would put a yogurt sauce with a hint of garlic on it (like tatziki).

Get all american buger: Best burger around campus! Delicious juicy beef patty topped with fresh stuff.

For lunch on the north side of the campus, it is either Nefeli's (mousakka) or Bongo burger (with one of the above)...Great food for good prices.

My standby North Campus lunch place for when I am really effing hungry.  Their Persian Burger (lamb) must weigh at least a pound, and paired with fries always leaves me in an afternoon food coma.  

Burgers are pretty average fast food, fries are a little below average.  They do squeeze fresh OJ and carrot juice, which makes for a much healthier (and more expensive) combo than a soda.  The black bean garden burger is also an option for the heath conscious, and is just the right amount of spicy.  The middle eastern fare is decent too, but not as authentic or as tasty as the Hummingbird Cafe across the street.  

The lunch rush here is a pain in the ass - go after 1:30 if you can swing it.

I tried the salmon dish, which comes with green salad, a choice of tabouleh or fries, and fried (?) pita, at about $8. The salmon was a little dry and overcooked, but OK overall. If you added some seasoning I suppose it might taste better. The salad had some sort of mediterranean-tasting dressing on it and some tomato and other light vegetables. It left a weird texture in my mouth when eating it. The fries were the same as come with the burger combo: simple but decent. The pita was too dry and a little flavorless, but maybe I was supposed to eat it with the salad. Overall, a decent meal for the price, but lacking in taste; my rating remains the same. The salmon dish is a decent alternative to the burger/fries, though.

They basically take frozen patties, cook them on a grill and add some standard toppings with standard buns. Everything here is ok, it's not bad. The patties aren't super preserved like McDonalds but they aren't mouthwatering delicious like Barney's. 

For those Berkeley kids (especially you engineering majors who get stuck in Soda, Cory, and Etcheverry). This is the place to go when the good places in Asian Ghetto are closed, but you aren't desperate enough to want to go to La Burrita or TC Garden.

My favorite fast food burger in Berkeley, bar none.  Amanda's  comes close, but their portions aren't especially filling.  Bongo Burger's are.  If I'm jonesing for a burger, I go here first.

I'm pretty pedestrian when it comes to my tastes in hamburger--a straight-up patty with lettuce, tomato, onion, mustard, and ketchup sounds pretty spiffy to me.  So I haven't tried all of Bongo Burger's various permutations yet.  But their standards--hamburger, cheeseburger, turkey burger--are all excellent.  So are their fries, and for about $8-9, you can get a burger-fries-drink meal, which is a decent value given how big their burgers are.

I've lived in Berkeley for close to three years and have eaten here dozens of times.  Their food has yet to disappoint.  Ever.  They've got that consistency thing down solid.

I got the turkey burger, and it was not the best--it was just really obvious that it was a frozen patty! 

But my husband got the Persian burger, and it was amazing. Great flavor! I definitely ordered the wrong thing! Get the Persian burger!!!

Bongo burger is a restaurant that caters to those who want classic American hamburgers or falafel/vegetarian alternatives for the vegetarian types.

Their selection of hamburgers and french fries are nothing out of the ordinary, except they taste above average compared to other burger joints within a few miles. However, my choice for a meal was falafel, hummus, and a salad, which consisted of green lettuce, tomatoes, and other greens with light salad dressing, where the hummus wasn't memorable, then topped with dark falafel pieces with pita bread that seemed very average for a $7+ meal without a drink.

The cashier who took my money and gave me my change did not smile nor seem happy when I asked for a small cup of water. When I went to get my food up it being ready, I wanted some more tartar sauce, but they smugly told me only the large bottle of ranch dressing was available, which they reluctantly gave me a small dipping cup for the ranch dressing upon me asking for one.

Overall, I'd give this place 4 stars if it weren't for the service that I received. However, it is above 2 stars due to my friend loving their burgers, which is their signature product (not their vegetarian alternatives that I ordered). I won't be coming back anytime soon to this particular Bongo Burger, but I think overall this Berkeley chain serves the best overall hamburger in the area.

4stars for having the same meal every Tuesday and Thursday for a whole year and never being dissatisfied.

Turkey burger. Fries. Green Tea. Wait for next class and surf the internet. Win.

I've been here on the regular since I moved to Berkeley.  I decided on the Persian buger since I am persian and I thought this would only be appropriate.  I wasn't too stoked about it though even though people love it.  I went in on Election night when Barack Obama won and feeling particularly proud to be an American at that point in my life I ordered the All-American Burger, I fell in love and thought it was fate that I should fall upon this sandwhich on such a historic night.  I enjoyed the burger and many many since.

The burger is ok.  And so are the prices.  

So little can be said about this burger place.  I had forgotten about it until I saw it on Yelp.
