Northside's Bongo sucks. I mean, the food is still excellent, but the service isn't as friendly. Dude actually tried to charge me for a refill -- I know it's their policy, but I've never had that happen at the Southside one. It's too bad I'll probably endup going to this one a lot 'cause it's so close to all my classes. Whatev.

I can't get over how much I love their crappy fries. God. Also, get the mushroom burger.
decent burgers for a good price.  lots of other random mediterranean stuff on the menu.

Went into Bongo on a random weekday for dinner.  There were 2 people working (one as cashier, the other as a cook), they both looked so miserable! Either that, or they were giving me death stares. The atmosphere was dreary and a bit creepy :(

Almost $9 for a meal consisting of the mushroom burger, some fries, and a small drink.  The burger tasted similar to that at Burger King (flame broiled flavor).  I thought the whole meal to be a bit on the expensive side, considering the meal was a bit on the mediocre side.

My sister who tagged along, didn't order anything but waited while I ate my meal, became thirsty.  But she was afraid to ask for water, claiming the employees and their death stares terrified her.  

I would not come here again.  I left full but sad for some reason.

My favorite Saturday and Sunday morning stop in Berkeley. Hands down. especially after the gym. Their Persian stuff is fantastic. The Med. plate is delicious and the Persian burger is tasty (get them to put mushrooms on it or it's a little bland) 

But what brings me back time and time again? 

The Mushroom Burger. 

I NEVER order the mushroom burger....unless I'm at Bongo. 

Sometimes I order two. One is usually gone before I get back to my girlfriends place (since everyone knows a surefire way to frighten off a new beau is by downing two huge burgers during a commercial break).....[hmmm...I wonder if she reads my Yelp reviews?] 

Just don't forget some of that white better than mayo sauce on the counter. [insert obligatory "white sauce" + orgasmic joke here] 

Helpful Tip: Do NOT try to eat the mushroom burger or apply sauce in your car. Yes, yes. i KNOW you're hungry. But unless you have a Nissan Xtera or something with waterproof seats, you'll regret it.

To me, Bongo Burger is both good news and bad news:
-Bad news: I discovered Bongo Burger 3 months before graduating.
-Good news: I ate there no less than 17 times during my last 3 months of school (which, come to think of it, is really bad news for my health)

During those 3 happy months, I mainly ordered the mushroom burger, a side of fries, and coffee instead of a soft drink. The thing I really like about Bongo Burger is that their burgers are simple, but everything is done just right. The beef patty and mushrooms are freshly grilled, the lettuce is crisp and thinly sliced, and everything is neatly stacked into a giant burger.  

Thank you Bongo Burger for sustaining me through many late nights working on ME 107B. If I had discovered you earlier, I'm sure I would've done much better in school.
Great burgers, especially the mushroom burger.  The breakfast is terrible....."Hella-Sketch"

Their persian burger is a must try. Other than that, their regular hamburgers are just average.

The only thing is that the persian burger combo is 7 or 8 bucks. A tad expensive for a college student

There's good Middle Eastern food around campus (Sunrise, Hummingbird) but no good Middle Eastern meat - there's a huge market hole for a good and cheap kebab place. Bongo's Persian pita is a decent effort: the lamb is OK (Niman Ranch, though you wouldn't guess) but without that extra spit-roasted goodness I remember from innumerable kebab dives on Queen Street in Auckland.

Falafel has a nice crisp crust but is kind of tasteless. Apply their delicate thin tahini generously.

I never get the non-Persian burgers anymore. In that price range near campus, I prefer Smart Alec's.
Their Persian burger is a good quality burger on a long French roll.  Neat and good.  Skip the falafel.

Black bean burger is amazing. I love it. Price is decent for how large the burger is. I'm curious about their falafel and other vegetarian options. It's always been not busy when we've gone, which is a plus. I'm sure it will get busy once school starts in a week :(

Got the half-Persian burger ($3.95).
Great price for the size and the fact you're eating LAMB.

Flavorful meat, good French roll, typical lettuce and tomatoes but luckily not wilted, light smearing of mayo adds a little decadence, and some ketchup on the side adds some tang.

Good composition overall. Fast service. Good, spacious area.

(I think their fries are wavy fries, which I think is funny because it reminds me of middle school or something.)

Will have to return to try their other burgers, maybe a falafel, and maybe their black bean burger if it's housemade.

Ate here for the first time for lunch today, and decided to go for the Mushroom Burger Combo. The burger was pretty good. The way the swiss cheese and mushrooms tasted together made it a pleasant palate experience. I liked how the sesame seed bun was warm and crispy, unlike most buns I guess. The fries were above average, the way they are cut makes them super crispy.

Honestly, after I sat down at my table while waiting for my food to be ready, I realized I should have went for the Persian Burger. I didn't see it initially because I was feeling a burger and only looked at the items they had under the burger heading. The Persian Burger was listed under Sandwiches. But damn, I definitely want to come back here to try that lamb sandwich creation they have. People here on Yelp think it's pretty good...

The burgers are great and the price is right but try the persian burger or the hummus combo plate instead--both are surprisingly excellent! Staff is also helpful and nice though sometimes it seems there is a small language barrier or communication problem since sometimes they speak quietly or mumble.
Good food. Nasty people. I'll stick with the Bongo on Northside.

First time I had a burger in Berkeley was right here: the mushroom burger. I'm not one to buy a gourmet burger that often ie Barney's even if it is delicious so when I can get an equally delicious burger at a cheaper price I take it! Try the mushroom burger you can't go wrong. Their fries are super yummy too!

Came here again for dinner. Instead of getting the burgers, I decided to try their Hummus Combo, which is consisted of falafels, hummus, and salad. Personally, I thought the portions were kind of small, considering that if you were to pay the same amount, or even less, you would be getting a huge burger. However, surprising, after I finished my dish, I actually felt pretty good. 

I have to say, their mediteranean food is legit. Not as good as Sunrise Deli's med food, but the hummus is pretty good. 

My friend got the Mushroom Burger and it was delicious. Definitely beats La Burrita and La Vals across the street if you want something good/tasty and slightly on the healthier side.
This is the only place I know of where I can get a tasty turkey burger to go, with decent fries.

In the Bongo, the patties come bigger than the bread that holds them.  Mid-chow-down your bottom bun has gone missing and your desperately gripping the rest of your patty by a sliver of your top bun.  This all makes for good lunch time entertainment and foolishness, while you begin to analyze and improvise on how to finish your burger while still looking cute for the geeky B-boys.  

Some days are Bongo days, when the need for a fat, juicy, turkey burger with lettuce bits swimming in ketchup and mustard takes over your mind late-morning.  A deal that leaves my stomach packed for hours at $4.94 (sans fries and soda).  Even though the crinkle fries are bomb, I resist to save my figure and instead plot to steal a few from my friends who order them.  

3 stars... well, because its Bongo Burger, not Barney's.   You'll only catch me here at lunch out of necessity not amor.

tastes are great , prices are moderate. I love taboleh salad and their frys.

If you have no experience with their food, I recommend you to have shish kebob sandwich, you will love it. 

The decoration needs to be remodeled.
Imagine my delight when I found out there was a second Bongo Burger close to the CS department!  Shorter walk for a Persian Burger...need I say more?

Middle Eastern tho? Really? haha.

Anyway.. this place is good. The combos are a bit pricey for lunch, but I guess it's not that bad for what you get since the servings are big. The fries are the best!!!! Mmmmmm

Tip:
Call order in ahead of time. It can be packed out the door during lunch rush!
It's a decent burger at a good price. There's basically no reason I'll ever need to go to a fast food chain again (which is nice, because Berkeley doesn't really have any).

I am very patriotic when it comes to food. I ordered the cheeseburger. The meat was very good, and they got it right when I asked for no mayo (many places take this to mean EXTRA GROSS GOOP). I liked the crinkle fries--haven't had those in a while. My only suggestion is to cut down on the bun size--it was far too fat and large. Though I guess I should take a long look in the mirror....

Anyway, ladies, this place was crawling with male specimens of the young and impressionable variety. Come, take advantage.

Mushroom Burger at 8AM? Yes I did. 

The burgers are pretty darn big but I feel like it's mostly bun. Delicious, but it gets unexpectedly pricey especially when you add fries and a drink to your burger.

conversation at work today...

me: what do you want for lunch?

stephan g: hmmm...well, i had a bongo burger on friday, pizza on saturday, and a burrito on sunday.

me: guess its a burger then, huh?

stephan g: yup, guess so.

bongo has great fries, decent burgers, and alternative mediterranean options for those people who don't want a burger...whoever that might be.

Bongo Burger is a top-notch fast food joint; high quality food, fast service and above average prices.
I have tried the Mushroom Burger, Cheese Burger and Persian Burger. The meat is always well-cooked, the cheese is a perfectly melted and the burger bun is toasted to complement the juiciness of the meat and the absorb the combination of sauces (ketchup, mayo and mustard)
The crinkle cut fries are under-seasoned but nothing a sprinkle of salt and dip of ketchup won't fix :)
The hummus is pretty average however, the serving is small compared to what other places offer.
The carrot juice is wonderful; fresh and cold. It is the perfect way to make myself feel healthy after the carb-a-licious meal that I consume!

Overall rating - - 3/5

I only get the turkey burger here, along with either french fries or onion rings, depending on whether I'm taking the food to go (onion rings hold up much better than do the fries). I love those three things at Bongo.

I give it five stars not because it's the best thing I've ever eaten but because I think it succeeds at what it sets out to do. Plus, I love that they have a (always chilled) squeeze bottle of ranch for you to serve yourself. Bad for you, but good for them!

Lunch can be crazy there, but dinner is practically dead most nights.

How good is it?
Let's just say, when it came to choosing schools....The Persian Burger was a deal breaker.
Enter this place, and it's easy to get confused. The semi-atypical mix of burgers and persian food may confuse some, but fear not. I will show you the delicious, meaty, light.

Order the persian burger. Order some french fries. If you like it order a doogh. The persian burger is a lamb sandwich/burger composition that never ceases to please. The french fries are cooked in very fresh oil and the ranch is delicious as well.

As far as the rest of the menu, i've only sampled a bit. But that is not even important. Order the persian burger and you will understand my enthusiasm.

This place is nothing much inside but, it fills a need or a memory....I don't know...but when I eat a turkey burger it releases my "happy" endorphins and "don't bother me" I'm in my own burger heaven. 
Maybe because it's grilled and that shredded lettuce? Or maybe because it's big and saucer flat kind of like old style burgers when I used to eat beef, back in the day....who knows....who cares really. All I know is I drive my sister crazy, who lives on the corner when I come visit...."Bongo Burger...Bongo Burger"...My mantra.....She finally breaks, even though she's probably eaten there already that week....and let's me have my juvenile moment of demanding and gives in..... Because she knows how much I love my Bongo Burgers! Oh and a few fries please too.

Serious burgers for the yuppie crowed. 

The portions are huge, and let me tell you--the onion rings are nothing short of a revelation: not too oily, very crispy and with parmesan cheese sprinkled lightly on top.

I would give five stars, but somehow my tummy would get overwhelmed every time I ate here, so I could only eat like one onion ring (so hard to eat just one!) and like half my burger. My eyes were always bigger than my stomach at Bongo.

Overall this restaurant is pretty good for burgers and fries.  The meat is flavorful and juicy and they have some interesting things on the menu, such as hummus and falafel plates, dolmas, persian burger, etc.   

However, you MUST order the mushroom and cheese sandwich - not the mushroom burger, mind you.  Yes, its veggie, and it's great.  The mushrooms taste delectable and there is this creamy-ish sauce that, along with the cheese, melts in your mouth.  I've also had the mushroom burger, which is also good, but I actually prefer it without the meat.  Either one is a great option for any of you mushie lovers out there.... Goes great with a side of fries!

YUM! Lovee them! The burger is so delicious (mushroom burger) and the prices are really affordable for college students. Definitely go with the old school favorites - can't say I haven't thought about trying some of the other items on the menu!

Er - How can I not have reviewed this? It's a lifeline to those nerdy science postdocs and grad students in the EECS department. Go for the standard, cheese, or mushroom burgers (though I hear the falafels are great too). Nice and juicy, and very fatty, of course. Do they only use organic meats? I can't remember.

The combo is probably not a good option - just stick with the burgers and avoid the fries/ soft drinks, which only save you about 20-50 cents and merely shorten your life span by years.

Thanks to Yelp I've discovered the Persian burger, and in turn discovered that Bongo Burger is a decent place after all. It's a long Niman Ranch (yay) lamb patty in a French roll with standard burger fixings, which sounds odd and simply must be tried to be appreciated. The meat is seasoned well and the bread makes for a delicious sandwich-- coupled with fries (don't bother) and a drink it makes for a big lunch.

The black bean burger is good, too, and the falafel is only so-so; fortunately I'll be spared these decisions in the future. Also, sadly, no refills, and sometimes-slow service is a mixed blessing: yes, it's made to order, but it's only a burger.

One of the experiences that ties all EECS students is having eaten at Bongo Burger (the other is TC Garden-bleh!)  So why here? I had noooo idea!  That's exactly why I took the effort to come here myself and be a part of this recent EECS trend.

I had ordered the mushroom burger (~$6).  It was #1 on the menu and usually #1 items are the best.  The burger is a good size to satisfy anyone's appetite for a quick lunch sitting.  Beef patty and sauteed mushrooms were tender and moist.  It wasn't spectacular, but nevertheless still a good burger.  If you frequent Euclid restaurants for lunch, it's worth putting this store into your rotation.

My friends recommend trying the Persian Burger and falafel; I'm no longer in Cal so I can't try it myself, but I'm just throwing it out there for those who are interested.

Oh yea, teehee! friendly reminder to my fellow EECS comrades: Bongo Burger is not a place for a romantic date!

I have been to Bongo Burger about 1 million times since starting grad school at Cal. It actually was the first place I ate at when I moved to Cal. I unpacked my boxes, strolled the area, and decided a burger would be delicious. How little I knew how many times I would be a customer.

Bongo Burger provides a good quality burger for a slightly above average price. The burger is delicious. I get the standard beef burger, but occasionally spring for the bacon cheeseburger. The beef is Niman Ranch and very juicy. A few times I have had it come back a little overcooked, but it usually is spot-on. The bun is crispy on the outside (warmed on the side grill). The fries need a little something...they are crinkle-cut, but lack enough salt in my opinion. Thankfully, ample salt packets are available.

The service is pretty good unless you go at the lunch rush. There isn't much room for standing there while waiting for a togo order. They people are really nice (and even have memorized my order!), but they do occasionally forget to give me my drink because of the crazy rush.

They take Discover! Woo hoo! Just don't ask if they take Discover, because even though there are stickers on the door, some of the cashiers don't think they do.

Overall, a good burger place. Standard burger combo runs $7.50, which is a lot, but pretty standard for Northside. Peppermint Grill is much cheaper, but also much crappier, and Vinnie's has a cheeseburger combo for a few cents less, but it's a toss-up between the two styles. All in all, if you're looking for an escape from endless ethnic food on Northside, come down to Bongo Burger!

I've eaten at all three Bongo Burgers near campus, frequenting the Euclid Ave one the most (since it's near the EECS and CS buildings, which I spent a lot of college days at). The mushroom burger and Persian burger are worth mentioning, but the turkey burger was a bit too salty on one occasion. The joint seems to have trouble having consistent taste and quality in their foods, such as the fries. I've had good ones and not-so-great ones where they were a bit limpy. In almost all occasions though, they were pretty bland.

The service is perhaps this joint's weakest point. The lady behind the counter never smiled, and in fact gave a bit of a cold stare when I or my friends asked for an extra tiny cup of ketchup or even more napkins. Other employees were better, but if the clerk behind the cash register doesn't put up a good face, it tends to lower my opinion about the place in general.

Another weak point is the pricing. Each burger could set you back at least six or seven dollars, which could be staggering compared to more conventional burger joints. Sure, the burgers here may be different and fresh, but inconsistency between visits makes me hesitant to justify the price.

Admittedly, the only non-burger dish I had was a salad entree (can't remember what it's called), and never had the falafel. The salad, by the way, was disappointing.

So if you really want to try an exotic burger, Bongo Burger would be your best bet, but try the other two joints, not the one at Euclid. My experience at Southside and downtown has been better.

I've gone to this Bongo burger occasionally these past 3 years. In general their food is OK. The main issues being an overtoasted bun and bland, dry meats. The only thing they get right are their french fries which are always cooked perfectly crisp

BUT, today at about 12:30pm I witnessed something and I will never be returning here again. I saw the cook indecisively place a slab of raw hamburger meat on the cutting board for a second. By the time he was ready to throw it on the grill it had created a puddle of raw meat juices. 10 seconds later, the guy who puts the sandwiches together placed two buns and a pita in the puddle unknowingly. He proceeded to serve these contaminated items to their unsuspecting costumers. I really think I should have said something, someone could get extremely ill.

So, proceed at your own risk.

When we were planning our wedding, we had to decide on a red wine.  We drank a bottle a night for weeks on end.  We discovered during that period the beauty and complexity of the Bongo Persian Burger.  As some reviewers note below, it's absolutely delicious.  A lamb patty on a french roll.  What could be better.  We ask for it with feta cheese too!  And it's absolutely out of this world- and it goes even better with a glass of red wine!!!

I took away one star because the one time we ate the burger there, we asked them to cut it in half for us and they charged us an extra $1.00.  HELLO?!  What is that about?!!!  To the owner's dismay, the next time I was there I just asked for a plastic knife and cut it in half myself (in front of her - yeah, I'm a brat like that).

P.P.S.  Hummus plate is alright.  Not terrible, but definitely not the best I've had!
Burgers are average and fries are okay. The lines are justifiable considering every other place on Euclid is packed like Bay Bridge toll plaza at 8AM...

I had gone to Bongo Burger once before a couple years ago and didn't remember it being that memorable, so I went in today with low expectations. However, I was pleasantly surprised as it actually turned out to be pretty good.

What I ordered:
- Mushroom and Cheese Sandwich ($3.95): sauteed mushrooms, cheese, lettuce, caramelized onions, tomatoes, and mayo

Although it's technically called a sandwich, it actually is a burger since it comes on a seeded, toasty bun which had a nice crunch to it. The mushrooms were plentiful and tasty, but they were a tiny bit salty. I really enjoyed the caramelized onions which added to the flavor, but they resulted in a very drippy burger eating experience. I think it was the onions at least. Good thing I was eating over the outer wrapper paper of my burger or else I would have had a pool of liquid on the table! Also, there was a little too much mayo for my liking, but the burger was still decently good. I wouldn't mind coming back here for the convenience, but I probably wouldn't crave it either. It is really cheap for a filling meal though!

There are definitely better burger places in Berkeley, but this one is probably one of the closer, more convenient locations near campus.

I used to eat here quite often during my days at Berkeley. So basically I would usually get a mushroom burger, fries, and soda.. The burger is pretty good, not too greasy, just the right size, and the other ingredients are fresh.. Fries are also pretty good but you can tell they come from the freezer.  

Then one day I decided to be adventurous (doesn't happen often when it comes to food) and ordered the Persian (lamb) plate.. Comes with some pieces of marinated/spiced ground lamb, side salad, and tabouleh salad. (You can also get fries instead)  From then on that was the only thing I ordered.  It's somewhat strange because I don't generally like lamb, it has a weird after taste to me, but when grounded up and served with spices it tastes pretty good.  The tabouleh salad especially is very fresh and tasty and this plate is much much healthier than the burger meal.  It also costs a little more but just think of it as insurance against a future heart attack.

It probably comes as no surprise that Berkeley's home-grown version of the short-order burger joint is a bit unconventionally spiced with a mediterranean pizzazz.  They have beef burgers, wrap sandwiches, falafel, middle eastern plates and even serve a cheap and good basic breakfast, but the real house specialty is the Persian Burger, which consists of a patty of charbroiled ground lamb, delicately spiced and served on a grilled soft roll with onions, lettuce and yogurt sauce.  Really unique and quite tasty, this is a great place for a cheap, quick slightly different lunch in Berkeley.

While I tend to like restaurants with large open windows such as the ones at their locations around the city and campus, there is something alluring about this one. It's narrow and somewhat hidden. The burgers are just the same and good. I like beef burgers usually, but their turkey burger has me convinced. The Middle Eastern food still somewhat lacking and I don't suggest the falafels.

If you would like a burger and you are on the North Side of campus - this is the place to go.  The food is nothing special.  Main draw, the abnormal ratio of men to women.   After spending all day in the School of Social Welfare, it is quite refreshing :)

Food: 
-Turkey Burger: SOO BIG! The bun was SOOO GOOD! it was all warm and perfectly toasted; crunchy exterior and a chewy center! YUMMY! Tasted like a baguette but it wasn't...you've just got to try it. The turkey patty was literally larger than life! But it was delicious! The burger came with lettuce, tomatoes, and some mayo spread (I think it was mayo anyway). 

Service: 
-None, you just order at the front, but the lady at the front was super nice!

Ambiance: 
-Just a chill burger joint close to campus. Nothing special. A good place to come for a quick chow down!

Price: 
The burger came out to be around $5. It was well worth it! I can't wait to go back and try the other things on the menu!

Back when I was a student, I had a few favorite places to get some food in my stomach between classes, and Bongo Burgers was one.  I think I only ever ordered one thing-- the Shish Kabob Burger with fries and a coke.  I probably ate that several times a week.

And we had such a love/hate relationship.

The fries were OK.  The coke is... coke.  The burger though-- oh, that meat was so damned good.  I think they sprinkled crack on it.  But the god damned bun... those things weren't buns.  They were mini loafs of bread scientifically engineered and baked to rip the roof of your mouth to shreds.  That delicate balance of pleasure and pain made for quite the culinary adventure.

I have certain predilections that I blame on that sandwich.

I only hope that the students of today can share in that one-of-a-kind experience.

Bongo burger is one of those restaurants that you're ashamed to admit you like. The burgers and fries really aren't that memorable, the service is perpetually nasty and unhappy, and the sodas are very overpriced. The burgers are overpriced for what you get, the fries are that weird crinkle cut frozen store kind, the burger is extremely thin/dry and any moisture comes from the condiments (although the flavor is good, they're a great size and the bun has a just right crunch). So why eat here, like I just did, when one is sober and there are other things open.

Because sometimes you just need a damn bacon cheeseburger. Sometimes you miss your lunch break and have a shitty day. Sometimes you have your work raped with red pen, have an entire room of moving boxes to unpack AND need to fix the red pen raped work before 9:30 tomorrow morning.

In short, sometimes you need a bacon cheeseburger, with fries, and a diet coke that's been watered down with bourbon...

Service was ubber sweet.  Checking whether i want their free tea and how spicy I wanted my food, but the lamb tikka masala was tasty, but the meat was tough as could be.  I was giving my jaw a work out.  The garlic naan was more on the too buttery side, but it was okay.  Probably the Lamb won't be my go to next time, if I gave them a shot.

Quite cheap for indian food for around campus.  Serving size was quite big as rice is included with most orders.  I had the a chicken and potato dish and it pretty good as the chicken was pretty tender and spicy.  This is definitely a place to go if you want to clear up your sinuses.
Nice to have an Indian meal option at this new  UC area food court. Generous portions spiced to order, free chai, decent service and very nice counter staff.
The veggie samosa and lamb vindaloo were a party in my mouth. Service was fast and friendly, and there was free tea, which was lovely. An altogether enjoyable experience.

Taste: 3
Value: 5
Service: 4

I come here pretty often, and they have okay sandwiches. For only $6.25 for a sandwich and two side salads, it's pretty cheap. Usually get the turkey avocado or the Bear sandwich on sourdough or dutch crunch. Last time, I asked for easy on the mustard, which they screwed up, so I wasn't too happy about that.

Having eaten at most of the other places on Euclid, this was an intriguing place to try out for lunch, although never hearing about this place before was a bad sign. Sometimes it's better to not let your curiosity get the better of you.

The location is small, there only being a counter over which you order and get your food. There's no seating, meaning you have to find your own place to eat your food.

For lunch, I went with the sandwich/salad combo, which comes in at $5.25 (tax included) for regular sandwiches and $6.25 (?) for deluxe sandwiches, which I would guess are the same size but have better ingredients. I ordered the roast beef sandwich and got a pasta salad with small, curled pasta and some kind of vegetable salad (no lettuce).

The sandwiches seem to be the same thing with different choices of meat. There's a decent selection of bread; I went with wheat, which was soft but also seemed processed  and not 100% wheat. It comes with a tomato, some dressing, and bean sprouts, I think. A light, if unspectacular, sandwich.

The salads were disappointing. The flavoring (vinegar-based?) was too strong on both them, and the ingredients of the vegetable salad, which included bell peppers, celery, and broccoli, didn't coalesce. The fruit salad might have been a better choice.

Service was fast and nice; there was a lady handling the register and the salads, and a man making the sandwiches.

If you go with just the sandwich, you might be moderately satisfied with the quality, but I would be wary of the salads.
That weird owner isn't there. The food is not even made here, and the guy behind the counter doesn't speak English.
This is my favorite place on the North side of campus. The sandwiches are delicious, but my favorites are the chicken and kefta wraps. Fresh ingredients, made-to-order, and extremely tasty.

Pretty similar to the normal hummingbird cafe, but more focused on sandwiches and quick lunches. Good selection of chips and drinks.

I kind of prefer the other location (a whole 20 feet / 5 storefronts away). I've always liked hummingbird for their smoothies more than their food, so the old location is still superior.

Nice to see another food place opening up - food on Euclid is generally so mediocre that any new competition couldn't hurt.
This is my favorite place at North Gate.  Everything is fresh and I always feel so welcomed when I come in.

I've eaten here once and the sandwiches here are OK but there is only one person staffing the place and he has to go between making the sandwich and handling money, with no gloves and no hand washing.  Paper money carries myriad bacteria and viruses!  That's just gross, and probably a health code violation.  The guy running this place should provide gloves so that his staff can prepare food safely.

Good to-go Gyro .

Came for really early fast lunch, owner seemed upset with the workers that they opened before 11am. They took a while to make my lamb and beef gyro, but they probably were still busy setting up. Keep in mind their is no place to sit and unfortunately it is cash only. Not the best gyro I've had, but it was fresh, comes with pickles, and not terrible value for ~$7.

I've been going to the Hummingbird Cafe (the other one) for almost 10 years and you can read my review of the original cafe elsewhere.  BUT today I was in a bit of a hurry and I thought I would try the "express."  Sadly it was not good, nor was it by any means "express."  There was only one, high-maintenance type, woman (not that "A" has anything to do with "B") ahead of me who wanted a "crab salad sandwich."  Now, that seems a little unusual, but in her defense it IS on the menu.  The person working behind the counter I honestly think did not know the word "crab" and so kept trying to make a "club" sandwich, which isn't what she wanted and only served to further irritate her.  She finally settled on tuna after an extended negotiation.

Now it's my turn.  Trying to learn from others' mistakes, I resolved that I was going to follow the KISS principle (keep it simple, stupid, you're in a hurry) and decided to order a simple ham and swiss on rye.  There was an indication on the board that cheese is available (although given the experience of the woman before me, I was not longer sure) but there was no cheese in sight.  So before I ordered something that didn't exist, repeating the experience of the person before me, I asked the simple question "do you have Swiss cheese?"  Honestly, the guy didn't understand "Swiss cheese", so I repeated my question more slowly--we weren't getting anywhere.  So then I thought--"just order, this isn't helping" so I ordered a ham and swiss on rye with everything (I thought trying to discern among toppings was going to be a disaster if we were stuck on the word "cheese".)  THEN, the guy didn't understand "ryebread"--which was apparent given his other difficulties, so I asked him what kind of bread they had--which was not on the menu board.  All he could really do was point to the plastic bags that contained the bread but he couldn't list the types. Then the piddly bit of meat he put on the sandwich had to be carefully weighed out, blah, blah, blah.  I finally got the sandwich and left.  This is "express"?

The sandwich sucked.

I'm sorry but the guy behind the counter has to go.

Ahhhhh, the newly reinvented Hummingbird Express.  Meat slowly roasting on a spit right in the front window is genius marketing...it, along with the flyer I received on campus, got me in there.  

Went in for a late lunch.  Not crowded, but it's so tiny that even with one other person inside I felt cramped.  The three guys working there were really friendly and enthusiastic, hollering at each other in what I guessed was their native tongue, I love to see that.  The menu has quite a few types of kabobs and freshly made spreads/salads plus some meat pies and desserts.  I ordered the lamb burrito hoping to get some meat off of the spit, instead they took it from a side container and threw it on a grill with oil.  I say burrito because it was wrapped in a tortilla as opposed to lavash bread or a pita, but I gotta say that I preferred the taste and texture of the tortilla over lavash or pita which tend to be dry. 

The wrap itself was fairly tasty but a bit greasy, likely due to the double cooking process. It had some mixed greens, cukes and tomato all dressed in a vinaigrette with some yogurt sauce, grilled onions and meat.  This thing was packed with flavor.   The $10 price, with a drink, puts it at the high end of the price spectrum for a quick lunch.

One small table outside crammed next to Nefelis tables so plan on taking out. I think a name change is needed to better reflect the new menu...but 4 stars to hummingbird express for filling the middle eastern void on Northside.

One guy offered some free dessert, I'm not a huge sweets so I passed but it was a nice gesture.  

Cash Only.

Terrible. Only takes cash. Soggy (crappy) wheat bread. Tuna "melt" has no cheese. Revolting amounts of mayo and mustard. Poorly configured sandwich.

Go elsewhere.

It seems like the draw here is the combo meal, which is a sandwich with two salads of your choice for about $5.  It's almost not worth it though because I've tried four of the salads so far and haven't enjoyed any of them.  The potato salad, for instance, is very heavily flavored by relish.  The sandwiches are okay, though, and it's convenient if you're in the area and aren't particular.

I went here today thinking it was the Hummingbird Cafe(wanted to go there because of its good Yelp ratings)...don't get confused, you'll see the Hummingbird Express first, keep going up the street and you'll reach the Hummingbird Cafe. 
Anyway, as far as the food goes I was not impressed. I ordered a vegetarian sandwich called "Fufu Vegetarian," and it was surprisingly...not that good. I didn't even think a vegetarian sandwich with sprouts, some avocado, lettuce, tomatoes, and cucumbers could be messed up. If you're looking for such a sandwich, subway is a much better (and cheaper) place to go. I would have given this place one star, but the owner was very nice and I don't know how good their non vegetarian dishes are...maybe vegetarian dishes aren't their speciality?

I'm writing this review just as I finished a $3.75 regular turkey sandwich from hummingbird express. It was delicious. I really don't understand why other people dislike it so much or not like it at all. I really would rather go here for lunch (for a sandwich) than go to Stuffed Inn and wait 30 minutes for a sandwich that's about $5.00 and not at all better. The "special" sandwiches at Hummingbird are about $4.25 which probably include like avocado and more meats and stuff like that.. which is totally good if you're super hungry, and still, cheaper than Stuffed Inn. Oh, you can also get 2 salads at $1 more if you get the "special" sandwiches. So you get like 1.5 meals (sandwich and a little bit of salad, save the rest of the salads for later..) for the price of about $5.50? I might be a little off.. but probably only so by a quarter or two. So cheap! 

Maybe I prefer these sandwiches because I like that vinegar-y taste... what is that taste... bitter? It's not bitter but the mustard definitely tastes a little different but for me, on the good side. I'm pretty sure their salads are like that too... I don't know but I love vinegar and I love the sandwiches here. They taste fresh and clean... do you know what I mean? It doesn't taste at all soggy or messy but crisp... The sourdough bread is really thick and chewy too. There are plenty of different kinds of salad--including a fruit one, a mayonnaise based salad, and like 3 other kinds. 

I was actually a little hesitant to try it first as well because it just doesn't look that big, they only take cash, and I didn't see anyone there. Now, I don't mind the size (I can eat at my desk), I save my cash to eat here, and I'm glad I don't have to wait in a super long line (seriously though, in and out in less than 5 minutes)!!!!

I'm not sure why this place is rated so low. Granted, I've only been here once...I didn't see anything I wanted on the menu, so I asked for a bagel with hummus, so they did it, and added tomatoes, cukes and sprouts for free. The coffee I got was from a warming pot, but it was fine. The people were both really nice, too. It's a tiny hole in the wall, but I'd totally come back.

I go here for lunch and always get the green beans and curry tofu or chicken. At $5.75 for rice and two sides, it will turn out to be enough food for two meals. 

Make sure you try the Vietnamese coffee! Half of the cup is filled with sweetened condensed milk and it will give you the jitters for the rest of the day but SOOO WORTH IT!

Downside: cash only.
Upside: great patio seating, good selection of beer.

Nice place to have a quick lunch. Like their outdoor seating. Very clean, friendly place. I thought it was a upscale french restaurant from outside. Food are OK, not excellent, but I will definitely visit again when I need a quick cheap bit around campus.

Cafeteria style Vietnamese food at a great price ($5.50 for a 3-item plate w/ rice) that tastes really good.  Lots of solid choices with beef, poultry, and veg dishes.  Only complaint was the food wasn't warm enough coming out of the steam table.  The place can get crowded so be ready to get your food to go and find a good spot outside.

Good lunch joint. Really liked the garlic eggplants (but I almost always like eggplants!), while the ginger chicken and the curry where just OK. The combination plate is a pretty good deal and the food from the buffet seem to be pretty freshly cooked (at least during rush hour).

The ambiance is very college-cafeteria like, but I guess it is to expect so close to campus..... also the lady at the counter had problems with the cashier and could not provide me with a receipt, which I kind of needed for reimbursement, I guess I could have insisted, but I just decided my time was not worth the price of the lunch.....

A pretty good buffet, but always a buffet.....
Ani! You totally brought me back. The deal of the century. Pretty, laid back, tasty eats. LOTS-O-FOOD. Oh Berk how I love thee!

I can only rate the sandwiches bc that's what I get - every time!! I do think their other food looks pretty good... but once you go banh mi you never go back.

Love the sandwiches, no other vietnamese banh mi sandwich compares. 

One downfall is I ordered tofu, and they served me chicken, and I took a bite or two, brought it back, and the "fixed" it by sending me the same sandwich (with my bites missing) but they pulled out the chicken and added tofu. Not cool by my vegetarian rulebook.

Other downfall is it's cash only and weekday only. Hello what about the alums who work M-F outside of the area, but want to visit Berkeley and get their favorite sandwich on a wknd???

This is the first place that I had Banh-Mi! While I've eaten Vietnamese food before, I still had yet to try Banh-Mi. After bumping into a friend and deciding on having some, we walked on over to Le Petit Cheval. It was around 5pm, and as we looked through the menu, we were told that they had run out of bread! (womp womp.) Since my friend and I were set on having Banh-Mi, we decided to come back another time.

On our return, we (with a few more friends in tow) came during the lunch rush. The set-up of the whole restaurant is a little confusing for a newcomer such as myself, especially during the rush. I believe there are two lines/cashiers... one for the lunch buffet, and another for those ordering from the menu. My friends an I stood around for 2 minutes or so, confused and unsure of what to do. But we eventually figured it out, and went to the line for menu items. the wait in line was about 5 or so minutes, and my exchange with the staff was pleasant, despite the lunch rush.

We waited under 10 minutes for our sandwiches, and as we waited, we sat on these nifty chairs by the cashier. We were soon on our way out with our banh mi in hand.

And for those of you who have had banh mi, you can attest to this: banh mi is amazing! This was my first time having it, and I've only been to one other place to have banh mi, so I definitely not a banh mi connoisseur by any means.

Regardless, I was really happy with my purchase! It was the perfect size for lunch, and left me feeling satisfied, but not pukey (which is always bad news.)

I've been back on several occasions, and have been met with the same satisfaction. I haven't tried the buffet, and I always take my food to-go, but by looking at the atmosphere and judging from my experience with the staff, I'm sure it will be an enjoyable experience.

So if you're around the UC Berkeley campus, and are aching for some vietnamese food at lunch time, head over here! It's delicious.
Close to campus & cheap. Lots of seating. Great place for a meal if you are strapped for time.

Cafeteria-style Vietnamese deliciousness. Good amount of vegetarian options, that are all usually the same: Eggplant Tofu, Green beans, some vegetable/noodle dish; something will be spicy, and something will be coconutty. You pay six or seven bucks, and get to choose 3 items plus rice. The food is surprisingly good for what you'd think! Although, it is never quite hot enough... hm! But the price (cheap cheap cheap) makes up for it.

The guy ladling out your choices will most likely be cranky, but that's just his way. Don't mind him. ;)

What else? Fountain drinks, trays, pay in cash at the end. The best part about it all (for us, anyway) is that you can sit "outside" on the patio, which has an open ceiling and sometimes little birds will fly through... Combined with all the plants and the burbling fountain, it is just the place to recharge after a long day of walking around Berkeley and campus. We try and hit this place up every time we're in town. 

Give it a whirl! It is no-stress, cheap, tasty, and atmospheric. Sit and chomp and watch the students mosey down Bowditch, and be glad you are not them.

Okay, it's cheap, but it's been seven hours since I ate lunch and I still am rolling around with a terrible stomach ache. The food does *not* taste good; the chemical, artificial stuff is highly noticeable. I didn't even eat most of it and I still got sick. Don't eat here. Lunch for $6.75 isn't worth losing a day to food poisoning.

Nice place to eat lunch. I also like their location (right across campus)... found it a very convenient meet up spot to grab lunch/dinner and then head back to campus in time for class! 

I had their clay pot, which IMO was a bit pricey for their portion size, but it was still really good (& hot!). Another day I had their Bird's Nest and found it a bit difficult to eat because I didn't know how to eat it without having my noodles flying a couple inches from my plate, but it was pretty good nevertheless. Also had a fried rice dish that wasn't too bad. 

I'd give it a 3.5 instead of a 3. 

Downside: It's closed on weekends! :T

I tried the lunch buffet today, and usually I hate buffets. But it was very good, and so much variety! This is no panda express, everything looked fresh and unlike panda express, was not dripping in sauce or grease. I especially enjoyed the tofu in coconut milk. The value can't be beat, 5.50 for three items plus rice? Beats Asian Ghetto any day.  They also have free wifi.

This place is so delic and they are consistent across all of their locations! Great for vegetarians, and, they have a full bar!! Only down fall is that it can be pretty loud cause they are always so busy but you can't beat the food, you won't be disappointed!

Wow, is this place really supposed to be Vietnamese?  I went there for a quick lunch and I'm pretty sure half the items were bad Americanized Chinese.  I had the beef noodle soup, and I can say with confidence that it was the worst beef noodle soup I've ever had.  The beef was dry and completely lacking in flavor and there was no variation in the cut.  At least this place is pretty cheap and quick.
So yummy!  Great value to boot! I love the beef watercress salad and can't go wrong with the Pho!

Pros:
VERY good food and for a pretty good price. I think I've tried some claypot cooked mixed rice, green beans, cooked beef... and all of it was amazing!

* update* - lunch.. is AMAZING. GO.

Cons:
Maybe it's just when I've been there (twice), but, it's a pretty spacious place with NOT a lot of people - so, a bit quiet - so, i'm giving an awkward silence caution right here if you're bringing someone with you. 

The gentleman that does most of the waitressing (and is american/speaks english) is pretty cool - he'll give you some good advice on what to order!

I LOVE this place. Killer lemongrass chicken!  I always get the lunch special with lemongrass across the board (meaning all my sides are lemongrass)  I just wish they were open on weekends and between school breaks!  Unfortunately, they stick to the school schedule so us residents can only go when there are students everywhere.  

The place is clean and has a lovely outdoor area when the weather is nice.  Friendly service too!

LOVE THE PRICES!

I loved this place when I was an undergraduate and graduate student at Berkeley.

The lunch specials is a great deal, as you get carbs with 2 usually pretty well made dishes - at a pretty cheap price.  The chicken pho here is also great post-workout, as they give ample chicken breast, and a good helping of noodles.  (Of course, you are still missing fiber.)  Again, the pho is very reasonably priced.  

My favorite dishes here are their tomatoes with stuffed tofu, their lemongrass chicken, and chicken pho.  The beef pho is also good here, but you will not get nearly as much meat as with the chicken pho.

I woud have rated this restaurant two stars higher if it weren't for the service. I'll explain in more detail later. But first the food:

I had the beef broth with chicken pho, and it was pretty decent for the price. I left pretty full and I could have had leftovers if I hadn't decided to leave it there. It would probably fulfill a pho craving if you're itching for one. Definitely not the best pho I've had though, but its super nice since its close to campus.

In terms of the food getting to the table, it was pretty fast, but this is not surprising because 1) its a monday night, 2) soup is generally fast to prepare since they've already made the broth in advance. 

Now for the upsetting service aspect: 

I'm generally not that picky about waiters, and I usually feel bad about their tips if I or some friends don't leave at least 15% regardless of the fact that I'm a 'poor college student', but the server Bill is either an asshole for certain people (in another review someone said he was nice, and maybe that's the case) or was just having a cranky day, or has some hearing problem that makes certain sounds annoying, because his behavior was rude and interfering for a waiter. When I first got in, I accidentally put down my water glass a little too hard on the table and made a noise, and I awkwardly laughed because I was being clumsy. Then Bill brought the menus and made a snide comment to my friend who was with me stating that he should 'not be sitting with me.'  For the most part, this didn't bother me, but later when my friend was leaving and I was reminding my friend to put in the tip, and I jokingly told my friend, "I don't trust you,' the waiter Bill buts in rather angrily, "WE DON"T TRUST YOU! SEE, she forgot about that glass slam".
 I was a bit surprised about this comment, but this made leave 86 cents of tip(because I didn't want change back) for a 14.14$ meal because that was incredibly rude behavior for when I was actively trying to encourage my friend to leave a decent amount of tip. Maybe he was having a bad day, or maybe the thuds of glasses hitting the table upsets him greatly (which is an odd characteristic, he's a waiter: that should happen often), but its never justification for acting like an asshole.

i came here for a big group dinner.  there was plenty of room for our group of 30 people - which was pretty impressive.  i ordered the bird's nest with soft noodles - per a recommendation from someone.  when the food came out, there was a huge pile of noodles and veggies, meat, and shrimp on my plate.  huge portions!  however, the noodles were flavorless and dry.  i took the majority home in a takeout box, which i'm planning to eat for lunch tomorrow...but i am tempted to add some sauce and re-cook it...

This is definitely the place to go for lunch if you want good food with comfortable sit-down place without having to compete with all the undergrads on campus.

I've tried many different entrees and haven't found anything I don't like!  Two or three items on rice is served warm and there is no waiting time.  Anything on the menu takes about 5-10 minutes to arrive, which is considered very fast for a place packed with hungry people who don't have a whole lot of time to spend on a lunch break.  Anything vermicelli with grilled or marinated meat on skewers is very delicious!!!  Best vermicelli I've had so far.  

My friend and I went for a late late lunch (around 2:40 pm) one day, and we decided to share an entree, usually costing around $6.50,  for only $5 with 3x the usual portion.  We left with 2 boxed-full of leftovers.

Here are the breakdown of some pluses and minuses:
Seating:  Ample room.  Both indoors and outdoors with flatscreen tv.  You will never feel awkward eating alone at this restaurant.
Price:  Cheap...too bad they accept cash only
Operation time: wish they have longer hours of service and weekends
Bonus:  Free iced-cold water in pitchers.  Just go N grab one for your table

Very cheap!
Great sandwiches for 4$!

Go here for the cheap and abundant food, and ample amount of space, not the service. The worst part about this place is that it's cash only (or possibly just has a minimum?) and, it can be kind of confusing if you don't want to do the lunch buffet but would rather order from the menu (hint: don't stand in the buffet line...it sounds stupid, but on really busy days, it's hard to tell where to go). Also the service is not so great (I've had a few rude, awkward encounters with wait staff here, in particular one man who is frequently at the cash register). Despite its flaws, this place is cheap, and you get a lot of bang for your buck. If you've never been here before, go at an off-time (e.g., NOT between 12:00-1:00 p.m. on a weekday when the undergrads are on campus), and come with an empty stomach. I love the garlic eggplant from the lunch buffet, and I also love the chicken sandwich on the menu.

I've been here for lunch once and dinner once. It just seems like a slightly fancier fast food Chinese place. They have all their food prepared and presented like you would see at like Panda Express, and you go through and pick how many items you want. Then you pick a seat (the dining area is much more classy). Food is average.

Side note: to get INTO the restaurant you have to climb up a flight of stairs.

Atmosphere: I came in on a Friday around 4o' clock with a few friends and it was completely empty (which was weird). What's also weird is that they don't open on weekends.

Food: My friend had been raving about their clay pot, so I thought I'd give it a try. I don't have such a dish often, but it was delicious! They give you a good portion of meats and vegetables, and the rice had a kind of sweet taste to it that made the entire meal really flavorful. I really enjoyed it, minus scraping off  the remaining hard/burned rice. Prices aren't bad too, I paid less than $10 for it.

Service: Average. Since there weren't a lot of people (more like, nobody else) there everything came out quickly.

I'd go again, but only for the clay pot. GET THE CLAY POT!

This place has really good Vietnamese food. I always came here to get the lunch special, in which you can choose two or three selections and it comes with rice. You pick it like you do so in Panda Express. There's lots of seats and the decor is really nice. Their curry dishes and their beef with black bean sauces are some good dishes to try. It's a bit pricey for their portions but it's indeed good quality food!
Decent but not great lunch buffet. A once in a while kind of place.

Came here once for dinner.  Apparently they're more of a lunch establishment, catering to students looking for the closest restaurant to campus.  This is reflected in their odd hours - as a CorySoda dweller, I usually only made my way to that side of campus for dinner or on the weekends, and unfortunately their hours are not so accommodating.

Yelp defines two stars as, "Meh.  I've experienced better."  That sums up this place.  While it wasn't a horrendous experience - the waitress was attentive and polite - the food was just OK.  I love pho, though as a non-Vietnamese person I can't claim to understand what real pho is.  I just know that, from what I'm used to, the broth was a little off here; some reviews have described it as sweet, and that could be attributed to the fact they added hoisin sauce without my asking (not a fan) but even then I can't put my finger on it.  I want to say it's some sort of spice.  Maybe someone can help me.

It looks as though few people come here for the pho and instead for the lunch specials (when I came for dinner, we were one of four tables taken).  I'd say that's a good call.  As far as dinner goes, I'm not going to go out of my way for this place, especially given their odd hours.

Two words: clay pot ($7.50)

OMG! Since a friend brought me here, I have been hooked ever since. Yes they have lunch specials and a full menu, but the ONLY item I will EVER order here are their clay pots. This meal is literally cooked in a clay pot with rice, veggies, shrimp, chicken and beef. If you want, you can definitely customize or tell them what you want left out...but I'm greedy, so I get it all. I have never been disappointed ordering this dish. 

Why four stars? I am not a girl who carries cash, so they CASH ONLY rule is probably the biggest reason I do not stop in more. Lunch breaks don't allow for ATM visits and food purchase (since its cooked when you order it). If they ever get an ATM/Credit card machine, I would definitely upgrade their stars!

I was shocked by the attitude of an old white waiter towards a young girl who seemed to be a student.  I like the food at this place, but they should watch who they hire.
I know  waiting tables is not easy, but I am scared of having that guy as my waiter in the future. Of course, I do not think he would dare to do that to my wife in front of me. These cowards think they're so brave. Please get rid of that guy whatever is his name...... He sucks.

"Vietnamese" food for white people and students.  Who serves pho without a plate of fresh herbs?  Le Cheval does.  Boo.  While the chicken in my pho was blubber-free, a total plus, and the broth was greaseless, another plus, the broth needed a major infusion of siracha to make it flavorful.   Not serving the customary basil is a major downfall.  Also, it may have made me sick.

The food is pretty good, and I come here sometimes to grab a quick dinner before class. 

Usually it's the same lady running the floor, and she does a good job of keeping it all together. But last night, she didn't give me enough change, and was ready to tear me a new one when I had to repeatedly explain to her the math behind $20.05 - $9.05 = $11, not $10. 

Luckily there was someone else behind the counter who was following the chain of events and very professionally apologized for the mixup and gave me my additional dollar. 

I was still tempted to leave a tip for the waitress - she was, after all, doing her job and trying to the best of her ability - but she spat some words at me in a language I couldn't understand as I was on my way out, so I just decided to keep my money in my wallet.

I might still come here again because it's convenient and affordable, but this was an unfortunate experience.

I heard this place was good from a lot of my friends.  I even tried it several times. Both the heat-lamp buffet and the menu items were very disappointing.  And you know how I love a cheap meal, but I still couldn't stomach the dried-out tofu, hard rice, and oily stir fry. 

Turns out my friends were talking about "Le Cheval" (http://www.yelp.com/biz/le-cheval-oakland) NOT "Le Petit Cheval".  Different owners--different quality.

I came here for Pho but what I ordered did not come close to what I expected. The broth was extremely bland and watered down. The serving of the meat was also meager. The only thing that stayed consistent was the rice noodle. I am glad they provided Siracha or it would have been difficult consuming this meal. I'm sure they have other great choices but Pho is not it. I'm disappointed because the eating area is actually quite nice, relaxing and comfortable. If only they had better PHO.

The Honest Truth:
Get the lunch special.  It's cheap and the food is decent.  Not amazingly flavorful, but nothing a little sriracha can't cover.  I wouldn't recommend the stews, curries, or the pho.  I would recommend the clay pot.  Its a little more expensive, but pretty good and it fills you up.  I like the environment and there are a lot of tables.  It does fill up around lunch time so be prepared.

The Details:
I really enjoy the atmosphere of this place.  Theres a lot of seating both inside and outside.  It's nice to come here to eat and study, but during lunch it can get pretty busy.  That being said, the food is decent.  You can get the lunch combos (2 items or 3 items) for 5-7$.  You go down the line and tell them what you want.  Most of the food is not super flavorful, but its like standard takeout asian food (Panda Express-style).  I usually put sriracha on it anyway to add a little kick and some more flavor.  I would stay away from the curries or stews.  You don't get that much meat and the stew was pretty greasy.  I usually get some sort of ginger chicken and some meat and vegetable (broccoli and beef or string beans).  If you're tight on money, get the lunch combo.  If you can spend a little more, I would definitely recommend the Clay pot!  Pretty much its just meat and seafood cooked with soy sauce over rice such that the rice gets all the flavor.  It comes out really hot and is pretty filling.  Also, I'm not a big fan of their pho.  Its a little sweet, and the broth is not very flavorful.

Vietnamese food??  Where?  Right across the street from campus!

From outside of the building, the restaurant looks way too fancy.  You don't really see people inside either, but this is a hot spot for lunch!

I decided to go against my normal habits and order food from the hot trays.  For $5.75 I got rice and two items (black bean beef and lemongrass chicken) while my lunch buddy decided to try the bun thit nuong ($7.50?) off the menu.

My 2 item combo...was nothing to rave about.  The flavors didn't come through and it wasn't enough food!  It's like a more authentic panda express.  Sadd

HOWEVER, the bun thit nuong was HUGE.  Seriously, biggest bowl I've seen -- maybe as big as my head.  Full of noodles, and the most tender, juicy pork kabobs.  Wow.  I wouldn't say it was the best I've ever had, but it is up there.

Perhaps I got the wrong entrees in my lunch plate, but I did enjoy it as much as the bun thit nuong.  For now, 3 stars.

The steam-table lunch is chock full of veges and brown rice.  The Bahn Mi and Bun and soups are world class.  The dining rooms, both inside and out are comfortable and attractive.  Everything is a dollar less than it should be.  And the staff is made up of The Nicest People in the restaurant business.  Yes, The Nicest People.

Six stars.

Go now.

This is one of the few places I've been to in Berkeley that I think deserve acclaim. 

When I moved to Berkeley I had all these ideas in my mind of cheap, delicious, plentiful meals available because of the college atmosphere.

True, there are plenty of cheap places...But so many of them are total crap! But you know I gave this place 5 stars so I'll stop complaining and get to the good stuff.

I went here after class, got the buffet of lemon grass tofu, rice, garlic green beans and mixed vegetables.  I was sure I could save half for later (I'm pretty disciplined about this) but I was totally unable to stop myself from eating nearly the entire plate! The same thing happened to the two other gals I was having lunch with. So to wrap it up, this place is my favorite eatery in Berkeley so far.

To top it off, it was quiet, spacious, and you have the option of sitting in their big lovely patio. Definitely eat at this place.

I rate things often by value.  Le petite cheval is a great deal for the price, which is rock bottom.  I went here recently with a friend, though the lunch was served in warmers, it was still fresh and had clearly not been sitting for hours.  The beef sandwich is a great deal at 3.50, yeah 3.50.  In this day and age its a hard price to beat for lunch, geez my morning bagel cost more.

I was seriously seriously craving a pho.  Anything resembling a pho would do.  Problems I had: they must have put steaming hot soup in my waxy paper container since there was raw meat on top of my pho (this is a no no in my world since wax melts when in contact with steaming hot soup), I found a fly in my soup (this could be because I was eating outside but generally things that fly into your soup arent also dead in your soup because they can fly away).  I may give it another whirl but.... maybe not.  And the cash only thing can be a real drag.

I LOVE their vietnamese coffee! Their lunch deal is also a steal! You get a LOT of food for $5.75! I recommend the garlic eggplant. Essentially, you get what you pay for, but it's worth it! There's a lot of seating, and it's good for crowds.

They have a pretty good lunch special! Your choice of 2 or 3 items with rice, and for only $6-8! They basically have all the dishes out in heated trays already, and you just tell them which ones you want. I tried the ginger chicken and the garlic eggplant, and they were both pretty good! And though they were very filling, they weren't too heavy and the items weren't drenched in starchy sauce like some asian fast food places. Next time, I'll try the coconut milk tofu because that looked pretty good too!

Their pho, however, was rather disappointing. The beef was rather stiff, and they didn't give us basil to go with the pho! (I love basil)

Overall, the restaurant has a very nice setting, with plenty of seats, and even cucumber water dispensers! Great place to grab a quick bite to eat in between class. Just beware of food coma...

Finally! A decent place to have Vietnamese and Chinese cuisine! I'm giving this place 4/5 stars because they have this buffet style lunch special where you can order 2-3 items for around 7 bucks, which is good and all, but that defeats the purpose of having fresh food made to order. Overall, they have a great selection (I'd recommend getting their ginger and honey BBQ chicken) and the staff is really friendly! 

CASH ONLY. That kind of ...sucks! 

Large outdoor seating, good ambiance, def. great for large groups. 
Come try this place for lunch. You'll get decent Asian food (which I think is so hard to find in Berkeley, or maybe I'm just a newb.)

alright i created an account just to review this place because it is so awesome. lunch buffet is $5.50 and you get a ton of great food. make sure you get the curry chicken. this place is the best value in berkeley, and there's a lot of cheap food in berkeley

If you've been to the Oakland Le Cheval and are expecting the same class of restaurant, then prepare to be disappointed.  It's a much more casual place, which reflects the college atmosphere that surrounds it as opposed to the City Hall/Civic/Business types that frequent the Oakland establishment.

If you go there for lunch, they have items you can quickly order from the steam table with rice, but you can still order from the menu though.  One thing to note though is that one time, i ordered something from the menu and for the vegetable side they just took items off of the steam table so it was a bit weird to have a nicely cooked to order portion sitting next to bland looking green beans and carrots that were probably cooked in the morning and had been sitting on the steam table for a couple of hours.
For dinner it's a bit different as they close down the steam table and offer only table service.

I've had different experiences here with the staff.  The first time I went here for lunch, the waiter brought out the wrong dish but insisted that I had ordered it and was very rude about it.  It was only after I produced my receipt that he took the dish back, but he didn't apologize.  Needless to say, I haven't see him any of the other times I have been there.  The rest of my experiences here with the staff have been better.

The lemongrass chicken and green bean chicken are both good. The dishes are slighty pricier, but the restaurant encourages family style dining. The only problem is they charge for rice and I tend to consume lots of rice in family dining so that was one thing I dislike about the restaurant. 

TLDR; They charge for rice. Lemongrass chicken and green bean chicken are a must have.
Not that great in terms of cuisine, but it is great for its lunch value and large amounts of food -- which is all that matters if you're a student.

2.5 stars. This place is very deceptive.  On the outside it looks nice and on the inside it is cold, large, and cafeteria like.  The waiter is very pleasant and nice.  The food is cheap and great lunch deals.  Great for college students on a budget looking for forgettable dining options that will fill you up.  Not good for romantic or special occasion dining.

This place is not as good as the other Le Cheval restaurant in Oakland and the food is not really 100% vietnamese.  The menu is very limited.

Their lunch combo plate is probably the best deal in town.  Their seasonings and flavors surprisingly mirrored that of my mom's; so, I had a soft spot for this place.  

My sorority also held a lot of events here.  It was good for banquets at a reasonable price too!

Me and my team of interns used to have our weekly meetings here because it was close to campus and had internet (not very good internet by the way)

but I got REALLY tired of the limited amount of vegetarian dishes they had here.

My favorite was the veggie birds nest, probably the best vegetarian dish they have here.  Its stir-fried vegetables on top of crispy fried noodles yum.  Its a bit of a challenge to eat but once the sauce soaks into the noodles its really good.

Some of the other veggie dishes here, not so good.
- Lemon Grass tofu: The dish didn't have much flavor and all I could really taste was the lemon grass mostly
- Orange Flavored Tofu: more like tofu flavored orange.  I was expecting some sort of a strong flavor like "lemon chicken" when I used to eat meat as a kid but sadly turned out to be a very weak taste of orange and the dish mostly tasted like tofu with a hint of orange.
- Vegetarian clay Pot: didn't think this dish was that great either, the rice was really bland and the vegetables had no flavor.

I really stuck with the veggies bird nest but got tired of it after a while.  

We stopped coming here because the workers here were having drama and getting us stuck in the middle of it.  One of the waitresses was arguing with the chef and another waitress which were basically trying to get rid of her.

As she semi-sobbed as she took our order, the owner came around to try and calm her down as she tried to get us to feel bad for her as she told us her side of the story (as we are trying to have our meeting) that they were being mean and trying to get rid of her.  the rest of the meal was completely awkward since we were like the ONLY people in there.  We didn't come back again.

Other than that, the food isn't that great for vegetarians.

Oh and they only take CASH

I have always seen this place walking home from campus. The exterior is an amazing place, which truth be told is a sign to me saying, "Stay away, I'm totally expensive!" Somehow I ended up coming here for dinner just wanting to give it a try, even if it were a bit pricey.

Le Petit Cheval ended up being nothing like I expected. I assumed that it was going to be French and Vietnamese fusion but I soon found out that the place was a reasonably priced Vietnamese restaurant. Every person at our table got something different and it was pretty nice to see the different dishes. The appetizers, as expected, were a bit pricey but the $5 imperial rolls (three) were fantastic nonetheless. I got a bowl of beef pho ($6), which had a decent amount of beef and a plentiful serving of soup and noodles! It was not the best pho I've had but it's certainly better than anything else I've had at Berkeley (and cheaper and better than Pho Me Now too!) The barbecue plates were a bit overpriced ($9-10) for what they were so I'd recommend trying them out for lunch, as I'm told that they are cheaper then. Also, $4 for any type of beer is decent. We might just order two each. :) Do not order their wine, however, it is ridiculously overpriced ($6.50) for regular table wine.

Service was quick and attentive. The waiter talked to us and even wasn't shy in taunting one of my friends for wearing Giants gear because he was an A's fan. We got there at 8 pm and while we were a bit put off when they told us that their kitchen was closing because they close at 9, we ended up staying a bit after 9 without a problem, which was great! The place is annoying because signs are plastered everywhere that it is cash only. What's up with that trend Berkeley? I hate these dang restaurants that are cash only!
Great food, but I wish their hours weren't so limited.

This is a review for their banquet service. Our club hosted a four-course dinner at Le Petit Cheval. Their staff was attentive and helpful from the planning to execution stages. The only disappointments: we wanted to have vegetarian options at every course and specified a menu thusly, but on the night of the both the soup and salad had chicken, with no other options. Secondly, they only had two servers for sixty-plus guests that night, including regular diners not attending our event. I thought preparing more employees would have streamlined the food delivery process. Overall, the food was okay. The flavorful and thoroughly cooked, yet juicy eggplant in multiple of their dishes stands out to me from the meal. 

Average asian food for decent prices. I suppose it's a nicer venue than most campus eateries. I would come back as an individual, if someone proposed it.

this place is actually pretty good for dinner. good ambiance, plenty of seating. love the crispy noodles and the bo luc lac - shaken beef. the hot lunch plates where you order 3 items isn't too bad either. it's cheap but those items tended to be very salty and greasy from my experiences. could have just been a bad day. but def come for dinner! its yumms!

This is a nice cozy location to grab lunch with a few friends. The environment is nice and casual. The luncheon special is a good deal, especially when you get double rice. It fills most people up and satisfies me quite nicely. The beef stew is exceptionally good, and sometimes you'll find them to have some delicious sides that do not show up every day.

I come here for the lunch special.  You can get a mountain of food for a good price.  I usually have enough leftovers for a 2nd or even 3rd meal.  For a starving grad student, this is a godsend.  My favorite lunch dish is the beef stew cooked like my mom's: tender beef and carrots in a hearty soup.  The ginger chicken is also pretty popular.  Not a fan of the kung pao chicken however; the celery has sharp taste I find jarring in this dish.

Taste: 3
Value: 4
Service: 4

I've come here for dinner and their lunch specials. Their lunch specials are pretty good and cheap, and their portions are pretty big. I've tried their clay pot rice for dinner, which is pretty good. Their sandwiches are also very tasty as well.

Unfortunately, they're not open on weekends, which kind of sucks.

There is no good reason for me to not have tried this place during my four years at Cal! And here I've been complaining that there is no decent Vietnamese restaurants nearby and this was within walking distance from my apartment.

Food: Characteristic of a summer day in the Bay, it was cloudy and cold in Berkeley today. When the weather gets like this, I get huge cravings for a piping bowl of hot soup and noodles. Someone on Yelp said getting the chicken pho would give you more meat, but next time I'll try the beef since the chicken breast was a little rough and I did not end up eating it all. But a big plus for giving a HUGE bowl of noodles. Broth was clear and flavorful. I only added a little bit of hoisin sauce and Siracha to kick it up a notch. It came with the standard sides of bean sprouts, jalapeno, basil, and a wedge of lime.

Price: $6.50 pre-tax. A wee bit more expensive than other restaurants I've had over in Concord, CA. Since Berkeley is surprisingly lacking in Vietnamese restaurants, I'd say this was an OK price. I feel like I paid for enough food to fill me up.

Service: Restaurant was a bit crowded because it was lunch hour, but there were only 3 other ppl in front of me in line. I placed my order, grabbed my number, and got my food within 10 minutes of sitting down.

Will I come back? Given that it's less than 5 mins walk from my workplace (Boalt Hall), I'll return to try some of their sandwiches or a beef pho! Nom nom.

I like their vermicelli rice salad with the imperial rolls. The clay pots are really delicious, too, with the crispy rice that can be found on the bottom of the pot. Pho is good, light, and refreshing (not too oily), but they don't have the trips and tendon that I favor at the down home pho restaurants in Oakland and San Francisco.

Their sandwiches are a REALLY good deal - $4.95 for the steak - and have tons of flavor. I have never had a bad meal here, and I come often for lunch because I work nearby.

Note: They have a $10 credit card minimum.

My quest to find pho in Berkeley has fallen short once again!

If you think that this place has good pho I feel sad because you, my friend, have yet to truly experience what a good bowl of pho entails. The beef bowl I ordered came with barely any meat! What meat there was, was dry, devoid of color, and tasteless... much like the broth. Meat is what flavors soup people!! "Where's the beef??" Each bite I took out of that rubbery bowl of noodles literally tasted like nothing. I feel like I am being a bit harsh, but in all honesty, that is my truth. 

I'm giving this place 2 stars because the man who came out to give me fish sauce was quite thoughtful and brought me chili oil as well. Also because there is a possibility that I will come back here to try their lunch specials.... So let's see how that goes.

soooooo groooossss. I couldn't finish it. I couldn't even eat half of it.
Let me list what's wrong:
1. the rice was extremely dry
2. the tofu was tasted like an old tire
3. the chicken was also tough.
4. none of these dishes are in anyway Vietnamese (It's runned by vietnamese, I don't know why they would put out such low quality)

Yeah its cheap, but do you really want to pay anything for disappointment?
probably the grossest place I've eaten at near Cal and I've had food at the Univeristy's dining commons (crossroads).

I like this place, but that doesn't mean that it serves authentic Vietnamese food.  I think it's fair to say that this place is just a mix of Chinese and Thai, maybe that's what Vietnamese is??

Anyway, my favorite plate is coconut milk Tofu, try it if you decide to come to this place for lunch!

I've been here on several occasions for lunch with co-workers. All of those times were not bad. It's an easy place to get lunch and there's variety in their lunch line. However, I discovered on my last visit that their banh mi sandwiches don't have any spread/mayo in them, so they end up tasting pretty dry in your mouth with all that french bread. I'll probably be back again for lunch, but I cannot eat a banh mi sandwich with no spread.

So slow. So slow. We came with a party of 10 ish and ordered around 5PM. We wanted to make it to a meeting by 6:30 but guess what? By 6:00PM only 3 of us got our orders (and those were the people that ordered cold items)...completely unacceptable! We ended up being 30 mins late and most of us took our food to go. Don't come here unless you call them in advance to order or you're willing to wait for a long time!

Last time I cam here, I got the 3-item lunch combo but was extremely envious when I glanced over at the table next to us and saw that they were eating something that looked uber chic and delicious - the CLAY POT. 
So today I came in here with a mission - to eat the clay pot.  And to take a picture of it (Bam! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/lWG0hyFKIgZISbZkEfMVsQ?select=oSjF4f6frTHE1rBLZzkNJg), because no one has uploaded a picture of that beautiful baby onto Yelp. -.-
