It took a while to come, but I completely understand why. My *very very slight* impatience with the restaurant instantly melted when the (literally) smoking hot clay pot was placed in front of me, making this beautiful sound of stuff being heated over a fire. One look at this pot told me, "Duh, of course this takes a little longer to make. I mean, look at it! It's BEAUTIFUL!!" Opening the lid, I was welcomed with a treasure trove of delicious, warm meats and very fresh-looking veggies. 

Everything about the clay pot was delicious and done right. The rice is perfectly seasoned, the veggies cook in the pot (and therefore taste FRESH, are vibrantly colored, and not over-steamed), and the meats (the hoofed, the clawed, and the exoskeletoned - a.k.a., the beef, chicken, and shrimp) were all flavorful and distinct. I had a bite of my lunch buddy's lemongrass chicken, but I don't remember what it tasted like. I was completely lost in my lovely clay pot. 

So now, after my second visit, I am a fan of Le Petit Cheval. I am going to come in here to try their sandwich (still have yet to try my first Vietnamese sandwich), their Bird's Nest, and their vermicelli bowl, because my go-to place for that has closed down. Good stuff!!

Great for the price!

  It was freaking cold today and all I wanted was some pho.  I headed up to Le Cheval in an effort to try a new place even though it's quite a hike from my South Berkeley home. Not only was their pho awesome, it was friendly on the budget since I am yet another victim of the economy. Their broth is flavorful( but a tad too sweet for my taste) and the beef is thin, tender and cooked to perfection. Their pho is definitely worth the walk and  yes, walking or biking is suggested because parking is limited...

As another reviewer said, "cheap, and not in a good way".  The south-of-cal-campus area generally has a lot of bad to unremarkable food.  Students don't want to spend a lot, and don't seem to be that discriminating.  One could argue they can't afford to be, but I think this is not true: there are restaurants in the world that make good food in the under $10 range.  In any case the result is a lot of stuff I don't want to eat in that area.  
The things I got, I didn't like.  My friend got the bird's nest, which is crispy, or I guess hard noodles with some normal, stewy sort of stuff on it that I've forgotten.  I don't remember what I got; it was a long time ago and I'm just looking for 1 and 2 star places to balance out my corpus of reviews.

What a disappointment. After a long, tiring day of classes and all that hoopla, I wandered over to Le Petit Cheval for a nice, warm meal. I ordered the Vegetables in Lemon Grass to go. When I got home, all the soy sauce had spilled into the bag because the food packaging was sloppy. This was especially pathetic since I ordered my meal when the restaurant was completely empty -- you would expect more attentive service.

The primary reason I chose this dish was because the menu claimed it was topped with peanuts, yet my order didn't have any. The quality of the vegetables was so-so, and even though half of the soy sauce spilled out, my rice was oversalted.

I'll probably come back just to try the acclaimed Claypot, but there's no way I'm expected anything more than subpar from the other dishes here.

MAN I love this place!!!
Really FANTASTIC food.  I love the older dude waiter, too.  He's one of the best parts about Le Petit Cheval.  He knows his menu and will give you suggestions whether you ask for them or not -- and they're always great.  
I try to get something different each time so I can try more things and L.P.C. never disappoints!  Such a good place!!!!

I went to this restaurant after 8pm on Friday.  They were already closed.   They closed at 8pm on Fridays. Then I went again on weekend.  They were closed.   The restaurant should not be closed early evening of Friday and weekends!  That is the time people go out to eat.  I guess they do not need money.
Anyway, I went there on Monday evening and ordered Noodle soup.  Soup was lukewarm and noodle was a little hard.  I only get bean sprouts with it.  Usually other restaurants offer you at least bean sprouts and coriander.   
The one at Oakland is better, I think.  I do not recommend here to eat good Vietnamese food, unless you do not have a choice.

Man!  Totally underrated place!

I really didn't expect authentic Vietnamese cuisine; most of the places around Berkeley are mostly just sorry imitations.  But the calamari and bo luc lac (shaken beef) are served exactly how my family in Vietnam would serve them, with rice and lemon-pepper-salt dip.  I love going here if I start feeling culturally homesick.  

I recommend the grilled beef sandwich for the less adventurous eaters and the mi xao dong (birds nest noodles) to the more familiar eaters.  Prices are fantastic for the quality of food, and busing your own table means you don't have to tip, even though the wait staff is extremely friendly.

Edit: I went here today to try their pork vietnamese sandwich which comes with a salad for $5.50. It was bland =(. I guess I'll have to try Saigon Express's sandwiches next.

Go here for lunch. $5.50 for your choice of three from the steamers plus rice. You may be thinking "fast food!" when you see the steamers, but the food is actually pretty good and in large portions! There's a REALLY long line at the lunch rush at 12pm, 12:30pm, and 1pm, but if you go nearer to 2-3pm then they give you extra large portions to clean out for the day.

If you're not feeling the selection, the pho here is pretty decent, better than Vietnam Village in the ghetto in my opinion. You get just beef slices or chicken pieces here though. I believe fish is extra.

If you want something from the menu, I recommend the claypot rice which comes with beef, chicken, pork, and shrimp. It doesn't taste too different from fried rice, but the texture it gets from being in claypot gives the rice a chewy/crunchy feel.

For the low prices, don't expect super service or greater than average food. It's good college food for the student looking for some variety.
This is a place you go to for the food, not friendly service or ambiance.  Most do the buffet and it's totally good and worth the very low price.

the vermicelli is really good, but the pho is eh according to my friends. the service is kinda on and off. sometimes the one old white waiter is attentive but other times he's reading a newspaper and just chillin'. 

it kinda sucks that they're closed on the weekends cause sometimes you just want to get some hot pho after a night of hard partying, BUT YOU CANT!!!

Very decent fast steam table food. They also have things you can order off a menu. I like the lemongrass chicken and chicken curry and their green beans. Some of the servers give you a holy ton of food - it comes with a nice mound of rice and then you seat your self in the large dining room.
Had lunch there - it was tasty.  I had some curried stuff and rice.

It really wasn't as bad as expected, despite all the negative reviews. I actually kind of liked it.

Decor and Service: I like the cheap paintings on the walls, and tables are set apart far enough to have a decent conversation. 

Food: I got the lunch combo with 3 items. I chose the Garlic chicken, Chicken curry, and the garlic green beans. I thought most of them were actually pretty tasty. The garlic chicken was a little dry (overcooked, probably because it was sliced into pretty small pieces), but the flavors were there. The chicken curry was a tad bland and I thought it could have a little more kick. The garlic green beans were cooked perfectly. I swear I could've gotten an entire plate of those green pods and finished it. DEFINITELY choose the garlic green beans. The rice was cooked to the texture it should be.

Verdict: I like this place. It's pretty cheap and the foods are tasty. I probably will come back with a friend or two... it's definitely better than any of the Asian food at ghetto for roughly the same price.

Went here a few weeks ago and it was great. Missed the lunch buffet by an hour or so and the place was empty. The food was delicious. The only complaint I have was that the pork we got was extremely fatty - to the point of being left on the side of the plate, uneaten, but I'm going to hope that's a fluke.

3.5 stars. 

recommend: birds nest, claypot, chicken wings, grilled pork bermucelli (is the spelling right?lol)

I don't know why they call themselves a Vietnamese place considering their food looks and tastes like Chinese.  Whatever, their lunch specials are super cheap and they offer lots of vegetarian choices which is good for the Berkeley bunch.
Use to always get a combination of Curry Chicken, Beef Stew, Eggplant with Tofu ( very flavorful ), and String Beans.  Definitely a filling lunch.
This place is nothing like it's sister restaurant in Oakland.  But it in a college town, so it has to be fast and cheap.  In that case it  delivers.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Le Petite Cheval!!! I used to eat here all the time when I worked on campus and on Telegraph. 

The prices went up while I was frequenting this place but they used to offer three items for $5.00! When they went up, it was maybe $6. 

I used to always get the Singapore Noodles and the Orange Tofu. The third item depended on what was offered as they rotated options every few days. It's a very simple, basically cafeteria style. Grab a tray, walk up to the food bar with about 1012 options and pick three. Dreamy! Or just pick what you want and get charged accordingly. Love it!

There's not much for ambiance though there is (limited) patio seating.
I would love to go back to Le Petite Cheval, I'll have to remember that the next time I"m near campus during the day. I think they're only open for lunch.

I came here for lunch once and it was pretty good. The place is bright, and has a lot of seating. The food is pre-made and you go up and order your items. 2 items plus rice came out to be under $6. The food was tasty, however it was more Vietnamese fusion than authentic.

The rice + 3 hot dishes ($5.50) was ok tasting but cold.  Cafeteria style.

Convenient to UC Berkeley (across the street.)

Get there before 12 if you want to avoid the line for lunch.

Shares the rest rooms with the YWCA

I ordered the Bún Tht Nng, which had vermicelli noodles, egg rolls, pork...(I can't recall what else was in there...veggies, carrots? SAUCE!). It was YUMMYYY! I've been searching for a decent Vietnamese restaurant in Berkeley since I miss them back in Sacramento.

My friend got the clay pot, and my other friend ordered the pho and spring rolls. They both enjoyed their foods. She mentioned that the pho was probably one of the really goods ones that she tried in Berkeley.

The price was normal.  I paid around $5-6 dollars for my dish. 

The decor was gorgeous!! I would've never thought how beautiful it was if I never went inside. Don't judge it by looking from outside. Go on in and give it a try!

"Yay! I'm a fan." says the four-star descriptor. Indeed I am.

I see the reviews giving this place a lot of flak for not having the most authentic Vietnamese food, or for offering generic Asian lunch plates. True. But none of those concerns addresses taste. What, are people afraid they'll be judged for eating something less than authentic? I'd better not see them walk into a Chipotle.

If you want a BIG satisfying bowl of pho on a cold day, go to Le Petit Cheval. If you want gourmet or home-cooked Vietnamese, um, go elsewhere. There are quite a few worthwhile options. You don't have to like everything on the menu to be a fan. And the people there are nice!

Today was the last straw LPC. You deserve this.

Today:  instead of getting the steamtable food, because no amount of sriracha can save it from being beige and bland, I ordered the LPC soup.  The woman behind the counter quickly informed me that they were out of dumplings?  What?  They just opened - why didn't they just buy some frozen ones before opening?  

Anyway, rather than waiting a short beat for me to order something else, she helped everyone else in line.  This person has always bugged me with their sullen attitude.  (In fact, both of the women who are there are pretty sullen.  One of them ALWAYS starts plating up some rice before I can say "to go" and then looks extremely put out by making a show of moving that rice to a to-go container). 

Anyway I made my order.  Three of us ordered off the menu everyone else got the steamtable.  I thought maybe there would be a 10-minute wait for our food, we'd eat a little later than everyone else, our choice.  

Nope, closer to 30 minutes.  It seemed as if there was one guy in the kitchen doing everything.  And the food was not good.  I had actually forgotten what I ordered and when they brought it, curry beef, it was bland and the beef was gray and tasted cheap.  Gross.

Too bad, LPC.  You're so close to my office, and years ago I loved Le Cheval in Oakland - it was a really terrific place to go with a large group and had really delicious food.  

But, congratulations on being so lame you actually motivated me to write something.

Good for cheap Vietnamese food.  Yummy imperial rolls (at dinner).  I went for a fast dinner before a show at Zellarbach last night, and man, do they need more staff.  There were never more than 5 full tables, but the poor server was literally running constantly all over the restaurant.  (They only have waiter service and a menu at dinner - at lunch it's buffet style.)

the first time i enjoyed food from le petit cheval, i had just moved to the east bay and my parents and sister were visiting. i actually didn't even go inside; my sister and mom just grabbed some takeout while i was sweating it out, assembling my newly purchased ikea bed. they brought back a variety of dishes which were all really tasty, especially the singapore style noodles. 

however, i just went back today, with an uncle and a cousin who is applying to berkeley, and was not that impressed by the cafeteria-style buffet. i really enjoyed the ginger chicken, but the long-life noodles were really bland and my "mixed vegetables" was mostly cabbage - i only counted two pieces of broccoli and minimal zucchini. i would love to see them ditch the buffet, and have everyone order off the menu, because their food is really good... when it hasn't been sitting under hot lamps for the last three hours.

This is a review for their lunch special which is served cafeteria style. 

I think they deserve 2.5 stars for the food, but service and price brings them up to a 3. It's $5.75 for a 2 item+rice combo and $6.75 for a 3 item+ rice combo. They give a pretty hefty amount of sides, which means the rice will probably come up a little short. Ultimately, their quality is really lacking. I try to come by on Fridays because the partner in crime loves the salty pepper pork chops (deep fried and delicious--probably the only good thing from the lunch special menu--but it's rather unpredictable if they will have it on that Friday). 

But, in more than one occasion, the food tasted like it was spoiled and the rice had dried up chunks that felt like they were going to break my teeth. The chicken curry had two small chunks of chicken and 2 whole potatoes. I didn't come late in the day either--it was only 11:45... so I don't know if they're cutting corners by reusing food from the day before (or worse... food from days before). I've had better luck with their a la carte menu, but I don't think I'll be going back for a while.

Very average. Somewhat forgettable.

The lunch special is a pretty good deal at $5.75 (tax inclusive) if you're hungry (two selections from the warmer + a small mound of rice) or $6.75 for three selections. Unlike a lot of places where getting 3 items means paying a dollar extra for extra variety but the same amount of food (Thai Basil's lunch special), the extra dollar here actually gets you extra food. 

The three items that I usually get is the garlic chicken, the ginger chicken, and the curry, which comes in a small bowl. Be sure to ask for no potatoes when you order curry go get more for your dough. 

However, my favorite thing that you can get there is the Tofu Sandwich. Not many people know about it, but for $3.75 + tax, it's a really good and filling deal. You get a lot more tofu than either beef, pork, or chicken, and it's so flavorful you won't even care you're not eating meat.

How could I not have written about Le Petit Cheval after all these years. The sustenance of a typical Cal graduate student. The convenience from campus. The large portions. The eggplant and tofu dish with the tofu taking on that purple hue of the eggplant. The combination plates. The yellow chicken curry with huge chunks of potato and carrot, and sometimes chicken. The drippings of oil. Lots of oil. Very very oily. The feeling of, woah, how can I hit the stacks again after eating so much.

The fact that their cafeteria food menu has not changed over the years.

Advice: The dinner cafeteria menu is basically the same as the lunch stuff, except that it has been sitting there for 6 hours. Which is unfortunate, because sometimes you just get really hooked on this stuff.

By now, I've had one too many bits of chicken bone in my ginger chicken.  It's cheap, but not in a good way. 

I'm going to search yelp for something better in the price range and location.
"Their lunch menu restores my faith in humanity."

Eventhough I hate the Le Cheval place in Oakland, I find myself coming here to Petit Cheval alot during my time at UC Berkeley. I guess I'm just a thrifty student, and this place is right across from campus. The 3 entrees combo for $5.50 is a bargain, and you have a place to sit and  water to drink. A sandwich at Cheese and Stuff cost 5 bucks already. The food is oily, and I suspect a lot are left over from the previous day. But it's still better than dorm food or the stuff they sell in on-campus cafe's.

This rating reflects the service I received Once during their lunch hours and once during dinner.  During lunch I went with my friend and ordered something from their cafeteria-style menu... When I got up to order the Caucasian waiter asked me what I got and when I told him he just kept saying "what??" like he couldn't understand me...  Then he must rung me up anyways.  At dinner another time the same guy waited on us and was particularly rude.  When I ordered my item he just stood there waiting for something else. Finally after what seemed like forever he said "and?" I just stated at him confused. He just walked away after that.  Not sure what's his problem but he is a dick.

I hate the real Le  Petit Cheval in Oakland, it's busy, overpriced, and crummy.  The Le Petit Cheval serves average tasting food but it's super cheap!  I recommend the lunch special: big scoop of rice and you select three items (big portions) from the steam table for only $5.50!  It's fast, filling (though probably not healthy), and budget friendly.  The chicken curry was too sweet for my taste, I guess I had the wrong expectations.  The eggplant tofu and long-life noodles are delicious though! 

The atmosphere is awesome too.  While the indoor seating and benches are fine, siting outside is fun because you're up on the second story so you feel very fancy.  The service is sometimes friendly but never rude or brusque.  The pho here is terrible though.

Overall, I think this is a wonderful place for broke, hungry students looking for a quick fix.

A nice inexpensive and fairly good steam table Vietnamese joint.  I really love the green beans -- mixed with a bit of garlic, they have wonderful flavor, a good heft, and just the right amount of snap to them.  I always get them as one of my items.  If you want to order from the menu, try the claypot rice.  Although they're a bit inconsistent with it, when it comes out right it has this wonderful layer of encrusted crispy rice on the inside of the pot.

I'm a sucker for a cheap, delicious lunch so I absolutely LOVE the lunch buffet here. Two entrees + rice is $5.75, three entrees + rice = $6.75. I usually get the garlic green beans and lemon grass tofu. YUMMY!!! Also would recommend the curry chicken, lemon grass chicken, and singapore noodles. Pretty much everything I've eaten here is very tasty. The portions are generous (which also scored brownie points with me). Water containers with cucumber or lemon are available. You are encouraged to bus your own tables. 

It's one of those cash only places ($10 minimum for credit cards). I like that there are several TVs mounted on the walls with sports or news channels going. Usually busy at lunchtime but the line at the buffet goes quickly and there is ample seating (indoor and outside).

A great choice for lunch if you are around the UC Berkeley campus!

Thursday, 8:15PM.

Berkeley has a nettlesome noodle problem - too many factitious venues claiming they serve that delicious unleavened dough. 

Some college buddies introduced me to Le Petit Cheval and was shocked I never ate here before. And for good reason: the front mien invokes "pretentious restaurant" (an abomination for students on tight budgets). Not at all!

Notables:
+Nice, funny staff
+Clean establishment
+Sweet patio area
+Big screens mounted on the walls showing relevant sports (at the time, it was MARCH MADNESS, oh yeah!)

Grubbed on:
1. Pho with chicken
     +Huge bowl of soup n' goodies

And then...?
The copacetic pho won't bring Berkeley's noodle fans out of ennui or anything...but sometimes the a warm bowl of soup is necessary for a cold evening in the east bay.

Mediocre Vietnamese food that is more fast-food than real food. If you're looking for something quick and cheap with lots of seating, this is a good place. I can think of almost no other reason to go though--even the Vietnamese sandwiches aren't memorable.

No resemblance to Le Cheval in Oakland.  
There's not a lot of Vietnamese food here.  There's some Chinese, vaguely Korean, and Singaporean food. There's kung pao chicken, broccoli beef,  honey bbq chicken - in steamer trays - much like Panda Express. 
The two vaguely Vietnamese dishes were the chicken and the tofu with lemon grass. They both use the same sauce (asked them, I was stunned, at least make an effort!). Tried both dishes and could hardly taste the lemon grass.
I went to Cal, and this is good food for the university area.  Unless you are stuck on south side of campus however, do not eat here.  Save your money and go to Le Cheval in Oakland.  No kung pao chicken on that menu, just delicious and fresh Vietnamese food.
I gave an extra star because they serve beer.
Le Cheval in Oakland--good.  Le Petite Cheval--not so good and oily

Maybe I'm just adjusting to campus food, or maybe I've just realized that their $3.50 banh mi is by far the best, healthiest, and tastiest meal around!  Chicken or beef, that's all you can choose from, but the cucumber & carrot are fresh and crisp, the bread is big and crunchy, and the jalapenos are a little to the side so that if you're a wimp you can remove them....but why would you.

Also, I''ve discovered that if I don't wait til 2pm, their buffet choices are much fresher!  They're actually quite good, tasty, and filling, with all my favorite southeast Asian flavors, and there are vegetarian and meat-based choices to satisfy all comers.  How do you say nomnomosity in Vietnamese?

Good noodle soup with fresh ingredients. You have to ask for hoison sauce though, but feel free to add all the sriracha you want! Don't stress, they have a buffet laid out for you to choose your favorite Vietnamese dishes in between your classes. Service is pretty quick and the rest is self-service. The bathrooms are in the YWCA, which was kind of weird: the girl's bathroom had a sitting room inside the bathroom. Who sits in the bathroom when they are not peeing? Well, food good. Sun shining through the windows, good. Patio breeze. Good. -Matt

Such a cute lunch destination for both students and campus staff. Good prices, good food, and I love to sit there and eat because it's so warm and friendly in there! 

However, their wheelchair-accessible way of entering Le Petit Cheval is kind of a pain, because you have to go around to the other side (YMCA), ring a bell, go in and around, go thru the YMCA, and then follow your nose to the door that leads to Le Cheval. But we do it anyway, because the lunch experience is good by Berkeley standards.

I was pleasantly surprised that it wasn't more expensive than it was. I went for dinner, which seems the rarity of the reviewers.

It was SO slow, which I LOVED. Granted, it was a Wednesday evening, but still... we were the only table there for 45 minutes then there was one other two-some, so it was nice and chill.

Cha gio were hot and fresh, but weren't served with the usual accoutrements, which threw me off; thought that was pretty standard. The mi xao was damned near perfect, very excited about that.

Gotta try it for lunch sometime to see what the cheaper menu is like. Overall a very positive experience. Not taking credit cards was a real bumer, 15 minute walk to the ATM and back. That cost them a star.

I feel badly for speaking the truth on the dinner that I shared with 4 other friends a while back----

Honestly, the food was a 2.5---slipped a few rungs down that ladder since the days that I frequented regularly. However, the kind owner and service was really impeccable, not having been bothered at all with some specific requests with our entrees ordered.

To be succinct, nothing truly stood out in flavor or presentation; however, the portions were stinkin' large! Prices were reasonable, and this was another plus (esp. for the graduate students among us)

It certainly ain't no Le Cheval from the Clay days in Oaktown, but one's sure to be walking out filled, and if anything, I call the food prepared here a slippery mix of inauthentic, but edible "Vietnamese" food.

And that's honestly my 2 ct's worth---

Le Petit Cheval is a great place to go on a sunny day because you can sit on the porch with some friends and have a relaxing lunch.  I've never had any of their pre-made food that they have in the front counter, but I've heard it is quite a good deal.  I did get some for a friend and he liked it until we realized he consumed peanuts when he was deathly allergic to them.  

I usually get the grilled pork bun, which is with rice vermicelli noodles, lots of veggies(lettuce, mint, bean sprouts, carrots, cilantro, cucumber) and two skewers of grilled pork,  You can even get an eggroll alongside this.  Many of the Vietnamese places I go to, especially in Sacramento, like to overcook their pork so it has a slightly burnt edge.  I don't really like this and that is why I love Le Petit Cheval; the pork is always tender and juicy and tastes amazing with the noodles and vegetables.  The food is always served very quickly and the guy that brings the food is always friendly.  You are asked to clean up after yourself but this isn't a big deal in Berkeley.  The only downside is that  you need cash =( but this is very close to campus and thus, to ATM machines.

Le Cheval always delivers.  Unfortunately the last time I ate there, it also delivered a healthy dose of food poisoning.  I've eaten here for about once a week for 2 years now, so I'm not truly bitter about it.  I actually debated mentioning the food poisoning at all, as I feel that I'm negating my ovvn review.

4 stars for the food -- once I find something I like at a restaurant, I never really branch out.  Completely my fault.  I always get the rice vermicelli bowl with imperial rolls (deep fried spring rolls with chicken inside), the chicken pho is pretty good, and they also have a nice beef sandwich.

They have a lunch buffet which is pretty inexpensive -- $5.50, I think? -- which people seem to go wild for.  It never really looks that good.  However, they do call-ahead orders -- once you know the menu, you can call ahead and your food will be ready in five minutes.  *Cash only.*

I have mixed feelings about this place.

For one, it definitely has the most pleasant seating out of any budget restaurant in the immediate southside. 

Second, the food here can be excellent. It definitely doesn't carry that greasy, unrefined taste of asian ghetto, and there is an extensive menu selection. 

However, about half the time I was here, the food was extremely oversalted, so overpowering to the point of discouraging me from coming back. If you decide to come here, which I totally encourage, it may be worthwhile to play it safe and ask for "less salt". The guy who (I think) runs this place is very friendly.

So, in the past week I've gone to this place TWICE!  Why you ask, well 1st of all, they have a great Lunch Deal, for 2 dishes it's like $6 and for 3 it's less than $8, and they give you HELLA FOOD! and it's pretty damn good food too.  Ohh the only thing I wasn't a fan of when I tried is was their Tofu stuffed w/ Chicken, i was just not feeling it that day! But their lemon grass chicken is delightful.. AND so for the second time i went there, it was for dinner, well early dinner, I had coffee for breakfast, skipped lunch and was studying ALL DAY and so clearly i was FAMISHED!  I hit up the Le Petit Cheval, and got to order from their menu (sorry no specials for dinner) and i Ordered their Orange Chicken (dont' worry it's not the kind that's battered and fried, although I wouldnt' have mind that, I'm tryin' to eat healthy now that I dont' have time to work out) anyway, i digress.  SO, My roommate joined me and he ordered their Singaporean noodles.. YUMMY. Plussses, good food, great wonderful service, the lady was soo cute and so attentive and she kept adding more WATER every time i drank from my cup, sooo good!  (i'm a big water guy = great water service = 4 stars) the only draw back... hmm nothing really. =)

Whenever I go for lunch, I always order the garlic eggplant and garlic string beans over rice. The food is on the greasy side and they are skimpy on the scoop of rice but the taste is super. For $5.75, the price is pretty reasonable for fast food around the area but definitely does not beat Chinese Express. 

My friend had the pho here and she was absolutely disgusted at the quality. I would shy away from the pho here and stick with the a la carte steam table during lunch hours.

I only order one thing here and that's the egg noodle won ton soup.  It comes with a side of bean sprouts and fresh jalapeno peppers, and I always ask for a side of hoisin sauce. The guy behind the register is friendly and I like his sarcastic humor.  The server who actually brings out the food always provides service with a smile.  I don't think I've ever seen him not smile when serving the food to the customers.  It can get busy here during lunch so I recommend getting there about 15 minutes before noon to avoid the line and the crowd, as well as to ensure preferred seating.

Longtime fan of this place. The cubed beef steak with green beans is panty-dropping delicious. Also love the lemongrass tofu, the beef pho, the Singaporean noodles, the claypot rice, the curries...

Prices are reasonable for lunch, but go up a bit for dinner. It's okay if you want a nicer dinner with friends but nothing too fancy. Plenty of seating, and the waiter is kickass awesome. He's funny, prompt, and polite.

Am I stuffed? Yes.
Was the food delicious? Yes.
Do I have leftovers? Yes. 
Did I love the service? Yes.
Did I love the price? Yes. 
Was it close to campus? Yes.
Was the "To Go" option easy? Yes. 

   Their vegetarian food is delicious. I can't say enough how much I like this place. I normally come for their lunch specials and get that to go. They have curry and noodles and rice, and all of it is so cheap and delicious (service ends for lunch at 3 pm, I think). Today, I got their veggie pho at 6 pm to go. The person who helped me, Bill, was amazing. He was so sweet and patient with me. I was tired and out of it, and he was really patient. Apparently they make their veggie broth in house on mondays and tuesdays (it runs out towards the end of the week I guess.) My meal came out to $7.06, and I have $1 tip. He also gave me some hoisen sauce per my request. 
   When I got the food (took about 10 minutes), it weighted a lot! The noodles and veggies (broccoli, mushroom, zucchini, tofu) were in one container, and the broth in another. There was also a bag with sprouts and all that other jazz. I have eaten half of the noodles/veggie and broth and that was 2 servings worth! This will keep me full for at least 2 more servings. I am impressed by the service and food. Thanks Bill :) 

BTW, the packaging was really great except for one thing. I really liked how the broth was easy to pour, and the container for the hoisen sauce let me dip my spoon into it. I wish the noodles were in a different container than the veggies, I felt like I ruined the shape of my noodles (cutting them in half) to get to the veggies. I understand this might be a hassel to do, but even like the noodles on top, veggies on bottom would be good.

Came here with four other guys around 7pm. There were a few people in the building which should have been a sign from God. Anyway, the server/manager (?) was a dick. He seemed put off that we even came in. He probably puts up with snot nosed Berkeley students, most of whom have their head so far up their own ass that they know little about common courtesy and manners... But I digress. He was rather crass and eccentric. Which is fine, but restaurant protocol was kind of thrown off the balcony during this visit. Now, I'm not saying you should kiss ass if you work at a restaurant but you should if you want to be tipped well. Maybe it was his off day, maybe he just doesn't give a shit. Maybe he thought I was a smart ass, maybe I am. But the point is, all of this made the experience very awkward and strange. All of this and I haven't even gotten to the menu. I thought it was rather expensive for the quality of food received. I had the beef with seasonal veggies. It was okay, but nothing that I couldn't make with my limited cooking skills. Maybe lunch time is the better option, but I don't think I'll be coming back here any time soon.

While I like both Le Cheval locations, Le Petite Cheval has a beautiful outdoor seating area and somewhat better service.  My stomach is growling just thinking about their eggplant with tofu.  The rolls, both spring and egg, are also quite good.

I've come here with time pressure before a show at Zellerbach a few times, and they've always been very accommodating.  Probably helps that their rush is at lunch, not dinner, but still, they do a good job of speeding up if you need them to.  Just make sure you have cash on hand if you're in a rush, because the closest ATM is a bit of a walk away.

Sit outside, order the eggplant, and try not to scarf it all down in three seconds unless you have to, because it's absolutely delicious.

Mhmmm sooooo good! I tried several other dishes lately on their cafeteria/mall style food.

Dishes Tried Recently:
Lemongrass Chicken
Beef Stew
Beef in Black Bean Sauce

Lemongrass Chicken:
Very standard taste. Good quality lemongrass chicken.

Beef Stew:
Very tasty! Lots of different spices, lots of tender beef. Wonderfully put together in this entrée.

Beef in Black Bean Sauce:
There could have been a little bit more beef. The taste was standard and quite satisfying. If you enjoy black bean sauce, you won't be disappointed.

this was one of those really good cheap fixes in Berkeley that I loved.  buffet style dishes that wont disappoint and will hit the spot.  generous portions, wide selection of food...whats not to love?  don't come here expecting a nice, sit down experience. think of it as panda express style food....you order at the food bar, pay, sit down, grub.  i'd take le petit over panda any day though.

the food is actually pretty good and cheap. 

BUT BECAUSE YOUR SERVICE SUCKED SO MUCH ASS TONIGHT THAT I LEFT, I'M BRINGING YOU DOWN, LE PETIT CHEVAL. 

i'm the anti-entitlted american, and so for me to call out a place for bad service means there was some baaaad service. baaaaad!

Eh! I only come here because it's the closest lunch place to the building I live in all day. And it's a great lunch place for those who just want to get something to fill up on. This place is quick and dirty. It's not gourmet and it's not spectacular food, but it's good enough. You get what you pay for. In fact, this place resembles more of a cafeteria than a restaurant. Their pho is really bland as as their sandwiches, but their stir fry dishes are pretty flavorful, if salty counts also. I am really curious about their vermicelli bowls with egg rolls, so that is probably what I'd get there next, and I know I'll be returning for sure. The location is just too damn convenient.

BTW, CASH ONLY

After being a UC student for a few years, you not only get sick of the dorm food but you kinda get sick of the Asian ghetto restaurants. The Asian American food there just kinda sickens me after a while. However on the occasions that I ever do want to eat out, my mind always wanders to Le Petit Cheval. Let's go down the list of reasons why mmk?

(1) Location: It's next to the YWCA and has tables. Therefore you aren't scrambling for seating during the busy hours of lunch and dinner. For some strange reason, the place is never too crowded probably because its location is somewhat secluded.

(2) Food: The food at Le Cheval is better than and just about as cheap as most of the food at the Asian Ghetto. I especially love their pho and their lunch hour specials are pretty killer. The food is not nearly as greasy as some place like Mandarin House.

Morale of the story: Go to Le Petit Cheval. Tis awesome.  Good food and chill place.

This is one of the few places around UC campus where you can go with a big group to eat. It has so many empty seats, and is pretty fancy!

The food isn't that great though in my opinion. I ordered pho because it was rainy and cold, but I didn't like it very much. The noodles were too stiff, and there wasn't a lot of beef/cube tenderloin in it. 

Maybe this place is only good for lunch.

Came here yesterday for lunch and apparently, in addition to ordering entree dishes, they also have the "buffet" option where you can pick 2-3 items. 

Overall, I think the food is pretty good. The beef in the beef stew were a little dry, but the taste overall is pretty good. They give a lot and it only costs around $6-7 for the buffett option. Definitely recommend trying it.

The restaurant also has indoor/outdoor seating and lots of space. Def good for large group eating.

Le Petit Cheval was my home away from home for the 3 years that I worked at the university.  Linda and I shared many good times at this place.  In addition to being a decent Vietnamese restaurant it was also conveniently located at the top of campus near my office.  I also really like the family that run this place.  I miss seeing them regularly and miss the good food and good conversation shared with my pal Linda.  

They have ample seating inside and a cute little patio in front as well as in the back.  On a busy day it can get pretty hectic, especially when the servers can't find where you're sitting (order at the counter get a number sort of system.)   

On most days I would avoid the prepared food - it's not horrible, but it's not great.  It is however quick and the green beans and chicken or tofu dishes are acceptable.

Here's a list of what I highly recommend:
- Bun Thit Nuong (vermicelli with bbq'd pork) - they do pig right!  Their bbq pork is plentiful and always flavorful and moist.  It's absolutely delicious with the vermicelli and crisp lettuce and veggies.
- Banh Mi Thit Nuong (bbq'd pork sandwich) - good because they do pig right!
- Pho Ga (chicken noodle soup) - always comforting on a cold day!
- Bo Luc Lac (cubed beef aka shaken beef - though my dad used to translate it literally as beef over here, over there :) which I like best) - they serve it over a bed of watercress which is the way I used to eat it at home.  The hot beef together with the cold, bitter watercress and the lime dressing is a perfect combination.  
- Goi Cuon (spring rolls) - the rice paper they use for their rolls is amazingly thin and perfect!  They're always made fresh with fresh ingredients so it's a perfect item to start with or have as a light meal.

I'm sure there are other good eats, but it's been two years and these are the items that stand out.  Enjoy!

This place has been invisible to me for the five years I've lived in Berkeley.  I don't know why I never tried it; I used to walk past it several times a day.  Maybe it has something to do with the fact that it required me to go up a short set of stairs and through a courtyard to get into the restaurant.  It  looks nice enough, but either seemed like it was always closed or empty.  Empty restaurants near campus are almost assuredly filled with transmittable diseases or assassins or Celine Dion music.

But a week ago I gave this place a shot - try something new - and ate there again this week.  It has lots of window and sunshine, potted plants, open spaces, wifi, and a well-kept interior.

And the food?  Cheap and really delicious!  I was put off by the idea of a Vietnamese buffet, but it turns out that LPC actually has a sit-down menu with waiter service and everything.  I got the Bird's Nest both times because it was SO EFFING GOOD.  Crispy noodles cradling a mish-mash of perfectly cooked veggies, tender beef, savory tofu, and zesty shrimpies.  I also got the chance to try the cubed beef and green beans (such a strong, tasty flavor) and orange beef, also very good.

Both times the bill was under $25 for two people and including two beers.  Not bad.  Very good, in fact.  The older gentleman who works there is very funny and will chastise your date if he serves himself first.  Haha, glorious!  Great quiet atmosphere, great food, great service.  FIVE STARS!

I think I may have had lunch here every single day in the Summer of 2004.  I was hella broke.  3 items for less than $5 is a gawd damn steal.  This place is more like a Vietnamese cafeteria than restaurant.  You wait in line and order your items, load up on a tray, pay and take a seat in a cafeteria type room.

I always ordered the spicy beans and a tofu dish.  It became 2 meals easy -- lunch and dinner.  A little greasy but not crazy greasy.  I was always satisfied.

For some reason I expected a fancy Vietnamese-French fusion restaurant. Haha...that was totally not it. But Le Cheval has been in Berkeley for 24 years so it must be doing something right!

Good things about it:
- AMPLE seating, not cramped at all (I also found it amusing there are two tables that are permanently reserved for some special people who have their name on a plaque)
- Large selection of either food-to-order or food-to-go; whether you're in a hurry or have some more time to spare, they've got you covered
- Seems like the ready-made food cycle every now and then...my friend went yesterday and saw chow fun, but it wasn't there today
- The beef stew is good, the string beans with garlic is pretty good
- A huge variety of foods, definitely not limited to Vietnamese; there's Chinese, Thai, Vietnamese, Singaporean...
- Generally friendly service!

Eh:
- Lemongrass chicken has good sauce, but the chicken was quite on the dry side
- Although there's a variety of dishes to choose from in the ready-made section, not many of them looked all that appealing. It kinda felt like Panda Express...but probably not as grease-tastic.

Overall, I had a pretty good lunch for a reasonable price (2 items + rice for $5.75, no tax or tax included, cash only). I'd come here again to try some of the things on the to-order menu, but I don't think this will be one of my staples. Don't get me wrong though, it's not bad!

There's nothing like the greasy garlicky goodness that is Le Petit Cheval's green beans. This place has many of the greatest hits of regular Le Cheval's menu but served up as I call it, trough style (classier people might call it  "steam table"). You can get three items and a drink for about $6. Lemongrass chicken is another winner.

Caveats:
They're never open weekends.
Parking is difficult. I used to park across the street in an underground lot by Sweet Dreams and make sure I ate in under 30 minutes, so I'd only have to pay $1.

Tip:

Lunch time special:
$5.75 for 2 items
$6.75 for 3 items

Extra 75 cents to get brown rice instead of white rice.

----------------------------------------

I absolutely love the lunch time special at Le Petit Cheval. It's basically like a lunchbox type of serving where there is a buffet table of different types of side-dishes you can choose from. Both lunch time meals come with either white or brown rice and you can choose 2 or 3 extra items. Here are a couple of my favorites:

Curry Chicken: This is my absolute favorite side dish it goes GREAT with white rice (I've never tried the brown rice) and the chicken is completely sautéed in the curry which is amazing!

Ginger Chicken: This is a great chicken side-dish as well. The chicken is very nicely flavored.

Beef Stew: This seems to be a big favorite among a lot of people. It is pretty full-flavored with carrots and large cubes of beef. I prefer the curry chicken, but it's also a good dish to pair the rice with.

Sautéed Vegetables: These vegetables are a great healthy choice among the side-dishes.  Yes they are sautéed pretty well in a tasty sauce, but it still feels light and not too heavy.

There are MANY more side-dishes than just the few I've listed. I'd say that you get to choose among almost 20 or so options. The portion is definitely a good enough amount to get you full. For $6 or $7 that's a really good value for the amount of food you're getting.

Aside from the lunch special I've also tried the Banh Mi sandwiches which are great as well! I adore the BBQ pork so that's the one I always buy. The Vietnamese Iced Coffee is AWESOME! They only give you a small amount, but that small amount is STRONG. It's strong but tasty. I recommend giving it a try if you like strong coffee.

I don't really understand all of the good reviews for this place. I have been here many times, but always because someone else really wants to go. First of all the space is weird, it's not obvious how to find your way in, and it feels like a dorm cafeteria once you get inside. It's also not so "petit" - kind of huge in fact.

The food is slop. Decent slop, but there's no denying that it is slop. There are a number of these restaurants around campus - pay per scoop type of Asian places - and most of them are fine but unremarkable. Le Petit Cheval is no different in this regard. The confusing part is that almost nothing is definitively Vietnamese unless you order off the menu - the lunch buffet is kind of unidentifiable pan-Asian curry, stir fry, and fried bits.

Go to Pho 84 in Oakland, or even Le Regal or Saigon Express in Berkeley (inferior to Pho 84, but actually serving real Vietnamese food), and see if you want to come back to Le Petit Cheval.

Alas, the newly opened cart where I got my Pho on, dropped it from the menu. However, I re-discovered Le Petit Cheval!

My lovely boss suggested we take a working lunch to get out of the office and go to Le Cheval. She got in the rice plate line and up front, I ordered up the Beef Pho.

Delivered piping hot to our table in the patio, I tasted the simmered beef marrow broth. Yum. Added the pepper and Thai basil, dropped a few bean sprouts, and my Pho was back on. 

Again, a happy meal!

Quality food right across the street from campus.  Stop in if you have a block of time to kill in between classes!

Le Petit Cheval has no resemblance to her older sibling, Le Cheval in Oakland.  This feels more like a lunch cafe, pick up your tray and move along the line kind of deal.

Plenty of seats with friendly service to boot.

Green beans are the bomb!!!

Pretty new, with plenty of seats. I went a couple weeks ago but it was already packed, though, so I suspect by the time midterms and finals seasons come around it will be very crowded. Has a lot of selection, with sandwiches, salad, and bagels --nice for breakfast and lunch. Friendly service and fair tasting coffee, too!

One of the best cafe's near campus for studying! It's very spacious (I love that the tables aren't all packed together), has tons of seating and OUTLETS, and has great lighting! The wifi also works well, and the staff is very friendly. They also have a variety of bagels, salads, and sandwiches, and even beer!

I only wish they stocked a larger variety of pastries, because I love picking up a pastry to eat while I study... (Though they do have a nice assortment of cookies)

This place is not bad at all. The hammerhead: coffee with an.espresso on top. Gave me jitters.

Lots of space, lots of outlets, not well known yet.

Gaahh, just take my money already.

I almost don't want to post this review so people don't discover Berkeley Floor! I love, love, love this cafe. It's spacious, there's always been a table available when I go, and more importantly, the wifi works well and there are outlets accessible everywhere! This has definitely become my go-to place for studying near campus.

They offer pots of tea that I always see people drinking, and their salads are huge and definitely worth it. Try the tuna salad! They have a great selection of drinks and food. They even have a TV showing the latest sports game, but it is located in a spot where not everyone will be bothered if they're studying.

All in all, a great place that I hope doesn't change any time soon! Love it!

Living just around the corner and having to walk by it everyday to school, I have seen the place get built up and it is very impressive. 

I have to say that I agree with many of the other reviews in that the food and drinks are good and that the atmosphere is both great for work or for chatting with friends. 

The only real grip I have with the place is the spotty service. I have gone ever since it opened and have gone frequently, about 2-4 times a week. I would say about half of the time, the service is good, and the other half is poor. They would forget my simple order of a pot of tea and I've had times were I was standing there waiting after just ordering, and then being asked what I wanted again. And at most of these times, it wasn't even busy. I've also had trouble with the register like not getting my receipt after asking for it and then them having to dig through a pile. I know that theses are minor infractions, but when they happen about half the time I'm there, they build up. I know the place is new and the people working there might be new too, but how a business begins is  very important to how many regulars they might get. Maybe more training for the workers or better way of re-organizing how people should be served?

Other than that, this place is definitely one to look into.

This place is great. Solid wifi and a beautiful open space. I should  emphasize dthat the openness is really the key to making this place great. even when "packed" it's still possible to have a conversation and totally able to give you the sort of background lull of conversation without being able to hear any particular conversation which as someone who can be easily distracted is unbelievably important in a coffee shop.

  Also, the art covering the walls is unconventional and wonderful to look at. I've rarely found a cafe that fulfills so many of my criteria for a perfect experience. This place is truly a find. I've been coming here for a little while already and plan to continue unless some of these things change.

Awesome new cafe that just opened up near the Berkeley campus! Even though it's a bit further down on Bancroft just a little past Haas Pavilion, it's definitely a good place to get some studying done away from the busyness of cafes much closer to Berkeley like Cafe Milano, Strada, and Cafe Med. 

Here are my reasons for why this place is awesome: free and relatively good wifi, tons of outlets, plenty of natural lighting, and a ridiculous amount of table space! The place also features a great selection of foods and beverages (of which I need to try still), but I'll definitely be planning on coming back very soon! They've also got a selection of draft beers, which is pretty unique from many of the cafes that are in the campus area. The sandwiches and salads range from $7-10 and the drinks are basically under $4 (not sure about the beers though).

Once again, I can't reiterate how spacious this place is. The big windows and numerous tables make this place perfect for independent studying and group meetings. I'll be back soon for sure! Hopefully the majority of students stay complacent and lazy with cafes closer to campus and the rest of us can take advantage of this awesome new place...!

Berkeley Floor definitely has an air of "wow-this-place-has-just-been-opened" which is apparent from the moment you step in.

The floors are hard rock, the tables are mismatched and not teeming with people the way other local cafes usually are. The back right corner of the store has yet to be filled with anything. There are some paintings and pictures hanging on the walls, but otherwise not much in the way of decorations. It's astonishingly barren and cold, in comparison to the warm cushy-ness I am used to expecting from a cafe. 

FOOD/COFFEE:
I'm actually not a big fan of coffee so I ordered a chocolate chai latte (which wasn't even in their POS system yet -- again, the newness almost spills over into the steets) and a sesame bagel. Both were delicious. I know it's hard to get a bagel wrong, but really, the way they prepared mine (plenty of cream cheese, toasted just right, sliced down the middle and delivered to me on a plate) was above and beyond what I get at other local cafes. Also, although I'm sure that this isn't the first coffee shop any of the employees have worked in, no one has slipped into that easy comfortableness that comes along with working the same job for an extended period of time. 

GOOD INFORMATION TO KNOW:
-Plenty of outlets
-Free (and very reliable) Wifi with any purchase
-Lots of chairs, lots of little tables
-Non-distracting music playing in the background (maybe a tad bit too loud)
-Really, what else do you need for a good study spot?

OTHER THINGS I LEARNED:
-This cafe is owned by the same people as Sacs on College
-One of the guys working there is from Ireland (and is not bad as far as eye candy goes)

So, why 4 stars? I honestly believe that this place has a lot of potential, and that in a few months it can be transformed into the essential center-of-activity place that other similar businesses have become. The only potential problem? Location. Although on Bancroft and across the block from UC Berkeley campus, the Berkeley Floor Cafe is unfortunately further west than where students usually go to look for places like this. Its also next to the Tang Center (our health center) and the RSF (our gym). Not sure how that's going to play into this place's future.

OK, so like most other reviews have already said, this place is good for coffee, a sandwich, and some good study time. 

I have been going there fairly regularly now that school has started, finding a table is usually not that big of a problem, but sometimes patrons hog more tables than they need (seriously sorority girls, do you really need one table for your laptop, and one table for your coffee? NO.)

The sandwiches are good, I like the flavor and they are also good size, same with the coffee and tea, I just wish they would carry better tea than the teabags they use, but that is just me. 

Internet is good and fast, and there is plenty of natural light as well. Oh, and there is a cute boy working in the kitchen!

This new cafe on the south side of campus is a welcome addition to the Berkeley lunch scene. It is very spacious with plenty of tables (fairly spartan decor), has wi-fi, and a good selection of healthy food options. I was SO HAPPY that they offer lots of salads. Believe it or not, it's hard to find a good salad near campus!

I've had the spinach salad with chicken ($9) and the egg bagel with cheese ($3.50). They also have a large assortment of  coffee drinks, sandwiches, and yummy cookies :)

It has a relaxed, chill environment with campus peeps who are studying, web surfing or discussing projects with friends/colleagues. Hopefully it will maintain a not-too-crowded feel to it. So far, never a line at the cash register!

My general rule of thumb has been to steer clear of any coffee shops within walking distance to UC Berkeley. I'm just too old to fight with kids over electrical outlets, ya know? So, when I spotted The Floor Cafe literally across the street from the UC Rec Center, full of empty tables, I thought...something must be wrong with this place. Where are all the kidlets with their textbooks and laptops and Bears paraphernalia?

Turns out, just 3 reviews ago, I (or you!) could have FTR'd this place (that's First to Review, for the non-Yelp-geeks). That's how new it is. And THAT's why the churren haven't swarmed it yet. 

And thus, it's great! One of the most spacious cafes I've come across, with gazillions of no-frills tables (very studious feeling), free wireless, non-intrusive music in the background, your standard cafe fare - coffee, tea, sammies, soup, cookies, soda - plus a small selection of beer & wine, with happy hour from 3pm til close. 

I could do without the big screen TV with sports playing in the back of the cafe (sound off, thank gawd!) but it seems that every business in the UC area feels obligated to show some jock love. In the meantime, I'll be sticking to the front of the cafe, in the sports-averse nerd section, near the big sunny windows, with an oatmeal-golden raisin cookie. Oh yes.

Have to give where credit is due. Sure there are some kinks that needs to be worked out, but the cafe is off to a good start. The space is spacious clean and it receives plenty of sunlight. The coffee is well price and at a dollar per refill it is definitely worth bring your school work here and power through it. Like previously stated, there are plenty of outlets and seating

As a self-proclaimed coffee snob with the dream of eventually owning my own cafe, I've got to say that I can't believe this place doesn't have more customers yet. 5 stars, to help them get the patronage they deserve. 

Sure, it just opened, but Berkeley students always seem excessively hesitant about venturing outside of their usual study haunts (Milano/Strada for students on south side, People's/Philz for those on north side). The location is great, and I am beseeching you to come give this cafe a try. I can't speak for the other drinks yet, but I ordered "The Floor Coffee" today (espresso with vanilla ice cream, caramel, crushed almonds, $3.50) and instantly felt a smile spread on my face. I was afraid it would be too sweet, but it was just right. The espresso had the nice, bold, well-rounded flavor that coffee fanatics crave while the almonds/ice cream served only to embellish it in the best way possible (and not drown it in a hodge podge of sugar). My boyfriend got some apple juice which totally blew the Minute Maid shit that most cafes serve out of the water and he refused to share with me after the first sip.

As for the cafe itself, it seems like a great place to get some work done. It's quite spacious, the music is conducive to productivity, there is solid WIFI, and there are outlets everywhere. It seems to attract a slightly older crowd (grad students/etc) which makes sense, since they also serve beer/have a happy hour which I'm really looking forward to utilizing to make working on my laptop less painful.

The coffee here is pretty good! I got an iced white mocha and my brother got an iced chocolate chai. The white mocha had the perfect amount of sweetness to it and with the sip that I had from my brother's drink, I thought the chocolate chai was pretty good.

Extremely spacious coffee shop! Lots of seating available. Looks like it'd be a nice place to get some work done.

I'm not too sure how this compares to other coffee shops in Berkeley because I'm new to the area, but I definitely will return for another cup of coffee.

This might be my most favorite campus-centric coffee shop to date! Unlike many other cramped, dingy places around, this cafe is airy and light-filled. The free wifi is easy to get onto, dependable, and there are plenty of outlets around. 

The coffee is very strong too, and deliciously single-dripped. However, this also means you might have to wait more than a few minutes for your coffee.  The food is well-portioned for the price, but also tends to dribble out of the kitchen at its own pace. 

I kinda love that they have happy hour every day from 3pm-close, with all beers at $3 (Guinness at regular price is still only $5!). 

Because sometimes, the only thing better than coffee to help get your work done is a modest pint.

i don't even know what was there before BFC, but this place is HUGE. it offers a wide selection of coffees/drinks, bagels, sandwiches, salads, and some pastries. staff is chill, although maybe a little understaffed. it takes a bit to get your order when it's busy, but that'll probably improve with time. 

anyway, the three things i believe ALL cafes MUST have, aside from good food/coffee, are:
1. free wifi
2. lots of outlets
3. lots of seating
it took me 3 years to find a place in berkeley that has all of the above, and i'm super bummed this place opened my last year. this is the ultimate study spot, and if you're like me and you like to have a beer or two while you work, you'll be happy to know BFC has a selection of beer/wine with happy hour from 3pm to closing. 

i watched the construction of this cafe all summer and thought it'd be just another one of those places that pop up in berkeley and leave as quickly as they come. but wow, i'm almost glad the power went out in my apartment one day and forced me to come here to study. i really hope this place is here to stay. i hesitated making a review, because a (large) part of me wants to keep BFC a secret. but i'm writing this because i think it's an establishment that deserves recognition. and even though it'd be good for their business, i just hope it doesn't get swamped with students congregating for group projects, meetings, etc. regardless, i'm going to enjoy this hidden gem as long as i can.

This is a review from the perspective of someone who needs a place to work all day.

Berkeley Floor Cafe offers plenty of seating and plugs, clean bathrooms, very good quality wifi (I was able to stream HD video without pauses), strong iced coffee, a convenient location near the RSF, and is open from 8 am until 8 pm (soon to be midnight according to one of the staff).

Frankly, all other Berkeley coffee shops pale in comparison. The lone exception might be Philz coffee, though they're much more expensive and I tend to avoid it because I have trouble coding while live music plays.

Haven't tried anything but their iced coffee. 

The only downside so far is their floors are dirty/dusty. Might just be related to the fact that they just opened. 

Will update this review as I try more of what they have.

Tips:

Accepts card no minimum.

------------------------------------

This cafe is conveniently located right next to the Tang Center so I stopped by after a doctor's visit. I believe this is the only cafe in the UC Berkeley area with a liquor license so they have a happy hour with $3 beers. I forgot the time.

The new cafe is VERY large and spacious with a lot of tables. I can just imagine that this will be a good place to study during midterm/finals week.

I got an iced white mocha here for $3.37 after tax and it tasted great! It's definitely got more of a coffee taste than a sweet taste which is good for those that don't like too sweet of a drink. I liked my drink! I definitely want to go back when I'm in the area and try something else on their menu. I might even give the food a try they have a very large menu to choose from.

According to a few of my friends, this cafe just recently opened in Berkeley. For those that have been to College Ave, the Floor Cafe has a very Sacks-like vibe. Not only is it very roomy, but there's a ton of seating!

I ordered a white mocha, which was rather bland in my opinion (what can I say, Starbucks has spoiled me). But my friend really loved the -----.

Regardless of the taste, though, I think I'll definitely be back. Keeping my fingers crossed that the Floor Cafe stays undiscovered. This place is so close to campus that I'd love coming here to study for finals- as long as. I don't have to fight anybody for seats!

Berkeley Floor Cafe isn't that accessible if one has a car. parking nearby is scarce and precious(pay the meter). BFC is ideal for people who live nearby. lots of floor space with dozens of minitables available.

menu: coffee, flavored teas, salads, sammies, draft beer/bottled beer, bagels (1.75), etc.

pour: drip poured coffee(2.18)
-definitely organic, medium roast, italian?
-well worth the $$, very smooth, robust, aromatic

coffee drips:
-quick acknowledgment of patrons, smiling service
-tv in a corner for the sports minded. "jocks are people/patrons too".

I was hoping it would be really good because I'm usually in that area around dinner time, but for the most part food just tasted alright.

Service/Decor: Looks pretty clean, there are a few tables inside to eat at, but you'll probably want to to-go your food and eat it elsewhere. They actually painted the ground outside the restaurant with white paint to give off that familiar Greek-tile vibe, so kudos for that effort. Service is slow, but staff seem pretty nice.

Food: I got a chicken souvlaki and a pork soulvaki, as well as their Greek fries. My friend ordered one of their salads, I can't remember what it was called. The chicken and pork were alright. The chicken was a little dry but the pork was cooked nicely, and both had nice sears. The Greek fries were a total mess. The portions were pretty small and it was SO SALTY. Heck, I love salty food, but it was completely over the top. The fries were salty and the feta was salty, and I cringed after tasting them. My friend's salad was just one of those common iceberg lettuce mixes with the little tiny carrots and purple cabbage drizzled with dressing, oil, and feta. Not appetizing. 

Portions are small and quality is lacking for charging the prices they do.
The rotisserie chicken makes this restaurant and the entire surrounding block smell heavenly.

I love Souvlaki!!! The $4 quarter chicken meal is such a good deal, and the chicken is delicious. The greek yogurt is also incredible -- thick, creamy, and just sweet enough. Souvlaki was just featured on this UC Berkeley news show -- check it out and see the review for yourself!  http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5vZfjVxSIMA

I got lunch here today and I was excited to eat at a greek place so close by and unfortunately I was disappointed. I got the sticks in a box with 2 pork and 2 chicken souvlaki. I was not impressed. There was like 10 fries and a sad looking salad. The amount of food is not worth the price or portion. The sauce and chicken souvlaki were good. The pork..not so much. One of my pork souvlaki was not thoroughly cooked. It was pretty obvious since the other one was much darker on the outside and on the inside it was pink. The quality of the meat could be improved as well. I was a little disappointed that this place wasn't a more authentic greek place. The only item they serve is basically souvlaki in different mediums (pita, box, sandwich).
The customer service wasn't great. It wasn't terrible service or anything, but then it wasn't very welcoming either. Overall, I think the place has potential, if they could improve the quality of their food. The place does look very nice though. It is very well decorated and designed.

greek style roasted chicken was ace! 
and the waitress was SO NICE. she was sooooo good at introducing food and actually engages you in conversation. it has great decor greek wise and I WILL SOOOOO COME AGAIN!!!!

Filling and satisfying meal. 

I ordered a half chicken combo and a meatball combo to go. The place has some cute decor looking like a traditional blue and white Greek balcony. Unfortunately, the tables and chairs are quite uncomfortable, so I was glad I ordered take-out. 

Both of the dishes were quite substantial. They both included a salad and a ton of fries. There were honestly WAY too many fries compared to the main item and the salad,  so it would have been better in the ratios were more balanced (unless you really like fries).

Overall, both were complete meals for pretty good value. I would recommend take-out over dining in as well.

I had the roasted chicken there today. The chicken was amazingly good and had a hint of a lemony taste to it as well. It is very cheap for what they give you. My roasted chicken plate only costed me $6.99 and it included fries and a salad. It is definitely a good place if you are interested in trying some Greek/Mediterranean food. The only con about it is that the combo did not come with a drink which is what combo plates usually come with. Another thing is that the tables there are quite small. Its not so small that I me and my friends were crammed, but its very noticable. Aside from that the food there was pretty good. I know that roasted chicken isn't really greek culture, but there are cultural foods there on the menu. For example my friend had the souvlaki plate which I heard he enjoyed pretty well.

The menu was a little hard to understand, so after a little misunderstanding, I ended up with a free side of salad and fries! Which is +1 star. Otherwise, I think this place is just mediocre-average and while I do wish this 3rd restaurant in this venue the best, I am doubtful of how long it'll actually last. 

Ordered the Pita Souvlaki (4.50) because I thought this was the meal that came with salad and fries (but turns out that is the combo deal, which is 6.99). The Pita Souvlaki is actually just the sandwich with pita, large pieces of meat, some fries, and their sauce. I had to ask the person behind the counter for the salad+ fries which they gave to me on the house because I was obviously confused. 

The sandwich itself was okay - it helps that I was really hungry. The meat was good, but kind of dry and chewy. The fries were just okay too - there were just about 2-3 of them in the pita (which was also semi-dry.) I think the best part of their food is THE SAUCE!! Even the owner came up to our table and was talking about how the sauce is special because it's a handmade sauce made by his son. 

I feel bad because of their nice service, but I don't know if I'd come back. I feel like though it isn't very expensive or anything, you can get more for 6.99 (if you want the meal) elsewhere, but not necessarily near Asian Ghetto which averages at ~8. I think this is definitely a place to try once though.

Good food, but RUDE worker who served me.  You have to take your trey outside the restaurant to bus yourself but I couldn't see this at first, and when I took it up to the counter the guy stared me down for 5 seconds without saying anything then rudely took my trey and mumbled something under his breath.  I don't have tolerance for this so I won't be going back out of principal.

Got a chicken pita and greek fries! really hit the spot and for me the portions were pretty decent.
split fries and greek yogurt with friend who got her own veggie pita as well.
Whereas I usually crave more feta cheese with my meals, I actually liked the ratio and actually had more feta then needed for fries :D a good thing really, yogurt was also so tasty that i wondered if it was even healthy anymore, wish i had a little more honey or fruit to yogurt but glad i split cuz greek yogurt, fries, and two pitas was a lot of food for both of us. They also have a little corner near the front  that has greek tabloids and snacks, very cute though i don't know if they are available for purchase

Short: Very satisfied with meal! looking forward to coming again

Food here are pricey for the portions and quality of food. The meat was dry and, the portions were REALLY REALLY SMALL. I repeat, REALLY SMALL. My friends also mentioned that it was unusual for a Greek restaurant to not serve lamb. 

I won't be coming back again unless there are some changes.

P.S. My Greek friend said, "If anyone ever ask you about the food here tell them, 'it's ehhhh.'"

I'm really picky when it comes to Greek food having spent many of my summers in Greece and with family members that are most definitely the best cooks on the planet. So, I didn't have high hopes for this place when it opened on Durant amongst a lot of cheap, greasy and mostly good places around it. I was pleasantly surprised by how good the food was! I ordered the Veggie pita meal and my friend ordered the chicken souvlaki meal. Our meals were very good, and the fries are DELICIOUS--they taste like they do in Greece!

Like many other reviews, I have to dock them for the small portion sizes. The second, (and third, and fourth...) time I went I ordered double of what we had ordered originally. Hopefully the owners read these reviews and adjust accordingly. There are a lot of other food options in the area and students are always looking for a good deal, but also know when they're being ripped off!

Overall this is a great option for fast Greek food-- I only wish they were open at 2am when the bars close!

I don't have much experience in Greek food, but Souvlaki was so conveniently located that I thought I would give it a try.

I came with a group of friends around dinner time, and the place wasn't crowded at all. In fact, post ordering, our food was ready incredibly quickly, and was pretty cheap considering. I wasn't partial to the main dish I ordered, but my friend ordered the Greek yogurt with honey and fresh fruit, and DAMN that stuff is good. I seriously would come back just for that (also the only reason this place got 3 stars).

The restaurant itself is rather small (think of a rectangular box, including the kitchen), and the seating is...unique. Souvlaki provides high, almost picnic-like tables with bar stools for seats. Obviously not the most comfortable, but practical in terms of space. 

Also I was a bit shocked by how..."stand-out-y" (for lack of a better way to put it) the bright blue and white color scheme is. It is really, really pervasive, both inside and outside the place.

Take note that like many restaurants in the area, Souvlaki does not have a bathroom.

I got the stix box and as everyone else said, the portion size was pretty disappointing for $8. I got three chicken and one pork souvlaki which came out in skewers. It came with fries (literally 10 fries...) and a tiny portion of salad (if you can call it that). There were four quarter pieces of pita and tzatziki sauce as well. 

The food itself was alright - not the best, as there are many other Greek places in Berkeley with better souvlaki. I liked their tzatziki sauce, though. 

Service was also pretty slow, which I understand because they're new...but the cashier took about 5 minutes to ring me up. 

Overall I wish them the best of luck, but I'm not too sure on its longevity.
Best rotisserie chicken in Berkeley. Well priced and super tasty. Good plate with a good portion of Greek chicken, French fries, and salad. Cheap. Fresh. Delicious.

Kind of odd that the reviews below this are negative. I think that they came out when the restaurant first came out. 

I always get the 1/2 chicken deal that's 6.99 with fries and salad. They actually add a LOT OF fries now. 6.99 for a half chicken that is amazingly seasoned? I'd take that as a deal any day, and the sauce that it comes with is okay.

I would give it 5 stars, but I tried their "sausage" stick, and it's literally a hot dog on a stick...nothing fancy. I've tried the souvlaki too, and its delicious, although slightly small. They give a LOT OF FRIES NOW GUYS. Seriously. They listened to the reviews. 

I really hope that this place survives, the locations is kind of cursed. I see the woman owner work hard everyday, and I mean it when I say you can tell how hard this little place is working. 

GO TRY IT! Esp the half chicken deal!

The food was okay. On the salty side, but okay.

But the service was really slow (despite their having about half a dozen people behind the counter), and the portion size was seriously laughable.

That being said, I wish them well. The place is darling (all whitewash with blue trim), and they're on a serial failed-business-venture location, so maybe they can be the ones to bring that spot to life?

(Owners, if you're reading this: there were _maybe_ three fries in my sandwich. When it was handed to me, I seriously considered asking if there'd been a mistake since it weighed practically nothing.)

4 strong stars for the Greek yogurt + fruit alone!!!! So good! I enjoyed the chicken skewers and Greek salad too. A healthy alternative :) 

Try the yogurt!

I would like to give this good-hearted little restaurant a stronger review than I have seen.  To be clear; I have only eaten there for lunch and I have stuck to the 1/2 roasted chicken.  However, I love a good roasted chicken, and I am quite picky, so I am willing to overlook some of the other down sides to the rest of the plate.  I agree--there could be more fries.  And I am just not all that crazy about the baby lettuce salad concept, as it is too easy for it  to go a little tired and limp.  But if you are in the mood for roast chicken, it is tasty and very moist and flavorful.  I hope the owners will review Yelp and continue to improve the restaurant.  I think they really care what they are doing, but they need to get a foothold in a location that has been historically tough.  I think this place is worth a try and they will let you have little tastes.  I am happy to have another choice in this area as I work in the area and have been getting very bored with the same old stuff.

I just came back from Greece and was craving Greek food. I saw that Souvlaki had just opened on Durant and decided to give it a shot. The decor is super cute; i almost felt like I was in Santorini again! They had clearly put a lot of effort into decorating the place. It looks 10x better than any of the restaurants around it.

I ordered a pork souvlaki gyro with Greek fries and a salad. I had read reviews before ordering and saw that people thought the portions were small, but I thought the meal was the perfect size for me. It tasted authentic and I love how they put fries in the gyros. The meat was well-seasoned and tasted great with the tzaziki sauce. They also gave me lots of Greek fries on the side; I couldn't even finish them. Overall, I was pretty impressed with the place and would come back to try the Greek yogurt.

In response to the previous review, this is definitely NOT the best Greek food in Berkeley... since I can definitely think of at least 5 other (and better) Mediterranean restaurants off the top of my head. 

I convinced my friend to come in with me for dinner today since it had literally just opened three days ago and I always like to try something new. I'm not sure why anyone would want to open another Greek restaurant in this exact location since 1. its predecessor Fa-La-La did horribly and surely raised a red flag or two 2.
