D'Yar right across the street has some of the most satisfying Mediterranean food I've ever had. 

My (male) friend and I wanted to get 1/2 of a roasted chicken, but they were all out (it was 7:45PM. C'mon now.) so we ended up getting 2 chicken pita wraps and a Stix Box. Portions were definitely NOTHING compared to what I can get for the same price across the street. The pita bread was a little smaller than the standard size, and there was hardly any meat inside. They put a couple of their regular french fries in the pita wrap, which was kind of nice but also made the wrap extremely dry - meaning there wasn't enough sauce. Speaking of sauce, they also cheap out with how much tzatziki sauce they give you with your food. The Stix Box, which has 2 chicken and 2 pork kabobs, came with a little plastic sauce container that was 1/5th filled. Our Stix Box came with 10-12 fries, some really bitter leaves drenched in dressing, a quartered pita bread, and the tzatziki sauce. I enjoyed the chicken, which I found very savory and juicy. The pork was juicy, too, but there wasn't too much flavour to it. If anything, the pita bread was the best part since it was really soft but still had a nice crunchy crust to it.

Everything came to about $19, which is pretty pricey considering how little food we got (more so for the pita wrap, $8 for 4 skewers actually isn't bad at all) and how unsatisfied our meal left us. We had to go across the street to Lotus House afterwards to get another meal! And this is coming from a girl who is on a pretty strict 1000-calorie diet. 

Since the store is oddly shaped, there isn't much room for seating other than in the very front (near the windows). The place is really clean and the interior is really WHITE, but I'd be worried if it weren't since they're barely a week old. Staff was decently friendly, but I could tell they were very green because they were openly discussing if some of the other customers had "paid for their Stix". Overall, I wouldn't come back since it's expensive and like I mentioned before, there are plenty of other Greek options around.

Walked by - STARVING and saw big shiny new signs for Greek food. The smell drew me in and I was greeted by the very friendly manager. Ordered the "stix box" (2 pork and 2 chicken kebabs) over freshly grilled pita bread served with their tzatziki sauce and Greek fries. 

They're still training their staff but it really looks like they have potential - could they be the ones to break the curse of this Durant nook area? Fresh rotisserie chickens rotating in the background, fresh meat being thrown onto the grill. It all looked GREAT.

The major disappointment was the portion size for the price: only got about a dozen french fries and the takeout box was depressingly underfilled. The meat was nicely flavored but the pork was pretty greasy. 

I'd be willing to come back again in a month or two when Souvlaki gets their menu and chefs a little better trained - still worth a try though!

$5 minimum for credit card purchases!

Yes the portion sizes aren't spectacular but the meat is well seasoned and nicely grilled. The fries are ok, some were a bit cold and you also don't get a lot of fries. Overall I was satisfied. 

I'd probably still go to Dyar for something similar.

------

(UPDATE)
How is it that this restaurants has four 5 star reviews all on the same day by people who have just started using yelp this month and only have a review for this restaurant? This just seems shady, well it doesn't seem, it is. Why not worry about improving the restaurant instead of just making up fake reviews. Listen to what these reviews are saying and adapt to their needs.

Souvlakl has the usual pitas, skewers, salads, fries, chicken. many entrees had the the 6.99 price point.
only the greek dog caught my interest

eats: greek dog(2.72)
-came with dap of spring mix salad, fresh
-lg dog(1/4 ib?) was juicy in warmed bun
-condiments of mayo, red onions.
-surprisingly satisfying and filling.
3.5 stars, above average

crumbs:
-open grill, food cooked to order (5 minutes).

Really?  Maybe I'm coming at the wrong time or getting the wrong things or ordering from the wrong people, but this place is pretty terrible.  The decor is that of a run-down apartment, the wait staff and kitchen take eons, and the food is less than impressive.  I mean, how do you mess up egg custard tarts?  Mine were lukewarm and not very sweet.

The BBQ pork buns are passable but that seems to be about it.   I deem this place a failure.

Really a 3.5.   Be nice to the couple who own it--imagine having a young child (toddler) and running a business (with just the two of you) at  the same time...what stress.

Lunch specials: $5.50....yummy and fresh.  Have not tried the hot pots or dim sum....but I say, give the little mom and pop place a try.  

On a bad day, the wife may be absent and poor pop is doing everything!  When the wife is there...she may not be smiling all the time, but can you imagine all the worries that come with trying to run the business with just two people--on Telegraph~?!

They have a dinner deal:  $17 for 3 dishes....may try that sometime when I don't want to cook....

Service was sloow.... Food was OK.
Went here for dimsum lunch yesterday with friends... we were a group of 10. Food came so slooowly... we spent 1.5 hours here... probably a good first 45 minutes just waiting for the food. Not extraordinary, but, pretty decent. The place is pretty nice and clean and it was easy to find tables, at least yesterday (Thursday noon-ish).
We ordered A LOT of food and it came to about $90 for the 10 of us.
Not so bad!

Chang Luong Restaurant is a secluded Chinese Restaurant that I have always seen, but never tried out. I was craving some Dim Sun so I decided to give it a try. I ordered the crystal shrimp dumpling, Steamed Shrimp Rice Noodle Rolls, Deep Fried Shrimp Bean Curd Roll, Steamed Sweet Rice in Lotus Leaf, and Honey Walnut Prawns.

Crystal shrimp dumpling is average. Steamed Shrimp Rice Noodle Rolls tasted plain since the soy sauce wasn't soaked long enough. The Deep Fried Shrimp Bean Curd Roll are the best tasting and give lots of shrimp. The Steamed Sweet Rice in Lotus Leaf was better than average and excellent for the price. The Honey Walnut Prawns I wouldn't recommend as they were too dry.

TLDR; This place definitely deserves more traffic as its prices and taste are on par with asian ghetto and its Dim Sum is mostly average with a few exceptional dishes.

I'm a current UC Berkeley undergrad, and I go to Chang Luong about once a month. I really like the Shanghai Spareribs and the Chang Luong Prawns. I have never gotten dim sum, so I can't really speak about that. Food wise, its pretty good!

Negatives: Service is not very personable, it is really dark in there, and also very empty at times.

Overall, a decent Chinese restaurant with above average food, but below average ambiance and environment. Adds up to a 3/5.

This place is the WORST.

Went in to ask for their hours and the...I can't even think of an objective description for her, let's go with "person"...glares at me. Mutha'effin GLARES. For no reason. And curtly tells me they're open right now with the most condescending of tones and immediately turns her back to me and goes back to whatever she was doing before. Because it's obviously more important then tending to the only potential customer in the whole place.

Do yourself, and me, a favor and never give this place your money or time.

As a student, I had been here many times, and I actually really liked their food. For a while, Chang Luong was my number one Chinese restaurant in Berkeley because of their food and because I lived in Southside. Their dishes were cheap and tasted more authentically Chinese than other restaurants such as Lotus House or Mandarin House. They didn't overly salt their dishes or add weird sauces, and it seemed like they did not add MSG. Sadly, the managers did a horrible job at marketing their restaurant and this place just felt... lonely. It seemed like the waitress and the cook are husband and wife and have a little baby. Although I really wish I could give them a good rating, I cannot give them a good rating because... when I walk out of this restaurant I just feel... sad. They never had this HubGrub delivery thing that the other reviews are mentioning, so they must have started the delivery service because they weren't getting enough people to seat in the restaurant. Their English is horrible and they don't interact well with the customers either. 

The two managers must struggle a lot. I mean, they even bring their baby to the restaurant when they work. 

So this restaurant has good, decent Chinese food. But, they don't get enough customers at all. Sometimes it makes me wonder how the hell they stayed in business for so long and if the quality of their food stays fresh. If they knew how to market themselves and interact with customers, they seriously might have become one of Berkeley's better Chinese restaurants. 

So: 4 stars for food and 1 star for service...

CRISPY DUCK - GOLDEN BEARS' GOOD LUCK OMEN

My cousin accuses me of becoming a food snob - which I have to go to some high end places to eat. But I do know a good service when I see one.

During the last week before the ban of foie gras in California, which was the last week of June, I went to Berkeley after work. I wasn't looking for foie gras but was just hungry. Before I went to the Durant food court I noticed a nice regarding this restaurant. Since I have never been on the second floor to eat I decided to try something new.

I was pretty impressed with the service. There was one guy who was the waiter and the cook. That's what you call being multitasked. I ordered a dish I never had before - a whole crispy duck. I've had roast duck and Peking duck many times, but I thought I would give the crispy duck a try. Initially I though it would be a dry, flat, butterfly duck - the ones you see at those Asian markets or eateries. When the crispy duck arrived on my table it was chopped into pieces like a fried chicken and also had that batter. Even the rest of the customers looked at my table to stare in awe of this crispy duck. To my surprise the crispy duck wasn't oily at all. It did not have that fatty content like a roast duck or Peking duck. It was moist and crispy like a fried chicken. Is it the best duck I ever had? No but it was better than any roast duck or Peking duck I've had in any Asian restaurant.

Maybe this is an omen but for this year's football season the Oregon Ducks will play against the Golden Bears at newly renovated Memorial Stadium on November 10th. I'm hoping my review of the delectable crispy duck will give the Golden Bears good luck. If the Golden Bears beat the Ducks this year I will definitely rush the field and after that follow me to head to Chang Luong for some crispy duck to celebrate. If the Bears lose then I will delete my post.

GO BEARS!

Chang Luong may not be the best or authentic Chinese/Hong Kong restaurant in the area (if that's what you're looking for, I'd get myself to San Francisco or Richmond Pacific East Mall); however what it lacks is made up by its convenient location, decent sit-in areas and cheap chinese food for hungry college students. Prices are great and portions are about right. But beware that you will leaving very thirsty because everything tastes like they contain MSG. They also offer pearl milk tea and have signs boasting that they have the best boba in town, but personally I'd rather go to Quickly's or Tea Fever for better drinks. Overall, it's not bad for a quick bite to eat with friends.

My roommate is an international student from China and she was not only refused service but kicked out. She said the waitress seemed to be in a very bad mood and treated them like she was better than them and looking down on them saying something around the lines of "even if you wanted to stay here you can't," referring to them not being U.S. citizens/ residents 

Atrocious service!

At the recommendation of a friend, my husband and I tried this restaurant last Saturday night. The dim sum was okay, but later that night, I felt queasy, couldn't sleep, then realized that I had food poisoning. No vomiting or fever, but the rest of the nasty symptoms, plus a big headache. Took me four days to recuperate, and made me miss an important concert.

My husband was spared, and we think that one of the dim sum I ate must have had a bad shrimp or something. I usually have an iron stomach. Never again will we go to Chang Luong!

I have not even tasted the food yet, but the service was terrible. We called in for delivery. They said it would take 30 minutes. Over an hour later, I had to call to see if our food was coming. They said a few minutes. Finally the deliver gal arrives. I asked why it took and hour when they said 30 minutes. She says, "Do you know how far it is to get here? We don't usually deliver to Albany." So why didn't you tell me that on the phone? Just say it's going to take an hour. She says, "Well, it takes a long time, do you know how much gas costs? Next time it will take a long time." I said, there won't be a next time.

Food is pretty good here. I came here with a friend to try their water boiled beef. It's a Szechuan dish that looks like beef floating in a bowl of chili. Very tasty but try only if you can handle spiciness. See the picture I uploaded for details. Large portions and great taste. Be sure to order rice with it and maybe a lighter dish to even out the spicy taste. The rice was a bit cold and clunky. We ordered a sauteed spinach, a bit too salty for me but it's still good. I just needed to chug a lot of tea. I can say they have real chinese food. They serve dimsum til late. Not the best ones but fulfills my craving. 

Service was ok. They don't have a lot of staff but the place is spacious. We came at the wrong time, they had two large parties and so ordering took long, food came out slow. The waitress was still nice and all. She came to check back on us when they were all caught up with the orders. Tables next to us were left unclean for a while because they were short on staff. Otherwise it was decent. 

I'm just so happy that I found a place close to campus with water boiled beef!

The worst place to get dim sum in Berkeley in my experience.  Maybe its just me as not being Chinese (as my experience at dim sum places is if you can't speak chinese, good luck) and vegetarian its a hard sell.

My friends and I ordered what appeared to be vegetarian dishes on the menu to only find out it had meat or shrimp in the dishes which wasn't really described in the actual name.

The only thing we were able to eat were sweet things and not very filling.  We left the place feeling very hungry.

The service was pretty bad too, although I have to admit that the hedgehog bun was pretty cute.

Of all the places to eat around Telegraph and the campus, I'd say this place is decent.  

We had beef congee and Hong Kong style chow mein.  Both were a little to salty for my tastes.  But compared to other restaurant options there: burritos, pizza, ramen, thai etc., I say go to this restaurant.

I came here with my sister for an afternoon of dim sum. In terms of atmosphere, the place is a tad bit gloomy, but I guess the food makes up for that =). The service was pretty good-- we were seated quickly and the servers were friendly, and I believe the dim sum isn't steamed until you order it.
The two of us ordered 12 containers of dim sum and the total after tax was about $32, but we were really stuffed and we had enough leftovers for dinner. Dim sum here is quite expensive ( $1.95 for the smallest order), but I think it's worth paying for since I only get dim sum everytime I go back home to LA. =D

Taste: 3
Value: 4

I came here a couple times about 1-2 years ago, and I didn't think it was that bad. We ordered from their regular menu, and tried out some of their specials as well. I have not tried their dimsum. Overall, I thought the food wasn't bad, and prices were pretty reasonable. Service could definitely be better though.

Agh! The only thing great about this place is that they serve a good selection of tasty dim sum all the time. But the negatives....

1) The restaurant is not that clean. One time I was here, I saw a dead fly hidden along the wall.
2) The service is ridiculously slow and grumpy.

This place sounds way better than it actually is. Their food tastes like they have used weeks old food and have revived it with the generous use of oil. Even worse, they took over 2 hours to deliver our food. Not to mention I specifically asked for no mushrooms in the comment box and the one thing they used generously, other than oil, were mushrooms. 

Please don't waste your time. I promise you any other delivery is better.

Arguably one of the best Chinese restaurants on the Southside.  The quality of the food is decent except that the water chestnuts taste 10 years old.  Also, the service is not very accommodating, with the hostess and waitstaff often in excessively sour moods with the English language barrier causing some tension.  However, I would recommend trying it as the service on any given day may be better than what I experienced.

I like to get their dim sum for takeout. I am a die hard fan of their peach buns. No joke. I know it's just steam buns with bean filling but I get it everytime and they're really cute to look at. The steamed pork buns are my comfort food staple. I just like getting small portions of food (their dim sum) since I'm not a big eater and so a few orders fill me up pretty well.

3.5

Out of all the restaurants that serve Dim Sum in Berkeley, Chang Luong has the most variety.  It's almost never super busy when I come here (except on a weekday lunch), so service is fairly swift.  My gf and I were seated right away. As we were ordering, one of the cooks came out and viewed our list. 2 minutes later, he brought two of our orders: Sesame Balls and Fried Taro Balls (the best!). Soon after, the waitress reviewed our order. 

The beef rice rolls lacked a little flavor, but it suffices.  The walnut prawns didn't have the best white sauce, but the walnuts were crispy.  Crystal shrimp dumplings were delicious and the spare ribs were tasty, but rather oily. All this, plus rice and tea, for $20. Not bad, not bad.

As for cleanliness...eh, it could be better. But it's college town Berkeley. On my way out, I saw the waitress scoop out water from a big red tub into drinking cups. So that's where my water came from. =(

One sentence wraps it up: You get what cheap stuff you paid for. 

Worst Dim Sum I've ever had. The har gow and sui mai was totally from one of those pre-prepared frozen boxes you get from Ranch 99 or something. Nothing tasted fresh. In fact, most things came out luke warm which means they didn't even re-heat it all the way. If you have a weak stomach and a love for dim sum, STAY AWAY FROM THIS PLACE! It's always really isolated and creepy. There was no one else eating there except me and my friend. It was very uncomfortable having the owners/waiters constantly staring at you. 

But it was super cheap. But I'd rather fork out an extra few bucks to get something much more worth my while.

This place has horrible service. The menu here says the minimum is $20 but when I called the woman told me it was $25. Fine. The delivery takes over an hour despite multiple attempts to confirm my address. Finally, the delivery girl comes and I go outside to look for her because she can't find my house and the person on the phone wrote down the incorrect house number DESPITE my multiple address confirmations. They also forgot my orders of rice. You need rice with Chinese food. Since I paid with a credit card, I was unable to NOT pay for the rice. However, instead of even pretending to be sorry, the delivery girl just stated rudely "there isn't rice with this order" and proceeded to give me a dollar for it.  First, two orders of rice is over a dollar, and second, it's not about the rice.  It's about the slow service, the failure to provide what was ordered, and then acting like it was MY fault that they were late and forgot part of my order.  When I called to talk to someone, the man, "John" hung up on me twice. The food was mediocre and every single person I dealt with along the way was incredibly rude.

My boyfriend and I love this place!  It's very cheap, and we've found that iy compares very well to dim sum in San Francisco.  There is a huge dim sum selection, as well as a substantial regular menu.  They also do hot pots, which look fantastic, but we've never been willing to deviate from the dim sum.  

The dim sum pieces are quite small, which I actually prefer. You get a good filling-to-dough ratio in every bite.  Also, you have room to try more dishes.  And each piece is so reasonably priced, that you can afford to, as well.  The food is definitely made ahead, and then either steamed or fried when you order it.  It comes to the table steaming hot and delicious.  

The one thing that is a little odd about this place, is that it's always pretty empty.  Often, we're the only ones in there.  The couple who runs the place are usually watching TV when they're not actually serving you food.  They are not overly attentive by any stretch of the imagination, but  it's pretty easy to get their attention if you need something.  

It's upstairs and kind of hidden, which is probably why it's not very crowded.  I noticed that some Yelpers found it "creepy" because it's so empty and the "the waitress doesn't smile all that much."  I personally have always found the proprietors to be friendly enough.  And as far as the emptiness goes, I choose to see it as a little secret gem... a quiet oasis in the bustling telegraph neighborhood.  Although it does take some getting used to, it's ell worth it for the cheep, delicious dim sum served all day!

Our usual order is 
Pork Buns (usually 2 orders of 3 pieces each) 
Crystal Shrimp Dumplings
Onion Cake
Sesame Buns
Mango Pudding
Our order usually comes to right around $20, and we are always STUFFED after leaving this place.

The lady server always looks pissed. Is she really upset????

Other than that , they serve mediocre Chinese food. The sauce sometimes is too oily and added way too much MSG...I haven't  tried their dim sum though....

Anyway their food is better than Mandarin House's.

It was a pretty empty restaurant.  Waitress wasn't all that friendly but not atypical of chinese restaurants.  One positive was the xiao long bao (steamed dumplings) that I ordered.  If you order it, you should request some ginger on the side so that you can dip the dumplings into your ginger/soy sauce mix.  
But I also ordered the crystal shrimp dumpling but would not recommend that.  The outside was getting so stuck on the paper underneath that I lost a good chunk of my dumpling to the paper. =(
So the xiao long bao was my highlight but still not sure if it's enough to bring me back there.

I never really go here because Oakland's Chinatown is nearby to get your cheap Chinese food fix. I came here for a friend's birthday dinner yesterday and it was decent.

Ordered: curried beef stew over white rice for $5.50. It was one of their house specials that included rice with the dish. Otherwise you have to pay $1.25 for extra rice, lame! Portions were big and it was surprisingly satisfying. 

Service: It was pretty quick since we were the only party inside. When our tea was refilled, the waiter filled our cups for us, which was nice.

Atmosphere: Lighting was a bit dark. This would be a good place for big groups because there are enough big tables and they don't mind too much if you're loud.

Would I come here again on my own? Probably not. But if a friend wanted to eat here, I wouldn't mind accompanying him/her.

Seriously, how can this place even have average of 3 stars? By far the WORST dim sum I've had in my WHOLE ENTIRE LIFE. I ordered chives dumpling, shrimp dumpling, steamed shanghai dumplings, and chicken feet. All three dumplings were terrible; they were hard, and the fillings were so dry. HOW CAN YOU MESS UP SHRIMP DUMPLINGS?!? It's the most common thing dim sum dishes!! Chicken feet was the worst out of the bunch. Portions were tad small, but I only paid 12 bucks for all... and I didn't even get what I paid for.

The prices are the best things about this place.  However, the age old aphorism of "you get what you pay for" holds true here, and chances are, you'll probably leave disappointed.  Very disappointed.

I've been here many times, for the their 3 dishes for $16.50ish deal, and also for their dim sum.  The dishes that you can choose from aren't necessarily bad, they're just . . . meh (the 8 Precious Tofu in Clay Pot is the only memorable dish that I've had).  Their dim sum, on the other hand, is not good.  At all.  Probably the worst dim sum that I've ever had (I've had my share of bad dim sum in both America and Hong Kong).  They don't use very fresh ingredients, and they over steam their dim sum, resulting in soggy and just overall gross, hardly edible food.

There's really not much going for this place.  I wouldn't come here again, or recommend it to anyone.

Today is the first time I went there, for dim sum, but I don't see myself going there any more. Some of the food was okay, but some tasted like they'd been there for a long time. The service was TERRIBLE!!!! Some other people there and me ended up waiting outside the kitchen to get someone to serve us, and the waitress was throwing a really bad attitude. At the end I had to go find the waitress, waited for her while she ignoring me, and "begged" her to give the check so I could pay and leave. Worst restaurant experience ever!!!!

Solid dim sum restaurant near campus. Well its also the only dim sum place near campus. The food is not too bad for the price and you get a boatload of it. Some how my fatass racked up $20 worth of food, definitely went a little wild with the ordering. Chinatown dim sum is better but this ain't shabby.
I agree with other reviewers that this place is  isolated and creepy. The service is not great, but not bad. The food is pretty good for the money. $20 for 3 dishes + rice

Food:
Pretty decent and at a good price. I really like their eggplant in brown sauce--the texture is perfect. Also a fan of their dim sum--closest dim sum around campus. 

Service:
Their service is the reason why i gave 3 instead of 4 stars. This place is own by a Chinese couple--husband cooks & wife serves. The husband is bearable but the wife ALWAYS has something stuck up her a**....She never greets anyone, never smiles, never utters more than what is essential in placing orders, and overall just extremely unfriendly. When she was pregnant she seemed to become a little friendlier but that all went away after she gave birth. I know most Chinese restaurants are notorious for their horrible beyond horrible service but Chang Luong is by far the worst I've ever experienced. I try to limit my visits here but i have got to give them props for their easily accessible dim sum!

I'm not an avid yelper, but this experienced compelled me to make a note on my phone for the specific purpose of writing this horrible review.   

My brother and I came into this restaurant at noon for dim sum because we decided to try a new place in the Asian ghetto.  When we walked in, it was dead empty and that should have been the first warning sign.  My brother wanted to leave, but I wanted to give this place a chance and help support local businesses.  We ended up waiting 5 minutes in the front before a little toddler walked up from the kitchen.  A lady shortly followed and didnt even acknowledge us.  She just motioned to us to sit at the nearest table and left for the kitchen.  Since no one gave us any service, I walked up to the counter and grabbed two menus to order.  When the lady came back, she told us we could only use one menu..... Seeing as how there were literally zero other customers, I don't know why this would be an issue.  (Also, it's just standard practice to give each customer a menu) 

When she came back 5 minutes later with tea, we placed our order: spareribs, egg tarts, chicken feet, and shrimp dumplings. She then informed me that they were out of spareribs.  I didn't see anything else on the menu that I particularly wanted so I just went ahead and ordered the other three items.  However, the lady started telling me (in an obviously annoyed and angry voice) that we had to order more than 3 items per meal.  I don't know where that requirement came from: it wasn't written on the menus, AND she never told us of this requirement before we ordered.  

At this point, I was getting kind of angry but seeing as how this was small family business (the little toddler in the background certainly brought out my sympathies), I decided to give her my business anyways.  I asked her if she could go ahead and cook our first items while we decide on more items to order.  Then she told my brother and I to leave if we didn't order another item.  (WTF?)  I was really offended and told her all I wanted was to give her my business and try her food.  She then proceeded to yell at my brother and I.  

That was the final straw, and I told her that we would be leaving as she commanded.  The the woman had the amazing brass to ask us to pay $2 for the tea which we didn't needless to say, we just walked out while she cussed us out in the background.  

Disclaimer: I never actually tasted any of the food.  I never got the chance because the lady (who is possibly the owner?) drove us out even when I wanted to be a patron.  The food might be amazing for all I know but given this experience, I'll never go back and I think I'm doing a public service by telling you guys not to as well.

This place serves dimsum at any time.  This is a definite plus if you get a craving.  At the same time, this restaurant is nothing special.  The restaurant is located upstairs, and is quite old and worn.  The service is good, but the place could definitely use some cleaning.  The food was nothing special as well; most of it was forgettable, and nothing stood out.

I had this place deliver last night through Grub Hub.  I have been here a year and tried about 8 different chinese delivery restaurants and they all have been mediocre at the best.

Chang Luong on the other hand was actually great!

They called to tell me they were out of crispy duck and threw in some extra pork to make up for it.  I got the beef fried rice, Mongolian Beef, Peking (I think) Spare Ribs, and pot stickers.  

Everything was great.  The delivery guy was kind and it came in exactly an hour on a Friday night.  

I FINALLY have a great chinese delivery place on stand-by.  Yay!

Yes, the dim sum here is cheap, but it's not even that good. The one time I've been here, I was majorly creeped out. I went on a Saturday morning, and not only was it completely empty and had a musky/dusty odor, the plates and utensils were sticky or oily. I feel like they just need to clean the whole place inside-out. 

The biggest thing was when I was halfway through my meal, I noticed a cardboard box maybe 10 feet away from me shaking. So I kept staring at it, and finally figured out that there was a cat (or some other animal) under it, with a pan over the box so it wouldn't get out. I love cats, but this was troubling considering the friend I was eating with was allergic to cats. 

The only reason I'm giving this place 2 stars is because they had really good turnip cake, and I LOVE turnip cake. Everything else was average, and service was slow.

The dim sum is really oily and the fried food tastes way too fried. If something sounds vegetarian from the description, be sure to ask to make sure, because some things had little random bits of meat (I think for flavor). Also, some of the fried vegetarian things tasted like the oil used to fry them had also been used for fish. Getting something "steamed" is not a guarantee that it will taste healthy.

Food gets one star. I'm adding another because the service was okay.

I've had dim sum like this, in places like this, before.  Tucked away in an upstairs location.  Faded walls and tablecloths (perhaps remedied since my only visit a while ago).  Everything tastes and looks like it was not prepared on site, and was reheated/steamed after being pulled out of a freezer.  Meats in a bamboo steamer, sitting in a rapidly congealing corn starch gravy.  

At least everything is dirt cheap, and you can eat a tonne for about $6 a head.

But.

Not again.

Not again.

So it is true that this place has cheap dim sum and it is available all day. However, it isn't that good. I should have expect it since the place was practically empty when I arrived. Unless you are craving dim sum for whatever reason I would typically avoid this place. I wish it was better but it isn't.

So this is a restaurant that really doesn't deserve 4 stars in terms of quality, service, or atmosphere; however, I give it 4 stars for the same reason as Kimchi Garden: consistently good food that I love. Specifically, the fried rice here is amazing. While I realize that most of this amazingness is due to grease and MSG, I can't resist this restaurant and always find myself coming back. My most favorite thing is the salt fish and chicken fried rice...it is delicious, comforting, and reminds me of home. I honestly can't ask for anything better than that and to me, that's what makes this restaurant a 4-star restaurant.

Well whet should I say.... dim sum was just OK nothing was super good even if we tried a decent number of plates, everything was generic tasting, as it tends to be in not too good but sort of authentic places (as opposed to americanized places were everything is just too salty). However, they have a pretty decent selection of dim sum dishes.
One of us got some sort of tofu from th regular menu and could not finish it because according to him it was terrible. Apparently they just added hot sauce to cold tofu with not so great results....

Anyhow, OK for a cheapish (and not too quick) lunch, but I am sure there are fa better place in the bay area!

Late night dim sum cravings FTW!

Okay, so not quite the best dim sum you'll ever find... but definitely one of the best in the area (I haven't even gotten to try any other dim sum places in Berkeley!), although a bit overpriced.

It's fresh though!... Although service is a bit slow.

Try the Shu Mai and Ha Gao :)

On paper this place seems pretty good:  dimsum served all day, (relatively) fast service, and pretty cheap.

however, these qualities do not make up for the fact that this place is the creepiest place to get food in berkeley. I've eaten here several times, and every time the place was either completely empty or had one other table with people at it. The owners just sit in the front watching loud TV, and they make it seem like they're doing me a HUGE favor by getting up from their show and serving us. Um.. if it's really that much trouble to serve the only customers you've had for the entire afternoon.... then i dont even know.

they dont bring water unless you ask for it, and sometimes it takes longer to get water than it does to get food. This is even more annoying because they put SO much salt in their food. Every time i've eaten here, ive ended up EXTREMELY thirsty later in the day, and feeling overall bad. Im not someone who usually has adverse reactions to chinese food, either. 

If you dont mind unbelievably high levels of sodium, rude staff, and any kind of pleasant ambiance, then this is an okay place to get dimsum all day. But if those things do bother you, then i'd suggest going somewhere else.

Best fried rice. (Get the House Special Fried Rice) its huge. and only $5.95
Huge variety of Dim Sum... like 30-40 options ranging from $2-4.

Discovered this restaurant when I was looking for a place to eat before a an Asian American Film Festival showing at the Pacific Film Archive. 

It's located in a building that's occupied by 4 different restaurants -- Lotus Little House (on the street) and Kimchee Garden (in back at the end of a walkway which may have been a driveway in the past) on the 1st floor and Chang Luong & Cafe Durant on the 2nd floor, which are accessed via a stairway on the left in a stairway (that's hidden from the street) in the walkway towards KimChee Garden.  Chang Luong is located in the back of the building opposite Cafe Durant which is in the front and offers an outdoor patio overlooking Durant Avenue.    

I've eaten at KimChee Garden and Cafe Durant before and they were ok -- not awful or great -- as far as I can remember.  However, KimChee Garden was closed, Lotus House looked too noisy and cramped and didn't feel like having Mexican food and it was raining, which ruled out Cafe Durant.  So, that just left Chang Luong.

The room was empty and looked somewhat dark and dingy -- took a table under the only skylight which offered a little light. 

Was just thinking of getting some BBQ pork won ton or chow mein for a quick bite but was surprised to learn they served dim sum.  So, ordered several basics: shrimp dumplings - ha gow, tripe, foon jow - chicken feet, don tat - custard tarts , cha seiu bao - steamed BBQ pork buns,  see jup pai gwat - pork spare ribs w/black bean sauce and new mai gai - steamed glutenous rice filled w/chicken, chinese sausage and other things wrapped in a lotus leaf. 

Was then surprised that the dim sum was pretty good -- not great but not awful either.  The ha gow was first rate, the tripe and chicken feet were also very good but I would have preferred a little more spice, the pork duns were ok -- not very large and no much filing but tasted ok.  The custard tarts were slightly overcooked but ok.  The pai gwat was a little undercooked and didn't have enough black beans but was ok and the new mai gai was ok too.  

There was a little mix up when I asked for gai lat (chinese mustard) and the foreign-born waitress thought I said "gai lan" -- mustard greens.  Blamed me in Chinese for not speaking clearly but my guest said she heard me ask for it correctly -- it's one of those foreign born towards American born Chinese insults/conflicts that only ABCs will understand.  BTW, got the gai lat but it was very watery and runny -- should have been much thicker.  

Guess the waitress was too pissed w/me to serve us again and another waitress (American born) helped us from then on.   Told her about the misunderstanding and she said the other waitress probably misunderstood because she's from China; speaks Mandarin and only a little Cantonese.    No service problems after that.   

I wouldn't go out of my way to eat at Chang Luong again but would if I'm in the area and am in the mood for dim sum -- and not Mexican, Korean, Indian, hot dogs, hamburgers, pizzas, etc. which are all options only feet away..  The food was fine, even if the decor were a bit lacking.  But, if it's a sunny day and you want to drink some a beer (and eat some Mexican food, which isn't required if you buy a beer) out on the patio, Cafe Durant would be the better choice.

Before you come here, you have to have the right expectations. If you want authentic or gourmet dim sum, it's the wrong place. But if you like to get some tasty, pretty cheap, easy to eat Chinese appetizers/dumplings/whatever, then it's great! If you have a big group it's perfect, since there's always lots of space and some big tables.

I like the potstickers and pork noodle rolls the most. I had a "what the hell" moment and tried the "Golden Bag" too. Not sure what it was, but pretty good. Probably fish paste or something.

I haven't given the entrees many tries, but the hot sour soup is good, war wonton not so much. Didn't give it 5 stars since the service is a bit slow and unfriendly. But if you come in expecting some cheap, pretty good Americanized Dim Sum, then you'll be satisfied.

I was really disappointed when I noticed Shanghai Restaurant had closed, but pleasantly realized that this was one of those "closings" and "grand openings" where the owner is exactly the same, the food is mostly the same, but there's a new restaurant name and slightly redesigned menu.

Anyway, this is the most authentic Chinese food I've been able to find in Berkeley, and I'm grateful there's a place that exists to satiate my periodic xiao long bao cravings. The menu is very extensive, ranging from dim sum selections and all manner of Chinese dishes. Lots of vegetable dishes too, which isn't always easy to find a Chinese restaurants in Berkeley. 

The service is so-so. As far as I can tell, there's only one waitress who runs around trying to keep up with eight tables. However, the restaurant is pretty quiet and it's a nice sit-down place to have a longer dinner. The flatscreen TV also provides quality entertainment, primarily in the form of cheesy Chinese soap operas.

One of the few acceptable sit-down Chinese restaurants near campus. I used to come here after work every Wednesday with a gang of 3-7 guys and the look of horror upon the single lonely waiter every time we walked in was pretty entertaining. That said, service was usually pretty fast. They have a special menu where you can order 3 dishes for around $20 after tax/tip. As long as you stay away from more esoteric options (pig's foot?) you can't go wrong. We especially liked the various braised dishes - large portions and plenty of sauce for your rice. 

I have to give special props to whoever painted this place, not everyone has the balls to paint Chinese-looking archways in neon orange. There will be no doubt where you ate should any pictures be taken...

This place delivers food to your table hella fast ~ so if you're starving, you should come here, you'll have food in front of you before you even order. Okay, well, not really. But yeah, it was amazing; made me wonder how they cooked it so fast...

I had salt and pepper chicken, which was pretty americanized and I wouldn't recommend it. Beef chow fun was excellent (I got it cuz others on yelp suggested it) and not too oily, not too salty. Sweet and sour pork was just the standard same ol' same ol'.

DIM SUM: I only had egg custards and xiao long baos, which were okay but considering how much frozen buns cost at Ranch99, I felt majorly ripped off. Egg custards - well, it's kinda hard to mess these up. They were okay.

Overall... the service wasn't that attentive, our table wasn't even set, we were given tea but no cups, had to grab our own cuz there was no waiter to grab the attention of. We ended up ordering directly with the chef who noticed we were just sitting there with menus. I guess the waiter decided it wasn't his job to wait on the tables. Food was pretty good and uber cheap, I'll go here for Chinese food if I'm in the area, otherwise I'm still gonna go to Richmond (Little Hong Kong on San Pablo).

P.S. Even though I didn't feel the food was that salty or heavy tasting or MSG-filled, I was pretty thirsty in the afternoon following this place... hmm...

3.5 stars, but this time I rounded up because I liked one of the dishes very much.  

Translated, the name of the restaurant means "long dragon".  

Chang Luong is conveniently located about one block from the UC campus in an area of Durant Avenue packed with inexpensive eateries.  It is situated on the second floor of the building where it is housed but its signage is very visible and they have a huge display with photos of their many dim sum choices on the lower level.  The photos are a bit misleading but more on that later.

I had business to conduct on campus so I swung on over for a nice hot lunch recently.  The dining room is very large with ample seating (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_mv3DhRD3L3okFXYjxX_Cg?select=0f97S9LJq_Widm0fJGEGlg), but I found it a bit odd that all the lights were turned off.  There is light coming in from windows located overhead and along the walls, but it was a gray, cloudy afternoon outside so everything inside looked about as dreary as it did outside.

One lady sat at the cashier's station when I walked in and she must have been concentrating on a specific thought because it seemed as though I startled her when I asked for a table for one.  Once I was seated she brought me a regular menu, a dim sum menu and a pot of hot tea.  They serve dim sum here all day along, and they give you a little foldout with check boxes where you can mark off the selections of your choice.  Included on the little fold out are their more popular lunch dishes such as chow meins, chow fun, porridge and a few chef's specialties.  I didn't look at the big regular menu, but if it matches their take out menu it's a huge menu with lots to choose from.

The waitress returned a short time later and asked if I was ready to order.  After careful consideration I selected the Crystal Shrimp Dumpling (Har Gow), the Shanghai Steamed Dumpling (Xiao Long Bao) and a Beef Chow Fun.  I poured myself a cup of hot tea and discovered they use loose leaf tea (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_mv3DhRD3L3okFXYjxX_Cg?select=bQyk_cBHWKAzAqldZ91yVg) here.  I've never been a big fan of tea bags, so this was a nice surprise.

The chef himself brought out my plate of Beef Chow Fun (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_mv3DhRD3L3okFXYjxX_Cg?select=VAh3X1XRa3KqgcPxF-GN9A).  They've replaced the bean sprouts with shredded cabbage, and it looked a bit unfamiliar, but because cabbage is so bland anyway it did nothing to change the flavor of the chow fun.  Just days ago I traded compliments with Yelper Gloria H about our likings for chow fun with huge chunks of rice noodle (fun), and here it was with big clumps of fun.  I loved this selection which tasted fresh with no MSG and no stale cooking oil.  Besides the big clumps of fun the slightly tenderized beef had that nice seared texture you often get from a hot wok where the edges of the beef were fried up nearly crispy.  I will order this dish again.

The dim sum came out separately as each were probably steamed separately.  I'm assuming shrimp stays in the steamer for less time than pork.  In looking at the photos posted on their lower level display as well as photos posted by previous Yelpers the size of the dim sum has really taken a hit.  The portions I got were little miniatures compared to the photos I had seen prior to my visit.

Both the Crystal Shrimp Dumplings and the Shanghai Steamed Dumplings are listed as "Medium Plates" and go for $2.60 for four pieces.  The Crystal Shrimp Dumplings (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_mv3DhRD3L3okFXYjxX_Cg?select=XxNuHLC3PxT_1viXipjSBQ) were okay in taste with just a bit of MSG in its flavoring.  The shrimp was nice and firm but the ratio of chopped bamboo to shrimp fell in favor of the bamboo which were hard and tough.  I didn't like the skin either which had good elasticity but was thick and gummy.  The miniature Shanghai Steamed Dumplings (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/_mv3DhRD3L3okFXYjxX_Cg?select=GSPTPT7TzDTBBJ_yj_j-Tg) had a solid pork filling and a nice burst of hot broth inside.  I could taste the faintest hint of ginger in the pork.  I didn't detect any MSG in these.  The failing point was once again the skin though which was thick and doughy.

The chef and the waitress don't smile too much, but they are efficient in their work.  If you're near the campus and have a longing for good Chinese food, Chang Luong just might be what you're looking for.  It's inexpensive for the most part, and I'll certainly be back.

I need to come back here for the dimsum to do a more thorough assessment, but I can tell you that Chang Luong is a much nicer place to sit down and eat compared to its close-by counterparts in the Asian ghetto. It's quiet and spacious.

Ironically, I just got take-out. House special chow fun ($7). The food took a while, considering that there were few patrons there. It was alright--really full of assorted yummy vegetables, which I appreciated, and also a good variety of tasty meat. Calamari, shrimp, chicken, beef, bbq pork. The chow fun itself, however, was a bit disappointing. It was not firm and chewy the way I like it, but rather...blah. They also gave me only a small portion of noodles. I could finish it in one sitting, which sucks--when I get Chinese take-out I always hope that I can stretch it to another meal or at least half. (I'm a student!)

Chang Luong does have some pretty sweet looking deals though. Choose from a LARGE variety of dishes, 3 for $16. They also had a few different pearl milk teas if you like that!

I guess the reason I haven't done dimsum here is because the experience is sooo much more fun when there are waiters pushing around carts, and you can just point to what you want. At Chang Luong you have to order items. Berkeley pretty much fails at dimsum...

This place is just pure fun. It's the only traditional-feel Chinese restaurant in the area, and you can order dimsum pretty much anytime it is open. There's nothing like eating tripe, fried taro, steamed spareribs, and chive dumplings late into the night to prove that you've been a naughty kid.

In general, the dishes hover around acceptable. Nothing around is going to help conjure up images of China and the food can get pretty heavy, but experiment around and you can get a feel for the stronger dishes relatively quickly.

The cashier/hostess always looks as grim as Steven Seagal, but I guess if anyone would look like that  if they had to endure the finicky and nitpicky patrons that often frequent the UC campus eateries. 

The food is authentically Chinese enough, although they don't have the slightest clue how to make Peking Duck. When I see the item on the menu read: 11 dollars for half a duck, then I expect half a duck on my plate. Not half a Peking-style duck-skin with about half an ounce of duck meat. 

So in conclusion, if you're looking for cheap Chinese food that's better than whatever they have at Mandarin Garden, go to Chang Luong. If you're looking for Peking Duck, do yourself a favor and trek the extra few blocks to Great China on Allston.

Taking it to 3.5 

Their dim sum still rocks my socks. But the still after how long we haven't been here, there is still no one in the place (i.e. patrons). And we were told one of the buns we ordered would take to long when we were craving AKA "get the hell out, you're done". 

Good food, not so good service. Oh well, I'll keep coming back regardless! So yummy with the funny :D

I've never come here for dinner, only dim sum.

I would say this is a pretty decent alternative if you can't make it over to Oakland or SF for really good dim sum.  It's cheap and they serve your food very fast.  

The dim sum is just ok.  By ok, I mean it tastes like something I could buy at 99 Ranch and reheat.  They serve dim sum all day so I suspect that's probably what they do.  They're fried items taste fresher but I think that has more to do with the nature of it's cooking process more than any sort of quality.  Their dishes are cheap but small.  Their baos are TINY!  Order two if you have three or more people.

If you're desperate, Chang Luong will do.  But if you can, drive out to SF.  Or better yet, BART it.  If you're a UCB student, I'd highly recommend putting that class pass to use and taking the 51 to Oakland Chinatown.

Okay okay, I know that the food quality is not all that great here but I give them credit because it's always FRESH!

My problem with a lot of dim sum places is that the food in the carts gets stale and isn't always served at its peak. Luckily for Chang Luong, they don't cook any of the dim sum until you order it. So although it may take a little longer for your food to come out, it's always hot and fresh which is why I eat here regularly.

Recommendation:
- SHUI MAI
- BEEF RICE NOODLE WRAP
- BEEF BALL

ENJOY!

Let's start with the good: free delivery, with a minimum order of $25. convenient ordering through GrubHub.

Unfortunately, the bad was BAD!
I should've known better than to order from a place in the main college area, but was attracted to the free delivery, decent prices, and seemingly authentic menu. Also, I've loved the food from Sun Hong Kong, which is also in the college hood. Too bad it's an $8 delivery fee at SHK!

I got: spicy beef chow fun, sauteed snow peas, salt and pepper pork chops, and chicken wings. In hindsight, I realize the menu is not cantonese-oriented, and more szechuan. Makes sense that the spicy beef chow fun was the most palatable item. 

Other than that, everything was greasy, disgustingly battered, and I could practically taste how dirty the kitchen might be. Forget eating leftovers for a few more meals - that was $28 worth of garbage. With the poor quality of everything, I can only suppose that the dim sum menu is composed of cheap frozen food that is steamed back to life for service.

I grew up eating dim sum and was really craving some and this was the only place in the area so decided to check it out.  Probably wont ever go again.  I can tell that a lot of the buns and egg tart (dan tat) are microwaved.  The egg tarts were served in foil and were cold in the middle but really, really hot on the foil.  I've had shiu mai there that tasted microwaved, too.  The food was cheap, but I'd rather pay to not eat their food.  Bad experience overall.  It's unfortunate that there's not much good dim sum in Berkeley.  Go to Oakland or SF to get the real stuff.

SHK had its run, but Chang Luong always delivers. This is really the most acceptable you can get on the Southside area for Chinese food without being pounded by grease and MSG (SHK). While SHK can't get beat for the price it offers at happy hours and what not, if you care about your health, you will not eat there and give some patronage to Chang Luong.

As always, it's understaffed and people are running around frantically, but the food gets to you in a timely manner. The food honestly tastes better than anything coming out of SHK to me because I don't get sluggish after eating. Try it out for yourself and see! They make a mean beef with bitter melon here.

chang luong doesn't just serve dim sum though it seems like it(from the posters). no cart ladies here.  they give you a checklist and the dim sum comes out  every five minutes.

dim sum review only pricing (s)1.95, (m)2.60, (l)  3.50
samplings
-steamed spareribs: mosty bones, gristle and fat accompanied by tender pieces of tasteless pork.
-b.b.q  buns(3) small  buns with semidry bbq within.
-beef balls(3) small  tender beef balls, so small they look like test.....
-shrimp in rice roll: large portion with large crunchy tastleless shrimp
-siu mai(4)  not even bitesize, msg enhanced.
-tea:gratis

leftovers
-pluckered msg afterstate
-only one guy in the kitchen, plus one waitress outside
--dim sum may have made offsite (commercially)
. heated up on kitchen.
-dim sum portions  very small except for shrimp crepe
-an hour later  had a craving for good dim sum but still sleepy from my lunch encounter.
-service not a problem, few patrons.

Whoever thought of this concept is pretty awesome. Picture your typical university town cafe, what do you see? You probably see a bunch of snotty undergraduates who think they're smarter than they really are sipping on syrupy lattes pretending to read books for their classes. You also probably see grad students that are trying to find jobs that don't exist. The walls are probably filled with classics that no one has touched or bothered to get rid of because they bring something extra to the decor. Well, Musical Offering Cafe brings that vision to life sans the fake snobs. 

Musical Offering Cafe is a fantastic little book store that also sells some cool classical music CDs. The restaurant looks like it was just added on but it's definitely awesome. I love just sitting in the middle of a bookstore being able to eat my overpriced sandwich, seriously! The sandwiches and salads rock. The cafe is basically typical Berkeley: it has that intelligent snobby air to it whether it is earned or not and everything is overpriced to make you feel good about buying local and organic!

I'm not a huge fan of the coffee here, but the ambience is amazing.  And honestly, if you come to a coffee shop for something other than a latte to-go, 50% of the appeal is its personality.  They play classical music and have a music section in the back of their store.  Also there are a decent number of chairs and tables--I saw several people studying or reading.  The staff was nice and friendly too, asking me if I wanted anything as soon as I walked in.  

Overall:  coffee = meh, ambience = cute.

This place has a sprinkle of pretentiousness to it, but the staff is friendly, the environment is social without being too loud and the food is one of the better places around the UC Berkeley campus.  

The simplest way to break down the cafe situation along Bancroft is...Strada's for the undergraduates...Milano's for upper-classmen and grad students (GSI/TA)...Musical Offering is for professors and grad students.

Back to the content.  I like this place because everything is fresh and home-made here. If you get there around 8:30am, the coffee cake is right out of the oven and the best around. Their lunches are pretty good and delicious, but the price will be $7-9 as opposed to $5-7 you might get at the other cafes. Also, I like their strawberry agua fresca, which isn't overly sweet like Cancun...and their Herbal Iced Tea.  Who else has that around here? The coffee is standard.

Anyhow, if you like this place, you'll end up becoming a regular and abandoning all other Cafes.

Kind of lame.  Everything is overpriced.  Their "dinners" taste good, but are really skimpy - $10 to $14 for 2 oz of meat, 5 pieces of lettuce, and some veggie shavings?  Uh, overpriced.  

Cookies are always stale.  

Chairs and tables are beat up and uncomfortable, and I always feel as if they are dirty.  They are really funky, and not in the good way.  In the winter it is too cold, in the summer, it is way too hot.  (why the hell doesn't anyone in Berkeley have AC?!)

Pass.

Lovely. - 8/2/06

I'm going to have to give an update on this place. Since August last year, the organization where I work moved into an office next door. The Musical Offering has become my M.O. (heh heh heh) and I need to add to the one word review I gave before. Here's a day in the life at the Musical Offering Cafe.

Let's begin with the morning time: their coffee is good and cheap! A real find in Berkeley... a latte or cappucino is 2 bucks, and they have skim milk if you're watching your waistline, or just saving the calories for something better. Speaking of something better, some of the morning baked goods make my very exclusive list of "worth it" - top of the list is the raisin scone. The blueberry muffin is somewhat dry, and I haven't tried anything else. No need, because the scone satisfies.

Next let's move to mid-morning coffee break. The office work is getting tedious, you and your co-worker might decide it's time for a trip next door to the M.O. to pick up whatever you didn't have for breakfast that morning or the morning before. Or perhaps you just decide to drop in to visit with their gorgeous staff (as advertised outside on their billboard - in truth, they deliver).

Lunchtime. Do you feel like soup, salad, sandwich, or some combination? Good - the M.O. is there for you. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND the tuna nicoise salad, the hot chicken on foccacia, or the butternut squash soup. Other dishes are good too - it just depends on what you're in the mood for. The herbal iced tea is delicious.

And it's 2:02pm, didn't you just take a lunch break? But you're still hungry. Or are you just bored? Be honest with yourself.

Once you decide to take the plunge to go back yet another time, you won't be sorry. I can say with confidence that there isn't a better brownie in Berkeley than the "Amazingly Yummy Brownie" at Musical Offering: crisp on the outside, chewy on the inside, chocolate that goes straight to your head. The ginger snap is also excellent - similarly crisp on the outside/chewy on the inside goodness.

Do enjoy! - 1/18/07
I took a friend here for lunch the other day and we had the most delicious black bean soup and brie/roast veggie sandwich. Reasonable prices and pleasant service. No wonder it's so busy.

I sometimes drop in for coffee and always end up checking the CD that's playing from the music store.  Ask the very knowledgeable man.  I've also had lunch and dinner there, both really good (they will run out of the special, as it is usually great and in high demand).

horrible cafe and will never set foot in there....

the bad: patrons are stuffy. mostly stuck up campus folks. and the wait staff is even worse.
the ugly: i went in there and was the only man of color in the place. and on the berkeley campus/surrounding establishments that faculty/students frequent for coffee, this is not a big deal... it's expected.  but there were at least 3 other people in line (behind me) to order ... i was COMPLETELY invisibilized! I waited patiently, but I was about to have a microagression. So much for a racially tolerant Berkeley... and this cafe takes the cake for needing a diversity training. sad!

the coffee is decent, but with the attitude and unwelcoming atmosphere, for the musical offering... no thanks... what a sour note... and waste of space on a prime spot on bancroft avenue... i think this place needs to get boycotted.

Delightful environment with a classical music store occupying the back half of the store. Good loose leaf tea comes in little teapots. Drinks and baked goods reasonably priced, and appeared reasonably tasty. Employees are nice and friendly.

Pleasant study spot, but no free wifi accessible if you're not a Berkeley student.

Great place to come to after a long day of classes. The ambiance is soothing, warm, and intimate. The cafe closes a bit too early to make it an awesome study spot, but at least when it is open it's considerably less crowded than some of the other cafes around. 

Haven't tried the food, but the coffee was good and cheap.
If you want cheap, this is the wrong place to go. If you want high quality, delicious food and excellent coffee, it's the *only* place (anywhere near campus.)

I truely love this place. I come here for lunch at least once a week, because it is the only place in Berkeley I have found that serves good sandwiches. I can recommend the Tuna Melt, it is absolutely amazing. It is very much like a European style sandwich place, which means the sandwiches are not packed with mayonaisse and 10 layers of cheese, instead they set on a good quality bread and reasonable amounts and combination of toppings. The service is always friendly. Only downside is that the bathroom is not in the cafe itself, but in the bookstore next door.

attractive staff...great classical djs...what's with the carpet?...good light, grand windows...tapas menu is new every week and the sandwiches are radical, the meat tastes like it's marinated for days...what's with the lunch lady who asks you to leave if you only have a biscotti and cappuccino? if it's that big of a deal, sitting area perchance as opposed to a music store with more space than it's good for...if you're a luncher, regular roasted red bell pepper and brie sandwich with balsamic instead of pesto, wow nelly...also, support university press books next door--books you can't find anywhere else, and part of a co-op with the cafe and classical cd shop...support local, even if there is a neurotic, socially awkward, maybe endearing if you knew her lady that's greedy for tables during the lunch hour.

Classical music

Cappuccinos

Cal professors

Class act.

Very relaxing  café! It has that warm and cozy feel to it!

The coffee is really good and I enjoy the amazing classical music that is played here.

...also the vinyl collection here is out of this world...Wow!!!!!!!

Ok, next time I come here, I pledge to get only a salad, which looks to be huge in portion.

Instead, today I ordered a Mexican special, the roasted poblano peppers stuffed with queso fresco, dipped in egg batter, and served with a spicy tomato salsa with jasmine rice and green peas, black beans, and two warm tortillas.

Translation: a tiny TINY bowl with ONE stuffed pepper and NO black beans.  The taste also wasn't extraordinary enough to make up for the absolute price gouge at $10 bucks.

In the end, I felt so unsatisfied I went next door (Espress Experience) to have shaved ice.

I LOVE this place. I come in really frequently for lunch or coffee and a snack. The staff is super friendly. The food is so fresh, healthy and delicious. All of the drinks are delicious too. I love the nicoise salad, the cobb salad, and the soup of the day! The herbal iced tea and strawberry aqua fresca are wonderful too. I generally spend 7-14 dollars when I come in. It's a really good value for how fresh and healthy it is.

My friend suggested we go here and I was very confused by the name. I really like this place and the concept. It reminds of something that would be in Boston or Western Mass - like Amherst/Northampton. Their scones are fresh, sandwich choices exciting (like a pulled pork cuban with cabbage), excellent drinks (like iced herbal tea) and my butternut squash/sausage soup was very very good. Don't think that they only have the food on their online menu, because they have lots of daily specials. Next time I want the roasted beet salad.

One issue - why don't they play classical music?

Chef Erick Balbuena is not only a chef with tremendous talent, but he is also a community contributor. Erick volunteers his talents twice a year to prepare food for Berkeley Food and Housing Project (www.bfhp.org), the East Bay's largest homeless service provider located down the street.

Food was... not as described on the menu. Meats were very rare. Portions were tiny and a bit overpriced. I'd say that the best deal would be the sandwiches, which are at once cheaper and larger than the other things on the menu; plus it garnered appraise from my friend. Drinks are subpar... it seems that the large collection of torani was just for show (either that or the person that made my italian soda was being stingy with the syrups). At least we got to browse for music while we waited for our food. Atmosphere was ambient, and the music did contribute nicely to the overall feel of the place. I think they do requests for what songs you would like to hear XD. Really gives a nice, small, italian vibe.

Sigh, I'm going to miss this place once I graduate.

Atmosphere: I love the ambiance of the place. Granted, it is a little small and can get crowded during lunch hours, but I love the decor and the fact that there is a CD shop and books next door. 

Food: I've had their Hot Turkey Sandwich before, and it was delicious. While I was with my friend eating lunch, we overheard this guy telling a friend that "the eggplant sandwich was to die for." Oh really, you say? Challenge accepted.

The next time I went I made sure to order it. After the first bite, I was like "alright, this is pretty good." After the last bite, I wanted to shed a tear for the fact that it came to an end. IT IS SUCH  A DELICIOUS SANDWICH. If you like eggplant, ciabatta, or balsamic vinegar at all, you will love this sandwich -it's light and tastes like heaven (or what I imagine heaven to taste like...if it were edible) Their brownies are also pretty yummy, and their Iced Soy Chai Lattes are sweet and great on a nice warm day. The prices here can get a bit on the high side though -one sandwich is about $9ish dollars; it's a good thing they're so delicious!

Service: The people that work here are so friendly! Love it.

I suggest you try it if you haven't yet. I'm pretty sure you've walked by it on the way to or from class, so take one day to actually step in.

Overall - 4.5* (Food - 4, Service - 0.5)

Came here today for a quick lunch with some friends, and I must say, this is currently my favorite restaurant at Berkeley! Rather than going to the same-old, dirty and crowded Asian ghetto for lunch, this place is definitely worth the experience because you get the equivalent of fine dining with just under $10. Besides, what could go wrong with some classical music? 

I ordered the Hot Chicken on Focaccia as recommended by most Yelpers. It was amazing. The melted cheese and warm, toasted focaccia bread with tender chicken truly complemented well with one another. My friends got the pepper and melted brie sandwich with pesto on baguette, and it was equally amazing. I am not a big fan of red pepper, but the combination of roasted pepper with pesto and seasoning gave a surprisingly delicious outcome. 

Lastly, the service at the restaurant was very nice. The waitresses were super friendly and accomodating. The only downside was that we had to wait for about 20 min for our sandwich. 

Overall, I will definitely come here again! Next time, I want to try fine dining dinners.

I'd never been in here until I had to meet with a GSI about one of my essays.  While I was waiting for my GSI i decided to get an apple and walnut salad with feta cheese. Let me just say, it was AMAZING. I could not stop eating it. The dressing wasn't too heavy and was just PERFECT. Though the salad was a bit pricey I think it was worth it :).

If you like classical music, or at least like to pretend that you do for the benefit of your friends, then this very slightly overpriced cafe might be for you. It's got a good atmosphere and isn't too loud. If you like studying in cafes (I do not), it's probably a good choice. 

As far as actually eating and drinking - the coffee and salads are good, with nice bitter greens, and the hot sandwiches are tasteful and not too greasy. Larger groups are possible around lunchtime.

I haven't tried much, but I will say this:

blueberry muffin + a cup of coffee = fantastic way to start the day. 

I'm generally a tea drinker (I've had theirs, it's standard), and I've tried both the apricot and raisin scones - they are pretty good, but sometimes the fruit pieces get burnt, which sort of takes away from the experience. Plus, the tea-scone combo is more expensive. 

The coffee is good, nothing special (I won't pretend to be an expert) but good - the blueberry muffin is delicious. De-licious. So, treat your wallet and your tastebuds... you won't regret it.

you know what is awesome about this place ... you can run over here during intermission from Cal Performances - and get cookies with no line!!! Then run back (and make sure you use the bathroom in the student union bldg b/c the lines are crazy at zellerbach) ... & have your cookies with no stress.

;)

I'm a big fan of classical music and this cafe is a perfect spot to get some studying done in a soothing atmosphere. It is half restaurant and half record store; there isn't a lot of seating because some of the bigger tables are reserved ahead of time. Sometimes the music is played too loudly though so if you reaaaaally don't enjoy classical music, don't bother..

Nonetheless, there are less students and tourists that visit here since it is a bit out of the way from Telegraph Ave. Portions are somewhat smaller than the price that you paid for. Maybe I'm just not the right person to be judging what they make, but my first impressions after visiting here for lunch seemed like they were trying to make a "high class, fancy, it-looks-better-than-it-tastes-on-white-plates" kind of menu. The food isn't fantastic, now I just go for the coffee and ambience.

Also, the bathrooms are next door in the bookstore ("University Press Books: Ten Thousand Minds on Fire" - which is a GREAT bookstore/is this an advertising scheme? To have me walk through shelves of wonderful literature just to go to the restroom?) - so it's kind of a pain.

But back the the record store... 10% discount on a musician's birthday and their selections in the World Music section is worth coming back for.
The Hot Chicken on Focaccia is bomb.

cute cafe, nice ppl, food is good, a bit expensive to me, but i guess its worth it
sometimes they have tapas, never been there when they do, but my friend said they are very yummy but quite expensive
the agua fresca, some strawberry drink, very good, try that for sure
the desserts are good too. i had a pumpkin cake and my friend had the carmel creme (flan looking thing) and it was delicious
the music is nice and the atmosphere is calming
good place to read, chat w/ ppl, grab lunch
Great food. Classical music - even live music on Sunday afternoons. Music store. Great atmosphere across the street from campus.

The ambience of this cafe is quite nice, and the food and coffee are always very good.  The creativity on the menu is refreshing, especially if you're not in the mood for the same old breakfast/lunch options around the campus area.

That said, the atmosphere tends to be a little pretentious and at times stifling with all the rules about separate hours for sitting and drinking coffee, hours for eating lunch, hours for eating tapas, hours for eating dinner, etc.  I often find it stressful to mentally plan coffee breaks there because inevitably there will be some restriction on how long I can sit there before a lunch customer will take priority for my seat.  I'm not sure how I feel about being asked to leave at 11:30 after I've been sitting enjoying coffee reading for some time.  I suppose they know how to run their business better than I do, but I think it's in poor taste to actually ask people to leave once they're already seated and settled.  Personally I think the requests to leave are excessive-- you usually feel the pressure to get out of there once the staff starts giving you looks that clearly indicate, "What are you still doing here, coffee-loiterer?"

Regardless of all the eating-in rules, I give this place 4 stars because the food and coffee are a cut above, and it's usually a fairly pleasant experience.  Also I think the owner is a very friendly and warm person (if I'm right in thinking she is the elderly woman with gray curly hair).

I think I may have found a new "go-to" place on the southside of campus. Most of my studying takes place on the northside or on shattuck, but I thought I'd stop into The Musical Offering since I was in the neighborhood (and based on a friend's recommendation)... and I really like it.

It's not as quiet as I was expecting, but the high ceilings and lack of undergrads make it appealing nonetheless. On top of that, they have good coffee... which is surprisingly difficult to find in these parts. I have yet to try the food, but from looking around, they definitely look like things I would consider eating. (semi-appealing food is also generally lacking from cafes in these parts.)

On top of that, I just feel smarter sitting in here. I don't know anything about classical music, but if someone saw me in here, they might think twice... (even if they'd be wrong)

The cafe to go to on the Southside if you want a grown-up, peaceful place with good coffee and baked goods and--of course--classical music playing in the background. (The real food looks good, too, but I have yet to sample it.) Between 12 and 2, you can't hold up a table with just coffee, but after that, you can take your time.
"Their music selection restores my faith in humanity."

Not a whole lot of vegetarian options here if you're looking for a substantial lunch- Fortunately for me the daily special was a meat-free quiche; and actually my friend was able to get a cheese and avocado sandwich (it's not on the menu).  It's a little more fancy/classy (read: large square plate with artfully arranged small-ish portions) than I usually go for. Also I'm not convinced that the iced coffee was at all caffeinated..?

I didn't go into the music store looking part, but the ambiance of the cafe part was nice, if a little crowded.  My (admittedly rather large) group sat at a table that had a reserved sign for 2 hrs later

Such a great place for everything!

I come here to study a lot because it's close to my house and they play GREAT music.  I use the tables by the windows even though it says reserved for groups of 5 or more.  Normally theere are already people using those tables to study so I'll just join them.  Voila - 5 or more!

There's great natural light in the front.  It's not too crowded.  They have a HUGE selection of music which I haven't had the chance to take advantage of.  They also give a discount if you by a composer's music on his birthday!

The food is always pretty good.  I've had two panini's that were great.  I've also had their bakery stuff and that was good too.

The service is always really friendly and all smiles.  I've never been asked to move so that's good....
Tastiest and healthiest food in town, lovely atmosphere. They even have wonderful live music!

An excellent place to go study if you don't need a huge amount of table space.  Used to come here to get reading done and I was always really productive.  On a couple of occasions I've seen musical groups performing here and they're really fantastic.  Otherwise, they're playing relaxing classical/romantic music.  I always get loose leaf tea - $2 is a bit steep, but you get free hot water refills and the ambiance is more than worth.  Would like to come again and try other drinks out but I always find the tea to be most conducive to getting work done.  Would really love to come for brunch/lunch though.  Seems like the perfect place for a weekend brunch.

Mmmm....this little cafe is a carb lover's dream come true!  If you ever go, make it a priority to get anything with bread which isn't really hard to do in a cafe.  I've heard some negatives about the service, but it redeems itself with the quality of food they serve.  It is a bit pricey for the quantity you get which is why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.  This place won't fall into my daily lunch line up because we're in a recession folks!  However, I could see myself craving the food once in awhile.

The Good:
+  Moist Peruvian Cornbread - and yes, they called it "MOIST" and they meant it!  Moist, not too sweet, and little bits of corn make the perfect cornbread.  It's heavy because I think they use cream to make this thing so be prepared to take some home or give it to the boyfriend (aka. your own, personal human garbage disposal) to finish it off.
+  Hot Chicken on Focaccia - chicken, cheese, garlic aioli, and tomatoes smothered between soft focaccia, courtesy of the Acme Bread Company (I know this because you can see the logo on their bread bags in the open kitchen).  It's a pretty minimal sandwich.  Sorry health nuts but there's no romaine lettuce, sprouts, pickles, or anything with dark, vibrant colors.  BUT that's the great thing about this sandwich because it's amazing without even trying hard!  It doesn't need the add-ons...it's simple and oh so good to the last bite.

The Bad:
-  The Tea - It's nice looking on display by the register, but don't get sucked in!  The teas were lightly flavored but at $1.50-$2.00 a small glass, I expected more flavor.  I've probably gotten more enjoyment out of a Lipton tea bag.

I've been here on a handful of occasions now and every one of them has been lovely.

The place gets a little busy during lunch but the staff has always been friendly in trying to accommodate sharing of large tables, etc.. 

The food rocks! Music is nice and the drinks have been wonderful too.

Great ambiance, very classy and unlike other campus cafes filled with stressed out students cramming for exams.
