A cafe to go to for a leisure environment in which to read the paper or a great book, not to cover the coffee tables with textbooks.  Their is great service as well, very polite/ attentive baristas.

I could give a rat's fig sandwidge about the cafe, but the music store is very find indeed, with lots of albums to find. I have gone in with lists and found many of the items I was looking for, plus some others. The fellow running the store is very helpful.  Reminds me of a very small version of the wonderful Tower Classical Annex once in San Francisco.

Great ambiance and hot sandwiches. I recommend the tuna melt - crusty bread with a bit of salad on the side... good place to come and chat with friends. A bit slow on the service (the wait was extraordinarily long for a hot sandwich), but not too expensive and good quality food.

Caveat: I work here.... but I work here because I heart this cafe, its food, and all the staff!

My recommendations:
HOT SANDWICH: Roasted Eggplant and Carmelized Onion... this is the only way I will eat eggplant.
COLD SANDWICH: Smoked Turkey and Apple... ADD Avocado... such a refreshing combo... and all the sandwiches are made with Acme baguette so you know it will be delish!
SALAD: Cobb... the cafe uses a lot of organic produce and much of it comes from Berkeley Bowl.. you can taste the healthy goodness
DRINK: Lemonade or Orange Juice... the cafe juices it's own citrus juices every morning (believe me, I do much of the juicing!)

Tip: Lunch hour is usually packed... so if you want to relax and do some leisurely studying... come in the morning or late afternoon!

Cheers!

Everyone who comes here is old! But that's ok, it makes me feel like I've been let in on a secret kept by professors and grad students. (Although I think the secret is that the lunches at MOC cost a few dollars more than at other places.) The soups and sandwiches here are delicious -- I recently got cold tomato soup and turkey with apple on a sweet baguette...mmm... The pastries, coffee, and juices are also tasty! There's a classical music store in the back, but I've never seen anyone buy anything there. I took off a star for a pretty average cookie I had once, and one time this really sour lemonade. More like lemon-water...not recommended.

My only regret about Musical Offering is that I did not come here before my last semester at Cal.

Perhaps it took me so long to warm up to the place because of two previous negative experiences.

The first was meeting an unpleasant GSI for his office hours here.  The tea was good, but he was an asshole (although I later found out he was an asshole to everyone) and associated negative feelings with this place.

The second time was a friend and my attempt to just get a bagel and coffee at the lunch time rush and were told we could not sit, since the tables were reserved for meal eaters.  The guy was polite enough, but the fact that I was denied a place to sit, sullied my view for quite some time.

I have finally found the positives of this location, which in my opinion outweigh any negatives.

This semester while slaving away at a thesis, I found myself at Musical Offering more and more often for the following reasons (mind you I usually go here in the late afternoon/evenings after the lunch crowd rush when there are numerous tables to choose from):

1. The food is delicious.  
When I first started coming here I went on a sandwich excursion trying a new one each week.  Granted given the time that I frequent the restaurant (after lunch) the specials are usually sold out, but the regular menu is certainly nothing to be disappointed with.  Two of my favorites is the turkey with apple sandwich (the honey mustard!) and my absolute number one: eggplant and caramelized onions.  The combination of flavors is really delectable and I've never had a bad one.

2.  The classical music is so soothing.
Sometimes going to other cafes where various music types are played (jazz or contemporary) it can become daunting and busy.  Coming to Musical Offering is like taking a sigh of relief getting to listen to some delicious opera or a requiem of Mozart.  It is really conducive to producing good work and I find that I get a lot more of my reading/writing done when enjoying the tunes from the store.  The vibe of this cafe overall is just really mellow and nice.

3.  The people are nice.
It took a while for the people behind the counter to warm up to me, but they have always been polite and cordial with me.  I get along most with the wait-staff who bring your sandwiches (that stocky guy, WHAT A BABE!) and they're always courteous about taking my plate once I've finished.

4.  The store is extensive and the staff knowledgable.
The main gal who works in the store picks the best pieces to play and is really great to talk to about works of music or if there's a piece I want to buy, but not sure which conductor or orchestra is best.  They're really into talking about music and know what they're talking about.

A couple of things to note, although not necessarily negatives:
-The prices are notable.  Not out of the question expensive, but a little on the hefty side considering the portions.  The portions are reasonable, but don't come here planning on eating a lot.  A friend of mine once ordered two sandwiches because he was so hungry and it put a bit of a dent in his wallet (but they're good! and he enjoyed both sandwiches).
-The bathroom is not in the store, but next door at the book store, which is awkward in part, especially because sometimes I get distracted looking at books to and from using the facilities.

Overall though this is a gem of a place and I'm so glad that I finally gave it a chance.  Would most certainly recommend.

Best cafe in Berkeley!

This place is my little indulgence-spot. I come here when I really don't need to accomplish too much reading. That way I can enjoy my extra rich, whip-creamed, hot mocha. Mmm. Honestly, the food and coffee is great (a bit pricey, though) and the service is wonderful. You'll feel smart and sophisticated with all the good music and such.

great place for coffee and for classical music fans. Every once in a while they have actual musicians playing in the cafe, which I absolutely love. I haven't been there in awhile, I need to go back and drift away to the sound of violin strings!

Wish I could do a 2.5 stars here, but I'll round up. You literally cannot beat the location-- it's right across the street from campus near zellerbauch, bears lair, sproul, and the gym. The food is nothing special, but it's pretty good. The drinks, I will admit, are pretty damn good. Try the hazlenut mocha if you're not on a diet. The classical music playing (the cafe is also a classical music store in the back) adds a great ambiance to the place. 

All this being said, it's a terrible place to study as there is only one power outlet in the whole place, the tables are tiny and wobbly, and you'll have to rely on the campus wireless for internet. The staff are pretty stand offish, but hey they are baristas and that job has a lot of prestige. All in all, this is a great place to grab coffee and a snack with friends, but not to study or hang out.

OMG I love this place, how have I not reviewed it yet?

First off, they have great coffee and tea if you just need to stop someplace to get caffeine. The pastry selection is small, but they're all really good -- particularly the cornbread and the brownie. 

And then there's lunch and dinner! Soups, salads, and sandwiches -- all are AWESOME. They'll happily pack anything off the menu to go, which is great when I'm working a show in Zellerbach and only have a little time to run out and grab something. 

No real table service. You order at the counter and they'll bring your food to you when it's ready. Fine by me, and there's never a delay. 

Best part about this place is that the slightly higher prices tend to turn most of the undergrad crowd away -- no freaked-out MCB majors occupying tables for four hours cramming for midterms! 

Easily my favorite cafe on Southside.

I know the graduate students and intellectuals like it and I would love it in theory, except for the fact they are terribly annoying about their rules. 2 3 and 4 person ONLY tables when NO ONE is there for instance. Another is sticking to the minimum credit card charge even when they had run out of drinks. It was a bit ridiculous and silly considering the person I was with goes there at least once a week.

19 years old. Exploring the world for the first time. I went to this cafe and met an older man. We would talk for hours. He would tell me about religion. We'd discuss music. We discuss drugs.  We'd once in awhile discuss sex.

One day he told me, "I am into men. But I wouldn't call myself gay. I think you're absolutely beautiful". Besides high school crushes, I remember this was the first time besides what had happened at Codys. That another man open about being interested in me sexually. He gave me his number, but I never called.

Maybe it was because times were different. Maybe it was because I hadn't fully found comfort in the world. But I learned so many lessons here and to this day, I wonder what happened to that old man with the sarcastic humor.

This cafe was wonderful in expanding my own universe.

This is a review of the music portion of the business. There's no question that they have some excellent CDs - classical only of course. The attitude of the staff leaves a lot to be desired. They seem snobby and arrogant. . Given the decreasing audience for classical music they'd help their cause if they were more helpful and less condescending. Perhaps they're defensive or something but I do not enjoy coming to the store. I'd rather buy my music elsewhere.

$10 for something called Galiada. What the menu described as basmati rice with chicken, sweet corn and peas turned out to be a small dish of too oily rice, chunks of chicken skin and fat, and corn and peas that were definitely frozen before cooked in my dish. Nothing against frozen peas and corn but for $10 and a small portion I expected some dank fresh produce. Oh and did I mention that there was a total lack of flavor expect for the salt and pepper I added myself? Will definitely never do dinner here again.

2 stars because the drinks looked good and I liked the ambiance, but the food was a huge let down.

Ambience: Cozy, with beautiful classical music or opera in the background, relaxing. I really love the classical music that always fills the air, and the music-inspired artwork on the wall. No wifi though - students take note: you can't study here (if you need to be online). But you can read, chat with friends, or browse/buy classical music CDs from this café. Just know that this is NOT the quietest café most conducive for studying.

Food Quality and Cost: Agree with the other reviewer that Hot Chicken Foccacia Sandwich is a hit or miss, but its Greek Platter is delicious. I like the hummus. Yummy. Food is slightly on the expensive side (considering the small portion), but coffee is reasonably priced. Good coffee! Not amazing, but good. "Today's Specials" are usually pricier, but again, are usually tastier, too.

Another Big Plus: the University Press Books is right next door! It's a beautiful book store, classy and sophisticated. Very intellectual, if a bit pretentious. Still, it's a nice place to browse books after your lunch at Music Offering Café.

A few more problems:
- The chairs aren't very comfortable. 
- It tends to get crowded and noisy during lunch hours. 
- Not enough salad to go with Chicken Foccacia Hot Sandwich.
- I wish the service can be friendlier.

quiet and cozy, very pleasant atmosphere, employees very friendly but not overly perky.

great coffee, cheap pots of tea, tasty sandwiches.

also the homemade scones are some of the best i've had in my lifetime.

overall, a great retreat from the hustle and bustle of campus.

Okay - super score...
I came by today because i needed a little pick me up for my afternoon work.  Not only is the iced chai latte pretty good, but there is a live string quartet playing by the window.  And - important because I usually really do need internet access while working - they are within range of an Airbears signal.  Really.  This might be my new weekend study spot...

This is a nice place to take someone if you want them to see the classier (yet still affordable) side of Berkeley. The sandwiches are nice, there's fresh lemonade... I just recommend you put sugar in it. Don't make the same mistake I did. It's a cute place with a good ambience. It takes a little while for your food to get to you, but it's nice to sit in a quiet place with your friends sometimes. I recommend the hot ham and cheese.
Not sure why I kept coming back, I often found tea leaves in my espresso. Not undergrad-friendly.  Minimum charge to sit during peak hours.  I nicknamed it pretentious cafe.

Just had their Smoked Turkey and sliced Granny Smith Apples sandwich and Freshly Squeezed Lemonade for lunch! My friend got the Hot Chicken on Focaccia. I must say, though, I like their Apple Toasted Walnut & Gorgonzola salad most. My sandwich (the turkey) was on a baguette, and the baguette was soooo hard to eat (too dry). I know baguette's aren't supposed to be super-soft on the outside, but maybe a little softer would make the sandwich even more pleasant to eat. Their lemonade was very sour (which is GOOD! I don't like too sweet lemonades), and very refreshing. Good place to go with a friend, and you can find all age-ranges there - I saw elderly people as well as college students and professors. Just note that this place is actually a CD shop and it's a cafe/bistro you're at, not a restaurant!

Food is ok but portions are small and it is overpriced. The service is snobby and THERE IS NO BATHROOM. They have strange rules about seating at the lunch hour. I go back occasionally because a friend of mine likes it but, I always have a snack before or after.

One of my favorite places to have lunch, Musical Offerings is a very serene cafe that isn't teeming with obnoxious college students griping about how they are so hungover or neurotically freaking out over their upcoming midterm. I recommend the walnut, apple, and gorgonzola salad or the grilled eggplant sandwich. The strawberry lemonade is very tart, but the herbal tea is extremely refreshing and compliments both entrees well. It is conveniently across the street from campus and offers a nice change from the Asian Ghetto or La Burrita.

Oh my fucking goodness.

Their Melted Brie and Roasted Red Peppers hot sandwich is a-mazing. It comes open-faced, cheese nicely melted along with the rind on one side and sexy ass roasted red peppers on the other (although the consistency makes me wonder if it was roasted and then thrown in a jar and then re-heated just to be thrown on top of my sandwich). Put it on a baguette? DAMN GOOD ASS COMBO. Comes with a small salad, which I didn't really care for because the sandwich reeled me in and kept me there. 

I've had their Hot Chicken on Focaccia before, that was damn good too.

This is my new favorite cafe in Berkeley. Its convenient location, scrumptious food, and cozy atmosphere make it my new favorite study spot/lunch spot.

ATMOSPHERE:
Cute, cozy, and sophisticated, the ambiance here is perfect for lunch, afternoon tea, or a study session. The cafe is lined with books and classical music CD/records. There's a lot of seating and I like to sit either by the window or "upstairs." 

Like others said, this place is a little pricier than most cafes in Berkeley, so the crowd tends to be more mature. You can find grad students, professors, and older locals catching a bite to eat at Musical Offering Cafe. It gets pretty busy but never gets noisy, like Cafe Milano or Cafe Strada.

The workers are friendly but this place doesn't really have waiter service besides them bringing the food to your table.

FOOD:
1) Hot chicken on focaccia with melted provolone, garlic aioli, and tomato
2) Peppermint mocha
3) Strawberry agua fresca

I took the advice of other Yelpers and tried the hot chicken on focaccia. It is scrumptious! My best friend and I always order it whenever we go here. The bread is perfectly toasted and I love how the tomato, mayo, and chicken and cheese come together to make a delicious sandwich. The chicken is a hit or miss; sometimes it's very juicy and tender, other times it's a little tough. The sandwich comes with a side salad drizzled with a light vinaigrette. I personally love the salad and i think it complements the sandwich well. The portions are just right-- I always leave satisfied and not overly stuffed.

The peppermint mocha is strong, which is good because caffeine rarely has an effect on me. It came in a pretty big glass, which was great because I felt like I got my monies worth, but it felt weird drinking coffee out of glass mug. The peppermint taste was subtle and not overpowering. It wasn't as sweet as the peppermint mocha from Starbucks.

The strawberry agua fresca is my favorite drink so far. I love how crisp and fresh it tastes. It's very refreshing and goes well with the many sandwiches they offer. I enjoy eating the chunks of strawberry at the end, too.

They have daily specials, which always sound delicious, but I usually end up getting the hot chicken on focaccia. The food here tastes fresh and relatively healthy. 

Overall, I love coming here on a sunny day. I just started coming here last year, mainly to eat, but I think I'll be coming here more often to study and have a cup of coffee.

Though I love Musical Offering cafe, mainly for the clientele and kitsch factor, I have to admit it's overpriced and kind of blah. The "salad" that comes with the hot chicken sandwich isn't really a salad at all. It's about two leaves drowned in vinaigrette that won't even spread to the two halves of the sammy to make it a lil more exciting. I mean, really, if you're gonna add a salad to the sandwich, then add the freakin salad. Don't tease me with a couple green bits. Maybe they think people prefer mayo to salad, cause they sure fly free with that.

The cafe was nice place to met people before a performance at Zellerbach, conviently located (across the street) and easy to find (I came from the South Bay).  The cafe was a bit small but seats quickly opened up.  I ordered a brownie and tea.  The brownie hit the spot, it was moist and delicious.  I was also pleasantly suprised that you could buy wine there too (that will be ordered on my next visit)!!!

Realizing that the swarming, seething masses of caffeine craving zombies (students) generally pick a no-frills fix ala Strada, Milano or god forbid Peets, I feel comfortable awarding Musical Offering Cafe five stars. Also, it seems to take the average student several years to find out about Yelp, let alone use it, so I doubt an additional positive review will cause a massive influx of sleep deprived midterm thumping fools.

Ok, now for an actual review... Musical Offering Cafe combines a delightful mix of classical music and delicious sandwiches into a single, wonderful, package. And it is a package I hope to... open again?...

Shit, its too early in the morning to be witty... 

Basically what I'm trying to say is that they have really tasty food and the music is a nice touch. Hooray Music Cafe!

A great alternative to more packed cafes like Milano if you're looking for a spot to study because....

+classical, calming music
+quieter ambiance overall (probably because the stuff is a tad pricier/classier; I've seen more professors/grad students/adults than college kids here)
+service: I've been here a couple of times, and the people who work there are really sweet and kind of endearing
+delicious gourmet options: arugula with brie on a bagel is AWESOME, as is their brewed tea that comes in a gorgeous little teapot! Their granola and yogurt is just more ordinary, taste-wise, but the presentation is still always flawless.


Overall, this is a cafe that pays attention to the details, with one exception:

The only reason I didn't  give this place at least 4 stars was the fact that one unfortunate morning all the tables I tried sitting at (THREE) were super sticky! As beautiful as the rest of the ambiance and my food were, I just couldn't get over how disgusting my table(s) felt, and the stickiness was not much ameliorated by  my attempts to wipe it away with a napkin and water.

I will visit this place again, as I really would like to give it a higher rating, but for now the three stars stand.

their lemon butter crepes were crap. dry, chewy and tasteless with UNmelted lemon-butter on top with a few blueberries. for around $6 for 3 tiny crepes, it is not satisfying in any way. 

stick with a bagel if you want a cheap, filling breakfast.

This review does not apply to the cafe.

Musical Offering Cafe was suggested to me by one of my professors at Mills College as a place where I might be able to find some of the more difficult to find recordings by some rather less notable composers.  So, on a nice May evening I decided to make the trip after a nice outing at Amoeba (which is right around the corner).  

If I was going to just visit this place and not park in the area around People's Park, parking could be an issue.  On a weekday Bancroft is quite busy during the school year, so look in the neighborhood behind the store for some free parking.  Avoid the lot next to it if you don't like paying an arm and a leg for parking.  

If you are going to visit here to look at CDs be careful walking through the cafe, waitresses and waiters come out of nowhere with trays of wine and food.  I say this because you have to walk through the cafe to get to the CD store in the back and I was almost clocked with a tray full of merlot.  Maybe it was my fault for going during peak eating hours.

The store has an outstanding selection of CD and they are ALL classical (and sub genres).  They do carry a limited selection of used CD, but nothing too impressive, but their new CDs all but make-up for the lack of used.  They also carry a limited supply of DVDs too which is also a nice thing to see.      

The reason that I give the store three stars is for their prices.  I found the store to be quite overpriced with most CDs falling in the $18 dollar range.  Though that is not outrageous, it is considering that Amoeba and Rasputin around the corner is much more reasonable.

classical cd store in the back, fresh and inventive cafe in the front.  hot/cold sandwiches, extremely fresh salads, and daily specials like lasagna and salmon linguini (which was delish!).  adorable.  attracts the professor/gsi crowd.

i must emphasize that i LOVE the salads here.  like, really.

(p.s. don't come for dinner.)

It's a bit pricey, but their hot chicken on focaccia is simply the best sandwich. Great, toasty focaccia, a generous amount of gooey cheese, and chicken, as well as a small salad (nice vinaigrette). I always finish wanting to get another one, but I can't both because of, well, my health, and because it's a little pricey. I wish I could comment on the rest of their menu, but honestly, I've never tried anything else! The chicken sandwich is too good to pass up. 

They don't allow you to sit in the cafe unless you order food during lunch hours, which is understandably frustrating. This isn't a great cafe to study at (even during non-lunch hours, since it's quite cramped), but I enjoy it as a nice, clean, and consistently yummy place for lunch.

A cafe that is soothing on your heart and mind!

 A cafe that clearly differentiates between cakes/cookies born the day before selling them at a dollar, and a cafe that has a cute guy behind the counter with an accent that is endearing and language that is perfect to the T!(don't you just love it when men sound like they belong from a novel of an era gone by ;))

And did I forget to mention that tea here is not the packed dip version, but real brewed tea served in delicate tea pots (even if it's a to-go order)

The perfect antidote to an insane world.

No trashy mass produced garbage here.

Just good clean pure classical music and decent food.

Great place to hang out, meet friends, study, be normal, human, whatever.

Love this Cafe 

excellent change  from  the crowds 

My usual is the Roast Turkey with 
with sliced tart apple, lettuce, mayonnaise, and Mendocino mustard on baguette.

Good place to relax  and have a pleasant conversation

I'd been here several times: for a tea; when a friend had art on display; after The Hard Nut with a small group; to browse.

I wandered in last week primarily because it was a convenient place to tell my husband to find me while I waited before the 8pm show at Cal Performances (Herbie Hancock). I was so please to find the very civilized presentation with white table clothes, a very nice food selection, and assurance that I could be served quickly to make it to the show.

The service was excellent. My wine was very nice as was my ahi tuna / artichoke salad. It was a reasonable portion of seared fish, a freshly cooked artichoke heart, and nicely dressed greens. It wasn't cheap, but it wasn't fast food. It was a meal, elegantly served, and again kudos on the excellent service.

I highly recommended The Musical Offering for a pre-performance meal in addition to being a nice place to sit and listen to music while drinking a cup of tea. Also, I have found the staff very knowledgeable when inquiring about music selections. 

Bravo!

Don't ever take out coffee here. 

The small coffee is.. REALLY small. NOT WORTH IT!

Beautiful background classical music, quaint tables, bright and warm atmosphere, cordial service, and the best roasted pepper and melted brie sandwich in the area. Despite several attempts, I'm utterly unable to study here -- I enjoy myself too much. It's a treat and a half.  

The minuses... As all Berkeley food venues, it is a touch overpriced -- but worth it for the general experience. Avoid crowds at peak hours: if you come during lunch-time, they actually make you buy lunch or ask you (albeit politely) to vacate your table for someone who is eating (!). Something to keep in mind. 

Note: their bathroom is actually located next-door in the book store, so they'll give you a key and you'll have to go around! I recommend tangent-ing and perusing their book selection on the way...

I bought a coffee there because that is how I judge a place (if you are a cafe and your drip coffee is sludge, you aren't worth much to me).  It was about 11 am and the fellow behind the counter informed that he would tap me when the lunch rush arrived to ask me to move because people buying food have priority over us coffee drinkers at the table.  He didn't tell me if there was a good spot to hang out and finish my coffee that I had bought "for here".  That interaction really rubbed me the wrong way.  Maybe the food is good, but telling me that I will be forced out of my seat later because I only bought coffee seemed excessive.  The establishment also seemed a little pretentious.
Good hot sandwiches, good fresh juices, lousy coffee, lousy baked goods... never noticed the music stuff at the back... do people actually do non-eating things there?

So I thought to myself...I could use a chocolate chip cookie!

I walk in, stand in line for a bit, then order that cookie.

Her: Are you sitting with someone who is ordering lunch?

Me: No...

Her: During our lunch hours you have to order lunch to get that.

Me: Okay...never mind then.
(Translation: you guys suck, but whatever.)

It's not like I even intended to sit--not sure if she realized that, but she sure didn't ask. 

Basically, this is the LAMEST CAFE EVER.
Horrible, horrible "service."

Gosh, w/all these reviews for the apple/gorgonzola, etc. salad, i'm gonna have to try it!
This is my favorite near-campus place to eat...for many reasons
(1) The food is really good: sure it's a LITTLE more expensive than other places, but that's b/c you're getting wholesome ingredients. I've had the pesto chicken warm sandwhich, tuna melt, hot chicken on focaccia w/provolone, and several drinks. Sandwhiches come w/a small side of greens
(2) Beat the campus crowd
(3) Overhear an interesting conversation among english/philosophy grad students or staff
(4) They accept plastic!!
(5) Relaxing music in the background

True, it gets really packed around lunchtime, but I've never not found a table, so it's not too bad. If anything, it's ok to grab a chair next to a complete stranger :)

Wonderful place that I frequented during grad school and now have "rediscovered" even though my campus office is very far away. A real oasis and place of calm. Nothing like some hot tea in the middle of a cold or bad day.

The staff and service are excellent. I happen to become friendly with Chef Erick because I had an extra NYT Sunday that I wanted to give away, and he was looking at some old papers at tables outside the bookstore next door. Another staff member gave me a brownie with a candle lit in it for my birthday! So Nice. 

New find -- order the Avocado and Swiss, but on a Baguette. It's supposed to be on Multi-grain, but one day they ran out and put it on a baguette. WONDERFUL. I ask for it that way all the time now.

This place is a nice alternative to the usual Berkeley lunch spot, however, it is a bit more pricey and you should expect to share your table with random strangers if you come at the peak of the lunch hour. 

My favorite thing here (ok, I've only ever tried two different menu items...) is the melted brie and roasted red pepper sandwich served on an open faced baguette. It is to die for! Though I have to agree with other reviewers, the portions are not huge. The other dish I've tried was one of their daily specials (they have different specials everyday, most of which usually sound pretty good), it was a salad/pasta type dish that was a bit away from the norm or what I was expecting but really quite good. 

I like to grab lunch here with a particular friend every once in a while, but the crowd can be a deterrence. And if your not a fan of the brie sandwich, you might be out of luck because their menu is pretty limited (nothing else on the main menu really sounds very tempting to me, but again, there's always the daily specials). The atmosphere is a plus as it is also the home of a music store and there is always nice classical music playing in the background. If you haven't tried it, give it a go, you might be pleasantly surprised.

One of my favorite places in Berkeley! It is quite an enjoyable place to study, eat, and relax. I study there quite often during the school year because it's much less crowded and far more relaxing than other cafes in Berkeley such as Cafe Milano or Cafe Intermezzo (though do enjoy these places from time to time).
I love how they have pots of loose leaf tea for only $1.50. The brie and roasted red bell pepper on baguette is amazing.. though I can't afford to eat lunch there every day. 
I love the ambiance.. less college students, more Berkeleyans, classical music, nice employees. However, there is one album that this one guy who works in the classical music part of the store plays that is dreadful... it's a collection of American folksongs that seemed to have come right off the Oregon Trail...

So Berkeley it hurts!  The first time I went in here, I waited for about ten minutes while the barrista chatted with her friend.  I finally just left and went down to Peet's to get some real coffee.  So, bad first impression.  I have since come back with co-workers and it's been slightly better. 

Usually full of intellectual-looking older students and aging hippies.  The back of the place is a classical music store, which I've never checked out because I mainly come in here after work when I'm rabidly hungry and/or in need of a coffee break. 

Minus two stars for the service. At least twice I've been in here, they've completely ignored me despite the fact that there was no one. else. in line.  

 On the subject of cleanliness - why wouldn't they rip out the carpeting in the seating area where food is served? I always see someone sweeping crumbs away and it never fails to perplex me. Who sweeps a rug?! It just seems so ineffectual and actually kind of unsanitary too. 

Plus two stars for the Coffee Tiger, which is Espresso and Half and Half, iced, with honey drizzled around the outside of the glass.   Also,  the Moist Peruvian Cornbread is excellent.

Best coffee in the UC Berkeley campus area.  Maybe even in Berkeley, the city.

My favorite combo is small coffee with a slice of pumpkin cake for a mere $3.  It makes for a pleasant breakfast and if you eat it slow enough, the pumpkin cake actually does fill you up.

Early morning (~9-ish) is the best time to come.  Too early and they're still baking the treats and you may end up having day-old leftovers.  Then as you're sitting there, they'll bring out fresh-baked whatever-you-just-ordered and you'll feel like a giant dork.

Espresso drinks are hit or miss, depending on who makes them.  In general though, the espresso is pretty well-done.  Try it con panna for the fresh whipped cream which is just enough to die for to suck up the calories.

Strawberry agua fresca is refreshing on a hot day as is the Coffee Tiger (make sure the employee knows how to make it though).

Hot chicken on focaccia is delicious and always hits the spot, though at ~$8 is a bit of a splurge-y treat rather than an everyday thing.  Their specials sound good, but some are rather popular and run out by early afternoon.

Prepare to stand in line at random times.  Often, they'll only have one or two workers and they won't assembly-line it--they'll take an order and scamper off to fulfill it, then move on to the next person.  Thus, if you stand behind a party of 3, prepare to wait for all 3 drinks/food treats to be prepared.

Classical music is calming in the morning.

Five stars for being an all-classical music store in a world where this is increasingly rare. Great selection, knowledgeable staff, and they always seem to be playing something interesting in the store. I have no idea what the cafe is like.

positioned right across from lower sproul,
it is a great way to get away from school & de-stress
great music, good food
Roast Turkey with sliced tart apple, lettuce, mayonnaise, and Mendocino mustard on baguette. is really good.

Hmmmm - maybe I should give this place another try for lunch, because my dinner wasn't great.  

I stopped by here with some coworkers before a performance at Zellerbach.  Everything was OK.  Just OK.  The menu for dinner was limited.  Very limited - 2 salads, 3 entrees (chicken, salmon, veggie) and 3 desserts - it was like going to a fundraising dinner or a wedding with those options.  And the food was definitely not really worth the prices - either in portions or taste.  The wine list was reasonable and we had a tasty inexpensive red.  

That said - I would stop by again for dessert - it was very good - or a glass of wine before a perfomance.

I came here on a recommendation from a friend. This is my friend's favorite place to go and chill. Why? She likes people-watching. She's also small and Asian, and she is quietly amused by the fact that 90% of the audience here is old white people. I couldn't believe that a single place could attract such a uniform crowd. But Musical Offering does. I walk in and what do I find? 90% old white people. HILARIOUS!

Needless to say, the menu is priced right, the portions are sizable, and the food is clean 'n tasty. I got a tuna and white bean salad and my friend got a sandwich. Both were huge. Both were good. I didn't even notice the extra bread that came with my salad.

The environment is ultra-pleasant and the coffee wasn't bad either. It looked like there were a ton of interesting items on the tapas menu too, which, unfortunately, isn't quite as reasonably priced as straight-up lunch. But if you wanna chill in a nice area and have a book to read or a person to talk to -- or if you just want to laugh at the fact that when you walk in, it *will* be 90% old, white people -- this is the right place. Tranquil, too. Definitely goin' back.

Let me start by saying the cafe has the BEST music for relaxing out of the stressful environment of mid-term or final crunch time. I mean, really, don't you want to maintain your sanity and tranquility while the deadlines are literally increasing your stress level?

This place is such a pleasant, halcyon respite for a stressed out me.

Check it out. The food is priced higher than the DIVES on Dwight. It is WORTH every penny to get fresh OJ, fresh salad, hot soup and just a wider variety of good re-energizing food closest to campus. Hey, I am sooo over greasy pizza. I need to keep my hot curvy curves for spring-ing that hot guy in my Sociology class.

As a graduate student at Cal, having a place like this around is a life/stomach saver.  My friend and I frequent this place many times during the week between classes.  

The pros:  Addicting healthy, fresh, and tasty food with a tiny gourmet twist e.g., their  Apple Gorgonzola Salad (granny smith apples, gorgonzola, and walnuts on a bed of organic greens, with an herb vinaigrette).  A homemade soup of the day e.g., their carrot ginger soup, and various homemade baked goods, and coffee drinks.

The cons:  I have to take away a star because the food is kind of up there in price--which doesn't make sense because it's right across the street from one of the busiest sections on campus, so you would think it would be more considerate to "starving students" budgets, but not so; expect to pay around $8 to $11 dollars w/o a drink.  The portions, however, are decent.  You'll get full, but not stuffed (though this may not be true for individuals with bigger appetites than my own).  

In addition, if you come around lunch time, it's very hard to get a table.  If you do get a table, they want you in and out, and make that clear with a sign.  So, if you come during lunch time just wanting some coffee and an opportunity to chat with friends, the manager will come over and ask you to buy some food or please leave.  Not cool. 

Other than that, the food is awesome :-)

nice atmosphere, if you can get passed all the "this table is reserved" signs. 

Wish they served other tea besides celestial seasonings (hello! Supports the war in Iraq!!). 

That said, I like to come here on rainy days.....it allows me the opportunity to pretend I'm on the heath in England.....or somewhere...yeah.....not exactly sure what that is about....

This is one of my favorite coffee shops around campus.  The tables are reserved during lunch for diners only, but on the weekends their amazing coffee and entrees make for an excellent place to study.  There are lots of tables and outlets, a great atmosphere and very friendly staff.

Pros: 
-Good, cheap coffee
-Right next to campus
-Grad students talking about Derrida

Cons: 
-Food is expensive but not spectacular
-Not a very good place to study; they don't allow you to sit there during lunchtime if you're not eating, they stop serving coffee pretty early. 
-Have to go next door to use a bathroom
-Grad students talking about Derrida

Overall, an average coffee shop and not a good place to study. Good place to meet up a friend for coffee, but I do that a lot less than I study.

We popped in after seeing the hard nut because it was pouring down rain and we wanted to have a hot drink to warm us up.  I'm a bit surprised by some of the reviews that mention being ignored by the people working in this cafe since we were greeted warmly when we entered and our orders were taken quickly, so I guess we were lucky and came in while the nice barrista was in.  The espresso and Irish coffee we ordered came out piping hot and delicious, unfortunately the chai latte while perfectly flavored was lukewarm at best.  I ventured into the music store at the back of the cafe, and though I didn't buy anything it looked like heaven for the classical music and opera lover.  After reading other reviews that raved about the moist peruvian cornbread I'm kind of bummed I didn't order some, oh well there's always next time right?

I'm a regular at this haven from low-grade student fare. The atmosphere is great--busy, but not so loud that you can't have an important gossip session with your close gal-friends. The service is impeccable, if a little slow for food orders.

As for the food, any dish is a good bet, the Cobb salad with extra bacon being my personal favorite. Their specials are often excellent, if a little unexpected (lamb, mint, and hummus go very well together on soft Acme bread). The beverages are also a pull, especially their famous strawberry agua fresca (see many other reviews). The coffee is a little less impressive than the food, but it does the job well when you need some strong drip or a sinful hazelnut mocha.

This fantastic cafe is worth visiting more than once a week, which I would do were it not for the slightly out of a student's league prices. The food is worth it, though, and most anyone would taste its quality.

Are you a grad student or faculty member at Cal?
Do you appreciate good sustainable food?
Would you like to purchase a CD while waiting for your lunch?

... Then the Musical Offering Cafe is your place!

This is my go-to for reliable food and a quiet refined atmosphere without the undergrad-laden clientele. I've only been here for lunch, and have enjoyed the wide array of soups (usually vegetarian), salads (my old-goodie is the apple, gorgonzola, and walnut), and sandwiches.  Portions are adequate for lunch, and the food is always fresh and light. Tap water is available self-serve, and they offer a decent cup of joe or loose leaf tea with pastries as well. It's a tad pricey, but I figure you're paying for the food and the atmosphere as a package. 

The cashiers have always been very pleasant and helpful. Can't complain. Some of the front tables are reserved for lunch, which is also nice since it guarantees you a seat.

The front of the cafe has a moderate amount of seating for a small group, with the back as a music/ CD store. It's relatively quiet despite the proximity to Sather Gate. 

In sum: a solid choice for reliable food at a moderate price. Not worth an extra trip, and nothing special, but just a good addition to reliable lunch spots near campus.

Want a calm location amidst the hussle and bustle of Berkeley, where you can relax and listen to interesting and often obscure classical music while sipping your espresso drink or Red Zinger iced tea and enjoying a tasty sandwich or salad?  Musical Offering is your place.  But avoid it if you don't want to run into graduate students -- the place is downright infested with them (which I like, but then I keep hoping their intellectualism will rub off on me).  And if you really like what you hear, you can go in the back and buy it, because the back half of the cafe is a classical music store.

Once upon a time. I rated this place 4 stars.The earth must have been shaken... 
I've received so many bad impressions since that I absolutely forgot all about my former mesmerization with the place. It has to be the music and this reminds me to mention that this review is !not! about the music store: I still think it is one of the best when it comes to classical music. 

So to make a long story short: I am never coming back. Never ever. This time they've gone over and beyond their mediocre food and general unpleasantness of service. This time i ordered at the counter, waited and waited for a spot to clear. Then as i was walking over happily to the free table, I was "caught
 by a staff member and told to sit outside - in the cold. 

His reason was not that I smelled, created public outrage or anything of that sort. No. His reason was that I order an americano, and not food, while waiting for a lunch companion. I explained that I have a firm plan to eat, but must wait, so that guy very sweetly suggested that I sit outside (and it was raining, mind you) until I am ready to order food. 

Then the guy who took the order from me apologized, but not to me! No... he apologized to the guy who told me to leave. 

So i figure that for such a bad americano, people deserve a kinder attitude (I'm ashamed to say that I am such a weak spirit that I cried over the meanness - don't laugh please - all the way uphill which I thought was a very aesthetic thing to do considering the heavy rains.)

No in-store WiFi but the Air Bears signal is strong, if you know what I mean*! ;) 

+4 stars for classical music, cute tea pots and tea cups and great ambiance for studying

-1 star for short hours and minimal outlets :(

*I'm using Air Bears right now ^_^

Great place to get away from the hustle and bustle of campus. Even though it's right across the street, it's nowhere near as crowded as the other campus cafes, and it attracts an older clientele. The food is a bit pricey, but I've heard good things about the tapas.

The music store in the back is great. It's rare to find a classical-and-jazz-only collection in these parts.

Musical Offering has the best pastries of any cafe around Berkeley. They make their pastries fresh in the morning and throughout the day they sometimes have additional batches of brownies or coffee cake coming out of the oven. Some of my favorites are:

-Apricot Scone: definitely the best scone I've ever had. Flavorful, crumbly, and pretty big. These usually run out pretty fast. Then you might have to settle for the raisin scone, which is good too.

-Blueberry muffin: these are very special.  They have tons of blueberries in them and the lemon (or orange?) zest make them much tastier than normal bb muffins. They also taste healthy to me. Some bb muffins can be greasy or too cakey or too sweet, but these are just right.

-The pumpkin cake, banana nut bread, and chocolate chip cookies are also good, but not as outstanding as the bb muffin or the apricot scone.

The only pastry that I have not enjoyed very much here is the brownie. They describe them as being the most amazing brownies ever, but I find them to be slightly boring and not chocolatey enough.
 
I heard the gingersnap cookies are great here as well, but I've only recently gotten into ginger cookies and I'm definitely going to try the ones here soon.

The coffee drinks are reasonably priced and the workers there can make a decent cappuccino, which is usually my test for how good the coffee is. But I usually get the Americano, which they make really well here. If you are not a coffee drinker, then you should try the loose leaf teas which come in adorable pots with accessories or the fresh strawberry juice.

As for the food, I have eaten lunch here a couple of times and it's always good, but slightly too expensive for the average undergrad to come here more than a few times a semester. The toasted brie sandwich is the best. I think it comes with roasted peppers on top. They have specials everyday.

The one downside is that they are so busy during lunch that if you are not eating there you cannot stay.

Best Cafe/Classical Music store in the Bay Area. Looking for Couperin and a Cappuccino, Brie Sandwich and Bach, Nicoise Salad and Saint-Saens? Look no further than MOC. It is the epitome of civility. Nice meet-up spot.

I did not eat or drink here but I stayed here for more than one hour just checking classical music CDs. 

I checked the clients but they looked all nice. 

This place is a mighty heaven for classic music lovers like myself.

Even though I had a good time catching up with a friend here, shelling out $9 for a sandwich and iced tea sorta sucked. But the hot chicken sandwich was perfectly toasted and very good. I thought with the little side salad, it was enough food to make me content, not necessarily super full. Maybe not worth $9 for that amount of food though. 

Nonetheless, it's a cute place. I won't go there often for sure, but I immediately thought my mom would like the place a lot if she were to visit. I realize that I have made mention of my mom a lot in my reviews hehe. I miss my mama.

I really like this cafe, it's been on my list to try for years and I've always walked on by.  I was about to walk on by today, but figured I'd check it out, encouraged by the strains of classical music.  I hit the tail end of the lunch rush, so there was a lot of hustle and bustle.  I was able to order very quickly, got my coffee and my number and sat down.  I'm not sure if the wifi I'm using is provided or poached by a neighbor, but it is available and free.  My sandwich (roasted peppers and melted brie, with pesto) was very tasty and came with a "side salad" (just a few greens, with dressing).  It was a healthy meal, which means I'm still pretty hungry.  

The clientele, as one would expect at a cafe of this type, is very nice.  Even with the loud hustle-bustle of the lunch rush, there were none of the characters that often annoy me at Bay Area cafes, primarily cell phone yellers.  That is worth its weight in gold.  

Minus one star for the steep price (A sandwich and large coffee was $9.46!).

This is a lovely place for dinner before a concert at Zellerbach or Wheeler, although the last two times we've been to a concert on campus we've gone to Angeline's on Shattuck.  This is probably a better choice on a Saturday night, as the waits have been shorter.  The food is good and the service has been pleasantly attentive.

Upon drifting into this dinner spot at sunset, we were greeted with subtle background music, a cello and piano adaption of Le Barbier de Seville. It set the sublime atmosphere of the place, and pretty much guaranteed a pleasant evening.

The waitress was personally engaged in making us happy and helped us as we struggled through the simple menu. Because she alerted us to the modest portions of each course, we knew we would have enough room for everything.

For appetizers, the chef was incredibly creative with the beet salad, and the red and golden beets they used were full and rich. Although this picture-perfect appetizer and the others are overpriced, it's very fun to experience the way these are presented.

The main course is again overpriced for the modest portions, but perfection on a dish is worth experiencing once or twice a year, right? The chicken with asparagus was deep in flavor and perfect in preparation. The Cuban-style pulled pork entre demands a whole article in Gourmet Magazine. It's obvious that the staff takes pride in serving this caliber of food, especially ahead of the Saturday night performances in the area.

The desserts were not particularly impressive, and I would have skipped this course and opted for bigger portions in the main course. A chocolate brownie and a cup of coffee later, and we got hit with the bill. One person cramped up and another made gurgling noises, but we bit the bullet and paid our share for a most excellent meal.

This restaurant and music store, notwithstanding the price, deserves five stars. Hopefully, the wonderful service is just as good any day of the week. If only they could drop the menu prices a little and somehow compensate by drawing more patrons into the music CD area, this place would no doubt win many awards.

I had a nice experience here. I had the apple/walnut/gorgonzola salad. The apples were flavorless, which was sad seeing as how they're in season. However, I loved the dressing and the greens were fresh. The gorgonzola was well.... gorgonzola. Good enough, certainly. 

There is an uppity feel to the place, though, which I really don't care for. The cashier was a little tart for my taste and they seemed overly eager to clear my table. Speaking of tables, I find it stupid that they have tables that are reserved for 4-5 people. It's right near campus so it seems there are a lot of individuals/couples, if today was any indication. The larger tables sat empty while smaller ones were highly coveted.

The salad was good, though, and several other menu items sounded tasty so I will like to come again. I'm amazed that I was able to pass up the macaroons today-- I doubt I'll have the strength next time.

this is one of my favorite lunchtime spots in berkeley.

all of the food is huge & delicious, including the salads & soups & sweets & the coffee. not to mention that it's quiet, except for little hints of conversations here & there & classical music, obviously, plinkering away in the background.

extra points for being the place i always had lunch with anna r. when she used to visit me in berkeley. bff lunches! wheeeee!

Nice cafe with soothing/relaxing classical music.  I recall the sandwiches were quite good which were served with a small side salad and they got agua fresca :)  I love agua fresca! Would like to try their dessert next time. Music for the ears & yummy for the tummy. What a combo!!!
I love everything that comes with foccaccia.

I've been here twice so far and both times I left satisfied. I've tried the italian soda and the iced soy latte. The italian soda had a good amount of syrup and I definitely recommend getting this drink to accompany a meal. Today, I got a medium iced soy latte for about $3.70. They filled the ice to the top of the glass which I was initially worried about being too cold since I have sensitive teeth, but after adding hot espresso shots, a lot of the ice melted and I was left with less than a quarter cup of ice. The latte wasn't strong enough for me, so I think I'll be trying the americano next time.

The seating is a bit cramped on the first floor (just the way the tables/chairs are arranged), but there IS a second floor, fyi. Other than that, it has a great atmosphere for studying if you like studying with a little background noise. Also, if you need an outlet for your computer, there is one on the first floor INSIDE a planter... so keep an eye out for that.  Free WiFi too...just ask for the password! 

Overall, I'm intrigued and will come back to try some of their food.

I stopped by Berkeley for the day and the first thing I wanted to do was to find a good place to grab an espresso.  Cafe Milano was nearby, but just didn't cut it.

Espresso: Decent - Decent beans, but the preparation left a lot to be desired
Pastries: Decent - Grabbed a croissant which was okay.  On par with an SBUX croissant.
Ambience: Poor - There's a good amount of seating, but the tables can use some work and the there were a swarm of flies hovering around the tables.  I actually would have said good if the flies weren't so bad.
Wi-Fi: Decent - It's free so they get a notch for that, but it's really really slow.

Cafe Milano's staff is very friendly and the service is excellent.

The food is average.  Even though I have come to enjoy their new pasta salads.

I think the hype about Cafe Milano is that fact that it has free wi-fi right across from the UCB campus.

There's never any seating and if you came for the free wi-fi you'll be lucky if you get a seat near an outlet.  There's not enough outlets, and although they try to make up for it with a multi-plug adapter, it's impossible to get an outlet in the middle of the cafe and upstairs.

On top of that, if you come on an extremely busy day you'll be lucky if you can stay connected to their free wi-fi for more than five minutes.

Overall I think Cafe Milano is a good place to use the wi-fi on a slow day otherwise I would recommend finding a new venue.

unlike the rest of the reviewers, i do not think that this was a good place to SERIOUSLY study. the music is loud and poorly selected and i think the coffee grinder is broken, like it has a bent blade or something- all of it was just a very big headache for me. when i study, i actually like to get shit done. maybe if you want to read a magazine or something light or just pretend your studying, this would be the perfect place. otherwise, don't come here.

Great coffee...awesome staff! I love this place, and the ambiance is wonderful. I spent plenty of hours studying here during my undergraduate tenure at Berkeley! Try their Café au lait...it's wonderful!

They make some decent coffee, there is free wifi, and everyone is pretty nice. It can be hard to find seating depending on the time of day and if school is in session.

Nothing particularly special about this place to up the stars and it's not a place I seek out when I am in town, but it will do when I am nearby and need a caffeine fix.

I like this Cafe very much. However, the Wifi connection is terrible! It takes forever to connect and it's super slow. I wonder when they are going to fix that. I don't recommend going there, if you need internet. Also, a bit too noisy, and crowded if you plan on quiet studying. But overall good.  I almost forgot, the guy working there makes happy faces and nice pictures on the drinks!

This is only for the Cafe Au Lait.

oh my god, it was so perfectly made, and it was exactly what I needed. They put a lot of care into how it was made even though it was only $2.25 and to-go. The foam was perfect, and the ratio of coffee:milk was as it should be.

Can't vouch for anything else though.

Got the Mocha, not bad at all, it was great how you could actually taste the chocolate, I'm not usually a fan of coffee, or bitter drinks but this was good :), my friend got the latte which was nasty as hell though. Prices decent, good amount of seating but mostly taken due to finals week I'm sure. Everything would have been perfect if the guy who was making my drink wasn't coughing up a storm in my cup... nasty.

Cafe Milano is a place where I walk in, get a cup of house coffee, walk back out into the sunshine.  In the café it's rather dark, very crowded, and you can hear the chatter from the sidewalk on the way in.  Not really conducive for doing good work, if you're easily distracted like me.  And there are too many tastier food options to settle for something from here -- if you want a sandwich, walk a block to Crepes A Gogo, Cheese 'N' Stuff or, best yet, Espresso Experience.  The baked treats and sweets up the hill at Caffe Strada or around the corner at King Pin Donuts are superior.

Milano's strong coffee is the real winner, making it a great pit stop if you're at Cal -- you get twice the flavor and twice the amount for half the price of the Tully's on Sproul, and better service.

Of the two cafes in Berkeley that I can actually productively study at, this is one of them.  I'm not a coffee person but their food items aren't spectacular, but not bad either.  The focaccia they serve with their soup is delish.  

The big thing for me here is the atmosphere.  The music is non invasive and the upper level is pretty peaceful and a good place to stay focused on reading.  It's a nice place to get a little respite from Berkeley.

Hot chicken sandwich on focaccia!!! It's so simple, yet delish. The side salad it comes with is a perfect compliment and the dressing is also good with the sandwich....YES, dip that thang in the dressing I proms you it is good!!

Hey, not too bad! Bike parking nearby, nice high ceilings inside, and typical Espresso Roma fare. If you aren't familiar with typical Espresso Roma, all you need to know is that it's good and that it's not overpriced.

Plenty of seating on two levels inside. There was a sign indicating they have WiFi but I didn't use it.

Good place to sit and get some studying done while enjoying decent food.

Service/Decor: Service is fairly fast; I got my sandwich in 6 minutes after I ordered. There are a fairly large number of tables downstairs, and you can get some studying done upstairs where it's quieter.

Food: I got the avocado sandwich on focaccia, which was $6.75 and came with a simple salad. I was actually very surprised at how delicious the vinaigrette was. It had a slight mustard-y taste and was tangy enough carry my salad as well as my sandwich, which was rather bland but actually really tasty with the vinaigrette (perhaps that is the way to eat it). The mozzarella was of low quality and the only thing awesome about the sandwich was the avocado, but coupled with the vinaigrette it was pretty good.

I'd say I'd return for the sandwich+vinaigrette. Very satisfying, I wasn't hungry for a few hours after. :)

The atmosphere is nice enough, but unless Strada is closed there's not much reason to stroll to Milano. My latte was bitter and relatively disappointing, and the service was typical Berkeley--annoyed and rushed. Nothing worth writing home about.

Despite what is written pretty much everywhere online about Cafe Milano, they only take Visa/MC. On foursquare there's a deal where if you spend $10 on a business you get $10 back if you spend it on an AmEx card, so my buddy and I figured we spend it here since it was an eligible place and we both enjoyed studying here. That didn't work since the guy at the cash register declined my AmEx card, saying the machine does accept it, but was told to only accept Visa/MC. Buyer beware.

Other than that, Internet is really slow (I end up tethering my phone). The sandwich and breads are always really tasty, and I would come back for it. I wouldn't get the soup though, they seem to have more misses than hits with it. Sometimes it would be too watery, then too spicy.

For a study place there's not enough electrical outlets to fuel my devices, and the chairs and second floor is really creaky. I wonder if I'm gonna fall straight through to the kitchen.

Other than that, decor is really neat and it's always crowded during midterms/finals times. Perhaps its the prime location.

Milano cookies, Milano Cafe...anything with the word Milano in it is fabulous.  And this cafe is no exception.

You get the typical Berkeley vibe walking into this cafe:  cheap, good food, and a diverse/interesting environment.  And a view of campus makes it in a great location.

I got the chicken pesto sandwich and an iced tea.  Another excellent Berkeley meal. And a go to a place for any Berkeley student.  

Happy Eating!

I've only come here to get their cheesepuffs to go and they are really savory!  The service has always been great too.

In the future,  I will come back and try something else.  I like this place so far...

Martin and company serve the lattes hot and serve it FAST.  My day will not go well without a soy latte from CAFE MILANO!

At lunch, Salads are yummy.  Foccacia bread and soups are consistently good.  The chicken breast and pesto sandwich with the mixed green salad is divine!

You will find the campus gliteratti are here... um, is it me or do staff and administrators in Sproul Hall have office cubicles and actual offices?  Why is everyone here at all hours of the day?

Want to feel the heartbeat of campus?... it lub dubs here.

This place is very close by campus and other dormitories complex so it's very convenient. I like everything that they sell here, very up to par and very fair with the portion. In summer, they open until 10 pm, but during school year, usually open late until 12 am. Don't expect to find any empty seat here during finals or midterm weeks since many people do come here to get their studying done. 

Contrary to what other people said, this place offers FREE Wi-FI, you have to ask for the password when you purchase their stuff. Wi-Fi can be a bit slow when there's way too many people, however you can always get connected via Air Bears. 

I recommend sitting on the first floor, next to the windows, so you can get a nice view and very close to a nearby power outlet!. Expect to bring your own outlet or extension cord if you want to study here.
the actual coffee isn't all that great, but it is a nice, cozy cafe to chill in...

Pros:
-cool, 2 story
-very "vegetative" atmosphere... much better than brewed awakening across the other side if you ask me

I used to come here almost everyday as a CAL student and enjoyed studying, chatting with friends, browsing on my laptop (wireless connection from CAL - airbears), and having lunch. I love the veggie sandwich with fresh slices of mozzarella cheese, and their soft foccacia bread is my favorite. Blocks of foccacia bread are provided with bowls of soup or salads. Their other sandwiches on the menu are equally delicious. I love sitting right next to the huge, open windows in the front during the hot summer days to people watch.

Service: 4
Taste: 4
Quality: 4
Variety: 4
Price: $2-10 (depends on if you get just a drink or food too)
Recommend to a friend: Yep

I've frequented Cafe Milano quite a few times, and so do a lot of other students. Their drinks are pretty darn good and there is a TON of study space. They have electrical outlets too, so you can always plug in and use your laptop. I've had some problems connecting to their free internet, but I've seen people on gmail and whatnot, so maybe it's just my laptop that's being funny. It's a good place to study or chat. If you want to study, try the upstairs -- it's usually quieter. I haven't tried that many different things here because I usually go with their iced tea with a shot of raspberry Torino, but their pastries are decent, and they sell soup and sandwiches too.

Oh, and they recently added a $2 minimum for credit card purchases, but most things are usually over $2 so this shouldn't be a problem.

This place is a pretty good place to meet up for just having a talk with a friend, but not so much if you want to get work or studying done.

The place is always stuffy, internet is slow, and the place is just too loud.

In terms of food, it's pretty mediocre. The price for a sandwich and salad is about $7, but the sandwich itself is pretty empty. The salad consists of a few greens and some balsamic vinegar. The sandwich is toasted bread, tomato, cheese, and your choice of meat (of which there is not much).

I wouldn't recommend going here for a meal, but the staff of the place are pretty nice if you ever get the chance to talk to them.

Chicken sandwich is pretty bomb. Nice guys behind the counter. Always cool with me.

What's with the crazy guy that posts up at the table by the door, though? I'm assuming he's a brother/friend of the wait staff. That dude is wacko.

i love the salads here
the italian with garbanzo beans, fresh mozzerella, artichoke hearts, roasted bell peppers... yum! also, the greek with feta, greek olives, peppers, tomatoes, onions... so good! 
the sandwiches are good too. the chicken on mexican roll is amazing. the coffee is alright, i prefer the espresso and mochas
the prices are good and the amount of food you get is good
the service is great too.  if you go here you should say hi to the ppl, they are really nice. i used to get a greek salad with artichoke hearts to go, almost every week, at least once a week, and the owner got to know me. he would give me free stuff, like an apple, some strawberries, free artichokes, he was so nice! 

it is a bit too dark for me to study there, but on a bright afternoon it is ok. i recommend just meeting up friends for coffee and food or getting to go.

Good place to meet up with friends. They have plenty of seating. They have two floors. I'm not a fan of their lemonade, but their cofee is okay. They also accept card with a minimum purchase of $2.00. Nothing too special about it other than its right across the street from campus on Bancroft.

I love this place. It's not so much the food or coffee that I love (although both are good) but the ambiance that leads me to give it 5 stars. It is the perfect place to study or meet up with a friend for a long talk. Their salads and sandwiches are good - nothing spectacular - but consistent. And I love how every now and then, the guy who makes my cappuccino will draw a smiley face into it. That makes my day.
Ordered the Mocha Bianca. Love the milk foam!

I went there because it was recommended by a twitter user after I sent a tweet asking about a good study space near the UCB campus. I really like the space, especially the loft area! They have lots of tables so finding one is usually not a problem. 

The lady at the counter was ok. I mean, she was nice, but no smile, just a very monotonous "Hi, what can I get for you?" Even after I switched to Spanish to talk to her she continued with the same attitude.

I had a latte, my usual drink, and went upstairs, picked a table and sat down to do my readings. The only problems I found was that it can get a bit noisy, but hey, it is a cafe, people go there to see meet with friends, I can not expect them to be quiet, that I understand completely. They other thing is that I could not find a plug any where close to where I sat, boo! 

And the last thing I didn't like was that for some weird reason my laptop would not connect to their internet. I'm pretty sure that was just my problem because everybody else was happily surfing the internetz. Oh well, I'm pretty sure I can survive not watching cat videos on youtube for one afternoon. Maybe next time I'll be able to connect, because yes, I'll be coming back, I really liked my latte and it is a great place to watch Berkeley boys.

I love this place. The cashiers and workers are genuinely friendly. Some workers are kinda cute too :). The food is not bad :) my fav is the Italian salad with Raspberry dressing. 

They have wifi, so it's a great place to study. :)

This was a great place to study, even on a weekend. 

My latte was nothing special, but the Avocado sandwich was very great! They don't skimp on the avocados. They could put less dressing on the side salad - but it's nice they add a side salad on at all.

I couldn't get my Internet to work after restarting my computer multiple times, so I wouldn't suggest relying on having internet while you're there. This place could also use some more outlets. However, for a place to meet with your study group or work alone, I'd say this place is ideal.

I understand that the location must be really convenient for students and the open lobby must be great for studying but I still believe that the rating for this place is a bit inflated.

I gave this place a two out of five stars for the following reasons:

Atmosphere: Again, I loved the open lobby and mom and pop atmosphere this place had. However, the chairs were definitely low quality and the tables were not that great in quality either. I think that if the owners of the cafe installed some comfortable seating (like couches) alongside the walls and replaced the tables, you'd find people spending an entire DAY here not just a few minutes. The majority of this place's customer base are students and should be catered to them. Therefore, Cafe Milano needs better seating and better tables for studying.

Now, the product:
I've come here to order at least four times and have had at least three different types of drinks. 
Caramella: Out of all the different types of lattes out there caramel is definitely my favorite. I ordered a 20 oz. the first time I came to Cafe Milano and it was average. I wasn't paying much attention to how the drink was being made but I can say the end product's espresso was a bit weak, the milk definitely re-steamed not fresh, and the foam's quality was average. Aesthetically, this latte looked like a basic latte you'd find maybe at Starbucks (maybe not as bubbly). The second time I came, I ordered the same drink and definitely payed attention to how the drink was being made. The barista there definitely did not keep his equipment clean. I watched him pull the portafilter out of the grouphead, dump the grinds and refill the portafilter without washing it beforehand. Even worse: he did not tamp the espresso inside the portafilter. This is probably why the espresso looked and tasted watered down, even the generous amount of caramel syrup he put into the drink couldn't hide the fact that the espresso inside my latte was weak. My second problem was the steamed milk. I clearly watched him make a drink before mine and use the same pitcher with the same unpurged and uncleaned steam wand, REheat the same milk and use it for my caramella. This is an absolute NO. 
The second drink I've had here is the Mocha Bianca (white mocha), and the problems were the same. Barista training in this store is at an absolute minimum. 
The third drink I've had here is the Cafe au Lait. Not a lot can go wrong with steamed milk and coffee, but I really wish the barista would have put some effort into the foam. WAY too bubbly. Again, did not purge or clean the steam wand. SIGH

All in all, this cafe is probably suitable for students who really just need something to keep them awake while studying. I do not recommend paying $3.40 for a handmade drink here unless you really are looking for a quick fix. For those coffee drinkers who know what I'm talking about I do not recommend anything but normal black coffee here.

i like the chicken sandwich with pesto?  or any hot sandwich in general

i would usually get the greek salad

if you bring in your own mug, they'll usually fill it up to the top and only charge you for a small

the place is kind of dirty/dingy...i wouldn't study there because of the flies, but i was a regular!

Though it has 2 floors, it's hard to find a seat in this cafe, and it's not really that spacious - you'll constantly find yourself excusing yourself as you bump and brush people. The outlets are a bit hard to come by, and the wifi is free but really fickle. 

The stars I give are mostly for the food/drink options.

The coffee is OK, but the place is horrid. The tables are old and the chairs are old... the place itself just is not inviting. 

The sandwiches are of good size, but nothing compared to that of Free Speech Movement (a coffee place on campus).

I've never sat upstairs, but just the atmosphere of this place is not cozy for me to study. 

The only reason I give it two stars is because there is always a table open somewhere.

Cafe Milano has a special place in my heart. When I arrived from Honolulu in late '92, I would walk down from my place on Dwight and Prospect when I was working as a lecture note-taker for Black Lightning and did a lot of writing there. 

Here's one: 

"The Smoke that Moves Toward Me

"It is quiet except for the conversation. The sun comes in the glass at the back of Cafe Milano, where a person sits. I can't seem to catch her eye as she ponders a book of math. It does not calculate, this formulaic mind that looks for hope in solitude and cannot even whisper, longing that must be readable, that must be desperate, that must not have seen sex for years. Whole years, pardon the pun, as if marriage were a place to put the stick and stir. What motions, what potions, what consuming fires cured?

"I rest, for even in my heat, I can see how truly graceful life outside can breathe. I see more than the woman's breath -- the smoke that moves toward me."

I wrote many things there. Over the years, I had shows of my art work and some of them involved large blow-ups of the pages of my books.

I love the place. It is one of the reasons I love Berkeley so much. It is alive with brilliant people. Thank you Cafe Milano for everything you've done for me.

Super friendly service, REALLY good food,  fair prices and generous portions, healthy, fresh produce, the food is consistently great. Since Cafe Intermezzo burned down, this is my new go-to salad and sandwich spot.

There always seems to be an epic line around lunch time, but fear not! They get you in and out with your food very quickly! 
Highly recommend it!!!
Sandwich and coffee are cheap but good. I got a pretty decent lunch there. I kind of like the deco of the place and their coffee is aromatic.

The stars are truly based on my love for their cheese puffs. Creamy, delicious goodness. The cashiers were always friendly to me & every time I am in the area, I make sure to stop by. 

Like any standard coffee shop. Great place to study & get work done. I love the natural lighting that fills the place.

Tried this place on a whim while I was walking about campus.

PROS:
-Lots of seating - downstairs AND upstairs!
-Affordable. Lots of baked items in the $1.50 range...great for poor starving students!
-Fast service.
-A LARGE variety of menu items to choose from
-Quiet (maybe it was because I came here at 10:30AM on a weekday, but I didn't find it all that loud. It was mostly comprised of students studying with a latte or their breakfast).

CONS:
-Can't think of any :)

Will definitely come back when I am on campus.

I want to give this place a 3.5, but there's no option. 

Since so many things to into a review, I'm going to summarize to start.
-Atmosphere: 4/5
-Coffee: 3/5
-Prices: 4/5
-Pastry options: 3/5

The coffee wasn't my favorite, and wasn't particularly strong. They put a beautiful decoration on top of the foam, and that was worth an extra star! They also had a nice selection of syrups.

If you're in the area and looking for a place for a cup of coffee, this place is fun. But you still might manage to get a better latte somewhere else.
The espresso is not bad at all, but the service is. It's not that difficult to be friendly. Especially if you're only a few blocks from Strada.

This is probably one of the worst cafe latte's I've ever had. I literally had to replace half of my coffee with half and half and overdose it with sweeter.  On a positive note, it's a spacious cafe with a lot of room where you can study.

For the three years I lived in Berkeley, this place was my haven (and during the one year in the middle that I spent studying abroad in London, I missed it!). Yes, it's usually crowded, but there is something wonderful about winning a table upstairs right by one of the railings, looking at what feels like half of the Berkeley community coming and going beneath you, and hunkering down to finish that big project or paper (or just that delicious sandwich). In the summer they open up the roof and there is no better place to be "indoors." power outlets are somewhat lacking, but I love this place so much that I took to keeping a power strip in my backpack, just in case I showed up and the weren't any outlets available.

As for food and drinks, I swear by their mocha bianca and almond croissants. That's a valid last meal, right? Also, their sandwiches are pretty delicious. The turkey on focaccia is my favorite, some of the best focaccia bread I've had.

And the service? It might be busy, but the guys behind the counter never get your orders wrong and always greet you with a smile. When business was slower, one of the guys would always draw faces in my mocha foam, always smiling.

Maybe it's just me -- but maybe this is one of the best cafes in Berkeley for sitting and getting work done.

Food: YUM! I love their focaccia bread. I always get the Greek salad because I love feta cheese. By the way, they sell mini salads, they just don't advertise it on their menu. However, I don't think the mini salads are really worth it because they are over $4 and a full size salad is $6

Baristas:...are a bit weird and not very friendly. They're always speaking Spanish and staring at people funnily.

Atmosphere: It's a very Berkeley place. Lots of GSIs holding office hours, students studying, and people discussing everything from politics to relationships.

Bathroom: Only one..and not very clean

Cleanliness: Not very. They don't make sweeps of the areas often..which I understand because they are ALWAYS busy and packed. The chairs and tables are old.

Outlets: Not many.

Wi-Fi: Usually not a problem, but kind of slow at times.

I love to study here around lunch and  after 8pm. I usually order pasta during lunch  and at night I sometimes order tea or hot chocolate The lighting is not so grate at night but love the vibe! This is an awesome place to study with friends!
