One of my favorite places to go when I went to Cal. The space is kinda old, but the decor is warm and inviting. The coffee is delicious and strong. They also have some really good salads and sandwiches; all at reasonable prices for a poor college student. 

It's close to campus and there is usually plenty of seating downstairs and upstairs. Milano was always a go-to spot for my friends and I to study, though studying often turned into chatting. Oh how I miss college...

A friend and I were wandering around Berkeley looking for a quick bite before her interview. We could not find what we were looking for after zig-zagging in and out of places. Finally, we stumbled into Cafe Milano and the Sandwich menu immediately appealed to me. I ordered a Chicken sandwich and she a turkey. The cashier decided that he wanted to save paper and put my friend's order on my ticket. We were okay with that. But when it came time for our orders, they completely forgot about her's. So we waited another 3 minutes and headed upstairs. The restaurant's exterior is plain, but the inside is to die for. :)

Cafe Milano has two floors that are significantly different in their atmospheres. The top floor is brighter & generally quieter with people studying and eating at smaller tables. The bottom floor has always seemed a bit drabby to me - cold and darker - but is equally populated with people meeting & studying. So overall, it is definitely a good place to get work done as most people around you will be trying to do the same. I am not a fan of their coffee or pastries, but their salads & watermelon juice are great. If you have to make a choice for the day, I'd say head down to Musical Offering Cafe or up to Strada to get your coffee & ambiance fix.

I only like the greek salad here. Drinks are really bad. I KNOW because I used to get drinks from strada and ONE day I got a drink at milano and I could definitely taste the difference. A BIG DIFFERENCE. Made class go by very slowly in the morning. 

Gross bathroom (even for Berkeley) and it's kind of unnerving that it's right next to the kitchen. 

Many more bums inside taking naps on those tables that we eat on...Almost ALL of the tables are uneven.... annoyingly jolting from side to side as you try to highlight, write, or read. I would definitely not recommend studying/spending money at this cafe....

Great drinks, friendly service, tasty sandwiches with a salad on the side, upstairs seating as well, wifi, power outlets, great location.  The only con is that due to all these great features, this cafe is typically over crowded, so seating is limited and you end up sitting very close to other people or competing for a spot, especially during exam seasons.  It wasn't quite so crowded (From my memory at least) when I first started at Cal, but since then, it seems to be have gotten very busy more often.  I can't recall ever going in the summer, but I imagine it is much more calm and enjoyable then.

Seriously, I love this place. There is no place or drink or name or anything that sums up my college experience than MILANO. 

I love how it is so difficult to see the name of the place, so when you have a friend who is visiting or new to berkeley it is kind of hard to tell them to meet you there. Then they come, then they love it. Milano isn't overpriced, their drinks are pretty good and the sandwiches are great (the chicken sandwich - highly recommended). I miss my mocha biancas from this place! The staff are friendly (especially the guy with the mullet - that guy is bawws) - if you're looking over at the cake at night before they close sometimes they just give it to you. And the guy with the mullet always draws smiley faces in your coffee. 

The place has two levels and always plays good music. It's a great place to eat, meet or study. In the summer they open the front windows/doors and the whole place becomes very breezy. If you sit close enough to the front you can get air bears (otherwise you have to pay for wi fi).

Berkeley has a lot of great cafes, but all of them fall short for some reason. Strada's outdoor seating is nice when the whether is good, but sucks if it is raining, and aucouqlette (sp?) is really overpriced and has no outlets for your laptop. In all ways, Milano's is the best cafe in Berkeley.

The coffee at Milano is mediocre at best and often just plain bad. Espresso is often burnt and oily. 

Service is nothing special, but it's not like they offer table service. 

The third star is for the food. I quite like their sandwiches, and the vinaigrette they put on their salads is one of my favorite salad dressings ever. It's dead simple, but has exactly the right combination of flavors I want in a salad dressing. If I knew where to buy it, I would. 

Plenty of tables, but wi-fi isn't free, which is super lame. 

A good place to study if you don't need (or want) Internet access and remember to stay away from the coffee.

one of my favorite cafes near berkeley campus, not because of their espresso or sandwiches, but the convenient location and the ambiance it provides. my favorite seating is by the wall window, especially during the bright summer days. i used to go there to work on solving last minute homework problems.

Ah, this place brings back memory.  I studied here when I was still in school, had good and bad times with friends while sitting on the loft, drank their coffee, had their sandwiches.  Wrote a few short stories and even took a picture in their bathroom (beneath the mirror someone wrote "I am love" and underneath it, in a different handwriting, someone else wrote "what's your number?"  I couldn't resist.)

Their food is filling and tasty, their coffee strong.  The background music, when they do decide to play something, is hit or miss.  The atmosphere is relaxed and un-pretentious.  After a few visits you'll also begin to see familiar faces.
Good upstairs seating. A good place to study!

Oh, Milano.

I suppose one might call me a "regular" to your hallowed coffee-steeped walls.

One of your barista always strikes up conversation with me,
(Service: *****)

I have sampled every muffin of yours under the sun, and concluded that only full fat muffins are worthy of my (parents') hard-earned money, though nonfat are an unlabeled but omnipresent option in the display case. Ask for them if you must.   

And who can forget the day I bought a Cafe Americano that sent so much caffeine pumping through my veins that I chipped my tooth on my fork eating salad? 

BUT somehow the saltiness of your amply portioned Lentil Soup rivals the tears shed by pre-meds and engineers upon receiving exam grades.(Value: ****; Taste: ***)

Why is this, Milano?

Why do I brave the noise, crowds, and the few outlets to come to an okay, but not terrific cafe SO OFTEN? (Ambiance: *)

Maybe it's the free wifi.
Mostly, you are just really damn close to campus, and such a fixture in college life that you are the "go-to" meeting place for group work, despite the ill-suitedness of your setting for such an undertaking.
Reading a book at this cafe, you can also enjoy a whispering preach from a "enlightenist" stranger...only in Berkeley.

I had a less than stellar experience here today. I have been here more than once, and their mochas are getting worse. Today really sealed the deal and made me decide that I will not be back for a long time for coffee of any sort. The mocha was so bland that I thought I was drinking very watered down hot chocolate. It wasn't sweet, and it had no coffee flavor. It tasted more like the paper cup it was in. I was disappointed. Like others before have mentioned, the place is dusty and dirty. There are flies. The only reason I am are giving milano two stars is because their sandwiches are decent and the location convenient. Milano, you used to be so good, like when I came for the first time. Now you just disappoint me.
Very good coffee...  but it's 2nd to Cafe Strada...

You can definitely get better coffee in Berkeley but Milano is a great place to spend some time and get work done or catch up with a friend. The cafe's on the grungy side but has its own charm. It's not the ideal but oddly feels like home. You will find all sorts of interesting people there who normally would not congregate. The workers are all super nice and make interesting latte art. I love the huge windows that open up in the front of the cafe as well as on the ceiling. They've got some good food offerings that are easy on a student's budget. 

They also have shotty internet, the bathroom should be avoided but you learn to deal.

Milano's a pretty nice place--their coffee is decent, and the upstairs loft area is really nice, especially on a sunny day. The sandwiches and salads are really good--I especially like the Italian salad (super yummy with the foccacia!). However, the place is a little on the dirty side. There are always flies buzzing around. Otherwise, the atmosphere is pretty nice.

The best lunch salads in Berkeley.

Forget Intermezzo.  Blech.  Piles and piles of sprouts and romaine do not a salad make.  Lines out the door do not lure me in.

For $5.50, you can get a huge Greek salad, with Kalamata olives, piles of feta, red onion, and a lovely blend of mixed greens.  For $5.80, you can get the Italian salad, loaded up with roasted peppers, chickpeas, and fresh mozzarella.  They serve their salads with a spongy and addictive focaccia.  Plus, you can call ahead.  I'm big on calling ahead.  Plus, the coffee is terrific -- Espresso Roma -- and when you purchase a pound of coffee, they give you a free coffee drink.

Finding a table isn't that hard, but during prime times you have to stake your claim amongst all of the undergrads doing their hours of homework.  Such is the plight of the college coffee shop.  In this respect, though, the table turnover is much higher than Strada -- another big plus.

The wifi is a little slow, but it's a nice and convenient place to go to study and get a quick fix of coffee, tea and sandwiches. It's usually packed during midterm season, but usually it's not too difficult to find a place to sit.

I love this cafe!  First, they accept credit cards which is extremely rare for cafes directly in this area.  Second, this cafe has a very open and welcoming atmosphere.  The entire front and roof of the restaurant are open air and the loft seating is extremely charming.  Third, it's convenient, inexpensive, and there are lots of other Cal patrons.

They put bell peppers on almost all of their sandwiches.  I love this but I know that not everyone loves peppers as much as I do.  The turkey sandwich, lentil soup (when they have it) and Italian salad are my favorites.  The drinks and pastries are meteocre (hence, 4 stars) but they have bagels.

This is a café I frequent when I was an undergrad during those far far away college dayz. It was where I met my GSI, had my lunch (my favorite avocado sandwich), chatted with my friends, spent my solo study hours. This is also the café that got me hooked to the whole "café culture." Ever since Milano, I judged every café with it as my yardstick (most, however, failed miserably!). I just LOVE Café Milano! This is certainly one of my favorite café spots in Berkeley (tied with Caffe Strada and Sacks). It is always breezy and airy, with the right amount of natural light and the perfect amount of "dimness" that every café needs. The exposed red brick walls are gorgeous. They have high, wooden ceiling with open roof, from which green plants hung and gleam under the sunlight. Classical music is always in the background, and the whole setting is very European and charming. There are flyers on and next to the staircase that tell you all the happenings (events, concerts, talks) in town. Staff is always laid-back and friendly. Food is always tasty. Walk up the wooden staircase to the second floor, and you're in a quieter space - perfect for reading or solo studying. Free wifi! Café Milano = Cozy, lovely, alive, and just beautiful.

Really good location especially if you go to college at Berkeley. I've only been here once but based on my experience, it was pretty decent. The amount of coffee and hot chocolate is pretty good especially for their prices. In my hot chocolate they also added a cute little design :) of an elf or something. But the real thing to get is the cheesecake. I have no idea why but it was insanely good. Its represents for all the cheesecake in the world. I think about it when I think about cheesecake.... Yes, its that amazing. Good environment to bring your friends! I would have to stop by if I were in Norcal.
never had the coffee, but i don't like the sandwiches.  try cafe intermezzo on telegraph or stuffed in on euclid instead.

Just graduated from Berkeley, and boy do I miss Cafe Milano.  I remember spending whole days at Cafe Milano studying for finals. This place is ideal - free wifi, food, drink, and no bed to tempt me to take a nap. Food was descent (minus their pastries) and the staff would draw cute cartoons in my delicious caffeine beverages.

Really great place to study and have a coffee. Prices are decent. My only complaint is that there aren't many electrical outlets, and wifi is spotty. But its close enough to campus to connect to AirBears!

This place is ok. I think the staff are all nice. I have never had issues with them. I like their drinks and they are very fast...I never have to wait long for my drink. The down side is that you can never find a table...the best ones are always taken.

Food is good, but coffee needs some work. A lot of work.

Basically, it's standard cafe roma fair - bad espresso, mediocre coffee, pretty good coffee shop food. They have a fair amount of space to study, but considering there is no free wifi I would definitely recommend somewhere else (I assume people who voted for free wifi as an attribute are probably referring to airbears, which (1) requires a berkeley login and (2) doesn't get signal in most of milano)

We came here for a little pick me up while walking around CAL and the man that took my order was just either a major grump or didn't think I was funny. (I think it was the former, because I'm freakin' hilarious!)

I had never been there (he might have thought differently since I'm Asian and we all know that CAL is populated with Asians) and I asked if the Mocha iced drink was delicious. He just looked at me and then said, "it's blended." Okay... not what I was asking for, but I ordered, paid the man and realized it's not delicious. It was too mochay and my boyfriend ordered the hot chocolate and his was too milky.

I'm sure this is a wonderful place to go, they had food and other drinks (the coffe smelled delicious, but I was already hot from walking around everywhere and wanted something cool) but the service I got from that grumpy bumpkin made me give this place a 2 star.

I would have given this cafe a one star, except they have good soups.

Last semester, I came here every week for study group sessions and would always order their regular coffee. First, their coffee TASTES LIKE SHIT. I know, i always order it and never learn my lesson, and end up throwing that shit away after taking a couple of sips. I started ordering the mocha coffee which does a better job since the chocolate powder masks the taste, but you could still taste the shitty coffee bean that they use. Second, i have ordered soups for here as well as to go. They give moderately well proportions if you order it for here, but when i ordered it to-go the second time, it was half the proportion for the same amount of price. Third, I ordered one of their sandwich two weeks ago since i've heard from friends that they make really good sandwiches. When I received my order, i was disappointed and pissed to find 2 FREAKIN LONG STRANDS OF HAIR running across my sandwich. Seriously?! I've been a regular at this place, usually ordering just the flavored italian soda since all their coffees taste shitty, so im sure the workers their recognize me, but don't give off that friendly vibe at all. seems like they're only there for profit.

i'd rather take my cash elsewhere, spend a couple more dollars and go further to starbucks or peet's to get a better quality coffee

So, I know I'm an astrophysics student, and have very little reason to be on the south side of campus, but I, for better or worse, know the south side much better than the north side, much to my chagrin. And of course like any student, I like studying, lounging, relaxing, chatting, and meeting people in cafes. And there happen to be three that I frequent on Bancroft. Milano is one of them.

In terms of coffee etc, its adequate. Pastries are fine, nothing to rave about, never had any of the sandwiches or heavier fare so I can't offer warnings/recommendations. But these, as many will tell you, is not the reason to go to Milano. What Milano has, that none of the other cafes seem to have, is the most awesome skylight and loft. I can remember more than once meeting people up in the loft for a chat or game of chess, and loving the skylight even more. Even the downstairs is a great place to relax. And the plants aren't fake!!!! If this makes a difference. ;)

So for a great relaxing place to drink, chat, and study, MIlano more than fits the bill.

Last time I came, Mocha Bianca was good pastrami sandwich was good.

This time, Chai Latte too watered down and carrot cake absolutely flavorless.

Wifi nonexistent.

I really want to like this spot. Maybe a third time will prove successful

Ok, listen berkeley. Today I have a special treat for you: I'm reviewing with my twinsey Susannah D. So prepare for double-time on this review.

Let's get the basics out of the way: 'cross the street from campus, okay for studying, split-floor and classical music (no lady gaga, for better or worse). More spacious than most cafes.

Susannah: Their chai's pretty good. Solid level of foam, which is sweeet. A water fountain, which is kinda convenient.

Asaf: Their coffee's fair, their soy hot chocolates makes me sad. 90% foam (we disagree about the plus-or-minus status of foam). Also, the service is "we get you your shit and you take care of the rest." As in, expect none, not even a "hello." I've had experiences here where I'm not even acknowledged, I just hand over the card.

On a more positive note, sandwiches are said to be of quite good quality, though neither of us have tried their "food food."

But all in all, "it's a pretty basic cafe." You gotta get some studying done (good for groups), get some chillin' in, come here. You're looking for more, gotta walk more than a block! This review happened in 2 minutes. During one of which Susannah distracted me. She's totally sweet spice and I'm bitchy spice, apparently. Whatevs.

The salads here are huge and come with giant pieces of yummy focaccia bread that just couldn't be good for you.  The tomato soup felt more like minestrone but wasn't bad.  The place is full of students but there are plenty of tables.

Atmosphere: 4/5
service (cashier) 5/5
Would definitely come here if in the area. Double the amount of coffee and better taste for half the price of starbucks. 

Cafe Milano is a nice place to get coffee and relax with friends. I went to get a regular sized latte for $3.10 and it was huge. I was not expecting it to come in a big drinking glass (like the kind you get for water at a restaurant) for that price. I could barely finish it. My friend also got one and thought it was great. I take my coffee without sugar or honey. Without anything, the latte was great and the thick layer of foam on top was very creamy. 

It was a warm day so the open door and glassless window made the setting perfect. My friend and I sat near the window and chatted. We had to move a table over because we both noticed everybody around us was studying and didn't want to bother them. You gotta use your library voices in here. It's not a loud place. Half the people were studying and half were having quiet chats and eating.
Never eaten here...just met friends here for coffee.  A great place to meet when the weather isn't so nice!  Coffee was always good and pretty reasonable.  Nice and close to campus!

Favorite coffee shop around Berkeley campus by far. Good coffee and espresso related beverages, no fuss nor nonsense, laid-back atmosphere with good music, and open reasonably late (like every coffee shop Should be!).

Only downside is that seating can get a bit scarce, but the melange of customers makes for ample people-watching or satisfying conversation eavesdropping.

Came into the cafe to grab a quick bite with my girlfriend while we were visiting the UC Berkeley campus. We asked the person working the front what the soups today were and he responded in Spanish, with his coworkers and kitchen crew laughing in response. Assuming he said something rude, my girlfriend and I just looked at each other and decided to ignore it. When we had decided what we would like, he made deciding the type of bread and salad dressings very awkward, barking out hostile confirmations to the questions we had already answered. I'm no sensitive sally, i'm 20 years old, but I could tell this guy was intentionally being a prick.. and it was quite upsetting that he ruined the experience. The man I am talking about was in his 30s or 40s, with long black hair in a pony tail. 

The food on the other hand, was delicious. What a shame to ruin it with the service that we couldn't stop shaking our heads about while eating. I highly recommend the pastrami. If you're starving and in the area, the food is delicious, but I believe that businesses striving to treat customers the right way should have your money, not this one.

I really like this place.  The guys behind the counter are really nice and friendly.  I frequent this place during the semester.  I'm totally in love with the caramel lattes (caramel sauce, not the syrup) and they are priced pretty fairly.

The food is pretty good, too.
The mocha bianca is fantastic but I wouldn't study here due to the spotty internet. But the guys making the coffee are always friendly and talkative.

open air sky lights
upstairs it's almost like a tree house
sweet smiles
numi tea

= more studying.

I spend a lot of time in this cafe, mostly for studying.

As a study location, this  place is pretty OK. They have abundant seating and free wifi. I've never been disappointed by any food or drink item I've gotten here. I normally go with a salad, which is big in size and come with some bread. Their cakes and pastries are pretty on par too. Teas and coffees are pretty good; nothing life-changing. 

The cons are that the lighting is not the best, especially on the second floor. There are also not nearly enough outlets to satisfy the number of laptops. If possible, bring a  power strip and be the hero of those around you. 

It gets pretty packed around midterms and finals, but overall, I enjoy studying here.

i'm not a fan of this place.. tho my 2 friends and former coworkers were regulars... i think more for convenience than taste tho..

granted ive only tried their house coffee, americano, mocha, and bianca mocha.. i gotta say it's overpriced for what it is - bad coffee. 

well.. once their peppermint mocha was nice.. so was their bianca mocha after a week of coffee abstinence.

always taste burnt (not in a good way cus i love dark roasted STRONG espresso/coffee) and service is not great unless you're all glammed up.. too bad for me when im rushing off to class...

Stopped into Cafe Milano on a trip to visit Berkeley's campus.  I had breakfast - an everything bagel with cream cheese, plus orange juice.  The bagel was actually quite good, but that's probably because I'm used to Minneapolis' strangely crappy bagel selection.  OJ was standard.  Boyfriend got a latte and chocolate croissant - both were fine.  Nothing to rave about.  A-OK.

I enjoyed listening to the guy behind me (possibly a TA) school a young girl (most possibly a freshman) on writing a book report.  He couldn't have been more pretentious, and she couldn't have soaked it up more.  Ah, young love.

Love to study here with the smell of coffee in the air and just the right amount of noise. I always get the mocha bianca. If you drink inside Milano, the baristas always draw pretty pictures on the white foam of your coffee. It always makes my day when I see it.

I would never come here to study but that goes for any cafe since I need a sterile environment to study in. So I cannot review it as a study place but as a restaurant I love it. Their sandwiches, salads, etc. are delicious and for a great price. I come here 4-5 days a week. I love Cafe Milano and am craving it down here in Southern Ca.

Highly recommend.
Strong coffee and nice staff.  Love the cappuccino drawings!

I don't drink coffee, but I was once a college student at Berkeley, and there was no better study spot than Cafe Milano, with it's amazing sandwiches and salads and ambiance. I remember writing papers here, hanging out with choir friends before a concert, meeting a friend weekly for lunch and gravitating every time to the 2nd floor for our usual sandwich-and-salad combinations. I DO have Cafe Milano cravings--in my opinion, this is the best cafe in Berkeley.
The coffee is mediocre and it's full of undergrads.  Yerg.  The food is... acceptable?  If you're hungry?  Of course the reason to go is that it's convenient to campus, and I can't deny that.

A really average place serving your average sandwich.

I remember having to drink 2 cups of water because the sandwich was on the dry side and the salad dressing was really sour. The flies in the store were a distraction, killing the peaceful setting of the calm music they had playing.

I usually go here when I need to study with someone and I DON'T need my computer. Outlets here are very, very limited. 

Atmosphere: decent amount of seating on both the bottom and the top floor. When it's busy, it can get cramped and crowded.

Food: There sandwiches are pretty good. I really like the tuna sandwich - it has this light flavor to it. The salads are pretty tasty too. Prices aren't too bad as well. You'll be paying about $6-$7 on a sandwich.

Drinks: Soy Chai Lattes are always good. Theyre never watered down which makes me a happy camper

Service: A little below average. The guys at the cashier can be kind of snappy sometimes. Makes me sad =(

Overall: Good place to get some work done (remember, WITHOUT a computer, unless you'll be using it for a short time). Food and drinks are good as well.

I spent a good portion of my time here eating lunch and reading Shakespeare last summer when I took classes at Cal. It is a very comfortable atmosphere and I like their food, their coffee and their prices. I miss it. Santa Barbara doesn't have anything like this.
This cafe is a must when visiting Berkeley. The coffee is strong and sandwiches are great! Plus, the staff is always friendly, which makes your experience quite nice.
Great location, good coffee, good snacks. The upstairs space is very conducive to groups studying, and is pretty cozy (though the tables are rather small). Try it out!

Their chai lattes and turkey/chicken pesto sandwiches are good. Wifi is practically nonexistent. I'd advise against the pastries... there are always flies buzzing around in the display.

The guy who takes my order will sometimes slip in some Spanish which catches me off guard ("Para aqui?" "What? Oh, si. Thank you.")

There's something quaint about this place-- their brick walls, the open roof letting in sunshine, the tree in the middle of the establishment, filled with the chatter of college students and the stench of the occasional hobo. Nice place to study or grab a drink near campus.

Cafe Milano in my life has served as mostly the place where I meet GSIs during their office hours here or where I meet up with groups and clubs I am a part of. The big tables up stairs are great for big groups and afford enough privacy to be able to talk about club business yet intimate enough to make the time pass while planning lesson plans for 2nd graders with other energy starved students.

In terms of food, I recommend the bagel sandwiches and washing it down with a yummy soy chai latte.

As far as cafes go, Cafe Milano is pretty average. There's nothing particularly special about their coffees or teas and their pastries are pretty good. Their sandwiches are decent and come with a salad, and are priced fairly.

This place could definitely use some renovations: their tables and chairs are all old and wobbly, and the benches along the walls are really uncomfortable. For a cafe that so many people use as a place to study, there's definitely not enough power outlets. The lighting is also way too dim, and although there's free wifi it's too slow to actually use, you'll spend more time trying to connect and reconnect than actually actually using the internet. If you sit by the window, you can get a decent but spotty Airbears connection though. This place also gets pretty crowded at times and it can be hard to find a seat. 

Not sure about other people, but the times that I've gone, the staff aren't particularly friendly. Also during the warmer months there seems to be an abnormally high number of flies.

Went here for NaNoWrimo write-ins this year, coming from the other side of the tunnel, and I gotta say that this place is worth it.  The space is absolutely amazing; you would never guess what a gem of a cafe fit into the narrow space.  I love their pastrami sandwiches, and they let you make some crazy coffee/tea drinks if you ask.  

Not a lot of outlets, but the atmosphere and the food make up for it for me.  

I'd write more but I'm really tired.  I LOVE CAFE MILANO.
It's a good place to study since everyone around you is studying, but not good if you can't handle crowds and noise.

I've only tried the Mocha Bianca here and I feel no need to try anything else. The first time I got it with a macaroon, which was most definitely not a good move on my part. Too much sugar in one sitting and I felt like a fatass afterwards. The macaroon is covered in chocolate and huge so this is a shoutout to all my fellow coconut-lovers out there! 
My friend got the ham&cheese sandwich and the price was pretty reasonable for the portions.

Get an iced latte, trot across the street, attend lecture, and actually stay frightfully awake and alert for the next hour or two. One thing I never liked is how GSIs often hold OHs at popular cafes like Milano ,and how I could never spot my GSI amongst the sea of eclectic Berkeley folk once I got into the Milano's darkened chambers.

Man this place is crowded during lunch hours. But there should be plenty of seating. I had the hot chicken sandwich and the side salad with lemonade. The prices are decent, slow service during heavy traffic hours, and good tasted good. I've visited many cafe's, and there's basically the same exact themes to all of them, and this one is barely different than the other 30948309483 cafe's around Berkeley. If you're looking for the status quo, come here.

The equivalent of Free Speech Movement Cafe, but on the southern edge of campus. However, there's no outdoor seating and it's generally a little dirtier. The sandwiches, on the other hand, are similarly tasty and it's just as good a spot to intend to do work and end up people-watching or bumping into an acquaintance. It's busy, crowded, and vibrant -- and the food and drinks are both tasty and reasonably priced. Hurrah for accepting cards! 

Beware: the restroom is pretty damn shady.
large bug in my salad today.  yuckkkkkkk.
The drinks are average, the ambiance is fantastic.  Beautiful upstairs seating area with sky lights and ample seating.

Cafe Milano is one of my fave spots in Berkeley for reading and studying or just pretending to do so. I love sitting upstairs and people watching, it can get a little crowded during peak hours but I always manage to find a table. Their salads are humongous, which makes me happy. It's funny to watch people vie for the two outlets upstairs, so be prepared. The bathroom is not the greatest, but the open skylight in the cafe more than compensates.

I'm not gonna lie, the primary reason I frequent Cafe Milano is its location. It's hardly a minute's walk from Sproul and is a good place to hang out with friends or get some studying done between classes, but that's about it. Their coffees have never impressed me and the decor is none too impressive either; their new paintings are nice, but their dirty restroom needs to be taken care of. 

I've never gotten any food here because I've seen flies in their food display case (where they keep the muffins, cakes, fresh fruit etc. ICK ICK ICK). This place isn't the best and isn't very sanitary, and it tends to get packed with students, particularly over the weekends. No really, it does. It's like CLAUSTROPHOBIA CENTRAL during midterm and final season(s).

Also, their internet is extremely slow and frustrating. I can only get the bare minimum done before tearing my hair out in frustration and heading to Philz. Sigh. Still, it's a decent Berkeley cafe.

A quick place to get a decent tasting sandwich.  It was pretty fresh and includes a side salad and drink.  For 6 bucks.  I had the turkey sandwich which was decent on whole wheat bread.  The salad had very sweet dressing which I could have done without.  Some place to chill at.

Overpriced sandwiches. Dirty cafe, full of flies. Once, I saw flies in the dessert case, crawling over the croissants. Don't come here if you care for your health. There are plenty of better alternatives in Berkeley. The salads are also overdressed.

Best white mochas ever. Great place for just hanging out, but it can get pretty crowded. Free wifi (you have to ask for the password), great food, excellent coffee, and a central location. I heart Milano!
Ordered a double cappuccino. They misunderstood and made two drinks. They insisted on giving me $3 back.

Very charming cafe with large, open window doors right by campus.  There is a cozy, upper level perfect for studying and they actually play good classical music.

They've upped the prices on the drinks, so get your Italian sodas elsewhere, perhaps Strada?  I haven't had the salads or sandwiches, but the raspberry croissants are heavenly, especially if you have them toasted.

I have to say that the cafe is not very clean, especially the ground level and the bathroom.  Often times, there are bums hanging around in Milano, but they are harmless.  It's also difficult to connect to AirBears, but they may have added their own wifi network.

Top three favorite foods: 

1. Tuna Sandwich
2. Italian Salad
3. Bagel with 'the works' 

Their honey-dijon dressing is the best!

cafe milano is the indoor equivalent to caffe strada. good coffee, great atmosphere, and a bit cozy. Often a favorite for professors to meet students to talk about papers or whatnot.  It's a great study place when its not finals and you can find a seat

I love Milano!!!! The staff remembers you and treats you like a person, the food is good, the coffee is yummy, and there's always nice music playing in the background. PLUS when it's warm outside, they open the large windows, which is excellent. It's the perfect place to study, have a meeting, or just grab lunch/coffee. Love it. 

My only critique would be that they need a couple more outlets. . .

This is another cafe where there's so many students going through that I have serious doubts about how clean the tables and seats actually are. I like their setup a lot though - there's a lot of indoor seating and indoor foliage.

Food is alright. I've gotten cakes, Italian sodas, salads, sandwiches, and bagels here. They burnt my bagel once, but apologized a lot for it and offered to remake it (I declined because it wasn't THAT big of a deal to me), so that was okay. Their actual meal foods are kind of average - plus, they seem to not keep all the ingredients they need in stock because they were unable to make me a salad once.

The seats at this place is fucking shite....a form of torture and dissuading many to stay there as little as possible.  The workers there are fine, they`re good people just trying to move you along.  The cafe is one of the remnants of *wanting to NEVER BE CAUGHT DEAD THERE.  But not everyone here is a hipster, so this place is as good as you make it.

I first went there in 1990, then 97-04 and recently in 08.

It's dirty and noisy and the pastries are not tops.

However, the coffee is good. Sometimes, too, the foam will be decorated, and I'm a sucker for foam art. Another plus is that despite the noise and crowdedness, there is always seating--albeit dirty, unbussed seating.

3.5 stars

the coffee is not all that awesome (read: burnt; if you like starbucks you might be just fine) but the chocolate croissants are above average and the lunch food is respectable.

If I'm in the neighborhood and can't stomach some blondie's or fat slice, I'd opt for cafe milano.

I come here once or twice a week to get coffee and have a chat with a friend. This is a coffee spot in Berkeley that takes credit card WHILE being reasonably priced. My impressions:
Drip coffee - Tastes like coffee rather than straight bitter. Take that, Starbucks...
Lattes/Cappuccinos - Pretty average, I generally prefer Cafe Strada down the street since they have some crazy milk steamer that makes perfect foam. However, if you don't order to-go they like to do some latte art (actually, probably just syrup). More likely if you're a pretty girl - my friend got a picture which she insists were a pair of nipples, but all I saw was a smiley face.......
Caramella/Mocha Bianca - Do you like sugar? 
Hot Chocolate - This one's just awesome. Moreso if you like dark chocolate. Good for when it's cold out and you don't need a caffeine fix.

All in all, it's a good spot to hang out. I don't know why people come here to study what with the lack of outlets and wireless internet.

I've always thought this place was okay.. like the people below me have said, it's crowded, noisy, and the internet's really flaky even though it's so close to campus. There's lots of seats, but the upstairs tables are kind of weird. At some tables, the chairs are connected so if one person gets up, we all feel it haha.

It's a great place to study at especially on a Sunday morning. It's probably a better place to socialize. The coffee and pastries aren't that fresh, but they're still affordable..My favorite is the ham and cheese croissants.
Good coffee, and great place to study. If only they had more outlets for my laptop!

I like it here! So wonderful how close this place is to campus. They have a good menu with lots of variety for breakfast, lunch, coffee and tea. Yay for options! I particularly enjoy the upstairs loft and the fact that they only play classical music. Don't like how there aren't any power sources upstairs.

The place is decent. I've been here a few times, ordered my coffee, and have never been impressed with the place. It is interesting as to how this place is always packed...maybe since it is close-by the campus...but there are definitely better places near campus to get good coffee.

They have two floors, but I have stopped checking the second floor, as everyone always guns for those first in choosing seats. Eh...
"Their coffee restores my faith in humanity."

The staff is friendly, the desserts are tasty, the soy chai is perfect if you ask for it strong, the internet is slow, the ambiance is conducive to studying, the high ceilings/ huge windows/classical music make a great coffeeshop atmosphere.

i worked at milano when i was an undergrad.  back then, all the cashiers were female students and the busboys and coffee makers were mexican men.  it was my first real job and the only reason i was able to stay in berkeley over the summer after my first year rather than moving back home with my parents.  i will love it forever for this reason alone.  

i lived near ashby bart and i would leave my house at 5am and walk to bart in the dark when i had to open and then run to catch the last train home when i closed, for barely more than minimum wage.   

i learned to drink espresso and ate almost all my meals there.  i was also generous to others.  we pretty much only served salads, soup and 2 kinds of sandwiches on focaccia, tuna and vegetarian.   i still can't look at focaccia bread without feeling sick and nostalgic at the same time.   

i met a lot of cool people as well as randoms who would recognize me later but whom i would have no recollection of.  the asian guy from harold and kumar was a regular.  having that job definitely made me less shy.  i quit after i got a campus job that paid more and didn't require me to get up at the crack of dawn or stand on my feet for 6 hours at a time before and after class.

My favorite coffee house in berkeley right now.


Great Latte, plenty of seating, 2-stories, free wifi, open late. Beautiful building.

Great ambiance (two floors, high ceiling). A great place to study or relax, though the loud mexican polka music detracts from the experience.

Food: generous portions for a low price. The sandwiches are OK. The salads are consistently overdressed. 

The espresso is especially harsh. You can see the barrista at work as you order. They don't know how to make the stuff -- I've never, in many visits, seen them tamp down the grounds before brewing, and this is a basic, fundamental, crucial, do-not-pass-Go, Espresso-making 101 step.

Still, the place is cheap, there's always seating, and you can hang out without feeling rushed. Two stars for the food and drink, one extra for the space. Just don't expect a good cuppa.

Great place to go and get some work done. I feel safe there and I trust my fellow study-ers to watch my stuff when I pop off to the men's room for a couple of minutes. 

The other patron's there are always civilized, they will watch your seat for you if you step away (even if you don't ask them to). 

And the employees there really know what they are doing and they don't bother you if you spend 8 hours there and only buy one thing. 

The only thing is I don't care too much for their food selection and I've had better mocha's, but other than that, I'm pretty much a regular at this place, I love it! and shopping is just around the corner if you're a shop-o-holic like me. :)

wifi gets a little slow and spotty at times, so just save it for the casual page browsing while doing some work/just enjoying coffee+food

the drink choices, while not terribly limited, aren't entirely impressive either with the variety.  The prices, however, are completely okay
My favorite here is the hot turkey sandwich, which they make with pesto, turkey, bell peppers, and cheese. I came here today and they gave me wheat bread instead of foccacia without warning me. Fumed silently for a while, but it was still good! all was well. 

If you enjoy studying in a cafe with some character and don't mind the little sounds of hustle&bustle, cafe milano's a great place, located conveniently sproul plaza (:

Sure, there are a few clouds of flies in various areas you have to walk through, but that's not a shock what with the open roof and windows.

On that note, I love the look and feel of this place. It looks almost like an outside cafe in a garden, except with most of a ceiling. Anyone know what they do when it rains? As much as I loved being able to see the clear blue sky overhead, it seems like it'd be a pain then... although I guess it doesn't rain much here. (This would never fly back home in Chicago!)

I only had an iced coffee (ordered a large, charged for a medium, woo!), but it was just what I needed. This was a great place to read, and I'll definitely be back soon with a new book and order a sandwich.

I often stop here if I have a moment to spare before catching a film at PFA or hopping on a bus. When weather permits I like to snag a table near the open windows, or enjoy the the cozy, wooden loft, which makes me feel like I'm in a treehouse. And who doesn't love a treehouse?

Great location, Great latte.

I love sitting in their upstairs loft area.  I used to stop by this place all the time between classes. I like their coffee. I noticed in berkeley they tend to put coffee in clear mugs. They do that here too. I like that :)

Oh, Milano!  Why so dirty?  The number of places near campus that get away with this level of dirtiness never ceases to amaze me.  Good for a coffee to go, but can't stomach anything more from this filthy spot.
Great, friendly staff and quality espresso drinks. Bagels were yummy and the open seating area is a plus. Perfect place to study or to relax.

A great place to duck into when walking down Bancroft and you're starving, needing coffee, and/or have work to do but not feeling like studying on campus. There's free wifi with purchase, plenty of seating, good access to outlets, and a nice open, airy feeling to the place. Yet there's nothing particularly enticing about the food or the coffee, which is why I specifically say "starving" or "needing." Still, I have every intention of being a repeat customer, because above all, it's an accommodating environment.

Milano fulfills two of the three requirements for a good study place for students. 

+ Lotsa' tables, decent sized too!
+ Decent food, drinks and snacks

Still missing some goodies...

-  NO WI-FI, WTF!?
-  Unless for the 2-3 outlets upstairs, downstairs is void of any (unless you use the x-mas lights)
-  Can't they stay open later?

Final Call:
Better than Strada and for Southsiders, this is a good bet for those that want to study into the early eve.

Oh Cafe Milano.
I remember when I passed by this cafe when I was doing college visit in Berkeley.
My first impression was, "EW, it's gross." However, it became my #1 cafe in Berkeley.
Aside the fact that it's super close to the campus, I love their food, especially Chicken sandwich, salad, and Caramel latte! 
It's very spacious, still it's hard to find sitting during midterm/final period. 

I love this place to pieces!
awesome iced cafe latte, i love it.

Like Strada, many people come here to study and do work. Or they just like having people look at them do work. Either way, good coffee and good sandwiches gives this cafe a classy feel that I would entertain because it's closer than FSM and safer than Strada. However, I still can't figure out whose idea it was to serve hot coffee in a pint glass.

It's ok. Everything about this place is ok: the coffee, the pastries...

Maybe everything is even "pretty good". But I don't understand the cult obsession. Berkeley friends of mine keep dragging me here, and it's always fine, but never something i crave or would chooseon my own.

This is a review of Cafe Milano's espresso.

Cafe Milano's espresso fucking sucks.

hints of motor oil, with strong notes of burnt rubber and battery acid, plus a lingering charcoal aftertaste.

And yes, I came back to give them a second chance, and was again astounded by the undrinkable sludge they SELL to hundreds of students every day...

lighting sucks.  really.

always feels awkward because you're way too fucking close to the people at the next table, and sometimes you're facing them...then you try to avert your gaze, and you look all psychopathic.

what is with those benches upstairs where your butt slides backwards in them and lodges permanently unless aid comes?  how does anyone get anything done there?

there is no obvious sign outside, so if you ask someone to meet you there, even people who've been at berkeley for 3 years can't freakin find the cafe.

**************start happy anecdote**************

one time, the guy making the latte drew a really cool cartoon face in the foam of my latte.  it made me smile. 

**************end happy anecdote**************

I had a second horrible experience that forced me to demote my two-star rating to one-star.
Cons:
Inattentive baristas.
Stale muffins.
Weak coffee.
Outlet deficiency.

Pros:
Across the street from campus.

I should have gone to the Coffee Bean.
----
They don't pay attention to the customer. I ordered a mocha glacier (a frappucino-type of thing) and they gave me a regular mocha. I wanted a cold drink, not a hot one. Now I'm heated up about it.

I have so many great memories at Cafe Milano during my undergraduate years at Cal. 

1. Studying countless hours upstairs for a midterm or final 
2. Thinking of and writing sketches with my sketch partner for jericho! Improv
3. Overhearing interesting conversations from the colorful group of people who often hung out at the cafe
4. Complaining about the music that played with my friend 
5. Hearing my dad squeal in delight after he had the chicken sandwich for the first time - 

About that. My dad is obsessed with Cafe Milano's chicken sandwich. If I ever came home, first thing he demanded was that I bring along with the chicken sandwich. Whenever he visited, no other restaurants would be even be considered for food. He'd pick the sandwich over a free meal at Chez Panisse. He'd pick the sandwich over my mom.

The food is delicious - great salads, great sandwiches (clearly). The drinks are so-so - the mochas, what I generally ordered, had good and bad days. Regardless, Cafe Milano is a wonderful cafe and a very "Berkeley" place to go

Negative point - no free wifi and shady with AirBears.

I spent almost my whole life in Milan..so I had to go in a place called Cafe' Milano... right? I was attracted by the location... and I found a very good, fresh and cheap lunch...
too good too fresh and of course too cheap in comparison with Milan... and this is cool!!!
good job gold star for u!

Yes!  I'm so glad I found this place because it is yummy, fresh, and affordable.  I just had a simple Italian salad, with big chunks of fresh mozz, peppers, art hearts, lots of fresh lettuce, tomats, yumminess.  Big slice of focaccia, not oily enough, but overall for about 6 bucks a great deal and a delicious lunch.

Not my favorite coffee shop in Berkeley, but good nevertheless. Their mocha bianca is a good blend of being both sweet white chocolate and espresso. I like it way better than Cafe Strada.

The service is good, they don't rush you when there's a line and one worker does one of those coffee art things on my mocha when he's working. Also, once received a free cookie, but it might be because worker was in the giving-mood ( the customer in front of me had a young son who was given a free cookie and I might have benefited by being directly behind and young looking...)

A decently yummy lunch place with good coffee, but I just can't take the ghetto-dirtiness of it all. The sandwiches are good and well-priced, my latte even had a little bit of artwork in it, but I had to move someone's old cup from my table (which, by the way was falling apart, I almost expected termites to come crawling out of the sides) and it was so crowded, I felt like I was eating on top of my neighbor's Mac book.

I think I would really like this place if they cleaned it up. If they are trying to work the urban-ghetto look of most berkeley cafe's... its just not flying.

Big thick and fat gangsta homemade bread meets a mound of meat, cheese, and all the fixings. How could you go wrong with their gangsta sandwiches? You just cant.

Now not only is this place infamous for serving up a hearty sandwich. They also happen to have one of the most insane salads out there. I mean you could finish these things but you probably are hurting. And that from a Salad of all things! Just imagine what the sandwiches will do to you. 

This is how my trip to this place usually ends. I eat way to much good food, fresh food at that, and I usually end up sitting on the sidewalk, back to a wall of one of the local telegraph shops, and napping. Only to wake up with a few pennies, a quarter, and the occasional gutter punk sitting next to me eating the left overs I could not finish.

FOOD COMA...

I am only here because I have no choice.

I needed a cafe that was close to Telegraph x College and indoors, as I have a laptop and it's forecasted to rain heavily this afternoon (which has all of the Bay Area freaked since this is the first major storm of the season. As an aside, I spent the last year in NY and I think a major storm here is still considered a light drizzle on the East Coast. But anyway...) Strada was out of the question as the indoor seating is about as plentiful as the parking in this area (read: nil).

So I arrived, scavenged for 10 min looking for a wall outlet (in this large cafe, there's only about 6 outlets TOTAL, most of which are upstairs). I couldn't find any so I'm now running off of very little battery power and was mad enough to spend it posting this review. I asked for the WIFI password. It cost me $1 to get the 20-character password. ONE DOLLAR? 

And, by the way, you can't really get good Airbears or Free WiFi coverage here; not sure why, as it is right across the street from Cal. Anyway...

Did I also mention that the food is mediocre quality? The coffee is certainly cheap ($1.35), but you get what you pay for: watered down, and flat-tasting. The food here is okay. Keep in mind, though, that SF Soup Company is 2 doors down... and Durant food court is 1 block south... and the food there is loads better.

The service is average. These aren't exactly the people who will smile at you when you order. They'll just ask you what you want, then give it to you. At least they usually get the order right.

Bathrooms: well, there's one. I'd say it's on the border between sanitary and thank-God-the-lights-aren't-brighter.

The seating makes me happy that I have built-in cushioning on my ass. It's predominantly wooden benches that sink backwards. As in further away from your table and workstation. Smart design, eh? There is also plenty of ambient lighting, thanks to the abundant windows and skylight. But the lamps are dim, so if it's not a bright day outside, the entire cafe is really dim. 

The crowd is mostly undergraduates who are chatting, so the ambience is noisy. I wouldn't count this as a wonderful, serious place to study without headphones.

In short: I'd come here more as a last resort. It's good for a quick-stop-cheap-coffee detour, but not a sit-down-and-spend-hours-studying cafe.

Not a bad cafe.  A little dirty, and I actually saw a mouse there once, but boy are the sandwiches good.  The coffee's decent, and probably the biggest wins for the place is location and proximity to campus, amount of seating, and it's a good place to talk.  Not a great place to study since wi-fi isn't free, hard to catch from campus, and the tables (and seating) are kind of crummy.

I do admit though, when they open the sunroof during the days and the light comes crashing through the two story lofted space, it's pretty nice.  I liked going there and reading.  Made me feel smart, especially with campus right across the street, and the big windows with people walking by looking in.

This joint has gotten me through many exams and papers. Love the brick walls, wooden chairs, balcony, and marble tables. Somehow that graces me (and everyone else in the cafe) with an amazing ability to concentrate and get work done.

Also, no one but me seems to be amazed by the fact that their skylight/sunroof opens electrically. Dude, that's so freakin' awesome!! What other cafe has such a cool feature? Combined with the fact that they accept credit, Milano may be the most high tech cafe around Berkeley.

Their music selection seems to vary by whoever's working there. Classical music is played on weekdays, but if you arrive early on the weekends (i.e. 8AM) to claim one of their 8 electrical sockets on the second floor, Spanish music blares down on you (and by Spanish music, I don't mean music from Spain, but songs sung in the Spanish language). This ethnic flair eventually gives way to full out pop music in the afternoon. I was just there yesterday, and Beyonce was telling everyone in the cafe to move "to the left, to the left," while Gwen showed us how to spell B-A-N-A-N-A-S. 

Like others have mentioned, nightime at Milano can get pretty spooky. If you do plan to be on the second floor, bring a flashlight...or better yet, a lamp.

Overall a nice place. I like the Mocha Bianca!! It's very sweet, but I still drink it every time I come here. I've had a tuna sandwich before, but I was surprised by how small it was. I seriously wondered if they forgot to give me the rest of the sandwich... The salad on the side was also something you can put together at home... nothing special...

I only come here to grab some food if I'm in a rush. I personally don't like studying here because it gets hot/humid sometimes, and it's loud and crowded (hard to find a seat--especially one near an outlet)... but I always see productive students studying. It's a nice place to chat with friends too!

As my favorite cafe to study in, I value Cafe Milano for its decor more than anything else.  The sandwiches are sizable and reasonbly priced and the mocha biancas are amazing.  Always bustling and never boring.

It's superrrr convenient for in between class breaks. I advise you not to visit during the huge rush hours btwn 12-1pm. But they are veryyyyy fast! They're obviously used to huge crowds and have an efficient way of tackling all the customers before anyone gets cranky.

I would have to agree that it's seriously not my kinda study spot. Too much buzzing all the time and light chatter. I think it's more of a place to hang.

But I LOVEEEE..
- the chicken pesto pasta 
for $4 seriously legit price and just enough to satisfy during lunchtime
- the coffee is pretty good
- hot mocha so yummy! 
and seriously shout out to the guy who makes draws me little faces in my mocha foam. way to brighten some of my gloomier days at berkeley!
- FROSTED LATTE 
absolutely delicious on a summer day. has enough caffeinne to do the trick and seriously delicious. great balance of yummyness and coffee (nothing like the too-sweet starbux fraps).
- almond croissant!

Milano you are my favorite stop before all my wheeler and barrows classes!

I ordered a latte here and it was pretty good! The store front looks small but when you go inside, you find out it was two floors. The top floor has this nice balcony ledge which you can look down onto the people on the first floor. It's quiet and offers a nice place to have a long chat with a friend or study for hours.

Cafe Milano is located right across the street from campus, and is often swamped with UC Berkeley students. Due to the large amount of seating compared to other coffee shops in the area, many people (including myself) use Cafe Milano as their primary meeting spot for group projects, coffee with friends, etc. Milano has a lively atmosphere, and is always an enjoyable place to walk into to. 

Milano offers all the pastries, coffee, and drinks of a typical coffee shop. My personal favorite item is the Cafe Milano Chicken Sandwich. The sandwich has warm chicken in marinara sauce with melted mozzarella and a nice side salad with tomatoes. It costs $6.75. 

The downsides of Café Milano: It's often difficult to access the Internet. When you are able to log onto the Free Wi Fi, it's extremely slow. In addition, there are only a few outlets in the entire café. 

In short, if you're looking for good conversation with friends, come here. If you're trying to work for a few hours on your computer, try somewhere else.

My local cafe when I'm on the streets of Berkeley. now I did work for Peet's so i have quite a high standard for coffee and Milano kinda makes it. Now i can't say that I do indulge in their espresso drinks anymore b/c i think its a lil messed up that no matter what size you order....its still a single espresso. But their drip coffee is actually amazing. With just a bit of soy and a small spoonful of brown sugar it is the best treat right before a class. 

Some times I actually crave this stuff. I'm not too fond of their pastries though. A few years ago when i was a freshman and didn't know any better i used to think they were good. Now being that I am 3 years wiser...their pretty bad. Do urself a favor and go on Durant and hit up Kingpin for a pastry.......

But I digress!

Sandwiches...on HIT! My personal fav is the Turkey sandwich with the roasted bell pepper...mostly b/c they heat it up. I can't figure out what the dressing is that they put on their house salad but its too is scrumptious! I do enjoy their mini salads which you can get on the go for that perfect amount to keep u awake in class or in a meeting without being offensive. 

A lil tip for the CalYellpers! Airbears does work @ Milano...HOLLA!

Nothing too special. The best thing this place is that it's big - so you'll always find a seat. Other than that I feel like it's a pretty standard coffee shop. It's decent if you want to study and be near the UCB campus. So in between classes is an ideal time.

Definitely what a cafe should be! I love the feel of Milano and could easily lose an hour just drinking coffee and eating sandwiches with a couple of friends. Such a chill place to be--other people are studying, reading newspapers, chatting with friends, playing chess, or doodling. Great place to meet up with classmates. Just remember to tell them it's next to Jamba Juice because I don't believe there is a sign...

I didn't even venture into the cafe until two years into college, but ever since, I occasionally return to pick up and sandwich and coffee (I love their mocha biancas!). Ahah, I actually went today. Recommended for a lunch with buddies :)

Down sides: No wifi (or really poor) and bathroom seems shady.

this place used to be my fav spot near campus where you can get a tastyy sandwich w/ salad w/ their famous dijon mustard dressing for 4.50!!!!!!! unfortunately during the summer they raised the price by a dollar or so; but still you can still get a turkey or tuna or ham sandwich in focaccia bread or mexican role for 5.50 and a refreshing side salad with it; the chicken sandwich w/ pesto sauce is really good, i think that cost like 6.25 or so? still not too expensive, but less attractive compared to before.

i like the ambience. i like sitting on the 2nd story and watching everyone be busy.
i went here with a friend and we got sandwiches, which were pretty much the same, with a choice of bread (i got foccaccia) and sundried tomato pesto sauce). the value is pretty good--you can get a big sandwich and salad for about $5.50. i wasn't a fan of the honey mustard dressing, but my friend was.
overall, decent food, but i won't be having any cafe milano cravings.

More like a 3.5 rating;

Over the summer they served this really delicious watermelon juice for like $2. Awesomeness!

Egg bagel = extra awesomeness!

Sandwiches are decent. They taste really good, but they're also around the ball park of $7. Comes with a salad.

Great location. Relaxed atmosphere. Pretty big cafe. It's not quite bright enough to do some hardcore studying, but it's fine for an hour of studying.

Really just mediocre, but the sort of place you (and everyone else) goes to a lot because its just there when you need it.

Coffee = fine
Espresso = fine
Food = fine
Prices = fine
Overall = meh

When I was at Cal millions of us could come in and study together and no one would be bothered by it. Somehow this place is sort of a study hall of students, but its dark and a little noisy and not so comfortable, and hard to find a seat, so I think we've all been duped into thinking its good--I used to walk whole blocks just to study there. 

Milano's is only acceptable for those who think that Berkeley = Telegraph.

i spent more time in here during my 2yrs at cal than i did in my dorm. 

their espresso is rich, and they use red pepper pesto in their lunch sandwiches

they used to let me in early before they opened, and i loved sitting upstairs so i could look up into the sky as they opened the sun-roof.

I was in a rush, so I couldn't really enjoy any of the atmosphere people described. I just grabbed a blueberry muffin and small coffee to go- and was pleasantly surprised with reasonable prices and the best muffin I've had at any coffeeshop around. Muffins tend to be bad in Berkeley coffeshops for some reason. The coffee was passable. What really sold me was the efficiency of the staff and general promise for a cafe.

I don't understand why this place is so PACKED during midterm and finals season.

Their coffee is horrible, their lattes all taste the same and the environment has a musty-like feel to it with poor lighting.

The only pluses I can think of are that there are a lot of seats and it's across the street from campus. And the sandwiches are decent.

Overall, a good place to meet up but a bad place to get any serious studying done.

If you need an indoor cafe to study at on southside, this is the place to go.  I like sitting upstairs because it tends to be a little quieter than downstairs.  There are very little outlets so if you need your laptop, be sure to bring a surge protector so more people can use a particular outlet.

I've gotten salads here before because I got hungry while studying, not because I came here solely for the food.  I thought the salads were fresh and decently tasty.  I've tried their poppyseed dressing but I think I'm allergic to something in it?  My throat became raspy and it felt hard to breathe??  I switched my dressing for a vinegarette without any questions asked and ate the salad without a problem!

One thing that absolutely grosses me out about this place is their fly/insect problem.  There's always those big fat black flies that fly around in circles in the open common area during warm weather.  They're sooo grosss!!!

Oh Milano, where coffee culture and academia come together like both were somehow destined for one another.  Despite the dim lighting and the lack of outlets for laptops, everyone loves Milano.  Because of the coffee; because it's cheap and strong... not regular strong, but rip-the-paint-off-walls strong.  Starbucks would never serve battery-acid coffee like this because the yuppies would go crazy.  Because hedge funds throughout the world would start trading too quickly, because the world would spin off its axis and disappear into the nether-regions of space.  
I spent a lot of time at Milano, during what I now know to be the good old days: hopped up on caffeine and peanut butter cookies, studying econ or psychology or math, trying to develop some kind of leveragable skills that would afford me a high paying job in the city across the bay.  And thinking about the nether-regions of the sorority girl at the table across from me.  
If you go often enough, the guys at Milano will start making your coffee when you walk in the door, they'll ask you how your semester is going and carve CAL or a happy face in the foam in your coffee; your finals and your morning-afters will be forever changed for the better.

This was my favorite place to get coffee in Berkeley.

The drinks weren't extremely good but were consistant.  I hated though that the guy making the drinks would always draw pictures in chocolate on the top of their mochas for women but never for me...thats no fair! SEXIST!!! lol

The food isn't that exciting or good either but was a good fix when I was cramming for a test or doing hw.

The thing I enjoyed the most about milano was its abundance of seating and I never had a problem finding a place to sit.  The best time to come was on sunny days to sit on the 2nd floor when they open the sunroof.  Awesome.  I came at least once a week during my undergrad experience at Cal.

One downside: not much places to plug your laptop into (so suggest to bring it fully charged) and there is NO free wifi here.  There is a connection but you have to PAY for it.  Gross.  You might get lucky and get a couple of bars from Caffe Strada's free wifi or airbears but its inconsistant and drops a lot.

This place is close to campus and convenient. They offer darker coffee if you prefer that. 

Pros: 
**Good classical music
**Close to campus 

Cons:
**Closes early - 10pm! (Berkeley standard)
**No free wifi
**Not many outlets 

I'm never actually studied here, but I guess it's good if you want to get away from the internet,

very cozy place and good, gigantic salads. the greek is amazing, although im not sure that pepperocinis belong in there. they use nice, dark green leafy (possibly organic, definitely delicious) lettuce and its sprinkled with feta cheese, tomatoes and olives. i almost broke my tooth on one of those things, but i dont blame the milanos. i blame the greeks. who has seeded olives when you can have them without? all im saying... big, cheap salad. oh, but few outlets to plug in the laptop. and iced coffee is okay (read: gets the caffeine in you). 

oh! and it comes with a fat slice of focaccia bread.
Another great place to study, but it gets a lot more crowded since it is NEXT to campus. Mochas and lattes are decent additions to my walks to lecture halls. Revved and ready for note taking!

too busy with too many people, but i guess that's why we all go there because of the location. 

the blueberry muffin was completely horrible, but the chai latte, tea, and all the other coffee drinks I have gotten there are agreeable.

good for interviews, bad for studying.

Homework zone thatz hella cool!

My study group and me always enjoy studying here and spending hours over fresh salads, heavy sandwiches and yummy dessert. Sometimes homework takes a backseat as we enjoy the bright sunlight and discuss dreams and ideals. We usually occupy one of the longer tables upstairs and always hope to come in early to find seats downstairs which we seldom do.

Love the staff- friendly, cheerful and efficient! and also two thumbs up to the background music, always refreshing!

Cafe Milano makes the best chai latte--and I've had A LOT of chai latte from various cafes.  I also like to rate cafes based on how they make their chai latte.  Their sandwiches are also tasty--I really like the avocado/mozzarella sandwich on Mexican roll.  The lighting is poor if you want to do some intense studying, but I go there to read the newspaper and drink my chai...YUM.

For students living on the south side of the Berkeley campus, Cafe Milano has been a staple for caffeine recharges and cheap eats. Since there's ample seating both downstairs and upstairs, I'm always able to find a table to work at, but the seating with available outlets is a bit tricky. They've got wifi that students can also use, but sometimes it's a bit spotty.

While I think it's nice that this place opens late (until midnight) and offers a lot more indoor seating than Strada, I personally don't think the beverages here are that great. I haven't been all that impressed with the quality of their coffee and the mocha ice blend was too icy in my opinion. In addition, despite the fact that their sandwich/salad combos are relatively cheap and tasty, I always notice that tables aren't clean and often have leftovers on them. In addition, there's always a number of flies flying around the cafe, which isn't particularly comforting when you're trying to eat your meal while studying or talking to a friend.

Nevertheless, this place has its perks as a cheap and quick coffee shop for students and it definitely is able to serve its purpose as a go-to for students who want to crack down on some reading or catch up with a friend on a rainy or overcast day in Berkeley.

I usually frequent this place when I'm too lazy to go far from campus. But I've noticed that the more I come here, the less I enjoy it. 

1. It's only at this cafe where I notice random bugs appearing on my workspace. I could be in deep study-mode and then BAM, an ant or other tiny creature decides to stride across my paper. This could be due to the fact that they have plants lined up across some of the benches where you sit, and it's hard to escape since that's where the outlets are :/

2. I've normally enjoyed their focaccia sandwiches, but their last sandwich made me race to the bathrooom. On top of that...that same day my partner found two pubic-looking hairs in his sandwich. (I don't think I need to further explain why that's extremely gross.)

3. Their white mochas are a lot more on the sweeter side (a little too sweet for my liking). At one point, it just tasted like hot chocolate. 

4. If you're looking to do heavy online work, I wouldn't suggest this place since their wi-fi is extremely slow, and thus you will be extremely frustrated when it takes like 5 minutes to load a page. 

5. They have one bathroom...and this bathroom is gross. 

6. The flilpside - they have a lot of tables and study space.

I love milanos because:

1. the crazy long hair cashier man that sells me everything for $1. 
2. THE HOT TURKEY SANDWHICH!
3. nice place to study

i dont like the bathroom though. it stinks. 
there's flies somtimes too.

i thought i was special discovering this place, its not that people dont come here an there isnt a line all the time....its that it's easy to walk by. and it seems most people do because they are headed for strada up the hill.

i don't feel special anymore bc now everyone's talking about milano.  oh well, its hard to be "unique" at berkeley anyway....

rant on cal later....milano now...but this is good, you're waiting for my review....waiting....see this is what you do in milano anyway.....there is always a line, and it curves too....38!!!!  still waiting.....41!!!! (those are orders being shouted into your ear while you wait by the way...has anyone else noticed they always call 38?) 

anyway....the wait is actually not bad, they are well staffed and everyone knows what they are doing. organization like this is refreshing. gooooooddddd espresso drinks, cheap (relatively) salads and they have a lot of seating.  not as many options for seating if you are looking to plug in your laptop, but airbears stretches here just fine...(no i won't tell you where to plug in your laptop, i dont want any more competition for that spot..nothing personal...). ooooooo skylight is a plus and the balcony area too..cute and cozy...

Currently my favorite cafe study spot in Berkeley. 

The setup inside has this disorderly comfortable home-y feel. At the same time it is such a pain in the ass to find an outlet sometimes. If you sit upstairs, there are only 2 outlets!! One at the table right parallel to the stairs and the other in the corner overlooking the entrance!

Opens until 12! They do this annoying thing where they flick the lights on and off when they try to get you to leave at closing...it's becoming amusing. 

There is one guy that works there that looks like he came straight out of a horror movie that makes funny faces in my hot chocolate...so i guess I have to take back the horror movie comment.

Negatives: saw a mouse running around once.....YEAH minus a star because of that....and the whole plug ordeal

Great place to read or study, especially upstairs. Coffee is a lot like the music in the place- you really NEVER know what you're going to get! I've listened to Strauss switch to Russian pop over the course of one chapter in my textbook. I'm still recovering from that.

UPDATE: I realized recently that Milano is my favorite place to write, read, or hang out with my laptop for three-four hours. This contradicts all logic and reason, but for me, this is the single best cafe on the planet. Five stars, baby!

I was looking for a place to park and get some work done and intended on going to another spot in the area but it was closed. I found this place and figured I try it out, though it was a disappointment.

1. Service was less than satisfactory. All I wanted was an iced tea so I asked the cashier what kind of tea they had. He said, "regular tea". I confirmed it saying so black tea? He said regular, I thought whatever and just ordered it.

2. Restrooms were VERY dirty. Paper all over the floor, smelled funny, toilet seat is too big for the toilet it's on.

3. I decided on sitting upstairs and found many of the chairs were dirty. Fabric seating that was discolored and kind of gross. I sat on a wooden chair.

4. Rafters/beams were dirty and dusty. As I sat there getting some work done I noticed it had an open ceiling and everywhere there was dust. It made me feel like crap may fall into my drink.

5. They provided a wifi passcode but I had difficulty getting online and didn't feel like asking for assistance. I tethered my phone and moved on.

I will not go back.

Ew.

I was sitting there reading quietly downstairs towards the front of the cafe, when all of a sudden at the corner of my eye, I see something move. I thought maybe it was just me hallucinating but when I did a double-take, it was a MOUSE!

I immediately hopped out of my chair along with my belongings and left this place for good. This place is obviously a dirty shithole.

I'm sure they're not the only place around Berkeley infested with mice, but come on now, if you have mice lurking around there, imagine what lurks in your food! 

Gross.

For coffee I'd rather go to Philz. But Milano's is super convenient if I just want to study in between classes since it's so close to campus!

And I LOVE the sandwiches here. The turkey pesto is so delicious and cheesey and bell-peppery. And hot. 

I'm eating it right now. And it's $6.

Oh yeah, their cappuccino's are cute because they make designs in them. They put a happy face in mine!

Stopped into Milano with a Berkeley alum to crank out some work. Good coffee house vibe. I especially liked that they played classical music in lieu of the pop that infects the airwaves of most cafes. It seemed like a lot of people were here to get work done, and I really liked that aspect of the place. Being surrounded by other busy bees promotes my own productivity. Also, you could stop in and do work without actually ordering anything since it's cafeteria style with a very laid back, sort of dive-y atmosphere.

Currently sitting here doing my Yelp reviews with my Mocha Bianca! 
I just have to say this place has given me a love for Cafe's. It's like a small mom and pop shop with great workers. The place is fairly large and I come here to study/chill all the time with the nice classical music playing in the background. It's just something about cafe's now that makes life so relaxing.  

I keep telling my friends that if I were to ever go anywhere in the world I will always make an effort to come back here and get a dose of my Mocha Bianca. Why is that? They make the foam just right (I have tried so many different places and it is just not the same). The foam is fluffy and fresh giving the coffee that extra oomph. If you get the right barista he will make a little picture with the foam which is one of the first places around Berkeley that I have seen done this. Not only that, but the coffee is strong even though the drink is sweet, so you know it's not just filled with sugar (ahem like Starbucks). 

Milano is right next to campus so I always relied on it for a nice warm cream cheese bagel and a mocha bianca. =)

Perks: Free WiFi, nice large windows to gaze out of, second floor with an open ceiling providing plenty of light, has food along with all their coffee and pastries.

As a student, I used to study at this place all the time.  The drinks are okay, but the service has deteriorated into a sloppy mess.  Recently on a trip back to Berkeley, I revisited this old haunt.  My girlfriend ordered grapefruit juice, and was served some lukewarm juice with no ice.  Who likes lukewarm juice?
