After asking the girl at the counter for ice, the girl furrowed her eyebrows and reluctantly gave it to the dude who usually works there (the guy with long brown hair).  He threw in some ice in and muttered, "B*tch" under his breath.

There were flies, and the bathrooms were hot and smelled like vomit.

Obviously, it was the last time I'll visit this place.

The tabletops of this indie café have been polished by thousands of Cal kids' resting hands and bookspines. The photon-spoiled, lofted space welcomes students by the droves; it's always bustling and buzzing with chatter no matter the time of day, and draws many a laptop so be prepared to battle for a plug. 

Gourmet this is not, but it's a leap up from motor oil and the staff's cheery enough. After a quick bite, it seemed to me that the people eat there because it's available, and to justify taking up space. 

Considering going back to the books but don't know if you can handle the student world again? If you can stand it here for a few hours without wanting to smack someone, you're well on your way to success.

How do I love Milano, let me count the ways.......

This is the first and last place in the USA that I tried espresso - ick, not for me.  But everything else there i adore.  I don't think I could add up the hours I have spent here, studying, playing on my computer, pretending to study, eating, talking to friends, trying to figure out what I'm going to do with my life.  This is one of the places that helped me to make it through college.  

Do yourself a favor and go to Milano when you have time to kill on a beautiful day, and sit near the open windows and watch Berkeley go by.

I find it useful to rate coffee places around campus in a few categories that are relevant to people who want a place to study/read and sip on something tasty.  

Milano is a nice, south side, close-to-campus alternative to Strada.  The largest differences between the two are the food (or lack thereof) and the seating.   

Drinks: (I only get iced or hot coffee or Italian Sodas here...)
+ The hot and iced coffee is flavorful and usually good.
-Sometimes they are stingy with the Italian Soda syrup, but that has only happened to me a few times...

Food
+ THE FOOD HERE IS SO GOOD.  Everything is reasonably priced and filling.  All of the sandwiches come with a side salad that has a killer vinegarette, and I haven't had anything there that I didn't like.  I recommend the vegetarian or tuna sandwiches.  

Seating
+ Milano has two levels of seating.  It is usually looks a little crowded, but I never have had trouble finding a table to eat/study at.  It is a little dark, and the upstairs is a little cramped, but the overall atmosphere and availability of seating is good.

Bathroom:
+ Often a little dirty, but free and usually not broken.  

Internet
+ Free wifi, always a plus!

Well...they have amazing coffee and the staff is super friendly. I have a problem with the seating, temperature, and number of outlet plugs in this place. The seating is not comfortable, its always too cold or hot in there, and also, they have very limited outlet plugs. over all, i like it...

I like this place for their roasted chicken sandwiches, which have sadly gone up in price (slightly). Most of the sandwiches are reasonably priced. When I lived in b-town, $6.00 could get you a toasty sandwich with sweet roasted bell peppers and a sizable salad with a pretty kickass vinaigrette. 

My friend was hooked on the vinaigrette after she tried it.

Milano's often buzzing when school is in session and tends to be a favorite hangout since it's close to campus. I frequented this place a lot.

I haven't been here in years, but 4-stars for the memories. Matt Plicner introduced me to this cafe back in High School. Lots of coffee drunken here with Matt, Gabe, Cruise, Paul, Rio, and Lisa S. 
I remember spending late nights on the top floor getting high on caffeine and thinking up ways to change the world with my friend Cruise. I remember this skinny guy with big headphones and these old Russian-esqe dudes playing chess on timers. They seemed to be here every time I visited. 
I particularly liked the mochas here, but probably too sweet for my tastes now. Oh, and they had large slices of chocolate or banana cream pie for like $1.50 or something. This was like, late eighties early nineties, so don't get too excited. I'm sure that's changed.  
It was in this very cafe that I bought Lisa her first Latte ever, while studying math late at night. It was a bit strong for her innocent pallate to handle, but I give her credit for forcing it down. After several more attempts in the weeks to come, she was drinking lattes like a veteran. I don't know what ever became of Lisa, but I ike to think wherever she is, she's still drinking coffee. I take credit, along with Cafe Milano, for effecting that change in her.

good place to hunker down on a giant textbook with kiwi italian soda in one hand. the cakes are very good - the bundts are surprsingly very moist!, the sandwiches are tasty (i like the turkey,) and of coures the coffee drinks are ace.

When a place servers mediocre coffee, then service matters a lot.  Why the hell is the dude who takes orders such a grouch?  I asked for soy milk because I CAN'T HELP THAT I'M LACTOSE-INTOLERANT.  Isn't it enough that God punished me by making me unable to digest lactose? I don't need the cashier/coffee pourer to give me a dirty look and actually growl at me.  I totally recognize that this person might hate his job, but I was not even rude.  I said please and thank you.  And smiled at him even after he growled at me.  ugh

Ahh yes, Cafe Milano.  Just thinking about this place makes me nostalgic.  This is THE place to go if you're a student and you think the library isn't exactly conducive to group studying.  Their caffeinated beverages are good, and their panini sandwiches are even better.  I have a friend who hates salads with a passion, but will eat theirs because it is soo good!  The people that work here and take your order are super nice and friendly too.  Even if you're just a tourist, definitely stop by here if you're craving delicious panini sandwiches. 

Nostalgic story time!: So this place is literally right across the street from campus.  Two friends and I were studying for a test for a class that's very heavily statistics based.  We're sitting downstairs right by the giant windows which were open since it was warm and sunny outside.  There were these tourists right outside--a mom with her two daughters (I'm guessing the daughters were both in highschool)...one of the daughters was on the phone with her dad and I guess they were trying to find each other, the conversation went something like this:
Daughter: "we're on Bancroft in front of a school...it's like, a university or something...it's some really good school....it's really big."  Ooh man, needless to say, my friends and I were dying of laughter.  

PS: There's wi-fi if you sit close enough towards the front, and can use airbears which is provided by Cal..otherwise, I think you actually have to pay for the wi-fi at Cafe Milano...I can't exactly remember.

Cafe Milano has decent coffee for a better price ($1.50 for a large) than coffee chains. I haven't really tried the food here, but they sell bananas! Yay! I was alarmed the first time I got coffee not to go, however, because they served it in a glass. A glass! The only other time I'd ever had a coffee-related beverage served in a glass, it was mostly alcohol.

I later tried to do some background research on the principles of thermal dynamics as they relate to glasses and ceramic mugs, and since glass IS a type of ceramic, I couldn't convince myself that one container was the superior insulator. But in terms of aesthetics, no! Coffee belongs in a mug! The only thing that looks weirder in a glass than black coffee is Mountain Dew.

At first I thought this problem was specific to Cafe Milano, but then I started getting coffee served in glasses throughout the Bay Area. And it hit me:

California is experiencing a Severe Mug Shortage.

I wish I had known sooner. I think I may have accidentally hoarded all the mugs, because I have tons of them. I eat cereal out of mugs. I once bailed out an overflowing toilet with a mug. My own mother once refused to accept a Mother's Day mug from me because she had too many mugs already.

So...uhh...sorry for being such a mug hog, guys. I guess I should start giving them back now. If you want one, I'll be outside Cafe Milano with a Uhaul full of mugs...

I miss Milano a ton. It doesnt have the best-quality espresso or anything, but I just want to give a special salute to my college time spent at this place, reading or having an extremely interesting conversation with some random Berkeley folk. There is a server who is especially friendly and does beautiful Latte-Art when the store is not too busy.

I used to love this place when I was an undegrad at Cal. The salads there were amazing and the coffee was pretty good. I still remember the countless hours I spent there studying for physics and organic chem - really glad that time is behind me but definitely miss this cafe. The 2nd floor of the cafe is the perfect place to read and sip your coffee. Great for a student budget!

If you're into early morning coffee and taking some time to gather your wits before you head off to school or work, this is a good place for that, because during down seasons (like summer or winter break), Milano's still opens early in the morning. And they have tasty croissants and bran muffins that are killer if you ask them to toast it for you.

However, sometimes in the early morning or right before closing, they blast the Mexican radio, so it would be advisable to bring your own music+headphones if that happens. The rest of the day though they play classical music, which is great.

There's also a lot of space, and the servers are swift. However, the ever-crucial outlets are in short-supply here.

So, all-in-all, a nice cafe that adds to the overall selection of cafes in Berkeley. Has its pros and cons, so giving it a nice, solid, middle-of-the-road 3 star. You won't be disappointed if you decide to chill or study here, for sure - especially if your other favorite cafe is packed or not even open.

Hot spot for UC Berkeley students to get studying done here since it is very close to campus!

Modern, spacious cafe - upstairs offers more seating!

Their Wi-Fi is somewhat slow and I got cut off a couple of times while using it.

Great place to chat or just enjoy coffee.  They have fair selections on sandwiches, bakery goods, salads and etc.

They didn't decorate my latte on top!  A bit disappointed because I see a few pictures from their business page that has nice decorations on top of their lattes.  What a bummer!

I dig their 2nd floor loft, multi-colored year-round Christmas lights, & their high ceilings.. I remember them having huge paintings on their brick walls but they took em down =(

The ambiance of this place gives you a sense of comfort & security, but the hustle & bustle of students studying makes this place really packed & loud.. The couple times I've been here, I tend to peer out their huge windows & people watch as Urban & American Apparel shoppers stroll by.. 

I've tried their tuna sandwich on Mexican roll which was nothing special, I should've ordered it on Foccacia bread! & the side salad that comes with it is the suck.. Their coffee was so so which was unfortunate but their croissants are the shniz!

The place isn't very clean but their staff is real chill..  It's a good spot to come study & relax especially if you're a Cal student, but definitely not someplace to feed an empty stomach

I LOVE CAFE MILANO! Its so cozy. Dim lighting: perfect for evening conversation, "studying," or just hanging out. I LOVE their chai tea lattes and the little designs they make in the foam. Super friendly service too. Its a win-win situation.

I first visited this establishment in 1992, I was a freshman in college and venture in to study and grab a cup of joe. I fell in love with it immediately. Its just what I imagine a cafe to be. You have students studying, people discussin politics/current events, people playing chess, listening to music, drawing, reading......a little bit of everything. A great place to people watch....and have a good cup of coffee. I am a coffee-snob so I only drink espresso and black coffee. They are similar to Italian roast and stuff you get in Italy. I can't say anything about the other versions. The only thing, I said is the bathroom is disgusting, but so is every other one in Berkeley....but I haven't been there in years.

To be honest, my friends wanted to sit down somewhere at 9 PM so we just went to the nearest cafe, which was Cafe Milano. I ordered a frosted latte, and it was soooo sweet. It was like a Starbucks frapuccino, but sweeter and with chunks of ice. I couldn't finish it. Way too sweet, and didn't taste like coffee at all (even though it's a latte).

Very dim atmosphere. We sat upstairs for more of a quiet atmosphere since downstairs was packed with college kids on their laptops and talking with each other. It was a lot quieter and less people were up there, but very dark. I don't see how anyone could study up there. 

Around 10, this guy who worked there said the store was closed and tried kicking us out. I'm pretty sure the cafe closes at midnight...

UGH!  Cafe Milano is the conveniently located, credit card accepting, office hours hosting cafe that I totally LOVE to HATE.  

Reasons why this place sucks:
1.  You 'can't bring outside food'---Alright!  OK!  I'm totally down.  If I owned a cafe this would probably be my rule also, considering how many kids come in with takeout.  But it is really bothersome when employees chase potential customers around telling them to throw out their elsewhere-purchased coffee and food.  Chill out.  I was gonna buy a cappucino when I finished my drip from peet's.  Really makes me not want to give them my business.
2.  Inconsistent temperature---Literally it is freezing in the darker areas in the cafe and unbearably hot near the windows where the sun shines in.  I know, I know, JUST MOVE.  Well, sometimes mobility is an issue when the place is crowded and I have my laptop, backpack, outside coffee, Milano cappucino, etc.
3.  The food is bad.  I can make everything they serve SO much better.  And I do.  Which is why I no longer purchase their sandwiches or bagels or salads or even their cookies (they should just purchase their pastries from a local bakery).
4.  Really, really newbie undergrads come here and have the most INSIPID conversations that make me want to die.


Reasons why I really love Milano:
1.  Alina Polyakova's Office Hours---If you ever have this GSI, DO NOT miss a chance to see her true brilliance at office hours.  She is awesome and rules all and because she has chosen this place to hold office hours, I now love Milano's cappucinos.  
2.  The cappucino---Perfect balance of espresso and foam.  So delicious I cannot stand it.  Even when they put it in a to-go cup, this drink is so so yummy.
3.  The awesome cashier and the awesome barista who fixes my cappucino.  I love you both.  Gracias por todo!  Me hacen sonrier cada dia!
4.  Freaking SO CLOSE to campus.  I get off of the 1 and it is less than a block away from the stop and class.
5.  They accept credit cards.  Hardly any one in Berkeley accepts credit cards.

I adore this charming pink little place. More specifically, I adore their foccaccia ham and mozzarella cheese sandwiches. I adore their tables upstairs with their little plugs for our little laptops. I adore their homemade salad dressing and their lovely coffee and desserts and most of all, I adore that they let me eat, date, study and relax here, with or without my dog.

What I do NOT adore is the fact that the wifi sucked, hence the missing star.

Other than this, this place will always remind me of my days at Cal.

This was my favorite cafe to study at when I was a student at Cal. They have great coffee and a ton of seating, but sometimes it can be hard to find a good seat. When it's nice outside they would open up the roof and it was the perfect thing to distract me from all that studying I had to do. They serve food, but I have never eaten anything from here except an onion bagel with cream cheese, but I must admit it was a damn tasty bagel. The crowd and energy of Milano makes it worth checking out, if nothing has enticed you so far.

Um... I like the design of the building.  I like that they are across the street from campus.  I also like their coffee.

I do not like that coffee served in glasses that are meant for beer.  I do not like food that hides its blandness under a pound of focaccia.  And I do not like studying without a laptop, which I am forced to do here because there are hardly any plugs and it's impossible to get a wifi signal.

Cafe Milano has great salads and sandwiches.  The sandwiches are nice and warm which makes this a great place to come on a cold day.  And the salads are pretty hearty - great to share.  Milano is also an awesome place to meet up with friends for a quick bite since its right across the street from Sproul.  I would give them five stars, but the espresso there is practically undrinkable.  It's the one thing on the menu I wouldn't get.

I like when the baristos 
do latte art on the top of my drinks 
but how come their smiley faces 
always look like a pair of boobs? 

A great place to study.

I feel sort of bad giving Cafe Milano such a low rating, but honestly, I *have* experienced better!

The few times I've gone to Cafe Milano, it's always been ridiculously crowded. The Internet isn't exactly speedy, to say the least, and the noise level is hugely distracting when you're trying to study.

Now, I understand that maybe Cafe Milano's not the best place for studying. But what about as a cafe? Even in this aspect, I've seen better. Their beverages and pastries are mediocre at best (I think I prefer Starbucks!) and their pricing is relatively pricy for the food quality. To be honest, I think the only thing Cafe Milano really has going for it is the awesome location. Everything else? Meh.

flies in the food case
open late and free wifi
food and drinks okay

Tips:

$2.00 minimum purchase for card. (Very easy to achieve.)

---------------------------------------------

I just have to say that I think Cafe Milano has the best sandwich in the area. It's super unique because the sandwich is on focaccia with a pesto sauce and peppers. It tastes amazing and I think everyone should give it a try. There's a selection between turkey ($6), ham($6), pastrami ($7), and many more. I think if you haven't tried it that it's worth giving a try.

I also really like their caramella and chai tea latte (more on the milky side without much spice). They even provide a simple syrup to  make your iced drinks taste sweeter if you prefer it that way! Any cafe with simple syrup is a great cafe in my book. (Because I tend to like sweeter drinks)

It's a really beautiful, inviting place to eat, but the food's just OK.  Don't get me wrong; I'm all for the thrown-together cafes on Bancroft, the ones at which the cook line is along the west wall and there are random Print Shoppe* clip-art signs everywhere that advertise their newest^ menu items.

But this place looks a lot classier than it is.  I really wish they would allow you to bring food from other places in here, because if they did, I would spend a lot more time here.  And yes, that might take away from their business generally because what restaurant wants to allow people to bring food in?  But they would make money off of me because I don't really come here very often now, but if I could bring other food in here, I'd camp out and order lots of overpriced drinks.

The upstairs dining area is really all you need to know about.

*Remember Print Shoppe?  If you don't, your life is not as meaningful as it could be.

^By "newest" I mean newest circa 2006.  There's just some weird thing some breakfast places have about updating their menus.  I realize it takes time to go through and add things in their appropriate places, but isn't printing up all those NEW ITEM signs also a lot of work?

I know iced tea isn't the greatest thing ever created, but man, thumbs up to the one Milano makes. Nothing beats having a cold glass of iced tea while a nice breeze comes through. Makes studying for finals kinda peaceful. 

The service is awesome as well. I wanted to add avocados to my sandwich yesterday but after the guy at the front told me it'd cost me $1.25, I told him to forget it (not in a mean way!) He said "it's okay this time" and ended up making my sandwich and me very happy by adding avocados at no extra charge. 

It probably won't happen again, but iced tea + nice seat by the open door area + delicious sandwich with free avocados = happy Jane.

In the five years I have lived in Berkeley, this is by far my favorite coffee shop.

Located right next to the UC Berkeley campus, it's within walking distance from almost any class. From the nondescript salmon-colored exterior, you would not expect to walk in to find weathered marbletop tables and 20-foot trees which touch the vaulted ceiling. Lots of sunlight can get through the tall windows on the right days, and the stark styling of the wooden benches and upstairs seating area oozes timeless character and color from brick wall to brick wall.

Milano has an assortment of sandwich/salad combos and all the coffees you would want. I personally love the lattes they have here, which they serve in glass mugs if you are staying for a while. My favorite sandwich is the chicken breast, which is simply a bun cut from a loaf of bread, with mozzarella cheese, green and red bell peppers, marinara sauce, and a chicken breast (the reconstituted kind, like at subway, not natural chicken breast, but it's still good) all toasted together. It comes with a salad, which has an AMAZING tangy dressing...I would say it's somewhere between French and Italian dressing, but trust me when I say it is awesome.

I always get these items when I eat here, and it's perfect for eating while studying/reading, since the sandwich will not make your fingers messy. It can get loud inside when it's crowded, so if you need a quieter coffee shop it's not the best place to go. But it's great to shoot the breeze or host a small meeting.

The only downside to Milano is the spotty wireless network signal. You can only use the campus wireless and you must be a student/staff to log on, and the signal is unusable unless you sit closer to the front door.

If you think Starbucks is the best coffee shop ever, I implore you to widen your palate and realize that the best things do not always come in corporate wrapping. For everyone else, this is the Berkeley hole-in-the wall coffee shop you were searching for.

This place only gets 3 stars because the building is cool, though I've been here at least once a week for the last few years, but only with the intent of studying. For the student intent on cramming, and not so concerned about products, here's what to know:

Wifi: The only strong signal requires you to pay. If you're lucky and near the front you might get AirBears. Sometimes there's another open network, but don't come here to watch YouTube or do anything more bandwidth intensive than Wikipedia.

Outlets: There are a few, but they never seem to be plentiful enough.

Good for group work/meetings

I've had countless drinks, tons of pastries, a number of sandwiches, and a few salads. Here's a breakdown:

Coffee: You better like sugar and cream, cuz this stuff is strong. And by strong, I don't mean good, I mean stomach-acid strong.

Espresso [based drinks]: I'm not sure whether the coffee or espresso is worse. I don't know why I continue to get lattes (don't dare get anything less diluted) when good espresso can be found at the Med on Telegraph

Pastries: Pretty standard medium/low quality Berkeley fare. Not to say that I don't get the occasional chocolate croissant or blueberry muffin, but none are spectacular.

Sandwiches/Salads: I haven't had them in a while, so I don't wanna review them, but I can say that I have good memories of them (...though the sandwiches are by no means large).

Employees: Either very nice, or very rude, though almost always sexist. Just watch the girl in front of you get a smily face drawn on her latte with chocolate syrup, only to be followed by gross stares as she leaves the register. I don't feel this should be included in reviews (as this happens everywhere to an extent) but this place just does it all too consistently and blatantly.

Summary: If you're not here for something school related, or aren't in love with one of their sandwiches (as a friend is) avoid this place. If you've got a long evening of studying ahead of you though, this place can be just right.

Cafe Milano, like 4 other Berkeley chains, use Espresso Roma beans to make their coffee and espresso.  Even though these chains use the same brand of beans, a lot of the end taste is dependent upon preparation methods and time.  Some other chains that use Espresso Roma are like French Hotel and Espresso Roma on Ashby and College.  I'm not fond of the methods Cafe Milano uses to prepare their espresso.  They're notorious for pulling their shots long.  This makes the espresso murky, black, runny and very VERY bitter.  I ordered an Espresso con panna (double shot of espresso with dollop of whipped cream on top) and they gave me a full cup (small sized) of espresso.  I gave the barista a look and my eyes kind of posed the question "THIS is a DOUBLE?"  His look back told me, "Yeah, don't worry."

I went back to my seat and look a sip of the espresso.  The consistency was that of water, but the taste was that of the most bitter espresso I've ever had.  They must've pulled this shot for at least 35-40 seconds.  I was wondering how long they were going to let that go on for and I didn't think I needed to even taste it to know how bitter it was.  After that sip, I just left the cup.  There was no saving that cup now, not even the whipped cream.

BAD COFFEE.  

I give this place 3 stars because their salads save them considerably.  Their salads resemble that of Cafe Intermezzos.  They use the same sized wooden bowls to serve their salads in, but they use more exotic ingredients than Intermezzos.  The salad isn't piled like Mount Everest like it is in Intermezzos, but I feel the quality definitely is worth it.  I usually order the Italian and that comes with fresh mozzarella, roasted bell peppers, garbonzo beans and other veggies.  This is topped with olive oil and balsamic vinegar and then with a big fat piece of focaccia bread.  The bread is so fresh - melts in your mouth.

The atmosphere is nice when you're there during the daytime.  The lighting becomes rather dim at night and doesn't make for a great place to study. If you're upstairs at night, you might as well be in the dark.  I've tried studying upstairs at night - you can't see a thing.  I'm really fond of their skylight upstairs that brings in natural night on sunny days.  The indoor trees also add to the positive ambiance.  Good place to study in the daytime which is why it probably reflects why they have a lot less customers in the evening.

Five stars for every cutie who works here and all the locals that take this place over every weekday morning.  I love those guys.  Everybody just brings a smile to my heart each morning when I fall out the doors of the 51 and hobble, eyes half-shut, to order my cappuccino for here not too strong.  Wow.  Now THAT is some strong ass coffee you got there guys!  Without this crack, though, I wouldn't be acing my italian class right now...  I owe it all to Cafe Milano.  Speaking of which, I should probably be studying for my midterm right now...

I've been going to Milano since I was an undergrad, first for the cheap and high quality infusions of caffeine, and then for all the people (the greek salads w/balsalmic aren't bad either).
Behind the counter you'll find Sylviano, bearer of goatees and creator of smiley faces atop your lattes.  Fabiola the pretty cashier has moved up Bancroft to the copy room at Boalt, but she stops by on occasion to chew the fat.  Jorge the hunchback is just about the friendliest fellow you've ever met, and you'll often see him mobbing around the streets of Berkeley in his white Honda Accord.
If you're seeking a spot of enlightenment, Milano has its own resident guru in Richard, who has MS, and can usually be found with a Dharma text in one hand and prayer beads in the other.

The one drawback is circa 11pm when the dudes want to clear out the cafe they start blasting mariachi music, which salts your studying/idle chatting game.

Conveniently located across the Berkeley campus, I can only imagine this spacious cafe to be packed with students during the school year.  I was glad we were able to check this place out on a lazy, summer Sunday afternoon.  I love the option of sitting upstairs or downstairs, near the window for people watching, or tucked in the back if you want to be secluded.  Stars for serving food, which from my observation, the salads and sandwiches seem pretty hearty.  I ordered the chai tea latte, which had plenty of foam....overall, it was pretty decent caffeine fix.

Berkeley has some pretty trendy cafes, but out of all of them, I would say this is my favorite. For starters, they have indoor balcony seating with a skylight and large windows on the first floor level. The service is always nice and friendly and there are plenty of seats available. Plus, unlimited wi-fi with a password that doesn't change with purchase, late hours, and a close proximity to campus are pluses.

I'm a big fan of the salads, muffins, chai lattes, and apple cider. I also love this place because the first time I came here, they played some sort of orchestra improvisation of The Beatles...
It's a great place to meet up with a friend for a chat - I always referred my friends to this place as an ending location for a date. :)

I'm currently sitting the cafe by its large beautiful windows. It's a great place to people watch. Mostly college students and hipsters, since it's between teh American Apparel and the Urban Outfitters along Bancroft. Nevertheless, very interesting. I just saw a kid with a Carrot Top-esque red afro. 

I come here every now and then. Their assortments of coffees and teas aren't anything memorable, but there are always plenty of places to sit. The inside is like an indoor/outdoor cafe. There are high ceilings (high enough to fit a small tree) and a lofted area. I'm also surprised to see that AirBearsBeyond wireless network reaches out here. It is most memorable for the cheesy music. I am currently listening to the flute rendition of "I Just Called to Say I Love You."

I was in Cafe Milano today to see my old friend, Martín and to get my 2nd coffee of the AM. I've known him, his sister, and his brothers for many years. With most of the students gone for the summer, the place was pretty empty. We caught up on the family, who is where, about kids, etc. A nice five minute visit and I'm off to campus.

So as I walk in the office a colleague says to me that "Milano coffee is terrible and how can I drink it". 
I made a crack that it's "all the same, wherever you go."
"No, The French Hotel  (near Cheeseboard) has the best coffee ever."

I gotta tell you. The coffee at Milano, French Hotel, both Espresso Roma Cafes, Cafe Sienna, Fillmore, and the I-House Caffe, all get their coffee from the same roaster, Roma, based in Emeryville. In fact, the company has fourteen stores in Cali.

See for yourself: http://www.espressoroma.com/store_directory.php

I checked each of these cafes' yelp reviews and they say the coffee is the best or the worst. Only the barista skills and the equipment might vary. I don't know.

You can yelp about the service, you can yelp about the food, you can yelp about the customers (students, what have you...), but for you self-appointed coffee affectionados, the coffee comes from the same roaster. Or as it has been said, "It doesn't fall far from the tree."

If you don't like Milano, try the French Hotel (Martin's brother works there), both Espresso Roma Cafes, Cafe Sienna, Fillmore, and the I-House Caffe. The coffee must be better.

Cafe Milano was so vital in helping me get through my four years at Berkeley. It was my go-to place for coffee and last-minute studying. Firstly, their coffee is made really well and 2) it is really cheap, especially compared to Caffe Strada. Not to mention Milano also takes card! I believe they are both owned by the same person (who also owns FSM), but Strada seems to be the snobby older sibling. I mean, why are there two Fs in "Caffe"?? The College Ave location is probably a factor for the pretentiousness. 

Milano also has food, and not just pastries. Another plus! The turkey sandwich or pastrami are my favorites. The greek salad is a distant third.  Don't get the premade sandwiches, however, they aren't very good. 

Milano is also a much easier place to study because although College and Bancroft is quite possibly the best corner to people watch, it is not the best place to be productive. I prefer to spend my (3-hour-break-day-of-midterm) studying in old church pews on the top floor of Milano. It's always good to remember, however, that when it starts to pour outside, the homeless all seem to seek shelter in Milano. This can make it quite hard to concentrate, since the camp songs move indoors. But, alas, if Berkeley has taught me anything, it is to accept others for who they are.

This place is nice for getting some work done.  It's close to campus, and has decent coffee as well as yummy-looking food (haven't tried their food yet).  

I need background noise in order for my mind not to stray, so I need to come to places like this to study.  Milano is perfect since it has plenty of tables and background noise.  

Thank you Cafe Milano for providing me with a place to study other than the catacombs/library.

P.S. - I don't know for sure if this place is an Espresso Roma in disguise.  I got my coffee in an Espresso Roma labeled cup.  *shrug*  There are also swarms of flies in this place, which makes me question the cleanliness of this operation.   Once I spaced out and watched the swarms for a while, trying to figure out their flight patterns.  Maybe I can train them to do my evil biddings.

Ever since I heard a certain former favorite Cafe of mine in the area was infested with rats and cockroachies, I've stayed away. As a result, I have sought refuge at Cafe Milano. 

Great place, good food, good service, what more can one ask for? There's plenty of room for people to sit: either on the first floor, or on the second, the latter having an open roof/skylight for people to enjoy on warm sunny days. Though I have to wonder, what do they do about the lack of roof when it rains??? The people who frequent this place are cool too, students studying, folks chatting, or lunch goers like moi!

The employees who work here are for the most part great. Today I got a free agua fresca watermelon with my sandwich order. It includes fresh pieces of watermelon, not too sugary and hit the spot! My recs for what to order: Hot Chicken Sandwich and Italian Salad (I always add chicken and minus the garbanzo beans to mine. Not a fan of garbanzo beans). As a cafe staple, their bran muffins are huge!

Prices aren't too shabby either. Another recommended Berkeley lunch spot!

With two floors, this café is spacious, airy, and vaguely charming in a haphazard way. It also has a ridiculously convenient location and a reasonably good tasting hot chicken sandwich. But I think those are where the plusses end. It has very few power outlets and despite being across the street from campus, it receives very weak AirBears reception making Internet usage an unlikely possibility - perhaps that's a good thing?

Came here to grab a cup of ice tea with some out of town visitors. After charging me for a large cup, they carelessly handed me a small. They weren't busy at the time so it was disappointing to see their lack of reaction when I asked about the error. Besides the point, this cafe provides a good space for studying where tables are plentiful on both floors. I also saw formations of study groups and office hours being held by graduate student instructors who made good use of the space to inspire intellectual conversations. Located at the tip of south campus, the ambiance is shape by students who very much view this cafe as a fabric of their campus life. Given my experience with the service, I don't think I'll be going back unless I have a meeting scheduled there.

The good: Big, open space and lots of seating.
The bad: No wifi and the milk in my cappuccino was burned.

This place is good for a quick caffeine boost, but if you want a place with full flavored espresso and talented baristas that take their job as an art form, skip it.

This cafe is in a prime location, just right across the street from the busiest side of campus. Lucky for them, they don't have to provide free wireless internet because most people can pick up the wireless from campus. Still, there are not enough outlets to go around and this place is always packed with people on their laptops or pretending to read. I don't know how anyone gets any work done in this place because I always find myself watching people. There's just too much going on here and too many people walking in and out. People should definitely not meet here for their group projects or office hours. There simply is not enough room and the table are small, though there are many. I like sitting upstairs where I think there is more light in the daytime because of the skylight, but I like sitting downstairs at night where it's not as drafty. The noise level in here is high. The service is alright. Their drinks are alright. Their coffee does not stand out, but I do like their hot apple cider! Their sandwiches and salads are okay too. One thing is for sure though, they need more cafes like these everywhere.

As a freshman at Cal I took German 1.  Midway through the semester, when we could string together sentences, our class had a debate: Was Cafe ist besser: Strada oder Milano?  

The debate got rather hyphy.  I myself used to prefer Strada for people watching, al fresco coffee drinking, and getting some sun.  But there is something missing from Strada that Milano has:  FOOD.

FOOD comes in handy when you are braindead.  When you have a Clinical Psych "midterm" during the third week of the semester. When you have to memorize Hamlet's first soliloquy to perform in front of one hundred people.  When you have to conjugate irregular verbs. Ad infinitum.  

The FOOD is good.  Big salads a la Seinfeld. Sandwiches. Not just cookies and croissants, although they have those too. 

One barista does some latte art, though he is a one trick pony.  It's always a girl's face and a big bosom.  Rather flattering depiction, actually. It's good to have some lovin' when you have four epic poems to read in two days, plus an illogical logic set to complete :)

Milano is not about the nuances of the coffee or the food, its about the entire coffeehouse culture.  The espresso is serviceable, and the food is fine, but what I remember about Milano is working on papers or meeting friends and soaking up cappuccinos among the crowd of tables, the bustling activity and interesting conversations, the late hours, the two story bare brick walls holding up some of the larger local art displays, the indoor tree and other plants, the large balcony with a skylight, and the fact that nobody bothers you no matter how long you stay there.  Milano and Strada are the pre-Starbucks, the authentic coffeehouses that hooked me on the entire coffee culture, one I still enjoy today.

4.5 stars 

Bookended by the temptations of Telegraph Ave. in one direction and the ever popular Caffe Strada in the other, It'd be easy to miss Cafe Milano. But that would be a mistake, because this is exactly what a college cafe should be. 

The coffee, from the same roaster that supplies cafes in the area, is solidly decent and Milano has all the standard cafe characteristics - Free, fast, wifi; substantial and surprisingly tasty food and  classical music. 

But what really sets Milano apart from the rest is it's atmosphere: All high ceilings and exposed brick, this place is so pleasant it's a shame to associate it w/ problems set and papers. There's plenty of natural light, several potted plants, an open air roof, and when it's warm out, the cafe's massive two-story windows are left entirely open. It's a wonder anyone gets any work done.

This is a completely biased review having spent 9 years *YES! NINE* years of my life as a student at Cal.  And I loved Cafe Milano then as I do now.

Besides the great coffee & tea and the adequate food & pastries for bargain basment prices . . . the entire place has that disgusting-dirty-cool-charm about it.

I managed to sit down at the table that I've sat down at about a million times before and chowed on the special:  a chicken sandwich with a side salad with a superb vinagrette . . . oh for 5 bucks.  It was subjectively so-so, but was real tasty like a home cooked meal.  Nostalgic bite after bite. Yummy.

Everything was the same.  Beat up chairs.  Crazy tweaker serving up the caffeine.  Insane 50-something year old bum in need of 12 showers and a make over . . . spewing out eloquently groomed italian to passer-bys.  Pimple faced graduates in cap & gown with proud parents (obviously divorced).  TAs having their last office hours. And Me.

A REAL coffehouse misunderstood by most except for those having experienced life . . . love . . . and final exams at UC Berkeley.

Every semester I always tell myself just how much I hate Milano. I say I won't go back unless I will literally starve and I say I will remember it the next semester.

Every semester, around finals week, I somehow have a GSI that holds office hours here, or a study group that decides to meet in this location. When that happens, I forget just how much I hate Milano

It's standard Cafe Roma espresso except worse... It's often very burned, the coffee is okay at best (my cafe au lait was barely drinkable... not quite sure how you screw that up) and the service is horrible except for one man who I presume is the owner. 

The cafe itself is spacious, including an upstairs area, but the bathroom is often dirty and located right next to the kitchen. The service is unpleasant, as I mentioned previously, and the muffins and super dense and chewy... I thought muffins were supposed to be light, not dense.

On the plus side, they do make a damn good Chai Tea, but hopefully now that I've yelped Milano I will actually remember not to go back.

This place is hard to stumble upon if you're not a local, but is frequented by many students daily during lunch.  The sandwiches are pretty standard.  Sliced deli meat on sliced deli cheese on your choice of bread, with your choice of condiments.  I really feel like I could make these types of sandwiches at home.  The prices are pretty reasonable for students (came out to 11 dollars for two sandwiches and two drinks).  Their ingredients are very fresh, but also very ordinary.  This is a great place to stop and grab a bite, but you'll have forgotten about it as soon as you finish the sandwich.   If you're looking for a more unique sandwich, try EZ Stop Deli on Shattuck.  The staff there has alot more character, and they use carved chicken and turkey for their sandwiches.

Cheese n' Stuff gets you the most bang for your buck when lunch time rolls around. They seem to have the same type of sandwich that most places around campus have, like the Bear's Lair and Sandwich Zone, but the service here is really great. The owner is super nice and makes an effort to know the regulars. Some of the fraternities even have meal plans here where they get like 5 sandwiches a week! They also do lots of catering for campus events, especially for Cal athletics.

My favorite sandwich here is the vegetarian. You get a huge, 1/2 inch thick slab of feta cheese, avocado, and all the veggie toppings. Its the perfect light lunch. My other favorite is the turkey delight, although this one can be pretty messy. It has turkey, cranberry sauce, and avocado. Turkey and cranberry is an A+ combo. Plus, pretty much every sandwich is under 5 dollars, most under 4. Can't get cheaper than that! Oh, they also have dirty chips to go with your sammy! So good!

If you're hungry, this place'll fix the problem for cheap.  The sandwiches are good -- not memorable, but tasty and filling.  You have enough cheese and bread options to get the sandwich you want.  Fast service, nice employees.  Nice place to grab a sandwich to go and then find a sunny place to eat.

Whoa! Fantastic Turkey Delight sandwich for under $4? Dolmas by the dozen for under $4? Cheese 'N' Stuff serves fantastic deli sandwiches for great prices (especially if you happen to find a coupon for their sandwiches). Service is friendly, and they offer a selection of salads on the side. Definitely a must if you want a good, tasty but cheap sandwich near campus. Try the Turkey Delight on dutch crunch!

i gave this place 4 stars because of its inconsistent hours! They pretty much open when they feel like it    :(  Lines can get long but it moves fast. The workers are really nice. This is a great place to get a quick, cheap, yummy lunch! You can create your own sandwich. You first choose the bread, then cheese, then meat and other toppings. If you're afraid of creating your own sandwich, I recommend the crab salad and chicken salad sandwiches!

All time favorite place for a sandwich! It's prices haven't changed much in 7 years... still under $3 or so for a filling sandwich. Their opening hours are sometimes erratic, as they open when they feel like it, but you'll know when they're open because there's a line out the door. Fast, cheap, fresh and delicious!

Not one of the best sandwiches around, but still really good for the price.

$3.95 to get a sandwich with your choice of meat, cheese, lettuce, pickles, onions, sprouts, tomato, and mustard/mayo. The sandwiches don't look big, but trust me when I say they are filling. I got the roast beef on dutch crunch and it was satisfying. My friend ordered the Chicken Pesto Panini, and he said it was a bit on the salty side...so maybe stick with the cold sandwiches.

Everything here looks and tastes fresh. It's close to campus as well so that's convenient. The people working there are also very cordial.

If you're craving a sandwich for a cheap price I'll point you in Cheese N Stuff's direction

who would have thought that such a shanty-looking deli would produce such great sandwiches? the turkey is great and around $3. they are CASH only though which is a pain, but they do accept the Cal1 debit card. 

just fyi, it is between durant and channing in that little cove area of shops.

I've been coming here for more than a decade now, and Sam and company are my favorites. Sam is always smiling, there is always a line, and the sandwich is always fresh.

Their prices are good, the sandwiches are generously-sized, and the banter is friendly. They make sandwiches quickly and, with the exception of one employee who I believe hasn't been working there for a couple of years now, they get your order right. (The employee of whom I speak was spacey and would, oh, forget to put tuna in a tuna sandwich.)

My complaints are that they don't have vinegar (because I want my sandwiches swimming in vinegar) and that they're really only good for lunch or snacktime, because they close fairly early. This is more than made up for by the fact that their rolls are fresh, the amount of sandwich filling that they give is reasonable, and the service is friendly. More than once, Cheese 'N' Stuff has gone above and beyond by preparing _and delivering_ a pile of sandwiches for a student organization event at the relative last minute. 

They always do this with a smile. Sam can't be beat.

Ugh.. this was college subsistence at it's best...

Between this place and IB's... this was the place where I'd go when I could barely scratch a couple coins together to muster a sandwhich out.  The hours were kinda weird, but the dutch crunch rolls were good... and they were no frills.

Kinda hard to find as they are in the middle of the garage.. but a solid, decent. honest sandwich.

Good stuff

To be honest the sandwiches were kind of dry. The portions were extremely generous; the sandwiches were overstuffed with meet. My boyfriend got the turkey delight. It was decent, especially the cranberry sauce part. I got the chicken pesto panini which was also alright but like i said both were pretty dry. The man there was really funny though if that helps.

This place is like a staple for the Cal Track team...or at least it was. Better yet, its was a staple for the Cal athletic population as a whole (circa 2006). Why? Because it has pretty decent sandwiches for a good price. I think it was around $3.25 when I was there, don't know if that has changed though.

Anyways, its good. Go there. Make friends with the owner cuz he'll give you free toppings if he likes you. Just throwing that out there.

Amazing sandwiches, for a great price and nice friendly employees. In school when I didn't have time to make my own lunch, Cheese 'N' Stuff was my staple. I go back here when I visit Berkeley for football games and Sam still remembers my husband and me!

I always get the deluxe, no meat, with avocados on dutch crunch with pepper jack cheese.

I used to come here frequently for the awesome price for awesome sandwiches.

Environment and Service: Not applicable, since it's not really a sit down and eat sort of place. Just take your sandwich and go somewhere else to enjoy it.

Food: I almost always get the poor boy deluxe, which has a few different types of meat, like salami, ham, bologna, and another meat I had no clue as to what it was. I order without mayo, and it's delicious every time. The sandwich is flavorful with its many different meats and the cheese that you choose (I generally choose swiss). I think above all, it's the price that keeps me back. It's a little less than $5 for a sandwich. Excellent pricing, tasty sandwich.

Verdict: Definitely coming back for low priced sandwiches.
Really good and really fast; and quite inexpensive!  Definitely a place I wish I had frequented more during my first 2 years here...  Guess I'll have to make it up before I graduate!

I wish I heard about this place earlier during my Cal career. I always get the Turkey Deluxe and it has never failed to fulfill my cravings. For what you get, it's an extremely good deal. Less than $4 for a filling sandwich. They have a variety of other things such as pasta salads and such. It's extremely convenient because it's right by campus and it literally takes less than 5 minutes to order, pay and go.

I used to come here for lunch almost everyday during my freshman year. I still come here often, but I've had to exercise more self-control. Haha!

You'd never imagine a sandwich place in the location that it holds in that Sather Lane-like place on Channing. But, the sandwiches they serve are pretty good and service is fast. 

IMO, all the meats are about as good as the other. I usually go for the pastrami or the pepper turkey with everything. For whatever reason, I've become a big fan of the sprouts they add to their sandwich. Add cheese. The swiss, nothing too fancy, is my go-to. Good selection of bread too. I wouldn't recommend the sour french because it makes a mess of the the contents in your sandwich as it slides all over the place while you try to tear a bit of the bread with your teeth. The Dutch Crunch is probably a better choice. 

Sam, the owner, is a pretty friendly guy, probably more so if you are affiliated with any athletics program on campus. But, just as friendly, if you're just another ordinary student getting some lunch on the go.

Damn, where else are you going to get such a large sandwich for $3.50?  NO WHERE!  

I love their falafel sandwich.  Sometimes I just sit in class and crave the damn thing and have to go grab it for lunch.  I also love that they have such a large selection of drinks.  I swear they have every single flavor of Arizona manufactured.  

Basically they have a bunch of different deli meats and you can put whatever else you want on it like lettuce, tomato, cheese, onions.  Not sure if avocado is extra, but I'm pretty sure it is.

I've only tried the turkey delight here, and that's the only one that I'll ever try cuz it's so damn good! It's soooo moist and I love the sweet cranberry sauce with baked turkey and fresh lettuce.  Plus it's really really cheap! I always say to myself I'll save the other half for later, but I end up eating the whole thing on the spot.  The only minus is that they don't have any seating, so you have to find somewhere else to eat, like home or sometimes I eat at bears lair when I have to stay on campus.  Their pasta things in the display always look sooooo good... I will try someday!

This place is okay.

A lot of people don't know where this place is so just go inside of that indoor shopping area next to the parking lot that's adjacent to Unit 3. 

Nice change for when im not feellike subway. The employees are really nice so that's a plus. I've only gotten the turkey sandwich and that one is really good. One time I got the grape leave thing and it wasn't that good and it was pretty expensive.

It's been a while since I was a student, but I see from the reviews that Sam is still going strong.

My standard lunch was always a veggie (avocado and feta cheese) sandwich on dutch crunch.  That, a bottle of marteneli's and lower sproul was all I needed for a peaceful break between classes. 

I miss you Berkeley! Miss you Sam!

Not a GREAT sandwich, but for $3.50? 

heck, I pay more for parking.

Great cold cut sandwiches, like what's available at the GBC and Subway. They have a lot of different meats to choose from and even offer paninis. The hot pastrami sandwich is a little soggy, but what the heck, it's only $4.25.

I used to love this place, now not so much. Their sandwiches are beyond bland, like eating soggy cardboard.  I couldn't even finish half of my sandwich because it was that gross, gave the rest to a homeless and even felt bad that he had to eat such a gross sandwich.
subway tastes better, and subway sucks!

For what you're paying and what you're getting, this is really the best place around campus to go for your simple sandwich. Less than $4 for a large sandwich with lots of meat? Yes please!

I just tried their regular sandwich with dutch crunch and roast beef. It was a cold sandwich with your average ingredients, but everything was great and really fresh! The bread was hard to chew through and the meat didn't have that much flavor, but I was satisfied and considered saving half the sandwich for later because portions were generous. Probably the best meal deal I could find around campus for under $5. NOTE: Cal 1 Card or Cash only!

The place is difficult to find and hidden under the orange parking structure. It isn't a place to sit and eat, but a place to grab a quick sandwich. They also offer a variety of bottled drinks, potato salads, and wraps. I would love to try these foods, but I still think the giant sandwich is a better deal. Subway can't compare (plus, this place doesn't have the lingering Subway smell or the meaty Deli meat smell either)

Service is so-so. They aren't the friendliest of people and they strongly enforce their cash only rule. I was the only one in the store, so I wouldn't say service is particularly efficient.

WILL I come back: of course! What more can a cheap college student ask for.
WHEN will I come back: When I am decently hungry and only have $4 to spend
WHAT will I do differently: different bread, hopefully they aren't all tough to chew through
Great sandwiches, much better then subway imo. If you want good homemade sandwiche and atmosphere come here.

I'm back in Berkeley, and this was the first place I went for lunch, as a new graduate student. It was one of my favorites as an undergrad.

I foresee it still being one of my favorites. Well, I've actually only tried one sandwich here - the vegetarian special for 3.75. It's good and cheap - challah!!

This deli offers various sandwiches, wraps, fruit salad, yogurt, and some baked goods. They also have falafel. The sandwiches are great and cheap. I recommend the turkey delight and the crab salad sandwich. Their turkey wrap is okay. I definitely look forward to coming here more often.

One of the best deals I've come across in Berkeley in 25 years.     Generous-sized sandwiches at bargain prices.    Good pasta salad.   They also have an impressive selection of cheese, which you can buy by itself.     But I hope they've hired a separate cashier than the sandwich-maker (all that filthy money ..... eeeeeyew!).

Pretty good sandwiches. Five stars because of the price ($3.75 for a deluxe). 

-Nice people
-Very fast
-Customizable without a fuss
-Doesn't taste like crap (subway)

This place is hard to find, and I didn't know about it until halfway through my time at Berkeley. It's in an alleyway under the Channing garage, between Channing and Durant, East of Unit 3.

My go-to sandwich is peppered turkey on wheat, ask for avocado.

This place is quick and cheap for what it is. You can run here between classes and get a great meal for about 4 bucks. 

The downside is that I've had some old tasting meat a few times, so its kind of hit or miss.

One of my favorite places to eat. I come here at least twice a week to get their great sandwiches. I've never had to encounter anything other than good fresh ingredients and that along with how cheap and fast they make things just has to earn them 5 stars. 

I recommend this place to anyone who needs a quick bite and doesn't really want to spend a lot of money. Usually whatever you buy will be under $5 along with a drink.

Yummmm. I love this sandwich shop. Even though it is a little creepy to walk through the alleyway to get here, you can't beat $4 for an awesome sandwich... and you can get two types of meat on your sandwich for the same price! Its cash only, but luckily Bank of America's just across the street.

This is my go-to place for lunch between class. Always in and out within 5-10 minutes with my wallet just a little lighter and with a large, delicious sandwich. The sandwich makers are quite fast and there's usually a line out the door but you can be out really quickly.

This is one store with character, there's loads of posters with funny jokes and cal pride. The owner Sam has been in business for a long time and you can definitely see that he genuinely tries to create a rapport with the customer!

The sandwiches are cheaper than anywhere else around campus and they are loaded with anything you want. Definitely suggest the vegetarian sandwich, haven't been able to find a sandwich this good anywhere around campus!

There's no seating so everything has to be to-go. Only thing I wish was that they take credit card!

Sandwiches are made quick here for the reasonable price.  

I never got their basic sandwich, since I must have those extras in mine.  However, their turkey meat in their turkey sandwich isn't that great, but extra points for them that they don't charge extra for pepperjack cheese!

I have been frequenting Cheese "N" Stuff for nearly 30 years, during my years as a student and ever since, on the way to Cal football home games.  Cheese N Stuff is worth the trip, always fresh ingredients, the best bread you can find, awesome service, and Sam's uncannily accurate game predictions posted on the wall.  Highly recommend!

Sam is the best!!

I ate here for lunch everyday for a week straight.  I don't know if that makes me crazy or what, but I did it.  I'm really picky with sandwiches and sandwich places and I have three criteria that make a perfects sandwich place for me: Taste, Price, and Speed.  Cheese N Stuff is usually very delicious (try the poor boy), but i wish they had the seeded roll more often.  You can't beat the price of Cheese N' Stuff, and usually they are very quick to make the sandwich.  Great place overall/

Beware the thing with cucumbers is just a cold wrap, it's terrible. Don't eat it, but the sandwiches here are good for the price. Pretty standard prices with decent quality. 

The place is full of frat boys because they apparently take meal points or some type of points for the athletic program. 

I wish I knew about this place before I left Berkeley (I actually only came here after I graduated).

I loved this place when I was a student.  Quick, cheap, and tasty sandwiches right off the campus.  It is sort of hard to find if you dont know where it is.  In the alley next to unit 3.  My favorite was the croissant sandwich.  It's 50 cents more but it's always worth it.  The folks there are really nice too, I was 50 cents short once and they let me have my sandwich and soda anyway!  I made sure I paid them back the next time I was there.  =)

They also have a good selection of pasta salads and all sorts of goodies available too.  I tried the greek salad once but it was a little too salty for my taste.  But the potato salad was nummy.

What's not to love? The staff here is amazing, the food portions are good considering the cheap prices, and the location makes it convenient to grab a quick bite here between classes! I LOVE LOVE LOVE their chicken pesto panini (so full of melty cheesy goodness) and get their filling vegetable wraps when I'm in the mood for something healthier. I love how all their sandwiches are freshly made and packed right in front of you. 

Minus one star because they're cash only, and their timings aren't very convenient. Oh well.

I respect quality and integrity in a business, and this place has both. They are a small locally owned sandwich shop, and they excel in that category. The sandwiches are excellent. They are large, and since the shop is so popular the ingredients are always fresh. The prices are really low - it almost makes you feel bad for not paying more. Given the quality of the sandwiches, the speediness of the service, and the price, Cheese 'N' Stuff is a far superior value to Subway, Toaster Oven, and every other sandwich shop I have been to in the campus area.
Fresh sandwiches, which are prepared with a variety of ingredients.  Cheap and quick.  Highly recommended.
Cheese N Stuff is a famous among the students, Good Tasty Sandwiches made in minutes, Good for People on the Go.

Cheese 'n' stuff is so efficient, and the people there are so friendly!

Cheap sandwiches with fresh ingredients.  I recommend the roast beef with pepper jack on dutch crunch.
Best sandwiches ever and very affordable :)
This place is cheap and delicious! Their tuna salad sandwich is awesome!

A decent sandwich for $5? Holy crap! It's a good deal for starving students. My residents and I would normally run by Cheese 'N' Stuff for a quick bite when we needed a break from the dining commons.

+ I repeat: $5 for a sandwich, that's riDONKulous!
+ Lotsa' beverage and chips options
+ Sandwiches are pumped out fast!
- Meat sandwiches lack a lotttta meat
- Food is a bit below par

Final Call:
Since I don't live on campus near this plaza anymore, I haven't been to Cheese 'N' Stuff. While it's super cheap, the sandwiches aren't good enough to make a trip all on its own if you're not in the area regularly.

********************

Munchies:
1. Pastrami with cheddar on dutch
     -where's the meat?
2. Vegetarian on wheat
     -overuse on the dressing
     -feta doesn't taste right

This place is dangerous.  You start off eating there every so often.  Then it becomes every week, and then maybe 3 times a week.  The good news is that it's super cheap.  The bad news is.....hmmm...I don't think there is bad news!

The line goes out the door, but the sandwich makers are fast!  The owner is always nice and chats it up a bit if things aren't too busy.  On top of that, he'll sometimes kick in a discount.

Get a regular turkey on sourdough or dutch crunch.  You won't regret it.

That's right. FIVE glorious stars for Cheese 'n' Stuff. I can't stop eating here. Anything with the crossaint is damn good. Yea crossaints are bad for you, but who cares when it tastes this damn good. And its cheap! Like 3.50 cheap. bf loves the turkey delight...its Thanksgiving in a bite. And it's real turkey...none of that deli slice shit. The tabouleh is good too. I like to eat it w/ my sandwich. But yea...try anything with a crossaint. The owner is super nice and funny too. It's located in the "other" alley...the one across from Yogurt park.

I've been wanting to try this place out for a long time since I've heard so much about their wonderful lunch sandwiches for great college student price. Our club decided to get catering from them and we ordered a variety of sandwiches including Roast Beef, Turkey Delight, Vegetarian, Pastrami, and Ham. Personally, I think the Pastrami is probably the most savory. However, I don't find their sandwiches to be particularly special. For the price that they're offering ($4) for a decent size, it's worth a try.

Tastes alright, and oh so cheap. Like a good homemade sandwich, but you don't have to do the work for it. Sometimes the bread doesn't taste very fresh, but there's a very large selection. Overall, a pretty decent sandwich shop.

I. Love. Cheese 'N' Stuff.

Simply put--this is an old-fashioned deli bar with some lively characters.

Service has always been ridiculously fast and friendly. The owner, Sam, remembers me every time I go in and he's there. Asks how my classes are, asks how my family is, and name drops some people I have mentioned in the past. 

This kind of place makes me want to go back time and time again. Really cheap food for really high quality ingredients. I've dabbled with getting sandwiches in the area--Sam's Market, Smart Alecs, SF Soup Co., and none of them match the sheer quality of good Customer Service and just an honest to goodness love of it. 

Kudos, Sam. Keep it up, and I'll definitely be going back.

My new favorite place to buy lunch.  I always order a sandwich that is so simple that the delis back home, accustomed to more complicated order, tended to get it wrong.  Cheese 'N' Stuff has always gotten my sandwich right thus far and, as others have noted, the price is extremely reasonable given the size of the sandwich.  

I also love that they have Baked Lays and a wide variety of soft drinks.  The cookies and fruit look very enticing, though I've yet to give in.  

The gentleman who owns the place is perfectly charming.  He always smiles and asks me how my day is going.  The other people on staff seem polite and work very efficently.  

For me, five stars equals confidence that I'll walk out with a  meal I want to eat, purchased at a price I don't mind paying.

It's okay, especially for the price and fast service. But I've just had so-so experiences here. 

Sometimes, the sourdough bread is really stiff.... and it's kind of hard to bite through the whole sandwich... kind of hurts my mouth... (that's what she said, har har har) 

Whenever I try to get the veggie (feta cheese) sandwich---they seem to be out of something that is essential to making it like feta cheese, or sprouts (must have sprouts!)... so after waiting in that long line, i just leave...and end up buying the feta cheese and sprouts myself to make it. 

so, i think the place is all right for a sandwich UNDER (or about) 5 bucks--depending on what you get... but I've just had some unfavorable experiences.

i wasn't sure if i should give it 2 or 3 stars, but i decided on 2 because i was just so disappointed. 
Now this could be because cheese n stuff is supposed to have good sandwiches, but i'm a vegetarian, so i just got falafel, salad, and beans. But still, a place should be good no matter what you get. The falafel was cold, not fresh, kinda hard, and lacked flavor. The beans had wayyyyy too much oil on them, an the salad had way too much dressing. The only thing that made up for this was that they take Cal1 debit, and that the prices are relatively cheap.

For the price, the service, and the food, this is as good as it gets. Sam is awesome, seeing him really brightens my day. I recommend getting the poor-boy on a croissant with feta cheese, avocado and spinach. The sandwiches are cheap and usually pretty good. Great for any people not on a Cal Dining meal plan looking for some quick food.

Places like this are what I'll miss about Berkeley when I leave: good food for cheap. Sandwiches are less than $5 and you get a generous stack of meat or veggie filling if that's your preference. I like the chicken salad and the falafel (not in the same sandwich).
Had the cranberry-turkey sandwich, and while it was $7ish (expensive in my book for a sandwich), it was still pretty yummy! The store people are REALLY nice.

One of my favorite establishments...for the price (less than 4 bucks) they make the best deli sandwiches around. The ingredients are fresh and piled high; I especially like the cheeses, but the salads are great too.

Try a pastrami and provolone--no mayo, of course--on a sweet french roll. You'll be hooked on the joint--Berkeley's Best for many, many years now.

Cute friendly place.
Fairly large sandwiches for the price.
Good quality & nice staff. Definitely beats the usual 7$ you have to spend at chain sandwich shops for less sandwich and less deliciousness.

This place is good for cheap food but not quality. Ive heard on more then one occasion that the meat freshness is questionable and also that a friend ordered a sandwich where the eat was still icy. Also apparently if your an athlete you can bypass the whole line and go to the front. Not a good deal for the rest of us!

It's been a bit since my college days, but I remember this was the place to eat for a poor college student. Not only cheap food, but healthy as well.

It's all about the pepper turkey on dunch crunch roll, with pepper jack cheese. Mmmmmmmm, now that's a sandwich!

LOVE THIS PLACE IT IS DELICIOUS! after being here for a year, this is definitely my favorite place for cold sandwiches. I always get the pastrami on dutch crunch with pepper jack cheese, and I'm always satisfied with my meal. Not to mention, the sandwiches here are only $3.95! The people are incredibly nice too!

Cheap, fast, conveniently located, and delicious. You can't get a much better combination than that! I used to go for the pastrami but one day found my meat to be filled with fat (this caused me to take about a year hiatus from Cheese N Stuff, regrettably) but I then switched to Turkey on a wheat roll and have never been disappointed since. At $3.25 for a sandwich and a smile from Sam (the cute owner man), you can't go wrong! I definitely survived many a hectic day by stopping into this place to grab some food on the way to my next class. With so many Cal grads in SF, I bet they'd make a killing just by word of mouth if they decided to expand...

A quick lunch favorite of mine, Cheese 'N' Stuff provides an awesome sandwich for a really cheap price (perfect for grad students!).  Go for the deluxe sandwich (meat and cheese of your choice) on a croissant and you won't be disappointed.  The croissants are super fresh, soft, and buttery and make the perfect ends for a filling sandwich.  My only wish is that the meat was sliced fresh to order, but it's good quality nonetheless.  You can't beat the owner and employees either; very friendly people.  Go enjoy one now!

the deluxe sandwiches are 3.25 with meat, tomatoes, alfalfa, lettuce, mayo and mustard and cheese - very filling, good quality, and super cheap!
i always get the Peppered Turkey and Pepper Jack! AGH.
And! their BROWNIES are NOT TO BE MISSED. yes, $1.75 is a little steep, but hiiiighly recommended! So GROOD.
also, they have an extensive energy drink selection.
This is a pretty standard deli.  Nothing to complain about.
such good sammiches! can't believe i finally ate at this place after 3.5 years of going to school here and living right next to it.

Sam's Cheese n Stuff is awesome. The staff is friendly, the line moves quickly and they have exactly what you need. I love getting the turkey and avocado on a croissant with chips and a drink. I've been getting the same sandwich since I first started going to CAL back in 2003. The price is reasonable and SAM is the MAN!!!

Not till I graduated Cal and moved out of Berkeley did I realize what a gem this place is.  Cheese N Stuff is a model of how a sandwich place should be run, even one that's obscurely nestled in a passageway beyond street view.  For $3.25 (though I'm sure more now) you were able to get your pick of fresh meat and your everyday selection of veggies and condiments.  My regular choice (at least twice a week) would either be a pepper turkey and jack on a sweet roll or, for a slight upgrade, the renowned Turkey Delight -- the best attempt at a Thanksgiving meal between two halves of bread.  The look of the place is that of a simple deli, albeit one frequented by Cal athletes.  Autographed photos of coaches and players line the walls, and I once wished the great Aaron Rodgers luck for his next game while we were both waiting in line here.

It's been awhile since I've come here, but I still think about the peppered turkey deluxe on dutch crunch I used to get once a week for lunch.  Their lines are often out the door around noon, but they're quick and cheap, so it's totally worth the wait.  Plus if you go often enough, you can befriend Sam and he'll kick $0.75 off your sandwich.  And when you're a student, a couple of those $0.75-discounts adds up to a mini frozen yogurt + topping across the street!

I'd give it 3 stars for the food, but 4 just because it's so cheap! This tiny deli is located inside the Postal Annex alleyway, so I didn't discover it until later in college. The sandwiches are filling and always stuffed with all the goodies I can point to for only $4! You can't really go wrong with this place for a quick, satisfying lunch. It's tempting to go to Subway when they have to locations, but this place is far superior. The line can get a little long sometimes, so try to avoid lunch time rush by arriving 15 minutes after. The line always moves quickly though, so you'll be set with your great sandwich in no time! Keep in mind though, there isn't really any place to sit inside, so plan to take your meal elsewhere to enjoy.

oh the memories. i used to get so many sandos here...half pastrami half salami on a sweet french roll for under 4 bucks...jeez, that's so unheard of now that i work in the city. we always make sure to stop by for a sandwich to bring into the game and see sam's prediction for a golden bear win.

I used to frequent this place when I went to UC Berkeley.  Not the best sandwiches ever, but I remember this place was cheap, fast, and convenient to go to.  When I was on this side of campus and wanted a sandwich, I used to come here for my fix.

Another convenient sandwich shop by campus. If you read enough of my reviews, location and convenience is super high on my list. This place is right next to bus stop and it takes literally 5 mins to get there and back for class. 

The service is super quick and the sandwiches are good. Order the deluxe, I love my condiments and the works. Ive tried the turkey and cranberry, its tastes like thanksgiving. Turkey is also really good, but most of my buddies enjoy the pastrami and salami.

It's a great value for a standard lunch. It really saves students when they don't have time to prepare a lunch but don't want to break their wallet. It is a lighter option than much of the asian ghetto food or la burrita/top dog.

Btw, the owner Sam is a great guy, he really takes the effort to connect with the community. A true family run business. It's only because of the service that this is 4 stars instead of 3 [food's pretty average].

Cheese n stuff is a reaaallly cheap place to eat. I think it's less than $4 for a quality sandwich which is a deal u can't beat. They also have a lot of good sides too, like salads, pasta salads, Mediterranean stuff (dolmas, falafel, etc), etc. Oh, and i think they have coupons in those Guide to Good Life books that makes this place even cheaper. So yeah, good food, good deal!

Deluxe.
Dutch Crunch.
Turkey.
Provolone.
Avocado.
Can't go wrong. Affordable. Perfect for college students!
Man, for the price, this place is great! Not your best sandwich, but damn, under 4 bucks for a bunch of meat, cheese, bread, sprouts, lettuce!

I walk into here knowing exactly what I want: the vegetarian sammich dealie. It simply tastes so good on all of the breads that I've tried (not to say that I've tried all of their breads, though) and always bursting with fresh, green ingredients. Mucho avocado and slices of feta cheese nicely complemented with sprouts and tomatos - it really was my sandwich of choice in my early undergrad years. I've always preferred the sandwiches here to the now closed Sufficient Grounds, despite the fact that they are considerably smaller. Lines can be long, but service doesn't clog up too badly. I wish that they had a place to eat so that I didn't have to walk into the units in order to find a decent bench.

They have the freshest deli sandwiches in Berkeley, hands down.

I've stopped by the small shop a couple of times whenever I passed through the seedy, shady tunnel in which it's located. They have a large selection of meat, cheeses and bread, all laid out behind a glass partition so you can watch them make it.

They're around $4 (or even less, sometimes) for a sandwich that will fill you up for lunch but not leave you feeling gross like you just ate a greasy burger.

HOWEVER, they have really short hours and sometimes they close earlier than they're supposed to which kinda sucks.
Cheap, yummy, friendly service.  I don't know what else to day.  I personally like dutch crunch and peppered turkey.  Oh, and I love that they put a good amount of mustard on (no mayo for me).

This is a deli where you'll get a great sandwich to your liking for a great price.  Its a deli, so you're not going to see places for you to sit and eat.  But if you're looking for a cheap and healthy eat, grab a sandwich from here and walk over to the campus (if its a nice day) and eat outside.

I always get the croissant sandwich - so delicious!

Best taylor made sandwich in Berkeley. I love this place, you can realy build your sandwich the way you want, they have great combo too.

Large choices of bread and meat, really my preferred sandwich place in Berkeley.

I got the pastrami here...and it was a sloppy, gooey, over-sauced mess.  No, I did not wait 1 hour before I ate my sandwich.  Not well put-together at all.

I usually get the Poor Boy sandwich and I will definitely stick with that if i come back.

This place is very consistent, fast, and one sandwich really fills me up. I like their turkey a lot. Moist, easy to bite, sweet french roll. Sprouts? It's worth the walk from Shattack to Telegraph. Take the sandwich to campus and find a nice bench to people watch as you munch munch munch. Just be careful of the squirrels, one distracted me while the other was coming up from behind as I ate my turkey sandwich...
