This place is essentially the same thing as The Coffee Spot on lower sproul, but with more things I think, namely cheese. They also have chicken salad, and I feel like their sandwiches may actually be larger. Minus points for the inconvenient location, however.

This great sandwich place is tucked in the belly of that obnoxious, ugly parking garage at the corner of Durant and Telegraph. Journey into the depths of the beast to have a sandwich from cheese 'n' stuff. It's delicious.

The bread is always fresh, as are the ingredients. The staff is fast and friendly, and there is a wide variety of chips, drinks and baked goods. (There are even vegan cookies, if you pay attention to those sort of things, which I do...while I'm paying for my roast beef sub.)

Warning: they don't take cards!

Everyone tells me about how great the sandwiches are at this place but I think they are all just blinded by how cheap the sandwiches are and not really considering how good they actually are. It's not like they are bad, but it's not that great either. Very mediocre, but it is SUPER cheap. Around ~$3 a sandwich, hey, for a starving college student that's low on cash, this is like an ant colony stumbling upon a tub of sugar! Indulge!

My only gripe is that they weren't open for dinner.

I love Cheese N Stuff, I've praised it to all my friends as the best value in Berkeley for food by far. It definitely shines with the price but the sandwich quality is *not* lacking at all. Just make sure to get here before the lunch rush, otherwise you'll be waiting quite a bit.

I also always enjoyed the predictions for Cal football games behind the counter. Go Bears!
Across from yogurt park in an alley. Delicious and cheap. I highly recommend the roasted turkey sandwhich. Killer.

The Honest Truth: Cheap, quality, fast sandwiches.  Fantastic for a quick lunch.  Check it out.

$4 for a quality sandwich.

Theres nothing that makes the sandwich AMAZING enough to be five-star worthy (no special sauces or crazy combinations of toppings), but the service is nice and fast, food is extremely cheap and its still good quality.  You can get a sizeable sandwich in between class (since its close to campus) and they also accept Cal1 Card.  I usually get a turkey deluxe on Dutch crunch with pepper jack cheese that never fails me. 

If you've never heard of this place, you need to go.  And if you have heard of it, you're probably a loyal fan

I've only been here twice, and yet when I knew I was going the second time I was anticipating my delicious roast beef sandwich with everything but the onions. Yum yum yum! Their sandwiches may be smaller in length than Subway, but boy do they make up for it with flavor and quantity of ingredients! The roast beef is delish... honestly, haven't tried anything else since it was so good the first time. I don't think I've ever had bean sprouts in a sandwich before. Turns out I really like it thanks to this place!

I came here originally because Subway and Blondie's didn't validate for the channing parking garage. This place does with a $5 minimum purchase. Works out since I save $6 on parking getting it validated here =D

Nice people. Very helpful for little ol' me that couldn't reach the Snapple I wanted on the top shelf.

Cash only!!

Today I walked in here and it smelt like thanksgiving. I then spent the next few minutes debating how much longer this vegetarian thing will last (6 years going) But really, I love their veggie sandwiches, they are always made with the same eye for quality, and everything always tastes fresh (with the exception of one week of bad avocados... but we all know that happens). All in all, this is a good place to grab a quick, cheap and dependable sandwich.

Heard great things about this little hole in the wall sandwich shop for years before I finally tried it the other day. And let me tell you, I was not disappointed. 

Ordered the hot pastrami sandwich for $4.75 with dutch crunch bread. The sandwich was absolutely delicious! Flavorful, satisfyingly salty, and nice and warm. 

I was eying the cheese tortellini in the deli case that I think I'll try next time. It was only 2.95 for half a pint. They have a good selection of chips, drinks, and candy as well. 

Service was fast and friendly. I had a quick little chat with the owner before I left. The normal, cold sandwiches are all under $4 bucks and they taste way better than Subway. I'll definitely be coming back!

My favorite quick lunch spot in the campus area, CNS is full of energy and the vegetarian sandwich is amazin. Though it's a little tricky to find, once you know this spot, you'll thank the sandwich heavens for this divine gift. The line can look pretty lengthy at times, but I promise even when it's out the door it's no longer than a 2-3 min wait. And in that time you can check out the hotties wrestling one another across the way.

cheap!! their sandwiches are like the ones at the Den or the GBC. i gotta say, i loveee my turkey with cheddar on dutch crunch. sandwiches are $2.75 for meat, cheese, and bread, and $3.25 for the "deluxe" option: choice of sprouts, tomatoes, onions, and lettuce. i really should try some of many other meat options here (roast beef, pastrami, dry salami, crab...) but i've been so happy with turkey.
my only complaint is that they don't toast your sandwiches. service is fast, and the guy at the cashier (manager?) seems to like to tease people (but not me so far).

Cute little deli tucked inside the...I don't even know what you call that place. It's the corridor that takes you from Durant to Channing, underneath the big orange parking structure. There are actually quite a few storefronts down there that may be of interest to people...but let's focus on these sammiches.

Cheap sandwiches at $4, but they're actually good. Make it a meal (soda and a drink) and walk out with lunch for less than $6. There can be a line though during meal hours...usually lunch.

Convenient sandwich deli to campus. Definitely beats subway in terms of variety. Service is always quick so this is a convenient, quick, inexpensive place to grab some grub in-between classes or study sessions. 

They have a wide selection of cheeses, deli meats and salads (chicken and crab) to fill your sammies with. Bread options are typical, although they do have dutch crutch rolls.

Good food. Good communications. 

The falafel sandwich is really good. The tabbouleh they have is as equally delicious. 

This is a good place to go for a quality sandwich between 3 and 5 dollars.

Okay, so there's this widely known sandwich place on the corner of Bancroft & Telegraph (that can practically be found on every block in America, aka Subway)-- but why not walk a block further and enter a real sandwich deli at Cheese 'N' Stuff? 

I've seen this place with a huge line out the door and other times have walked right in, but either way it's fast and wonderful service. They give a great amount of meat and fresh bread that always fills my hungry student appetite. Best of all, the reasonable price makes the sandwich that much more enjoyable, knowing that walking that extra bit from campus not only supported an independent owner, but it didn't hurt my pocket any more than if I would have went to the franchised alternative.

Memories of not being able to eat my Cheese 'N' Stuff sandwich while I had my braces on because the bread was too hard prevents me from giving it the 5 stars! As if having braces wasn't torture enough, I had to eat my sandwich without the bread after multiple painful tries. With my braces off, nothing should prevent me from biting into that dutch crunch bread now!
If you are living on the "poor college student budget," then come here. Cheap and delicious sandwiches for $3-4 and they are big. Their dutch crunch rolls are the best.

For the price, you're not getting a gourmet meal, but you are definitely getting a something quick and easy, which makes it one of my go-to places for a cheap student lunch.

I'm actually not a huge fan of the crowd favorite Dutch Crunch Roll just because it tends to be TOO crunchy and hurts the roof of my mouth, though it is delicious. One of the great things about Cheese "N" Stuff though is that you can pretty much customize your sandwich in any way you see fit.

I like:

Turkey Delight with turkey, avocado, and cranberry sauce. It's rather juicy, but so very very tasty.
Deluxe Falafel Wrap that is bigger than any other item on the menu and great if you love falafels.
Paninis! They actually make very decent ones here and though pricier and smaller than the rest of the menu, they're a good choice if you want to splurge.

The owner and employees are also quite friendly and fun to chat up.

Big sandwiches for almost no money. Don't let the bro/frat boy/athlete scare you off - the sandwiches here are awesome.

Definitely stick with the sour dough-based rolls (seeded is my personal favorite) - the others just aren't filling enough. Also, I try to buy drinks elsewhere. Their selection is pretty good, but a little pricey (compared to the $3.50 sandwich, $1.50 for a good soda is steep).

You get what you pay for, but that's a good thing. Nobody wants to spend a ton on a sandwich. They'll slap together a serviceable sandwich in seconds and you'll be satisfied.

Back in the day, I had a thing for the Scandinavian girl behind the counter, lol.

I guess for the price it's a steal ($3.50? cheap cheap cheap).

Imagine the GBC or Peet's sandwiches but for much cheaper and that's basically what you'll get here. 

I tried some sandwich with seafood (probably a bad decision in retrospect) and my tummy was ANGRY after that D: It almost turned me off entirely to Cheese n stuff.

Came back and gave them another go though with their thanksgiving like sandwich (turkey, cranberries) and it was decent. 

Lesson learned: don't get any sandwiches with mayonaisse or any possible chances of creaminess. Stick with the classics.

I LOOOVE CHEESE N STUFF!

Really just a great sandwich place. One of the best, basic sandwich places for this ridiculously low price.

You can get pretty much anything you want in a nice little sandwich (my guy friends complain this is too small compared to a Subway footlong...buy two then, they're cheap enough).  And it's sooooooo ridiculously cheap!  I almost always get a deluxe salami sandwich on sweet french with cheddar cheese, all the toppings except mustard.  Although, I switch it up every once in a while.

The ingredients are fresh - unless you come at the end of the day.  I recommend stopping by for lunch... past 4pm and sometimes they run out of stuff =(

Otherwise, Cheese 'N' Stuff is amazing - I hope they never go away.  FYI, they only accept cash or Cal 1 Debit card.

I first started coming to Cheese 'N' Stuff my freshman year of college, when with the Cal tennis team.  A noble sponsor of Cal athletics, Sam knows how to take care of his athletes -- keeping them fed, energized, and faithfully supported.  For us, he made sure to have sandwiches, drinks, and sides ready -- for all the players, managers, coaches, and even the chair umps -- every day of every tournament, and all of the matches too.   

My favorite was always pepper turkey with pepper jack cheese on a sourdough roll, hold the mayo.  The sandwiches are huge, filled with the freshest deli ingredients, and perfectly assembled with careful attention to the proportions of each ingredient and every topping.  

These days I am not playing as much tennis as I used to, and have since graduated.  But, when I'm in town I always make a point to stop in for a sandwich -- and more importantly to say hello to Sam.  On my most recent trip back, Sam greeted me with an endearing "Hello stranger! Long time."  He then proceeded to fix up my usual order as we caught up with local news, sports, and each other's lives.  Thanks Sam, for always having my back!

I finally fulfilled my long-time desire to try the famous Cheese 'n Stuff and got the deluxe falafel wrap today for only $3.95 (minus $0.50 with the berkeleygoodlife.com coupon.) Is this place related to The Coffee Spot? They are very similar, and both popular because of their large and very cheap meals. There was a long line after class let out at 12:30pm, but it moved fast. They only have to assemble simple sandwiches, after all--the meats and fixings are laid out in front in a glass cabinet. Some of the ingredients looked a little old and unappetizing, but I certainly would not go expecting a gourmet sandwich, and definitely got what I paid for! The falafel sandwich provided lunch and dinner, which makes for two ridiculously cheap meals . The homemade hummus was interestingly very nutty, and I daresay I tasted a hint of peanut butter, which is weird and probably just me. The only disappointment was that it did not include cucumbers. I guess I just assumed the regular mediterranean side veggies.  

It is sweet that there are so many regulars that are friendly with the owner. The photos and notes from famous Cal athletes on the wall are a cool addition. Cheese 'n Stuff feeding celebs! I have a thing for good ol' sandwich shops.

You shouldn't come if you're indecisive. Too much stuff.

Forget Subway. It's all about Cheese 'N' Stuff. Cheap, fresh, big, delicious, and friendly! You can't go wrong here. If you're broke, they have a poor boy sandwich just for you too! Choose your own sandwich destiny from their wide selection of breads, meats, cheeses, and toppings. One of my favorites is the roasted turkey. It's got hot turkey with cranberry sauce tucked into a roll! Thanksgiving in every bite! Another favorite of mine is turkey with avocado. That combo is so money. Finally, complement your sandwich with some chips and a drink from their well stocked selection. They also have Greek salads and side dishes, which are also pretty dang good.

Tips: Find this little gem in the alley going through the big orange parking structure.
Cheap fix for a starving student.  Do get the Cranberry Turkey.  Do not get the potato salad.

Before I found Cheese N Stuff, I ate Top Ramen. Then I told myself... No, I will not have that stereotypical college ramen.  So I started eating at Chipotle. Yeah, I'm original. You don't have to tell me. But thank you anyways. 
Well I was too much a stingy bastard for Chipotle. So I switched to $3 6inch sandwichs from Subway, but deep inside, I was disappointed, like a chain smoker who switched to nicotene patches.
But one day, one glorious day, I saw a little sign that said "Cheese N Stuff" and I wondered... wtf is stuff? Is it wine? Crackers? Koala bears? Well I went in and found out.  "Stuff" is cheap, delicious sandwiches made to order from a variety of breads, cheeses, meats, and toppings. It's also salads that I haven't tried. But all that matters are the sandwiches. Seriously, go get one... now. You're wasting too much time reading this shit.

You know that satisfaction that people seem to have when they unwrap a sandwich and nonchalantly eat it while working on something? This guy came into one of my art classes with this gorgeous sandwich and I wanted to share his experience. When he told me that it was from a place called "Cheese N Stuff," I was INTENSELY intrigued. What a genius name for a deli.
It's nestled in those weird tunnels off of Telegraph. Not only is it a precious hole-in-the-wall with lots of tasties, but it's insanely cheap! You can get the vegetarian with an iced tea for like 5 bucks. The guy there always tells me to "stay away from boys! They're trouble!" And how right he is.

I'm a fan.

Delicious sandwiches and such a wide variety of meats! The sandwiches are also super reasonably priced. I got the pastrami sandwich and it definitely filled me up. 

I came here to buy sandwiches for the officer team of my club. They make them very quickly and it tastes really fresh - you can call-in and order beforehand. The owner/cashier is also a super sweet and friendly guy.

I wish they had more marketing/a better location - so many people don't know about this place, and they are missing out!

I've been at Berkeley for over three years now, and Cheese N' Stuff is still my favorite sandwich stop for lunch. With it being ridiculously cheap, you could get a filling sandwich for less than 4$! The location is convenient also, as I've found it possible to stop for a quick bite to eat within a 20-minute time frame and be back on campus in time for class. 

Although I have read the reviews before and some people comment upon the immediate stomach pain after eating one of these sandwiches, I can say that happened to me a couple times also. However, the majority of the times have been good, and its pretty much one of the cheapest meals for broke college students that you can find in Berkeley.

This is the perfect place for a student on a budget. Tasty sandwiches, good portion size and, best of all, cheap! It's also close to the dorms and campus.

Things to note: lunch time = long lines because most people know the above and it's right next to Unit 3.

Recommended Sandwich: Turkey Delight. Turkey, avocado, and cranberry sauce. It's very thxgiving-y but quite delicious. I never got tired of this sandwich.

I've forgetten how I heard about this place, but the first time I tried it was three years ago and I still love coming here. I always get the salami deluxe on wheat (I don't even like wheat, but its good here) and am perfectly satiated at the end of the meal. How can you beat a tasty $3.50 sandwich??

Good sandwich - well put-together, made quickly, tasted great, inexpensive. Ordering was easy, no confusion, no difficulty, food was made quickly. Took get a fifth star maybe I wanted to see a bit more pesto on the chicken sandwich, maybe a bit more lettuce on others. We'll see though, I'm only one visit in so far - a few more and that elusive fifth star might well appear.

very quick service! and very friendly~

definitely try the poorman's sandwich - a VERY delicious sandwich for just $3.50? yummm! :D

plus, if you want your own personal sandwich - they had a pretty good selection of meats, cheeses, 5 or so types of breads... some side mixed salads...

I just happened to park in this garage this afternoon and so on the way back to my car my stomach started making that rumbling.  I was just going to keep walking to the ticket booth when their sandwich board caught my eye: $3.50 for a veggie sandwich?  No way!  And it was tasty too.  They made it in probably less than a minute and for $3.50 you got quite a bit of stuff in it.  Alfalfa, cheese, tomatoes, and other things I can't remember.  But it was good.  Plus I got half off of from validated parking.  Not bad at all!

Times visited: 1

This is such a bargain; fast, cheap and delicious.  I am a HUGE fan of the Hot Turkey Sandwich.  Its like Thanksgiving on a roll!  Also be sure to try the chocolate covered Halvah they sell for dessert, ALWAYS makes my day brighter.

Falafel sandwich is a party in your mouth.
Other sandwiches are great too
Perfect place to hit up, grab some sandwiches, then hit the UC campus or go into the gardens above

Just wanted to update this review to say that Cheese N Stuff continues to be awesome.  I stopped by here on Saturday (yes, Cal Day!) and got a delicious "deluxe" sandwich (mayo, mustard, tomatoes, pickles, lettuce, sprouts) on their delicious Dutch Crunch bread.  I got salami but the pastrami looked delicious too and my friend who got their chicken panini was very pleased.  The vegetarian sandwich also looked delicious and they have some of the best Tabouli/tabbouleh I've ever had.  Love this place!

pepper turkey with cheddar, on dutch crunch. no mayo. no pickles. everything else.
maybe grab an izze.
with a s'mores cookie on the side. 

and you're set. and you still have money in your pocket. and time to spare.

I really don't know why students go to Quiznos and subway when this gem of a place exists. Not only does it have the perfect ratio of cost to quality but it has 'stuff' that's supposed to be standard deli fare but is somehow lost in translation when they go franchise. Prime example- the beloved Dutch Crunch roll. How subway and Quiznos could neglect Dutch Crutch is beyond me. This place also has a ton of middle eastern 'stuff' ...

no, not opium. 

I'm talking about dolmas, tabouli, falafel and all that good jazz. But it's still really all about that cheap delicious sandwich. The deluxe is $3.25.... pick yr of bread/meat/cheese/toppings and go munger around the disgusting filth that is the Berkeley campus southside.

I love this place! Not only does it take Cal1 cards from students, but you can get a large, tasty sandwich on delicious bread for under $4.  The owner didn't take long to learn my face and engage me in playful banter.  Service is super fast and all employees are friendly.  Don't waste your time at Subway.  I'll forever be loyal to Cheese 'N' Stuff!

I tried on three different occasions to find this place because I thought it was in that other alley near telegraph. D'oh! I finally got better directions from my coworker and found myself in the little nook of Cheese 'N' Stuff.  And it was ok.  Turkey sandwich on a big ol' roll - nothing too special all-around.  Like many things in Berkeley, maybe you enjoy this place more if you're a student.  I think I'd rather go down the street and brave the line at Intermezzo. Like I do pretty much every week. Like I just got back from doing. I need help.

You want to know why there's so many panhandlers in Berkeley? It's because collecting change for two hours in front of Fat Slice is enough to buy you a pretty delicious sandwich here.

The reason there's so many crazies is because the Dutch Crunch really scrapes the shit out of the roof of your mouth.

What was it about that old girlfriend from high school that you really liked? 

Oh yeah, she was cheap and reliable. 

Same here. Get a good sandwich and stop the hunger pains.

Cheap and strangely addictive. Once you try this place you'll be going back. It's not necessarily remarkable in any way but it's reliable and portable -- sometimes that's your top priority.

I had a funny run-in with the guy that runs the shop. I accidentally dropped a nickel or something in the garbage can and it turned out that the can was empty and he'd just washed it. He implored me to get my change back. "Don't worry, it's clean," he said.

"Sometimes you gotta let the hard ones go," I replied.

He got really upset that I would just throw money away like that. He made a huff and walked away, disgusted. His reaction amused me so much that I think it was worth it.

Hooray for a sandwich shop that is tastier, faster, bigger AND cheaper than the local university dining commons.  I ordered a pastrami w/provolone on sour french bread - deluxe: only $3.50.  I turned around to talk to a friend as I walked over to the register and the guy was already there ringing up my sandwich - it was amazing.  At the DC, I'd wait at least 5 minutes for the guy to slowly put my sandwich together, put it through the slow toaster, and then slowly wrap it up, to receive an okay sandwich - and that's with no line.

The sign on the door says something about sometimes not being open..? whatever - its good.

Mmmm Sam's notoriously tasty and cheap sandwiches. You can basically get whatever combination of meats, chicken salad, tuna salad, even crab salad. You get your choice of bread, cheese, and all the fixings. All this for $3.50? Hot damn. You can even ask for extra meat and what not!

They also have this Aram sandwich, which is basically a wrap, for $2.95. It's made fresh that day and is a real bargain for how big it is. It's basically a sandwich in a tortilla, and it's just as a big as a Chipotle burrito in terms of filling.

These sandwiches are so simple and tasty and the people work really fast. Expect a line out of the shop at peak lunch times (12, 12:30, 1). Thumbs up for nice people and tasty cheap sandwiches that won't break a college student's wallet.

I went to Cheese N Stuff on a pretty regular basis during my Freshman year of college (regular means about once every other week when I just couldn't stomach the dorms or on-campus cafes anymore but wanted something cheap). I used to get their pastrami sandwiches or roast beef, which were all filling, delicious and insanely cheap. $3.50 for a great sized sandwich that would fill me the rest of the day.

I moved to the other side of campus and try to cook most of my meals at home now. I haven't been to Cheese N Stuff in over a year, but I decided to go back just to try it and see if it was as good as I remembered.

It was the same people working there as before, same line and same efficient service. I had the turkey delight on wheat, which is oven roasted turkey, lettuce, avacado and cranberry sauce. The sandwich had lots of cranberry (which I love) but the avacado was texture-less. Not slices with substance but smooth guac paste that didn't really have flavor and didn't add much to the sandwich except extra calories. The turkey was more dry than I remembered but I was starving and devoured that sandwich at a rate that's almost embarassing.

Was Cheese N Stuff as good as I remembered? No. I would certainly choose it over a subway any day of the week, but I feel there are much better choices for sandwiches in the surrounding area for just a little bit more (the little deli supermarket next door to Walgreens is surprisingly very good and makes a GREAT Reuben). Granted, those are all going to be in the $6 range instead of $3.50, so I suppose Cheese N Stuff is amazing for its price point.

-1 because the sandwich is still 4 stars but not 5 as I would have rated it 2 years ago.
-1 because they nickle and dime you to death for sodas and chips (luckily I don't eat either of those).

amazing! cheese n stuff is my new go-to lunch spot when i'm at school.  i was in and out in about 5 minutes and my sandwich was only $3.95!  i go the turkey delight with roasted turkey and cranberry sauce.  the turkey was delicious and moist, like thanksgiving turkey no slimy deli slices, and every other part of the sammie was good too.
one tip- bring cash, you can pay with your card but their little atm machine charges you $1

Great sandwiches for a moderate appetite! Perfect for a lunch stop!

Sometimes I hate how the sandwich portion sizes at Smart Alec's and Cafe Mattina are sooo huge.  You almost will always have to take half of it to-go in order to avoid food coma during class after lunch.  Cheese 'N' Stuff FTW!!!

Very tasty sandwiches and for cheap!!  Expect to spend less than $5.  Many different deli ingredients to choose from to put in your sandwich (e.g. cheeses (obviously), meat, bread, other veggies).  Don't go to GBC for your sandwiches to-go, come here!

This place does not have the best of location; I didn't even know about this place until a friend took me here.  It's in that hallway to the parking structure next to Unit 3.
I talked to the owner and apparently he was listening to Deadmau5's "Ghosts 'N' Stuff" when he came up with the name for his shop.

Oh Dutch Crunch Roll how I miss thee!!! I try to explain you to people who are not familiar or not from the Bay Area and they just don't understand!

Great fresh deli sandwiches, cheap and a hidden gem. Really, you can't see it just driving by! The sandwiches are filling and always kept me going for a marathon study session in VLSB as an undergrad.

To do it right: $4

I've walked by this place dozens of times without knowing it and would've kept on walking by had I not asked my coworker where she got her sandwich.  

Being Saturday and all, I wasn't in great shape from the night before and intended to go and get my usual Oh-God-why-didn't-I-leave-earlier-last-night?-crepe over on Telegraph (greasy crepes help to soothe the tummy).  However, I opted to try this place instead.  It's tucked into the alley next to the parking structure on Telegraph and in pretty deep, but easy to find if you're looking for it.  I walked in, ordered a turkey and swiss on wheat with mayo, mustard, pickles, onions, lettuce, and sprouts.  The price: 3.75.

By the time I got my change, the sandwich was already bagged--ridiculously fast to say the least.  What about the sandwich?  Actually, very good.  it's not the best sandwich I've had by a long shot, but it could very well be in the top three I've ever had under $5.

Final Say: Crazy cheap.  I don't think I'd do it every week, but from now on, if I'm walking by, hurried and hungry, it'll be hard to pass up.

This place serves cheese and stuff.  I had the stuff.  It came with cheese.

Actually, Cheese 'N' Stuff is a total misnomer.  This place is all about the sandwiches, although they also have some tasty enough looking macaroni salad-type things.

Here's the lowdown:

1. Customizable.  Dangerously so.  When I was in line, I had Sandwich Panic.  It's a terrible condition where you forget the names of all breads and cheeses in the world.  I managed "sourdough and American," but barely.  I don't even like American cheese, and it tasted funny with my crab sandwich, but that was my damn fault.

2. Cheap!  Insanely cheap!  With a $1.50 drink I barely broke $5.  How is that humanly possible?

3. Fast.  That line moves quick, and you're out of there.

Not the best sandwich I've ever had and not the greatest locale, but you can't beat the price or the speed.  The perfect college place.

Cheese N Stuff always brings the tasty.  The sandwiches are cheap, fresh and delicious.  I always spring the extra 25cents for the deluxe sandwich, which includes lettuce, tomato, onion, and sprout, and if I am feeling super decadent I will get the "Turkey Delight" sandwich.  The Turkey Delight is tender roasted turkey (not deli style), cranberry sauce, avocado!, lettuce, tomato, etc.  They have a great selection of chips and drinks, and the side salads are quite yummy as well.  There is nothing like a cheap good sandwich, and Cheese N Stuff knows how to deliver!

Turkey delight!  They use real oven roasted turkey, not that crap deli meat that tries to pass itself off as turkey.  The cranberries are perfect with it too.  Haven't tried anythign else there, this is worth walking down an obscure alley to try the sandwich.

If you were a Berkeley student and you never ate here as a student, they need to revoke your diploma. 

I LIVED at Cheese n' stuff. 

I was a broke-ass student on financial aid and the $3 sandwiches were large enough to actually be a meal and it was cheap. 

I would have the pastrami sandwich on dutch crunch about 2x a week. 

The lines at lunch are rather long but if you go in between classes you're good. 

Next time you go be sure to look at the walls and see all the cal alums who have been there (especially athletes).

This is one of my favorite affordable places to eat in Berkeley.

Cheese N Stuff is well-known among Cal students despite its location which is buried deep inside a building on Durant.  The location is knowledge passed down from senior students to the new breed each year.

My favorite joint from this place is the ever popular pre-made aram sandwich with roast beef.  This is a tortilla wrap style sandwich that you can just grab and eat.  Aside from being tasty and not loaded down with bread, they're dirt cheap.  It's pretty much the cheapest thing you can get there that still works as a serviceable lunch.

If you're a student, this place is worth adding to your rotation.  If you're a tourist or visitor try out IB Hoagies instead, it's a block up the hill.  It's not as healthy but they make a damn good cheese steak.

Cheese N Stuff is probably my most favorite sandwich shop ever. Strong statement, I know, especially coming from me as I am obsessed with sandwiches. I could eat a sandwich for breakfast, lunch and dinner and I wish they were all from Cheese N Stuff! My favorite was the pastrami and provolone on a wheat roll, a close second would be the roast beef and cheddar. They have this delicious watery mayo, which may sound gross but it was heaven for me because I don't really like mayo all that much. There can be really long lines around lunch but they move really fast. Also, Sam the owner almost always runs the cash register and he really loves Cal athletes...and we love you too Sam!!! He hooks it up!

Old school sandwich class in Berkeley. CHEAP, tasty, and fast. I think the place is family-owned, and if you close your eyes a bit and listen to the chatter, you can almost believe it's a storefront for something a bit more insidious. But then, you think to yourself, c'mon, not here and quickly snap out of it.

I always go for the deluxe, and they're good about accommodating if you want two types of meat in your sandwich (like roast beef and ham with swiss). Great for lunches, and the price can't be beat relative to the other sandwich places on the south side: Quizno's, Sufficient Grounds, etc. Plus, since the place is mom & pop's, you feel like you HAVE to frequent it and be a patron. No nonsense, fast. Perfect for student life on the go.

Cheese n' Stuff is a legendary sandwich shop in the middle of one of a weird subterranean mini-mall near the Berkeley campus.  If you have a break between classes or need to grab lunch on the way to a football game, this place is great.  The sandwiches are cheap and very reliable - the prices go up about 25 cents every three years or so.   I switched to the deluxe sandwich recently, and I feel that the sprouts and tomato are well worth the extra 30 cents to upgrade the standard version.  Plus, the counter staff will respect your healthier, high-class ways.

Roast-beef-and-swiss on a seeded roll is my personal favorite, and while it's a close contest, I have to say I prefer the Stuff to the Cheese. Signs forbid kissing, spitting, Stanfurd fans, and knife-chasing inside the shop, so be warned.

Cheese N' Shit...it's what the locals (read: students) call it.

I always got the Turkey Cranberry...that some good ass shit. 

Cheapot Depot!!  I lived off of those my freshman year.  I still stop by sometimes and get one...mmm.

I'm hungry....*drool*...

A dietary staple in a college students (CAL students) life. 
Roast beef sandwich, with everything, bag of chips and a vitamin water. 

Cheese N Stuff is a perfect choice for a quick, healthy meal on the go. Dont mind the line, the staff is very quick and the sandwiches are always made to order.

A pleasant cafe with delicious, refreshing panini.  I had the alpino with proscuitto, anjou pears, and walnuts, which was an interesting, good mix. The cosmos is bomb  and never a failure! I suggest the alpino if you are more adventurous and cosmos for definite satisfaction.  Though it is a bit pricey, the quality of the bread, meat, and other ingredients is of superb quality.  The employees are also friendly!

I have had their fruit salad and grilled salmon dish and they were both really fresh. The people working there are really friendly and helpful and it's a nice place to sit down and have lunch with a couple friends.
Fantastic coffee, bagels, pastries.  I've only had one sandwich from their lunch menu, but it was delicious and unique.

10 Reasons Why I Will Walk Uphill For Nefeli Caffe
1. I'm too impatient to wait for a bus.
2. Their small cups of coffee are actually small. Like "tasse a cafe" small, made for the few people left who prefer not to have 24 ounces of coffee sloshing around in their stomachs or making 5 jittery trips to the toilet. The lattes are also nicely done.
3. Though their seating is limited and slightly cramped, the table by the window makes me feel like I have my own breakfast nook.
4. The menu is decently priced. You'll see a good deal of 6s, 7s and 8s, but just look at what is being offered! All of their panini are worth trying. (I have to try not to visibly salivate when someone near me is eating one.) They have tapas after 4 pm and cute little wine selection if you feel like Europeanizing your evening. Their idea of fruit salad is a far cry from a maraschino cherry half perched on a pile of unripe cantaloupe: strawberries, pear, walnuts, and honey make an appearance, as does the miracle that is Greek-style yogurt. Even the croissants seem better than usual.
5. They have croque monsieur. They have croque monsieur. They have croque monsieur. To anyone who wants to tell me that this is just a glorified grilled cheese sandwich: well, yes, but how often do you find just a good grilled cheese sandwich on the menu when you need one? Almost never. And of course I'm always craving one.
6. The counterpeople are decent human beings. Really.
7. The walls are painted with that heavenly Greek blue with touches of tomato red and yellow. Awfully cheerful.
8. Sometimes they play bossa nova. (Though, sometimes you can't hear yourself think.)
9. They have Limonata.
10. Who doesn't enjoy a tree-lined street named after an ancient mathematician?

While most places on the Northside of campus support a fast-paced, in-and-out style dining to accommodate busy student schedules, this place is an exception to this trend.  

If you have an hour to kill between classes, definitely come here for a quick bite and lounge around.  Bring a friend, get some coffee and chat (If you want to study instead, I suggest going to brewed awakening across the street.  It's like study central in there with more table space to work on)

I've only tried their Alpino panini with a side pasta (cashier's recommendation).  It's pretty tasty.  Personally, the portion size was more of a snack/light lunch and was a little pricy.  (I'd recommend going to Hummingbird Cafe or Stuffed Inn if you want a more substantial sandwich for more or less the same price)

I work up the street so I come here every day, the greek yogurt is the best, the sandwiches are better than anything else on northside, and the owner and employees are the coolest. If you go on the weekends they have a poached egg thing that's really good.

The greek salad is not at all like what most people would expect (like with lettuce...) but it is basically only tomatoes, cucumbers, bell peppers, red onions and feta cheese. The dressing is what makes the salad and I felt it could have used a bit more vinegar because it wasn't as tangy as I would have liked. 

My boyfriend got the ham pizza.... and the ham is like literally like sandwich meat ham... not very appealing... I saw them preparing the pizza and it was frozen--and I'm not even sure if they make it themselves. 

The cafe itself is pretty cute and cozy but maybe it is better for coffee/drinks than for its food. I just wanted to find a decent greek salad.

I went here with high expectations about their coffee after reading the many raving reviews about it. Perhaps I shouldn't have gotten myself all hopeful because I was surely disappointed and a bit embarrassed since I told my fiance that they were known to have really good coffee. 

I ordered the soy chai latte. I liked the fact that we were able to grate our own nutmeg over our own drink. But, I felt as though my drink had way too much soy that it took away the flavor of the drink. My fiance also said the same thing about his cappucino--just too much milk. 

I did order the infamous greek yogurt that everyone talked about. I agree with the majority-- it is good. The portion size was more than enough, too! It had honey drizzled in it, sliced strawberries, whole walnuts, pears, and grapes all on top of the yogurt.

This is the place to go if you want quiet, tea, and a nicely toasted bagel. The service is nice and the patrons are respectful. Even the homeless people here are nicer than elsewhere. Cute little spot.
Excellent place. Bold coffee, good sandwiches and hot soups. I like the Athenian and Cosmos sandwiches that are worth every penny.

Eh.

The food is ok.  The coffee does the trick.  Couple of tables outsite.  If nothing else is open, go here.

The espresso drinks are very good! My friend had 2 with her lunch. The sandwiches are very simple and portions are decent sized--servings will fill your tummy but not overload it. The side pasta salad was also very good. I had the Athenian sandwich and I highly recommend. Seems like they prepare their sandwiches in advance because the dishes come out very quickly but it's not a problem because they are still very good. I was pleasantly surprised by the ease of finding street parking. If you are on/near the UC Berkeley campus this is a great lunch spot. Oh! It's a small place inside so if you are wearing a jacket or other gear you have to be careful not to fall on top of the people around you or slapping them with your scarf. Pics on the wall are great to look at while you wait.

I had been meaning to go to this little cafe for quite some time, but never really got around to it until now. With all the libraries closed for the holiday, I decided to hike up to Northside to check it out.

Needless to say, I was not disappointed. The cafe itself was a lot smaller than I had imagined, but it was a perfect place to study alone. I really regret not ordering a cup of the highly lauded Illy Coffee, but I really need to rid of my dependency on coffee. -_- Instead, I ordered a cup of hot tea, which was satisfactory.

After five hours of sitting on my bum and studying, I ordered the Kosmos panini (can it even be considered a panini?) for an early dinner. The size of the sandwich disappointed me greatly, considering that I paid over $7 for it. However, IT WAS SO FLIPPING GOOD. Gahhh. The creamy cheese, the delectably cooked bell peppers and mushrooms... making my mouth water just thinking about it. The pear really ties everything together, flavor- and texture-wise. I feel compelled to put pieces of pear in all my sandwiches now just so I can relive that experience.

Overall, I was very pleased with my experience. -1 star for the itty bitty sandwich, but it's something that everyone should definitely try. :)
God I love this place.  Good coffee, good food, and a minimal number of douche bags.

The espresso here is by far the best around Berkeley. Sure, it's not Ritual or Blue Bottle, but it is pretty good (especially compared to the crap they try to sell on southside / any of the espresso roma's). They don't have any power outlets or wireless internet, which I'm pretty sure is purposeful, but it is a great place to come read or hang out with friends. I've definitely spent way too much money here over my 4 years at Cal, although my caffeine addiction thanks me for it.

Also, they have some of the best food on Euclid. Which isn't saying much, but it really is quite good (the mousaka really hits the spot on a cold rainy day).

I've passed by this place hundreds of times, and went in for my first time today.  I ordered the coppa panini.  It was just ok.  It looked neatly put together, but I wish it was grilled.  There was also too much sun-dried tomato, which felt like it overwhelmed the sandwich.  Oh, and it was also a bit expensive, at $8.50 for a cold sandwich and no sides (I got it to go).  But since so many people seem to like the Alpino and it costs 2 bucks less, I'll have to try that next time and maybe update this review.

I'm here now and the coffee is great, but the tunes indoors are a little too loud for my taste.  Great Airbears signal which is nice.

Outside there is ample seeting, but it stinks a little because I'm sitting next to a plant that seems to have been recently fertilized.  (If you're standing on the sidewalk looking at the front door, it's the large potted plant to the righ tof the right bench.  Also it's a little chilly outside since they don't get sun midday or in the afternoons in the winter (totally not their fault, but just so you know).

A nice bonus is that parking on Sundays since there aren't as many folks on the north side of campus.

Overall a great place to hang out, grab some coffee, and wait for Doe library to open up at 1pm.

One of my favorite cafes in Berkeley. I had never been impressed by a cafe's chai latte until I tried theirs, which is absolutely heavenly. Their cafe au lait and espresso drinks are really good as well. I'm quite picky about my coffee but whatever they use stands out and isn't too acidic either. The ambience is nice as well, you can catch up with a friend or pop in to get some work done.
Quiet Saturday afternoon lunch with some excellent eggplant tapas and the best soy chai we've had in Berkeley.
"Their lattes restore my faith in humanity."
Great coffee here, nice home-y food.  Fast, friendly service.  A little too small inside to sit here comfortably, but good to go.  I should come here more often.

Main reason it took be longer than I expected to move to the city away from Berkeley. Great food -- try their dinner once! Amazing sandwiches. Nicely made drinks with Illy Espresso available on demand. And the best vanilla chai latte I've ever had. Outdoor seating completes it as a model experience for me.

Yummmmmmy Fantasia Panini: turkey, arugula, orange chutney, avocado, AND bell peppers: such a wholesome combination! ALthough i'd like a bit more chutney, it was bit too subtle.

I love that they give you a side of lentils w/zuchinni and carrots which I wasn't even aware of! And to top that off, it was ready w/in minutes of ordering- I barely sat down and got comfortable!

Reasonable price, as well....but they were out of most desserts when I went at like 5. oh AND any restaurant/cafe that takes plastic in Berkeley is already on my good list =D
My lunch provider for almost six years. Decent panini selection. Good coffee too if the place is not so packed that you need to wait for hours to get it. The lentil side dish is very good.

Good sandwiches (I recommend the roasted eggplant panini) and good portioned salads. Fresh, clean, great location. My friend recommends their coffees as well. It's a great place to meet up with a friend and sit outside.
a cute little cafe on euclid with great greek lunches and decent lunch wine selection as well.  i heard from a number of people that it's berkeley's best coffee, but i haven't tried it firsthand.

This place may be fine for other coffee (I haven't tried), but I gave it 2 stars because like many other so-called "great" coffee places around Berkeley, this one too makes its Iced Lattes using 2% or skim-milk. Maybe it got lost in translation somewhere, Latte means milk, not some 2% watered down drainage fluid which turns into 1% ditchwater when further diluted. Please for heaven's sake: at least offer the choice of making a real latte with real milk!!

I'm having huge trouble finding a good coffee place in Berkeley that makes Lattes with real milk!

My favorite coffee spot on the Northside! 
Their barista, Jose, is as nice as they come, and makes the best latte's and mocha's.

Also, I've never been disappointed by their food: pizza, polenta w/lamb,and salads, all delicious.

Really cute, small cafe with european feel. Espresso drinks are much better than anything else in the area, and not very expensive. I haven't had the chance to eat lunch there, but they serve modest proportions of what looks to be delicious, yet simple fare. One of my personal favorites on the North Side of campus.

Number one place to get coffee in the northern area off/on Berkeley's campus.  I'm a daily frequenter of this place.  Nehal N. is right, this totally is an aberration for off-campus spots.  I'd go as far to say that they're the only Euclid shop that stresses quality, no offense Brewed Awakening.

The thing I like to do in this place is sit and enjoy an espresso beverage.  I think their espresso is really good and there's something really charming about the interior.  I particularly like their mocha, which is not too heavy-handed with chocolate.  Their sandwiches are delicious!  I agree that they're slightly expensive for the size, but if you eat in the sandwich comes with lentils or greens.

I've only had a chai and one of their smoothies (don't remember what it's called, but it's made with plain yogurt, orange juice, honey, and strawberries). 

The vanilla chai was amazing. The best chai I've had - aside from the freshly brewed chai I used to have in high school when I went to my Indian friend's house for dinner. So, I'd say that's some pretty damn good chai.

On to the smoothie... It was more of a juice. But a delicious juice, I must say! 

I've never come here to study, just people watch. It's a nice place to relax if you have time between classes on north side.

This place makes good coffee and espresso, though they are overpriced. The interior has a European feel (plus), but the tables are tiny, and when every table is occupied it's a very unpleasant place to be (minus). I like their soy latte, but I'm still weighing whether it's sufficiently better than that of, say, Brewed Awakenings (down the street), to be worth paying more for a smaller amount.

Great staff and great coffee drinks.  The guys that work here really know how to steam the milk so it gets nice and thick and frothy.  Jose, the daytime barista, is really polite and friendly and will know your order after a few visits and start making your drink while you're waiting in line.  Gotta love a place that knows how to treat regulars!

This is my FAVORITE cafe in Berkeley.  
*great coffee -- illy brewed correctly served with suuper smooth milk
*great food -- their greek style yogurt is so light yet creamy and tangy but sweet.  
*mellow, hip atmosphere -- the decor makes me feel like I've left the country, the music is cooler than anything in my ipod and the rotating photo exhibits are thought-provoking and beautiful.
*When I was in college, I came here all the time to study -- and can honestly say I owe any good grades to them.
*When teaching courses, I held office hours here -- perfect place to stimulate conversation.
*Now, I live nearby and come in faar too often before work.  
*The guys behind the counter are good people who make great food and drinks.
A true gem.
Outstanding lattes and nice, quiet atmosphere good for reading/working or chatting with a friend. It's a great alternative to the always-packed Brewed Awakenings.

I don't know about you guys but I like their Greek-style yogurt. Their other food is only mediocre. I'm not entirely sure what I had but I know that I tried a few different selections in my desperate attempt to find something different to eat on Euclid.

Great coffee, real baristas, awesome food, nice service, always clean. It is a little COLD in the winter in there, I wish they would run the heater a little higher and I would go there more instead of Brewed Awakening across the street where the coffee is horrible but I wont freeze! Love cafe Nefeli on a warm summer day!

Among all Berkeley cafes, Nefeli has got to be my favorite. 

Not crowded with students chatting over computers in club meetings;
No GSI holding last minute office hours.
It's a simple place for dreary souls every morning with revitalizing espresso of decent quality. I feel like being on a tranquil Mediterranean island at Nefeli.

Price is reasonable avg. $2-3 for the caffeines.
Only down side is I wish they had a wider variety of coffee food--my favorite croissants, bagels, and scones. It'd be excellent if they even baked 'em fresh.

The panini is wonderful I heard. I must spare a lunchtime for that.

A welcome exception to my theory that all the food options on Euclid and Telegraph suck.

I've always enjoyed their sandwiches and salads, as well as their desserts the couple of times I've tried them. I'm not a coffee drinker, but given that every single person in line in front of me gets coffee (and the time they take to make it) that must be good too.

I also like how it has a European feel. No, that's not code for "dingy and pretentious" (like other Berkeley cafes), it actually has a nice, relaxed, classy feel. If you're one of the many Berkeley grad students from Europe, this may be your place.

Now I finally understand why the untamed Kurt Vonnegut reading hippie sits at same nook every time I walk by. It is a cafe that both fills your tummy with great tasting food that requires cognitive appreciation. For example, the Kosmos panini features apple creamed with goat cheese, smothered with this sauteed mushroom concoction- all sandwiched between two toasted French baguette. 

It is important how you eat there. You can simply grab a quick energy boost- I highly recommend the chocolate Frappe on a hot summer day. If you are lactose-intolerant, they also can substitute soy milk for cow milk. A decent full meal can cost around $15, but you will be nourished with the finest Greek food. 

Try the dolmas, the rice and pine nut combination is a killer. It's all cooked in some curiously tangy sauce, I craze for more after the first bite. 

If it is solitude you seek, you can go early and catch the corner in the back room. If you like people watching, there is nothing better than the outside spot, you can enjoy the meal while pondering the life of Berkeley academs. 

I live a block away. It's very tempting to go there every morning.

For a Greek cafe it is a little strange that they play international music and the people who work there speak Spanish. O well, I like how they decorated and they have tasty things for sale. The food is on the pricey side, but it's a nice spot to stop by for a snack.

This should be one of the best cafes in Berkeley.  Their coffee is above average. Their food is good by Berkeley cafe standards.  They have a large and varied menu, including wines and tapas.  The atmosphere is great...so what's the problem? 

For one thing, they seem to "run out" of items on the menu more often than should be expected, but that's not a major problem.  The coffee is sometimes not very hot.  Their selection of pastries is small, and they run out quickly.  The music can be too loud.  And there are occasional whiffs of what smells like raw sewage.

Raw sewage...WTF??  I've tried to figure out where its coming from with no luck, but it seems to be strongest right in the front doorway.  It can get bad on hot days; on others its barely noticeable.  When the door is closed the smell mostly stays outside, unless you're sitting at the table right by the window, but every time someone walks in the door there's a little blast of sewer smell.

I really want to give this place a higher rating; now that I live in the neighborhood I would probably be here almost every day, and it really saved me when I had to study before a final and nothing else in the neighborhood was open...but WTF raw sewage??!

If you're craving spanokopita, like I was, then this is the place to satisfy it. I liked the spanokopita best of the three tapas I got. The other two, stuffed eggplant with feta and a "cigar" with fennel and mushroom, were both good, but didn't quite hit the spot.

Best in Berkeley for cappuccino also the cafe food is good as well
I spent many days catching up on my reading here
I spent quite a bit of my college years in this place 
and some after as well 

Best cappuccino on the northside

A cappuccino and an Athenian will jump-start your day. (Make sure you get the lentil salad to accompany it.) Friendly service and, if you go frequently, the servers warm up to you. Intimate and tucked away, it's good for just about any occasion -- if it's sunny, grab a table outside to people-watch on Euclid!

I love Nefeli.  Their coffee is nice and rich and thick; they serve exclusively Illy espresso if you are a coffee follower.  It's not for the timid.

It was on the way to Soda Hall, so you can imagine I went here a lot.
A real illy espresso, I don't know if it's the grind, if they properly preheat the machine, or what  but they do a hell of a job

I have found a place in my heart for this cafe.  I have been going to the Brewed Awakening Cafe up the street quite regularly.  Unfortunately, they began to get my order wrong rather consistently (I blame this on the fact that they are always way too busy), so I decided to step across the street and try Nefeli Caffe, and I can definitely say that that the grass is greener on the other side.  

The atmosphere is really relaxed, and the food and drinks are good.  In the morning the cafe gets some wonderful light through the windows, which makes it a very pleasant place to drink my coffee.  Last week I had their bagel with cream cheese, cucumber, tomato, and onion, and today I had the Greek yogurt with fresh fruit, nuts, and honey.  It was all very delicious, and perfect for a quick breakfast.  I had the food just about a couple minutes after I sat down.  Lately I have been getting the house coffee, but even that is extra special, because over by all the creamer and sugar they have whole nutmegs that you can grate over your coffee.  I will definitely be coming back more often.

Great coffee.  Their espresso drinks are better than their drip coffee.  Not the best place to work because the tables are super small and rickety, and there are no outlets (literally.  I think there might be one.)  They also take credit cards (which is a huge plus in Berkeley, esp. on Euclid, where every place seems to be cash-only).  I think there's a CC minimum of $5.  The almond croissants are excellent.  Also, was surprised to see they have a great dinner menu of tapas-style food.  I am a fan of the veggie pizzetta for lunch.  And the music selection is great (jazz, random world music, etc.).  

Caveat:  I should note that my sister says that I'm pretty much a "wannabe European" and this cafe does remind me of the places I left behind in Paris from my few years there.  So keep in mind my ridiculous nostalgia/semi (but unintentional) pretentiousness when reading this.  :)

The only good coffee in all of Berkeley.  And by "coffee" I don't mean soya-mocha-latte-cino, I mean espresso.  The nicoise salad is quite good and the rest of the food is just decent but the quality of their coffee still puts it head and shoulders above every other cafe around campus.
I like the coffee there! And people there are super nice, especially Jose!

I absolutely love the decor here. The service is very friendly and the coffee is fantastic. The prices of espresso drinks and coffee are comparable to everywhere else in Berkeley (mostly cheaper for the things I order). Nothing not to like!

I went faithfully to Brewed Awakening across the street for 5 years before actually discovering Nefeli. It's a decidedly different atmosphere; for one, you don't have the hordes of people studying or pratting away on laptops. In addition, the cafe doesn't have the...approachability of Brewed Awakening. Strange words adorn the menu, which is probably why I felt intimidated for years and contented myself to furtive glances through the glass as I walked by from La Val's.

Yet I finally found the courage to go, and I'm glad I did. The illy espresso served here is superior to any other coffee product I can ever remember tasting, and the sandwiches are tasty and healthy-looking, even if they are a bit expensive at ~$6. If I had more money to blow, I think I could live happily on the food on a regular basis.

The atmosphere is decidedly different--for one, there is no wireless, and there are no available laptop outlets. Yet if your goal is to cozy up to a book by yourself, or possibly cozy up on a casual date to the person across the table from you, I'd say that Nefeli actually provides a superior venue than Brewed Awakening. The place is quiet(er) yet has an intimate feeling. Alas, as an engineering major, that wasn't my case, but it's a fun little shop that I wish I could take with me from Berkeley.

A note: there's a bathroom here, but it's hidden. You actually have to go behind the counter, through the saloon-style doors, and past the dishwashing area to your left. It was a bit intimidating at first, but you'll get used to it.

Street parking is terrible during peak times, but what else did you expect from campus?
Best latte in the Galaxy :-))... well, for sure in Berkeley.

Oh Nefeli, your greek yogurt and fruit covered in honey and walnuts is so deliciously satisfying, I can overlook the fact that the yogurt is Berkeley Farms -- no more greek than me!

Otherwise, good hot chocolate.  And the salads are pretty good, if a little heavy on the dressing.

I think they offer very good mocha (heavy chocolate and coffee taste but not overpowering with one another) and I love their sandwiches. They have very good pastries as well.. the downside is that they do not offer wifi so you can only use airbear from campus (which is pretty slow)

This is a great cafe.  Excellent coffees and teas.  Great lunches.  The daily lunch specials are outstanding.  I recently ordered lamb chops that were among the best I had in years.  How do they do such good cooking in such a seemingly under-prepared kitchen space?  

A bit pricey, but worth it.  Did I mention the cool university crowd?

I come here for lunch once in a while. Really cute place in the north neighbourhood. The panini are all resonably priced for 5.50 with a side salad, they use very fresh ingredients. I pretty much have tried all of them, they are all very tasty.. I dont drink much coffee myself, but according to alot ppl i kno, they say this place has the best coffee =) They also have interesting dishes on their daily specials, which is more expensive. In general, the quantity of the food isnt much, but the quality definitely deserves a 5 star.

Two magical times a week, I go to Nefeli. Wednesdays I go during my break in class, and Thursdays I take the long way to school to get a delicious double Illy latte. I commented on what a great espresso they make to the owner, and he said that when he was a student at Cal, he would go all the way to SF to get some Illy coffee. I'm so happy he is not condemning us to the same cruel coffee fate. 

I had the chai once, and I thought it was very good when I first sipped it, but it started to suck as it got colder. You can tell it's from a powder mix, but I kind of enjoy the artificial crapiness. It's a bit like the garbage that is Tapioca Express--blatently fake, but it's artificial yumminess. 

I have never had the food here before, but every time I am in here people are eating delicious looking food. I plan on eating here soon, though.

Cash only if your charge is under $3.00. Not sure when they close; I went here between 8:30 and 9:00 and they were closed. I was bummed.

YUM got the cosmos panini ($7) SO GOOD, came with a little pasta salad, the baguette they used for the sandwich was amazing, fast service here, got the large chai latte ($3.25, only .25 more for large!!) and it was really really tasty
seating is a bit sparse and can be a bit loud for studying, but there's a sweet spot with a sunroof that has the perfect amount of sunlight!
Excellent coffee, from the year it opened to the present day. Clean marble top tables. A great place to prove and disprove ideas.

Tips:

$3 minimum for card (Any coffee should be over $3)

--------------------------------

Nefeli is a nice cafe to sit and chat with some friends. I haven't tried any of the food yet so that's something that I still have to experience. I've had the Caffe Latte and the Nefeli Latte. (There is no difference between the two, it's just that the Nefeli Latte is bigger in size) I always get it with hazelnut flavoring which gives it a really nice aroma. These latte's are more on the milkier side for those that prefer a milkier coffee.

I've also had a couple sips of my friend's Chai Latte and it is very yummy! It has a very heavy spice flavor to it along with the chai which is what makes it special.

There are a lot of small tables at Nefeli so it shouldn't be too hard to find somewhere to sit, but  the tables are positioned pretty close to each other so it can get a bit crowded if all the tables are taken.

This is my standard coffee place on the north side. Espresso is good, as is the drip coffee most of the time. Most of their food is good, if a bit pricey -- the yogurt and fruit is great, if you feel like splurging $5+ for breakfast.

Overall, it's not super cheap, but it has good coffee and lots of options for good food -- a pretty good (if busy) place to study.

My favorite Euclid Avenue establishment. The coffee is excellent, the music they play in the background is always good, and if you close your eyes to the outside world, you'll feel like you are in Greece!

Half the menu was not available! The guy taking the order seemed high or something bc he could not remember the order nor did he wanna write it down. however, the baked polenta was amazing! the rest of the food was decent.

I've been disappointed with the coffee that last few times I visited Nefeli. I didn't want to say anything. I thought, maybe someone was having a bad day, maybe the barista was new, maybe it was the way I asked for the coffee but the cappuccinos I so looked forward to have been a disappointment. They tasted a little burnt and the foam was dense and white with tiny bubbles. The milk, while fine, did not taste as fresh. I've walked past this coffee shop without going in, something I didn't think I would do until now.

So far I have only had the Tombo Tuna Salad from Nefeli, but it was very close to a religious experience--on top of the freshly shredded tuna (onions were involved too), it came on a bed of arugula tossed with olice oil, three slices of tomato, and three small slices of baguette. It was the perfect lunch, and didn't leave me feeling heavy afterward whatsoever. It was a bit pricey for my receptionist's salary ($7.75)--but it was worth it.

Their mochas are fantastic.  I like their panini with goat cheese and salami, but sometimes the bread is a bit too crusty.

This is a great place to have a meetings for club officers or get together with friends to catch up.
Good coffee, but the food is typical, bad cafe food.

Decent Lunch food, relaxing atmosphere, and helpful service.  The place is very much a cafe, not a full service place.  The place is unique and well put together, I felt very at home when I was there.  Highly recommended for lunch, their salads are good and nice portioned.

The coffee drinks are well-prepared, the salads and Greek tapas and desserts and sandwiches are very tasty, and even getting a glass of house wine and hanging out is worth it. It is a relaxing cafe to spend an hour reading or chatting with a friend.

The cafe is almost almost a 5-star, but there are two problems, which may either be major or minor for you. First off, an occasional mysterious smell of rotting wood may waft by while you are savoring your perfectly prepared Illy's cap. If you have ever lived near a paper processing plant, you know exactly what kind of scent I'm talking about. 

Second of all, your reverie may be broken by a self-important conversation expressly held at a volume loud enough for neighboring tables to hear. If you have ever lived near a university or in Los Angeles, you know exactly what kind of conversation I'm talking about.

Met up for a coffee date and picked this place because... well primarily because I'm a pretentious foreigner who has to go through the "special" line every time I go to the airport. I feel at home amongst my fellow Axis of Evil citizens, dammit! 

The place has a nice homey feel with a fun, mellow atmosphere that is hip without feeling forced, the coffee is excellent and the food is delicious. Great place for a quick cup or a coffee/lunch date. Cool enough to impress, casual enough to make it look effortless. In other words, much like just happening to forget to shave for a day or so before meeting someone, it falls into the "Oops I didn't realize I was sexy" category.

Solid spot. I chomped on the Athenian Panini - roasted eggplant, red peppers, feta, braised onions, olives on slight toasted panini bread. It came with a mixed green salad. I inhaled it. It was on point. Simple, tasty and pretty cheap...$5. 

Bonus...the vibes of the place were solid. I was very calm and focused (w/ quiet intensity) during my stay. I was able to clean up my resume with ruthless efficiency (time and quality). Peep the energy.
I'm totally addicted to the chai. Wow, expensive, but very very good. The atmosphere is nice and I like the diversity in selection. Tapas and sandwiches and smoothies, etc.

This is a really quite an aberration for college-area food. Its a little slow, tasty, and got a fresh cool Greek character that makes you want to stay longer than your meal!.

The coffee is a little pricey for the volume you receive, but the quality is better! The barista is friendly and can keep a conversation for a while.
I've gone frequently in the morning for their Bagel special, which is cheap and has everything you want (cheese, tomato, cucumber, onion), perfectly toasted, and generous with their veggies. I've had these often and they never fail me!

I've also had the Fantasia paninis which was Turkey, Avocado, and spinach. They use a crunchy rustic baguette, but the sandwich is small so if you're looking for a filling lunch you've got the wrong place. But it is DAMN tasty! 

Its a little pricey compared to the rest of the coffee places or even Brewed Awakening across the street. But if you want to a have a tasty bite to eat, or meet up with someone  for a quick college lunch, this place is good for Northside.

Best espresso and latte in Berkeley. Period. Miles above Strada / Roma / Milano.

Friendly staff, good service. Cosmopolitan college crowd.

No wireless (though it's covered by Cal's AirBears network.)

dolmades were flavorless and so dry that i couldnt swallow without scratching my throat. chai latte was from a mix and overly sweet. guy behind the counter was rude and strange. maybe the other food is good and other people have had better customer service, but im not other people and i did not have other food; therefore a one star review.

This place is a little expensive, but it is worth it for their soy chai lattes. At the little bar where this is sugar, milk, lids, etc. they have a plate of whole nutmegs and a little grater so you can grate fresh nutmeg into your drink. I tend to go crazy with the nutmeg grating in my drink, but i don't care because drinking my nutmeg soy chai latte makes me feel happy inside.

Came here after a whole winter break's cravings of their sandwiches. 

I've been getting lunch here since last year because it was close to the North side of campus. Always always the Kosmo sandwich (apple slices, roasted mushroom & red bell pepper on a toasted bread and walnut paste). 

The Prosciutto sandwich is also my BF's fav. 

Great for a quick lunch near campus. They also serve blue bottle coffee!

Nefeli is a cool place to hang out if you like people watching. They have a few tables outside with built-in benches into the cafe so you can take a backseat and enjoy the scene of people walking by.

Coffee is good, and I'm not a coffee person. The lady friend approves of their coffee so I'll give it a +1/2 star extra. Brownie points for serving my mocha in a big cup teehee.

We got the Alpino and Fantasia panini's:

Alpino - prosciutto, cheese, pears, spinach (I think?)
Fantasia - turkey, avocado, spinach

These sandwiches are pretty damn simple, but pretty damn tasty. I think the kicker is just the bread, as its rustic French bread. Crunchy outside and chewy inside. The portion is minimalist, so if you're hungry look somewhere else. Sides range from lentil, pasta, or green salad. It's pretty random so it's whatever they have on hand.

Prices on the higher side. $6.25/50 for paninis so it's not bad to try out one day. Definitely a good place to meet up an old friend or to have a lunch date, but not something I'd go for on a regular basis.

A 3 for now... Def returning to try the true Greek cuisine. When I went here I ordered a blargin' sandwich. What a bad decision.. The sandiwch was awkward to eat since it came in this narrow bagette (that was chewy btw). The lentils they provide on the side were good. They weren't undercooked and they were seasoned nicely. But, I need to try this place again and order something better.

For coffee, i've gotten the nefeli mocha, which was not good.

I've had one of their sandwiches too.  I don't remember what it was called, but it had cold cut turkey, peppers, and some other things, but I don't remember them all.  It was pretty tasty.  Also, the service is really fast friendly.

I ordered a mocha frappe and it was shit--one of those chalky mochas that taste like there isn't really any coffee in it. And it had the consistency of chocolate milk instead of the cold shake you want on a hot day. And it cost $5.10. I'll admit the food looks like it's probably good, but I don't take my chances again at places that have already gyped me. They're on my blacklist.

I frequent Nefeli a lot because I live two blocks away.  Today I went in to get a small coffee and a sandwich. I believe the owner was working (older guy with a ponytail). Nefeli coffees are smaller than usual, but I pay for them because they're good...until today. The owner gave me a cup that was less than 3/4 full after I told him I wanted it black and was not using cream. WTF! I barely got any coffee. I'm only annoyed since I spend so much money at this place and firmly believe I should always get what I pay for...particularly if the owner is working. And then when my to -go sandwich is ready he points at me and grunts to indicate that I need to pick it up. Usually the guys at the counter treat me well.  No more Nefeli. Going across the street from now on.

This is definitely a small place, but it wasnt too busy when we went.  Its close to the campus, so we took a nice little walk before getting there.

The food was not great, I ended up choking mine down and the girlfriend was planning on where to go afterwards because hers was bad.  The only redeeming thing to come out was the Papusa in a diavolo style sauce.  The sauce made everything a bit better, and I was able to enjoy my sandwich when dipped in it.  Not someplace I ever need to come back to.
They get 5 stars for their coffee and 2 for the food.  The cappuchino is the best you can buy around campus.  The food doesn't taste bad but it is over priced and way to small.

Fantasia and Alpino paninis both pretty good. They often have really good soup which is great when its cold and rainy in Berkeley.  I really like the lentil side salad that comes with the paninis but they dont have this everyday (and with my luck i tend to come on days when its just green salad mix on the side). The iced tea is not good here though, i think they dont make it daily so it gets kind of funky, you're better off getting tea across the street. However their espresso is really good and for the few short months I was a cappucinno drinker (coffee hurts my tummy) i did love me some nefeli caffeine.

they were supposed to be good for coffee? 
i'm not the biggest coffee fan, but i could tell the difference between good coffee and watered down coffee.. 
maybe i should try something else next time.

Worth the daily (or twice-daily) trip uphill from Dwinelle. 

Nefeli's is a gift. It's cheap, comfortable, adorable, and far away from the crotch of Bancroft-Telegraph while still being practically on campus. There always seems to be open tables when I go. I've never tried the food.
I don't get it.  This place sells mediocre, watery coffee for 50% more than any place around.  I guess if you're mainly going for ambiance then this is the place.

Came to this quiet little spot with a friend for lunch recently. Amidst Urban Turban, Bong Burger, La Val's, and all the major joints on Euclid, It's pretty easy not to notice Nefeli. I wanted to try something different, so this was a pretty decent option.

I got the only sandwich on the menu that had meat on it, which was pretty surprising. I forgot what it was called, but it had turkey and some greens, along with their standard cold pasta. I wasn't too impressed with the whole dish, but it made for a good lunch. It was fairly simple, to the point where I don't know if I would come back for something I could make myself. 

The ambiance here is great. Very nice and cozy with plenty of free water. The owner is very friendly and cracked a couple of jokes with us. Overall, a nice and quiet little place with mediocre sandwiches. If I was a coffee lover, I'm sure I would have enjoyed it more due to all the great coffee reviews it gets.

I felt like the food came with attitude and, although it was decent, I paid too much for that to be okay. My meal was close to $11 for a (*small*) greek salad and a bowl of flavorless black bean soup. Are the professors keeping this place alive? Because I certainly can't afford it too often. I'd definitely like to go back and try something else, maybe the lasagne or panini.
If you like tiramisu, you owe it to yourself to try it at Nefeli.  The staff is friendly and the espresso is good.  A nice little northside cafe.

The espressos are perfectly made with excellent beans (Illy Caffe) that are imported from Italy in vacuum cans.  I was somewhat skeptical of Illy Caffe after Mr. Espresso (the person: Carlo) told me that his coffee always wins out over Illy Caffe in the Bay Area because Mr. Espresso is fresher.  However, I was won over by R. W. Apple's October 24, 2001 profile of Andrea Illy in the NY Times ("Discovering La Dolce Vita in a Cup"), which was quite affectionate.  I appreciated Mr. Illy's comment that a good cup of espresso is made with a 25-30 second pour.  Lots of people on the Net tell you that 25 seconds is the longest pour you should tolerate, but I go to 30 seconds quite frequently.

Anyway, I come here for lunch occasionally and usually order the tombo tuna special -- the tuna and a double espresso come in at a tad less than $10.  The portions are not large; I'm still a little hungry when I walk out.

When I'm done eating, I do walk out -- I don't get up from an outdoor table.  Tommy S. thinks that he was sitting next to a plant that was recently fertilized, but I say that there's a sewer problem more or less in front of Nefeli's front door.  It has been there for years, by the way, and it's especially bad in the summer.

After Nefeli was up and running, the owner(s) opened a place called Odyssia at the location that's now Liaison.  Odyssia was problematic, but Nefeli has always been a winner.

Somebody please tell this manager: You're location is amazing!  You have fantastic food!  You're coffee keeps me up!  BUT!  All this matters not when I open my mouth to laugh in between bites and fruit flies fly into my mouth!  YUCK!  Also, if you sit outside to avoid the fruit flies, it just smells like sewage.  At least they accept cards.

100 Yelp reviews.  Finally.  I've reached this benchmark.

I didn't yelp for a while because I had to think about my 100th.  But after talking to the hubby, who told me I was overthinking it, I decided to Yelp Nefeli Caffe.  It's a simple and brilliant choice.  

Nefeli has the best coffee.  They use Illy, from Italy, and the coffee shop is exactly how you'd imagine a coffee shop should be.  Quaint, cute, decent service, and on one of the most beautiful streets in Berkeley.  Euclid Ave.  I like the expresso or the cappucino.  Both are strong, but smooth.  I also drink my coffee with a cookie or small dessert.  Salads and sandwiches are okay, but I'd come here for the coffee not the food.

Still, Nefeli gets 5 stars because it's a 5 minute walk from my house.  And the hubby and I end many of our Sunday afternoons with a cup of coffee from Nefeli.  There's nothing like a truly good cup of coffee and a good conversation to end my weekend.

One sip, and I feel like life is good (which it is).

One of the best lunch places. I always go for their specials.
