Mousakka, lamb chops, vegetable lasagna, and sausage with polanta are my favorites so far...Really tastes like home made and as a Mediterrenean I think they are very authentic. The atmosphere and music are also intriguing. Simply very enjoyable.

To do it right: $7

I stopped by Nefeli Caffe today, wanting to try something new for lunch. Upon walking in, I immediately felt comfortable in the slightly cluttered, slightly dingy interior. The very helpful guy working at the counter recommended the Alpino panini (prosciutto, pears, walnuts, fontina, and arugula on rustic bread), which I ordered.

I took a seat near the window and watched people go by for about five minutes before my sandwich was brought to my table.  It came with mixed greens drizzled with a bit of oil and vinegar, which was nice. My initial impression was that the sandwich was small, but a little prosciutto goes a long way. The sandwich was good, not great. Softer bread, less oil, and a riper pear would have improved it greatly.

Summary: Overall a pleasant lunch experience.

There are many reasons to make your visits to Nefeli more frequent. What I can tell you about is their Alpino Panini, my favorite reason to visit Nefeli.

 Prosciutto, havarti cheese, and spinach are interestingly matched with walnuts and thin slices of pear on a baguette. The result is just the right amount of salty, savory, fresh, nutty, and fruity. The predominant flavors are the prosciutto and havarti but the walnuts and pear slices liven up the panini with their own very distinct flavors. And the juiciness of the pear is an unexpected way to add some moisture while maintaining the dry textures of the meat, walnuts, and baguette. Right as you're noticing a mild thirst from the saltiness of the meat, it's quenched by a slice of pear. 

 The Alpino isn't something for twice a week, but I've always been happy when I've ordered it. It might seem strange to combine meat, cheese, nuts, and fruit but think of one those fancy party trays. The ingredients work well together while maintaining their distinct flavors, kind of like a party in your... baguette. 

 And if you're lucky, the side you're given will be lentils which I somehow only enjoy with an Alpino Panini. Their side salads are also good, which leads me to believe that you will like whatever else shows up on your plate. I always order their iced tea with my meal, which just seems right. With all the other flavors vying for my attention, a nice subdued refreshment is all I need. 

 It's important that you eat your lunch there. Otherwise you'll miss out on the possibility of lentils and the experience of a lazy meal in a cafe with some character. Next to you will certainly be students silently trying to consume their books with their eyes as well as pairs of people having some intriguing conversations you can eaves drop on. The people watching is also worthwhile as traffic to or from campus or North side is fairly consistent. No one in Nefeli appears to be counting the minutes left in their lunch break before rushing back into the world. Many are actually having an afternoon glass of wine, something I'll have to try with my next Alpino Panini. 

 Sure, you can order lots of other sandwiches and salads at Nefeli and I'm sure many of them are good. But where can you order a panini with walnuts and pear on it? While you're thinking that over, head to Nefeli and try their Alpino Panini. And give yourself time so you can nurse your iced tea, chill out, and contemplate the flavors going on in that little panini of yours.

I enjoy coming here every now and then to do some work while enjoying a yummy drink. My favorite is the Chai Latte (even though it's made from powder) and it definitely beats the chai from Brewed Awakening across the street. I've also had the Iced Nefeli Latte, but I thought it was rather standard tasting and there wasn't anything special about it. 

One of the gripes I have about Nefeli is that all the tables are super tiny. This makes sharing a table with someone virtually impossible unless you want to feel very cramped. It's okay if you're eating I guess, but if you're studying and have a laptop and or books, you'll probably want your own table. Also, once when I came here, the wifi stopped working for at least an hour which would have annoyed me since I primarily went there to work, but since I was doing some reading, I didn't mind as much. However, it's still no excuse since I feel like nowadays most coffee shops are expected to have internet for customers to use.

They have a new frappe drink that sounds really good which I'll probably try whenever the next heat wave hits.

TIP: You have to spend more than $3 to use card!

While waiting for the hubby to finish his PhD qualifying exam in the nearby Etcheverry Hall, I stopped in on this cold, windy, rainy day for some espresso.  My double latte was delicious, freshly steamed milk with the perfect amount of dense creamy foam served in a tall glass mug, for only $2.50.  I grabbed a seat by the window, overhearing faint conversations of Berkeley students and professors on the first day of classes.  Reminded me of being in college again.  It's the kind of place that's quirky, like the town in which it resides, but homey, comfortable and capable of fielding varying philosophies and life's tough questions because it knows who it is and where it stands in life.  It's nice to be good at what you do and provide the space for others to make the same discoveries of themselves.

It's a cafe, but more than a cafe 'cause not only is their coffee supersized (or "nefeli-sized), it also has the most amazing paninis. I had an Alpino panini with prosciutto, pears(!), roasted walnuts and arugula. I immediately could taste the arugula, making it kinda herby. And then as i bite in more, the pears added such interesting/sweet taste to the ham, and the walnuts added textures to the tenderness of the ham. I was so surprised of how good they come together. A must try (:! My friend had a fantasia, 'cause he thought it was the only panini with meat in it, he said it was okay, it has avacado, peppers, turkey and spinach. mmm, avacado. Going back to the coffee, i had a nefali latte, it was big and foamy, and I love how they make it so quickly and in front of you! It's a bit quieter than northside cafe, so if you just want to be on your own, it's a great place to be too. Definitely one of my escape location (:

My first Nefeli experience was a little disappointing because I was foolish enough to get my sandwich to go.  But now I know the secret.  If you eat there, along with your sandwich you get a delicious warm lentil salad.  Lentils rock my world, it's as simple as that.  And anywhere I can get a delicious eggplant sandwich with feta AND a lentil salad?  That's golden.
Hand's down the best espresso in Berkeley.  I challenge you to find better!  If you do drop me a line.

Best chai latte ever! It's made from powder, but still so goooood! Go for the large, since it's only 25cents more, $3.25 total. Sometimes the guy is nice and charges you the same price as a small anyways! :D Definitely get it hot, as it's kind of watery iced.

fantasia. $7.07

Only a sliver of avocado. Couldn't find the Orange chutney.Good strong taste of roasted red bell pepper, though it only had a super thin slice of it. Served with lentils I believe.

Overall slightly sweet flavor bc of bell peppers, making for a pretty refreshing sandwich. Turkey wasn't salty or dry which is awesome. 

The bread width and size is about the same as a Costco hot dog bun.  

Literally came out 1 min after I ordered, so that was exciting.

If you are looking for a good cup of coffee, or an amazing shot of espresso, this is the place to go on the North side of campus.  Sure, Brewed awakenings has ample studying space, and Humming Bird has cheaper prices, but Nefeli's has the quality.  Definitely the best in the neighborhood.

Food: 
Blue Cheese, Pear, Pecan salad: Pretty fresh ingredients but a little heavy on the dressing. I liked how all the ingredients came together and the presentation of the dish was very nice! But overall, it's not a super spectacular salad, just average. 

Ambiance: 
VERY SMALL and cramped inside. When you sit at the table, you could probably elbow the person on the next table if you get too excited during a conversation and start using too many arm gestures. But it gives a very intellectual, "I'm a college student" type of feel inside. Seems like a nice place to just enjoy a cup of coffee with a friend for a LONG, lazy afternoon chat. 

Service: 
Very friendly cashier with friendly staff 

Price: 
Reasonable for north side and the quality. 

Overall: 
I don't know if I could come again to dine here because this is not my cup of tea, but I would perhaps come here for a cup of coffee.

i have recently been having a macchiato or cappuccino here almost everyday after lunch. historically, i'm not a big coffee guy so i'm learning from my colleague, stephan g. 

now, stephan is a busy guy as he has a young family, is about to return to dresden to start a lab, and is trying figure out how to publish a paper before he leaves, but if he had time to yelp, he'd tell you that nefeli's is probably the most consistently good coffee near the berkeley campus. actually, here is what he did say:

"usually i drink espresso there, with the occasional macchiato at times. for fifty cents extra, money well spent, you get a sweet, balanced and round illy. it has a hint of roastiness and a subtle, shifting bouquet of flowers, fresh leather, spice and apricot that deepen toward chocolate in the cup."

wow.

the employees are generally friendly, but a note of warning: don't try to impress them with jokes about how women order lattes more than men...it won't work.

I should come here more often, except, you know, money. The panini here are the best sandwiches on Northside, quality bread and fresh deli meats. Sixish dollars a panino is only a little high for the area, but I keep thinking about better sandwiches I've had in Oakland for two bucks and change (not to mention the ones I make myself when I manage to wake up an hour before classes, which is never). On the other hand, some months ago I had a fennel salad here that I thought cost way too much, but the fact that I still remember that salad suggests it might've been worth it.

Summary: Good place for your prof to take you to.

Do they put crack in their Chai Latte? Cause I think they do... I was giddy and couldn't stop smiling until I finished my drink.
I swear, if I lived in Berkeley or went to Cal, I'd have one every day, then end up broke living in People's Park. 

CAUTION--One small downer though: they use scoops of powdered Chai mix, then simply dump in the steamed milk. If you want the real Chai stuff, go somewhere else. That said, it was delicious but kind of pricey for a powdered drink mix.

5 stars for their tasty drink, but no stars for the art of making true Chai Latte. I'll definitely come back for some more crack-infused Chai Latte, but if you want a true homemade Chai Latte with real tea leaves, skip Nefeli.

Believe me, Nefeli is but a shadow of its former self: it used to be at least 5 times better.  My feelings toward Nefeli now are like those toward an ex-lover.  This is where I met many of my friends; three of whom worked here; we knew the owners; I can't recall the countless hours my buddies and I spent here studying, hanging out, reading the paper, cracking jokes, talking nonsense while ordering the 2nd, 3rd, 4th cappaccino.  It was the default location to meet.  We ended up calling it "the office".  

Alas, rumors had it that, about four years ago, the partners that owned the cafe had a little falling out.  Then my two favorite people working there left.  After that, I noticed that the business has not been well maintained.  The coffee quality has degraded and prices gone up.  Two large bins of trash outside keep sitting there and smelling bad.  :-(

Nefeli, I really hope you would return to your former glory.  I want to come back.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Trekked here for lunch with a friend, who was skeptical because he couldn't find a menu for this place. But the popularity of this place convinced him to stay, and I'm glad we did!

Stood in line for 3 minutes before placing our orders. They take credit, which is fantastic. If you order solid food, they give you a napkin and fork. You're welcome to sit at any of the small tables they have--most looked like they seated duos, some quads, and for the small amount of space they have in the front area and the cozy back nook, they maximize their layout fairly well. They have water in a large container near the display case with all the tantalizing pastries, which you can refill at your own leisure.

We both ordered a panini, which quite literally arrived a minute after we sat down. This service was faster than fast food!

|| F O O D ||

ATHENIAN PANINI: roasted eggplant, roasted red peppers, feta cheese, braised onions, kalamata olive spread, and parsley [$6.50]
- I mainly tasted the olives and feta cheese. I somehow glanced over the olives in the description of the sandwich, as I'm not particularly fond of olives...and I just can't place what I don't like about them... Anyway, the main reason why I ordered this panini was because of the eggplant! I love eggplant! But perhaps I'm used to stir-fried eggplant, as I felt the subtleness of the eggplant was dominated by the pungent taste of the olives and cheese. I still enjoyed the panini, but I would have enjoyed it more with some soy sauce and no olives. :c jk about the soy sauce...maybe.
- Each panini comes with a serving a cold pasta; it's nothing fancy, but it's a good complement to the hot, chewy baguette.

KOSMOS PANINI: grilled mushrooms, roasted red peppers, almond/walnut spread, thinly sliced green apple, and goat cheese [$6.50]
- My friend said his mainly tasted like apples and mushrooms, which seem to be the dominant players in this sandwich. There were a lot of mushrooms! And 4 slices of apples :P

|| C L O S U R E ||

I enjoyed my meal, the atmosphere, and the price. I'm coming back to try the Kosmos!

my sandwich was ready by the time i finished paying. 

WTF?!

this scared me a bit at first (is the food pre-prepared?), but i forgave them when i realized how deliciously simple the sandwich was.

Absolutely without a doubt the best espresso in Berkeley. The cappuccino is practically perfect in every way and the sandwiches (I'm partial to the eggplant) come with a delightful lentil salad if you eat at the cafe. The food is a bit on the expensive side, but enough for a meal that is delicious and satisfying. They are open until 9pm and offer a nice assortment of wines, desserts and appetizers in addition to the coffee and sandwiches.

The people are nice and it really is the anchor of all the Euclid establishments. It is always crowded at lunchtime, but when you can find a table inside or out, it's almost as if you've been transported outside of berkeley to a small european bistro where the coffee is strong and the dolmas provide a perfect flavor contrast. Just bring a good book and you'll be set for a lazy afternoon of people-watching (and Euclid is the perfect place for that sort of activity).

Love Nefeli. Love that it's a block away from my house and love that it takes cards (which, I've discovered, is a major accomplishment for many small establishments in berkeley). I dislike their lack of free wi-fi and lack of outlets within the shop (minus 1 star)

I've lived around the corner from Nefeli for almost a decade and it's consistently been the best cafe I know of in Berkeley.  I've been to Royal, I've been to French Hotel, and I've done my time at Brewed Awakening - none of them are as good.

Why?  Well, pull up a chair and I'll give you three good reasons to go.

First of all, they use illy coffee, which is one of my favorite commercial brands, and they bang it out FAST.  I pull in there on the way to work and they're usually asking me for money with the drink done before I'm done rolling a smoke.  That means under a minute.  Their fixin's are raw sugar, nutmeg w/ grater (fresh nutmeg powder!), non-fat and low-fat milk, and cinnamon.  I don't think these things are ever not available or empty, and I've been there thousands of times.

Second, they have fresh-squeezed orange juice.  That may not sound like a big deal, but I challenge anyone to show me a place that consistently delivers a top-grade glass of OJ like theirs.  Get it once and you'll remember why OJ is f'in delicious.  I get a small and down it at the counter before I head out with my coffee to go - that's how good it is.

Third, all the food they serve there is made fresh, from excellent produce, and is delicious.  I appreciate places that pay attention to their entire selection and Nefeli doesn't disappoint.  The sandwiches, the hot plates, and the often-mentioned yogurt-fruit bowl are all teh yums.  My only disappointment is that they're all a bit too European-style, which is to say small.

So there you have it.  Why didn't I give it 5-stars, you ask?  Good god you're an inquisitive sort!  I took off one star for the relatively expensive prices - it ain't cheap - and the occasional lapse in service.  Sometimes the "Euro" atmosphere means that the server's phone call or casual discussion with someone takes precedence over getting your order.  Not often, but irritating when it happens.

Avoid the double armpits of La Burrita and La Val's and head here for the best food on Northside. It's basically a little coffeehouse with a painted blue sky ceiling, but their salad and sandwich offerings are quite good. I like their caesar in particular. Nefeli has a very relaxed and European feel, like you might want to linger over a coffee here in the afternoon while you read a book.

Best expresso in Berkeley!  I know a few people that won't go anywhere else - its either Nefeli or they make it at home/in their office.  I am not quite so picky about coffee but I must admit they make superior coffee.

Nefeli is, clear and simple, the cultural stronghold of the Euclid Strip.

Of course, the Euclid strip is no Gourmet Ghetto or Elmwood.  You probably don't even know what I'm talking about if you don't live a UC-centered life.  But I would at least compare Nefeli's status to that of a national hero in some lame island country.

When somebody says they like Northside, it means they like Nefeli.  And that's why I rate them so highly - not necessarily because of the food and drinks they serve, but because they fathered a microculture.
For the price of a cup of coffee, you get to experience a region.  

You know when you go to Mexico, and sit somewhere at a counter and order a taco, and you look around and everyone has straw hats on, and there's a jukebox playing mariachi music, and then you hear the whack of a meat cleaver, and suddenly there's a paper plate buried in cilantro in front of you and a really skinny dog sniffing at your feet?  You take one bite of that taco and think, "Man, I am SO in Mexico right now."  It isn't really possible for that taco not to taste good.  It simply tastes like the experience you're having.

So that's how it is with Nefeli.  You could get stuff to go there, but why would you?  You can't pass up grating your own nutmeg (seriously, with a cheese grater) into your polka-dotted mug of coffee while sitting at a marble pedestal table and listening to Manu Chao.  Throw in some tapas served in a cazuela (a cylindrical clay dish) and you've got a genuine North Berkeley stamp on your passport.

When you finally get sick of the semi-grimy south side and it's high school kids trying to be school/ hobo esqueness head to the North Side for some quality campus side digs. I just started going to Nefeli this year and don't know why it took me so long. 

The Illy coffee is superb, and the food is good for a cafe but the service is hit or miss. The 1st time I was there I ordered the tortilla espanola (a tick slice of Spanish omelet with patatas and herbs) and the guy behind the counter pointed out the time (it was 1pm) and the prominent "TAPAS ONLY AFTER 4PM" sign. Didn't I feel sheepish. Then he leaned in and whispered "But for you, anything. Just don't tell anyone". 

Gush

And the omelet was wonderful, like one you'd actually taste on La Ramblas or something. Which is kind of silly since it's a Greek restaurant. Good enough to skip class and sit on one of their outside tables for hours.

But once, I waited at the unmanned counter for about 5 minutes just to take my order because the server (different person) was on the phone. OK, I'll let it slide, you guys hooked me up last time. 

Go Now! While the weather is beautiful. Life is at it's best on a breezy summer day sipping coffee while random strangers make conversation with you on the sidewalk next to the Nefeli Cafe.

This place is tiny. I would probably only bring one other person here if I were to bring anyone here. That said, I've only been here by myself. I've tried to do light reading here before, but to no success. It's too dim inside and it's too distracting outside. Yes, there are little small tables inside and little metal tables outside. I've only had the drinks here and they're pretty good, but I have yet to try the food. I hear the Greek items are recommended.

I spent half my law school career studying in Cafe Nefeli's back room with the bright blue ceiling dreaming about everything but the contracts textbook in front of me.  Amazing espresso, the best affogatos this side of  Europe, yummy sandwiches and a constant cast of characters that made even the dullest study sessions palatable.

First pineapple on pizza and now pears on my pannini.  

The world is going C-R-A-Z-Y!!!!!

Damn . . . I liked it.

Curses you Italian good food makers!

The best part was sitting outside on a sunny Friday afternoon just watching people/students/slackers scurry down the sidewalk like little ants, while my lazy butt was thinking, "Yeah, I am a pastor . . . and this is part of my job!"  

Life is good my friends, life is good.

The smell that this place gives off is ultimately enticing. I can never resist unless I'm broke (which is most of the time, unfortunately). The best part of this place is the cilantro sauce which you find with your plate and/or sandwich, and the mango smoothies.

Highly recommended. Try the mango smoothie and tri-tip sandwich/plate. You won't regret it.

It almost tastes like Korean barbecue. That's probably why it's soo good.

I went to the Brazil Cafe Truck today because I was feeling anemic and wanted red meat. I got the tri-tip rice bowl because they are famous for their tri-tip (or it seemed so anyways). It was $6.99+ tax. Came out to $7.68 and the food came out fast enough. I was disappointed by the size because it did come out to almost $8 but beef is sold at a premium in Berkeley.

Tri-tip rice bowl comes with rice, tri-tip pieces (not a heaping amount, but enough that when you mix it all together, you can see the pieces all mixed in a homogenous sort of way), ricotta cheese, and their cilantro garlic sauce. Also comes with two small slices of french bread smushed inside.

All in all, filling for me, but I'm a small girl.

I've been at Cal for 3 years and have always heard great things about Brazil Cafe. But wait - has this truck always been there? Didn't it use to sell hotdogs? 

I was walking down Sproul yesterday, stomach a-rumbling, when I saw the food truck and decided to give their famous tri-tip sandwich a try. I got mine with ricotta cheese and jalepeno (I was going to get Pedro's World Famous Tri-tip sandwich but didn't want olives, tomatoes and pineapple in there so there was no point). It came to a little over $8 so it was a pretty expensive sandwich, but it was decently sized and really good. The meat was okay, but it's the cilantro spread that makes the sandwich. Everyone in line ahead of me ordered the mango smoothie, which came in a puny cup. 

Will definitely stop by from time to time to grab a quick bite for lunch since it's so conveniently located!

The food truck craze has spread!  For fans of Brazil Fresh Squeeze Cafe and its sister shack, now you can order their menu along with Desi dogs at their new food truck. It seems like a collaboration or takeover of the Desi Dog truck. I was walking on Telegraph and couldn't miss the giant Jesus picture that replaced the sexy fiery Desi lady (I kinda miss her...).

The owner handed out tri tip samples and I ordered my usual tri tip sandwich for $6.99. Most folks in line ordered their mango smoothie and a sandwich and others got a Desi dog.  The tri tip comes with an addictive cilantro spread and grilled onions. It reminds me of Vietnamese shaking beef, which is comfort food for me. Sandwich portions are big, smoothie portion is small and wait is longer than the old Desi truck, but they'll get faster.

Most amazing sandwiches. Got the Obama fav with pork & pineapple and it left nothing to be desired.  BOMB!!!

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED - this is on my top 10 Sandwich List!

I gave this place three chances.  The first one, I got a vegetarian sandwich (I think the menu name is "carnaval").  It was tasty.  BUT...it was the soggiest sandwich I have ever eaten. Sandwiches should not be so soggy that you need to eat them with a fork!  The second chance, I ordered a veggie dog, but as they ran out, they offered me a sandwich and told me I would not need to pay the difference.  This was the same veggie sandwich I had tried before.  Since it tasted good, and I was in a hurry, I accepted, and just expected to have to eat it with a fork.  This second time, the taste seemed off--like something was missing.  And yes, the sandwich was soggy again.  At that point, I decided to not ever order that again.  I then went back a third time yesterday, wanting to give them a more than fair chance.  This time I got the veggie dog as they actually had them.  I eat meat, but I had enjoyed the desi dog veggie dogs, and since I had been told that the dogs were the same as before, I gave it a shot.  It was the most disappointing meal ever.  The bread was stale.  And overall, the veggie dog was so dry.  The onions and peppers they added to it did not taste like the ones that used to come with the desi dog veggie dog (I think he used to put serrano peppers before, and these tasted like plain bell peppers).  And on top of the grilled onions and peppers, they stuffed a bunch of raw corn and carrots.  No condiments were available, as there used to be when it was just a desi dog truck.  And I could not finish it because it was just way too dry.  If they would bring back the condiment table, complete with the pico de gallo, that the desi dog truck always had, it would have been edible.  And so, I just cannot recommend eating here.  When the sandwiches are so soggy that the bread is completely wet and falling apart, and a simple veggie dog is dry, dry, dry, and served in such a stale piece of bread, well, I cannot reason every going back nor ever recommending this place to anyone.  I give them two stars because the first veggie sandwich I had at least tasted good, even though the bread was soaked through. Oh, and if you ask me, this truck is just way too overpriced for the quality of food you get.

Not sure if the other locations are better, but my first experience here did not live up to the hype...

The Pedro - it's a great concept, and a good sandwich, but nothing to write home about.  Reminds me of the philly steak wars and who uses the better beef.  The tri-tip was not as tender as my sample (some pieces were quite chewy!) and meat flavor seemed bland.  The combination of pineapple, olives, and sauces added great flavor, but was so drenched that there was literally ounces of liquid in my tray... not the easiest-to-eat street food.  And it's $8?  With tax and a drink, you're easily over $10-11.

Service was fast and friendly, yet I doubt I will be returning anytime soon.  I wasn't wowed by the tri-tip, nor impressed with the mess it made, and can easily find better places to spend $10 for lunch.
Loved this food truck soooo much, but where did it go? It hasn't been on Sproul for a long time...
great addition!!! I would recommend Pedro's favorite the works. The little chicken croquettes are awesome too.
The food here is very tasty! I love the freshly baked bread and super cheap mango drink. The meat is perfectly seasoned and overall it's pretty cheap. As a college student, this is wonderful!

Brazil Cafe's Food Truck is an institution at Berkeley.  When I was in school, they were located on University.  I guess they got so big that they moved right on to campus at Sather Gates.  

They are known for their tri-tip sandwich.  Pedro walks around giving out samples of tri-tip with the green sauce to lure customers in.  Once you have a nibble, it's hard to get away because the meat is that good.  I really enjoyed the toasty bread with all the condiments and heaping mounds of meat.  It's a messy sandwich so be prepared for that.  For $7, you get a very satisfying meal.

My friend asked for a special order to make a tri-tip sandwich.  Omg...that was so much better.  Probably the best salad I've ever had in my life.  It was that good.  It's pretty much everything in the sandwich but without the bread.  

You must try Brazil Cafe if you are in Berkeley.  I miss Berkeley's cheap, good eats.

... is this real life? Did one of my favorite Berkeley eateries set up camp on campus?!

I was ecstatic to see Brazil Cafe's truck sitting on Bancroft and Telegraph on the first day of class. A little skeptical at first, I walked to look at the menu, only to be greeted by a familiar menu filled with Brazil Cafe favorites, like Pedro's Favorite, and of course, the mango smoothies.

The line is never that long here, which is awesome, and the staff is still as friendly as ever. They honor the UC Berkeley "Press Pass" discount cards so you can still get your FREE MANGO SMOOTHIE!

The quality of the food hasn't gone down, so now I can happily get my tri-tip sandwich fix whenever without having to trek all the way to University.

... although I wish they had the wish bracelets at the UC Berkeley truck :(

Perhaps one of the best sandwiches (Get Pedro's Favorite!) I've ever had, and definitely the best from a stand. Not super cheap for the size, but delicious bang for your buck. 

Mango Smoothie isn't that great, but sometimes they'll give it to you for free if you're ordering around when they're closing up their stand :)

This is a special thing. Everyone loves Brazil Cafe and the unusually close Brazil Fresh Squeeze Cafe, but finally they opened a more practical location right at the foot of Berkeley campus. I believe they bought out the pretty solid DesiDog hot dog stand. But pretty much same as the old Brazil Fresh Squeeze Cafe.

Get a little sample of tri-tip. Just for fun. And then get a Tri-Tip Bowl, Sandwich, or Plate. I recommend the plate and then grub on that with some hot sauce and whatever sauce they got. And get a Mango smoothie if you have that coupon.

Then get this little ribbon band that is apparently impenetrable and grants three wishes you make after tying three magically impenetrable knots. Fun stuff I suppose.

Good job Fresh Squeeze on opening a stand at a prime location. An excellent choice indeed. See you there!

I really enjoyed the sample of meat that I was being handed out along the sidewalk. The meat in my tri-tip sandwich was fatty fatty fatty. The cilantro garlic sauce that coated the meat was the only enjoyable part of my sandwich. 

Overall, I would come back and give this place another try.

I love this place.  Outside on a nice day eating some of Pedro's Favorite....They have excellent mango smoothies that go well with the food.  From the plates to the sandwiches you got to give it a shot.  Oh and the owners are super nice and friendly.

I don't know if they just run out of things quickly or if they are just falsely advertising. They said something about not having any plates or bowls...

I originally wanted a tri tip rice bowl (one of their daily specials) but they did not have it so I ordered the tri tip sandwich instead. CBS said it was the "best tri tip sandwich" so it must be good right? WRONG. The sandwich I got was mediocre at best. The sandwich came in one of those paper baskets for fries and cost me $7.49. The bread was mushy and wet because it was slathered in the garlic cilantro sauce (which was pretty salty) and dripping with sauce from the tri tip (also very salty). Usually when people are looking for a sandwich they expect the bread to be toasty or crunchy... For vegetables on my sandwich I got one small lettuce leaf, a handful of wet, soggy onions (definitely not fresh...), and a slice of tomato. If there had been more fresh vegetables, the sandwich would not have been so repulsively salty. Overall the sandwich that I got lacked balance in both textures and taste. 

The only reason I haven't rated this as 1 star is because I only tried one thing. However if this is the best they've got I'm unwilling to try anything else on their menu.

I haven't written a review for a while, but I came back just to write this review. Let me clear the air first and say that I love Brazil Cafe. I always get the tri-tip plate because it has the most bang for the buck in my opinion, but the truck does NOT have this option.

I went during a short class break and I was in a rush to decide what I wanted as my first meal of the day when I spotted the Desi Dog truck transformed into a blue mass that is now Brazil Cafe. Pedro was there handing out samples of the meat to passerbys and that was my cue. The sample meat tasted great so I got Pedro's Favorite which is the sandwich.

First time I ever got the sandwich, but it fit on a tiny tray that a hot dog would snugly fit in and they got it all wrong. No pineapples. No jalapenos. So when I went back and asked them to add those things, they did it immediately but when I took that first bite that I so longed for, there were olives in there instead of jalapenos. Didn't expect that. I also didn't expect my meat to be bleeding onto the bread. This was not what the sample tasted like.

I was already late for my return to class because I had felt the extra 7 minutes I waited would be worth it. They weren't. To top it off, this tiny sandwich was over 8 dollars. I legitimately miss Desi Dog and the sexy hot dog that used to be on the side. Pedro, you're cool but I'm going to stick to the stand on University.

Brazil Cafe offers many kinds of sammies and dogs.  same  dogs were  previously known as "desi dogs". brazil cafe is located not too far from sather gate.

eats: brazil dog (5.50+ tax)
-polish dog with lots of corn nibbets, tomato bits, olives, red onions, cilantro, and  crispy shoestring potato.
-hoagie bun fell apart from the moisture of the veggies.
-dog had a sweet, fatty taste like cheap a cheap dog. miller's?
-pricey for nonpedigreed bite..  top dog and district dog a better and tastier deal.                                   2.5 stars not good value.

dog bits:
-tri tip a better choice? also pricey.
-got a number though i was only one at window
-service ok.. dog not.

Desi Dog + Brazil Cafe = Desi Dog by Brazil Cafe

This food truck serves the same overpriced (in my opinion) hot dogs from before offered by Desi Dog, in addition to the few favorites from Brazil Cafe.

dogs ($4-6):
american dog, brazilian dog, polish dog, veggie dog, hot links spicy dog, chili cheese monster dog, breakfast dog

fries ($4-5):
regular, garlic, cheese, chili

The tri-tip sandwich is $7 and the Pedro's favorite tri-tip sandwich is $8.

There's also a ton of toppings all around 50 cents. There are also a couple of appetizers, fried bananas and chicken croquettes. I wouldn't come here without a coupon for a free mango smoothie too. At prices like these, I almost expect it. The service though, is outstanding. Pedro is sure dedicated to his business and is often found at the many Brazil Cafe outposts that now exist.

I'M SO GLAD THERE'S A BRAZIL CAFE FOOD TRUCK ON BANCROFT AND TELEGRAPH NOW! Such a smart location. Makes it so much easier to eat some delicious tri-tip sandwiches with friends after class on Sproul steps or the grass nearby the truck!

I have to admit though... I ordered my fav Brazil Cafe sandwich (tri-tip sandwich with the works) today (for $7.99), and it didn't taste as good as the one from the Brazil Cafe on University. I got less meat, onions, jalapenos, etc. in my sandwich so it was flatter than usual... Maybe today was just an off day. Usually they are filled with tri-tip pieces covered in some delicious green sauce. Sandwiches are juicy and aaaaaammmaaaaazzzziiiiiinnnnngggg!!!!!! 

It also makes me smile when I see the guy that owns it!! (The guy whose picture is on the truck). He's soooo nice and friendly!! And he gives you samples and coupons for their amazing mango smoothie!!

BTW, unlike the Brazil Cafe on University, this one is CASH ONLY.

This place just sold me the worst sandwich I've ever experienced (which is an impressive feat).  Maybe it's just me, but I don't like tuna - laced with mustard, mayonnaise and sweet pickles - that's so soggy it won't stay in the sandwich.  Neither do I like stale bread.  

Maybe their other sandwiches are better, maybe it was a bad day, but if you like tuna, do not chance getting a sandwich here.

I'm giving two stars instead of one because the factory-packaged bag of chips I also bought was pretty good.  I am never going to buy any sandwich at this shop again.  Candy bars, sure.

My sandwich here was one of the worst food items which I have ever paid for at a restaurant. I ordered a chicken panini and all it was was chicken dripping in mayonnaise served between two limp slices of white bread. It was not grilled so it did not resemble a panini in the slightest. It was overall AWFUL and I would never eat her again.

Very basic mom and pop establishment. Small menu, vague pricing, average tasting food, and takes a while to get the food out because when we went in the morning for breakfast there was only one guy act as a cashier and as cook. He got pretty overwhelmed handling the customer orders and making our croissants in the kitchen. When we finally got our food I found hair in my ham and cheese... sigh..

Came here on a Saturday afternoon to drink some tea and do some reading. What a great place. The owners were really nice. I was the only person, so they changed the radio station to my liking. It does have several fridges with soft drinks and one with icecream which screws up the decor, but...
there's wifi, wall plugs, a large menu of hot & cold sandwiches, hot & cold drinks, and both indoor and outdoor tables + a couch.

I needed a chocolate milkshake.  
Instead, my $3.50 bought a cup of milk blended with small ice shards and only the palest of chocolate coloring. It definitely didn't taste chocolatey, and it definitely didn't taste like a milkshake.

Ugh. Don't know what to really say about this place other than DON'T GO!

Ordered a sandwich and the lettuce tasted stale. Like, more than several days old stale. YECH!

Only thing going for them is that they're somewhat cheap. But they're not even the cheapest option around. So it's not at all worth it, given the wealth of options available for lunch in Berkeley.

This place is amazing and sustainable! They often do not have a menu online because everything is so fresh! They even will give you an actual fork instead of plastic because they don't want to waste plastic. What a wonderful place! You must check this place out, located in Preservation Park! What a treat!

The Honest Truth: Small sandwiches, more bread than meat, bread is dry, price is decent ($6)

The Details: I needed a quick bite to eat before heading to class and I decided to stop here since it was on the way.  I got my sandwich and headed off to class.  When I decided to eat it, I was a little disappointed.  There were only 3 flat slices of pastrami and the bread was pretty thick.  The bread was also pretty dry, so the combination didn't make it very good.  The price was decent (6 dollars including tax), but if you're near shattuck, there are a number of places that would give you better sandwiches... Sorry Cafe Rio!
Wants to charge me 50 cents to buy a $1 candy. WTF.

I agree with reviewer Anton W. I wish I had read his post before going here-- I ordered a chicken panini as well, which is not a panini, but a piece of tasteless chicken microwaved with nasty (and yet also tasteless) cheese on two insipid slices of bread. Simply gross. I am still dry-heaving.

Spend your $5 anywhere else you can.

Ugh.  This space was a really cute organic cafe (Soy?) for about 3 weeks during the summer of 2009.  The food was really good & the owner very nice.  But the cafe went out of business very quickly (without the student traffic to support it?) and the people who own the convenience store next door expanded their store to this space and called it Cafe Rio.  As far as I can tell, they basically just moved a few soda coolers over and their espresso machine, and kept the design of the original cafe (which was very nice & elegant).  The chip racks & soda coolers seem so out of place in there.

I haven't patronized the convenience store often because the "fresh" food they sell has been moldy quite a few times (like the bagels & muffins), the espresso drinks are burnt tasting, & one of the owners once gave me the wrong amount of change after I gave her a $20 and then continued to insist that she was correct, even after I tried to correct her.  Basically, it's good for junk food, gum & cigarettes.

So great, they expanded their store, and now have twice the space to sell junk food.  Nice work, landlord.  Compared to the variety of other fresh, delicious food on that block, this is sad waste of space.

Cafe Rio has espresso and sandwiches and bagels, and a few tables to sit at, but it's more like an AM/PM than a "cafe"-- full of refrigerated drinks, an ATM machine, racks of candy and chips.  The coffee isn't very good and the place seems a little dirty... but I keep coming back for the muffins, which you can find nowhere else!  When I asked the owners (a very sweet couple) where these muffins come from, the man blushed and said, "my brother makes them."  I strongly suggest the Carrot Raisin Muffin.  I can't figure out what the ingredients are, but they are so harmonious and delicious!

I ordered a breakfast sandwich here -- menu listed a price of $3.25 and they tried to charge me $5.75... what the hell? I find it kind of hard to believe that was a mistake. If you get overcharged here, definitely speak up. That's not ok.

Reading the reviews and seeing how completely empty this place was, I feel a little bad for the couple running Cafe Rio. They probably aren't making enough money, but it's still not ok to overcharge! If you want it to cost $5.75 fair enough, but put that price on the menu and don't try to tell me the difference is "tax."

The sandwich itself was fine. Pretty standard cheap breakfast fare.

Dropped by Cafe Rio for a bite of breakfast on my way to Berkeley; it's a small little mom-and-pop store that has a convenience store feel to it. They seem to offer a wide range of selections, and I got a "breakfast mit" (a.k.a. bagel) with egg, spinach, and mushroom. It came out piping hot, and had a decent amount of mushroom and spinach; service was friendly too (they bring the food out to you). However, the listed price was $3.25 (not including tax), and I somehow got charged $4.45 for the sandwich... reading some of the earlier reviews on Yelp, looks like that's a theme. I'd like to believe that this overcharging isn't intentional, but there seems to be a pattern here. Oh well, that's what I get for not reading the Yelp reviews first. Food is good, and you get free wifi (and plenty of spots to hang out), but definitely be cautious about what you end up getting charged.

Recently, I was in Downtown Berkeley, looking for a cafe with a hotspot so I could use the internet. To my delight, I saw a quaint cafe that was open.

I gave Cafe Rio a chance, but boy, did I regret it! While I really enjoyed the attention given to me by the cashier, the food was absolutely terrible. The sandwiches were overloaded on certain condiments that I had to scrape off. The soup was definitely canned and cold.

I would recommend any other cafe if possible! The only redeeming factor here is the customer service.

Got overcharged for an ok special of the day.

WATCH HIS CHARGES and your change

The Yelp photo here is out of date, the place is actually now next door in a renovated place that is nicer than the old one. A very pleasant older couple seem to run it - and I eat lunch there a few times a month, always ordering the same thing: lentil soup and toasted buttered bagel. It always hits the spot - I haven't ever tried anything else there. Admittedly for sandwiches, I would probably prefer to go around the corner to EZ Stop Deli, but for soups and sodas and bagels, this place is fine, and very convenient to campus - while also usually not being that crowded.

I'm kind of shocked that this place hasn't been reviewed yet.  It's right on the path that everyone takes from BART to campus.  

I've only been there once, so the four star rating is the result of optimism and one really good experience.  

My day was off to a not-so-great start.  I needed coffee and something substantial for breakfast.  A lot of places near my office don't open till 8 AM, which is when I need to be at work.  This place was on the way, so I ducked in, disoriented, hungry, and dying for coffee.  I ordered egg and cheese on a bagel and a cup of coffee.   I can't remember what I paid, but I think it was pretty cheap and the coffee came in a huge cup.  It was also delicious - strong, but not bitter.  My egg and cheese on wheat bagel was tasty and the man who made it seemed nice, friendly, and understanding of how hard it is to think when you need coffee.  

I definitely want to go back: they have lots of muffins, bagels, patries, etc.  A surprising variety of options available and you can even dine in if you so desire.  I wasn't paying attention when I went that morning but, according to Yelp, the place is also a deli.  Don't know what their lunch is like yet, but breakfast is worth trying IMO.  UPDATE: they have veg-friendly lunch options, always a plus.

This cafe is SO overpriced! For less the the cost of a water, small bag of chips, and a donut you can go 15 feet down the street and get a huge slice of pizza! Also, one time I stopped by just to buy a small bag of Chex mix, and it was $3.00!!! 

The clerk there is never friendly anyway.  Or perhaps I should be taking it personally? Perhaps he's only unfriendly toward ME? Doubtful.

Cafe Rio has espresso and sandwiches and bagels, and a few tables to sit at, but it's more like an AM/PM than a "cafe"-- full of refrigerated drinks, an ATM machine, racks of candy and chips.  The coffee isn't very good and the place seems a little dirty... but I keep coming back for the muffins, which you can find nowhere else!  When I asked the owners (a very sweet couple) where these muffins come from, the man blushed and said, "my brother makes them."  I strongly suggest the Carrot Raisin Muffin.  I can't figure out what the ingredients are, but they are so harmonious and delicious!

I can understand others' complaints but so far, I am a happy camper. Honestly, the main reasons I keep coming back are that they are conveniently placed on my way to school, really friendly people, and make me a delicious chai latte. Yeah, it is more than I want to be paying but whatevs, I would rather go here than lame-o Starbucks.

I didn't want to give Starbucks my business, and Cafe Rio was the only coffee shop closest.  I ordered a latte and have no complaints about the taste, though it was a bit expensive (but it probably is a really high rent here).  The man behind the counter was really nice, polite, and very quiet!  But he seemed really sweet.  I liked the table lay out.  My only complaint about the store itself is the refrigerators hum very loudly, kind of taking away from the experience.
Cute little mom and pop shop. Hard to find and tiny inside. But these guys are fast, quick, and nice. It's a nice cafe that specializes in many breakfast foods.

Cafe Rio.. I wish the title would stand up to it's name.

Am not saying I will never go back here but it's shame that the really sweet husband and wife haven't figured out why they aren't busier. 

Maybe the should read their Yelp reviews..{wink wink}

The place is huge and they have a variety of breakfast and lunch sandwiches  to your hearts content. Although the prices are quite high for a Mom & Pop cafe, they do have great service.
They offer free WiFi and really comfortable chairs to relax in.
And they have the most beverages I have ever seen. You name- they got it!

I ordered an egg salad sandwich. By the time I grabbed a bag of chips and decided upon a drink, my lunch was ready. That's great and all, but do I get to pick my bread or let you know which condiments am allergic too? Guess not.. I should of been more specific when I placed my order.. Not sure how I ended up spending $9.75 but I did enjoy the chair I parked my butt in as I write this Yelp review!

Cafe Rio has moved one door to the west; its address is now 2146 Center Street.

The new location is more open and generally much nicer than its old iteration, and whereas I never saw anyone sitting at the old Cafe Rio's tables, both times I've stopped by here I've seen people actually sitting down--and enjoying themselves?

So why am I knocking them down a star?  It's nothing personal, really, but $2 for a twenty-ounce soda is a ripoff.  I'm not saying I refuse to be ripped off, but I refuse to be ripped off by a five-star entity.

The drink selection at the old location was better (they had more coolers), but I get the impression they're still getting used to their new space.  The owners were also less friendly than normal both times I came, but maybe they're nervous about having spent all this money to upgrade.

UPDATE:  11/26/10
===============

I'm bumping Cafe Rio back up to five stars because they've slightly lowered their soda prices--and because everyone else has raised their soda prices.  The owners have also settled down nicely in their new digs.  Unfortunately, a new breakfast place has opened up next door in their old location, but for some reason, I have faith that Cafe Rio will survive.

Oh, and if you buy something, even just a soda, they'll let you sit at one of the tables and work on crossword puzzles until it's late enough that you're not too early for work.

All i have to say is sometimes you need a tray of 100 enchiladas delivered to your frat...
they do it with a smile!
thanks

Celia's in Berkeley has not only AMAZING food but a great catering menu as well. 

I had their food at a gathering I went to and was so pleased that their food is not only delicious at the actual restaurant but also great for parties.  The food held up great and was delicious leftovers the next day.

HIGHLY recommended for businesses, parties, basically any event.  They have tons of choices and the prices are really great.

My family and I love this restaurant so it was an obvious choice to use them for catering. Plus, when I asked my daughter (who was turning 3) what she wanted to eat for her birthday party, she exclaimed, "Enchiladas and rice!", which is her favorite dish at Celia's. The food was prepared on time, packaged well, and of course delicious. We had many guests rave about the food and ask where we got it. We had to let them in on this gem of a restaurant.

Growing up in Berkeley and living in San Diego, I have had Mexican food in every form and fashion. I consider Celia's to be second to none.
Celia's delivers on great food, reliable staff and overall VERY high quality ingredients.

Went here with a bunch of people from the East Coast, psyched to get some better burritos than the so-so fare you'll find in Boson, Philly or NYC. The guys who work here are super nice, but when the food came, my friend took one bite and said, "This tastes like an East Coast burrito." Yeah, my enchiladas tasted like the kind you buy frozen and then heat up in the oven. Not horrible, just, well...East Coast.

Finding a reliable, affordable and most importantly *DELICIOUS* caterer can be a drag - luckily Celia's is all of the above!

After calling multiple companies and speaking to many different so-called "specialist" I was just about to give up and go to Costco grab some munchies for my friend's birthday party out in Oakland.....

Then, thank the good lord, as I was drowning my catering blue's with the fantastic margaritas at Celia's of Berkeley, I found out that they catered!

We got trays of beans, rice, chimichangitas, & enchiladas as well as some burritos. Everyone loved the food and I felt like a hero! It was easy to setup, eat and clean.

The best part is that it is affordable and very professional. Will be using Celia's for catering in the future.

I'm a fan of brunch. It's just the best meal. And this place does not disappoint. The orange French toast is really good and the orange flavor doesn't overwhelm it. My friend got a vegetarian eggs benedict that she really enjoyed. The prices are fair, and the upstairs seating is nice. The place is small, but cozy. The orange juice is really good, too. There are menus outside the door and then you go up to the register, make your order, and find a table. It's a cute little nook just off campus. Check this place out.

Taste: 5
Value: 4
Service: 4

Came here after running the Nike Women's Half marathon, so I definitely had an appetite. On recommendation from our friend, I tried the Alameda. Two pieces of french toast with thinly sliced ham and sauteed mushrooms in the middle. Top it off with two eggs, over easy, and hollandaise sauce to top it off. The bottom has a balsamic vinegar reduction which complements the sweetness of the french toast.

I got a breakfast burrito for ~$10 brunch at 11:30am. And it was literally all I ate that day. So, for the entrees that easily last multiple meals, the priciness of Sunnyside doesn't amount to too much. The homefries are delicious! Crusty potato skins left in the mix, and cooked to crusty perfection. Of course, I have a deep and genuine love for all types of burritos. Reheating the arm-sized meal for dinner made it just as if not more scrumptious than earlier because the flavors had time to settle. The eggs are cooked to a really fluffy texture, which I am curious to learn.

The service is not great--one negative aspect is the wait for a table. They should crack down on people who get food to-go but snag a table or two anyways. I wanted to reserve a table of four, but the cashier said I couldn't until my party arrived. Once they did, we had to wait another 10 min or so for a place to sit. I know that people wait very long times for the Sunnyside in Albany, though. I was also surprised that they are a pay-before-you-sit operation. I guess you don't really pay for service, then, so I shouldn't complain. But midway through the meal I had to run inside to ask for a salt shaker, and I also would've liked condiments i.e. ketchup, mustard on the table. 

In general, I feel that American brunch places are overrated because, perhaps I am just not used to seasoning my food while I am eating it, but the breakfast fare at such restaurants is always on the bland side. Nothing against the restaurant, just how I feel about the cuisine as a whole. I would come again, though. The dilemma would be trying to order anything other than the burrito, which is a great deal.

Breakfast is the easiest meal to make and this place sucks at it. We asked for egg whites they made a mistake then the waitress had nerve to ask would you want to try this instead of me taking it back? Well u made the mistake so NO take it back!! The veggies in the omlett were so soggy and cold. Oh..and their breakfast potatoes are so horrible and if you are planning to socialize afterward then you should skip potatoes since it have more garlic than potato......Their other location on Solano is so much better in every aspect: service, quality of food etc. So if you want to try this café go to the Solano location.....

This is my new favorite brunch place. Dare I say... better than La Note? Every time I've been to La Note, I was nicely filled up to bursting, but never like OMG I WANT TO GO BACK. But with Sunny Side Cafe, I WANT TO GO TO THERE. I've only eaten three things off the menu so far (technically two cuz I mooched off my roommate's), but they all exceeded my expectations. 

Solano Benedict - I got this with a side of garlic roasted tomatoes, and you should too!!! The tomatoes were soooo gooood and of course it helps that it's tomato season, but the garlic! It's like they injected each tomato inside and out with essence of garlic. So good. Oh and the hollandaise sauce was perfect too. Most that I've tried elsewhere have always been too heavy and left me wanting some hot sauce after a few bites, but I this time slopped up every last bit.

Tofu Scramble - This was my roommate's, and I only got a bite. The tofu scramble was good (not a huge fan of tofu, but my roommate is, and she liked it), but I was in love with the homefries. You know how some places' homefries are not crispy enough on the outside? Like totally lacking the FRIED component of homefries? Well this place got it right. I don't think I've ever seen homefries look that good. They looked so crispy and delicious, I snarfed some before my food even came.

Basil & Tomato Pigs in a Blanket - This was written on their specials board. I thought the basil and tomatoes would come on top of the pancake, but they're actually IN the pancake batter. The mix of savory and sweet was surprisingly delicious, and the tomatoes weren't your standard beefsteak; maybe like heirloom cherry tomatoes..? The pancakes were also the best I've ever had. They were huge and fluffy and perfectly crisped on the outside (does this place have a magic grill or what?!) with the perfect crumb/texture. I wanted to keep eating just for that mouthfeel. You get two piggies in a blanket with two eggs any style. I got mine scrambled, and I guess that was their one weak point. They were meh and had to be rescued with ketchup and Tapatio.

The interior is airy and clean, with some upstairs seating, and I love how the whole place just has a bright, cute, cozy atmosphere. If you sit at the counter facing the kitchen, be sure to utilize those hooks under the counter for your bags! Also be sure to tip the nice cashier lady who takes your order; she also brings your food, refills your water, etc etc while running up and down to greet new customers. And she is super nice! She didn't try to kick me out or give me the evil eye when I was still eating after they closed. =] Even though it's a bit pricey, you get enough food to make two meals out of it, which I'll have to do as a poor college student. Because I'll definitely be going back.

So I decided one day to take the Bart from San Francisco to Berkeley (The downtown one by the University). I was hoping Top Dog would be open but unfortunately it wasn't. I arrived in berkeley at about 8:30 so I didn't expect too many places to be open. So I was hungry and I was there in the morning and I was hungry. Since it was a Sunday a lot of places were closed as it's before the first Football game. I walked a few blocks and ended up on Oxford Street. I noticed the place that looked very familiar. It was Sunny Side Cafe. I heard there was one not too far from there (turns out it is located in Albany and I started to have flash backs). So anyway I decided to go down with a friend. I ordered an omelette and more breakfast stuff. The food and service was EXCELLENT!
This Cafe is quite similar to the one in Albany but a  little different.  You order in front as oppose to sitting in your table but the waiters bring the food out to you.  It was good stuff and I will definitely come back to this location (since it's very Bart familiar). Now I have options other than Top Dog when going to berkeley.

uh, yeah, not a fan. I ordered the "Alameda" with high expectations after reading an East Bay Express review. It was nothing I couldn't have made at home. I was truly underwhelmed after my first bite. Nothing was wrong with it, it just wasn't up to par. It was also just this side of lukewarm. I didn't have the energy to complain. Nothing is worse than being disatisfied after you've saved your appetite for a yummy Sunday brunch. Not much I can say for ambiance. It's very student oriented I'd say. You order at the counter. Sit wherevs, some of the booths are right in front of the kitchen. Felt a little cramped and not in that charming Parisian way where everything is smaller. I do have to say that service was great. Very friendly and fast. If I was a student, I'd probably return to this place, but since i'm not....

Yes, this was THE most expensive breakfast I've ever had, but it was totally worth it.

I got the Portobello Mushroom Alameda special and OMG IT WAS SO DAMN DELICIOUS! Two perfectly done crispy French toasts sandwiching a giant Portobello Mushroom, roasted tomatoes, spinach and cheese, and topped with two easy over eggs and hollandaise sauce. I cut into it straight down and got a little bit of everything. It was orgasmic I tell you, ORGASMIC! I went with my roommate and she also really liked it. Everything from texture to flavor just came together really well. I was super hungry when we went in but I couldn't finish it all. The 1/5 I took home, I scarfed down a few hours later.

As for the service, the cashier person/waitress was very friendly. The decor was cute and the place was clean overall. I especially liked these hooks they have under the counter table so the people there can hang their stuff since they'll be sitting on stools. How clever of them!

My only complaint is the price of their orange juice. $4.50 for a glass of OJ? Come on! I know it's fresh squeeze but oranges don't cost THAT much! Regardless, I look forward to coming back to try their to-go sandwiches since one customer who came in to buy a scone swore they're good. But overall, I must say it was a total splurge, although it was ridiculously yummy, I doubt I'll be able to afford frequenting the cafe.

TSSC is small, unassuming and very clean. Not exactly "hole-in-the-wall" but as casual as you can get. Not that I would, but dining here in sweats would not embarrass me.... much.

Eggs benedict with blue cod instead of the usual lox? Genius. 
A side of home fries? Only rivals the unbeatable Cafe Brazil's (you Texans know what I mean) rosemary potatoes. 
French Toast? Perfecto. 
A side of fruit salad? Fruit and slight hint of mint--would never mix the two but y'all did it well. 
OJ? Fresh and squeezed.

Finding a table can prove to be quite a feat. If you're dining in, don't come in a party larger than four.

I happened to find this place to have brunch, particularly their two eggs and meat combo, and it has become one of my "to go" joints whenever I work at Berkeley. The sourdough toasts are done very nicely, toasty and crispy, and their generous serving of two eggs (I like mine scrambled or sunny-side up), three smoked bacon pieces (or of course, choose from a multitude of meat options!), and home fries (choose one from three sides) really made my brunch very satisfying. I am definitely looking forward to coming to this place more often when my tummy screams "bacon and eggs!"

This place has the most wonderful eggs benedict I've ever had. I also am not a fan of eating tomatoes by itself - but my god! was it good.

-1 star for the price. If I recall, I paid about ~$15 for my meal + o.j. Kind of ridiculous even for me who is generally down to pay for some bomb food.

What is it that those PSAs served (on the side) with Saturday morning cartoons used to say? "Knowledge is power?" "The more you know?" Is one of those actually from G.I. Joe? Regardless, if I hadn't eaten here, I wouldn't know better, so.

The staff isn't chatty but they're not rude and it's a cute enough tiny space - airy, even, for something near campus due to the somewhat open two-floor styling. But the food! O, the food. 

I was picking up a Cinnaholic order (where the cashier/baker/all-around swell guy was rescuing a rogue bee that had gotten inside: Cinnaholic, I love you!) and my sweetheart ordered me a House Specialty "vegan on request" tofu scramble. I imagine it is "on request" because otherwise the toast (on the side) is buttered. It's nice that they have a vegan option - online the menu says you can replace the eggs in any egg dish with tofu at no extra charge, which opens up more options but I didn't notice this while looking at the menu posted in the window! The House Specialty tofu scramble, while colorful, was really, really bland and a little watery. It tasted a little better when I mixed in some of the black beans (on the other side). The beans were very salty on their own. 

My omnivorous sweetheart had the avocado and Swiss egg scramble, which was overcooked. I am pretty sure it is a mortal sin to cook avocado at all - it turns so bitter! Yuck. The homefries (you guessed it, on the side) were burnt on the outside, soggy on the inside - and bland, to boot!

The soy lattes were unremarkable and overall the price was a little high. However, I like that they use fresh and organic ingredients - but my tofu scramble sure didn't taste like delicious, delicious Hodo Soy. If we had been more satisfied I don't think the price would seem inflated.

And now I know! And now you know! Know more? Have more power? Knowledge is awesome!

What's so great about this place? Nothing!

Burned toast
Over-cooked eggs
Rosemary in the potatoes (not their problem)
Sour pancakes
Doesn't open until 8am
Frozen solid butter

This place wasn't bad, but it wasn't that good either. For the price I would expect table service (you order at the front and then they bring it out to you). I asked for salsa with my omelette and when they brought my food out they forgot it. So I walked up to the front and asked for my salsa and also asked for a new glass of water because mine had a rubber after taste (gross!). They were super apologetic and brought out my salsa and water right away. Even after I dumped the salsa all over my omelette and homefries the food was still bland. The place itself is super tiny so I would not recommend coming here with more than 2, maybe 3 people. You probably won't be disgusted by the food here but you won't be impressed either. Do yourself a favor and go a few blocks down to Venus or La Note (I originally did but I didn't want to wait 30+ minutes for a table for one).

I've been here twice and everything I've had has been very good. 

The restaurant itself is quite small (it took a year in Berkeley for me to notice it) but they have a huge breakfast menu plus an array of coffee/espresso drinks.  This last time I ordered the orange french toast.  I'm not sure how orange was part of the equation but it's still the best french toast I've had in a long time.  Almost everything is reasonably priced but omg they charge $4.50 for a large orange juice!!  

The service is fast and I've never run into a crowd, so it is a really convenient stop on the way to class.

After trying to go to Betty's for breakfast, and nixing that idea based on the huge lineup outside the door, looked to yelp for another suggestion. I was more than pleased with my experience at Sunny Side Cafe. Not only was I able to get a lovely booth by the window, I had a delectable breakfast which was amazingly similar to what is dished out at Betty's. Had one of the scrambles with the garlic roasted tomatoes and their muffin of the day (blueberry). Everything was very yummy. Pricewise, more or less equivalent to eating at Betty's. But with no wait for a table, plus much more comfortable seating (booth vs counter), I'd come back here instead next time I'm in Berkeley.

i love this place and my family has come here for years.   excellent quality food, nice staff, good coffee and never too loud.   the one on oxford street is a little more self-serve but again, nice, clean and great staff.   i have gotten the eggs and bacon breakfast;  the avocado/cheddar/bacon omlette,  tuna fish salad, and all are great.   my husband gets the benedicts or scambles; my son gets pancakes and we're always all happy.   it isn't cheap but good food just isn't cheap!

I'm rounding up from 2.5 stars since they're making an effort to support sustainable providers and reduce their carbon footprint.  That said, the food was only adequate and most definitely overpriced.  I got the "two eggs with meat" breakfast, plus a coffee.  The sausage patties were on the dry side and everything else was just ok, though the home fries were nice and crispy and the herbs were a nice touch.  Nothing really to complain about except for the price of $12.50 + tip.  More expensive than Fat Apples and Sam's Log Cabin and both have better food.  Maybe I should have tried one of the specials or the apparently otherworldly Alameda, but I feel like the standard breakfast plate serves as a pretty good assessment for any cafe like this.

I've been wanting to try The Alameda for a while now. I wish I hadn't. At first I thought with such great reviews it would be a great combination of flavors, but it's literally a stoner's dream and not in a good way. It tastes like someone took whatever they had left in the fridge and made breakfast. The restaurant was hot, not well ventilated, and poorly designed. You sit above the kitchen and it's disgustingly humid. My girlfriend ordered the Pigs in a Blanket. Someone decided to get fancy with the sausage and put a bunch of weird herbs in it. Denny's would have been a better choice. Luckily I was still on a food-high after having eaten at Chez Panisse the night before.

I came here for brunch. The menu was very appetizing and had a hard time trying to decide what to get so I ended up splitting an order of orange poppyseed french toast and apple cinnamon french toast with a friend. It was really good, but I couldn't really taste the orange flavor very well. Oh well, it was good. Would definitely come back again to try the famous "Alameda" menu items.

PROS:
-Good food, no complaints from anyone at our table
-Decent price for quality (7.50 for french toast)
-Not too crowded, we actually managed to get a seat on a Saturday morning

CONS:
-Drinks seemed rather expensive.....in the $3-$4 range for juice (no refills, I assume).
-You have to wait in line to order your meal at the cashier...it makes it hard if you are trying to secure seating with your party while ordering (however, a waitress does bring your food to your table).

Had a pretty good burger here on Saturday. The place is pretty small, but the service was friendly and the burger was good. I recommend getting the bacon on it too, it's nice, thick cut applewood smoked bacon. Good stuff =)

Stopped by here for breakfast with a friend. We were initially going to go to a different place but it was so crowded and we were running low on time so we decided to try Sunny Side Cafe instead. 

Sunny Side Cafe is quaint but easily accessible. It's pretty close to the Berkeley campus so it's likely that you've passed by it a few times. 

My friend and I ordered the Alameda and split it between the both of us. That was a good idea mainly because it's a pretty big meal and it's pretty filling. Overall it was tasty and I appreciated the hearty meal. It was also at a reasonable price considering the location. 

Good place. Cute place. Nothing extraordinary, but I liked it.

Wow.

I mean, I haven't been eating much lately. Not enough time to cook, not enough food to cook enough to stuff myself silly. I had to skip breakfast this morning. I still have a lot left to do today and I needed one solid powerful meal to lift me through the rest of the day.

Found it.

3-egg Bacon/Avocado/Cheddar omelet with homefries and a blueberry muffin. The avocado is to die for. I have had my share of delicious avocados, fresh off the trees and ripe as can be. The avocado present in my omelet was quite possibly the best avocado I have ever tasted. Blueberry muffin was fresh, berries were whole and juicy. Delicious.

The weak link of this meal were the homefries. I was torn between them and the garlic roasted tomatoes, and went with the homefries out of a calorie hankering. Definitely wished I had a side of the other.

Bonus points for offering an organic cup of coffee at a competitive price!

The Alameda.

It's like nothing I've ever had before! It had the best combo of ham, mushrooms, tomatoes, emmenthal cheese all between two french toasts. Over easy eggs were on top with Hollandaise sauce and balsamic reduction. I enjoyed cutting through the toasts and eating all the glory of "The Alameda" with hot sauce! (This is because I love hot sauce on practically everything haha but it was good without it too!)  I loved it because it was such a savory taste in my mouth and was so convenient to eat. Usually my breakfast dishes come with so many different types of foods that it gets overwhelming to focus on one. But this dish had everything together so I was able to experience its goodness in every bite!

Giving it 4/5 stars though because I tried the homefries my friends got and it could have been much better. The potatoes were too squished and a bit on the burnt side.

First timer...

I ordered the Wildcat Benedict (bacon and garlic tomatoes). Never have I seen this combo at any other breakfast place. It was......decent. The English muffin was super soggy when I first received my order. The hollandaise sauce wasn't anything special and actually didn't have much flavor. The eggs were poached a little too long and weren't runny enough. The side of homefries was okay; I ended up adding a lot of ketchup and tapatio to them. Overall the meal was just okay. Definitely edible and not close to gross. Just okay. I've had a lot of benedicts from various places so maybe I expected more? My friend's scramble looked good...so maybe I just didn't order the right thing?
Sunny Side in Albany is SO good. This location was not good. Plus the waitress was not around.

This place was pretty good.  Prices were nothing to be a fan about, but the service was as good as the food.

I had the eggs benedict and the wife had the Crab Alameda thing.

The hollandaise sauce was only ok... the hash browns were seasoned with tyme and rosemary... and I can't say that I really liked it.

I didn't try my wifes, but she said it was good....  but for the price, it was something that really should have been great.  when you consider a breakfast dish for $13.50 + tax + tip... that better be really good.

the pancakes were pretty good as well.

If you want brunch on the weekend then this is the place to be. 

I prefer this place over Venus just because they have larger portions. The eggs Benedict was great and so was their omelette. 

Service is average here. The restaurant isn't too big, you can sit upstairs but I'd recommend just ordering to go and eating it in the cozy confines of your home especially since the restaurant can get quite busy during brunch!
I had the pumpkin pancakes house special. I guess its a Halloween special. Was delicious and its pretty big so I would recommend going for the smaller stack.

Got the chance to eat brunch at The Sunny Side Café during a weekender to Berkeley, and it was muy delicioso! We tried the Alameda special, which was a savory French toast sandwich, with mushrooms, ham, cheese and roasted tomatoes, topped with two eggs cooked over-easy and a light balsamic vinaigrette sauce. We also got the short-stack Blueberry Pancakes, which included 2 large pancakes infused with whole blueberries, complete with syrup and butter on the side.  

The portions are pretty big--especially on the Alameda, so I was able to share the special and the pancakes with two other girls. I like that the Blueberry Pancakes weren't too sweet, and the blueberries in the pancakes were real blueberries served whole, not manufactured, over-the-top blueberry flavoring. For the Alameda special, the balsamic vinaigrette sauce was just right, the cheese wasn't too overpowering, and the yolky over-easy eggs topped it all off for me.  

I'm not much of a breakfast person, but this place was like the house in "the three little bears story," where everything was just right. I definitely recommend The Sunny Side Café as a relaxing weekend brunch place... it's very quaint, and you can choose whether you want to eat downstairs or upstairs.

3.5 stars

I came here for a weekend brunch with the roommates, so the company was definitely very nice to have :) However, I feel like this is probably somewhere that is worth trying once and not coming back for...

I paid $13 (including tax) for The Alameda, which is the most famous dish here. Admittedly, it was very delicious, but I'm not sure if I would pay $13 for it. I appreciated how much meat they gave but I wish it had come with some arugula or some greens because of all the vinegrette that was doused over the dish (nothing wrong with vinegrette though!) 

It's very hard to get seats on the weekends. However, if you come on for brunch on a day with good weather, it's more enjoyable to sit outside than in one of the seemingly squished booths inside.

Very good food! Came here the morning after a night of drinking and dancing needing a heavy and filling breakfast. Ordered the eggs benedict, and was very satisfied. My friend got a different type of eggs benedict (don't remember which was which) and it was really good too. My boyfriend ordered the french toast and it was exactly what I would want. I had to order a mimosa and it was perfect to my taste - pulpy.

The location and atmosphere makes it even better. There were a good amount of people but not too crowded. We sat upstairs and hung out for a good couple hours just eating. Also, the location is overall good (walking distance from our apartment).

I'll be showing up here on random weekends for sure!

I've wanted to go here forever because it looks like a great place to get a decent meal. The boy had been here before and had a pretty good experience. The prices are a little high, but if they really do use all fresh, organic etc. ingredients I'm fine by it. First of all it took 30 minutes for our burger and egg plate to arrive...they weren't even that busy. Second, they cooked my eggs incorrectly and I had to send the dish back and that took another 10 minutes. Then I got my food and my egg was great and the rest of my food was cold by then. They didn't bring butter (or jelly for that matter) with my toast and I had to get up to get it. Then I found a pretty good size eggshell in my not-so-great potatoes. Nevermind the entire staff looked like they hated life. All combined, it was enough to make me never want to come back.

The service here is incredibly helpful, friendly, and patient!  And the food's pretty good, too.  It seems expensive, but the portions are ginormous -- maybe too big.

The home fries have rosemary in them, which definitely puts them a cut above most breakfast potatoes.  I was there for lunch, but would love to go for brunch.  For $10 I wouldn't need to eat for the rest of the day.
