This is a solid B range place, which translates to about four stars on Yelp.

The Good:
Service is friendly and excellent.  The counter staff is really attentive.  The clientele are mostly local students and faculty, since UC Berkeley is literally across the street, so it's got a real neighborhood feel.  The open kitchen is really clean and neat, even when they're cranking out a lot of orders.  The food is a good value for the money in downtown Berkeley, that close to the university.

The Bad:
The special I had was guilty of overreach and real confusion of flavors.  Raspberry flavored steak in a citrus Hollandaise sauce?  Not really my thing.

The Ugly:
Overcooked eggs and soggy muffins in an Eggs Benedict, which is something they're supposed to be know for.  WTF?

The food was a roughly 3 star experience.  The service, atmosphere, and ROI was in the 4-5 star range.  Overall, I'm more than happy to go back.  But, I think I'll be staying away from the specials. 

I've got more details up on my blog - http://www.chubbypanda.com/2011/09/sunny-side-cafe-choka-berkeley-ca.html

I enjoyed a satisfactory brunch at Sunny Side Cafe this morning.  We arrived around 9 o'clock on a Sunday morning -- the restaurant was at 50% capacity, which was a relief given all the other reviews mentioning crowds.

My partner and I shared the Eggs Benedict, and a scramble of ham and garlic.  Both dishes were prepared excellently, avoiding normal bad brunch pitfalls (two examples:  the Benedict was *lightly* dressed in Hollandaise sauce, and the home fries were lightly crisped and not too heavy).

The meal was pricier than expected, unfortunately -- we spent $27 on a meal for two, before tip.  Our ice teas were probably more than we expected.  Service was okay, it's an order-at-the-front-and-take-a-flag experience.

As I said, a satisfactory experience.  I wouldn't rush back, unless I was entertaining hardcore brunch-goers.

While The Sunny Side Cafe isn't my favorite brunch place, the food is good and reminds you of the comforts of home. I ordered the Pigs-in-a-Blanket with scrambled eggs, tasty but average. The eggs were pretty mediocre, but the buttermilk pancakes were soft and filling, and the sausages had a nice flavor, despite being a little bit sweet. The cafe is a small place with additional seating upstairs, and great for grabbing brunch on a lazy Sunday with friends. I would come here again!
Love coming here! I've had eggs benedict and omelette. Def want to come back again to try all their other dishes. Their breakfast sandwich thing is really good too ( i forget what it was called ).

If you don't wanna wait an eon at Venus or La Note to get your breakfast fix on one of those lazy sundays in downtown Berkeley, this is the place.

I've never had to wait for a table and you order up front, then they bring it out to you. This is good since foot traffic can cause problems in this tiny place.

Everything I've ordered was awesome, especially the Mandarin Orange French Toast.

Just don't bring your entire dorm floor w/ you. I don't wanna start waiting for a table.

Finally had a chance to try the breakfast here!  After eating, I can only give 3 stars.

My reasons: 

First, the price.  I ordered the Wildcat Benedict (Eggs Benedict with grilled tomatoes, bacon, and a side of potatoes), which came out to about $12.  For that price, I feel the breakfast could be better, considering there are other places around Berkeley that can offer breakfast of the same quality for less money.

Second, the food itself, specifically the potatoes.  I will say that the Eggs benedict was pretty good: bacon was cooked well, loved the tomatoes, and the eggs/english muffin combo provided a good foundation.  However...the potatoes were a big disappointment.  It's literally a pile of potatoes cooked on one side, so one side is extremely crispy...but the rest is just a pile of mushed potatoes...not enticing to eat.  (I did notice that they keep a pile of potatoes at the ready on the cooktop...not fresh maybe?)

Overall, I felt it was average.  The environment is nice though, from the outside I would not have known there was a second floor!  We ate on the 2nd floor, which is reminiscent of an European cafe.

When: 11 AM
What: Ham, Pear, some cheese, sourdough sandwich
Price: $4.95
Comments: Excellent flavor combinations. Simple and tasty. I plan to come back again in the future to try all their other amazing sounding items. The Alameda (The Alameda  mushrooms, Golden Gate ham, roasted tomatoes, and emmenthal cheese, sandwiched between two
pieces of savory French toast, topped with two eggs over-easy,
Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction  ) sounds freaking delicious..till next time.

It is what it is.  A nice little spot for breakfast with an assortment of standard items, decent coffee and cozy confines.

I would go back!
Great breakfast food and coffee near Berkeley campus. Fast service too!

They have an extensive breakfast menu and a decent variety of sandwiches, but I can't stop ordering their burgers because they're juicy and served on a poppy-seed roll that compliments the meal so well. The place is small so it's easy to walk by and not notice it, which would be a big shame because the food is delicioso. The interior is cozy and clean and the customer service is very friendly.  The menu is big on organic/sustainable food and I heard the tofu sandwich is definitely worth trying (covered in curry and deep fried) and sounds very tempting.

3.5 stars. this was definitely a pleasant, accidental find. in search of a new brunch spot, we were walking over to Gather - and never made it there. just a block away we walked past the tiny restaurant front of sunny side cafe, and awesome smells lured me in as i followed my nose. lots of brunch options and delicious wheat germ pancakes. and a breakfast wrap bigger than my head.

Came here with a couple of my girlfriends for a book club meeting (shout out!)  

Service was excellent, I thought the staff was very patient with us considering we sat outside for a really long time, well after most of the patrons had left and they didn't rush us or anything.

They have a huge menu, my girlfriends and I had such trouble choosing we ended up picking 2 of the specials that week: the Sloppy Joe and the blueberry pluot pancakes with meyer lemon syrup.  A's for both dishes!  The sloppy joe had a perfectly cooked egg on top, (the yolk melted over the sandwich) and it wasn't too oily.  I especially loved the meyer lemon syrup with the pancakes. We all left extremely pleased and very stuffed.  

Prices are reasonable, and portions are pretty generous.  I would definitely come back as there are so many things I still need to try on the menu!

Cute little hole in the wall. It serves breakfast all day, which is a plus because it's the most important meal of the day, and having it at any point in the day, especially for college students who get up at 12pm to take a nap, is a plus. I had the chicken sweet jalapeno sandwich with a side salad. I have to say that it was small portions, but the cafe mocha was good and tasty. They love giving out the sun dried tomatoes with every dish, doesn't matter what you ordered. You can sit upstairs, which is a plus, because I originally thought it was too tiny to begin with

We love this place! We have ordered egg dishes, sandwiches, and salads which have all been great and large portion sizes. We also are a fan of their bloody marys! Staff is very nice and seating outside gives a pretty view of campus.

Only downside is the seating is limited, so don't come here with a large group. Also, they can run out of certain items on the menu the later in the day you come, but there are so many great choices, you still can't go wrong. This isn't the cheapest place for breakfast/lunch, but it is definitely worth it.

Went here with my friend for bunch and was completely satisfied. The atmosphere and decor of the place was very relaxing and truly reflected both Berkeley culture and energy. I had gotten the Alameda, which was one of their signature dishes, and I really enjoyed the meal. The meal had balsamic reduction which was perfect and the food was really filling. However, this place fails to get a five star because of the poor service and when I saw my friend's glass of orange juice that was about two dollars, but was roughly the size of a scotch glass, I just wanted to laugh. 

Overall, I would recommend coming here since it is a pretty good brunch place in Berkeley and the wait is not too bad. However, if you come here, be ready to pay a lot for a drink and order at the cashier, pray that there isn't a line.

Good place for sunday brunch, walked there with my girlfriend midmorning and had no wait. There are a few small tables in the sun outside. I had the alameda special and she had the eggs benedict. Food was great allegedly organic and local which may be why it tasted so damn good and put me in a food coma. Definitely worth checking out the tab was maybe 40$ with drinks.

I'm going to keep this short & sweet: I stumbled across The Sunny Side Cafe while wandering around the UC campus. If I recall the name correctly, I ordered the wildcat eggs Benedict which came with garlic roasted tomatoes, bacon and also a side of potatoes with extra yummy bacon. I also ordered a spicy bloody mary. This truly hit the spot. Their hollandaise sauce is exceptionally good. My friend ordered the Alameda which was also very delicious. If you're in the area and looking for a quick breakfast in a cozy environment, come here and come hungry.
This place makes a pretty darn good bacon avocado omelet. Their home fries seemed kinda lacking but it was still good! I'd definitely come back. The service was great too!
"Not that good" --Fu

One thing I have learned about the Sunny Side Cafe (both the Berkeley and Albany Locations) - this is the perfect place to bring your parents for brunch. The food is delicious, it is not a cheap diner, and the ambiance is very homey. 

I love the scrambles (the Grand Canyon is my favorite!), but it is the rotating weekend specials menu that really keeps me coming back. Specials always feature an egg dish, a fancy pancake/french toast, and a fun interpretation of eggs benedict (also a fave). 

I must admit, I prefer the Albany location over the Berkeley location. Although it is usually a bit packed, the Albany location has servers vs. counter ordering. It's a bit nicer for a brunch outing. Also, seating is very limited, and the upstairs seating does get pretty hot on a warm day. I think I would probably enjoy it more if I were a college student. Good thing it is adjacent from the Cal campus!

That being said, I would never turn down an invitation to Sunny Side Berkeley!

I'm from Alameda, so when I found out this place has an monster sandwich named after my fair island, I had to go there. However, the sheer size of it put me off- if it were TRULY an Alameda it would be scared of wheat bread (see what I did there?). Anyway, I got the  wildcat benedict, which had bacon instead of ham and also grilled tomatoes. The hollandaise was good, lighter than the normal one I make at home. Overall it was tasty but just needed a bit of a kick- more salt, or citrus, or spice. The home fries were kind of plain, I should have ordered something else in place of the fries. Service was fast, although a bit confusing with the self-seating, then ordering. I liked the available water pitchers and glasses though. A bit pricey but brunch is usually a little bit more expensive than normal.

Food was nice. I got a Bacon avacoda omelette. The price is a little high but you get a decent amount of food. They are a bit forgetful on somethings. My main gripe with the place is the flies. I spent more time swatting than eating.

I was pretty excited to try this place after reading so many positive reviews about it. My friend and I went to the Oxford location on a Saturday around noon time. You order your food at the cashier and then they'll bring it over to you when it's ready. They have specials written on a chalkboard above the cashier, by the way....so be sure to check those out before committing!

I had the buttermilk pancakes since I LOVE pancakes and a lot of people said their pancakes were delicious. Unfortunately, they didn't have any special pancakes that day.....

Anyway, it was alright - not bad, not excellent. The short stack (2) was enough to fill me up (but I wasn't stuffed...)

My friend had a scramble, but the eggs were a little too watery/oily/runny and was a bit bland. 

I must admit, I was a bit disappointed. Maybe I should have gotten their famous item The Alameda.....

I wonder if the Solano location is any better?

Other things: 
Friendly staff. 
Street (metered) parking. 
Average prices.
Outdoor and balcony seating available.

Having a nice Sunday morning with my honey n we decide to try something new. We ordered a Benedics and a regular egg breakfast. The Benedics I had is fair, a bit salty , big portion. The organe juice is freshly made, with lots of plums. The egg breakfast is fair. Overall, no big surprise on food but decent decoration n nice environment for breakfast or lunch.

Passing by, this seems like a simple take-out counter, but upon further investigation they have a very cozy upstairs section with a few small tables and some booths down on the ground floor.  The lunch is not as cheap as I would expect from what seems like a hole-in-the wall, but the quality matches.  The burger was good, made so by quality toppings and bun, not so much flavorful meat.  That was my one complaint.  The sesame chicken sandwich was a big hit with my friend.  

Where they really gained ground was the service and atmosphere.  Being obnoxious Berkeley students, we took up a table with books and papers for the better part of 3 hours.  They were courteous and tolerant and even let us stay 30 minutes past closing time.  The upstairs is quiet with just a hint of music playing (both from the dining area and from the kitchen making impromptu mash-ups of pop rock and salsa music).  It was well lit and without too much foot traffic, which I appreciate when studying, but wished they had more business to keep this place running.  It's a great place to eat and study when you are just sick to death of the library.

+ Decent food

+ Good service

- Seating

+ Great location

- Little pricey. 

Overall, one of my frequent spots I hit up for breakfast.

The website said they opened at 7:30, so in we went at 7:45 only to be yelled at "we're not open, wait outside". A small crowd had gathered and when they opened the door at 8, we all marched upstairs. After waiting upstairs for 10 minutes with no sign of a waiter, I walked downstairs and the same rude guy barks "you have to order down here", thanks for letting us know before we went upstairs! Opening at 8 I guess means organizing and making coffee at 8. We waited  and waited and finally got our food that might have been good if it was hot, but instead was lukewarm. Awful service, awful place, stay away. Perhaps they are better at 9:00 once they have done their setup but I won't be going back!

Interior is very clean, and feels cozy
food is good - not spectacular, but you can tell that it is fresh, and it's one of the nicer breakfas/brunch places in Berkeley - and huge lines are to be expected on weekends
Price is a bit on the pricey side for students, especially for breakfast, but it is one of the nicer breakfast places within walking distance (it is actually right across the street from campus) of the Cal campus
This is definitely a place that I would go if I have parents visiting from out of town - for breakfast/brunch

Gotta give them 4 stars purely because they will substitute tofu for ANY egg dish!

I'm a picky brunch eater -- I prefer savory breakfasts over the sweet stuff but I HATE HATE HATE eggs.  Luckily in the Bay Area there's usually one vegan option per menu.  But at Sunny Side I have multiple options! Because they understand that a great breakfast doesn't have to include eggs. 

This place really has something for everyone - from the over-the-top sweet French toast to the protein blast egg (or tofu!) scrambles to the hungry-hungry-hippo style Alameda....thing. What is it? A sandwich? Eggs Benedict?  Who knows?  Just eat it, if you can.

i went with a friend last weekend, and it ended up being amazing! I had been here before and gotten omlets and I really was not impressed by the egg or the filling. However, today we got the blueberry pancakes and they were delicious! their syrup is also very good.  The meal that stole the show was the breakfast burrito.  The tomato toritilla is DELICIOUS. The portion was EASILY large enough for two people to share -- its a giant burrito!

Anyways, if you're going to eat here I highly suggest those two dishes along with their fresh orange juice :)
It is w bit expensive, but at least the food is somewhat authentic.. the orange juice was bangin' too.

Meh. This place is cute and quaint-but really tiny. I think there are probably less than 10 tables total in the restaurant. We ordered downstairs and sat upstairs. The upstairs and these two flies kept circling around our food/table. I ordered the french toast special. The french toast was okay, but it came with this tart blood orange marmalade.  It just was not a pleseant mix with the maple syrup and toast.

Unfortunately, I have only eaten their sandwiches to go. I highly recommend the ham, pear and egg sandwich. I have tried all three of the sandwich options but that is my personal favorite! The service is great for what is essentially a take out window. They are always friendly and offer outdoor seating and water while you wait!

I came here on a weekend morning for brunch and it was quite satisfying! I ordered the "Alameda", a dish of french toast with ham, eggs, vegetables, hollandaise sauce, and a touch of balsamic vinegar around the edge. Everything pretty much melted in my mouth! If you ever decide to come here, try this dish. It was both delicious and filling!

4 stars for food, 3 for service, 2 for price.

I've wanted to try this place forever since I pass by it on my way to campus nearly everyday. Like everyone else says, you are paying for hype... I ended up paying $17 after tax and tip for the Alameda and a small glass of orange juice. 

The Alameda- mushrooms, Hickory smoked ham, roasted tomatoes and emmenthal cheese, sandwiched between French toast, topped with two eggs over-easy, Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction. Gotta say, it sounded amazing when I ordered it, looked amazing when it came (see picture), and tasted amazing (the balsamic reduction was the perfect complement to the amazingness listed above). And ohmigoodness I don't think I've ever consumed that many calories in one sitting before noon before... I practically had to roll myself down the stairs and out the door. I would highly recommend this item, but to share with another person... unfortunately everyone else in my party had ordered their own item. 

Their orange juice is so expensive! It tasted more like tangerine juice than orange juice, and was really sweet (not unnaturally) and not very tangy (imo... my friend said it was tangy). 

Overall I liked the place and would want to come again and try more of their menu, but it's really pricey, especially given its vicinity to campus.

When you say brunch a lot of people in Berkeley automatically think of La Note. In my opinion this place is underrated, and might be even better than La Note.

It's typical brunch, but their ingredients are fresh and they do try to give their menu a twist. Beautiful place to sit on the sidewalk and have a plate of pancakes. Their French toast and eggs benedict are good.

I don't think this place deserves over three star ratings OR its price.

1. the food doesn't even look good...
2. eggs Benedict for 14 bucks? ew...
3. muffin seriously overbaked, so hard to cut or chew
4. the sauce...i guess they put too much butter in it...so it's rich in grease, not flavor.
5. They gave me STEAK knife to cut the muffin! It's not something I'd expect at a place whose price range is around $20. and you can tell how hard the muffins were?
6. The home fries...I don't even wanna talk about it...
7. The environment of the restaurant...so NOT cute.
8. The serving size of the dishes are really NOT big.

I'm never gonna go there again...

The location is great- a block from Berkeley Bart. The space is small but cozy. I recommend sitting upstairs though (more room). What I love the best is that you can order roasted tomatoes instead of home fries!

I love the original place better for the mere fact the customer service went to shit at this one. 

I hated the fact that  the "hostess" didn't even really greet or bother to look at us when we were clearly one of the very few in the cafe. My boy friend and I didn't understand whether or not we were supposed to walk in and take our own seats and then be helped with a menu and a beverage... No. The "hostess" mumbled something and I just thought we'd sit down because I didn't hear/understand what she muttered to us. After already sitting there for 5 minutes and then finding out she wasn't going to come to the table again we had to get up and go to her and order. 

I didn't understand this. I thought it would be like the other cafe on Solano, where you'd be seated and then helped by the waiter. This was no where near clearly stated by any of the employees. 

This weird and almost rude experience ruined the visit.. But the food was amazing as usual. I love the food. I absolute love it. But today's visit was not the best, and disappointing. :(

I'm not going to go to this location any more. I absolutely adore Solano's Sunny Side Cafe.. I'll definitely be visiting this location again and again.

I have to rate The Sunny Side Cafe as my favorite place for brunch in Berkeley! The service is great, and the food is exceptional!

I've been here a couple of times now, and I've tried many of their breakfast items. I recommend the Avocado and Emmenthal Scramble and the Pigs in a Blanket.

For those with a classic taste, their "2 eggs any style with meat" is always a pleaser. I love how they have chicken sausages, rather than those wrinkly pork sausages at many diners. Their homefries are really good as well.

Tip: Even on the rainiest of days, this place still seems to cheer you up!
For the mutigrain pancakes .....soooo delicious! Friends ordered  ton of things and they were all good as well. I miss them pancakes

Atmosphere: Order at the front and seat yourself. It's small, but the art is cute and the upstairs is pretty.

Food: When I go to breakfast places, I enjoy trying the different and out of the ordinary things. I ordered the Alameda, which is basically stuff on top of stuff inside of stuff...covered in stuff. It's basically a monster of mushroom, ham, french toast, eggs, hollandaise, tomatoes, balsamic, and cheese. Don't get me wrong, the first few bites were delicious! I absolutely loved the balsamic flavor. After a short while, however, it became way too heavy and sickening - and the portion is big enough as is. By the end of it, I felt like rolling over and dying. But hey, if you like heavy breakfast food, I dare you to try it! Next time I'm opting for something simple - most definitely. My roommate ordered the 2 stack of blueberry pancakes and he really liked them.

Service is good, and the prices are a little above average. I'd come back to try other things
I love the Alameda! You can't find it anywhere else!

Great, cheerful staff, and generous, tasty portions of breakfast foods! What's not to like? Got the tofu scramble plate here and it was delicious- it's not La Note but it's a close second for good brunch foods!

So delicious! Sunny Side is the perfect brunch spot right by campus. It is small and cozy but the food is truly delicious. Although the brunch is the best, the croque Monsieur sandwich is good as well!

Great breakfast spot. And really good service. I usually order the Alameda or the Pigs in a Blanket. The pancakes are so fluffy and moist and buttery. And i love the roasted tomatoes. the only bad thing is it closes at 3pm so if youre on summer vacation and wake up at 5pm craving some breakfast it wont be open. Other than that, great place. Relaxing environment with a little niche upstairs and also seats by the window. I believe ingredients are also fresh and organic, for the most part.

This place was YUMMY! After a heated match of tennis, my friend and I decided to grab some breakfast on Sunday morning at this local spot. There was small line out of the door, but we able to place our order in only a couple minutes.

I had the avacado, bacon, and cheese omelette with wheat toast. I know it's the classic California trick to put avacado on everything but this was seriously one of the tastiest omelettes I've had in recent memory. The potatoes had a unique flavor and spice to them, and I'm always a sucker for what looks like fresh jam (though I'm fairly certain it was just Smuckers in a little dish). My buddy ordered some fresh-squeezed orange juice which was definitely the real deal. Make sure to get a glass.

I have to subtract one star because of the high prices. Our entire meal was over $25 (for two people) without tip. To me, that is a little pricey in a college town, but being neither from California nor attending Berkley, I cannot say one way or another.

Love it! We were in Berkeley for my step-daughter's graduation. Graduation day was wonderful, full of activity, emotion, and oh so  long!  As a result, the morning after we were in dire need of a major caffeine fix and sustenance. Thank you, fellow Yelpers for leading us to this little jewel. 

First, the coffee: I had a latte that definitely satisfied the caffeine need. My husband had their house coffee blend, Peru Organic, which he raved about and is now on a mission to find so we may enjoy at home. 

Now, for the food, SO satisfying! Step-daughter and I got the bacon, Cheddar, and tomato fried egg sandwich. The bread is dressed with a tasty jalapeño aioli that has just a hint of spiciness. Thick and crispy applewood smoked bacon. Thick juicy slices of fresh tomato (I love tomatoes), topped with a fried egg and slice of Cheddar cheese. The sandwich is grilled just long enough to crisp the bread and melt the cheese. My hubby ordered the Mexican scramble. The salsa was not spicy, which would normally be a disappointment for us, but in this case hubby said salsa was flavorful enough it was not an issue. Now, for what surprisingly turned out to be the 'icing on the cake', the black beans served with the scramble. Perfectly cooked so they were tender without being mushy in a thick broth so flavorful, the beans can be a meal on it's own. I don't know how they are seasoned, but I was able to see that they add onions and red bell pepper (roasted?). Delish! Once we had a taste, we had to have more spoonfuls. Serving portions are not huge, but they are certainly larger than one should have, and definitely enough to last the long drive back to L.A. 

Locale is small, three tables and about 4 seats at the counter downstairs, 3 (or 4) bistro tables outside and a few additional tables upstairs. We were impressed with their very efficient use of the limited space. Staff is super nice and efficient. We are only sorry we did not discover this gem on earlier trips so we could have enjoyed it  more often. Fortunately for us, we will be back in Berkeley next weekend to move step-daughter home, which means we will be able to enjoy breakfast at the Sunny Side one more time. Looking forward to it.

I had their special on the weekend Asian apple pear french toast. It has a good flavor. However, I would recommend them to put more of the fruit than just a tiny bit in the center line. Food and service are a bit higher than the price. Atmosphere is good and relaxing. Don't seem over crowded.

Service: Friendly but incompetent (no napkins/utensils even when asked for)

Food: Ordered a plain burger, grilled medium. Got plain rare/medium rare burger with extra watery onions. Country fries- half turned into mashed potatoes. Where's the country love in them fries?? 

*Note: Only tried the burger, but never going back to try anything else.

Atmosphere: Seating is cramped. They would do well to put cute tables rather than have giant, heavy booths. Its supposed to be a cafe, not a donut shop.

Way too pricey when all factors combined. Owner should take responsibility for his/her service and quality deliver if wants to operate for more than 3 years.

I came here on a Sunday afternoon with my sister, her best friend, and her best friend's son.....  Extra points for the organic menu and the cute decor. This is a definite must for Sunday breakfast/brunch. I had the Tilden Eggs Benedict (Good.... a bit heavy, but that's Hollandaise sauce for you) with the side of home fries. My sister got the chicken salad sandwich and her friend got the Golden Gate Sausage and Spinach scramble. Everything was good. I'd try the pancakes or french toast next time. Yum-o.

It's been a while since I've been genuinely impressed by a breakfast eatery...

Came across this place *completely by accident*... after ditching La Note's unreasonably huge line (my hunger pains convinced me that no breakfast was worth waiting 30 minutes for), we drove around the corner and there it was... a cute little egg logo & awning, perched quaintly above a group of people dining on the curb. Calm. Serene. No line. No huge crowd. Just food.

We popped in and I was instantly amazed.

The menu is diverse, the seating is generous, and everything about the place is 'cute' and delightful.

+ house made sausages
+ BEST home fries i've had in quite some time
+ strong, bold coffee
+ excellent and attentive waitressing
+ pay when you order (up front)

We walked out and decided that this place would be added to our weekend breakfast rotation...

As a brunch lover, I find this place totally wonderful! Sunny Side Cafe has a great assortment of omelets, eggs benedicts, scrambles, pancakes, and other brunch essentials... all for a good price with a nice atmosphere. I can't wait to come eat here again!

Some of the best scrambled eggs I've ever had. Perfectly cooked, with the delicious garlic-flavored cream cheese oozing throughout. Yum. I ordered sausage on the side, which I did not enjoy, but only because it was super healthy-tasting, and I really just wanted some processed meat, I realized. But that doesn't take away from the fact that my meal was fresh, prepared quickly, and the atmosphere is absolutely adorable. I felt happier just after sitting in there for 5 minutes. All of that combined justifies the 5 stars. I think I just won't get the sausage, cause I'm sure any of the other options would be amazing.

We sat down outside on a nice sunny afternoon, watching the people walk by on the sidewalk and counting Priuses (Priui?) as they passed by.  The cafe had a pleasant atmosphere and service was friendly albeit slow.  

I ordered a cheese burger with a garden salad and an orange juice. The orange juice was super tasty, but $2.25 for about 4 oz of juice was a bit steep.  My burger was decent with a light poppy seed roll, some nice greens, tasty slices of tomato, and pickled red onions.  I asked for it medium-rare though and they cooked it medium and they forgot to give me cheese.  It tasted more like an $8 burger than a $10 one.  Overall, I would say it was a nice place that I would go back to, but not good enough for me to give it 4 or 5 stars.
This is the spot you want to go to for breakfast and brunch. Food here is amazingly good with an friendly atmosphere. Try it out!

This little cafe make me happy, like a little girl who's about to get an ice cream sundae happy: eyes wide... quiet as a mouse. Just ask my boyfriend who sits smiling next to me as I watch the cooks create delicious meals. You can go upstairs or eat outside, but I prefer the stools in front of the kitchen. The staff is really nice and the waiters are helpful. I love the fact that you order and pay first, makes things so much easier when you're ready to leave. So far everything I have tried there is delicious (there bacon is amazing, yes thats right..bacon), can't wait to go back to try there french toast...yummy. 5 stars in my eyes.

Sunny Side Café
Berkeley, California
11am Sunday 12th August 2012
Four Stars

With a slight line out the door, we waited patiently for a Sunday Morning Brunch.  We asked for a table, ordered at the counter, sat ourselves upstairs, and then the wait staff brought our coffee, water, and food.  I enjoyed the daily special Sunny Side Hash which came with Beef, a couple tomatoes, yellow cauliflower, green beans, not-so browned potatoes, 4 pieces of toast, and unevenly cooked Over-Easy Eggs (one side over easy, one side over hard).  Overall, the combination worked well together.  I also had some of Pete's Alameda which was way better.  This dish stacked Hickory smoked ham, roasted
tomatoes, mushrooms, and emmenthal cheese between two pieces of French Toast + two over-easy, eggs and then drizzled with Hollandaise sauce and a balsamic reduction.  This Breakfast monstrosity is what you should order!  The service was pretty attentive for how busy it was.

Kobacha pancakes and lemon French toast.... Out of this world.  Only thing we didn't like was their "pork" sausage.  Dry, tasted like ground turkey,  and way too many herbs. But you MUST TRY this place! :)

Awesome, a much more satisfying breakfast than the inexplicably overhyped Venus. A cute bit of counter seating affords good views of both the street and the expert action on the griddle as home fries, egg sandwiches, and bacons of various forms undergo preparation. Had a benedict with a decent Hollandaise, a little bit too citrus/acidic for my taste but still way better than the bowl of watery vinegary poached eggs I've been served elsewhere in this city. Food came fast even during Saturday morning brunch. APPROVEDDDD

Sunny Side Cafe is my FAVORITE brunch place in Berkeley. Really cute little restaurant. Generous portions...the Alameda is orgasmic! The cheddar/bacon/avocado omelet is my fav.

Wouldn't recommend going for the brunch tasting menu...they really don't give you all that much food, definitely not enough to serve two. 

Other than that, I love Sunny Side Cafe!

This place is pretty cute. It's unfortunately kinda small and hidden, so it's easy to overlook. The food was tasty--I had the Alameda. They say no substitutions, but I just hate swiss cheese; I got jack instead. Yum yum! I definitely couldn't finish the whole thing. My friend told me that we were lucky to get a table early in the morning, so apparently it's a popular place. I felt bad for the cashier who was also the waitress--way too many tables to serve! We got our food in an orderly fashion, but the service would run much more smoothly if they had someone to bring the meals out. I know that in theory paying up front and getting your food afterwards is meant to be quicker, but when people start to line up and your cashier is also your waitress, it gets frustrating really easily. 

-1/2 star because not only did I not get a refill of coffee, but their sugar packets were all half-used and weren't replaced with new ones. Boo. 
-1/2 star because the tables were super cramped together.

yes.

yes.

and yes.

apple cinnamon syrup with buttermilk pancakes.

yes.

thank you.

Yum! I came back from Sunnyside a few hours ago, and I'm still stuffed! I had the bacon & avocado omelette with sourdough and homefries (comes with the omelette!). It was DELICIOUS. Very generous with the bacon & avocado. It was also a lot of food. Very hearty. I definitely recommend! The homefries were okay, not the best I've had, but good enough. The sourdough came with butter & jam. Pretty standard.

I tried some of the buttermilk pancakes (short stack), and it was good, but not awfully special or anything. Maybe it's just that I don't really like pancakes, but I would try something else if you're there. 

PS They also have good taste in music :)
SO STUPID.  Our check was $22.73 and I left cash tip.  Few days later I check my credit card and I was charged $22.75.  Are you guys illiterate?

On my way to the Bart, my friends and I came across The Sunny Side Cafe. It is a cute, French-style place. I was not very familiar with the type of food on the menu, but all over the walls, there were signs about the Alameda, the best breakfast. It looked like a heart attach on a dish, but I do like a good heart attack so I ordered one.
I swear, the tables around mine literally shifted to gawk at the Alameda getting delivered to our table. I even heard someone say "tres bien!" And mind you, that is purely based on it's appearance.
It was ah-mazing! It is golden french toast stuffed with ham, mushrooms, roasted tomatoes, topped with eggs and Hollandaise sauce, and the best part is the balsamic sauce on the bottom of the plate. 

I am not a fan of breakfast foods, because it is too heavy, but, honestly, every bite made me MmmMmmmMmm. I just cannot explain the savory, perfectly crafted dish, where every ingredient was tasted and complimented one another. The flavors danced in my mouth with every bite! 

The Alameda was ahh-Mmmmazing!

Their website says they open at 7:30 am, but they lie.  A few people left because they weren't open that early and the line got too long.

I'm glad I waited for the food here because it was delicious!  Definitely my new favorite breakfast place.  Not comparable to La Note only because La Note is fancy food.  I think I would describe the food here as very Californian.  A lot of fresh veggies mixed with comforting breakfast foods that you would normally expect.

The cashier/server was really nice.  I love it when I can chat it up with them.  I told her I've been dying to go here because I never wake up early enough to eat breakfast and they close at 3 pm!

I would say, however, that things are a little pricey here, but it's worth it.  Compared to, say, Ann's Kitchen where you get really good value, this food is a lot more elegant and takes more skill to prepare I think.  

I got some kind of sausage scramble with roasted tomatoes and sourdough toast.  Yeah, it was really good.  I ate too fast and made myself feel gross, but it was good.  Also nice: they didn't charge me for soy milk in drip coffee!  Horray

Favorite Berkeley brunch place! I like the system of ordering and then having them bring it to you - streamlines the process. 

I always get the egg scramble (usually with avocado) with sourdough toast and roasted tomatoes. Perfect amount of food for me. The specialities like the Alameda are good but there's just way too much food and it gets pretty heavy after a couple of bites.

5 stars for service and ambiance, but the grilled vegetable pesto sandwich I ordered was a little too greasy with too little flavor. My friend ordered an Eggs Benedict with ham and perfectly poached eggs - now THAT was good. I'm definitely coming back for pancakes or french toast, and the belly-busting brunch is also calling my name.

The place was pretty busy when we got there for a Saturday brunch, but we were able to snag a table upstairs. It's pretty tight quarters, so I hope you like getting cozy with other diners.

Foodwise, we ordered the special alameda and the burger with roasted chiles. Boyf seemed to enjoy the alameda, which is basically every breakfast item mashed together.. which did not thrill me. The burger was decent, and the homefries it came with were perfect. The portions were pretty generous but the prices still seem pretty steep for what it was.

This place is packed, and designed in such a way as to make it impossible not to create a traffic jam that goes out the door.  Luckily it's in Berkeley where the weather is always an improbable 70 degrees, so no one ever gives a shit.  The kitchen works full bore like the engine room of a submarine, and works just as fluidly.  

The alameda was like a deconstructed omelet drenched with Hollandaise sauce, which meant that the entire dish tasted like Hollandaise sauce.  Not terribly impressive.  The burger was decent, but nothing to write home about, not even if you had specifically been asked to write about Sunny Side Cafe's burgers.  

I've also watched the steady inflation of breakfast prices with growing dismay.   Breakfast should cost 7 bucks and come with coffee, not 10 and coffee is extra.  Cost too much for what we got.

I went for breakfast with a friend a few weeks ago, had always wanted to try it.  What a disappointment!  We were seated upstairs, and I noticed that there were stacks of cooked bacon in the kitchen, and that the cook was making fresh bacon, which smelled great.  When I tasted my bacon, it was obvious that they didn't give us the fresh slices. The bacon was hard,  dry, and   tasted  like it was reheated rather than fresh bacon that was  cooked a bit too long.  There is a big distinction in taste.  The waitress disappeared after serving us, and never once came by to ask how the food was. She appeared when the meal was over to bring the check. The eggs were ok, but the breakfast basically sucked.

Don't waste your money - better to go to McDonalds, Homemade Cafe, or even La Note for better food than this rip-off joint.  There didn't seem to be a manager on the premises, the employees were just hanging out, talking with each other.

Went here for Sunday brunch. We got here JUST before the brunch hour so there was no line and we were seated very quickly. I ordered french toast with two eggs sunny side up. My friend got her food WAY before I did. I thought maybe it was because she ordered something different (an omlet) so we waited patiently for my food to arrive. And we waited. And we waited. And then finally the table next to ours got all of their food (even though they came in much later than us) so I finally asked when I would be getting my french toast. The waiter said he would check on it. I'm pretty sure they forgot about my order. 

They rushed me my french toast and said the eggs would be coming right up. The french toast was soggy. The eggs, when they finally arrived, were most definitely not sunny side up. I think they tried to make it quickly seeing as how they forgot about my food. The edges were super crispy and one of the yolk's was completely cook through. 

I was so disappointed with this place I don't even have the energy to make this review cool and/or funny.

Their breakfast food is AMAZING!! Having brunch here really brightens your day :)

I'm not much of a brunch food person, but decided to come here after hearing all the good stuff about this place. Ordered the famous "Alameda", which consists of french toast  with ham, tomatoes, mushrooms, hollandaise sauce topped with an egg. it was absolutely amazing!! the french toast was perfectly toasted and buttered. eggs were cooked perfectly so that as i cut down into the sandwich, some yolk seeps into the sandwich. the ham was slightly crispy to give the sandwich an extra texture. and the mushroom and tomatoes just blends in with everything else. 

definitely recommend trying their signature dish!! the service was also incredibly amazing! 

recommend coming here on the weekend when the weather is nice and the sun smiles at you~

We ordered poached eggs.  They were DRY.  Yeah, totally dry and NOT even runny.  That's a total breakfast SIN!  I didn't feel like being a bi-atch and asking for new eggs, though I should have.  Coffee was also lukewarm, water down, and NOT strong (HELLO, we're in BERKELEY, there is no excuse for this).  I asked for a second cup, and the same thing.  Yuck.  I know this joint is new, though, so I'd maybe come back if these things get rectified.   On the upside (because I try to make sure to note every upside): it's clean, pleasant, and the servings are huge.

I came here for lunch and it was extremely crowded. There were only two waitresses and despite they were busy taking orders and serving people, and helped us put some chairs and tables together that were scattered outside and made a table for 4! They were very willing to get our tables and food ready! The food is amazing for such a small kitchen. I got pigs in a blanket and it was soooo good!!!! The orange juice is FRESHLY squeezed and the cafe ole come in a pint sized glass! Very worth going to!!

I was completely under whelmed with this place. I had a blueberry pancake short stack with applewood bacon. The pancakes were just ok -- nothing to write home about. They actually could have been better.  More tender and less leathery.  T o their credit the applewood bacon was tasty. If in Berkeley, do yourself a favor and have brunch or breakfast at La Note. The lemon gingerbread pancakes with poached pears are absolutely divine. Enjoy the friendlier atmosphere, vibe and wonderfully delicious food.

Good breakfast. Casual, yet pricey. 

I had tried the Solano St. location before, and had a pretty good experience. This location is smaller and doesn't feature full wait service, but the location is really convenient. You order and pay for your food at a counter when you come in. It is then brought to your table.

I ordered "The Alameda".  It consists of mushrooms, ham, and swiss cheese sandwiched between two places of french toast. The whole thing is then topped with a sunny-side up egg and hollandaise sauce. 

The whole thing is pretty massive, mostly because it has about an inch-thick layer of ham piled on the inside. 

The dish was satisfying and filling, but it had its shortcomings. There was so much ham relative to everything else that the saltiness of the ham pretty much overwhelmed all the other flavors. I could barely taste the french toast, egg, and hollandaise. Being a huge fan of  those three items I wish they had a bit more presence in the dish. They also used canned mushrooms, which seems somewhat unacceptable when there is so much great produce around. ( they also pride themselves on their ingredients on the menu, so I found it surprising)  The Alameda costs about $12.
 
My friend ordered scramble n ham.  (scrambled eggs with ham and green onion served with toast and jam) It cost $10.

Overall, the experience was satisfying, but it did seem somewhat expensive. 

If you are looking for a quick, satisfying brunch experience  close to downtown Berkeley, I recommend you give it a try!

Typical American brunch menu, although they do use organic, local ingredients and niman ranch beef.

A nice casual restaurant for brunch. Personally, I only find their "The Alameda" worthwhile. It's their most famous dish, so I recommend giving it a try when you come.

Came here for brunch yesterday. Overpriced, oversalted food. 

Price: My omelette was ~$10. A tiny cup of freshly squeezed orange juice was $4(?). I will concede that the portions were enormous, but the food was not good. Which brings me to my next point.

Food: I got the mushroom-and-tomato omelette with organic whole wheat toast and a side of home fries. The home fries were bland, while the omelette was too greasy and salty. The toast was also mediocre - nothing special. The only thing I enjoyed was the orange juice - freshly squeezed!

Service: Average. The employee was nice enough but nothing out of the ordinary.

Food wasn't good enough to merit the price, so I won't be back.

Massive portions of breakfast/diner-style food. Nuff said.

I come here every so often for a casual lunch/brunch. But it's often overwhelming even for my big appetite.

Order up front and have a seat upstairs or downstairs, where ever you please. 

This time around, I ordered a sausage and broccoli Alameda "special" and my friend ordered a Mexican scramble. That with a glass of orange juice and Arnold Palmer came out to ~$32 before tip.

Experience: 3 (It works)
Service is pretty simple and straight forward as you order from the front counter, take a number, and then have a seat. Fast-food style, if you will, though the food is far from being fast food. Parking is also a little challenging in this particular area, but not impossible.

Value: 4 (You get what you pay for and it's worth it)
The prices may seem high, until you see how massive the portions are. Normal-sized appetites could easily split an entree into two full meals. Bigger appetites will find themselves...quite full.

Food: 4 (That was good...)
Quantities of quality ingredients. They're organic, farm fresh, humanely raised everything. And while I personally can't taste that much of a difference...I can certainly appreciate it.

Overall: 3.66 (Rounded to 4)
For an abundance of quality breakfast food, look no further. Sunny Side Cafe has your meal ready.

Came here with wife after reading good reviews.  I always try the eggs beny when visiting a new brunch place for the first time.  It's the ONLY way to grade a restaurant.  So here goes:

Hollandaise lacked tartness, but has good consistency.
Ham was too salty, but they give you stacks of it.  
English muffin was nice and vaguely sweet.
Eggs were poached perfectly.

Side of potatoes nice... and the cream they served with the coffee was surprisingly ice cold.  I rarely get ice cold cream with my coffee.... and it added wonders to the mug.  

My wife's scramble (avocado and cheese) was good.... better than the beny.  

I would come back, but probably won't have the eggs beny again.

as a vegan, I usually get SCREWED when going out to brunch (bowl of $6 oatmeal, anyone), but I can find quite a few items here.  

love that they will sub tofu for eggs in any of the omelets & scrambles free of charge!  they also have veggie sausage.  the b-fast burrito is super yummy.  they offer gilled tomatoes & black beans as sides, which is a nice change from just potatoes & toast.  the fruit cup is a little $$$, but yummy.

wish they had some kind of vegan pancake, waffle or pastry, though..

coffee is only so-so... I think their espresso is bitter.

beware: the wait can be long & there is very little space inside on a cold morning...

Big Portions = Worth it. I'm so glad I tried this place. I got the House-made Golden Gate Sausage and Spinach Scramble with
sautéed  red onions. I got mine well-cooked as I didn't feel like runny eggs that day (i know, i know :-p) and I was very pleased. Everything was just right - potatoes were nice and crispy, but not burnt at all (just nicely browned :D). The place is a little small but it's alright; not many people are awake 9am on a Saturday.

Friend got the popular Alameda and loved it. Portion sizes were again huge for that as well as the breakfast burrito. If you can't eat much, like me, be sure to bring a friend and share :).

If you're looking for a solid breakfast experience that won't break the bank, then this is the place. It's small and quaint, and everything one expects from a corner cafe in Berkeley. 

Everything I tried (scrambled eggs, french toast, potatoes, eggs benedict, strawberry mimosa) was good but nothing was extraordinary. The portions were a bit smaller than I expect at this type of establishment, but still enough for me. The service was great, though there was a short (ten minutes or so) wait to be seated.

This may become one of my favorite places to eat in town because, 
1. Close to campus
2. Pretty fast service!
3. The people working there were SUPER nice!
4. The decour of the place is pretty cute!
5. For a sucker like me who loves breakfast foods at any hour (yes, I am guilty of having eggs and pancakes for dinner, several times now), this place is great! (although, they're only open 'til 3pm... but, hey! breakfast for lunch is still great, too!)

Came here today, as an informal Easter get-together with my friends, and speaking for all of us, I must say that this place was great! The price ranges were about $8-15 or so, and they certainly had an array of breakfast options - leaving people like me very troubled with the important task of actually deciding what to order!

In the end, we had: the special- Mushrooms and Spinach scramble, Pigs in a Blanket, Grand Canyon Scramble, and sauteed mushroom & garlic tomatoes omellete! All of which, were soooo good! The "homefries" there were definitely great, with rosemary infused with the roasted and panfried potato-ey goodness! 

I'll definitely have to go back - not only to try the things on their regular menu, but to also see what their daily specials are! (Today, they had such great sounding things like Strawberry Mocha pancakes, Tiramisu French Toast....   all I can say is... DROOL.)

I ordered the Alameda and I enjoyed it. I hear mixed opinions about the Alameda because of the balsamic sauce that they generous put in the dish, but I wasn't bothered by it. Large portions, very flavorful. My friend ordered pigs in a blanket here (sausage wrapped with pancakes) and it definitely reminded my of chicken and waffles. Again, portion sizes were large. 

Breakfast here is a bit more expensive than at other places like Ann's Kitchen on Telegraph, but this is a cute place to go to, particularly early weekend mornings when the place isn't too packed. I don't know if I would come here if I were on a student budget, but for those working, this place is definitely worth trying out.

This place was so good, my parents and i had to come back the next morning for a repeat.

I really enjoyed the garlic tomato benedict..!

Servicepeople here obviously have to deal with a large volume of customers, and are good at it.  The cooks are working doubletime, and your food comes out very promptly.  No dishes were forgotten, and we got our coffee almost as soon as we sat down.  What nice people, too!

The bathroom could have been cleaner, but this is probably just me being a ridiculous stickler.  I could very clearly see they have a lot of folks coming through there on a weekend morning!!  I work in a cafe myself, and sometimes it's just not possible to get out from behind the counter..

Great homefries, perfectly done eggs, not too salty.   This may become a new haunt.

I've been here three times - two of which... let's just say that my judgments were a bit off considering that I was still recovering from a state of inebriety. Today wasn't one of those (un)fortunately. Haha. 

I ordered an Alameda sandwich. It's a french toast sandwich with mushrooms, ham, roasted tomatoes, and emmenthal cheese, topped with two eggs over-easy, Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction. It was food porn at its finest! The sandwich called out to me and seduced me. I was so enticed by it that I devoured this heart attack ravenously, resulting to a palatal orgasm. After I was done, I was gasping for air, breathing heavily. "I'll ravage you again next time," said I to what was left of it. Satisfied, I left with a smirk.

When a friend of mine took me to Sunny Side Café for breakfast/brunch, I wasn't expecting much. He told me to order scrambled eggs with bacon, and I thought that it was just going to be one of those undeniably gross breakfast meals with soggy scrambled eggs and extremely greasy bacon. BUT I WAS WRONG.

I ordered two eggs (scrambled), with a side of meat (apple wood smoked bacon). All egg dishes (except Mexican & Grand Canyon Scrambles) are served with toast, and your choice of home fries, garlic-roasted tomatoes, or vegetarian black beans. The times that I've been there I've chosen sourdough toast and home fries (sometimes the garlic-roasted tomatoes), and it all cost me $10.30, which isn't too bad since the quality of the food is soooo good.

All in all, I love the food there. The service is great, and the staff is really friendly! The portions are also generous, which you don't see too often at a breakfast/lunch place, so that's definitely a plus.
If there was anything I would pick on, it would be that the bacon was a little dry, but then again, that's just me.
Nevertheless, you will definitely find me at Sunny Side again!

Picture this: mushrooms, Hickory smoked ham, roasted tomatoes and emmenthal cheese, sandwiched between two pieces of savory French toast. Topped with two eggs over-easy, Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction. I can go on about how satisfying and decadent this meal is, but you should just go and experience it for yourself.

I'm sold on this place! LOVE it!

Food: 
-Avocado and Swiss Scramble: It was almost like an omelet but just messier. It was very tasty! Some places make it very oily, but this place didn't have that problem! It came with Toast and another side of either home fries, grilled tomatoes, or something else, but I picked grilled tomatoes and it was DELICIOUS! They seasoned it just right! YUMMY!

-Orange French Toast: Very interesting flavor of french toast! I really liked it! Not too oily, overly sweet or dry! I really liked it! 

Service: Cashier lady was really nice but there is basically no service. But the people that worked there were really nice!

Ambiance: LOVE it! It's cute and cozy! It's very small but they totally work it! There are a couple of booths downstairs that you can sit at and look out the window at people walking by on the sidewalk OR you can go upstairs to this private dining area. It's very quiet and nice! I went with a friend in the morning and no one was there so it was like we had the whole restaurant to ourselves! Everything was very clean and new! I had a great experience! 

Price: ~$10 an entree, maybe a little less. It's kinda a bit on the pricey side for a breakfast entree but it's very representative of the portions and quality they give you! 

Overall: I would definitely come again! LOVED the food, Service, Ambiance, EVERYTHING!

3.5 stars.

This place does not compare to La Note, but its still pretty good. The service is great, location is prime, decor cute, and the food surely comes in filling portions. You order at the register located just inside of the entrance, get a number, seat yourself, and they bring you your food. Despite how small this place looks, there were plenty of available seats -- outside seating, bar-like seating facing the kitchen, and a whole 2nd floor. 

We came at about 1pm; 2 of the 7 specials were already sold out. We opted for 'The Alameda: mushrooms, Golden Gate ham, roasted tomatoes, and emmenthal cheese, sandwiched between two pieces of savory French toast, topped with two eggs over-easy, Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction' and the 'Golden Gate Sausage and Spinach Scramble'. The Alameda is extremely HEARTY; if you can handle a big and hearty breakfast, than I'd recommend it.. especially with its nice addition of a balsamic reduction. The scramble was meh with huge chunks of salty sausage patties.. 

The price is on the verge of being high for food that is pretty much average.. nothing spectacular like you'd expect from an establishment like LaNote. Next time I'll opt for their french toast/pancakes and see how that compares.

I love Sunny Side.  In fact, I'd venture to say that it is my favorite brunch in the Bay Area.  Yes.  That is correct.  I usually go to the Albany location, but this week I decided to give the new Berkeley location a try.

My favorite dish of all time is the Pigs in a Blanket.  It is a delicious pancake wrapped around a sausage (in my case a vegan sausage).  If there is a special pancake that week, you can ask the to use it instead of a plain pancake.  Amazing.  

Aside from that, the weekly specials are amazing.  This week it was the winter veggie hash.  And there were also lemon and brown sugar pancakes. Wow.  Just wow.  And don't forget to get a special mimosa!

If you are vegan, you can substitute tofu for eggs in any dish.  How awesome is that?!  If you want to go that route, I recommend the Mexican scramble.  Mmmmmm.  It comes with delicious black beans.

This location isn't very big, but we didn't have too much of a wait getting a table on a Sunday.  I'm so glad they opened this location so that the students will come here instead of invading the Albany location.

Went for the first time about a week ago. I'd had an operation I had needed to fast for so I was hungry. The time being 2 o'clock, our favorite brunch spots were closed. Then we passed this gem. Open until 3, they serve breakfast all day - and I don't mean any ordinary breakfast. Amazing, unique stuff. If you want a gourmet brunch experience this is the place to go. The prices are also extremely reasonable and the staff are super friendly.

I was eagerly anticipating the opening of the new Sunny Side, mainly because I'm a fan of the Solano restaurant, but also because it is an incredibly short walk from both my apartment and my office. That said, I'm stoked to have a Sunny Side Cafe in Berkeley, but I think they have to work out a few bugs before they're up to the same level as the original. I've been something like half a dozen times since they opened, and the food is great, but ordering at the counter before taking a seat is really odd. Especially considering that the counter is about six feet from the door. If you're with a group, it's pretty easy to block the entry and it just makes the whole ordering process awkward. Everyone's really nice, though, and again, the food is excellent, but yeah, they need to get a couple servers in there and take orders...

I've come here several times now...and I must say it's quite delicious. I've only tried 2 dishes...my fav being the Bacon/Avocado/Cheese omelet...soooo scrumptious. The bacon is still crispy in the omelet and the avocado is ripe and yummy, with just the perfect amount of cheese. Their homefries are crispy and need just a tad more salt and pepper than what they season it with. Coffee is pretty good and they do come around to refill which is nice. Coffee and omelet cost just under $13, but you def get a full meal. This place would be a five-star if it was full on table service rather than this order at the counter then take a number thing they have going on, considering that the price is a bit on the high side for breakfast (in my opinion). I've also tried the Sausage/Spinach scramble...not a fan of cooked spinach, so that was my fault but the fresh eggs and sausage saved that dish. 

All in all it's a great place, however this won't become a frequent haunt, just when I'm in the mood for a really fresh and full breakfast, since it is a bit pricey for a college student. If you want something cheap and easy, try Ann's Soup Kitchen on Dwight and Tele...but if you don't want to feel quite so icky after breakfast (the cheap places tend to be the greasy ones), this is the place!

As I write this I am bursting at the seams with fullness.

It didn't take me long to decide that I wanted some eggs benedict since I had been craving some for awhile now. I ended up going with their Solano Benedict. It wasn't the best benedict I've ever eaten but it did the job of filling me up. The place is a little pricey for what you get but meh. Whatever. Their coffee is pretty good though.

NOM.

The breakfast grilled cheese sandwiches are delicious, not too heavy, and pretty quick (and $4.95).  My new Friday tradition is a morning ham, cheese, pear and cheese sandwich to see my through to the weekend.

It's a bummer they don't have wifi, but I understand - the place is tiny.

Ahh, what a cute little brunch place! I don't know how they do it, but their omelettes are amazing- the perfect mix of savory and buttery. Mmm! I ordered a ham & mushroom omelette, which was delicious and super filling- by the time I finally finished, I was completely stuffed! Given the price, the portions are completely suitable. Not sure if I'd be able to come here everyday, but I'd definitely love to drop by again next semester- so good!

I don't really get the hype about this place - maybe it's because I didn't order their Alameda special, but really, this place is nothing special.

I ordered something very simple: 2 scrambled eggs, which comes with your choice of toast (wheat for me), and house potatoes.

The eggs were normal, but the toast and potatoes were NOT good. The toast was as hard as a rock -- barely warm at all, and just way too hard to chew on. The potatoes were very mushy, barely burnt or cooked at all. I had to overdose my meal with Tabasco and Ketchup in order to eat half of my meal. 

For something worth $7.88, I expected a lot better. Disappointing, I really had faith in this one :/

THE best breakfast by far in the bay area.  yeah, i said it.  awesomely nice staff, fair prices, locally grown ingredients, and the chef is a genius with the specials menu that changes almost every day (and often has seasonal dishes too).

all i gotta say is go and order the ALAMEDA... the best breakfast you will ever have.  if you're not in the mood to eat something bigger than you are, then all of the benedicts are solid too.

When I first came here and saw the menu, I was like 'WTH. overpriced.' But there's a reason why the food here costs as much as La Note despite lacking in 'ambiance'. The portions are HUGE. Get the Alameda and something else (The Sweet Jalapeno Chicken Sandwich is decent.) with a friend and share. That breakfast specialty hasn't won awards and has been numerously recognized for no reason.  The Alameda has mushrooms, hickory smoked ham, roasted tomatoes and emmenthal cheese, sandwiched between two pieces of savory french toast.  Then it's topped with two eggs over-easy, hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction. WOWWWZZ. (Note: You should ask for the hollandaise and balsamic on the side. The flavors can get kind of overwhelming.) So when you're dying to be 150% full, come here for breakfast/brunch!

Clean. Delicious food and friendly staff. Nice fresh ingredients.
Close to campus.

This is the place to go for a weekend brunch and you don't want to wait at La Note for 45 minutes. 

I've been here twice even though I used to be in walking distance from this place. I feel like the places on Oxford next to Starbucks don't get as much attention as they should have. This place is small, has about 4 booths and bar seats, upstairs seating as well as outdoor seating. If you're a claustrophobe, you might feel a bit cramped in your seats. 

I've tried their Alameda and their Chickens-in-a-Blanket. Let's talk about their Alameda. If you have a hard time deciding on what kind of breakfast food to get, you can just choose this one. I've never seen this much breakfast meat, sides, carbs slapped into one dish. It is pretty much like a heart attack breakfast, with the heavy ingredients and large portions. I shared it with another and still feel full. There's definitely a lot of flavors, you have the eggs, the cheese, the french toasts, the meat, and it's also served in balsamic vinaigrette. What? Is? This? Yeah, that's The Alameda. It's definitely worth trying. Each bite is blasting with layers and layers of flavors. But I wouldn't recommend this as part of your daily breakfast, for the sake of your health.

Now onward to the Chickens-in-a-blanket. I wanted Pigs in a blanket, but felt like I should "try" to be healthy. I tried the chicken sausage option instead. It's two tiny sausages wrapped in some giant fluffy pancakes, served with eggs on the side. This is definitely a simple breakfast dish, not as flavorful as The Alameda, but you can enjoy that soft fluffy pancake. It's so fluffy!! I'm gonna die!!  

The prices are a bit on the expensive side, but then the portions are huge. Technically, you might be paying for La Note's prices, but you can definitely get more. The two are of different styles of breakfasts, but if you're getting brunch in Berkeley, might as well be a hipster and give this place a try.

I do not know why I never noticed Sunny Side Cafe on a street I've frequented for a while.

My very reliable friend suggested it because she had been meaning to check it out.

We were greeted quickly, casually like part restaurant part cafe.  We had ample time to check the menu and get a coffee warm up before I chased someone down to order. For sure I would do that somewhere else for some reason far different to have been made to wait at least ten to fifteen (or more) minutes to order.

The speed of the delivery of the food was inversely proportional to the time it took to take our order.  For this I almost forgot how long pahse one had take.  Speedy delivery to the table included, Sunny Side Cafe easily met and even exceeded my expectations.  A thoughtful menu with a many cool veggie and even vegan options - everything sub'ed for tofu - solid.

A bit quirky and a bit plain, Sunny Side Cafe was busy on a sunny Sunday on Solano Avenue, and rightfully so.

[End]

It had been such a long time since my last visit that I had to get the Alameda--which had made a HUGE impression on me--again! 

The Alameda is a French toast sandwich of mushrooms, smoked ham, roasted tomatoes, and Emmenthal cheese... topped with two over-easy eggs, Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction. It was just as satisfying as I remembered, but this time I found the balsamic taste to be too acidic. Perhaps it was because I was sharing the Alameda and a pancake with my fellow companion last time.

I also had a cup (+ free refills) of organic coffee to cut into the acidity of the balsamic reduction. 

The cafe is a cozy place to enjoy brunch with a dear friend. Be wary of potentially long lines during the fall/spring semesters at Berkeley; I tried coming here near the end of a semester and witnessed an enormous line of hungry folks (possibly the family and friends of graduating students).

Boo; tempted to go over to my Albany review (http://www.yelp.com/biz/the-sunny-side-cafe-albany?q=jun) and lower their stars too. 

I don't know if my palette has changed, but honestly, the Alameda, that I once loved so dearly was not good at all.

It was oversalted, the flavors were strange, it didn't meld.. and yeah, it was just no fun.  It was nothing like what I was looking forward to..

The atmosphere is nice and the service abruptly switches between brusque and kind.  I don't get it.

My friend S got the Grand Canyon scramble thing, and the beans that came with it were pretty salty.. and yes, I understand that it's "soft cooked" but honestly, it was kinda mealy and bleh for me.

Also, overpriced imo.

This is coming at you as the last thing I will write for Yelp before I take the California Bar Exam.  Well.  Maybe.  I might be able to squeeze in a few more reviews before Tuesday morning,  since, I'm suppose to be on hiatus from studying.  And study I did.  If you ever want to know what it's like to push a block of flesh through a wood chipper, just look at my brain.  And my face.  It's not pretty.  The stress?  The fear?  The loathing and self-hatred?  All of it shows on the outside.  And yeah, fear has a distinctive smell that I'm going to be trying to wash out of my hair for the rest of my life.

I came here on Sunday morning with the BF.  THE Sunday before the bar.  The final day of studying, 2 days before the exam starts, the edge of glory.  He's been very patient and understanding with my bar-induced tantrums, hissy fits, random crying, sudden freak outs and 0-to-100 hysteria.  Yes.  I said "HYSTERIA."  As in Mr. Freud's favorite topic.  

One look at the menu: pigs in a blanket.  Yes.  Pork product, carbs, the name describes it all.  It's comfort in a tube-shaped.  And it came with eggs.  Not too fond of eggs, have I told you?  I want to tell you what I like, because it's all going to end soon for me.  And I feel like we're familiar enough, in a long term relationship, that we should know what the other likes.  The eggs made the meal "value priced."  Because otherwise, would you spend $11 on 2 halves of a sausage wrapped in delicious, perfect, fluffy buttermilk pancakes with just a hint of sweetness, billowing texture and browned like a sand baby?  

The BF liked his Wildcat Benedict which is an Eggs Blackstone with a East Bay hippy twist.  Roasted tomato and bacon with a poached egg, home fries.  Sauce on the side.  He snarffed it down so quickly, I didn't even get a bite.  Then he ate all of my fluffy pancake that I meticulously and ridiculously pulled off my pig (I'm watching my caloric intake, and acting weird while doing it because I have no common sense anymore).  I thought the home fries were ok.  But it hurts to eat since I grind my teeth in my sleep.  Gnash them, like a howling mother bear.  And I've chewed up the insides of my cheeks.  Jaw clenching, teeth gnashing, shredded soft tissue.  I'm a flipping mess!

This place is very delicious and filling. I don't even think I ended up finishing all of my food. Their servings are pretty huge. I had the avocado cheese scramble and it was good. The place also came with your choice of bread, and awesome potatoes. The staff there were really nice as well. The meals are quite pricey though so I will definitely come back here again when I can afford it.

I've been meaning to check out The Sunny Side Cafe ever since they opened their new Berkeley location.  I've heard rave reviews for the Solano location so I figured this location would be just as awesome!

I think the reason why I'm writing a three star review is because of mis-ordering on my part.  They're pretty much known for their specials like the Alameda but I didn't want to order something that would instantly put me into a food coma when I got back to the office.  There was a strawberry pancake special on the board and I decided to opt for that.  Let me say that strawberries do not belong in pancake batter.  They end up becoming warm/hot mushy tasteless lumps within the pancakes.  Not so good...

On the more positive side I like the outdoor seating area on the sidewalk - great for a sunny day.

Will I be back....?  Perhaps, but probably not during the work week...  Or I might just check out the Solano location...

I was unimpressed the first time, but came here with my friend to give it another try. 

Ordered: 
-Pigs in a blanket
-Bacon, egg, cheese sandwich

Still unimpressed. The pancakes were a bit soggy. The sandwich had a good jalapeno spread and hearty slices of bacon, but tasted like something I could make at home. Tried the Alameda last time... HUGE PORTIONS but all I could taste was the balsamic sauce that they put on it. 

I don't think I'll be coming back.

What I had there:
an Alameda special
Blackberry white chocolate chip pancakes

Kind of pricey, but gives large portions. Alameda was pretty good. Next time, I want to try their egg benedicts, home fries, etc.

This is a great place to go for breakfast if you live and/or work and/or go to school in the UC campus area.  I wouldn't go out of my way to come here for breakfast based on the size of the place (itty bitty tiny tiny, but a very cool vertical design...great use of the space they do have!  Next time I'm sitting upstairs)  and the parking in the area (Berkeley parking near campus always...ALWAYS sucks). 

The ordering process has its pros and cons:  Awesome that they take cards, not so awesome that you have to order at the register.  I mean, I WANT the place to have a "sit down" feel rather than a "fast food" feel, but considering the student volume, It does make a lot of sense why they do it that way.  Not to mention I bet it makes the food come out way speedier.  (Speaking of...it wan't crowded, but the downstairs was full, and it wasn't too loud, which is a plus for a "I haven't had my coffee yet" breakfast.)

On the plus, its super close to BART and the Bus lines, and really great for meeting up with people...nice convenient location and easy to spot on foot.  This place has got a really nice vibe...again, if it weren't for the size, it would be a place that I would take out of town guests.  Reminds me of a few places I used to frequent in Eugene, OR.

Now for the food....WICKED AWESOME!  Everything could have used  more salt, but the way I figure it, it I'd rather salt it at my table than feel over-salted at the get-go.  I fell in LOVE with the potatoes, and my husband...the black beans.  Love the gratuitous use of avocado!  Also, the plates were nice and big so totally worth the $9 scramble!  I was totally impressed!  The quality seemed fresh, and they get Simifreddis (probably butchered the spelling on that one) Bread and Pastries in addition to their own house made muffins.  Next, I'm trying the Chicken Salad Sandwich....it looked too enticing to pass up! Oh yeah...almost forgot, the coffee was great AND they had Mimosas with fresh squeezed OJ...F*%K YEAH!

Totally going back again and again (after the dreaded 8am class) and recommending it to others, as it was recommended to me. 

In short:  awesome vibe, great location for students and employees in Downtown Berkeley, Great food (needs salt though).  Fresh food, fresh coffee, fresh OJ, takes cards, outside seating for those like us who always have their doggie around, AND friendly.  What's not to love?!?!

I guess we hit this place on a bad day.  We got there at about 9:30am on a Saturday morning to find out they were out of Buttermilk pancakes.  Say what?  How does a breakfast place "run out" of buttermilk pancakes early on a Saturday morning.  Is it just me, or do you send someone to the store to buy the ingredients so you can serve buttermilk pancakes for the weekend crowd?

So I went with the multi-grain cakes instead.  They weren't really my thing.  I had to send the first order back because the pancakes were burnt.  I also didn't care for the orange-infused syrup but didn't want to pay an additional $1.75 for the New England maple syrup, so I stuck with the orange-flavored syrup.  On a positive note, they did a good job on the bacon.  I asked for extra crispy and they were indeed extra crispy, just how I wanted them.  

My wife ordered eggs bennedict and one of her eggs was essentially a soft boiled egg as the yellow was just about fully cooked.  Service was a bit inattentive as my wife had to take her coffee mug downstairs to get a refill.

I thought the prices were high for a breakfast place.  My short stack of multigrain waffles (they add a $1 for the multi grain) and a side of bacon was $11.25.  Breakfast for 3 adults and one 4 year old came to just under $50.  I definitely didn't feel it was worth that kind of price.  For those prices, I'll go to Rick and Ann's and get better food and service.  For an everyday type breakfast, I'll head back to Sconehenge.

Day 1 of MWLAWMBF:
Oh a whim, my boyfriend and I decided to start our food and cultural journey here for almost a week. Breakfast is always needed to start out a nice day of - well I got my nails done and my boyfriend cleaned my room and watched tv shows. So maybe our first day together wasn't the most productive. 

Food:
Bacon, avocado and cheddar omelet - I thought this was well made. I've been on an omelet craving lately I guess, getting omelets when I go and get breakfast. It's nice though - eating breakfast and stuff. Pretty good from what I remember. Potatoes were decent, but I couldn't finish them.
Pigs-in-a-Blanket - At first my boyfriend was in love with the pancakes, but later, he didn't like them as much. It's a pretty good pancake and idea. Pancakes wrapped around sausage. YUM.

Overall, I had a nice time at Sunny Side Cafe. Pretty small location, but there is seating upstairs. Delicious food for the start of a great week!

OMG, it's HUGE!

...

[respectful break for those wishing to crack, "That's what she said."]

...

This was my reaction as my Classic Eggs Benedict dish arrived.  Not that the eggs were gargantuan or the English muffin was any larger than the average English muffin.  Rather, the large plate was filled mostly with homefries (not a complaint).
