This is a pretty low-key place, so I wasn't expecting perfectly poached eggs or frequent water glass refills.  Way to egg-ceed eggspectations, Sunny Side Cafe!   (Sorry, couldn't resist!)  

And that seemingly huge portion?  Finished it without a problem...unless you count lapsing into a food coma afterwards during class as a problem. Probably should have taken a cue from my friend who boxed up half of her dish.  Oops.

Last month, after a rousing bikram yoga class where J&I burned at least 700 calories each, we contemplated our brunch options near FDB. Gather too pricey and frankly, after my 2nd experience and 2nd $80 tab for two people, came to the conclusion food wasn't worth it though I love the decor. Venus on Shattuck is good but there is always a wait. J wanted coffee and didn't feel like Vik's Chaat, so we checked out Sunny Side near Gather.  We ate upstairs and ambiance pleasant. Service prompt. Food - omg - organic, local and I could request "vegan" without any additional charge. Today (our 2nd time eating at Sunny Side) we dined at the counter where there were Purse Hooks! Both times, I ordered the breakfast wrap with tofu instead of eggs and vegan. Comes with potatoes, black beans, spicy tomato salsa and wrapped in a tomatillo tortilla.  Portions are ENORMOUS. 

First time there was no line; 2nd time (today) there was a line but no wait for the counter. J&I enjoyed watching the cooks in the kitchen (organized and clean). 

J paid $28 including a 20% tip. This included 1 coffee, 1 Arnold Palmer, 1 Grand Canyon, 1 Breakfast wrap. 

I love the focus on local, organic, sustainable food.  There is even a flyer posted about the type of tuna they serve.

Decorations are homey but not cluttered. 

Servers are terrific. You order and pay at the counter and get a number.

Bring your appetite.

Parking: we found parking 2 blocks away fairly easily.

i would rate it a 3.5 

I was really excited to try the Alameda even though it was pretty expensive. Sadly they told me that they "were out" :( so sad. So I got the Classic eggs benedict. They told me they were out of Hollandaise sauce but I said it was fine since I was going to ask for it on the side anyways. Then when they brought out my food, they had the sauce on the side which made me skeptical about the Alameda being "out." Nevertheless, the eggs benedict was pretty good. It also came with shredded potatoes, hash brown style. Overall the portions werent that great;  I was able to finish everything but I didnt leave hungry. 

My friend got one of the omelets. The ingredients definitely tasted fresh and I liked the big chunks of red onions but I dont think it was worth the price. 

There werent that many places to sit and eat at this location. There were about 10 seats outside and three or four tables inside with benches. Luckily we were able to find seating though. 

I'll probably come back one day to try the Alameda.

i love when you want into a pretty regular looking breakfast place and get surprised with something like...oh yeah so we know mr. niman, of niman ranch, who has since left niman ranch and now he raises his own cows and hand feeds them herbs and flowers and only gives his meat to a select few restaurants. 

oh really? hell yes i would like to eat mr. niman's flower-fed cows. 

and oh my god. why can't we feed all cows flowers? the world would be such a happier place. sunny side took this amazing beef and put it into a brunch sandwich with roasted squash spread, raddichio, sourdough bread and two eggs over medium on top along with some hollandaise dressing. it won't be there long but if you can get it before it's gone, it will in fact blow your mind.  

we also had a delicious bacon, fontina and rainbow chard scramble. and they are generous with the bacon here my friends. 

we also had just about the nicest server in the world. the food came out quickly and hot. i'm super down with this place.

The Short:
Quaint little place with a great view and delicious food! My first 5-star review :D!

I'm a frequent visitor here because this place is simply awesome. Most of their ingredients are from local farms and they emphasize this in their menu items and daily specials-- a nice plus if you're into eco-friendly restaurants. More importantly, their food is downright tasty! I've had their Alameda (mushrooms, Hickory smoked ham, roasted tomatoes and emmenthal cheese, sandwiched between 2 slices of French toast all topped with two eggs over-easy, Hollandaise sauce, and a balsamic reduction) and its one monster of a meal. Its got a wonderful texture and packed with savory flavor. The emmenthal cheese really makes it creamy!  

I could go on talking about how good their pancakes, eggs, and To-Go sandwiches, but I'd recommend that you try it yourself!

Recommendations:
- Any French Toast
- The Alameda (a signature dish, very rich and filling!)
- Lemonade (Fresh squeezed with the perfect amount of sweetness)

Pros:
+ Delicious food and great menu variety.
+ Nicely made drinks (from the coffee to the lemonade)
+ Homely interior that has plenty of sunlight!
+ Tasty to-go sandwiches if you're looking for something nice for $5.

Cons:
- Slightly pricey, but you get great food for what you pay!

The food is really good.  The portions are a little bit small--and, thus, the prices are a little bit high--for my liking; but I'm not the fittest, healthiest person on the block, so maybe I need a little bit of portion control.  I really like the space, though I've only sat downstairs, so I can't really comment on the upstairs.  They've got a strange plastic canister of bay leaves that I'm sure they'll never exhaust.  I mean, how many recipes call for bay leaves?

I haven't used the restroom, so I don't know about the overall wheelchair accessibility, but there's only one table--and it's in a bad location--that a wheelchair user could sit at, so I doubt I would consider the place truly accessible.  I'm holding off on dinging that star, though, because I need positive proof.

They have sandwiches that are only available to go.  I might try one of those for lunch.  Until then, I'll probably only visit this place when my parents are in town.

I love their Alameda! It's french toast with eggs, ham, cheese, mushrooms, and hollandaise + balsamic sauce! This sounds and probably was super unhealthy, but it's also really filling, and I took at least half of it home. So spread across two meals, the calories count can't be too bad. :p

I also like that you pay first for your food, so it's easier to come with friends and not have to split the bill. However, it is a little on the pricey end for one meal, so I don't think I'd come that often. But no wait when I came in the  morning and lots of empty tables to study at while waiting for friends to arrive. :)

When...

... the world gets taken over by mutant cockroaches that eat everything else in sight

... radio waves no longer penetrate our atmosphere

... eggs become extinct

That's the day I will accept the tasteless breakfasts at The Sunny Side. "Today we'll be serving the Bland Benedict and Watery, Half-Cooked Scramble. Oh, what's that? You want some Weak OJ? Coming right up!"

I try and look past it: "Gee whiz, it's so clean. Is that a mimosa on the menu?! Wheeee. And what a great sun-filled mezzanine area! Plus the staff is so kind." But shelling out thirty bucks for counter service and mediocrity sans alky ain't fine by me.

Sweet Jesus.  If I could give Sunny Side 6 stars out of 5, I would!  Having seen impressive reviews from friends and fellow Yelpers alike, my bro and I decided to give this place a shot:

-The Alameda with Brie (weekend special tweener of their signature dish): O.M.G. this dish was MAD delicious!  The layers of flavors and textures from the french toast, eggs, ham, mushrooms, and brie were easily distinguishable yet came together seamlessly.  The creaminess of the hollandaise sauce also contrasted nicely with the balsamic reduction.  It's indeed on the heavy side, but hands-down worth every last morsel and penny.

-Carrot Cake Pineapple Pancakes: BEYOND AMAZING!  Of the numerous pancakes I've sampled in the Bay Area, NYC, and Boston, this was far and away the best I've had yet.  The cakes were huge, but thin at the same time.  More importantly though, they had an absolutely delightful, airy softness that made me say, "Mmm" with each successive bite =)

Might I also add that their coffee is fantastic with bold, velvety flavor and thick body.  And of course, the service was great with attentive staff, quick refills, and check-ins to see how we were doing.  

I sooo cannot wait to come here again and give their tasting menu a try.  As Joyce B. noted, brunch here really does brighten your day =D

If you're like me and love a good breakfast, then stop on in to this cute little spot and grab a meal that's made for champions...because face it, breakfast is amazing.

Although this place is very small, it's conveniently located by the Berkeley campus, there is indoor and outdoor seating, friendly staff, large and well priced menu, and if you don't want to stick around, you can order your food to go. It gets packed on the weekends, however if you come around 9am and beat the morning rush, you can snag a good seat indoors, perhaps even a booth.

I would highly recommend their home fries or vegetarian black beans as a side (both are delicious). I had the bacon, avocado, and cheese 3 egg omelet and wow was it filling, affordable, and very tasty! I would highly recommend it if that seems to tickle your fancy. Their bacon is cooked super well, crunchy yet soft and packed with flavor. Not sure where they get their bacon but I will say, it may be the best bacon I've eaten in Berkeley!

I would definitely come back again! Thank you for the tasty food and friendly service :)

This place is a gem.  It's pretty cute inside. they have a couple tables down by where you order and then they a little sort of loft above where there is more seating.  The place overall seems pretty small for the amount of people it attracts, but they offer to-go so thats probably really nice if you don't want to deal getting a table and being close to other people.

We ordered buttermilk pancakes, an omelet with avocado, cheddar cheese and I think bacon in it... Oh and a side of house-made sausage pattys.
The buttermilk pancakes were the best pancakes I can ever remember eating.  I tried the omelet and was immediately jealous that I didn't order it for myself.  It was amazing.  The sausage I didn't really like, but not at any fault of the cook or quality of meat.  I think it was only my personal taste preference.

I definitely recommend this place.

Oh shit. I forgot the size of the portions at this place so I totally overestimated, but at least now I have enough leftovers for a full meal. We had the chicken in a blanket, tilden benedict, and coconut french toast. I regret getting the coconut french toast because it was super dry. Believe me, it was huge and filling, an entire four thick slabs, but it was too dry and the shredded coconut was fried to a crisp as well. Plus, that's all you get. There's no side of anything other than a thin slice of orange. The chicken in a blanket was great. I loved the chicken apple sausages. It was not salty at all and the pancakes were done perfectly. It comes with a side of eggs and they did their sunny side up perfectly. The tilden benedict was great too. It came with a heap of homefries, but it wasn't as good as other homefries I've had. The iced tea was unsweetened, thankfully. The lemonade was quite sweet though. Anyway, it was still a great brunch on a hot sunny day. The service was great and we sat there forever. In total, it was about 40$

Yesterday I went out for brunch at Sunny Side with a friend who was leaving town that morning. I'd never been before, but I was highly underwhelmed with the meal. It was not as at all memorable and "meh" is the best description I have.

I ordered the Golden Gate Scramble with sausage, spinach and onions. it came with rye toast and home fries. It sounded promising at first, and it should have been for a $10 breakfast.

The portions were very generous, but the eggs were watery and flavorless. They hadn't been salted by the kitchen, but the vegetables inside were overcooked and the texture of the eggs was completely wrong. Additionally, my rye toast was only toasted on one side (not sure how that happens). The home fries were good, but it's pretty difficult to screw up potatoes...

I'll give it to them that the space is cute and the service is friendly, but the extremely underwhelming food will prevent me from going back.
Kimchi Gardens is a find!  If you want to have a little beer with your bibimbap, this is the place.

The food I have here is consistently bland and terrible. Once I ordered a bulgogi that was swimming in liquid (NOT a sauce, a liquid); the bulgogi was bland and terrible. I am also incredibly against having to bus my own table if I'm eating out (though that's just me).

The one redeeming quality Kimchi Garden has is its gigantic TV. If you're ever in the dining area by yourself you can watch whatever you want. While eating my Korean food I got to watch Paula Deen use a horrifying amount of butter in one of her cooking shows.

Not great, but not so bad that it deserved 2 stars. Not much in the way of service, you order at the counter, pick up your food at the window and bust your own table. BUT what I did like was that for $5, you get a huge order of Kim Bap (Korean sushi roll w/ veggies and beef), like at least 20 pieces if not more. 

Their seafood jajungmyeon was not very good though. The noodles were a little too chewy for my taste, the seafood was not too fresh, but the sauce was too bad though. So meh. 

Not sure if I'll ever be back for anything other than the Kim Bap.

Okay Korean food - this coming from Korean - and the serving sizes are generous. The food is basically Asian Ghetto quality (Asian Ghetto being the collective name for the restaurants in this area, although not all of it is Asian). 

But the only thing is the service. The food takes forever to make. So it you're looking for a quick bite, don't come. You need to dedicate at least 20 minutes to 30 minutes for food to come out.

People hate this place. Yet, I ventured in and was surprised both times.
I recommend the spicy pork for the skeptics, and the Seafood Kimbap is very good as well,

Other than the door bell going off from me walking in the door, the place was dead silent. I should have taken the ques from the silence. I was drawn to the pretty pictures of food on the wall and then memorized by the old rotary, wall phone near the register. The food, not memorable...but I've had worse.

Terrible food. Terrible service. Simply, just a terrible restaurant.
This place has no right to falsely show pictures of delicious looking food and serve dog food.

If you want Korean food, go to Bear Ramen or Crunch instead. Heck, I even recommend Steve's.

There are only two reasons to ever really come here. I find that this place is good for hosting events because the owner is liberal with alcohol policy and it is spacious. Secondly, you should come here if you have never been here before to see how bad it is. This only applies to people who know what Korean food is supposed to taste like.

Being its so close to the campus, I think owner is just not caring at all. Service is basically none existent, and food is okay at best. That is coming from a Korean. if someone else who are not familiar with Korean food comes here and try the food, I am afraid they may think thats how Korean food supposed to taste like.. well its not.

Me & the boyfriend wanted to stay in one night but we didn't want to cook (just one of those days) so we decided to grab some Korean from close by.  This was actually the 2nd time we went to Kimchi Garden; the first time we went they were closed...even though the doors were still wide open.

This time we went a lot earlier & got ourselves some decent food.  I ordered the BBQ ribs plate which had a lot of slices of short ribs that weren't too fatty or tough.  He got a Bibimbap which he enjoyed a lot.  On top of the entrées, we also liked the kimchi dishes that were made with spinach & tofu skin.

On top of the food, we really appreciated the service; even though we were ordering to go.  The owner (I guessed) invited us to sit down while we waited.  The other owner (?) packed up everything, brought it to our table & had a really warm smile on her face.  Loved it.

The food is not super duper but this is a good place to come to when you are having one of "those" days.

I ordered tofu soup to go and it was the worst tofu soup I've ever had in my life.  It was bland and watery.  I don't know if the tofu soup is better if you order it from a table in the restaurant.  So whatever you do, don't order tofu soup from here!
Kimchi Graden replaced Gomnaru with more expensive and crappier meat. The food here is crap, its not spicy and the ramen I'm pretty sure is from one of those instant ramen cups.

decent food and reasonably priced! i came in wanting something soup-y to eat and i walked around asian ghetto but none of the soups at thai basil looked good and bear ramen was all full, so i decided to make my way to kimchi garden. i ordered the chicken noodle, which i thought was a good deal at $4.99/bowl. it comes in a regular plastic white bowl, though, not one of those stoneware bowls that the picture shows. 

for $5 i got a very generous helping of soup, ramen, and chicken thigh meat. there were probably about 6 good-sized chunks of chicken thigh meat. i also got some broccoli, onion, cucumber/zuchinni, and carrots. i would've liked more veggies to balance out the carb/protein overload, but it's better than nothing. the noodles were pretty chewy, which i like, but it was all in a big clump. i derno if it's because i should've mixed and separated it up a bit or something, though. my dish also came with bean sprout and cabbage kimchi. the bean sprout was normal, but the cabbage one was a bit sour.

since i finished the soup before my noodles, the lady came to me and said i should try adding the hot paste. and i did. and it was good! the hot paste is a bit watered down though, maybe because they're being resourceful? the chef/owner was really nice when i asked for more bean sprouts though, he said if i could always get more bean sprouts if i wanted.

i've never tried the jajyungmyun, but it always seems to be the daily special. one friend said it wasn't great, and another friend said it was pretty good.

overall, the food was decent, the owners are really nice, and if you get their specials, they are cheaper than their neighbors.
Hi Kimchi Graden. I just wanna say don't put too much MSG please.

You get what you pay for. Kind of a whole in the wall. My friend brought me here since she knew about it.

We both got the bimbipap omg i don't know if i am spelling it correctly but it was only $8 and comes in a stone bowl. It was yummy. Wished it came with more side dishes but then again you get what you paid for.

Instant hangover cure. 

Friday night was slightly too fun, and as a result Saturday morning was less than ideal. Some sizzling spicy pork and a bowl of spicy beef, bean sprout, & egg soup was exactly what the doctor ordered. 

Apparently ownership recently changed, which came along with an improvement to the quality of the food, and luckily  the cheap prices were kept. 

Food came out quickly, it was satisfying, and it was exactly what I needed at the moment.

I like coming here to grab lunch. The restaurant is pretty big with a lot of seats. Their is a bit of wait during the lunch time rush, but you can sit and wait for your food. To go orders are nicely packed, and the people working are always friendly.

This place has all the usual fare for a Korean restaurant. The restaurant itself is ginormous and you can definitely bring your whole bevy of friends without worry. So indeed it lacks the atmosphere of a bustling eatery, but it's not all that bad. The service is good and you won't have to worry about getting the attention you need. Entrees come with a couple of side dishes. I would not recommend the bibimbap, but I'll vouch for the soondubu. It comes out hot like it's supposed to and it's just the type of comfort food one needs on a rainy day. It's not amazing food, but with prices like these, what can you say?

I'm always surprised how empty this place is. Its not super amazing food but it has a solid dine-in area, two TVs, a bathroom, good service, free coffee drink, one of the only places in Durant Food Court that accepts card, and is amazing for groups. 

I almost always get the spicy pork, because its a reasonable price and reasonable portions. I guess they don't have as many small dishes as other Korean restaurants (only kimchi, fish cake, and spiced radishes), but its better than the other nearby restaurants which have no small dishes at all. Recently, I think the spicy pork has been getting more bland, however. 

Food aside... last Friday we came here to watch the Olympics opening ceremony! I also watched one of the NBA finals games here before. If you don't have a TV at home, and you don't want some crappy stream quality, this is actually a great place to watch a game over some food. The owner is nice and will change the channel for a big event if you ask!

Meets the standards for the average college eatery. Generous portions of solid food for $7-8 per meal. Nothing to complain about! I liked my kimchi fried rice. I wasn't a huge fan of the ham--maybe spam?--in the rice but I liked that it was just the right spicy-ness level. Again, gigantic portions: food comes with miso soup, and three banchan of tofu, kimchi, and the tasty potato kind. I actually never really noticed Kimchi Garden, even though I've passed by it to go to Cafe Durant plenty of times. The dining room is really casual and pretty barren. Seems like a go-to spot for students to eat while studying or recharge after a studying marathon. I would come back again!

Honestly, I really like Kimchi Garden. I don't remember coming here before the owners changed, so I guess I can't really compare before & after. I've gotten kimbap, soft tofu, donkatsu, ddukboki, "udon" (which is really kal gook soo), soo jae bi, yook gye jang. I liked all of them. Donkatsu sauce is very interesting - not sure how to describe it, but it was a little hmm fruity? it was.. interesting, but it wasn't bad tasting at all. I really like getting yook gyejang and soojaebi here - both are always yummy! And the portions are pretty big, so I always end up having leftovers. Don't be afraid to drop by!

Staff wasn't super nice, food was sub par, and the wait felt like it was forever! I went in a group of 8 and there was at least a good 30 minutes between when the first person's food came and when the last person's food came. 

I ordered the stone pot bibimbap which was pretty plain., though very filling. The little cup of miso that came with it was cold and the kimchi was the worst I've ever had. We also ordered the seafood pancake (which we had to ask/remind them about towards the end of our meal) to share, which I do not recommend. 

We were lured in by the picture menu posted outside, but I don't see a return visit in the future. I have a feeling they won't be in business much longer unless they change the way the operate.

Never bothered coming here until recently because it's location was too far removed compared to the other restaurants of the Asian ghetto. Upon entry my first impression was a good one. Plenty of seating, clean, AND a TV. If you're dining in the Asian Ghetto and your restaurant has a large TV then you know you're dining in style. 

The food wasn't too bad and reminded me of the food from some tofu houses back home. The Omelet Fried Rice was awesome but kimchi fried rice was pretty standard. 

I think i'll be making more visits here due to the nice and clean atmosphere this place has.

When I was a freshman  the food was terrible. the service was extremely slow and the food was meh. They have new owners now and the food is a lot better. I have eaten the dwenjjang jjigae the kimchi jjigae as well as the bibimpab. i usually get those three. the rice and chapchae are not good at least not to me i wouldn't recommend that. They have free wifi which is really cool and a really big tv. overall the food is good. it's not the best but it's good. service is pretty decent and it's pretty cheap.

Kalbi, OB, Soju...off the hook.  Kalbi with an egg on top!  Nuff said.  Price point and value point beats any other Korean spot, bar none.  

Don't listen to the low reviews.  Those who gave it low reviews are high-maintenance and are pseudo-foodies...you don't know real food, nor have you ever felt how it really feels to be hungry.  

Stay spoiled but don't knock Kim Chee Garden.

I'm surprised at the poor overall rating; I personally love this place.

My favorite dish hands down is the Seafood Kimbap (Beef Kimbap is good too). Not that kimbap is anything super fancy, but you get at least 22 decently sized pieces for less than $6. A steal for any college student. I always try to save some for the next day, but end up eating it all because it's so addictive.

Their soups are nothing too special (like the Potato Sujebee or Tofu Stew); I'd rather go to Toust for those. This place is a really good alternative to Toust for Bibimbap and Kimchi Fried Rice, since Toust is pretty pricey.

They only have three or four people working in the kitchen, so when there are a lot of people there, it takes a long time to get your food. Other than that, this place is awesome. They have flat screen TVs so you can watch soccer or basketball games while you eat, and an endless supply of Korean coffee mix!

Ate their Korean Black Noodle (jjajangmyen) here. Nothing special.. the noodles weren't chewy(!). I've definitely had better noodles. One positive is that they have a nice and spacey eating area, good for large groups. Other than that.. food is mediocre, you can find better quality for the same price elsewhere.

Considering how I walk past this place all the time, I figured I should try it out. Ugh, not the business. I came here around 7pm, which is like the peak dinner hour, right? Uh, not for this place. A sign said "90 persons capacity" or something, but there was only one occupied table of 4 people. That should've been enough of a sign for me to gtfo, but of course I ignored it and didn't. 
Service: The food came in ~5 minutes, but then again it's not like they were busy so their speed wasn't all that impressive. 
Food: I didn't come into this place with high expectations or anything so I ordered the bibimbap bc I figured it'd be hard for them to mess that up. Boy was I wrong. The bibimbap was tasteless and I had to use a crapload of gochujang, which is the sweet & spicy, ketchup-looking sauce that they give you, just to eat it. This dish will fill you up, but not exactly leave you satisfied. It came with miso soup and 2 sides of panchan - kimchi and fish cake. Eh, whatever. 

Basically, come here if you are one a budget and ravenously hungry. Leave your expectations and desire for tasty food at the door or risk being highly disappointed.

Okay, let me preface this by saying that I only even ventured here because Toust, Berkel Berkel, AND Steve's were all closed.  I blame memorial day weekend/summer/berkeley.  Ugh.  Anyway...

The place was empty save for two korean guys yelling at the HUGE tv blasting some basketball game.  Um, sorry, is this a sports bar?  I ordered spicy chicken which tasted like the spiciness was trying desperately to mask the odor of rotten chicken.  I asked my dinner mate to taste it because I could feel the food poisoning coming over me as I ate.  Speaking of my dining companion, he ordered bibimbap and got some beef sushi rolls.  WHAT?!  No.  No, no, no.

I probably wouldn't even come here as a last resort again.  If the better places (read: every other Korean restaurant in a 50-mile radius) are closed, take it as a sign that the gods don't want you eating Korean food and trek across the street to House of Curries.
The staff is pretty nice especially if you initiate the taking with them, however the food is just Bad. Quality is Low, because most of their stuff is pre-cooked and microwaved when ordered... Lame.

Boohoo the korean students don't like the food here because they're parents cooked homemade Koreannmeal is better that right? 

Well, this place cannot live up to nice parents' cooked food forsure. but it's still a fairly okay restaurant. there are pretty good dishes for cheap prices.

you just have to get the right dishes i guess... but for me this place isnt too bad. i go there anyways lol

ok, we might have been spoiled by our delicious place in sf, and had super high expectations. food wasn't bad, but we were just disappointed. also we had a buzzkill that night, so that might have also led to this bad review.  i can't complain about the place at all, it's very college-y. laker game was on in the background, so i wasn't even paying attention to the lack of customers. 

portions are pretty big and everything comes with an egg, unlike some other korean places. although our dishes only cam with fish cake and one kimchi. sad. kimchi fried rice wasnt bad though.

honestly, i'm surprised at the low ratings. i love kimchi garden and come here every week (though a lot of that decision also has to do with how indecisive i am) and have tried almost everything on the menu.

the food is not mind-blowing, but at $7-$8 it's a pretty good deal because the servings are huge. the beef kimbap is good and definitely worth it. the soondubu soups are good on a cold day. not a fan of the kimchi fried rice though. it has a very mushy consistency and tastes sweet? i'd rather go to bear ramen for KFR.

the korean couple that works here is very nice and they always give me a little more extra food than usual. good place to come chill/study if you have large gaps in between classes.

this by far is the 2nd worst korean place ever. There were NO people at all and so I had a bad feeling about this place, but I had a monstrous craving for korean food. Sure the staff were nice, but the food wasn't what I expected. rice dishes came with rice, miso soup and kimchi, but since I ordered takeout there was no miso soup or rice bowel. No prices for drinks so I'd stay away to avoid being ripped off. They do have kimbap, BUT there is only beef and imitation crab. my kimchi bokumbap was alright, but just for kimchi bokumbap I'd sure as hell waste my gas for kimchi bokumbap at 99 chicken just for that.

Asian Ghetto is a safe place to eat with friends. When people get Thai, Chinese, or whateverr, I usually get Korean food from Bear Ramen or KIMCHI GARDEN! I love their Kimchi Fried Rice, Ton-Katsu, Kimchi chigae, bulgogi, jjajangmyeun, & their KIMBAP!! I tried a lot of their dishes & I liked them =) The food comes out fast && it tastes good for a reasonable price. ^^

Let's see. What can I say about this place. Average prices for okay portions though some portions are very large for the price (i.e., kimbap). However that depends on the  rice capacity of your stomach so kudos to you if you can consume all of that not so tasty dry rice and seaweed. They don't stuff the kimbap with as much wonderful goodies as I'm used to. 

It seems accommodating for large groups and I know a lot of clubs have socials here. 2 stars cuz they have a huge ass television screen that enabled me to watch the London 2012 Olympics while inflating my tummy with rice and water. I think I'd go back to watch tv.

Even my EMT instructor suggested I avoid this place, but on a random whim, I came in.
I got nice service. Food was fast. And it was really, really good. Go for anything vegetarian. That's what I did :)

Just an okay place. I always get the Soft Tofu soup, and it's served pretty well. I don't really like the small dishes that come with it though - they don't taste anything like what kimchi should taste like (I don't know what the other small dish side item is called)!

Pretty interesting how they have a giant tv in the corner, so the upside is that you can watch TV sometimes. I am still against having to bus my own plates away when eating out, so minus points there.

I get beef kimbap all the time with korean hot sauce

kimbap's pretty reasonable for its portion

but other menu's are kinda pricy for poor students like myself

they have huge space inside with huge tvs

I wish I could give this place a higher rating because the staff was so nice. Unfortunately, the food is just sub par and takes too long to produce compared with other Korean joints in the area.

+ Nice staff (Kim and Fred are super nice)
+ Spacious: lots of big tables AND they have a big screen!
-  Food is bland: complementary kimchi lacks spicy and flavor
-  Limited menu; costs more here to change certain things (like adding rice cake than at other similar places)

Final Call:
The couple can make this place a hit if they stick with a traditional menu and not overcook stuff. One lifeline used!

********************
Munchies
1. Vegetable ramen
     -  Couldn't taste the veggies; bilked on the ramen too!
2. Rice cake
     -  Gravy had no flavor to it, which is key to this dish!
If you want greasy noodles with way too much salt, ddukbbogi that has no spice, this is the place for you.  Plain and simple - disgusting food that I had to throw away.

I wish I can give it no stars.  Sure the staff is somewhat nice, but that's about the only decent thing you are going to get here.  I don't know how they stay in business.  I seriously think they need to either start cooking better food or close the place.

I ate at kimchi garden last night, and left very satified. The place was empty as usual, but I think that's mostly because the restaurant is kind of hidden, not because the food is bad. I ordered two things, the Egg ramyeon and the kim bap (which comes with like 20 pieces!) and my total was only $10! Also I got a soup and 2 sides for free. I think the food is tasty and the portions are generous. Sometimes you have to watch when they ring you up though, I've been overcharged a few times...depending on who the cashier is.  But whenever I'm in Berkeley and I'm craving korean food, this is the place I go!

Honestly, it's not bad at all. The place felt like a ghost town; then again, it was before noon. My friends and I ordered the following:

Kimchi bokumbap (fried rice)
Kimbap (looks like a sushi roll)
Sundooboo (soft tofu soup)

Each one was decent. The kimbap was an especially large portion; they served 3 big rolls to my friend, and it only cost $5.50. We all agreed that we'd come back in the future for lunch. The fish cake banchan was delicious, but I was not a fan of the kimchi (it's a different style than what's usually served). Try it sometime, you might be surprised.

worst bi bin neng myun EVER.

WORST.

I always get the Tofu Stew here, sooo good.

I'd also highly recommend the spicy pork.

Overall: really good prices and big portions.

Not so good. We wandered in for a bite after a bike ride... the giant cafeteria-style arrangement wasn't such a big deal, and the staff is perfectly friendly. But the food is really not good. The sauce on the sizzling beef tasted like hamburger helper. The pork I had was coated with some sort of seasoning - but it was hard to get around the strange texture to enjoy what I was eating. Sadness.

I'll give it an extra star (originally 1 star) for its massive seating areas. This location has so much potential, yet all it has been over the past several years is Korean restaurant after Korean restaurant. By Korean restaurant, I don't mean an actual Korean restaurant; I mean a Korean-owned restaurant that serves "Korean" food to students looking for a cheap bite.

That's really all it is; it's a cheap meal. It will definitely fill you up and you'll leave feeling full, but the wait for the food is long and you do have to get your own food from the service window and subsequently bus your own table.

Maybe you can come here if you and a large group of people need a last minute group dinner/lunch location, as there will ALWAYS be plenty of seating space, but I definitely would not make this a default for the daily "What should I eat today?" conundrums.

The inside of kimchi garden is actually extremely large. Lots of open seating and an extremely large TV. Fairly clean and not noisy at all. There is also free wifi, so coming here to do work is fairly viable.

The beef kim bap is my favorite dish here. Only $5.50 and comes in 3 giant rolls so it's great for lunch or a smaller dinner. The free kimchi is actually pretty good unlike Steve's Korean bbq or other places catered to college students.
For the price, this place is good. $6 for bimbimbap with soup, salad and unlimited tea. I thought it was respectable.

4 stars for being open late on a Friday night!

2 for sub-par Mushroom Soft Tofu Soup. Granted, this is my first encounter with Korean tofu soup in Berkeley, but oh my god the restaurants in LA do so much better. 

REAL mushroom tofu soup has more variety in fungi than your cheap white button mushrooms. It comes in a stone pot hot enough to actually almost cook the egg that gets cracked into it. The liquid inside the soup is not so thin it resembles more of a broth than a stew.

I may come back again, but only because it is open so late.

(Also, because they have sake.)

Remarkable large place especially in the asian ghetto. The food was okay, nothing to rant and rave about because I ordered the bbq beef and it came with nothing but bone, so it was hard to eat. But the place is nice, clean and the service was fast. Once you finish, you just throw your tray near the kitchen, which if you weren't a regular, you wouldn't know or figure out. Come here when everywhere is busy during lunch time. The prices were okay

The food took a long time to come out.  I've had the bulgogi here, and it wasn't very good.  I had to cover the bland vegetables with loads and loads of chili paste.  I really love Korean food, but I don't think I would ever go back to this place.  

Did I also mention that the food is extremely overpriced?

Kimchi Garden used to have a really bad rap when I was a freshman so it took me around two years to finally get around to trying it (around when they got new owners, I think, and the food got a lot better).

Get the beef kimbap (!! my favorite), ddukbokgi (way less sweet than Espresso which is precisely why I like it), donkatsu, and bibimbap. Can't vouch for any of the other dishes - it's pretty hit or miss here.

I'm giving this place 4 stars solely for the beef kimbap.  I must admit that I haven't tried anything else, but if you order the kimbap, you won't be disappointed!  They give you two rolls plus a small side of kimchi and fishcake for $5.98 (I know, sad.  Don't judge me.)  Takes about 15-20 mins if ordering to go, but I like how they give you a fork, spoon, AND chopsticks + napkin.

Never again will I order kimbap from Tako Sushi!
Nice place. I generally get the BIm Bim Bap, with Tofu, and it's great. I love it.

If I could give this place less than one star, I would.

I ordered the Hot Beef Stew. My food came out 20 minutes after my friends' plates came out. The guy muttered a half-hearted sorry to me.

The food tasted like absolute shit. My beef stew was a glop of bean sprouts, frozen beef, and old onions boiled together with some Jin Ramen flavoring. This shit probably cost them 50 cents to make. 

The best part about my meal was the rice. The kimchi sucked, and so did the pathetic little side dishes that came with it.

Never coming back.

Really, I say it's 2.5 stars but it's seriously not as bad as people say it is so I'm giving it a 3. 

The place has nice, comfortable seating...very big and I'd say it's pretty clean. Serious kudos for large party groups. 

Anyway, I ordered their nengmyun (cold buck-wheat noodle soup) and I was surprised at how biggggggggg their portion size was! But when I looked at it, I was kinda disappointed with the amount of noodles they actually gave me...serving portion was not proportional with the bowl! :( They also only gave me 2 "slices" of beef which wasn't cut thinly like how beefs should be served in nengmyun...kinda like small slabs of 'em. 

But overall, it really wasn't that bad. Yeah, of course I had better, but it wasn't so terrible that I'd never go back again.

The service here is somewhat slow and in terms of portion size, Steve's is a better value.  An old korean couple makes the food, which gives you the comfort of knowing its more authentic than steve's.  Still, it's cash only and I've had much better korean food in LA.  For a starving college student though- by all means give it a try.
Soft tofu soup is goood!!!

Their foods are GROSS, however, the place is spacious and you can enjoy watching a big TV.
So I would recommend this place to anyone who wants to have some Korean booze and food with buddies in a quiet setting.
I hope the owner of T-toust will take over this place, so I can get a much better food in a better setting.

Now the food at Kimchi Garden isn't the best I've had (in fact, I have a pretty high benchmark since I grew up in K-Town LA yo!). 

You must be questioning, why do I rate this place so high. One word, PRESENTATION. For a lower-end "asian ghetto" type vibe, Kimchi Garden presents itself very well with adequate service and a friendly environment (at least through my experience). 

This is the kind of place where you can listen to kpop, with some friends, at a birthday, with the Laker's winning the NBA Championship on that big "freaking" screen TV they have, all while enjoying some good ole' home cookin' "Seoul" Food folks. 

If you want a friendly and pleasing environment, eat here.

I don't get why this place gets such a bad rep. I totally love this restaurant. No one is ever there, you get the whole place to yourself and there is huge TV which you get to control and watch cable TV.

I like the food too. Sometimes it's a hit or a miss with how salty it turns out but I think it's really delicious. One time, I was curious about something on the menu so they brought up half portion of that food with my main dish for free. They're nice.

And I'm telling you, I love that TV! It's a good place to come and talk with your friends, it's never too loud and you can watch your trashy reality while you're at it.

Yay!

I'd avoided coming here because my mother makes excellent Korean food and I knew eating Korean food anywhere else would be a definite letdown. However, my friends wanted to eat here so we came.

Environment:
-Stained, boring walls, no exciting colors anywhere. It almost felt like an office space. There were, however, 2 flat screen TVs in side the restaurant that made looking anywhere seem slightly more interesting.

Service:
-Incredibly slow. I ordered a simple comfort food that normally would take anyone a maximum of 10 minutes to cook, but I ended up waiting there for around 35 minutes.

Food:
-I ordered a Kimchi fried rice that came with complimentary fish cake, mook, and kimchi. The fried rice had a dry, overcooked, sunny side up fried egg on top of it. The fried rice itself had a mixture of kimchi, spam (or so I think... there was a very meager amount of it) and rice. The dish itself tasted funny. It almost seemed as if they put a large amount of sugar into the kimchi fried rice. Or it might just have been the msg. Pathetic that restaurants feel the need to use msg to make their dishes taste "better." 

Verdict: Appalling. Absolutely appalling. This is my only one star review.

I've had very few bad experiences at Korean restaurants, but I have to wonder why this is a local favorite unless it's for convenience.  Although it's decently priced, the potato sujubee noodle soup, seafood pancake and kimbap were all mediocre because of a bland taste and lack of texture.  Perhaps I should try the traditional dishes before I judge it.

Service was friendly, but they forgot to put meat in my kimbap despite repeating it twice due to a request to clarify my preference.  The decor and ambiance is simple and spacious with large plasma screens to watch sports.  Parking is tough on the street, but there are public garages nearby.

Second review since I'm still getting the hang of Yelp, but really! I don't see what's so completely bad about this place now. I remember trying it out in freshman year, about three years ago, and found the place to be pretty bad in terms of food and price. Never went again afterwards, having that etched into my freshman mind. For such an ideal location, I thought it was a waste of a spot and poor example of good authentic Korean food then. :(

But I went back about three weeks ago and was really surprised! Heard that they changed owners a while ago, so  maybe that's why it's so different from what I remember then. 

(1)  Their portions are huuuuge. From what I remember in freshman year, they were definitely not that generous with their portions. I stared at my meal a good ten seconds or so cause I wasn't sure how to eat it all in that one sitting. 

(2) The taste of the dishes really weren't that bad. Maybe it's because of the food I ordered with my groups of friends, but they certainly weren't disappointing. I got the Omurice then actually and tried a bit of my friends' Pork Bulgogi and Sujebi. Omurice you really can make yourself at home, but the PB and Sujebi were pretty okay. Honestly, I wasn't too impressed then, but noted in my mind that it wasn't as bad as I remember. The next time I went (last week) I got the Tonkatsu, while my friends got the BoolGalbi and Sujebi again. Jesuschrist was the tonkatsu enormous! That was the plate I had to stare at for ten seconds. I came with two guys and they couldn't even finish their own meals. Speaking of which, the galbi is actually pretty bomb. That was -the- dish that made me realize, wow, they really did get better. I actually ordered that today too when I went there for a meeting with my fellowship, haha.

(3) Price! Pretty cheap compared to other Korean restaurants in the area. And considering how much food they actually give you, definitely worth your money. Seriously. 

Didn't think I'd write this long of a review, but honestly, re-check it out! I think it's worth to at least give them another chance. Especially if some of you guys are leaving Berkeley soon like me. :)

I've been here as a freshman and I've never gone back since. Their food may not be that pricey for the portion, but I don't know so much about the quality. Also, they had a huge mix up with my credit card and charged me twice. Then they said they couldn't cancel it because their machine wasn't working, and told me to wait a month. Eventually got the reimbursement, but still wasn't the best experience. (I paid like $50 because I went with family!)

I've given Kimchi Garden so many tries, but I really do think it's just A-OK. You can't really leave here with your mind blown of how good the food is.

I've tried the soft tofu soup multiple times, and tried to be adventurous with the japchae bap. No and no.

 The food is cheap, however. The soft tofu soup and japchae bap are both in the $6-7 range - for BBQ beef items, pricey at ~$10. 

What IS good here? The kimbap and the potstickers. My sorority always has an event here in the fall, and the kimbap and the potstickers are always very satisfying.

So the people who operate the joint are super duper nice. Unfortunately, no one at Kimchi Garden seems to know how to cook. I returned here for the first time since the lone previous visit the year before, when KG opened. They had (and still have) a chia jiang myun special for cheap, so I ordered that the last time and had not been inspired to return since.

My reluctant decision to retry this restaurant was an ill-fated one. The beef hot soup is absolutely inedible. It's not cool but forgivable that they seem to make the soup base with ramen flavoring, which I find alarmingly to be the norm around here. It's surprising and disheartening that there isn't any gosari (aka fernbrake, or a type of fern weed that that stinks when boiled but has an indescribable texture and flavor that is essential to the soup). It's infuriating that the soup was not spicy at all as promised by its moniker, but It wasn't enough to make me put my spoon down. But there was piles of horribly old, gristly beef in the soup and not much else that flavored the broth--that is unacceptable, appalling, horrifying. A few pieces even had the silvery sheen that tells you to stay far away. This meat came from the trimmings of some cut, you could tell, because each pair of small triangles of meat was enrobed and coupled in fat. I just couldn't get past the flavor of that meat in the soup, and had to put my spoon down after four tries.

O., being the kind of "vegetarian" that eats around meat, has no problem with broth, and took over. Maybe because he doesn't know what meat really tastes like, he didn't have much of a problem with it. Maybe I'm just a spoiled brat, I wondered out loud, which O. did not immediately, vehemently deny. Whatever-- I know my Korean food, and that was not even food.

O.'s kimchi stew was edible but unspectacular, but I was surprised to taste pretty tender, good-quality pork in there, as well as a few rogue cubes of Spam-like meat. Our side order of jap chae, though heavily overcooked and overseasoned, was the most edible thing, especially with some rice to dilute it all.

So do I miss Gomnaru? Maybe just a smidge. I wish well of the owners of this restaurant, but the meal I had tonight at Kimchi Garden has officially been bumped up as my worst ever in Berkeley. NEVER again.

The location has changed names 3 times in the last 4 years and it serves the same food except now it cost a little bit more and they take a little longer to cook it.

Food is mediocre, portions are big. Nothing too traditional, just basic korean food.

The giant big screen TV inside has lasted through all the owners. Cheers to the TV.

I think this place used to be Gomnaru.  Whether it's owned by the same people remains a mystery.  

A dining companion and I where craving Korean, but too lazy to bike to Sahn Maru in Oakland (and also too lazy to walk a couple blocks further to Koryo..it was HOT ok?!) so we settled for this place.

1) Place your order at the counter from a menu on the wall.
2) Get your order stub and take a seat in the dining area.
3) Wait...and wait...and wait for your food.

The seafood pancake appetizer was probably the best thing about the meal.  Though there wasn't much evidence of seafood, the bottom was nice and crispy.  The seafood soft tofu soup was bland, and the only evidence of seafood was a single octopus tentacle hidden beneath some tofu.  My friend's ja jang myun was very funky tasting with odd little bits of potato.  I dunno how the Koreans do zha jiang mien, but it sure doesn't taste like the Chinese version.  

I think the saddest part was that the meal did not include banchan.  I received a little dish of kim chi and julienned potatoes- neither were good.  

I would like to advise those who are craving Korean food to learn from my mistake.  Walk a little further, spend a dollar more, and get some decent Korean food.  Now excuse me while I try to get rid of this MSG dry mouth.

Good portion and price, need i say more?  the food was good too.  i went on a tuesday night and we were the only ones in the place, it was kinda cool i enjoyed the peace and quiet.  im coming back.  save me a seat.

The food is not that great, but I've never had anything terrible. (okay, the jjangmyun is pretty bad)

Compared to most places in berkeley, kimchi garden is huge. Problem is, I've never seen more than 2 tables occupied any time I've gone there. I feel so bad for the nice old Korean folks who run this restaurant.  

This is why I keep coming back. 
A tiny part of me thinks that I can single-handedly keep this place open by dropping by every week with a new friend alongside me. 
I'm hoping to convert them to my cause of keeping kimchi garden in business, and maybe once they start having more customers, they'll be able to hire better cooks? 

I feel like I'm helping them by being a customer and when you feel good about yourself, food tastes better. 

go and support.

I've came here twice.
First time to celebrate a friend's birthday.
Second time was because Toust (another Korean restaurant) was closed.

I must say that this restaurant holds the notorious title of LONGEST WAIT ever for my meal. I just keep waiting and waiting...only to see that people who ordered after me get their food first O_o...and then wait some more.

First time I had some pancake thingy.
Second time I had fish covered with some sauce and rice.
..Shows how memorable it was. -_-

I'd recommand Toust just down the street on Durant (in Sather Lane I believe)

I don't think this place is TERRIBLE, but it's nothing special. The Korean BBQ ribs and BBQ beef are pretty good compared to BBQ Steve's in the Asian ghetto. I usually only order the beef and ribs and they've always been pretty good but I can't say anything about the other dishes. A bit pricey but if you're looking for a hot meal, not a bad place to stop.

I love Kimchi Garden and maybe it's because I only stick with two items on the menu. These items - kimchi fried rice and kimbap - are consistently delicious. While I do agree that the wait time is slow, I think the food is worth the wait (although generally arriving at 11:30am seems to yield the fastest cooking time in my experience, which is after they open so they have time to prep and before the rush comes in). The kimchi fried rice is so good; I honestly think it's the best kimchi fried rice. I like how the rice clumps together, the spice level is great, and the satisfying taste of kimchi (that is not too sour), spam, sesame oil, and gochujang make this the perfect comfort food. I must have eaten kimchi fried rice every week for an entire semester...consistently good. When I don't order kimchi fried rice, I'll have the kimbap. The orders are huge...you get about 20 roles for $5. The rice is always soft, the sesame oil flavor is great, and the meat to veggie to radish ratio is always to my liking. I prefer the beef kimbap over the seafood kimbap and I find that 1 order is enough to last two meals or if I eat it all in one setting (which has happened before), I'm tied over for the entire day. The downside is that the owner is quite unfriendly...even though I've been there multiple times and very consistently throughout the last school year and a few times over the summer (and once this semester), he refuses to acknowledge me or make conversation with me. I've tried to talk to him in Mandarin and Korean as well...but I guess he's just not that interested. Oh well, I'm giving Kimchi Garden a good review anyways because when I crave kimchi fried rice or kimbap, this is the place I go and it satisfies me every time.

This place is great! I know people complain about the time, and that is a slight issue...but it doesn't make the food any less great!

The place is huge with big TV and good for group gatherings (also a private area). Also, the food is so authentic and they make it fresh (so it takes a pretty long time). I always get the kim bap (it's $5.95 after taxes) and they give you a GENEROUS PORTION! The ddukbokkie is the only one I didn't like as much, but their bulgolgi and hot plates are just TDF.

So, definitely not one of the better Korean restaurants I've had... but, the food is DECENT, and it's such a great price, I shouldn't be complaining. 

Currently (Oct 2010), they have an amazing deal where you can pick between dukbokki/seafood pancake/and something else + BBQ chicken/spicy chicken/pork + soju for about $20 + tax. They even sometimes throw in a free ramen when you order the deal. I mean, how amazing is this pricing?!

The service is pretty n/a, because you order at the counter and pick up your own food. The size of the restaurant is pretty good for big groups/parties (unlike all the restaurants around the area).

Okay, I miss gommaru. Why did they have to change owners?

This place actually tastes pretty good because I like the soup. However, when I was going through my pescatarian phase, they did the unmentionable thing and added pork to my tofu soup. I SPECIFICALLY ASKED IF IT'S ONLY SEAFOOD and the lady said yes. Well, of course, when I was busy chowing down, I discovered pieces of flesh. 

I just left and didn't even finish my soup! I figured, why bother reasoning with the owners when they can barely speak English? If they didn't understand me the first time, why would they the second time? There goes $7 down the drain.

My friend keeps screaming to me "GIVE THEM TWO!! Just give them TWO!!" because he feels bad and thinks that if I give one star Kimchi Garden will go out of business.

...

GOOD.

Hellllllaaaaaaaa nasty ass chia jiang myun. 
It's disgusting. 

The other stuff looks, at least, edible. Gross ass chia jiang myun. go away from me.

I know there isn't really any good Korean food in Berkeley. Nothing quite like the hometown where the local kids will say you can rate a restaurant's Korean food by the number of Ahjussi dressed in golfing apparel. For a non korean, Gomnaru was bearable just ordering soondubu. Now it's not even that great and the price went up as well. The couple that works here is really nice and they give large groups free food, but even then Berkel Berkel is better here.

Alright after a long Yelp review hiatus we come across to the grand opening of this Korean spot called Kimchi Garden.

The people who were accompanying me in the vicinity were as follows: Christine L., Shirley (Christine's friend), and Jake (my friend). We entered the premises and it is small and quaint. Nothing fancy, what made things sort of different is you have to place your order at the counter prior to being seated (Korean McDonalds anyone?). As we were seated, the atmosphere seemed a bit quiet. However there is an HDTV blasting with sports on.

Awaiting for our food, we all decided to have a conversation about the infamous Cal Game going on that way. Shirley was moping, I didn't care and neither did Christine and Jake. After some more banter, within a span of 20 minutes the food arrived. I ordered bulgogi (beef dish) and so did Shirley. Christine ordered her pork dish, while Jake ordered the ribs. Nobody complained about the food, but it was decent.

But the one thing that made the experience all the better, is the conversations we had. The topics ranged from adventures in Santa Barbara, Dorks (the actual thing, not the cliche), and lastly the comparison between Science Majors and Business Majors. Good times...good times indeed.

I'm usually not that good with spicy foods. Picture an Asian girl, hyperventilating & crying uncontrollably, and you'll understand. Nonetheless, yesterday was my first time diving into the deep end of the kiddy pool- I got kimchi fried rice! :D

But other than losing my spice-virginity (yes, I realize how weird that sounds), I was a bit disappointed with Kimchi Garden this time! I went with a group of 6-7 friends on a Wednesday night and it was pretty crowded. In other words, it took almost half an hour to get our food! One of our friends picked up dinner from somewhere else; he ended up finishing ling before we had even gotten our food!

Kimchi Garden, your food and portions aren't bad but, man, could you be any slower...?

I went into the guy's restroom here accidentally once. The BBQ short ribs came out sizzlin' hot. You know your food is good when it starts talking to you. 

Everything else is just so-so, what do you expect from a place right next to a food court?

The lady that owns the place is real nice though! She acts like she's my really friendly aunt whenever I come to eat & read a book :).
Champong was surprisingly good! Chewy noodles with lots of veggies in spicy broth. Perfect on a cold day.

Cuz the other korean place was bereft of empty seats, i ended up here.
at Kimchi garden, you order and pay at the counter. they bring the food to your table when it's ready. . there are about 20 entrees to choose from, the usual fare for korean eats.

flatscreen: food channel

sampling: seafood soft tofu(6.50)
-came boiling hot, nice fresh soft tofu with bits of mussel, shrimps. oysters, and clams. flavoring was msg, chilies, and or seafood msg mix.
-ordered mild, came a little spciy, can see chili flakes.
-2 banchan, kimchi and a gluten something was ok.
-bowl of lukewarm rice.

banchan:
-courteous service
-mostly self serve here
-prices cheap and the food reflects it.

It's rough here on the outside -- it's dirty, busy and people are asking you for money.  But this is Berkeley, so how much are you going to let it bother you?  Inside the shops, there's Italian food, Chinese food, Korean food, Japanese food, Thai food, Vietnamese food, donuts and bubble tea.  There's Indian and Mexican food across the street, and hot dog and burger joints nearby.  I find that pretty exciting for a small city square.  Most places don't take credit / ATM cards or have a minimum purchase, but the trade off is that they're generally inexpensive eateries, they're open into the dark of night and they're good.  I've had some of my best meals here.
Thai Basil and Gypsy's kept me fed during midterms and finals.  This place is conveniently located here campus and the dorms.  College kid budget friendly.

Pro

open late
variety of food available
Seating indoor and outdoor
some (note some, not all) cheap options - college budget friendly

Con
all the smelly ghetto homeless people that hang out by the place
no public bathroom
some of the restaurants are not exactly clean
average prices have been rising fast - and no longer 'ghetto'

Super popular food court a block away from the south side of campus. Everyone comes here when they don't have another place in mind immediately. It's the place you automatically walk to with a group of indecisive people.

With that said, Asian Ghetto has, surprisingly, some of the better tasting food near Berkeley. Note I didn't say "healthy"...most of it is pretty oily, greasy, laden with calories. But that's just what college students need, right?

It's not all Asian food, but the Asian food here is what most people come for. A lot of them offer free water/tea too.

My favorites are:
Viet Nam Village -- despite the name, this place has great and fast Chinese food...the owner is really nice and will bring your food out to you if you're waiting outside. I've only ever sat down to eat inside here once. My favorite dishes here are beef chow fun, crispy noodle with shrimp, and scrambled eggs over rice with shrimp. Cash only.

Bear Ramen -- delicious Korean food made by a really nice ajuma. My favorites here are ddeok ramen, kimchi fried rice, ddeokbokki, curry rice, and seafood pancakes. Actually, I don't think you could really go wrong with anything here. Cash only.

Thai Basil -- this is a favorite of many people. I like their pad see ew and their satay chicken. They have good specials too. Credit card or cash.

Gypsy's -- Italian food, the only thing I really like here is the seafood angel hair pasta. The garlic bread is amazing b/c it's actually a roasted piece of garlic that you can spread on the bread...mmmm. Credit card of cash.

King Pin Donuts -- awesome selection of donuts, what more could you say? As one of the first shops in the Asian Ghetto, it's hard to resist that smell of fresh donuts as you walk by...

Sweetheart Cafe -- has always been a staple for boba. Moccacino on the other side (along Bancroft) is a good competitor. Quickly's (also in Asian Ghetto) is subpar, but they do have black sesame milk tea, which the others don't.

As for the rest, I wouldn't recommend Steve's Korean BBQ except for those who want value and don't care too much for quality. Pancho's Mexican isn't too bad. Mandarin House is subpar super unhealthy Chinese food (go to Viet Nam Village for good Chinese food), and I've never tried the gyros place or the Japanese place.

I'll have to admit I'll actually miss this place after I move out of Berkeley.

The only reason why I can see this place is called the "Asian Ghetto" is because of the number of Asians here. There's a Greek, Mexican, Italian, and donut restaurant all here too. That's half of the establishments in this food court! I just call it the "Ghetto."

Anyway, the place is pretty janky. The tables outside appear to be glazed or something, and the place is always filled with random puddles, pigeons, hobos and overfilled trash cans. It's pretty cool to eat in the Ghetto as a college freshman or if you're just visiting Berkeley but after a while it gets really old. I'd rather just grab my food and just go home and eat. 

The one redeeming factor? The fact that it's so convenient and the food served is pretty good!

The only places I know of that take credit cards now are Steve's Korean BBQ, Gypsy's, and Kingpin.

Lots of options for the student or person in/near Telegraph area of Berkeley.  Lots of pretty so so food.  In the past, this place has even had not one, but two bars.

Gone are the halcyon days of House of Kabob, replaced by a similar, but not as friendly and not as good Cal Gyro's.  Had to ask for the garlic sauce.  The pitas weren't spiced and grilled.  And the overall sauce flavor was inferior.  And the owner's daughter told me that they were way better than the old place (there from at least 1994 to about a year ago).  Oh, well I'm sure your opinion isn't biased, heh.

Mandarin Chinese is still there and after my one time there I decided going back wasn't a necessity.  Poorly made food, largely flavorless, honestly it gives Chinese (which can be a pretty interesting and fun cuisine) a bad name.

Thai Basil has been there at least 13 years, replacing one of the bars.  They make a terrific yellow curry chicken.  They make you wait forever, it's like being in a non-heavily touristed part of a third world country.  I've strayed from the yellow curry chicken a few times and was never pleased with the results, all pretty mediocre, quite unusual for what is usually pretty interesting in all that is Thai cuisine.  If you work really hard, even a white guy like myself can get very spicy food.  I like the really spicy, but if you don't, please don't be a hero as people that think they like spicy, but really don't have made it extremely hard for me to get the spicy.  Ask for 3 stores, be emphatic and you'll get it the best possible way, really spicy which I know is somewhat inappropriate for yellow curry chicken, but that's how I like it.  :)

King Pin doughnuts has great hours (any time) and solid, fresh doughnuts.  The doughnut lovers that I knew were all VERY fond of this place.

I've found Gypsey Trattoria badly overpriced and it's very inexpensive for Italian food.  I can easily make better and I'm decent, but probably only on par or slightly inferior to the average Italian restaurant.  Kind of a long wait.  It's very popular so maybe one of the largely uninspired, simple to make menu items that I haven't tried (all but 8 or so) is a lot better?  Or maybe people just think it seems cool, don't have that discriminating of a palate and go there because it's close.

Given the high turnover rates and incredible location (near something like 15,000 students living Southside), I suspect it's a pretty tough place to run a business.

There's a Japanese/sushi place that I used to like, but it changed owners and got more expensive.

Steve's Barbecue is a long term staple.  Cheap, large portions of marinated beef and kimchi, pretty basic, enjoyable as a quick food fix.

Vietnam Village was nice enough to introduce me to rice nuggets and has a large, fairly interesting menu.  It's cheap, it's an adventure, it's not a bad option.  Fairly fast.

Satay House has never impressed me.  Flavorless Thai?  How is that possible?

It's slummy, the outdoor seating has every seat right next to a typically almost overflowing trashcan and bums will ask you for money on your way in and out.  Great for a quick fix in the area and good for those on a budget, otherwise, I'd look elsewhere to get fed, generally.

Not all options apply for all restaurants.  Some may not take cards.  I'm not actually sure ANY places serve alcohol.  

Cal Gyros and the mixture of sensible pricing and many restaurant options are why I give them 3 stars, otherwise, they'd get less due to dirty Bohemian atmosphere and generally mediocre food.

No UC Berkeley Asian student can make it through their education without the nourishment from the Asian Ghetto. Ironically there's nothing really ghetto at all besides the overfilled trash cans towards the end of the night and the bum sitting in the front panning out.

before I came up to NorCal,
my friends who graduated from Cal warned me to stay away from this place

but I wanted to give it a try, since it's pretty close to our campus

my first impression was that 
this place was very DIRTY!! as soon as I walked in, I realized why people
call this place Asian Ghetto
anyways, I usually go to Thai Basil or Gypsy's
and I think their food is over price
also, they recently reduce the size of food.

I love this place! Whenever me and my friends visit Berkeley we'd always go to the Yogurtland on Shattuck ave. and the Asian Ghetto. It's just a nice little hangout spot with cheap but delicious food. It's especially wonderful that the restaurants are open till very late. I always recommend friends to go here and they all love it. I can't wait to come again this week.

this is just a review for the food ghetto and not its restaurants. it's exactly what it sounds like. don't expect anything fancy, we're not stanford. great grub though, if you live on the southside, it's just a must to eat here atleast a couple times a week.

The "Asian food ghetto" (I put in quotation mark because it is not all Asian. In fact barely over half of the joints in this place are Asian.) provided me some decently delicious food without breaking my bank when I used to live in Berkeley and down on periods of financial hard times.

I mostly patronized the Thai place, the Korean BBQ place, and the Gypsy Italian place.

Never been much of a doughnut fan, so can't comment too much about King Pin. And I think the Mandarin Chinese place has the worst food of them all.
Pretty good service.. But the have too much extra charges.. Lol, like 15c for box and 50c transaction fee.. I understand the transaction fee but the box? Lmao

Asian Ghetto! 5 stars just because this is what fed me during my freshmen year as a starving college student ... so many good memories here!  When you're a poor college student, you can't expect more than this.

This place is simply fantastic for delicious cheap food. I was born and raised in San Francisco, so I can't get enough Asian food, and I have very high standards. The Asian Ghetto meets those standards. The Vietnamese and Thai are my favorites, but it's all good in my opinion. 
    By the way, don't forget about what I call Asian Ghetto #2 on Hearst Ave. (across from North Gate next to Etcheverry). It's a food court that has Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, and Thai, with an American grill and a Top Dog for good measure. It's also worth checking out for sure.

A good conglomeration of a variety of mostly-Asian-themed food places. There IS a gyro place, a Mexican place, and an Italian place here too though. Overall, food here is cheap, and this is an easy meeting place for groups/people who don't know what they want to eat/people who want to eat different things/people who want to eat late at night. There's a center area with a good amount of seating, though it could be cleaner.

First place most group of friends think about when we want to find a place to eat. Variety of food makes the majority happy. Downside now is that most of them don't take credit card anymore. Shouldn't be too big of an issue since there's a BoA and Walgreens nearby.

Sometimes the hobo in front Ghetto plays super loud old-school music that can get annoying if you're eating outside and trying to have a conversation, but he's a nice dude.

I personally come here a lot at night for the boba.
What's not to like, a small area for just Asian food in the heart of Berkeley?  I wouldn't drive from the South Bay for this place unless i'm the area but the food is good and decent prices.
This place has a good variety of different kinds of food. Not a fan of all of the restaurants, but that's why there are so many others.

This is part of my Berkeley retrospective series.

A comprehensive review will take too long. So briefly.

1) Thai Basil - 4 stars. Nicely done Thai food. I admit I haven't been adventurous enough with the menu, but I dig the Basil chicken and garlic pepper chicken dishes (ordered really spicy, of course). They remind me of Thai joints in Houston, which is a good thing. Comfort food.

2) Gypsy's - 3 stars. Initially a fantastic experience, but the overwhelming use of heavy pasta sauces eventually dulls the taste buds. The "light" dishes are just not tasty, period. Use of herbs and appropriate seasoning is absent, use of HEAVY WHIPPING CREAM is abundant. The lingering aroma/odor of stale mozzarella cheese is present in the air. Busy.

3) Mandarin house - 2 stars - Inferior to the other place outside the ghetto. Store owner really hates you for some reason. Not too packed usually.

4) Fantasia house (sp?) - 3.5 stars - never tried their food, but their smoothies are the bomb. That's all.

Ah, memories.  I will always remember late night runs to the Asian Ghetto to get food before it closes during finals or lazy days when we didn't feel like cooking for ourselves.  Or grabbing some food in between classes and bringing it on campus to eat in the grass on nice sunny days.  The food is cheap and there is a good variety to choose from.  The location is super convenient for Berkeley students.  My favorites were the Vietnamese place for their varietal menu and Steve's BBQ for their delicious meat and kimchi.  Asian Ghetto has never disappointed me!

I love this eatery! It has all the food that I like. Convenient, reasonable prices, and they open late.

Hate the nickname for this place though.

Cal Gyro has a really nice gentleman that guides you on what to order. Keeps you entertained while you wait. The chicken gyro is delicious! 

Thai Basil hits the spot every time. Loveeeee the daily special! $5.75 for a whole meal is the bomb.

Sushi House of Berkeley is all right but still good food. The lunch special is a good price for a little bit of everything.

Quicklys is small and a little dirty but $1.50 for a taro milk tea - that ain't bad seriously.

This is the place to go for hungry ass college students, esp. when you haven't eaten the whole day from studying or grinding on that paper. You can run over and grab a quick bite, for that moment you can just chill out on some good, cheap food. :)

Oh how I love DURANT SQUARE!

Convenient, decent prices, food is alright. The new Mexican place and the Korean place are probably the worst ones. Gypsy's is a classic and Thai Basil is always satisfying. The food is much better than the collective of Asian restaurants on North Side.

The Ghetto, a place of fine dining, wonderful decor, and wonderful company.....j/k.  But seriously, the ghetto is a cool place to get a lot of variety.  The Thai place is good, but the food takes forever, the Korean place is the place to get meat! (the spicy pork is good for the amount you get), the Vietnam Village is solid, Gypsy's is bomb (just make sure you're not lactose intolerant) and King Pin Doughnuts....fresh doughnuts at midnight...need i say more? :)

Its called the asian ghetto for a reason, and it is a goddamn beautiful place. If you arent asian (and im not), you should probably do a lap first. You will see tons of college kids eating indescribable foods from styrofoam boxes. I normally try to spot the awkward skinny girl sitting by herself eating some strange concoction that involves a whole squid or baby octopus. Look around, there is always at least one.

Anyway, most of the time you will end up at Thai Basil, but i suggest branching out from time to time. I mean the WORST that could happen is your immediate and untimely death due to an allergy to some strange food product you didnt know people ate, right? Thats a risk worth taking.

Pretty much the "chinatown" of berkeley. Here you can find all sort of asian food. From korean to vietnamese to Ethiopian! what else can u ask for? 

A lot considered it dirty, but I consider it cute & convenient. I can walk way with a delicious plate of combo Pad Thai with shrimp, tofu AND chicken, pretty decent kbqq ribs and my ultimate bubble milk tea from quickly (or sweetheart)..... and ALL in the same location. WHEEE!

THE place to be if you're a Cal student. Everyone comes here.

The favorites: Vietnam Village, Steve's Korean BBQ, Thai Basil, Gypsy's, Bear's Ramen.

Always the lunch spot to hit up. Not always the cleanest though.

Asian Ghetto, my best friend during my time at Cal. It's actually not very ghetto except for the fact that there is a bum or two panhandling out front, it's a little dirty due to the constant presence of pigeons (watch out for the one with only one foot, it's mean!), and the trashes tend to overflow. Hmm, on second thought, maybe it is a little ghetto. But cheap and tasty food always brought me back here. In fact, Gypsy's still draws me back when I'm in Berkeley.

Gypsy's, Bear's Ramen, and Thai Basil are the places to eat. I wouldn't bother with the rest. 
For boba, Quickly and Sweethearts are equally decent.

If you're a Cal student, be prepared to run into a good amount of people you know as EVERYONE comes here.
Effing convenient when you don't have that much to grab lunch and are with a group of people who don't know what kind of food they want.

This is where my friends and I go when we can't really think of any place else to eat...the ghettoooo

There really are a lot of different types of food you can get in the ghetto from Italian at Gypsy's, to sushi at that one sushi place, to thai at the thai place at the end...haha guess i never really pay attention to the names. 

The prices here are great for college kids on a budget. And usually portions are pretty big. Also Pancho's is open till 3 am so it's perfect for late night nachos!
Oh and don't forget a donut from kingpin

I've had spoiled meat from Steve's Korean BBQ, spoiled eggs from Thai Basil, too-heavy-cheesy-everything from Gypsy's.  That, and the piles of plastic containers and what not surrounding every trash can and spilling over onto the tables and chairs and floors, kind of killed it for me.  

I would say come here for cheap food, and nothing else, but for that, I go to Blondie's or Smart Alec's.

I don't think anybody in the world can even count all the times I've been to this area to grab a meal. So many...so many...

There is no restaurant here that doesn't have something I truly enjoy to eat. Oops double negative. Luckily the Asian Ghetto is a double positive in my book. Zing!

Good memories of the Asian Ghetto! This was the only place that consistently had good cheap eats from morning till late at night. My favorites were Bear Ramen House and Thai Basil. 

It's called ghetto for a good reason, though. The outdoor tables are next to a lot of trash cans, flies, and bums that are constantly harassing you for change.
