My favorite memory was of a bum who asked me for change and called me a fucking chink after I told him I had none (I really didn't have change). Ya gotta love this place!

This place is a cool place for college food. I like coming here with friends to grab a bite, but i can't say eating in the area has been pleasant. 

If you sit outside you are constantly hounded by pigeons, spiders, and a variety of insects. 

I'd come here again on any given day with college friends. 

I ate at the sushi place inside the ghetto and it's ok. Nothing great or fancy. In my particular opinion it's overpriced food in general for regular asian food.

The Asian Ghetto is truly ghetto: the dining area that's in the center of the ghetto is always filthy and nobody ever cleans it; right outside, there's always homeless people hanging out asking for money; there's hoards and hoards of pigeons walking around picking up food people dropped onto the ground. All this, makes for a very nasty place to eat at. If you come later in the day, there's also a funky smell here, from all the discarded food and the homeless people that run through the place. 


The restaurants themselves are not bad (I have reviewed them separately), but this is a review for the square and the square is no good. I went down to UCSD recently and their food court, the equivalent of the ghetto, is incredible. Infinitely cleaner than the ghetto. 

Note: most restaurants in the Asian Ghetto are cash only.

Asian Ghetto is the ultimate places to get food from, this square has a selection of Italian, Japanese, Vietnamese/Chinese, Korean, Gyros and Donuts. All suitable for Students who are on the Go, because of fast service and cheap prices But with a Good Quality set of food selections as well. All CAL students know this. 

- Go Bears!

Bum on the trailhead of Asian Ghetto, bumpin' a boombox of remixed 2Pac classics for late night entertainment. Fine 18-yr old undergrads flooding the joint all hours of the day and night. Trash dumpster divers rummaging through the huge trash cans - just be wary of that dirty 'ish. If no one in your large group can decide on where to go, this is the choice epicenter of informal food eats at UC Berkeley. One block from campus, it's the spot really for its accessibility at all times of the day/night, good with groups, and variety. 

My latest visit Friday night, only after Gordo's on College Ave. closed, was the newer member of the Asian Ghetto called Pancho's taqueria. The chicken burrito was x-large. Just be sure to get plenty of hot sauce with your order so you can drench the burrito's inside.

By the way, this place is for people on FOOT or BIKE. Not much parking so get with the new decade 2011 and ditch the motor vehicle.
I love this place! Every time I visit my friends at Berkeley I always make them eat here with me. It's good cheap food!

haha! it's actually listed as "asian ghetto"...i thought that was just a nick name locals used...and not listed on yelp!  that's awesome...

I digress...it's perfect for late night munchies and boba.  it's convenient, inexpensive, and convenient. The food has variety..and, it actually tastes good..unlike overpriced Asian food restaurants (ahem, va de vi's)...

The best "Asian food on a budget" one-stop shop...

Taste: 3
Value: 5
Service: 3

Mediocre/crappy food, but apparently great for college students. I feel sorry for the people who think food from the Asian ghetto is "really good." At best, it's "all right" or "okay." Like people have said, seating is sometimes a pain. At least it's quick and close to campus.

hahahah
first i saw the "durant square" and i was about to write a review saying "whats that? you mean the ghetto?" then i saw the rest of the title. a few of my friends used to get so upset that it was called the ghetto :P they are like, super azns that fight for azn rights, i mean, nothing against them, i totally support their cause, but come on... (irene, that was for you :P)

anyway, this "square" is great. the food is great, cheap as all hell, fast and open late. love the thai basil, bear ramen and gypsy's
also, since they "remodeled" the place, its cleaner and the flooring isnt as weird, but i think they just poured concrete over the old cobblestone so now when you sit outside, the benches seem a lot shorter... does anyone know what i mean?

oh and the boba places are dirt cheap too
but i think i like sweatheart's better than the quickly

So many great places to choose from. I love going to thai basil, steve's korean bbq, gypsys for pasta, and sweetheart cafe for boba and popcorn chicken. All of them are affordable and open late. It's the perfect spot when you're with a group because there's something for everyone.

This place is one of the main reasons I cross the Caldecott tunnel to get some food!  I love hitting this place up!  I almost always hit up the Ramen House and get my usual order, kim chi fried rice!  The "Ghetto" has Japanese, Vietnamese, Thai, Korean, and Chinese food.  I love hitting up Sweetheart Cafe and getting boba.  And the donut shop is great, especially when you get the fresh donuts they just made. 

It can get pretty busy here with all the Cal students, but there are plenty of tables outside to eat at.  This place is definitely a must whenever I'm in Berkeley!  I'm getting hungry just thinking about it!

Tried Steve's Korean BBQ at Durant at GFC (Ghetto Food Court)...  

The BBQ Beef ($7) was delicious....generous portion with kimchi and steamed sprouts... the BBQ Chicken ($7) was tasty but rather dry...  

It was strange to see four Hispanic guys running the place and not one asian worker in sight....   

Also, it has a clean bathroom for customers...

Since there are so many small places in here I would prefer to comment on them all as a whole compared with individually listing each place. To save some time I will talk about the 3 places which I find the most interesting the first being Quickly. Yeah yeah I know, how un-unique could I be but hear me out for a second. This is one of the only places that serves tapioca (sorry "boba" fans) in the area and their drinks are very well priced. From offering great specials to catering to a large group of Asian-American students they have done a good job preparing high quality drinks for a low price. Outside the fact that no matter where you go there will be a slight smell of garbage around along with the usual homeless person asking for spare change, it's nice to know that a community like Berkeley can have an area specific to Asian Americans.

With that said there are two places which stick out in my head more than any others. I know there are many other places around and one day I may update this post to reflect that but due to writers block I will keep things simple and suggest 2 places to go to no matter what. First off is Steve's Korean BBQ. Recently I have noticed that they have been raising their prices (due to inflation and the economy) but there is no where else can you find yourself satisfied with meat, rice, and a generous helping of kim chi on the side. It's in my opinion the best deal in the area. Second is King Pin. What is this you may ask? Well think of it as Krispy Kreme but much better. Not only is it open late at night but the items they serve here are much more superior to the fast donuts that they serve at Krispy Kreme. I always enjoy coming here early in the morning to get a donut getting my fix on sugar. The food made is always extremely fresh and it's nice to get to know the staffers as well.

With that all said there are many other places to check out, and there are other reviews that you can read that go into further detail that what I have written about. Regardless of who sez what, if you ever find yourself in the area, this is the place to check out.

a star for convenience as a cal student, a star for good prices, a star for tasty foods, and a star for all of the homeless people.

but i can't give you anymore stars, asian ghetto! 

also, if you have a car, do not try parking here.

Best hang out place around campus. A variety of food to choose from and a fairly moderate price. And all are open quite late ~1pm on Weekends? Anyway, my favorites are the kimchee fried rice and ramen at the Korean place. Go Bears!

You were the place where I had many intimate lunches between classes.

You were the place where we had large crowds take up the benches.

You provided food and comfort whenever I desired.

You had all the Asian selections I could possibly have dreamed off.  And you never once tried to rip me off.

But best of all, I can count on you not to change much for years to come.

There is a reason why whenever my feet go on autopilot after a meeting or practice or class, they take me straight to Durant Food Court everytime - I can always find something to eat here.

Whether it be a Calzone at Gypsy's, Taro Milk Tea at Sweethearts, BBQ Beef at Steve's, or Pad See Ew Chicken at Thai Basil, DFC has become my most frequented eating spot in Berkeley.

True it can be a lot cleaner, and use more seating, but the food is both cheap and delicious - a must-eat-here for the college student and the Cal visitor.

Durant Food Court is not just an Asian Ghetto.

Review is for Steve's Korean BBQ only!

GREAT deal, huge portion enough for 2 girls, tons of meat.

Tastes: WEIRD tasting kimchi, really weird, it's got this pineapple taste to it, soggy and gross. The chapchae was good, sprouts was good. My Kalbi was FATTY...but it's hard to avoid eating the pure beef fat because the marinate is so dark. It upsets my stomach badly afterward...

Korean BBQ right? None of the people worked there was Korean, go figure!

Ate here a total of 4 times during my first few months at Berkeley. Then I found better friends. (Better because they never tormented my taste buds with the likes of "Asian Ghetto" food.) Adios. Never again. It was not nice knowing you.

Yes, it's great mediocre college food. Yes, it's conveniently located near campus and the dorms. But to the people who really think the food from the Durant Square is "tasty and really good," from what rock did you crawl out of?

The food here isn't even that cheap. There are so many options out there for the same price! I cry at the accepted lowered standard every time I pass by this place. But I suppose this is all part of what college experience is supposed to be.

What's that you say? You're craving some cheap Asian food out of a styrofoam container & want to eat it at a table that's missing some chairs in a dingy alley-like place, while being accosted to "Spare-a quartah?!?!?!" by various homeless people? You're in luck! Durant Square meets all of your requirements!

Seriously though, the food's not all that spectacular (though it is spectacularly cheap) & what the hell is up with the bizarre seating? It's like they originally planned to have tables with some benches & some chairs, & then someone stole all the chairs (probably one of those homeless people, who then sold them for a quartah. I don't get it.

But hey, it doesn't seem to bother Berkeley folks too much, so I'm not about to get all uppity about it. When you're done downing your greasy (Chinese, Thai, Japanese, Vietnamese, Italian (wtf? I thought this was the ASIAN ghetto)) food, head over to King Pin & watch the donut man dunk his delectable treats in (chocolate, powdered sugar, etc) & then spend a few of those quartahs (that you're not planning to share because you know they'll just spend it on drugs anyway) & get some donut holes.

Bring cash. I don't think any of those places take cards, & while they have an ATM in the back of one of the restaurants, with BofA & Wells Fargo half a block away, there's no sense in wasting your money on bank fees. & finally, keep in mind that all these places close ASS-EARLY. Like 9. Or earlier. Isn't this a college town?!

Ahh Asian Ghetto... how I love thee, let me count the ways... 

Meesha's 
Steve's BBQ 
Bear Ramen House 
King Pin Donuts 
Thai Basil 
and more....

You never disappoint with your cheap eats, your savory flavors, your heart stopping goodness.  Something for everyone in a little outdoor terrace packed with people and college kids.  The best concentration of street food in Berkeley.  Sigh...

Ah, the Asian Ghetto. The dirty benches, the row of instrument-playing bums, the overwhelming smell of garbage...what is there not to miss about this place?

Here's a rundown of my favorite restaurants (ranked in order of tastiness):

1) Steve's Korean BBQ (5 stars): Where else can you get nearly a pound of meat atop of a heap of rice and generous sides of kim chi and sprouts all for about $8? Although they've been raising the prices, the amount of good food you get makes it totally worth it. 

2) King Pin (4.5 stars): The 2am, post frat party hot spot. Best. Donuts. EVER. No matter what you are--drunk or sober, fat or skinny--you're bound to love King Pin Donuts. The donut holes here are amazing (especially when they're warm).

3) Thai House (4 stars): Incredibly slow service and a bit overpriced, but their Garlic Pepper Chicken is incredible (as is their Pad Thai).

4) Mandarin House (4 stars): Two words: general chicken! Not to mention their boba is arguably the best in Berkeley.

5) Gypsy's (3.5 stars): A bit too oily and fatty for my taste, but you can't deny the huge portions you get of such Italian staples as the Gnocchi, Chicken Carbonara, and Pepperoni Calzone, all for around $6. The food is good--not great--and come with a pretty tasty garlic-topped piece of toast. 

6) Bear's Ramen (3 stars): Kim Chi fried rice with spam! Though that's all I've ever had here. The rest of the menu doesn't seem appetizing to me.

7) Lotus House (3 stars): Good pan fried noodle with beef, decent everything else (including boba).

UC Berkeley wouldn't be the same without Asian Ghetto, its lower-end culinary pride and joy. Over my 4 years at Cal, this place kept me sane, happy, and very full. Despite its sketchiness, the Ghetto has a unique charm about itself. It's always crowded and the food certainly tastes better than you might expect.

I have no idea of why a review doesn't exist for the ghetto overall already, but rather only for it's individual restaurants.

I can see how many Cal student's lives would have been much more worse at school if it weren't for the presence of this group of restaurants.  They literally seem to have something for every taste you're happening to crave.  People will end up having "favorites", and ever argue about what the best dish and deal are at the ghetto.

The asian ghetto's food shines compared to the Emeryville Public Market (which is what I'm closer to now) and I'll gladly drive here from work for lunch because I miss it.  I can see how things could get old if you come here everyday, but it would take a lot longer to get old than if you went to ONE restaurant everyday :)

Some Favorites:

Crazy Alfredo at Gypsys.  Pad-See-Ew at Thai Basil.  Spicy BBQ Pork at Steve's Korean.  Spam Kim-Chee Fried Frice at Ramen House.  Donuts!  and much more!

One of the best places to get food at when I was at Berkeley visiting my brother. Almost hole in the wall type place (hence "ghetto"). I've tried the Thai and Vietnamese restaurants and have had good experiences with both. 

If I went Cal.... I would eat there A LOT. Very inexpensive, convenient, and a variety of places to choose from.

This is really good. Came here on a free meal day. Delicious, tender beef and tasty chicken, with some interesting pasta and some rice. Don't know why people don't know about this place. More people should come!
Delicious food, great service, very nice people! I really wish they had more business, but their location is unfortunate.

Best koobideh I have had in Berkeley. Overall kebobs better than Diyar just up the street, much better quality ingredients especially in salads and cheaper - pretty big meal for ~$7. Lamb kebob was excellent.
Good for groups as ample seating, will be back to try one of their wraps next time.

One thing that would make this place really great and make me want to spend time with my laptop (to take advantage of free wifi) would be Turkish Coffee/ Persian tea from those little tiny cups or glasses and baklava and/or persian rice cookies!

The grilled Veggie Plate was outstanding! The Koobideh on a plate or in a rap is delicious and authentic Persian.

The service is very friendly. Stop in the next time you're in Berkeley.

Fairly decent food considering this is in Berkeley (especially when you compare it with Asian ghetto stuff) so this place really deserves more attention. The sandwiches taste very fresh, and the kebab meat is tender, unlike some Berkeley restaurants that make you chew on meat-like pebbles. Definitely drop by here especially with their buy one get one free promotion still up!

update:
they gave the interior a new paint job and it's much more inviting now. check them out.

This is a new place that opened where sufficient grounds used to be, and the space is redecorated and very open. I felt like the decorations were kind of tacky, but the seating was nice, and the owners were super friendly and attentive!

We tried the BBQ chicken sandwich and tilapia sandwich. They were more like wraps than sandwiches, although instead of tortillas they used a thin sheet of bread to wrap around the ingredients. All the vegetables were very fresh, and the bread was freshly made and really yummy! The tilapia was very healthy-tasting, but lacked flavor, but the chicken was pretty tasty, and I really liked the pesto sauce (you can choose between different sauces for the sandwich).

Planet Kabob doesn't have all their signs up. nevertheless the most important one was up:            .   "GRAND OPENING SPECIAL
                                       $5   all menu items"


menu: bbq greek burger/ground beef, bbq chicken, tilipia, grilled veggies, grilled lamb  sandwiches (5.95), plates (7.95)-basmatic rice, salad, and meat..

drink: L. coffee(lappert's, 1.25)
-very smooth, almost silky, not harsh at all, hawaiian? close to ethiopian. 4 stars

eats: grilled lamb plate (5)-grand opening special
-2 strips of tender lamb (demi glance sauce), had a bit of lamb taste
-meat looks like sparerib strip but boneless, tender like meatloaf.
-basmatic rice fluffy, cooked right
-salad has Tzatzina sauce, some cheese too, vinegary,  tartness of olves. very nice
-4.5 stars

leftovers:
-all ingredients tasted fresh. dave, the owner, says everything is.
-dave has 2 other eateries in contra costa
-planet across from yogurt  park.
-haven't tasted much greek food, this is da best so far!
-dining room not cheap furnishings, upscale wood.
-grand opening special great value!
-not sure of wi-fi.

Great place to eat for lunch! I came here for an avocado spread and definitely left full. 
The sandwiches are a bit bigger than 6 inches long but definitely piled very high. The avocado spread has a generous helping of avocado, my favoriteeeee :) 
The only downside would be that I wish there was more sauce/flavor to the sandwiches - I think I will ask for extra mustard next time or something. The sandwich only cost me $5.75.

There is a ton of seating and not a long wait for food (although I did come by at around 2pm). I like the quietness of the atmosphere because a lot of people seem to come here to eat alone / study.

The next time I come, I will definitely get a bowl of soup as well. The soups are only $2.50 and look delicious!
I prefer the corner store up the street.

A great cheap lunch option. I probably come to Stuffed Inn at least two times a week during the busy lunch hour. The staff is super friendly (family-run?) and they've memorized my order by now. I usually get a ham and cheese or the turkey avocado (so good!) and get out the door pretty quickly despite the lines.
Decent sandwiches that have customizable options. Funky decor seating inside but I kinda like it. The place can get busy but that's a good sign.

Nice cute sandwich shop that offers cheap prices for tasty sandwiches.  I got the Avocado Spread Sandwich with Turkey and was surprised at how much meat and avocado they give.  Granted, these items are cheap when you buy in bulk but they do their best to give great value in their sandwiches.  I recommend this place for anyone w/o a car on northside.  It is one of the better places to stop by.  Good eats are scarce on the northside of campus

truth is i haven't been here in years, but when i randomly saw the stuffed inn review on yelp, all sorts of memories surfaced and i had to add some words of my own. this place has a special place in my heart as i came here almost every lunchtime for a full semester my freshman year to eat lunch with a greek-god-looking boy i knew from my italian class. the soups and sandwiches were superb - fresh and delicious and appropriate for a student budget - and everything was fun and rose tinted by my unspoken crush. recommendation: eat with someone you adore and good food will become even better.

I lived right around the corner from this place from 2000-2003, and I'll admit to going over to the Stuffed Inn for a fabulous sandwich when I had the basic ingredients sitting in my own fridge at home.  Why?  Because IT'S JUST SO GOOD.  I have no idea what they do, but I remember the sandwiches just being absolutely delicious.

I go to stuffed inn probably 100 times per year. The food is all fresh, the options are healthy, and the cookies are amazing. On top of that, the owner is a really nice guy, the staff is amazingly friendly. The fastest lunchmaker, "cheeto", remembers like everything anyone has ever ordered. I get the same thing every time, Chelsea's Chicken Salad, so he has an easy job. But I've had friends tell me they had a 6 month hiatus from the place, had only been there a couple of times, and he still remembered their order. Incredible.

Cheap, tasty and healthy. This combination itself gives anyplace a five. I will also say however, the service is very good, the line is a little long during lunch hour (5-7 mins) and the place is defiantly cozy. If you never been here, I recommend the Turkey Avocado sandwich.

The sandwiches don't seem terribly exciting from the menu, and honestly, I've only ever gotten one, but I do love that darn avocado spread sandwich. It really has everything I could want in a sandwich (avocado, meat, cheese, sprouts, cucumber, lettuce). 

It's a good spot for a cheap, reliable lunch. Not the snazziest, or most exciting, but a solid choice for a quick and tasty bite.
This place is my lunch room. Always will be till I am here!

I'm a fan of their turkey and avocado sandwiches on wheat-- with all the fixings!  Mayo, lettuce, tomato, bean sprouts, cucumbers, and pickles, I think.  ~ $5

Their split pea soup is so, so good.  I usually get it with a bread stick or two for an extra $0.50.  Very filling.  ~$3

The people who work there are also very nice, so that's a plus!  Also, I usually go here after my 12-1P lecture, and there hasn't really ever been a line.  The longest I had to wait was about 5 minutes to get my food.  

I did subtract 1 star because the sandwiches are a bit overpriced.  If I had the time, I could just buy all the ingredients and make a week's worth of sandwiches for the same price as about 2 (1/2) of their sandwiches.

Known for their inexpensive made-to-order sandwiches, this is the best place to eat north of campus on a student budget.  Or even not on a student budget.  For a while I ate here frequently enough that the staff got to know me.  And what can I tell you from all my meals here?  Get the avocado and turkey without peppers or pickles on soft french bread.  It's a great combination of flavors.  As an added bonus, it's healthy too.  Besides sandwiches, they serve fine soups and salads and very large cookies.

Warning: if you go during the school year during regular lunch hours there will likely be a line out the door, indicating approximately a fifteen minute wait.

Mom and pop sandwich joint. It's got a cool, ol' school feel (when I say ol' school, I don't mean retro...I mean like the waaaay back in the day). For example, their tables look like the ones from the medieval taverns. 

It's on the North side of UC Berkeley's campus so it's kind of outta the way unless you're a fellow grad student or 'live' in Corey/Soda Hall. If you make the trek across campus and up the mini hill, you'll find a 'homey' lil' deli. 

+ Tastes like good, home-made sandwiches.
     *Fresh ingredients
+ Sammies are made hella fast! 
+ Cheap grub: around $5-6, woohoo! 
-  Lack of nutritional content
-  No information on where the food came from (ie. Farmer's Market, chain market?)

Final Call:
The Stuffed Inn is a healthy alternative to the rest of the restaurants in North side. Sandwiches are simple, good but lack that pizzzzaz. It can get old fast but at least you'll live longer eating this stuff. I'll be back only if I'm on this side of campus. 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Munchies:
1. Hot pastrami sandwich with cheddar on wheat
     + warm wheat bread's a nice touch
2. Double pastrami sandwich with Swiss on Rye
     + They actually double the amount of pastrami!
3. Egg sandwich with cheddar on wheat
     -  Bland egg mix
4. Chicken noodle soup
     -  Lacking flavor, too bland

Never quite understood why there is so much expensive food around a campus of (mostly) broke students.  That being said, I usually pack a cute bag lunch, but some days I don't have the energy.  I tried The Stuffed Inn because I found it on yelp.  I got a big sandwich (for me) and a cup soup for about 7 bucks, and they were both really good and really fresh.  Also, whoever was working was super friendly, which I always appreciate (hey it does make food taste better!).  It was super good AND prepared my brain for my midterm (Too bad it didn't give me an A).  Will be back!

I don't remember what I ordered exactly, but it was a salad with tuna and half an avocado. I asked for the sour cream (and chives?) dressing. The owner was super duper nice and gave me an extra thing of dressing for free when I asked! It was a really really yummy salad, however, my stomach paid dearly for it. I highly suspect the sour cream dressing, which may be why he was so willing to give it away. Anyway, despite my bathroom troubles, I still give this place 4 stars. I'll have to try it again some day to be sure.

I love this place!  I used to eat here a few times a week and the people remembered me and would greet me. So nice! The sandwiches are great and the soups are pretty good too.  I would recommend almost every sandwich on the menu, plus soup and a sparking apple cider to drink!  The one thing I don't recommend, however tempting they may look, is the cookies.  They are pretty tasteless. Grab a spot by the window for some prime people watching in their homey, cozy seating area and enjoy!

very good egg salad.  nothing special bread.  homemade pea soup.  nice people.  I don't eat meat, but the two times I brought a roast beef sandwich from there, the people I bought the sandwiches for complained that the roast beef was weird tasting.

What a great place! Quiet, healthy, vegan options, and dirt cheap. I get the split pea soup every time--you can get a bowl and a refill plus some bread for under $5. The worst part of Stuffed Inn is the lunchtime line, but if you're just getting soup (or anything else that's self-serve or can be ordered at the cash register), they let you skip the long line of people waiting to order and cut right to the cash register line. Be careful when you do that, however, not to actually cut off anyone who has waited in the line, got their food, and is ready to pay. Oh, and although the line often stretches out the door, there's always room to sit down.

Definitely deserves all the hype. We got here at around 11am to avoid the crowd (the line was out the door less than an hour later). I had heard that the split pea soup and turkey avocado were all the craze, so I tried them both. They were nothing short of amazing. My parents got the pastrami so I was able to sample that, and it too was delicious. Both sandwiches were under $7. To top it all off, the sandwich-making staff were a funny filipino family that seemed to enjoy what they do. Next time I'm in the Bay, I'll be coming back.

My go-to lunch spot!  I love these guys.  Super friendly.  Delicious fresh food at a great price.  I love the soups and salads.  And the smiling faces!!

If you go between noon and 1pm, expect a line out the door!

Good but overrated. I say this because it's frustrating to wait in line for fifteen minutes because I'm too lazy to heat a can of soup and make my own sandwich for lunch. (Which is why I usually go to Hummingbird Cafe across the street, which doesn't have a line).

I like that you can add a modest bowl of soup to your sandwich/salad for only $1.75. They switch it up daily, but I've never come across a bad batch yet.

Even without the lunch-hour rush, the entrance and the deli area is cramped. However, they make it up by providing good seating in a unique woodsy interior. Definitely the coziest place to eat on Northside.

I've been coming here since I was an undergrad more than ten years ago.  It's still the same delicious bargain it was back then.

For six bucks you can get a sandwich, bowl of soup (split pea and the most awesome tomato soup), and simply the best cookie available in Berkeley (made on-site).  Enough veggie-friendly sandwiches to keep a non-meat-eater very happy.

Being a family run shop, the service is always very friendly.  Contrary to previous review, Intermezzo's oversize-hunkabread sandwiches cannot hold a candle to what's available from Stuffed Inn  Very highly recommended.

Really good sandwiches and soup. I always get the turkey with avocado spread and provolone on dark rye.  I want to try others but this is so good I can't help ordering it every time.  The split pea soup is very tasty.  So is the tomato.  Go early for lunch or there will be a line out the door...
Turkey Avocado Goodness!! So veggies are fresh and filling (half a sandwich will get you full!). Cheap, fresh option!

I'm kinda surprised that I haven't discovered Stuffed Inn until now, but better late than never. Here are the basics that you need to know:
1.) They're efficient, and even though the line is usually out the door, its never a long wait.
2.) Their sandwiches are a reasonable size, and a cheap price (the most expensive sandwich is $5.50).
3.) The sitting area is too cute! Have you seen the booths.
4.) Definitely one of the freshest places I've ever eaten at. It's totally healthy.

Even though I haven't really tried the soup, Stuffed Inn already has my heart. I definitely want to try the tomato soup next time.

Ah, Northside-- I love everything about you except the hills. Luckily, Stuffed Inn makes the vertical climb worth it.

ATMOSPHERE
The restaurant is split into two rooms with two doors: one entrance and one exit. The room with the entrance is extremely narrow and small, so naturally there is always a long line... but don't worry! It moves relatively quickly.

I recommend sitting in the adjacent room because it's cozy and has a ton of natural light. There are wooden booths and tables-- all with a Snow White homey feel.

FOOD
Jock's Avocado Spread (mmm...): meat, cheese, alfalfa sprouts, tomatoes, cucumbers, and lettuce.

You can add mayo, mustard, spicy mustard, peppercinis, jalapenos, onions, etc to every sandwich-- all free of charge.

I appreciated the variety of bread. The soft sweet French roll was so fluffy and delightful. The only odd thing was that they didn't have chicken as a meat! They stuck to traditional deli meats.

I paired my sandwich with a bag of Ruffles and a fresh squeezed lemonade. I highly recommend the lemonade because it's only $0.90 for a pretty big cup of tangy goodness.

Sandwich + chips + drink = $7. Not too shabby!

This has become one of my favorite sandwich shops in Berkeley. It may not compare to Sufficient Grounds (RIP) but it's still a great option if you want to pick up a bite to eat between classes in Northside.
Not the best place I've eaten at for sandwiches. However, I'm in love with their soups! Highly recommend the Chicken Noodle. mm mm GOOD

Their sandwiches are arguably among the best in Berkeley. After my first visit here I found myself back three other times that same week for the exact same sandwich. The place is always packed, the line nearing or out the front door. The service is fast, but extremely friendly. You hear conversations and exchanges between workers and regulars, assuring you that this place is a favorite.

After having the avocado spread sandwich with turkey, I am having a hard time trying anything else. The ingredients are fresh and delicious. The sandwiches stuffed and made the way mom used to. I love the addition of sprouts in the sandwich, makes you feel like your sandwich is extra healthy.

I did try the split pea soup and it's good, but not extremely exciting. That could partly be due to the fact that it's been getting a bit too warm in Berkeley for soup.

Overall, this place is worth trying for sure. I will likely be back weekly for my sandwich fix. It's going to be hard eating another at another sandwich place after trying Stuffed Inn. Also, prices can't be beat, the sandwiches average around $5-$6. Perfect for busy, struggling college students.

as the parents money well dries up, stuffed inn has picked the slack in offering a wonderfull assortment of sandwhichs and soups. Tuna (toona) isn't awesome, go with the turkey, and splurge on the avacado.

Also, isn't northside nice. I mean it doesn't have as great as a fun fun scene but something is nice about it, mmm turkey and avacado.. mm

Bread + meat + Veggies = Sandwich 
That's what the Stuffed Inn is all about.  It's simple, it's basic, it's reliable.  It's never extraordinary or bad.  I find this a good place to take lunch groups near campus when the south side is overrun with undergrads.  The lines can still be pretty long.  
Highlight: their oatmeal cookies are just so good and taste like real oatmeal may gone into them.  Yum.
Lowlight: I find it slightly annoying that they charge for so many extras like a refill or a pickle spear.

I wasn't sure about this place at first, the line is usually out the door at lunch but the sandwiches seemed pretty basic.  Well, this place as grown on me and become a regular lunch destination.  The sandwiches are simple but always delicious with fresh bread and produce.  But it's the soups that are the true standouts, I especially like the Clam Chowder on Tuesdays and the Tomato Soup with lentils served daily.

The staff is friendly and quickly start to recognize your face and remember your order.

Love this place. 
Great sandwiches and nice and friendly staff.

I will sum up my opinion of Stuffed Inn in convenient bulleted list format:


--The best sandwiches I've ever eaten--hands down.
--Fantastic vegan split pea soup, every day of the week.
--An "express lane" where you can bypass the line and get out faster.
--Great cookies.
--Extensive customization ability for every sandwich.
--Did I mention that they have great sandwiches? You leave this place not feeling like you've just swallowed a few dozen bricks.

The only downside to Stuffed Inn is their salads--I've tried a couple, and I didn't like them. But this is still the best food on Euclid, and I try to go here as much as possible. Oh yeah--and it's CHEAP. $2.00 for a bowl of that great soup, between $4.00-$5.00 for sandwiches, $5.25 for huge salads.The entire venture is just a great buy.

I have never in my life enjoyed split pea soup.

Until I ate here one day, and scooped out the wrong kind in my bowl (the label was wrong and I didn't notice).  Rather than waste it, I took a few bites and found it GOOD.  Thinking this was a mistake on my part, I immediately went and had split pea soup elsewhere (two other places, actually) and ICK!  Couldn't hack it, but at the Stuffed Inn, I enjoy it muchly.

As good as the soup is, though, for me, it is their sandwiches and salads that make me smile.  Chelsea's Chicken Salad is SO good, and I love the Turkey & Cheese sandwich.  They overstuff every 'wich so YOU are stuffed when you are done.  Their salads are HUGE!  They do not stint on any ingredients, but keep their prices low anyway- for five bucks you can get a HUGE amount of really good lunch-food.

Also, their cookies are heavenly!  Steamed on site instead of baked, they are moist, soft and so yummy.  The potato salad is also really, really tasty; I will order it with a mixed-greens salad and just go to town.

Get here early, though!  After about 11:45 the line goes out the door, and although they are quick in the makings, that is still a long time to wait for lunch.

This place is perfect for when you're craving a cheap sandwich like the ones your mom used to make you for lunch...but a bit fancier. 
The sandwiches here are reasonably priced and come with a decent amount of toppings and bread choices. I personally love that some of the sandwiches either have meat or avocado (yum). The prices range from 4.50-6.00 depending on how fancy you get with it.

They also have amazing split pea soup. It's actually the first place I tried it and fell in love. The soup is really a steal and is super filling. They always have either tomato vegetable soup or split pea and a 3rd that changes daily. Today (Monday) I had the cream of broccoli and it was delicious! 

On top of good soup and yummy sandwiches they also have yummy cookies, breadsticks (2 for$.60) , chips, and drinks. 

Definitely a place to try.
Lots of good stuff for super cheap. Great lunch place. A star off for their sandwiches being about 1$ more than those at the Coffee Spot on lower Sproul.

For posterity, the soup schedule as of 9/3/2008 is:

Monday: Cream of Broccoli
Tuesday: Clam Chowder
Wednesday: Corn Chowder
Thursday: Chicken Noodle
Friday: Clam Chowder

With the (amazing) split pea and the (disappointing) tomato garbage soup served every day.

I am a new englander, and the clam chowder is some of the best I've ever had.
Food is alright for the low price.  But there are many more better choices if you are on Euclid and have an appetite for sandwiches/salads.

The amazingly long line did not justify the quality of sandwiches I received for my lost greenbacks. Soup is definately a better value. Perhaps this place is better during non-lunch hours, but I had school at other times!!! -_-

I get a sandwich, soup, salad, and cookie almost every week here since it's so close to campus. They deliver to campus if it's a big order!

Soup: Split Pea and Clam Chowder are my usual orders. Clam Chowder is only available Tues/Fri I believe.

Long lines but I usually fax a group order in for next day delivery!
Great prices, great cookies, great sandwiches! Relaxed atmosphere and friendly service.
The food is great, especially the soups.  Between 12 and 1pm there will be a huge line.

So I love sandwiches. I mean I really LOVE sandwiches. When I came back to the states after 4 months of studying abroad, the first thing I did was buy a deli sandwich and inhale it. But for some reason, there doesn't seem to be very many affordable sandwich places around the Cal campus. Thank goodness for The Stuffed Inn! It's affordable, simple, fresh, and delicious - you really can't go wrong here. For a couple of dollars you can add a bowl of soup to your sandwich!

To illustrate the awesomeness of The Stuffed Inn, I have developed this complicated equation:
Turkey sandwich + clam chowder soup (Tuesdays) = complete, utter lunch bliss.

If this place wasn't so far from my apartment, I would probably be here everyday...
This is my local sandwich shop near work, love the tuna salad sandwich always get that with all the trimmings, any place that puts sprouts and hot peppers on their sandwich is my kind of place.
Converts you into a vegan split pea soup lover.   Enough said.

This place feels like it was dropped right out of the 70s. I do like the weird nook and cranny seating there.  I always hated their choice of sandwiches (all basics like turkey and ham). They all tasted fine but they were definitely nothing special.

The tuna sandwich on Rye bread was delicious, and they have cherry coke in their soda fountain.  Their soups are very tasty, too.  My favorite is New England Clam Chowder.  Simple menu but everything tastes just right.

Tasty, unique sandwiches! I had an Angel's Veggie Melt sandwich on dark rye and a Big Ned's avocado sour cream sandwich on an onion. Both were delicious! Bread and ingredients were fresh.
Vegetarian-stamp-of-approval.
Also, beautiful rustic day-lit seating area.

Yum! Didn't even know about Stuffed Inn until last semester, but rest assured I've been making up for lost time! The food is great, the service is amazing, and its just an awesome place to go eat. 

I love their pastrami sandwiches but my current obsession is the egg salad and ham. Amazing. Their cookies are also really good. I can't get enough of this place. 

Also: Clam chowder tuesdays. Enough said.

This place always has a hefty line at lunch, so I finally decided to go in there to see what all the fuss is. I got a pastrami with provolone on a French roll and found it aggressively average. There are two other shops on this same block that make sandwiches from scratch, and they're all about the same price -- but the others put a lot more meat in it, and they also shred the lettuce.

This place also put my sandwich in a steamer, I guess to melt the cheese, which made the sandwich kind of limp and and soggy. Although you have a lot of options for ingredients, they'll put it together with lettuce, mustard and mayo unless you make a point of asking for the specific things listed, like red onions, peppers, and dressing. I was eager to try out the dressings, but it never came up. The communication level was underwhelming. And this was after the lunch rush, so it's not like they were distracted.

I've heard that their soups are good, but I don't see much point in coming back, since the sammy was relatively small for the money. The popularity of this place is a little mystifying.

I went back to Stuffed Inn after a bit of a hiatus, though I've been frequenting it for lunch for the last six years. Their sandwiches are always consistently good and their staff friendly and sweet, and today was no exception.  The veggies in sandwiches and bread choices are fresh and healthy - the same quality I'd make for myself at home, but stuffed even more full of ingredients than I would be able to reliably stack in a sandwich - and the prices are great ($4.75-6 for a sandwich; a few dollars for a bowl of soup).  I'm a vegetarian and almost always get the same avocado sandwich, customized to how I like it, and I know I can always expect the same quality each time. Simple, fresh, and delicious food, and friendly chats with the warm staff leave a smile on my face every time: I couldn't ask for any more from a lunch spot to get me through some long days.

Excellent family owned place with delicious thick chunky soups.  Their salads are big and fresh.  Their sandwiches are ok.  I like their pastrami cuz they heat it.  

it's all about their soups though, the split pea is thick and very tasty.  

As someone else mentioned, the service is excellent too.

I've been here over 50+ times, and every time I come here the family who runs it is so nice. They always remember my order, and even say Hi when I  see them around North side. 

Food:
I usual get a pastrami and swiss heated up with everything and spicy mustard. The sandwich is nowhere near Ike's level in SF, but for the price and quality of ingredients it's a good deal. You can't get this type of sandwich for $5 in SF. Their soups are good and cheap, my favorite soups are the Tomato and split pea soup. 

Overall this a good spot if you just want grab a sandwich and soup and get stuffed!

Ive been eating at Stuffed Inn for the last four years. I try go at least once a week.

The staff is extremely friendly, remember your orders, and chat with you while moving through their massive line efficiently. While the sandwichs aren't the most original, they are well made and extremely fresh! Definitely try their hot sandwiches or make up your own order to fit your likes.

The soups are excellent. I especially enjoy their Monday's Cream of Broccoli and their Wednesday Corn Chowder. 

Be sure to give this place a try! They are cheap, fast and fresh... my favorite lunch stop in North Berkeley!

Recently, I started checking out places on the north side of campus where only cs and engineering majors dare the venture.  I heard about this place and their great sandwiches from some friends. They compared it to some other sandwich places that serve mean, hardy subs so I decided to check it out.

The line was decently long as it extended out the door adding to my expectations. I ordered the Pastrami and Cheese while my girlfriend got the Turkey Avocado.  The time it took to prepare them were moderately long for a simple sandwich.

A couple bites into the sub, we both admitted that this was not what we expected. We came to the conclusion that these were just mediocre, hyped-up sandwiches.  They did not compare to the great sandwiches that our friends said they were, instead I would most relate them to on-campus or Safeway sandwiches.

If you are starving with no place to go..I would check this place out, but if you're looking for something worth your money and appetite, I'd pass.
Most convenient sandwich place in Berkeley! Always packed at lunch. The Turkey Avocado is my favorite.

Let's see, I've had the chicken salad several times.. not bad, not bad. Pretty generous portion, especially the take-out version. Just had the Jock's Avocado Spread w/ Salami & Swiss. They were VERY generous with the avocado spread, soooo good!

But, what really won me over at Stuffed Inn is their peanut butter chocolate chip cookie. It's under a buck and if you grab one, fresh out of the oven, EFFING AMAZING. I'd keep coming back just to grab one of these :]

Stuffed Inn's sandwiches are large, filling, and for the most part, tasty. However, if you are a bread connoisseur, you might want to think twice. They only have bagged stale-ish bread. Maybe I'm missing one of the key bread offerings or the secret password to get better bread, but I feel like decent sandwich places should at least get freshly baked bread or do it in house. Heck, even Subway does it. So I rate Stuffed Inn as average..good sandwich toppings and menu assortment, but lacking in the bread department.
Yummy sandwiches for pretty cheap prices in comparison to the $8+ I normally spend at Genova's. I've spent many an undergrad lunch here. It's also super cute on the inside.

Everything here is super fresh, delicious, and college-student-priced. My favorite lunch sandwich ever is the Normal Ned's (avocado) and their egg salad sandwich is light and delicious as well. They've convinced me into loving split pea soup, and I've never found wilted lettuce (common problem in berkeley) in my meals.

To top it all off, the service is very friendly and efficient. Also! I love this Level Up app they now support (it's handy to pay with my phone).

Really disappointed the first time I got here. I did absolutely not understant what the waitress was telling me. She could,nt get what I was saying either. That resulted in a choice of sandwich I was not satisfied with and a bad experience overall.

That could have ended it and have earned them a 2-star rating. However, I got back following Yelpers and friends. And the next experiences (note the s) was much more satisfying.

I tried the Egg-salad sandwich which is really satisfying and the rostbeef sandwich which is classic but good. Family sandwiches you can easily make at home but fresh enough, not too expensive and next to the lab. 

The difference probably comes from the soup, which at $2 really made a nice side and complete the meal.

At prices this low, pretty much everything tastes good.  Stick with the sandwiches (egg salad!) because the soup tastes like congealed air.  I had to give it full points because of the bus-'boy': a dear, elderly Chinese man who keeps earphones in at all time and will smile at you before he collects your trash.

Normal Ned's avocado with no sour cream (that is the weirdest thing to put on a sandwich, really). 

Vegetarian split pea soup, which I didn't even know existed.

The cookies look really good. Someday.

Yay, I like sandwiches and i like puns. Clearly I am a fan of the Stuffed Inn.

I really appreciate that they have super silly names for their sandwiches (the Hemmingway is a Tuna sandwich??  He liked the ocean... I get it! So clever). 

Anyway, I recommend the pastrami and cheese or the veggie sandwich. Either way, all the sandwiches are nice and big (perhaps I would call... STUFFED?)

Salads are yummy and I really do enjoy the split pea soup. Friendly local restaurant that all cal students should try!

Ughh I am hungry just thinking about this. PLEASE GIVE ME SOME NOW.

This stretch of Euclid is interesting. It looks like it used to be hopping, (or maybe it is when UC is in session) but is kind of depressed feeling with a lot of empty buildings/vacant businesses. 

We were searching for a quick snack before doing some physical labor that involved furniture, boxes and a truck. 

I had my doubts about Stuffed Inn, but I was craving a sandwich. The place looks like an institution, but is kind of dirty feeling. I usually seek out hole-in-the-wall places, but for some reason this seemed not ok, especially with perishable sandwich condiments. 

Despite my apprehension about rancid mayo, I went with the egg salad on rye. It was surprisingly good. Not too much mayo and just the right amount of mustardy zip. 

Stuffed Inn is dirt cheap, which I'm sure is appealing to all of the UC students.

i just don't get the whole intermezzo HYPE...i mean, it's JUST a salad. get over it. i don't even think it tastes that good....poppyseed dressing and all...just tastes like dirt to me. i would much rather walk up a couple hills to euclid and enjoy a scrumptuous sandwich at the stuffed inn with one of their tasty soups. i used to LOVE their turkey and avocado sandwich. the only downside is i think they named that sandwich "the hemingway" who's definitely not my favorite author. Whatever...that's beside the point. It's SUPER affordable and you can even grab a tasty coffee from either brewed awakening or nefeli on your way out too. superb!
A great place to get a delicious sandwich!!! my fav is the Bryan sandwich! yum!!

Used to come here at least twice a week on the way to Soda.

- Great sandwiches!  The turkey and avocado is my favorite.  Fits easily into your backpack.

- Usually got a Sunrise Salad.  Lots of fresh vegetables.  Avocado, which I love.  Plenty of sprouts.  Jack cheese.  But most of all, the amazing ranch/sour cream dressing.  Haven't had anything else like it.

- Who knew that Split Pea Soup could taste good?  I don't know what possessed me to try it the first time.  Try it!

- Damn those cookies which stare at you as you wait in line.  Always ended up picking up two.

Besides the food:
- Inexpensive, even for Berkeley.

- They accept credit cards.  Avoid that ATM trip.

- Great, friendly staff.  They remember you.

- Lots of seating to enjoy a leisurely meal or hang with friends.

Sandwiches ~$5, chips and drinks ~$1, soup for ~$2, and fast and friendly service. This is the best place to get sandwiches on Northside, and you can pay with credit card.

As for soups, I liked the corn chowder, clam chowder, and chicken noodle. Don't get the tomato soup.

I've become a creature of habit here, which is the reverse of my normal, meandering-about-the-menus style.  So that must say something about the quality of what I've found and settled upon:

The avocado turkey has a tasteful amount of sour cream (doesn't make you feel icky like a mouthful from a not-sufficiently-diversified burrito bite), which is the secret to it's consistency.  

I guess some say there's a secret ingredient, but I don't like that very much, I guess my secret irrational fear is that the secret ingredient is spit from the head chef (who is the only irreplaceable cog in the machine hmmmm) or hair from the cat out back (that's why no other restaurant has it), and ok maybe i've just ruined secret ingredients for you for the rest of your life, but hey, maybe they're keeping IT hidden from the public for a REASON.

If there is a secret ingredient, it is delicious, but I think the oomph added by the sour cream is all the mojo they need.    

The split pea soup is so thick, and speaks for itself.  I don't have enough experience with various degrees of split pea soup, so no connoisseurial yammer, but, yah, it's flavorful and filling (for a soup).

Nothing really wrong with the place, and the sandwiches are rich and wonderful, but as far as sandwich places go, this doesn't get the 5th star.  (Maybe I just get off on being withholding)

I was waiting in line, looking at the large board featuring all their sandwiches which are named after people. I ordered Bernstein's Big Hot Double Pastrami and Cheese sandwich... This is one tasty sandwich with plenty of meat. Avocado seems to be what most other people like about this place (i.e. Big Ned's). I strongly dislike avocado, so I tried Bernstein's Big Hot on dark rye. This was so good. Classic looking sandwich with sprouts, lettuce, tomato, pepperoncini, and pickles. The pastrami was flavorful and tender. The dark rye was tasty as well. The one negative thing about my sandwich was the structural integrity of the bread itself. It seemed to want to fall apart after each bite. Other than that, this quaint little shop has me hooked and I will be coming back for sure to try their clam chowder and split pea soup. 5 STARS!

Since I work close by, I go here regularly for lunch. They have a good variety of sandwiches, salads, and soups for reasonable prices. As others have said, the staff is very friendly and they know what I tend to order. Lines can get long at noon, but they usually move quickly. I don't wait long at all if I get there 15 minutes before or after the peak lunch hour. I recommend the tomato-barley soup.

Great bread. Fresh, just out of the oven, cookies for 75 cents. Slices of avocado and a surprising cream cheese/sour cream/secret ingredient dressing on the great bread, followed by the 75 cent cookie, made for a satisfying lunch. I've only been a few times for a complete lunch, but I go back for the cookies all the time.

Sunny day??? Grab a freshly made sandwich from here, eat it on Memorial Glade, bask under the warmth of the sun and realize how great it feels to procrastinate!

Sandwiches here are typical ones you can make yourself at home, but let's face it, we're busy college students and don't have time to wake up early enough to pack our own lunches anymore.  

Prices hover around $5.  You first choose the type of sandwich you want from the menu, then choose from a variety of bread, cheeses, and extra ingredients that you want.  My personal favorite is the egg salad on wheat w/ provolone, lettuce/tomato, sprouts, and avocado...(yea the avocado texture is lost in the egg salad but I still love my avocados teehee).  Soups are great as well; they serve a pretty tasty, hearty tomato-based veggie soup.  

Definitely go to this place if you're cash strapped and looking for a healthy meal.

Love love love.  It took about two years before I finally went there myself instead of just complaining about their delivery sandwiches being a bit soggy, but now I just can't stop thinking about a delicious stuffed inn sandwich full to the brim with sweet avocado goodness.  Somehow they always manage to have delicious avocado, which is great on the Ned's (avocado, cucumber, special sour cream sauce), big Ned's (Ned's plus cheese), or the mother of all california sandwiches, the Farrah's - turkey, avocado, sprouts, tomato on wheat bread goodness.  Sometimes the line can get a little long, and sometimes the cookies make me feel a little sick, but the people who work there are so nice, the prices are reasonable, and the line usually moves reasonably quickly.  The soup is also pretty great too - I'm a big fan of the split pea, which tastes a little like smoky bacony goodness but is actually totally vegetarian.  I love you stuffed inn!  I'm sorry it took me so long to appreciate your majesty, but I hope you never change.

To be fair, I haven't been to The Stuffed Inn for a good couple of years, but honestly, the experience I had then still gives me an aftershock of nausea every time I pass their storefront. 

As a roast beef connoisseur, of course I had to try theirs. I got a rb sandwich and potato salad. The roast beef was unmemorable, bland, but edible, all that. What happened after has stuck with me: violent, floor-hugging, food-poisoning. Like, BFF with the floor of my community dorm bathroom  that previously I hadn't even wanted to put my bare feet on. 

So, I would not recommend. Unless you and your bathroom floor have been drifting apart and you need one of those "we'll get through it together"  experiences.

This is the place to go when you need comfort food after non feeling so great about that engineering exam you just took.  

It's also a good place when you are in the mood for something healthy!  

The soup is decent, it's filling but not always the most flavorful.  Sandwiches are great.  
I like their iced tea a lot for some reason.

I love this place.  Cheap, WHOLE FOOD (homemade soup, real salad dressing, homemade croutons, lemons from the owners tree for iced tea) and relatively fast.  I always get a salad - sometimes a big green, sometimes a sunrise.  The Sunrise has $5 worth of avocado in it alone and it only costs $5.75.  Fresh, delicious.... were it not for the annoying Cal lunchtime rush I'd go everyday.

The most attractive thing about the Stuffed Inn has to be the prices, which are the fairest in the area. The sandwiches are good, though the fact that they use the same bread as my college's dining hall is a little off-putting. Avocado is abundant on the menu and its inclusion on the generous Sunrise salad should be noted.

One thing, though: All three times I had the potato salad it's given me a stomach ache (don't ask me why I kept trying it).

If you haven't been to Stuffed Inn, shame on you!  Just kidding.  Please go though.  You'll know what you've been missing out on.

I haven't been disappointed with any of my orders and I try to mix it up!  If you eat in, for extra happiness, get a warm sandwich.  Don't be picky either!  For a low price, you can get all the add-ins (tomato, lettuce, mayo, mustard, sprouts, onions, jalapenos).

My favorites:
- Pastrami sandwich
- Turkey avocado
- Chicken noodle soup.

On my most recent visit, I just recovered from a terrible flu.  So as a treat, I got the pastrami on light rye with swiss cheese and a side of chicken noodle soup (only $2 extra) + all the house made croutons you would ever want.  One sip of the soup and it was clear to say that I am never going to SF Soup again because Stuffed Inn stole my heart.  At the end of it all, I was STUFFED.  5 stars hands down.

I've only had Stuffed Inn's ..er... *stuff* delivered; I've never eaten there.  That's a good point in itself, since my work is pretty inconveniently located and very few restaurants will deliver without an outrageous surcharge. 

Anyhow, I have to say the first thing that is notable is the prices.  Really, really low prices.  

Their menu's cute, the old named sandwiches bit gives it some character.  If you need your sandwich shop to have 'character'.

I wouldn't advise having their hot sandwiches delivered;  they just wrap it up in foil so they might get a little soggy.  Still pretty tasty, though, and the french roll still had a nice crunch on the outside.  The wheat was a lost cause.

The sandwiches are a generous size, and at these prices, you really can't go wrong.

I have eaten far too many stuffed inn sandwiches since I've been in Berkeley.  It's kind of embarrassing.

It's a reasonable place to have a cheap and fast lunch, but their sandwiches are nothing that you couldn't just make yourself with minimal effort, and even less money.  They're well liked for their clam chowder, which is actually pretty good, but don't expect a fresh seafood experience.  It's good because it's rich and creamy.

Quick summary: mediocre sandwiches, decent soup, and reasonable prices.  If you are a student at Berkeley, then you will inevitably eat here at least sometimes, but don't make the trip from too far away; you can probably do better.

2nd time here. First time 2 years ago, got a good avocado turkey sandwich. That was my first sandwich with sprouts, so I was impressed and thought it was really good.

This time I got tuna on onion roll with sprouts, tomatoes, pickles, cucumbers, lettuce and mustard. Nice that you can customize toppings however you want (avocado and cheese are extra though). It was good, decent. Not anything spectacular though. Simple quick fast and cheap.

Split pea soup is good like others say it is. They have house made croutons too, but it's just their old bread baked, but it's cool that it's a mix of all their breads: rye wheat white etc.

The oatmeal raisin walnut cookie looks like an amazing scone (ie huge). Wish I coulda tried it but my friend's friend got the last one. Oh well, next time I'll be back with 90 cents! 

Service is friendly. Note: they bus for you so you can just leave your trays when you're done.

After being gone from Berkeley for over two years, the family at the Stuffed Inn remembered both me and my sandwich. We could talk, catch up a bit, and still not hold up the line. These folks rock. They definitely helped me make it through grad school, and I miss they daily return to sanity that the Stuffed Inn granted me.
Good cheap sandwiches. Love that all the veggie sandwiches come with avocado. Really want to try the soup sometime!

Not the best sandwiches, but the people there knew me well.  I came in and the owners (who were Filipino) would recite what I wanted.  There's this really old man that would clean the tables.  Quite cute.  The place is pretty spacious as well.  Friendly service, cheap hearty soups and nearby soda, what else could a girl ask for?

what's not to love about this place?
Prices are good.
Sandwiches are fully customizable.  You want a hot double pastrami and cheddar on dark rye, no mustard, easy on mayo, some sprouts, exploding with pepperocini? Oh you got it.  And they don't glare at you with heavy sigh like you're an anal bastard who customizes sandwiches.  It's like they're happy to give you exactly what you want.  Crazy, I know.
Oh and try the split pea soup. Seriously.  I'm not a soup person either, but this stuff could probably cure malaria AND diabetes, because it just is that good.
One last thing. I love the little elderly man who buses your table while you're frantically finishing physics homework.  I don't know what it is. I'm probably just kinda crazy.

As far as pastrami goes this place is a fail - it's just some packaged lunch meat with a gross iridescent tint.

However they have some other items that make this place A-Ok - namely the cookies and the split pea soup. Don't get the tomato soup, get the split pea soup; you'll be much happier. Don't forget an oatmeal chocolate chip cookie on the way out. 

The pastrami didn't impress and they didn't have rye bread (ran out they said.) - a major faux-pas for pastrami sandwiches. I think next time I would go with a meatloaf or roast beef.

"this sandwich is pretty good"

"YOUR MOM's sandwich is pretty good"

"actually, this is the mom's* sandwich" 

*mom's sandwich = meatloaf, cheese/lettuce/tomato, & ketch-up (or mayo if you prefer)

And they provide real, physical newspapers (remember those?) for afternoon reading material.

I like how this little sandwich shop has an old feel to it.  it's emphasized by the wood paneling and quaint set-up.  

i'll usually order a sandwich or bowl of soup, on hungrier days I order both, plus a cookie.  

besides the food being freakin' tasty (yummy breadsticks, too) and affordable, their staff is friendly and really knows how to make a great sandwich!

Years and years ago, when I was either working or matriculating 20 hours a day, I spent a lot of time near Euclid Ave. in Berkeley.  During those years, I spent many a lunchbreak studying and eating here and Bongo Burger, next door.  If it wasn't between noon and 1pm, there was plenty of seating, where I could crack open a few books and get a little work in over a combo-deli sandwich.

The staff was courteous and quick, and the food was great and reasonably priced.  This being more than a decade ago, I shouldn't say much more.

The only problem I had was that the hours were never late enough for me.  When "lunch" comes at 10pm, there weren't too many options.  Hopefully this has changed for the current crop of students.

To do it right: $7

Note that to do it right, you have to get soup too.  I had the split pea, which was good, but could have used a bit of salt in the form of pig or well, salt.  I also ordered a pastrami on light rye and just told the guy to make it how he liked it; he laughed.  In about a minute, I had a hot pastrami and swiss on soft rye with lettuce, onions, pickles, lots of spicy mustard, and a bit of jalapeno.  Nice touch.

The service was excellent--specifically, friendly and fast.  The seating looks a bit rundown, but it feels a little more comfortable that way.

Summary: Another highly recommended Euclid-based sandwich.

A gem.

Good food, great prices, very comfortable North Side location when you are no longer a freshman and want to get away from Telegraph.

You will find young students, old students, professors, staff and locals here - and most are repeat customers.

Ok ok, it should get 4 stars, but any place that is stiff this good in a college town after 20+ years deserves that extra star.  First time i came was when I was in college back in the mid 80's (yes, i am THAT old...sigh)  Used to live 2 blocks away fro almost 9 years and was a regular there and even then the SPlit Pea soup was THAT good, as was the Clam Chowder.  
Fast forward 20+ years after living away and abroad, I find myself in teh Eastbay again and so one day i opted to pop by Northside to see what was still there.  I was rewarded with finidng Stuffed in still there AND, the same people owning and running it (albeit a bit older than i remember ;) )

The Stuffedwich was just as i remembered it as was their Split pea.  I have made it an almost weekly place to stop by for lunch, despite having to drive down (feel a bit guilty a bit even after paying to offset the carbon emissions) but I really love this place.  Homey, down to earth sandwiched for both Ominivores and Herbivores.

Price has gone up a bit in 20 years but not by that much relatively speaking.  Using fresh ingredients to make the sandwiches and presented wit a smile, it is still one of the best values around.

Taste: 3
Value: -
Service: -

They always serve Stuffed Inn sandwiches at the BSAC meetings. I think the sandwiches are okay, but they're not anything special. It'd be nice if the cookies were fresh.

How have you all failed to mention the half-sandwich/cup-of-soup deal? It's like, $3.50, which is unbelievable these days. I used to have a low-paying, soul-sucking job on northside, and that cheap soup and sandwich combo saved my life on a daily basis. It's better to call in your order if you have to go there around lunchtime, though.

This place serves the best split pea soup in the bay area. It's the kind of place where they remember your name if you show up every month, and they're happy to see you. 

Excellent service, great food, and cheap prices - this is my favorite soup/sandwich shop hands down.

i prolly go to this place 4 times a week for lunch since i work in north campus. i still couldnt figure out why their sandwich taste so good giving they use all normal ingredients, nothing fancy. and the bread are just store brought ones. Anyways, i always order my sandwich w/ the soft sweet roll; personally i think the hard one is way tooo hard to chew and the soft sour roll is too sour for a sandwich. The line may be long between 12 and 1 but they work really fast; it usually take less than 10 minutes to wait in line until its my turn. I have tried their: tuna & cheese, beef & cucumber & sour cream, turkey & avocado, ham & egg salad, pastrami & cheese; they are all very very delicious. and they have tasty clam chowders on tuesday and friday as well.

My first visit to the Stuffed Inn was today.  Why?  Because there is always a line.  i could never figure out why there was a line out the door here, but not at the other restaurants that I frequent on the North side.  I now know.  You get delicious food, fast and cheap here.  The perfect place to go on a budget.

I LOVE going to this place for a quick and healthy lunch to go! The food is always fresh and made to order. The toppings are generous and if you order anything with deli meat in it, they seriously STUFF it full of it. It's seriously the real deal. Recently, I've been loving the egg salad sandwich. It's lighter than the deli-meat sandwiches so when I need to eat, but not extremely hungry, it's my best option. It's really good too!

The guy who makes the sandwiches is always super nice and friendly. Go for an early lunch before noon to avoid the long lines!

Soup worth hiking for.  The split pea, as others clearly attest, will make you yodel. But I have also relished every other soup they've served. Big  lumberjack bowlfuls too. They don't skimp.

I love how their versions of boring food that I would normally make myself somehow fulfills me deep down in the part of my soul that loves fairy-tales and wants to watch "The Courtship of Eddy's Father."  

I have my master's degree now.  I don't hang on Euclid anymore. But I will hike my ass and a five $ bill up the hill every now and again (through the little 3 Billy Goats Gruff path that goes over the creek - you know the one) and go home again to the Stuffed Inn.

During lunch you definitely have to "stuff inn" to this place in order to get your lunch.  It is quite cozy though, and I do have to say that I rather enjoyed  it.  The menu has a whole bunch of sandwiches to choose from, all of which have wonderful names.  My sandwich, the Normal Ned, had avocado and sprouts, plus everything else on it.  Everything includes the usual veggies and condiments plus pickles and hot peppers.  Oh I love my hot peppers!  The sandwich definitely hit the spot, and for the area, you get the biggest bang for your buck here.

I don't like coming here with a group here because service can get pretty slow. Every time I came here, there were two people behind the counter, and only one of them was making the sandwiches for everyone... so I try to avoid this place around noon. I usually get tuna sandwiches, and once in a while I get soup on the side since the sandwich and soup deal is pretty nice. Definitely a good, cheap, and healthier place for starving college students with a limited budget... even better for UC Berkeley engineers who live in Soda, Cory, Etcheverry, and other buildings on north side of campus.

The sandwiches here are always made so fresh. If you get avocado you can believe that it will be bright green. I always get the Farrah's sandwich with Turkey avocado and sour cream and cucumbers. Now that I've tried their sour cream and cucumber I am very satisfied. There's always a long line outside during lunch and I think it's worth the wait.

This place is also a small family owned shop and all of the staff there are very friendly and nice. I highly recommend stopping by for a quick sandwich that is made fresh to order.

I never ate on the north side of campus while I was at Cal and my younger sister really likes this place so we decided to have lunch here one day.

Decor is definitely drab and cold but the freshness of the food makes up for it.  I like how all the sandwiches have names to them.  My sister and I split the Normal Ned's (avocado and sprouts) on multigrain bread.  All the veggies were so fresh and you only end up shelling out about $4!

Service is super friendly and nice.

I would come back.

My favorite sandwich place in Berkeley.  Super friendly staff, and the man that makes sandwiches is really good at remembering people and what they like on their sandwiches.  My favorites are the meatloaf, the toona salad, and the pastrami.  I especially like it because I spend most of my day on the north side of the Berkeley campus, so it's convenient to go there. Prices are good, and the quality is consistent.

although cafe intermezzo on telegraph has far better food, stuffed inn still provides a decent salad/sandwich, but what really makes this place stand out is the service.  the asian guy who normally works the counter (whenever i'm there) is really friendly and almost always remembers what i order!

I remember my first meal on Euclid Ave.  I was staying at the Faculty Club on campus, but I was advised by a colleague to skip the free breakfast there and to get a really great meal at the 3 C's Cafe on Hearst (a bit above Euclid).  When I showed up at the 3 C's bright and early, I saw an encouraging sign on the door: "Breakfast served all day"!  That was great, but it turned out that the place didn't open until 10:30AM!

Not wanting to wait for several hours, I went around the corner and walked up Euclid.  There was a breakfast place with an open door; it's where Bongo Burger is now.  I ordered my meal (two eggs with an English muffin, perhaps).  I was alone in the place with the employee behind the counter.  She asked for my name and I told her.  Was she going to ask for more?  Not at all -- there was silence.  Why did she want to know my name?  "So I can call you when your breakfast is ready."  Sure enough, 10 minutes later I was treated to a chipper "Ken: breakfast!"

That establishment is long gone, and so is the 3 C's.  (I went back to the 3 C's many times to order mushroom and spinach crepes.  Our waitress was Audrey F.)  Cafe Espresso, which used to be on Hearst just below Euclid is now an office of UC.  (Its main attraction was that the food was so bad that there was always a free table at noon.)  The world has changed.  Northside has changed.

The Stuffed Inn remains the same.  I liked it when I first moved to Berkeley.  I even put up with the glacial pace of the line.  (People would write checks to pay for their sandwiches.)  I was last there a few days ago, at 2PM on a Saturday.  There were 3 people ahead of us, but 15 minutes passed before we got to the head of it.  ("If I order the Chinese chicken salad, what kind of dressing do I get?  Are there any nuts?")  I had the Big Ned's (an avocado sandwich).  It still tastes like Big Neds did in the old days, but I feel like I'm in a sandwich museum.  Whenever I come here (about once every six months), I kick myself for not waiting in line at Nefeli instead.

A quaint and usually quiet soup and sandwich joint tucked into the Euclid neighborhood, it gives you a real Northside experience with its rustic 70's-style wood paneling.  This place is really convenient and the prices are so reasonable here. They have an extensive menu of sandwiches named after famous literary and political figures and three or four soups are available in hot kettles, self-serve style, near the counter.  I highly recommend the split pea soup with a wheat demi-loaf for dipping.  I recall they used to have a great hot pastrami and swiss on rye as well.

5.5 Stars

This sandwich shop is owned by a fellow Pi Alpha Phi, so 1 star just for that.

As far as their sandwiches go, 4.5 stars.

I haven't actually tried many of their sandwiches, but their Turkey and Avocado is so delicious that it's almost too much of a risk for me to try anything else.

They use very fresh ingredients, freshness that you can actually taste. If you've ever had Vietnamese spring rolls before, and you know how good spring rolls give you that cool crisp refreshing kinda sensation, as if you just took your first sip of an ice cold 7-Up after days of wandering in the dessert with no water; well, their turkey and avocado sandwich emulates just that. 

I think the freshness has to do with the proportions of the ingredients in the sandwich since they are very generous with their avocado and alfalfa sprouts (yum yum). If I had to describe how the proportions in the sandwich worked out, just imagine how the basic food guide pyramid looks and then translate that into how it would look if the pyramid was actually a sandwich instead. It has just the right amount of everything.

It's also great that they offer like 10 different options for bread that you can choose for your sandwich, varying from like french roll to wheat to dark rye.

Oh, and did I mention the sandwich is only 5 bucks no tax?

So if you happen to be in the area and want a sandwich that can give your mouth that just brushed clean and fresh kinda feeling, please pick up a sandwich here. It'd almost be a disfavor to yourself not to.

Well I've been eating here pretty much every week for the last few months and have grown to love it. I usually eat their soups (the clam chowder is the best) and their salads. There's always a line through the door which shows good business), so to avoid the lines go before 12p or after 1p. 

Random:
I like that they don't charge a fee or have a min fee to use your debit/credit card too.

This place is always a nice break from my job on North Campus. Pretty standard "classy" sandwich fare--e.g. sprouts, choice of mustards, various breads--with quality deli meats so your lunch is usually as good as your choice of toppings.  Daily soup offerings split pea and tomato barley are satisfying and better than average. Salads are pretty typical diner-style food; good, but the chicken is occasionally rubbery. My typical lunch is a turkey or salami and cheese sandwich, chips and a bottle of Martinelli's sparkling apple juice--a simple meal that hits the spot. I sometimes grab one of their oatmeal chocolate chip cookies, which are really unique in texture and are one of my favorite snacks in Berkeley.

Note that Stuffed Inn can get pretty crowded around lunchtime (1130-2) as scientists from LBL and professors from UCB file in for soup and a sandwich, so avoid these hours if you can. 

This place serves its purpose as a Berkeley lunch counter very well, but long waits can be annoying when you're just looking to grab a quick bite. Three stars.

My review is based SOLEY on their DELICIOUS GREEN PEA SOUP.

Gluten-free/Vegetarian/Vegan Yelpers of Berkeley, rejoice! Alas, food we can eat without being sick for the next few days (or weeks)! 

Can't say much about their freshly made juice/smoothies or coffee, but if you are hungry and craving sandwich, salad or their DELICIOUS GREEN PEA SOUP, give this place is a chance.

Just a block up from the North Gate (Berkeley Campus) and a friendly owner who will greet you with a smile and if you go often enough, remember your too! :) Go, go, go!

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Hot damn, this place wins over any hoagie or cheesesteak that Northside has to offer. The food is fresh, service is fast, and the prices are competitive. And the sandwiches all have names!
