There are two doors: the one on the left is the entrance, and the one on the right is the exit from the dining area. You walk in past the Stuffed Inn Express, which has pre-made sandwiches. There is a counter to your left that is piled with fruit, and that's where you start. After staring at their large green menu (but be quick!), place your order to the man or woman behind the counter. They'll whip up your sandwich in a few minutes, and you walk down the counter to the cash register to pay. You can add a bowl of soup to your sandwich or salad for $2.25. If you're opting for a bowl of soup, you pay for the soup first. Behind you, there will be a small counter with three pots of soup and some ceramic bowls for your use. Ladle yourself a bowl of soup, sprinkle on some homemade croutons, and head to your right to the eating area.

Their eating area has 8 or so table, with 3 booths lining the side wall. The atmosphere is calming and laidback, with sunlight trickling in and pseudo shrubbery lining the walls. Most people order food to go, so it doesn't get too crowded.

My sandwich was made in 1.5 minutes, no joke. My friend's sandwich took about 4 minutes, since his was being toasted. TOASTED.

Menu: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/PUK0RoIvq8pgi38FSCg7cQ?select=BrzepQDiUXld-WlxZLKrVw

Sandwich customization: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/PUK0RoIvq8pgi38FSCg7cQ?select=kNhHTrddSicPhHF9Uz78Ig

|| F O O D ||

TURKEY & AVOCADO (Farrah's): [$5.25]
- I chose the onion roll, and boy was I glad I did! The onion roll is akin to an onion bagel sans the hole in the middle. The bread was soft and chewy, and the subtle onion bits on top were great!
- This sandwich is STUFFED with avocado! The avocado is mushed to the texture of guac, and it oozes out of your sandwich with each bite. The avocado isn't flavored much, but I always get avocado to add that smooth texture to my meal. Seriously, I've been saturating my diet with avocado!
- Large leaves of lettuce and tomato slices. I would have liked some more turkey though. But the turkey wasn't too salty as a deli meat, so that was appreciated c:
- Got me some sprouts in my sammich. With the avocado, it was a good addition. Mmm mmm healthy.

PASTRAMI & CHEESE (Ali): [$5]
- My friend chose the whole wheat bread, which is like your regular sandwich bread. But the smart boy got it TOASTED. And since he chose provolone as his cheese to pair with the pastrami, IT WAS INGENIOUS. There was enough melted cheese to completely smother the huge mound of pastrami in his sandwich, and with his few pieces of lettuce and tomato, it was a great, tasty sandwich.
- So much yummy pastrami! So much yummy cheese!
- I'm coming back to eat this one!!!

CLAM CHOWDER: [$2.25 with purchase of a sandwich]
- At first I thought it might be free refills, but my friend said it costs either $1.25 or $1.50 for another bowl. Boo :c
- I liked their soup, as it was very creamy and not as chunky as canned soup. It seemed like it had a hint of cream of corn to it though. There were some generous chunks of clam too.
- My friend said the soup was a bit too toned down in flavor, but that may have been because his pastrami & provolone sandwich was a kick to the taste buds in comparison to the soup. Then he said he liked Progresso clam chowder better, and I gave him this face: -___-
- Their homemade croutons are nice and unflavored, and they absorb soup at just the right rate to give it a slightly soggy/crunchy edge :P

|| C L O S U R E ||

The only competitor to the Stuffed Inn's sandwiches is the Hot Pastrami at Northside Cafe. But the prices here cannot be beat, and neither can the quality of the ingredients. With the perfect balance of bread, meat, cheese, veggies, and love, Stuffed Inn comes out as the top contender of Northside eateries for me.

I highly recommend the pastrami and cheese (aka Ali) with provolone, and mix it up with an onion roll! Ask for it TOASTED too!

Well, its almost 2 years later and I'm still in grad school and I still have their split pea soup coursing through my veins. 

The soup is now $2.25, still a serious bargain.

super yummy sandwiches.

the bread is always fresh, the middles are always stuffed full & the dude making sandwiches always gets it right. combined with chips & juice, it's really an almost perfect lunch.

I don't know what inspired me to purchase split pea soup on a hot day like today from the stuffed inn. I must preface this by first saying that I usually hate split pea soup and think it's one of the most vile things ever created aside from chocolate chip muffins, beets, SUVs and Vista.

But today I got a to go bowl of split pea soup and a mini wheat loaf because, being a student, I had exactly $3 cash on me at the time and there was very little food in my house. Their sandwiches were cheap too (around $4 something) but the soup was the only thing in my price range and the other choices of corn chowder and tomato all seemed less appealing).

I took it home and it was one of the greatest split pea soups I've ever had! It was creamy while still being vegan (impressive) and I actually enjoyed it and ate every bite. I loved the soup and the 60 cent mini wheat loaf had a slight honey sweetness that was light, fluffy, and not overpowering. It was a full, filling meal for only $2.85, and on a student budget that's really spectacular.

There's not a lot of seating room (but in a place called the Stuffed Inn you shouldn't expect it). They had a sign hat talked about clam chowder but there was no clam chowder available. Additionally, if you eat in store they only charge $1 for a refill on a second bowl of soup, which is a great plus if you're that hungry. It would have been a lot better if it had actually been soup weather, but it was still good.

I know it's not the greatest place around, but I'm a fan of any place that can make me like split pea soup.

i love split pea soup, and their split pea is delicious!  chunky, hearty and savory - mmm mmm good!  their caesar salad is also worth a mention.

but what's really worth a mention is what a steal this place is!  for two, we split a salad, ordered two soups, and a cookie, which amounted to under $11.  awesome.

Great sandwiches.  Fairly priced.  Come early before noon or expect a line out the door!  Loved that they put sprouts on the sandwich.  I got the King arthur which I would reccomend!   Most sandwiches will set you back 5 bucks!

Ive always want to try smart Alecs and I eventually did with a friend when we met up to catch up. I usually go to cafe intermezzo for my big fat delicious salads but ever since it close down ive been desperately scrambling to find a replacement. I got the garden delight salad and it was okay. It wasn't out of the world but it did do the job and ended up lasting me a couple more meals because of its size. I haven't tried anything else but their garlic fries are pretty good.

I would go here for burgers, but definitely not again for salads. Their salads are just lettuce and cucumbers, absolutely nothing compared to Intermezzo. If you want a good salad, please, go to Intermezzo right down the street. And.. if you absolutely insist on getting a salad here, at least get the corn bread rather than the wheat bread. The corn bread is fresh baked and the wheat bread is just a slice of oroweat like sandwich bread.  Their burgers are pretty good. Not too fatty, yet juicy and tender. And the idea that the bun is whole wheat sort of makes burger eating a healthy thing.

Bring a test with an A and receive a free order of garlic with any order!

P.S. Be careful when you're around the area, especially at night. My friend got punched in the face for absolutely no reason right outside by a drunk. He's ok, so were his expensive glasses. Wtf tho.

I've been going to Smart Alec's for 8 years now.  You can beat their prices for the quality and quantity of food you get.  Some of my favorites are: Big A Burger Combo, Tofu Salad, and Cornbread.  The only thing I don't like on their menu is the smoothies.  This is some tasty, if a bit "granola" food.

everything seems healthy to me. there's nothing wrong with that. where they fail is that everything tastes like paper. all the food is flavorless. i had to use salt and ketchup and soak my food in it. It was pretty depressing eating here.

i appreciate that they aim to be healthy, but at least make the food taste good.
All I can say is CORNBREAD is amazing and for that alone I will give five stars
Love this palce and the food. esp the VEGAN BROWNIES
For the burger and fries cravings without the guilt.

Not totally vegetarian, but lots of veggie options. It used to be good, when it was the only restaurant, but once it opened a branch in WC, the quality went down. I loved their fresh breads, but last time I went, it was pre-processed bread. Their air-baked garlic fries and chowders are good though.

I have to start out by saying I was a skeptic. This restaurant calls itself smart fast food. Now that's a misnomer if I've ever seen one! 

I give this place a try by turning in my History blue book from my midterm. Apparently free fries for each A means you must have a non-Scantron, blue book exam in which you've gotten an A with a $3.95 or more purchase. It was my first time and I made that clear so I got my small garlic fries for free, thankfully. The garlic fries were amazing. It still surprises me that I can get garlic fries and regular fries for the same price. I have to say that I was definitely pleased with all the garlic that they put on my fries. I'm just so used to getting ripped off for garlic fries when all they really do is scoop out some garlic from a jar and shake a bag. 

I came back with my roommate when we were running errands together. I got the burger combo meal with some garlic fries yet again. I was definitely pleased with my burger that was just oh so juicy. The garlic fries, again, did nothing but please my stomach. I got my first stamp and I can't wait to get some of that corn chowder that I've heard so much about! 

Smart Alec's, while I doubted you, I have realized that you are pretty awesome. If only you were a bit neater, your bathroom was cleaner and more easier to get into, you accepted credit cards, and your employees would be kinder.

This place is a great choice fro someone on a budget but also watches their waist line. Its also god for that person that just likes good food. i've been going here my entire stay @ Cal. Its right on the corner of Durant & Telegraph so its not too far for students to go right before class starts. 

What I dig most about this place is the atmospheres and the price. 1/2 a sandwich and a soup for 5.44? I'm down! Their veggie burger is better than Boca and shits of the Garden burger. Their Hummus sandwich is also off the chain. But what I find to be the best combo...1/2 a chicken breast sandwich with a bowl of the corn chowder that just happen to come with a great big slab of cornbread to make this lil black girl proud. 

And in closing ladies and gentleman, this is the only place that you can A. get guilt free fries & B. not get charged extra for the wonderful dollop of garlics and parsley!

P.S bring in a test with an A or better on it and you will get a free basket of fries! Sorry scantrons don't count! 

Hey they don't call it Smart A+lek's for nothin!

Atmosphere is crummy (although not as much on a nice sunny day), but food is good.  I like it, and I like the salads a lot more than the CF chef's salad at Intermezzo (or whatever its called these days).  

Fries are really good.  

A very solid 3 stars.

Normally, I avoid fast food places like the PLAGUE. But these people almost make me wish I lived in Berkeley. I can have their veggie burger and fries almost every day of the week, and they have a tofu brownie to DIE for. I always HAVE to order it for dessert whenever I am there.  I love how low the prices are, as well!  I wish they would open up a branch in San Francisco to replace some of the sub-standard burger joints we have in this city.  But I know if they did come here the prices would be hiked way up. Yet and still I think about their food. A lot. When I am in Berkeley it's hard for me to go anywhere else, even though Berkeley is full of wonderful places to eat.  These guys are THAT good.

I visited Smart Alec's for the first time today... and yo ucan be sure it won't be the last. The food was NOT greasy, which is a first time for a fast food place. The fries (I got a few more than I should have, because I have a hard time keeping my blood sugar values low with potato) were surprising: not fried but air baked... they tasted great and they had almost no oil. It was the same with the burger I had.

The only downside: they only take cash, but at least they have an ATM across the street.

Smart Alec's is a great healthy option for people looking for vegetarian food at an affordable price. On our visit, my fiance and I shared a gourmet veggie burger with basil pesto and a side of large fries. We spent just over 7 dollars and couldn't finish all of our food. 

The fries are just over 2 dollars, and you easily get enough to feed 3 people. We got the garlic on the side, but I would imagine that the garlic fries are excellent. 

The reason I am giving it 4 stars is based on the basil pesto on the veggie burger. The flavor of the burger was stronger than the pesto, and the pesto was quite thin to be used on a burger. I think that the BBQ veggie would be much better... other than this slight misstep, we had a good meal for a great price.

The service is also good and the staff is nice with very speedy service.

Taste: 3
Value: 5
Service: 4

I've been to Smart Alec's over 20 times. I know that because I've gotten two of their frequent diner cards completely stamped. I guess I just really wanted that free bowl of soup and didn't care that I liked Smart Alec's less and less with each visit? 

That said, I've probably gotten their half chicken breast and corn chowder soup combo about 15 times, trying out their Big B, Basil Chicken burger, turkey sandwich, eggplant melt, and potato leek soup the other times. Oh, and their fries too.

The food's okay, but after going so many times, I'm totally sick of it and won't be going back. Sure, the food's pretty healthy. However, healthy food rarely tastes really good, and this place is no exception. If I really wanted a good-tasting burger, I'd probably drop by Bongo a couple blocks away.

I love this place!

So after passing by Smart Alec's a few times, I decided to stop by when I finally had a bit of time in the area. Their salads are HUGE. My friend got the Caesar, and was barely able to finish it, so she took it for lunch the next day. I ordered the Basil Chicken burger, and a hefty piece of cornbread. The burger was a bit dry, but that can be expected from chicken, so I just asked for more sauce. The plethora of lettuce, tomatoes and onions was a plus as well. Maybe I gave them such a high rating because of the cornbread. After a healthy meal, I didn't feel guilty after eating the whole piece of what is usually my ultimate food-guilty-pleasure.

Sure, the burgers are good, but there are a lot of other items on the menu that really hit the spot when you are too exhausted to cook after class. This place was my go-to spot for delicious soups when I was sick with a cold. All of them are oh so yummy (my favorite was the corn chowder), and coupled with the cornbread, Smart Alec's makes for good takeout/lunch.

Plus their "special sauce" is better than In and Out's. No joke.

I ate at this place the first time I visited Berkeley and found myself fairly disgusted. If I still liked fries, I would recommend the garlic fries. Otherwise, I got a sandwich (it was either tuna or roast beef, I forgot) and remember that it was a terrible sandwich. Too much dressing (probably mustard) that made it taste really odd. The tables seemed pretty dirty, even though there were barely any customers in the store at the time. I've heard from friends that the salads are really good though, so I wouldn't mind giving the restaurant a second shot. But I feel like there are much better places to eat, especially with IB Hoagies just across the street.

The food here is fresh, often organic, and good quality. However, the taste is just okay. 

They have awesome garlic fries and corn chowder though. Get them here and go next door for a good hoagie at IB Hoagies.
Burgers are ok, but fries not fat, so not tasty and dry. Not my favourite place for this kind of food!
Delicious...and healthy!

I always come here and get the corn chowder. It's dairy free!! I don't believe it. I also love the cornbread that comes with it. It's kinda grainier than other cornbreads, but that's why I love it. Sometimes I go in just to buy a piece of cornbread. 

More recently my friend discovered the sesame tofu salad. I've been ordering that a lot too, it's really good! Sometimes they put too much dressing though. I always order the half salad and am full after. The full is enormous. I'm also a fan of the cranberry turkey sandwich. For some reason I've never gotten around to trying the burgers, I should one day. 

I only get fries when I get an A. Bring an A grade and they give you fries for free :D

(vegetarian reviewer)

I used to come here a lot because serving sizes are nice and large (I have a big appetite), and I love their cornbread/chili combination. The atmosphere is pretty nice, too.

Unfortunately, when I came in to buy my girlfriend a dinner right after Christmas break, the lettuce in our salad was frozen. Not exactly a great casual date. Maybe they froze food over break when the students weren't around to create less waste or something. But my appetite for Smart Alec's has been pretty much filled for now.

I've been to Berkeley many times, and I've always passed by Smart Alec's. It never really appealed to me though since I'm not a burger kind of person. This visit around, I ate there, and I thoroughly enjoyed myself. It's good, considering that it's relatively healthy and how fast they give you your food (even during the lunch rush, they were speedy). The corn chowder was delicious and both of the sandwiches that I got were quite tasty (first time: eggplant, second time: grilled chicken). 

I did have a few complaints though: all the breads are way too dry, which is probably a side effect of trying to be healthy, and the french fries were so-so (again, probably a side effect of trying to be healthy). I wouldn't say the fries were cardboard; they just lacked consistency: some of them were way overcrisp, some of them were soggy, and some of them were almost comparable to deep fried french fries.

Overpriced? Definitely not compared to places in San Diego. I paid $7 for the 1/2 soup and 1/2 sandwich combo, and I was stuffed for the rest of the day. The same thing in San Diego would give me a soup half the size, no corn bread, and a much less filling sandwich.

I wish they had an Alec's down in San Diego.

Like Intermezzo, their salads are enormous. I like 'em better, though, because the wheatberries are a nice touch and the chicken breast is reaaaaalllly good and almost always warm. I just skip the bread. Also, diet Coke machine. A+.

I have to give kudos to Smart Alec's for making the Big A burger their veggie burger

(lol my roommate sometimes forgot that the Big A burger was a veggie patty and would come home saying "OH GOD NOOO!!! its not meat! bleh!")

but the veggie patty isn't the greatest....it has a sort of weird after taste that obviously reminds you that you are NOT eating meat.

The other sandwiches are pretty good and the soups are decent, my favorite sandwiches are the eggplant melt and the marinated tofu.

I've only been here once, but I got the veggie burger with avocado, and I still think about it all the time. It was perfection.
The garlic fries are also delicious, if you like garlic (I love garlic).
I love that it offers options for everyone--vegetarians, vegans, and omnivores--and there were plenty of delicious sounding things on the menu that I'd love to try again.
The only reason they don't get 5 stars is because the staff isn't the friendliest, and the bathroom is reallyyy dirty.

I literally ate this 7 days a week while at Cal....

To this day, I still travel to the east bay just for a slice of the cornbread.  Well priced, good portions, and healthy options!

Definitely worth dropping by!

When I lived in Berkeley, I used to stop by Smart Alec's all the time to pick up a piece of their cornbread. No one else makes their cornbread the way Smart Alec's does. It's super dense and moist, with a touch of sweet. Perfect.

I've tried their soups, salads and burgers. They're decent, but nothing special.

Smart Alec's is not a restaurant I would die to go to. Burgers and salads seem to just be average or below average. Other sandwiches seem to be just ordinary. The one thing I do like, however, is the soup. Particularly, the Potato Leek soup is something that I have found to be a good comfort food with a side of cornbread. Their cornbread is better than I anticipated and it goes really well with their soups.

I am madly in love with the corn bread here (yes, love is possible with Maize).  I think I go in there more for the corn bread than the great salads and I must say - decent veggie burger! The portions are out of control (and I love it!). I had their corn chowder and it was good, but I think I prefer the corn bread. Did I mention their awesome corn bread? LOL! Lately it seems I am in this place at least once a week. I tend to stick to the salads, but I plan to branch out - except with the corn bread. All in all, a great hangout to get healthy eats.

I think every Berkeley student has had Smart Alec's at least once.  I mean, it has the best location on Telegraph and it's hugeee. 

The food is pretty good.  It's nothing spectacular that you crave, but it's never bad.  When I can't think of something to eat, Smart Alec's is a good choice.  They have soup, salad, sandwiches, etc.  I usually go in for the salad because I try to tell myself that I'm healthy.  The full salad is huge for a pretty decent price as well.  

I also don't understand the hype of the cornbread, although I do find it a better selection than wheat bread - which is just one slice of regular wheat bread.  I usually try something different there each time because nothing has disappointed me here.  I like the chicken sesame salad the most but it could use more dressing but it has super duper muchacho amount of chicken!

I really don't think this place is that healthy, unless you're really diligent about salad preparation (ie keep it crouton-free), but I like it and go here all the time. Obviously, like Mattina, my review is contingent on not having a vermin experience, and it's probably only a matter of time. The cornbread, again, probably not that good for you, but they give you that big piece, so you have to get it. Like someone else said, you get sick of this place after a while, but after some time off it's safe to go back.

I had the sesame tofu salad and split it with my cousin because it was so huge.

It was good overall, except for the tofu which was way, way too salty. Both of us ended up eating everything but the tofu.

The cornbread was alright, not as great as some people here are saying, but then again I'm not the biggest fan of cornbread. It's alright!

When I'm in Berkeley around evening, I literally try to make room for this place (and that's probably a good idea, considering you almost get what you pay for.) It's not the most novel idea (traditional American fast food that won't clog your arteries) but damn if those veggie burgers don't leave me wanting more. The food is very delicious and I think vegetarians will be very pleased. Nonvegetarians, however, might be less forgiving.

DELICIOUS. but slightly expensive :(

I always get their salad, or half sandwich/half salad. Their roasted tofu or eggplant melt is to die for! I'm not as big a fan of their burgers... but still yummy. Their garlic fries are airy and delicious... and I can't help myself from their special sauce ;) Their cornbread is ridiculously dense (and oily) it can practically serve as a meal on its own... but I don't mind getting it with my meal ^_^

I personally like Intermezzo better for salads (just because it's larger and I get more ingredients ie avocado, kidney beans, better tasting egg) they get me here with the wheatberries and edamame. Once in a while I treat myself here, but if I really want to go for the healthy alternative, I say Intermezzo.

I love this place. Their salads are ENORMOUS (I can eat a lot, but I had to take half home), with good ingredients (WHEATBERRIES! I LOVE WHEATBERRIES!!!!) and incredibly cheap prices. Plus, the sliced wheat bread that came with my salad was amazing. I would kill someone to have that bread right now.
Another clever name. Good cornbread. Huge salads.

Smart Alecs is probably the only place on the planet where I feel safe eating "fast food." Most other places are frightening when it comes to ingredients, but these people have the right idea.
    The food is simple, clean, and relatively healthy. Eating birdseed and other macrobiotic material may be good for me, but I'd prefer to eat something that I'm excited about. The burgers are great, the salads are enormous, and the fries are pretty darn good for not being fried. I really like the combination meals, I always leave feeling satisfied, not weighed down and bloated.
    I find myself craving the strange dichotomy of "healthy fast food." I wish they were open LATE...

I ordered the Sesame Tofu Salad and it was quite large. They say that it's grilled marinated tofu, but for you Asians out there that know what I'm talking about, it's nothing more than the brown bean curd you can buy at Ranch 99. The sesame vinaigrette that they put into the salad is a bit on the sour side. Towards the end, the tofu really soaks up the vinaigrette and it becomes almost too sour to eat.

The corn bread, as all the other reviewers are saying, is really good. My only beef with it is that around dinner, the corn bread has been in the case for a good morning and whatnot so it's not as fresh as it could be. 

I'm a pretty health conscious person when it comes to eating, and I can say that the salad is not *too* bad. The crunchy noodles is not the best thing health wise. Also, save some calories by asking for dressing on the side. The corn bread you should definitely stay away from if you wanna save yourself at least 300 calories. The thing's huge, so I think 300 might actually be an underestimate. 

Generally, their food is not healthy. Intelligent Food is more marketing than truth. Most of their salads have fatty dressing, their soups are cream based, burgers are burgers more or less, doesn't matter where you get it from. Air baked fries are no different than fries at McDonald. If you get garlic, there's a really strong garlic smell/taste, but they're just as oily, if not more oily compared to McDonald.

I would definitely go again for the price ~$6.50 for a full salad and huge portion of cornbread is included. I wouldn't go again if I was trying to eat healthy.

It was ok for what it was.  Service was good, and the food was cheap. The salads looked pretty decent but I ordered the burger and garlic fries.  The burger had decent flavor but there was this weird metallic odor that lingered over the table and sort of stuck in the back of your throat.  I dont know if it was the garlic fries or the burger but it kind of annoyed me.  From the other reviews on here I'd say skip the garlic fries.  I think if you're trying to find a healthy option, there's better tasting food out there on the same street. Want burgers and fries?--just go to jack in the B and work out a little harder the next day.

"Mediocre" comes to mind. I've tried a few salads and sandwiches here, but they are all unmemorable. There are many cheaper and/or more delicious options nearby.

They only take cash, which can be annoying.

The only reason I come here is for the air-baked fries, but without garlic since all they do is dump a clove of crushed garlic on your fries. Just add your own salt/ pepper!

The fries are worth the trip though, if you are in the area.

Smart Alec's was one of the first places I that caught my eye when I attended Berkeley. For some reason though, I never got around to stepping in. Perhaps it was the intimidating line of people or the intoxicating smell of french fries that caused me to stay far, far away. 

Things changed once my close friend started working there though. From the very first moment my teeth sank into the oversized-soft-yet surprisingly-dense cornbread, I knew it was love at first bite. This affair continued throughout my two years there and I still dream about the cornbread. Sure, I've tried their famous air-baked fries and their eggplant melt sandwich and their salads but let me tell you... nothing, I mean nothing (at least in my opinion compares to the cornbread here). There were literally days that I just purely lived off the cornbread. Sure, it wasn't the healthiest of choices but it did the trick -- two pieces of cornbread a day was all I need to fuel my brain. 

I love this cornbread so much that when I went up a month ago to help my sister move-in to Berkeley (yay another Cal Bear!), I insisted that our first stop before anything was to stop by Smart Alecs. Of course, parking is a disaster so I literally just jumped out of the car and told my mom to circle around the block and pick me up. I jumped back into the car with two gorgeous servings of cornbread and started eating away. My sister, of course, had been dying to try these famous treats and let's just say it was also... love at first bite!

The main reason I'm giving this three stars instead of two is that it's so incredibly cheap. The food is definitely not "good." But getting an "A" burger and fries here is satisfying in a way that you only really understand if you're vegan and haven't had a burger-and-fries meal for twelve years. The smoothies, which are also vegan, are pretty tasty as well. It would be nice if they used fresh garlic, though, the stuff that comes on the garlic fries tastes like the pre-minced stuff from a jar. Yech.

I'm a vegetarian, so you'd think that this place would be right up my alley.  Unfortunately, it just isn't.  I don't understand why there's always so many people eating here, with better eats all around.  The food is good but bland and somewhat generic.

There are a lot of good, cheap ethnic places in the area that are a lot better and more flavorful in the same price range.
Solid burger, good soup, great lunch spot

To all those who bashed this place because you think it's wrongly called "healthy fast food" understand this: it's fast food. If you really want to be healthy, order the salad and quit looking for excuses to complain. It is FAST FOOD, burgers and all, but they do provide healthy alternatives to beefy burgers and greasy fries such as soups and salads.
I've never had any issues with the food. I usually order the avacado burger (with beef) and it's always tasted delicious. I took my dad there once while he was trying to lose weight and he ordered a salad, corn bread and water. The salad was big and we brought what wasn't eaten home as "linner" snack.
I really enjoy sitting at the big, opened windows in the summer time and people-watching as I eat my lunch.
For the most part, the employees are fairly friendly but usually don't engage in small-talk with the customers (not sure whether that's a good or bad thing).
Moral of the story: Smart Alecs = VASTLY better than McDonalds.
(Not that I, in any way, endorse the eating of McDonalds).
Even though I end up smelling like onions later, the big A burger and the chicken pesto burger never fail to satisfy! Fries are excellent too.

Smart Alec's is a pretty big disappointment as far as food goes. As far as fast, healthy food, I think they get their job done; but that is only based on the fact that I am assuming what I eat is actually healthy and that the service is relatively fast. What is more important is taste and experience, and I don't think either really qualifies for more than 2 stars here. The food I've had (salads, veggie burger, and soups) is generally flavorless. The environment is clean, but there's nothing warm or inviting about the place. After giving the place about 3 or 4 tries over the past few years, I'm resigned to not returning.

so many times when i go to berkeley i try to persuade myself to eat lunch somewhere else but just end up back here. it's so good, and cheap. i love the cornbread & the big slices of wheat toast that come with the salads. the salads are really big & they're good. the veggie burgers, regular burgers & baked fries are near mouth watering. i had the baked tofu and avocado sandwich last time i went. i wasn't too into the flavor of whatever the tofu had been marinated in, but i think lots of other people would like it, it just wasn't the flavor for me. this place is good. go there.

Healthy burgers and fries?!?!? What else do I have to say?
And their special sauce is really yummy too. That's why I always get a combo that includes fries so I can dip it in a cup of the sauce XP. I'm drooling just thinking about it haha.
What's more is that no matter how may orders that have, they are always super fast too!
The only thing for me is that I haven't tried showing them an A on any of my test because I know I would be kind of embarassed to do so just for some free fries.,.

Not sure how one can mess up a tossed green salad- but they did. No flavor and the lettuce was soggy. Why must you always use plastic - try eco-friendly "to-go" containers. 

Will not be returning.
Cheapish veggie burgers? Yes. Cheap fries? Yes. Dirty tables EVERY time I've been here? Yes. I still like the food though, will definitely return.

A well done, basics, menu makes this place another one I'd tack on to my frequent visits list!

Ordered a Special Burger combo w/ the fries and beef patty. Their hamburger is a very good, simple rendition that allows you to taste all the goodness of the meat of your choice. The wheat bun isn't too starchy, and the sun-dried tomato pesto really helped put this one into the excellent lunch category.

But far and above the thing to rave about is their air-popped fries! Talk about a healthy alternative to your oil-soaked goodness! These fries came out smoking hot, crispy on the outside, well seasoned and were just a pleasure! The weird thing was that although these fries were crispy, there wasn't any oil running around the bag. I got the garlic version, but on hindsight I should have gotten the plain fries for the sake of enjoying all the air-popped goodness! The garlic version essentially asks them to dump about 2 teaspoons of a chopped garlic/parsley mixture into the bag, and it isn't tossed so be prepared to do a little shaking yourself.

Overall, a great find for me. I'm glad I decided to just walk around and try something new. at $5.98 for a burger, fries, and a shake, this is a definite place I'm going to return to.

Really wonderful healthy food.  I've been here a few dozen times and have almost exclusively eaten the Superior Chef Salad.  (The only better salad is a chef salad from Cafe Mattina down the street.)  Really huge portion, excellent meat options (roasted turkey is very tasty), good mix of extras (edamame, sprouts, egg) and great dressings (sesame vinaigrette is my fav).

If everything was as good as the superior chef, it would get five starts.  The burger and fries can be kinda bland.  I know you are a healthy place, but that doesn't mean normally unhealthy food needs to lack flavor.  The garlic fries were unimpressive, just get regular fries.  Smoothies are really good, definitely worth a try.

Overall, one of the best choices for fresh, tasty food on Telegraph Ave.
I think most of their food is so-so. It's reasonably prices and you get it fast. I only go in for the salads- which are huge, the ingredients are fresh, and they fill you up.
Good fries. Okay service. Boring burgers. Always too crowded!

It's very average burgers for a premium price only because it's only mediocre [non-McDonald's] around. The only other option for burgers near campus is GBC, which isn't exactly much of a competition. So, it's not worth the price, but the only option if you want a halfway decent burger.

Their fries are better though than most places nearby, and are a filling snack. It's easy to grab and go. Expect to wait a little bit for the fries [not too long] but it's expected of fresher food.

I like this place, I really do. Everyone keeps saying how nasty the fries are but that was one of the first things I noticed-How good they were. I'm a fan. I love the burgers and sandwiches. I wouldn't get a salad because they actually don't look that fresh. looks like cosco salad if that makes since. The cornbread is amazing.
Smart Alec's cornbread, you are one of the things I miss most about Berkeley.

I wanted to like this place. I really did.

Smart Alec's seems to have a great reputation around town as a "healthy" restaurant, with organic, fresh food and all that shit. I usually see a lot of people in here, so I figured it must be good. 

I got the marinated tofu sandwich with avocado, and literally, everything about it was bad. I am definitely NOT a picky eater or a food/health snob in any way, but I could barely even stand to eat half of this sandwich. The tofu tasted like it was marinated in salt water with no flavor, and the avocado tasted like it was way past its prime. The bread was also pretty generic, cheap wheat sandwich bread, and overall, I don't think it was worth what I paid for it. My friend got a burger, and he said it was ok, but that he'd had way better burgers for $8. 

Service is pretty good, and the place is pretty clean, but I don't think that's enough for me to come back to this place again.
Hit or miss. Sometimes I love it. Sometimes it's dry as hell. Great fries, though. And I highly recommend the Vegetable Soup. Yum

Smart Alec's is great! I love the air baked fires. I don't know if they really are "healthier" than the fried counterparts, but they're sure just as yummy! I hear their cornbread is quite yum, but I haven't tried it. 

The burgers are quite good. It's a convenient location for students!

As a Cal student, this was my favorite restaurant on Telegraph. 

Why? Because it's fast, cheap, and good eats!

Combo of a great sandwich + salad or soup with your choice of cornbread or whole wheat slice for something under $8. 

I'm pretty sure I've gone through 20+ Smart Alec's cards already and have ventured their entire menu in the last many years, so here's a recap of my favorites:

--Sandwiches/Burgers--
1) Turkey + Cranberry Mayo: Sweet and savory all in one!
2) Tofu + Avocado: Always so heart-warming and wholesome, and the healthiest of their selections.
3) Eggplant + Basil Pesto + Cheese: grilled wonderfully, and always hits the spot when you want a hearty sandwich!!!
4) Big B Burger with Avocado: this is really fulfilling and hearty, too!

--Soups--
1) Potato Leeks
2) Corn Chowder
3) Chili

--Salads--
I always enjoy their cesar, but their honey mustard dressing is spectacular. 

--Other things--
The fries are AMAZING. Get the garlic fries and that special thousand-island influence dip of theirs and you're good to go!

Try ordering a bowl of their chili + their fries separately ...mm...

Rest assure you will be well satiated and won't feel guilty at all!

The food here is super plain. It's not super cheap, just convenient. The fries aren't super crispy, and the burgers aren't super juicy. Everything is just ok. I do like the soups on a cold day, but that's about it.

Their:

garlic air popped fries = bon!
corn bread = bon!
vegan burgers = their good with some avocado. yes.
potato clam chowder soup = yum!

And its cheap. :) And filling. Only thing about it - remember cash! But there's a BOA right across the street from it, so you should be good. :)
Oh, eww.  Cute name, baaad food.  Their fries taste like salty cardboard.  And yes, I *have* eaten salty cardboard before.  It tastes slightly better than Smart Alec's fries!

i just don't get what people see in this place.  all the food tastes like cardboard.  if you want a burger, go to raleigh's, and if you want sandwiches/salads, go to intermezzo...they're only 2 blocks away!!

Quick, decent, relatively healthy food.  I like their hummus and grilled eggplant sandwich, and their corn chowder is soooo creamy and awesome, especially with their corn bread.  I've tried the tofu salad and the chef salad, and both were decent.  I would have given four stars if they didn't have the cash only thing, but I guess since the atm is right across the street, it isn't such a big deal.

so, i lived in the apt's above smart alecs for a year. every morning the lobby would smell like a mixture of cornbread (which is delish) and garlic fries (not so much). so i woke up to strange smells...
but as for the food, its pretty good. portions are good and prices are good too. the vegeburger i think is over rated but its ok. the fries are good for being airbaked (whatever that means). i enjoy their smoothies and the corn chowder soup. it is a very hearty soup and fills you up more than you'd expect.
my friends who arent vegetarians love the burgers and chicken sandwiches.
it is VERY crowded during lunch time
Love love love the eggplant melt. Good salads & fries too. Healthy for you & your wallet

I had heard good things about this place, but was sadly disappointed with the experience i had here. Maybe it's because my expectations were too high that the only way things could go was down. 

I ordered an avocado burger and fries. The price was good and there was a lot of food, but the burger seemed premade and not freshly grilled. There wasn't much flavor in the burger, though there was plenty of avocado. Although i usually don't discriminate against burgers, this one just didn't impress me. I still ate it, but i would not go back. The fries were also terrible, i know they're air baked, but i think fries need to have some texture. My fries were just a soggy mess. Maybe i ordered the wrong thing, but i'm pretty sure this won't be my stop for burger and fries.

Let's get to the bad news first, and then the good news. There is only one NEGATIVE comment I have to make, so I'll get it out of the way.

HOLD YOUR BREATH IF YOU GO INTO THE BATHROOM! No, it's not like someone bombed the toilet 30 seconds before you went in. It's just a reeking smell of... bathroom? Horrible bathroom - comparable to the gas stations. Hidden in the corner that requires key to access, I really expected it to be more decently kept with air freshener or something.

Now for the good =) 

We were walking around Telegraph deciding what to eat. And I was told that they use good ingredients and cook in a healthier way. Burgers? Healthy? I'm down.

I ended up order the half grilled eggplant sandwich with a tossed green, and also a strawberry smoothie. Strawberry smoothie - like any other, but refreshing indeed. The eggplant sandwich was a good choice. The salad shocked me quit a bit, because it was HUGE for a half salad! And they definitely did not skimp on the ingredients or the dressing! The salad was already dressed and mixed (with a little too much I believe), so I'm glad they left the alfalfa and croutons undressed. It almost seemed like an entire salad to me! I don't like cornbread (never really have), so I don't know why I ordered it with my salad instead of wheat. I took a couple bites, and confirmed my prior feelings towards it. Other than that, it was a great deal for under $7 (the salad & the sandwich). 

Overall clean with plenty of tables. I can dig it. Minus the restroom.

Oh, I love Smart Alec's.  Though it may not be as healthy as it claims, the food tastes fresh and delicious.  I'm totally in love with the hummus sandwich - they have some of the most flavorful hummus I've tried in Berkeley.  The garlic fries are yummy, too, and you don't feel as guilty eating them.  I often end up dipping them in the hummus that ends up spilling out of my sandwich at some point.  Definately a messy experience, and the atmosphere is noisy and can get really crowded, but they have some amazing food and I've always had a place to sit in the restaurant.  My friend really loved her grilled eggplant sandwich, and they have yummy, huge salads here too, along with $1 thick slices of cornbread!  I've tried their potato leek soup as well and it was pretty standard but yum.

This was my favorite restaurant to go to in my stay at Berkeley. I came here for their soups and yes, I've tried all of them. The best ones are corn chowder and the chili; in the vegetable one you can see the grease so that grossed me out, the lentil one is inconsistent in quality, and sometimes the potato leek soup has too much potato. And here's a tip: always choose cornbread. It's so worth it!

Other things I've tried are their garlic fries and their Big A burger and Guacamole burger. ALL GOOD. omg i'm so hungry now..

This place is very close to campus and at an affordable price too! The service is very quick and their foods are all very healthy and yummy!

Smart Alec's is a great lunch time food. Everything is pretty fresh and made right when you order. Plus, they prepare the food quick, so it's a perfect place to go for a quick lunch between class. 

Their normal hamburgers are okay, just a plain hamburger that aren't any different from what you can bbq on your own grill. I would choose their chicken alternative, it has a pretty good sauce. 

If you order fries, order garlic fries, they put a heaping amount of garlic on the fries, so for garlic-lovers you will love it. 

Their salads are good and i love the corn bread that comes along with it.

I've gotten their tofu sandwich...it's pretty sour and I didn't like it so much but if you're a fan of that kind of thing, it's pretty good.
The thing I love about this place is the fries! I always come here to split a large garlic fries with a friend...huge order of fries for a dollar per person, quite a deal! :] The garlic is a bit strong but hey, they're garlic fries so they might as well do it right!

Cash only is annoying so I always come with lots of dollar bills ;D

Smart Alec's is my go-to lunch place close to campus. Their location is ideal (literally a block from campus!) and they always serve very fresh food. 

I have come here a ton of times as a UCB student. They give you free fries when you get A's and their corn bread is to die for. I remember I used to keep it in the fridge all the time and one day my roomie thought it was stale and threw it away and I was SO sad that she had to buy me desert to make up for it....:) 

I get their caesar salad with chicken all the time. Its very yummy and the dressing is wonderful. Their garlic fries are my other favorite... they're not as oily as garlic fries usually are. So tasty! The burgers are pretty good, comparable to other burger joints in the area (I prefer Bongo Burger). 

The service is decent... it's kind of self-service so I don't mind that. The decor is comparable to that of any other decent burger joint. A casual place to grab a good, healthy lunch!

You darn Smart Alec!

I literally go out of my way to taste their chicken cesar salads! They're giving less chicken these days but they include a side of corn bread - which is delicious! 

They definitely loose a star because their infamous veggie burger was horribly bland to me.

I used to stop by here semi frequently as a freshman. However I realized there are better places to try for burgers nearby in Berkeley.

The past two times I've come here, the buns have fallen apart, ripped, and were soggy. Just no. It's also pretty oily feeling, despite toting its name around as a healthy food place in Berkeley. I'm pretty sure the reason they're still in business is because its located really close to campus/the dorms, and the interior is huge. It's a nice place to sit down and eat. 

If you want better burgers though, I'd try Bongo Burger down on Dwight  or IB Hoagies on Durant near Asian Ghetto.

I only had the garlic fries, but it was pretty good... I can see this is the healthy choice on campus with a enormous staff. It seems that the way the prepare food is fresh and on the spot, so I guess it's reasonable so many people were behind the counter. Wasn't busy when I was there, but I can imagine it could be.

I wish this place was closer to me. My favorites are the garden delight salad, the corn chowder, the turkey sandwich (with cranberry mayo), and the air-baked french fries (free if you are a student and bring in an A paper/ exam from the current semester). I highly recommend Smart Alec's for healthy, quick, delicious food!

I waited 12 minutes for fries today!  Mid way through my wait I asked the workers what was going on.  They pretty much ignored me and went about goofing off. 11 minutes later and another order came up.  I was so mad.  I asked for my money back and vowed never to return.

this review is purely for the food and drink mentioned below:
last summer i was taking a language course at uc berkeley and pretty much every week i'd stop at smart alec's on my way back to the dorms. i'd get their grilled chicken sandwich with pesto mayo, letture, tomato, and red onion on a delish whole wheat bread and a berry wild smoothie. SUPER GOOD!!! it's been almost a year since i've left berkeley and i'm still craving that meal!

Woah did I just spend like $6 on a breakfast sandwich? 

I've been here for a couple of times during lunch and they have much better prices then. Their salad is great and even comes with corn bread. It's become my new salad place after Cafe Intermezzo burned down. The burgers are ok, they're big and filling but there are other places around with better burgers in my opinion. Although I do like that they have wheat burger buns instead of white burger buns, that's a plus.

Air-baked potatoes? What is this shit and why is it so delicious?
6 grams of fat as opposed to Jack-In-The-Box's 19 or so? 
As healthy as french fries can be while still tasting authentic.

The vegetarian burger was just aiight to me.
But my eggplant melt sealed the deal of digestion trust here.

I don't even give a care that they gave me a chicken-ish sandwich by accident, first.

Even though I've only had their Caesar Chicken Salad every time I've been there, I'm going to give it 4 stars because this place is legit. And plus, their Caesar Chicken Salad is good. 

You get great food for the small price you pay. Their serving portion is pretty big (I get full eating only HALF my salad plus a choice of two types of bread) and it tastes so fresh. Definitely not those wimpy, shrunken-looking lettuces you see at some restaurants. The location is also very convenient for college students who need a good place to eat before heading back to campus for class. 

I'm going to try their hummus sandwich next time I go. Oh, and their infamous garlic fries that I keep hearing about.

They only accept cash! Very inconvenient but it happens at some places. My family eats very healthy especially my husband. But the last time we were in Berkeley we went with my little brother in-laws who don't share our taste and believes with food. So Smart Alec's was an awesome choice! We were happy and they were happy. Did feel like we were feeding them junk but they still were able to get food they enjoyed. The place is fast foodish (yeah I just made up a word ;) ) but much more healthier and better quality. 

Items to try: Baked Garlic fries and the Big B Burger! Yum!

Against the recommendation of others, I decided to try this place out. The chicken sandwich was great and the fries weren't greasy. Instead of the usual post-lunch food coma, I felt lively for the rest of the afternoon! Definitely will go again!

This is a great place for healthy and fast food.  Usually, I'm not a huge fan of veggie burgers but the veggie burgers at Smart Alec's are great and inexpensive.  There are plenty of vegetarian and meat options at Smart Alec's.

I used to eat here pretty much every other day with my roommates, so I've tried most of what they have to offer.  We'd trade off between Chipotle and Smart Alec's, trying to cleanse our bodies of all the saturated fat from Chipotle by opting for a guilt-free lunch the next day at Smart Alec's.

Let's break it down now, shall we?

Salads:  They're OK at best, so if you're looking for a good salad I'd suggest you go a couple of blocks down Telegraph to Intermezzo, which I guess is now called Matina.

Sandwiches:  I'd really only suggest the chicken sandwich, the others are a bit bland and tasteless.  The sandwiches are also a bit pricey for what they are.

Soups:  Stick with the corn chowder.  I'm not sure how a vegan soup can be so creamy, and I've always been afraid to ask.

Now, to the good stuff:  The burgers aren't bad and come out pretty quickly.  I used to be a hardcore carnivore, but I've been trying to change my eating habits so that I can live past the age of 40, and the veggie burger here isn't bad either.  The air-baked fries are usually a hit or miss.  They taste pretty amazing for non-fried fries (is there such a thing?) when they're freshly made, but when they've cooled, they take on kind of a cardboard-like consistency :(.

Still, I'm a huge potato addict, so I used to make a stop at Smart Alec's before heading back to my apartment from campus just for hot air-baked fries + Smart Alec's "special sauce" (which I think is really just a variation of Thousand Island like all of California's burger joints' "special sauces").

My sweetie and I just tried Smart Alec's for the first time today and plan to go back frequently. Their food is fast, reasonably priced, and reasonably healthy. 

My fiance ordered the basil chicken burger and I ordered the Avocado burger with beef. I'm a sucker for avocado and will always try to get it on my food when it's an option. 

We also ordered a salad and shared a large garlic fries, which were both fantastic. The salad was filled with fresh lettuce and other veggies, and the fries are baked, or so I read on Yelp. They had really fresh and tangy garlic with herbs squeezed on top and they were honestly some of the best fries ever. 

The ability to get up and get our own ketchup, napkins, etc. is really a plus in my book because I can get those things much faster than if I had to flag down waitstaff, and I can get only as much I need, helping to reduce trash and waste!

All in all, a 5 star experience!

Yea so I love the vegan brownies, how they get that thing to rise so thick and fluffy and chocolatey without the eggs and stuff is beyond me. I want this recipe! 
I would remember going there in 2006 and there was like 2 model girls working there one was gorgeous swedish blonde and the other looked like a double for jessica alba. The swedish girl would see me walk in and would ring me up, "one brownie right!" she said with her perfect smile. Damn you! skinny b*%#&es.. I wanted to say umm actually i'm going for the salad, but I would always say "yea one brownie", and hang my head in shame, as I fastiduously  scanned the display for the largest moist one there, not all are created equally.
I am not a big fan of salads but my mom loves them here she can't finish it all. I love the soups and cornbread mmm.. especially the chilli but the potato leek is also good.

I don't find myself in Berkeley often (thankfully), but this place is good to go for cheap, veggie options. 7 bucks for a mediocre veggie burger and fries. still convinced they tried to sneak me meat. but i have to trust the Berkeley hippies.

yumm!

huge salads, DELICIOUS cornbread! chili soup is great, since 1. it's healthy (no meat) 2. great tasting! Highly recommend getting the eggplant sandwich, yumm!

The best sandwich is the Basil Chicken Sandwich. The basil mayo sauce they use is so delicious. 

Their soups are okay. But their garlic fries are delicious. 

Their corn bread is the best, especially the side pieces!

After passing it up so often, I finally decided to try something new. I got the eggplant melt, which was FANTASTIC!!! Basil pesto mayo?! Yes please!!!! The bread was charred so you get the taste of toasted bread while it being soft enough not to scratch up my mouth. It was weird at first, but soon I appreciated that the bread was soft; all my yummy fillings would've been squished out! The sandwich was HUGE too. 

The fries were interesting. Since they were "air-baked" they didn't have the grease quality one would expect. However, I liked them though my gf said she's had better. I'd love to try the garlic fries next time.

It's good to know there's a healthy fast food joint around.

Personally, I think their burgers are amazing, but their fries leave much to be desired. 

Prices are fairly reasonable, although I do HATE that they don't accept cards. I always forget (especially when I am STARVING), get to the register, order, and realize I have no cash on me. It's always the icing on top of the cake.

I work just down the street and often find myself drawn to this place.  I LOVE their air fries as long as they are hot.  When they get cold they most resemble cardboard.

Every time I go I swear I will try soup, a different salad, or a sandwich but I'm always drawn back in by the Garden Delight, which is enough for 2-3 meals.

Their veggie burgers are not my thing but their menu is so veggie friendly there is lots of other things to eat.

My cousin introduced me to this place.
I love their vegan soups.
Their salads are really good too!
Everything is decently priced.
Took my mom here once and she said the chicken burger was really dry.

Fries were cold, burger bun was soggy and the patty bland.  My friend took me here and her soup was cold and way too salty.  She was kind of  embarrassed for saying we should go there.  There are so many other good options on Telegraph I don't get this place.  The staff was rude and the place was dirty.  I like Bongo Burger or Intermezzo a lot better.

I can't believe that it took me until junior year at Cal to try a legitimate meal from Smart Alec's...don't make the same mistake, guys! 

Smart Alec's is conveniently located close to campus (just a tinnnny bit less of a walk than going to Asian Ghetto) and is a great place to eat for lunch. I got the standard burger+fries+drink lunch combo and it came out to around $7 (+tax). I think I can eat a lot for a girl, but for some reason, even though I had lunch at 1pm that day, I was full after drinking my iced tea and eating my burger - I had to save my fries for another meal! The burgers are very huge and tasty. 

I think that next time, I would come for the soup+salad combo or just a plain salad. While I was standing in the long lunch line, my eyes were definitely wandering over to the plates of people with the huge salads. Sigh...I need to find my Intermezzo replacement, fast. Maybe Smart Alec's will be the one

I think I ate at Smart A's almost everyday for 3 years.  God I miss this place!  Favorite things on the menu are

- Sesame chicken salad (dressing on the side!) 
- corn chowder
- brownies
- and they have an exceptionally good soda fountain

I don't know where else I can get a huge salad, a piece of wheat bread, and a medium diet coke for $7.50

Love it!

This place is awesome for many reasons:
1. Super casual place to hang out with a group or get quick take out
2. Seriously, so quick. 
3. Healthy! Or at least, healthier than most fast food places. Their food is never greasy and the ingredients are fresh. 
4. Garlic (air baked, not fried!) fries with chunks of garlic alllll over. 
5. Corn bread + leek soup = amazing chilly day lunch. 
6. Chicken pesto burger is so good, and this from someone who doesn't really like burgers. 
7. Chinese chicken salad is huge! Great for lunch and leftovers for dinner. 
8. Pretty cheap prices! And you get a loyalty card so you can get a free meal after eating there 10 times. 

The only thing that's lame is that Smart ALec's is cash only. Sometimes I forget and have to run to the ATMs across the street after I've already gotten ahead in line, but it's worth it!

I've given Smart Alec's *3* tries, and they failed all three times.  No matter how much I stressed  my hamburger be cooked Medium Well, it was always cooked rare, and they couldn't be bothered to remove the plastic from the cheese slice or toast the bun.  Plus the fries always tast like they were made 2 days  ago, and sat out since then.  Won't be going back, even if someone else paid.

Been to Smart Alec's many times over the past few years. I love it because the burgers have nice unique flavor, don't drip with grease puddles, and aren't dry. The cornbread is good to. Cash only unfortunately so plan ahead.

meh..its ok...i get their veggie burgers w/ avocado. Its expensive for a veggy burger, if anything, hit up trader joes and just make ur own for wayyy less. its cash only, but there is a bank right across the street, so that is not an issue.

Maybe I am just extra picky when it comes to sandwiches since I can readily make them myself, but this place is still a go-to lunch spot for me. I have to admit I love their turkey cranberry sandwiches and their soups. If you want something healthy (or at least healthier than Asian ghetto), then come here.

Wow, I haven't had a healthy burger place in a long time.  The fries have 0 trans fat and very little fat overall compared to other places.  Sweet!  Guitless fries.

I went with my co-worker for lunch, found parking pretty easily (amazing!) and got our food fast.  I had the basil chicken burger, and wow, it was really good.

Fresh veges, and the fries are good.  I need to try the smoothies next time.

Lots of college kids walking around, makes me miss college!  I'll stop by there again sometime.

I never feel bad eating here. Their only downfall is CASH ONLY. I love their veggie/non-veggie burgers (but you gotta eat it right away, otherwise the bread with be soggy and cold), turkey sandwich, salad, and soup w/ CORNBREAD. I think thats everything :)  I think it's one of the best cornbreads I've ever had. It's so good I never even tried the brownie. They're displayed in the same box and whenever I look at their cornbread, I have to get it. On the days that I'm not very hungry, I like to get the soup w/ cornbread... 3 bucks for a fulfilling meal. 

True, if you're craving a dirty burger, don't come here. It might not satisfy you. But otherwise, a really good lunch and dinner option.

Close to campus and relatively healthy, tasty food. 

Compared to Cafe Intermezzo, two blocks down Telegraph from Smart Alecs: the wheat bread is much less dense and chewy and satisfying, but they have cornbread instead. Except the cornbread is super oily and sweet--but they give you a large large chunk. The salads here are pretty much the same size, but no avocado, the tomatoes are mealy slices of a large tasteless tomato, and the egg is cut in half rather than in many slices. They don't forget to put sprouts in the salad like Intermezzo always does with mine. There are wheatberries and edamame in Smart Alecs' salads. The dressings are similar (poppyseed, check!). The sandwiches are slightly smaller and the cheese is greasier (somehow). They serve air-baked fries and burgers, while Intermezzo has more baked pastries. Less of a cozy hippie atmosphere than Intermezzo. 

And there you have it, in case you were wondering. I know I was.

The garlic fries are good.

The burgers are good.

The prices are cheap.

This is yet another pretty good campus eatery at UC Berkeley.

what an institution. 

for a while, i was addicted the tofu/avocado sandwich. the burgers are excellent, and the fries are very good. smoothies, salads, tons to choose from. incredibly affordable (barely anything is more than $6). it's no wonder that this place is popular!

I appreciate the attempt to re-direct people seeking fast food away from mcdonalds and toward something healthier.  That said, the food is pretty good and the menu is very vegan-friendly.  All of the soups were vegan last time I was there, and I highly recommend the lentil soup.

I think it's a great place for healthier lunches if you're in the area, and the food is very filling, which is always a plus (sprouts don't always hit the spot, you know?). The fries are pretty damn good considering they're air baked or something exciting like that...and they serve fresh, home-baked nutrient-packed bread on their sandwiches/with salads. I don't know what they hell constitutes a "special sauce" but it was pretty delicious...and the coolest part is that upon dining, they have a little survey thing which I found neat considering it's an independent establishment...it really makes me feel like the owner cares about what the customer thinks, which is nice!
The only annoyance was the pitiful state of the bathroom, but that's probably a Berkeley thing, no? With everyone and their momma pry' using it...

I love this place and I'll admit it is for the air-baked fries and a good burger.  I will say the cooking staff has indifference down to an art form, but the cashiers are usually nice!

Living in S.F. I am surprised there aren't more places that offer air-baked fries.  Until I find one, I will keep driving across the bay to Smart Alec's.

It's no secret why Smart Alec's best combo is an A+.  It's vegetarian and amazingly delicious! (or you could say vegetarians get A's?).
 
If I order something unrelated to even imitating a burger I usually order a half Caesar Salad- their salads are a massive mound of greenery- so I stick to the half size ones.

No matter what I'm ordering though I can guarantee a side of cornbread is needed.  It is quite possibly the most perfectly constructed piece of bread my mouth has met.

Cornbread, cornbread 
Oh how you make my head
...say mm.

Yeah, that's a poem I'm working on.

Note: I'd say it's one of the best of Berkeley.  I know it's a fave of mine:)

Smart Alec thinks he's got the secret to healthy fastfood.  Sure, the food here is healthier than McDs, et al., but it's not always good.  Smart Alec's serves sandwiches, burgers, salads, soups, and fries.  I've practically given up on everything but the big salad; the ranch dressing they use is my favorite, with a great undertone of garlic.  I like the housemade bread on the sandwiches, but their turkey is way too dry and unappetizing.  They serve gourmetized veggie burgers with sauces like artichoke or sundried tomato, but these burgers are always a bit mushy and have no texture.  The soups I've tried taste like cafeteria food.  And their fries are not deep fried, but baked which makes them limp and somewhat gummy.  They serve regular and garlic fries: the garlic fries derive their garlicness from a mysterious powder that could shut down a post office and raise the terror level to Orange.  It looks nothing like crystallized garlic powder you get in a spice rack, and it just tastes weird.  For a healthy eating habit, I suggest sticking to the big salads at Smart Alec's and occasionally indulging in a burger (or a veggie burger) and fries from a real burger place.

The menu advertises that their beef contains no additives.  I ordered a burger and it arrived covered in spices (pepper).  Unfortunately I cannot eat pepper (allergic).

I took my burger back and asked for one without spices.  It turns out they all come with spices, and the chicken is marinated (with spices) too.

I ended up getting a tuna sandwich (which was good).

A question to Alec's - Why do you say the beef doesn't have additives, yet it does and isn't available without additives?

Prime location and good food. Smart Alec's offer a good variety of healthy burgers and salads that can satisfy anyone's hunger. You also can't go wrong with their corn bread and brownies. Not the best burgers I have ever had but pretty darn good

I used to go here a lot, back when I lived in Bersekely. The breads were good, and salads too large. The burger wasn't my favorite though, and the fries tasted too healthy. I like, though, when they open the windows onto the street, and customers are confronted with the magical Bay Area breeze. God, I love it there.

They purport to be healthy.  Yet if you watch for a while, you'll see mostly what they sell are burgers.  And burgers are not healthy.  And their burgers are unremarkable.  You can get healthier chicken burgers instead, though they're similarly unexciting.  Fries are baked and therefore healthier but also don't taste as good as ordinary fries.  Salads are pretty good.

Not bad, Telegraph.

You would totally think this is one of your thoughtless UC student eateries, but the food is totally good. They have awesome cornbread as a side (!) and many, many tasty vegetarian and vegan options. (Based on that, I'm sure the meat ones are good too.)

I like their: salads, cornbread, hummus sandwich, and french fries.

The salads can compete with--are are very much like--those at Intermezzo, so Smart Alec's is a good alternative if you don't want to wait in a long line down the street. (Not to say that Alec's should come second--it is definitely a worthy competitor, yumminess-wise).

Smart Alec's is also inexpensive, has lots of room to sit, and is speedy. 

Way to go.

For what it is, it's not bad.  I also have to admit, I haven't tried their burgers or sandwiches yet, only soup, salad and fries.  And coffee.  
Service should get 4.5 stars.  People are nice, the line moves quick and you get your food to order pretty fast.  
Cash only :(.  
Go french fries!  Baked, not fried, and the garlic fries will keep vampires away from your apartment for days.
Salads are HUGE.  And you get it with a slab of cornbread carb joy, or wheatbread.  The caesar is pretty good, but I had the cobb and it was a little soggy.  The chicken on the salad isn't the best chicken ever, but there's a lot of it and it will satisfy your poultry cravings.
The coffee, one lone carafe with a jug of ballsy half and half and a sugar shaker next to it, is honestly the best cup on the block if for the only reason that it's incredibly strong and everything else around is weak, something I wouldn't have expected in Berkeley.

"Let's go to Smart Alec's".  

Whenever I hear these words, my mind skims over the menu: okay sandwiches, okay salads, okay soups, okay smoothies, and oooh, their delicious cornbread.  

"Y-y-yeah, let's go to Smart Alec's!"

Okay food, really overshadowed by Intermezzo down the street. Everything is a little pricey, and I've never really like the service, but overall its a pretty good place for lunch. Bring in an A paper/exam, and get the avocado burger along with the free fries.

Smart Alec's really isn't all that bad, food-wise. Of course, I've never had any experience with rats each time that I went there.

Let me start off by describing the environment. It's one of the reasons why I enjoy going there. They have these huge windows that they keep completely open that bring in nice fresh air, and offers a constant view of people passing by, which I just find cool. Most of the time, the door is open too. Light from the sun is always pouring in, and sets a great mood of calm/relaxedness while you're eating.  I think its my favorite part about the place, because the food isn't THAT amazing.

The food is average overall. I don't really see much of a difference in its healthiness when compared to other fast food places, except that it offers vegetarian food. Taste wise, the food is alright. Nothing more. I feel like its sort of bland- which is why I don't recommend visiting the place constantly. But every once in a while its an alright choice for lunch.

I would have given this place 4 stars, but there's ONE thing, or rather person, that knocked off a star for me. Every time I've been there, the same cashier always takes my order. I feel like she always gives me a nasty look as I'm ordering, and by her tone of voice, I'd say she always seems to be annoyed by me. I don't really get it, I walk up, smile and say hi, place my order, and smile and walk away. But she always has this frown on her face that just speaks "fuck, not this guy again" to me. And it's not just my imagination either, multiple friends who have been there with me seem to notice the same thing. She doesn't seem to act this way with other customers from what I've noticed. Just me. 

Other than her though, Smart Alec's is a pretty okay choice for that hungry stomach of yours and the extra 7 bucks in your pocket.

When I want a big salad bursting with different fresh ingredients, I always come here!  I either get the Sesame Tofu Salad or the Superior Salad with tofu and the sesame vinaigrette that is absolutely addicting!  I love that the Superior Salad has wheatberries, edamame, corn, sprouts, carrots, etc.  It's filling and super healthy.  

Just a warning: the tofu is usually dry and over-baked.  Intermezzo definitely has much better tofu.

Smart Alec's always give you the choice of cornbread or wheat bread.  I know wheat bread's healthier, but the cornbread is so good here!  I usually save the cornbread until I get back home and pop it into the toaster oven so the sugar in the crust gets caramelized.    

As for sandwiches, I like getting the Eggplant and Avocado sandwich and the Rosemary Chicken.

Garlic French Fries and cornbread are a MUST when you come to Smart Alec's. The fries are thick slices of potato tossed with fresh garlic condiments. Yes, it is oily but every now and then a little indulgence is acceptable! Cornbread is thick, moist and carries strong corn flavors. 

Their soups, salads are okay. Nothing special. Burgers are on the dry side, imo. I like their eggplant sandwich the best; it's unique and extremely juicy. 

I can't agree that Smart Alec's is a place to grab "healthy" food, as they self-proclaim. But its menu items are nicer options over food from McDonalds or other fast-food chains. Service can be a little slow at times but bearable. Also, they close a little early, compared to other restaurants in the area.
Big ass salads are hella good.  Corn bread is the business too.

5 stars for the salad. The poppy dressing isn't as good as Intermezzo's, but for about $7 you can get an absolutely enormous salad with tons of variety (expensive, variety-less salad is a pet peeve of mine), and that price includes an extra buck for some yummy grilled tofu. Plus, the line moves much faster and is smaller than Intermezzo's (b/c they are so quick at getting orders out).

First time I got a salad from here, I was in high school. They drenched it with over-salted dressing.
The second time I walked in, it was empty and flies were everywhere. I immediately walked out.
one of my favorite restaraunts in the bay area!!!!!! very cheap as well. if you are in berkeley go here for a meal
Excellent cornbread, skip the wheat bread. Good salads, garlic fries. Sandwiches and burgers are okay.

I sure don't feel smarter after eating here, but I'm satisfied with their offerings. As a carnivore, I often go for the avocado burger with garlic fries (for some extra flavor). Their secret sauce isn't bad either. My one complaint with their burgers is that they tend to be fairly soggy, almost as if everything melts in your mouth. While some may find this tantalizing, I'd prefer to chew my food. The garlic fries are epic, so make sure you bring gum or breath mints, even though you'll still be burping and tasting garlic for a few hours. Not a bad choice if you're in the healthy market, as they also have a wide variety of salads, soups, and corn/wheat bread!

tasty salads and sandwiches with slightly high prices.  if you can get something with the flavored mayo, it's delicious.  the brownies are a disappointment so don't bother.

I used to always get the garlic fries but it seems like they've cut back on them.  instead of the chunks of real garlic, it's just covered in garlic powder or salt or something.  not as great...

The fries are delicious, and the thousand island they offer is really good.  The cornbread is also pretty amazing!  The burgers however, are a little bland. I don't mind eating them, but I've had better burgers.  Do try the 'air baked' fries though! It's so good :D :D :D

Haha. Smart Alec's. What a great name.

Anyway, my friend & I decided to stop by here because one of the cute girls we met at a shop recommended it to us. We were really hesitant about trying the place because we weren't really feelin' the gourmet burgers & salads.. But after debating it & comparing other options, we decided to try it.

We both ended up getting a Big B combo with Garlic Fries. Service was hella quick for such a rush hour, too. Wow. Tell me why that burger got us full for the rest of the day! I was definitely satisfied with what I ordered. I didn't really recognize the "special sauce" the menu claims to offer & ended up having to add extra condiments for flavor. I seriously didn't want my burger to end, but for some reason, after my last bite, it was like I ate the perfect amount. Couldn't even finish the garlic fries, haha. Stuffed. My friend hates pickles, too, but she loved the ones they had here. Weird.

But this place was packed! Hella folks were getting huge salads that looked crazy. Definitely worth a stop.

Good place to stop by for lunch in between classes...

Their turkey sandwich with everything (including cranberry mayonnaise.. it sounds weird but it adds the perfect touch) and as a MELT is delicious. 

I can only eat half due to my small stomach, so its less than $8 bucks for lunch for 2 days!

I had heard from a friend that this place was really good, and as a visitor from New England, I really wanted to get the Berkeley student experience.

For about $9 I got a meal, which included a sandwich, a soda, and a side of fries.

I had the basil chicken burger. The bun was whole wheat (big plus) but the meat was dry, tough, and rubbery. I could hardly taste the basil in the mayo, which was thick and creamy.

The fries (regular, not garlic) were dense with a texture like Play-Doh. I didn't like it enough to eat the whole dish.

The beef burgers did look "hella" juicy, though. I wouldn't go back unless I was with a friend who really insisted on going to Smart Alec's. And if I did, I'd try a beef burger and the garlic fries.

P.S.
A local friend told me that if you bring a midterm or a final that you scored an A on to Smart Alec's, they'll give you fries for free!
The burgers are pretty decent but the fries that they create all their own hype about? not so awesome.

So many things to love about Smart Alec's, and only a few disappointments.

The lovely parts: salads, burgers, fries, soups, CORN BREAD that gives me a mouth-gasm.  I've never had the veggie burger, but the beef burger is fabulous, juicy, filling, wonderful, on a yummy whole wheat bun.  Fries are good if you eat them hot, sort of nasty once they get cold.  Drinks are, for some reason, HUGE.  

I've had the Caesar salad and it's fine, although I prefer my Caesars with more garlic, and they skimped a little on the dressing.  The corn chowder is fabulous, and I can't say enough good things about the corn bread.  

Downsides: cash only, crowded dining room, occasionally-surly counter people.
The lunch portions aren't bad and the prices are good. Basically, when you go to Berkeley, you gotta mix it up and if you sometimes end up here then so be it.
