The salads are decent as long as the dressing doesn't become overwhelming (ask for it on the side). I wouldn't go so far as to say the food is amazing, but I do appreciate the Smart Alec's effort to be affordably health-conscious and edible.

I love this place, since I've gone on the Insanity diet/workout I always turn to Smart Alec's for healthy, reasonable priced food. 

Pros: 
Great service from Jude ;)
the cornbread is a must
air-baked fries- my life line alternative to junk food cravings

Awesome and healthy food.  Nice and clean, organized.  SMART!  I love it.  Ate there about 15 times.  Always yummy.  As a vegetarian they keep me happy.  Prices are set just right.  One of my favorite places to eat.

After feeling unsatisfied with yesterday's Smokehouse chicken burger, the sixteen extra cents at Smart Alec's was well spent: freshness, avocado, real jack cheese, full-leaf lettuce, onions, tomato, on a whole wheat bun (it's surprisingly flavorful). It's not amazing but it's certainly a Yum!

I've been to Smart Alec's at least 3 times this summer.  Their Sesame Chicken and Sesame Tofu Salads are too good to pass up after a tough workout at the RSF!  The combination of crunchy asian noodles + lettuce + cucumbers galore + chicken/tofu + dressing make this the most filling, healthy, affordable meal!

If you're terribly starving, the salad will fill you up without the bloated feeling.  However, if you're not too hungry, expect to take leftovers because in addition to a bowl of salad that's large enough for me to fit on my head, you'll get a hefty block of cornbread (or whole wheat slice if you're health conscious unlike me).  Nice, dense, delicious.

And don't forget to bring your A papers/test.  :)  I make sure to collect on my free fries!

- 1 star because their restrooms are really really gross  x_x

Oh Smart Alec's.  I've lived about a block away from Smart Alec's for the past two years, and I find myself going about three times a week just to buy their air-baked fries and vegan brownie (I'm not vegan, this just tastes like delicious moist chocolate cake).  This place definitely supplies me with my guilty pleasure junk foods.

Other than that, their salads are pretty good (especially their chef's salad with poppy seed dressing and tofu sesame salad).  I will also get their Big B burger from time to time, but I would rather visit Barney's for my burger fill.  I do love their turkey sandwich because of the delicious cranberry mayo.  Their soups are also pretty good, but don't go in expecting the chowder to be like the creamy chowder you normally get.  The soups here are all dairy free!

Overall, Smart Alec's is a convenient and cheap go to for lunch or dinner for me, but it is easy to get sick of their regular foods (burgers, sandwiches, etc.).  However, I will never get sick of their fries with the thousand island dressing and brownies!

This place is so so, basically it's a place to come if you're feeling fat about yourself and you want to do something to allow you to sleep easier at night, is the food really that much healthier? Perhaps, I'm not health specialist, but I sure hope it is because if it's not then there is no excuse for their lack of taste. Not that the food is horrible, it's not bad, but could be better, but hey if it is healthier then by all means this place is awesome. The price is a bit higher, but I guess it's worth it if they use healthier things and fresher veggies. Salad is not bad, sandwhiches are not bad as well.

I love smart alec's for the air-baked fries and super fast service.  plenty of seating.  

Location: 1.5 blocks directly south from campus.  Food: veggie burgers are good.  don't taste like real burgers but then they're veggie burgers.  Good alternative for me since i'm such a red meat eater.  Special sauce is key for burgers.   Specialty Sandwiches are tasty.  But i think it's really the fries that get me here. If you're daring go for the garlic fries. 

Price is ok.  sandwich fries combo is like $7-8 with a drink. 

They also have a bathroom inside, which is wonderful for Berkeley.

I was here the day they opened. Food seemed okay then, but today it was terrible. 

Fries were stale and veg burger tasted like medicine. Maybe herbal medicine, but medicine nonetheless. Hamburger bun was dry and stale too. I ended up throwing away 90% of my food. I came home and tried for a second round of dinner. 

This place was a good idea 10 years ago, but today there are plenty of other much-better options. It's time for Smart Alec's to close up shop.
The brick of cornbread alone merrits 4 stars.  I dont really like the salads at all.  Intermezzo down telegraph is much better.  I would recommend the corn chowder though.

This review is purely based on the corn chowder!

I LOVE IT.  I sometimes stop here just for that chowder, which says a lot because I live in Sacramento.  

Beyond that, nothing has stood out for me.  Maybe I should try it again, and try something more than the chowder. But for now, the soup's the one!

Surprisingly, despite being at Berkeley for 3 some years, I have never tried Smart Alec's until this week. 

WIth Intermezzo still not opening up after being closed down (which I am still devastated about), this place probably is a decent substitution for an Intermezzo salad. 

NOTE: If you bring an academic paper, test, or midterm and received an "A" on it, you get a free order of french fries or garlic fries! 

My friend and I split a Chef's salad that came with either cornbread or whole wheat bread (naturally, we went for cornbread). The cornbread is supposed to be delicious here and while it is not very healthy for you, I feel like it's okay to indulge a little bit every once in a while. 

The Chef's salad was nicely proportioned, meaning that it was the perfect amount for two hungry girls after a hike, or that it could be split into two different meals. We chose the grilled chicken with a light amount of poppy seed dressing, and everything came out together so well. The croutons are homemade, salty, and crunchy, and there was a nice mix of protein and greens. Everything tasted fresh, and it was so nice to have some type of Intermezzo-salad again. 

All in all, the meal came out to be less than $10 and we even split it, so it was probably around $4.25 for the both of us. Cheap lunch, nice and healthy, and will definitely come back again for the salads!
Good avocado burger and I like the cornbread. Not to expensive, either. :)

I haven't been in a while but definitely have plenty of experience eating here. 
My favorite meal at Smart Alecs is the Basil Chicken Burger. It's a pretty tasty burger and a healthy alternative to traditional fast food. Their fries are also tasty, they are "air baked" I believe, and taste good. I like to double dip them in keptchup and tapatio haha yum.

Their service is great, they usually have long lines during the lunch hour (which in Berkeley starts at around 1:30. Nevertheless they manage to take your order and serve you in about 8 minutes even with the long lines. 
It's not the cleanest place on earth but for a berkeley restaurant near campus it's not bad. 
Overall I would recommend that you try this place out if you're a student and have not had the opportunity.

I didn't love it. I barely even liked it. I ordered the soup/salad combo. Tossed green salad with poppy seed dressing and corn chowder to be exact. My salad greens weren't fresh and the soup was only so-so. To make matters worse, the complimentary cornbread was dense and dry. UGH!!! Had my mouth feeling like the Sahara. :/

I really like their chicken basil burger and chicken sandwich, not so much a fan of their salads anymore. Their combos are reasonably priced and very filling. I like to go here when I want to get some food rather quickly and conveniently (I like quite near)

A staple for Berkeley students. Great soups, salads, and sandwiches. Their cornbread is especially delicious. Garlic fries with real garlic bits are a must try. I've since graduated but whenever I'm in the area I always go back to visit.

3.5 stars!

I always walk past this place and finally gave it a shot. They basically have soup, salad, sandwiches and smoothes here. All the S's!  They accept cash only with very reasonable prices averaging about $7. Its a very chill college environment and  self service. You pick up your food at the counter and clean up your own mess.

I ordered the soup and sandwich combo: corn chowder and grilled eggplant sandwich. The were both very good but nothing spectacular. 

If your hungry and need a quick bite the food is worth trying.

It's good. It's very good, but only if you order the right things and love garlic. The burgers are fairly generic; tasty, but with nothing special. However their salads are massive, and their sandwiches let them use their unique health food alternatives more wisely than in a regular burger.

Then there are garlic fries. The fries themselves taste good, but with an extra large kick of garlic their oven baked fries are delicious.

Great soy burgers and air-baked fries; a nice "fast food" option if you're a vegetarian. Cornbread is ok and the soup is decent - served piping hot and full of the star ingredient, and the salads are pretty standard. Nothing terribly special but still decently tasty, fresh fare.

Really awesome selection of healthy food. I love both their avocado burger and their chicken caesar salad. It is a little expensive though so I don't come here often. If I do I don't usually get the soda since they have easy access water here.
This place is sooo grub!! A must hit up every time im in Berkley. Healthy, good, affordable food!

Great place for vegetarians/vegans and non-veggies to grab some comfort food. My dining companion said it was "one of the best burgers I've ever had", while my veggie patty was definitely a step above the defrosted Gardenburger on the menu in other burger joints. The fries could be better, but since they're (hopefully) less likely to kill me, I'll make some allowances. Be warned: if you get teriyaki sauce on your burger, bring wet-naps or grab a stack of napkins at the counter - the sauce is decent, but they put about a gallon on your order.

Their corn chowder is like slop on a plate.  WTF.  When I saw the server pull a huge ladle out of those metal vats I already knew that it would be disgustingly thick.  Seriously?  Why did I get that.... why?!?

I got their soup and half sandwich deal.  I got the eggplant melt.  Again it's a texture thing.  Everything was way too soft.  The bread got really soggy really fast and the eggplant was just too soft.  

Fries are good though.  I won't go back for slop on a plate, but I would steal some fries off my bf's plate if I can.

This place has gone down in quality. I first went here 3 years ago and enjoyed the hamburger. It was juicy, the cheese was melted and just perfect. Even the fries were ok. I went there again this month and it was not the same. The hamburger felt like it was made quickly and it really didn't have any special taste. The fries were nothing special either. I left disappointed and and like if I wasted my money. Probably not going there again. Maybe its time Alec's gets a little smarter!

As a student in Berkeley I became a happy regular to Smart Alec's.  On a student budget it works great and I always leave full and still with money in my wallet.  The salads are huge so be prepared to eat a lot!  I'm a huge fan of the potato leek soup, turkey sandwich, avocado burger, and cornbread.  Sometimes if you get the edge of the cornbread it'll be a little dry and overcooked but that's my only complaint.  Also, for how busy it gets the wait isn't much during lunch time.

Smart Alec's offers some wonderful options for all.  I am a huge salad freak so I LOVE their Veggie Salad (I can't remember the exact name of it right now but its the biggest one).  It comes with lots of beans, egg, tomato and a choice of protein.  I recommend the salad with tuna and poppy seed dressing!  The Big A is also excellent, as is their clam chowder.  Their famous air baked fries are delicious and all for a good value.  Another option in their chili cheese fries which are delicious and don't make you feel like sick after eating it! :)  Definitely stop by if you can!

MMmm veggie cheese burgers and air-baked fries.  SO GOOD i'd walk clear across campus once or twice a week to get me some smart alec's.  The portions are insane (and im an extremely "healthy" eater) for the price.  They're pretty quick, but it is really full during lunch / dinner hours.  They have a bunch of extra fixings available on the side, like ketchup, mayo, mustard, etc. which i really enjoy.  I also LOVE the really big drinks, and ability to re-fill at will.  The cornbread is crazy good. 

BUT, i've had a salad before with their wanna-be "ranch" and it was NOT a good experience to be upchucking it on Telegraph where there are no public bathrooms, while my ride was getting a tattoo. NO FUN!

2009 update:  No more re-fill at will option! :(  Oh, and they only take cash.  Still yummy tho..
they served the shores of the pacific ocean to my friend and it's his bday tomorrow :[

This place is really good! It's healthy, and the healthy slogan always gets me. 

When you order soup, it comes with either wheat bread or corn bread. I like BOTH. The wheat bread kind of has a sweet flavor, and is so delicious and chewy. I believe they make all their ingredients from scratch! Their cornbread is also very good, but I might be biased because I just like to eat cornbread.

Their combo burgers are also delicious! I don't feel as guilty when I gobble up one of their burgers because it's "healthy." I don't know how healthy it is, but who cares! It's delicious :).

I like how vegetarian friendly this place is too. I have tried the eggplant sandwich, and it was pretty good! The tuna sandwich was good, but had too much tuna in my opinion. 

Overall, I'm a fan. :)

cash only, closes early and it smells kinda funny.... 

but they have pretty huge, delicious salads. try the garden delight with poppy seed dressing (comes with corn bread on the side). 

close to campus and fast service. oh, and if you bring in an A paper, you get free fries.

I don't really love the burgers, but the air-baked garlic fries and corn chowder are good!  More places should air-bake their fries, which is a way of baking fries so they still have the same quality if they were deep fried.  

My friends sometimes ask for extra garlic on the side and they use this for topping their fries at home later that day.

I've gotten the burgers, soup, and salad here before, and I've even brought in a midterm that I got an A on and gotten their free fries. Food tastes alright overall - not anything too special. The salad is huge, but they tend to douse it with too much dressing. I'm personally not a cornbread person, and so I've never known what to do with their piece of cornbread. The people are nice and the restaurant has good amount of seating.

Healthy? hahahahahhaa, if you count big juicy burgers and fries as healthy!  True you can customize your own vegetarian selections, but I wouldn't label this place healthy...its a nice big space good for people watching at a good location though, and the food really is concrete and reliable every time.  Nice place to grab a bite to eat and watch all the exciting people and things unfold outside on the street...

three stars from foodmonster!

I love this place! The food is great, the service is pretty speedy, and it's not too expensive. I really enjoy the fact that you can eat food that is typically considered "fast food" but that it is cooked in a more healthy way (or so it's presented). 

I've several different sandwiches (beef, turkey, veggie) they have all been great. I'm also a huge fan of the fries that they have. They are apparently "air fried" or something. . .I don't really now what the process is, but it produces one delicious fry! 

They loose one star because they do not accept credit cards and I've run into a problem with this on several occasions. . .sort of an inconvenience, but the food's still really good!

I really love the fries here- they are seriously addictive! And the tofu salad is OK although it's a bit too crunchy with all those fried noodles. Soups are pretty good too! The thing that I really don't understand though is why the veggie burger is so gross. I think it might be a boca burger, and maybe I just don't like these, but it's completely limp, oily, and dense. Blech. Why don't they make their own handmade veggie burgers like Amanda's does?

Like everyone one here has said before, their cornbread is amazing. I usually like mine warm so I ask them to warm it up and they don't seem to mind doing so. As a non-vegetarian, the vegetarian options they have are really tasty and filling. The garlic fries are OK, I've definitely had better, but it's nice that they give them for free after a small purchase if you show them something you got an A on.

I miss living in the dorms right across the street! I used to get their corn chowder with corn bread all the time! Mm :) I also really like their avocado and tofu sandwiches. Recently, I've been getting their chef's salads a lot (with grilled tofu. either honey mustard or poppyseed dressing, and wheat bread) simply because, along with being delicious, it can last me through lunch and dinner!

I have to say though, I don't seem to be as much as a fan for those garlic fries compared to everyone else. But maybe they're worth a second try..

Pretty boring food. Nothing special; unless you're a health food nut looking for something fast easy and a bit bland. I had the Turkey burger, meh. Would be better if I liked health food. (Fiances note: beef burger was dry, cheese was lacking, might as well have been white bread. Fries were good.)

This is one of my favorite health food places in Berkeley.  Their salads are wonderful and huge (get the honey mustard dressing); I used to split a salad with my big sis.  I also love the veggie burgers and the garlic fries.  True, the garlic fries might not be as crisp as the really bad for you places, but they are air baked and thus much healthier for you!  I like to dip the fries in the thousand island dressing available in large pumps next to the ketchup.

so i was walking down telegraph looking for a healthy lunch and decided to give this place another try since every other joint on the street seems like a pizza place. anyway, tried the A burger this time and really enjoyed it. i never thought i'd be a veggie patty kind of girl, but alec's does it right... converted me into a fan.

Smart Alec's is always my fallback option when I can't think of anywhere else to go between classes.  It's quick, it's cheap, and it really fills you up w/o the massive guilt trip.  The soups are great.  The fries are not greasy and yet still tasty.  The Big A burger is a healthy, decent-tasting burger at a cheap price.

Sandwiches are a more risky option as are the salads.  Some of the sandwiches are not very substantial and can taste quite dry.  The salad greens can be sort of wilted if you go late in the day; the dressing is also average.  If you want a good sandwich/salad, go to Intermezzo just down the street on Telegraph.  But if you want some warm and healthy convenience food, Smart Alec's is the way to go.

I tried this for the first time recently, and the service seriously sucked. Really inattentive. I got the lentil/barley? soup and salad and I was pretty unsatisfied. I highly doubt the "healthiness" of this place too... And don't get "wheat bread" with your soup. It's just a slice of grocery store bread, straight from the bag. The salad was huge, but just vegetables...Bleh. I'm not coming back.
This place ig great. Friendly staff, nice place to stop and eat if your on the go. And the food is healthy fresh and tastes amazing. The chicken & avacado sandwitch is the best.

I always got a half salad/half sandwich combo.  Whatever the chicken sandwich was with a green salad and a side of cornbread. I LOVED the cornbread. I would purposely eat all my salad, then save my half sandwich and cornbread for dinner. l've also tried the garlic fries and they're really good! I was tempted to try a burger, but then realized that they were microwaved so I decided to skip out on it... hmm..

Big fan of Smart Alec's. I always get the Big B Combo - a fabulous avocado burger with fries and a drink. The food is fast. The food is tasty. The food is healthy - especially compared to any other burger-and-fries joint. The service is scooty and good. And it is inexpensive. A Telegraph institution. Brilliant place.

Potato/corn chowder soup - good.  I am happy with this every time.

Cornbread - good, but it should be called corn CAKE.  If you are actually a healthy eater, you can taste the loads of sugar they've GOT to have pumped into it.  

Fries - yuck.  I don't care if they're more healthy, they taste like shit.   FRY my fries, damnit.  Don't give me this dried-out crap.

The Chili - ew.  Just ew.  Don't go there.  It sucks there.  Ew.

Veggie Burger (The" A" or whatever) - not so great.  Terribly cheap, very low on taste.  It filled me up, but I've had better, and believe me when I say that, as I've been a vegetarian eater for over a decade.  I'd rather pay more and get some flavor.  

All that said, it's a great place for a student to grab lunch with others if said student is on a budget.  Hell, I'm sure the homeless people like it too, for cheap, prepared food.  Also, it's always fucking loud, even with only one other person eating, so I take it away.

My sister insisted that I try their cornbread since I have become a cornbread-aholic. It was slightly warm, very sweet with a bit of a crunch. I typically like my cornbread with a huge, thick crust that you usually get from using a cast iron pan...while Smart Alec's doesn't use this method (I don't think!), their bread is still great. It would be the perfect accompaniment to a bowl of chili!

The food was pretty good. Up until I found a piece of bug on my fork. 

At least I had some extra protein in my salad. 

Went there the second time and had a sandwich. It was fine. 

Went there just last night for another salad. Didn't find any bug on my fork, but there was something fishy with the smell. I guess you just can't trust their salads. I'll get a burger. Without the side order of salad.

I have been going to Smart Alec's pretty frequently two years ago.... during that time... i thought "hmmm.... their soup and corn bread is pretty good"... but I recently visited them again and thought otherwise... the quality of the soup has been downgraded so much that I think the soup is like baby food .. the texture is really mushy and it doesn't look or taste good.

A staple restaurant for Berkeley students around Telegraph.

For a place that talks about "intelligent food" and healthy fast food, it's quite ironic that the only time they trump their nutritional info is on the trays. Even then it's only about the fries!

Non-healthwise, they make good salads and soups, but their burgers aren't anything to write home about. Pretty much any non-burger item on their menu is good, although I'm not a fan of tofu or eggplant in sandwiches. I usually get a half caesar salad and half tuna salad combo, or a superior chef salad with poppyseed and beef patty/tuna.

I'm sure I don't need to talk about the cornbread. It's loaded up with sugar and milk and obviously bad for you, but it's really good!

Smart Alec's also has a rewards program where if you get enough stamps, they'll give you a free bowl of soup or vegan burger along with free cornbread. I don't know how many times I've gotten this, but it keeps me coming back.

Cash only, although Bank of America and Wells Fargo are close by. Prepare to bring about $6-10. They've recently installed wifi too!

Holy God, the copious amounts of food this place give you for cheap!!

I thought I was being smart & intelligent for ordering the soup and 1/2 sandwich combo.  But no!  The soup was a giant bowl of potato leek (delicious) that came with a huge slice of wheat bread and a sandwich that was so big, it could have been it's own regular sized sandwich.  The turkey sandwich I had was amazing, and when I am back in Berkeley, I will certainly come back here.

I can't believe the horrible reviews this place gets.  When I was living in Berk I LOVED this place.  huge windwos make for excellent peopel watching and the food is tastariffic.  Highly recomended with any order is the garlic mayo.  It's like you put an entire garlic clove in your mouth.  Good LORD, I stank for days, but totally worth it.

Solid student food.  tasty.  man.. I miss living in the Bay...

I like this place because it's healthy and I like their veggie salad.. however I have to give them -2 stars because the customer service tends to be horrible.. In a previous review someone had mentioned that the girl at the counter was pretty unfriendly, and i agree 100% Whenever I come to order something she is not very nice and appears to not want to be working there at all.. I also was surprised when she didn't give me my change back, it was only .81 cents but still.  I stood there waiting for it, and she just looked at me like i was crazy.. 


p.s. credit cards are not allowed, and yes the flies that you see while you walk up to order,  are always there.

So I come here for their awesome tossed green salad and HUGE chuck of cornbread. I've never met cornbread I didn't like but this bread is especially delicious with the perfect moist/crunchy ratio. The salad portion is big but they drown it in dressing so maybe ask for that on the side. 
Also, I suggest they step into the millennium and accept debit cards. It's really heart-breaking to almost have to walk away from my would be eaten cornbread but thankfully my friend was there to cover me.

This place has a good feel to it. They have the BEST cornbread ever...moist sweet and fluffy! Have that with the soup...mmm. They have chicken,beef and a really good vegetarian burger. You can add bbq sauce or yummy pesto to any burger, create your own. there are other sauce as well. They have healthy fries.....watch out for the garlic fries unless you like or can handle very strong loads of fresh garlic chunks...wheew! Sometimes its packed so finding a seat might be an issue. Other that that give them a try its good food.

Just happened to walk by on a rainy Sunday night. What a great surprise! Healthy, cheap and yummy. I had the soup and sandwich combo: eggplant melt and veggie soup Yum! The soup tasted home made and the sandwich delicious. My friend had soup and salad combo with potato leek soup and Caesar salad. Really good. We shared the fries.  Lots of healthy yummy food for not a lot of money.  No complaints! Will return.

healthy? really? no way! wait... actually, i dont know where i got the idea that this food is healthy. is it?

but with that aside, the food was pretty good. i tried the eggplant melt and garlic fries. and man do i love garlic. dont hate (even though my breath smells).

If there were more places like this that sold healthy food, I would eat a lot better.  I don't know if friend and I just hit them on a good day, but everything we had was delicious!  I could not believe the amount of food we got for just over $6 a person!  I had the half-salad and soup combo with a caesar and potato leek soup.  The soup was amazing, even though I usually hate vegan fare.  The salad had a unique dressing that I really enjoyed.  And the giant piece of cornbread...oh my GOD, it was SO good!  I ended up over-stuffing myself because I didn't want any of that cornbread to go to waste!  Overall a really satisfying meal at a great price.

It was my first time going to Smart Alec's, and I'd heard that the food there was both tasty and healthy. I got "The Big B Combo," which basically consisted of a 100% beef hamburger (with onion, tomatoes, lettuce, sauce), garlic fries, and a drink (soda, tea, or water - I got tea). The food didn't strike me as anything special for the $7 that I spent, but I feel like you can't really go wrong with burgers and fries.

Now, up to this part, I would've given this place a 4, but the salad that my friend got was simply boring. All it had was some parmesan cheese, croutons, lettuce, and I believe a light caesar dressing. The lettuce was all of one variety, and the large portion made it seem more like a curse than a blessing in finishing it.

So, unfortunately, I'm giving this place a 3 for now, but I'm hoping to give this place another chance to try the cornbread that I'm hearing a lot about.

Delicious AND healthy? Sign me up! Their salads are gigantic (I get the sesame tofu one) and come with either corn bread or wheat bread. The corn chowder is great as well, as are the air-baked fries. It's pretty reasonably priced, there's easy free water access, and the wait time is minimal after you order at the counter. Highly recommended.

3.5 stars 

I love their asian chicken salad! and yes, cornbread is really good too..:)

I... can... barely... type this... because... of my... Smart... Alec's induced.... food coma. Thats right, Smart Alec's gives you a ridiculous amount of food for an excellent price. Their Garlic Fries are soooooooo good and I don't feel guilty eating them cuz they're like air fried or something crazy like that (read not ridiculously greasy). The veggie burger is great and that Asian Tofu Salad is TO DIE FOR! If you have 5 bucks and you're really hungry for some quality grub, this is the place.
Two words: food poisoning.

I've been a few times, and my favorite thing to get is the sandwich/soup combo. For $6.21 without tax (I believe), you get half a sandwich, a bowl of soup, and a slice of bread.

For sandwiches, I like the roasted turkey breast and grilled chicken. They're plain, with a basic dressing, lettuce, wheat bread, tomato (I think?), and meat recipe, but they go down easy and taste fresh.

For soups, I like the corn chowder a lot, but the vegetable soup is decent, too. You get a generous portion no matter what kind you get, and it goes well with a sandwich.

For the extra piece of bread, you can get either cornbread or wheat bread. The cornbread is a large cube-ish chunk with a crumbly consistency, while the wheat is basically a full-slice of the sandwich bread. The cornbread is tastier, but I would bet that it's less healthy. The wheat bread is a little plain on its own, but dipping it in the soup helps.

There are also the hamburgers and fries. I haven't had either in a while, but from what I remember, the fries are the standout of the two. The burger is solid and a little healthier than your typical one. The fries are air-baked and also seem healthier than usual french fries. I wasn't a big fan of the  fries with garlic because the garlic was just put on top of the fries, not mixed in well, and it was also a little too strong for me. The pricing for a burger/fries combo is about the same as the sandwich/soup, I think, and it's still a satisfactory amount.

Service is quick and efficient. You line up at the counter, order, and pay (cash only), then get a receipt with an order number on it. After that you can get a table and utensils and free water and wait for them to call your number when your food is ready, which usually takes less than four minutes.

As an aside, to use the restroom, you need to ask the cashier after you order to unlock the bathroom door with their electronic buzzing system, and then by the time you walk to the restroom, which is in the back corner, it should be opened for you.

There are no real problems with Smart Alec's. It's true that some of their food offerings are less appealing than others, but you get a tasty, fairly healthy, and filling meal for a good price regardless of what you choose.

Awesome corn chowder soup (very filling and YUMMY)! Also, they have one of my favorite hot sauces-Tapatio. Unfortunately, this place is a cash only establishment, and parking bites...so...had to rate with three stars.

Ummm, burgers and fries = healthy? Um, no. 

Sure sure, they oven bake their french fries, but that makes no difference! Fries are unhealthy and starch-filled, period. I'm quite disappointed with this place because their food is just not up to par, either. The salads are just...BAD. I ordered their tofu salad, and I swear the dressing is from Costco. I know i've had that dressing before...somewhere. I also tried their teriyaki/sweet chicken burger which was, again, average. For the price, i'm seriously expecting something of higher-grade quality. But unfortunately, it's majorly lacking.

I read so much about the garlic fries and corn chowder so I decided to see what the hype was all about. The fries were nothing special and when I tasted the chowder it wasn't warm enough. The only reason I would go back is the cornbread.

Although I am extremely dubious as to the veracity of the "100% Fresh Beef" claim, this place and Bongo Burger are the only two burger places I've been to on southside, and I liked it better here. Because it was cheaper.

Smart Alec's has pretty good food, and healthy too.

I love going here to get a bowl of salad or a tofu & avocado sandwich. Everything here is super fresh and super tasty, and although its healthy it won't break the bank.

The only times I've ever had problems here, is when I go to the register. It always seems that I'm dealing with someone new, and the manager is always by his/her side to teach them how to ring someone up. 

Other than that, I always have a great experience eating here. Especially with the big windows on all sides of the restaurant, great for taking in the sun or people watching while you eat your food.

The food here was good. It's better for you than your average burger and they taste good too. They even have wheat buns for those of you who want a burger, but want to make it healthy somehow. The salads are really good too. The fries are baked and not soaked in grease like most fries and they were really good.

It's clean and the food came quickly. I'll come here again if I'm in the mood for a burger when I come to Berkeley.

One of only 2 healthy places to eat if you're on the southside of campus.  The other is Cafe Mattina (formerly known as Intermezzo).

They sell burgers, veggie burgers, sandwiches, salads and soups.

I love to get the 1/2 sandwich, 1/2 salad combo deal when I'm indecisive.  All the sandwiches you can choose from are very tasty.  My current favorite is the turkey sandwich.  It has real turkey meat with cranberry sauce.  As for the salad, you can only choose between tossed green or ceasar salad (sorry, no specialty salad).  The salad portion size is STILL generous even though it's a 1/2 salad.  The meal is definitely worth its price.  

Specialty salads are also worth getting.  I like the sesame chicken salad.  Beware that portion size is HUGE (comparable to those at Cafe Mattina if you're familiar).

and the best part of all...you get cornbread!!!  Very yummy in your tummy cornbread.  If you're full from your meal and can't finish the big block of cornbread, save it for later!  You'll regret ever throwing it away.

Just back from Smart Alec. Got the avocado burger with chicken patty and garlic fries. My boyfriend got the Big B with beef. We had checked the menu on Allmenus.com and maybe it's them who screwed up here, but my chicken wasn't fried and the combos were a $1 more for each one. Let's pass on the burgers which have nothing out of the ordinary. The fries are without a doubt the most disgusting ones I have ever eaten in my life. You think I'm exaggerating here ? Wait til' you get a basket of half frozen cardboard and half toothbreaking hard fries. So maybe, I'm not appreciating the "airbaked" concept which, I confess I'm not too familiar here. Maybe those were just old. But then, how can you really trust a place when you might get old stuff ? Anyways, come on guys, even Mc Donald's fries are better than these anyday. As far as the garlic, they were huge balls of chunked garlic everywhere in the basket. We both left extremely disappointed. We will not be back. "smart" Alec who can't even make decent fries, you are totally overrated.

I just wanted to get food, but use the restroom first. Is that too much to ask? Apparently here it is. The women at the counter, It's... for....customer's. So, what, do I have to order first to use it? (She nods)  I have food sensitivities, so I said what do you have that is organic, grassfed and soy-free?[ The soy in the air is already messing with my head] Soy-free? she asked. Yeah.....I guess I just thought she would know her own menu..... The whole interaction was frustrating and slow. I gave up. At Gecko Gecko the guy was much more accommodating and helpful. I just expected as much for the price.

Smart Alec's serves grass fed ground beef burgers and air baked fries.  It was the first time I ate a combo meal like that.  Delicious!  The burgers are served on a whole wheat bun with lots of veggies.

The restaurant also serves sandwiches including dolphin safe tuna, grilled chicken breast, and roasted turkey breast.  The garden fresh salads include homemade cornbread or wheat bread.  The fries can be plain, garlic, or chili cheese.

Prices are reasonable.  Cash only.

They have SUPERRR Yums corn bread!!!!!

Their eggplant melt and avocado burgers are some of my favorites, but their burgers are pretty good in general. The soup is hit or miss though - I got the chilli soup once and it was all beans and nothing much else. The smoothies are mediocre, except this one time their mango smoothie tasted extra amazing for some reason.

A good joint to go to with a friend or two when your feeling smart. =)

I like the concept of healthy fast food.  The staff is certainly nice and patient, even helpful, when it comes to ordering.  The whole baked fries thing threw me off.  But I got my order just fine.

The food is...good.  The burger tastes sort of plain, so I resorted to dumping lots of ketchup on it.  The fries weren't bad.  I'd say the meal was okay.  It was certainly not the best one I've had, but it would do.  The price was decent as well.

The setting is clean and spacious.  But there are times when it seems to get a bit crowded.  I found myself waiting in line, and that sort of made me more eager.  The whole "long-line" factor may have raised my expectations of the place.

I've been traversing Berkeley since 1997, but I have never hit this place up until recently. I didn't feel like the usual pre-CREAM food (which is usually Fat Slice.) I finally decided to try this place for something different.

I went here the other night before getting a pint over at Jupiter (where I usually head to after CREAM). The place is super spacious and chill. Not as busy as i've seen it from the outside like usual, so the whole process of ordering and getting my food was pretty quick. I ordered a burger and garlic fries. Burger was nice sized, pretty hearty.A little on the dry side though. Maybe I should have asked if they could cook the burger medium rare. I'll try next time. Garlic fries weren't that great to be honest. They were hard through and through. It was sort of like eating potato chip sticks, which is what I don't usually look for in a french fry.

I will probably be back to try more of what they have. I would also like to see if I can get the burger cooked medium rare.

Smart Alec's has great burgers. They're big and taste good despite being "healthier". Not In-N-Out, but it's up there. I'd also always heard about their garlic fries, but when I first ordered it, I was really surprised to find that the garlic is not infused in the fries, it's actually just normal fries with a big scoop of minced garlic on top! My disappointment quickly faded when I mixed it all up and tried it. Yum! You'd better really like garlic though, and not have a hot date tonight (unless your date also went here that day).

And it's true - bring in a recent exam with an A and get free garlic fries with any order!! They'll stamp it with the Smart Alec's "A+" and give you a separate order for the fries. Sweet deal! I've brought in some of the easier quizzes in optometry school and really felt a sense of achievement as I ate my garlic fries that I earned. ;)

Delicious. Convenient location. Friendly workers. Healthy. Affordable (kinda, but at least their portions are big so they can sometimes last for 2 meals!)

I haven't tried that much on their menu yet, because I usually end up getting a salad cus I want their cornbread (which is bombbb btw), but from the couple times I've tried their burgers & sandwiches, they were pretty good (= 

Recommend: Sesame Chicken Salad, Cornbread!!

The food here is definitely on the healthy side. The burgers aren't as filling as your normal burgers since they aren't as thick. The garlic fries aren't even that good since its just normal fries with a whole bunch of garlic stacked on top. Smart Alec's needs to learn to fix the garlic into the fries with a bowl or something.

TL;DR; Garlic fries can be better flavored. The burgers are leaner and smaller, but organic.
The Cheesburger was great!

Do I wish I could eat a Smart Alec's grilled sandwich every day?  Yes.  Do I wish they accepted credit cards? Yes.  I take back one star for that alone - I mean, c'mon, at Christmas time, Salvation Army donation kettles accepted credit cards.  Even 8 year-old Girl Scouts let me pay via credit card/iPhone, now.  Payment-wise, it sucks to have to remember to always have Smart Alec's Cash on me at all times (this is literally the only place I pay cash for anything).  Waistline-wise, it's always nice to know exactly what you're eating (nutrition info), but I'm pretty sure it's better to stay in the dark - the sandwiches, so bread-y, cannot be compared to a flimsy (yet low calorie) six-inch sub from Subway.

Grub-wise, the chicken sandwich is perfection here and the main reason I stopped going to Intermezzo.  Intermezzo uses prison-grade sandwich meat.  The breastesses at Smart Alec's are pounded pretty thin (which I'm into), the veggies (lettuce, tomato and onion - keepin' it simple) are surprisingly fresh, the spiked mayo spread is a nice touch (and has never been too-liberally applied in my 30+ times eating here) and of course, the wheat bread is thick, seeded (unlike the mayo, this bread is, indeed, carb-overload - I wouldn't have it any other way) and reveals thumbprints when (if) you put your sandwich down.  It's that fresh.  They cover the sandwich in waxed paper and cut it in half for easy transportation, or you can eat it there and feel a whole lot less dirty than you would sitting at fly-infested Intermezzo.

Your breath will smell geriatric after this sandwich - lotsa onions - and no amount of brushing and Listerine seems to kill it, so if that's a problem for you, ask for no onions.  But your sandwich experience will suffer.

A year ago, I would have given this place 3 stars. But now, in a post-intermezzo world, I have tried most of their salads and realized how tasty this place is! 

First off, yes this place is cash only. But there is a BoA literally right across the street with a bunch of ATMs and a Walgreens less than a block away where you can get cash back. Stop hammering this place for being cash only people!

Now, onto the food. Their Superior Chef Salad is a lot like Intermezzo; a huge salad with a bunch of delicious fresh toppings and a heaping pile of your choice of meat or tofu on top. Its not as masterly crafted as an Intermezzo salad but its pretty damn good. Their Asian Chicken Salad is also really yummy! If you aren't in the mood for a salad they have lots of burger and sandwich options. My favorites are the eggplant sandwich, the basil chicken burger, and the chicken avocado burger. Their fries are also really good and supposedly healthier than your average fry. The garlic fries aren't there to mess around, they mean garlic business. You will either love them because they are the most garlicky thing you have ever consumed or hate them for the same reason. These things are so garlicky that they will make those stupid vampire twilight books disintegrate if you brought one within 20 feet of the establishment. Smart Alec's also has some fantastic corn bread. Like really really good. I would highly recommend it paired with a warm bowl of soup on a rainy day.

Did I mention you get free fries if you bring in a midterm that you got an A on? Now if only I could get one of those...

I ended up coming here with a small group of friends because we couldn't agree on any other dining location and this place seemed like a safe choice.

I got the potato leek soup with corn bread (normally I am  not a soup for dinner kind of gal) and let me tell you, it was thick.  Very hearty and filling only a quarter of the way through.  The flavor was decent, I personally thought there was a lot of dill in the soup and normally I love dill.

I didn't feel that there was anything really special about the menu.  They had soups, sandwiches, burgers, and salads.

I found myself in Berkeley a few days ago for a meeting and ended up grabbing lunch at Smart Alec's based on a suggestion from a student that I spoke with on the street. 

With a mixture of professionals and students eating there, it gave a great vibe to the place and was refreshing for me to not be surrounded by suits like in the Financial District of SF.  Overall, the food was okay, but I think I just enjoyed being in Berkeley on Telegraph again.  It had been a while since I visited the area.   I got a chicken sandwich and fries.  I thought that the food was good, but nothing to be overly excited about.

I think since Intermezzo closed down, this is definitely my new to-go place for salad. I don't know if my standards have dropped too, but I think their salads have gotten a lot better too! I especially love their sweet poppyseed dressing mmm. 

I ordered the half sandwich, half salad combo wiht medium fries, and the total came out to around $8.50. Not bad, considering all the food lasted me 1.5 meals too. I particularly like their grilled tofu and avocado sandwich. Their fries are nothing much though, but I can go on and on about their special sauce which they have a whole bucket of. 

I've been to this place multiple times before too, and was never really disappointed. I've had their avocado burger, their regular burgers, and one other sandwich. I'd skip the garlic fries and get regular ones because they put just way too much garlic on their really simple fries.

the garlic fries are amazing! perfect size, perfect flavor.

the smoothies are also really good, not too sweet like most places.

the burgers are so good too! very fresh and the service is fast. 

i used to come here every time i went to berkeley but realized berkeley has so much amazing food i have to try more places...if you haven't tried this place, though, definitely a good place to go!

I was really pleased. I got the Veggie Burger with Jack, boyfriend got the regular burger with jack cheese. Both were really good in my opinion. I recall the meat tasting pretty lean and it had good flavor and my Veggie Burger looked like the real burger, but you can tell the difference by taste.

I really enjoyed the Air-Baked fries. I didn't even feel guilty sharing a Medium.

I want to come back and try the soups and corn bread. 

Set Back: CASH ONLY! Thank god we had a $20 bill tucked in the wallet. Also, the food comes out FAST. Almost too fast... as if the patties are cooked far in advance. 

Will be back.
Don't get their brownies...

I really give this place about a 3.5 I really like their corn bread and their brownies are pretty good. I thought it was stupid that they charge extra for garlic on chili cheese fries when garlic fries are the same price as the regular ones. Portion are also a little small, for college food, ya know?

I don't really get why people rate this place so high. I tried to like it, I did. As a vegan, I was happy to see the veggie options. But everything is so DRY...I had to be generous with the ketchup on everything just to be able to swallow. The fries are cardboard-y. The salads, also, aren't as large nor as well-made as the ones at Intermezzo down the street. Blah. Not awful awful, but I won't be back.

I enjoyed the garlic fries, smoothies, chili, their avocado burger, eggplant sandwich, and vegetable soup. It's all very satisfying :) 

the brownies and cornbread...it's cakey and soft and moist... they make me so happy!

-1 star because i got really sick off the corn chowder once.

smart alec's.. you've never failed me!

this was one of my favorite telegraph spots to catch a healthy lunch in the good ol college days. the prices are pretty reasonable and i always leave feeling full!

it's all about the cornbread folks, that MONSTER chunk of cornbread they give you with a salad (or soup, or just ordered by itself) - it's DELISH. dense, just the right sweetness, SO GOOD.

i usually come here for their salads - they're pretty reasonable priced -about $3.50-$4 for a small - and it's not even that small!  the garlic fries here are really good too - plus the fries are air baked! so heathy... not gonna lie though, the garlic fries at IBs across the street are KILLER - it's just got that fried goodness to it. (kat c. and i actually got salads from smart alec's and fries from IBs last night puahahahah) but anyways, smart alec's fries are still yummy =)

don't forget about the frequent buyer card if you're a regular and also for you students - if you get an A on any paper, assignment, whatever and bring it in - they'll give you free fries!!! cheers for you smarties!

Hmm...it's clear from reading the reviews that people have very different opinions about Smart Alec's! I guess I'm one of the people who really loves it! I love a good cheeseburger and fries (um, just went to In-n-Out), and I love it here. (Also because I feel somewhat healthier w/the air-baked fries.) The couple of salads I tried were good (I usually end up with a cheeseburger; the veggie burger was good too). My friend LOVES the cornbread.

Yeah, no credit cards accepted. (Luckily there's an ATM across the street.) Long lines to order, but super-quick turn around once your order is in.

First time I went there I had the burger combo, which was great. 

I tried the chili & cheese fries yesterday. I guess it was not what I was expecting. I had a takeout of chili & cheese fries. The fries are put into a microwavable container; chili put on top; a large handful of shredded cheese on top of that and that's all microwaved together. I have had chili cheese fries elsewhere that are better because the chili has fewer beans and a bit more meat and the cheese is a nacho cheese that is ladled onto the top of both.

the tofu sandwich is kind of meh.  the only thing i REALLY REALLY adore is the hummus sandwich... so amazing :D
their garlic fries are okay good but soooo garlicky you def need to brush your teeth afterwards

Bluh, the service was fine, but the food sucked IMO.  Keep in mind I've only tried the vegetarian foods, but those were pretty sub-par to other places at Berkeley (think of Raleigh's just a block away on the other side of the street).  The best thing I've had there was the tofu salad, and even that got kind of old within a few minutes.  The cornbread was just OK - it tasted like any other corn bread.  Another minus, the last time I checked they didn't take credit cards.

Well, sure it's very affordable, and you know why if you eat there. 

I've been there so many times now, it's so close to campus and choice is not really great around - still, I do believe you can find way better food at similar prices.

Their burgers are really not tasty and always too dry. They claim it's a healthy place - well, if healthy means no flavor, you definitely win the price! Baked fries are possibly the only good thing there. 

Today we went there for lunch, and I am sorry to say I won't go for a while, I've definitely reached the lowest point there. My friend and I we both got their half soup/half sandwich combo. The lentil soup we got was really awful, none of us was able to clear our portions up. Also, the cornbread which comes with it is not bad, but it's so much you always have to throw some away!

The sandwiches are not terrible, I had tuna today. I definitely don't want to investigate what they put in their tuna mix, but at least it tastes decent. Still, the huge salad place down Telegraph is way better even for sandwiches.

Finally, nothing personal against the guys at the cashier, I realize they have to speed up and the job is quite stressful, but avoiding attacking customers and clearly trying to harry up as much as possible with orders would really help!!

I love the chicken sandwich and corn chowder soup combination. AMAZING! Their cornbread is heaven on earth. The food in mostly affordable and the environment in manageable. THe only annoying thing is that they only take cash. Cheap way to save a buck.

Smart Alec's best advantage is its proximity to a prime location of the campus. Beyond that, it's nothing more than an average  burger joint that you'd never want to frequent if you didn't live right next door to it.

The garlic fries are great; when somebody else gets it you always want to ask for a fry or two. The burgers are decent but still it's not going to impress anyone.

The cornbread is probably my favorite part about it. It's worth a try if you're ever in the area, but beware of the long lines of students looking for a quick bite in between classes.

Vegan and vegetarian friendly.  They started serving meat a few years ago as well.  The veggie burger and fries combo is cheap and excellent if thats what you are looking for and are too lazy to make it at home.  The fries are no good take out but are great fresh.  The burgers are way above average, better than any I've found to buy.

Shockingly healthy and tasty for the street. If you like their tofu sandwich, ask them for just tofu...they'll give you a soup cup of heaven.  Their corn chowder is perfect for a lazy, hungover Sunday afternoon. Great place for vegitarians on the go.

I only give this place 5 stars because it was the place I ate at seemingly a few times every week when I was at school.  I think the food here is very good, healthier, and very filling for lunch.  I ordered pretty much the same thing everytime I come here becuase I'm an extremely boring eater and can eat the same thing over and over again if I like it.  

I basically always ordered a half soup/half sandwich/ or half salad combo.  Their tossed salad with a vinagrette dressing is very good.  It has this sweet tangy taste to it.  I normally just go with plain ranch on house salad's but the vinagrette they have here is good.  For soups, the potato leek is the best I think with the corn chowder a close second.  They're very hearty and good for cold days.  Their sandwiches are served on wheat bread, which I normally don't like but tastes good here.  The sandwiches I like are the turkey with cranberry mayo sandwich, pesto chicken, tuna, and hummus.  That's practically all their sandwiches.  They also offer garlic fries which are good, but fail in comparison to the ones at Pac Bell!  If you're a vegetarian or feel like eating beef, they have burgers and non meat burgers also.  Their salads and sandwiches also come with a big ol' piece of corn bread and I love corn bread.  Go try it, it's better than Intermezzo.

This place actually impressed me - I wasn't expecting much from how busy it was and basically pretty much self service....But it was good! Staff are super friendly and have a good attitude - very rare to find.  The menu isn't overly complicated, if you want to stop by for lunch sometime you'll definitely find something good on the menu.  

The line to order moved very fast, and the wait for food was hardly anything, and we were there when it was PACKED - 12:00 on a Saturday.  The windows were thrown open so that atmosphere was abuzz.

We ordered the Chicken Basil sandwich - it was ok.  The Caeser Salad was good - and a HUGE portion, we ordered a half size for 3 of us to share and we barely dented it.  The Lentil soup was good, and I loved the hummus sandwich.

Bus your own table at the end and keep it clean, $17 for lunch for 2.5 people.

3.5 stars. 
Overall - a pretty cheap canteen-style eatery on Telegraph.  
Pros: cornbread. large salad with edamame and wheat berries. air-baked french fries for a potato fix, veggie burger, better dressing than Intermezzo. did i mention cornbread? 
Cons: keep away from the cardboard-imitating chicken, scary bathroom. marinated tofu can be a little tough sometimes.

Yum!!! The fries are SO good! I always get the chicken avocado burger, and it never disappoints. The service is very friendly and the atmosphere is great!
Last night I was craving soup like nothing else. I got the potato leek soup, and it was heaven!!! I was very happy with my choice. It came with a HUGE piece of cornbread! It was only 3 bucks and some change plus tax. ah! so so so good!

I LOVE Smart Alec's!  I love the free fries with an A paper, and I love the cornbread.  I also like the garden delight salad with sesame vinagrette dressing on the side, and the eggplant sandwich is delicious.  

Ahhh ... I miss Berkeley.

Within a radius of a few blocks, there's much better options. I'll give it one thing, the food is SUPER FAST. My friends rave about the cornbread and brownies. I want to love them, too. So badly. But they're average, like everything else here. And half of it doesn't seem that healthy, either...

Affordable and tasty salads! Whenever I eat here, I always experience death by salad (in a good way of course!). The only thing is that the ingredients in the salad are pretty standard. All leafy greens, no tomatoes, avocado, beans, or anything special. For their tofu salad, they give you loads of tofu, but the tofu is not too special and a bit on the bland side.

As for bread, I absolutely love their wheat bread! They give you a nice thick, chewy slice filled with a subtle honey sweetness. 

Their fries are pretty good AND they are air baked so it's "healthier" yay! Guilt-free fries~

Anytime I'm craving a hot cup of soup, I go to smart alec's "intelligent" food. I love their potato leek soup the best, but I like the others too. Aside from the chicken burger (which is sometimes overcooked), the burgers are crap. I'd rather eat a burger from Mac D's than here. Both the beef and veggie patty are pretty yucky. The marinated tofu is a joke, unless you're into that hard, overcooked piece of rubber. I like the fries here. I dip them in the "special" sauce that you gotta pump by the concession area. It's not healthy, but it's damn good with the fries. The dining area looks dirty. Like McDonald's bathroom dirty. Not so intelligent...
sesame tofu salad...but then again I LOOOOVVEEE sez me.

I've eaten here too much, which is annoying because there really isn't that much on the menu. What is there is good, however. Everything is ridiculously fresh and makes you feel healthier even after ingesting the calories. The fries aren't so good, but the cornbread is amazing.

Vegan options: Tofu avacado samdwich, hummus sandwich, eggplant melt (w/o cheese), fries, soups, all dressings except ranch, brownies and Big A Burger.

Psudo-vegan items to watch out for: Wheat bread, cornbread & crutouns.

Good food in a pinch, but also a close walk to Maoz Vegetarian, which has more vegan options.

Vibe was not great in here: very health-aware and a tad of "above-ness."
Did not think the burgers really stood up to any good standards- a little dry, not much flavor, disproportionate amounts of ingredients (more lettuce- what a surprise). Bottom line: Decent enough, but I definitely won't be back

Taste the same as any other burger joint in Berkeley lol. I cannot tell the different between regular beef and grass fed beef. It taste exactly the same if you'd ask me.
However, the fries are fking amazing. You get an amazing portion and you get a choice between regular and garlic. Other then that, I do not want to offend anyone about beef comparison. It is just that my first time experience with grass fed beef was at this restaurant. I can detect that it is a good quality meat but it just does not taste special at all. I have had aged rib eye and that taste so fcking amazing compare to non aged rib eye you buy and cook immediately. You can taste a whole hell of a difference compare to regular.
Still love this place.  Alec you are really Smart!

I have this never ending conflict with garlic fries.  They always sound so good, but end up usually being far too overwhelming.  Why is this?  Garlic bread almost always has the requisite amount of garlic to be delicious, but not fire bomb in your mouth.  Anyway, I wasn't a fan of Alec's garlic fries.  I got an avocado burger to accompany my fries.  Eh.  It was more guacamole than avocado.  Kind of a different flavor profile.  I could barely taste the cheese.  It was sort of a very bland situation.  Which was so stark in comparison with the fries, which were beating me senseless.  Yes, Alec, your food may be intelligent, but when it comes to taste, you are sitting in the middle of the bell curve.

good place, go there a lot for the garlic fries and chicken burger (which is the same as the chicken sandwich, but with a bun instead of bread, yet it costs like $1.30 less). salads are good as are the sandwiches. half salad/sandwich deal is one of the better deals on telegraph. cornbread and brownies are solid.

So I have been here a few times now. I like the food. It sort of makes me feel like I am eating healthier even though I know I am probably just evening out. I go for the veggie burger and leave it plain with the fries (unfried). The patty is actually really good. Not rubbery like ones in stores. The location and inside are also pretty cool. There is a lot of seating but it is usually filled. Since the tables are small you end up with the road blocked situation with a group of 4 people, and two tables open just at different ends of the room. 

All and all good stuff.

Good customer service.  Always redo my order when I forget to ask for the sandwhich without the "special sauce." I always forget.  Good prices.  They can feed vegetarians.  Didn't give me S$*t for drinking a jamba juice in the place.  (impulse rate)

i dont know how healthy this place can be considering the size of the dishes but it's worth the price. :]

garlic fries - has good and bad days, but always a good deal cus you get a ton for like $2

a burger - i love me some veggie burgers. and ive had my share. this is sooo morningstar griller's quality. either a knockoff of that, or plain jst morningstar. BUT DELICIOUS. 

that's all i ever get here. i always come at the wrong times cus the lines always reach the door when im here..

in the summer.. i think their onions go bad or something cus twice ive had heartburn from the super strong tasting onions enough to think i was dying..

Smart Alec's is kinda cheap and it will fill you up.  It is pretty fast.  Their veggie burger leaves something to be desired and their fries aren't that great.  I've only been here once, not sure if I will come back because there are many other delicious options in Berkeley.  If you are in a hurry and want a burger and fries though, it's an ok choice.

I prefer Smart Alec's over Intermezzo because of one simple item: the generous helping of CORN BREAD.  Their cornbread is moist, sweet, and oh so delicious!  I always get the half eggplant sandwich (w/ petso, swiss, onion, lettuce, and tomato), a half green w/ honey mustard, and of course the corn bread

We just stopped in for a quick snack but i'd have to say the air baked fries we had were the best that i've eaten in a long time. And it tasted super fatty but turns out they're really healthy! Looks like a lot of people got salads and burgers and those are probably really tasty and healthy too. I think i'll come back for more fries next time, they were really cheap too and much better than fast food places!

Ah, how I love Smart Alecs. Cheap, close by, and very generous portions.

My favorite thing to get there is the 1/2 sandwich, 1/2 soup combo. For just around $7, its seriously the best deal near campus for the taste:price ratio. I always get the eggplant melt (no onions) because its just so freakin good. The "special sauce" is really just caesar dressing and mixes very well with the melting cheese and pesto spread that goes along with it. Every soup I've ever had there has been phenomenal... probably like the vegetable or potato leek the best. OH, and it comes with a piece of cornbread that could be a meal all itself? Seriously, this place rules.

Plus, the garlic fries are a STEAL for $1.55 for a medium (which is bigger than a large at any other fast food place).

Minus one star for being cash only, otherwise, perfect.

garlic fries are eh. its really just hype imo.

good price for the combo of burger, fries and drink.

the sandwiches are better than the burgers but they're around 7 bucks and it doesnt come with fries or drink! salad & soup are around 7 bucks too :/

Ew! Worst overpriced sandwich ever! Stay away. Don't let the sassy name fool you. This place was not good eats. Well I had the Avocado Turkey sandwich on whole wheat bread. First the bread, I'm all for organic, but not at the expense of taste. Yuck! And the rest, was "Meh!" at best. Go eat elsewhere

I love the Garlic Fries !!!! 

I want to come back and try other menu items but for now this review is simply on the fries

The burgers here are ok.  Not a bad alternative for non-meat but I've had better.

Air baked fries were strangely good though.  Those I could get again.

Good location with fresh air eating.  Not bad on a good day.

Came here for lunch one day. It's very busy, but we got there before the rush. Fries were bland, and the burger was dry. The service was also slow. Good thing is, they give you ample amounts of food and a very good price. Clean restaurant too.
The food doesn't stand up to the hype.  I found the food okay, and not very exciting.  I'd go here only if I'm really desperate for fast food.  I'd rather get a smoothie at Jamba Juice.

Another place I like to eat when I go to Berkeley! Air baked fries= zero grease, it sold me and the soup was really good and usually I'm not a soup kind of girl. I def. reccomend if you're craving good american food.

I wanna give this place more stars then i am because the food is soo delicious but the service is craapppy! I love A guilt free lunch! The food is fresh and tasty! Get the cornbread! Now back to the crappy service... It's all kids which doesn't surprise me considering it's down the street of UC Berkeley but they treat their workplace like their own personal hangout spot. But once you get past all that you get to enjoy a tasty healthy meal!

Where can you get a GIANT bowl of creamy delicious lick your bowl clean NON DAIRY soup AND a huge hunk of finger licking good corn bread for UNDER $5?
Why, Smart Alec's of course!

I know I oughta branch out and order other items on the menu but I just can't seem to get beyond the potato leek soup or the corn chowder.  Well, OK,  to be honest, I have "tried" a few other things: the veggie burgers are good, their salads are also good (homemade, vegan dressings!) and they make a good sandwich, too.  
But the soup ... OMG!

Good, inexpensive, healthy food!

This place offers burgers, soups, salads, sandwiches, and cornbread. Ah, cornbread. I've only been here once, but I definitely look forward to going there often this summer. I ordered the tossed green salad with vinaigrette. I love how the salad came with a big chunk of cornbread (I love cornbread). The salad was actually pretty good--good variety of veggies. The prices are very good too-- less than $4 for a green salad and a less than $5.50 for a half salad half soup or sandwich combo. Can't get a better deal than this...

I never really understood why all of my friends love this place.  I just don't get it.  It's cash only....the cashiers make mistakes and aren't very nice about fixing them.....the tables are always messy.....and the food isn't very good!  I've had the veggie burger a few times but it has a strange taste that I never got used to.  The fries are ok, nothing special in my opinion.  The only thing good about them is that you can get them for free if you get an A on something.  I suppose for starving students that's a great incentive to like this place, but for me, ehhhhhh.

85% of the time, Smart Alec's delivers great food.  That's a B, but I'll give them extra credit and a B+.  I come here a lot.

The vegetarian burger option is average with a tasteless patty, but there's Bongo Burger to make up for that.  It's the eggplant and avocado sandwiches I get from Smart Alec's.  Minus the onions.  Incredibly yummy and filling.  

The salads are also incredible.  Sometimes I'm torn between Smart Alec's and Café Durant for salad, but Smart Alec's usually wins.  There are so many dressing options, too.

The fries are amazing while they're warm, and terrible when they cool.  Funny how that works.  And sometimes the lemonade tastes strange, so I never order it anymore.

Soup and cornbread makes for a nice meal, too.  The soups aren't filling, but the cake-like cornbread is!

This is a very high traffic, noisy place.  Usually the staff has it together, but sometimes their order mess-ups are hilarious.  I asked for no onions, where's the other half of my sandwich, what's with this weird paper and why is this wet?  

It's fun to sit down here and eat with a friend on occasion, but I usually get food to go and eat someplace cleaner and calmer.  The afternoon sun in the windows can be blinding, and the space gives me high school cafeteria flashbacks.  But I love Smart Alec's.

This place was alright. We were starving after driving all day from Socal and since my friend lived only a few blocks from there we decided to eat there since there were a few vegetarians in our group. I got a Chicken Cesar Salad which was huge but the price was also a match. I think they had an option to get a half portion but since I was starving I just went for the full size. I was completely disappointed with the chicken which was completely rubbery. The dressing tasted like it was made from 80% yellow mustard and they pour way too much. To top it off the lettuce was warm and wilted. The only thing that salvaged my meal was that a friend split their cornbread with me, which was great. 

The location itself was chaotic. The line was super long and people were standing around aimlessly waiting for their food because they could not find a seat. When we found a table we had to clean it ourselves because it was completely filthy and there didn't seem to be anyone going around to do it. The drinks area was a mess. At one point they didn't even have plastic utensils so 2 of the people in our group had to wait like 5 minutes will they brought more out. 

I dont think I'll coming back. I think the only reason I would be back is if I went to school there and I was too tired or lazy one day to go somewhere else since it so conveniently located next to campus.

BEST CORNBREAD EVER!! It breaks my heart a little everytime I see people with the wheat bread instead of cornbread. They don't know what they're missing out on!

The fries are yummy and healthy. The burgers are normal, nothing special. The potato leek soup is thick and delicious, but the corn chowder is awkwardly sour. It tastes kind of like potato salad, but in a thick liquid form with corn. I've also tried the eggplant plant sandwich which is okay, but really mushy. I've heard amazing things about the turkey cranberry sandwich, so I'm going to try that next!

Sure it's healthy, but it doesn't really taste good.

One time, when I wasn't looking for some of my usual UC area fare like Top Dog, Naan n' Curry, Blondies or even IB's  I decided to give this place a try.  Healthy is a good thing, at the time I was eating a little too much junk food.  I looked at the menu, prices were a bit steep so I ordered the burger combo, which is the cheapest thing there.  When asked if I wanted to upgrade to garlic fries I said sure, a free upgrade to garlic fries is always welcome.

Except for this time.

The garlic wasn't even really cooked, it seemed like somebody scooped some minced garlic from the big Christopher Ranch tub you can get a Costco on the fries.  No other seasonings or anything else.  The garlic didn't even stick on the fries.  The burger was also dry, somehow these guys made Niman Ranch beef taste like the plain non-organic stuff you can get at Food 4 Less.  That's oddly amazing.

One extra star for being "healthy" but in this day an age, healthy doesn't need to equate to "tastes like crap."

Not a breakfast place apparently. We came in at 1030, group of four, ordered, and were told that a couple breakfast items we wanted to order weren't available. One of them after we paid, so they had to give us a refund. They didn't charge us correctly, but we let that slide because it was in our favor. Then the food comes out and two of the sandwiches were not what we ordered, one of them didn't even look like anything on the menu. Too bad, because the sandwiches probably deserved three stars.

Go to Smart Alec's for "smart" fast food! Everything from soup, salad, sandwiches, even burgers and fries! They have whole wheat buns too. It's sorta hard to believe that their fries are as low in fat as advertised but I'll take their word for it. Though I have a feeling it's a mere mix of ketchup and mayo, I dig their 'special sauce.' When I'm craving a burger + fries for lunch I go here and don't feel bad after.

Lots of room to sit though it gets crowded midday. They have to do something about their trash station, the itty-bitty circle they have to dump your stuff in gets bothersome after couple of visits. Random but I had to mention it, me and my co-worker share laughs about this when we're there.

I ordered an eggplant melt, which was just OK.    It needed flavor - the 
"special sauce" didn't cut it and there wasn't enough.     They claim to have been voted Best French Fries somewhere (maybe The Bay Guardian), but they were virtually inedible.     I won't be going back anytime soon.

I actually frequented Smart Alec's when I was a student at Cal many many years ago and was pleasantly surprised to find that it is still around.  Had a Garden Salad and a large garlic fries.  

Bottomline:  A great healthy option for the UC campus area and very affordable.  The garlic fries continue to be yummy.   Would definitely recommend if you want to have healthier meals while you are there.  

What we liked:

(1) The large salad loaded with good ingredients - in addition to greens, there was alfafa sprouts, edamame, chickpeas, wheat berries, boiled egg - plus, you can get the dressing on the side, which is great so they won't accidentally drown your vegetables. 

(2) Generous portion of garlic fries - not as good as regularly fried ones, not as crispy, but for a healthier alternative, it was very good.  I am surprised not more places have air-baked ones.

(3) Affordable - all the above for less than $8! (something like this would cost $10+ in San Francisco/Palo Alto

There are definitely better salad places in the Bay Area (Pluto's being my favourite!) but overall Smart Alec's will always have a place in my heart because it reminds me of the good ol' college days :-)

I am halfway through their stampcard!! Free fries, here I come! =D
I love their fries and their sesame chicken salad. Their sandwiches are also very delicious... and so is their cornbread.. their brownies look fabulous on display at the counter too... ok, everything is good here.

Love the food, especially the tofu sandwich, but service was an issue. Cashier arrogantly and rudely refused our $20 bills from the 1980s because he couldn't find a watermark (there wasn't one back then) and his special pen mark didn't fade. He didn't even check the date when we told him it was quite old. I understand the need to be cautious, but no need to be rude.

I love Smart Alec's for their burgers. Every time I go, I get a Big A Burger Combo that comes with a choice of regular fries or garlic fries and a drink. All that for about $6. 

The Big A Burger is cooked nicely and topped with lettuce, tomatoes, onions, pickles and mustard. The garlic fries, I think, have a bit too much garlic on them, but since they are the same price as regular fries, I get them. 

I have to deduct a star because of the inconvenience of being cash only. It is a very central spot, near campus and also near Bank of America in case you did forget your cash. 

Also, if you get an A on a paper, you can get free fries! That's always great.

Overall, I love the restaurant and enjoy eating there...once in a while.

I'm a big fan of the sesame salad with the cornbread. The regular size is enormous, so I usually get the half.   It's quick and delicious.  CASH only! I always forget that and have to walk over to the bank after waiting in line. And, the girl that works the front counter has really pretty eyes!

This was a weekly stop for me when I was up north.  I used to get the chicken sandwich with avocado, etc.  Mmmmm.  I was actually addicted to this combo with the fries and would oftentimes take it to go, sneak it into my room, and eat it in perfect contentment.

Smart Alec's was okay. The few times I went I got the B Burger which is basically a burger with avocado on it. It was pretty good and I liked it just fine. The fries are really good and crispy too :)

The servers weren't very friendly and it's always been super crowded when I went so it was hard to find a seat. It was a bit inconvenient how they only take cash but I think a lot of places in Berkeley are like that. 

Overall, it's a good place to eat but the food wasn't life-changing or anything.

Smart Alec's has recently downgraded all their plasticware, and not in the eco-friendly sense. Their previous high-quality utensils are now of the cheap, shiny plastic ilk -- but that I can ignore. However, they now package their soups and salads in much smaller, less sturdy containers. Note: that means smaller serving sizes! I mean, they're still pretty decent portions, but it's just not the same when a dollar buys you less. Times are tough, I guess. Fortunately, the quality of the soups and salads has stayed the same (yum!), so I'll still be around for a healthy food fix.

This may be the one of the best veggie burgers I've had.  Everything else is overall great for the cheap prices.  Big salad portions with amazing cornbread (and I'm from Texas).  I just wish the burgers were bigger.

The best part?  The frequent buyer cards!

Every time that I've eaten at Smart Alec's (which is too many to count,) I have never been disappointed. The portions are generous, the ingredients are fresh, and the food is quite simply--yummy!--especially for the affordable prices.

Some of my favorites (which is practically most of the menu):
-The Big B burger--great portion, great flavor, fresh, and nothing like those other fast food joints (ahem, McDonald's)
-Basil Chicken Burger--chicken is never too dry, the basil mayo sauce is amazing
-Eggplant Melt--grilled eggplant, basil pesto, cheese.. you know how sometimes the taste of eggplant can be overpowering? not at all, in this case. just right!
-Roasted Turkey Breast--delicious cranberry sauce!
-Corn chowder
-Potato leek
