-Tofu salad--love the sesame dressing
-Air baked fries--the best fries I've ever had!
-Cornbread

Now only if they took credit/debit cards! They make up for it w/ the "A" deal (bring in an exam or paper that you received an A on and you get free fries!)

This place is wonderful. I'm absolutely certain I have discovered the best combo on the menu, which is the half-soup half-salad combo with their corn chowder and sesame chicken salad. The corn chowder is everything a chowder buff could ask for, filled with wonderful chunks of potato and celery; I did a double-take when I realized it was not made with any dairy! The sesame chicken salad is also delightful. Sure, the salad mix may not contain heirloom lettuces, but the freshness of the cucumbers, combined with the tangy dressing, tasty chicken, and crispy noodles provides a wonderful combination of textures. Also make sure to go for the cornbread. It is a bit heavy (I never end up finishing it all), but provides a sweet foil to the rest of the meal. The amount of food you get for the price is also incredible, and I've been back more times than I can count while I've lived here.

I remember having a very bland burger the first and only time I ordered one here.

Too bad that was the only thing I had to judge this place off of.

I just have to say first off: best cornbread ever. Now on with the review: I realized recently that I love Smart Alec's. I've had their veggie burger, hamburger, soup, salad, and more. Today I couldn't decide on just one item from their tasty-sounding menu so I got the half-sandwich half-salad combo for ~$7. Their hummus sandwich is delicious: I'm not sure if they add something to the hummus, because it tastes lighter and creamier than the store-bought kind. The wheat bread for the sandwich is hearty and tastes high quality. Also, the "half" salad is really only slightly smaller than the full: the tossed green salad includes small savory croutons and a variety of leafy greens, but more tomato would be nice, as they only include a slice. Although it is easy to overlook as a side when you're contemplating the menu, the very, very best thing about Smart Alec's is the aforementioned cornbread. It's supremely moist and sweet--okay, maybe more cake-like than bread--and thus absolutely scrumptious. Just looking at the giant trays of cornbread in their kitchen cut into generous ~3"x3" squares makes me salivate--even after I've failed at finishing my large meal. They market themselves as a healthy option, which I don't really believe since their food, including burgers, fries, and the works, seems like typical American fare but whatever--it's yummy.  

The line moves super fast, and they also serve up orders within minutes! I've never presented them with an "A" paper/test to get a discount, which I've heard can be done. I may try it, though, since I plan on coming back many, many more times in the future. 

Pros: cornbread, specialty sandwiches, fast service

Cons: cash only

Edible but not worth returning. I've been there twice (yes I made that mistake). The first time I got a burger which was dry and forgettable. The next time I got a turkey sandwich which was so dry and fell apart so quickly that I decided to post this review. Not a good choice considering caffe intermezzo is a block away.

This is my favorite place to eat on Telegraph.  I often complain that there's not very much good food on Telegraph Ave (I work on UC's campus), but this is the exception.  The veggie burgers are delicious and healthy.  It's also very reasonably priced.

Simple food, low price, nothing fabulous, but its very consistent and chain-like.  I really enjoy their soups... particularly the leek and potato or the corn chowder, and it comes with a huge piece of sweet cornbread.  A really good value.  The 1/2 soup/1/2 salad combo feeds you for 2 meals... its quite nice.
this place is worse that mcdonalds

If I could like this place, I would be okay with that.   I seriously tried. 

I ordered nothing out of the norm for me, but here, at this place?  I was greeted by the bad hand of the diarrhea man.  Once I felt nauseated.  The other two times I ate there I got violently ill - food sickness style.  What is IN that food. Barf barf barf. 

Smart A's will always remind me of being stuck in a car with 2 best friends, and a bridge full of traffic as that old diarrhea came to see me. 

ick.

Vito and I were quite surprised with how much we enjoyed Smart Alec's. We shared the veggie burger (with cheese, of course) and the chicken sandwich/tossed green salad combo. The food tasted really good and it made both of us feel good to have such straight forward fare. 

Great value, excellent food and cute girl at the register, made the experience a win. A great alternative for fast food.

I don't care what anyone else says, their fries are amazing.
i don't eat fried food so whenever I can take the 40min. BART ride to Berkeley Smart Alec's is the first place I go to.
My friend, who practically only eats fast food said their fries are awesome.
So all you haters can shut it.
Their veggie burger is good and for people whining about it being plain or simple, LOOK AT THE PRICE! It's cheap healthy fast food!

I just stopped in here for a veggie burger yesterday while visiting my brother, a Cal employee. I went with the Big A burger, veggie burger and garlic fries. It was not the best veggie burger I've ever had, but it was decent. The garlic fries were solid. Much like the Berkeley population, they were baked, and are much healthier than the average fry.

All in all a pretty nice place. Check out a full review on my blog. 

http://fastfoodreviewed.com/half-baked---smart-alecs-healthy-food-fast/

S'alright. What seems most attractive about Smart Alec's is the restaurant's philosophy: they make their own stuff, natural, not bought from big suppliers.  It's like an American Apparel for food.

Carnivores: even the meat tastes slightly vegetarian.  If you're vegetarian or anything of the sort, you'll be happy.

My wife liked the soup and salad but I got to tell you, the hamburger leaves a lot to be desired.  It tasted pretty neutral and had the consistancy of a boiled hockey puck (man, I haven't eaten one of those in YEARS!  Good times ...)  

Really, the food is ok but you know what ruins it for me?  The environment.  The damn resturant is like eating in a warehouse space.  It's so noisy with so much ambient reverb all you want to do is stuff napkins in your ears but then you will have to listen to yourself chew which will ruin any meal no matter how good it tastes.  If you must eat here, and it is fairly inexpensive, then I suggest taking your food to go and eating it someplace quiet like your car or on a street corner or in the Touchless Car Wash a few blocks away.
Only in Berkeley...

There's a lot of food to choose from in this part of Berkeley, so I was definitely a bit skeptical when my friends chose this place ("I've heard they've got great veggie burgers!") over the many nearby tried-and-true grease joints, like IB Hoagies. With little energy to argue, I relented and we headed to Smart Alec's.

I hate to give out just one star but there was absolutely nothing about my experience here that was enjoyable. 

It was crowded when we got there - not necessarily a bad sign except I think Smart Alec hired his brother Dumb Bob to organize the dining area. After I ordered, there was nowhere to wait for my to-go order (too many occupied tables inside), so my buddies and I just awkwardly lounged around, having to tell customers who had just walked in "we're not in line" multiple times. That awkward lounging lasted for 15 minutes. I was relieved to hear my number and get out of there. (Also, weirdly, their numbering system is not coordinated between the two registers, so they were calling out numbers in the twenties AND seventies at the same time.)

When I ate my $8.30 meal (burger + garlic fries) five minutes later, my regret had crystallized into this one star review. The burger was the epitome of mediocre. I could tell this before I had even taken it out of the bag. Bland, lame, got any other meh words? My drunk friends can cook a better burger on an unevenly-heated grill while blindfolded, and let's not talk about how this compares to In n Out. The bun was whole wheat (which sounds ok i guess) but soggy and prone to falling apart too soon (before the last 3-ish bites). I'm glad I didn't spend another $0.60 on cheese because it would not have helped an already sad situation. I don't know why people like the fries here. I guess "garlic" means "heat up some garlic and dump it in the bag after the fries." The garlic was too undercooked for my taste, and wasn't chopped up or evenly distributed amongst the fries. 

I'm no die-hard burger aficionado. But I'm also smarter than Smart Alec's. This place is pulling a fast one on all the naive, smiling fresh-freshmen: there is healthy food in Berkeley that tastes good and doesn't hurt your wallet, and you will not find it at Smart Alec's.

I am a pretty forgiving person, but I still hold a grudge against Smart Alec's from 6 years ago!

Here is the story:
Really hungry one afternoon, I went there with a friend, and didn't realize they only served vegetarian. To be sure, I even asked if they made regular burgers with real meat and the lady at the counter said they did. So I thought, cool maybe they serve a burger with quality meat on whole wheat buns with fresh toppings, and I ordered one of the "intelligent" things.  A little while later, I happily received my burger, ravenously bit in, to taste what only can be described as cardboard with lots of mustard. EEEW! So I immediately proceeded to the lady I ordered from and said I had the wrong order. She looked at it, and said I had the right thing, so I asked her where the meat was and what this grayish looking patty was. She said they didn't serve meat, and I reminder her she said they did when I ordered, then asked for a refund to which she absolutely refused. My "burger" was deposited in the nearest garbage can because I didn't want a bum to suffer from it. 

So, Smart Alec's always makes me cringe.
I know this is suppose to be a health concious spot but the food is so blah. Come here if you wanna pay to eat grass, cardboard chicken breast, or that kitchen sponge they call cornbread.

I usually fall back on eating at this place when I come to telegraph for some walking, talking, and light shopping with my bestie.
I've never had a bad experience here but some things do stand out to me:

Perks:
-good, fresh-tasting ingredients. mostly organic.
-decently fast service
-friendly enough
-good ppl watching
-gargantuan sized portions
-love the cornbread as a side to salads

Dislikes:
-so overlycrowdedinthere
-not a clean restroom, ladies have to hover
-the burgers are kinda funky
-as big as it is, there's hardly ever any seating

Smart Alec's doesn't really taste smart..o_O.  it actually taste pretty salty, the salad dressing is not special at all, the egg plant in the sandwich is burnt.....not a smart choice to avoid cancer...i probably can live without it for a while!!

Smart Alecs helps demonstrate that healthy food and deliciousness are mutually exclusive.  I tried a tofu sandwich with air baked fries (a.k.a. sliced baked potatoes) and I actually felt like I accomplished something when I managed to finish it.  Go here if you want bland food that won't give you a heart attack.

The traditional burger here sucks balls. It is expensive for the size, salty as fuck, and tastes no healthier than any other beef patty sandwiched by mediocre buns. You can find a better burger practically anywhere someone knows how to cook. Their tasteless advertising also makes my ass muscles clench. 

I added an extra star for the vegetarians who seem to be satisfied by their menu choices. Then again, there's no way to really make chloroplast unhealthy and anger-inducing.

Mmmmmmmmmmm their cornbread is so moist and sweet and yummy.  Literally, it rivals my mother's cornbread (but don't tell her; she'll die).  Also, their homemade vegetable soup (which should actually be called carrot soup, since that is the vegetable that is most present) is just amazing.  For $3.50, I can satisfy my desire for home cooking with a bowl of veggie soup and a HUGE piece of corn bread.  

The air-baked fries are good too and if you bring in an "A" paper you get a serving for FREE. 

The veggie burger sucks.  Go to IBs or Barney's or pretty much anywhere else for a good veggie burger.

y'know... i walked by this joint for years, never knowing what was in there.  with a name like smart alecs, in a city with the nations no. 1 public university, i NATURALLY thought this place was a tutoring center... and the owners' name was alec.  don't laugh, i'm serious.  i kid you not, i walked across those HUGE windows and must've not once looked inside.  i was too busy focusing on rare/bargain cd's and fat slice/blondies pizza.

so when i finally went IN that place, naturally my reaction was, "this place serves FOOD?!"  and pretty good food at that.  i've had their burger, and i wouldn't even know that it was healthy if it weren't for the lack of grease.  

the garlic fries are good.

the hummus is good.

the chili is also good.

healthy food never tasted so good.

I actually really like Smart Alec's.  It's good healthy fare that makes the hippie inside me scream with joy knowing that the extra $3 I paid for an organic multigrain wheat bread with dolphin-safe-tuna, pesticide/fertilizer-free-lettuce, and free-trade-recycled-water-tomato is going to a good cause: assuaging my environmental guilt for leaving an air conditioner on full blast when I go to the RSF so I can return to a cold room.  I get the soup and sandwich combo since their potato leek & chili is pretty bomb, especially with a hunk of corn bread thrown into the hefty mix.

The fries are a hit or a miss with me sometimes.  I've had heavenly crunchy fries and then another random day they'll have the texture of soggy tapioca balls.  I see people rave about how awesome it is that the fries are air-baked, like it's the greatest invention since the iPhone, internet porn, or internet porn on the iPhone.  OMG, 0G TRANS FAT, PRAISE DA LAWD HALLELUJAH!!!  It's frickin fries, why would one even care about the nutritional value of pure carbs in grease?  It's still loaded with starchy diabetes-inducing goodness.  Hostess Twinkies are baked,  I'm pretty sure they are also "baked with/in air" (air-baked lolwut?) is that sh*t still healthy?  

One gripe I have is that this place needs to start accepting credit cards.  If you aren't allowing for credit cards in 2010, you might as well regress your business, ban cash transactions altogether, and set up a barter-system for point-of-sale exchanges.  I'll trade 2 Camel Turkish Silvers and a page of my Econ 140 reader for half a turkey sandwich please.

TL;DR: Healthy food that doesn't taste like cardboard.  In fact it's ridiculously good.  The exercise you get from walking one block to the Bank of America ATM so you can actually eat at Alec's synergizes with your yuppie new age lifestyle.  Tighten those strings on your hemp running pants, take a deep breath, and smile smugly champ!

This god damnned place tricked me into eating a veggie burger.

What would you like sir?

I'll have the (um...)  (ummm...) (oh crap better order somethin fast...) the Big A burger.

So you figure the big A would be the signature dish.  Now any other God loving place in america would have a dead animal as the centerpiece of the meal.  But this was DIRTY-HIPPY-LEFT WING-IT'S-OK-TO-BANG-YOUR-SISTER-AS-LONG-AS-YOU-DRIVE-A-HYBRID-CAR -BERKELEY-CALIFORNIA.  And these bastards have the brazen to have a god damnned veggie burger as their signature dish.

Well I wasn't gonna have it.  I spit that bite out into the sewer and gave the rest to some bum.  I tricked him into thinking it was a real beef patty.  Boy did I get that guy good.

And then I went down to top dog to have some real food.

If there is one city in the Bay Area that would have a restaurant that served healthy fast food, it would definitely be Berkeley. Am I right, or am I right?

 I've tried about 3 different burgers/sandwiches here, and liked each one. I like how they make their fries...it's like they always have the right amount of "crisp" about them. I've never had any of their soups or salads, but I'll definitely have to try them next time I'm here. As a couple of other reviewers have noted, it's kind of a trip eating stuff like burgers and fries here, but not feeling guilty about it since the food at Smart Alec's is a healthier alternative to the typical burger joint. 

In terms of location, it's at a pretty good spot to sit, eat, and do some people watching since it's right at the corner of Telegraph, across from what used to be the old Rasputin's, if I remember correctly. It's not too far from the Cal campus, and is close to a number of the other cool shops and street peddlers' tables on Telegraph. 

FYI: make sure to bring cash, since they don't accept debit/credit cards here.
The fries are just the way I like them - thin and crispy.  The basil chicken sandwich was okay.  Despite the crowds, there was ample seating (even if a little bit cramped).

I had high hopes for this place. Every time I make it out to Berkeley I see that it is very busy. Busyness usually means that the food and service is good, but both were mediocre at best. 

The overall ambiance is nothing special. The place didn't look that clean and the set up was not inviting. The girl who took our order was rude right from the start. We didn't ask complicated questions, but every time we would talk she would look at us like we were inconveniencing her. She made my friend and I feel like idiots. 

We ordered a roasted turkey sandwich and a strawberry smoothie. The sandwich was dry and tasted like gross packaged meat even though it looked more like turkey from Thanksgiving. The bread was tasty, but that was the only redeeming aspect. The smoothie was good, but had some unrecognizable chunks on the bottom. 

I was very unimpressed. Not only was the service bad and condescending, but the food wasn't even good either. I won't be visiting again.

The bathroom is nastier than gas station bathrooms.  My burger was seriously gross, I had to throw it out.  The fries were limp.  I wanted something fast.  Better to have edible food slow than garbage fast.

Veggier burger, air-BAKED fries (garlic or regular), AND a huge drink for a fiver? No way you say... but YES, at Smart Alec's, its possible and awesome. The caesar salad tastes mustardy in an extreme way, but I have a very strong aversion to mustard so you can go try it if you want. Vegans and meat eaters are all satisfied with their cheap prices and healthy eats. Convenient location and very fast.

ATTN: Berkeley students

If you bring in an A paper or exam, Smart Alecs will give you free regular or GARLIC fries!!!

I basically only come here when I can take advantage of this deal. Then for only about 4.50, I can get a big burger and a heaping order of fries!

Would I pay full price for food here? Probably not. 

But if you like rabbit food, the salads here are humongous. Like you may need two people to eat it. 

The soup I ordered once was satisfying too.

So really, only come here when you can take advantage of the deal I just told you about and you will leave satisfied.

Oh and it's cash only FYI.

If you're SMART, you'll avoid this place. 
I keep coming back and I don't know why....it's probably because I like putting my stomach under stressful situations, and also because I'm NOT smart...
Every time I come here, I get these stomach aches throughout the day! The aches are terribly uncomfortable for me and for nearby noses....if you know what I'm saying.....

Their salads even make me queasy!! The only thing I don't have an adverse reaction to is their corn chowder. Today, I got the chowder and decided to treat myself to some garlic fries. 
1. The fries were limp, stale, and greasy
2. The garlic was really clumpy and too strong. There was no balance in flavors. 
3. I tasted the garlic on my breath 6 hours after I ate the fries and even after a vigorous brushing.
4. I haven't stopped passing gas since I ate here for lunch at 1pm. It's 11pm right now.

God, I feel so bad for my roommate.... 
AND she told me not to go to Smart Alec's a few weeks ago when we both came home with stomach aches. I've learned my lesson.

It may be healthy, but the food here tastes horrible and it's way expensive for what you get.  Given all the amazing yet affordable restaurants in Southside Berkeley, I can't believe this place is still in business after all these years.  "Healthy fast food"?  Give me a break.

Unless every calorie counts, skip it.  Even then you might be better off going to Subway just down Telegraph, Jared-style.

I have come here a couple times lured in by the name, all healthy and smart-sounding.  But each time I have come in, I have vowed to never come back.  I guess its my fault that I went back!

I have ordered something different every time I have eaten there, and everything has been severely disappointing.  Same goes for the poor shmucks eating with me.  

I would rather grab a sandwich, burger, salad, whatever at a few other restaurants in a 2-block radius.  They say A+, but I give them a C-...barely passing

3.5* to be fair.

When I had my salad phase, this place was the place to go for me. Salad was large and filling, had plenty of protein sources (which would be an issue for vegetarians or vegans) and came corn bread (instant win). They also have a card stamp system dealio, so if you frequent the place enough, you'll eventually earn a free something-or-other.

I frequented this place when I was a good, 'ol student at Cal. This is a great place to get a healthy, fast meal. Their menu consists of things like salads, soups, burgers, sandwiches, and smoothies. When I feel like a burger, I get their vegetarian burger meal, which comes with their famous, huge corn bread, their famous air-baked fries, and a drink. I absolutely love their CORN BREAD! SOOO GOOD! If I don't get a burger, I always settle with their vegetable soup and their corn bread! YUM YUM!

You have to got to eat here...Don't be intimidated by the long lines though...they go pretty fast, since many people already know what they want when they get there...

Why do you only have a total rating of 3.5 stars, Alec?! I'm going to help you out in the star department, because you were one of the best things to happen to me (dining-wise) in college. 

Ok, so. The food here is healthy because they don't smother things with oil (for instance, fries are baked). The ingredients taste fresh, and the food options are health-concious - wheat buns and bread, salads-a-plenty, veggie and breast meat burgers, etc. 

Also, the food *is* fast- I've never waited more than 5 minutes for anything. OH, and they have loyalty cards, which I am not ashamed to admit I've filled up numerous times.

 If I were to suggest one thing, it would be for them to offer low-fat salad dressing.  Please? :)

The food here is questionably healthy. 

However, the portions are big, the burgers are tasty, and the prices are very affordable.

Service: 2/5
Food: 2/5
Cleanliness: 4/5
Area: 4/5
Price: 2/5 - not worth it.

Not really familiar with this area since it's been so long since I've been here and we were looking for a semi-healthy place to eat and Smart "A+"lecs Intelligent Food "advertised" healthy looking food.

First of all, the cashier who took my order was not so helpful when it came to helping me choose the right soup. I specifically asked her a question, and she gave me a blank stare...then replied with a smart-remark 2 seconds later. RUDE. 

If you like big servings and choose quantity over quality tasting "healthy food". This is the spot. Big proportions are neither SMART NOR HEALTHY, period. I ordered a caesar salad and potato cream soup combo. The bread wasn't even toasted, the salad was so bland, even I could make a better tasting one at home.  

I know Berkeley is supposed to be known for good tasting food, and I've tried many good places around this area, but I've got to say this place was a mistake.

As soon as I saw "Avocado Burger" on the menu, I knew I was going to eat here. Prices are a little up there for a sit-yourself hamburger restaurant, but I have to say...it was worth it. The wheat buns are fresh and have a nice, earthy texture. The vegetables are fresh and the guacamole was well-prepared. My sandwich came with a special sauce but I honestly can't point out what it was; it tasted great, nonetheless. 

When I come here again, I'm bringing a friend so we both can enjoy!

In the city of Berkeley, Smart Alec is probably one of the most popular places for healthy fast food. You also do get your typical greasy hamburgers and fried, but there's also a choice of salads, soups, and sandwiches. There's even a small rewards program for frequent eaters at SmartAlec. I believe if you eat there at least 10 times, you would get something free.

Located in a close to UCBerkeley campus. And only a couple minute walk away from the Berkeley BART Station.

I don't usually come here because I don't find their food particularly special. They have burgers, which I am not a huge fan of, and they have salad, but I think Intermezzo beat any salads around Berkeley. I've walked by this place a billion times but only came here 2-3 times. 

I came here a couple of days to get fries for my friend and discovered that their fries are ridiculously cheap! For a large, it's only $2, which is way cheaper than McDonald. Also, the fries are very yummy. Also, they have hands down the best corn bread. It's super moist and delicious.

for what it is, it's good. i swear.

i wasn't expecting anything, considering it was already supposed to be "healthy fare", however, it much exceeds your expectations of the bland faceless foods that you expect from "healthy". 

for the health-conscious and the dieting, this would be a nice occasional spot to turn in and dine without too much guilt, as they do have the novelty of a burger, fries and soda. however, the fries are air-baked (a total of 6 grams of fat per serving of fries? take that, mcdonalds.) and there are chicken breast sandwiches on whole grain buns (again, suck it, mcd's.) then there are also the soups and salads; you can eat yourself content for about 6$ a person. 

i myself had a basil chicken breast sandwich; the novelty was nice, but the chicken was overcooked (or precooked and reheated, not quite sure which) but it was actually quite tasty outside of the dryness. the fries were nice and crispy, salted just right, though not "piping hot" like they just came out of a fryer. 

if you're in the area, stop by, it's a cheap healthy meal. if you'd rather pay the same amount for a la burrita burrito down the street, stab yourself. think about your health.

For health nuts, Smart Alec's is the place for you. With nearly grease free burgers and air baked french fries, they have everything to send you to cholesterol free heaven. However, for the normal customer like me, there is much to be desired and not much to be had. The burgers are flavorless and bland. Even with their unique toppings (red pesto, guacamole, and teriyaki), their burgers still lack the kick to make me crave one. Taste-wise, the french fries are average, the salads are average and the chili is just down right gross! Nasty after taste, strong lasting taste something terrible in their chili. It is also too thick and loaded with beans. GROSSSSSS. If you love to be super healthy, come here, if not go somewhere with more taste (i.e. IB's Hoagies, Bongo Burger, etc.)

Pros:
- Healthy
- Big salads

Cons:
- Gross chili
- Flavorless burgers
- Pricey
- Cash only

This place seemed to get a lot of traffic when my friends and I went in here which is a good sign. Another good sign was that people were getting their orders fairly quickly, so that means we wouldn't have to wait for long. The prices for burgers here are pretty good as are the price of friends (under $2 for a large order of regular or garlic fries). Sandwiches will cost you a little under $5 if I recall and salads range from $4 - 6. 

I got the 1/2 Sandwich 1/2 Salad meal along with a large order of fries not knowing that my friends had also gotten a large order of fries. The sandwich I settled on was the Chicken Breast Sandwich and I got a regular tossed green salad with sesame dressing. The wait for my food was around five minutes I believe and the portion of salad was fairly large. My biggest complaint with the tossed green salad was that I got only one tomato slice, and that the sesame dressing (on the side) was really salty. When I think of sesame dressing I think of something kind of sweet, but that wasn't the case with this sesame dressing. The sandwich was very "meh" I'd say. I could SEE the basil mayo that comes with it, but I couldn't taste it because frankly I don't think it added any flavor. With this meal comes your choice of corn bread or wheat bread and yes the corn bread is absolutely huge. The corn bread had the consistency of somewhere between pound cake and Angel food cake, so it wasn't really heavy but it also wasn't terribly light. 

Initially the fries basket looked pretty small, but in reality it was a good amount of fries they gave me. They had a good portion of shaved garlic on the fries too, so that was nice as well. The sauces offered for dipping fries consist of two types of ketchup, mustard, 1,000 Island, and mayo in packets. The fries are touted as being healthier than regular fries because they're air-baked and these fries definitely tasted way less greasy than regular fries. These fries were actually really good and crisp, and they were good enough that I bothered to eat the limp fries.

This place touts itself as a healthier restaurant and according to the nutritional data it offers for certain items it seems that way. If they're really healthy who knows and anything in excess is just asking for bad news. The next time in Berkeley I wouldn't mind giving this place another go.

Went here for lunch today. I ordered a tuna sandwich and fries. The sandwich was runny, way too much mayo and the tuna probably wasn't drained thoroughly.  The bread however, was delicious, thick and flavorful. 

The fries were decent. I wouldn't brag about them nor would I dis them. They were too salty, but its good to know that they aren't fried in oil. 

The whole meal was ready in like five minutes and the woman who took my order was pleasant. Definitly a step above fast food quality but still ready quick and very inexpensive.

Smart Alec's defines the three star experience. While all the food prepared here is (to the best of my knowledge) healthy, and finding a vegetarian or vegan option (when I'm in the mood) easier then most places in the larger Bay Area, I've neither been blown away nor tragically disappointed by my numerous meals here. 

The Salads? They're alright, the half is enough to fill me up (a difficult feat), while the full is enough to feed a small family. Otherwise, the dressings aren't that exciting, although I do like the concept (much more then the execution) of their "Vegan Caesar Dressing". Every Salad comes with a piece of cornbread, which is always a pleasant accoutrement. 

The Fries? Pretty Good. While the Garlic Fries aren't the best I've ever tasted, they certainly are good enough to warrant an order from time to time (especially if you bring in a paper with an A grade, at which point they're free).

Service? Quick and highly efficient. Even on the busiest of days, I usually get my food within 10 minutes. Their cash only policy is a pain in the ass, but I can understand that it expedites the service.

Ambiance? Probably the best part of the dining experience. Large picture windows overlook the crowd on Telegraph, and old rock plays in the background. If you're dining alone, the counter-like window seats are probably the best way to soak in the Telegraph Avenue vibe without actually having to deal with Telegraph Avenue itself.

I'll usually make a stop if I don't feel like walking far afield from campus, don't have much time to nosh and want to pretend to be living a healthy lifestyle. I'll re-review if I have a chance to try their breakfast options (which look to be pretty good).

The vegetable and potato leek soups are some of the best soups I've ever eaten, vegan or otherwise.

The wheatbread is sweet and tender and has quickly become one of my favorite sandwich breads. (Apparently they get it from a bakery down in Santa Cruz.) 

The vegan brownies are unbelievably good, and match my idea of a perfect brownie 100%. 

The air-baked fries, though not perfect, are much better than the vast majority of fast food fries (with the exception of McDonald's and In and Out). I actually used to think they were bland, but then I realized that they simply weren't seasoned enough: add 2 packets of salt and a bit of pepper, and they'll taste much better!

The burgers and sandwiches, on the other hand, are rather mediocre in my opinion, though admittedly the vegan burger is the best I've tasted.

sometimes you need a big ol' salad-- the got um.
sometimes you need some fries and don't want to feel guilty later-- got um
sometimes you want one of those "thanksgiving" sandwiches-- check!
sometimes you want some vegan soup-- yep
and other times you just need some cornbread-- all of the above comes with cornbread!!!!

woah!

"Meh."
Campus food stop.
I've been here at least 4 times already and all 4 times I order what amounts to be just, "meh." I'm nice though and I give them the benefit of the doubt. I always, and still do, tell myself that I just ordered the wrong thing. I just ordered the wrong burger, the wrong fries, the wrong sandwich, or the wrong salad. Next time will be better. But heck no. This place is just "meh."

What more is there to say really?

It's places like this that make me wish Yelp allowed the use of half stars in their reviews, because I had a tough time deciding whether to award 3 or 4 stars to Smart Alec's.

In terms of health consciousness and service, this popular Telegraph joint does everything right.  I love their commitment to affordable, fast food that supports a healthy lifestyle.  What's more, the cashiers are always friendly and helpful; on many occasions they've graciously indulged my "mix-and-match" habits, letting me order items in variations/portions which aren't necessarily offered on the menu.

And the food?  It's good...no better, no worse.  I usually order their veggie burgers because they're cheap and filling, but the flavor is really no more spectacular than something you could find in the frozen foods aisle of any supermarket.  The fries are okay, but then again, Pluto's garlic potato rings have probably spoiled my taste buds.  The only items really worth making a special visit for are the salads: big, yummy things with creative toppings (like marinated tofu and crispy noodles) and great dressings.  Opt for one of these with a piece of cornbread, and be prepared to enjoy a casual dining experience worthy of 4 solid Yelp stars.

May have cheap food but you get what you pay for. After I thought that I had made it clear to the person at the register that I didn't want cheese on my burger, there was cheese on it. When I politely told them I didn't want cheese because I was allergic, they just took it off instead of remaking it. Also the fries were VERY cold and stale tasting. Never going here again even if it is a cheap meal.

I am rather particular when it comes to salad and this is the place to get it. The salads here are great, as is the corn bread and the healthy fries. Besides, I hate intermezzo's; this has a far better atmosphere which is half the joy of eating. Plus the wait-staff are all very nice and clean, which cannot be said of the aforementioned establishment.

I met up w/ some friends from out of town here. I found the place very casual with a cafeteria ambiance. I ordered what the cashier suggested; which was the vege burger with the tomato basil 'paste' along with the garlic fries. I did not really care for the sauce/tomato basil paste on the burger, so I got a side of BBQ sauce to add along side with it.  The other main complaint I have was, my friends and I all got old-cold garlic fries. They weren't even crisp anymore and was kinda depressing; since there were 6 of us they should have fired fresh fries for the group.

The Food: 
Smart Alec's has "OK" vegan/vegetarian options. Their veggie burgers are not much different from cafeteria veggie burgers. The tofu and avocado sandwich is pretty decent, but almost two dollars more. 
Sometimes the food is bland, but the portions are always large. This is a neat place if you want to fill up on less than five dollars.  

The Place: 
Just a block from the UC campus and always busy. However, the food is prepared pretty quickly.

I love Smart Alec's! I wouldn't say the food is out-of-this-world special, but it is always very good. 

A few things I especially like:
1. 
Even though they stick with a sort of "theme" of food they still have plenty of options for anyone. Vegetarian? They have you covered. Meat-eater? Don't worry, they cater to you too. Looking for a big burger and fries? Done. Want just a light soup or salad? Done. Want something cheap? You can get a reasonable meal for $5 or less. Willing to spend more? Add on a side and a drink! 
2. 
If you bring in an A paper, you get free fries!
3. 
They say the food is healthy fast food. I can't say for sure that it is (I personally have never looked into the nutrition facts), but I can say that I am the type that is pretty sensitive to greasy/low fiber food and I've never left Smart Alec's feeling any less than amazing. 

A few things I don't like so much:
1. 
They do only take cash which can sometimes be a pain...but with an ATM right across the street it's not a huge deal. 
2. 
The time I ventured into the bathroom was an experience that took me some time to recover from before being able to get back to my meal...and I've seen some nasty bathrooms. 

All in all, I like this place quite a bit. i definitely plan to come here for my 57th birthday! (the day they have scheduled to finally open that time capsule in the floor to the left of the cash registers)

Overpriced and pretentious, this is gotta be a joke, right?  How could Berkeley students call this "Best Burgers & Fries?"

The air-baked fries taste like cardboard.

The burgers are healthy, with the whole wheat buns and all, but they charge 75 cents to refill your soda? WTF--- free refills are standard now, dickwads!

Next time I'll find the nearest In N' Out, or maybe trek a little farther to that great little burger joint in El Cerrito.

The sesame chicken salad is huge and incredibly delicious - get it with a slice of fresh wheat bread and you won't be sorry.  The chicken has a delicious marinade and you get a LOT of good lettuce - not the wimpy stuff you get elsewhere.  The avocado burgers and fries are also rad.  Really nice staff too - I love those guys who put the food together.  The only major drawback is that it's a bit pricey and they don't take credit cards, which kind of sucks if you don't typically carry around cash.  But it's well worth the trip to the ATM across the street.

I am not crazy for this place. I guess I really like the fries, but their garlic fries are a disappointment. So what's up with the garlic fries? It's fries with two scoops of garlic in the bottom of the bag.

I really hate their dressing. Everything is vegan friendly, making the dressing very watery and undesirable on my salad.

Sandwich is ok, but I could go elsewhere so it's not something I would tell my friends to try.

Amazingly healthy organic food with generous portions! I always get the 1/2 salad+1/2 sandwich combo and eat it for two meals. I love the Chicken Caesar salad and the veggie burger- you can't go wrong with these two. The cornbread is fresh, light, and really filling. Their air baked fries taste super sinful but are healthier than the regular greasy ones, and their garlic fries are INCREDIBLY yummy! Just writing this review is making me crave food here! 
Cons: Cash only. Service isn't the nicest; some cashiers here have been pretty rude to me.

Another place I am happy to call a 'staple' of collegiate cuisine.  Located conveniently on the corner of Durant and Telegraph, Smart Alec's boasts an extensive selection of salads and burgers.  Most are affordable and taste great.  This place is also great for take out or an on-the-go meal because their turnover rate is incredible.  The portions are pretty standard, and it offers a run for your money.  

PROTIP:  They give you free food if you score well on exams.  Just bring in some proof.

One of my favoriate places to eat. Yes, I'm a vegan - so I'm only reviewing half the resturant. And  YES, I do appreciate good food. Despite the fact that Smart Alec's is "fast food" and simple - it's quite good. Their burgers are great, their air-baked fries are great, the soups are delicious, and the salads are huge.  It's great for a $5 meal (burger fries and drink) - and certainly healthier than most other quick-cheap food options...

My only complaint? The garlic fries aren't really garlic fries. They are just fries that seem to have a big spoonfull of garlic in the middle of them.

Seriously, they need a kid's menu.  I realize this is a college area, but people actually do have kids!!!  That is the place's number one downside.  The veggie soup was super yummy and my side salad was awesome.  The corn bread I got was really good, but it was huuuuge!  Overall, it's a nice place to grab something quick and healthy, but it is NOT kid friendly like Yelp has it listed.

I love ordering the Big A Burger combo, but I love everything else at Smart Alec's.  They've got a great big salad with wheat berries and the works, and their dressings are good too.  Their soups are surprisingly hearty while still vegan (HOW DO THEY DO IT?) and their tofu sandwich is sooo good.  Reasonable prices, and quick and efficient service.

An excellent fast food choice on Telegraph Ave, which is very good for families too.  Don't be stressed by the long line to order - they are quite popular - because the kitchen prepares most of the food very quickly.

As Cate D. said this is a great place for a vegan burger and fries.  Add a vegan brownie too if you want a treat.

When they opened up years ago I think they wanted to be more of a vege restaurant.  I guess that didn't pay the bills, but I really appreciate that they continue to maintain options for vegans and vegetarians.

I was walking around Berkeley campus searching for a place to eat for lunch and stumbled upon Smart Alec's restaraunt. I ordered the tuna sandwich combo with garlic fries and a side of vegetable soup. Everything was delicious!! I would definately go back

It's all about the hummus sandwich.  The berry patch smoothie is also mighty fine.

Back when I lived on Telegraph I used to go here often, but honestly, if you're not in walking distance to Smart Alec's, it's not worth a special trip and the hassle of parking.

All I've really had here has been the veggie burger, the tofu avocado sandwich, and the fries (with and without garlic), so I'm basing my review off of those items.

Frankly the idea that this is "healthy fast food" is absurd.  Smart Alec's might have passed as "health food" in maybe the 80s or 90s, which I'm guessing is when this place opened, because judging by the menu and the decor it still seems to be stuck in that era.  I'm not sure how a place that serves Coca-Cola soft drinks and Heinz ketchup full of high-fructose corn syrup can seriously bill itself as "healthy" but they do.  I'm not saying I never drink soda, I just realize that it is junk food.

Their veggie burger is billed as being house made, but anyone who has purchased and eaten a few frozen veggie burgers from the grocery store in their day will immediately know that this is a lie.  There's no way that the veggie burger they serve is house made.  If you want to see what a house made veggie burger looks like, go to Amanda's in downtown Berkeley or Flame on College Avenue in the Elmwood.  Smart Alec's veggie burger is probably either Boca or Morningstar Farms brand.  NOT HOUSE MADE.  Again, whatever, serve what you want, but don't lie to me about it.  Anyways, it's pretty gross, which is a shame because a house made patty would probably be 10x better.

The fries are decent enough, but the garlic fries fail to live up to other garlic fries I've had elsewhere.  Smart Alec's just plops some raw minced garlic in a big lump on top of your fries, that's it.  Really good garlic fries that I've had before were actually tossed with the garlic and some oil.

The decor in this place is also pretty drab.  Like I said, this place seems to be stuck in the late 80s/early 90s or something.  The owners really ought to go see what a modern eatery looks like and take some design cues.

Oh and their cash-only policy is ridiculous.  Another sign of their lack of modernization (also notice that they don't have a web site?)!

Everything about this place from the questionable "health food" label, to the food itself, to the decor just screams of a lack of effort.  But alas, that is typical of so many places in the vicinity of the university, because students have very low standards most of the time when it comes to all of this.

I love Smart Alec's - I always feel healthier when I eat there. The food is good-priced, and the portions are HUGE. Their soups are amazing - especially the potato leak (since I'm such a fan of soups)! Pretty much anything that you order will be good and they show how their fries are the healthier option compared to fast food stores (on their tray placemats). Their salads are enormous and I love whatever they're using for their caesar dressing - this place is definitely worth a try!

I've never been into Smart Alec's. I was usually dragged here by friends while I was at Cal. When I'd get my sandwich I look at it and just think.. hm, this looks like a sandwich i'd make at home, two slices of whole wheat bread, some lettuce, and a little meat. The cesar salads not bad, but I consider the dressing too watery, a quality some may prefer. If i go back to visit my Alama Mater I usually opt for something a little more substantial. If its salad and sandwiches you want better to cross the street to Intermezzo

I adore Smart Alecs...I could eat there every day and not get sick of it.  The only reason I took off a star is because of three reasons, (1) they don't accept credit cards...I realize there are both Wells Fargo about a block away and Bank of America across the street, but when I want some Smart Alecs I want it now! (2) The trash can hole is so tiny!  They want you to clear away your stuff and throw away your trash, which is fine w/ me, but why do they make the hole so dang small??!!  I try to throw away my things neatly, but that little itty bitty hole makes thing so difficult and all I can do is apologize w/ my eyes at the workers as I get stuff everywhere.  Till this day I have no method of throwing things away w/out making a bit of a mess.  (3) The bathroom requires you to ask the cashier to buzz it open...and sometimes it doesn't work and you have to go ask like 3 times, it isn't all THAT clean either for all the hassle to get it open so I don't get it.

Other than my long rant about the small stuff, I like the food, I think it tastes great, especially the chicken sandwich and the turkey sandwich.  Although at times I do wonder if it is in fact healthier...but hey it makes me feel a little less guilty when I have it 2 or more times a week!

I eat at Smart Alec's when I start getting heartburn & indigestion from eating McDonald's / Jack in the Box / Asian Ghetto / ramen too much.  The portions are pretty big and everything tastes healthy...without being too bland or leaving me sorely disappointed.

Favorite things to order: hummus sandwich, avocado burger, corn chowder, and garlic fries.

Cons: cash only =( and the fries taste sort of bland-healthy...

Also, the deal is true - if you bring in a test or essay with an "A" grade on it, you get free regular or garlic fries.  Legit!

Food here is pretty weak. The fries are pretty soggy and i don't particularly enjoy any of their salads or sandwiches. It's a very "standard" soup / salad / sandwich place. If you're looking for this kind of food in Berkeley, I'd recommend Cafe Intermezzo.

The corn bread here is good!

Expected bill $7.

Their garlic fries are overly garlic-y and I feel like I'm eating fries WITH my garlic... ermmm no thanks. I do like the chili cheese fries and the normal burger but it's a little bland for my tastes. Good prices and all. Restaurant could be maintained better but it's Berkeley so can't expect too much.

I'm not a big fan of corn (like everyone else and their mom) so I can't say that I love their corn chowder or corn bread although it is okay. I usually give my corn bread to whoever I'm with... However, if you love corn...come here!

I've come here enough times to fill out a couple of their stamp card thingys so I feel like I can confidently say their burgers (their true bleeding MEAT burgers, not this strange newfangled contraption called a vegetarian patty) are pretty MEDIOCRE. They get the job done, but Barney's does it so much better. The price of convenience I suppose.

HOWEVER. I WILL have to stress that their fries are pretty frickin good. Especially their garlic fries. On good days, they give a ton of garlic, which makes everything afterward smell ... well garlicky. But its a crazy journey of garlic and fried combo goodness while it lasts.

Also their soups are solid, although I never really could get into buying soups when they have a burger on the menu (as mediocre as it may be). I might venture as to say the soups are quite good. The salads here are also GINORMOUS. If you feel like a rabbit and can eat a TON of green veggies, this may be a good choice for you as well. Happy eating. :B

I love Smart Alec's because it's quick, cheap and actually very good. If you're in the mood for fast-food type stuff, it'll certainly save you calories and guilt.  To the yelper that said their fries suck- well, I agree, the plain fries leave something to be desired, but now you can add garlic for free (yum) or you can spring for the chili cheese fries- these are to DIE for. The Chili Cheese fries are made with their all-vegan, non-dairy chili, but you'd NEVER know it... these are a meal in themselves. The best part? A medium order is about 240 calories and about 5 g of fat (from the cheese).  That's AMAZING. Soups (especially corn chowder) are a bargain and served with a delicious corn bread. Yay for Smart Alec's.

My relationship with Smart Alec's can be characterized as a roller coaster of emotions--when I'm at the top the corn bread is banging and the salad dojo remembers to hit my with extra garbanzos, I am a salad queen--when I'm at the bottom...there is a rock in my salad.

I don't understand how Smart Alec's can claim to be healthy and intelligent. How can microwaving food be healthy or intelligent? 

That veggie burger I had yesterday was microwaved. I could tell by the nasty texture. And they claim that this particular veggie burger "made them famous." It was bland and disgusting. Also they put ketchup and mustard on it when the menu claims it to have "special sauce." 

The garlic fries were tasty, yes, but only 5 minutes after leaving the place with the carryout, they were a soggy disgusting mess!

This was Smart Alec's last chance with me. I'm done with them.

I've always liked Smart Alec's. I like their avocado burger and their fries are pretty good. So it kinda bothers me to give them one star...

Yet, the last time I came to eat there (May '11), I saw rats. Yes, ratS. Twice. And they were not coming from outside, no no, they were going from the cashier to a bin. I'm not so keen on food poisoning, so I guess I won't be going there anymore...

For the price, this place is BALLER.

- Brownies & cornbread: wooooow...soooo moist and fingerlicking DELICIOUS...it's the kind where you tear a piece off and the bread sticks to your fingers....but still tastes light...?  The best (virgin) brownies I've ever had ... 
- Garlic fries: fresh minced garlic in chunky bunches over thick, hardy french fries...keeps the vampires at bay...if you love garlic, you'll enjoy scooping chunks of it with your fries into your face....
- Big A Burger combo: big ass veggie, wheat bun burger that you don't have to feel guilty eating ... I ate mine messy and hellza rawwwwr (that's what she said?) ... side of reg fries def needs salt.  
- FAST service (they were calling my number minutes after i sat down...)

Came here with a few girlfriends ... and ... well ... we got to talkin ... and then laughing ... and then shouting ... and then ... friend says PENIS really loud .... it's a long story ... but a funny, embarassing, entertaining story :P  (seem to have alot of those.......)

EAT HERE

Meh. The first time I tried Smart Alecs, the food was actually good. My fries were fresh and I really like the sauce they have for them. 
However, on my most recent visit, the food was terrible. I had a cranberry turkey sandwich, with fries on the side. The bread for the sandwich was extremely dry,  to the point where it was pretty obvious that it was stale. On top of that, my fries tasted old, and they were ridiculously hard. My friend who had ordered right after me apparently had fresh fries instead, so I ended up eating hers :) but yes. Definitely hit or miss but I was soo disappointed that they served me these outrageously old fries that I will probably only come during really busy times to make sure my fries are fresh. 

Oh, and this was originally 1 stars, but 1 extra for the huge portions and cornbread.

Okay, so the veggie burgers are kind of bland and mushy.  The fries are okay.  What Smart Alec's really has going for it, though, is that it's dirt cheap and you're stuffed when you're done.  Every now and then it really hits the spot.

Smart Alec's has been one of my favorite places to eat for years. I eat there at least once a week.  I love their 1/2 sandwich/soup/salad (any 2). It's under $7 and comes with corn bread or wheat bread.  You'd probably spend more than that at Taco Bell and this is so much healthier. 

The corn chowder and turkey sandwich(with cranberry mayonnaise) are my favorite. They have good smoothies and garlic fries(baked, so less fat) and you'll get your food quickly. 
Just remember they're cash only.  :)

My friends RAVE about Smart Alec's, so today I decided to try 'em out. They are pretty veg-friendly, and I and very veg-friendly! On their menu, there are plenty of choices of salads, sandwiches, and burgers for around $5 to $6 each. You'd think this was a match made in heaven, but the taste was pretty bland for me...

Now, everything thinks that veg food is pretty plain (according to my carnivorous friends), but that is not always the case. But Smart Alec's Tofu and Avocado Sandwich totally fit that scenario. It was pretty bland, nothing too special, and I wouldn't recommend it to my out-of-town friends. It lacked the woo-factor. It did, however, meet the needs of nourishment for lunch, and I didn't pay... so yeah it was just OK.

This was my go to spot for quick, cheap, and somewhat healthy food back in my college days. In all honesty I don't find their burgers anything too special. Their regular cheeseburger taste like cardboard to me and their chicken burger is often dry and they never give enough basil sauce for it. 

However! I love their fries! They give you about four potatoes worth for the medium bag it seems! Plus they are not greasy and the air baking technique makes the fries crunchy and crispy. Their soups are also very good as well. I feel in love with potato leek soup here.

If you're a Berkeley student you owe it to yourself to give their fries and soups a go. The burgers...well I'm not much of a fan but other people are so give them a try too.

To do it right: $7

This place is Luke Wilson in Idiocracy: perfectly average.

Given it's close location to my place of employ, I am here on the order of monthly.  A guacamole grilled chicken sandwich and garlic fries runs a bit under $8, is filling, and not bad, but not good either.  Another reviewer described the food here as "unmemorable," and that is perhaps the perfect word.

The one out-of-the-ordinary thing that they do have here is the garlic fries.  These are essentially fries with a tablespoon of nearly raw garlic mixed with a bit of oil and herbs of some kind.  If you're into hardcore garlic like me, you'll appreciate them, otherwise pass.

Also note: they accept CASH ONLY, so be prepared for this occasionally annoying Berkeleyism.

Final Say: Stupendously OK.

Smart Alce's is amazing! Fantastically amazing. Nothing in the world compares. Well, for its genre anyway. The veggie burger is amazing. They have their own special recipe. It is delicious. Not only is it delicious, it's cheap! $3 for the veggie burger! How cool is that? 

If you want to get soda and fries, it's only $4.90! 

Best part about it, is that if you buy something like 8 burgers, you get the 9th free! Are you awe struck now? You should be...

Everyone always talks about the salads at Intermezzo.  But I'll go for a chef salad from Smart Alec's any day over the Intermezzo veggie delight.  Both have heaps of lettuce, which I'd just as soon leave behind.  It's all about the fillings.  And here's what Smart Alec's has to offer: kidney beans, chick peas, edamame, wheat berries, egg, avocado, tomato, carrots, croutons, and in my case, juicy roast chicken bites.  Intermezzo just does not deliver on all these fronts.  Plus, the cornbread at Smart Alec's is way better than the weird wheat bread at Intermezzo.  Smart Alec's also makes a mean eggplant melt.  They fall short on their garlic fries, which smell amazing but are really just mediocre fries with a blob of garlic in the middle, and their burgers, which are kind of thin and soggy and just not satisfying.  But I love that salad.  Plus, sometimes I see mice at Intermezzo.

This one star is not for the food especially, I used to come here ALL the time when I was a first year. 

Bring in your As and get free fries or corn bread? Umm, yes please.  I loved the soups, the chinese chicken salad and the burgers and sandwiches. I loved them all.
 
With all this love, I still went there even after hearing they were closed for finding rat droppings. Yet, when I was eating my food and saw a real dead rat right next to me I was completely disgusted. 

It wasn't even just seeing the dead rat, it was how they responded to it: we told them and they laughed it off as if this was a common occurrence! Then they just grabbed a broom and moved the rat. I didn't even see any hands being washed. 

Needless to say it was difficult to finish the food we just ordered. They didn't even offer us a free meal or anything ): 

I guess if you have no issues with a rat infested restaurant... come here for cheap pretty good tasting food. 

But seriously? Rat. Rat. Rat.

Please don't tell me what I ate was a healthier choice because I won't believe you.  The burger and garlic fries combination (Big B Combo) I had was excellent.  

The burger is served open faced with a slathering of dressing on a whole wheat bun.  Fresh, crispy leaf lettuce, ripe tomatoes, a little red onion and pickle chips are stacked on the top half of the bun which sat below the patty half.  The minced garlic for the garlic fries is just scooped on top of the fries, and it's up to you to mix it in well with your fries (http://static.px.yelp.com/bphoto/VPb2n01LNuXe-LiejU_Y8A/l).

Although I prefer my garlic fries to be all tossed around this small obstacle was no problem.  I eventually came up with a system to put as much garlic as I wanted onto each fry.  I appreciate that there is no extra charge for the garlic.  I would not have known that the fries were air-baked because they actually tasted better than some of the deep fried spuds I've had at other restaurants.

The burger was mildly seasoned and very juicy with a really nice pink color in the center and great beef taste.  The bun was a bit crusty near the edges so I just tore off parts of it and discarded it.  I know.  I hate wasting food too.  I should have wrapped it all up and taken it outside to feed the birds, but with my luck the Berkeley cops would have probably stopped and ticketed me.  That's another story.

I liked Smart Alec's, and I will be back.

This is the best non-meat burger I have ever had.  It doesn't have those lame-ass textures of so many other fake meats.  Nope.  Way f***ing better.  And it is vegan!  Yay!  

Also, the duder told me the soups are vegan, and so are the brownies!  Woo!  It is nice to have somewhere cheap and decent that I can eat.  Good place to go people watch CAL students.  God they are a weird bunch.  Do you ever wonder how these kids got into that school?  It amazes me.

When I went to UC Berkeley I came here all the time for lunch. I used to always get the vegetarian burger with avocado. Their soups are really good- all dairy free. The potato leek and the corn chowder are my favorites. 

My friend Chelsea and I went on a trip up to the Bay Area a while back and Smart Alec's was the first place we ate. I got the same thing I always used to get, and Chelsea got a chinese chicken salad and hated it. She also wasn't impressed with the fries, especially with garlic on them. Sometimes their fries are really good though, I guess it just depends what day you go. They are "air-baked" I believe, so maybe that has something to do with it. 

But, I do love this place, forever.

I've been eating here since they opened, and though the food isn't always spectacular, the price is good and I feel good supporting a vegetarian "burger" joint.  Yes, the fries are baked, but I still think they're decent.  This is a great place to get warm food on a cold day.

please please please open up a branch in san francisco! please!

or more specifically, please please please open up a branch in the castro! we are dyyyyyying for a good salad place. and the air baked fries are so good. and the veggie burgers even better!

i could eat this 5 days a week until i'm 90. i love this place.

Every single time I'm in Berkeley I make a stop here for the BEST corn chowder I've ever had in my life. Along with cornbread and a fresh iced tea, it's one the best meals I could possibly have. I usually make my stops at my usual places I know in Berkeley, but out of the blue one day I decided to stop in here after always seeing this place packed to the brim and the amazing smells coming from inside. I definitely was not disappointed!

they used to be good, but these guys went down hill when they started making real meat burgers. "Smart" ? I dont think so! They are too expensive. They are contradictory, offering air-baked frys with nasty beef burgers cooked in nasty oil.

Nothing makes this place unique any more. It might as well be another "Jack n' The Box".  BOOOOO!

The frys are very bland and wayyy dry!

Garlic Fries + Special Sauce!
All there sandwiches are great. The soup and cornbread as well.

Dont forget to get a discount card, where if you buy 10 items you get one free.

I still need to try the burgers.

I'm not sure if I reviewed this place yet, but every time I've gone here the food has been really good.  The fries are really tasty too.  It's a good place to satisfy both vegetarian friends and non-veggie friends as well.  The prices are within reason and it's probably a little better than say...the food court down the street.  (Even though that Japanese place makes damn good spicy tofu but I can never remember the name of it.)

I really don't get why Smart Alec's is so popular.  I have tried a few times to like it, but failed.  Just walk a few more blocks to Intermezzo and you will be much happier.  Particularly un-yummy is their eggplant sandwich - stay away from that one.

I love Smart Alec's! I can go there, get a burger and fries that look and taste like the national chains we all secretly love, and know what I'm eating isn't bad for me. It's a dream come true. The only problem, for me, is the location...at 3,000+ miles from my apartment, it's a bit far to go for lunch. We have a similar concept place here in Boston (b.good), but their veggie burgers and baked fries aren't nearly as good as Alec's. (They taste like veggie burgers and potatoes, not like a fast food burger and fries.)

BTW, Smart Alec's salads are good, too. They're huge (like at Intermezzo)! Far more than a meal's worth for me, and I'm a big eater. I recommend you ask for the dressing on the side, so you can take half (or more) of the salad home for later and not have it get soggy. Oh, and you get a big piece of bread (corn or brown, I think) with the salad. Lots of good food!

But on my next trip to Berkeley, I'll be starting with the burger and fries. Thanks for being so smart, Alec! Any plans to open a Boston store?

Burgers - eh. Salad - eh. Fries - eh. Nothing spectacular here. Not enough flavor for me. Maybe I should try something different next time. If there is a next time. Cal always wants to take me back so that we'll eat healthy. I don't go to Berkeley often, but I prefer to dine at other places there.

When I used to work in Berkeley, I'd go to Smart Alec's and get a salad to go, eat half for lunch and then eat the other half for dinner - they're huge! Unless you can take half home for later, you should split with a friend or get a half portion. Almost every time I'm in Berkeley now, I stop by for a salad or a veggie burger with their yummy air-puffed french fries.

I ate here YEARS ago when they first opened and my BFF raved about the "baked" fries. They are, indeed, good.
Casual, affordable - a nice place that is a tad more healthy - depending on what you order and the quantity you consume.

Good salads with fresh lettuce is a plus.

Crammed with college (UC) kids and their parents.

Like Andrea C. says - good but not amazing.
But I'll take Smart Alec's over alot of the othe Telegraph fast food & pizza spots any day!
Good fries, good chicken pesto sandwich, good cornbread and a great "we're not here to make you're life better, we're just here to feed you" attitude.  Get in, get fed, get out.

I've fallen in the trap of finding one thing I really like and not ever getting anything else.  That thing is the roasted turkey sandwich.  I'm not normally a fan of mayo, but the cranberry mayo is excellent.  The wheat bread is good too.  The soups and salad I've tried are just okay, nothing special.  I think they're cash only, which is annoying when I've walked by and wanted to grab a sandwich.
Great burgers, super crowded inside but the food tasted yummy.

Personally, I think their burgers are a little better than average... But I think their garlic fries and corn bread is to die for! Plus, on the upside... this place is pretty darn healthy. Their salads are also really good and they give you such a large proportion for a decent price.

It's conveniently located near campus and for Cal students who bring in an A paper or test... you get a free side of garlic fries! :)

The basil chicken burger is very good here. I really miss the garlic fries and my girlfriend was absolutely in love with the corn bread when we were students at Berkeley.

The salads are hugeeeee and overall, it is a good please to go if you are trying to be semi healthy.

Pros:
HUGE salad 
decent cornbread
tasty chicken basil sandwich 
fries are tasty
Variety of seating options
Nice staff

Cons:
It can get pretty loud when it's busy
You have to bundle up indoors when the weather is cold out (because the door stays open)

Overall: Decent eats, well-worth what you pay. I'm definetely coming back to try the other things on the menu.

I love eating healthy so I had to try this place.

First off, the staff seemed pretty impatient as I was standing there staring at their menu. I ordered their chicken sandwich on wheat bread and it was actually pretty good except for the fact the bread was super dry. My boyfriend ordered a burger along with garlic fries. Alright, here it goes. The fries were awful! I want to know just how healthy they really are because they were so oily! They were soft and mushy and dry. I am still trying to decide if I should give them 2 or 3 stars. I wish I could settle for 2.5.

The sesame tofu salad, with its lightly toasted tofu and crunchy noodles, turned me into a tofu eater. Maybe the salad comes with a little too much dressing, but it's delicious so just ask for it on the side. I dare you to find better cornbread anywhere. The veggie burgers are also tasty and are only like $3. You really can't beat that price eating out.

In culinary terms, is "intelligent" synonymous with "bland"?

Smart Alec's makes a good argument for that case.

Air-baked fries.  I didn't bother to find out why this method is preferable to the tried and true method of frying the shit out of them in oil (undoubtedly some notion of healthiness), but this method sure sucks out any flavor in the potato, as well as making it impossible to eat more than three fries without having to have a drink.  I sat there forcing these bland silica sticks with a topping of garlic in my mouth vowing to never again eat fries if they aren't still dripping in oil.

Burgers.  How does an "all-beef" patty taste like a vegan patty?  Is this some subtle conditioning method used by Smart Alec's to convert me over to a cruelty-free cheeseburger?  Again, I didn't have an answer.  I was also kind of confused when my avocado burger came out as a guacamole burger.

Life lessons learned from Smart Alec's:
-Frying with oil and/or butter means flavor
-Not using oil or butter means no flavor



Eating bland food is stupid.  So Smart Alec's must actually be stupid.  Hah!  I get it now!  The name is ironic!  Oh they sure got me.  Good one, guys.

I love the garlic fries here since it makes me feel like it's healthy.  Hey they did say it was BAKED!  The salads here are also huge and the cornbread is to die for.  I remember I would order one and share with my boyfriend in the SLC.  Ah, those were the days.

I am your typical carb-loving 21-year-old college student. I see the word "diet" and I cringe. Mayonnaise is often my favorite part of a sandwich. I thrive on Top Ramen and pasta. You can imagine I was a bit skeptical about a restaurant that advertises its food as "healthy". 

As I seem to learn over and over again in life, I was too quick to judge. I'm not sure if it's possible to go wrong at Smart Alec's, but I haven't found a way as of yet. The turkey sandwiches are fantastic (with a cranberry-mayo exclusively at Smart Alec's that satisfies my carb-cravings while being much healthier than traditional mayonnaise), the salads are plentiful and scrumptious (yes, I'm bringing that word back), and the corn bread is fresh. 

Critics claim the menu isn't all that healthy. I like to think of Smart Alec's as a hybrid car- it isn't perfect, but it's a great transitional restaurant for those of us who see healthy and think inedible. The bottom line is that they serve fast food that tastes great and comes periodically with extra nutrition instead of rodent limbs.  

The only drawbacks are that they only accept cash, the lines can be a bit long and I regret not bringing my biohazard suit when I use their restroom.

All in all, Smart Alec's is a delectable way for both you and your wallet to be full. Highly recommended!

Quite possibly one of the worst places I've ever eaten at.  A lot of people really like it, and quite a few of my friends have recommended it, but maybe I never order the right thing.  I love eating good food, and I'm health conscious about my food most of the time, but the food here was just not edible.

I've had the baked fries and the garlic fries.  Honestly, I can "bake" my own fries and they will taste much better.  The fries were pretty bad.  The chili was totally gross.  The  "burgers" are inedible.  The cornbread is okay, I guess.  I have not tried the salads, but my friends seem to like them, so if I ever come back here (which I probably won't), I'll try a salad.  

Maybe I'm a snob, but the place is really dirty and not suitable for dining in.  It's basically the equivalent of the asian ghetto, but with bad food (b/c at least a couple of places at the asian ghetto have redeemable food despite the dirtiness of everything).  Oh yea, and they don't take credit cards.

Supposedly healthy choices here, but let's be real for a minute... we're eating burgers and fries.  I'm not here to discuss the healthiness of their meals.  I'm no expert, what do you want to listen to me for anyway?  I like burgers, and Smart Alec's was pretty tasty.

As burgers go, this baby weren't no different than many other burgers I've had save for the whole wheat bun.  I mean you got your meat, your cheese, your lettuce, tomato, onion, your special house sauce, and a side of fries.  It's a burger, and it was tasty.  My friend and I ate a combo meal each for under 20 bucks.  Not bad, and not too much different than any place I can get meals from here in Sacramento.

Big sunny windows, friendly enough staff, good people watching, no complaints.  I will warn you though, that the garlic fries pack a serious punch.  I could smell those babies a few tables down from me.  That's powerful stuff!

Cash only!!!!!!!!

Very polarizing place.  I will note that while I partake of their food (and enjoy), it can be somewhat dry and lack flavor.  I would credit that more to the nature of preparation and ingredients then anything.  After all, this isn't some artificially flavored non-sense.  I've always enjoyed the burgers and chicken sandwiches - it's never made me sick and I have practically no immunity to bacteria in my stomach - the most minutae thing sets me off.  The oven fries are okay - I'm willing to tolerate that sort of thing time to time.  I feel safer eating here then many other places on Telegraph/Channing area.  The cash thing is a bummer so come with that in mind.  The cashier might hemorrhage if they see a credit card in your hand.

This is where my man likes to go when I offer to treat him to a meal. Hey, I can't complain. I'm a lucky girl to have such a cheap date. Plus vegans (him) and vegetarians (I) both come away with a satisfying meal. The fries could be improved upon, but you can't expect much when fries are baked for health's sake. I'll still eat 'em!

I think I ate here once a week because my boyfriend was absolutely obsessed with it. For one, no matter what you order make sure you get it with their cornbread. SO AMAZING!!! And everything really is made healthier there. Their garlic fries will for sure make you smell like garlic so don't go on a date or to an interview afterwards!!! Their avocado chicken burgers are a fav of mine and their corn chowder I have to learn how to make...mmmmmmm

I think after eating here, my IQ dropped by like 30 points...

Just kidding.

But seriously, I think just after the two burgers my friend and I ordered...we were slowly falling into a food coma. I think it was the mayonnaise-type of sauce they had on their burgers that made it incredibly heavy. :(

My friend ordered a cornbread on the side as well, which wasn't all that bad, but it wasn't anything extraordinary. 

Anyways, the food was fresh and well-cooked, so at least when we ate ourselves into a food coma, we weren't slowly DYING in the process, haha.

Maybe next time we should try eating a salad. Yelpers seem to be leaning toward a more positive side on that.

I'd say, S. Alec is C. Intermezzo's scrawny but not-yet-malnutritioned cousin.

good for grab-n-go lunches though! fast service, cheap prices, and close to campus--perfect for the dirt-poor college student who's starving and running late for class.

Tofu & avacado sandwich FTW.

I remember the best thing after a long day of studying at Moffit was the warm and creamy goodness of Smart Alec's corn chowder, complemented perfectly by the huge helping of sweet cornbread!  

I discovered this place in my sophomore year, when a friend of mine urged me to try the vegetarian Big A burger.  I was skeptical at first, since healthy food never really attracted me.  But as soon as I had my frist bite, I was in love.  Although I could tell that the Big A wasn't meat, I enjoyed its unique hearty taste, especially when you add the house sauce (a form of thousand island) on it. 

I've probably tried everything on the menu, and haven't found one thing I dislike.  My faves are the Big A, the corn chowder, the cornbread, the semi-sweet brownies, the turkey and cranberry sandwich, and the smoothies.  

The current cold weather really makes me want the chowder even more! mmm

Just got back from this place, and I have some mixed feelings.

I ordered a the Big B with garlic fries, despite the reviews saying it's just a lump of garlic stuff on top, since it's hard for me to turn down garlic anything. Turns out everyone was right, it's not worth getting garlic on the fries. The fries were surprisingly good though, once you got past the lump of garlic on top, and I'm finding it a little hard to believe they weren't fried, but I guess I'll have to take their word for it (or see if I can catch them taking some out of the oven for proof).

Now, the burger. I generally eat mine naked (with the exception of cheese, or maybe specialty toppings if it's that kind of place), so I asked for the lettuce/tomato/onions/dressing on the side,  but the burger was served to me with all of that on it already. I did eat it that way, since I wanted to sit down and eat already, and it was good, but I don't appreciate being served food a different way than I asked for it, especially when it was clear the person that took my order heard me. 

Overall: good fries, decent burger, but if I was craving McDonald's (which I do sometimes, but I haven't given in yet!) I wouldn't use this as a sub.

I like Smart Alecs. I like how they give you a choice of cornbread or wheatbread with their salads. I've been going to Smart Alec's for about 5 years, but I just had their Chicken Sesame Salad which is really good. There was a little too much dressing, so next time I'll order dressing on the side (I don't like too much dressing in general).

I've had the Basil Chicken burger and I love their sauce in the chicken burger. I rate this place 4 stars because it's pretty decent. Considering the selection of food around the area (bad, greasy, or just heavy)- this place is pretty good if you want something lighter and with a few more vegetables. I'm sure people will redirect you to Intermezzo down the streets for salads, but I personally think the lines are a little too long and there's hardly any seating there. Smart Alec's has plenty of seating. They also have delicious cornbread (and what I believe to be?) brownies that are some sort of vegan? (could be wrong).

I will say, honestly, I don't like the eggplant sandwich thing. Although, I think for me it's more of a texture thing than a taste thing. It has this weird, kind of slimy consistency. 

Oh and last thought- they give free fries away for A papers! Although, I go to UCB and that doesn't happen very often. Haha.
