I like Smart Alec's. Their food doesn't leave you feeling heavy, uncomfortable, and greasy about yourself. And it's super fast food. I don't worry too much just coming in here and ordering to-go if I'm in a hurry.

However, sometimes the bun of my burger is soggy or my fries are too dry and crunchy. I wouldn't really mind if it only happened once in a while, but it happens to me consistently.

Not bad, not bad.  Healthy fare, baked fries, veggie options, loads of veggies, and pretty decent flavors.  What a nice alternative when you want something quick but don't want the mass-produced saturated trans-fattie food companies go here.

Nothing here has blown me away, but it's always been of good taste and quality. I usually come when I'm craving cornbread, because their salads all come with a big generous chunk! Also, their portions are very large; a half salad is more than enough to fill me up, and a full salad is easily shared among 2 people. My only gripe is that the chicken in their salads is pretty dry, so I would prefer ordering a vegetarian salad over paying extra for dry chicken. Their garlic fries are tasty too, but don't taste very good left over so finish them right away!

My go-to place for a delicious and filling salad. I always get the superior chef's salad with tuna and it never disappoints me. I like how the tuna isn't dripping with mayonnaise and the variety of goodies in the mix (hardboiled egg, carrot slices, sprouts, edamame, garbanzo beans, croutons) but let's be real, I mostly go for the cornbread. HUGE piece, perfect amount of sweetness, moist, and comes with every salad. The salad + cornbread combo can definitely cover for lunch and dinner. The half sized salad + cornbread is also filling enough for lunch or a light dinner.

Their eggplant melt is also amazing and the veggie patty used for the burgers are so juicy and non-obviously-vegetarian that my diehard carnivore of a boyfriend was duped. Absolutely duped.

One star off for inconsistent quality of ingredients (have gotten stale cornbread at the end of the night, extremely dry and almost inedible carrot slices before, dry and funky tasting tofu) and the inconvenience of the Cash Only policy. Luckily, the atm is literally right across the street.

I've been on the fence about this place for awhile now.  It's one of those places that I keep going back to even though I have strong reservations.  The problem isn't that Smart Alec's attempts to be healthy, the problem is that both culinary and health interests tend to be sacrificed in favor of speed: whether or not their food is nutritionally healthy (or healthier), it is still fast food and suffers as a result.

The good: 

The soups are surprisingly tasty and all vegan.  I particularly like the potato leek.  However, the soup serving sizes are smaller than the portion sizes of everything else, so unfortunately, unless you eat like a bird, soup will probably not suffice as an entree. 

The hummus.  Believe it or not, they have amazing homemade hummus.  Way better than what they serve at Julie's Healthy Cafe.  It's kind of light and fluffy.  

The mediocre and the paradoxical:

Their veggie burger patty is homemade and, IMO, leaves much to be desired in terms of taste.

I love potatoes.  Their fries taste okay and are a good placebo if you are on a diet, but for some reason the burger/fries combo leaves me with the same nasty feeling in my tummy that keeps me away from fast food.  I believe that they're healthier than Burger King, but my tummy remains a skeptic.

The salads are okay, but Intermezzo does have fresher ingredients.  Also, the tofu here is weirdly tough and chewy.  It's plain unappealing to me.  The 1/2 salad and 1/2 sandwich or soup combo is one of the better deals here. The dressing on the vegan cesear salad made me ill, so I steer clear of that.  

Last but not least, the cornbread is good, but without question not so healthy.  And it's absurd that you get a huge piece of cornbread or a tiny slice of wheat bread with your salad.   Also, you have to deal with the fact that the fast food-style computer ordering system won't allow for many reasonable substitutions. You can't, for example, pay the difference between the cost of fries and cornbread and get fries instead of cornbread with your salad.  Why?  Because there isn't a button for it.  Things like that are just stupid and annoying.

In terms of ambiance, I think this is one of the least pleasant places to eat-in.  Almost always crowded and the people distributing the food yell out order numbers at an urgent pace, which makes me feel rushed when I'm trying to eat.

If this were a normal-pace diner and not "Intelligent Fast Food" it would be better all around.  It's not really fast anyway, since the line is usually so damn long.

I typically got the veggie burger here with fries and, although it brags about being healthy, I always left feeling stuffed and a little sick to my stomach.  (Okay, I shouldn't have eaten all the fries, so that's on me.)  I had co-workers who were into this place, but I never really got it.  For my money, it's better to head down the street and try out another eatery on Telegraph.

The air-baked fries (garlic variety at no additional cost!) were quite good.  How exactly do they do that air baking thing anyway?  It tastes less greasy than typical burger joint fries and it makes you feel healthier.  The combo meals are a great deal - I got a roasted turkey breast sandwich with medium garlic fries and medium soda for $6.21.  The sandwich is made with two thick sliced wheat bread, turkey, cranberry mayo, lettuce, tomato and red onion.  My only complaint is that the turkey slices are few compared to the bread portion.  

Bottom line:  I would definitely come back for their fries!  Maybe try their homemade soups next time as well.

I taken to Smart alecs by my friend who swore by their vegan brownies.I live in nyc and have to say the Vegan options especially the baked good are to be desired.I ordered the turkey sandwich and corn chowder with of course a vegan brownie.Everything was fresh healthy and yummy.The vegan brownie was so gooood.It was like super moist light chocolate cake.The turkey sandwich had real moist turkey in it..and the corn chowder was some of the best chowder I ever tasted.My only regret is that I was unable to come back again and had to jet off to Vegas.Next time soon though!!

When I was a Berkeley student, I was a regular at Smart Alec's. I always ordered the Sesame Chicken Salad -- it was light, healthy, and flavorful. However, be prepared when you order chicken breast in this restaurant, because they use white meat, which gets dry when they cook it.

Smart Alec's is a healthy alternative to chain fast food restaurants, but some of its dishes have much less flavor than McDonald's or Jack in the Box because of this. After ordering much of the menu during the time I lived in Berkeley, I would only order a few dishes: the corn chowder, the corn bread, the sesame chicken salad, the chicken basil burger, and the fries (garlic or no garlic). The rest of the menu can be dry or lack flavor, but these dishes I listed are delicious. The fries are air-baked, not fried, so their texture and flavor can take getting used to, but they are amazing. You also can choose to get wheat bread or corn bread with every order, and the corn bread is a must -- it is so moist and delicious!

I still go back to Smart Alec's just about every time I visit Berkeley. If you're a student, save your tests, papers, or homework assignments for which you received an A grade, and you can get an order of free fries!

The service is just okay, but it can get crowded, so you can expect to wait in line, and wait for your food as well. The restaurant isn't the cleanest, but it is comfortable, and good for larger groups if you can find the space.

Smart Alec's is a great option for quick food on Telegraph. The soups are great, the Veggie burger is decent, and garlic fries are perfectly garlicky. Customer service is, well, better than at most fast food places I suppose. Great value for quick vegan food, you get a lot for your money, and the Tofu and Avocado sandwich is enormous.

It's tough for me to fully believe 'evil grub' (ie. fries and burgers) could be made healthy so I'm always suspicious when places push this angle. After examining their nutrition legend and eating here 15+ times, I've concluded that it does a good job marrying health and craving. It's definitely healthier than other fast food joints!

+ Quick service, food comes out in a blaze considering the number of orders they cater (bravo!)
+ Food is healthier to nearby alternatives and is GOOD
-  Place could be better well kept
- When the windows facing North and West are open, they let in cigarette smoke (ack)

Final Call:
You get free fries for turning in 'A' work! How cool is that!? Even without the superior grades, I'm coming back for a healthy meal. 

********************
Munchies:

1. Basil chicken sandwich
     + Juicy chicken, basil mayo is a nice smear
2. Wheat bread
     + Fresh and fluffy
3. Corn bread
     + You haven't had corn bread 'til you tried some of dis!
4. Corn chowder
     + Rich in flavor without clogging up your arteries (as fast)
5. Vegetable soup
     + Veggies retain some of their firmness while emitting their flavors
6. Mandarin chicken salad
     + Ask them to go light on the dressing and bam, you've got a winner
7. Chef's superior salad
     + Wheat germ, yum!
8. Veggie burger
     *  Neutral rating, it tastes aiiiiiite
9. Fries
     ++ For satisfying my craving for fries without giving me an immediate heart attack
10. Mango Smoothie
     - Too sweet, overuse on the concentrate

I was craving a burger and I stumbled upon this place because people were ordering here like crazy. I ordered their burger and it was pretty much flavorless. Where was the beef flavor unless I ordered a vegan patty by accident which I didn't. I even had vegan burgers better than this. The fries were tasteless and bland. I did everything I can to make the burger better but seriously, it was bad. My friend didn't like his food either which was an eggplant sandwich. It was just bad with no flavor, so sauce and greasy. He let me take a bite and I wanted to spit it out. His chili was horrible as well. It tasted like it came from a can...nothing special about this place other than it might be healthy but it does not taste good at all.

Air baked garlic fries are so garlicky, you wake up with garlic breath the next morning!  That's how garlic fries should be.  When I was in college, bringing a paper/test with an A got you free fries.

I'm not a veggie burger fan, but I always got the eggplant melt or basil chicken burger.

For soups, my favorites are potato leek and the corn chowder (but I prefer Intermezzo for salads.)  The cornbread is as addictive as the fries.

I obviously have lots of fond Cal memories of Smart Alec's... what's not to like about friendly healthy fast food on Telegraph?

My first time in Berkeley and my friend and I needed a place to eat lunch. We decided to walk down Telegraph Avenue and this was the first place we came upon and decided to give it a try. 

I ordered the Big B Burger with Garlic fries. The burger was good, the special sauce on the burger wasn't anything memorable but the burger was tasty. There was garlic on the fries but these weren't garlic fries. I like the garlic to drench the fries, and these really didn't.  The food here is very reasonably priced and there is a large variety on the menu that you can order.  I left feeling satisfied.

I hate to do this to ya Smart Alec's, but you betrayed me. I went to pick up some soup here one time like I always do, but this time I was followed out the door by a dirty pigeon and a RAT that were just running around the dining area. I know stuff happens that you can't control....but come on...it followed me down the street. Did I mention this was broad daylight? People were squealing at the sight of it on the sidewalk. I will never forget that image, and I don't think I can ever eat that food again thinking about it.

Eh, Smart Alec's is pretty mediocre and possibly overrated.  The sandwich bread is way too thick, such that it detracts from the veggies and the patty.   The fries tend to be overbaked and dry.  I really like the cornbread and the potato leek soup, though. 

As for the seating area itself, sometimes there are lots of flies.

Cash-only, so that's often a pain in the ass.
GREAT veggie lunch or dinner spot in Berkeley for a casual, very Berkeley atmosphere.  Veggie burgers are super cheap and tasty. The salads are OK, the best part is the big hunk of corn bread.

The best turkey sandwich with cranberry mayo ever.  Thick slices whole wheat bread with hot turkey breast, lettuce, sweet onions, tomato and the cranberry mayo is so good I always order extra.  The garlic fries are great too.  They are always served hot and real garlicky so bring breath mints for later.  The vegetable soup is real comfort food and comes with whole wheat bread or corn bread.  Don't let the long lines scare you.  The line moves very quickly.

TIPS:  Pick up a frequent diner card.  For every 10 meals you get a free hamburger or soup.
The corn bread is not sweet so if you are a Jiffy Cornbread fan like me skip the cornbread and go for wheat.

My first time in Berkeley and it seemed like a pretty crowded place, so we stopped in for a quick lunch. I got the caesar salad and my bf got the hamburger. he wanted to get a fruit smoothie too, but they were out. I guess the AC wasn't working either, It was really hot inside.

I couldn't finish half of my salad because the leaves did not look healthy. The dressing was only so so. Overall, I do not think I will be coming back.

The burger here are ok. Nothing really special about it, it taste the same as burgers everywhere else. The fries were really good though. I love the garlic fries here because they actually put a good amount of garlic into their fries.

I also tried the salad here and it is pretty good. It is interesting how there is a pot full of chicken pieces and they just scoop it on top... it didnt look that great when I saw them do it because the chicken was watery. But it tasted fine. The cornbread was really good, and they give you a really big piece.

The cornbread and the fries here are probably the only reason why I would come here.

I love how healthy and quick this place is. To me, they give huge portions leaving me full and extras to save for later. Their Tuna Sandwich was delicious :) Salads were decent, I would prefer ordering the half order instead of the full order because the full order is humongous! Salads come with cornbread or a piece of bread but I would definitely recommend getting their cornbread.

I love this place. They make everything themselves, from the bread to the hummus. Even their italian salad dressing has a unique, amazing taste. I come here almost every day and have yet to be dissatisfied with their food.

First timer at this place. I was surprised by their cheap prices and it's definitely filling. Also my first time making a review for yelp... so here it goes!!

SERVICE & ATMOSPHERE: Good friendly service as expected, super fast service got my food in less than 5 min. Spacy place a lot of places to sit and eat.

MY ORDER: I got the #1 combo Big A Burger w/ Garlic Fries & Coke
I had no idea I accidentally ordered a veggie burger, but after taking my first bite I had no regrets ordering it, it was so good I might even go vegetarian because of this veggie burger. Their fries was eehhhhhhh whatever.. nothing special but pretty good still. I thought their garlic fries was gonna be good but all I got was a littly lump of minced garlic on the side.

The good thing about all the food here is that it's supposedly really healthy. I'm definitely coming back here to try out all their other stuff. Their name got the "A+" in it but I'm gonna give it an A-

No, I don't think Smart Alec's food made me more intelligent. It's pretty hyped for a lunch place (now opened for breakfast). During lunch hours, the line can go out the door. This place is cash only like your usual Berkeley food spots.

They're famous for their burgers, their vegetarian burgers. I guess my meat loving side just can't really deal with it. It's very bland in taste and very dried in texture. The bun is a bit soggy from the juice of the patty. Their burgers are not very interesting for me to comment much about.

They do serve soups and salads. I didn't find their garlic fries as tasty as others have said. Last time, and the only time I had it, they put this giant scoop of raw garlic on top of regular fries. I think I preferred to walk half a block to I.B. Hoagie's for their LEGIT garlic fries.

Oh and if you ever paid attention to their placemats, bring in an A paper/exam and you get free fries. Also, you can read about how healthy their food is (maybe that's why it's so bland and gross to me. I'm a true believer of burgers being moderately greasy.)

It's been 4 years since I was a student at Cal...but eating here this past wknd brought back TONS of memories of being a student there.  I used to love Smart Alec's for their amazing salads, and it is jst as good now as it was then.  

I brought my BF around Telegraph because he's never been, and we decided to have lunch here b/c I have such fond memories of it.  I ordered a superior chef salad with chicken...which was HUGE!  My BF ordered a avodcado burger combo, but we ended up just sharing my salad and eating some garlic fries, and saving the entire burger for later.  The salad was more than enough.  If you are a salad lover you will really love it here...the ingredients are so fresh, the serving size is fantastic, and they have the besssttttttt poppy seed salad dressing (highly recommended!).  Their fries are also "air-baked," which are supposed to have only 9 grams of fat (in a large) as compared to b/w 25-33 grams of fat in fast food fries.  I'm obsessed with fries so any excuse is good to me :)  

I really wish they had a place like this around where I live.  It would be a weekly fixture in my life.

I like this place a lot. It just FEELs healthy. 

The ambiance is really casual, your usual Berkeley fast-food-ish place. The best part is this place is actually pretty fast. You only have to wait like 10 minutes max even if it's busy.

I usually order the regular burger. It is SUPER filling and can get soggy near the end but good for that burger fix if you are fiending for it and don't want to eat McDonald's (not too many burger places in Berkeley. I guess there is IB's across the street and Bongo Burger around but Bongo Burger has a less healthier feel. Don't know if that makes sense.).

Today I ordered the half salad half sandwich which I found to be delightful as well. Portions are big, and the cranberry mayo made the Roast Turkey sandwich absolutely delicious. It had a sweet tang that made it pleasant to eat. Just enough of a sandwich to get your fix and you don't have to be overwhelmed or bored by the second half. 

Friend and I then shared the large garlic fries. Freshest fries he's ever had at Smart Alec's, he said. They were warm, crunchy, and even though the garlic wasn't exactly evenly spread, you can't ask for much more.

I don't ever dig the cash only aspect though.

cheap, fairly healthy, and so good. 
i love love love the eggplant melt, the salads and soup are fantastic, and the cornbread is AMAZING. 

food comes really fast as well :)

Berkeley is where I discovered baked air fries.  I love fries.  I could be a fry-a-holic.  The salads were huge... I love fiber!  The burgers organic.  This is just the kind of food I like:  fresh, healthy, organic and a good deal.

garlic fries and super moist fresh cornbread with soup...

* two thumbs up*

So maybe I was just hungry but their burgers are REALLY good! 

Food: 
- #2. The Big B: A regular beef patty with lettuce, tomatoes, spread, and onions on a soft wheat bun. I'm not sure what's in the spread, but it was pretty good. The wheat bun was so soft with just the perfect amount of spongy kick to it. Just the way a perfect wheat bun should taste. I think my patty was only half cooked...so I'm going to pray that I don't get mad cow disease, but despite it being only half ready to serve, it was still really good. All the veggies complimented it really well. Great job on a nice burger. 

Service: 
I'm normally really tolerant of BAD SERVICE, but the girl at the counter today was just down right AWFUL. So I get up to the counter to order and she gives me this glare because I just interrupted her conversation with her co-worker. I order my food and hand her a credit card (not knowing they only take CASH) and she just glares at me again, rolls her eyes and points at this sign that says "CASH ONLY". So I apologize and pull out some cash. I wanted to look for 2 pennies but she just threw me my change and my receipt and just went back to talking to her co-worker. I had to pick up my change that she threw on the counter along with my receipt as she just ignored me. I'm not saying that you have to treat me like I'm going to give you a $50 tip, but you can at least treat me like a person! Someone needs to teach this girl some manners! 

Ambiance: 
Right on the corner of Durant and Telegraph, so all the windows open out onto the corner of these two busy streets that show a good reflection of undergrad Berkeley life. It's a pretty good place to hang out and chill with some friends. 

Price: 
Under $5. Being as poor as I am...I can even afford that :) 

Overall: 
Aside from the horrendous service, I liked this place. I would totally come back for another burger or to even try the salads!

Smart Alec's offers pretty tasty food for being on the healthier spectrum; I'm definitely a fan. I always get the Basil Chicken sandwich combo with regular (not garlic) fries, which are air baked. Granted, they don't taste quite the same as the deep fried variety -- but they are delicious for being better for you (then again, I never met a french fry I didn't like...!). As for the sandwich itself: it's served on a wheat bun, and the basil mayonnaise is delicious. The chicken itself is not bad, but it's not the best I have had, either. Other points worth noting: Cash only, and the sun can be blinding if you're sitting near the windows. All in all, Smart Alec's is worth a trip!

I had the homemade hummus sandwich and I have to say the actual contents of the sandwich were very good, I just don't care for wheat bread at all and that really ruined the taste for me. I am certain that if that same sandwich was on say a french baguette or sourdough or some other bread I would have given this place 5 stars.

Their fries were excellent, they were flavorful but not at all greasy or oversalted. 

The service here was really quick as we each got our orders by the time we turned around to find a seat - a trend that seemed to continue as more people came into the restaurant in the time we were there.
salads here bigger than your head ,great sesame dressing. The burgers and faux burgers are a little on the not so tasty side, but hit up those salads bigger than your head.. you won't be sorry

Healthy? Don't know about that.. but hey it's a good place to watch the interesting Bezerkeley people outside.

The basil chicken burger was really really good.. I must admit. I'd much rather go here than Mc Donalds or Del Taco.. on second thought I'd rather throw up in my mouth than eat Del Taco, but that's an entirely other topic.

Also don't even think about getting the garlic fries unless you want everyone you come in contact (within 4 feet of to be exact) with for the next 8 hours to hate you. TRUST ME you could run off a overweight, hairy, 50+ man at the POWER EXCHANGE with this kind of breath.. not that I'd know anything about that.. I'm just sayin..

I wish Smart Alec's was around when I was a student at Cal.  The food is relatively good and affordable, very important when you're a college student on a budget and very hungry.  And a great alternative to fast food.  A had a delicious tasting tossed green salad consisting of lettuce, carrots, red cabbage, spouts, tomato, croutons, and ranch dressing with cornbread.  The sandwiches are also pretty good, I enjoyed my grilled chicken breast on wheat sandwiches.

I had Smart Alec's long ago as a freshman, and recently stopped by again. 

2 1/2 years ago, I came and ordered the corn chowder with corn bread. Man oh man. That was some good creamy CORN CHOWDER. And the cornbread that comes with it? A whopping 3" by 3" cube of glory. I've baked cornbread from boxes and from scratch multiple times before, but NEVER have I been able to get some cornbread as good as Smart Alec's. Their cornbread DOES NOT CRUMBLE on impact! It's surprisingly hefty. Just sweet enough too.

Past couple weeks, I went two more times. First time, I went and got the BIG A BURGER (~$3.50). Got my A+ assignment stamped and got a FREE SIDE OF GARLIC FRIES!!! The burger was delicious, lemme say. Not like a Boca, not Morningstar either. Just good stuff, Tasty and meaty enough to be like a real burger but light enough to know it's not artery clogging meat (I'm not a vegetarian, but I do love me some veggie burgers). Comes with lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, lotsa mustard and ketchup. Good stuff. They also have this flavored mayo that makes dipping and spreading some kind of delicious endeavor. I got some to go. :E

(Note: friend got the avocado burger. Straight-up, at least a half of a fresh avocado slathered on. Yummeh)

GARLIC FRIES; they accidentally messed up and gave me a large order. I ain't complaining. :P Shared it with my friends and was enough for TWO MEALS I made at home later. Very yummy, but BE WARNED. It's a LOTTT of garlic. Some green herbs in it too. Maybe parsley. (Waittt, they're BAKED??? No way! I thought they were normal fried fries!! Crazy! They're so good!)

Tried my friend's MANGO SMOOTHIE: not very smoothie-ish. Very liquid-y. I don't recommend it. I'd much rather buy a lassi from somewhere else.

Yesterday, though, they disappointed me. I got the LENTIL SOUP ($3.22 sans tax) with CORNBREAD. The lentil soup was all right. Simple vegetable soup with some (lemme stress, just some, not a lot) lentils and potatoes. Decent, cumin flavor was a little misplaced. Eating cornbread with it helped add some flavor while hiding the strange cumin. I'd recommend just going back to the corn chowder.

All in all, Smart Alec's, you are one tasty nerd, and I'll keep coming back. Need to try your other soups and a sandwich one day.

Food: 4/5
Price: 4/5
Atmosphere: 3/5
Service: 3/5 (cashier is only ever "decent", 4s and 5s saved for really amiable, talkative, helpful service)

Smart Alec's in the other salad place in Berkeley (other than Intermezzo) that serves huge portions, the way salads should be.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: three stars.

I cannot begin to express how good their caesar salads are, with the fresh lettuce, parmesan flakes, and crunchy croutons. The best part, however, is the huge chunk of cornbread they give you. Definitely one of the most substantial meals you can get in Berkeley.

Note: I did not say "most substantial HEALTHY meals." It is, after all, a caesar salad.

I am not as much of a fan of the other things on their menu, such as the garlic fries or burgers. But that is alright. I would go back just for the salad.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: one star.

Smart Alec's is in a very convenient location, and with wide and tall windows, a great place to observe the goings-on in Berkeley. So, you basically get a show as well.
delicious and perfect for those times when you want a (vegan) burger fries and a soda, or just want to feel really fat

the eggplant sandwiches, air-baked fries, corn-bread, and side salads are terrific!! get the sesame dressing.
i have never been a corn-bread fan but smart alec's does it right. great values too...you can get half sandwich+soup/salad combos with a huge square of cornbread/wheatbread for about $6.
i would, however, stray away from the sesame tofu salad. i tried it after reading rave reviews here. it was pretty much the most boring salad i have ever eaten and i felt sick about halfway through the enormous thing. the marinated tofu was tough and salty...ick.
I didn't like it.  Dry black bean burger + dry bun + soggy fries/workers who look eternally unhappy = blech.

All I'm gonna say is that every single time I eat here, no matter what I order, I undoubtedly provide the Tums company with a huge boost in sales. 

TMI? Oh well, deal with it (and the inevitable gas you'll get if you eat here).

What an awful place. This restaurant is a loud, insistent answer to a question no one asked. 

You want healthy, go have some pho or a wrap or eat only tempe+veggies or look in the mirror and feel disgusted and skip the meal all together. Don't be an amoeba and order the abominations they serve here.

Places like this are why conservatives hate us.

I think this place is as good as it gets in terms of healthy "fast food." 
I've been going here for years and it never ceases to amaze me. The food is consistently healthy, fresh and overall great.
The portions are huge and easily shared with another, I rarely finsih my salads when I get them.
I love their cornbread and their veggie chili too.
Everything can be made vegetarian which is also a huge plus for me.
Whenever I can't make up my mind about what to eat when i'm on Telegraph, Smart Alec's never fails me.

Such a treat to eat here whenever I'm in Berkeley!  Been eating here for years.

Some of my favorites:
- Chinese chicken Salad
- Corn Chowder
- Lentil soup
- Corn bread
- Brownie
- Turkey Sandwich

Very casual, laid back feel.  Food is quick.  Healthy food at healthy prices! :-)

It's expensive; the fries are soggy; the burgers are dry. I really don't have much more to say about this place other than you could do far better in Berkeley. Take your money and spend it on better food. At least the wait is never too long for a bite.

The letter "A" in Smart Alec's has a plus sign next to it, and it could be interpreted as the letter grade assigned to the restaurant's seemingly health-conscious menu, or the average grade on the transcripts of nearby UC Berkeley students. But given the university's notorious grading curve, that "A+" is more likely associated with Alec's garlic fries and burgers.

Though the restaurant prides itself in providing healthy foods, the garlic fries may be an exception. The grease is enough to give you trouble picking up the fries. But with a great calorie count comes great taste. These fries are loaded with garlic: be sure to spread it around before eating, and bring some mints or gum for after. The flavor of the garlic feels stronger because these fries are not heavily salted, which is a nice departure from other places' garlic fries. All combos come with a medium serving of fries, which is actually a large enough portion for most. Better yet, garlic and normal varieties are the same price.

Alec's burgers are definitely above average, with juicy all-beef patties and fresh vegetables. Your first bite might feel foreign if you order the A burger: the wheat buns offer a rougher texture that is immediately noticeable. I'm used to seeing wheat buns on subs and chicken sandwiches, but not on burgers. Its a step forward for health reasons, but a small step back for taste.

They also offer a wide range of vegan and veggie foods that do not compromise on taste. The popular veggie burger is a prime example. For skeptics that refuse to believe any hamburger can be a healthy food, there are a wide range of salads and soups to choose from. I didn't get to try any, but they seem to be very popular. Alec's also sells fruit juices.

The restaurant is located on busy Telegraph, and there are plenty of windows for eaters to people-watch. The place is very clean, and orders are made quickly.

But the college students' main concerns are always price and quantity, and Alec's delivers. The aforementioned A combo (A burger, medium fries and medium drink) will only set you back a little over 6 dollars, but is more than enough to get you full.

And as a bonus for students, bringing in an assignment with an "A" grade will net you free stuff. I wouldn't know, though. I'm not a Berkeley student and I don't get As, but Smart Alec's definitely makes the grade.

Note: I want to give this a 3.5

Smart Alec's is my go-to place when I'm hungry, but don't want to pay the consequences of overindulgence later.  

The sandwiches are simple and delicious.  I usually grab a few bags of mustard and a bottle of Tapatio to spice things up.  

Alec's also has "air baked" fries.  I like these better than the fried fries.  The "air bakedness" makes the fries dryer and more crispy.  MMMM garlic-y air baked fries.

Their salads look really good, but I always get lured by the sandwiches.  I'd rather get a salad here than at Cafe Intermezzo.  

Supposedly, if you bring in a paper or test with an A on it, they'll give you X amount off of your meal or free fries or something.  Pretty sveet!

I ordered the double cheese burger.

A sign outside stated it was chosen as BEST BURGERS in the city or something to that effect.

I don't agree, but I also haven't tried every single burger in the city.  I will always remember a burger I had in NYC, but that's NYC.

Crowded near the pickup food area, and staff was not the friendliest. They seemed upset.

Haven't been here in a while, but from what I remember this place is great.  I'm not vegetarian, but am a huge fan of their veggie burgers. Their fries are also pretty interesting, they make them differently from other places. And the special sauce is delicious.

Tips:

Cash only

---------------------------

$9 for a "gourmet burger combo" which is basically the choice of a chicken or beef burger with a "special sauce" (teriyaki, basil pest, etc.) which they have a list of. I thought why not give the gourmet burger a try and I got the pesto basil sauce along with a B Beef Burger. The burger is pretty good and it goes great with the whole wheat bun. I'm not sure if I'd try the gourmet version of the burger again. The basil pesto sauce wasn't distinct in any way and I think it isn't worth the extra $2 to get a gourmet burger. (Just my opinion)

I also didn't like the regular fries. I'm not sure if I just waited to long to eat them because I finished my burger before indulging on the fries, but they seemed cold and hardened already. (Only about an hour after)

My burger combo wasn't that great, but they do have VERY large salads and the cornbread is DELICIOUS. Burger alone I'd give it 2 stars, but for the cornbread I'll add in one more star.

This place has the most amazing corn chowder soup I've ever had. I'm vegan and one of my favorite foods used to be clam chowder soup, and their corn chowder does a mighty fine job of satisfying my nostalgia for it. I like both their regular and their garlic fries, the tofu sandwich, their garden salad, and their veggie burgers. Only complaint is that they don't serve organic ketchup. Their smoothies are on the sweet side and are more like slushies than anything else.
It' also be awesome if they had compostable forks and such (although they have silverware, but there's only so much).

A few of my teammates and I wandered here for lunch last week for lunch on our way up to Sonoma. Thankfully we beat the lunch crowd in because minutes after we placed our order, there was a line out the door. 

I ordered the chicken sandwich and a side of corn bread. Sounds like an odd pairing but when I overhead someone behind me say it was delicious, I had to give it a try. My friend ordered french fries so I figured I would be able to sample a few of his if I had to urge. 

When I received my sandwich, I thought it was tasty enough but it wasn't anything special. I think the real winner was the corn bread - the impulse purchase. ; )  I ended up just eating half of my chicken sandwich and the entire piece of cornbread which was a large serving. I did manage to snag a few french fries from my friend and realized they were baked and not fried. Pretty tasty for baked. 

I wasn't too thrilled about this spot but at least the corn bread was a good find! = )

It's been a while since I've been to Berkeley. So when we passed by Smart Alec's, I knew we had to go in.

Avocado chicken burger. Still oh-so-good! The combo comes with fries and drink. So much food! I always get this but can never finish it! (http://static.px.yelp.com/bphoto/Uqi87wFqbo7GhrzxJ65MKw/l)

They only serve whole wheat buns. So unfortunately for those who are allergic to wheat, you can't try their tasty burgers. But they do have many other delicious options. I highly recommend the soup & 1/2 salad combo. Their corn chowder is sooo goooood!! (http://static.px.yelp.com/bphoto/MJSiTtt5wYmOLA1Apd9i3w/l) Loaded with corn and potato. Hearty and filling!! And with the 1/2 salad, you can choose between mixed greens or caesar salad topped with a giant cornbread! (http://static.px.yelp.com/bphoto/bE_89mR-tnoU4KNymk-Luw/l)

Yummy! =D

I used to come here like 2x a week because my friend and I were on this "healthy diet." I definitely don't think Smart Alec's is anywhere near as healthy as they claim to be....

HOWEVER the sandwiches are good (not amazing) but they give you this huge, bomb ass piece of cornbread or wheat bread (apparently the wheat is good) but I always get the cornbread just because I love cornbread. And it tastes healthy and yummy :D the soups are okay as well. But cornbread FTW

This place offers huge, cheap, delicious salads with an amazing variety of vegetables. I usually ask them to hold the wheat berry though, since it's not particularly interesting. If you're more hungry, they can add a chicken, beef or veggie patty to it. I also recommend the garlic fries. I never realized what a garlic could burn until I ate them. Now I get them every time. Ouch!

i once LOVED smart alec's. shortly after i became a vegetarian (january 2008) i discovered this place and fell in love with the garden delight salad, which i would get almost every single day.

but lately they've been horribly fucking up my salad (the garden delight). for example, a couple days ago, my salad had a huge piece of paper towel in it, which I only found by removing from my mouth something I was chewing on that was strangely not disintegrating. I reacted reasonably--I removed it and continued to eat, but my entire salad then had the taste of musty paper towel residue. sigh.

and, even worse, a few weeks ago, on two separate occasions, there was a bunch of sand in my salad. sand, i say! totally unacceptable.

so now i need to find a new place to frequent. =(

update: my rating was originally two stars, but shortly after I posted this I was contacted by a Smart Alec's manager [stefani(sp?), the girl with the nose ring]--she messaged me here on yelp and accused me of fabricating the experiences I posted, rather than apologizing for the shit i went through. what a shitty thing to do--giving a loyal customer two terrible experiences, and instead of apologizing, attacking him by accusing him of lying.

i've never gone since.

I've been here before, at least twice I think.  Yesterday would be my third trip to Smart Alec's.  Wonderful lunch spot for hungry visitors and college students.  It's relatively cheap, especially with their combos.  I went with a chicken basil burger with garlic fries and a medium drink for $7.01.  Not bad at all.  I'm surprised the garlic fries and regular fries are the same price!  The kicker is that these are baked fries.  Not exactly my favorite side, but if it's included, I won't complain.  

And there is the debate about whether this place is actually that healthy.  I say it really depends what you order, can't expect everything to be under 300 calories.  I ate it, smiled, and walked away happily.  Enough said.

Next time I'll try a soup and salad combo!  CASH ONLY!

Okay, I am such a fan of Smart Alecs  food because of the non fried, no oil used, healthy food  options that are on the menu. For all those " IN AND OUT " lovers, in my opinion  Smart Alecs is Way better because: 

1. no oil used  -- NO GREASE!
2. fresh vegetables
3.dolphn safe tuna 
4.large portions
5.weight friendly
6. Roasted turkey
7. less then $10  per person

I tried their corn bread, salads, chicken sandwiches, burgers, french fries- plain and with garlic  and the next time I go there, I will order the corn chowder. 

I seriously feel that  I'm eating a diet burger and diet french fries when I go  here. 

Love this place!!

Go for the Combo Number 5:  Avocado Burger (Choice of Beef, Chicken or Veggie Burger)...comes with delicious Air Baked Fries and a choice of Soda.  Apparently they only take cash...which would explain the hold up with the group that was ahead of us.  Never forget that cash is king!

We visited during a crowded lunch rush one day, and still got a clean table and very fast service.  Parking was actually easy on Durant street just around the corner.  I'm not sure they should claim it to be "healthy food"...but it was as healthy as cheeseburgers and fries could get, I suppose.

SO when I want a burger I am not exactly worried about the healthiness of it unless I make it at home. However this place is supposed to be "intelligent fastfood" sounds like an oxymoron don't you think lol. Anyways I came here with my boyfriend of the time on our little telegraph stint and I liked it overall. I had the real beef burger and he had the tofu burger. IT was pretty tast and the fries were really good I was happy they didn't wanna give me carrot sticks instead jk jk. Nothing special but if I was in the area again id stop by still...the fries were good n the burger ok but the place itself was cool...I liked the openness of it. Worth the money oh and on that note bring cash that is the only way to pay here!

I've lived in the Berkeley area for 9 years, went to law school just blocks away, and what do you know, I've never been to Smart Alec's!  My husband got a veggie burger, and I got a chicken breast burger.  We shared a large fries.  Everything was pretty tastey.  For "baked fries," it wasn't at all dry.  Very impressive.  The burger wasn't the best I've ever tasted, but for a more "healthy option," I did enjoy the food.  Brings me back to my student days...I'd definitely go back.  For two burgers, fries, and a drink, we paid around $11.50.

Minus one star for the janky payment policy.  No credit cards allowed (cash only!), and no bills over $20.  That's so ghetto.  We only had a $50, and had to go to Blake's to break the bill.  What's up with that?

I don't know what the hype is about this place. Granted, I am a loyal patron of Bongo Burger, but in my defense, I tried Smart Alec's first. I was going to give this place a 2.5 stars, but the free fries bumped it up to 3 stars.

TIP: Bring any academic paper, test, or midterm with an "A" on it to get a free order of french fries or garlic fries!!

ATMOSPHERE
There is a lot of seating, which is nice, but the doors are always open and it gets really cold inside the place. I don't like shivering as I eat my meals.

The workers are friendly and fast; your food comes out almost immediately and you can see them make your food in the open kitchen behind the cashier.

FOOD
I usually order the AVOCADO BURGER with AIR-BAKED GARLIC FRIES. 

AVOCADO BURGER- to be honest, the burger isn't that great. I appreciate the generous avocado spread, but the burger gets really mushy and super messy. The bread is probably what disgusts me the most. It's not firm enough and the patty slips back and forth while you eat it.

The FRENCH FRIES are good for the first 10 minutes and then they start to get soggy and limp: 2 adjectives that should never be used to describe french fries. I appreciate their effort to be "healthy," but I like my fries crispy! The garlic is real garlic (none of that garlic powder), so the taste is extremely strong. Bring some mints if you plan on going back to class or to meet up with friends.

My friends often get their salads, which seem pretty big but it seems like they get the salads for the cornbread. I'm not a fan of cornbread so you won't see me with one of their plain looking salads.

Overall, there are better burger places just down the street from here. The only redeeming quality of this place is their free fries with any "A" work.

The salads are the reason I come here, although those fake burgers and grilled chicken sandwiches with avocado always tempt me.

Don't fool yourself.  That cornbread that everyone is raving about is basically a big piece of delicious, heavy, yellow sheet cake.  It's even sold in the same case as the chocolate cake!  Put some frosting on one of those pieces of cornbread and you'd fool a lot of people.

I usually get the Asian Chicken salad, minus the rice noodles and I add edamame.  

The annoying thing about the take out orders is that it's really easy to forget to not ask for your dressing on the side (it has to do with the way the cashiers prompt you for your preferences...).  And they put a ton of salad dressing on their salads - my salad has literally been swimming in a rather deep pool of sesame vinaigrette dressing when I forgot to tell them.

The soups are trustable.  Again, I would bet you anything that the popular Corn Chowder is probably not as "healthy" as you would like to think it is.

Everything at Smart Alec's needs to be taken in context.  The food is all okay but nothing really spectacular.  

The salad is huge & pretty cheap but the veggies are fresher w/ more variety at Intermezzo.  
The fries are good if you like healthy food.  If you like In n Out fries then you probably won't like these. 

Things that are good w/ out the need for a disclaimer:
The soups (and all dairy free!).
The hummus.
The speed of your order - lightening fast!

Things you need to know:
1.  I'm pretty sure they only accept cash.
2.  Do NOT talk to the painted faced, knitted cap selling crazy woman outside the restaurant!!!  She is crazier than a mo-fo and will never, ever stop talking to you once you're caught in her web of lunacy!
3.  If you need to use the restroom, tell the cashier and they'll buzz you in.

You Bay Areans sure are spoiled. Did you know that it's actually NOT normal for restaurants in this country to be plentiful with veg, vegan and healthier options?

I liked that this place didn't overreach. Typical fast food offerings just tweaked a bit- fast food wasn't invited to be outrageously gourmet and opulent. Yet, I still found my picky ass decided between several different things that sounded really good. I settled on the basil chicken sandwich- which was good- and the baked fries, which were awesome. Pretty cheap, too. 

I know OMG CHAINS ARE SOOO EVIL GUYS but I'd be down with a few more locations of this place. At least put one by my office, thanks.

best restaurant ever. amazing cornbread and caesar salads. their burgers are not to be beat, especially for how healthy they are. i still make the occasional hour-out-of-my-way detour just to eat here.

A less picky eater might be disturbed by the fact that the meat in the chili may or may not be meat.  It sort of looks like meat, but it could also be some type of soy fako-meato product.  I like it, and eat it pretty frequently considering I don't know what it is.  They serve it with a big piece of cornbread.  I like that too.  Pretty good eats if you ask me. 

I also tasted Britt's corn chowder...sooo good.  It's definitely real corn and not soy fako-corno, so if you are into corn chowder get that.  

(If you are into corny girls take Britt...skip the chowder)

I like this place.

Okay okay, yes this place is supposed to be healthy. But dammit I wanted a burger and the supposed "best fries" in Berkeley? ROfl the fries are god awful. I've been here once since my friend made me go, and haven't been back. 1 star because it's near campus, another because it's "healthy". -3 stars for their awful taste and disgustingly long lines. Jeez *gasp* even Bongo has better burgers/fries. Omg I can't believe I said that! Baaaarneeeeeey's.
Smart Alec's is an OK because of the price. It's basically healthier fast food, with veggies burger options and air fries. The food doesn't taste great but it's a better choice than McDonalds.

this place i feel is more like 2.5 stars.  the burgers are really ehhhhhhhhh and the garlic fries are terrible. 
i forgot why i stopped going to this place until tonight when i decided to give it a go again.

also, a homeless guy came in and started asking me for money for a good minute before going on to other customers.  it took smart alec's employees some time before they kicked him out.

OK so there are only a handful of items I order here but they are SO GOOD! 

My favorite is the veggie cheese burger with fries!! The patty is super flavorful and the fries are always crispy and...no extra charge for garlic fries!!!!!

The eggplant melt is really good as well. The eggplant is always cooked really well and whatever sauce they put on this is creamy and delicious!

When I want to pretend to be healthy, I get the tofu sesame salad with a fat piece of corn bread! Nom.

Everything here's reasonably priced and comes in huge portions but if you're really on a budget, get a bowl of soup with corn bread. Super filling and under 5 bucks.

Also, get a stamp card..fill it up and you'll get a free veggie burger or bowl of soup!

I remember walking past this restaurant as a high schooler wondering what the hell it was. Something about getting good grades I guess. I didn't know that is was a glorious, vegetarian haven.

I am a new vegetarian, and this restaurant made my conversion so much easier. It's affordable and it's right by campus! Big A Burger Combos are one of the greatest deals in history, ranking only slightly above the Louisiana Purchase. Veggie patty, choice of garlic fries or normal fries, and a drink. Oh sweetness. 

I've also tried their delicious Gourmet Burger with a veggie patty and pesto sauce. That shit is good, but the burger combo is pretty much bomb for any starving college student.

Their big salads are great too. They're huge! And they come with that sweetass golden brick of cornbread. 

Don't worry, they cater to carnivores as well. Sweet deals all around. Eat! Enjoy! Eat again!

I'm hungry...but I don't want to go to Fat slice...I kinda want a salad...a huge salad...a salad sooo big I won't be able to finish it.

Oh...thank god...Smart Alecs is across the street.

I loves grabbing a water, fries and a salad here. I have a punch card...and someday...SOMEDAY...I will get my free whatever it is.

A staple to any Cal student's budget diet!  I have come here more times than I can count, been through more stamp cards that I care to remember... 

one essential tip: use your stamp card to get the SOUP.  NEVER get the vegan burger "for fun".  It's not worth 8 visits, even if it is "free".  

My favorite: Tossed Green Salad with Poppyseed dressing.  You might think this is like a side salad just because it's cheaper than the others.  This is untrue.  Finish a salad with your piece of bread (corn or wheat) and then tell me you're hungry.  I DARE YOU.  Asking for light dressing is enough.  Too much salad dressing can ruin a salad.  The carrots are chunky and fresh.  The sprouts are cool, not too much.  The croutons I could live without.  Funnest part : finding a random lentil or edamame in there.  

Best soup: Corn Chowder.  Totally filling, piping hot, flavorful, satisfying.  Second: Vegetable.  Makes you feel healthy and it tastes good.  The potato soup is weird and not a fan of chili.  

Smart Alec's turned me into a cornbread liker, when I used to be a cornbread hater.  If you buy it by itself, I think it's $1.08.  Maybe inflation has changed things now. However, if you let it sit in the paper bag for long enough, you'll probably lose your appetite as the grease seeps through layers upon layers of paper.  I shudder at the thought.  So I try not to think when I devour it because it is that good.

You can never substitute the corn/wheat bread for the scrumptious looking piece of chocolate cake/bread in the glass case.  I must have asked on 10 separate occasions and have always been denied.      

The sandwiches are alright - I haven't had too many so I'm not too opinionated on that front.

Bring in an A paper or test and you get free fries!  Garlic fries and reg fries are the same price... go figure.

PS: Try not to go to the bathroom here, it is annoying.  The door buzzes to let you in and sometimes it doesn't work and everyone who sits by the door stares at you - not fun.

PPS: The service is hella fast!  You will be in and out of there in 5 min tops (as long as the line's not out the door)

They have a frequent rewards card system. If you order over $5, you get a stamp. When you get 10 stamps, you can get a free Big A burger or soup. If you get an A on any assignment, bring it here to get a free order of fries! You don't have to order anything with it.

The default Big A burger is vegetarian, so don't be upset if you did not specify beef. The vegetarian version is not the best burger I've had, but it's not bad. Veggie burgers just inherently cannot be as great tasting as beef burgers. The eggplant sandwich is super good. I absolutely love the garlic fries. They are air-baked and have real chucks of chopped garlic on them. The salads are huge, but not as huge as the ones at Cafe Intermezzo and comparable to the ones at Sufficient Grounds. Salad choices are little limited. Soup choices here include veggie soups, chowders, and chili. The soup comes with cornbread. The cornbread here is known to be the best in the area. It's nice and moist when you get it, but it will turn rock solid the next day.

There is a lot of seating, but... my favorite thing here is the bar seating by the huge open windows so you can people watch while you eat and make people jealous of your food.

Okay here's the deal, back in the day (like 1992-1998) I was a vegetarian.  I know, I know. Shut it.  From 1995-1997 I was a vegan.  Hey asshole, I SAID "shut it"!  Now those years were unpopular years to be a vegetarian of any degree.  We were burned at the stake, denounced as witches and viewed with suspicion and scorned for having too much fiber in our diets.  Hell I think people thought I smelled bad or something.  I DIDN'T.  
Through all those times of uncertainty, Smart Alec's was the bastion of my kind.  We made pilgrimages there to have air-popped fries and vegan smoothies.  Like Mecca I would worship in Smart Alec's general direction daily and talking of their food would often put a far-off look in my eyes.
I'm no longer one of the sick and afflicted aka vegetarian.  I've since also realized that Smart Alec's ain't all that.  The smoothies are decent but everything else is not nearly as good as other vegan and vegetarian cuisine that is now found mainstream throughout the bay area.  Smart Alec's needs to step up, they aren't the only game in town.

Smart Alec's claims to be healthy, but how healthy can a burger get?
I got the Eggplant melt + soup combo and it came with a side of cornbread. The potato and leek soup was very thick and filling. I like my meat, but the eggplant melt was good to the point where it silenced the carnivore within. The cornbread was amazing, but I seriously doubt how healthy it is.  
If you come with an A-grade test/quiz/paper, you get free garlic fries! Im not that big a fan of the fries but free food is free food. When you're a college student on a budget, you don't have the privilege of being picky. 
So much food for under $10! Come if you're running low on $, don't if you're tryna lose weight.

My idea of a healthy diet is to only eat things that taste good, and not to waste calories on bad food. So I have absolutely no use for "air-baked" (what other substance would you bake in?) fries. Lower fat, yes, but the taste-to-calorie ratio approaches zero. Give me fried-fries any day. If you're worried about trans fats, fry 'em in lard.

Fortunately, there are menu choices that aren't particularly healthy. Burgers are good for the price point, probably better than Bongo (not that I've ordered burgers at Bongo for a long time). I also like the potato and leek soup, salty enough to raise your blood pressure a couple of points. Worth detouring a couple of blocks for.

Alec, 
overcooking your tofu in way too much vinegar is not intelligent.
A ball of minced garlic plopped into a basket of your regular fries does not make them garlic fries. 
Enriched Wheat Flour bread is not the same as whole grain.

Your food is neither healthy nor intelligent. You are demoted to just "Alec's" fast food. 
 Good day, sir!

Afforable, good food.  Staff is friendly & the place is clean.  I got the avocado burger B combo.  I wouldn't go out of my way to come back here.  I did notice some strangers salad & I was thinking I should have ordered that, it looked big and tasty.
You get a pretty big chunk of cornbread for a dollar. That alone is worth 3 stars.

i love eating in college towns, b/c the food is so damn cheap.  you can get a huge veggie burger, air baked fries, and a huge drink for under $7.  the veggie burger was pretty good, and i added avocado to it.  i loved the fries, and you can either regular or garlic.  since it's baked, the fries are not greasy at all.

We visited Smart Alec's yesterday with some friends we introduced to the Berkeley area.  I was dreaming of poppy seed dressing over mixed greens and half a hummus sandwich, which I promptly devoured shortly after receiving my tray of goodness.  The hummus is a simple sandwich but packed full of flavor and has a great crunch from the cucumbers. The combo is decently priced and we shared a large order of garlic fries.  They definitely didn't skimp on the garlic. We had to high tail it back to the car for some gum before finishing our tour. 

Not sure why they offer another piece of bread or cornbread with the 1/2 salad since I am already eating the sandwich.  Definitely don't need all that bread.

I am amazed that this place is still in business.  I chalk it up to new freshman trying it every year.  Even if you're a health freak, every now and then you want a good burger and fries.....DON'T GO HERE WHEN THAT'S WHAT YOU'RE CRAVING.  Go here when you don't wan to finish your meal because they're trying to ruin a good thing by making it "healthy".

Hated it!

DIRTY HIPPY #1:  Dude, this place is sweeeet!

DIRTY HIPPY #2  : Dude, seriously.  That's some killer veggie fare they have on the menu!

DH 1: Seriously.  Too bad the Alex dude who owns this place sold out and started selling animal flesh. *in special political voice* SELL OUT!  SELL OUT!  LAME!  

DH 2:  Dude. *shakes head* That's tragic.

DH 1:  I know, dude.  Anyway, what are you going to get?

DH 2:  Dude, I don't know either the veggie burger or the soup and salad.  The soup comes with cornbread, dude!!!

DH 1:  Dude, people dig that cornbread.

DH 2:  Dude, is it really that good?  

DH 1:  Dude, I can't tell you for sure.  I only eat macrobiotic.

DH 2: Macrobiotic. Right on.

DH 1:  Dude, I know.  I've never felt healthier since I went macro. I can't believe I ever put those toxins in my body.

DH 2:  Dude.  That's awesome.

DH 1:  I know, dude.  Hey, do me a favor and order me a garden salad with goddess dressing and extra spouts?  I'm gonna step outside and have a smoke.

I remember when Alex opened his revolutionary veggie fast food joint here in the mid-nineties.  It was a breath of fresh air for me, a veggie hairdresser who spent my days cutting the hair of cheap thankless nerds on Telegraph Avenue. As I'd run a #3 Wahl acrpss the pimply scalp of some greasy-haired statistics major in between trims with mom's Flobee back LA, I would fantasize about my lunch break and  biting into the yummiest fake meat this side of Yentl. 

Today, some of the great stuff on the menu (like their delicious soups and fries) still exists, while others, like the yummy teriyaki tofu and veggies have been swapped out for meaty options like real burgers and chicken sandwiches.

I won't lie, I was kind of sad to see Alex go omnivorous on me.

But I will let you in on a secret: I used to cut Alex's hair, too.  And when he changed his menu over a decade ago to include chicken and tuna (and later, beef), he told me how he was lambasted by the veggie community.  At one point, he even showed me some of his hate mail--mostly postcards with "STUPID ALEC'S!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" written in red Sharpie across the front.  I was scurred.  

But Alex also informed me that his profits went up significantly--VERY significantly--after he implemented those changes.  Profits he needed at the time to meet the exorbitant overhead of running a business on Telegraph Avenue.

Over a decade later, two of the salons in which I worked on Telegraph have relocated due to the skyrocketing rents on the avenue. Many of my other frequent lunch haunts from my hairdressing days, including Zona Rosa, Pasta Pomodoro, and The Coffee Source are also boarded-up. 

Even some of the street kids who panhandle outside of Amoeba have had to downgrade their cell phone plans and start BARTing in from the suburbs to save on gas money. 

Smart Alec's, however, seems to be doing pretty well.  I still go there every now and again for a tasty veggie burger and their fries.  Their corn chowder is still delicious.  And their Caesar salad is better than most non-vegan versions you get at lower-priced restaurants--tart and super garlicky.  Really nice.

Yeah, it's kind of dirty.  So is Telegraph.
Yeah, it's not what it used to be.  Neither is Telegraph.  

These days the avenue is a wasteland.  Nothing seems to be able to stay in business besides Walgreens and Noah's Bagels. Personally I'd like to see a small business like Smart Alec's that serves tasty, healthy, mostly-vegetarian fare stick around.  If slipping a little meat in here and there helps pay the bills, so be it.

Dude, these are perilous times.  Sometimes you have to swallow a little meat to pay the bills.

As I have not yet eaten at this restaurant, I cannot safely say to eat or not eat here.  However, I'm not sure how intelligent the food can possibly be if after ordering a bottle of water, I am given a number.
Used to be quite the hotspot in my day.  However, once the meat appeared, the deliciousness went away.  I used to like the soups...

Very affordable (half salad, half sandwich, and a big piece of corn bread all for a little under $7!), filling portions, super close to campus, and quick service. All that itself is 4 stars.  But if I had to rate this place in terms of quality, it's only A-Ok.  The tossed salad wasn't very fresh...perhaps it was towards the end of the night and they had the scrap pieces, and the wheat bread fell into crumbs when I bit into it...definitely not my type of sandwich.  I'd rather walk a few steps down and wait in the trailing line at Intermezzo for their sandwiches. 

Whether or not this 'intelligent' food has made me any more smarter, we'll have to wait until the end of next week to see if I get those A+'s....

This place is the very definition of dirt cheap. It's so cheap, it's filthy cheap. Five of us hungry wanderers needed sustenance & Smart Alec's was an inviting, airy spot that beckoned to us from across the street (we were shopping at Bear Basic.) 

We ordered a variety of things: vegetable soup, a beef burger, a veggie burger, a green salad and i had the sesame chicken salad ($7). The salads were big enough for 2-3 meals, comes with a huge slab of cornbread & tastes healthy & filling. And just to make sure our meal wasn't too healthy (god forbid), we shared an order of garlic fries. 

Total: $35 (super sized portions for next-to-nothing.)

Bring cash or be prepared to withdraw some money from the BofA ATM across the street because they do not accept credit/debit cards.

their cheese fries are delicious but i've never had bad cheese fries before so i'm thinking that it's not that hard to accomplish. their smoothies are also very tasty, if i were to come here i would just buy one of those and then go to intermezzo. 

i was expecting a lot more out of my marinated tofu and avocado sandwich. it was like i ordered shannyn sossamon and got natalie portman instead.

Smart Alec sells a bunch of stuff: burgers, fries, sammies, pizzas?, and coffee

pour: santa cruz coffee, "java ,mocha", 2.18
-smooth, bold,.knocked me sleepy head awake...
-probably organic & fair traded too
-only place that charged tax on coffee, but then this isn't a "coffee shop"
-fast friendlh service in the afternoon

cash only

I like Smart Alec's primarily for the convenience factor when it's Thursday, I'm at work, and I had to run of to class at 7:45 before having time to prepare lunch. I grab and orange to go with me, but when it gets to be around 1 and I head into work, I'm absolutely starving by that time and head into one of my old standbys.

I order the same things every time because honestly, I've tried the other things on the menu and those are the only options that are worth getting over again.

The Asian chicken salad is huge and well flavored (and they go light on the dressing if you ask). The tofu salad has kind of a funky taste (too much soy sauce) for my liking, though I would normally prefer a tofu salad under different circumstances.

I also really enjoy their eggplant pesto melt, though not exactly the most healthy thing on the menu. Have the half sandwich with vegetable soup and a hunk of corn bread. Mmmm

And those are the only two things on the menu I will ever order, depending on my mood. Their burgers really are not good and their other salads are lackluster at best. Their soups as a whole aren't great but they will do in a pinch.

However, it is reasonably priced and the service is fast and efficient. I'll keep coming to Smart Alec's in the future, if only for their corn bread.

I've walked by this place over 1000 times (it's on my way to campus). I've always pooh-ed the notion of healthy "intelligent" food, opting rather for the rib-eye steak, fish and chips, or chili burger.

I'm going to lunch next week with a new friend that is a Vegan. In fact, she thinks eating meat is much like smoking, an unhealthy crime. Little does she know I also enjoy a cigar too. Perhaps this friendship is doomed.

But I'm committed for a lunch date, just where do we go? My colleague wanted to eat out today and suggested Smart Alec's. At first, I was going to "punt" the idea, however, I went along to try this "vegan" lifestyle.

The place smelled great, just reeking with garlic (from the air baked fries). As I gazed at the large plywood menu, I saw the A burger combo (vegan). Upon ordering, I did have a few questions:

Me: Are your A burgers vegan?

Alec (woman): Yes, they are.

Me: Do you prepared them completely separate from the meat orders?

Alec: Yes, we do.

Me: OK, that's great! I'll have a B cheese burger combo (meat) with garlic fries and a diet.

Alec: I thought you asked about the vegan burger?

Me: Yeah, I did. But that will wait till next week. You see, I met this woman... she's a vegan.... lunch next week...

Alec: [smiling] Gotcha!

Before I could say, '"Dolphin Free Tuna," my order was ready! The B burger (kinda like being on the JV team) was on of the best burgers I've ever had. The honey wheat bun with seeds (I dunno what kind) was so good. Fresh lettuce, tomato, and sliced red onion topped it off! There was some kind of mayo or spread already on the bun, which was fine with me. The air baked fries were a little dense, but with a douse of salt, they too were delicious.

Next week, I'm ordering the A burger (w/out cheese) looking forward to meeting someone new, enjoying the whole vegan experience. Who knows, perhaps I will give up the steaks and cigars.

Hummm? Can't really say. At this point in my life, I can't make commitments.

My fiancé and I were in town last weekend for a concert at the Greek, and we needed something to eat before the show. We walked to this downtown area, saw Smart Alec's on the corner, pulled up the iPhone Yelp app, and decided to give it a try.

I ordered a sesame tofu salad (served on romaine lettuce with LOTS of cucumber and crispy noodles) with the dressing on the side and a piece of cornbread that came with it.

This was the salad that never ended! I kept eating and eating, and it seemed like the salad got even bigger. I don't get it. I was definitely full after eating for 20 min., and it looked like I hadn't even touched it. See picture: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/Q0j0-u8WHHczEg5c9DPQKg?select=8kZbg9l9zGdrgLpyyT7E5w

My fiancé ordered garlic fries (the ones I tried sans garlic were pretty good) and a gourmet burger with BBQ sauce. He seemed to like it.

Overall, a good place for a pre-concert stop, even though I felt kinda old there in this college town.

Did you know Smart Alec's gives you free fries if you get an A on your exam? Well, I didn't until my friend told me about it today, so all you smart alecs (har har har), flash your grades for free fries!

4 stars for that offer and the soups only. I am not a big fan of their other items on the menu. Burgers and sandwiches are decent, salads are pretty filling, but meh. If I want a burger, I'll definitely go elsewhere. The soups, though, are very good. My favorite is the potato leek. Surprisingly, a bowl with your choice of wheat or cornbread can  fill you up for only $3 and some odd cents. 

And watch out, they take garlic fries quite literally. Plop on the garlic and you have garlic fries, so don't expect some kind of garlic-y seasoning.

Dude she gave me corn bread with my salad. Well, at first she asked "wheat or corn bread with your salad"? Then I asked,"which is better"? Then she said, "OMG I just ate the biggest piece of corn bread like a moment ago, can't you tell"? So, when I gazed deeper into her eyes I realized the cool calm collective manner of her expression....and then I KNEW IT....this women had eatin cornbread and didn't give a damn who knew. So, I ordered the cornbread. Brilliant.

i have yet to be competely blown away by smart alec's.  

yes, it is convient. 

yes, it is fairly decently priced.

yes, it is decent food.

but not amazing. garlic fries are a decent fall back, salads  are pretty solid. it's not perfect, there will almost always be a better alternative, but if youre just looking for something... just something, then here we go.

Full Disclosure: I was one of the sad souls in college who scraped extra money together by working at one of the on-campus cafeterias. Over-sized gray jersey, smelly black baseball cap, and stained maroon apron were de rigeur. Don't feel too bad for me though - I brass-knuckled my way into the coveted sandwich station post. People knew me as the "sandwich girl" and it proved to be a popular mating call at parties. 

This job also gave some insight as to what happens in the kitchen of the mass eateries. With the exception of the sushi and wok stations, most of the food was made in bulk. And I gotta tell you, it was nasty.

As I found myself at Smart Alec's a few weeks ago eating some corn chowder and a caesar salad, I started to have flashbacks. The salad was drenched in dressing, making it more of a wilted lettuce caesar soup. The corn chowder was a bit better, but it had the taste of something that had been made 8 hours earlier in a big tub in the back. In other words, Smart Alec's is for that small portion of the overall population who miss dorm food. 

They get plus points for stuffing their sandwiches with extra avocado and sprouts - any sandwich maker will tell you, that's the key to winning over the public's heart. Also, and I'm speaking from experience, inexpensive messy sandwiches posing as healthy = good looking patrons. Trust me on this - it's the only reason I was able to effectively stalk the university's water polo team without being a total creeper. Avocado is love, love is avocado.

Day 21 - Being Vegan...Let me first say CASH ONLY!!!  Someone who I will not mention there name, recommended this place to me.  Ummm...can I say why???  Has he slipped and bumped his head and thought this place was good.  To be honest after 20 days of eating vegan food, this is by far one of the worst one's I've gone to.  What's sad is this place is only around the corner from my favorite ice cream shop "CREAM".  They were voted Best Burger and Fries by the Daily Californian, 2 years in row.  I'm guessing it's their regular burgers and they should stop selling the vegan burgers.

What did I order:

Big A Burger $3.49: According to them "our famous homemade veggie patty"...umm how the heck can this be famous, it's so dry.  If it was crunchy you can pass it off as rice cakes.  Better drench that baby with ketchup and mustard to make it juicy.  Homemade, its better if you go to Raley's and get a Morning Star veggie patty in the freezer section.  It's about the same, probably better. 

Chili $3.22:  This was edible but nothing exciting.  It has a spicy kick to it but not enough species.  

The good thing about this place.  Yes there is a good thing. Is the amount of space.  Lots of seating and the fries are air baked but taste just like oil fried, very yummy.  That alone gives them 2 stars, until I saw the bathroom.  It says "restrooms available only for customers"....it should say "restrooms available only for male customers", because there was no toilet seat, only a toilet and there was tissue and paper towel everywhere.  Totally disgusting, even the public bathroom at the parking garage was cleaner.  

I'm done reviewing this place.  You couldn't pay me enough to eat here again.

I must have walked up and down Telegraph three times before finally settling upon Smart Alec's. Quick, healthy food, big salads, counter seating near a huge open window = pretty ideal lunch spot.

I almost felt like I was in a dorm cafeteria with all the undergrads buzzing around. And as I grabbed my tray once my number was called, I glanced throughout the dining area for my clique. No such luck so I took a seat at the counter by the window. People watching was stellar. A girl walked by with a box over her head and right after, a dude walked by with a bird on his. Ah, Berkeley. 

As for the food, be warned, the salads are absolutely huge. If you're two people, just get one and split it. The lentil soup was chunky, definitely homemade and though lacking in flavor, it felt good putting carrots and potatoes into my body. It's a fresh approach to quick food and a simple menu with the staple lunch options. They've also got a number of veggie friendly items, so if that's your bag, they've got your number. Just keep in mind that it's cash only. And there you have it.

If you're Vegan or Vegetarian & you're looking for a healthy fast food, look elsewhere. The healthiest part about this place is the fact that the food is so below average that you probably won't finish more than half of your order.

The burger may have been one of the worst veggie burgers I've ever had. Too dry & chewy, I doubt there's enough condiments that could make it edible.

After the nasty burger I was looking forward to diving into the chili. With very little chili spice, it was more like beans with tomato sauce. Maybe even a bigger disappointment than the burger since I was looking forward to the chili more.

The lone saving grace of the place is their "air baked" fries. So crisp & yummy that we were both questioning "how do they do it?"

It's also cash only. Not normally a big deal to me since a trip to the ATM isn't a big deal if the food is worth it. They don't need to incorporate a credit card machine to earn my business. They need to have better food. The only reason I would have to return here would be for the fries then going somewhere else for the rest of my meal. At that point, why bother?

my favorite holiday is thanksgiving. four days off in a row, lots of football (including UVA vs. VA Tech - GO HOOS!), all of your family and closest friends, and naturally, the food. mac and cheese, mashed potatoes, stuffing, pumpkin pie; they're all winners, but pale in comparison to the star of thanksgiving - the turkey. i mean, we call it "turkey day," for crying out loud. according to the USDA, more than 45 million turkeys are cooked and eaten on thanksgiving. that's a lotta turkey.

well if like me, you desire turkey more than once a year, fear not! for delicious turkeys are being freshly roasted and carved every day by smart alec's' chefs. forget the slimy deli slices of your past and come here to embrace the thick-cut, tender, and juicy cuts that smart alec's offers. they use it to top salads and serve it with cranberry mayo in a sandwich that's thanksgiving personified (sandwich-ified?). 

there's nothing like the warmth and comfort of thanksgiving, but when it's just the eats you're jonesing for, check out smart alec's roasted turkey.

Im from Socal, so this obviously isn't "as good as it gets," lol but it''s fast, cheap, tasty, and just really good food when ur drunk. They should totally start having carne asada fries then place would be freaken AAmaazinggg

La Burrita, without a doubt, was my favorite "I only have 5 dollars to eat today because I spent all my money on books and readers" restaurant when I went to Cal. I don't know why, but there's something strangely fulfilling about devouring two enchiladas, guacamole, sour cream, beans and rice. 

A hop and skip from anywhere on the southside, La Burrita is a stable of the Cal student diet.

Truly a food staple if you are a Berkeley student looking for cheap eats.  While not gourmet on any level, this satisfies much desire in terms of quantity and availability.  This place is open well into the AM hours, so come grab your drunk munchies.  It's also situated in a very accessible location for students on the Southside.  Best of all its cheap.  Four dollars and change can get you a huge burrido that will raise your blood pressure and put you into a food coma.  I've tried most of their meats and I would have to say asada is still king.

PROTIP:  The one on northside gives you free (unlimited) chips.

Acceptable reasons to eat at La Burrita:
-You're drunk
-You're really hungry
-You're really drunk

If you are going to eat here, go with the pollo asada super burrito or wet  burrito.

Coming from a predominantly Hispanic hometown, I find it hard to swallow the blandness of Berkeley's Mexican food choices, but at least for the price, location, and speed, it's hard to find much better near campus without traveling far far away.

It's not totally unusual to walk right in and pay for your food (with credit card as a bonus!) and then be out and scarfing down a generously sized burrito in under 5 minutes here, but you can tell that most of the ingredients have been sitting out and mellowing for a while, especially the meats. Nothing here tastes particularly fresh or authentically Mexican. 

The one highlight of La Burrita is their unlimited salsa bar, which actually introduces some much-needed flavor, especially if you like the spicier salsas. The free chips that come with their burritos are nothing to rave about, but I like it because most of my friends give me their chips and that's just more food for me!
