As a corollary to that, skip the nachos here. They microwave them and the chips are just not durable enough to stand up to the heat and the soggy toppings they put on top.

Tip: if you want your meat grilled, order something with fajitas and it comes with some tasty grilled meat that hasn't been sitting premade in a pan. The only downfall is this is a bit pricier and takes a LOT longer to cook.

I would give it a lower star rating, but it's late night status fed my nocturnal ass my first year in Berkeley. Everything sucks and is pretty gross aside from the Nachos. Those are okay. No, wait, it still sucks. It just sucks less. Still, it was good to have another alternative to Top Dog in the AM.

Best burrito in Berkeley!  My personal favorite is the La Burrita Special with carne asada.  Unlike the regular burritos that come with rice, beans, and salsa along with your meat, the Special comes with sour cream and guacamole.  The Wet Burrito is another fave, although you can't really eat it while walking to class because they cover it in sauce and melted cheese.  They also have the best chips that I think they make themselves.  Perfectly crispy and salted!  My roommate and I used to ask for a little more, and they would gladly give it to us.  They go perfectly with their super fresh pico de gallo.  If you are a Berkeley student, this is a must try!
great place small but great if ur near the campus or telagraph area an want mexican food this is it fast service gbreat people an best of all great food love rthe carne asada burritos

I'm from San Diego and occasionally stop by Mexico to get myself some good bean, rice, and cheese burrito-eating. (My favorite.) I feel like I've definitely had better.

I'll definitely give this place another shot. Maybe something off their meat section is better.

LA BURRITA....is there when Chipotle just isn't satisfying.

Great food with cheap prices. What more could you ask for? Wait for it.... Fast service AND FREE chips!! It just gets my Asian senses tingling...

If you order the chicken or carne asada burrito, you can be in and out in just FIVE MINUTES when they aren't very busy.

The food is great and there's a large selection (including seafood, plates, etc.). The salsa bar isn't too shabby either...not as many options as Cancun but if you're in a hurry, it's probably best that there aren't so many options.

Anyways, the SHRIMP burrito is AMAZING! They make it fresh with large whole shrimp. NOM NOM NOM. Perfect for those times when I have seafood cravings.

On a final note, there is one downside, no UNLIMITED chips which they have at the La Burrita on northside...but they still give you a decent amount. And also the seating is limited.

Two main things about La Burrita to recommend it are that it is reasonably cheap and it stays open late.  It's not always bad, but it's not especially good either.  It's the kind of place you go because you have a hunger for some Mexican food, but then you eat it and it doesn't fill that craving since it's not even good or satisfying.  It's better than Taco Bell, but that's not a huge recommendation.

Most of the time I thought the one on the north side of campus was better than this location, but even then it was very inconsistent in taste and quality.

Of the Mexican places I've eaten La Burrita falls into the bottom 20%.  The bay area seems to have a glut of mediocre burrito shops like this, but even for the low Bay Area burrito shop standard it doesn't excel.  It's about the same, maybe slightly worse than the rest.

Once again, if you're up late and need to eat. This is also the place to be. The food is good. The food is fast and if you happen to be waiting outside, you might be solicited for some coin that will be accompanied by a dance move or two. 

This place has good burritos and quesadillas. If you're brave, try to do both. 

But of course, all else fails, go to Top Dog. Right next door!

La Burrita (aka La Bo) is a quick mexican restaurant that is open late. The food could use some more spices to give it a little kick, but for the price it's nothing to complain about. The carne asada super nachos are my favorite! Definitely the place to be if you're drunk and it's 2am and want some mexican food.

im giving it 4 stars: cheap, fast, open late, pretty yummy

my friend andrew LOVES the wet burritos. i have fond memories of late college nights, starving and crawling our way to la burrita. and besides the already cheap prices, get the guide to the good life coupons! sucha steal!

i prefer mario's la fiesta on telegraph, but la burrita is faster, cheaper and open much later. also there are a bunch of vegetarian selections. the portions are nice and the people are friendly. it is also more authentic than chipotle, i mean... chipotle? come on!

this is my favorite mexican restaurant.  really cheap and i think authentic tasting.  i really like their chips too.  i would much rather eat here than chipotle.  food comes out really quickly too.  i would recommend getting it to go cuz they don't have a lot of seating, but if you really wanted to eat there, it's not bad either.
affordable (5-6 bucks per burrito), yummy, quick.  decent food at ok price earns them 4 pts.  much healthier than eating fast foods like mcd or jack in the box!  i wished they had one in south bay...

Four stars for BIG tacos, baby. Not the best, but definitely the BIGGEST, and that counts for SOMETHING...especially when I'm starving and only have two bucks. Plus free chips and a good salsa bar. Eat at La Burrita. I would be starving without them.

Even though I know that they're microwaving my chicken and putting my burrito together with hands they might not have washed, I'm still strangely compelled to go back, I think it's cuz it tastes so good :-)

Thank you Campuscred for the voucher this semester. You make this poor college girl studying for finals happy this week.

Tried their cheesesteak burrito for the first time ever. This is a genius burrito. Ooey gooey cheese and beef plus generous portions of salsa, guac, and sour cream?? Bad for the heart but good for the tummy! My favorite part of the burrito was actually the grilled onions...lightly caramelized, soft but still had a bite to them. And all you can eat salsa bar. Nom.

With my voucher ($10) I was able to get 2 small cheesesteak burritos (one for me and one for the roomie) and 1 horchata for only $2.95. And I had a bunch of credit from Campuscred to get the voucher so this meal was almost free. 

Atmosphere:
I never really eat here cos there's barely any room and my apt is just up the street. Definitely a place to go for a quick meal if you're in a hurry. 

Service:
The cashier was really nice and just had me write my name and voucher # down on a pad of paper since they didn't have the list of coupon redeemers printed out. I got my food in less than 10 mins.
Used to my favorite mexican joints to hit up in berekeley.  Cheesecake burrito was awesome and the option for their wet burritos are also pretty money.  I definitely also recommend the nachos.

Been craving a burrito ever since my hangover two days ago (I know, personal information that no one really needs to know) and heard much about La Burrita being excellent. I finally went, so excited to see what was in store for me. I ordered the Wet Burrito, which is a burrito with guacamole, enchilada sauce, and sour cream doused over it. It comes with a side of chips in the box, which is nice. Finished it all in about less than 15 minutes, which is rather fast for me.

Well, the burrito was okay. Since I was very hungry and ate the food pretty fast, I didn't focus too much on individual ingredients. Just take my word for it and believe that there are better burrito places than La Burrita. I'm sorry to not love it like a bunch of other people do, but this is my take on it. I personally like Pancho's in Asian Ghetto way better than here. I'm glad to have given La Burrita a try, but I won't be a frequent customer. I appreciated the kind service though. 

Oh, and one note: THEY ACCEPT DEBIT/CREDIT CARDS! :) However, there is a $0.30 charge if not using cash.

I've been coming here for over 10yrs, and I've NEVER been disappointed. Awesome quality for "fast-style" Mexican on the go. They don't have much of a seating area. I love the open Salsa Bar - def got to check out the green verde sauce it the bomb!! I'm a pescetarian, so my review is somewhat biased towards the non-meat options. 

Heres a list of a few of my FAV'S @ La Burrita:
Very Veggie Burrito
Shrimp Burrito
Fish Tacos 
Wet Burrito
Cheese Enchiladas
Vegetarian Tamali Plate
Avocado Salad

BEST THING about La Burrita is they are open LATE! I think till 2 or 3am, the best late night grindz you'll find [even better than the taco truck!] :)
i had the chicken fajita plate and the salt level was too much to handle - just too much salt in the beans and chicken.  food would have been much tastier with less salt.

This isn't the best Mexican food your going to eat in your life. But by god, its the only one open until 1:30 in the morning that doesn't suck. The salsa bar is fantastic. The shrimp burrito is delicious, and the quesadillas (though oily and heart-attack inducing) are great.

Cheap! this place has a good salsa bar, cheap burrito's, and some tasty meat. There is not much room so don't roll looking to eat there. 

Burritos for cheap. respect

This is the quintessential cheap, college, Mexican place. Its open until 2am each night. Though I enjoy a La Burrita at any time or the day or night there's nothing quite like showing up at midnight on a Thursday night when school is in. Since its located right below the fraternities you get lots of drunk frat boys and sorority girls showing up. Quite hilarious. 

My favorite burrito is the large, ground beef burrito on the yellow chipotle tortilla. Its a nice creamy mixture of beans, beef, guacamole, and sour cream.

It is nice to see a place that offers small or large burritos to suit different appetites (and lunch budgets). But everything else about this place sucks. I had to tell the cashier my order three times, and not because he couldn't understand me. He simply wasn't listening. After my first attempt to order, he said, "what," and then began talking to the other employee just as I started to repeat my order. And even the third time I don't think he was listening. In any case, my burrito arrived with black beans (I ordered pinto) and lots of lettuce (I asked three times for them to hold the lettuce). I got my food to go and I was too lazy to go back to have them fix it, but I will never, ever go back. PS: The chips were soggy with grease. Yuck.
If you want bland crappy burritos come here.  the salsa actually isn't half bad and they have all you can eat chips at the Euclid location only.

I really like the chesesteak burrito. They have an open salsa bar which is great too. Furthermore, they make the order right in front of you. They also get to your name if you go there enough and their plates are underrated in my opinion.


Could open a larger place for more seating and maybe a breakfast.

We grabbed a quick bite here before our marathon movie experience at the Berkeley Pacific Film Archive.  It was cheap and fast, two of my requirements at the moment.  Next time I will probably opt for Top Dog next door instead.

Now that I think about it, the main reason I really like this place is because of their salsas. I really don't know what the food tastes like because I just drown every bite in either the spicy verde or the roja. 

Although I did get the philly cheese steak burrito once and that was pretty unique. I'm a fan of the gimmicky food, like CPK's cheeseburger pizza.

But seriously, the salsa.
THE BEST carne asada burrito you will EVER have.

Fast mexican food. Very tasty. Usually only go here after a night of going out in Berkeley but have occasionally had it for lunch as well. I recommend the pollo asado chicken burrito, hold the rice. The wet burrito and enchiladas are good too!

The shredded chicken isn't great here.

Expected bill: $5

My most frequently visited -- if not favorite -- burrito joint in Berkeley. It's cheap, quick, and quality.

I always get the vegetarian burrito. Vegetarian burritos are pretty hit or miss. Some come with wayyyy too much vegetables than I'd prefer (it IS a burrito, after all -- I'm not expecting anything fancy or healthy here), while others leave me wanting a bit more than the standard beans, cheese and rice combo. La Burrita's veggie burrito is served with just the right proportion of pinto beans, rice, cheese and lettuce mix. The small is just the right size for a person who's used to sharing her food (i.e., eat half and save half for later), but yesterday I bought one and ate the entire thing in one sitting. It also comes with free (but not unlimited) chips, something I've been spoiled with after living in Davis and taking advantage of the tortilla chips bin at Guadalajara's. 

Overall, this is definitely a place to stop by if you're craving a quick bite and are shopping/exploring the Telegraph area. I usually stop by during my lunch (noon or one) and I've never faced a long line. The place is small and seating is limited, though. If you're planning on going out of your way and drive here, don't. It's Berkeley, and it's Telegraph. Parking generally sucks.

EDIT: 
After two years of trying places, I've decided that La Burrita has the best nachos in South Berkeley - Large quantity, generous toppings, consistently pleasing. 

---
There's a fierce battle between Chipotle sheep and La Burrita freaks as to which is the better choice. I side with Chipotle because I'd rather have a free soda than a free bag of chips, I like my burritos thick rather than lanky, and I like the option of having it double wrapped because why have one tortilla when you can have two. 

The La burrita burritos are also unnecessarily wet, so you get sauce everywhere. 

What it does have going for it is the fact that it actually has a complete menu, so there's lots to try.

Salsa! I love their salsa! If they didn't have their special house salsa, I wouldn't think this place was so special. I could take shots of their salsa. Perhaps it's just a personal taste thing, but I love how their salsa is fresh, not too spicey, just the right amount of cilantro, and a tad peppery. Love it! I eat their burritos for their salsa. Now, if only they had larger plastic salsa containers, instead of killing the environment by making people like me use 10 of those containers to fill the salsa.

This is one of those places where I don't think I could provide a sober review. Why you wonder. Well because out of the dozen times I've been here, I have been plastered after a night out on Telegraph. However, it always served it's purpose and it's an oasis after a full night out.

So I am no longer in the target market for La Burrita...that being college students.  When I was a student though I would give this place probably three stars.  On the plus side it is open till 2am and it is full then too.  The food is not that great.  I do like their enchiladas, but other than that none of the food is really that good at all.  They make most of it in the microwave.  I use to feel a little sick sometimes after eating there too.  If you have a car, jump in that and go down college ave to the burrito shop or any of the other great taquerias in Berkeley.

I don't know what kinda food you've all been getting there that deserves anything more than a sad face and two thumbs down.

I've only eaten here twice, and both times I didn't finish my food. It wasn't good, the beans tasted like they were burnt in the pot, and the rice was super dry. I didn't care for the meat, wait, was that meat, I couldn't tell. 

To be absolutely honest, I'd rather save myself a few dollars and hit the Taco Bell drive through if it came down to eating some kind of horrible mexican food.
decent carne asada burrito. i ate here mainly b/c it was close to my house.

I went here for the first time tonight.  It was the only Mexican place open after 11.  We ordered the super nachos with chicken, but took them to go, so they were a bit soggy after 15 minutes in the car.  The horchata was delicious and the service was fast.  I will definitely come back here for my late night cravings.

Got two carne asada tacos.  Surprisingly, the carne asada didn't taste like that classic smokey, soft, slightly chewy, juicy taste.  I was pretty sad.  The rest of the ingredients were pretty cool with me.  ~$2.50 per taco.

The complimentary chips that come with the meal was a big plus.  The chips were very crisp and warm.  The jalapeno salsa is extremely spicy but so damn good!

Lastly, the horchata was not great, but not bad.  It lacked the cinnamon-y taste and was a tad too sweet.  Oh well!  A large was about $2.

Burritos are pretty good here! I like Northside's La Burrita better though because they give you a basket for chips and you can serve yourself with unlimited hot ones! Combine that with their salsa and you'll be hooked! Try mixing the salsas too. Food usually comes out really quickly here, and everything is quite cheap.

I'm sort of a hard sell because LA has some good hole in the wall Mexican restaurants. I went to Cal for 4 years so I was a regular here at La Burrita. Compared to other Northern California hole in the wall, this was pretty good, but compared to Southern California Mexican, this was sub-par.

The Carne Asada burrito is the staple here and it is pretty good. They give a side of chips which are good most of the time, but occasionally they come out stale. What I did like was they had a decent salsa bar, but nothing like the salsa bars at your Americanized Mexican places like Baja Fresh and Poquito Mas.

The selection of meat isn't very diverse; they didn't have pastor which is a killer for me. 

You can't really eat in the restaurant itself; it's tiny, noisy and hot.

Oh, "La Boo", you aren't even authentic Mexican food! I just don't come here anymore because after trying everything on the menu, I can only be satisfied by the vegetarian burrito because it doesn't taste nasty or greasy. I wouldn't come here craving for Mexican food, but I'd come here to satisfy some munchies because it tastes so heavy.

Everything here is just a step above Taco Bell / Del Taco food, but it's open late and it's "relatively" cheap ($3-$5) so it's a favorite for the college crowd.

If anything, I'd recommend their super nachos because they give you lots of food. Good enough to share with two people or if you are particularly drunk. Look elsewhere for authentic cuisine, but look here for convenience and munchies. They accept credit cards, which is a bonus.

I went to La Burrita because my friends that went to CAL said it was delicious and the burritos were huge and the super nachos were awesome, etc, etc.

I went, ordered the bean & cheese burrito (it's what I always order) and it was alright. I felt like it tasted just like any other burrito (a lot like Hugo's in LA). The chips were delicious, I will say. The salsa selection was good too, but it was all the way in the back right next to the soda dispenser and there was a table right smack dab there too (kind of awkward to get to)

There is very little seating inside and outside there were 3 tables, none with an umbrella, so if it's full inside, raining or super sunny, nature will attack you.

This isn't legit mexican food at all and if you really want fake mexican food, just go to chipotle.  I had the large sized carne asada burrito and when I got it all i could think of was "if this is a large then the small must be tiny!"  Anyways, the burrito itself lacks in girth and the ingredients are compartmentalized and don't blend well at all.  The salsa bar is above average and the horchata does taste like, well, horchata.  All in all, I'll have to keep looking for authentic mexican food because La Burrita simply doesn't cut it.

I heard about this place before I ever moved to Berkeley, friends kept telling me I HAD to try this place! so I did and I was totally hooked after the first bite. Been 3 years since then and I am still a faithful patron of La Burrita...don't even care that Chipotle is around the corner! La Burrita has always been for me when I need a late night study break, or when I'm stumbling drunk down Durant at 1am and they're the only place still open. Their shredded chicken burrito will always hit the spot. And also, I have good reason to believe it prevents hangovers. =)

Generic Mexican food, but if you're carless, it's a pretty good option. If you have a car, visit Picante or Juan's instead.

The cooks are very friendly and love it if you try to order in Spanish (even if you fail miserably).

The people working here are pretty nice but the food sometimes takes a while. The cheesesteak burrito is very yummy! I once got a enchilada combo and it wasn't hot, so I had a feeling it wasn't as fresh? 

Either way, this is good for a late night snack and a place that all Cal students should eat at in their time there. There's not much seating inside, but good thing is it's near campus, so there's always someplace to sit and eat lol

This is the real La Burrita (take that, North Side La Burrita!).  I always get the pollo asado burrito and am never disappointed.  I'm sure it's not super authentic Mexican food but there must be crack or something in the burritos, because I love them.  They're cheap and the large burrito could be 1.5 meals.  

I also highly recommend them as a drunk food.  Way better than Blondie's.

There are probably a lot of mixed reviews on this place but I can't seem to get enough of it. I love the carne asada wet burrito in its sloppy yumminess. How can you go wrong with a meal in the bay that costs less than $10, is served hot and quick, and is finger-licking good? I know, it sounds like I'm stealing from KFC's ad campaign and I am with this catch: the food here actually lives up to that.

My favorite activity in Berkeley was to get hammered and pick up a super burrito from La Burrita on the walk home....

I miss their burritos so much! And no, they weren't amazing just because I was drunk. I had them many times sober too and it is just as fantastic. It is definitely the best burrito place in Berkeley, so if you're a student and didn't hit this spot up yet, you're missing out!

I knew I was in trouble the moment I noticed it had won 'best burrito' from the Daily Cal, something like 10 years in a row. Call me a cynic, but students have no taste. Same thing happens in every college town, the restaurants right next to campus get all the foot traffic, and somehow all the rave reviews, no matter how much they suck. 

La Burrita is a prime example of this phenomenon, it's a stones throw from campus (even for someone with a weak arm like me), and as a consequence it's always busy. That doesn't mean it's good, because it isn't. The food lacks the wonderful cohesiveness that good Mexican usually has. The flavours in a good burrito meld together into a wonderful whole, at La Burrita, they just kinda sit there blandly. Good Mexican has a wide array of textures, all interacting, La Burrita, its all kinda chewy. 

I guess the moral of this story is always eat where the locals eat, never where the students eat.

Pretty solid place for when you need a mexican food fix in the bay area. I usually get the super nachos, which are delicious, but I've gotten the la burrita special with carne asada before, and it's pretty good, not amazing or the best burrito I've ever had, but good enough. 

Also,it's open late, until 3am on the weekends, which is awesome and delicious when you're on the way back from bars/wherever. Overall, if you're really craving mexican food, especially late at night/while drunk, then labo is the way to go.

First thing you should do when you come here is look at the sign. It reads, "La Burrita: Fine Mexican Food," or something like it. Notice that there's no mention of the place being a taqueria. That should set off an alarm immediately.

I'm a masochist, so I tried one of their steak tacos anyway. It was the sloppiest endeavour ever -- it was more like a burrito, but without enough tortilla to wrap it. Their chips are mediocre, although their salsa is passable. If you're going to eat here, their burritos are the safe bet.

Anyone who thinks this place has 'the best burrito ever' needs to go to SoCal or even the Mission District in San Francisco. The only two things this place has going for them are its late hours and its reasonable pricing (~$5 for a burrito).

This is another late night favorite 

and too lazy to walk to much further down 
I love these buritas
especially the muy caliente green chili salsa 

Note 5 star is based on limited options and limited time frame 
Also good alternative to Top Dog

The chips are nice and oily when you're in the mood for that, but the one time I ordered a burrito the cheese was all gross and watery.  Never been back, but the smell outside when walking up Durant sometimes tempts me...

One of the restaurants I miss most from my college days. Where else can you get a shrimp burrito for less than seven bucks? There's also complimentary chips and salsa. Plus there is a cute patio dining area in the back, good for sunny days.

La Burrita gets the job done.  That is, if you're hungry at midnight, and it's Monday or Tuesday, which means Late Night at Crossroads is closed.  The burritos are damn cheap.  I mean you can't get a more filling burrito for $5.00 than La Burrita.  There have been many nights where I'm just craving a burrito and I go straight to La Burrita.  I normally just get the La Burrita Special because you get both the sour cream and guacamole.  

But you get what you pay for.  Unless you're absolutely hungry, I would just wait until morning to eat.  Upon further inspection of the burrito, it looks like globs of industrialized food wrapped in a tortilla in foil.  It taste really good when you're hungry and less so when you're not.  

I think I'm reaching a point in my life where I can afford to eat healthier and higher quality foods than burritos.  But if I'm hungry and it's midnight, I know where I can turn to fill my tummy.

I've had better burritos. I've eaten here about three times and I'd just like to say that the only thing that has saved this place is how cheap it is (thank you randomly mailed book of coupons). 

The food is average and isn't horrible. I actually like Chipotle better, which is definitely not an insult in the sense that Chipotle is crappy (hey I actually love Chipotle) but an insult in the sense that the Daily Cal rated La Burrita the Best Burrito in Berkeley and that Chiptole is a chain that serves American-Mexican. 

At least it's open late and is served quickly.

I've seen it written here before, and it is true! Skip the rest of the menu and go straight for the fajita burritos! They cost a little more than the others, but they are the freshest burritos you can get (and perhaps even a little healthy!) I'm a fan of the chicken fajita burrito - freshly-grilled chicken, onions and peppers, with a bit of guac and sour cream if you like! 

Most of the negative comments refer to the meat/fixins that've been sitting around hours - what can you expect? Go fresh! Be happy!

Salsa bar is great!

Only drawback is that sometimes the quality slips. By far most of the time I am super pleased! Enjoy!
MMM la burrita.  open late (3ish) with delicious chips & salsa, and cheap, quick service. can't go wrong.

You should only eat here if it is late at night and you have the desperate munchies.  Otherwise, it is pretty gross.  The only thing I can tolerate here is the nachos (but have them hold the beans-- trust me HAHA).


EDIT:
Okay, the chicken quesadillas are legit late-night food.
Tasty, and cheap.  I'm not a burrito fan, but I like to get an enchilada a la carte and a soda.  Under $5 and more than enough food.  They don't skimp on the meat here.

I'm a fan.

I've been here twice. I've gotten the beef quesadilla and the philly cheesesteak burrito. Both were clutch. Very tasty and filling. 

Open late, too ;) Probably why I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 3.
Super nachos with beef after battling an all day hangover = NOMNOMNOMNOM to the billionth degree!

My friend and I went to see Weezer a few months ago, but before we did, he suggested we stop by La Burrita for dinner.

The place isn't exactly spacious, but that isn't a problem. I order a steak burrito with a bunch of alterations that I can't really remember. I do remember that they got my order right, which was impressive since so many places forget to incorporate my alterations into the order. The burrito was big and filling, but definitely not the best burrito I've ever had. But it was cheap, so that made me happy.

It has a pretty impressive salsa bar, but I didn't get to try anything.

Get their Philly Cheese Steak Burrito, sounds funky, but it's really tasty.  Then grab a dog at top dog next store.  After that go to Henry's on Tuesdays and get yourself some cheap drinks!  Bargain central!  BUT if you're looking for authentic mexican fodd, this is not the place.

La Burrita kept me alive Freshman Year with its late night hours. So for that, I love this place. 
If you're ever in dire need of good Mexican to-go, La Burrita is the place to go. I can proudly say that I have eaten half the stuff on the menu and most of it is pretty good. I recommend the super nachos because it comes with everything! Really, everything.
Simply put, good place to eat before you get drunk or the morning after. A lifesaver, if you will.

I ordered a couple of burritos here, and they've never impressed me. The individual flavors of the ingredients don't really stand out. It would probably taste much better with a decent salsa, but everytime I go there, the salsas are sour. 

Still, this place is way better than Chipotle (I hate that place). And it's open late, which is frustratingly rare around this area.

Unless you can eat a lot, like more than a chipotle burrito, go for the small.

I had the carne asada burrito, and it was delicious. The flavors aren't too overpowering, so that's a plus. It doesn't get sickening like Chipotle does after a while. The meat's nice and soft, and the guacamole and sour cream they add is great. The salsa they have goes great with the chips they provide with each order. I usually only get a little bit, but I couldn't keep myself from getting up and refilling my cup of salsa.

And the burrito looks skinny, but it's very, very filling. And a good price too!

La Burrita is for poor college students - cheap food, convenient location, and students' tastebuds aren't usually refined until they graduate and start earning the big bucks.

That being said, I went to La Burrita when I was a student at Cal. I didn't like it back then, and I still don't like it now. The food is bland, the rice is too ketchuppy, and their menu is so generic.

For latino fare, I much prefer Juan's Place or Tacubaya, but they are too far away and expensive for most students. So, kids, study hard so that you can afford better food in the future. And coerce your parents into taking you to Chez Panisse for your graduation dinner. ;)

wasn't that hungry so i decided to try the taco salad with grilled vegetables. 

the good:
everything tasted fresh
lots of toppings 
overall salad was decently big
couldn't resist visiting the salsa bar - added more of their tasty salsa on top of my salad (it came with pico de gallo)

the not so good:
usually if cheese, sour cream, etc are listed as toppings on a taco salad, the menu will list guacamole if it's included.  i hate guacamole (leave me alone, i just do, okay!) so i was sad when my food had a bunch dumped on top. oh well - next time i'll ask.

still tasty overall and definitely would return!

I picked up a beef burrito here for about six dollars and I have never seen a smaller burrito.  The burrito was pathetically small for the price and the bag it came with was literally half filled with tortilla chips.  I didn't pay for tortilla chips, I paid for a burrito.  Whats even worse is that the burrito tasted exactly like a taco bell burrito  and had didn't have the authentic Mexican flavor I was looking for.  If you want something that taste like Taco Bell, go to Taco Bell instead for a fraction of the price.  Very disappointing.

Great Mexican food near campus with fair prices while on a college budget. Popular hangout for drunk/stoned coeds in the late hours.

Their burritos and super nachos are the best thing to cure pretty much any college emotion imaginable. 

Just won the Big Game? Let's go to La Burrita!
Just lost to USC, again!!!??? Let's go to La Burrita!
Have a final tomorrow and can't study anymore? Let's go to La Burrita!
GF dumped me. Let's go to La Burrita!
Just ate at La Burrita. Let's go to La Burrita! Again!

The food is some of the best Nor Cal Mex food I have had and the service is always friendly. 

Overall: If you go to UCB you will eventually go here. If you are not a student, you should try it!

Quite simply: eh. 

I usually begin reviews with at least a little bit of floral language to set the tone.  But I feel the above is more symbolically fitting. La Burrita is the essence of straight-to-the-point food. Painfully one dimensional, it is college grub at its most fundamental. 

The steak, in the grand tradition of carne asada, is springy and modular, like little hunks of brown eraser, the beans are beans, and the rice is generally pretty soggy. All of it, drowned in exorbitant quantities of cheese and sauce.  I hate to sound like "that" guy, but having hailed from SoCal, let's just say it is unjustifiably liberal to call this stuff Mexican food.

Re-examining things, maybe I'm being intentionally hateful. I mean, for all the shit this place gets (and gives), it's still here, outliving countless other stores. Plus, anyone who's even taken a step on south side is familiar with the frustratingly out-the-door lines all day, every day. So something's gotta give, right? 

Yes.

That something? Drugs. What's being given? A gross profit. I realize none of those words are contextually accurate, but it was funny in my head so whatever.

At 1 in the morning, loopy headed, I will admit nothing sounds better than a wet burrito, quite frankly because few things come as packed to the brim with so many different ingredients at such a low overhead cost. So we can, at the very least, agree that on a calorie-to-cent basis, not much has LB beat. 

But is there anything really worth eating here when not tripping major balls? Surprisingly, the lengua that seems to be the perpetual daily special (which begs so many questions) isn't bad. Stewed tongue is the embodiment of beefy flavor, and has a tender, stewed texture to boot. Some people consider it unpalatable, but some people are bastards. And for just over three bucks for a bagful of chips and a large corn tortilla stuffed to the brim with soft, flavorful meat, it's no shabby deal.

So there's La Burrita. Basically nothing I have said above hasn't been heard a hundred thousand times over. It's pretty shitty. We know. It's cost effective. We know. It's not real Mexican food. We know. In the end, I suppose this spiel is just one big promotion for beef tongue. I guess that's something to La Burrita's credit.
Sorry guys but this is gonna be the worst review I ever written but STRAIGHT UP, five stars for its memories. Thanks La Burrita.

Haven't been here in a long, long time, so things might be different now.

The food here is just all right, but they were one of the few late night options other than Top Dog next door.  Their regular burritos are nothing spectacular...the meat was a bit dry for my taste.  Their wet burrito (sounds so wrong) wasn't bad...different having all those unhealthy toppings slathered on top instead of inside the burrito.  Tacos were average...nothing to specify as something that stands out or sucks.  Plus points for their little salsa bar though.

If it were closer, I would definitely go to Gordo's.  But considering the other lack of options (especially late at night) and the decent portions to complement their student-friendly prices, certainly not a terrible way to satisfy those post drinking food urges.
LOVE this place!!! I could seriously live off of their bean & cheese burritos. I am vegetarian and their veggie burritos are great also. My bf loves the chicken burrito and tacos.

I LOVE this place! Really good food. CHEAP, GOOD, AUTHENTIC, HEARTY. 

You've go to try the WET BURRITO. The Large is only $5.99! And its huge! It actually looks more appealing than in that picture above. 

It's got everything, the burrito, enchilada sauce, cheese, guacamole, sour cream. Yummmmmerz.....

Go and check this place out.... no frillz.... just really good and inexpensive food! =D

I would give 4.5 stars for my fussiness, but Yelp has yet to get to the half-point system. Bummerrrrr.

This is about a burrito that was born in April 2009. 
It wedged itself into my mouth, feisty and humongous after an almost 2 hilly mile nonstop trek around the Berkeley campus (+ walk to the rose garden). 
And my taste buds got up and started a Burning Man dance around the fire that the rice started. 

The world was so beautiful in the half hour after the burrito goodness digested. 

So I was dying, starving, and any food would taste great, one would think? And I wasn't used to good burritos, being an East Coaster? If you call me out on all this, I'm going to be critical here:

The place was slightly greasy, but it's a neighborhood place, what DO you expect? There was a good number of people when it was between main meal hours (good sign), and it's been around for a while. The burrito itself was moist, but who wants a dry burrito? It was the perfect size and had a fabulous ratio of rice, beans, chicken, guac. The packaging was beautiful. Service was sweet and snappy. 

Could not have asked for more in a neighborhood eatery. Cheers!

La Burrita is possibly some of the worst Mexican food(if you could even call it that) i've ever had. I used to say that it was a late night bastion of cheese covered mediocrity, but that--i've come to realize-- is giving it way to much credit. In the case of La Burrita, in fact, it's almost an award. "Oh, but the nachos are so good" fans of this place will say when you cite the incontrovertible fact that their meat is reheated in microwaves and that the burritos are  nightmarish, tortilla encased slumber parties of guacamole and sour cream colored goop. I can't believe that the place is run Mexicans/Central Americans too. I would love to ask these guys if this is what they cook at home...if this is how Mom used to make it. I doubt it. It's a good thing that Berkeley has a constant supply of visitors and students who don't know a lick about good Mexican food, because this place would be out of business. You should only be so luck to be blacked out when your night of drinking Winner's Cup Vodka lands you at this haunt.

I ordered the tamale and cheese enchilada, and I'm thinking I ordered the wrong things.  The enchilada was like one big chunk of cheese rather than a nice blend of cheeses that were nice and melt-y.  There was very little sauce on top of that.  The tamale was dry.  The portion was good with beans and rice, but I don't think I'll be ordering either of these things if I come back here.

I like their crispy nachoes. They are just really fresh and good. If you have their burrito which is really affordable($3-5) they give you those tasty chips. The foods come out really fast so you don't need to worry so much. Also, you can get a drink for a dollar and refill it anytime you want (I mean, while you are eating). But don't forget that they only allow 2 people to share one drink.  Nice place :) 

Uhmm,.. well, the place is pretty small and has not enough seats.. This is kind of a thing that need to be fixed.

This is a great place to go for a late night snack, as it is open just as late as the bars! I wouldn't say the food is that extraordinary or anything. Basic Northern California Mexican food. But it's cheap, filling, convenient, and it comes with chips! The nachos are great for late night munchies!

Stopped by here once with a few friends and tried the shrimp burrito.

For the price, portion size is decent, nothing spectacular.

The quality of the food however was pretty good, the shrimp burrito was very good, the fruity pineapple salsa was very unique, sweet tangy and a great compliment to the grilled shrimp (probably not authentic, but good none-the-less). 

There was also complementary chips and salsa available. 

The service was quick, though the time we went was not too busy. 

Overall, the food is decent for a college burrito joint and a establishment that I will come back to when visiting friends at UC Berkeley.

i like that they cater to vegans, but honestly, that burrito was nothing to write home about. literally. the whole time i kept thinking about all the burritos i ate when i lived in southern california. the salsa bar and free chips were pretty exciting though.
Excellent seasoned ground beef burrito with the hot tomatilla salsa (the thicker spicier one of the two tomatilla sauces) is a flavor bomb! Open until 1:30am on weekdays! Across from King Pin Donuts.

I'd give this place a 3.5 but yelp doesn't have half-star options..
So anyway...
I lived in the units during my freshman year and having come straight from so cal, I used to hate this place that and that it was a sorry excuse for Mexican food.. but after being in Berkeley for 3 years.. I guess I've been brainwashed by the lack of good Mexican food -ness of Berkeley but I find this place OK. 
The food is OK, but nothing amazing. The reason that I give it 4 stars is because this place is open late (which is very important for a college student like myself and even more so if they are a night owl) and because you can usually find really good coupons in guide to good life in berkeley or any of the other whatever coupon things that come through various sources that you can get your hands on in Berkeley.
It is fairly cheap if the coupons are used and can get you filled up for not too much money (again, important for starving college students)
If it were only food, I would give it 3/5 but the late night open thing and good bang for the buck gives it 5/5 which averages out to 4/5... or 3.5/5


but I would never go there without those coupons.. just an FYI

Food: Mostly delicious; burritos come with chips (get tons of salsa because the salsa is delicious and the chips taste like nothing)

Location: not much seating, but you should be able to sit as people eat quickly

Service: workers are okay

Wait Time: fast-food service, but not always super fast depending on your order

Price: Most (maybe all) items are under $9

Great for late night hunger, through the surrounding area doesn't always feel welcoming..

cheesesteak burrito - that's what i crave the most when i go here. great place for late night eating, especially when you've been out on the town. Definitely a favorite of mine while i was at Cal. great place to get your fill when you're hungry.

The food isn't really that great, especially compared to the much better Mexican food you can find down in Southern California where I'm from.
I appreciate the salsa bar though, and the plate is a good quantity for what you pay.
Wet burrito with ground beef I like somehow, even though you watch them microwave it to melt the cheese and ugh.

Pretty much everything tastes the same, and the meat can get greasy.
Would give 2 stars if it wasn't open so late, and a 1 if there were other, better Mexican fare around. But since it is, and since there aren't (and the food isn't terrible, or even bad), a 3 seems rightish for Berkeley. Lot of drunk people late at night though....

Not much space for seating at all, good luck, lol.

so my boyfriend and i went to this spot because it was close to top dog. his family wanted to try top dog, but i honestly didn't want to go there. so we chose la burita. big mistake. at first i was stoked to see they had carne asada nachos. but these were probably the worst i've ever had. their carne asada is tough and tasteless. their chips are ok. but this is just a big plate of grease! living in so cal, there's the best of the best of mexican food. but i'd had carne asada nachos that were cheaper than these, and didn't have so much grease. so why did i eat here? i heard they had a bunch of awards for being best mexican food in berkeley. what were these people thinking? it's really not that good. service is fast, though but it gets pretty crowded in there. i guess people like it here 'cause the prices are cheap, but i've had waaay better.

Went back to teh Berk for the Cal v. Tennessee game.  

Celebrated the win with a late night pollo asado burrito from a good old friend.  My relationship with La Burrita goes back to my freshman year at teh Berk, which has been a looong time.  I'm glad that with so much changing that there is still room for a place like LB.  I think it is exactly what the student population needs there.

The burrito itself was pretty much what i remembered.  Rice, beans, salsa, cheese and pollo asado.  Not a whole lot of places have pollo asado, which is why I like LB so much.  Most of the time when you ask for a chicken burrito, you get stewed and shredded meat.  I prefer the grilled texture and flavor of the asado.  Overall, it wasn't exactly like I remembered it, but then again it was a late night with TONS more people than I remembered.  Still a great deal!

Why such a low rating? This place packed with college students during lunch, dinner and late night hours.

Why? Because they are good if you stick with a couple of menu items.

What do I usually go for?
Cheesesteak Burrito. It usually takes a little longer to make but well worth it. A little on the greasy side so if you're on a diet, this burrito is not for you.
Carne Asada Burrito. Can't go wrong with this one at most burrito shops.
Shrimp. An abundance of shrimp in your mouth.

Chips included in your order of course. As much salsa as you want.

Good times.

shrimp burrito is tasty - generous portions of shrimp, grilled onions and bellpeppers with pineapple salsa. a little heavy on the sour cream though. was a little hesitant about this place at first because i am a mexican food snob. my friend noted all the "best of berkeley" accolades on the walls, but seriously - it aint like berkeley is a hotbed of mexican cuisine. the competition is slim! but its tasty - i put my stamp of approval on la burrita.

the other thing is the large burrito can be stretched into two meals. i always feel accomplished when i can stretch a meal into two bcuz it makes me feel 1) dainty and ladylike and 2) economical. and that's important.

had a small carne asada burrito. 

thumbs up:
offering the option of a more manageable size
carne asada (it is pretty hard to mess up)

thumbs down:
beans not cooked as well
rice too sticky
cheese an undiscernable mess
the included salsa subtracted from the overall taste

redeeming factor:
salsa bar

anyone who knows me knows i love the spice, and the brownish-reddish-peppery one (wish they had names i could refer to) had just the perfect amount of kick.

Unsanitary! I watched the cashier make my veggie burrito without even washing his hands. After I finished paying, I watched him make another burrito with his filthy, I-don't-wash-after-touching-cash hands. I gave my burrito to a homeless person, and I bought another lunch somewhere else.

This used to be an essential foodsource during freshman year and I still can't get enough!  Their burritos are cheap, big and pretty damn delicious.  Go with the special ones for a little bit more, the sour cream and guacamole make the burrito less dry.  Their wet burritos are also good too with a thin tangy enchilada sauce and lots of cheese.  I love their thin chips.  Their salsa could be better but it gets the job done.

It's not the best mexican food out there or even the most authentic but it's tasty enough for me.

If you really want unhealthy, go for the super nachos with ground beef.

Best Mexican food I've had after being drunk! :)

I usually go for their combo plate (taco, enchilada, tamale), which is decent...but tasted amazing after bar hopping after my 21st :P And this place is open quite late also! Otherwise, this is probably the 3rd place I'd consider for burritos (after Chipotle and Gordos...)

Otherwise, a decent Mexican food place that gives free chips and salsa with your meal that is close to campus

After a long day of walking in the city, we were famished college students. It was 12am and did not have too many options so we turned to La Burrita. I ordered the carne asada burrito, which cost only $4! I tried all of their salsas, and I have to say that the green salsa was the perfect compliment to my burrito. I added onions, lime, Tapatio (chipotle), and cilantro from home, and I was quiet for a good 5 minutes. 
It definitely wasn't the best burrito I ever had, but at midnight, when you are starved for sustenance, La Burrita will hit the spot. 

If I could give half stars, I would give this a 3.5.
great when i'm drunk, and that's the only time i go. so as far as i'm concerned it's great

Been coming here now  for years. A+++ I probably have to say the best Mex food in Berkeley. God bless this place for staying open past 3am. You can't go wrong with their steak we t burrito. Two thumbs way way up!

Why are people so down on La Burrita?? The baby burrito is simply to die for: awesome, fantastic.  I only get to enjoy La Burrita on an occasional basis, so maybe this is why I yearn for it so.  It is far better for a quick bite than Top Dog, which is good going down, but regrettable later.

there must be crack in this food.  I crave it like no other.  now that i can no longer eat the special chicken burrito for every meal, i feel a void in my heart. Its not persay the most fabulous culinary delight, but it's good substance that has magical powers to help you ace your midterms.

I had a small wet carne asada burrito (guacamole, sour cream, enchilada sauce). The steak was okay. Lots of sour cream. Was pleasantly surpised the burrito came with chips with melted cheese.. Good value for the price (less than $6 including tax.)

Came here to order a steak super burrito and was disappointed. Instead of receiving a steak burrito, the guy behind the counter gave me a bean burrito. Unlike other places where burritos with meat are more expensive, I was charged the price of a steak burrito despite getting a bean burrito. This trip was disappointing.

Another time I went, I tried to use a CampusCred voucher for $10 and the guy accidentally deducted only $5. It was a bit annoying that I had to assert that the voucher was for $10 a few times.

If you're reading the reviews for La Burrita, you will see that, Elaine L. who wrote a review today, same day as me, also had the unfortunate encounter with the same guy I dealt with and also ended up receiving a bean burrito........

WET BURRITO

i come from a small town and the closest think i knew about burritos before college was the local taco bell... imagine how lost i was when i first heard "WET BURRITO" 

wet burritos however have become my favorite. i'll admit its a bit weird eating a burrito with a knife and fork but it's well worth it to get that extra sauce and melted cheese that blankets the burrito. 

whether its an early lunch or a late night munch- La Burrita is the place to go. 

until next time

cheers!

Pretty darn good hangover food - especially since they`re open late. You can get a LOT for $7! The service is nice, the food is sometimes heart attack inducing, but maybe I`m just being paranoid. There`s little room though, even for standing.

This place has one of the best wet burrito in town.  Make sure you tell them to make it with both chicken and steak.  The price is really reasonable and it's right next to cal campus so there's always alot of hotties.

Holy ****! their shrimp burrito's are so awesome! The mix of salsa and sour cream makes such a great sauce that compliments the shrimp (obviously fresh from tasting it). And the free chips that came with it tasted great too!
i like this place a lot....the burritos are packed so tight! love that it's not messy. the salsas are awesome too!

Well as the name suggests this is a fast food mexican place complete with burritos, tacos, nachos and low prices. I had the super burrito which was good but I've had better. It's a cool place if your hungry after a night of partying or if you're on the go and need a quick bite.

If you're drunk enough to choose La Burrita over Top Dog, you should by all means help yourself to one of their burritos. I'm sure it'll taste delicious in all its wonderful greasiness.

Would I come here sober? No.

1 star for price, 1 star for the patio in the back, and 1 star for decent service.

Mmmm... La Burrita

Delicious juicy Carne Asada that is enough to fill me for hours...free chips...free salsa...fast service...GREAT prices...

The Carne Asada is so good I've gotten it about 90% of the times I've been here. I did try the wet burrito once and it was a little bit nasty, and too much for me to finish.

I don't know much about Mexican food, but I know La Burrita is delicious, and definitely worth it considering how cheap it is for the amount of food you are getting. What more can you ask for?

I'd rather go here than Chipotle (although Chipotle has its merits) because I'd rather have chips + salsa than soda.
You can't beat it walking home from Kips at 2:00 am.  In the afternoon, however...I've had better.  Go for the nachos.

I'm half-Mexican and was raised by my loud Mexican mother who happens to be a great authentic cook and quite a snob when it comes to Mexican food, which unfortunately was passed on to me. I'm always on the quest to find the perfect bean, rice, and cheese burrito with a homemade tortilla. (There is nothing worse than a burrito with store-bought Mission tortillas) That being said, La Burrita's tortillas fall into the store-bought category but the burrito is still delicious. The small size is perfect and the chips are bomb.

Not bad for Mexican fast food. The burritos are built perfectly for eating on the go: just peel back the foil and start chomping! No mess, clean hands, but a vicious garlic aftertaste. But hey, that's what tic-tacs are for right?

The price is right and they are quick to prepare your order. With a fully stocked salsa bar, there is something for everyone and for every application. I cringe every time I see them grab chips with their bare hands that they used to take money, but I'm still alive, so I won't complain.

This place is GREAT for satisfying those late-night hunger cravings. They're usually open until 1:30am on weekdays. I usually come here and order a steak quesadilla (with sour cream and guacamole, of course). I'm usually pleased with how my meal is prepared. The tortilla skin is crisp, the filling is warm, and the beef is pretty tender itself. I adore their tortilla chips because they're usually fresh. They have a killer salsa bar. A word of advice: if you're going to get salsa, usually you'll need 5 containers per meal because they go down pretty quickly. 

The restaurant is pretty small, however. It's easy to bump into people during crowded days. I remember being knocked over and spilling a container of salsa just by standing. There's another La Burrita on Northside, which also has unlimited refills on their tortilla chips. The Southside La Burrita also uses paper utensils if you're going to eat inside the restaurant. The Northside one uses non-disposable utensils for those dining in...

Haven't actually eaten at the restaurant, but us optometry students always order food from them when we have meetings and need to feed lots of hungry students for cheap. Even when we order over a hundred of burrito, they warm and each tightly wrapped. I've had their chicken, steak, veggie, and carnitas burrito. I like them all except the veggie. For some reason the veggie is always runny and the rice just tastes like ketchup rice. Pretty good chips and guacamole, their salsa is ok.

I don't know if I would ever crave their burrito enough to go eat at the restaurant, but I highly recommend getting catered by them for meetings.

Used to come only for cheap savory burritos in Berkeley with free chips, but later discovered their Wet Burrito. SUPER luscious, hearty, and crazy delicious. Try out their different tortillas - spinach, tomato, wheat - awesome! Skip out on the Chipotle on Telegraph, and check this place out!

this place is disgusting. 

if it's midnight and you find yourself hungry, walk 5 feet to top dog. don't punish your stomach by buying something at this place.

now i do realize that this place cater's to a very specific student demographic, but it still pains me to see this place consider itself a 'fine mexican'  establishment. *sigh*

Let me preface this by saying that my boyfriend is OBSESSED with La Burrita. So going in, I obviously had high expectations. 

Much as I love my five star restaurants, I think I love the little hole-in-the-walls even more, especially when they don't pretend to be anything else. 

We ordered a small ground beef burrito and a small "wet" carne asade burrito. Trust me - the smalls were definitely enough for the two of us. My boyfriend had the ground beef burrito on a regular basis when he was in school and it was just as good as he had said it would be. The "wet" burrito - dressed like an enchilada and enjoyed with a fork and knife - wasn't quite as good, but it's also not probably something I would have ordered on my own. 

All in all, I will definitely be back here the next time I'm in Berkeley.

La Burrita is especially good for a late night snack! I usually get the Super Burrito. 

Love: 
-bag of fresh chips comes with burritos 
-large size burrito is definitely worth it! 
-open salsa bar (has limes & onions too)
-VIP Card (must ask for one) 

They only have ~5 tables in the front and ~4 in the back, so I always do take out.

If you're hungry and craving Mexican food at 1:30 am in the morning, La Burrita is the place for you. 

Seriously, how many other places give you a warm, delicious burrito with free tortilla chips and an unlimited salsa bar up till 2 am? 

 However, as much as I love this place, you really have to be careful with what you choose. Their burritos and tacos and made on order before your very eyes, but their nachos, tostadas, and enchiladas are tossed into a to-go box and simply nuked in the microwave. 
   Stick to the burritos. Better yet, the small carne asada burrito, which is less than 5 bucks. Although, the shrimp tacos/burritos are pretty good, too. 

They take cash, debit, and credit, which is really convenient, and they have sodas and horchatas, if you so desire. It's small place, with very few tables/chairs, so you should really get it to-go. Don't forgot to grab some salsa, jalapenos, and limes while you're waiting for them to make your food.

Maybe it's not the cleanest, freshest place in town, but it's delicious, cheap, and speedy, which makes up for everything

First of all, you have to take it as it is: cheap college food. So given that, if you want some foie grois, this place isn't for you. But if you want some food that's worth every cent, this is the place. Like everyone else, I must recommend the special carne asada or the nachos. Try to hit it up when it's not crowded, so come for an early lunch (opens at 11 i think) or a late dinner (closes at 1?). It's small, so take your food back to your dorm, apt, frat house, whatever. And their salsa and chips hit the spot too, so yummo.

As a starving student, your belly will be the only thing you're busting, not your wallet. =)

Been there twice and I thought it was pretty good and decent for the price. I had the steak fajita and it was pretty good. I mean, it wasn't top quality beef, but I have definitely seem worse. I really like their salsa bar. the best thing is  they allow you to choose what kind of tortilla so i feel less of a fatass with the wheat option.

This place is so good, quick, and cheap!! Definitely get the wet burrito grande, it's like having a giant enchilada! Their horchata is delicious too.  Plus, if you get your burrito wet, they'll essentially turn your chips (that come with every meal) into nachos.  It's an unexpected plus.  Also, one of the only places in this area of Durant that accepts credit/debit cards.

It's open late, the food is pretty good for a place that isn't a sit down restaurant, and the prices are very reasonable.

A much better choice than the neighboring Top Dog.

That's about all there is to say about this place.

This seems to be a default for a lot of Berkeleyans for a nice big burrito - for good reason! It's nice, big and DERICIOUS. 

Though the size isn't quite as massive as Sam's down the street, I think La Burrita is much better than Chipotle.

After having a... social night with friends and you're cravin' some nomnom, you're gonna wanna tap this.

I tried the tostada and wasn't super impressed. I felt a lot just like a deconstructed taco, which is okay, just not what I was hankering for. 

Stick with the burritos, they are the bomb

Besides providing it's Cal students with one of the most authentic fast food burritos on campus, I must also add that their guacamole is one of the best I've ever had at any Mexican restaurant. It's base is creamy and flavorful and the mixed in tomato/onion chunks give it body. I always get a side of their guac to go with their carne asada burrito/chips. There is usually a line out the door especially late at night and seating is limited but I've eaten it standing up outside the establishment and it's even better then. Fast, cheap and comforting, it was my go-to spot during my 4 years at Cal and even now, I crave it.

the food is mediocre. service is quick. food is cheap. quality is not too bad. overall a good option if you have 5bucks on hand and are hungry. but if you want nachos, go to panchos across the street!! la burrita nachos are not worth it.

This is an all purpose place.

When I first came to Cal, I needed to find a Mexican place that could compare to my love for King Taco back home in So Cal... La Burrita definitely did not replace my love, but it did find a way to be appealing and a way to keep me a frequent customer.

My favorite food item here are there "Tacos Rancheros." You get three tacos, your choice of meat, and a side of chips.  They're delicious. I would add some lime and get their green sauce.  Perfect lunch meal.

What else is great about La Burrita? Well, aside from the friendly staff, it's a fantastic late night food stop.  Leave the bar, arrive and order, and then FEAST! Anyone remotely tipsy, or beyond that point will most definitely enjoy their late night adventure into this place.

All in all, it's one of my Berkeley staples. It doesn't get five stars because it's not a stellar place, but it is great, and good, and the service is great!

Back before I had explored the Mission and knew what a true burrito was, I was a lowly, poor Cal student who enjoyed the fine dining of Americanized burritos. These aren't terrible burritos, but they definitely cannot compete with those you would find in any taqueria in the Mission. However, I will say this - they offer healthier choices, such as black beans only, no rice, less greasy meat options, and spinach wraps. The burritos are also a manageable size, and they're dirt-cheap, far cheaper than a Mission burrito, so it's your call. I'll grab another for old time's sake if I'm in the area.

4

Kind of pricey, but overall a decent choice when you want something on the go. Waiting time is not bad and taste is decent. I don't know of many places that offer a Cheesesteak burrito!  Parking will have to be on the street.  What else I like about it?  Open late, and if you change your mind last minute you can go to top dog right next door.
Not so good. Kinda flavorless, and everything in the burrito just seems like a uniform paste, even though visual inspection shows multiple ingredients.

This place has a lot of good things about it. One of them is not parking. But other than that, it was pretty good. The people behind the counter were nice. I had a burrito and my husband had tacos & enchiladas. It was all good. I am from Southern California and I find it hard to find good Mexican food here. But I would definately go back. The place was clean. It's open late. The salsas were great! They had some very tasty salsas that reminded me of Mexico. I would definately go back. It is reasonably priced, good variety, good hours. Very quick & convenient. The super nachos looked amazing!Truly, everything looked good. I will come back, but meanwhile I continue  to search for really good, authentic Mexicsn food

Food is better than decent and quite cheap. I had a small carne asada burrito - which comes with more than enough tortilla chips - and it was a bit more than I could finish. (I finished it all the same.) Excellent place for hungry college students with a limited budget.
Delicious wet burritos!

Words cannot express my love for La Burrita.  I get such strange cravings for it that I would cross the bay to get my hands on one.

The prices are low, the service is quick, the chips are crunchy and the salsa is fresh.  Their super steak burrito (hold the beans) is the bomb.

This is the original place I would go to when I decided to try Top Dog.  I found this place just cruising the city one nite, saw tons of people in line and got right behind them. The people are truly nice.  I like this place, to think I would drive over 20 min to get here.  Just for a 6.00 burrito.  I like the sides of onions and salsa that I pack myself.  Great for the late snack.

Not the biggest fan of La Burrita. Definitely think there are lots of things they could improve on like the taste of their meat and not drenching the burritos with sour cream. 

Nothing really takes me here anymore unless I've been partying and feel the need to make a stop to eat on the way back. Everything they make is mediocre or bad so I feel like I have many better alternatives when it comes to Mexican food.

Even though its RIGHT there from campus, I've only came here once a few years ago and recently for their free burrito through TAGGSTR.

I dont know if its because it was free and that was why the quality of the burrito was so poor but I didnt order a bean burrito thank you very much. I did appreciate and enjoyed the salsa bar and free chips though. Its also another plus that its open late and actually has a few tables inside. 

But eh, I probably wont be back unless I'm really desperate. Campus cred this week is $5 for $10 though :)
tried the wet burrito. much better. not the best burritos around but pretty damn satisfying!

The meat they use in their tacos is unsavory and greasy, not the type I would have expected in a "soft" taco at least.  They should consider altering their menu a bit because the plates look either too big or awkward. Not coming here again at my will.

After two bad experiences in a row i'm never going back there. The first was I ordered a shrimp burrito and all the shells/tails were still on the shrimp. The next time I went there I ordered a chicken burrito and I think I got food poisoning because I was sick and vomiting for the day and a half.

Definitely the place to go to when you've gotten the munchies BAD, especially after a night of drinking, and you're craving cheap, greasy, unhealthy food. The chicken super nachos here are amazing, and you get much more than you can possibly eat at a single meal! I like their salsa bar because it includes onion and japapeno slices, and you can help yourself. Not the biggest fan of their burritos though.

I haven't really had a problem with La Burrita, even though some people try to give it a bad reputation.

I've ordered their quesadillas a couple times and they came out pretty hot and nice to eat, along with a little lettuce and chips. Not a bad deal for your money.

I would put Chipotle and La Burrita at basically the same level. Only difference is that La Burrita is more local and Chipotle is more of a chain-restuarant.
Excellent salsas. Pretty fast service especially when you don't go during meal time. It's a classic spot next to Top Dog that college students eat at.
Great for a late night bite!  Good price for delicious food.

The food here is definitely subpar as far as Mexican food around here goes. I'd give it two stars if not for the fact that it's open very late and its very reasonable prices don't burn through the average college student's wallet.

Of the select times that I've eaten here, I think I've only been here once while sober. And let me tell you, it's not good eats when your logical and inhibitory systems are at full go. The food is sloppily put together, the attitudes of the people working there is less-than-friendly, even mean at times, and there just isn't enough seating.

In addition, the chips are gross. WAY too greasy and salty.

Northside La Burrita, on the other hand, is a whole different story...

I was in a rush recently and in the area. I stopped for two regular tacos with corn tortilla and ground beef, romaine, a white cheese, their special sauce and perhaps tomatoes, I can't remember, but the price was $2.19 for each taco. The tacos were hot in terms of temperature and I added more salsa, the ground beef was like a paste and the cheese was melted inside. They were sublime. I ate the accompanying tortilla chips and sipped water. Had I known, I would have gotten there much earlier. A day or two later, I bought three more and took them to my mother. They made her very happy. Try this simple and inexpensive item and you will see. They reminded me of when people cook from scratch and employ the recipes from generations or from areas, where the soul takes precedence over commerce.

One of the only places you can get mini super burritos. All I have ever had was the carne asada. It is usually salty and juicy. Green Salsa is pretty good, but it's not spicy at all. Go to spot if you have already eaten Top Dog the same day.

dude so gross, I got a chicken burrito more like a cat food burrito because that's what it tasted like! I took a bite and gagged! The cashier was looking a me struggle to eat it. Don't eat here , you get better tasting food at taco bell!

best burritos in berkeley.  the cheesesteak one is great, but if you wanna keep your blood flowing through your arteries you're better off with a chicken burrito (it's not bad).  

and don't even think about going to the one in northside ;)
I don't even like mexican food normally, but when I see La Burrita, it makes me want an enchelada with a side of beans and rice. Nom!
when you're from san diego... this is no where close to mexican food.

The only reason that this gets 2 stars from me instead of 1 is that it is nominally better than the mexican food on campus. Compared to actual mexican food, however, this is barely edible, and I feel sorry for all the students who don't know better.

Speed: La Burrita is perfect if you need to eat in under 10 minutes, because the food is always ready *before* I have even had enough time to fill up my plastic container with salsa.

Taste: This is clearly not gourmet food. The food is crap, but it's somewhat tasty crap. The carne asada is usually very fatty, and lots of the meat is loaded with filler, but this food hits the spot when you're in a jam.

The Pros: Open late, takes credit cards, doesn't take forever to get food.
The Cons: The food sucks.  I've regretted every bite of food I've ever taken here.  

Stop by for an horchata and then walk around the corner to Mario's La Fiesta... or jump in front of a bus.  All better options than eating at La Burrita.

Oh and the workers talk shit about everyone in Spanish.

"Yes! Yes! Yes!" screamed a hungry, young Asian man. With carne asada burrito in one hand and green salsa in the other, the young man was ready to finally silence the angry cries from his stomach. He drenched the salsa on his burrito and took a large bite that required him to smile in the process. The smile, however, didn't go away. It remained as he nodded in approval of how amazing the said combination was. The only thing that held him back from jumping up and down for joy was the small size of the burrito.

A legitimate California burrito joint; what else can I say?

It used to be my favorite place to eat in between classes until a Chipotle appeared a block away. Nonetheless, I still love the cheese steak burrito at La Burrita because it tastes like heaven in a tortilla. They don't charge extra for guacamole, which I think is just magical.

Every order comes with chips with which you can then visit the salsa bar and load up on something nice.

I must say, though, that it used to be even better. Something happened gradually over the latter half of the decade that diminished the quality, though I'm not sure why. Even so, it's still the best burrito in Berkeley and I would get it in an instant if I were in town.

late night 2 am runs for la burrita. oh jeez, i'm getting hungry now. quality burrito and awesomely delicious salsa. i used to get like 6 containers to eat with my chips and to drown my burrito in. can't wait til memorial stadium opens up so i can stop by for a bite here.
Passable burritos and enchiladas, but doesn't match the food quality nor ambiance of the La Burrita on the north side of campus.

It's all about the cheesesteak burrito.  Yum yum yum! On my trips back to Berkeley, this is also another one of my staples down memory lane - it's cheesesteak burrito from la burrita and then a lemon chicken from top dog.  Don't have such a big appetite, share with someone, but I guarantee you, one bite into the cheesesteak burrito and you'd wish that you hadn't agreed on sharing.

La Burrita is one of the better late night options when youre stumbling home from Kips!  I always get the Cheesesteak burrito and it never lets me down.   Its greasy, the meat is tender and its a freaking cheesesteak in a burrito.  What can you ask for more.  Best mexican food in Berkeley

the only mexican food thats acceptible in berkeley.

favorites: carne asada burrito, fajita burrito, taco salad, and wet burrito

actually, come to think of it, those are the only things ive ever ordered at la burrita and all of them are terrific!

its also one of the only places open late, so when u have those late night munchies from whatever u've been doing, this always hits the spot!

I had the Pollo Asado Burrito and it was one of the best that I have ever had. The chicken was bursting with flavor. Everything was on point. Highly recommended. I dont know what other people are talking about re: watery and tasteless, but I will return many times for this pollo asado burrito
Good burritos, love the variety of sauces, good option for a quick lunch to go.

This has got to be my favorite place for a burrito---not just any burrito---A WET BURRITO!  It's a huge burrito, covered in sour cream, enchilada sauce, pico de gallo, and guacamole with chips with cheese on the side.  It is so big, I usually eat it in 2-3 meals.  I like their salsa a lot and usually add scoops of it onto the already wet burrito.  I don't get anything but the wet burrito here.  It usually makes me really thirsty later though.  It's probably pretty bad for you but it's definitely one of the must-haves in Berkeley.

My favorite mexican restaurant, expensive places included.  It's like the taco stand I wished I had growing up in LA.   The Carne Asada special burrito is probably the only thing that will be served at my wedding.  Maybe there will be pinkberry too. 

I've been here probably close to 100 times in two years and they have never once messed up my order or my change.  

I'm a big fan.

Good, big, cheap burrito.  I really took you for granted when I had you.  Now that I am in New York, I would give my left nut to have you back.  Do you know that they put lettuce in burritos out here? Lettuce!  And forget about even finding a Super-Burrito, they have a hard enough time mastering the plain old regular burrito.  Although you might not measure up to the Mission Burritos or So Cal Burritos, you are really under appreciated as the go-to late night study snack at Cal.  What I would give to have you back.....

I was lured into La Burrita because they have a massive TV screening the FIFA world cup... and I wanted a taco. 

The staff were quick and friendly. The taco was fine, fresh salad and salsa, the chicken meat was quality and had a very mild sweet sauce. The shell was very soggy, but the taste was overall satisfactory. 
It was ~$5 for 2 tacos and a bowl of chips with salsa.
Every time I've eaten there, I didn't like it. It just seems really bland for Mexican food.

La Burrita is a landmark restaurant at the flagship UC campus. It's not great, but why would you expect that of a restaurant that makes money by taking advantage unknowing freshman/drunk students. Gets the job done, but don't come expecting gourmet mexican (which is near impossible to find in the area anyway).

This is my favorite Mexican joint on southside.  I always get the burritos, and I haven't tried anything else. A small burrito is less than five bucks, and it's already pretty filling. A large burrito is also pretty cheap compared to the other Mexican food places nearby, and is really filling. The orders are also made really quickly, which is a big plus. 

The only bad thing about La Burrita is that it sometimes gets pretty crowded, especially around the fountain drinks, so you awkwardly have to maneuver yourself to collect your salsa and utensils, but other than that, this is one of my favorite cheap places to eat near campus.

La Burrita is great food at all times of the day! My favorite is at midnight for the some midnight munchies. I always get the super ground beef burrito. If you're a student, you can use a "Press Pass" and get a free drink. I've had them mess up a couple of my orders over my years as a college student, but they just take it back and remake my order correctly (somewhat begrudgingly).

Regardless, their food is good and worth it's price. It's not too expensive and tastes of generic taqueria food that you'll find in many locations around the East Bay. It's essentially cheap, quick stop, authentic-ish Mexican food.

BTW, the chips are delicious with the salsa verde.

****3.5

After a decade, I finally decided to give this place a try.  I've always passed this place up for Top Dog or other good eats at the Asian ghetto.

The prices are reasonable so I can see why it's always busy.

Service is quick, and I love the salsa bar.

Decor-few small tables, not good for large groups.

I ordered the La Burrita special with pollo asado thinking it would be the best item on their menu since it is their specialty burrito.  It was good, but not great.  The chicken was really moist, but the downside was that I didn't find any guac until halfway through my burrito.

My friends ordered:

-super wet burrito with steak (beautiful presentation compared to my foiled wrapped burrito with a few chips tossed on the side of the tray).  It was good and I enjoyed the chips that were topped with melted cheese and salsa.

-cheesesteak burrito-hands down the best one out of that night and I would actually return just for this burrito.  It had nicely grilled onions and tenders pieces of steak.
