all in all good prices for a college town.  Would I go out of my way to eat here?  Only if I'm craving a cheesesteak burrito :p

i had the vegetarian burrito the first time i went and thought it was pretty good. but by my second visit, i couldnt even finish it. la burrita kind of grosses me out now. i get nauseous just walking by it... 

but a lot of cal kids like it because it stays open til 2a, which is fantastic so i can smell their restaurant at all hours of the day. and hear all the drunken foot traffic walking past my window.

3 stars for the burrito ONLY! the place was filthy. the salsa bar looked like it came off the set of an old burt reynolds movie with the dark woodgrain laminate  and salsa covering the table and parts of the floor. (isn't salsa supposed to be inside the salsa containers?) seating is non-existent unless you cower over people that are already eating and stare at them long enough to make them eat faster and eventually leave. lucky for us, a big group was leaving as we picked up our order. it's a good place to fill that void in your stomach at 1:30 in the morning but thats about it.
I love this place! I was addicted! Best hangover cure everrrrrrrrrrrr

I love Mexican food, but this place does not deserve to be put in that category.  Although it has the same "dirty" feel as a lot of Berkeley restaurants, the food is sub-par and I feel icky eating in there.  The portions are big, and the prices are cheap, but the meats are only ok, the salsas are mediocre, and overall, there are just too many good food choices in Berkeley to go to La Burrita, unless you have one of those late night burrito cravings (which I understand).  There's not really much else in terms of Mexican in the immediate area, so you may have to go here.

I had a small veggie burrito, and I liked it.  I really did.  But I asked for no beans.  What do they do?  Give me beans.  That just killed it.  Sauce tastes good, especially the dark red brown ish one.  Oh, and the tortilla chips are rather dandy as well.

duuuudes. i don't know what most of these fools are talking about. La Burrita is a staple in my life. Although i'm an even bigger fan of the La Burrita on Northside, this place is amazingly delicious. 

That said, i would like to defend La Burrita on several counts:

1. Yes, they microwave their nachos, so that instead of getting some neon-orange-velveta-"cheese"-sauce, you get some serious shredded molten cheese goodness. Sure, it's not prepared in an oven, but it's fast food, and i'm hungry, dammit. 

2. i always get carne asada on everything, and its always been delicious, whether they've been stuck to my nachos, in a wet burrito, in a hot quesadilla that's bursting with cheese, or in a fajita plate. To be absolutely fair, Chipotle has better steak, but it's never been bad, and certainly not to the point where i couldn't stomach it. 

and duuudes, it's cheap, it's more filling than top dogs (i always need at least 2 hot dogs from them), and their chips and salsa are the best in the area. seriously. Chipotle chips has got nothing on them, and La Burrita's salsas are crazy addictive. 

it may not be authentic, it may not be a stellar establishment, but i'm a college student and the sight of brown bags filled to the top with chips warms me to the tips of my toes.

Its alright for a burrito, nothing special, no special taste, but it opens late at night and is really good for those late night hungers. One things I use to like to order is the wet burrito, its huge and fills you up, but recently I found out that they microwave them, and I am not such a great fan of that. I guess if I wanted a wet burrito just splash some water on a regular burrito, stick it in the microwave and call it wet. There's also no flavor on their meat, it seems like they just cook it and thats it, plain as ever.

The one thing I do like is unlimited sauces, which are pretty good, they have a whole bunch you can choose from and take home, and they are really delicious.

First let me start out saying i eat at alot of mexican spots, taco trucks and such. This is not the best place for a greasy burrito or a super saucey taco. But it does have its own taste to it. Its more of a americanized taco, burrito joint. What i like about it is how they make it their burritos. They mix all their ingredents together for a well balance bite. Everytime you take a bite it has a little bit of everything, not like the burrito trucks and taco trucks. At the taco trucks they just whoop everything together and sometimes you start out with only meat and then you end up with only sour cream or rice. At La Burrita every bite you have an equal amount of rice meat and sauce.

Food: Taste great, something differnt from the other burritos joints.
Service: Fast, prompt.
Atmosphere: Alot of college kids and locals.

Opens late night, thats always a plus with me. (Late night eater)

4 Stars for La Burrita

If you're in desperate need of a cheap burrito and don't care if it tastes bland or watery, then this is the place to go. 

While as an undergrad, I always bitched about the quality at La Burrita - but, I still ate there, often. The location was convenient and the prices were affordable (less than $6, generally).

Then I grew up and realized there are better places outside of the UC Berkeley-radius. Much better places.

Finally stumbled here when I wasn't drunk and had a super meat quesadilla and it was AMAZING. The meat had that wonderful "just cooked" taste and the cheese was slimier than I expected. That made it a plus. GO NOW.
Fast, cheap, open late. Generally good consistent food (though once I got a burrito with too much salt in it...). Very filling Mexican for a low price.

Ok food at ok prices.  The shredded chicken burrito was mostly chicken with the occasional slathering of beans and rice, but the chicken didn't lack flavor.  There was no hot salsa at the salsa bar.  Otherwise, 'meh' is a good way to describe the food.

The burritos are pretty decent, but not as big as a Chipotle burrito.  Taste is somewhat authentic.  My favorite thing to order was the steak burrito with shrimp.  However, on the menu it says add shrimp to something and it's only 50 cents but when I order a steak burrito and say "add shrimp" the cashier always rings up a shrimp burrito and adds a $1.50 for adding steak.  It's a good place to go if you want some food late at night, but I don't think it's very healthy.  I'd say if you want something a little more authentic tasting than chipotle, eat at la burrita, but it still has nothing on a real Mexican restaurant.

A pretty forgettable burrito aside from the gnawing pain in your stomach which will subside only via time or Tums, but it's a warm feeling to show up after not being here for mulitple few years and the La Burrito crew still remembers me.

i am mexican and love carne asada burritos but the meat here is kinda gross, so i always end up getting a vege burrito instead. They have great chips (free) and a variety of tasty salsas, so i am thankful for that. The food doesnt compare to the real stuff but it passes
I shared their Wet Burrito with a friend. We both thought it was very delicious. Their regular burritos are also excellent!

Despite being such a popular destination, I've only been here twice in my three years at Cal. If you're not sure what to get, go for the two steak enchilada plate! My friend recommended it to me stating that each enchilada was as big as a burrito - they're not - but overall it was still quite good for being just above $7!

There was a great amount of steak and the rest of the ingredients were well proportioned. For $7 there was a good amount of rice and beans, with substantial amounts of guac and sour cream. on the side. There was just something about eating all of those things together at the same time on the same fork that makes the food here special. BEST EAT YOUR FOOD WARM! Plus free chips and unlimited salsa!

I don't understand why the southside la burrita didn't have an open chip bar but the northside one does. Anywhoo, they make a good burrito for cheap, and the carne asada is certainly more seasoned than the chipotle down the street. Gordo's used to be pretty far for me when I was a student, but La Burrita was serviceable until I found time for Gordo's (although now Gordo's is on telegraph too!)
Update: Staff is a little clueless sometimes; we asked for an order to go and they gave us uncovered paper plates (?); this seems to happen with other people as well.
This is pretty decent food. They don't really do custom orders like other places. I would only give them 2 stars but their horchata earned them an extra star.

La Burrita is beyond good. Its a small little Mexican place in Berkeley. Open late for hungry students. When I was in school, I ate here all the time. Now, I'm in LA but I will always eat here on visits up north. I took my boyfriend there, who is the biggest Mexican food fan, and he still talks about La Burrita. I personally think La Burrita beats all the burrito places in LA, a city filled with Mexican food. I love the service, too. They know what they're doing and they are all so nice to the students and visitors.

Good, cheap, plentiful Mexican food. Nice salsa bar with unlimited house salsa, onion+cilantro mix, jalapeños, and verduras en vinagre. Used to eat here en seguido when going to UC. Now I still make the journey every once in a while when I'm in the mood for it... for the favorable taste:value ratio I'll even mingle with the angsty undergrads who remind me of one of several past versions of myself.

The staff are nice too. Just busy as heCK.

Everything here is a good size. Food is good, fast, and hot. The salsa bar here is good and I always take a little more than I need.

I wouldn't come here with more than 3 other people because that's pretty much the most you can fit at the biggest table and there are only a handful of tables. The good thing about this place is that it is close to the residence halls for the university and it's open late so you always find a bunch of students lined up, especially after a game. Combined with Top Dog 2 doors down, it always smells greasy in this area. I feel bad for the apartments across the street, which I considered living at before I considered the smell of hot dogs & beans in the morning.

There is always a burrito and fountain drink deal on the coupon cards that go around campus at the beginning of the school year. Find one of those cards if you want a free soda with your burrito.

Not a bad place for late night drunk food. Cheap and large portions. Service was fast. I also liked that I get to practice my spanish, as it is probably the only language spoken here. Had the carne asada burrito, it was good.
This is my go to lunch place on the south side of campus. La Burrita gives very good value for money, and their salsa bar has some awesome variety of flavor.
Burrittos that are big, cheap and tastey...  What more can you ask for in a college town..

I like this place. They recently changed their ingredients so it's a lot better now. I mean, it's no gourmet food, but for a student budget, this is pretty good. I've only gotten the burritos, though, 'cause frankly, their other food isn't worth getting. The burritos are fairly large, and they accept credit card.

I was a regular back in college, but my horizon has expanded and I have to say: why on earth would one microwave cheese and chips and call those nachos??? Ugh!

Their "special" vegetarian burritos are still delicious and I have to give them props for no lard. Chuck the microwaves and I'll start going back.

Split a large chicken "la burrita special" with my mexican lover food boyfriend. We both LOVED it. We came to try one or two other places after that, but it seems difficult for me to find one in which the "cooks" actually spread the guacamole and the sour cream inside the WHOLE burrito and not in one single little spot like in some other places.
Dear La Burrita, I realized my mistake, I promise that I will be visiting you for my next Mexican meal.

Pretty decent burritos.  They aren't great, but you don't really get tired of the burrito before you finish it, which is the case with a lot of other burrito joints, or whopper wraps like the nearby chipotle.  The chips are thin and crispy but can taste a bit stale [but they're free/included with the burrito].  The carne asada burrito with everything, fajita burrito, and wet burrito are my favorites.

They get a fat star for being open late alongside top dog [figuratively and literally].  You will know of la burrita if you're a Berkeley student. 

They have some seating in the back if you didn't know.

I definitely expected better considering there are some pretty decent places to eat on Telegraph, but the food I got here wasn't great. I didn't have any problems with the service like other reviewers did. I got my food pretty quickly and it was okay, but it wasn't anything out of the ordinary. They just have your basic tacos, burritos, quesadillas, etc to choose from and do an average job at it. No complaints but I was hoping for something better. If I'm ever back in the Berkeley area, I'll probably just eat at one of the other restaurants on Telegraph.

Wet burrito is nice.  Employees are friendly, clean, very cheap and very good food.  Great outdoors courtyard especially when not crowded also shared by La Vals' pizza in case someone in your party feels like pizza, pasta or beer.

When I first discovered the Durant La Burrita, I thought it was AMAZING! However, after discovering the Euclid La Burrita, I've had a change of heart.

The Durant La Burrita location is a bit smaller, so it gets crowded very quickly. Also, there isn't much dine-in space; they only have a couple small tables.

Try their Super Burrito and Wet Burrito. Be sure to eat these while they're hot because it's not so amazing when it cools down.

Late night munchies? Well get your grub on some authentic mexican food! I had the large super burrito which definitely satisfied my craving of food. I also had the horchata which wasn't up to par, but def needed some thirst quenching after seeing crystal castles that night. Would come again to get my fix!

You either love La Burrita or you hate it.  There is no shame in either choice, I just happen to fall on the "I could eat La Burrita forever" side.  If you are looking for authentic Mexican food, go elsewhere - but if you are jonesing for something pretty delicious, La Burrita will always be a favorite.  My menu item of choice is the Super Burrito with Chicken.  Never fails me.  I have also in the best gotten the Wet Burrito (a classic) or the Nachos, (pretty good).  Again, not for those searching for authentic Mexican - only for those on a quest for something to satisfy.

This place is fantastic, especially for late-night Mexican cravings.  I had the super nachos, which were great - they put beans in the nachos, which i LOVE. the chips got a little soggy by the end, but overall, they were fantastic. Plus, they were well-priced, super fast, and stay open late!
some of the least flavorful mexican places i've ever been to.  it's fine if you're drunk or don't like spice....
I live in the Mission, and I still miss this place.  A burrito for under $4???  Unheard of.  And oh man, that chicken...so moist, so flavorful, so not chewy.  Yum.
Nothing better than a large burrito for my girlfriend after a night out....they close at 2am

La Burrita, unless you are a starving college student or a transplant from the East coast, you had better Mexican food. Its open late, so great to hit up after the bars. However, the food is greasy and a gut bomb, so go there if you want that feeling, otherwise, you have a Berkeley establishment right next door with Top Dog!  a way better choice.

An overall solid Mexican restaurant. The unlimited chips and salsa as well as free refills on soda is a huge plus (except health wise). Having to ration your drink, especially with spicy food, is a huge negative. That being said, their food is only above-average.
5 years ago this place was great. Get it together.

The food is OK. I only go there when I want to eat something fast and cheap. Although the chips tasted good they were soaked in grease. I prefer going to Chipotle even though they're kind of expensive but at least you get a free drink with a student ID.
Very bleh Mexican food.  Doesn't even compare to Chipotle.

My favorite moment at La Burrita was when my little sister at 13 years old came to visit me while i was at Cal.

I took her to La Burrita in hopes of exposing her to some down and dirty food, that didn't come from our snooty hometown of Carmel, where they dont even HAVE a good cheap mexican eatery! Man I can't figure out how I survived my time there amongst the foie grois and arugala salads.

ANYWAY....I asked her to go ahead and order...and she says to the gentleman at the register,  "I  will have a vegetarian with...chicken".

3 stars to the cashier for not cracking up at my sister, thereby not destroying her fragile pre-pubescent ego.

Other than being open late and being accesible on those binge drinking(sorry mom!) nights in college, La Burrita has a great salsa bar (yummy) and HUGE burritos for $5.

It isn't the best Mexican I have had, but it isn't the worst!

Cheap and filling...magical words to those poor college students on a budget.

Came here one Saturday night to sate my stomach's appetite, but my stomach was flip flopping on whether it was starving, or sick of the thought of food, so I got a salad (Chicken Fajita Salad, for those of you who must know).

The place was pretty packed - although it's a late Saturday night in Berkeley and there's very little else open nearby, so is that a surprise? - and it took a few minutes to get my order, but it came out quickly considering the volume of people there.

We had our food to go. Sitting around there and eating wouldn't have been possible, and we had a nice calm place to enjoy our meal at a friend's apartment. Got there, opened the bag and box, and "Oh my gosh, that's a lot of salad".

I could barely finish half of it. If you're not really very hungry, don't order the Chicken Fajita Salad. There's just too much of it.

As for the taste, the chicken was all right and the salad was good. If I had space in my stomach for that much food I would've finished it, but instead I ended up sharing it with 2 other people before ultimately throwing a small bit of it away the next morning. I'm pretty sure they all liked it as well (well, the last one didn't get any chicken but that wasn't La Burrita's fault, heh).

It seems like a worthwhile place to try, and I've experienced their burritos before, which IMO were more impressive, so if you've had too much Chipotle lately and want something else (and the AG across the street doesn't look appetizing to you), then stop by and try it out. You'll probably be pleasantly surprised, if not by the taste then by the portions.

Or you could show up drunk and hungry at 2 AM and have no other options.
I used to go there all the time when I was in college. There's always a line but you never have to wait for long. Good food, cheap price, friendly staff, and fast service - can't complain.

Really??  This place is pretty bad.  The one thing I give them is that their salsas are actually pretty good, and there's a good number to choose from.

But everything is pretty bland.  You get the grease but not the flavor.  Yes, it's cheap and central for Southside, but it's definitely not delicious Mexican food.

CampusCred (UC Berk's version of Groupon) has once again led us to try another place and we are so glad it did! How could we have missed this place? Perhaps we've been too busy sticking to the food we know best at Asian ghetto--busy enough to not look across the street at that smiling donkey.

The groupon was for $10... we had two...we only used one because the prices are just THAT cheap. They're not dirt cheap or anything, but the average is $5 - $6 for quality food. What's even better is the serving given, and that is the main aspect that factored into this 5 star rave. 

In addition and most importantly, the food tastes great. Any entree is served with chips, hand made and oh so good. They have a salsa bar and I think their selections are upon the best I have ever tried; I'm not even exaggerating.

Johann ordered a lengua special burrito. It was amazing. It's the best burrito I could have ever possibly had. No joke-- my eyes literally rolled back when I took my first bite. Either I just really love lengua or I've only had crappy burritos until now, haha. 

Melvin ordered the Shrimp burrito and was surprisingly very well pleased with it. Our experience is that when we order anything with shrimp in it for what we consider a reasonable price, we only get 3-4 shrimps, 5 at best. But this burrito was not stingy at all. Bite after bite after bite...shrimp! The only complaint he had was that all the sour cream was .  amassed at just one end of the burrito-- but whatever.

As for their horchata, it's better than Baldos. I'd say it is the 2nd best horchata we've tried.

But yeah, the best thing about this place are the very affordable prices and the generous servings that accompany such a deal. We will definitely be coming back. We do, after all, have one more groupon :)

Or as my and my friends benevolently referred to is, "LaBo." This is not a fancy, white table cloth restaurant, this is a place to get a quick, and delicious burrito. During my time at Cal, this was one of my favorite places to go at night. It's one of the few places that are opened late and accepts plastic. I've never been disappointed with the food here. To be perfectly honest, I've gone here on numerous drunk food expeditions with the same sense of fulfillment. I give it 5 stars because if you come with the understanding that it's not supposed to be fine dining, than it meets all of your expectations. (Go for the burritos cause that's all I've ever really had!)

The first time I ate a burrito here, I was shocked at how small they were. They're like 2 inches in radius. The idea of a "large" is basically two tortillas instead of one and adding some sour cream and guac. Even with my super saver coupon of a dollar off... I felt gipped for 5 bucks. the taste is pretty good but I wish they'd give more meat. 

Sometimes you just really want a burrito though and this is pretty much the only game in town. I guess I've been spoiled by Socal burritos and the Mission district

It really deserves 2 stars, but I'll give it 3 for it's convenience around the UC campus.  The food is super heavy and yucky - you'll definitely feel nasty and sleepy after a meal. But if you're a lazy student like I was, you'll end up going here due to the lack of choices around the southside of campus.

I've tried everything from burritos, wet burritos, enchiladas, tacos, tortas to their philly cheesesteak burrito.  Nothing's memorable or special - it's filler.  They're open very late, so definitely kudos for that.

If you have a car, go to Gordo's instead.
Get the shrimp burrito and you'll agree with the five star rating. Plus they're  nice people. :) And it's open super late. Win.
when you have a terrible case of the munchies, and it's 2 am, come to la burrita.  they'll do ya right!

I got love in my heart for La Burrita.  I can't speak for anything else on the menu, but as far as I'm concerned, their Carne Asada burrito is the best thing on God's green earth.  I love this place so much that there have been days where I've had it for both lunch AND dinner.  I am so attached that I gave it up for Lent one year, and let me tell you, that was no cop-out sacrifice.  I suffered.  In a big way.  When it was over, I swore La Burrita and I would never be parted again.

One night, I got trashed and had the second best wet burrito of my life from here.  This is one of the better Mexican food places I've been in my lifetime..even for a local college joint.  I still prefer the likes of taco trucks late at night but this place still seems to do just fine!

The perfect midnight snack that is walking distance if you live in the dorms. I love the salsa bar as well as the carne asada taco! It looks small, but for a small girl like me it fills you up!

Definitely something you have to try if you live in Berkeley.
great food. healthy? hell no! too fatty... but great after exams
Great chips and guacamole...other than that I don't really crave much else from here. But it's a favorite for a lot of my friends who need a quick, filling, and relatively cheap lunch.

If one day you find that your starvation is so intense that you might not live to see tomorrow, then La Burrita is the way to go. 

Because I skipped both breakfast and lunch today (I had a full day of classes), I was so hungry by the time I was done that it felt like my stomach was literally trying to eat itself. I had a huge craving for Mexican food and so I RAN to La Burrita to get my fix. I ordered a large La Burrita Special with ground beef and a soft Veggie Taco. Both came with tortilla chips. The total with tax was $8.23. 

The wait time for my food was pleasantly short -- just long enough for me to fill up 4 containers of salsa. If you are as clueless about salsa as me, then you might assume that the thin and runny green salsa is only mildly spicy, while the thick and chunky bright red salsa is flaming hot. This is not the case! The red one actually has zero spiciness and goes well with the chips. The green one should not be underestimated because it's pretty hot! But it tastes amazing and will make your burrito a thousand times better if you pour some inside. 

The La Burrita Special was soo good that I plowed through the whole thing without even taking a break for air. I've had burritos before where I could  identify exactly what I was eating at the moment because all the ingredients were divided up into sections. But this time,  instead of thinking, "here's that dollop of guacamole" and "now there's the handful of cheese", I was surprised at how everything inside the La Burrita Special was mixed together so perfectly that it created a unique, blended flavor of its own. By the way, I don't care if this is supposed to taste authentic or not. My taste buds loved it and it filled me up! Though the size didn't look that big (I expected a large to be bigger), I was feeling full and satisfied by the time I finished. 

That is, until I decided to unwrap the aluminum foil around my veggie taco and take a peek inside. It looked so appealing that I had to eat it too. YES, I eat a lot... The soft tortilla was warm and good, but it was also soaked from the excess amount of salsa they dumped inside. And since there was no cheese, the rice tasted a a bit dry. 

I am not a big fan of the tortilla chips as I find them to be too thin and crispy for my taste. I definitely like the ones you buy from stores better. However, finishing a ground beef burrito and a meat-less taco left my teeth desiring something to chew on, so I dipped the chips into the red salsa and ate about 1/3 of what they gave me.

Overall, this was a wonderful experience and I'll stop by again next time I hear my stomach loudly protesting my neglect!

The food here is not authentic Mexican - however, the meals here taste great ( a poor college student's dream!)

I have eaten here at least three times in the past month. My personal favorite is the Ground Beef burrito with sour cream and guacamole. It is far tastier then most burritos in the area, and can even compete with Chipotle in my eyes. This place is open very late - about 1:30 A.M., so you can stop by here whenever you're up before that time.

One tip: Always order the small burrito, especially if you eat here often). I did NOT notice a difference in size between the two (I'm sure it exists, but it is minuscule). Although a large is only slightly more expensive, it is essentially the same size, and is not worth it.

I graduated from Cal two years ago and EVERY time I go back to visit for football games or for some dubachery, I'll always go to LABO. Its cheap,its yummy, its fast, and the service is great (when I was in school they even remembered my order). "As good as it gets!"

This is my default place to eat when I go out for lunch. The burritos are very greasy but totally delicious. They never seem to have any shredded beef for the burritos, though, but I'm generally pretty happy with either the ground beef or the chicken. They usually include corn chips with every order as well. Definitely a good, cheap meal.

The only time I will ever eat here again is when I am too drunk to know what the hell I am consuming. The chicken nachos were terrible (really, how hard is it to screw up nachos?). The only positive is that it is open late. Took a long time, but granted it was right after the bars closed so it was pretty busy. If I do eat here again I will try something else besides the nachos.
**Disclaimer: I am from L.A., home of the best Mexican food outside of Mexico, so I am pretty hard to please.

How could one expect a Mexican restaurant in the heart of the Berkeley food ghetto that's open until 2am to really be that good?  I would think that most college campus Mexican restaurants would suck and be an only option type thing late night, which is why La Burrita is so good.  Its actually  decent.  I still don't know what the bathrooms look like, which is a great sign.  I graduated last year, and I still crave it.  Dare I say its the crack of late night snack?  No, that belongs to Jack.

La Burrita is pretty dang good, especially after a night of drinking. This location does it even better than the North Berkeley branch. I tend to order their super nachos because for the price, they're the best bargain. Service is minimal and smiles are rare, but the food is good!

La Burrita, a.k.a. the burrito place next to Top Dog, is a staple for Berkeley college students.  The burritos are cheap, and most importantly, La Burrita is open late.  Unfortunately, the burritos just aren't that great.  If you're drunk and wandering the streets of Berkeley at one in the morning this very well may be the place to go, but if you're looking for a great burrito this is not the place.

Bland meats, the burritos fall apart easily, and there are hordes of drunken nimrods waiting in line.  It's a staple of the stumble up the hill after a night out, but it pales in comparison to Top Dog (which is next door).

Low quality, cheap food. It's open late. It might give you a heart attack after eating too. It's not "BAD" food. As in, it tastes okay, except for the fact they put way too much sour cream in the burritos. The pollo asado has a lot of flavor. I'd avoid anything "wet" or "nacho'ed". It makes everything soggy. It's cool they have a variety of tortillas too. Plus I love the salsa. And the accept credit cards!

Ah, La Burrita, the lifeblood of my freshmen year of college.  What?  My parents have already paid for a meal plan in the dining halls?  Screw that, get me a burrito!  Open later than practically everything else in this town, I'm always glad to take a small detour to La Burrita whenever I'm hungry in Berkeley.

I'm gonna say NO. I had a carne asada burrito that had BEANS! Never have I had that  happen before and it was not at all appetizing. Sorry pals but if you want good cali-mex food you gotta go south to San Diego! This place is jokin....

I've passed La Burrita dozens of times and never seriously entertained the notion of eating there.  When the drunchies struck, Top Dog was the only thing to satisfy my craving.  So when we went to La Burrita for a late lunch, I was intrigued and happy to try it outside of a late night setting.  I ordered the shredded chicken burrito and it was cheap and tasty.  It came with chips and there was an easily accessible salsa bar we took full advantage of.  Maybe still not enough to sway a loyal Top Dog customer during the wee hours of the morning, but definitely a great option for Mexican food during the day :)

The best part about La Burrita is their salsa bar.  Unfortunately, in order to take full advantage of it, one should eat in as you can't really take seven of those little plastic tubs to go (although I suppose you could....).  The reason that this is unfortunate is that I only ever go to La Burrita when I have an awful, irrational, late-night craving for something heavy and rich and cheesy and tortillay - and that means that I'm too embarrassed to ask someone to go with me, and that I'm too embarrassed to eat a burrito in the actual place by myself.

La Burrita burritos are very sauce-y and cheese-y.  Very appropriately late-night food.

Note: I am not from Socal.  I do not know what "real Mexican food" is.
Whenever I have a fix for mexican food this is the place to go! Everything there is good and cheap. I dont see the need to open the Chipotle nearby didnt make me think twice of where to go.

WET BURRITO - sad that they have to microwave it for the cheese on top to make it "wet" but otherwise its really good.

-OR-

CHEESE STEAK BURRITO - pretty much a philly cheesesteak wrapped in tortilla (no rice), NOMS.

They bake or fry their own chips so its fresh and hot & you can take however much salsa and lime you want!

This place is close to campus, so it's good for all the students who live on south side. It's really tiny and uncomfortable to be in, and the food is decent at best. They have a salsa bar with about 6 bowls of salsa, but I suspect that a couple of the bowls actually have the same salsa. I have had the super burrito (carne asada) and a super quesodilla (carne asada). The burrito had nice texture and good proportion between all the ingredients, which is rare, most burritos have too much rice or too many beans. The only downside to the burrito was that it was a bit small. The super quesodilla was your standard meat and cheese, but they packed it with meat, which was surprisingly delightful (I have made another trip to La Burrita for this item). They also give you free chips with your order. The chips aren't anything to brag about, but hey, they're free, get over it. In the end, I say that it's definitely worth a try at least once.

did not disappoint and believe me, it was hyped up enough. tasty food, though, i could have gone without seeing the person who was making my food, use the same gloves she was wearing to wash the dishes...

This is the better of the two La Burritas.  The one on northside has more sitting room and self service chips but I like this one better because when I order the wet burrito to go, they throw it in a box and slap on a bunch of sour cream guacamole and cheese and the throw in the chips and it all melts together into a crispy, cheesy burrito goodness.  That almost sounds like a Taco Bell commercial.  That's really the biggest reason why I like this better.  The food is good, but I also don't know of too many Mexican joints I've been to where the burrito isn't good.  It's pretty hard to mess up a burrito you know.  If Asian people can make it good out of a taco truck, it better be darn good coming from Mexican people in a restaurant!  They're also open late so come on by after getting drunk at Henry's or if you're up for your 4th straight night studying for finals and need food.

I love this place.
Seriously the best burritos I can find in the area.

They have a whole range of choices, to the point
they even have a philly cheese steak burrito. 
I recommend this one.

They have amazing combo meals as well. 

The decor is whatever and theres a usually a line, who cares 
I love their food.

La Burrita has won my heart over in Berkeley.  Hands down, they make my favorite burrito in Berkeley.  I probably go there at least once a week.  They are quick and always make great quality food.  The Super Burritos and La Burrita Special come with a great amount of free chips and the salsa is delicious as well.  The only negative thing I can say is that they don't serve carnitas but otherwise it's my favorite place to eat near campus.

Large portions, food is decent but a little too saucey for me (no pun intended). The tortillas are sometimes soggy which I really dislike. Good food at a cheap price during times of late-night cravings. I got sick from the food here once and have not gone back since. It'll never be the same!

ugh. soupy liquidy burritos that are as thick as the cardboard tube in a roll of toilet paper and not much longer. and incredibly bland salsas. this is the kind of place college kids from parts of the country that don't have anything resembling decent mexican food love because they don't know any better. i bet alot of these college kids also love chipotle and go to la burrita on days they're too lazy to walk the extra block to the absolute disgrace to mexican food that is chipotle. 

take it from a bay area native who grew up on the best mexican food in the country....go somewhere else.

Open late and right next to Top Dog. What more could you ask for? 

If you really want something gorge yourself on at night, you must come here for either a wet burrito or the super nachos. Don't bother with their regular burritos because they're a little on the dry side. Get a wet burrito because it'll be covered in guac and sourcream...mmmmmmm.

Warning: If you have any love for your colon, do not order anything with plain beef. Get the carne asada instead.

I finished my "large" pollo asado in 8 minutes.

I attribute the record breaking time to my high hunger level rather than the tastiness of the burrito itself.  

But the burrito deserves some credit.  I did tell my friend, "Wow...that burrito was soooo tasty!  Much better than the first time I ate here....."

for some reason i like la burrita better than fancier mexican restaurants. i get the enchilada taco plate which is my favorite. i like how they dont smother the enchilada in the sauce and they fill up the entire box. this is the food to  eat when you are starving but are too busy to walk to the swankier northside gourmet ghetto b/c of finals. la burrita really fills me up.

the things that i don't like is that they dont give you that much tortilla chips,  and if you order to-go w/ a friend they will combine ur chips in one bag so they dont have to give you as much. also, the stupid little containers for salsa are annoying since i have to get at least 6 of them for my meal, which really annoys the lady w/ the freckles.

MORE PLEASE!

Before I went to school at Cal, I hated Mexican.  Then I discovered La Burrita, aka LaBo.

FOOD:  The Carne Asada Wet Burrito enough said.

SERVICE:  Fast, friendly.

AMBIANCE:  Quaint little place to have a bite to eat, and they have a nice little patio in the back.

OVERALL:  GO!

OK Mexican food for an affordable price.

Service/Decor: Service is terrible. Sometimes the staff don't understand what you're saying and they're not particularly polite about it. There are a few tables inside but chances are you'll be to-going it anyway.

Food: The food is really cheap and most meals are under $6. You can get enchiladas, nachos with salsa, burritos, etc., most types of foods associated with Mexican cuisine. I haven't found anything particularly appetizing, and I absolutely hate that they microwave ingredients like cheese to melt them. There is something seriously wrong with that.
A boisterous environment that is perfect for enjoying that burrito you've been craving all day. The food is pretty good, the service is quick; but the salsa and chips make the meal.

GREAT super nachos!
staff is friendly and puts up
with me when i'm drunk :p

This review should probably be taken with a grain (or few) of salt - I've been revisiting a lot of old college haunts and destroying a lot of precious memories as a result, so the taste of La Burrita may have just been a welcome reprieve. Or perhaps the pouring rain just made a wet steaming burrito that much tastier, much in the same way that being piss-drunk does. It's certainly not better or equal to many of the other Latin American 4-star restaurants that I've been too, but La Burrita does hit a certain sweet spot.

Being winter break, my old roomy and I were the only ones in the whole joint, so for once, we opted to sit in and eat. I, again, defaulted to one of my old usuals, a large wet chicken burrito. Five minutes after ordering, I was digging in to about a pound of food covered generously in guac, sour cream, and all of the salsas that they had to offer. The chips that come with the meal were still as tasty and crispy as I recalled, and the flavors of the salsas and the burrito mingled well. Sure, the chicken could have been done a little bit better, but in some ways I'd say that La Burrita is tastier than Chipotle - just all comes down to the mood you're in.

Sadly (but not unexpectedly), prices have gone up here as well. My order came out to $7.12 after tax, up from the $5-6 it was when I was still a student. But hey, like then, they still take credit!

As someones who's traveled to mexico many times and is originally from much closer to the border, I have to say that La Burrita just can't compare with authentic mexican food.
That being said, it's open late, it's really filling it's cheap (a poor college student's dream!) and it's pretty tastey. 

I recommend the carne asada burrito with lots of green sauce (the salsas are all self serve) and an horchata. And if you want to sit down and eat I recommend you find somewhere else to do so since there's very limited seating and the restaurant is pretty cramped.

In terms of the service, I wouldn't say that the guys working there are friendly, but they aren't rude either and considering the hoards of drunk students that they have to serve on the weekends I don't blame them. 

La Burrita is a nice meal to pick up if you're studying and find yourself craving a nice filling meal in the late hours of the night.

This was my first taste of Mexican food when I moved up to the Bay Area in '01.  I was disappointed then and I'm disappointed now.  I'm aware that this food is designed for undergrads with undiscerning palates but is cheap street food and they manage to put some deliciousness in their food somehow.

The highlight is that it's open to til 1 or 2am which when you're stumbling home from a frat party makes it alright.  Don't call it Mexican food whatever you do.  It's cheap drunken Berkeley food made for cheap drunken Berkeley students.  Enough said.

If you play with fire, you're gonna get burned.  In the case of La Burrita, fire comes in the form of undercooked pollo asada and the burn radiates from your butt after an excruciating night of chronic diarrhea.  Food poisoning is a bitch rocking a giant strap-on.  To be fair, I have been back multiple times since the aforementioned incident.  And I'm still alive.

I love La Burrita.  I must've eaten a hundred of their burritos while living across the street from them in my college days.  I go back every once in awhile.  I remember the first few times eating there I couldn't even finished a regular sized burrito, and skipped eating the chips altogether.  WIth years of practice I'm proud to say I finish off a large AND the bag of chips.  I don't know why but I feel proud of this scary fact.

You don't come here for gourmet, you don't come here for great Mexican. You come here for a quick, fast, cheap, tasty burrito that will get you stuffed for 5 bucks.  Their food comes with free chips and a salsa bar too.  

I always get a large chicken burrito with 2 green salsas for the burrito.  The green stuff is spicy but perfect.  Chips go well with their red salsa.  

There must be a ton of sodium in their food because I drink a gallon of water after eating their stuff but I don't care.   =]

La Burrita - a haiku:

Authentic it's not
But super carne so yum
Load up free salsa.

Born and raised in Chula Vista, CA...I grew up eating Mexican food.

So um...yeah...no...

While la burrita's mexican food is mediocre, the deceptiveness and pointlessness of their frequent buyer card is quite unique.yes, many businesses try to wiggle out of their promises of rewards for loyalty, but read on, and i think you'll agree that this "policy" is so unique and nonsensical, i have to tip my hat to it.

Recently, having to buy food for a meeting, I bought 15 burritos from the one on north side. I immediately thought, "hey, this will fill up one of those cards, and I can get a free burrito".

I went to the one on south side, and they wouldn't accept it. I noted that the address of the south side location was also on the card. What I did not realize was that instead of having to buy 10 at one location, I had to buy 5 from each location.

FOOLISH ME!!!!

How could I think that I earn a free burrito from simply spending money at only one of their locations? Surely, to really appreciate la burrita, you must sample the subtleties of both the north and the south side.

Needless to say, I was really pissed, and was not about to spend any more of my money getting holes punched. Who knows what excuse they would think of next? Perhaps, o, "you bought too many burritos, we cannot let you consume one more, to protect your health." or, "your card has been punched more than 10 times, clearly you lost your chance".

I have been to Top Dog next door for half my life but untill recently i haven't been here.The food is great and the salad bar is decent also.Just watch out for all the salsa drips and mess around the bar.
the food is always good I been here twice and had the Taco salad. Very fresh and light.

List: Berkeley's Cheapest Eats

Bean and cheese burrito, 2 baskets of chips, salsa, and soda water with lime: $3.25.

The cheapskate beauty of La Burrita is found in the extras: basket of chips, free soda water at the soda machine, and free limes, radish, salsa, and jalapeo at the salsa bar.  La Burrita is second only to Dollar Curry House in value.  Five out of five top ramens.
Mexican. Decent. Late-night.  Get the super nachos, make sure to ask for pollo asado instead of chicken, otherwise they give you shredded chicken, which is VASTLY inferior.
I've had better, but it's decent enough when there's nothing else around. That's really all I can say.

WTF are you people thinking?  I read the reviews thinking this was going to be something special.  Instead, I stood in line for 10 minutes for the most average burrito around.  I ordered the Super Carne Asada Burrito.  It was smaller than the kids burrito at Ramiro and Sons in Alameda.  The flavor was bland, and the salsa bar was mediocre.  You should take your money next door to Top Dog, and thank me later.

So being originally from San Diego, home of awesomely good carne asada and california burritos, carne asada fries, and to die for mexican seafood by the beach(droooool) I naturally have high expectations for Mexican food.  The first time I had La Burrita I was shocked (in a bad way).  Microwaves?? Unheard of!! This place wouldnt last a day in San Diego.  NorCal Mexican food is just weak.  Even the places ppl rave about on Mission St in SF.  It just doesn't compare to places in SD.  But I digress. 

Having endured Berkeley for four years, I got used to La Burrita.  It's not bad for NorCal Mexican food, especially in Berkeley late at night.  Hence three stars.  Also, the Durant location is better than their Northside location.  Northside is cleaner but their burritos are dry and small.  But do yourself a favor and go down south for some good Mexican grub before you rate La Burrita at 5 stars.
Decent burritos at reasonable prices. Worth a stop if you're in the area with a hankering, but otherwise there are a good 10+ Mexican joints within 5 miles which are much better.

ok... uhm ewww??? why is this place so crowded every night?  Is it because its open late and they have nowhere else to go? The burritos were the most tasteless burritos i've ever had... and the nacho supreme... more like stale supreme. Never again...
Skip it.

This place is certainly better than Chipotle, the food is good for food with friends if you want to stay close to UC Berkeley.  The place is a little too tiny, and the lighting and atmosphere isn't all that comfortable.  Simply said, the food was okay, and I wouldn't go back unless my friends wanted to go.  So I guess only go if others want to go.

Aw hell naw. When I went to Cal, my dorm was just up the street, and my apartment a few years later was nearby too. But I will never ever eat at La Burrita. It's convenient that it's open late and your taste buds are dulled by cheap beer but even that can't hide the nastiness. I felt nauseous the few times I came here. And the worst part? When you walk by early the next morning and they are cooking up whatever it is they cook and the smell wafts through the air. When I'm hungover or tired and it's 9am, I do not want the smell of cooking lard in my nostrils. Blech!

La Burrita is consistently good. I think that's why I always come back... 

In fact, when I'm starving to death, they're definitely five stars.

Ladies want a budget lunch? Get ONE taco (try carne asada), to eat in. It'll come with a bunch of chips on a tray. Basically, one taco comes with two tortillas and enough meat for three tacos. Thus, combined with their ample and oh-so-tasty salsa bar and chips, you can be full for a grand total of $2.40. 

I've been here countless times and they've never screwed up an order, which is saying a lot (I HATE when mexican places put sour cream on a burrito when I ask them not to).

Best salsa is the dark red chipotle sauce. I could literally drink it out of a mug.

Come hungry! They wont disappoint. 

And they're open til 3 AM!!!!

Why is it that Berkeley doesn't have any decent burrito places open past 10pm? Sometimes you're just in need of a late-night burrito, but it seems the only option you have is either La Burrita, or something of non-burrito form.

Now, I've had worse burritos, but this place just rubs me the wrong way. First, they don't have carnitas... what self-respecting burrito joint doesn't have pork? they also don't have black beans...

anyway, the burrito was just okay, but just gave me heartburn instead of any sort of gastronomic satisfaction. However, they do have pretty good chips there.

If you're in the area, and need food, skip this place, and opt for top dog or something across the street.

Let's be honest, this place is a glorious haven in the late night/ early morning hours. Open until 3am on weekends, La Burrita hits the all the right drunk spots. 

Granted the food is mediocre, but the cashiers/servers are plenty nice especially when they can tell you're inebriated. I particularly favor the carne asada burrito, the chicken nachos and their house salsa. 

Credit cards are accepted!

Decent cheap Mexican food if you're in the neighborhood... can't say that it was good enough that it would bring me back if I weren't right there, though... shrimp burrito was good but really poorly assembled and fell apart on me.

Yum.  Yum.  Yum.

a "small" burrito is huge.  Less then $5.  

Burritos have an unusual tomato base (marinara-ish) taste to them that is a nice change
up from traditional taquerias.

I scarfed this food down.  Yum.

This place used to be good back in the day.. like 2002.

It has since digressed and is incredibly disappointing. The meat is no longer flavorful, the cheese stingy, and the rice dry. What happened to you guys?

Came here last week and was very disappointed. Perhaps they changed owners or chefs or something, but you can definitely get a better burrito in Cali. Try Gordo's around the corner on Telegraph.

The shrimp burrito is definitely a refreshing change from the usual carne asada/chicken/pork burrito... chock full of crunchy shrimp and tangy pineapple salsa and a mess of other stuff. Mmm

The wet burrito is a safe bet too... a giant burrito hidden under all that sour cream and guacamole and cheesy goodness.

I just ate here. And I mean JUST, ate here, like 10 minutes ago. And it was so bad that I made a mental note in my head while i was eating that pig slop, to come home and write a negative review about this place. 

Anyone who thinks this is any kind of mexican food is fooling themselves. Forget mexican food, this isn't even real food. The salsa was half assed, the beans and chicken were tasteless. None of the ingredients even meshed together to produce any kind of real flavor. It was like I was eating the mexican food from the cafeteria in elementary school. 

I'm originally from SoCal and I will tell you this. This place sucks. the food sucks, the people suck, the everything sucks.
Much like the one on Euclid, but with less seating. Burritos that are tasty and cheap. Especially the fajita burrito, grilled while you wait.

This place is great when you're aching for a burrito.  I usually get the super burrito with GRILLED chicken -- you gotta ask for the grilled chicken otherwise you will get this nasty, goopy shredded chicken.  I think their salsas are pretty good, I just wish they had the spicy peppers/carrots available like other taquerias do (i.e. Roberto's in Las Vegas/San Diego, hands down my favorite taquerias!)  It is a small place that can get crowded around lunchtime.  There is a small patio area in the back where I can usually find a table.  

I haven't been to the La Burrita on the Northside, but apparently they have a large outside patio area for dining.

If you went to Berkeley and never went to La Burrito...you're probably pretty lame. La Burr as we called it was THE place to go after midnight if you were starving. Go here on any weekday night and you will see a long line of loyal La Burrita addicts. The burritos are actually above average and priced fairly so it is a hit with the students. There is very limited seating so most people take their food to go. I have great memories of La Burrita. I love their carne asada burrito.

Usually, I avoid eating La Bur late at night because the food is just greasy and unhealthy; however, one night, Charles L. and I, in our drunken stupor and empty stomaches, paid this place a visit.  In my last minute, late night, fake attempt of being healthy, I ordered the Chicken Fajita Burrito (it's got bell peppers.. kinda healthy.....right? =( )

The Fajita Burrito actually exceeded my low expectations.  Instead of grabbing all ingredients from the pre-cooked trays in the burrito assembly, the meat and bell peppers were cooked when ordered, but due to this process, the burrito takes ~20mins to make!  Didn't fly too well with a hungry drunk like me. When I made my first bite in the burrito, however, the taste was worth the wait.  The burrito was served hot.  Meat was very juicy compared to the other burritos.  Bell peppers..sour cream.. guacamole... yummm..(you might think my senses were skewed by my drunkness, but I came back another time sober and I would give it the same review!)

I've tried all the other mediocre items on their menu before and I'd have to say, if I had to eat something from here to survive (or when I'm drunk, same thing), my fav would be the fajita burrito.

The Honest Truth:  For mexican food in NorCal, its not bad.  Being from San Diego, it isn't that great.  When I am craving mexican food in Berkeley, I will come here.  Usually I get the nachos or the wet burrito.  The meat isn't flavored too well and the tortilla is kinda chewy, but enough salsa will mask the flavor and its a filling meal if you're hungry.


Details:
La burrita is great for the late night meal.  It's open till 2 and the service is pretty fast.  They have a salsa bar, which is something the other mexican places don't have up here.  Their carne asada isn't very soft or flavored well, but their portions are sizeable and enough to make me full.  Their tortilla is kinda chewy and doughy an the bulk of their burritos goes to the rice and beans.  I enjoy their nachos, although you have to eat it fast or else the chips go soggy pretty quickly.  In general, the flavors of their food aren't too outstanding, but covering it with salsa does the job.  Again, not the greatest mexican food, but it gets the job done in Berkeley.

2.5 actually. "LaBo" is not guilt-free.
I sometimes think, at least this burrito has vegetables in it, but who am I kidding?

I end up here when I know one Top Dog will not satisfy whichever munchies I have at the moment.

The chips are hot and made there. Salsa bar has the essentials. I usually go for the regular cheese steak or carne asada burrito. You hear a lot of people say that it's not real Mexican food, but out of the places I've tried around Berkeley, here and Gordo's is probably the closest you could get. (Maybe Steve's Korean BBQ too because that is def not Korean food) &It's affordable and filling for starving college students.

I've actually gotten food poisoning here from the nachos with cheese and the works, but I tend to have a strong stomach for these things so I've come back once or twice. Not for those nachos though.
It's one of those Delicious & Affordable, long lines but short waits, open til 3AM type places. 4 stars for making me crave you days or even weeks later.

cheap mexican...what one would expect.  the food doesn't compare to anything in the mission, but if it's lunch time in berkeley and you're starving, you won't leave here hungry (even though you might die of starvation while waiting in line).  just one note:  the people who work here are *seriously* sketchy.  once we were here (admittedly late), one of the workers kept staring at my friends and me and licking his lips.  he later followed us out of the store even though we tried to ignore him.  we dodged into blondie's down the road only to come out 15min later and find that the guy was waiting in the street with his car to follow us.  i had to whip out the phone and tell him i was calling the cops to get him to leave!!

The Food is low quality and greesy as hell, but it does make the perfect drunk munchies. Just like its neighbor, Top Dog, La Burrita is open til 2am every night. There is a few tables inside the place, so you don't have to stuff your face outside like the Top Dog customers. All orders come with a side of chips. There is a salsa bar which is pretty legit, with 5 different kinds with varying degrees of spice. You can eat for about $6. 

Don't come here if you're looking for quality Mexican Food. I'd recommend visiting the new GORDOS location that just opened up around the corner on Telegraph.

For a delicious burrito in Berkeley this is where I go. I love that I can get it late night too.  GO for the WET burritos, they'll put cheese and sauce on the chips which essentially become Nacho's at that point.   And for a HUGE portion of food (even that half sized one) you'll be paying under $6.  And unlike so many Berkeley small restaurants, they'll take debit/credit.

You can say all you want about La Burrita, but I love the place.  Open late, delicious burritos.  My favorite's gotta be the chicken super burrito or the pollo asada - either way, their chicken burritos are the best.

They have great salsas and hot sauces - though they're not all particularly hot, they're quite flavorful and delicious.  The brown sun-dried tomato one is awesome, and the dark-reddish pepper-ridden one is the spiciest.

Protip:  Though it's not explicit stated, they have a selection of tortillas:  Regular, Spinach, Sun-dried Tomato, & Garlic.  None of them taste that much different, but I find I like the spinach one best.  Gives you the added bonus of knowing when they're making yours, since, ya know, the tortilla is green.
Chunky burritos at a great value. That really is enough said. You Need to make it out here. -Matt

A place to get a Burrito when on campus. They have good burritos, better than decent actually. I like how you can personalize your burrito to have black beans or a healthier tortilla option (wheat,spinach). I wish they had carnitas, a personal happy medium when deciding between chicken and carne asada but they don't.... 

The burrito is a bit expensive for the size you get, but it's either this or chipotle. Options aren't very plentiful. So this is my go-to Cal taqueria. La Burrita, please!

I"m getting hungry just thinking about this place. This place is twice as good after midnight...but then again probably every Mexican place is. The pollo asado burrito is so soft and just melts in my mouth...yum. I don't really like the salsa here. The green one is okay but only because it's spicy. The cashier secretly added like a dollar to my burrito but good thing I caught it! So be careful

Cheap. Standard fare, fast service, near-by Mexican joint. I eat here more often than my 3 stars imply, but i just KNOW what good Mexican food is and what great Mexican food is, and i dont even know if i can put this in that catagory. But this is my husband's spot... he's all about the ground beef burrito. Note that I stick to vegetarian fare when dining here.

i first had the chicken burrito here and it was great. another good place in berkeley to satisfy your hunger pains. unlike some other burrito places, their ingredients are fresh and they pile them on like no other. try the nachos. its a meal big enough for 3 people. it's cheap, its fast, and they are open super late so if you're drunk in berkeley, stop at la burrita

Oh La Burrita.. what happened to you.
Used to be one of my favorite places. Theri burrito was always warm, fresh and tasty.
Now it's just .... Maybe they lost customers over to Chipotle, and have ingredients sitting around for longer, or maybe I just picked the wrong day (haven't back here since my last visit)
I'm disappointed. Pre-disappointment, this was a solid 3 or 4 star place. Now I wouldn't give it more than 2. I'd try La Burrita again sometime in the future, when the horror of my last burrito here is gone from my memory... but not anytime soon
I didn't downgrade it to 1 because of all the fond memories I have of La Burrita
Good food for the price. The pollo asada wet burrito is good and very filling, but I've had better nachos elsewhere. I'll try the shrimp burrito next time!
i only have delicious memories of you

This used to be one of my favorite spots to eat, and I stop by when I can! The food here is as close to authentic as you can get. Their chips are freshly baked and lighly salted and go perfectly with any burrito. My friend usually gets the vegetarian burritos and they're as quality as you can ask for. The salsa bar is also really fun. You can choose and mix any of their salsas. Service time is also very fast even when busy during lunch hours. EAT HERE

I don't know why this doesn't have better ratings.  La Burrita is the perfect meal to grab after class.  I think the magic in these burritos is the wrapping.  The burrito is so tightly wrapped, that the flavors meld together and you never have to worry about rice spilling out.  My favorite is the pollo asado, although I have heard that people think its too dry.  I think its fine and well seasoned.  My friends also love the carne asada.  And the special burrito is the best (sour cream included in burrito).  And the salsa is of course perfect!  This is the best meal for the price you pay.
Your classic, hole-in-wall, California burrito place.  Inexpensive and generally good food that fills you up.
When you make the Asian Ghetto look like Chez Panisse by comparison, that's not good. Not good at all.
Carne asada burrito was pretty good.. not GREAT.. but good.  Nachos were whatever.  I'd probably come back though :) just because "open late + pretty good = great" :D

PROs:
+Delicious WET burritos
+Cheap!
+Friendly staff

CONs:
-Drunk frat guys like to fight outside
-Not enough inside seating (but that kind of adds to the "hole-in-the-wall" feeling... so we'll make this a neutral point)

The familiar and typical burrito joint. 

This location of la Burrita is not bad and offers a few more options than the northside one. I was surprised to see lengua (beef tongue) as one of the meat options so I went ahead and got the tongue quesadilla. It was alright and not bad value for $5.50.

Not my favorite burritos in Berkeley, but a safe choice for a quick and casual meal.

The food at La Burrita is nothing spectacular, but it is spectacular when you're drunk after a long night of dancing! This place gets packed around 1:30 AM, and no one in there is sober. It is also very cheap, which lured me here during my college years. Just stick with the burritos, and make sure you get lots of chips and salsa :) The chips are pretty go

In actuality should I be giving this place 5 stars? Probably not. Did I think this place was practically fine dining when I was college? Of course. Have I been there while sober since graduating and thought to myself "This place is okay...but not as good as I remember it?" Yep. Have I been there as drunk adult after a Cal football game and remembered why I loved this place so much in college? I just did recently!!! 

Like I said, La Burrita is not the greatest Mexican food in the world....especially when your 1) sober and 2) you've put your education into somewhat good use and are able to eat at places a step or two above this. But dammit...it's LA BURRITA and still tasty. 

I had the pleasure of going here after Cal's opening football game this season. Well, not right after the game, but after downing several pitchers at Henry's after the game. I'm happy to report that nothing has changed. The same people still work there, the menu is still the exact same, the salsa bar is the same, the crappy soda fountain is still the same, and I think the prices are still the same. 

Most of the time in college I opted for the chicken or carne burrito and a small is pretty filling.  This last time I went with chicken.   Of course I get it with guac and sour cream (you know I'm drunk when I get sour cream), and I'm a pinto bean kind of guy. Even if your not a fan of La Burrita you have to be impressed with how tight they wrap those burritos...there's nothing falling out of those!!! 

And of course in typical drunken La Burrita night fashion I woke up the next morning with a ton of extra salsa and chunks of tin foil from perfectly wrapped burrito scattered throughout my hotel room (only in college it was my dorm room or bedroom in frat house). I miss college...and the comfort of La Burrita only being a few blocks away :)
The best burrito I've had in my entire life. And I've had alot of burritos. Five stars food alone.

I moved to Tucson after graduating and even with the plethora of Mexican food available, I still dream about La Ba. For me, the onlyyyy thing to get is the wet burrito. Shockingly, it seems they are one of the few joints to get that right. How I miss you.
Cheap, no thrill place for a fast meal.  The carnitas doesn't taste like    grilled; instead it's diced meat slobbed with beans, rice and salsa.  It reminds me of Taco Bell.

Another restaurant that I miss a lot in Berkeley besides Gypsy's. I used to come here at least once a week to get my greasy Mexican food fix during my college days. The price is cheap. The portion is big. They made it fast. The location is convenient. The burritos are yummy.

My favorite is the Carne Asada in tomato tortilla with guacamole and sour cream, without the beans. And lots of salsa for my chips. They even have outdoor seating at the back. How fancy!

I'm not much of a burrito fan, so I can't speak about those. I had their nachos once and was so nauseated I never went back. Simply inedible. End of story. Whatever sober person (sober being the operative word) thinks this is good Mexican food is seriously deprived and/or delusional. Go to Mario's La Fiesta down the street at Haste & Telegraph. You will thank me for it, I promise.

i LOVE this place. their wet burritos are so yummy for what you pay. i would be sad if this place ever closed -- the salsa bar is great too, and I don't even like cilantro. working in sf for awhile now makes me miss the easy accessibility of a cheap, greasy, mexican food fix from the good ol' berkeley days.
I'll drive about 30 miles on occasion just for the steak burrito and spicy carrots! This place is delicious!

-----Visits
Many!

-----Service
The service is exactly what you want at this restaurant, which is designed for take-out. It's quick, efficient, and the employees are happy to help with any weird, random requests. They are very polite and friendly for a fast food place, but I may be getting extra good service because they know I am Mexican.

-----Food
One of the only places in which burritos without  meat are very filling. They have rice, beans, salsa, and sour cream or guacamole for a little more. You can change the tortilla type at no extra charge (there's tomato, spinach, and wheat). An awesome place for vegetarians. The Enchiladas are okay, nothing to write home about.  But if you want a little jazz with your burrito, get it wet---enchilada sauce+cheese melted on top of it with chips. I don't eat meat but I have heard from my carnivorous friends that meat at La Burrita is questionable and should be avoided, so I'll pass that on.

-----Price
Really great prices. The prices have gone up a bit (about $0.40) but they're still pretty good. About $3-4 for a small and $4.50 for a large veggie burrito. Oh, and people frequently going to Chipotle are getting ripped off. I'm sorry, but at $8-9 a burrito, no matter how big or many calories, you're paying way too much. La Burrita gets the job done for half the price.

-----Atmosphere
Definitely way better to take it to go than eat there, since the place is cramped and always flooded with people standing around waiting for their food around lunch time. But if you do want to eat there, you should take your food outside to the back patio seating. It's quite pleasant on a nice day.
ew.

First burrito I had here was so wet. And that IS what she said.....it was pretty gross.

But every burrito I've had after that has been not too shabby considering it's like a 4 minute walk from my dorm :) I like the shredded pork. Definitely not the best burrito I've had but it's nice that they give you free chips even though I hate tortilla chips.

If you're eating with a large party and someone finds something in their food, chances are it's going to be me.  Yes - I am the person who always finds something in my food, and yes - I am always greatly disturbed.  Usually I stop eating.

La Burrita is a staple for Cal students.  One day I got my burrito to go.  As I bit into it, I found a rubber plug (for the trays they keep their meat in) in my burrito.  Unphased, I kept eating it.  That my friends, is how much I like La Burrita! 

Their red salsa is the best!

Alright, forget about all the dopefiends, crackhead, hippys, and crazy people berkeley has to offer. It also offers one of the best burrito spots which is this place, La Burrito. I get the same thing everytime which is the steak la burrito special burrito (no beans and salsa). Although it is not greasy and oily, it still hits the spot. Sometimes too hard, and puts you right to sleep. It is consistent everytime i have gone, it has tasted the same which means a lot to me because it never disappoints and is ALWAYS what i expected, a delicious a** burrito. The ingredients in the burrito are done just right, not too much or too little of anything. The service is also superb, they will have your order out and done with the quickness whether they are busy or not. They have always got my order right even though I am picky because I don't like frijoles(AKA beans) and salsa. The employees once gave my friend a whole bottle of tapatio for free just because he recognized us and how we always ask for it which I thought meant a lot because it sure as hell ain't free for them. All in all, best burrito I have tasted in my life. If your lucky and come late night, there will be bums willing to dance for your coins or dollars so bring some extra change.

Two words: Cheesesteak Burrito

Greatest burrito without beans ever.

Getting a special, carne asada burrito here is always a colon-ary delight. From day 1 back in '96 to this day, I've returned here like a crack addict returns to her pusher. I don't want to play up their food. Cheap, college mexican food can only be taken so far. But their burritos smothered in their Special Red Salsa is the BEST! AND you can get that at roughly $5 (give or take depending on what size you get). 

Throughout college their large burritos would fill me to the point of belt-busting pain. Several years ago I had to transition to the "regular." Call it old age, I guess. This is definitely cheap college food at it's greatest.

People in college are idiots.
College students are just the concentrated version of why the entire world hates Americans. Fuck college. Just loud, obnoxious artistic deficits that crave attention. Just because your parents are spending a small fortune so you can binge drink and get a degree in some obscure field doesn't mean you are ambitious.

This place. Whatever... it was ok, I guess. Fast and impatient (was that redundant?)
Not particularly vegan friendly. I asked for no cheese or sour cream but am pretty sure traces of ingredients go flying everywhere. To be on the safe side, skip this place if you are vegan. Otherwise, decent yet barely passable at best. 

Probably your favorite if you are a frat boy with a nickname like chongo or beta. Fuck you social butterfly, sycophantic, insecure idiots. You are grown men for Christs sake! What are you doing in a secret club!? Get a job and stop jerking each other off long enough to realize that whether you like it or not, high school has to end eventually.

In theory, La Burrita is amazing. It's the perfect place for starving college students to ward off the onset of scurvy and rickets another week. Simple, large sized, cheap burritos coupled with a great location, late hours, and additional bonuses like free chips and salsa.

But all of that means very little if the food is inedible. My first few times with this place was years ago, and was scaring enough for me to swear this place off for life. Maybe I just had a weak constitution? Since then my palate, tolerance, and mind have all expanded greatly. I decided to give them another chance when I found myself escorting a group of friends here one evening. Against an almost psychic nagging against the selection, I ordered a regular carne asada burrito.

Ignoring the gut-wrenching stomach aches that ensued, even the ingredients were bland, dry, and unappetizing. The carne asada was tough, chewy, and tasted like cardboard. The salsa and guacamole had little effect besides making the tortilla soggy. The rice and cheese seemed to only add padding and filler rather than be a tasty ingredient.

I couldn't force myself to finish my food, and (surprise) it was even worse the next day when I tried giving my second chance burrito a second chance of its own. If you're down with cheap, intestinal punishment, visit La Burrita. Otherwise, any random taco truck will give you better food.

La Burrita.  Another one of those unexplainable Berkeley cravings.  I love it.  I mean, really, you can go to Chipotle and hook up a solid carne asada burrito with extra cheese and all the fixings, but will it have that unmistakably LB orange liquid dripping off the bottom?  I don't think so.
I think this was the first late-night drunk food I ever had, so that probably gives it an extra star...

This place defined my college experience... I probably ate here at least twice a week for the five years I lived in Berkeley... and at least twice a month for the rest of my time in the Bay Area. 

My burrito of choice is the Ground Beef Special (#9?). You have to eat it with the spicy green sauce for the full effect. 

People will say, "you can get better burritos in the Mission or LA"... And you know, that might be true... I've had some pretty great burritos in both places. But extremes aside, it's a damn good burrito. 

To me La Burrita is like eating my mom's cooking... there may be better, there's definitely worse, but La Burrita is home.

I went to Mills and, in case you didn't know, everything in East Oakland closes down when the sun sets.  If we wanted food we'd grudgingly have to make the trek to Berkeley.  Point is, La Burrita serves a huge, and I mean huge, plate of beans and rice at 1 am for something like a dollar.

La Burrita is every students favorite stop shop for a quick cheap lunch or satisfying late night snack to fill their over-the-legal-limit tummies.  And while i do miss this cute little box of a restaurant near my former school, i can remember it being just... "OK"

The only acceptable items on the menu are the burritos.  They are big and cheap (like, $5).  Juicy and filling.  I always ordered the Carne Asada Burrito with Guacamole.  I wouldn't recommend any other items (i've tried them).  They just don't live up to what i feel good Mexican food should taste like.  They are too... watered down.  But, the burrito is enough to lift this place to fame.

Stop by for cost and convenience.  But don't give up on the search for better Mexican food.  I'n my own person stamp of "Good, Better, Best Mexican Food" i would give this place a "Good Mexican Food" label.

5 stars, 4 based on service alone.  I used to come in here at least 3 nights a week, always past 11:30pm.  

Me: Can I have a burrito please
Them: Small #12, no lettuce, wheat tortilla?
Me: Yes please
Them: $4.01
Me: Thank you.

Sometimes I would be getting dinner for my boyfriend as well

Me: Can I have 2 burritos please?  On the first...
Them: Small #12, no lettuce, wheat tortilla?
Me: Yes, thanks, and for the second...
Them: Small #6, no cheese?
Me: Yes (looks down)
Them: $7.58
Me: Thank you.

No matter who was at the register, there was someone around who knew my order, and would have it ready within 5 minutes of me walking through the door (even if there was a line).  The burritos are filling and genuinely good (you're definitely not going to find anything better after midnight) and you can't beat the chips and salsa with a stick.  If you're really wanting to do some damage, get the burrito wet (smothered in cheese and enchilada sauce), but don't say I didn't warn you...

How long have they been at this location?!?  Have we been so blinded and focused on Top Dog that we never knew its existence?!? 

On our way to Top Dog, always one of the reasons to visit Berkeley, I noticed this place.  Looks like a good local taqueria.  Hubby said he thinks it has always been there but we just never paid attention - no way!  Debate was Top Dog first or ?  Yes, Tog Dog must come first but we will come back for a taste of something.

We returned as promised.  The kitchen is to the right, the register and burrito counter in the middle and 5-6 tables of 2 and the salsa bar wraps up the place.  I believe they do have outdoor seating in the back.  

The menu is on a large board behind the counter.  Your standard fare - choice of burrito, taco, and some combo dishes.  We decided to try their taco with carnitas - were told they don't use carnitas?  Ok, what are our meat choices?  chicken, beef or steak.  Alright, let's get the carne asada.  We also ordered a horchata.  The total was about $4 ONLY!

Ok, the horchata was not bad.  Not cold enough, they didn't give too much ice - surprise!

The taco was good.  For the price, you get two corn tortilla, lots of flavorful meat, lettuce and cheese.  The salsa bar is AWESOME - I scooped a couple of the hot sauce and grabbed a container of the salsa for the chips that the taco came with - all for $4!  We will return to try something else.
