We love this neighborhood because of all these wonderful cheap eats...you can fill up any tummy with $5 and less!

I remember this burrito shop as not having any refried beans and being of just passable quality.  Two stars for being a refuge of late night sustenance (although Top Dog is right next door so why even bother with this place).

The Great Taco War...
I was reveling in my recent Victory at El Grullense, being a bit smug, handing out nylons to the local hotties.  Dive Bar - we drank, we smoked.  
Ok, then Jack , you get the enemy a bit tipsy, then... AMBUSH.
Jack:  "Oh, I know this little taco joint, let's hit that."  Indeed, how long have you had this one tucked away??
The tacos are huge, absolutely staggering amounts of beef.  Salsa bar with great choices, including a killer hot sauce.   They give you your tacos on a tray and literally throw 11 or 12 chips aboard - like shrapnel.  It was about 11p and the place was alive with everybody getting their late-night fix.  Limited indoor seating, so if you spy an open table, have somebody commandeer it.
Jack:  You may have won the battle, but not the war.

Was hungry and was craving a good burrito. Coming here, it was a success. It was an early Saturday afternoon and there were two patrons in there. The menu hangs over the counter with the register and a salsa bar. They had burritos, tacos, tortas, nachos, etc. The salsa bar had at least five different sauces plus lemons and limes.

I ordered the Steak Fajita burrito to go with extra sour cream (yum!) and took a mild chunky salsa container and the green jalepeno sauce. The burrito was small in the bag in comparison to other restaurants. But when I bit into it for the first time it was sooo good. The jalepeno sauce was awesome that I didn't even bother tasting the mild salsa. There was plenty of good steak and like a friend's review, it was juicy. And tho I thought it was a small portion, I only ate half of it and saved the rest for later.

I think I'll eventually try the carnitas, tacos and nachos.

YOU MUST KNOW WHAT TO ORDER! 

If you go to any restaurant, most places don't make EVERYTHING on their menu very well. With that said, most of the items on the La Burrita menu is mediocre but the item that redeems this entire restaurant is their SHRIMP BURRITO.

WHY SHOULD I ORDER THE SHRIMP BURRITO?
1. You get at least 1 shrimp per bite. Who does that?? No one else gives that much seafood in any seafood item.
2. PINEAPPLE SALSA is soooooo good.

Order nothing else, PERIOD.

ENJOY!

Get me wet baby... super wet... mmmm...

SUPER WET BURRITO! 

Get your mind of the gutter kids...

On a budget? Starving enough to believe there is a small and malnourished country inside of your belly? This is where to go.

Open till 3AM! Make sure to hit it up sometime and get SUPER WET! (^_^)

I  would give La Burrita 4 stars, but I'm throwing an extra star in for sentimental value-- my husband and I met at Cal and one of the first meals he ever bought for me was a super chicken burrito. What can I say, I guess I'm a cheap date.

There were many nights when we lived in the dorms that a group of us would go to La Burrita to pick up burritos in the wee hours of the morning. After all these years, the burritos still taste the same as the first time I had it.

I hate eating dry burritos, so their "liquidy" burritos are right up my alley. Actually, I wouldn't call them liquidy, just moist. I especially like when the cheese is still hot and melty.

Whenever the hubby and I visit Berkeley, we always try to stop by La Burrita to pick up some burritos-- it's makes us feel like we are in college again.

(read: the night before Christmas)

It is the night of winter-wonderland and all through the house, cheep vodka is flowing, straight into my mouth.

I'm dressed as an icicle, my best friend is too, another girl is a polar bear, with fuzz on her shoe.

As the party gets going, I get much too wasted, and decide LA BURRITA would be satisfying and tasty.  

We hike the 5 blocks, white fishnets and all, with platforms so high, I'm surprised I didn't fall.

La burrita is packed, but we order with ease, burrito and nachos, super grande, extra cheese.

Our food was wrapped up, and handed to me, and when I took the first bite, I giggled with glee.

The burrito was good, the nachos were better, if I ever go back, I'm bringing a sweater.

La Burrita doesn't offer a lot of food options, just a "fix" menu. burritos (only carna asada, chicken, shrimp, etc.) very small space similar to top dog a few doors over.

eats: carna asada burrito(5.29)
-grilled steak with beans, rice, cheese, cilantro, quacamole extra
-narrow long tube-like burrito, first half satisfying, last half so so.
-came with "flat" tasting chips
-salsa bar available.

frijoles refritos:
-only about 5 tables available for sit down
-order ready within minutes.
-la burrita not a value, but a viable option.

The gluttonous day was far from over after hitting up Top Dog next door.

If the line for La Burrita snakes out onto the sidewalk, don't be too worried, the counter/cashier is just a few steps from the front entrance.

Above the front counter, a giant whiteboard outlines the menu; make note that its absent of the usual variety of [meat] choices that can be found at more authentic taquerias.  Chicken, steak, ground beef, and (though its not on their website menu) shrimp.

The indoor dining area is minuscule and there are probably too many tables/chairs for the space allocated making the little space feel cramped and uncomfortable.  There are also a handful of rickety tables in the back/patio (al fresco!).

The food, though a far cry from anything I'd call authentic, wasn't bad.  It was flavorful and fresh, and cooked-to-order, if the moderate wait is any indication.  In my case, I had the shrimp burrito (Rice, Grilled Onions, Bell Peppers, Pineapple, Salsa, Lettuce and Sour Cream).  Even without the rice, the burrito was hearty and surprisingly filled with shrimp in almost every bite.

Then there's the self serve salsa bar.  What is it about self serve salsa bars? Is it our inherent "oh, sh*t... free?!" consumer response?  Is it that they totally cater to a yearning to be a culinary mastermind?  Or maybe we're just relieved to find some modicum of control over something, ANYTHING, in our topsy-turvy lives, even if its the small consolation of condiments we can call "ours"?  No? Just me?  Nevermind. I have issues.

Not a bad place for affordable eats, lack of authenticity not withstanding and crowded walkways allowing.  Wouldn't seek it out, but if I'm in the area, sure...
__________________________________________
Next time, I'll order nachos, just for the fact that they make no apologies for their use of a microwave.  No pretensions here.  Chips, pile on the shredded cheese, place in microwave, set to "molten goodness", proceed.  Top with self served salsa. Nom.

If you're going to stand out for selling Mexican food in California, you're going to have to bring your best game. While this little taqueria off University Ave. is clean, quaint and accessible, they didn't deliver when it comes to their biggest selling point: the food. My burrito was a mushy, poorly assembled mess of beans, ridiculous amounts of guacamole and gamey chicken. This may fly with drunk and starving college kids but I couldn't even finish it when eating cold sober. To make things worse, it was skinny and small and cost almost 8 bucks. Sad to say, but I think I could find a better - and far cheaper - burrito option at Taco Bell. Time to make a run for the border.

Chipotle's line came out, all the way onto the sidewalk, so I decided to seize the opportunity and try the famous La Burrita before graduating.

I like tacos, not burritos, so I ordered the Taco Rancheros with shredded chicken, for less than $5. So far, so good.

The tacos took a while to prepare, for whatever reason. And even worse, they don't give you salsa--you have to get it at the stand, in these tiny plastic containers. The result is that it takes FOREVER to get your sauces. Bunch of dudes with 5 containers lined up all pretty, slowly filling them up one at a time.

The tacos were forgettable. And tiny. Chicken, onion, and brown sauce...boring. Call me strange but I like cheese on my tacos...and corn is pretty good too. As for the free nachos, I ran out of salsa immediately. I regretted not filling up 5 containers as well...

I could have sworn I saw microwaveable Taco Bell cheese dip at Walgreen's though. Hmmm...

It was the night of Halloween, and this place had a line that stretched about a 1/4 of a mile long. Or so it seemed, since I was tired, drunk, hungry, and my feet were killing me from wearing 3-inch high heeled boots.

Well, the long wait was worth it. I was satisfied.

I have to penalize them for serving ground beef burritos. Mexicans do not use ground beef in their cuisine. 

Other than that, this place is a solid option for late night eating if you are in the Berkeley area.

I give it 5 stars because they seriously have the best chicken tika masala around. I've yet to find a place in LA, OC or London that tops this place. The owners are extremely nice and genuinely appreciate every patron that walks through the door. (After ordering): "Siittt doooowwwwnnn! Have some teaaaa!" 

House of Curries = WIN.

This is my favorite Indian restaurant near the Berkeley campus. The best free chai tea I had. It's great that it is self-served, so you don't need to tip. I like getting the eggplant curry or chicken tikka masala with aloe or garlic naan.

This is the best option for Indian food on Southside near campus.  The food is not spectacular, but everything tastes good and is reasonably priced.  It's also nice that they have free chai.

The naan here is pretty consistent, too.  I've never had it be dry or too thin.  House of Curries is a good, dependable Indian restaurant.  If you want the best Indian food in Berkeley, you can head down University Avenue, but if not, House of Curries is "A-Ok!"
Very good, but not as good as the one on College (the naan has been overcooked every time I've gone).

Amazing!!!! A girlfriend of mine who went to Berkeley introduced me to this place! Super affordable and great food! Free chai tea that taste like hk style milk tea. Everything is self served. The last time I was there I had the mushroom and the char boiled chicken. Delish! Can't wait till I come back again,

Now that Indian Flavors Express has appeared, House of Curries is no longer my goto for Indian/Pakistani.  House of Curries has better naan (thicker and/or fluffier, and the aloo naan is great), but the chicken tends to be tough and hasn't had the sauce soak in.

Don't be confused by the sign above that says Beau Sky Hotel, cause definitely the first time I walked by, it sure as hell confused me.

I went here last night and nom-ed my way to happiness. We ordered a paneer tikamasala and the lamb vindaloo, with 2 nan. The tikamasala was delicious, and could only be described by creamy goodness. The lamb vindaloo was definitely more on the salty spicy side, but none the less good.

Overall, House of Curries hits the spot. The guy at the counter is always nice and friendly, and so far, all there plates and utensils look clean. Yay for Indian!

love this place because it is so cheap and close to my university apartment. the quality is good for the price, I always get Paneer tikka masala or a biryani. The garlic and the stuffed cheese naan are very good with a creamy curry. Always hits the spot with quick service, good samosas and chutneys and the option to sit outside on a nice day.

I listened to Yelpers' recommendations and ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala. The cashier asked if I wanted to order some rice or naan with that, but I told him no, not realizing that the Chicken Tikka Masala is just curry and chicken. Thankfully, my friends ordered naan so I got to share with them!

The Chicken Tikka Masala was greattttt!!! There was a good amount of chicken, but because it was pretty dry, I had to cut up the chicken into smaller pieces so that it could soften a little in the curry. I kept thinking about how good the curry would have tasted with rice, but the naan was great too :).

When I got home, I also realized that I had a bunch of coupons to this place!! Not that this place isn't already affordable for college students, but look around for deals/coupons for this place because they are out there!!

I just ate the aloo palak (spinach with potatoes). It was good, nice amount of spice, big portion. I also had naan. Huge portion, but not too flavorful. The decor is nice, and the employees were pleasant. Just an average experience.

This restaurant was located in a small hotel and looked pretty nice on the outside. There were a lot of people sitting outside but we chose to sit inside. We got the chicken tikka masala and lamb curry with plain naan and garlic naan. It was pretty good, but the flavors were strong and we felt really full after eating. I didn't like the chicken since it was kind of dry. The plain naan wasn't thick enough to hold in the sauce, so it got a bit messy. The garlic naan was pretty thick and flavorful. The chai tea was nice on a 60 degree weather afternoon. Will come back again and try the other curries and order some biryani :)

Upside: Good food, Good Prices, Located across from the asian ghetto, quick

Downside: Dirty, bus your own table (but isn't that most of Berkeley, HA!)

Bottom line: I've eaten here repeatedly when I am in Berkeley and will return to eat here again.  I recommend this place.
I like the karahi gosht.

I love this place.The lines are long, but they go fast. The wait for the food is longer. Finding a table can be very difficult. Hence the minus one star.

You can't beat the free chai.  I especially love the Lamb Tikka Masala. I've been here so many times, and you can't go wrong here.  

The service is pretty good and the people at the register are very friendly.
One of the best Indian restaurants in Berkeley, hands down.

I've been coming here a lot recently on nights when I don't want to cook and am too lazy to find a friend to eat with. Yes, I eat by myself, and no, it's not awkward and lonely. I usually get the Lamb Curry or Chicken Tikka Masala with Plain Rice. I tend to get Garlic Naan when I come here with friends, so everyone can share.

I've never had this type of Indian/Pakistani food before coming to Berkeley, but I must say I've fallen in love. Granted, there are better places to get curry but House of Curries is super convenient and cheap. Food comes out really fast, and the staff is always friendly. The restaurant isn't too clean, but it isn't dirty, either. Lots of space inside and a cute patio for outdoor seating. And when I'm done with my meal, I just walk across the street and get a drink from Sweetheart Cafe!

I went here yesterday for the first time with my friend from UC Berkeley. The actual building from the outside is very noticeable -- it's this big white building with a white fence around it.

You order your food at the register, and then you get an order number and it is brought to you later. You have to pick up your own plates, utensils, water cups, etc. though. And they also offer complimentary hot chai tea, which was nice.

Honestly I don't think it was the greatest Indian food I've ever tried, but it was decent. A little overpriced in my opinion...my friend and I nearly spent $27 when we could have gotten the same amount of food at a standard Indian lunch buffet for way cheaper! 

I got the chicken tikka masala and I was a little disappointed that there were only a few chunks of chicken in there. I thought that the portions in general were a little on the small side. My friend and I also shared the palok paneer and that was pretty good. We got garlic naan and I was surprised to find saffron (or at least I THINK it was saffron), on top of it! That was delicious.

Definitely a decent Indian restaurant near the UC Berkeley campus. Not the greatest place ever, though.

I'm surprised I haven't written a review for this place yet because I am a huge fan of House of Curries! Definitely my favorite Indian place in Berkeley. When I was going to Cal, I ate here at least once, if not two or three times a week. Delicious Chicken Tikka Masala - creamy, spicy, and so good! The Chicken Saag is also delicious! The naan is good, though sometimes it's a little too crispy.

The service here is really friendly, and the pricing is reasonable. And bonus, they have free chai! It's strong on the caffeine though, so I have to remember to limit myself to 2 cups. hehe.

Great place to come to on a rainy day, or really any day. 
I remember spending several rainy afternoons in here, eating & studying :)

I love their spicy chiken tikka masala here(you have to order it specially spicy). I also like their rice and their garlic naan. The only thing is that it is a little pricey. I always spend more than $10 for a meal here.

For the same price you can get all you can eat at Na'an and Curry at only slightly less quality, for very little more you can get something far tastier at mount everest on telegraph, or on west side. Really just an indian option across the street from asian ghetto, the flavors certainly weren't very robust.

The day House of Curries took over that old hotel building on Durant from an Italian restaurant that was, alas, pretty good but getting walloped by Gypsies across the street, I dropped Naan n Curry like a bad date.

The chicken tikka masala is amazing and the servings on all of their curries are impressive. Can't go wrong here. Poor Naan n Curry, no longer the Indian place to go on Southside.

This is a great indian place close to campus.  The Chicken Tiki Masala is quite good and the prices can't be beat, everything is less than $10 and the servings are reasonable, not huge, not petite.

Unfortunately the Benghan Bharta (eggplant) has too strong of a mustard taste, or it would be a 5 star place.
Let me live in a house of curry with chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, and unlimited chai tea, and I would die a happy man.

http://www.berkeleygoodlife.com/coupons/house-of-curries

If it weren't for that coupon, I would not frequent House of Curries often. Their curry is okay, and the naan is usually nice and fluffy. Sometimes they burn my naan, though, and that makes me sad.

Chicken Tikka Masala is a safe choice, but try their other curries! I have enjoyed Chicken Palak, Cholay Chicken, Chicken Vindaloo, and Saag Daal.
I can't even count how many times I've eaten here in the last two years!! I always get the paneer tikka masala, but each dish I've tried is really good!!

I went to House of Curries to compare the dishes I usually get from Naan N Curry.  I found mixed results on comparing the two.  I liked HoC's garlic naan better.  It was both fluffy and crisp, and more uniform than NNC's.  I liked the chicken in HoC's chicken tikka masala (it was more tender and they gave more chicken than NNC), but the curry wasn't as creamy and rich as NNC's.  If you like chicken tikka kabab, NNC has more tender kababs.  I have yet to try other dishes to compare the two places, but I wouldn't mind eating at HoC again.

Limited seating and gets very busy! There's a secret and I'm not sure if I should share this but....there's more seating in the back! =X More seating that not many know about because its on the other side of the restaurant. 

Loved the vegetarian curry, garlic naan was perfectly crisp and flavorful, chicken tikka masala and chicken tandoori were also tender. The portions are small, it's good to order a variety of dishes if you are eating in group of 3 or more. 

Great complimentary chai tea of course and friendly service!

Great food and vibe, with large portions at a good price. Kreaky B. loves hanging out in front, drinking chai and eating tasty lamb curry. HOC also serves great palak paneer and squash. 

Sure, there is are a lot of good Indian restaurants in Berkeley that are as good as HOC (one of them is around the corner.) But those other places close early and don't have a front porch with the view like HOC. So stop by if you are walking around Telegraph.

Average Indian food at a relatively convenient location. Service is pretty friendly--order, sit at a table with the number and the server brings it out. 

Usually get the ever so classic CTM (yes, if you have had Indian food, you'll know what that stands for). Portion-wise, it's not really that much and you get a few chunks of chicken. Enough to get a person to that "just satisfied" phase I suppose, if you eat slowly. I've gotten the samosas once, which I liked. They came piping hot, but was a little on the greasy side (deep fried after all...). Also have gotten the cholay chicken because I love me my garbanzo beans and that dish was just okay too. Nothing spectacular. 

Naan here tastes comparable to other similar Indian restaurants. I kinda do like the tea they have, but it always runs out quickly and then refill time varies. :\

I live in a San Jose and I will drive all the way to Berkeley just for House of Curries.  And if I am in Berkeley visiting friends, they know that we are going to have to eat at House of Curries for one of our meals.

This place isn't so fancy, but it's friendly, inexpensive, and has a Chicken Tikka Masala that makes my taste buds sing.  I especially enjoy the free milk tea that comes with meals.

A curry and a side of naan or basmati rice is a nice amount of food (with a little bit left over to take home or to share with a friend)

I consider this a decent place to grab Indian food on Southside. Not the best, but it wasn't horrible. I'm just grateful this is walking distance from my apt.

Food: I usually get the Chicken Tikka Masala (chicken is usually soft and sauce was flavorful). I consider this my go-to Indian dish. Note to self: explore more of the menu. I  I did try the lamb curry for the first time last night and I was STUFFED after finishing it off with an order of regular naan. Sauce was nice and spicy but a bit on the oily side. I was a little disappointed in the lack of lamb, but the lamb flavor was infused throughout the sauce. Half of my lamb was a bit on the tough side though. 

Always a fan of free chai, so that's a plus. 

Atmosphere: I get a laugh out of the Chinese lanterns in this Indian restaurant. There's usually enough seating for small parties (up to 5 or 6 ppl). I would love to dine alfresco at  night when the weather warms up. 

Price: The cheapness of this place earns an extra star (I would give 3 stars for the taste of food alone). But if I can walk away from a restaurant feeling stuffed for less than 10 bucks, then I'm a happy gal. My roommate and I definitely fell into a major food coma after eating here last night. 

If you're ever feeling up for a snack, stop by for their naan. Garlic naan is the bomb! Just chew some gum afterward and everything will be peachy. :)

If you took advantage of the Munch On Me promo, make use of it soon!

Great curry =)

Their paneer tikkimasala is excellent and it comes piping hot. Goes great with naan or rice(I prefer rice). And you get free chai with your orders. You get more than enough for a filling meal for 7-8 bucks!

Their flavored naans aren't really worth it, neither are their biriyani. Everything else is pretty good and made to order too.

I only wish it was a bit cleaner and handicap accessible.

If I could, I would give House of Curries a 3.5 star-rating to be more accurate.

House of Curries is definitely the best Indian food on southside, but it's not the BEST. Their vegetable korma masala is tasty, but is incredibly greasy.  After letting the dish sit for 10 minutes, the sauce and the grease separated leaving a THICK layer of oil on top of the korma masala -- which was definitely a major turn-off for me.

Another delicious, but lighter dish that I prefer here is the yellow lentil daal.  Their naan is always fresh and never dry too!

On the down-side, there are always flies flying around the restaurant, so I prefer to pick up food to-go.

This place is really casual.  You order at the register, bus your own table, and sit anywhere you like.  Prices are dirt-cheap, lunch for two was about $10.  We ordered the chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, and plain basmati rice.  Unfortunately, they were out of raita that day.  The selection of items is pretty good, although I was a little disappointed that they don't have have my sweet naan, chicken makhani, or matter paneer.

The sauce for the chicken tikka masala was delish, however I felt that the cubes of chicken were on the dry side.  My husband really liked the naan, he felt that it was crisp, fluffy and garlicky, however I didn't think it was garlicky enough...though its fair to say that I'm a hardcore garlic lover so I can never get enough of the stuff.  The rice was pretty standard and complemented our dish nicely.  I just LOVE the tea with lots of sugar...sweet, fragrant, creamy goodness.

All in all, House of Curries is not great, but not bad.  Decent eats for the value.

This is the only Inidan food place I've been to in Berkeley since I dont go to school there/live there, but Im sure there are far better places.

To start, I want to say that the guy was nice and accommodating.  The food was okay and that's the end of the good stuff. Oh and the restrooms were clean.

Now to the bad.  My friend and I placed our orders one after the other.  My food came out in about 10-15 minutes, but my friend had to wait and extra 15 minutes or so AND we had to go back and ask them about her order.
Another thing, the curries do not come with rice, naan or anything else.  The price for some was low, but a few of us ordered lamb and special ones which costed around 8-10 bucks, and on top of that we also had to pay more for naan/rice.  Not worth it.  I would give them a try on the cheaper ones maybe, but other than that I'll try a different place next time I visit cal.

House of Curries, located inside Beau Sky Hotel, has relatively cheap food that is tasty, a convenient location (very close to campus and right across from the Asian Ghetto), and friendly service. Also complimentary tea (quite delicious). Everything I've tried there has been pretty good - it's not high-quality food, per se, but it's much better than Naan n' Curry. I have yet to be disappointed.

I came here a few nights ago for the Phi Sigma Pi fundraiser for my friend. I ordered the lamb biryani (fried rice) and garlic naan. The biryani was $7.99 I think and the naan was a little over $1, bringing my total to $10.98. It took a while for the dish to cook and arrive. But the portion was a heft one for the biryani. I'm not used to eating lamb but my friends told me it's like chicken. It's not. Just the thought of eating a lamb is a bit surreal and gets me queezy or whatever the appropriate word is. The garlic naan was delicious, although a bit on the cold side when it arrived. I definitely recommend it. It's not the thick naan you get at Trader Joes but it's more of a thin Chinese green onion pancake style.  There's also free tea with the purchase of a meal and the drinks are off to the far left of the counter. The rice wasn't spicy at all. I tried to add hot sauce but i couldn't find any. Strange, I thought Indian food was on the spicy side.
i like naan n curry soooo much better. their chicken tikka masala was too sweet with not enough spices. naan was dry. service is good though.

I can't say that the food here is really noticeably better than Naan 'N Curry (but that could be because that after they opened up, Naan stopped leaving their naan and curries drenched in oil...) but like other people said, the environment is much better. It's definitely better kept up and the manager is a really nice guy. That said, 4/5 stars.

Salmon tandoori. Eggplant curry. And a whole wheat naan that I couldn't resist. Ten-fifty well spent. Pretty healthy and it kept me pleasantly stuffed seven hours later til dinner time. Needs more outside seating, but House of Curries should be any college student's to-go joint for tasty Indian cravings.

I like this place A LOT..
Its kind of a self serving place, canteen style. U grap your own drinks, the have CHAI tea for you, water jar and glasses.

We had Shrimp tendori...FANTASTIC ...
Garlic and Onion Nan... .. FANTASTIC
salmon Curry... not impresive at all. the salmon was burnt...have that burnt taste and ruin the curry ...
So far, it s a cool place.  Two tumbs up.

The chicken tikka masala here is unbeatable.  This was the first Indian curry I've ever tried, and I instantly fell in love.  Try the aloo naan as well if you like potato! I usually stick with the onion naan.

This place was A-Ok, because I have experienced better. It is in a nice location and its pretty big with indoor and outdoor seating. The pricing is good for the amount you get, but the quality and taste? Not the best. 

Me and my boyfriend came here and got the chicken tikka masala, plain rice and naan, and we were not satisfied. We dig in and both thought, "wow this food is pretty bland". Indian food is supposed to be spicy and sweet, so this was NOT what we were used to. The food wasn't horrible, but it wasn't worth finishing. Our taste buds just weren't liking it. 

Location is on a busy street and you have to park on the street. You order first, pay and then find a table to sit at with your number. This place looks like a hotel and not even a restaurant, but it's good they have a little sign out on the street with their name written on it.

good chicken curry with soft tender chicken breast meat.. the naan was soft and good

hmm the service was really NON EXISTENT tho!! i know we are not hard pressed to pay a tip but i wasnt offered utensils, my table wasnt cleared, .. would go back again for the food, though.

I came to get some chicken tikka masala. They had a huge pot of it already and my order was complete before I had finished paying. However, they keep the entire pot piping hot which means all the chicken is overcooked making it try and tough despite the creamy sauce. I also think the chunks of chicken are about twice as big as they should be.

3.5 star

Naans are good although they are sometimes burnt.. Chicken Tikka Masala and Palaak Panneer! :)
I love the free tea...the naan is pretty good, though i find the curry a little bit too watery.   Good atmosphere, and seating area.

This was the first Indian restaurant I ever tried in Berkeley, and still my favorite in the area.

I like the chicken tikki masala with garlic naan - $6 + $2.50 = $8.50, which amounts to about $9 with tax. It's a little bit of a pricier option compared to other cheap UC Campus eats. 

Sometimes, the chicken is a little dry, but for the most part, it's tender. I enjoy the creamy sauce and well-flavored naan. Also, they have free chai tea, which is nice and milky. I've always experienced friendly service here, so no complaints :)

Tip: Come with a friend, split the curry, and get two naans - there's always more than enough :)

Chicken Chollay was good and so was the garlic naan.

I just don't understand why they don't have metal forks.  It kind of bothers me to eat with one metal spoon and a plastic fork..... hopefully this is a temporary problem.

I would go back here over Naan n Curry any day.

Chicken Tikka Masala is the best thing here. The Chicken curry is good as well.  This place is open late at night; one time i was walking home from choir and starving and I got a cup of curry and some naan and it was amazing. It's located across from campus which is great, and the service is pretty good. There's plenty of seating, with some seating outside as well.

Paneer tikka masala is amazing! Have it with garlic naan and I'm in heaven. This place was definitely me guilty pleasure while at cal. (the dish is really creamy and naan is not that great for you either). The Paneer tikka masala has this tangy or lemon-yness that I haven't tasted anywhere else and it makes it delicious. 
I'm also a big fan of the free chai that they offer. It can be hard to find a table with bigger groups so be ready to camp out for a spot in certain nights. Service is nothing special, and on the days that  i feel like it's sub-par, i just think about how amazing the food will be once i get it and then my mood quickly turns around.
And you'll see once you're inside that the utensils, plates and water is self serve.

House of Curries is the best place in the greater telegraph area for cheap food.  I will attempt a proof by way of discounting its competitors.  

Just up the block from the venerable House of Curries (or House of Curry as its devoted tend to call it) are two other standbys of cheap Berkeley food: La Burrita and Top Dog.  

Neither one can really hold a candle to House of Curry.  La Burrita, it must be admitted, is really not that great for Mexican food in California, even for its price.  A burrito and a drink will cost you around $7 anyhow, and as we will soon see, a better meal can be had at House of Curry for less money.  

As for Top Dog, $3 for a hot dog means that it will cost about 8$ to be really full (2 dogs and a drink), and you also can't sit down, so Top Dog is really only useful for grabbing a bite on the way home.  It's only mentioned here because it seems to come up fairly frequently in arguments about cheap food in the area.

Smart Alec's limps into the ring as the final contender, but it's easily dispatched: you aren't making it out of there for less than about 9$ all things said and done, and if you aren't eating vegetarian the meat on offer is less than satisfying.

Enough of the negative: At house of curry, two people can order a chicken (or paneer for us vegetarians) tikka masala and naan, binge on free chai, and have spent only FIVE DOLLARS.  Before you start whining about having only ordered one entree, give it a try, it's really very filling. 

 Not only is it the cheapest, but House of Curry legitimately has solid americanized indian food every time.  If you are looking for authenticity you might be disappointed, but really, it tastes good, so who cares!  The atmosphere sure beats the hell out of the competition, and you can almost always find seating for up to about 8 people pretty easily.

If you don't love House of Curry, you're nobody.

This is my--and in my opinion the greater Cal community's--go-to Indian spot. I always get spinach curries when I go to Indian restaurants. This time, I tried the aloo palak, which is spinach and potatoes. Yummy! The spinach still had a vegetable consistency, not stewed down to be a salty mush that I've unfortunately experienced elsewhere. There were tough plant/herb pieces and a large bark-like structure in the curry that puzzled me, but the latter smelled good so I think it was some essential spice that makes the dish. As a fan of all carbs, of course I could just eat layers and layers of their naan and nothing else. The workers are generally really nice. My friends and I sat inside for more than two hours and midway through one guy took away our dirty plates for us, even though wait service is technically not included. I saw innumerable plates of ctm (I won't even spell it out because it'd add to the yelp keyword counts) carried out. How can people just stick with that one dish, and not try all the other delectable-sounding items on the menu? I wonder if it is only popular here or if it is indeed a staple in India. There are so many other different and awesome flavors that I could come again and again and not be disappointed.

Why do I always go to this place and have their 'A-OK' food?

Hmm, it's cheap. If you need some Indian food and feeling a bit frugal, you go here. I always get their chicken tikka masala (like most people do). I pair that with plain naan. Their service is really fast (ordered there and ordered online through LivingSocial). The reason for this is that they don't really make your food from "scratch." They have the sauce/masala pre-made and the chicken is also cooked too.

The chicken is usually dry so I usually have to cut them into smaller pieces and have them soak up the yummy, creamy sauce! I finish their not-so-small serving in one sitting with the help of my plain naan, which is sometimes burnt but still good.

They have different kinds of naan, but I usually just opt for plain (less calories as compared to their cheese option and also the cheapest). Their naan is fluffy sometimes, but it can get really, really flat.

This is a self-service place: you order your food at the counter, bus your table, get your own utensils and water, etc. Not bad for Indian food here in Berkeley.

TIP! Always look around for "deals" -- CampusCred and munchonme unfortunately stopped offering deals, but LivingSocial is partnered with House of Curries for TAKEOUT and they usually have some type of deals. :)

Paid $4.22 for chicken tikka masala with plain naan! Not bad.

My favorite restaurant! Always, always worth waiting in line on busy saturday nights after home football games.
All the dishes are perfect and the portions very large! One dish is enough for two people. Naan has the perfect texture and the biryani is seasoned to perfection. 
I personally like aloo ghobi or tikka masala (lamb, chicken, or paneer) with a side tandoor dish. Tandoor Chicken is juicy and evenly spiced throughout the meat, and the sheekh kabob perfectly compliments any curry dish.
All you Naan 'n Curry fans out there, check out House of Curries; it's cleaner, has much nicer staff, and of course tastier!
The owner, Sajid, is very nice and is always happy to take your order.  Want to try something new? Just ask Sajid and he will be happy to recommend a dish for you.
Too bad I graduated and no longer live in berkeley. =(

I'm not very impressed at all with House of Curries.  If you want to get some fairly cheap Indian food with pretty small portions and most of the dishes doused in way too much sauce then you should come here.  I highly recommend going with a group of people that want to eat family style so that you can get a little variety.  Naan and rice must be ordered separately and come in orders that are too much for just one person, so that's a hassle too.  There are very often many flies around the open-air restaurant, so that bothers me too as I can't really deal with bugs around me while I eat.  This is a small step up from the Naan 'N' Curry that this originated from.

Hands down, my favorite Berkeley restaurant.

While I was an undergrad, I ate their Chicken Tikka Masala at least once a week.  The sauce is nice and thick, with lots of flavor and just enough spice.  The portions are generous.  As much as I love the food, part of its charm is its location in the Beau Sky Hotel.  I also enjoy the guy who takes orders...and always has on a pair of sunglasses.  He needs to strap a boombox to his back and play the "I wear my sunglasses at night" song on loop.

I don't know what it is about Berkeley that makes Indian food so cool. I've always been a moderate fan of Indian food getting it whenever one of my friends or my family craves it but I've never really sought it out ever. Indian food just doesn't do that for me until Berkeley. Everyone and their mother wants to eat Indian food, what is up with that?

The Berkeley Indian food craze has definitely rubbed itself off on me and as expected, I've definitely had my fair share of naan and curry here at House of Curries. While I do like Naan n' Curry more just because I have those good memories of chowing down with my family down in Judah in San Francisco, House of Curries is pretty good too. Yet, I will always say Naan n' Curry is definitely better, especially since they rolled out that buffet where I can eat all the chicken tikka massala,  Indian fried vegetables, and naan I want. 

House of Curries seems to have a more mild chicken tikka masala. There isn't that much spice and it really seems like there's more cream or milk than anything else. I tried their vindaloo and I must say that their potatoes have some sour kick to them that I really can't stand. It's such a shame too because I just LOVE potatoes. How do you put so many potatoes and not let me eat them? House of Curries, you suck for that! 

Regardless, the restaurant is clean and they work quickly to get you your food. I also love just sitting outside and doing my share of people watching and sometimes, I'll bump into a friend or two and have an awesome quick conversation. I have to say, House of Curries can't be beat for that though! I just wish the food were a bit better!

This is my favorite Indian restaurant in the east bay area.

I love the chicken tandori here, but the order does take alot longer if you order tandori.

Also love the chicken tikka masala, garlic naan and free chai!!
craving for Indian food? this is your place! pretty good food - the naan is pretty good more bread like than thin cracker. the env. is cleaner than most other Indian fast food places.

Pretty decent Indian food at a good price. There's a lot of seating, and you basically order at the register and they bring your food to your table. They also have free chai tea. (But not a huge fan of it) 

I love Chicken Tikka Masala, so that's what I always order, but their chicken chunks are kind of dry, as with most places (I just like the sauce haha). But any dish paired with naan is super filling (yay carbs!), and it's easy to share a couple dishes between friends.

I LOVE THIS PLACE.

If you can deal with the fact that you'll be surrounded by college students, talking about weird things.  Bros and their lingo and just the general crowdedness, then you should definitely come dine.  I've never had a bad plate.  Pair anything with garlic naan and you'll be in heaven.  Love the fact that there's free chai tea and the staff is amazing.  They are all really friendly, fast and good looking. ;)

Pretty standard fare - better, IMO, than Naan n' Curry it's nearby competitor, because they are more aggressive with their spicing. The service is sub-par; frequently food waits to be delivered to your table while they finish your naan (which is not particularly worth the wait).

This is my favorite place to get Indian food in Berkeley.  The naan is huge and tastes a lot better than Naan n' curry's naan.

The entrees are quite cheap but make sure you order naan or rice with your curry or just expect a plate of curry.

Plenty of veggie options but tends to get busy during lunch/dinner and isn't great for large groups and its a little hard to carry conversations when they are blasting Bollywood music a little too loud.

Favorites: Aloo (potato) or eggplant
love the tap water on tap and spicy curry and amazing naan. chicken was weak, though. prices great.

Delicious, hot curries... warm, soft, pillowy naan... 
I've tried a lot of the curries here, and none has disappointed me. The best thing about this place is you get free chai tea with your order and can drink it till your bladder bursts! Yaaayyyy!!!!!!!

Their lamb curry is so delicious... Mmmm... Baaa~~!!!!!

I regularly drive past many Indian places to get to House of Curries. Chicken tikka masala you are my only reason to live. Garlic naan is freshly baked and wonderful. Double up orders of these two things and chow down - theres no reason to even get anything else (though I have and it's awesome). It's also not too spicy - just enough to make my stomach go "WTF MAN I THOUGHT WE HAD A TRUCE!"

The guys who work there have always been super nice to me/joke around/all smiles etc. Also - If you dine in you can get endless amounts of Chai Tea as well. Can you beat that? I think not.

This restaurant is pretty good - their free Chai is delicious and their portions of naan are very generous (although too thick and tough for my taste).  However, my tongue is very sensitive to spicy food and this restaurant really loves to turn up the heat.  Sometimes I can handle it, but more often than not, my tongue needs to be rehabilitated with ice cubes, tears, and profanities.  Oddly, I never turn down an invitation to eat here and sometimes masochistically suggest it myself if I am in the area.

For some reason, I've had a good number of experiences here, and I find myself re-ordering just one dish: the chicken tikka masala. Pretty solid, as is the garlic naan, but I can't really say I find anything else all that spectacular. And when there's a ton of people in line, it really doesn't feel worth the wait. One thing I do enjoy that I'd like to highlight, though, is the free chai that comes with a meal purchase. But be warned, it runs out quick!

I wished my stomach would expand more so I could eat more and try different dishes. Definitely coming back in the future. 

I had lamb curry and shared an order of naan with a friend. The curry was the right amount of spicy and the lamb was tender. The naan was so soft and warm. I LOVED the unlimited tea.

I started eating Indian food in college, and House of Curries was one of the first places that I tried for Indian food.  Honestly, I don't really taste the difference between Naan N' Curry and this place, but I think both are pretty decent.  I didn't have a stomach ache or anything like people say they have after they eat Indian food.  I think they have an assortment of naans and they're all really good-- I think I particularly liked the potato one and the onion one.

I LOVE this place! Any time I am in Berkeley, I make a point to stop in and have House of Curries! 

I haven't had anything I didn't like here and especially like their saag dishes and their vindaloo dishes (although those are really spicy). The tikka is very creamy and a little sweeter than I like, but still really good! 

Only downside is that the dishes aren't served with rice, but they do have complimentary tea which is so warm and wonderful. 

Try anything here and you won't be disappointed. Of course, it isn't the best choice for a hotel unless you want to smell curry all day and night....but as a restaurant, YUM!

Indian/Pakistani restaurant that offers naans, curries, samosas, chicken tandoori, etc. Good food at good prices. Service is friendly and I love the free chai. I recommend their garlic or potato naan with any curry dish. Their baigan bharta is pretty spicy, and their palak paneer has less oil compared to Naan N Curry.

* 4/24 I came here today for dinner and ordered the sada bhindi with roti. I have to say, their naans and rotis are bigger and fluffier than those of Naan N Curry. I went to Naan N Curry twice last week, and their naan and roti were a bit disappointing. I think I prefer House of Curries over Naan N Curry now....

Good place if you're with a friend because you can each order a curry dish to share. If you prefer to solo it, the portion, along with a side of naan or rice will keep you full for several hours. I'm a fan of the chicken masala, which I get to go with a side of rice. The chicken is usually a little dry, but that can be fixed easily by shredding up the chicken and letting it soak in some of the saucy goodness. I'm a little uncertain as to how they get it to that bright of an orange, but I'm sure I'd be happier not knowing.

Chicken Tikka Masala and Garlic Naan!  That's how I roll here.

My gf hates eating here because she just sees it as just dipping thin bread into a thick sauce with pieces of chicken; No nutrition except the protein in the chicken.  I agree with her perspective, but I differ in that I just simply enjoy eating it!  It's pretty tasty.  For those who don't know what it looks like, it's chicken in a puddle of orange-colored spicy creamy sauce.  My only complaint is that it's overpriced for what it is.  It costs about ~$9.  Can't it be sold for $5 and still make a profit?

My girlfriend and I make our way to House of Curries at least once a week. We have not ventured outside of Chicken Tikka Masala because we are so satisfied with it. We compliment this dish with garlic, cheese, and original naan and rice. The free hot milk tea is also amazing. If we need to, we can get in and out extremely fast, but the atmosphere is pretty cool. When the weather is nice, the outside patio is an amazing place to eat and people watch. I will continue to go to House of Curries until I find better Indian food, which I have not yet. You order your food and they bring it to you, but other than that, everything is up to you. You grab your drinks, silverware, plates, water, and whatever else you may need. I also put my dishes away every time, but some people just leave their dishes on the table. I am definitely confident bringing visitors from out of town to House of Curries.

The food was great! And free cha (tea) as well. I love the outdoor seating. I had paneer tika masala, my mom had chicken tikka masala (or butter chicken) and my dad had a lamb curry. The naan was delicious, we got two naan and one rice. The naans are huge but if you have a good appetite like we do two naans are perfect for three people. YUMa!

Lately, I've been craving Indian food and this place definitely hit the spot.  I love that you pay up front and although everything is self-served the restaurant is very clean and the staff is very friendly.

The dishes I ordered were Palak Ghost (spinach cooked with lamb), Prawn Vindaloo, and garlic naan.  Everything came out at once and once I started eating, I was in Indian food heaven.  

The lamb was extremely tender and it went very well with the naan.  I love how spinach is prepared with Indian food and the flavors of spinach did not overpower the taste of the lamb. 

The prawn vindaloo is something that I have never tried before but if you like spicy food, then this is a dish you have to try.  The prawns were extremely large and they were very generous with how many they gave.  The sauce had a spicy taste that kicked in after a few seconds and it tasted delicious with the rice.

Overall, I will definitely be coming back here!

This is one of my top favorite places for Indian places.  Chicken tikka masala, lamb + spinach (I forgot the actual name), samosas (both veggie and meat versions)...yummmmm.  I love clean plates and silverware.  Free hot tea and iced cold water was always a good thing.

My friends and I usually come here for lunch because the service is quick, and the food is cheap and delicious.  They also do take out if you want.  The place is clean and BIG so it never really looks crowded.  There are both indoor and outdoor seatings to suit your liking.  I wish they did delivery though....

Okay, I may not know what authentic Indian food is, but for the price and the flavor and quality you get, I'm giving it 5 stars. The Naan is wonderful. Make sure to talk to the people behind the counter, they love to get good comments about their food. I think sometimes the students are too in a rush to appreciate great food. Yes the location is a little below good, but call it a "Hole in the Wall" and now you understand what I mean. The best places I find are "Holes"!!!!

I've been to House of Curries several times over the years. My most recent visit was with a friend for dinner. The weather was great and we were craving Indian food, so we made our way over to Durant to partake of some outdoor seating.

The food here is just okay, and the prices are a little higher than the competition. I ate the veggie korma and aloo naan, and my friend had chicken tikka masala with onion naan. The curries had a mostly forgettable flavor, and the aloo naan was lifeless (and perhaps a little bit soggy). The chai was free and drinkable.

Our tab ran about $4 higher than it would at Biryani House downtown, and the food there is much better. But sitting outside on a nice evening can't be beat! House of Curries has its uses, but I wouldn't make a habit of going here in search of tasty food or low prices.

A couple other things: (1) Bad weather means having to dine inside, and the dining room is less than appealing. (2) The cash register is programmed to overcharge tax. Hopefully the extra moolah finds its way to the man before the man finds its way to HOC.

My favorite place to get Indian food in the Bay Area! This might have a little bit to do with nostalgia and remembering the "good ole days" when I went to Cal (ok I graduated last year, not that long ago) but I have not been to an Indian food place I've liked better.

It's great for take out or to get a quick meal and seating is usually not a problem. I have tried multiple items on the menu and I've loved them all. It's spicy, but not TOO spicy. I also love that there is free tea to drink. Their garlic naan is yummmy too. Don't expect luxerious dining, but if you have a hankering for Indian and are in Berkeley, this is the place to go.

The food is good but definitely not fantastic. It comes at a good price though and the free tea is awesome. I honestly go there mostly for the tea and na'an. I have had much better Indian food but because of the location and prices, I keep coming back for House of Curries.

What a dump.  That being said, this gets four stars for what it is.  A great dumpy Indian place with really great food.  The ordering system is a little confusing, and the service was somewhat slow, but when it arrived we were in heaven.  I had the Chicken Tikka Masala, which was creamier than I have had in other places, but wow was it good.  My friends had the lamb and another the spinach paneer.  All around big thumbs up and their naan was rocking.
Naan is often burned, the flys are not encouraging, the service is often slow and the food is overpriced and nothing special. I much prefer Biryani House.

When I first came to Berkeley, the only real game in down for curry was Naan 'N Curry. It was all right, but I definitely knew there was something lacking in it. Then came along House of Curries, which, since its opening, has been my place to go to satisfy my curry needs.

My favorite dish, the chicken tikka masala, has always been done fantastically, full of flavor and lots of curry to soak up with your bread. The chicken is great but the best parts are when I'm chewing on naan that was drenched in the curry. I'm always full (and usually pretty warm) when I come out of this place, very content on my visit.

Love the free tea they provide as well. I've heard that they employ it as a trick to make you feel more full from the meal (and thus wanting to come back more), but shoot, I just can't help myself! And the prices here are super reasonable, adjusted perfectly for a student budget.

And love the staff here as well, very friendly. I can't help but smile when I'm paying my bill (a rare feat, I'm sure). However, is it just me, or do they usually let their Indian customers pay after the meal, while everyone else pays before? I'm not calling foul of anything, it just seems like the times I go here with my Indian friends, the order is a bit reversed.

I love that you can eat on the deck here! Its awesome, you can just kick back with your chicken Vindaloo and Tiki Masala and read a book outside. It's a very laid back atmosphere and the decorations are great too!

The food is very good and reasonably priced and the staff is super nice. They moved a lot of the staff from the location on College over to this one and I have only been back to the College House Of Curries once since. 

Free tea!!!

Oh House of Curries how I love thee.
You have always been there for me post midterm. 
When I was starving you came to my rescue with your delectable onion naan and cholay ghosht
You may not be the cleanest place in the world, but I forgive you

Once again, the chicken tikki masala is very delectable, and the garlic naan is the best. Don't get it to go, or your naan will get soggy, since it is served fresh and hot. Also, best chai in town! I've been here 3 more times, not getting tired of the same order. Rare for me. I mostly come here when it's either cold or rainy, and a cup of complimentary chai is just what I need. Who needs boba from the Asian Ghetto when you've got wonderful, fragrant, drool-inducing chai? Also, their lassi is good. Tastes like all-natural yogurt. I'll definitely be back!
Small portions, and the food was pretty awful. Naan N Curry just 1 block away is SO SO much better.

The food here is pretty good and not too expensive compared to the other Indian locations in the Berkeley area. Bishal, one of the guys that work there is a pretty cool guy, so chat him up! The lassi is average, the naan is usually really good, and the tikka masala is hit or miss, but more often than not it's delicious. Give it a shot!

House of Curries on Durant (HOCOD) is a Berkeley staple.  Visited daily by hundreds of hungry campus patrons -- many of whom hail from our very own Yogi's chemistry lab -- HOCOD is loved by many.  We crossed the threshold into the converted house with little idea of what was to come.

Dank, freezing, and lined with mirrors covered in a thick film of vindaloo grease, the interior was less than welcome.  We made our way across the slippery tile floor, whose waxen residue hadn't been removed in ages, to our first table, which nearly collapsed.  Moving to the other side of the loud, cavernous interior in search of better structural integrity, our hopes were dashed when the mere placement of a mug on the edge of the table sent it reeling as if stunned by an earthquake of non-trivial magnitude.  We gave up, and gingerly lifted our menus off of the teetering surface.

While imbibing vast quantities of mediocre chai in an attempt to keep warm, we attempted to order chicken tikka masala, the usual eigendish, just to discover that they had run out!  Does a New York City hot dog stand run out of buns?  Does Starbucks run out of venti half-soy 365 Kelvin triple-shot skinny vanilla lattes?  No.  We were aghast.

Luckily, there was still aloo ghobi ($6) to be had.  Unfortunately, not only was it underspiced, but the potatoes were undercooked.  The lamb vindaloo ($8) was somewhat better: spicier, with slightly less undercooked potatoes, and with pleasantly tender lamb.  The appetizer of pakora ($3) that accompanied the main dishes wasn't outstanding, but was a truly gourmet dish when compared with our naan choices: a virtually potato-free aloo naan, and a regular naan, both of which had been burned!  Again: does a Mexican restaurant burn its tortillas?  Does a soul food joint burn its biscuits?  Precisely.

Overall, the tasty lamb, good pakora, and pleasant views of Durant push HOCOD up to a generous rating of two samosas.  The food was cheap (one rupee), but even so, the samosa-to-rupee ratio is an unimpressive 2.0.  Needless to say, despite its exalted position among near-campus Indian eateries, HOCOD fails to deliver.

Firstly, i'm totally not a curry aficionado, and i don't know anything about Indian or Pakistani food, so this is just a newbie talking. 

This should probably be more like 4.5 stars, but i can't give the in between. The only problems I've had with them is that sometimes their "spiciness" is more related to the burning sensation and not actual spice/flavor, and they've mixed up my order more than once. In the end though, i couldn't care really. 

The curry is good, like really good. I love the chicken tikka masala and the various vindaloo and if you ask they can tailor the burn to your taste. It's cheap, it's probably not super awesome, but for less than $10 i can get my curry of choice, a plain naan, and a cup of mango lassi to wash it down. Not to mention the infinite water and tea. And i always leave either over stuffed, or with left overs. Every time i desperately crave curry when i'm still in school, this is the to-go place. 

They also let any number of people eat there provided you can snipe the tables. They are always friendly, and in general just provide a pleasant atmosphere. If you're going in a group, make sure you tell your last orderer to inform the cashier that they are the last so they know when to cut off the check =3.

Used to be favorite Indian place but then once it picked up popularity, the quality went downhill. It's got super oily and they really jip you on meat and tofu that they put in the curry. You are better off at Cafe Raj or Naan n Curry!

Maybe I'm picky becuase I used to live in Singapore, but this food didn't completely satisfy my Indian food craving. Overall the food wasn't savory or spicy enough for me. Maybe I should have tried the vindaloo, but the chicken tikka masala was tasty.

I turned up at this place with friends on a whim after reading yelp reviews of it. I have to say I wasn't very impressed. 

The Achar Gosht (spiced goat) was spicy and the best thing we ordered. Cholay Chicken (w/ chick peas) and Paneer Tikka Masala were so so. Garlic naan was tolerable but the roti was barely edible. Mango lassi was poured into my glass from a milk container pulled from the fridge. That's food blasphemy.

I love Indian food, and am usually not too harsh on Indian restaurants. But I have to bring the hammer down on this one.

Verdict: Rejected. Naan and Curry is just down the street, and has better food.

I'm starting to think I've been spoiled by the awesome Indian food I had in Boston, because I was just not feeling this place. Price-wise it's okay--I could have used more meat in my 7 dollars worth of curry chicken. 

The naan was pretty good, warm and soft. The rice was just fine, nothing extraordinary or bad. It falls down on the chicken. First, it was mild. I have nothing wrong with mild food, but I wanted to have some semblance of spice. That and they used white meat, which was tender, but extremely dry on the inside. 

I had a sweet lassi, but I'm fairly sure I'm just not a lassi person. It reminds me too much of regular milk, which tends to upset my stomach. They actually forgot to bring it out with my order, but it was brought out to me when I went to the counter.

I wasn't sure if you pay before or after you get your food, but apparently they don't really care. The cashier seemed to be...okay. He was nice to me, but I noticed his stare lingered just a little too long on the customer in front of me. It might have been because she had a tremor in her right arm and he seemed to know her.

Tea and water is free. Apparently rice and naan comes extra, because I can't believe I was charged three dollars for a sweet lassi.
Decent, but I don't understand the hype.  Convenient location.

In the past, I've enjoyed House of Curries mainly because my friends and I frequented the place after late-hour seminars. The owner is a good guy and would occasionally come out and chat with us, tell us about the ingredients and spices, etc. The Paneer Tikka Masala, Pakora and Biriyani are delicious. This place is good but not the best. For excellent Indian food, go a few blocks South for Tandoori Kitchen and try the veggie wrap, or Vik's.

Five of us came here and got three curry plates, four servings of naan, and a plate of rice. Couldn't finish it and only paid $6 each. It's actually pretty good flavors and helpings for such a low price! There's a very nice patio area to eat outside. This and Naan and Curry are pretty much the same, so just go to whichever you are closer to (though they' themselves are close).

I had my first ever indian dish at House of Curries. I wasn't too sure what to expect, and I had no idea how to eat any of it. The concept of dipping the flat bread, later known as naan, into some sort of sauce was interesting to me. I tried the chicken tikka masala. And since the first time I had it three years ago, my choice of dish has never changed. I absolutely enjoyed every bite of it. I soon learned about different flavors of naan. I have tried the garlic and potato naan and both are pretty delicious. The free tea is a plus. It's one of my favorite things about this particular place. 

I haven't had much of a craving for indian food in a while and not many of my friends eat there because they don't care for the curry too much. But every once in a while I drop by and I'm glad that they have a to-go option!

Good Indian food. I had one sad experience with their paneer tikka masala, where the curry was very thin, but the other two times I went, (Malai Kofta and something involving eggplants) the sauce was thick and well-spiced. They do an amazing job with vegetables and meats alike, and the naan is incredible. They have an open kitchen so you can see the naan being made. The downside to the atmosphere is that people don't realize that they have to bus their own tables, so it's definitely not a place you can have a romantic evening.

not sure if it was cuz we were their first customers that day, but the chicken masala was cold.  The hot nann made up for it, but after it gets cold (it's really really big), you have nothing else to look forward to but the free chai.  I hear the chicken vindaloo is good.  I'd at least come back to try that one.

I think the food here is decent & i enjoy the chai as well. the people here are so nice.

oh wait, and then there's the cheese naan. DID YOU KNOW ABOUT CHEESE NAAN?? it's naan.. and they fill it with cheese... it's amazing. order it; you won't regret it.

The only thing I would be back for is the free milk tea (with a big tub of sugar next to it).

Right when i walked in, I wondered to myself "Is this place clean?" The kitchen looked gross and greasy. The tables were all "self cleanup" type so depending on the last customers sitting there, you get what you get. 

The cups you get milk tea with are all ceramic, so you kind of just guess and hope that they used a decent amount of dishwasher soap to clean them. I had to "find" myself a clean cup. shrug.

The food took a long time, but hey, I'm willing to wait for great food. The thing was that, it wasn't great. the sauces were only to moisten up the n'aan. It was edible. They have sauces in a little minifridge. I didn't even know they were sauces. They came in those squirt bottles, and they had crusty tips from the dried concoction inside.

I'd be back for the unlimited milk tea, maybe.. if I remember to bring my own cup.
The naan was huge!!!! My paneer was decent, not the best, not the worst, just okay. The food came out fast and it was a great place to sit and chat.

Chicken tikki masala and freshly made naan. Mmmm. This was our last meal before leaving town, and it was SO good. We sat in the patio, where there was a nice breeze (okay, it was a bit brisk and we had to use our drinks to keep the napkins from flying in our faces, but still).

One word - or three?? CHICKEN TIKKA MASALA!!!!!!!!!!!!! If you haven't tried it, TRY IT. My ex-boyfriend who survives on a diet of chicken strips and subway sandwiches (i.e. doesn't like anything ethnic) loves it too, and that's saying something because he is the pickiest eater ever. Me, on the other hand, I love my food, and the chicken tikka masala here is amazing. I AM a little disappointed because they tweaked the recipe a little bit, but it's still worth it.

A lot of students from the Berkeley campus eat here since it's across the street. The curries are decent. I like the mushroom curry. The naan is made fresh and it's oh so good. The drinks are self served. Thus, you can have as many servings of milk tea as you want.

3.5 stars. Halal meat is served here. Owners are known Muslims. Had food catered from here at a CAL Alumni event. The food was good but not spectacular. The CTM and other chicken dish was pretty watery. Not enough cream in the sauces. Later on at night I went with some friends to get some chai (tea). The tea was good, although not free. Seating inside with some seating available outside as well.

Grabbed a small dinner with a friend here. 

The place itself is okay. It gets filled up really quick because it's been a stable business, it's cheap, and easily accessible to the students at UCB. 

We ordered the chicken tikka masala and 2 orders of original naan. We had chai tea on the side too (free). 

The chai tea is MAD hot. Do NOT drink it right away. It's pretty good when it cools down though. 

The tikka masala was okay. It only had like 6 pieces of chicken and a sad amount of curry. The flavors weren't quite as intense as I would like, but it was still okay. I'd be less disappointed if there was at least more of it in the dish.

The naan was okay but it was way crispier than naan should be. I like crispy breads so I was okay with it, but I know that naan is supposed to be pretty soft. Fail on their part. 

Overall, not a bad place but there are better Indian food places around the area.

I'm giving it 4 stars because it is pretty much the only Indian chain restaurant I consistently eat at and although I love it and have never had better Indian food, it's possible that there might be something else out there.  I'm praying that they'll open a location in Contra Costa County closer to me because it's too far to drive to Berkeley whenever I need a fix.  I've done it, though.  I am totally addicted to the Chicken Vindaloo (very spicy), the veggie samosas, the mango laasis and their naan is great.  My hubby and BFF both love the chicken tikka masala.  I don't think I have ever ordered something I didn't like here.  All the food has BIG flavors (which I love), and reading the item on the menu gives you a good idea of what you're getting - no surprises.  I remember once ordering Chicken Vindaloo at this place in Concord and it was nothing like the one at HOC.   

Anyway, others have said it too -- the free tea and cold water make the experience more pleasurable and the employees are really sweet.  I went with my BFF to the location on Solano and we took our two sons (ages 7 and 4).  The boys were curious to see the kitchen and the guy working the counter gave them a full tour!  He was so nice.  The bottom line is, you can't go wrong eating at any of the HOC locations.  YUM!

I would agree that the atmosphere & cleanliness at all of the HOC locations (College, Durant, Solano) are better than NNC (on Telegraph), but to me, the food is pretty much the same.

Price is kinda high for a college student.
Chicken Tikka Masala is extremely good though. But due to the pricing it loses one star.

a lot like naan n' curry, but spicier, which to me equals better. The chicken vindaloo and lamb with cauliflower were good and packed plenty of heat. Their naan bread was the best. They bake it right in front of you when you're ordering, very crunchy and fresh!

My boyfriend and I are stuffing our faces with garlic naan and some ridiculously spicy mixed vegetable curry as I draft this review. This place is intentionally kitsch and it looks like it's having an identity crisis. Chinese paper lanterns and a pirate ship chandelier inside an antebellum plantation hotel building? It's like an acid trip, but I wouldn't know because I've never done acid, so I'm only speculating. I probably wouldn't ever come here during the daytime but the food tastes delicious, and at midnight, what more could you want?
For the price and quality, you absolutely get the your bang for the buck! I didnt like Indian food at all before coming here and now I do!

Went on a lunch date again with my friend/old co-worker. We both heard about House of Curries and we both wanted to check this place out. The first thing I was surprised was not just the location (an old hotel, perhaps?) was that it was a typical order at the counter eatery. The prices are also not too bad either. 

My friend and I first tried to order their Veggie Samosa, but they were out (how do you get out of an item?!). Instead we ordered their Bhaingan Bharta (eggplant with veggies), Saag Daal (spinach and lentil), Vegetable Biryani, and Garlic Naan. Roughly $21 for the both of us. We also took advantage of their free chai tea and water; which you fill and serve yourself. The serving of the food is awkward as the server has to go on a search for your number which you have to place somewhere where he/she can see it (i.e. flat on the table?). The food was good and filling, but I was quite disappointed with their garlic naan. The piece I took for myself was too doughy. The saag (my order) was good, but not overpowering in flavors when I first had tried this dish elsewhere. 

Other than that, the place is busy which means a pretty long wait for food, which was odd when people BEHIND us got their food ahead of us. However, I still would give this place a go.

It has okay food, better than Naan and Curry down the street, but I literally waited 40 minutes for my food to come out, and it was still only half of my order, and I was told to wait ten more minutes for my tandoori chicken. 

I asked ten minutes later where it was, and they said ten more minutes. 

Ten minutes later, I asked for my money back. ($3 for the chicken leg)

NOT worth the wait. AND it's happened multiple times. 

Each time I come back I ask myself, WHYYY?!?!?! But don't worry, I won't be back ever again.
The best Indian restaurant in Berkeley, hands down. The prices could be alittle better, but it is definitely worth it. The lamb curry and chicken tikki masala are amazing!

Not gourmet indian food, but a solid cheap meal.  After exploring many other indian food in the area, this doesn't necessarily stand out, but I still return for the simple satisfying creaminess of the tikka masala, and hella good naan.
Very good Chicken Tikka and Naan. A few dollars too pricey (in my opinion) for everyday eating, but a great treat on occasion. Plus free tea!

This is a really descent Indian/Pakistani place to hit for an informal meal. The best part of this establishment is the atmosphere. It makes me feel like I'm not in California anymore, in a good way of course. I especially like the weird ornaments hanging from the roof and the free tea.

It's also a place where the waiter will tell the cook to make the food spicy enough for my liking. I recommend the bihindi vegetarian curry and any of the lamb curries. I have an affinity for okra, and they cook it well here. The rice and naan are as good here as any other place. 

I'm giving this place 3 stars because there are better Indian places in the Bay Area that make more fully flavored and complex curry dishes. I still haven't tried any appetizers or tandoori, so I will update this when I do.

Great and cheap place. Food is not so spicy and free tea is great!

Pity that the sun doesn't reach the terace!

I'm not too crazy about anything other than the NAAN! That's the only reason I go. The food is pretty so-so, but the naan is AMAZING!! I usually always order the spinach and cheese with 3 plain naans. For me, the naan is like the salsa/tortillas of mexican food. If it's not good it really doesn't compliment your food. Kinda spoils everything else.

Overal the service is friendly and the setup is a bit dingy but it's the best Indian restaurant I've been to around the East Bay. 

Just a side note* I hate it when I go to an Indian restaurant and the cooks are so stingy with the naan, ontop of that the naan doesn't taste chewy and fresh. With House of Curries they make the bread as soon as you order it so it's fresh and chewy and delicious. It's literally the size of a medium pizza. It's awesome!! 

Nom, nom, nommmmmm

This is my 2nd visit here (unknowly). First time, one of my good friends brought me here as a side tour of UCB. Second time, it was destiny that brought me here. EL O EL! 

Anyway, good indian food and very affordable. It gets super packed (I remember from my first visit) but b/c I went on a holiday, it was sorta empty. We ordered the naan, tandori chicken, and chicken tikki masala-- all good. It was a meal for 3 people and the total was just under $21; pretty sweet. 

The people working here are nice (even though the place is sorta self service).

I got take out here the other day when I was wanted to try something new.  Usually I go to Naan-n-Curry for nostalgic reasons (see my review).  Overall the food was good.  The garlic naan is tasty and the meat dishes actually have chunks of meat in them.  I definitely think it is equivalent to Naan-n-Curry if not better.  Given the choice I don't know which one I would go to.

Also, be aware of young looking cops asking you to buy them beer.  They had a sting operation going on here the other day.  There was about six undercover young looking cops with shaved heads and sunglasses asking people to buy them booze.

I'm a huge Chicken Tikki Masala fan so whenever I go out for curry this is what I'll always get. I really do love House of Curries Chicken Tikki Masala, it's creamy and tasty goodness! Their naan is alright, I'd say that the best naan comes from Indian Flavors over at Bancroft. I have to say that I love their basmati rice the best out of Indian Flavors, Naan n Curry, and Indian Flavors.

This place is more expensive than Naan n Curry, but I'd say the Chicken Tikki Masala is worth it. $6 for Chicken Tikki Masala and about $2-$3 for naan. PS I'm a huge sucker for chai tea.

This is the kind of place where you order at the counter and then they bring the food to you.  They only have prawns on their seafood section of the menu, and all those platters are $9.99.  Everything else on the chicken, beef and vegetarian menus are reasonably priced, from $2.49 - $7.99, giving you the flexibility to order many things a la carte.

I give them a three because I thought their service was bad, but their food was good.

This place is pretty tasty! Their naan is fluffy and just made, and their curries are fairly cheap. I like to come here fairly often to order to-go. 

You can also get free tea when you sit and eat. However, I question the cleanliness here...

The food is good for the price, but the sauces are usually more watery than I'd like them to be. Come here with the occasional munchonme deal (curry for $4-5) and then it seems super worth it! The onion naan is delicious and I think the portions can definitely fill you up.

8/16/07

Wow!  It's be awhile since I've been impressed by indian food in Berkeley, but this place was great.

I ordered chicken tikka masala and garlic naan.  When the curry dish came to the table I thought, "that doesn't look like a very big portion" but in a few minutes came my huge 10-12 inch piece of garlic naan.  It was the perfect lunch!  I tore off pieces of naan and would dip it in the curry, then I would have a piece of chicken.  The seasoning was just right!  The chicken was wonderfully marinated and tasted of lemon and married well with the curry spices.  The curry had a very nice heat.  My friend had the chicken vindaloo which was spicier.  By the end of my tikka masala my mouth was very warm, but not unpleasant.  I thought that I would have had to give up on the vindaloo or drink much more water if that was what I had ordered.  I do like spicy foods, but not so much that you feel more heat than you can flavor.  My friend had an order of rice to accompany her vindaloo.  It was nicely perfumed with cinnamon.

I will definately be coming back here to try more dishes as they have a plethora of curries to try and are very reasonably priced.  It was $10 including tax and tip for my meal.  Very good for the college budget.

***UPDATE*** 8/25/07

Came in with my aunt and her english friend (who is quite an efficiando when it comes to indian food).  Naan breads were still great.  We ordered lamb tiryani but got chicken tiryani instead (it's a rice dish...I think I spelled the food wrong).  English friend said the chicken tikka masala tasted like tomato soup.  It wasn't as good as it was last time.  The rice dish was over spicy.  The place was very busy saturday night and I think the chef cooking was not the same last time I came in.
