The food wasn't as good this time around, but I think that was due to the overwhelming crowd (school starts 8/27 and berkeley is overrun right now with new freshman) and the chef.  Go to this place when it is less busy, maybe on friday afternoons to get better food.  I still enjoy this place and will try and figure out who and when the food is good and not good.

8/29/07

The food is sometimes variable depending on the chef.  Today it was delicious like my first time coming here and unlike the 2nd time.  The naan is consistently good.  You can order your dishes to a desired degree of spiciness.  I find the vindaloo dishes too spicy, so I'll be ordering them a few notches less spicy.

Oh and by the way, the bathrooms are filthy.  Do not plan to use them unless it is an emergency/your-life-depends-upon it/etc.

Came here with a couple of friends for lunch and had the Chicken tikka Masala with Garlic Naan. I'd have to say for college for this place is good. 

The main dish was prepared exactly the way I like it and the garlic naan was fresh and warm out of the oven. 

The seating situation may get uncomfortable as they get busy, but overall I will be coming back to get my Indian food fix from here.

I'm not a huge fan of Indian food (i like meat, and Indian people apparently do not).  HOWEVER, this is the ONLY indian restaurant i will eat at because a) the free tea is awesome, b) the owners are super cool and c) food is good too.  the naan is gi-normous (i think that shall be a word). Upside: u don't come out smelling like food.

I love going here for Indian food when visiting my cousin.  It makes me sad that I can't find good Indian food back home.  I'm always surprised that even when I eat a lot, there is always something to bring home.

What can I say about HOC? When I was a Berkeley undergrad, I would come here 3-5 times a week (lol, sometimes)! HOC is delicious, inexpensive, and will become a must-have comfort food. I've spent countless hours with my friends at HOC, and wish I still lived in Berkeley just so that I can go back. Pretty much everyday dish at this place is good, and their CTM/PTM is unparalleled, anywhere!

I never knew this restaurant was located in the "Blue Sky Hotel" and was the reason why I never came here. I think they can do better than the "House of Curries - Indian and Pakistani" sign they have outside.

I ordered the chicken tikka masala as my first Indian restaurant experience. It's definitely a lot better than Naan N Curry down the street.

The meal didn't take that long to cook, and the naan was fairly soft-a little burnt.

I suspect this place amounts to an Indian-American version of Denny's, but I like it.  My favorite dish is the Chicken Tikka Masala, though it is quite rich.  The main thing that sets this place apart from Naan n' Curry for me is that the naan is a little bit better, not quite as greasy and the food on the whole doesn't seem as heavy (although that's not saying much).  The fact that it's a hotel (not sure if it is defunct or not) is interesting and its proximity to the campus/dorms/south side apartments is ideal.  Great place for a student and brings back a lot of memories.

I remember coming here a couple times and each time, I had a good experience.

Be prepared to drink a lot of water because the food here will make you sweat. They offer free milk tea when you sit down to eat which is a nice little touch. The curry here is really yummy with the right amount of flavor and level of spice.

They also offer a nice variety of naan. I usually order the garlic naan and its one nice and think piece of bread. Price is pretty good for what you get. It just sucks that its in Berkeley and street parking might suck throughout most of the day.

Probably the best Indian food near UCB campus. The pricing is comparable to other places (Naan n Curry) but it is generally agreed to taste better. The naan is good and the other dishes are tasty (I'm partial to the chicken tikki masala... yes, I'm American-ized haha). Costs about 10/person for an entrée and naan. If you are looking for a nice sit down and are feeling Indian food, this is the place to go.

I...Love this place.  If I'm ever showing someone around who's unfamiliar with the area, I take them here.  Hell, I joined yelp just so I could give this place five stars!  The menu is simple, the service is fast and courteous, the chai is free, and the food...is DELICIOUS.

I would have given them 4.5 stars if I could have, only because some of the tables are wobbly and some of the chai mugs have little chips in them.  Both of these things are easily fixed/avoidable.  It gives the place character.

Pretty inexpensive, too!
This place has its off days but I'm usually not too disappointed whenever I come here. Chicken Tikka Masala is always a must

I went to this place yesterday after reading some good reviews.  This place is not up to par with my Indian Food standards and I'm an Indian food connoisseur.  I will not go back to this place...ever because of the following:

1. Dirty plates and cups 
2. Water tasted like warm tap water -- dirty (I should have brought my Nalgene)
3. The tea was bittersweet -- even added sugar to try to alleviate the bitterness
4. Naan bread seemed stale and not luxuriously fluffy, like it should be.
5. Dishes were spicy (which is actually good because that's how Indian food should be), but spice does not equal taste.  The spiciness was so overwhelming that the taste was somewhere lost in transition.
6. The rice came with little chunks - poor Basmati rice etiquette.
7. The chicken in the Chicken & Cauliflower dish (I forgot the name, but besides the point) was EXTREMELY dry - disgusting; it was like the chicken was cooked separately and thrown in as an afterthought.

I will never go back to this Indian food place again - I was so disappointed.  Naan & Curry is WAY better than this joint (and a little cheaper, too - and they have clean dishes/cups!)
Not bad, but not as good as it could be.

This isn't high quality Indian food, but it's tasty. Like everyone said, the chicken tikka masala is probably the best dish. The location on College is, interestingly, a little higher quality (for example, the naans here tend to be a little overcooked), but this is solid and dependable. Basically, chicken tikka masala + free chai + garlic naan = a great meal.

i really liked this place... haven't been bad for a year or so... i went back 1 week ago... got my favorite dish... chicken marsala... total disappointment... it was not that bad... but just so much worse than 1 year ago... the chicken was not tender.. the sauce waso only ok...

the milk tea was still good. it was free. 

would i go back? pbb not.

I've started writing reviews for Yelp again - maybe it's because it's my last year at UC Berkeley and I'm going to reference my reviews when I come back to Berkeley for food 

I love House of Curries! I always come here with friends or with my boyfriend, and their chicken vindaloo is delicious! Chicken, potatoes, and a little tomato, and always hot and spicy, yum! Personally, I don't find it too spicy, but maybe it's because I always eat it with naan and green milk tea. Unfortunately, once I find something good, I stick with it, so I can't describe anything else that they serve. I can't even tell you how the rice is. It's not very expensive either; it always comes out to under $10 and the portions are big. Plus, the environment is great; whenever I come here with my friends, we just eat and talk for 3-4 hours. I just wish I had more friends that liked Indian food so I could come here more often. 

It's also kind of nice that they're one of the few places near campus that has (clean) restrooms.

One caveat: be careful about the jugs of drinking water. I don't know if the staff there cleans the jugs properly, because sometimes that water tastes bad; sometimes like plastic, sometimes like soap. But hence, the milk green tea (they also have free tea for customers).

This place is great! Though the food is really slow, it is worth the wait. I usually don't like meat, but I order the Chicken Tikki Massala every time (it seems to be the favorite). I don't go anywhere else for curry!

Best Yellow Lentils (Daal) and, as everyone else says, Chicken Tikka Masala. It's about as cheap as Indian food gets and makes me very happy that it's walking distance from my apt. Not sure if I'd travel a long distance to get there, and the ambiance isn't ideal, but you don't have to pay tip and the outdoor patio is pretty nice!

I can't eat very spicy food, so everytime i come here, i tell them to make it MILD. which it never is. once i ordered the regular naan and it was spicy. Basically if you can't eat spicy food you shouldn't come here because it's going to be spicy. period.

This is hands down the greatest Indian food I've ever had. Wow. The garlic naan and mushroom masala wa incredible, and perfectly spiced. I don't know if I'll be able to order anything else now... it was that good.

I went here with a friend I met at DVC a few semesters back. I remember when the building was under construction/ wasn't open for a while. Good to see that it is cleaned up now.

+ Order at register, self serve water, good fresh food quick. We were there @ about 1:30pm? Decently busy, but not packed. Perfect timing for us.

+ I liked sitting outside on the patio, kickin' it with my homegirl and people watch while we eat. The weather was perfect that day, I felt very relaxed.

+/- The food I had was okay. The Chicken tikka masala was kinda bland, and Naan tasted so-so.

Conclusion: I've been to better Indian restaurants. This place decently priced, and nice atmosphere. If you get cranky like me when you are starving, and don't want to walk another step until gets food in your belly, this place is alright. But If you can wait another 10-15 minutes, there are other really bomb restaurants on University/ Shattuck to check out.

Oh these guys are quick! One of my favorite Indian food spots in the area. I always call in my order as I am driving over there to pick it up and my food is always ready right when I get there. Naan is excellent. Free chai tea - also excellent.

I wish there were more Indian restaurants like House of Curries.  It's inexpensive, has great food and is casual.  Knowing that I can order paneer tikka masala (which is amazing), a side of basmati and a side of naan, all for under $10 is fantastic!  I usually have enough leftovers for a small lunch the next day as well.  At most Indian restaurants all of that would cost at least $16-18.  It's a shame I live halfway across the country and can't indulge in cheap Indian food anymore.

I came here to have dinner with some friends. It was my first time at this particular House of Curries (I've been to the one on Solano Ave in Albany, and the one on College Ave in Berkeley). I ordered the Mushroom Masala and a plate of rice. I paid $8.25. The meal arrived very quickly, but the Masala portion was smaller than what I felt like I paid for. However, the dish itself was delectable - not oily/greasy, and very flavorful. The rice was good as well.

The main problem I had with this place was the atmosphere. The restaurant looked pretty dirty and disorganized. I felt uncomfortable using their utensils and drinking their water. I found a piece of caked-on unknown substance on my cup.................I'm not a super neat freak or anything nor am I super fancy...it's just that I expect a place serving food that goes into my body to be cleaner.

Years ago, I ate my first Indian food here, and remember being totally wowed. In the years since, I've had a chance to explore other options for Indian food, and even learn to cook some of my favorite dishes. I know I changed, and maybe House of Curries changed too, but it just is not that tasty to me anymore. The palak paneer is often bland, the potatoes in aloo gobi undercooked, and the last couple of times I've gone my naan has been charred. While House of Curries will always be special as my first, there are enough other good Indian restaurants in the area that I do not think I'll be eating here again.

House of Curries, or HoC as my friends call it, has a special place in my heart. It was the first Indian restaurant I had ever tried, and while it was impressive two years ago, I can't recall if it's their food that's gone down in quality or if my standards have just become too high. Needless to say, their food is subpar. It's the type of food that'll have you questioning whether or not you'll be hovering over the toilet at 2AM. 

I ordered the chicken tikka with naan. Why did the chicken tikka come to me lukewarm? The naan was also really bready... I can usually down two of these puppies, but these were just so heavy. Maybe i's because they set up that buffet... I'm not sure, but if I ever wanted a fix, I'd head down to everest down telegraph. Their food costs a teeny bit more, but the quality is miles ahead.
go to the one on college ave., its way better. not just better though, like its really good indian food.
I can't believe that HOC is rated so low!! I have been to dozens of Indian/Pakistani places around the country and HOC cannot be beat. The cholay ghosht is a m a z i n g.

I had a hankering for Indian... and my friend agreed to go with me despite having the stomach flu. That's true friendship. So off to House of Curries we went...

Food was decent. The naan was huge and prices are very reasonable. I think I've been spoiled by Shalimar in Fremont, but the curries here just weren't nearly as flavorful and tasty as they are there. I love lamb curry.

My friend also had a really gaseous night. Don't feel bad for her -- I was the one sharing a bed with her after all.

I don't get it, why does this place have a higher review average than naan n curry? The naan here, for one, is significantly lower quality (and harder) than the luscious naan I've experienced at naan n curry. Also, the sauces do not taste nearly as good. The customer service is great and the restaurant itself might feel nicer, but the food is what I come for, and I would personally get my naan and chicken tikka masala at naan n curry instead, despite it being a block further from where I live. 
Maybe there are other menu items that are better that I have not tried, but I believe the staple foods of the restaurant to be of utmost importance when determining its quality.

Yeah, is about as bland as chalk on a plate but its a DOLLAR people!
You want excellent seasoned Indian food? Go hop your critical ass down to Dosa.

The naan, lentils, and salads are worth it. I go here when I'm having a bad digestion day and eat totally vegetarian to clean out my system. The meat dishes aren't that good, everything feels and tastes like it was boiled prior to being dropped into some form of sauce.

I got a mango lassi, naan, lentils, and okra for under $5.  So much better for you than McCrap.

If I don't feel like cooking, and I don't feel like eating Italian food, this is the default place to go.

I always order the two same things: Lamb Vindaloo and a plain naan. I loooooooooooove spicy (and when I say spicy, I mean burn your tongue and burn a hole in your stomach spicy) food, and I always ask them to make their Lamb Vindaloo as spicy as they can. They always warn me before I complete my order, but they've only been able to give me a mild or slightly spicy curry. The college ave House of Curries, on the other hand, burned several holes in my stomach. The naan is typical of what you'd get at any other big Indian restaurant in the area. Good when hot, not so good when cold. 

Even though the place isn't amazing, I still love coming here because I like curry (though I would like more spices), the free tea is great, and the owner is so sweet you can't resist not coming back for some more. Don't use the bathroom though, it's pretty gross.

A 3.5 rating from me.

Basically, I think I would've enjoyed dinner if my dish were not insanely,beyondlogicalreason SPICY. 

I ordered the lamb vindaloo and asked for medium/mild and basically had my tongue scorched off and one layer of my stomach lining burned away. Seriously, I can't even tell you what it tasted like because it was SO. SO. Spicy. I couldn't taste anything...

On the positive side, their Naan was warm and toasty, and after my death-by-spiciness dish, I tasted a friend's Chicken Tikka Masala and it basically was amazingly creamy and sweet. (But remember, I already had half my tastebuds burned off at this point so...) 

If you order something, tell them to keep it very mild! Unless you have a tongue of iron or enjoy not really tasting your food, you will have a rather unpleasant experience.

2.5 stars.

30 min wait for our food (they weren't even busy!) and everything came out lukewarm :(

SERVICE: Order at the counter. The guy working the cash register seemed a bit impatient with me.

AMBIANCE: We chose a seat by the window, which was great. They share a space with the Beauregard Hotel, so it looks a bit lobby-ish.

FOOD: 
- I don't remember the exact name, but it was a chicken curry with bell peppers: Good taste but a relatively small portion. Also, it came out lukewarm :(
- plain naan: nicely sized with good crispiness. This also came out lukewarm and quickly turned cold :( :(
- basmati rice: Again, lukewarm. It even had larger hard chunks, indicating it was reheated unevenly. :( :( :(

OVERALL: I have fond memories of House of Curries... sadly, my most recent experience didn't live up at all! Bring your A game next time!

Ewww...My bestfriend when to the bathroom and was GROSSED out..the food portions are TINY and the naan was HARD! We paid about 10 each for two dishes, one rice, and one naan...no thank you...

P.S cobwebs in the corner and a long wait time..

Oh House o' Curries.
I came to Berkeley thinking that Indian food sucked (save for Vik's Chaat) and didn't visit any of the local Indian eateries for the first year. 

Then I tried House of Curries.

My go-to dishes are the Chicken Tikka Masala and the onion naan. The tikka masala is hot, creamy, cheesy, and filled with spices. Not spicy at all, yet still flavorful. The chicken goes great with it. I like to dip my hot, freshly baked naan in the tikka masala, and I always ALWAYS leave satisfied. I can probably eat this meal everyday of the week and not get sick of it.
They have free chai, although it's really not my thing. Also, the upstairs seems to be some kind of hotel/motel. Somewhat shady. 

My only downside to this place would be that it doesn't open as late as some Asian Ghetto restaurants, and that it can be dirty at times. The bathrooms are usually in need of some cleaning.

i've been to the HoC on college and had a good experience there.
unfortuanately, i wasn't TOO thrilled about my paneer tikka masala at this one on durant. the taste was really tomato-y and, while i understand that tomatoes are used in tikka masala, this honestly just tasted like the creamy red pepper tomato soup at trader joes. the naan was good, and the curry was thick and creamy, but the taste was just off to me.

The food is a 3.5-4 but the place is really loud and poorly insulated.  Also there is something about it that makes it feel very dirty.  

on another note, i was here with my co-worker early this week.  Sitting at the table across from me was a European couple that was full on making out.  Like the woman was partially sitting on the guy, their bodies were pressed up against each other, they were running hair through fingers (sometimes pulling each other's hair), running hands under shirts and basically eating up each other's faces with their curry breath.   Serious face licking, crotch grabbing, and whispering sweet nothings to each other between licks.  For twenty minutes.    They were caught up in their love bubble that they never even looked up to catch people's dirty looks!   The employees didn't even say anything so it was up to me to step in.  

They didn't stop until i asked them to stop.  When they finally left the dude apologized and said in a very genuine tone "I hope that some day you will feel the way we do."   You mean so self-involved that I hump my partner at a cheap (but tasty) Indian restaurant?  Um okay.  Talk about goals

Cheap cheap cheap! The chicken in the curries can be hit or miss though. At times they were REALLY tender and other times, I couldn't bite into it at all. If you come with two people, just get a curry and two naans :] It'll be MORE than enough food. The chai tea is SUPER milky. Cannot even taste the spices of that tea... but it's free so can't complain! 

Seating area is kinda dirty. Has those flies that fly around in circles...(why do they do that?) and the tables are unstable (put elbow on table and then the whole table sways...ugh).

Mediocre food. Good prices.

Also, kinda dirty place. I realize that the area and the place do not promise anything more than quick and tasty, but that doesn't mean I have to feel disgusted looking at the opaque glasses, and sauce-splashed tables.

After reading some Yelp reviews, I decided to try this place.

I walked to location, the building is a large white building with pillars, you don't really see the restaurant until you walk up the steps. 

There were a few customers eating inside, I walked up, greeted by the gentleman by the register. I ordered palak paneer, garlic naan, and some rice on the side to go. I sat down and waited for my food. The gentleman at the counter doesn't speak very much english but said I should get some tea. I politely refused, saying that I was just going to get my food and be off. He still pulled out a to-go cup for me and insisted I have some tea, which I thought was sweet of him to do so. 

Glancing around, I see that much of it is self served. You get your own plates, forks/spoons, napkins, tea, and water. They have carafe with water in a refrigerator and a tea dispenser. The tea is a little watered down but not bad after some sugar and milk. 

Now the food: the palak paneer is great. It's tasty and spicy. Now, as far as spicy is concerned: I come from LA, where Indian fast food roams free. What I expected is a good solid heat from any Indian fare I eat. If you like spicy, this place is great. The rice was lightly flavored and awesome with the paneer. The garlic naan is fantastic. They give you this huge round piece of naan, it's the right amount of garlic and spices, good just to munch on it's own. 

All this for $10.95, what I got is enough for maybe two meals. I will return again.

This is by far some of the best tasting curry I have ever had, though my experiences are limited to a few restaurants back in AZ and the few I've tried here in the bay area. By my foodie standards, though, the price is cheap ($6) for the curry, but you have to pay extra for the rice or naan. Still, $6 for a tub of curry to go it pretty cheap if you can make your rice at home.

The only thing is that I ordered paneer and chicken tikka masala on two different occassions and both time there wasn't enough cheese or chicken. I wish they included a little more substantial food and a little less sauce, but you can always add your own meat! Haha, really what makes the tikka masla is the sauce and the lack of a large amount of spiciness for me, so this is perfect!

Oh and one time I ate there with some friends and just nibbled on some of their stuff, but the wait was really long. Somewhere around an hour and a half...and it wasn't even that busy when we got there. It was busier when we left, and I noticed some people who ordered after us got their food first. They should work on that.

But free chai tea while you wait! :)

1 star for the free chai and gulab jamun given to us.

I've walked by here many times while living in Unit 2, and my roommate and I decided to try it out tonight for dinner. I am a pretty big fan of Indian food, but my experience here sucked to be honest. I placed my order with the cashier (owner?), and he seemed pretty nice until it came to paying for my meal. My total came out to $9.32, and I gave him $10 but he said I only gave him $9. He made it seem like I only paid $9 and he was being "nice" for letting the 32 cents slide. I realized after that I definitely gave him $10 when I looked at my wallet, but losing 68 cents was no big. I considered it a tip and didn't dwell on it. My roommate (who isn't from America) also said she wasn't given her change, and when I told her that it happened to me too, she confronted the cashier/owner about it. My roommate has a pretty thick accent, but you can definitely understand every word she said to him. The cashier looked at us and gave a big stupid grin acting like nothing happened. He kept saying "No problem! We are open on Friday!" acting like he didn't understand what we were saying. We tried explaining, but he still gave us the same act talking about some other subject that wasn't even remotely relevant. We gave up, and angrily ate our pretty bland meal. My curry was nothing special, and the garlic naan was lukewarm and not soft/fluffy like the way naan should be. The cashier came by later and gave us two pieces of gulab jamun maybe because he felt bad that he tricked us. But no amount of sugary goodness will make me forget my horrible first experience here. I probably will never eat here again.

I've recently started to love Indian food, and this is one of my go-to places whenever I crave Chicken Tikka Masala. 

As you can guess, I only order the Chicken Tikka Masala and it's a pretty good price considering how full you get. I recommend spending the extra $1 or so to get the garlic naan to go with it; it's just not the same without it. The naan is always hot, fluffy, and never dry, and goes great with the Chicken Tikka Masala. What I love even more about the food is the complimentary hot chai tea: SO DELICIOUS. I'm a big tea lover, and this is definitely something I love to sip on when I'm catching up with friends. The only downside is that the chicken can be a little dry at times, but soaking it up with the curry sauce does add some moisture to the meat.

The restaurant can get pretty crowded at times, but I love to sit with my friends on the patio on a gorgeous day. It's a very relaxing atmosphere, and no one is pushing you to hurry up and finish your food. 

It's a really good go-to spot for some cheap and quick Indian food that is actually pretty tasty. Also, this is where a lot of Berkeley students go to eat as well, so if you want to learn a little more of what Berkeley college life is like, check this place out!

I come here almost every week.

probably the best Indian restaurant near the Berkeley campus.

the place could be more clean but its awesome curry and naan makes up for it.

Employees are super friendly and they remember what you always get.

I noticed many people get Chicken Tikka Massala but I suggest you try other dishes as well even though they are bit more pricy.

My stomach doesn't like curry as much as I do, and this chicken curry simply isn't worth the sacrifice.  Naan 'N Curry tastes better, but I would take a date to House of Curries.  Free tea is a definite plus and I can drink gallons of it.  

I think most people who want Indian food expect some spice, but my ex thought it was too spicy.  I love spicy foods and disagreed wholeheartedly.  I actually think it could stand to be spicier.  The naan was good--typical naan.

best naan hands down - order them one at a time so they come out fresh!

we get the aloo vindaloo (not on menu), tikka masala sauce (not on menu), and the chana masala - the best in berkeley and the price is perfect.

Love this place. I eat here with my friends all the time because their curry is so damn good and addicting. Don't know what it is, but I want to steal their recipe. And I come here so often the cashier gives me a little discount. +1star

And when my friends came to visit Berkeley, where did I take them? Sure sure, I let them try Top Dog and Cheeseboard - but it wouldn't be right to see them off without House of Curries! My tourist-friends later told me it was a good restaurant choice and finished every last bit of curry and naan. i'm such a good host hehe

Cheap. Fast. Delicious. (Authentic?) 

Recommendations: 
Tikki Chicken Masala: Almost everyone orders this 
+ Garlic Naan: a must! regular naan is tasty too though  
+ Mango drink: sweet, fruity, thick - the way i like it 
+ their milk tea 
= Two Thumbs Up!

Great food, probably the best in Berkeley, but I think it is really hard to give them 5 stars because it is a bit more pricy than usual, and moreover it is not full service.   I have no problem paying more for good food, but service is very important, experience is key to going back to a restaurant, but the food is probably the best, very vegetarian friendly, nice staff.  4.4 Stars if I can give ratings like that.

I'd say I come here every week or two and always order the same thing: chicken vindaloo with garlic naan. I am rarely disappointed. The vindaloo is spicy, and the naan is perfectly crisp.  The staff is very friendly and are always saying how they are so happy to see me.  Good seating for Berkeley standards, and it has a nice little patio in front.  The inside seating can be a little drafty/dark, but a good place for a moderate size group.  Also, they are open until 11pm which is nice.  It can get a little slow if they are busy, so I recommend calling in your order ahead of time. 

I would have given 5 stars, but every 1 out of 10 visits or so, they vindaloo is not up to par and seems to be missing one of its normal spices. I'm not sure if they sometimes have a back up cook or something.  Overall, the food is still excellent, but in those instances just not what I expected.
Chicken tikka masala is the dish to get. with potato naan

There's only a marginal difference between this place and Naan N' Curry, but I'll always prefer this place.  First, it's closer to campus. Second, it's cleaner, and third, they have patio seating.  We almost always get the chicken tikka masala with garlic and potato/aloo naan.  Good stuff.  The place is semi self serve in that you get your own water and tea.  It's always filled with students and the waiters are always friendly.

Hmmm I think it might be the nice scenery/interior and the cheesey naan thats encouraging me to give it 3 stars.  It wasn't terrible but it wasn't fantastic. Except the cheese naan. That was pretty darn good imo.  But then again I'm no curry or naan expert.  This place was pretty crowded, and we were served fairly fast but I might have to come back again sometime to comment on the curry.  For now it's 3 stars for the cool location and cheesy naan! Oh and the mango lassi wasn't half bad : )

Whenever I crave cheap food or want to feel REALLY old, I eat around the Berkeley campus. Came in last night for some Indian food and we ordered a LOT of food for under $20... shocking, really.

Fought through the hordes of college kids to order our food and find a table. The place is a little grimey but for $6 Indian food, it's to be expected.

The food was great. Having been vegan for about 4 months now, I love how I have a ton of options when ordering Indian/Pakistani food.

There's a House of Curries opening up in my hood on Grand Lake - I wonder if they are related?

With friendly service, munchonme deals, and delicious Chicken Tikka Masala, House of Curries is my go-to place for Indian food, whenever I have the craving.

It's a little more expensive than Naan n Curry, but the restaurant, to me, seems cleaner and does not smell as much like curry, like Naan n Curry. Also, the Naan is fluffier at House Of. Much rather prefer that :)

OK, not sure if their prices went up or if I was underestimating, but CTM + naan will run you $8.49 including tax.

Still worth it though... This is pretty much the only place that me and my buddies will walk 15 min across campus to eat at.

the place says it all. if you love curries it's the place to go. i ordered lamb curry, it was delicious, spiced right. they serve huge naans too. the place is kinda tight tho but that shouldn't stop you from checking out this place.

This is one of my favoritest places to eat.  The chicken vindaloo is sublime spicy yumminess ... if I go more than a few days without it, I start to get the shakes.  If you like spicy food, I can't recommend it highly enough.

House of Curries is the place I go to for comfort food. My friend and I love coming here after midterms/finals. I love coming here to sit and chat, especially on a warm night.

ATMOSPHERE:
I've never been to the one on College Avenue, but the one on Durant is located in a quaint white building that is actually a hotel. It's odd, but fits in perfectly with the rest of the oddities in Berkeley.

I enjoy eating on the patio and there are umbrellas that shade you while you scoop up the remaining curry off your plate. Inside, there's ample seating. It has a very cozy feel to it and you can see the cooks preparing the curry and bread behind the register.

FOOD:
I always get the chicken tikka masala with their regular naan. I got their garlic naan before. It was a little salty for my taste, so I stick to regular naan.

The chicken is good and comes in large chunks. I always have to cut it up into smaller pieces but it's pretty tender so it's easy to cut. I'm not an expert when it comes to Indian food, but I do know that the CTM is very tasty. The portions look deceivingly small when the servers bring it to your table, mainly because the naan is huge. However, there is definitely enough curry for you to eat with the naan. The naan is fluffy and airy.

Also, when you order, you get complimentary hot chai tea, which you sweeten with their giant bowl of sugar that is conveniently located next to the dispenser. You can also get a large pitcher of iced water and bring it to your table. The tea is delicious and tastes great on a cold day.

I love coming here, but I'm starting to question the cleanliness of this place. I found a strand of hair in my curry and my friend said he found a whole fly in his rice. Hopefully my food is clean the next time I go, because I'll be devastated if I can no longer come here for the comfort food.

I am not much a connoisseur of Indian food but I figured I should review this place because its on my labs "approved list" of places to go for lunch.  

1. Atmosphere --Clean and spacious unlike Naan and Curry.  They also have a nice outdoor dining area.

2.  Indian curry makes me sick so I have only eaten tandori chicken breast here.  It is not dry like some places, spiced just right and the tomatoes are always fresh.  If going with the chicken I recommend getting an aloo naan.  The potatoes inside give it better flavor and it isn't as dry as a regular naan.

I recently had an epiphany: I love curry. So, there's no way I can ever give a curry joint less than 4 stars... unless its reaaaaaally bad. So 4 stars it is! I always get the paneer tikka masala with 2 garlic naans. Fills me up for lunch twice. I like how you don't smell like you bathed in curry after eating here (unilke Kabana, but it's worth it!) and there's outdoor seating. I love outsoor seating. I deinitely prefer house of curries over naan and curry for quality and if I'm on southside.... but if you're a big eater and want variety, the buffet at naan and curry might be a better fit.

I love this place. They make tasty and cheap Indian food and they do it fast!

Their chicken tikka masala (I know, not really a traditional Indian dish, sue me) is delicious, as is everything else I've tried, but I'll be honest and say that I pretty much always get CTM. Naan is huge and well cooked -- hits that perfect balance between fluffy and crunchy every time. 

Free chai tea with your meal is a plus. 

If you're getting your food to go, call ahead and place the order over the phone as you head out the door -- it'll be ready and waiting by the time you get there. I do this all the time and it's so great to skip the long line that sometimes forms for ordering.

House of Curries is one of the many Indian restaurants in Berkeley.  I usually get the Palak Ghosht or Chicken Palak, which is a spicy spinach dish with whatever meat.  I like the palak here better than Naan n Curry, but its TWICE that they've burned my naan here.  Burned naan ruins the whole meal, since you use the naan to scoop out the morsels of meat and spinach and you come to realize that the restaurant doesn't care if they serve someone burned naan, as long as they got paid for it.  However, this has only happened twice.  

I really love Indian Chai tea but it is sooo watered down sometimes, it's insane.  I feel like I'm drinking hot water that happens to be brown.  

The food is pretty consistent and the service is okay.  It's nice because you can choose to sit inside or sit outside on the porch.

As a Cal student, the option is usually between House of Curries or Naan N' Curry. I tend to frequent the latter more often, but decided to go out to House of Curries with a couple of friends the other night and try to figure out the difference.

The menu is pretty much the same, but I feel like Naan N' Curry has more variety and selection. I ordered the Lamb Curry with rice. I decided to get it so I could stray away from the typical Chicken Tikka Masala but still have a taste of my favorite meat. However, I just wasn't that impressed. There was plenty of meat, which is great, but the taste just lacked a lot. I felt like I was consuming watered down curry, and the lamb itself wasn't seasoned too well either.

Maybe it's because of the rush of customers that night, but most of my experiences at House of Curries have been just alright; nothing too spectacular.

We got three different chicken curries and a garlic naan. They were all flavorful, but a little on the salty side. We also went during the dinner rush, around 7:30pm, so the seating in the front was full, but there was seating in the back, and the cashier was very nice about making sure we got our orders despite the longer than usual wait time. The food overall was delicious, and the chai tea was super good. I had two cups and wanted more.

It seems like this place shouldn't be that great. They play really awful music, on repeat, really loudly. It's almost always packed with obstreperous Cal students, it doesn't look like much and it's incredibly cheap. Plus they fail my basic test of an Indian restaurant: the quality of the yogurt. Their raita sucks.

But otherwise? The food is GREAT, and they are always consistent. The baingan bharta here is unlike anywhere else I've had it and it's absolutely delicious; it's cooked down to the point where it's almost like a thick creamy sauce, and the taste is fantastic. The tandoori chicken legs are spiced perfectly and never dry. Lamb dishes are all winners, and the tikka masala sauce is so wonderful I've known folks who simply ordered a plate of nothing but the sauce to eat with naan or a spoon. (I know, I know, tikka masala was invented to satisfy white people...it's still darn tasty)

I went through a period last winter where I ate here daily for weeks. I always leave here feeling nourished, perfectly satiated and warm all over.

I love this place. When I'm in the Durant/"Asian Ghetto" area and I'm wondering which place to eat at, this place always wins my vote. Their garlic naan is the best - nice and fluffy and pretty big). I love their paneer tikka masala - its perfect, and their paneer doesn't taste like readymade paneer. The people are always very nice, friendly and humble. I get cravings for this place, it's that good :)
I ate here almost once a week when I was in college.  The food's good and the service is great.  Plus, the free tea is a total perk.

This place is DA BOMB!

* THE FOOD
One of the better indian foods I've ever had. Everything is well seasoned with the perfect amount of spices where it isn't too overpowering. Additionally their naan is to die for! However their roti was just so so. Also I don't usually like tandoori, but I decided to try their shrimp tandoori and was overwhelming surprised at how great it tasted and not dry or bland. Also their chicken tikki masala is perfect! I say EAT THIS! 

* THE AMBIANCE
It's definitely a casual setting meant for your locals so don't expect anything fancy.

* FREE CHAI! I REPEAT FREE CHAI! Now go try this place already.

The lamb curry is one of my favorite alternatives to the Chicken Tikka Masala. Now that they are the same price, I would definitely go with the lamb curry since it's not as creamy and heavy. 

The garlic naan always comes fresh and hot, ready to go. The garlic taste isn't overpowering and mixes well with the lamb curry.
Great food and great prices! Excellent menu selection! Seating can be sparse at times.

While I attended UCB, I must have tried just about everything on the menu. The chicken tikka masala is, by far, the tastiest item on the menu. If you are looking for something on the healthier side (the owner himself will tell you it's jam packed with heavy cream), I'd try the Saag Paneer, a whipped spinach puree which is spiced to perfection and topped with cubes of Indian cheese. The naan is always fresh and the free chai tea is always welcomed by the patrons. There are lots of seating areas and you never have to wait around for a table.

A restaurant with an unimposing (but has stairs) entrance, and a great place to find reasonably-priced Indian food. I really love their chicken tikka masala, with its creamy and spicy consistency, which is perfect with their wonderfully-baked naan bread to dip into... No need for soda here because the great taste of the naan dipped in masala sauce makes you forget about ordering something sweet for a while!

Average curry

I ordered the Lamb Curry, Shrimp Biryani and an Aloo naan. All items were fine, quite tasty and good quality but nothing stand out.

Staff were friendly and super polite service, it is convenient to campus and open later than others in the area.

Free tea is a nice touch while you wait for take out.

their homemade naan is amazing! sometimes they overcook it so its burnt which is a disappointment. my mom ordered a dish that was too spicy and they refused to let her exchange it. if they are going to have something that hot, they need to have those little spicy illustrations to let people know... because who would know that chicken tandori is hot? and most indian places ask how how you want it. my dish, the tika masala, was amazing and mild. 

free chai tea and water :)

Ordered the chicken tikki masala (the thing that everyone usually orders) and am 100% sure I will never come back here again, not even on a CampusCred discount which was the reason I came here this time.

The chicken that I had in my meal was inedible. To be honest, I think all the chicken they serve here is inedible. When I ordered the chicken tikki masala, here's how the prep went: get a pan, dump about a cup of oil into the pan, get a spatula full of the curry from a vat that's pre-prepared, and then get four 1 in. x 1 in. sized cubes of chicken *from an uncovered plastic bin that's been sitting out for the whole day* and then cook it. No wonder it tastes so terrible. Probably not even sanitary... The chicken is clearly an afterthought in the dish. Would not come here again.

I only ate here once, but it really hit the spot.   I was in the mood for a nice rich creamy tikka masala with hot fresh naan and house of curries delivered.  Wonderfully spiced curry and soft steamy naan.

I'm still pretty new to Berkeley and I haven't tried a lot of places in the area but my friend (that went here for undergrad) brought me for a random Thursday night dinner.  We got the Chicken Tikka Masala, eggplant curry and 2 garlic naan's for $18.  Skip the eggplant curry but definitely get the Chicken Tikka Masala if you come here.  

It's not mind blowing but it's pretty good.

I have been going to House of Curries (or "HoC" as my friends and I like to call it) since my freshman year of college.  I have been an avid fan since that first fateful night I walked into this delicious temple of magic.  Alright, so the place lacks ambiance, and the decorations are less than authentic (Chinese lanterns at an Indian restaurant?), but that just adds to this place's charm.  

Having eaten at literally every Indian restaurant in Berkeley, I can hands down say this one is my favorite.  The food is flavorful.  The servers are friendly, and in fact one of the cashiers asks how my family is every time I go in after meeting them one time! 
 
If you are looking for a fancy sit down place that will take your order at the table, then you have come to the wrong place.  But, if you are down to order at the counter and clean the fuck up after yourself after eating the best Tikka Masala, Biryani, and Naan in town, then House of Curries is the spot!

Seriously this food is so good.  Go eat there now.  Do it.  I'm jealous I can't join you.

if i could have paneer tikka masala, garlic naan, and samosas every meal...I WOULD. however, my bf doesn't think it's good for my health so we have it about once a week...more if i ask him when he's drunk! =]]] one time we were allll the way on warring st at 10:26...i thought HOC closed at 10:30, we ran our asses down there to discover that it was open until 11....best meal ever!!

Recently got take-out here.  The food was so-so in terms of flavor...for the money, you can definitely get better Indian food in Berkeley as this place is just about average in terms of $$ for generic Indian food.  I had the chicken tikka masala (sauce was ok but not super flavorful, and chicken was very dry) and the palak paneer (super bland).  

Unfortunately I found a piece of cardboard in my palak paneer mid-way through eating it - EW.  While I suppose that's not the most disgusting thing you could find in your food, it certainly does not give me a ton of confidence that the conditions are sanitary and that the food is high-quality.

Definitely wasn't impressed with this place. First off, the cashier laughed at the picture my atm card and was like "hohoho you had a lot of hair".  Yeah, thanks.

Also, going along on that wonderful service note, some of my friends orders took forever to come out. My friend ordered right after me, and her food came out a good 10 minutes after mine came out. 

For the food, I've had plenty better curry elsewhere. Their curry is the type that gets worse and worse the more bites you take of it. Halfway through I was just like "no, I can't eat anymore of this. its making me sick". The naan also was pretty bad. It wasn't soft at all. Really dry and hard. 

Sorry, but I won't be returning.

I have never craved curry until I had House of Curries curry. 

I love the curry here. Although I only ever get the chicken tikka masala (with paneer because it's awesome), I always come back for more.

Not only is the curry delicious, the staff is very friendly. My friends and I have befriended one of the cashiers, Bishal, and he's always nice and smiley. "The same?" he asks when we enter. Yep, he's awesome.

Gotta give a shout out to the tea too. YUM.

House of Curries is a fun, simple, inexpensive and delicious place nestled quaintly inside of a white facade hotel. It's a bit incongruous, but the overall effect works very well.

Their food is undeniably delicious, and falls perfectly into that cheap comfort food category. All of their curries are spicy and very tasty. Nothing is overly greasy, or even greasy at all. The portions are perfect for a single person. Not to mention their incredible naan, which doesn't have even a hint of grease to it. Everything is just exceedingly well prepared, and quickly too. You'll maybe wait 5 minutes. Also at maybe 10 dollars a person, it won't kill your bank account. 

The free tea, and pitchers of water are a nice touch.

Not much can be said for the staff. They're actually really quiet, but nonetheless polite, and speedy. They'll gladly answer questions about anything on the menu, and generally seem willing to help you however they can.

As stated before, it's nestled inside a hotel. The whole feel of the place is quite fun because of it, and the outside patio area is really nice to eat on, especially during a beautiful day. Definitely take advantage of that.

Yup, cheap, tasty, nice atmosphere. 4 stars.

FOOD:
1.) Chicken tikki masala= This was good
2.) Chicken something curry = Hella spicy! I'd prefer the masala one next time.
3.) Garlic Naan
4.) Chai tea = omg free chai tea that tastes just like milk tea if you add some sugar, mmm!! 


SERVICE:
Order at counter and they bring it out to you. The workers here are pretty nice. The prices are really cheap too


ATMOSPHERE:
In an old colonial building aha pretty random. But it has a nice patio area to sit at, and big windows with overhanging chandeliers.
First time I ate lamb curry was at this location and it was delicious! Everybody should try the lamb vindaloo ,basmati rice and naan...yum!

House of Curries is so damn tasty!  

I went here randomly last night...I was originally supposed to go try this fabulous taco truck with the sis, but since it was closed we opt for some curry which she insisted was "the best curry ever!"...

Boy was she so right! I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and told the friendly owner to make it extra extra extra spicy ... I also got a side of naan and actually wished I paid more attention to the menu because I probably would have saw that they had garlic naan and got that instead...BUT still the original naan comes out toasty, soft, and warm =) 

My Chicken Tikka Masala was served pippin hot (just the way I like it) ...the chicken was a teeny bit dry but the sauce totally made up for it...I made good use of the naan and wiped my dish clean... it could have been a bit more spicy but then hey I'm actually glad it didn't because I had a real bad tummy ache when I went to sleep... 

Despite having to get up in the middle of the night to use the bathroom for about two hours ( I know TMI) ....I would still absolutely go again... maybe this time though I won't tell them to make it spicy x3    =P

I come here a lot.  I guess it helps that I live right down the street from it.  

House of Curries has both its good days and it's bad days.  The food is still mighty tasty (though it may not be authentic).  Most of the time, the naans are cooked well, the biryani is tasty, the curries are flavorful (favorites: Chicken or Paneer TIkka Masala, Daal Gosht, the lamb saag ,and chicken vindaloo).  

Occasionally, the naans are burnt, the tikka masala has been diluted with cream, the lamb curry/vindaloos was too oily, the biyrani was dry.... I think it happens when you go in at a slow time, or they haven't anticipated the number of customers. 

Of course free chai is a plus. 

All of the flavored naans are also very good. love the onion and the garlic naans especially

Flipping DEEE-licious.  Chicken Tikka Masala was super tasty.  I also had a sliced eggplant dish that was fabu.  The chutney was amazing.  
It was the depth of the flavor and the freshness of the ingredients that won me over.  Plus, the price is right (though the portions are small) AND they DELIVER.

Okay so I have eaten at house of curries three times in three weeks and I have had nothing but good experiences. First off I walked into this restaurant for the first time on a whim, my boyfriend and I were hungry and we just had a feeling about this place. So walked in and the guy at the counter was extremely friendly. He asked if we had been there before and we said no and he was eager to go over the menu with us telling us what he recommended. I would like to note that he didn't point at the most expensive item on the menu like some other people would do. He then told us the deal. You seat yourself and get your own utensils and there is free chai while you wait. We ordered Lamb, Chicken Tikka Masala, Rice, and naan all for $13. The food was great. Even if the service had been bad we would have come back. Every time I come here I enjoy myself. I have come at all different hours and with other people and the general consensus is that the food is good, the service is great, and the price is right especially for a college student.  

I recommend the potato naan it is delicious.  The filling has a nice texture to it but you need to make sure to eat it while it is hot so it doesn't get to soggy. I will update this review as I try everything on the menu.

I discovered my love for Indian food when I began studying at Berkeley. The only problem is, I'm not Indian so i can't really tell if a place tastes good or bad. But, I've formed an opinion about House of Curries..it's decent at best.

I generally love naan with my curry, but almost every single time I come here, which is probably at least 3-5 times a month, my naan is burnt! =[ If you order the garlic naan, the burnt parts aren't too bad since the strong taste of garlic cancels it out. 

All the curries here are pretty good. They also have a big pot of chicken tikka masala ready so if you're in a hurry, just order that. The paneer dishes here aren't too bad, just not fresh. I love the vindaloo, but alas! It's spicy, spicy so beware if you can't handle the pain. You're tongue, tummies, and bowels will be paying for it later that night and the next morning. 

It's hard to find seating here at times, esp during meal hours, and service is kind of slow, but if you want Indian food near campus--this is the place! A better option and if you dont mind a bit of walk will be Biryani House on University and Shattuck.

I really truly enjoy House of Curries. I had my first Indian dish at House of Curries 3 years ago and this is still one of my favorite Indian places. 

Personal favorite? Chicken Tikki Masala. I'm not a fan of too much spice so I always go with this. The tikki masala with some naan [either garlic or regular] is great! There is free tea and water which is great to enjoy with friends. 

The customer service is great as well. There's not too much table side service, but there isn't need for any. You walk in, order and then sit down where you want to. The waiters will find you and bring you your food. I know people don't often clean up after themselves, but I just find that cleaning up and placing all my dishes in the bin kind and courteous! 

This is my apartment's go-to Indian place. We love it!

Very average Indian food, pretty expensive for what it gives.

Service/Decor: Usually very loud, service is decently fast, unlimited chai is definitely a  plus. 

Food: I'm not a huge fan of the food here. I got the Palak Paneer like I usually do at Indian restaurants, and it was pretty greasy and bland. The naan isn't seasoned properly and some of the rice in their dishes are hardened. Honestly, I can't even tell the difference between Naan N Curry and here.

I have nothing negative or positive to say about this place.

It was just a-okay for me. The food was okay. The naan was cooked well and the curry dishes were flavorful. 

Not the best Curry place in the area and certainly not the most memorable, but it is pleasant enough and tasty enough.

Many students frequent this place for their inexpensive price and generous portions.

got some tikka masala chicken with a munch voucher but passed on the rice since i didn't feel like paying 1.69 for it.

the sauce was creamy and a little spicy but the chicken meat was very dry, not tender.

friendly and fast service. fast cuz food was premade. would be 3 stars if the chicken was tender and more bitesize, not the size of meatballs.

Being a fourth year at Berkeley, I can't believe how long it took me to try this place out. My first time here a while ago was fantastic. I ordered a garlic naan and a chicken tikka masala. I was stuffed and still had enough leftovers to last another meal.

The next time I came, I was sure to bring my boyfriend so we could team up and finish everything while it was still fresh. We still got the garlic naan and chicken tikka masala, but added a side plate of rice. It was delicious! The sauce was rich and creamy with a hint of spiciness. I happily picked away at the naan while he scooped up spoonfuls of sauce drizzled rice. The bill was $11, which is way cheaper than getting 2 separate dishes from the ghetto across the street.

However, I came here today and was extremely disappointed. We got our usual, but the tikka masala sauce was way diluted. I couldn't tell whether I was eating sauce or water. Also, we usually wipe the plate down with the naan. But today, there was a whole layer of sauce left on the plate. (Either attributed to too much water, or just because it wasn't that good.)

I'm still going to give it 4 stars, because I'm forgiving and maybe they just had a busy/bad day. But I probably won't be thrilled to come back for a while. And I just hope that next time they will treat me right.

Sigh...........I would give a 0 star if that's an option.
and I feel bad to feel 'obligated' to disclose my experience

We went in one afternoon.  There were no line, about 4 tables were seated with scattering crowd.  Totally not busy.

We ordered samosa, aloo gobi, a vegetarian curry dish, rice and one naan.  There were two staffs in front, one cook, one cashier.

We waited, and waited, and waited.......for 30 min, 40 min.  We went up to the cashier, he said, it's coming it's coming.......ok, food arrived, partially, after 45 mins after we ordered.

All the dishes we ordered are not impressive at all.  Very blend, naan's not so great, sauce not so good.  I would say it's below average.  I would've gave a three star review just to be generous......but here's the deal breaker......

as i said, the food were partially arrived.  We had to waited for another 10 minutes for the aloo gobi to get to the table, while our naan, rice and curry had showed up 10 min before hand.  I asked the cashier (who's also the runner for food) that we are still missing the samosa.  He replied, it's coming, it's coming.......

We finished our food and waited for another 5 min.  There's a mini line start to form as it's the early dinner hour (around 5pm) and he's busy taking order and receiving payments (it's a pay in front operation).  We gave up.  I went up to the cashier, requesting a refund for our samosa.  He got anxious, checked the ticket, opened the 'microwave' and GRABBED THOSE TWO SAMOSAS WITH HIS HANDS, WHICH JUST TOUCHED SO MANY BILLS AND WHO KNOWS WHAT ELSE, AND PUT THOSE FOOD ON A PLATE.  I was stunned.  He said, here's your samosa.  

Maybe it's not a big deal for some, but, well, it'll never be justified in any health code standard.  Dirty hands touching food?  

I said to him, I can't eat it, I saw you taking cash from customers and went on grabbing my food without washing your hands.  Please give me my money back (and I am having this urge to call the Health Dept).  He pounded the samosa on the prep board and open the cash registered, took some cash out and gave it to me, didn't ring the credit in and didn't say a word.

I am sure he's not the owner........and I would've fire this guy if I am the manager there:(

I can't recall that I have ever have such a terrible experience at ANY Indian eatery ANYWHERE, including the ones I had complaints before.   House of Curries on Durant really made ALL THE OTHER competitions a much better choice.

I am sorry to post this terrible review but I think yelpers should know...

chicken tikka masala and garlic naan. 
all you can drink piping hot tea. yum. 

always a solid choice.

I was waiting in the parking lot of Andronicos for the hail/snow to melt before I drove home because I didn't want to crash (it was a crazy weather night!), and this guy comes up to my car and asks me to roll down my window, and asks for a ride, says he owns the house of curries and walked to andronicos, and if i'll give him a ride he'll treat me to dinner.

It was really nasty out, and I felt bad for the guy, so told him get get in & I'd give him a ride. As he's getting in the car, I have that 'oh f*ck' moment when I realize maybe it's not a good idea to give strangers rides on Friiday nights on Telegraph Ave.

And as we're pulling out of the parking lot, he's talking about how he used to want to be a meteorologist, and how there was a tornado sighting in the bay area.  It is then that I realize I may have let a crazy person in my car.  There are no tornadoes in the bay area, and if there were, I would know about it!

So I drive him to the house of curries and drop him off.  I tell him I'll be right in.  For a moment, I think about just driving off and never coming back.  But then I decide to just go with it and enjoy his kindness- I go find a parking space, and walk back over to the restaurant.

I had a great dinner on the house, the owner was super nice, and now I have a favorite place to go in Berkeley!

PS - When I got home, I checked the news, and there WAS a tornado ;)
So good. I fucking love old man curry.

This is the place to go if you're on south side and are looking for Indian food. The food is really good, and it's affordable too.

Perhaps the best thing about this place is that they have a lot of weird curries that you can't find at a lot of the other chain Indian restaurants. The bittermelon curry is an example of this (try it, it's really good).

The chicken tikka masala is mindblowing and the naan is delicious.
The free tea is pretty bland by itself but try adding a couple spoonfuls of sugar and it tastes a million times better.

The cooks are super pervy. They were all gross and smirky, blatantly taking camera phone pictures of me and my friend when we were paying. Yuck.

All in all, it's so good to find an Indian curry place that doesn't give me the runs or make me shit out blood.
It's worth smelling like India until you bathe and change clothes.

Horrible, horrible service and I only was able to take a few bites of the $9.00 dish I ordered.  Oh, and the "service" part is practically inexistent. You serve yourself pretty much, so it is already not worth how much everything costs. And the atmosphere even leaves something to be desired. However, the FOOD was the most disappointing of all. I ordered the mushroom masala and it was pretty much a PUDDLE OF GREASE (and a really small portioned puddle of grease...not at all worth the $9.00 I paid for it and the wheat roti, which was burnt and practically flavorless) . I asked about the oil and the server was completely inattentive. Also, I had to remind them to bring out the roti. Ughhh. I am extremely unsatisfied with this place and will never go here again! (And I was really hungry too...so considering that I found the food here really disgusting on an empty stomach...that's how bad it was....) All in all, my experience here was an extreme bummer. And my stomach is starting to squirm just from a few bites of that oily mess.

Did you hear that explosion? No? Well you should have because this place is BOMB!!! Food is awesome, service is even better (customer service, not really table service because there isn't any). My favorite thing to eat here is the Naan because it makes you feel like you're eating a warm, crispy, fluffy cloud of goodness. 

Side story of their awesomeness:

My gf would always order a plate of tomatoes and onions on the side with our food because it makes us feel healthier and they taste good with the curry. One day we came in, ordered our food, and Rashad (one of the workers there) remembered to add the tomatoes and onions, for free! On a later visit, my girlfriend and I were eating our food contently and out of nowhere comes a waiter with a plate of tomatoes and onions! This was months after our last visit and we were so happy and surprised that they remembered such a thing. 

Rashad ( I hope I spelled your name right) thanks for the awesome service man, we will be back!

DISCLAIMER: My reviews of Indian food are written from the very partial perspective of an Indian person from the South Bay, where there are very good Indian restaurants. With that said...

This place is disgusting.

Come here if you want curry that tastes like Easy Mac.

2 stars because I like sitting on their porch, eating samosas and sipping on free chai. And the people inside are really nice.

But honestly, what I've eaten here is tied with Naan n Curry for the worst Indian food I've ever had.

I ordered the lunch special Chicken Tikka Massala and was quite disappointed. The chicken was very dry, and the sauce was bland.  The veggies that came with the plate actually had flavor and weren't that bad. I would've traded in half of my enormous mound of rice for maybe one more little piece of chicken, the plate only came w/ three pieces. Definitely not coming back.

I used to dislike house of curries, but then, eating there means you're not eating at one of the places across the street, and also, I really like the free chai.

I've had a bunch of the dishes on the menu, and in general, I prefer the vegetarian dishes (even though I am not a vegetarian).  The veggi korma is what i usually get.

One thing that is very important, though, is to go in a big crowd and have everything family style. All of the dishes get somewhat old after a few bites, so it's nice to mix things up.

As I give the rating, I am conflicted, because the food is 5-star but the place/environment/service is hardly a 2 star. Ever since this place opened, just like Nancy said, I never ever went back to Naan N Curry again.

HOC's naan is infinite times better, and I get chicken tikka masala all the time cuz I like things sweet. Yes, sometimes the 5 pieces of chicken you get in the curry is dry and overcooked, but I don't eat it for the meat, I eat it for the hella delicious naan, so fluffy and angelic. Garlic naan also hella good, I'd say there's $1 worth of garlic on there, so it's worth $1.99 if you wanna splurge.

If you eat curry for the meat, try Raj Cafe in Albany on Solano instead. But if it's for the naan and the curry sauce, this place is awesome. =]

BUT there is the bad... the environment. Water smells kinda funny, utensils and plates aren't quite clean... one time, I waited almost an hour for the food to come, and all 5 of us were starving, it was ridiculous. We had to ask multiple times, and then they brought us some curry, which is great, but the naan didn't come til like 10 min later so the curry got cold.

I love this place! It tastes great, not pricey, and doesn't give me a stomachache like Naan N Curry does!! And the location is great. Close to campus. Friendly cashier too. I always get garlic naan + chicken biryani + lamb curry + chicken leg tandoori. Chicken tikka masala is great also. Sho good. Recommended!

Now that I've graduated from school, I don't get to come here as often as I used to as an undergrad at Cal. However, I make sure to stop by for a meal anytime I happen to be in Berkeley. Any east bay residents in search of Indian restaurant should definitely check out this place; not only is the food good, but excellent customer service as well. The cashier has become familiar enough with me to give me a warm and friendly greeting when I approach the register, and he even remembers my usual order so that I don't even need to tell him. A much appreciated gesture considering the fact that the workers at many restaurants and fast food places act as though they don't recall ever having seen you before in their life no matter how frequently you order food there. Extending the courtesy of not only a friendly demeanor, but also bothering to remember what specific entree you order, are indications that a business truly does appreciate its clientele and I can honestly say that is the customer service I've received from the cashier here. 

As far as the food itself, one thing you can definitely count on at this place is consistency; the chicken tiki masala is always delicious every time I come. And although you might think that since it's a considerably popular entree, most Indian restaurants serve good chicken tiki masala, that is not the case. I've eaten some very bland versions of it at other places, which makes me appreciate House of Curries all the more for the reliability of its consistently good food. Oh and something else to appreciate about this place is the complimentary tea! Most Indian restaurants charge you for ordering a cup of tea with your meal, but House of Curries offers a free tea to its customers when purchasing a meal. This is one gesture on their behalf that I most assuredly appreciate and serves as yet another reason to become a regular customer here. 

Another quality I enjoy about this place is the actual space of the restaurant itself. Since the building is actually an old hotel, it gives the place a certain degree of old-fashioned charm to it, which is much preferable to the more contemporary-looking buildings that house most of the other businesses along Telegraph near the campus. I especially like the outdoor seating areas; perfect for lunching with friends on sunny afternoons in the spring or summer. Ever since my friend Nancy introduced me to House of Curries, I was immensely impressed with this place and would regularly come to eat here in between classes. I prefer this place so much over Naan N' Curry on Telegraph, and I highly recommend House of Curries to anyone planning to be in the Berkeley area and who's craving some good Indian cuisine. Trust me, you won't regret giving this place a try; in fact, you'll most likely keep coming back for more.

I hated Indian food and all its cousins--Ethiopian, Egyptian, etc.  Until I tried this place a year and a half ago.  The naan and chicken tikka masala won me over, and since then, my palate's ever-expanding, which is probably a good thing.  

Ambience is okay.  Better than most other Indian restaurants I've been to, and while the prices aren't necessarily cheap, the man behind the cash register's got a pleasant enough demeanor it makes me think, "He's not ripping me off, and I think he likes me."  It's a good place to hang out and talk with a couple friends, isn't awful dirty (which is a restaurant prerequisite for me), and makes for a tasty (albeit food-coma inducing) meal.

This is a fairly decent Indian place if you're in the mood for Indian food and don't want to travel too far or pay too much for solid Indian food.

I like their potato naan.  & their chai tea.  The chai tea is free, and this makes me very happy.  I normally order the chicken tikka masala and the chicken tikka kabaab.  I don't really like the chicken actually.  It's really dry, but I find this to be the case with a lot of Indian places...so maybe it's just me.  They give you a lot of naan, but it's just okay.  Definitely nowhere near the best naan I've had.

The pros: cheap, convenient Indian food fix.  free chai tea :)
The cons: mediocre food really, about as clean as all the other places on telegraph and durant...
This place is great!

I was really confused for a while because I always had thought this place was just a hotel since it never had a House of Curries sign...but turns out it's both! They finally added the sign recently and I came to eat with some friends.

The food in general was good, I got the chicken tikka masala. I'm a big fan of the sauce. the meal comes with a large piece of naan you can enjoy. Service is sorta slow though.

My friends and I always take the circle table under the hanging ship from the ceiling near the window.  Countless times we have sat here studying or after an exam and indulge ourselves with the DELICIOUSNESS OF INDIAN FOOD.  

I was so happy when this place opened.  I never stepped foot in Naan & Curry again.  The foooooooooood is so good.  Aloo naan, garlic naan, or plain naan so fresh and delicious and big coming out of the kitchen in piles.  I like the GHOBI GHOSHT (lamb with cauliflower) the besssssst!  Sometimes their specials are very good so don't be afraid to try something new.  Get some of that green sauce from the fridge, i like it on my rice when i get biryani.  Don't forget to get a tall mango lassi too.  

The guys behind the counter are the friendliest people ever.  I've become very good friends with them and the owner (see my pictures!!!).  

I brought them the newspaper when they were voted Best of Berkeley 2007---which they most definitely are!

Great place for that Naan and Curry craving.  I suggest the Garlic Naan with the Chicken Tikka Masala, and a cup of milk tea to go along with it.  Very good food, very cute atmosphere and good, fast service.

This is the best indian food that I have had and I've had quite a bit of indian food. Actually I have had a couple places that were equal, but for higher prices.

If you each have a curry and your own rice/naan, it will be about $10 each. But if you do 3 people on 2 curries, or even 2 people on 1 curry, each with their own rice/naan, it will be about $7 each and you'll be satisfied. Also there are some great vegetarian curries that are cheaper, and probably healthier. Plus you get free unlimited milk tea!!!! 

Service is great. They used to be bad about refilling it, but I have not had a problem with it in the past year. They are very friendly and you can request it mild or spicy and they will actually oblige you.

I love the: chicken vindaloo (potatoes mmm), chicken karahi, and the vegetarian mushroom curry (lots of mushrooms mmm). The rice adds a lot of flavor that the naan does not so I prefer it. 

Their mango lassi and desserts aren't nearly as good of quality as their main dishes though.

If you have a friend who says they don't like Indian food or spicy food, have them order the chicken tikka masala mild (which, btw, goes much better with naan than the rice)

I'm pretty happy there is a better curry place (than naan n curry) near the UC campus because, although they're supposedly run by the same people, hoc is way better than nnc. 

i wish i could get vindaloo without the potatoes and more meat. my favorite spicy dish there *mouth watering* the garlic naan is amazing as well as their green sauce and free milk tea. sometimes the milk tea is empty and you have to bug the workers to refill it. nice location and the restaurant kind of livened up that area otherwise known as weird hotel in middle of durant. 

it's probably not the most authentic indian food around but it's close, cheap, and yummy.

This place truly deserves a 0 star rating. The food is terrible, the customer service is pathetic and the restaurant seems extremely dirty. 

I have been to this restaurant twice and both times have left unsatisfied. Initially, I thought it was just one bad experience and I should give this place another chance. Unfortunately, I was wrong. The food was completely tasteless - case in point, the chicken jalfrezi tastes like chicken dipped in salt water, and looks regurgitated. 
They don't seem to have the slightest idea about what Pakistani/Indian food is - case in point, the chicken biryani had huge slices of partially cooked tomatoes and green chillies, and tasted like boiled rice with salt.
The presentation of the food is completely unappetizing and the quantity is minute compared to the other Pakistan/Indian restaurants in Berkeley (that's a blessing in disguise!)

I would not even recommend this to my worst enemy.  Yelpers, be warned!

Confession: I've never really liked Indian food... until I came to Berkeley! Seriously, chicken tikka masala has to be THE most delicious dish in the history of dishes. I'm pretty darn obsessed.

As for House of Curries, this place is "okay". Personally, I prefer Flavors of India on Bancroft because their dishes come with rice (an essential for chicken tikka masala!).

House of Curries is pretty conveniently located though- it's right across from Asian Ghetto, but as far as overall Indian food goes, the quality is about average. The tea they served was a little too watery, the chicken tikka masala was too spicy (and not creamy enonugh!), and the garlic naan was all right.

Nonetheless, there are so many Indian restaurants in Berkeley, that you shouldn't limit yourself to one- try them all!

I have yet to have a better Paneer Tikka Masala! The samosas here aren't as good as Naan N Curry, but they are still worth ordering.

They also open until midnight, so it is sometimes a good idea to stop by after bears lair! But... just be careful the next morning = )

Second time I've been here, first time I ordered to go. This time, I took my parents to "try something new" ^^ It was Game Day so it took a while to get our food, but when we did it was delicious and they thought so too! +1 for good daughter points!

I ordered for us four servings of naan (garlic, onion, 2 regular), Chicken Curry, Chicken Tiki Masala, and a vegetable plate that I forgot (cauliflower + potatoes?) In the end, I still like the regular naan and the Chicken Tiki Masala the best. For three people, this was more than enough, I still brought home a bit of leftover naan.

Anyway, I haven't had much experience with Indian food, but this place makes me want to have more! I really want to try the lamb dishes or the prawns next time yay.
Place isn't bad. Would call it a college-student staple. Chicken tikki masala is good, lamb vindaloo as well...but hey, can't beat the price and the location.

Though not the best indian food ever, its super reliable, fast, and cheap. Definitely 100x better than Naan n' Curry. The food is always tasty - I've never had something I didn't like.  Occasionally they have cool specials like squash curry - mmmmm.  Also, free chai tea! The servers are always friendly as well.
This is the nastiest chicken tikka Masala I've ever had yuck! Even the garlic na'an was nasty and how you mess up bread I don't even know! But the one star is for the tea that was delicious.

My friends are probably reading this review with a shocked expression. I love house of curries, and continually boast about it all the time. I'm even in the facebook group, "House of Curries kicks Naan'N'Curries' Ass!" So why the four stars?

One star is for the fact they're cheap. Paneer tikka masala (enough for two), debuts at 5.99, last time I checked. They've raised the price of naan, but it's still a ginormous circle that will fill you up for just a dollar sum'n. You could take a date here, go dutch, and leave with 5 dollars out. YES PLEASE.

Now, moving on to star two, cheap is not always good (though always preferable). This place has amazing food. Absolutely delicious. The Paneer tikka is my crack, though their Daal is also good. Sometimes the naan is warmer than others, but it's still pretty solid food.

The location is also great. It's close to campus, it's got a nice deck for good days, it's spacious (though sometimes a bit noisy), and for christ's sake they have a crystal pirate ship chandelier. Heck Yes!

The owners are also pretty friendly. The owner of said location calls me "Zoff" (he can't pronounce my real name, that just makes it cooler!) and has given me free naan and dishes! before. Testifies to how often I come here! (and why i'm constantly in debt!)

But listen, guys. I wouldn't be real with you if I didn't kvetch a little -- hey, no one's perfect! It's sometimes a toss-up between creamy tikka and feeling gross sometimes afterwords (the infamous "delhi belly"). Unlike other indian places, House of Curries puts milk in the free chai  tea beforehand (annoying for vegans). 

But it's free chai. it's cheap food. it's good service. Some gripes, but "Zoff's" a fan.

Mmmmmmmm. Chicken tikka masala. They do it good here. Good I say. The chicken was "eh", but the sauce was where it was at. A must get whenever I visit here.
