Their chai is kinda watery, but what do you expect with free chai? At least you can add as much sugar as you want to it. Enough to give you the jitters while dipping your naan in your tikka masala sauce oh my god i'm so hungry right now.

Haven't tried the location on College Ave, but its on my list. Another time perhaps.

amazing curries.

wonderful chai.

tandoori is legit.

more people need to enjoy the samosas.

but try vik's.

I come here all the time, one of my favorite places in Berkeley.  It's not a fancy place, but you get your food fast and I've never had a problem with not getting a table.

I've had pollack paneer, tikka masala and lamb curry here and it's ALL delicious.  The naan is hot and fluffy.  And of course, all the chai you want, and they're pretty good at refilling it when it runs out.  I have to say though that the chicken in the tikka masal is rather dry, but the sauce makes up for it.

It's a little more expensive than Naan N Curry but well worth the price and you get a lot.  I usually split one curry with a friend.

I'm full. And pleased with what's inside me. (Yes, that's what she said)

I can't believe I walked past this place so many times without trying it! Met a friend here for dinner. Yes, the beverage area is a tad sketchy, but it's a nice place for a meal and conversation (if you find a non-wobbly table).

They have some interesting tea that comes with the meal. Try it! It's good.

2 things that set House of Curries apart:

1. Ample indoor and outdoor seating, yet you order at the counter, so you don't have to pay a tip!

2. It's raised above street level, but not quite on a second story. It looks like you're dining in a more expensive place, but you're paying the same as any other indian place (hah).

I had the Chana Masala, which is garbanzo beans in a really yummy sauce. It was tasty by itself, and killer with naan. And I'm even happier now that I looked up the nutritional value of garbanzo beans: http://www.whfoods.com/genpage.php?tname=foodspice&dbid=58 Apparently they're really good for you!

My friend recommends the Chicken Tikka Masala, because it's his usual, but he warns that sometimes they chince out on the chicken.

Even the guy at the counter was really friendly! I was fully satisfied by all aspects of my experience here, and I think it deserves a higher average rating than 3.5.

(Addendum after I saw someone's review complaining about the music: I love the music!!! It sounds like indian techo/dance music or something. I wanna know where I can find some of that music.)

Richard P, I had to write about this place as soon as I saw your review so I could urge you to try ANY other Pakindian near the Berkeley campus.  House of Curries is guilty of everything you say they aren't guilty of; it's precisely Indian for white people.
Since they opened I've tried them maybe once per semester, each time hoping they'd get better, but they haven't.  I won't actually say they're bad because they don't deserve so harsh a word.  It's just... there's a certain magic to good Indian food that House of Curries doesn't understand, or perhaps shies away from.  You know?  The food does its job on me, but it doesn't give me a hard-on.  And good Pakindian should.
Granted, HOC is cheap and convient (particularly for Berkeley students), but so are a fair handful of places where there is indeed magic to be found.  My very favorite thing about Berkeley is that I can make it through any lecture by dreaming about what I'll eat when it's over.  And House of Curries just isn't on my dream list.

I came here today with a Munch on Me special ($3.75 for Chicken Tikka Masala).  Great deal!

The restaurant is in an interesting setting (converted house), casual decor, plenty of tables inside and on the patio, and centrally located in the campus area of UC Berkeley. There were a lot of flies buzzing around but fortunately none of them tried to land on my food. The guy at the counter was very friendly and even gave me free naan since I only had a credit card (they take credit cards, but apparently he didn't want to bother with charging me $1.50 for just the naan and just told me to pay another time). 

They offer free chai tea with a meal (serve yourself). The chicken tikka masala had plenty of large chunks of chicken and a wonderful sauce to soak up with naan. It wasn't very spicy so next time I will make sure to ask them to spice it up! 

Seems to be a very popular place, judging on the number of people eating there. I'll be back!

In brief:
- Hands down, 100%, 5 stars, no question about it - this has the BEST indian food in the bay area. Nay, in the world (except, most likely, India). 
- I may not be that exotic in my choices, but I've tried a variety of their dishes. Every single one is full of flavor, heat and spice. The winner, though, is their Chicken Tikka Masala. 
- The Durant location is randomly placed at the front of a hotel, but don't be dissuaded from going in - you will not be disappointed! Go in and order at the counter, grab some utensils, plates and water and you're good to go. 

In depth:

- I went to House of Curries several times a week through most of college and never ever ever got tired of it. The service is personable and quick, their selection is diverse and the food is just absolutely perfect. 

- I usually get Chicken Tikka Masala because it's just too good not to. I know it's a bit boring, but their chicken is flavored to a T and the masala sauce has a slight kick that just makes my mouth water. I seriously have never had a better dish than this anywhere in the U.S.

- The people behind the counter are all very sweet and patient. They even remembered me after 2 years of being out of college - I'm telling you they are fantastic people. 

- Overall, I am giving House of Curries my highest recommendation of 5 stars. I would travel across the country to get my hands on their food. In fact, I have.

cheap, delicious indian FOOD!

I usually order one dish and one naan, and share it with another person if i am not super hungry. 

I really like the chicken tikka masala here. I guess if they threw in a couple more pieces of chicken, it would be 5 plus; but then again, it wouldn't be at that fair price.

YUMMY!!!

lamb vindaloo, spinach paneer, chicken tikka masala are all delicious here! and the indian family next to us ordered the same things as us so we felt like we must have ordered the right things, altho you probably can't go wrong with anything here. same with the naan - garlic, onion, regular. all good. altho i can't really taste the differentiate the three, maybe because i keep dipping it in my curry so the flavors get all entangled. 

warning: the lamb vindaloo is not for the faint at heart. it is SPICY and even my friend who claims he has a large tolerance for spice had a hard time finishing his portion.

Although I've mentioned House of Curries in my reviews of other Indian places, I just realized that I've never actually written a review of House of Curries... So here it is!

House of Curries is my favorite Indian place in Berkeley. I've tried a variety of things on their menu and haven't been disappointed yet. My favorite, though, has got to be either the Chicken Tikka Masala or the Veggie Korma with their Naan or plain rice. I also really like their mango lassi and even their complimentary tea.

Although there are other Indian places within the proximity, this is the one I always recommend to people. The food is great, there is good service, and the atmosphere really makes it a great place to eat.

I discovered this place with my boyfriend. We were in Berkeley on an errand, and I was craving Indian food. I ordered takeout from here when I moved. 

What I've tried so far:
+chicken tikka masala - yes, I know it's not authentic Indian fare, but it sure as hell is tasty! Their chicken is a bit dry, but the sauce is so good that I don't really mind it so much.
+veggie samosas - yum! Stuffed with a perfect blend of potatoes, spinach, and spices. Plus, they're a pretty good size, and they don'd scrimp on the filling.
+Aloo naan - So yummy, great for mopping up the tikka masala sauce!
+Garlic naan - I love garlic naan, but I wasn't impressed by theirs. This is the only thing I've tried here so far that I've been disappointed in.

I really need to try some new dishes here, but I love the chicken tikka far too much!

Hungry after long hours at work, we realized that our chances of meeting the following requirements were unlikely:

-Open late Monday night
-Not expensive
-Not too divey
-Within walking distance of downtown Berkeley
-Flavorful

Thankfully, House of Curries was there to save the day (err late night) with some great Lamb Vindaloo ($7.99) and Ghobi Chicken (6.99). All of our requirements and then some were met. Hungry, grumpy, pessimistic Nick H. was converted to stokedness.

Pluses:
- Nice and attentive staff who genuinely smiled and laughed it off when Mari C. dumped about 5 gallons of Cha on the floor.
- Significantly fresher tasting than its nearby competitor Naan n' Curry.

Fundraiser for Ecuadorian children here TODAY (Thursday 6/17). Bring a flyer.

Also I still love the paneer tikka masala. I don't know what they do here that's different but their paneer here is one of the best!

The food is cheap and tasty, the naan is massive and it is close to Zellerbach, campus, and Telegraph for all of your dessert and shopping needs.  Though if you are looking for cloth napkins, table service and a laid back place to chill, than I would pass on House of curries, this is a serve your self type of place.  That side, they have a killer patio and a lot room for groups.

** I am a native of India who has eaten at every single Indian restaurant in Berkeley at least 3 times each, read the bottom of the review for my complete ranking list or look in my Yelp Lists ** 

** Begin Snobbery ** 

For higher rated restaurants, my reviews are very thorough with lots of explanation. For inferior Indian offerings such as this place, I don't bother with elaboration. 

** End Snobbery **

Oh dear, the humanity!

This is why Yelp needs to implement a 0-star option.

-- Entree Taste: 1/5

-- Naan: 1/5 

Is this Naan or a cracker?

-- Price/Value: 2/5

-- Service: 1/5 

Dirty forks / spoons not washed properly, put back to be reused. Complaining results in grins and shrugs from the employees. 


*********** RANKING LIST ****************************** **************

-- I will keep updating this ranking list as I get time --

1) Flavors of India / Kabab and Karahi (tie)
2) Himalaya
3) Punjabi By Nature
4) Chaat Cafe
5) Priya
6) Viks (yeah, I know I'm going to get a lot of flak for this one, but it's true folks, severely overrated due to bandwagoning)

7) Breads of India (OK, but overpriced)
8) Biryani House
8) Khana Peena (the one on Solano, a little better than the other one)
9) Pasand (OK, but severely overpriced)
10) House of Curries (College)
11)  Kabana (Great food loses massive points for racially based treatment of customers)
12) Tandoor Kitchen
13) Khana Peena (the one on Shattuck, absolute trash, avoid) 
14) Indus Valley Restaurant (literally serves frozen vegetable curries)

**Now if I called Khana Peena Shattuck trash, then you can imagine how the following are...yeah...these don't deserve to even be ranked**

House of Curries (Durant)
Naan N Curry

A few friends and I can here last night for some post-meeting food. Indian food is known to be pretty spicy, right? Right. Since I'm a spicy-food addict, I ordered my chicken vindaloo extra spicy. It came and I anxiously scooped up some sauce with my naan. Mmmm...the delicious spicy taste of Indian spices...is what I expected. But my dish was just slightly spicy with a much stronger tint of sour. Sour? Yes, I said sour. House of Curries used to have pretty good chicken vindaloo, I don't know why/when they began making it taste sour. This wasn't the first time either, I went with a couple buddies last summer, and it was the same taste (which at the time, I thought was just a fluke). The short drive to Vik's on 4th Street or Chaat Cafe on MLK/University is worth it for better quality and tasting Indian food.

Anyway, the vindaloo+naan came out to $9.33 after tax, which is about 50 cents more than Biryani House. House of Curries also uses white meat, compared to Biryani House's dark meat. I'm a dark meat person. I'm also a person who likes my Indian food spicy...not sour.

No thanks to House of Curries, I'm sticking with Biryani House!

This homey establishment is located directly across the street from the infamous Asian Ghetto. Went here for dinner and I have to say the dishes were pretty solid and moderately priced. 

This thing that sets this place apart for me was the FREE Milk Tea. Thats right, all you can drink milk tea with your meal. WIN.

When you're in a hurry for cheap curry, there's two options this side of town and after today's meal, I'll conclude they're equally as awful. Were it not for the palate-dead majority of Cal kids, this place wouldn't earn cent except from the obliterated and/or desperate. On the plus side, this bite and bounce joint has a great patio with a view of scenic Durant. The staff's pretty chipper and helpful, the naan is a perfect circle and the chai won't make you any poorer. 

But that's where the party stops. Sure, it comes out quickly, though what does that say about the freshness and quality? The paneer is firm and bland, and palak literally look like what comes out of Popeye's can. It leaves a distinct aftertaste too. The tikka masala is basic cream and tomato sauce, lacking any trace of spice kick. And despite basmati having 40% more olfactory goodness than other rice, it's bland an unaromatic. The saving grace is the garlic naan. 

Curry on out of here, quick!

Four stars for all-you-can-drink Indian chai tea! I could sit here for hours drinking mug after mug of this stuff.

Food-wise though, I love their delicious garlic naan. It's fluffy and warm on the inside and crispy on the outside, perfect for scooping up bites of mushroom masala.

I make my friend take me here whenever I drove up to visit. Must find an excuse to come back soon!

This might be a biased review because in my mind, I keep comparing it to the appalling Naan N Curry.

I had the Chicken Tandoori and loved it.  A breast for just $4.99 = awesome.  It was just spicy enough for a little "tssss" when I was finished.  I couldn't suck the bones clean though because there was a little part that was bloody.  Not today, Salmonella. 

Tried some Chicken Vindaloo and was satisfied.  

Bummed I didn't know about the free chai before hand.  But you can be sure I'll be all up on that next time.

I have House of Curries on my cell speed dial. The only other people/entities that premier on this very VIP list are my mother and BearWalk. From campus I have to walk down the entire length of the main Telegraph riff raff to get to my hood, so the prospect of making a pit stop at House of Curries always makes the bum insults more bearable. 

My usual is paneer tikka masala paired with an onion naan, always leaving me beyond satisfied. I have been too faithful to this combo, but my experiences with  the other vegetarian dishes have been at least 3-star quality. I've heard the less frequently ordered dishes by gringos and college students, such as the salmon curry and lamb dishes, are pretty good, too. I'm really critical about naan, but the naan from HOC are pizza-sized and just the right thickness (could be a bit thicker, perhaps), perfect for generously swiping curry or tikka into its well-seasoned folds and into your mouth.

Some asides: 

The self-serve chai is a nice touch. The guy at the front desk (who has come to recognize my voice via cell) unfailingly encourages you to take a cup, even if you're just waiting for takeout. 

The takeout containers are plastic, most convenient, but if you get takeout here often you might eventually start your own HOC containers collection. Unless things have changed since I last digressed to Naan'N'Curries, "over there" they use paper-based Chinese takeout cartons which don't cut it with tikka massala. You just end up with a mess inside of your plastic takeout bag. Which usually has a hole.

So, do the right thing and go to HOC. On moral grounds, if anything.

J: "That guy with his high school son at the next table keeps looking over at us. I think we're being too loud and inappropriate."
D and A: *takes pictures of themselves making funny faces in my camera*
Me: "Do you think it was the breakup talk, the random sexual encounter talk, or the drinking talk?"
D: "Probably all of them."

It's not amazing, but jesus guys it's not bad. It's more aestetically pleasing than naan and curry, and the food is slightly better quality. It's not great indian food, but it's cheap and fills the spot. I love their spinach and lentils and the homemade cheese they have here. 

So I went in last night with some friends from out of town. We got a table on the patio, some free tea, lots of garlic naan, and had slightly too loud and very inappropriate conversation. It was us being in college and enjoying our immaturity while still possible.

The tiki masala is okay. Their mango chutney is bomb and I am a fan of all their vegetarian dishes (I do eat meat, yet I feel they often overcook it here). Everything is well spiced, rice is never burned, and the naan is good.

I've  had better indian food, but when you want something cheap and convenient, this is the place to go.

And in the middle of the meal as man and son are leaving:

Man: "Excuse me, what year are you girls"
J: "Third year students."
Man: "Okay..." *walks off*
Me: "Oh god, he was probably thinking that's what his son will be like in three years."
A: "Actually he was probably thinking 'Oh god, my son will be dating a girl like that in 3 years'."

Great memories, good food, hilarious incidents.

Okay, due to time management issues, I'm going to try for shorter reviews. Is that even possible for me!?! I dunno, we'll see =3=

I've visited this house at least 5 times, one for a Hep B Project fundraiser (HEP B AWARENESS YEEAAAHH), and all other times with some sort of voucher. No shame!

But amidst my frequent visits, these are my true feelings.

House of Curries: you burn my naan, you make my chicken tikka masala oily and clumpy, your chicken is dry, and you provide me with wobbly tables. Why do I keep coming back? Oh right--because you keep doing MunchOnMe and CampusCred deals. Arggghhh my kryptonite.

The service is fast, and food is out in 5 minutes. There is complimentary chai tea to the left of the cashier. And there are at least 15 tables, inside and outside, to sit and chill. And enjoy their wobbly tables.

|| C L O S U R E ||

Dun come here. Go over thar.

If I were to rank the Indian places I've eaten at, it'd go:
1) Currylicious (in Oakland)
2) Indian Flavors Express
3) Mount Everest Restaurant
4) Shalimar
5) Naan N' Curry
6) House of Curries

Attached to a hotel, House of Curries occupies the front part.  Cheap, delicious food is what is offered here.  Let me just tell you that the Chicken Vindaloo is spiiiicy. (I am a spice weenie.). Let's just say that a drip of sweat was streaming down the side of my head.  Tandoori chicken, naan, and samosas were all solid.  Plus, free chai is always a plus.  Water pitchers are located in the soda fridge.  Help yourself.

Six bucks for a steaming plate of chicken tikka masala curry and three bucks for a fat slice of garlic naan...enough to satisfy two hungry girls! Delicious and ideal for poor, starving college students. They also have this non-sweetened milk tea (the boba kind) for free on the side. The only downsides are that the curry doesn't have any veggies in it and that the chicken is a tad on the dry side. Granted, it's ridiculously cheap, but still, it'd be nice to have some colorful veggies to keep the ever so slightly dry chicken company.

You don't go to Naan N Curry or House of Curries for spectacular Indian food - you go because it's cheap, fast, convenient, or open 24 hours for those late night tikka masala cravings. That said, I have to admit that I have a soft spot for the House of Curries on Durant. Before H.O.C. opened here a year ago, this was a mediocre pasta restaurant that eventually closed down because having two mediocre restaurants right across from each other is redundant. Gypsy's thus ended up being the "favorite" mediocre pasta joint amongst the college masses.

Which begs the analogous question: why H.O.C. over Naan N Curry? They have the same menu, the same deliciously free (or freely delicious) chai, even the same ceramic cups and orange-juice jugs of water. For one, the H.O.C. on Durant is much cleaner and aesthetically appealing than the Naan N Curry on Telegraph, with decor on the walls and Indian music playing. But the real reason why I love this branch so much is the service - the guy who takes your order, presumably the owner, is unfailingly friendly. He greets you, acknowledges if you're a usual customer, and asks if the food was to your liking.  Considering that they get so many kids coming through here for lunch and dinner everyday, that kind of courtesy is practically unheard of.

Food - 3 stars. Service bumps it up to "Yay! I'm a fan" 4 stars.

I'm so happy to have found good Indian food in the neighborhood. The vindaloo is HOT HOT HOT spicy. Love it! The chicken tikka massala is so creamy I can feel my love handles growing as I eat. And the naan is really soft and smooth. I know it's just bread, but somehow it's so much better than bread.

It's one of those places you order at the counter and they bring you the food. The atmosphere is quite informal, but clean and friendly (unlike nearby Naan 'n Curry).

This is a really great place for Indian food.  They have the water on the side and CHAI!!! I love Chai and it is right there and readily available for all.  Food is excellent, trust me.

Problems: bring down the prices just a little bit, please!

My sister will be going to Cal this fall and we were here to see her counselors so before her appointments we thought lunch was in order. So many choices around telegraph its hard to choose. But I'm a fan of HOC on College, she's never tried Indian food so we figured its time for her to expanded her horizons. She tends to be  "particular" about what she eats so I was a bit worried, but we ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and Naan. Got some rice too and for me some Aloo Gobi. She seem to like the Tikka masala and dipping the Naan so for an introduction it seemed a success. I hope once moving to Berkeley she'll be more adventurous or at least head over to House of Curries now that we've been there. The price is right and they give you plenty for your money. This location has a nice deck to sit outside on a warm day, which was very enjoyable and relaxing.

Will I come back to this location? Well only to have lunch with her, because I still like the College Ave. the best. But if she calls me up and says "lets meet and get Indian food" that's close to the dorm, so yeah I'd go back to this location again.

It's always a satisfying experience here, but nothing gourmet, which is somewhat expected as it's located a block away from campus and is constantly filled with rowdy college students.

I like the vegetarian dishes here the most and though I personally do not favor the chicken masala that much, most people I know recommend that. Do get the garlic naan though.

+complimentary chai

went there with my husband and kids .I got the lamb and beef plate,my husband got the falafel and the kids got beef gyro and chicken gyros.
To start with i loved the cleansiness of the place since its really small and crammed between a bunch of  other food places ,it was really clean ,small but clean.
Preparing our order didn't take more than 5 min.
my platter was huuuuuuge big portion of meat which i loved the most and the salad was so fresh yet lacked some seasoning but still loved it .The hummus dip was great too and i loved the lavash bread waaaaaaaay better than pita bread you get at mediterranean resturants.
i got a bite from the kids gyros didn't like the chicken one but the beef was great the kids really loved it and finished the whole thing and i really didn't expect them to do so since the gyro was so big.
The falafel? oh wow  that another whole story. Now i'm from the middle eastern origin and i really know my falafel and which is good and which ones are not.  these falafel tasted the closest you can ever find here in the states to the real deal falafel in egypt. absolutely,amazingly reeealll good.
i'm definitely  going again for the falafel

Not sure what all these negative reviews are all about? Sure, it's not the cheapest place in the world, but the food is great! I had an Adana (lamb) Kebab - nice, seasoned lamb with rice, salad, and pita with hummus - for $10. Didn't take too long either. I'll definitely stop by next time I'm near Cal.

The food is somewhat bland. Also, it's slightly more expensive than D'Yar around the corner, doesn't have a soda fountain, and has an $8.00 minimum charge on credit cards (although they rang up my $7.90 tab on a credit card with no complaint).

The lamb gyro was good, a bit on the pricey side though. Somewhat salty but I'm not too familiar with Greek so I'm not sure if that's normal. It had some delicious sauce and fresh veggies: tomato, cucumbers, onions and lettuce. 

The other time I was here, I got the lamb plate. I don't recommend that. The meat was too rough, I couldn't chew it. I think I'll stick to DYAR instead for that plate. All the times I've been there, no one else is there so its good because the service is faster.

Ok i usually never write reviews but this was a must. I came here in the afternoon a couple days ago and I was amazed with what I got. I ordered a lamb and beef gyros sandwich. The meat was delicious and it was stuffed with fresh veggies. I payed around $8 for the sandwich and a drink, not bad at all for the size of the sandwich! Not to mention, the owners are very friendly and the restaurant was super clean. It seemed like they were always cleaning.. I would definitely come back here again!

The place is a tad too expensive for the meal but their baclava is the greatest thing I've had. 4 stars for the best baclava I've had. If they reduce their prices a bit, this would be a really nice place to eat.
I just had a lamb gyro and man was that good. it's kind of a hole in the wall place like all the restaurants here but I really recommend it.  it was just under $8.

Cheap food and fast service, can't get any better than that. I would appreciate if they had more "diversity" on the menu. I believe me, and most other customers, would come purchase their food more often if they offered more different meals.

Came here late one night because we had just left Kip's, and it was nearly 2am...so there were not a lot of options for us to get a warm meal. We stumbled upon Cal Gyros, just glad to see that they were open. However, we didn't know that the place was cash only, which probably started us off on the wrong foot with the owner. We ordered a chicken gyro, which came out looking nothing like a chicken gyro! More like a small watered down burrito, it was so bland! Perhaps I just have a higher standard for gyros, because the first chicken gyro I ever had was in Greece and it was REALLY awesome...but this "gyro" was at the very bottom of that spectrum.

Bottom line, the service was rude, the place feels dirty, the food is shabby...probably not going to be back here again, unless its 2am and they're the only place open.
I haven't had much experience with Middle Eastern/Mediterranean food, but I thought this place was fine. The owner seemed quite friendly, which is always a plus.

Definitely not the best gyro I've had and I like to try a lot of these places. Their portion was very small and I didn't really like their choice of veggies or sauce. I would also say it's a bit expensive for the quality and size ($7) Although, the owners were very polite and nice even during their late hours.

Pros:
Owner is nice, service was fast, open late!

Cons:
Expensive for what you get.  The flavor was just off for me on the beef and lamb gyro wrap, but I know others who like the taste.  The meat is cut pretty thin, which is probably a disservice to the owners because it makes the wrap look smaller.

Not really sure how this place stays in business to be honest.  There's better tasting and cheaper Mediterranean restaurants, but sometimes it's late at night and you feel like giving the owner some business.

Lamb plate-10 dollars, got it recently and was really disappointed. The meat she shaved off was very tough and should have been discarded. The person who got served after me got the really good juicy meat.  I've seen other places toss the meat away when it is obviously old.  There was a lot of rice and it was a bit hard and tasted dry.  The cucumber tomato salad was actually the best thing and unfortunately the smallest portion.  Like another person who reviewed the place, I also thought it looked like a lot of meat, but it's arranged so you only see the meat, then later you see it's a thin layer. The slices were thin and kind of sandpapery in texture  I guess they don't care if people don't return, I'm certainly not!!!!

The owner is a really nice guy but the gyro I had was not a "Greek' gyro  No pita or tzatziki sauce, despite the pictures showing otherwise.  The meat itself was greasy, greasy, greasy. Maybe if I hadn't tried the lamb/beef it would have been better but I think I'll just stick to other places for gyros.
I used to go this place more often when I was a student at Cal. They have all varieties of gyros and kebobs both wrapped and on plate. I prefer their plates with yoghurt sauce on the side.

Find this "hole-in-the-wall and you will be rewarded with a Gyro that actually has all-fresh ingredients as well as the most authentic tasting (LOT'S of fresh roasted LAMB with garlic and spices!) wrapped with a beautiful Lavash rather than a "doughie" pita that drowns out the flavor. 

I'm from NY (big deal, I know!) and I've had the best that the NY greeks in Astoria and Brooklyn have to offer and this place rivals them, right down to the kalamata olives in oil!

After the bar closes....definitely come here.....the owner is a really nice guy....fast service..good tasting food...only negative is the $8 min purchase for ATM...I recommend the lamb/beef gyro..or the combo...be sure to get it mild or spicey....

I decided to try this place a while back. To be honest, I expected a lot better for what the owner raves about all the time, fresh ingredients, real meat, blah blah blah. When I got it, I didn't taste it any of those, cuz the gyo was just WAY TOO SALTY. I even had to buy a drink immediately after so I could actually eat it. I actually ended up throwing away 1/3 of it after I finished my drink, it was just too unbearable. His drinks were ridiculously pricy too, maybe that's his strategy of making a few extra dime. Definitely stick to the more well-known places around the area like sunrise deli or dyar if you want Mediterranean food

I got the lamb gyro plate. Around 10/11 bucks which is sort of expensive....

You're given a good amount of meat slices but they were way too salty and the salad even was bland. I had to buy a drink to wash down the saltiness. You're better off with another Mediterranean place down the street since there are a couple within the campus area

Sitting with my meal writing this review.. Wow, i really miss the guys that ran this place back in 2000-2002.. I've been coming back every so often and each time it's a new owner, new menu, higher prices and less amount of food.. Today is the first time i couldn't get what i've always ordered, a simple chicken plate (grilled chicken over rice topped w white sauce and sprinkles of something with a large* side of hummus and salad).. Today the only option is gyro or chicken kabob (over taxed=$12).. She handed me the sauce to top myself, no sprinkles :-(.. the flavor is still good but i think its time to let go of my dear memories and find a more consistent restaurant! Let the new Mediterranean chicken plate search begin!

Honestly, this place is a rip off. There are so many other places to go to for legit Mediterranean food. My chicken gyro (no other side dishes) was a woopin $8..like are you kidding me? I thought as a little extra service, they would add in extra tzatziki sauce in a small container, but nope, only a little bit of sauce inside the gyro. 
The gyro isn't even a gyro. They use tortilla as a substitution for pita bread..in a gyro?! The chicken is juicy I admit, but everything else was a hot mess. The gyro was more like a burrito than what it was supposed to be, which is very disappointing. I'm a person who loves Mediterranean food and I don't expect much (just good pita bread and tzatziki sauce) but this just didn't cut it. 

The service was okay. The ladies were fast with cooking the food, but with the amount of people there, it could've been better.

I've gotten a gyro from here once, and I honestly cannot complain at all. The owner is this amazingly friendly man who engaged in conversation with me for the entire 15 minutes that I was waiting for my food.

He was talking to my friend and I, and he handed me a plate of rice along with chicken, lamb & beef to try. He told us that he made his own hot sauce, and that hot sauce was SOO good!!! I had the falafel gyro and it was deeelicious. It was pretty big, so I had half for dinner and half for lunch the next day.

I would definitely come back here since they're open so late and that man is such a sweetheart!

IIRC, this place is where Meesha's used to be. Is there an Asian Ghetto rule that the same kind of restaurant needs to take over when one folds?

Anyway, I love me a tasty lavash wrap (Much prefered over pitas for me) so I was excited to see they made their gyro wraps with it here since Meesha's did their wraps in pita. 

I got the beef/lamb gyro in lavash. It looked good when first presented (maybe a little on the small side) and the eating started out OK too. Grilled lavash, cucumbers, tomatoes, shredded lettuce, tzatziki at the top . . . but then a bite later I got to the meat . . . and it was doing a nasty dance on my tongue. It tasted dry, burned, and weirdly plasticy. 

I was raised to always finish my food. You know people starving in Africa and all that, but two bites later I'd had enough and tossed the rest into the trash. It was the worst tasting meat I've eaten that I can remember.

Meesha's wasn't exactly gourmet, but they never invoked my gag reflex. Sunrise Deli is 2 blocks away and is great. Go there if you're in the area and  jonesing for a tasty wrap.

Top Dog. Ahhh yes. The best thing to grab after a long, late night of boozing. There is a solid variety of sausages, plenty of relish, sauerkraut, onions, mustards (love the hot mustard. It's mouth-burningly spicy!), and ketchup to add on top, and a gruff but sufficiently friendly staff. This was a regular late night spot for me in college.

I last came here with my brother and cousins after drinking at Thalassa on Shattuck this past Christmas Eve. Top Dog was actually open at 2 a.m. on Christmas morning. The guy working the grill was super cool and goddamn the bird dog I ate really hit the spot!

This used to be my favorite place to go to after a day of studying. There is a good variety of hot dogs to choose from and there is always a hot pot of sauerkraut. My favorite was the chicken apple. The place is pretty small so dont expect to stay there to eat, but it is definitely a great place to go to get a quick bite to eat!
The veggie wienie with spicy Russian mustard kicks some major ass!

I've actually made special trips from sacto with friends just to grab a top dog....

open late, bock wurst, surly dog servers, and politico cartoons all over the place. what more could you really ask from a hot dog spot....oh wait ...i do have a complaint... diet rite cola and rc?? are you serious...wtf is this the early 80's...??

bad soda aside...seriously this place rules my world.

i dono which ones i've gone to, but i've been to 2 of the 3 in berkeley. 

THE LINGUICA (in my opinion) SUCKS BALLS. i thought i would be adventurous and try somethin new ....... never again. 

stick with what you know here. LOL. and gatDAMN i love that russian mustard :D

How can a Cal Bear dislike Top Dog? It's a Berkeley establishment! 

ATMOSPHERE
It's a tiny place, to say the least. Expect to take your dog to go or eat outside on the curb. There's barely enough room to fit those who want to order a hot dog, let alone eat one!

The workers, especially the main guy, is very interesting. He doesn't like to chit-chat and he's not that friendly. He's actually pretty pushy but it makes sense since he's trying to get in as many orders as possible.

I love the eclectic decor inside this little joint-- it's very Berkeley. I recommend browsing the walls while you wait for your dog (that is, if the loud worker lets you stay inside...).

I never come here for a meal; I only come here for late night cravings.

FOOD
I've tried:
1) Calabrese (Italian)-pork, paprika, chili, fennel
2) Hot link (Louisiana style)- beef and 4 kinds of pepper
3) Lemon chicken
4) Chicken apple

They're all really, really good. The dogs are juicy and bursting with flavor. I like the bun as well because it's toasted/grilled and it's crispy. 

My favorite has to be the HOT LINK but damn, they don't lie when they say it's REALLY hot. My mouth always catches on fire when I eat a hot link. A good alternative is the calabrese if you want a dog with heat.

The CHICKEN APPLE is also one of my favorites whenever I'm not feeling anything spicy. 

There are a row of free condiments on the other side of the "restaurant," which include mustard, relish, sauerkraut, onions, and ketchup. I only get my dogs with ketchup, but then again I'm a simple girl when it comes to hot dogs.

The only reason why I'm giving this place 4 stars is because it's pretty pricy for a hot dog, considering Costco sells bigger hot dogs WITH a drink for $1.50. The portions are also pretty small; I'm never full after 1 hot dog.

BUT! Don't be fooled-- if you visit Berkeley, you MUST try Top Dog. It's like taking a bite into Berkeley's history.

i don't care what other people say... top dog is awesome. if you hate it, then you're obviously not awesome.

ps: don't forget to pour on the russian mustard ;)

pps: don't order "hot dog, please" you'll get booted. it's "top dog". get it straight.

Entrusted with the task of planning our company's annual summer BBQ, I called up top dog to see about having them do the catering for us.  EB was great to work with, and even went to look at the picnic site up in the Oakland hills to make sure there was enough access for them to get in there.  Elliott was our grillmaster, and he arrived promptly. set up quickly, and was exceptionally friendly to me and our guests.  We got 4 kinds of dogs and some yummy pasta salad, and everybody loved it.  One thing I loved that our guests would never know: they only charge you for the dogs you consume, so I didn't have to worry about paying for food for people who had RSVP'd but didn't show up, and we actually ended up spending less than what I'd expected.  The only reason they get 4 stars instead of 5 is because they ran out of pasta salad about an hour into their 90 minute serving time (I'm telling you, it was good!), but otherwise everything was perfect.  Thanks EB, Elliott, and Top Dog!

Should be called "Tasty Top Dog!!" Just thinking about it makes my mouth water... yummy.  Go now & enjoy.  Small joint, grilled to ordered, just a simple hot dog place with some deliciousness behind the counter.  Quick & friendly service.  Recommend the "Bird Dog" and they have RC Cola on  fountain too.
this is the place to eat after you've been drinking all night.

I'm usually not a big fan of hot dogs, but Top Dog is by far the best hot dog joint in the Bay Area.

I usually come here after late nights at Kips or the city. They have an array of condiments that will surely satisfy your hot dog needs. 

I highly recommend their hot link or linguica, paired with ketchup, Russian mustard (AMAZING!), and any other condiments.

A trip to Berkeley isn't complete without a top dog! My favorites are top dog, chicken apple, bratwurst, hot link, linguica... pretty much all of them! The express line before each Cal game is awesome. It seems really long but it actually moves very quickly. You will be able to enjoy a hot dog within 10 minutes.
For the best hot dog in the area, come here. They also sell 'uncooked' dogs, buns included, that you can grill yourself at home - which is great for parties.
Damn!  What can I say but it's always delicious even when I get a late night after dinner-dinner craving! Thank goodness for top dog!

What can I say, the hot dogs are flippin amazing. I hesitated whether to give 4 stars or 5, considering I've always been drunk when I go to Top Dog and I'm not sure whether I love the dogs because they're really that good or it's just the drunk munchies. But considering I make it a point to go to Top Dog whenever I go drinking on Shattuck, it's safe to say that they deserve a 5.

Besides the hot dogs themselves (which really are quite superior - I think) they deserve a 5 because of the sheer efficiency with which the place is run. To echo one of the reviewers below, you better know what you're ordering when you get to the counter, and you better not let your drunktard status get in the way of the cashier doing his business.

One memory stands out vividly in my mind because I will forever refer to it as the Soup Nazi experience I had at Top Dog. It was after a bar crawl, and my drunk ass had recently experienced Top Dog and had a craving to get a dog. So we trek it over and immerse ourselves in the clusterfuck that is crowding around. I am really impressed because there are only two guys working - the cashier who is taking orders in an almost ruthless manner while simultaneously handing out 10 dogs at once (and remembering each and every person's order correctly), and the cook who is grilling rows upon rows of dogs. I make the mistake of inadvertently trying to question the guy when I get up there. (Hey, I was drunk, ok?)

"Two chicken apple sausage and a kielbasa."
"Umm nooo I don't think that's what we ordered."
"Yes it is."
"No no, I didn't order a chicken apple sausage."
This exchange continues a few more rounds while cashier is getting visibly irritated.
(BF to me): "You did order a chicken apple sausage. Eat your damn hot dog."
Death look from cashier ensues. If he hadn't been busy taking and serving other orders I'm sure the cashier would have happily throttled me and tossed me out of Top Dog.

The moral of the story: don't bother getting to the counter if you don't know what you want. And never question the cashier. He's always right.

5 minute walk @ 2am when everything else is closed.
$3 - for an all beef 'TOP DOG'
free toppings: relish, ketchup, mustard, sauerkraut, etc.

complimentary crackhead outside the spot, spittin' a hot 16.. priceless.

This place has tasty food. I got the smoked chicken and apple sausage while my husband got the top dog (hot dog).The condiments on my sausage included warm sauerkraut and Russian mustard (beware this mustard is kind of spicy like Chinese hot mustard). It was so yummy. You can't beat it for $3 each. There are so many sausages that I want to try. All there sausages are $3 unless it's their daily special.  I have found a new cheap eats place for late night. :)

So many delicious memories, Top Dog never disappoints. The Durant location is def better. I know it's the same products, but maybe it's the grill? No idea, just go here.

The Hot Link is my personal fav, choc full of flavor until your tongue goes numb from the peppers. You might even tear up a bit, but that's just because it's so damn good. 

The German Frankfurter is also a sure bet, especially for garlic-lovers who want a more traditional dog. The Lemon Chicken and Smoked Chicken Apple are good options for a lighter fare, but I always find chicken hotdogs too mushy for my liking.

If you're vegan or a vegetarian, they'll make your order on a separate grill when requested!

One of the many reasons why I moved from NYC to Oakland!  This place is sublime at 2am.  Nights are judged as Top Dog nights or non-Top Dog nights.  

A Top Dog night is a night that lasts a lifetime... or at least till the next weekend.

Favorites: Hot or a bird w/ chili

Remember to be patient!
Great place to go for hot links. They are so spicy and the buns compliment them so well. Never a disappointment. I love the entertaining stuff on the walls, and the employees are kind. :)

Top Dog is really amusing. They totally have a socialist/anarchist thing going on. Their rule is that they have NO LINES. Very interesting. Every one just kind of piles into the tiny little shop. They have many varieties of sausages. I ordered the Linguica, which is a vinegar-cured pork sausage. I liked it, but I wasn't too crazy about the texture - it was a bit crumbly/chunky so it was pretty easy for bits of it to fall out when I was eating it. My sister had the Bockwurst (part pork and part veal); and my cousin had the garlic frankfurter. 

I think the best part of these hot dogs is the bread. Instead of the typical hot dog bun, they're actually served on french rolls. Genius. So much better. They also offer unlimited sauerkraut, onion, relish, ketchup, and mustard toppings that you serve yourself. Two kinds of mustard, by the way - deli and yellow - that's fancy. 

The one man show behind the counter was pretty awesome. He takes every one's orders and collects the money (cash only!) and cooks. He's super efficient and has really good memory about every one's orders. This establishment would be the opposite of Georgetown Cupcakes.

You can't say you've been to Berkeley until you've been to Top Dog.  

All of their dogs are tasty, so you really can't go wrong.  My recommendations are the smoked chicken apple and the calabrese.  Hot dogs are $3, served plain and made to order.  You can top your dog at the side of the store (at no extra cost) with ketchup, mustard, spicy mustard, sauerkraut, relish, onions, and more.

The service is abrasive, but I suppose necessary to move the lines along and get everyone served as quickly as possible.  There has always been a line whenever I come, but the line moves quickly (never waited more than 5 minutes to put my order in). At night, expect a great deal of drunk people.

Guy behind the counter points at me. "One brat please..." *pause*

"Actually make that 2!"

I walk away happy.

Oh, I miss Top Dog. And your crispy on the outside, soft and airy on the inside buns.
Great dogs, silly employees, and very very Berkeley.  Get one now!  What r' you waiting for?

The hot dogs are great, but nothing where I'd bite into it and go MMPPPPHHH!! sooooooo good, because at the end of the day, it's just a hot dog. That being said, I can't think of a place that has better hot dogs so this gets a 5.

the dogs are freakin awesome nigs. i be eatin three of em at one time naw what i am saying???? I had the polish, italian, and the chicken apple and they were all delicious. the guythere is very chill and easy going, he may be impatient at times but thats because so many people eat there and love their long, juicy, dogs.

For my money, this is the surest food recommendation I can give.  I'm from California, but my food experience tracks all the way to New York.  This is the standard by which I compare all wieners, and I have not found another that compares.  From the dogs to the buns to the condiments--solid!  My personal favorite is the hot link, which come the way they're supposed to: fat, hot, and spicy.   Serious quality, no bullshit, and bay area attitude.
This is FASHO the best grilled sausage spot on the west coast PERIOD. I always splurge with the lemon garlic, and calabrese on the sesame seed bun.. Take a hotlink home after. mmm mmm

Best hot dog in town.  If you are ever up at UC Berkeley this is the place for a hot dog.  There is a dog for every taste but for me it's all about the original top dog.  Loved it from the first bite!

seriously addictive.
the mango habanero... is spicy but soooooo tasty! it's become my new favorite. i also recently tried their apple juice and i am definitely coming back for more! It's the unfiltered thick kind, so its heavier than the regular Treetop apple juice you usually see around town.  The apple juice will be perfect to offset the spiciness of the habanero next time.  

Beware though... if you've been drinking and you're not feeling too fancy and need something to fill your stomach, i would NOT order the mango habanero. Let's just say...it does not taste as good coming up as it did going down..
Cal alumni in the house!! Needless to say I love this place. It's the best after a night out drinking. The chicken apple and the hot link are delicious!

I learned everything I know about different hot dogs and sausages here.  My roommate and I used to come every wednesday, order 4 dogs between the 2 of us, and go through the menu 4 or 5 times each semester for 2 years.  My favorites here are the brat, and chicken apple, but they have a menu of about a dozen different dogs.  If you're in the area, you have to try it (by it, I mean several).  Even the vegetarians, they have one for you.
Most amazing hot dogs I have ever tasted.

I don't get this whole thing of specialty hot dogs. Tastes pretty good.


Too expensive for its taste though.

Can't really remember much as I was hammered and la burrita was closed and came here. From the mustard stain on my jacket, I probably enjoyed it. Late night drunk's paradise! You will meet lots of other drunkies like yourself here as well
i really like this place. everything is good. the only complaint i have is the size of the hot dog and yes size does matter. i can eat 3 dogs no problem. the quality and flavors keeps me coming back.
haven't had a hotdog there i didn't like, one of my favorites when i was in school!

Its one of those "it hits the spot" places, especially late at night. $3 for a hot dog is a little much compared to my other favorite Costco, but its worthy of trying and returning for. Trust. 

I love their original top dog because the weiner is longer then the bun, and I'm not eating plain bread, but chicken apple is also really good. 

Another reason why I rave about this place is because of their bread. They toast their bread, which makes it even better!
Good, cheap, hits the spot. Reminds me a little of Annies Kiosk in Denmark. Yum! Fast pace in the door out. Russian mustard no joke. Italian was legit.

Dirty Place to eat.  I paid the cook with $ and he went over to cook the hot dogs w/o putting on sanitary gloves or wash his hands.  The hot dog was over cooked.  Bad experience.  The other Top Dog location on Center St. is clean.

Over the weekend, I stopped by Top Dog during a trip to the Bay Area.  This location is definitely my favorite - it's the classic way to enjoy a Top Dog on the streets before all the other locations started popping up.  And it's right across the street from the Asian Ghetto if you're still hungry.  

It's been about 8+ years since my last visit and the reunion with the hot link was awesome, and HOT.  What made it more amazing was that the price only went up $.25 after all these years!  Aside from their delicious dogs, their buns also get a piece of the attention with the toasted exterior, chewy inside and fragrant sesame seeds.  Best part is you can mail order these hotties if you don't live nearby!

walked in half drunk at 2 something in the morning. let the pros order. scarfed down half of the hot link and polish, struggled to save the other halves for my passed out friend in the car, but managed to resist the tempation and watched her eat the rest half-asleep. made me sad watching her. I went away with a mustard stained scarf and a satisfied smile. i'll come here again.

1. There is no line.

Don't wait in line late at night when you're starving hungry, skip the crowds of the uninformed and head straight for the counter.

Came here for late night and got the chicken apple sausage, seriously good especially at the time.  The Russian mustard is seriously spicy, unless you're into that be careful of how much you throw on your dog.

Great food and only $3 for a hot dog, definitely an awesome late-night spot for Berkeley.

i went to berkeley to visit a friend of mine :D she recommended this place
so here i am with my hot dog craving.. it was soooo gooddd... and the price was awesome! xD~ oh well.. no wonder it has lots of stars in yelp!
u shud go and try some hot dogs~ it was unique...

Oh Top Dog, how I miss your delicious delicious sausages. I swear everything on the menu at this place is bomb. You can't go wrong here. However I would recommend the bratwurst and the caprese, my two all time faves. Yum!

It's been YEARS since I've had a top dog.  I had chicken apple, and it was yummy.  Did they change the bread? It tasted different...maybe it needed to be toasted more.  Or perhaps I'm just more picky bc I'm no longer a poor Cal student thriving on boxed and canned food. I'm surprised the place is still of the same cleanliness it was almost 10 years ago.

Mmmmm Top Dog.  No trip to berkeley is complete without a quick jaunt  into top dog for a bird dog or lemon chicken.  Gotta love the faded propaganda and newspaper clippings that are *so* evidently Berkeley.  It's great going to Top Dog with newbies who don't know that they need to be able to recite their order - loudly - in 0.06 seconds before you're quickly passed over and won't have a chance to order until Guy Manning The Grill   With Tongs comes back around to you.

This place is definitely overrated for what it is.  Top Dog simply serves hot dogs, just like Pink's in LA...only they don't have as many meaty combinations, so you just leave feeling unsatisfied.  Then again, if you're me...you would probably need to eat like 3 of these to feel full.  Le sigh.  This place is definitely not for the light eater and the hot dogs are stinken pricey for what they are.  If you're really craving a hot dog, just go to Costco - for $1.50, you can get a quality dog, plus a drink!

The good: Great for late night munchies. I recommend the hot link, kielbasa, and the chicken apple. Condiments are ample, try the russian mustard if you dare.

The bad: Small and dirty store, nowhere to sit. Can get super ghetto at night. Expensive prices for sausages.

Overall: Although the ambiance and prices are less than desirable, the call of a hot link swimming in ketchup and mustard on a freezing Berkeley night keeps me coming back.

paid $3 including tax for a german hot dog.  i don't know which one i got.  i actually ordered both kinds but i gave one to my friend.  the buns are really good, different than regular buns

pretty good for $3, but not that big of a hot dog compared to costco
i've tried pinks.  i've tried gray's papaya.  BUT NOTHING COMPARES TO MY TOP DOG.  they know what a real hot dog is supposed to taste like.

The. Best. Hot. Dog. You. Will. Eat. EVER. 

My friend's cousin introduced me to this place. I got some kind of spicy hot link, and wow. It was SOOOOOOOOOO gooood. And I'm not even a hot dog kind of person. Too bad it's so far from where I live though. Big bummer :(

i am so excited that i am the first to rate the original TOP DOG! top features of top dog: 1. open til 2. that means if you leave the bar at last call, you will get there just in time for a gorgeous, big, juicy dog.  2. if, like me, you could use a little more fat on your bones, and want to do it on the cheap, you have come to the right place. 3. while youre waiting for your top dog, you can a. have your photo taken by itinerant photography students b. observe inebriated frat boys c. meditate on the "road to success" poster, even more inspiring whilst tipsy 4. stefania and i have considered moving into the city, but every time we go to look for apartments, we always come back to the same, sad fact: if we live in san francisco, we will be farther away from TOP DOG.
BASAS!  See you there!

A good place to eat for late night drunchies.

I've tried a few of the hot dogs but my favorite by far is the hot link with ketchup and onions. No sauerkraut or relish for me!

The bun is pretty good, as it is coated with sesame seeds and toasted before being stuffed with the sausage. I thought it was a bit expensive for a hot dog but a good late night snack.

I love top dog!! I haven't had it in 2 months! This is by far the longest because I moved out of state. I usually get the lemon chicken and the hotlink. Yes, I can eat 2! Sober or drunk. LOL. I looked it up online and they can ship it out and it's $100 minimum but geez what am I going to do with all that much hotdogs when I live by myself?! Lol. 

My point is, this is the best hotlinks I've ever had!! Haha.

Disappointed. Not the best hot dog in the known universe; probably not the best within a 2-block radius. A disappointingly sparse selection of toppings (No tomato?) will accompany a sausage that has been sitting on the grill so long that you'll have to spit out the unchewably tough skin.
The libertarian propaganda posted everywhere is entertaining though, and makes me want to meet the owner over a beer in a dive bar.

i love this place. I get the same thing every time i come here, which is a kielbasa with a little bit of mustard. The cooks are most times conversational, but other times are in such a rush that they push you in and out of that little hot dog stand once your food is ready. with a good amount of variety in the different kinds of dogs they have this little chain is definitely something to look into if you like sausages.

The best place for hotdogs and sausages around.  I went to a reunion for a Cal class, had the usual 'reunion catered' dinner, ate nothing, but went to TD for my 'dinner'.  Great hotdog.  Wish I had had two!  Bad for my BP because of the salt, but the best.

Where else can you get a top quality piece of sausage at 2am?

Everyone else has said it in these reviews, this is what a hot dog should taste like. Flavorful, juicy, and nothing beats the sizzle when the guy gets it ready. I miss their hot link, it's got a nice kick to it. 

This is a Berkeley institution.

Worlds.  Best.  Hot.  Dogs.  No -- there's no arguing or negotiating.  It's a fact.  In fact, so good that after a debacherous nite of Henrys (Anchor Steam for $3?), Top Dog, Steve's BBQ, Kips ($1.25 domestic pints... are you serious?), Fat Slice veggie pizza, King Pin donut holes... I had to get one more for the road.  My favorites are lemon chicken and apple chicken, although everything else on the menu is pretty good.  Def. use the sauerkraut.  And hot mustard.  And onions.  Ketchup.  You can't go wrong.

I ordered the top dog.  It was good, but tasted exactly like hot dogs I've eaten at baseball games - nothing special.

I like that they have a lot of options, and the service was impressive. My husband and I agreed that if we went to Berkeley, we would be making frequent visits to Top Dog.

I've grown up with Top Dog my entire life and I am so glad I have. The most amusing part of top dog are the people who work there. There are a couple dudes that work behind the counter and they all seem to have my mentality about the college students that populate that area. They are to the point and sometimes down right rude, but ya know what? I think its great. I appreciate their high stress cooking and I get why they would be annoyed all the time. The Spanish soap operas that seem to be always on are also hilarious. 

If you can fight your way through the overly privileged and usually hung over CAL kids to get yourself one of these dogs, I suggest you do it.

The dogs are so good. They are always cooked to perfection with snap and some tasty charred goodness. The condiments may seem a little scary but trust in top dog and put them on, or forgo them, should you be a purist.  The other thing I really like is that they still serve RC Cola, it brings back good memories for me. The only thing about this joint is the limited seating or lack there of, but fret not, the dogs are still good when you are on your feet.  Go bears!

This is Da shit... no doubt.

anytime i have a friend visiting the bay area, i take them here.
Berkeley has many great restaurants, but dear sweet God this one is good! All of their dogs are awesome and they are open late enough to get one on the way home from the bar.

I'm on a bit of a yelp tear as of late, so I wanted to throw in my two cents.  Top Dog is not just a hot dog, but it's the experience of Berkeley.  I used to be a Chicken Apple fan, but it's now clear that the Kiel is better by leaps and bounds.  Make sure you top it off with just a bit of russian mustard for that kick, and you will have a moment of clarity.

dropped by berkeley.  tried the polish sausage, topped with lots of condiments (mustard, onions, relish, sauerkraut) and it was pretty tasty.  the dogs are pre cooked and the heated on the griddle when you order - I asked for extra charred on the outside which I like.  the place itself is a tiny no so clean or inviting looking shack.  the price is a bit steep $3.

Top Dog is classic Berkeley!  As a matter of fact, there are three (count e'm THREE) locations around the perimeter of the campus.

The service hired is typically a group of badasses so they can handle the late-night drunk mob.  They're badasses in the daytime too; I once caught one of them chewing a customer out for having attended an Objectivist club meeting.  

The dogs are DEE-LISH.  I go through phases, although my all-time favorite is the CALABRESE.  The Chicken-Apple, Lemon-Chicken, and Kielbasa are all winners, as well.  Beware of the Hot Link, it is HOT!

The best part of Top Dog is its reliability.  It has the same hours no matter the weather of time of year.  When all other businesses close during the break, you can always count on Top Dog for a late-night snack.

It's a fast, cheap hot dog place with lots of variety. No, it's not the place for vegans, and yes, they don't wear gloves and they handle your money and food with the same hands. It's a fast, cheap hot dog place. Those who demand something else have a zillion other options within 2 blocks of here. =)

This place is good. It's small, its crowded at night, its open late.

I've set my stomach on their kielbasa and calabrese [kiel and a cal].  It's a tad pricey @ $3 a pop, but they're pretty big.  I believe each sausage weighs the same, which explains why the thicker, more spice-filled dogs are shorter than, say the original frankfurter - it's on a paper explaining the top dog sausage, at least @ the hearst one.  They have HEAPS of sauerkraut [good sauerkraut], onions, mustard, russian mustard [spicy], and ketchup.  All I really need is mustard and sauerkraut [maybe ketchup if I feel like it].

I would rate a 4.5 because its THAT good, but a 4 because $2.50 would be perfect.  It used to be 2.75 but they raised the price recently.

If you crave the dog at home, you can buy 6 buns and 6 cold dogs for $7.50 or if you're having a cookout you can have bulk packs for a super discount.  

I wish I could give it a 5, but man three bucks.  The older guy who works here is a bit cranky when it gets busy sometimes too.  The anarchistic paper clippings and articles on the walls are a bit of a humorous read too if the place isn't too busy.

I'm going to go out on a limb here and say I liked it better than pinks. [flame suit on]

Some people drink water, others eat bread.

On a night that I know I'm going to have a hangover I go to Top Dog.  Great way to end a great night.  Staff is awesome and the huge crowd moves quickly.  

Read the other reviews they all have great ideas of which dogs to eat.

This is the my all time fave hotdog place to get any type of dogs!!! from a regular hotdog to my personal favorite CHICKEN APPLE...my mouth jus waters thinking about it!!! I try to order 3 of my all time fave.  1 to eat before I get to the car, the 2nd one to eat for the ride home and the 3rd to eat when i get home...at times I order a 6 pack to cook at home....lol!! this great for after the clubs even if you're comin from frisco.  They are always open till 3am!!!

My Dad was a Berkeley resident back in it's heyday, so when he came to visit my in Rockridge last month, he had to come to Top Dog. Man those dogs are delicious. You can actually taste all the different spices that make them unique. Dad still loved it, I loved it, wallet loved it.
NOMMMERS. Twas a good Polish dog. I want to go back and try some more!

this place is a historic institution embedded in a college town.  

All their dogs are fantastic and extremely flavorful.  My favorites are the hot links and lemon chicken.  These dogs are terrific for curing the munchies and subtle drunkenness during the middle of the night.

Criminally simple. Delicious sausages to go, available late into the night at little cost. One of Berkeley's perfect drunken (or sober) late night foods, delivered expediently into your mouth in exchange for a few minutes' wait in line. The only downside I can conceive of is dealing with enormous hordes of UCB dorm-dwellers, but if you're either a student or a nearby resident, I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.

I've only had the pleasure of eating at the Telegraph area location, but I'm pretty sure the other one is identical, only with less hours. The sheer convenience and simple ingeniousness of the place combined with high quality meats cooked to order make Top Dog a good reason to live up here. If you have exceptional self-control.

Sometimes I have a hankering for a warm sausage wrapped in a bun and Top Dog satisfies my need! The hot link is nice and spicy and the chicken apple dog is tasty and a little sweet. Plus I love that it's open late!

There is no better hot dog place on earth. 

There, I'm on record...

Grilled dogs and grill-heated buns with your choice of condiments, read the word "choice"... Not like so many other establishments around the country that impose their taste on you with their subset of condiments. I need only Heinz ketchup, preferably the organic one, to make the experience. Nothing else is needed on these dogs. It's in the meat, 'stupid'! 

Anyway, that's how I see it!

PS: I've been coming here to enjoy these dogs since 1977. Yup, I've come back over the course of every decade since then and even driven here straight away from the airport with my bags in my rental. The experience is that fulfilling.

I came here with a hungry family of four who had just sat in a moving vehicle for 4+ hours. The lemon chicken dog certainly hit the spot. Not sure if I'd deem it the best hot dog I've ever had, but it was delicious. It was my first time in that part of Berkeley and the weather was cool and Bike Party was out making rounds  and I was sitting in a minivan eating the chicken apple with plenty of sauerkraut...sounds like a good meal to me.

After 4 years at Cal, I can honestly say I tried every dog on the menu. My favorite is still the Chicken Apple Sausage. Bottom line- their dogs are the BEST! Chicago and New York, you got NOTHIN on Top Dog!!!Thank you, Top Dog, for being open late night to satisfy my drunken munchies cravings!

Wow... this brings back memories! :-) The number of times "2 New Yorks and an RC" served as my lunch or dinner are too numerous to count! :-) The tasty dogs and toasted buns... yum!

Must remember to go by next time I'm up there. :-)

It always amazed me the ability of the cook to keep track of quite a few orders all in his/her head AND be keeping track of the dogs already cooking and paying customers.

If you want a good hot dog this is it! simple and tasty, plus the rolls they come on are nice and chewy. regular hot dog buns get mushy and fall apart, not these! I'd eat like 10 but then my jeans wouldn't fit.

Smoked chicken apple hot doggie on a warm day before the UCLA v. Cal game...yum! Line was long, but it moved fast. Friendly people in line always a plus. Some of my Berkeley friends don't like this place, thinking it's gross. Perhaps the dogs are pretty greasy, but they are just so tasty!

I'll probably only go back if every other place is full or if I'm extremely hungry. I just say this because I'm a bit of a foodie, but I'm definitely a fan.

As a former Berkeley student, I know that Top Dog is an institution of college life. I actually used to work upstairs from the Top Dog building and ate at Top Dog probably more that I should have. I've tried every single dog on the menu, and pretty much everything is good. (The veggie dog was meh, but I heard they use a different veggie dog now. Also, I'm not a vegetarian, so I have no idea what constitutes a good veggie dog.)

I've eaten all of them without condiments to taste the full flavor of the dogs, and yes, they have lots of flavor. My old staple used to be the Lemon Chicken and the Chicken Apple. The Hot Link is one of my favorites, and probably the most popular. The Calabrese is probably my favorite all time here. But trust me, whatever you're feeling, you can't go wrong here.

There are condiments galore here if that's your thing, with ketchup, different types of mustard, sauerkraut, etc.

For Cal football games, they'll have their most famous dogs, such as their Hot Links, already cooked and kept warm in a cooler. They also have cans of soda on ice. If you want to grab a quick bite to eat on the way up to Memorial Stadium, grab a Hot Link and a soda and go. Best gameday food ever.

Drunk food after a late night partying at Henry's or Blake's? Top Dog closes at 2am, but be sure to get there early before they stop taking orders. You don't wanna be waiting in line and get let down.

Want Top Dog at home, or want it for a BBQ or camping trip? You can buy cold dogs and buns to cook on your own. Delicious.

For soda, they serve RC Cola here. I love it. For sides, you can get a bag of chips, but me, I'd rather get another dog as a side. In fact, I almost always do. :)

There's other stuff I haven't tried here, like the fresh juice, chili, apple turnover, etc. One of these days, I will try them all to complete my sampling of the Top Dog menu.

I will also say that the folks that work there are all quirky, and watch strange things on the TV, but they're really cool and very nice. They can all handle tons of orders and they always get everything right. And the guy that I've heard is the owner looks like my old manager at work, who also lived in Berkeley for a while. I bet they've probably met face to face at some point, had a political discussion, and caused a rupture in the space-time continuum.

I highly recommend Top Dog! I need to get a Top Dog shirt one of these days.

Late night munchies? The dogs here will hit the spot. Beats going to the McDonald's or Jack in the box Drive-thru. 

I've been here randomly a couple times, and rain or shine, early or late- this place is always crowded. BUT, even with the crowd, the service is pretty fast. The owner can be a little intimidating, but as long as the foods good, I ain't complaining. 

I usually get the hot link or chicken apple, but recently tried their chicken mango jalepeno special. That one is a must try!

A must stop when I'm in the bay area. I always get a polish and a brat, or 2 polishs, or 2 brats. Try the russian mustard. It kicks my ass everytime. Nothing's cooler than trying to hold two of these with a coke and its 40 degrees, no where to sit, sauerkraut dripping allover your hands, while you eat on top of a trashcan or by the pay phone. Then i go buy donuts over at tiananmen square. You can even get dogs and buns to go. Even better.

YUMMMMMMMMMMMMM! it's a great spot for a quick eat for the CAL students and I bring all my out of towners here who love HOT DOGS and crave gray's papaya.  This is my version of gray's papaya.  I have yet to find something better.  Good stuff - tiny but still good stuff.  It's one of those get your food and move it along establishments.  nothing wrong with that.

As many of TD's patrons are, I am a Cal alum and continue to make an effort to eat here whenever I am in town for a football game.  Though I was not a drunk-off-my-ass-at-2am student Top Dog patron, I ate my share.   As an adult (marginally) I still go for Keils and Hots - and be forewarned they are really hot.
You know that scene in the great Japanese foodie Western movie "Tampopo", where the cowboy takes the pretty noodle lady to the noodle shop at commute hour and tells her to watch the cook take, remember and serve all the orders with perfect recall?  That's what the TD cooks are like - shout out the order, he takes your money, gets your drinks and sides, and calls out your dogs when their done - I've never seen them mess up.
TD Northside is not quite as great as TD Durant Ave, but it does have outdoor counter space and you can get beer from the mini-market next door

I've only had their chicken apple, and I love it. But it's kinda expensive, especially when I know I can get a polish sausage and a drink for $1.50 at Costco. And I end up not eating a lot of the bread at Top Dog because it's too much. But other than that, it is tasty.
Definitely on the list of things to do in Berkeley.  Tasty dogs,unexplainable.

There are 3 top dogs around the Berkeley Campus, and this top dog is the original one.  However, for some reason I think top dogs only taste great after midnight.  Opening till 3am, this place opens even later than the FOB square across the street.  

The hot dogs are good, especially the chicken apple sausage.  Although the Kielbasa and the Hot Link are decent too.  There was so many memories of late study night that we end up here just to take a break.  Despite it being overpriced (we can get costco ones for cheaper), it gave us a perfect excuse to have a study break.  

I did try eating here at lunch after college couple times though.  For some reason it loses its flavor.  Maybe is psychological, but one of these days I would drive back to Berkeley late at night just to relive the experience.
Lemon chicken - that is where it is at!

I don't care how full I am from a previous meal.. or if the place is kinda dingy.. I WILL COME TO TOP DOG!!!!!!!!!!!

My favorite has to be the lemon chicken. Mmmmm... a little mustard and onions go a long way!  So flavorful! ..it must be the years of grease on that grill that make them so tasty!!! ;)

What else can I say that hasn't been said? Best hot dog I've ever had. (Yes, I've had all the other big names - including the mushy mess of a Sonoran hot dog in Tucson and Grays Papaya in NYC). 

Top Dog wins with a quality bun, something that 99% of hot dog places overlook. Gimme two Tops and a Bird, with mustard!

If i ever want a sausage, it has to be from here! I came here with some friends and the dog still hasnt let me down....bratwurst with mustard, onions, and sauerkraut is the way to go...btw if it aint on the menu, u aint gonna get it so dont ask for anything crazy like grilled onions

These are the best hot dogs I have ever had. And while you wait for your dog you can read their libertarian literature, plastered on all the walls. A nice antidote to the left-wing socialist pap everywhere else in Berkeley.
Top Dog catered my wedding and was a hit! People still talk about how delicious the food was, and the service was great. Can't wait to have an "anniversary" some day and hop in and enjoy the food!

Best dog in sf bay area!
Try kielbasa or garlic frank or bratwurst; all excellent!
And, d bun lightly toasted n all dcfresh condiments u want at self serve.

If u haven't tried, u miss a lot.
Also try d unfiltered apple juice. Delicious.
Awesome veggie dog on a French roll. Great fixins. Cheap and quick. Open late. What more can I ask?

Taste: 4
Value: 3
Service: 3

Like Desi Dog, I can't believe this place has four stars and is one of the most highly rated places in Berkeley. The hot dogs are pretty good, and they have a decent selection, but in the end they are still hot dogs, and rather expensive ones at that (~$3).
I love Top Dog. The sausages are tasty, cooked perfectly and there's something about those buns. "A Bock and a Hot" is my usual order, a perfect spicy sweet combo.

Reasons why I visit Berkeley:

#1 Top Dog
#2 Visit my cousin and friends

These are the best hot dogs i've ever tasted. I bought one to take back to so cal, but I couldn't resist and ate it 5 minutes after i bought it.

This is my go to place when I visit Berkeley

There's always a good crowd forming around this little shack, and the cooks inside are always cool

I've tried a few of the dogs and my favorite has to be the smoked chicken apple because of it's apple aftertaste.  sounds like a weird combo with meat but its delicious

The dogs always come piping hot wrapped up in a hot dog bun and there's a counter with condiments and toppings

This place is a landmark and should be visited at least once in a lifetime

If you're in Berkeley and want a great hot dog, Top Dog is the place to go to. This isn't the typical hot dog that you would find in a grocery store; there is a vegetarian one (Weenie dog), chicken ones (lemon chicken, chicken apple), hot links, and a variety of other dogs depending on your preference. 
 
I've always been a fan of their chicken apple and lemon chicken, but imagine my surprise when I came in and noticed they had a Mango Habanero Special AHHH. Note: this is the first time I've ever seen a special at top dog, but the sign read "special of the week" so this may be a continuing thing (!)

Final piece of advice: this place gets packed on Friday and Saturday nights when students come a knockin' in their their drunken stupors so it may be best to save your late nate cravings for other days.

This place tastes especially good at around 1am haha, but during the day it's pretty good too.

i usually order the hot link which is pretty spicy and sometimes they have the mango habanero chicken which is a little less spicy. they are both good :] the chicken apple is good too and not spicy at all.

I think what makes this place stand out though is the bread, they toast it on the grill while they are grilling up your hot dog YUM

$3 each. BRING CASHH!

(-1 star) for the service. they attend to you, but aren't the friendliest. a smile would've been nice :/

Awesome dogs, mustard (Beaver brand mustard could well be my favorite logo in the world) and potato salad.  I continue to be amazed at the fact that the dude at the grill can keep track of 40 simultaneous orders at 2:30 in the morning.  Always love reading the overbearing libertarian literature plastering the walls.

And anyone who complains about the price can only be comparing to an AM / PM microwave dog, and can be ignored...  Top Dog is Top Notch Cheap Eats.
Great place to go after a late night of studying or partying. Good selection of hot dogs and awesome service. Can't really ask for more.
Calabrese. 'nuff said.

So I'm visiting Berkeley this past weekend to watch my Bruins get throttled by Cal.  Before the debacle, I'm just glad that I was able to partake and enjoy my first Top Dog.  I had heard that Top Dog was an institution since I listen to Petros and Money sports talk radio.  I had zero expectations and zero knowledge about what they served.
