This little shack has one of the best veggie dogs I've ever had. Other than that they have a great selection of different dogs and sausages. Their hot link is the greatest and just the right spice level.

The only con is this place looks filthy dirty. But if you can get past that and enjoy the food it's all good. :)

Always there when you need a good weiner in your mouth. 

My favorites are the Lousiana hot link, and the kielbasa. 

Fast, easy, and reasonably priced. 

Downside - no other buns besides the white hoagie roll, and STILL after all these years, cash only. :-(

Quality ingredients. (NOT ALL lips and assholes)
Once you weave through the slalom course that is the drunken line of really awesome post bar college humpers, you'll be rewarded with the best dog this side of the Mississippi! Honestly, I normally attempt to eat healthy but Top Dog hot dogs are unique in quality and addictive taste. I suggest flagship dog, named appropriately on the menu "the Top Dog"

As an added bonus they are open late on the weekends. You may even be able to see an obliterated sorority gal faceplant and drag  down her friend in front of the place. (she was fine) What is is that makes me laugh at wipes?! Sauerkraut and buns in the hair.

Go to Top Dog with a Vet...cause they will abbrevs the order.  You will hear "Brock", "Killa", etc...I love ordering "Chicken Lemon", but I just say "Chicken Lemon".  I should make something up like "Tweety", but I don't want to get dogged (get it).  This place is great and it's fun seeing drunk college students tumble in and out.

The best place for drunk munchies!

Open late: check
Quick: check
Cheap: check
Delish: check

Get the hot link -- only $3. Amazeballs.

959th review? Ok! It's worth bumping it asymptotically closer to five.

It's Top Dog. That's all you really need to say. I'm not even going to recommend any one sausage over the others. Even the veggie one is good.

Covered with classically conservative (now called fiscally conservative, socially liberal) and generally anarchistic sayings, one can hope some of that rubs off on the patrons.

Ah, I have fond memories of leaving Doe Library at 1:45 am and heading over for a bockwurst.

I miss hearing "Ey, who's got the bock?  Alright I got 2 kiels and a german.  You all owe me two and a half, cough it up!!!"

Makes me wanna do college all over again.

First week back from A-town* to B-town*, and of course I roll by Top Dog for my first meal purchase. La Burrita (don't snicker) was a close second, but I just couldn't resist the amazing aroma of the links. Got a cal and a lemon chicken, and she even butterflied both for me. Awesome. I had been missing the sensation of stone-ground in the back of my throat burning my nostrils. Ahhh sinus-clearing hot dogs, where else can you get that? Even my native C-town's* Vienna dogs, while good in their own right, get defeated by that almighty Top Dog.

Hope the dude with the long dreads still works there.

Good flavors.... good condiment choices...and the guy working there sure knows all the lyrics to every kanye song

But too many times I try to take a huge honkin' bite of the hot dog and wind up with a mouthful of mustard and onions and bun. Seriously i feel like half the hotdog is just a mustard and onion sandwich... or an whatever-condiment-you-put-on sandwich.

Also seriously $3? If only there were a costco a block away that opened til 3....


get the hot link.

Dogs good as ever and I'm sure I've tried every flavor by now but I usually stick with a chicken and apple or a hot link. Can't go wrong with that. Closes late so that's a plus especially on the weekends when you need to eat something at 2AM. Does get packed at certain times so that can get annoying, but hey...it's popular I guess.

Delicious hot dogs and sausages, and while you're waiting for your order you can enlighten yourself by reading the numerous libertarian/anarchist (yes, I know there's a difference, but the distinction is blurred in this particular establishment) cartoons and political tracts that plaster its interior walls.  Also, it's the only place I know of other than 7-11 where you can walk out the door with a piping hot hot dog AND a fresh pack a cigarettes.

I don't know if it's a combination of food and alcohol at 2:00AM, but I LOVE ME SOME TOP DOG. :)

i think i've only been there once during the day time, but any other time, the dogs are awesome.  Normally I get a Top and a Lemon, and it always hit the spot.  Service is fast, not too "friendly" (in the sense that they don't really chit chat with their customers), but really who cares.  If you're hungry and want quick, delicious hot dogs this is the place.

Came here hearing that this was the place to go to when at Berkeley.  Not surprised because of its close location to campus and simple menu but hearing the hype, I wish I hadn't because it might have ruined it for me.

Food - Hot dogs and sausages.  It's good, yet, average.  Nothing special here to be honest.
Price - Still a cheap place but $3 per is a bit much.
Service - This is the awesome part.  The guy is lively and willing to take orders from everyone whenever you're ready.  There's no line, just when your food's go to eat.
Environment - Small cramped place but really gets you to know your neighbor.

Still a decent place to get a bite to eat and worth it if you're willing to drop $3 per link and looking for a late night snack.

Suggestion - Any sausage ... not that kind.

Last week Top Dog catered a fundraiser at the middle school across from my aunt's house.  I happened to be painting the fence in the front yard when the distinctively delicious Top Dog smell wafted over.  It was a weirdly dissonant moment because here I was, in Moraga, smelling something that I've always associated with late-night shenanigans in Berkeley.  At the time, I didn't know Top Dog was catering the event, but there I was, standing in the front yard sniffing at the air, confused and unexpectedly hungry.  I had to go over and see what it was.  Once I found out it was in fact Top Dog I started re-evaluating my relationship with the establishment - more specifically, the oddly Pavlovian reaction that Top Dog elicits in me and the sad (or awesome) fact that I can identify them by smell.  

I stopped thinking about it so much the next time I got Top Dog.  There's not a whole lot more I can add to the stellar reviews this place has gotten, but I will say that it's all well-deserved.  Everything I've gotten here (hot link, calabrese, lemon chicken, kielbasa) has been amazing and satisfying in a way that you wish all late-night food was.  Looking forward to my next experience!

I LOVE THE HOT LINK!!! 

Also, about 2 years ago, I ran into Usher!! 
I got to take a picture with him :) (embarrassing, but hey- it's USHER!) 
& Yes, THE Usher was getting a Top Dog! 

Good things can happen at Top Dog.

I ate here twice and will no longer come here again. My first experience was great because I was drunk and hungry and the line stretching out the street "seemed" promising. That was my first experience. So I was in the area last night and was craving some hot dog. By the way, this is no PINKS, but it will have to do. It was good as usual. But the next morning I had the worst stomach ache Ive had in a long time. I traced back my steps to what I ate the night before and it all comes back to Top Dog. Don't let the huge menu fool you into thinking this is any better than the Mexican guy selling dogs out of a club. Costco hot dogs are ten times better. 
I feel sorry for all those naive young Asian students who go there thinking their getting a good old American hot dog.

hands down the best  "gourmet cuisine" experience you'll ever have!

rated 4.5 stars

the first time i came here... i was with some friends and then girlfriend (now wife). we didn't know how to order so we were standing around the doorway looking at the menu. the only worker there (who was doing the grill) yelled out  "if you're not going to order... get the f out of my doorway." we jus looked at each other confused and shocked. we continued to look at the menu trying to see what we wanted.  he then shouted "are you guys deaf!... get the F out of my doorway!!" so we finally ordered and then asked for 2 drinks (didn't specify what kind). he was like.. "are you going to tell me which kind or do i have to be a f-ing mind reader." WHAT A FREAKIN JERK! 

but you know what... SCREW YOU MR. TOP DOG DUDE!... I LOVE the links here. The original top dog, hot link and kielbasa were my favorites. my least favorite was the lemon chicken. I can't wait to go back and try some others.

Regarding the holy trifecta of foods for a 21-year old male college student like myself with no regard for his health- the pizza, the hot dog, and the hamburger- I've always considered the pizza and the burger to be in a deadlock for first place with the hot dog lagging far behind. It isn't as flavorful or satisfying as the other two. Of course, that all changed when I tried Top Dog. Particularly the Calabrese, with ketchup, spicy mustard, onions and tons of sauerkraut!

What is there to say about this place that hasn't already been said? It kicks ass... everything about it. Just because it's three in the morning doesn't mean you have to settle for shitty or overpriced food! You can still come here and buy two dogs, one for you and one for that girl you met at the frat (and hopefully it's not the last wiener she's going to see that night!).
The only sausage-fest that I'll ever walk out of bearing a smile.     :)

This place is my favorite sausage spot ever.  I always come here after a day of lounging down Telegraph.  I usually get the hot link which I add raw onions and ketchup/ hot mustard to.  What can I say, I'm a simple kinda girl.  The bread is perfect and I'm not left throwing away half of the bun cuz it's way longer than the sausage like at other places.

I'm not gonna lie, I wasn't really sound of mind when I ate here but from what I remember it was really, really good. I had the hot link and it was juicy with just the right amount of spicy-ness. Well worth the price and kudos on being open late (then again, anything open past midnight is pretty good for an Irvine girl). If I ever get the chance, I'll try out their other dogs!

I'm not sure which Top Dog location catered our corporate event today, but I figure the product should be pretty consistent with the main store. We had the choice between an original Top Dog, a hot link, a chicken apple sausage, and "the wienie" (their vegetarian hot dog). 

I chose the chicken apple sausage, which came on a toasted sesame seed french roll, instead of the typical hot dog bun that I am used to. There was a condiment section where I added chopped onions and some stoneground mustard. 

Overall, it was just okay. The chicken apple sausage was good, but nothing special -- I have had chicken apple sausages in the past from grocery stores that taste about the same. The bun, although a different concept, was also just okay. Even the stoneground mustard and chopped onions didn't give it a pop of flavor that it so badly needed. Texturally, there was nothing memorable about it, either.

If these hot dogs are supposed to be amazing, I could try giving it the benefit of doubt since they were obviously prepared in advanced, wrapped, and stored in coolers to keep them warm, but it's hard to believe that even advanced preparation could deprive them of flavor.

This was my first time having Top Dog (apparently my Mom was a fan of them when she attended UC Berkeley back in the day), and it will probably be my last. Even if my work provides them for free again at another event, I would likely try the other food they have instead.

I don't really like hot dogs, but this place has the best dogs I've eaten thus far. Gourmet dogs for a great price. I love eating their Chicken Apple sausages. The service is pretty fast, so don't mind their long lines at night. Another great thing is that you can order boxes of their hot dogs for parties, and they're also decently priced. This is one of the few places I miss while living on Telegraph Ave, and being a college student...

Cash only...

Old school fast food.  No seats.  Just order, step aside, pay, receive, condiment your dog, and eat outside or on the run.  Quintessential American paced dining.  

Good quality dogs and snausages, grilled on a flat-top grill to sizzling perfection at fast food prices.  Good value.  The brat and the German showcase good Euro flavors, the Calabrese is a great Italian style, the linguica is pure Portugese greasy goodness and the hot link is hot, seriously.  Good selection of mustards so knock yourself out.  

Extra star for being open late, 2-3 am?  i've pulled up to this location from being out n about, to illegally park, run in and get our late night fix @ 1:45 am and back on the road a happy camper.   A great occasional indulgence.

Top Dog has the best selection of hot dogs in the Bay Area, and their prices are quite good. I'd check them out if I was going to cater an event.

I have bought uncooked hot dogs from their stores to grill at home. $7.50 gets you 6 dogs and buns, and the per-dog price goes down if you buy in 25-30 dog packs.

Meh, it's ok .. you can't really cook a sausage wrong  .. unless you're an idiot.

The hotlinks ... aren't hot.  Get Ohberto hot links and this will be the top spot.

The hype is what this place is, I grill better stuff myself.

Hot damn I love hot dogs.

The top dog with all the fixings is all I need after one too many whiskey shots. It just puts me in a good place. They also have RC Cola, which is old school man.

Minus one star because I no longer know any of the employees and can't get any more free dogs. Guess I only have myself to blame for that one. 

Regardless great place to get your wiener fix.....and no, not that kind.

Best hotdog you can buy. I got the beef frank with everything on it and it was so good. Im not usually a huge fan of hotdogs but the meat quality along with the toasted sesame bun was epic. 

I go to school in Austin so ive got a thing for local businesses. This place is not only local, but is really unique and literally a hole in the wall a stones throw from university avenue. You have the option to add a drink and chips to your dog, and the food comes out really fast.

This place is really popular with students with visitors alike, so come prepared to wait in line. However, ive eaten hotdogs in new york and the one at top dog upped it 98345093x. 

Also, if youre a libertarian go here! You will love the cartoons and articles they have posted all over the wall. 

Come hungry, leave happy. Just ask them to give you their wurst :)

i can't believe it ..my last New York at the Hearst branch sucked as well as Giorgia's we both thought it and the kraut tasted off...i hope it was an anomaly cause i've only had good dogs there until that disaster

Adding to the list of iconic Berkeley eateries (for students) there is Top Dog. 

Like La Burrita this place is open late as well so it has a loyal student following. It's also cheap. 

I'm a fan of their chicken apple hot dogs and the way they grill the buns.

Most fun nights as a student ended at Top Dog. Thanks a million!

Oh dearest Top Dog, how I love thee.

It's been 4 years since my last Top Dog but the memory of its taste has not faded a bit.  Their menu is VAST, but I seem to always end up getting their top dog frank and the kielbasa.  The hot dogs and buns are both cooked on the grill.  There's self-serve sauerkraut, chopped onions, ketchup, and mustard on the counter as well.  DELICIOUS!!!!!!!!!  So good I can't even put into words -- you just have to try it yourself to understand.  I've had so many friends say they don't like and refuse to eat hot dogs...until they try this place.  The taste and quality has been consistent among all of the three Top Dogs I've visited around the Berkeley campus, although the one on Center Street is probably the newest/cleanest of the three and with more seating too.  I have yet to find anything that comes close to Top Dog...*sigh*

YUM! I usually don't even like hot dogs but top dog is pretty good. I've tried a few different types but the chicken apple is definitely the best. 
3 bucks isn't cheap for a hot dog, but I would definitely recommend trying it at least once.

Can't beat Top Dog if you want something quick. If you are looking for a deal, go to Costco. If you are looking for a grilled dog with all the fixin's you want to add and difference choices for everyone in the group, then stop by the Top Dog.

We tried the Top Dog, the hot link, even the vegetarian one - all good. Toasted bread/bun a plus. Just dogs, chips and sodas. No fries or anything like that, but hey just walk down the street. Oh, the funny part is they sell bucket's for $1.

I am so sick of giving 5 stars.  However, I have only been going to old standards recently, so I guess I have no choice.  But I really don't like giving 5 stars.  How do you recover from that?  It is like losing Yelp cred every time you do it, right?  You are putting it all out there--saying, I love this place and I can't even think of 1 thing I can knock it for.  And that's not a yelper--especially not an "elite" yelper like yours truly.  Yet I am Mr. 5 Star lately.  Top Dog, I will lose more cred for you--you are worth it.  
Top Dog is a classic that never changes.  In a good way.  
Let me explain.  I went to Cal.  I ate at Top Dog all the time.  I had a friend who worked there, and well, we were hooked up for 2 years.  It was incredible.  And we would be spiteful (not as spiteful as the staff, but there was plenty of spite) of all the yuppies that came in to the joint and ruined our little pinko-commie sausage party.  
Now, fast forward many a year.   Berkeley continues to yuppify.  I, unfortunately, have continued to yuppify (that admission really hurt).  But Top Dog, no way.   Resistance baby.  
I was in the original joint a few weeks ago after the Arcade Fire show.  I was with several friends, all of whom exhibit varying stages of yuppification, but still think they have indie cred.  One of my most indied-out yuppie friends entered Top Dog for the first time.  Then she does the unthinkable--whips out her cell phone and starts chatting!  I mean, I winced.  But then I got nervous--would it be tolerated?  Has Top Dog lost its swagger?  NO!!!!!!!!!!!
The staff, the patrons--me--all shot her dirty looks.  Then the main dog-guy put the smack down on her little chit chat.  She had to grovel her way back into the good-dog-graces before she was served.  Outside we all ate our dogs in bliss, and she just knew she was shamed.  She also knew she was eating sausage heaven.  

Top Dog, you are timeless.

Libertarian strong hold of Berkeley. The cook isn't nice cause he's not here to baby you, he's here to take your money and give you a top dog so don't expect patience. The food is great and what you want for food that's prepared quickly but isn't from a fast food chain. Does not take plastic so beware.

Look, I live in Clark Kerr, and Top Dog is one of the few beautiful things I'm willing to drag my ass down to Durant at 1 AM for.
Chicken apple sausage + mustard + onions + relish. $3. Delicious when drunk, delicious when sober. I don't know what else to say, this place has been reviewed a thousand times, I JUST LOVE IT SO MUCH.

The hot dogs here are alright. I've had the hotlink, the chicken apple, and the lemon chicken. They are all super small, and very pricey (all dogs are 3 bucks). Honestly, the hot dogs seem like things you can find at a local Safeway or Trader Joe's, nothing special about them what so ever. 

The place is really crowded and trashy, and the guy that works there is a complete d-bag. My friend was with me and he didn't know what to order, so he was looking over the selection, and my friend literally only spent like 30 seconds looking at the menu, when the guy working there, told him to "order a dog or leave"...what a jackass

Awesome! Especially on a cold day. Small establishment that basically just serves hot dogs and sausages. Not sure if they're made there or are frozen then just cooked. I've had better elsewhere, but if you want a quick snack then check it out.

Note: Nothing happened to me, but my friend got really sick after eating here. Could have been something else, but makes me a little wary to go back.

i know what you're thinking. it's just hot dogs, and the prices have been going up like crazy. well, hot damn, they are good hot dogs with lots of selection, the toasted buns make me salivate, and the price only went up twenty five cents, you cheapo college students. there are just days where you really crave a top dog, and i think we all try to hide how impressed we are that the people who work there recognize each dog at a glance and know exactly what everyone has ordered (even with 20 people crowding that tiny place) and who's paid and giving it out to them in the right order.

edit*******did you know that they serve fresh apple juice at top dog!?  i just bought one for $1.25 -- it came in a glorious paper cup emblazoned with "7up" -- and it ain't bad at all!  random random.

Who would pay $3+ for a freakin' hot dog? Some would argue you're paying for the "experience"...some would when it's midnight and EVERY OTHER FREAKIN' PLACE in Berkeley is CLOSED. 

Cashiers/cooks are witty, smart@$$e$ but do their job right. They whip through the crowds, gets their orders correctly, and can do some quick math. 

+ Food is good, I've never paid for a $3 dog elsewhere
-  They cook the vegetarian dogs on the same area/grill as the meat ones
-  Place can use more frequent cleaning

Final Call:
It's a novelty for people from out of town. A pit stop. Or when it's midnight again. I'll also be back to try the "Curry Dog" - how cool does that sound!?

I love TOP Dogs! You have to go to this one. The one in Oakland isn't the same. Its just something about the campus environment and the way they grill their dogs that makes it soooooooo delicious. Its like doggie dog heaven with each bite.... droools... 

My normal orders are: hot link, chicken apple and lemon chicken! Yes, I said three! And yes, I do eat all three. Hahaha Try it yourself and if your not satisfy its probably becuz I wasn't there too. Hahaha

Top Dog has always been on top to me, from the quality of their dogs, to the quality of the dog experience, its as good as it gets. I grew up skipping school and going to Top Dog to watch Incredible Hulk at noon and crush dogs. Bird Dogs and tops dogs, alternating back and forth until I could explode. You cant beat it.

Are you drunk? Is it around 3am? Are you in downtown Berkeley? Well then, you better head down to Top Dog, purveyor of quality dogs to drunken students for many a year. They have around, what, 25, 30 different kinds of meat dogs, and exactly 1 kind of veggie dog, called the "weenie". When I was there one time with my vegetarian friend, he naturally ordered the veggie option. When it was done, the owner shouts out: "One weenie, who's got the weenie here?" 40 drunken college students couldn't have been happier. Aah, the old ones are the best ones.

I have Top Dog cravings. 
I've been going to Top Dog since I was a kid--my parents introduced me to the one in montclair (which is no longer there) and I always look forward to going there for lunch when I'm in the area. There's nothing like their hot dogs :) 

I LOVE TOP DOG!

Excellent hot dogs. All of their selections are scrumptious and are accompanied by excellent buns and a satisfactory range of condiments. The sausages give a little pop when bitten into, and as the juices flow out, the well-cooked links burst with flavor. Great location, great personnel. Expect a line during busy hours!

I would've given more stars but the girl working here Wednesday (Aug 15.) afternoon made my first visit a very...UNFORGETTABLE one (in a negative way). The girl working was very rude to all the customers, shouting "NEXT" and "Move out the door way"...and these were not asked kindly but plain rudely as a demand. Next time I'll probably go to the other location and hopefully staff will know what customer service is all about!

But the dogs were really good!
happy memories of the old days and their unique dogs. the gourmet mustard, relish, it's all good! beats wienerschnitzel anytime!

stopped thru here after a whole day of skiing in tahoe. typically am not a hot dog fan, but these taste more like sausages, and they are GOOD. small dingy place, one girl taking ur order and making ur hot dog. the inside floor is littered with onions, mustard, and ketchup. basically, dirty. but the hot dogs are sooo good. if you're looking for a quick fast meal, this won't let u down.

Their veggie dog is Field Roast, which is the most legit vegan sausage out there.  I wish they would carry the other two flavors that Field Roast offers, though (Apple Sage and Mexican Chipotle), to give us non-meat-eaters a little more variety.  Still, the price is right and it makes for a good lunch once loaded up with some onions and 'kraut.  The "cash only" policy is a little annoying, seeing as how other Top Dog locations accept cards, but I kind of understand it since this place is so tiny.

EDIT: Downgrading this place from 4 to 3 stars because of all the idiotic and in-your-face libertarian propaganda.  I'm just looking for a meal, not to join the cult of Ayn Rand.

TASTY THREE DOLLAR HOT DOGS SERVED LATE

Sometimes I get a craving for a good hot dog and Top Dog is where I stop to satisfy my desire.  I like how they char the hot dog on the grill and their substantial sesame seed roll instead of the usual bun that falls apart.  I like their rules for ordering which states that there is no line, to pay with cash, and not comment on their enormous ice machine.

It was crowded as usual but the cook was very friendly and took our order promptly.  We paid in cash and patiently waited in the narrow space and read some of the interesting newspaper clippings.

Hot Link
I ordered the beef hot link filled with four kinds of pepper and my mouth was feeling a little burn after the first bite.  I topped it off with deli-style mustard and sauerkraut; be sure to stay away from the hot mustard unless you can take the pain.

Calabrese
My friend L ordered the semi-hot pork dog filled with paprika, chili, and fennel.  His comments were, "sweet and succulent on a dense sesame seed roll."

Top Dog? This place has over 350 reviews!! I had to give it a try since all Berkeley alumni rave about it. I ordered the Polish and the Hot Link. They both had a good snap to each bite, a must have in hot dogs. The flavor was good and it was tasty, but I just feel Pink's Hot Dogs in LA are better. I think I need to try the lemon chicken next time, apparently everyone orders it. Another thing, the dogs are just too small for me, need to be bigger!!

Probably the best Hot Dogs in Berkeley...maybe even in the East Bay.  I honestly wouldn't rate the service at all because it really isn't necessary.  Just walk in, check the menu out and order something.  

The Top Dogs there:
Hot Link
Apple Chicken

I refuse to give business to anyone who would make a young girl cry.

"Isn't this a review for a hot dog place?" you might ask.... Yes it is.

I pulled up with my girlfriend and dog and was super excited about the place cause we moved from NYC a few months ago and I hadn't had a good hot dog in a while.  I waited by the car with my dog while my girlfriend went in to grab a couple of franks and sodas.  Sounds like the greatest lunch ever right?  About 5 min later, my girl comes storming out of the place saying "f--- this place, we're going somewhere else".  She made me drive away before telling me the story because she didn't want to make it a bigger issue.

She goes on to say that she was making small talk with the nice college girl in front of her when the guy at the counter starts yelling at the college girl who is next in line.  The girl happened to be wearing headphones so he assumed she didn't order immediately because she was listening to music when she was actually just being nice to my girlfriend.  He goes on to say she's self important, inconsiderate, etc...  He was apparently really mean to her and she was so embarrassed she teared up.  After confirming the girl was OK my girlfriend left Top Dog and I'm sure we'll never go back there again.  

I remember being a college kid and putting up with bad service because I didn't realize I had power as a consumer.  $1 = 1 Vote.  Give Top Dog your $ and you are saying you agree with their terrible attitude towards YOU.  Coming from New York City my girl was shocked because she'd never seen someone in the service industry be so rude to a customer.  ...And that's the harshest city in the world.  This is Berkeley!  I thought it was all about peace and love?  Top Dog needs to adjust before everyone catches on.

yes, yes it is a wonderful - nay, the BEST - selection of weiners, brats, chicken dogs, and spicy links...we all know that...what gets me really excited about top dog?

they cater! 

yes my friends, top dog caters parties - go for it.

I was going to write a review of the newly opened Top Dog location on Lakeshore Ave in Oakland but I'd be betraying my loyalty to the location that got me hooked on these delicious dogs to begin with! (BTW, No actual canines were harmed in this review... *insert rumored Asian dog eating stereotype here*)... Top dog never fails to satisfy an appetite whether you're intoxicated or just looking for a light snack and the dogsmiths have an amazing memory when it comes to your order.

+ Hot Link (the HOT) is my FAVORITE dog because I heart the heat but like a bag of chips, you can't have just one... Yeah Frito-Lay, I just jacked your slogan!

+ top dog FRANKFURTER (the TOP) is one of the best hot dogs I've ever had! All beef with the perfect snap (Oscar Mayer who?)

+ Lemon Chicken has a hint of tang/zest but doesn't come with the guilt of biting into a more fattening dog. Fab-U-Lous!

+ Bird dog is another favorite of mine... How can you go wrong with low fat, low cal, spicy bite and best of all... CILANTRO!!!

+ I've had the CAL (Calabrese), BOCK (Bockwurst), KEIL (Keilbasa). GERMAN (German Frank) and the WIENIE Old (Soy based as opposed to the "New" which is wheat protein based) a few times but they don't compare to the ferocious top 4. I don't think I've had the Linguca but if I've had.. I don't remember it. My only gripe is CASH ONLY at certain locations and the price increase from $2.25-$2.50 to $3+ since I've been at CAL. Go Bea.. DOGS!

since we were going to the arcade fire show, we didn't have time to eat anything fancy beforehand and ended up here.  for $9, we got 2 veggie dogs, 2 bags of a chips and a soda.  what a deal.  i always loved the sausages here before, but this was the first time i had the veggie one, and it was actually pretty good.  the toasted bun also adds a nice touch.
Now this is the OG of the top dogs, and as yes it is pricey dogs that are extremely tasty. Good thing about this one is that it's open laaaaaate for the bar and dorm crowd. W00t!

The Top Dog grill master achieves super zen state. It's game day and 25 people crowd the holy sausage shrine. Only through perfect concentration, memory and superior customer service will he grant the holy state of sausage fulfillment. 

Asking for abuse, the orders rain down like assassin bullets. Two bocks, one lemon chick and an RC cola from the stoned student. Three franks, chicken app and delicious potato salad for the alumnus. Will the onslaught ever stop??? Never!!! And that's how Top Dog gets its sh** done.

There are few things in life more satisfying than a perfectly grilled chicken apple sausage with mustard, ketchup and heaps of onions, potato salad and an RC cola. Who the f*** sells RC cola any more? Thank god for Top Dog. The sausages are uber high quality, similar to Wisconsin's myriad of beer brats. For such little cost Top Dog delivers mega meat enjoyment.

I can't not give Top Dog five stars.

It is what it is.
And it does a spectacular job of being 'what it is'!

The hot dogs are not dirt cheap, but they are also the cheapest thing you can get to eat in the area, and they are open until way late.
They draw a huge crowd after the bars close, because it is awesome drunk food (trust me, I lived across the street from this place in the summer, and even earplugs didn't help on Thursday nights!).

I am also guilty of going there at least a few times a week over that summer for lunch and dinner.

I love the lemon chicken.
And the Hot Link is sooooo gooooood!
But it gets way too spicy, especially since I love the Russian Mustard.  I had to tell myself repeatedly that it wasn't worth it.
The Top Dog is also a good choice if you want to play it safe - it's all beef!

The people working there can be a bit gruff (to say the least), if customers stand staring at the menu and block the door.  The inside of the place is tiny, so it's best to know what you want before you enter, or decide quickly.  I know some people like to dawdle with menus, but come on, it's a $3 hot dog stand - not a restaurant - and all of them are pretty good.

This place seems entirely unsanitary to me, especially since I was in there so often and saw employees handled money and hot dogs with the same hand; but... I shall not be a mysophobe.  
As I said, it is what it is.
If you care about things like germs and politeness, you probably should steer clear.

It really is the best hot dog in the bay. And you can't say it's the 2 am effect (where everything tastes AMAZING at 2 am when you're starving) because I've been here at regular dinner times and am still impressed every time. My dogs of choice are the kielbasa and the chicken apple. Plus I really like the buns they use.

Also, if you haven't done it already, buy their six pack of any uncooked dogs + buns ($8.50), take them home and cook them yourself! Cheaper, and still all of that top dog goodness in the comfort of your own home.

Holy mole mole mole mole mole guacamole. 

(Not that there is any guacamole here.  You'll find all other necessary condiments though...including sauerkraut). 

With or without ketchup? I say without.  Add a little mustard, correction, add a TON of mustard, some onions, sauerkraut and that is the perfect top dog.

Top Dog is a Berkeley classic. They even have a veggie dog. The bread is delicious. 

Also, doggie treats

You can also get the supplies for a bbq at a cheaper price.

This is a good place to eat hot dogs even though the buns are not that great but other than that the dogs are good. My favorites are the garlic frankfurter and bockwurst. Besides the food, the people that work there are really friendly and like to engage in conversation with people and often times it's entertaining since most of the people who go there are drunks and potheads.
Been to other sausage places but they can't match top dog. Go Bears!

im always like... how good can hot dogs get? they are meant to be free/cheap....so cant expect too much right? That's why i never stepped into the premises of top dogs in berkeley during my 3 years of being here. Never even considered it once.

But today, i had the biggest cravings for hot dogs, so i decided to try top dogs. I got two hot dogs: hot links and lemon chicken.

Hot links: Very crunchy. I cant taste the spiciness but it was delicious because i added russian mustard, onions, and kraut.

Lemon chicken: Definitely very flavorful and light at the same time. This is the type of hot dog where you dont really have to add much sauces on it because it already has so much flavor.

Bun: like everyone said... its good! Basically a french bun unlike the cheap crap at IKEA or Cosco.

Portions: 1 hot dog would be a snack. 2 COULD be a meal. I have a huge appetite so I was still hungry after 2 hot dogs.

I dont like how they don't have take out packaging though. i stuffed my hot dogs with condiments so they slip out from the openings when i was walking home! Oh welll....no big deal i guess.

I've read reviews to where this place was supposed to be better than Caspers, errr.. don't think so, but the Hot Dog was nicely grilled (despite waiting 4 minutes ) and the dog was delicious.   The help behind the counter was nice also.

5 star for the delicious hot dog

-2 stars for the horrible service and the unsanitary HANDS! wow i really dislike that guy, he looked like he hasnt gotten any in years. and after he handled my money, he went for the hotdog buns WITHOUT WASHING HIS HANDS. and sorry kids, he did not have any gloves on.

i would go back there, but before i do, im definitely checking who the cook is. if its that guy, haha no way am i even stepping in there, thanks.

Whether you're visiting Top Dog late at night or for lunch, this place always tastes delicious. For the price, I'm sure this could be a staple for many students. I'm pretty impressed by how much one worker can shell out so many hot dogs! So you'll have to know what you want when you come, or else just stand aside and let someone else order first. I usually get my hot dog (lemon chicken is my favorite) butterflied on a toasted bun, topped with mustard, lots of onions, and sour kraut. yum...
A fantastic hole-in-the-wall place and the folks here have always been cool.  Haven't been here in a while, but whenever I'm in town, I always make an effort to head out here.

4 years ago before i became a vegetarian, i had a hot link here. man, it was hot and juicy.
they updated their vege-dog and it is much tastier than it was before 
my friends love this place and if they are hungry late night or in between meals, they always get a top dog. the hot link and chicken apple are the favs
ive never had a problem with the service, but some of my friends say the owner can be an ass at times, also, steer clear of politics talk, unless you really want a heated debate...
the service is pretty fast, but it does get really crowded late at night. it's almost always flooded with drunk college kids, fratty frat boys, sorority girls teeter-tottering in their 4 inch heels, bums asking for change. really it is a berkeley landmark. yay for top dog

note: the russian mustard is quite powerful, i put a bunch on my vege-dog once, thinking it was of the spicy brown deli variety, oh big mistake. talk about stinging through the nose, burning the mouth and throat in that spicy horseradishy sort of way. i almost cried. but couldnt stand to waste a top dog so i ate it anyway. what a champ. try it if you dare

You can't fuck with Top Dog.  I ate there so often I had to get a job there to subsidize my hot dog habit.  BTW working at this Top Dog is also one of the coolest jobs to have while in college.  I love Top Dog.

Excellent hole in the wall atmosphere; there isn't even that much room so most people stand outside.  The hot dogs are good and the price is fair.  Feels more fun than the SJ location hence the higher rating.  There is a lot of choice available which is a huge plus.

I heard rave reviews about this place, but was pretty disappointed with my dry chicken apple sausage.

I would have tried the brat, but after seeing the list of every ingredient, my appetite was gone. Isn't the point of a hot dog that you have no idea what is in it?

OH MY what an amazing place!! I was told by my friends to come eat at Top Dog when I came to Berkeley and let me tell you. DEFINITELY NOT A LETDOWN. I had the chicken apple and hot link when I first went there and both were delicious!! $3 for a hot dog is not too expensive. Plus, the service was quick.

The hot link definitely tasted better since I love spiciness so I got the hot link again the second time I went and definitely WORTH the $3! I would highly recommend the hot link for newcomers, especially if they like a bit of a spicy kick in their hot dogs.

Another bonus is the location of Top Dog. It is in the "Asian Ghetto" so there are other restaurants and dessert places to go! I like to get a hot link (with EXTRA sauerkraut) and go to quicklys to get a large milk tea (only $2). That's more than a meal and it only costs $5!!

I have yet to try the other sausages but I'll make sure to try more when I go back!!

Great Hot Dogs for a few bucks... Lemon and Apple Chicken dogs are my favs. Cool lil spot to grab a bite when you are looking for something different on the strip. Dont like the serve yourself Kraut and onions. I would rather pay a bit more to have the employee put those on. Public access to the jar makes me avoid the fixins

like the fact that they're open way late.  menu is simple and cheap, but the place is 24/7 packed with college kids roaming the street.  when i was in college...i was studying...not eating top dog and walking around in the street.  kids now adays :)  came up in here after the Janet Jackson concert in September.  someone suggested top dog.  it was aiight.

Can I say yummy.  Needless to say it's not in my typical diet to be eating hot dogs and sausages, but I had to make an exception because it's different.  

They use a very unique ordering system, just shout what you want and hand them money.  It's as easy as that and the person behind the counter for the most part keeps track of who ordered what.  They prep your orders in bunches and reheat as you order.

We passed by the one in downtown berkeley, but that just seems too commercial.  

Here is what I have tried:

Hot link, wow hot and peppery, very good
Chicken Apple, a flare of healthiness by providing apple in a sausage
Kielbasa, great as well

I wish I could try them all, but I may not survive.

ITop Dog is a fine establishment with the usual characters being the smoked-out college kids, late-night nerds, the crazy guy with a wild eye and random asian girls in their pajamas.

In college, Top Dog was THE place to go to after a night of drinking and frat partying. Nothing killed a crave like a Top Dog. (Smothered in your choice of sauerkraut, relish, onions, ketchup, all sorts of foreign mustards, etc.)

Nowadays, Top Dog is THE place to go to after a night of binge drinking and pub crawling. Kidding. But it's open late and is the perfect late night snack. They have a wide assortment of sausages/dogs to choose from. Be on your toes when they take your order and when you pay. They run a tight ship.

oh so many drunken nights at this place... i miss it.  i wish there were more top dogs in the world, especially in the southbay... and LA...

its not that theyre so AWESOME either.. maybe its jsut taht everytime i eat it, im piss drunk.

The guy working the grill can be a real prick but dammit I love dem top dogs. This is one of my favorite baller on a budget places to eat. I usually get the apple chicken, regular top dog or the hot link (CAUTION: it may cause excessive sweat) I find the clippings taped on the wall right across the condiments to be very entertaining.

I'm gonna keep it really brief on this one. I have eaten here many, many times, and have been satisfied with my food each and every time. This is where I was introduced to a chicken apple hotdog, and it's become one of my favorites by far. I knocked off a star for the guy who makes the dogs and for the price. My friends and I agree that the guys working the grill are pretty douchey, and I'd say this price is a little bit on the pricy side. But these things shouldn't stop you from eating here because it tastes great!

Very small shop that is order to go. Extremely busy and extremely crowded. If willing to push through the hoards of people and strategically get your order to the very skilled head cook, the hot dogs are definitely worth the wait. Apple chicken is a definite must. The prices are fair ($3) and the hot dogs are grilled extremely well with fresh bread buns. There are several of these places in Berkeley that can be visited, however as far as hot dogs go these are the best you can get.
what everyone else said

This place is awesome for late night snacking because they are open so late! Its a bit of a travel from where I live, but it's worth it when you are craving a delicious dog. 

They are on a busy street so parking is usually tough, but its best at night because the meters are free. Their pretty small and the place is only "to-go". They also have a line on condiments on the back wall which is good. But they are missing one thing that I love getting on my dog...cheese! 

Their variety of dogs are diverse and they have about 10 different types on the menu. They have a german dog, Italian Dog, their original dog, a chicken apple dog and even a Veggie dog! I love it! 

When you bite into these, it is nothing but bursts of juices and flavors which are to die for. They are always fresh and delicious, and they toast the bun which makes the hot dog even better. 


Honestly, the only reason I won't give this place 5 stars is because the cooks are pretty rude here. Not all of them, but especially this girl that I've encountered twice. VERY rude to me in front of other customers for no reason. But I wont let that spoil my yummy dog! I always go back!

They're good for when you want a really good hot dog. This is basically as good as hot dogs get: great almost crispy buns (perfect because I'd rather not eat hot dogs on cold bread or a warm crouton) and the meat is just perfect. But I think their toppings really finish it off. I personally enjoy the sauerkraut and won't think it's Top Dog without it. It just complements the link itself better than any other pairing I've ever seen. Overall really good hot dog.

So why not 5 stars? When it comes down to it, it's still a hot dog. A lot of my measure is based on: would I recommend it to someone visiting Berkeley for the first time, and it's still no. This is food good for grabbing on the go to classes or as a snack on your way back home. I'd say $3 for a hot dog is a little steep. It's a nice treat every so often, but not on the top of my "treating myself." I would recommend it if you have like a class at Li Ka Shing (aka middle of nowhere) at like 5pm (telebears just really didn't work out this semester)... Grab one after classes on your way down to wait for the 51B

There are times in a person's life when you need to fill an unexplained void. I have found fulfillment in a hot dog. This modest hot dog shop serves up a wide variety of hot dogs, sausages and more hot dogs. From the Top Dog to kielbasa to the Chicken Apple, this place does you right. Come for one, stay for many. Top Dog is worth any trouble to get there. PS never got a straight answer about "Weeds" on the menu. Anyone have info on that?

Let me be frank: This is not a review of the hot dogs but of Top Dog itself, as an establishment and a venerated Berkeley institution.

I like hotdogs but you'd have to really love hot dogs to go apeshit for this place like so many fratboys/sorrority girls/basketball players do. For me, spending 3.75 on an albeit tasty apple sausage is just crazy, but hey some people love 'em. You can hear/get into some crazy talks about libertarianism, sarah palin, women and politics any time there, especially with the crazy hobos who come in later at night around 1-2AM.

Mediocre dogs served by rude employees with patrons who think they're being counter-culture because the dude serving the dogs is in a service role but isn't being service-oriented! How bad ass.

Yeah, right.

I remember Top Dog tasting incredibly mediocre when I was hammered. That's pretty bad considering the Unit 3 DC was my own personal Gary Danko on some rougher nights.

My uncle recently came to visit from Chicago for my sister's wedding. We picked him and his family up from the airport around 12:30AM. We didn't even get to go home to drop off bags; he made us stop at TopDog at one in the morning. It was that serious.

These dog's are so good its not even funny.

I've heard that in order to graduate at Cal, there are several things that must occur: 
- Watch a drunken guy jump out of a 3rd floor window
- Have an awkward date with a girl you have nothing in common with
- Eat at Top Dog

I got my chicken apple dog, and decided to go to a quiet spot.  It was a glorious warm, sunny day as I sat at Memorial Glade.  The nice ambient nature sounds in the heart of campus hides the urban dwelling where Top Dog lies, and provided a nice respite for a suburban kid.  I took a seat by the main stacks, admiring the Frisbee throwers and the beautiful co-eds going to Evans and Soda Hall.  (ack!)  And I believe that's when it started going downhill.

Like a blind date that has been hyped over and over, I expected Top Dog to be THE best dog, EVAR.  The high expectations were unrealistic.  She had pimples all over her face, had bad breath, and a smile like the Joker's, hiding the sinister plans underneath her splotchy skin to part me with my money.  Wait.  What I meant was the bun was dry, the dog was nothing special (Aidell's Chicken Apple tastes better!), and the 'piece de resistance' was that with that first bite, the onions and relish that I had loaded up on my dog fell gracefully, landing on my brand new white shoes.  FML.

I've tried Top Dog on 3 other occasions (most recently in 2008), and each experience cements my initial try.  Oh well, at least I graduated.

Yay, another 5 star review for Top Dog. But what do u expect, its pretty deserving of that validation. The hot dogs are great and very affordable. Seriously, some people complain about its shadiness and how its so cramped and dingy looking. But really, no one gives a crap because that's how great hot dog places are. So suck it up. It adds to the charm of this place, though charm isn't what I would use to describe it in a nutshell. Anyway, I always make an effort to stop by and grab a few hot dogs whenever I'm in the area and suggest anyone else should do the same.

For me, its best to come here at night when its cool outside, like after a night of being on a drunken bender at the local pub. I don't care what I get and I don't care what you get, just make sure you dump some sauerkraut on that dog before you stuff your face in it. Take your food outside, find something that's kind of clean to lean on and chow-the-fuck-down. Perfect snap in the hot dog and just enough crunch in the bun. Watch the juices ooze out and the smoke drift away in the cool breeze. Eat a few here and take some to go. Then call it night...

***Giving the homeless man change is optional***
***Perfect for ballin'-on-a-budget***
***Good for the munchies***


The gist...

High points: Good hot dogs and sausages. Loving that warm sauerkraut too. And it's very affordable.

Low points: It's in Berkeley, so yea, at night it can look pretty shady. But don't be intimidated, the bums wont bite.

OH NO HE DIDN'T.

THE GUY MAKING THE SAUSAGE WAS TOUCHING THE BUNS ON THE GRILL, AND THEN HANDLED THE MONEY!!!!! THIS IS WHY RESTAURANTS IN THE BAY AREA NEED A RATING SYSTEM LIKE LA COUNTY. 

...enough of this rant. Anyways, it's a sausage/hot dog for $3 bucks. 

...do people like this place because of the food, or because of the fact that it's cheap? I'm a bit torn. Yeah, it tastes good, but not out-of-this-world delicious. I've definitely had better sausages (I ordered the Chicken Apple and the spicy sausage). Cheap-tastic.

Top Dog's been a staple in Berkeley a long time now and they won't do you wrong when you're craving a plain ol' dog...a polish...a bratwurst...a chicken apple sausage...you get the idea.

Return Visit = Yes

You know, you can dress up a hot dog and make it look like other things,.... but it's still a hot dog.

Now if you are desparate for a hot dog, then this is the place to go.

I really wouldn't recommend it though....its still all lips and assholes.
I was desparate and had the chicken apple sausage.......$3.....still burping.

Overpriced for hot dog.

Honestly, if you want a good old-fashioned american hot dog...hit up Costco!

Usually overcooked, that is if you know what a real hot dog is supposed to taste like.

Check-in:
So I have been receiving much hate mail regarding my one star rating, and that I praised Costco hot dogs. 
Thus, I decided to go back and and see if top dog is all it is hyped up to be. 

Conclusion: I stick with my original statement that for an old-fashioned 'american' hot dog, costco is the place. Because a lemon dog or a bird dog on what looks like a subway bread is not a 'hot dog' 

However, I will say that Top Dog bring flavor to the table, and variety. And will therefore, up my review to a two star.

Great for college students in need of munchies after a late night drinking... Greasy, fast, and cheap, but I couldn't help noticing that the guy took my money and used the same hand to press the buns on the grill... I guess it's something you'd overlook in your alcohol-induced daze.
Terrible vegetarian hot dog!! Dry and tasteless. I took one bite and threw it away.

Chicken and Apple was absolutely delish! I would bart up from Fremont to Berkeley just to get one and then bart back!


I am truly amazed by the person taking our orders, he managed to remember 10 people's orders at a time. Amazing!

Wish they would somehow be more organized with the influx of people going in and out!

Mmmmm.. those were some really good hotdogs.. i like the bun sooo much.. not your typical hot dog bun...
i got the frankfurter (?), something with 50% veal, pork, and something else.. who knows.. lol     i put onions, sauerkraut, and ketchup on it and it was fantastic!
i would definitely come here again and try other kinds

After hearing rave reviews, my girlfriend decided to check out Top Dog. Since, we have gone several times, but weren't impressed at all.

Top Dog usually only has one employee at a time, and because of the usually large crowds, customer service is very poor. Combine that with how unclean the place is - for example, the employee will touch your coins and dollar bills, then grab your food with the same hands without any gloves and without washing his hands in-between - and Top Dog isn't a place we'd recommend. And that's before even reviewing their food.

I'm a vegetarian, so I've tried the one veggie item they have twice, and think that even frozen veggie dogs that can be purchased from supermarkets taste a whole lot better. My girlfriend, who does eat meat, has tried a variety of items, but none of which she likes.

I've heard a customer there say that the food is delicious when you're drunk, and maybe he's right: Top Dog is often packed late into the night, especially on weekends after bars and clubs let out.

Like the 2007 Cal Bears football team, this place is overrated. The hot dogs and selection are good, but not for the price. The only benefit to this place is the late hours so the drunk zombies can come feed.
You really can't find a better dog than this. Yes, I've tried everything on the menu, and I will stand my ground and just say calabrese for the win!
Uhm, let me just go and take my $3 to Trader Joe's or Berkeley Bowl.  I can get more food for the $3.

Libertarian propoganda, opinionated and offensive staff, regular hot dogs, and rc cola.  

Aidell's sausages are better and the staff is too much of a hassle when not showing a out-of-towner around.  I usually pass.
Sure this is a classic Berkeley place and sometimes it is the best thing (only thing) open, but .......$3 for a hot dog?  Are you fucking kidding me?

Oh I really hate having to give this place a bad review.  I'm sure food poisoning isn't the norm here, but I don't think I will ever forget the days my friends and I spent in the restroom that followed a trip to top dog.  It was a cheap tasty eat i'll admit.  But there were just things about my visit that just didn't sit well besides the food poisoning.  For one, on this particular night, there was this awful stench that we couldn't avoid.  At first i thought it was maybe the bum who sat in the corner of the room, but after he left, the deathly odor just stayed.  It was like the smell of like moist moldy animal fur.  The guy manning the grill didn't seem to care or notice, but I'm hoping that this scent is an unusual experience for everyone else.

AWFUL experience here - please, never go here if you want to be treated like a human being when and a CUSTOMER. I mean it.  BOYCOTT THIS PLACE.

The guy behind the counter (presumably the owner) chose to ignore me and take orders behind me as I waited patiently in line in the mess of a room for people whom I thought were ahead of me. Being a polite person, I asked one family if they had ordered; they said they had, so I was waiting for the person next to me to order. Well, apparently I wasn't fast enough for Top Dog Hot Shot because he proceeded to ignore me, take 3 orders ahead of me, deliberately ignore me, make rude comments about "people who are too confused to order", and laughed about it.

Is this how one treats customers in Berkeley these days? I don't care how many students you deal with who accept this kind of behavior, but as an adult, I do not.

I encourage every ADULT and STUDENT who wants to be treated with at least a modicum of respect at the counter to NEVER PATRON TOP DOG.

In the end, I never even ordered a hot dog. The kind man behind the counter informed me that if I wanted a real line, I could go to La Burrida next door. I did.

Really? People are rating place this as good?  Compared to what?  Thank god I have the years of training choking down MREs in the military.  Berkeley it turns out is another country, who the hell thinks its okay to serve a hot dog on a baguette.  Evidently no one rating this place has ever had a bacon wrapped hot dog from SF or LA, or for that matter never chewed broken glass... both opposite ends of the spectrum in which top dog couldn't even hope to rate on.  A serious disappointment considering how much this place had been talked up.  

The guy working the counter seemed to be in a rush even when there was no line, I guess my relaxed ordering speed was interrupting his star trek on DVD.  For a better experience just buy a pack of cheap hot dogs from a market and see how far you can fit one into your eye socket.


sidenote: I was just told by the friend I proofread this too that I am being "sassy" and I had to reiterate:  "I have never hated a place so much that seeing positive reviews made me even more disgusted"
I don't see what's so special about this place.  Its all hype. Its just fucking hot dogs how great can it get.

How could one not love Top Dog? The only legitimate response to this is that the time is not 1:30AM. This is the perfect place to get your fill late at night. 

Tip#1: Don't forget to order correctly...unless you like being yelled at. 
Tip#2: There are two chickens on the menu. So saying chicken isn't enough.

I think the best thing about my living at Unit 1 my freshman year at cal would have to be its proximity to Top Dog.  Outsiders won't know why hot dogs have all us locals and Cal grads all giddy but that's only because they havent tried the perfection that is Lemon Chicken.

Everyone has their own fav top dog.  Mine just happens to give you the nastiest, stinkiest burps known to mankind afterwards. Seriously. I unleashed one in my friends car one night after grabbing Top Dog and he almost passed out.

Best when piled high with onions and ketchup/mustard.

Yes, the hot dogs are amazing.  However after my experience last Saturday, I can't give this place any more than one star:
Basically I ordered a hot dog and asked for water. I need to update this, not because the sausages are any less delicious, but because the guy behind the counter was nauseatingly rude to people who were stopping in for sausages in the midst of their sunny saturday afternoon strolls.  Allow me to state my case:

1.  You don't call somebody's grandpa a waste of space just because he didn't know what he wanted the moment he stepped up to the door.  Especially when his grandkids are with him.  

2.  A condescending "theeeere ya go" after someone places their order after 3.7 seconds of deliberation is wildly uncalled for.  

3. You don't fly off the handle at a mom with three grade schoolers in tow because she called your offerings "dogs"  instead of "sausages."  So maybe its technically incorrect to call a linguiça a dog, but the place IS called "top dog,"  not "top sausage," and a mom with three little ones frankly has more important things to worry about.     

The place was crowding up with families when I was there, people coming in with a good mood to get a tasty top-dog, and the guy at the grill (who kept on calling it "my store" when he was berating people) managed to infect everyone there with his stress and tension.  Even though it was  sunny day, we scowled for three blocks after we left.  

Rudeness for rudeness' sake doesn't fly anywhere. Not in south bronx, not in the outskirts of Beijing (both much grittier places where meanness might command respect), and certainly not in sunny, family-filled Berkeley.  This wasn't a display of the admirably strong political views posted all over the store (which I appreciate),  it was just gratuitous, senseless meanness that, in my view, makes it a business not worth soliciting. 

I'm not your typical sensitive type.  Just read my other reviews.  But I do take offense when sweet mommas and grandpas are belittled needlessly in front of their kids and grandkids.  Imagine being six and hearing someone say mean things to your mom.  Or grandpa.  It doesn't matter who they are or what they're grilling. It's just wrong. 

I'm taking my money and my cravings for well-garnished things-on-buns elsewhere.

Hmmmm....I usually write all of my reviews in the same way (btw, I think I'm funnier in real life than in my reviews), so let's mix it up this time with a story!

One night, not too long ago, after a movie at the Metreon...

Friend 1:  Dude, I'm hungry again...dinner sucked.
Me:  Haha...yeah, me too.  Where should we go?
Friend 1:  Let's go to Berk and get some Top Dog!  I am dying for a Kielbasa.
Me:  Ohhh....I could go for a Lemon Chicken or a Hot Link right now.
Friend 2:   Are you serious?  That far?
Me:   It's not even that far...and you're not even driving!
Friend 2:  But it's just a hot dog...
Me:  Whoa, hold up...they're sausages ok?  It's classier.
Friend 1:  Haha.  It's true.
Friend 2:  What the hell...why are we going out there?  Just get the chilli dog at Mel's...it's right there.

*dead silence*

Friend 2:   Okay fine, you're right...not the same thing.  But there's a De-
Friend 1:   Don't say it...
Friend 2:   -nny's...
Me:  Haha...he said it!
Friend 1:  Wait....have you even been to Top Dog before?
Friend 2:   Well, not really...
Me:   Ha!  So we're going then.

*20 minutes later*

Friend 1:  OMG, this kielbasa is SO GOOD.
Me:   Haha...I can't believe you bought two of the same.
Freind 1:  What?  You got two.
Me:  Yeah, but at least mine are different.  Plus, I'm saving one for tomorrow...NOT for about three minutes from now...
Friend 1:  Whatever, It's like college.
Me:  You didn't even go to Berkeley...
Friend 1:  Anyways...so (Friend 2), what do you think?
Friend 2:  Okay, the chicken apple is pretty good...
Friend 1:  See?  Aren't you glad we dragged you here?
Friend 2:  Wait, I'll be right back.
Me:  I guess he wants another one for the road.

* Five minutes later *

Friend 1:  OMG I'm so full right now.
Me:  Told you...
Friend 1:  So what did you get this time?
Friend 2:  Chicken apple, Hot Link, Brat, and Lemon Chicken
Me:  You got...four?
Friend 2:  Huh?  Oh, no...I bought a dozen.  Oh hey, you guys want to BBQ tomorrow?  I want to eat more of them.

The moral of the story?  Be like pre-Top Dog Friend #2...you just have to try it out when you're in Berkeley.  Then, you just might end up like post-Top Dog Friend #2...a much happier person (minus the dozen sausages/buns...maybe).  Top Dog is probably the best hot dog (I mean sausage) joints in the Bay Area until someone can point me to a better one.  And the best part?  IT'S CHEAP AND OPEN LATE!

Despite actually attending college some 200+ miles south of here, I do have some drunk undergrad memories of this place. After all, we did have some geek friends in common at UC Berkeley. More interesting than that, however, is that I was well into my mid- to late twenties before I actually appreciated the East Bay institution known as a Top Dog.

OK, there are both Top Dogs and C/Kasper's (can someone tell me the damn difference between the K and the C dogs?!)...and I love them both differently, but equally.

Anyway, my current "Michelle S. Couch-Surfing Homecoming Tour" has landed me in Berkeley this week. And let me tell you, these fine hot dogs taste just as delicious when you're a responsible adult as they do when you're a drunk, degenerate, undergrad. And the RC Cola somehow tastes better than actual American Coke. 

Notice how I specified American. No soda trumps Mexican Coke.

So, I was super happy that my friend cancelled lunch yesterday because I had this instead. They sure don't make hot dogs like these back East. 

And for the record, chicken apple is my favorite. :)

Definitely deserves a spot on anyone's best cheap eats in the Bay Area list - $3 flat gets you one of a dozen high quality sausages served on a sesame roll.  They keep it simple - you get the sausage and roll and then customize it to your liking at the condiments bar.   There's one vegetarian sausage and a new sausage: tandoori chicken - oooh, that sounds good.

I had the Louisiana Hot Link (made with pork & beef) with three kinds of mustard, chopped onions and sauerkraut.  Before I took my first bite, I caught a wonderful whiff of "grilled" meat.  The sesame roll is soft but slightly crunchy from the grilling.  Yum.  The sausage isn't that spicy but it's definitely juicy and rich in flavor.  The roll gives you plenty of room to pile on the condiments. Scrumptious.  

The condiment bar has Beaver Russian hot mustard (highly recommended - slight sweet and powerful), Morehouse stoneground mustard, Morehouse yellow mustard, ketchup, onions, relish and kraut.  They also sell drinks and potato salad.

The ambiance is perfect for a hole in the wall sausage joint.  You can see the grill and hear the dogs sizzling.  The surf music, limited menu, stools, and low prices all add to the appeal of the place.  The sausages are superb but not as fancy as the ones at Rosamunde (no wild boar here).  I think that actually adds to the Top Dog charm.  They're much faster than Rosamunde as well.  Great bun, great sausage, you customize it, $3, open till late - no wonder this place is popular.

True fans can buy a Top Dog shirt or cap for $15.

Top Dog's FAQs (Frequently Asked Questions )

Question:  Oh shoot, all I got is $3 bucks and I'm famished.  What do I do?
Answer:  Top Dog All Beef Frankfurter.

Question:  Does Top Dog have German food?  
Answer:  Ya ya, its a Bockwurst (1/2 pork and 1/2 veal = all tasty).

Question:  Buon Giorno, where can I find some late night italian food?
Answer:  Top Dogs Calabrese (all pork seasoned with paprika, chili, and fennel).

Question:  "I'm stuntin' like my daddy" and she's gonna "lick-lick-lick-lick it like a lollipop".  How can I eat and pay homage to Lil Wayne's hometown?
Answer:  Git yo'self a hizzle linkizzle (Hot Link) at T-Dizzle!

Question:  Let's eat healthy, salad perhaps?
Answer:  Top Dog has potato salad, lemon chicken (low salt and low fat), bird dog (turkey, cilantro, and peppers), and the wienie (veggie with wheat, soy, tofu and chili).

Last Question:  Where can I get a delicious hot dog for a few bucks?
Simple Answer:  Top Dog.

SNAP!  No, I'm not one of those people who use "snap" as a way to refer to cool things.  Snap! is the noise you make when you bite into one of Top Dog's wieners.  I love crunchy wieners.

Their original Top Dog and Calabrese are my favorites so far.  I love how the Top Dog wiener doesn't fit the bun because that's how hot dogs should be: more wiener, less bun.  The Calabrese sausage has a mild, but tasty spiciness to it.  I have a pretty high tolerance for spicy foods, so I've definitely gotta try their Louisiana hot link.  After hearing people rave about their Lemon Chicken dog, I tried it and wasn't impressed.  Not hearty enough and too healthy for me.

If I lived closer to Top Dog and was hosting a BBQ, there's no doubt I would shell out a significantly greater amount of money on their wieners, instead of their cheaper counterparts you find at supermarkets.

I went with a few friends and we'd been warned. I felt like Costanza... I was super prepared and still felt nervous. Then we had an Elaine in our group. 4 stars for Top Dog!

How has it been i have yet to review Top Dogs after living in Berkeley for over five years?  Welcome to Top Dog, a Berkeley institution since my father was going to law school in panchos and flip flops.

Stoners, drunkies, and night owls unite over the additional option of late night munching.  Top Dog stays open late into the night to feed your rumbling and over the legal limit tummies serving up some excellet dogs.  From a classic Bratwurst to hot links to the local favorite of chicken apple, nothing says "good morning" like a 2am bite into tube filled goodness wrapped in toasted buns served with the venerable classics of mustard onions, jalepenos and the balancing sweetness of relish.

Do you want a Coke with that?  Hell to the no!  They don't serve the evil corporation Berkeley is known to disdain.  It's all RC Cola here.  Say what you want about this d-list cola, it reminds me of my grandmas house and how she stacked the stuff in the corner by the dining table because she would stock up when on sale.  Delicious.

Are you a tourist?  Then don't stand at the counter and ponder over the menu (i mean, really... there are like 8 items in total).  The efficient and hard hitting men behind the counter will give you about five seconds to order before moving on to the next customer, but not before providing you with a sarcastic pep talk to not waste their time.  It's serious business here.  After all, as Anthony Bourdain would say, is there anything better than meat in tube form?  No, i dont think so either.

I might be one of few non-berkeley students to rate this place so you should trust my opinion more. 

Top Dog is awesome.
My crazy bald friend and I drove up to Oakland from Los Angeles because we were craving Top Dog. We wondered if there was some kind of addictive substance in it that made us keep going back for more. 

Apparently, it's not just the sausage that was calling us, but the whole culinary experience of devouring those juicy sausages. When we got there after a long drive, we sat, ordered, and hungrily waited for our perfect sausages. The liberal newspaper clippings and strange workers always provide for amusement until we get our hot dogs in our greedy little hands. The workers will tell you that contrary to popular belief, sausages are not bad for you at all. One lady told us that she ate three sausages a day! Now, that's just crazy.

Anyway, I love the hot link (especially after a night of drinking) and the Kielbasa is just an awesome squirt in your mouth. 

I'd have to say in terms of quality, Rosamunde's is the best but a Top Dog experience is always a fun experience. We decided not to buy the frozen packs. It just wouldn't be the same without actually being there to experience it.

I have not been back to Top Dog since my college days when I thought $2.75 was very expensive for a hot dog when I could buy and cook my own. 

But this time, I returned with a friend, and it is a good deal in comparison to all this other food out there. The guy was also very cool. I tried their calibrese and linguica, while my friend had her favorite lemon chicken. It was all simply delicious.

If you've waited in the ridiculously long line at Pink's in Hollywood, you definitely have to go try Top Dog up in Berkeley. It blows Pink's away.

Lemon chicken, kielbasa, bratwurst, bockwurst, chicken apple sausage all grilled up and served on a warm toasty sesame bun.  Holy crap I was in meat heaven.  It was also where my love of sauerkraut was born.    

Not the cleanest hole in the wall, but worth it just to feel/hear/taste the delicious snap of the first bite of one's Top Dog.

So I'm a vegetarian.  That limits me to exactly one kind of top dog -- the vegetarian dog.  The vegetarian dog just isn't that special.  If you aren't vegetarian, this place is probably fantastic, but if you are, Top Dog isn't anything special.

Does anything else really need to be said about this place?

Great food. Great prices. Great service. Great place. 

The buns alone are worth it, let alone the amazing quality of the dogs. 

They catered our wedding and they were remarkably easy to work with. Best Ever.

worth the wait!
i love top dog!!

One of the few times I wouldn't mind walking around with a ton of sloppy  mustardy and ketchupy goodness on my face since the food is so damn good. Quick and tasty, & totally the best way to go.

Also surprising that I touched a Polish sausage, though being Polish myself I dread those things. However, Top Dog's were really something great.
The best hot dog shack in the world.  Period.  Always.  A must-try on any trip to Berkeley.

i live a block away and can't stop going here. one of the few businesses actually open past 10pm in this city. super quick service, quality of sausages are unparalleled (my favorite is chicken apple), no room for dawdling so you can get your food and be on your way. can't get enough top dog.

i don't even like hot dogs and sausages, but top dog changed my mind.  this is the BEST sausage joint ever!!!!! cheap, no line, quick, deliciousness.... i don't know what else to say...better than pink's, costco hot dogs, dodger dogs!!!  i had the chicken apple and it was absolutely amazing.  you add toppings yourself, and there is basically no seating inside so you'd either have to take it togo or enjoy it on the sidewalk with the homeless.

would come back in a FLASH!!

When I moved out to San Diego I met someone who would eventually become a very good friend and not too long ago he asked me about Top Dog in Berkeley....2 weeks later we flew out to the Bay Area(only cus it was thxgiving break tho) and my San Diego friend went back to San Diego with 10 hotdogs in a cooler.....nuff said.

As a full time New Yorker this is a great stand alone hot dog. No crazy toppings like Pinks in LA or Crif Dog in NYC...just a plain dog.

Great 2am drunk food and I am glad this is one of the few places that are open that late! When I used to live in the East Bay my friends and I would always hit up his place after going to bars. Every time I come back to the East Bay to visit I make sure I get some Top Dog!
The best Hot dogs in the Bay area. All their dogs are the bomb, but if i were to pick my top choice would be the lemon chicken.

Now living in Los Angeles I recently Yelped a review for "Pink's Hot Dog Stand."

Pink's is "the dog" down here.  The lines often stretch down the block, and there's a good chance those in line might be treated to seeing some celeb drive up and get a dog or two.  But as I wrote in my review, Pink's is less than squat when going dogo-a-dogo against a "Top Dog."  I doubt they're even in the same USDA food group!  

Many, many years ago my older sis attended UC, and I'd drive up there to soak in some college atmosphere.  (Sadly I didn't attend college; I went to San Jose State.)  While there she exposed me to the seamy Berkeley underbelly, including Barrington Hall (where she existed for a few semesters) and, of course, Top Dog.  

It's a pleasure to say that since then nothing much has changed at Top Dog.  Why mess with perfection?

Well, one thing has changed, the price.  Back then a Top was only 75 cents!  I knew I should of stocked up when I had the chance!

Unfortunately I don't have the opportunity to frequent Top Dog much anymore, but we try to make a quick stop there a priority whenever we visit the Bay Area.

Long live TOP DOG!

this place it a no brainer.... been eating them since 82'  as a high school kid running around with the crew tring to crash frat parties... top dog was always great after drining late night... but dam these bomb hot dogs taste great drunk or sober... had some for lunch and yep hella good.  ever see the line here at 230 am?

If you're gonna get a hot dog, where else would u go BUT top dog???

It definitely hits the spot if you're looking for a midnight snack.  I don't usually come here by myself for dinner because I would have to order 2 or more of them!  However, if I'm with another and we split an entree then we'll each also get our own top dog :).

I think the chicken flavors are kinda bland.  My favorites are the Hot Link, Kielbasa, and Linguica.  The Linguica is pretty weird tho so if you're feeling daring check it out, but I don't guarantee anything (all I know is that I like it :).

Whoever started this place had a genius idea. Good joint that requires low maintenance, but offers all the services of a legit restaurant.

You kind of just walk up and order as there is no formal line. It could easily get over crowded in the small shop, but the worker is pretty good at remembering who ordered what.

The food def lives up to the hype. I actually was a fattie and had two dogs. I think the most notable thing was their bread. It's not a regular hot dog bun. It's more like a sandwich bun you would see at quiznos. Regardless of what it resembles, it makes the place stand out. I had the Bird Dog and the Hot Link. Just so you know, the hot link is actually HOT as the name suggests... I failed to make the connection and suffered the consequences of chugging my quickly's to put out the fire.

If I went to Cal, I'd be going here all day, errday

If you're in line, be ready to order within one and a half seconds when called upon. If you hesitate and look unsure, the guy behind the counter will scowl at you and move on to the next person's order while you scratch your chin, peruse the menu, and look like you're contemplating the meaning of life.

I am amazed by the efficiency of Top Dog's [usually one man] operation. Hot dogs of all kinds for a flat $3, simple and straightforward. No tickets, no receipts. I give cash, move aside, then get handed my food when it's ready in three to four minutes. There's three or four other pending orders, all handled by that one guy, and my order always comes out right every time.

Served until 2am.
Top Dog saved the day again with hot wieners at 2 in the morning. Thank You Top Dog!

Everyone has said everything that needs to be said.

But I LOVE this place.

It doesn't even bother me that the guy behind the counter takes my money and handles the hot dogs all with the same hands without gloves.

But the food is sooo good, you don't care.

I think this place stays open til 1am... which is also great.

When I'm in the area, I usually drop in a for quick "dog" bite... The price is right, and there are many dogs to choose from.

I haven't been bitten by a bad one yet.

I really can't think of anywhere else to go when I'm in the mood for a hot dog (although I do enjoy the ones at Costco---before they took away the kraut...)

Love the kraut and all the other fixins at Top Dog!
I like how they're mean to me. Good dogs.

Gotta love these dogs.. beef, kielbasa, lemon chicken, smoked chicken apple, bird dog, hot link .. oh my.  (My fav's are the bird and top dogs.. with sauerkraut, please).  WARNING:  Avoid The Weiner (veggie).  As tempting as the name sounds, it does NOT satisfy.  Trust me, no Weiner for you.
