Top Dog is one of those things you specifically begin to crave once you've had a taste.

Apart from the food's ability to always hit the spot, you can pile on as much sauerkraut as you want, and with great late hours, it makes the perfect drunk food, though you may be depriving yourself of the full sensory experience there... My favorite flavor thus far has been the mango habanero, and unfortunately, I think it's only a special and not a regular menu item (I could be wrong). If you have time and aren't shuffling out of there as soon as you grab your meal, it's also fun to read the walls, which are plastered with more libertarian propaganda than a tea party HQ.
Trusty.

i eat here everytime im in SF.
and get the SAME thing every single time:

hot link + ketchup + tons of relish.

mmmm im drooling. *tear
lets just say...i drove to berkeley from SF twice a week for the entire summer just to have their amazing hot links. (i gained about 5 lbs that summer) It was sooooooo worth it.

leaving the bars at closing in berkeley, you have but two options: pizza or hot dogs. um, yes please and thank you, but i'll take top dog every single time. 

nothing like shoving your way through a bunch of drunks, screaming your order at some ornery old dude (although they're never ornery with me, since i've been knowin' 'em for years and all...), putting too much mustard and ketchup on your chicken apple and... stuffing it all into your mouth. that first bite, when you crack it open and the juice squirts out... man, i know this is starting to sound sexual, but it's really just drunk food transcending all else.

i love top dogs. 

also, since i like telling stories sometimes:

one time i got waaaaaasted at the bar and headed over to my friend diana's house. diana lived in that apartment building next to top dog at the time, the one on whose steps people often sit while shoving dogs in their faces, you know it. wasted, wasted, wasted. upon arriving at their house, i took it upon myself to begin making frequent high-pitched monkey noises and drinking cheap branndy right from the bottle, in gulps! 

i was very much even more wasted than when i left the bar when i stumbled (yes) into the kitchen and noticed a banana on the table. BANANA! 

q: what could go better with high pitched monkey "OOOOK"s and brandy than a banana?

a: nothing!

okay, right, so i commence stuffing the banana into my face, alternately swallowing some bites and spitting others (100% pure monkey style) into the astonished faces of other people, who were much less drunkenly also hanging out in diana's apartment.

moments later, i was on the front porch, throwing up all over the steps.

moments after that, i was commanding my friend eric to go and get me a chicken apple top dog, saying it was the only thing that would make me feel better. he complied, and it really did work.

i slept like a drunken baby that night.

(p.s. i used to work here, and just for informational purposes, i have to tell you that there's a handwritten sign in the bathroom that says "IF IT'S YELLOW, LET IT MELLOW. IF IT'S BROWN, FLUSH IT DOWN." i'll never forget that.)

My first Top Dog experience occurred during college when I was visiting our local Fraternity Chapter. Whenever I'm in Berkeley, I always make it a point to stop and get a hot dog. There are several options to go with along with several options to top the dog off with. Watch out for the Russian mustard!

Hard to go wrong with anything on the menu. I always like the brat, polish and the regular top dog.

A nice perk is having RC cola on tap. Very hard to find in CA.

The only downside is there isn't much room to eat inside because of the small location. There is limited seating inside or you can just eat out on the sidewalk or as you stroll the streets.

This used to be a 5-star review. Since they bumped their prices up to $3.00 a dog, it no longer deserves that fifth star.

Every time I come in (probably drunk), I get a Brat and a Lemon Chicken, each with just a little sauerkraut and a kiss of spicy mustard. Totally makes my night, and talking to all the fellow drunks/stoners lined up outside at 3am on a Saturday is a hoot.

a no.brainer: top dog gets obviously gets a 5.star yelp, even despite my rule of trying to reserve 5.star yelps for like "nicer" restaurants, like "fine dining" establishments.  honestly, when i was a student at berkeley, even though i loved top dog hot dogs, i was a little uneasy about how it was more expensive than buying cheap hot dogs like from the vietnamese $1 shop in the asuc underground (does that even exist anymore) and weren't like superfilling.  however, later, i learned to enjoy top dog as a tasty, gourmet snack more than as meal.  still, i guess oftentimes, people just buy more than one dog in order to make a meal, and that's fine too.  the price really isn't so bad, considering they are really tasty hot dogs served in deliciously hot, toasty buns.  i guess i have even more of a appreciation of the value now that i live in the silicon valley because food in general is cheaper up in berkeley.

of course, the fact that top dog (especially the original, durant location) is open late is a major plus.  after all, the only reason i was inspired to yelp about top dog after all these years is because i was up in berkeley last night djing a party for haas business school students at the hotel shattuck plaza and needed to get a bite to eat after the party.  i got a $3.25 mango habanero chicken sausage.  perfect!

recently, i noticed fake top dogs here and there.  i noticed on yelp that, down in socal somewhere, there's a "berkeley dog."  obviously, they're copying top dog.  i'm sure nothing beats the original.

Review number 530 just to prove a commitment to the savory goodness. 

PRESSURE. 

UNDER PRESSURE.

ahem...minor musical interlude. 

any case, ordered the standard top dog. it was:

a) juicy?
b) crispy and warm?
c) all beef goodness?
d) all of the above?

all of the above bitches. i added ketchup and onions. (these are important on normal less flavorful hotdogs, but i think it actually quashed some of the original flavor of the meat so you really don't need it. take a bite and then decide. 

important notes someone should have told me before i went to the adventure that is top dog. 

1) there is no line. so just fucking speak up and say, hey I want "X".
the guy is cool but unless a lot of people start filling in, he's focused on the ones he's cooking already. ( i have a hard time opening my mouth in these situations -- hope you are more brave)

2) you need cash. it's really cheap and there's an atm on the way to it on telegraph. you only need a little cash, nearly everything is 3 bucks. soda is less than 2. 

3) it's not the all saving all grace of God hotdog. but it's a good hot dog. so accept it as a hotdog and enjoy it. 

4) they do have vegan hotdogs. they do have german, italian, chicago style, and the other ethnic groups that have decided to attempt work in the hot dog.


(whisper) under pressure. boom

I don't remember many things when I'm drunk. Scratch that; this particular night, I remember close to nothing. But I remember coming here hella drunk and getting a hot dog, so it must have been pretty damn good because that's the only thing I really remember about that epic, epic night.

I also remember dropping it after I had eaten half, and being hella sad. Apparently I tried to eat it again. LOL. This could only mean that that hot dog was reaaaaaaaaally damn good!

i fucken love you.

that's all i have to say.

i lied. top dog and a hot link.

god damn i love you.

i lied again.

RUSSIAN MUSTARD?!?! eat that shit when your sinuses are clogged, it'll clear it up and taste delicious.

Top Dog is just your average wiener. Have you ever seen the "Soup Nazi" episode of Seinfeld? Well, subtract the soup and add hot dogs and you have half of the Top Dog staff.  If they yell at me one more time about my wiener selection I might just flip over their onion and relish containers. 

The food is okay when you are drunk but they need to clean up the transient traffic outside. After being harassed by the Top Dog staff while ordering the last thing someone wants to deal with are the homeless wizards congregating outside--who havent showered since the Nixon administration.

+1 hot dog selection
-1 staff
-1 transients

Oh man oh man o shevitz...

In the not too distant past I lived in Berkeley just around the corner from this place.  And the place ultimately lead to me being kicked out of my apartment, so that's why it didn't get 6 stars.

It went down somethin like this.  After a long night of drinkin corn syrup, me and a friend went to a top dog.  Well he was from outta town and is also a glutton, so he wanted to know what to get.  I told him that everything was good.

So this fat piece of crap orders four hot dogs.  Well, not to be outdone, I order four as well.  Well the guy behind the counter is eggin us on... why don't you just order the whole damn menu?

So 35 dollars worth of hot dogs later, the guy gives us a free top dog post card that says "I ate the wall" and has a bunch of anarchist bull shit on it.

We get back, and start doin' shots of hot dog.  No we didn't grind them up in the blender (I usually reserve that treatment for the body parts of my victims), but we cut em half, and cheers'ed each one of them and were screamin "TOPPPPPPP DOOOOOOOOAAAAAAGGG" after each bite.

Anyway, after that night I was asked to "think about finding a new place"...

So for $3 per dog, I have to say I'm quite impressed. Top Dog is another reason why Berkeley students/residents are lucky to have places like this that are open late. After hearing much hype about this place, I finally got to see what all the fuss was about over this. Now I'm writing the 605th review for this place, and I heavily approve of Top Dog. 

The wait was short at 11 in the evening. I walk in to see the worker grilling the dogs, playing heavy metal on his boombox, and watching Letterman. He kinda had a douchey attitude in asking us what we wanted, but I guess that's what happens when you're working that late and you're the only one working the stand. 

I ordered the Top Dog and the smoked chicken apple. I topped both with onions, ketchup, and deli mustard. Fair warning: use the deli mustard very lightly. As good as the hot dogs were, my nostrils were under fire with every bite. It's not that I was thirsty or anything, its just I felt like a rocket was going to shoot out of my head and my nostrils were the exhausts pipes. 

Other than that, the dogs were amazing. The Top Dog was juicy and well complimented with the grilled bun. I saved the smoked chicken apple since it seemed more flavorful than the Top Dog. Boy was I right. Each bite had a hint of apple to it, but not too overbearing. I also sampled the spicy dog my friend ordered, and it was well... rather spicy. I think I'll actually get that next time. I'm sure I'm going to try this again, and I'd like to give the other dogs a try. I was very content with my food, and I look forward to stuffing my face here again... sans the deli mustard.

I am reviewing top dog even though i'm still in my jammies at home...i  am heading for berkeley a little later...uncle bruce is going with me.

i am driving from san mateo to get dogs from td...even though there is a costco within spitting distance....i love the dogs a td..i will order three and pile 'em high with relish,mustard and kraut...can't wait....

My favorite hot dog place of all time!  

I always get 3 spicy hot links, put a little ketchup, a little hot mustard and a little bit of sour kraut.  Dooooood!

Little known fact, they have a Top Dog in Oakland inside of a 24 hour Longs Drugs, although the Top Dog closes at 9pm!  I used to get my fix there.
The perfect food to snack on or get as a pick-me-up.  The sausages are perfectly juicy, and the buns are perfectly toasted.  Pinks is nothing compared to this place.

the best hot dog i've ever had! my favorite is the chicken apple...

the hot link is spiiiicy and oh so good. gets you by surprise. the kielbasa and bird dog (turkey) are pretty good as well. 

so nice after a night out. i miss this place!

5 stars is not enough for this joint./establishment.  You have to experience the great dogs,,,,,lots and lots of choices of dogs from kilbasa, polish, german, top dog, bockwurst....on these sesame buns....boy my mouth is watering.....Also, this is a place that really lets you feel like you are in Berkeley.

This is a great Berkeley institution (although there are now locations throughout the Bay Area now). There is nothing finer than ordering a couple of dogs and chatting with the Top Dog grill master while your dogs and buns are freshly grilled.

My personal favorites are the Lemon Chicken and the Bockwurst and they always seem to hit the spot. The 'grill masters' also have a great way of multitasking -- taking multiple orders, grilling, and collecting money. Not a job for any average Bear! May Top Dog continue its successful ways!

Lemon Chicken baby!!!!  Used to come here after partying in San Francisco back in our partying days and you could tell we loved this place because we lived in SF, partied in SF, then drove out to Berkeley just to get a Hot Dog and then drove back to SF....  

A little crazy but we did it pretty often so yes, we all agreed that this was some damn good grub after the club.....

There are so many reviews for this place...one more won't hurt. Haha.

I tried this place today and I think it's pretty good. I had a frankfurter, but wish I would've gotten a calabrese. Actually, now that I take a closer look at their menu, I wish I couldve tried all the dogs. haha. I did have a taste of my friend's lemon chicken, and omg... I'm craving one now. 

I'll definitely be back for more topdog.

ehhh... not that great! LOTS of hype, and way to hippie-ish for me. I woudl say that this is definitely a freshmen and tourist spot. The dogs aren't bad, but nothing out of this world, the staff are full of them selves and not friendly. (I know that is the point, but its stupid.) The chicken apple dog is pretty good though. 

I would rather go to LaBo or the Asian Ghetto...

MY GO-TO DISH: Chicken Apple Dog.

Apple Chicken Hot Dog, I love thee.  This place is delicious.  That is why I always battle my fear of the Top Dog guy to get myself one of his delicious hot dogs.

To the reviewer that equated him to the Soup Nazi of Seinfeld, I totally agree!  You need to know what you want, say it straight out, and get out of the man's way!  He writes nothing down, just memorizes it all.  Maybe that's why he gets all pissy if someone tries to mess with his mojo.

I once was suckered into going back into the shop to order my friend another hot dog.  What I fool I was for saying "Excuse me..excuse me..."  He simply looked up and yelled "Get out!"

But how can I hate a man that brings me such delicious joy?  Just make sure you know what you want when you order and don't even think twice about changing your mind.  You won't regret what you order anyway.  All the sausages are pretty delicious.

I like 'em fruit-flavored:
lemon chicken & chicken apple FTW.

but like all undersized weiners, OVERRAAAAATED...

If I were a guy, I'd feel pretty insecure...I mean worried that I wouldn't be full, so guys, order two.

I just re-visited this place for the first time in years and it was AWESOME! The folks working the counter were kind, attentive and not flustered by the luch time rush. The vegetarian weenie totally satisfied a yearning I haven't been able to sate for months! It was so inexpensive I bought lunch for my whole office and they raved about the all-beef dogs I got for them. Keep up the great food & service!

UC Berkeley is getting ready to play their opening game this upcoming weekend. 

Can't wait for football and Top Dog. What a combo.

Even though I'm a newbie to the Berkeley area, I was quickly informed that Top Dog was a place that I couldn't pass up.  Their hot dogs are super affordable (about 3-4 dollars for a decently sized hot dog) and they have a pretty good variety of hot dogs.  Being the indulgent eater that I am, I immediately ordered the regular Top Dog with Chili and Cheese.  The chili DOES have beans in it, but it was very tasty.  The toppings complimented the hot dog and the soft bun very well, however, my only complaint is that neither the chili nor the hot dog itself were hot enough to melt the shredded cheese that was sandwiched between the two.  Weird?  I mean, I get it; it's not 7/11, but melted cheese is a must on a chili cheese dog in my opinion.  

Whether or not the dog's temperature was hot enough to please my internal thermometer, it was definitely a pleasing meal for my taste buds (and my hips, I'm sure.)  By the way, be aware that Chili and Cheese are two separate and additional costs to the hot dogs.. Still incredibly inexpensive.  I'm a fan.

Still the best hot dogs ever! Over the years, I've tried everything on the menu. My favorite was and still is the lemon chicken. Not sure when they raised their prices from $2.50 to $3. But its still a great deal, and an excellent option for a late night snack. 

Top Dog has really ruined hot dogs for me forever. I can't eat one without thinking, "meh, this isn't as good as Top Dog..."

I'm reluctant to give this place any more than 3 stars because it just wasn't as great as everyone makes it out to be.  Sure their buns are toasted and the hot mustard is definitely a plus, but I gotta say, even Costco's hot dog is better.  Maybe this is one of those places that you can only appreciate after a night of drinking, but since I visited during lunch time, it just didn't shake my world.

I miss this place!

It's been a couple of years (won't tell you how many) since my hubby and I graduated from Cal.  Top Dog is definitely one of the most missed places in the area!  Every year we try to go up at least twice to see old friends and the campus.  And we always squeeze Top Dog in between our meals!    

We heart the apple chicken!  I've tried other stuff but always come back to apple chicken!  We always put lots of condiments and it's just sooo yummmmmm!  Ohhh, I'm making myself hungry!

Top Dog, Top Dog, please don't ever change!

Snack haven for CAL students..
For the short time i attended school at CAL, i used to come and eat here 3 times a week..

Garlic Brokwurst..
Lemon chicken..
Chicken Apple..
and my personal favorite.. da HOT LINK..

for all you folks who cant decide, just order the top dog
and for you vegetarians, order the veggie dog.. its pretty damn good...

think they use colombo bread and they toast it just enough so it gives the dog that perfect crunch..

It was only a few short years after Top Dog in Berkeley opened in 1966 that I/we discovered the best hot dogs west of Chicago.  I remember the National Guard marching down Telegraph avenue toward campus and thinking, 'save Top Dog.'

My personal favorate is the Calabrese (Italian) and my wife loves the Kielbasa (Polish).  The buns are soft and grilled on the same grill with the dogs so you get some good flavors going.

Seating is very limited and the people who work there like to talk politics, sex, or any other topic you wish to be challenged on.  You will meet some very interesting people here and really like the dogs.

Everyone knows Top Dog is amazing, but here is a hint:

Ask them for uncooked dogs!!!  We brought home 6 uncooked dogs with their delicious buns and it only costs like $8!  It is cheaper, just as delicious, and you can eat at home and put on whatever you'd like!!!

Changed my life forever...

Alright, I confess, I've been a Cal student for the last 4 years, and just two days ago, I finally tried Top Dog. My bf forced me. And, I liked it!

The lady who was making our hot dog was a total A-hole! After requesting to chicken apples, we noticed the sign for the daily special--mango something--so we quickly changed our order. "Sorry, can we change one of the chicken apples to the daily special?" No reply. The other costumers looked at us and we all shrugged. She then saw me holding a camera and immediately stuck her hand in my face and said, "No pictures." Uhh..don't worry, I dont want a picture of a fat lady, but of my bf, but thank you, I'm flattered if you are. The lady then threw paper bags and napkins at used when we asked her if we can have them to go. And, when I said threw, I really mean physically throwing. Half of the stack of paper bags she gave us fell on the floor and the other half landed all over the counter. Bf and I are nice people so we cleaned up the mess for her. No thank you from here. Not even eye contact. Uhh..You're welcome by the way. 

We left our hot dog on the kitchen counter for breakfast the next morning since we were full from dinner. The next morning, the hot dogs and buns were hard! We threw away the buns and sliced the hot dogs in half, microwaved them, and nom nom nom! They were yummmyyy! I wished I had the chance to try them when they were fresh..and perhaps, when I was a younger more innocent freshman.

$4 hot dogs are not my daily thing, but if you're up for it...why not? I would go here for a special treat and midnight snacking since they're open so late.

One bite of the Frankfurter at Top Dog and it brings back memories of the first hot dog I had in Queens NY.  Their hot links are great too.  Great hot dogs.  The guy Paul that works there is way cool.

Mmmm... hot dogs fresh off the grill!  Unlimited condiments!  All so delicious.  

The perfect place for a snack after a drunken night with friends.  

The place is really tiny and has two doors to go in.  They have a total of 4 stools to sit on.  It gets stuffed in there so the best thing to do is stand outside on the street.
Don't know what it is, but the dogs here are to die for. I always get the calabasa with loads of saurkraut. At $3 bucks a pop, not too cheap, considering I usually need to eat 3 to be full.

I'm yelpin for top dog.. because even though I just had a hotdog down in LA, im cravin top dog.. 

seriously, the best place for the best dog you will ever had.. kielbasa, top link, garlicchicken.. toasted bun?!?!?!?!? for almost no $.. why yes, i would apply to UC berkeley just so i could come here every day.

no place to sit, but so what.. just hang out and eat our dog outside. oh and then go to king pin across the st. for a donut hole.. and if you're really feelin it.. get a boba at the boba shop too.

top dog. you rule my world.

Not only is Top Dog the perfect way to end a good night, it's the first place you hit after frat row and it's all downhill. They have a menu for everyone from lemon chicken to the wienie, the veggie dog, which is surprisingly really good. They have all the toppings including spicy mustard and sauerkraut, as well as the usual ketchup, onions, and relish. There is a standing area to the side, but it's cramped and people normally stand outside. The cool weather in Berkeley makes the hot hot dog even better. 

The service is brisk and almost rude, but they're used to serving drunk people at 2AM and it's justified to an extent. There's almost always a line, but it generally moves fast and there are comics, cartoons, and newspaper articles to read all over the walls to keep you entertained. I'm not a big fan of hot dogs, but it's worth the wait.

$3 for one of THE BEST hot dogs you'll ever eat! 

I always order the Mango Habanero and it's always perfect! My friends always order the Hot Link (apparently the spice is addicting), so I'd suggest you try either one of those! You won't regret it! 

Let me tell you what makes Top Dog such a great place to grab a bite in Berkeley...
OPEN until 3am! "Whoooo!" Great for college students who either stay up studying and get hungry at weird hours of the night or for those who stay up drinking and have the beer munchies at 2:30 am! 
SUPER CHEAP! $3 flat for a hot dog! You can't beat that! Again, GREAT for college students since we all know college students are on a budget. 
QUICK SERVICE! You order in 3 seconds and you're out in 5 minutes! This is great because they always have lots of people, especially weekend nights! 
GREAT FOOD! The hot dogs are amazing! The bun is delicious. Plain and simple. You must try it!

Top Dog will never let you down- how can you go wrong with a delicious high-quality hot dog with all the fixings?  Its a win-win scenario no matter what you get and I have never been disappointed- good cheap dogs served by nice people- perfect.

everytime me and my friend hang out around telegraph, we just gotta get some top dogs. i love their keilbasa. i heard thier bird god is good so gotta try that next time. and you guys are right, even if there are know seats, this is the best top dog location.

I don't like hot dogs.  Top Dog serves grilled sausages - and they are fine, if I can say that about a sausage.

I used to eat here occasionally during college.  Now, when I travel to Oakland on business, I'll come over to Berkeley for Top Dog. 

I just love the Hot Link and sitting there and watching TV with the grill guy.

Top Dog sets the standard for hot dog stands for me.  I'm afraid to try other places because of the severe disappointment waiting me.

2:30 A.M. on a Friday night, Elisa C. and I decided to stop by this bad boy (or should I say...  BAD DOG? Ha ha ha) because we heard great things about it.

So, there's hella people in the place even at that time of night, but our orders are taken within five minutes of us standing there and in our hands not more than seven minutes later.  I quickly unwrap my garlic dog, put some onions in, and run outside just to unwrap it again to take my first delicious bite.

I ran outside alone out of excitement to finally have food in my hands, and my friend made fun of me when he saw me stuffing that hot dog in my mouth...  "Couldn't wait?"  I felt so fat.  But no, no I couldn't wait...  sigh.

A day later, I could still taste it in my mouth.  Not in a disgusting I-didn't-brush-my-teeth way or anything (because I did brush my teeth).  In a that-was-so-freaking-delicious-I-will-forever-remember-its-awesomeness way.

Kudos, Top Dog, you have won my heart.

EPIC HOTDOGS. I'm from so-cal and I've had my fair share from the hot dog community, but this blows the rest away. It's just epic. There's all kinds of meat and happiness there. Great place to stop by for quick good and cheap food.

This place is better than any in Chicago and New York. My favorite hot dog joint in the country. A plethora of choices: bratwurst, bockwurst, kielbasa, calabrese, linguiça, chicken apple, lemon chicken, louisiana hot link, ... need I say more? How about choice of russian mustard? And toasted buns from a local bakery? Only a little over 2 bucks a dog! The absolute best hot dogs in the country. An absolute staple during my undergrad years.

Great dogs, but Top Dog fanatics will be saddened to hear that their dogs have been replicated by several places across the bay in San Francisco. I must say that they were a main stay of my early years in Berkeley before I expanded my tastes and you can't really go wrong with any hot dog here.

I miss the days when they were cheaper though. It's usually a last resort to go to Top Dog now in my post-student days, but for the new students, it's a must-have experience.
Love the hot link.  Spicy, Delish.  Opens late, fit for late night cravings.

FIVE STARS!

The chicken apple and kelbasa were killer.

great dive for fast food. the cashier (+ host) was entertaining and the price is great.

definately want to go again.

Amazing dogs!!!! I love the garlic whatever it is.... love love love. Best place ever after a night out! 

SENSITIVE PATRONS BEWARE:

It's a dog eat dog world and this place is not for the shy people to patiently stand in line and wait their turns. It's more like a "hot dog bar" where you just get in there and yell out your order. Don't be afraid! It's worth swallowing your fears and speaking up to get the dog of your dreams!

I had forgotten all about this place that I used to visit a TON when I lived in Unit One, until... at a BBQ we had today, a friend of ours brought the dogs. They were absolutely spectacular. The good meaty flavor and texture in a dog rather than the smooth processed carbo-loaded hot dogs that they generally sell. It put my Costco 1.50 hot dog + drink to shame. Alas it is too far to get unless someone brings it down for a BBQ. But it brought back all sorts of nostalgia and delicious flavors.

Only bummers?  Parking and no where to sit.  Taste and cost wise though, you CANNOT beat this place.  Bockwurst and Chicken apple = win.  Love the fact that there is sourkraut (sp) and all the other usual condiment dressings right there behind you.  If you're in a rush and on a budget, this place can't be beat!

Great for a quick bite or late night eats. I always love bringing out of towners down to Top Dog for a late night eat or after coming home from a Giants game. Gotta go with the Lemon Chicken Dog each and every time I go.

Lemon Chicken 
For those who thought that a hot dog is just a hot dog..... go to top dog. Personally, I wasn't a big hot dog fan before trying this place out. The smell of mustard, ketchup, and radish ...gross. But Ive been converted! My freshman 5 ( instead of 15) was because of Top Dog. I had to limit myself to 4 a week to keep myself from obsessing.

i came here to visit an old friend in UC Berkeley and stopped by this joint to see what all the hype was about. to my surprise, the store was quite small and one guy was doing all the cooking. 

despite the long wait, the hot dog i ordered did not disappoint. i wanted to get in line again but then by the time i'd receive it, i would be eligible to cash in my retirement fund. jeezus, lol.

great spot for a quick bite if you can stand waiting a bit.

Cheap and open late!

My favorite is the Lemon Chicken + Krout + Ketchup.

A good deal if you're craving something fast, clean, and easy! EVERYONE has to try this if in Berkeley!

I use to hit up Top Dog for a midnight snack when I was in college. It's quite surprising that I didn't gain my freshman 15 during that first year, when I only lived about a block away from Top Dog on Durant. 

I love the Chicken Apple dog, although I always felt that it was a little small for the price in comparison to the other ones. The regular top dog is delicious as well. 

This place is what sustained me throughout freshman year dorm food.

This is an institution in Berkeley.  The meats are grilled right in front of you with the option to add an assortment of toppings. What makes this place worth the trip are the variety of sausages and links to choose from and their funky fillings.  This isn't really a sit-down place to eat.  It's more like grabbing a bite to eat and walk around town.

Each of their "dog" is $2.75 each, and there are many to choose from.  My favorite is the Kielbasa (polish hot dog).  This place kind of reminds me of the Soup Nazi...don't upset the man in charge of the orders, or else NO DOGS FOR YOU.

Bottom line:  Perfect for lunch, pre-game chow, late-night snack, or really anytime.

If your craving a hot dog, sorry I mean a sausage and it happens to be anytime between the hours of 11am and 2am this is the place for you.  You can't go wrong with Top Dog!  They have a couple more locations but this one is open the latest.  Grilled sausages on a warm sesame french bun.  Three different mustard to choose from with sauerkraut and onions.  The linguica is good with great red wine flavor and spices, but is a little dry. My go to is the Sicilian and the Hot Link.  The Sicilian is just an Italian sausage and has good flavor nothing special and the hot link I don't care for anymore but it's not bad.  But when you need a sausage could right and fast they are the place.
sooo good!!!...i like the regular top dog best...

OK I always try to hit up this joint when I go up north.  I dont know what it is about this place but I crave it when that bay chill hits me.  Is it the bucket of kraut and the different kinds of mustards?  Im not sure.  Is it the different sausages?  Still not sure.  I think it might be because you have to stand up outside to eat your sausage and have toppings fall to the sidewalk.  Or it might be listening to the blabbity blab blab of all the Berkeley freaks, oh so cool they all are.  All I know is that a Fat Slice or a Blondie Pizza compliment these dogs well.
If you're out in Berkeley and want to grab a bite Top Dog has the best hot dogs. I like the chicken apple, but everything is pretty good.

After the bf and I returned from Chicago, he planned a Chicago Pt. 2 for us. Top Dog was on the list (along with Zachary's). He knows I base my love for hot dogs on the "snap" of the casing and this place was perfect! Don't get me wrong, it's got nothing on my chardogs, but it's better than anything else I've tried in the bay. Plus, they grill your buns and there are free books to read while you wait! Anyone else notice how anarchist this place is?

After 4 years of Top Dog, heres my list of favorite dogs:
1. The HOT LINK: nommmmm. Louisiana hot and spicy sausage link... real spicy, real good!
2. The BIRD DOG: turkey, bell pepper, and cilantro... yummmm!
3. (The Special) Mango Habanero Chicken: sweet and spicy, very juicy! 

Top Dog will always have a special place in my heart. Sausage of your choice grilled at command on a seasoned iron flat top, served in a toasty sesame bun, and topped to your heart's desire with onions, relish, (sauerkraut, mustard,) and ketchup... its Berkeley's finest. The guys behind the grill can be moody and curse having to serve up rowdy drunk college students, but they are also witty and fun when you catch them in a good mood. I'll miss all this now that I'm gone, but I'm sure to stop back whenever I come visit!
Yummy toasty roll, garlic sausage was hot and grilled to perfection. Toppings bar is great, service was fast. Good solid hot dog joint.

My favorite hot dog place! The hot dogs are delicious! I really like the toasted bun as well. Yum! The top dog  frankfurter, with ketchup, mustard, and relish is all I need and I'm a happy camper.  Simple and reliable.

One drunken night, I ordered the chicken and apple sausage at Top Dog. Holy holy crap. First of all, there was no wait, and that was one darn diggity delicious dog.

So worth it. I can't remember what the price was, but wow, I'm definitely coming back here.

The first time i went there, My ex who is was with for a long ass time (almost 7 years) took me to Berkeley to try out the top dog's hot dogs,  he told me that the hot dogs is good, and said that i should try the lemon chicken or the smoke chicken apple. So be took me to this place and i've notice how small the place was, plus i'm short so i could see past the table thingy. I know right, me short. damn asian parents. lol jk

At first i thought it was just regular dogs that u buy them from a grocery store, but man i was wrong. 

The dogs were big and juicy (for a moment that doesn't sound right). I tried the lemon chicken, and the smoke chicken apple was good. but my most favorite is the smoke chicken apple. The price is very fair. I recommended that if your in Berkley and you wanted a hot dog. i suggest you go to TOP DOG. anywhere in Berkley that has its name. cause their dogs are delish! With a capital D!

I am so glad that my friend and I walked the distance to try this place! It was quite delicious! So, we had the turkey apple and I'm not going to lie, the place looked a little sketchy so I was a skeptic at first, but it really wasn't bad! It was crowded for a Monday night so that is always a good sign! 

The buns are what won me over!!! Love the sesame seeds and it was soft yet had a nice crispyness to the outside :) the turkey apple part was alright overall. I didn't know about the toppings so I just went with traditional ketchup so maybe that's why I didn't absolutely LOVE this place. I mean honestly, my $1.50 costco hot dog could be this amazing if only it had that HEAVENLY BUN! hahaha so yea... the moral of this story is you must try a hot dog with a non traditional bun :)

First, I love hot dogs. Secondly, if you don't eat meat, there are some veggie options. It's great. It's also fun to read the cartoons, quotes and articles plastered all over the walls, covered in yellowing Scotch-tape. Thanks to my brother for taking us here!

Oddly I never braved Top Dog before, as the tubular meat offerings didn't beckon to me. 

Then last night I happened by and stopped in for a $3 Bockworst and glass of fresh apple juice. One healthy shot of spicy mustard later, I ended up with one cheap-n-tasty meal. 

Hell, for $5 and change I was taken back to my summer vacation in Switzerland. Only downside was that my summer vacation cost more than $5 and now I regret not having stayed home and taken the digital camera to Top Dog everyday.

Oh well, live and learn.

if I was a talented enough writer, I would write an ode to sausages, namely the sausages at top dog; similar to the reviewers before me.

but since I can't, I will say this:
places like top dog make me wish I was in college again, when eating junk at 2 am is not just encouraged, it's a required prerequisite for graduation.

&what delicious, sweet junk it is. meaty mcMeat, perfectly grilled, on a bread roll no less. mind blown. the bun made it. crispy and soft. not sure if I can look at a Costco hot dog the same way again.

a plethora of toppings to choose from. 3 mustards! unlimited ketchup! relish, onion, and saurkraut. nom.

can't wait to pay Cal campus another visit for another top dog. next time, I'll be sure to stay out and drink copious amounts of beer and see how damn good top dog can really get.

I've been a fan of 'TopDog' for the longest time! I fell in love with this establishment a few years ago and continue to eat here with little complaint. 

Make sure you know what your ordering, because if you don't the person taking your order will pass you up! This place is perfect for a late night after party meal in Berkeley. It's a small shack without seating, so when you order please dress your wiener' and step out. 

I hope your eating skills are good because you'll be eating standing up. Late night this place is popular with all the local college students, so prepare yourself to wait in line. 

I wish i could suggest a favorite dog of mines, but i LOVE THEM ALL!

top dog FRANKFURTER
All beef - kosher style

GERMAN FRANKFURTER
3/4 beef, 1/4 pork, fresh garlic

BOCKWURST
1/2 pork, 1/2 veal, milk, eggs

KIELBASA (POLISH)
2/3 pork, 1/3 beef - hearty

CALABRESE (ITALIAN)
Pork, paprika, chili, fennel -- semi-hot

HOT LINK (LOUSIANA STYLE)
Beef and four kinds of pepper -- h-h-hottt

BRATWURST (GERMAN)
Pork, marjoram -- genuine old world taste

LEMON CHICKEN
Chicken, fresh lemon & garlic -- low salt, low fat, no preservatives

SMOKED CHICKEN APPLE
Chicken, juicy bits of apple -- low salt

BIRD DOG
Turkey, bell pepper, cilantro --slight bite

THE WIENIE (VEGGIE)
Wheat Protein, Bell Peppers, Fennel, Eggplant and Fresh Garlic. No preservatives 

LINGUIÇA
All pork, wine vinegar cured, smoked

LOVE TOP DOG!

The hot russian mustard there is so fantastic... Tastes like horseradish mixed with mustard... which is great for me because I love them both!
The lemon chicken and chicken apple sausage is probably my favorite... both are very flavorful and the cooks are very welcoming. Mmm.. I like how they have a hot fresh pot of sauerkraut in the condiment section.. mmmmm... haha I'm craving it right now even though last night I just had 2 Hahah!

this place is amaaaaazing!  worth the trek through traffic and drunk berkeley kids, worth the pushing and shoving in line to order.  it was late and we were running out of options of things to eat.  i wasn't expecting much thinking how good can a HOT DOG be?!?!?!  let's just say i was proved wrong and i'm so grateful.  hot links plus chili plus all the toppings you would want at an unbeatable price!!!!  woohooo!

The dreadlocked man who worked (works?) many late nights at the Southside location was a savant.  He could cook upwards of four dozen dogs at once, warm their accompanying buns, keep track of the orders of another three dozen often-drunk people, sell cigarettes, check IDs, and fill the occasional RC Cola, all while watching a terrible late-night TV program and never, ever, making a mistake.

Yes, they serve RC Cola here.

"Bock and a hot" is my classic order, though you can't go wrong with the kielbasa or the lemon chicken.  I say, spend the extra $2.75 and get two dogs.  If you're planning ahead for a barbecue, a six-pack of cold dogs, plus buns, only runs $7.50.

My friend liked to challenge/punish himself by loading up his hot link with hot Russian mustard, something I can recommend only as a spectator.  There's a large variety of dogs, an even more impressive array of condiments (four kinds of mustard!), and low low prices.  My one experience with a Top Dog-catered event was well-run and quite delicious, though disappointingly free of the yellowed libertarian newspaper articles and comics I've come to expect from Top Dog.

Chicken Apple Sausage on a freshly toasted bun topped with Russian mustard, ketchup, and sauerkraut = heaven. 

And this was lunch time when we were not buzzed nor hungover.

I went here after the recent MSU @ Cal game, and after hearing so much about this place, I was not disappointed.  After a few drinks, my friends and I thought hot dogs were in order, so we went next door to this place.  I picked up a Chicken Apple dog, and not gonna lie, it was fantastic.

There were two people working, a black guy taking orders, and a white guy grilling up the dogs.  I have no idea how the system worked, but the black guy was taking in about 15 orders in, and just keeping them in his mind.  Then he'd pass it on to the cook, and he'd do the same, and eventually, everyone got their dogs.  It was pretty amazing to watch.  As a bonus, they were pretty cool cats, and we talked a little music (they had Dead Prez on).  The fact that they were solid music fans pushed them over the top for me.

I liked that first dog so much, I went back for a second.  I wasn't really hungry, and I'm also a smaller guy, so I didn't have the room for it, but you know, I wasn't going to be back here again, and it was good enough where I wanted another.  I got a Hot Link for my second pass, and it was also great.

As a bonus, for non-Cal fans (I went to ASU), there are plenty of Cal folks milling about, and they are ripe for taunting.  You can have a few drinks, eat a good hot dog, and rail on some wimpy Cal fans.  What more can you ask for? ;)

WHEN EVER I'M IN NORCAL I TRY AND STOP BY THIS PLACE!

Dare I say it, no LA hot dog place can hold a candle to TOP DOG.

Smoked Apple Chicken is one of the best, even the chips they offer are good.

check the anarchy literature on the wall while you wait.

I was super excited to eat Top Dog again because the last time I ate it, it was really delicious.

I ordered the hot link and it was pretty hot, but not as spicy as I thought it would be. I love that they don't use regular hot dog buns, but everything together just wasn't working for me.
I didn't really like the sausage so I just gave it to my friend and ate the bread with onions, mustard, and ketchup.

Plus side: open late and very affordable.

eh :/

The hubster used to go to Cal and takes me here on his Berkeley Food Tour (BFT).  The BFT visits his favorite college food establishments on and around Telegraph Ave.  The tour is best enjoyed with another person, in order to share food items and maximize the number of places to eat!

We usually get a Hot Link and cut it in half; the hubster puts onions and ketchup on his half, while I eat mine with just ketchup.  The Hot Link is an apt description, because it's nice and spicy. The grilled bun takes the hot dog to another level.  Just writing this review is making me crave one!

The people who work here are definitely characters, sometimes you get a guy who is super-friendly and jovial, and sometimes you get a guy who is all business and yells at the customers to not crowd the doorways.

Speaking of crowding the doorways, the shop is so small, it's almost impossible to not crowd the doorway.  But the crowding isn't a problem, as the newspaper clippings and cartoons on the wall make the wait bearable.  In the end, getting the dog makes it all worthwhile. :)

One thing to note is that you can get the dogs to take home and grill, generally 6 dogs and 6 buns for $6. Grilling and eating the hot dog at home is not quite the same experience as eating in Berkeley, but sometimes you gotta do what you gotta do!
I was surprised they stayed open until 2 am.  I went there for a chicken apple sausage.  No frills, just a good quality sausage for $2.75.  What more could I ask for?

Top Dog is the perfect late night place after a few beers.  If it's 1:00 in the morning and you're debating one more beer or getting Top Dog, choose Top Dog. The hot dogs are good, reasonably priced, and come on a toasted bun.
chicken freaking apple. 2:00 A.M.  that is all.

Its a hot dog stand, nothing fancy, but if you get the odd (very odd) craving, top dog, located right next to the dorms, will not let you down. 

This place will always live in my memory because as a freshman my aunts visited me and we went here for a late night snack. One dropped the last bit of her hot dog and it went rolling downhill on Durant while she yelled, "I lost my weiner!"

I miss Berkeley

simple no frills hot dog.  sure the dog is good, but it's important to remember the bun is equally as crucial.  solid 5's on both ingredients.  everyone has their favorite, and mine would be the hot, lemon and cal.

nothing fancy.  i love the workers there, i love the fact that there is no line, and no sense of order, but the cashier always gets it right.  it's exactly what you would expect in berkeley.
Still the same after 21years...

Got 2 hot dogs because I heard amazing things.... 

and what a disappointment because they just weren't that amazing.

Kielbasa. With Ketchup, Mustard and Relish. It was alright, tasted like a normal hot dog. I wasn't a fan of the bun though, I prefer normal hot dog buns than bready. Nothing that special, in my opinion.

Louisiana Hot Link. With Ketchup, Mustard and Relish. This was alright too, nothing special though just a spicy hot dog. Umimpressive.

I was pretty disappointed by this place, not to mention the fact that the girl at the grill was rude. But I wish they had special ketchups or mustard like other hot dog places, that would have made it much better. The hot dogs by themselves would have only been worth 2 stars since I've definitely experienced better at the Hotdogger at Davis. But -1 star for rude girl at the grill. 

See photos of food, http://potbellypanda.tumblr.com

I make a point of coming here every time I visit the Bay Area from NYC.

The sausages are flavorful and charred to perfection. The toasted sesame bun has the springiness of real bread and doesn't dissolve like a typical processed hot dog bun. It's fast, affordable, and best of all doesn't overwhelm your mouth with that nitrate-laden meat aftertaste that comes with most substandard links.

The hot link is fantastic; snappy with just the right amount of cayenne kick. Wash it down with a cup of unfiltered apple cider and you're golden.

There's nothing better on a cold, late night than a chicken apple sausage from Top Dog.

In college this combination left me all warm and inspired to write papers.
BEST LATE NIGHT food in Berkeley.  I've tried almost every flavor and I've got say, my favorites are the Chicken Apple, Hot Link, and Calabrese.

The guy who works here is the funniest guy ever.

I have never been dissappointed here, the price is right. Its filling, its inexpensive, its homey :)

The only think is, its really small and super busy on weekends.

Mmmmmmmm, the best late night food stop EVER!  

Personally, I like to go get the cold dog special: For half the price, they give you the uncooked dogs and buns in a six pack.  

This place is open till ungodly hours and gets particularly crowded late at night.  Also, unless you absolutely need it, I would avoid during game days.  Too crowded for my liking.

Normally I hate hot dogs.

 But I am filipino so there is only one way I'll eat a hot dog...in spaghetti. 
 But then something happened..before I lived in California and I came from Washington just visiting my dear old cousin decides to take me to top dog to rid me of my hate of this mixed meat delicacy. 

Well there it was, me and the chicken apple. AND OHMYGOD it was orgasmic, it was pleasurable...I ate it. 

Top dog is the ONLY place I'll eat hot dogs on a bun!

Generally I try to eat healthy. But I have a few weaknesses...fried chicken is one of them...mmm fried chicken. But I digress. My other weakness is a damn good hot dog. 

Top dog is one of the few places I will partake in all that is a damn good hot dog. The choices are endless! I always stress for the few blocks before...what do I want? A chicken-apple and a hot link? A top and a garlic? Ahhh! 

I usually wind up at top dog after a show at the Greek. I now find myself craving it as the show ends...yum!

Simple, to the point, you know what you are getting, no distractions....just a grill....a guy with a greasy tank top....and some TOP dogs....

Come down to LA, Top Dog...I miss you!
I was all very good until I saw a huge rat the size of my forearm casually walk from top dog next door. Gross...

This review is based on the ONE BITE I took from my friend's 'dog (because I already ate lunch and was too full to have just one hot dog).

Every time my friend and I go to Berkeley, she raves about Top Dog and always stops by to get her fix, and a few more to save some for later. Don't ask why, but she really does love her wieners, especially when she has multiples to last her a whole day (who wants to call it?). My friend offered me to take a bite at least, so I did. Normally, I'm not a big fan of hot dogs, links, sausages, and other phallic meats, but for some reason, this really stood out. The casing snaps as you sink your teeth in the bun and 'dog and the flavor oozes out in your mouth. My friend must've gotten the hot link, because it was spicy, which I love. The condiments were great also. I'm a fan of their spicy mustard!

Man, if only I could've waited a bit more, I would've had the full experience. That one bite was a teaser.

This review sounded so dirty, but what can you do? Food = porn.

hello??? the best place to get hotdogs. i tried different ones - polish, hot link, and the white ones..but i always order the hot links.  daughter LOVESSS this place. we always cap our day here :) 8 pmish.

 top dog fed me through my college life and now is feeding my hubby & daughter whenever we are in Berkeley for a quick bite.

in fact, my bros and sis get this same initiation for my berkeley experience, sans the starving college lifestyle.

Basically a hole in the wall everyone in Berkeley knows (or has heard) about. Living in Berkeley for only 2 days, I already visited twice.

The Bird Dog (made of Turkey and Cilantro) was so good. I loved the texture of the sausage. The casing was nicely burnt and the bread was toasty hot. 

The second time around I had the hot link. Freak'n AMAZING! The spice builds up in the back of your throat. It isn't too spicy, but at the end of the dog, you'll be wanting some water. 

Sauerkraut has a smokiness to it. The first time I had it, I though the bread was burnt, but after a few bites I fell head of heels for it. 

If you are ever in the area, stop by Top Dog. Only $3 for a quick and on the go lunch.

I love Top Dog.  A good hot dog is seriously underrated, and I do not understand why -- unlike say NY -- we don't have decent hot dog stands scattered everywhere.  I hear there's one outside the ball park through the 2nd inning on game day, and when I'm Berkeley-bound, there's Top Dog.   I love it.  If I lived here, it would be an addiction.

Here's another Berkeley staple that I was eagerly looking forward to, that also ended in (slight) disappointment. After dropping by King Pin, I noticed the familiar yellow and blue sign across the street, and decided to make a lunch out of donuts and a hot dog.

As I did in the old days, I opted for one of their spiciest dogs, the hot link for $3, loading it up with some Russian mustard, ketchup, relish, and onions. The heat was definitely there, in both the link and the mustard, served up in a perfectly toasted and slightly crisp bun. But, to be honest, I'm a bit spoiled by the fancier (but also pricier) hot dogs up in Seattle now, served with things like grilled cabbage, salsa, and cream cheese. So while Top Dog edges out with a solid 3.5, the lack of wow factor prevents them from getting a 4.

Still, they make for a great late-night stop for the hungry (drunk) college students in the area. For everyone else, you're better off just ordering their bulk packages (either in-store, or mail-order from their site) and grilling them up at home.

TOP DOG! I WILL NEVER FORSAKE YOU! 

YOU OFFER CHEAP GOODNESS FOR THOSE POOR COLLEGE STUDENTS, FOR THE DRUNKARDS THAT COME OUT AT NIGHT (ahem), and for anyone who just wants a good deal.

I love this place and I wish they had it in SoCal. They tried to have a sister chain similar to it called "Berkeley Dog" in Irvine, CA but it's not the same. It's less affordable and it just doesn't call to you like Top Dog.

*Warning - only takes cash.

Ah, Top Dog. Nothing like a red hot at 3 am after spending the last 24 hours cramming for finals and/or underage binge drinking. A friend of mine actually had them come out and cook for her wedding reception, as sort of an after-dinner snack. It was excellent. The northside location is a little more chill, and doesn't seem as frantic, and you can actually sit down somewhere.
Over rated.  Hot dogs are good but come on, waiting in line for dog is pretty hard to justify.  The dog here is also expensive.  Forget it, goto costco for the 1.50 hotdog and drink combo.

Best hot dog/sausage place ever... I always got chicken apple or the spicy kielbasa or whichever sausage was spicy.... They have pretty good potato salad there too.. My ex and I used to always eat there when he came up to visit me in college... Guys are always a fan of this hot dog stand. =P

Top Dog is a Berkeley staple
just like Canada's leaf that's maple
As you'll see it's completely legit
From the lines, u see it's a hit
once you start eating, you won't quit

Went to top dog like twice in three days, the calabrese is my favorite and the hot links aren't bad as well.  People I know love the chicken apple but I personally have a bias against fruit in my meat.  But hey, it's cool.  The bread they use is toasted and is amazing, and like another user said, the russian mustard is bomb.

Four stars for staying open til the wee hours of the night.
This place always has a line outside-- hungry college kids on budget drunk college kids who want late snacks after their late night drinking (or early morning drinking... or they mid-day drinking). In any case, this place is always packed and there is a reason why.


The smell that wafts out of this place entices even the vegetarians because, yes, you can smell this place a block away. And it is tempting. I highly suggest you give into the temptation, because when it comes to hot dogs, top dog is as good as it gets. Near campus anyway.


This place, along with La Burrita, deserves four stars for location, convenience and price. Top dog is probably responsible for feeding 1/3 of Berkeley undergrads for perhaps 1/3 of the year.

Chicken apple with sauerkraut, mustard, and onion!

This place doesn't need another lengthy review. Best Hot Dogs in the area. Enough said.

For those who live or have lived in Berkeley, there is no explanation needed.

For those who haven't, maybe a little bit of explanation would be nice if you've only tasted the hype and not their Hot Links.

1.  When they ask what you're ordering, they just want the dogs.  Chips, salad, soda, all come later when you pay.
2.  The Hot Link is hot.  The Chicken Apple and Lemon Chicken are good and something new.  The Kielbasa and German Frank are meatilicious.  The classic Top Dog is, well, classic.
3.  If you're looking for a meal rather than a quick fix, the dog + potato salad + drink combo keeps me happy enough at lunch time.
4.  $2.75 might seem like a lot for hot dogs, especially since they were $2.50 just a year ago, but you're paying for the experience as well as the dog.  And what a better way to experience Berkeley than to eat outside on the street at 2am with drunk college students, homeless folk, and a drugged up worker who takes orders at 50mph and keeps yelling, "get out of the doorway if you're not going to order!"

The dogs are good but they're still just dogs... four stars.
But getting in line as the post-party rush arrives and biting into that fully-loaded Hot Link after a good night out with friends... I can't even begin to count the stars for that.

Didn't understand - at first - what the big whoop was about hot dogs. I mean, really, how good can hot dogs be? But then I had one. Eh, the first was okay. But by the 3rd or 4th time, oh man, these are pretty bomb hot dogs, with the toasted bun and all the sauerkraut you want. 

Definitely don't wait until senior year to get this like I did.

If you want to get down to the basics, a good quality hot dog you gotta come to Top Dog. I thought Pink's in LA was the best until I tried a top dog. Pink's tends to add a lot of fluff, but it's all about the sausage at Top Dog. No nonsense dog. The louisiana hot link is muy caliente! But my all time favorite is the kielbasa with some spicy mustard. The prices here are great but depending on when you go there could be a long line. This location is usually pretty busy so I would try the location north of compus.

The only drawback to this place is.... if you've read any of my previous reviews... they don't serve beer!

What goes better with one of the best bratwurst, knotworst or any other worst for that fact?  When in Rome - nothing that a brown paper bag and a twelve pack can't cure.  In fact, you'll fit in with the locals more so.

Louisiana hot links are PHENOMENAL!  Douse that with all the fixin's from the mustard to the sour kraut!  Trick is to eat it without dropping any of it.  If you're going to make the trip, it's gotta be a 3 dog minimum.  Do try their many other varieties and like fine wine, it does take a while, 10-15 minutes, depending on if it's after frat party rush hour or not.

Not a problem, during the wait, refer back to the paper bag scenario.

Figure flying to Berkeley's cheaper than going over to Europe for a kick-ass dog!

Top Dog is exactly what it is - TOP DOG!  Wow, the first time I came upon this place many many many moons ago - I was overwhelmed.  I am not a hot dog person by any stretch BUT this place is damn good at doing what they do best!  They used to have buckets of warm sour krauts for you to pile on top - I LOVE sour krauts... AND different kinds of mustard too - didn't see either last time we were there.  Nonetheless, the dog was still as good as we remembered.  

They have a good selection of dogs to choose from and I love that they toast the rolls...have you seen the guy at the grill?  They have the system down packed!  The bockwurst and hot link are my favorites but everything are good here - you just can't walk away disappointed, seriously.  

What better way to spend a nice afternoon in Berkeley than munching on a top dog piled with sour krauts w/ loads of mustard and relish on a doorstep with juices dripping all over you and the sidewalk?!?

Their "six pack" of dogs is a steal - 6 dogs and 6 buns to go at $7.50? 

Love this place..we need to go back soon!

we passed by this place several times through the day and there was always a line so we knew it had to be good. Sure enough it was, All there hot dogs were 3 bucks, cant beat that. They had a large variety even veggie dogs. loved the fact that it was just a small whole in the wall. Your in and out, there's no seating. Perfect for on the go or if your in a hurry

May 2010

Perfect hot dogs since I was a child. The personnel change, some of the locations have come and gone, but the efficiency and attitude remain.  I love every flavor, though I miss the New Yorks. I'd eat here every day if I could - and there were times that I did.   Brought my daughter in before our trip to Fairyland the other day and she loved her Top. 

This location is the most well oiled machine, almost everyone understands the drill: stand at the margin and when he looks at you place your order. He'll say it out loud to make sure it's right. Eventually he'll look at you again and repeat the order and ask if you want anything else - be ready!  Order a drink or chips or whatever and then he'll tell you what to pay. Pay your bill and a few minutes later he's handing you your dogs and you're on your way. 

In the day there are a few stools at the counter but it's too busy at night so they take them away.  

Something completely random and insipid on the ancient TV? Always.

Top Dog kicks Pink's ass in taste.  I crave Top Dog all the time, I wish there was one here in So Cal, but it wouldn't have the spunk that the Berkeley location has. The guy that owns the place doesn't mess around, you better be ready to order your dog.  I also love that they ship their hot dogs. I'll order some for my next bbq.  My favorite is the lemon chicken, it's also low-fat!!

Back in my good ole' college days in UC Berkeley, I came here a couple of times usually after midnite whenever i get the munchies.  I pretty much stopped going here after I noticed the cook was handling the cash, then grabbing the hot dog buns with his unsanitary hands and, I'm speculating here, probably picking his nose and what not and wiping it on the buns....it was just too gross.  I clearly remember I had very bad stomach aches the last 3 times i went.   It either has to be from the cook sometimes undercooking the dog, the dirty buns, or unfresh chopped onions and relish that's sitting right next to one of the walls out in the open, where it's highly probable that somebody could just spit a lugee in there with the relish and mix it around (nobody would notice)....arghh.....too many reasons.... That's why I stopped adding those things on top of the dog.   But despite the uncleanliness, those were still pretty darn good tasty hot dogs tho.... I always got either the chicken apple or the bachwurst (i forget the correct spelling).  The price at the time (2001), I believe it was no more than 2.50 or 2.75 for a dog.  Legend has it, they use to sell Mary Jane here...err thats what I heard....Anyways, it's part of the Berkeley  experience to eat here.

Veggie dogs are my shit! This is the place to get them. Simple with mustard and I'm a happy girl.

They might put crack in the gods because I FIENE for them!

Top Dog is the ultimate 2:30 am food. I am constantly amazed at how deftly the staff handles 20+ people and their orders, all the while offering a inexpensive and highly satisfying hot dogs. There is truly something for everyone (in terms of hot dogs) and the throwback to the truly Berkeley feel is not lost on someone like myself. 

I have to give this place 5 stars, there are so few places that deserve such adulation and support, but this is truly one of them.

There is no line!

I had my pre birthday night in Berkeley. After a few bars top dog is definitely the right spot!

Go in look at the small but diverse menu. I Asked the guy at the counter which chicken dog he likes the best, the man answered "Lemondog" so I say Yes!

I was not very stoked about the bun as I like whole wheat but that thing was crunchy and delicious. 

I then proceeded to the condiments: sauerkraut, Deli mustard, relish, ketchup, onions. Mmmmmmmmm

See my picture; although I had a few drinks, it was amazing!!!!
I didn't pay so I did not see the prices, probably a good deal with how "low key" they are.

Underwhelmed.  It's by no means bad, but let's just say I would be perfectly content if I never had Top Dog again.

I tried the chicken apple sausage.  Probably my first mistake.  You don't get nearly same amount of flavor in a chicken sausage than beef.  The sesame roll was nicely toasted, but completely split apart half way through eating my dog.  Hate it when that happens.

Do they have grilled onions or peppers?  I don't even know because I wasn't offered any.  The standard toppings that they leave out certainly don't cut it.  Granted, this place is probably great if I were still a broke college student.  And it's probably a lot better after a few drinks.  Meh.  I'd take a Danger Dog (from LA) over Top Dog any day.

calabrese,  hot link... or just a plain old top dog, it can never go wrong for me.  Top Dog has and always will be my top dog.  it has been for 20 years.  20.  twenteeeee!!!  (yes, and you're just now getting my review!)  there are few great dogs out there, throughout the country,  but none ever as great.

simple.  pay the $3, get a great dog.  hot sauerkraut and your choice of mustard, brown, spicy etc.  the bun is a standby, never changes, always toasted.  very simple.  the dog is not dressed up or sauced up with all sorts of fancy things.  they're just delicious dogs, and less is definitely more.  

so glad i can always count on my top dog.  don't ever change.  love you just the way you are and always have been.

Summer of 1993, my first top dog. Since then there has been no other for me. Top Dog, you are the best. I don't care if you don't come with a free soda like at Costco, you are simply the best hot dog anyone could ever have. Especially your German and Kielbasa and your toasted buns. I don't care if service can be sketchy or if you're too crowded sometimes, it is all worth it. Whether I live 2 buildings down or 12.8 miles from you, you are worth it all!

Cheap quality hot dogs in the cold streets of Berkeley = thee life. its not the coffee that keeps me warm, its these hot dogs!

No wonder they call it TOP dog! its the best. reviews speak for themselves. Lots of selection. they cook it right off the grill with the buns.  Hot dog is juicy and delicious, top it off with some mustard and take a stroll around telegraph...

small, no chairs, line out the door... what else is new? :)

Please, God. Please. Please give me a miracle and let Top Dog open up a shop in Marin. I grew up on Top Dog (yes, I was indoctrinated with leftist propaganda pasted on the walls) as an innocent young girl in Berkeley and I am forever ruined for any other dog. Oh, Top Dog. How I miss you. How I dream about you. How I may drive many, many miles to eat one of you so very soon. 

Please, God. Please???

Whenever I take a visit to Telegraph, I just have to make a stop at Top Dog! Famous for their hot dogs. The buns are yum as well. MUST add sauerkraut. THE best toppingggg. Only thing bad I would say is that they have a bad selection of soda. RC Cola gets watery and flat so fast!

I enjoyed my Calebrese (Italian) dog on the toasted bun. I think it's good cheap eats for a late night after the bar. Not sure if I would make a speacial trip out here just for their dogs, but if I was in Berkeley, doing a little drinking, yea maybe. Had a bite of the bf's Hot Link, liked it better than my Calebrese. Also had a bite of the Khielbasa, eh it was alright.  The 5 of us ordered 9 dogs between us and they were all gone. Cash only!

Serving up an assortment of delicious snappy dogs on toasted sesame rolls and serve-yourself bins of sauerkraut, relish, and chopped onions, this Berkeley institution is a savior for hungry Cal students at 2 am. Faves are the Bratwurst and the Chicken Apple. I usually order a couple dogs for about $8 because I'm a fattie. Cash only!

I like being able to grab food with a friend, and walk down the street with it, catching up and people-watching. Top Dog in Berkeley is perfect for this, both in style of food and surroundings. The freshly grilled hot dogs are just wrapped up in a paper and handed to you. And the fellow who was working their that evening was super fast and very nice.

They have a veggie dog, which I applaud them for. Not the best I've ever had, but it's pretty okay! The toasted sesame seed bun and the different kinds of mustard, really makes up for any flavor that the veggie dog itself lacks. Not something I'd search out again. But if I happened to be in the neighborhood, I'd pop by.

Shoot, I don't even like hot dogs!!

When some friends wanted to eat here I was thinking yea sure why not.  In the past, I've had hot dogs that people rave about and was never impressed.  Pink's in LA was a serious disappointment for me.  

But top dog is the TOP DOG.  I don't wanna hype it up but I don't know what other type of hot dog I would want in the future.  

Christine B. & I split the chicken apple dog.  I loaded my half with ketchup, mustard, onions, and relish.  

First thing I said after my first bite was "Mmmm!"
And then tears were starting to come out.  Real tears.  Because no one told me how spicy the mustard was lol.  

But the chicken apple is super juicy and sweet.  I think the bread makes a HUGE difference in the quality.  Normal hot dog buns aren't that good but the bread they use - great choice.

Now I understand why people come here to appease those late night munchies.

drrrroooool I went back three times while i was in the east bay. could not get enough!! crispy pop on the dog, awesome grill bun. I kept it simple with the frankfurter i tried my boys weiswurst and hot link but i stuck with the simple and classic. 

one tip, their not kidding when they said that russian mustard is outrageously hot. you might take a dab and go oh it's not that hot, but in mass you start breathing it it's like breathing napalm. 

at $3 a piece there isn't much better you can do. ooooo ya, they have fresh cider that's their apple juice. yumms. 

if you like hotdogs you gotta go, even if you don't like hotdogs you should go just walk down a block from there and tell me you don't want once after smelling that grill.

definitely the Top Dog in my book...visited this place last night after the Beastie Boys show and it was perfect end to the evening. the excellent service was a show in itself, watching this guy take orders and toss the dogs on the grill then yell them out as the orders come up...fun! price with tax included makes it easy to figure out how much you owe (especially if you've been drinking)...i had the frankfurter, it was hot, juicy and served on a french bread bun with sesame seeds. i used yellow mustard and it was all it needed...yummm...it's a must visit even if you're not hungry.

One word: Yum.  Top Dog has quickly become one of my favorite destinations to grab a bite when in the Berkeley area.  It is a great "after climbing treat".  I haven't really tried anything other than the Hot Link (it's that good), but I hear lots of people like the kielbasa as well.  

The Top Dog experience is unique.  It's not a big place...just enough room to get a couple of people in to order, enable a few to sit down to eat at the counter and that's about it.  Be prepared to know what you want to order...the normal people that work here have a weird personality, but it makes it a fun experience.  

My only complaint about this location is that they don't have the Russian Style Hot Beaver mustard like the one on Hearst St!

I've resisted buying the cold dogs to go, just because it probably won't taste the same at home.  :P

my mouth waters at the thought of top dog. it's the best late night snack at an affordable price, inebriated or not.. Even when this tiny space is packed to a brim, there is a constant flow of traffic, so your wait is never long. i always get chicken apple or bratwurst.. mmm... meat.. drool* 

their pressed apple juice is pretty damn good.. no sugar added, and it's probably the best i've tasted.. in fact, top dog is calling my name...  

*door slams, sound of ignition*

Top Dog does it right. Great hot dogs, topped with what you want and properly done too! Hit the spot after a night of drinking. Last I remember they take cash only, and I know I tried to convince the dude to let me get away by paying the rest of my hot dog in cigarettes but I guess the hippy movement is dead. Thats cool though, ended up getting feds and munchin out on some BOMB hot dogs. MMMM MMMM MMMM. Cal kids got it good.

Ghiradelli chocalate is to San Francisco as
Top Dog is to Berkeley,what a great traditional combo

Before I go to any Cal Sporting event, I always pound two hot-dog and a small can of Diet-coke before I go in.  Every single kind of weiners are very tasty including the Kielbasas, Chicken-apple and Polish Dog.
The owner(S) of this popular Berkeley hangout has found a goldmine.

I may not attend CAL. But you UC Students are very lucky to have a great hot dog place in Top-Dog.

What can I say?
Same ole' goodness and the same for the last 17 years I have been visiting this place.
Always good sausages!

I love the wieners at this place and their spokes dog is so cute!  For a large variety of different flavored wieners this is your spot.  If you're looking for a place that has a whole bunch of different toppings, this isn't so much the place for that.  Otherwise a good place to get atypical hot dogs that are freshly made.  This is by far the best place for hot dogs in Norcal!

I remember the first times that I ate here many years ago. The hot dogs here have not changed at all in that time. Consistency is key. They have good hours here and is frequently visited by the late night party crowd with munchies which sometimes requires you to bump elbows with some drunk people if you have a late night urge. Its never really been a problem for me, but I have seen some friction between an exasperated cashier/cook and a clueless bleary eyed mob.

Depending on whether I'm grabbing something here as a snack or for a meal, I usually grab a kielbasa or both a kielbasa and a bockwurst. The lemon chicken is alright and the hot link is frigging GOOD. Unfortunately the bockwurst JUST barely budges out the hot link out of my top 2.

The hot dogs here are pretty pricey as they have slowly raised the prices over the years, with 50 cents here and there. Its just not economical to eat here often anymore. The service is usually pretty friendly, in a curt sort of way. It is usually best to decide quickly of what you want and let the guy know clearly. Otherwise you might be subjected to some... *gasp* grumbling when you finally decide or get your order right. It might be annoying to some, but to me it just adds more character to this place.

Lemon Chicken and Apple chicken are all I eat when I go to this spot.  The flavors are good and the buns are nice, toasty and hot.  It's a great place to go to after a night at the bars.  Once you get into the building make sure you make yourself known and know what you want.  If ya sit on the sidelines hoping they will recognize you then be ready to wait.  Lines can be long late at night so there might be a wait.  Happy Eating!

Before the dawn of Chicken apple sausages . . .

. . . before the invent of condiment dispensers . . .  great tubs of sauerkraut and sweet pickle relish, with real spoons

Kielbasa & Polish were KING

I was with nfactorial and we were waiting to be joined by our friend D so we could begin our rockin' junior high school reunion. D called in to tell us to go ahead and eat, so now the decision was if we should get Top Dog or Fat Slice Pizza. 

I went with Top Dog (N decided to pass because they don't separate the veggie dogs the same way they do at the other TDs, or something like that...) and got my fave - the hot link (added on the kraut)! Actually, I don't think I've ever tried anything other than the hot link, so I can vouch for its tastiness only. $3 well spent!

"Get out of the doorway!"

"What do you want?!"

Hey, if I had to take orders from a bunch of drunks at 2:00 am I might be mad at the world too, but I'm just here to grab my dog and go.  I come to Top Dog for the hot links, some of the best around, so if I have to deal with some gruff service it's a small price to pay.  I'm going to pass out 10 minutes after getting home anyway - life could be worse.

Celia and Jeff love love love Top Dog! 

It's waaay better than the one on north side. When we were there, they microwaved my hot dog before grilling it. It turned out to be as dry as a slim jim.

Anyway--- this place has the BEST hot links. All of their hot dogs have the "snap." They just "snap" and then it gets juuuuicy. 

The store is really small, but it smells great and there are a lot of interesting anarchist-like stickers. There's definitely no seating space though (like most hot dog places), so you'll have to take your top dog to go.

Jeff loves to mix sauces and he always piles on the sauerkraut (which is so fresh and the best i ever had), onions, and relish, making everything mushy. Actually it makes everything more delicious and you have to do this to get the best top dog experience. No you don't. 

Bottom line(s):
It's cash only. The top dog snaps like the top dog it is. You can eat however you like. But you have to add the sauerkraut.

When the place is run by just one person, it is amazing to watch him/her handle 20 persons' orders in 10 min from hot dog to payment to drinks to more people!  Impressed with the service and quick turnaround.  Bun is like a hybrid French roll - hot dog bun = divine!  $3 hot dog worth every penny.

Best hot dogs I've had yet.  It's good enough that I used to take the 880 up to Sacramento instead of the faster 680 just so I could stop through and get a top dog on the way.  Calabrese is still my fave, but you gotta love them all.

As if $3 a dog isn't cheap enough, you can buy them by the dozen or half dozen and cook them yourself.  It makes for a great tailgate at, say, Oakland coliseum, or for bbqing at home.

This location is the best I've had.  There's one in San Jose by the SJSU campus, but it's just not the same taste or feel as this joint.  Still think this place is better than Pink's hot dogs in LA and just about any other sausage in a bun.

Parking is a shame though, I've actually gotten written up twice by parking enforcement at Berkeley, so watch yo backs!

Here's the deal.  If you want a freakin' good hot dog, one that doesn't follow typical hot dog trend, then be sure to stop by.  Seriously,  what can possibly beat the lemon chicken?  Umm, maybe a bite of heaven?  I don't even like eating chicken on a regular basis, and yet this is what I buy along with a hot link...which brings me to my next hotdog.  

If your taste buds have been sheltered your whole life...this is not the route for you.  Buy another lemon chicken. This stuff is really hot!  Be sure to grab a few extra napkins to wipe your nose, as it will definately start running.
top dog has the best hot dogs around!

Ever since I moved back to LA, I just always think about Top Dog!  I've never had a better hot dog anywhere else!  The hole-in-the-wall thing really gives the hot dog the grittiness it has to make you feel cool and edgy.  The people behind the counter are always really efficient too.  They find out what you want, take your money, and give you your hot dog without any problems, even when the place is packed and it's hard to distinguish the many [Asian] faces.
