The bread too!  So yummy!  I wanted to try all the different kinds but never did it.  Live out my dream!

They opened another Top Dog in Irvine and it really doesn't feel or taste the same...

Yes... another 5 stars for Top Dog. Its amazing.  If you like hot dogs you have to go here.  Totally unpretentious.  Call out what you want, hang for a few minutes catch up with the guy behind the grill, order a drink and chips, eat and hang, or take off. Easy as that... great prices too and lots of dog choices, even veggie options.

Likes: Lemon chicken and smoked apple chicken are my go to hot dogs

Dislikes: This space in the location is very small, almost no where to sit.  Best to just pretend this is like a drive through, go in with money and out with a hot dog.

i think top dog is concentrated with reviews from people reliving their drunken, 2am treks to asian ghetto, desperately stumbling about for something to eat.

incidentally, top dog offers several different types of hot dogs - the hot link, the lemon chicken, the bratwurst, the etc. etc. and it's open late.
 
now, i'd hate to downplay the emotional attachment to the shop and all, but seriously guys. it's a hot dog.

It begins and ends with Top Dog.  

I have been going there for 30 years.  There is no better hot dog place, anywhere.  Not the streets of New York or Chicago, not the hipster places in LA.  

Scan the menu, get in line and order.  Experiment with them....New York, Kielbasa, Louisiana.  Then have another.  

The ambiance is bar none.  Don't fraternize with the staff unless they make a bid to do so. 

It begins and ends with Top Dog.

I am not big on American food....really! But, here is another big weiner!!!! Five stars!!!!

I came to the other Top Dog location long ago with the hipster bearded wonder Fabio and enjoyed it. I knew that this location was the popular one and I wanted to come here but Fabio wanted to avoid the crowds.This time was the dogs were as tasty as the first. Great hot dogs!!!! I had the Smoked Chicken Apple dog. My friend Balle had a Veggie Dog. She said it was very flavorful. Yes, they have dogs for veg heads here! I thoroughly enjoyed my dog! The taste is a bit subtle I must admit but it is tasty still! I probably should have gotten another flavor like the linguica ( I think that's what it's called). They even have special dogs. Today they had a chicken mango habanero dog....wow!!!!

This place is tiny! There isn't enough room for all the cool stuff they put on the walls of the other location. Nevertheless, this place has some cool stuff to read and look at on the walls. The service is great. The guy at the grill is a hard worker. I'm really glad I came here! I highly recommend this place!

'EFFIN AMAZING HOT DOGS!
theeee BEST, EVERR !!!

Every time I'm in Berkeley, no matter how much I've eaten (or drank), I always find my way to Top Dog. It's a muuust, along with the boba and donuts on the side... :X

Disregard my love for food munchies (drunk munches, whatever you want to call them), and let's focus on the magical little shop on Durant. Top Dog just stands out in the middle of the night, with its brightly illuminated sign. It silently beckons you with the mini-crowds it draws, and the drifting aroma of sizzling hot dogs from grill. 

Love the art and decorations on the wall. It's full of attitude and good humor, like the workers here :] Just take your time and read some of the comics on the walls. I promise, you'll be amused!

my recommendation: the hot link!!! :D

Crisp bun with a flavorful and nicely seasoned meat. Simple and delicious! The condiments are on the side to help garnish your hot dog.

Remember to bring cash :]

$3 for a gourmet hot dog! 

There is so much to try here! I ordered the hot link which is super spicy but oh so tasty. I also had the Calabrese (Italian), which was probably the better choice. It was mildly spicy with lots of flavor. 

The hot dogs were served in  square toasted sesame seed buns. I usually dig chili but their chili was full of beans so I passed. However, there was plenty of sauerkraut, ketchup and mustard and the condiment table.

There may be a long line for this tiny place, but it moves fast. There are no tables or chairs so plan on standing while eating. Hopefully it isn't too cold out. The gourmet hot dogs are the best around and super cheap. Cash only but hey, tax is included in the price!

Definitely worth a visit if you love hot dogs.

this place is the shit, you love weiners, wursts, furters, and sausages they got. what more can you ask for? cookers are always cool with the tv always on espn. just a quick skate from 510 skateshop. and its open pretty late too

You like-a da sausage? I like-a da sausage! Specially from here! 

There is no place finer for a hot spicy hunk of meat to settle the drunken stomach, or the hung over stomach or the post final stomach, hell its just good any time.

Stop reading and get yo butt up and go to top dog right now and order some meat(or a wienie if you don't eat meat)!! (ask for a butterflied top at your own risk)

With so many choices and breakneck speed service, you can not go wrong. 

Oh and one more thing its CASH only so don't try to pull out your card all you'll get is annoyed looks and someone else eating your dog.

There's a reason this place has 4.5 stars after over 700 reviews.
The reason is because this place is awesome.

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- --

It's good for a quick bite at lunch time,
it's good for a quick bite at dinner time, and
it's best for a quick bite late at night, after a night of drinking.

It's open late, and often has a wait but is worth it.  

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- --

They have a ton of options.

They even make some attempts at grilling the Wienie (which is their veggie dog) on a different part of the grill than the non-veg dogs.

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- --

Don't come here if you're looking for fine dining with excellent service, but do come here if you're looking for something quick and really tasty.

((Minus one star because it's not the cleanest.))

In the same way that no man will ever feel entirely comfortable eating a banana - the dreaded sausage presents a similar sense of trepidation. So good on you lot for sticking it in a slab of bread.

On a side note - today I became a man, having recognised an actual bonefide yelper outside the confines of this website. When you left your seat, I sat in it and bathed in the educated heat of your posterior... bless you, tall asian girl...

It's so simple, but it's so good. I can't believe it, it's just a hot dog, but I crave Top Dog like a mad man!

 The drive to Berkeley to taste a Top Dog hot dog is worth it every single time for me. $3 for a juicy dog is a steal! My faves are lemon chicken, German Frankfurter, and the classic hot link. You should order 3-4  at a time because they're that good and you wont have to keep waiting for another one if you decide.There is no excuse not to love this place...the dogs are dirt cheap and the buns are toasty warm...yummm.

CASH only, Standing room only although there are bar stools. 

Things nearby: BART station, Cal Berkeley campus, telegraph ave, ATMs. Also open until 2am so if you're from the city/peninsula you can decide to go as late as midnight and still have lots of eating time.

Backstory paragraph... Ever since I got back from a trip in Chicago, I've been having hot dog cravings and no, I did not go to Boys Town there, it's because of those damn Chicago hot dogs, which I recommend.  To me, my Californian hot dog and Chicago hot dog are at equal levels for me and I wouldn't choose one over the other; it's all about my preference at the time.  And so as I would come back to California, I went to Costco to get a polish dog, but that didn't quite satisfy my appetite.  I then set my sights to the famous hot dog eating destination in Berkeley, which I've never been.  Therefore...

When I got there, there was a line going out of this tiny venue and the guy behind the counter is yelling over everybody to get everyone's orders, so be prepared to answer when he calls on you or you might upset him; he seems very abrasive for some reason like a feeling he's apathetic to the job but loves the money raking in that he can come off like a snarky, comedic jerk, but I'm sure he's a nice guy normally.  Enough with the speculation, the place has several kinds of hot dogs all for $3.00 from beef, pork, chicken, veal, turkey, or a mixture of the meats.  I ordered the Garlic Frankfurter because I love garlic.  And it's a sight to behold of the formidable amounts of sausages being grilled in the back to prepare for the flood of orders; there was probably more than 50 sausages on that grill.

I got my hot dog and it was surprisingly smaller than I thought.  If you're familiar to the Costco dogs, I would say it's about 2/3 that size.  Their hot dogs are all served on French bread buns that are slightly toasted to get a crisper taste.  So did the dogs here captivate my taste buds?  It was a good, solid hot dog I have to say.  There was a slight mix of flavors in my Garlic Frankfurter that's not apparent in other hot dogs I've tried, but I was disappointed that the garlic flavor was extremely subtle and could've used more.  And the best part, the hot dog actually tasted fresh!  Not your typical Costco or Oscar Meier wiener, and an actual original flavor to their sausages.

I enjoyed the hot dog thoroughly, even though the hot dog's size is slightly insubstantial, and for $3 for one is really not too shabby unless you're a cheapskate and refuse to pay more than a $1.50 for hot dogs due to Costco spoiling you, then that's just narrow mindedness.  Anyway, I would go back again, but not too often because its over 40 miles for me to get there.
A hot dog at Top Dog is better than a steak at the Ritz.

Top Dog: certainly a Berkeley institution. The dogs are grilled just perfectly and juicy. They're good for a meal or a snack. You can slather on the condiments at your pleasure. The potato salad is bomb. Buns are buttery and flaky.

but,

$3 for any hot dog / sausage is decently priced if these weiners were big, but they are not unfortunately. Size matters.

It's a long wait for something you'd think would grill fast. On top of that, the lines here are long on game days, lunch time, and late night. You need to stand around outside for your order in anticipation because there's no system whatsoever, like numbering. The service is just bad, rude sometimes even. It's cash only. So yeah, you guessed it, the bottom line is: overrated.

If I were to play the 100,000 pyramid and was asked for "Things I associate with Top Dog," I'd say:

College...
Delicious...
NFL Sundays...
"Study" sessions...
Late night munchies...
The reason for the late night munchies...
Take home exams...
Kielbasa...
Chicken apple...
A frank discussion about what a chicken apple is...
Sneaking in a few for the A's dollar Wednesday game...
Beer...
Condiments galore...
Hangovers...
Berkeley...
By the way, these are all good things (well, except for take home exams).  Oh, the memories...and I still don't know what a chicken apple is...

This will be a little strange because I'm writing this review based on experiences I had nearly 40 years ago when I was a student at UC Berkeley. Since leaving Berkeley so long ago, Top Dog epitomized the Holy Grail of hot dog eateries for me & became the standard which I measured my hot dog experiences & looking for my new  'hot dog heaven'. Could I ever find the Holy Grail anywhere else?

Maybe my memories from back in the 70s was fueled by youth, rebellion & hunger pangs enhanced by certain 'substances', but getting a "TOP DOG!" was almost a nightly thing for my friends & I (when us poor college kids could afford it) and any selection on the menu was OH SOOOOO GOOOOD!

Since then, my quest for the Holy Grail of hot dog eateries has been a major fail. No place have I ever found in the nearly 40 years has even come close to "Top Dog". At best, a weak 3 stars.

Since it had been so long ago that I had left Berkeley, I had assumed Top Dog had long departed the face of the earth & became only a fond memory of days gone by. Today I was lamenting my fruitless quest for the Holy Grail of hot dog eateries & decided to google "top dog berkeley". At best I thought I might get some historical info on their life & demise ... what I really expected was to get nothing useful ...

HOLY CRAP! THE HOLY GRAIL STILL EXISTS. I SEE THE OLD BRICK STOREFRONT. MEMORIES FLOOD BACK & HOPES RETURNS. I NEED TO GET TO BERKELEY ... START ONE HERE IN SD, PLEASE!
Who doesn't want a hot sausage in their mouth...wait what?!
maybe it just me and my friends, but our sausage was just ok. the bread was stale. our coke was flat. We were thinking about complaining about our coke, but ehh. I don't think I'd come here again.

I love Top Dog!!!! It's incomparable & the BEST HOT DOGS! After moving to Sac for college, I could never find any place to serve good hot dogs like Top Dog! If I'm ever in the area I make sure to grab myself some and then I walk across the street at Sweetheart Cafe for some fried calamari..Ok, I'm getting off track now. I've tried pretty much everything on the menu but my top favorites are Hot Link,Kielbasa, and Top Dog with everything on it and a RC Cola! 

The lines are always long but well worth the wait! It's a CASH ONLY joint so make sure to bring paper & change! It's cheap and open until 2am!!!

One of a kind, a Berkeley institution. Tastiest dogs ever. Great selection of dogs and toppings. Love the ambience, service. Sometimes interesting clientel. Open into the wee hours. Street parking may be difficult.

Update 10/28/07:  Did the lemon chicken shrink or somethin?  I swear the guy before me got one too, but the worker said his was a bratwurst.  He grabbed mine out of the bucket.  What are those, the reject little sausages?  I hope the owner reads this, but I doubt he would care anyway.  

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

This was my favorite spot when I went to school at Cal, especially on the weekend around 2am.  You don't have to be drunk to enjoy it though!  I love the lemon chicken on that toasted bun with a bunch of onions, mustard, and a touch of ketchup.  I know it sounds  weird to get excited over a hot dog, but these are way better than anything you had before!  Trust me!

I'm surprised it took me this long to write a review of Top Dog. 

Living in South Bay and never having any business to be in East Bay, let alone Berkeley, I am not afforded that many opportunities to sample Top Dog.  But when I do, I'd like to make the most of it.  By buying a bunch of them at once.  Now granted, I have not done it for good eight months if not more - blame it on insane work schedule and rising gas prices.  

However, should I ever venture up to Berkeley again, Top Dog would be my destination of choice.  There's nothing better than a grilled Louisiana Hot Link with lots of Sambel Cap Jempol (Indonesian hot sauce) - Bro, a Top Dog fanatic, missed it so much that he requested that I brought a couple of packets of these babies last time I went to visit him.  However, taking into account the 21-hour plane ride and multiple stops, his request was respectfully declined.  

Best East Bay late night post-party nosh.

Best hot dogs in the Bay Area. Well... sausages actually. They usually have about 12 different kinds so you can find out exactly what combination of beef, pork and veal taste the best to you.

I have a friend that would always get two hot links with hot Russian mustard. He bullied me into doing it once and I was hurting by the second hot link. My eyes went hazy and I started sweating. But I kept eating until every last ounce of sour kraut and hot link was gone. I'd do it again in a second. Viva Top Dog!

I reckon Top Dog and myself have quite the history. I can't even count the late night adventures that has ended in Berkeley just for one of those gratifying dogs.

The place itself is minuscule. People are constantly packed in there like some sardines. The cooks can be intimidating at times when they bark commands at people in the back but please understand it's for efficiency. 

Tilt your head up and look in awe at your choices of mouth watering ambrosia. Can't go wrong with the calabrese, kielbasa, german frankfurter, or the hot link (Louisiana style!). Served with a toasted french roll: crispy yet soft and oh-so-appropriate. Condiments are on the back wall, don't be noob and ask them to put anything on it.   

Be prepared for various vagabonds who frequent the area. You might get asked to take a hit of nitro or witness a street brawl that started over a piece of already-chewed bubble gum. Just smile, cross your eyes, and nod. Have patience when parking and you'll do just fine.

This place is extremely overrated and I have no idea why it is such a Berkeley icon.

Three dollars for a decent hot dog?  You could get nachos right next door or a grilled burrito at Mario's for a similar price and be much more satisfied.

The service sucks.. the guy serving you is almost always rude, though I guess that fits the idea of a hot dog place.

The hot dogs here are not significantly better than what you would get at Costco, and they are a lot smaller.

You almost certainly could make a better hot dog yourself.

Seeing that there are like 500 five star reviews of this place blows my fucking mind.  People are saying its cheap?  I mean, I know most of the people reviewing this place are spoiled UC Berkeley kids buying stuff on their parents dime and used to paying way too much money for food and housing already.. but how can you say getting a pretty small hotdog and a fountain soda is a steal for 6 dollars?

That is insane.

It's open until late, and they have lemon chicken. Condiments are facing the counter, and it's all you can squirt, later, rinse, repeat.

Not sure if the Black guy with dreads still works there. He's a math genius though. He's pretty robotic, as far as efficiency goes.

Oh yeah, they even ship sausages to you. That's pretty damn useful.

Lemon chicken!!!

I really like Top Dog..best hot dogs I've ever had. I'm not really a fan of hot dogs, but there are days when I crave the chicken apple hot dogs from here...so good.

Not only are the sausages delicious (chicken apple and hot link are my favorites), but the bread is sooo yummy! I don't know what it is (probably steak roll?), but it's definitely different from the typical hot dog buns that you get at the grocery store. 

Top Dog is really cheap too (3 bucks for a hot dog), so any broke college student can come here and grab a quick bite. For me (and probably most Asian girls), one hot dog is satisfactory. But guys probably need around 2-3 hot dogs to be content. 

The only thing about Top Dog is the cleanliness...I mean, I understand that it has character. But one of my friends got food poisoning from their hot dogs...yuck. Yeah...it's a bit unsanitary. But what can you say? It's a hot dog stand in Berkeley...

Anyway, anyone who's visiting Berkeley should give Top Dog a try!

The smells are extraordinary when you walk into Top Dog. There are so many choices of hot dog, but usually there is only one to go. They serve soda that screams nostalgia and their service is always as quick as could be. And you gotta love their sign on their huge soda machine on how things work at TD. Remember to have cash ready, because its the only thing that is accepted.

Its the whole in the wall places that have the best tasting foods!!!! In this case, the best hot dogs ever! 

I went to visit my friend that is attending the university up there and she was raving about this place (since I love hotdogs). We came here and the line was out the door, given the fact that once your inside, you order and get out :) Not a place to sit down and eat. 

I got a hot link. One bite. That was enough to know that I should have gotten a 2d or 3rd one. It was juicy and plump. Just the way I like it!!! :D My friend told me that this was the spot to go after a night out. I say... its a place to go any time of the day!!!! 

The only con I see is that the hot dogs are too small :(

Wikipedia has the following history on hot dogs:

"The American story of the invention of the hot dog, like the hamburger and ice cream cone, is often attributed to the 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition in St. Louis, Missouri. However, similar sausages were made and consumed in Europe, particularly in Germany, as early as 1864. The hot dog's association with baseball also predates the 1904 Exposition. St. Louis Browns owner Chris von der Ahe sold them at his ballpark in the 1880s.

Hot dogs were frequently known as frankfurters or franks, but the name "hot dog" became popular by the 1890s. In the 1830s, it was widely rumored that the dogs that roamed urban streets were regularly rounded up (by "dog wagons") and made into sausages; by the 1840s, the term "dog sandwich" was used. The 1860s popular song "Der Deitcher's Dog" (written by Septimus Winner and known by the lyrics "Where oh where has my little dog gone?") contained:

Und sausage is goot: Baloney, of course, 
Oh! where, oh! where can he be? 
Dey makes 'em mit dog, und dey makes 'em mit horse: 
I guess dey makes 'em mit he. "

While I'm pretty sure the would never make a hot dog out of my weiner Lola, she was most welcome to come in while we waited to get our yummy gourmet dogs.  

The Top dog griller is cool, nice and fast!  We came here on a Saturday afternoon and had a lemon sausage dog.  with some onions, deli mustard and sauer kraut......supper yum!

I don't consider myself a hot dog connoisseur but I have had many dogs in my life, and this my friends is probably the best!.....takes a bite of the lemon sausage dog......yum tangy....most definitely the bets hot dog around!

Oh and you can buy uncooked dogs to go too!

In honor of National Hot Dog Day!

I had my interns compile a calendar of events so we could plan our content features for August/September, and it turns out that today is National Hot Dog Day.  That's pretty cool.  'Cause, you know, I like hot dogs and sausages.  By the way, I don't mean that sexually.  I figure I should point that out since it's sometimes hard to convey context when there's so much to read between the lines.  But my love for hot dogs is completely subtext-free, I assure you.

Anyway, I thought I'd celebrate by eating a hot dog for dinner, and that got me thinking about where I wanted to get it.  Here are my Top 5 Hot Dogs:

1.  Top Dog (Berkeley, CA):  All of my college memories are tied to this place and their awesome bratwursts.  It's nice to eat something loaded with sentiments and nitrates.  I think my favorites were the Louisiana Hot Link, Bockwurst (pork, veal, milk and eggs) and the Bird Dog (turkey, peppers and cilantro).

2.  Toronto Dogs (Toronto, Canada...duh):  I loved pretty much every single street vendor dog in Toronto.  I think it's the variety of condiments that you can add, including olives and peppers, that rock my world.  Well, that and back in the day the U.S. dollar had some value and I would laugh at the Canadian dollar with every delicious bite.

3.  Tijuana Dogs (Tijuana, Mexico...duh again):  The bacon-wrapped dogs that I tasted on my first and only trip to Tijuana were so damn good that they were my benchmark until I discovered Top Dog.  The bacon-wrapped dogs you find outside clubs are alright, but I miss the mystery of the Tijuana versions.  Is that really meat?  Will it kill you?  Oh, so much fun!

4. Jody Maroni's (Venice, CA):  I know it's a chain, and that seems like a sell-out, but I actually really like their sausages.  What I especially love is the pepper and onion mix they put on the dogs.  Sure, digesting that mix usually results in friends and family members getting violently ill, but I think it's worth it.  Sometimes I like to eat their garlic fries as a combo, but only when I feel down on society and think it's time to dish out some justice by finding the most crowded parts of the city and simply breathing amongst the people.

5.  Let's Be Frank (Culver City, CA):  Ok, so they cost $5 a piece and aren't all that filling, but they are reported to be healthier thanks to fewer nitrates and Omega-3 additives.  All that balances out to eating 4-5 "healthy" hot dogs and a sizable bill.  I like to pretend that I'm eating white sushi.

So there you have it!  Now go out there and chow down on some sausage.  You can take that one sexually, if you want.
great for a late night snack (after clubbing if you can get back from the city in time). i've been here maybe 3x, and i don't remember what i ordered but everything i've tried has been yummy.

tooooooop doooooooooog!!!! 

top dog!! top dog! top dog!!! top dog!

When there are over 300 reviews for Top Dog it almost seems pointless to add another. Yet I must review. 

Basically, my dad introduced me to Top Dog, he was a student at UC Berkeley in the '70s and he told me that Top Dog helped him survive dorm living. Today I proudly wear my Top Dog shirt that I got for eating three tops in one sitting and driving a Top Dog employee to SF. Oh Top Dog, don't ever leave us.

the original is still the best!  went to a newer, less grungy top dog on the west side of campus and well, just not the same.

the dogs here are grilled to crisp and juicy perfection on that yummy sesame topped french bun!

my top choices:  1)  Top 2) Cal 3) Kielbasa

amazing how the guy with the pony-tail (who looks like the missing member of the red hot chili peppers) is still working there after 10+ years!  so commanding with those steel-tongs, he really has the aura of a bouncer and not a hotdog griller.

ADDICTION.

I'd eat at Top Dog several times a week if I could get away with it.  Sooo good.

The thought usually starts during the "where should we eat" negotiation.  My girlfriend always nominates the asian land of Foodcourtia across the street, and I reply "sure, that sounds good... or we could go to (whispered)Top Dog...."

A pause.

Then... shouted... like a kid wanting ice cream.  "TOP DOG!!!"

But then she's always like, "my tummy can't handle that right now, I think I'd rather have some noodles..." and because I'm a good boyfriend I don't push it...

*sigh*

Lemon Chicken.  

Oh, how I wish I could go back and relive the first time that my taste buds were introduced to this sweet concoction of citrus and fowl.  Too be honest, I couldn't really taste any lemon...and I'm not sure if it's really made of chicken...but I do know that it tastes great!

I also like the bird dog, and the hot links.  The best is to get a pack of cold dogs and grill them up yourself.  But if you just want to grab one make sure you ask them to butterfly yours as it tastes much better grilled that way.  

TOP DOG ROCKS MY SOCKS!

YES YES YES.

This is the best invention ever. It really is. I guess they cant be given the credit for inventing the hot dog, but they have definitely made it one of my favorite foods. 

When I first started going about 6 years ago, it felt very  "Soup Nazi-esque" and it kind of still is to a point...I think they train people like that. I made the mistake of not explaining that to some friends who hadnt gone there before and they took a little too long to order and were basically sent to the back of the line. 

Some people might find that as rude...but when the food is as good as it is you get over it quick. Learn the ropes, learn the short versions of the names, be alert, make eye contact and be assertive and polite otherwise..."NO SOUP FOR YOU!"

Ordered the top dog today, but decided to get my money back since the cashier was the cook and after taking my money proceeded to prepare my food.  Something about touching money and then touching food grosses me out.  Gloves would have been nice.

Would've been a 1 star, but the employee didn't argue with me about getting my money back.

Meh, over-rated. This is what hot dogs should taste like most of the time, not the cheap mystery-meat ones you get at the store. I come here on guilty occasion to get a sausage in my mouth. No, I didn't just make that sound awkward.

$3 flat for any hot dog. Cash only.

It might just be me, but I seriously can't taste the difference between most of the sausages except the ones that are blatantly flavored like something. They all taste like the beef, pork, chicken they're supposed to be though, which at least re-assures me its actually meat. I enjoy the french roll/bun they use here instead of the standard hot dog bun.

I've had everything now here so here's my personal opinions:

Top Dog Frankfurter - All Beef - particularly more salty than it is beefy - underwhelming, tastes like a saltier regular hot dog

German Frankfurter - 3/4 Beef, 1/4 Pork, Garlic - tastes like a breakfast sausage, you know the ones that can come in patties too? yeah it's super salty too not really any garlic taste

German Bockwurst - 1/2 Pork, 1/2 Veal, Milk, Eggs - okay this one is interesting because it's sort of the lighter/blander tasting sausage because it's not as salty, it breaks away easier when you bite into it because the casing seems to be thinner, you get a mild flavor so it goes great with mustard, onions and sauerkraut if you're into those

Kielbasa/Polish - 2/3 Pork, 1/3 Beef - tastes like a....hot dog. it's just a different shape, seriously you can't really pick out any flavor except the salt, but what do you expect?

German Bratwurst - Pork, Marjoram - aka it's the pork version of the break sausage, just bigger. You've probably tasted this before because it's just ground pork. No marjoram tasted.

Portuguese Linguia - Pork, Wine Vinegar Cured, Oak Smoked - tangy sausage because of the vinegar, slight smokey aftertaste at the end, try it with ketchup and relish

Italian Calabrese - Pork, Paprika, Chili, Fennel - my favorite probably, paprika gives it savory-sweet, chili gives it a bit of heat, and fennel gives it earthiness, top it with mustard and onions and you're set for some great flavors

Louisiana Hot Link - Pork , Beef, Four Kinds of Pepper - real spicy, but you can't taste the pepper because your mouth is already burning from the cayenne hitting your tongue, good if you want the heat, I suggest ketchup and onions

Bird Dog - Turkey, Red & Green Peppers, Cilantro - the less guilty option, but it tastes kinda bland because the peppers and cilantro are more like specs than actual pieces you can taste

Lemon Chicken - Chicken, Fresh Lemon, and Garlic - less salty than the other sausages, VERY SLIGHT hint of lemon (wanted more), and trace of garlic, not that worth it

Smoked Chicken Apple - Chicken, Apple - love/hate here depending on what you like, depends if you like a savory-sweet in your sausage, less salty than other options, and a pretty solid choice for first-timers

The Wienie (Veggie) - Wheat Gluten, Eggplant, Bell Pepper, Onions, Garlic, Fennel, Red Wine - really awkward taste and consistency, I want it to taste like vegetables, but it really tastes just like a bad salty sausage that has a hint of confusing herbs mixed in there just to stick it to you even more

Open late night for the drunk crowd, and the person behind the counter can be a a little impersonal depending on who it is.

3.5 Last year when I was in Berkeley for a conference I skipped out on this one, but this year I had to give it a try. I split a hot link with a friend. I probably wouldn't have chosen the hot link on my own, but it was pretty good. The best part about it was the bun. Crispy and grilled, a little bit chewy. Yum. The link was good too. A bit of spice on the back of your throat, but not unbearable.
I also got lucky and snagged a bite of another friend's calabrese and I liked it better. Overall, good late night drinking food. It's not a must have for me, but I'd take a bite of yours ;)

The guy warming your dogs thinks he's Gordon Ramsay. Listen mate, you can stick your attitude in a bun with some sauerkraut. I get abuse all day at work, I don't need it at lunchtime as well.

The food was feeble, like a ballpark, only a bit cheaper.

Top Dog you delicious bastard you have broken my heart and have left a sick aftertaste in my pristine palate. Maybe Da' Town (Oakland) has spoiled me, MAYBE I'm delusional to think you cared about vegetarians, MAYBE...not all Top Dogs are equal. 

The vegetarian options at this location consist of a single sausage, chili and potato salad. The gentleman (expected me to know the menu) wasn't sure but it didn't matter because it was all he was serving. I found my self at the end of a dog burn into a charcoal weenie with tasteless chili over it. The dog was garbage.

Other Top Dog locations offer many other options and my review only reflects the shitty stand on Durant.

The Honest Truth: Four stars for being a Berkeley staple! The sausages are good.  Great flavor in all of them.  The buns are toasted nicely.  Make sure you listen to the cooks and know what you want because they don't mess around.  Open till 2! But beware of drunk and high college students late at night.  Cash only.

The Details:
Why not five stars you may ask? First, I think their sausages are a little small for their bun.  The first two bites you have to fight through the bun to get to the sausage.  That being said, the sausages are really good! The lemon and the chicken apple both have very good lemon and apple flavors respectively.  Hot link is nice and spicy.  Garlic is good too! Pretty much all of the sausages taste good. Secondly, its a super small joint, gets really crowded, and the service is pretty harsh.  Granted, those things are a result of it being really popular, but sometimes its too much and I'd rather go to La burrita for a late night snack. The cooks will get mad at you if you take too long to decide and you have to constantly make sure someone doesn't steal your order.  I do understand that they're trying to be efficient and I'd get mad at drunk/high college students at 2 in the morning too, but I do appreciate good service as well.  They are fast and efficient, just be prepared for it.  This is definitely a must try if you're in Berkeley!

After just reviewing Chez Panisse I figured it was best to balance things out by giving a nod to the antithesis. Hello, Top Dog! I'll spare you from the corny sausage-in-the-mouth, juicy long meat puns and suffice to say: go hot link or go home. For those of us who don't eat the swine, it's all beef baby, yeaaaaaah. Veggieheads, go for the potato salad. The vegans even have a dog for 'em too. 

Served up but a surly, sarcastic dude with excellent taste in satirical/political comics, your 3am inebriated thought webs will go crazy places.

I fucking love Top Dog so much that I can't help myself everytime I go there and always over-order and end up with hot meat sausages stuck in every orifice of my body.

Chicken Apple in the left ear, Lemon Chicken in the right ear, Kielbasa shoved down my throat, Bockwurst up my nostrils, the all-beef Top Dog up my belly button (I'm an "innie" FYI), and two Louisiana Hot Links shoved up my ass because those are the spicy ones and I'm a size queen.

Like a ten year old slumdog living under a tattered canvas sheet in the bowels of urban Philippines holds onto a spat-out Jolly Rancher found on the street while pickpocketing tourists and giving high-fives to the locals, Top Dog employees take your order, handle your cash, ring up on the register, give you back your change, pull the sausage from the cooler, split open the bread, then serve you the finished product. 

ALL WITH THE SAME HAND.

OK, I admit it, I am a shamless sentimentalist.    I love these hole-in-the-wall "restaurants" that have existed since I was a  child  (can I even call them restaurants?     They serve food).
Yes, the  food is good, but Top Dog is near and dear to my heart because a brother of one of my best friends worked there and helped expand it into a chain ...  when I stopped by I was offered a free "dog" but I declined because I thought I had to pay for it, and i was very frugal in those days.
Try a "dog" ... you won't be  disappointed.

Top Dog hot dogs are quite good. Note that I typically stick to the standard Top Dog Frankfurter, so the 57 varieties of hot dog (exaggeration) don't particularly excite me. Also note that I'm an odd one; you'll probably be excited by the variety if you're less odd.

I don't particularly love their buns, though. I feel that they were better four years ago, although I can't put my finger on what the difference is. My mom feels that they were better back when she went to Berkeley, but she also can't put her finger on the difference. Perhaps they were never really better at all. (Or perhaps they actually deteriorate in tastiness every few years, although that would be an odd business decision for such a famed establishment.)

Warning: do not crumple or fold your cash! If the dude who yells at people for crumpling or folding cash is taking your order, you will be yelled at! And if you cry easily, you will cry!

I wouldn't recommend getting the Top Dog Hot Dog b/c it tastes just like a hot dog from grocery store. I would get the hot link or any of the other sausage type things. Shit I'm getting hungry just thinking about this place. I think I've gained weight just typing this review.

OK, lemme preface this review with full disclosure.  I worked at Top Dog 'way back when, like when a top dog was 35 cents, small coke 10 cents (that'll be 47 cents man, condiments right behind you...NEXT!).  Most expensive dog was the New Yorker at 40 cents.  

To appreciate Top Dog (Southside and Northside anyway), understand the floor show is part of the fee.  Figure in the fair price of the dog and the entertainment from behind the counter (and often on the customer side too) and its a bargain.  

Southside is a zoo -- at best.  The rough trade coming thru those two doors either makes the Dogtender stronger or kills 'em off fast.  Tough Love starts at midnight on Friday and Saturday nights -- drunks in groups large and small, freaks of all shapes and sizes, taxidrivers, hookers, pimps, ex-cons, faculty, shiny-eyed undergrads away from home for the first time but the tie that binds 'em all is their love for the Grilled Dog in all its incarnations.  People either get the freewheelin' close-to-chaos thing or they don't.  The ones that don't stand out from the crowd 'cause they've got a shellshocked look on their faces and tend to back out of the shop as fast as they can, dog in hand or not.  The keepers are the tough breed, the doglovers who have learned to roll with the punches, to dig in their heels, shout out their orders and have their money IN HAND when called upon.  Turn the TV on to Reverend Gene Scott, put KSAN on the radio, lay a six-pack of brew in the ice machine for the crew and their friends and start takin' orders, your shift has begun.  

Northside, on the other hand, is the retirement home for burned out dogtenders, those sensitive individuals who can't manhandle the Southside crowd into submission any longer.  Tame grad students saying 'please', engineering students who are sharp enough to add up their own order and proudly hand over exact change, Divinity students from Holy Hill (so polite they squeak) and classical music lovers of all shades are the Usual Suspects at Northside -- truly a Higher Class bunch of meateaters and apple fritter junkies ("no, I'll have the ORGANIC applejuice with my Louisiana Hot Sausage thank you!).  Ah, many the quiet and peaceful evening there, playing my guitar, gabbing with the pacified regulars and drinking Wild Turkey until closing time.  John Buechenstein dropping in with his Yamaha 6-string, me with my Fender 12 or banjo behind the counter, sharing a pitcher of beer and making music to entertain the lonely Lost Ones.  Victor from Palestine bringing in his oud for a world-music jam session sometimes.  Friends made on both sides of the counter.  

It ain't just the dog you're buying.  And you weren't just a bockwurst and a coke either.  You were PART of it. 

One of the best jobs I ever had.  Working for the single BEST boss I've ever had.  Bar none.  Thanks Dick.

YOU IN THE BACK! WHAT DO YOU WANT?

Step up to the plate, and yell back your order! I have many fond memories wolfing down hot dogs outside after midnight next to the two payphones. There are twelve tasty flavors from which to choose: top dog(tm) frankfurter, German frankfurter, Bockwurst (German), Kielbasa (Polish), Cooked Bratwurst (German), Linguia (Portugese), Calabrese (Italian), Hot Link (Louisiana), Bird Dog, Lemon Chicken, Smoked Chicken Apple, and The Wienie (veggie). They will toast the bun and even fly the dog if you ask. And then there's the 5 or 6 different degrees of mustard and tubs of onion and sauerkraut! It's hot dog heaven! In college, I told myself I was going to try every variety of hot dog before I graduated, but I never got around to it -- I always stuck with the lemon chicken and hot link. Which one is your favorite?

Tips: Don't feel like waiting in line? Buy some cold ones and cook them at home.

Good! I like how they burn the sides of the dog to perfection. Nice brown-black color. I also like the bread. It comes out warm, it's easy to bite into, and it doesn't get shmooshed. 

I like how late they're open till as well. Stopped by here 130am and there was a line.  It's nice to have places open late in Berkeley.

oh.        so.          good!!!!
that pop when you first bite in! i used to almost always get the hot links.

mmmmmmmmmmm cheap and yummy!
i tried to go healthier and got the chicken and apple sausage - which was very good... but then I tasted hubby's Top Dog and wished I had ordered that.

guy behind the counter was very nice and overall i was VERY please.

We hope to get back there at least once before we head back to NY.

Tasty Hot Dogs are hard to find at home... especially at a place like this... you have to buy them and make them at home.. so any place that has a hot dog shop, is ok in our eyes!!!!

After sampling a cheesesteak at Geno's in Phialdelphia, I have a new found respect for Top Dog.  Yes, they try to push their libertarian ideology but at least the food is good and they are not racist.

woo hoo! too bad i do not eat meat anymore.  but when i did, i would wind down my night here with a calabrese or hot link.

the soft gentle crunch of the warm toasted bun and the first break of the hot and juicy sausage skin will forever glisten in my memories of drunken late berkeley nights.

also, this was back when i was young and single and fresh from a club, so it was fun to look cute, feel randy, and stand packed like sardines along side college meat heads, hippies and punks.

The stars are boarding on five... oh yes, it's serious. I love the Soup Nazi nature of this place. Get in line, shout it out: "Calabrese." "Lemon chicken." "Linguica." Move to the right, move to the right... And then there are the huge tubs of mustard and relish and ketchup. I could eat here every day and have no damn shame. Good thing I'm across the bay, because this my friends, is hot dog Utopia.

3 stars, but giving this 1 extra just because it opens super late

I was super hungry and wanted  a quick fix for my stomach. Usually I come here when I have drunk munchies, and I fly up to heaven while eating this baby. But this time, I am hungry as hell and sober... all of a sudden, it doesn't taste so great anymore!!! Maybe it was the hot dog I got, I'm not sure... but $3 for this late night meal isn't bad at all. 

Too bad Costco doesn't have their own hot dog stands out in the streets, because I'd totally choose their $1.50 + drink BIG hot dogs over this!

This is definitely becoming a habit. Bring your cash, a hungry stomach, and forget about that diet. My goal in life is to try each of the different hot dogs (I'm easy to please). So far, I've had the Chicken Apple and Lemon Chicken. Sounds like I need to get eating.

* UPDATE: I had the Bird Dog (3/4/2008)
Calabrese (3/21/2008)
Wiener Dog (4/15/2008)

Downright AMAZING dogs!  My favs are lemon chicken & polish!  

This location can seem a little gruncgy.  Always feel kinda dirty after going here.  I guess I've outgrown the Telegraph Ave. street urchin scene.

Oh man, I can still remember the first time I tried their hot dogs: it was April 21st 2003; a monday night... my friends dragged me out of my house to go all the way to some hot dog place in Berkeley. 

Ok, so I don't remember the first time I tried their hot dogs =), but I do remember thinking they were the best ones I've ever had. There's something about them that makes them so damn good. The simplicity of their hot dogs makes it even better. There's no fuss to it; just a dog in a bun. Done. It's good and it's cheap. Can't beat that. Just with they would open up one on the other side of the bay, though.

Oh Top Dog.  You are like the loyal puppy that is always there when I need you.  Which always seems to be 1:45 in the morning.

And you're everyone's loyal puppy, staying open until we are all giddy with our food in our hands.

Your chicken apple never fails to make me happy.  Excited as a little schoolgirl every time I take a trip to you.  I just wish you were nicer to me than everyone else, but I understand you're a business and I'm just another loyal returning costumer.

I forgot how hot the "Hot" really is.....burning both ways.

Same great dog for over 20 years now.
What else can I say. Yay! I'm a fan

Off the Heezie fo Sheezy... Closest thing to New York Hot Dogs on the West Coast but NYC Sabrett's are Numba One!!!   http://www.sabrett.com/   Check out Gray's Papaya in NYC (see: http://www.yelp.com/biz?biz_id=TzfuYZcsxHathtI6NYEBRA&sort_by=date_desc ) 

There is no greater Dogg in the Bay Area - Bar None!  Hmmm...but I do recall a segment on "Bay Area Back Roads" (see: http://www.bayareabackroads.com ) about Rosamunde Sausage Grill that I have yet to try ! ! !  (see:  http://kron4.com/Global/story.asp?s=3157151 ) 

On the UC Berkeley campus.  Lots of variety.  Great prices (i.e. affordable student pricing).  Parking is non-existent.  Double park and order...

Excellent after a day of sailing with "Cal Sailing" (see: http://www.cal-sailing.org/ ) or http://www.yelp.com/biz/Soz-35lUdP8_giS1MxVX7Q 

Highly Recommended!   Why can't they have a peninsula branch?  Hmmm.... I wonder if I can franchise with them???

Gruss... "jimbo guanzOn"

Pretty damn good for a non meat hot dog! My boyfriend is a super guy. He loves his hot dogs, burgers and beers. He use to always come to top dog with his friends but was a little iffy about taking me since I didn't eat meat. He remembered that this place had a veggie dog and suggested we get some to go. We bought some to take home over the July 4th weekend because we were going to have a BBQ. I got one weinie and he got a bunch of bird and chicken apple dogs. 

We bbqed them the next day. My weinie was so delicious! It had so much flavor and the casing held up well to my knife and fork attack. The sesame bun that came with it was perfecto! Everyone else in the house loved the other dogs, but for me, I was totally sold on my weinie. I will be back and this time I'm grabbing a dozen to go!

mmm.. top dog. what can i say, i usually don't even like hot dogs but this place is sooo good! can't leave without eating 2 or more. just wish there was one just a lil closer =P

i love the listing info: reservations: NO, dress code: CASUAL. it's a freakin hot dog stand!!

Since I was visiting up in Berkeley, I HAD to try Top Dog because everyone is always raving about it.

The menu's short and lists hot dogs in many varieties of meat.  The wall is drowned with political angst.  And the guy cooking the dogs is watching Arrested Development (I like!).  However, he's not wearing gloves and he handles money and dogs all the same (bleh!).  
   
So, I get the dog part...but the top seems to have escaped me.  It's much larger than most of the hot dogs I've eaten but the taste was mediocre.  I blame the people who hyped it up.

Another place recommended by friends who went to Cal.

Great tasty hot dog on an awesome grilled bun.

Plus RC Cola which I haven't had in forever.

I want to go back and try the rest of the choices on the menu!

If you ever find yourself a) slightly broke and hungry b) hanging around the university area or c) craving some meat (real or fake) in your mouth...Top Dog is the place to go. 

Don't expect anything fancy.  But do expect to get a good dog at a good price quickly.  Just walk on up and order and scoot onto the right and wait for your dog and then head on out to the lovely streets of Berkeley with your portable treat! 

I myself am vegetarian and love that this place has a homemade veggie dog.  It's not the best but it definitely has a great flavor and when I'm in the mood for it, totally hits the spot.  My meat eating friends have enjoyed their dogs as well.
I usually don't care for hot dog too much, but this place has this hot dog that made with chicken, garlic, and fresh lemon.  So tasty and different.

Late night dog?  Afternoon snack?  Low budget dinner?

These are all great reasons to come to Top Dog if the variety of great tasting sausages aren't enough to have you coming back for more.

My favorites are:

Calabrese with Russian Mustard and Onions
Chicken Apple Sausage
Hot Link
Bratwurst

With the reasonable prices here, I always leave with an order of two!

This place is definitely a mainstay on the favorites list.

Okay so there are one thousand and one top dogs through out the east bay... and honestly, they're all just as frickn' snap-tastically good, but ... for fun, I'm writing a review for this particular Top Dog because it is home to many a drunk muncie night. After a full evening of acting like I went to berkeley and tossing back the brews... i usually found my self in line waiting for my weiner. Tasty, fast, and usually attracts an interesting crowd of weirdos...this is my place!

Smoked chicken apple FTW

One of the first times I went here, I was pretty drunk.  I thought it was the best hot dog I had ever tasted.  I was hesitant to try it when I was sober, but when I did, I was extremely satisfied.

Although the place doesn't look that great, the food more than makes up for it.  Often, there may be a line waiting for food, but it goes pretty quick.  There are clipped-out comics and articles along the walls to pass the few minutes of waiting.  Every dog is $3 and there is a lot of different choices.  Another thing to mention is that they only accept cash.

A definite recommend to anybody looking for a delicious hot dog.

Very yummy dogs and I wasn't even drunk.

I bet Top Dog is a top late night (after the bars) destination among Berkeley students.

Cheap, quick, hole in the wall place to get hot dogs. I had the hot link and the chicken and apple. Both were good, but nothing amazing. I did like that they didn't use traditional hot dog buns but used sort of like baguettes like they do at Lee's sandwiches or something. They grill it along with the hot dogs, and the hot dogs come with grilled onions if you want. 

Overall, the hot dogs were pretty delicious, and the prices are very reasonable. The downside is that it's cash only, which is pretty lame especially considering the reputation/following this place has. I took off one star because when I went there, the guy handled a bunch of money and then cooked the food, using his hands on the dogs and stuff. Pretty unsanitary, if you ask me. Plus I got a rude vibe from him. If you're looking for a ghetto place to get a quick hotdog fix and eat standing up(seating is very limited) then this is the place for you.

This IS the go to spot for the following:

1) If you're on a Budget
2) Want to hear the Cook yell at customers taking too long to order
3) Late Night munchies
4) Drunk and everything else is closed
5) Just want a Freaking Juicy Honest to God Good Chicken Apple Hot Dog
6) Drunk and just want to hang out 

I miss Top Dog! I can honestly say that with it's simple menu and quirky workers there's no other place that can come close to this Bezerkley landmark!
Late night? Want some cheap food to go? Get a Top Dog! I recommend the chicken apple. It's fast, it's tasty, and it's all sorts of goodness.

Delicious and interesting flavors, addictive bread they use for buns, affordable prices, late night hours...what more can you want out of a hot dog joint?

I'm craving one right now.  Damn those buns!
THE best place for an APPLE CHICKEN dog. It's love in a bite.

This place helps bring back memories of my days as a college student at Cal. I occasionally stop by here whenever I'm in the area and usually order the chicken apple...make that 2 of the chicken apple.

What was the best thing about living on South side during college? Walking by Top Dog on the way home every day. It was a test of self control not to eat hot dogs everyday. In fact, I would intentionally walk down Bowditch on my way home to avoid temptation because if I didn't, I'd walk away with two dogs. When my brother was in town visiting, I introduced him to it and he would order three!

College years were part of my abstinence from red meat, and just so you know that started before my hippie green Cal days. Unfortunately that means I've only tried the chicken apple, lemon chicken and bird dogs. I was appreciative of their selection of meats for the non red meat eater. Furthermore, these aren't your everyday bland chicken and turkey dogs. They're juicy and flavorful and simply amazing. I've made it back to the bay area about once a year since graduation and will go back for a taste of the others. Prices have gone up a bit. Each dog used to be $2.50. *Sigh*, the glory days...

Top Dog used to have this incredible cook who simultaneously took orders from 30+ people crowded haphazardly about the tiny room and spilling out into the side walk, all of whom were ordering different combos of dogs. He worked the evening shift, never took notes and NEVER made a mistake. That man was legendary. The food was still amazing but Top Dog was never the same after he left.

These. Hot Dogs. Are So. Good.

Would have knocked a star off for how tiny tiny tiny and crowded this place could get, but then I remembered that this place is open until like 3am on weekends, and I tapped that star once more.

All their dogs have a delicious snap to it. The dogs aren't huge, but they come out super hot pretty quickly. Every time I come here and get a dog, I leave satisfied. 

Not a super good place if you're dying of starvation unless you dont mind eating two dogs in one sitting. Super good place if you want delicious top quality dogs :D

The best hot dogs i have ever had.  

A couple of notes
1) The hot link is awesome - but very very hot
2) dont forget the potato salad - it is really good
3)  don't go in here wearing any stanford gear (trust me here)
4) Be sure to pick up a 6pack of uncooked hot dogs & buns to grill at home yourself

This is the best Hot Dog spot to go to at 1 in the morning after a great night of drinking... The chili dog is sooooo GOOD and they are fast. It really makes me wonder how they can keep track of everyones order but I guess when you are that drunk anything that simple might appear to be quite difficult. Anyways back to the dog, they have various flavors, toppings, and sizes. All in all it is sooooo worth the $4--$6 it costs. :)

um wtf? They have hot dogs that pop ever so crazily in your mouth. The bread has the right amount of flakiness to softness ratio that does wonders. Hot links are hot as F*** but whatever, I like it anyways. I love this place. OBVS sauerkraut must be added. Whoever doesn't add that condiment is an idiot. 

Oh yea the dude yells at you, so you better know what you're getting.

Me and my friends drive all the way from San Francisco at midnight just to get satisfy our late night Top Dog cravings.  I can never eat just one of these puppies.  I love how they toast the bun because it gives it more texture.  There are several flavors such as chicken apple, keilbasa, polish, and others I can't recall at the moment.  But they are all pretty tasty.  Its simple but pretty friggen good.  I wish the place was just a tad bigger to accomodate more seating but its all good.  I'll eat outside in the cold... just as long as I get my Top Dog fix.

WHERE DID THE TANDOORI CHICKEN SAUSAGE GO??!?!?!!!? it was the best. Ok, that's a lie. Lemon Chicken will always be the best, but close 2nd.  I don't know where Railroad root beer is from either but it's A-OK in my books.

Hot diggity dog! Holy crap is this place good! No wonder why there's like a zillion of these places around the Berkeley campus!

Food: The dogs here are varied and scrumptious!!! Not only are they served hot off the grill, but they're firm on the outside and juicy on the inside. Okay, that sounds kind of gross, but it's a tasty combination. I tried the lemon chicken dog (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/qHmamQPCAKkia9X0uryA8g?select=Iv_budfTredvqfXU0JjGMA)  and dressed it up with tons of sauerkraut and mustard. It was pure heaven. Also, since there are several bins filled with ketchup, relish, onions, mustard, etc. you can accessorize your meat to your liking. So what's the secret to these delicious dogs? Personally, I think that something special happens to the meat since they're stacked on the grill for a long time before they're actually cooked. Either that or the fact that you can smell this place a mile away somehow influences your tastebuds. Or they put crack it them. 

Service: The grill guy is like a robot. He talks so quickly and smoothly that he sounds like an auctioneer. Anyway, the guy knows what he's doing and it shows. 

Atmosphere: This place is essentially a shack with some seats, but I wouldn't eat here unless I really wanted to tick the other customers off. You'd be blocking the counter where you order and pay. Who designed this place? As an added bonus, the walls are plastered with all sorts of Berkeleyesque paraphenalia. 

Synopsis: Top Dog makes top notch dogs.

This is actually more of a 3.5. I would've given this place a a full 4, even 5 star review if it weren't for the cranky attitude we received while paying our bill. Granted we had made the bill paying a little difficult for ourselves (envision two people collectively trying to pay a $6 bill, but unable to find our singles or agree on who and how much should each person pay). "The bill is only $6, you guys gotta project [on getting the $6] or summthin'? Geez..." Give me a break. I had really wanted to come here, too, ever since visiting friends in college and having heard freshman stories as well as positive newspaper and television reviews of Top Dog.
The hot dogs at Top Dog are pretty small, but adventurous and tasty. Another friend, who had been a Berkeley alum, recommend the Lemon Chicken dog for my next visit. This time I had a Kielbasa, evoking memories of my own college days back East. With (pat on back here) my personal selection of sauerkraut, onions and hot mustard, it was delicious, but still... not as good as Pittsburgh, PA's Kielbasa, given size and lack of comparable juiciness, but still pretty decent in comparison to other Bay Area offerings.
I do like the fact that, in addition to variety they have very quick (albeit irritating) service and are open really late (we were there around midnight on a Friday). It does suck that one small dog is $3, and I'd probably need two for a hungry beer night but one has prove to suffice as a filling snack. Yes... mixed feelings, but good times so... I will make it back here one tawdry evening, I'm sure.

Best hot dogs in the bay area as far as I'm concerned. I've had about half the dogs on the menu and tried all the mustards and have never EVER been disappointed, great food for a great price, eating here at any time of day or night is never a bad idea. Although it gets kind of crazy on game days.

The service is definitely unique. There is no line (there's a sign mentioning this) and the cooks/cashiers will skip over you if you're indecisive. Some people are off put by this, since it's not exactly the friendliest customer service, but I think it definitely gives the place some character. It is reminiscent of getting drinks at a crowded bar, if you know exactly what you want, ordering and wait time are very short and painless.

Top Dog was everything my friends hyped it up to be and more.  My friend insisted that we split the hot link - warning me that it would be spicy and blow my mind.  The hot link was indeed savory, spicy, and juicy but it was the toasted sesame bun that won me over.  When we returned to Top Dog the second night in a row, I opted for the "air dog" which was just the toasted bun which I stuffed with sauerkraut, hot mustard, and ketchup.

My friends love the hot link and regular top dog.  My vegetarian friend even got them to cook her veggie dog on foil so that it wouldn't touch the other meat sausages/hot dog links. I cannot wait for my next trip up to Northern California because a stop by Top Dog is inevitable.

Oh my Top Dog!  I miss you so much.  SO much.  
Those were the days in Berkeley, I'd go get myself a hot link somewhere around 2 or 3 times a week.  Incredible.  And they serve RC Cola!!  Seriously!?  Who serves RC these days?!  That's right, that's how these guys stick it to the system, and I love them for that.  I love the anti-establishment propaganda on the wall.  I love how the servers will berate you if you don't know what you want to order, but can instantly do complicated math calculations in their heads to determine how much change you are owed.  And seriously, I haven't even gotten to the food yet.

The buns - incredible, just, like, the perfect size, weight, and texture.  Grilled up just a little bit for that extra crispiness around the outside.

The mustard selection - stoneground AND brown mustard?  I lesser stand would only give you one of those, maybe even only yellow, but the wonderful people at Top Dog want you to have just the right mustard for yourself.

The sausages - man oh man.  My personal favorite is the hot link, but I've never had a bad dog here.  I don't know exactly, but they must have somewhere around 10 different sausages to choose from.  I love this.  This isn't Pink's, you don't get a choice of 2 types of sausages and then they just pile on the cheap toppings, Top Dog really focuses on the product:  the dog.   

Damnit I hate writing these reviews because it just makes me want something I can no longer have.
Why oh why can't you migrate down to Los Angeles?  Why can't you just follow me anywhere I move?  Really, I don't mind having a stalker if that stalker's inital's are T.D. (oh and happens to be a small hot dog establishment and not some creepy guy like Ted Daniels or Theo Davis).

Come in, get verbally abused by the Top Dog dealers, and then enjoy your wonderful Top Dog (I usually get the Chicken Apple, though any sausage on their long menu is sure to satisfy).

If you want to deal with less aggressive Top Dog dealers, and perhaps find shorter lines, you can always go to the quieter, more peaceful Northside location.  

Top Dogs are especially good at 2-3 am for some reason.

Simple, no-nonsense, no-frills establishment.  As good as fast food gets.  Love the bread rolls they use and the plethora of sausages available.  I still haven't managed to get through the entire menu, but my favorite is definitely the smoked chicken apple.  A close second would be the spicy bratwurst.  Beware the hot mustard, though.  It's not for the feint of heart.  Also, unlimited sauerkraut is always a plus!!  

Just avoid this place on Cal football game-days!

I love hot dogs. It's the all American girl in me. Burgers, fries, dogs - the ultimate comfort food.

We walked in and interrupted, errr I mean ordered a polish from the worker, no rapper at the counter singing along to Tupac's greatest hits. (gotta love Berkeley) 

$5.34 and One Pac song later we strode out of there with a polish dog cut in half and a 7 up to wash it down. If it were up to me I would have returned for an encore and another polish dog!!

I never would have guessed that hot dogs could even be that good.  Actually I don't even normally like hot dogs in real life and skip them...but Top Dog is delicious! They have a million different types of hot dogs with all the sauces and it was such a great meal overall.

I would definitely go back again and wish I could have one at this very moment.

A well cooked calabrese with a side of libertarianism - perfect for the late night drunken stumble home or the for the post four hour midterm binge study session.

Ron Paul would be proud.

the things i do for yelp.

like going to -- a hot dog place? why the fck does Top Dog have 225 reviews? 

night. it was lightly raining. there was someone in there being trained. this guy told a story about passing out champagne to everyone last new years eve at the top dog, and wondering if he should do it again. got the dog. there is a *heated* container of sauerkraut. and fancy mustards. 

walked down the street, the light rain coming down, bit down, and was in top dog heaven. wow. this is why. yes. i understand. 

i walked some more, slowly down telegraph. the dog was perfect, and yet there was something missing....

"HEY. HEY. I need to eat. Give me some money. Hey. HEY!"

the guy was literally on my back, walking right behind me. i tried to ignore him but he kept hanging on me. i turned around and he's not even dingy - he's all dressed up, carrying some case, and obviously tweaking out of his mind. 

the top dog experience was now complete.

Tonight was my Friday since I took this Friday of to go to Drakes Brewery Friday Tastings Yeah. So I was craving a Midnight Snackie snack . So Top Dog in Berzerkley called out to me LOL. I could get a snack and people watch at the same time. So I wander in and at first observation FREAK SHOW. A couple of Gals were making out and groping each other, the Counter guys are watching Star Trek but taking orders Seinfeld Soup Nazi style and 5 other guys waiting on their dogs are watching the gals make out. I ordered a Linguica Dog. Their Linguica is supposed to use the same recipe That Stuart Alexander the infamous "San Leandro Sausage King " used. So the Trekkie's served me my Linguica Dog and I dressed it with condiments and enjoyed the hell out of it . While watching the freak show.

Dingy exterior + A don't ask, don't tell policy regarding where and how they store their ingredients + Large vats of mustard, relish, sauerkraut, onions and GASP....Ketchup!!!!  (for a hot dog!  BLASPHEMY!) + Just one step shy of self-service kinda service = NIRVANA.

Somehow, the math just works out.

Great hot dog -- they toasted the bun nicely!! The sausage has the right amount of kick in it! 

It is a little hole in the wall kind of place, but it was packed even in middle of a night!

This is an amazing Berkeley icon.  You walk in to what amounts to a closet with a grill and short counter, and are immediately hit with the savory aromas of grilled gourmet sausages and a chaotic visual hodge podge of lefty radical cartoons and articles plastered over every square inch of the tiny shack's wall space.  Its open very late, and you can always count on a hot grilled German Frankfurter or original classic Top Dog in the wee morning hours.  Just walk up and hollar, "gimme a top!"

Lemon Chicken is hands down my favorite! The Beef Frankfurter is delicious too.

Open late nite..what a plus! 

Great place for toasted Buns and a good size Weiner!!

Great Hot Dog.  Huge fan of the Hot Link and Chicken Apple Sausage is not bad also.   The Hot Link is the best and they always have plenty of condiments and flavors of mustard.  Also the workers are always very chill and good people.  Love the Top Dogg.

One of the over fifty 5 star reviews. A Berkeley institution and perhaps a historical landmark (but please, respect the neighbors). Twelve types of dogs, grilled to perfection on the well seasoned flat top, four choices of mustard, and of course, the sauerkraut. However, I do have a minor concern that the sauerkraut begins to resemble a Cassoulet after a few days. I always dig down deep and drain it before throw it down on my tube steak. And there is still the option of miso soup, served only at the Durant Mothership. When you dine-in, there is the All Top Dog TV Station. I swear, you can't get any of these channels on cable or the dish. Buy a t-shirt and wear it proudly home!

I told my friend how good Top Dog was and she said "I wouldn't peg you as being a hot dog person."  That's the thing - I'm not, but I still really like this place.  The bread is different and the hot dogs are excellently flavored.  My favorite is chicken apple (but I've only tried chicken apple, hot link and lemon chicken).  I want to try the original 'top dog' b/c I saw a lot of people ordering that last time.  Next on my list!

I'm not a big fan of hot dogs, but wow Top Dog makes them seem like gourmet food. I haven't tried any of the sausages that I can't pronounce, but I've tried a bunch of their flavored hot dogs. Hehe flavored hot dogs, sounds like they should be different colored too. Anyways, my favorite is the lemon pepper turkey dog. It is so juicy, and the hot dog itself has a bite of a crisp bite outside, so when you bite into it, it goes snap! then smush!

I really like the food here, although I hear from my friends at Cal that this is the place where people get into fights and shank each other at night, so if you're out in the area late at night on a weekend, beware!

I would crave for hot dogs randomly at timess...

I like all of them... chicken apple, kielbasa, hot link, calabrese, and etc.... Pretty quick service, friendly people, quick food to go...

I mostly had these wonderful hot dogs after going out though around Berkeley... or a study break if i am sick of Peet's or the DC or the Asian Ghetto..

One of the few places that are opened late!

I can never eat just one though to get full.. i need TWO :) what a pig i am!

Berkeley classic. Have to come here. Things you should know:

* Hot links and chicken apple recommended
* Perfect for the late night grumbling stomach
* The griller/cashier is always loud and has an impeccable memory for each patron's order
* The griller/cashier is mostly rude too, which is part of the place's charm
* "Butterfly" and they'll cut the dog in half and grill the inside too
* Delectably toasted buns
* Russian mustard rocks here. Get a lot and pour it on. Your stuffed sinuses will thank me.

Go Bears.

Need a quickie? Well, step into this nookie and you'll end up with a sausage in your mouth in no time!  Make sure to wipe the juices off your face, we don't want to look sloppy do we?

After a long day/night, a quick somewhat filling snack is always good, and top dog fills that spot pretty well.  Regular sized and jumbo sized dogs filled with a assortment of fillings waiting for you to munch on.

The chili here was eh, I loved the one in San Jose (before they changed ownership), and this wasn't quite as good.

All and all, still a good place to drop by for a quick bite or two!

What can I not say that isn't good about this place?

Dirt cheap, great eats, open late. Oh f*** me, I'm in heaven.

WARNING: CASH ONLY!

Top dog = Great food and great prices

The San Jose location is FAR better than any of the Berkeley spots. It has lots of outdoor HEATED seating plus a 7-11 next door. The restaurant nearby shares the outdoor seating so you can eat a bowl of beet soup with your dog!

I've only been once, which was recently, and the hot dog/link or whatever was nothing to write home about. I hate the bread they use too. First it's way too thick just for that sized dog and second it's dry as hell. But also the two guys behind the counter were some assholes. We walk in and they're too busy watching Chapelle's show (like it was a brand new episode or something) cracking up and ignoring us. I'm like "Hello!" And one guy takes our order without even taking his eyes off of the tv screen. They were just too rude. If the food was great and they were rude I could look past it, but blah food and bad service does not fly.

This has got to be the ONLY anarchist hot dog store west of the Mississippi.  The first time take in the surroundings, the 100 square foot store, the fact that every square inch of the walls are blanketed in anarchist newspaper clippings, the staff.  Choose your hot dog from the many varieties avalible, while its being cooked converse with the employee, its always enlightening.  
The cardinal rule of Top Dog is sauerkraut.  Take your hot dog and drench it in all the glorious toppings, in russian mustard (But be careful, its damn hot), in chooped onions and relish and the all important pickled cabbage.  It makes the dog near impossible to eat without making a mess, but it tastes divine.  
To sum up Top Dog in one sentence, "They make a Vegi-Dog taste good"

let me set the scene:  it was 2am on a warm autumn night.  i was 21 years old, and drunk,  in search of berkeley's soul after emigrating from the slums of boston/cambridge.  the tantalizing aroma of roasting meat drew me in from off the street.  the sausage man and i had a long-winded conversation about the gay affair freddie mercury had with david bowie (that was news to me)....

the hot dogs are great!  i've had the calabrese, kielbasa, and chicken apple and all three represent some of the best cuisine one can hope for after ambling out of a bar post last call!

the walls are plastered over with blisteringly anarchist and nihilist clippings.  the people represent a full cross-section of berkeley's eclectic population.

top dog is the essence of berkeley!

great $3 hotdogs with perfectly grilled buns.  what impressed me a lot was the guy's memory of everyone's order.  anyway, only nonstudent there at night, and this block has all the quintessential late night college diet: hot dogs, pizza, donuts, ice cream sandwiches, etc.

Oh how I love you, Top Dog. You are the best when it is late and i am buzzed and hungry. I love your classic Top Dog and your Hot Link and your Kielbasa. I love your potato salad. I love YOU.

When you walk into this Top Dog, you need to know exactly what you want immediately. Otherwise you will get hated on. They have three mustards, relish, ketchup, and onions to decorate your food with. I utilize all but the ketchup to enhance my dog.

My other favorite late night food spot in this area in Fat Slice. Next time I am with my friends from High School, I have promised to buy a Top Dog, dress it up with all the fixings, and then go to Fat Slice and wrap my dog in (fat) slice of greasy pepperoni. I'll have to update after I survive that.

Before I came to top dog I was not a big fan of hot dogs. After I came... yepp, still not a fan. This is one of those joints where everyone has to at least try once if they go to Cal. Well, I tried it once and that will be about the only time I ever go there. A buddy of mine had told me that he wasn't to fond of hot dogs, but he came here and liked it. I ended up going with his recommendation of the chicken apple dog. My recommendation is to just go to costco and buy a bulk pack of chicken apple sausages and save yourself the hassle. 

Heaven forbid you don't know what's on the menu before you come in here, because they will skip right over you with no hesitation. Not only will they skip over you to the next person in line, they will keep skipping you and forget you even existed. The worker didn't use gloves so they handle the money, scratch their balls, pick their nose, and handle your food all at the same time.  Such a great multi tasker I must say, but at least he wore a Japanese little head band which kept him from sweating on the food. It was like the over the hill and over weight black karate kid flipping dogs. 

In the end of it all... 

the dog was just OK and the bun is about 3x to big for the weenie. That is unless you plan on stuffing it with endless amounts of toppings, which then it becomes not a hot dog imo. 

Ill save you guys the trouble and...

"that's what she said"

Well, back in the '74-'75, a "Top" cost .47 cents.  Then it jumped to .55 cents.  There were only two shops back then, Southside and Northside.  Both had 13" b/w TV's showing reruns of "Leave It To Beaver."  The owners were always upfront if they had to change vendors - switching from a New York style dog to a Chicago dog for example.

Top, Kiel, or Bock with a healthy dose of stone ground mustard which is no longer available ;(     My head is spinning.   (Although they have added potato salad, cole slaw, and ice cream bars, I've always wondered why they didn't add French fries.  One response was that it was too complicated and would have distracted from their core business).

The business model is perfect - a one person operation -  grillmaster, cashier, quartermaster, and sometimes peacekeeper.   Many a Top Dog griller have become *very* successful in business, science and medicine.

With lines around the corner during the wee hours of the night, the $3 hella-hyped up dogs are worth the wait... open til 3 in the A.M. on weekends makes for the perfect drunk food haven.. Lemon Chicken dog always is on hit with their top dog frankfurter in close second.. 

It's always funny listening to the order taker yell at the people that aren't ready w/ their order & watching drunken double fisters trying to put on their condiments in the crowded condiments table.. A berkeley trip is never complete without hitting up top dog..

Simply MOUTHGASMIC!!!

Even after graduating from Cal 7 years ago, Top Dog continues to not fail.   You can't go wrong with the Chicken Apple or Lemon Chicken.  Whether you go here at 2pm for a late lunch snack or 2am for a late night drinking snack, you will have an orgasm in your mouth.  And just like sex, once you pop your cherry, you're going to want more.  YUMMMMMM

Because 400 miles separates us, I don't have the luxury of eating here very often.  But when I do plan a trip up north, TD is one place that I always have to stop by.

The Hot Link, Keilbasa and the Bockwurst are my favorites.  My recommendation: if you get two or three dogs per visit like I do, eat the Hot Link last; due to its spiciness, anything you eat after that will taste pretty bland.  (BTW, I add Russian mustard on all of my dogs... even the Hot Link.  It's awesome.)

Also, their buns are SO GOOD.  I think it has to do with the way they "toast" them on the grill.  
  
And it might be a good idea to know what you're getting before you stand in front of the counter... sometimes the guy behind the counter isn't in such a good mood and he'll yell at you for not knowing what you want and make you go to the end of the line.  Some people find this rude but I think it's hilarious; I like to call it the Berkeley Charm.
hello lover...i am a person who loves hot dogs fancy or au natural... and top dog is very nature-all!!! simplicity at its best i must say!  awesome after a fun night parttaking in partaying!!!!!!!!!!

It's really quite impossible to hate Top Dog. Actually, I don't understand how anyone can even dislike it. Top Dog has been and always will be one of the fondest memories of my times at Berkeley. 

When I had under $5 in my pocket and everything else was too expensive, Top Dog was there. When I had an intense case of munchies after a long inebriated night, Top Dog was there.
