When I just needed something interesting to read while chowing down on some of the best hot dogs that have ever invaded my taste buds, Top Dog was there.

Everyone likes to do it their own way (that's what she said?), but my perfect hot dog goes like this: chicken apple on a slightly toasted bun, with relish, onions, tiny bit of mustard, and lots of ketchup. It...is...HEAVEN.

OMG people, calm down.

1. It resembles a stand - that's embedded into a building.
2. There are no seats.

If those are not big enough hints that the hot dog buns are NOT going to taste like a 40dollar Wagyu hot dog bun or the establishment may not have Ina Garten / Alton Brown-esque kitchens, you may want to invest in some COMMON EFin SENSE?

Seriously - I don't know what the f*ck some of you people expect. It's cheap. It's good. And the people are nice. 

My recommendation = The Top Dog Frankfurter.

Bockwurst: 1/2 Pork, 1/4 turkey, 1/4 veal, plus eggs and cream. Or at least that's what I (think I) had down pat in 2002, but the somewhat mystifying website currently challenges that notion: http://www.topdoghotdogs.com/colddogs.html

Do you know how goddamn hard it is now to find a bockwurst anywhere, let alone one that tastes like the stuff here at the iconic Southside location? In the golden days, I had no idea. I took it all for granted.

Top Dog on Durant might have been the first non-DC place where I ever ate in Berkeley when I was visiting the one friend I knew who was already at Cal. I had already enrolled in the school, sight unseen, and was being shown everything I had to look forward to. 

When I became a bona fide Bear, I found a total social scene here right after the bars closed. The line rivaled the mob at Blondie's, and was quickly forced outside because the place can only really fit four people at a time plus maybe two brokeass drunkies jostling about to jack a handful of burning hot sauerkraut on their stumble back up the hill (guil-ty!). 

During more decent hours, everyone was still doing it Top Doggystle at all hours of the day. Soon enough, the furtive professors and random locals in broad daylight looked no less manic than so many frat boys and Oakland teens in the cloak of night.

By sophomore year, I'd easily eaten every sausage twice, whether I was aware of it or not. My favorites: Bockwurst as already mentioned, spicy Calabrese, filling Linguica, Lemon Chicken, Apple Chicken...yeah, that really doesn't narrow it down, but that says something, right?

I learned a whole lot as well from the gruff men and enigmatic women who worked the counter solo. For example, freshman year, I got into a big phase of The Who. As I walked in, a strain of one of the band's more recognizable anthems struck up to accompany my entrance. Semi-wasted (no doubt because this dulled the caustic treatment by the no nonsense workers), I exclaimed, "YEAH! TEENAGE WASTELAND! I LOVE TEENAGE WASTELAND!" The brother behind the counter barked, "It's BABA O'RILEY." Then again, for emphasis, "BABA O'RILEY!!!" A friend of mine got schooled when she was on her cell phone and the man with the spatula shouted, "Get off daddy's cell phone and make your order, or get out!"

So intense was my devotion to this place that I once found a quiet moment to ask for a job. A couple days later, I hauled ass to the Northside location (with a drastically different clientele of residential families and engineering students with the occasional hipster searching for something better than the shit rotting in the walk in friedge of their co-op) to meet the owner. He took a chance on me, and I worked a couple shifts in both main locations, which was about how long I lasted before I got my $20 pity tip from the jar from an awesome girl who helped train me and gave it up.

It was in my few shifts as a Top Dogger that I learned some essential things, such as don't hand people a glass by the rim, don't hand people utensils with your fingers on the part that go in their mouths, don't leave a sack of coins on the street by the owner's car while you take in a 50 lb. box of Brats to try to impress him with your expediency. Funny how I didn't learn this from my anal-retentive parents, but from a go-with-the-flow grassroots entrepreneur who earned his street cred once and for all during the Age of Aquarius.

I also got to see the inner workings of this. Did you know there's an office behind the counter? It's stacked to the ceilings with unruly papers. Can you believe that they line up your sausages chronolically by order, but can also identify them by sight at any stage of cooking in case you forget your place in line? Did you ever pay attention and realize that the workers still don't use electronic registers? They calculate all the tax inclusive prices in their heads while under pressure of a bunch of 'dog fiends, so think twice before you change up your drink selections and sizes, you dipshits! These people are hard core. In the end, I was the chaff that got separated from the very special army of top dogs who can really hang. But hey, I'm happy just to be a layman stuffing my face.

It is way too ironic that the owner (whose name I have forgotten, probably out of pure shame at failing him, even if he was nice about it) was born to German immigrants in New York because I so heavily associate the dogs with one place only; that tiny ass shack in Berkeley as if it is independent of time or location...as if it is a concept or a fabrication floating through the universe of my memory. Also, I have yet to find dogs like this anywhere in the five boroughs, especially at such a selection or with the same ambience. Not that I've looked that hard. Why would I, so long as this place stands?

Whenever I'm working near the UC campus, I always make time for a trip to Top Dog for my lunch.  My personal favorite is the Calebrese which is an Italian sausage made of pork infused with paprika, fennel, and chili. The spices really does it for me.  

I would have given 5 stars, but they don't offer cheese as a condiment.  I got to have my cheddar!!  Oh well, love the German mustard.  

The people who work there are always friendly.  Beats that national chain any day...

This is a glorified hot dog stand. I mean it - really! There is no cash register - they do it all in their heads. Also, the same guy takes orders, cooks your dogs, has conversation with you, gets you drinks, adds your bill - even if it's 1am, even if it's noisy and crowded, even if you're drunk and don't know what you're ordering. The staff's that good. Plus, the other great thing about it is you can sit at the counter, if you don't feel like standing around outside and eating your hot dog.

These hot dogs will make you feel better after a crazy night. And, out of all the Top Dogs, this is the one that has the best crowds and is open the latest (I think). My personal favorite is the chicken apple sausage dog. Plus, all the prices are really cheap. Then I wash it down with lemonade - or worse, get a boba across the street at Sweethearts. But more about that on my Sweethearts' Cafe review...

Top Dog was one of the first places that my RA took us to my freshman year. I was young, and on my own for the first time. Walking here seemed like it took forever, but as I look back...Clark Kerr isn't that far. Haha. The store is small, just a counter, the grill, condiments agains the wall and the exit. I ordered the chicken apple (my favorite) and stood there. The guy looked at me like I was a special kid because I was waiting to pay, and he said some sarcastic comment that made me want to cry. I finally got my chicken apple sausage with yummy grilled bun, paid, threw on condiments, and ran out of there!

As I matured (well, at least I think I matured) and returned a bajillion more times, I realized that the sarcastic comments and bluntness is what makes Top Dog so special. Coming here after a night at the bars is hilarious because of all the drunk people and the cook spitting out witty comments. Almost better than paying for a comedy show!

I would have given this place 5 stars, but I noticed that during my time in Berkeley, the prices slowly creeped up. I still crave Top Dog every once in  a while, and I definitely miss that cook.

P.S. There's a "Berkeley Dog" in SoCal, but it's just not the same. It has the same sausages as Top Dog but they don't have the spunk.

This place is a notch above Pink's on La Brea. I've been there for all occasions and had enjoyed almost everything on their menu. I especially like the bird dog, bockwurst, hot link, kielbasa, bratwurst, and linguica. Slide these gourmet sausages between warm sandwich buns and top it off with a thick bed of sauerkraut, onions, and other condiments and you got yourself something really special--all for $3. My friend who lives in LA said this is the first place he would visit whenever he's in Berkeley. It is good enough to make your day. Standing room only. Take out is encouraged.

If you worked at this fast-moving, order-after-order, late-night joint, you'd be pretty abrasive too when drunkards yelled at each other and wandered aimlessly around instead of placing their orders when the line is down the sidewalk at 1:30am.

Hate to say it, but I love it when the guy behind the counter calls out some drunk idiot for holding up the line and being obnoxious. If you want your hot dog fix, you're going to have to man up and pay attention. Be ready with your order (chicken apple is a solid go-to) because the guy does not have any tolerance for your crap.

During the day though, the same guys are much nicer and ready to converse about books, TV, and current events with a lot more patience. I even got the Samoan-looking guy to offer to lend me the Harry Potter 7 he was reading. Awesome.

Minus 1 star because they raised their prices (I know, it was a while ago, but I'm still not over it) and because I often leave still hungry.

Last night, Top Dog earned a fifth star from me.

I didn't catch the guys name workin last night, but he was hella friendly and chill. I went in last night with my brother and a couple friends last night, pretty late and Top Dog never tasted so good. I don't know if it was the fact that we were all hungry, or that the food just tasted spectacular last night, but it was on point!

After we were done eating our food, we were hanging around out front and the guy workin the shop came out and talked with us for a couple of minutes, and was real chill. One of friends was super thirsty, and kept on bugging him for refills, but he was super friendly and laughed about it. 

It was an all around great TD experience last night. Kudos.

The first time i went to top dog was 2 years ago, when my cousins from san diego visited. You cant miss the place because its right across the street from fraternity/sorority house, but parking is a hassle you gotta find parking on the streets.

There are 12 types of hot dogs to choose from. from top dog FRANKFURTER all beef to the veggie hot dog called the wienie. My fave is the polish hot dog kielbasa. i took a bite from my cousin's hot dog and she had the bratwurst and thats very delicious and the smoked chicken apple is good as well.

Prices are very reasonable.

This place was a popular attraction back in the day.  From what I see now, it still is.  

"Two chicken apples, please".  

Anyone that went to school at Cal or frequented any of the bars surrounding Shattuck and Telegraph will know of this place.  After the bars close, where do people go?  They go to Top Dog.  For many, the purpose of eating here was to sober up from the bars and reflect on the memorable moments of the night.  I, on the other hand, used to go to the bars in hopes of going to Top Dog.    

Since my college days, I haven't gone back.  So I decided to take my Bun there since I never got to share with her the joy of Top Dog with her.  Whether it was raining or hailing, I was determined to get us some dogs.  When we got there, the rain stopped periodically for us to walk around.  We got there around 12:20AM, which was the perfect time since, the drunkard rush haven't hit the spot yet.  Right after we put in our order for two chicken apple sausages, it began.  Five Asian kids walked in carrying with them a cloud of alcohol intoxication and the munchies.  While waiting for our dogs, I peered out the door and saw a few crowds walking in Top Dog's direction.  We missed the drunkard rush by a hair.  

Our order was as I remembered.  Bundled in a toasted sesame seed bun and masterfully wrapped at insane speeds in a protective sheet of paper was a fresh from the grill chicken apple sausage ready to be sent to my belly.  With a bar of condiments at my disposal, I loaded the puppy up with everything possible.  Condiments of choice include the usual relish, sauerkraut, onions, and of course the ketchup and two kinds of mustard.  I can't get enough of condiments.  Back in the day, I could slam dunk two into the rim of my mouth.  Being late and all, thought I'd just get one.  

From what I saw, everything's the same.  Same little cashier, same grill, same menu, and same crazy unorganized lines when busy were present.  Those same memories of fun and college idiocy came right back in an instant.  One thing different is this time I had the opportunity to share my dog with Bun.

Here it is.  Hands down, bar none, this place has the best hot dogs in the universe.  Sorry you NY transplants and sorry you Pink lovers but they couldn't hold my Top Dog Kielbasa to shake it.  

10 years ago I used to get a hot link and a pack of cigarettes.  Now, it's the Kielbasa but all their dogs are good and college student priced.

If a hot dog place was any more happenin', it'd be a nightclub. I've been dreaming of these dogs for days now. I know that was a weird sentence, but screw you. This place is awesome!

I apologize for calling them "hot dogs." They're sausages to me. It took me a long time to want to try Top Dog. I was so used to paying over $3 for crappier-than-Costco hot dogs that I just couldn't bring myself to eat anything non-wholesale. This has changed, as Top Dog is both delicious and cheap! $5.50 got us a Top Dog Frankfurter and a Hot Link. Both were extremely delicious! The low fat Lemon Chicken was really good, and I didn't feel like I was dying after. 

No cash registers, just order and the give the guy money. They remember everything. I can't even remember where I live, half the time... They described customers based on clothing, "guy in the hat, what do you want?.." I was "guy in striped shirt." Apparently, I wasn't familiar with my shirt, and had to pause to glance at it... sad.

Order uncooked sausages and buns in a pack, and sizzle them up at home. 

Cash only. Street parking or pay for the garage (haha, right).

Hot dogs.  Best served late and drunk.  Or mid-day after a trip to the Strawberry Canyon Pool.

Either way, nothing beats a simple, piping hot wiener in a bun.  Everyone knows that.  I don't even need to be telling you.  

Even if other restaurants were open to draw in the drunk/high/backfromthelibrary crowd that rolls in around 1:30 am, I still believe Top Dog would maintain a customer base with an almost religious zeal for their meat sticks and bread. mmmmmmm... meat sticks....

I just realized I made a Berkeley list, but never reviewed Top Dog.  What a travesty!

The Top Dog on Durant is a Berkeley staple.  You can't visit Berkeley without trying Top Dog.  Things to know:

-Cash only, have it out and ready when you order (but don't be stupid and count all your money in the street)
-Know what you want to order before stepping inside.  The guy working there will yell at you and skip you in line if you don't know what you want.
-You can buy packaged Top Dogs to grill yourself at home
-They have vegetarian and kosher options
-My personal favorites are the lemon chicken and original Top Dog, but I don't think you can really go wrong with anything on their menu
-If you're hungry, order two (or three)
-If you don't like waiting in lines or servers with some attitude, just go to the Center or Hearst locations... they aren't open as late but the people working there are more chill
-They are open til 2am during the week, 3am on Fridays and Saturdays. Expect drunk college kids in line past midnight.
-If you are a drunk college kid and miss the 3am deadline, sorry...you're gonna have to find a way to the 24 hour Jack in the Box on Telegraph!

HOW DID I NOT REVIEW TOP DOG YET?!

lemon chicken
apple chicken
hot link

sis: i miss being in norcal
me: dude...don't u miss the good food?
sis: i'm hungry...wats open? (1:45am)
me: nothing...this is norcal....top dog?

so we hella rush over to top dog....arrived @ 1:55am (HELLL YEAH JUST IN TIME)
0 to 60 in 1.5 min bitchess~~ GO CAMRY!! eat my DUST!!!!!!!!!!!!

1 lemon chicken
1 apple chicken
by 2am....the place got PACKED.....as always....ahhh~ memories hehehe


they've been trying to be sneaky with the price increase. the hotdog guy swears it's been the same price for the last 5 yrs but i SWEAR 5 years ago they were 2.25...i think it's now 2.75!? whaaaa~~~ but watever....still soooo worth it~

i wear the beaver mustard stained tshirt...with pride.

Top Dog,  yes.

So many many choices. Standing outside, late at night, with no real line, just a wall of people like a bar standing, waiting and watching as the different orders warm burn and heat on the grill. 

This was the ending to many wonderful nights.

So many choices, that you never got bored.  I never asked what the different meats were or what the names meant, i didn't care. I just felt sorry for vegans.
this is what a hot dog place should be...

part of the magic was watching the cook remember each order and the order each person arrived....

Not that it matters but they sell cigarettes here, and never refused a book of matches.

I am a lemon chicken kind of guy. You'll find yours.

This is serious hot dog place, no really I'm totally serious.
How much do I love this place? Well one of my prized possessions is my dark blue "Top Dog" T-shirt. The only downside to the T-shirt is that I think some girls are reading a little too much into it.

Good memories this place while I was a student at Cal.  Where else would I go grab a kielbasa between classes, or hot after a late night studying at the library?

A bunch of us old Cal guys met for dinner, and wanted to go to Top Dog afterwards.  Yeah, we were still hungry, and made room for something from Top Dog.  Good to know that this place still hits the spot.

me:  i'll have a chicken n' apple hot dog.

hot dog guy:  ok

me:  oh, do you have any french fries?  garlic fries would be killer!

hot dog guy:  [looks at me sternly] I DON'T FRY ANYTHING. [then turns away]

me:  ok [walks away with tail tucked between legs]


ok, so everyone knows Top Dog has got some pretty damn good hot dogs.  great.  what disappoints me is the service.  it's the i-am-so-popular-i-don't-have-to-be-nice attitude that will keep me from ever coming back.  what makes it worse is that Top Dog is not a service-heavy joint... it's a stand up, order-to-go fast food establishment.  this doesn't require heavy effort on their part.  

although not terribly horrible in any sense, this condescending service has happened enough times for me at Top Dog to prevent me from ever coming back.

i just wanted some fries.  =/

******

5/15/07 update:  this review applies to the location on Durant.  i just visited the Center location this past wknd with no issues.

Vegetarians beware, this place is completely disgusting.

I wanted to try something different and new today, so I walked in, asked the guy behind the counter if they had any veggie dogs.  He replied yes, and I asked him if they were any good.  He replied yes again.  So I paid him the $3 and tipped a dollar and waited a couple of minutes.  

While I was waiting I stared at the menu intently, noticing a very disgusting option called "Bird Dog".  Then I noticed he used his bare hand to grab about ten hot dogs out of a plastic bag and placed it on the grill.  Is this for real?  Whatever happened to plastic gloves?

Minutes later he comes out with a yes--a veggie dog--but it's burnt black on all fours, and it was not even good--it was disgusting.  The bun was disgusting and unfortunately, the KETCHUP was disgusting, too.  Can you believe it?  The KETCHUP.  Seriously, the ketchup lacked that three-dimensional tomato vinegar taste.

The place stinks and I say nay.

top dogs seriously shits on what is notoriously claimed to be the best hot dog  - pinks (in LA)! BUT perhaps, i shouldnt even compare the two as top dogs is more sausage than hot dog. moving along...ive been a faithful top dog muncher for a little over 9 years now.  a friend of mine introduced me to this fine establishment when i was a sophomore in highschool and ive been hooked ever since! during the time i lived in berkeley i stuffed my face silly with top dogs atleast three times a week! TOP DOG IS THE SHIT! 

my two top favorite flavors are the lousianna hot link and the calabrese. the word "spicy" or "hot" is to often used and abused i pay no attention, and usually order food extra extra spicy [if a certain place is able to adjust the level of spicyness] or add hot sauce to kick it up a notch. the "hot" in the lousianna hot link lives up to its name that i dont have to add additional condiments [russian mustard] to kick up the spicyness. the calabrese is a burst of flavors and spices! all hot dogs are so flavorful i can eat them without any additional condiments and enjoy the pureness of what i know to be the best hot dog EVARRRR! 

top dog 1 holds many fond memories in my heart. from post clubbing grub during my highschool and up to my college days, to walking 3 blocks over to meet friends for a snack at 2 in the morning, to random trips to berkeley just for top dog with friends. 

some usefull advice: know what you want to order in advance if you want to avoid being ignored! look up the menu online, ask a friend, seek advice from the homeless people right outside of the joint , do whatever you need to.  during peak hours once you are called upon to place your order and if you take longer than 5 seconds to answer you will be skipped and ignored! trust me, thats not an overexaggeration. if you want an authentic top dog experience try it one saturday night after 1 am :) 

chains like DOG OUT's that ive seen sprout throughout san ramon and san francisco... SHAME ON YOU!!! for over pricing your dogs but most of all for not living up to what it truly means to grill top dogs like the true top dog grillers at top dog 1! true top dog grillers move fast and give effecient service! although sometimes bitchy, they know how to show starving college students, newbies, and drunk post partiers who's boss! they will surely put the smack down! 

Top Dog 1 on durant is the real deal!

----

5 stars: i am a loyal customer and cannot live without this place/restaurant!

4 stars: consistently great food. a place i would definitely frequent if i dont already.

3 stars: good food. id come back for more if a particular craving for something specific they offer hit me. 

2 stars: for the sheer reason of convenience and semi mediocre food [but convenience being the majority of reason] id come back.

1 star: id never be caught dead in the place ever ever again.

A Certain Someone has raved about Top Dog for a while.  It's not that I have any issues with Top Dog, but really could a hot dog be that good? 

So I finally went to day - and the answer is: I guess.  I had the Bockwurst with russian mustard.  It was very good.  

Did it live up to the completely mythic stories...not so much.  But it was very good

(Dedicated to Ignatius Jacques Reilly, Hot Dog Vendor Sans Pareil)

I find it just a little scary
That this review (my centenary)
Is not some careful dissertation
Of some chef's cutting-edge creations.
But instead, I sing of rockets
That don't burn holes in gourmands' pockets
This screed is an examination
Of classic, lowbrow delectation.

Why, you ask would someone blog
A paean to the humble dog?
No 'Best Friend' would, through its ingestion
Engender bouts of indigestion!

I'd counter that those with good friends
Will come to know that in the end
That any friend, however nice
Is freighted with incumbent vice
We must embrace  the total package
Just as we do our hot dog snack-age

I studied vice --- perhaps, with relish?
In NYC --- I don't embellish ---
When I declare to you, "Hands down,
Dey got da BEST dogs in dat town!"
Nathan's and Grey's Papaya claim
A transcendant weenie fame
But even carts on its dirty streets
Will furnish existential treats
They're small, they're cheap, they've got some snap
They come anointed with standard crap
Not like the salads that often cover
The meat of a Chicago sausage lover

Top Dog comes about as close
To giving me a West Coast dose
Of New York Heaven (on a bun)
So I guess (for here) they're number one
Their dogs are thin; they're grilled and hot
(I also recommend their Brat).

Remember, as the Germans say,
When you are over Berkeley way
"All things come to an end, it's true:
- except the sausage, which has two."

"HOT DOGS RULE, YO!"

"What'll you have Optimus Prime?" 

"I have a Hot Link for Optimus Prime!" 

I plan on walking into Top Dog with my Optimus Prime shirt every time now.  Being called Optimus Prime is just too good not to.  

Man does one of the mustard burn like wasabi.  Me loves it.

Oh Top Dog...how you draw me in with the savory smell of fresh hot dogs and the sweet sounds of Erykah Badu in the background.  Made it here a few days ago to fulfill my hot dog craving.  Joey P, Marc, and I ordered the Top Dog, Kielbasa, and Hot Link.  All were very tasty.  I love the many options of meat you can get here, but I did feel as though I was missing something.  I was missing that 'snap' you hear when you bite into other hot dogs.  I guess I was hoping for something similar to Hot Dogger in Davis.  But all in all, Top Dog is one of my go-to spots for hot dogs out here in the bay area.

In my recollection, the only things that changed about this place are its price and employees.  And that's not even by that much.  I remember going to Top Dog when I was 16 years old, ordering up a Kielbasa or Hot Link, and enjoying my dogs in the wee nights on the street in front of the shop. None of that has changed.

I was craving a quick fix by 12:30pm yesterday and since I just stopped by Berkeley Hat Company, I immediately thought of Top Dog.  I knew hungry students wouldn't be swarming around since it was a holiday so I took a quick stroll there.  As soon as I walked in to the tiny red brick shop, I nearly found the whole Berkeley Fire Department and a Berkeley Police Officer ordering lunch there too.  The guys were nice enough to let me squeeze in the door and order my Kielbasa (See picture).  After ordering from the front door, I went to wait for the dog through the back door and observed their set up.  Nothing had changed.  Everything was still in its original places; a condiment row consisting of ketchup, mustard, mayo, sauerkraut, onions, and relish.  Oh...the fond memories!  Every hot dog is only $3 tax included already. I paid my $3 and in a few more minutes it was ready to pick-up. For $1.25 more, you can get a small soda.

The only condiments I always eat with my hot dogs are ketchup and relish.  I found everything I needed and more.  With my mouth salivating, I hurried outside to consume my prized possession.  It was the exact same as I remembered it; I was biting into a hot juicy kielbasa wrapped in a toasted sesame white roll.  With each bite, there was a sort of crunch as I broke the sausage casing and immediately felt a burst of flavor and juices dancing around in my mouth.  I savored each bite until there was no more.  The time it took me to consume the whole hot dog took no more than 1 minute.  The trip was long overdue and definitely worth it.  

Check out Top Dog if you want a cheap hot dog with good flavor, fast friendly service, and a place to call your second home.  It'll hit the spot!

I love sausage.  

Top Dog is a sausage lover's heaven.  

Normally I am a Calabrese or Kielbasa kinda girl but lately I've had a hankering for something spicy, really spicy.  The Louisiana Hot Link has filled my spicy craving and then some.  Literally this sausage was so hot I was sweating.  I had to dab the perspiration off my forehead...but it was delicious and worth every spicy bite.  

I like that you can get your dogs hot and enjoy them there (pre music shopping at Amoeba) , or you can buy some cold dogs and take them home for later.  These are great for parties, camping trips, everyday...and they taste just as delicious when you BBQ them yourself.  

Also the guy behind the counter is awesome.  He's always got like 10 orders cooking and somehow he never misses a beat.  5 stars for that guy.

Thank you, thank you, thank you for being open late whenever I'm about to faint from hunger at 2:30 AM or so. And for the "STFU and eat your damn hot dog" signs on the doors, and liberal propaganda on the inner walls. And for the way the people at the grill always remember who ordered precisely what flavor. That never fails to charm and impress me.

In retrospect, I suppose no one really knows what goes into hot dogs, do they? In that case, add Tops (with kraut, ketchup, and relish) to my growing list of undeniably suspicious guilty pleasures.

You mention Top Dog to me and I'll probably come back with about 50 different drunken college stories that involve this place. I must have went here 3 times a week when I was in college (no joke).  Especially after practice with a few teammates where I would eat two, drink a root beer then pass out. If i still had eating habit like this I would weight 400lbs. 

Typical Friday- drink, drink, drink -- hungry? Top Dog.  I'm still amazed how the grill guy knows exactly who has paid and whos hot dog is who's without something to write on. That's really an impressive skill when you have 100 drunk college kids screaming at you. 

My vote is the Chicken Apple with spicy brown mustard. Also the Railroad root beer might be the best soft drink anywhere. I just can't seem to find it anywhere else but here and believe me I have tried.

The classic Top Dog, Bock, and Lemon Chicken also get top marks.

I only make it here about once a year now but each time I do I'm in Heaven.  Now if they could only open one on Polk street....

Top Dog is the Top Dog.

I don't really have anything to say that hasn't been said about Top Dog in it's 225+ reviews, but who cares.  

Top Dog has the BEST dogs in the Bay Area.  There, I said it!  They offer a load of different dogs, but they all taste the same...  DELICIOUS!  

I always get the Lemon Chicken Dog, however I have heard good things about the Bird Dog.

They are usually crowded during Lunch, Dinner, and "After the Bars Close" hours, however they still manage to get your orders right and to you quickly.  

You can't be a sanitation freak or claustrophobic if you plan on coming here.

Okay.......Top dog at Durrant is not just about the dogs. It is the Top Dog experience. Lets face it There are better Dogs to be had(casper's in the Dimond).

What could be more fun at 1.30 am in sleepy Berkeley town than hitting up a crowded, drunken, rocking Top Dog. The African American front man Repeating 10-15 orders and always adding to it...(an amazing feat not easily accomplished).....His side kick the grill master extraordinaire railing through orders with just as much proficiency as the ringleader. Never have I received the wrong order and I always leave satisfied and ready for bed......Is there a better Dog...yes. Is there a better late night experience in Berkeley...Hells no.

Amongst my friends and I, this place is called Top "drunken" Dog.  Oh the fond memories of stumbling in late at night after parties. There would usually be a line by then, so we'd huddle outside in a group, waiting for our turn.

The freshly made hot dogs always taste delicious. I love how the bread is grilled as well, and the sausages are always plump and juicy. The condiments (ketchup, mustard, onions, relish, sauerkraut) are placed at the side, where you can self cater to your liking. The top dog, lemon chicken and hot link are amongst my favorites. 

It's open until 2am, perfect place for a cheap yet delicious bite to eat. And remember, cash only. If in need, there's a BofA ATM conveniently located right across the street.

when a dog rivals costco, that's when i even consider it a good hot dog!.... i'm serious

I ordered the frankfurter "all beef from the east.. maaaan" for 3 bucks.. you get to eat a top dog without paying top dollar!

the dog tastes good and its on a toasted bun! yumm.. the man making the dogs knows his stuff, but it's kind of a turn off when he handles your money then uses his bare hands to touch the buns.. THATS A NO NO..

the other dogs are good too.. smoked apple was interesting

the place is really small.. only standing room enough for one group to finish their dogs as the next group files in

the condiments are self serve.. i made the mistake of putting the russian mustard.. IT WAS TOO HORSE RADISH POTENT FOR ME.. i nearly died every other bite!

love that its open late!.. would come back& recommend to others!!!

Open late: check!
Fast moving line: check!
$3 hot dogs: check!
French roll buns: check!

Bratwurst is bomb. Sauerkraut at the condiment station. I'm in love. Except for the cash only biznass...

Ya know, I was expecting like some sort of specialized hot dog sort of place. Not exactly like a gourmet hot dog spot...but like a hot dog place offering cheese toppings, grilled onions, jalapenos, bacon wraps, etc. Something sinfully fatty. 

I can't exactly fault them for these expectations I conjured up, but I hope they would consider these suggestions?

The good thing about this place is that your hot dog is made to order, so there will be some waiting. The prices are pretty good, around $3 a pop. 

Hot dogs:
Hot Links
Chicken Apple Sausage
Lemon Chicken
Frankfurter
Linguica
Vegan (sorry, but your hotdog is cooked in the same area where the meat ones are)

I don't know what else they've got, but there weren't more than 12 varieties I believe. 

They are open until 3am. They've got mustard, ketchup, sauerkraut, spicy mustard, relish, etc. All the cool articles, bumper (they sell some) stickers, cartoons, etc. are a reminder of how long this Berkeley fixture  has been around. 

They also sell donuts and chips. Definitely a visit if you are out late, craving a hotdog, or need a Berkeley experience.

ONE IMPORTANT THING: CASH ONLY. The closest ATM is at the plaza across the street inside the Mexican restaurant.

ok.... i usually don't go to this place sober.  i can't say how i get there un-sober either (i just don' t remember).  

but after top dog, i am back to the norm.  

"that hits the spot!!!"

you'll always hear  this from me or someone with a similar experience...

I really like a good snap to any hot dog or sausage when you bite into it, which is what you get with Top Dog!

Friday 8/10/12
6pm-ish

LOCATION: Block away from Cal Berkeley. On Durant Ave btw Telegraph Ave & Bosworth St. Garage parking few blocks in vicinity or enjoy the "trips around" trying to find street parking.

RESTAURANT: It's quite small with 3-4 stools at the counter, 2-doors for entrance/exit, & condiment station. Pick your choice of "dog", place your order, stand to the side or by the door, wait for your dog, put your condiments on, then step outside to let others in. Very common to just see ppl standing outside eating their Top Dog.

EATS: Dogs cost $3 bucks & they have about a dozen to select from (Thanks Pamela S for menu shot http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/qHmamQPCAKkia9X0uryA8g?select=nFfca2I2F0Az2JmGQmAipg#zTIWbTl8Z5QlTYHa7hLq-w) BF-J & I have YET to go wrong with anything from Top Dog over the years. Great eats & continued patrons right here!

$3 Garlic Frank of satisfaction http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/qHmamQPCAKkia9X0uryA8g?select=nFfca2I2F0Az2JmGQmAipg#bKxNRyjFENiPc5mysBIJyA

It's a known fact that if you are ever in Berkeley, it's a must to stop by at Top Dog and try their hot dogs. Low prices, late-night hours and convenient location make Top Dog a popular destination for students and sausage devotees of all ages.  Sausages range from hot links with a serious kick to classic kielbasa to  vegetarian and even chicken-apple. The chefs cook all sausages to order on the grill, and even the buns are griddled to a golden crisp.  But beware it gets packed during late-nights especially on the weekends.  And the brotha running the joint has no patience for you if you don't know what you want to order.  One night I had a friend order a beef hot dog and the dude skipped her because she didn't know the name which was "The Top Dog"... Kinda funny actually! LOL! Aside from that, In my opinion, this is quite possibly the best hot dog joint in the bay area. Trust me just go there and try one. 

Pros: Inexpensive, Open Late, Best hot dogs ever

Cons: Bad Parking, Small establishment

Well, it was good, but not "The Best Restaurant in SF Area" good.  For several weeks in the summer of 2006, my main Yelp page (with downtown SF zip code) showed Top Dog 1 at the top of Best of Yelp for Restaurants category.  I guess Berkeley was close enough to my zip code to include Top Dog 1 in the ranking.  We Yelpers make fun of Citysearch's Best of List, but having Top Dog #1 over all the great restaurants in SF indicated that Best of Yelp is not perfect.

Two kinds of places to be cautious of when looking at strong Yelp ratings:
(1) Places populated by drunk people.  The influence of alcohol may have contributed to why they had such a great experience at the establishment.
(2) Nostalgic destinations.  Looking back at college days, when you are sick and tired of dorm food, but you have very little money, Top Dog might have tasted like a piece of heaven, and going back to Top Dog may bring back great memories.  However, for a non-Berkeley graduate like myself, it's just good hotdog.

So, while I didn't think Top Dog was the best restaurant in SF area, I did like their food.  Buns were not the usual plain soft buns, but deli sandwich kind, and they toast it on the hot surface.  They have a good selection of meat choices, including Hot Link (spicy, $2.75).  For drinks, they only have RC products; no Coke or Pepsi.  Place is very small with only 5 counter seats.  Plan on carrying out.               

Being a food crazed idiot I am, I actually crossed the Bay Bridge and made a trip to Berkeley for the purpose of trying Top Dog 1.  It sure wasn't worth the bridge Toll I had to pay, but I would definitely go back if I was in Berkeley for another purpose.

I have never craved a long hard juicy piece of meat in my life like I had when I was trashed last week. 

I mean honestly.... being drunk totally gets me wanting that shit like mad.  I couldn't take my mind off of it?  My body was aching like crazy for it.   I only needed one to go wild and to fill the need.  I wanted one thing in my mouth and nothing else can measure up.

Mmm.....sooo gooood.  

Lemon Chicken Dog at Top Dog.  Nothing is better than that.  Talk about a delicious juicy and just plain perfect specimen of meat.

$2.75 for a late night snack??  Oh yes.  And they have fantastic condiments, like the uber-spicy (like wasabi-spicy) Russian Mustard and yummy yummy sauerkraut.  I had the Bockwurst...next time I make it out to Berkeley, I will try more...and most likely, my rating will go up to 5 stars!

Inna brought lunch back to the office a few days ago, and I had the all beef New York Style frankfurter with cheese.  By the time I had my dog it was pretty cold, but it was still really good.  Can't wait to try it hot, and something spicy!  Yum.  I heart Inna.   =)

4 stars if your sober, 5 million stars if you're not.  I've read a few of the other reviews, and rather than re-hash the thousand drunken moments, the beggers outside, the amazing memory of homey inside, or the stumbly bumbly times outside, I thought I'd just write a poem.

Oh toppy toppy toppy dog
you taste so good you clear the fog
devine invasion for the drunk
you lifted me out of my funk

and though I drank enough to yack
you cradled me and rubbed my back
and brought me back from the abyss
I went out back and took a piss.

*sigh* i miss you top dog.

Them dogs were good.  Small little joint run efficiently making sure you get your dogs hot.  I went with a bunch of ladies (and AJ) and it was almost more fun watching them chow down.  Every once in a while, everybody loves a good hot dog.  And when I say everybody, I mean all you meat eaters.

Top Dog has been a Berkeley Icon for decades! The only thing that has changed is the prices have gone up over that time. Everything is still the same.

Great weiners. I used to love the original Top Dog, Then I branched out into the Kielbasa, Brockwurst, and finally the Louisianna Hot link! Yum!
Mustard, relish, and kraut! I think these still have the same condiment dispensers from long ago. Same articles and stickers on the wall, like "Malarky". Irreverance to read while you stuff your face with a tasty, hot dog!

A "Top" now costs $3. Soda a buck. 

I used to stop here at night before I walked to Moffit Library to study for an exam late into the night, the only time I would have studied. Then I would go home, sleep, and wake up just before the test, and went strait to the test. No interaction anywhere before, because I would forget what I crammed the night before with each conscious interaction of my brain, draining my memory banks from what I filled them with the night before.

I was a terrible student with bad study habits, but I tested pretty well. 

Was it my strategy library and no pre-test distractions, or was it the Top Dogs?

Recipe:
 
Toast 1 hot dog bun.
 
Add 1 Hot Link sausage or hot dog?  Call it what you will... it was juicy and spicy.
 
Squirt a straight line of Russian Mustard (good stuff) over the hot dog.
 
Pile on a mountain of delicious hot sauerkraut - my favorite.
 
Glare at the Ketchup, and say, "Ketchup is bad, ketchup is BAD."
 
 
Admire.
Sniff.
Devour.
 
Take what's left of Rob's and eat that, too.
 
Yummy to my tummy.
 
I can see now why this place is so well-known.  It's a good hot dog, for sure.  
Next time, I will try the other varieties.

Service was friendly.
Food is cheap.
What more do you want?


NOTE:  Cash only - there is an ATM at the end of the street.

Second stop of an indulgent day away from the usual grind, much to Cal Alum Sarah E's reminiscent excitement.

Ahead of me, the petite and slender Kay T. orders a classic Top Dog Frankfurter (kosher, all beef). Next, the slim and svelte Heather E. rings up a Lemon Chicken (chicken, fresh lemon, garlic).  Then 5'5", 210lb orc-ish me...
 
"Can I have the Veggie, please."
He pauses, double takes, and asks...
"You know there's no meat in that, right , big guy?"
"Yes, sir", I laugh.

For the next few minutes, the griddle sizzled and popped with the occasional clatter of tongs turning and pressing buns and sausages to crisp perfection. The little closet of a shoppe wafted with savory aromatics, as we waited, all the while being entertained by ranty witty soliloquys of socio-political aspersions.

A minute after that, I stood outside, diving into one of the tastiest kraut, onion, and mustard slathered veggie-dogs I've ever had.  Head spinning from beer and rapid-fire discourse.

One of the best ways I can think of to spend $3.
_____________________________________________________
Ah, Berkeley... I kind of have a crush on everything about you.

I don't know about some of these clowns in here with their reviews.  This old Berkeley standby still serves up the juiciest, most flavorful hot dogs anywhere.  Trust me, I've tried Nathan's in NY, Pink's in LA and almost everywhere in between.  You can't top Top Dog!  

I believe the dogs are still no more than $3.  What a deal on a real hot dog!  And they grill them here like they're suppose to, not steamed or boiled.  

Try the Frankfurters and the Kielbasas with some sauerkraut, onions and mustard.  I don't know about all the other foo foo stuff they serve up now.  I don't remember so many options being offered when I lived up north.  

A most appropriate title...Top Dog is still the king of dogs!

In all my years of visiting Berkeley, I never stopped into Top Dog.  It was only after finding out that La Val's had closed, and I was left to eat a depressing slice of pizza at Fat Slice, that I decided I needed something else to cheer me up.  I stopped off at Top Dog for a Brat.  It hit the spot...really well.  You really can't mess up a dog...but quality ingredients do count alot.  I almost wanted to order another.  But, I had my fill for the afternoon.  I'll save the double-order for the next time.
The veg wrap is cheap and filling. The service is super quick. Nice place to go to if you need something healthy and inexpensive in a hurry.
That crappy owner isn't usually there. The people there are friendly.

A good replacement for the inexpensive/fast Northside sandwich shop.

I'm not sure what the deal is with this place. They are somewhat affiliated with Hummingbird and Hummingbird Express. My theory is that Hummingbird is where you go if you want a custom sandwich (or one of their Middle Eastern plates/shakes), Hummingbird Express is for not customized sandwiches, and Zach's Snacks....is....ummm.....not customized sandwiches + snack items? Or maybe just if you're too lazy to cross the street to Hummingbird?

I'm also not sure about the name.....they sometimes flyer Northside, and on those flyers, the store is called "Zak's Snacks". But the name on the store is "Zach's Snacks". That's how I spell my name, so let's go with that.

Food: Generic sandwich. I had the tuna. Large quantity of tuna - good! Not much mixed in, so that's ok because I'm pretty picky, although I would have been OK with some diced pickles. The bread was kinda tough. It did include a tomato slice and slice of pickle also.

Price: $4.99 for a sandwich, chips, and drink. Pretty ridiculous deal. Especially since a burger meal is like $6.50-$7 everywhere on Northside.

Service: Very friendly! When I was there, it was the girl who often flyers Northside. Glad she didn't have to do that today in the rain. No complaints, very fast.

Overall, I'm adding Zach's Snacks to my list of places to get sandwiches. I really miss Seven Palms for their cheap + customizable sandwich, but Zach's Snacks is a reasonable (and cheaper!) substitute.

Sorry guys, you had potential to have your own niche. But the food is boring and there is nothing unique. And hummingbird cafe across the street is a lot better. I got the tuna sandwich and the bread is so hard and meat w/e. And macaroni salad was gross.

General: I come to the I-House Café often, as I live right next door to it (just about as convenient as it gets)! You walk up and order at the cashiers, pay, and then wait for your number to be called (which can be found on your receipt). Indoor and outdoor seating is nice, especially since they redecorated this year! This is a prime location for study groups and meetings.

Food: The food is pretty delicious. I love the Farmer's Market Salad; I add the strip steak to it! You can't go wrong with any of the build-your-own sandwiches. The gourmet sandwiches are good, but the ones I've tried aren't quite as filling. I love the late night flat bread pizzas, although fair warning -- they usually have run out of many of the ingredients by the time I get there, and my options are limited.

Beverages: Most of the time, the staff keeps water sitting out in a big container with mint or fruit slices in it, which is so good that you don't even need a soda. The coffees are great, but a little pricey!

Service: This is the one downside -- don't expect quick service, and don't expect your food to come quickly. They have two registers up front with one to two people working the front at a time, and they get pretty caught up taking orders, making coffees, and calling out the orders. It won't take years, but it could take a solid 20 minutes.

Great location, nice interior. The staff isn't bad either. The food is pretty good (I wish they served breakfast all day). They stopped closing at midnight, which sucks. They could also use way more outlets. But a good spot.

Good = Not having to get something in order to study. Well, at least getting away with it because the workers didn't seem to care. 

Bad = Random people coming in and doing random things like staring at other people. Like literally, just staring. 

Good = Having a plug close by.. sort of. Not as many as I would like. but adequate enough. 

Bad = Parking is bad unless you go on a holiday like i did. I can only imagine a regular school day, fo-get-aboutit!

Good = Cool flat panels that flash front page news articles from around the world.

Bad = Quite small with small selection of goods. 

Good = Cool old building with a cool history and reason for existing. Read about it. http://ihouse.berkeley.edu/i/history.html

Bad = Young folks all around making me feel old. 

Good = Hours are great... if you can get the parking. 

Overall: Good but not great. Haven't had their food/drinks/service. Good environment overall and good hours. Only 3 stars because i have to go back to get the aforementioned items in order to have a complete review. Otherwise it'd be premature and unfair, right?

I used to love this place, but after reading a couple of bad reviews I was a little nervous. I had a latte in the morning, and I was actually suprised at how good it was.  I decided to go back for lunch and try some of their food.  I tried their lamb shwarma and it was amazing.  I'm really excited to have a place on campus that I can go to study and get good food.

This place is a perfect place to stop by on the way to class and pick up fruit or coffee or a delicious chocolate croissant. 

They have self serve water on the side and the staff is really chill. 

Also a great place to hang out and study.

Food here is ok. Not much flavor. The best thing on the menu is the nachos, lasagna, and breakfast burrito. I really only go to I house for their coffees which are good. It also is a really popular place to study. And their staff are nice.

The I House Cafe is well worth the hike up the hill to get there.  With coffee, snacks and wifi, what better place is there to study?  As an added bonus, the chicken pesto is delicious and they serve wine and beer for the much needed occasional study break.  And who can resist that foreign charm?

Alas, the I House of my youth has changed.  While the views and charm of the interior remain, the food and management seem to have undergone a decidedly downward change.  The I House of yore did not take over 30 minutes to make a simple sandwich, did not callously disregard increasingly angry customers, did not serve a salad with overly oily, soggy lettuce.  Ah, nostalgia, you are a fickle friend...

So I guess I-House Cafe changed its management! Food is a bit overpriced, but actually pretty good. Granted, I've only tried the sandwiches, but I've seen other people's orders of the pizza and quesadillas and other yummy things. I've heard the quesadillas are a must-have. 

The coffee is good too! 

Only thing is, their closing times are extremely arbitrary.. it seems to depend on what time the employees that day feel like closing. Sometimes it's 11pm, sometimes 11:45pm, sometimes 12am. Not a huge deal, but can be slightly inconvenient. 

Pro tip: If you come here when they're almost closing, sometimes they give you your order of coffee or pastry for free.. hehe :)

Really convenient place to do some light studying/ people watching. I-House Cafe gives off such a cool vibe - probably because of all the international students in the area. People are easy to talk to, and I think old(er) men play intense games of chess in the back in the evenings. All of these things make I-House a special spot on the UC Berkeley campus. 

Foodwise: 
Their sandwiches are honestly pretty standard. Make sure to get it on focaccia bread though (nice and herby with a great crunchy/chewy texture)! I usually get the roast beef with sprouts, tomatoes, onions, lettuce, mayo, mustard. Again, standard.

Service: 
Usually fine, but when I went earlier this week the cashier was being an impatient jerk. I ordered a roast beef sandwich right after my friend and he decided to put in the order right away - assuming I wanted the same condiments as my friend. Eeehhhh so I ended up a very boring tomato-less, sprout-less, bland roast beef sandwich on whole wheat bread that tasted like 

I wanted to ask them to remake the sandwich for me... but didnt want to be a total biatch and nibbled on the plain sandwich unworthy of my 7 bucks. =( and for that, minus one star! 

(The actual i-house is AWESOME though!! I stayed there summer '08 and had a blast. met tons of cool people I still keep in touch with)

This place is OVER PRICED for gross food. 
I would only go back if I was on the run and needed a bagel or something. 
I had the cesar salad from here and my dressing literally looked and tasted like flavored mayo. 

They have a "vietnamese" sandwich that looked like Roger Rabbit assembled (spinach with sliced carrots in my banh mi??? YUCK!)

Go to the Boalt Law cafe, better food at the least!!!!!
I really like it here, not because it is that fantastic (it would be closed by now if it was anywhere else) but because it is convenient, quiet, eatable food at an affordable price.

S.e.M. and I, curious to compare this spot to la Strada, the coffee house we more habitually frequent down the hill and down the block, 

Getting there: if you're on foot or on a bike coming from the west, it's a shlep, as the International House is perched at the uppermost part of campus. [For those of us seeking a modest aerobic challenge this may be a good thing.]

The tea, of the bag variety, is unremarkable, but it does have  a variety of selections. By Berkeley standards barista speed was excruciatingly slow.

The outdoor seating pace is ample, with separate northern and southern patios, although there's a feng shui issue that could likely be worked out with more tables. 

S.e.M. liked the indoors, with lots of wood and odd iron light fixtures from the Olde West. I thought it seemed like something from a cheap Zorro movie.

Points for a couple of vertical plasma screens above the coffee accessories bar displaying the front pages of newspapers from across the globe. 

We might well go back, even venturing to try the food, if only to verify the horror stories recounted by the other reviewers.

Pastrami sandwiches should be bursting with pastrami! One thin slice of pastrami?? ridiculous. Luckily it was a delicious slice, though sad in portion, so 3-stars. The focaccia was decent as well.

Mocha Bianca. I was sipping away when suddenly I realized my stomach was hurting. When I found it was because my coffee was too sweet, I went back to fix it. The barista was friendly and added more milk, but the sweetness was too overbearing. I ended up throwing it away after a couple more sips.

Nice setting to study, ok food, but Caffe Strada a block down is a better alternative.

I drink coffee and study here. The coffee is pretty decent, and the food is allright, I've had their bagels with egg, and Turkey Sandwich. Pretty standard, but the plus is if you are actually able to score a place to study.

Bumping them up one star because I visited today and saw they had updated food options. Ordered a chicken sandwich and it was as delicious as it sounded! Only thing is that it's expensive for how much you get. I paid $8 for a fairly small sandwich and a "side salad" that was actually just about two large spoonfuls of barely flavored pasta salad.

Ordered a white mocha again and wished I hadn't because it was still powdery. Come on, at least mix it a bit with espresso so that it all dissolves and so I don't have all that powder collected at the edges of the bottom of the cup + floating around on top. Even constantly mixing between sips didn't dissolve most of it. The way they put it together is strange. Most places do syrup-espresso-milk but this place does powder-milk-espresso...which is prob why their powder is not mixing well -___- makes me question if the powder is actually white chocolate or just some powdered creamer. At the very least, glad their espresso machine isn't completely automated like some other places

Noticed their interior was renovated with new chairs and seats, but it's quite dark! So I'd stick to studying by the windows (only one outlet by the door in that area, unfortunately)

This is a pretty convenient place to grab a quick bite and some caffeine during the day. However, the food tends to be pricey and I wouldn't recommend the coffee here. I usually get some kind of Tazo tea and the spicy chicken sandwich or the pesto chicken pasta. The chocolate croissants aren't bad either.
Coffee isn't the best (as you can see from the other reviews), but this is a great place to go when it's too wet and cold outside.  Beware of the school schedule, you might not find a seat!
International setting with an americanized menu which is deliciously satisfying..although my phone cannot find the free wi-fi, but its cool

Food: I ordered a typical breakfast meal, spinach omelet, toast, bread and soup. The food was very bleh for my taste. It wasn't very good but it wasn't very bad. It's just your typical breakfast that you could probably make at home. Nothing really special about it, but then again, it is a dining hall. How special can it get?

I really thought I was just going to go in for a quick bite and get out but they take quite a while to prepare you food! I originally got it "for here" but because they took so long I had to get "to go". So if you are on a time crunch, this is NOT the place to go!

Price: It was decently priced. A little bit of a rip off for what you get, but I guess they have to factor in the price of paying someone to cook it for you. 

Service: Wasn't any, you bus yourself, like any other dining hall. 

Ambiance: kinda dark and old, musty looking. I thought it would be more quiet but it's actually kinda loud in there. It's the neutral, background type hum always going on in the background (I guess from making food or something?). So it's still a nice place to go and study but not if you want it really quiet.

I've only had a couple things on their menu, but have been satisfied so far.  For less than $6 you can get a large mixed-greens salad with 2 scoops of tuna and a wedge of foccacia.  This is what I usually get, when I feel the need to eat salad.  I prefer this place to Cafe Zeb (in the law school) - it's cheaper and you get your food faster.

Asked for the chicken sandwich with no bacon. In the past has come with a generous side salad, this time a tiny spoonful of rice was given, but I decided not to question the person working at the cash register and just take my food. Got home and bit into my sandwich to find EXTRA bacon. I clearly stated no bacon two times. This is the first time I've had pork in two years. And my frio was awful.

i like the ambiance here, but i never seem to get what i order. case in point: chef salad, hold the ham. it came with turkey (lunch meat), whole black olives, gigantic red peppers, 5 cucumber slices, 1 hard boiled egg, shredded cheddar cheese and red onion. basically, they concocted their own salad. but for 6 bucks and change, they throw in a piece of focaccia and lint on the egg. sit outside because the view is nice and you (hopefully) wont get sticky-gross tables.

This place deserves 4 stars for their amazing hummus and mezze plate alone. 

But wait there's more:
-Awesome view
-Cool flatscreen with the day's international headlines from newspapers around the world
-Myriad of accents and languages being spoken around you
-Delicious iced chai teas

Another Berkeley favorite of mine :)

yes yes...coffee and food suck.

the only reason why i'm giving it 3 stars is because i live upstairs and sometimes i want a beer....or a pitcher. sometimes i want to study. this is a great place to do both. simultaneously.
Coffee and food are awful.  t one saving grace is its location.  Nice place to study since it has outlet and wifi for Cal studets.

This is probably one of the more convenient coffee spots for people living on Frat row. They just got new ownership so the place is looking a lot better. However, the line for the food and the wait for your drink gets a little excessive. Not to mention the fact that their stuff is pretty darn overpriced. 
Pro: they take credit card! (Getting rarer and rarer in Berkeley).

I work on campus toward the top of the hill, and for lunch I usually head to north side or telegraph.  And whenever I get really tired of those options, I think and think and remember that I love the sandwiches at the I-House cafe.  I always end up choosing between the portabello sandwich and the eggplant sandwich, both of which are hearty, tasty sandwiches served with a nice salad.  The last time I went, I made the mistake of ordering the mozzarella sandwich, which was just mozzarella, tomato, and mustard on a white roll.  Not good at all.  But I'll still go back for the portabello or eggplant.  They also toast up a pretty decent bagel with cream cheese, tomato, and cucumber for those mornings when I need something more than my usual instant oatmeal.

In antediluvian times (that's long ago) they didn't have food in the cafe, only soft drinks and coffee. In those days - remember, it was after Adam and Eve, just before the big rainfall - Starbucks & Co hadn't invented all those frivolous mixtures of caffeine, chocolate, soy, skimmed milk, chai, syrup, and other ingredients that make out of a 35 cents cuppa a drink that costs now approximately as much as a full tank of gas cost then. Espresso machines were fairly new then, and the coffee was good and bitter, at least in my memory. The rest of my lunch money was spent on carrot cake, a perfect balancing act to the coffee. What was best then, is still the best today at the I-House Cafe: the atmosphere to read, study, discuss, hang out, philosophize about the world, professors, and the relatively bad food at the cafe. I still go there once or twice a year. Every student should. There are better places for drinks and food on or near campus. But the I-House cafe is a destination like Cody's Books. No, wait, that has gone out of business.

Can't stress how much I love this place. Mood-lighting is great, very warm. Late hours. Cool, friendly, international people. And I recommend the mocha glacier drink if you miss Starbucks-style frappuccinos. Yum!

Only 3 strikes against this place: 1) long walk up a steep hill, 2) sometimes seating is hard to find, and 3) romantic lighting is dim lighting, which is not very conducive to studying. 

Nevertheless, iHouse cafe is probably my favorite cafe in the area.

I ordered a caramel frio. um... this is my first time, so I thought it was supposed to be some sort of a blended drink, but they gave me a latte-ish looking drink. okay fine. I'm not sure if it's supposed to have THAT much milk, but the lady basically filled up the cup mostly milk... and i paid 4.08 for that. I mean... I think it's kind of pricy. the "frio" was okay, but I could go somewhere else. 

for studying, it's nice. but i feel like it's packed most of the time. 

maybe they should have a couple more workers...

Wow, I think I just found my new escape from the library! 

Find a seat next to the window and just sit and relax. Window seats offer a great view of the bay. Cafe is rather relaxing and not so crowded (maybe bc it's spring break) 

Here are the pros!!
**Good location 
**Free wifi (Airbears)
**7am-12am daily!
**No foul smell or homeless people (not to mention there a few good looking europeans once in a while =D)

Cons: 
**Pricey food/drinks + small portions (food is not so good)
**Slightly dim inside
**Not so much outlets 

Recommend that you come here and study sometimes if Stacks gets too depressing :)

I have to say the only thing that the I-House Cafe has going for it is how close it is to me, the fact that they have beer, and the atmosphere that I find awesome for studying, dicking around with friends, or just playing some bridge with some crazy grad students. 

The food is quite bland and a bit overpriced for my tastes. It is pretty filling but I wouldn't go out of my way for it. There aren't that many seats in the place because a lot of people come and don't really buy anything. A lot of people don't even seem like they're I-House residents. I come here to study or play bridge but at least I buy something! A lot of people also leads to really bad acoustics. There have been many times where I can't even hear what the person across from me is saying unless I try awfully hard because it does get packed and a lot of people talking just doesn't work. 

The I-House Cafe still rocks though!

I work at I-House and will pop into the cafe for a cup of coffee or an occasional bagel/breakfast burrito. The coffee is okay, I enjoy their bagels (the cream cheese for some reason is my favorite thing, I will eat all of it!), and a breakfast burrito is very filling. I've had a sandwich here once, it was okay, the bread seemed a bit stale. Some of the pasta salads are good if you need a quick snack to go. The service can be slow, especially if there is a line. 

I think the best reason to come to the cafe is for the atmosphere - there always seems to be tons of students huddled over their laptops studying intensely. It also seems to be a good place for study groups. And it's true you can study here without making a purchase - the cafe staff is pretty relaxed.
Nothing works, not the outlets, not the tables, not the internet. Never going back.

It's a beautiful, stimulating study spot where you don't have to buy anything if you don't want to. It's warm, it's cozy, you get a great view of the bay through the large windows, and you can get strawberry-or-lemon-flavored water for free! The one time I bought hot chocolate, I got it within a minute of ordering it, and it was delicious. Same with the chocolate chip cookies here. I love taking a walk here just to grab a seat and do my homework.

why o why are the cookies so bad?


but love the patio and the hours....
I don't understand the hype regarding this place, the food here is just ok...nothing special.  Basically its a bunch of students sprawled out on multiple tables with their laptops.
Yeah, I agree with the last post, 2 stars for the coffee, six stars for the hotties.  As far as Berkeley goes, of course.

When I lived upstairs in the International House and missed a meal at the cafeteria, I twice made the mistake of eating here rather than going out.  Both meals I had tasted as if they were leftovers that had been sitting in the freezer and simply thrown into the oven or microwave when I ordered.
Also, they have Italian sodas and coffee and such, but I never bothered getting any.

A lot has already been said about the International House Cafe. It is a great place to study, but there's not many outlets. The food is kinda pricey and has a limited selection. You have to really know what is good. Living a block away for a whole year. I have gone through the entire menu more or less. Here is my recommendations:

- Breakfast Burrito
- Pesto Chicken Pasta
- Arugula Priscutto Pasta
- Spicy Chicken Sandwich

I am a former resident of the house, and when I lived there, I went to the cafe a lot, for the atmosphere mostly. There are language groups that meet frequently during the school year for conversation hours, as well as weekly chess games. My friends and I spent many hours studying at this spot. I remember being pleased with the morning bagel or croissant sandwiches, and the occasional latte. 
It's an amazing view of the bay on a good day, too.

And, yes, my favorite coffee in Berkeley is a block away (at La Strada,) so only in a hurry did I buy it here.

I ma bias because I worked at this joint in the 70s and I will always remember the regulars.TRhis place has a crowd problem and now a problem with freeloaders.This place is still a business that must make money to exist.The internet is good and bad for the cafe.I feel thatsome of the campers"like me" who use the internet and milk a latte for hours,at least you bought a latte,some folks are only a small coffee cheap and then stay on the internet.I will buy some food also along with a couple drinks.I feeel that it is money well spent.The food can vary from employee to employee but that is human nature.Some of the breakfast items are rather bland.Lunch is better.The sandwiches are good.Prices sure have gone up,but that is the way it is everywhere.I still will always like to people watch here.The people are from all over the world just like the name of the cafe.Never boring.

Met up with a buddy here yesterday to get some practice games in before the National Scrabble Championships beginning next weekend.

I only had a large chai tea. Sweetened, which I like, but a bit on the sugary side (works for me, maybe not for everybody). Next time I come here, I'll try some food - prices seemed fair.

The inside is pretty dark, and the front room can get pretty sunny (and hot!), so if you're hanging out in the afternoon, you may find yourself moving inside.

But yeah, a fun option all in all - I'll return!

As an aside, it's also a nice change from having to drive through downtown Berkeley.

The I-House Cafe is one of my favorites near campus since it is usually not too crowded, has beers on tap in addition to coffee and tea, and serves tasty food including healthy options for cheap.  On my most recent visit, I got a large beet salad with generous amounts of red and golden beets, portobello mushrooms and cheese for $6.  It was very fresh and satisfying.

There is also outdoor seating with great views and a dog-friendly patio.

The ambiance in I House Cafe definitely makes it a great go to place when you want to meet up with friends, or just study on your own.  But I'm not here to rate the environment or the service - they're both somewhere in between decent and good in my book.  But the food that they sell here is a little off.  I tried the various different pastas that they offer, and...  well, I'm not going to try to get fancy describing these: they're not good.  The bread on the side is good sometimes.  Really hit or miss - get it while it's fresh, it's great; get it while it's a few hours old, yea... big Meh.

Okay, the coffee is kinda crap which is why one should always get iced. Then it's supposed to be a little watery. 
Here is why you go. There is this huge building with a lot of international students. Seriously, who can resist the cute accents and men with good shoes. Also it is across the street from the law school. 
If you want to meat (I mean meet) some friendly international sophisticated types you should definitely spend a little time here. Sometimes, a sexy type A law student finds their way in here as well. I never leave without at least one suggestive smile.

The electronic newspapers are pretty cool. You don't really see many of those around too much. They are a great thing to read if you are waiting on your food or beverage. This is a great place to study as there is free internet and decently behaved people around you. They never have any shady people there because of some reason.

I get the Nachos here quite a bit. I wouldn't recommend them though. If you are feeling like munching down on some good nachos, La Burrita would be a better bet. Sometime I'm just too lazy to walk down the hill so I go for these.

The best food item here is without a doubt the Arugula Priscutto Pasta. Get that little buy and you'll be set. Foreign students are always super nice and willing to meet new people. They are more often then not good looking as well ;-D

The International House Cafe is the best cafe in Berkeley to engage in that practice known as "eye-f*cking."  (Please see review of Free Speech Movement Cafe, Berkeley CA, for the definition.)

It is the cafe with the highest number of attractive people, most of whom you will see only once and never see again.  The typical clientele consists of a whole bunch of international students, fraternity and sorority types, the occasional co-op denizen, and the permanent homeless person.

The drinks are average, the food is decent.  The mezze plate and the hot chicken sandwich are pretty good, as are the fruit salad and nachos.  Most of the tables require jimmying with napkins to stop the wobbling, in addition to a quick wipe-down to remove the traces of biscotti that seem endemic to this particular cafe.

Good luck finding a table at night!  Be sure to arrive early, or hope that one of your friends has a table to him or herself in the corner.  Be sure to strip down to all but a t-shirt as it gets unbearably hot.  There are usually a few good hours--usually around dinnertime to about 8 pm--in which to get anything productive done, as later than that the stereo turns to crazy beat-heavy dance and world music and international kids come down to drink glasses of Salmon Bay chardonnay, and down pitchers of Heineken.  I usually studied through the resultant noise, trying to read up for poli sci but ending up eye-f*cking that one girl from the sorority down the street.  

I miss college.

I've totally forgotten about this place. Back in the day, there weren't too many places that were open past 10pm so this was a reliable hangout after those hours. Good international people watching to boot

Better than most student cafes in the area.  Its up a hill, so only fit foreign people go there.  Great place to people watch - you'll see and hear a lot of different types.  One of the few places fit for coffee and studying but also where you can grab a beer or two with pals.

Coffee's alright... most of the food is overpriced, but tastes pretty fresh (I'm talking about the cafe, not the cafeteria - GROSS.)

There's big windows to look down Bancroft and - unlike Cafe Milano - more than four outlets!
I stopped in before a concert at the Greek Theatre and grabbed a cappuccino.  Good quality milk and espresso beans, hot, and excellent in flavor.  Service seemed good.

A touch on the overpriced side, but there's a good vibe, plenty of interior and exterior seating, and they have yummy mozzarella-tomato salad that goes well with that much-needed glass of white wine on an otherwise tedious Wednesday afternoon. Hurrah for transnational drinking and dining!

I-House Cafe is a great place to grab coffee with a friend. There is always an ample amount of seating, the coffee isn't bad, and the foreigners are always up to something in the cafe. It's probably one of the best people watching spots in Berkeley. On a nice sunny day, the balcony is a pleasant spot to sit and watch the hoards of students walking to and from class. I don't think the food is anything special. The cafe serves basic sandwiches and a few pasta dishes, but I wouldn't go here just to grab some food. Make sure you order your sandwich on focaccia bread, which is very greasy and adds tons of flavor to the sandwiches.

Newly renovated, has some very nice view down bancroft. The iced white mocha is on the sweet side. I heard they offer late night now! Great place to go study if you're sick of libraries - I personally prefer here because I can actually eat, talk, move, etc. without getting shushed or having my food taken away by library staff :). Free wifi, open till midnight.

The food here is usually pretty surprisingly good! BUT the service is horrible. They all stand around and are so inefficient. They are not helpful nor friendly. Boo to the bad service, but at least the prices and food are ok.

Living close-by over the past few years has meant I've tried most things on the menu. I guess this means things aren't too bad. 

I really enjoy the:
tomato mozzarella salad
arugula pasta salad
avocado mozzarella sandwich
mezze plate- flatbread, dolma, feta, salad, and hummus. 

The coffee is pretty below par... if you need caffeine you should try an espresso drink if you don't want burnt coffee. And, avoid the mocha bianca if you don't want to feel like you are drinking pure syrup.


Overall, a nice place to study or catch up with friends with a beautiful view of the bay.

I lived at the I-House for some months. I stopped getting coffee here as soon as I discovered Cafe Strada, one block down. It's watery and not too tasty. But then again there's a fabulous patio and lots of people eager to make friends.

The food (sandwiches and salads, nachos, etc.) is suitable if you're living there. If you're not, it's not worth walking up there.

Oh, I-house.  How I miss your overpriced burnt coffee and greasy foccacia.  

No, seriously.  I attempted to analyze many an angsty French novel here.  If you're going to do the same, may I suggest ordering the beer instead of the coffee?  It really gets the creative juices flowing.   And try to avoid the nachos when it's late and you're tired and wishing you were a physics major so you could invent a time machine and go back in time and kill Proust, who was a pompous ass.

I have a love/hate relationship with the I House cafe... On the one hand, it offered me the ability to escape the library and be more productive in my studies. On the other hand, it gave me the ability to be more productive in my studies because I spent at least 20 hours a week there studying during my undergrad career. I had always been one to avoid the library (really, it kind of gives me the creeps, I used to tell people I had a library-o-phobia) and so I discovered this cafe early on in my college years, probably about halfway through my freshman year and it blessed/haunted me the rest of my years at Berkeley. 

The coffee and food are both so so, they always played loud annoying music that I had to cover up with my own from my laptop, there was a huge lack of outlets and it was always a fight to get one (or a kind request to share an outlet), the staff seemed to think they were the coolest kids on campus, and there were always creepy old international students hitting on young unsuspecting undergrad girls, but for some reason the I House cafe was my safe haven for studying. 

There were a lot of tables and my favorite were the two or three about halfway back along the mirrored wall (apparently everyone elses favorite too cause they were always the most coveted). Despite the decent amount of tables for a cafe, it was necessary to get there early or hope to get lucky because this place was always packed on a weeknight (somehow though the smelly chess players in the corner always managed to get their two or three tables and keep them all night...or maybe they just never left? either way they were ALWAYS there). 

Oh I House cafe...how I love/hate/miss you...

This dining common is close to campus and has a beautiful wooden dining room with massive high ceilings for that collegiate feel. Prices are decent, but there is free wireless internet. The food is not the greatest, but it is good enough and quality is compensated by the wide selection. There's no service here as you have to bus your own tray afterwards. The patio on a sunny day is the best place to sit and inside is perfect for feeling melancholic on rainy days.

I-house recently changed ownership, so everything before August 2011 is void.
