(Normally I don't write really mean reviews for not-so-good places, but I just had too...)

I used to think I hated the old ownership, given that they couldn't make a white mocha or latte correctly... but that has all recently changed. I've come into here a few times as I love studying here (they always have tables and it's a nice cozy environment), but let me get to why I rated them one star:

I came in around 4pm and ordered a Caramel Frio (obviously, a Frio is something similar to a Frappucino right? Anyone who ever goes to Starbucks can figure that out no? Shouldn't someone who works in a coffee shop WHERE THEIR MENU HAS IT DISPLAYED know what a Frio is? OBVIOUSLY somewhere my logic is flawed somewhere because I end up having to wait 15 minutes for my drink... And normally, I wouldn't be TOO happy nor unhappy about this, but seeing as everyone else AFTER me had gotten their drinks right away... I was getting a little frustrated.

But, that's not the worst part. After waiting for 15 minutes, I go up to the cashier and I ask her (pretty nicely), "Hi, excuse me... are you making my Frio by chance?" And she just kind of looks at me very confusedly. She then proceeds to help out the customers (it was a pretty busy day), until 5 minutes later, she asks the boss, "What is a Frio?" UMM HELLO. WHOAAA ALARMS GO OFF IN MY HEAD. And the boss asks her to ask the Chefs. She comes up to me, again 5 minutes later, and says that, "Oh, actually we don't have a blender at the moment... so we'll just refund your money."

Hmm okay, frustrated off my beeping a** and then I have to wait another 5-10  minutes for my refund from the owner, who gives me an extra dollar because I'm guessing she could sense the frustration in my face/body/tone-of voice.

But, to talk on the quality of the coffee, my roommate often goes to I-house and she let me try their coffee/mochas a few times and they are horrendous. Powdery and nothing like how coffee should taste. 

Given that they seem to be specializing more towards food, I will cut them a little slack..... Meh, no. 

Given that I had to wait 30 minutes for my NO DRINK and hello, no compensation for waiting (how do you guys actually run a business? I drink a lot of coffee, so retaining me as a customer probably would have been better for business) got me to writing this lengthy and very angry review.

Well actually, I want to say one nice thing. The girl who was new and didn't know what a Frio was turned out to be very nice and sincere, so I have to say if she gained a little more experience... she would probably make for an excellent barista/cashier.

I-house = NO-GO. At least until they learn how to be a cafe.

another thing i miss about living in berkeley:

wednesday nights, before i would head to blake's and get drunk and act ridiculous, i would go to the international house cafe to participate in the italian conversation hour. i needed the practice, sure, but i obviously only went so that i could have beers and make eyes at the italian professor who presided over conversation hour: giovanni.

almost every girl i knew who took italian with him swooned. it was no surprise that italian conversation hour consisted of about 90% girls who had a crush on giovanni and 10% dudes who actually were interested in speaking italian.

whatever my motives may have been, those sessions were actually useful. giovanni taught us all the swears and lots of rude hand motions, things that were frowned upon to teach in a normal classroom setting.

the food at the i house is also pretty decent, as is the coffee.

i never ate food, drank coffee or studied at i-house.  i worked at milano for less than a year but for years after that, i could get free drinks whenever i wanted so my loyalty stayed with them.  

i would only go to i-house for beer.  it was almost always free because if you worked at one cafe in berkeley long enough, the employees of the other cafes recognized you and it was a unwritten rule you just gave each other free stuff, especially if you were female.  i don't know if that's the case anymore but it worked out well for me back then.

i am thinking of i-house because amber and valentine's day are on my mind.  amber, because i wish she still lived in the bay area so she could be on my pub trivia dream team (she'd kill that music round) and valentine's day because it's around the corner and one year a bunch of us spent the evening drinking pitchers of beer on their patio right before candy punched a guy in the face for calling her a bitch and broke her wrist.  

on sunny days, that outdoor patio is full of foreigners, some hot, some not, but fun nonetheless.

Between Strada and I-house I I probably spent like 15 hours a week studying at Cafes. 

Why lie? I hung out at I-house because it was a block from my house and there were always fun foreigners there.

The drinks were ok but the food made up for it. It was a bit on the pricey side, but nothing exaggerated. 

It gets a bit crowded on the weekends.

Maybe my most recent Yelp compliments are ironic, because to be honest I'm really not.that.cool.  Yet I've known the words to every single from Rihanna, Chris Brown, Akon, Lady Gaga, Usher, and Kanye that has come out in the past year, all thanks to the I-House Cafe.

There's something soothing about listening to hip-hop in a loud room where tree-sitters bathed, international students drink beer, the creepy guy gives you dirty looks for taking "his" table, and the smelly chess corner gets animated.  Plus, taking a study break to look up and see my friend Greg (photo of Greg's ipod here: http://george.hotelling.net/90percent/pics/npr_podcast.png) awkwardly bouncing his head to rap never gets old.

The coffee's terrible and the food mostly comes out of a microwave, but those nachos are pretty hard to resist and the lasagne isn't half bad if they re-heat it all the way through.  I'll keep studying here until the university realizes I've stolen my sister's wireless password.

I'm a fan of the I-House Cafe!  The space is cute, it's conveniently located to Haas and the Law School, and everyone on staff just couldn't be nicer.  It's a great place to stop in for a coffee or a snack, and prices are super-reasonable.  It's never too packed, and it's nice to relax on a comfy couch, a table in the glass room in the back, or even outside on the patio on a nice day.  Definitely worth it, even if a visit involves a walk up the big Bancroft hill!

During the time when I lived at the I-House, most of us hated this cafe. It was consistently crowded, dirty and was basically full of drunk kids seeking random encounters. 

Several years later, it's looking much better. They cleaned up the place fairly well. There are now flatscreens that display foreign newspapers, which I think is a pretty cool concept. The drinks are decent, though the pastries are still not very appetizing. We might get around to trying the sandwiches again... 

But we'll see when that's going to be, because I'm still a fan of Cafe Strada down the street, which is also looking better than ever.
Not surprised.

Pasta Bene is the shit. I can't even tell you how many times I've been here... Whether it's for their delicious $5 lunch specials, or when my club has a banquet, Pasta Bene is the ideal choice for a meal any time of the day. I'm so glad it opened up, because it's a much better alternative to the shabby Cafe Milanese across the street. It's been packed ever since they've opened, and the crowd there is a sure testament to its deliciousness!

My favorite dishes:
1. Gnocchi Sausage!!!!!!!
2. Penne Bolognese (available for $5 during lunch)
3. Pollo Pizza
4. Lasagne
5. Fried Calamari
6. Garlic Bread
7. Tiramisu

The interior is spacious and squeaky clean, with nice, CLEAN bathrooms (heaven-sent, since it's Berkeley we're talking about). The service is great, and dining-in here is always a joy. There's also several tables outside for those who wish to dine under the sun (or rain). 

Go here for the $5 lunch specials! Every day during lunch time, they have a select few dishes available for FIVE DOLLARS. YES. FIVE. FUCKING. DOLLARS. Go.
Food is excellent. And the older woman who is usually behind the counter is incredibly sweet and helpful.

This place is great!  We stumbled upon it and we were pleasantly surprised.  Great Italian food, cooked fresh, fast friendly service and CHEAP prices.  We had the ravioli and the lasgna.  Both were wonderful!  And they came with the best bread!  We also had the tiramisu for dessert.  It was so creamy and delicious.  The prices can't be beat, only one entree over $10 and that is for the Salmon.  Every other item is around $7-9.  The apps and the desserts are priced from $2-4.  And, the lady who owns the place is a lovely true Italian women - strong, kind presence, and grateful to serve you.  This place has only been open for 7mos, but she has 28 years experience in the restaurant business (We know this because she shared it with us - in a very casual non-invasive manner).  It was great.  Try it for yourself - way different than the frozen entree' Italian places you stumble upon all too often.  This place has it all.  Oh yeah - and the atmosphere is intimate yet casual.

I chose this place for a "after graduation luncheon" when my son recently graduated UC Berkeley.  

While waiting to be seated my mom asked to use the bathroom and the owner told her it was out of service when it wasn't.  Well, my mom still hasn't gotten over that and I found that to be disturbing.

On the plus side, the food on the day was good and they even helped us at the table when they normally don't do table service.  So, all and all it was a good time, comfortable and casual.  Besides the issue with my mom, everyone had a good time and enjoyed the food.  Great for a fast, cheap place to go!

    +4 stars for food quality and service
     -1 star for saying the bathroom was closed when it wasn't

A loud and resounding "YES!"

So finally, there's an Italian restaurant in Berkeley that can give the incumbent Gypsie's a run for its money.  I'll go ahead and say that they're equally priced, but the dining experience at Pasta Bene makes me feel... less cheap.  (Alright, I realize this is merely a comparison so let's get crack-a-lackin' w/ the review.)

Food:
Standard Italian pasta choices ranging from Ravioli to Lasagna.  Their menu appears to be straight-forward and is flexible to custom requests.  The serving sizes are apt, the sauces are in my opinion, quite balanced- (not too overwhelming, but also not lacking in flavor), and the dishes are well made.  Given that I've dropped less than $10 bucks for a drink and pasta, I'll say the food tastes exception.

Now, of the 3 italian restaurants in Berkeley I can name off the top of my head (Gypsie's, Trattoria la Siciliana, and Pasta Bene), Pasta Bene seems to be the one with the best dollar-per-taste/dining experience ratio.  While Gypsie's has delicious dishes for under 10 bucks, you have to cope with the incessant "Numberrr 29?!" announcements over the microphone for other orders.  Trattoria la Siciliana is substantially expensive despite ample portions, and only accepts cash.  Contrast this w/ Pasta Bene... scrumptious dishes at legit prices, with your selection of a cold beer, all without any noise pollution or ATM-runs.  

Well done, Pasta Bene.

Marco polo is a must try! Fettuccini with cream sauce, prosciutto, and I substituted the green peas with mushrooms. Delicious! Calamari is fried very well, next time I'll ask them to make it more salt and peppery.  Friends got the seafood specials: lobster ravioli and seafood linguini. They both enjoyed the meal. 

The place looks great, the owners did a stellar job remodeling the restaurant. It's too bad I graduated before this place opened. I really hope it does well.

The best Italian place near UC Berkeley.

Very nice restaurant.  i got the chicken marsala.  pasta was a little al dente but the chicken was super tender (not dried out at all) and a little heavy on the wine sauce for me but mushrooms were fresh and sauce was smooth.  

as for the decor, i loved it.  i like the feel (bright and clean) of the place.  owners (who take your order and cook your food) and workers are very friendly and there's a nice atmosphere.  the outdoor area is about 4 tables but very quaint. very visible kitchen.  and super clean bathrooms!  i think they got free wifi as i saw people with laptops open and hanging out. 

i like it above gypsies.  the only negative about this place is that it's a bit far from the rest of campus.  but afterward you can get a nice cup of coffee at peet's.

I'm very tempted to say that this is my favorite pasta place in the area, but I can't because I haven't tried all of them yet hahaha well anyway Pasta Bene is at the top of my list of favorite Italian restaurants in Berkeley. I love their reasonable prices yet amazing quality of food!! 

This is what I've tried so far...

Gamberetto - fettuccini with shrimp & mushroom in tomato-cream sauce - this is the one I (almost) always get!! And it's still soo good every time (: Not too greasy, with just the right amount of sauce to make it flavorful and delicious!

Carciofi e Pollo - linguini with chicken breast, artichoke hearts & vegetables in olive oil-herb sauce - almost has an oriental hint to its flavor! the linguini tastes amazing and the chicken is also very good, but I don't like artichokes :( BUT it's still very delicious overall

Pasta Bene - linguini with tomato, basil, garlic, capers & seasonal vegetables in marinara sauce - this one's good but it's nothing special hahaha

Cheese Ravioli - stuffed with spinach, ricotta & parmesan cheese in marinara sauce - pretty good if you're looking for a light meal (: if I ate it when I was actually super hungry I think the portions might be a little too small

Fettucini Alfredo - fettuccini with chicken breast & mushroom in alfredo sauce - I usually don't get this since I get it all the time, but I ordered this the other day and man, it was amazing!!! Maybe I was just super hungry that day but I felt like the everything was perfect about this dish!

Tiramisu - A MUST-GET DESSERT!!! for $3 it is sooo worth it because of its amazing quality and flavor and texture... and it's only for $3!!!! I can't emphasize that enough! I'm craving it now just thinking about it...

So yeah everyone should definitely check out this place! Oh and the service is decent & it's good for groups too! (:

Quality: 4/6
Service: 4/5
Value: 3/4
Total: 11/15 = 4/5

Pasta Bene is a good value.  Like many places in the area, you order at the counter, and they bring the food to you.  The staff was very friendly, but I did miss the "extras" of a true sit-down Italian restaurant (abundant fresh bread, olive oil, etc).

Their Gnocchi was delicious!

Pricy, small portions, and bland. I remember when I first tried Pasta Bene many, many years back in San Francisco it was much better. Now the one is SF closed. Looks like they have gone way downhill since then. Go to Gypsy's for pasta instead.
Great place.  Excellent service, decent food, great prices, good variety in the menu, and clean.  It's a pleasure to go to a place where you can get a good meal without getting stuck with a big bill.

I bought lagsana, Chicken Mushroom fetuccine (alfredo) and Salmon pesta pasta. I got all 3 dishes to go. Very fast 15 minutes.
People answer the phone is very polite. 
I could say this restaurant only get 4 star , not 5 stars, since the food is OK(on the good side) , but not excellent. 
I guess I got what I paid for. The price is really good for berkeley area.
I don't think other pasta place could beat this price.
Restaurant's sitting is clean and look nice( I know I did not sit down there). Definitely will go back again.

Great calamari appetizer and good salads. OK house wine. Generous portions.  Canned mushrooms used for chicken Marsala but fetticini was fresh.  Pasta Bene dish had fresh vegetables.   Friendly and efficient staff.  I will be back.  

Crowd seems to show up after 7 pm on Saturday.

I originally thought that this place was an italian restaurant. However, this is like a cafe, with an italian twist. You order your food at the cashier and they bring it to you. I had a chicken breast with a side salad. It was very good and tasty and the service was fast and excellent. Nice location, and very clean and classy place. The owner was very nice too, he thanked us while we walked out.

The $5 lunch special is now $5.95 unless I'm mistaken. Anyways I tried the Penne Bolognese, one of the lunch special pastas, and it's served quick and fresh. The pasta was almost too hot to eat, but the aroma was irresistible. The noodles have a chewy texture and are fully cooked. The ground beef is really oily so when you finish your meal, you'll see a layer of oil at the bottom. 

TL;DR; Lunch special is $5.95 now. Tried the Penne Bolognese and it's pretty good, but slightly oily.

Can we say AWESOME?  

Food is tasty and inexpensive.  

No long waits as you order at the cash register and the food and drinks are brought to you.  You don't have to wait for your waiter to bring each item at a time, you don't have to wait for the check.  When you're done, you go!

Decor is pretty nice in spite of being in an area trashed by millions of dirty, selfish, self-entitled, self-centered lazy students.

Great place for an inexpensive meal with the girls.

If you sit outside, beware the homeless and local students who will actually ask for a taste of the food you paid for with the money you earned.  That's right.  Even the students in the area feel they deserve a piece of your meal despite being total strangers who didn't in any contribute to paying for your meal.

Pasta Bene is decent. I'd come here again: the atmosphere is nice, service is good, meals are cheap and completely satisfactory. The pasta is alright, probably the best for its price range around Berkeley (and infinitely better than Gypsy's in Durant Food Court/Asian Ghetto). 

You pay at the counter (giant menu overhead) and then sit down. Servers will come by intermittently to fill your water and bring your plates but they don't take your order. 

Pros: $5 lunch special pastas. Nothing beats this in terms of value---even though it's pretty limited, I think it encompasses a lot of the popular entrees so it's good if you're a mainstream consumer. For other aficionados, the regular menu is still of course available during lunch hours and there are a number of options there.

This place is EXCELLENT for groups. No extra service charge, they take reservations, and it makes it super easy to split the bill if there does not exist a combined bill (as everyone individually orders at the front). I've thrown birthday dinners here and other group meals, and it just makes life a lot easier. 

Dessert tip: Their vanilla ice cream is amazing. They've achieved the perfect consistency of cream and liquid and the additional garnishing with strawberries and warm chocolate sauce make my day. I hardcore crave Pasta Bene ice cream, even if the "real food" options are just adequate. 

Cons: If you're an Italian cuisine connoisseur looking for gourmet goodies and fine wine, etc., this is not for you. In fact, not much in this radius of a UC campus will give you what you're looking for. The food is good, but it isn't smashing---I don't look forward to Pasta Bene all day before my meal but am content when I'm actually eating. So no complaints at all. Essentially this is more of a 3.5 than a 3, if that were possible. I'd definitely come here with friends or anything casual, but if I needed to impress or wine and dine somebody, this wouldn't quite cut it.

I was in the area shopping and stopped to get a quick bite to eat.  So.....I wasn't totally impressed with the food or the service.  But, the food wasn't bad.  I think that Pasta Bene is a good option for students where they can eat something more than fried/fatty foods.  In addition, the place is clean and airy.  The prices are reasonable and the food is served quickly.  So, you can get in and out.

5 Bucks!  WOW... lunch special of top pasta dishes freshly cooked.  The dishes were delicious.  Pasta are well done with excellent flavor.  Lots of vegetarian options and great for large party.

This is a gem of casual Italian restaurant in Berkeley.  Great pricing and excellent Italian food, including a good selection of Pizza. Stop by if you would like a great meal lunch or dinner.  I think you will agree... this place is a great catch for food at a decent price.

this place serves good fried calamari with garlic sauce like from cheesecake factory. What else do I need to say? XD
And the pasta never fails to dissappoint and the prices are very reasonable too. I'm just sad its kind of far from campus.
Also, they have a lunch special: only $5 for select pastas from 11 to 3PM

Cheap, affordable pasta. Definitely not the best but sufficiently delicious for how much its worth. Better than Gypsys at Asian Ghetto and Milanese Cafe, so hungry, yet not too rich college kids craving for some decent pasta should definitely stop by. The portion seems to have decreased in size lately. The tiramisu  is pretty great too! Very amiable staff

The food is very good for the price. We beat the dinner crowd that soon came after us around 7pm.

Carciofi e Pollo - fresh vegetables and tasty sauce.  Nothing special w/ the linguine pasta.  But overall tasty.

Beef Lasagna - very tasty, especially with the gorgonzala cheese.  Definitely going to try adding that the next time i make at home.  Problem was that it was wasn't very hot... pretty lukewarm when it was served, compared to the other dish.  We were too lazy to complain though.... looked cooked all the way through, they just didn't re-bake/heat enough.

Tiramisu - Pretty good.  Have had better, but have also had worse. For ~$3, not bad.

The pizza looked pretty good from the table next to us.

Food: 3.5 stars
Service: 3 stars
Ambiance: 3.5 stars (much better than Gypsy's.  Sort of like Pasta Pomodoro)
Overall: 3.5 stars

Pasta Bene was just okay to me. 
After a couple of hours walking around Berkley, 
we were feeling a bit hungry at lunchtime.

There were a variety of restaurants around the area,
but I thought a chicken sandwich would fulfill my cravings.
We ordered a couple of things from the lunch menu- garlic fries, beef penne, grilled chicken sandwich.

The garlic fries were tasty. They weren't drenched in oil like I others I had in the past.
My sandwich was just okay. The chicken was little dry, and part of me wished that there was some other sauce element because the aioli wasn't that flavorful.
I got to try the beef penne as well. The tomato sauce it was didn't really excite my taste buds. 

Prices were really reasonable, and the crowd was majority college kids. 
Not sure if I'd come back the next time I visited Berkley, but it was a decent lunch stop.

Pasta Bene is a nice little place for some Pasta, naturally. There's a number of selections, many of which sound good. They serve beer and wine, which seems to be popular among the few diners I've seen there. It's just starting up though, I'd expect the customers to increase over time and once the semester starts. The flavor is there, but the portions are a tad small for the price (7-11$). 

On a second trip I had the turkey/eggplant sandwich, which very much hit the spot. They say their focaccia is house made, and it's very good. Comes with fries, a good deal for $7.00

Very friendly service. 

I'll definitely be going back to try much more of what they have to offer.

They've recently introduced new specials, which puts them above gypsy's and milanese in my book.

Being a young and hungry college student, I always look for decent-tasting, cheap food that can at least be satisfactory in terms of fill factor. Pasta Bene is everything but the latter. I do feel like I have to get another lunch or buy another dish to even reach the point of satisfaction. Their Penne Bolognese is good, but nothing special, which can be said with some of their other pasta dishes. Service is a bit on the slow side, but it has a nice environment to it.

I saw that this place was opening a few weeks ago where there used to be a bakery. A couple doors down from Buffalo Exchange. It opened sometime in the past couple of weeks and every time I've walked by there it is completely empty.

Well my fiance and I decided to go there today. It has a nice atmosphere, very clean, They were playing an online Jazz radio station for music.

We went up and ordered and the cashier was friendly enough. We then sat down and waited a few minutes for our food. It was not exactly as fast as I have come to expect from other fast-casual type Italian places.

Next the cashier bumbles out and asks if the food he has is ours, no it is someone else's food. He does this three times. There were only 4 tables of customers... at last he gave me someone else's lasagna and when I told him I didn't order that he went and traded with another customer for my chicken piccata. It just seemed like everyone there was so new and they hadn't gotten everything figured out yet.

I'm giving this 3 stars because the food was decent (not amazing, but alright for cheap Italian) and I liked the atmosphere. I also have a feeling that if things pick up they will figure things out more and the service will get a lot better in the next couple months. This remains to be seen but hopefully it will change for their sake...

I first entered this little bistro almost a year ago. I had no idea what to expect in terms of service or food quality, but the price was right, and I had a yen that day for Italian food and imported red wine, so why not? We were lucky enough to have Farhad wait on us. (Farhad and his lovely wife, Ladan, are the proprietors of this quaint establishment.) After inquiring about the wines, he offered to let me taste a few. In no time at all, I  landed upon the one that made my mouth explode with one velvety-chocolate taste sensation after the other (and this without food, yet!), the Piccini Chianti, 2009. I was sold! If the service and wine was this sensational, how good must the food be? Needless to say, I was delightfully correct in my guess - 'twas incredible. Fresh, healthy, succulent, and perfectly seasoned..one mouthgasm bite after the other followed by smooth sips of Chianti, I was in heaven! But even better than that, if at all possible, was the service. We sat outside, while most sat indoors, yet Farhad not once made us feel as if we were an inconvenience. In fact, quite the opposite, he checked on us frequently, kept our glasses filled, made me feel like a Queen, and after inquiring,  shared a bit of his story with us. His Energy was warm, compassionate, and Real. I almost forgot I was eating in a college town restaurant! Indoors is classy, lit perfectly, lending toward casual to more intimate date nights, and the place is spotless, including the loos. Truly, very nicely balanced decor. We have been back several times since, and have also more recently met his Beautiful wife and co-proprietor, Ladan, who is equally as amazing in character. We don't live close, so we cannot get in there as often as we wish, but no matter how much time lapses betwixt visits, Farhad and Ladan always remember us, welcome us with genuine joy, and make us feel like royalty! I highly recommend this place if you want to feel swept away from the usual hustle and bustle of city Life and pretend, for a moment, that you're back in the old country being treated like a humyn Being, all the while eating incredibly home-cooked Italian-style food at the lowest price around. My only disappointment is that I did not review this establishment a year ago.

Very Casual - This nice sweet restaurant appeals to students and yet food was very good and inexpensive.   It is the pay at the counter and get a number for your table kind of place.  Very nice employees.  Telegraph is a funky area of town and yet I would go back for a simple Italian meal.  It has a modern twist and it is light on ambiance.  Sat outside and got some creepy stares and cat calls so I will be sure sit inside next time.

Wow ! There's nothing more to say.Good food... Fast service which is a plus considering it located bye Cal campus.. Happy hour is cool beer, wine that's it. Oh the price are so good that I felt like I rob them... Lol please go it a must ....

Nothing TOO great, but pretty decent Italian food on Telegraph. I had the King Salmon...the fish was dry....the pasta was dry. It wasn't unbearable, but I've had better Italian. 

Love the clean interior. It's a very home-y environment. Employees are very helpful and friendly. I would definitely go again if I happened to be in that area of Berkeley again.

I love this place. Went here for the first time yesterday because I was craving pasta and wanted to stay close to home. The prices here are very good, ranging from $6.95-10:95 for an entree dish, which is very good considering that most past dishes are at lest $10 or more. Everything on the menu looks good and are inexpensive. The staff are very nice and welcoming. I think it might be family owned, though I'm not sure.

My boyfriend and I ordered the crab cakes as an appetizer and the Marco Polo and beef lasagna as our entree. The crab cake was so good. Probably one of the best that I've ever had. It came with 3 crab cakes on sliced napa cabage salad with ranch sauce. The salad was really good too. I'd never have thought that eating napa cabbage raw would be so good since I've normally had it cooked for hotpot. 

Our entrees came out and they both looked so good. They both came with 2 pieces of garlic bread. He got the beef lasagna and I had the Marco Polo. I'd  have to say that the beef lasagna is the best lasagna hands down. There's no way you can get the lasagna that soft unless its made themselves. The Marco Polo was fettuccine alfredo with mushroom, prosciutto, and green peas. Also really good and the sauce was fantastic. It didn't leave that itchy feeling at the back of your throat like store bought alfredo sauces do.

Totally recommend this place if you're craving Italian food. The only problem is that it's on Telegraph so you might have a hard time trying to find parking on the street. We almost didn't go because we drove around the block so many times looking for parking but got lucky at the last second.

I just have one word for this place "Scrumptious" ...OMG what a fantastic little place and a very friendly staff too. Check out the prices, service is great too. I am not a huge fan where you walk to the counter and placed you order but, this place rocks.... I am so spoiled!! he, he, he. To make it short the food delicious, the service is prompt  most important you can taste the fresh ingredients in each dish. Below are my recommendations, save room for dessert it is soooo yummy!!
 
* Eggplant parmigiana
* Calamari
* Greek Salad
 
* Rustica (on the pastas) sooo good!!

*Tiramisu (mmmmm) 
 
I can't wait to go back. I hope you enjoy it as much as I did

I tried the cheese ravioli today and was blown away - fresh house-made pasta and very flavorful sauce and stuffing.  The portion was generous too.  Perhaps the best $6 Italian lunch special I have ever had.  Very nice vibe and good jazz on the stereo too, will go back.

If you want your Italian fix, come here instead of Gypsy's! It's not even that much farther from Ghetto. It's like the same price too, but so much better.

I came here one for lunch and dinner. Lunch, I got the hawaiian pizza and it was delicious! There's a $5 pasta lunch special too.

Dinner I got one of the pastas, and it was good.

Overall, it's a restaurant where you'll order, and they'll bring you the food. They're pretty fast in general, only maybe like 10-15 minutes of wait. 

The owners are usually REALLY nice! When I went to get a to-go box because I couldn't finish their HUGE portions, the lady asked me how my meal was (:

My roommate and I finally decided to come here after a long day of work and shopping in SF. We have already the tiramisu here multiple times, but never sat down and ate the actual food. I'm glad that we did though. 

We each got one dish because we were just hungry. I got the Gnocchi Sausage on the suggestion from fellow Yelper Dmitriy S. It was freaking delicious. Although the gnocchi itself could have been more tender and less chewy, it was good regardless. We both scarfed down our meals in about 10 minutes and went back to our place which was a 5 minute walk.

You order up in the front and then sit down. It's a bit classier than the other Italian restaurant, Gypsy's, but really the service wasn't amazing or anything. Just average. It's pretty cool that you can see into the kitchen if you're sitting on the right side of the kitchen and the owners and servers seem pretty nice.  

Definitely for similar prices to Gypsy's I'll becoming back. I would have to just get the tiramisu though, I feel like the food is just about the same standard of Gypsy's - maybe a bit better - but the tiramisu is what is amazing.

We stopped in on a whim and were very pleasantly surprised. The food was good, the service was excellent, and the presentation of the desserts was that of a fancy restaurant. We loved the laid-back atmosphere.

Really really cheap pasta! I wanted to try more of their menu, but it was kind of limited. It's kind of like a fast-food pasta place because you order at the counter and sit down and wait for them to bring your food. But it pretty good and rather quiet. They could have done with some music with such high ceilings. They only got 4 stars because it was a bit difficult to find parking and I'm upset that they replaced the bakery that was there 10 years ago.

Lasagna, King Salmon, and Gamberoni are the best things on the menu (out of the things I"ve tried so far.) 

Was very disappointed on their Bolognese, Pasta Bene and some veggie pasta. 

Definitely a good pasta option on campus but if I had a car, not the best choice for italian.

This is a great little Italian place, that is very affordable. If you're ever in this area, I would have to choose Paste Bene over Gypsys for multiple reasons:

1. Pasta Bene has a much more comfortable setting than Gypsys
2. Pasta Bene is the same price, if not cheaper, than Gypsys
3. Pasta Bene has tastier and more elegant food than Gypsys

After saying that though, if you're on campus, making the trip out to Pasta Bene may not be worth it. It is the further yet better option, but the cost of the time travelled may not outweigh the benefit of the better food. 

So 4 stars, considering just the food and place itself.

Came here for the first time with my boyfriend, brother and my inlaw on our double date. the food here are so cheap! & to top that, the food was DELICIOUS! my spaghetti looked like it didn't have flavor cause it looked plain, but when i took that bite, it was on hit! It gets busy near dinner time, glad we got there at 5-ish close to 6pm :)

They have a good variety of vegetarian pasta. I went here with a few of my vegetarian friends and we all ordered different items and they all tasted good. The ambience is nice and the food is not pricey.

The classy and refined version of Gypsy's http://www.yelp.com/biz/gypsys-trattoria-italiano-berkeley#hrid:1xH20Z5XVulpCq9XzGUS-w. Italian food, it can be expensive right? Italian restaurants, overly romantic right? Well Pasta Bene solves those problems completely. You can get close to equal quality and taste of a fine italian restaurant for a fraction of the price.

I like this place tremendously. Love the idea behind it. Classic pasta dishes made freshly with excellent flavor for a more than affordable price. 

I'll definitely be coming back to try other dishes as I heard the Gnocchi sausage was really good but last time I came I ordered the Chicken Marsala. It was exactly what I expected and satisfied my pasta craving thoroughly. The chicken was cooked well and perfectly bathed in the mushroom-marsala wine sauce.

My friends ordered the tiramisu to share and it was a nice finish to the meal. 

The ambiance and aesthetic are quite simple. The process to get your food is the same also. Just simply stare at the giant menu hanging on the wall above the register and order. The food is brought out to you in a timely manner. Simplicity at it's finest.

Typical Pasta. It tastes fresh, healthy, nicely served and the waiter was really nice. The reason why Im only giving this place a 3 star is probably cause i just wasnt wow-ed by the place. I mean, the food is really good, dont get me wrong but i find the place is too plain and there isnt something that makes it unique. Maybe i just had WAY too high expectations that it kinda makes me already think in the beginning that this place is really great. Well, considering that this place is targeted for college students, id say that this is a pretty decent place, and cheap too!

Lasagna has been one of my very favorite foods since I was six. The beef lasagna I had at Pasta Bene was my favorite, far and away, of all lasagnas preceeding it. It was absolutely incredible.

I love the atmosphere; the kind Italian couple who manage the place greet you with a smile and take great care of you. Great on any night of the week.

WIFi is very fast. Place was absolutely clean and accommodating staff at counter. You'll feel at home with the place. Couches on the side with a large mirror hanging on the wall. And the seating outside is perfect for a sunny weather while having a Tiramisu! It is a must try! :) we had gnocchi sausage and tropicana pizza! Niiice

This place is a restaurant that will stick around for a while. Despite its location further down Telegraph, everything about the place makes me certain that it will bring foot traffic down to my end of Telegraph.

[Skip down to the bottomline if you don't want details]

So I've been taking chem lab over the summer at Cal during the evening slot (we get out at 10p, 9:00 if we're lucky) so alot of the conversation during experiments is about how hungry we all are and what could possibly be open after we get out that is tasty and worth eating. Someone mentioned Pasta Bene! (Open 11a-10p @ 7days/wk)

Glad they did, I've seen the sign--noticed it subconsciously--but never thought to check it out. After having poor quality pasta at basic tier/budget/college town restaurants, I was skeptical, but after the enthusiastic review..it was a must try.

You walk into a spacious dining area with open kitchen you can peer into over the cashier counter. Walk up to order, seat yourself and they bring you your food. **Another perk is they have a few beers on tap as well as an assortment of wines. Happy hour is 3-7pm :D

Anyway asked for a recommendation and the welcoming man who seemed to be running things led me to carciofi e pollo (linguini w/ chicken breast, artichoke hearts&veggies in oliveoil herb sauce), which he said was his favorite. So cheers to your favorite, sir! It was delicious.

As I sat out in their patio to soak up some of the summer sun with my pale ale in reach, the boss-man brought me a free appetizer, a few dolmades (wild rice-stuffed grape leaves) with a slice of lemon soaked in just enough oil to be moist and tasty but not greasy. TASTY!

Soon enough, came my entree..let me say, it makes me happy to get a plate of pasta that is piping hot, but not hot enough to stop me from digging in immediately. There was just enough flavor that I didn't salt--but I did (red) pepper it to get that extra hearty kick. After a few forkfuls of the linguini which was cooked perfectly, I realized to my dismay that I have so much more chicken than I thought and I will soon be left with only chicken and no noodles if I don't start attacking the pollo. The ratio must literally be 1:1 chicken:pasta with about half as much artichoke/veggies.

The portion was perfect, I finished the whole thing, wasn't overly bursting, but wasn't hungry at all and the price was just right.

Bottomline: Tasty pasta, Good flavors, Legit portions, Alcoholic beverage license, Clean atmosphere/bathrooms. You can't go wrong!

I love this place! The pasta is decent, the service is fast, and the atmosphere is nice. 

I tried many of the $5 lunch special pastas, and they were all very delicious. The portions are not huge but will get you comfortably 70% full. In my pasta bene order the vegetables were perfectly cooked, the noodles were very fine and coated with sauce, and the whole dish was savory. The triangles of bread were fluffy and crisp.

Service is satisfactory. You order at the counter, but they bring your water and dish to your table and bus you table. The environment is calm and  breezy, and both the indoor and outdoor seating are comfortable with excellent lighting. The hanging chandelier lamps and mirrors add to the ambiance, and I always feel relaxed while eating at Pasta Bene.

I am giving this place 4 stars not exactly for the food, which is decent but only a tier above the pasta you can make at home, but because of the overall dining experience. I would gladly come here for the good meal, fast service, convenience, and lovely environment all for just $5.

WILL I come back: Yes
WHEN will I come back: During lunch for the deal; dinner prices aren't as worth it.
WHAT will I do differently: Maybe try a pizza (also pretty cheap, ~$8 for a small pizza)

I just went to Pasta Bene with 5 friends and all of us left stuffed and happy.  We ordered 4 pasta dishes, 1 large pizza, 1 plate of calamari and a piece of tiramisu between 6 of us and finished everything. The restaurant looked aesthetically appealing, the decorations were sophisticated, and the bathrooms were very clean! The waiter was extremely friendly and my roommate thought he was cute. ;). In addition, he willingly split our check for us at the end upon seeing our hesitation in deciding how to pay. What a nice gesture!

The pizza was delicious. We ordered the contadina which was a perfect balance of meat and vegetables. Our favorite pasta dishes were the Carciofi e Pollo and tortellini. The sauces weren't too heavy and were just the right consistency. Of course, we had room for the delicious tiramisu!!! Highly recommended even if you are stuffed. You won't regret it.

The Gnocchi Sausage was really good, especially for the price! I got a teeny bit tired of it after awhile but saved it for later and loved it again! Plus, the cashier was really friendly and sweet. My order was take-out, so I just sat at a table and waited no more than 10 minutes, which is pretty good in my opinion. When I got my order, I opened the box and was immediately met by an eruption of yummy scents. I got some pepper from the table I was sitting at and dumped some on my food so that I could have it later when I ate. But when I looked in my bag later, I realized that they included a little thing of cheese and pepper! How thoughtful! At least in my experience, people only do that with pizza and I definitely like pepper on all my other food too.

This place was so awesome! I had their $5 lunch special and it was so filling! It was worth every penny. The menu had so many things to choose from it was hard to choose just one. Their prices are very reasonable. Its nice inside and also nice that they have outdoor seating. I definitely can't wait to go back and try more dishes and desserts!
$3 Tiramisu.

Overall the meal was average. It was cheap and fast, but this wouldn't be on my list of places to go back to anytime soon. I'd rather pay more and have better quality. The 
Bruschetta was alright, definitely had better, couldn't eat the Eggplant Parmigiana, it was a soggy mess and didn't taste good. The Gnocchi Sausage was not bad, but wasn't anything special. I guess its a toss up though, because for $9 it was alright. Personally I think Olive Garden has better sauce on their pastas though. Lastly the 
Tiramisu was ok, usually I like Tiramisu to be more rich and creamy though.

This restaurant is a fantastic addition to Berkeley's southside! Awesome features include:

1) Super clean. No tablecloths -- it's not super fancy -- but the tables are always cleaned after people leave and everything looks like it was purchased yesterday. I really appreciate a clean restaurant, and Pasta Bene gets an A+.

2) Affordable. I haven't been to Gypsy's in a while, but I would generally say the prices are comparable. There's an unbeatable $5 lunch deal that I highly recommend.

3) Delicious. The prices may rival Gypsy's -- but the quality is several levels above. All the food is served extra hot and is always tasty. The menu has a good variety -- from typical pastas and pizzas to more creative entrees. 

4) Friendly. The servers are really welcoming and bring water promptly to your table, and the woman behind the counter (I believe she's the owner/manager) is always smiling. 

I've already been twice and will definitely make it a regular stop for meals!

The food here is nothing special, but I think it is one of the better places to go to for Italian food in Berkeley. They're well known for their $5 lunch specials and have a pretty wide variety of dishes. The atmosphere is also really cute and clean. However, I don't think that in general (regular prices), I would choose to go here if I had the option of going to Gypsy's instead.

I went here for the first time today for lunch and was impressed with the quality/flavor of the food. It was also dirt cheap compared to other pasta restaurants in the east bay. 

For lunch I had an order of bruschetta (2 pcs) and the spaghetti and meatballs. The bruschetta was excellent and served on a garlic toast. The tomato mixture had a very strong garlic flavor with a hint of black pepper. The spaghetti was light with a touch of red pepper (I think) and mushrooms. It is served with 4-5 little meatballs that are also very flavorful and delicious. My bill came out to less than $10 AND I still have a ton of leftovers. 

The portions are appropriate with the costs and this a place that I would recommend to all my friends. I can't wait to go back and try the other dishes. Oh and the service was excellent!!

Menu: http://pastabenesf.com/resources/Pasta_Bene_Berkeley.pdf

This place is pretty awesome. This is almost like a quick-dining pasta place. I'm sure they do a ton of to-go orders, and there are a good amount of people that dine-in as well. The set up is simple: order, pay, and wait for your food. That is also why I didn't quite expect so much. However, I was quite surprised! Yelp's 4 star was more than correct for this place, which is not always the case nowadays. We had two different types of pastas: one was a cream sauce tortellini and the other was a pesto base. Both were freakin' delicious, and we cleared our plates. Dishes are pretty much all below $10, and the flavors were similar to the more upscale places. Clean set up, variety, delicious, and easy on the wallet. We will be back.

This is about as good as you're going to do within a few miles of the berkeley campus for reasonably-priced Italian food. It's far better than gypsy's. Really, there's no comparison. Gypsy's is cheap, cheesy, fatty, inauthentic Italian food. 

Prices are super reasonable for lunch and fair for dinner. I've tried the various pastas, tortellini, bolognese, the lasagna, the salmon - all were good, pretty comparable to what I'd expect from a place charging 50% more. Service is good - I'm a voracious water drinker and my cup stays full. The atmosphere is simple but clean and modern.

We travel often to Berkeley because our son goes to CAL. We typically eat at the "in walking distance to the campus" food places on telegraph. Getting tired of the same ole, we opted to drive somewhere. This place was awesome. For our huge family that goes on these weekend trips. It was the perfect setting, kid friendly, large group friendly AND the food was great!

The bruschetta is great as is the garlic bread! I had the chicken marsala, yummy! In fact probably four of us got this meal and we all LOVED it! The kids shared a pizza and I didn't try it but it looked good. I also had the gorgonzola salad and my husband had the soup and we loved both. 

My husband got the gnochhi and he is a gnochhi snob and italian so he is used to fresh, homemade gnochhi. It didn't taste fresh, meaning probably bought frozen and cooked. Good but if you like true gnochhi I probably would not order this item. 

So many great choices and I can't wait to go back and try the next item!

$5 lunch specials!!! You can't get lower prices for pastas as good as the ones here!! Although the lunch special menu is limited to only a couple of dishes, the regular menu has a variety that you can choose from. The best dish in my opinion is the Gamberetto!!!!!!!! SO GOOD. Please try. 

This place is perfect for hungry college students that have thin wallets. Cheap, clean, and fast. I don't know what more busy college students can ask for. It's also good for coming with big groups because you don't get effed over by tip/service charge!

The people that work here are also very kind. My friends and I threw a surprise birthday dinner for my friend, and we had a lottttt of people (25+) trying to squeeze into the corner where the bathrooms are... and although we kind of got in the way of the entrance to the kitchen, the workers were very understanding and nice about it. They even wanted a picture of us attempting to hide haha.

Only con: Tiramisu was whatever... but it's okay because this is PASTA Bene...
Yummy pasta, and the restaurant is actually NICE..I like that you just pay at the cashier (easy to split checks). I occasionally order their lunch specials

I love pizza, pasta, garlic bread, and all things Italian ... but my husband doesn't eat dairy. This makes it a little bit difficult for us to go out to Italian food together at most places.

So I was really excited when I looked at the menu at Pasta Bene, because they have plenty of standard Italian restaurant fare for me, but also plenty of dairy-less options for my husband! He got some kind of chicken sandwich, and he said it was quite good. I ordered a pizza (which cost around $8.50) which was big enough for two meals.

The restaurant was informal, as you order at the counter and then find a table and wait for your food, but the dining room was relatively pleasant. There are large windows that face out onto the street, which allow a lot of light to come in. There's also a small outdoor seating area beyond the front door, but I'm not sure how much traffic might disturb diners sitting out there. Perhaps I'll check it out next time.

I WISH THIS PLACE WAS CLOSER TO CAMPUS! 

I ordered the Bruchetta and the Melanzane. The Bruchetta was a little too cold, feels like they prepaid it and just took it out of the fridge. But the Melanzane was delicious! Beats Gypsy's greasy oily-ness. The Tiramisu had raspberry sauce on the plate, and it was the perfect fluffiness and taste of coffee. 

Definitely coming back again for their pasta and dessert! c:

If you'd like to be hit in the face with a salt donkey, then this is the Italian place for you. I ordered the chicken parmigiana, and the sauce tasted as if it were straight out of a can but with an entire shaker of salt. The chicken itself was hardly fresh, and I'm fairly certain it was some pre-made, frozen chicken parmigiana patty that was microwaved with a piece of cheese on top. It tasted rubbery.

Even with the pasta that came with it, there was no cure for that over-salted chicken and marinara sauce. My god, Ragu or Preggo sauce tastes better than what I was served.

We also ordered bruschetta, and it, too, was salty, and it was obvious that the tomatoes were not fresh and had been sitting around somewhere. I swear to god, it was as though today was Salty Sunday and they decided to put your full-daily intake of salt in every bite of the meal.

The bruschetta was also soggy by the time they brought it to us.

Epic fail.

In terms of Berkeley Italian food, this is as good as it gets in the campus area. This place has a good variety of pastas and the portions are filling, but not over the top. I wish there were more selections with pesto, but the Rustico is my favorite. I've never had a lunch special, but for $5 it's pretty hard to beat. Also, the bread served with the pasta is super tasty!

There is always plenty of seating, and this place is great for students. Very clean and very cheap with a good location.

I've been here several times, with my first experience being quite negative. I don't recall the details but I remember arguing with the owner about an error with my bill. Since then I've had some reservations about coming back here.

For this experience, the food has remained the same since my last visit. Can't blame them for not changing anything considering the popularity of this restaurant. My preferred option is the Beef Lasagna, and it's now only $6 during lunch. A good deal considering the difficulty in making the dish in an Asian kitchen, but the dish is pretty standard. It seems to be getting smaller and smaller though...

I really wish they would put greater effort on putting out all the dishes at the same time. The last dish on my table arrived more than 5 minutes after mine came out. Cold lasagna = not good.

Great for groups!! Each person buys their own meal at the cashier, so there's no bill to split.

This place is great for so many reasons

The decor inside is warm and welcoming. Small but still spacious.

The menu offers just the right amount of options. I'm never afraid to try something new each time I go because it always comes looking and tasting great!  The dishes are so elegant and look expensive but the prices are very affordable. 

They know how to treat their customers...you don't have to wait forever to get your order taken and the food comes at a very reasonable amount of time. 

Definitely one of my favorite places to go with the family :)

Was hanging out with my friend, working on her computer that just survived a virus attack, before deciding we were both hungry. We noticed this place just opened recently so we decided to give it a try.

The restaurant employs an order-at-the-counter system. The cashier was extremely nice and efficient, double checking to make sure she got my order right. The food came out quickly.

Garlic bread: Crustless!! First time I've had crustless garlic bread and I think I like it that way quite a bit. Medium-heavy on the garlic, light on the butter, just how I like it. 

Crab cakes: It's SO easy to make crab cakes spongy or rock-hard due to poor execution. These were just right. Not overly-greasy and retained the flavor of the crab very nicely. The inclusion of the lettuce countered the spunk of the hollandaise and tartar saucy nicely, as well as adding another layer of texture.

Penne bolognese: Similar pastas like this one at Gypsy's and other establishments overwhelms you with greasiness that makes you feel sick after eating. This one doesn't. The amount of sauce on the pasta was just right so the dish wasn't saturated in sauce. Could've used a little bit more flavor but a dash of black pepper fixed that.

Tiramisu: Twas yummy. Had a cranberry or raspberry garnish that gave it a zesty kick.

The owner was extremely hospitable and friendly, a nice change compared to those working at Milanese Caffe and Gypsy's. Will definitely come back here for my Italian fixes from now on.
Great food, good atmosphere, good location, good service. The best Italian food for the price range.

I was allowed to customize my order! There were several really appealing items that I wanted to try and opted for the melanzane (fettuccini with roasted eggplant, sundried tomatoes & garlic in marinara sauce). I swapped the marinara sauce with alfredo and added chicken for $1 more to bring the entree to $7.95. I also ordered the garlic bread because I love garlic bread! The food took a bit long but it was certainly delicious! I need to come back for the highly-recommended tiramisu next time.

My pasta got a hair in it...though the pasta tastes not bad 
It is okay.

Fresh, light, and tasty is how I would describe their Italian food. Got a cesar salad, tried the bruschetta, and had some of the ham pineapple pizza. Everything was awesome, and I loved the service and decor. Very relaxing, modern, and peaceful. If you are looking for a nice place to sit down and relax in Berkeley, which is sometimes hard to find, I would definitely recommend this place.

Decent food at a decent price. I am a fan. 

However, this is where I realized I don't like mushroom soup, which was the soup of the day. It wasn't creamy like I expected. I took it home since I can't pour money down the drain. Later that night, I cooked spaghetti noodles and used the soup as the sauce. That actually came out delicious.

Other than that, everything else was pretty good.

Very healthy but fulfilling portions, and you can taste the fresh herbs in the marinara sauce! 

Best bang for the buck if you go there for lunch specials (11am-3pm), then you pay $5 for great Italian food. 

I got the Beef Lasagna ($5) and Tiramisu ($3). Both were really good and didn't make me feel guilty. I'm definitely coming back!
Food was really good spinach cheese ravioli was fresh but left hungry wanting more
Good value, good food!
Great Food , service and the owners are a delight to talk to. Went here with my aunt and uncle and they are regulars at this place for a long long time . Delicious !!!...

Yes, this place is delicious! I've ordered their apple walnut salad three times, and their Rustica is hearty. 

Portion size is a medium to large so I always get leftovers to go.  Very affordable and the food has yet to let me down.  Truly, the flavors taste fresh.  I ordered the salad and they were kind enough to add my missing mushrooms...particularly the cute waiter who also loves mushrooms.

Their tiramisu is so gooood and I don't care if they got it from a box, it's still wonderful!  Happy hour with beer is also awesome.

Best Italian restaurant around campus, better than Gypsy's and Milanese. Their pasta bene is so good! The vegetables all taste fresh and the capers are so mmmm. Their carcifio e pollo was also good, but it only came with two half artichoke hearts. The chicken was moist. 
Nice and clean place. 
They serve you your food. 
$5 specials from 11AM-3PM.

Pasta Bene is a nice little retreat away from the craziness of Telegraph Ave. The prices are great and the food is delicious. Family owned restaurant. They care about the quality of their food and are very sweet. Definitely give it a try! I found it on Yelp and am now spreading the word. :-)

I got the Gnochi Sausage based o my friends advice, and it lived up to my expectations, it was delicious!
My friends also suggested the tiramisu.  Its pretty cheap for just 3$, and seems homemade, tasty, but it doesn't have a very strong coffee flavor.
The food comes pretty fast, but the service isn't spectacular or anything, didn't get a water refill.
I will definitely come back next time im in the mood for italian, probably for the lunch special.

Have been to this place on numerous occasions as it's a 3-block walk from where I live. I was highly sceptical of it when it opened a couple years ago but it's more than proven itself worthy. It's a cute cozy place, good for both lunch and dinner. You order and then seat yourself so there's no bill to take care of afterwards. They have pasta, pizza, salads and sandwiches, as well as a few beers on tap and wine. There are lunch specials and happy hour to take advantage of. My favorite dishes would have to be Marco Pollo, Gnocchi Sausage, and Beef Lasagna. Plates are nice size (usually end up with leftovers) and VERY reasonably priced for italian food. This place is just a bit farther down Telegraph from campus but tends to get crowded during peak times b/c there's not an overwhelming amount of seating. Overall, the food, service and atmosphere are great and prices are very reasonable. Comparable to Gypsy's in Asian Ghetto but a bit more spaced out and quieter. Highly recommend for lovers of Italian food.

Don't come here if you have kids. The staff are friendly but the female owner will scold you if your kids laugh too loud. This is NOT a high end or QUIET restaurant. My kids voices drown in the atmosphere. All I can say is DON'T come if you have kids.
Good! &comfy clean seating.

I love pasta so when I heard that there was this new place that had opened in Berkeley, I jumped at the chance to try it. I met up with a friend for dinner so I suggested that we go to pasta Bene since I'd seen that the reviews were pretty good. The atmosphere was pretty nice and we were immediately greeted and shown to a table. They had a wide variety of dishes and I was happy to see that prices were not so bad. We ordered the Bruschetta, Seafood Linguine (which just happened to be one of the specials), Marco Pollo, and a Tiramisu. Each dish was equally delicious. The Bruschetta was topped with a ton of tomatoes which I really liked. The seafood linguine had a kind of spicy zest to it that I found very appealing. My friend ordered the Marco Pollo. I was a bit skeptical of the dish since it had peas in it and I'm not that fond of peas, but I tried a bit and it was fantastic! The tiramisu was in a world of it's own as it came with a few strawberries and I believe with a bit of blueberry jam. 
The waitress was also very friendly and talked to us when she came to fill up on water (which happened quite a lot) and to take our plates. 
I saw previous reviews that mentioned that the portions were small, but I was pretty filled by the end and even had a bit leftover to take home. I would definitely suggest this place to other people and will be going back for multiple times to come.

My best friend and I went to Berkeley to walk around today when we saw this place called Pasta Bene.  We weren't sure if we wanted to go inside or not because it looked like it was a little out or our price range.  The place was very nice and clean looking, so we decided to check out the menu and the prices.  To our surprise,  the place was very cheap!  We sat down and ordered an order of bruscetta first and then for the main course,  Gamberetto and Chicken Parmigiana.  My family is from Italy so I am a pretty big critic about my Italian food but....this place is AWESOME!!!!!!!   The brusetta reminded me of visiting Italy in 2001 and the food was even better.  We were so amazed...we are now official regulars of Pasta Bene.  The sauces are home-made, pasta and ingredients.  The owners and servers were very nice and I felt like we were home.  Thank you Pasta Bene for the beautiful taste of Italy!!!

Came here after my final because I was craving something Italian, hearty and warm & this place hit the spot. 

My friend and I were the only ones there when we walked in, and an older man (the owner, I presume) greeted us warmly and explained to us his menu. He was really sweet and accommodating, he basically told us "here is my menu, but I can make whatever you'd like." I ordered the eggplant fettuccine and my friend ordered the penne bolognese, which was the daily deal for $5.95. 
We paid and sat down and waited for our food. Really nice environment, with dark wood tables. It felt a bit fancy even though we ordered at the counter. 

The person who took our order was extremely attentive, he brought us water 2 minutes after we sat down, and we got our steaming plates of pasta soon after. My eggplant fettuccine was okay, it was nice & warm, but it lacked flavor. On the other hand, the Penne Bolognese was amazing! It was meaty, cheesy & tomato-y. It packed a punch, you could tell it took a long time to cook, and there were bits of juicy mushroom pieces in it as well. For $6, it was worth it. They provide pieces of toasted bread with the pasta for leftover sauce-dunking, which was perfect. One odd thing I noticed though, and this may be my OCD, but both our pastas were a little past al dente, almost soggy but not quite. Our server came by a few times to make sure we were doing okay, which was nice.

Overall, good food, great service, but I'd like to see how they'd fare with more customers. I'd recommend going there to try them out. They have pizzas, pastas, and meat entrees. The owner highly recommended the chicken parmigiana, i'll have to come back and try that some other time.
Best value food for the price. Very affordable and very delicious.

Well...After a long break from Yelp, here I am. This reviews also pretty late so I'll try to sum up all the importants. 

To be honest with all of you guys...I'm not THAT fond of Pasta Bene. Sure it's clean and it has a great atmosphere that's usually buzzing with people and great weather but I feel like the food just isn't up to it. I've tried a few dishes such as Tortellini Primavera, Gnocchi with Sausage, and some others. My favorite was the Tortellini Primavera. They also give you huge portions for what you pay and it's a lot. The food is pretty heavy from all the carbs and whatnot so you'll leave feeling full for sure. The appetizers aren't bad. I actually really like the calamari and the fries were good. I wouldn't go the way to order fries but I'd definitely steal a few of my friends. 

Service is good with attentive waiters but when it gets packed...oh man...Distance wise is awesome. I pretty much live a few blocks from it and it's definitely walkable. I wouldn't recommend driving but I'm sure you'll be able to find street parking within a block or two away. 

I don't hate this place but that doesn't mean I love this place with a passion like the reviewer that's several reviews above me who has symbols and capital letters every few letters. :D

6 dollar lunch specials, but too bad theres only 5 selections.

I had the eggplant marinara one (no meat!). The pasta was pretty bomb - it made me forget completely that I wasn't eating any meat. Hell, I wouldn't mind going vegetarian for a week if I had Pasta Bene. 

Will definitely come back next time

ambiance//****
spacious . large windows . high ceilings!

service//****
super nice an efficient...i asked to swap out my pasta and they gave me every choice out there!

food//**
the food in iteself was alright...a good deal for what you pay for

~*~
cheap eat for a uni student...but not for the foodie snobs
we came here because maoz shut down! =(

Didn't even know this place existed until my friend took me here so when I saw it I didn't expect much from it, but surprisingly this place is really good. 

It was kind of awkward because we were the only customers in here (it was so quiet...I felt as if the workers were eavesdropping on us) but I guess that's because they just opened and many people didn't know about it. Our waiter was extremely friendly and nice and was always making sure we had everything we need. Well, maybe too nice? I felt as if he was watching our table from afar making sure our glass of water wouldn't go down the 2/3-full mark. 

Anyway, nice, cheap, Italian food. Definitely the cheapest Italian restaurant I've been to so far around Berkeley, which is a (+), and your portion size is generous too! 

Coming back here again for sure.

Pasta Bene is definitely better than Gypsy's. I love their atmosphere, service, and food. I've tried their Marco Pollo, Gnocchi Sausage, and Beef Lasagna - all were satisfactory. One thing is, their price seems a bit too pricey. Yes, their food is great especially compared to other places near campus, but honestly it's a bit overpriced for the objective quality. Nevertheless, their Lunch Specials make up for that, and I'd be glad to go back any day to grab lunch with a friend.

This place is great. I highly suggest coming for their cheap lunch specials that puts Gypsy's to shame. The only difference is you do get more food with Gypsy's but also more grease and indigestion.

My favorite experience was having an awesome conversation with the waitress who genuinely seemed to love working there and talking about the food that they make from scratch. I had the Chicken Ravioli which she recommended and I could not have had a single regret. For $8.95, I had a decent portion which filled me up and I would have taken it home for leftovers, but the rest of my party couldn't keep their forks off my plate. Delish!

For the price, the food is definitely worth a dine-in experience to experience all of the great flavors in their dishes. I will be back very very soon to try out the rest of their dishes. :)

Sunday afternoon was pretty empty so I was a little skeptical to go in but glad I did. Good portions, decent prices, and tasty. Tomato cream sauce was delish. Not a fancy place but clean with plenty of seating area.

This is an update on some of their food.  

Their Gnocchi Sausage is soo good. I think I just fell in love.  It's chewy yet not tough.  The sauce is not watery, but not too thick either.  
I also had their Tropicana pizza, yum! Crispy crust, and awesome combination of toppings.  
The Chicken Piccata is also great, I love their lemon and caper sauce.  OMG So good!!!

Honorable mention: Marco Polo, Chicken Marsala, and the King Salmon.
Crab cake was horrible, def. frozen......Pasta was alright, not spectacular. Wouldn't want to go back again.

I can't believe this place is on telegraph and I've only ever recently gone to eat here, I did NOT expect it to be so good! The pasta was so good, the portions were big and the best part was everything was under ten dollars! If you're looking for a good cheap Italian meal in Berkeley I'd definitely tell you to go here!

I really liked the layout of the restaurant, was really nice interior and plenty of seating. They also had pitchers for 13 bucks, would of totally got one or two if I had a bigger party. I had the Beef Lasagna which was pretty cheap, I think it was 6.95? Cheap eats + good service = always good.
Price is a spice. Decent quality at a great price.

There are sooo many things i like about pasta bene!

FOOD - delicious! I have yet to be disappointed. My favorite is the Tortellini Primavera...tomato creme sauce with tri colored tortellini and fresh veggies. (Get there before 7 p.m. to get $3 pint / $12 pitchers!) For their $5.95 lunch special i usually go with the Melanzane which has perfectly cooked eggplant in it.

SERVICE - they are all soo nice! from the sweet owner lady to all the college student servers. Very timely service, always refilling waters and checking in on you at the right moments. 

AMBIANCE - i love all the hole-in-the-wall restaurants in Berkeley, but coming from Orange County sometimes i just miss eating at nice, clean, new-looking places. Pasta Bene is neatly set up, has good lighting, and low-key music. They also have a lovely patio to enjoy on nice nights and sunny days. 

PRICES - i think the prices are decent. You get a good amount of quality food for under $10 (or under $6 at lunch). ** Also, you order and pay at the front when you get there, so it's great for groups so you all don't have to fight over how to split the bill!

Overall this place is great, absolutely no complaints. If you live in the UC Berkeley campus area, it's definitely worth trying!

Love, love, love this little place! I stopped in tonight for dinner with my sister. I wasn't at all expecting everything to be as good as it was!!! What a surprise to have such a delicious meal for such a great price. I had a house salad and a pasta dish with eggplant!!!! I was in heaven. The service was fast and friendly too. Perfecto!!!!

Pasta Bene, you are awesome. I think you were made just for me. The best time to come here is around three when the lunch special ends (order some $5 pasta and enjoy) and happy hour begins (hello, $10 pitcher of beer). It's perfection.

Customer service is obviously not one of Pasta Bene's priorities. They want your money and want you to get out as soon as possible. The angry cashier assumed my party of 5 was with the group of 15 other Asians that came in before us, and tried to charge us a 20% gratuity. She threw a fit when we told her that we were a separate group and reluctantly gave us our money back.

As far as the food goes, it's nothing you can't get at any other cheap Italian take out place like Gypsy's. Standard pasta, standard prices.

Pros:
-Noodles cooked well
-Lasagna

Cons:
-Service
-Mediocre dishes


-Joseph

While the location may be a little odd, Pasta Bene is probably the best affordable Italian food in the Berkeley Campus area. The prices are comparable to the other Italian places around town; but with the new specials and daily happy hour deals; Pasta Bene comes out as both the least expensive and the best tasting. 

I had a pint of Sierra Nevada and the Chicken Parmesan; for under $15 the meal was filling and satisfying. I would recommend the Chicken Parmesan as well as their Eggplant Sandwich, also try to snag some Foccacia bread with your order.

Love this place!  I've been here at least five times and never once have I had a complaint.  The pasta dishes are great and of decent portion sizes, restaurant interior is nice (a much better place for a sit-down meal compared to Gypsy's in Asian Ghetto), and I've had probably some of the best service here (compared to other places around campus that usually have mediocre service for college students.. ugh).  The bread that they give you with the pasta dishes is really delicious too, IMO.  $5 lunch specials are great as well! 

Location on Telegraph is not ideal, but at least it's usually not too difficult to find parking if you go for dinner.  Am definitely starting to frequent this place... yum!

It's a nice little romantic Italian restaurant.  Not pretentious, and pretty casual.  Great for groups.  Despite being located in the university section of the city, the clientèle range from college students to young professionals.  

The food is great.  Generous portions for the price, and always pleasing to the tongue.  All in all, a place to go for a casual date night, or with a group of friends.

Perhaps the real problem for me was that I had a different expectation. No, it was more than that. It was the food. Really mediocre.

Pronouncing the word Chianti with a soft "Ch" by multiple staff people. Let's start with that. Pasta overcooked to the point of mushiness. A sauce that had no flavor. Eggplant parm undercooked. Yum.

It's a total college scene, much louder than I anticipated. That's fine. Overcooking pasta by a mile is unacceptable in a place that is "italian".

On the flip side, the prices are cheap and the service is friendly. But I won't ever go back.

new pasta place opened in Berkeley! not very populated yet, but I predict it will be quite the joint once school is in session. 

Came here with three friends and ordered their pasta dishes: Chicken Marsala, Gnocchi, and some type of ravioli. I would highly recommend the Gnocchi since it was delicious and flavorful! I ordered the chicken marsala and noticed how the mushrooms were drenched in wine previously, so the whole meal deserves 4-5 stars because of their deliciousness! The chicken came in one piece and was super tender. 

Overall, this Italian place hits the spot for me. Not too creamy/rich but just right to feel not so guilty eating a carb-ful meal. 
Also, the service is absolutely lovely! Gracie, the waitress, split our bills four ways without us informing her that we would pay individually, which made our exit much faster & pleasant. 

I'd also recommend the Tiramisu cake - layers of delicate combo between cake/chocolate/musse. Absolutely delightful!

Two words...Chicken Marsala. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water.  It's so good! So much flavor and the chicken and mushrooms are perfectly marinated and give off the most wonderful aroma.  

If you don't like marsala, I'd say go for the Tortellini Primavera. It's a vegetarian dish, but really good. The sauce is creamy, but not too dense.

If you go here, you have to try their garlic bread! They make it themselves, so its always fresh.

I've ordered business lunches here a couple of times and you get a really good deal, if you pick up your order you get 20% off of the total cost.  Everyone in my offices loves this place now, so I'll definitely be ordering from them again :]

I think they might have misunderstood my order, so my wait was a little longer than my friends'. I ordered the Chicken Parmigiana, which comes with bread and fettucini. When it finally came, the food was nice and hot. It seemed like they spared no haste in getting food out as soon as it was prepared. 

The chicken had an immediate punch as soon as I tasted it. It was rich in texture and seasoning, and the cheese was sweet and wholesome. The pasta was okay; I was too full to finish it (as is the usual case when I eat at an Italian restaurant.) The bread was so awesome! It's warmed with butter and browned, and it went down so smoothly. 

Definitely hitting this place up again soon.

I came here a second time with my mother and brother for lunch because it was so close to my brother's apt. 

Bummer they increased the lunch specials from $5 to $5.95. But still delicious! 

MELANZANE: Fettuccini with roasted eggplant, sundried tomatoes & garlic in marinara sauce. I love anything eggplant! Their roasted eggplant was breaded before roasting, so there was a slight crispy layer on the outside while the inside was nice and soft. The sundried tomatoes provided a sweet and tangy bite to the pasta.

PENNE BOLOGNESE: I ordered this dish for my mother because she's not a big fan of cheese, but likes heartier dishes. This definitely hit the spot and was a big portion with a nice meaty sauce.

BEEF RAVIOLI:  my brother wasn't that hungry so he got the beef ravioli. They were big ones, but only came with 5, which is surprising compared to the size of the other dishes. I would say don't get the ravioli for the lunch special because the portion isn't that big!

This remains a cute little place in this area of Telegraph. You can definitely sit outside or by one of their big windows during a nice day for a relaxing lunch.

After restaurant-hopping to see what we wanted to eat, my friends and I finally chose Pasta Bene for an Italian Dinner. 

The food:

I ordered a Cheese Ravioli, which was about $7.62. The ravioli was supposedly stuffed with spinach, ricotta, and parmesan, served in a marinara sauce with two pieces of bread. I say supposedly because I couldn't taste or see any spinach at all, and instead it had mushrooms, ricotta, and possibly parmesan, which I also didn't see or taste. I don't know whether or not they made a mistake or the menu was wrong, but either way it was bland and boring. Don't order it, unless you just want something with smaller portions on the cheaper end.

One friend ordered the Carciofi e Pollo, which consisted of linguini with chicken breast , artichoke hearts, and assorted vegetables like carrots and zucchini in an olive-oil herb sauce (also with two pieces of bread). We shared our food, and I found this dish to be fine; the vegetables were cooked well, the pasta was freshly done, and I'm generally a fan of olive oil-based sauces. It was slightly bland, but a little pepper and salt sufficed. The portions were also generous.

Thoughts on the food: The dishes themselves seemed to be very basic. The Carciofi e Pollo was basically a mix of linguini, chicken breast, and vegetables that could have been made easily at home, and there were no extra spices or other method of cooking that made the dish special.
