The Cheese Ravioli was just a double bummer because it was different from what was on the menu and it didn't taste the best. The only thing I really enjoyed from that dish was the bread.

The service:

A little disappointing. We ordered and waited for 10 minutes, but they didn't give us water until we asked for it ourselves, and the lady at the cashier acted surprised when we didn't already have the water. There were a few customers, however, and there was one table with about 12 people, so I guess that's forgivable.

Overall result: For somewhat decent food/portions and lacking service, a 3.

Not crowded Friday afternoon. Got one of the lunch special deals, and it was just decent. Probably not coming back here again. Maybe i got the wrong item on the menu but this place just didn't cut it for me.

This place is still awesome. Have tried a few other dishes and they are all good. I am so impressed with the quality of the food and the atmosphere for the price. They're business model rocks and they're so nice too!

I'm going to start off by saying that I love that there's an older, fatherly/grandfatherly man in charge in the kitchen.

Thanks to Yelp for helping me find this place! The food was a lot better than I would have ever expected, especially since the prices for everything were so reasonable. I ordered the Marco Pollo and it was yummy in my tummy. No joke. I would recommend trying to eat all of it at the restaurant though as the sauce separates and a good amount of oil comes out of the sauce... not the most appetizing sight. But that aside, the service was very friendly so I would definitely come back if I'm ever craving some good Italian in Berkeley again.
Great environment. Good food at a great price. The food is nothing special, so not something I would go out of my way for.

This place is great.  The food is fantastic, We had the calamari which was perfectly done.  I do not always like fried calamari, if it is too deeply fried, but this is perfectly done and it had a little cilantro (i think thats what it was) on it and that gave it a great flavor.  Then we split eggplant parmagiana and  a pasta called rustica which had sausage and eggplant.  Both were great.  The eggplant dish was very large.  It was so inexpensive and listed as an appetizer so we expected it would be small.  The food was very fresh.   It was done perfectly.  I have this dish many places and this was about the best, and I think it was $5.95.  The Rustica pasta was also perfectly done.  The red sauce was a little sweet and really good.  The eggplant was freshly sauteed.
They also have a good selection of beers on tap.

I think this place is the best value that I have been too in a long time.  It is also kind of fun because it is near campus, so lots of students, but lots of others as well, and parking is easy down there.

Everyone seems to mention the service in the yelp reviews.  They were so friendly and attentive.  The food came very quickly and they kept refilling our ice tea and water  We also talked to the owner as we were leaving.  She was really really nice and you can tell she really cares about the food.  This is not a woman that would skimp on quality.  You gotta try this place.

My only problem with this place is I want to try other things on the menu, but want to have exactly the same things as well!

Underappreciated (hidden?) gem of a place. Nothing on the menu is the BEST ____ you've ever had, but everything I've ordered has been reliably good, and the pricing is attractive, especially if you're a student. My personal favorite items are the lasagna and the gnocchi with sausage. The pizzas aren't bad either.

I Love Pasta !!! And really Pasta Bene is the spot !!!

The only thing I would change it, is that I would do it Full Service .. 

It is not much work going to make the order, BUT its also a pleasure to seat and be served. And the waiters almost do that, but when you tip for service, is difficult to do it before eating.

Service and food is the best at Pasta Bene !!!

Next time I'll say to the owner about the full service, is better for us and for the waiters .. they deserve it .. that way it is fair for everybody !!!

May be the focus would be Students .. but the restaurant doesn't  look that way from outside. 

See you there ...........

My boyfriend and I tried this place out for the first time because he and I were craving Italian food. And instead of going to Gypsy's (which to me doesn't really count as Italian food, for some odd reason), we decided to try out this new place. I checked out a few reviews on Yelp and they seemed promising. And true to many reviewers' words, the pricing was pretty darn good. 

We walked in and were a little confused about whether we should seat ourselves, order first fast food style, or what. But the workers were very helpful and kindly seated us at a table and handed us menus (even though there is a huge menu behind the counter). We ordered the crab cakes as our appetizer because many people mentioned it in their reviews. It was smaller than I thought, but pretty tasty. For our entrees, my boyfriend ordered the salmon dish and I ordered the chicken parmigiana. I guess I should've been a little more adventurous, but I had the waiter help me choose between two dishes. I think I'll try to go for the other one next time.

Overall, I enjoyed it. It was pretty empty inside, but it didn't feel too uncomfortable. I might drop by and just order to-go next time because it seems pretty quick and easy since we saw many others come in and do just that.

Cashier was super friendly. 

Food was good, and cheap too. This place is made for students who are on low budgets. Happy Hour is from 3-7pm, $3 for a pint of beer, what more can you ask for?

Great hang out place for a group of friend =)

I have been consistenly eating here since it opened not long so long ago. They were so good that they drove the other Italian place across the street to extinction within a few months. I also cycles through their menu as a Berkeley student and I have two favorite dishes: 

- Pasta Bolonese fills the tummy and is one of the six dishes on special during their lunch hours. Perfect for the budget conscious. 

- Chicken Marsala is my ultimate favorite because they give me a fat piece of chicken with angel hair-like pasta drizzled with a wine sauce and some wine-soaked mushrooms. Protein, check; carbs, check; mushroom nutrients, check. Although sometimes when the mushrooms taste too wine-y I don't eat all of them. 

When they just opened, I came with a friend and they served us complimentary bruschetta. How nice! :) Alas, now they are too popular! 

The ambience of the restaurant is relaxing too. The cute old Italian couple who operates the restaurant also add to the ambience. Perfect for gatherings or for casual dates (which I see all the time...)

Cafe Bene is reminds me of a more upscale version of Gypsy's Trattoria Italiano in the Asian Ghetto. It's got a similar set up with your classic Italian menu except no calzone at Pasta Bene. It's also super cheaper and very affordable for college students nearby. Some differences: (1) Pasta Bene is cleaner with actual dishes and silverware, (2) servers at Pasta Bene brings you the food (you get a number tag), (3) Pasta Bene serves alcohol. 

Overall, I must say that I still like Gypsy's better... but perhaps, it might be for old times sake.

Since I live nearby, I come pretty often. The lunch special deal is really nice, although it used to be cheaper. The portions are just right and the ingredients are very fresh! The staff is also super friendly and nice. The restaurant is a nice, peaceful place to study since it's in the less busy area of Telegraph.

i recently went with a friend to eat dinner here. it wasn't that crowded, but maybe it was because it was the middle of the week.

we sat down and were given water and menus. i don't remember if the waiter came and took our order, or if we went up to the counter and told him directly, but the food came out quickly.

i had the marco pollo. it came with two small pieces of white bread. the pasta was really good. the portions were pretty filling. 

i would come back if i were ever in berkeley looking for italian food.

I've been eating here for a good 6 months now since I live across the street.  I get it to go, I eat in with friends.  Its never failed to provide a cost effective solution to my italian food cravings.  I've pretty much tried everything on the menu.  I have to recommend the Chicken Picatta and the King Salmon in the pasta department.  Their pizza and bruschetta is also delicious and not to be overlooked.  The old couple that owns / manages the restaurant is very friendly and attentive to customer needs.  I've never had trouble with a large or small party here, although at times the line can get plenty long during busy hours.   So far, the food has been consistent and feels very traditional Italian without the hassle or cost of a nicer sit down restaurant.

Great service and mouth-watering food.

Penne bolognese was the entre choice of the night!   I also ordered a tantalizing side of bruschetta for ONLY $2!  All of this and the bill was only about $10!!

Great dinner near Berkeley campus!

While the prices-for-the-food-and-decor is still hard to beat...

After having a full dinner service experience the first three times I went to Pasta Bene, I was forced to order and pay at the front (and get a plastic number) my last time. It made me kind of sad, since the food was still good and I still had my water glass refilled by a waiter.

Their bathroom was still squeaky clean though. I'll give them that one.

I'm so sad.  This used to be a great, locally owned bakery that I used to get my fresh bread from when I was still a student at Cal.

It's one of those, place your orders at the register then find a seat, places.

It was moderately busy with a lot of seating.  Although there is really only one waitress, but I'm not complaining.  She did come around a good 3-4 times to see how we were doing.  Hats off to her since she was flying it solo in a somewhat packed place.

They have very decent portions for some yummy Italian food at moderate prices.  I got the Chicken Picatta which was pretty good.  I'd like to see some vegetables with the dish as it was basically pasta with chicken and capers and some bread.  Some veggies on the side would have created the right balance of carbs, protein and vegetables.  I also found a lemon seed in my chicken, but nothing to complain about, it happens.

Although I have to say my heart still belongs to Cafe Milense down the street as the food is a little cheaper and helped fill me up when I was a po' college student.

I highly recommend!

I tried this place for the first time today and I left quite satisfied!  It's a bit further away than the campus than I'd prefer (since I have classes on Northside), I liked the contemporary and open setting.  Definitely did not expect that kind of atmosphere.

I ordered something simple, Cheese Ravioli.  Partly because it's one of their $5 lunch specials (which is a great deal!), but also because I wanted to try something more basic for my first experience here.  Service was very friendly, but it took a decent bit of time for the food to come out.  Overall, the ravioli had a nice, al-dente texture, but it was slightly lukewarm and slightly too much sauce for my taste.  It also came with two pieces of bread which were okay.

Overall, I liked this place, but next time I'll try something a little more extravagant.  4/5 stars for now!

This place really was damn good.  I am indeed a fan.

I half-service.  You order and they bring your food, drinks, and check in on you.  All of the staff members were great.  The cashier was nice as could be, and the server was attentive and friendly.

The food was great.   All of our dishes had a great presentation.  I had a special, which was a chicken pesto ravioli in alfredo sauce.  It was divine.  I loved it.  The portion was a little small.  I only got 5 raviolis which weren't that big and the plate costs $9.  A lot of the other reviewers talked about how cheap and how much food you got, but that was not my experience.  But what I did eat was very tasty.

I will be going back, and that's really all that matters.

Pasta Bene is one of my favorite restaurants near the UC Berkeley campus.

Let's talk about the food. Delicious, fresh and affordable.  Everything is made upon order. You can view their items on their large menu or see a regular sized menu when you get up to the register to order. They have a great lunch special from 11:00 a.m am until 3:00 p.m. consisting of a $5.95 entree item.  They usually have choices that change every day.  

My personal favorite is the "Chicken Breast Sandwich" with french fries on the side. Always delicious. It's a great mix of flavors. The chicken is always well season and it's always a pleasant meal.

The service is outstanding. The servers are cordial and the owners are almost always  present at the restaurant.

Overall, I have not had a bad experience here. Definitely a must have for either lunch or dinner. 

It can be a quick bite or a nice sit down place.

Just try it!

Hmm. I've heard a lot of people tell me how good Pasta Bene's is, but I don't like their food  Went once, thought it was average.  Heard everyone raving about it, and thought, "Maybe I just got a bad dish, I'll give it another try!"  But when I went I was disappointed again.  

I can't really put my finger on an exact complaint, other than that I've had much better Italian food.  Maybe it's just my personal taste, and I can't name a better Italian alternative to Pasta Bene (Gypsy's, maybe), but just not feelin this place.  

Overall:  I've heard a lot of good things about this place, but I didn't find it remarkable.
The food was delicious and well presented with sizable portions and a reasonable prices.  The place looks clean and the service was great.  I would come back for more.

You know Pasta Bene is too good when you forget to write a review and end up coming back again and again.

I can't count how many times I've been back here trying new things on the menu. Everything is delicious and reasonably priced! Even though it's a little further from campus than Gypsy's, I personally like Pasta Bene more because the pasta isn't as oily. Another plus is the bread! It's much softer than the one at Gypsy's and complements the pasta sauce well.

My personal favorites are the Gnocchi Sausage and the Gamberetto. Don't forget to try the tiramisu!

I also really like the place since it's great for large groups. The staff that work there are very helpful and always do a great job with the food and the service.

The Honest Truth: Not bad.  The environment is nice and its a good place to sit down and have a casual meal.  The food is presented well, but I wouldn't say that the flavors are anything too too special.  Portions are not that big, but enough to make you content.  Service is good.  Get the gnocchi sausage.

The Details:
I've been here a couple times.  I haven't been amazed at the food, but its decent and I like the environment of the place.  Its casual, but its a good place to sit down for a meal in Berkeley.  I've had the rustico, lasagna, gnocchi sausage, and the chicken parmigiana.  I thought the rustico lacked a little flavor, although most people say they like it.  The lasagna was good, but its just lasagna.  gnocchi sausage has good flavors, but the portion isn't that big.  Chicken parmigiana is decent as well.  I like the tiramisu that they have.  The service is always friendly and nice, but the food is only decent for me. I like the flavors of gypsy's but Pasta Bene is definitely cleaner tasting and not as heavy.

The place looks really nice - and also serves beer and wine - which makes you think that it's more upscale and expensive. BUT - they're actually just as cheap as Gypsy's - and the quality seems better. I walked out feeling like I just ate a meal instead of feeling like I ate a lot of oil/grease - though I admit both are delicious. We ordered the garlic bread, cheese ravioli, pasta bene, and spaghetti with meatballs. 

Just a note - we ordered the garlic bread thinking that the entrees wouldn't come with bread - but they did (not garlic bread though)! We still managed to finish all of it though - because it was so delicious. Their bread is light - but becomes more hearty and filling when you eat it. 

The cheese ravioli was really good - and even though the marinara sauce in it looked exactly the same as the marinara sauce in my cousin's pasta bene - they tasted pretty different. Looks like they pay attention to make each of their dishes something new. I didn't get to try the spaghetti - but my other cousin said that he was surprised by the number of meatballs he got - aka. we got our money's worth. He also said they were better than Gypsy's meatballs, which I think are terrible. I'll definitely be back.

I had the Chicken Marsala. The sauce tasted weird and it didn't taste as good as Gypsy's. It's also pricier, about $11 including tip. The service wasn't anything to write home about either. I'm not sure why everyone loves this place.

Food = 3 Stars + 1 star because the cashier and waitress was really nice to us.

I got the Penne Bolognese, which was decent.  I would order it again.  My friends ordered the Chicken Parm, Chicken Marsala, and some kind of linguini with proscruitto and peas.  I mean, all the food was really decent and so was the service, but there was no character.  The food is comparable to Gypsy's and La Val's, but in a cleaner sleeker environment.

Would I go again?  Yes.  But they should change their wedges of bread (that come with pasta) to garlic bread! That would really be delicious.  Maybe they'll read this review and take a hint.

yay for pasta bene!

At first I was a bit skeptical of the place since it was always empty and reeked of mediocrity (most likely due to its initial emptiness), but after several recommendations I decided to check this place out and have since been a frequent visitor!  At a very affordable price, you can get different types of the many pastas that you'd otherwise pay a lot more at other dine-in italian restaurants.  Its more elegant and comfier interior setting is also a big reason why I'd visit pasta bene over durant food court's gypsy's.

I have been visiting pb on a fairly regular basis, and I have yet to be disappointed by them, whether it be the quality of their food or their awesome staff.  The waitress was more than happy to substitute my eggplants with mushrooms, and they're super quick and welcoming!  It is no wonder that the place no longer holds the same emptiness that it once had but instead is always filled with loads of happy diners!

try their gnocchi!!
Had a big banquet here and it was awesome! Food was great. Loved the cheese ravioli!!!!! The bruschetta was good too! And service was friendly and accommodating.

My go-to place for inexpensive pasta in Berkeley! The food quality is great, and the portions are pretty big! The entrees also come with this super light and yummy bread! I wish I could just order a basket of that stuff, haha. 
I usually get their meat lasagna, or chicken marsala, which totally fills me up but isn't horribly heavy. I've come multiple times with both big groups and small, and I've never had a problem with the food or the service.

I was going to give it 2 stars but I'll give it 3 because, judging from the reviews below, it may have improved since I came here a year ago. I remember the portions being really small for the price. Maybe it's because I'm from so-cal and am not used to the expensive prices in the bay area.. The good thing is the location is really close to campus and where I lived. The garlic bread here was amazing. The pasta wasn't bad, the portions were just too small. I'm just sad it replaced that cute little bakery. Berkeley needs more affordable bakeries!
Pretty good food, fast service. Price for a full pasta entree was a bit pricier than gypsy's, but for those who don't mind paying more it tastes better.

Pasta Bene just opened up in April 2010. I noticed that it was finally open and excitedly told my housemates about it. We went a couple of days later and were quite impressed.

Let me start by saying that this place is a lot better than Milanese Caffe right across the street (sorry, Milanese! you're tasty, but you overdo the cream sauces, your garlic bread tastes yucky, and you kicked us out at 9pm!!!). It's very fresh, creamy but light, and flavorful. 

ATMOSPHERE (4/5): Very open, spacious (see pic). Very clean shiny big tables. My friends loved the nice bathroom. Big counter that you can see into the big clean kitchen. High ceiling. Beautiful decor with mirrors. At nighttime, they light candles for each table. Cute, but the romantic side a bit lowered due to being too spacious. 

SERVICE (3/5): Nice waiters. Young, tall, (must admit nice looking, guys and girls). Simple, good service. 

FOOD (5/5): Delicious. Good Italian fare that's much better than the fast-food feel of Gypsy's and Milanese Caffe. Each pasta dish comes with two cute triangles of focaccia bread. Good stuff, much better than the garlic and pizza bread at Milanese Caffe. And super cheap! It's only $6 to $9 or $10 for pasta dishes. Even the salmon pasta dish was like $10.50 or sometohing. We ordered...
*Chicken Alfredo: looked good. Chicken, fettucine alfredo sauce, mushrooms. I had a mushroom, tasted good, and my friend liked it.
*Pasta Bene: spaghetti and vegetables. I don't know if I tried this, but my friends did. (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/QQIjsdcokFermi2ugoD6ow?select=WNi4du_hBtvV2wyhGjKvfg)
*Tortellini: multi-colored (veggie?) cheese-filled tortellini in a light tomato-cream sauce. Not too heavy despite being a cheese-filled pasta dish. Just right. (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/QQIjsdcokFermi2ugoD6ow?select=6CMjvONYO6i5-axxbbwhGg)
*Melanzane:  roast eggplant, fettucine, sun dried tomatoes, garlic, marinara sauce. I really liked my dish. The eggplant wasn't soaked with oil. It was flavorful. Fresh, light, tasty, recommended! (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/QQIjsdcokFermi2ugoD6ow?select=3UBYfBEZ9tCNswcxUeyqtA)
*Tiramisu: OMG, a huge piece that almost needs to be shared between 2 people. It's beautiful and has a blueberry sauce around it. So delicious and light and tasty. (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/QQIjsdcokFermi2ugoD6ow?select=czH7oPdNJDM9K4BIrsilyA)

This place is very tasty and I hope they maintain the quality for the years to come and that they stay in business despite the recession. Definitely a must try for the taste and the price and the atmosphere!

Great portion sizes. Friendly service. 

Ordered:

- small salad (awesome)
- eggplant Parmesan (awesome)
- bruschetta (awesome)
- pasta rustica (awesome)

Nice seating area inside. A more senior employee was training a newer employee and was doing an excellent job of remaining attentive to customers while explaining procedures to the new person.

Highly recommended.

Excellent pasta with vegetables and chicken dish at an affordable price!  Very clean, great service, just a gem of a place in Berkeley.  We were just passing through town, and luckily found this place on Yelp.  Thanks!

My BF and I were hungry and was craving Italian, so we yelped places and discovered this great little place!!  We had the calamari for an appetizer, I had the Marco Pollo and he had the Chicken Marsala.  We loved it, the food, the place, the service and even the other customers/guest.  Can't wait to come back!! Tirimisu was good too!!

mmm this place is perfect in every way. Their pasta is so cheap for what it is! Each dish is about $7-$8 on average, but they give you a LOT of food. The setting is very relaxing and fancy, perfect for a casual lunch or a formal dinner! Definitely try their Fettucini Alfredo! The bread that comes with the pasta is definitely a no-regretter!

I've only been to Pasta Bene once but it was great food. I would definitely visit again when I am in the area.

Very low prices for the quality of food you get. You will leave satisfied.

This is a great place to have affordable Italian food. It's very casual so you order and pay at the counter (tips are not required). However, the server was so attentive! She brought our food quickly and asks us often if we want more water. I ordered melanzane, which is a vegetarian dish but was very good. I felt very healthy and happy eating here!

This place is spotless and the staff are super friendly. I love the pasta with veggies and the cheesecake is pretty good too. The panini and garlic fries are great for lunch. The prices are very reasonable. They have a few beers on tap and a happy hour! I am always greeted with a smile and they don't mind if you study quietly for a few hours. I love hanging out in this calm little place, away from the nuttiness on Telegraph.

Service: 5
Taste: 4.5
Quality: 4
Variety: 4
Price: about $10-$15
Recommend to a friend: Yes

People: The employees at Pasta Bene are so friendly! Especially the lady who works there- so sweet!

Food: I am no connoisseur of Italian foods, but the quality of the food here is really good, so I often find myself asking whoever the cashier is at the time what his/her favorite dish is. I know the old lady's favorite dish is the Chicken Marsala, which is AMAZING! The gnocchi is pretty delicious too! Make sure you like gnocchi though; it has a particular texture and flavor that, for me, got a little boring after I was 3/4 of the way finished with my meal. But I have to say, Carciofi e Pollo is where it's at. YUM. And their Tiramisu (which, by the way, is only $3+tax!) = heaven in your mouth. It is plated very masterfully, but make sure you don't sit and just stare at it for too long -- the bread will get soggy and not taste as fresh.

Tidbits: Overall, the food isn't too greasy, and the portions are pretty filling but you probably won't be taking home a to-go box (unless I just eat a lot..?). It's been pretty busy every time I've gone, but the place is pretty spacious, so it's rather accommodating. 

PS: I need to try their pizzas as well (they look phenomenal), so I will be updating again once I try one!

We had dinner late at night and food the food wonderful presented, good fresh salad and the service was very friendly. Nice atmosphere. Good spaghetti. Prices were very reasonable. Gluten free was available.
You order at counter and they bring to your table.

Just walked by with a hungry belly. I love Italian so I dropped in for the first time to this place. Loved it! The minestrone soup was filled with a bit too many beans, but the flavors were awesome anyway. Their sandwiches are very fresh with vegetables and grilled chicken piled on some amazing fresh focaccia. It was soft and delicious!

The inside seating area is large and could accommodate a huge party. The staff is very nice and attentive. The prices were perfect. A full entree for less than $10! The food was something special and I'm looking forward to going back here to try more of their menu.

This place offers GOOD value !  Where else are you going to get hot pasta dishes on the cheap.  The students were away as school wasn't in session.  A perfect time to go there where there are no crowds.   Looking for a hot meal at a reasonable price ?  You found the place.  Enjoy.

Pasta is cheap and delicious. I loved the chicken Marsala. 

They won't let you wait for a table when they're full. You have to get your food to-go. Call early to make a reservation.

Fresh food. Awesome value. The chicken parm was great. The food is on par with almost any overpriced place in north beach. I actually preferred ordering at the counter over having a server. They still have people circulating refilling drinks and bussing tables. I'll be back. Also, I challenge you to find a better piece of homemade tiramisu, and for only $4!?
Good food, fair prices, and $10 pitchers during happy hour (3-7pm).  Hope they start growing livers for transplant soon.

Mmmm Tiramisu....

Pasta Bene opened around April this year.  It's the second location, the first is in SF.  Since I don't live here anymore, I don't get to try places often.  I was surprised by this place! 

Let me start by saying the service is amazing!  I went 2 days in a row! Everyone was really nice, welcoming, and helpful! The first night I just went for Tiramisu with a friend who lives nearby.  The second night we actually ate there (and yes, I got Tiramisu again!).  I wasn't sure what to order.  My friends love their chicken sandwich.  I asked for a recommendation from the waitress, and she asked what I was in the mood for.  All i said was chicken and nothing too creamy or rich.  She recommended the Carciofi e Pollo, which is delicious! Highly recommended.  It was flavorful, the sauce was relatively light, and the pasta was cooked just right! Definitely end with some Tiramisu!  It's not your typical tiramisu. It's a little more cake like and has fruit toppings. 

It's also a pretty good deal.  You order at the counter and they give you a number and bring your food to your table.  We got ours really quickly, but they also weren't too busy at the time. They do accept credit cards, which I know not everyone does.
Good prices, service, and food.

5 DOLLAR LUNCH SPECIAL that just screams "poor college students."  you can choose from pasta bene, spaghetti & meatballs, beef lasagna, melanzane, or the cheese ravioli.
meat-lovers should steer clear of the melanzane bc it's basically spaghetti with eggplant and tomato sauce.  
i recommend the tiramisu if you still have space in your stomach since the portions here are pretty good. 
Stay away from the bruschetta - two slices of toasted bread topped with olive oil, diced tomatoes and cheese. The bread tasted stale and was not crunchy at all.

It is sooo freaken good  for the price and the portion. 

After a night out in the town...... pasta bene just hit the spot :)

Will I ever eat the food here and be magically transported to memories of beautiful, amazing Itay and their food which blows most countries out of the water? No

Will I get to place my order with a friendly cashier, and get heaping portions of good food quickly? Yes.

That is worth 4 stars, memories of Italy notwithstanding.

Pasta was dry, not that flavorful, WAY too greasy, and small portions. 
The owners were rude and the cashier didn't seem like he wanted to be there.
It wasn't worth the money I paid

It's nothing special and I would recommend Gypsy's or Pasta in a Box instead-cheaper and better pasta.

They have these amazing $5 dishes until 3pm. 
Their menu is really affordable especially on a college budget.

I ordered the meat lasagna. It's about 4''x3'' which I think is a fair size for lunch and $5! The meat sauce was yummy. 

I am definitely coming back when I am in the area.

I stumbled opon here after a sojourn in the Berkeley/Oakland hills and I was craving carbs after a date with my bike. I'm one of those indecisive types so I let the Yelp iPhone app do the work. A few swipes, and a jaunt from the corner of College and Ashby near a certain yoga outfitter where I was standing at to Telegraph I ended up here. Me and my riding buddies liked the outdoor seating, it was bike friendly in the fact that we brought our steeds into the patio. 

As for the food goes, it's standard issue Italian. I had the chicken marsala and except for the pasta being a touch undercooked, it was satisfying. Washed it down with a $4 Black Diamond ale. My friends had the fettuchine alfredo and the gnocchi and I sampled it and it was good as well. 

I'll mirror some of the other reviews there in that the ambiance is a step above Gypsy's. The service is walk in, order, sit down and food will be bought out to you. A sweet Italian lady took my order, and a girl who I've seen at the East Bay Bike Party was our waiter which I thought was cool and unexpected.

Gnocchi sausage. 
ehh it was alright. Sausage was pretty salty and the gnocchi with the sauce was kind of bland. I added chilly flakes and parm. The atmosphere was pretty good and definitely like the idea that you get to order the food and pay and then sit and eat. Easy to go out with friends to eat i guess. Wouldn't specifically go out there to eat but if nothing else wouldn't mind. 

They have a lunch special with certain pasta for 5 bucks. Price is normal i guess for italian food not during the lunch special area which is around 7 bucks to 10. They also have happy hour for beer 3-7 i think 3 bucks.

I don't know where to start with this place. My friend recently graduated from UC Berkeley and after graduation she decided to come here for her dinner celebration. Of course she called in weeks in advance and made reservations for a party of 20. So we get there, and we are seated and given menus. After looking at the menus we all decide to order our food. The owners gets upset because everyone decides to pay separately (you prepay for the food) in doing so she gets an attitude and tells me " ugh you guys are making my job a lot harder, so your gratuity for each of you is 18% not 15%." I then explain to her that 1. I'm a guest of the dinner 2. The menu says gratuity for parties over 8 was 15%. When I point that out she says " oh no, that's old" . So I end up paying for my food because I didn't want to mess up my friend's big day. I get my food, which by the way was disgusting, and not once are we checked on, or asked is our food ok. What's the point of paying gratuity? And to make things worse, everyone congrats the Cal graduate, and our "waiter" comes to the table and claps for the graduate and sends her well wishes. And the owner comes over there and tells her, mind your own business, and don't clap for them. The waiter quit right on the spot ( which tells you she was fed up with their rudeness). And when it is time for us to leave, the owner asks us to bus our own tables because the waiter quit...but remember we paid gratuity so of course we didn't bus our tables. We did have to get up and ask for to-go bags though..smh..I then told the owners that they were both very rude, and that's not how you treat customers, and maybe this treatment had a lot to do with the fact that most of the party was African American..she then says " no I'm African American too" which clearly she wasn't..I WILL NEVER BE GOING BACK!!!

On the one hand, this place is pretty much like Gypsy's--with roughly the same menu price--except with the added waiters and tips.  On the other hand, their tiramisu blows every other Italian restaurant away.  Walk the few extra blocks to this place if you're up for a change, have a few extra minutes/hours to spare from classes, or because you believe that their TIRAMISU IS JUST SO GOOD.

Pasta Bene's lunch specials are awesome!

For a decent price, you get a good amount of delicious pasta and bread. I came here with two friends, and ordered the Melanzane. It wasn't too garlic-y, which was great, yet still very flavorful, and just the right portion for me.

However, the lunch specials did increase in price compared to the last time I remember. Now, they are $5.95 rather than just $5...

In any case, I like how you can order at the counter and sit down, having the waiters bring over your food when it is ready (and water), since it made for a nice and uninterrupted much-needed catch up between my 2 friends and myself :)

Definitely a fan and a regular at this place.  I used to live right next to this restaurant and saw the construction of the place but moved to SF before it opened.  BUTTTTT since I go to school in Berkeley, the first chance I got, I went and tried it.  Hella worth it, duh. 

Let me start off with what I LOVE:

-Service: small staff but SUPER friendly.  Nice Asian guy waiter and super nice Italian guy who looks like the owner
-CHEAP prices: appetizers are 2-6 dollars. entrees are 7-10 dollars
-FOOD: i got the bruschetta (1.95) and i absolutely LOVE it. It's only two pieces of bread but it is just so delicious and it's not too pricey so you don't mind paying two bucks for two pieces. I've had the Tropicana pizza (7.95) and it was so delicious! It's a pretty good size.. it has six slices.  I secretly want to go back after dining with my friends and order one of these without them knowing and eat it right away at home. hehe. I've also had the Melanzane which was probably the only thing that i didnt absolutely love.  I think it would've been better if the noodles were cooked in the sauce for awhile because the sauce was pretty good.  

I got the tiramisu for free one time because one of my friend's is a super regular there! It was nice that they remembered her and that they do nice things like this for their regular patrons... not to say that they should expect it all the time.  

Oh, they also have a happy hour from 3-7!!! I don't even know what a cheap happy hour price is at this point because I've gone from Sac where prices are super cheap to SF where prices are ridiculous but a pitcher of beer for 10... I LOVE! esp cause they have my baby boo - Sierra Nevada Pale Ale. they also had this other local beer i think called boont or something like that but they were both SOOO good and i thought 10 dollars was a good price. 

PASTA BENE - YOU HAVE WON ME OVER GYPSYS!!! LOVELOVELOVE

This place is AMAZING. High quality Italian food, reasonable prices, $3 daily happy hour draft beer, modern yet comfortable environment, patio on Telegraph, and the nicest employees I've seen in a restaurant for a while. I rarely give reviews but this place really deserves one.

The tortellini dish I ate here was amazing! The vegetables it came with were cut so thinly it was so good to eat. This was a non meat dish though, but that is okay because there is always dessert. I decided to go with their cheesecake, and that was amazing as well. It came with a blueberry sauce with real blueberries, a strawberry, and mint leaves to garnish. The ambiance was really great too since the decorations/ chairs are really nice. It is great for groups because you pay individually for your meal so there is no worrying about the hassle of splitting the check. The waiters are also very nice! They offered to take group pictures of our group.
Portobello mushroom raviolo was absolutely delectable. I'm very particular about my pesto sauces, but this dish was perfect. Even better that you can reserve a table for large groups.

This is a nice little joint where you can meet up for something a little more special. It's like Gypsys but better in that it has a little less of the college restaurant vibe you get at Asian Ghetto. Keep Pasta Bene on your list of a little bit nicer of a sit in place that's still close to campus.

I ordered: Melazane: fettuccini with roasted eggplant, sundried tomatoes & garlic in marinara sauce. The sundried tomatoes really completed everything with a nice sweet and different texture, while the eggplant went really well with the sausages in the dish. Overall, okay dish. There was enough for leftovers.

So all in all, it's a nice sit down place for only $3-4 more than normal. Not too bad.
Inexpensive, good quality and great service! I would definitely eat here again- $5.95 pasta is the best.

Amazing Italian Restaurant. Everything here is made from scratch. 
I think it seems to be out of place, since the prices are way beyond what college student can afford on a daily basis.

I just had to try this place due to amazing reviews by my fellow Yelper friend (right below me). They had a special that day that wasn't on the menu, so I figured I'd be risky and try that--it was seafood linguine I believe? 

The place was really pack with a large party, so it's understandable that my dish took awhile to come out. The dish was a little on the dry side--not enough sauce. It might be because a friend and I both ordered the same thing, so they didn't proportion it right. So we kindly asked the waiter if we can just have more sauce on the side. Instead, he came back and said that the chef would remake it for us and took our dishes away. Whoaaa we didn't expect that! THAT was really good service. All we wanted was some sauce on the side and they ended up re-making our dish (of course not a complete brand new dish). The "new" dish was pretty delicious. 

I would definitely come back and try some other dishes when I have pasta cravings.

I was very happy to stumble upon this place.  Being from out of town and not doing the proper research before hand, I was just bumbling around Berkeley in search of something more than a hippie hangout.

I just needed some good food and a good beer.  This place was just what I wanted.  The owner lady and servers were super kind and made me feel really welcome.  Casual dining room with nice soft music.

The food was great.  I had the fennel sausage pizza-well cooked, great size, especially for the price.  Topped with fresh arugula, it was presented as if I hadn't ordered it at the counter.  I was impressed.

Here is the thing. This place has good pasta no doubt. They are a little stingy on the portions though. The price is reasonable, but not the portions. They surpass Gypsy's on certain dishes. But you leave not entirely full... per say.

1st of all, the atmosphere of this place KILLS Gypsy's.  It's almost as if this place doesn't belong on Telegraph at all.

I wish I could say that about the food, though.

So far, I've had the lasagna, bruschetta, and chicken parmigiana.  They lose major brownie points on their red sauce...it's like something is missing.  And the lasagna was definitely light on the ricotta.  I mean, that's why we get lasagna, we want some cheese up on that shizzzz.  The bruschetta was like they took some bread from Safeway, sprayed some butter on it, and put some chopped tomatoes on it.  Not. good.

However, they redeemed themselves recently, as I decided to give them one more try.  The chicken parm was juicy, a good size, and I love how they didn't over-bread the breast.  Not too greasy, but I wish they added just a little bit more marinara to cover the side of fettucini they serve with it.

Good and attentive service, though.

If you want great and authentic Italian, you'll have to venture away from Telegraph!

Love the chicken fettucini alfredo! 
cheap, fast, good portions and delicious!

So tasty and really affordable! I was shocked by how delish my pasta was, as well as by how large the portion was for only $7.00. The service was friendly and quick. The restaurant was clean with nice, simple decor. I will definitely be back here!
P.S. The bread that comes with any pasta dish is AMAZING.

Do not come here if you are in a large group.

The food is okay, as usual, but the service was so shitty. 

We came in a large group and were pressured to sit down and get our orders taken (for a fixed gratuity, of course). Fine, whatever. But when we asked the waitress if she could split the bill amongst 4 cards as we had no cash on us, it was like asking for her first-born. She informed us in this nasty, awful tone that she had "told us if we wanted to pay separately we were to do it at the counter" (when she did no such thing) and that she would "do it this time but next time we had better--" at which point we politely told her how much we appreciated it and handed her our cards. Uh, hello, weren't you the one who chirpily told us to inform you if we wanted it split a different way as you handed us the bill? Stupid wench. Never coming here again for my mediocre pasta. I'll take Gypsy's gruff cashier guy anyday!

I've only tried their lunch specials and so far, so good. I still don't know if I would take this place over gypsies though.

Some of the things that are better than Gypsies: 
-The waiting time is less here than at Gypsies. Is it more or is it kinda awkward waiting for your to-go pasta at Gypsies and you start seeing every single classmate you've ever had since freshman year? 
-The dishes aren't as heavy and oily as they are at Gypsies, which is good because you don't feel as bad after eating it. 

Overall its a great restaurant. The portions are a good size and they have really nice lady who offers water every time you order your food.

I was very surprised to find a high quality Italian restaurant  nestled right next to such stores as Buffalo Exchange and the Dark Entry. Being completely honest, I had such low expectations of this place, that this review may be more positive than the restaurant actually is. It's probably just a 4 star restaurant, but I'm giving it 5 stars because it just blew me away. There are so many outside factors that led me to think I wouldn't have a good meal here. First off, it's on Telegraph Ave, a street not known for it's culinary prowess. Second, the prices are cheap, especially for Italian food. Third, it's not really a sit down and order restaurant. The ordering is much like a fast food restaurant. You pretty much just walk up to the counter and order off an overhead menu. All this varied so much from other Italian restaurants I've been to, that I just didn't expect my meal to be good at all. But my meal was great.

I ordered the Chicken Masala. It came out pretty quickly in a huge portion. My piece of chicken was huge and it was covered in the sauce and mushrooms. The mushrooms were the best part of this dish. Sure, they're just naturally good, but with the combination of the sauce, noodles, and chicken, it just totally blew my head off. The chicken was cooked pretty well as well. So many places just don't know how to cook chicken. It's so easy to dry chicken, especially a large chunk of breast like I was served on my plate. But the chicken here was plenty juicy and not dry at all. Each dish came with a few pieces of bread as well. Normally I wouldn't mention something as mundane as bread, but the bread here was delicious and it was such a nice addition to the plate. First off, I was able to use the bread to soak up the excess pasta sauce. Second, the bread was ever so slightly burnt. I don't know why, but the flavor of this burnt bread was just perfect to me. I can't even describe it. Burned things normally taste terrible, but this burnt bread tasted sweet for some reason. Gotta go and try it yourself.

Can't wait to come back here and try out some more of their dishes! Great food for a great value.

My favorite Italian restaurant within walkable distance from campus!

-Food, 5 stars-
I've tried the 
- Chicken Marsala: my favorite, despite the fact that I hate mushrooms
- Chicken Parmigiano: chicken is always tender and juicy
- Beef Lasagna: looks tiny, but it always fills me up just like other plates
- Cheese Ravioli: looks like a small plate, but very filling
- Melanzane: a perfect plate for a lighter meal (no meat)
- King Salmon: only plate with pesto (my favorite sauce D:), Salmon is a bit small and a bit too much pasta compared to the salmon
- Tropicana Pizza: I ate it after it turned cold, so it wasn't that great, but I will give Pasta Bene benefit of the doubt.
- Portebello Mushroom Ravioli Special: SUPER GOOOOOOOOD but it's not offered regularly.  
- Tiramisu: YUMMMMMMMMMMMMM
- Cheesecake: YUMMMMMMMMMMM

-Service, 4 stars-
PB always has awesome service.  However, when I went yesterday, I realized the waitress did not catch one of my orders over the phone so it was not made when I got there to pick up.  At the same time I was re-ordering, the Italian lady (owner?) walked past by the waitress and said "she said no sausage" while holding a plate of Gnocchi Sausage.  Yup, you guessed it.  

I mean, despite the fact that she messed up, she was being very apologetic and friendly about it.  As I was waiting, the Italian lady apologized to me for the wait and told me it would take a few more minutes because the chicken breast needs some time to be fully and well cooked.  

In my opinion, customer service is not always about delivering error-free service, but more about the attitude of delivery.  I'm sure all of us have run into super-rude customer services before, but PB treated its mistake very professionally. 

Therefore, service gets 4-stars. 

- Atmosphere-
OWNS Gypsy's. 

- Price - 
I always enjoy the 11-3pm lunch specials when I don't feel like spending much on lunch.  But they have raised the price across all items recently, including the specials.  

I dislike the price increase (umm who would like it), but I find it reasonable.

The only tiny set back is that portions are a bit small considering its price.

I think the pastas are decent. Fettucini alfredo or the gnocci are good. All the dishes here are extremely thick and cheesy, so the taste gets to be a bit too much sometimes. Makes me thirsty after a few bites. The bread, oh I'm so disappointed in the bread. I am a bread person, I LOVE bread. This place is probably one of the few places where I'll leave the bread uneaten. Don't know why, but its crunchy-but-not-really texture on the outside that is actually soggy in disguise is just so confusing to me. Is it trying to be crunchy or chewy? It comes out being neither!

Pizza, on the other hand, is amazing. The dough is chewy, crunchy, and filled with the amazing floury taste of bread. It's a tiny bit sweet, so it couples perfectly with the salty toppings. Not a lot of people think to get pizza here, but in my opinion they might be even better than the pasta.

The atmosphere is fantastic. Live band playing if you catch Pasta Bene on some weekends. Sun pouring in from the front windows, reflecting off the clear water glasses and shining silverware. Mmmmm, the decor might be one of the best things about this place.

It's sad that the place is fairly empty. But also makes me feel like I have my own little pasta place.

Pasta Bene offers good and cheap food in a very clean setting (as every other review has said). I really recommend the Bruschetta. It's like 2 dollars for two hefty slices of bread topped with tomatoes/basil/olive oil. So good. I honestly might just get 3 orders of the Bruschetta and call that my lunch next time I come. And yes there will be plenty of next times. 

I would deter from the Calamari until they give that batter recipe some more flavor. Other than that, everything else, including the service, was great. I highly recommend it for anyone seeking an inexpensive and friendly meal.

Delicious pastas, delicious pizza, delicious appetizers, delicious desserts, all for a reasonable price!

I've tried many different pastas, one of their pizzas, their bruschetta, and their tiramisu. I was most impressed with their gnocchi because you won't find many places that are willing to put the time into making it. 

A word of advice, do not order the lasagna. I found that thoroughly disappointing because I got a dish with cheese that lacked the intense cheesy taste that people associate with lasagna and a sauce that was sweet and reminded me somewhat of barbeque sauce. After eating a few bites, it was hard for me to finish...

Would have given this 5 stars but was disappointed with lasagna and atmosphere was not very good. There is a line that extends between two large tables in the center so it gets pretty crowded in there.
The service was great and waitress was very helpful and friendly. Her recommendation was delicious The cook seem invested in the food he served, and I can see the effort he puts in the food he makes.

I expected Pasta Bene to be overrun with college students during dinner rush, but there was actually a good mixture of students and non-students.

The restaurant is pretty big and roomy. So, this is a good place for big and small parties.

To me, Pasta Bene is a mix between the higher quality Italian restaurants and the fast-food type Italian restaurants. High quality because the quality of the food is superb, and fast-food type because you order and pay at the counter when you first enter.

I ordered the Gamberetto, which is fettuccini with shrimp and mushroom in tomato-cream sauce. The Gamberetoo was a little bit on the salty side, but overall very tasty. In addition, the portions were very generous. I could barely finish it!!

Overall, Pasta Bene offers good food quality, service, and atmosphere!

It's rare to find a place that is so clean and good in Berkeley. It is an adoreable, clean, modern restaurant (yup, I am that blown away by the cleanliness). I also love that it's a mix between a fast food place and sit down restaurant- what do I mean by this? They have waitresses come by to fill up your water and clear the plates. It's just a really nice experience. 
The food is also delicious. A club I'm an officer for decided to use Pasta Bene to cater and all the food was great.
I came here and ordered the chicken piccata--yum! I don't even like fettuccine and I ate the entire thing.

Almost forgot to add- they have happy hour everyday 3-7.

This restaurant has relatively cheap Italian food for good value.

For Cal Students, all you need to know is this:

Better than Gypsy's at the Asian Ghetto.

It's worth it to walk a few extra blocks down Telegraph to get some Italian cuisine that tastes great.

one of the best pasta places in the Berkeley Area. It is better than Gypsy's in my opinion. The prices are great for a student like me who doesn't have a lot of money to spare. I usually get the Gamberetto which is fettucine with shrimp, bell pepper, and mushroom in a tomato cream sauce. It is only $10!

I must say, this place is beautiful. Hidden among telegraph's crazy, wacky stores this place is beautiful within. Outdoor seating is pretty nice. The interior inside is elegant, contemporary, and beautiful. Not only does it have a great presentation, the facility is nice and clean. The customer service is quick, friendly, and genuine. 

      Did I mention that the price was inexpensive? Great price for what you get and totally worth it. The dining experience is wonderful. I ordered the Gnocci Sausage. It was made with creamy, tomato sauce, sliced sausages, and potato dumplings. The serving portion was fair and reasonable relative to the price. The potato dumplings could be a bit better, but that's only my own preference because I like usage of heavy butter- it was really light on this dish so not as flavorful that I thought, but great nevertheless. Definitely will revisit when I am tired of Gypsies.

On a visit to Berkeley, I stumbled across Pasta Bene on Telegraph and decided to give it a try.

They had a $5.95 lunch special going on with a selected menu of pastas, so I picked one from there: Melanzane.

The pasta came out surprisingly fast and I know why. The presentation of the dish was well done, but as soon as I bit into a mouthful of pasta, I could taste how undercooked it was. It seemed a couple minutes shy of being "al dente." The eggplant was not cooked well, but there was not enough sauce. The eggplant was extremely plain because it seemed as though they tried to make the sauce from the pasta season the eggplant completely--which failed. The inside of the eggplant was not even cooked evenly because parts of it was raw.

The only upside to this place was the service because the woman at the register was extremely friendly and welcoming. I would definitely come here to try another dish, I just wouldn't choose the Melanzane Pasta again.

Each time we eat here we are satisfied. The portions are good, considering the relatively decent prices for the food. The customer service is also very good. If you're looking for affordable Italian food, minus the fanfare and hoopla, this is your place.

I don't know if this is *quite* 5 star material, BUT, I really want to emphasize what a fantastic addition Pasta Bene is to Southside.

I studied abroad in Italy, and after 4 months of unspeakable quantities of pasta and pizza, I've found that I eat Italian food once every 4 or 5 months since coming back.  But Pasta Bene might just change that.

I won't name names, but the only other alternatives on Southside are a) just simply not that Italian, and b) overpriced for pretty low quality.  Pasta Bene treats Italian food as it ought to be: a cuisine that can be fresh, flavorful, and INEXPENSIVE.

I can't remember the exact price, but for instance, the bruschetta here is only a couple of bucks, and it is actually delicious.  The tomatoes have real flavor, and there is a wonderful balance of olive oil, tomatoes, and herbs.  Add it to whatever else you order!

I get the impression you can't order wrong here.  Go with your gut on whatever strikes your fancy, because everything I've had here is delicious and filling but not too heavy.  Awesome.

SUPER CHEAP ITALIAN FOOD.
(and the portions are pretty good too!)
How about that.

Before even walking in, I saw a sign that displayed a hearty Italian dish for a lunch special of only $5! That's right, a FIVE DOLLAR Italian plate. How often do you come across something like this?!

The place itself is very clean and not cramped, despite having a small interior, plus friendly staff. Sampled the crab cakes ($5.95) for appetizer - looks really dark on the exterior, but it's not bad once you take a bite out of it. Crispy, but not overdone. For the main course, ordered the Pasta Bene ($6.95), which was essentially spaghetti. The sourdough bread that came with it was amazingly soft! Usually, I prefer eating only the inside and removing the hard crust, but it was so soft and delicious that I ate it all! My friend ordered the Chicken Piccata, which had tons of capers. For all those who would be hesitant to order chicken dishes for fear that the chicken will be cooked dry, I totally understand, but this chicken was tender and juicy so have no fear ordering this dish! 

What's more?? The desserts are only $3!! CRAZY. The cheesecake isn't the best in the world, but for this price, not only does it taste decent, but it also looks pretty darn fancy.

Definitely worth coming back!

I feel like this is one of those places where, no matter what you order off the menu, it's gonna taste good. I look forward to eating here again =)

This restaurant is clean, open, and feels.. quaint. Like you're in a country kitchen.. a very big, open country kitchen X)

Gorgonzola Salad: usually walnut-apple salads with gorgonzola cheese are served with raspberry vinaigrette or some other vinaigrette, to provide a contrast to the richness of the pungent gorgonzola cheese. I think this is the way this salad should go - chuck the gorgonzola dressing for a sweet/tart vinaigrette, because there's just too much gorgonzola going on there. Now, I know it's a gorgonzola salad, but it was quite overwhelming. I kept having to ask for apples to freshen it up. X) Still, it was good. =)

Contadina Pizza: Mmm. Delicious. What great flavors, what fresh ingredients. This was great. 

I pity the UC Berkeley student who only goes to Gypsy's for Italian food because s/he is unaware that Pasta Bene is just a few blocks away (I was one of these people, so almost never ate Italian). Walk that extra little distance, and reward yourself with delicious, affordable, fresh, high-quality Italian fare.

Good Italian food for a great, student-friendly price.  All of the pasta entrees were under $10, except for the Salmon pesto fettucine. No wonder it was packed during dinnertime on a Sunday.

The lasagna was good. The garlic bread was pretty garlicky - they put a respectable amount of chopped up garlic on it.  I really enjoyed the Tortellini Primavera.

While the pasta here isn't top-notch, it's pretty tasty & a great value.  I'd rather pay $9 for "pretty decent" pasta at Pasta Bene than $16 elsewhere for pasta that's only slightly better.

One drawback: Because the line gets long during peak times, if you're sitting at the tables in the middle of the restaurant (where the line forms), it could feel pretty cramped.

Had an early dinner meeting here, and unsurprisingly at 5:30 on a weekday, the place was almost completely empty. I had heard a few good things about the place and had a hankering for some standard italian fare. The menu isn't too exciting, but it probably does have more options and dishes than any other italian spot near Cal campus. 

First the bad. I ordered the garlic bread and bruschetta, and considering how inexpensive they were, I wasn't expecting much ($1.50 and $2 respectively). The garlic bread was on foccacia, which would've been fine, except it was stale and under toasted. If they had just toasted it more, it might've masked the staleness, but then again, the quality of the foccacia wasn't great to start with. 5 finger length slices came with marinara dipping sauce. The bruschetta came with two toasted pieces of bread topped with just too much tomato. It seemed to over power. If they added some garlic and more basil, it would've balanced this better. Very limited beer on tap (i think they mentioned 3). 

On the plus side, the entrees, while not spectacular, were solid dishes, though on the heavy side. Portions are very good and the prices fit for a college student's budget. My friend ordered the Chicken Parmigiana and I had the Marco Pollo: fettuccini with prosciutto, green peas & mushroom in alfredo sauce. I actually liked my dish a lot and it was exactly what I wanted to satisfy my craving that day. My friend, though not a picky eater, said he liked his dish, and it came with a huge piece of chicken breast. 

Service was pretty good, but then again, we were the only table he had to worry about while we were there. 

2 apps and 2 entrees after tax and tip and we still managed to get out of there for $26. Too full for dessert, but enough value here to come back and try again.

What a nice surprise! After walking by this place nearly every day to and from campus, and being intrigued by the happy hour prices, we finally decided to stop in. I would advise against the appetizers; the bruschetta topping is quite good, but the bread is hard and oily. The garlic bread is similarly mediocre, though both prices are good. The pasta / entrees, however, are really good. I've stuck mostly to the Pasta Bene (no capers), but I've also tried the tortellini, ravioli, eggplant pasta, and some pizza. Everything is been good, though not oustanding. The tiramisu, at $3/plate, is a perfect way to end the meal. The service is consistently excellent, with constant water refills. Overall, a very good experience around campus, and probably the best "cheap" Italian food (miles above Gypsy's). I definitely recommend you try this place out!

Horrible service - the old woman got my order wrong, and then argued about how she knew what my order was (I hate capers!). When my real order came out 25 minutes later, the chicken and bread were burnt. Didn't even have time to eat it by that time. Would never come back if my dad didn't like the food here. Saw her another time (my dad wanted to eat there again) on the phone sitting down instead of taking orders. I almost thought I was on tv for worst service ever.

I live right next to this place, and it's definitely my go-to place for pasta.

My favorite is definitely the "Marco Pollo", its similar to "Godfather's Favorite" at Gypsy's.. except Gypsy's have chunks of chicken in it.

Another reason why I like this place so much is because I love the service here! I feel like I walked into an Italian friend's home and her mother is serving me delicious pasta! Very homely decor!

Setup: order at the cash register, and they deliver it to you. To-go options are available. 

The only reason that they are missing the last star is because it's definitely nothing toooo special, but still a great place for Italian Cuisine!

Mmmm really good pasta considering the price. The atmosphere is great for a casual dinner date if you're scraping for cash, want to impress and don't want to make a dent  in your wallet by going to a pasta restaurant on College Ave. I really recommend this place if you're looking for a change from Gypsy's too. 

If you're looking to cater, look no further because this restaurant has modern classy feel to your catering needs. Me and a fellow club member looked at this place as a catering option for one of our semi-formal club dinners. You'll be speaking directly to the manager on this matter and her service is above and beyond. She asked us to have a seat to discuss the options and offered us water. Even though we were still considering her restaurant to cater for us, she still sat down to help us get an accurate pricing and recommendations if we did get them to service us. Hands down an amazing woman. She gave us a discount. It was a moderate price we were looking for but I have to say it was well worth it. They even let us borrow their burners, catering utensils etc and we returned it of course.  
Our club members couldn't help but comment on the amazing pasta.

Pasta Bene is great in all aspects from the arched ceiling, the bountiful indoor/outdoor seating, low prices, and always coming through with affordable Italian food.

My recommendations include
- Beef Lasagna 6.95(5.95 during lunch special 11am-3pm)
- Eggplant Parmigiana 6.95
- Meatball Sandwich 6.95(ask for extra roasted bell pepper)

I've never liked Pasta Bene as much as my friends always have (most people do say it's better than Gypsy's, and that much I agree with - much less greasy) but I've grown to like the place. Nice clean interior, good location, great prices. 

As for the food, for the first 5 or so times I went here I was very displeased with my food. I've had the pasta bene, ravioli, and lasagna which were all subpar - wouldn't recommend any of the lunch specials or any marinara sauce dish, for that matter. I distinctly remember once that my lasagna tasted a bit like cleaning solution which grossed me out. 

Still, the more expensive dishes are solid, like the king salmon or chicken picatta. I also recall liking their tiramisu a lot. Obviously not the best pasta in Berkeley, but it's the best option for pasta near the UC campus.

I've always considered italian as super pricy for the tiny portions we get BUT this place has  
GREAT price and portions for italian! with 
SUPER friendly service!! and a 
COMFY seating area inside and outside! 
Nice and cozy ambiance which is nice for a date also!

Why haven't I find out about this place earlier?! I think I will for sure come back as a regular whenever I'm in the area to try their other dishes!

It is really hard to disappoint me when it comes to Italian food. Craving for pasta and tired of Gypsy's? Give this place a try!

Not only do they have reasonable prices, they also have big enough servings to fill you up. I usually get their pasta plates which range from 6 (lunch specials) to 11 (King Salmon), depending on the type of protein you want. I have been here many times and they never really have disappointed me. Is it really good/special that it stands out among all the other Italian food places I've been to? No. It is just regular food, good for college students.

I also have tried their calamari but it is a bit too rubbery for me. The breading falls apart when you pick a piece up. Not good.

Look for deals on Groupon or try takeout/delivery on LivingSocial and save a little bit more $$!

Last bit that I don't forget whenever I come here? Their tiramisu! Very, very reasonably priced and really light and awesome.

seriously, this place is fantasticcccccccccccc. 
ive never been here for the lunch special prices... blah!! but its good to  know that they have it...

ive tried a variety of pastas and a couple salads. and theyre all terrific!!!
i love their daily specials!! mmmm i remember that crab raviloi.. SO good. it was cooked to perfection!!!

and the service here is great! everyone is very nice and helpful. its the kind of place where u order at the register and then find a seat and they bring the order over to u. nothing fancy, perfect for a broke college student. lol. too bad i found this place AFTER i graduated.. not that i went to CAL anyways. but still i wouldnt have mind coming here on the weekends lol.

what else.. their appetizers are appetizing! i love the calamari!  and they dont skimp on the portions either. which i definitely appreciate.

and dessert... their tiramisu is the booommmmmmbbbbbbbbbbb. lol i have to order it when i come here... have to... lol. even if my bf tries to make me rethink it.. i order it anyways. hehehe.

plus they have some good ale on tap! happy hour from 3-7? good stuff!!!

all in all, i will definitely be back!! (i actually came here 3 days in a week one time with the bf. hehehe)

Pasta Bene, you are so much better than Gypsy's. Period. 

I can't believe I haven't found this place sooner. A couple post-doc friends and I decided to eat here since we just finished a long day at the lab. Hands down, this place is like a treasure in a cove. The restaurant is VERY clean, and the bathroom was a plus (hey, coming from a dude who's been in crappy bathrooms, having a nice place to wash up was something I def. needed make a comment). Ordering food is very simple: you get in line and order at the front desk, and they bring the food to you. This method, I believe, makes it very easy esp. for large crowds since you don't have to worry about splitting checks. 

For starters, I got the calamari. Crispy and you can tell they used fresh seafood since it didn't smell old. Goes great with ketchup and ranch. I got chicken piccata (which, as one of my Italian friends pointed out, isn't really an authentic Italian dish, so fail on my part). I didn't get to try the tiramisu!!! Next time, I'll be sure to try that. I heard it was pretty delicious.

Overall, the restaurant has great ambiance, great decor, and great people. Try this place out!

I think I just found my new favorite italian place around campus. Forget the crowded gypsy's or milanese cafe that's slightly overpriced. This place is perfect. Food is great and the portion is large. The price is very reasonable. I particularly like the atmosphere. It's very clean and classy. The staff is pretty friendly. 

We got the crab ravioli, which was the special of the day. It was pretty good and comes with extra bread. We also got the tiramisu. Highly recommend getting it! It's probably one of my favorite just because it wasn't too rich and the display was very pretty. 

Recommend coming here!
Very good food at reasonable prices. I definitely recommend the Chicken Marsala, it was excellent. Food quality was also substantially better then most places in Berkeley at this price level.

I used to go here often, not because of anything special about its pasta (I'd rather eat at Gypsy's, Milanese Caffee or Trattoria la Siciliana) but for its convenient location near my house and its cheap lunch specials.

I stopped eating here ever since my friend found a strand of hair in her pasta. yeahhh.. no thanks.

My friends and I were looking for a restaurant to meet up in and one of them suggested Pasta Bene. The pastas are really affordable and during the weekdays, they offer Lunch Specials for $5.95. We enjoyed their:

Pasta Bene: The dish was pretty good and for the price, it can't be beat! They gave a good amount of noodles and it also came with two pieces of bread.

Melanzane: Both of my friends ordered this dish and loved the vegetables and the flavor of the pasta. 

Overall, the food is about 3 stars but for the price, it deserves 4 stars. Where else can you get pasta with two pieces of bread for only $5.95! Also, the service was really good and they kept refilling our waters. There is also a really lovely seating area in the front in the patio area.

This place is so cheap and the food is ridiculously good. The lunchtime special is such good value, $5 for a big portion of delicious pasta and bread (which comes free with the dish). I've eaten there twice this week. 

I'd recommend the meatball pasta, really tasty. Also if you get it to take  away they give you little pots of the condiments including cheese. 

If you're 21+ a big plus is the fact they serve alcohol and between 4-7 (I think) its happy hour so the beer is $3.00.

The service is pretty excellent too. The guys in there are always friendly and they bring iced water to your table as soon as you sit down. 

Best pasta joint in berkeley.

I love Pasta Bene! It's definitely my favorite spot for Italian food in Berkeley. The restaurant is super cute! They have outside seating for sunny days and the inside is kept really clean. There are a lot of tables (including booth seats on one side :)), so I've never had to wait for a seat even when I come with large groups. The service is also really great! The restaurant is family-owned, and all the employees are super nice. If you come with a large group, they help you put tables together. The dishes are served quickly, and they're good at checking up on you. :)

Here are some of the dishes that I really like:

- Bruschetta: Two pieces of bread heaped with tomatoes! This is so yummy! And at under $3, such a steal.

- Gnocchi Sausage: My go-to dish! The dish consists of potato dumplings, sausage, and peas in a creamy tomato sauce. The dumplings are really soft and chewy, and the sauce is delicious. I love coming here for this since I found it hard to duplicate at home. I tried making gnocchi from scratch, and I couldn't get the soft texture that they serve here.

- King Salmon: The most expensive pasta on their menu, but definitely worth it. It's a seemingly simple dish of fettucini with pesto sauce and a piece of salmon on top, but larger portions.

- Chicken Pesto Ravioli: This was the daily special when I came. I can't describe the sauce, but it was superrrr good! I think it was butter-based but also creamy. The ravioli itself was okay though. I felt like the filling was a little dry and I didn't taste much pesto. 

- The bread!!!! Okay so this isn't on the menu, but they serve two pieces with all the pastas, and it's sooooo yummy! It's simple toasted bread with butter, but it's super soft  since it's thicker, and just the outside is crunchy. So yummmm

I think this would be a great restaurant to take your family! It's cleaner & fancier than most, not as crowded with students, and has great food. 
They also have a pasta lunch special from 11am-3pm, which runs at $6. But I feel like the selections are all really boring, so I usually pass on this. 
The daily special is usually really interesting; I think once they had a pasta with mussels (yummmm). However, these specials aren't any cheaper than the normal menu.

Very mediocre. I mean it's certainly not bad but for $10, I could boil some water and make some store made pasta that tastes the same for much less. Looking at the menu, there's really nothing that stands out - everything is pretty normal. 

If you haven't been here before, I'd recommend checking it out. Note: they are a bit slow putting food out from the kitchen

$5 lunch specials from 11-2pm!!! The pasta isn't even drenched in butter and oil like Gypsy's! And the decor is classy!! Also they have beer.  

Definitely coming back.

This place is no less than a 4/4.5 stars. Been here for dine in and togo, and I am definitely not the only one with good things to say. I've heard great things from 4-5 people already (most of them whom I did not dine with here).

Simple spot, clean, great decor. 

Cheap prices, quick & friendly service, delicious pasta.

Really, you cannot ask for more for the prices they offer here. Pastas are about $7-$10 for most, and they can definitely beat out some of the $17-$20 pasta dishes I've had elsewhere. 

Way to go Pasta Bene! I will be back!

This place smacked the hell out of me. I expected Pasta Bene to be typical Italian place, serving decent food but nothing to write home about, boy was I wrong! Bring your pen and paper because mom needs to hear about this place.

First and foremost you will notice how attentive and accommodating the staff is. Everyone was extremely courteous and helpful for a joint with counter service.

I ordered up a small margarita pizza, expecting a decent tasting, fill me up meal. Wow, I was wrong! When my pizza arrived my girlfriend and I could smell the fresh basil topping the 8" pie. The tomatoes were fresh and juicy, the mozzarella was fresh and plentiful. What a great pie!

I would definitely go back to Pasta Bene next time I'm in Berkeley. Great food at a great price!

While my friends love this place, I thought it was just all right - nothing amazing. I've had the beef lasagna and cheese ravioli on separate occasions, and both times they were kind of bland. The sauces weren't rich enough and the pasta tasted plain. I tried a bit of my friend's gnocchi and it wasn't bad, and the portion was relatively large (compared to my lasagna). 

The restaurant is conveniently located a few blocks away from campus, with lots of seating space so it's a good spot for bigger groups. I actually prefer Gypsy's to Pasta Bene, but probably because I like my sauces heavier and my portions larger. Pasta Pene definitely offers a better environment for dinner dates or group dinners, though!

the gnocchi is incredible, i get it every time!! but all of the pastas are delicious and such a great deal! you get a lot of food for the price. the people that work here are soooo nice and welcoming too! It is always my number one spot for Italian, especially on a college student budget.

happy hour is long and at convenient times with good beer only $12 pitchers

I came here with a group of friends on a Friday night. There were 20 of us but the restaurant was still quite accomodating. With about half of us in line to order, it took the sweet (albeit, slow) old lady almost 30 minutes to take everyone's order down. Then, it took the restaurant another 30-40 minutes to serve us our food. Granted, there were 20 of us. But, oddly enough, they decided to wait until everyone's dish was made before serving all of us. I understand the benefits of this type of service but with 20 hungry college students on a Friday night, it didn't bode too well with me. 

Nevertheless, our server was excellent and even though she was extremeley busy with the rest of the restaurant (as she was the only server of the night), she did manage to bring us our waters and untensils in a timely fashion. Props to her! Please do remember to tip, even though the service is somewhat self-serve. 

My friend and I split the Cantido (?) pizza and the sausage gnocchi. The pizza was made with fresh ingredients and even the small size was considerably large. The gnocchi was delicious, although I would've liked it a tad more soft. The sauce was not too salty and the sausages went really well with the pasta. I had a fleeting chance to grab a bite of the tiramisu, which was presented in a nice plate and served as a large portion considering the price ($3).

Overall, a great place to go with friends, but probably not for a large party like our's. I would definitely want to come back to try another pasta dish and get the tiramisu again. Currently, I believe they have Happy Hour drinks all day ($3.50/glass of house wine, etc.)

Portions here are large, the sauce is not too heavy, and the ambiance is perfect for all types of occasions -- from a casual one-on-one to a small, cozy banquet. Wait is usually not too long, though it could get packed around 6pm, and service is more personal than that at Gypsy's in Ghetto. I would say this place is fancy yet not over the top. 

Oh, end your meal with the Tiramisu! It's a delightful finishing touch, trust me =)

This place is a real gem. The food is fantastic and the people are wonderful here.

I've been a handful of times and every time it's been delicious. It's different every time I come but always in the best way.
