You know they're making everything from scratch and with just the right imperfections to make it  interesting. I always leave feeling great, satisfied and with leftovers for later even!

The prices are extremely affordable (especially the lunch prices!) and the appetizers are only a couple dollars each so you can get bruchetta or garlic bread (or both) every time and it's not like ordering a whole other dish.

I've only ordered vegetarian pasta dishes so far but I'm excited to try the pizzas, sandwiches and possibly even some of the amazing sounding meat and seafood choices hopefully very soon.

This place is a great go-to place for higher-end affordable pasta (compared to gypsy's!). Especially since the restaurant is very well-kept and clean, so it makes a nice place to sit & chat with friends.

My favorite is the Marco Pollo and the Calamari is also good for a beginning appetizer. 

I love the service of the place and I definitely think it is a step up from many of the restaurants here in Berkeley!

I stopped by on a rainy Saturday afternoon and was delighted by the friendly service. I ordered a melanzane to go and was offered a glass water as I waited by the counter. The nice waitress kept me updated on the progress of my food and I watched the cooks top off my pasta with some freshly grilled bread.

The pasta was delicious and had large chunks of eggplant. I enjoyed dipping the bread in the flavorful and bountiful sauce but the bread wasn't all that great by itself.

Will definitely revisit for the extremely reasonable prices, generous portions, and friendly service!

Pasta Bene just opened in Fall 2010 but it's had pretty good service for it's so far short-lived life! I think this place is actually better than Gypsy's. It has a cute atmosphere of a sit down restaurant that doesn't really have waiter service because you go up to the register and order separately.

They have a good menu selection that includes appetizers and desserts!! TIRAMISU. I love the stuff. I ordered the Chicken Parmesiana and Bruschetta and also tried the Eggplant appetizer. All three were good! The pasta and chicken were cooked well and the chicken wasn't dry...it was smothered with mozarella...so delicious. The Bruschetta is a personal favorite. Let me say, I don't even like tomatoes and I ate them all up! The bread has a good crunc and the flavors are so savory. 

They have this $5 deal if you go from 11-3 which is a crazy good deal.

Very decent experience. It was a blistering hot day. I walked in and the distinguished gentleman behind the counter was friendly and handed me a paper menu when he saw me squinting at the one high on the wall.

I ordered chicken marsala with linguini, di casa salad and an iced tea. There were plenty of clean tables and they brought over the tea and water right away. the salad followed and was quite good - fresh greens, good olives, good tomatoes slices and a nice dressing. The pasta arrived right after I finished the salad. The chicken was perfectly cooked, a good portion and still tender. It had lots of mushrooms and a pleasant wine flavor. The sauce had the shiny look of perhaps being thickened by cornstarch instead of a roux and was a bit bland. The pasta was good and the dish came with two small pieces of grilled foccacia. 

I would have like to see more vegetables on the menu and more things not in cream or marinara sauces. But all in all a very decent experience in a relaxing atmosphere.

A side note, the younger man who brought the food out paid extra attention to a very disabled man in a wheelchair. He attended to his needs kindly and effortlessly. 

Looking forward to a return visit.

Absolutely LOVED this place!  If you love pasta and wine, do yourself a favor and go here!

I went here with some friends and we were so shocked at how cheap the food was and the portions were big!  Everything was delicious! We also got a bottle of wine for only $20!  

They also have a special on certain days where the bottles are $10.

Good food, good wine, and yummy dessert! 

Great place if you want great food and don't want to spend alot!

Nom nom nom...

"Happy Hour" during lunch time is awesome! Six different dishes for only $5 each!

I ordered the Beef Lasagna and it was really good. Filled with beef, cheese and spinach, the order was quite filling. The pieces of bread that came with the order was really good with all that marinara sauce beside the piece of lasagna.

I finished lunch with a piece of tiramisu. Light, yet filling. The berry reduction goes well with the subtle coffee flavor in the cake. Awesome way to end a lunch!

I came here with three other friends for dinner one day when a restaurant across the street was closed. I got the "Penne Bolognese," which was pretty good. I'm not a fan of Italian food, but I'd be down to come here again if someone were to suggest it to me.

Pros:
- Large portions (similar to Gypsy's portions)
- Reasonable prices for the quality of the food you're getting
- Nice/clean interior and atmosphere
- Helpful staff

Cons:
- A bit further away from campus

I'd say that the lunch prices are the best, but this is a nice place to go to for dinners too. Bring your dates here! ;)

This is my new favorite pasta/Italian place in Berkeley, PERIOD.

I was honestly blown away by the pasta bene (a vegetable pasta dish with mushrooms, tender carrots, and capers!), which has this light but really flavorful tomato-based sauce. It comes with a couple pieces of soft garlic bread. Portions are generous; I eat a LOT but I still had enough leftovers for a good-sized lunch.

The staff is so lovely and courteous, the setting is clean and cute, and a quick glimpse behind the counter reveals a spacious, well-staffed professional kitchen.

I'm coming back. Will update on the truly beautiful looking tiramisu and cheesecake when I return...

(P.S. Better than Gypsy's? ABSOLUTELY)
$5 meals between 11am and 3pm!? Awesome!!!

Came here with fellow Yelper Tory L. and a couple of other friends. I've noticed this place before while walking down Telegraph but never really wanted to try it because most of it seemed like simple pasta dishes that any college student can make with some effort. However, this place gave me quite an insight into what I've been missing.

I ordered the Gnocchi Sausage, which consisted of gnocchi, sliced sausage, garlic, green peas and mushroom all in a tomato based sauce. The whole dish was wonderfully prepared. Nothing too raw like many other Italian restaurants, and every piece of the dish, even the mushrooms, were bursting with flavor. The sauce wasn't too tomatoey and had a nice creamy texture to it. The portions seem normal when you get the plate, but I left ridiculously full. 

The Tiramisu was also pretty good, and a great deal for only $3. The service, by the way, was great as well. We were waiting for a couple of people and the waiter, Gracie, was very courteous and let us take our time.

The selection here is pretty vast, although a good amount of the dishes were pretty basic. This place really made me realize how much I miss eating gnocchi. After spending a couple weeks in Italy, I can say Pasta Bene just might be better than most of the food I ate overseas. Bravo!

In Berkeley, Pasta Bene is definitely my go-to for delicious Italian food. Don't get me wrong- Gypsy's is great & all, but it's definitely not the same.

Pasta Bene always has large portions for reasonable prices (try the lunch & summer specials!), fast & efficient service, and a wonderful atmosphere.

And the icing on the cake? Their tiramisu is HEAVENLY.

Ah, I really hope Pasta Bene sticks around! I'm so excited to have a great, cheap, no-fuss Italian restaurant so close to my house. Everything about my experience at Pasta Bene last night was great. Our waitress was really sweet and attentive, the food and bill came very fast and the restaurant itself is clean and pleasant. This is such a good alternative to Gypsy's because I can go here and satisfy the same Italian food craving on the cheap without feeling disgusting afterward. I've tried the cheese ravioli and the greek salad, both of which are excellent.

Update: Pasta melanzane, pasta bene and cheesecake are all great  as well!

Tips:

Go during lunch time for $6 pasta dishes!

There's always a special of the day not on the menu, go to the front check-out to take a look.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Pasta Bene is delicious. They have good portions and great prices. I've had from the ravioli, chicken alfredo, tortellini primavera, crab cakes, to the King Salmon Alfredo dish. After trying all those dishes I was never disappointed. Their pasta is great I highly recommend anyone in the area to try it if they're craving some pasta.

The tortellini primavera ($7.95) is a nice light pasta with a creamy tomato sauce. It has LOADS of vegetables for those that want to go the healthy route. The chicken alfredo is VERY creamy, but so satisfying. Everyone loves some Alfredo once in a while. The King Salmon is the most expensive dish at $10.95, but it's not bad of a dish for those that love salmon. Personally I'd choose to go with the lesser expensive dishes.

The crab cake appetizers are great as well! Cooked very nicely and I had it for an entree once because I wasn't that hungry and it filled me up nicely.

The atmosphere and setting at Pasta Bene is really nice too! It's a great place for students to bring their parents if they don't want to bring them to places like Asian Ghetto or anything. I will continue to come to Pasta Bene to get my Italian fix!

Been here a couple times. I've tried the Chicken Marsala and Gnocchi Sausage...but before we dive into the goodness of food, let me mention this place is very spacious unlike many Berkeley restaurants. You will feel clean and comfortable dining here. Okay with that said...

Chicken Marsala - Excellent dish with a whole chicken breast and mushroom and fettuccini. The chicken isn't dry and goes well with the mushroom and wine sauce. 4 stars; would be 5 if the portion was just a tad bit bigger. 

Gnocchi Sausage - Potato dumplings with sausage in tomato creamy sauce. There were mushrooms which were delish! The potatoes got kinda tiring after awhile, but overall it was still good. Could have used more sausage. ~3ish stars for this dish.

Average that out to 3.5 stars. Service and environment makes this place bump up to 4.  I would definitely come back if I was craving Italian food!

Hands down, my favorite Italian restaurant in Berkeley. It's a sin for it to be so close to my apartment...I always want it!

Atmosphere: The place is nice and clean looking. It has a good number of seats and most of the time you order up front. I remember the first time I came here though they sat us down and took our order from there. I guess it depends on how busy it is.

Food: One thing to positively note about the food here is how fresh everything tastes. You know you're not eating a pasta with sauce straight out of a can. I've tried a number of things here, but I really enjoy the Chicken Marsala and the Spaghetti & Meatballs. The Chicken Marsala is wonderfully light and perfect for someone who doesn't like creamy pastas. The Spaghetti and Meatballs has the same light taste to it, and the tomato sauce is delicious, fresh, and not too heavy. The meatballs are also really tasty and full of herbed flavors. The portions are sizable and will get you full! Plus, now they have five dollar lunch specials on the plates that are usually around six dollars (spaghetti/meatball being one of them!).  

Their tiramisu is also pretty good, but I've had better.

Service: The service here is wonderful. The owner is friendly and always helpful.  Out of the many times I've gone, I've only had one instance where I had to wait relatively long for my food, but that was because a huge party was before us. If you want lunch, I'd suggest you call and place the order first then pick it up. It saves a lot of time.

Overall: This place is great and I'd highly recommend it.

1 of the very few remaining perks of my workplace (which will remain unnamed as they do monitor social media & do frown upon any denigrating remarks) is footing the bill for a free lunch after specific "years of service" milestones are reached. After a coworker surpassed 20 years with our employer, I was lucky enough to be an invitee to the ensuing lunch.

Pasta Bene was the chosen venue. With the entire front of the restaurant being windows facing the street & high ceilings inside, Pasta Bene is open, airy & bright. Decor is nice, clean & simple. Service was friendly, but, since we were a large group, a bit disorganized.

We ordered a few sets of Bruschetta, Calamari & Crab Cakes as appetizers for the whole group. I ordered Gnocchi Sausage for my entree & Tiramisu for dessert. The food was a little slow coming out, but really not bad at all considering the size of our party.

The Bruschetta was very good, but the Calamari & Crab Cakes were both just OK. The Calamari, which was fried light & crispy on the outside, was more chewy than tender on the inside. The Crab Cakes, while having decent flavor, had too much breading & too little crab.

My Gnocchi Sausage was a big heaping bowl of heavy heartiness. & with the potato dumplings & sausage acting like a variation of meat & potatoes, it was delicious in a soothing, comfort food way. The gnocchi itself was good, but not the greatest. A sentiment that was repeated with the Tiramisu.

For what we had, I would rate the food 3-ish stars. What gives Pasta Bene the bump to 4 stars for me is price:

Bruschetta - $2.95
Calamari - $6.95
Crab Cakes - $6.95
Gnocchi Sausage - $8.95
Tiramisu - $3.95

Though not exceptional, the food here was still better than the last Italian joint with 5 star prices I ate at in the City. Decent food in a nice looking restaurant for cheap? Hey, I'm a fan of that.

Pasta Bene is my favorite Italian Restaurant in Berkeley. It's cheap, clean, and... YUMMY! I think I go here once every 2 weeks? LOL I might be exaggerating BUT it is pretty close. I love Pasta Bene =)

My first time at Pasta Bene, I had Spaghetti w/ Meatballs. Honestly, I didn't really like it. Why? Well, my mom makes better spaghetti... However, I ended up going back to Pasta Bene after a week or so. I ordered Gnocchi (something different.... very unlike of me) && it was FREAKING GOOD!

After that... I ended up going to Pasta Bene to try other plates on the menu. I honestly think that I tried more than HALF of the plates on the menu... not embarrassed AT ALL!! LOL So... my recommendations (favorites): Pasta Bene, Gnocchi, & Carciofi. Try these!!

The appetizers are good too!! I only tried one... but yeah CALAMARI!! ^^ Oh, && don't you DARE leave without their dessert! OMG their cheesecake & TIRAMISU is LOVE!!!! Especially the Tiramisu! They are both ONLY 3 buckssss!

 I prefer this place rather than Gypsy's (the only other Italian places I tried in Berkeley).  PASTA BENE is zee shizzz!! WOOT WOOT

p.s: from around 11-3? = 5 dollar menu!!!

We came here right before Berkeley's graduation. My friends and I ordered three dishes and shared:

Melanzane - my favorite! I really like the eggplant! I RECOMMEND!!!!
Spaghetti Meatball - very good, meatballs were delicious!
Beef Lasagne - this was alright. Some parts of it tasted weird.

Each dish came with two pieces of bread. Since we came between 11AM-3PM for their pasta special, they were only $5 a dish! They were all freshly cooked & filling but not too heavy. 

5 stars for fast & friendly service, cleanliness, and for cheap eats!  If I ever come back to Berkeley, I'm definitely coming here again especially for their happy hour!

Actually sitting here right now so this review is fresh as it gets. Wooow.

Decor seems pretty minimal, clean, and fresh. They only have 3 beers on tap at the moment and their entree menu seems pretty standard for a cheap italian place. Digging the cleanliness and the small sidewalk eating area, although the surrounding area is a little unsightly.

Got the "tropical pizza" and it did an adequate job in defeating my hunger. The pizzas here are pretty thin (like reallllly thin) but surprisingly filling. So far I'm liking this place over Gypsy's and Milanese Cafe just down the street although since they just opened up like last weekend, I've yet to try most of the stuff on the menu.

3.5 stars, so they luck out by rounding. Rating subject to change upon further visits.

When you leave thinking, "I'm going to write a good review on Yelp about this place," you know it's legit! Pasta Bene's food is not only tastily satisfying, it's also extremely affordable! Many of their pasta dishes run under $10. The ravioli I ordered was around $7 and the portion was perfect! I loved how they didn't drown the ravioli in marinara sauce like the way Olive Garden does. Pasta Bene also knows how to make garlic bread the right way, and by "right" I mean good. Crunchy on the outside and soft in the inside with just the right amount of garlic and butter. Their garlic bread was mouthwateringly delicious, along with the marinara dipping sauce that accompanied it. I highly recommend ordering it! To top it off, the employees are very kind and welcoming!  

I look forward to my next visit.

So you are traveling to Berkeley and you stumble upon Pasta Bene. Congratulations, it might just be one of the most serendipitous food encounters you could have wished for.  Before you sit down and make yourself comfortable, take a look at the menu above the cashier window and place your order there first! 

There will be a variety of pizzas and pastas to choose from, all of which offered at a fantastic price. The lady who helped me spoke with a thick Italian accent, and she even corrected my pronunciation as I was having trouble uttering what I wanted. 

Looking around, the place is brightly lit and decorated with large posters on the wall, but I paid very little attention to any of that once my food appeared on the table. I had the Melanzane, and it was just DELIZIOSO! I might be a little biased as I am a fan of eggplants, but my friend who called the Chicken Marsala also liked my dish more than his own, so I think that's saying something. 

Whether you are vegetarian or not, I say go for the Melanzane if you are cool with eggplants! Even writing about it right now is making me salivate...

I am so glad that Pasta Bene is doing great business. I am a fan of their lunch specials which used to be only $5.00 but I think recently they increased their prices to $5.99 or something like that. I usually get the Penne Bolognese! It is one of my favorite dishes that is also apart of the lunch specials. It has a perfect blend of ground meat and thinly sliced mushrooms. The pasta is never soggy or over cooked; aldente! When I feel a little adventurous I get the Gamberto, which is a creamy tomato sauce with shrimp. You can not go wrong with seafood! (unless you are allergic :[ )

Appetizers I would recommend is the bruschetta. Delicioussss!!

So this is the third time i've come to pasta bene! it's so delicious, i just had to come back. This time I ordered the King Salmon. WOOOOOOOH! And that's why pasta bene gets bumped up one more star to a 5-star rating. Their King Salmon is nearly identical to the $27 salmon pesto I ordered at Trattoria La Siciliana. Guess what? The salmon at Pasta Bene is only $10.95! Soooo ridiculously good.

Conclusion:
- King Salmon -  Highly Recommended
    - creamy pesto sauce with fresh angel hair pasta topped with a perfect 
       grilled salmon fillet

Just went to Pasta Bene for the first time this past month and I have to say I was pretty satisfied with their food.

Here's the break down:

Food: Decent, not extraordinary or terrible but for the price Pasta Bene is worth a visit.

Service: Pretty bad, every time I have been there the restaurant has been packed and they only had 2 servers for the whole place. It took forever to order, get food, and get refills. 

Value: Worth it. Better than Gypsy's oily messes of cream and pasta and for roughly the same price.

This is considerably my favorite restaurant in Berkeley.  For college students, this is the place to go for lunch, dinners and large party events. Fast service, clean and bright environment. I much rather go here instead of Gypsy's in the Asian Ghetto- even with the extra walk from the dorms. 

I first came here for my birthday last year, as a surprise from my girlfriend, and I've been loving it since. Very friendly middle age couple owners with very good service. They even gave me a free Tiramisu cake on my birthday.  

Recently, they have a lunch special deal for 5$ for a few particular dishes. If you aren't feeling that, the other dishes are very affordable as well, without the lunch special.

I definitely recommend everyone to come here.

Want to know what got me to come here? ...that sandwich board right outside on the sidewalk that mentions their awesome deals, that's what!

Smart marketing tactic + awesome deal = you now have me as a repeat customer! For $5.95 during happy hour lunch time, you can get a variety of food and a great portion size at that! My husband and I walked by a bunch of times and saw the sign, then one day, we wanted to go out for lunch and remembered this spot.

Came in, were greeted by all staff members, and saw a lot of people happily consuming their Italian dishes. We both ordered two different pasta dishes and we sat down, one staff member brought our food out to use, nicely presented on a dish, and quite the size for that price. We were pleased. The pasta was delicious, had fresh vegetables, tasty sauce, and soft bread to dip into the sauces.

Their non-happy hour prices are just a dollar more but they are all less than $9-10 and are a great portion size that you may even have some left overs! Happy hour for appetizers and drinks starts at 3pm and those are some awesome specials as well. $10 for a pitcher of beer, yes please!

It's nice for a casual little date or if you just need to take some food to go. There is a small outside area out front to sit in as well as inside. It's clean, nice, and comfy inside...I would highly recommend this place if you want some tasty and affordable Italian food in Berkeley!

Wonderful service, cheap prices.  The food itself wasn't amazing.  I have had better, but not for a similar price.  Also, this is a college undergrad hangout, as in, it is loud.  Call me a old-fashioned, but I like restaurants that have an atmosphere that promotes eating leisurely.

Another Italian joint on Telegrah. Inevitably comparisons are going to be made to Gypsys. I really wanted to like this place given its nice decor, clean bathroom (by Berkeley standards) and friendly owners however I could not in good conscious give the place more then three stars. We ordered the garlic fries, King Salmon and the gambertto. The prices were reasonable and comparable to Gypsys. The garlic fries were unimpressive and uninspired (stick to the ones at Smart Alec's). As for the main courses my sister and I were in agreement that although the food was ok it was definitely not worth a trip back. I had the King Salmon which was decent. Pasta with pesto sauce and a hunk of salmon. The pesto sauce was good but the salmon good have used a little more flavoring and the garlic bread was well...not really garlic bread. It was just a regular hunk of bread which would have been acceptable if it was actually tasty and complemented the pasta well but it didn't. All in all a mediocre meal that did not hit the spot.

Bottom line: Gypsys (greater than) Pasta Benne 

Fun Fact: Yelp does not allow reviewers to use the greater then symbol in reviews.

One of my favorite pasta places in Berkeley (although I haven't tried Trattoria La Siciliana, a more classy Italian restaurant). 

I love Pasta Bene because of the atmosphere and it's cleanliness. And the pastas aren't greasy or too heavy at all! I HATE Gypsy's because it's so greasy and it makes me feel like I'm going to die of a heart attack, but Pasta Bene really prepares delicious Italian dishes that will leave you feeling less guilty.

I've tried Carciofi e Pollo and Pasta Bene, and both are delicious choices. The calamari is good and the tiramisu is sooo yummy (must try!). But back to the pasta--Carciofi e Pollo is interesting because there's no traditional pasta sauce (kind of feels like olive oil mixed with other ingredients). It isn't heavy at all, and if you love mushrooms + chicken, you'll love this.

I thought I'd get the pasta bene because you know, it's the name of the restaurant. This was a more traditional, marinara pasta. It was pretty good, but it definitely isn't my favorite.

Next time, I want to try to gnocchi sausage.

BUT BOTTOM LINE: affordable and tasty Italian food at a clean restaurant with a lovely atmosphere.

try it!

Some places close up when the UC students are at home during the holidays.  Business is slow especially around campus on the north-side (Euclid) and on Shattuck, Telegraph and College.  But that's a great time for non-student Berkeley residents and out-of-towners to enjoy some cheap but good food at some of the local student hang outs, diners, dives and eateries without having to stand in line and fight the crowds.

I'm a former UC student but I still like to check it out.  We did that at Pasta Bene and were happy we did.  Everything was frest and delish.  We started with bruchetta and calamari for appetizers, then had some salads, pasta and pizza dishes, wine and dessert too, when it was all done and our party of ten including momma had a really tasty and filling family dinner.  We did this for just about $20 bucks per person with no discounts or happy hour specials.  What a deal!  

The owners were there and they and their staff provided great service.  Even though, PB is a walk-up, place your order and pay place, they provided us table service since it was so quiet and since we were having a single check dinner for the ten of us.  I'm not sure they would do this regularly since they aren't staffed to service tables, they did it anyway.  That's great service from owners and staff who care.

I was going to give PB four stars but when writing this review, it occurred to me that for the niche of home cooked family style italian dining (nothing fancy but just simple, fresh and delish) plus great service, they deserve five stars.  Yeah.

HI JENNIFER W.

So the above took us to Pasta Bene one fine Friday afternoon/evening (we couldn't decide which it was....it was 5:15pm). Distraught over Bear's Lair line, we headed to somewhere close and comforting. We were all feeling like pasta, and Pasta Bene was new and worth trying.

EVEN THOUGH I was in a pasta mood, I was convinced that pizza would be better. It was a good decision. The pastas looked too creamy (and supposedly they are even creamier than Caffe Milanese...bleh), so it was probably a fortuitous decision. Andrew and I split up garlic fries and a Tropical themed Large pizza. 

Fries were not garlic-y, but fried well. Worth the $3 I suppose...but other places do them much better.

Pizza was pretty OK/average. It's thin crusted pizza on a no-frills white flour dough. For toppings: red onion, ham, cheese, tomato sauce, and pineapples (NOW that's tropical ;) ...). It was probably the best choice from their pizza selection, and it was good. It was definitely no Cheeseboard, but what do you expect? I would order it again if I'm ever in the neighborhood. 

For Beer they offer 3 selections on tap...Red Tail...Sierra Nevada...and one more. They charged us $13 for the pitcher, but are offering $10 pitchers starting this week (boo, we missed out). 

Def sink your teeth into this place. I can tell it'll be great competition with Caffe Milanese. Since I dislike Milanese, this place will be my default "I feel like pizza but am too lazy to make it and it's cheap enough so whatev" locale. 

PLUS, service rocks your socks. Sure we were one of 3 parties in the place on a simple Friday evening, but the servers were fantastic. Loved it. I'll def try the $3 Tiramisu next time.
$5 lunch specials! $10 pitchers this week! spread the word!

This is my weekly go-to restaurant for brunch during the weekends. I usually order the house special which comes with your choice of eggs, potatoes, and 4 sexy triangles of toast. To add a healthy dash of protein, I always add the chicken apple sausage for some extra bling. The portion size is huge and my stomach always leaves feeling satisfied. Taste good. I have also tried the breakfast burritos before. Taste pretty good too.

Not a bad cafe. My biggest complaint is that the drinks only come in ONE size (large) which is nice if you like a good amount, but I cannot handle that much liquid and it makes for a rather expensive beverage. I got a chai latte when i was here and it was pretty disappointing. It was watery and could have come from a poorly seeped tea bag. 

It is, however, at an extremely convenient location. The natural lighting is fantastic, and it makes the entire cafe super bright and cheerful. Their pesto chicken panini is AMAZING. it was perfect-- crisp on the outside, tons of melty cheese and pesto on the inside along with a nicely flavored chicken. A tad bit pricey, but definitely worth it.

The newly opened Northside Cafe is the perfect addition to Euclid Ave eateries! The high ceilings, skylights, and large windows give this place plenty of natural light and a welcoming, airy ambiance. Everything from the floors to the kitchen has been renovated, making this a beautiful place to have breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

Located directly across the street from the north gate of the UC Berkeley campus, Northside Cafe couldn't be a more convenient lunch hour restaurant. The owners and staff are very friendly, and the food preparation is fast, VERY convenient! 

Their food is excellent, using the best ingredients. I recommend their turkey cranberry sandwich. The turkey is carved, not sliced coldcuts, which is a huge plus! I have it with the lentil salad, but orzo salad is also a delicious companion. 

The breakfast menu also looks delicious. I can't wait to go back and try everything they have. Give this place a try, and you'll become a regular customer!

I've been coming here for breakfast all semester and this place is delish (especially given it's proximity to campus). I've tried their breakfast scrambles and their panini's and they are just to die for. Something about Northside Cafe and the food they serve is fresh, simple, and simply irresistible.

For breakfast, this place is relatively good. And between classes, the place gets crowded quick. There are a couple of tables, but I definitely would expect more given the space they have. Additionally, the name is kinda confusing. It's not so much a cafe as their main specialty isn't drinks. Likewise, there is no internet and the connection you do get to Airbears is unacceptable!

However, a quick bite and breakfast here is a must. Northside is great if you only have a short hour for lunch1

This place is very convenient and close to my work -- I only have 30 minutes for lunch, and they are super fast!

The only food I've tried so far is the Turkey Cranberry Sandwich. It sounded delicious from the description, but... maybe I'm just a picky eater. It's really natural turkey (as in from an actual roasted turkey) so those who like Thanksgiving will really enjoy. However, I'm really picky about my meat (it has to be in a circle and not look like anything or have a weird texture)... so not the sandwich for me! It was also a little on the greasy side... I felt a bit ill after eating it, but then that might have been my own psychosis. The ingredients were all fresh and the portion was hefty. The side salad was also nice. (I'm always happy to get a side salad without raw onions!)

I'm going back to try the tomato and mozzarella salad today -- I think I just chose the wrong menu item. So: for my fellow meat-hesitant picky eaters out there... stay away from the turkey items unless you want the real deal.

They have pretty decent food and coffee here. I usually try to order a panini, or if it's still early, I'll try something like their egg plate. But food is really pricy here...7 bucks for a sandwich...? You're better off using that money for something else that isn't breakfast food. Great decor and friendly staff. Make sure to double check your order because they almost forgot a side of bacon when I came in for breakfast...
I ordered the fruit and walnut salad and was absolutely disappointed. My salad was drenched in dressing in an unappetizing way. I am on the search again for a great salad around Berkeley :(

My friends and I Yelped for a quickie breakfast spot this morning and came here because the reviews were high and it was cheap. Would I come back here? Yes, but probably only in the morning on weekends when no one is at school or awake yet.

It was clean, there was parking (granted in was 9:10 AM), food was presented well and came out rather quickly. I also like that the kitchen is open so if you wanted to you could watch them cook your meal. 

I had the Eggs Benedict with the breakfast potatoes for around $7. The potatoes were yummy and I would return just to get a side of those. The cup of coffee was huge I was too full from the food to finish it. 

Cute place.
Came here for lunch ... Chicken Florentine Panini. It was tasty though the chicken was tough. I'll be back to try some of their other dishes. Plenty of seating at 11am.
Nice place near campus.  Food is yummy and it can be packed during peak lunch hours.   Get in line, decide what you want (to help move things along), stake out a table and enjoy!

Had a Vegetarian Sandwich (~$7): warm (with sautéed mushrooms, grilled eggplant, roasted bell peppers, avocado, red onion, spinach, tomato, fresh basil, sun dried tomato, Swiss cheese, honey dijon mustard, & mayo) on fresh baked bread with orzo on the side. Food was tasty, staff was nice (they made sure I got the right order after I was mistakenly handed the wrong one), and the ambiance was unique for The North Side (i.e. a little more spacious than most spots).

NOTE: The cold case has a pretty wide selection of drinks... but no regular V8.

The crew at Northside are such a pleasure to work with, and the best at helping with catering details!  The food is excellent, and they will make just about whatever you request! I have relied on them for catering some of my largest events (over 300 ppl) as well as just dropping by for lunch myself, and never had any problems.

I tried the breakfast after recommended by another yelper and got it with bacon. However, the bacon gets soggy and stringy in the burrito and texturally tastes gross.
The salsa in the burrito Pace, which the opposite of fresh salsa and I dont want to pay $5 for commercial salsa. I urge Northside to switch to a homemade salsa. The tortilla was also lacking. 

But the redeeming fact is that the potatoes are very well seasoned and I would recommend getting a basic breakfast plate with potatoes.

The most disappointing thing was that a breakfast joint didnt have fresh OJ. It has the nicest natural lighting of all the northside cafes.
For the price, 7$, I got the chicken florentine sandwich which was definitely worth it. Food was tasty and seemingly healthy. Place is new and clean also.

OK, I admit I'm a breakfast burrito snob, having spent 10 years living in L.A.  It's tough to match the quality and variety of Mexican food down there.  Northside gives it the old college try (haha).  My breakfast burrito with bacon was pretty good, nice and big, filling, but a little bland.  Put some hot sauce on it to give it some kick.  The cappuccino, like the burrito, was good but not spectacular.

The best things about this place are the location and atmosphere.  Right on the corner of Hearst and Euclid, it couldn't be any more convenient if you're headed to or from Northside Berkeley.  Lots of sunlight, good people watching, etc. on the corner.  People camped out working on laptops or chatting with friends.  Music cranked up, which was pretty good except when fu****** Chris Brown came on, or when the radio station turned to blaring local ads.  (Ever hear of commercial-free satellite radio or playlists, people?)  Girl behind the counter was about as friendly and cheerful as you could expect.  Overall, a solid choice for breakfast or lunch.  I'd hit Brewed Awakening around the corner for a long, caffeine-fueled study or work session, though.

Not a big fan of their coffees. I had their chai latte one it tastes very strange to me .. and then I tried their mocha but it lacks that "punch" for me .... HOWEVER, I really enjoyed their breakfast menu there :)

Sandwiches/salads/paninis.  Baked potatos.

This place is so redundant of the other businesses on Euclid.  I had an OK veggie panini served with an orzo salad.  Nothing great about it and it took awhile for them to make it.  Perhaps the employees hadn't really gotten into their groove yet.  I'm concerned that they only have one register.  No big deal for summertime, but there's no way that's not going to be a problem in the fall.

Yes, it was clean and big but it doesn't have any charm.  I see no reason (price/taste/location) to come here over Hummingbird or Stuffed Inn.

I love this place.  Been going there since they opened.  I get the #2 baked potato, it comes with bacon, cheese, sour cream and chives.  It is to die for.  Each time I get the potato, it is better than the last time.  I highly recommend this place.  Yum Yum
Amazing Breakfast Wraps! My favorite thing to get when I'm working on Saturdays. Convenient location too, right across my store!!

The two times I've tried eggs benedict here, I was impressed. It's one of those dishes that's complicated, but if done right is a pleasant treat. The eggs were perfectly poached, and the Hollandaise wonderfully accented with some diced chives on top--a welcome sight for someone who loves chives as much as I do!

I drop by to grab a sandwich for lunch quite often. My favorite is the veggie press, and the only thing I can complain about is I wish they'd stick it under the press a little longer to make the bread crispier. I've tried some of their other sandwiches and have been equally pleased. The potatoes I've seen people order look like a potato-lover's dream: huge baked potatoes dolloped with all the fixings (sour cream, cheese, chives, bacon) and more one could ever hope for. I haven't ordered one myself, but, hot damn, they look good!

They seem to move pretty fast no matter how busy or slow business is. I also enjoy their mango iced tea. It's the best iced tea I've found in the neighborhood of Euclid/Ridge. 

I'm definitely coming back, and one day I'll try one of those potatoes that looks like a boatload of yumminess!

Northside Cafe is such a cute little place! I ordered the tomato & mozzarella salad. The vegetables were all very fresh and the balsamic vinaigrette was just the right amount of sour and herby-tasting. It came with two slices of focaccia bread as well. $5.99 was a reasonable price to pay for all this yumminess. I will definitely be coming here again. 

Also, I love that there are windows everywhere. I hate it when cafes are dim and stuffy.

Came on a weekday afternoon, got a Chicken Florentine panini. Very good, but small in portion, so not as satisfying as it could have been. Their coffee is kind of pricey. I got a chai latte, which was a whopping $3.75, unheard of for chai, but it was served at such a perfect temperature (~80 deg C), in such a delightfully large round cup and saucer, and it was indeed, perfectly foamed at the top. That chai made up for the panini and more! Ahh... I will probably go back someday just for the chai. You get what you pay for. The cafe itself wasn't that relaxing, the atmosphere wasn't right, and the decor seemed bland and tasteless, like an office. I mean, it was clean and sparkly, but it lacked a certain... culture. I felt like I was sitting at a display in Ikea. Overall, a nice place to get coffee, but not really to stay too long at.

Come here really often for coffee and breakfast. This is one of my favorite places for breakfast and it's actually affordable! The portions are always enough (or even more than enough) for me and the employees are all fantastic. Good place to stop at if you're running between classes. Can get really busy though during lunch time.

Got out of class and had to hang around Northside 'cause I had another class there later. And on top of that I was hungry. So I walked to Hearst and saw the Northside Cafe across the street. Convenience!

I had whatever their salad with meat on it is called, as I like salads with meat on them -- screw carbs, man -- and it was excellent for the price. It was pretty busy because I came in during what I assume is their lunch rush but my meal came out really quickly. I actually think the dude called my number twice and I just missed it the first time.

Will go back regularly because I have classes on Northside and enjoy meat on my salads.

Love this place for lunch on the weekdays! I usually grab a soup and call it a meal because the soup portion is pretty generous and filling. My favorite is definitely their chili, the beef is tender and the soup is tasty! 

Everything is reasonably priced with pretty good portions. Tons of selection from sandwiches to baked potatoes. Definitely a place to visit if you need a quick bite to eat around campus!

well, what do you do when your year old pancake mix fails you, and your guests are not so impressed...you offer to take them out to brunch.  I've only done Saturday breakfast here, but it was perfectly satisfactory for the price.  Kind of reminds me of the Jersey diners I used to get when I lived there.  Cheap, greasy, and tasty.  Actually the eggs were some of the best over-easy eggs I've ever had.  I just wish they would serve something other than the uber-cheap high-fructose "grape" jelly.

I look forward to trying their lunch options.  It's really nice to see this stretch of Euclid getting revitalized with some new options.

This is the cutest little cafe, and it has awesome food at an equally awesome price.  It's an absolutely beautiful place to sit and have a nice cafe lunch, or perhaps study.

The food here is really good too!  The hot vegetable panini is outrageously delicious.  The baked potatoes aren't something I've seen anywhere else, and they're fun and cheap.  Definitely going to be coming back here frequently.  The only thing I can't attest to is the coffee -- some other people aren't liking it, it seems like.  I haven't tried it here, but this is more of a sit-and-stay kind of cafe then a get-your-coffee-on-the-run kinda place to me anyway, soooo... shrug.

It's great to have a breakfast place on the Northside now.  I had a scramble and it was decent.  The place had just opened, so they hadn't gotten into the swing of cooking yet.  I think the identity of the place feels a bit unsure.  I for one think it should have went full on breakfast and lunch diner, instead of the sparse almost convenience store-cafe ambiance it currently has.

We did breakfast here and we were very pleased with it! The "scrambles" are among the best I have had, and the big windows and high ceilings make it a cheery place to have a morning meal and gaze at passers-by. Also: no table service and easy on the wallet.

This place is good for a quick lunch by campus. The place gets super crowded during lunch hour but getting food to-go is always relatively quick. Their hot sandwiches are particularly good (my fave is the turkey cranberry), but sometimes I stop by for a salad or a baked potato as well.

The coffee isn't spectacular but it's not horrible on-campus quality either. Sometimes when it's busy the quality dips though - I've had the orzo salad that comes with the hot sandwiches forgotten in my to-go bag, and once I found a piece of cut off rubber glove finger wedged in my sandwich - that put me off my lunch and this place for a few months. But how much more do you expect from the nearest place to north gate?

Technically this place is now my 2nd closest lunchtime venue... so of course we had to try on the opening day!
It was a typical Euclid street cafe lunchtime crowd, but the staff were fast, friendly and efficient. It took them about 15 minutes to get through the 23 orders ahead of mine. 
I ordered a chicken pesto style ciabatta sandwich - it was a generous serving of chicken for a sandwich and the pesto was just right. It came with a small side serve of lentils in the takeout tray. 
The nice thing about this place is the location and the space. Large windows with a high ceiling and lots of table space for groups of up to 4 people.

I came here because of the campuscred deal.

Got a steak and mushroom panini and a side salad...Salad had way too little dressing and was quite literally a bed of leaves with a couple tomatoes and olives. Definitely not worth $2.50. Panini and the orzo salad side were pretty good, but probably not worth $6.50plustax given the size.

Everything was fresh and the panini was nicely warm, but I don't think I'll be returning.

My boyfriend and I came here for a quick lunch to go. I got the famous Turkey Cranberry sandwich - it was delicioussss but I wish they gave bigger portions for the price! I guess I am too used to Haas Cafe portions...

However, the sandwich itself was a great combination of salty and sweet. The cranberry jam tended to ooze out while I bit into the sandwich, making eating it just a bit messy. 

The side pasta-salad-thing was disappointing...I think it got way too hyped up on Yelp so I ate it with high expectations, haha. It just seemed like a normal pasta (wait, is it even pasta?! mystery grains) salad with sun dried tomatos and olives.

Wandered into this place with ABSOLUTELY no expectations and it was wonderful! A great place to grab a quick cup of coffee and a delicious sandwich (I tried the chicken pesto panini with accompanying salad and it made me SO happy yum). My friend tried the mango tea here and highly recommended it. I love how this place is clean and not as crowded as some other Berkeley cafes, thanks to its location. Going back here soon for sure!

Best (and only) place for breakfast on northside.  The breakfast wrap is  huge and a good value, but the croissant breakfast sammie is incredible.A giant fresh croissant with eggs bacon and cheese, I know it sounds simple, but man is it good!

I find this place to be lacking in personality (atmosphere-wise) compared to other places on Northside, although the service is friendly and prompt. I have had good luck with the brunch food being pretty tasty, and bad luck with the salads being wilted. I really wanted to love those salads.

I've been living on Northside for over six months now, and today was the first time I tried this place (I know, who am I?) I wish I had known about it earlier!

Their breakfast wrap (or breakfast burrito) was delicious, cheap, and a great value for the money. It's only $4 for the basic with eggs, potatoes, cheese and salsa, and I paid the $1 to add bacon. I was starving and still only managed to eat half of it, so if you came here to split this is definitely a viable option. My roommate got the house special breakfast plate, and said their sausage was really tasty too.

Can't speak to the lunch side of things, but I will definitely be back for breakfast!

This place is the best place to eat breakfast on northside. Their post breakfast menu and hot beverages are great as well .
I would especially recommend the baked potatoes along with Bacon and melted cheese, it is delicious and really fills up your appetite as well. 
Their breakfast burritos and breakfast lunch plates are well fine and the bacon is always crunchy. 
The only downside is that this place closes quite early and is not the place for you if you like to sip a nice hot cup of coffee throughout the evening. It is also a bit pricey , though it is well worth it.

You can't go wrong at this café, unless you need wifi.  The coffee is good and so are the sandwiches.  The veggie panini is my favorite.  Everything tastes fresh, the service is fast and friendly, the owner is attentive and remembers his customers.  This café also has a nice, quiet ambiance and plenty of space for studying.

Nice little addition on the Northside of campus. The food is nothing too crazy, but it is definitely good. My boyfriend and I shared the breakfast wrap with eggs, ham, potatoes, and cheese and were decently content. For about 5 dollars (ham was an extra dollar) I think it is a good deal. I have also had the fruit and walnut salad which is delicious. The fruits and veggies are fresh and the combination of subtle pear and tart blue cheese worked well together in my opinion. They give you a good amount of food so you'll definitely leave content.

The place itself is clean and relatively quiet. It can get busy during the lunch hour on weekdays, but nothing to worry about in comparison to the line at Urbann Turbann. The mornings are quiet and seating has never been a problem for me.

The variety of choices on the menu and the good food at a decent price will have me back here on multiple occasions.

Simply delish. A fresh and inviting place, and a little homey environment. What wins me over is the perfect pairing of a good breakfast to great coffee. The food was awesome and cooked very well, quick make and great pricing. Seating is nice, with windows walled all around.. only thing I would've changed maybe is a switch up from the ambient techno music lol.. some of the same beats over 10 min spans drove me a lil' nuts for such an early morning, but just my personal taste... 

Overall, nice spot for the morning. This is certainly a new favorite breakfast place.

I tried their Fruit&Walnut Salad ($6.25), and I loved it! Lots of greens, pears, strawberries, candied walnuts, and dried cranberries. The raspberry vinaigrette was just right. Very good portion considering the price, too! While I was waiting for my order, I saw a lot of people getting the same thing, so I'm guessing it's one of the best menus there. I bought the salad to go and had it with steak, and it was great. I just wish it was closer to my home so that I can visit more often.

I love their paninis and the house salads that come on the side. The orzo one is still my favorite but the lentil mix wasn't bad either!  
Also, their baked potatoes are frigging HUGE. I mean it when I say huge. Go try them!

i love sandwiches, i eat them regularly. so when i got a salami sandwich at this place i was disappointed to find about six slices of thin salami - barely visible! the fear sandwich lovers have when they order out...will the bread be meek and sad? mushy tomatoes? brown avocado? hardly any meat???

other than that it was good. everything was fresh. and i got a great baked potato. i am always on the north side of campus so hope to get a thicker sandwich next time i go...gotta say i'm not a big meat eater, but when i eat it i wanna taste it!

We stop by for breakfast at least once a week on our way into work. It never fails, the food is always super yummy and fresh. The breakfast wrap and the campus scramble are my top faves! The prices are reasonable and the service is fast...not much more you can ask for.

I really like this place for a little corner street restaurant. It's nothing super fancy, but it's also not fast food.  It's just like the name says, a simple, clean and fresh cafe. The food has always been fresh for me and very tasty.  When the cafe first opened, the wait times for food were a little long. However, now it's about as quick as you can expect for things not being put together/made until you order- which I think is a good thing.

The prices are very reasonable, with everything on the menu being less than $7.  For a hot panini with a side salad or breakfast that you'll be full from, I think this is great.  Their loaded pototoes are a neat alternative to other items you typically see in other cafes or restaurants.

The only "drawbacks", if you can call them that, are you have to get your own cutlery when you start, but this must be part of the reason why their prices can be so low, since they don't have that much extra staff.  On that note, the cashier/server can seem a little dragged out/not as cheery as other places. This is not the case the majority of the time.  99% of the time, the staff is great!  But, on 2 or 3 occasions, the cashier seemed to be a little off put that we only gave a $2 tip.  I don't feel a big tip is necessary when I'm the one setting the table and getting up to get my food.  

All in all though, the Northside Cafe is a great addition to the restaurants at the north gate and a great value. I will continue to go here and constantly recommend it to others.
So I have recently fell in love with their Chili Bake Potatoes. They are of very healthy portion (big) - and will definitely fill you up.

I got a freakin' ENORMOUS loaded baked potato here for less than $6.  This is definitely a cheap, tasty meal I can share with my guy.  I'm not going to try to pretend that the tons of cheese, bacon, and sour cream were good for me.  

No wi-fi, so it's not that kind of cafe, but I'll definitely be back after walking down from a morning at the rose garden.
They have plenty of good stuff, hot sandwiches, deli sandwiches, salads...  It has become one of my favorite places to eat around Euclid.  Highly recommend this corner place!

I was about to get in line at Stuffed-In but then I decided to stroll back down the street and check out all the new places that opened on the corner of Hearst and Euclid (3 right next door to each other!?). 

Northside Cafe didn't have a menu on the door, so I walked in and then felt I should order something since I was already standing there in front of the register, and well, the menu looked good. A bit pricey for being right off campus, but it is north gate and cheaper than Nefali. I also wasnt sure what to expect when I ordered the Fruit and Walnut Salad. They had a large selection of cold beverages which is nice.. mmm passion fruit Juice Squeeze. 

When I got my huge salad I thought  for sure I'd be taking some of my salad to go, but it was really good with tangy raspberry dressing, pears and cranberries. I definitely finished the whole thing.

Solid lunch spot that will enjoy dominance on Euclid because the other places ain't got nothing on Northside Cafe.  Fresh, well- priced, yummy food and friendly service.  I love the layout too because I can get my Berkeley people watching on while I wait for my food or grub down.   My particular favorites are baked potatoes, chicken caesar wrap, and the BLT.  You know a place deserves 5 stars when at 10am your tummy begins growling and your salivating thinking about running up here at lunch and grubbing down.

I came in for breakfast on Sunday because it's served all day long on the weekends and I was quite impressed. 

Food: 
1) Pancake platter: pancakes came with eggs (cooked any way you liked). I ordered scrambled eggs and it was as good as scrambled eggs can get. The pancakes were nice and fluffy with golden brown edges that was nice and crispy. YUMMY!  
2) French Toast platter: The french toast looked better than it tasted but it was still some solid french toast! It came with eggs (any style) and some potatoes. The potatoes were really good (this is coming from someone that is not a big fan of potatoes, so that's saying something!). They were cut in cubes that weren't too big or small. Crispy on the outside and nice and soft on the inside. The skin made it extra texture-y. YUM!

Service: 
You bus yourself, so no service. 

Ambiance: 
This cafe is one of the many string of new restaurants that were newly established on the Euclid. All the furnishings and decor were really new and clean. There is a ton of window seating so you can just kick back, enjoy a cup of coffee and people watch a little. 

Price: 
Everything was under $10, so not bad :) 

Overall: Great food (for being so close to campus), good prices, and clean! What more can you ask for?

I go here only for breakfast - haven't been here for lunch but I'm a frequent visitor (at least once/week) for breakfast and coffee
coffee is good and reasonably priced (especially for student budget), location is super convenient (at the corner of northgate)
food is good, fresh and not greasy ! - very important
Interior is clean and nice - not ghetto like some of the south side places
portions are generous
I really don't have anything to complain about this place. Please don't raise the prices, or drop in food quality - just keep what you are doing !
It's more cafe styled, so it might not be a fancy place where you can go to dine in, sit down, and relax, but that's what they are - cafe for students to grab quick bites to/from classes

This is a overpriced pathetic place with poor service.

I waited 10 mins just to get an egg and cheese, which itself was OK, but had to see it getting made, and then just sit there on the kitchen counter for 10 mins when the cook was doing all other random things. This was a non rush hour weekday. The earlier little coffee shop here, which was demolished to build this huge structure, was better!!

(I changed it to 4stars after receiving prompt attention by the owner thru email on my review!!)

This is my go-to spot between classes. 
Their french toast breakfast is so affordable its ridiculous. I have only had their french toast breakfast, their caesar salad and their minestrone soup and I have enjoyed them all. I will expand and buy something else at some point but their caesar salad is just so good! I crave that salad almost every other day.

I have class in Etcheverry half an hour after my class in Haas so I don't have time to get food on southside. I usually just get Top Dog or starve. After living in Berkeley for two years, I am sick of Top Dog, but I don't like starving either. So today on my way to class I'm thinking "ugh Top Dog it is" but for some reason I decided to look to the left as I crossed the street and noticed this place. I see on the window "baked potatoes" and I was like ouu because I've been wanting a baked potato for a while, so I decided to try this place.

They had a lot of selections. I chose a baked potato with mushrooms, broccoli, and provolone. As I was waiting for my baked potato, I was watching the kitchen and noticed that all the food they used looked nice and fresh. My potato was big (though I was still hungry after eating it) and it was pretty good. I liked the mushrooms and provolone, but the broccoli wasn't all that great. The ratio of salt and butter could have been better. There was too much salt and not enough butter. The potato itself was okay, but overall I was pleased with this place because 1. of the location and 2. they had baked potatoes. I will be getting food here now when I go to class in Etcheverry.

This is where you come when you're in need of a cup of coffee and a good sandwich. 
I personally really like it because it's super clean and new unlike the surrounding Berkeley area. Also the owner is really nice and recognizes me when I come in. I haven't eaten here much but remember ordering a sandwich with pesto on it once which was good.
Also the mango tea is really good too. Definitely somewhere that I have to try more.
I love the chicken pesto panini with the side Orzo salad! I have tried nothing else and don't think I will -- but it was a good call and absolutely recommendable for a fulfilling lunch.

I can't really comment on the food, but their drinks are solid.  It's a really nice place to get some work done if you're on the northside of campus.  I really enjoy the lighting that the cafe receives since it's situation on the corner of Euclid.  

Check it out, order a beverage and get some homework done(:

This cafe has quickly risen to become my favorite food spot on Northside. Their orzo salad is da bomb! I almost want to say that is outshines the sandwiches that it accompanies, and the sandwiches are pretty darn tasty as well. I've gotten their veggie sandwich in the past: a delectable fusion of eggplant, avocado, mushrooms, spinach, pesto, etc. I'd say their raviolini soup is just o-kay because the little ravioli packets with cheese remind of those frozen italian pastas you can get at a grocery store. Also, I had their veggie sandwich for Cal Day catering, and it was sadly not the same as their usual food, so don't expect spectacular group orders for events. 

Service can get a bit slow during rush hour (noon) which is especially annoying if you only got something small like soup to go, but the workers are really nice, attentive, and make sure everyone gets their order in a reasonable time. Looking forward to tasting all the rest of their sandwiches, especially the turkey cranberry and chicken pesto. Also, from what I've observed their baked potatoes are gi-normous!
These guys aren't making good food- it's GREAT FOOD! Simple- favorable, good portion-sizes. Fresh and filling! Breakfast was quick, fresh-made-to-order. Will be a RePeAT customer!!!!
Good place to go for a quick meal or a takeout breakfast or sandwich. Great breakfast burrito. Definitely a cafe, not a whole lot of indoor seating, and a somewhat limited menu, but good!

North Side Cafe is blessed with a highly visible location.  There are other cafes on north side, but this one pops out on the corner of Euclid and Hearst.  Every time I pass by, the place is packed with people who look SUPER productive.  So you know...naturally, I went on in.

At 11am, I was caught between lunch and breakfast options.  I decided to order a simple cold Pastrami on Dutch with provolone cheese ($5.76 with tax).  Expensive, man.  Why did I get this?  The sandwich itself was everything I expected -- a ~1 foot long with the standard veggies and condiments.  All in all, not impressive.  Stuffed Inn still wins for my favorite North Side sandwich joint.  Although North Side Cafe isn't a great sandwich place, their breakfast plates look much tastier and a better deal for the starving college student.

Also, AirBears internet connection makes it here.  YES.
The stools by the window are great. :)
And the establishment is SO CLEAN.  The counters and beverage bar sparkle I swear.

Egg-cellent Southside Scramble (spinach-mushroom-bell pepper). They melted the cheese over the top instead if mixing it in, but I kinda liked that.  The house potatoes are perfection -- be sure to try them!  

Ambiance is a bit bland, and they had no fresh-squeezed juices (only Tropicana).  But hey, I'm just picky.

Northside Cafe offers a quick option for breakfast and lunch every day of the week. My personal favorite is the Chicken Pesto sandwich, no tomatoes. The orders come with a side of Orzo pasta, which is pretty tasty; but the portion leaves a little to be desired. I like the atmosphere of the place; it's open and welcoming. The staff is the same pretty much everyday and maintain a very friendly relationship with the customers. My only complaint would be that it is a little pricey, expect to spend between 7-10 dollars per meal.

Nice place for a breakfast, especially if you're up early and around here before the other shops open. Had the breakfast burrito (called breakfast wrap here) with ham for about 5 dollars. Shared between my girlfriend and I, we were both content afterwards.

Although I prefer Ann's kitchen breakfast burrito, this place takes a close second. Basically your typical breakfast burrito with eggs, potatoes, cheddar cheese an salsa all wrapped in flour tortilla. Bacon or ham is an extra dollar. I wish the salsa was more like a pico de gallo than just salsa but that's personal preference. Still enjoyable nonetheless. Clean and quiet atmosphere from what I perceived on a 9 am Saturday morning. I'd come back again to try other things on the menu.
North Side Cafe has excellent food.  The service is quick and  efficient which I love.  I recommend this cafe to all my friends.  The ones that have gone enjoy every bit of it!

I usually end up getting lunch here twice a week. My favorites are the chicken florentine panini and the baked potatoes. I've found everything on the breakfast menu to be great as well. Gets a little crowded sometimes, but it's popular for good reasons!

I hadn't been back for a while, but wanted a salad, so I stopped by Northside. Unfortunately, the taste of my chicken caesar salad reminded me why I stopped going - the whole thing was bland, the chicken had a tough texture and no flavor, and the croutons and lettuce weren't much better. Apparently, they also started charging an additional 25 cents for credit card transactions. Given their already high prices relative to other restaurants around Hearst and Euclid, such an increase is hard to justify.

Got the Southside scramble (spinach, bell peppers, mushroom, onion, tomato, Swiss cheese) and I thoroughly enjoyed it. The scramble comes with four pieces of toast and potatoes. I loved their hot sauce, and along with the very satisfying portion size, made for a very good brunch. 

Seating at the cafe filled up very quickly around 11am and I noticed many students with books and papers out studying, most of whom were not likely to leave until a few hours after their meal. 

I definitely want to come back and try something on their lunch menu. Northside Cafe is located perfectly at the cross street, and with its inviting and collegesque atmosphere, won't be long before I pay another visit!

I'm working at my desk on the Northside of campus when my cubicle neighbor comes back from lunch with a dish that smells and looks amazing. I ask what it is, and he responds a panini....sounds like a bikini, and I like those, so why not?

I had the Steak and Mushrooms Panini. Fantasticly delicious. I am not really a mushroom fan, but it isn't overpowering.

I was a little sad about the lack of drink selection. When I went, the soda fountain was out of half of the drinks available. Since they have Pepsi products, I was very excited that they had Mountain Dew, but disappointed that they had it in neither fountain or bottle form...only 12 oz cans :( A tragic mistake given the location right next to the engineering buildings.

I really like the ambiance here. Very clean and new. Bright lights and lots of windows give off a much better vibe than many coffeeshops on northside (in my opinion). I understand that by keeping it dim, people fall asleep and buy more coffee, but that isn't an environment I enjoy studying in.

Service was acceptable....I waited about 10 minutes for my food, which came to a little over $8. A little pricey for Northside, but the food was great.

I tried it three times in the first week, with something different each day....

* Day One: The panini sandwich. Very tasty and good, though the service was a little slow -- my friend who ordered a salad got theirs about 10 minutes before my sandwich was ready. I assume this will get quicker as they learn the menu, but it has deterred me slightly from ordering a sandwich at the lunchtime hour again... The orzo salad was not that good, but I think that's my own personal taste - I'd rather have it without the add-on.

* Day Two:  The mozzarella & basil salad. Delicious. Oh my, so much better than the other salads in the area. Fantastic. I will definately be coming back for their salads.

* Day Four (took a break for soccer-watching): The baked potato. Nom nom nom. Needed some butter underneath all the fixin's, but I will certainly be coming back for this in the winter time.

Staff is very friendly. Only one cash register, which will slow them down once the school year starts, but once their kitchen staff learns the menu more, they will get quicker in service time. The layout is nice, lots of tables and counter space, although the noise is a bit much when it's crowded.

FOAM!!! [jumps up and down, as promised]

haha.  I had to wake up early in the morning for an interview today, and since I was up the night before studying for an impending midterm and prepping for the interview, I was knocking out midday.  I walked over to Northside Cafe and noticed another server/barista, who I probably now figure could be the owner.  

Anyways, I ordered my double macchiato again and got pretty decent foam!  [YAY]  Maybe next time I'll sit down for a latte or au lait [with foam!] or perhaps a HOT pastrami, per Soosh's [owner] recommendation.

btw. I knocked out 30 minutes into my following lecture...  that just means I need more sleep - like now.

I grab breakfast here before every midterm or final I have on the northside of campus.

I usually grab an omelet or sandwich while reviewing my notes or doing the whole last-minute cramming routine. So yes, food comes out pretty quickly but is it spectacular? Eh, not really. Are the employees nice and friendly? I didn't get that vibe. And to be honest, I don't think this place gives you the best bang for your buck. Most menu items are about $7, and everything is plain imo. 

I can tell you people who come here are interesting though. I wasn't eavesdropping on the table next to me or anything, but there was a 40some year old man giving advice to a similarly aged woman advice on how to change careers. She was a middle school teacher and complaining about how kids can't write these days. Freaked me out a little and gave me something to think about as I finished my sandwich.

TWO GIANT OVERSIZED MONSTROUS THUMBS UP..

Really nice place, very clean, high ceilings, windows all around, its really the kind of place I want to eat in.

The food is good as well havent tried too much yet, but I will get around too it..  Maybe the owner will throw in a free lunch or two for my good review???

I think he had music going on, but I would have appreciated a little more T.I. coming thru the speakers. But hey not worth deducting a star, and i'll be a returning soon.. Great place i do reccomend..

Love love love this place!

Me and my husband have been here 25 Times and only lived in Berkeley for 2 months! I'm not saying this is hands down the best place to eat ever but for me I love it! Every dish i've tried has been desirably good. The White mochas are delish. The workers are fun and energetic! I really do love this place.

Came here to study for my final and wow! Not one of my best ideas.

As far as cafes go, the Northside Cafe is "okay", at most. And in terms of a study location, it's pretty bad. There's no Wi-Fi and it's pretty freaking loud! That being said, if you NEED internet, you can try connecting to AirBears, but that'll be pretty spotty at best.

Anyways, as for food, I thought I would just be studying the entire time, so I just ordered a Mango Iced Tea. I was a bit disappointed with the Iced Tea, as it was very watery and tasteless. Not very much mango, if any ):

I really wanted to like this place, but sadly, it just wasn't meeting my needs. Maybe next time?

I came here once for breakfast, and had the breakfast burrito and chai. The burrito was completely tasteless and the chai tasted mostly like warm milk with a little spice on top. When I asked them to make it stronger, I had to pay extra and still received a watered down chai. 

I went back again for a lunch sandwich and got their steak and mushroom panini, thinking it would be like a grilled sandwich version of a philly cheesesteak. Instead, the "steak" was hard, tough, dry strips of meat, and there was A-1 sauce inside! It was terrible! Their side salad was just a box of lettuce covered in a mound of black olives and a sprinkle of cheddar cheese. I've never had a worse side salad in my life!

OK but not great all around. Has a good selection of diner food on top of the usual cafe stuff. None of it is the best in the neighborhood, but it's not bad either and they have better hours than most places around. Good place to grab something to eat on the northside on the weekend.

This place is too loud to study in.. too much goin on around you and definitely doesnt have that cozy berkeley study cafe vibe you get from places like Peoples Cafe. I ordered the breakfast wrap/burrito.. tasted very Denny's like... but for 4 bucks.. you cant complain too much. I probably won't be back here with the abundance of coffee shops in berkeley.

UPDATE: Im bumping them up a star because the owner/manager/whoever sent me a message defending their place WITHOUT getting confrontational/taking it personally. Thank you for caring about your business, all the while having the decency not to attack yelpers for ... well, yelping!

I always get their fruit and walnut salad here! It's so good. mixed greens, with a raspberry vinagrette, with strawberries, candied walnuts, blue cheese crumbles, dried cranberries, and focaccia. Highly recommend this for lunch!

This place isn't all that exciting for being a cafe. I came here on a day where Cal had a huge event and people were roaming the streets, the sun was shining, and shops were earning!

I came here to grab a coffee and possibly try their cold cuts, but never happened. Unfortunately, I just had an ice cold lemonade can with a bottle of water :/ The vibe wasn't there for me. The service was boring and the shop didn't have that fresh brewed smoke in the air. 

The worst part that happened to me and my gf was getting "kicked out". The store was closing soo damn early. I understand it was Sunday but damn, the store didn't have to close around 3 hahaha. I saw people who were just getting ready to settle down with their kids at the table but had to move out fast. Usually, the people already inside are allowed to finish while closing the doors to the public but this place doesn't do that deed. I hate it!

Breakfast Burrito: $5.38 total ($3.99 + $1.00 for bacon) = heaven in my mouth. 5/5

Northside Salad is also pretty good. 4/5

French Toast: Hrm... I wish this came with some fruit, and some more powdered sugar  and a bit .. harder. It was not one of my favorite things here, 2/5.

Coffee!!! If you bring your own cup, you actually get a discount!!! How awesome is that!

Hot Pastrami Sandwich = 5/5 
I had a sandwich on a ciabatta roll (apparently its also good on sourdough - note to self: must try) and oooomgggg it looks and tastes sooooooo good. Thinly cut slices of warm pastrami that is balanced well with a mustard sauce (not sure what it is exactly) with pickles and greens.. oh my! my new favorite sandwich at the northside cafe.

I've been wanting to check this place out since I always see it whenever I die hiking up the killer hill to Soda Hall, and I finally got to try it yesterday. I ordered a Steak and Mushroom grilled panini. It comes with grilled sirloin, sauteed mushrooms, grilled onions, swiss cheese, and house steak sauce, along with a side of house orzo salad. The panini was okay. Pretty dry... I enjoyed the house orzo salad more lol... I tried some of my friend's Ham and Cheese grilled panini, and it was very salty.

No wifi!!! You don't get AirBears here either! :( Limited outlets as well. I guess I would come study here if I wanted to avoid temptations of wasting time on social networking sites.

This review is based solely on coffee: drip coffee and espresso drinks.  Never eaten there, though the food looks good.

I often stop in in the morning on my way to lab, and am always greeted by polite and speedy service.

Today, I stopped by after a lecture for an afternoon pick-me-up while still trying to curb my caffeine, so I ordered a decaf coffee.  Dude behind the counter took my mug, then stopped short in front of the decaf drip machine, turned around said he'd give me a double americano because he wasn't sure how fresh it was.  (He said lunch was really busy, so wasn't sure when the coffee was last made.)  And, he still charged me the same price as a regular coffee.  Thanks, dude!  A grand gesture that speaks volumes about their service.

ps. Bring your own mug! It's green and saves you an entire quarter.  With that, you can park for about 2 whole minutes in SF, or get 10 minutes on your dryer.
What a great addition to the North side of campus.  Plenty of light and outlets make this a great study space with healthy, yummy food.

I was looking forward to coming here because many people have been talking abou how great this place is. I got their soup of the day, Minestrone. Unfortunately, I found it overly salty and the soup tasted liked it came out of a can. The focaccia bread that came along with it was not only small but a bit dry. Overall, I liked the decor of the place but I didn't find it anything special and the food was not very good

I had my first breakfast burrito in LA.  Ever since I've been searching for a similar breakfast burrito (or wrap as they call it). Simple but delicious, eggs, potatoes, cheese and salsa in a tortilla with the option to add bacon ham or sausage.  The burrito was not only huge but delicious.  I wish they put whole strips of bacon in the burrito though. I also ordered a cappuccino here. Perfectly made with Mr Espresso. (Maybe not as good as Nefeli next door.) If they had free wifi and were open later I'd be here much more.

Sometimes when I know I have a long day ahead of me, I like to stop by Northside Cafe on my way to class and grab a breakfast wrap ($3.99) to go. They only serve these until 11:30am on weekdays, so you have to wake up early! The burrito is seriously HUGE and stuffed full of yummy goodness. It comes with scrambled eggs, potatoes, cheese, and salsa. You can also add bacon, ham, or sausage to it for a little extra. In my opinion, this monstrosity is definitely the best deal here!! It can last me 1.5 meals and is a super cheap way to get full! Plus, it's portable and easy to eat when you're on the go. The potatoes are seasoned nicely and when I'm lucky, are cooked to the point where they're a crispy golden brown. Then, this thing is really amazing. At other times, they are a bit softer but the wrap is still very satisfying.

There's ample seating with tables and also counter seats near the window so you can people watch. I find that a lot of people come here to work or study too.

Quick update: 

The owner was gracious enough to contact me and explained that the milk they use is 2% --- which makes sense now. 

With the now-tempered expectation, and what is pretty cool service in my books, I'm moving it to a 3 stars.

I will try the bites next time, but I'd recommend one shouldn't expect a "bluebottle" cappuccino or latte and it should be fine.

============
I had a latte and the milk was too thin. There was a tiny layer of dry foam on top and that was it --- none of the smooth silkiness of a latte well made. It sucked.

I enjoy sitting and eating my breakfast here as I  watch the people cross the street to and fro the UC-Berkeley campus. 

This is our weekend breakfast place :) we always get the pancake platter with a side of toast and it is enough for the both of us. The price is extremely reasonable and the food...delicious! The delicious, cheesey scrambled eggs and the warm buttered toast, with the pancakes and maple syrup..mmm..

Baked potato no. 2 (cheese, chives, sour cream, we do not get the bacon) is super yummy! It is baked to perfection and at $5.25 is very filling for one person.

We tried the french toast platter but the french toast was extremely dry and was not to our liking. Similarly, we tried the Breakfast wrap   and found it to be extremely soggy with no distinct flavor(s) as such.
