However, I am now reconsidering ever coming again because you are SO UNBELIEVABLY RUDE. WOW. I get that my friend had a long day of midterms and drank beer and was resting her head against the wall. It was not like she was sprawled out on the seats or had her head all over the table or doing anything inappropriate in anyway. And you have to come up screaming like a lunatic, telling her you're going to call the cops and put her in jail, and tell her her dress is too short. WOW REALLY? YOU'RE A FREAKING JERK.

Way to be a such a great manager with such amazing customer service skills. If I knew who else to complain to I would. You suck! Hope you're proud of yourself for yelling at college kids/loyal customers.

The Bear's Lair has always been a place that piqued my interest. It's on-campus drinking permissed by the UC system, but with a type of bar experience that lets you down a lot more than a private bar in town that has real character.

You'll notice it immediately in the not-very-attentive bartenders. They work for the UC system, not for you. And certainly not at a bar dreamed up by an entrepreneur who is looking to push the envelope and give his clients the best times possible. There's a sense of corporateness and "rah rah rah" to the bar's atmosphere, and it's decidedly fake to me.

However, you avoid a lot of the problems you see off campus with cantankerous drunks, and even though it gets really crowded, people still seem to stay at bay as far as violence goes.

I think only freshmen or out-of-steam Van Wilders looking to relive college glory are going to get anything out of this, and yet freshmen aren't allowed in. But what do I know? The place has 4 stars.

I am a huge supporter of college campuses with amazing Pubs.  I have a soft spot for College Pubs that are on campus and good.  Because sometimes a smart girl's just wants a beer after lecture.  Sat at the bar and was there for the pop quiz Night which was fun even though my friend and I didn't participate, we felt the energy of the space and the power of the brain no matter how many adult beverages one consumes.  

Almost gave the bear lair 5 stars but I held back because of the bathroom.  What's up with that?  Is it just one stall because they are going green or something?  Or just in case some of those people from people's park stop by and need a place to kick it?  

Other than the bathroom (I shiver just reviewing about that bathroom) this pub is bomb dot com.
Pubs on school grounds are always a plus.
The outdoor seating area smells bad, and sometimes it smells very bad.
Typical college bar. This is actually a fun place to watch Cal football games at if you don't have tickets. Cheap beer, fun crowds. What more can you ask for? It does get a bit fratty at times.

Maybe it's depending on the size of the university, but this pub, for a campus pub, is relatively large.  That is, compared to my small campus anyway.  A good number of booths, a good number of beers on tap, and not to mention the good ol' set of televisions set to sports.  Gotta love it.  Their hef isn't particularly great, but the environment here is enough for a good hangout with friends maybe in between classes.

Unfortunately, I visited this bar when beat the clock was not in effect.  I'm sure that if it was, I would lean closer to giving this place five stars.

BEAT THE CLOCK!!! Fridays, come around 4pm and have the time of your life... plus run into everyone and their mom!  LOVE IT.

Their cheesy fries are great!

I can not discuss  much of what has gone on here, to protect the innocent, the guilty, and the satisfied.  But trust me when I say....


Giggity, Giggity!

This is a chill place to have a beer and some basic pub grub. The pulled pork sandwich is orgasmic.  Get someone to lick your fingers and God only knows how your night will end.  Do NOT go here in your fancy Friday nite best or with your pointy-est hooker heels.  Wear some jeans, comfy shoes, and a tshirt with a cute saying, it gives people an excuse to look at your chest.

Ack. Crowded and hot!
Beat the Clock was all right. It's definitely something to do before you graduate. Beer tasted bad though. No idea what we got but we got a stout and a hef for sure. Also wtf line to the bathroom?! Why?!

As an aside, even though the drinks were bad, the atmosphere was not. Crowd consisted of a lot of people I either recognized throughout my 3+ years at Cal or friends. It was somewhat nostalgic in that light. Though I'm not really the sentimental type, it felt like it symbolized the coming together of good, smart, and sweet Cal people representing the diversity that is Cal. :)

PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT

If you're a student at Cal, take advantage of beat the clock. One of my regrets was not spending enough time here. I always had somewhere to be, and didn't sit down to have a drink. In my defense, I had to be at the RSF and showing up to the RSF a bit drunk is not a good idea. But always loved this place. Hang out inside or on the patio on picnic tables, drinking with friends. Enjoy it while you can.

Nice large bar with plenty of TVs for sports and great Jupiter beer on tap. It gets even more interesting outside, especially when there is a band playing in the courtyard, trying to compete with three guys at an outdoor table pumping spanish music through their portable speakers. Combine that with the Steely Dan playing on the inside and you have quite a combination of sounds...

I don't really have much to say about this place. The fact that its an on-campus pub pretty much speaks for itself. The place is usually filled with students, former students, etc. There actually is an OK amount of seating, but because its so crowded during peak hours, it seems that you're standing all the time. 

The prices here are average normally, but pretty cheap during happy hour, when they have beers which start cheap but increase in price every hour. The selection of beer is OK, but they have occassionally run out of the selection of beers I wanted. The food selection here is actually surprisingly decent, although very pricey. I've come here to just meet people, chill, and watch football games and every time have had a fun experience. Just don't expect too much.

GO BEERS! 

No CAL football game would be the same without a stop at Bear's Lair.  It's everything that you need to make you feel like you're in college again.  The place is always packed and the service does a really good job of always remember to fill your pitcher.  Good pizza, better beer, big TV's.  What more could you ask for?

I've only starting going here AFTER i graduated... i was wondering tomyself.. what the heck was i doing during my last year of college here....i've been missing out

3 words to describe this place when I hear Bear's Lair

BEAT THE CLOCK....BEAT THE CLOCK.. BEAT THE CLOCK

just keep buying those cheap pitchersssss.. keeeppp chugging on those beerss.. keeep feeelin that buzzz... while being with all of your friends!!!!!!!!

food here is pretty good too.. FRIED fooood plus beer.. what more can you ask for.. perfect combination..

beware of stuffiness, huge crowds, buzzed students on any happy hour/  beat the clock time!! That is all.

I have to pay homage to the Bear's Lair of yore when they had the beer patio and students packed into the fenced area and drank their brains away each and every Friday afternoon to early evening.  The gallon challenge....I almost made it then blacked out a half pint away from victory.

As far as the revamped Bear's Lair:

The best place to ever be when Cal is playing a football game!!  They have outdoor and indoor seating.  Grad from far and wide come to watch the game and pre-drink and post drink!!  Their beers are not the best but when it comes down to drinking beer for football games no one is too picky!!

They have muchies as well. Chicken tenders, fries the usual bar fare along with some actual food.  On game days they have a hot dog and burger cart.  

Glass wall and open doors connect the bartender inside to the boozer's outside...on a Sunday day the tables and benches can't be beat.  Inside are booths, leather chairs and a fireplace....cozy.

We were looking for a place within walking distance of Zellerbach for a bite to eat and some beer before the Sufjan Stevens show.  Bear's Lair had everything we were looking for- tv's to watch the A's game, solid pub food and tasty beer.  The bathroom was gross but I guess that should have been expected from a bar on campus.  If you're looking for a spot to go pre-game or pre-concert you could do a lot worse than the Bear's Lair.

Shout out to Karen W. and Jeff C. Yelp Elite crew at Bears Lair.

Jupiter brews on tap. My choice is the Hef for drinkability. Honey wheat was good too, though. I went here on an empty stomache so I'll need to plan ahead next time because I ended up staying for a good amount of time without food.

Lines are crazy so you might wanna arrive a little before 4pm on Fridays for BEAT THE CLOCK.

They raised prices, but $6 pitchers till 5pm is still a monster deal. Great scene, and you'll probably see just about everyone you know there some time or another. See ya there!

- THE GOOD: Three words - BEAT THE CLOCK. Paying the clock hour for a pitcher of beer + junk food + good company = Friday afternoon debauchery.  Bear's lair's beat the clock gives you something to look forward on those dreadful Mondays.  Great memories of drinking beers and eating delicious bar food with my girls.  Great place for random run-ins with people you haven't seen in a while and making new drinking buddies.  And you won't find a better place to catch the Cal game or March Madness on the big screen.  

- THE BAD: Table space gets taken quickly during BTC (beat the clock), so you should arrive early if you want to sit down; otherwise, it's standing room only.  Especially during BTC, service can be slow.  You're better off going to the bar to order than waiting around for someone to take your order.   

- THE UGLY: Steer clear of the bathrooms!  Use the bathrooms next door at Eschelmen (sometimes closes early) instead of risking getting STDs from the disgusting bear's lair bathrooms.  

Bottom line, not a bad college pub.  Bear's Lair makes you long for those carefree days of college.  Good bar food, decent selection of beer, fun crowds - sure-fire combination for good times.

So this place gets 1 star.  Why... you might ask?  here it is.....

So it was the rainy day of Cal vs USC football this past winter.  My group of USC fans decided it would be fun to get sloshed before the game with all the local fans (USC and CAL).  We figured we live in a civilized world where a man from another fan "race-hood" would be welcomed with open arms into another fan's "race-hood's" lair and enjoy some porridge together.  We couldn't be more wrong.  I don't care what flack i get for saying this but the average "liberal" in Berkley is less "liberal" than my nra card carrying, conservative slime-ball, Bentley driving neighbor in Corona Del Mar.  The reason for these audacious accusations are due to the fact that each and every bartender completely ignored me for like 45 min.  Even a few nice "liberals", whom the bartenders were attending to, were appalled by the most unprofessional behavior directed towards us.  Being ignored is one thing but then being told "we will not serve you because the color of your jersey" ...no she di-ent!?!  I laughed to which she then replied "it's not a joke".  I should have punched her in the FACE!

Thankfully we found, on the other side of the tracks, a sports bar that would serve our kind.  Oh... and USC ripped em a new one that day.

This is THE place to be on gameday. 

Outside patio, large TV's and plenty o' beer. The crowd is pretty rowdy, primarily because most people drink here hours before gametimes so they are pretty sauced up come kickoff time. You can by slices of pizza here and are very close to telegraph in case you need a quick bite elsewhere.

A little bit gross, a little bit grungy, a little bit drunk... Some words to describe your time at BTC.

A large selection of beers ranging from the blondes to the darks juxtaposed with a not-so-large selection of drunk foods, limited to pizza, chips, and some fries here and there.

Good place to meet up with your friends and bump into those awkward facebook friends you never really talk to. What's better than beer to smooth over that initial awkwardness as you invite them to your growing table and pour a few cups? There are no sad pandas when everyone is laughing.

Note: Pee before you come! The bathroom lines get long and the toilets considerably gross as the hour turns.

I almost never came here during college but now that I'm a seasoned alum, I realize my folly. 

Here's a little word problem, geeks. On Fridays, there's a special happy hour deal: If we denote the hour after high noon with i, then from i=5 to i=8, the price of beer is i dollars and from i=9 until they close, the price of beer is $8*. In terms of i, how loaded can you get? 

This isn't theory; it's empirical. Get over to Bear's Lair and gather some fucking data.

*For you Nutri Sci majors, this means they have $5 pitchers of microbrews from 4-5, $6 pitchers from 5-6, etc., etc. and they max out at $8.

There are all these annoying signs all around campus that have huge pictures of students' faces on them with written quotes about their favorite thing about Cal. 

*Barf*

If I had been asked to be on one of those blatant propaganda posters I would only have agreed to do it if mine could have had "Bears. Lair." scrawled under my over-sized, black-and-white face.

But seriously, I never have anything but a ridiculous time here. Shameless Halloween make-outs, shamelessly getting half the bar to dance to Journey with me and my friends at the end of the night after drinking since 4 p.m., shamelessly sneaking out to do naughty things then shamelessly returning, shamelessly stomping around and saying "Hi" to people I barely know from class who don't really know who I am, cause I'm not so sober. Basically this is the place where shame goes to die in a pitcher of Pabst Blue Ribbon.

Thursdays are the BEST. Beat the clock on Fridays are neat ($5 pitchers till 5, $6 pitchers till 6, etc.) You will have to wait a very long time to pee. :(

Just dug up this gem from the archives of a blog I used to keep a few years ago (have since moved onto other internet blogging outlets... holla, Yelp!). I still think it's pretty funny. Here you are- Vintage Anna K.

This muffin is gross... and I am drunk.

My morning so far:

Awakened at 7:45, by my dad yelling: "What the hell are you doing, we're supposed to be leaving right now!"

Perhaps I should preface this with what I did last night. Michelle was home for spring break, and it was her final hurrah before heading back to the East Coast. So, the two of us headed out to Berkeley for what was supposed to be a mellow night... not so much. We arrive at Kips to meet Kara and Patton, its dead, so we head over to the Bear's Lair... where we immediately are accosted by a Canadian rugby team. 

I wasn't going to drink, but as it turned out, the sky opened up and God said, "I give unto thee a barful of shirtless Canadian men."

Game on. Ended up getting hammertime, got home at an unholy hour.

Cut to this morning. 

7:55, Walk (let's be accurate, stumbled) out the door... good thing I still have all my makeup on from last night.
8:30, Arrive at Starbucks. When Barista asks if i'll have my usual, (a double tall nf latte) I inform him I'm gonna need a triple thanks, and something to eat because I think I just may die. What do I want? I don't care. Surprise me.

Poor decision.

9:45, Still working on my disgusting muffin with inidentified fruit bits protruding from its every orifice. 

Aaaand, still drunk. F-ing Canadians.

Beat the Clock!

Here's the down low: This is a great place to meet up with old freshman floormates you haven't seen in 3 years and catch up over a pitcher of beer. There is a great selection of beers for you to choose from however, Beat the Clock is only worth it if you drink between 4-5.

1 Pitcher at 4:00: $7 (YES IT'S SEVEN DOLLARS NOW)
Every hour there after is an additional dollar and honestly, you can find better deals in Berkeley for a pitcher without the chaos and long lines for bathrooms (or having to sneak off to Eshleman to pee in the garage).

I liked Beat the Clock the first few times I went but after a while it kinda gets old. I'll still give it 4 stars though.

ENJOY.

Being a pub on a university, we you can imagine the mayhem that ensues here. It's rowdy, crowded, hot, and grubby. It's the college experience! The pitchers here are fucking cheap ass on Friday. It used to be that pitchers were priced at whatever time it was, but now pitchers are $6 starting at 4PM and goes up a dollar per hour until 7PM. Afterwards, it stays at $9 until closing time. 

Through all the noise and chaos, I failed to find out what I was drinking yesterday. I do know there was some sort of malty porter, watery hef, and the Axe IPA.

Good luck getting a seat and be prepared to rub shoulders with your neighbors. Go Beers.

GO BEARS! YAY!!

I'm giving it 4 stars for the fellow Cal students that I saw during my two times at Beat the Clock, glowing tomato-red like the true Asians they were. I came twice and had a lively time x2. Sucks how you have to go to Eschelman (was that the name of the building?) to use the restroom though. And it's hard not to feel the urgency when you're chuggin' beer all evening long. The proximity of students (squished together on the benches is the norm) keeps you from freezing your ass off in cold Berkeley weather.

I miss this place. Had some good, good times drinking here back in college - mostly between classes :p The beer selection is pretty good, prices are decent, staff is always friendly and only really crowded on game and big concert days. Sure there are other, better pubs around Berkeley but I'm a Bear so I'll always come back to the Bear's Lair.

Through SarahE's storytelling, I have an affinity for the Cal/collegiate life I never experienced, and Bear's Lair proved itself to be just as vibrant as I could imagine!

The atmosphere and vibe is youthful and optimistically rambunctious.  Like an hours-long recess.  On a Friday.  With no yard duty.  The day before summer vacation.

Drinking copious amounts is the order of the day and the crowd here excels at the task! In a matter of minutes, as we waited for the adorable Rebecca A, I'd smashed through two pints of Jupiter Red and the remainder of a friend's Soju-something-or-other. Guys walked around drinking straight from pitchers.  Uber-cute coeds strutted about sipping from steins bigger than they were (not really, but yes, really.)  Mmmm, girls that drink beer... *sigh*

And the bartender?  Unbuttoned blouse + double-sided tape + switchy strut and low-rise jeans + spitfire attitude and a wink = Evil. EVIL!

Me likes.
____________________________________
I would have gone to college if some one told me it could be like this?! 
Ah, to be young, energetic, and free spirited... *middle finger to my adulthood*

I want to like this place.  I really do.  It's on the campus of my alma mater.  It's the only bar actually on a U.C. campus.  It's called the Bear's Lair.  In college I spent way too many Friday afternoons drinking quarts of $2 draft beer out in the sunshine and doing my best "Stop, drop and roll" impression when UCPD would roll in and start checking IDs.

But there are a number of issues here.  For one thing, they haven't cleaned the bathroom since I graduated (2001).  Also, the food is absolutely horrendous.  I ordered chicken strips the other day and the strips were all batter and no chicken, the fries had no salt, and the ranch dressing was watery.  I mean, how do you screw up chicken strips?

More offensively, before the Cal-Tennessee game, people were lining up outside waiting for it to open at 11am.  Now, that game was the biggest home game for Cal in 25 years, and they weren't open early.  Not to mention that while about 100 people were waiting in line, the staff inside was puttering around, drinking beer, and eating their lunch, while a horde of people was waiting to go inside and spend their money.  Very, very bizarre. 

And don't judge me for being angry that I had to wait in line to get into a bar at 11am.  Don't do it.

Sigh. Nothing like celebrating the end of a tumultuous thesis writing journey by guzzling beer for four hours on a Thursday afternoon. 

Why the 3 stars then? Their Guinness on tap blew. Hard. Enough to merit 2 stars on its own, but the other beers we had weren't bad, company was great, and the garlic fries hit the spot. But really, their Guinness was the worst I've had. At $17 a pitcher, it was flat, watered down and tasted like fail. 

Stick with Hef and some of Jupiter's other goods.

A respectable burrito considering the lack of good Mexican food in Berkeley. The carnitas was dry and in huge chunks which made it hard to eat and the guacamole was extra. Since I have moved here I have yet to find a really good Mexican place and Gordo is no exception.
Best burrito place in Berkeley.They have a large variety of meat and tortilla wraps. Also, it is quite affordable and fast. I recommend the carnitas. The meat is very juicy and tender.

I've eaten at the original Gordo's over on Clement in San Francisco, and that was pretty good.  The new one here on Telegraph didn't quite meet my expectations, and it's also competing against two other well known establishments in the area.  

I got a Chili Verde Gordo Plate here, and it really came up short.  It was very "heavy" and not spicy, and the beans seemed overcooked.  The whole meal was pretty much flavorless.  Not at all like what I had in San Francisco a few years back.  I don't know why I would ever go to Gordo Taqueria here, when Chipotle offers a greater level of customization (as well as depth of flavor), and La Burrita offers shrimp (!!!) burritos and tacos.  

Sorry Gordo, you're gonna have to step it up a bit.  You've got some stiff competition.

They make really good burritos here. The menu is really straightforward here and not complicated. They make flour/corn quesadillas, tacos and burritos.
The food here is inexpensive and portions are enough to fill you up without making you feel bloated.

Great tacos and burritos.  I suggest the carnitas super burrito, they pull out a slab of fresh pork and slice it to order!  The tacos are monstrous and delicious.  The price is on par with chains (Chipotle, Qdoba, etc), and the ingredients are fresher.  They have decent corn tortillas for gluten free folks.  The guac is tasty and is a cheaper add on than at chains.  I'll be coming back soon!

Gordos: best after a gamday! I LOVE their quesadillas! But they arent ordinary quesadillas: they're open faced. They're more like a soft taco really, but they're very unique, and perfect for someone who is looking to not eat as much tortilla (not a fan). The Salsa here isnt really salsa, but pico de gallo with HUGE chunks of onions and tomatos. Taste all the goodness in EVERY bite. The guac here isnt great though. Not worth an additional $.65 or whatever. I get a soft drink and chips/salsa (which is just pico, not salsa). The chips and salsa isnt great (I prefer La burrita) but its something to snack on. The portion sizes are great too.
Great place for a quick burrito or the like. Better than that other place down the street, and cheaper too!

A cheap and good burrito. That's what it is. For under $5 you get a good sized burrito that'll fill most people up (I'm a little on the bigger side, so I would need a super though.....). 

Today I got the chili verde, and it was pretty good. Just like what everyone else has said, it seems like their meat has been laid out there for a while, and the chili verde didn't seem all that fresh. But it was still pretty good. At least it was tender, not soggy or anything. 

In terms of taste, it can't beat Chipotle. The ingredients just aren't as fresh, or rather they're just not as tasteful. This place can't beat the super fresh salsa, the bomb corn, and the sour cream that chipotle has. 

The one thing that you have to get at Gordos is the extra sauce. The spicy green sauce makes the burrito 10x better and gives it much more taste - if spiciness counts as a taste. So, get the extra sauce! 

Ask them to grill your burrito also, it'll taste better - like a crispy tortilla on the outside. 

The place has a lot of seating too, and theres even bathrooms. It's a good place to hang out. 

Get the extra sauce, and tell them to grill your burrito. Hope this helped.

I was craving a big fat burrito one day and decided to try this place out.   Relatively new?  Wasn't there a few years ago.  

I got a chicken burrito and .... it filled me up but it was nothing special.  Also of note is that it looked so lonely all by itself in a paper bag.  I wish they gave some tortilla chips to keep it company.
this place isnt too bad. price is great and fills you up. i would like it if they can wrap burritos better though... i hate it when the burrito explodes right when you hold it...
awsommmmmmmme

Like a kid unwrapping a sweater on Christmas morning, I was disappointed. First of all, Gordo's "regular"-sized burrito is ridiculously small. Who is this intended for? 8 year olds? The burrito itself was pretty standard. I suppose it tasted healthier than say a burrito at La Burrita, but honestly, who gets a burrito to be healthy? Also, the service is super slow. With only two people in front of me, it still took over ten minutes to get my order. Personally, I would rather not skimp on taste, size and efficiency in favor of a marginal increase in potential healthiness. Next time, I'm sticking with Chipotle.

Good prices. Tasty tacos. Much better alternative to Chipotle. Make the walk down Telegraph! It's worth it!

Now, if I only they would validate my parking. Oh well, Cream across the street does, so head over for some ice cream sandwich desserts and validate your parking that way.

Gordo's has quickly become one of my favorite burrito places in the UC Berkeley Area. This is written more for students since that is where my experience with this restaurant lies. 

The burritos are pretty good, not very exceptional, but not bad either. However, there are two other things that shine about this place. Whenever I go, I get my food very quickly I'm in and out with burrito in hand in about 5 minutes. Even when the line looks long, the people behind the counter work quickly and the line moves swiftly. Moreover, the burrito is cheap. At about $6, I can't complain much about this place. 

Overall, if you're looking for exceptional burritos, this isn't really the place for you, but if you're just looking for a pretty good burrito that will definitely fill you up without breaking your wallet or wasting your valuable time, this is the place to go.

If you are going to label a restaurant Gordo Taqueria, it better be the best tasting place on the planet. Gordo, translated in English as the word "fat", will definitely make you fat, but sadly it doesn't make the cut as "phat". Ya feel?

Although the restaurant does maintain a clean casual atmosphere with speedy service, the various meat offered lacks flavor and spice. Beef, chicken, pork, veggies, whatever is your thing, you will find as ever so slightly above average. This epidemic plagues the tacos, burritos, and plates alike.

When dining at Gordo's I would recommend upgrading to the super burrito since doing so will add more ingredients, which is dire since its simplistic non-super version literally tastes like nothing. It's not that anything here tastes bad, it's just that nothing tastes very good either. Maybe a double edged sword, maybe the wrong use of the phrase.

Anyway, as much as anyone else I hate to admit it but Chipotle down the street beats Gordo's in close to all categories. Chipotle may be ridiculously unauthentic and part of a much larger chain, but Gordo Taqueria chains your tastebuds to boredom. Take your pick. 

Order at the counter. Under ten dollars. Okay but not great. Three Stars. Boom.
I probably eat here once a week. Get the guac, it's awesome.

So excited when Gordos opened up, and I def. fell in love.

Like most Mexican, sour cream and a guac is needed, so remember not to skimp!

Love the quesadillas. They're super sloppy, but super delicious! The gordo plate is good too, if your looking for something a little more civilized.

Also, they are super quick. Like ninja quick. I'm amazed at how fast they can prepare food.
This new location has accurately captured the greatness of all the others.  Some of the best burritos ever, fast service, fair prices.  It's hard to say anything bad about gordos.

I had really high expectations for this place that weren't quite met. However it was still a good experience. I shared a burrito with my boyfriend. the carnitas were really good, but the pricing was a lttle difficult. you paid for like every topping on your burrito. Also, I wasnt a big fan of the slice of cheese they melt on your burrito. I like shredded! But overall, I still enjoyed it. :)
Not worth it. There are plenty of great eats in the Berkeley area and this place definitely falls short. The food and drinks are always sort of bland.
Best place to get a simple bean and cheese burrito!

Meh. From all the extraordinary things I've heard about this place, I was expecting more.

I got a beef super burrito, which wasn't all that super. It wasn't even that big, and the difference between the regular and the super burrito was a bigger tortilla with some slabs of cheese on it that were supposed to be melted. All the meats are soaked in their own juices, making them look gross and unappetizing. Guacamole ($.65) and sour cream ($.45) are extra, but I guess it's still cheaper than a burrito at Chipotle (though Chipotle definitely has bigger burritos). I was able to finish the "super" burrito and not be overly stuffed.

I guess for ~$6 it was edible. I probably won't come back for their burritos, but I might go to try their quesadillas. I'll stick to Chipotle for now to get my burrito fix.

I heard about the new Gordo from Jennifer W. and trotted over for lunch today to check out the new addition to the Cream area.  I've had very little in the way of Gordo experience; I can remember going to their Solano location once or twice, but I'm not a regular.

My usual Mexican place is Picante, and my usual order there is the chile verde or carnitas plato.  Today I went for a chile verde plate at Gordo, specifying black beans and no extra sour cream or guacamole.  The chile verde was very good, and I was happy enough with the rice.  The warmed-up corn tortillas were totally fine.  I thought that the black beans were really meh and that the salsa fresca was more salsa than fresca.  It was pretty bad, actually.

I stand underwhelmed for now, but fate may bring me back some day soon.  As Jennifer pointed out, the interior is very pleasant (and Gordo's looks nice from the outside as well).  There are definitely rest rooms, although the customer who was trying to open one looked like he was struggling with the key that he got from behind the counter.

Gordo's has delicious burritos. The location is so convenient for students, and the prices can't be beat. My only complaint is that the burritos aren't rolled as tightly as I'd like, but that just means you should unwrap them as you eat. Sometimes I ask for an extra piece of foil to enhance the structural integrity.

I have grown up on Gordos. I've been to the gordos in San Francisco, Albany and Berkeley ( College Ave). This newest Telegraph location is no exception to how good this place is. Best Carnitas in the bay, but you can't go wrong with any of their menu. Everything is fresh and delicious.

I was excited about this spot opening up in my area.  The burritos look decent sized and the prices are not bad.  Note: The prices don't include if you want extras in your burrito other than rice and beans.  

I came in looking to try something other than a burrito and was happy to see they offered quesadillas.  I ordered one and was surprised to see him make my order the same way he was making all the other burritos.  I asked if that was a quesadilla and if they could put some lettuce in my quesadilla.  He said they dont carry lettuce. Really? 

How the hell does a mexican restaurant (fast food) not carry lettuce? (didnt actually say) 

I didn't feel the love so much when they were making my food, so dont ask for lettuce. 

There is definitely much better.  Places with lettuce too.

Much like its location on College, Gordo on Telegraph offers large burritos at cheap prices that are packed with flavor.  The meats are juicy and well-seasoned. The grilled veggie burrito also looks excellent and my vegetarian friend seemed to enjoy it.  You can ask for beans on your quesadillas and then they are basically like fried burritos without rice and with extra cheese (i.e. excellent).

Don't forget the hot sauce for an extra kick!

Biggest thing that bugged me right from the start?
The fact that the workers don't use gloves AT ALL to make all the burritos/tacos/etc etc
GROSS.
This definitely made it more difficult to eat my meal because this was primarily all I could think about as I took each bite. I don't know if it's better to know how disgusting your meal actually is or just to eat it ignorantly - either way, you're still consuming extra ingredients that may not necessarily be good for your health. JUST SAYIN.

Other than that, it's a super cheap place (I got a decent-sized chicken taco for under $3) and the place is relatively clean in the seating area. Menu is fairly straightforward; the font and spacing makes me feel like I'm reading an elementary book. The fillings for the burritos/tacos are the usual options (beans, rice, tomatoes, yadda yadda yadda), but guac and sour cream are extra.

I'm sure many other taquerias don't use gloves too, but that's what makes rating this really difficult. I'm thinking 2.5 stars is more accurate, but that's not an option on yelp.

AL PASTOR! Gordo's finally has it! This is the only location that has it. Even though the locations in SF are the best, I would have to say that this location is a close second. If you're like al pastor, what the @$%& is that? Well then you gotta try al pastor tacos from Gordos!

I tried Gordo for the first time recently, even though it's been a two block walk from me ever since it came they came to Telegraph. Based on what I've heard from friends about the other locations, I had very high hopes for Gordo. After trying it, however, I can conclude that it's pretty much a solid 3.

When you order, all of the ingredients are laid out for you. You can see that the meat has been sitting there for a couple of hours and that nothing is really that fresh. I got a Super Burrito with Carnitas, which included all of the basics, but with two slices of cheese. For less than $5, it's an awesome deal! The taste of everything was very typical, though. Typical Mexican rice, nice and tasty carnitas, some guac, sour cream, lettuce, etc. It definitely wasn't bad, but it was nothing too special. Just your average mediocre burrito.

Conveniently located and for such a low price, I most likely will come back if I have nothing to cook for dinner. I'll still most likely choose Chipotle over Gordo any day due to how fresh and delicious their burritos are, but Gordo comes in at a close 2nd.

As a Berkeley student with a taste for Mexican food, there aren't too many options in the area: Gordo, La Burrita, and Chipotle. After having La Burrita and Chipotle for a few months, I decided to try Gordo. SInce that moment, it has become my absolutely favorite burrito place in Berkeley, and one of my favorite of all time.

First off, Gordo is far more authentic then La Burrita or Chipotle. I wouldn't really go so far as to call it "authentic", but the way they cook and prepare the meat is much more so then most places. For example, if you order a carnitas burrito, they will take out the carnitas and cut it in front of you. Every single one of their meats that I have tried (carnitas, chicken, carne asada/steak) have all been amazing, and I alternate between them when I come here.

Unlike Chipotle, Gordo does not skimp on the meat and toppings. My most recent time at Chipotle, the person making my burrito put one "scoop" of carnitas on my burrito, and then proceeded to take off half of what he put on and place it back in the pile - IN FRONT OF MY EYES! At Gordo, they will easily give you twice as much meat as Chipotle does (and I already mentioned, this meat is far better in quality). Furthermore, they also give a perfect amount of beans, rice, and cheese. They may not overload on the guacamole, but considering it only costs 50 cents (as opposed to 1.80 at Chipotle), it isn't a big deal. Furthermore, their prices are unbeatable for the quality. My usual order (super burrito - any meat - with sour cream and guacamole) comes out to 6.90. Meanwhile, a similar burrito at Chipotle will cost 9 dollars. 

Also, this place rarely has a long line (the longest I've ever waited was 10 minutes, at the peak of lunch hour on a weekday), and the service is always great. So, when you see the 30 minute line at Chipotle, just walk another block and a half to Gordo Taqueria, and you won't be disappointed.
Chicken burrito with black beans, guacamole, and sour cream was the best I have ever had.

Food: the super burritos are huge and can fill you up. Definitely get it with the guacamole, worth the extra cents

Service: the service in the Gordo's Taqueria on College is better. I get kind of disgusted when they roll the burritos with their bare hands though. The meat on the grill just sitting there seems unsanitary too, I hope they will do something about that in the future 

Quality: a-okay
Gordo Taqueria is a less expensive less tasty Chipotle.

This place really caters to students.  I came in with a Groupon and they were shocked that I ordered over 20 dollars worth of food when every student ordered a burrito.  I actually felt guilty when the server looked as if he didn't want to make that much food, what an imposition for him!   We had a Gordo plate with extra carnitas, two steak tacos with guacamole, one chicken taco with guacamole, and their new veggie burrito. 

The chicken and steak tacos were generously stuffed with tender meat.  It's one of the best tacos I've had and I grew up with good Mexican food.  My veggie burrito was less good.  It had one whole carrot in it!  Giant clumsily cut carrots (each one inch long) and hard.  Yes, the carrots were undercooked.  There were also lots of red bell pepper and red onions.  Honestly, the burrito was just weird.  

The Gordo plate comes with beans, rice, tortillas of your choice, and any kind of meat that you want.  Not bad for about 6 dollars.  You definitely want to order extra meat as they don't give you that much per plate.

All in all, a solid culinary experience.  I recommend their tacos with guacamole.  The guacamole is only 65 cents more so it's affordable to spice up your taco.  Unfortunately, the amount of guacamole you get is totally not standardized.  Our three tacos each had different amounts of guacamole.  I honestly think Chipotle is a better deal but the flavors are definitely more authentic at Gordo's and they are generous with the meat.
Gordo has finally answered the call for edible burritos in the UC campus area. I've had the chile verde and carnitas so far... everything seems to be up to snuff.
My favorite meat is the chile verde: moist, tender, flavorful.  Get a gordo plate, and you'll have enough food for two meals, all for less than $6.  Good food, great value.

Loosely translated, Gordo means fat...and the portions at this place are definitely a little on the chunky side. Long gone the days of paying almost $3 for a "designer" taco. Here, the $2.65 (before adding sour cream, of course) is totally worth the price, as the cooks in the back slab it on heavy for you. I got two carnitas tacos and they were definitely worth the price, if not a little more. Did I overlook Carne Asada on the menu? I don't think I saw it...it would have been my first choice.

The quesadilla comes wrapped up like a burrito! It's really cute until you bite into it and then it gets messy and squirty.

I love it when food gets sassy.

I'm a fan.

I will enjoy this place even more once they get some beers through their doors.

Cheaper than chipotle or la burrita, more local-ish, faster than the one on college. The All Meat burrito is a revelation, something to be cherished, but not taken lightly. Two meals would best be made of that thing.
Dry.

Really wish they would serve a breakfast burrito. . .Gordo, hear my cry!

Other than the lack of eggy-chorizo breakfast burrito yummies, Gordo is a standard burrito place, with a few notable plusses. 

The upsides:
* Their carnitas is super-yummy, and they chop up a huge chunk right before your eyes when you order a carnitas burrito. La Burrito on Durant doesnt even OFFER carnitas- how can they still call themselves a tacqueria? 
* Love that in addition to pico de gallo, they offer pureed salsas in your burrito. 
* Order avocado- they add quite a bit! Such a bargain. 

The downsides:
*Pureed salsas don't add quite enough moisture to the burrito, largely because
* they put too much rice in their burritos. My advice is to order with 1/2 rice. 


Plus, it's right downstairs from my apartment, so how can I resist? It's pretty good, and they are SO very convenient.

The bean and cheese here is better than the bean and cheese from Los Primos. Didn't think I'd ever say that but i think it's true. 

Way better than La Burrita and obviously better than Chipotle.

I ALWAYS get the quesadilla.  Trust me, it's delicious.  Get the flour tortilla, add the guac and pico de gallo, and get your fav meat - I prefer chile verde.  Highlights every ingredient and just as filling as a burrito.  ~$5.  Just be careful, it can get messy.

5 stars for the quesadilla.  4 stars overall.

For a while I was trying to find a decent burger place, and somehow ended up here.

Still, I don't regret my purchase. The employee's are relatively new and sort of fumbled around with my order (one of them accidentally dropped green hot sauce on the rice in front of me; didn't really seem to matter). But the carne asada burrito was good, and when I mean good, I mean that meat was awesome. It was juicy, and tender.

Seriously. Let's pause here--I want to emphasize how good that carne asada was. Far better than anything I've tasted at Chipotle.

Go here for authentic Mexican fast food. Their grilled chicken burritos are my favorite, the rice and beans taste like they would at my parents house, not like they came from a can/box. Also, slightly cheaper than Chipotle if you don't add sour cream/guac.

Gordo has good quality and delicious food for cheap. I particularly like their chicken quesadilla with rice, beans, pico and hot sauce. The melted cheese, crispy tortilla hold everything together nicely. Most items are $5 or under.

The new location is in a great spot!

This is my preferred taqueria on the telegraph area. The burritos have quite a bit more flavor and character than la Burrita, and especially Chipotle. My personal favorite is getting no rice, and half meat, half vegetables. It's a decently healthy meal! (I recommend the refried beans with it). The horchata is also quite delicious and cheap.

Another thing, try their corn quesadillas. They're totally unlike normal quesadillas; more like tacos. It's a thick corn tortilla, grilled and then filled with meat, cheese, etc. I haven't had anything quite like it at other taquerias, and it's very good.
Quite tasty and fresh burrito.

I'm at a solid 3.5. Haha.

Their carne asada (beef) is well seasoned, and not too dry or salty. Some other places in the bay seem to have that problem.. When you pay extra for guac, you really get an ABUNDANT amount. Haha. So it could be bit overwhelming, but regardless the regular burrito was good. Their burritos are fairly cheap as well. Nice seating area in the place, and has a style similar to Chipotle.. just a bit more authentic.

The restaurant itself was nice, with a good amount of seating, and the people working there were nice. The food itself wasn't that great. I had a chicken burrito, and it was just bland tasting. I was only given rice, black beans, chicken, and barely any pico de gallo. I mean, I understand that I'm only paying like $4 for this burrito, but I really expected it to be more tasty.

Oh great usurper. Gordo is now the go-to spot for my near-daily burrito fix. Only one criticism: the hot sauce is kind of underwhelming. Here's a tip though. Always get a super burrito. The regular sizes are maybe an average of 50 cents cheaper even though they're so much smaller.

Recommended by a co-worker, I had really never noticed this place even though I have been living just 2 block away from it for over a year now. 

Can't say I regret it.

Gordo's isn't all that great, but then again if you like Chipotle, then you'll like Gordo's. They offer a simple selection of meats for your tacos and burritos, but not as authentic as I like my mexican taquerias to be. 

I got the super burrito, which I soon learned wasn't really all that "super", I mean...its just bigger. Still have to fork over the extra $ to have guacamole and sour cream. No, thanks.

Their selection of salsa is...umm...well, they dont have one. They only offer their green mild salsa and thats it. Being a guy who loves mexican food largely because of the assortments of salsas mexican cuisine is known for, you would think a taqueria would have more than one. 

My advice, walk the extra block and eat at La Burrita.

I came to gordo's with some friends last tuesday and chose here because they told me this place was better than la burrito. although i dont agree and still think la burrito is better, this place does give large portions and it ended up becoming my left overs. i thought my burrito was pretty dry and not juicy at all, so i might have to come another time to give this place a second try before i made any decisions. this service is really fast and i came at a time when there was no line at all.

I didn't know there was a Gordo on College until one opened up here on Telegraph. When this place opened, the line was out the door during the entire first week, and I finally had an opportunity to see what I was missing.

Gordo offers Mexican food at CHEAP prices. The plates are the best deal as they come with tortillas (enough to make 4 tacos) and then you still have leftovers to just eat by themselves for less thatn $6.00. The ingredients are so much better than Chipotle down the street. Not only that, but for burritos, these guys actually give you more than just a ton of filler rice and beans like Chipotle. I normally don't choose chicken since chicken is cheaper than beef, but the chicken here is clearly better so I would highly recommend it. 

The people working at Gordo are super nice too. I wish the place was a little bigger and the people behind the counter were quicker though. I would definitely come here again, especially for the plate and the tacos.

Only tried this place because of a family members craving... Mmmmmmm it was ok.
I got a super chicken burrito that just screamed blah. Now, I'm already skeptical of trying new Mexican/Taqueria places because it's usually a hit or miss situation, like here. But giving the benefit of a doubt  I did try a piece of my son's carnitas meat and THAT was pretty decent. All I know is of the 6 of us who got burritos here 3 of us were not impressed. I WILL say you get a decent amount at a very fair price. But hey don't take MY word for it!

Really not the best place to get Mexican cuisine. I guess I'm not terribly disappointed.

Decor and Service: Seemed pretty clean. Service is pretty bad. The employees making the burritos really didn't want to answer the simplest questions and get us through the line even though there were only 2 behind us. Pretty much bottom tier in this aspect.

Food: I got the all-meat super burrito, which was probably the size of the smallest chipotle burrito I've ever gotten. The burritos are pretty tiny, I could've easily eaten two of them, and it came out to around $7. Definitely not impressed with portions. As for flavor, it was just o.k. There was very little guacamole and cheese, and the burrito oozed the meat water. The least they could have done is drain it, especially because it tasted incredibly salty. The tortilla absorbed the water and tasted soggy. 

Verdict: Would rather go for Chipotle even if I'm sacrificing authenticity.

This place was really good! I got a chicken quesadilla but although it was yummy, the presentation wasn't all that great. The quesadilla ended up being all soggy because of the tomato salsa they add. I was also hungry within 2 hours I had eaten. Next time I shall order something more filling and without that tomato salsa.

The southside of the Berkeley Campus area lacks an adequate amount of Mexican food, so Gordo Taqueria is a frequent and convenient choice for many Cal Students. The only items I have tried are the burritos and the plates. The burritos are heavy (if you get the super burrito - if you get the normal-sized, it's just right). 

Overall, the burritos are good. The warm rice, beans, meat, and cheese make a delightful comfort food. Also, the salsa that they put in the burritos is tasty. Also, the plate comes with not one, but TWO tortillas! Made me super happy!

The sauted vegetables that they put in the veggie burrito/plate are completely tasteless and often undercooked. I also thought that it was kind of weird that, as a taqueria, they do not have lettuce. Also, the Horchata is disgusting and has a weird aftertaste. 

All in all, a good place for quick Mexican food on southside. A good vacation from Chipotle.

I have many fond memories of Gordo.  When I used to watch movies at the Four Star, I'd forgo the popcorn, grab a veggie burrito at Gordo, and watch the latest Hong Kong import.  The Gordo on College was the only taqueria I'd go to regularly in the east bay.  Now that I'm back in the bay, I get to Gordo's again, especially since they've opened shop near the Berkeley campus.  Nostalgia is a funny thing.  It has the power to seduce you into romanticizing about the past because I remember their burritos being much better than they actually are (at least as they are now).  After having a couple of burritos there, I'm surprised by how their food is an explosion of murky flavors.  There's nothing really distinct or special, other than that they are filling and reasonably priced.  Maybe if I move out of the area again, I'll start remembering Gordo more fondly.  As of now, it's just another burrito...not the worst, not the best, but they'll always taste better when I don't get the chance to eat there.

Price: Very cheap. I got the regular chicken burrito with guac & sour cream for ~$5. I also like how they have a regular and super option, for those of us that can't eat as much. Guac & sour cream are extra.

Food: The chicken is very flavorful, but I don't like the beef. The rice is nicely seasoned & the tortilla is very soft.

Comparisons: Gordo's tastes more authentic than Chipotle. La Burrita is more of a late-night, "dirty" Mexican taste.

Service: Fast. In and out. However, I do feel like they're pretty stingy with their guac, salsa, and meat. I felt like my burrito was mostly rice - it tasted pretty dry because of that.

Bottom Line: I'll be eating here again when I'm craving cheap Mexican food. However, I wish they wouldn't skimp so much on the guac and chicken!

Gordo's is better than Chipotlé. Plain and simple. After a good day Beating the Clock at Bear's Lair, there's nowhere I'd rather go to satisfy my drunchies.

The burritos are (rolled) tighter than superhero spandex.

Filling burritos--carnitas is my fave.

The chorizos are ok... The seating, with a criss-cross of cured leather, is a nice place to rest one's bum.

I like how quick they are.

If you have wheels, use them to go to a DIFFERENT Gordo's as this one is lame.  Perhaps they reduce the quality because they realize students don't demand much?  Perhaps they increase the rice because students don't mind the carbs?  Whatever the case, this is the worst Gordo's of all in the Bay Area.  Use your wheels to take you to the Albany location, or maybe even to another burrito shop ......that includes more than rice in their "Super."
my chicken burrito was perfect

Gordo is a great place for Mexican food, but their service staff isn't the friendliest.  They tend to treat all customers as frequent visitors, so when I asked a question as a first-time consumer, they answered me as if I was stupid or something.

They also don't tell you what things cost extra when added to your burrito.

Those negatives aside, Gordo is a quality restaurant with above-average food that I would recommend to a majority of my friends.

Yet another cheap but fundamentally dismal student eatery on Telegraph Ave. A cold uncomfortable place with barely ok food. I would give them more stars if they had decent salsas (it's not that hard to make a decent salsa - even I can do it) to mask the blahness of the food and gave you free  chips with your taco or burrito. But no. Nobody who works here seems the tiniest bit happy about it. Please god give to Telegraph Ave. a decent taqueria. It can't be that hard. Death to Gordo's because the person who owns this place just is not trying.

You get a fat burrito for a relatively low price (~$5.50-7.80), depending on how many extras you desire.

And unless there's a line or some ass ordering six burritos, you get your food pretty fast, usually under a minute.
Best priced burrito around. Thanks to my fellow yelpers, I tried the CARNITAS burrito. Best carnitas burrito ever. I can't wait to go back.

I'm going to say that this is the best burrito in Berkeley. I know all those San Diego kids will tell me they're absolutely gross, but I mean come on this is Northern California we're way farther from the border. 

I've been going to Gordo's since freshman year when they only had one on college so when this one opened up I knew I had to double the times I went to the gym since these are so good. If you're new to the area I highly suggest you make your way here at some point becasue it will probably be the best decision in your life.

So they recently had a deal on campus cred where you pay $5 for $10 worth of food--aw hells yes!

Brought my friend and we each got a taco (I got steak, she got carnitas). Since they are so big and come with 2 tortillas each we split the meat and switched so we could each try the different meats.
The carnitas are SOOO good.

We also got some chips and guac on the side...still not my fave place to get it but good.

This is a casual restaurant where you order and pay at the counter, then sit and serve yourselves. I enjoyed the crispy tacos and burritos here. When I'm feeling like eating something light, I just order 1 taco and top it with vegetables for dinner.

Burritos contain lots of meat (2,3 scoops of it), and it's also cheaper than chipotle. The meat is delicious, but the only thing I don't like is the lack of vegetables. The tortilla mixes really well with the rest of the burrito and tastes great. 

TL;DR; Burritos are cheap and taste great. Lack of vegetables makes me sad, but I'd pick this place over chipotle.

Hey La Burrita, check out out my new friend:  Fatty's Taco Shop, as it would translate to in spanish.

By the four stars, you know the burritos are good, so I'm going to start with the sauce. They have two the verde and rojo. The thing about sauce is that it could, on its own, be amazing, but the true test comes from how well it pairs with the burrito. And lemme tell you they are like match made on match .com. lol 

The tortilla is like 1 part flour, 2 parts butter, and 5 parts softness. It. It's so light, you feel like you went down a pant size. Speaking of pant size, the meat is quite tender. Make sure you ask for cheese, they melt it onto the tortilla before they add all the ingredients. 

So, the one bonus over chipotle for the ladies, is that they have both super and regular burritos based on you appetite. Not to be sexist, but a majority of my lady friends usually only finish half a chipotle burrito. So this is a great alternative. Moreover, they don't serve the fake mexican,  white rice with cilantro. But rather real mexican rice with all the seasonings one would find in the la ciudad de Mexico. 

So, go be a fatty and don't ever let anybody tell you that you can't have your burrito and eat it too!

Large portions, cheap prices.  A little heavy on the salt (I get weirdly thirsty after eating their burritos) and could use some more "fresh" flavor for some liveliness (cilanto/lime/lettuce, etc. although their chile verde is fine on this front).  Much better than La Burrita.  The guy rolling up my burrito stuffed it so much that the tortilla split  all the way down and it was all sad and awkward.  He rolled it up in another tortilla though (double cheese!), so it was all good.

Think the one on college & in the city are  still better, but maybe that's just because the other two are older and have a more authentic vibe. This one's just too clean and Chipotle-espe to seem legit. =)

It's still pretty good though. Carnitas.. yum.

Unfortunately, two stars less than before. 

I visited Gordo today because I was craving Mexican food. I ordered one pint of guacamole and a carnitas burrito with hot sauce. Except I could not taste the hot sauce AT ALL. AND the carnitas was not flavorful. 

BUT... the guacamole was absolutely divine. Maybe I should just get a guacamole burrito next time!

I live around the corner from this place so I had to try it out when it opened.  First trip, I had a burrito and honestly, NOT a fan.  I actually reviewed this place as 2 stars.

Then, in a weak moment, I went again but tried the taco based on what I saw others ordering. THAT was the moment I started enjoying Gordo's!  Just avoid their ricey dishes, its bland and filling without a lot of taste I think.  However, if you go for more proteins, its great. A little on the heavy/greasy side, but really good. I also recommend their quesadilla's...I don't order those anywhere else, but essentially their giant versions of their taco's.

Growing up in Albany, I have allegiance to Gordo's as the standard spot to get my burrito, but even though this one should be the same somehow it was not as satisfying. I asked for black beans in my burrito and when the guy who assembled my burrito put pintos in, the initial guy who took my order definitely looked me in the eye, knowing it was wrong/checking if I was paying attention, but decided not to remedy the situation if I didn't complain, which I didn't. Still, he should've at least asked me if it was okay instead of simply hoping I wouldn't notice. They also messed up my friend's order. Sounds silly, but the cleanliness and newness of the space seems unnatural and also does not agree with the small, greasy Gordo's of my childhood.

Do you ever walk on Telegraph Ave under the blistering sun, wishing that Peet's didn't charge almost $5 for that one freddo you really like?

Gordo Taqueria has agua frescas for just over a dollar, available in flavors ranging from strawberry (my personal favorite), pineapple, watermelon, and horchata (and if you're like one of my friends, you mix horchata with strawberry *barf*). The cup is also the size of  Starbucks large (you'll never make me say venti, bastards)!! Stay thirsty my friends.

From now on, I am going to Gordo instead of Chipotle. I like how they offer two sizes, regular and super-burrito (which is like your big Chipotle burrito). Sometimes you just don't want to stuff yourself with a huge burrito, so the smaller one is a good option. 

Besides that, Gordo is slightly cheaper than Chipotle and the flavors are more authentic. I've had excellent chili verde and carnitas burritos.

Now that they've opened up a location on Telegraph, this has become my go to burrito place in Berkeley.

The super burritos are gigantic and are definitely worth 5 bucks. I usually get carnitas with everything, including sour cream and guac. I think it's kinda weird how they apply the cheese, putting a block of it on the tortilla before it gets steamed, but it works. 

I've never ordered the tacos, but they look gigantic. Also, I've had many recommendations for the all meat burrito. 

I've eaten here 3 days in a row before, so worth it. 

There are no legit, SD style mexican places in berkeley, but this hits the spot when youre craving a big burrito.

Finally. You'd think that Berkeley would have had a good burrito spot sometime earlier this century. Detractors, don't even bother. La Burrita is the height of mediocrity, and Chipotle barely counts as Mexican food. Mario's sucks, and it was still better than most. Gordo is cheap, delicious (HOT SAUCE), quick, and close to campus. Win on all counts.

Service: 4
Taste: 5
Quality: 5
Variety: 3
Price: $5-10
Recommend to a friend: Yes

Gordo's is still open! Yay! I've tried their burritos, but I am a super fan of their quesadillas. With carnitas, if you can eat pork. Otherwise, their chicken is pretty good too. You can also grab a Jarritos (Mexican soda) -- my favorite flavor is limon.

So where do I even start about their quesadillas.... Be aware that you will be eating a lot of calories. They put a slice of white cheese on a tortilla and then begin to fry it with some oil on the grill. This melts the cheese and gives the tortilla a crisp on the outside. I get the carnitas (super flavorful!) with tomato salsa and the hot salsa. You can get sour cream and guacamole for extra $ but I think it's sufficient without it. Please use a knife and fork when eating this quesadilla. It's basically made for knife and fork usage. But also make sure not to eat the foil under it, as you'll find yourself scarfing this bad boy down in a flash.

First off, I created a Yelp account just to give this place a bad review. 
Ill start off by telling you that the workers are terrible. They slopped beans and tomato salsa on my burrito before I could tell them that I didn't want either. On top of being difficult to hear and understand, the workers seem frustrated and peeved when you ask too many questions. But it is hard not to ask questions since their method of applying cheese to the burrito is completely unprecedented. They melt cheese slices onto the tortilla unlike every other Mexican restaurant the sprinkles grated cheese into the burrito. In addition, they meat (I've tried the dried-out beef, and the salty, oily carnitas) has little flavor, if any. Instead, you have to rely on their hot sauce, which too lacks much flavor and spice. 
Ultimately, your left with a bad-tasting burrito, and poor customer service that tastes even worse.

I have been to every Gordo. I like them all. I suppose this one isn't the best. Why isn't it the best? I don't know. Maybe because I ate here alone.

What is good about Gordo? The tortilla isn't like chewing on shoe leather, for starters. In fact, it's perfect: fat slices of cheese are melted into the tortilla, vacuum-sealing all of the warm contents within, presenting a burrito with the consistency of a banana. 

I will say this: I am not a college student. I am thirty-two god darn years old. I was in downtown Berkeley purely on accident.

My reason for writing this review for this particular Gordo -- and not the Gordo on College -- is because of the precise location of this Gordo:

If you are in downtown Berkeley and you are even thinking about going to the Chipotle across the street from Gordo, you should probably go to a psychiatrist first. Then you should probably go back to school -- there's a fairly nice one of those a few blocks away.

Yay!

Maybe I dont know what real burritos are suppose to taste like but I wasnt too impressed with Gordos. I guess I am used to all the stuff that comes in chipotle burritos, so I found Gordos to be missing something (the sour cream that I didnt want to pay extra for, or maybe the extra lettuce and corn I always ask for at chipotle) 

The guacamole texture was funny. I would find huge chunks of avocado and random huge chunks of tomato and onion. I prefer the onion and tomato to be diced and evenly mixed in.

The meat was soaked in what looked like water so it didnt look very appetizing or fresh. 

I got the super burrito thinking I could take half of it home since according to some reviewers, I could split it in half with another person. I didnt find it that big, and only took less than 1/4 home which I ate as a snack later. 

Overall, I wasnt too impressed so I'll stick to chipotle when I am looking for a burrito. I might come back to try the quesadillas and tacos

YUM!

I just got back from visiting my friends and this was one of the places they took me. They obviously are obsessed with this place, as their dog is named...Gordo. Fantastic, reasonably priced burritos. Everything tasted super fresh and I loved the selection of tortillas. After hiking around campus for a few hours, the burrito definitely hit the spot. I went with the carnitas, which the burrito maker chopped up fresh in front of me. 

If I'm in the area again, I will be stopping by!

Gordo's is great! I've never really been a fan of Chipotle's (perhaps I just don't know how best to furnish my burritos, but I find theirs bland and unappetizing, albeit filling), but I love the strong burst of savory flavor that Gordo's supplies. I usually order a carnitas burrito with guacamole here and have not yet regretted my decision. I hadn't noticed until reading some other comments, but it's true that your server doesn't use gloves. However, the food is very efficiently prepared and wrapped, and I'm sure it's not a big issue in any case. Of course, the price is quite nice, as well.

I've been to two Gordo locations: College and Telegraph. The winner of the two? Might just have to be this place. 

I actually thought there was a line out the door that extended to the end of the block but it turns out that line was for Melt. I'm glad there's a location here because it's easy for those who are on their way to campus or just shopping nearby. 

I ordered two crispy carne asada tacos with everything on top. Please just try this one! The shell isn't as crispy as your thinking at Taco Bell, but of course, this is freshly made crispy! The biggest down fall of this place is the cost. But the fact that they give you generous portions make up for it somewhat. Seating is plentiful not like the limited seating you find on College but you can always just grab and go. It's small enough to just eat out of your hand, but it might get a little messy. My biggest concern is the price. Two crispy tacos cost more than one super burrito. So I'm starting to reconsider my options next time. 

I'll be coming back around here if I get that mexican food craving again!

filling burritos
less flavor than chipotle
but also costs less

I didn't know Gordo was on Telegraph. Therefore, I was pleasantly surprised this morning when running into one. Forget the pizza, I want a burrito!

The (black) bean and cheese with sour cream, cheese and guacamole has always been my favorite. Add hot sauce and I was a happy camper.

YUUUUUM. 4.5 stars

This place is a great alternative for people living on southside of Berkeley and are sick of always getting La Burrita (whose burritos are meh) and Chipotle (which I still get random cravings for sometimes, but definitely can't have more than once a week). 

I got the Super Beef Burrito and it was sooo good. You get so much steak and the burrito is huge! It's also very reasonably priced at around $5-6 dollars. Inside, there's way more seating than there is at Chipotle or La Burrita. There's also many kinds of salsa on the side (I'm quiiiite a sucker for salsa.)

Hmm I wonder if they have loyalty/membership cards here? That would definitely draw me away from the other burrito places...hehe.

In my opinion, this place definitely gives some competition to both La Burrita and Chipotle.  Its in the same general area, and the target audience for all three is broke college students.  Gordo's accomplishes a difficult feat:  it's extremeley quick, affordable, and tasty.  In terms of speed, this place is like an assembly line for burritos; you walk in and order and pay at the front, with most patrons opting for togo.  Their seating area is limited.  Its very affordable.  For just north of five dollars, you can get a loaded burrito including specialties like guac or sour cream.  Now, in my opinion, this place trumps both Chipotle and La Burrita in taste.  Maybe its just because their turnover rate is so quick, but I feel like the meats always taste substantially richer in flavor and freshness.  Also, Chipotle has almost an 'Americanized' Mexican flavor feel to it, while I would compare Gordo's taste to the taco trucks in downtown LA.

PROTIP:  Get the burrito bowl!  Huge portions and you can save it for later if you don't finish.
5 Stars, 2 enthusiastic thumbs up! Best burritos EVER!! Highly recommend Gordo's.

Came here twice, once when I first saw it and once with my friend who is absolutely obsessed with this place (he basically wet himself when I texted him that one had opened close to UC campus). 

There isn't really a better way to describe this place other than Big Cheap Burrito or "BCB."

- BIG: The super burritos are very large. They will fill you up. Even if you are very hungry. YAY!
- CHEAP: The normal burrito is 5 bucks, the super is around 6. If this isn't cheap, then I don't know what is.
- BURRITO: It's what you usually eat at Mexican Taquerias.

bonus: the chairs don't make you feel like a giant sitting on a child's stool as they aren't ridiculously tiny and old and saggy like the ones at the College Ave. Gordo's. (but if you're into that kind of thing you should go there instead).

Overall: solid burrito, don't expect anything fancy or gourmet, but you really won't be disappointed here.

A good, cheap(er) burrito. A regular burrito here does not come with sour cream, cheese, or guacamole, which each cost about $.50 extra, so you get a smaller burrito (compared to other burritos around Berkeley) for a cheaper price. Still a deal, and still a decently large meal.

Taste is great! The meat is tender and the tortilla really molds around the contents of the burrito, preventing the insides from falling out and loosening while eating.  I love that the burrito is completely warm and fully "melted" on all sides.You really get a uniform, well-mixed taste throughout the burrito, instead of chomping on some lettuce for a bit before finally discovering the meat later. I wish their salsa had more taste, but I only tried mild and medium.

Service is efficient, though they workers don't really smile or make an effort to. The restaurant itself is just okay; there are always a few flies flying around the entrance, but other than that everything is pretty well kept. NOTE: seats are a little hard to sit in, they are more like woven backless stools

WILL I come back: yes!
WHEN will I come back: when I'm not too hungry but want something cheesy, meaty, and filling
WHAT will I do differently: get spicier salsa...if I dare :O

NOTE: the reason I give Gordo's 4 stars not 3 is because their flexible ordering system allows you to order a cheaper burrito with the minimum burrito contents, but also allows you to order more for more money. EXAMPLE:  Chipotle has a set price for their burritos, so you feel obligated to get everything in your burrito to make it worth your money, even if you aren't that hungry. I enjoy the flexibility at Gordo's

Summary based on 1 visit at this location and a zillion visits at other Berkeley/Albany locations:
--great ! carnitas regular burrito.  Maybe it was toward the end of the day, but the carnitas was the best ever.
--good service with guys I recognized from other locations.  Cashier was new, but fine.
--terrible Telegraph parking
--bathrooms!
--large dining area

My friends told me about the new opening here after I returned from break. I decided to try it out with no expectations, really. I ordered the steak burrito which was slightly filling. It was pretty cheap; my regular burrito came out to $4.77. This is one of the few Mexican restaurants that I've came across that doesn't give you free chips! Even the ghetto Mexican burrito place in Bear's Lair gives you complimentary chips for free!

Overall, the restaurant is nice and  fairly clean. How long will that last? I don't know. Situated on Telegraph, I wouldn't imagine it to last. There were already fruit flies flying around. As others have mentioned, there are bathrooms!

If I was in the mood for a burrito, my ranking goes as followed (for south of campus):  1. Cafe Durant 2. Chipotle 3. La Burrita 4. Gordo 5. Panchos (check my Panchos review for why Panchos is ranked so low).

Gordo's is the best burrito near campus.

Yes, my fellow Cal Bears. I mean better than La Burrita and Chipotle. The burritos are not so small that they're not filling, yet not too big that they fall apart and cause a mess. More importantly, they taste amazing. Gordo never fails to remind me of being home in the city. It's a classic example of The San Francisco Burrito.

I usually just get a regular (or Super, if I'm feeling extra ambitious) chicken burrito. Unlike Chipotle, Gordo melts a slice of cheese onto the tortilla instead of just sprinkling it in along with the other ingredients. Trust me, that alone makes a world of difference. And don't forget to get an agua fresca or horchata with your burrito!

Typically, I'm not a HUGE Mexican food fan- kind of blasphemous for a SoCal girl-- but I really loved this place!

First of all, I was surprised that I'd never heard of it, especially since it's located so close to campus (Channing & Telegraph). The burritos are pretty decently priced and you get a good amount for what you pay for! And aside from the practicality, the food is downright delicious! I ordered the Beef Burrito, which was chock full of steak, beans and guacamole. Love it so much that I might drop by and get the Super Beef Burrito next time!

My only complaint is that it's a little difficult to order. I don't know if it was just me, but the servers are really hard to understand (and they speak so gosh darn FAST!).

Oh Gordo's you are so good! Although you fill me up and make me feel like a little gordita when I leave, I love you oh so much!

This taqueria is by far THE best one in Berkeley. From their veggie, to chicken, carnitas, chile verde burritos and quesadillas, it's all mouth watering and scrumptious. You won't leave a crumb on your plate, I can guarantee that.

Not only are they inexpensive, you get a great sized portion, even if you just get a regular size. They have delicious horchata (try some!) and they do take credit cards. Their location is very convenient, right on Telegraph, there is plenty of seating inside, staff is smiling and friendly, and you can order in or take it to go.

ps- try their guacamole, it's amazing!
pss- Hey Gordo's, you know how you could get me love you even more than I already do?....get a sauce bar! :)

Gordo's lives up to anyone's expectations for a Mexican Taqueria. The food is cheap and tasty, and the place is kept very clean. You can eat here for dirt cheap by ordering a super burrito for $6 and splitting it with a buddy. Throw in some chips, and you've got a filling meal for $3 bucks a piece! 

Gordo's is a nice addition to the UC Berkeley Southside, and all my college buddies and I are raving about finally having a good quality Mexican Taqueria. This place is always a joy to have a meal at, and I've yet to leave unsatisfied.  Also, the place is very quick to prepare your food, so it's the perfect place to stop in if you're starving! Enjoy!

I'm like'n Jennifer W.s' Yelp, so I stopped off at Gordo's on my way home from campus.

Gordo's is a welcome addition to "Tele." Nice and clean without the weird chairs that haunt the College Ave store. [Updated: Same weird chairs, just new & not sagging]. The bathroom is spank'n clean too and let's all hope it stays that way. Since the majority of food is eaten by hand, this is important. The tables have plenty of napkins so you can wipe your "mug" with a clean one after each bite!

Gordo's is always consistent, not matter what store you choose. It's not Cancun, it's not Picante, it's better than Chipotle, it's not a health risk like another taqueria up the street, and you don't spend $8-10 for your food and fountain soda. Quick and tasty, the $5 reg. burritos are always a value.

The only competition will be on Tuesday Taco Night at Larry Blakes and it's only because they have a liquor license.

GORDO OPENING! All the same food from your favorite location, except in a clean, brightly-lit, and contemporary-looking building at 2404 Telegraph Avenue. There are a good amount of small tables for seating. There are restrooms here too! Not too many staffed, but probably because school is not in session.

There's something about coming here that just doesn't feel right.

It's probably the fact that I'm still conflicted because my original Gordo is the one on Geary in the city, but since my brother doesn't live in the Richmond District anymore, there's no real reason for me to go out there except for nostalgia's sake, so instead, I go to the 9th Avenue Gordo.  That's fine--and I actually like being in that one better, even though ain't nothing like the real thing, baby; you never forget your first time; I'd rather live in his world/Than live without him in mine; etc. etc.  (And no, I'm not gay.  Sorry, guys.)

So I'm further conflicted because this is a new Berkeley Gordo.  The original Berkeley one, which I hope still exists, is on College; and I've never been there.  But I kind of want to go because Patty P. wrote some interesting things about it, and I miss Patty P.  She hasn't written a review in so long.

But the Gordo on Telegraph.  It's a spectacular Gordo, really.  The food, ordering, and preparation are exactly what you've come to expect and love.  And even though the people working here weren't any of the regulars I recognize at both the Geary and 9th Avenue locations, they have similar builds.  It must be all that free or discounted carne asada.

The seating area is huge.  I took mine to go, so I didn't get to experience it, but it was strangely empty even though it was 12:45 and there were a bunch of people out enjoying the beautiful summer day.

So Berkeley does have decent burritos, and if I really want one, it's not that far from work.  OK, maybe it is, but I'm really lazy, so it's not.

First off, I'm not a vegetarian, but my parents are, and I've had my fair share of vegetarian "meat". Having said that, I was very curious to try the burgers here at Saturn because this place is famous for serving all vegetarian (and some vegan) food. I love the atmosphere of the restaurant; waiters are extremely friendly and down-to-earth, the decorations were hip and although I saw glitter and pink everywhere, it wasn't kitschy at all. After our meal the manager/owner also came by to chat with us for a bit, even though the place was really busy (we came for lunch on a Friday).
