Now, the food: I got the guacamole burger and my sister got the california burger. Both were DELICIOUS. I got a cup of tomato bisque with mine, and it was thick, creamy and really filling. The sweet/tartness of the soup balanced my guacamole burger really well. The burgers come open-faced so you have to put your two sides together. Mine had heaps of salsa and guacamole so I had to spread it out with a knife before I could layer it all together. The combination is great! The patty reminded me of chicken, even though the texture was very soft and tofu-like. We were both too full after our meal but we'll be back to try the desserts! They open until midnight so if I'm craving something sweet I know where to go, haha.

Drove in on a rainy weekday for a 1pm lunch. Snagged the first two hour parking spot I saw on Allston way, which is a few blocks away. The parking spots closer are 90 minutes or less. 

We were seated promptly but the service was slow. It was a quiet afternoon and there was only one spacey server. The short server's response to a question about a special was, "I'm not sure, it's a new special." Hmm. It's part of your job to know what your restaurant is serving isn't it? And if not, maybe be proactive and at least offer to ask the chef? 

Ordered up a vegan cheeseburger and the portobello sandwich with tomato soup. Food was ok. The portobello sandwich comes in strips instead of a full uncut mushroom so be prepared for a structurally unstable sandwich. I recommend cutting in half before attempting to pick up and eat so you're not chasing food with your mouth. Vegan cheeseburger nothing special. 

Spacey waitress charged the wrong price for my "special." I just deducted from her tip rather than explain math to her.  

Not really worth going out of my way for, but if I'm in the area it's a safe vegan/vegetarian option.

Comfort food at it's best. An old school (vegetarian) diner, complete with a full breakfast/brunch, lunch and dinner menu that includes burger, fries, and decadent milkshakes (most things can be made Vegan).

This place took me back to my childhood, when I enjoyed the Jetstones while I ate a superb club sandwich. I loved the decor and the full vegetarian menu. Service is still inexperienced but friendly, I'm sure they will improve over time.

Good vegetarian/vegan place with a great selection and enjoyable food. A friend of mine was visiting the area and so I decided to take her here.

Atmosphere: straight up out of a 50s diner. It's adorable. The booths have themed decorations - ours was a picnic table =). When the host sat us, he was like "Do you know who Sarah Silverman is? Well, she sat at this table last night." Good to know, man.

Food: My friend ordered the Vegan Banana Walnut Pancakes and I opted for the "Chicken" Avocado Sandwich with Fakin' Bacon. My sandwich was tasty but nothing too amazing - I applaud them for really good veggie meat though! The thin cut fries are really delicious and crispy as well - and they give you A LOT of it, which is cool. My friend enjoyed her pancakes, and although I didn't try them, they looked good and HUGE. About $10 a plate isn't bad for what you're getting either.

Service: Service was average. The day I went, however, the computer shutdown and they were only taking cash, which is out of their control. 

Overall: It's a nice casual place to get some good vegetarian and vegan food, and I'd recommend it.

What a fun and funky place to grab a bite to eat! Pretty decent food, but don't order too many dishes - portions are huge (and vegan doesn't necessarily mean "healthy"). Enjoyed the nacho fries and the milkshakes. Would recommend this place to anyone and look forward to bringing friends/family/visitors here in the future.

I've stopped here for dessert a couple of times and they always seem to be out of something I want. Mostly the mud pie, I think. The one time I managed to get the mud pie, I thought it was rather small but pretty good. The milkshakes and fries are still pretty standard, too. Food's still okay. 

The service, though, has definitely gotten worse, I think... I've sat on sticky seats, and one time I went they didn't even have enough menus? We sat around with no menus for a good ten minutes. When we finally flagged down a waitress for a menu, she was kind of rude about it too, not apologetic at all. I don't know what happened so I can't sympathize, but I was pretty annoyed regardless!

I was so excited when I found out Saturn had opened in Berkeley. I've been there numerous times, solo and with friends (veg and non-veg). I've eaten at this location numerous times in recent months.

Pros:

 - selection of vegetarian and vegan options
 - ice cream (vegan and dairy options)! 
 - open late
 - downtown Berkeley location is convenient to access via transit
 - portobello mushroom burger with fries is delicious.
 - even when they've seemed busy, I haven't had to wait for a table
 - wait staff are always friendly
- service is usually prompt


Cons

- too much soy: the majority of entrees have some form of soy protein (not necessarily tofu). It's unnecessary and makes eating out very difficult for the increasing number of us who have soy allergies.

- they aren't set up to answer questions about ingredients (for example, when trying to avoid certain foods due to allergies). The staff are friendly and very willing to try to find out, but there doesn't seem to be an ingredient list readily available for all the entrees.

Hard to beat a vegetarian diner.  Sometimes I just want regular food without the animal products.  
Fakin' Bacon, Lettuce, and Tomato sandwich.  Muffinator (a veg version of the McD breakfast muffin sandwich).  Salads and club sandwiches.  Good basic diner fare without the meat.
The service can be a bit relaxed.  Portions are generous.

I didn't get to buy the CampusCred deal last semester for Saturn Cafe since I didn't know about it. But my friend from Harvard visited me during her spring break yesterday and I chose Saturn Cafe because I got a 20% off card from the PLAYGreen Festival and I wanted to eat vegetarian food. 

Upon entrance, you'll feel a fusion of Mel's Drive-in and pink. That's a pretty good way to describe it. The dining room wasn't full but we still had to wait to be seated. Our server was really kind and patient. It took us a bit of time to familiarize with the menu items. I've never ordered from a full vegetarian/vegan menu. I was choosing between the jalopeno burger and the space cowboy. I decided on the jalopeno burger with steak fries. My friend got one of the omelette with garlic potatoes and toast. 

The food took a while to cook so we chatted for a bit. There is free wi-fi but you have to ask the server for the password. Our server gave us the wrong password and I had to ask another for the correct one. Weird how neither AirBears nor at&t wi-fi from Starbucks reaches Saturn Cafe even though I can access AirBears at the ACTransit bus stop on Shattuck and Allston. The wi-fi access is valid for one hour. 

The food finally came and mine looked pretty appetizing. I was finally going to eat some imitation meat. It was tasty, yet messy since it was a tall burger. I like to put fries in my burger so I stuck some in there for some additional height. I couldn't keep the burger together so I had to split it in half to eat. The portions were appropriate. my friend couldn't finish her omelette but I was able to finish my plate. I had to ask to refill water several times but other than that, no peeves. Our total was $18 with discount and tip.

I'm a new vegan in the Berkeley area and I have to say, this restaurant meets almost all of my expectations for what a vegan wants in taste and adherence to vegan qualities, even if it's mainly a vegetarian restaurant.

Been here multiple times already - their brunch selection is great (scrambled tofu!) and their jalapeno burger is amazing! However, after eating that burger their other burgers just don't seem to compare..

Service is great - one time we waited 30 minutes and they ended up giving us our vegan nachos for free. They came in periodically to check up on us and to tell us how things were going.

Would get 5 stars if their cupcakes weren't so fluctuant in taste! I loved their zucchini and carrot cupcake, but the other ones were too sweet.

Great place when you want a friendly, casual place to enjoy some casual type cuisine. Long-time customer of their Santa Cruz location and have been to their Berkeley location several times, as well.  I'm a big fan of their veggie burgers, vanilla and peanut butter shakes (the chocolate is good) and their amazing garlic fries.  Their vegan cupcakes are absolutely delicious. Gimme a shake and fries and I'll be quite happy until they're all gone.  I'm glad they've come to Berkeley, and that they listened to their customers who filled out comment cards asking for more vegan options.

I came here with a friend because I had a $20 for $10 groupon.
We ordered the half order of vegan nachos, saturn spuds, and the hot and spicy omelet. 
The food took forever to come, but the waiters were all friendly and came by to refill our water every 10 minutes. 
When the food came, it was already lukewarm/cold. They waited for all the food to be ready before they brought it over, which is weird because I don't understand why they didnt bring the nachos out first.
The food itself was whatevs. It's kinda pricey, so I don't think I will come here again unless I have another groupon.

Totally awesome diner food! As a vegetarian it came as an amazing surprise that all the food here was vegetarian and even vegan (some of it) friendly. They have vegan milkshakes and nachos. I suppose all of this isn't quite as exciting if you're not a vegetarian or vegan but anyway, it's very, very exciting if you are since diners are awesome but not usually that veggie friendly. This place has a great vibe and is open late. I had a great salad and some nachos. Tried a shake too which was yummy.

YES. I give Saturn five stars, because for the entirety of my month long vegan pledge, it was the one place I could depend upon for a delicious, filling meal. I always got the vegan spuds for brunch and the waiter was so attentive, he got my soymilk for my coffee without me having to request it! Impressive service- and this was the case every time I returned here. The food doesn't disappoint either- their scrambled tofu is ridiculously good (has a curious egg-y flavor) and their rosemary rubbed roasted potatoes are HEAVENLY. Go try them. You won't regret it.
I love the funky, eclectic decor, and while I'm not a fan of the hot pink walls, it certainly went with the theme. My friends and I loved the 'Audrey Hepburn' tabletop, full of clippings, pictures, and make up from an older, glamorous era. Love this place and I'm going back here for brunch soon!

super tasty veggie burgers! get a sampling of 4 different types with an order of sliders. So very good.  This is not your hippie dippy bullshiz kinda place. This is an American diner that happens to not serve meat. It's great. I've gone twice so far and the food and service have been great. There's a large menu too which is different for a veggie place. I love it.  Oh my one complaint is that it is pricey for the burgers. $10. I'd come here for lunch once a week if they were $6. Oh well.

I went to Saturn Cafe on New Year's day around three in the afternnon and it was pretty crowded (15 minute wait). I was with my family because I wanted to see what Berkeley's campus was like and across the street from the entrance of the school was this weird-but-cool diner. 

We waited about 30 minutes to get our food and they looked like they were short staffed (well it was New Year's) but my breakfast burrito was worth the wait. My mom ordered some fries which were amazing!
They have a great menu, especially for brunch.

Saturn Cafe's a cool place and I would definitely go back again.

OMG I love Saturn Cafe, and was so excited when they decided to open a location here in the bay area! I was able to go in and eat last week, what a beautiful space very much like the Santa Cruz Saturn's style except they stepped it up a bit, very classy, I love the retro 50's diner style concept they applied to a vegetarian cafe, such an amazing concept. The food matches the atmosphere, my party of 4 shared a generous helping of nachos, yes I love my cheese but they do offer a vegan option, for those who don't do the dairy. They actually offer a lot of vegan options, I flounder between being a veg and vegan so I love that they're is a place that serves both. I've always thought the classic diner food served from a vegetarian/vegan perspective to be innovative and inspired. I got my regular Cowgirl Blues Ranch salad, and it was spot on, in fact everyone in my party said they're food was delicious and was exactly the way they remembered the Saturn cafe on they're trips to Santa Cruz. All in all, I am just happy to have them in Berkley! Saturn Cafe is an excellent and unique addition to all the great eating establishments in the bay area. Five Stars they deserve it, it is obvious they have worked very hard to match and even out-do the Santa Cruz location. I'd say to any naysayers give the place a chance, make suggestions to the management if you have one, before you yelp. It's only been open a week seriously give them some time to let the dust settle. I wanna see this place thriving, so be happy for them and us, we now have a nice environment, to share quality vegetarian food with our families and friends. They seem to have an awesome staff and once the basic first few week kinks are out, I am sure the service will be as good as the Santa Cruz location. No doubt in my mind this place is gunna be a hit!

I had a Pulp Fiction moment when I ordered my 6.00 milkshake.

As a vegan, this is something I had only dreamt about.





It was worth every penny.

I feel like i'm being VERY generous with 4 stars. I feel a 3.5 is in order.

Their nacho fries and their shakes are whats up. Really tasty. But I give them a four because they're the only vegan diner joint. I dig that. But as a vegan. I expect them to up their game.  I also recommend their salads. You get a HUGE plate of awesome greens. Just tell them to grill the tofu a bit. Im not too into raw tofu myself.

Oh! The fries are delectable! I know...they're just fries but they're hella good.

Come here to eat some all right vegan foods.

-The service was great, friendly and attentive
-cute decor and staff, must have great style to work there!
-the food was just okay, hence the 3 stars.

I'd come back to this place for the ambiance over the food. Check out the website and that pretty much sums up what the place is going to look like.  

I ordered a Portobello Burger and substituted the fries for sweet potato fries. It was hella expensive if you ask me. An extra $2.50 to substitute and the burger was already $9.50. 

For dessert we split a Mini Madness which is completely chocolate overkill.  Its one thing to try to please chocolate lovers, it's another thing to want to make someone feel sick. 

Being a meat eater, I don't find it worth paying so much for vegetables and fake meat. My vegetarian friend (which is the reason why we ate here) found it to be good so if you're a vegetarian go ahead and try this place out but prep your wallet cus it ain't cheap.

Service was very good, as was the soup of the day-- a Moroccan  bean stew.  However, the soup came with white sandwich bread, and the house salad was unimaginative with sesame vinaigrette that was completely flavorless.  The vegan nachos were again flavorless, even with jalapenos on them, and the accompanying salsa without any heat at all.  The chips seemed stale, as well.

Don't get me wrong, i love my meat, but Saturn's cafe is so good that all non-vegetarian people should go for it. It's so much healthier and the atmosphere of the restaurent is very creative and retro. 

I ordered a burger, the fries were really good, and the burger actually tasted like a burger, even better than the burgers from Jupiter Restaurent. After my meal, i ordered a milk shake, they even give you the shaker that they make it in, so you basically have almost two milk shakes. 

The great thing is that they are opened till midnight, so it's perfect for late outings. I gave it a 3 stars just because there weren't that many choices.

OMG! The chicken avocado sandwich! I love that sandwich! They have the best vegetarian meat I've ever tried. The first time I ate at a Saturn Cafe was in Santa Cruz, and I loved their sandwich. 
Their prices are moderate, but if you want good vegetarian meat, then this is the place.

What a cool surprise finding this gem in Berkeley. I've eaten at the Santa Cruz location many times and found this one quite similar. I got a portabelo sandwich on Saturday which was stunning. I got mushroom on top of sandwich. I agree with assessment:

More Vegan Options
Add Daiya Cheese for lots of vegan treats!
Add Gardein products

A nifty vegetarian dinner at a great location in Berkeley? I'm definitely a fan! 

I've been to Saturn Cafe several times and have always walked away with a nice, full belly and a box of leftovers. I'm always impressed by the menu. Always takes me forever to decide. The Heavenly Benedict is simply heavenly. The Chicken Avocado Club is another of my favorites. So delicious and filling. The Sampler appetizers are huge! Bring your friends! 

The staff are friendly, but not the most attentive. Seems like they might need a few more servers. When it's crowded, it takes forever to get the check. Probably not the best place to come when you're starving or in a rush.

I'm a fan of the interior decor of Saturn, but not a fan of the crumbs that are accumulating around the edges of the glass on the larger tables. Also, is it just me or are some of the seats a little sticky?

Yay!! I was so excited to hear my favorite Santa Cruz vegetarian diner was opening up another one in Berkeley. I've been going to the Santa Cruz location for almost 20 years and was skeptical that the new one in Berkeley could stand up. But it did. The chai was spot on, the house-made burger still one of my favorites, and the service was super friendly and efficient. 

I'm going to be a regular for sure.

Good food but the rude server refuses to warm up my soy milk for me which makes me sad because their coffee is so strong.  I tried the buck rogers burger (vegan) and the vegan huevos rancheros, as well as the fries and the ranch sauce.  Everything has been amazing so far.  Oh and I tasted the seasonal pumpkin pancakes and those were also equally mouth watering.

You know that saying about how actions speak louder than words? If that were the case and I were to write a review of actions in regards to my experience at the Saturn Cafe, the only things you'd be able to hear would've been my friend and my groaning in edible ecstasy. And I don't know about you, but that would probably kill most people's appetites...

So instead of actions or words doing the speaking on this one, I'm going to let my photos of Saturn do most of the talking. But allow me a few words first before I get on to the fun food photos.

The wait staff are busy. BUSY! Do you get that? They've managed to glue their heads back on and are friendly in spite of running twenty tables each, but they are busy! So for their sake and yours, make sure your order is ready and any accoutrement you might need is ordered at the same time. Otherwise, you might be waiting a bit. 

The food is, in my book (or my plate), mostly phenomenal. You can't go wrong with the super sampler. But you must -- you MUST -- try the chipotle sauce. It is literally one of the best sauces i have ever put into my facehole... The jalapeno burger had a lot of flavors to it and a well-textured veggie patty. And the veggie chicken salad was good (the only thing I would've changed is the tofu-based ranch dressing was on the dull side). They also have the option for milkshakes and microbrews!

What with the lovably kitschy ambiance, I felt like I should've walked in wearing either a poodle skirt, a letterman's football jacket, or a robot costume straight from The Day The Earth Stood Still. The decorators really managed to pack a punch with the 1950's theme. 

As a side note, there's also a room attached to the restaurant that is used for special events such as art exhibits, burlesque shows, poetry and music nights. Lots of good stuff happening at this Berkeley hot spot. 

Now that I've got this review written, I know where I'm going for lunch tomorrow!

I'm following up since apparently my bestie, Anthony H., already wrote a review about our experience. So if I may...

It's true, the vegan nacho fries are a MUST. Three of us split a half-order while we were starving, and were still left wondering how huge a full order would be cuz we sure as hell would not have been able to tackle it. 

I had a vegan California burger (with subbed "meaty" patty..forget what it's called) and it was delicious as always. They don't skimp on the avocado! I had like 6 slices, it was awesommee. For those of you who love avocado and hate how it costs at least $2 extra at restaurants (and you get a tiny slice pshh) know how much you gotta appreciate the extra slices!

I was a little bummed that they were running out of stuff..they ran out of their soup of the day RIGHT before we ordered, so we had to get more fries with our burgers (they went straight into to-go boxes). They also ran out of chocolate vegan ice cream, and there was nothing to make fruit salad with.

However, our server, Andy, still managed to make a chocolate milkshake for us (by using chocolate syrup with vanilla ice cream). He was super obliging and sweet. Actually, all the staff we interacted with were pretty awesome and down to earth. 

The space is really cute and clean. They also have an adjoining little bar/lounge type area, which apparently hosts fundraising events for not-for-profit orgs? God love you, Saturns. I am a little disappointed that they don't have the awesome gender neutral bathroom signs that the SC location has, but at least the bathrooms were clean.

Basically, this place is pretty awesome. Good vegan diner food that's open late? That's enough to make me love a place. But when you add the chill staff, cute space, and vegan nacho fries...really..what more can you ask for?

I went here for a friend's birthday dinner. I was a bit concerned since I am very picky and Saturn Cafe is vegan, but fear not. The food is delicious. There is plenty simple, comfort food along with more gourmet vegan dishes. The mac and cheese is to die for. I will make the trek to Berkeley for their food. The wait staff was a bit inattentive, but nothing to seriously complain about.

Best. Nacho Fries. in Berkeley!!

I CRAVE their nacho fries if I don't get eat them for a couple months - they are humungous servings at only $10! I always have to split it into 2 meals.

Even though this place is vegetarian, even my (meat loving) boyfriend really likes it. They have good brunch food too! I got eggs benedict and it was really good. 

Next time I go, I want to try one of their sandwiches, because they come out STACKED and the servings look huge! I'm definitely using Saturn Cafe as my sole source of vegan-food-trying experiences... 

The only downside and reason I would give this place 4.5 stars rather than 5 is the fact that service is typically reaaaaaally slow, no matter how many people are in the restaurant, so definitely don't come here if you are in a time crunch.

Great "American Food" for us vegetarians.
Love the atmosphere and staff.

Yay for Vegan shakes!!

On a rainy day, my friends and I trudged through the pouring rain, thunder, and lightning just to have a nice junk-food feast at Saturn Cafe. We ordered a full order of Nacho Fries (fries with nacho toppings like beans, salsa, etc) and a Super Sampler (includes fries, sweet potato fries, zucchini sticks, taquitos, and onion rings). There were four of us and we were pretty full and/or satisfied after eating all that. The fries were my favorite part. They were so crispy and delicious. The nacho fries get soggy pretty quickly, so I would recommend eating them up quick! The Super Sampler came with two dipping sauces and we picked ranch and bbq, both very delicious. The taquitos were the only things that were a bit bland and disappointing. But everything else was excellent. Although none of us had any real entrees, but the sandwiches and whatnot at the tables near us smelled pretty good.

Also, the restaurant itself is a pretty cool atmosphere with the glittery columns and pink diner theme. I also saw a sign for karaoke, which could be cool. Overall, I am definitely planning to come back and maybe get the garlic fries and jalepeno poppers this time.

We had a fun time in the private room during a 40th birthday celebration. It was awesome that the birthday boy and others could rock out on amplified instruments in there. Also props to the staff, they had to try to serve us with a bunch of screaming kids running around, and they did a good job.

I had a bunch of beer and some mac and cheese and left happy!

Saturn Cafe is a great vegetarian/vegan restaurant with a fun atmosphere!  The menu is labeled with which items are vegan and which items can be made vegan upon request. Both the service and the food is great! I had been to the Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz and I was excited to hear that one opened in Berkeley.

Two friends and I had dinner there last night and had Andy as our server. He was extremely nice and helpful when any of us had questions. He brought my friends samples of the soup of the day so they could decide what they would like to order.

I ended up ordering:
appetizer - 1/2 Order Vegan Nacho Fries $5.25
Vegan Jalapeno Burger - $9.50
Vegan Vanilla and Peanut Butter Milkshake - $6
(the milkshakes are normally $5.25 and $0.75 to add peanut butter or any other of their add-ins)

The 1/2 order of vegan nacho fries was enough for all three of us to enjoy. It was really good! I would definitely get it again. The jalapeno burger was very good! Just remember that jalapenos are spicy! haha! My milkshake was also very good! It was very thick because i added the peanut butter but that just stopped me from drinking the entire milkshake in 5 minutes! lol

I can't wait to go back! =)

my favorite diner/restaurant in the bay area! i LOVE their pancakes, the vegan milk shakes, and the tofu scramble is awesome. this place takes all my money! 
the waiters and waitresses are super nice, and professional. 
and my drinks always get refilled immediately. 
if you're a vegan or vegetarian, this place has great options.

Not a bad bite for a Vegetarian/Vegan joint.

Although I'm not Vegan, I am mostly a Pescaterian and enjoy eating healthy foods. The burgers here have a lot of flavor and big enough to split. My hubby and I ended up sharing a jalapenio burger with cheese. It was a bit too spicy for me and although the sauce was great, I'm not too big on beans which is why I couldn't give thier burgers a better review because the patties are made out of them. 

We also tried thier coffee milkshake which was thick, rich and creamy. It had a good coffee flavor and was big enough to split.

For me the place was just OK I guess. I wasn't blown away by the food but I might just try it again someday. But if you're somehow that does care for bean burger patties than you most likely will appreciate thier unique presentation and the mixing of flavors.

Zucchini sticks. Fries. Onion rings. 

I could end my review of Saturn Cafe right there. 

Very much a carnivore, I was hesitant about eating at Saturn. But, I was pleasantly surprised. The super sampler was great - taquitos were yummy! Space cowboy and chicken burger: it was okay! Although, I think I will try the salads and sandwiches next time around. Nachos looked good too.

Points for the ranch dressing. I dipped everything I ate that night in ranch.

Saturn has a fabulous diner feel and spot-on service. Check it out!

Fun place! Kinda wish I was in college again, this would be my hang out. The food was good. My friend and I split several items and liked them all. The service and the portions was good too. It is so nice to go a veg only restaurant and know that you won't have to deal with any meat on the menu. Thank you Saturn Cafe, keep up the good work.

An all veggie dinner type place. 
Has several vegan options as well. 

Run down of what I ate-
Appetizer- Japaleno poppers- They are made with cream cheese instead of cheddar. That was a little disappointing but the batter made up for it. Instead of tasting oily and deep fried, the batter gives it a rich taste. I recommend them :)
I tried the chicken club with a half salad half soup. 
The club was awesome. It has "fakin bacon", breaded "chix chicken" and all the fixings. The fake chicken tasted a little to real for me, but the bacon evened the taste out. 
The organic green salad was pretty big. I had it with blue cheese dressing, which i totally recommend. 
The soup that day was pozole. I was surprised that it came close to the taste of traditional Mexican pozole. 
To drink I had the Porter Beer. I believe its an organic beer. It was very smooth, one of the best porters I've had!

All in all its a good option for veggies and vegans alike. I had been searching Berkeley for a fast-food-ish place where I can grab a veggie burger and some fries (other than Smart Alecs). This place answered that search. 

One note- parking is very tricky since it is just one block up from Shattuck, so public trans would be your best option.

OH MY ! I never knew there was a restaurant like this, THANKS TO YELP! my first week of being a vegetarian, I was very hungry and confused on what to eat. First few days, I had veggies & rice only. I was craving for something different so came on yelp to search. Right away, I came here!! I was amazed when I walked in. The place is soooo nice!! I will post pics tomorrow. =) Been here twice in the last few weeks. First time I ordered taquitos, muffinator, and coffee ice cream =) my bf got the california burger which i thought was okay. The Muffinator was yummy though!!! 2nd time, I had the Chicken Avocado Club sandwich which wasn't bad.

Service is not bad at all.. iuno what you yelpers are talking about =) Good thing about this place is that it opens til 12am. WHOOOOO ! it looks like one of those 80's cafe/diners so I feel nice being there.

OOOOO & OMG I want to try the EGG BENEDICT!! it's only served til 4pm sadly =(

I have to give point to Saturn Cafe for being a alternative, healthier option to typical diner food. The restaurant is completely vegetarian and offer vegan options for just about every dish. There are a myriad of dishes, ranging from burgers, salads, "milk" shakes and even stir fries. I appreciated the cool, retro vibe that Saturn's employees and decorations gave. It's definitely a nice, casual place to have enjoy dinner. 

My friends came here on a Friday night, when Saturn was holding a music event in their Saturn lounge. The atmosphere was poppin' and everyone had a good time. I loved the way they decorated their tables. Together, we ordered the California burger? Portabello Mushroom Burger,  Vegan Nachos, Fiesta Salad, Vegan "Milk shakes" and Lev's Original Kombucha. Everything was delicious, although I would say that the salad was overpriced and probably would never order again. The milkshakes were extremely divine, completely made with soymilk; kombucha is a drink made from fermented mushrooms. Despite it not sounding very appetizing, kombucha is a citrus-filled, refreshing drink, similar to champagne. 

Their burgers were juicy, sandwiched between two soft sweet rolls, rather than the typical dense burger bread. Veganaise is used in place of mayonnaise. Furthermore, their thin-cut french fried and sweet potato fries were great. Crunchy on the outside and soft in the inside. Note that although their dishes are vegetarian, it's still diner food (greasy). However, you can feel assured that their cooking methods and ingredients are healthier than typical, greasy diner food. 

I would definitely come here to enjoy some creative, flavorful vegetarian food! Who knows? Maybe you'll be enticed into becoming a vegetarian too :)
Garlic fries are great. And it's great to have an all vegetarian restaurant. Service was fine and portions were generous. But food overall was just ok.

I'll give this place gets four stars for my first visit. Great place to go for the vegan/vegetarian dinning experience! Yummy food, friendly service, (it was saturday afternoon, not that busy) and the waitress wasn't a B*&#$ about splitting the check three ways. 
I definitely will come back for the healthier diner experience as opposed to things like Denny's that is not so vegan/vegetarian friendly.

As a vegetarian I've gotten used to finding a few viable veggie options on a menu and picking from those. Looking at the menu at Saturn never ceases to simultaneously please me and overwhelm me. They not only have typical diner food like burgers, but also things like a peanut sauce dish (that I don't remember the details of) and taquitos. Every time I go I say I need to come again to have something else "next time." I'd be lying if I said I haven't gone more than once in one week. 

With the exception of their tomato soup, I've never eaten anything there I didn't love (and you can ask for a soup sample to avoid this dilemma if you'd like). 

The staff is comprised completely of "hipsters" with tattoos of birds and icecream cones and such who somehow manage to be both friendly and aloof. I wouldn't say the service is always the best or the most friendly, but I wouldn't have it any other way.

Vegetarian diner food! The service is great every time. I L-O-V-E the Cowgirl Blues salad, the BBQ Ranch burger, and the side of Mac 'n Cheese (I imagine the entree-size would be too huge). Husband likes the chicken avocado club. Stay away from the dessert; we had the apple pie and it was a disaster.

Vegetarians need junk food too sometimes. I'm so glad Saturn exists.

There are already almost 200 reviews up for this place, so I'll just add my point of view rather than review.

The service and the food as very hit and miss. While the jalapeño burger tops the heap, other food options are really not very interesting at all. Same can be said of the service - varying from good to bad.

But I suppose that a vegetarian diner is both unique and welcome. I'm happy the place is around but I don't get too excited to visit very often.

Awesome decor, awesome staff, awesome prices, and awesome food! I used to head to Rudy's Can't Fail Cafe in Emeryville for my diner cravings but I will direct my attention towards Saturn Cafe from now on. The "Chicken" Avocado Club Sandwich is a standout and the thin cut fries are perfect. I will definitely be making myself at home here more often.

Well...my second time at Saturn. The service is slow and its shocking how unfriendly the people who work there are. They seems so upset and just pissed off. The food was mehhh...and just more mehh..the only thing I liked is the shakes. I am a vegetarian and I coulda made better food at home.

Awesome vegan shake - I tried the chocolate peanut butter. I'll be back for it!

I also had a salad with the fried soy (which was supposed to taste like chicken). The lettuce and veggies were organic and fresh, and the fried goodies were crispy & delicious.

Organic beer from a Santa Cruz brewery - most light, refreshing, subtly flavored one I've had.

Diner atomsphere with a Berzerk-eley twist.

Great food, great people. Maybe not the place to take your dad or your 45 year old boyfriend (a grump who complained about how loud it is), but for a group of 20 something year olds, this place is perfect. 

I wish it stayed open as late as the original Saturn in Santa Cruz. Nothing like getting a veggie burger and fries after a night of drinking!

I have been to both this location and in Santa Cruz.  I love the sweet potato fries! The salads and the burgers are really good, especially their own patty.  I have tried other entrees and have never been disappointed with the food.  The decor is fun, each table is a conversation starter, especially if your party contains several generations.  My non-veggie parents enjoy meals here when we dine together, they are quite happy, even though there is no meat.  Dad is always impressed that they use bleu cheese in several dishes, it satisfies the cowboy in him.  Just a great little veggie diner, and we will continue to frequent when in town.
yum on shakes, fries and tofu salad. portions are huge though.  i did not finish my salad... prob because I was preoccupied with my vanilla with berry shake and my partner's steak fries.
Great atmosphere, great menu. Plenty of vegan options, too. Must go place if you want a vegan version of classic diner food.

it's nice to have a somewhat late night vegan option close by. the burgers are great. the nacho fries are delicious and the breakfast burrito is tasty.
give the vegan buck sauce a try, you'll be hooked for life.
my two requests would be to have a vegan "chicken" patty and to have daiya cheese for my nacho fries.

Went to this restaraunt while at a conference. The place had great ambiance but was super crowded. The wait was long, and there wasn't enough places to sit for our wait with my large-ish group (11 people). The place was great for what we were looking for, we had a vegitarian in the group and someone who had an allergy to Gluten. I had the baked Mac-N-Cheese, It was just ok, a bit bland, and that the was general concesus with the 3 other people in my group who had the same thing. My sweet potato fries were a bit on the burned side, and were really pricey for a basket of fries if you ask me. The restaurant was just average, but if you are looking for a hip, veggie, Berkeley type restaurant this is the place for you.

I LOVE this place. For someone who is vegan and loves that typical american food Saturns Cafe is one of the best places to go. Their milkshakes, nachos, fries, vegan ranch, burgers...ahh it's all just so good. Only concern is they seem to always have different wait staff there, so I hope that managment is treating them well. And a good portion of the staff seem anti social and boring. For such a fun themed place it is a surprise.

I'm not a vegetarian, but I have to say whatever my "chicken" bbq burger was made of was simply awesome! It was served with a delicious dressing and bbq sauce, and I had the soup of the day - corn with cilantro - and that was a big plus, too. For dessert we shared a coffee ice-cream mud pie and I had trouble 'sharing' it, it was so good. My friend had the cowgirl buger, which she enjoyed and I had some of her crispy fries and they were great. 

I really liked the lay out of the establishment and the staff themselves earned this high rating: they were all friendly, and made sure we were well taken care of. 

I most definitely will be going back!

I came here on a Tuesday night for a friend's birthday dinner.  We had an insanely large group (roughly 22 people) and were seated to another huge birthday group (maybe 15-20) but the staff - besides being understaffed - did a phenomenal job.  Our waiter seriously was awesome.  He kept all our water pitchers filled - was good at communicating with everyone as we worked his way around the table, and dimmed the lights and got the whole restaurant to sing happy birthday to our table!

I like vegetarian food but don't go too far out of my way to check it out, but was curious/excited to try this place.  It did not disappoint.
Ordered a mint milkshake which was UNREAL.  Super thick, minty, chocolate-chippy delight.  Also ordered the jalapeno burger, which had a way above average veggie patty (I believe they make them in house from scratch). The burger had a good spice kick to it.  The sweet potato fries were more sweet potato than fries, which I am in favor of but some others aren't.  I'd say the way to go is the skinny fries  (they also have steak fries).

Long story short, I have to emphasize what a great job they did accommodating such a large party (when there was another one right next to us!).  Everyone at the table loved their food and not a single order was screwed up! Awesome place, can't wait to come back and try more items on the menu.
Love veg-meat, but the food on my first visit (lentil soup and bbq chick'n burger) was only so-so.

I really like Saturn. I come here about 2 times a month, but usually at night when most other places are closed. The service is FANTASTIC, but the reason why I am giving it 3 stars is because the food is good but not amazing. I love that you can get most things vegan, super accommodating and easy.  The burgers are good and I love that you can customize them. Cheese, avocado, special sauce, etc.  I usually come for the Sante Fe salad and the fries (either garlic or sweet potato). The salad is always good, super tasty, but not as fresh (the lettuce) as I'd like it to be. The fries are always fantastic, good old classic fries. The service is great! 

The milkshakes are good, especially the vegan vanilla with peanut butter added, but I wish they had something other than soy! Can you guys do almond milk, rice milk, coconut milk, hemp milk? If you want a vegan dessert its most likely 100% soy, and that's a lot of soy!

A good spot if you want some American style [unhealthy] vegan food. :)  It fills the void!

On a side note, parking over here is very hard to find unless you come late enough. If you come during busy hours, it can take forever, or just not happen... Once we  came on a Friday night, circled for literally 20 minutes, and ended up saying screw it. The area was just too frustrating.

A bit overpriced but a legit vegetarian diner. I was surprised by their chicken patty... it was so delicious, my veggie buddy was not a fan of it.

Didn't get a chance to try their fakin' bacon so that was a shame. Next time. For a non-vegetarian, this place is a good spot for lunch but really not that amazing. Lively decor and nice staff but it really comes down to the food and I definitely have had better. For a vegetarian, this place has the appeal that you can order anything here.

Let's get the complaints out of the way first. There is better and cheaper vegetarian / vegan food in Berkeley. Not that the food is bad, but at $10 a burger, you expect more.The fried things and desserts are all pretty delicious, and their organic salads aren't bad. But all in all the noms underwhelm considering the price.

Also, the tatted / pierced staff demonstrate that non-conformists make pretty frustrating waiters. They're awfully coy- it takes a while to order or get another glass of water, so be careful before you consider that spicy mac and cheese. They also do not hesitate to crank Nirvana at 11 pm on a Sunday. Come now- this is a diner, not 924 Gilman.

So why 4 stars any way? Why do I still love this place? Because:

1. Saturn is like that chick who is so hot she can get away with anything. The decor is absolutely rad. It's transporting. It's everything you'd ever hoped a diner in space would look like and more.

2. They have events that are an awfully refreshing alternative to bars / clubs (see next paragraph).

3. The hours are lovely- they're open until midnight every night.

Since it's loud and with the meh-service you're probably going to be there awhile, I'd say this place is best with a bunch of friends who aren't in a hurry. Make a night of it- they have a lounge area in the back where a few nights each week they host events like live music, comedy, that lovable combination of the two (karaoke), and even the occasional burlesque show (schedule listed at http://spacelounge.saturncafe.com/) .

my sister has been talking about "saturn's great salads" for a while and for some reason i always envisioned Jupiter down the street at the sound of Saturn's (what's one planet over another?).  i must admit i like the concept of an all vegetarian/part vegan DINER. diner food is never mind blowing but i can order anything i want without worries.. AND pretend i'm still a college student. i only had a late night taco salad of some sort, but would love to come back to try a "burger" or "FLT" (fabacon lettuce tomato).

Vegetarians and vegans will love this intergalactic cafe. The ultra cool space theme is noticeable throughout this place. Our server was super knowledgeable and friendly. There was also a book signing in the room adjacent to the restaurant. I tried the Jalepeno Burger which had a good kick to it. It filled me up without giving you the "I just ate a greasy burger" feeling. I can't remember what my friends got but I think they had sandwiches which they also enjoyed. The fries are quite tasty too. I'll be back if I'm craving a vegetarian dish. The prices are reasonable as well.

The new Saturn location in Berkeley does not live up to the standards of their original Santa Cruz location. The restaurant wasn't busy and yet the staff took a long time to take my order and bring me the bill. The Space Cowboy was disappointingly smaller and the slices of tomato weren't fresh. Before they came with my bill, my arm was raised with my credit card in hand. The waiter quickly placed the bill on my table and left without taking my credit card.

Really wanted to like the place with its location and kind of cool  atmosphere, but you generally go to a restaurant for the food, and the food here - at least mine - was really bad.  I ordered vegetable soup and thought it had as much taste as dishwater with a few vegetable thrown in. I couldn't finish it.  My daughter ordered the eggs benedict and was disappointed with everything about it, especially the overcooked yolks.   Would not consider going back.

While Saturn's a quirky place with a 1950-60's ET-diner setting, the food did not deliver. I'm not a vegetarian but many vegetarian only options in Berkeley have been pleasant surprises. Saturn was not. I ordered the Peanut Royale, which was terrible. It was bland, with an abhorrent curry undercurrent and even my friends, avid Saturn Cafe lovers, didn't much care for it. Maybe I should give the place another chance, since it's unfair to judge it based on one entree alone, but it was a big enough flop for me to decide never to come here again. I'm giving it two stars mainly because it's a cute place, but the food is not something I'm ever going to pay for again.

oh my ga!!!! i went nuts here......i love going to a restaurant where everything on the menu is veggie/vegan. the decor is out there and loved our server- very friendly and if he sat down with us and shared some fries, I would not have minded! 

i wont speak for my other friends who were missing a meat burger (tho they did like the fries and shakes and hadnt had meat substitutes before- i think that they are still figuring out whether they like the 'chicken' patties or not)...i had the Jalepeno Burger which could have been more spicy. Portions are huge, great atmosphere, great spot for people watching-  will be back when I need my veggie junk food craving settled in a big and bad way!
I got the Vegan California burger. Wasn't terrible, but was not worth over 10 bucks. Good beer, but everything else was pretty....meh.

It takes a lot of effort to make really good vegan/vegetarian food - I know, I've been eating crappy imitations of chicken and bacon for years now, and it's taken a ton of trial and error to find something my meat-eating friends especially will like. Saturn is champ when it comes to making soy protein isolate taste like chicken nuggets.
The atmosphere is a little loud, even when only a few people are inside, but the decor and ambiance is still a lot of fun. Waiters and staff are nice too (except for one very bored-looking girl who was playing door host for the day, who for some reason couldn't raise her head off her chest when we said hello to her).
Food - well, it's great. One friend had the "Chicken" club with "bacon" and avocado. I had a bite, it was totally excellent - tasted more or less like the real thing. I had a breakfasty egg-type dish, which was wonderful as well. They don't skimp on cheese or french fries (good but not great), which I find is one of the main tests to whether or not a restaurant is more serious about its food or its profit. 
I'll definitely be coming back...

Saturn has done a great job adding more vegan items to the menu which is much appreciated!  Unfortunately they charge extra to sub vegan cheese which is unfortunate given that it is a veg restaurant.  Oh well.  

I actually don't end up coming to Saturn very often these days because I always feel a bit disappointed after eating here.  So many of the options are not house made which kind of takes away from Saturn and when I have tried their house made burger I was grossed out due to it being so soggy it totally killed the bun and everything just fell apart, it didn't have a good flavor either.  C'mon now, it's really not that hard to make a decent veggie burger!    Basically I just have a hard time wanting to spend a lot of money on crap I can buy at the store myself and re-heat.  Sad but true.  

The brunch offerings are decent.  Last time I was there I got the tofu rancheros which came with a modest amount of decent tasting tofu scramble that had a ranchero sauce and not very melted diaya cheese (vegan cheese must be melted thoroughly to acheive optimal texture and taste!!!) on top of a corn tortilla as well as a side of beans.  I had to order a side of avocado for an extra $1.50 which felt like a rip off because it seems like this would come with that already.  My partner got the Rosarita tofu scramble which came with tofu scramble that was mixed with chopped jalapeno and salsa, roasted potatoes, and a slice of toast.  He though this was okay but just wasn't that flavorful.  

Iced tea was excellent!

All in all I think Saturn needs to up their game by putting some effort into their menu because the one they have seems like it was made by someone who doesn't have a background in cooking and that bugs me when it comes to restaurants.

I've never eaten at the original Saturn Cafe, but I was totally psyched for a Berkeley-centered combination of my two favorite things, vegetarian and diner food.  I first got the opportunity to go there for brunch this weekend.  

First off, the decor is over the top!  Bright pink, glitter everywhere -- not much like the softer, retro-50s display on their website.  The tables in each booth also function as glass display cases full of geeky stuff like comic books and Lego figures, and there's a slightly annoying quote from Che Guevara over the entrance to the bathrooms.

We got french toast and the fakin omelet breakfast -- the food was pretty good, but nothing I couldn't have made at home.  I'll have to go back again sometime and see what the burgers are like.  This place is open late (unlike the rest of Berkeley) and I'm sure that's the time when it really shines.

This is the first Berkeley restaurant I decided to try this summer.

The whole idea of the Saturn Cafe is intriguing.

I remember while checking out their website, I liked how they said,
"Stepping into the Saturn Café, you know you have arrived on another planet...This is a place where dressing up in a costume can happen on any night of the year, where the foods of childhood fantasies are even more delicious than you remember, and magic might just lie around the corner of every sparkly, pink booth."

Their description does a good job of convincing you to visit them and try it out.

So props to their idea.

The food, however, was pretty average. They get a star for offering healthy alternatives though because there definitely needs to be more of those nowadays.

I ordered the muffinator and my friend ordered the Space Cowboy. Both were presented really nicely that I had to take my phone out and capture the images. :)

Good restaurant to try! I recommend it!

i can only comment on the vegan milkshake because it was a quick grab before seeing David Henry Hwang's play, Chinglish, at the Berkely Rep---Saturn Cafe is the only place that i know of that has dairy-free milkshakes. 

and boy are they good---so good, i got really damn paranoid while scarfing it down and kept asking the staff if they're sure it's vegan: no milk, right? no bits of dairy? no lactose at all? what about the chocolate syrup? the chocolate chips? is the cup made of cow at all because this taste like a milkshake from my childhood and those milkshakes were full of cow bits.

my only woe is that it's almost $6 for a medium sized cup (though that size is plenty, let's not go all gluttonous gary.) and the straws are wayyy too thin to actually consume the heaping amount of blended vanilla/mint chip soy ice cream you want to shovel down your throat all at once.

i popped into a tapioca store near by and grabbed one of their straws and finished my milkshake in a record 2 minutes. i disgust myself so good. 

i'll be back to try the food! the service was nice and quick, a bit lackadaisical but that's ok. it's not chilis; i don't need someone to hand me my milkshake while doing a jig, lights and streamers around their neck.

Went the other night for a late evening snack. I was skeptical of going to a vegetarian restaurant - I was hungry and didn't want to spend a lot to get full. Boy was I surprised. The food was awesome and not over priced. I had the Mexican omelette - cheese, black beans, green chilis with potatoes and toast (toasted the proper way - one one side). My friend had the Asia peanut sauce brown rice dish with veggies. It was a big plate of food and looked good. And surprise - my free water didn't taste like they drained it out of a car radiator! The wait staff were friendly and efficient. The food came quick. The atmosphere is hip and modern and the piped in music was excellent! I hear the place is open later, too! I'm not a vegetarian but I'm going back. I love a place that knows what it is and does it well. This place rocks - good quality, tasty food, done right at reasonable prices! I guess there is room in Berkeley for another restaurant named after a gas giant planet.

I'm a happy omnivore, and I love Saturn Cafe, especially the house-made SATURN PATTY in the CALIFORNIA BURGER.  It's incredibly flavorful and satisfying, so I'm always torn whether to get it *again* or something else.

Also delectable/deadly addictive: JALAPENO POPPERS.  Dang.  So good.

Lastly, it's seriously a business with a conscience.  I full-on trust and support the Saturn's labor, food and business practices.  They host countless events for non-profits and are so ready to be a long part of the community, all packaged in a fun, clean, comfortable space -- what's not to love?!

I am a huge meat lover but this place is very interesting without the meat! I wanted to try something vegetarian and vegan so my gf and I wanted to try this place. I ordered the jalapeno burger and steak cut fries. The burger wasn't bland whatsoever and the flavor was there. I found the service so friendly and the atmosphere like a diner type. The price is soo expensive and that's why I only gave it 3 stars. The food got me pretty full but the price was just too high. Great experience! wouldn't want to go back though.

On my mission to eat at every planet in Berkeley, I came by this place earlier last week with my friend for dinner and was really impressed. We ordered the nachos for appetizers, and I had the "Chicken" avocado club sandwich.

Food:
Nachos- these were just decent; kind of plain. (Chips, beans, cheese, salsa, guacamole) I wouldn't order these again. 
Chicken Avocado Club- I've never had fake meat before, and this definitely impressed me. The sandwich was REALLY big; I ordered the 1/2 sandwich, salad, soup combo for ~8.50, which is really great considering my sandwich itself was $9.00. I was really full after my meal. The sandwich was also DELICIOUS!! Big pieces of avocado, and the fake chicken was really good - pretty much as good as real chicken. 

I'd definitely come to Saturn again. I felt really clean, healthy, and full after my meal.

I have found my fun, spiritual vegetarian restaurant home.  Well, not spiritual in the traditional sense...this place is the embodiment of kitsch and Berkeley veggie hip.  An all-veg restaurant in downtown Berkeley, it's a couple of blocks away from the Downtown B BART station (convenient), and a few more blocks from the Berkeley Repertory Theatre (where I was headed after dinner).

This place is a hipster diner gone wild with fun.  Tables are all themed.  My friends and I got soooo lucky.  They sat us at the Lego table.  (who knew there were scorpion Lego pieces?) The enormously adorable family at the big booth behind us told us enviously that their par was far too big for the Lego table and that we were the luckiest ducks in the restaurant.  Exploring the table through the glass top provided the four of us an endless amount of conversation and fun.

The pillars in the restaurant are painted silver sparkle, the walls are pink, pink pink!  The are quasi-futuristic metallic mini skirts and hot pants tacked up on the walls for decorations and the bathrooms have robots painted on the doors (blue boy robot and pink girl robot).

It's a fun, family friendly veggie place that even our dedicated meat eater at the table agreed had really good food.  Our party ordered:

Cobb salad with fakin, tvp chick breast (yummy)
Cowgirl blues salad, fakin, buffalo wings chik breast (very delish)
Triple decker BLT with fake meats...
Vegan nachos (OH SO GOOD)
tomato soup
Mint chocolate chip shake
Chocolate madness dessert (chocolate fudge, choc mousse, choc ice cream, choc brownies) - I'm not the biggest chocolate fan, but this was quite delish

The service was stellar, nice, efficient, fun.

Good time was had by all.  There is also another Saturn in Santa Cruz, I'll check that one out soon.

Saturn Cafe is a vegetarian's dream diner!  Stellar ambience (pun intended!) and a good selection of both all vegetarian (and many vegan) brunch and dinner diner fare, this place hits the spot whenever I'm craving a good meatless burger.

And it's in Berkeley too!!  My girlfriend and I came into the Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz for brunch/lunch while down there on vacation.  We left loving the place and bummed that we'd have to wait until the next time we were back in Santa Cruz to come back.  Not so!  They've recently opened a new(ish) location right across from the Berkeley campus by the David Brower Center in downtown Berzerkley.  (Best place for a vegetarian diner: next to a big lefty university and a new hug for greenie non-profits!).

Recommendations: If you like spice (as I do!) try their jalapeno burger with chipotle aioli.  It's amazing!  Comes topped with a brilliant innovation I've only seen at Saturn Cafe: "bottle-caps" -- aka little deep-fried ringlets of nacho-sliced jalapenos.  (They come as an appetizer item as well, along with your choice of dipping sauces if you'd prefer them outside of a bun).

I've also had their "chicken" club, which was great as well.  Big, triple-decker sandwich the way clubs are supposed to be with fillets of breaded, fried fake chicken.  

The sliders special is good for those who can't choose between the burgers (you get a small version of all four of their mainstay vegetarian burgers), or for a sampler to share with friends.

With all burgers and sandwiches, they give you your choice of large seasoned steak cut fries, or my preferred option, lightly breaded, thin-cut shoestring fries.  Onion rings are an option too I think.

Only thing: bring a healthy appetite and steer clear if you're on a diet! The helpings are large, lots of it is fried, and it's oh so tasty, so you'll want to eat the whole thing!  

I hear the milkshakes are great too, but have never had the appetite to down a burger, fries and a shake here...

I think they are good at a few key things and not good at others.  The milkshakes were the most delicious milkshakes I have had - so definitely get a milkshake!  My friend got the "chicken"-avocado sandwich and loved it - so sandwiches seem like a good bet too!

But - the potato tacos?  Two bland tacos stuffed with potato, small next to a giant salad. Cilantro salad dressing was good, but the main taco entree lacking in flavor. The jalapeno and mushroom quesadillas?  Four quesadillas looking lonely on a giant plate, and the cheese not particularly interesting, the tortillas not tasty either.  The "huevos y papas" burrito also small, and bland, wrapped in a tasteless tortilla.  Not enough spices and no sauce to speak of, and for the $6.95 price, I regretted not going to a $5 sandwich store around the corner.

In short - get the milkshakes and sandwiches and fries and you'll be happy, they've got those down well - if you try the Saturn "Mexican" food you'll be disappointed.

I happened upon this place with a friend while looking for a semi-quick place to grab lunch.  neither of us realized it was a 100% vegetarian restaurant until my friend ordered a cheeseburger and asked if they had bacon.  The response was "We have Fakin' but no bacon. We are 100% vegetarian."  As a 99% of the time vegetarian, I was stoked.  The waiter was really nice and tried to console my non-veggie friend assuring him that the veggie burgers are really good.

I ordered the grilled cheese which comes on really thick sourdough.  I asked if I could add tomatoes and Fakin and they were happy to oblige.  My friend got a boca patty with cheese and we both opted for the skinny fries.

I thought the food was a solid B or maybe a B-.  Nothing special.  I didn't particularly care for the thick sourdough as it ended up being a bit dry.  The fries were good and I like that you can choose between thin and thick cut.  The service was great until we were done eating and then it took a while for us to get our check and pay.  Nothing major though; we were deep in conversation and had kind of lost track of time.  

I will definitely try this place again and see if I just happened to order something that wasn't a great choice.  There was a Tofu, veggie and peanut dish that looked yummy.  I am really happy to find a completely veggie place that isn't just Asian fare or super-pretentious and expensive.  Just good comfort food for those of us who don't want meat.

Great delicious healthy hearty food! Went there with a group of friends and ordered
Raw vegetables with brown rice topped with peanut sauce
Scrabled eggs with potatoes and vegetarian sasuage, & soy milk shake
Soyrizo"imitation chorizo" burrito 
vegetarian burger with a side of fries
All great food, but only have one complaint, Potatoes are NOT ORGANIC! So whats the point of having an organic/ vegetarian restaurant if the potatoes are not organic. The reply I got from the waiteress when I asked her why they dont carry organic potatoes was unsatifactory, she stated that they could not obtain Organic potatoes in bulk, Really! I am a stickler when it comes to non orgranic potatoes because it has a very high pesticides and fertilizers count. So Be advised. Make your own decision when it come to that. Other than that the food was delicious and fresh ,I will definetly be a repeat customer!

Awesome, awesome vegetarian food. I have no idea how they do such justice to diner fare without using meat. The first time we came here, my girlfriend was convinced that my bacon turkey club was real. Service is great and insanely fast. The decor is definitely unique, but the awesome tabletop art really distinguishes Saturn from the rest. Definitely try the potato tacos, and the 'beef' taquitos. Probably went here about three times a month while I lived in Berkeley. Only the highest of recommendations.

Yum, yum, yum. I am such a huge fan of Saturn. I love that it takes me forever to decide what to order - something I as a vegan don't usually experience.

I've tried lots of their menu items, but by far my favorite thing is their nachos (where else can you find vegan nachos?!). Their orange soda is also pretty spectacular.

I'm always really impressed by the servers, they seem to go above and beyond to help you out and make the dining experience wonderful.

This is a very quirky diner. Upon entering, you would assume it's some weird homosexual man's fantasy. But it's just a retro vegetarian diner with many vegan options. I'm naturally a meat eater, but my friend had a very distinct taste for food and limitiations. I had the space cowboy, and not a gay reference, it's a vegetarian burger, and I had an organic side salad. I honestly could not tell the difference if I was tasting meat or not, also not a gay reference. I had milkshake mint mixed with berries, a funky mixture, but pretty good overall. Fast and friendly service, out of this world decor. Great for people, like myself, who have a very irritable stomach.

I've seen Saturn Cafe whenever I take the lab shuttle down to Shattuck.  It always looks really popular and neat so I finally got my coworkers to come along with me to try it out.

Saturn Cafe is an American Diner that serves Vegetarian food.  I did not know that until after the food arrived and I was looking at my sliders wondering why the patties looked a bit odd.  In general though, the food was good.  My sliders were interesting tasting and the sauce on the spicy slider (they gave you two types, one a jalapeno spicy and the other regular?) was really good and they had some deep fried jalapenos that also went into it.  

The wait staff was quite attentive and nice and the food was good.  I'm not a big American Diner fan and well, I kinda did want to eat meat so I wish I was aware of what I was getting into before I got into it ... 

Overall, great experience.  I just don't think I would go again because it wasn't my thing.

This place is AWESOME! Maybe I'm a sucker for diners. The guacamole griller burger was super tasty, as were the nachos. I love the whole vibe here. I also love that they have so many vegan options and try to use local organic when they can. So great. A+.

hmmm.....a vegetarian diner.

Guess you could say I was a tad bit skeptical when I was told this place was vegetarian. I mean...vegetarian? How good can a diner be if it's vegetarian? But boy oh boy was I wrong.

 Saturn's Cafe. Cool name. Okay location. and good food.

 I came here because CampusCred was offering this 10 for 20 deal. Figured that would be the best opportunity to try this place out since I was so skeptical about the whole thing....

Came in on a Sunday and WOW. it was packed!!! Parking was hard to find (I was here around 12pm). Everyone was looking for parking and I just kept driving in circles just to look for parking. The only consolation is that all parking on the streets are free. But on with the rest of the story.

My friend and I got seated within 10 minutes or so so despite it being packed, the wait wasn't long. We took a while with the menus though (so I do suggest you take a look at the menus before you go if you've never gone before). Our waiter was really nice though. Asked us how we were doing and if we were ready. He didn't seem to be in any rush to make us order and seemed like he just wanted us to enjoy our diner experience.

We ended up ordering one omelete plate and a burger (apparently their burgers and milkshakes are a must try but we skipped on the milkshake since the omelete and burger plates were almost $10 each). So let me talk about the two separately.

The Space Cowboy Burger - IS IT REALLY VEGETARIAN?! its a veggie patty with fakin' bacon and BBQ sauce. But if i didn't know that, I would have thought I was eating a BBQ Bacon Cheeseburger. I find it pretty hard to fake a good burger but this one does a pretty good job (although I'm not saying that after a few bites, you wouldn't have figured it out. It's good but not THAT good). We got thin cut fries with our burger and those were a big yum as well.

The Street Bourbon Omelete - uhh.....slightly misleading.  The omelete doesn't actually wrap around the filling. It's just that one layer of egg over the top. It has fakin bacon, oinions and chard inside (I didn't know what chard was so it was worth a try. But for those of you who are interested in knowing, it basically taste like a mix of spinach and seaweed). Other than the misleading look, the omelete was okay...i could definitely find better omeletes elsewhere. The homefries we had were kind of burned too. So basically, don't come here for their breakfast menu. I would stick to the burger and possibly try out that milkshake.

Ultimately, it was worth a try. But for the price (and the fact that I'm not a vegetarian), I probably won't come back again. unless of course theres another deal.

Came here for lunch today with a friend. They have a gluten menu for her (allergic) and it's heaven for me, a vegetarian.

The hibiscus cooler was very good. I had the cobb salad and they graciously removed any trace of the blue cheese I hate and substituted other ingredients. The salad was huge; no leaving hungry here.

Service was a little slow at first, but the food came fast once we ordered and they let us eat in peace and talk. $22 plus tip for both of us -- not bad for such big portions and good food. I'll be back!

Full of a craving for a Caesar salad and really just salad salad salad, me and my lady came to Saturn yesterday to check it out. Sadly there was no Caesar but there was a bleu cheese and apple Balsamic salad and it was the bomb. Amazing. Good flavors. Awesome. I needed some protein as well so I got the house made veggie patty. It was good. I would order it again for sure. My lady got the peanut veggie stirfry-esque thing. It was more sweet than savory and we both felt like a little more kick and savory would have made it meet our taste better, but it wasn't a bad dish. More for those who like their peanut sauce mellow and sweet though. 

However the total win? The vegan chocolate milkshake. I couldn't even believe it was vegan. We had to double check. It was insane! So stupid good. And considering that Gratitude now charges almost $10 for their (not nearly as tasty) non dairy shakes, you can bet we'll be coming back here when ever any of my non dairy people need their ice cream fix.

What?? A fifties diner in the middle of Berkeley that's not Mels- I have to love it. Well, despite the somewhat loooong wait until my server spoke to me, I was pleasantly 
suprised by the 
incredibly quick delivery time for my entree and water.  My waiter seemed to be having a rough night, so I really don't mind. And yes, the Cowgirl space burger (fake chix,)
 salad and strawberry shake were all delicious. 
I will be coming back with friends. 

gracias for reading!

Awesome vegetarian & vegan food. Very well-seasoned. Fooled my dad into thinking it was plain old meat. The pink walls were bright and fun as were the hostess & waitress who was more than willing to provide us with some hot water + lemon. :) Also as you await your order, there are plenty of comic strips to read spread out on the table underneath the glass.

This diner is a good choice for late dinners or if you can't get seating at Gather next door.

RECs:
1. Chicken Club Sandwich--you can certainly share this between 2 people.
2. California Burger--I love avocado, so this worked out perfectly. The bun was awesome and the vegan patty was perfectly seasoned.
3. Thin Fries--perfectly cooked.
4. Vegan Nachos--GUACAMOLE and sour cream and beans and tomatoes and cheese and lots of yummy-ness. Mmm.

CON:
1. Parking as always sucks in Berkeley and any other big city. However, you could always walk from Cal or the Downtown Bart station.

Everything was okay, the french fries, the "award winning" milk shake...so average I don't even feel like finishing the review.

Although I did appreciate the gender neutral bathrooms and friendlywait staff so i've added a star.

I love taking anyone here - friends, family, the boyfriend. Every trip here has been a blast and the food has always been delicious and satisfying.

Service here is great and attentive - they check in frequently to keep you stocked up on your drink orders and water and clean up the table for you promptly when you finish.

Atmosphere here is very quirky with every table having a different theme and the booth seating having more elaborate table decorations.

The menu can be a bit intimidating as everything here looks delicious and can be on the pricier end of things. However, everything I've ordered has been great! I've had the Portebello Mushroom burger before (yum), the Cowgirl Blues Burger (I think that's what it was called - chicken patty with bleu cheese), and a grilled cheese sandwich. The side salads, while called "mini" are actually quite large! I know many people love ordering the fries here, but the salads here are so good and their dressing too! I got cilantro lime dressing last time.

I've also had a taste of their milkshakes and loved their mint chocolate chip ice cream shake mixed with berries!

This would be a great date spot but it's honestly an ideal place to bring anyone, and with their vast selection you're bound to please everyone.

I'm originally from LA and know a thing or two about delicious vegan food. This place really blew my mind. Everything I ordered was very tasty. The "chicken" club sandwich was the best Vegan food I ever ate. I also had their nachos which were excellent! If I ever return to Berkeley I will definitely come back!

Saw that place just opened and went to give it a try today.

I got the western burger (or whatever their name for it is); it was pretty damn good. I would suggest replacing the patty to their house made-- it was probably one of the best veggie patty's ive ever tasted. However, it was the fries that were the showcase of the meal. THEY ARE AMAZING. Thin cut, super crispy and salty and just over all delicious. Got them with ranch and was very, very happy. 

Only downside to this place was the bill; slightly expensive for diner food. Burger was $9.50 and the side of ranch an extra $.75. Not terrible, but not an everyday kind of place either. Either way, I'll probably be back again... need to try those nacho fries...

I can't believe I haven't gotten around to reviewing this place. Since it opened, I've been here a shockingly high number of times. I feel like I gotta support them with my dollars. 

Listen folks, their menu just got a massive vegan overhaul. Remember how everybody kept saying, "How come they only have a handful of vegan options?" Well, those days are over. The pancakes are vegan, french toast is vegan, and they debuted a vegan ranch. All of the burgers can now be vegan. 

My partner and I usually stick with the vegan Buck Rodgers or the vegan guacamole burger, though now that all the other burgers can be vegan I think we need to branch out. I tried the jalapeno burger this week and was a fan. It was a total, saucy mess, but it was spicy and delicious. I also often get a side of vegan Buck sauce for the fries. It's tasty. I think I might try the ranch though now that it exists. 

I'm also a huge fan of the vegan nachos and the nacho fries. There's something that makes me feel guilty about eating the nacho fries, but they really hit the spot. 

The best thing though is the milkshakes. I've always been a fan of the chocolate shake, but the vanilla one is great. I think it may have pipped chocolate in my heart. The new comer is the peanut butter shake. One of our servers suggested it and I want to thank her. It was a revelation. I want one right now. 

So yeah, this place is solid. It's not the healthiest, lightest food out there, but it's vegetarian and mostly vegan. If you want that? Go somewhere else. If you want good veggie diner food, this is the spot for you.

This place is the best vegetarian place in Berkeley. I am a big meat lover, but I must say that this place makes me forget I'm not eating meat. Their food is always really good. I especially like their shakes. I really love having breakfast/brunch here. I get the Heavenly Benedict usually. The eggs are cooked just right and the hollandaise sauce tastes just right. The service is really great as well, and I really like 50s feel of the place.

My husband and I tried Saturn Cafe last month. I was looking forward to the fake BLT which did not disappoint. However, the chicken sandwich with blue cheese that my husband ordered could have been better (more cheese please!). Good place if you are craving vegan or veggie comfort food though I do feel the fake meat they serve is the same I could get at the grocery store and throw onto a bun with other toppings easily myself. The chocolate milk shake was delicious. The staff was friendly. The portions were generous.

I like Saturn Cafe-- A LOT!

Fun crowd, friendly staff, sweet decor, and TASTY diner classics with a veggie twist! Alsooooo, the most AMAZING DELICIOUS DECADENT MILKSHAKES. 
Ever. 

I highly recommend checking this place out. 
Definitely try: Spartacus Salad, Peanut Royale, Nachos, and MILKSHAKES.

Have FUN :)

I had planned on waiting to check out the new Berkeley Saturn Cafe until a few months had passed & they had it all dialed in (and perhaps added a few more vegan options to the menu). But I was in the neighborhood today, and my other two choices weren't happening so I went to Saturn in a combination of whim and convenience. It was fairly slow for brunch time on a Sunday, but I didn't mind since that meant rockin' service. I had coffee and soymilk in no time flat, and my tofu scramble arrived about ten minutes after I placed my order. The scramble was fairly no-frills-- just seasoned tofu, homefries and toast-- but tasty. I'm not usually one for vegan approximations of omnivore food, but there was a nice fluffiness to the tofu that brought back vague memories of scrambled eggs. The waiter was great about topping off my coffee (I eventually had to start covering my cup with my hand to signal 'no more'), and the bill was fairly reasonable-- $10 for the whole affair. I'd go back if I had omnivore friends to appease, and will wait patiently for a little more 'vegan love' to be added to the menu. You're off to a good start, Saturn!

Our quest for the perfect tofu scramble brought us to Saturn, a new vegetarian  diner in downtown Berkeley on the edge of the Cal campus.

Saturn's interpretation of tofu scramble is dry, crumbly, and yellow.  It's just tofu, with no vegetables mixed in.  On the side are thick slices of toast (sort of like Texas toast) and cubed fried potatoes sprinkled with green herbs.  The scramble's okay in a plain-Jane way.  The toast is too thick, and the cubed potatoes suck, as always.

(Note to restauranteurs:  cubed breakfast potatoes are a terrible idea.  The surface-to-volume ratio is wrong for browning and crisping, so the potatoes never rise above blandness...and throwing in a lot of inappropriate green herbs is NOT the answer.  The best breakfast potatoes are shredded or sliced paper-thin and fried in sufficient oil, till golden brown.  Potatoes prepared this way are delicious with nothing more than a little salt and pepper.  Got that?  Just say no to cubes!)

Saturn serves a large range of breakfasts, burgers, shakes, mac and cheese, and other diner foods without the meat. The dark-roast coffee is strong but drinkable (not Peet's brand, which helps).  The vegan chocolate shakes are out of this world--definitely the best thing we tried.

Mediocre at best.
