I really wanted to like Saturn, and I wish I could say I feel satisfied after eating there.  But I don't and I can't.  The burgers are bland and the service is frustratingly slow.  I was going to give them 2 stars, but will give them 3 because the salads are usually okay.  But that's not saying much for a vegetarian restaurant.
Thanks for the awesoome response and changing your policy.  I love thus place (writing review from Saturn now) .
Still rockin'  I am amazed at how many people are here on any given day, but they always get me in and out quickly (unless I want to nurse my coffee).  More vegan options than when they opened.

So, I came up to visit my brother for the weekend and we ended up visiting Saturn Cafe for lunch.

The good:
Awesome and varied vegetarian/vegan menu
Really fun vibe/atmosphere
Yummy burger (I had the cowboy burger)
Best sweet potato fries I've ever had

The bad:
Very little parking
Waitress forgot our drink order
Only accepts Visa and Mastercard (and of course cash)


I only took off a star because the service was kinda sluggish, but I absolutely recommend the food.

So a couple of things you should know about this place. 

1) It's vegetarian/vegan. You should not complain about this, they do not in any way try to hide the fact or trick you into their food. They are upfront about it, and it is what it is.  Seeing reviews here saying they couldn't get past the fact it was all vegetarian is just idiotic.  I don't go to a Italian restaurant and get pissed because they don't serve Sweet and Sour Pork.

2) Most of the menu is good, but not all of it.  Knowing what to order is key and you typically don't know until you've been a few times. The salads are really straight forward, you should know based on the ingredients if it's something you'll like. Only a the Chix and Homemade patties are good in my opinion, the rest are whatever. The fries are usually great.  Mac n Cheese is still not there, they've improved it but still not as amazing as it could be. Their soup changes daily, if they aren't insanely slammed, ask them for a sample and they'll be happy to give you one before you make a whole order. The tomato soup that is on the menu everyday is typical but always satisfying..  Chicken Avocado Club is easily the best thing on the menu.  Their salsa sucks, only worth eating if you get a nacho plate. The vegan nachos (must get it with tofu spread) is really satisfying. I typically only go for the eggs and potatoes kind of breakfast, the burritos aren't worth it, Soyrizo isn't good in any application so don't bother. 

2b) They have comment cards, if you don't like how something tasted, tell them. If you know you're vegan/vegetarian food products that you think could make for a better solution to something they already have (or don't have)... tell them. I think I had a hand in indirectly helping improve their Mac n Cheese via the comment cards.

3) This place is not a fine dining experience, it is diner food, expect similar to what you'd get at Rudy's except all Vegetarian. Speaking to the reviewer that was upset they didn't get artisan bread with their soup.  They are incredibly accommodating and attentive unlike other aforementioned diners. I also think its totally reasonable, there is half sandwich, salad and soup combo that is about $8, quite the steal if you ask me.

4) The service, is absolutely what brings this review up from a 3.5 star to a 5 star review.  I and many friends frequented the Santa Cruz location when we lived in the area and just put up with the absolutely awful service that seemed to be stuck in purgatory there. I don't know what the state of it is now, but a few years ago it was absolutely painful to go.  Since Day 1 at the Berkeley location I've been blown away by the staff there, they've always been friendly, attentive, and apologetic if anything went wrong.  Seriously 6 stars for the staff, who keep their composure even in the worst circumstances. I don't know how they keep this up.

5) Get a Vegan Milkshake, it is just as good as the real thing and I'm going to go get one right now.

get the fries.

this time, i opted for the california burger...which i decided needed real meat in it. 

but...the fries. oh the fries. 

my friend got the eggs benedict. and i really just wanted to eat off her plate constantly, because they looked so good.

I went to Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz many years ago when my friend was going to ucsc and I was eager to try their raw cookie dough dessert and it was delicous. When I heard there was going to be a Saturn Cafe in Berkeley, I was really excited.  I love Santa Cruz and it just felt right to have a Saturn Cafe in Berkeley.  You kind of have to wait a long time for your food, but for a vegetarian and vegan restaurant, this place has pretty good food.  They even have vegan milkshakes and fake bacon that tastes and smells like bacon!  And it's good too!  I think the tastiest food I've tried so far at Saturn Cafe is their thin cut fries.  They have a coating on them that is fab!  Their deserts are good too.  One time I had a coconut pineapple ice cream and it was so yummy I got some to go to bring home to my boy-friend.

This place is very cute with a catchy name and fun decorations.

The waiters aren't really attentive, and passed by us a couple of times without any consideration that we were ready to order, even after we closed our menus and placed it to the sides.

The food was okay, nothing too special. I ordered The California Burger with thin cut fries and half a side of nachos to share. The nachos were delicious! The burger was alrightl. The fries were quite tasty - not oily and not extremely salty. 

They have an array of dipping sauces: wasabi, guacamole, ranch, BBQ, and bluehorn(?).

It's a fun vegetarian/vegan place to experience, but it will seem pricey to people who love (real) meat.

I came here again with some girls and had a blast. 

Although the service was still as slow as last time, we had a better time with it. Our server, Andy, was just so funny and somewhat awkward. At the end when we wanted a picture of all of us, he kind of took a picture of himself and then a awkward upward shot of us from the floor to get the saturn picture on the wall and then a normal one. Although I found this kind of weird, it was funny as well.

Food:
Avocado Cheese Sandwich - This was really good although all of the ingredients were in the middle which made the crusts really gross to eat. For an additional $3, I could get sweet potato fries which is what I did. I am in love with sweet potato fries right now and these...were just about average, but the sandwich was delicious. I could be able to make it myself, I know, but it was good. 

Overall, I had a great experience with friends and more of all, the service although slow, was great from Andy. I hope I get you next time I go if I end up going again!

This is definitely a good place to hang out with friends while eating some good food. I've been there 3 times so far (in 2 months) and i will surely come back again.
They have quite a many choices to choose from: Burgers, Tacos, Salads, desserts, milkshakes... As well, it looks like it is a nice place to get your vegan meal if you prefer such food. And they have like the best steak-cut French fries that i've tasted so far. And i love their homemade ranch dressing. Yum, Yum :)
Once you enter the door the staff people greet you and name their house specials. The downside is that it is close to UC Berkeley campus, and so many people go in there especially on game nights. Last time i went there with a friend we had to wait like 5 minutes to be seated down and another 10 or so minutes for our order to be taken, but please do not let this fact to disgust you and walk away. It's definitely worth waiting, food is great, atmosphere is very friendly, and prices are reasonable.
I see that people often comment on the actual state of bathroom facilities. So here is my review: Amazing! Other than bin being loaded with used paper towels, ladies' bathroom looks great. Nice. Clean. With mirrors, and i even love those tiles on walls :)))

My co-worker and I came here for lunch. I was much crowded from what we expected, as the UC students were out on Christmas break.    I ordered the spaceboy cowboy burger and she, the pumpkin pancakes.  The pumpkin pancakes were delicious.  The spaceboy cowboy burger...let's say that some things should remain non-vegan.  Don't get me wrong, I luv my vegan food and entrees. But this burger just didn't seem to work. The fakin bacon tasted like a fake, something like bacon.  The burger patty tasted more like a chicken patty than beef.  I would have enjoyed an all beef patty with bacon.  Sorry to all the vegans.Maybe I ordered the wrong burger. I'm glad I tried the meal here, but I don't think I will be back.

Good news! This Saturn gives you the same stomach rot with marginally less bitchy service! Made me miss nights of drinking too much at the Asti, then heading across the street to inhale a Buck Rogers in roughly 2.5 seconds. Don't worry, Santa Cruz nostalgia is there and I will likely be back.

Great atmosphere.    Excellent place for vegans or vegetarians who want diner food.   I had the portobello burger and thin fries and shared a vegan milk shake with my son.   Great price.   Excellent food.     I'd visit again in a flash.

Saturn Cafe is a breath of fresh air for Berkeley.  The location is impeccable, yet the turnover of restaurants that inhabit this building has been shameful. Perhaps because like an undergrad, once you finish your degree you get the hell outta dodge and move on to a bigger , more pretentious lifestyle.  I have a feeling that Saturn will be a long-stay in this town.  Vegan,  vegetarian menu, late night dining, with a "commitment to social and environmental justice," totally fits the Berkeley bill!  

Me and my co-workers get overly excited at the thought of lunch at Saturn.  Not being a big meat-eater myself, I haven't had a corn dog in years.  Saturn gave me back my childhood corn dog diet.  The chicken burger is mouth-watering, the thin cut fries kick McDonald's ass, the nachos rock and breakfast anytime...? Sold!  

I always have a fabulous lunch here...Service has always been great, the price is right, and there is nothing cooler than a diner decorated like life on a pink planet with Michael Jackson playing in the background. And fakin bacon may be the thing of the future if pigs were to go extinct.

I love the style of Saturn Cafe, diner but vegetarian/veganfied. The vegan taquitos are super good here. The nachos are also very yummy. Meat eaters and non-meat eaters alike usually find this place tasty. The vegan milkshakes are delicious, definitely try one!

I was walking to CU Sushi, and the decor caught my eye. After ordering I realized that it was vegetarian which was perfect because I just came from the gym :D. I ordered the Jalapeno Burger and my sister orders the sampler and mac and cheese on the side.

Spicy sampler platter: the sampler was pretty good but the proportions of each 'sample' was a bit off.  4.5 stars.

Mac'n'cheese (side): the mac and cheese was a bit disappointing. The texture was perfect for me but it was hard not to sprinkle a little black pepper onto it. 3 stars.

Jalapeno Burger: the patty was moist and the chipotle was a good balance of spice. 5 stars.

Overall: 4 stars.

OK, I admit that I'm probably biased based on many fond memories of ending up at the Saturn in Santa Cruz after a good show at the Catalyst and being hammied, but my meal here was darned good. 

I had the "Chicken" Avocado Club and it was perfect. I gave up bacon when I was 9, but with the smoked gouda and fakin bacon on the sammie, it was as good as it gets. Definitely not a healthy veggie meal, but a satisfying one nonetheless. My meat eater friend had the BBQ Ranch "Chicken" Burger and she finished her entire plate. 

We split the pumpkin milkshake (flavor of the month) and it was delish. As we were leaving I looked at the booth next to me and saw another set of my friends about to order. As I was beginning a recommendation they said that they had eaten at Saturn the night before so they didn't need any help. This place is that good. 

I will definitely be back soon!
Veggie burger! cool retro place
Saturn is the bomb!  We are so excited we don't have to wait for our Santa Cruz trips to get some delicious fake-meat meals.  We reccomend... EVERYTHING!

We love the veggie burgers and fries. Also, a nice selection of other dishes. The place was crowded when we went, but we had good service and friendly people. Any flaws seen earlier were probably due to the fact that they just opened.

I was very excited when Saturn opened. I loved the concept, the decor, the menu. But my experience there has been very uneven. The burger was great, the side salad was ample and awesome, the milkshake was yummy. The peanut royale, as another reviewer noted, was very bland and boring. 

Two times of my three visits there, the service has been horrendous. There seemed to be only one server working the entire restaurant during a busy lunch hour. She was too harried to take our drink order when we were seated, or ask about beverages when we ordered, or check back to see if everything was all right. I predicted that I wouldn't see my beverage until after I'd finished my meal, and I was right, even though I reminded the server as she walked by and she said it was coming.

Oh, and every time I've been there, the seats and table have been sticky. I really hope they can improve the service and cleanliness, because I think the place has great potential and I'd like to see it succeed. That location has seen too many restaurants come and go.

YES!!! Where have you been all my life, Saturn Café?!

I was having an awful night, and I just wanted a crap ton of hot food... but it was 11PM and I'm vegan.  I had never been to Saturn Café, so I was excited that they had vegan food and were open until Midnight.

I got a vegan sampler and a vegan quesadilla, and I'm way beyond impressed and satisfied.  The sweet potato fries are AMAZING, and the vegan quesadilla is EPIC.  Not only is the food delicious, the portions are large (I got a quarter of the way through each box) and the prices are right.

I ordered to-go, but the atmosphere inside looked super cozy.

I don't know how I'm going to keep myself from going back every freaking night.  THANK YOU FOR EXISTING, Saturn Café!

If I could give 3.5 stars, I would.. but since it feels more like a 3 than a 4, we'll go with 3.

The feel was overall of a slightly hipster diner that's not a chain,
the decor is intentionally cheesy with sparkles and lots of pink,
and the portions are enormous.
Totally fun as a group get together, or if you want a casual bite,
but keep in mind that even vegetarian, it's still diner food ;) 
so don't expect organic heirloom tomatoes in your burger.

We had great service on a week night!
Fast and friendly staff that took turns taking cheesy pictures of us.
A lot of us didn't finish our food, but few took leftovers home..
the idea of reheating a burger and soggy fries is rarely appealing.
Prices were reasonable for the type of food, and the shakes were quite noms.
Would definitely be back if we're in the area and feeling diner foodsy..
but wouldn't make a trip specifically for it.

Veggie burgers! And they're open late. A fantastic option for vegetarians and vegans who are craving diner food or comfort food. It tastes pretty much like the "real" thing. If you're in the East Bay, this should be on your late night take out list, especially if you are veg. The staff are extremely sweet, too.

i hate the way this place looks but i cannot fault a cherry chip vegan milkshake that actually comes to you in the same manner of a regular diner. it actually pieces of cherry too which was nice. the prices are reasonable considering the relative rarity of the products. one of the people i came with had a root beer float with the dairy ice cream and was satisfied, not impressed.

The last time I was @ Saturn Cafe I was there for a school event & all I had were a few celery sticks.  This time I took advantage of the menu & spent a good few minutes & scrutinized the menu from from to back, top to bottom.

I finally decided on the vegan breakfast burrito with tofu spread, guacamole & fresh salsa o the side.  I had never had a vegan dish before but this was way better than I thought.  The burrito had homefries & tofu scramble on the inside.  The tofu scramble was so good.  It was curry flavored but not overpoweringly so.  Loved it!  The tofu spread was also very tasty & it tasted a lot like potato salad.

The service was mediocre but it was because someone didn't show up for work.  My server was actually pretty nice once he stopped @ our table; he even drew a robot on the back of my check.

Saturn Cafe isn't exactly my first choice for eating out but I won't count it 
out for when friends &/or myself feel like having something different.

Quick note: This place is CASH ONLY.

mer. food overhyped. sorry bout' it.

HOWEVER, service was awesome and our waiter brea (?) was funny and super cheeel.

Wow, really good. I'm nowhere near a vegetarian, but the Space Cowboy (seems to be the signature item) was superb. The steak cut fries were some of the best fries I've had in a while, and i'm a big fry snob. 

Service was laid-back, frequent and super nice. Decent location (close to Shattuck but away from a lot of the noise; close to BART). Definitely will have to make another trip.

It's awesome to find a vegetarian restaurant and not a vegan restaurant.  With soy allergies, it's great to find a place that still serves dairy, but meat free.  The food was really good and the fries were probably the best part.  Everyone talks about how great the milkshakes, but I was so full after this meal that I didn't get one.  

Bathroom labels are a little confusing.  Just open the door and look for the urinal or lack of urinal and you were be set.

The atmosphere reminds me of the old terminal in the Las Vegas Airport... how people in the 1950's pictured the future, except with a modern flare.  It is hard to describe.  

Excellent, glad I went here.
LOVE IT! so amazing! so down for that chicken bacon sandwich! it was the shiiit!

My trips back to Berkeley often orbit around this celestial gem. My friends and I paid it a long overdue visit today after months away, and I was not disappointed. I would give the place 4 stars alone for its friendly service, but the place's vibrant decor (great for large groups!) and spot-on vegetarian cornucopia really seal the deal. I've had their pumpin pancakes in the autumn, and I ordered the "fried chicken" salad today. Admittedly, the salad itself was nothing super special, but their soy (?) chicken is amazing, and great for anyone looking for a semi-authentic taste without the heaviness or guilt of real chicken. Saturn Cafe is by far my favorite of the planetary series that has taken up residence in Berkeley, so definitely give it a try if you haven't!

3.5 rounding up because the people that work at Saturn Cafe are very nice.  

I'm very skeptical of fake meat, so I opted for the portobello burger.  I expected to get a big hunk of portobello, but instead got a few strips of mushroom tossed together with roasted peppers.  Nevertheless the flavor was spot on and I enjoyed my order.  

I also got to try the jalapeno burger, which was tastey, but there was something off about the flavor combination.  It was sort of one note and salty rather than flavorful.  

This place seriously confused me because it looked like a diner on the outside.  And it's so freaking crowded.  I can't tell if it's crowded because it's good, or because people are dumb like me and didn't know it was vegetarian/vegan until I sat down in a booth.  But still, I've had much worse at Fin's so this place is like heaven compared to that.  

Get their fries as your side to your burger.  Steak cut fries are really crispy on the outside and sooo good on the inside

We came here because my boyfriend and I decided we wanted to do a Berkeley/Oakland area Vegan feast! So, we wanted to start at Cinnaholic, move to this place, and then Souley Vegan. Too bad Cin and Souley are closed on Mondays :(

But...

This place is GREAT! Normally, for a Monday in a vegetarian restaurant, I expected us to be the only ones there! Nope! This place actually had a good amount of people in it for lunch time, which is always a good sign to me.

The decor was great, very space age-hip. The tables were neat with inlays of records, cds, mixtapes and musical things. 

The food was excellent. I had the Vegan Cheeseburger special w/ chedder cheese. It was so yummy! The fries were great too,

My boyfriend had the Vegan Huevos Rancheros and was in heaven, he hadn't had that in over 5 years!

The service was fast, as well. The guys that worked there seem kind of "douchey hipster" but it didn't bother us too much.

As a self-described carnivore I almost can't believe I'm writing this but I'm actually giving a good review to a Vegan/Vegetarian restaurant. 

Saturn gets thumbs up from me for a diverse menu, good execution and decent prices. The faux-meats weren't bad at all, at least from the "chicken" i had on top of my Santa-Fe Salad. The Milkshake was pretty decent, though I still like Barney's Better, and the Nacho Fries that everyone talks about was quite excellent (though i could go for spicier jalapenos). Great portions for everything.

My friend had the portabello burger which looked delicious but messy. 

All in all, while I'm not planning on declaring veganism to the world any time soon, I was very satisfied with my meal and wouldn't mind going back when I next feel the need to graze for extra fiber and foliage. 

Service was decent, maybe could've been a bit more enthusiastic, but friendly enough and efficient.

i absolutely LOVE this place. there food is AMAZING! i am a vegan and there are so many great options! I dont like vegeterian burgers but there are great! and i also love the pancakes! the atmosphere of the place is cool and fun, i love the decor and how each table has a different theme. i would give it 20 stars if i could!

This is an update to my review of last week.  The manager contacted me after reading my review and was genuinely concerned and wanted to address the issues I encountered.  She even offered a gift cert. if I wanted to return.

I went again tonight, and the experience was a big improvement.  They got the food order correct and the service was excellent.  I took a friend and she said if I hadn't told her of my first disappointed experience there, she never would have guessed it from the quality and service we received tonight.

I was really impressed that whatever went wrong the last time, the staff at Saturn Cafe certainly made it right! Thanks.

I've been to Saturn a few times for dinner and lunch. Aces! My only quibble was the Cowgirl Blue burger (kinna on the small side, but otherwise delish).  I mean, let's be clear - even a veggie burger should be the size of your head. The garlic fries are a favorite; really if I didn't have to eat other 
foodstuffs to be functional, I could reasonably live off garlic fries alone. 

The space has a Jetson's diner-vibe, which is the only time I find I ever appreciate pink and space sparkles. (I always get confused by the pink and blue robots for the restrooms though. Uh.....???).  The staff are young and hip and always very cool. Usually they're playing 80s pop, which is my generation and the best music period ever.  

Did I mention the garlic fries? I did. Okay, there's also the sweet potato fries (#2 with a bullet). There's also this ceasar salad thing, which is excellent and they serve kombucha. Yummy and cool local spot!

I'm so excited about this concept! A vegetarian 50's diner. Sounds good to me:-)  I really enjoyed the service and the food at Saturn. 

Here are a few fun food tips:
1. The steak fries (thick cut) are wonderful! If you are going back and forth between these and the sweet potato fries-- get the thickums!

2. Yay vegan vanilla and chocolate shakes and malts!!! Can you say mmmm:-) My friend got the seasonal pumpkin shake and loved it also.

3. The Brunch menu looks awesome.  I haven't had it yet but they have a plethora of veggie breakfast options--I can't wait to try some of them.

Thanks Saturn!

P.S. I also really appreciate the spotless restrooms!

I had lunch with a friend here a few weeks back.  I ordered a Jalepeno burger.  I had such high hopes for this place, being a fan of vegetarian food. 

Good location, space and cute/fun decorations.
Pretty good service.
Food is where I had to shave off a star or two.  The burger tasted ok but the jalapeno bottle caps were kind of strange.  Bland tasting with the batter falling apart into a mushy mess as I ate my food.  

I will be back to try something else, but for now  a 3/5.

Great place for a date, especially if your prospective partner is vegetarian. They have lots of fakin' bacon and other imitation meats or vegetarian choices. But is also good for meat lovers: their burgers are mostly creative Californian twists, nothing too greasy. They also have some seasonal Santa Cruz beer on tap, also a plus!

Also: those gay boys are VERY attentive waiters, and not half bad to look at... meow!

Ive been here a few times because I like to support vegetarian restaurants, but Saturn is pretty hit or miss depending on the type of patty you choose.

The jalapeño and cowgirl burgers are tasty, but I didn't want to swallow my bite of the California burger.

Went for brunch on a Saturday and got a booth right away. Ordered the Vegan French Toast and the Vegan Spud Scramble. Both were DELICIOUS. Also, very cheap! My boyfriend and I ate our faces off for $20!!!

The service was just ok, typical unenthusiastic hipster waiter, but the food made up for that. The restaurant is also a no frills place, which I love, but don't come in your Sunday finest.

It is right by the downtown berkely BART station and right next door to Cinnaholic, the vegan bakery, so it is the perfect place to stop by for a quick bite before exploring Berkeley.

The restaurant also supports Farm Sactuary and other animal rights causes- which I love.

I have been a huge fan of Saturn Cafe since my first visit to their Santa Cruz location about 5 years ago.  By far my favorite place to go for veggie burgers, fries and shakes.  I was so excited when I learned they were opening up shop in Berkeley.  I was disheartened to see the negative reviews of the Berkeley location on Yelp.  When we went yesterday, we had a wonderful experience.  The waitstaff was friendly and attentive.  We received our food promptly.  The veggie burger and steak fries were just as amazing as they are in Santa Cruz.  We also got a vegan vanilla and peanut butter milkshake.  I can't think of anywhere that makes a better shake.  It's hard not to inhale the whole shake in one gulp.  As a vegan, I would love to see more vegan options, but I am quite happy with the ones that are already in place.  The ambiance was funky and it was nice and bright with plenty of giant windows.  The menu (same menu as Santa Cruz) met my needs and I thoroughly enjoyed my meal.  Looking forward to my next visit.

Basically a vegetarian/vegan diner, so simple, so yummy, and the perfect combination.  Today was my first time there and I had a BBQ "chicken" sandwich with the thin fries.  The sandwich was incredible, it had ranch dressing on it and the fries were really good.  I had the sliders too, which were very satisfying.  I can't wait to go back.

It's like they read my mind... I've been hoping and praying for YEARS that someone would open a place like Saturn Cafe.

GREAT diner food. Some of the best fries I've ever had (2nd only to Rudy's in Emeryville).

I should start by saying I'm a vegetarian. For those who are bitching about this place having fake meat... well, that's like complaining the food at an Indian restaurant was spicy. 
Anyhow, LOVE this food. Best Nachos ever, and my meat eating friends agreed with me on that one.
I got the sliders and was really happy.
Now, for the down side: the service. They are really nice, but working out the kinks of a new place still. It takes FOREVER to get anything there. Don't go there if it's packed. I hope they work this out, because I really enjoyed the food. I will add stars if they fix this. ;)
Oh yea... glad to see there is a place that employs hipsters as their entire wait staff... heehee

It used to be a totally reasonable trip to get in the car and drive two hours just to go to Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz...the vegan buck sauce is that good. 

Now that the Berkeley store has opened, I'm afraid I'm never going to eat anywhere else. 

They're delicious, open late, and fairly cheap.  And if, after all that, you could ask for more...they're opening a performance space for local artists. 

These guys rule.  

So many of the buildings on that street have turned over time and time again (once it was a Persian food restaurant then a yoga shop, ect.) I really hope that Saturn is here to stay.

I like this place even though I'm not a vegetarian. They still have eggs so I always get their eggs florentine. You can eat here as a carnivore and still respect yourself. Plus it's open until midnight and has this great hot sauce - ask for the one with the Caribbean dude on the label it's delicious.

I tried taking a group of non-vegan friends here for dinner.  I never told them that the entire menu is vegetarian.  They finally figured it out, but they still were very fond of the food.  As a vegan, I enjoy coming to the Saturn Café when I crave comfort food.  The atmosphere is very retro, the vegan burgers are tasty, and the vegan shakes are delicious.
the jalapeno burger was great but the chili was pretty unstellar.  seems like a good venue for a private gathering and i believe they rent the place out

After so much hype, I finally decided to visit this place. Interior is very ... sparkly and pink but it is much better than the pseudo-dinky Italian/Mexican/lots of other things restaurant that used to be there. 
Maybe I had my expectations too high , but compared to some of the raving reviews I've heard, I didn't see anything amazing about this place. I am an omnivore by nature, and realize this is a vegetarian place. I don't know how this place compares to other vegetarian places, since I rarely go to them, but food seems quite a bit pricey as well. 
I would go back to try their milkshake (since I didn't get to try that one, and that seems to get positive reviews) but so far, food seems fresh, but not really amazing in terms of taste. 
Another thing that ticked me off was that half the time I've been there, tables were super sticky, and also the waiter/waitress never came around except to take order (after 10 minutes of being seated) and to bring over food and the bill

With the exception of our server, I could not be more disappointed with my experience at Saturn. I ordered biscuits and gravy, and one poached egg. The egg was hard, not runny the way a poached egg should be, and the biscuits and gravy were dry and tepid at best. I sent the egg back, and was pleased with how the server assuaged the situation. The second egg was on point, and the server made sure as much. He is the only reason that I would give them a two star, and not a one star review. Next time I want a vegetarian brunch in berkeley, I'll defer to the guerrilla cafe on shattuck.

I was pleased to find this place was all veg. Nice. Had a living social and is right near work, so the boy and I went for a quick dinner. I agree with others, the prices are a tad inflated. We got the jalapeno poppers-which basically were amazing. My boy's spicey mac and cheese was pretty good. I think I got a great deal of 1/2 sandwich, small cup of soup, and nice green salad with topppings for $8.95. It was the perfect portion. The tomato soup was good, although the texture was a bit heavy and felt almost like a really good pasta sauce to me. 

The decor was diner-disco, fine. The wait staff was attentive. One guy was great and the other waitress would not leave us alone and was as awkward as awkward is. 

Good for a lunch spot or quick dinner...although I might choose to stop by Jupiter's instead...unless I'm craving a milkshake.

When they write chicken, they really mean "chicken". I'm not a vegan or vegetarian by any stretch of the imagination, but they have pretty decent burgers and excellent fries. In general, food is pretty good and will definitely try one of their milkshakes in the near future (at $6 it was a little pricey). If you want a dripping, juicy, meaty burger, look elsewhere.

I'm a sucker for retro diners, and a veg*n diner is right up my alley... but every time we go, it's always a little disappointing. The service is bad (even when it's empty), and the prices are high. The music is loud and often upbeat, even when it's empty, which isn't very enjoyable.

I have to say, I don't think it's really hard to make diner food vegetarian-- meat substitutes are everywhere (and this place makes full use of them), and dairy and eggs are the basis of diner food. But it's hard to make diner food interesting without the cheese and eggs. I wish there were better vegan options-- the "Fakin" faux bacon is just frozen Morningstar Farms pink smokey-flavored cardboard instead of something higher quality like tempeh bacon; bring back the marinara sauce for the zucchini sticks; the lack of vegan hot fudge is just disappointing-- and slightly lower prices.

I especially wish there were some decadent vegan desserts. Apple pie is nice, but not hard to do. Why not make those delicious dairy-based desserts dairy-free? Save the planet, shower the vegans with some love, and make the lactose-intolerant happy.

The Good: Super tasty food!   I love the Jalapeño burger.  Order extra chipotle sauce to dip your skinny fries in.  You probably can't go wrong with anything on the menu taste-wise.

The Bad:  Service is hit or miss and they always seem understaffed.  Parking is hellish.  And the decor / theme is... uhh Space-Cowboy meets Che Guevara.

Definitely a cool setting to get your grub on. The tables are like shadow boxes full of retro pop stuff. It was cool looking at everything, plus it keeps you occupied while you wait for your food. I liked that it was all vegan/vegetarian diner food. And it all tasted pretty good. Their shakes were tasty though. We were too stuffed to finish them but it was no problem because we got to take 'em to go! Usually, if I can't finish a shake at a restaurant, I don't take it with me because it usually melts or isn't as good by the end of my meal anyway. But not here.
We eat here almost every weekend. There are very few bad entrees here, so go ahead and experiment. So glad they expanded to Berkeley!
WOW, incredible! Great place for omnivores, vegetarians, and vegans. Caters to everyone!
I make a really good veggie burger at home but their California Burger was Heaven. Great vibes, terrific waitstaff all add up to a best bite for the bux.

Nice little joint, full of delicious types of vegetarian food that can still be satisfyingly gut-busting, so be careful you don't translate vegetarian as healthy when it comes to downing some cheese quesadillas or fried "chickn" sandwiches. I protest too much...it's good stuff.

The beer here is good, sort of cloudy and sweet in that organic local beer type of way. The people who work here are very friendly. The only bummer here is the you-need-a-key-attached-to-a-giant-novelty-item-to-get-into-the-restroom situation. I guess it's related to the density of itinerants, vagabonds, and uncouth students in the neighborhood.

I really want to like Saturn cafe, I really do, but the 5 or so times that I've gone I have walked out disappointed. I think Saturn Cafe is a much better experience for vegetarians than it is for vegans. The only two things I have had at Saturn that were good are their fries and their milkshakes. That's it. Last night I ordered potato tacos. The tacos came and they were just potato tacos, no salsa, no lettuce, no guac. It came with a side of black beans and a side salad. My biggest complaint is that everything is so bland. I never use salt shakers, but I have to at Saturn. The beans didn't have any seasoning and the salad dressing (tahini) was so light that I couldn't taste it. Add that to my taco shell filled with potatoes and I was just all around confused. Sadly, my mom and I bought several groupons here, so we feel that we have to use them, but there are way too many great vegan restaurants in Berkeley to waste money on so-so food. I hope that they will one day expand their vegan options like most of the other restaurants in Berkeley. I mean, even Gather has more vegan options than Saturn and they are a meat serving restaurant!

The food is super yummy, not amazing but pretty darn close. The prices are okay, sometimes I think a little more pricier than I like. I LOVE the decor and vibe here. It's not as cool as the Santa Cruz location, but pretty close. I had the taquito plate (4 taquitos, guacamole, brown rice, black beans, and salsa) and the spicy appetizer sampler plate. I also ordered The Pack (2 corn dogs and fries either steak cut or thin) and a vegan cupcake. Yes, yes I eat ALOT, let's move along now. The cupcake was chocolate w/ raspberry frosting and it was pretty awesome for something that was vegan I won't lie. I've been craving vegetarian corn dogs for the longest time and I couldn't wait to chow down on this and my gosh it was SUPER yummy! My steak cut fries were delicious also, but I found my taquitos to be a little over toasted and the salsa was eh. Everything they seem to serve seems pretty healthy and it wasn't too crowded on a Sunday afternoon. Our waitresses/hostess were super friendly and would stop by to check up on us to see how we were doing and etc. Definitely would come back if I was in the area, however I still do prefer the original location in S.Cruz. :)

Friendly greetings and great diner food, especially the sweet potato fries, egg dishes, nachos, ice cream.  But, as I would advise at any diner, I don't suggest the "entrees" -- stick with the diner-style foods.  Example:

My friend ordered the "peanut royale" entree, which the menu describes as "seasonal organic vegetables...with a mildly spicy peanut sauce..."  In Berkeley, you would think these veggies would be fresh, not frozen, and maybe be a little crisp, but instead they were soggy and obviously pre-frozen.  Instead, the dish was simply a plate of mushy (boiled?) broccoli and cauliflower drenched in a flavorless, runny peanut sauce, with some rice and tofu mixed in.  Blech.  I think Saturn should just take this item off the menu.  And they should have offered to replace or comp it when my friend politely complained, instead of replying, "It's always like that."  

Other than that, I'm glad there's finally a diner in Berkeley that's open late and has yummy diner food, without the meat.

Saturn Cafe is one of my favorite haunts in Berkeley. 

However, I think I am more turned-on by the novelty of a place where I can order anything and not worry about if it is vegetarian or not as opposed to being in love with the food itself. I think some of the food quality could be improved, but some is downright awesome (I recommend the soyrizo breakfast burrito or the cowgirl blues chikn sammich).

I also don't like their beer. In general, I like beer. A lot. But for some reason, the stuff from the Santa Cruz brewery that they carry (which I understand wanting to support local business) is not so tasty to me, and I can appreciate a wide variety of brews.

 Perhaps I should try and convince them to at least switch to a Berkeley or San Leandro brewery for the Berkeley location instead of complaining on the internet.

Hate to only give it 2 stars. The food is good , but I waited 25 minutes for a salad and the place was only half full. The servers did not really seem to care either. They never checked in to let me know how the order was coming, did not apologize for the long wait. Maybe that's just how Saturn is?
Staff was friendly and the food was tasty!!  The california and jalapeno burgers were yummy and the sweet potatoe fries hit the spot!!
vegan shakes were pretty decent.  being lactose-intolerant is tough, but nice to know that there is a dairy- free option for my late night craving :)

I've eaten here quite a few times, but hesitated to write a review. Not sure why. Everything I've eaten here has been relatively ok... nothing too special. However, this past Saturday, I think I finally found the meal that is going to keep me coming back. "Chicken" club with tomato soup. Very comfort-food-esque with a vegetarian twist. Be sure to get a shake as well, they're top-notch.

I really want to give Saturn Cafe four stars. The concept alone (vegan/vegetarian 50s-style diner) deserves applause. The male and female robots on the bathroom doors, as well as the creative shadowbox tables in the booths, almost earn a star on their own.

But the first time I tried to eat here, I actually left because the server never came to take my order or even get me a drink... I waited at least 15-20 minutes.

The second time, I was with my vegan friend who was so excited to be able to get a burger and fries for dinner that he was almost ready to forgive any flaws. Me, however -- I'm kind of a vegetarian patty connoisseur, and my pet peeve is patties that are too "squishy" and ooze out the bottom of the burger when you try to eat it. The California Burger patty was way too squishy (although the flavor was good) and the avocado was not quite ripe. Further, although I am THRILLED any time I can get steak-cut fries, these were not fully cooked in the middle. 

Overall my sandwich was good, not great, and I really wish this place could work on service and execution a bit to really live up to its full potential. That and, obviously, open a restaurant in San Francisco -- Berkeley's too far to be a frequent stop in our dining repertoire! :)

This place is great all around. Food options from healthy to non, and the fried stuff is just as good, if not better, than at any comfort food restaurant. Sauces are the best. Ranch dressing, bbq sauce, tahini dressing, tofu dip, guacamole, salsa fresca, etc. Saturn has novelties and creative recipes to boot.

The graffiti and the art deco tables are something to see. I was constantly looking around, never bored, and the music was great, too.

It just opened, and the place already looks like a fixture in this neighborhood. Great location and prices and friendly people. An anyone/anytime kind of place.
The veggie burgers are bean-burgers. Somehow mushy & dry at the same time. Not a fan. Points for being a veggie diner, but not impressed otherwise.
i like it! yummy food! i like the atmosphere, too.

This place was great! Went here and the person I was with didn't tell me it was vegetarian tell I got there because I usually am not a fan of vegan/vegetarian resturants but this place is awesome will for sure be going again. the vegetarian food with fake meat products tasted just like it would with real meat had the Avacado Club sandwhich it was HUGE and I ate the whole thing. The only reason I cant give this 5 stars is because im a meat eater and it wouldn't be right. 

Also for guys there are college girls everywhere in this place! Just the view was worth the trip. ; )

Saturn Cafe is delightfully weird (quirky, interesting, whatever you want to call it). The food was great and the vegan cupcakes were even better than I thought they would be. I think it was pretty reasonably priced and the sparkly pink decor is fascinating. :D I was hoping there would be more vegan options, particularly dessert, but other than that it was great and I'll definitely go back!

Good stuffff. 
I like me some vegetarian junk food once in a while...and this is definitely the place to go for that. 
One of the things I really like about this place...the portions are BIG. At first, I was a little bit skeptical about $10 for a sandwich and fries. But really, not bad when you can split a "chicken" avo sandwich with your boyfriend, and both leave full!
This place has a really cool atmosphere as well! I saw some Neutral Milk Hotel and Of Montreal album covers under their cool glass table covers. Me likey.
And, oh yeah, the sandwich and the fries were good too. The fries were extra crispy and oily on the outside...just how good, fatty fries should be!
I can't wait to try one of their burgers or their nachos. Nom nom nom.

Vegan diner!! Woot woot! 
I love my meat but I have to give it up for Saturn Cafe for being vegan. The decor is a little funky, but this is Berkeley, right? Saturn is here for me after a long day in SF, an evening film showing, a boring night in Berkeley, and even after midterms! The service can be slow and sometimes nonexistent, but this place will always have a special place in my heart!

**Must Try**: Appetizer sampler plate! It comes with fries, sweet potato fries, fried zucchini, etc etc, as well as a selection of sauces. Great for groups.

Nacho Fries! Get them steak cut and you won't be disappointed! Served with generous helpings of salsa, cheese, beans, and guac.

French Toast! Delectable even at 9pm. Large portions, super sweet!

Chocolate Shake! Tin included! Much much much MUCH better than the shakes at Fenton's. They'll split one for two people if you ask!

**Meh**: The salads are very generously portioned, but leave much to be desired. The ingredients of various salads don't really come together all that nicely. If you must try one, try the Cowgirl! I, for one, don't really like fakin' bacon :\

Sure Saturn Cafe isn't fine dining, but it is still a decent place to get a meal. I appreciate their emphasis on vegan, vegetarian, and organic food. The organic lemonade was very yummy and the baked Mac N Cheese was delicious! May not have been original, but it was sure yummy!

Our waiter was very nice and polite which always scores well with me!

The decor was a little tacky: sparkly pillars, neon stars pasted to the walls, and different aprons displayed in the front. The tables were interesting though. Each had a display under the surface that had anything from CD covers and posters to t-shirts and books. Was quite entertaining to look at it all.

Lastly, they have recycled napkins and compost-able straws, which is nice to see. (But be warned, the straws crack really easily so you can't squeeze or bend them like plastic straws!)

Overall, good experience. Good food, good people, and good price. :)

So so sad to be giving a vegetarian restaurant near my house a bad review.  But the food just sucks.  I'm sorry, it does.  We've tried twice, the first time we went was in their first week so we thought we'd give em another chance.  And the second time was worse. Everything took forever to come out, tasted like it had been reheated and the salad was a little stale.  The three stars is because at least they are trying- but really need to get fresher ingredients!

Fun atmosphere for brunch-- I just really love diner-style booths.  The french toast is only so-so (just didn't think there was enough flavor and they were a little too dry), but I'm a fan of the spicy omelet with the fake meat.

My friends who had just graduated from Cal were leaving town so we wanted to get lunch. I had work and I literally work across from this place, so we decided to meet here. 

The atmosphere is pretty nice. It's always crowded every time I pass by and when I went in to eat it was no different. We did not have to wait though luckily since they have a lot of seating. Their decor is pretty funky but cool in its own way. 

I did not really like the service that much. Our waiter seemed kind of out of it. He brought us 2 napkins when we were 3 people. When we asked for a third one he disappeared for a long time and seemed to not remember so we had to flag down the buser( who was nice!). 

The food, however. was delicious. I got their jalapeño burger with fries and it was super yummy. Their steak cut fries are really unique and good quality, not like the ones you get at usual joints. I loved it. I think my friend got the avacado burger and said it was too much lettuce but except for that really good. The food was brought out pretty quickly too. I was able to be seated, down food and leave in 40 minutes which is always good if you are out on your lunch break:) 

Overall, a pleasant experience and I will surely return. A nice vegetarian diner.

I was a huge fan in Santa Cruz and am so glad there is now a restaurant in Berkeley. The staff are always friendly, quirky, and fun. I love the food here: my usual is the nacho fries with a peanut butter/chocolate milkshake. However, I've tried much of the menu, from the burgers to the salads, and the food never disappoints me. For me, the prices are more than fair for the quality and quantity of food you get. This kind of is my go-to place: I get a milkshake to celebrate finishing writing projects, and I go here to console myself when I've had a bad day. If you're looking for a fun place with delicious food, Saturn Cafe is definitely worth checking out.

This place has the most amazing guacamole! I have tried several of the appetizers and the sweet potato fries with wasabi are fantastic. I have yet to try their version of the veggie burger but everything I have had has been outstanding.

Great diner food choices for a vegetarian. Brunch is served all day. Prices are reasonable with big portions. I had their Space Cowboy Burger which could not have been more satisfying. I will try all of their Mud Pie flavors.
Super friendly staff too.

I went here tonight with my pre-optometry group for their spring banquet.  I tried the mesquite "chicken" cutlet burger with fries and had coffee ice cream for dessert.  I haven't had too many vegetarian or vegan dishes, but the burger was quite tasty, moist, and I'd definitely like to come back here soon.  :)

Saturn is an excellent vegetarian diner.

We came here for vegan brunch; the soyrizo and vegan pancakes (with real maple syrup) were completely delicious. They really make amazing, well-thought-out dishes here, and I can't wait to come back... Next time, I'm going to try something from the full lineup of veggie burgers.

The service was also amazing! Everyone was really warm and inviting and made the overall experience twice as good as it would have been otherwise.

The decor is adorable -- pure space age kitsch. If you don't like silver glitter and FontDiner typefaces, you should steer clear. But I loved it. =)

The coffee was the only downside for me, but only because they didn't have my preferred coffee paraphernalia (skim milk and Splenda).
'
Other than that, excellent experience, will be back often.
Pumpkin pancakes with real maple syrup = one satisfied New Englander!

Saturn is on the line between 2-3 stars.  I'm calling it a 3 because I always like to support any restaurant that exclusively serves vegetarian items and makes it easy to know which items are vegan and/or can be made vegan.  Saturn was strong for this--if this is important to you, give them a try.

The diner atmosphere was "cute" and despite a truly spacy hostess, the waitress herself was friendly and helpful.  

The food was ok, but I wouldn't go to great lengths to have it again.  Next time I'm in Berkeley, I'll probably be looking for another vegetarian place to compare this to.

Pretty good food and service.  Skinny fries were delicious.  Loved the buffalo sauce on the jalapeno burger.  The fried zucchini sticks came out as a log cabin.  Awesome robot paintings on the bathroom doors.

Once their "space lounge" opens, it'll be a great place to go for beer and bar food.
Best fake chicken mini burgers in the bay.  After your meal walk down the block to cinnaholic for a sweet sweet cinnamon bun.
I actually really liked the eggs benedict here. Didn't realize this place was vegan! Haven't tried anything else but judging from the eggs benedict I had, I really liked it.

We just tried this place for the first time because we had a coupon. The decor was fun. The waitress was very nice. They even sat us at the table with legos and micro machines (pretty cool conversation piece!). But the food was unimpressive. I ordered the banana walnut pancakes and a side of eggs. The pancakes were soggy, I couldn't finish them. Was cool that it came with real maple syrup, but just didnt make up for the texture. My bf ordered the southwestern omelet. He thought it was just ok - disappointed that it didn't mention toast but came with white toast, and he would have requested wheat vs white. And his potatoes were on the burnt side. In general the place is clean and brightly lit, but don't expect the food to be higher quality than diner food.
Saturn is still waiting on its beer license.

This is by far my favorite place to eat in Berkeley! They have the best vegetarian/vegan food that I've had.  There's a great selection of stuff, and the kind of stuff that you wouldn't expect to be Vege/vegan.  

The beer was also really good, organic.  And the wait staff was very attentive and friendly. I will definitely go back again soon.

They also have great seasonal specials like pumpkin ice cream, which can be made into a shake and chipotle corn chowder for their soup, among others.  If you are into veg/vegan food you should give it a try and even if you are just into diner food you should try it as well.  It was pretty amazing!

Great food - all vegetarian. Great service. Vibrant atmosphere. We drank their cola & hibiscus cooler - booth great. For food we had the santa fe salad which was incredible. The jalapeno burger with thin fries was equally good. The mac n cheese was bland, so I won't order that again. The mini madness was a chocolate delight.

Their BBQ ranch 'chicken' sandwich deserves 4+ stars in its own right. They use Quorn, aka the best texture for faux chicken ever, and manage to perfectly marinate it in BBQ sauce. The homemade ranch was the 2nd star of the show, I'd probably buy it in a mason jar if they sold it. It was incredibly fresh tasting and wasn't super thick. Saturn just keeps getting better!

Great food, great service. 
BEST fries. BEST vegan milkshakes! I suggest the peanut butter one!
Want more vegan options- my only complaint!
Vegan cheese (daiya!), vegan breakfasts, pancakes, french toast, a vegan chicken patty....please please!

Great concept and cool diner environment - as vegetarians it felt great to come to a place with no risk of meat stock in the bean or rice etc..

But the food was quite disappointing - maybe it was just lack of good ingredients but the tomato and avocado in the eggs benedict were completely tasteless and the sauce was bland too. Grilled cheese was just ok too.

3.5 stars. Saturn cafe is pretty good for what it is, great, even--house made veggie burgers, with lots of cheese and guac and onion rings and fake bacon to make them palatable... fries and milkshakes look good, but I didn't try them this time. 
I was disappointed because in spite of being vegetarian, I felt the menu wasn't very health conscious --buns on the burger were white, no option for whole wheat, my friend's salad was leaf lettuce, no option for more healthy greens like spinach or arugula, and I couldn't go near the coconut soup (the only option today) because of the saturated fat in coconut. Surprisingly, there aren't a lot of healthy vegetarian options in downtown Berkeley, and unfortunately this place is more of a splurge (both for the pocketbook and my cholesterol count) than a go-to staple.

There's something really bittersweet for me about finding a fabulous restaurant when visiting a foreign city.  A local friend introduced me to Saturn Cafe and let me tell you, it almost made me cancel my plane tickets home.  Who needs friends, family or a day job when you have some of the best vegetarian sandwiches I've ever eaten?

We split the "chicken" avocado sandwich and the barbecue "chicken" sandwich.  They were both delicious in completely different ways.  The former had a perfect mix of flavors and textures - rich avocado, chewy chicken, sweet tomato, smoky gouda, sharp bacon - all on lightly buttered, crispy toast.  The barbecue chicken was soggy with barbecue sauce and mayonaise, but that somehow only made it taste better.

I briefly considered forgoing the fifth star, as their much touted blueberry ice cream tasted distinctly vanilla, but then I remembered that the table we sat at contained a lovingly crafted Lego display of robots, deep sea divers, and giant squid.  In fact, each of the tables is uniquely decorated - it's worth going there for that alone.  So 5 stars it is.  I only wish I could take it back to Boston with me!

I've only ever been here for garlic fries and the dessert.

The fries were covered in fresh minced garlic (nice!), but it seemed a little overwhelming even for a garlic lover like me. The fries were chunky (think steak fries) and pretty good otherwise. Probably a 3.5.

But the reason I always come back here is for their delicious desserts! I always get the supernova. 2 scoops of dutch chocolate and vanilla bean ice cream topped with their special hot fudge, cookie crumbs, nuts, and whipped cream. All over an organic banana. 5 stars!

It's also nice that they're open late even on weeknights.

Love that I can feel like I'm eating at a "normal" diner but it's all vegetarian! Cool decor, nice people...food is just your typical diner food ( don't expect gourmet ) its more for the atmosphere and showing your non-veggie friends that we have fun choices too!

Mother's Day Brunch, perfect! I am a fan of Saturn Cafe! 
Three different items, three delicious meals. Try the Bourbon St Omelet with Gouda, or the Muffinator or for vegan, try the Rosarita Scramble. Wow, presentation and taste will keep your coming back. Throw in a glass of fresh squeezed OJ, you are set for the day.
Parking is on the street, worth the effort. Service was friendly, water glass was never empty. 
As for their diner decor, comfy booths, spacious, lots of windows to people watch. Located across from the UCB campus, get there early, it fill up f-a-s-t!

I love Saturn Cafe! Honestly, if you are a vegetarian or meat eater, try their chicken avocado club sandwich, it is delicious! I am not normally a fan of fake meat but this was amazing. Also, their thin-cut fries are delicious! 

Also, the table decor is pretty awesome. 

So why the 4 stars? Well, I must admit, not everything on their menu is so great.; for example I would not encourage you to try their Mexican dishes.

I hated this place when I first tried it, I got the Guacamole Burger with the thin-cut fries. I expected a lot more from it because all my friends raved about this place. But all in all, it was tasteless and unappetizing. My friends dragged me here again, and I tried the spicy mac n cheese, nachos, and THEIR CHOCOLATE FUDGE BROWNIE SUNDAE!!! ahh at first I thought it tasted kinda strange (the sundae) and then I was in heaven by the end :D AND their nachos are surprisingly deliciousss! However their Mac n Cheese disappointed again. If I come here again, I'm definitely coming back for the nachos and the sundae. 
Overall, its fairly priced and a fun, casual place to hang out with friends. It's not on my MUST GO BACK list but I wouldn't mind coming back.

God this place is so amazingly good. I try to come here at least once a week and the different foods I have tried never disappoint me. 
Also every single server I have had is phenomenal. Those guys really don't miss a beat. I would really recommend pretty much anything on the menu. The house made patty I'm not really a fan of, but they always replace it with the grilled patty which is awesome. And they have wifi. So awesome.

Unfortunately things at Saturn are changing, and not for the better.  They've changed their breaded chicken, their house made patty, and their delicious 'award winning' fries. It seems like they are catering to vegans which is a little disappointing because vegan food is bland just like what Saturn is becoming. C'mon Saturn go back to your roots! The service is still great, they just need to step it up on the deliciousness of the food.

Came here after a yelp event across the street. Great, friendly servers took immediate care of us. Love the retro diner decor. The skinny fries were excellent -- perfectly crispy, though they could have used more cheese -- and came in a humongous portion reminiscent of the late, great Ann's cafe, the ultimate more than anyone could possibly finish eating experience. My friend's steak fries were good as well. I loved the quesedilla but she wasn't at all fond of the soy-type burger. As she said, we'll both definitely want to return soon, just not for the burger ever again.

Came here for a club banquet..huge room! Ordered the Peanut Royale. Thought it was OKAY..thought it was slightly bland but still satisfying and definitely tastes "healthy." =p

The mud pies are DELICIOUS. definitely recommend trying one :)

Simply terrible. Until Saturn Cafe, I have never before exited a restaurant thinking "I hated this place and I hate my friend for taking me here."  

The food was alright, we went to accommodate vegetarian friends. But the problem was the surly hostess and terrible music. They only had one waiter working who took 30 minutes to get to our table. The hostess just stood there and did nothing, refusing to take our order. Also, for some reason they had a "band" playing in the back room. I literally had to leave every fifteen minutes to flee from the headache inducing "music." Not only was it too loud to even have a conversation, it was baaaaaaaaad "music" (calling it music is certainly a stretch). Why did they have a terrible band playing? I have no idea. 

Maybe I'm not their target demographic so I couldn't appreciate to the music.  I guess this place appeals to hipsters because it's so bad? I mean, the food wasn't good, the decor was tacky and the ambiance was awful. Maybe I just "don't get it" but mediocre food, crappy service, and a terrible experience warrant a bad review IMO. Two stars because once the waiter did come to our table he was great and the food came out quickly.

Great place for a cheap, healthy meal but in a clean surrounding and with great service! I love that the menu is vegetarian and is super affordable - my friend tried the heavenly eggs benedict and indeed, it was heavenly. Another friend got a burger with fries and let me tell you - those fries are addicting. I got a soup (tomato bisque), half sandwich (the "chicken" avocado club) and salad - for 9 dollars it's a great deal and a pretty substantial amount of food. The soup was amazing as was the sandwich and the salad fresh and generous. 

I definitely want to go back and try some other items, mainly, a milkshake (which apparently they won awards for) and more of the breakfast items!

Good vegetarian burgers with yummy fries at a retro diner...very good but not good enough to turn me vegetarian. 

2.5 stars for the burger, 4 stars for the fries. I'm not a big fan of fake meat, so I'm glad all their burgers come with sauces, mushrooms, guacamole, etc. to provide some form of taste. My guacamole burger was okay, though I wish it had a little less onion taste. The buns are so-so, kind of flaky and dry. The thin cut fries are ridiculously good, and probably one of the best I've had in Berkeley.

$9.50 for a burger; I would rather spend half the cost on a burger with real meat (because I'm not vegetarian; If I were, this would be my favorite restaurant for sure)

The vegetarian/vegan milkshakes are great, and taste just like any other non-soy milkshake. The mint milkshake is very palette cleansing

The restaurant is a retro and upbeat diner decorated with lots of sparkles and astronomical/Saturn references. I almost expected the servers to start rollerblading. Service is excellent; all the employees there were friendly and fast (5 minute wait between ordering and eating!)

WILL I come back: probably not, maybe for the fries though
WHY not: Since I'm not vegetarian and prefer real meat, Saturn Cafe isn't a good deal or good match for me

NOTE: their sundaes looked pretty freaking good, even from a distance
Been here a few times.  Solid service but kinda bland food. However, I am an omnivore so that may be a contributing factor.  Kitschy decor, good hours..

I actually came here because I had a coupon for 20% off. I didn't expect this place to be vegetarian, but even better! 

i ordered the FLT and at first, I didn't expect it to be good but it was pretty good for fake bacon. It had a lot of flavor and actually filling. I give this restaurant credit for keeping healthy alternatives for, otherwise, fatty fast food.

So good.  It's exciting to go to an all veggie place with a ton of meat substitutes and options overall. The jalapeno burger (substituted w/ a chix patty) is tasty. No bad experience with wait time or staff. The place overall is pretty hokey and not that inviting appearance wise, but it's nothing that would keep me away.

I love the concept of a space-themed vegetarian diner. I appreciate that not all of the menu items are super healthy. Vegetarians and vegans want satisfying junk food too, now and then! In walks in their vegan mint chip milkshake. Ah, I am such a huge fan of this shake! The fries at Saturn Cafe are also seriously addicting. The fake bacon is intriguing and delicious, though it's very cracker-like and therefore hard. I love the FLT sandwich but that fake bacon hurts the roof of my mouth. Maybe they can cut it into smaller pieces because it is delicious but is just too hard to bite into when there are several pieces stacked on top of each other. :(

My favorite item on Saturn's menu is the space cowboy burger. I also really like the chicken avocado club sandwich, jalapeno burger, and, as I mentioned, the FLT. Overall I think their menu is solid and fun, with a mix of healthy dishes (lots of good salads) and more indulgent ones. The prices aren't cheap but the portions are also huge and I frequently take some of my food home in a to go box, so I think it's worth it. One minor complaint is that they seem to be out of an ingredient practically every time I go there. Maybe I just have bad luck, though.

The service at Saturn is always fast and the waitstaff is always attentive and upbeat. 

The atmosphere in Saturn Cafe is also awesome and puts me in a cheerful mood every time I go there. The decor is really fantastic. This is one of my favorite spots to catch up with a friend who I haven't seen in a long time. The vibe is just so conducive to good conversation and overall happiness.

I used to go to the Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz approximately one million years ago when I was a student at Berkeley, headed out for the weekend.* They were open late and I could eat anything on the menu, so exciting! When I heard they were opening a satellite in Berkeley, I was both excited and fearful: was I remembering my midnight diner runs with rosé-colored glasses?

One early Saturday morning after a run of errands in the neighborhood, my sweetheart and I popped in at opening. We have somehow turned into those people who'd rather take in an early brunch than a post-pub late night snack. I don't know. If I had a lawn I'd chase those darn kids off it.

The service was prompt, attentive, and friendly; the decor was bright  and retro (my sweetheart: "garish" but also "excited to eat anywhere that isn't Herbivore"). The coffee wasn't great, but  I wasn't expecting it to be. I got the French Toast (vegan!) and it was delicious, spiced and slightly sweet. I think they use a pumpkin base? Is it bad that I couldn't tell? Or good? Either way, it was tasty, not at all soggy, and I appreciate that it is made with a whole grain bread. Our server made sure to check and see if I wanted vegan butter as well. This is especially thoughtful since I overheard him talking about eating fish and chips, so I'd assume he isn't a vegetarian of any stripe but understands the finer points. My sweetheart got the Huevos Rancheros which were "decent, eggs a little overcooked, probably try something else next time." The pricing is incredibly reasonable - I don't know that we've ever spent less than $20 for brunch anywhere else and been satisfied.

I'm super excited that they do takeout too, for nights that nobody feels up to cooking - we'll definitely be back to try that out as well back for brunch againl. But probably not for dinner, 'cause of those darn kids.

*here's a bummer: the jitney seems to have been discontinued!

I love that there's a Saturn in Berkeley and I come here on the regular for dinner and brunch. I don't usually go for the burgers as they tend to be little on the low side of my expectations, but things like the nacho fries keep me coming back. I mean c'mon, where else are you getting vegan nacho fries?! My favorite thing on the menu is now the breakfast burrito. It's got scrambled tofu, soyrizo, potatoes, guac and vegan sour cream, and it's just so tasty that I'm often stricken by cravings for it.

Cheap, gut-busting veggie food and organic beer. No complaints here.

i don't want to like saturn as much as i do, but man i could eat the jalepeno burger with sweet potato fries like every damn day of the week and never tire of it. sure, i'd weigh 40000 lbs but that is why i don't... the servers here forget things like they are stoned out of their gourds and the decor looks like a john waters 1950s gaudy nightmare but please keep shovelling sweet potato fries into my face hole.

I asked for coffee at the end of my meal. Then I needed it to go. The lady at the coffee bar said it was "no problem" to put it in a paper cup and did I want it topped off? While this seems like an everyday, mundane exchange, I find that this very basic customer-oriented service is very scarce these days. Saturn seems to have a lot of enthusiastic, happy people working there. 

Also: nacho fries. Oh man...there was never a problem that a plate of nacho fries couldn't solve. Note to owner: please introduce some sort of "Fatty Special" = Nacho Frings featuring thin and steak fries and onion rings. Served on a special shame plate.

I won't do Saturn Berkeley the disservice of comparing it to Saturn Santa Cruz. (Berkeley has a better/cleaner vibe.)

As a vegetarian diner, it has surprisingly few vegan options. However, some of those options are well worth it (ESPECIALLY if it is after dark when Berkeley seems to shut down).

Vegan milkshakes! Vegan burgers (not a highlight). Vegan nachos!.. Let's spend a moment on the nachos and nacho fries. I prefer the nacho fries as soggy fried potatoes are superior to soggy tortilla chips. All the fixins are here! Beans, guac, tomato, onion, and something similar to a tahini cheese that blows my damn mind! 

Three stars might seem not that great. The nacho fries are almost enough just by themselves to push Saturn to 4 stars but I had to keep calm.

I happened to drive by one day and almost got into an accident because I saw Saturn Cafe! In Berkeley! Having gone to UC Santa Cruz, and a regular of the original Saturn in my collegiate days, I called up some UCSC alumni friends who had also migrated to the east bay to make a trip there.

We arrived at Saturn in true Santa Cruz style (we basically HAD to pre-game), and were pleased to see some of our favorites on the menu: the Pack, FLT, mud pie, shakes with graham crackers...
Sadly, some things were missing (chix parm! where did you go?!), but it was all good. Lots of things changed since we graduated. ($6.75 for the pack?! WTF!!!)

To my relief, they had the same tofu spread for the nachitos that I would KILL for. No, really. It's that good.
And I don't know what they do, but they have the BEST ranch dressing in the world. I can almost drink it. I stopped eating ranch dressing after college because nothing compares to Saturn's ranch.

I'm also glad to see they kept the same motif of decorated tables. I want to sit at the Lego table next time.

Being new, it was definitely weird seeing things that were new. The vinyl seats weren't cracked, the chairs matched, the paint was fresh... Too bad they don't have a juke box.
And the waitress was hot. If I were a college student again...


This place can never replace the original Saturn in our hearts, but at least I can drive 15 minutes instead of an hour and a half to get some good-ass vegan nachitos and/or steak fries with amazing ranch dressing.

Before I moved to California from Europe, this is how I imagined a typical cafe would be here. Great food and service, and everything is vegetarian. 

Well, there aren't many places like this; it's far easier to find chicken wings, steaks or Mexican mystery meat. 8% of Californians call themselves vegetarian, so where do they all eat? Are they too polite to complain at getting one item on the menu they can eat, and they have to ask nicely to find out which one? It's a mystery.

The Saturn Cafe's new location is just as good as the Santa Cruz version, and a lot closer for those of us in the Bay Area. Park at the parking garage round the corner from the restaurant: $3 for 2 hours. Go, give them your money, and eat well.

Who in their right mind thought a Vegi Diner was a good idea? Some sadistic crunchies from Berkeley apparently.

I drove past this place, and thought I could take the family in for a quick and tasty dinner...I walked in salivating for a big bloody hamburger with bacon and some steak fries...it's a Diner right?  Apparently NOT! I ended up having a salad instead At least they kept the tofu and fakey bacon off. 
I was appalled to see biscuits and gravy on the menu. I guess the crunchies can pretend they are eating real food like the rest of us. Povrecito crunchies. 

Saturn cafe gets 3 stars because the salad was fresh and as tasty as salads get, and my kids ate all their Mac and cheese. Hmm,  I wonder if it was chofueese?

OMGAY!!  My prayers has been answered!  Saturn Cafe and I go way back in Santa Cruz.  I don't remember who or which deity told me about this amazing vegetarian diner, but suddenly I found out awhile back that the owners decided to magically create a location in Berkeley.  Wonderful decision on their part.

My fave item on the menu is the chicken avocado club sandwich.  With the bread grilled with a little oil goodness and packed with fake chicken patties and veggies, it is comfort food to the max!  Their battered fried fries are to die for and so addictively sick.  (wait can I use that word (sick) when it comes to food?  Sorry I'm clueless sometimes...wait...take that back...i'm clueless most of the time!! ;D).  

Ok so this part deserves it's own separate paragraph isolated with spaces before and after.  My most recent visit (5 visit so far which is a lot since I'm avoid east bay and a big SF snob) I had the most delectable mud pie with coffee ice cream, perfect crunchy crust, topped with chocolate liquid lines.  Oh (wo)man!!  I could have died after eating that dessert.  It was murderously delicious!

I also tried the sliders.  While I loved their homemade veggie patties, it seemed a bit dry mostly the bread.  The sliders weren't as flavorful as I would have liked it to be.

And lastly since I don't consider this a criteria for restaurants in general is the service.  The service could be a little hit or miss.  What happened to smiling staff members in restaurant establishments??!!  Could I have at least one smile, gurl/boy frens!!  It's not that their service is bad; it's just not as good as their battered fried fries.  ShooOOO!

Overall, I am always happy to visit this restaurant whenever I am in Berkeley, which parking could be a bit difficult.  Happy stomach = happy me!!

I am not vegetarian or vegan what so ever. I am stupid. I came craving a delicious burger. I was so hungry, that I believed all diner looking places sold meat burgers. Oh! Did I tell you that I am illiterate to? As I drooled over the menu, look at the Grilled Meat burgers and failed to notice the (V) for vegetarian next to it. Maybe Im just blind! My first bite, had all the components of a burger, a guacamole burger to be exact BUT the patty tasted i have no idea=[ But I used my imagination , and ate the whole thing. I'm disappointed, but I didn't feel filled with fatty fats in my body when i left. I would recommend this place to someone that is V or  VG! 

I wonder if I should become vegetarian because it's soo healthy!
Vegan brunch so good you'll swear it's vegetarian.

The tomato soup is definitely a reason to come here. 

This place is fun, good for groups, and reasonably-priced.

Oh man, what can I say.  It's great vegan food which is hard to find.  It's one of my favorites, but lately it seems like they just stopped trying to improve.  I used to be able to walk in and see new specials, but the ones they have now (urban salad, potato tacos) have been there for at least 6 months.  Their menu is pretty small if you are a vegan, but it was never a problem before when they always had a new special.

Also, I used to come here for the vegan chili on Wednesdays, but now they don't have a traditional rotating soup of the day.  Their schedule fluctuates because their "soup of the day" is now "soup of however many days it takes us to sell all of it", which is ew and hard to plan for on my end.

Their wait staff is either the coolest and nicest people ever, or just plain rude, uncaring, and inattentive.  I've had to take their water and cups from their waiter station after still not having a drink after we received our spicy salty meal.  They also often blast their music way too loud.  I know your music is cool and all, but I'm paying you money to have a nice time on a date and hear conversation.

Finally, their portions vary significantly.  I once ordered the half plate of nachos and ended up getting about a quarter plate size, while sometimes its a 3/4 plate.  

What's the deal?  Where's the love for the food you serve and the people who eat it?  Even H&R block employees seem to be more excited to do what they do these days.

I love diners and I love places with tons of vegetarian options, so it should seem obvious to love Saturn Cafe...however, the overall experience was just okay. 

My hubs and I had enjoyed ourselves at the Yelp Helps event at the David Brower Center across the street, and then when we were good and hungry we popped in to Saturn Cafe. It was pretty bustling, but not insanely packed -- still, we waited a good 15 minutes (menus down, ready to order) and our server still never stopped by. I thought hubs was going to flip out -- he was getting that crazed hungry look in his eyes.

Finally when the hostess came to refill our water, we just placed our order with her because it was clear to all of us that our server was not going to appear (well, technically he was standing five feet away, but he failed to come to our table).

Our food was fine, but throughout the meal nobody stopped by to ask us how the meal was, bring by extra napkins (chipotle sauce + veggie burgers = mess).

For what it's worth, I'd rather go to Rudy's Can't Fail Cafe for diner food.

When diner food is what you crave, it's pretty hard to go wrong with the choices in Berkeley, but Saturn Cafe brings something new to the table with all vegan/vegetarian fare that actually tastes just as good!
