Don't kid yourself by thinking anything on the menu is healthy just because it's vegetarian, but my favorite are the appetizers such as the Spicy Sampler Platter and the Nacho Fries that can definitely feed a whole party. 

As for the burgers: The vegetarian "chicken" patty is superbly flavored and has a nice chewy texture. The regular meat patty is definitely very good for being vegetarian considering a friend's only complaint about it was that it seemed a bit dry, and this was before he knew it was not real beef! My all-time favorite patty is the Saturn veggie patty that's made with actual vegetables because I love veggie patties that don't try to pretend that they're not meat, but embrace their organic heritage.

The service and atmosphere here is great, even though it can take a while for servers to get around to you if it's a busy night (and it often is, who can blame them) and I love the different tables with various pieces of pop culture built in. Great place for late night munchies with friends!

Incredible service! Always such nice people. Super sampler is a selection of fried goodness. The menu is a little expensive, but for the price you get a LOT. I live and work nearby. The late hours are convenient.

The vegan milkshakes here are awesome! Most of the times I've come here, I got a vegan burger with avocado and some skinny fries. :) Classic diner food. Gotta love it! I think once or twice I got some vegan pancakes. They were delicious and served with maple syrup and Earth Balance buttery spread.

Overall, nothing fancy. But if you do come here, you must get a vegan milkshake!

I really appreciated how hard the waiters were trying when I came to Saturn Cafe for the first time this past weekend. The waitress who sat us down brought us our water and stared at my glass for a bit. It was a dirty glass of water, so she hastily brought out a clean empty glass and poured the water in front of me. That was a bit strange. But hey, everyone was very friendly. 

The food? It was mediocre at best. I shared a milkshake and a half order of nachos with my boyfriend as an appetizer. Big mistake. It was portioned for ogres. I felt totally stuffed by the time our burgers came in. 

Needless to say, we didn't come near finishing our food. The burgers were just all right...Nothing too special I suppose. 

I would recommend not coming here for dinner..but maybe for a late night snack if you have a sudden craving for deep fried anything in the middle of the night.

The service was good, I liked the vibe and the menu.  But the food left something to be desired.  I had the taquitos plate...the taquitos were dry and bland and kinda hard, not flaky and chewy and oily like they should be.  The rice and beans were flavorless.  The guac and salsa were okay, but...here's where the restaurant went from three stars to two...

They only have one kind of bottled hot sauce!  It is called "Brother Bru-Bru's African Hot Sauce."  When I asked for any Mexican-flavored hot sauce for my Mexican-style dish (Tapatio, Cholula, whatever) I was told that they have an arrangement with the guy who makes this hot sauce.  WTF?  I tried it, the hot sauce tasted good, just not on this dish.  It just doesn't make sense---a huge chunk of their menu is Mexican-inspired, and hardly any of it is African or Caribbean inspired.  What restaurant in California doesn't have a Mexican style hot sauce?  No sooner do I want an African-flavored hot sauce on my taquitos than I want Tapatio in my Thai food.  You'd think Californians understand that.  Sheesh.

I want to like this place more than I do. We've been at least 6 times now and my husband is a solid supporter. A 20-year vegetarian with a fondness for fries, he's on-board with the American diner experience translated for vegetarians. I find the food to be mostly good. The salads are nothing special, though and the Peanut Royale curry thing I had last time was rather bland. The shakes, however, blow me away. Especially the vegan vanilla-peanut butter. Scrumptious. My fave item is the Cowgirl Blues burger. The service is a bit patchy but generally kind. The kid's menu is very good. In fact, this is a great place to take children. The breakfasts are good but the portions for breakfast items are a little small for the money. Worth a try. Especially if you like veggie burgers.

Been going to the SC one for years, so this was a nice change of pace in that it's CLEAN.

I can't stand the decor, but other than being gaudy there's not anything wrong with it. 

The food is the same as the SC one, just meh, decent. The fries are always odd, reminds me of waaay back when, when I was an omnivore, and Burger King changed over to those weird battered like fries. Pretty much the same thing. I'd really like it if they served plain ones. They also charged me dollar more for Vegan cheddar cheese, but noticed later they put Vegan jack. Oh well.  

Overall; nice people, the bathrooms were clean, the food was junky and good.

I love the Jalapeno burger and I end up ordering the same always. I like their thin fries too. However, my review is not for their food which is available in many other similar restaurants in Berkeley, but for the cool socially conscious events they host!

They say on the cheque that they love us their customers and I truly believe that they love the community and help us enjoy and engage our spirits :)

Saturn Cafe mesa loves you!

Closer to 3.5.

To echo what others have said, the service was really, really great. Our server was genuinely super nice. 

The food is ok. Tastier than other veg places I've been to and I like that it's veg without being pretentious. Eaten there twice so far and great experiences with both. First time I got your standard eggs with fakin bacon and home fries. The fries were kinda blah, but I appreciate the effort with the rosmary. The eggs were fine and the fakin bacon was good, but it's hard to get over the chalky texture. They serve organic Santa Cruz beer, delicious. 

Second time I went for brunch and got the eggs benedict. Very, very good wit avocado and tomato and sweet wheat english muffin. Sadly, my poached eggs were closer to hard boiled. Tasted good, but I miss the runny yolk. :( Husband got the banana walnut pancakes. The tall stack comes with plenty of food, and they were wonderful. Lots of banana flavor, moist, and a hint of cinamon. Good times.

Also went for a school event in their rocked lounge. I hear from event organizers that it was super easy to get the space and it was a perfect size for our party of about 75. A bit loud, but good service and an excellent location in Berkeley (close to campus and BART).

I like the vibe of the place: hip but not hipster, your basic good food. Will be back again and would definitely recommend. And the price is right!

Was wandering around with my friend looking for a place to eat. As we turned the corner a swarm of silver, pink, and kitsch caught my eye. I didn't even bother looking at the menu and declared that we were eating at the diner.

The seats still had some bounce to them and looked like something from a space station and our table had a mix of Lady Gaga and a cover from a Jules Verne book which I thought was cute. I opened the menu to find that it's vegetarian and items can be made vegan as well which is awesome in my book. I settled on the Sweet Potato Fries with Wasabi dipping sauce while my friend got a Grilled Cheese Sandwich with the Pumpkin Soup. 

Food took a lot longer to come out than I would've expected considering it wasn't that crowded. The Sweet Potato Fries were lackluster and didn't have much flavor to them. Seeing how much oil was on the lining paper made me die a little inside. The Pumpkin Soup came out with the consistency of baby food, but I was told it tasted okay. Grilled Cheese Sandwich was good just because you really can't mess that one up unless you burn it. 

Even though I'm sure the requirement is to be a hipster before you can work here, they were actually very nice and our waiter came back often to check up on us. I wasn't blown out of the water but I would come back to try them again for breakfast or something.
Just had their biscuits and gravy and wish I could give them 6 stars! Cheddar-Bacon Biscuits with the most delicious gravy I've ever had. I love this place!!!!

Tricked into coming here by the lovely picture of eggs benedict from CampusCred.. Wasn't even worth the $10 I paid for $20. 

Wait staff was unattentive and slow.. food was below average.. my "heavenly benedict" was far from heavenly, and CampusCred's rendition of it was extremely misleading. Food came out lukewarm. The homefries served with the benedict were tasteless.. I can seriously make better ones myself.. People sitting next to us were VERY weird..

I would give this place 1 star for being the worst restaurant I've ever eaten at in Berkeley.. but I will reserve 1 star ratings for truly TERRIBLE places.

I'm one for happy hour and happy hour was lovely.

I went during their anniversary where we got free cupcakes and this fermented tea drink. The decor and environment is spazzy and unique. I don't know if it's just that day but our server had the cutest barber shop outfit on! KUDOS for that one.

Here, I got the chicken avocado club sandwich and it was delicious, but like every place, ask for recommendations and they'll list you a few customer/personal favorites that you should choose from!

In the back, there's a neat little club-like scene with a dj and bar; would have had no idea that was there if we didn't go use the restroom. Check it out :)

Crispy fries were good.  For a $1 more you get a basketful.  If you ask for a VEGAN chipotle sauce 75 cents, you swear it's not vegan.

Daily homemade soup changes daily is made fresh and very good.

Just swing by and peak inside the decor.  Very nice and "out of this planet"

Well, having gone to the Santa Cruz location so many times I can't help but to compare the Berkeley location to there. It has the same feel as SC, but the food was ok and the milkshakes were not quite that flavorful. I'll definitely go back and give it another shot and update my review though.

I went here with a friend for dinner because I had the Campus Cred deal: pay $10 for $20 worth of food. She got one of their breakfast choices (something-burrito) and I got their Jalapeno burger which is vegetarian. 

I really did not like my food. It was cool because there were these Jalapeno bottlecaps inside, but the burger itself was smushy and the bun kinda just melted away because of the sauce. And the sauce tasted really...weird. Almost watered down, but just also tasting plain weird. One redeeming quality of the meal was the fries though. They didn't mess those up..they were good!

We split a hot fudge sundae for dessert in order to get up to the $20 amount and it was just a normal hot fudge sundae. Like, I feel like I could have made it myself at home.

I don't know. I think Saturn's is kinda overpriced in general. Like my burger combo was about $10 and that sundae was over $5. Their milkshakes looked good too but I think they were about $5 also.

Decor was cute..kinda weird. I think they wipe down their tables with vinegar which is cool because it's eco-friendly and cheap..but it means the restaurant kinda smells weird. 

ONE THING: the bathroom's are hecka confusing. Robots are men and aliens are women...I think. I might have switched those up. I got into the right one by peeking into "Robots" and seeing urinals. Why are robots, men, and women alien?????

CAMPUS CRED FOLKS: Make sure you bring in the text message that Campus Cred sends you with your number or like printout of the confirmation page. They don't let you just give the number.

Tasty food, open late, not very expensive... hmm... the holy trinity of cafes and diners all rolled up into a vegetarian joint that does karaoke on Thursday nights? Whoa.

We tried the taquitos with 'beef' and a burger with jalapeño (note, chrome just corrected that to include a tilda over the n, how does one type that in?) bottle caps and enjoyed them both immensely. The rice and beans that came with the taquitos were okay and the skinny fries that came with the burger were great. Next time we'd get the taquitos on their own and order a side of Mac 'n Cheese or some of the sliders that looked pretty good too.

I'm not a vegetarian but I don't really like (red) meat all that much either so I was kinda excited to try this vegetarian diner out. butttt mehhhhh.

I went with one other friend and we ordered ... kind of.... a lot of food.... i guess. hehe. everything on the menu sounds really good while you're reading it until the food comes out and you realize it's not real meat.  but i won't hold them against that because I mean, I asked for it for going to a vegetarian place.  

We ordered the nacho fries, baked mac n cheese, banana walnut pancakes, and the cheeseburger with bacon (i forgot the name of it - rodeo or something like that) The nacho fries was the best thing we ordered and I wish that was all we ordered.  It's verryyyyy hearty and they load a lot of toppings on there so you get a good bite of beans/cheese/jalapenos/sourcream/etc in every bite.  I wanted to like the mac n cheese because i love mac n cheese in general (and by love, i mean i even love kfc mac n cheese to the best one you can have in the world) but saturn's needed work.  I didn't really taste the cheese part of mac n cheese and it was kinda watery - which i think is the worst.  The pancakes were just regular pancakes that you can make from mix at home.  The burger "meat" was actually pretty good but the "bacon" did not even taste like any artificial meat (or even chicken as most artificial meats taste like to me).  I wouldn't really recommend anything that I got from that list except the nacho fries.  

The service was also just mehhh.  It took them awhile to take our order even though our menus were closed and we were staring down the waiter as if we were about to do a drive-by, straight face like the uc berkeley gangstas we are (har har - yeah, i said it), not even talking to each other to add to the intensity because we'd been ready for awhile.  He came by once to refill our water when we could've used a refill 3 times in the time it took him to do it once.  

However, the price was really cheap.  All that for 27.something.  If i was a vegetarian, I'd probably come again only cause I can't eat meat buttttt otherwise, mehhhhh.

Best Vegan Burgers EVER!

My fave is the Jalapeno Burger (vegan version:  no cheese, no breading on the jalapenos).  It's SO good!  The burger patty actually has flavor and the sauces and all go so well together.  It's got that great greasy feel that is perfect for the morning after ;-)

Vegan Nacho Fries!  - So freakin' Awesome!  A meal in itself, these guys are irresistible!

Thin Cut vs. Steak Cut Fries - Thin Wins.  They are crispy and awesome, but the steak cut fries are pretty great as well.

Bruncy breakfasty items - Vegan French toast is awesome!  The pancakes...well, they taste very "wheat-y" but they're not bad.

I'm a fan, I've been here tons.  I actually took the BART over one day last week just to come here for a burger because I've yet to find a decent vegan burger in SF.

I'd give it 3.5.

I haven't had pancakes for a good two years and was craving it so much that of course I got their two-stack Pancakes. I'm pretty sure I would've found Saturn Cafe's pancakes your typical all-American dining pancakes but I found it to be exceptionally tasty. Really hit the spot well! Satisfied my pancake cravings :) (Wish I got their three-stack instead of two-stack...)

I also tried a bit of my friend's potatoes & toast. It was good too! 

Will def come again to try something else!

We frequented Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz quite often for 3 years while we were students at the University. We always had great memories of Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz so when we found out Berkeley had a Saturn Cafe too we were very excited to give them a visit. 

The Berkeley location is nice. The staff is SO MUCH more friendly at the Berkeley location than compared to Santa Cruz but the food is not as amazing as we remember. 

Perhaps the cooks were just having an off night. More likely, our taste buds have changed over the years, as we now prefer much healthier, less processed foods than compared to our college years. Regardless, we still enjoyed our meals here.

If you're looking for vegan / vegetarian diner type food (burgers, fries, sandwiches, shakes, etc) Saturn Cafe is the place to check out.

With the very pink retro decor, Saturn Cafe is the Johnny Rockets of vegetarian food serving faux burgers, sandwiches and the occasional burrito.

Prices are reasonable, considering vegetarian restaurants usually upcharge (ahem Cafe Gratitude), and the food is standard. For Sunday brunch, the soyrizo burrito was filling and my taste of the fake BLT was satisfactory. Everything's just average.

Service is slow with the exception of the awesome barista. Saturn has a lot of workers, but most of them don't seem to be doing much. 

If you're not a vegetarian, Saturn's few perks are that its open til midnight and the place is so big you'll likely always get seated with a large group. Otherwise, it's an average diner joint.

I've been here as a Vegetarian and a Vegan. I really love the way the place looks, I mean everything from the tables, to the bathrooms! (Robot or Alien?) When I was a vegetarian I really loved this place but now that I'm vegan I'm a little bit more limited to certain things. The last time I was there (as a vegan) I got vegan nachos for a starter and they were really good!! I was never a nacho fan but I will have those any day! My Boyfriend got a vegan jalepeno burger with steak cut fries and I got a bbq "chicken" burger with garlic fries. I'm not a big fan of fake meats so I liked the jalepeno burger a lot better but the bbq "chicken" was really good too. My dad, who eats meat, went crazy over the piece of "chicken" burger I brought home. My garlic fries honestly weren't very garlic-y at all so next time I'll probably just stick to my usual sweat potatoe fries or ask if they can make them extra extra garlic-y (because I like A LOT of garlic :P) 
The only reason why I'm giving this place 4 stars is because the last time I went I really was looking forward to having some onion rings but they weren't vegan. That really disappointed me :[

I thought Saturn had forsaken me.

I was jonesing all Sunday afternoon for their vegan chocolate shake. then I get there and soy chocolate shake is off the menu. Their waiter did offer to bring me a vegan shake made with chocolate syrup and vanilla soy ice cream, but no, that wouldn't hold a candle to their previous chocolate syrup and chocolate soy ice cream and it's chocolatey intensity. 

Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!!!!!!

Despite what I thought was a boner of a menu decision, I mean, replacing soy chocolate with soy mint chip, I mean, c'mon, I had to be honest and let them keep their four stars. 

Because the garden burger was still yummy (so long as you don't try to eat the patty all by its lonesome; it's the totality of the sandwich that rocks)

Because the vegan apple pie was yummy yummy yummy in my tummy tummy tummy (Almost had to dock them a fractional point for the attempted upsell for a la mode, but forgiven as they brought a napkin upon which they placed my dessert tableware, avoiding my squick when tableware is placed directly on the table, thank you)

Because the service was polite and friendly (aside from the upsell attempt)

Because when I made a mess of the garden burger (their flimsy buns remain their downfall), they offered to bring me an extra napkin, which counts as good service

Because they refilled my water glass

Because they played Country Death Song by Violent Femmes (hooray!) at a low volume (also hooray!)

For all that, Saturn Cafe, retains their four stars

After my initial version of this review, I got a very nice note from Jeanna, the front of house manager, saying the Berkeley location never had vegan chocolate. But I was sure both times I got this shake that when I dug into the thickness at the bottom of the container I saw chocolate ice cream. Turns out sometimes the ice cream re-freezes, meaning the vanilla ice cream became chocolate ice cream all by its lonesome. Never underestimate the laws of physics!

Anyway, now that I've edited this review, I need to go back and get that shake.

I don't know what sort of theme they're going for, but it works. Aliens? Sure. Sparkles? Sure. Comics? Okay. 

We had some major confusion over what was vegetarian, vegan and meat. After talking it over with the very nice server, we ordered (everything is vegetarian) and oh my gaaaahhh the nacho fries are amazing. Don't worry, I only had a half order. If you get the full, you should share- don't do that to yourself. 

The shakes are ammaaazzzzinnnnggg. Fries are awesome too. They seem battered ?? They're very crispy.
Interesting place, but why do cheese and lettuce cost so much!

Two words.

NACHO. FRIES.

Oh yes. I got $9.50's worth of nacho fries.  I got a mountain of nacho fries (thin cut) topped with jalepeno peppers, melted cheese, salsa, freshly made guacamole, black beans and green onions. Heaven. And way too much for me to eat by myself, but somehow it fit in my stomach. Next time I'm sharing a plate though.

Everything I sampled that my friends got was equally excellent. The breakfast food definitely looks like a cheap and safe bet. 

Extra star for the sparkly columns and all other zany aspects of the decor (complete with color coded robots on the bathrooms to distinguish gender). 

Come here if you:

1. Aren't afraid of trying an all vegetarian restaurant

2. Dig waiters with awesome hipstery glasses

3. Like water that's closer to room temperature (it's good for digestion)

AND it's open til midnight! Pending approval to be open til 3. 

All I know is, I've got a bunch of vegetarian friends that are gonna love this place. Heck, I enjoy this place very much and I'm a staunch meat eater. 

In sum, HEY SHEEP: travel down below *gasp* Ellsworth *gasp* and discover this delightful place. You won't regret it.

So I was really excited to try this place specially that they advertized it to be a veggie place. So went in to order to go. The staff were really friendly specially the girl behind the counter. So I got fries (it was ok.  I mean how can u screw up a fries).I also got fried zucchini. Nothing special...also got their burger with nuts. When I bit it fail apart it looked more like a ground meet than a burger....it tasted ok. But the price is what got me. It's like over $10 for a burger! Please give me a break its not a gold burger its veggie? So if I ever am hungry for a fries I'll go to Razan at least their fries are made to order. Way tooooo expensive for what they offer.

Went here again for dinner, and still hella good.  Ordered a regular burger with a side of ranch (the BEST ranch in the bay area; you HAVE to get it), and split a chocolate chip cookie dough milkshake with my friend.  I don't know how, but the veggies on the burger (tomatoes especially) tasted like it came from a local garden; and during this time of the year, that's a feat. Service was quick, efficient, and pleasant.  All the staff in general are very personable and nice and the food is still hella good, may be a little pricey, but it's so worth it.

So I knew it was a vegetarian place, and I'm not a vegetarian. I thought from its flashy fun exterior and fun name that it was going to be Out of this WORLD!  I was ready to be sent into orbit about eating veggie.  Instead it was a big ole crash landing.

a) Tasteless.  My soyrizo breakfast burrito was so bland and boring, I used up their bottle of Tapitio on it.  My BF got the nacho's and again, bland and boring.  No focus on flavor or texture, just slop food.  Even the Vanilla ice cream in the sundae was "meh".  

b) Fried?  Whats up with a vegetarian restaurant that seems to be celebrating all things fried and unhealthy?  Its called the Saturn Cafe but its really the Saturn Diner.  And unfortunately its not as tasty as Mels diner down the street.  I was very disappointed in the menu, I was there to make healthier choices and I practically couldn't.

c) Presentation was just bad.  Nacho's looked like vomit almost and the buritto was so lonely on its white boring plate. The Sundae was cute I guess, but it had literally 2 times as much whip cream as it did ice cream or fudge. Not cute.

I really wish this place was better but its a gimmicky non-tasty unhealthy diner that tasted more like Uranus than Saturn.

As a vegan who loves good diner food, I have loved the Santa Cruz location for years. Now that they have this location in Berkeley, they have even more vegan options, like pancakes! Mmm.

I have rarely had a bad experience at Saturn, and I admit I am rather biased towards this place. I especially love chili on Wednesdays, the vegan Buck Rodgers, and vegan chocolate shakes.

Most of my meat-eating friends also like Saturn, though it's not for everyone.

I was thrilled when news broke of Saturn Cafe's arrival in Berkeley. I am life-long vegetarian, so having a vegetarian diner nearby sounded wonderful. My friends who went to school in Santa Cruz said the one there was awesome, plus this one would be open until midnight (which is about as good as it gets for late-night hours in Berkeley). It sounded like a winner!

I've been to Saturn Cafe half a dozen times since it opened, either with friends or by myself, because I wanted to try a variety of food items. I won't be back, and my friends probably won't be either. The food is bland, expensive, and served lukewarm. Waiter service is extremely uneven. I even messed up a pair of pants once because somebody had spilled jam or syrup all over a seat and it wasn't properly cleaned before I was seated there.

But even if I let the service and cleanliness slide, Saturn Cafe deserves 2 stars because of the food:

The veggie burger is served with the most disgusting patty I've ever tried. Even the BK Veggie at Burger King tastes better than this. I ordered a veggie burger with fake bacon, and the facon was COLD and flavorless.

The avocado and cheese sandwich was served soggy and cold. I had to ask my waiter to get it toasted so it was edible. The cheese was surprisingly flavorless.

The nacho fries were decent, but the "salsa" was completely lacking in any sort of spice or hotness. Note to Saturn Cafe: I may be vegetarian, but I do like flavor with my food!

The Peanut Royale is so bland it's unbelievable. I asked my waiter for hot sauce and was given a flavorless swill with a drawing of an African guy on it. This dish needed soy sauce and an Asian hot chili sauce to stand a chance of being good. Alas, Saturn Cafe has neither, so all I could do was put salt on it. :(

Biscuits and veggie gravy are one of my favorite dishes at Pork Store Cafe in the City. Saturn Cafe has nothing on Pork Store Cafe. Not even in the same ballpark.

The grilled cheese is the only solidly flavorful food I've had here. It may have been satisfying, but guess what? I can get grilled cheese almost anywhere. I can even make it at home!

Milkshakes here are pretty good, but they're really expensive if you want cookie crumbs or malt added. Like the grilled cheese, though, milkshakes can be had just about anywhere.

Summary: Don't bother! I really wanted to like this place, but the food is just plain bad and the service is blah. Oh... I complained about the damage to my pants... They apologized and offered to do something about it if I called the manager the next day. I had to call back twice over the course of two weeks to get a response. I was offered a gift certificate but it never came in the mail. I happened to mention it on a subsequent visit, and they did have it on hand. Turns out it hadn't been addressed correctly. Sheesh!

I had breakfast here and it was terrible. 

The service was good, especially given that they had just opened, but the food was a total disappointment. Dry bland crumbly tofu scramble, passable but whatever potatoes, and I honestly can't remember anything else we ate. I love a hearty breakfast, so I was sad. As someone who sometimes feels like I'm being held hostage in "ugh, Berkeley" I can get behind the revolt of vegetarian un-health food, but, like, it still has to taste good.

In the past I've made a lot of empty threats to never return to places but I think I might mean it this time. I waffled between 1 and 2 stars, but the staff was on their game and I guess I wasn't poisoned.

I really wanted to like this place, but just wasn't happy with what I found.  I feel like the restaurant wants to be everything to everyone: Vegan - Vegi - Carnivore - Ice Cream Shop.  Some places can pull it off, but here too many of the dishes just missed the mark.  
The space has a fun diner feel and seemed clean.
Our waiter was WAY OVERWHELMED and I think he lost our order.  
Not only did it take about an hour to get our food, but then when it did arrive it wasn't how I had requested it (onions were raw and the cheese wasn't the type I'd asked for).
The high points: AWESOME hibiscus cooler beverage & sweet potato fries.
Low points: the mac and cheese had a weird chivey flavor and an odd, granual texture; the fried chicken club with faux bacon was just plain and not very appealing.
Middle: Peanut Royale.  I love thai tofu with peanut sauce over spinach and hoped that this would be like that, but instead it was just okay and kind of all over the place.
Maybe we should have gone with breakfast items, oh well.
Hope this place can get their service issues together and can figure out what type of food they want to serve.  If you wanna be eclectic, that's great, but you have to deliver the flavor and bring a better product.

I had recently finished up a kickboxing class and I thought to myself: self, you should eat something healthy.  But I was hankering for a nice and greasy burger.  I shuffled over to Saturn to combine the burger with the healthy.  Boy, was I disappointed!  I got a Space Cowboy.  My fakin bacon looked like doggie bacon.  It was an unnatural red color.  It tasted like plastic.  The patty itself had absolutely no flavor and somehow, neither the BBQ sauce, nor the cheese were able to pinch hit for the lack of meat.  Now the meal did come with a massive side of fries, but even those were lacking in taste appeal.  Only be dipping them in their chipotle sauce were my tastebuds revived.  I was, however, charged 50 cents for the side of sauce.  This was not such a huge burden to bear, but if that's your policy, it would have been nice to put it on the menu or at least inform me of its cost.  I could easily have opted for mayo, which I assumed would have been free.  Our service was less than wonderful.  Despite not being crowded, our waitress seemed a bit distracted.  She finished better than she started though.

Had it not been for the lettuce, my California burger would have had no flavor! The ambiance is a nice diner-style setting, the place is new and clean, but I just couldn't get past this being a vegetarian-only place. Everyone seemed to know but my table.

The fries were good and all the vegetation was fresh and crisp (onions, lettuce, tomatoes, pickles). Like I mentioned, the patty itself was devoid of flavor.

Prices were pretty high too, considering, but I don't usually dine at veggie restaurants, so it may very well have been market prices.

With that said, I probably will stick to Indian Cuisine when I get the craving for vegetarian food.

Honestly, you can probably save yourself money and very, very long wait by picking up a pack of Boca Burgers and hamburger buns at Safeway. At least that way, you'll have a meal of similar quality to what you'd get at Saturn and be able to enjoy it in a quarter of the time.

It took 45 minutes for our greasy appetizers to hit the table and by the time they did, I noticed that the hostess was having to bus tables to try to compensate for the sorely understaffed waiters. The rest of the food was bland, expensive, and cold because it had been sitting around for so long. The restaurant looks like Hello Kitty threw up in it, took her logos, and bailed. Which wouldn't be such a bad thing, really, but at the time of our visit they didn't yet have a liquor license. Just sayin'.

Overall, it was an expensive check for a mediocre meal and a ridiculously long wait. The staff was pleasant enough to interact with - on the rare occasions we were able to catch their attention. I'm going to give Saturn the benefit of the doubt and just assume we came in on a night when a few people called in sick. I'd try them again, but probably only as a last ditch, late night alternative to Taco Bell.

Saturn Cafe has the best Vegan milkshakes I have ever had!   It's great to have it in Berkeley now.   I loved the one in Santa Cruz so I am now covered in my 2 favorite smaller cities.   My favorite shake is the Vegan vanilla milkshake with organic peanut butter added.   Simply divine!  They also serve one of my favorite veggie burgers.
 
I love the new location.   The space theme is cool and the service was great/attentive.
The only issue is that it is not completely Vegan.   As a Vegan, I think it is unnecessary to not go fully Vegan but I appreciate what Saturn has to offer and that it is at least Vegetarian.   If all restaurants were at least Vegetarian, the World would be a much better place.   Still, my rating system reserves 5 stars for purely Vegan restaurants so 4 stars is max here.   My suggestion to Saturn is to shoot for the (5) stars!   (Gosh that was corny)

All business - No pleasure. Don't let the pretty pink sparkles fool you because all that glitters is not gold! The only thing saving this place from getting a one star review is the vegan milkshakes....and that's just because I like that option! The mediocrity of the food saddens me. I loved the decor, why do they have to disappoint me on the food?!?.....The super sampler was blah, and the saturn patty was just so bland and dissatisfying. I could have made a better boca at home on the grill. The space cowboy was a waste of jaw energy. It was just...sad...as was I....turning to the only thing that seemed like it could fix things...a vanilla vegan shake. Yum - but not O...and I wish they had mint n' chip as a vegan option. Also the hibiscus kombucha is just average, like each one of my 4 experiences here. Sad to say it but unless I am really stoned or out of my mind I wont be coming back.................................
..
P.S. the service is always super slow even on deserted nights, so please do keep that in mind....and also the fact that you could just save your money and head on over to Berkeley bowl for better more satisfying options.

Not as good as the Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz. I came to this one with high expectations, because the one in Santa Cruz was BOMB! But the food was alright and the service was TERRIBLE! Had a super bitchy vegan waitress that looked like she was 12.

Had the jalepeno burger, and it was not good. Bun was mushy and had a thick coating of flour on the surface. The vegetarian meat patty was mushy as well and had no resemblance of the texture of meat. Try using textured soy protein or something! (Their patty, as I understand, was made from black beans and brown rice)

I really felt the burgers were way overpriced for the quality. I expected...

- a more decent bun, well-toasted, crispy crust and chewy springy interior...not mushy crap dusted with flour so that it looked like mold
- a vegetarian meat patty that actually has texture (not a brown rice/black bean latke...and not even quite a latke. It wasn't even crispy)
- ripe tomatoes (or at least salt the tomatoes)
- more flavorful greens (maybe arugula or really high quality lettuce)
- and paper-thin sliced onions. You can't put raw onions in a burger if it's thickly sliced!

If the burger had all of the above, then it would've been worth the $10 or so I paid. 

Probably will not come back here until then.

I've been going to the Santa Cruz location for over ten years and was ecstatic that a new one opened.  Sadly, I was disappointed.  The service and food are entirely inferior to that of the original location.  My all-time favorite restaurant dish ever, the vegan nachos, tasted absolutely nothing like those at the SC Saturn.  I couldn't even eat them and when I commented about it to the server she was apathetic.  Won't be back here.  :(

Saturn I want to like you.

You have messed up my vegan orders several times in the past. Please can you at least make all of you vege burger patties vegan (do you really save that much having the one with dairy/eggs in it, would the vegetarians care as long as they can put cheese on top of it, speaking of cheese  how about teese or daiya only)

You mix chocolate syrup with your vegan vanilla ice cream to make chocolate shakes ( a standard diner practice I know), but it tastes so much better when it is actually chocolate vegan ice cream. (herbivore does this and their shakes are superior, sorry they are)

You will probably be around for a while due to your location, but I will only stop by if friends want to go or I am desperate. Perhaps if your food was as  friendly as the atmosphere I would give you a better rating. I do appreciate the attempts at becoming more vegan friendly, hopefully you will continue to work in that direction. 

wait staff is hit or miss, I have had some nice people and some aloof jerks. (but that can happen anywhere.)

We had an awful experience here.  We made a reservation for a big party weeks in advance and by the day of, they lost our reservation.  When we arrived, the service took forever and the food was mediocre at best.  (The kids thought that the fruit salad was salty.)  It was 1:00 in the afternoon (they open at 10) and they were out of many menu items, including cupcakes, which was fairly disastrous since we were at the restaurant to celebrate a birthday.  The service was snotty and unhelpful.  I will definitely not dine here again.

I'm wondering if the Saturn Cafe could use some of the profits from my $10.00 breakfast to invest in seasonings so the food isn't so bland.  Maybe they could spend it on training the wait-staff? It wasn't busy but man I sure would have loved to get my food in a timely manner, which brings up another issue. Maybe you could heat my wife's food up thoroughly, so you know, she could eat it right then and there? I didn't see that there were any take and bake options on the menu so why did you serve it to us like that? I've given this restaurant about 6 tries at all of the times when one might like to eat typically and have been failed. I just don't see what ANY of the accolades are for. I had a friend say "when you go there you've got to get the nacho fries!"  Why not stop wasting time and just go get respectable, SEASONED nachos and the lovely Mexican food place across the street?  To anyone wanting to try this food, if you like well seasoned,  hot food that comes to you in a timely fashion don't come here. However, if you're just jonesing for vegetarian hospital food that was likely purchased at the frozen section of costco... No wait, I still recommend that you go elsewhere. If you're going to eat it might as well be good right?

The food was alright, though nothing to write home about. Both the vegan chocolate and choco-peanut butter milkshakes are dynamite. And I would go back again for the mock BLT, but alas! our server was a wretched witch and treated us like lepers. she didn't check up on us once, and when i requested some spread on the side she huffed and puffed and made a big stink about it. she was just plain nasty. and it was enough to put me off to berkeley's saturn diner for lyfe. LOUSY SERVICE, and the food is just meh. It could never compete with the ambiance and service of the santa cruz location, and as a vegetarian I will never eat at this veg. diner again.

I was so excited about this place because when I went once in Santa Cruz, it rocked.

Service was beyond horrible. Nonexistent and rude all at the same time.

and the worst food I've received in a restaurant since I moved out to the bay area 7 years ago. I actually spit out my California burger. Just being flavorless would be one thing, but turning to the consistency of gluey goopy paste in my mouth actually made me gag.

Ugh. Worst. Seriously, get a snack at walgreens if you're hungry and nothing else is open. This is a serious waste of money.  BLECH.

I've been to the Santa Cruz location a few times, so I was jazzed to see this one open up.

Feeling a little hungry? Try these on for size:

1. Nacho Fries - hello, yummy! They're best with the thin cut fries and large enough to share with up to two people. Who ever thought putting nacho toppings on fries would be so... good?

2. Chicken Avocado Club - a crazy mix of breaded "chicken", avocado, fakin bacon and everything else you'd expect from a club, but without the meat! Triple decker sandwich cut into quarters = messy eating with hands... Order it with the tomato soup!

3. Vegan Breakfast Burrito - burrito stuffed with tofu scramble, served with home fries and soyrizo. A great way to start the day.

I 've experienced slow service a few times on busy weekend mornings, mostly because they were understaffed. My most recent visit yielded a better experience, with my food coming out in less than five minutes after placing my order with the cheery waiter.

Meh, this place was alright. I guess I had higher expectations because I really like the atmosphere.

I came here with a group of classmates, and we had just gotten back from a service trip in Oregon (which was awesome). I guess Saturn is really accommodating to vegans and vegetarians, but I'm not so I guess that's why I didn't really like the food.

All the dishes I tried (my friends' burgers, mac and cheese, and my own fried chicken salad) were flavorless. I didn't even finish my small salad.

And they have a little ATM which charges you extra fees (because they don't take like more than 2-3 credit cards).

Not coming back.

Dear Saturn Cafe,
There was a BIG GREEN BUG in my SALAD, possibly more than one, possibly on my Club Sandwich also. I showed it to you, alive, and you showed the whole staff and laughed and said i get extra protein. Who knows how many bugs i ate, i am a vegan, don't want to eat bugs. I Ordered $25 worth of food and drink alone and you knocked off $2 from my bill.  I have worked in restaurants for 20 years and ALWAYS refund a customer if there are bugs or anything terribly unsanitary or off their diet accidentally in their food. Generally, that is protocol, along with a serious apology if you want the business back. I love this place. But won't go back unless offered a gift certificate to try it again. I have driven to Santa Cruz over the last decade JUST TO EAT THERE...i drove from SF just to eat there this time so , i could be a loyal customer. But, not with no concerns for health department issues. please make amends.
Christie
415 861 6250
i am happy to write another review after another try, on your tab, as it should have been offered whilst i was there. Please do the right thing. Bugs in food is a serious health issue you should consider, not joke about.

Not that great. The sparkled pillars are JUST to die for... Jk. The food might make you want to ... Leave some for the bears.

Great place to take someone who has trouble holding their end of a conversation. Know why?: the decor and themed table tops can distract them and will likely (without fail) encourage them to talk to you about trivial bull shit (if they weren't already).

Dates: Come here if you need a fucking break from a tense date, or need to send the message that you are not looking for anything serious. But only if you are hungry, and can get excited about 20% off your half of the bill. 
Aka: cheap date hot spot.

Otherwise: still blase.

I like Saturn Cafe, which is basically a vegetarian diner.  I'm not a vegetarian but I can always find something to eat there, and it's a really fun place to bring out-of-town vegetarian guests.  They have a gluten-free and soy-free menu, which is really important to me.  I can get a diet cola that isn't made with aspertame.  Also, sweet potato fries!  This is a great place for people with food sensitivities.

Atmosphere is kitschy and fun, and there's usually interesting people-watching both inside and outside.  The only drawback is that it's a bit pricey for what it is.  Service varies, but I've had more good servers than bad.

MEH.

Went here for dinner with some friends and everything was just... mediocre. I ordered the soup of the day, a tortilla-tomato southwestern-style soup, and it wasn't bad. They asked me if I wanted sourdough, whole wheat, or chips with it and I asked for sourdough. I assumed that it'd be from one of the MANY, MANY amazing bakeries from the area (Berkeley sourdough, c'mon!) but it was a piece of sliced sandwich bread. It wasn't toasted but instead just dried out, so it was like eating very stale bread with my soup (I didn't really eat it).

The servers barely came around to refill water so I refilled my own. Not a travesty, I just felt awkward and infringing on their territory.

My friends got the veggie burger, the nacho fries, and the sliders. I tried the nacho fries, which were a great concept, but the fries got soggy almost immediately. I also had some of the plain fries that came with the veggie burger. They were mediocre.

Everything was just... mediocre and slightly flabby.

Our lego table was amazing!
No thanks.  I'd rather starve.

Love the vegan nacho fries as well. Small size (steak cut) can easily feed two as a meal! Very delicious. Very fresh. Also had jalapeno burger. Incredible! :-) 

It's a great place to frequent when staying in Berkeley.

it makes me feel like im cussing at my self under my breath on the floor of my kitchen, and everyone there looks like they write bad hardcore band lyrics, and when they come up to the table they are going to read them to you. it made me feel like an adult baby. but boy oh boy! they can mix some relish and veganase  ! fuck you secret sauce....
buck rogers was just gentrifying space for the white man.
Yucky frozen food for college students and senior citizens.  They buy corn dogs and veggie sausage from trader joe's.

A great place to grab drinks or a snack with some friends.  Casual, no frills dining.

The hibiscus cooler is absolutely delicious and goes great with the nachos that happen to be some of the best I've ever had, which really surprises me as they're vegan!

They've got great organic beers on tap.  The coffee stout is great, but the red bitter (?) was my favorite!  Definitely check those out if they still have them on tap.

I also hear their karaoke nights on Thursdays are fun. The room, with its glittered walls and kitschy decorations, certainly looks like it's got potential for lots of random nights.

I'll definitely be coming back the next time I'm in Berkeley.

This is my go-to Diner Date Place. Great Service, water glasses always full, and amazing specials.
My usuals are:
-Nacho Fries (thin or thick/steak fries): The avocado (which is my favorite), black beans, cheese, sour cream, and salsa work so well on their signature thin fries (which I have a bias towards). A full order is very huge, so order it when you have at least 2 others to share it with. A half order is great for 2 people.

-BBQ Ranch "Chicken" Burger: They make their own special dressings, which compliment the "Chicken" nicely. I often dip my fries into it 'cuz it's so tasty. The patty itself is an (almost) identical substitute for a chicken breast.

-Chocolate Cake: Is wonderful. Nothing else to say on that.

Their Ice cream is very good. Even if it may not be "creamy" like traditional ice cream. It's even better as a milkshake if you can save room for dessert. 

Will update often, since I try a lot of the menu.

This place purports to have two major things going for it: a solid veggie menu and late night hours.  Now it also has beer apparently.  

We came in because it was the only thing open around 11:30 along our trek from the Greek Theater back to Shattuck.  Group of 6, half hour before close.  The greeting that we got was borderline rude.. sort of like, ugh, why are you guys coming in now, we want to close this joint up.  The host/waiter very begrudgingly got us a table in a closed off section, because, guess what, when you're like the only joint open in Berkeley at 11:30 on a Saturday, you're going to be busy.  They were in fact pretty busy.  The rest of the meal continued with a ton of attitude from the waiter, despite us being pretty nice and basically sober.

So how was the food?  Well, they were out of a lot of stuff.  Guacamole, most of their desserts, the normal garlic fries.  The nachos were really great, the chocolate silk pie was gross, and everything else was fine to good (milk shakes, onion rings, beer).  Food quality and portion seemed pretty well aligned with price.

Here's the thing, if your staff doesn't want to be at work late at night and you're not going to have any food left, perhaps you just shouldn't be open.  Your customers shouldn't be made to feel bad for coming in a half hour before close.

San Diego might have set the bar high, but shame on you, Saturn.  Vegan cuisine shouldn't have to cost as much as it does here.  

The food here is decent, but it's no excuse.  Fun decor aside. 

Craving a shake, my boyfriend and I came and paid $6 for what ended up being Trader Joe's Vegan Chocolate Cherry ice cream thrown into a blender.  No joke.  The lack of creativity was startling. 

Berkeley has such a solid base of vegans.  Playing up the novelty of a Vegan option is unethical.  Why punish a good cause?

Same tasty Saturn food  but in a cleaner space.  

I come here when I want to be an unhealthy vegan.  I have to admit  never quite go as bad as I would like to.  My new favorite entree is the vegan breakfast.  It comes with breakfast potatoes, tofu scramble and toast.  I  think it's the perfect size and not an overwhelming amount of food.  

This location seems to have a few different selections then the place in Santa Cruz.  They have a Jalapeno burger (which can be made vegan).  My BF tried this and it was very good.  It was seasoned with Buffalo sauce which I love.  

The decor is space aged, with some lame outfits hanging up.  Although I enjoy clean spaces, I somewhat like the grimy vibe of the place in SC.  Maybe that "aged" look will come in time.  They have a lounge that apparently has karaoke on Thursdays.  I would go if I lived closer, because I adore singing Tom Jones and TLC in front of strangers.

Overall, I had a great experience.  Good Food (as always!) and great service.

Not that great at all. 

I have never really minded vegetarian/vegan food, and actually have wanted to try out this restaurant for the longest time (all part of my trying almost every restaurant in Berkeley before leaving). I ordered a vegetarian burger (the California burger it was called?), made from a veggie patty that was a specialty of the Cafe. All I can say was that every part of my meal tasted bland--the burger had absolutely no taste and I could only really taste the avocado and pickle. The steak fries that came with it were bland as well. Granted, they were huge fries, but were soggy and I could taste something after drowning it in globs of ketchup as the potatoes themselves were bland. Moreover, the veggies (lettuce and tomato) that came with my burger did not seem that fresh; I didn't get that crisp crunch that I usually get when I order a burger from a restaurant. My friends ordered a Santa Fe salad and a mushroom burger, and both weren't too thrilled about their meals either.

The atmosphere was also a little odd. I know they were trying to go for a futuristic theme, but it seemed like the decorations were half done. The walls were mainly bare, with only a few shirts or something hanging over the counter. The tables however, were pretty cool; they looked like glass display cases with cool objects inside of them. 

The service was pretty lackluster; our waiter was cordial, but not particularly friendly. He never really came to check up on us, and it took us forever to grab his attention to get our bill, even though the restaurant wasn't crowded at all. Also, I would say that this place is pretty expensive in terms of getting a burger; everything cost at least $10, including the salads. 

Overall, I'm glad I tried it just to say I have, but I wouldn't go back there again.

I visited Saturn today for the first time.  I liked the "diner" feeling of the restaurant and our server was very friendly and attentive.  My complaint is the really small portion of protein in the cobb salad.  My salad was mostly lettuce and was $10.  It was definitely not a meal.  Very little veg chicken, eggs and blue cheese in it.  I had to order a large side order of fries as I was still very hungry.  Good cobb salads are chock full of stuff.  This was so skimpy that I will not return.
Can't say anything good.  Wait...waiter was nice.  Waste of a meal and money.

Came here to watch some friends improv on Tues night for a free show. When I got there, a sign said that there was a $10 minimum PER PERSON to watch the show. I found out later that improv group was unaware of this underhanded move and that's why I'm writing this review. I won't be eating here again and Saturn's should be put on notice for sucking so hard. And by the way, I would have spent more than ten bucks if I hadn't been given the stipulation at what we all thought was a free show!

I went here no knowing at all it was vegan. As a meat loving person this was a bit of a shock. The menu was absolutely confusing at first since I have little knowledge of vegan food stuffs.

however the food was pretty impressive. I ordered the eggs Benedict and despite its vegan nature, it was pretty good. Nice an healthy, not super cheap, but I actually enjoyed a vegan meal. Its great to see normal food that vegans eat instead of just tofu and veggie patties

So glad to see another veg restaurant on the block!

I really enjoyed the avocado sandwich and fries.  Please please have more vegan items on the menu. 

I was SO excited when I read there were corn dogs on the menu, but totally bummed when I found out they were not vegan :(

Daiya cheese would be a great addition indeed.

I cannot review the food since I walked out of the cafe before our food arrived. I overheard some of the staff making extremely racist remarks, presumably assuming that no one could hear them, about an african-american employee. I was absolutely outraged, and when our server came back I told our server how disturbed we were about the behavior of the other servers and his response was to basically tell me that I must have misunderstood. When I quoted what I heard he was extremely rude about the incident and didn't offer to get the manager. I asked to speak with the manager and he told me there was no manager on duty.
Needless to say, I was shocked, sickened and outraged. Obviously I will never return, but I hope you will avoid this place as well.

Not. Good.  Food.  Vegetarian or not, the food is very mediocre.  I adored the concept, but as my dining companions and I were discussing, it's rare to hear a vegetarian gripe that they can't get enough crappy fried food to fuel their fires, and Saturn makes the assumption that deep in our meat free hearts, all we really want are soy products that aim to resemble meat.  This is false, and nothing about our veggie burgers made me think, "mmm, is this cow?".

Went w/ a party of 6 on a Friday night--the service was quite friendly but totally inattentive--I think they were understaffed--most of us had burgers--we went for their Saturn patty, which is home made--done in the California style.  Came out barely warm and the steak fries were luke warm and mushy.  They had none of the delightful crunch with a creamy center that I know and love from other steak fry experiences. 

Briefly:  

- Steak fries = total tease.
- CA burger = decent patty, but so small!  Not luscious, barely any avocado, the best part was the potato roll it was perched upon.
- Sliders = great concept, weird execution
- Other burgers = PRE MADE.  This is berkeley.  Come on.  You're giving me a food service garden burger?
- Sweet potato fries = weak, weak sauce.  For an additional $2.99, I wanted more than 15 fries.  D-.  And they were thin.  
- Santa Fe Salad = the only item we were served that was appropriately priced--decent salad, though w/ enough fried and cheesy goodies to qualify it as a "salad that will definitely lead to an untimely death" 
- Vanilla milkshake = weird, cloyingly sweet.  Gross.  But looks pretty!

Overall, a 100% disappointment.  For where we are, it's totally unacceptable to get away with passing this slop off as vegetarian food, and I was embarrassed to have taken an out of town European guest here.  For the 6 of us it was $72, which isn't bad in real standards, but the price to portion size ratio was a bit off....we all left hungry and grumpy.

Saturn, you mean well, but really, it's just a pricy McDonalds, minus the speed and delightfully sinful McFlurries.
Not only is this place really terrible, with no redeeming qualities whatsoever, but I once found a piece of cloth in my food.  Disgusting, disturbing and absolutely gross.

Six of us met at Saturn for dinner on a Saturday evening at 6:15.  The place was hopping and pretty noisy, with lots of families with small kids.  We had high hopes because we're vegan and some of us had liked the  Santa Cruz original.  

To cut to the chase:  we encountered big problems with the food service:  
 a) The mixed appetizer plate, which consisted of french fries, fried sweet potatoes and taquitos, took an inordinate amount of time to arrive and when it finally appeared, everything was cold.  As you can imagine the fries etc. were pretty much inedible.  
 b) When we pointed out the problem to the waiter nodded and said 'sorry,' but did not offer to replace it.   
c) The main plates also took a long time to arrive and again were not even warm. Burgers, fries, soup, rice and beans were pretty much at room temperature.  
d) One dinner order, which was for a soup, half-sandwich, and small salad platter came 15 minutes after the others.     

We don't know whether the problems were with the kitchen -- i.e. cooks putting cooled-off food on the plates -- or with the waitstaff -- the waiter letting the filled orders sit too long before serving.  In any case, Saturn has been open for 3 months, so even on a busy night, the staff should be able to serve food hot off the grill.

Toward the end of our meal, our waiter came by and gave us  a 10% off card for our next visit.  He said he appreciated that we had made our complaints politely.    We appreciated the gesture.  Still, it's hard to know from the cold versions of burgers, fries, soup, beans etc. that we ate,  whether the food at Saturn's is tasty enough to lure us back.

I was so disappointed, having had been to the sister location in Santa Cruz and loved it. The food here is mediocre diner food at best, I can make better dishes at home. It also seemed like the food sat for a while before coming out because it's wasn't hot. I am kinda offended they serve such crappy food with all of the other amazing food they serve in the East Bay. Go spend your money at Rudy's Can't Fail in Emeryville, they do veggie better...

Saturn cafe is in almost every sense a disappointment. I've been taken here twice by friends who have attempted to accomodate my vegetarian tastes, and both times I've been unimpressed. 

The good is that the decor is pretty interesting. It's a diner type interior that serves vegetarian food, which is just kind of cool to see. The service is also ok, they bring lots of water haha.

On my first visit, I had the fake chicken and avocado sandwich. This was decent although the bread was very bland white bread, which I didn't like. It wasn't wonder bread, but it wasn't anything I would ever buy for myself either. The fake chicken and bacon were decent, but they were both identical to products I had bought in the store in the frozen food section. I'm not accusing them of making frozen food, but when I go out I like to have something more than stuff I could have just microwaved at home. The "curry" that came with the sandwich was horrible and felt like a weird sort of vegetable mush with absolutely no flavor. This meal was decent and much better than round two.

On my second visit I had a breakfast omelet, which was made with powdered eggs... The potatoes on the side were also hard and not good and the bread was again the worst white bread possible.

Overall this place just doesn't have a strong commitment to quality in ingredients and it really shows. Additionally, the food is pretty unhealthy for how bad it tastes. To add insult to injury, they charge prices that I would expect for food with meat to cost instead of typical veggie prices. I won't be coming back here; there are many both cheaper and better options.

So this passed Sunday a friend and I were trying to decide which spot to go to for breakfast. After a little brainstorming we decided on trying Saturn Cafe in Berkeley. We had never been there before and I've been wanting to try it for the passed couple of months. We walked in and were seated immediately. 

I started to look at the menu and was having a hard time deciding. I feel like the menu needs work. I've never stared at a menu for so long trying to decide what to get. After looking it over I noticed "fakin' bacon." and little V's and VS's next to certain items. It was then that I realized we were in a vegetarian/vegan restaurant. I wish it was made more clear on the menu or near the front door that they don't serve meat there. We walked in and the place seemed pretty spacious and nice. Had a nice diner feel and was very clean but the placed seemed quite bare, lacking art and there were some weird random shirts or dresses on one part of the wall near the kitchen.

I ended up going with the "muffinator" as well as a fruit cup. Sounded tasty. Basically an egg and cheese sandwich with a meatless sausage patty served on an english muffin and potatoes on the side. As we were waiting for the food I noticed that half of the restaurant was empty yet the waitress and waiter were having a hard time seating the dozen or more people waiting to eat. This went on for the entire time we were eating and it was starting to get annoying having to watch all the hungry people up front waiting for a table. The waitress and waiter seemed on edge and sort of clueless as to what they were supposed to do. The whole vibe was sort of a chaotic mess. I noticed customers having to get water themselves because the waiters and waitresses were not being attentive. 

We got our food ten or fifteen minutes later and wow... What a sloppy fucking mess. What I got was an english muffin with 3/4's of the egg hanging off the side, cheese dripping onto the plate and a tiny "sausage" patty taking up half of the muffin. The potatoes were very dry/bland and tasted like they were cooked earlier and reheated on the grill. The fruit cup was nothing special. My friend ordered the Southwestern Omelette that came with extra hard toasted white bread, with no butter or jam. Our water cups were filled once when the food arrived and after that we weren't acknowledged by our waiter until we had to tell him we wanted our check. After a 5 minute wait for our check I was pretty disappointed. 

I was considering to use their restroom to throw up my disgusting breakfast, "dine and dash," and get a real fucking meal next door at Sunnyside Cafe.

I'm going to tell people to stay away from this place. Horrible food, and bad customer service. This place needs a lot of work.

The service my coworkers and I received today was downright shameful. It took FOREVER for our meals to be cooked. I mean, in the 45 minutes that we sat at the booth, we received neither our appetizers nor our entrees. We were on a time crunch as it was our lunch hour, key word being 'hour', so after waiting wayyy too long, we had to walk away frustrated, faint and famished. If you come here for lunch on a weekday, be prepared to wait a long, long time.

This place has the potential to be good, but it really just isn't. The service is slow and inefficient, and the food is something I could throw together from bottles and boxes myself. 

My friend got the buffalo burger, which they didn't bring. They brought her the California burger, and then 30 minutes later and after I had finished my food, brought her the buffalo burger. At that point, she was so hungry, she didn't feel like telling her that it was missing an ingredient. 

I ordered a salad that basically just had tofu and carrots on it, and what tasted like bottled salad dressing. It was completely lacking in substance and flavor. 

I really wish this place was good, but I was just disappointed in every aspect.

Update: The manager contacted me and apologized for the service. While it doesn't change my experience, nor my intention never to go back, it's good to know that the situation has been addressed and hopefully others will not have my same experience. I still think the idea of the place is very cool, even if the execution of it was severely lacking in my personal experience. May you have better luck if you decide to go.
___

This was my second time at Saturn Cafe. I will not be going back. Since my mom has a gluten allergy and they seemed pretty gluten-free friendly along with being what seemed like a pretty awesome space (I have a weakness for retro diners), I decided to treat us to lunch there. I wasn't expecting particularly attentive service -- I hadn't gotten that the first time I came, but I wasn't worried and the food had been good.

We were seated right away, water set down right away -- good signs. It took the waiter a little while to get to us to take down our orders, but nothing too long. Food and drinks ordered, we started to wait. And we waited. And waited. And waited.

I flagged down the waiter since it had been fifteen minutes and my drink hadn't even come out. He said that there was a back up with their drinks person. Lie number one. The restaurant was not even half full. Other tables seated after us had already gotten their drinks. Lie number two came when ten minutes after that he said our food would be along in a little bit but that one of the chefs had had an injury and that had slowed down the kitchen. Lie number three came when he told us that the chef had lost our ticket. No, hipster boy, I don't think so.

Clearly he had never put the order into the computer properly in the first place.

We got up and left. No real apologies were offered and we had to flag down the waiter in order to get any information (which were mostly lies) in the first place. Utterly and completely pathetic. Having served my time in the "customer service" industry, I have major sympathy for anyone working in such a position. But this took all my sympathy away -- took it into the alley, shot it and ran it over with a car. Repeatedly.

Maybe he was having a bad day. Maybe my low-top chucks made me look like a poser. But whatever the reason, I guess good service is too mainstream for Saturn.

Anyway, we decided to walk to Gregoire instead and had much better service and much better food (even if no dedicated gluten-free menu) for the same price if not cheaper than what we had planned to have at Saturn. I will be warning people to stay away from Saturn.

SATURN CAFE GLUTEN FREE MENU IS NOT GLUTEN FREE AT ALL!!!

They take no care in separating ingredients. The Fries and such go in the same fryer as everything else. Thank GOD I asked about this instead of just ordering off of the GLUTEN FREE MENU! WTF, people? It is Low gluten at best. I wouldn't trust these chefs to make me anything. When I asked about the cross contamination and if they kept the gluten free things separate, the server told me, "we're a vegetarian restaurant, not a gluten free one." Nice. So why bother even having a gluten free menu? I will never never never eat here again.

For now, if you have a hankering for a veggie burger and excellent fries, go to your nearest Barney's. I suppose it's possible that Saturn Cafe will get their act together....that food will be delivered to your table before it has turned cold, that you won't grow weary waiting for it, that the circus will find a ringmaster. Maybe the burgers won't even be a crumbly fall apart mess. 

I suppose I would give them another try after they've been open longer, but there are so many tempting options to try in the area that it will be a very long time.

My first trip to Saturn Cafe was with a friend of mine, we both are artists and have quirky sensibilities, are children of the 80's and so it was the very groovy space age simultaneously 80's and Retro/Vintage decor that hit us first when we walked in.  Glitter is always awesome so the silver glittering columns, and pink and white glittery  vinyl seats made me giddy. Our server was actually really nice and funny and my friend, being a very funny guy joked with him and he was very receptive to it. 

We both ordered Mint Chip Milkshakes, and were not disappointed, they were think and creamy and had lots of whip cream on top with chocolate syrup and chocolate chips. Yum!! Now, I have been back to Saturn Cafe and had a milkshake and it wasnt so good.  I think it depends on who is making it, and that's too bad because according to the Eastbay Express, they are award winning. They are also a bit pricey, at $5.25.  Which really dated that scene in Pulp Fiction with "The Five Dollar Milkshake". Anyway, he ordered a Space Cowboy burger and loved it, gave me a bite and it was pretty good.  Now, I keep kosher at home and eat vegetarian out, so it was really awesome to have cheese, "meat" and "bacon" all in the same bite and still be that nice modern orthodox Jewish girl I am. I ordered the Cowgirl Blues Burger, and was pleased, although I had to ask for extra sauce. The fries were hot, crunchy and good. Their vegan cupcakes were so good I wished they sold them in 6 packs to go!

I have returned to Saturn Cafe four times since this first time and I always try to order something new. Their salads arn't bad, I had a cob salad. Its not the place to go if you are seeking out a meal of an amazing salad. This is a Burgers and Fries joint. Actually, their nachos are pretty good. And they have a Thai-style peanut sauce dish. What keeps me coming back is the fact that they are 100% vegetarian and have many vegan options too. Since I am careful about what I eat and where, its nice to know that Saturn is Vege friendly. There are surprisingly few vegetarian restaurants in the East Bay.  Or maybe I just don;t know of them.... Anyway whether its the funky atmosphere, good yummy comfort food, decent service, awesome tables (each one has a different theme), convenient downtown Berkeley location to movie theaters, and such (ie. perfect place for a date if you are vegetarian), I will be coming back to Saturn! Last time I went, our waitress even gave me a free Saturn Cafe Sticker when I asked. Something to put on my guitar case. 

The California Burger with the house made all natural all vegetable and grain veggie burger served with jack cheese and avocado was fabulous, and great with extra sauce. Yum, thats my favorite one so far. Its just a really good veggie burger.

Drawbacks? Okay so the food is good but not mindblowingly amazing. The prices, yes, as an artist and currently unemployed at that I have a very tight budget, so I found everything to be $2-3 more than it should be. The burgers are almost $10 which is kind of nuts. If the prices were lower, i would go like whenever I was in Berkeley.  I suppose for the location, its about average, still, i think its on the pricey side. which like i said is too bad. Service on the first time was great, on other times, was a bit delayed and other times the food was out almost as fast as you ordered it, so it seems like the quality of the service and the food varies depending on who is working there and who is cooking.  

So yes, it would appear that Saturn has had some fair and poor reviews, but I think you just have to be creative, if the food is too dry, ask for some sauce, if the milkshake is not to your liking ask them to make a new one, they will do this! If the service is to slow, perhaps kindly hint that you have a movie to get to or something.  I love Saturn Cafe, its a fun place.  So give it a try!

I have a special place in my heart for Saturn, which was the go to place for vegetarians after midnight back in Santa Cruz a decade ago when I was there.  

I am glad there is a location here in the east bay with plenty of decent and a few really tasty vegetarian options.  The variety of vegetarian dishes gets it 3.5 stars in my book, but for non vegetarian people you might not be blown away by this diner style restaurant.  The nachos and milkshakes are things many vegans will love, and can have in few other places.  

In an environment where vegetarian food is abundant, Saturn will not blow you away, but its a good place to have around.

This place rocks. I stumbled in after a concert on Sunday night and had one hell of a meal. They were wearing Zombie makeup because it was Easter and it was the day Jesus rose from the dead. HILARIOUS.

Food:
I ordered the Jalapeno Burger with steak fries, the give you the option of skinny but I choose steak every time. The veggie patty was amazing! I wanted to buy it but apparently they make it in house. Just means Ill have to go back!

Service: 
Seriously our server was super patient. We met some random girls on the BART who said they were hungry so we asked them to join us. WRONG DECISION they were super obnoxious. One kept going on about how her family used to own dinners so it made her an expert. This chick has not worked a day in her life. When she found out the pancakes were whole wheat she threw a fit and was super rude to our waiter. The waiter on the other hand was really cool and didn't seem fazed at all. 

Why four stars not five?
I was drunk but i couldn't really tell I was in a veggie only restaurant until I looked at my patty. I wasn't pissed and it tasted great. There may even be huge signs that i missed. Either way this place is great!
GREAT food and awesome atmosphere. A new favorite!

Long story short. I didn't know this place was all vegetarian until after I ordered!!! Haha. Oh my. After walking around Shattuck, killing time before a movie, we couldn't decided on a place and ended up at the Saturn Cafe..

No wonder there was "V" all over the design on the table!! Duh!!!

Not to say that the food was not good. It was good, but not to my liking. It didn't hit me until after reading the menu (on auto-pilot) and just ordering whatever. Space Cowboy Burger, and Vanilla Bean Milkshake.

The decor it a mix of Space, Ed Hardy in the 80's sprinkled with glitter. Weird. But fun!


But yeah. Vegan restaurant. I won't forget that.

Try harder! The tofu scramble is despicable. Even if this (previously frozen) tofu scramble existed at a (meat) greasy spoon, it would still be unacceptable. The tofu is tasteless, dry, oversalted, and boring-- no sauce, no options for add-ins, and not a speckle of spice. For comparison, try the tofu scramble at St. Francis Soda Fountain, Pork Store Cafe, or Boogaloo's, where you will appreciate flavor, variety, succulence, and creativity.

On the positive side, it's a vegetarian restaurant. And this kind of exclusivity is hard to get. The location is great, and the service is friendly. 

I appreciate Saturn for being an all vegetarian restaurant, but why are there so few vegan options on the menu? It's not a far cry. At the very least they could offer the option to ask for menu items to be converted.

I've heard mixed reviews about Saturn Cafe, and as a Berkeley student, it only seemed fair that I give this place a try. Luckily, there was a Phi Alpha Delta alumni brunch held here, which gave me the opportunity to try out their specialties.

ATMOSPHERE
The decor of this place is really strange. It makes me feel like I'm in a weird 80's movie, what with the metallic colors and the odd futuristic paintings and wall decor. It actually feels a little out of place in Downtown Berkeley, but hey, Berkeley's all about individuality, right?

For large groups and banquets, you're placed in a huge room in the back, which is nice because it's isolated from the rest of the restaurant and you really do have your own room to yourself. The wall is lined with a bunch of random paintings, and there's a small stage at the far back of the room.

The service was okay. Nothing memorable. 

FOOD
I ordered the SATURN SPUDS and I tried some of my friend's BANANA WALNUT PANCAKES.

1) Saturn Spuds- presentation was cool, but it looked more like an omelet than anything else. It wasn't out of this world, but it did the trick.

2) Banana Walnut Pancakes- these were fluffy and delightful, but only when paired with the syrup.

We also tried the apple juice, which literally tasted as though you were taking a bite out of an apple-- I guess it was pretty damn organic.

The most memorable part of the meal were the home fries, which were given in abundance. I'm pretty sure my friends and I devoured 1-2 plates of them. They were an overload of carby goodness.

Overall, Saturn Cafe isn't a destination worth trying, and there are other good breakfast/brunch places in the area that are more worth your time (and stomach space).
Get the pumpkin pancakes while they're still around!
I would become a vegetarian if this place will feed me everyday.

I'm a fan. Very exciting to have all options be veggie at a diner. Excellent milkshakes. I'm excited to try the vegan version of them. Veggie burgers are home made, fries are thin-cut. Wish they had gluten free buns. They aren't hard to find these days! Finally, I appreciate the gender-neutral bathrooms (aliens and robots, ha!)

Cool venue. Awesome mud pie. These two things in combination make up for anything about Saturn Cafe that is sub-par (e.g., their food). 

Ambiance:
Can't say it has "ambiance," but its interior is definitely cool. Super fun, funky retro mod decor. I like! =D 
Walk in, look up overhead, and notice the round light with a pink disk around it, resembling the planet Saturn. Take a trip to the restroom and be greeted by friendly painted robots on the doors. From the tacky-but-cool glittery silver columns to the impressive and beautiful graffiti art over the diner/kitchen area (i love that graffiti!), to the super-fun tables (each table is different - some are filled with really fun/interesting stuff that keeps you entertained while waiting for your meal!) - there's so much to look at here, and it just makes your dining experience that much more enjoyable. 
Our table had Lego pieces in it! Hahahaha! So cool! It was funny because I kept putting my water glass over the black octopus Lego and thinking that he'd much rather be in my water rather than under the glass covering my table. X) 

Food:
In general, food is bland (at least, the food we ordered). There was a Yelp review featured on their menu raving about Peanut Royale and Baked Mac-and-Cheese, so these were the items we orderd.
