Overall, we weren't really too impressed with the food. Maybe because it's supposed to be healthy and low-sodium and stuff, but it was really .. bland. I never EVER sprinkle salt over my food, but I found myself asking for hot sauce and then finally resorting to the salt shaker to enhance the taste of both dishes. Baked Mac-and-Cheese was rather... boring. Bland. And quite white. X) Peanut Royale had good flavors going on there, but no taste. I hope that makes sense. Fresh ingredients, lots of good stuff, but disappointingly bland. Oh well. Salt helped. And I'd MUCH rather eat bland food that super-salty shiznit. X)

And now for the star of the show:
MUD. FREAKING. PIE. 
aaaaaaaaaahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh
I almost cussed when I ate this. (And I am a very good girl, so I don't cuss ^^). Mint chip mud pie is to diieeee for. I'd come to Saturn Cafe just to have mint chip mud pie. It's why this place gets 4 stars rathere than 3. Whooo~ Super-fly mud pie.. You so fine.... Mmm mmm

I do enjoy the food at Saturn Cafe but there are definitely hits and misses. The one in Santa Cruz has better service than this place. I went to Saturn a few days ago with a small group of people. I ordered the Buck Rogers with skinny fries and a side of the fake bacon (don't like them when they are in the sandwich cuz it gets soft and spongy)

The burger was awesome and being that I am a die hard meat lover, it really didn't even make me miss meat. it was that good. The chipotle sauce is not too spicy and makes for a great dipping sauce for your fries too. My fake bacon never came and our server didn't come by our table to check on drinks until we were all done eating. I had asked another server about the bacon and she said she would make sure it came but I guess she forgot. I ain't hating on this place and everyone forgets but I think maybe they get overwhelmed a little easily? 

In either case he apologized and took it off the check and probably helped save me a few calories. I have a lot of vegetarian/vegan friends and this is a place that we can always agree on so it's a thumbs up in my book.
Amazing food! Love going there for brunch or lunch. Really pleased they've added more vegan brunch options. Try the vegan shakes....they're to die for!

I've been going to Saturn Cafe in Santa Cruz since the ripe age of 13 or 14 when, after being vegetarian for a few years, I finally cracked and decided that I missed diners and that I needed to find a vegetarian equivalent. This place is great. 

If you are a vegetarian who misses the taste of traditionally meat-filled things (like a turkey BL(Avocado)T), or if you are a vegetarian or vegan who never wants to eat anything resembling meat, ever, this place has something delicious for you. And desserts. And it is steps STEPS away from Cinnaholic (delicious vegan cinnamon rolls).

Win!

I spent $15 to eat a bowl of spicy mac n' cheese and split a peach shake.  Meh.

Things I can do and not feel bad about when my boo is out of town:
1. grow a beard
2. subsist on garlic, jalapenos, and cheese

With their spicy mac n' cheese, as well as their garlic fries, Saturn Cafe helped me realize #2.  At the same time, the beard helps me fit in.  To get right down to it, the mac is not $9/bowl thrilling or generous.  A smattering of shells, all too thin/few cheeses, and a light layer of jalapenos on top really weren't doing it for me.  A similarly and somewhat disappointing milkshake, which really could have used a more robust ice cream, did not fix it all.  Finally and unfortunately, service was really slow, though friendly (while the place was quite dead).  There is a silver lining here, however, Saturn is open late and way better than Mel's.

If you're hurting for fries and a shake, I still recommend Barney's.  That is, if you can get past your carnivorous surroundings.

As a vegetarian, is is supremely difficult to find any decent vegetarian food open past 10pm. And if you do find a place like this, it also serves meat and is an asian style restaraunt. The problem with this is much of the food is cooked on surfaces, in oil, or has sauces that contain meat. 

It earns its first star for that. Star 2-3 are for above average diner style vegetarian food and the multitude of choices. 

The fourth star is for the good service and great location close to the bart. 

I can't give it a full 5 stars as the food had sat for a little bit, and certain items are uninspired. 

If you are a meat eater, definitely pass. If you are a vegetarian or especially a vegan (as many dishes they can make vegan) this is a must see. 

As in all vegetarian cuisine, you have to find the great dishes by spending a little money to experiment (go with friends so all can get different items). 

I personally will be back, but only late night, to avoid the long lines.

I have many fond memories of the Santa Cruz Saturn, so I was rather ambivalent when I heard they were opening one in Berkeley. I knew they'd try to replicate it and fatefully fail. They didn't -- at least, not as bad I portended. The food is pretty much the same (though I haven't been to SC in years) and they may have more menu options here... 

For breakfast, do not get the Heavenly Benedict and don't set yourself up for severe disappointment by ordering the french toast -- which doesn't use eggs. It's vegan. 'nough said.

For lunch and dinner, everything is game and I usually order the Cowgirl Blues burger. The non-vegan shakes taste like they're made with Horizon milk -- blech.

Overall it's a good option when it's late and you're feeling hipsterish. I just wish they'd make it feel more Berkeley.

So here's the thing, I love a greasy spoon type of place. A guy needs a good shake and some fries sometimes. Other times I just need a cup of coffee. This really IS the place to go. 

Saturn is hella good. I repeat, Saturn is hella good. Nacho fries? Are you f***ing kidding me? Amazing. 

I've even hit up their karaoke night on Thursday a couple times and it's such a cool environment. Very hangout-ish. It's not like karaoke at a lame ass dive bar where everyone's hella drunk and tryina creep on chicks. It feels like I'm just hanging out with my friends. And the girl that runs it is super welcoming and inclusive.

The waiters and waitresses are hella cool and make really good recommendations too.

All in all, I think the only competition is Rudy's, but that's all the way in Emeryville. And they don't have events there.

Go to Saturn. You'll be the complete opposite of bummed out.

P.S. I'm totally not vegan or vegetarian, and I'm still hella into this spot.

This place is like a hipster, Communist spaceship. But in a good way. The eggs benedict are fantastic, the potatoes are well-seasoned, and the portions and price are more than reasonable. I tried the fries, and I'm definitely getting some next time. For a vegetarian restaurant, they have so many options. I am so coming back!

I find this place highly overrated.

The food is okay -- nothing exceptional. I wouldn't even call it "good." Rather, it's "good enough." 

I've had the BBQ Ranch (veggie) Chicken sandwich with (faux) bacon added. It's a treat to have a combination like this after not having eaten the real counterparts for years. That said, I can't report that it was memorable. I'm not opposed to going back, but principally because it's open until midnight every day, which is fairly late for the East Bay -- but it's not the kind of food that would make my salivate or dream about. It's adequate, lowbrow, college-town fare. The price is right. It has a young vibe. 

The sandwich came with a choice of sides. I got the steak-cut thick fries. Meh. Not greasy, but a bit on the dry side. It certainly didn't quench my cravings for fried indulgences. 

I arrived at 11:30p. The restaurant was about 1/4 full, and the lounge was rockin'. There were some raucous folks who were quite loud while I was there. I wasn't crazy about that part. 

The service wasn't great. It took about 15 minutes to get someone to come over to take my order, which is odd given that there weren't that many tables being served. The waiter who was servicing all of the tables around me -- who evidently wasn't assigned to my table -- didn't look at me or ever tell me that my server would be right with me. Another staff member saw me looking around from a distance and was uncertain who was attending to my section. Eventually, I ordered, but no one ever came back to check on me after my food came. Was it because I was there late, and the servers were busy cleaning up as it was near closing time? 

Upon returning from the restroom, I passed by the shake station, where Saturn's famous vegan (and non-famous, non-vegan) shakes are prepared. I inquired about the brand of vegan ice cream used and the types of vegan shakes possible to order. While the staff member answered my questions, she gave me a questionable look as if I were inappropriately probing her about the time she lost her virginity. Yes, the service and staff could be improved. 

In theory I'd like to give a higher rating because of the vegetarian nature of the restaurant. Bravo. The quality of the food and the quality of the service remind me of what one would expect at a college-city diner. In a word, I'd call it immature and unsophisticated. Interestingly, however, I haven't had this kind of experience in Berkeley elsewhere.

Saturn Café Berkeley - I have been a long time fan of Saturn Café of Santa Cruz as a meat eater, vegetarian, and vegan, so it's safe to say I was very excited for the new Berkeley Saturn.  Upon my arrival, I was impressed by the actual restaurant - everything was so bright and eye-catching.  The host was very friendly and social, something that Santa Cruz is deeply lacking.

Even though I was not surprised, I was really hoping that they would have changed their menu; however, that was not the case.  I order mostly the exact same things I would typically order at their Santa Cruz location.  Given that Berkeley has a strong vegan population, as well as several vegan restaurants within miles of Saturn, I would have expected that Saturn update their menus to incorporate Daiya cheese, Gardien meats, vegan pancakes, etc.

Like most of my trips to Saturn, I enjoyed my food.  My girlfriend and I ordered a vegan peanut butter shake, vegan nachos, a vegan burger and a vegan breakfast burrito which were all very tasty and pleasing even though they got 50% of our order wrong.

I would recommend Saturn to anyone who has not been there before; however, if you live closer to Saturn in Santa Cruz there is no reason to go to the Berkeley location, since they are literally the exact same thing.

As a final note, Saturn if you are listening, please provide vegans with more options!

As a college student, I had many experiences with the original Saturn in Santa Cruz.  Though I'm no longer a California resident, I make my way back here every so often, and was really excited to be able to visit Saturn that is much more close to home.  (Yes, Saturn is good, but not necessarily a 2 hour drive good).  
I have to say that the food was just as good as I remembered.  Sticking with what was my usual order (mint chip shake & cheese fries), I remembered why I used to go so often in Santa Cruz.  The milkshakes are great, as are the cheese fries.  
One nice change at the Berkeley one was the staff--Santa Cruz often had not so nice staff, though the staff at Berkeley was really nice.  The hostess was very friendly, and she always made sure we had water and were comfortable.  She even ran over from bussing tables to ensure that we were okay.  Our waitress was also great at constant checking on us, making sure that we were okay.
Overall, this was a great experience, and definitely lived up to my memories of Santa Cruz.

waaaaaaay better than the santa cruz location (sorry guys).  still slightly confusing bathroom signs.  but the food is much more vegan friendly.  the vegan nacho fries are pretty much the best food you can purchase.  coconut curry soup is also excellent.  sweet potato fries and crazy wasabi dipping sauce...couldn't get enough.  i'm not a huge fan of their burger...it is probably fine but i tasted lots of mushrooms and i'm not a mushroom fan at all.  and why is the bacon not vegan?  i wanted a vegan bacon cheeseburger!  please work on that.  can't wait to come back and try the pancakes.  with a side of vegan nacho fries of course.

A lot of the time, I think I could go vegetarian. Saturn is one of those places that supports this conviction. Their "chix"-patty burgers are delicious, and their thin-cut fries are PHENOMENAL -- I could eat those for the rest of my life, if I didn't care so much about my waistline. I took my out-of-town friends here once (who are less enthusiastic about vegetarian food) and they liked it, though they weren't rave-about-it-all-day in-love. To be expected from omnivores -- even I can't give up beef for good. But when the meatless mood strikes me (and that's pretty darn often), Saturn will be there. What a beautiful thing :')

I've been to this location three times and the Santa Cruz one more times than I care to admit. This one is about the same as SC service-wise and the menu is pretty much the same. Essentially vegan junk food but tasty vegan junk food. 

I was in today with a friend and we both had salads. They were full of fresh veggies and very tasty however, the lettuce in both of ours was full of grit. I sent mine back but my friend didn't insisting they'd monkey around with her food if they did (yeah, I've seen those "hidden camera kitchen" episodes of 20/20 but my reasoning was hey,  it's an open/exposed kitchen. We could see if they put spit in the food or rubbed the vegan chicken patty down their pants). My friend watched as the server gestured toward us and the cook gave us the hairy eye ball shaking his head no as if I were full of crap. The server then told other servers who looked over at us as if we were the table full of people masturbating with the ketchup bottles.  God, I hate that kind of thing. Why make the customers feel uncomfortable like that?  What's to be gained by lying about sand in the lettuce? Did I say it was a friggin' finger tip? Am I trying to extort a lifetime's supply of free vegan cupcakes out of you??? Just a hint, if you work in an open kitchen, people can SEE you! 

So, to wind down my megillah here, the waiter brought out a new salad that was equally full of grit. I pulled a few grains of sand off the salad and showed them to the server who said, "Well, it IS organic." Look, I buy organic stuff at the farmers market. Sometimes, it's not only full of dirt but bugs (which I coax off and put in my garden, those cute little nuggets!) but I wash the stuff. A bag of rocks and an old banana peel can be organic, for chrissakes. That doesn't mean I want to put  ranch dressing on them and then pay someone $10 so I can eat it. In the end, he took our salads off the bill and said sorry but it could have been handled a bit better.

I'd had the mud pie here once and checked in, but I wanted to have something more substantial to warrant a review. I had my opportunity today to join a few members of my chain gang for brunch today. 

I settled on the southwestern omelet with a side of their fakin' bacon and steak fries - since they were out of home fries. The omelet - besides the fact it didn't have any animal derived meat(besides the eggs and cheese of course) was pretty delicious - the eggs were on the fluffy side, the steak fries had a deceptively meaty, unami-my taste to them which made think these might be infused with some kind of meat flavor but that'll be the subject of further investigation. The fakin' bacon was interesting - it has the salty, smoky flavor of the real thing but the mouthfeel and texture was... strange. It wasn't soy based as there wasn't a chalky, gritty taste/feel to it. I also had a few of their appetizers - typical fried fare. Now, I wanted to finish off with a slice of their mud pie - and I was bummed they didn't have any but the waitress made it up for us by bringing out ice cream to share! 

Now, there are a few things to be left desired and it was understandly busy - but I'll have to come back to get their fries again!

Where's the beef?  Not literally, as this place is vegetarian, but in the sense that my burger* was on a fluffy bun.  Fact: Did you know that the old Wendy's ads were designed around the fluffy bun idea but that Where's the Beef lady stole the show.  Fact!

Last night I ordered the Buffalo Girl, as I am that secure in my manliness, and because I love buffalo wing style sandwiches (nod to Ike's Place in SF).  The burger* has a faux-chicken patty which in itself is was dandy, but the problem lies in the fact that there is a slider's worth of patty on a full-bun's worth of bread.  Hence, it is a fluffy bun.  If the patty simply filled the burger* (or they gave you two), I would give this place 4 stars.

Four stars because:
1) The service was extremely friendly.

2) The vibe is relaxed and dinerish, yet not tired and filled with smoking old blue-hairs named Flo who want to know "what you want Honey."

3) The steak fries were perfect and plentiful.
3a)  bonus info:  As a nod to a weird food habit of mine, I LOVE when the ketchup is in a squeeze tube with that super narrow glue point tip so I can put a perfect bead of ketchup on each steak fry just before I eat it.   Yes, I know I am weird.

4) I came about 20 minutes later than my group and was served quickly and seamlessly.  As opposed to having a long delay and creating the awkward watch everyone else eat, then watch me eat dinner party/theater experience.  

5) My dinner group randomly had a need to split up the check oddly and the waiter was extremely friendly about it and helpful. 

Summary,
Good place, 3.5 stars really, would give it four if/when when I go back they double up the meat* to fill the fluffy buns.  

*by this I mean fake chicken aka (Ficken, Chickfu, Toicken)

I love Saturn Cafe! Every time I'm in Northern California, I am sure to stop by one of their locations. I am always satisfied with my food there, but my last visit to the Berkeley location inspired some critiques.
1. They charged extra for a side of BBQ sauce. I understand that they need to make money, but 75 cents for a small cup of BBQ sauce seems a little excessive. Nonetheless, I'll probably order a side of BBQ sauce again and endure the 75 cent charge. 
2. I don't eat meat, fish, or cheese with animal rennet (I'm transitioning slowly into veganism.) I asked my waiter if he knew whether or not the cheeses were vegetarian friendly (i.e. vegetable rennet instead of animal rennet) and he didn't know. He had to ask several other people there in order to get me my answer. I appreciate that he took the time to find out the correct answer, but I feel that the employees of a vegetarian and vegan restaurant should know something like this? Maybe I'm just a nitpick.
3. Our service was a bit slow, but it isn't usually like that.
I love Saturn Cafe, they offer amazingly delicious vegetarian and vegan dishes. The food is so good, I've contemplated hopping on a plane from SoCal just so satisfy my cravings! I'd recommend it to anyone, meat-eater or not! The food is THAT good!

MMMM! 
Love this place. A ++ !
Great food, great service, all around fun time. 
I love the "chicken" burger and the vegan milkshake!
Yes pls!

Me go in a vegetarian restaurant??? You've got to be joking. I usually live by the rule of "I can't go more than a day without meat." Of course, I had meat earlier in the day so this was not a problem. 

I decided to try this new place out with fellow Yelpers Nina Y. and Tiffany N. after hearing about it from Kathleen W. She raved about how amazing it was, so I decided to swallow my pride and try it out.

Upon walking in, the decor is very 50's with a quirky space theme, which just made everything pretty awkward. We were quickly seated, but had to wait at least 10 minutes for our server to come around. For a full house, they only had 2 servers working. Minus points for that! 

There's a good selection of burgers and sandwiches here, as well as breakfast items and desserts. I decided to try out the Chicken Avocado Bacon Sandwich, which pretty much describes itself, except for the "chicken" part. The portion was huge, but the sandwich was so-so. The bread crust was very toasty and just made the whole thing feel like it was mostly bread. Kind of reminds me of Sufficient Grounds hehe. The "chicken", to my surprise, was pretty good, but there was a small portion of it. In general, everything except the bread in the sandwich was pretty sparse. The fries, by the way, are some of the best I've had in a while.

I wouldn't say that I totally hated this place, but I doubt that I'll come back again. However, with Berkeley being a vegetarian's paradise, I have no doubt that Saturn will stay alive for years to come.

My first visit to Saturn was in Santa Cruz on a weekend trip. I love the whole diner experience but as vegetarian it is pretty impossible to get a proper meal off just milkshakes and fries. Besides, I they will have way more veggie ingredients than in most diners and I kinda prefer the kitchen to be free from meat. Basically I loved the concept from the beginning and still do, however, the Berkeley location needs improvements. 
I had their amazing pumpkin milkshake at both S.C. and Berk. location which then became my main reason for coming back but the rest of the food has repeatedly been just OK. The food looked pretty sloppy at times and there were no standout flavors which is what vegetarian and vegan (or all) cooking should have. After getting a pretty burnt 'chicken' burger today with a long black hair in the middle, on top of the fact that the pumpkin milkshake is out of season, I feel I'm out of reasons to come back. I probably will though, but only because they have wifi and are close to school!

5 stars on the food, 2 stars on the service. Although our server was nice when he got to us, he was not super on top of it. Being a server myself, I know when it's packed and things get a little difficult and when it's reasonable to wait. They could have done better. Plus all the servers need to PULL UP THEIR PANTS! I should never be able to see a male or female crack at any point, it is unsanitary. 
Besides all that stuff, the food is FABULOUS! Just converting to vegetarianism, this is an awesome treat.

Well maybe they had a bad day today. I went in there with my veggie friend like we usually do and I kept getting startled by the waiter. Who called me a wimp and then to top it all off my Cowgirl Blues Burger "chicken cutlet" was incredibly burnt. I wasn't going to complain and have them sent it back, because what if they spit on it! haha Jk I know they'd never do that but still I ate a burnt burger. The steak fries never fail me though so I know I will go back and saturn will redeem itself!

Saturn deserves 3 stars because the food's not very inventive or exciting.  I gave them an extra star because they have a diaper changing table in the ladies' room.

I didn't know what to expect when my friend suggested this "vegetarian diner."  The super-cute decor mixes classic 50s diner with glittery disco (and the saucy vinyl aprons adorning the walls truly allude to porn, but whatever).  We had lunch on a Tuesday, so it wasn't very busy.  The waiter was friendly enough, and it was intended to be a leisurely lunch, but our service was kind of slow.  I wasn't especially impressed by the menu, but with the billing of "diner" I guess I should have expected greasy burgers and lots of fried sides and toppings.  We both chose salads; I had the Urban somethingorother Salad and liked it very much.  It was lots of different fresh veggies with some crushed peanuts and a yummy cilantro-lime sauce.  She had the Spartacus salad, which is basically a Greek salad with faux chicken.  We split a chocolate cupcake with raspberry frosting for dessert, which was great: the cake part was very chocolatey but still light, and the frosting was intensely flavored with real raspberries.  Not amazing, but good, very healthy food in a fun setting.

Saturn Café is a college student eatery. 

We tried the portabella mushroom burger here which was fine but a tad over grilled.

The California burger wasn't all that great but the waiter was nice enough not to charge us for it and we got it exchanged for another entrée.

I think it's a decent diner place and most importantly they stand for a good cause so props to that.

First of all, HUZZAH to Saturn for taking on this cursed location.  It was a brave, bold move.

And it's the right fit.  I think the last restaurant to do well in this spot was The Good Earth back in the dark ages of Members Only jackets and Jazzercise. But where Good Earth sold "healthy food" in a kind of upscale package, Saturn is all about selling vegetarian cuisine but in a diner package.  The result is I get to pretend I'm eating healthy while chowing down on nacho fries. 

That's right- I said "nacho fries"...cheese, beans, guac, sourcream and salsa, not on chips but french fries. 

But it's vegetarian.  So it's good for me. 

Shut up, I said "it's GOOD for me!"

Plus, they have Hibiscus cooler, which I adore.  It's like tea, but it's like juice. Seriously -- if you haven't had it before, you're missing out.  And it goes great with sweet potato fries. Or chili-"chicken" sandwiches. Or any of the other awesome (and very large) offerings at Saturn. 

Oh -- and they say they're going to try to be open after hours.  And in Berkeley, that can mean any time after 8 p.m. So the fact that they are going to go for 2 a.m. is another brave, commendable plan. I look forward to seeing you drunken fools there soon.

my sister went to UC Santa Cruz & we always made a stop at the Saturn Cafe there when we were visiting.  I's so glad to have a Berkeley outpost!!!

all veggie diner fare (burgers, fries, eggs, shakes), with a slightly edgy/hip/cool decor & staff.  vegan options... but I wish they had more

something about local sustainable commitment to the environment blah blah blah, I was too busy chowing down on my vegan breakfast burrito.

The waitress behind the bar is as sweet as pumpkin pie.

The heavenly benedict is.. wait for it.... so heavenly. It is the best eggs benedict I've ever had - and I'm not even vegetarian! I went back to order it a second time today and it was just as delicious!

I love the decor - it reminds me of something you would see in a B-52s music video.

I actually got an account on yelp just so that I could share this joy with the world.

Nah! nothing special, maybe because I love meat burgers, but also I believe I know to appreciate a good vegetarian or vegan food, I don't feel that way about this place. The service normal and the food tasted like frozen food from a box.

Truly amazing. The food was fantastic. I had the Muffinator. Service was extraordinary. I was torn between a soy milkshake and a beer. She recommended a Porter Soy Float that was out of this world. Only at Saturn.

We were in Berkeley for 18 days. We ate at Saturn five times and never had a bad experience. The vegan nacho fries were fantastic. The muffinator, delicious! I'm not vegan or vegetarian, but I never missed the meat. I sure wish I lived closer!

I hope to return and re-review Saturn in the next couple weeks to give them an upgrade to "Yay!".  We were there on their second day and they were obviously still working out a lot of kinks.

The food was all great.  I enjoyed the jalapeno burger with a side salad.  My wife enjoyed a bigger salad.  Each of my kids had the steamed rice and tofu - though I can't say that either of them enjoyed it.  This, of course, says more about them as kids and us as parents than it does about the Saturn Cafe.  I also enjoyed, very much, a vegan vanilla shake.  This was the highlight for me - who'd of thunk that nuts and soy milk could taste so good.

I think Saturn Cafe will be a 4 star... eventually.  First, they need to work out the details of staffing and timing.  Everyone was very nice and the food was good, but it seemed they were a little short handed.  Our table wasn't set when we sat down and no one brought silverware until we asked for it.  It took forever to get our orders in and forever to get the food delivered. My wife was served the wrong meal, though she didn't realize it until she had sampled a couple fries (which she said were good).  It took 12 minutes to get our check AFTER I had requested it and another 10 minutes for them to run our credit card.

We have 2 kids and it took so long my wife left to get them home for bedtime while I waited to finish paying for dinner.

I will be back for another vegan burger and shake and to test their service for y'all after they have been open a little bit longer.

Went with a friend for lunch yesterday. Long time waiting at podium to be seated. Greeter said she'd bring water. She didn't. Waiter took about 8 minutes to come to the table. Was friendly, took our orders, said he'd bring water. Food came relatively fast - within ten minutes. Forgot to remind waiter about water. He was no where close for another ten minutes. there were only two people waiting not including the greeter and the place (inexplicably) was packed. I ordered a salad with greens, blue cheese, candied pecans and shredded carrots. It was fine, not fantastic and was somewhat overpriced. I also ordered the mac and cheese and besides the boxed variety which I didn't have until I was 19 and doesn't count anyway this was the more boring and bland version I've ever had. I added pepper and then believe it or not I added some salt. Don't know what kind of cheese they used but it was not so tasty. Waited another long ass time for the check. The food and the value of said mediocre food did not stand up to the extremely slow and inattentive service. Not good enough to give them a second chance.

My friend suggested coming here for dinner with a larger group, she raved about how the vegan meat here really tasted like real meat and how much she LOVED the food here so we all gave it a try...

Food: 
1) Portabella burger: so I was thinking it was going to be served as a HUGE whole mushroom cap but instead it was chopped up into thin slices so that was a little disappointing. The mushroom tasted ok, but the whole burger seemed a little bland. I wasn't too blown away by it presentation or taste wise. 
2) Guacamole Burger: I'm a HUGE fan of guacamole so I got suckered into ordering this. The guacamole looked like guacamole but it was lacking flavor again. The texture of the guacamole and for the most part, the presentation, was there but each bite was not as satisfying as if the guacamole had been more heavily spiced. I think a touch more lemon/lime or perhaps a bit more salt would have done the trick. The patty was convincing texture wise, but very bland taste wise. The bun was pretty good. Very soft and lightly toasted, too bad everything else in between wasn't up to the standards of the buns. 
3) Award winning fries: Tastes like regular fries you get from anywhere, but since they were pretty crunchy, I'm guessing they either double fry them or fry them for an extra long time. 
4) Spanish soup: broth based soup inspired by the Spaniards, filled with garbanzo bean sized corn and some other things I couldn't identify, it was also a bit bland for my taste. I think for something to be Spaniard inspired, it should have been bursting with flavor. 

Ambiance: 
Very space aged inspired diner. Pink and silver sparking pillars is what really stood out in my mind. A lot of pink. I think it's a pretty fun place to take kids. 

Service: 
Nice. No complaints. 

Price: 
$9.50 each burger. Pretty typical I guess but I wasn't all that impressed with the food. 

Overall: 
Nice to try, but I don't think I'll be coming back.
As a non-vegetarian, I found their milkshakes worth forgoing meat for a meal.

The boyfriend, who's a vegetarian loves this place.  I don't get it.

The service has always been super SLOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOW and rude.  When we went to brunch, I got the tofu scramble (not a vegetarian just hate eggs) and when I asked for some soy patties, I got snapped at b/c they weren't Vegan.  I told her that's okay, I'm not Vegan but the waitress rolled her eyes and walked away before I got the sentence out. 

At Rudy's, they get it and the food is a million times better...at Saturn they couldn't give a F*ck.  

Two stars because the decor is cute and the Vegan shakes are very good (get the chocolate and PB...so good).

I'll preface this by saying that I am by no means a vegetarian. I met up with some friends, a couple of whom ARE vegetarians, so we could try this place and while it was okay, I probably wouldn't go out of my way to go back. 

I am admittedly opposed to eating fake meat products like tofurky and fakin bacon (which is super clever and an awesome name btw), so i struggled to find something on the menu that was appealing to me, which of course I am not going to hold against this place. 

I did try a sample of the lentil soup which seemed pretty tasty, and I was eying the quesadilla (probably made with soy cheese) when the waiter suggested i try the mac n' cheese since people go out of their way to get it. I took his advice and ordered the mac n' cheese, which was unspectacular but filling. My buddy's fries were cold but the waiter quickly fetched a fresh batch and apologized for the inconvenience.

I also ordered one of their Santa Cruz Mountain Brewery beers, the nut brown ale, and it was okay but again, didn't really do it for me. For dessert we ordered a decent pumpkin pie, and a very grainy Turkish coffee milkshake, which was also decent.

The waiter was nice and honest about all the things we asked him, including which items he would really recommend people try vs. items that might not make a good impression. The decor in there is hilarious, including somewhat ambiguously sexed robots on the bathroom doors, but thank god for society's insistence that blue is for boys and pink is for girls otherwise I might've walked into the wrong bathroom. The diner getup and neon colors are certainly fun enough, and I think I saw on a poster that they have karaoke and disco nights?

Like I said, I wouldn't go out of my way to eat at this place, but if my veggie friends wanted to come back I wouldn't turn down the invite.

I'd been looking forward to trying this place out for a while, as their decor looked really funky and quirky and apparently their milkshakes have won awards. Well, last night, my husband and I decided it was time. 

The service was really slow, right from the start. We were seated quickly enough, but a server didn't appear for ages, and when he did he took the orders of people who arrived after us first. We ordered a vanilla bean milkshake each and a Mini Madness to share. It was another long wait before they appeared, and I'm not sure they were worth it. They were nice enough milkshakes, but no better than elsewhere in Berkeley. Their straws are really crappy - they split at the slightest amount of force exerted on them (which is necessary as the milkshakes are so thick). The Mini Madness was nice, but very rich.

I wouldn't bother going back, the whole time we were there we were virtually ignored, and the milkshakes weren't that great.

A year in, and apparently Saturn #2 still hasn't found its groove.  Bottom line: we spent most of our visit next to a dirty table, were served cold, barely-edible food--and the place wasn't even busy.

Backing up: we've been to Saturn Santa Cruz many times, & were excited when a new location opened up in the Bay Area.  

First impression: cool sign outside.  Inside, they made a stab at the decor, but didn't reach the level of the original.  What's with the lame lamé aprons hanging up near the ceiling?  What's with the plain restrooms labeled "men" & "women," rather than "robots" & "aliens?" Oh, well.

The greeting up front was pretty quick, but we still had to wait for a dirty table to be cleaned for us.  Friendly hostess, and the server, when she came, was friendly as well.  We ordered the Super Sampler appetizer & two sandwiches.

The food, when it came, came all at once.  What's wonderful about Saturn's open kitchen, by the way, is you are able to enjoy the sight of your meal festering under a heat lamp while your server stands just feet away from the line, with her back to it, rifling through the bill wallets at the register.  This happened repeatedly--but it only bothered me when I had a hunch it was our food hardening behind her.

So the food all came at once.  Super Sampler: Room-temperature french fries are not fun.  ESPECIALLY since Saturn (Santa Cruz)'s thin-cut fries have always been my favorite item on their menu.  Never had them cold before.  Don't recommend it.  Sweet potato fries, same problem.  Cold zucchini sticks?  Yuck.  The taquitos are so bland & lifeless, I don't think they would be good even hot.  Best thing on the plate ended up being the onion rings-- but they still would have benefitted from being served freshly-cooked.  As for the sandwiches: my bread was tough, everything on the club sandwich was the same temperature--hardened edges--BAD.  Just a couple of weeks earlier, I'd had an amazing--FRESH--version of this sandwich served to me at Saturn #1.  Here in Berkeley, we left a lot of food behind.

Now, why has this never happened to us at the original Saturn Cafe?  Our food has ALWAYS been served hot down there--and it's not because the place is not busy; we often have to wait for a table to become free.  Here's the difference: when the food gets cooked, it gets immediately delivered BY WHOMEVER IS AVAILABLE.  In Berkeley, only our own server ever approached the table.  The same person, you know, who was so interested in whatever was going on with that stack of bill wallets.

Where was the manager (was there even one in the building)?  Why didn't one of the other two servers--or the hostess--grab the food & bring it to us?  Are they teritorrial at this location?  Doesn't this go against the ideals an employee-owned collective?  I'd think at some point, the cooks would start yelling, & refuse to let that food be served.  I don't blame one person at Saturn for what happened; I blame ALL of them.

Reading the other reviews of Saturn Berkeley, a common theme I see is that Berkeley has better vegetarian restaurants to try.  Next time, I'll seek out one of those.

Vegan/Vegetarian Yelpers, take this review with a grain of organic salt.  I am not a vegetarian, and don't have the proper palette to determine what makes good vegetarian restaurant good. I am a carnivore, and only eat animals that are themselves on an Atkins diet...  

I live pretty close to this restaurant, so its usually on my route when i'm walking about the streets of Berkeley.  Every time I pass, I'm drawn in by the interesting decor.  It looks like a diner you'd see the Jetsons eating in. 

So its a real weird contrast to see such a perky place, occupied by some of the most  apathetic and morose looking patrons ever.   People don't smile, and they don't look like they're enjoying their food. Or life.

Well, the mystery is solved.  After me and 3 other friends came here for lunch (one a vegetarian), I can safely say that the people of Berkeley aren't slowly withering away into zombies.  The food is simply bland.

I ordered the Space Cowboy Burger -- First off, I nearly made a dork of myself when I ordered this and almost asked for it to be cooked medium rare.  The menu might list a patty, bacon, and cheese as being main ingredients in this thing, but that is merely to trick people into forgetting that they've stepped into a Vegan restaurant.  All these ingredients are made from a soy / cardboard processing plant, and tastes that way.  I suppose I already felt like a dork anyway from having to say "space cowboy burger."

The gf ordered a Tofu Scramble, and I watched in amusement as she kept drowning it in ketchup to try and give it any semblance of flavor.  And finally, my vegetarian friend barely touched her tofu salad.  All bad signs.

The milkshakes were the best part of our lunch.  Probably because it came from a cow.  A real one.   

It might seem that I'm being overly judgmental towards a Vegetarian Restaurant. I do think there are some awesome ones out there, and there needs to be more of them, but Saturn is not gonna make me consider a dietary change anytime soon.

Is this a bad joke. Frozen food reheated to order. Frozen processed burgers, frozen fries. Heat and mix. You can make this kind of food at home really easy and so far better so why bother.
Great concept but terrible execution. This place is for those who want nothing but the low common denominator. Very sad.
For a vegetarian place it sure is NOT vegan friendly.

The draw of this place is clearly its vegetarian/vegan options but other than having options, the food isn't spectacular.  Its basically mediocre diner food with lots of veggie burgers.  Nothing was horrible but I wouldn't rush back.  The soymilk ice cream milkshake tasted ok but had a super weird texture (I say this as a non-vegan).  The fries were tasty but the California burger was average.  Decor is kitchy but a little cold/sterile.

If I opened a vegetarian restaurant, it would be a lot like Saturn.  Food that's veggie, not "veggie food".  I love that you CAN get "bacon" with that, and  extra cheese and no one even looks at you funny.  And they had me at "space themed".

But next time, I'm ordering a chik'n ( its pronounces with extra emphasis on the NNN) patty because that veggie burger was shameful.  It was worse than a garden burger and quite soggy!  I know they don't make everything in house, so why can't they offer a Boca burger?  Then all would be well!!!!

-EDIT they DO offer a Boca Burger, it's just not on the menu.  That seriously does change things.  Now if only they would open in Sacramento...

I know, I'm picky.  The long and short version is that this is a great place to eat, especially if you don't feel like vegetarians should always be relegated to health food.  Just be sure to order a Boca or chik'n patty if you are picky like me!

Man I was so happy to find a dedicated all vegetarian, retro 50's diner, but was pretty disappointed in the food.  We ordered up a breakfast plate of biscuits and gravy and the eggs, toast, sausage, and home fries potatoes.  The biscuits were dry as hell and tasted like unleavened, stale cardboard bread...to top it off the cook cut the dry-ass biscuit in half and toasted it making it even drier!!! the gravy on top of the biscuit was tasty but not enough of it was served to counter the dryness of the glorified "biscuit cracker"...Bisquik biscuits would've been better than what they tried to bake...do yourself a favor and hire a real baker that can whip up some fluffy and moist buttery biscuits super easy... there's nothing more annoying than bad biscuits for breakfast...also, the gravy came out lukewarm, how about cranking up the heat on the gravy pot before sending out cold food??? 
the potatoes were half cooked and had that annoying raw crunch in the middle that you never want to taste with home fries...both plates were served lukewarm, not good when there were literally like 3 other customers having breakfast in the entire place...I'd give them one more shot but not until I see some better reviews...AND BETTER, MOISTER BISCUITS!!

This is my 4th review update. 

I intend to keep reviewing Saturn Cafe (berkeley) until they have stellar outstanding customer service, but also I will continue to return as a customer. Saturn team- I do love your atmosphere, food, location....I just want to be treated with outstanding customer service. Something that has lacked in the past.

OK, update-

My bestie & I decided we were in the mood for some late night eats and what better place than SC...

Here's the PROs-

- greeted w/ a smile at the door
- both the greeter (Anna) & server (Cameron) introduced themselves
- Cameron had an awesome sense of humor that put us at ease & he  couldn't do enough to provide items requested or to apologize for anything not available 

SIDENOTE: I have received personal correspondence from a manager @ Saturn so its nice to know that they're actually reading the feedback and responding to requests. Thank you.

Continuing... 

The NEGs-

- I would like to see lemon added to the complimentary water 
- We were charged a $1 extra for BBQ sauce which should be easily substituted for ketchup perhaps?
- I don't particularly like the "raw sugar" in my iced tea. Perhaps add other sugary options? 
- and... my biggest rant of all:

Saturn Team- 

Please increase your late night hours, at least Fri/Sat to 1:00 AM. 

Is that too much to ask? I believe you are popular enough & its rather crappy that your location in Santa Cruz stays open so late vs. you guys. talk about getting a bad reputation just for that.

I feel like my Saturn reviews are becoming a blog, lol.

Till next time!

I was pretty impressed for a vegan place. They even have gluten-free options. The menu is pretty big. There's a section of salads, sandwiches, burgers, desserts, and hot entrees. I'm a sucker for mac and cheese, so that's what I got. It was pretty good, nice and cheesey, just like it should be. Be sure to find out what the seasonal specialties are. It was my luck to chance upon some eggnog ice cream. They also have cupcakes and other baked goods. They even serve kombucha and beers from Santa Cruz Mountain Brewery. The decor is crazy. I felt like I should've been in roller derby or something. I don't know how it compares to the original Santa Cruz location.

I brought my meat lover friend here without telling him it was vegetarian/vegan food only. He ordered a chicken sandwich, devoured it, and refused to believe me after the meal when I told him it was imitation meat. We had to call the waiter over to personally convince him that it was true.

I always get the Saturn burger with thin fries. Pretty much everything else is amazing too. The milkshakes, while stomach fattening and wallet lightening, are incredible.

If you are any sort of vegetarian/vegan etc in Berkeley you cannot miss this place.

Okay. So I came here last night with my mom for a late dinner. Once you walk in, it has a total diner vibe. It's very "glittery" too. We were seated by a sweet hostess and was greeted my our kind server.  

I had the Vegan Taquito plate. It was a nice helping of 4 taquitos, guacomole, salsa, veg sour cream, black beans + brown rice. It was nice, but I don't think I would order it again. It didn't really taste like anything. The guac didn't taste like anything. Nor did the veg sour cream. Now I think about it, I don't know why I ate it.  The highylight was my Vegan Vanilla Milkshake. That was wonderful. Okay. Next time. Milkshake only. 

The people here seem really cool. The waitstaff is great. My current rating is for the food. Maybe next time I just need to try something else. I think I also just don't like diner-esque food anymore.

I have been to this place a handful of times and have enjoyed every meal each time. What do I usually order? 

Well thats simple, the delicious vegan platter. Why? Well it has a mixture of the tastiest appetizers which are guilt and animal free! The taquitos and fried zucchini sticks are absolutely delicious. I would claim them as my favorite and a must have every time I come here. I have also tried the mac n' cheese, the onion rings, the french fries, the burgers and sweet potato fries! Everything is made with love. I often burn my tongue after eating here, because I can't help but dive in right away when they bring the food out. Oh you poor taste buds of mine. 

The service is good, I've always been seated right away without waiting, and we get silverware and water right away. The restaurant is very clean and they have very nice decor inside. I love love love the space theme. 
Parking is a hit or miss depending on what time of day you go because you have to park on the street. But hey, thats Berkeley. 

I have heard many good things about their vegan milkshakes, and that is next on my hit list. I'll be seeing you soon, Saturn Cafe!

I think this one is just consistently better than Santa Cruz in terms of customer service.  Vegan shakes are the bomb.  Nacho fries (only need a half order!) are a steal at 6 bucks.  Tons o' food.

Their little space lounge is cool.  I did vegan speed dating there and went to a book signing.  

Proximity to Cinnaholic is also key.  Vegan paradise brothas and sistas!

I love Saturn in Santa Cruz, so was super-excited when they opened the one in Berkeley. And when they opened it, they seemed to use that time to expand the vegan options in both locations - double win. 

So, as you probably already knew, Saturn is a vegan diner. I grew up in Jersey, land of the diner, and since becoming vegan have really missed diner food. (10+ years). Here you can get an awesome milkshake, burger and fries and be totally satisfied. YUM. 

I love that in the menu redesign they added vegan nachos. And not just vegan nachos that leave out cheese, etc -- they are using daiya cheese (it melts) and tons of beans, soyrizo, etc. And their vegan 'sour cream', while very different from regular sour cream, is amazing. I think it's way better. 

And a vegan sampler plate? YUM. My only complaint is that we asked to sub out the wasabi for BBQ sauce and they charged us extra for it. BOO. 

And extra points for having RC cola instead of coca cola. I grew up drinking RC, and it brings me back! And when you get a soda, it's ENORMOUS. 

A few points taken away for service. The folks were super-nice. But they forgot to fire one of our friend's orders, and delivered the regular meals along with our app, so three of us had food plus app while we're waiting for the 4th friend's food. Everything got a little colder while waiting.

But super-good! I'm so glad to have one closer by! And it's near Cinnaholic, which is a dangerous confluence of delicious vegan food in one area.

Came here after a dinner at Gather across the street and decided to try the Rootbeer float.... Was not disappointed. I liked that they gave extra Rootbeer on the side (comes with).

However, I'm giving this 3 stars because the service isn't that great (we paid in cash because it took too long to wait for the waiter to come back and get our card). Also, I saw the waiter wiping down the tables with the same rag he wiped down all the seats with...yuck. 

Rootbeer floats are a plus... Just don't touch the table if u can help it.

Dear Saturn Cafe, your vegetarian "chicken" and "bacon" blew my mind.  

I checked out Saturn with my new-to-Yelp friend, Nick L, and I was instantly impressed!  PINK MENU, PINK ACCENTS, JUKEBOX, RETRO, SPARKLES!  This place rocks.  At that point, this place was already at least 3 stars because of the super chill atmosphere.

Between the two of us, we ordered:

1)  Mint Chocolate Chip Milkshake - Very minty and not too dense.  Good to split.

2)  Saturn Spuds (Nick's brunch dish) $7.50 - organic eggs, home fries, sauteed with mushrooms, onions, bell peppers topped with a zig-zag pattern of melted cheese.  Excellent presentation!  For a dinner dish, it wouldn't fill me up, but those eggs are just the way I like em.

3)  Chicken Avocado Bacon sandwich $9.50 - I ordered off the recommendation of the waiter and like I said, "FAKE BACON AND CHICKEN?"  This is so good!  You won't see any bacon fat drippings though.  I also found out what a "triple decker" sandwich is.  Basically, it's a TOWER of sandwich.  The "meat" was complemented nicely with fresh avocado, gouda (mmm), sourdough bread, and tomato/lettuce/onion.  You get a choice of side too:  fries (wedges or thin cut) or soup (tomato or special).

Love the options.  And all-around great service.  I will have to come back.  & Thanks for dinner, Nick  :)

Saturn Cafe is so fun! Fun decor, comfy booths, friendly and great service.

They have a great menu with all sorts of options, breakfast all day, and the prices are unbelievable compared to some other places in the area. A huge breakfast platter for about $7.95...awesome! I love getting their Huevos Rancheros, and now I'm craving them since this review has me reminiscing how good it was. 

My favorite booth is the Lucille Ball one in the corner, awesome table decor, comfy big booth if you come with a larger group. If it's open, snag it!

The food is prepared fresh, tastes delicious, and arrives in front of you super quickly! They have awesome milkshakes (would highly recommend them) for about $5. I am not vegan or vegetarian but I love all food and highly recommend this place if you are. Their "meat" is tasty and everything my friends and I have ordered there was delicious, we were all pleased. It's turning into one of our favorite spots in Berkeley.

Healthy, tasty, and out of this world..stop in if your are hungry or thirsty!

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Let's start off with my friend's unofficial review of Saturn: he had been here a few times before and tried their chicken burger, "beef" burger, and omelette. He said the vegetarian entrees were meh, as it tastes very obvious to him that the pseudo-meat is not meat. However, he did say the steak fries were great, which, along with the restaurant's location and hours, kept him coming back.

Fate had me chance upon this place for a late night dinner after a midterm. At 9 PM on a Monday night, there were only 4 other parties. Service was decent, water refills were diligent. Desserts arrived within 8 minutes of ordering, and food followed after 3 minutes.

What convinced me to dine here that night was the Yelp check-in offer: if you check-in anytime on a Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday, you get 20% off of your meal! There's nothing more convincing than that!

|| F O O D ||

NACHO FRIES: Nachos served atop Saturn's award winning steak cut or thin cut fries [$9.50 for full order | $5.25 for half order]
- Got the full order with steak-cut fries. I was expecting phenomenal fries, as my friend really liked them. I thought they were okay. The fries were bland and slightly dry, but they are fun to bite in to. 
- The toppings were plenty. Well, maybe it could have used more guac and cheese. And the cheese is win. Mmmm, melted cheese.
- Jalapenos not too spicy, which I liked.

VANILLA BEAN MILKSHAKE: Made with McConnell's premium ice cream Vanilla Bean [$5.25]
- Yummy! They even give you the extra portion that they can't fit into the mug!
- Topped with a mint leaf, hehe.

CHOCOLATE NOVA: chocolate ice cream, Oreos, bananas, whipped cream [$5.50]
- Decent, but I didn't really eat more than a bite of the chocolate ice cream.
- It melts quickly.

SWEET POTATO FRIES: [$6.95]
- AWESOME. The best thing we ordered.
- The fries come with this tangy orange wasabi-ranch-onion sauce that is MAGNIFICENT. I even dipped my steak-cut fries in his sauce. The best combo is nacho fries with lots of cheese, chives, and guac dipped in this orgasmic sauce. Beast.
- The fries are a bit on the oily side, but they're crisp and crunchy.

At the end of our meal, I realized that we hadn't tried anything vegetarian. Oopsies. :P

|| C L O S U R E ||

Total bill + tax + tip - 20% Yelp check-in = $27, $9 per person. With all that food, it was worth it. I highly recommend the sweet potato fries and the uber dipping sauce that comes with it! The waiter was cute, and +5 awesomeness for being seated at the Pez table!

What a wonderful part of Berkeley's colorful and intricate tapestry! Saturn Cafe has so much going for it - adjacent to the UC Berkeley campus, veggie swank, friendly associates, great prices, and social events. Saturn Cafe represents so much of what I love about Berkeley.

Here's the only problem...the food...meh, so so. The Saturn Scramble (or something like that) was just so so. It's a dish with scrambled eggs, home fry potatoes, bell peppers, and cheese. Takes me back to my Grandma's near-signature dish....except that their version doesn't have much flavor. Maybe my expectations were too high. The pancakes were big, dense, and crude (like the UC Berkeley linemen), but needed more butter or something to add some flavor. Thank goodness the maple syrup was so darn good. Couldn't get enough of that.

I really like the vibe at Saturn Cafe. Lots of diverse families, groups, and individuals. An all around great place to go...just don't expect much on the flavor scale.

I recently eat at Saturn Café and found the food here quite delicious.  Even if you do not describe yourself as a vegetarian or vegan, the food at Saturn Café will satisfy even those that prefer to eat meat!  After much deliberation on what to order, I decided on the FLT sandwich (Fakin bacon, lettuce, tomato and mayo on toasted sourdough) and fries (thin cut).  Both the FLT sandwich and fries tasted so good.  The fakin bacon even had the same texture and crunch as the real thing!  Eating a burger or a sandwich at Saturn Café really feels like a guilt-free pleasure.  Next time I will definitely leave room so that I may try out the awesome desserts sold here!

Awesome hibiscus cooler. 
Slightly awesome jalapeno rings, but Del Taco may have them beat.
Creative veggie "club", but executed poorly and tastelessly. 

Just...really mediocre fried food. Sorry, Saturn, you have an awesome concept, but I won't be back.

I'm sad to say that the new Saturn really let me down :(

I've been known to drive down to Santa Cruz just for this late night fully vegetarian diner but when I heard that one opened in Berkeley I got super excited!!

Anyway, my experience there was the worst Saturn experience yet. I got the avocado club. Seriously, 80% of it was bread and not just your everyday bread it was GROSS bread...thick white SUPER buttery soggy yucky bread. The little tiny chick patty in there was pretty good but really for 10 bucks?? They need to give you a good tasting, full flavored tasty sandwich. This just wasn't right. I seriously couldn't eat the bread (note: I am FAR from a picky eater...really. I'll eat almost anything) I ended up just eating the chick patty and the avocado, leaving the 99% of the bread on my plate. I could have bought a whole box (4) of patties and an avocado at Safeway and still had a few bucks left. 

AND, the hominy soup tasted like nothing. Seriously, if I would have closed my eyes I would have thought I was eating a bowl of tap water...I guess that's better than tasting like shit.

2 stars because the service was good and the people seemed nice. The restaurant was also very clean.

AND, they don't have the Chix Parm. How can they downsize their menu when opening a new location?? The new location should have MORE stuff so that people are EXCITED to try it.

I've now had 3 visits to Saturn Cafe in Berkeley. Service on the first visit was harried & spotty.  Second visit, service was so quick and efficient - a much slower Monday night.  Third visit was this evening - it seemed like they had more customers than expected but my server Drew was super fast, efficient and professional.  He did his job very well on an exceptionally busy, rainy Valentine's night.

The food is mostly pretty good but you definitely have to pick and choose.  The little taquitos are delicious but not soy-free.  The garlic fries and sweet potato fries are outstanding - tremendously delicious!  You could do yourself to death on fried food here. 

They use plenty of meat analogs so it would be great if they had more info on their menu about which items were vegan vs vegetarian - they have a great soy-free/gluten-free list on the website - but that information is not on the menu.  

However, they do have a portobello mushroom burger which the menu specifies comes with vegan mayo.  The ever attentive & particular Drew actually heard me when I was asking about soy-based foods -- I don't do great with stuff with soy protein isolate.  I didn't even think to ask but he put in my order for "No Nayonnaise!" on my burger!  Pretty rockstar if you ask me! 

The burger itself came on a fluffy bun and wasn't really a burger - I was expecting a nice big juicy portobello mushroom -- but it was sauteed strips of mushroom in a GIANT pile of onions, with two slices of tomato and a small piece of romaine.  The mushrooms & onions on bread is not a bad idea (and would be better with bbq sauce) but it made the soft bun so soggy that it was impossible to eat it as a sandwich.   The garlic fries tonight were amazing as usual.

The crispy tofu salad was a bit disappointing - the tofu wasn't even crispy!  My friend had the Cowgirl salad - and wisely ordered the small version - and was very satisified.

I highly recommend the cilantro lime salad dressing - yum.  I'm not sure about the desserts because nothing's labeled well enough on the menu as to soy/no soy -- if the milkshakes were made with Rice Dream or Luna & Larry's - I'd totally get one in a heartbeat; but if it's made with "Soy Delicious" -  I know it will be yummy and then I'll be queasy the rest of the night.

I haven't yet had brunch here - but have heard from one vegan friend that the pancakes disappointed her.  I'm willing to go the extra mile for Yelp to try them and report back to update my review.

Meanwhile, if you see Drew - give him a really good tip.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is so cute. It has some retro spacey feel to it with all the decorations and the way the waiters/waitresses are dress.

This is the first vegetarian burger joint I've tried and it was actually satisfying! I got a chicken, bacon, avocado sandwich and the sandwich was large. The menu said triple decker, but since it's vegetarian I honestly imagined this dinky little sandwich, not to discriminate!

The service is really friendly and waited patiently for me and our friends to make our decisions on our orders.

I hear they have delicious nachos. Something to look forward to during my next visit here!

I've been to this location along with the original Santa Cruz spot several times. I've never been compelled to leave a review 'til now. I was craving a nice vegan brunch & couldn't think of a better place nearby.

The last time we were here, the service sucked, to put it mildly... This time around the service was fantastic! Our server "Bree" (gorgeous, stacked, & courteous) did it all! From seating us, to taking & delivering our order, all the while refiling our drinks. 

Of course she had to do it all since they seemed to be woefully understaffed as evidenced from the "now hiring" sign posted on the front door. Also, it appeared there was only one cook working in the kitchen. Our food took an inordinate amount of time to arrive. Normally not a big deal but we were in a bit of a time crunch. Hopefully they add a few more girls like Bree to get this place movin'!

As for the food, I appreciate that they seemed to have increased the amount of vegan options from when they first started up. Unfortunately it's still Morningstar or bust for the breakfast "meats". Although according to some people. they're "the best" even if they're not vegan. The french toast was delicious as always. I can't believe I never tried the breakfast scramble. Super good with just the right amount of nutritional yeasty goodness! A vegan biscuits & gravy woulda been the proverbial cherry on top if they had it. 

Can't wait to make a return trip, if only to sit @ the counter n sip some coffee or have a few beers...

To all Vegetarians out there: This is THE PLACE to go for BREAKFAST.  I just got back from there for brunch. The ambiance is clean, hip, and warm. The staff is all mildly attractive (meaning: non-threateningly attractive).  My server RYAN is very cute, nice, and friendly.  He makes great suggestions, first timers, ask for him.  His recommended Soy Vanilla Milkshake with Peanut Butter is AMAZING, he even makes it in-front of you!!!  I got the Muffinator, it was really good, even better when I realized (after eating my meal), it was one of the cheapest things on the menu.  This place is like a timeless hipster joint, it is all American, but all Vegetarian, AWESOME!!!!

The BF and I had a GroupOn here, so we enthusiastically decided to give it a try.

Instead of two stars, I wish I could give this place two black holes.

Our taste-buds were definitely disappointed as we experienced the acclaimed Saturn Cafe, consuming our breakfast burrito and nachos.

While the presentation deserves an honorable mention, the taste certainly falls out of orbit.  There just wasn't anything special, and each bite goes bland after a few moments.  Bring in the tapatio and extra salsa to make it memorable.

Then there was our vanilla bean sundae that was seriously 80% whip-cream.

The place is cute, but the service and food needs definite improvement.

I saw the Berkeley Players (http://www.yelp.com/biz/berkeley-players-berkeley) perform here on a Friday night.  They have a nice little performance space in a separate area from the restaurant, just past the bathrooms. 

Saturn Cafe is BARTable, always a plus in my book.  

We got there early for the show and grabbed a seat in the restaurant.  Some friends who were sitting at the bar were told they couldn't order drinks without ordering food.  They didn't seem thrilled about this but I understand that it may have to do with an attempt to prevent "bar creep" and maintain a healthy food to drink sales ratio.     

I ordered an IPA and it was tasty.  All of the beers they carry are from a Santa Cruz brewery.  I wasn't feeling very hungry so I just ordered the soy taquitos appetizer.  They were pretty darn good with the fresh salsa and I snagged a couple zucchini sticks from my honey and enjoyed those as well.  Prices seemed very reasonable - good for a college community. 

The service was fine, although a bit distant and it did feel like we had to flag down our server a few times.  I heard that there was service in the performance space but never saw anyone after we sat down for the show.  I also heard that it was one person working that area and the place was packed so I am sure it would have been nearly impossible to move through the crowd to take and deliver orders. 

I would return to try some other dishes - definitely before another Berkeley Players improv show held here.

Stopped here for a midwinter's snack - we had a groupon (yeah, yeah, I know, someone called me "Coupon Royalty" this week and I can't deny it) and it was a perfect place to stop for a late lunch after a morning spent running errands.  Love the theme, and veggie/vegan food in a hipster joint is right up my alley.

Our waiter had a tee on that read "Keep the Earth Clean - It's Not Uranus!" which is worth one star right there.  Here's a link - it was a nicer looking shirt than this one, but the message was the same:

http://www.teehugger.com/Keep_The_Earth_Clean_It_s_Not_Uranus_p/thas1031.htm

Saturn Café.  Uranus tee shirt.  Get it?  Good.  This set the tone, and we both ordered sammiches.  I got the "chicken" avocado club, a "triple decker with breaded 'chicken', avocado, fakin bacon, smoked gouda cheese, lettuce, tomato, mayo, and red onions" and a side salad.  Could have used fewer onions, but damn was that sammich good.  A few too many onions, so I set 'em aside.

One quibble about the sandwich was that one of the toothpicks holding it together was in backwards, so imagine that you are supposed to pick up a triple-decker quadrant of a sandwich , pull out two toothpicks, and eat it without it falling apart.  Not too easy when one of the heads of the toothpick is imbedded in the middle of the sammich and you have to pull it apart.  Still, amazing dish that I'd get over and over again.  Protein and avocado in a tasty package - mmmm.

Washed it all down with a delicious pint from Santa Cruz Mt. Brewery and that was that.  I'll probably be back soon and many more times to come.

Saturn, you really only deserve three stars.  But I want to give you four stars because your entire menu is vegetarian and you have the best steak fries in the Bay Area.  But you also have well-meaning but inattentive waitstaff, so three stars it is.

Considering that I often get my lunch on Allston, I come to Saturn relatively rarely.  My supervisor comes more often, and she loves the Santa Fe Salad, which I introduced her to.  It is good, but it's overpriced for what you get.  One could argue that the entire menu is overpriced, but that's more a function of Downtown Berkeley than of Saturn specifically.  I almost always go with either the Space Cowboy or the Cowgirl Blues Burger.  Both are delicious, but unfortunately, the Space Cowboy was the first thing I tried here, and it's the best.  I say unfortunately because there's really nowhere to go but down when you start off at the pinnacle, and the service does begin to wear on you.

My coworkers and I were really excited to come here on Saturn's birthday for the free cupcakes.  I actually got my lunch from here but didn't have any cupcakes because I knew we were coming back as a group.  When we returned around four p.m., there weren't any cupcakes left.  The server told us more would be ready in a little while, which was fine, but he also said, "Well, they're really only for people who eat here, but since I saw you [he was referring to me specifically, not my coworkers] earlier today, I guess you can have some."  

Thanks for your generosity, dude.  Yes, I was here earlier in the day, and no, I didn't take any cupcakes then, as you should have remembered because you offered them to me and I turned them down.  And my supervisor comes at least once a week, so you should have recognized her as well.  But all of that is beside the point.  The signs said FREE CUPCAKES.  They didn't say FREE CUPCAKES WITH PURCHASE.  That might not seem like a big deal, but this was supposed to be a big celebration, and Saturn was supposed to be thanking us for supporting it the past year, and you're going to be borderline snarky?

But the steak fries.  Almost all can be forgiven.

Service- The employees were super nice but not attentive at all. My friend and I waited way too long for everything, including the check. I had to get their attention a couple of times just to get them to take our order. Like I said though, they are super nice.

Food- We started off with the vegan sampler. The choices were BORING! The vegan sampler comes with sweet potato fries, garlic fries, chips & salsa and taquitos. With the exception of the taquitos, everything else is already naturally vegan. Chips and salsa!?! Really? It was partly my fault for not reading the menu thoroughly. Consider this your warning, though!!

Next, we split the peanut sauce-tofu-brown rice-broccoli-cauliflower- bean sprout-pad thai-wannabe dish. It was good but a little on the dry side. The peanut sauce was thick and made the brown rice the consistency of oatmeal. We should have gotten the corn dogs or mini sliders or vegan pancakes.

I had a vegan wheat beer. It was very nice. I had a good buzz. 

It's really close to the Downtown Berkeley BART and close to Jupiter and down the street from Venus.

That's about it.

PART ONE:

My biggest gripe about vegetarian dining in the Bay area is how pricey and sort of full of itself it is.  I was therefore thrilled to hear about the Saturn Cafe - veggie diner food, at only slightly above diner prices!

I went a couple of weeks ago with my girlfriend -- a lifelong vegetarian.  She also recently found out she has a wheat allergy, which makes eating veggie difficult.  She was overjoyed to find out Saturn Cafe had a house-made gluten-free veggie patty.

We each ordered burgers, hers with the gluten-free patty and mine with the griller patty, advertised to taste more like meat.  I was told they were out of the grillers (I overheard several other customers being told they were out of several other items, as well), so I changed it to fake chicken at our server's suggestion.  I also got a chocolate/peanut butter vegan milkshake, just to see what that was like.

The food took a loooooong time to come out.  When it finally arrived, my girlfriend's burger had the same fake chicken as mine.  Annoying at the best of times, but totally inexcusable after our conversation with the server about her wheat allergy.  One bite of that and she would have been very ill, at the least. 

We had some trouble getting anyone to take care of the mix-up, but once our server came back she was very helpful getting the burger replaced.  

After another loooooong wait for the replacement food (after which time mine was practically stone-cold) we finally got to eat.  The food, thankfully, was great.  My burger was drowned in chipotle sauce, but I didn't mind because it was probably the best chipotle sauce I've ever had.  The shake was also better than expected.  Dairy, schmairy.  My girlfriend loved her burger and fries.

I think most of the problems of that visit were due to the place and the staff being new.  Still lots of kinks to work out, but lots of potential.  Definitely worth returning.

PART TWO:

Yesterday, my girlfriend and I were out with a group of friends and we were hungry.  Given that Saturn Cafe was the only gluten-free diner in the area, we made the 20-minute drive to eat there, only to be told the wheat-free burger had been taken off the menu.  Why?  Well, according to our server the people who make the patties only felt able to make one kind, and it was impossible to make a wheat-free burger that was also vegan.  So even though there is already a vegan patty on the menu, it was decided to axe the wheat-free one for yet another vegan option.

I don't get this.  It doesn't make sense ethically, nor does it function from a business perspective.  Gluten intolerance affects a sizable part of the population, and the numbers are on the rise.  Why throw away a customer base that you would otherwise have monopolized?  Especially when vegans already had a burger option.  Do they really need two at the expense of people who have no other option?  Especially in a city like Berkeley, which already caters so strongly to the vegan crowd.

I don't mean to open a discussion on the ethics of veganism, but let's not forget that being vegan is a choice, whereas gluten-intolerance is a medical condition.  Vegans believe in what they're doing, and that's great, but they don't actually get violently ill / die if they eat a piece of cheese.

I want to give Saturn Cafe a better rating, but between the amateur management of the place, and now the removal of one of the major menu items which set it apart from the crowd, I just can't.  

The food is tasty, and the wait staff is super, but whoever is in charge over there really doesn't seem to know what they're doing.

I imagine supply/stock issues will improve over time, as will the speed of the kitchen staff.  If that happens, and they put wheat-free burgers back on the menu, I'll eat there regularly.  Until then, there's just no reason to bother going back.

Also, the graffiti style sign up over the shake counter is stupid.  It doesn't fit the decor at all, and is just distracting.

What can I say? It's Saturn Cafe. Their Santa Cruz location makes up easily 50% of my college memories. 

Now I can take a visit down memory lane whenever I want by simply strolling down the road during my lunch break. Can't put a star rating on that.

I LOVE MEAT. And yet, this still held my attention.

I was under the impression that the Saturn Cafe simply featured vegan and veggie delights, and was not strictly veggie. I was under this impression up until our food was in front of us.

The menu is pretty extensive, burgers and breakfast food.  Its hard to find nice places open a little later, and this was a winner.

The interior is so cool, I love the vintage diner look and their tables are stand alone pieces of art.  

We got the sampler appetizer, which was insane. The fried zuccini was awesome, but my favorite was the tostadas by far. The onion rings were huge and they are known for their sweet potato fries, and understandably, they're way too good.

We then shared the slider plate that had one of each burger they feature, fakin bacon, pancakes, and a corndog. For two girls, we eat a lot. 

Each of the sliders were insanely good, my favorite was the guacamole burger, my friend liked the one with avocado. I couldn't make it past the sliders. But, from what I hear, the pancakes and corn dog were awesome.  I did get to pick at some fakin bacon, which was more like a bacon chip, but still delicious.

We also split a mint milkshake, and being the good bff that I am, I mad her split it with me with two straws in the glass (blah blah, generic two girls one cup joke, blah blah). 

So,despite having nothing that once had a pulse, I enjoyed my meal and was very happy (if not bloated).

YUM.

I love that this place is open late! They provide all of the necessary diner-style goodies likes burgers, shakes, and fries. They offer pretty good portions, quick service, and a large variety of menu items. My advice is to stick with the classic items like waffles, sandwiches, burgers, etc. because those are definitely the shining stars that you will be craving when you are anything but impressed with other items like the breakfast burrito, quesadilla, or biscuits & gravy.

Oh, you're about to get your Vegan on, are ya? Well bring your purple wigs and robot tattoos, because Saturn Cafe is the perfect spot.

Like it's father restaurant in Santa Cruz, this Saturn Cafe is a solid hit. Wonderful staff, outstanding veggie and vegan menu, and flavors that truly make you forget that you're eating cardboard! I mean de-lic-ous.

The menu ranges from breakfast food to soups, to burgers or full on entrees. At the Santa Cruz Saturn Cafe we had the eggs benedict and the turkey club, both were amazing, so i'm assuming they'd be just as good here at the Berkeley location. However, at the Berkeley Saturn Cafe we tried the mushroom burger- which was totally awesome. Also, the BBQ ranch chicken burger- which was even more awesome and made me forget it was fake chicken! We will so so so be coming back here soon. 

A great veggie restaurant, open until midnight, has a groupon, right next to the campus. I'm a fan!

I really wanted to love Saturn Cafe. I really did. But...I just didn't. Sorry, Saturn. You just didn't do it for me. It's not because I stood in the entry waiting for my dining companion Daisy S. while numerous groups entered and were seated, although nobody seemed to notice me (I must has the invisibility!!). Naw, that's more my fault for not being assertive enough. It's not even that I sort of felt like the girl who seated me hated me and wasn't sure why. Whatever. It's a Berkeley hipster spot, so I kind of expect inattentive/unenthusiastic service. What really disappointed me what the food. And that's what I'm sad about.

We decide to split the vegan sampler, because why not? Garlic fries, sweet potato fries, chips and salsa and taquitos with two dipping sauces. We swapped out the ranch and wasabi for chipotle and BBQ sauce, and it's nice that they don't mind doing that. I also ordered a brown ale (organic Santa Cruz Mountain Brewery, baby), and it was good. I had high hopes for the taquitos, given what I've experienced at Flacos, and even though Claudia V. had told me that these weren't as good, I held out hope. Well. They weren't as good. They weren't bad, okay? Don't think that. They just weren't exciting.
