And, as Daisy pointed out when the sampler arrived, we were at a place with vegan options and 75% of the platter was food that's vegan anywhere you go. The fries were good, although my mouth tasted like garlic long into the night, even after a vigorous tooth brushing, and so if, unlike me, you're there on a romantic evening, maybe skip the garlic fries. 

After that, we decided to order an entree to see what the food was really about. We got the peanut royale, which I mentioned (once it had been ordered, being too passive, as per usual) hadn't received the best reviews on yelp. Not being a foodie, and not being terribly difficult to please, I enjoyed it. But I see what people mean about it. The peanut sauce tasted like peanut butter and was very mild. I felt like it needed salt or a kick of some sort. Wasn't blown away by it, wouldn't order it again, but it was pleasant. Also ordered another beer (the amber this time). It was good. The beer was probably the highlight of my meal, actually. 

Our server was nice, too. I think he thought we were a little strange, but he was nice. And the person refilling water was probably the most attentive person in the whole place, and never let my glass remain empty for too long. Even joked with me about my "problem," as I have a tendency to drink obscene amounts of water/any drink refilled for free when I'm out to eat. 

I think I'll be back to Saturn. But next time, I'm going to try something a little more special. Like their little sliders (I've been obsessed with sliders for almost a decade and have never had them on account of my vegetarianism) or corndogs. And maybe one of the vegan desserts. 'Cause what I ate last night, while pleasant, didn't do much for me. But I think I should give Saturn another shot. At some point.

I was a big fan of the old Joshu-ya, so this was my first visit to the new version. It's definitely fancier! I appreciated the "brasserie" style, but when it comes down to it, I just want sushi at Joshu-ya, not fancy chef's menus with wine pairings. The sushi is consistently good, although minus one star for higher prices than the old Joshu-ya. But I'll still come back :)

Since they have switched over management, it's much faster. MUCH faster. Quality is decent. I went with a girlfriend and she ordered the Lion King - the baked salmon was a bit tasteless and commented that the house sauce used to have a bit more kick. Took a bite and she was right - nothing too special or flavorful about the roll.

I ordered the Paparazzi roll and it was pretty good. The salmon and tuna on top were fresh. Wasabi wasn't as much of a kick in the mouth as in other places, though still good. 

Service was great. Attentive. Hot tea was always refilled before empty. Positive and were friendly even though she and I got caught up in conversation way past closing time (women, I know). 

Overall experience was so-so, on the better end of decent. As a Cal alum and having been here many-a-times, it's always one of the first places I think of to go to. Convenient location, reasonably priced, good seating and nice atmosphere.

The new Joshu-ya's pretends to be a bit fancier but the quality of the food's stayed the same. Unfortunately they've removed a lot of rolls from their menu! I guess they've kept only the most popular ones. My fav's are Lion King, White Orchid, and Lucky Danny. It's a bit pricey, but not overly so for sushi. After all, you don't want your raw fish to come too cheap.

Food is expensive and so so. Only sushi is worth the money. Other dishes, like ramen, teriyaki and anything else, are completely disappointing. It's kind of crowded and noisy with those small tables. I live a block away from it and only go for their sushi lunch special. Now they changed the lunch special to an $8 one which is again disappointing.

Summary: Very good fusion food, service, and atmosphere.  Its sushi rolls were mediocre in comparison.

* Pomme Frites - fries with duck fat - was the best we've had.  Very crunchy thin outer layer, with soft center.  
* Equally good was the beef sliders: topped with kimchi and garnished with arugula, and the patty was THICK and juicy.
* The 6-hour pulled pork belly tacos had some secret sauce that's light and balances out the flavorful (aka fatty) pork.  We did not want to think about what it would look like when cold and solidified, but it sure tasted GOOD.
* We also had sukiyaki and a eel roll - these were just OK.  When everything else was so good, we wondered if these items came from another kitchen...

3 stars for the Japanese items, 5 stars for everything else (including great value for the price)
Excellent and affordable artistic omakase.

This place had fairly good sushi.  I wouldn't give it the full five b/c some of the maki rolls didn't seem to be wrapped tightly enough.  But the important thing is that the food was great.  The Lion King roll (had salmon) must have been baked or grilled since it came wrapped in tinfoil!  And the portion sizes were excellent.  Would definitely go back again.
Everyone there was very nice and attentive. And the food was excellent. I wish I would have discovered this place sooner!

Pretty tasty -- all of the fish was tender and fresh -- and for the quality, prices are quite reasonable. I'm not sure why this place doesn't get the attn that Kirala does, for I find it to be just as tasty. Oh, and decent selections for non-sush eaters, outside of the standard teriyaki, etc. Service is friendly, but a bit spacey. 

Overall, a win. Din for 3 will run around $80-100, w/o dranks.

This is my 2nd visit to this Restaurant again.

I have to write again because I was surprise this place CLOSED?!?!. Noooo they changed the name!
It used to be Joshu-Ya Sushi (old) - Joshu-Ya Brasserie (current)
Plus Jason own the owner to this place!

anyway I came back and the service is much better than it was in the past, yay no longer slow.

Food: well I look at the menu I notice the lunch special and this caught my attention right away. They serve BURGER at a sushi place? WOW I was impressed, so I had to order it and it pretty good. 

Rest my case NOM NOM NOM!

I am in love with this place!! I have been here twice and Im blown away. 

My first experience was shortly after the restaurant had major renovations to become what is now the brasserie. Everything looked great, especially the outside patio. My family and I were greeted by a friendly hostess and immediatley seated. My parents thoroughly enjoyed the OMAKASE tasting menu, which had the freshest of fish. My sister and I had the beef, these were cooked to perfection. My brother raved about his pork belly soba noodles. We ended the meal by sharing three different deserts. The tempura Ice cream and two different ice cream scoops. All were completely delicious, the tempura ice cream I could eat everyday. We left satisfied and happy.

My second experience is what really blew me away. They added some great new creative dishes and tapas. This time around I was with a few friends. We started with the kimchi sliders and the pork belly tacos. These opened my palette to some creative, exciting layers of flavor combinations I would never expect. They were sooo good! As well as the spicey tuna hand roll  and duck fat fries, as far as Im concerned should be cooked no other way. Can you say Ahhhhh-ddicting. For my entree I had the Duck Confit which was absolutely delicious and would just melt in my mouth.
 
Joshu-ya, I am a fan and will most definetly be back for more to come. Thanks!
HUGS and Kisses!

Since we were already passing by Berkeley, I wanted to go somewhere I didn't usually frequent in the area. Joshu-Ya offered a fresh take on things that piqued my curiosity.

For starters, we ordered a few nigiri pieces. Unfortunately, the cuts were not smooth and the meat was thinly torn in several areas. Fortunately, the meat was of decent quality and the sweetness came through.

I had the confit de canard (duck leg confit), which was served over soba suspended in a bonito-duck broth. The duck was executed well with its crispy skin and delicious fork-tender flesh. The soba, however, was ordinary, much like the broth it was served in. While the limelight may have been intended for the duck, the abrupt contrasts between rich and light often distracted from its inherent fatty flavor. And on the flip side, the duck overpowered the other ingredients. The dish felt like it was missing something that could have connected the two cuisines. Bonito-duck broth by itself is a little naive. The dish was also a little difficult to eat without drowning the duck in the broth. It's like rinsing a piece of freshly grilled steak with water.

I was pleasantly surprised at their chirashi, which at $18 is actually a pretty good deal compared to most other places. Here, their deceptively small chirashi bowl is actually densely packed with tasty slices of the chef's choice of fish (better than our nigiri) and other items over well-prepared rice.

Charming, cozy interior with decent service.

I am kind of obsessed with Joshu-Ya. I eat here every chance I get. If I'm doing sushi in the bay area this is it. The fish quality is phenomenal and the chefs do a great job.
My favorite things to order off the menu:
Chirashi
7 piece sushi dinner
hand rolls(usually spicy tuna or salmon/avocado)
Marilyn Monroe roll
Cinderella Roll
Warm Soba Lunch Combo

This was a recommendation from a foodie friend while I was in the SF area. The drive to Berkeley was not inconvenient at all so it is definitely accessible from the city.  
The exterior is chic with a bit of a Japanese garden feel where you can sit outdoors. The interior is cozy decorated with local artists' paintings. Everyone was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu and sushi. 
We started off with live scallop sushi as per recommendation of the server. It was fresh and tasty. Great presentation using the scallop shell. Next we had the slow cooked pork soba noodles. The pork was soft and fell apart and melted in your mouth. We then had the sushi lunch which was six chefs choice nigiri sushi. Wow, I was impressed at how fresh the fish were. I used to work at Morimoto NYC and the quality is definitely comparable! A highlight of this dish was the seared salmon with a homemade truffle creme. And finally, we finished with dessert, which was the perfect finish to our meal. A tapioca and homemade red bean ice cream. Delicious!!! Creamy yet very flavorful without being too sweet. 

Overall we were very happy and pleased with our experience. I would come back again when I'm in the area, but this time I would try the omakase. I hear Chef Kwon is the mastermind to the new menu so defintely be on the look out for what he does next.

So happy with this place. The service is awesome, food is awesome, price is awesome! I love eating here and every time I do, I get so happy. I wish they served a mini salad though (like they used to)...
Just another over priced Japanese sushi restaurant .the food was alright. i wouldnt eat here again

months, maybe even years, after driving by and wondering what this treehouse sushi fusion place was like, we finally went. very pleasantly surprised! located inside a house, joshu-ya brasserie serves quite a variety of sushi, from the standard to live (aka still wiggling) uni, to cooked entrees, to daily specials. hope to come back!

An interesting blend of Japanese/Sushi/Tapas/French going on here, which is certifiably exciting, but also a little expensive. I really want to try the chef's tasting menu but you need everyone in your group to commit to 35$/person first, which is easier said than done.

A standout in upscale-ish dining on south side, the sushi was relatively fresh and the presentation was great. It has major competition on the non-sushi Japanese front from Norikonoko and Kiraku which are a block away.

Great place for a fast and efficient lunch; but it is spring break, I'm sure this place is busier when schools in session.

I had the soba lunch. It was good! I didn't manage much of my soba as the salad as handrolls were so filling. The spicy tuna handroll was especially yum.

Also the duck fat fries - to DIE for! I couldn't stop eating them and they were meant to be for the table. I shall be back. Let's leave it that. Think I will come with the hubs and explore the tapas menu. Yum!

I am a frequent visitor of this sushi place since it is the one decent sushi place near the Berkeley campus. Although I really love the sushi here, the service here is just plain bad. Hence the one star rating. The last two times I've been there the waiter has just been non-existent. The first time I came with my friend for lunch. The waiter took forever to get our order and bring out our food. He was not attentive AT ALL. He didn't even bother to give us our check after we asked for it multiple times. Me and my friend were seriously close to just walking out without paying. The next time I went was less than a week after. My roommate and I ordered a to go order. After waiting for half an hour, our food was still not out. I had to go complain to the waiter before I FINALLY got my food. I don't know how long it would have taken if I didn't go and complain. My advice to the staff of this place... GET BETTER WAITERS or get more of them. This place always seems to be understaffed because I never seem to get the service I pay for.

I guess 3rd time is not a charm.  I keep coming back here hoping that the food will somehow get better but I think it has gotten worse. 

(-) Lion King. Typical lion king roll. Nothing special. It's either the portion got smaller or the plates got bigger every time. The salmon was not hot enough when it was served either! 

(+++)  Murasaki: I'm not going to lie, this one is probably my second favorite sushi roll I've ate in Berkeley. The spicy tuna was just melted in your mouth and the shrimp tempura on top accompanied the tuna really well. However, the portion was tiny! I can't believe it was $10.50 for 4 small rolls. I swear I could have finished the 4 rolls in less than 2 minutes. 

This place is too expensive for broke college students in Berkeley, especially because the portion is too small. The service here was really slow. We waited more than 40 minutes for our food ( order of 4 rolls).  The waitress was really nice though. She kept checking up on us and refilled our drinks every 15 minutes. I secretly think she was trying to make us full with water so we wouldn't realized how long our food was taking. If I took my money and time to a different place in Berkeley, I swear I could have gotten a feast.

I think they have the best sushi within the UC campus area. Though it's kinda crowded for dinner, they have amazing lunch specials, like a 5-item bento for less than $10! What a deal! I personally love their Danny roll, the best! The atmosphere is a plus too

I wasn't quite sure what to think of a restaurant serving French and Japanese fusion but I was not disappointed at all.  The sushi was delicious and fresh.  I had the jalapeno hamachi carpacchio, pommes frites,  zoolander, Marilyn Monroe and Amsterdam rolls.  All incredibly good.  I paired the sushi with some riesling wine, as good a pairing as cab and steak.  The pommes frites were fried in duck fat.  It had a rich flavor that just doesn't compare to frites fried in other fat although this was bordering on the salty side.  Just for fun, I ate some sushi along with the frites which was surprisingly good.  The sweetness and spice of the sushi along with the savoriness and crunch of the frites actually paired well.

This is one of the nicer places to eat around the Berkeley campus. 

I tried it once before it was converted into the brasserie.  I thought the first Joshu-ya sushi boat was okay as much as others might've liked it. 

I tried this one using the coupon from Munchonme.  I'm glad I bought it because I love porridge and have never tried non-Chinese porridge before.  Their pork belly porridge was SOOOOOO good.  Their California hand roll was also one of the best California roll I've had.  P ordered a nigiri/sashimi lunch plate and thought it it was better than Tako but did not live up the hype.

The atmosphere is very nice and so was our waiter.

The sushi and other menu items here were hit or miss for me. I enjoyed the traditional nagiri sushi, the fish was fresh and it was presented well. However, the rolls were over priced, and didn't blow me away. Other menu items are good as well; so far I have tried the kobe beef burger (best in my opinion), and the bento box (average).

Haven't been here for a couple years, but I like what they've done to the place. Looks more modern! The food is just as I remembered it, still fresh and delish. The sake and beer is definitely a steal during HH and if I wasn't so ful I wish I had gotten a chance to try the pork belly tacos! I ordered the cherry blossom roll very good! We were in a rush so didn't get to eat everything like I wanted to, but it's nice knowing there's a good sushi spot in Berkely if I ever venture back out here.

I'm a huge sushi fan! It's probably one of those things I just can't get enough of. So, when one of my friends suggested meeting up at Joshu-Ya for her celebratory birthday dinner I was excited (even though I had sushi twice during the week). I was even more excited when she told me that there was a parking lot designated for their customers. Do you know how difficult it is to find parking (much less, FREE parking) in Berkeley?! It is quite difficult. So, this was definitely a plus!

We met up at 6:30 on a Friday night, and I was expecting a long wait. Perhaps we were lucky because we were seated immediately. We were seated in the newly renovated area, and it looked quite fancy. Other than the fact that there was another boisterous group of college students celebrating a birthday (they were so loud that I could barely even hear what my friend was saying), the place was pleasant.

This place has wonderful customer service. I like to gauge the level of customer service by how full my cup of water is. The entire time we were there my cup was full or near full, so I'd say our WAITERS were very attentive. That's right...WAITERS! Our table was attended by at least three or four waiters (which is something I'm not used to). But, hey, I'm not complaining (another plus!).

Aside from a sushi buffet, I've never been to a Japanese restaurant that didn't have a Bento box as an option on their menu. So, that was a surprise to me. But, no worries because...I become more indecisive when faced with more choices. So, at this point, I'm divided between the "Joshu-Ya" roll and the "Spider" roll. Did I want unagi or soft-shelled crab? That was a tough decision because both sounded delicious, so we ordered BOTH of them. I'm so glad that we ordered both because they were scrumptious (not to mention, each of the rolls looked like food art...great presentation)! And to top it all off we ordered their tempura green tea ice cream. This thing was GINORMOUS! This thing could easily feed two or three people.

Since it was my friend's birthday, it'd only be appropriate for me to cover the bill. But, of course, she's too courteous to allow that to happen, so we both end up fighting over the bill...in front of one of the waiters. Awkward, right?! He ends up taking both of our cards. But before he left our table, I did tell him it was my friend's birthday (I was hoping he'd take that into consideration when deciding which card to ring up). When he came back he told me: "I hope it's really her birthday." (Which indicates that he charged it onto my card instead of my friend's) And because of that, I tipped him a bit extra.

I really liked this place. There were so many great things:
+ Free parking
+ Little to no wait
+ Food came out quickly
+ Artistic food presentation
+ Great customer service
+ Great food
(But, I had to give it four stars because, even though the food was great, it was a bit pricey.)

This is my favorite place to go for Japanese food in the Berkeley area.  All their sushi rolls are terrific, and their entrées are good choices if you want to avoid the hefty cost of rolls.  I recommend getting the beef sukiyaki; it is very filling and delicious. On top of their good food, their service has no flaws.

If you want dessert, go with the tempura fried ice cream.  It consists of a soft, warm breading (tempura), strawberry gastrique, with a nicely-contrasting cold ice cream.  The flavors I have tried (green tea, vanilla, red bean) all go well with the tempura.

Came on a weeknight for dinner with some coworkers. I loved their Papparazzi roll - clean and simple - Yellowtail, Tuna, Salmon, Avocado! Shiro Maki roll was also ok - albacore and fried onions. The waiter was super friendly though - great plus! I also had the tempura soba to share with my colleague Gina. It was alright - nice and light after a hard-working tiring day on our feet for 6 hours. It's a super cute place - nice for a date!

This place is very very nice for japanese food. It's very inexpensive too. The service was fast and friendly, and the selection huge. Lots of hot waitresses too. Parking lot on the side, which you have to pay. Outside seating if it's warm enough, although they have heaters.

This is by far my favorite restaurant still existing in Berkeley. My friends and I have always said, in the far away future if our kids end up at Cal, one restaurant we would have to revisit is Joshu-ya. Sushi is not the most sustainable food for students but Joshu~ya has some good appetizers and specials that are priced comparably well to some less-delicious food around campus. Pork Belly tacos are a good $8 appetizer, as well as the $6 Katzu Chicken. The burgers, the udon, you can't miss. The fish has always been good in my experiences as well. I've been so often that I have tried almost everything on the menu and it's all delicious if you're a sushi lover.

I've come here for lunch on several occasions and it's quite a steal. They offer some of the best tempura just about anywhere and their sushi has been nothing less than luscious. I have not found a lackluster item on their concise seasonal menu yet. 

Note/Request/Plea: The best part about this place was a dish they used to offer... pork belly porridge. I could curl up in that bowl and hibernate for indeterminate decades. Bring it back and I'll come daily!

After waiting about 10 minutes to a half empty restaurant all the while ignored by a bitchy- looking miniature Asian girl (we heard her on the phone with a customer saying "well yes, as I said, take out will take 45 minutes..." in a slightly irritated manner), we ended up being seated at a completely different side of the restaurant at a table that had been ready for us the entire time we had waited anyways. We quickly ordered from a friendly guy in a black shirt who I think was some kind of manager.  My boyfriend ordered the chicken udon which he said was too salty and they used a stringy piece of chicken thigh meat which didn't really go with the soup very well. The noodles tasted good, but it was just very salty to him. Just when my boyfriend was finishing up his soup my first roll finally came. Joahu-yas is really great for quality rolls, and my spider roll was fantastic! When my second roll came the black shirt guy gave us a complimentary spicy tuna roll for waiting so long. Thank you very much that action really made up for bitchy Asian girl hehe! Would be five stars for him and the amazing sushi, but minus two for the bad start and salty soup.

This was the second time I went to Joshu-Ya, and both were for friends' birthdays so we had around 20-25 people. Overall the restaurant isn't too big but they'll accommodate large groups very well which is nice. Except this time we had a reservation for 6PM and didn't really get seated until past 6:30 which was sort of annoying. BUT they're really nice in letting you split up the check, unlike other places that have rules like max three checks for big parties, they asked us how we would like to split it and I think most people just partnered up, meaning 10+ checks, so that was cool!

I ordered a chicken udon, and my friend Alice ordered the ton katsu. The udon came out in a reasonably quick time, and wasn't anything special, but I was satisfied since I was really hungry and with the nice thick noodles and soup too I was quite full by the end. My friend's ton katsu though took longer to come out, and was oddly VERY salty in some parts. I don't know why, some pieces were just extremely salty, and the sauce that came with it didn't seem that impressive. Other people who ordered sushi and special rolls seemed to get their food pretty fast and enjoy it a lot though.

Oh, also ordered a Strawberry Sake-tini for the birthday girl...not that bad a drink really, a bit sweet and you can taste the sake, but not really strong. Anyways since we were in such a large group, we probably were 90% of the noise in the restaurant and I felt bad for being the stereotypical "large, obnoxious group" but eh, couldn't do much about it lol.

Joshu-ya is alright, probably wouldn't really choose to come back again unless it was for an occasion like a birthday.

This place is only ok by SF-standards, but since it's Berkeley, this place is considered pretty fancy haha.

Try the Kimchi Kobe Beef Sliders, those were yummy! They're like mini hamburgers with kimchi, bacon, kobe beef, and some other things. The pommes frites were okay, a little too salty so we couldn't finish them. Rolls and sashimi are all average, slightly on the small side. Apparently, they also have fried shrimp heads! I didn't get to try them, but the couple next to us seemed to really enjoy them, and they were HUGE!

Also, they have this hidden parking lot that I didn't know about until I graduated from Berkeley. You have to drive down this tiny little alley next to the restuarant...it's totally missable. Look hard for it if you don't want to park 5 blocks away from the restaurant.

2nd time this week and I've only become more impressed with the menu and food. I found out from our waiter that the restaurant is under new management now as the owner's son has taken over. 

The food was on par once again.. All my friends got different dishes and I was amazed at how fresh (melt in your mouth) the sashimi was and how there was salmon roe in the duck confeit soba dish! The food was beautifully presented as you can tell the owner is really passionate about his creations. 

Even better, their menu changes every month so there will always be something new to drool over!

I don't go often, but it seems like it has tried to improve itself to the next level to be a bit more fancy. Personally, I was surprised, since my expectations were defined by my last year-old experience. I'd rate it as almost-fancy, 2.5x $.

It has nice decor though. The outside (also a seating option) is well decorated. I appreciated looking out the large windows as well as this window where it goes into a little fountain. I'm not as much a fan of the interior room, however.

The service is nice. There are some spirit options.

They also took away bento boxes for dinner.

But what really annoyed me was this dish that was some $17. We thought it was a main-course dish, but it wasn't and was more like an appetizer with just 5 pieces of fish plus avocado. There are some fancy dishes, and that would be nice if we were expecting it as just a side-dish portion, but we felt mislead, and that took away from my experience of that night.
The new owner remodeled the place.     Unfortunately the food has gone way downhill and the service is intrusive.     Don't waste your money!    It is really too bad!

joshu-ya has been my go-to sushi place since I've arrived in berkeley, but I'd like to highlight a recent experience with them.  I stopped by to order two rolls to go for my girlfriend who was sick.  joshu-ya has expensive rolls (12 dollars each, roughly) but they're huge and just one is enough for a light lunch.  I picked up a paper and started to read while I waited, but a server interrupted me and asked if I wouldn't want to sit and have a glass of water while i waited, and gestured to an open table.  after a somewhat lengthy wait, he came back and gave me a bowl of miso on the house for my patience, and not long after that, brought my order, packaged and ready to go.
Joshu-ya has an incredible atmosphere, day-fresh fish, skilled chefs, large portions, variety, and the best waitstaff in the entire world.  it's not a cheap place, but it's not expensive and it's well worth the money.  I highly recommend it.

Food wasn't bad but service was pretty bad. Servers act like they're all really really high. Don't get me wrong, they all were very polite but had absolutely no memory.

Simply solution was found very quick - ask every waiter what you need (there were 3 of them) and at least one eventually will bring what you ordered :)

The food here is really excellent. 

The nigiri is fantastic because the fish is fantastic.

The atmosphere is also great!

The food is not overpriced for its quality. People just think the food is overpriced because they're used to eating $5 meals in the Asian ghetto. I think Asian ghetto food is overpriced because those horrible ingredients probably cost the "restaurants" $1.50 per dish. Don't ruin this businesses ranking because you expect them to magically make amazing dishes with the freshest and best ingredients at Asian ghetto prices.

Joshua's is the best sushi place in town. I have tried different sushi's here and have like all of them. There secret awesome dish is there sweet potato fries. 

There servers are nice and quick. They really know there sushi. When ever I want sushi I am there.

I came here on a Tuesday night around 7:30 so it wasn't too crowded. The patio area was full but we were seated almost immediately. I had the beef sukiyai, which has beef, onions, glass noodles, napa cabbage, carrots, etc. It also comes with a side of rice. The broth was light and flavorful and the beef had a good texture. 

I will be back to try the rolls and the tapas!

I can only speak for the sushi, but it's way better than Tako. I've only been here twice, but each time was a success. The fish tasted fresh! I really enjoyed the lion king and zoolander rolls! The venue is chill and there's a patio outside that you can eat in on a nice day. To be picky, a waitress offered to refill my tea and she never did. Other than that I thought the service was fine, and worth the extra bucks to eat here rather than Tako.

The fish here is very fresh.  I ordered nigiri and enjoyed it.  However, the service here is pretty crappy.  I came during dinnertime and found myself waiting a long time for food to come.  One of the orders we put in included some fish they no longer had, so rather than make the rest of the order or inform us promptly, the kitchen decided not to make it without informing the server.  We had to input a different order and it took awhile to get to us as well.  Our miso soup (even though we asked for it) never came and I kept having to wave the guy down to refill my tea.  Meh.

I'm glad there is a decent restaurant so close to campus, since pretty much everywhere else in Southside is so sketchy.  

It's a good fusion of traditional Japanese dishes with a modern innovative twist.  I got sick of typical Japanese food awhile back because it's always the same dishes, but here there are some uncommon dishes like the Novata Yaki, and traditional dishes are more upscale, like angus beef teriyaki.

The sushi is very good quality.  A bit on the pricey side from the perspective of a college student, but I think it's worth it.  It's like 10x better quality than Tako sushi but only maybe 2x the price.

A downside is that it is kind of busy and crowded.  Ichiban has a much nicer setting.

Service was pretty fail though when I came here for lunch.  Even though there were only a few tables and several waiters, they seemed to forget a bunch of things.  They gave us the specials menu after we ordered, and they didn't give us tea until I asked them after the miso soup arrived.  Also, my lunch came with handrolls, which I had to remind them about two times.  It came like 5 minutes after I finished the entree.  Maybe the waiter was preoccupied with the table behind us... they ordered some fancy sashimi and sake, and we just had lunch specials, lol.

Oh and there's a window next to their door that looks like a door, so it's always amusing to watch people try to open it...

One of the better sushi places in Berkeley! The ambience is very cute and welcoming, and the food is delicious. I always get the rolls--Lucky Danny and Lion King are my favorites, but I've tried most of the rolls on the menu and they are all very good! 

I've also had the beef sukiyaki which is good but a bit on the salty side, and all of the nigiri and sashimi have been very fresh every time I've ordered. I got some type of shrimp nigiri last time (I think it was raw shrimp + fried shrimp head? I don't remember what it was called because my friend ordered) but that was really surprisingly good. 

The desserts are okay--I've gotten the mochi and the friend tempura ice cream. Nothing too special; it's your typical dessert.

Overall, the place is great. A bit on the pricey side but I feel that the food justifies the price.

Came for dinner for a party of 8

Ordered:
2 orders of short ribs with potatoes 
French fries
Soba noodles 
Mussels 
Pork belly tacos
Kobe sliders
Amsterdam roll 
Hot N Spicy roll
California roll
Tiramisu

Nothing special or spectacular. A lot of it didn't have any flavor. 

Don't order the soba noodles.

The potatoes served as a side/decoration for the short ribs TASTED  a lot better than the main part of the entree which is the short ribs.

The pork belly tacos were good though
Tasty, tasty! Portions are large, food tastes super fresh, the staff is friendly. The menu was a little confusing though.

I love Joshu-Ya! It's definitely the best Japanese restaurant around campus.
If you always get sushi from other places around campus, when you come to Josu-Ya you know how good it is. Everything's so fresh and warm and tender. The rice and the fish and everything have very nice texture and taste. I've been there three times and my favorite are Amsterdam and Lion King roll. Soooo good!!!
The deco is awesome, very Japanese and classy. The waitresses are just awesome. Super nice. 
I'll definitely come back often.

07/23/2012

My friend and I went there yesterday, Sunday, hoping to try their Sunday Brunch Special. The waitress told us that they no longer have the brunch special as of that day. We were told about this special less than 2 weeks ago by another waiter. We were quite disappointed as there are no more specials or bento boxes available. We ended up ordering a spicy crab, salmon, avocado roll and a pork belly soba. My friend enjoyed his roll and I enjoyed the soba except the noodles were way overcooked. Most Japanese like their noodles al dente like the Italian do. The dish would have been stellar had it not been for the soft soba. We will probably go back for other items and maybe the bento boxes will be back.
Good quality food, Inventive menu. The duck fat pomme frites are awesome!!

Tasty but expensive. Came in here for lunch on a Thursday afternoon while wandering berkeley with a friend. Their lunch bento box is a steal,and their sushi was fresh and delicious. I thoroughly enjoyed my sashimi salad although the dressing is spicy, beware! This is a fun spot I will visit again if I am ever in Berkeley.

Absolutely wonderful meal for daughter's birthday!  Beautifully prepared, creative ingredients, so fresh and tasty and staff was attentive and kind. Grandparents and adult kids and grand children - all had a really great meal. I had the Cinderella sushi and it was spectacular and the sushi with the tempura soft shell crab was extra special. Fabulous technique and sooo good!

Very fancy, maybe too fancy? overrated? I've come here a couple times and their food is great, but they are just overwhelmed by people. The first time I came, the waiter helping us was very attentive at the beginning but then disappeared. He never brought me the hot sauce I asked. The prices are a little too pricey for me as well. Maybe I was just used to the older prices. I've also had the chance to eavesdrop a conversation between the chef/owner of the restaurant talking with some of his friends at a table in front of us. He came out to be very snobby about his talent and his background. Is flaunting in front of your customers a good thing or bad? He didn't even smile or say a hello. I don't know, in the past when someone like that is out in the public they at least acknowledge their customers.

The new Joshu-Ya has stepped up the decorating giving a new, fancy-like restaurant feel that isn't too fancy, for lack of a better term!

The sushi isn't the cheapest, but it is a bearable cost.  For some reason they tried to mix in some new appetizers that stray away from the usual Japanese food, I guess that's the "brasserie" part of it.  

So I decided to try the french fries fried in duck fat.  I really like french fries, so I could tell a slight difference in the taste of the fries, while my other friend couldn't really.  Slightly expensive order of fries I might say!

The sushi was fine.  I got the Zoolander which had a mix of different fish rolled in with cream cheese.  I'm definite biased toward the cream cheese part because i love cream cheese, but I thought the fish wasn't too bad at all, decently fresh and tasty.  

My friend on the other had had the Paparazzi roll, which had a different combination of fishand mainly avocado down the middle.  The fish here was fine too!

Though these rolls were both over $10, but it did have a good amount of raw fish.  These were the "signature rolls," there were cheaper more common rolls like the crunch roll, spider roll and such.  

I usually like my sashimi, but these signature rolls were kinda like a transitory roll from the general maki roll to sashimi/nigiri, as there was a lot of raw fish involved!  So these kinda rolls are great if youre trying to transition out of the sushi stage where you only eat maki rolls, YOU KNOW WHO YOU ARE :)

In a short comparision to berkeley, this place is a step up from Tako sushi, probably about even or a little better than CU sushi, but definitely not as good as Kirala and Shattuck and Ward.

happy sushi eating :)

Came here for lunch. We both had the sashimi lunch special.  Service was super friendly- they were very concerned about the comfort of our sleeping baby - although they were definitely overworked. Sushi was great, and dinner menu looked amazing.  Really great place.

Granted, this place is better than the sushi places closer to campus but the service is SO BAD that I'd rather not eat sushi at all. 

I went with some of my girlfriends and it took us 20 minutes to our food! And we SAW it sitting on counter AND our waitress had like maybe 3 tables total to handle. Fail. 

Then it took us god knows how long to get the actual bill. 

Food is average. Expensive for the quality they gave us. 

Oh, and they remodeled. It looks a little nicer but doesn't compensate for their horrible service and high prices.

I went into this restaurant with fairly terrible expectations, but I was pleasantly surprised by the service, ambiance and, most importantly, the food.

Service, Decor:
It's true that this place looks like a ghetto eatery from the outside, especially since it's so close to hippie-crammed telegraph, but inside it's actually quite lovely. The dark wooden chairs and tables give a certain elegance and it was quiet enough for my family to sit and chat. I had my misgivings about the service after all the negative reviews on yelp, but our waiter was actually quite fast and responsive to our needs, refilling our tea multiple times and asking how our food was. 

Food: Everyone knows sushi around Berkeley isn't very good and we'd rather just get cheap food that'll fill us, but I actually liked the sushi here. We got the combination sushi, Paparazzi roll, Beef Sukiyaki, and the Tempura Soba. All of the sushi that we got were very fresh, and I was even surprised to see some fatty salmon on our Paparazzi, which was delightful. Both dishes were presented nicely, though I found the dangling sprigs of thyme on the combination sushi to be slightly overkill and the roll to be a bit messy (as if the knife needed to be sharpened).

The Tempura Soba was a little bland for me, but my parents liked it very much. The tempura was crisp and not oily, which means the chefs did a good job in cooking it at a very high temperature and drying it off immediately. The Beef Sukiyaki was a little sweet and I was a bit disappointed to see chunks of steak instead of the customary thinly-sliced beef, but it was still satisfying to eat with its mixture of jelly noodles and vegetables. If it weren't for my few grievances, I may have given this place a five.

Despite my quest to find cheap and delicious food, I believe I will be coming here again. Yes, sushi and Japanese cuisine tends to be expensive, but if you're taking someone on a date or you want to go somewhere quiet to eat and chat, this is definitely a place you should consider.

P.S. The ownership has changed, so if you didn't like it before, I say it's a good idea to try again.

Vegan review! - Went here in the afternoon and didn't check to see if they had any vegan options. However, the servers knew what 'vegan' was and were very accommodating. 

I got the Garden roll after confirming that the onions were fried in vegetable oil. Was quite fulfilling and fresh (only about 5 pieces though). Skip on the miso soup because depending on the cook there that day, it might have fish flakes in it. Later asked for a side of rice but they came out with it after we got our dessert, so I got it free of charge :) 

Friendly service and nice atmosphere. Would go there again!

Sushis were ok, but $7 the small sake...

EDIT: There was a mistake with my bill, small sake are $4.

Not the same anymore. 

It's kinda sad. I am not sure if there is a new owner or they just renovated the place, but it is definitely not the same menu and quality sushi they used to have. They also changed the name of the place to "brasserie" I supposing to make it more Japanese-American.I remember reading some American dishes and the some fusion of both cuisines.. (wtheck?!)

When I came here last time, my friend ordered the Chicken Katsu dish. My other friend ordered the Spicy Tuna roll and Chicken Udon. I ordered the Unagi roll.

The Chicken Katsu was definitely too salty. The dipping sauce that usually comes along with it wasn't even needed. My friends and I had to eat extra rice to balance out the salty-ness, therefore making us full really fast from all the starch. I was so disappointed since I remember it being much better when Joshuya had their Bento Box deals. 

The Chicken Udon was mediocre. I mean... it didn't taste horrible, but it was nothing special. 

The only decent items were the spicy tuna and the unagi roll. They completely changed everything else. I am giving two stars for the quality of food. But I might say the renovation made it more romantic! 

BRING BACK THE BENTO BOX! :)

Went here for the boyfriend's birthday. Saturday night, didn't make reservations so it was about a ten minute wait. It's a small restaurant, about 20 tables tops, along with an outdoors patio. 

we ordered;

LIKES:
POMMES FRITES: these fries were BOMBDOTCOM, esp the spicy aioli sauce that came along with it. Potato fried in duck fat, a genius idea, and even more genius, that spicy aioli sauce. mmm, I mainly snacked on these.

Jalapeño Pork Belly Soba: this was an interesting and delicious dish. the soba noodles were soft yet they still had a bite to it. and the crunchy jalapeno and radishes were the perfect touch to the soft pork belly. mmmmmyum.

DISLIKES: 
Lucky Danny: nothing extremely extravagant. the sushi rice felt lukewarm, not entirely cooled nor warm. it was an odd feeling. 

Spicy Crunchy: might as well name it Soggy-Bland. there was barely any "crunchy" bits in the sushi roll. also it wasn't even spicy, and I don't even typically eat spicy!

Lion King: I would say the boy enjoyed this a bit more than me. I personally didn't care for it that much. It said it had a parmesan sauce, but no where did I get a whiff of parmesan what-so-ever. 

Service was slow, and food is overpriced.

Overall, this is a one-time place for me.. I wouldn't come back for their rolls but if I was ever in the area, and craved some fries, this would be my stop. I would order fries to go, and eat it on the little bench across the street.

I stopped for a spell, I had French pressed coffee and my favorite Unagi (baked eel).
 It was so good, and the service was absolutely excellent.
I will definately be back very soon.

This is without a doubt the best sushi I have had in a very long time.  It was fresh and top quality.  The food was artfully presented and professionally served.   The manager, Natalie, was especially helpful with suggestions which was much appreciated.
This place is awesome. Great food, great atmosphere and always a fun time! Not only is the sushi the freshest in town, but the other entrees are great too!

This is my first time writing on yelp because I hope that this review will at least make few people not to waste their money.

I do not know why this place a four star restaurant!!

I would have given 2 stars, but since it is high rated, i am giving one star just to bring it down.

I have been to many restaurant but this place is not the place you want to go.

Food is mediocre and is in small portion even compared to nearby Japanese restaurant. It not worth the price to pay 15 dollar dish for Mac Donald level of quality.

Even though the waiter was nice, it takes him 15 minutes to get to you when there is only 3 groups of people.

Design of the place is good, but with the ridiculous food price compared to quality of the food. I DO NOT recommend going into this restaurant! EVER!

If you are craving for sushi, you are better off getting it from nude sushi.

To the Manager/Owner of Joshu-Ya Brasserie:

I've never been to a Japanese restaurant where we were told that "tea" is not available today.  Yes, we are "out" today!   R U kidding me?

Isn't your restaurant a Japanese restaurant as we've been there back in the early 80's when you were Joshu-ya?

Your food is quite delicious and very generous in portions.  We would like to return.

HOWEVER, you need more waitstaff.  We were there for over 1.5 hours for a party of 3. 
We counted only two waitstaff and two sushi chefs on a busy weekday lunch.  

One of our party got the special for the day and was finished while we waited and WAITED for our sushi order.  Upon glancing at  the sushi counter, our order sat for 20 minutes before it was brought to our table.

The party next to us finally received his food when we were ready to leave and he was there when we ordered at the same time. 

We were at the very popular Sanraku in SF a few months ago and we were in and out in 50 minutes.

Their Zoolander roll is the BEST roll! Might be the "cream cheese" that gives it its unique taste. Sashimi here is also pretty good. Aside from that the other rolls at this place is decent, nothing "great" but nothing really bad either. I would recommend this place to anyone who wants some good quality sushi/sashimi in Berkeley.

tiny place with attentive service and best of all, good food. we stopped in for a quick late afternoon bite and tried the pork belly soba and one of the rolls.  they were pretty good sized portions which left us pleasantly full. 

even at 5pm a steady stream of clientele stopped in. next time well try the prix fixe dinner.

i'm pretty sure i walked by this place a half dozen  times in my adventures in berk, and unfortunately i was unable to experience the original version of this sushi joint.

And last night i finally did visit this place. aesthetically it is definitely a step up i think, though the old place did have its charm. I came with a party of 20 and we were seated in the courtyard. The table was a little awkward as an L but they gave us nice heaters to keep us warm.

The service was super prompt and friendly and the sushi was delicious. Well, made, presented and of course tasted great. Price is a little bit much compared to the standard berkeley fare, but I would definitely come back.

note: awkward step between rooms inside

I was visiting my cousin at Berkeley who suggested Joshu-Ya Brasserie for dinner.  I read some of the Yelp reviews and was a little bit on the fence because of the mixed reviews.  To be honest, I expected this place to be one of those "fast food" sushi places that caters to the college crowd.  I was extremely surprised that this place definitely rivaled the sushi restaurants I go to in NY!

The fish quality was excellent and I couldn't believe how cheap it was!!  For example, the chutoro was $10 for two pieces not for just one...this is absolutely unheard of.  We ordered every fish off the specials menu and they all melted in my mouth.  The owner definitely takes pride in bringing in the best quality fish here.

Some of the other dishes we ordered were:
- Wagyu beef special: this was quite interesting since it was cooked as a French dish.  The beef was cooked perfectly with the right about of sear and the lentils that complemented the beef made this dish quite memorable.
- Seared albacore tataki with fried onions: so tasty I wish I could bring this back to NY.
- Sweet shrimp sashimi: came prepared with cucumber and an awesome sesame sauce.  Absolutely loved that they even fried the shrimp head which tastes exactly like a cracker.

Other thoughts:
- Didn't order but would have: Braised rabbit.  We were surprised to see this on the menu at a Japanese restaurant.  It was something we would have ordered but we wanted to focus more on sushi so didn't have room in our bellies.  :(
- Uni/sea urchin: I noticed that this was on the menu but wasn't able to order since there was a back order for two weeks.  The owner Jason came over to explain this to us which I greatly appreciated.  
- Servers were young, attentive, and friendly.  They checked in at the right times making us feel very welcome and well taken care of.  However, I could see that when things get busy it might be difficult to get this kind of TLC but this happens at every restaurant.

We had made a reservation in advance and were happy to be seated in the alcove near the sushi bar which was the best area of the house since it was quiet and more intimate.  If you want a quiet dining experience, try to get seated here.  If you have a large party, try to get seated outside (they have those fancy heaters to make sure you're warm and comfortable throughout your meal).

I had a lovely time at Joshu-ya Brasserie and wish everyone could see how great this restaurant is.  I went there the same night as other diners who wrote that the fish was "too red to be real" or fish was "too cold"; I think some of these comments were off and a bit strange. The food portions are huge and the prices are incredible.  I understand that this place could be a little pricey for students, but for those who want to get top quality fish with quite interesting and innovative specials (like the Wagyu and rabbit), I wholeheartedly recommend this place.  Next time I make my way to Berkeley, I'll be sure to stop by Joshu-ya Brasserie.

At first I was a little hesitant because the restaurant had a slight fishy smell but that all quickly went away with my first order of sushi -- kanpachi.  It was shiny, fresh, buttery and delicious.  Everything I ordered after was fresh and delicious.  My only critique would be that the rolls have too much eel sauce on it.  I would come back in a heart beat.
GREAT service, GREAT food, GREAT dining experience! Price was reasonable, too!
Loved it here, yummy sushi and great service :)

Whoa! I was not exepcting such deliciousness for what I thought was going to be a 'just another lunch'.   Our group of 4 devoured the seared albacore tataki, jalapeño Hamachi Carpaccio, Brasserie Tacos, Pommes Frites, Tempura Mix, Beef entree and Chicken entree. We finished it off with the tempura ice cream and the desert de jour. 

The tataki and the carpaciccio were the perfect appetizers. The seared albacore combined the right textures and flavors: the crunch was provided by shredded fried onions and the tangy sauce rounded off the sweetness and richness of the onions with the buttery albacore.  The hamachi carpaccio had just a bit of spice (it had one piece of paper-thin jalapeño) and the sauce did not overpower the delicate hamachi. 

Don't be fooled by the 'chicken and beef entree'.  They are definitely not as exciting as the other items on their menu, but their meat was perfectly cooked and had delicious veggies that went along with it, so if you have someone who doesn't like sushi or raw fish this won't disapoint. 

The duck fat pommes frites are a must-have appetizer or side dish! They are crunchy on the outside and soft inside.  I didn't even dip them in the sauce because they were so flavorful already.  I've only had duck fat fries in another restaurant in the City and wasn't impressed.  Get these and report back, I'm always in search of delicious french fries :)  

For all you sushi purists out there, they have a wide selection of nigiri and classic rolls and even some intersesting signature roles that they feature.  I didn't have them, but if the food I had for lunch was an indication of the sushi, I'm in! 

They have a full bar, so I'll definitely be back for dinner and go crazy!

Wow... Good sushi, shitty service.. You'd think at 2:30 pm on a Sunday afternoon you wouldn't have to wait a long time for a roll, but despite the fact that there were only a few tables, after waiting over 10 minutes to order (or even get water), one roll took over 20 minutes to come out. Our server was moving slower than a turtle, we had to ask for napkins twice and ask for water refills... Shouldn't they just keep the water filled? Didn't get any plates for the sushi, so had to ask for that too, plus he completely forgot two of our rolls, even though we clearly ordered three rolls...  sushi is good, the service is not... don't go here if you're in any kind of hurry or you're super hungry

I know Japanese food, and this is not it. 
Just because you throw white linen on top of wobbly, old tables with obviously 2nd hand looking chairs, doesn't mean that you can start charging 1.5x the price of neighboring Japanese restaurants. This place is pretends to be 'relatively upscale' and it is kind of, considering the nearby sushi ko, but this place still is sub par quality. You can tell the interior was hastily thrown together. I don't mind dinky interior as long as the owners recognize it as a sort of 'hole in the place' and make up for it with food quality. I think the only reason that this place is surviving is because of its location. 
I am forgiving of higher prices if the food is good, but even if they were cheaper, I would never go back to this place. Rice in the rolls was way too sticky/overcooked, sashimi was of cheap quality and tasted like plastic. Cheap quality food, that is not cheap, is just wrong.
I have been debating whether to give this place 1 star or 2 star, but settled on the one star because I know that I will never return to this place. I reserve 2 stars for places I would not return to voluntarily, but will go depending on circumstances, or if they are really cheap/convenient

An interesting fusion of french, spanish, and japanese.  Well - not actually a fusion, but rather distinct items next to each other on the same menu.

I ordered the best sounding plates for myself which included: pork belly tacos, fries fried in pork fat, a couple pieces of nigiri, and a couple sushi rolls.  Each was excellent, but I knew before I ordered that it would be a horrible combination.  Proving my instincts correct, my stomach was aching for the rest of the night from the abundance of fat and the clash of flavors.

When I return, I will stick with one part of the menu.  And probably the nigiri, which was the best I've found so far in Berkeley.  Excellent for the price range. 

Since I love eating outside for some reason, I'll mention that they also have a nice outdoor seating area with heat lamps.

Love the eclectic menu.  Never thought I'd remember this place for their tacos but their pulled pork tacos were tasty.  The sashimi was fresh, seared salmon sashimi if you're squeamish of raw fish.  

Tip: Run to C.R.E.A.M. (ice cream sandwich shop) around the corner for dessert, thank me later.

This is a little gem of sushi goodness sitting on the corner of Telegraph and Dwight. I must say it adds a little class to this gritty part of Berkeley. And for the life of me, I don't know why I never ventured here during my four years at Cal, but I was glad to make a little dinner detour here with the younger brother. 

FOOD
- Paparazzi roll: yellowtail, tuna, salmon, and avocado
- Shiro Maki roll: seared albacore, fried onions, ponzu, cucumber, and avocado 

We both split two rolls, since we were snacking in the Durant Food Court a little earlier in the day. As lovers of sashimi with no fear of raw fish, both of these rolls were pleasing to our stomachs! The fish were fresh, sweet, and firm. I love salmon, so I was happy with the Paparrazi roll (and will admit I partly ordered it cos I was thinking of Lady Gaga). However the Shiro Maki roll really blew me away. It's a light roll, but the fried onions on top really made things stand out. 

SERVICE
The staff was so attentive! Our waitress was chatty, but didn't linger too long and was more than happy to recommend dishes and specials. I disagree with the earlier reviews that they were slow. It was a Friday evening and they were quick to seat us, give us dishes and water, and take our orders. And we even got a plate of edamame on the house! ;) 

ATMOSPHERE
Choose the outdoor patio if it's a nice day out in Berkeley. There's heated lamps in case the night turns chilly, but I always feel a certain charm in dining al fresco. Otherwise, the seating indoors still look inviting with its cushy booths and bay windows. It's the perfect place to catch up with a small group of friends or take a date. 

My main sushi haunt in Berkeley was Manpuku (really more for the prices), but Joshuya is a tad classier and much closer to campus. Definitely coming here again when I'm in town.

3.5 stars (but 4 because sometimes service is very good)

I think this place is pretty overpriced if you are just coming here for sushi rolls, but the lunchtime deals are pretty good! I usually get a bento box because they give you lots of food for the price. The atmosphere is very nice so it's a good place for dates or group dinners. They have a wide selection of sushi rolls, and the presentation of the rolls is very nice and classy, but I still don't think I would pay that much for a roll if I could just go to CU Sushi or something.

Joshu-Ya has stepped up its game and cleaned up the kitsch. The restaurant now sports white walls and red trim, devoid of multicolored party lights and paper lanterns. It's too bad because I liked that fun-loving scene than this seemingly clean and sophisticated look. But now that the focus is off the restaurant walls, it's all on the menu. It is true that prices seem to have gone up, but so has the quality. At least enough so that they now serve omakase here at a $35 minimum. More evidence are the akimono and seared albacore tataki. The pork belly porridge and the pork belly soba both feature what I thought it would come sliced, but a shredded, cold, slowcooked pork. The soba was not served separate from the jalapeno ponzu sauce either, which I rather it was. It does not keep well, so eat it all up. The beef sukiyaki was rich and too salty. The broth reminded me of Better Than Bouillon. I did like the generous amount of veggie, tofu, and beef. The beef itself was incredibly soft and tender. There is only one sukiyaki (beef) and three udons (chicken). For those who still remember the sushi rolls of the past Joshu-Ya, the best are still on the menu (Zoolandar, Lucky Danny). The nigiri is more impressive now, so hit those instead. Check out the specials board above the sushi bar too. Service still terrible. Not only was it slow as ever, but a whole cast iron cauldron of soup almost slid onto us. Please put a napkin underneath it please.

Their lunch specials are a really good deal and you get a lot of food. I have had the "Joshya special", soba combo, and udon combo. The soba and udon was rather medicore but the sushi was delicious. For the soba combo, you get to choose between cold or hot soba; next time I'll definitely try the cold because the hot soba was basically served in a not-so-flavorful broth with some carrots and broccoli. Kinda bland.. but the handrolls that came with it was really delicious. I've only been to a few sushi places in Berkeley, but so far Joshu-ya is probably my favorite :)

Even after the name change and the interior redesign, still the only place in Berkeley to get a decent cut of fish, albeit even more pricey now.

I would say their strong fish is the albacore and salmon, and the weaker one is tuna and white tuna.  Their cooked foods are decent, but any sort of teriyaki or grilled food should never be a concern at well established Japanese restaurants.  I've never cared much for rolls, so I usually settle with nigiri or the chirashi.  From what I've tasted and seen, the rolls probably give you a better bang for your buck that does sashimi, nigiri.

The service is mediocre; they usually hire students to work here, so tip generously!  If you have access to a car, I would recommend:  Coach Sushi in Oakland, Geta Sushi in Oakland, or Sushi House in Alameda all three of which have better value and higher quality.

as a native of manhattan, i've been spoiled by some of the best sushi restaurants in the country.  and up until i found joshuya brasserie there has been a mega void in the eastbay/sf sushi scene.  

i ate at joshuya last week and was extremely IMPRESSED by the food.  sushi was some of the freshest i've had and was tastefully and artistically presented.  i also had a chance to meet the new chef/owner who came and conversed with us during dinner.  very energetic, friendly and down-to-earth. 

if you are looking for a special and different kind of sushi experience, you do not want to miss joshuya.  the omakase at $35 is a must -- seriously, the best deal i've had all year (similar omakases i've had have ranged from 75 to 125).  i can't imagine they make much of any profit on this....  also try the salmon salad and the pork belly soba.  you'll be in for a serious treat!!

joshuya will definitely be a must-visit every time i pass through the bay area.

I'd been searching - for years - to find a sushi spot that could claim the title of "My Favorite," and as I write this review I can finally, happily close the case. Joshu-Ya Brasserie is so It. 

What stands out most about Joshu-Ya is the way they've balanced the traditional art of sushi with an avant garde, urban spin on things. I was lucky enough to meet chef/ owner Jason Kwon, who described his inspiration for each dish in a refreshingly bold New York fashion (he's a NY native, which has no doubt heightened his culinary creativity). As we cooed over his newly-added 'Brasserie Tacos', he admitted he was up all night perfecting the recipe, until finally settling on the pork belly, avocado, radish, jalepeno and cilantro pesto combo. One man's lost sleep is another's gastronomic gain. Lucky us.

We were blessed with an onslaught of wow-factor treats, from the orgasmically creamy Uni hand rolls, to the buttery-smokey torched salmon sashimi with truffle cream, and tender tuna belly with blue cheese and toasted garlic. Definitely not your grandma's sushi restaurant - Joshu-Ya is shaking things up, and our jaws were consistently dropping...between bites. 

We were ready to slip into a blissful food coma when the prospect of dessert came up: Yuzu Cheescake and Black Sesame Creme Brulee were the specials du jour, and being the polite gluttons that we are, we gracefully obliged and had one of each. The Yuzu Cheesecake was a revelation - ultra dense, with a carmelized crust, and the perfect infusion of citrus. The greenish-hued Black Sesame Creme Brulee was another marvel that we filed away in our "never been done before" book: silky, nutty, and exotically decadent.

The whole evening was an adventurous diner's dream. The crowd is your typical sampling of Berkeley's diverse demographic: students, professors, double-dates, birthday parties, young and rowdy, elderly and subdued...whatever you are, you'll fit in just fine. Especially if 'foodie' is your main distinction. 

There's a cozy outdoor patio area, private dining room for Chef's Tasting diners, sushi bar, and a large dining room for the inevitable overflow. Reservations seem like a good idea, and the Chef's Tasting is the perfect way to get acquainted if you're a first timer. 

Overheard: "Why do they call it a Brasserie? Isn't that like...Spanish?" I must admit, I was wondering the same thing, minus the linguistic error, and gathered that the casual vibe of Joshu-Ya, plus the fun, creative, seasonal menu make it more a Brasserie than an Izakaya. Plus, they've got the friendliest sushi chefs you'll ever meet. None of that stone-cold samurai treatment. 

Next time I need to impress some jaded food-snob friend (or myself), I'm heading straight to Joshu-Ya for their latest and greatest edible inventions. You should too.

I've been going to Joshu-Ya for years (long before they became a brasserie). I always order their cinderella roll, which is a vegetable tempura roll topped with avocado slices and wakame. This is the perfect lunch dish and I crave it all the time. I also love getting edamame and/or sweet potato tempura fries. This place has gotten so much classier over the years. The latest incarnation of Joshu-Ya really is exceptional. Their menu has improved greatly. The decor and also the plating of their dishes are both elegant.  Lately I've been venturing out and going there for breakfast, which is also a treat. My favorite thing about Joshu-Ya is their consistency. I've never been let down by one of my meals there. I hope they stay in Berkeley for many years!

Hands-down best quality sushi in Berkeley (hey, it's actually worth the money you'll be spending!). Innovative and unique non-sushi items as well, along with good and courteous service and generous portions.

Standout Items: (1) kimchi kobe beef sliders (house-made spicy sweet kimchi that contrasts with the rich fattiness of the kobe beef, further set against a tangy cream sauce AND home-made soft brioche rolls. These small sliders pack so much flavor in each bite they could be stand-alone entrees. (2) Chirashi: EXCELLENT and thick cuts of fish. No stringiness, no excessive fattiness, no half-assed cuts of fish (which is a HUGE problem with most sushi places). They do not skimp on the quality of the fish. (3) Pork belly soba: unusual and absolutely delicious combination of crispy pork belly and cold soba noodles in a salty and slightly sour broth. The cold soup and spicy-bitter bite of radish chunks balances the inherent fat of the pork belly, while the soba noodles give the dish body and fill. (4) Sashimi salad: Fresh fish and delicious greens blanketed with a tangy vinaigrette. Surprisingly delicious and filing for such a simple salad.

I've tried at least 5 other sushi restaurants in Berkeley (multiple times too!). Joshuya's is a tad bit more expensive and bourgeois than average, but definitely worth it. GO GO GO!

Favorite sushi place in Berkeley hands down!  Fresh sashimi. Creative fusion dishes like the kobe-kimchee sliders and sweet potato tempura fries. Haven't been able to try all the rolls yet, but the Lion King is my fav so far.

Lunch deals may be a little pricier than places two blocks from campus, but the quality of food at Joshyu-Ya's is worth it. Even the California roll tasted authentic, not like those cheap versions you find at Costco or Tako Sushi (sorry Tako, I still love your Dragon Roll). My friend and I shared the pork belly tacos and the five item bento, which includes two gyoza, tempura, four California rolls, a small salad, and teriyaki chicken over rice. The pork belly tacos were so well-done. Every bite was soft and full of flavor (meaty goodness!). The mini tacos were embellished with jalopenos, roasted red peppers, and leafy greens, all combined with the pork belly and all on top of a small tortilla. Though $8 for 3 mini tacos was a little expensive, I definitely thought it was worth every bite.

The five item bento had some good pieces as well, such as the fried gyoza and the delicious California rolls. Honestly, I have never had a better California roll. It must have been the toasted seaweed that made it taste amazing.

I did dock off a star because the last time I came here, my friend and I ordered the beef sukiyaki and agreed it was a bit bland and watery. The beef was all right, but the overall dish was just not remarkable.

Overall, you can find quality meals here, so I suggest taking your family or significant other here for some hearty, good food.

Decided to finally review this place after coming here close to 10 times already ...

[General]
- Have eaten better sushi and had better service
- I still come back because there is nothing better around in Berkeley!! :( .. and it's closet to my apartment...
- pretty pricey for rolls ~$10+ ~ $14

[ATMOSPHERE]
- Recently remodeled on the outside and looks pretty nice (indoor and outdoor eating area), but apparently they only give you the small bowl of miso soup and cheapened out by removing small salad that used to be offered as well

[FOOD]
What I've ordered ... 
- Lion King:  Default order.  Baked with salmon and this delicious sauce on top.  However, my experience with this was totally ruined when I was served a barely lukewarm roll ... The part I loved about this was the warm fresh baked feeling from biting into a piece.. Did I forget to mention this was at around mid-afternoon when there were barely two other tables seated for 1 waiter?  

- Orchid:  Another baked roll, really good, but prettyyy pricey for a college student ... about 14 bucks for this

- Spicy Tuna:  A nice spice in this roll, but I've had fresher tuna ...


- Fried Green Tea Ice Cream:  Pretty decent ice cream... the batter around the ice cream has a subtle lemon zest to it... it's topped with some whipped cream and chocolate

- Bento lunches:  My parents always order these, they given a pretty generous amount for a reasonable price

[SERVICE]
- not very good at all ...
- the only time they can be found is seating you, and delivering your food late
- never really met a friendly/welcoming waiter/waitress in all my times here -- except when my friend worked here, but that's biased.

[OVERALL]
- decent sushi, but overpriced.
- I still come back because nothing else better or closer

They just remodeled the whole restaurant, so it looks modern and very stylish now!

Food wise it's an absolute heaven! We just asked the chef to make us whatever he wants and all the food that was coming to our table was absolutely amazing.

The restaurant is pretty large, but it still feels very cozy and comfortable. They have a very nice looking outdoor section with heaters, I can't wait to go back there during summer and seat outside!

I have a bit of a trouble rating this place because if I compare this sushi restaurant to my experiences in SF, it definitely doesn't compare at all. 
But if I compare this place to other sushi places in Berkeley, it definitely has a bit more class and concentrates less on creating fast, convenient and "to-go" service.

I came here with a friend and it looked really cute on the outside! We ordered 2 rolls, and tried this fish type of appetizer. It was decent, but the tuna on our rolls looked way too red for it to be normal, causing us to believe that maybe they're injecting red dye into the fish!?!? It was too bright red for it to be normal ... 

It's a nice atmosphere and the servers are probably all college students so you can't really expect them compliment your meal because they dont' know much about the menu or the type of fish they're serving. They're really just there to take your order, heh. 

overall, it was decent.

I came here for the second time a month ago for a family dinner. (The first time was when I was a freshman at Cal, too many years ago.) I didn'tremember much about the restaurant from my first visit, but I thought that was a good sign (if it were really bad, I would probably remember even after all these years.)  
Sushi/Japanese tends to be our go-to cuisine when my family goes out to eat, which is why my brother made a reservation here. We were seated promptly at our reservation time and ordered 4 dishes: paparazzi roll, tempura soba, sushi combination, and beef sukiyaki. 
I remember our food being brought out promptly and I was pleasantly surprised by the overall quality. I thought the presentation was "clean" (I love the look of colorful food on large white plates). The fish on the sushi combo and the paparazzi roll tasted fresh, and I found the fatty salmon to be a nice touch. I also enjoyed the tempura that came with the soba--very crunchy and not oily-tasting. I was not a huge fan of the sukiyaki though. I generally love everything sweet, but the broth was a bit too sweet, almost syrupy, for my taste. 
Service was friendly and accommodating without being too disturbing. I could see it being a hit or miss here though. Maybe it's because we were seated in a corner, but sometimes it took a while to get our server's attention. Not an issue when we were there, family reunions are becoming more and more far in between, and I don't think any of us were in a huge rush or anything. 

Note: I think this place has become more "fusion" since the last time I visited. There are more non-sushi items on the menu (they have some kobe beef entree and no udon? a little strange for what I thought was a sushi restaurant, but I guess they're going for something different now.) Also, this is the first sushi establishment where I have been served by a non-Asian person. Not making any judgment calls on that, just an observation :)
Pretty good stuff.  Get the seared salmon nigiri thing for sure!

You have to be kidding me.

First, if I found out that every one of the wait staff had never worked in a restaurant before, or that this was all their first job ever, I wouldn't be at all surprised. They have no idea how to deal with customers and present themselves. they had loud discussions about shifts and tables right in front of us, took our order without asking for any further directions and generally behaved in a clumsy and awkward fashion. 

We ordered the omakase and everything they brought us was covered with sauces- like soaking. I have never seen anything like this before. The last thing they gave us was some nigiri which wasn't too bad, but wasn't fantastic either..

I thought this place was going to be great. In reality, it was a mess.

the food here is gooooood.
I came with two friends and we ended up getting the lion king, spider roll, and beef sukiyaki. The lion king was a bit heavy for me, but I loved the spider roll and beef sukiyaki. The sukiyaki came with so much food. There were tons of beef, tofu, carrots, cabbage, rice noodles and onions, and the broth had a hint of sweetness. 

Since we were sitting at the bar (there were no tables available) we got to watch the chef make the rolls and they moved at lighting speed! I was actually pretty disappointed when they said they only had seats at the bar open but it turned out to be pretty entertaining. While there, we saw the chefs make this gorgeous roll garnished with kelp on the top and eventually found out it was called the Cinderella. it looked so good, and I'm definitely getting that when I come back.

As for service, we ordered really fast and the food came really fast. but we were done for a good 15 - 20 minutes until our check came. 

All in all, it was a good experience and I'll be back!

Thank God it's still here! The new patio is nice. The sushi is even better. The fish was fresh, and there was more of it. The rest of the menu is a bit confused...but who cares! Lucky Danny is a must.

The Joshu-Ya of past is much different then the 'Joshu-Ya now with a Brasserie' of present. Years ago this was the spot for college students to get cheap sushi, but once sushi house opened I imagine most the kids go to asian ghetto for the cheaper sushi fix. I just so happened to take a date here a couple months ago and as it turns out the decision was brilliant *pats own back*.

The menu has been completely revamped and there is a modern flair to the traditional fair you get at sushi bars or restaurants. The food is refreshing and innovative. 

Items ordered:
Kobe Kimchee Sliders (caramelized kimchee-bacon, ny cheddar, homemade brioche, 3 pcs)- These were divine. So juicy and incredibly flavorful. I never had caramelized kimchee and I must say completely brilliant. Highly recommended.

Spicy Crunch roll- Was good for a roll. In retrospect I would stick to the entrees as they sound way more interesting. Rolls can only be so good.

Beef Sukiyaki (angus beef, mushrooms, tofu, vegetables, sweet potato noodles, fish cakes, sweet dashi, rice)- All the ingredients above were swimming in a flavorful broth. Very enjoyable.

I plan to make a return visit to try all the other dishes I missed out on. The sharing tapas stand out to me. The Ambiance is serene and romantic especially at night when there is outdoor seating and lights strung up. Service is accommodating and attentive.

I don't know what's with the change of names to Joshu-Ya Brasserie, but I can't detect much of a change - which is good news, since I love their rolls! If I had to point out a down side though, is that non-susi/roll dishes weren't that good. But if I was craving rolls, I'd definitely go to Joshu-Ya. It's just unfortunate it's in a location that I feel unsafe going to in the afternoon without a car.

This is by far one of my favorite Japanese restaurants in Berkeley. The only reason they didn't get a full 5 is because I honestly miss Joshu-ya's before the added Brasserie. They used to have a ginormous specialty sushi roll list and now it's down to like 10....very disappointing. I also feel like it's not AS good as before but it's still good. I still go here whenever I'm in the area.

My go-to sushi place when we're not sure what to eat for dinner. The menu changed a bit (I guess so did the name) but some of the favorites (Agadashi tofu) are off the menu. I think if you ask, they'll still make it. The place is leaning toward more Japanese hot foods than sushi/sashimi basics. But their sushi is seriously amazing, great portions and really fresh ingredients. Also the sashimi plate is great! A bit pricey to eat on a regular basis, but still love this place!

I was really disappointed in this place. The food was overpriced, the place was cramped, and the service was slow. How does it take 20 minutes to pick up a roll of sushi from the counter..The sushi kind of just tasted like any other sushi place to be honest. I much rather go wait in line at Kirala than come here again.
