Some gal pals and I were walking around Berkeley and randomly stopped into this place for happy hour. The menu prices and selections were great, but the service was meh.We ordered every roll and appetizer on the happy hour menu as well as several of the drinks.The food was yummy and the drinks were strong, which made this a successful happy hour!

One of the best sushi in town. I have been here a few times for friends birthdays and dinner get together. 

I have ordered a few of their rolls and they have been really good. The place is really well decorate. I recommend this place for any situation whether it is just a casual lunch, dinner with friends, or for date. It is a really lovely place. The place is quite small, so you may run into problem getting seats. It has never been a problem for me, but it does gets full.

The service is great. The staffs give you a lot of attention. Their rolls are really good. If you enjoy non traditional japanese food, you will love this place.

Just had lunch here and the server was awful. As someone that has worked as a server for a few years I understand that it is hard work, but this was ridiculous. All of the neighboring tables were also having some issues such as 
- drinks not being served after multiple requests
- he spilled soy sauce on a woman's purse (a COACH purse at that!) He then proceeded to scrub the hell out of the material with a wet wash cloth from the kitchen
- he forgot to bring us plates for sushi
- we asked multiple times for water, additional napkins
- we were never checked on
- he forgot half of our order and when we asked about it he said he didn't write it down and are we sure that we ordered those items. WTF

I'm usually pretty forgiving for service issues, but the server moved in such a lackadaisical manner that I'm also appalled that the manager has not addressed these issues and he is allowed to even carry himself in such a sleepy/uncaring manner when at work. 

The food despite the service was good, but this was normally my go to sushi place... I don't feel like I would return after this experience.

I was completely impressed by the new and improved Joshu-Ya. 

The lunch bento box is a great deal for about eight bucks. The lunch special is also a great deal. Its a great place to take out of towners for a nice lunch or dinner. The best Japanese restaurant on southside and its not even close.

After possibly changing owners, my coworker was recommended to try Joshu-ya Brasserie.  Since it was a nice day, we decided to take the walk up here on Tuesday.

Located blocks from UCB's campus and right off Telegraph lies Joshu-Ya.  Though it won't break your wallet, Joshu-ya is a bit pricier than most restaurants in the area.  There's indoor seating as well as outdoor seating which has a tiny waterfall setup.

FOOD:
First off, I would like to state that their presentation is lovely.  My fries and chicken were served in small baskets, the type you would deep fry something in.  My soba was well presented.

*Pommes Frites ($4) - Delicious! Thin cut fries are fried in duck fat which gave it a little extra flavoring.  The fries were extremely crispy and served with an aioli sauce that had a small kick to it.

*Chicken Karaage ($6.50) - Good and tender!  The chicken had a nice panko exterior while the chicken itself remained moist.  Definitely make use of the accompanied aioli and A1 like sauce.

*Jalapeno Pork Belly Soba ($9) - Although the noodles were good, the pork belly was a letdown.  I decided to order the pork belly soba because a lot of Yelpers recommended it.  The buckwheat noodles were delicious and had a nice sweetness from the ponzu sauce.  Unfortunately, the pork belly lost its appeal when it was served shredded.  It lost the tenderness I'm use to and tasted more like stringy pulled pork.

My coworker ordered the sashimi and thought it was delicious, fresh, and flavorful.

SERVICE:
Our waiter was nice, pleasant, and made sure everything was to our liking.

There was so many things on the menu we wanted to try so no doubt, we'll be back!

The food was decent. I got the Marilyn Monroe and my boyfriend got the Lion King. We also had an order of the pommes frites which were fries fried in duck fat. It sounds pretty gross but honestly they were really good!
The Marilyn Monroe had an array of raw fish but it was too spicy for me. I felt like they overstuffed the sushi with spicy tuna.
It was also kind of crowded. The tables were so close together that there was barely any elbow space and you can hear everyone's conversations next to you.
The best part of the night was the fact that the waitress forgot to put in my boyfriend's lion king and she gave us edamame and green tea ice cream on the house!! 
The lion king was good just pretty typical lion king, can't really go wrong with it :)
oh and they give free miso soup!! which is a bonus because miso soup is the best!!

Oh wow. We stumbled across this place after doing a sake tasting and wanted some Japanese food. We were pleasantly surprised by the outside as it looked cute and welcoming. We had gone expecting to get some rolls but decided to order from the seasonal menu due to the waitresses suggestion. 

I decided on getting the:

BLACK MUSSELS CON CHORIZO - LOVED IT. I wish i had asked for my bread to dip into the sauce. 

POMMES  FRITES- Fried in duck fat. Kinda gross to think about.. but SO WORTH IT. I loved the flavor.

My boyfriend was boring and ordered some of the Nigiri. He had some fatty tuna belly and something else. He said it was good, but it didn't stand out like the plates that I ordered. 

I def recommend coming here and ordering off of their seasonal menu!

I'm downgrading this restaurant from 4 to 3 stars.  I went back for the first time in a few months and found that its patio had been nicely redone.  However, the price of that remodel was well reflected in the 30-40% hike in the lunch menu prices.   I also noticed that the lunch specials no longer include a salad and that the sushi portions are smaller than they used to be.  The service is still extremely slow and the waitress ran somebody else's total on my credit card (instead of crediting the amount back and reprocessing the transaction, she left it and gave me change on the difference).  Anyway, I don't know if the place is under the same management, but it's not as good and it's likely that I will not be back any time soon.

Joshuya's is my FAVORITE sushi place in Berkeley! Yes, it is a bit pricier than the average college student meal, but if you ask me, it's totally worth it. Their fish is really fresh and I like the ambience (especially their outdoor seating). My favorites here are the spicy Audrey Hepburn, dragon roll, and the deep fried roll with crab (I forget what it's called). I even like their Marilyn Monroe, though I usually dislike tuna in my sushi. Their tempura green tea icecream is amazing!

However, their service sucks. It takes forever to order and receive your food, so don't go here when you're starving. Also, it gets really crowded here most of the time, so don't forget to reserve a table, especially if you're going here for dinner.

This was the first place I've been to when I got into Berkeley. Compared to C U Sushi and Tako Sushi, this is EXPENSIVE to a college student. It's a cute little house with patio seating. They do offer more variety in sushi and rolls and not bad quality either, just your typical traditional Japanese restaurant menu. This was before they revamp the place, changed the menu.

Four years later, I came back here again. I had this feeling of this place has turned into Japanese fusion. Not a bad thing, just that I don't truly enjoy the fusion in sushi rolls. I always felt like it's a way to cover up the lack of quality in sashimi grade fish. So I didn't really try their rolls at all.

Anyway, I really enjoy their jalapeno pork belly soba. I'm not a big fan of soba just because of this weird aftertaste from the noodles, but I'm a big fan of pork belly. There's so much flavor in pork belly, and luckily that covered the weird soba taste I disliked. The noodles are not drenched in sauce, so it's not overly soggy or anything. It's kinda hard to make soba soggy anyway. It's a simple, lightly flavored dish, very filling. 

I think I liked this place after it has changed its menu. The fusion does work after all! Well, just on the entrees side. I'll decide if I want to give into the rolls. 

Lastly, if you're a beer drinker, do get this one beer called Echigo Red Ale. I haven't seen it in stores like at Bevmo or other places. This beer is so light and aromatic, it's a must try!

I had high hopes for this placed as I walked in to see the most perfect patio. The menu also looked pretty interesting from seeing it on Yelp. Whenever the place looks nice, I ask please please please, let the food be good too! 

Unfortunately that wasn't the case.

First, they were waaay understaffed. They had one waitress for the whole patio, and I could see other people getting frustrated too. It really wasn't her fault, but I was pissed when we waited 20 minutes for our food and she tells us they ran out of the Kobe Beef Sliders my boyfriend ordered  as she put down my Chirashi. Really? You couldn't say this BEFORE I got my food? It is my personal peeve when food comes out at vastly different times, but now I had my food and my BF had to wait a whole 'nother round of ordering until he got his pork tacos. More on that later.

So now I'm sitting there with my Chirashi, which I can't really leave sitting since we are sitting outside on a hot day. As I awkwardly start eating by myself, I bite into the salmon - and it's FROZEN. WTF? Jesus christ, never have I had frozen sushi even at the worst of sushi joints I've been too. The texture was like eating a Sashimi slushy. 

Another 20 minutes pass, and everyone around us who came in later than us is finished with their food and they are waiting for their checks, while my boyfriend's tacos still hasn't come. We are trying to get somewhere on time so we tell the waitress to forget about it. Oh, did I mention our water glasses never got filled once on this hot summer day, until we asked her for the check? She stammers to say she will check on the tacos, and they come in the nick of time. My boyfriend has a bite...and they are too fatty to be any good. We just leave them there, $10 wasted.

I still feel like I could give this place another chance...Many people seem to love this place. I think everything that could have gone wrong for them went wrong this day. Their nigiri looks pretty decent from pictures so I will have to try that sometime.

I am giving this a 1-star review, not because I don't like the food at Joshu-ya's, but because I've been a dedicated weekly or at least monthly visitor for the PAST 6 YEARS!!!!! I am very upset with a lot of the recent changes in menu and of course PRICES! I used to love knowing about an inexpensive hidden sushi gem that gave lots of freebies to students and customers...free miso, free salad, free tea, and all I had to order was my awesome roll, maybe an appetizer or dessert to make the perfect reasonably priced meal!

Now I don't know what to say, they are trying to cater to a whole different crowd, taken away the perks, and really lost one loyal customer. I hope they read this, struggle with this new concept menu, and go back to the old Joshuya's!!! All they EVER needed to do was improve the at times painfully slow service, and clean up a bit! Not a fan of the complete overhaul. :(

Sushi restaurants are always about the quality and the preparation of the fish. With that being said this place deserves 5 stars for that alone. 

The quality of the fish exceeds the price you pay for, a great deal.

The service is always great, every time I come here the waiters are super nice and helpful. 

Anyone in Berkeley area wanting great sushi should definitely check this place out.

DINNER DATE: 1.2. 2012 @ 6:30 PM

I rang in the  New Year not with Jingle Bells but with a JINGLE BELLY. 

Yikes!  Time to detox from those rich holiday turkeys, tamales, cookies and pies. 

Sushi was the perfect choice to start a healthy New Me (and Mr. P). Sushi is raw, unprocessed, full of protein and good fat. Minus the rice, it is the perfect food. 

And thanks to Joshu-Ya, our first sushi meal of 2012 was very satisfying. The sushi was of good quality, super-fresh and very pleasing to the palate.

DECOR/AMBIANCE:
Joshu-Ya is cute. There is fenced-in,  front attractive patio with heat lamps for al fresco dining. The string of holiday lights added magic to the place. The sushi bar area is more conducive to fun dining since it looked out into the front yard. 

The other dining room was too cramped with low ceilings.  I would ask to dine at the sushi bar area next time. 

SERVICE:
There was only one server but she was efficient. The food came  well-spaced out. The sushi chefs were friendly and welcoming.

SUSHI DINNER:
We had quite a feast and had the following:

MANGO SAKETINI $5: It was refreshing and could have been made with real fruit juice but it was not well-chilled and not strong.   http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sxIPX4ZAipVl3ZCkkqXqZw?select=zGVjKRiNnPaqsxtYPhg1YA

GYOZA $4: Not necessarily healthy but Mr. P loves this little fried dumplings. I almost always ignore these at other restaurants because a lot of times they are greasy and sometimes rubbery. Not these little morsels of joy--hot, deep-fried but not a trace of grease. Very good! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sxIPX4ZAipVl3ZCkkqXqZw?select=MPjo7r2jPsWzZ7iZA9IQOw

ANKIMO (MONK FISH LIVER) $9: 3 round disks of yummy firm monkfish liver  with roe on top without the slightest hint of unpleasant fishy taste. Very good! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sxIPX4ZAipVl3ZCkkqXqZw?select=X4ytShKfW2YPG6yR3CNkFw

SASHIMI APPETIZER $13: One of the freshest sashimi I have had in a while. 2 hefty slices each of tuna, fatty tuna and salmon. Pure joy!!! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sxIPX4ZAipVl3ZCkkqXqZw?select=hwXJSGK6SGNcULo72z42bQ

CHIRASHI $16.50: Just like the sashimi appetizer, this bowl of delight provided super-fresh and firm fish slices of salmon, scallops, tuna, seaweed, etc over rice. I have learned during my sushi eating life that the true test of the freshness of the fish at a sushi restaurant is the mackerel. The mackerel at Joshu-Ya passed the freshness taste test with flying colors. And speaking of colors, the colors of the fish were healthy and rich--and indication of the freshness of the fish. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sxIPX4ZAipVl3ZCkkqXqZw?select=6-1czLeP_ggOEIUvGAEaBA

AMSTERDAM ROLL & HAWAII ROLL: I am a sushi purist and do not care much for rolls. My man ordered these and enjoyed them. They were huge rolls and according to him were also fresh and good. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/sxIPX4ZAipVl3ZCkkqXqZw?select=TdqWD28bnonb_nZYunutKA

CHECK: $93 including tip, soda and Mango Saketini 

VERDICT:
Joshu-Ya was a nice treat and a delightful surprise in Berkeley.  The consistent theme of their sushi was "super-fresh, generous and delicious." The presentations of the food were colorful and very pleasing to the eyes.

However, as good and super-fresh Joshu-Ya's sushi was, they were not "melt in your mouth."  The best sushi I have had in the past were full of flavors and of excellent quality  fish that I had to close my eyes as they were "melting" in my mouth. I did not experience this at Joshu-Ya. 

Joshu-Ya's sushi is still a cut above the rest and worthy of 4.5 Stars.

Thank you, Joshu-Ya, for providing us with a very delighful first date night of 2012. Hopefully our dinners for the rest of the year are as delicious as what you have provided us!

One of my favorite restaurants in Berkeley. I've been going to Joshu-ya for years now... I used to go a LOT back when I was in college with my best friends (like a LOT, twice a week at least! & then for countless friend's birthdays & other occasions - anytime we met up it was at Joshu-ya haha), especially because we lived right down the street, literally. My housemate worked there for a long time & we knew the owners (very kind & wonderful people) , so i have a lot of fond memories of home there & it has a really special place in my heart :)

I always used to get the Lucky Danny roll (salmon, spicy crab, tempura, avocado) or the Cinderella roll (really yummy veggie roll with wakame on top). Also, my big sister treated me to the green tea tempura ice cream for my first time on my bday one year (2007 I think?) and it has been one of my favorite desserts ever since (although I miss the lemon cake batter they used to use, it was my favorite - now it's a more traditional pound cake batter but it's still yummy :)

Since that time, it has changed a lot but everything I loved about it is still pretty much the same, and they've added a lot of new items to their menu - my friend & I tried the pork belly tacos appetizer a few days ago & loved them (soo tasty!), although they were a little bit too oily. I would go back just to get them again. For my entree I ordered the salmon porridge, which I actually really loved - the porridge was really yummy & comforting (although a bit sweet for my taste), & the salmon was delicious, perfectly cooked & flavorful. I just wished it had come with more veggies (came with a few pieces of broccoli). 

I really want to get the pommes frites next time, ooh & also I want to try the chirashi, I heard it's really good!

Oh Joshu-ya, I love you :) so reliably delicious & satisfying always!

Very good and mostly traditional nigiri, sashimi, and maki rolls. Everything tasted delicious. There is an outside patio which on warm nights must be fantastic. The inside is very small and the bathroom is ridiculously small to the point you can hardly fit into the door to use it (only negative thing about the place). 

Our server was friendly and didn't mind that we stayed for hours. We left very very happy.

Some like it raw..
fresh, 

and pink.  

I know I've certainly found all of the above here.

Starting with a mouth watering mango saketini to help quench my dry palette. The shashimi salad was completely tantalizing, just the right amount of creamy miso dressing and mixture of fragrant greens. The yellow-tail in my Paparazzi roll was very buttery, yet offered a nice bite to it.

Cute, intimate, and heated outdoor patio seating.. and  very attentive service.  I can't wait to come back for fresh, but sloppy seconds.

The gyoza was absolutely amazing. Super fresh, hot, and flavorful. The mixed tempura was average. Came with 2 shrimps tempuras and a bunch of mixed vegetables. 

The chicken udon here is extremely good. The chicken is well marinated and you can actually taste the meat without any additional sauces. The udon noodles are quite chewy, but not too tough. 

The spider roll was slightly disappointing cause it had like cucumbers and carrots inside, which made it taste kind of odd. The soft shell crab was okay though.

Tips:

My favorites: Amsterdam Roll and Super Crunch Roll

--------------------------------------------

So I've been to Joshu-Ya's before the change and now after the change. Joshu-Ya did keep a lot of their classic rolls on the menu so I'm glad for that. The new addition to Joshu-Ya is their seasonal section of the menu that takes into consideration all the seasonally fresh foods and incorporates them into the dishes. I was talking to the waitress and she said the chef actually went to school in Europe and brought a lot of the cooking styles he learned overseas to Joshu-Ya. I was pretty impressed with the menu selection, Joshu-Ya definitely seems a lot fancier now.

Black Mussels in Chorizo: Two different staff members raved about this appetizer dish so we decided to give it a try and it turned out pretty good! It's $15, but they do give you a good portion of mussels (although some lack the meat inside). The sauce in the dish definitely makes the whole dish come together. They give you fresh oven-cooked artisan bread that tastes GREAT with the sauce. I would recommend this appetizers to seafood lovers.

Amsterdam Roll: (Soft Shell Crap with crab meat topped with avocado) I think out of the 3 rolls that I ordered that this is my favorite one. I just love soft-shell crab so that makes this roll delicious.

Super Crunch Roll: This roll is deep-fried and it tastes great.

Lion King: Baked salmon roll which tasted pretty standard.

Overall the sushi tasted great and I highly recommend coming to Joshu-Ya for a special date because the atmosphere is quite romantic.
This place is amazing. Won, the sushi chef,  is the coolest. This is the place to come if you are in Berkeley.

The HECK man? When did this place get the "Brasserie" part added to it's name? Well apparently this is the same spot as the this: http://www.yelp.com/biz/joshu-ya-sushi-berkeley-2

That being said, my sentiments for it are the same as before, so thusly, here is my review from before (circa 2007):

Some of the best sushi to be had in the bay, HANDS DOWN. Sure, it's not much on ambiance, but let's forget about that for the moment. Order something, anything, off of the menu. They have sushi galore! Each piece is just so savory (and fresh I might add)! One thing I do enjoy about this place (besides the super friendly service, no complaints there) is that the sushi usually comes in nice jumbo-sized portions. I love it! It's rare one dish of sushi can get me full, and it's here at Joshuya where such a thing occurs. 

And talk about affordability. Whether you're noble or a savage or a noble savage or a savage noble or a nobel prize winner, the prices here will fit anyone's budget. Sure, fancy fufu sushi places are great and everything, but when money's tight and you want a great night out eating with your friends, this place can't be topped. Although yes, time may be of an issue to some, I can definitely say it's totally worth it. It's great food and when you bring some friends along, it is MOST DEFINITELY good fun.

After being on a quest for a good sushi spot to satisfy my cravings, I was happy to discover Joshu-Ya. This small yet welcoming little sushi restaurant was quite nice. The servers were all very friendly, quick, and knowledgeable with their menu items which was great. 

My friends and I ordered a bunch of stuff to share and everything was delicious, however I thought it could have been more flavorful compared to every sushi place I have visited in Seattle where I previously lived. I miss that amount of flavor in each bite and am still on a quest to find it. I did like this place and plan to return though! The ingredients were fresh, the pieces were prepared quite quickly, and they have a great amount of variety on their menu at decent prices. The music selection was a bit off for the atmosphere (it was some bangin' hard house) but for a tiny, quaint, little spot like this, we couldn't help but laugh at the awkward music selection. 

I did notice that they have a pretty rad happy hour that I'm excited to check out next time and suggest you do as well. From 2-6pm, M-F, they have some great drink and tempura fries specials. All of their dishes are decorated very nicely and I can't wait until I return on a nice day/evening so I can hopefully get a seat on their nice outside seating area. I love the look of this place!

If you like a good roll, I would suggest trying out the Zoolander, Lion King, Cinderella, and Joshu-ya!

haven't been to Joshu-ya since they went Brasserie. after today, some minor regrets..

the interior looks the same albeit spfiffed up. service definitely much better.
they even have lunch specials!

eats: New York Brasserie Burger(9) with miso soup, mixed salad greens.
-miso soup
very nice, no msg tasted. yummy
-mixed green salad
mixed greens, broculli crowns, sliced red cabbage, carrot schreds with french-like dressing.  likewise yummy
-burger, med. rare requested
looked medium, seared on outside, tender on inside, no meat taste, non greasy
angus sirloin, ny cheddar, mayo, carmelized onion, tomato,
-mildly disappointed, but's as good as or better than any other burger elsewhere

sashimi (7 pieces, $15)
-3 lengthy aji slices, horse makeral-japan: didn't taste oily like typical spanish mackeral, more like albabore?
-3 small sake
-3 long wavy tuna.
-many veggie sidebites
-worth it! pretty fresh.

temaki
-excellent service
-not fusion, but co-partnering cuisines.
-definitely can't wait to try more lunch spcecials, changes monthly?

Ten years ago Joshu-ya was a dirty, divey sushi place famous for sake bombs.

That sushi joint is gone, replaced by a restaurant so classy and elegant I can't believe it's on Telegraph.

The service was great -- fresh-faced, friendly, attentive, and eager. A sake-based cocktail list with a rotating chef's selection. Tapas and French fare to complement the Japanese food. 

To top it off -it was an unbelievable value. Four cocktails and two full dinners for two with dessert came to under $45.  They polished it off with a miso-maple ice cream over brioche french toast.

Don't go here, because you'll ruin my new favorite restaurant in Berkeley.

Japanese Tapas  taken to the next level, tucked away on the humble corner of Dwight lies a diamond in the rough.

Chef Jason's interpretation of farm to table cooking infused with Japanese and Korean roots, makes for a playful presentation of aesthetic dishes when deciding on the Omakase menu option. You can decide between $50.00, $75.00 and $100.00.

So I  chose the $75.00 Omakase and got two additional dishes so let's review those first.

-Hotate (Hokkaido Scallops), definitely fresh and buttery. The quality is similar to Ohshima (Orange, CA) and Sushi Wasabi (Tustin, CA).

-Pork Belly Tacos: I'm a a fan of pork belly (one of the savory gourmet delights of my personal palate). The Pork Belly was nice and juicy, the lime added enough acidity to cut through when necessary and the other components were held together by a mini tortilla. The only con was it was somewhat messy to eat. The taco fell apart immediately after the first bite and the juices ran rivers through my finger tips as I finished my last bites.

-Kanpachi Carpaccio: I'm not a big fan of avocados, I didn't fully understand the purpose it served in this dish. Since the kanpachi and in-house sauce that supplemented it were good enough for me. 

-Sesame infused Uni Hand Roll: There was smoke, crunch and richness in the uni texture all at once. I thoroughly enjoyed and I am not a fan of uni (slowly becoming one though).

-Salmon Sashimi w/Truffle Aioli and Mango emulsion: Looks nice, the salmon is fresh, Truffle wasn't overwhelming however the Mango was underwhelming (at least to me).

-Tuna (Toro) Tartare w/ Caviar, Avocado and In-House sauce. This dish had a lot of control. I thought it would be too rich and milky considering, the avocado and fatty toro was in the same circular mold. However everything came together and nothing was overpowering in my palate. 

-Mussels Con Chorizo: Probably my best dish of the night (a new dish they just placed on the menu). Mussels cooked well (I don't even like mussels) and the Chorizo broth was addicting. To the point of licking the bowl like a dog, type of addicting.

-Omakase Dessert: Homemade brownie, infused with Green Tea Ice Cream and layered into a Chocolate Mousse. It was sort of like molten cake but not really.

After spending $116.00 dollars (tip included) the experience was enjoyable. Service was excellent (replaced silverware after every dish). 

However, it was really hard for me to "get messy" as Chef Jason put it when a nicely plated dish is presented to you. I probably used the same amount of napkins I would normally use in an All You Can Eat setting. And, I do find the price point a bit higher than expected with Omakase. After cooking for less than a decade, I respect Chef Jason for bringing his A-Game here in the east bay. Overall, I look forward to his growth and evolution in the coming years. Cheers, 4.5 (but I had to round down to a 4).

After almost a year after having first discovered and reviewed Joshu-Ya Brasserie, it has never failed in appeasing me, from the service to the food itself. 

Although several reviews are primarily focusing on the price relative to the college atmosphere, it is imperative to keep in mind that its location is not not necessarily "on campus", being a bit further down telegraph closer to Oakland. The restaurant easily caters to people of all ages and there is bound to be something on the menu that just about any stomach will delight in. This is because of its' "California Cuisine [with World Influences]" along with traditional Japanese dishes and sushi. 

Joshu-Ya can get a little busy, but the feel, comfort and experience you have at the restaurant combined with the ever so delicious meal you have, are all worth trying. Do yourself a big favor and discover how amazing it can be to fall in love with eating all over again.

Overall, this was a truly memorable experience.   I will definitely be back here again.  The products are fresh, the food is creative, and plating is very nice.  

As our first course, my table ordered the Jalapeño Pork Belly Soba.  I'm typically not a fan of soba because it's usually somewhat boring.   However, the thought of jalepeno and pork belly combined with soba was too interesting to pass up.  This dish really blew me away.    There was a subtle spiciness from the jalapeño that worked extremely well with the savory, slow roasted pork belly that was married superbly with the ponzu and soba noodles.  This was a very satisfying and refreshing start to our meal.

For our second course, we ordered a variety of sushi pieces including tuna, salmon with truffle cream, mackerel, and uni.  There was a generous ratio of fish to rice.   The mackerel  and uni were particularly impressive as these items are only enjoyable if they are very fresh.   Really all of the fish was very nice and had clearly been handled with care.

To wrap up our meal, we decided to order dessert.  It's fairly rare that I order dessert at an Asian restaurant, but everything had been so delicious up to that point we decided to give it a shot.   The waiter recommended the Grean Tea Pop Corn Ice Cream, but we opted for the Tapioca Red Bean Ice Cream.  The Tapioca Red Bean Ice cream is fantastic.    A scoop of homemade red bean ice cream lies in a small bed of tapioca balls.   It's the perfect way to finish off the meal.  It's inventive, refreshing and delicious.

After finishing my meal Joshu-ya, I tried thinking of a better overall experience that I've had at a Japanese restaurant.  Nothing came to mind.  Joshu-ya was memorable because of its creative food and extremely fresh ingredients.  I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone who appreciates quality food.

Date & Time: Tuesday January 10, 2012 @ 3:43PM.
Company:  Didn't mention on the receipt or address themselves. But the owner did introduced himself, Jason Kwon! 
Crowd:  So zen. They come here to eat and relax. 
Vibe:  Peaceful with mingling beats with minimal lyrical lines. 
Music:  Electronic-ish, instrumental-ish, zen-ish, hip hop-ish.. music. Words that can't describe.
Decor:  Very small small. The outside looks so expansive, heightened buildings and almost-legit Japanese garden on the front with outdoor seatings. Japanese dividers on the crowded area.  
Service: Promptly & well taken care off. The girl (Caucasian, whom I do not know her name) is super attentive. People mention the service is slow, I agree but me & my buddy were lucky to be the only 2 customers at the brunch time. 
Imbibe:  Hot brown rice tea & ice water (free!) 
Devour:   Warm miso soup to shoot our gastric. Joshu-Ya Lunch Special (appetizer, not really an entree) that comes with mixed tempura (even has mushroom tempura), 3 pcs. of fresh nigiri from the sea (sake, maguro, & unagi - salmon, tuna, and eel in English translation), tekka maki, 4 pieces of CA. rolls (for newbies like me, but not really a Japanese sushi master or sushi sensei, either. It just taste good) & house salad. Lion king roll as another order as well. My buddy got the NY Brasserie burger which consists of juicy angus sirloin burger, NY cheddar, caramelized vidalia onions, tomatoes, spicy mayo mixed with garden salad. Yuzu Cheescake and Black Sesame Creme Brulee are to die. It will slide your tongue with katana! 
Total:  $42.89 USD - deal! NOM NOM NOMDESU!

I was really worried when I found out Joshu-Ya was under new management. I've been going there for over 7 years and have always loved it. (So much that my husband and I had our rehearsal dinner at Joshu-Ya) And my experience with new management always changes the quality of food. 

Thank goodness that isn't what happened with Joshu-Ya. The owner's son took over and the sushi chef is still the same. Went here on Sunday and had a feast, the sushi is still amazing and the cooked food is even better than it was. The restaurant is stunning, clean and modern with hardwood floors giving the customer the real feeling of a sushi restaurant. 

We started with Wakame and Edamame (the usual) which I alwlays enjoy. Its the standard, flavorful Wakame and Edamame to start off the meal. The sashimi was as fresh as it always has been. We ordered the sashimi platter which came with ahi, sake, hamachi, scallops. We moved onto the Omakase (chef's choice) platter. In the Omakase, there was a salad with fresh asparagus, followed by the Jalapeno Hamachi Carpaccio with ponzu which I already thought was amazing, fresh sashimi topped with a jalapeno slice, but then came the Seared Albacare Tataki which is spicy seared albacore, fried onions, scallions, ginger dressing and its absolutely delicious. 

If you think we'd be full after that, you're dreaming, we went on to order the Lucky Danny and Super Crunch rolls, both which are delicious, followed with mixed tempura satisfied my craving for fried things. Or so I thought.. we then had the Ton Katsu, which I highly recommend. Their cooked dishes have definitely stepped up and have a more modern, complimentary flavor to them. The Nabe Udon was just sort of a side dish for those who wanted soup, it was good udon, but I was still mesmerized with everything else.

Then came dessert (with the Omakase) they brought out tempura ice cream, 2 with green tea and 1 with red bean. I definitely liked the green tea better, but I can't say I didn't enjoy the red bean tempura ice cream.

And finally, after all that, Jason, the new manager and executive chef came out to greet us. He was very nice and welcoming and brought back that hospitable feel we've always loved. He had us try two new desserts: a scoop of rose ice cream on lemon gastrique - quite possibly the best ice cream I've ever eaten. We also had their cheesecake on the lemon gastrique which was also really good. 

I'll definitely remain loyal to Joshu-Ya Brasserie as the quality of food and innovativeness has gotten even better - I didn't think that was possible for a restaurant I already thought was one of the best out there. 

Bring your appetite. It's worth it.
This place has really full-flavored Indian wraps. There isn't much room at all for dining in which is a bummer. It's good food for on the go.

Quick, easy, and yummy. Definitely try this place out. This is a good place to run to if you are in a rush, but want something good to eat. 
My go-to combo is butter chicken in naan, everything except cucumbers and jalapenos, and mild coconut. I usually don't like coconut, but the guy behind the counter recommended it with butter chicken so I took his word for it. And it turned out to be absolutely delicious! So if you're wondering what kind of sauce to put on your stuff, then just ask for their recommendation.

I go here around once a week now. It tastes delicious and is a great value. They make some giant "burritos" and you can have them add all these dressings and condiments on top (like Chipotle). It's very messy, and some liquid always leaks through my aluminum foil wrap (make sure to grab some napkins yourself if you're getting them to-go). I wish they were open on weekends. Amazingly busy too--I was here once at 5pm, and there was already a line of a few people.
Naan-wrap is SO good! How innovative is that! Basically Indian Style Chipotle but much more tasty :)

This is a great choice for affordable on-the-go indian fusion. I tried a tandoori chicken rice bowl with brown rice and tamarind chutney as well as a mango lassi. I thought the flavors were good, spicy enough for my mild tastebuds, and I loved the produce add ins. The chicken was a little dry, but that's probably because it's boneless chicken that is cooked early in the day. The mango lassi was also very good with plenty of fruit. I would definitely come back again to try their wraps and other items if I were in the area.
The food is tasty and a nice change of pace. Prices aren't bad either and the service is fast. Go for it!

I went back because I was hungry in the basement of Evans and I wasn't in the mood for Top Dog. This time I around I knew what I was doing so ordering was a little easier. Also, after my first review, the owner e-mailed me and apologized about the staff issue. I did appreciate the gesture so that kind of gave them a bonus in my opinion too.

Still, a four is what they get because of their prices. It's pretty average for restaurants near campus and they are pretty generous with the food portions. However, it's not something you might want to stop by at more than twice every three weeks (maybe that's just the broke college student in me).

Been here a few times. 

The food is quality, always a quick line, never have to wait for change, all workers are in Cal gear, and the owners are nice people.

Samosas are good during lunch time when fresh.

Its a 4.5 star restaurant for what they bring to the community.

Interesting concept, although with all the fusion concepts out there now (ie Korean tacos), Indian wraps aren't that big of a stretch.

I got a naan wrap with chicken (tandoori? it was saucy though, more like tikka masala) with veggies plus sweet tamarind sauce and hot mint and cilantro sauce. I also added a samosa just so I could try it (at $1 dollar it's a good deal, but it wasn't fresh).

Overall, it was tasty and relatively inexpensive (could have been a little cheaper, but still a good deal). I also wish the samosa would have been hotter and fresh out of the fryer instead of sitting under the heat lamp.

Like everyone else has stated, Urbann Turbann is similar to Chipotle but with Indian food. Every time I have come here, I always get the naan wrap. I've tried butter chicken, tandoori chicken and pork vindaloo--ALL DELICIOUS! The best part about Urbann Turbann is that they definitely do not skimp on the ingredients, and when I need help deciding which chutney to go with my wrap, the workers are always really friendly and excited to give me suggestions.

I think it's too easy to get carried away with all the ingredients they have. This place is certainly appetizing, but somehow the two times I've gone I have not been completely satisfied with the meal, to no fault of the store operators. The first time I got a pulled pork naan wrap. I know this isn't a frequent complaint, but the server put a hugely disproportionate amount of meat in the bread. I actually got sick of it before I wanted to stop eating. The wrap is very large, though, and definitely splits into 2+ meals. The second time I went I got a half butter chicken and half mushroom filling wrap. The wrap kind of fell apart without the aluminum casing, and it's difficult to eat without deconstructing. The food is super flavorful, but it's kind of overwhelming when everything combines together, so I would use restraint when choosing fillings. Urbann Turbann is a good deal when you consider ~$7 split into at least two meals. I recommend the mushroom filling! The servers are super chill and friendly.

I completely agree with all the other reviewers - this place is best described as an Indian Chipotle. Instead of a tortilla, you get a choice in a variety of naans. Instead of steak and chicken and all those meats, you get choices of potato or (my favorite), lamb. Instead of salsa, you get a choice between a bunch of different kinds of sauces and spices I'd never previously heard of (but I really recommend the mint one!) and the rice is also very delicious. The burrito is cheap and you get a huge amount (just like Chipotle). I love this place and would go here much more often if I didn't live so far!

I love this place - think Chipotle for Indian food - burritos made out of naan and Indian fillings. Super delicious, although much messier to eat than a traditional burrito.  The mango lassi was fantastic also.  My only complaint that it would be nice if they had more inside seating, since these are messy enough that they're tricky to eat on the go.

wanted to give them 3.5 stars, so adding this update.  mostly because of their cal pride.  i still think the price is a bit high, but the fact that it includes tax, and considering other places don't necessarily use all-natural/organic ingredients, the price isn't that bad.  the place isn't that much to look at, but i don't think they make any pretense of it being a nice place to eat and hang out, so for what it is, it's a nice addition to the choices we have here on northside.

The portion sizes are excellent, and the food is delicious. My favorite thing to get here is a naan wrap with seekh kebab. I don't like the pork so much but the chicken isn't bad either.

The mango lassi also tastes great, although its a little heavy on the wallet at $3.

The staff here is excellent. A lot of times I dropped by they were out of the seekh kebab, but the staff is always very apologetic about it. I once was waiting a little long (not more than 15 minutes) -- by my choice, I might add -- for a new batch of seekh kebab to come out. The manager personally apologized to me and gave the meal to me on the house. I was genuinely impressed.

Dude come on, what's not to love?

It's indian food, with potatoes, in a naan wrap. The butter chicken in naan, with potatoes, vegetables, some shredded coconut, and cilantro-mint sauce is ohhh nom nom nom.

:) One little set-back though, is that the butter chicken is ridiculously oily (what else do you expect?), so it soaks the naan rather quickly. These naan-wraps should definitely be eaten fresh, because they tend to get soggy after a few hours.

Great place! Might be a bit on the pricier end, but definitely worth trying.

Just finished off my pork wrap- YUMM!  Everything looked fresh and tasted fresher.  The veggies were crisp and refreshing (important when you are eating spicy indian food) and they had a huge variety of toppings to add to your wrap- a lil something for everyone's taste buds.

We had the raspberry flavored yogurt drink for dessert- very refreshing!

Look forward to my next visit there so I can try the chicken and the Samosas.  Overall a very filling and satisfying meal... a great alternative to the standard food places in town.

GO BEARS!

First off, this place has no heater so come bundled up or wait until the weather warms up. It was freezing inside. I was huddled around a table with my friends and we could see our breath in the air. 

The naan here is delicious but it doesn't really work quite as well as a wrap, not like the way a tortilla skin does. A third of the way into my wrap, it began dripping on me. My recommendation is to stick with a bowl and pay $1 to get a naan on the side. The food overall was good, but I couldn't shake it lacked the strong/intense flavors that I usually associate with great Indian food. The tandori chicken was a bit dry and needed more tandori. The pork vindaloo was just so-so. I found the mint & cilantro chutney/sauce to be too mild, but the yogurt raita (extra $.50) provided an excellent cool and refreshing compliment to my wrap

Urbann Turbann is a good lunch spot for students who find themselves on Northside and the workers here are very friendly and helpful. Props on the extremely generous portions.

This is far and away my favorite fast food place in Berkeley.  So many flavors to choose from.  I usually go veggie with the garbanzo dish which is great, today I had the kidney bean one, really wonderful. The additional chutney's and sauces a great plus.  I can go hot or less so depending on how I feel. They are always friendly.

I got a huge veggie wrap here for a good price, on the advice of a helpful employee.  I'm a vegetarian, hoped to avoid anything spicy, and wasn't quite sure what that left on the menu.  The wrap turned out to be tasteless and five times the size of my stomach, so I couldn't finish it.  I really hate wasting food.  But if I weren't a vegetarian, I'd probably try this place again.
All the meat choices are deliciously flavored. EXTREMELY good. Slightly pricey though: around $8.

I love Urbann Turbann! Props to my friend for recommending this place or I might never have given it a shot.

It really is an Indian food Chiptole-style place. Though not super authentic, it's worth it for the portion size, price, and taste. I am addicted to the butter chicken wrapped in naan with a little of everything and a drizzle of habanero chutney. It is so delicious, the butter chicken is flavorful and filling and the naan is yogurty perfection. for about $7 I have lunch and dinner or lunch for 2. 

The location is definitely convenient being right off of campus. The service is fast and friendly and the food is worth all $7. I anticipate eating here once a week or once every other week when I have school.

This place is basically the Indian chipotle in many ways. I got a rice bowl with butter chicken (which is just their "tandoori" chicken drenched in a masala sauce), with various other things in it. The potatoes? DELICIOUS. I couldn't stop eating them. I also really liked that they had cilantro as an ingredient, and that they're very generous with it. Also just like chipotle, this place is about as authentically Indian as chipotle is authentically Mexican, which is to say not at all. That said, the food they serve is delicious.
Like butter chicken and tandoori chicken. Very fast choice.

even though they are very friendly and i like the concept of the restaurant, the food itself tastes okay. I tried it twice over there. one time i got the really spicy beef wrap. the other time i got a sweet pork rice bowl. however, both times i was not satisfied with the taste and the texture of the food. Even though it does not fit my taste, I do think people should try it just for fun because their food is pretty cheap. Keep in mind there is no seating for the restaurant

This is not indian food. This is Chipotle for Indian food, and just as Chipotle is not Mexican, Urbann Turbann is not Indian.

I am Indian. I love Urbann Turbann (and Chipotle). it's a great model - delicious food that's not authentic. I'm a Tyler Cowen fan. All food is ethnic food - it's what the people of (here) ate during the time period of (now). If it's objectively delicious. Naan for $1. Large portions. The mango lassi was okay - more like an Odwalla than a real lassi, but that's fine too.

I love this place.

There is not much seating (two tables for two people), but the food is delicious. The naan is always soft, moist, and chewy. The butter chicken is delicious with just the right amount of spice; the veggies are fresh. The staff is friendly, the service is fast. A great place to grab a bite to go.

Simple and painless. I found this place quite endearing and the ambience of the color palette and vistas pleasing. The music was a plus and I was very impressed by the all-around server/preparer. I got the naan mushroom mattar with potatoes, all organic and the fiery tomato, habanero and cumin chutney (huge plus!). I also had the chai to balance out the chilly weather and wide-array of flavors I was about to embark upon. While all of this was going down, my friends and I had a blast with the music selection and light fixtures.

As for getting down and dirty, I was familiar with foiled burrito-type foods and the inconsitency of flavor so I knew my first bites were going to be bomb, which they were, and the latter half lacking and exhausting. With this knowledge, I truly enjoyed my veggie naan burrito extravaganza! The mushroom batter was just right and the cumin chutney played well with the peas and potatoes. Free refills on the chai was to die for.

I'm not such huge on Indian food but this place was a great munch after a play at the rose gardens or kick back with friends. I'd come back only if I really wanted wet-burrito style naan/curry but for now I'll wrestle with the once a semester tear and dip format of Indian cuisine.

This is a great place for quick Indian food, made burrito/bowl style! Their food is freshly cooked, and the naan used for their burritos are nice and thick. As a student at UC Berkeley, it's a quick solution to grab a bite to eat when studying long hours in the library or at Stanley Hall.

I always order a bowl with their Tandoori Chicken, which as been really creamy and refreshing. I recommend adding the sweet tamarind and hot mint and cilantro chutneys to whatever you order, as they aren't spicy, but add a sweet and tangy flavor to your dish.

Here is the story of how I lost my Urbann Turbann virginity. I walked out of class at 8 pm. I had not eaten anything all day except for a salad at 2 pm. My hunger had passed the point of hunger- I barely had the energy to walk from Northgate Hall, across the street to this location. In fact, I was actually on my way to the Northside Asian Ghetto, but I just didn't have the energy to walk a few steps up the hill. Instead, I was drawn in by Urbann Turbann which was conveniently right across the street behind Northside Cafe. There was no line, and I could smell the herbal chicken from a mile away. 

The worker was extremely patient as I stared at the menu for around five minutes. Finally, he decided to give me some help, explaining my options- I opted for the rice bowl this time (but I'll definitely try the wrap next time). I got the half-half butter chicken and tandoori chicken... Which is basically the same thing because the butter chicken is tandoori chicken with sauce poured over it. So note, if you get it half-half, it's basically the same as getting the butter chicken (but maybe less sauce..) Anyway, as I do at Chipotle, I of course decided to add every topping. And unlike Chipotle, the super nice worker packed my to-go bowl with veggies and sauce. The rice bowl, if you get all the toppings, comes with: brown/basmati rice, choice of meat/vegetarian, potatoes (free!), tomatoes, greens, onions, peppers, and different sauces. I got the fiery hot sauce and it is quite good! (pretty similar to the hottest sauce at Chipotle- if you can handle it, it's great.) 

I ate 1/4 of my bowl outside and was immediately full. But because it just tasted SO. GOOD, I went ahead and shoved another fourth in my stomach. But honestly, I finished half my bowl, and I am ready to food coma... This is A LOT of food. And it's just so extremely filling, I have no bad words to say for my $7 rice bowl (no coins! 7 dollars flat! so easyy). It left me extremely satiated, was easy on my wallet (especially since this bowl can probably last me around 3 meals) and did I mention IT TASTES GREAT??? You'd expect for such a price that the chicken would be dry and all the ingredients wimpy, but the chicken is really tender and the butter chicken sauce is bombdiggity. 

Great place... I just wish I lived closer to it :/

Really really good.

I love their tandoori chicken and they let you mix stuff and get as many of the chutneys as you want.

Urbann Turbann is a great place for Indian food with a modern twist. It's good food fast, not "fast food". The food is fresh and full of flavor.  The servings are incredibly filling and everything I've ordered (which is almost everything on the menu) has been great. For $6-7 (which includes the tax), you will be full from their wraps or rice bowls.  

It's much like a sandwich shop, but using Indian influenced ingredients - naan instead of a pita, pork vindaloo instead of pulled pork, Tandoori chicken instead of chicken salad, and more.  To give you an idea of the freshness, they have a tandoori oven to cook the naan right in the store and only pull out the naan after you order it - so it's hot and fresh.  If you have had old naan, you know there's no comparison to hot, fresh naan.

You choose your meat or vegetarian choice (i.e. seasonal veggies, mushroom mattar, etc) and then customize your veggie toppings (cucumbers, tomatoes, etc).  You then get to choose from some of their wonderful sauces like hot mint and/or fiery tomato, habanero with cumin.  

Instead of sides like chips or fries, the have handmade samosa you can get as a side.  This is a great idea, but, to be completely honest, the samosa quality can vary a bit.  For example, one time the samosas were crisp and quite big (I normally have trouble finishing my wrap due to the wrap size. Since I the samosa was so good and I just had to finish it, I definitely had leftovers).  However, the next time I ordered a samosa, it was smaller (which wasn't a bad thing since last time it was too much), but it was greasier and the filling was a little overdone having some burnt pieces and almost paste consistency.  About 60-70% of the time the samosas are great.  

All in all, the food at Urbann Turbann is great.  If you'd like to have good Indian food, quickly, this place is definitely one not to be missed!
This is my new favorite restaurant - had lunch there yesterday and was back again for more today. Delicious!!!!

Mmm. As many have said, it's pretty much the Indian version of Chipotle. Except it's not. For one, it's on Northside, not South. It's Indian-fusion, not Tex-Mex. But besides that, it's pretty much the same style.

With that said, I usually get a rice bowl with chicken. I've learned that I can get half-n-half, which is a pretty sweet deal. The sauces kinda confuse me on what goes with what. Definitely wish there was a sign that had some suggestions.

My only issue with urbann turbann is that it seems to be a bit dry. As a result, you need to get a sauce. Several maybe.

In all honestly, I love Urbann Turbann because it's super quick. I've never had to wait long, so I'm in and out in a matter of minutes.

I've been frequenting this place a bit more now that it's summer, and it's a good place for me to grab a quick lunch to-go before heading off to study.

I always get the rice bowl with butter chicken (YUM!) and the only chutney I've tried so far is the Hot Mint and Cilantro, but even then, I'm not exactly tempted to try another one because it's pretty good (and I love cilantro!). I've seen other people get the half/half meats option but since the rice feels a little on the drier side to me, I always want to get a meat that has more sauce to it so that's why I stick with butter chicken...but that's just me.

Also tried their Mango Lassi! It was delicious, but a little pricey. It was $2.50 for a very small cup ):

Like others mentioned, it's good, but a little on the pricey side so I'll be stopping by every now and then, just not all the time. Great alternative to Chipotle if you want something a little different and fresher-tasting!

I really like the wraps here. I had a delicious butter chicken wrap with some green curry I think, and it definitely hit the spot. It's the Indian version of a Chipotle burrito and is made right in front of you so you can tell them exactly what you want and the amount of it. That specific wrap was $7.50. I have yet to try their bowls, but next time I plan to. The service here is very accommodating and it overall is a nice, good quality take-out place. I definitely recommend coming here, especially if you're a student. I wish I would have tried it earlier!

Food: Super fresh, ridiculously filling, and apparently a lot of it is natural, too? You can pick between brown rice, white rice, wheat roti, and buttery delicious naan.

Location: not much seating, but the area is pretty nice

Service: workers are very friendly

Wait Time: ultra fast service

Price: Wraps range from $6-$8 I think? Totally worth it.

The people who work here are nice, compostable products are cool, and I think they are a great local business (their tip jar goes to random causes).

Check this Indian Subway out!  It was delicious and filling :)

I ordered the Seekh Kabob in a naan wrap and it was delicious!  They gave me 3 big pieces of meat, which I felt like I got my money's worth.  Also, they had leafy green salad as an option (rather than only having the iceberg lettuce= more nutritious!).  The sauces were delicious; they had the cilantro-lime, tamarind, and more.  All I can say about the food was- it was HELLA good :)  BTW, they make naan as soon as you order it, super fresh.

Price was very decent.  Similar to Chipotle but even more cheap.  

Along with many restaurants in  Berkeley, this place was tiny.

This place is delicious! I recommend the butter chicken naan wrap for sure, with all the fixings and the coconut + hot red sauce. It's often been compared to chipotle because of the structure, however I would say it is waaay better then chipotle, they pack it with more meat/goodies. It's kind of a walk since it's all the way in north side, but a trip well worth it!!!! You will not be disappointed.

I got the buttered chicken naan-rito and it was really good!! can't really go wrong with curry and a burrito. it was sloppy though, I got it all over my shirt, jeans, and flip flops and all over the library steps ooops. It was delicious nonetheless

Urbann Turbann is great. I came across it last semester passing time in between classes. I love the idea of naan wrapped Indian food. And what is better is that I get to chose what to put inside. It is a small unit, so if you come during peak hours, chances are you will be taking it to go.

It's too bad I'll not be going here again, their food is affordable, healthy, and tasty.  
I don't get a lunch break at work (taking lunch is an admission that you don't have enough to do and don't have a good work ethic), and I came here once during a particularly busy week for me.  I was the only customer in the store, but all the employees seemed most concerned with making themselves a plate (probably due to the lull).  After waiting for someone to help me a few other customers started coming in.  Since I wanted a wheat wrap and not a flour wrap I was asked to step aside and let the other customers go ahead of me.  After waiting a few moments more I decided to eat elsewhere.
At the same time that my burrito was done at La Burrito, the owner of Urban Turban came in and wanted to know why I left.  After arguing with him for awhile inside, we went outside and argued more.  He was trembling and cursing and I though for sure we were going to fight.  I have never had someone track me down to another restaurant like that and it was extremely awkward, not to mention quite insulting.  I was happy to see that there was affordable and healthy food near my work, now I'm sad that the owner is nuts.

LOVE LOVE LOVE LOOOOOOOOOOOOVE THIS PLACE!!

I will admit that this review is biased because indian food = love. Anyways, I always get a rice bowl (because I can never finish a naan wrap, which gets soggy and hence unenticing) with half paneer and half butter chicken with tamarind sauce. I must say I love that I can do half half because I get variety, and I also feel healthier.

Their paneer is hit or miss -- sometimes it's overcooked such that the paneer is rubbery and golden when you bite into it; other times, it's heaven in your mouth. The bell peppers are sometimes undercooked and overly crunchy, other times it's just perfection. So, although it is sometimes good sometimes bad, I still eat it.

Their butter chicken is ALWAYS right on. So delectable, creamy, flavorful, YUM. The one time they ran out of butter chicken I gave the tandoori chicken a try -- big mistake! It was so dry and no flavor :( Definitely always get the butter chicken: can't go wrong!


Only qualm... their price went up so it's now $7.50 for a wrap or bowl. That, and I think their serving size decreased... the rice bowls used to be 1.5 meals for me... now I can finish it in one go (on the last two times I went). :(

Awesome, cheap, indian food.

Great because you can get  mix of cooked vegetables, and garbanzo beans, and fresh veggie toppings! with awesome salsas! Perfect for a vegetarian!

The lady who served me was super nice and helpful! She gave me huge servings in my rice bowl and helped me decide what to get!

So glad i ventured over to try it, will definitely be back many more time for some inexpensive, delectable, excellent portion for starving college student indian food!

It's like a college student's version of Indian food. YUM!

Indian food Chipotle style? I was dubious about this concept, and took a long time to muster up the courage to try Urbann Turbann (I'm very picky about Indian food). I was pleasantly surprised! Their naan isn't the best, but their curries and vegetables are good! Their chutneys (especially the tamarind and cilantro) are sweet and tangy and make the meal much more enjoyable. I succumbed to temptation and bought the samosas; they tasted pretty good, though they were really greasy. I will definitely be hitting up this place again, especially if I'm on the Northside of campus.
I went here again recently and they had a new dish: butter chicken. Wow, this is good stuff - not spicy heat-wise but has a lot of flavor and definitely tastes Indian. I'll be back for more!

ok, ok, so if you read any of the other reviews...its pretty much an Indian version of chipotle!
I really wish they had more seating.  
the food was really wonderful but super super spicy (and I just got butter chicken naan wrap!) and trust me i can handle spicy.
will probably be back though, because its about two meals worth, inexpensive, and does satisfy the indian food craving pretty easily...yum!

Exactly what I expected after my friend told me to try this Indian version of Chipotle. I always have classes on north side or find myself studying closer to north side and this place is definitely one of my top choices to grab a quick lunch or dinner. 

I always get the butter chicken naan wrap with a combination of the sweet and spicy sauce. I have been told mixing the butter chicken with the veggies is a super good combo. There are quite a few times where the Naan will fall a part but have no fear because the bowl is just as good especially if you're craving some rice.

Conclusion - This place has yet to fail me.

within a day of my last review, i got a note from the owners saying that they had talked to their kitchen staff about not putting too much ginger in the paneer.  i have a lot of respect for people who can take feedback from customers with a positive attitude and improve their business that way.

that being said, i went back and got a wrap with the cholay instead and it was the perfect choice (with tamarind and mint chutney).  the wrap held together well all the way until the end and was really really filling and yummy.

Have been here before and it is delicious but...Second time this week trying to get a kabob wrap. the first time I went they said they ran out of kabob.Today I go in at 3:40pm and they ran out of kabob again with no mention if they were going to make more. Are you not a business? Do you not want my money?Please remove items you cannot provide to your customers. It's like a pizza parlor that runs out of pizza. Absolutely ridiculous!!!

MASSSIVE wrap thanks to the friendly server. I know it was a friendly gesture but I felt he put too much chicken and potatoes, leaving no room for the veggies and ultimately ripping my entire wrap. 

The butter chicken was good, but I was glad to have gotten the hothot sauce with it to balance out the starchy-ness from so much potato and creamy chicken. The cilantro added a great flavor and really saved the heavy wrap from being too much.

I'll try a rice bowl with extra veggies next time to avoid an exploding wrap if the same dude serves me.

the only indian food i have ever eaten , but i liked it! 

Unfortunately, I didn't get to try it in the restaurant, as I had it for dinner at a catered party. I had the naan + butter chicken  + hot mint w/ cilantro. Good but so spicy that I went through like 04 cups of water. 
Then again, I never really handled spicy well anyways!

Looking forward to see how much I like this place once I actually go to the restaurant .... and pay for it myself, haha.

I stopped by at 4pm on a Thursday, so I was the only one there.  I chatted with the woman who runs the place and she was friendly and seemed really eager to run a good business.  This seems like an obvious thing, but I find with a lot of shops that sometimes the customer service gets thrown out the window in lieu of a "cool idea" (see the crappy new "coffee shop" that opened at the corner of Euclid and Hearst).

Given that the place was new, and my head was full of student-type garbage, I just asked her to make me whatever she thought was the best.  I eat meat, and like spicy food so I ended up with a Chicken and potato wrap with tamarind and mint chutney.  I got a drink and the total was somewhere around $8.

The food was really good and very filling.  I'll have to sample the other choices, but I know I'll be back.  I'm just hoping (for my sake) that when the undergrads rush into town the line won't be too long.    Urbann Turbann + la burrita + hummingbird cafe = all the choice you need for under $10.

4/5 only because I wasn't blown away.  I liked it and I have no complaints, but this isn't necessarily a place I'd drag my out of town guests  to in the same way I make sure everyone stops by cheeseboard or breads of india

I live nearby and was thrilled when the doors opened at Urbann Turbann.  The food is incredibly fresh, well seasoned, and the staff are friendly and accommodating.  And, the prices can't be beat.

I was lucky enough to sample their food during the week it opened and they asked for feedback which immediately altered things.  I's a good sign when a business asks their customers what they want and actually listen.

This is a great take-out place with phenomenal food.

The flavors are spot on, the price is right, service is great. I usually have a pretty big apetite, and I've found that ordering a rice bowl with naan on the side ($1 extra) gives me that nice full feeling, and gives the perfect carb to meat ratio... because really, they hook it up with the meat.

The best way I can describe this place is it's like an Indian Chipotle.

This is a great lunch spot. It's become a weekly event for me.

The wraps are tasty (naan and roti are made fresh to order!), and once you find the right combination of toppings, they have a lot of flavor. It did take me a few tries to find the right combo of chutneys and accoutrement . (If you like sweet with a little spice, I'd recommend the sweet tamarind chutney with a small splash of their fire roasted tomato.) I always get the cholay (chickpea curry), which is hearty. It's not the most amazing Indian food you'll ever have, but it's good quality, fresh, and reasonably healthy. Definitely a welcome addition to my lunch routines. 

There isn't much in the way of atmosphere here. It's more of a grab and go place. The servers have always been on the ball when I've been here. They are especially prepared for the campus lunch rush. I walked in today, saw a long line, and pondered going somewhere else. But within a few minutes, I was already ordering my wrap. Kudos for that!

And did I mention the price?! Having a REALLY filling, fast lunch for just $5--perfect. 

Honestly, my only complaint is that some of the servers aren't great at constructing the wraps. I sometimes end up with blobs of chutney/toppings rather than having it spread throughout the wrap. And when that's the fire roasted tomato chutney....oh boy. Those are sinus-clearing bites!

I've always wondered when Indian food could become fast food, and here it is.

Urbann Turbann, the Indian Chipotle. Prices are even comparable to Chipotle. Instead of tortilla, you get naan. You get chutney, butter chicken, and a bunch of spices. Confused at what to order? That's okay, the service is great and they'll walk you through each step of the process with pleasure.

Burritos (should they be called that? Or Naanritos) are a bit dry though, and  they definitely fill you up fast. I really want to try the lassie next time I'm here.

If this place were on Southside I'm sure it would be jam-packed every single day!

Apparently, while I was busy wasting away my summer, three new eateries opened up on Euclid and Hearst. It's probably shameful that it has taken me so long to notice, but I've recently been punching sustainability in the face and have been driving myself around Berkeley. Discovering this place five days before I move away for good is evidently my punishment.

Seeing that I consider Chipotle to be a sign of the apocalypse, the description "Indian Chipotle" certainly didn't inspire much confidence. Fear not, as the wraps at Urbann Turbann are so much more than this. I entered and was greeted by two apathetic looking employees who ignored me and continued stirring their mushy-looking ingredients in various steam tubs. My heart sank. I opted to go with a mix of the mushroom mattar and the chicken tandoori in my wrap. As my wrap passed on to the veggie bar stage, I requested that the server put just a tiny bit of onions, cilantro, and mixed greens on my wrap. Instead, I got a mountain of greens. Next, I requested a small serving of spicy mint chutney. PLOP! By this point, I fully expected my wrap to taste like absolute garbage. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find that the flavors were rich and very well balanced, with the perfect mix of spices. It turned out that neither the vegetables nor the chutney ended up washing out the flavors of the two main ingredients, and instead perfectly complemented them. Everything also tasted surprisingly fresh, considering that most of the ingredients had emerged from hibernation in those dreaded steam tubs. I ended up getting quite a bit more than I bargained for (which probably explains the Chipotle comparison), for a princely sum of $7. I actually found the wrap to be considerably more appetizing than the meals I have had at Naan'n'Curry and House of Curries (not exactly the pinnacle of Indian cuisine, I know), and even better than that new Indian Flavors place that my all my Indian friends seem to be raving about these days. I would definitely come back. Four stars for the food.

Minus half a star for a complete lack of seating. There are zero seats, and what appears to be a couple of disassembled tables in the front. Minus another half a star for not putting any napkins or utensils in my bag. You're serving a heaping mound of semi-wet ingredients inside an open-ended naan. Don't skimp on the napkins, please.

Northside has always lacked a variety of cheap quality eats, but now with the emergence of three new restaurants, it seems like the oft-forgotten Euclid area is making a comeback.

UPDATE: The owners have informed me that the seating arrangement is being worked on, and that they're currently wading through some red tape to make it happen. Also, I've been informed that in order to cut down on waste, the napkins and forks are there for customers to help themselves to them. I guess someone has to be sustainable in order to make up for me raping the planet in my SUV... It would still be nice to get a napkin or two in to go orders though, so that customers in a rush (such as myself) won't be left with messy hands and nowhere to wipe them. Either way, star reinstated. The food is also sourced from local farms, and is apparently made in small batches to fill the steam tubs (unlike an evil pseudo-Mexican chain that shall not be named). A+ for sustainable supply chain management and supporting other local businesses! Don't miss this place if you're looking for a quick, relatively healthy, and tasty meal!

I already miss this place. Having gone each week when I took my son to a class on campus I tried many of the combos. They are way generous and the sauces all taste great to me. They cook up the Naan right there in the super hot special oven. The staff there were friendly. There is minimal seating but we always took it to go. Having the wrap as a sort of salad or bowl is even better and they sell the naan for a buck. Overall I love this place!

Oh man, the food here is so good! I've recently been trying Indian places and Urbann Turbann is one of my favorite places. Fast, easy, and decently priced. What more could you want?

I personally would suggest the Rice bowl with pork vindaloo and butter chicken and everything on top with the greek yogurt and sweet tamarind sauce *drool*

Parking is not too bad in this area, you just might have to park a lil further up on Euclid.

Love the concept! Chicken, potatoes, your choice of veggies and sauce, all wrapped in naan! I like how they use naan for their wrap instead of a tortilla, because it just tastes THAT much better! The burrito is HUGE, so you might want to share it with a friend.. and if you ask for spicy, it's REALLY spicy (you have been warned). It's also kind of hard to eat, so come prepared.

The Indian version of Chipotle. 

What can I say about this place? Only that it is SO GOOD. I have recently become a fan of Indian food, and wanted to try out this place because my friend was constantly raving about it last year. Usually all that hype makes me a little disappointed with the quality of the food, but not this time! 

Like I mentioned, it is essentially like an Indian version of Chipotle. There is an assembly line where you can choose your different ingredients--butter chicken, etc. You can have the option of putting it in a rice bowl or a naan burrito, which is exactly what I did. They also let you combine different things together if you are super indecisive (like I am). 

I got a naan burrito STUFFED with chicken and this mushroom mix (because I was indecisive) along with yogurt, a sweet chipotle sauce, an assortment of vegetables, and potatoes. I can't exactly remember what the chicken and mushroom dish were called, only that they were so good combined together. And when I say my burrito was stuffed, I'm telling you it was FULL, almost to the point where the server could barely wrap it into a burrito. They are very generous with their portions, and I was able to eat my burrito for dinner and lunch the next day. 

When I bit into that first bite, it was absolutely divine. All the spices gave the food so much flavoring, but it wasn't too much where it overpowered the different ingredients. I can't do spicy, and it was the perfect balance between spicy and sweet. The chicken was not dry at all, and were cut into nice bite-sized portions. While there was so much food that I had to use a fork to scoop out food during parts of my meal, what was nice was that my server wrapped it so tightly that it wasn't messy to eat at all. I couldn't stop eating it, and it was really nice to enjoy it while sitting at Memorial Glade with great friends. 

The staff is also very friendly and my server was really helpful in getting my first burrito here together. He also gave me extra portions when he overheard how hungry I was. They also have a deal where if you register the code on your receipt online, you get a free burrito after every $65 dollars spent!

Pork vindaloo with naan! I got it with potatoes, peppers, lettuce, tomatoes, and the brown sauce that was kinda sweet. It was seriously delicious, largely portioned, and cheap! I was able to split it into two meals. It's a must-visit in Berkeley. Parking may be a problem during busy meal times and after 6pm. But otherwise it seems to have ample street parking!
By far my favorite place to grab lunch in Berkeley. The food is fresh, the portions are great and the staff is great! Definitely a go to spot if you're looking for some quality food!

dang. i luh you. everything on their menu is delicious. it's so great that you can eat indian food like a burrito especially when you're busy and can't sit down to eat. i had the butter chicken wrapped in naan with potatoes and coconut chutney.  make sure you ask them for a little bit more chutney cause it gives the kick that it needs.  the naan was hot and the ingredients seemed fresh.  sometimes, thoughts of urbann turbann pop up in my head randomly during the day. it's that good.

A great twist on quick-serve Indian Food.  It's a "Chipotle" style model where you choose bread, meat (multiple veggie options), and fillings.   The food is very fresh and their are lots of different styles and combinations, hot and mild, that really suit any tastes.  The employees are happy to help you navigate through the menu if you aren't familiar with the different offerings.  

Quite frankly, the prices aren't bad when compared to other options and the amount of food that you get.  $7 will certainly fill you up and even adding a Samosa and Drink can get you out of the door for around $10.00.  

I will most likely be back when I am in the area looking for something full of flavor and filling.

Butter chicken naan wrap. Killer.

The other reviewers aren't lying, it really is the "Indian version of Chipotle."
This means that they move you down the burrito assembly line, and you pick what you want, and they throw it together for you.

It's damn good, too.

Like many other people who've written reviews for this place, I heard that this place was like an "Indian" version of Chipotle. I love Indian food, and Chipotle has become, in recent times, a staple of my college-student diet (namely because of it's high caloric content). So, what could go wrong?

The first time I visited, I ordered a naan wrap with tandoori chickens, no potatoes, tomatoes, onions, chilies, cilantro, and coconut chutney. It was honesty a life-changing experience. I would never have expected that they make naan right in front of your eyes. I don't think Chipotle could even attest to that, despite their claims to "Food with Integrity." 

I went back several times after that, going through all the meats, chutneys, fillings, and adding the potatoes. (The potatoes are crucial!) I'd have to say, the naan wrap still remains the best item on their menu. The best meat would have to be the tender, juicy pork vindaloo and the best sauce would be the sweet tamarind, although all the sauces are pretty good. 

The price is very reasonable, considering the size and quality of the food you're getting. The wrap is about 1.3x the size of a Chipotle burrito (one that has been stuffed beyond the comfort zone of the employee making it). All the meats are freshly prepared and flavorful. All the veggies are fresh as well. 

All in all, I'd say I'm coming here for lunch anytime I'm on the north side of the campus. Actually, I'd make the mecca even if I wasn't.

HELLO INDIAN CHIPOTLE OF NORTHSIDE BERKELEY~~!!!

Honestly, it is the indian chipotle. You got your naan bread wrap (tortilla) with choice of different types of meat (like at chipotle) with some potatoes (like the rice at chipotle), All at a great price!

I came here with my roommate who has CURRY FEVER (love for both stephen curry and indian curry/food) and we LOVED the place.
