How do I know this is a great food place? Food coma of 6 hrs!! We most definitely are going to come back and hopefully they'll have their samosas cause last time they ran out! 

The seating is very limited so if there's no space just go back onto campus and chill and eat some indian food!

The offerings: 
This place is quick Indian to go.  You can get a rice bowl or naan or roti wrap with a veggie or meat topping/filling.  There were a couple veggie options (paneer and red peppers, something with mushrooms), and two or three meat options including pork and beef.  $5 to $7 for the wraps and rice bowls.  $1 for veggie samosas.  Think Chipotle reinvented for Indian food.

The verdict:
Really tasty!  Nothing like a wrap made with naan.  Kind of high price to quality/portion ratio.

The food here is mouth-wateringly good. I usually don't worry too much about customer service, but the employees are also exceptionally nice. Butter chicken rice bowl with hot mint chutney = perfect lunch/dinner experience.

I totally agree with the reviewer that this place is the Indian version of Chipotle. Right next to campus, this place is tiny, so it's best to grab food and go. All meals come on a bed of rice or a naan wrap. They have three veggie options-the paneer is delicious and then fresh toppings. Also have mango lassies and samosas. Limited menu, but everything you need for Indian on the go. The place is always clean with friendly and efficient staff-but if you get there during lunch don't be surprised to find a line out the door, but ti moves fast. 

Lunch is about $7 and you get plenty of food for one meal, often I can't eat it all in one sitting. Completely authentic Indian food-no. But a delicious, reasonably priced lunch place on the go to mix up your week!

Nice cozy place

INDIAN FOOD IN A BURRITO WRAP?? I WISH THERE WERE MORE OF THESE PLACES IN THE WORLD

dam do i wish urban turban was on south side.

7.50 for a huge indian burrito with a ton of meats and potatos is a deaaaalll

Finally got around to eating at this place that is rumored to be the Indian Chipotle. I think the idea alone is pretty innovative and I don't think I've seen it done anywhere else. 

The portions are hearty and the price is good. I tried the Butter Chicken and the Tandoori Chicken both wrapped in Naan, which worked surprisingly well as a pseudo-tortilla. It wasn't too thick but still retained a nice fluffy texture. The chicken was well flavored and not too dry and the assortment of fresh veggies and sauces all mixed together quite nicely.

It might not be true Indian food, but I would definitely come back and try some of the other options.

I just had to come here after hearing glorious things about Urbann Turbann from my friends. Berkeley bucket list CHECK!

First off, everything here is massive and supersized. The burritos are humongous, think every type of indian entree you can think of, plus rice and greens wrapped in a large, THICK naan. Talk about food comas on the go! Their salad box is pretty much the same except you have to order the naan separately which is a kind of a bummer. However, it does allow you to enjoy the meal for a day or two because the naan won't get as soggy. I like the fact that the staff does not limit how much customers chose to stuff in their burritos, because there are many types of sides to choose from (including a good vegetarian selection). I like the creamy potatoes, orange tofu/paneer thingy, mango lassi and sweet and sour sauce. In the end, everything mushes together and begins to taste the same so I recommend either eating everything in one sitting or sharing with friends. Portions and prices are very generous. I'd say this is a must-have experience before one leaves Berkeley--Indian style Chipotle.

Super-fresh, super-delicious, super-friendly too.  My first try today, and I love this place.  I ordered the choley in a naan (which they make to order right in front of you - the best!) I meant to take it home, but took a bite and then, well, that was that.  Gone in a flash!

Have been here three times, and I do like this place.
Is it the best Indian food ever? Well I'm no Indian food connoisseur, but there are definitely better Indian restaurants. So I'd seek elsewhere if you want mindblowing Indian food....
The idea is just like Chipotle as others have said. There is naan, roti ("healthier" option), or bowl. And then there are choices for meat/vegetables. They'll also give you potatoes if you want them. Of course, then comes vegetables and finally a variety (~5 or 6) chutneys to choose. The raita (yogurt) does cost 50 cent extra...worth it? Eh. Maybe the first time. But my problem is that I don't really taste it with so many other items in the wrap. 

The meat (I typically get the Butter Chicken) is generally pretty good/vegetables are fresh tasting. Portions are definitely generous...takes some time to finish, even for a big eater as myself. Watch out if you're getting this to go in a wrap because it can and does get soggy. Dripping messes are no fun. 

Restaurant itself is kind of small with limited seating inside and outside. Workers there are nice and my first time there, the guy gave me a recommendation of the chutneys that complement the meat. Prices are standard at ~7.5 for meat and a little cheaper for vegetables/cholay.

Had an order of the Seasonal Fresh Vegetables Wrap (~$7): kale, potatoes, lettuce, tomato, cucumbers, mixed greens, chillies, cilantro, and red onions with spicy tomato chutney in a fresh naan. Food was delicious, staff was fast, and the ambiance was lively.

umg this place makes me sad I live on Southside!

So I have this burrito obsession: I want at least one every day.  But today I was stuck on Northside.  I knew about this place so I decided to check it out.  IT IS SO GOOD.  Obviously the flavor profile is different than the standard burrito, and it's a nice change.  I love that you can put a bunch of fresh organic veggies in it.  THE NAAN IS SO CHEWY.  Good lord.  The warm, stretchy, chewy tortilla is what I love about burritos, but having the naan as the wrap doubles the chewiness.  Whoever invented this was a genius.

Delicious! 

What's different about this Indian naan-wrap place is they make the wraps in front of you. Consequently the process is quick, efficient, and the wrap is made to your satisfaction. The service is very friendly and helpful; as it was my first time, I only knew what meat I wanted (butter chicken, a childhood favorite---tandoori chicken covered with a coconut milk based curry).

The server gave me suggestions about the chutney and other things that I was unsure about. And it was a delicious, delicious wrap. I also bought a samosa (they threw in another one for free as it was closing time) and these were also very good. Seems a little bit primed for the American palate; spiciness is very toned down. I was thankful.

I'd come back, but probably not a good place if you want to eat inside (not much seating, especially if you have a large group). But it's close enough to other outdoor seating areas so, worth it.

I have to give this place five stars. This place is so good and the food is so cheap. I know it may not be authentic Indian food, but what can you expect from fast food places. Chipotle is definitely not real Mexican food, Yoshinoya is not real Japanese food, and Panda Express is not real Chinese food, but people still love to eat at these places.

All I can say is this place, at least for me was really good. Its like a chipotle for Indian food. I got a warp with the potatoes and the pork vindalu. The ingredients are super fresh and they stuff the wrap with tons of meat. It is a perfect place if your wanting to grab a quick bite to eat.

The people that serve you are very friendly and the restaurant is kept pretty clean.

The only thing bad about this place is that the wraps can get a bit messy so try not to eat this in class or while wearing white.

I couldn't really imagine what the Indian version of Chipotle was supposed to be, but now I know what everyone means. Basically, you just order everything cafeteria-style - you choose a wrap or rice bowl, add the main meat/veggies, then fresh tomatoes/cilantro/onions/etc, and finally select a sauce. I went with a tandoori chicken naan wrap with sweet and sour sauce and miscellaneous veggies. I walked out with a hefty wrap all for only $7! Really easy to order, clean place, cheap (and no tax?!). Definitely worth stopping by if you're in the area. Probably healthier than Chipotle too.
7 dollars gets you a HUGE naan wrap stuffed full of meat, potatoes, veggies, and chutneys. The naan is freshly baked.  Great food!!!

This place was awesome! First and foremost the prices were great because everything on the menu includes tax. I had the kabab wrap with the potatoes and raitha. The meat was very flavorful and the naan wasn't burnt like other places! 

The place itself is pretty nice. Defiantly catered toward people on the go, as most of us are! 

Awesome food prepared fast, great customer service and very reasonable prices!
good food! It's the only place northside I've found where one can get a good amount of good quality food for $5-6 including tax. There's not a lot of variety, but the quality is pretty consistent.

Urbann Turbann, is like the indian chipotle... but extremely better and awesome! Cheers mate! this place is super bomb man, for a little under 8 bucks you get a FAT, no offense to anyone... but a FAT ole "indian burrito" your choice of meats... (you can also mix n match) i tried the butter chicken with potatoes, and everything with coconut and EXTRA Habanero sauce all wrapped in a delicious piece of na'an. Let me just warn you, first bite you're like woah... second bite.... you begin to enter a state of euphoria...third bite... or maybe it's your 4th,5th, 6th? you'll lose track of time and end up going in for 1 more! haha come out to Urbann Turbann it's an awesome place, very flavorful... and indeed something different!

I loved this place from the very first time I tried it out. I think its brilliant! They have kept it simple but tasty. The fusion of the Indian food in burrito style naans works really well. I also love that they have chutneys to spice things up a little more! 

My favorite is the pork vindaloo but  almost anything is good.

Urbann Turbann presents an Indian version of Chipotle, making assembly line wraps with Naan or Roti instead of a tortilla.  I usually get a Naan wrap with Tandoori Chicken and Tamarind chutney, which is a tangy and delicious combination.  Overall, it was well executed, with my only complaint that the size of the wrap is a bit small and not very filling.

great Indian wrap
kinda pricy for a wrap though
the portion's pretty big and it does fill you up

Delicious and nutritious!  I had the cholay-roti wrap, with their spicy cumin & habanero pepper sauce, and it was everything I hoped for and more : )  The pork vindaloo was also delectable, highly recommended!
Went there yesterday. The wrap is GREAT! Need more seats and it'll be perfect if they have Taj Mahal beer.

Close to campus, passably tasty Indian food.  Ok, so my first impression of this place was confusion.  Something about the layout and the menu made me just not know what to do.  You get two options:
1) a rice bowl
2) a wrap with either naan or whole-wheat roti
It's meant to be quick take-out style.

I got the Cholay (chickpea wrap) in a roti.  It was fine.  The roti while fresh didn't actually taste that good...bit of a cardboard texture.  The cholay was fine although clearly "white-people" spiced...meaning a bit bland.  I ate the overall product although was a bit under-whelmed.

I'm giving them 3 stars (instead of 2) because they're new, and I hope they improve.  If they read this, they should:
1) Re-orient their ordering process or make it a bit clearer.
2) Get a bit more adventurous with the spice.
3) Offer some sort of combo options...especially on the vegetarian side.  This is distinctly oriented toward meat-eaters.

thankfully it's super cheap.  Roti + a drink was $6.26 with tax.

This place has completely changed my campus dining experience. After six years of eating the same old thing i was in desperate need of something new. With fresh, organic, spicy, and affordable food, Urbann Turbann truly delivers.

An extra bonus: The owners (a husband and wife team) and their staff are super nice and are always willing to accommodate the customer.

My favorite: a brown rice bowl with 1/2 beef kabob and veggies, followed by a mango lassi. 

The chai's also fantastic.

Like all the other reviews said, this is basically an Indian version of Chipotle. 

I like Chipotle: big burritos, fresh, fast, tasty if not authentic.

I like Indian food.

Why not combine the two?

The combination works for me. It might not work for you, but it's worth a try to see. The abysmal selection of decent lunch spots on North Side only makes this place even more welcome. A bonus: payment is nearly instant with a credit card, no signature required. Portions are large. $7 for my very filling wrap is a good deal.

I wish I had pre-planned my meal here by at least looking up the menu beforehand.

I was STARVING when I stumbled in here and ordered sporadically from the menu without really seeing all my options.

Ended up with a naan wrap containing all the veggies and chicken tandoori with no chutney. (I have a palette for bland foods)

The naan was chewy but I wish it was more doughy and overall, the flavors complemented each other well (the chicken wasn't too spicy or salty for me). My biggest complaint is that the chicken was dry but that could've been my fault for not adding any chutney.

In any case, the service was great and the cashier tossed in some recommended sauces which he said would enhance the flavor.

Urbann turbann, I love you. You are the chipotle of Indian food with that exclusivity for you are only located in Berkeley, to my knowledge. You were closed for too long during the winter holidays. I love Indian food and you managed to make it easy to eat on the go. Perfect and ingenious business model. 

Butter chicken, habanero chutney, add that coconut goodness too. Yea, that is all. Quick trick, to get extra you ask for the potatoes, meat, then extra potatoes so you don't get skimped on the meat. You're welcome.

So good!!! Quick, friendly service, and they don't skimp with the toppings, unlike Chipotle. 

You can ask for half-half meat options, so get half butter chicken and half something else. The potatoes are delish. 

The naan was good but not overpowering or crammed, unlike the giant tortilla wads you see at the bottom of typical burritos. 

Get the chutneys, because it'll be a little dry without. 

Only like 4 tiny tables, so expect to get it to-go, or just hope to be lucky.

Okay. Whoever thought of this...deserves mad, mad props.

I mean come on. Indian food. IN A NAAN-RITO. Must have been some tandoori god come down from culinary heaven. And on the fourth day, there was pork vindaloo. And it was good.

Of course, there are some tiny nits to pick. I wish the naan was thicker and more full-bodied, and it got a little soggy towards the end of my Urbann experience. If you're going to have naan, why not have garlic naan (a tiny change but more delicious) or chapatis? I also sort of wish that there were naan-cos (naan tacos) and naan-chiladas. Maybe even a naan-edilla (With or without paneer? Another pressing question!) There are so many possibilities that could be realized here.

The space is always bumping good music and the workers are very friendly. With plenty of options for vegetarians etc., this almost has me wishing I had moved to Berkeley. If they add some naan-chiladas to their menu, I just might.

I love everything about this place, except for the lack of seating availability.

The food is fresh, tasty, and satisfying.  They give you a lot more meat/beans than Chipotle.  The flavors from the seasoning are distinct and unique, but not overwhelming.  A lot of fusion restaurants tend to be a bland version of the original food, but I feel like Urbann Turbann retains authentic Indian cooking while transforming it to an American format.

I had a roti wrap with garbonzo beans, which was okay.  It was on the cold side, but I guess that's expected since most people have the butter chicken.  It was still very good, and probably the best food you could get with $5.50.  I had it with the tamarind sauce, which was sweet and went well with the wrap.   

Service was good; the people were friendly and the place was clean.

I admire that their menu prices actually include tax.  Most places do not, so something that's $8 on the menu ends up being $11 with tax and tip.

I want to come back and try everything else on their menu!

This is basically the Indian version of Chipotle!  

The butter chicken and tandoori chicken are both delicious, and I ended up getting both in my naan "burrito". This would have been a 4-star review if my naan hadn't gotten super soggy and nasty by the time I reached the bottom of my wrap.

While the minimalist Indian wall décor contrasts sharply with the SportsCenter telecast on the big screen TV, the rest of interior is unremarkable. Depending on the day, the storefront may accommodate as many as five seats and two tables. Judging by the line of patrons that often stretches out the door and onto the sidewalk at high noon, we can only conclude that Urbann Turbann (UT) is not a dine-in establishment. What UT lacks in ambiance, however, it compensates for in speedy service, with meal latencies rarely exceeding five minutes, even under the pressures of peak, mid-day volume. UT achieves high throughput by reducing the fine art of rice-bowl and wrap preparation into an assembly line integrating interchangeable curry, vegetable, and garnish components.

Most of the kitchen is in plain view, but is strategically shielded from the untoward sneeze of a sick patron by thick plates of Plexiglas. Our careful, albeit brief, examination of the kitchen area yielded no red flags. We were pleased to find that UT exclusively uses compostable containers, utensils, and cups.

The menu breaks down into the two broad subcategories of wrap and rice bowl. Wraps may be constructed from a naan or roti foundation, whereas white or brown rice may form the base of a bowl. A superstructure may be constructed from meat- or vegetable-based curries with a choice of fresh vegetables (greens, cucumber, tomato, onion), with garnishes to top it off. The vegetarian eigendish, a roti wrap with a chickpea curry, fresh veggies, diced jalapenos, and spicy red sauce ($7), performed admirably and was decently spicy, especially for a fast food joint. Not only was the wrap filling, but the fresh veggies also provided at least the appearance of healthfulness. The meat-containing eigendish, a naan wrap with chicken vindaloo, fresh veggies, diced jalapenos and a mildly sweet tamarind sauce ($7), also receives high marks, particularly for the sauce. While we commend UT for stuffing each wrap to maximum capacity, the poor tensile strength of naan and roti, particularly when wet, leads to premature fragmentation of the wrap all too often. Indeed, for those who prefer large quantities of sauce, we highly recommend a rice bowl instead of a wrap to minimize the risk of meal failure.

Overall, UT excels in providing rapid service, a clean environment, comparatively healthy options, and large portions, making it an ideal choice for lunch and well deserving of four samosas. UT's modest prices warrant a single rupee, resulting in a very high samosa-to-rupee ratio (4.0). Thus, while UT bills itself as Indian fast food, we think the term "good food quickly" is more appropriate.
Tastes great. The butter chicken is my favorite and the vegetables they use are delicious.

I avoided urb turb for a while because the line is always so long, but I finally decided to wait and I was well rewarded.  The line actually moves very fast and since it's an assembly line you get your food as soon as you're out of line.  Lot's of people are calling this the Indian Chipotle, which would be true if Chipotle made their tortillas fresh to order (yes the nann at urb urb are rolled out and baked fresh as you wait!), and if Chipotle had more vegetarian options than just sauteed bell peppers (the mushroom and peas at urb are amazing!).

The restaurant is a concept that I have long believed would be successful, has finally come into fruition: A restauarant that wraps South Asian curries in naan or roti. Essentially, curry burritos to make Indian food fast food.

I found this restaurant by accident. I happened to be on the north side of Berkeley's campus, which I rarely am, and saw the joint while I was looking for a place to pick up food. Curry wraps are an idea I have had for a long time, so I was more than glad to try this place out when I saw it.

 I walked in and there was no line. (This is probably because the school year is not in session). Anyhow, restaurant serving process is akin to what you would find at a Subway or Chipotle. You choose your bread (naan or roti), then choose your curry, then get to add vegetables and chutneys optionally. (Masru (i.e. Indian yogurt) costs extra in your wrap.)

The chief asset of this type of restaurant is that it is supposed to make Indian food a non-messy fast food option. This is great if it fulfills that goal. However, the restaurant had some problems. First, the service was not that fast. Second, the naan was not that tightly wrapped so it could become messy if I was really in a go. Third, even though they are a fast food place, it would be nice if they had some seating area.

But despite those criticisms, it is a pretty good place to hit up. I ordered pork vindaloo, which was good enough for fast food. The service was friendly and courteous. For example, the worker did not like the quality of naan he was about to use for my wrap, so he decided to make a new one, which took longer. (Personally, I thought the naan looked fine. I didn't mind the small burned portions, that's part of what you expect with naan.) The employees were also friendly and willing to strike up conversations. They told me they opened up last monday, so they are very brand new. Also, they have a "curry" called "cholay". I told them they should call it the "Sholay Cholay" in honor of the 1970s Bollywood megahit.

Anyhow, here is some advice on how the restaurant could improve. First, they need to get a device that allows them to cook several naan at a time in advance. They should have five available freshly cooked naan and 5 roti at any given time to be ready for customers, given their primary differentiation from other Indian restaurants is that they are supposed to be fast. Second, I would add the option of chapatis instead of just rotis and naan for the wraps. Third, they should reverse the direction of the "assembly line". Customers have to go all the way to the other side of the restaurant to start their order. The assembly line should start near the door and the cash register should be at the other end. Fourth, they need to figure out a better way to wrap the food. While they do a reasonably admirable job, there could be improvement. They could either increase the size of the bread so that it is more all to wrap all the contents like a burrito. Another option is to reduce the amount of curries and vegetables they put into wrap. Fifth, and this may not be something they can do immediately because of the space they have, but at least have a table or two in restaurant or the sidewalk. 

All that said, this is wonderful concept and the owners (who I believe also are the servers) sincerely into the idea. I hope them much success and I hope these comments help them improve. Please eat here. It is worth it at least once.

Urbann Turbann is pretty much a healthier, fresher Indian version of Chipotle.

I got their Seekh kabob (beef) wrapped with roti. The flavor of the beef kabob was pretty good, but it was a tad dry. The roti was chewy, but not as chewy as the naan. I loooove the potatoes they put in the wrap. It's well seasoned and cooked just right. 

I personally like their sweet tamarind sauce.

I tried my friend's tandoori chicken naan wrap too. The chicken is tender and not dry. The naan is very chewy and flavorful. I'm definitely getting the naan next time I come here. 

The price is reasonable. I paid $7 for my beef roti wrap and that's enough for two light meals for me. The wraps are a tad smaller than a chipotle burrito though.

It's like chipotle but with Indian food! Also, workers aren't creeps, portions are huge, and the ingredients are pretty fresh (freshly made naan!) 

I had a naan wrap with the spicy kabob. It was amazing. They put so much food in your wrap. I also had one of the samosas. When I first had the samosas, it was amazing. Super fresh, super tasty. I went later that day because my friends wanted to try urbann turbann and the samosas were definitely not as good. You have to get them when they're fresh to get the most out of them. 

But overall, would definitely eat here again. Really good place, great idea for a restaurant too.

What a great idea for a restaurant! 

Not all the flavor combinations are completely sound (like at Chipotle), so it will take some experimentation on my part to find something great here.

Solid 4 stars, good for togo, great as left overs, great service.  I think it is really hard to give Urban Turbann 5 stars because there are way too many Indian Food around Berkeley. I do like house of curry more, but this is the place to go for togo Indian food on north side.

I love Indian food and I love burritos so I assumed this would be my kind of place. This first time, it was....but I have to admit it has gone down hill every time I go. 
There website is down on and off always. 
The guy wrapping the burrito the last 2 times should have been elsewhere on the assembly line because he could not wrap burritos to save his life and instead of grabbing a new nan and trying again he just threw it in a box.
 I still long for my first experience here and always hope that the next time I go will be amazing, but I am about to give up.

I love the concept of gourmet Indian Burrito and their food is excellent.  Although the first time I visited this establishment my server seemed stoned or have bad short-term memory

Server: What can I get for you
Me: I'd like a kabob burrito please

S: [grabbed naan but seemed to blank out for 10 seconds] what filling do you want
M: beef kabob

S: [puts beef on naan] do you want rice?
M: yes rice and all the vegetables

S: [adds rice] do you want lettuce?
M: yes, and all the vegetables

S: [adds lettuce] do you want tomatoes?
M: yes, and cucumbers and red onions and cilantro

S: [adds tomatoes] do you want cucumbers?

... 5 minutes later ...

S: do you want chutney?
M: yes, tamarind and mint chutney

S: we don't have tamarind chutney
Casher: yes we do, the chutney is in the little sauce cups

S: [adds tamarind chutney] do you want another kind of chutney
M: yes mint please

Despite the whole process taking a long time, I do like their kabob in a naan burrito

It didn't take much prodding to get me to try this place out. 

The four F's come to mind when I think of Urbann Turbann:

* Fresh ingredients
* Flavorful curries
* Fast service
* Fair prices

I got the naan wrap with butter chicken (tikka masala) and added all the veggies, topped with the mint and tamarind chutney. Now, while the flavors were great, the wrap itself was soggy because of all the excess liquid. I wouldn't recommend getting a wrap unless you're going to eat it within 50 yards of the restaurant, and within 3 minutes.

Yes, some people call it the Indian Chipotle, but this is really something else, altogether. It's definitely worth a try, and a re-visit. For $9, I got my wrap and two samosas.

The only drawback is that you can get a buffet meal at other places for about the same price. If you're really into AYCE basmati and curries, then this isn't for you. but if you're looking for something different, and would like some real flavor in your food, swing by Urbann Turbann. The size of the wrap is about equivalent to two trips through a buffet line, so enjoy!
Another Indian Chipotle.  What's not to love?

I've only had it once, and I'm not sure how I feel about it. The prospect of an Indianized burrito is exciting, but the execution feels a little off. One thing that Chipotle does so well is to make their burritos large yet still manageable. The wrap I got at Urbann Turbann (on a wheat wrap, not naan) was bursting at the seems.

Younger me would have been really excited for the extra food, but it kind of just seemed like overkill, and it was pretty messy. 

I am also unconvinced that Indian flavors are generic enough such that you can slap on any sauces you want.

I ordered the naan with butter chicken with mild coconut. They put the shredded coconut in a corner and I ate all of it in one bite but no big deal. The naan was fluffy and much better than the flour wrap at Chipotle. It's a bit pricey, $7.50, but I'll go back when I find myself in North side again because it's just a quick 1 min uphill walk from North Gate. The portion size is just right and it's very filling. I think the little brown bag they give you to put the wrap in is adorable. 

There's no outside seating and if you go to nearby restaurants for their outdoors seating, they'll ask you to leave. Go to Memorial Glade or Qualcomms to sit down and enjoy your wrap!

i'm reviewing this place right now because i am dreaming of you, naan burrito...naanrrito, and the enormous food baby you impregnated me with.

I lovveE the endless combination possibilities that surpass those of chipotle. plus it's indian style, so i might even argue you are better than chipotle because i would have curry alll day every day if i could.

My roommate (Eugene B. below) and i came here and left with a food coma that truly did last 6 hours. we always talk about coming back here and we hope that next time i can have you with some samosas because last time they were sold out!!!!!!   

MMM can't wait to come again!

I had heard of this place opening around a year ago, but didn't really realize what it was. Then when a friend told me it was Chipotle with naan burritos and Indian food, I was instantly down to try it out. Turns out that I LOVE this new style of food!

Brags (+): You can get exactly what you want, and there are a huge number of ingredients so the permutations are endless. They slabbed on a whopping portion of butter chicken and potatoes, and stuffed the whole thing full of onion, tomato, cilantro, lettuce and chutney. Being able to choose what you want is perfect, and I think all of my ingredients meshed well with the creamy butter chicken. The final creation was HUGE and I was definitely struggling to finish the whole thing, which I don't often say for a single serving portion of food. At $7.50 even, I'd say it's a pretty good deal.

Beats (-): I got some spicy ingredients (hot peppers, fiery tomato chutney, and I think they claimed the butter chicken was spicy also) but I did not register anything on the hot-o-meter. Spiciness is something I definitely look for in my Indian food... so that was slightly disappointing. Oh, and they wrapped the foil so that the foil edges were opposing each other, so it was kind of hard to open without ripping all of the foil apart like a barbarian. #firstworldproblems

Variance (~): The wrap wasn't too well-mixed. Homogeneity is something I enjoy, and I don't particularly like it when one bite is pure chicken and the next is a mouthful of lettuce. But YMMV and some people enjoy the different taste of each bite, and I'm sure I could ask them next time to mix it up a bit.

The "burritos" are either wrapped in na'an and roti and they're freaking DELICIOUS. I got a half tandoori chicken/half butter chicken and it was perfect. It's easily 2 meals for $7.50. 

Whoever came up with this: you're a freaking genius.

Dear Urbann Turbann,

Your wraps are delectable, but your hours are unobtainable
Because your website is down, we have to leave town
 Without enjoying the naan-wich and paneer

I quite liked the food and thought I'd come again if I were on Northside.

Service: It operates like Chipotle, except with Indian food. Service is fast and they're usually pretty nice.

Food: I usually get the Tandoori Chicken and put all the toppings in it, which included rice, cucumbers, tomatoes, etc. It actually doesn't come up to be as massive as everyone seems to make it out to be, and I could've easily eaten another after the serving. But I found the flavors to be quite nice, and it was a delight to eat it. I think the price is right for the food, as well.

I stand by the same comments posted in my last review, but just had to give a quick update!

Today was such a sad, dreary day that I was craving something warm and spicy to make me not feel bitter about trekking across campus in a rainstorm. 

I discovered something that is not on the menu--BUTTER CHICKEN! It was recommended to me by one of the staffers behind the counter. I got a white rice bowl and paired the meat with the mild coconut + fiery tomato chutney (also recommended by the staff). It was delicious! The chicken was tender and smooth and the chutney and jalepenos warmed me up today.

I love how $7 can get me lunch AND dinner here.

Here is my "substantive first-hand experience" with Urbann Turbann:

The Naan they served was cold, the chicken and potatoes were dry and not very flavorful, and they charge extra to put add a small little dollop of sauce. C'mon are you serious? 

First take, I would not return to this restaurant.

So , In the one year that I have spent here separated from home cooked Indian food I have tried almost every single Indian restaurant here , striving to find food that is authentic.

Urbann Turbann might seem to be a simple fast-food wrap joint , but it is A LOT MORE THAN THAT. 
I have had the Tandoori Chicken , Butter Chicken and the Seekh Kabob wraps ( with naan bread ) here and I must say that the quality of these wraps is GREAT. 

The Butter chicken is especially a favorite of mine , eaten either as a wrap or in a rice bowl.
If you are looking for authentic Indian tasting food , Urbann Turbann is the place.
The service is generally fast and hygienic. And I also like the fact that they always have NBA games on their TV.

As a student living on west side I had never heard of this place.  When I walked by for the first time earlier this semester I thought "What kind of restaurant spells urban and turban with two N's?" Basically, I wasn't sure whether this place was trustworthy. After reading all the amazing reviews, I finally decided to stop by after class (which ends at 5:30 in GSPP, what a trek home!). I must say, the food here was tasty. 

I was a little nervous ordering because I didn't know how the system worked, but the guy behind the counter was super-duper friendly and gave me lots of helpful suggestions. I decided to get a wrap with butter chicken, potatoes, and that mint-green-sauce-thing (clearly I don't really know Indian food that well). Mmmmm. Obviously there is more authentic Indian food elsewhere, but Urbann Turbann is the perfect place to grab some portable Indian food to go when you have the munchies. Also the portions are HUGE. I was starving and forced myself to finish an entire wrap in one sitting. I regret it. Food-baby lasted for a week.

Affordable, clean, great service, delicious. I will definitely return. Highly recommend!

I really wanted to like Urban Turban, but found myself very disappointed. I'm no Indian food expert, but I've had my fair share of it over the years and tried a lot of different restaurants. The best restaurant for comparison is probably Kasa in San Francisco, which likewise specializes in Indian wraps. Unfortunately, Turban simply doesn't seem to measure up to it's sibling across the Bay.

I will qualify my review by saying that I've only tried the Karahi Paneer. Perhaps some of the other fillings are better, but I'm pescetarian, so my options were already somewhat limited. The potatoes in the wrap were ok, but didn't strike me as anything particularly special. The Karahi Paneer, though, was a major letdown. This filling is my absolute favorite over at Kasa, so I had high hopes for finding a good source of it in Berkeley. The paneer was decent in itself, but the vegetables were not well cooked and the dish was not flavorful--it tasted like it had been made with bland tomato sauce. Also, the naan had clearly been sitting around for quite a while and was very soggy and rubbery, beyond what one would expect from it being used on a wrap with wet ingredients. Also, Turban doesn't do unda style, where an egg is fried onto the flat-bread--check minus! The addition of red onion, cilantro, mixed greens, sauces, etc. was unable to rescue my wrap. It's true that they don't skimp on the portions. But when I have Indian, I expect some spice and flavor, so Turban's large portions were more of a liability than an asset.

Add to this the fact that when I arrived, they were out of the Karahi Paneer. Since Turban claims to be about speed, having to wait an extra ten minutes for them to cook up the dish was a bit off-putting. Nevertheless, they did allow me to jump the queue when the paneer was ready, which was nice, and overall the staff were very nice and helpful.

Bottom line: Urban Turban is a good idea with mediocre execution. For better Indian head to Biryani House, or better yet, Vik's; for better Indian wraps, check out Kasa when you're in SF.

I gave this place another go, as the owner wrote me a personal email about why the food tasted the way it did that day. 

After trying the naan wrap again I was surprised that it was actually pretty good. Especially the fresh naan, cooked the traditional way. I like the choice of sauces too. 
But for some reason, I cannot get myself to give it a four stars. This is the first review I have felt so unsure about, it seems lie a hit or miss.

The next time I go I will have a definitive opinion.

I just came here the other day having heard of this place as the Indian Chipotle. Now I'm a fan of Chipotle AND Indian food so I thought I would try this place out. 

I got the naan wrap with the butter chicken and potatoes. The potatoes and chicken were amazing, although I was very conflicted! Should I have gotten the tandoori chicken instead? Both looked super good. I got my fair share of potatoes and some samosas, which by the way, they rock for not charging me for the two samosas I added on having bought three wraps! The samosas were a bit small but very fluffy with a crisp shell and soft filling of potatoes and peas. For me, I'm quite particular about my sauces so I asked them not to put any in my wrap but on the side. I would highly suggest that so you can try the two without it ruining your entire meal if you dislike the tamarind or the mint cilantro. 

Overall, this place was fantastic. Although, I don't know if it is worth $7 for the wrap. I feel I get my fatty on better for that same price at Chipotle.

I've never even thought this kind of place was possible. It's like chipotle except with Indian food, LOVE IT! Prices are decent too..I ordered a na'an wrap with buttered chicken and all the veggies and it was around $9. It was huge too! Probably around the same size as a chipotle burrito.

I spilt a paneer wrap from Urbann Turbann on a recent afternoon.  Turbann's wrap customization is nice, and the final product was satisfying.

Knocks: The person behind the counter was fairly slow and not terribly helpful with my order.  Also, the roti was inextricably tied into the aluminum foil insulating the wrap.  Unrolling the wrap was a lot like performing brain surgery, and I lost a bit of the wrap in the process.

After seeing the string of new restaurants opening on Euclid, I was intrigued by Urbann Turbann, which, as someone else had said, was like an Indian Chipotle. I decided to get the roti wrap with cholay (spiced garbanzo beans), potatoes masala, cucumbers, cilantro, tamarind chutney, and habanero-cumin tomato chutney. Along with a mango lassi (mango, yogurt, rosewater), my total was $7.50. Not bad, since (excluding drinks), the meal would be cheaper than at Chipotle. 

I thought the food was only mediocre. (Though it could have been my choice of the fillings.) The roti wrap tasted a bit grainy and perhaps a bit stale, not chewy and springy like all good bread should be. The fillings and chutneys were not bad, but I felt the flavor the spices were very one-dimensional and lacking complexity. I tasted mostly cumin. On the mango lassi, I thought it was too sweet. It almost tastes as if they used Kern's nectar or something. It definitely needs more mango and less sugar. Considering that this is only a fast food restaurant, I give it three stars.

Definitely agree with what people have said about this place being like an Indian Chipotle. I had the pork vindaloo wrap with the tamarind and the spicy cilantro chutney and it was really good and made me incredibly full. 

This place has good Indian food in the same way Chipotle has good burritos that aren't quite real burritos. I wouldn't go here looking for the most authentic Indian dishes, but its the place to go for your Indian burrito fix.

Urbann Turbann is a solid four stars. I've only gotten naan wraps here, so I can't comment on the roti or basmati rice bowl options. The naan is fresh as I saw someone making them with the tandoor oven by the cash register. lol The naan is soft and fluffy, perfect for wrapping. 

As many other reviewers have stated, Urbann Turbann serves up their food Chipotle/taqueria style. You can choose what you want and see them put your food together. You pick a main filling and can add on any veggies you want + chutney. 

The first time I chose to have the pork vindaloo as my filling. The wrap was huge, and the pork was cooked perfectly and super flavorful. I decided that the masala potatoes weren't contributing anything positive to the wrap. They were pretty bland and just made me more stuffed than I should probably be. 

The second time I tried the seekh kabob and opted out of adding any potatoes. The amount of meat they gave seemed significantly less than when I had the pork vindaloo, they give you like three pieces of kebab vs. a huge scoop of the pork. It was still a good amount of meat for me though, and I found it to be quite delish. I could really taste all the different spices they used.  

Both times, the veggies I added in all looked and tasted fresh. I've tried the hot mint cilantro and fiery tomato, habanero, and cumin chutneys. They didn't taste particular spicy to me, it might have been due to the fact that they don't give you very much (a small spoonful for a huge wrap). I will definitely ask if they can give me more chutney next time to see if the flavors can actually shine through. 

I give Urbann Turbann props for bringing something interesting and different to the northside Berk dining scene.

I really really wanted to like this place, since the concept sounds great. I ordered the pork vindaloo in a naan wrap with potatoes, lettuce, coconut and cilantro toppings. The first half of my wrap would be 5 stars with juicy, perfectly spiced vindaloo. But then I got to the second half, and the pork was ridiculously dry, as if all the wonderful juices evaporated. It was so dry that it became hard to finish and I eventually gave up. I pushed the pork to the side and tore the naan, eating it the traditional style with the other toppings.

Portion was good, price was a bit pricer, but I still can't get over the dry ass pork. I would try this place again and order something else.

This place has quickly become my favorite lunch place near campus. The ingredients are fresh. The service is fast, friendly, and served with a smile. You can tell the people that work there really care about making you the very best meal. They will make suggestions and listen to yours. They are very good about customizing your meal the way you want. Do you love mango chutney? They'll add extra. More rice? Yes sir! They have seating inside but I usually like to head back to campus and sit on the lawn. Writing this review makes me look forward to lunch. Welcome to the neighborhood Urbann Turbann!

I'll be brief: I REALLY LIKE THIS PLACE.
Tried the butter chicken on both basmati and brown rice, tried different chutneys (hot mint with cilantro, mild coconut, can't remember now but others), and the much-raved-about mango lassi. NO REGRETS. I know credibility kind of lessens when someone uses caps lock and trust me, I try to avoid using it, but.... YOU MUST UNDERSTAND HOW AGGRESSIVELY I LIKE THIS PLACE. 
Flavorful, filling, generous portions, delicious chicken, good prices (except for the mango lassi; wish it were cheaper), and fresh fresh fresh. I usually can't finish the meal in one go unless I'm super hungry, so I end up taking it home and reheating it for the next meal in the microwave. Nuke that good stuff and it's STILL delicious (in my opinion). I haven't tried it naan/burrito style, only bowl - maybe it's because I'm lazy to deal with the potential mess, or I don't want to hold it up - but someday. Someday burrito style will happen. :) The mango lassi is creamy and yummy! First time I tried lassi was here, and I'm glad I tried it.

If this place were in South Side, I'd go way too often.

The Indian Chipotle! (note: I am not a fan of Chipotle though)

I've been meaning to try it for a while but never wanted to trek up to Northside - totally worth it! The curry is really flavorful, and the selection of organic produce and yummy chutney complements it well.

I got the butter chicken wrapped in naan, with potatoes (my favorite part!), cilantro, cucumbers (also my favorite), and coconut chutney.  I can't eat spicy, so I was really glad that they had mild options.

Yup, the owners of Urbann Turbann followed a successful, well loved, fast food model (Chipotle) and put an agreeable ethnic twist to it.  
Everything from the ordering process to the relatively simple menu, the assembly line on-demand preparation, and the organic & sustainable ingredients pledge fulfill a nice niche in the UC Campus Northside eatery choices.

I went out to lunch with a friend and ordered the naan + tandoori chicken + tamarind sauce + all vegetables imaginable!  It was gooood.  Felt really fresh too.  I loved how the workers rolled out the dough and made naan as you ordered.  Did I mention how much I love naan?  No?  Well I do!

My friend ordered the pork vindaloo.  Usually vindaloo is unbearably spicy and too much for me to handle, but this time, the pork was shredded to a barbacoa texture and flavored with the right amount of spice.  I think I'll try that one next time!

Like others said, you better watch out for sauce dripping out of the wrap as you eat.  It ruined my pants :(

Indian food wrapped in Naan. This place is the 'chipotle' of indian burritos. You decide exactly what goes into your burrito on an assembly line system 

The price is right and the place is fast, clean, convenient, and just good. The pork vindaloo is quite good, and is like an Indian version of barbacoa.

My boyfriend and really love Indian food and both were intrigued by the concept, very clever! 

So instead of going to our regular Pizza and Curry we had decided to try something new and make a trip to Berkeley! 

We get there paid $18 for two wraps, a fountain drink and a chai tea. The wraps were HUGE, nicely portioned. However there were chicken bone(s) in both of our wraps. An absolute turn off, ended up throwing almost one full wrap and another half wrap away, what a waste of money =/

The tandoori wrap was dry and not that flavorful (a true crime against Indian food) So I would definitely not recommend that (or this place at all, but maybe it was a bad day?). The butter chicken was better, had better flavor wasn't as dry but still not good enough to make another trip down there. Would have liked some more tamarind sauce, when I asked if it cost extra she said no so I would suggest you get some extra on the side just in case! (=

 The girl helping me was pretty helpful however the girl helping my bf was (apparently) snobby.

Limited space, was lucky enough to grab a table before the rush (ate around 5)!

The tea is not something I will judge them on because it is all personal preference.  It was definitely more of a spicy chai, where I personally like the sweeter chais. So if you are like me I would advise against the chai tea.

Side note: Had the fiery tomato sauce with the tandoori and it was not spicy at all (this coming from someone who has a hard time eating hot cheetos half the time)

This was unfortunately not a very good expierence for my boyfriend and I so we won't be coming here anytime soon (or at all)..but at least we got to go out for ice cream afterwards! (=

Indian food in a naan burrito? Yesyesyes please. 

This goes against everything that I stand for but nevertheless, here it is: I'd actually recommend the vegetarian option. Specifically the MUSHROOM MATTAR. 

The mushrooms and the snow peas soak up all the wonderful spices and creamy flavors and makes for a rich, moist, extremely savory wrap stuffing, whereas the chicken tends to be more dry and under-seasoned. Even with my wrap drenched in different chutneys, the mushroom matter held its own. Sadly, my buttery doughy naan couldn't quite keep up with the sheer force of everyflavorpossible inside and disintegrated a little near the end. Literally, a finger-lickin' good experience!
 
The bad: the fruit lassi. SO THICK and yogurty and bland and not even cold! As I struggled to suck up the lassi through my straw, I wistfully thought of the mango lassi at Vik's. Oh well.

Get the vegetarian, skip the lassi, ask for chutney recs, and don't forget the extra napkins!

Since my last review the place has really grow on me, and it really does seem like they're giving out more portions (meat usually overflows the naan wrap. PERFECT!). But, more importantly, this place is now officially good luck. Just took MCB C100A, a class with 3 midterms. 

- First MT: No Urbann beforehand. Scored half a standard below. Queue panic and nightmares of being rejected from every single grad school program I apply to.
- Second MT: Happened to have Urbann before. 1.5 stds above. Hmm, studied less but did better, I wonder why? Maybe It was Urbann. I'll get it anyways because it's tasty!
- Third MT: Tried getting Urbann before. 1.5 stds above, again. I think I'm onto something!!
- Final: Urbann before. 1.5 stds above... finalizing my transformation from getting a B- to getting a solid A. It HAS to be the food!

This also happened to my friend Hanson Z. So with this large of a sample size you know it's basically proven.

Thanks Urbann!

Food & Drinks: Naans and meats were freshly made from a small tandoor in the back. While it looked delicious, the food tasted unremarkable. The tandoori chicken was dry, and the combination of chutneys and vegetables clashed in flavor. You finish your meals feeling full but not satisfied. However, kudos for the price ($7 with all prices listed post-tax) and gastronomic novelty.

Atmosphere & location: Very Chipotle-esque. Urbann Turbann only has a few tables, a restaurant meant for fast service. I felt cramped along my friend, but at such close proximity to the Berkeley campus, I can't complain. 

Service & People: Quick, easy and elementary. Your food is made à la assembly line. 

Overall Recommendation: Acceptable as a quick meal/foodie discovery but not as a returning experience. In other words, try Urbann Turbann once but not twice.

Urbann Turbann is a new restaurant that just opened up last week near U.C. Berkeley.  It is tailored towards students on the go as there is nowhere to sit down inside or outside nearby.  You just get in line and get your Indian wrap or rice bowl, for about $6 or $7.  

The food is quite good, tastes fresh, and is definitely filling.  The food is also very unique--it's essentially Indian burritos.   

You can get naan or roti for the wrap or a basmati rice bowl, add masala potatoes, and then a filling of vegetables or meat.  I'm impressed--they actually slow roast their pork for over two hours.  
The meat is all free-range, organic, and from local farms.  You can then add fresh produce, which is also all organic.  Finally, they have some chutney (sauces) to add, which are quite good.  

I definitely recommend it, if you are looking to grab a quick bite near Berkeley campus.

Opened a few days ago and one of the new spots in North Berkeley.

Think of it as an Indian Chipotle. Same system where you order a wrap or a rice bowl. The basmati rice seemed a bit overcooked and they forgot to add the peas. The girl forgot and as she was pushing my plate down, I asked her to add some vegetables. She told me "please tell me before I move it down." I didn't respond, but I thought it was kind of rude that she felt it was necessary to state that when she was at fault. And they just opened. Where did customer service go? Everyone else was really friendly though.

You can choose between chicken, a beef kabob, and pork meats with lettuce, tomatoes, and chili peppers. There were different sauces available and I got a mild coconut mix and tried the sweet tamarin (don't quote me) sauce. Like I said, really similar to Chipotle, but Indian style. There were even $1 samosas - like chips on the side you know? Pretty good, but remember, it's fast food-like.

You can get chai tea for $2.50 and mango lassi as well. With my basmati brown rice without the peas and a samosa, my total came out to $8 even. For the time and price, I give it 3.5.

I'm a fan.  Love the bright, airy space, the cool turban'd sardars with the handlebar mustaches and, most importantly, it's flavorful, filling, not too expensive and fast.  Definitely a welcome addition to the North Side.  It's in my regular eating out rotation!

TIP #1: Portion sizes are HUGE. Be sure to ask whoever's making your wrap to cut it in half for you. They're even kind enough to wrap each separately in foil after cutting. 

TIP #2: You can ask for half and half of the fillings--for example, half chicken, half chickpeas. Great for if you want a variety of textures and flavors in your wrap. They average out the price if one is more expensive than the other. 

TIP #3: Don't be afraid to ask what the different sauces are, or what flavors go well together. The people who work there are knowledgeable and patient.

Imagine your standard-sized naan from House of Curries, stuff it with potatoes, chicken, beans, sauces, what have you, and wrap it all up. Delicious, hot, spicy if you so choose, filling, and satisfying! Flavors are spot on. Choose roti over naan if you want a healthier wrap. 

If you're on the fence, try it at least once, because it's an interesting twist AND it tastes good. If you're on Northside but you crave House of Curries or Naan and Curry, try Urbann Turbann. One other perk is that it's portable, so no need to fret if the limited number of tables at the restaurant are full--cross the street and eat your wrap on Memorial Glade.

Urbann Turbann, I knew I'd fall in love with you the moment I saw your opening. 

And now, finally after months since you have opened, I have come in.

And fallen in love.

Today, for dinner, (seirously, just an hour ago) got Urbann Turbann with a friend. The guy with the big hoop earrings is so nice and helpful and accommodating! He let me try the mushroom peas thing, let me get a wrap, but with the naan on the side and all the fillings in a container! You can put two different fillings, plus the masala potatoes for only $7! Trust me, it's enough for 2 meals. I got seriously full even before reaching halfway. The naan may be even huger than the ones at the Indian restaurants around here.

KARAHI PANEER: yummy, light, refreshing. Loads of bell peppers and onions. Pretty good, but gotta say that the...
MUSHROOM MATTAR: was the steal. Very hearty tasting despite being meat-free. Delish delish delish. Smoky, warming.
MASALA POTATOES: creamy and tasty

The tamarind chutney is great for dipping with naan. The coconut chutney is almost like a dessert! Pairs well with anything it seems, as its flavor isn't too overpowering. The really spicy red sauce (actually not too spicy, I just forgot the name) was yummy too. Not too spicy that it masked the food's flavor.

Other Plusses: as much organic produce as you could want to pile on top of your wrap or rice bowl, natural meats, freshhh. Authentic tasting (at least to an Asian who's eaten at a Vik's, Naan'n'Curry, Curry House, Tandor Express). Compostable material, Chutneys in mini to-go containers, $1 samosas, flat screen TV. Tip jar going to charity is an awesome thing they do.

If I wasn't so stingy a college student, I'd go here every week. I'll definitely have to come back and try the butter chicken (tandoori chicken plus cream sauce, yum sounding right?).

You reading this, go here NOW.

What's the most politically incorrect name for a restaurant in Berkeley?

Despite the name, I am very thankful that Urbann Turbann has filled part of the void of empty storefronts on Euclid Avenue. I went in on Saturday for their sort of soft opening when they were giving free samples to those who came in for lunch. By free sample, I don't mean a couple skimpy pieces of tandori chicken, but a full wrap or rice bowl. That's very generous. 

Given the space and their limitations of college student food, I was impressed with their options. You choose between a naan wrap, roti wrap or rice bowl. Then add your filling (choices of garbanzo beans, tandori chicken, paneer, cumin beer and a couple other vegan options. Then add your veggies and your sauces. It's a Chipotle style operation in that respect I suppose.

The staff were all very friendly and explained the menu and concept of the restaurant thoroughly. The roti was a little chewy and the tandori chicken was slightly dry, but they had an excellent roti and a spicy mint cilantro sauce that infused my wrap with quite a bit of flavor. I was impressed by this, and even more impressed by the portion size.

In total, the price for a wrap was somewhere around $7 if they had not been free that afternoon. It's nice to know there are now more options on Euclid.

I was brought here by a friend who teaches at UCB and I must say I was impressed by the concept and execution.  Naan and roti are always fresh from the tandoors so you know you are in for a treat.

Many people are discounting the authenticity of this food.  But in my opinion this food is as close to real home cooked Indian food as it gets.  The cholay is an especially wonderful mix of spices that the chef has taken time to procure.  Another reviewer very ignorantly stated that the food is spiced down for the american crowd, I would say that it is spiced down for the Indian crowd.  Many restaurants will just load up on chili and onions because they are cheap and easy to  find.  That's probably why so many people equate spicy Indian food as authentic Indian food, but that is not the case, especially when it comes to northern Indian mughlai style food (the type of food served from Delhi through punjab and parts of Pakistan).  Mughlai cooking focuses on rich complex flavors and local ingredients, the type of food you will find here at the Urbann Turbann.  I prefer their food to some of the supposed authentic restaurants in the area ( naan n curry, biryani house etc)  They do however stray from tradition by serving pork, but the pork at Urbann Turbann is delicious and the meat goes quite well with the Indian flavors.



Highly recommended.

I use to make fun of this "Urban Turban" name. However, when I realized the ingenious idea that this restaurant was..I was blown away.

INDIAN FOOD CHIPOTLE STYLE?
so down, soooooooooooooo down.

I don't even remember what I had just know this: all the good Indian things wrapped in a delicious soft yummy naan!!!

SO good, will be back. Although I do believe 7.50 was a bit too much and hence the 4 stars, nevertheless it was still really good!

Speedy, perfect when you need to stop by somewhere quick for lunch. Love their butter chicken wrap, you can mix it up and put other meat options but I usually like to keep it plain. 
I would opt out of the potatoes, it takes up space and it was a little too bland and overcooked. 

I love how its like 'chiptole' style, you get to add whatever toppings you want and sauce. And the sauce are delicious: go with the cilantro and the yogurt sauce (gives a hint of tang and lots of flavor). 

Also their naans are pretty fresh, you can see them making it right there.

I lived at Foothill Dorms for my freshmen year at Berkeley, and if there was one place I would love to go to within extremely short distance, it was Urbann Turbann. A little bit on the expensive side for food, but the portions are so huge, you could probably replace two meals with one Naan Wrap.

Like everyone says, it is a Indian Food Style Chipotle. And they pull it off well. I really wish it got bigger and became a chain restaurant, but until then I am content with walking across campus for their wraps.

When I first went there, they wrapped the huge portions perfectly with a huge naan, but lately they've really failed on wrapping my food well, and it really falls apart after I've consumed half of the wrap. This makes me sad. Please please please try to find a new way to wrap the food, or make bigger, and better naans. 

Butter Chicken is a safe bet for first timers, but don't be afraid to try their other flavors, since they are all pretty delicious. 
Their sauces at the end are what can really make or break your wrap, but I've found in general they all taste great. Tamarind for sweetness, Habanero for the spice, and Cilantro for the herbiness type deal. 

Definitely recommending it. Tastes fantastic! Try it, it's pretty different from the other grease-filled thai or fried foods that litter all over Berkeley.

This place is bomb. It's like Chipotle but for Indian food.

Instead of tortilla, you have naan or rice bowl. 

Instead of barbacoa, carnitas, chicken, or steak, you have vindaloo, chicken curry, etc. 

Instead of salsa types, you have yogurt or cilantro toppings.

It's almost exactly like an indian food version of chipotle and i'd highly recommend it!!!

INDIAN CHIPOTLE. DON'T GET NO BETTER.


I got half butter chicken and half tandoori because I could and allll the fixings. Lol. I ate half and was pretty full. They are NOT stingy with meat and are hella nice when I told them it was my first time. 

The price is pretty good, if you eat half and save the other half for later.. Your meal consists of only 4 bucks.

Try this when you're visiting Berkeley.

Great concept, good food.

I've tried both the rice bowl and the wrap. I prefer the wrap - it's easier to eat, and for some reason I feel like I taste all of the flavors more than when I get the rice bowl. 

My sort-of "usual" (granted, I've been there like, three times) is the tandoori chicken with coconut mint and all of the vegetables in a naan wrap with potatoes. It is EXTREMELY filling and has a fresh taste to it. I like how simple it is to order what you want. 

The service is usually friendly and fast, and the price is reasonable ($7ish).

I like it, and I'll probably go again.

Even though I'm stuck in Etcheverry Hall most of the time, I tend not to eat out on North Side too much. I think that just might change now that I've tried Urbann Turbann. The concept of Chipotle with an Indian twist first seemed impossible to me, but is now nothing short of a dire urge. 

I ordered the naan wrap, with seekh (beef) kabob, tomatoes, cucmbers, red onions, cilanto, and mild coconut chutney. First of all, their naan is made fresh in house, and you can really taste it when you bit in. I had to wait a bit for my beef kabob, but I sure am glad I did. 

The kabob was made right in front of me, baked on skewers in a tandoor just behind the counter. Sadly, their tandoor is gas-powered and isn't too authentic, but having an actual tandoor in their kitchen would mean shipping it from halfway across the world. 

The veggies are all extremely fresh and you can really taste it from the first bite. The coconut chutney wasn't too sweet and I kind of wish they put more of it in there. 

In the end, I got my huge wrap for $7 and it took me a good half hour just to finish it. One thing that bothered me a bit is that the kabob was a bit spicy, but nothing as horrible as typical Indian food. Just a little bit of spice that I didn't really expect in the first place. Other than that, I hope to see Urbann Turbann thrive as a business and a part of the engineer-filled North Berkeley community.

indian food in a burrito? i love it!

came here with my Yelper friends Kevin J. and Connie C. today for lunch. i got the naan wrap with pork vidaloo and omg, it's so frickin good! be careful though because it could get messy. but seriously, i'm not a fan of burritos but i love indian burritos! they have a large selection of chicken, pork, beans and different kinds of sauces. the servings are huge and it was only $7. also, it's literally right across from north gate, so it's super convenient for people taking classes on the north side. 

finally, a good restaurant on north side :D

I love this place... especially the freshly made naans. And I always ask for extra spicy sauce, because what's indian food if it's not "burn going in and burn going out" spicy, right?? :)

1 star off for being kind of hard to eat... so don't come here wearing anything nice or white.

What a great addition to the Northside.  I had been avoiding this place for months due to it's lack of seating and fast-food feel.  But the word around campus persuaded my to try it out.  I shouldn't have waited so long.  I got a huge rice bowl with paneer and a mix of tamarind and Mint Cilantro chutney on recommendation from one of the employees.  So good.  and so inexpensive.  Will definitely be back.
Great place, easy to follow menu. Think Subway or Chipotle. The rice bowl is awesome, big portions, tasty ingredients, fresh... I am already planning on coming back.

Urbann Turbann, aka Indian Chipotle, I like you. A lot. 

I've tried butter chicken, chicken tandoori, and pork vindaloo. My personal favorite is chicken tandoori tho! The others always make my naan too wet, and as you keep eating, they get too creamy and salty, respectively. The brown sweet sauce, cilantro sauce, and chili sauces (if u want it spicy) are must get. Samosas are okay (only $1 ea) and they come with two sauces. Mango lassi wasn't good tho.. :( 

Come here when you are sick of eating at Chipotle~ Overall,  I wanna give 3.5 but I will just round it up cuz people here are so nice!! :)
Get the butter chicken and fiery tomato, habanero, and cumin chutney.  Delish.
Try the pork naan wrap! The pork is super tender and the sauce is delicious! Beware of dripping sauces though :)

With all the seemingly good Indian Restaurants in the Berkeley, I can't believe this place is rated so high on Yelp.  Yes, the idea is fun: an Indian Chipotle. But the gimmick wears off really quickly when you've had their food.  I've eaten here three times (It's across the street from where I work) and I can honestly say it's very poor indian food.  

The Karahi Paneer is the best thing I've had and even that is missing something essential. I don't know what, but it just is. 

The cholay is blah.  I'd rather eat the frozen trader joe's cholay than have this.

If this place was a dollar or two cheaper, then I'd boost it a star, but the paneer wrap is $7, which is more expensive than a chipotle burrito (and not even close to being as good).  

The best thing this place has going for it is it's convenience to the UCB campus.  I might still try it on an odd day when I'm sick of eating at Northside Cafe or Jasmine Thai, but I don't imagine it happening anytime soon.

Why, hello, deliciously naan-wrapped, Indian burrito. I am your fan.

I've been here several times and have never been disappointed by the disproportionately large serving/burrito size. Larger portions usually equate less-tasty food, but that is definitely not the case at Urbann Turbann. Everything is so good and so fairly priced ($7.50)!

I know everyone raves about the burritos, but the bowls are just as fantastic. In fact, I prefer them. Ask them for extra potatoes - sometimes the servers can be skimpy on those, but are always kind-hearted deep down.

Recommended items:
Tandoori Chicken, naan-wrapped, with everything + spicy sauce
Buttered Chicken rice bowl, white rice, with everything + chutney & sweet sauce

A tip to those who have not ever been here - don't bring a large party unless you are purchasing to-go. There are at most 2 tables inside and perhaps 1 or 2 outside.

Exact cost of a wrap: $7.

Do I need cucumber, jalapenos, and mint chutney with my tandoori chicken and masala potatoes?

Do I need pork (WTF?) vidaloo?

Have I been looking for a more convenient, less messy, all-in-one serving solution for my Indian food?

No, no, and no.  However, I do like having these options.

For a quick stop by and pop in for lunch scenario, I was very impressed.  Not surprisingly, their food, prices, and hygiene put Naan 'N Curry and House of Curries to (further) shame.  Unfortunately, with only two small tables, one inside, one outside, UT is not an ideal destination for a sit-down lunch.

Basically, Urbann Turbann is to Indian food as Chipotle is to Mexican food.  Quite frankly, I think there exists a space in my belly for exactly this type of on-the-go, alternatingly authentic, yet tasty, "blasphemy."

This place is great. You get some really tasty food for a decent price, and the employees are great. The butter chicken naan wrap seems to be the favorite, but you can customize your wraps with a bunch of combos and fresh veggies.

Highly recommended in you're near campus.

I think this place is overrated, but I can't deny that it is delicious. I just think people hype it up too much. It's basically curry and vegetables inside of a naan toritlla.

I've gotten the roti and naan burritos with tandoori chicken and butter chicken. I suggest you get all the add-ins since that's what sets Urbann Turbann apart form just any other burrito place.

The line is always super long; a testament to how popular they are. Their portions are huuugeee! I shared a burrito with my friend and we each got a samosa each ($1 each) and we were stuffed. Their samosas are pretty good, too.

*If you get roti, sometimes it takes longer because they don't have as many roti tortillas ready-made.

This is like an Indian Chipotle. Such a novel idea and also pretty affordable for the amount of food you get.

Though I find the concept very exciting, I have a few gripes with the execution. #1 it is chaotic while ordering, probably the worst time to come would be lunchtime on a school day. #2 the lack of seating sucks but there are plenty of places on campus nearby to eat. #3 the naan as a wrap is kind of hard to manage while eating. Let me elaborate.

So I LOVE naan and can eat it for breakfast, lunch, and dinner all day, every day. Unfortunately naan as a "burrito wrapper" is better in theory than reality. It gets this very chewy texture after sitting in the aluminum foil for too long, and you find yourself gnawing at the thick naan while the desired amount of filling is already in your mouth. Gross. 

Also do I really need potatoes and/or rice inside my naan wrap? Nah. But if it's your first time, of course you want to try the potatoes! And the rice!

I like the assortment of meats - I got the butter chicken, but they also have tandoori chicken, some sort of beef, and pork vindaloo. 

I also like the selection of sauces but they really need to label everything or tell you what goes good with what meat because I felt pretty ignorant and just picked some condiments under pressure because of the wait behind me. I guess if you're the trial-and-error type of eater then that's okay, but I am less comfortable taking risks with sauces.

Next time I'd go for the rice bowl just to have a more pleasant and cleaner eating experience. The quality of the ingredients is good and I find this to be one of the cooler lunch spots in Berkeley.

YUM! I'm not a huge fan of indian food, but I did enjoy this place (given that it is probably not authentic). I was a bit skeptical after my friend suggested that we eat at yet another indian place, but I am glad we came here. Like others have said, it is the indian Chipotle.

I got a BUTTER CHICKEN NAAN WRAP, and their portions here are HUGE! The wrap was so large that the person making my order had to use four pieces of foil to sufficiently wrap the sucker up. Being a first-timer here, I got everything in my wrap (tomatoes, cucumbers, romaine lettuce, chillies, mixed greens, cilantro, onions) and asked the worker to suggest what kind of chutneys to put in it to compliment the meat since I figured he'd know best (he suggested sweet tamarind and the mild coconut). Everything was so flavorful but not too pungent like a lot of other indian places. I am a fan. The only gripe I have is that the veggies made the wrap a bit cold in some places. I'd prefer to have my food warm/hot.

Overall, this is a good place to go for a cheap, quick bite to eat.

Usually, when I'm doing research in Berkeley, I'm looking for a quick, tasty, cheap and filling lunch that doesn't involve me going far afield from the Library. Urbann Turbann fits those criteria nicely AND caters to my love of all food in wrap form.

While the concept of an assembly line-style wrap place is nowhere near unique (exhibit 1: Chipotle), filling a gigantic moist piece of naan with delicious Indian cuisine is certainly an effective way to get close to my heart. 

While the possible combinations are nearly unlimited, I'm especially fond of a butter chicken/mushroom maatar combination with potatoes, all of the vegetables, and a combination of sweet tamirind and tomato habenero sauce. Service is exceptionally quick, which helps to mitigate the long lines that can form at lunchtime, and their huge portions always fill me up for a long afternoon in the Morrison Stacks. 

The only potential downside is that the fillings can be a little less then warm at times, but their high turnover of ingredients ensures that the food is fresh.

Urbann Turbann is definitely one of my go-to places in Berkeley during research season, which, to be honest is year-round at this point (hooray for Graduate School?).

Nice idea, but it's nothing special. There is good reason that Indian food isn't generally prepared in a wrap / burrito style format... the juicy oh so good liquids that bathe delicious morsels of Indian cuisine also create a messy unstable handful of disaster while eating. 
I had the chicken tandoori wrap, $7.50 + tip, the flavor was good and the waiting time was minimal.

There are several reasons why I like the UrbTurb but first let me tell you a story.

The last semester me and my boy Justin F. took MCB C100A. (You may have heard of him, he's Yelp Elite, nbd). Well not being MCB majors, we were bound to get beat down. BUT.... (long story short) (for the long and boring story you can read his review) we noticed that eating an Urbann Turbann bowl or wrap before each midterm would result in a statistically significant domination of that midterm. So having both done poorly on the first one, we proceeded to gorge there before the midterms and final, and consequently got A's in the class. We're hoping to publish these results of finding positive correlation between the number of Urbann Turbann bowls/wraps you eat the day of the test to the number of standard deviations above the mean you will get on that test. Look for it in the next issue of Nature.

Onto the less important stuff, the service is super friendly and fast. You get a heap ton of food too and it's all really good. You can add as many chutneys as you want for a full rainbow of flavors and I like putting on the Hot Mint and Cilantro and the Fiery Tomato/Habanero/Cumin. I think what I especially like about this place is the fact that everything comes in even dollar amounts. 

In conclusion come here if you are at all hesitant.

Quite good, and the first "Indian" food in the Euclid eating district. I say "Indian" because this place feels and tastes a bit more like Chipotle with essence of Indian then say House of Curries. However, one of their owners is Indian and I am told that the food is traditionally prepared.

I've had the chicken and pork wraps, both are quite good. It isn't cheap by Northside standards, but it's on par with the pricier places.

UPDATE: The owners tell me that although until now they haven't had any seating, they are installing places for 6 tomorrow. Apparently some sort of Berkeley regulation getting in the way (surprise surprise). So I guess they will have some seats, if you get there early!

Food: 
1) Tandoori chicken bowl: The chicken was alright. Nothing special. We got brown rice with our bowl and it complimented the chicken really well. I recommend ordering the bowl with the yogurt chutney. It's 50 cents extra but it's worth it. Gives the bowl some flavor and makes it all together less dry and everything sticks together so it's easier to eat. 
2) Pulled pork roti wrap: The pulled pork was really good and flavorful. The pork was really tender and melted in your mouth. YUM! Using roti to wrap the "indian burrito" was really creative. It's pretty interesting combination of different food groups in your mouth held together by roti naan. 

Ambiance: 
Just like a chiptole, but smaller. There's an order line, a couple of small tables and that's it. It's really new, so that means it's clean. I recommend skipping the dine in experience here and take it to go to enjoy it at home in front of the TV/comp with a good show running. 

Service:
It's like chiptole, you order, they make it, you eat. There's virtually no service aside from putting the food together so you can eat it. 

Price: 
Total was around $14 for everything. Not bad for the amount of food you got and how it tasted. 

overall: 
I liked how this place re-invented the burrito...Indian style! It's new and creative! I like it!

MMM, Indian version of Chipotle...

Nice place if you're travelling on the Northside of Berkeley campus and are feeling a bit *adventurous* for some new food. You can ask them for half/half meat if you really want to try different flavors of new things! The taste isn't quite as strong as Indian restaurant food, so if you're looking for something less mild... try this place out! :)

As others have said, Urbann Turbann is the Chipotle of Indian. As you move down the line you
- Choose wrap or bowl
    - If wrap choose naan or roti
    - If bowl choose white or brown basmati
- Choose main filling (Chicken, Paneer, Veggies, etc)
- Choose veggie toppings (lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onions, cilantro, chilis, etc)
- Choose chutneys (raita is +$0.50)

Paneer & meats are $7, veggie options are $5 (cholay) -$6. Samosas are $1 ea

I went with a butter chicken naan wrap, samosa, and mango lassi.

The wrap is similar in size to a super-sized mission burrito (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/-t6JanEk_V6VzctlTyr6eA?select=T25Oxh50TxbhPiTZLgzWig).

The samosa was good. Not greasy. Crisp, flaky shell. Not super flavorful filling, but comes with a tamarind dipping sauce which helps with that.
