I've seen mixed reviews which is probably because the samosas are made in batches and under a heat lamp so timing from when the batch was made will impact quality.

The naan is chewy and stretchy. Perfect for encasing your wrap. Pretty generous portion of meat (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/-t6JanEk_V6VzctlTyr6eA?select=sorqFodK6D7Sa60SB0auYw). I swapped the masala (potatoes) for cholay (garbanzos). The butter chicken sauce was very flavorful, but some of the meat pieces were dry.

They use compostable cups (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/-t6JanEk_V6VzctlTyr6eA?select=5jN78nVTtSWYQhIC4R4Wjw), though the little sauce containers from the same company are not from the compostable line.

Wrap: 4 stars
Samosa: 3.5 stars

Pretty good value. Friendly staff.

I hate to repeat what everyone else has said, but it really is the best way to describe it: this place is the Indian version of Chipotle. 

I've been meaning to try this place since I started working in Berkeley, but it's quite a walk. It was definitely worth it though. The place is tiny (what else is new?) but luckily there wasn't a long line when we arrived, and the servers are quick. 

The menu is laid out in an easy-to-understand way if you've never been there before. I decided to go with the bowl since I'm not a fan of burritos/wraps in general. My co-worker recommended the butter chicken, so I ordered that topped with cucumbers, lettuce, and potatoes. The total came out to about $7 (so pretty pricey), but oh-so-delicious! Definitely shouldn't have skipped out on the sauce though. Next time.

I'm not the hugest fan of their food. That being said, it is what it is, right? They're not trying to be super authentic or uppity-- it's large portions, cheap and fast, to a bunch of indiscriminate college kids.

As far as I am concerned, however, their catering and/or delivery for larger groups is AWESOME. I have ordered from them twice and the food is hot, fresh, and as ordered. The people who delivered it were friendly and efficient and everyone who ate it seemed thrilled to have something a little different. 

If you're buying food for a student group or department meeting, I highly recommend Urbann Turbann. They get shit done.

Fantastic! Big, fresh, yummy naans packed with tandoori chicken, aloo, jalapenos, raita, chutneys and other spicy goodness, for $7.50, tax included.
My husband had the pork vindaloo one and he loved his, too. In fact he said this place was better than SR24!
I wish the (gori) counter staff was more knowledgeable about the food -- she didn't know what "pickle" was, for example -- and they don't make chai on the weekends for some ungodly reason. 
But it's still a great deal for some kickass "sasta" Indian food. CANNOT beat that.

Urbann turbann dispenses indian bowls and wraps ala el faro's speedy assembly line. all ingredients are in plain view. just tell the server what you want, meats, veggies, chutneys, sauces and it's ready within minutes.

eats: butter chicken wrap (7.5)
-pretty tasty and good sized
-choice of what you want and don't

bites:
-got a munch deal
-line moved fast, got order within minutes
-definitely going back
-lots of food for 8 bucks.
-smiling service all around.

** I am a native of India who has eaten at every single Indian restaurant in Berkeley at least 3 times each, read the bottom of the review for my complete ranking list or look in my Yelp Lists ** 

My new default day-to-day eatery (or at least it was till I started working in the city). 

OK, so this review has been a long time coming. And sorry to my fans for not having written a review in about a year, got really busy with work. I ate at this place literally TWO TIMES A DAY EVERY DAY for a good year, not exaggerating. I know, it's disgusting and wrong to do this to yourself...but that just speaks to HOW AMAZING Urbann Turbann really is as your default go-to on-the-go meal. Read on...

-- Entree Taste: 4/5

Ok, so this is a double edged sword. You want healthy, but you also want it to taste good. Let me preface by saying this, does Urbann Turbann have wraps that I'd give a 5/5 on the taste scale? Yes, it is called the Chicken Tikka Masala  with Naan wrap (probably the only one I'd say).

But for someone that is eating 10 wraps a week here for 50 weeks, you just cannot abuse your body in that way. At that rate, you have to go healthy...which means Cholay filling with roti. Now I'm going to be blunt: going SOLELY OFF OF TASTE, i'd give a Cholay with Roti wrap a miserable 2/5. It is simply boring and uneventful, even when you mix up the sauces / spices. The cholay at this place are quite bland, no matter what they do to them. The roti is horrid half the time, and the other half you need to eat it within 1 minute off the oven (read below). That said, the roti with cholay wrap is a WIN as a food that you can eat every day for the rest of your life and not want to throw up out of boredom and disgust, it SIMPLY DOES NOT GET OLD. Now the taste rating also gets a boost because as you know, I am severely biased in favor of RAJMA, and any Indian business that chooses to serve that as an option automatically goes AAA Gold +++ S & P Rating in my book. 

A GREAT HEALTHY OPTION (if you go cholay+roti). 

-- Naan: 5/5 

You know, shockingly good for a fast-food style Indian restaurant. Some of the best I've had. Soft and almost yogurty in the way it stretches, perfect balance of chewiness.

--Roti: 2/5

 Can't say the same about the Roti (although it's much healthier). The roti really punishes your jaw if you let it sit for more than a few minutes out of the oven; it also lacks flavor. Still, had worse at House of Curries (it's a cracker over there). 

-- Price/Value: 10/5

NO THAT IS NOT A TYPO!!! Value is A+++ , IF (and this is a BIG IF) you stick to the Cholay/Rajma wraps for $5. Man, you get an amazing-sized wrap with a generous serving of cholay and toppings (more than you get in any other wrap I've ever seen) and it can easily last most people 2, maybe 1.5 meals. 

Don't bitch because the Raita costs extra. The economy is tough, not everyone likes it, and if you don't want it, you save 50 cents, think of it that way. (I usually don't get it, but that's just because I'm cheap). In a way, they are actually making the food cheaper rather than charge everyone 5.50 for a Cholay Wrap whether you want Raita or not.

The fact that SALES TAX IS INCLUDED IN THE PRICE makes me want to give the loveably huge owner a manhug. 


-- Service: 3/5 

It's fast and efficient. The owners are a nice couple (congratulations on your baby if you are reading this!) and they started recognizing me after a while (which is a good and bad thing considering how much I used to go). 

*CRITICSMS*:

-  Too much cholay thrown in, they skimp on the tomatoes. 
-  Some days the owners will pretend they don't know you, other days you are old friends
- Hot as hell in the actual restaurant many days
-  Roti needs works (too hard / flavorless)

*********** RANKING LIST ****************************** **************

-- I will keep updating this ranking list as I get time --

1) Flavors of India / Kabab and Karahi (tie)
2) Himalaya
3) Urbann Turbann ($5 Cholay wrap: best value for your money, period).
4) Punjabi By Nature
5) Chaat Cafe
6) Priya
7) Viks (yeah, I know I'm going to get a lot of flak for this one, but it's true folks, severely overrated due to bandwagoning)

8) Breads of India (OK, but overpriced)
9) Biryani House
10) Khana Peena (the one on Solano, a little better than the other one)
11) Pasand (OK, but severely overpriced)
12) House of Curries (College)
13)  Kabana (Great food loses massive points for racially based treatment of customers)
14) Tandoor Kitchen
15) Khana Peena (the one on Shattuck, absolute trash, avoid) 
16) Indus Valley Restaurant (literally serves frozen vegetable curries)

**Now if I called Khana Peena Shattuck trash, then you can imagine how the following are...yeah...these don't deserve to even be ranked**

House of Curries (Durant)
Naan N Curry

The wraps here are DELICIOUS. The place was small, but looked bright and clean, and I liked the modern design of the menu boards. The layout of the place reminded me of Chipotle, where you get to choose the type of wrap, meat, vegetables and sauces you want. I spotted the workers making naans at the back, and when I ordered my wrap, they picked up a naan that was just freshly made.
I chose the naan wrap with Chicken tandoori, lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, mint cilantro and mild coconut. The fillings were generous and the wrap itself was huge, almost as long as my forearm. We also got a Mango Lassi. It was smooth and rich, and I tasted some sort of herbs which gave it a nice flavor. As mentioned, the wrap was delicious, fresh and bursting with flavor and spices. I loved the texture of the naan as well.
We paid $11 for the meal, which is definitely a good price. 
I cannot wait until my next visit, I already have what I want to order in mind...a Butter Chicken wrap...mMMmmm

Stumbled in here to grab a quick bite to eat. I ordered a wrap, medium spicy, which was perfect for me. Loved everything about it. The place was surprisingly big inside but had an empty feeling to it. Friendly staff, large menu, good portions for the money.

I only wish I would have discovered this restaurant long time ago! I stumbled upon it after searching for Indian restaurants on Yelp, and even though there were a few negative reviews, I was so tired of House of Curries and Naan n Curry that I had to give it a try.

My experience was wonderful. We ordered Chicken Coconut and Lamb Tikka Masala (with Garlic Naan and a side of rice), both ''medium'' spicy. They also sell some local beer at this location, which is great - I tried Speakeasy, an it was very pleasant.
The place was empty except for two other couples, which I didn't mind at all, since I instinctively relate emptiness to quick service. Indeed, the food arrived in less than 15 minutes, and it was simply delicious! The Chicken Coconut was the most authentic I ever tasted, and the Lamb Tikka Masala was just perfect - we also discovered that by mixing the two, we got a completely new, balanced flavor. Both were medium spicy just like we requested, and there was a good amount of meat in both dishes.

Based on this experience, I went to Indian Flavors Express twice afterwards, and both times it was great. Now it's my go-to place to satisfy my weekly Indian food cravings, and it never disappoints!

I came here for a quick lunch with a co-worker. We both decided to go with the lunch buffet ($8.99). For the most part I haven't found any indian buffets I like too much but they had a pretty decent selection here (along with free tea). I definitely piled on the garlic naan (my favorite), chicken vindaloo, and veggie korma. They also had a mini salad bar with dressing and seasonings which was nice. The place itself is pretty big and surprisingly clean! Would definitely come back since it's so close to campus.

Do actual Indians come here?  I keep getting dragged here by friends since it's right near my office, but it definitely does not meet my white person with lots of Indian friends standards.  While their introduction of the buffet made it more economical, I find their naan and rice substandard (maybe both are too oily?), which definitely doesn't help shape my perception of the rest of their food.  Everything I've had there is at best mediocre.  Mount Everest is far better (and Indian-approved).
Tasty food at decent prices.

I used to go to House of Curries all the time, but nowadays I make sure to walk the extra block to come here instead. Their butter chicken is amazing! It definitely tops any chicken tikka masala I've ever had. Unlike House of Curries, their chicken is completely boneless and so much more tender. My boyfriend has a theory about how they cook the Chicken Tikka Masala in bulk at House of Curries so the chicken ends up tough from being overcooked. The wait is also significantly shorter here. I seriously waited over an hour for my food several times at House of Curries. Pro-tip: call ahead to place your order if you don't want to sit there and wait.

Why this place doesn't get five stars:
1. I've had better garlic naan
2. The atmosphere is extremely dreary due to the decor (or lack thereof)
A great place for chaat! (Indian snacks with lots of chick peas, yogurt, spices). And they serve beer and wine :) highly recommended.

I was craving some Chicken Tikka Masala one day and just kinda stumbled into this place. I also ordered Garlic Naan, but I wish they would include naan in the price of the dish, or give a discount when it is purchased with an entree because they are on the expensive side. 

I really think this restaurant is a 3.5 The atmosphere is nice and it looks clean albeit empty. I did enjoy their food more than HoC and that new place next to Yogurt Park (Sham-something?). HoC CTM had very overcooked chicken since they just make a huge batch and keep it hot over the stove (so the chicken is inevitably over-cooked. The Sham place by Yogurt Park had awful CTM. I saw the cook in the back dumping curry powder from a box in it. Plus, it was super greasy and there was 3 times as much rice as curry and just as much of this chick pea masala stuff as CTM. All that with naan was just $5 but I still would not call it good value.

I usually strongly dislike self-service places, but Indian Flavors Express definitely delivers enough in the flavor aspect for me to make an exception. Affordable and good-tasting food.

I love lamb and I love spinach. I thought they did a pretty good job with their palak gosht.

Good deal.  Chicken tikka masala with naan, rice, and a salad for 8.99, beautiful. Everything tasted good and I loved the amount of seating available.  I was not going to stay but I changed my mind when I saw how calm and open the seating was.  To find calm and open in that part of Berkeley with good food... I will be back
For sure
not bad. the aloo gobi dish had tomatoes, which seems weird to me though.

The prices are on the high side for curries and breads, but they make a good tikka masala and vindaloo curry so I keep going back. However the samosas are pretty greasy and not as good as others I've had.

Just discovered my favorite curry dish in all of berkeley: BUTTER CHICKEN @ Indian Flavors is BOMB

I lowered a star because they changed the chicken tikka masala recipe and now its just taste like garam masala, which is funky

Wow. The reviews for this place are just all over the place! 

I was sitting in lecture today, thinking to myself how ridiculously famished I was. I wanted something big, heavy, and salty. So Indian food came to mind! Which was perfect because I have been meaning to come try this place for weeks. 

I ordered the chicken tikki masala, and the whole wheat naan. 

When it first came out, I was soooo hungry, so it tasted pretty good to me! But as I kept eating and eating, I realized...it was just my hunger speaking.

The chicken is really dry and tough. The curry itself was a little too creamy for my liking. The naan was...not as great as I hoped it would be. It was kind of oily too :(. I probably ended up eating 3 out of the 8 or so chicken pieces they gave me. 

It's nice that there is complimentary chai tea though. 

I was wavering between giving this place 3 or 4 stars throughout my meal...but the big drop of curry that splashed from my naan to my econ notes drew the line.

Three stars it is!
Ok, so the only thing I have ever ordered is the chicken saag. But it's soooo good. So flavorful and it makes my mouth so happy!

Probably the best Indian place near campus. Actually, I don't know why I don't come here more often, because the price is comparable to that of House of Curries (which is only a block away). Will take this into consideration the next time I'm headed to HoC.

I find the food here more flavorful and heartier than the other Indian restaurants. I love that they offer Lamb Tikka Masala, because I really like lamb and Chicken Tikka Masala... and now I can have the best of both worlds. Their rice and naan portions are huuuge, and their Garlic Naan is super fresh and seasoned perfectly. I should definitely come here more often. Maybe I'll even be adventurous and try some of the other items on the menu!

On a side note: their store space used to be occupied by Quiznos. I MISS YOU QUIZNOS!

Definitely low quality Indian food but the buffet is SO WORTH IT! I think it's ~$9-10 but I ordered 2 naans and a chicken curry at House of Curries which came out to be $13 in the end. So this is money well spent. The curry here is really creamy and heavy though (which is nice if you want to carbo load)....and the chicken is really tough and dry. The naan is too crispy and well-cooked for my taste--I like my naan soft, warm, and fluffy. Albeit low quality food, it's nice to come here if you're hungry, craving Indian food, and on a budget.

I used to be a big fan of another local Indian restaurant, but I noticed their quality and portion size declining recently.

Indian Flavors Express is definitely my new favorite Indian place in the area. The curry is always thick, not watery, and the quality is very consistent. Highly recommended.

My boyfriend brought me some of their aloo naan and chicken tikka masala takeout. I was first struck by the oddly yellow color of the sauce and more oil than I'm used to seeing.  It tasted extremely creamy/oily and peppery, the chicken was alright, and the aloo naan was nice and fluffy. There were some key flavors missing from the sauce that I couldn't quite put my finger on at the time because I was too hungry to care. An hour later after I'd had some time to think...a revelation! The cook seemed to have left out the tomato puree. And the garam masala. Ultra fail.

Berkeley tends to have a lot of Indian and Thai restaurants, so in order for a particular place to stand out, they really have to do something special. This place is good, but not good enough. 

The restaurant itself is situated within an alcove-type thing -- i.e. it's a walk IN from Bancroft. Up a flight of stairs to a deck with some outdoor seating, then into the restaurant proper. It's a lot bigger on the inside than expected, and since they don't have any windows, the space had an almost warehouse feel to it. 

There are both high cocktail tables as well as regular height tables, and since I enjoy high places I always sit at the cocktail rounds. 

I ordered a lamb curry and naan, and asked for as mild spiciness as possible. As we sat and waited for our dishes, my friend and I couldn't help but notice that there was no one else in the restaurant. A little disconcerting, especially since the interior isn't the newest looking thing I've seen. 

The naan itself is less fluffy than I like, and the curry dish had a very distinction, overpowering spice that I didn't really appreciate. Still tasty, but it lacked the lamb-is-featured feel that I was looking for. Also, it was spicy. And I can't handle spicy.

That being said, my friend ordered the chicken tikka masala which I was able to get a brief taste of and which turned out to be VERY interesting. If I had ordered that dish instead, this review might have gone differently.

Decent buffet lunch!

The saag paneer was tasty, the garlic naan was almost properly cooked, the gobbi pakoras were a little too soggy. But for the price I was able to fill myself up and will probably go back. They have a chaat menu too so I think I'll try the papri chaat next time.
WOWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWWW GREAT FOODDDDD GREAT SERVICE. I ORDER ONLINE THE OTHER DAY TROUGH EAT24HOURS.COm AND DELIVERY WAS FAST.  IF YOU DINE IN 5 STAR Service it was hella good.

This is the only place that I know of where I can get samosa chaat in Berkeley. It's just samosas with a garbanzo bean curry and it's delicious! The only other thing I've tried here is the naan which is soft and a little chewy. I have yet to try anything else but I'm definitely a fan of this place.

Girlfriend and I came here to sample something new. After four years of living here there has to be somewhere we haven't tried yet. Boom! Indian Flavors Express.

Like Naan n' Curry, this place has a $9 buffet, with much more variety than its counterpart on Telegraph. Don't bother going a la carte since it's generally about $1-2 cheaper than the buffet for one dish with no naan, while the buffet itself has about 6-7 to sample.

The Indian food is extremely filling, chicken tikka masala is always gone (which is expected in Indian buffets), and all of it is really delicious. I am a fan of the fact that they have garlic naan as well as the regular naan in the buffets. 

However, I am not really a fan of the atmosphere here. Naan N' Curry dresses themselves up for a better experience, and Indian Flavors Express doesn't appear to try that at all. It's really a no-frills type of place. But what should I expect for a place that has the word "express" in their name?

4.5 stars.  Great food, so-so space.  They always run out of the free chai when I am there!  (But I really enjoy it while it lasts.)  This place has really wonderful naan and meat samosas.  I like the self-serve unlimited sauces and condiments.  The staff are always friendly and it always seems to be open when I'm craving Indian food.  Like the semi-outdoor seating option.

This is a good place to go for a quick meal! The atmosphere is not that nice but there is a pretty large seating area. I think usually at lunch here they have a buffet, never tried it though!

So i've been here twice and both times I ordered their chicken tikka masala (extra spicy) with a side of basmati rice. I think it comes out to be about $10. The tikka masala was disappointing because it wasnt spicy even tho i asked for extra spicy.

I actually really like the flavor of the food here a lot, but for some reason it doesnt seem filling for the price that you pay. I'd rather go to Mt Everest or something and it'd be a few dollars more but its a bigger portion. 

I'd like to come and try their buffet though!

I don't really understand why there are multiple Indian restaurants within 5 minutes of each other, but hey at least that gives us options, right?

As a loyal House of Curries patron, I was skeptical about trying Indian Flavors Express, but my friend brought me here so I decided to give it a shot.

The food wasn't outstanding and I put it on par with that from House of Curries. My only issue with the food is that it was WAY TOO OILY! My curry was swimming in oil.

Also, like other Yelpers, the food wasn't spicy enough. I asked for spicy and was disappointed when I couldn't taste the "kick." 

Fortunately, the portions here are actually pretty big. The dishes they come in look tiny but they actually fit quite a lot of food. I definitely had enough for another meal.

I also tried the mango lassi, which was mediocre and not that memorable. Stick with water.

The only thing that really stands out is how clean and spacious this place is. There is a ton of open seating and it's not cramped at all, which is a rarity in Berkeley. It felt very clean inside but it also felt very empty and cold.

Unfortunately, this place doesn't top my list of best Indian restaurants in Berkeley. I wouldn't come back when there are a bunch of alternatives with better (and less greasy) food at a fraction of the price.

I didn't have anything here except for the vegetable samosas... BEST samosas I have ever had. 

This place is kind of hidden in that it's deep inside a seating area/doorway place, but it's actually a pretty big space, with abundant seating on the inside and available seating outside. Prices are average, comparable to every other Indian restaurant in town. 

I recommend the samosas to every Berkeley person I know.

Ambiance: 1, Service: 2, Food: 4.5!  Now I can't go to Zellerbach without my Chicken Tikka Masala here. YUM. They serve two kinds of wine: "white" and "red." Take your pick. Oh, and the red is kept in the fridge. But it WAS a new bottle. Of something. Red.

LOVe this place!!! I miss Berkeley for this reason! I miss you Basal!!! I would go in every friday and order new things that he would suggest for me. Love the tea, Love the workers, CREAVE and desperately miss the curry :((

Love this place!! I've tried other indian places in Berkeley and this is definitely my favorite. I always order the Paneer Tikka Masala and it's wonderful with a side of naan. I'm pretty addicted to this place and usually crave it once a week! Now that I go there enough, the people at the counter recognize me and it's nice that they're friendly. I usually order take-out and they package it up very nicely.

Ok so I've been walking past this place since the beginning of this semester seeing a sign that says "Indian Flavors coming soon". I've been secretly excited for this new indian place to open in the UC area. So far, I only like to go to House of Curries. So finally today, they had a "Now Open" sign which was very exciting  :D

Food:
I tried this place today with my sister. They give you three spice-level options: Medium-spicy, spicy, and super spicy for each entree. We ordered a chicken wrap (but with chicken tikka instead of the thigh meat) (spicy), paneer tikka masala (medium spicy), and garlic naan. The paneer was good, and it didn't taste like ready-made paneer. The sauce was good for medium-spicy. I ordered it medium-spicy because I didn't want it to be too spicy, but I think it will be better if next time I order it spicy or super-spicy. The garlic naan was very similar to House of Curries' naan, which I liked. 
 
Interior:
Although I ordered takeout, the restaurant and tables looked very clean and orderly. (Hopefully it stays that way). Compared to most restaurants in Berkeley, this place had ample sitting space.

Service:
The guy taking our order was patient and the wait for food wasn't too long. It seemed like they put more care into take out packages than other places. 

Overall, it was a positive experience and I think I would go here again, especially since its along my way from the Wurster area. I gave it 5 stars because it is probably one of the better places around the Berkeley campus in terms of cleanliness, availability of seating, food quality, and variety of options. If you like House of Curries or Naan N Curry, then you will probably like this place too.

The food here was average, nothing to go out of your way for.

Service/Decor: Another restaurant where you order at the front and wait for your food at a table. Service is fairly slow, and the staff don't seem all too happy to be there.

Food: For once, I got the Lamb Biryani instead of my usual Palak Paneer (which I use to gauge most Indian restaurants). I ordered it mild, which it was, but it was SO SOUR. There must have been a pint of vinegar in it. I barely finished the dish because it was so sour. The price was around $8, and it was NOT worth it.

I was looking for a nice place to meet with some business partners by the campus and went to Indian Flavors. Large area for seating, clean and large restrooms and best of all the food was GREAT.  The sauces are fantastic and it was a great break from the craziness of Telegraph.  The prices seemed reasonable especially since you really get great service, large pitcher of water for the table etc..  I really like the food and highly recommend the restaurant.  I will be back often.

Not exactly a cheap, under $5 lunch, but the portions and quality were worth the price. I had the lamb biryani with a complimentary raita, and both were quite decent. The biryani had a good complexity in spices and wasn't too spicy. (Though next time, I will ask for a slightly hotter biryani.) My only complaint would be that the biryani was a little too salty. Other than that, I enjoyed the meal very much.

I'm normally a huge fan of Indian food, but Indian Flavors Express was quite disappointing. A friend and I dropped by for dinner while in Berkeley the other day; the menu offered a wide variety of options, and the seating areas (including some outdoor tables) was quite spacious. The restaurant follows the fast casual model - you order at the counter, help yourself to utensils, water, etc., and they bring the food out to you. They also have free wifi, which is always nice.

I ordered the bhindi masala; okra is one of my favorite foods, and I've experienced wonderful bhindi masala at other Indian places. My friend got the prawn biryani, and we split garlic naan and some roti. I was quite excited for the meal, until the food came out. While the portion size of the bhindi masala was fairly generous, it didn't come with rice (not a big deal, but something you would think would be provided). In addition, the bhindi masala did not have the normal, scrumptious blend of spices that I've come to expect in Indian food. Instead, the bhindi masala was simply salty - not the kind of flavorful and delicious salty that balances out with naan or other foods, but the kind of salty that makes the food not as enjoyable to eat. It seemed like the food had been cooked with an overzealous amount of salt to compensate for the lack of other flavors; in addition, I had been asked how spicy I wanted my dish, and had asked for "medium". There wasn't anything more than a slight kick to the dish - nowhere near what I would consider mildly spicy - and again, it seemed like they had added salt to compensate.

The bread was a little better, but still a little disappointing. I've definitely had better garlic naan, and for nearly $2.50 we only got one naan (cut into four pieces). The roti, too, was underwhelming - it was tough, undercooked, and in general, uninspired. I've had much better roti and naan elsewhere. My dining companion agreed with my assessment of the naan and roti. He did, however, mention that the prawn biryani was OK.

With the disappointing food - along with service that didn't wasn't overtly warm or friendly - I'm going with two stars for Indian Flavors Express, and will be trying other places next time I'm in town and want Indian food.

I had the Lamb Vindaloo here and it was really good! However, it was definitely more spicy than expected and pretty pricey (around $9 I believe?) Including naan, my meal came out to about $11 for lunch, which is expensive compared to other Indian restaurants nearby of similar quality. This place is also kind of hidden away in a little plaza thing on Bancroft, so there is usually not much business happening there.

When my friends came here, they got the Chicken Tikka Masala and it was really watered down, which was disappointing. 

I like how they offer chai tea on the side though!

Wayyy better than House of Curries or Naan and Curry.  Really delicious chicken tikki masala. Unlike HOC, it isn't dry chicken and you can actually taste the cheese in the sauce and not just spice.

Also, 10% off for all UCB students right now.  Try it!
One of my favorite Indian restaurants. Although the place is pretty small, the quality of food is amazing. I especially like their naan :)

I got the lamb vindaloo. For the price, I would have liked more lamb. The flavor was good but I was expecting spicy! I guess they tone it down for us non-Indian customers but still! I ordered it because it had a chilli pepper next to it on the menu!

The naan was fragrant and delicious. 

I had a good experience, but I expect a bit lower prices seeing that it is a self-service place.

Food: Always had enjoyable experience with the food. I like the tea also (complimentary with meal). +Vegetarian options, +Vegan options

Location: spacious seating with combining table options 

Bathroom: nice bathrooms for the area (though it smells a little like cleaning solution at times)

Service: A+, nice people

Wait Time: normal

Price: probably about $8-10 per person

Overall: 4.5/5, Good food and meat/veggie options / good building / good service, I wish they had more popularity as I like this and my Indian friends like the food.

I ordered the chicken tikki masala with rice because I've noticed that every time i don't order that at an indian restaurant, I end up regretting it.
The chicken tikki masala I had here, however, fell far below expectations. The chicken was tough and dry, and I only continued eating it because I had already paid for it. The curry was also too creamy for me.
My friend got the vegetable korma, which was delicious! 
The vegetable pakora was mediocre. I've definitely had better.
Btw, there's complimentary chai tea with every meal, but it tasted insanely watered down. But I guess if you want a decent beverage, you should be willing to pay for it.

If I was basing this review solely on the Vegetable Korma, this place would get a 5 hands down. Too bad I'm not!

Good quality and good cooking!

This place is best for family style.  It's extremely filling, so you have like 3/4 of the rice left.  Also, it's nice to try different dishes.  

I've had the yellow lentil dish (very satisfying), vegetable biryani (tasty, large portion, not oily, comes with yogurt sauce which is also good), chicken tikka masala (very filling), and the eggplant dish (lots of vegges, good spices).  

The tea is pretty good too!  It has a touch of ginger.

Note that spicy is really spicy.  I've always thought I had a good tolerance for spicy food, but I had a stomach ache after I came here once because I had too much spicy food.  (or maybe I was being stressed about a midterm)

Lovvvved my first two visits: saag paneer (tho the paneer was a little stiff), then lamb coconut with basmati rice. I prefer the very mild on the hot meter, but the flavors were great. Those are still my two favorites so far. The employees seem very nice-if they don't greet you with a huge, jovial smile I take it as that they're really busy trying to keep everything moving and multitasking. They've seemed very careful and conscientious (why no women?). I would like to tip them but if the employer doesn't pass the tip jar to them, then what to do? I am not Indian but I see Indian people eating there. The long distance from the sidewalk to the front door is compensated for by the 5 foot tall menu out in front (people, stop complaining). It is so pleasant inside, away from traffic and noisy people, this is my favorite refuge for Indian food now in the campus area.

Indian Flavors Express (IFE) is my new goto Indian/Pakistani food joint (the previous was House of Curries).  IFE doesn't overcook its meat, so it's moister and more tender and absorbs the sauce more.  The sauces are also better: IFE's tikka masala is nice and creamy and flavorful while House of Curries has a strong note of tomatoes.  House of Curries does make better naan, though.

My wife is Indian and I must admit that the best Indian food is home cooked, but occasionally you can find a nice Indian restaurant as well.  You'll be surprised that the nicest restaurants often times have the worst food and the run down hole in the walls make some truly delectable naan and curries. 

IFE is neither run down nor upscale, but rather plain and simple...even boring.  The menu is all over the place, trying to cook south Indian, North Indian, chaat and dosas.   This should have been the first signal not to dine here.  Typically a good Indian restaurant will specialize in one regional style of the cuisine.  This restaurant was a colossal failure.  The chaat was horrible, lacking the spicy sweet balance so important for these street food dishes.  The curries were watery and had a stale flavor, the restaurant is a little hidden and was not busy so that may explain why the food tasted "old", not enough turnover.  The naan, while cooked fresh, had a horrible texture and flavor, like eating cardboard. 

Oh well, there are plenty of other restaurants to try and even if they all fail as badly as IFE  I can always count on the home cooked stuff!

Without a doubt, this is the worst place I've eaten at in Berkeley. It's been a while since I've visited Indian Flavors Express, so I can't recall exactly what I ordered on the menu, but I do know this:
- the portions are tiny
- everything you order is in a puddle of oil
- they don't know the first thing about spicy as nothing is actually spicy
- spicy to these people actually means extremely sour
- the amount of rice you get is enough to feed a small bird. 
- the price is about $6-$9 for the dishes and then $1 or $2 for the nann or rice.
- this place is empty most of the time. i should've taken this as a clue of how terrible this place is
- to the reviewer who said you walk in and are greeted with the smell of *hand ground* spices... how in the world do you get this? if anything, there's a reek of vomit from the place

I would highly not recommend going here. i ended up eating 1/4 of my order, and then getting some la burrita after.
Dhal makhani with tandoori roti - pre class ritual!

I am addicted to their Chicken Chole. I got it by mistake and it is now my favorite Indian dish! Unfortunately, they changed their menu and took off many of their best dishes (including the chicken chole). I have no idea why they did this and would have given them 5 stars if they hadn't. In any case, this place is still way better than house of curries or naan and curry

When they first opened, I tried their food and thought, a much better alternative than House of Curries.

However, after ordering takeout, and eating a naan that still tasted like raw dough and finding a hair in my chicken tikka masala, I must say I can't believe they've sunk below House of Curries. That's just bad.
One of my favorite restaurants in all of Cal, go here and I promise you won't be disappointed.  I heartily recommend the Kashmiri Nan and tandoori chicken.

Authentic or not--I have no idea, but I really like the food at this place.  For those of you that don't know where the restaurant is, it's where the Quizno's on Bancroft used to be. (Man, I did NOT like that Quizno's, just the fact that there's a new place there that's decent makes for a happier day in my opinion.) Because I spend a lot of my time in Barrows Hall the location's extremely convenient for me, the service is pretty fast, and it's not overrun at lunch time--three big pluses. Everything I've ever ordered here has been quite tasty (usually I get one of the lunch specials) and frankly, lunch doesn't cost much more than a sandwich and chips at the Golden Bear.  I also have gone to Naan 'N Curry quite a bit and I think this place beats Naan 'N Curry for decor, cleanliness and being able to leave the place without smelling like a Tandoori oven.  Indian Flavors Express will definitely stay in my lunch rotation.  The people are very friendly.

Tried this place the other day, had chole bhatura it was $6.50 with tax .
it was good warm, fresh and served on time. place seems nicely decorated will try there famous chicken tikka masala which was well talked about on this site for next time .

3.5. This place seemed like it just opened today. It was clean, empty, weird music playing, IKEA paintings on the wall.
I ordered chicken tikka masala and garlic naan. Both were surprisingly good. And I'm cheap so I was psyched when I saw FREE lemonade and chai. If the service were adequate and the prices a tad lower, I'd bump it up to 4. But, I'll probably crave it and go back and bump it up anyway.

After all the raving I heard about this place from my roommate, I decided to go check it out.

I just ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala with the plain naan. I've had better Chicken Tikka Masala, but I have to say that the naan I had here has been my favorite so far. When I got my food, the naan even looked like it was going to be amazing. Their complimentary tea was just alright.

Although I still prefer House of Curries, this place definitely hit the spot on a cold day.

I enjoy going here during long breaks between classes. Great value for the price, and very flavorful dishes. Only thing keeping me from giving them five stars is that their buffet doesn't have many vegan/vegetarian options, though their menu has a handful of vegan dishes.

gave Indian food another try at Indian Flavors Express, I was on a 10 minute time crunch to get back to class so I just picked the Chicken Tikka wrap, and it was ready after 5 minutes. First bite in, and I was amazed, the chicken was NOT dry and the flavor was really tasty! :) I'll most likely come back and try something else on the menu.

BEWARE: i found a couple bone fragments in my chicken wrap, when i didn't expect it. hence the lost star.

This is one of the best Indian buffets in Berkeley. Their food is fresh and they keep refilling the entrees when it gets low. They have a good selection of curries and tandoori chicken. They also have both garlic and regular naan. The buffet is also reasonably proved at 8.99. Too bad it's only during lunch.

More greasy and sodium-rich than other Indian places, including nearby House of Curries. I got the chicken saag because I love spinach curries. I expected to get the rich, thick green curry that I'm used to but their saag was a completely different brown color, more salty, and tasted more like regular stir-fry than exotic herbs. Also, this restaurant is more expensive than surrounding Indian options. I had leftovers that my dining partner happily finished off for me, but $9 is too much to pay for lunch. Maybe it was just the hot weather combined with the spicyness of the dish, but I would not come again to satisfy my curry cravings.

I saw their "coming soon" sign a long time ago, and finally managed to try this restaurant out. I have to say this place is just plain amazing. Out of all the Indian food places around Berkeley, this is THE place to go if you want good Indian food. The prices are about the same, but the portions are much bigger and the flavoring is just right. The naan is actually soft, unlike other places that make it really flaky and burnt.

The only thing is that the decorations and style of chairs/tables is a bit off. But even without the atmosphere, this place deserves a 5-star based on the food they serve.

Close to campus, good location, clean, new, good food and service! It is cheaper, about the same tasting, cleaner, and has better service than House of Curry AND Naan and Curry!

Food: I got the CHICKEN TIKKA MASALA. My all time favorite! I always get this at every new Indian Place I got to so I can compare Indian Curries from one place to another. I really liked the dish here! It wasn't as tomato based as I usually like it, but it's different, so that's nice. The chicken was tender and pretty juicy. 

Price: CHEAPER than House of Curry and Naan and Curry! Only $5 something for a curry and $1.89 for Roti! YUM!

Service: Even though it was a "order at the front counter" type place, they still checked on us to make sure we were doing ok and they were very pleasant and nice!

Ambiance: You have to walk into this one secluded area to get inside to the restaurant. So it's nice in the sense that it feels like it's remote and secluded from school so you get a sense of escape. You can sit outside in this covered area so that was nice!

I liked it! I would definitely come back!

I freakin love this place. Since it opened a week and a half ago, my boyfriend has gone 4 times already! And everytime the food has been awesome. 
I tried one of the chicken wraps (mild), and it was to die for!! I was so excited, because I love the flavors of Indian food, but I'm super pansy when it comes to spicy stuff. So, usually whenever I go to an Indian restaurant and ask for it to be "mild," the food usually comes out still too spicy for me, and I leave with burning tongue. :( Not so here! The spice was perfect when I asked for it mild, and the flavors were delicious! If you like spicy food, though, you should ask for spicy or extra spicy, and skip the medium.
In his 4 visits to this place, my boyfriend has tried the Chicken Vindaloo, Lamb Vindaloo, Chicken Curry, and Chicken Chole (sp?), and he said they were all awesome.
We love this place and recommend it to everyone!

Personally, Indian food has always been the black sheep of food for me. I always ignore it and I never considered it to fulfill my fatass desires. However, my BFF took me here and all I can say is that Indian Flavors Express makes me BELIEVE. 

IFE is a great place to get a savory rich lunch or dinner. I've never been a fan of curry because it can be spice-overload, but the curries here are BOMBDIGGITY. It's lip-smacking good.

The Lamb Tikki masala and butter chicken deserve encore seconds. The curry was so rich and I loved how they only give you the curry and the meat. I hate it when other places put yucky vegetables (yup, im a kid at heart.) because A) it takes up plate space that could have been filled with curry instead! and B) VEGETABLES?! REALLY?! YUCKKKK! I loved that there was no veggies to dilute the rich spicy meaty taste. Also, for those of you who might complain about the size, the size is more than enough. Curry is super rich in flavor, and if you can finish a whole bowl, you might want to consider investing in some running shoes because it's going to yo THIGHSSS. :D hehe

Also, the garlic naan is DELICIOUS. Make sure to get this with the curry ^__^. It has this awesome crisp that goes well with the curry. Gotta love texture! The potato naan was okay. I didn't appreciate the chickpeas . 

Tips: Don't come expecting amazing service. It's basically you order your food. Get a number. Sit down. and Wait for happiness. Also, there are pitchers of water in the open cooler. So you can just grab one and bring it to your table. BOO HOO. They don't poor water into your cups.

I was craving Indian food while laboring over my finals studying so I checked out this new place on my way back from the library one night at around 9 30 PM without having had anything to eat since noon so I was starving. I like how it's open pretty late, but I guess anything around southside is open that late. 

I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala after reading some reviews, and I think it was great. I'm a big fan of indian food, and I've had the other places too. I honestly think it's about as good as naan n curry and house of curry, though. Also, I thought it'd be cheaper but it still totaled to around $8.50 including tax and and tip. Their tea was free, but it was just alright. I especially liked their naan, though, and only because I'm not too picky about my naan. This naan definitely is oilier than other places, but that doesn't bother me- it was great naan. Very crispy and fresh. Their chicken tikka masala was also as good as everyone says. 

Overall, good food. I left satisfied, even if it cost more than I expected, but that's only because I'm a cheap college student. Make sure to ask for it extra spicy though.

11:30 (lunch rush) and the place is deserted except for 2 other customers. i hope this place doesn't die .. especially when they seem so nice!

tandori chicken wrap.
not bad at $6.50. super filling; naan wrap, nice moist tender chicken. medium is not spicy whats-so-ever.. could have used a bit more flavor/spices, and rice?! regardless, a good lunch stop.

The buffet special is not worth it at all. Its like $9-$10. Stay away. The food was cold and bland. Also the buffet area was extremely messy. You're much better at getting a regular meal. It will be cheaper and better quality.

I'm a huge fan of Indian food and consider myself to be a Chicken Tikka Masala connoisseur because every time I'm in an Indian restaurant, that's what I order. Every single time - without fail. I came here to sample their Chicken Tikka Masala and was not disappointed.

Ambiance:
Was a little run-down. Our table legs were actually uneven and it shook a bit. It wasn't ABSOLUTE shit though so I'll give it that. The establishment was very spacious, just plain. Also really conveniently located close to campus!

Customer Service
You order and pay at the counter, then find a table and the food is brought out to you. The service wasn't very friendly, but wasn't terrible either. They seemed a bit bored, but the food came out at a respectable time.

Food:
Obviously, I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and it was great! The chicken pieces were cooked to perfection and the sauce was tasty and creamy. I had a side of Aloo Naan as well and it went great with the Masala sauce. I also ordered the Mango Lassi, but was taken aback by how sour it was so I wouldn't recommend that. I went over to get some of their free Chai Tea and it was pretty bad - coming from someone who normally loves a good chai. I just went for water in the end.

---

Overall, not your 5-star establishment. But for a quick bite, it's definitely worth it. The prices are reasonable and if you're into Chicken Tikka Masala like me, you won't be disappointed.

Lets be clear. The restaurant name is terrible. "Express" makes it seem like a fast food take-out joint, with food sitting under heat lamps all day. But this joint is just like the nearby House of Curries--food made to order and delivered to your table
 I dropped by to try it out. The menu offers a bit more than the other Indian places around campus: including "Indian street food" (under $4), dosa ($4-6), tandoori wraps ($5-6 and HUGE), as well as tandoori entrees ($7-8ish), biryani, various types of naan (keema, parantha, paneer,..), etc.
Prices are very competitive. I was stuffed for under $5.
They give you two bottles of sauces to compliment your dish.
The decor is quite nice as well-very clean, very new, well spaced.

MISC
* their "spicy" was not at all spicy
* mostly see indians eating here

I love this place! I always stop by here for late night snacks since they conveniently close at 10 PM. I always get Chicken Coconut because I love the hint of coconut with tikka masala. This place is not only clean but also quick. 

I also love their naan. I prefer Indian Flavors Express a lot more than other places like Naan' Curry and House of Curries because it has a nice environment and it's at a nice location.

This place used to be my go-to Indian restaurant in Berkeley. With Vik's being so far away and Naan N' Curry being the only option for "indian food", I was excited when a new restaurant opened down the street. Nested inside a food court in a space that used to be a Quizno's store, this place used to serve delectable delights with large portions for cheap. The waiters aimed to please and they used to have these amazing lunch specials which would fill you up and leave you wanting for more.

Now, however, they keep raising the prices to the point that it's really expensive for what you get. The food too has gone down in taste, although there are some gems still in the menu (the biryani and baigan bhartha). The warmth of the customer service has gone down and is more mechanical now. Still a good option for quick Indian food around Southside. 

If you're looking for a good Indian meal and are willing to travel a bit further, check out Zaika or Udipi Palace.

I stopped in here for a quick snack to go while on my way up to Cafe Strada.  It was cheap, had samosas available, and was close to campus - a perfect storm for the business of many a hungry student.  Being an alumnus myself, I can appreciate a hearty, yet thrifty meal in such a convenient location, but as a visitor there are just too many competitive options within a short drive.

The samosas themselves were quite a deal, but nothing particularly special.  Great bang for the buck, as 2 large fried dumplings were $2.99 (pre-tax).  They had a generally stronger ginger flavor than what I'm used to tasting in samosas, but definitely a good balance of flavor.

The establishment itself is a bit depressing.  First off, from the street it's difficult to realize there is even a restaurant here.  Secondly, there isn't adequate lighting inside.  If you don't get food to go, you'll be eating a very drab and dark location.  It's just not conducive to a friendly eating environment.

The service seemed suspicious as well.  I felt as if they didn't really care if they had my business or not.  Perhaps they were indifferent because I didn't order very much, but regardless there is more that can be done to improve a place by a communicative smile.

I would consider trying this place again if it wasn't so sullen looking.  But for now, I know more lively and delicious places to spend my money.

My friends and I decided to try out this new place and see how it compares to House of Curries and Naan 'N' Curry. We ended up ordering: chicken korma, paneer tikka masala, meat samosas, dosa-crepe, and plain naan. Overall, the meal was pretty good! 

The curries were easily the best part of the lunch. The flavoring is definitely more complex than the typical fare, but was oddly also more bland just because it lacked the same amount of kick and spice that you typically get at House of Curries. As a friend said, another major plus was that there was less filler in the curry- not only do they give you a lot more than other places, but it just has a more rich, dense texture to it. I also loved the way they cooked the chicken! It was definitely more moist and less chewy than what you'd get at House of Curries (Can you tell I go there often?). 

The rest of the meal was just okay. The chai tea is infused with ginger, which might be tasty to some people but definitely wasn't my cup of tea. Compared to the rest of the meal, the dosa was definitely the least favorite just by virtue that it was so dry and flavorless. 

In general, this is a pretty good value for what you pay. Alas, House of Curries will still remain my one and only for Indian food in the UC Berkeley area because I love their biryani, and no curry can measure up to that.

Just down right gross.  I mean Naan N Curry is bad but this place makes it seem like Bukhara (Best Restaurant in India) by comparison.  On top of a dirty restaurant, rude staff and really awful food, I've had horrible stomach pains all night.

I'm Indian and usually give food from my homeland the benefit of the doubt, but this is just too bad.

I went here for my first and last time yesterday. The service was very quick and the prices are hands down the cheapest out of all the Indian places in Berkeley I've been to, but the quality of the food was lacking to say the least. First of all the fish pakora my friend got us as an appetizer was dry and left a bad aftertaste in my mouth. When my main entree came (malai kofta curry with paneer naan) the sauce was bland, the koftas tasted stale, and the naan was very undercooked (doughy).

My friend said the saag was better, but I'd rather pay more at better quality places than waste my time here again.
I came here for a Chicken Vindaloo and all I left with was a stomach ache and a whole lot of toilet action.

Keeping rating at 4 stars.

I came here again to grab some chicken tikka marsala and garlic naan to go since I was short on time. The wait was somewhat long (nearly 15 minutes), but I treated myself to their chai tea while I waited. The food was okay, probably worthy of 3 stars, since the naan was cold and a bit soggy by the time I got back to my place. Also, I feel like their chicken portions were smaller. However, I'll give them the benefit of the doubt since they did try to wrap it up nicely.

Tip:
Food is never as good to-go. Always dine in if you can. Especially if it's indian food.

I can honestly say that my friends and I are the most qualified people to review this restaurant. Collectively, we've probably eaten here 30+ times between us in the short time it's been open. The standouts are: the chicken tikka wraps, the naan (esp. the kashmiri naan), chicken madras, and all the chaat items. Some of the vegetables are a little too bland (dal tadka, navratan korma) or a litlte too oily (chili paneer). The service is quite good. The chai is pretty good (a little creamier, but not as spiced) as that at House of Curries. Overall, this food is not as heavy and probably a little better spiced than at House of Curries. I recommend!

An unassuming, nondescript doorway on a dimly lit stretch of Bancroft is all that marks the entrance to Indian Flavors Express (IFE). But do not be deceived: the modest entrance leads to a cavernous interior that rarely exceeds 10% occupancy. Two large wooden pillars of questionable structural significance dominate an interior that is distinctly reminiscent of a Quiznos.  The popular sandwichería most assuredly occupied the same site in the not-too-distant past, as suggested by the space's ultramodern wall décor, and leftover Quiznos fridge and condiment bar. While we question many of the decorative choices that have been made here, we view this as an overall positive since we expect the décor to be the focus of lively dinner conversation.

In terms cleanliness, much to our surprise, the water carafes and tumblers appear free of the whitish calcification that is so often the cause for suspicion at many Indian restaurants. Indeed, the porcelain chai mugs, plates, and utensils also appear clean after manual inspection.

A standard spread of the usual North Indian dishes is punctuated by nine naan options, as well as a wrap section. As is the general trend (vide infra) the menu lacks any hardcore South Indian items, which is perhaps for the best because the restaurant staff, while authentically brown, do not appear to be from the South.

A unremarkable offering of free chai is complemented by a thick, tart mango lassi.  IFE performs well in the two meat-containing eigendishes examined: lamb vindaloo ($8), and chicken tikka masala ($7). The meat components of both dishes taste like real meat, and the tikka masala is amply spicy, creamy, and full-bodied. IFE makes a more mediocre showing in the vegetarian eigendish category, aloo gobhi ($6), which lacks sufficient spiciness and contains slightly undercooked potatoes (horror!).  And while the samosa chaat ($5) was excellent, there was variable performance among the other styles of naan.  Most notably, IFE resorted to one of the oldest Indian baker's grifts in the book: fake cherry pie filling in the Kashmiri naan ($2.5).

Unlike most restaurants, IFE excels by allowing the client to choose his or her own spiciness level by providing jalapeño slices and hot pickle relish.

Overall, despite some peculiar missteps, the quality was generally good and we find the exceptional cleanliness, unique décor, and complimentary condiments sufficient to give it a solid  (three samosas, our rating system). Given the middle of the road prices, one rupee is most appropriate. Given the high somosa-to-rupee ratio (3.0), we suggest you give this cavernous gem a closer look.

This is large place, although you couldn't tell from the street, because it has no street frontage. (And it would be valuable Bancroft Way street frontage, which is the street right across from the campus of UC Berkeley, right across from the famed Sproul Plaza, where the Free Speech movement of 1964 started, where protests against the Vietnam War with sit-ins all occurred, where 80% of students pass through.) 

It would be great if this restaurant had street frontage, because all the Indians, after IIT in India, all Indian Comp Sci or EECS majors want to go here, to world famous UC Berkeley. 

After all, it was at UC Berkeley, ranked #1 by US News for CS, that created BSD (Berkeley Software Distribution) for Unix. From BSD and its later versions, Sun Microsystems developed Solaris for Unix Workstations, Microsoft used TCP/IP (Internet Protocols) for WIndows, and Darwin, the basis for Apple's OS X were built upon, as well as the beginning of other Open Systems.

So you see, it would be good to have street frontage so Berkeley students, including Indians, could come in and have a cup of FREE CHAI! (Yes, they offer free chai tea, but don't tell anyone!)
 
But it doesn't. It has only been open 5 days, and the place has a seating capacity of 113, and I came here on Cal Day, a huge open fair for perspective Cal students, thousands of potential customers for today and the next 4 years roaming Bancroft. And nobody knew about this place. 

So I grabbed some To-Go menus, and went out front to Bancroft Way, and started shouting 'FREE CHAI" and handing out menus. Because that is how I roll, just trying to help a new business make it. Many businesses have failed in this exact location because of the same problem: huge space, and nobody knows it out on the street to come in. 

I also suggested to the owners that they should offer FREE WIFI and have a large screen TV showing Bollywood DVDs on the back wall. And someone (like a cute, exotic, starving UC Berkeley student) should be handing out coupons out front. Like Jamba Juice, 3 doors down was doing. And they didn't need to. 

They have a large menu here, with all your typical Indian offerings, from Pakoras and Samosa appetizers, Chicken and Lamb dishes of all variations, Vegetarian dishes, a dozen Breads, even Indian street food. All the prices are reasonable (Chicken Vindaloo $6.50, Rice $1.50, Mixed Veggie Pakoras $2.99, canned soda, $1). 

It is designed for quick meals for students, with a order and plastic table number system if you eat in. Food is pretty good. I was stuffed. 

So come in here and get the Indian food now, because this place will fail. Trust me, the odds are against them. Large rent, large place, little street access, large menu, no Wifi, no Bollywood movies, a lot of competition, students paying higher tuition so with less money, no catch to get you to come in or keep coming. Except for the Free Chai.  

I tried to help. This place is a 3 star now. If they put in my suggestions and survive a while longer, it is worth 4 stars. Hurry!

We ordered butter chicken, chicken tikka masala, three orders of naan, two orders of rice, and lamb and chicken samosas. Medium spicy for the curries. 

Okay, so the place is spacious, bathrooms are clean, and the entire place is clean. It does feel empty, but whatever. Free tea and the water tastes pretty alright. Eating utensils are also clean, but the mugs are chipped. I have no complaints on the water glasses or the pitchers. Plates are clean.

Onto reviewing the food.

So you order at the cashier, and you get a number and they will ferry your food over. You get your food fairly quickly. I like that.

I've had butter chicken and chicken tikka masala, and for some reason, this place's curry strongly reminded me of pumpkin. It's rich, sweet, sour, and whoah, not spicy at all. I've eaten this dish at several other places. and never have I had this pumpkin feeling. Also,  apparently, my chicken tikka masala and my dad's tikka masala have different spice levels, which is weird, because we ordered the same thing! Mine apparently is spicier, according to my brother. Now, the spice levels for all of our dishes were not spicy at all, especially compared to other curry places. I was expecting a kick that never came, which was a little disappointing.  Overall though, the dish is quite mild in taste and heat.

My brother's butter chicken, I felt, was almost inedible. I tasted a headache in that curry. It was very... heavy. I much preferred my own dish. Minus one star, because I actually do love butter chicken A LOT. 

Naan and rice were nice. The naan wasn't burnt, and had some crispy areas and some chewy areas. There was something oily brushed across it, but I didn't feel any of it on my fingers, nor did I taste it. Tastes pretty good!

The samosas, according to my brother and his girlfriend, were so-so. The lamb samosa was overcooked and way too salty, and she ended up dumping out the filling and replacing it with curry to make a diy curry puff. Minus one star.

Portions look small, but actually they are quite big. Very stingy with the chicken though! And the chicken wasn't like it was super special either! I don't remember how the chicken was, but I remember I didn't have much. 

Overall, a pretty alright place. Decently cheap, and portions can be shareable. I don't get the heavy feeling that can come from eating curry, but maybe it comes from not stuffing myself with Indian food to begin with.

I thought it was pretty sketchy at first because I came and the entire place was deserted....Hahah. I was literally the only one there other than the cashier and cook. But I decided not to judge since it sorta is in this hidden grottolike location.

I got the lamb tikka masala! My favorite indian dish (other than son naan). It comes with only the sauce and lamb, typical for Indian places and it was about $8. I think it's more expensive than House of Curries/Naan and Curry. 

The place is roomy and really clean! There's a bunch of seating and you can get your own toppings and stuff. Berkeley has plenty of other Indian food locations that I think are a little better

Having lived in India pretty much all my life, I believe I have a fairly good idea of authentic Indian food and this AIN'T IT.

 I am especially wary of Indian restaurants where the owners and/or cooks are not Indian. Call me prejudiced but in my experience, when you walk into an Indian restaurant and see non-indian cooks and owners, its probably going to be pseudo-Indian-tailored-for-american-pallet  type food which can be good sometimes just not authentic. 

Anyway I had the aloo tikki chaat at Indian Flavors Express. It is traditionally considered street food and consists of potato patties, garbanzo beans and any number of spices. Their aloo tikki was pretty bad.The only thing I could taste was a lot of salt and chaat masala which made this dish way too tart. The potatoes patties seemed like they were made a week ago.

I might give this place another shot since a friend highly recommends it. But I am disinclined to get anything from their series of street foods ever again.

i want to like this place so much.  ive been a number of times.

first off, it would be SO much better if they didn't dump a ton of salt into all their food.  seriously, some of their dishes are inedible due to salt overload.  and the food seems to be getting saltier!  such a shame. on the plus side, perhaps customer feedback can help them realize what they are doing wrong (hint hint)

second, if you want spicy, when they ask how spicy, reach across the counter and slap the dude, and say, "this spicy, times 10".  they just dont seem to get "spicy", "deadly spicy", "indian spicy", its like they just put in more salt when you ask for heat. 

their service can suck pretty bad too, if you eat in.  if you don't get your food in a reasonable amount of time, hassle the staff, there's a good chance they forgot.  don't expect to have your wait acknowledged with an apology or comped food either.

Two days ago I learned that I'd been accepted to both of the graduate schools to which I had applied, and I'd been planning my celebration dinner ever since.  I knew my celebration would be Indian food, and I was planning for House of Curries.

I saw this place on my way to class today - Grand Opening!  When I got to class the girl next to me was eating some kind of soup that smelled like delicious curry, so I knew I'd be stopping in after class.

I *often* get a craving for House of Curries' amazing Chicken Tikka Masala (spicy!), but I have a disability and my mobility issues usually prevent me from making it over to Durant Ave.  This restaurant, on the other hand, is perfectly located for me!  (There is a small set of stairs going into the restaurant, and I didn't see a ramp - for those who need to know.)

I was really surprised by how nice, clean, and big the place was inside.  (Previous reviews have accurately covered it in detail.)  The man who took my order seemed genuinely friendly, and I sipped the yummy FREE chai while I waited for my to-go order.

Now, about the food.  I always get the same "sampler" at a new place:

*Chicken Tikka Masala ($6.50)  I ordered it "spicy," and it was VERY mild.  I would definitely go for the "extra spicy" next time.  Lots of tender, juicy white meat chicken chunks (WAY more than House of Curries!), and the sauce was well-spiced.  It was creamier than I'm used to, and a bit more bland, but this may have been due to the lack of mouth-searing spice that I usually get.

*Lamb Karahi ($6.50?)  also "spicy."  This dish seems to run spicy everywhere I've had it, so this "spicy" version was pretty hot (but not too much so).  Very generous with lots of HUGE chunks of lamb.  So, I've had two kinds of Karahi: one that was basically fajitas - just meat and sizzling chunks of vegetables.  I've also had Karahi at House of Curries, where I was surprised to find they had basically put all the ingredients in a blender (except the meat chunks) and the result was totally a puree.  Indian Flavors Express is in the middle of these two versions, but definitely leaning more toward big chunks of vegetables.  It was actually a perfect balance.  Unfortunately there was a TON of oil floating on the top when I opened up my to-go dish at home.  Overall, delicious but disconcerting.

*Vegetable Samosas ($2.95) Fabulous!  However, the bottom of the paper to-go package had a large pool of oil which had even begun to soak through in the few minutes it took me to get home.  The samosas themselves were large and really well spiced, but so greasy (like, super shiny and slippery).  Bonus points for including mini containers of chutney and mint without me even having to ask!

*Plain rice ($1.50) Good!  Not as oily as House of Curries, which is a plus.

*Plain naan ($1.50)  I just wasn't a huge fan.  The naan was hot, thick, and soft, but it definitely had a doughy taste, kinda like eating Bisquick batter (don't judge me, you know you eat Bisquick too).

I ate my fill tonight - celebrating my success!  I also have enough left overs for 2 to 3 meals in the coming days, which is perfect because who has time to cook or go out during finals.  

I'll definitely go back when I get my curry craving but can't get over to House of Curries.  Free lemonade too, btw!

This place is alright, we wanted to try it and contrast it with House of Curry, but House of Curry is still much better.  We had the chicken tikka masala and the paneer tikka masala with garlic naan.  The naan was delicious, although I usually prefer it when it's more crispy, and it was more squishy and soft/doughy.  The flavor of the tikka masala wasn't bad, but I think I still prefer house of curry's tikka masala.  They also offer free chai tea like at the house, but it just wasn't as good.

This place is WAY overlooked! Their naan is sooo good. I don't know what they put on it, butter? It must be butter because it comes out fluffy and crispy. I can just eat the naan without the curry. 

Curries: lamb vindaloo 
Curry didn't separate like, huge oil blob on the top and curry at the bottom. Everything was tasty 
Can't go wrong with Chicken tikki masala 

Super roomy inside, clean, & service is friendly. Definitely check it out since its across the street from campus (lot closely then HOC).

Okay, due to time management issues, I'm going to try for shorter reviews. Is that even possible for me!?! I dunno, we'll see =3=

I've graced this place a total of three times: two for the chicken tikka masala, and once for the buffet.

Their chicken tikka masala is sooooooooo creamy. Like, cream^2! The only place that has a creamier creamy tikka masala sauce is Currylicious, but you have to hop on the 51B AND the 51A for that. And I'm pretty lethargic (unless I'm on a treadmill lulz).

The chicken is sometimes dry, sometimes tender and moist. I haven't been here often enough for statistics to give me an answer.

Their buffet is a GOOD DEAL. For $10, you get their chicken tikka masala, along with a million other things that are all pretty tasty! Service is a bit slower here, but at least there's free chai tea!

|| C L O S U R E ||

The chicken tikka masala here is so good. So so good good.

If I were to rank the Indian places I've eaten at, it'd go:
1) Currylicious (in Oakland)
2) Indian Flavors Express
3) Mount Everest Restaurant
4) Shalimar
5) Naan N' Curry
6) House of Curries

Don't be afraid of venturing in this little alcove, a nice little Indian restaurant await you. They've got lots and lots of tables, but also great for take out if you prefer. This place is big and they can fit more tables in if they want to, but unfortunately, this place is still a little deserted. Though that could be a good thing if you're looking for a quiet place to grab a bite during lunch. There is even a few tables outside for patio seating. The service is good and they are well staffed. They have individual items and items for sharing. I tried their lamb biryani and it was pretty good. You get a choice between mild and spicy unlike most other place. I got spicy of course, but it was actually not that spicy. It was a nice, big, steaming plate so I have a little box leftover for a midnight snack. The tandoori wraps are pretty big too, about the size of a super burrito. Like most place, they have free chai and the chai here is good! Yay!

Cute little rooftop restaurant with honest, simple thai food. Not fancy, but tasty and filling. Went on a Sunday afternoon for a pre-dinner snack. 

ATMOSPHERE:
-cute, quaint. located upstairs on a deck, with flowers and trellises and wooden deck tables. great on a sunny bay area day.

FOOD:
-garlic pepper pork: tasty and rich. a little fatty for my taste, but not so much that i wouldnt order it again!
-pad see ew: it was ok. it was normal thai noodle dish, nothing particularly great or bad.

SERVICE:
-great. quick without being overly intrusive.
-quick clean up and water refills.

Who can forget the restaurant on wooden planks? My recent visit was my third or fourth time at the restaurant, but unfortunately it was my least favorable experience. The quality of the food has hit a low. It's still a great place for groups with the quiet setting and long tables though.

Here's what I ate:

Calamari was very average. About  10 small pieces of seafood on a big bed of lettuce. Nothing special.

Stuffed chicken appetizer. Two decent sized pieces of chicken, but overall was considerably expensive. Stuffing was a bit dry, but chicken was fried well.

The pumpkin curry with pork was a huge disappointment for being an item on the executive chef's menu on the front page. The curry was way too watery, and was really bland. The pumpkin, along with the veggies, did not contribute at all to the dish. I did not taste any pumpkin flavor in the curry 

Papaya salad was really boring. Small dish with barely any taste. Was hoping for large orange papaya slices, but received thin crunchy white papaya slices.

I don't know how all these dishes failed to impress, but Jason, if you're still in charge, you gotta do something!

Good food, reasonably friendly service - slightly more than student food, slightly less than a restaurant... 

Food: I had the Thai Beef spaghetti - a fusion dish using clear Thai style noodles served as spaghetti in a bowl, topped with beef, broccoli and a smooth peanut sauce. Large size portion thanks to a generous serve of noodles beneath, though the other dishes served to my friends were significantly smaller.  

$1.50 for a can of coca-cola. 
$6.95 for lunch.
+ tax
+tip (they precalculate 20% on the bill)

Unfortunately they were anxious for us to leave - bill on the table before we had finished eating and asking every 30 seconds if I was finished while still chewing food, fork in hand and noodles still in the bowl.

I like this place better than Thai Basil, in the Asian Ghetto. 

Their chicken kabobs are good, their pad thai is good, their curry is good. Overall, I enjoyed my meal here with some friends. 

I also recommend getting their dessert! They have tasty sticky rice with mango. 

I also like it because you can use your cal1 debit card!

i think their chef changed or something because i stopped going there. the pad thai was awful; overcooked noodles and just a nasty aftertaste. 

however, in my first time actually dining there (the others were take-out), they redeemed themselves. the coconut soup was perfect and not too spicy. and the special for the day- the pumpkin curry with chicken- was amazing. 

service was pretty bad but they were busy. felt very rushed whenever they came over and were not there when we needed them.

I used to come here all the time because I lived on Channing Way for a year and a block away for another year. I must say they have gone downhill in the last couple of months. 

The last time I was here the service was horrible. 

I had told my boyfriend how much I loved this place and wanted to go back so we went there for dinner one evening.The waiteress seemed unattentive and lost, and I literally had to flag her down. Finally she came over and we ordered. My boyfriend wanted to substitute his sriracha for curry sauce and we offered to even pay a little extra. We do this all the time since he does not like hot food, and usually this service comes for free. The lady came back to inform us that we would have to pay an extra $8. $8 for SIMPLY sauce?? We said no thanks and moved on to finish ordering. 

The food was overpriced. I swear their dishes used to be reasonably priced but the last time we were here, the portion size had gone down and the prices were WAY higher than before. The portions were so little that I ordered a shrimp curry and my boyfriend ordered some fish curry but after we finished these dishes we were still hungry and had to order another dish.  My shrimp curry had 4 pieces of shrimp in it. True story. 

The place did not took too clean and seemed very congested. I think it had to do with their inability to sit people properly. Tables with 5 chairs had 2 customers on them and tables with 2 chairs had a third chair added to seat another person. 

I don't know what happened to them. Like I said I used to LOVE this place for years, I really hope they get their act together soon :(

The portions and food here are good, not outstanding. All of our portions were huge and the price was great ($8 for a huge bowl of noodles, yes!). I had the chicken noodle soup which was yummy, but I noticed there was very little chicken in it! All of the other dishes my friends had were good (pineapple shrimp rice, spicy pork). The service was so-so, our water was only refilled ONCE and it was at the end of the meal. But for the price, a good meal!!!

Wow it's been 2 years since I've been here?  Time flies.

Came here today, a nice Sunday afternoon, for lunch.  This time I eschewed the tried-and-true pad see ew and had...garlic pepper pork!  For $7.25 you get a generous portion as the lunch special, including rice, salad, and a little samosa-like appetizer.  

As someone previously mentioned, the pork is tasty but quite fatty.  It's good for a once in a while indulgence.  The samosa-like side was crispy and potato filled, also very good!  I could probably eat a whole plate of those.  Mmm.

Didn't have enough room for dessert, but I asked for a mango sticky rice to-go, since the rest of today is going to be spent holed up studying and I'll deserve a reward for that right?  (later edit: the sticky rice was amazing and had lots of big chunks of mango, I'm a fan!)

They didn't have duck curry as a lunch special otherwise I would have made good on my vow from my last visit and had that instead; but the pork was a good substitute.

If ever I am craving Thai food this is the place to be! 

We walked up a flight of stairs and were greeted with waitresses right away. They asked us to sit wherever we wanted and since it was a lovely sunny day we decided to sit on the patio.
