The outside patio was not very busy and had plenty of tables to accommodate people if it gets super busy. We then got our menus and began to order right away. We knew what we wanted. We ordered: the spicy pad sew ew, garlic pepper pork and pineapple fried rice. Some of the items weren't as pricy because we went during lunch time during the weekend and they even had a lunch menu even on the weekend which is a plus!!! In addition, to our food we had ordered thai iced tea and ordered their deep fried bananas with coconut ice cream for desert! yum!!!

The service was great too! The waitresses were very accommodating and making sure we were good. We didn't sit outside for very long because there were flies that were attacking us. LOL So we decided to move inside. This didn't really bother us because it was originally our choice to sit outside. But the FOOD is GOOD. TWO THUMBS UP for this THAI SPOT!

Decent. 
Initially for Thai places, the 1st visit i always get a pad-see-ew to see if i like their style of a common dish i can never get tired of. But because of the flaunting of "the original home of the garlic pepper pork" and the fact i would only be in berkeley for a couple more days, i decided to order the Garlic Pepper Pork and a Thai Tea for lunch. 

Service as an overall is just average, nothing too flashy and from my walk around the area before stepping into the building, i didnt notice any Rats like a previous yelper mentioned.. (truthfully that scared me a bit) 

Anyways Garlic pepper pork; the lunch set version of this came with a mini salad topped with pesto, a vegetable somoas, about a cup of rice, and the garlic pepper pork.. oh and a slice of orange; what type of meal would it be without that orange piece? xD 

To start out, i thought the salad was interesting and dove straight in with the green paste. I was more than happy that the salad was dressed lightly with pesto. This is a combo I have never seen at a restaurant (but then again i rarely get salads...) And hey, pesto is good stuff. The Somoas was nothing special but it was crisp and only made the meal as a whole more complete and filling. Now at the pork, it was oily and fatty but Ok at best. Nothing too special about it either which was slightly disappointing. 

Thai tea.... too much ice, mediocre at best =[ shame really...

I initially was going to give this place 2 stars but because of their performance in the quality of delivery food ( and you know how bad that can turn out to be...) and the pleasant lunch I decided to go with a 3 Star instead. 

Will come back, no rush though.

The garlic pepper pork was so tender...very similar to bbq pork but there is that hint of garlic that gives it something extra. The pork is so tender..you can cut it with a spoon. The green curry was the perfect amount of sweet and finished off with that kick. The veggie were crisp and the chicken wasn't dried out. The curry over rice is pretty heavenly. The price tag is more than affordable...around 7ish for lunch and 9 for a bowl of green curry.

Mediocre Thai food.  

Okay service.

I've had their pad thai and pad see-ew.  Both okay.

I really like their shrimp rolls though.  Shrimp marinated in garlic spring rolls served with this tangy sweet sauce.  I come here just for that.  But the rest of the food is kind of just bleh.

I like the outdoor seating.

I have to say the basil eggplant here is among the best I've had at Thai places in the bay.  The other dishes I like are the green curry, although it is more standard Thai fare, the ubiquitous spicy curry that all know and love.  The meat eaters favorite is the honey bbq pork, very flavorful and has a great BBQ taste.  

To top it off the service is always good, and the owner often comes by for a friendly chat.

The seating outside was great and the service wonderful (responsive and checked in on our food and water 2-3 times). However, my dish, the red curry chicken, was lacking. It just wasn't very flavorful, and the cuts of chicken were somewhat fatty. I also got the Thai iced tea, which was mostly milk rather than tea, so not too delish. My last complaint is that they only had white rice as an option--for which they charge (but so many charge extra now that rice actually costs money with energy issues and the yin-and-yang of biofuels). Those I went with seemed happy with their dishes, however, and I tried one of theirs--some beef dish, and that one had some flavor. I guess it's a hit or miss, and for the money, it's worth a try. But, stick to recommended dishes, I'd say.
the pad see ew was really good. but it took FOREVER for my food to come out. don't come here for lunch if you have to be somewhere at a certain time.

If this is your first time going to Thai House, you HAVE to try the Garlic Pepper Pork. It's their most famous dish, and after eating it, I went to that restaurant every other day for lunch, for a month straight. It's THAT good. The flavor is absolutely delicious. 

That being said, I also love the duck fried rice (it's hard to find on the menu). The flavor is very distinct and the duck really adds to the taste. 

My friend and I go there so much that the owner of the restaurant knows us now. He really cares about his customers, so if you go when he's around, you'll have a good experience.
Grossly underrated by me when I was in college, this place is pretty darned good!!  :)
good thai, good prices.
Ordered Chili Beef lunch special, beef was so tough, couldn't even chew it.  Told the wait staff and she got the manager, and he told me that's how it is. REALLY? Bad FOOD Bad manager!!!!

Amazing food, great thai iced tea, wonderful service. I was with a club with about 15 people and the servers here came by frequently to make sure the food was good and always kept our water glasses full.
Delicious Thai food. I specifically enjoy the noodle dishes. Service is good and quick. Prices are completely fair. One of my new favorite places to go.

I ordered for delivery, and got Basil Eggplant, Spring Rolls, and Red Curry. The spring rolls were alright, and my roommate said the eggplant was so-so. However, the red curry was horrible. Completely flavorless -- I could have made better with the store-bought thai paste. I had to add honey and peanut butter to try to make it tast better -- worked slightly. What a waste of 10 dollars, I threw half of it out.

Several years ago I thought this place was good.  More recently though (2007), the curry seemed too thin (watery) on one occasion.  And I'll never forgive them for the worms I found in my green beans on a separate occasion.  They didn't charge us for THAT dish but the owner-lady wasn't all that apologetic.  Try Cha-Am or Dora (Laos-Thai) place next to it on Shattuck and Cedar instead.

I am totally, genuinely, happily surprised.

I've been to a number of Thai restaurants in Berkeley and they were okay but nothing special. Most were basically a step up from Thai fast food, and only Sabuy Sabuy II was worth remarking on. The other night, though, I ordered Berkeley Thai House on a gamble from Eat24hours.com. I started worrying when it had been 1hr15m with no sign on the food. Luckily, just as I was on the phone with BTH the driver showed up, very apologetic about the traffic and demonstrations he'd been caught in.

As soon as I cracked open the containers a delicious, rich aroma greeted me. Once I put it in my mouth (tee hee!) my taste buds agreed with my nose. This is really good Thai.

Here's what makes it so good: well-balanced, not overpowering, rich flavor with fresh, quality ingredients. I like a lot of flavor, but nothing left a really strong aftertaste, my place didn't smell like fish sauce, and the leftovers were startlingly good. Prices were reasonable and the delivery option is great. 

I will absolutely be back.

Addendum: I've ordered several more times. Sometimes delivery is quick, sometimes it takes 1h15. Sucks. Most of the food has been delicious but some is decidedly meh. Best so far: Pad Kee Mao, green curry, Param Vegetables.

I have been looking for a Thai restaurant that makes delivery and so I tried Berkeley Thai, as the reviews are decent.  I can't say how the food would have tasted had it been hot (it was lukewarm by the time we ate it), but, as it was, I found it inedible. We ordered the pepper pork, which was extremely greasy and fairly tasteless, the green chicken curry, which had very little flavor (couldn't taste the basil at all) or chicken in it, and the vegetarian egg rolls which were mushy inside and out.  I don't like to give bad reviews and don't, unless I feel people need warning: the food was not good. But it may just have been a bad night.

I had a tofu pad thai (with egg ok) at a spicy factor of "2." It was decent. 

The service is very good. The restaurant is clean and has that kind of Thai flare you would see in most Thai restaurants. The water was limitless and my glass never went empty. The location is great; close enough to "stuff," but also far enough to be tucked away from all the hustle and bustle from the campus. Dinner for two was about 26$ not including tip, which isn't conducive to most college student budgets.

Beautiful outside seatings. They accept credit cards for orders of 10 dollars or more.

Ordered pad see-ew. Flavorful. Second time, ordered green curry chicken & rice. Delicious. 

They have lunch specials during the day where the rice comes with the dish.  No specials for dinner, and they charge for rice. Maybe a dollar or fifty cents per head or so for rice.

I think they have coupons on their website also. Give it a go!

I hadn't been here in years, so I was cautiously optimistic about returning (I don't remember my past experiences as being good or bad). 

I like the ambiance, but since it was a cold night, it was really crowded inside the restaurant on a Sunday evening at 6pm (and no one wanted to sit outside, obviously). Nevertheless, my party of 3 was seated within 10 minutes, so not too bad. But in general, the service throughout the evening was pretty slow - it seemed like there weren't enough servers to accomodate the amount of people there.

Anyhoo, on to the important stuff - the food!

We ordered: garlic pepper pork ($8.95), pad see ew with beef ($7.45), and the pad scallops special ($13.45).

Garlic pepper pork was delicious!! Pretty good portion, but it was just that it was so tasty that we all wanted more of it! Great mix of spices and flavor with spicy dipping sauces on the side. I really appreciated that because I don't like spicy food but my friends do so they enjoyed the sauce.

Pad see ew w/ beef was also really good. Nothing out of this world, but well cooked and decent amount of meat and flavor. Just wished there was more of it!

Pad scallops were really great too. It's a little pricier, but they had big scallop pieces and we each got about 4-5, which I guess is OK. 

The overall feeling of Thai House is that the food is great and flavorful and yummy and tasty. The problem is that they just don't give you enough of it. The portions are smaller than I would have liked (or what you would normally get at like Thai Basil) so I left feeling slightly hungry and a little gypped.

Would come back, but not my first choice for Thai food in Berkeley.

The Waitresses were very friendly, however the Owner seemed a bit Lazy, but did come up from her Highness Chair to ask how we were doing.

The Pad Thai & Thai Coffee was delicious!

When I come to Berkeley I'll know to hit this place up again.

My friends and I went on a busy Thursday evening. The host was kind of intense. We were seated, and ordered. We were all sharing our food family style... but apparently you have to order one dish per person in your party. That's minus a star. There were five us, four dishes was already more than enough. This is the only place I know that does this in Berkeley. I think it's a little mean in a college town. 

Part of the price of the meal definitely goes into atmosphere. The decor is Thai authentic.  

Anyway, the food was pretty good, especially since all of us were Laotian or Hmong (the cuisines are similar). Though all of us were encouraged to order dessert we passed, but received free Thai Tea on the house!

Just went there for dinner for the first time with friends, the place has nice decor, but I would not go back again. I would not recommend people going there especially in a large group, they will charge you a  $0.20 fee for splitting the check and 15% gratitude for groups with 6 or more people. 

Overall the food portion are small for any dish especially for the price (at least for dinner). Garlic pepper pork was decent, but Pad Se-Ew was horrible that it was very greasy and salty.

I do not like their service, there is almost no service (but given that the place was packed when I went), they almost forgot about my order since I came in late to meet up with my friends and we had to remind the waiter. In addition, they charged a fee for splitting the check and 15% gratitude even though there was not much service at all except when they brought us 2 jug of water.

Do you like alien spit? Go here. Loads of bland, slimy sauces volumized with corn starch. Hair included.

I learned my lesson not to pay attention to restaurant reviews by college students. They are a different class of eater.

Okey.. STAY AWAY! This is a complete disaster! 
I was here for a night to celebrate my friends birthday. We called in advance, ordered a table for 30 ppl, and even paid a deposit! We were 27 people who came, and they still had no idea how to handle the situation. It started with a complete chaos just setting the table. The poor server was bossed around and yelled at by the owner and it took aout 20 min just to get water on the table. We then placed our orders. One of our friends, who live in San Fran was just stopping by, but H to the no if he was allowed to even sit there unless he ordered something. He got peanut sauce... (was not good at all i might add). It then took us from 7.30pm to 8.32pm to get the first dish. I believe the last one was on the table at 9pm. I had to send my food back in because not only was there no flavor, it was also cold. They then popped in the microwave and sent it back in. The average mood of the table was pretty annoyed when the food finally came, and only 2 of the 27 guest really liked the food. Most were just like.. its O.K. So we wee running very late for the birthday party and had to run. It then ooh us approx 1 hour to pay even though we had made it very clear even before we ordered the table that we wanted to pay serrate. So he even charged us for splitting the bill, but also added on the standard 15% tax, which is 15% more then any of us had planned to pay. In the end it turn out that we paid for the same swish twice, and when we present our receipts to show him (the owner I'm guessing) this, he gets very upset and claims he has not done anything wrong. We even had the receipts! He then just walks away and say that if we have a problem with it we need to file a police report... we are seriously considering it.. =/  So to sum it up. The food is not even worth the money,and the horrible service and long waiting just makes it a nightmare!

For $12, the seafood curry was definitely worth it. There were prawns, scallops, mussels... in a creamy coconut milk curry--you know, the kind that could make it into a Body Shop lotion bottle or something.

If I remember correctly, they had a pretty colorful menu, as in, there was yellow curry, red curry, green curry... slow down, stop, and go?? yeah, I dunno... they were all spicy too, including the green. cuz I got the green and it did not GO well... ha...ha--okay, bad pun.

but seafood curry, go get it! everything else curry, stop right there.

cute rice pots though. reminded me of genie bottles.

Both times I've been here they haven't been so busy- it looks like when they're busy they can get too rushed with customers, but luckily for us the service was friendly and not at all rushed. The Thai Iced Coffee was supposedly really good (I didn't have any) but the Thai Iced Teas were mostly ice which was disappointing. They are very good at making it as spicy as you want it; order it medium and it really comes out medium- they don't assume you can't handle spiciness just because you're white. The beef was broccoli was yummy- lots of sauce, the garlic pepper pork was just as good as everyone says, they do tofu and eggplant really really well, and they have very good peanut sauce. My sister was a little turned off by the whole pieces of basil leaves, but i didn't mind since they worked well with the dish. I've sat outside both times, never been inside, but the patio is certainly nice.

tasty that food that's close to campus, but there are better thai places (Racha Cafe). I used to eat at Berkeley Thai House a lot more until on one occasion my friend did not like his food (he also used to eat here a lot), and when he requested that the food be taken off the bill since he hadn't eaten more than a bite or two, the server rudely denied his request and slapped the bill on the table. I've been here since and everything has been fine, but i can truly say the food quality/taste has slightly declined since I used to first eat here.

Something I've noticed. A lot of restaurants around Berkeley have hundreds and hundreds of yelp reviews. But when searching for the term "vegetarian", there are fewer than a dozen matching, and when putting in "vegan" nothing comes up. I find it interesting that a place with so many reviews in a veg-friendly community doesn't have enough reviews to help others find vegan friendly food. So here it is:

A group of 13 of us came here on a weekend night, including 2 vegans, and a couple vegetarians. They got a table ready for us in about 25 minutes. Service was really nice, but the bill splitting had to be limited, which is understandable. 

I ordered the standard Pad Thai with tofu. It was a very generous portion, and was very delicious. It wasn't dry at all, but was actually full of sauce. There was a nice spicy kick to it. However near the end of the plate, the sauce got overwhelming. It was too salty and had more of a reddish color than the usual orange tint that I'm use to seeing at other thai places. The red wasn't from hot sauce or chili powder either. It's like they make their pad thai sauce out of something that's not tamarind. Or they combine it with something that's usually not seen in other pad thai places.

Service was great and they were super friendly. Paying the bill is always a challenge, but we got it done. I ended up not having cash, so I paid the bill in its entirety with my card, and everyone paid me back in cash.

Overall great place, but I'll order something different next time.

Just had lunch here - I got their spicy eggplant lunch dish, which was quite delicious! It came with rice, a small salad, a slice of orange, some kind of fried yam (I think?) appetizer, as well as a decently-sized portion of the eggplant and veggies. The eggplant is well cooked, and I enjoyed the appetizer and salad as well. However, service was so-so - I came with a friend, and it took quite a while for them to bring out the food, and in general the waitstaff was pretty inattentive. In addition, at the end, there was some deal with using credit cards to split the bill and our fare went up by a slight bit. Not a big deal at all, but because of those issues, I'm knocking down this place from a four-star rating (for their food) to three stars overall.

I have not tried too many Thai Restaurants but I have to say I love this one. Service is ok; the guy that works there is the nicest one :) Can't wait to go back and order some sticky rice and mango :) ... and the eggplant dish of course!

What happened to this place?

I used to love Berkeley Thai house - the food was good, the service was prompt and polite, and the decoration is adorable. 

For some reason, the last three times I have eaten there I was very disappointed. I usually order the Pad-see-ew or the Pad Thai (classic staples of thai food). Anyway, the last times I went there, the food had changed flavor dramatically. It seemed like the sauce was completely different, and the food was drowning in grease and sauce. Also, the orders my friends made tasted equally bad. Maybe they got a new chef? 

Needless to say, I don't think I'll be going back. The service is still good and the decor is cute, but I am disappointed with the food. Too bad because this used to be my favorite Thai place in Berkeley. :-(

If I were you I would NOT order delivery from this place EVER, especially if you care about service.  I require so little from delivery guys... this guy calls me from his car to inform me he can't find parking and I have to come downstairs. When I protested there was parking right here on my street, he told me to Calm Down Ma'am! over and over.  What a jerk.  Then when I tried to point out his attitude was harsh, he said, whatever lady, then order from somewhere else.  I said I will, and I'll be in touch with your manager.  He said as he walked away "well I'm the owner".  SUCH a jerk.  He doesn't deserve your business.  Call someone else, who cares about his customers and his service and doesn't take delivery as an  opportunity to lay his bad trip on someone else.  I'm keeping him away from my home and I suggest you do the same.

Berkeley Thai House is one of the better Thai restaurants in the bay area. Located in the heart of downtown Berkeley. The restaurant environment is very welcoming. It's literally a house that be retrofitted to a restaurant. The food is exceptionally good.

The pineapple fried rice is sooooo so good here. Best around the area, IMO.

My friends and I ordered a couple entrees and decided to order another dish of pineapple fried rice because it was that good.

Other dishes were okay though. We ordered the satay chicken, pad see ew, and pad thai. I've had better at other Thai restaurants around the area. The pad see ew here was a little tasteless and the noodles weren't as chewy as I would've liked it to be. I think the pad see ew is tastier at Thai Basil than at Berkeley Thai House, but maybe I went on a bad day haha.

The waitress was super accommodating when we asked if we could switch tables since it was really chilly sitting by the door. She said she couldn't do that, but she closed the door for us instead.

Overall, it was a good meal. It's a little bit pricier than other restaurants, so I won't be going here all too often (college student budget ftw) I will definitely order some pineapple fried rice to go sometime soon though!

OK for dining in.   Delivery is horrible.  They get lost, and if they don't want to deliver to your area, even if it is on the map (I am in the Berkeley hills right now) they will add another $10 minimum charge and still take 2 hours to deliver it.

Just last weekend I took a mini trip to UC Berkeley.  My friend who lived in the dorms was trying to think of a place to eat at which had vegetarian food for me.  We decided to yelp up some places around Berkeley which had vegetarian foods and Berkeley Thai House showed up. My friend then told me that she ate there before and claimed that it was "pretty good."

I must admit, she's right. Upon entering the place, I was surprised to see how much more fancy it was on the inside in comparison to the sign that I saw outside.  I guess looks can be deceiving.

Anyway, after going over the menu, I picked out the Basil Tofu (btw,  I was very pleased to see all the vegetarian options they had. YAY!).  My friend ordered some type of pork (Garlic Pepper Pork pehaps?).  All of that was with rice for two.  I really enjoyed my Basil Tofu, mostly because of the sauce that everything was mixed in.  The bill came out to be $21.30 or something as such, which I found to be reasonable.

Employees were kind enough to refill our drinks every time they were near without us having to ask.  I found that to be a plus because I never run into waiters and/or waitresses that do what they be doing in this house. Hooray, I'd come back again.

-Vegetarian Review- 

This place was quite pleasant. We ate outside on their patio for lunch. Nicely decorated with statues and plants. It was probably my favorite part.

The food was good. I ordered Pad See Ew. Being one of my favorite Thai dishes I  probably have too high of expectations. The dish is quite common so I try it everywhere and I can't find a satisfactory replacement for my memory of Pad See Ew from a restaurant that is now long closed. 

Their's was good but not the best I've had (not including my memory). I wasn't really a fan of the sauce, although it was plentiful whereas this dish usually seems to be dry. Decent amount of broccoli (always a plus).

The best part of the meal was the potato curry puff type thing that they give you with ever dish. We liked them so much that we ordered more. They were stellar. The Thai Iced tea was also quite good.

**I did feel a little off after leaving this place so I think some piece of the meal may have contained some fish sauce (I'm very sensitive to it) or other meat sauce/oil. On the other hand I did eat it quick so it may be that. Not sure either way.**

If you are in Berkeley and looking for a sit down Thai place I would recommend this one. If it is nice out by all means sit on the patio.

4 stars for good food, very good service, and great patio!

Berkeley Thai House is one of the better Thai restaurants in the Berkeley area. Although dishes are a little more expensive compared to other restaurants, the food is definitely of better quality and is totally worth the price. 

Meals are designed to be sit-down and include dishes that are shared. You can also order dishes for yourself. One that I would HIGHLY recommend is the Garlic Pepper Pork! I've heard so many amazing things about this dish, and the dish even surpassed my expectations upon tasting it. The pork reminds me of KBBQ-style ribs, except served with sauce on the side and not nearly as oily. This is a dish you just HAVE to try if you ever stop by here. I also tried the Pad See-Ew, a noodle dish with meat and vegetables. The noodles were extremely flavorful, but I felt that the beef was a little bit overcooked.

I also ordered the Fried Banana with Coconut Ice Cream. I've had better fried banana, but the coconut ice cream makes up for it. The ice cream contains little chunks of coconut that blend perfectly with the taste of the ice cream.

Great food! I really love the beef salad, it's one of my favorite dishes! Overall a great experience with friendly service, just be careful about parking in the lot across the street. I almost got a ticket because of expired time!

i always thought pad thai comes with shrimp, not chicken or beef.... anyways, the food was alright. i saw some place that said that it was home of the original garlic pepper pork, but i didnt see it on the dinner menu

i heart thai iced tea. my friend, who doesnt normally drink liquids, finished the whole thing!

This was the first restaurant I ever ate at in Berkeley, and I've eaten there many times since, but it remains my favorite Thai place.  Like Allison B. said before me, the pad see ew is absolutely delicious, and their barbeque chicken is also way, way tasty, with a huge portion for the price.  Sticky rice with mango, a dessert staple at most Thai restaurants, is truly excellent here during the right season.  The atmosphere is great, little decorative touches going a long way to set the mood, and the front patio area is a lovely place to sit when the weather is nice.

Their food is okay, depending on what you order. I remember ordering their sweet rice banana fried desert, which was good, but not differentiating from others in any special way. I recently went there and ordered their basil beef, which I highly do not recommend because it tastes just plain awful, but my friend ordered the regular Pad Thai and grilled pork, which looked reallyyy goodd. Just a word of advice to stay away from the basil beef, and probably basil chicken as well.

Decent food, nice decoration, and close to campus: 3 stars.

Long wait and no parking space: minus 2 stars.

It's good. I like it. It hit the spot when I want to upgrade from asian ghetto.

the things on the 'specialty menu' section are pretty good. Pra-ram (veggies, meat, and peanut sauce) hits the spot. Pad thai is really tasty here.

Finish it off with the fried ice cream. It's good.

Don't get the thai iced tea. You'll feel nasty because it's so filling. Especially with all the strong flavors of thai food, you don't want to overload your palette.

Overall, a chill place to eat, or to take that date that you're interested in at the moment, but need to go study. It can be an excuse to hang out'on the way to studying'. You nerd. 

Go bears!

My experience was quite positive here. I'm a vegetarian and I found a fair amount of choice here. The food was excellent and in contrast to other reviewers so far the service was very good.

I went at about 7 PM on a Saturday evening, so it was quite full, but they managed to get us a table v. quickly and were quite attentive throughout.
The price isn't unreasonable given the overall quality of the food.

probably the best thai near UC in berkeley, but that's not saying a lot.

also, it seems like they charge extra for *every special request*, even if you ask for "less _____."  weird.

but if you're stuck near campus and need some decent thai, this is your best bet.

Nice restaurant with average food and a great place to eat outside when it's sunny, but please can the waiters/waitresses avoid to take your glass with their dirty hands when they take your water glasses to fill it :)

+1 for ambiance
+2 for food
-1 for unidentifiable, murky & wet food item on the outside of the glass of my thai iced tea (debatable whether the glass was clean on the inside)

Haven't come here in about 3.5 years. This brings some nostalgia as my first ever food review on Yelp was to complain about the service. Some things don't change.

I usually come here only for their Mango Sticky Rice and Fried Banana with Coconut Ice Cream.  The mangoes are always incredibly juicy, sweet and ripe.  They have real pieces of coconut in the coconut ice cream.  So good!

If you want decent Thai food, come here.  The food isn't amazing or unique, but it's good.  I like the Pad See Ew, Eggplant Basil, and Green Curry.

I went here a few days ago with a few friends for a birthday. I actually never heard of the place before. To my surprise it was pretty good and the price was not too expensive. The people there are very nice and go out of their way to make you comfortable. I love the environment . The mango sticky rice is  one of the best I've had in a while. This is a place I definitely recommended to others!

Mediocre 

Found this place while walking on Telegraph. This place looks and smells good, but is nothing special.  I stopped by because the stomach was growling.

I had the lunch order - Basil chicken ($7.95). It filled the void, but it definitely didn't  fill the urge of eating good food. Not much chicken in on the plate..More sauce

It came with a salad .. yay?

Went here last nite w 5 of my sisters,  Ordered a bunch of different plates and everything was delicious, service was FAST & prices were low.  Our total bill was $80, including a meal to go.
Nothing comes with rice, so make sure to order that on the side, $1 per person. 
Please do yourself a favor & order the Garlic Pepper Pork!! mmmmmmmm, I want a plate right now.. 
mouthwatering*** my absolute fave. 

xoxo

i came here a few years ago and it was okay, nothing that I would particularly go back for but my friend suggested it so I went with it. 

I ordered the Pad kee mao. Where are the noodles, I ask you!? I felt like I was eating stir fry instead of noodles. There were a lot of bell peppers which I am not too fond of and like i mentioned, very little noodles :( I was sadly disappointed. I paid almost 8 dollars for a dinner that didnt fill me up. :( FAIL. 

On the plus side, I guess the restaurant was cute, the napkins were soft, and the staff was pretty attentive. SMH. I guess I'll wait a few more years to come back.
Love the environment, food is okay but a little bit over-priced. I'd recommend Bangkok Thai noodle if you don't chase for  elegant decorations.
Really tasty Thai.  Prices are good, but not great... service can be hit or miss.    Good ambiance.

Thai house is one of the places in Berkeley I don't go to very often because it's a little expensive for every day eating, but I love it every time I come.

My staple for a long time has been the yellow curry with rice, which I always request mild.  It's very flavorful with a small amount of kick to it.  The chicken is perfectly cooked to be soft but chewy, and the potatoes are soft while still having a little bit of crunch to it.  The yellow curry sauce over rice is always satisfying and can feed me for two meals.

Recently I discovered that Thai House has beef noodle soup, which has been perfect for the cold weather!  I love Thai soups because they're salty but a little bit sweet at the same time because of the spices, but not in a way that makes it unsavory.  Thai noodle soups have much more flavor than other soups I have had.  I love the meatballs (which like all Asian meatballs do not have the texture of meat at all), and the chunks of beef are soft and tender.  It's the perfect thing to warm a tummy when it's cold and raining.

My boyfriend ordered the green curry today, and liked it.  It was spicier than expected, but the vegetables (string beans, carrots, zucchini) were not overcooked at all, maintaining their fresh crunchiness.  The only thing that bothered him is that rice does not come with; you always have to order it on the side.

The usual pad thai and pad see ew are good!  They also have free delivery that you can order online, but there is a minimum purchase of $20.  The service is very attentive, and my water glass was never less than half full.  The ambiance is very nice and quiet--classier than a lot of places are UC Berkeley campus.  Thai House is definitely my favorite Thai place around the area.

So maybe I'm picky because I used to live in South East Asia, but I feel I've become aware of what good "American" Thai food is.

Ugh. Have been here several times because everyone on campus likes it, and I really don't. Their pad Thai and curries are far too sweet, even for Thai curries. It's not the right balance at all. Their Thai beef noodle soup is way too salty. Their pineapple fried rice isn't bad, but I really don't remember it being that great either. 

The thing that keeps me coming back is the waitstaff. I always come with a million people and they always gladly accommodate us.

They're food has been the same as 4 years ago; and its good! Previously, I would get the duck red curry, which is my absolute favorite. This time I got the duck noodle soup, which is not bad either. There garlic pepper pork is super good! The pork is tender and they marinated it the perfect way. Its so amazing. You must get the garlic pepper pork, if you come here!

The service is good. The thai ice tea is good too. And also they are pretty quick for an one hour lunch period. 

My club at Berkeley always do business with them, and they are so friendly about it! Jason, the manager/owner, is the best guy ever. He truly wants to help the clubs out and is always happy to do fundraisers for us.

I've always really wanted to like the Berkeley Thai House, but I never really seem to want to come back. I can't seem to place it... the food is decent, but just not the type that makes you crave it like other Thai restaurants.
Good lunch options, I always end up getting pad thai, pad-see-ew. But Tom-yam noodle is good too!

This is an ideal place to have dinner with a big bunch of people due to its ample seating. Its proximity close to my old apt meant that I frequented this place a lot for reunions w/ old floor mates. But other than its space, I'm not too wowed anymore with this restaurant, especially with a huge variety of other Thai places around campus (i.e. Thai Noodle II down on Telegraph).

Food: All of the main dinner items DO NOT come with noodles or rice. You have to add another extra dollar to get that, which blows my mind. You can literally go to another Thai restaurant nearby and get the same dish (i.e. BBQ chicken) and have it served w/ rice for the exact same price. The last time I came here I got the Pineapple Fried Rice, which was very bland (I had to keep adding chili sauce to it for an extra kick). The only upside was the portion size. 

Price: Expect to spend about $10-12 here for dinner, which is decent compared to the area. But I personally think you can get better quality food at other nearby restaurants. If you come with a large party, you can get split checks for an extra $0.20. The last thing that irks me is they INCLUDE gratuity (15%) into your bill. I personally feel that as a customer, it should be ME that has the final say on what tip I give you. 

Service: nothing exceptional that warrants a 15% mandatory tip; they do take reservations though. We had a party of 8 and it was slightly annoying when they made us squish into 2 square tables instead of spreading us out over 3. 

If you want a better Thai restaurant experience, go to any of the Thai Noodles (on Telegraph or Shattuck) instead. Or even go to Thai Basil! It'll be cheaper.

I just had this for lunch earlier today and I'm still burping Garlic Pepper Pork...and it's still good. Earlier this week I had the Pad Se Ew and it was the best (it always has been). It's no wonder Thai House is the favorite of many locals. 

Don't order the Garlic Pepper Pork if you're outdoors in the daytime. The bees will do anything to go after the sweet chili sauce that comes with it. The waitress was kind enough to transfer us indoors.

This place is pretty ok. Cute ambiance (in a converted old house), vegetarian-friendly, clean bathroom. The menu is rather typical, but the curries taste good--I think it may be the case that I've only ever had the curries here, in fact. Two caveats: when it's crowded, it gets LOUD inside, and when it's cold outside, it gets COLD inside. 3.5 stars, I think.

Solid lunch option near campus. I enjoy most of their dishes, but their yellow curry noodle soup and the garlic pepper pork are my favorite. Sometimes I deviate from these choices, but I always wish I hadn't. Their outside patio is nice on a sunny day. 

Good prices for good food. 

Note: for the time being, they're not validating for the Channing Garage anymore. The garage changed policies and many stores/restaurants don't validate for them right now.
Pad Thai was great! I like the outdoor seating!

We haven't been here in a month or so and I'm sooooo craving my thai shrimp rolls and Pad Kee Mow!  This is by far my FAVORITE Thai Restaraunt.  The food is great.  The wait staff is very sweet and the owner completely ROCKS!  See you soon Jason!

This place is about the same as nearby Thai Basil foodwise. It looks a lot classier though, food is presented attractively and they actually have waiters. I would recommend any of the dishes with duck - they do a damn good job roasting those birds. Portions were a little small. The waiters are pretty friendly and it's definitely a laid-back environment, especially if you sit out on the patio for lunch.
Pretty mediocre Thai food. I love Thai, good or bad usually. This was so mediocre I wish I didn't choose Thai.  Service was slow even though it was a slow night.

I've eaten a lot of Thai food in the bay area and I always find my self coming back here. It's probably because I'm always in the area blowing most of my money on music. There lunch specials are cheap and every thing is really fresh. Theres a nice outdoor area for dining and just chillin.

I used to go there all the time after my classes to get my Thai fix.
Honestly, I usually judge the yumminess of Thai food by how good is their Pad Thai. 
Their Pad Thai is rather sweet but still very good.
I love their outdoor sitting area when it's sunny.
Strictly mediocre.  The only reason they get two stars is the patio is so nice on a warm day.

Not the best food I've ever eaten, but I like the atmosphere (especially their patio) and the lunch deal is good value and taste for the south side.  When I worked at UC on the south side of campus I'd really struggle to find someplace decent for lunch with coworkers and this always ended up being a favorite. There's enough selection for everyone to find something they fancy (I always go for the red curry veggies) and it's spacious enough that we never had to wait.  It's a bit sucky to pay an extra dollar for brown rice, but it is really lovely and you get a little fried wonton, salad and fruit with every meal. Can't beat that.

We ordered 2 Thai iced teas, garlic pepper pork,  combination seafood, and sticky rice with mango. Bill: $33!! Sounds like a good deal for a nice sit-down restaurant.

Firstly, their garlic pepper pork is AMAZING. The sauces that come with it are delicious and perfectly complement the pork. It was so mouth watering delicious that I'm drooling just thinking about it at the moment. Love love love. It's their signature dish for a reason. Perfection.

Combination seafood was blah. Would not order it again. Sure it had plenty of mussels, scallops, and some shrimp, but the flavor was mediocre. Maybe it's because we had the garlic pepper pork first so this dish was so crappy in comparison.

Loved the sticky rice and mango too. We ate it so deliciously slow to enjoy it.

Overall, the meal was very satisfying; we weren't stuffed silly with large crappy portions, but we weren't hungry. Perfect portions.

Best fried rice with roasted duck in Berkeley. The staff is very friendly, food has never been disappointing and the prices are very good. We come here regularly for lunch and it is so difficult for me to change my order to something else rather than fried rice with duck!

I would give you three stars but for being by campus I give you four (even though it doesn't matter because I don't live by campus anymore). What does matter is DELIVERY! 
The other day, I had one of those days, where I didn't want to get my ass up and I had no excuse for it. I got really hungry and still couldn't get my little ass off the stupid couch (and no, I wasn't high. I'm just fing lazy). So I just decided to call Thai House and YIPPEEE they have delivery! $20 minimum. They take about 20 minutes and its delicious. 
I love the eggplant garlic dish. Their curries are decent. My bf LOVES mango and sticky rice and they do it well here. 
It is definitely worth spending an extra dollar or so to get decent thai food that won't give you the runs. In other words go to Thai House not Thai Basil!

Ordered the Pad See Ew and split an order of Fried Bananas with Coconut Ice Cream with friends for dessert. Delicious and impressive. I also took small spoonfuls of the green curry and red chlie tofu dishes from my friends' orders; both were great and I look forward to trying the green curry with rice next time I come around.

And yes, I'll definitely stopping by again soon! 
The dessert was BOMB, people. It's a lot so I suggest sharing. My group of three (including me) managed to be totally content with one order of Fried Banans and Coconut Ice Cream. There are other options, like Fried Ice Cream, both Fried Bananas and Fried Ice Cream... Be adventurous and give it a try.

Go there as a place to sit outside on a nice day, that is off Telegraph Ave.

Food: Portions stingy for the price...add a bowl of soup or complimentary salad--please!

Service: not too fond of the service here - it can be a bit slow at times, especially when waiting for the change....

All in all, the food is decent, but for the price, I think i can get better Thai food elsewhere for cheaper.

Best dish: chicken soup (really rice noodles, chicken and tofu in a yummy coconut curry sauce to slurp down)...cost $7.25.

Not spectaular, not craptacular.  A little lacking in taste. 

The beef was a bit too sweet, and disturbingly tough.  Very tough. 

Yellow curry (with chicken and potatoes) was almost all chicken, no potatoes, and had an odd flavor.  

Pineapple fried rice was disappointing - lacked flavor, had very few bits of pineapple (soggy), had only 4 shrimp, and had tons of onions and was loaded with raisins.  (Raisins, wtf?)  

Veggie Spring Rolls - I've experienced way better, wouldn't bother to get these again. 

The Man was happy with his choices - a vegetable plate, a load of peanut sauce, and eggplant thingy.  But he was hungrier than I was.  

I wouldn't get food from here again on purpose.  
The free delivery was great, as was the online ordering (LOVE!) but the taste didn't justify the cost.

One of the better Thai places around UC Berkeley. 

Food: decent 
price: reasonable
service: ok
decor: very unique. i liked it!

This place gets kinda crowded so try to beat the rush during dinner time by coming before or after dinner prime time hours. 

It's very typical Thai food, nothing too special but it was pretty good. I ordered the all the curries, green, red, and yellow. They all tasted the same to me and had practically the same stuff in it, but it wasn't bad. Rice was pretty tasty and I don't normally like rice. Worth trying :)

Let me begin with the fact that no one ever approached my table to take my order. After a long time of waiting, I had to go to the cashier to make the order. A few minutes later, my food arrived and I can honestly say that half of the pork I got was pure fat. The thai iced tea was disappointingly tasteless, the water cups smelled and were dirty. I will stick to thai noodles II down the street from now on.

On a strong recommendation from a friend, I tried this place three times.  Each time I got a lunch special, and each time it was disappointing.  One time I had the chile beef, supposedly a house specialty, but it really tasted like mediocre mongolian beef with basil substituted for onions. Another time I had prawns with red bell peppers, baby corn, and oyster sauce -- nothing was very good individually (I'm sure the peppers were frozen and the corn canned) nor did anything go well together.  One time I had the basil chicken with chiles, onions, etc. and that at least was okay, but still I certainly would not go back there again.
Great for when you're in the mood for a sit down restaurant, of which there aren't that many in the area.  Very accomodating to large groups too.
Friendly service complements very delicious food! The restaurant is in a cool, converted house, which made for a nice, relaxed atmosphere. The Chicken Satay and Red Curry are not to be missed!

Quick. Lunchable. Blend.

I walk past Berkeley Thai House everyday on my way to solve challenging problems. I can't help but be distracted every time I walk pass here. From the stairwell entrance, the luring smell entices me to have a civilized sit-down meal. 

Quick service here for lunch. If you are on a time crunch and want a decent healthy meal, perhaps even vegetarian, Thai House has an ample selection of curries, noodles, rice dishes for the budget-aware Berkeley students. 

Lunchable. I am impressed by their lunch specials. Today they had prawns with Thai basil, red & green peppers, mushrooms and bamboo. The proportion is good enough to split between 2 people. It is a cool spot for a casual lunch date on the weekdays. Several sunny yet private locations for intimate conversations. 

Blend is the name of the game for Thai food in the Bay. I am quite disappointed by the lack of spice, vigor and heat in their dishes. If you are a fan of hot, spicy food, make sure you tell your waiter to jazz it up a notch. 

Here's my personal experience with Thai places. Please do not take offense. Before I started going to Thai places with my girlfriend, when I ask for hot, it's full of heat & grasp. However, due to my girlfriend's ethnicity, even though she adores the hottest food on the planet, sometimes even more than me, the waiter always seem to tone it down according to her skin color....I don't know why...but just a thought. 

Bottom line: Cheaper if you split the plate. Get lunch specials. Skip the long lines at other places.

We went inside and didn't even eat. My group and I were so turned off by everything! Lol.

Though I didnt give them a chance to taste the food, I just wanted to share my experience with thee yelpers! (So that ONE STAR is towards SERVICE)

First off we walked in and and was turned off by the aroma. It was like being at one of your aunt's stanky house, doesn't turn on the fan when she cooks or open any windows, just let the steam & smell stick to the walls. Ha.

So the waitress was walking us to a table that already has PLATES & SPOONS and all the jazz while all of a sudden another waitress goes "NO, that one!" Okay I guess.....?

When we sat down the table was realllly wet!!! Like HELLLO? You could not WIPE IT down with a DRY PAPER TOWEL!?! or give us a DRY TABLE!?!? Then they get the plates and spoons put it on the table. Give us our water. BTW! The water is already poured in their cups and they are all right next to the door. Uhhh, I wanna drink water that comes right out of the sink/fountain. Dont even know how long that water has been there for?!? Eughhh!

We ask for straws for our water, so she grabs some and puts it on the plate while one of them fall on the WET table, while she SAW it fall!! She didnt even get us a new one!

So then that's when I check reviews on yelp and saw that the food wasnt great at all. 

With that said we left, cuz we did not want to waste our money on BAD SERVICE, yet alone BAD FOOD.

Ordered the pad see ew and Thai iced tea. The pad see ew noodles were flavored well and did not have too much soy sauce. The beef was tender and flavorful. The Thai Iced Tea is one of the better flavored ones, not too sweet yet when the ice melts it does not taste diluted.

I love the food here, especially the garlic pepper pork lunch special. It's really lovely. The service, however, leaves a lot to be desired. I ate there for lunch today and for the first time they told me there's a $10 minimum on credit card purchases. I didn't make a stink about it, and told them to charge $10 for my $7.88 meal because I didn't have any cash. They were kind enough to only charge me the $7.88, which I appreciate. What I would have appreciated more is if they had told me before I tried to pay with a credit card and had signs prominently posted, as well as a note on the menu.

In addition, I witnessed them outright deny two customers who wanted to use a coupon because it was "already used". When the customers explained they had tried to use it before but were told they couldn't use it because it was after 5PM. Unfortunately, the restaurant must have entered their coupon code before telling the customers that they couldn't use it the first time, after that it was no longer valid, even though it hadn't been used. 

The type of rigid service I witnessed today is both unfortunate for the restaurant and the servers who work there. I know that if they had charged me the full $10, that extra $2.12 would have gone straight to the pockets of the owners, The server would've gotten a nice note from me thanking them for their service and explaining how the restaurant managers had taken the tip I had planned to leave by implementing this stupid policy.
Berkeley Thai house has the best thai food in Berkeley bar-none. I've had most of the menu, but what keeps me coming back is the pad-see-ew which is to die for. Definitely would be my last meal.

We accidently stumbled upon this restaurant and  decided to try it.
The decor is quite authentic. Most of the servers with the exception of a couple barely speak any English.
We had ordered soup,appetizers and a few entrees but the entrees showed up way before everything else.
They have a spicyness rating system 1-5, we ordered everything 2-3 spicy, half of our food was WAY BEYOND even a 5 and was not edible by anyone in our party. They did however correct their mistake eventually.
Our service was super rushed, they try to get people in and out as fast as humanly possible. The cheque showed up at our table a minute after we finished eating and even before our table was cleared.

The quantities were adequate. I would rate the food quality to be average. There are nicer Thai restaurants in Oakland/Berkeley.

I came here last summer for a friend's birthday & I actually liked the place.  With a good first impression & a good catering deal, I decided to come back here fro food for a school event.

At the beginning everything was great.  I gave the manager/owner my budget & my order & she took care of everything.  I was quite impressed because she held her composure throughout the process even as I was having her split up the check every which way.

The day of the event rolled around & everything was fine: delivery was on time, the order was 100% right, & the service was amazing.  Sad to say, it all went down hill from there.  The food was cold, bland & just all around not @ the same standard as the meal I had before.

After the event was over, the experience only got worse.  Part of our order was paid for by a purchase order (PO) from the school.  For some reason unknown to me, the PO didn't get processed.  At first, the owner/manager called me & was very nice about it.  As time went on, the PO still wasn't processed (for reasons still unknown to me) & the number of called because more frequent & more aggressive to the point of rude.  Eventually, the school took care of things & the calls stopped.

This experience left a really bad taste in my mouth with this restaurant & with the way it is managed.  I am giving it 1 star since it gave me an OK previous experience.  With that, I will not return to this establishment again.

Ok, I don't really use yelp but this time is an exception.

Me and my other 2 friends went to this place after our meeting. There was barely anyone in there because it was 2 PM. We decided to sit around the table where there was a sun because the weather was rather cold.

Then, one of my friends said that the sun is in her eyes. So, we decided to move to the nearby table. Then, I heard them talking among themselves in Thai. What they don't know is that I AM THAI AND I UNDERSTAND THAI! They started to talk behind our backs in Thai just because we changed the table. One of the waitresses even went into the kitchen and told the chef about us. These were some of what they said: "why did they choose to sit at that table in the first place if they want to move afterward?" "Pretend like you don't know they changed the table and make a confused face when u serve them!" This went on for around 10 minutes until one of the waitress noticed me looking at them.

I was going to go yell at them but my friends told me not to. I didn't even finish eating and they soon gave the bill to us! So, I ate my food even more slowly. Then, my sister called. I thought of myself, "it's time for revenge." I talked to my sister IN THAI! I made my voice loud enough so that they could hear me. Too bad I couldn't see their faces...

Moral of the story: DON'T GO THERE. YOU NEVER KNOW IF THEY WILL TALK SHIT ABOUT YOU BEHIND YOUR BACK!

Great ambiance, outdoor seating area is WONDERFUL (friendly squirrel last time I was there--that may creep some people out, I loved it), warm atmosphere inside, great service, YUMMY thai iced tea, GREAT food (i have NEVER had anything I wasn't absolutely thrilled about)

The best part for me is that i stopped coming when I moved away a while ago and I came back and the one server (maybe he's part of the fam that owns the place?) remembered me and my favorite order.  

it has a great family run feel.  Last time I was there, my friend wanted something garlicy and so the server recommended something for her (based on a couple extra questions).  She was totally thrilled with her food.

3.5 stars -- Good food at good prices.

I've come here on several occassions - dates, birthdays, out of town visitors - and have always enjoyed my food. Its a good place to dine and get away from the Asian ghetto once in a while, but is still very affordable for the college students. On a sunny day, its nice to grab lunch out on the patio with some thai iced tea. The calamaries are right on (not all rubbery like some places) and their bbq pork dish is very tastey as well. If you have room for dessert try their tempura ice cream. It's a simple dish, but yummy. They don't make the tempura batter too thick. Thumbs up for this place.

For the longest time I did not like this place because they did not serve my favorite green curry fried rice plate. So I always would either conform with their pineapple fried rice or a dish I didn't know. But my last visit I had the Basil Shrimp dish and it was amazing! I would definitely come here again for that dish. The service is really great too.

Pretty good thai food.  Not my favorite.  Nothing really stands out here, but at the same time, there is nothing here that is distractingly bad.  If you are in the mood for some OK food, Berkeley Thai House is fine.

I've ordered here a couple of times for my fraternity. They've catered some of our dinners before. We usually get trays of some type of curry, beef basil, rice, and some pad thai. While I'm not usually a fan of Thai, sometimes I do crave it and I have to say, I wouldn't come to Berkeley Thai House if I were craving Thai.

While the people who work here are very friendly and genuinely care about me getting a good deal and enjoying their food, I have to say that their food is relatively lacking. I love their beef basil but everything else I really wouldn't say I enjoy; it's pretty lackluster.
The best Thai food in Berkeley.  Good for big groups.

I came here for lunch and ordered the lunch special. Some sort of vegetarian curry that was a little too sweet, but that's how most Thai food is in America. Went back again for a la carte lunch and still wasn't impressed. The prices are pretty reasonable, but if you're looking for Thai food that will kick you in the head good, don't come here.

So delicious!!! The red curries are excellent and the sticky mango rice for dessert is the best. The service is excellent, your glass won't be half empty for long. The have a nice outside patio that's off the street so you can get some air without the bustle of Berkeley. Try it!!! You won't regret it.
This restaurant was recommended by our hotel down the street.  We had pumpkin curry which was excellent.  Service was great, and you could choose to eat inside or out.

I went here with a couple friends and got the duck curry. They both got pad thai and didn't think it was that great. The duck curry was really good though. Tender duck with skin on, red curry sauce, and veggies. I gradually put my side of rice into the curry bowl to soak up all the sauce. MMMM :P

Service was good. We arrived around 7 to beat the rush as there was a line at the door when we left. Prices are pretty reasonable for Berkeley, my dish was $10 plus $1 for rice.

This place is good and sometimes it's fantastic. Portions have gotten smaller as of late, but they still make the best eggplant tofu I have ever had, and their brown rice tastes better than most. Service is SO friendly. If you have to choose between this and Thai Basil which is a block or so away, I would pick this place any day.

FOOD:  Authentic, and yummy.

SERVICE:  Good.

AMBIANCE:  Very cute little place with it's own patio.

Reading all the reviews below, I just had to say something. A bunch of people keep complaining that if you like this food, you don't know Thai. College students don't know how to give reviews, blah blah blah.

I revisited Thai House yday and it was just as good as I remember.

While I may not know Thai, I certainly know YUMMY. And yummy it was. I think the phrase best used to describe the food is orgasm-inducing. Especially the mango curry and friend bananas with ice cream. YUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM.

I love Thai food.   Wherever I travel I always stop by somewhere and try to find something that compares to the Berkeley Thai House.    I've been to the "award winning" places in Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles and elsewhere in the Bay Area.   I've only been to a few that even approach the Berkeley Thai House.   Service was always good.  I probably went once a week for 3 years and am always sure to stop in when I'm in town.     The Pad Thai and  Garlic Pepper pork are top notch.  The Fried Banana is a great way to finish.

WORST PLACE EVER!!!! The rule of a minimum of one order per person is enforced by a semi-bald, overweight, Asian man. He gave me and my friends crap because some of my friends wanted to share, while another didn't want to eat. He claimed that each of his seats are worth $10. He also went on to say that he should just close the place if people came into share. What the heck is wrong with sharing?! In addition to the horrible service by the obese gentleman, they brought out the ice cream before the main course meal!! Ridiculous! However, beyond all this BS, there is a woman who is very nice here, but that's it. PS, remember to read fine prints.

Overall, I would say Berkeley Thai House is good, but not great.

The night we visited the service was excellent - glasses never went empty and dirty dishes did not languish on the table.

The food was acceptable although a bit more pedestrian than is my taste.  To someone who does not consume Thai food regularly, I am sure their preparation would be considered to be quite flavorful, however to me, most of it tasted bland.

We ordered chicken satay, green papaya salad, beef salad, yellow chicken curry and organic pumpkin curry with tofu.

The satay was unlike any that I had ever had - this isn't to say it wasn't good - it was just different.  The standard peanut sauce was replaced by a sweet sauce reminiscent of jam.

Both salads were quite good, although the beef salad lacked any cucumber which is normally part of this dish.

The curries were the major disappointment of the meal.  In Thailand, pumpkin curry is generally too spicy for foreign tastes.  At Berkeley Thai house, it was quite flavorful but had no heat whatsoever.  It tasted more of coconut milk than of curry.  The same can be said of the yellow curry - although this is generally a fairly mild dish.

For pudding we had sticky rice with mango and fried banana with coconut ice cream.  Both were quite good.

I would return here to eat if I were in the area, but I would not make a special trip.  Although I don't know much about the restaurants in Berkeley outside of the "Gourmet Ghetto," I am quite certain I could find better Thai.

Taste: 4
Value: 3
Service: 3

I've been here a few times. The food is good, pretty typical Thai, but nothing special. They're usually packed, so it's hard to get a seat sometimes.

Thai House was just okay. The service and atmosphere were nice, but the portions were SO skimpy. I got the Pad See-Ew with tofu for $7.45 (not including tax and tip) and I left hungry and unsatisfied. Maybe I would have felt better if the noodles were fantastic, but they weren't... They didn't have enough flavor. The tofu and broccoli were exceptional. I just wish I had gotten more. Next time, I think i'll pass on Thai House and go right on to Thai Basil in the Durant food court. I think it's only $6 for the same dish except Thai Basil gives SO much more.

My final say: Money is money and if you don't want to waste it, go elsewhere.There are so many other Thai places nearby (Thai Noodle on Shattuck, Thai Basil on Durant) that will give you more bang for your buck.

Went there in a quite big group of people, probably about 15 and they did a very good job at seating and serving us. I was actually surprised by how efficient they were!

I had the garlic pepper pork which was really really good! I also tasted some of the dishes from other people and they seemed all right.

Not sure I love this place, but I definitely like it a lot!!

The staff here are very friendly, and the service has always been good in my experience. It's walking distance from Campus, and a good place to take out of town friends.

A few weeks back I took 10 people here, ordered a variety of items and mainly ordered what the waitress said were her personal favorites. We were all pleased. The whole fish w green curry was probably the best, although not everyone tried it. 

Good beer, good soup, good service.

I have had A LOT of their dishes... all of which were good, but nothing spectacular. I mean, don't get me wrong... I order from here because I know I'm never going to be disappointed with their food (which I can't seem to say of many other Thai places in Berkeley). 

I especially love their Garlic Pepper Pork and their Pad Se-ew. I always order one of these when I go :) Their curries and fried rice are DECENT, but I would go to Racha Cafe if I was craving those. 

Their service could use a lot of improvement, but at least the food has never taken too long to come out. A good place to try at least once :)

food is pretty good.  smaller portions considering the price in comparison to the very close thai basil, but quiet seating is worth it i think.  pretty good thai iced teas and excellent fried banana with coconut ice cream.  i could go just for this dessert :)
Not a bad Thai restaurant.  The place was kind of dirty.  Food was good.

Ordered shrimp pad se-ew. Got seated quickly on a weekday afternoon. It soon got very busy after 1. 

Food came fast, portions are so small!!!! I was not full what so ever. $8-9 for a small dish? Not coming back. 

The pad se-ew was too flavorful, as in too salty. It was smothered with sauce and I had to keep driving water, probably 3 refills. 

Overall, it's ok.

When I lived in Berkeley, I used to go to the Thai House pretty often. It has sentimental value to me because of the great dinners I had there. 

The most notable dish there for me is the Pad Thai, I would say it's among the best I had. It's very flavorful and sweet and has a very strong taste; not bland. 

I do like the venue though; it's a nice wooden place that has a romantic ambiance.
Mean staff; lied about delivery of food when we were told they would deliver.

I used to think this was the best place for Thai food in the Bay Area, as the only better Thai food I've had is my grandma's and mom's home cooking.  But the last time I went there, the service was sub-par.  Come to find out that the host has left the restaurant and has opened his own restaurant, Sumo Grub.  It's not the same type of food, but it's a great place to go and eat!

Everything I've ever had has been amazing-especially the eggplant dishes (I've tried a few) and the Thai style broccoli! Try any curry dish too, there are variations in spice so don't fret! 

Family style with a group is the way to go!  The service is good, the food is easy, casual and wont hit your wallet too hard!

You also MUST have  a Thai iced tea!

got their basil chicken which was pretty good :)  pricey for the amount they give you though especially since there are so many cheap options in berk
really cute inside :)

Pretty average Thai food.  Yellow Curry Chicken was pretty bland, with overly large chunks of undercooked potato.

I asked for Fish Sauce with Thai Peppers to spice it up a bit, and got Fish Sauce with Jalapenos - big disappointment.   And the Spicy Chicken also used jalapenos.  No Thai peppers, no return visit for me.

Update:  Went agin the other day and had the Green Curry, which was excellent.  And when I asked for fish sauce with thai peppers that's what I got - none of the jalapenos I complained about earlier - so I raised my ranking form 3 to 4 stars!

This is my favorite Thai place in the Bay Area.  They have the best pad-see-ew (sp?) and cashew nut chicken.  There's usually not a huge wait and the service is excellent.  The thai ice teas are pretty bomb too...I really have nothing but good things to say about this place.

Tasty food, and quick service. Likely the best Thai place in Berkeley, with a cheery atmosphere and cool ambiance.. A-OK.

We were in a huge hurry (like ordered & ate in 25 minutes) so couldn't savor the food or experience, which was our fault. Had pad-sew, which was good and some grilled beef dish (also good but meaty). Frankly, we should have ordered more veggies or papay salad- but the experience and food were good.

So I used to really like this place until I ordered the Red Seafood Curry. Honestly, that was a $15 worth of disappointment. It was very watery and the flavors just weren't right. They were pretty generous with the amount of serving though.

I tried the BBQ pork and the owner/manager claimed "the best you will have in Berkeley!" It was pretty good, but I don't know about being the best.

I got really pissy one time when I really wanted papaya salad and they didn't have it.  

The eggplant dish I had once was way too sweet.

Overall, wouldn't go back there unless I am with company that wants to go there.

I really did enjoy this food.  The service was wonderful and I loved being seated on the patio to enjoy the beautiful day.  The prices were reasonable (that's the only thing all those students is good for.. heheh) and the food was great!  Flavorful and fun, a good choice for Thai, although I have other favorites...

I love the decor of the restaurant, the tables, the silver cups, the convenient location, the seats, etc. but the food is nondescript. 

I can't even particularly remember what I had but every time I go, it's nothing special and I kind of regret not having just gone to Thai Basil where you don't have to pay tip, you get more, and it tastes better. Plus, I feel like they use some ingredient that kind of leaves me feeling a little gross afterward. I'm not sure if it's just because I associate negative memories with that place. 

Their delivery comes cold even though they don't even deliver that far out of the Berkeley UC Campus area. Maybe the place is good for like, one or two dishes, but the 3 times I've been there, it hasn't been worth the $. I don't want to go to a restaurant for ONE good dish. 

+1 for having sticky rice with mango (although the best I've ever had was at Krung Thai in San Jose)

"I don't know if I like the decor or ambiance better."

Cool place, though. Co-workers and I came here for a lunch and while the food was very tasty, the portions were underwhelming.

There was a feeling of "oh... that's it?"

We got Spicy Tofu, Red Chili Vegetables, Garlic Pepper Pork, Basil Chicken, Spicy Pork. All of them had touches of red curry here and there, and tasted very flavorful, but we wished there was more.

Prices were $7/8 for lunch with small portions, so mehhh. At the time of this writing, I am actually still hungry. Sigh.

If they increased their serving sizes I'd come back, but it's actually very delicious given it's sort of a hidden restaurant right next to a Princeton Review... Guess I'll come back if a group of friends wants to go, but I wouldn't go back for any other particular reason until a fellow Yelper recommends me a dish that has a heaping portion.

Five words to summarize: Two hairs, two different times.  

I enjoy Thai food and there are many options for Thai food in the Berkeley area, we all know this. BUT, I have found two hairs in my food two different times at Thai House. The first time was about three weeks ago, food from Thai House was ordered for a meeting. I was the first to dig into the Pad Thai and I pulled out a VERY long piece of black hair that was mixed in with the noodles. I have been to the restaurant several times, and opted to forgive said hair. BUT, I went here yesterday for lunch and I found another hair mixed into my Pad See Ew. This time, a short piece of black hair with the follicle still attached. I cannot forgive two hairs at two different times, something is seriously wrong with kitchen cleanliness here. 

The food and the ambiance aren't bad. There's outdoor seating and it's not that crowded at lunch time. But, clearly this place has sanitary issues, go somewhere else instead, perhaps Thai Noodle II right down the street.

As far as sit down dinners go, this place is pretty good. Expect pretty standard Thai offerings, nothing spectacular. They have a great patio area if the weather is nice. Small point, watch out for the squid. They didn't clean mine very well, and got a mouthful of grit when I decided to sample the sauce. Yurgh. Other than that, good standard Thai fare.

I'm a sucker for curry, thai curry especially. So when I was at Thai House during one beautiful Saturday afternoon, I ordered the Chicken Noodles Soup. According to the description, its "thai noodles with chicken, tofu, bean sprouts in mild yellow curry broth". Yuuuum.

Sounds delicious, doesn't it?? Well, it looked delicious, smelled delicious. But heck, it sure didn't taste delicious. The "broth" was just the usual thick yellow curry. It would've been good if it was on the side or just some on rice. But to have your noodles swimming in a whole bowl full of this stuff was not good. It just became too salty and heavy.

I ended up packing most of it home. My sister liked it. But that's only because I told her to add water before reheating it. So there! Point proven!

Sticky rice with mango was yummy though! And the outdoor seating/patio is a plus! =]

My first Berkeley Review! 

I came to Berkeley Thai House for a welcome dinner. The place surprisingly held tons of people inside without it feeling like we were sadines, wish we could've eaten outside, but oh well. Maybe next time I come. 
The thing with Thai is that I never know what exactly I'm getting, I always rely on other people on what to eat.  So I honestly have no idea what I ate, but I promise you it was good! 
Boyfriend had chai tea and he thought it was pretty good. 
The food was pretty good and came quick, and the girls were very attentive. They weren't exactly snatch happy with the plates, but they did want to keep feeding us!

They had these little fried things with vegetables in them that were the best! My boyfriend wolfed down a couple.

Dessert, amazing. Fried bananas with coconut ice cream. I'm craving some now actually...maybe next week I'll make the trip down since I live in northside....and actually know what I'm getting !

I come here a lot because the service is always good and their sticky rice and mango is to DIE for! The curries and rice plates are always good. The pad thai is pretty bland. I always asked for extra extra spicy but its always disappointing. other than that, its a great place.

I came here once before and it was great.

Just went back for dinner, and it wasn't all that great.

I got a noodle dish that was pretty darn good (and I'm sorry, for the life of me I can't remember what it was called... though it ended with "Mau").

The boyfriend got the beef in peanut sauce. I didn't like it, but I don't like peanuts. So don't listen to me. He's had beef in peanut sauce before, and he said that theirs was awfully sweet and molasses-y tasting.

We ordered the fried banana with fried ice cream for dessert (don't judge!). It was listed as a single dessert. We ate it, it was awesome... until we got the check and noticed it was near $9 for the dessert. When we pointed to the menu price of the whole dessert for $4.25, they said that it was actually 2 separate desserts (hence, the $9). 

That alone, was not cool at all.

I've come here several times and it became my favorite Thai restaurant in Berkeley.  The pumpkin red curry and garlic pork chops are excellently made, with seasoning that is spot-on and really bring out intense flavors in the dishes. The fried rice and noodles dishes are also really well-made. The ambiance is nice and the patio seating is an extra bonus (although it's too chilly in the winter).  Thai House is one of the more classic thai restaurants around Berkeley and certainly worth visiting.

Good alternative to Thai Basil if you want more of a sit-down atmosphere, rather than fast food.  Dishes are a tad pricier, but you get sit-down service.

All of the dishes I've tried have been decent.  I think my favorite was the duck curry.  Tom kha is also good (big portions too).  And FYI,  the pad thai is a little on the sweeter side.

Soo convenient now that they take Cal 1 Card.  Overall, I recommend if you are in the area & want to get a nice, casual dinner.

Thai Basil is the better place and it's a block away. The only advantage this place has over it's competition is that is a sit down place. Come here if you are entertaining your family; if you are looking to grub go a bit further up.

you down with GPP?! yeah you know me...

okay excuse the little diddy, but that was an on going catch phrase my friends and i had while we were students at CAL.

for those of you who aren't familiar with the thai house lingo, GPP is their infamous garlic pepper pork.  it's definitely the one thing i always make sure to order whenever i pay this establishment a visit!

for you calamari lovers, their calamari appetizer is on point!  the calamari pieces are HUGE and they come with a sweet dipping sauce too!

if you have room left after your meal, try their fried bananas with coconut ice cream ;)

Average Thai restaurant.  Good food and drinks.

Berkeley parking lot discount is available . (50% off)

However, In Berkeley there are a lot more Thai restaurants where 
you can find better than average taste and services.
Went with my GF, her sister & brother-in-law for dinner tonight.GREAT service! The Pad Thai was just OK and the 'money bags' appetizer was bland everything else was VERY good.BEST iced tea EVER.
It's decent, but I'm still not convinced that there is anything that makes it worth the price other than its great location. Check out Racha Cafe if you want a sit down Thai place.

I hate this place.  The food is decent, which is why I'm giving it at least 2 stars, but the service SUCKS.  The restaurant is crowded, and the waitresses don't pay attention to you.  What else do you expect in an Asian restaurant right?  Well, that's fine, but you're paying restuarant prices for this food, so you should get restaurant service.  Plus, once I was having a bad day and came here to treat myself to Pad Thai.  However, I barely ate any of it and decided to take the rest to go.  The waitress went to box it up and came back, saying that she dropped my dish.  Too bad, no refund, no preparation of a new dish.  To this day I hold a grudge.

This place is pretty good. We had this place rented out for an event. Most of the food wasn't too impressive but it was great location. It really is a very cute restaurant in a house. I think the curry could be spicier and the pad thai could be less sweet. But overall, I ate in a group cater portion so maybe another try at a smaller table order might do it justice. Jason, the manager, is super nice though!

Best Thai food in Berkeley. Love this restaurant, and they have by far the best and fastest delivery. The chicken satay is one of our favorites, and when we have ordered for delivery it always comes hot and fresh. I didn't think it could get even better, but it did when we ate at the restaurant one night. Conveniently located, good food, and really great service. This place definitely gets 5 stars all the way!

As a Cal alum, Berkeley Thai House was a cherished part of the four years I spent as an undergraduate.
