Eating there was always like eating at a friend's home -- the servers used to recognize me because I ate there so much!  Their food is simple, straightforward and errs on the sweeter side, which is what I prefer.  :)  Nothing fancy -- just scrumptious, no-fuss Thai at great prices.

My typical meal at Thai House: garlic pepper pork, chicken pad see ew and pineapple shrimp curry (with juicy stewed tomatoes).  Save room for a fried banana and coconut ice cream for dessert.  

Anytime I'm in Berkeley I have to satisfy my nostalgic craving for Thai House with a visit.  It's worth a trip.

Friend recommended this place for the garlic pepper pork. That was pretty good, but everything else was just mediocre. The service was okay, ambiance and decor was a little out of my tastes - I suppose very traditional tableware and deco. They also have Cal 1 Card advertisement galore like they're trying to lure in freshmen.
You could dip anything in the peanut sauce and it would be awesome. Seriously, try it, just pick up whatever you find lying around the house.
The people at Thai House are really nice.  They hosted our intern banquet last year and were able to work within our budget.  The food was great and there were leftovers!
Place was pretty good

this place is hella small! but nice decorations and warm atmosphere

we ordered pad thai, red curry, eggplant, and chicken... they were all delicious! The guy gave us a free appetizer which was the "tong-tong"? because he lost our reservation for ten people... not bad of a deal. 

The thai tea wasnt that great.. it tasted too watered down and too sugary. the fried banana with ice cream was super delicious though!!

You know, this is actually a pretty nice place to go if you're in the area and you want some authentic Thai food.

The place has both indoor and outdoor seating; both of the areas have a relatively nice vibe to it. The food can easily compete with any Thai cuisines in the area, and the prices are reasonable as well.

I've been here on several occasions for group gatherings near the campus, and it has always been a pleasant experience for me. If you're in the area, this is definitely worth a try.

This is my favorite Thai restaurant near Campus.

They provide both indoor and outdoor seating and can accommodate large groups.

The menu is slightly more expensive than other restaurants in the area, but I think it's worth it for the higher quality.  They also have a cheaper lunch menu!

I always order the pad see ew or pad thai (typical..) and they're both really good and less oily than Thai Basil.  I also tried their praram tofu and pineapple fried rice.  The praram tofu comes with the best peanut sauce I've ever had.  The pineapple fried rice comes in a huge portion and is also very delicious.

good food, cheap prices ($8-$9 per dish) and very attentive service.  but maybe it just seems cheap to me because i live in sf and haven't been in a college town since, well, college.  and we won't get into how long ago that was...

they have both indoor and outdoor seating areas (with heat lamps, although they weren't on when we went) and seem to be a meeting up place for groups of friends as well as couples.

I came here a lot when I was a student, even had my graduation dinner here. The lunch specials are a good deal - your choice of entree with a side of rice for $7-9.  They'll have the daily specials written on a board when you walk in. It's true what everyone says - the garlic-pepper pork is simply amazing. So tasty! It hasn't changed in 9 years, still the best item on the menu. The pineapple prawns dish is also delicious. A good blend of spicy and sweet and generous with the prawns. Recently I tried the chicken noodle soup, which was ok, but I wouldn't get it again. The yellow curry broth was too rich for me, and it had a lot of tofu, but very little chicken. If I'm here with my brother, he will always order the crispy calamari appetizer. I'm not a fan of calamari, but these are very good.

Cute place, really accommodating waitstaff, but the food is just alright. I've gotten the pad kee mao and the garlic pepper pork. The pad kee mao was okay. The garlic pepper pork was actually good, but they gave such small portions for the price. For me, that's the biggest thing about this place - they have good decor and service and decent food, but it's just not worth it to me to pay nearly $8 for small food portions.

I went here yesterday with my friend.  I ordered the fried rice while she ordered the pad see-ew. It was nothing special, though it definitely satisfied my hunger.

The place seems okay, and the waitresses were so nice that they kept on refilling our water glasses after only about a sip or two.

It is worth trying.

We had Thai House cater our largest end-of-year club event. They take purchase orders, which is a big plus. We had a strict budget, but they were clearly excited to get our patronage for an 80+ person event so they gave us a discount to make the meal within our means. It was helpful that they took care of everything, including utensils, delivery, drinks, and dessert. At the event, the food was a big hit--I liked the chicken pad se ew and also the eggplant entree. It is more expensive than other Thai restaurants, though, so I probably wouldn't go on a normal basis.

First time was dinner with friends, second time was lunch with my family. Both times were great. This is one of my favorite Thai places in the Bay Area. Vegetarian options are extremely tasty, especially the Pad Kee Mow. Tofu in their curry just bursts with flavor.
not bad, but the garlic pepper pork was VERY garlicky. be prepared to taste it for the rest of the night... and maybe the next day too.

Went to dinner here for a Berkeley event.  The person organizing it told me she always made faculty dinners here because it was always empty, so it was nice and quiet and easy to hear everyone in our conversation.  The fact that it's always empty made me worried about the food, of course.  I ordered one of their specials, the organic pumpkin curry, and was really excited because I love pumpkin and i LOVE curry, but I was very disappointed.  The vegetables were not cooked all the way, the chicken was dry, and the curry was almost tasteless.  

I'm probably going to another of these faculty dinners, so I'll try something else and hopefully it will be better.

p.s. I talked to my friend who ate here and she had the curry too and said it was pretty bad.  So I guess if you come here just stay away from the curry and you should be good.

This place was always a solid go-to when I was a grad student, but it has nose dived in the last few years.  I could swear they had run out of coconut milk the last time I went, maybe subbing with low-fat milk and sugar instead?  It's a shame to see a place go down hill like this...

I've been to Thai House before, but it is never on my "hot spot" for frequenting Berkeley Thai food since the entrees are more pricey than the rest.

On a weeknight, the restaurant was not too crowded so as expected, the service was attentive.  The waiters were very transparent in telling us what the extra charges would be -- ex $1 extra for white rice, $2 for brown rice, extra expenses for creating separate checks for every individual.  It was nice that they let us know, but still not too convenient.

I was plagued by the amount of choices in the menu so I decided to get their *famous* garlic pepper pork ($9 with rice I think) and thai tea.  As their signature dish, I expected this to be absolutely amazing, but when my food arrived, I received a plate of sliced pork that looked, smelled, and even tasted like Korean BBQ.  Bummer.  It was not too exciting!  As for the other dishes, two of my friends ordered an eggplant/tofu based dish with a lot of vegetables. It looked like simple stir fry with a mountain of vegetables, but it was pretty good!

So I had a coupon for a Free Thai Tea on my next visit from using my Cal 1 Card to pay for the meal and I cashed it.  All I know was that it was pretty fussy getting the bill handled.  Apparently I needed to pay for this meal with Cal1Card again?  I don't know.  Handling the bill could have been less of a headache.

You climb the stairs to a large patio oasis.  It  is a block away from Campus and it is a true escape from the grime of Telegraph Street.  The Berkeley Thai house has hung a big banner on the street that says "Voted Best In Berkeley" so it is easy to find.  I now realize that I see that same sign everywhere.  I am no longer lured by the word "Best...... in Berkeley".  It is just never quite so!  You hunker down into a funky yet spiritually themed interior decor.  It seems like a big house and it actually has great potential to be a relaxing neat space. However - The table glass even even has signs on top of the table cloth to let you know if you are under 30 you will be asked to show ID and cal promotion specials . So if they would take down the hundred plaques, award signs and clutter on the table it may just start to be a warm escape from the urban roar outside their front door.   It just needs to be cleaned up!  The food was average and service seems to forget about you once you are in a chair.  A lot of Cal Berkeley Students in and so it is affordable and okay for a visit if your expectations are minimal at BEST.

Okay - I am never going back after reading the Rat on the Deck post!!!

I am a regular customer at this place and I think it's great food for the price you pay. Even though the food can get a tad bit better their amazing customer service makes up for it. Not only have they been amazing on a regular basis when I go. But I recently had a bday dinner here and we were late on reservations, we were loud and obnoxious and they dealt with us. They lit candles on the cake, gave us a knife and serving plates to eat the cake. He even let one of my friends bring outside food in even though its totally against the rules. I asked them for soo many favors and boxes and bags and not once did they complain We split the bill by like 6 ppl and they didn't care. It was amazing--other places usually give attitude. I LOVE THEM 

Now they recognize me and always know what I am about to order which i LOVE.

A solid thai place but I have other favorites throughout the Bay. The garlic peppered beef is a favorite at this restaurant and I'd highly reccomend it. This place gets very busy especially during Football saturday's and other big Cal events.

Can never get enough of this place. It was a favorite when I was a leaping college kid, and whenever I come back, still a must-have. The place and food is legit. The waitresses are very nice and prompt. I recently had the Pumpkin shrimp coconut curry, which was a special on the menu. Not knowing what to expect, it came out great. With a creaminess to the pumpkin and a nice spiciness from the curry.

I would recommend coming out here when visiting. The prices are decent, so try somethign you've never had before you might be surprised
been goin' here for years...can't say I get much outside of the Gai Yang and yellow curry...that being said get out and get some in this nice intimate spot.

They serve pretty good garlic pepper pork here and their pad thai is average but safe to go by. The servers are nice and accomodating. The price is about the same for most Thai restaurants around here- neither here nor there, pretty alright.

I wonder why this place has only mediocre reviews. One thing that I like is their fast service and the food. I really liked the pad thai and pad kee mau. When I go to thai restaurants I tend to only order rice noodles and maybe their specialities like garlic pepper pork and duck egg rolls. They were fairly good and filled me up. Their satays were also tasty. 

I just wish they had the thai iced tea ice cream that they used to have. 

Whenever I'm lazy, I always come to Thai House because I know I can get good food fast and have a nice thai iced tea to go with it.

Being stuck in a store as the only employee, I cruised yelp looking for affordable, deliverable yummies. I have a soft spot for Thai food and despite some of the negative reviews, decided to try Berkeley Thai house (it's also one of the only places near me open for lunch that delivers).

First off, please note that if you need something delivered for lunch, they charge a ridiculous extra $10. They don't put that on their website or on their menu, understandably so. Since I was desperate, I paid the extra 10 bucks and just ordered two dishes so I had something for lunch the next day.

First, I tried the pad thai. In my opinion, a good thai place is only as good as it's pad thai. The flavors need to be spot on with the right amount of spice. The pad thai from BTH was one of the worst I have ever had. It was bland, had a funny after taste and the tofu had a weird, chewy texture. They also put way too many sprouts on the side, making me think I paid more for a semi-nutritionless veggie than a greasy heap of noodles.

I then tried the green vegetable curry. This dish was significantly better than the pad thai, but still was lacking something I still can't put my finger on. The overall taste was delicate with a little spice, good for a "murmur" of curry when you aren't looking for something to blow you away. I might be a little biased considering I am full fledged fan of bursting flavor and a consort of spices. I also wish the lunch special had tofu in it to add a little protein. Zucchini and rice just doesn't seem sufficient.

I am still in need of some great thai in the berkeley area... the search continues. I probably wouldn't order from BTH again, unless I magically stopped being a veggie and tried the pepper pork.

Hmm...everyone told me to try Berkeley Thai House because it's "really good!" I've been here 3 times now and I always seem to get mixed feelings about this place. 

1st time- I found this place like every other Thai restaurants around Berkeley. I mean, the food isn't terrible, it's pretty tasty, and the price isn't bad too. Maybe people hyped it up too much for me? Maybe I had high expectations? Idk, but I thought it was just okay.
2nd time- I was pretty hungry that day so I found the taste to be better than normal. I also tried Sticky Rice w/ Fresh Mango which was really good. 
3rd time- It was okay. 

I guess overall their food is good. I'd come back again.

I officially hate Thai food.  It makes me so bloated the next day that I just can't stand it, and now, unfortunately Berkeley Thai House has to take the brunt of this hatred.  I ate there last night, I was disappointed by the lack of variation between all the seafood dishes - almost all were shrimp with vegetable and some different sauce.

I can see why the food here is tasty - a lot of the portions have a lot of fat to them. The food here is a little more expensive than other Thai restaurants in town, and their specialty is the 'Garlic Pepper Pork'. This dish is really flavorful but the cuts of pork they use have a lot of fat to them. The noodles are good here, but honestly not greater than other places in town (the noodles are a bit too oily for my taste). Portions aren't very big so it might not be a good idea if you want to split dishes. 

The food is presented very well, the service is friendly (though slow at times especially when getting your bill) and their desserts are delightful (i.e., mango sticky rice, fried ice cream). My advice: avoid beef dishes, as each time I've gotten beef the beef wasn't tender but rather rubbery.

It's a pretty good deal that the average price per dish is ~$8 but it is expensive compared to the food ghetto and the other surrounding places, but the food and ambiance is also better...making this place one of the few "date" places on the Southside of campus.  But that's not why my friends and I were there - we wanted a quality, quick, sit-down bite to eat before the Arcade Fire concert!

We had the coconut milk soup, pad see ew, red curry and prawns with green beans; the pad see ew was the best entree by far.  Everything else was solid and tasty.  The desserts were actually really yummy - fried coconut ice cream and my favorite - mango with sticky rice.  I know it's so bad for you, but they cover the rice in condensed milk.  Delish.

The first time I went here, I didn't know what to order. Our waiter recommended their pork, saying "it'll be the best you ever had". So I ordered that, & it was delicious. And after visiting a many number of other Thai restaurants all over the bay area, I have yet to find pork as good as Thai House's. So far, it really is the best I've ever had

Place makes the best garlic pepper pork!!! On a good day, you can enjoy the seafood pumpkin curry and my favorite dessert is the sticky rice with mango....Jason, the renaissance man never fails to please, he's always attentive, friendly and ensures his customers are getting great service, kudos guys!
the pad thai and the pad see ew was so salty. the women were really nice and inside it was decorated very orientally (idk if this is a word).

This place is amazing--from their service to the food, my friends and I love coming here. There's outdoor seating and very group friendly. I've had multiple dishes, but I just keep coming back for their duck curry. Boneless duck in their red curry I believe. The veggies are fresh and the portions are pretty large. They're also fine with allowing you to split the bill--even huge groups.

Cute location in converted house.  The  restaurant is a huge room which became really loud.  The service was average and the menu was typical.  The food was also average.  The only reason why I only give it three stars was that my Tofu Green Curry came with chicken and missed our 2nd order of our Coconut Soup.  

Not one of my favorite places but the company was good.

VEggie Friendly:  Yes

I've been to Berkeley Thai House two times, but the last time stuck in my head (granted, this was in October):

I came here with my brother and his friend and his friend's gf. Now, my brother and his friend have both LIVED in Thailand, so, I give them clout for their opinion of Thai food, but they are hippy surfers, not the picky types. Unfortunately, one of the dishes that came out smelled like wet cat food. My brother's friend's gf tried to eat it, but she just couldn't, and so my brother and his friend tried to eat it as well (again, they are not picky and were looking at this plate like 'score! more food for me!'). With everyone agreeing that something was wrong, we asked the waitress if we could have it taken off the bill, as there were about 4 bites taken out of the dinner sized entree. She got the manager/owner, who came to our table, and asked if there was something wrong. After telling him, he told is in no exaggeration that that's the way the dish was supposed to taste, and if we had ever been to Thailand, we would know. As I stated above two people at our table have lived in Thailand, so they did know. Needless to say, the manager got more and more unprofessional, to the point of saying 'I don't need to hear your life story' when my brother's friend was explaining that he has indeed lived in Thailand. Rude. In the end, the manager told us that he couldn't take it off of our bill because he has margins to make, to which I responded, I work in a restaurant too, and we would do take this off of a customer's bill in a heartbeat.

I will never be coming back here based on the rude service I received from the manager.

Living on the same block as Thai House makes me really want to love its food, but all my experiences there have been fairly disappointing. My yellow chicken curry was extremely bland, and the chicken satay was dry. Not only is the food unmemorable, but the price is a tad higher than you would pay at nearby Thai places and the service is, at best, lackluster. The waitress brought one of my friend's plates out a good twenty minutes after everyone had been served, despite repeatedly assuring us that it would be out "immediately."

The place is good for groups or people looking for a somewhat more sit-down restaurant setting than, say, somewhere in the Asian Ghetto. But overall, I'd recommend Thai Basil (on Durant) or Racha Cafe (Telegraph/Dwight) over Thai House any day.

i second Anne S! Thai House's fried rice is delicious! it's a little greasier than traditional, Chinese fried rice but the taste is at once more delicate and more flavorful. squeeze a little lime on top and you're in for some crotch-kickingly good eats. also try their spicy eggplant tofu! so so good. only 4 stars because thai house is considerably more pricey than most of the other thai places in berkeley.

This review is probably slightly skewed because I was absurdly hungry when I ate here. I practically inhaled my food. I think the staff was impressed by how fast we were out of there...

The service was fast and pleasant. We were seated immediately and given water. We knew what we wanted so we ordered pretty quickly. Our table was a little dirty from the last person who had eaten there and I had to, in stealth, sneak the chopsticks off another table. Oh well.

My food was great. I ate my fill of the pad thai and Ted ate his chicken. We even had enough left over to fill two take out containers. It wasn't really cheap but for the amount it's not too bad. If I was back in Berkeley again and craving some Thai I'm sure I would come here.

I can't take a place seriously if they can't make something as basic as Jasmine Rice. It had such a strange texture and flavor that it definitely ruined the curry we got. The red pineapple curry by itself was ok, but just ok. The Satay chicken was also just average, but the peanut sauce was quite good. 
Service was average, and we actually got slightly dirty silverware the first time, but they replaced it.
Overall, not going back. Much better Thai within walking distance.

Went here with my advid Yelping sister, Joanne T., and we were both highly disappointed!

Calamari: It's one of those dishes that you like the more you eat it. The batter's really light and the calamari has a bit of firmness to it, which I personally like. 

Siam chicken: Salty salty salty bamboo, sour bell peppers and very dry chicken. I love saucy rice but I couldn't even drench my rice in their sauce cause it was too salty! Oh yeah, and it was not spicy at all.

Prawn soup: Tasted like the soup left over from a $.10 Asian ramen. Not even a $.50 ramen. Yes. A TEN CENT pack. I mean, don't get me wrong, I love cheap ramen but this was just too salty. Would've been good if they lightened up on that salt. 

Sidenote: Um... serving warm, iceless tap water is not cool... If I get the shits from your water I'm coming back and burning your restaurant down!!! =P

We had an awesome time at Berkeley Thai House.  All the food was delicious, especially the Tofu Tad and Roast Duck.  The house white wine was pretty good for cheap table wine.  The best part was our waiter, whose name I didn't get.  This guy had the most beautiful, soothing voice I've ever heard.  It was deep and clear, and he was a born radio star.  You'll know him if you ever get him.  We'll be back!

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

I was invited to dine at this location because of a hectic midterm scheduling fiasco that translated into a complimentary lunch, courtesy of the head GSI. Although that night's chaos wasn't exactly equivalent to lunch at a Thai restaurant, I was grateful nonetheless.

The layout of this restaurant is interesting, as you walk up a short flight of stairs to a small outside patio area. The inside dining area is dimmed and soothing, and the service is prompt. We were seated in the back of the restaurant, although the special written on a board near the front of the restaurant caught my eye.

I can't remember what Dan ordered, but I ordered the special. We also ordered two Thai iced teas, which (amusingly) came in a glass beer mug.

|| F O O D ||

Lunch special: Sauteed shrimps with fresh mushroom, bell pepper, jalapeno, onion, carrot in garlic sauce served with brown rice and salad [$8.95]
- I was careless and didn't read that there were jalapenos in this dish @__@ It was spicier than my tolerance level for spiciness could handle, which made me appreciate my mound of rice and my iced tea.
- They include a fried wonton, which was yummy! I recommend eating this early on, as I saved this for the end and the crispiness wasn't at max level.
- The complimentary side of salad is okay. The sauce is strange and bitter.
- Not too many shrimps, lots of onions and carrots. Would have preferred more bell peppers too. The shrimps were well cooked though!

Thai iced tea: [??]
- Just the right amount of sweetness and creaminess. The mug is large, but about 1/3 was filled with ice, sadly. But the drink lasts the entire meal, woohoo!

|| C L O S U R E ||

A decent meal with decent portions, but I wouldn't return.

This is the true story, of... where they used to hold auditions for "The Real World" back in the day.  Yup, right here at Thai House.  Food is great, dishes have lots of flavor and a nice splurge for any college student since it's a pretty nice restaurnat and NOT inside the ghetto food court.  If you've got parents in town, this is a good place for y'all to lunch or dine (but not wine.)  Any curry dish here is great, and of course...let's never forget about the Thai iced tea.  Let's face it, any good Thai meal wouldn't be the same w/o sips of the frickin' awesome iced tea.  mmm..mmm.

Two years and many Thai restaurants later, I still think generally the same things about Thai House (ooh, it looks like their overall ranking has gone down though). Their prices are comparable to typical Thai places, but I really disliked the fact that they charged for a bowl of rice, and their food is very very oily. I do like the fact that if you order a meat dish, it comes with a lot of meat -- they don't skimp in that respect. I would say, overall, there's nothing special about this restaurant.

On a side note: They are very smart/crafty because they include the tip on the bill and THEN after you pay with credit card, they have a space for you to add tip. Potentially, if you're not paying attention, you could end up paying 30% tip instead of 15%.

Had lunch here with two co-workers. The food was cheap with decently sized portions and service was good. They came multiple times to fill up our water glasses and sometimes a little too eager to take away our plates.

Definitely order the garlic pepper pork. It's their specialty and it's really good. The meat is tender and very flavorful. The only problem was with the basil chicken. There were too many large pieces of chili peppers, some the size of okra.

For dessert, we had the fried banana which was really good. The bananas were sweet and perfect with syrup. We each had a thai iced tea to go to bring back to work. We'll definitely be back.

Something to note: they have seating outside which is nice especially on days with good weather.

One of my favorite Thai restaurants in the Bay Area. It's perfect for groups, either for formal occasions or informal. But I'd probably stick to the informal since its right off of Telegraph. It's definitely a family style service place, which makes it a lot of fun for a big group of friends. The prices are adequate for the quality of the food, so its definitely more than anything you're going to find in the Durant Food Court.

This is my first 1 star review (and hopefully it's my last)...

ATMOSPHERE
The restaurant itself isn't very cleanly. Once you step inside, there is an odd smell that lingers even after you leave. Blech! The cups were also a little dirty, which says a lot.

The only perk about the atmosphere is that there is ample seating, which is good for groups, but caution: they give poorer service to large groups.

The reason behind the 1 star is the SERVICE, which is TERRIBLE. The workers here are very inconsiderate and do not listen to their customers' orders, nor do they accommodate their dietary needs.

One of my friends is severely allergic to eggs, nuts, and shrimp, which made it difficult to order anything. However, we decided to order Pad See Ew for him, but without shrimp and eggs. We specifically told the waitresses that he was allergic and could NOT have these items in his dish.

When they served it to him, they even said there weren't eggs or shrimp, but after 1-2 bites, my friend discovered that THERE WERE EGGS in his dish!

When we notified the waitress, she simply shrugged it off and didn't even say "sorry." Within 10 minutes, my friend started to swell up-- he had an allergic reaction and couldn't breathe. Despite the chaos that ensued at our table, the waitress showed no sympathy or remorse.

FOOD
We had 12 people and we ordered:
1) Basil beef
2) Basil chicken
3) Pineapple prawns
4) Duck red curry
5) Pad Thai
6) Garlic pepper pork
7) Red curry with chicken
8) Pad see ew

**Note: lunch specials come with a side salad and a potato wonton**

Now, don't get me wrong-- the food was pretty good: flavorful and savory. The portions were decent, especially for lunch specials. However, no matter how good the food is, if the service is terrible, the food isn't worth eating.

There are WAY better Thai restaurants in Berkeley with significantly better service. Hell, there's even a few within 2 minutes walking distance from here. So take my advice: go somewhere else to satisfy your Thai food craving.

Pretty good overall restaurant for students and casual dates.
I haven't ever been wowed by anything here, although the currys, satays and rice dishes I've ordered have always been tasty and provided me and my dining partner with plenty of tasty leftovers! Even when extremely hungry, I have yet to go here and not leave with leftovers.

Food: Good
Atmosphere: Very Good
Prices: Ok
Got me hooked on Thai food.

Didn't get off to a good start when I called for an order for delivery. I was told that they could not deliver. So I was thinking that it was busy and they were swamped. To substitute for the no delivery, I was offered free thai ice tea. 

I then went to pick up my order. To my surprise, the restaurant was not busy and there were plenty of people working in this restaurant. When I went to pay for the food, I pulled out my credit card and was told "our credit machine..." so I gave the look. The look of death. I was visibly not pleased. Luckily, I had cash. Then my free thai ice tea. It was only one! One thai ice tea! Clearly, I had enough food to feed three or four people. I asked if I could have one more. The employee had the nerve to tell me that she could do it this time, but next time she would not be able to. I thought to myself, there would not be a next time. 

As for the food, it really wasn't that good. The Pad Thai, too much fish sauce. The duck, surprisingly good. But overall, sub-par. 

So, you should not fill your hungry void with food from this place. Marginal service, marginal food. Keep reading my reviews for good choices to make!

I LOVE Thai Iced tea. It's my favorite ethnic beverage. Never been a big fan of horchata or chai but the iced tea, yes. There's only one problem with thai iced for me - it sets off a time bomb in my stomach. Every time I order it I know I'm flirting with danger, which is why I calculate the probability of reaching a clean facility within 45 minutes of ingestion. Life is tough when the things you love the most cause such pain.

My favorites are the Pad-Seew and the Garlic Pepper Pork. Dinner orders are really expensive but they do free delivery for dinner so that's a good option if you dont feel like going out on a cold dreary berkeley night. 

I feel like they are a little overpriced, though and sometimes their food can be over oily.

Good place to eat though. :) And I love the architecture of the restaurant. Patio is awesome.

A friend of mine swears by this place, and I thought it was decent, but it certainly didn't blow me away. 

Had the lunch special, a shrimp curry dish. The shrimp were plentiful but felt inexpensive, the little mini-shrimp that you get at the grocery store that aren't particularly large, fresh, or flavorful. The sauce itself was so standard that I lack the words to even describe it. It wasn't complex, wasn't unique, and just wasn't special in any way to make it memorable. So, yeah, just standard-issue mediocre thai food.

Sawatdee!

Berkeley Thai house doesn't exactly qualify as cheap college food. The prices are moderate by normal standards, but not something your average college kid would eat on a daily basis. But if you're a poor college kid and you want to take a date out, this a good option.

Within walking distance of campus, the Berkeley Thai house has nice decor. They even have a nice deck during those warm summer nights.

The food is quite authentic and if you ever get the food Thai spicy, be ready to call 911. Everything is quite good here so you can't go wrong.

Under New Management. Better Service. Awful Food.

This restaurant was one of my favorite Thai restaurants for almost ten years running. Unfortunately, the food quality has gone downhill after the original proprietors retired this summer and a new restauranteur took over.  The new owner is very personable and has made  improvements to customer service. Unfortunately, the menu has been pared down and even those old favorites that survive do not taste anything like they used to. After giving them two chances, I have written them off.  During our  last visit, my squid was undercooked and my friend's duck curry was plain inedible. A pity!

The peanut sauce on my tofu pra ram was disgustingly sweet. The only hint of peanut flavor was from the small bit of crumbled peanuts on top. Otherwise it just tasted like some kind of candy syrup. I had a Coke with lunch, for whatever reason, and the sauce was literally sweeter than the Coke. I felt ill. I'd like to think I eat a lot of peanut sauce, and this was the worst I've had.

The other dishes might be great though, who knows.

Thank god I finally found a place to deliver to Panoramic Hill.  Not many drivers will brave the cliifside windy one lane road.  And to top it off, the food was decent!  My favorite dish that I ordered was Pad See Ew with duck - quite tasty.

Pretty good thai food for reasonable prices.  It is usually full of Berkeley undergrads and their families.  I like their beef with spinach and peanut sauce dish.  The pepper garlic pork is great too (like the dude below said).

This restaurant used to by my favoriate Thai place in Berkeley. However, it seems like the tough times are really showing because this place has really decreased in quality. 

I have ordered the Pad Thai and the Pad See Ew in the past and they were fantastic. However, nowadays I can really taste the restaurant cutting corners with the ingredients. The noodles are really, really overcooked and mushy. The food is not as flavorful or as delicious as it used to be.

The Thai Iced Tea is still good, but they didn't even bother mixing the milk when they gave it to me the last time I came by.

I have been to Thai House many times and kept coming back because their pad thai and garlic pepper pork is one of the best I've had.  We've been here with friends, family, for graduation parties and work lunches with an overall fair experience in terms of service.  

I made a reservation for a going-away party and had a pleasant experience with the woman on the phone.  She was very courteous, but when our party got there it was a whole other experience.  I felt like I was buying a used car from the gentelman who took our order.  Even though we ordered an appetizer and some of us ordered drinks, he told us there had to be a minimum of one order per person.  I would be fine with it if it were really a rule applied to all patrons and adhered by all staff. On their menu it says a minimum of $5 per person, NOT one order.  He said he'd "give us a break" by letting us get 9 orders (I think after overhearing us complain).  To top it off, when we paid our bill -- we gave an additional over the 15% gratutity that is automatically added to groups of 6 or more -- the woman came over and said we were short when we had actually given them more!!  It is not only rude in front of a group, it showed how inept she was to come over before counting it twice.  Luckily, I was with a group of friends, but I would be utterly embarassed if I took a large group of my family and coworkers - for such a horrible experience!

Summary based on 1 lunch:
--ok, somewhat Americanized
--ok, friendly service
--free wifi
--cold inside in colder weather; large outdoor area, which would be nice in warm weather
--average prices for cheap Thai in Berkeley
--usual terrible parking in campus area

Not sure why some of the reviews say authentic since it serves American broccoli for one thing.  Thai Noodle II a block away is a better choice.

Here was our order for a party of 6 adults:

* appetizer: stuffed chicken wings - apparently they're famous for this. It was stuffed with some rice, vermicelli, veggies. It was alright. I wouldn't get it again.
* appetizer: tofu tod - really yummy, especially w/ the glaze sauce.
* garlic pepper pork - kind of like thai barbecue.
* param long song (beef) - tender, although the sauce a bit too peanut-y
* basil prawns
* pumpkin curry - sweet, and not bad.
* eggplant tofu - oldie but a goodie. This was tasty.

Service is very pleasant and attentive. Portions are a bit small, so the general rule of thumb (1 dish per person) doesn't quite work out. Might need 1.3 or 1.5 dishes per person. Tastes good though.

We didn't order fried bananas this time around b/c we had a lo-sugar cadre in our dinner party, but that's a surefire winner.

Caveat: by my 5* rating, I mean to say I think it's the best Thai food in Berkeley based on my standards

I frequent this establishment roughly once or twice every other week and this has been going on since freshman year. My usual orders include some of the following: Pad Thai, Stuffed Chicken Wings (appetizer), Garlic Pepper Pork, Duck Curry, and Eggplant Basil. 

They have a good selection of curries, the red and duck curry being my favorites. Their pad thai compares favorably to competitors' (although if I just wanted it for takeout, I would go to Thai Noodle ii). 

The portions are generous despite what some have said, and I'm a big boy. $1 person for unlimited white rice by the way. Their Thai ice teas are also good (not great), but compare very favorably to some other Thai food locations in Berkeley. They used to give you the option of ordering large Thai ice tea/coffee served in big beer mugs, but for some reason no longer have that option.

There's also this bear-like Asian man who works there, whom if you ask what he recommends on the menu will most definitely yell, "NUMBER 20, GARLIC PEPPER PORK! BEST PORK YOU EVER HAD--GUARANTEED!" So my first time there, I asked, "Do I get my money back if it wasn't the best I ever had?" "No." Well I ordered it anyway, a good recommendation after all. Now I make all my friends going there for the first time ask the guy what he recommends, and sure enough, "NUMBER 20, BEST PORK..." Happens every time without fail, a surer thing than getting drunk munchies after a night out.

They also offer quite a few fruit juices, as well as dessert options including fried ice cream (dank!) and mango sticky rice, but I can only vouch for the fried ice cream and the fried ice cream + banana sundae.

Price is midrange. A meal with myself or split with a friend usually comes out to around $15-20.

They also have pleasant outdoor seating under individual parasols (or pitched things) with heating lamps. 

Note: My only bad experience eating here was ordering one of the shrimp (prawn) dishes. The entree came out smelly very...fishy (bad seafood smell) and not very fresh. So I never order the prawns anymore, but everything else has been solid.

Lunch will run you $11, all told.

Are you a Cal undergrad who wants Thai food, but doesn't know any better?  What's that, you're poor?  And you live in the Southside dorms?  Well, I've got the place for you to round out your freshman 15.  Thai house--go nuts.

I love the location.  It's just barely far enough away from campus and Telegraph to be reasonably peaceful, yet convenient.  I love the interior.  Most Thai restaurants have a serious IKEA feel to them, but the beaten up chairs, weather-damaged wood, and sculptures here are quite endearing.  I love the service.  They're typically very attentive and warm.

When the food comes out, however, Juliet picks up the dagger and my tragic romance with Thai House ends.  I wish I could give more stars, but the food is really that poor.  It isn't bad in that it tastes offensive.  In fact, it barely tastes at all.  For some of the most vibrantly flavorful cuisine on the planet, they do a phenomenal job of making the dishes incredibly boring here.  For locals, I'd describe it as the Thai analog of Naan N' Curry or House of Curries.  From the lack/separation of flavor, it is clear that the spices aren't worked up properly and that Protein A is added to Sauce B and Sidedish C from separate, pre-fabbed pots in the course of 5 minutes.

O, Berkeley Thai House, you have my heart!  If only your food was good, you'd have my wallet too.  Nearest reasonable alternatives: Lucky House Thai or Dara.

We went on a busy night, but there is still no excuse for what happened.
The last time I went here was a year and a half ago and will never go back again. Especially since the food is just OK.  As I said, it was a busy night, so I was  okay about them not refilling our waters or even checking in on us. But while I was still eating, they dropped the bill on our table. So, my husband politely asked if we could order some dessert. The woman replied, "Sorry no, we need this table." The "I am pissed" radar went off.  I was pissed because we were there for no more than 20 minutes, since the bill was dropped in the middle of dinner. AND, I am a dessert fiend, I would have inhaled the freakin' thing in no more than 5 minutes, TOP. I am not that particular when it comes to restaurants, but I will say that if one denies me dessert, I will never go back there again.

So Berkeley Thai House, poo on you.  I hope you crap on yourself.

Bottom line:
God, this place is such a mixed bag. Food is pretty good but last time I was there I saw not one but TWO GIANT RATS ON THE DECK!!! 
Everyone, when there is smoke there is fire. You've been warned, and I'll add these were not mice we're talking about here. The food is fine, so I will bump up my review when they take care of this disgusting vermin problem. 

The atmosphere at night (and often in the day) tends to be LOUD. Don't come here if you're looking for a quiet date, unless it's warm out and you can sit outside - I highly recommend the deck, it's beautiful and won't lead you to wear out your vocal cords by the time dinner's over.

Waitresses are very sweet here, and I can say that they've never messed up the bill for us. They'll obsessively refill your water after you've taken one sip so if you're like me and find that annoying while you're trying to eat and converse with your comrades, hide your glass or something.

Food report card:
Dishes overall tend to be not so hot in temperature - Thai food is not the kind of cuisine to eat cold! Most veggie entrees run around $7.95, meat entrees $8.85, and seafood entrees around $11.95 or so. Note that they do NOT INCLUDE RICE usually - it's an extra $1 a person, and that is a royal pain. 

Pra Ram / Peanut Satay w/ Napa Cabbage - (C+) The peanut sauce here is missing some sort of spice, and I still can't quite figure out what it is. This dish has always been lukewarm (in temperature) when I've ordered it, and I've had it twice. Methinks this is just too much of the kind of thing you could make at home on the stove with the white-bread cultural experience even us Berkelians have foodwise. This is the kind of thing your uncle Joe might make for homecooked Asian night - you know, the guy who insists the only word he needs to know how to spell is "USA." Now, he's a good cook, but he's just too damn simple at it.
Green Curry - (A-) I have yet to find a Thai restaurant who has screwed up green curry. There's just something about it. Well done.
Pad Thai Tofu - (B) Average-sized portion; tofu was a little overcooked and noodles too chewy but the sauce was near perfect. Warning: They skimp on the green onion/leeks in here, at least to my taste.
Red Curry Vegetable - (A) Spicy but not blow-your-brains-out hot; this was cooked perfectly and there was a great curry-to-vegetable ratio which I've found a lot of other places have trouble with. Curry itself was perfect.
Fried Banana with Coconut Ice Cream - (B) Smaller portion of that excellent banana than one would like, but it was pretty good nevertheless. Ice cream was to die for.
Jasmine Rice - (B) Average-sized portion; I've always considered the rice quality to be synonymous with how good the restaurant is (usually). This stuff was a tiny bit dry but nevertheless did the trick.

This is by far the best Thai place in Berkeley. Their pad see ew is my favorite--it's much better than Thai Basil's, which always seems to have a charred taste to it. 

The service is also great--they always seat you immediately and seem to have plenty of people on staff at any given time. 

The deserts are phenomenal--my favorites are the sticky rice with mango and the fried banana with coconut ice cream. You can't go wrong with these, even when it's not really mango season they make it taste great. 

Also they are super speedy with take out orders! Definitely a plus.

My only complaint is that the decor needs some work. From the outside and the inside it looks a bit sketchy. I wish the atmosphere was on par with the food!

Here are the reasons to go to this little berkeley treasure besides their fast and great service and an awesome patio to sit on when the weather is good here are the others:

Pineapple prawns
Basil chicken
Green curry
Garlic pepper pork
Pad thai
Thai iced tea and thai iced coffee
Bananas in coconut milk
And yes.....drumroll....................FRIED COCONUT ICE CREAM!! yes i said fried ice cream, so now I know you want to go here just to try that ha

enough said? I think so heh

berkeley thai house was not our dinner destination of choice. i had originally suggested ryowa because i wanted some butter corn ramen. but one of the girls doesn't like ramen, so i deferred to her preferences and we settled on berkel berkel, our usual spot. but they were closed! so we were left to walk around and find some other place. one of the other girls pointed out thai house and since we were all deliriously hungry, we all just decided to walk in. (keep in mind, the original non-ramen-liking girl hates thai food as well. so i totally could have dragged her to ryowa and she would have been at the worst, equally unhappy.)

so that started off my dining experience on a bitter note. and i couldn't find anything on the menu that i was salivating over so i just went with a simple pad thai and thai iced tea. simple enough, right? well, that's what i thought. iced tea was fine and dandy. and the pad thai looked like any other typical pad thai dish. but once i started eating it, it became quite obvious that it was overly and unnecessarily sweet. in an attempt to make lemonade out of this lemon of a dish, i squeezed all of my lemon wedge over the noodles, but still, too sweet!! i could only finish maybe half of it before my tongue told my stomach that it had had enough.

so sad. i even enjoyed my somewhat soggy six-hour old sandwich eaten along the river bank, more than i enjoyed the food here.

yummy and cheap praram tofu.

this is my favorite place to get praram tofu in the east bay/san francisco so far.  i hardly eat anything else when i go this restaurant, since i can't get peanut-sauced tofu yumminess this good anywhere else!

the peanut sauce is apparently made on site, according to one of the male staff there.  it is not spicy, but creamy with the right amount of fluidity, and sweet.  i order this with rice, and it is superbly yummy together.    at lunch time, the deal is superbly cheap, and is just the right amount plus a little extra to take home.  dinner is only a few dollars more, but too much for me, could last a few meals of leftovers.

customer service is good -- they are attentive and quick to seat you, and are never too far away should you need the staff's assistance.  seating is available both inside and outside on their balcony, which is great for warm weather.  there are heat lamps outside for the cold evenings which are nice and toasty.

parking is not good in this neighborhood due to the busy-ness of being near the university of california only a handful of blocks away.  better take bart, ride a bicycle, a motorcycle/scooter, or a bus (the 51 that goes up durant nearby).

This place is pricey, but the food is really good.  If you're in this neighborhood of Berkeley, you really have two choices when it comes to Thai food: Thai Basil, or Thai House.  Thai House is by far the more upscale of the two, and has some better dishes too.

The atmosphere is really nice here, and I've gone here a number of times for people's birthdays or special events for work.  If you want delicious Thai food in a nice setting, visit Thai House.

Food: 
Have the basics of Thai here. Solid tastes. Not anything out of the norm. Just your average Thai food. Pad Thai is pretty tasty and meats I have eaten here tend not to be ovecooked, which is good, and noodles pretty firm(also good), and rice, fresh. All plus signs on those. Flavors you will find here are more simple and if you're looking for a place to just eat simple, good, and predictably yummy, come to the Thai House. 
 
The desserts are pretty idiosyncratic and nonetheless, excellent. Try the fried ice cream or the fried banana(a little mushy). It is not like your conventional tempura ice cream or other fried ice cream and comes in coconut flavor. Enjoyable, for sure! Other desserts are more Thai and less western-influenced(like fried ICE CREAM, which isn't in my best guess traditionally Thai). However you wanna walk on the wild side a little, go for it. You're actually not risking too much because they're also pretty yum yum to the tum tum.  

Decor:
It is dimly set in a traditional Thai themed interior design. Nothing fancy shmancy or impressive, honestly. Usually busy at regular lunch and dinner hours. Noisy but not raucous. Well, maybe sometimes. If you're looking for more intimate, go during less busy hours like before 5pm (weekday most likely) or after 8pm's dinner rush.

Service:
Service is a little disappointing usually. Yet, when it is less busy, they are usually good about refilling waters and taking orders promptly. But normally, Thai House is not too service oriented. If anything, they're a little rush rush, eat your food and get out. But not horrible. Decent.

Cost: 
This is a cheap eat. The average $7-$14(maybe more for the seafood or more special plates) per entree. Appetizers are good too. Apps and dessert will push the cost up a little but, overall, affordable, dependable, predictably delicious.

Overall:
Value-wise, this place is pretty fantastic. But I do weigh the food/cuisine/taste part of my evaluation pretty heavily. So with that, I give it 2/5 stars because it's not so crude or bad to get 0 or 1 star, but it is average and sometimes better than average, enough to get 2/5 stars. Conventional Thai and Thai-American(this is probably more Americanized Thai than Thai food actually from Thailand.) food, average decor, and decent service. Are you feeling Asian? Are you feeling cheap? Eat Asian, eat cheap, at Thai House.

I like Thai House. The food is always good and they have some unique specials. I like the pad thai, crab fried rice and pineapple fried rice. The atomosphere is great.  They have large tables for big groups, and outdoor seating.  Way better than Thai Basil.

I don't get the hype about this place. Sure, they have pretty good pad see-ew. But the rest of our order -- the fried rice and chili/spicy beef -- was forgettable. Large portions, but you pay the price.

Great location. Great atmosphere.

The food is AMAZING!!!

3 Words: Pricy Thai Food. 

And it's not even that great... (well that was more than 3 words but you get it) 

Berkeley has a lot of Thai food and unfortunately Thai House is not the their best. The only dish I recommend are their desserts. They are on point with the fried banana and mango and sticky rice dishes.

My first time to Thai House was almost two weeks ago and overall it wasn't such a bad experience. I give it 3 stars. Here's why:

I ordered the Roast Duck. It came cut in a decent number of rectangular slices on top of some boiled vegetables (I think cabbage?) and it tasted pretty good. It was savory. There was a side of rice and some spicy soy sauce for dipping. The sauce was okay, but I prefer to dip my roast duck in a honey sauce.

My best friend ordered garlic pepper pork and I had some. Very, very good. His dish came with a honey dipping sauce (which I used with my duck). I'll probably order my own garlic pepper pork in the future.

His cousin ordered the Pineapple Fried Rice with Prawns and I really wanted to try some but didn't want to look like a pig. It came in a big fish-shaped bowl with large chunks of pineapple and with these prawns that were gigantic. I was expecting little shrimps that most restaurants try to pass off as "prawns".

So, some time during the dinner someone from our table found a dead bug in the glass of water and he had been drinking from it for awhile now. He was kinda grossed out and a bit upset, and asked the waitress for a new glass. The waitress promptly got a new glass of water for him and awhile later a supervisor type person came out and made small talk; asking us how the food is and being friendly. It was obviously a PR move to save face, but the gesture meant he cared enough to come out. Also, it meant the waitress felt the need to report it to her supervisor. That shows a responsible attitude. Not bad.

I realized why there was a bug in the water in the first place. They pre-pour the water into glasses when they're not busy, and let them sit next to the entrance until new customers come in. Part of it is bad luck that it happened, I guess.

Its not typical that my boyfriend and I go out to eat to a Friday night. Not being a fan of crowds I tend to save weeknights and weekend afternoons for dining out. But on this rare occasion we decided to check out the eats on Telegraph.

Though I remember this particular Thai restaurant because of the elevated outdoor patio, the weather restricted the service to indoors.

We were greeted with friendly, fast service and the menu was easy to read and well organized, better than some Thai restaurants I frequent.. Listen, I'm a white girl from the Baja Canada who didn't have Chinese food until I was 15, I need to keep it simple!
  
I opted for the Seafood Red Curry and David went with the Roast Duck Curry. By the time the waitress poured my Sing ha we were presented by a HUGE fish shaped platter of red curry swimming with green mussels, squash,shrimp, squid and large 2" scallops. The bowl of duck curry arrived shortly thereafter and was teaming with crispy roasted pieces of waterfowl and tomatoes in a similar red curry sauce.
The seafood was probably the best I've had in terms of Thai- Fresh and the different pieces kept their unique flavors. Surprisingly, none of the seafood was rubbery or flat, which can occur in making a stew of sort.

The duck, and a large portion at that, was succulent and flavorful and the fat had a delightful effect on the red curry sauce. The one thing I didn't like were the large tomatoes, but I dont care for hot tomatoes in any dish.

Even though the place was quite busy, our water was constantly topped off ( I'm a big water fan while dining so this is important) and
our check was presented in timely matter with smiles.
I highly recommend this place if you are in the area and will anxiously await the chance to dine out on the patio.

This review is for the delivery only. The delivery was a 5 star experience for me. They seem to be the only campus eatery with a map of campus -- they delivered right to the building! I'm usually stuck hauling food from a major intersection to the buildings. So 5 star delivery for you Berkeley Thai house!

The food was OK (the spicy eggplant was a standout) and if you're ordering for a large group you can get a lot for your money. However, the food wasn't good enough for me to actively seek this place out. If you organize a lot of campus events, this is a good place to order from.

The best thing about Thai House is the free delivery for dinner!  There's a minimum order amount of $20, but I always just ordered two entrees and saved one for my next meal.

My favorites are the spicy beef, eggplants, and any of the chicken curries.  Their mango sticky rice dessert is really good too!  The portions might seem small if you're used to the giant boxes of food from the ghetto, but the food here is much better quality.

Probably one of the Best Thai Restaurants I've tried in Berkeley, I also think the Atmosphere of the restaurant brings a high sense of romance and homelike presence. The food was delicious, and the service was very kind. Awesome place!.

Got up late on a Saturday morning so we looked for a place in Berekely to eat lunch.   Dropped in at the Thai House.  We sat outside and the weather was perfect. The Thai ice tea is good.  Sweet but not too sweet.

We ordered the Roast duck. It was really good. I would eat this again. Served with Rice and over cabbage it's perfectly cooked. The sweet soy sauce isn't really needed but it was a nice touch.

Also tried the rice noodles (pad se ew) . It was good. I've had it before at other places and it's one of my favorite dishes.  We only had two dishes so it's tough to really judge someplace on two dishes.  The roast duck was really good so I'll up the rating to 4 stars just for that. 

They don't serve a whole lot of food, so there's no extras and it's not served family style.  But over all was a good experience and I'd go back to try some other things. The desserts looked good.

Way back when I was a freshman at Cal my friends and I ate here a lot. I mean so much that when we walked in the front door they didn't really have to take our order, they knew what we'd be ordering (pad prik king with tofu, chicken satay, and some kind of curry) plus thai iced teas.

it is decent thai food, but there is certainly better in berkeley.

the staff is really nice though

Good calamari, but everything else we ordered was WAY salty and the water wasn't even cold!

Siam chicken - not "very spicy" as advertised, and overly salty

Prawn soup - extremely salty - I could only eat the shrimp and mushrooms out of the soup

I actually don't like this place that much and I get confused why people give this place such great ratings. Firstly, their prices are not that cheap, secondly the wait is pretty long, and thirdly their flavors in general aren't that good... try Racha Cafe on Telegraph instead........

Garlic Pepper Pork is a must try - if you can eat pork. I also love their pad thai! It's one of the best I've ever had. I consider the price average for Thai food. The portions are a lot for one person, but I'm not sure if it would be enough for two. 

If you're up for dessert you need to try their fried banana with coconut ice cream!!! They put FRESH coconut in there. It's awesome!!!! And the friend banana part is just as good.

we ordered the garlic pepper pork since that seems like the thing to do, pretty good stuff but not really garlicky or peppery but still good stuff, we also ordered the eggplant, pad Thai, chicken satay, sticky rice with mango, fried banana with coconut ice cream and Thai iced teas, we finished everything, even the little iceberg salad that the chicken satay comes on, (there's a little green sauce under the lettuce which was pretty good), the actual chicken satay itself was just okay, I've had better, the thing that I really remember about this place are the desserts, the sticky rice with mango was the best I've had.  I wouldn't mind coming back for everything else either. I Probably won't go out of my way to come back....parking is a bee-yotch since it's so close to the campus, probably really convenient for students but no so convenient for out of towners**after we parked I saw a sign that said "we validate" not sure which parking garage  that was for.

Decent place. Your apetite will be quenched. Haven't been here any time recent but from what I remember there weren't any problems. *Oh look at this napkin *pull pull *RIIIIIIIIIP hahah

If anything get the fried banana w/ vanilla ice cream. Can never go wrong with that.

Thai House is a nicer sit down restaurant  (for South Berkeley) that is actually close to campus!  There are better Thai restaurants in North Berkeley and even on Shattuck but that involves a trek...  (Does this make me lazy? Shattuck is far!)

However, the Duck Noodle Soup is amazing!  The broth is extremely flavorful with a perfect balance of sweet and savory.  There are ample pieces of duck and bean sprout garnish.  In my opinion this is the entree that differentiates Thai House from all the other Thai restaurants in Berkeley.  However, I think it is only offered at lunch.

Now you have an excuse to be lazy (during lunch only though)!

Once, I came with a large group and we all got free thai iced tea.

Once, I went there when the kitchen was about to close in 5 minutes. I asked if they would still let us dine in or would we have to do take out. They let us dine in, but they were really eager to rush us out of there because they were about to close by the time we were almost done. They should have just told us in the beginning that it was best to take out. 

OVERALL: They deliver in a Honda Element. There is plenty of seating inside and outside. The decor is kitschy, but cute. I think there may be a handicap ramp somewhere, but the main entrance is through some steps. The food is good overall, but quite heavy. I had to eat pad kee mao with a side of rice!

Better service and food, compared to nearby Thai Basil. They used real plates and silverware, and you get your water in glasses, instead of styrofoam cup.  Overall, a much nicer dining experience for parents of college students.

Every time I come to Berkeley Thai House, I feel like I'm visiting this secret "hidden jewel" type restaurant. Probably because the entrance feels so secretive & mysterious... Anyways, I'd definitely recommend this place for a date! The atmosphere is pretty classy compared to the usual Berkeley restaurants, and though the menu is slightly pricier, the food is pretty well done.

Last time I came here, I tried fried ice cream for the very first time- not bad at all! Although, I felt that the fried dough layer was a bit thick- more ice cream please! I also tried the Pad See Ew, which I feel is the perfect go-to for people trying Thai food for the first time. It's very nutty & savory!

This Thai establishment holds a special place in my heart. The best Thai food in Berkeley - the only Thai place I frequented when I was an undergrad. Martin, the guy who owns it is always all smiles.

The beef salad is the boooooomb.

This is my go to for Thai food. The food is really really good and comes in large portions. It's a bit more expensive than Thai Basil but way better! AND they'll make your thai tea/coffee with soy milk if you ask! I usually get pad kee mao with duck but also like their pineapple fried rice and curries.

The restaurant itself is pretty nice and has some fun decorations. It's pretty large and rarely gets too crowded so it's good for big groups. The wait staff is always super smiley and sweet.

Good food, good service.

This place has very interesting decor, I especially enjoyed the stair railing placed in odd places... The outside patio seems nice too, but it was too cold so we sat inside. Inside the women's bathroom there appeared to be a framed picture of Trojans' ad?! Random. 

We ordered Calamari, Green Curry, Garlic Pepper Pork, and the Praram Long Song. I liked the Praram Long Song the best because of the peanut taste, which was very sweet. And served with steamed cabbage so you've got your vegetables too. 

The portions seemed a bit small at first, but turned out to be just right and enough to fill four girls. Only complaint is that we found a hair in the calamari... and they offered us three more to make up for it. Would've preferred having it complimentary, but moar fried things is good too!

Overpriced for their limited portion sizes =(  (I'm a poor growing boy who needs food to grow that extra 0.5" to reach 6'0"!!!) More food please!

I come here sometimes to satisfy my craving for some tasty, fatty duck.  I get the Duck Curry, Roast Duck, or Spicy Roast Duck with a side of white rice.  They all taste great, rich in flavor, but I'm still left hungry.  Come here with someone who has a small appetite so you can eat their leftovers..teehee

Decor and atmosphere is of a nice Thai dinner restaurant.  Definitely a step up from the ghetto-er looking restaurants closer to campus.

Tonight was my second time here. I went here as a group of 6 and we were immediately seated (by our request, outside). They even have cool little table inserts to combine tables for larger parties. So efficient!

We ordered 5 dishes for 6 people because that usually works, right? So we got:

- 5 orders of rice (Korean girls don't eat rice anymore) - 3 stars - came in a cool pot, but it either wasn't Thai jasmine rice or didn't look like it...still ok though, $1 per person.

- Duck Curry (red curry) - 4 stars - yummy! And I don't usually like Thai curry. Tastes good over the rice...only one person didn't really like the curry. The rest of us did.

- Chili Beef - 3 stars - pretty good, but beef was a little tough.

- Combination Seafood - 4 stars - pretty good, but my friends ate all the scallops before it got to me. So I only got to eat a couple squid and a prawn, which were good. =( I don't like zucchini so I didn't touch that.

- Kang Jued - 4 stars - good! 

- Pad See-Ew with Chicken - 5 stars - MY ABSOLUTE FAVORITE DISH IN THAI FOOD, and this place does a good job. Yum!

Well...turns out the portions are kinda small, so everyone was still a bit hungry after, and we placed another order for Garlic Pepper Pork, their signature dish. DELICIOUS. 5 star dish. Korean friend said it tastes like kalbi so she wasn't that impressed, but dude, that stuff is bomb. The dipping sauces are both good too.

We also had a coupon for free Thai iced tea with purchase of 2 entrees, so we got 2 Thai iced teas...well first of all, they were really watered down. We figured it's probably because they were like, "Oh, they're getting it for free. Let's just make one tea and divide it into two cups. They'll never notice." Well...yeah. We didn't even finish it cuz it wasn't even worth it. And guess what, it's NOT technically free. We had to pay tax on it. WTF! It was only 40 cents, so whatever, but...you should tell us that.

Even funnier that that...at the end of the meal, we chipped in for the bill. They conveniently added in the 15% tax for us (I find that more and more common at restaurants these days), so we divided it up. Well, since most of us had $20s, and it was $13 per person (actually $12.60), one guy had to go get change. When he got back, I was like, "Did you give K back $1?" and he said, "See, here's the thing. The waiter said we gave him $85 when our bill is about $76 including tip, right? He said, How about I just give you $5 back? and I said OK."

Us: o_O WHAT?! YOU KNOW THAT $76 INCLUDED TIP RIGHT? You're supposed to get $9 back, not $5!!!

Him: Yeah...

Us: So we basically gave a $4 extra tip on top of our 15%.

Him: Well, I'm not a very good bargainer...

Us: That's not even bargaining! OMG...

Oh well, service was pretty good I guess. The waiter was smiling really big when he came back to collect our plates. I wonder why...

Coffee candy is good. Mmm...

went here a lot in college. best Thai food near campus. i really like their massamun curry (delicious!) and their pad thai is pretty good. prices are decent. 

here's a tip: check your water before you drink it...I've found a small fly in mine more than once! but even still, never kept me from coming back.

HOHOHO.  Its almost indulgently fun to write reviews about restaurants like this.  Almost as fun as spotting the typos on the menu...

Nothing was good about this place.  Not one thing.  I got the spicy beef, with a side of brown rice that evidently I have to pay extra for, thanks for letting me know after the fact.  As I could have predicted, the bowl was 70% onion and pepper, and the beef was like paper.  No seriously.  Haven't you ever tried to eat a tiny piece of paper?  That's what the beef was like, chewy and flavorless, not to mention indigestible.  The omnipotent clove-basil? flavor was overwhelming, and the only source of spiciness was the serrano peppers.  I could have just brought my own serranos.  What a cheap way to create heat.  However, it certainly wasn't cheap economically, considering I had to add a gratuity tip because I was with a large group of people.  Nothing irks me more than being forced to tip services that do an abysmal job.  

Lastly, a random thought:  on one wall they have a certificate hanging up that thanks Berkeley Thai House for a donation to the Child Abuse Foundation.  Um, shouldn't that organization be called the ANTI-Child Abuse Foundation?  yikes

With all the decent eating places seemingly closed, or closing down in the area, this place stands out as a shining beacon of relief. The staff are wonderfully polite and attentive. The food (red curry beef and pad thai) was different than I've had at other Thai places, but the difference was very positive. 

Eating on the deck above the noise and traffic, hidden by flowing bougainvillea and bright red geraniums was a very welcomed escape. I really felt like I was away from it all and was allowed to eat my meal in exotic Thai bliss.

C'mon guys, this place is rated only as high as Thai Basil, and that's a freaking insult. This place is way better.

Garlic Pepper Pork is a way of life, not a dish.

The basil beef and mushroom chicken are excellent. There's a chicken dish on their specials menu (Siam chicken) that should be avoided at all costs. It's weirdly spiced and inedible. When I was in college the garlic pepper pork was about my favorite food anywhere.

I must warn you that I am alway starving when we come here, so I might not be very objective.  That being said... 

We traditionally come here after a long day of rafting on the Sacramento River, so we are always ready for large amounts of food by the time we get here. 

And we always leave happy.  They have great Thai Iced Tea, and everything we get is faboo.  Maybe I should get Guri here to review this place... he's much tougher a critic than I!

It was a friend's birthday so I offered to treat her out to lunch. She was craving for some Thai food and we decided to give the Berkeley Thai House a shot since we've always avoided going there. I now have a legit reason why.

It was around dinner time and it was just starting to get a little crowded. We were seated and the waiter was very pushy for us to order so I went for the Pad See Ew. When I got my food, I couldn't help but scrunch my face a little. My dish looked so greasy and oily that I was scared to take my first bite. I only got through half of the dish before I had to give up. I started to feel sick. My friend had the Pad Thai and she was unsatisfied. 

To make up for the awful food, I told her maybe their dessert could save the dinner. When the waiter came back to take our plates away, they didn't even bother to check with us if we wanted to order anything else and slapped us with the check. When I asked for the dessert menu, they glanced at the growing crowd of people waiting and shot me a scathing look as if I had done something wrong. I was so pissed that I put down the cash and we left immediately. Why would I want to further support a place that was so rude? Afterwards, I had an awful stomachache which I blame the Pad See Ew for.

 I was disappointed with the service and food and will not being coming back again.

We came here on a Friday summer evening around 6pm, so there weren't many customers. The three of us ordered the pad thai, red curry with chicken, and a beef dish I believe was called praram long song. All were very delicious, but I probably wouldn't get the red curry again. The thai tea here is great. They charge $1 a person for jasmine rice, but it's never-ending, and the three of us were really satisfied after the first pot. Service was quite good when we came here--the waiters always made sure our glasses were filled with water, but probably because there weren't many customers at the time. I would definitely recommend this place over Thai Basil, even though it's a bit pricier.

I'm surprised that I haven't visited this Thai restaurant sooner!

A group of friends and I came on a Thursday night and the staff was extremely accomodating about us adding more chairs and tables to our "reserved" table of 6. We were able to order quickly and get our food quickly, which was surprising considering the number of people eating there and the fact that there were other large groups as well. 

I had the Pad Kee Mau which was really good! I liked that they put huge chunks of jalapenos in the dish instead of just adding chili peppers or chili sauce. The noodles were not very oily like other places usually make this dish. The portion was also very good - as I was able to bring most of my plate back home to eat as leftovers. A bit pricey for $8.99 or so but you get what you pay for here! My friends had the fried banana and ice-cream which looked really delicious ($4.99 - a bit steep in my opinion). 

Service was excellent. As I stated before, everyone was extremely accomodating. Our waiter was attentive and our water glasses were never empty. With such a large group, a tip of 18% (I think) was already included on the bill but our waiter still did his job instead of taking the tip for granted. 

Overall, a great place for Thai food. I wish I knew about it sooner!

i'm not sure why but this is my favorite thai restaurant in the east bay.  i think it might be the endless red hot tea, which i have yet to find its equal (what kind of tea is that?  i can't find it anywhere!).  as a vegetarian, i find their tofu dishes superb.   the red vegetable curry is divine. 

i also book the thai house for large group dinners for my company after we do events @ UC.  they are AWESOME serving large groups (as long as you give them warning/make a reservation) and it's super cheap for group meals (compared to say, Shen Hua). Our clients always RAVE about it afterward, esp. the seafood, although i can't speak to that myself.

Great lunch special. $7.95 for lots-o-food. The green garlicky salad dressing is a delight. The pumpkin "shrimps" was very good and thick, though the pumpkin was a tad mushy. I loved eating outdoors -- the setting is great!

I love THAI HOUSE! I have great memories of going here on good dates with my not-so-great ex-bf! Oh well! Bad decision of company for a great decision of restaurant is ok in my book!

Loved going here! The red curry was just perfect, as was the pad thai - never too sweet as some of the other thai restaurants in the bay area will mistakenly do.

Oh how I miss you. We need to be reunited ASAP!

Berkeley Thai House is pretty good. My boyfriend and I brought our parents here after we finished moving in for the semester. It's a great sit-down atmosphere for a nice dinner with your parents. The Pad Thai and Pad Kee-Maw are great here! 

So if you really like these signature Thai dishes then this is a great place to go. I've also had the Yellow Curry and the Pork Curry. The Yellow Curry was really good and it comes with chicken. I'd say the Yellow Curry is very reminiscent of the normal sweet Thai curry. The Pork Curry I didn't like very much. The curry is definitely not sweet and more spicy. I don't usually like spicy foods so the Pork wasn't something I'd usually get.

I still need to try "Racha" which is another Thai restaurant on Telegraph near UC Berkeley so that I can compare the two.

Tucked away on Channing Way, Berkeley Thai House gets it done right for the price of fast food. Today I had Pad See-Ew, the Thai version of Chinese Chow Fun. Pan fried, not greasy, it was great. Broccoli not over done and the braised pork was good enough. My office mate has the Thai House Soup that looked fantastic with spicy & sour broth, prawns, scallops, squid, green mussels, carrots, onions, hot chili, cilantro, lemon grass, and lime leaves. There was enough for two servings. The soup will be on dance card next time!

Some friends of mine really like this place, so I've been here often. I don't mind that, the food is adequate. But there's so many Thai places in Berkeley, it's difficult to understand how a place with awkward service like this can be so popular.

I have to agree with Cris L., service here is quite awkward. The last time I was here they forgot my drink and they tried to politely kick us out. But you can never be polite when you ask a well paying customer to leave. The place is always packed and all the servers are too quick to take away your plates. We were a big group and yes, we wanted to take more than 1/2 an hour to eat our food, but we're paying too! Just like the next guy. Food is adequate, but I can find better Thai elsewhere.

About a decade ago, my Thai boyfriend (now husband) took me here on a date. At the time I had little opinion about Thai food, but he obviously did...and this was one of his favorite Thai restaurants. All I remember from that night was that he had requested every dish to be ridiculously SPICY, yet it was all quite delicious.

We revisited Thai House recently, and we naturally had high expectations for the food. We ordered noodle soups (duck and seafood) and salad (yum neau) that tasted pitifully Americanized. Based on this one disappointing meal, we figured something must have happened over the past years. Moreover, the prices had increased; they are no longer so student-friendly.

The place looked more worn out, too. The service was slow. Maybe we went on the wrong day. Maybe not. 

SUM: We've definitely experienced better, and I'm sure there are newer and more authentic Thai restaurants in the city of Berkeley yet to be discovered.
Way too soggy.  I don't have anything else to say.

DUDE how did I live on the south side of Berkeley for TWO years and not eat here?! I finally caved in to the bacchanalian urges that college students are predisposed to: drinking and then late night eating - and ended up here when I saw that the line at Top Dog was too freakin' long. Forget Top Dog! For six dollars, IB Hoagies gives you enough sandwich for TWO meals, loaded with cheese, vegetables, and... EGGPLANT PARMESAN, which is honestly my favorite sandwich in all of Berkeley now. I asked the man behind the counter, "Is it good?" and he said, "With everything, it's amazing." I believed him. Bought it. Ate it. And believed him with a further intensity - it's seriously an amazing sandwich. I will probably need to eat one once a week.
