They're all crispy and amazing. Seriously, I can probably eat my feelings all day on any of these sides. Try it out sometime.

The curly fries here formed the greasy base of my food pyramid as a freshman. They don't skimp on the steak on the sandwiches at all, my only complaint is that I wish that they were open later on the weekends.

I can see if you are a student at Cal that this place would be the business. We went here because a friend who is an alum raved about it and we wanted to explore the area. 

Being the Philly Cheese steak connoisseur that I am I have high expectations... 

I got the basic Philly Cheese to judge the shop in its purest form. The sammich has the small chopped up onions (no bueno). The sammich is too dry and doesn't have enough meat for me. The price is a buck or two cheaper than a normal Philly. 

We got the garlic fries and they weren't nearly as crispy as I like, but they do give you a grip that we were able to split three ways. 

In general, hit this place up if you're walking around and have a cravin' for a philly cheese, but if you have wheels, go somewhere else.

I adore this place.  The cheesesteak is probably the best I've had.  I'm not a cheesesteak expert, but I've had my fair share, and nothing compares.  The seasoning is excellent, the size is amazing, and it's just plain old fabulous and a bargain.  I wish they had one of these in Los Angeles.  I still can't find a good one.  :[

I recommend the cheese steak with hot peppers. This is not only delicious, but will kill any virus, germ, and cure cancer. 

If you don't want sizzling bung-O afterwards, add fries to the above as a buffer. 

Oh, and they had to discontinue their old 'frequent diner" punch card because some dickstick was counterfeiting them.

I love these cheesesteaks, especially with bacon. Bacon combines well with everything. Love bacon. Must have more of it. Hummmmmm.... Sorry - this is not the place for that. Back to Ib's:
These are the only cheesesteaks I've had, so I can't compare. I've heard they're so much better in Philadelphia (some day I'll make a trip to test that proposition), but no-one was ever able to tell me where to get better cheesesteaks around here.
If only the seating were better...

The hoagies are good, but I'm a burger guy.  I love the Bacon Cheeseburger w/ Seasoned curly Fries... The meat isn't dry and everything else is good.  It could use some more bacon, but can't everything? ;)

One of the better burgers in Berkeley...

Seriously, one of the workers dropped an F-Bomb on me when I went to grab a togo sauce container.  The food is pretty good, but keep in mind, it is good because it is drenched in oil and the fries are deep fried, if you want something like that you can basically go anywhere.  Yeah, the rude service ruined my meal.

K, this is not a real philly cheesesteak but the best around in Berkeley.  not as salty as it should be.  probably need to get it with extra cheese in order to get the taste right.  

but still i love to eat here.  next to the cheese steak, their bucket of fries - make it curly fries or chili cheese fries - is what you have to order. 

college town food. 

no bathroom and like 2-3 tables to eat it so plan on taking it to go.

This is basically an enlarged food stand next to the street. They make around ten varieties of hoagies, and I have tried them all. I was always puzzled why they all basically taste the same, despite having different ingredients. But that taste is honestly pretty good, so I don't mind. They also make some mean curly fries, which dance on your tongue with salt and spice. Combined with a hoagie, it's hard to beat this place for a quick lunch.

However, it's a bit expensive, especially compared to the other food that dots the rest of Durant Avenue. I would give it another star if it was cheaper. $8+ for a regular-sized hoagie which doesn't entirely fill me? I'd rather wait for my tax return to eat here.

Just to preface this review I don't eat red meat and not a big fan of chicken sandwiches, but since a friend wanted to go I went.

Well what a surprise!  I had a Veggie Combo and it was surprisingly delicious!  Who knew a cheese steak place could do a veggie sandwich right.  The bread was perfectly toasted, the cooked veggies seemed fresh and the combo of avocado and cheese did the trick.

so the cheesesteak is not bad for the west coast.  the bread is weak and they seriously need to lay off the mayo.  i mean I love mayo as much as the next person but my cheesesteak needs to taste more like cheese and meat and less like mayo.  but hey it's good and cheap.

I really don't understand how this place can have a 4 star review.  Maybe there just aren't many good options in this part of town.  Maybe the college budget doesn't let other Yelpers taste better food.  Maybe most Californian Yelpers haven't been to the Northeast to experience an authentic Philly cheesesteak.  Regardless, a more well-versed palate will surely dislike this establishment.  Not only is it bad food, it is bad food poorly trying to replicate a very particular kind of specialty food so you have shattered expectations to weigh it down as well.

I asked for my cheesesteak with only grilled onions and cheese, the Cheez Whiz-like kind.   A lot of fixings were offered by default (lettuce, tomatoes, mayo, mustard, etc.), but I wanted to make my experience as Philly-centric as possible even if the menu wasn't geared for that by default.

I received my cheesesteak with some crappy white sliced cheese.  Either the cashier didn't understand me or didn't care or both.  Upon closer reflection, this place may just not even comprehend to serve Cheez Whiz-style cheese on the cheesesteak as the authentic version should be.  This is weird though, since they obviously stock that topping for the cheese fries toppings.

The meat was pretty low quality and overly burnt.  The hoagie roll was decent.  I've had much worse interpretations of Philly cheesesteak bread, but this hoagie roll bore some semblance.... about the only redeeming quality.

I didn't know what to get for my first visit here, and a lot of the sandwiches looked good. I eventually opted for the regular cheese steak with everything on it. I liked that they had a small self service area with jalapenos and peppers, which I added to the sandwich. The toasted bread was still soft and fluffy and the sandwich as a whole was really flavorful. I enjoyed it on the sidewalk at one of their tall tables. I had to remind them about the fries I ordered, but that was no big deal. The fries were nice and crunchy and well salted. No frills, no health benefits, no Berkeley pomp. It was a good change of pace.

i ordered their chili cheese fries before we went to drink at henry's for my very first birthday in norcal.  it ended up in throwup-format on my bed by the end of the night.   I still think their food is good!

The sandwiches here are greasy and delicious, and the service is generally pretty quick.  This is great place to go for comfort food.

The challenge, of course, is the fries.  Last time I checked, fries came in two sizes: "regular" and "bucket."  The bucket is easily more than twice as large as the regular by volume, but costs only like $.25 (maybe $.50) more.  Simple economics dictates that it is therefore irrational to buy regular fries.  And yet very few people can eat an entire cheesesteak and a bucket of fries.  This had led to an all-too common situation where a hapless customer, recognizing the economic ramifications, actually elects the bucket of fries as their meal, and foregoes the sandwich entirely.

Apart from this logical conundrum, however, I greatly enjoy the sandwiches, and usually just skip the fries.

This place is always the place I turn to when I have the fried food munchies or am in the mood for a cheesesteak. The food is cheap, fast, and satisfying!

They have garlic fries (which can be very strong), curly fries, cheese and chili fries, burgers, and cheesesteaks with a large array of toppings. It smells so good when I pass it it's pretty hard to resist on an empty stomach.

I ate at Ib's almost everyday during my last two years of highschool. They have amazing cheesesteaks and fries. I love their chickensteaks. mmmm. I saw Adam Lamberg(Gordo from Lizzie Mcguire) there once and I almost peed.

Visit #1 : food poisoned.
Visit #2 : food poisoned.

Two other friends' visits? Food poisoning galore.

Does anyone see a pattern here?

On a side note, I've only been food poisoned by cheese steak places in my entire life despite loving cheese steaks to death. :\

Traditionally, Berkeley is a mecca for yummy cheap eats. IB definitely keeps up that tradition with their delicious and filling cheesesteaks. My faves are the pepper and onion steaks (cuz I love peppers and onions, duh). I made the mistake of ordering the chili cheese fries once... and almost died from a heart attack. There was a lot of groaning/moaning and belly patting after I got about half way through the bucket (yes, they serve it in a bucket).

According to the Yelposcale, two-stars means "Meh. I've experienced better." That is exactly how I felt today after eating a pepper-steak at Ib's Hoagies. 

It was one of those days where I was looking to maximize the calorie to dollar ratio, and Ib's did come through in that regard. But I've certainly enjoyed a gut-bomb a hell of a lot more than what I ate today. 

My main complaints are that the hoagie just didn't have much flavor, and that the meat seemed pretty low-quality. I could barely taste the grilled peppers/onions, and I kinda had to force my way through the last 2/3rds of the thing. 

"Better" hoagies I've enjoyed in the past typically had nice fresh chunks of grilled veggies, thicker cuts of quality meat that isn't overcooked, good cheese and a nice sauce. So Ib's gets good marks for calorie to dollar ratio and speed, but negative marks for flavor and quality.

Cheap eats for college students, close to campus.

Their sandwiches are decently sized and quite delicious for the price you pay. I always passed by this my freshman year, but finally decided to try it. Soo glad that I did! Instead of going to GBC and buying overpriced cheese fries, I can get them here freshly made, and cheaper! I haven't tried the sandwiches, but they are highly recommended. 

Everything is cooked to order.

I like to think the heavy brick weight greasy sandwiches here could actually cancel out the amount of calories I've consumed. I mean, the sandwiches could essentially be like lifting weights, therefore working off the fat while I lift for each bite... Yeah? ....

Well even if my logic is whacky, I absolutely love the food here! I ordered a large Mushroom Steak ($7.99), which was insanely heavy filled with a generous portion of meat, mushrooms, and thick cheese! The cheese really makes the sandwich! Even I was full off half the sandwich (so a large is good for two!). Now the chilli cheese fries were to die for too! A HUGE portion (since they only have one size, it could be a meal in itself): thick cut fries, good hearty pieces of beef, and drenched in yummy cheese! 

Now the place isn't too big, with a few bar stools and tables, so it seems as though most take it to go. Don't let the car ride home be too long though, because things can start to get moist & soggy. Other than that, the service here was fast and friendly. And most importantly, cash only kids! 

Glad I don't live too close or I-B routinely having a sandwich workout to tone these guns *flexes arms* ;)
Who knew something as simple as a hoagie could be so delicious.  I loved every bite.  Portion size is HUGE and def worth going back to again..

Five words:

BUCKET. OF. CHILI. CHEESE. FRIES.

Five stars.

FRIES PEOPLE.. it's seriously all about the FRIES when you come to IBs.
i'm not a big fan of the cheesesteaks actually - i would say i just plain don't like them. so this review is really about the fries (you know how much i love them!)

they used to serve their fries in those big cups that you'd see at county fairs or festivals but now they've switched over to the biodisposable stuff (kudos to you).  the garlic fries are REALLY yummy - they put tons of garlic on.  curly fries, regular fries, chili cheese fries - you name it! it's all pretty good.  the bf likes the tator tots (they call em "tator rounds" here) - you really can't go wrong.  the prices here are pretty cheap too! 

mmmmm....

I'm surprised that in my 3 semesters here, I was only able to try a hoagie a little while ago. I will say that I was pleasantly surprised.

Environment: Don't eat at I.B.'s Hoagies unless you're getting to-go to eat elsewhere. There tends to be a lot of homeless people asking for your change and you end up feeling rushed in eating your hoagie.

Service: Not really applicable. The cashier was nice but it's really a take your food and go sort of place.

Food:
I got the garlic steak and fries. The fries were seasoned well and crispy on the outside while soft on the inside. Pretty fantastic, exactly how I imagine fries to taste.

The garlic steak. My goodness, I have never been so wowed by a hoagie. It was absolutely delicious. There was exactly the right amount of garlic flavor in the sandwich and the meat to bread ratio was perfect to slip into your mouth. The meat was tender and the cheese on it melted to keep the sandwich together. My only regret is that it was pretty salty, and I felt like I had to drink a gallon of water afterward, but the hoagie was bloody delicious.

Verdict: Excellent hoagie. Doesn't look like much but would definitely recommend.

A cheesesteak. My favorite food hands down. Though the first and only time I only had a true original Philly Cheesesteak when I was 8 years old, I have to settle with the cheesesteaks that Bay Area has to offer.

I.B's Hoagies are pretty damn good. Especially at it's price point. $5.49 for any of the hoagies and all come stock with Lettuce, Tomato, Mayo, Mustard, Pickles, cheese and Hot Sauce. I got the Shroom Steak and the Boyfriend got Teriyaki. We also got a side order of Cheese Fries and a tall can of Arizona Green Tea. Total came to roughly $16.

I wanna say this is a 6 in. sandwich and it's packed really neat with minimal mess and a filling meal that I had half left over. The Cheese Fries ($2.50) were a heaping full and had tasty cheese in every bite. 

Definitely a good choice for a East Bay Cheesesteak Treat.

Going to telegraph i always enjoyed eating at 3 diff. spots and they were all on the same street.  Theres this joint, top dog across the street and this underground spot underneath the old tower records that served shitty pizza but u can play games and drink beers there.  

IB's is delicshshsh....always a hard decision on this and top dog since that pizza joint closed.  Bucket of cheese fries or garlic fries with your cheese steak and ur set to go..... i usually go next door to the liquor store and get a different drink while they are making the cheesesteak cus the thirst quenching options are limited....not much room for seating here...oh and the hot sauce make sure to get some of that ....try grabbing the bottle and hogging it until someone has to ask u for it....

(theres this other cheesesteak joint on E....1 ...FO..... in san leandro that would be good competition for IB's if they ever had an iron chef "hoogies/cheesesteak" edition, Bobby Flay would get his ass kicked)

Great sandwiches. Awesome cheese fries. Fair prices. Would probably come again.

The manager needs to watch how he talks to his employees though. Saw him yell at an employee in front of customers while asking incredulous questions. I was thinking, CALM THE F DOWN, BRO. Not cool. Minus 2 stars.

I got a Hoagie here the first time I visited the Berkeley campus back in my HS days.  Since then, I've been hooked.  The sandwiches were much cheaper back then but whatever.  

I've tried most of them and I absolutely love the bbq steak.  It works really well with the spicy sauce they use to create a spicy/sweet combo.  They put lots of meat and the buns are toasted to perfection too.  

If you really want a heart attack, get the chili cheese fries.  They come in a huge bucket and you'll be full for days.

This is the first place I ever ate at when I went to Berkeley as a student.  Awesome cheesesteaks, chili cheese fries.

Sweet Jesus I want some now.

I hesitate to write an updated review after my eloquent and stirring first review, but here goes nothing:

Best chili fries in town!

This place is just greasy and delicious.  Pretty standard cheesesteaks but what gets me going there are the chili cheese fries.  It's a little trashy cus they use the fake nacho cheese like you get at smart and final, but man when you're eating that kind of food, trashy is the way to go.  

whoever invented chili cheese fries should get some kind of award... for being the cause of our nation's obesity problem.  

just kidding i heart grease... but seriously go to the gym once in a while, please.

You know when you're super hungry, you want something fatty, fast, and cheap. When you get a Hoagie from here, as you unravel the beast that is the sandwich, you will start to notice how the paper is becoming transparent. It's great for splitting. Spend a couple dollars more and get a large and you'll have a 14 incher that you can split with a friend. I got the garlic fries,  but they werent as good as I remember. Maybe it was because I came late at night and got the soggier than a fresh batch, but I was still a happy camper. Definitely fulfilled my craving.

i was driving back from work a couple of weeks ago when my roommate left me a message saying, "hey, i forgot that you work late in berkeley some nights.  can you please pick me up an ib hoagie?!?!?!"  i was like, wtf???  what is an ib hoagie??  well, last week i finally picked up one up (yes, i got the roomie one too!) and i thought i was going to die driving back to sf that sandwich smelled so good.  i had the garlic cheesesteak hoagie and it was super cheesy and wonderful :).

I don't come here TOO often because it's pretty fatty but if you're in the mood for a quality, greasy sandwich, this is the place. Every now and then we all need to indulge a bit. I'd recommend trying one of the chicken options with a side of curly (cheese) fries.

Expected bill: $7-$10

Love this place. I'm still exploring the menu here, but so far the mushroom, pepper and bacon cheesesteak are amazing. There's always a good amount of cheese on their cheesesteaks, and I can't wait to come back and try something new. Portions are huge, the sandwiches are greasy as it should be, and it won't break the bank! Just the way I like it. If you order the largest sandwich with a large bucket of fries, it'll last you two meals. No kidding.

Every item you order here is made to order, meaning they won't make it until you order it. That's why some of the food takes a long time. Even the fries takes about 5 minutes since they're deep frying them on the spot. 

This place is a hole in the wall too. It's always cramped during peak hours, and there are some bar stools to sit on and eat at, but most people order out for convenience.

If you have a Spendgo account, this place accepts it. All credit cards are accepted here.

The best cheesesteaks I've found on this coast.  One wouldn't think making cheesesteaks -basically frying meat and onions- would be that hard, but I've lived on the coast for nine or so years and I've never found anything passable.  These are heads above the rest.

If you crave something greasy and full of meat, run, don't walk here.  This hoagie shop makes some great cheesesteak type sandwiches and other fried things to handle your most dire need.  You get a french roll loaded up with chopped meats and all the fixings and cheese.  These are so good I have had people come up to visit from out of town with stopping here for lunch as one of their goals.

Combine the hoagie with some curly or regular french fries and if your arteries survive, you'll be a happy camper.

I used to get the 'mushroomsteak' when I was a regular here.  I would argue to myself that mushrooms are kinda healthy, so this makes it ok to eat, or something?  Either way, it's good, can get crowded during peak hours, but that's because people recognize good eats.

Their chili cheese curly fries= yum yum in my tum. I actually ate a whole bucket full myself....:X I'm a huge sucker for good fries. And their chili burger is good too! This place is great if you're craving fried food or looking to get a heart attack.

Another essential stop on our Berkeley Food Tour.  I'd give my right arm for a mushroom cheesesteak with a large bucket of curly fries and a giant soda... but then I'd have trouble eating with my left hand!  The meat is tender, the cheese is melty and the bread is fresh.  Can't ask for much else.  Oh wait, there is more.  The fries are crispy and also super fresh!  I do wish the sandwich bread was toasted but that's a slight change in the face of such all-around greatness.  

PS:  Don't offer to share the bucket of fries with anyone.  It looks quite large but when you start dippin' those babies in ketchup, you won't wanna give any up!

A few words about the place:
Located at the hub of south side, IBs Hoagies lures you in with the smell of fresh chili cheese fries($4.50) and melty cheesesteaks (~$7) as soon as you turn the corner of Durant Ave. With quick order turnaround(10min or less), always available seating, and reasonable prices, you can find me perched outside on a high stool during lunch hour. 

What i recommend:
Just order a garlic, mushroom, or bacon cheesesteak sandwich with your fixings (tomato, lettuce, pickle, 1000 island dressing, mustard, etc) to go and take your drink with you enjoy the outdoor seating either there or on sproul. I usually go for the 6" sandwich and that fills me up right but opt for the 12" ~$9 when im feeling monstrously hungry. If I'm feeling fat the chili cheese fries in my opinion are the best in Berkeley.

Bottom line:
There really isn't anything like this in Berkeley. But what I like best is, if you get no dressing, and no mayo, you really have a rather light cheese steak sandwich. IBs actually uses good quality meat with a lower fat content than many cheesesteak places, making for a tasty, cheesy sandwich that doesn't have you clutching your heart 30minutes after you finish eating. It's fast, convenient, friendly, and delivers exactly what the same thing time and time again; a good hot sandwich.

Is it a genuine philly cheesteak? Do I care?

Whatever you want to call them these things are heaven on a bun. 

In my brief tenure at Berkeley I tried to limit my IB's hoagies consumption to 1x a month. 

My favorites were the bacon cheesesteak and cheese fries. For about $8 you can get a cheesesteak and a drink. 

The lines are about 15-20 min during the lunch rush. Forget about trying to get food here on football game days. 

These things are seriously tasty and affordable. 

Heart attack on a plate, no doubt.

I love Hoagies, cheesesteaks, and sandwiches. Came up here to visit my homegirl up in Berkeley and we stopped by this place and I was very very impressed. I only got the sandwich but I was very impressed with the softness of the bread and how meaty the sandwich was. I got your typical Hoagie with the works and I can't remember if I added a few items but I was more than impressed with the size, the quality, and most of all the price! Next time I'm by CAL I will be checkin' this place out.

Why did you have to wait til RIGHT AFTER I graduated Cal to start serving GARLIC fries, huh? hUH? HUH?!!!!!  WHY?!?!  You knew that's what I always craved and always dreamed of while snacking on your delicious bucket of fries.  You get minus 1 star for depriving me of garlic fries and then shoving it up my face after I move away.  The cheese steak sandwiches are aiiight... they just add some variety to a "healthy" college diet.

Best. Customer. Service. Ever.

I went here yesterday with some friends.  I only had a credit card and desperately wanted garlic fries, but since there is a $5 minimum my friend ordered my fries for me along with his eggplant parmesan (which he said was dericious) and when we got our order, we realized they gave us an extra curly fries.  My friend looked at his receipt and said "oh, I guess they charged me for that, oh well" because their curly fries are awesome and just $2.  The owner overheard us talking and he said "you didn't order these? Wait a second" and he goes inside, talks to the cashier, and comes out. He hands my friend $2 and tells us to enjoy the fries.

SO NICE! We did not even complain, we were fine with the extra order and fine with paying for it, but he just overheard us talking and wanted to do the right thing. 

I love this plaaaaaaace!!!

I use to come here in College , since then its been 5 years since i returned.I ordered the Philly cheese steak with added modifications of extra garlic and mushrooms with the curly fries.
When it arrived on my plate, the sandwich was a good portion and full filling . The meat balanced out the soft roll bread with a generous amount of mushrooms  and tinge of garlic  looking at the sandwich , it looked small, but when I finished it, i felt that i over ate. It just proves that  my eyes are hungrier then my stomach. So much food, for less then 6 bucks. !! 

This place constitutes the saying" GREASE IS GOOD"..  don't come here if you are on a diet..The menu is not figure freindly.

So GOOD but soooo BAD.

I miss their curly chili cheese fries. Ohmigoodness, the fries are pure ecstasy in your mouth. One of the reasons why I was a chubby monkey in college.

Oh man! Junkie comfort food at it's finest!!!

I had a chicken hoagie my first time. It wasn't anything special, but still good. And then there was ...(duhn duhn duhn)... the cheese fries.... Oh the cheese fries! They were so yummy!! We got a bucket to share between 3 people and I had a hard time not scarfing them all down. 

*You know when your sharing something so yummy, you watch what pieces and how much the other people are taking, and you feel a twinge of jealousy when they take the pieces that you have been eying, and a twinge of disappointment as the supply dwindles.*

I would make my boyfriend drive me to Berkeley at least once a week for a hamburger and cheese fries! The hamburgers were pretty decent. 
And I (hangs head in gluttonous shame) would often ask for extra cheese on the side and put that on my hamburger. Sooo good.

I am lucky IB's wasn't close to my work, otherwise I would have had cheese fries everyday for lunch! 

Okay, enough already! Just go try them!

kim-van t. and I are on the same boat with fries... NOM NOM NOM

I heart you, IB garlic fries.  Hot or cold, you are dericious with a kick.  I couldn't stop staring at the curly fries another set of customers were indulging in... *googly eyed*

Beer me...IB fries me... and let the good times roll.  

Another thanks to the cashier for my random request for 5 paper bags.  

EAT HERE

IB craving these cheesesteaks and hoagies.

IB stopping by here when I go to Berkeley for a Cal Football game.

IB inhaling these hoagies.

IB going here since college (and I didn't go to Cal!).

IB impressed with this spot.

IB never let down.

IB giving IB hoagies 5 stars!

i haven't eaten at this place since i graduated, but now that i've been in the real world and tried many a hoagie (or cheesesteak, as it's popularly coined), i haven't found anything better.  

they're greasy, but the good kind of greasy, if you know what i mean.  try the chicken with mushrooms for less guilt.

Went here with the gf yesterday and got a mushroom hoagie to go since breakfast kept us full for the whole afternoon. So i actually ate this hoagie when we came home later in the day and ate it cold because I didn't want to ruin the bread by reheating it. It was still crusty on the outside even 5 hours after I bought it. Amazing! Five stars... this was the best cooked-then-cooled hoagie I've ever had.

Be careful, the tables and stools that are parked outside can get quite hot!
Totally overrated. Didn't have either meatball or the Chicken I wanted. I had their roast beef oven sandwich. Cheesesteak's underpar. If a little cheaper, would be worth bad-average taste.

Sure, food here is satisfying on hungry days (curly fries...mmmmmm....)

HOWEVER, every bite I take, a new pimple pops out of my face. And then I would not step on the scale for days afterwards because I feel so disgusted.

Best words to describe this is: GUILTY PLEASURE.

I wanted to become a regular here, and for a short point in life, I came close. The stocky guy behind the counter seemed to have recognized me,  but that's not why I wanted to go so often. All of my actions were motivated by that Hoagie card. Yes, that card which indicates that you've bought ten hoagies before and have reached "hoagie regular" in which they reward you with a freebie. Needless to say, I failed. I should've kept that card in my wallet, so that I would bring it there consistently. The quality of the sandwiches were not good enough for me to have that often, so eventually I lost my card too.


Nowadays, to mask the pain of my failure, I slowly kill myself through the consumption of their chili cheese curly fries.

Purists probably wouldn't call these cheesesteaks, and even "hoagie" may be a bit of a stretch. Whatever they are, they are seriously tasty in the trashiest greasiest way possible. The garlic cheese steak is amazing, but it not a good idea to eat one if you plan on talking to anyone face to face for the rest of the day. For the seriously indulgent, go for the bucket o' chili cheese fries, and make sure you wash it down with at least 20 ounces of Dr. Pepper. After eating here, prepare to be in a greasy salty stinky haze of happiness - but don't ever think about what you are eating or doing to your arteries, or you'll kill the buzz.

Okay where can you get a bucket of fries for $2.75?  And garlic fries at that with fresh diced garlic?  IB's Hoagies caught my attention because I was in the mood for a Poh'boy sandwich.  While they did not have a poh'boy they did have a yummy Philly cheese steak sammys!  What a fricken deal! $5 for a big frickin sandwich.

Ya gotta love coming into a college town, good cheap eats and lots o' options!

Jr. had the curly chili cheese fries.....in a bucket of course...I'm having that next time!

3.5 stars. 

I am as big of a fan of I.B's Hoagies as anyone. So much so that I've been frequenting the joint that I hold close to my heart since 2005. Back in the day when I was in college I would order a large chili cheese fries, chili cheese burger, and a donut from King Pin donuts. I'll thank early 20's metabolism for being able to survive such glutinous behavior without becoming a whale.

Of recent I feel like the quality is not quite the same. It's used to be a solid 4 stars for me, but I'll dock it a half a star just for a couple recent experiences.

I still would highly recommend IB's for anybody just looking for some greasy 'I want a heartattack' type of food. The value is second to none. An order of a large cheesesteak could easily be 2 meals for only $8.99.

Must orders:
Mushroom Steak: mmm mushrooms, grilled onions, and all the fixings on a toasted french roll. Can't go wrong. I haven't found any other cheesesteak place better than I.B's in the east bay. Enjoyable!

Chili Cheese Curly fries!!!!!: THIS IS MY FAVORITE. Curly fries don't come by that often. Throw on that pippin hot chili and steamin cheese and it's all good in the hood. 

Chili cheese fries: Same chili, same cheese but just with regular fries instead of curly. Still devilishly yummy.

The garlic fries and chili cheese burger are just so so. My next visit I want to try the garlic steak sandwich since they put fresh whole grilled garlic on it. 

Please don't expect a nice dining experience at I.B's. It is in the heart of Berkeley college town. You will get your fair share of obnoxious frat boys and bums just loitering around. The seating is only a couple small circular tables with bar stools. It's a no frills type a joint which is my type of place! It's all good in the hood.

got a "munch on me" voucher for a pepperoni cheesesteak here. curious that my name and the address of this place was whited out on the voucher. had to log onto yelp to find the address.

munch on me promotes single item specials, not entire menus.
sampling: pepperoni cheesesteak (3.99. 33% off)
-surprisingly, pepperoni didn't taste like pepperoni which was a plus.
-hoagie had pepperoni, lettuce, peppers, pickles, mayo, relish in an toasted hoagy bun.
-filling but taste was that of mayo or was that cheese? no meat taste.

crumbs:
-easy using munch on me voucher. they take the voucher and verify the code using their ipad.
-service efficient, couteous.
-metered parking.
-may try burger next, no mo hoagies.

I'm not sure if the sandwiches got bigger or I started to shrink.  This is something that happens with age.  The spine starts to compress, and slowly, if the person doesn't die first, they might wink into nothing due to gravity.

I came here on an impulse.  It was a planned, thoroughly researched impulse.  The impulse to get some cheese fries.  Then my mother convinced me that I should bring a sandwich home so we could all have a nice lunch together.  I order a large sandwich.  And a large cheese fries.  A few minutes later, I was handed a package that cleverly hid the mammoth proportions.  It was like spanx for a sandwich.

As I unwrapped the paper around the mushroom cheesesteak with everything on it, I could feel myself blushing.  "Hey dad, grab the tape measure!"  After dutifully measuring it, the sandwich was 16" long.  And cost $9.  Half of that sandwich and the cheese fries fed a family of 3.

I hate san francisco, and I am moving back to berkeley.  Also, I found out what 5 year old Oreo Cakesters taste like.  It was not pleasant.  Not pleasant at all.

This is the one place I don't get sick of in Berkeley. Their garlic fries/ curly fries/ cheese fries are AMAZING! omgg best place ever. Their cheesesteaks are a good portion for the price. It always lasts me for two meals. I love their mushroom cheesesteak. However, their garlic cheesesteak wasn't all that good to me. But it could just be my taste. Their hamburgers are giant and so juicy too. mmMmmmMmmm

My only criticism...slight slight criticism is that they don't take credit card. I always have to walk to an atm before going to IB's. still totally worth it.

this place reminds me of a walking-distance version of smokehouse. 

i don't remember enjoying my meal much, but i do remember holding back my vomit.

so why two stars instead of one? i like things that are bad for me.

It's places like I.B.'s that makes me wish I were an overweight boy who didn't give a crap about what I ate. Always delicious, but so fattening :(

I love getting the Hot Link or Hot Pastrami sandwich, and I load it up with mustard, hot sauce and jalapeno peppers (tastes better than it sounds, trust me). If I'm super duper hungry, I'll get an order of curly fries (the best kind of fries!). And then I'll stop eating for the rest of the week. 

For the price, the sandwiches are really large (I can split mine into two meals and a snack), and they are generous in how much meat they put in there. The meat is always hot and juicy, and the fries are crispy perfection. I'm getting hungry just writing about them. I'd love to explore the menu a bit more, but that also means I'd have to hit the gym twice a day... I'll think about it.

There's not much seating inside the store itself (it's like a counter and two bar tables and a couple of stools), but they have tables and seats on the pavement out front. Great for evenings, but I hated eating my hot sandwich with the scorching sun on my face. Not very classy at all (actually, nothing about this review is very classy... haha).

gah its like a heart attack in a sandwich. there are just some days that i just crave crave crave for an IB's hoagie.  it just hits the spot like no other. I usually get the mushroom or bbq hoagie.  it's big enough to share or save for dinner.  their curly fries are awesome.  burgers arent bad either. and cheap!  but i suspect there are better hoagies out there since berkeley isnt exactly known for cheesesteak sandwiches so until i find a tastier version i can only give three stars because IB's is just okay.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here on two separate occasions: one with a friend for lunch with two MunchOnMe voucher's in hand, and one solo visit with a third MunchOnMe voucher. I swear, I'm like a walking MunchOnMe ad.

Service here is fairly quick. On my first visit, our two hoagies took about 10 minutes to be served. We sat outside around one of the small diner tables and scarfed down our meal in the sun. On my second visit, my cheeseburger took about 10 minutes to be served as well. With the quality of the food they serve, the wait time was well worth it.

The cashier doesn't seem to enjoy smiling, but she's courteous and quick. In any case, I smiled plenty for the both of us c:

|| F O O D ||

SPINACH CHEESESTEAK: fresh Angus beef cooked with spinach, grilled onions, white bread, cheese, iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, mustard, mayo [6" $4.99 | 9" $6.45 | 15" $10.99 | 9" $4.99 with MunchOnMe]
- I tried to be healthy by opting for the spinach cheesesteak, but there wasn't too much spinach to make me feel healthy. And it's a cheesesteak, for goodness sake. Why do I even bother???
- The beef is tender! But I felt that its flavor didn't really come through, unfortunately. It was overpowered by the vegetables and bread.
- The melted cheese is soooo good.

PEPPER CHEESESTEAK: fresh Angus beef, green bell peppers, pickled peppers, grilled onions, white bread, cheese, iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, mustard, mayo
- My friend said it was decent, but not spectacular.

AVOCADO CHEESEBURGER: Fresh Angus beef (or chicken or veggies), grilled onions, wheat bun, cheese (optional), iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, ketchup, mayo, mustard, 1000 Island dressing [$4.99 | $3.99 with MunchOnMe]
- You can choose between white/yellow America, Swiss, provolone, and cheddar cheese. They also have various patty options: garden, Boca, chicken, or turkey. I opted for the default beef patty with provolone.
- The burger is MASSIVE. It's like 1.25x the size of an In-N-Out burger, and 4x the size of a McDonald's hamburger. When the server handed me my take-out bag, the weight of the bag was immediately noticeable.
- They're very generous with the avocado! As usual, the avocado, which has a slight guacamole texture but is pieced in chunks, doesn't contribute much to taste. But it adds a wonderful creaminess to each bite.
- The meat is well cooked, although there is a whopping amount of veggies and sauces piled in there. But they don't skimp on the size of the patty, which is always appreciated. There is just the right amount of every topping, and it miraculously sticks together till the very end. Also, there isn't a lot of sauce/veggie-water run-off from the bottom of the burger, so your last few bites won't be soggy and gross! Yay!

|| C L O S U R E ||

In terms of taste and flavor, I prefer their burgers. On the other hand, their hoagies are a better bang for the buck because I still felt a remnant of hunger after finishing my burger. But if you order a side of fries, the price matches that of a 9" hoagie, AND you get some fries. And word on the block is that their fries are good. Mmm, looking forward to my next visit already.

Cheese fries. Cheese fucking fries. With that ooey gooey nacho cheese sauce. 

The small bucket/big cup is enough as a meal for me. 

Now, leave me alone as I indulge and continue with my artery-clogging guilty pleasure.

I think their hoagies are just okay, but oh lord...their FRIES...I simply can't get enough...but I do try to limit myself. To only going three times a week. Just kidding. I think. 

They're always freshly deep fried so while you have to wait a few minutes, you are also rewarded with a highly satisfying crunch on the outside and a softness on the inside. IB's sure does know how to salt them too. After I purchase and receive my regular sized order of fries for $1.62 (inc. tax) to go, I inevitably reach into the brown bag to eat a few while hurrying down Telegraph to get home and savor the rest.

CURLY FRIES!!!!  yummm, Fresh and crispy; perfectly fried.  Only quick pit stop to satisfy your curly fries craving on southside.  

I haven't tried anything else, so can't offer any other insights besides that there are only 2 small high tables w/ stools to sit and eat at.  You might need to head over to the asian ghetto to sit down and eat.

Can't talk, eating.   

That's what their cheese steaks do to me.  They render me unable to say anything other than "can't talk, eating" until I finish.  When I was in college I had a routine of coming here for a sammich after every final and watching tv until I fell into a meat and cheese induced coma.  The fries are yummy too.  The only reason I can't give it 5 stars is that there's not a lot of places to sit and eat, and the fries don't travel well.  

FYI - A meal from IB's is best consumed within 15 minutes of when they put it in the bag.  It just doesn't re-heat well

I just tried their cheesesteak hoagie for the first time and now am definitely feeling the food coma coming on. Anyway, it's a good sandwich, fatty yet satisfying, but nothing to call home about. I wish they toasted their bread a little bit; soggy hoagie = no good. Their fries, on the other hand, are fried to perfection. I haven't tried the garlic fries yet, but the curly fries are ace.

From now on, IB's will be my outlet when I am feeling stressed and/or sad and/or need to indulge. I will be coming back for the fries more so than the hoagies.

I was having one of those hectic, messed up days and IB's Hoagies saved me. I had eaten no breakfast or lunch, and my stomach was planning a coup. I had about 5 bucks, so I chose their $1.99 bucket of fries and a smoothie. It was a good choice. 

The fries are large (they're practically wedges) and still steaming when you get them. They are crispy on the outside and tender on the inside...no wimpy, wilted slivers here. And the bucket is huge: I was starving and I couldn't even finish more than half. 

The smoothie was tasty, but for the price I expected a bit more fanfare. Whipped cream, or drizzled chocolate or something. True, I did see them blend the 'real coffee and ice cream' together, but I can't help the fact that I've become spoiled by Starbuck's. But my tastebuds were satisfied, and that's all that really matters.

order the chili cheese curly fries. then go next door to johnston's and buy stewart's ginger beer. go back to ib's to pick up your fries.
sigh. delish.

I heart cheesesteak sandwiches. I think it started back in junior high when my mom would take us to the mall to eat sandwiches there. So when I felt I needed a light snack on a sunny SF afternoon, we headed to I.B.'s Hoagies in good ol' Berkeley. 

Ordered the mushroom steak, with everything on it, and curly cheese fries. The mushroom steak was good, but I think the chicken would've been better. Halfway through it, I realized what was missing - ranch dressing. I asked for some and the sandwich immediately became better. What a waste of half of it with no ranch! Stupid stupid stupid! 

And then the fries. There are cheese fries. And then there are I.B.'s CHEESE. CURLY. FRIES. They must pour in the cheese and the fries together in harmony, because no fry is cheeseless. A small is a huge tub, plenty to share between two people. I could've bought another regular fries and dumped it in there to lighten up the cheesy goodness a bit. 

And if you sit at one of the two high-tops inside, you can people watch all the students and freaks walking by. Or like us, see someone showing his friends the new bong he just bought. Sweet!

Always a nice, affordable stop when you're near UCB. Before or after a hit is up to the individual.

First things first. This is NOT a Philly Cheesesteak shop. They will readily admit this to you if you ask so don't go here hoping for Cheez Whiz or you will surely leave disappointed.

I got the regular cheesesteak, hold the lettuce, tomatoes and pickles (yes, I de-hoagied it). The regular was $5.98 w/ tax (same price for all the variations) and was an 8" soft french roll with about a 3/4" layer of cheesy grilled onions and beef.

The rolls are perfect for the sandwich. Sturdy enough to hold together with the moist fillings, but with a soft crust that isn't going to gouge your gums when you take a huge bite. I really enjoyed the sweet flavor of the grilled onions and just the right amount of cheese oozing between the pieces of chopped steak. A few gristly pieces of meat are bringing this down a notch.

I've had much more consistent hoagies at this location vs. the downtown Oakland one on San Pablo.

Sometimes fake is better.* 

The chili cheese fries at Ib's are some of the best I've had anywhere. 

The cheese is nacho cheese (which I LOVE!), and the chili is super processed and contains no trace of beans (which I HATE!). All that on top of perfectly crunchy-on-the-outside-mushy-on-the-inside fries = perfection. Just look at the picture. 

*Note: Does not apply to people, handbags, or boobs.

I lubs their tubs of fries. 

regular fries, curly fries, garlic fries, cheese fries, chili cheese fries, curly cheese fries -- I want them all.

My favorites are the peppersteak, mushroomsteak, and garlic steak. The large is about the length of from my elbow to fingertips. This place is best for those greasy spoon cravings on the go, but unfortunately, they always take way too long with orders.

Cheesesteak with mushrooms, bucket of garlic fries, large sprite.

Have TUMS handy.
My college boyfriend worked here and always smelled like a hoagie to me.

It's kind of sketchy looking, and the Chinese food isn't the best, but it IS cheap for the amount of food you're getting, and the people who work there are some of the nicest restaurant people I've ever met. I would literally come back and eat here again just because they are so nice!

A-OK for fast food Chinese. They have a variety of choices and we got a ton of food for under $11 including tax.

We ordered the small family meal with white rice instead of fried rice. For the entrees we got spicy chicken and fried pork along with two egg rolls. 

I wish the chicken was more crisp, but because of the buffet style service that is unlikely unless you can get it when it comes out fresh. I didn't like the chow mein, but I had the fried rice before and it's fine.

Panda Express will always be my favorite for fast food Chinese just because I like their orange chicken.

(p.s. woo this is my 100th review!)

it re-opened! everything is super cheap! its your typical chinese food really. greasy, oily, cheap, and a shit load of msg!

its not that great but honestly you are getting what you paid for, which is ridiculously cheap btw!

the chow mein is quite bland. I really liked the spicy tofu though, but the spicy chicken (which is supposed to be the orange chicken i guess) was weird. 

they dont take card either so bring cash!

Your typical Chinese fast food take-out joint, with chow mein, lemon chicken and whatnot. The food is quite greasy, but it's pretty decent, compared with all the mediocre Chinese places around here. I've practically tried everything at this point, since I actually live on top of the place. The portions are generous and it's really really cheap, like only $4 for a two item combo.

Eh. This place is not that great in my opinion. But I guess lots of people like to come here because it's fairly cheap. And college kids are broke. 

This place kind of tastes like Panda Express. You know-fake Chinese food. I'm not a huge fan, but some people just like that kind of stuff.

My experience here wasn't all that great. I thought I'd give it a shot because some of my friends really liked this place since it's cheap and pretty good. So I ordered just 1 entree with tofu. But the tofu was kind of cold, and tasteless, and the rice was very hard. I regret spending my $3.08 here. Even though my friend paid for me. 

But if you are someone who doesn't really mind fast Chinese food, then I'd suggest this place for lunch. It's fast and cheap!

You can't fault them for 'unabashingly' playing the role of cheap, gut-busting, hyper fast chinese food of the neighborhood. For the amount of food you get at the price, it would be unethical to be so critical of this place. However, it is hard to get over the fact that the food is unidentifiable and taste very similarly of the overbearing sauce, across the board. But unlike many other 'express' chinese places, you can visually identify some other colors than brownish red, such as some greens and oranges from vegetables. Also, be ready for the 'chinese food syndrome' as you'll likely overdose on MSG after one meal.

I'm giving this place 4 stars not because it is the greatest Chinese food ever, but because of the quality of Chinese + the price.  I used to come down here (my apt was literally right upstairs...dangerous) and order the spicy chicken + chow mien.  I think this totaled to about $3.  CHEAP!  I came here all 4 years I was a student at Cal... thus the freshman 15.  (not because of the crappy DC food)

For students around the area, or just anyone looking for decent food on a tight budget.
It's a fairly new place, kinda your typical Chinese a-la-carte type of fast food place. The food is above average in my opinion, and fairly cheap, too. The $2.75 special ($3.00 +tax) I believe is still on, and basically it's steamed rice with one entree. Just add a dollar for another entree or chow mein. 

It's cheap and good for days where you just don't want to cook your own food. If you know what Panda Express is, this is basically the same thing, but better food and cheaper. The teriyaki chicken and broccoli are awesome, and basically all the other entrees. They taste good (but that's probably because of the MSG).

It's a small store with a few tables, most people just take-out. Tables are small, from 4-6 person tables.

They ran out of Chow Fun and Orange Chicken, and the cook rudely told me he wouldn't cook more.  Wouldn't have been so bad had there not been a significant wait, but I ended up waiting for ten minutes, only to walk out the door within the next thirty seconds.
Lots of food, super cheap, decent taste. They use ALOT OF MSG though. So be wary. I would recommend the green beans and chicken and the teriyaki chicken.

This place is like Panda Express but for wayyy cheaper. I'm not really that into Chinese food but for when I randomly get a craving this place is perfect. 
I'm pretty stingy when it comes to spending money on food so this place is great for the price. And although it's cheap, they pile on the food. I was able to save half of the food to eat the next day. Honestly if you want Chinese food in Berkeley come here. Other places taste the same so why not pay less?

Also it's cash only and open till 9.

What could be better than dirt cheap, deliciously unhealthy chinese food during finals? 

Great for the price. It's not as delicious as panda express, but then again, it's way cheaper than panda express. 

You can get yourself a decent meal of chow mein and orange chicken for 2.75, no lie. 

Sometime the entrees are gross, sometimes they're frickin delicious. I have no idea why. 

It's cheap food. Cash only, obviously. If it looks old, don't order it.

Known more by Berkeley students as "dollar chinese", this place used to be $1 per item, but I heard it's around $1.50 now.  

I gotta say, this is the only restaurant I know where all my chinese friends refuse, absolutely refuse to go to or get takeout from.  Being non-chinese, however, I had much lower standards.  I gotta say, even at $1.50/item (rice counts as an item), this place is DIRT CHEAP.  Perfect for the starving college student.  As a bonus, being at Channing, it was only about a block from "Roach-dale", my crappy (but also dirt-cheap) college apartment.  I have walked home from classes  and gotten fried rice or chow mein w/ one meat item (usually fried chicken), ate it back at my apartment and got full for a little over 2 bucks.  In that respect, this place totally serves its purpose.

Food quality is a bit similar to what you can buy off the deli section of your local asian supermarket.  Not great, but edible in my opinion.  Though I haven't been here since I left Berkeley years ago, I will always have a soft spot for this place, for keeping a starving student from starving completely.
Cheap and greasy. But cheap. Larger selection, and fresher than the place that used to be there.

This place advertises $1.49 lunch...  Need I say more?  It is a convenient restaurant/buffet if you have a hangover and just want to pick up a cup of soup or something, but it is cheaper and lower quality than a food-court Panda Express, so it is probably not too good for your overall life span.

I would say more around the level of 3.5 basically because it is very super fast and cheap, because it has that panda express take out so there is no waiting for your food. The price is very cheap, ranging around 3-5 dollars. The food is alright, nothing fancy or special so im not such as huge fan of that. Very greassy and oily, their chow fun is okkaayy... mainly go here for their price and its location between my house and the school.

Also the portions aren't so large, you get one rice or chow main option onto the large portion of your plate, and then a choice of item in one corner of the triad plate, so a very small portion of meat.

Yeah..dollar chinese is not particularly tasty, nor does it taste like "real" chinese food, but honestly its about 100x better than the dining hall across the street. This place saved my ass so many times when I was living in the dorms and could literally no longer stomach dorm food. I just got the fried rice (mmm) with the only tofu dish they had there and it was always edible and almost tasty! I've never gotten ill, nor has anyone else I know that has eaten there. That being said, I think it'd be a bit risky to buy any sort of seafood dish there.
The same guy is always serving and he's really nice. I stopped eating there once I moved a few blocks down, but if you're in the area, hungry, and only want to spend about $2.50 for a filling meal, this is the place.
You get what you pay for. Cheap and lots of variety, but the food is mediocre at best. Most items are too salty and/or oily. Avoid unless on an extraordinarily tight budget.

Good cheap Chinese take-out that's not too greasy or salty.  My co-workers and I come here and order the large family dinner to split between 3 and always leave full and satisfied.  If I go by myself, I  normally get the 3 item combo with can soda.  The portions are very generous.  The orange chicken is good for fast-food quality.

Cheap and edible, that's about all you need to know. If you're looking for a quick fix for a few bucks, this is the place go. The wide range of entree options makes it easy for the meal to be hit and miss, but the very simple knowledge that there exists within the possibilities something that tastes and feels alright is good enough for me. Three stars sounds about right.

Won ton soup for $1.65
lots of fat and salt in every dish
nice people
Patrons include homeless to emeriti
avoid the overcooked*

*Special tip: for dishes with vegetables, only get the ones that still look green....duh

i got their 4 dollar meal which was one entree, fried rice/ noodles, and eggroll/potsticker. i was really satisfied with the price and the amount of food that came with it which lasted me almost two meals. i got their spicy chicken and chow fun. both were really good and i can't wait to go back to try the others. however, i wouldn't recommend the potstickers. i thought i'd get 2 potstickers instead of 1 eggroll, but they still give you just one potsticker and it's really not that good. the skin was all dry and not warm so i'd go with the eggroll next time.

This place is the Panda Express of Berkeley. Stupid berkeley noobs decided to prevent Panda Express from opening a location on campus, even though it would raise revenue for the school and the current location is still unoccupied. 

The food at China Express is honestly pretty bad. It's about as good as panda express. This place deserves four stars because it's the only Chinese-fastfood style restaurant in the entire campus area. This is important if you don't feel like waiting at a sit-down restaurant, such as the nearby Sun Hong Kong.
The best cheap food in town. I frequent this place. Never been sick. AWESOME/quick service from people who actually appreciate it.

I. Loved. Dollar. Chinese.

Unfortunately this last time I went out to the area, I found out that it wasn't a dollar anymore. And when I drove by to get some, it wasn't even open. Did this place close? If it did, I'll be very sad, because it was great. Similar to Panda Express or Manchu Wok, but individually made and delicous. And a dollar. 

Yep. I loved it. And now it's gone.

I live a minute away from this place and decide to try it. I'm a vegetarian, so I ask if I can try a piece of their tofu dish. The lady tries to give me a vegetable. I ask her for a piece of tofu, she gives me a dirty look then does it. So, I order the fried rice, veg. roll, and tofu dish to go. She gives me a ton of fried rice, four pieces of broccoli and 2 pieces of tofu and a veg roll. total was $4. the portion of rice was ridiculous and the one thing i did want (tofu) I only got two pieces of...kinda silly..i know, you get what you pay for. They use MSG so I prob. will not go back here again. The lady was mean too...I asked her how she was and no response, just a dirty look.

My favorite place to get kung pao chicken. It's extra spicy, inexpensive, and delicious.  I love that I can get a box of chicken and a box of rice for about 4 dollars.  Pretty awesome.  The place is kind of old and looks kinda gross, though. Lol.

Great Cheap Chinese Takeout!

I always get the 3 Item combo with Spicy Chicken, Broccoli Beef and white rice. It comes out to exactly $5. Super good deal.

I usually avoid the fried rice and chow mein because there is just wayyy too much MSG. The lemon chicken is also pretty tasty. I come here for lunch all the time, especially when I want a ridiculous amount of food.
I've gotten higher quality food in microwavable tv dinners from safeway

Great lunch destination.  Quick, easy, and good.  No waiting in line for very long.  I got the three item combo for just over $5 and choose the fried rice, mongolian beef (nice and mildly spicy), and fried chicken (which is basically the chicken they use for sweet and sour chicken, without the sauce. nice and crispy. yum).  

My only complaint is that they take cash only.

cheaper than panda express, but not as good. quality is really lackluster here, even for a quickie place. they've upgraded the look and the prices are good, but most of the stuff i've tried wasn't too good. potstickers were nice. chow mein and fried rice were below par. as was orange chicken. don't think i'll be returning.
My broke-ass student type friends took me here and the food was nothing to write yelp about but it was super cheap and we had a good time.

Food: Pretty darn good! I've had a variety of Chinese food in my life, everything from Americanized Panda Express to the spiciest of noodle bowls in the outskirts of X'ian. Of course, they curtail their Chinese menu to the bear necessities for college students: you will always be able to find orange chicken and sweet-and-sour pork. Still, if you've ever gone to Panda Express feeling wronged by the clearly re-heated frozen foods and scant portions, Chinese Express will ease the pain, while still providing fast and fresh foods.

Atmosphere: Not a place to sit down. The restaurant is clean and orderly, but the size and table arrangement isn't conducive to sustained conversations of any sort. Besides, who would want to chat with their friends at a place where everyone in the restaurant could hear every word? I have only ever gotten my food to-go here, and I don't plan on changing that.

Service: Fast, efficient service. The workers don't have the greatest grasp on English, so you may need to slow down and repeat your orders.

Take-it-from-Me: This place serves HUGE portions. I am a 6' 2" man, and I could not come close to finishing a 2-item combo. No need to spend more money on a bigger meal. Always choose less at Chinese Express!

Nothing better than food court chinese. Chewy beef..decent chicken.
I asked for a knife.."We don't have knives" What?
dirt cheap chinese joint that definitely hits the spot. the chow mein was downright adequate and the orange chicken was completely fine.

I was craving some Chinese fast food one day and decided to give this place a go.  I had passed by before and noticed it's super cheap -- $3.75+tax for a two item combo, which gives you chow mein or fried rice (I think you can also get chow fun), an entree item and an egg roll.

There was hardly a wait which was nice.  However, the food wasn't so nice.  Now I know you have to hold this kind of food to a different kind of food to a different kind of standard -- you should expect your food to be greasy and MSG-laced.  I'm totally fine with that.  You won't find a bigger Panda Express fan out there than me!  

But honestly, the food here just tasted.... OLD.  I don't mind if food has been sitting in a heating tray all day as long as I can't taste.  But I could definitely taste it.  The chow mein was indeed greasy, as other's have pointed out.  But more importantly, it was flavorless and limp and... like I said OLD.  The fried part of the orange chicken was really tough and chewy despite the copious amount of sauce.  The chicken itself was dry as well. The egg roll wasn't bad, though not very crispy.

Maybe you just need to go earlier in the day when the food has just been made, but from the way things tasted I wouldn't be surprised if they save their food for the next day....  I think I'll try this place once more, just because the price is so good.  Hopefully I'll have better luck next time.

My friend and I were craving for Panda Express and since there's none in Berkeley, we decided to try this out. Compared to other Chinese restaurants around, I would say this is the cheapest you get. However, what you pay is what you get. The food is mediocre, not as fresh as I would like and definitely greasy. The restaurant is small and looks kinda dirty also.

This is probably the cheapest place around Telegraph for what you get. Don't expect high quality though. 

Don't get the orange chicken or sweet and sour pork. It's mostly  bread/batter/fat covered in sweet sauce and not actual chicken or pork. Stick to the entrees that are mostly vegetables because at least you know what you're getting. 

The shrimp/broccoli is good and also is the other dish with green beans 

Also fried rice was kinda dry...

I love everything about this place. This is your typical Chinese restaurant albeit smaller, fast food style, and close to campus. It's cheap, greasy, filling, and plentiful. The place is a bit like Panda Express except it's not a chain but a family owned restaurant. It's also a bit more fresh but not as much as a regular sit down restaurant obviously.

My roommate and I came here and got three entrees and a big pile of fried rice and fried noodles for $11 total. You can try anything you want and we literally sat there and tried almost everything. They didn't complain and were happy to hear us out. 

It's not fancy so for no frills, cheap Chinese that is close by come here! The name does not lie. The only thing that was annoying about this place was cash only. There were a few seats but this place is mostly take out. I think I counted about 20 or 25-30 seats max but most people take out so it's all good.

The food is greasy, comes in large quantities, and is extremeley filling and dirt cheap.  They make traditional 'Chinese' dishes and you select a few items to be paired with fried or steamed rice.  The choices are really Americanized stuff like orange chicken and broccoli beef.  All the choices sit under heatlamps for god knows how long.  Every dish is teeming with MSG (you'll probably take a nap after eating here).  The place was remodeled not too long ago, but still has quite a dirty feel to it.  If it weren't for the speed (i get togo usually) and cheap price of it, I would definitely rate it two stars.   Nothing spectacular, but definitely a place to drop by if you're hungry and short on cash or in a rush.

Oh yea, and its cash only.

It's mediocre pricing, but value conscious in relation to everything else on Telegraph, but it's really bad quality. I mean bad quality as in it leaves you with the greasy lazy feeling after eating a meal there. It will hit you within 15 minutes, and you'll want to sleep during class. Their fried rice is either raw or reheated. It's just not soft enough.

Quick service Chinese tends to be lousy.  I mean, we all eat it or at least I do.  It's cheap and filling.  Chinese Express, however, steps it up a notch.  Their dishes sitting in their little tray holes actually look fresh and tasty.  It took me a while to decide what I wanted because everything looked good. 

Some points:
1. Their chow mein actually had chicken and veggies in it.  They were not just flavorless and limp noodles.
2. Their chicken dishes all tasted different and their spicy chicken had some real heat to it.
3. I got a ton of food for 6 bucks with tax.
4. I want to go back now as we speak.

A minor detractor:
1. Hey, why not put your water station out where the customers can use it?  Your spicy chicken made me thirsty!

you need 2 Fast and 2 Furious China Man in da House Ninja Take Out to Go for Cheap and dont wanna pay money, but Panda Express too Far??  COME HERE..

best place for poor hungry students who want chinese and dont care about getting obese.. both guys and girls come here so obviously health is not an issue when it comes to getting cheap late nite chinese food.

The food is better at Panda Express cuz its way more fresh and also WAY less MSG + grease + oils in your mouth.. but its way more expensive..

I give Panda express 4 stars.. so why does this place also get 4 stars?
Cuz for students, its CLOSE, HELLA ghetto AZN cheap, Nice people, and the nice hot ready food is super seasoned to the point that you have to love it..

Again, HOLY crap on the seasoning and the MSG aftermath: coma.. maybe a headache.. belly huge.. gut coming outside pants..muffin top for sure..

but seriously, for the price you pay and the nice service.. its perfect.. especially for poor students who study late and need something super quick and fast..

all the Yelpers on this board are telling the truth when it comes to massive food combo and price.  you will feed two people well for $10 here..

The Point:
Great price and food turn-around is pretty good.
They dont have orange chicken instead they offer a twist;
--Lemon chicken
--And sweet/spicy chicken! (Personal Favorite)

Noodle:
Try the chow fun, its rare and goes well with kung pow chicken.

Chinese Express aka ChineX as my friend affectionately calls it is OFF 
THE HOOK. I straight up went here six days in a row.

This place is FAST and CHEAP. And kinda good (notice the emphases). It's CASH ONLY and a two item or three item combo will be plenty of food. Don't waste your money on a four item combo - it's the same amount of food as a three item. 

You know how whenever you watch people scoop food into your plate/container and you see them pause and then hope for one more scoop of food? You ALWAYS get that here. That's the beauty of Chinex - good, fast service for less than 6 bucks. Don't come here expecting gourmet dumplings or steamed fish. Come here expecting to stuff your face with slightly unhealthy fast-food style Chinese, and you will not be disappoint.

Since coming to Berkeley, I've been looking for a place that is similar to Panda Express. Although I've found some edible chinese places here and there, none really appealed to me. I tried Chinese Express yesterday and I was in awe!!!! I finally found the Panda Express of Berkeley. Their food are so fairly priced compared to the overly priced food in Berkeley in general and the quality is amazing!!!! Not to mention the people there are very friendly!
I immediately called my roommate to share my happiness and told her that she must try it also!! Screw all the other chinese restaurants, I'm going there only from now on!!!

I always come here when I'm craving cheap Chinese take-out! I'm seriously such a huge fan of it because it's so cheap and I don't feel disgusting after I finish eating stuff from here like I would at other Chinese take-out places. Once in a while when I have friends over and we're feeling lazy, we'd buy a family meal for $20 and it can seriously feed 5-6 hungry college students/college graduates. It's sooo worth it! If you're feeling extra cheap, they have combos with an entree with white rice for about $3! Personally I love the Spicy Garlic Chicken, but I haven't really had anything I absolutely hated.

Anyone giving this place a bad review... set their standards way too high for Chinese take-out. If you want some gourmet Chinese food, you shouldn't be looking here.

This place is a hidden gem! The epitome of cheap Chinese food. There was a vast variety of chicken entrees, it's unbelievable. I ordered a 3 entree meal with fried rice. Delicious. I just didn't like that the string bean chicken had mushrooms in it but that's alright.

So I have been craving that Combo A or Combo #2 ghetto Chinese food for the longest time. I actually even went to this restaurant three times around 8:45pm for quite some time, but they would always be closing and refuse to service me. I would argue with them that they close at 9, but they just apologized and sent me away.

I don't know why people like this place so much. Okay so let me talk about the food for starters. Maybe it's because I only go at night, but Chinese Express tastes like it was delivered by express mail or something because that chicken, rice, and chow mein is stale! It was disgusting. I did gobble it down because Chinese food is always pretty good, but mine was hot out of a frying pan and it still wasn't very tasty.

Another thing is that they only take cash. I had to go run to the ATM to get some cash and upon paying the cashier gave me the most janky, pink colored $5 bill that was ripping as my change. I asked to get another one, but he was super stingy and said he closed the register as he was actually closing it so he wouldn't be able to give me a different $5.

But if you're looking for cheap chinese food with pretty good portions eat at this place. It's not anything you MUST try, but its just that typical cheap chinese take out food so if you're broke and feel like eating paper. Go hit this place up.

the Great,
GumZ

3 dollars for dinner is a win

they have a couple decent vegee options

gotta love spring breans n tofu

no credit cards

This is a great take out Chinese place. They pile on the food, and it's cheap!

The food's pretty good. Definitely better quality than Panda Express. If you've ever had Lucky's, it's a bit like that. I got fried rice, with string beans with peppered beef, and orange chicken with onions. The peppered beef dish was a little bit salty, but the string beans mixed in made it okay. And the orange chicken was a bit too Americanized, but just eat with the chow mien or fried rice, and it's fine. I liked the fried rice the best. Often times, these take out places don't have very good fried rice, but I liked this one.

It certainly did quench my craving for Chinese food since I've moved to college.

I literally live several yards away from this low-cost joint, and do take out there at least twice a week. Food is cheap cheap CHEAP (two item combo and drink is less than $5), and pretty delicious too! If you want to eat healthier, they do have several vegetarian options available.

Note that I am basing my rating on the quality of food for the price. It's good for the college undergrad who is already paying way too much for rent.

OK, let me just start by saying that my three stars are not a recommendation for or an endorsement of this place.  I've eaten food from here, and I might do so again in the future, but you're probably risking your health and you're definitely risking your conscience if you do so.

So this place is really cheap.  That's about its main draw.  I'm talking really cheap.  Someone's got to be getting exploited in this equation; there's no alternative.  Either the owner loses money left and right, or you're eating unsafe food, or he buys his ingredients from places that use slave labor.  Or I guess he could work for the VA and he gets a bulk discount.

The food is really spicy and not terribly good.

This review is dedicated to MK & AK.

This place has a special place in my heart. When my roommates and I first moved into Palazzo (on Telegraph between Channing&Haste), we would run down and get the 3 entree combo with a drink for only $5. This was before it got renovated and became 'Chinese Express'. There was flashing neon sign that said $1.45, and we fondly called it 'Greasy Chinese' (the boxes weren't clear then, and the food usually left lots of grease strains). Upperclassmen always warned us NOT to eat here and made fun of us for doing so, but we did anyways. It was as good as it was cheap.

Then it closed. That was a sad year, we had to resort to Thai Noodle (also downstairs). That was good too, but couldn't really fill the void of 'Greasy Chinese'. THEN, IT WAS BACK. Better than ever, no flashing neon signs, new tables and chairs. It basically looked liked a Panda Express. Everyone that hated on it, started to recommend it. But we knew 'Greasy Chinese's ' secret: The BOX! They switched from the old paper-like box that soaks up the grease to a really nice plastic one.  But they had the same cashier, same cook, same food, and the same CASH ONLY policy.

So, I like what I like. This is what I've consistently ordered for the past 29833 times I've gone:
Half Fried Rice & Half Chow Mein, Orange Chicken, String Beans, Welch's Grape Soda. 
(The Orange Chicken is especially good if it's freshly made)

I've also catered family/party packs for guests on many occasions. I would just run downstairs 15 minutes before they're about to arrive, pick up the food, plate everything, and VOILAA! ready to serve. If you're ever on a time crunch to get food for a large group of people, GET FOOD HERE. 

You get what you pay for, so how can you be unsatisfied? The only big downer in my opinion is the CASH ONLY policy. Since it was downstairs from my apartment, it was pretty inconvenient for me to go to the bank and come back. There was a time when I paid with laundry $ and with a $100. But cash is cash! So if you want that  'starving, college student' experience, GO!

Hells to the no. I dont know what I was thinking the first time. Maybe within that year, the quality has gone down but yeah.... Last time I got it, super oily and made my stomach hurt the next morning. My friend got it recently and he was moaning from the pain in his stomach. Maybe there was some bad meat or something :( I avoid this place now.

I am officially hooked on this place, specifically for the Broccoli and prawn dish. If someone at UC Berkeley can figure out what this place does to make their Broccoli taste so good, in my books, they desirve a Noble Peace Prize. The sauce in this dish is so minimal, but so dang tasty. Also, for a place like this, one would expect packaged frozen gross veggitables, but it seems like they use actual fresh produce. 

I also always grab a box of their chow mein along with my $2.95 combo A.

Couple of things, since reading the prior reviews, people seem to bag on this place.
-why the heck do other Yelpers get their panties all in a bind over "cash only places??"----ok yeah, i can agree, credit should be offered at a sit-down table-clothed joint, but at a $5 take out dive? Perhaps, there will be a Sophomore economic class which you may learn the reasoning why places like this are cash only---stop griping! Jeez, you should always be carrying a $20 on you for emergencies. 

-yup, if you come at odd hours, slow times, if the food has sat under a heat lamp, and has begun to turn brown on each corner, yeah, you will probably find it gross once you eat it----my  suggestion towards world peace to you, don't order the food which looks like that---

speaking of which, I would like to update my review with what i call my course in Chinese Economics------this in the Spirt of UC Berkeley, and the fact that I am Chinese, and that at one time I wanted to be a teacher-

So, here we go-
Of late, I have been gung-ho over their so called, "Family Dinner Specials"----they offer two of them

a. 2-3 persons, $9.95
b. 3-4 persons $16.95

So one would think, "dinner specials" means you are getting a deal by buying more than a $1.79 box of fried rice----right?-----oh, these is where Chinese economics comes in-----

So, I have been happily existing with my head in the sand, buying the 2-3 person $9.95 special-----it just dawned on my to add up what I was getting and to then revel on my savings. 

so here we go, for $9.95 you get 1 medium fried rice, 1 medium chow mein, your choice of 2 egg rolls or 3 pot stickers, and your choice of  2 medium entrees------OK, savings, start piling up, you say!!!

lets do the math
a Medium rice or chow mein off the menu costs $1.79
a medium entree of your choice costs $3.00

1.79 x 2---$3.59, 2x$3--$6-----so we are at $9.59-----wait, that is less than $9.95 you ask, ---but oh, the 2 egg rolls----which they basically give to you for .36 cents------
that my students and friends is Chinese economics----

questions? good you all get A's, and next time at China Express, just order what you want a-la-carte, it is cheaper-

class dismissed

Large Family Meal (says feeds 4-5, or you know, 3 hungry Asian girls) for $15.95: Large chow mein, large fried rice, 2 large entrees , and 6 potstickers/4 eggrolls.

Entree we chose: General tso's chicken and teriyaki chicken with the potstickers. 

ALL SO GOOD. They left some skin on the teriyaki chicken, and it has a slight curry taste.

The worker (owner's son?) was VERY nice. When he was packing our food he asked "no vegetables?" and my friends said "NO, we want to get our money's worth!" His response? He threw in green beans and only charged $15. 

OH, and did I mention he whipped out toothpicks so we could sample and choose? HELLA NICE.

I AM A HUGE FAN OF CHINESE EXPRESS.

Best deal in Berkeley, period. To be real, Chinese Express is no fancy 5-star restaurant but their food is all pretty good. For less than $6 you get 2 items + fried rice/chow mein AND a drink. Dude, no one not even Chipotle, Panda Express, or Subway can cook up a deal better than that. 

If you're a broke college student looking for a meal to fill you up for 2/3 of the day, Chinese Express is the way to go.

RECOMMENDATION:
3 ITEM COMBO + Drink

Good friends, good food, ENJOY!

I absolutely LOVE Chinese take out food. I don't care man. I really don't care if it isn't authentic. It is diabetes in chicken mode and that's all I need.
