I have dreams of eating out of tiny containers on an apartment floor, I love it that much.

You know what pack of Asians, that were staring me down as I ate Orange chicken, silently judging me?
You were there too. I'm Mexican. I don't know any better. 
I don't complain when you eat at Taco Bell.

The guy behind the counter didn't judge me. He took my order with a smile. Definitely do come back here several times. In the beginning, I was starting to doubt this place. It was just me and the guy behind the counter. Then the construction crew came in. Medley of everyone! And they looked happy too :)

I haven't had Chinese take-out in a while, but there is something about those little red and white boxes that are so luring. As far as Chinese take-out goes, I like this place, especially when I'm on a budget. This place has been remodeled, looking a lot more modern now. It looks pretty clean, probably because no one really eats in here. There seems to be a small, but steady flow of customers who come in, but order take-out. It's a shame because there are lots of tables.

The boyfriend and I didn't want to fight over chow mein or fried rice, so we went with the small family dinner combo for 2-3 people. It includes a large box of fried rice, chow mein, an entree, another entree, and 2 egg rolls or 3 dumplings. We picked the egg rolls over dumplings. We also picked the orange chicken and shrimp with broccoli as our two entrees. The guy who served us loaded up the boxes past the top, then smushed it all down to get it all in. Those were some packed and heavy take-out boxes we left with. It was $9.99, $10.92 after tax.

They also have a large dinner combo for 4-5 people. They also have a one entree plus rice deal for $3. There's also a four entree combo for $6. Seriously. That is cheap. That is really cheap.

bottom line: cheap + plentiful

cash only

Two college students are sitting in their rooms wondering what to eat for dinner. One says "Man I want some Chinese take-out. I don't care how shitty it is. Just Yelp the closest place and we'll go."

Fast forward 10 minutes and my roommate and I are standing at Chinese Express. Everything looked really fresh and steaming hot, so we decide to pick what we want to order.

Instead of getting the 3 or 4 item combo, the guy behind the counter offers us a deal we can't resist: rice, chow mien, 3 entrees, and potstickers/egg rolls. ALL FOR $10. At this point it was just too good to be true, but we went along with it anyway. After paying for the food, it was a struggle getting it back to our place because the bag was SO HEAVY. We were in utter disbelief at how much food we got for $10.

As I sit here finishing my last bites, I'm still in shock. Compared to Panda Express and other cheap Chinese take-out, this stuff isn't too bad at all. The boneless beef short ribs are really good, and so was the orange chicken. 

This is probably the best deal in town for a poor starving college student. I would probably die from MSG poisoning if I had it every day, but it's good once in a while. The guy behind the counter was really helpful and was the one to introduce us to this deal in the first place. 4 stars for food + 1 star because it's so ridiculously cheap

When I started at Berkeley, this place was $0.99 per item, and during my student tenure here, it was raised first to $1, then to $1.10, and then to $1.25 per item.  I'm sure it's hovering around $1.50/item here now.  It was known as "the cheap dollar chinese place."

This place is DISGUSTING.  Seriously.  When I was living in the Unit 3 dorms across the street, this was the closest place to get something quick and cheap.  I kid you not, though, one time I was going home for Thanksgiving and was busy packing, so I didn't have enough time to eat.  I picked up some GREASY chinese food here, and it literally made me ill.  I threw up twice - once in the dorms, and once on the plane ride home, and it actually ruined my Thanksgiving dinner.

Oh, how I hate you.  You kept me from my mother's sweet honey roasted ham, you devil restaurant you.

I didn't eat at Chipotle for the longest time (2 years) because of its treatment of farmers a few years back. According to http://www.betterworldshopper.com/r-fastfood.html, they've improved so I started eating at Chipotle again a few months ago. That website is a factor among others that I use to guide my decision on where to eat when necessary.

+ They move customers through there with ease
+ Good service, never bilks when I ask for "more" cheese, beans, or chicken
+ Clean joint
-  Bummer that you can't exchange your student's 'free' drink with a bag of chips instead
-  Nutritional content and source of ingredients?

Final Call:
Decent, quick food that's convenient on the go. This is ideal student food because I was mobile and constantly needed to eat on the move.

I think the food at all Chipotle locations taste the same. The star ratings came from the portion size compared to a lot of other locations I've been to and the looks you get from the workers who definitely don't want to be there. It's usually busy when I go so it's always hard to find a place to sit.

I'm sure you've tried Chipotle before, so the taste is always pretty standard. Before you read on, you should know i LOVE Chipotle and avoid walking down Telegraph to go home because I know I'd be tempted soon as I see their logo. (Steak Burrito Bol w/ tortilla on the side: extra rice, no beans, corn, mild salsa, small bit of sour cream, cheese, lots of lettuce = amazing!) 

Portions: During the student rush, they sometimes skimp when they add all that noms chicken/steak/corn/rice. But the servers are always really friendly and will oblige if you ask for extra rice or lettuce, etc. 

One thing you HAVE to try if you haven't already: SMOKED Chipotle sauce! I'm not the biggest fan of spicy, but this makes the burrito so so tasty. If you don't see one lying around (*ahem to the people who steal them), ask the cashier and they always bring out a new one for you. 

There aren't too many tables to sit and eat your food, so I usually take my food to go.

Man do I love Chipotle. I'm so addicted that I'm willing to stand in the line that goes out the door and into the street during lunch hour. Thankfully they've got deployment down and can move the line pretty quickly. The quality is always good, the workers are mostly friendly and the food is always tasty. I also love that even though the company stopped giving free drinks to students in college, this location still does it.

I truly don't get these places.

The only Mexican thing about Chipotle is the name and the people working behind the counter.

Other than that ,it's just a generic attempt at  food lab Mexican .

No taste.
No character.
No reason to come here.

I love huge, gigantic, calorie filled burritos that totally ruin your diet plans but are so totally worth it 

one delicious piece of goodness wrapped in aluminum foil. 

Being the stingy asian that I am, I usually get burrito bowl (it seems that they give slightly more) with extra rice and extra lettuce with tortilla on the side (they wrap it for you in aluminum foil). 

yumyumyum

Another one of my favorite places to go when I'm looking for something fast and delicious to eat before my next class. Lines may be long, but it goes by pretty quickly since the workers know what they're doing and they do it at a fast pace too. 

I've been to other Chipotle's in San Jose, and their portions are MUCH larger than the one in Berkeley, but I won't complain since I get a free soda as a Cal student. Honestly, all you have to do is ask for extra helpings of what you want, and they'll give it to you since they only charge for the meat. I normally ask for extra rice (and by extra, I mean a lot) and they willingly throw in one or two more scoops of the rice. I haven't tried any other meat except for chicken, but perhaps I'll give steak a shot one day. 

I always order a rice bowl with extra rice, fajitas, chicken, hot sauce, and lettuce. I know, I know, it's not a lot, and I've gotten plenty of weird looks from people when they look at my plain rice bowl, but I wouldn't have it any other way. I can honestly say, I think I've become addicted to this place. Service is great, the food is good, and it keeps my tummy happy (although my wallet has taken a heavy hit from all the frequent stops to Chipotle).

Definitely the place to go if you want something quick and easy to eat while you're on a break.

Ok, so the foods amazing. Of course! However, the staff is RUDE and STINGY. They rush you while you're trying to order and they yell at you if you are not ordering fast enough. I know they have to rush and everything, but they could at least be polite to their customers. Also, they barely fill up the bowls. Ugh. But i guess the food is good...tho its overpriced.
Good Mexican fast food. I love their burrito bowls, but they definitely need to stop being so stingy about their helpings.

i love chipotle ... but mann i got a bowl yesterday ... it wasn't as good as other chipotle. i was disapointed... the chicken was really burnt and kinda cold-ish. but anyways it was edible ... wasnt tooo terrible ... but still hah

Can't really review a chain restaurant. But, the service at UC Berkley one is not the best, since they are stingy. 

Otherwise, I love the burritos and quesadilla(off the menu)

This Chipotle is more expensive than others, and the prices just keep creeping up. 

That being said, Like most Chipotles there's decent food, but service here is the worst that I've encountered. 
The first person on the line appears to have a problem with selective hearing; I'll ask clearly for a bowl with a tortilla and the guy/girl will just plop in some rice/beans and toss the bowl aside. This has happened three times in a row now. Then today, the next person (that handles meat) didn't even ask what kind I wanted and gave me steak. She was so focused on adding in meat that she didn't even notice when I tried to tell her [twice] I wanted chicken. It wasn't that big of a deal since I was in a rush, but what if I 'd been seriously offended by the beef, or hadn't been willing to pay the extra  45 cents? To top it off, it's just plain annoying to open the bowl and find that ten minutes of walking has shifted the contents enough to reveal a bowl that is barely two thirds full. Come on, I'm already hungry enough without my tortilla :( 

Basically, I only put up with the crappy service and pitiful meals because like almost everyone else, I need the napkins.

I hate to call Chipotle "fast food" But that's what it is..
I love the fact that they support the local farmers as much as humanly possible. Being that this one is Cali, you know it's all out local.
A lot of the stuff is organic, but mostly natural.
Vegan/Vegetarian/Carnivore friendly, straight down the middle!
Quick in and out, or sit in and chow.
Can't beat these Burrito's. I've tried to find one near Oakland, this is the place for a Burrito..so far!
Chipotle is a very good place to spend your money. They donate to many true charitable causes. Check there very cool site for more info and news and events!
Read up on the history of Chipotle,you may find yourself quite surprised..

Good Job Chipotle!

The food here is alright. I like getting the burrito bowls because I can easily save it if I can't finish it. There are usually extremely long lines here during lunch hours.  I try to avoid getting lunch here because of the lines, but I've heard from other people that the staff work very efficiently when there are long lines and even if the end of the line is out the door and several stores long, it'll only take about 10-15 minutes for you to order your food, pay for it, and be on your way.

Cal students also get a free drink with their meal. Yay for free stuff!
Can you really trust medium rare meat in a fast food restaurants?

quality (mostly) organice ingredients. great value relative to other berkeley eateries. great service, line moves quickly even if it is long during rush hour. free drink with student ID.
not great for groups because seating is limited, but that's how 90% of the places in berkeley are so you should be used to that by now.
i've never had a problem getting exactly the quantity of food i want there. if you complain it's not healthy then stop asking for extra cheese and sour cream you idiot. it's more healthy than most mexican food places because you can see what they're giving you and ask for proper quantities. the ingredients are also organic so it has that going for it.
lastly, burritos aren't mexican food so if you're complaining that their burritos aren't authentic then maybe you should order tacos because burritos aren't really served in mexico.

what the hell. first, you run out of veggies and make me stand there awkwardly, expecting me to ask for meat. do you really expect me to ask you for meat when i'm a vegetarian?? I stood in like for 10 minutes, and then had to wait another 10. the guy was super stingy with everything, i had to ask for more! I weigh a 118 pounds..so it isn't like i'm being greedy for anything...then I pay. way to comp me somehow for my time...then I get home, and the beans aren't even cooked all the way!! WHAT THE HELL...so over this place. la burrita has my heart again.

The worst portion sizes ever!!! I'm from socal, and the chipotle by my house gives a substantially larger amount than this one. At home, I can eat half a bowl and feel stuffed. I can finish the entire bowl here. The portions here are ridiculous, and I'm wondering why different locations would be trained to give different sized portions.

The place is crowded every time I walk past it, and frankly I don't know why.  Disappointing.

The price you pay for the quantity of food you receive is simply a rip off.  I've gotten twice, maybe even triple the amount of same-quality food at other Chipotle Mexican Grills.

The service is poor.  Workers are stingy.  Place is cramped.  Definitely avoiding this one from now on.  For $6.50, I would've at least liked to have a full scoop of rice.

I used to eat here a lot, then I realized it all tastes the same --like nothing. Plus you're supporting large corporate chains by eating here. Do yourself a favor and try one of the many other locally owned places nearby. Sure you get a free soda, but you really don't need a soda on top of your 2000 calorie burrito.

I know that chipotle is very americanized mexican food, but I dont care. I just love it. 

This place was pretty crowded tonight, but the people working there had it under control. The line was to the door, but I had my carnitas burrito in less than five minutes.

The quality is consistent, but the proportions are extremely tiny. I swear the guy was counting how many tiny cubes of chicken he should put in a taco--it came out to about a tablespoon of meat. And they are extremely rude. I had been going here for a long time (not anymore), and the old staff were better.

I've been to the Chipotle on Gilman and the one in Alameda, and both are good.

Nice staff, good food! It's a pain sometimes when school is in with the long lines..they use to give a free soda to staff/students on campus with your ID but I haven't had this happen for quite some time now..

Your standard Chipotle restaurant.
Prices are around $5-7, and Cal students get a free drink!
Pretty good service and their citrus-infused chips are pretty amazing.

I appreciate their effort to use good ingredients, and to let customers know if they are not able to get the best ingredients at the moment. One thing is I hope they don't burn the chicken so much. Carcinogens!!! :( But maybe phytochemicals in veggies will balance it out? I'm always up for some good burrito bowl with lots of peppers and onions,lettuce, and corn!
Used to love chipotle, until I found Pancho's nearby. Could never look back. Farewell chipotle... ^, . ^~

It's the end of a long day...7 hours running around between hiking and grocery shopping, and I am STARVING.  Oh my god, Chipotle?  What a great idea!

Seriously, this place never disappoints me.  Definitely the best chain restaurant in the campus area, and getting a lightning fast uber burrito made of chicken and god is always pleasing.

ok ok, so we know its fake mexican food.  it's still bomb, ya dig?!

lines are usually long, but it goes by fast.  don't order the chicken (wayyyy too much grissle to be chicken meat).  Also, i had to bump down a star cuz they aaaalways be outta the chipotle flavored tabasco sauce (the bbq flavor one).  

I love the carnita burrito bowl with black beans, veggies, mild and corn salsa, sour cream and cheese, lettuce.  can't get any better than that, ya heard.

A staple restaurant for a Berkeley student. 

First, if you have an iPhone, download the Chipotle app from the App Store. This will save you from lining up at this Chipotle and let you just waltz up to the cashier and ask for your order while everyone else is in line staring at you, wishing they did the exact same. If not, their assembly line production is quick and efficient. Expect about a 15 minute waiting time, 20-30 if the line goes out onto the street during peak hours.

As for the actual food, it's really just a standard burrito. They sometimes skimp on the materials and price is rather steep for what you're getting. It's not bad, but definitely not a place I would want to eat every single day. 

Still, when I'm at school I eat here at least once a week as part of my lunch rotation. It's called a staple for a reason!

Oh Chitpole, I used to be loyal to you during my first and second year at Cal. But then I became promiscuous and decided to cheat on you with other local munchies...

Yes, ladies and gentlemen, they NO LONGER give complimentory free drinks to students. To make it worst, they raise the price from $ 5.85 to $6.10(for the lowest priced burrito). 
Granted that this place belongs to a popular fast food industry in the USA, it's always packed with students during busy hours. So be prepared to live like a sardin to sqeeze in their tiny store. Whenever I go here, I feel tramautized by my clusterphobic nature...very sad indeed :(
The ingredients are usually fresh, yet the portion can be very inconsistent depending on the time you order (shrink in size during rush hours) and who's making it (tip: let out your doe eye, bambi).
Overall, for a burrito and a drink, it's a passable meal for $7-8

Super small location and super long lines if you don't go at the right times. (Saturday lunch is fine; my friends and I even actually got a table)

I usually get the tacos here, but I branched out and tried a burrito bowl for the first time today. I'm a believer now. Their lime-flavored chips and guacamole are also good if you are able to splurge.

Any Chipotle-goer knows the portions are huge. If you're health conscious...I wouldn't recommend eating that burrito in one sitting! ;)

Cal students get a free drink! :)

HAPPY LEAP DAY!! (I only get to say this once every 4 years...)
Now on to the review...

Chipotle....

I love Chipotle! And, moreso, I love this Chipotle, particularly. They rock.

The flavors are delicious. Here's what I always order from here: "Barbacoa bowl to go with tortillas. With 2 scoops of white rice, no wait, please add more rice. Mmkay, that's good. Black beans please, and also those yummy grilled peppers. And barbacoa (the awesomest shredded meat) Thanks."  On to the next server in the line...   "May I please have hot salsa, more please...(Yes, I love things extra SPICY). And the corn and the cheese. Thank you so kindly"   That's exactly how I always order.

Chipotle rocks, they also have good chips and guac, which is really filling, especially on those days when I'm not starving, yet still need a little snack!

Also, I recently had them cater a student event on campus...the manager gave me an awesome deal! But even besides the good discount, I still am very impressed by their professionalism and care.

Rock on Chipotle, rock on! :-)  And thanks for the deal ;))

Considering how much business they get, you'd think they'd be more liberal with their serving portions.  Unfortunately, that's not the case. They're incredibly stingy compared to all the other Chipotle places I've been to and HERE'S HOW TO BEAT THEM.

1. Order a Bowl.
2. Ask for extra rice/beans.
3. Ask for extra meat (if you think you can get away with it).
4. Throw on all the sides.
5. Ask for the tortilla on the side (free).
6. Get the free student drink.
7. Eat at the Burrito Bowl until you get a burrito-sized portion.
8. Dump the rest onto the tortilla and wrap it.
9. WHERE DID THIS NEW BURRITO COME FROM?

4 stars because I can't help liking Chipotle and their (usually) filling/massive portions... just not this location : (

This is my second time visiting this Chipotle. I have limited time for dinner in between classes, so I order online and skip the line. There is a notes section, where I ask for brown rice and extra fajita veggies.  Last week, both were ignored. Upon arrival tonight (I was early) I asked the cashier, Jesus, to ensure there was brown rice.  He told me I'd get what I ordered. Got my food. Brown rice, check. However, few veggies (I don't eat meat) and no black beans as ordered. When I brought this to Jesus's attention he rolled his eyes and asked for my receipt, then looked through the computer... Like I was trying to steal beans that are always included. Then, tok my food, put it aside and went to deal with something else for five minutes. All you have to do is scoop some beans! Finally, he asked someone to add beans. It was quite the ordeal. I love chipotle, hence three stars, but won't be going to this location again. All chipotles have long lines,so the proximity to Cal and resulting lines isn't the issue. I've been to many locations and never seen so many screw ups, or worse, been treated like I was a problem.

Was in and out in probably less than 5 minutes--had to get dinner fast, and needed my regular burrito fix. They have brown rice now, which I actually think tastes less strange than white rice in a burrito. The barbacoa was relatively good, more flavorful than the steak-like beef since it's shredded. Like most chains, you get what you expect. The burritos are more expensive than the regular ones at La Burrito and Gordo's but they are also bigger. Sometimes, I get weird vibes from the servers, which creeps me out. But I'll still go for fast, California-fied Mexican food.

It's chipotle. 'nuff said.

However the burrito is SoCal is much bigger...

I have always been a fan of good Mexican good and if you can make a tasty meal at a quick to go spot, then I am down. I have been to Chipotle's competitor while living in Seattle and loved it there and since they don't have it here, I had to check out Chipotle since I've heard good things! My friends were definitely right in recommending this place to me because I love a good quality burrito on the go!

I was pleased by this location, it was small, but service was friendly, quick, and there were a decent amount of places to sit down and eat inside. Their menu is a bit small compared to other places of this caliber and I was really craving a chicken quesadilla, but they didn't have that here. I tried a burrito bowl instead and it was really tasty and appropriately priced! Their chicken has a sweet flavor that I really enjoyed and I highly recommend putting some of their corn on your food as well, gives it a nice flavor!

I kind of wish they had more options on their menu, but other than that, it's clean, fresh, quick, and tasty. I'll definitely return to try more of their burritos again!

I lived on Southside the last 2 years and ate at Chipotle at least once every week (got Chipotle cravings if I didn't). I don't understand why the ratings on here are so low because almost everyone I know loves this place.

The burritos are huge and you can choose exactly what you want in it, and you get a free drink if you're a student. The location is super convenient and the service is fast. Five stars from me!

3.5 stars

Perhaps the greatest feature of this staple to the Cal student diet is the fast service. No matter how intimidating the line looks, you can generally get your food in less than 10 minutes. They even offer occasional deals like free chips and guac for students who show their Cal IDs! (But you have to be on the lookout for those, and they come once in a blue moon.) What's sad is that Chipotle used to be a better deal because they used to ALWAYS give free drinks with their meals if you were a Cal student, but they took that offer away :( - ironically at a time when more competition entered the market (aka Gordos)

If you are looking for a burrito that gives you tons of meat, you're better off going to Gordos for their steak burritos, because they give a ton and are cheaper. However, if you are like me, sometimes you will just have a craving for Chipotle and Chipotle only. I love their burrito bowls (I get the tortilla on the side) and because I love the corn so much, I always ask for extra. The line moves fast here at Chipotle, but don't be afraid to ask for more things if they don't look like they're giving you enough. I think this Chipotle has definitely gotten skimpier over the years I've been at Cal. 

Overall, the price for the meal (especially because there's no drink anymore and they've gotten skimpier on ingredients) is not really worth it compared to the better deals in the area, but I still come back a few times a semester when I get that craving for some steak burrito bowls.

I am a fan of Chipotle.  I think its the best burrito place near UC Berkeley.  

The seasoning on the meat is quite good.  I like the spices in their Carnitas and herbs in the Barbacoa.  They also have bowls if you don't like burritos.  The chips are lightly limed for a nice taste--very good with guacamole or salsa.  It's a great location, right next to campus.  There is often a line around lunch time, though it moves quite fast.  A drink is also included here.  

The place is usually crowded, but the weather is usually good enough just to find a nice place to sit down around Sproul.  

The meat and vegetables are organic, and they avoid using meat from animals that use antibiotics or hormones.

Ehh. If you're starving and rushing off to class or a meeting Chipotle will do the job. It's pretty average americanized mexican food but I would much rather eat at Gordo's down the street or even La Burrita on Durant. For the price I'm paying for a rice bowl (about $6-7) it's not really worth it to get 70% rice and barely any meat. Service is pretty poor but you get in and out fast. There's usually a long line during the rush hours but if you have access to a smartphone or internet I would highly recommend placing an order online - you can just walk up to the front and tell them you have an order for pick up!

It's always difficult to review one location of a fast food chain as the food, ambience etc is pretty standard across different locations.  The customer service here, however, is better than that at other locations.  The staff is always very friendly to me.

I don't go to a lot of Chipotles but this one is really clean and very quick. The people work really quickly and never seem to lose their cool despite the pressure and a dozen hungry eyes. Also, if you are a Cal student and show your ID, you get a free drink!

I'm not a mexican food snob, so I don't really care that the burritos aren't authentic. The only thing I care about is if the thing I am eating tastes good. The burritos here have been hit or miss. Usually they overload on the guacamole which is delicious in moderate amounts but not when it is nearly half my burrito.

My favorite part though is the chips!! I don't know what they put on but it tastes like they infuse them with lime juice or something. It reminds me of when I use to try the salt from my mom's margaritas. Good times.
they're pretty stingy here on the meat, my only complaint, besides that it's your run of the mill chipotle

Pretty standard Chipotle with good food and great staff, but the space is awful. There is always a long line that are right on top of the very little amount of tables they have. The balcony offers more seating, but there are always tons of flies and there is a 90% chance you'll be accosted by a typical crazy transient of the Berkeley streets at some point in your meal.

Good location to grab lunch in between classes. Food is relatively inexpensive for the large portions they give you. Some of the servers are a bit rude but most are very nice. I would not recommend getting the chicken because whenever I get it it's always pretty chewy (gross). I like the burrito bowls and if you ask for a lot of something they really give you a lot. Chips are lemony and VERY salty so I can't usually have too much of them. Long line during rush hour (noon, etc.) but it moves pretty quickly. Not likely that you will find a table so just get it to go and eat on campus. Overall, good portions for a fair price but if you can try something else more "Berkeley," I'd say do it.

My service with them today wasn't too great. And thus I lowered a couple of stars to this delicious place. I placed my order on my iphone like I normally do. When I arrived at the appropriate time, the cashier had no clue about my order. He then asked his coworkers and they hadn't even began to make it yet. They then realized that they hadn't made 3 other people's orders. I waited for at least 7-8min for my order. I might have as well waiting in line like a normal person. I also noticed that they got new staff?? I miss the old staff! They hardly messed up. At least never this bad. Oh and by the way, they only gave me a cup of water to compensate for my wait time. Lame....
Carnitas... :O I like that they give you a free drink here. Yummy burritos.
The food here tastes like what you expect from a Chipotle, and tastes great.  It's a convenient distance from CAL and clean.

No, it's not authentic Mexican. But no, it's not freeze-dried cheddar-laden, grade D-beefed-out Taco Bell, either.
Chipotle makes their burritos fresh on an an assembly line - they ask you at each step what you'd like to add and how much of each item. For a control freak like myself I do love that idea. I tend to be reminded of this style of Mexican as "Californian"/grill as they use little cheese and your traditional refried beans, and instead opt for more "fresh" additions like cilantro rice, fajita vegetables, corn salsa, and the like. 
Guacamole is unfortunately an extra $1.30 or so but SO worth it; it's made fresh "up to three times a day," according to Chipotle. Chips you'll have to pay extra for as well, but honestly, the burritos are big enough you may not even want them.
Meat here is organic and/or antibiotic-free (and grass-fed), I believe, but don't quote me.
Oh yes, and free fountain drinks (real unsweetened iced tea as well) with your order!
The best part, though, is the constantly smiling, friendly staff - in an urban place like Berkeley, I've had more run-ins with bored or downright rude salespeople than I can count, and these guys are quick, attentive, and all have infectious smiles.
Don't be fooled by any long lines - the guys and girls working are very fast, and it's worth the wait.

OH EM GEE! Chipotle how i love thee !

Ok, So I love Chipotle! But believe it or not there's a big difference among different Chipotle locations. I have to say I love Berkeley's. They give you great portions, their chicken is cooked (well done, not squishy and half raw like other places), and theyre fast and efficient in getting through their line.  Also, for a $6 dollar burrito, you get so many fixins and a free regular size drink.. cant be beat.. especially with so many other places stretching and crawling their way to $10 for student meals bleh.

And for those of you complaining about service. Seriously? Me being the self proclaimed princess of demaning decent customer service,  actually like them. THEY ARE considered pseudo fast food, so kep that in mind. They have a line out the door, they cater to your needs with all your little "double wrap burritos, melt my cheese, extra this and extra that..". Show a little love, they're awesome!! :)

This happens to be one of the few chain restaurants around the campus. It provides fast , relatively cheap and decently healthy food.
Their burrito bowls would be the item I would recommend here along with their selection of tacos , both crispy and soft. 
Go here if you are on sproul and want a quick Mexican bite but don't want to walk further away.

I'm not exactly an expert on Mexican food (unlike my many Southern California friends, who tend to complain about the Mexican food in Berkeley only slightly less than they do about the weather and women), but even I can tell that Chipotle's offerings leave much to be desired.

To begin with...they put way too much rice in the burritos. The first time I came here I left with a burrito that was close to 60% rice. The salsa is distinctly lacking in taste, as are the beans. And unlike all the other Mexican places I've been to, they don't give you chips when you order a burrito (nor do they let you take your own salsa). However, I do like the fact that they offer fajita burritos, and the barbacoa (spicy shredded beef) is pretty good. Also, students can get a free drink with their student IDs.

For the prices they charge, the burritos just aren't worth it. The tacos aren't anything to write home about either. And who goes to a Mexican place to get a salad?

To me, Chipotle's burritos are top 3 in Berkeley...maybe it is because I like the taste of their steak, or maybe it is because I ALWAYS use up so much of their Chipotle smoked tabasco...whatever it is, I know that I would have been a regular here if I used yelp at Cal :P

The burrito sizes are decent, not the biggest...and you don't get free chips like La Bur, but at a pretty good price and a free drink for students, Chipotle is a good meal for the typical college student.

During lunch hours, it is ridiculously crowded, so beware of that, but you can also politely ask for extra rice and beans most times and even double wrap the burrito if you are planning on stuffing yourself :P
pretty standard and reliable.

It's chipotle. I mean, it's guaranteed to have good food.

The reason that it gets 4 instead of 5 stars is because

1) almost impossible to find seats to during meal time
2) the staff really do skimp on the food - especially the meat and the salsa. How do I know ? because I've been regulars at other chipotles.
3) They do creep the prices up periodically

Not bad for a chain restaurant. It's assembly line production is quick and gets the long line moving very quickly. It may seem a bit overwhelming to see the line down the street during lunch, but it dissipates within 15 minutes. You'll get your order quickly if everyone else knows how to order, and changes are they are college students that have been there many times before.

The burritos are fresh and light, compared to the traditional taquerias like La Burrita up the street. I always ask them to pack in extras for me - meat, lettuce, salsa, cheese, etc. and they do this for no extra cost. I also think its pretty cool that you can order via your iPhone because Chipotle has an app made specifically for those kinds of orders.

Grab a burrito, sit in their small patio, and enjoy a nice meal as you people watch.

Compared to other Chipotles establishments (ie the one in Alameda's South Shore), this place is awful.

Cons:
-the staff who serve meager amounts of food almost every single time I come here. If I'm paying $2 for guac, I'm expecting more than a teaspoon. If I ask for extra rice and corn (because I'm not getting beans or cheese), it really wouldn't kill you to give me extra. I swear they must tell their servers not to give out very much of anything. 
(Note: Every other Chipotle establishment fills your burrito bowl up to the max, and the servers at least try to sound happy to give you your food. Not the case here). 

Pros:
-Super filling. Can easily be food enough for both lunch and dinner.
-The food in general is amazingly delicious, per the usual of chipotle.

This place would have warranted a 4 or 5 if I didn't have to leave semi-pissed every time. Gah. I seriously have a love-hate relationship with this place.

I eat here as often as I can afford to!
Great food, Great service, Great price!

I like how they have lettuce and cilantro.  I like how you can be reasonably sure of their meats' sources.  I like how there are calorie counters online and how you can pretend that your burrito is only 900 calories.  I like their free-for-students drinks and how you can squeeze free lemons into it.

I do not like how it is temptingly between my residence and school, no matter which route I take.

The line is always ridiculous.

Okay, so here's the thing: I love Chipotle. I've come to terms with that. I used to make all these excuses for going there, "Oh, it's quick and cheap and blah blah." Fuck that. I can no longer disguise my love. Also, I don't really even think of Chipotle as Mexican food, so I go in not expecting authenticity. 

Anyways, on to this location. If it wasn't so close to campus and all that, I would drive over to Gilman every time I decided to have Chipotle. Last time I ate at this location I was still hungry afterward. Fucking blaspheme. It was the tiniest Chipotle burrito I've ever seen. I watched the girl doll out these little portions of rice, beans, and carnitas. It was depressing. One of the main reasons Chipotle is so good is the fact that it is a good deal for a decent price, but when you are stingy with the ingredients it defeats the purpose. I usually plan on just eating Chipotle the days that I do eat it, so it sucks when it's not enough to hold me over for the rest of the day. The guy who did my salsa and what not was pretty much eye fucking me the entire time, which made me feel reallllly awkward. I suppose the extra guac he gave me is suppose to compensate for that? 

Post-Berkeley, I don't plan on ever going to this Chipotle again.

There's not many Chipotle places in the east bay as in San Francisco. 
I was craving a burrito bowl since my last time was when I went to my NYC trip(about a month ago). 
First, the place is too small and barely has seating for a group of people and especially for one person you've got to struggle a bit. 
When I first got in line the person serving the rice, beans and meat really DID good service and with great enthusiasm so I was happy to get that. 
When the next person serving the sour cream, cheese, salsas, guac, corn, and lettuce he barely knew what to do; but I at least got what I wanted. 
Lastly when I went to pay my food the women was almost like yelling at me if that was all or acted as if i did not listen well to her.

The food was good but when i opened my bowl everything was on one side. Kinda bizarre but okay. I really did not know where to sit since the place is too small. I was thinking of going to the campus to eat under a tree or on some steps.
Will i come back yes, since It's one of the few in the east bay. Pretty much Berkeley and Alameda are the only places I know.

It's hard to go wrong with Chipotle. It's dependable food, the way McDonald's is dependable; the way In-N-Out delivers on expectations every time I go. That said, the flip side is that Chipotle isn't going to delight nor stun the palate.

Going to Chipotle with my friends on numerous occasions taught me how to be immigrant-style and get more bang for my buck:

1. Ask for a second tortilla if you want more carbs and want a more filling burrito.
2. It's perfectly legitimate to ask for extra scoops of stuff. I frequently ask for extra fajita stuffs (like bell peppers and grilled onions). Sometimes they'll even give an extra scoop of meat if you ask nicely.
3. Personally, I get the fajita bowl. And I can always ask for the tortilla on the side. It costs the same.

Yes, the Asian in me is proud. The college-degree genteel urbanite that I am today, however, is rather sheepish about this post.
Looking back at this review totally cracks me up--to think that there was a time Chipotle was new to me :)

Just because I know I can get my steak burrito bowl here, just the way I like it, it wins. 

Smaller than other locations. 

But with the little patio in front you can people watch in the heart of Berkley by the UC Campus.

Regardless of whether this is authentic Mexican food, it is still really really really addictingly good.

Now, normally I don't eat food that falls apart - it just gets on my nerves. So I've gotten many quesadillas here. I thought it was really nice how they never hesitated after hearing my order to make my quesadilla or argued about how it wasn't on the menu. Soon though, I got hooked on the BURRITO BOWL. Best of both worlds, because now I don't have to worry about my food being messy. I love the chicken burrito bowl; for a while I had it up to twice a week. Chicken, black beans, rice, pico de gallo, corn, cheese, lettuce. Who knew this combo could taste so delicious?

In terms of service, I mean, they make the food as quickly as they can. This restaurant is across the street from the school, so it's always crowded and full. The wait time isn't too bad, though it is nearly impossible to eat in (extremely limited seating). The Chipotle workers are always polite and nice, so plus points for them!

AND, if you are a Berkeley student, you get a free soda. You really can't beat this.

Love this place. My room mate and I should legitimately be sponsored by them since we ate it at least three times a week. Conveniently located in the heart of the UC campus area, it serves the primary lunch spot for Cal students, nearby store employees and the occasional out of towner. 

Anyways, long story short: delicious food, normally fast service and a free drink for Cal Students! The workers are a bit stingy in terms of the ingredients but you can always ask for more. If you're loving for a good, and filling meal, come here an indulge in deliciousness.

this place is ok
I always get the same burrito when I go to this place, and I've never been able to eat there because it's always packed (not because of the customers, but the place is small)
line is usually long, and they usually are out of hot sauce
Delicious and fresh ingredients, relatively inexpensive and always reliable.  However, some of the staff at this Chipotle can be rude and disorganised!

Standard Americanized Mexican cuisine.  Comparatively, I would say this location skimps a bit on meat portions.  Regardless, it is staple to any college kid's diet.  Its cheap, easy to eat and transport, and filing.  The line is usually almost always out the door during busy hours.  If you feel like you need a change up in taste, try Gordo's down the block.

Why so many haters?? Sure, it's always packed up the heezy, but it's such an affordable staple to all of our college lives that I'm surprised it only has 3 stars.

Service: 3
Taste: 4
Quality: 4
Variety: 3
Price: $6-9
Recommend to a friend: Yes

I almost always get the chicken bowl with a tortilla on the side -- the tortilla on the side is free. I like the bowl option because the burritos are messy and fall apart too easily (the tortillas rip because they're really soft). The chicken is pretty flavorful, and you get your choice of beans and other things to put inside your bowl/burrito/taco/salad.

I will agree with other Yelpers, though, about how it's not as great as it has been in the past. They gimp out on the amount of meat they give you, and the price has gone up. The increase in price is probably just due to the increase in input costs for the company, so I'm not that concerned about that part. I think they could give you a bit more meat, though. And the price of extras like guacamole is pretty ridiculous. You don't even get that much guac for the extra dollar or two, so unless you NEED it, I would suggest not to get it.

Also, the wait can get pretty long, especially during lunch and dinner, but even on off-hours, there will likely be some sort of wait time. Keeping that in mind, there isn't much seating -- 3 tables inside and 5 or so outside. It's probably best to get it to-go and sit on the Sproul steps while people-watching. That's what my friends and I always do.

I just don't get it!  I mean, WHY would you put lettuce in a burrito?  And then put it all into a bowl instead of a tortilla?  Me thinks not!  I know we're in California but that's not an excuse for turning something like a burrito into a salad!  Okay, okay, not everyone puts lettuce into their burrito, but I have other issues about their burrito.  It's too dry.  The rice is flavorless and there's too much of it.  Oh and I think it's a rip-off compared to La Burrita (a dollar more and you still get less!)  Oh, and La Burrita gives free chips and a drink!   Unless something radical changes at Chipotle, you can count me out!
For what it is chipotle is good cheap affordable and healthy mexican fast food. I can get a bowl for 460 calories and get completely satisfied. Don't expect authentic expect good fast food.

ok so i love chipotle.  if i'm ever hungry, and i see one, it's high on my consideration list.  it's a great value, the ingredients are good, for the most part they're all pretty consistent, and the decorum always feels familiar.  i just like it.  and you know what, up to this point, i haven't really written any reviews for chipotle at all, so it's kind of sad for me to be writing my first one with such a negative review.

i feel that the staff does not do a very good job building burritos.  they are often in a rush (or so they seem) and don't seem interested in building a good burrito at all.  only once did i feel like they adequately filled my burrito to what i have come to expect as standard.  usually they skim on the ingredients and one can only remind them to fill it so many times.  call me a snob, i don't care, but i have contributed so much $$$ to the chipotle franchise that i feel like i have the right to bitch about this one.  =)

Chipotle is pretty mediocre when it comes to burritos. The ingredients aren't the freshest, the burritos aren't wrapped the best, the price isn't that great, but overall, it's not bad.

I went yesterday with a buy-one-get-one-free coupon and they honored it so my meal was a really good deal. If you're a Cal student, they also give you a free drink so that's another plus in my opinion (with refills!). Guac extra is $1.65 but they give you a pretty generous portion of it which is nice. The burritos used to be a lot larger; they used to put a ton of rice and other ingredients into their burritos but they've made the quantity smaller to keep with the times. The workers are quick behind the counter so the line (which always is pretty long) isn't that bad to get through.

Wouldn't come here for a place to study. Just grab your meal and go. It's much too loud and crowded here.  Pretty good, but not excellent experience.

Great location for students, since it's just right across campus. The staff are usually very friendly, though recently there have been a couple that are in a big hurry. Fast service, varying portions -sometimes my burrito is kind of small, but other times it's so big it rips through the tortilla and they have to double wrap it! Very tasty and filling.

Eat Here! You really can't go wrong... it's clean, organized, friendly, well-lit, and you get a ton of food for your money.

Oh yea, Cal students who show their ID get a free drink!

The people are super nice and friendly, even though they're being over-worked. It's hard for me to imagine working as hard as they do... I mean there is usually a pretty constant stream of people coming through the door and these guys / gals just keep on slinging burritos. They really take the time to make sure that whatever you order is the way that you want it. I also often see them cleaning up the tables / floor / drink area / bathrooms to make what little space they have as friendly and hospitable as possible.

This place really gives you the option of making your food as healthy as you want it to be. I've ordered burritos, soft tacos (off menu), quesadillas (off menu), salads, and burrito bowls. All of the ingredients are fresh and freshly made!!! I usually get a Chicken burrito with black beans, grilled veggies / fajitas, corn, mild / tomato salsa, guac, and lettuce. The burrito does wind up being huge... probably 3-5 pounds. 

If you're really trying to get the most bang for your buck, this is the place to go. A burrito can easily last you 2-3 meals and, at $6-$7, is cheaper then most of the other places in the area.

Chipotle is Mexican fast food, so don't come here expecting legit Mexican cuisine. The burritos are amazing and HUGE. My husband and I always get the veggie burritos, and because we're piggys, we ask for everything when we get to the salad/salsa/sour cream/guac station. Most of the time, the foil wrappers for burritos just aren't big enough to contain all that yummy goodness. :D

The service is usually pretty efficient. Usually the reason things are slow is because someone at the front of the line is trying to decide between a burrito and a burrito bowl. Seriously?! Be warned: when Chipotle has some kind of coupon, the entire student population of UC Berkeley will be there.

I still remember the day this Chipotle restaurant opened during my freshman year at Cal.  Little did I know that it would become the standard by which all my other meals were judged by for the rest of my college career.

If you're coming to Chipotle seeking Mexican food, you're doing it wrong.  

I don't come to Chipotle to satisfy my Mexican food cravings.  Hell, I don't think I really even get Mexican food cravings.  What I do get from Chipotle is a large, filling, tasty meal made with a mixture of foods that I enjoy (meat, cilantro lime rice, tomatoes, corn, guacamole, lettuce, sour cream, cheese, etc).  All their ingredients are always fresh and of high quality.  Although the workers seem rushed at times (gotta keep the line moving), they are always willing to add more scoops of non-meat ingredients if you ask for them.  It all comes at around 7 dollars, and they give you a free drink if you look like a student.  No other place in Berkeley can match the quantity and quality of food that Chipotle can offer.

Kudos for the whole grass fed free range thing, but if  that grass fed beef has no flavor or even a hint of salt then what's the freakin' point? I don't know if it's this particular Chipotle, but I tried the barbacoa and the steak burrito and it seriously lacked flavor. Just weak. And it's ridiculous to pay $10 for a burrito with guac, chips and salsa (guess they threw in the drink, but still) when the hole in the wall across the street or the burrito truck five minutes away will give me all that for like $6 or $7 (with a drink) and it's FULL of flavor. They need to get it together. Blah.

Favorite Chipotle #4 (Part 4 of 4)

As an avid Chipotle fan who has tried Chipotle just about everywhere (and believe me, ingredients and quality vary greatly), I've picked four of my favorite ones. This is number 4.


Chipotle - South of UC Berkeley campus on Bancroft/Telegraph

I went to school in this area. Needless to say, this Chipotle accounts for more than 50% of my lifetime Chipotle visits. It's a very crowded one given the limited seating areas, but I can say that this location has definitely tailored itself toward the college campus crowd.

The ingredients are on par with what you can expect from eating in the bay area, and the occasional student with a burrito buried behind an O-Chem book is always an entertaining image.

The only thing I'd say is that at times their portion may be smaller than the average Chipotle primarily due to the great traffic that frequents this location. During off-peak hours, however, you can expect your portions to fully satisfy or exceed your expectations.

Free drinks for people with student ID's!

Thanks for always stuffing my burrito with plenty of corn and meat.  I wish I was heftier so I could actually finish one of the burritos by myself.  

I also think it's amazing how well the employees work under pressure.  The lines are just insane during the lunch and dinner waves, but they seem to have no trouble making our orders.  And they aren't all grumpy like the folks working at La Burrita, so I really appreciate it.  Though, I feel like a sell-out for liking a chain burrito place.  Oh well I love their rice!

What can I say? It is what it is. It's fast, it's food, it's fast food.

Comes with all the implications of fast food: high calories, general unhealthiness, and regret.

With that said, I love Chipotle; their burritos just taste fresher than La Burrita's, due to something.. probably the lettuce. For less than $7 you can get a thousand calorie burrito stuffed to near bursting, and a free drink if you're a student or can pass for one.

Maybe you'd want to forgo the tortilla and get a bowl if you were watching calories.

The chips are absolutely delicious when eaten with the corn salsa, but again, that's like 570 calories right there, 240 from fat, not even counting the salsa's contribution...

My advice is to eat here sparingly..
I like the crispy tacos and fresh and yummy guac and the people are very nice. I'm not a fan of their rice though and that's a deal breaker for me.

Whee. This is the go to place for a quick lunch in between classes. My friends and I always go here whenever we can't decide on where to eat.

I always get the steak burrito bowl (with a tortilla on the side!), and the portions always vary from barely filling half the bowl to overflowing. I feel like this Chipotle tends to gip you on what they give you in comparison to other locations. However, all you have to do is ask for extra anything and they'll give it to you (they only charge for extra meat).

The line can get pretty long, but don't fret! You'll be ordering your food before you know it. If you're impatient, order your food beforehand online or on your phone. That way, you can skip the lines and pick up your food at the front. I've noticed that you tend to get more bang for your buck if you order beforehand, too!

The Berkeley Chipotle gives students a free drink with their purchase, but I've found that if you look of age, they give it to you anyways since they don't check IDs.

Lots of people seem to hate this place, but I actually like it. I usually get a chicken fajita burrito (or bol). I also happen to like the rice so I don't mind that the majority of the burrito is rice. In fact, I usually ask for extra rice! In yo face you chipotle-rice-haters! So yea...I also add the corn salsa. Lots of it. And that's it. Simple and tasty.

Ingredients taste fresh and delicious, and it's probably one of the better deals around Berkeley for the price. I like the chicken burrito because the red meats offered are a bit tough or gummy. They work quickly during meal hours. It's not authentic Mexican food however; I like to call the burritos "fresh ingredient barrels."

This is the place with which I compare every other lunch/dinner spot within walking distance of Cal. The price:satisfaction ratio is just that good. Free drink for anybody who looks like a student +  bowl of meat and salsa and beans and meat and rice and meat for ~$7. It tastes fan-fucking-tastic -- just don't come looking for an authentic experience (and seriously, you're a chump if you're looking for authentic Mexican food here WHILE YOU'RE IN CALIFORNIA). I'll admit that the portion sizes can vary, but you can always ask for more, so no excuses.

try one:
got a veggie burrito, next day i was sick with the flu. coincidence? i think not, two other people who I know (a coworker and a friend) who went at a different time then me both came down with a flu...

try two:
free coupon for faculty, would not let me use mine since I am a staff, but yet students use it? FAIL

chipotle you suck, fake ass mexican food.
did i mention they are OWNed by mcdonalds?
EPIC FAIL!

Throw a bunch of beans, rice, sauce, corn, carrots, and other random vegetables into a wrap and you have Chipotle. Awful Mexican food that should be fed as animal feed to farm animals.

FOOD IS AWFUL and TASTELESS. So it's cheap and the burritos are big, people who think this place is actually good have no taste at all.

Price? Under 10 bucks, but who cares?! Food is awful. I can't say it enough because I see people stuffing their faces with this hobo vomit all the time and wonder why they are doing so.

This is the first Chipotle I've ever been to and I hate it. No DETEST it.

1. Hardly any seats
2. The saltiest chips I've ever had.
3. Dumbed down, Americanized food.
4. No horchata

I'd skip Chipotle and head to Mario's La Fiesta or La Burrita and get authentic Mexican for a cheaper price.
Never coming back here again. Stupid server gave me super small portions. I've never had a Chipotle burrito before that was this emaciated.
ehh its ok

If I could give this negative stars, I would. I am admittedly a Mexican food snob, but even evaluated on its own merit, this place is an abomination. The burritos are large enough to feed a small African family, so you will have plenty to contemplate about as you try to devour your bland and tasteless brick of processed ingredients. Having trouble choosing which filling to get? IT DOESN'T MATTER, BECAUSE IT ALL TASTES THE SAME. You can't tell the difference between the meats because they've all been stewing in steam tubs since the dawn of time. I can't even begin to describe the sensations that follow devouring one of their monstrosities that they call a burrito. In short, it feels like Bruce Lee has put his foot through your lower abdomen and out your spine. This doesn't even cover the struggle to digest your 290321838 calorie meal, but I'm trying to keep this a G-rated review.

Avoid. Your rectum will thank you.

It sort of looks like a burrito, except for the fact that they roll them by essentially mashing it into a ball.  It smells kinda like a burrito, except that instead of big flavors you just smell unseasoned meat.  

Seriously, if you want a flavorless, expensive, Americanized, chain "Mexicanish" burrito, go to Chipotle. All others should go to La Burrita just one block away and get an actual real burrito.
two words- raw meat

What is the most over-ratedest thing in Berkeley besides football? CHIPOTLE. 

This restaurant should be required to put parenthesis around the "Mexican" in  Chipotle Mexican Grill. 

The food is bland, the atmosphere dominated by students looking for sustenance between classes, and the rice tasteless and dry. I hope this place goes out of business and leaves the better mom and pop burrito joints on Telegraph and Durant to do what they can do better: serve decent Mexican food.

Where do we begin?

1) the rice is wrong. It's not Mexican rice. It's some sort of cheap knock off of Uncle Ben's 5-minute rice. Perhaps it's Uncle Ben's long lost cousin Jed's 3 minute rice. Anyway, it's not the right rice for a taco or burrito.

2) the beans are wrong. They're not Mexican beans, but some sort of newly concocted GMO-laden soft pebble which might fit in the physical space typically occupied by pinto or black beans, but nonetheless, inadequately fill that culinary gap.

3) The salsa is wrong. Wrong chiles (I really don't know how they could have gotten this wrong--?), wrong flavor, it's not Mexican salsa. Nor tex-mex. Even less relation to Mexican cuisine than Taco Hell.

4) Produce. Fans of tired lettuce and soggy onions rejoice, you have found nirvana. For the rest of us, who perhaps expect a bit of crispness in the lettuce and onions, go elsewhere.

Now, some of you might be thinking: "Mexican food purist!" Perhaps you're right. My philosophy is this: if you want to do creative fusions with food, fine, but they need to be at least as good as the original foods you're fusing, otherwise, what's the point? This is substantially worse than any food I've ever had in my many trips to Mexico. It's flavorless (I guess if you hate Mexican flavors this food might appeal to you). Guys, it's not all that hard to make a taco or a burrito with flavor. Ingredients are tantamount. Chipotle doesn't seem to care.

To be fair (look on the bright side), the service was not as bad as it typically is at fast food joints. And the ice dispensed from the soft machine dispenser was correctly sized and flavored (it tasted like water). There was available seating with no wait.

Oh how I wish there was good Mexican food near to campus... perhaps one day...

The service at this location is amazing. The staff are wonderful :) 
Ordering online is really simple & your order is always ready for pickup at the time specified. 

This is a standard Chipotle meal. You should not dine here expecting authentic Mexican cuisine. This is just a reliable meal, made from good, fresh ingredients. 

I frequent Chipotle quite often. I like to split my burritos up into two smaller meals (I'm a poor college student). It works out great because there are 1000+ calories in one chicken burrito. Great place for Cal students!
Place to go when you're in a hurry and want to get some food fast + free drink. I only get their chicken burrito bol because I like their rice and can split it into two meals (I'm a petite eater)

Who wants to go to Chipotle for an authenticate spicy mexican burrito. This place isn't meant for that. If you want a large amount of food on the cheap with decent quality meat, this is the place. 

The thing that Chipotle really really fails at is flavor, there's just no flavor in most of the salsa they have, at least not a proper flavor. The tomato and corn salsa don't really do anything to the taste, the rice is bland. But the fact of the matter is you can spice it up and add a little bit of flavor with the extra sauces they provide in bottles and you got a decent meal. 

Oh, and free drinks for students is nice.

It's a Mexican chain food restaurant... So you get that quality out of all of the stores. 

Mediocre. 

The rice is yummy but the meats are always on the dry side. You have to make sure you order salsa, guacamole or pico de gallo with it to moisten it up. The burritos are tasty but tiny. 

I like that you can watch what they put into your dish and you can tell them to put more without an extra charge because they can't argue with you. :P

Not the best Chipotle, actually probably the worse I've been, the service is minimal, but most importantly the portions are small, wayyyy too male centric, where are the girls????  Also just go to La Burrita is you want to go to Mexican.  Two stars because I do still go there, but probably less than once every 6 months.

I LOVE CHIPOTLE! During lunch rush, they're awesomely fast and won't really have to wait THAT long... usually depends on the number of workers. What I don't really like is the small amount of tables. But it is located smack dab in the middle of college town so it's what we can get. If you show your Cal ID, you can get a free drink! This is pretty cool because the drinks cost like almost $2 for regular folks.. yay for being students! Anyway, this is my default place to go to whenever I'm in the mood for fast black bean burritos. There are other more authentic burrito places in Berkeley, but this hits the spot whenever I'm craving black beans!

I am a huge fan of Chipotle, and I think they make some great quick burritos. However, this Chipotle location is phenomenally awful - I have gone here about a dozen times and it seems to have gotten worse every time. Though I still occasionally go here if I've had Gordo Taqueria too often, I would highly recommend against going to this location.

First off, the line at this Chipotle is outrageous, even for a Chipotle. I have seen the line stretch outside of the place and about a hundred feet along Telegraph. I have never waited less then ten minutes here (the one time that there was no line, the server was busy making an order for pick-up, and didn't bother noticing me for about 10 minutes), and average wait time is about twenty minutes. Now, for something absolutely amazing, a long wait can be worth it, but it shouldn't be for this place, considering Gordo's burritos are far better.

Secondly, the service here is downright abysmal, and it is consistently like that. The servers rarely address you at all, and because of their ignorance, often mess up your order. I will describe several experiences here:
1) My burrito was passed on to a second server who takes care of toppings (salsa, sour cream, guacamole, etc), and when she asked me if I wanted hot salsa, I told her to NOT put any spicy salsa. She takes a huge glob of it and puts it on the burrito. She did not seem the slightest bit remorseful, and didn't even offer to make me a new burrito...
2)I ordered a carnitas burrito, and the server proceeded to put one scoop of carnitas on. He then realized he may have put SLIGHTLY too much, and just took half of it off and tossed it back in the bowl. That has to be a joke, right?!
3) The incident I mentioned earlier, where a server didn't notice my presence for ten minutes because he was too busy making an order for somebody who had not even yet arrived.

Honestly, the service here is so pathetic that it ruins the eating experience, something that I can rarely say about food places. They CONSTANTLY skimp on the food, including the 1.90 guacamole (good luck if you get half a scoop), cheese (when I ask for lots of cheese, I often get an angry scowl), and the meat (usually less then a scoop). They are never polite, and are often downright rude. 

I would highly recommend against going here. Chipotle is a great food establishment in general, and I really enjoy going to them, but this one is the absolute worst one I've ever been to. Walk two blocks south along Telegraph and try Gordo Taqueria instead.

I'd like to clarify, this review is not for me, but for my fiance. 

All he can say was not worth on penny. the burrito was tiny, and i mean tiny, compared to ones they make in castro valley. he said when he asked for extra rice and beans, they literally put a pinch extra. He said the chicken was burnt, and there was no flavor what so ever. 
The burrito could fit in my 2 hands and they're tiny hands. As to other burritos he's received from chipotle they're twice as big as this one was. 
I recommend trying somewhere else, because your not going to get much out of here.

Good ingredients wasted in poorly assembled burritos. 

The problem with Chipotle is consistency and quality control. They could be much better if they simply cared more about how they assemble their burritos. They use good, organic ingredients. Their corn salsa, for example, is quite tasty. The ingredients are unfortunately just randomly thrown into the burrito without any regard for quantity or placement. There have been countless times when I have taken a few bites containing nothing but guacamole and sour cream. I once ordered a barbacoa+carnitas burrito that ended up being 90% rice. The net result is mediocre burritos. I have simply had much better ones. 

I have eaten over 10 burritos at Chipotle, and will probably eat a lot more during my time in Berkeley. Their awesome online ordering system is simply too convenient to pass. It is great for group orders because it sends an email to everyone in the group to notify them of the group order. Individuals can then choose what they want to add to the order.

If you can't resist the convenience of their online ordering system, you might have to give Chipotle a try. Just be warned that you might end up with disappointing burrito.

I really like chipotle, but I hate this one! The staff is hardly ever friendly and they barely give you anything on your burritto. Other chipotles happily give you more if you ask, but the staff here must be trained to be super frugal! Plus its always so crowded and I'd rather just grab food at another place. I love the chips tho. so addicting.

The newest branch of this chain opened to the public today. To kick off its grand opening, they offered free burritos & taco to all Cal student. Well, when items are offered free... everyone and their mothers were there. The feast started at 12pm and lasted until 7pm. The line was consistently long throughout the day and it extended around the block!

After waiting in-line for 45mins in the cold frosty weather, I finally got my foot inside the door. Another 10 min passed until I reached the counter...to my surprise, they ran out of beef. The guy in front of me order the last helping of carne asada...(I wanted to run him down) GRRR!!  Thus I was left with chicken or pork as the only option; well a salad was available too, but there was no way in heck was I going to get grass after freezing my arse!

The pork fajita burrito was not bad; I would have prefer a carne asada.  The ingredients was freshly made and season well. If given a choice between a burrito at Chipotle or Cancun, hands down I would pick Cancun. Cancun's 20+ salsa bar option is unequivocally the best in the Bay Area! But for a ~$6 burrito and proximity to my apt, I'll probably dine at Chipotle again.

Update: I forgot to mention that Chipotle started this new online ordering system called D.S.L -- Don't Stand in-Line (www.chipotle.com/dsl). Simply put in an order online, go straight to the register and pick it up.

Chipotle isn't bad. As with most chains, you get a pretty consistent meal.  If you're looking for good mexican food, don't come here.  If you're looking for a filling meal, come here.  While it tries to be a mexican style fast-food joint, it really deserves its own category.  The food isn't bad, and I definitely come here often being a starving college student.  Since it is called a "mexican grill" I have to give it less stars for trying to be mexican food.  Being from San Diego, it's definitely not mexican food.  But I would give it five stars on a fast-food scale.  3 stars also because guacamole is so freakin expensive!

Here are some tips:

-Feel free to ask them for more! Usually they're kind enough to give you more.  And even if they aren't kind, they'll still give you a little more.

-Cal students don't get free drinks anymore so don't ask them for it.

-if you have an iphone, order it through that and go pick it up! You can bypass the line especially during peak hours.

- get a burrito bowl and ask for a tortilla on the side.  I think you get more food that way.  Also, I like to shake up the bowl to mix everything together :)

What is up with all the hate, Yelpers? This is Chipotle, and Chipotle is awesome. Food tastes great, prices are low, portions are large, service is fast, seating is plentiful, and restrooms are decent. I guess these traits are generally expected from Chipotle as a chain, but they're reasons I go there more than other places with higher ratings.

I read this article about how their barbacoa and carnitas are cooked "sous-vide" (http://www.slate.com/articles/business/moneybox/2012/02/chipotle_is_apple_how_the_burrito_chain_is_revolutionizing_fast_food_.html) and now I'm a barbacoa devotee. Good stuff, friends. I also like how they ask which salsa I want and I can have them pile on three different kinds.

That they try to use a lot of local/organic/sustainable ingredients is just another bonus at this point.

2 stars because it's Chipotle.

Having said that, this Chipotle is the worst one I've been to. The servers are very unfriendly, and they have the stingiest servings I have ever seen. I usually get a burrito bowl, and when I order it from the Chipotle in San Rafael or Pinole, they just HEAP the portions on. Here? Sometimes they even take portions back if they feel they've given you too much. The bowls are significantly smaller, probably 2/3 the weight (on a good day) you get at other Chipotle's. Calorie-wise you can't complain, but you can't help feeling you get somewhat jipped every time you go to this Chipotle.

Even though I am a fan of the Chipotle franchise, compared to the handful of Mexican restaurants in the Berkeley and the other Chipotle restaurants I've been to, this one is definitely sub-par.

The burritos always vary in size and the servers were never consistent. The meat for the burrito is only lukewarm. They have raised their prices (A vegetarian burrito costs the same as a chicken burrito?) and ended the free drink deal.
NOTE: You will NOT get a free drink here, even if you are a student!

If you are not that hungry I suggest getting a single soft taco instead of a burrito. The only difference is the taco has no rice and a smaller tortilla roll with about 2/3 the amount of food, but the taco is about 1/3 the price of a full burrito. NOTE: don't get 3 tacos; get 1

The service at this Chipotle varies as much as the burritos do. The servers are happy sometimes but grumpy at other times. The restaurant has the iconic Chipotle look with the steel furniture and Aztec, Mayan-looking wall decor. It is pretty clean and well kept.

WILL I come back: Yes
WHEN will I come back: When run out of plastic forks and napkins at home
WHAT will I do differently: nothing

I love... L-O-V-E... love Chipotle's everywhere even though they are owned by McDonalds.  I mean if the food's quality, then screw everything else.  The point is that the food is good for a starving college student such as myself.  The line was out the door but is aided by an online ordering system so you don't have to wait at all.  It makes the experience much easier, quicker and just as delicious.  The chips were a too lime induced to a point of almost sickness after just three but the burritos and tacos were top-notch.

brown rice, grilled bell peppers, tender carne asada steak, and fresh guacamole and salsa. sooo goood, and the burritos are huuuge and worth the $5-10 that you pay depending on if you ask for extra meat or guacamole. an absolute must!!

The Telegraph Chipotle disappoints me every time.  Fine by me that they don't have enough space to accommodate the students or lines.  Fine by me that the people serving us are rude.  I'm fine with all of that, because I like Chipotle, I'm hungry, and I got to get back on campus quick-fast.

HOWEVER, it is not fine by me that they are stingy beyond comprehension with their vegetables!  I get vegetarian tacos or burritos and all they want to give me is rice & beans with a garnish of salsa.  I finally started telling them no rice (because when you say "only a little" they STILL put too much).  Black beans are healthier and easier to take off, so I let them put those in my meal, but when it comes to the salsas, they will literally put a little salsa on the TIP of the spoon for your entire burrito (which means you're eating mouthfuls of just beans and rice)  HOW does that make sense???  That's NOT healthy.  Not to mention I'm paying $6 for essentially tortilla with beans (cheapest items in the entire world, which explains why that's all they want to give us)  NOT OK.  

I'm not going here anymore.  I'll spend $7 at San Francisco Soup and get a 12 oz soup, wheat roll, and half a tuna sandwich which ends up being two meals instead of one, for me =D  and SF Soup is amazingly delicious and closer to campus.

2 stars go for their cleanliness & efficiency (they will get you in and out quick, but remember, they can be rude and they go so fast that they can't hear your requests at times)

Yes! I finally got to have my Chipotle after being away from California for 2 plus years. Amazingly, it tastes exactly the same. However, it was a lot smaller than I remember it. Don't get me wrong, it was still tasty, but after reading other people's reviews I guess I am not alone in the complaint about the size. 

This location's staff was too small for the amount of people who were waiting to be served. That being said, they were all nice. I'm just not used to having to wait over 20 min for food at a Chipotle. Also, the parking in the area is terrible. I don't think it's being helped right now by the rather large construction site nearby that cuts off both the street and sidewalk. 

They nicely gave my friend veggies and lots and lots of chicken instead of beans and rice. However, they still skimmed on her salsa and lettuce as they did my own veggie bowl. Not to be a stickler, but I think they can afford to give a bit more lettuce.

Overall, I had a happy tummy for my kinda-fast meal, but will probably stick to other places in this chain that have parking next time or eat at another place in the area if I have more time to sit.

Tried it today to make sure I wasn't missing anything. The marketing had successfully convinced me that they make huge burritos. 

The hell they do. I got a small spoonful of chicken and plain rice. A similar amount of beans, a drop of sour cream and hot sauce and a huge dollop of guacamole on a giant tortilla. Obviously corporate management is trying to keep costs down by micromanaging the portions (the only thing I got alot of was the guacamole which I had to pay over a dollar extra for anyway)  The burrito was mostly tortilla and guacamole which is not very appealing.

No refried beans, bad rice, bland dry meat. NOT big burritos. 

The Bay Area is the birthplace of the Mission super burrito. How the hell can Chipotle even do business out here?
Yuck. Makes you sick. The staff could care less about service or food quality.

Many people are quick to point out that Chipotle is owned by McDonalds when they are trying to dissuade someone from going to the popular Mexican chain. I say why make the guilt by association argument when all you have to consider is that these people put white rice in their burritos. In addition, all their ads are pictures of the burrito wrapped in foil. I imagine they do this because they steam their tortilla, and don't grill them. The popularity of this inferior method of making a more elastic tortilla has vexed me for some time now. The Bay Area is littered with local Mexican restaurants that vary from good to transcendent. There is no legitimate reason to patronize these white rice a-holes.

Bitch, please. The only reason you would be going here is if you wanted to fulfill your daily caloric intake in one fatal stop or have some American-ized Mexican food. That didn't make any sense at all did it?

Originally brought to you by the same awesome guys at McDonalds, Chipotle manages to succeed in giving everyone a piece of the American Dream : being overweight.

Let's take a standard burrito that alot of people get: the chicken burrito. You feel less guilty eating it because chicken is less fattening than pork/steak yadayadayada. Okay so tortilla, rice, chicken, black beans, regular tomato salsa, cheese, and lettuce. No sour cream thanks.

*drum roll* 915 calories and 30g of fat. WAIT WHA?! In addition from getting over 2400mg of sodium (more than 100% of your daily intake), you might as well have just eaten a stick of butter for dinner.

I came here around 8PM on Monday (2 days ago).

1. staff was rude
2. the manager was rude and rude to his staff
- he told my girlfriend to stop asking for salsas (when she only asked for two- medium and mild) because the lines was very long
3. we were basically bottom feeders of the meat - looked like they haven't replaced it in a while.

I can somewhat forgive them for 1 and 2 because there is a lot of stress given that the line became long suddenly.
