However, 3 is the problem. I ordered barbacoa- and I got food-poisoned. Yes, I haven't slept tonight because I am still sick. This is seriously a problem- I am guessing the meat was left out for a while and left neglected. I love chipotle and this might be a unique case (therefore, the 2 star), but this is certainly unacceptable. Probably a good idea not to goto this place later in the day when the meat/cheese have been left out for a while. How did I know it was from this place? My girlfriend also experienced food poisoning- but not that severe. She ordered carnitas but only had some of my barbacoa. We both experienced food poisoning symptoms the night of.

Pretty much like any other chipotle. Lines get really long around 12pm and 6-7pm and sometimes the wait can be 15-30 minutes. 

I love getting the burrito bowl with tortilla on the side. Extra rice, extra lettuce, extra beans, extra corn, extra fajitas, just ask for it. The only catch is extra meat costs extra. This place tastes better than La Burrita and certainly doesn't mess up the order.

Unfortunately, students no longer get free drinks here.

Come on Chipotle, you're better than this. Your Telegraph Ave location is a glaring example of how poos customer services can really be. 
Not only did I have to tell four different people what I wanted, I had to tell them ALL twice. Nobody was listening and they were goofing around the whole time I was ordering. 
The worst part was that the cashier added a drink to my order and charged me for it 1. without me asking for a drink and 2. WITHOUT TELLING ME! I didn't even realize until I got back to my office and saw a cup IN the bag. I know it's only $1.50ish, but I really feel cheated. 
Boo Telegraph Chipotle...

I've said this before on a previous review and I'll say it again:

I know NOTHING about Mexican food.  I went to a Tex-Mex restaurant with some friends and they had to describe to me the difference between a flauta, enchilada, taquito, chile rellenos, etc.  

That being said, I really really heart Chipotle.  My stomach really doesn't care whether or not they're "authentic." It just cares that it's tasty, and that it fills it up.  

Get the chicken burrito, add all the veggies to make yourself feel better about the stuff-fest you're about to embark on.

I'm also slightly ashamed to say that I regularly eat the entire 2000 calorie burrito in a single sitting (in my defense I usually minimize or hold off on the sour cream and cheese so I don't have an apoplectic attack).

It's remarkable what a difference 400 miles makes, since this place serves nothing like the Chipotle burritos I ate at my home in Southern California. I don't know what they did with their meat, but it was always tough and dry during the 2-3 times I visited.

And so, the Mexican offerings surrounding the UC Berkeley campus continue to be a vile joke to this day.

Ugh.  Don't do it.  Just don't.  

You know, Telegraph Ave. is in enough trouble as it is.  Somewhere in the vicinity of 10+ storefronts closed on the Berkeley stretch of Telegraph Ave. alone last year - in fact, a girl working at Amoeba informed me of their concern over lack of business.  This is the ORIGINAL Amoeba Records we're talking about here, and they're actually concerned about getting enough business.  Unreal.

Point being, Telegraph is nowhere near what it used to be, but at least it still has some of the restaurants and storefronts that make it worth visiting on multiple occasions (Cafe Intermezzo alone could do this, but I would live at that damn place and sleep in a bowl of lettuce if they'd let me).  

You put in crappy, craptastic, craptacular places like Chipotle here, though, and it's just sad.  Gross and sad.  Telegraph deserves better.

When Chipotle first opened up on South Side a few months ago I was among the crowd that wasn't sure if we needed another Mexican place on Southside, but I like everyone else, ended up waiting in line for an hour and a half on opening night for the free burrito (and soda) that they gave away.

Chipotle is actually pretty darn good. I really like how you go down the line and select exactly what you want in your burrito and corn is a great addition, by the way. My only complaint is that steamed white rice is just not right for a burrito. 

Other than that, the place is great (and the guacamole is worth the extra price.) It does not replace La Burrita for Berkeley Mexican...Chipotle is just a different option.

Double-wrapped burritos for the win!

This is just like any other Chipotle... Of course, it's not really Mexican food you get here (people know this AND still complain about it), but it is a good deal worth your money. ESPECIALLY since they give you a free soda (and, right now, a free bag of chips/salsa if you are a Cal student and pay with your Cal1Card!).

The service is really nice, and they always speak to me in Spanish.. Um, Gracias? 

Convenient since it's right across from campus! I go here at least once a week ^_^

I don't know what it is, but about once a month, I crave a Chipotle fix. I am not the only person I know like this either (it started as a regular lunch spot when I worked in Walnut Creek). Here's why this location is A-OK by me:

-Long lines, but they move through them at a tolerable place given my addiction.
-A couple of their employees have been there for awhile and they are good at what they do.
-They give out free sodas (though not always consistently, so I get confused about whether it'll be a Coke day or not).

Burrito bowl, rice, black beans, steak, one scoop of corn salsa, two of hot salsa, splash of sour cream and cheese, handful of lettuce = scarfed down every time.

I was actually pretty excited when my friend discovered this Chipotle location. My friends and I decided we'd go there for lunch & it was all I could think about during the morning, haha.

Looks like any other Chipotle. Nothing special. Ordered my usual steak bowl. Note to self: do NOT get the hella spicy salsa. I definitely regretted it later. I'm a baby when it comes to spicy things. But if you like spicy, then I say go for it. Nonetheless, the food was yummy. 

The tables inside filled up really quick during lunchtime. By the time we got our food, all the tables were taken, so we headed to the outside tables. There were tables open; however, we were turned off by the FLIES that were all over. It was pretty disgusting that we couldn't eat there. We ended up finding somewhere else to eat lunch. 

I'm never really in this area, but good to know that a Chipotle exists here.

They have fast fresh food down!  They have a very nice staff and for a quick mexican grill place - the Guacamole and Chips are awesome.  I like the fresh burrito bowl which is healthy, low cal and light.  It is affordable good food.  One of the better cal student eateries downtown on Telegraph.  They take credit cards which is unique for this neighborhood.

I was able to bypass a super long line and went straight to the register after I placed my order online. They had it ready when I got there. I was in and out in about 3 minutes. Got my free drink also since I am a student. but they didn't ask for student ID. 

I only gave it four out of five stars because this is my first time ordering from them. The soft tacos were great, I wish I ordered more though. The Red-chili salsa didn't seem "hot" at first but 10 minutes after eating the tacos my mouth is still burning, :-) I love hot stuff.

I wanted to like Chipotle - I really did. I work on Southside and am always excited when a new place opens up - food or otherwise. I had many of the same issues that others complain about namely that they cannot wrap a burrito! I had the burrito do-over that Warren G. describes and I also had an exciting 2 tortilla burrito that was constructed by half wrapping in one flour tortilla and then, when there was no more tortilla geography left, finishing the wrap in a second flour tortilla. I should have been grateful for that free tortilla because they sure do charge for everything else! Try walking out for less then $8 - for mexican food!

being from santa cruz (which is sans chipotle and most addictive chains for that matter), i ALWAYS get my burrito fix here when i am in berkeley. these cravings are so serious that sometimes i actually consider driving the 17 hwy from SC to get me a burrito. clearly, i over-hype this meal and expect magic in mouth when i get it. this particular chipotle on tele does not deliver that. 

first of all, parking is impossible in the whole area, and chipotle doesnt validate parking. LAME. next, only cal students get their free drinks, not UC santa cruz students. umm, excuse me, i can barely eat my burrito without a free iced tea. cal already overshadows santa cruz in everything else, now this too?!?! third, watching the people artfully craft my burrito behind the counter KILLS me when they toss it around and dont evenly distribute the beans/rice/guac situation. this seems to happen more often here than at other chipotles.

i still have an undying love for these delicious 1000 calorie burritos, but i think i will avoid the one on telegraph from now on. gilman isnt that far.

I finally broke down and got my lunch here yesterday.  I ordered a pork burrito with black beans.  What I ate tasted like it had been made by a British chef who cooks for a corporate cafeteria, someone who had never been to Mexico and had seen a burrito made exactly once.  This surprised me because my meal was made in front of my eyes by people who were speaking Spanish to each other and Spanish to the customer ahead of me.

Everything in my burrito had a bland taste to it.  The rice especially tasted flagrantly non-Mexican -- it seemed to be basmati rice!!  The different flavors in the burrito hadn't melded together at all -- there was the rice section, the salsa section, the meat section, and so on.  The good news, on the other hand, is that the whole assembly struck me as healthy and somehow squeaky clean.  Maybe "sanitized" is the right word, and I'm not sure that the news is exactly good.

I'll be back again, but it won't be any time soon.  Maybe during the week between Christmas and New Year's, when many local businesses are closed.

Update: I was here on May 15 to get a free meal -- Chipotole was a sponsor for Bike to Work Day and gave a free burrito (or salad or burrito bol) to everyone who came in with a flyer and one of the "musette bags" that were being distributed to bikers at major intersections.  There were lots of people with bicycle helmets and musette bags in line, and we were all very happy to be getting fed.  Thanks, Chipotle!

I had a burrito bol instead of a burrito; I picked up this tip from Yelp reviews of a Chipotle in Morgan Hill.  Get lots of salsa and lettuce, and you're OK.

I stopped by Chipotle today to get a burrito with a friend.  This was not my first time eating at Chipotle, but it was my first time at this particular location.

The burritos were, as they always are, quite good. If you are a vegetarian I would definitely recommend the vegetarian fajita burrito.  Chipotle has very distinctive burritos that have great sweet corn  and grilled onions and peppers (if you get them fajita style).  You also get to see them make burritos right in front of you, which is always good.

One last thing that I am very particular about is how well wrapped burritos are.  Some people are just not qualified to wrap a burrito in such a way as to lend the burrito a high degree of structural integrity.  The masterful burrito wrappers at Chipotle have no such problem.

YUM! Give me 1300 calories wrapped up in a gigantic carb intensive tortilla and you've got yourself a Chipotle Burrito!! 

I can't really help myself from eating here. The quantity is impressive and I think that's what really gets me. I'm more of quantity over quality type girl. 

My recommendations for things to put into the burrito:
--chicken
--EVERYTHING (who cares about the calories! Eat first, diet later!)

I realize Cal students from LA/Sac can't live without their Chipotle and went bat-shit crazy when it came to Telegraph.  Personally, I can't get over the fact that they don't use Mexican rice, and their main draw seems to be a "burrito bowl."  As a *burrito* lover, I will take Gordo's, Cancun, or Cactus instead, thank you very much.

Chipotle Grill gets bonus points for using naturally raised meats, and *some* organic beans & veggies with a goal of 100%. I love little mom & pop Mexican restaurants, but when it comes to the quality of meat you're eating, you may as well be in a fast food joint.

That said, the salsa on my tacos was so cold it made the meat cold. I really, really wanted to love this place, because I like to support restaurants - even if they are chains - that utilize good meat and organic produce.

Finally, a place to get cheap burritos on the way to campus. Too bad it's 17 years too late for me. Maybe Little Q will opt to go to Cal...

Fuck you Chipotle for the 10 lbs I've gained the past couple of months. Damn my chicken fajita burrito with extra corn, sour cream, fresh salsa with hot sauce, and a side of guacamole. It's OK if no one in Berkeley wants to eat you, I'll do it. The whole damn thing. 

On the plus side, they sell beer. I love sitting on the patio with my huge-ass burrito and corona watching the Cal madness from afar. 

One star off for absolutely no parking, and when it's lunch time, there's not a single table or seat available. And also because of the McDonald's deal. Past or present, it doesn't matter.

Everyone knows how the burrito tastes here. No complaints regarding the taste.

I like this place and free drink for Cal students is also really cool.

My only problem. Everytime I ask them to give some extra stuff

(extra rice, fajita, cheese...etc) they only put a tiny bit more which

is pretty meaningless asking. 

When you go to the one on Gilman and ask them for the same thing, they put hell of a lot more than these guys do.

For the reviews that said This Chipotle location skimps on fillings, I have to disagree. 
I can share my food with someone else and still be full. You just need to ask for extra fillings. 
Of course, this isn't authentic Mexican food in any means, but it's really convienient when you have a gap and want to get something quick. Sometimes long lines will get very long, but the workers are efficient and you won't be stuck there long.
You can also order online, by phone, or via the Chipotle iPhone app, and then pick up your order in front without having to wait. 
I never went to Chipotle during my freshman year because the portions scared me, but now it's become a once almost every week thing for me. How embarassing.

Oh, and there is very limited seating, so if you want to eat there, then you'll have to swoop on an empty table asap.

Since it's pretty useless to review a chain restaurant, I'll compare it with other Chipotles I've been to.  

service: relatively quick, they know when the lunch rush for college kids and theyve got the assembly line down to a science.  Try to get the tall skinny dude to serve you, hes pretty liberal with the meats and good stuff.   

ambience: small.  if you are use to the bigger chipotles, you'll feel very crowded in this narrow corridor of claustrophobia, especially during the midday pileup when the line is out the door.  don't expect to find a seat there during lunch time.  outdoor seating is available.

an added bonus is they give you a free drink when you show them your student ID, which not all chipotles do.

i never ate at chipotle back in los angeles; im more of a baja fresh girl. however, chipotle has quite a convenient location next to campus. 

try: chicken burrito. its big, overly full and will make you wish you never ordered it in the first place. the burrito bol is another option (everything a burrito has minus the tortilla). you can taste the delicious rice more.

Coming from SoCal, this Chipotle was kind of a disappointment. 
First, let's talk about the service. I've observed a great deal of attitude by the servers who get very frustrated when new people don't know what the options are. Yes, we know that you guys are in a hurry, but isn't about quality over how fast it's being done? They're fast at what they do, but there's no sincerity with assistance at all.
Second, what's with the portion size? I've had bigger bowls back home with the choices I wanted, not just because I didn't put more stuff into it.
Also, this goes for not only this Chipotle, but Chipotle's in general: the prices keep moving up, and the food pales in quality to real, authentic Mexican restaurants which is a lot less cheaper.

Mmmmm Chipotle is always yummy and satisfying. I used to get burritos, but after I tried the burrito bowls, I've never looked back. The bowls are just waaayyy easier to eat since the burritos are oftentimes super messy since they're stuffed so full. Also, it's a healthier option since you get all the delicious stuff inside without the calorie-packed tortilla! Although, you can also ask for a tortilla on the side (at no extra cost) if you're determined to have it!

I always order the Veggie Burrito Bowl ($6.25) with rice, veggies, black beans, lettuce, guac, and salsa. The awesome thing about getting the veggie option is that it comes with guacamole, so you don't have to pay an extra $1.90 to add it on! The bowl is always consistently good and I usually can't even finish the whole thing in one sitting! The location is great since it's right across from campus and ingredients are usually already made, so all they have to do is assemble your order. 

TIP: Order online ahead of time so you don't have to wait in line and can just pick your food up!

I don't understand the oh so frequent bashing of Chipotle. Sure, it's not authentic Mexican. It also is a chain that was once owned by McDonald's at that -- we get that but still judge it on its food and service. 

It's a fast food American-Mexican restaurant. It's definitely better than La Burrito; the burritos are huge. I am a friggin' fan of Chipotle and whenever I want a 1000+ calories and have around $6 to spend, I'll most definitely get a fajita burrito with carne asada, sour cream, lettuce, and extra corn salsa and cheese. Damn, I'm getting hungry just writing this up. 

The service is quick and efficient. You don't get treated like crap like at La Burrita which is just rude sometimes but don't expect five-star quality service either obviously. There aren't too many seats available because the store is pretty small but I'm more than happy to get it to-go and eat elsewhere. Screw the non-sensical Berkeley hate for Chipotle!

Pros: Okay I'm aware that this place is obviously not entirely authentic, meaning I don't need yet another white person to tell me so, since they're apparently the experts on Mexican cuisine.  Just because it isn't 100% traditional doesn't automatically make it bad.  I happen to like a little variety.  I can appreciate BOTH "authentic" Mexican food and more contemporary stuff like Chipotle.  These places are becoming common enough to where I (a hungry vegan) can get a good, filling meal for relatively cheap when there might not be many other options around for me.  Basically everything you'd think would be vegan, is: tortillas, rice, guacamole, salsas, vegetables, black beans but NOT the pinto beans, those are cooked with bacon, fyi.  Also at lunch they usually just assume you're a student if you look young enough and give you a free drink cup (because students get free drinks), so that's a bonus.

Cons: Long lines at lunch and some chance of cross-contamination (cheese falling in the guacamole, etc).  A burrito is a LOT of calories, like somewhere around 1000 just for a fully loaded veggie burrito even without sour cream or cheese.  Google some of the Chipotle fan sites that have nutritional fact calculators for your exact burrito's calorie count.

Oh and for the record McDonald's USED to own Chipotle.  They divested from them quite some time ago now.

service is quite fast
they give me two scoops of rice
lots of free napkins

I don't know why, but there is always people rushing into Chipotle! It amazes me... The food is decent at best, and there are so many other places around where you can get the same, or maybe even better, food. Maybe it is because I know its a chain restaurant (owned by McDonald's).

Overall, the food isn't bad here. And as a CAL student, you get a free drink. 

Once in a while is okay, but I hear about people eating here on a daily basis.

Okay, so my friend recommended that i try this place...and let me say that that will be the last recommendation that i take from him.

I ordered a Carnitas Burrito...
First thing i notice is that the carnitas are completely submerged in liquid...which was not so appetizing.
Once they finally put all the stuff on my burrito, they guy rolls it into some kind of cube like thing! O_O  I have never seen a burrito with all dimensions being equal...it freaked me out. 

So...on to the actual taste of the burrito...
Rice: More cilantro than a Vietnamese sandwich...Not good at all (and I like Vietnamese sandwiches...)
Carnitas: Soggy...very very soggy. Very salt-tastic as well.
Sour Cream: I don't know if it was the sour cream, or the hot sauce i got on top of it, but it turned into a really wet and disgusting combination.  

Total: $6.47 (came with a drink cuz i showed my student ID)

Well anyways, don't make the same mistake I did...do yourself a favor and hit up Gordo or Chino's in SF, cuz they know what they're doing.

I've been here 3 times and it's just really good. The only better food I've had is from select taco trucks (ever try one one that's near Best Buy in Emeryville? BEST EVER ; O )

Reasons why I like this place:

**Clean. Every time I come here the restaurant is immaculately spotless, I mean to the point that I actually go "God it's clean in here...". I like the patio in front too!

**Simple, organized, and efficient. Whoever organized the line for the food must be a demi-genius. You can get a burrito or 4 hard tacos and get out of line at the same time, because of how the ingredients are organized

**The workers are awesome, they let me order in Spanish and they make me laugh

**The food is really good. The hard tacos are yum ( I know its not traditional Mexican food, but you like what you like), and the salad is really good. I love the BBQ chicken

**The prices are decent, considering they always get my food right

I wish they had Soy Taco Meat, (if that sounds gross, don't knock it till you try it ; ) )

ATTENTION CHIPOTLE -

PLEASE CONSTRUCT A STORE IN THE ROCKRIDGE AREA.

I am tired of driving all the way over here to get my burrito bowl on.

This store is awesome but sometimes they skimp out on the tomato salsa and chicken.

PLEASE BUILD A CHIPOTLE IN ROCKRIDGE or NEAR ROCKRIDGE.

I always get dragged here....I did try it a couple of times, but once I had dinner with a friend and there was A FLY IN HER BURRITO. 
That's just gross. And this is coming from a girl who will gladly eat cheese off the floor. 

The guys are nice, I guess, but no, I don't want flies with that.

I'm from SD.
4 Stars to Chipotle? Am I nuts? WHHAAAAAAAAT?

"So-cal Mexican food is so much better Wonjun. You're an idiot."
Trust me. I know what real Mexican food is. I lived 15 minutes away from Mexico.

The thing is, you just have to accept that Chipotle is simply not legitimate Mexican food. Then you can start to appreciate it. 

It's kind of like going to Panda Express and then saying "Wow this place sucks, I can get Chinese food so much better at ___________"
Well, no shit dude. 

Chipotle gives what a college student needs. Fast service, and filling proportions.

"How do I get filling proportions?"
Get a burrito bowl. Then get a tortilla on the side, free of charge.
Wrap your own burrito before you start eating with half your burrito bowl.
Now you have a burrito and half a bowl.
Filling.
(P.S) Even if you get a meat, you can still get some cooked veggies in it.

It's pretty good though on a general food scale. Lots of flavors, (Since I like putting in everything) and I love the texture of each bite.

I should try other things then Steak. I always choose steak hoping that one day God will reach down into Chipotle, take all their steak away and fill it with Mexican Carne Asada before I ask them. Ah well.

Anyways. Chipotle is good. You can't deny that.

So I love Chipotle in general. I used to always go to the one in Alameda so I decided to try the one here since I'm at Berkeley now. 

I wanted a steak burrito with no beans. 
I told the first lady this and she gets another lady to make it for me. This lady has a strong accent and she asks me me a question of which I thought was "beans?" I said no. Then she skips the meat and goes on to the other stuff (lettuce, corn, etc). Another dude rolls my burrito. I'm like "wtf? Where's my steak?" I try to call for his attention but he's busy talking to another girl. I finally get aggressive with him when he's done rolling (even though I'm sick) and he's like "oh you said no meat!" I'm like "no I said no BEANS". The lady with the accent starts speaking in her language and throws him another piece of aluminum foil. ATTITUDE. I apologize (even though I am the customer) but she still mugs me. Now I am eating a burrito where all my steak is on the bottom. 

All I'm saying is she could have been more mature about it and understand that I misheard. She should have had less attitude. 

Food is good. Customer service sucks.

I'm a huge Chipotle fan. This establishment is the worst I've been to, however.

They'll give you a free drink if you look remotely like a college student and ask. However, the guys that work this place LOVE to skimp on the portions. I once asked for extra rice and the guy gave me the dirtiest look and said "this IS extra rice". The scoops of meat are like, 3/4 full, and you know how some places give you a little extra scoop if the meat chunks fall off? Not here, no way. Let those meat chunks fall back into the tray, I imagine they are thinking. They're also just pretty unfriendly and don't look very happy about having to serve college students.

Chipotle is not authetnic mexican cuisine, but neither is the burrito. If you really want to eat what mexicans are eating, then go eat some tacos. I recommend Sinaloa in Oakland. 

I'm surprised at the number of 1-star reviews for this place. I bet the people who gave this place one-star probably eat here anyway but are too snobby to admit it. 

This is the best chipotle location I have been to. They always hook up the free drink and are capable of dealing with large crowds. They have an adept team of skilled mexican burrito-wrappers that process customsers faster than any restaurant I can think of. 

There's no such thing as real mexican food in Berkeley. The taco truck on bancroft is probably the closest to being real mexican fare. This place is for getting in your major food groups: protein, veggies, and carbs. It's cheap and quick. Faster than McDonalds even with lines going out the door. 

Stop complaining cuz i bet you're eating chipotle RIGHT NOW you stupid noobs.

Man I love their chicken quesadillas. Kind of lame that they charge you the same price as a burrito (if you add salsa). I love this food, but I must be a masochist because my stomach always feels like a witches cauldron minutes after I've stuffed my face. The indoor seating is nil, so head to the outdoor patio and look at all the street vendors selling tees you could easily make yourself at CafePress.com.

I love chipotle.  

I go here probably twice a week on average, and I can always count on having an awesome steak burrito bowl whenever my stomach is needing it.  Lines can get kind of long (as it's a popular choice amongst students), but it's worth it if you have the time.  People complain about getting ripped off with lack of food/meat.  Just ask them for more! Most of the time they'll kindly just scoop a little more meat and thats that! 

Bottom line: Best fast food option in Berkeley!

WOW this place was awful. I'm usually a fan of Chipotle and I figure it must have been something to do with the all-new staff that comes with an all-new location. No less than five people handled my burrito and not one of them knew what to do with it, except maybe the guy at the tortilla steamer. I ended up with a burrito that was literally cold. Poorly wrapped as well, but the awful part was the chilliness. Jesus. I don't know if it was due to the excessive amounts of salsa or inadequate heating of the ingredients, but this burrito was frigid and nasty. I don't know why I even went here in the first place, considering the alternatives in the neighborhood.

Leave your Chipotle large servings expectations at the door because you won't find it here, but feel free to take a Tabasco sauce on your way out. You deserve it!

This Chipotle is wack! I mean... I love Chipotle and I will continue to go here because of the convenience of its location and the deliciousness that its franchise has established. But this Chipotle located on Telegraph Ave in Berkeley has to be the most stingiest restaurant with its ingredients. It has people lined up so the demand is high here, but I am upset at the lack of meat each time I eat my burrito.

I made a ridiculous bet with a friend and was able to finish two of these burritos in under 10 minutes. That just shows how small these burritos are. But hey it's still Chipotle and it's still delicious, which is why I give it one more star. But I really wish they would just spare at least one more cut of some steak?! Sigh... Oh well time to go to Chipotle.

the Great,
GumZ

Came here for lunch today. I don't walk down Telegraph that often, so I hadn't noticed yet there was a new business in this space. Turns out, it's been here for almost a year!

It looks clean, so we give it a try. There was a bit of a line, but it moved fast. There's not that many options, I picked the fajita burrito with carnitas and guacamole (because pork and avocado are two of my favorite foods). It was good. A bit too much rice, but the guacamole was awesome, and the carnitas very tasty. I'll be back.

Reading the reviews here, I learn that burritos are not supposed to have white rice. Never knew that. Who cares? It's not supposed to have salsa either. Nor cheese. Nor sour cream. If you're willing to bastardize the traditional Northern Mexican burrito by adding all these things, how come you're not willing to try it with a different rice?

My first and last experience with Chipotle:

*I order a beef burrito

*Guy overfills burrito with rice, beef, peppers, guacamole, sour cream, cheese

*Guy attempts to wrap burrito and the insides splurge out from the sides and tears the tortilla wrap

*Guy takes burrito and drips the filling into the new tortilla

*Guy re-wraps burrito up into a 3x3 inch square stump. 

My burrito come out deformed, and it tasted bland. This location is full of college kids who don't know how to make burritos. Next time I'm craving a burrito drop by Gordos thank you very much

I had never heard of Chipotle before I went to Cal for college. There is nothing like it in Vancouver (and Canada in general), and I must say we're missing out! It obviously isn't authentic or traditional Mexican cuisine (what is, nowadays?) but it's FAMAZINGGG. Especially if you're a freshman who is sick of the unappetizing dining hall food. I swear I had Chipotle at least twice a week during my first two years of college, after which I realized the amount of calories I was gorging on and cut back drastically. But I still enjoy it every once in a while.

I always order the burrito bowl with white rice, no beans, steak, sour cream, cheese and lettuce. The meat is always fresh (especially during rush hours) and they've really cut back on the butter in the rice over the years. The best thing is that they offer Cal ID holders a free cup for drinks. 

Service is amazingly fast and friendly, and a 30-person line goes by in about 10ish minutes, so don't be discouraged when you pass by and there are people piling out of the door! Oh, and the employees always compliment me on my blonde/red hair, so extra points there O:)

To set things straight--Chipotle isn't owned by McDonalds anymore. 

I've always had a just-fine experience here. The guacamole is good and the food tastes fresh and clean. They use mostly sustainable ingrediants, if that's your thing. I have had an experience with too salty rice--and yes, it's odd that it is white--and the cheese isn't necessary since it doesn't melt. You can request a mix of salsas, though, and I like that.

It's fast food, and for fast food, it isn't bad at all. The vegetarian burrito is less greasy than the one at La Burrita's, and so it just depends on what you are in the mood for.

I ordered online for the first time the other day and got a burrito bowl with extra corn and lettuce. You tell them when you will come by to pick it up and I chose to pay at the store so I just cut everyone in line. I was in and out of there super quick. I will always order online now....

This place used to be an old pizza place and has be renovated to Chipotle! WIN.

Chipotle has a standard taste among the restaurants, so the food is as legit as any other Chipotle. Prices are the same, except that this location (being in a college-student populated area) gives free drinks with student ID. Other Chipotle locations do not.

The location is pretty awesome -- close to campus. It is best to get here by foot, seeing as parking is till a few blocks away from the actual place. It is really small inside, probably only 30 in total capacity, and it gets JAM PACKED like sardines during the lunch hour. I'd say that the iPhone app is very useful for this specific location. 

Will have to agree with Eugene, in that when you ask for a little extra of something, the workers are pretty chintzy about giving you more.

This is Mexican fast food, so you're getting what you pay for. The food is good when you're hungry, but not the best. So three stars for the food, and the extra star? Its for the workers there as they are extremely friendly and always smiling.

The burritos here are really big, so I don't often come here unless I'm feeling up for the challenge of eating a monster burrito. They also have burrito bowls and salads if you want a healthier choice. You can always tailor the ingredient to your liking. For example, during my most recent visit, I ordered a burrito bowl. I ordered just rice and no beans, and the worker scooped some rice into the bowl. He then said to me, "you want more rice, don't you?" I nodded enthusiastically, and he gave me two more generous scoops of rice. Same thing happened with the corn. Free fountain drinks are for students, but they usually throw it in anyways if you look about the age. 

I hear that the service varies from chain to chain, so luckily for me, I have a good one nearby.

Chipotle is crappy expensive Mexican food. It's very Americanized, not that good quality, and way overrated. Especially overrated for one in Berkeley. If this were Wyoming or some random state with no Mexican food, then maybe Chipotle would be your best bet, but c'mon people, you live in Berkeley! There are SO many better Mexican food places around you; go look around!

Man, there seem to be a huge group of Chipotle haters posting about the Berkeley location.  Fans of Chipotle need not worry, this location is definitely up to par.  Every time I have been here, I have received a proper sized burrito made exactly how I ordered it

I read some of these reviews and wonder if any of these people have ever been to a Chipotle location before.  Yes it is a chain, and it is "fast food", but you don't go into Chevy's, Taco Hell, Del Taco and go complain about how non-authentic it is, because it ain't news kids.. everyone already knows.

And what is wrong with having Americanized Mexican food once in a while?  Are carne asada fries Americanized?  I think so, but does that make them any less delicious? No.

There are times that demand authentic Mexican food in which a legit Taqueria is in order.  And there are other times, when I crave the cilantro lime rice, that is Chipotle's trademark, and their delicious corn salsa.  Variety is the spice of life, and I loves me some Chipotle.

This location also gives out free sodas to students (or anyone else that looks to be of student age).  Props to them for that.

OK, after bad mouthing Chipotle (see my Gordo's Yelp), I was persuaded to try them again for lunch.

OK, nobody in there but three Berkeley Cops. A good sign.

OK,I order a Carne Asada burrito w/everything, except lettuce.

OK, when I ask for no lettuce, that means don't put it on my burrito. And, if you do after I've told you, don't try to pick out. Please make me another.

OK. It must be the way they wrap it, because every time I've been there, it's like a "California Roll." All the fillings are not "mushed" together, i.e. one bite, meat, one bite, rice, another bite, beans. I want my burrito and the fillings "pasteurized."

Not OK, I still paid $8 for a lunch (no drink) that I didn't enjoy. Really a one star experience, however the woman who took my money was for this lousy burrito was smiling and pleasant. Make it two stars.

Be honest.

Having the authentic stuff is amazing because, well, it's legit Mexican food. But once in awhile, you just need a Chipotle burrito.

...

Or am I the only one?

I looooove Chipotle. I've had plenty of burritos in my day, ranging from authentic taquerias to the lamest of fast food joints. In my opinion, Chipotle is the tastiest of them all.

But this Chipotle on Telegraph? Ehhh.

The food here is still amazing, so no qualms about that. But there are other issues. There is absolutely nowhere to sit and parking is a pain in the ass. That's true for everywhere on Telegraph, I know, but I don't want to deal with parking issues for Chipotle when I can just go to the one on Gilman and park easily.

Also, it looks a wee bit tacky on Telegraph and kinda messes up the whole vibe of the place. It kinda sucks when big businesses find these areas where small businesses have built up large crowds and then move in and poach all the people. I don't know the history of Telegraph at all and could be talking out of my anus, but that's the impression I get, anyway.

I'm sure I'll be frequenting Chipotle as long they're around and I don't need to go on a diet. But this one I'll skip.

The verdict is in: I enjoy crappy "Mexican" food.

Give me a few tortillas, pile on some flavored chicken, cheese, tomatoes, corn, and lettuce and I'm happy. Oh Chipotle has guacamole, sour cream, chili-salsa, and the likes...but I don't need that.

The people who work here are nice, and the tacos taste flavorful and fresh. I love being able to stare at the ingredients and tell them exactly what I want. And no, I've never tried a Burrito here. Beans, sour cream, and rice? Gross.

Today was my first time visiting a Chipotle since I left Saratoga High, where for the Class of 05, Chipotle was THE place to be...for reasons I can't quite comprehend actually.

I don't even really like Mexican food. I only went to the South Bay location at the urgings of my then-boyfriend. Never would I have envisioned 4 years ago, that right now, I would be lying here in bed, giving Chipotle 4 stars on Yelp. But hey, my taste buds don't lie...to me at least.

I really like eating here because I usually have a lot of classes in Haas.
My usual drinks that I buy are iced tea and mocha. Love the iced tea.

I've tried a lot here:
seared chicken burger w/ fries: I really enjoyed this burger. The bun was really delicious and soft. The chicken has that grilled taste, and the fries are crispy!

seared ahi tuna sandwich: This was an interesting sandwich. The ingredients inside the sandwich appealed to me because it just sounded really healthy. Taste wise, it wasn't so bad, it was interesting, not sure if I would get it again.

mongolian beef rice bowl: The beef was really tender when I tried it and it reminded me of Korean braised short ribs. Something I would get again if I was in the mood for rice + meat.

bbq chicken quesadilla: I think I like this bbq chicken quesadilla more than the one @ FSM. 

breakfast burrito: Has chorizo, potatoes, eggs... really good. Looks a little gross but the eggs are really soft and the chorizo makes this breakfast burrito a burrito, w/o it, it would just be a breakfast wrap to me. I drizzle a lot of tapatio and ketchup on this before every bite. It tastes just fine w/o it but I like it better with those condiments.

falafel plate: the falafels are really good. I love the extra things that come with it!

soups: their soups are usually hearty and delicious. I really liked their vegetable soup with tomatoes,  potatoes, garlic, barley? Wasn't salty and was super tasty and healthy. The chicken gumbo was a bit salty and not very satisfying. Usually comes with a piece of bread.

I'm pretty sure I had more but can't remember at the moment. I generally like all the items on the menu. I heard that the turkey avocado?? something avocado sandwich was no bueno though. Haven't tried it myself so can't really judge, but after hearing that, I don't think I'll try it...

First time back since the renovation. Although I (like many) were sad to see the Asian rice bowls go, I really like the looks of the new menu. The first thing I saw was the new fried chicken sandwich and that pretty much ended my search. 

It came out pretty fast, relative to before the renovation. Although to be fair, the semester is over now so the lunch rush was a lot quieter than it would have been a few weeks ago. The sandwich was pretty solid - chicken was moist and delicious, and although it was probably a little over done, the breading added some nice texture. The accompaniments ("spicy kale slaw and aioli") were tasty, if a bit mild, and the bread (Acme torpedo) was fresh and chewy. It also came with a small salad of greens, which was nice to contrast with the sandwich. 

Overall, for the money and speed, it was a very good lunch. I'll definitely be back, to get the fried chicken again and also try out some other items on the revamped menu.

PLEASE BRING BACK THE ASIAN BOWLS. Cheap, tasted great for the starving student, and fast. 

Now the menu and cafe has been replaced by slow service (albeit they are really nice) and overpriced food that tastes bland and in pretty small portions. If I'm paying like $7 for some fancy shamncy sounding curry rice bowl thing I expect it to taste relatively good and not as if I completely wasted my money. Salads are mediocre at best as well. I usually just get their soup of the day which doesn't taste bad and fill myself up with the piece of foccacia bread that comes with it. They're pretty fast with all your drink orders though. And there's plenty of seating so that's a step up from before.

I like their lemon hibiscus tonic/juice(?). But other than that, menu has no appeal. 

They basically took out all the Asian food (as far as I could see), and substituted curry (which used to be more Korean) with Indian curry. I have nothing against Indian curry and I actually enjoy them, but I think it would've been nice to keep the other version too since it was so good! I guess they're different caterers from the previous ones, but couldn't they have just worked with the other caterers? 

I hear a lot of people wanting the Asian bowls back, because they were just so good. I feel the same way. If it wasn't for the lemon hibiscus tonic, I really wouldn't buy a thing from this place.

FIFO @ Haas Cafe took over for the previous vendors in this space. They are owned by the same people as nearby Strada and Cafe Zeb in the law school. They are still tweaking their menu, as they were told to initially try and offer the various types of asian food as the previous vendors. They haven't had much luck, and I would prefer they stick to what their other locations do well - hearty salads, soups, and sandwiches. I appreciate that they use fresh, organic when they can food - such an upgrade from the previous vendor!

Their feedback thus far for their rice bowls has been that it's bland, but again, bland is better than the gross, fatty meat rice bowls that the previous vendor offered. I am giving them 3 stars until things settle down and they are able to figure out their permanent menu.

They DO have the best mocha biancas and espresso drinks around town though! And I love that there is no credit card minimum or surcharge. More one-off lattes for me - yay!

Give them a chance to get up and running before giving them a negative review. They appreciate the feedback in that little clear box on-site. Service is so much better and friendlier, too!

FIFO opened up recently and I was excited because the baristas are from Caffe Strada. It makes sense since they're the same owner and it was nice to see their familiar faces. HOWEVER, I don't think their coffee/quality of service is as good.

I got their iced coffee, which I always get at Strada, and they skimped on the coffee ): I literally got a plastic cup that was only 75% full. Next time, I got an iced mocha since I love it at Zeb, Strada and FSM, but they served it to me in a paper cup. Mmm..that is not cool. 

Anyways, overall, this place is alright. I had their salad once and it was just Meh. The place is always filled with Haaskies, but I notice there is less traffic than the old place. 

BTW, I don't know how I feel about the expansion of the Strada cafe chain. FSM, Strada, Zeb, Fifo....I like being able to get my iced mocha at four different places now, but it kind of takes the fun out of it. Hmm..

TIP:
-Get their Cafe card if you go to any of those four cafes a lot and you're like me and  never have cash on you! Right now they're having a promotion at Fifo and Zeb to give you a $5 reload coupon when you put $20 on you card.

When there aren't thousands of first year UC Berkeley students around then this Peets is actually pretty good. I like the convenient location, but I was always strayed away from going because of the other students that seem to cause this location to have long lines. I got a caramel latte which was very good in my opinion. I'd definitely come again in hopes that I'll hit an off time to not run into a long line.

This place is actually not so bad, minus the fact that my orders aren't always right and the service can be slow. It's run by mostly college students. I've even seen a sign indicating "cashier in-training," which is as bad as having to drive behind a car with a sign that says "student driver!" Avoid or have patience.

There often tends to be a lot of people, so there's a greater chance for orders to get mixed up. But in terms of the menu: Peets - the white hot chocolate isn't on the menu, but it's pretty good. I particularly like the freddos, hibiscus iced tea, and white chocolate mocha (which I discovered by accident when I was given the wrong order). Sandwich side - you get a decent sandwich for the price you pay, ordered much the same way as at Subways, except on paper. It can be confusing for a newcomer because there's no sign to indicate that you have to give your paper (order) to the Peet's cashier before your sandwich is made on the sandwich side. Another thing that many people miss are the java boosts and the smoothies. The sign is up there, but not too many people order them. The Java Boosts are tasty. They're cold though, so best to drink on a warm day.

The merchandise is mostly a rip-off, but when you've got a ton of leftover meal points at the end of the semester, buy them early because those things disappear before the end of the semester!

I've come here a couple of times and have had pretty good service. I'm not a fan though when it is packed. Other than that they sell pretty much what other Peets sell, even holiday drinks. I like how there is seating outside so that you can have a conversation outside once you get your drink. They accept cash, meal points, and credit card.

I Hate, hate this place. For the couple of years that I've been here at Cal, I've tried to avoid it as much as possible, except when I have leftover meal points at the end of the semester and have to use them up buying overpriced $6 sandwiches. 

I really have no idea who had the bright idea of having two lines at this place. It would take so much less time if it worked the same way that the Golden Bear Cafe works. The line is always extremely long just to order and then you have to wait until the people on the other side of the store make your sandwiches, by the way orders are always wrong! 

It seems like this place doesn't care on improving service since people have already paid for their meal points so there really is no reason to get better since students have to use their points somewhere.

It's packed here during prime hours (morning, noon, mid-afternoon), so come in between (10am-12pm, 1-3pm). When its packed it's beyond ridiculous.

I always preferred these smoothies over Jamba Juice. For roughly the same price you get a lighter smoothie that's just as tasty. The sandwiches and smoothies are exactly the same as GBC, and their sandwiches are outrageously overpriced.

They also sell Peet's Coffee, and since I don't drink coffee I can't give a review on that. 

There's plenty of places to sit outside of Crossroads for long conversations. The Den accepts cash, credit card and meal points for Cal Students.

Sandwiches take too long to make. The workers seem to talk more than work, and you end up waiting for at least half an hour for a simple sandwich. Then there's the coffee. It's always charcoal tea, and I've had this experience with all Peet's coffee. It's one thing to roast coffee beans. It's another thing to turn them to charcoal. Peet's coffee is just harsh.

Ridiculous lines, especially in the morning. The whole system of calling out "NEXT!" is terribly inefficient and I've found myself waiting 15 minutes to pay for my $1 apple.

There's also a clusterf--- inconveniently by the only entrance/exit of people waiting for their order to be called. 

The sandwiches are hefty but not usually delicious. 

On the plus side, there are a few cashiers who are terribly warm and welcoming and generally can brighten your morning (which was previously sabotaged by the aforementioned ridiculous line)

Their latte sucks. I tried it once or twice but they failed it horribly and since then, I don't go there. A wait is long, too. Their primary customers are college kids who need to use up their meal plan points. No wonder they have no incentive to improve.

Just a quick grab-and-go spot for cafe drinks, smoothies, sandwiches, ice cream, and soft drinks. Okay, maybe I was a bit too lenient on the "quick" part in the previous sentence. If there is a line, count on being in The Den for at least 10 minutes. The sandwich and Peet's Coffee queue is never a good thing. The Freshens smoothies are probably the fastest if you are in need of something good. Don't forget to ask for your boost! I am not a fan of soda but Coca-Cola company is available (Odwalla included). The grab-and-go sandwiches and sushi are catered by local businesses: Panini Time and Slippery Fish. The sushi really isn't the best, especially for $4+. The sandwiches are ok. There is occasionally fresh strawberries for $5 which are pretty good. The made-to-order sandwiches will take a while but I lived on those for many nights during my sophomore year. My sandwiches were always about $10 since I kept adding meats, guacamole, cheeses, etc. I wish there was a Freshens frozen yogurt stand inside or outside (maybe in the future).

probably the worst Peet's coffee I've ever been to, but I think it's because it's kinda like the watered down, budget-cut affected, UC Berkeley version of Peet's. probably the only thing keeping me from giving this place one star is my undying loyalty t Peets coffee and all things associated with Peets coffee. I mean don't get me wrong, the coffee itself is still good (not burnt like starbucks or too mild like coffee bean), and the drip coffee is always flavourful, but there are just a lot of little things that make this location not satisfactory
- first of all, their pastry selection is crap; pastries are my life, they are like a food group in my diet, a substantial part of my subsistence comes from them, and the pastries here are just not up to par. first of all, their pastry case is like 1/8 the size of a regular Peet's coffee pastry case, which means less selection. second of all they seem to run out of non-dessert pastries (such as croissants and muffins and bagels) long before noon, and after noon, all they have is cakes and cookie. I myself always prefer scones, muffins, or bagels..........I don't really like super-sweet toffee bars or chocolate cakes, which is what they offer most of the time **however, they do normally have free pastry samples, this does not make up for their terribly disappointing pastry selection, but it is something good to know**
- the wait is always farrrr tooo long! i think it's because people also order stuff from the sandwich bar located in the den from the Peet's counter, so that makes the line long, but the wait to get your drink once you've ordered is also long
- this brings to my third point, i believe that part of the reason that the wait for drinks is so long is poorly trained staff and also understaffing; a lot of the time it is students working there, and it is possible that I am just extra-harsh because i know a student is making my espresso, but i feel like the espresso and the lattes I get here are never as good as at a regular Peets coffee (although they're still not bad by any means), and they have gotten my order wrong a few times
- finally, there is pretty much no seating inside this Peets, so if you were looking for a nice, quiet Peet's coffee to study at.....then this is NOT IT!!

I should emphasize though, that my rating is relatively harsh, and it is a rating based on comparisons to other Peet's coffees in the area. this place still makes good fraps and lattes, and coffee drinks, just not up to par with most other Peet's locations, but if you need a coffee, and it's between here and somewhere else, just go here
it's peets.........it's always gonna be good, no matter how bad

I've tried all the seasonal specials, with the exception of the eggnog latte. Their drinks are served rather sweet, so taste before adding sugar. Overall, good coffee for the price, and a wonderful place to spend excess meal points. If you're paying cash though, I would suggest a different peet's location as this one can get messy/crowded.

I came to this Peet's when I was living in the dorms. The drinks were never the way I wanted them to be. My hot drinks always had too much milk or too little. My blended drinks always too sweet. But who cares when you can pay with your meal plan, right? Seriously that was the best thing ever. I really enjoyed the sandwiches here too. They've never messed up an order before, but this one time, I accidentally took someone else's sandwich. We had the same name! Oops! Good thing she ordered a good sandwich ha!

peets has okay coffee, but i would say your best bet: 

white chocolate mocha iced coffee with soy milk. 

they sell baked goods (cookies, macaroons, etc) and across from the coffee bar place is the den. this is where you can order a sandwich for under $5 (hummus, turkey, etc). they sell kettle chips, odwalla juices, some panini time products (pre-made sandwiches), haagen daz, coke, vitamin water, etc. sometimes they are super slow with orders and mess up it up half the time, but the people who work there are crazy funny. one of them likes to call me her beautiful pumpkin.

Alright, this is the 3rd Peet's that I've reviewed.. there's quite a few of them in Berkeley. So, this one I used to go all the time when I was still living in the dorms and could just use my student ID card and swipe for coffee or whatever else. So, it felt like it was free coffee all the time. I also liked the older man who worked at the cashier -- never knew his name, but he was super friendly and remembered my orders.. I became a usual. :o)

So, 4 stars only b/c I swiped my dining points here; I wouldn't come here to order drinks and expect to sit and chat. This place is mostly for Cal students living in dorms and ordering drinks to go.

I give this place a 4 because of the amazing customer customer. Every single Peets taste the same but the customer service always varies. The people here just really know how to brighten up your day. There's Ahmed who's just so sweet and always ask about you. He knows me by face so he always give me some extra pastries and always make sure I have a good breakfast. There Lamaar who is just hilarious and always brighten your mood by making jokes! There's also a lady who tells you you're beautiful to almost every person. You seriously can't get better customer service than this.

As for the coffee, it's not bad. I always get the Caramel Latte or White Mocha. The quality is consistent every time. The Green Tea Frapp is one of my favorite drink. Can't go wrong with this one if you need something refreshing to drink in the summer. The lines for this place is ridiculous in the morning because it's next to Crossroads so I wouldn't recommend it if you're in a hurry for class.

My frapps are never perfect, but for a college student with meal points galore, who cares? 

And I must say I love the people, who work here. They're so adorable, funny, and really try to make your drink the way you want it to be.

The coffee here is stronger then start bucks. There is a huge homeless population who goes here. I have been here a few times and one time a homeless man offered me some of his nuts. He had a can of mixed salted nuts and was trying to give me some. It was really random to eat someone else nuts. I'm not use to guys offering me their nuts. That sounds like something one of my questionable friends would take.

Best Slice of Pizza in the Bay Area!  
All you Blondies fans don't know what you're missing!

How could I forget to write about this place?  I love, love their veggie pizza.  I would always stop here before or after my LSAT classes to get a slice.  Just a warning they do charge you an extra .25 for that to-go box!
decent pizza. i like their fluffy crust. large slicees..or should i say, FAT slices. i'm so funny

I gave this place three or four chances. It's not even fine or good for the value. Every time I eat here, the crust gets stuck in my throat because it's only semi-cooked and way too thick for human digestion. The cheese is decent, which is why this doesn't have only one star. Sometimes I really just like some cheap, greasy pizza, and their cheese satisfies that much. But I cannot get past the crust, which is deplorable.

Who knew someone could name their restaurant after something they serve! I mean... there are no Dominoes @ Dominoes, and all the tables are square at my local Roundtable!  So let's review the "fat slices" at Fat Slice.

Berkley is a college city...so late night eateries are essential to the starving/partying student.  But don't get me wrong, this establishment is open during daylight hours as well!

The slices are humungous... probably equivalent to a whole small pizza @ your local pizza joint... or 2 slices @ costco... thick too!  I usually get Plain pepperoni... but they have a lot of other toppings like most pizza places.

While the taste is nothing out of the ordinary, the pizzza is far from bland.  The marinara could use a little seasoning, but if you order a lot of salty toppings (which pizza toppings usually are) then you should be just fine!

The only gripe I have, is sometimes the pizza comes out undercooked... not doughy...but if a slice is gonna b that big, id like to have it stand on its own when I pick it up! Pizza is a hands-on type food, I shouldn't need a knife and fork!

Big.... greasy... bready....

So ... for the record, before you read further, realize that this rating of 2 stars is in relation to all pizza known to man... not your typical "telegraph-by-the-slice" pizza vendor, cuz it's not that bad... not called on to be that great... and serves a purpose in any college student who is willing to visit here for a snack.

Yeah... grab your stack of napkins at the same time...  lay it on top to soak up the grease... then recover the toppings with generous portions of the peppers and parmesean... and you might not have to taste the stuff anymore.. it's filling..... for about 5 minutes, but it's cheap enough so that you don't have to care too much.

it is ridiculous how much i love this place. i always watch for the coupon guy on bancroft and telegraph on mondays and tuesdays to take advantage of that red quarter sheet that gets me a slice of pizza and a drink for $2.25.

It kinda gets annoying because you have to deal with a bunch of drunkens fromf blakes next door on wednesday and thursdays... but it is completely worth it! 

not a big fan of the specials because they kinda just sit there all day, but the pepperoni pizza really hits the spot. find out why they call it fat slice...
It's not great pizza--it's just a great option at night. I would have given five stars, but it wouldn't be fair to Cheeseboard to have this place a star away.

Been craving pizza and after passing this place a million times I decided to stop in. I got a cheese slice. 

It isn't the most elegant place. They give you the pizza on a piece of wax paper, which makes it kind of weird if you're not eating it there. Walking past all the homeless carrying a big slice of pizza and what not. That can be forgiven. What gave this place 2 stars is the pizza. Ton of bread and super seasoned sauce. It reminded me a lot of the pizza I used to eat from the school cafeteria when I was a kid. Is it horrible? No. But if I really want pizza I wouldn't go here for it.

Several things are true about Berkeley...there are signs warning you it is a nuclear free zone, it leans left, and it has Fat Slice. I suggest trying a green slice...pesto, spinach and artichoke. Not a thin slice but a light crust and definitely a fat a$$ slice. And watch out for those bears and nuclear attacks. Lol.

Fat Slice is my favorite since:

1.  their slices are fat - i like that they are thick - I cant stand thin pizza. 
2.  THeir vegiie slices have a lot fo vegetables, perphaps not as much as blondies, but blondies has some weak thin dough.
2b  their slices are less greasy than blondies. 
3.  their coupons are great - and easy to reproduce since they are made on cheap paper.

the restroom was very dirty the second to last time i went- the last time i went it had improved and didnt smell much.
The dining room can be nasty looking at times. 
They need to change those posters of Jeffferson Airplane playing at the Fillmore - LOL.

The street kids asking for change while they  sit in front of defunct Berkeley Market dont help either.

I couldn't believe the size of the slices they serve here - they are double the servings of any other pizza joint! Not only do they have hearty portions, but the quality of the pizza is also amazing. I got a veggie slice and it came loaded with tons of every veggie imaginable. I was so full yet still managed to finish the crust because it was that good! they also let you sprinkle your own parmesan, pepper, and rosemary on as much as you want. I'm definitely hooked!

We were kind of leaning towards 4stars, but then we remembered that we used CampusCred at the time we ate here, so we drop it back to 3 (we were thinking 3 in the first place anyway). 

The slices are definitely larger than your usual, but for ~$3 a slice, it's nothing special. 

Melvinsays: I actually decided against pepperoni and towards the veggies one because that slice just looked so unhealthy. I'd probably feel bad if I ate it. 
Johannsays: I went with plain cheese and it tasted like, well, cheese. Oil dripped out of the pizza and down my lip with my first bite so I see where this 'ew, too unhealthy' feeling comes in.

The place is pretty chill, nothing too special again. There are tables in the back and the bathroom needs a key, so don't assume that someone's just been in there for a long time, haha.

Not hating on this place though, but we're not considering being regulars either.
If you're drunk and it's late at night.... Go for it! Just don't over do it. You will regret it soon enough.

$3.42 for a slice of cheese that is all dough, no sauce, no cheese for something that costs them 40 cents (if that). No thanks. To describe their pizza as mediocre would be spotting their pizza points. I shouldn't have to bring in web coupons (search Inside the Good Life dot com for all you need to bring their prices more in line) to pay what I should pay for this low quality crap. Not impressed.
Delicious!

If you want a heart attack or a near-death experience with a mugger...come to Fat Slice. If you want good greasy ginormous slices of pizza....there's a Blondie's less than five minutes walk from here. Seriously the stuff here is just disgusting and the restaurant is a dump service is awful.

I've never actually been mugged outside here but my friend has. One look at this place and I never doubted him. Yes, it's cheap but you get what you pay for and it tastes terrible. There are so many pizzza places around why in god's name would you go here. 

If you're homeless or trying to kick a drug problem this is your place it's very very cheap. Judging by the suspicious paraphernalia I found in the bathroom you wouldn't be the first.

Dirty.  Fast.  And I'm always praying they give me the slice with more pepperonis on top.  The pesto pizza is nice but usually requires a slight wait.

It's pretty cheap for what you get, especially if you use one of the discount coupons ($1 pizza!) they sometimes hand out by Sproul Plaza, or from newspapers and other things Berkeley students get.

I used to eat here 8 years ago. The slices have not gotten any bigger, but they doubled in price. At this rate, since they've been open since before 1970, the slices will be $4.00 each in 2012 (and for just 1 dollar more you could get a whole pizza at Golden Gate pizza on San Pablo and 61st).

One of the landmarks on Telegraph street --- Pizza Shops

Go to fat slice if you are craving a classic pizza --- cheese, pepperoni, or veggie. Like all the reviews will tell you, the live up to their name. 

Go to Blondies if you crave pizza other than cheese and pepperoni because they have great daily specials for around $3 (i.e. pesto chicken, margherita, etc) 

If you are in Berkeley and do not mind driving down Shattuck then...

GO TO CHEESEBOARD!

Having frequented this place almost weekly while in college, I am disappointed with how they treat their customers lately.  A couple of years back, upon asking if I can place an order, they said only for whole pizzas and hung up on me before I could even respond.  

Deciding to give them another chance, I went back yesterday only to have them charge me for 2 pizza and drink combos (over $9) vs. 2 slices of pizza which should be under $7.  I'm not sure if it's because he doesn't speak or understand English but when I asked three times why I only got 10.80 in change from my $20 for something that is $3.20 a piece, he gave me a blank stare.  Eventually he pointed to the receipt which clearly states cheese drink.  When I explained he charged me for a drink combo per the receipt, he crumples the receipt and threw it into the garbage to get rid of the evidence.  I told him I didn't want the drink, just the pizza so please give me the correct change.  He opens the register, gives me only $1 vs. the $2 back and walked away all without speaking to me.  Unfortunately there was no one else around to speak with and I left completely frustrated at the whole experience.  If it is due to a lack of communication, I would highly advise management not to have someone who cannot speak the language work the register or interact with customers as it left a bad taste in my mouth and no reason to return again or recommend to others.

Here's a glimpse into my uninspiring youth on most Saturday afternoons:  Go to Telegraph, grab a veggie slice from Fat Slice, soak up as much grease as possible with napkins, and head out to the sidewalk to scarf it down while doing some people watching.
Big slices, very thick, but it's got kind of a simple taste, kind of bland, no real pepp to it. The price is alright and the food is fresh, but for better taste try zachary's or jupiters
Yum, yum yum. Three topping pineapple, jalopeno,and Canadian bacon sooooooo good!

This place used to be really great when I was younger, but I guess now that I'm grown up, it ain't so golden anymore.

The sauce on the pizza tastes very bitter...like it's spoiled or something on the sort. I've noticed this taste the last couple times I've visited. The decor needs some work. I mean, I don't expect MUCH from a pizzeria nowadays, but I would definitely expect more from an institution that has stood the test of time like Fat Slice (my first visit here was about 11 years ago).

There is better to be had, so search it out...down the street.

If you're drunk, starving and it's 1:30am, then you'll probably appreciate Fat Slice.

Otherwise, , , , not so much!

not the best pizza in the world, but it sure is a deal.  i came here after the cal/ucla game yesterday to drown my sorrows, and i found fat slice to hit the spot.  a gigantic slice of veggie pizza and a soda for $3.35!  i need to hang out in berkeley more!

The pizza is unbelievably greasy and doesn't really taste that great to begin with. But it's cheap as hell (although not quite as cheap as wherever Asher Roth went to school) and it saved my ass a few times when I've woken up late and needed to get some food in me before class or whatever. I haven't gone back since freshman year, but if you haven't gone there at least once in your time here, it might be worth checking out. Just make sure to get extra napkins to soak up the oil that settles on top of your pizza (seriously). On second thought, only go if you are starving or broke.

Great great place! I love the pizza even though it's not the best. Sometimes one wants pizza thats greasy. Check out my review of cheap Berkeley eats:
http://www.examiner.com/x-7424-Alameda-County-Headlines-Examiner~y2009m4d11-Five-Great-Eats-for-Cheap-around-Berkeley

one of my favorite pizza places in berkeley! it's cheap and you get a lot!!! service always sucks here and the place to eat it in is pretty divey but i love going here. good memories and good pizza! make sure you get the pepperoni! that's it!
Quintessential college food... quick, cheap, and greasy... but questionable with respect to cleanliness. Not my favorite slice of pizza in Berkeley.

It is what it says it is. The slices are huge, but the prices are very reasonable. I ordered a veggie slice and a medium Mountain Dew and it came out to be $4.25. The pizza is really good too, even if it is anything but healthy. In reality, the place is about a 3.5, but Yelp won't allow half stars. I'd recommend it for a quick, inexpensive, and filling meal.

Fat Slice ain't the best pizza on earth, but it's cheap as f*** and reasonably tasty.

When you're only laying down around $4 for an ENORMOUS veggie slice (2 slices anyplace else) and a soda, what the hell do you expect? This isn't gourmet food, it's budget dining, and for that it's more than adequate.

I'd give the place 5 stars but the seating and bathroom here are hella grody. Totally puke-tronic. For real.
great pizza for late night after drinking food. this no gourmet pizza, but good size and decent quality

Welcome to Cal.  

Fat Slice is a fantastic deal, and they take competitor's coupons.  The slices are huge and very filling.

Flash your id on your bday and get a free slice.

Downside - they charge an extra $.50 if you want a box for a to go order.

Wow, not sure why I haven't written a review on this place yet. After all, i've only been eating here since 1997. Yowza. Well then, it's time for a good old fashioned interview then, isn't it? Let do this.

When I first went to Berkeley, I was super young. Like I mentioned above, it was 1997, so that would have made me about 16 at the time. My friends were budding DJs, so they were combing the selections of wax at Rasputin's and Amoeba. Meanwhile, I would sort of just be standing around, not really knowing what to do. At that age, I didn't have a whole lot of money, not even allowance (we were a family of pretty meager means.) I did have some change scrounged up though. With that in mind, I eventually got hungry. So I traversed the streets there for just a bit, finally running into Fat Slice. The smell of fresh baked dough and toppings were in the air and boy was it ever tempting. I peeked in to look at the prices and saw how cheap the slices were! I ordered a slice of pepperoni, paid, and then was immediately shocked as to how FAT the slice really was. It was the biggest I had seen before then. As I scarfed it down, I was in food heaven. It immediately opened my eyes to the fact that there was really good food out there.

All of that being said, this place is just as good as the when I first had it. It's not the most fanciest of pizzas out there, but it's one of the best tasting, that's for sure. You get a big ol' slice of pizza here on the cheap. There's some toppings you can choose from, but don't expect something all out there like this was CPK or something. This place has all the standards, and when it comes to pizza, I feel it's important you do the standards strongly. This place does for sure. It might be a bit ghetto/hood for some people, but that's part of the charm. Service here is fast and friendly, so no need to fret. Oh, another bonus: you can have dessert a few feet away at CREAM!

Fat Slice is always going to be one of those places that I am going to go to whenever i'm in Berkeley. It's that good.

The daily special of hot sausage and bacon pizza sounded pretty good, I grabbed a slice and it was okay. I got some spice out of the hot sausage, but it was lacking in flavor. Their pepperoni is definitely a lot better.  

There is a strong smell of Windex around the tables in the back.  I would usually excuse this smell and think maybe they had just cleaned something up, but the last time I was there in college --  six years ago -- I also came across that strong smell of Windex. So I'm thinking it might be a permanent smell.

I scarfed down my pizza, which lives up to it's name -- itt is definitely a fat slice, and one is enough to fill me up. Its flavor is the classic pepperoni that I often crave -- very satisfying, with a bready, thick crust. The slice is topped with cheese, pepperoni and grease, just how I like it! 

Fat Slice would do better if they put more cheese near the crust area, otherwise, when the cheese is all gone, it's like eating a bland piece of fluffy bread. Fat Slice should also get creative and serve each slice with a ball of garlic butter to spread along the crust. That way instead of the crust being thrown (which I willing to bet, it often is), it will be eaten.

I'll still be going back to Fat Slice on football game days.. when Memorial Stadium opens up again next year.
I've been going to this place for years! The price has definitely gone up since I was 10 but still great big fat hunks of pizza and definitely delish!! There's no chairs so it's best to get to-go.
better than blondies, in my opinion. fat slice literally gives you a FAT slice of pizza. its huge, but so good :) i'd like to try other pizza places in berk though

Fat slice is a nice complement to nearby Blondie's because the pizza is also very good, but  a litle different.     I thought about suing these two establishments because I put on a few pounds from eating pizza there every day ...
(KIDDING!)

Greasy pizza, but cheap. They have your typical slices, pepperoni, cheese and veggie. Quick service, pizza served on the spot...no waiting. More like food for people who are on the go. Open late til 2am everyday. A spot for the late night people who are hungry and want to get a quick bite to eat...clubbers and smokers most definitely try it.

Went there today and had the pepperoni, mushroom, and olive combo - I'm still dreaming of the taste. Just not the ambience... the dining area in back could use some serious sprucing up!

$3.25 a slice (came out to about $3.50), and my friend ordered two that he couldn't finish.  The slices lived up to their name.  I've been by here so many times and now I won't be able to ignore it anymore... in my personal opinion, I think it's better than Blondie's (just down the street with comparable prices).  Fat Slice just has a better taste and the crust is lighter, more doughy, not to mention tasty! :)

It'd normally get 5 stars, but when we arrived initially, we both got excited seeing the PESTO ARTICHOKE HAM special sign (yes!!)... only to order the special and have the cashier go "Oh, is that still up there? Sorry, that's from yesterday." Dang, way to lead a girl on.  I was pretty let down, but I was definitely glad to have gotten the REAL special for the day.  I seriously ate every bit.

I'll be back, soon as I round up $3.50 for another fat bite.

For a cheap fill me up I'm starving slice, 5 stars. In the 80's everyone was bragging about blondie's pizza. And i went there with my friends a lot. But being a pizza freak i had to try the" Fat Slice" and I never went back. Except last year when me and my son did the Blondie's / Fat Slice challenge. My son also picked Fat Slice. Blondie's is the out of towner trendy place to go.
The pizza is kinda bland. The only thing robust is the bleach odor in the seating area. At least their pizza must be clean. Or, bleached.

Fat Slice is better than Blondie's, but it's still pizza with the uber thick bread-like crust that I cannot endorse.  They do load up the veggie slice with a garden variety of vegetables, in which case it makes perfect sense to have a 1/2 inch crust.

Guys working were totally indifferent food was pretty good better when it's hot and fresh not so good after it gets cold. Would come back if in the area and wanted some pizza. Hard to miss on telegraph. Small business and kinda dirty looking...
Been eating here since I moved to Berkeley and while it's not the healthiest snack, it's pretty damn good.

yumyumyumm. Slices really are big but very doughy. I had the vegetarian and it was deeelicious but I don't think there was enough sauce. Maybe it's just me, because I like my pizza with tons of sauce :D but it was still really good and cheap (3.90 with a soda). The place is dirty though...tables weren't cleaned off and they need to mop the floors.

Decent enough pizza when it's 11pm on Sunday night, there's nothing else open and you're starving. Portion size is great for the price, but I've had much better before. Sbarro pizza is practically gourmet compared to pizzas at Fat Slice.

Came in here for a quick bite on a monday evening. I got a fat combo, and it is a giant piece of pizza with all the toppings you can think of. It was huge, and I got a sugar free rockstar with it. It was about 5 minute wait time and it wasn't bad. Moderately priced, but the place could use some sprucing up. It seems like it's been beat up pretty badly. The tables were dirty and grimey, but the service was nice and friendly.
Tasty, addictive, and probably really terrible for you.
