Three stars because of the quality but I truly do like this place.  OH and they have 2 dollar Coronas..holla!

Different strokes for different folks. I get it. Some people like their pizza NY style. Others like theirs loaded with goodies. Personally, I like mine fatty and filling (my food mantra, really).. but I truly dislike Fat Slice's brand of fatty and filling. My pepperoni slice was all tasteless bread, cheap cheese, grease and no sauce or flavor to speak of. And let's not even discuss the disruptive bowel movements that followed my lunch here. Not worth saving a few dollars when you have other cheap options on Telegraph.

Also: janky as hell. I love me a grungy place, but the food's gotta be good, ya dig?

What has happened to the pizza. I am a long time regular to FS. Never liked Blondies until the last time I went to Berk. Past two visits to FatS have been awful. So bad I got my money back for last trip(had to practically argue with the guy for a refund) pizza was like greasy foam Bread. I only get the veggie slice, so there isnt an excuse for all the oil and off taste. Hard to ruin Pizza, but FatS has done a fine job  If I could vote a middle finger I would have
Sometimes competition actually makes things worse.  Like Blondie's sucks, so Fat Slice can suck just across the street.

Low quality pizza.  Staff doesn't seem happy. Worst pizza for the price in Berkeley. Explanation: 1 moderate sized slice of pepperoni pizza is $4.74.  Soda purchase with pizza is apparently required.  This may have been a trick by the staff.  I didn't ask for the soda, told them i didn't want it, and left it on the counter.  No refund offered.

Ranking of pizzas by quality in Berkeley:
Tier 1: Cheese Board $$, Zachary's $$
Tier 2: Lanesplitters $, Arinellis $, Bobby G's $
Teir 3: [blank]
Tier 4: Blondie's $, LeVal's $
Tier 5: West Coast $, Pepe's $, Fat Slice $$

I'm giving this 5 stars for no reason other than I hate Blondies so much.

The pizza here is about the same as Blondies up the street, but the people working here aren't as dumb and inept.

Fat Slice....it will fill you up and it's not Blondies.

Go Fat Slice.

Go to Blondie's. The pizza dough they use here is chewy with weird texture as if they used SO much oil the bread molecules didn't get a chance to bond. So I feel.

The sole appeal is the shear amount of pizza they give you for $3. They give you a ginormous slice. Like epic big. (Well Costco pieces are bigger..) So only go here if you're dying of hunger and only have $4 on ya. Otherwise, do. not. try. this. place.

Cheap, fat, doughy pizza. It's not going to change the world but if you're hungry and in the neighborhood, it's worth seeking out. 

There's a nice East Coast vibe to eating your food standing up at a the counters that run along the wall. Plenty of parmesan and red pepper.

This use to be my favorite place to get a nice fluffy fresh slice of pizza and I'm not saying the quality of the food has changed but the restaurant it self is discusting. The tables are always nasty, and to top it off their was rat poop in the bathroom and on the top counter where they keep the fan. Yuck can you imagine the discust I felt after eating a slice of pizza and going to wash my hands and seeing that, then my cousin turns around and spots lots of it on the counter.....Wow they need a health inspection FAST!!!!

Fat Slice always seemed like a healther alternative to Blondie's.  Their vegetarian slices were pretty darn tasty.  The layout was bad but they had more seating.  In my opinion, they probably had a lot faster service as well.

Greasy, greasy pizza.

But oh so delicious and the slices are indeed "fat".

A slice of pesto pizza and a soda for under $5.

Grab a bunch of napkins, so you can mop up the grease on the tables and your face.

Greasy and like the name of the place, "fat slice".  Greasy + Fat Slice = Typical college food. 
This place will always bring back college memories.  
To Fall Out Boy's "Thanks for the Memories":
"One night and one more time. 
Thanks for the memories. 
Thanks for the memories. 
Pizza taste so greasy but bigger."

On our way to the Conga Lounge last Friday, we decided to stop in at Fat Slice. If you don't know of it, the Conga Lounge makes a scorpion bowl that might as well be named the tropical roofie.  I thought it might be a good idea to eat prior to taking a drink of something designed to hit me over the head like a sledgehammer.  

As far as truth in advertising, it is indeed a fat slice.  I got the pepperoni, and it was good,  but not great.  It had puffy, bready crust, which isn't my favorite. The sauce was fine and there was lots of cheese. It was greasy in a good way, but not disgusting. The tables, chairs and floor were very disgusting, though. Based on what they allowed in the dining area, I didn't dare go to the bathroom here - I have a feeling I might never recover from the horror.

In the interest of research I then went to Blondies one block over and got a slice.  As far as I'm concerned Blondies won, but if it wasn't around, I would go to Fat Slice before I hit Arinells or Xtreme Pizza.   

Whether you go with Fat Slice or Blondies, I highly recommend the two slice strategy prior to a night of scorpion bowls as it soaks up just the right amount of alcohol. You will still get buzzed enough to dance like an idiot, but not so drunk that you miss the "STD " in flashing lights on Rico Suave's forehead.  Thanks, Fat Slice!

The student population at Berkeley can be divided in half quite easily - patrons of Blondies or patrons of Fat Slice.  I was a Fat Slice boy, since well, the name is better.  It's FAT slice.  And Fat is the new orange.  In fact, Fat is so cool, I had to make a top ten list.

Ed M.'s Top Ten Reasons Why Fat is Cool. 
 
10. You can describe so many things as "fatty." (i.e. a fatty j, a fatty shit, a fatty burp) You can't describe many things as "thinny."  
 
9. Fat Albert exists. Skinny Albert does not.  
 
8. If you're really really really fat, you could probably hide something really cool between your fat rolls. Like a sandwich! Mmmmm, sammiches...  
 
7. Fat makes great soap (see Fight Club).  
 
6. Fat people get to have the arm flappies. How cool would it be to have HUGE ASS arm flappies! Like arm flappies down to the ground! Dude, you could probably cradle a baby in your own fat! Skinny people do not have that option.  
 
5. There are tons of "Yo mama so fat" jokes, but there are NO "Yo mama so skinny" jokes.  
 
4. Dude, how funny is a really excessively fat dog? Puahahahaha!  
 
3. Fat and fart have only one letter difference. And honestly, who doesn't love a good fart?  
 
2. Fat old people are way way nicer than skinny old people. And I bet you the fat old people could totally beat up the skinny old people too.  
 
1. I bet you God is fat.
I now like fat slice better than blondies. Especially love it when they are handing out coupons for $1 or $2 slices. I always get the pepperoni.

This pizza is HELLA good! Hot, Fresh, plenty of toppings, very cheesy, and great portions! Can't go wrong if you need a slice or two to get your pizza fix! Pesto and veggie slices are also good if you want to break away from your more typical toppings.

The place to go when you want a really unhealthy oily huge slice of pepperoni pizza. For my own health's sake I don't go here often but it hits the spot when you want something bad for you every once in a while.

I was never that big of a fan of Blondie's, thus Fat Slice, after La Val's, was my goto pizza place.  Since La Val's shut down, I've been forced to narrow my choice.  I've enjoyed the slice size and crust here in the past...it's usually crispy, yet a little chewy.  I typically prefer a combo slice, but I opted for what was available at that moment, which was a veggie slice.  The slice I had was somewhat luke warm.  I suppose I could've asked them to warm it up in the oven, but that would delay me from my feeding schedule.  I dunno if it was too early or what, but there weren't any lines, which meant the pizza was probably sitting around for a while.  Maybe I need to go back to ordering combos.

Oh, Fat Slice. It was late, I was drunk, and you provided me with a slice of veggie pizza which I ate with glee. It absorbed the booze in my tummy, and tasted great to boot. I'm sure anything would have tasted great at the time, but you had something extra. I'm sure of it.

Conjures up nostalgic feelings of when I was a little one, and being amazed by how the pizza guy tosses the dough in the air with utter finesse. I thought maybe I wanna do that when I grow up! If I have a taste for pizza I'll choose Fat Slice over Blondie's any day, though Fat's menu is much more streamlined serving just pizza. 
You may want to get your pizza to go as the stark atmosphere is not that conducive to enjoying a meal. Really delicious pizza!

3.5 Stars...

This pizza is also good after a night of drunken debauchery...and I think they stay open 30 minutes later than Blondies...

The pizza is good...dough is soft...very cheesy (again, adding MORE cheese to ANYTHING makes it better!!) and the sauce is cool.  I would recommend this place as well.  I wish they had beef (or turkey) pepperoni like blondies does....ahhhh such is life.

I remember one night having a Pizza taste-off...buying a slice from both Fat Slice and Blondies...but I don't remember the outcome...(probably too much aforementioned debauchery) but lo! I will do it again and report back.

Signing off!
The Veggie Slice with a Pepsi is the Truth!

Didn't expect to like this place at all.  And my review should be taken with a grain of salt, because I only eat the crust of pizzas....but Fat Slice has some seriously delicious crust.  Hated the wait.

When working in Europe I had an Italian colleague who rhapsodized about...

You guessed it: Fat Slice.

He knew it wasn't really pizza like anything he had ever had.  But he really did like it.  And heck, for the price, and being close to campus, I understand.

It's not great pizza, but the crust is crisp and puffy. 

And most importantly, it's better than Blondies.
My favorite pizza spot!

If you like stringy cheese that keeps stretching and stretching then this is the place to go to.  The crust is crispy even though this isn't a thin crust type of pizza place.  So far I've only had a 2 topping slice of the italian sausage and mushrooms.  The sausage is thinly sliced which makes it light and easy to chew as opposed to chunks of sausage.  When you order a slice of pizza with toppings that aren't already displayed or made they simply take a slice of cheese and pile the toppings on top with more cheese and stick it in the oven.  A 2 topping slice of pizza and a small soda cost me $5.10.

They have seating available inside.  There tends to be bums hanging out outside and there is an odd stench lingering inside the restaurant similar to the smell of cheese but not in a good way...

But aside from the environment they do serve up a decent slice of pizza.

Ahhh...Fat Slice.  It's so bad for you and yet...you can't say no to the suggestion.  Of course, said suggestion usually comes after a round of drinking and pot smoking but nevertheless Fat Slice won't let you down.  What sucks about it is the thugs that hang out around it and infect it with a pervading sense of shadiness.  You're not sure if you're going to make it safely back home after eating your pizza.  I like living on the edge, but not when I'm getting a slice of mediocre pie.

My cousin recommended this place as soon as I got off the plane at Oakland airport.  It was about a 15 minute drive from OAK to Berkeley.

11:00pm and no line, so I got two slices, veggie slice, and a pepperoni slice... and I manhandled those bad boys.  Yeah they were big and had alot of ingredients on the veggie slice, but they closed off the sit-down section. =\ They close at 12:30am that night.  Keep in mind that we were there at 11pm.  I asked for a refill on my drink, she said "50 cents." I said ok. Then she goes, "you don't have to, what are you drinking?" Thanks for not charging me lady! I mean, I only tipped you in that jar ya got!

As I was moving on to my next and final slice, a line started forming. And they got a mini rush.  There's also alot of bums just hangin out in front so be prepared to give them some spare change... or not.

Stopped in after flying in to SFO, we were hella hungry and trying to find a place to get a bite to eat.

Sister in-law suggests this place after our first restaurant choice was almost ready to close for the night, so we have no other option but to settle for Fat Slice.

Fat Slices, yes, but nothing really outstanding about the taste or quality.
They didn't even warm up our slices like most places do-room temperature pizza? No Bueno! 

Okay, but not all that....ALOHA!!!

I can really only say.......MMMMMMMMMM. oh yeah that place can bring out the fat kid in anyone!! cheese or just pepperoni will do it for me! i like the excellent and fast service.....oooooh yeah. lol The only frustrating thing is when it gets packed because the place is super tiny, its hard to get over to those delicious toppings like the parm and red pepper...:(  yum yum yum though is all I can really say!!

If I had a penis, I would call it "Fat Slice". 

I used to go to Fat Slice almost everyday back when I went to Cal ... those were the days.  Breakfast at Noahs, lunch at Fat Slice.  While to some, having to blot your pizza before eating it might be gross, you get over it when you're a college student ... or when what lies beneath, is just that good.  My staple was usually the slice and drink combo.  Slice of Pepperoni pizza + Dr. Pepper - wow, talk about waxxing nostalgic.

Haven't been there in a while ... but last time I was back in my hood (and no longer a college student selling platelets for money), I rolled up in my stretched Humvee (okay, it was a rental for a birthday) - we called ahead, ordered 10 large pizzas - did a drive by and then went up to the hills to watch the sunset.  Slice of fat slice, Dr Pepper, good friends watching the fog roll in ... good times.

I usually like only pepperoni pizza so I am not sure how bias my review might be. I went here for the first time last night, my step brother really like this place and so did everyone else it seemed since the line was way out the door by the time we arrived.

There was a really interesting guy in line who at first seemed really weird but as he talked more started to get into sports and how Cal was doing in football. He ended up amusing us enough while we waited in the long line. 

So after that I got up to the front as was lucky they brought out a fresh pepperoni pizza, the pizza slice was nice and large and the price for that and a regular soda wasn't all that bad. I think it was under $5 for me. 

Inside the place is nothing amazing, pretty bare bones. Just some tables and counter tops that you can eat at. We sat down and ate for around 10 minutes, at least they offered some sort of seating inside the place. 

Overall the pizza was pretty good, I wouldn't say it has the best ingredients ever made but it tasted well enough for the price and I enjoyed my strange time enough in line and inside that I would go back if I am ever in Berkley again.

This is so cool reading the reviews for Fat Slice...all of the positive reviews seem to mention the jokeman! It's funny because when i think of Fat Slice i think of the jokeman too. He knows all sorts of jokes and they're all pretty damn funny! I'm sure this guy makes a pretty decent amount of money. OK now onto the pizza place known as Fat Slice...

The pizza is just way better than than Blondie's IMO. The crust is thicker leading to a more fulfilling experience both in taste and in alleviating hunger pangs. The pepperoni actual has some sort of flavor. Lastly it is cheaper than Blondie's! The pizza at Fat Slice is quite good, but not quite good enough for the 5th star.
this is the best hole in the wall pizza joint you will ever find. excellent pizza it puts blondies pizza to shame. a must go to place. it's located in the uc berkley area. in a nice area.

Its sure as hell not gourmet, but its cheap and filling.  Think of it as comfort food.  Nothing as satisfying as a good veggie slice after hours of browsing on telegraph.  Be warned, its a bit...dirty on the inside, but dont let that discourage you.

Pizza was great, root beer was cold. What more could I want? Stopped in late night with a friend last week and grabbed a slice of the veggie pizza and a drink - super cheap and more than filling. 

Really nice toppings and crust - made for the perfect little meal. Will definitely check it out if I find myself in Berkeley again.

Ok,  This one really does live up to it's name.  These slices are F A T.  Sometimes they've been sitting under the heat lamp a little too long.  But do what I do...Ask for a new slice.  They'll make you a brand new pizza on the spot, and by the time it comes out, you've been smelling pizza long enough to eat a whole one alone.  

    It's like the commercials.  Imagine pizza that really does string along the cheese like it's hanging on for it's life when it's sliced and picked up.  There is that much.  Also, if you don't like going with the crowd, try their vegetarian.  It's surprisingly good.  

    Mind you, they're about 8,000,000,000 calories.  But trust me, your mouth will thank you.  Just not your thighs.  Oh, and gut if you get a beer with it.

Every trip to Berkley comes with a stop at Fat Slice. There pizza is so yummy and at a great price. The place looks run down, but come on people its Berkley. When I'm walking up, or down telegraph (guess it depends on where my car found a home) The aroma moves up and down the streets and I always find my way to this place. When I think of Pizza in the bay this is what I think of first.
I never knew how good pizza could be until I came here. Shoot, I didn't even LIKE pizza, but this place changed my whole outlook. And, it's affordable! Woo hoo!

I love fat slice.

always get the veggie. 

i can only consume one slice -- and that says a lot about the quanity because I EAT.

i love the peope who work there, they are all nice and efficent. :]

the only thing i dislike is i feel really dirty sitting at their tables. I mean i feel like im eating in a bath room where homeless come to pee on the walls. 

If it was cleaner I would definately add stars.

What I like here are the pesto slices. sadly, they didn't have any last night, when I came by after an earlier appointment. The veggie slices, while well-piled with rather fresh veggies, could stand a further infusion of flavor. And the crust, well, not the most interesting texture- and flavor-wise. Other than those points, a good value for a quick pick-me-up.

FAT SLICE FTW!!! a big O fat greasy slice and a soda for $4 bucks cant beat that when your shoppin on Telegraph! Their pizza is always fresh and hot since their always busy and lots of ppl go in and out.  Theres always 3 kinds available pepperoni, cheese, & veggie.  mMMMmM drool*

I only eat here is when I'm too hammered to walk to Shattuck for a real pizza place.

The first time I came, I thought I was getting an entire pizza for $4. But I only received 1 slice, making possibly the worst pizza deal I've ever heard of.

If you need more than 1 slice to be full (aka if you are a guy) you'll probably go broke. One time after coming from Kips I ordered 8 slices for myself and it was like $40. Fortunately they accept credit cards since who carries around $40 in cash?? I recommend Little Caesar's for a superior value. Also, Pepe's pizza now offers slices.

If you eat your pizza at Fat Slice, you have to stand like livestock along this trough on the side wall. I wish Little Caesar's had a similar setup.

Cheap, greasy, and simple. The pizza here isn't necessarily amazing, but it definitely satisfies those late night cravings and/or drunchies. I had to say the crust here is deliciously buttery and flavorful! Definitely the best part of the pizza for sure in my opinion. There's a variety of pizzas to choose from including veggies, pepperoni, cheese, pesto, and the special of the day. 

All in all, a quick and filling late night snack for under $5 (with a drink). Not necessarily the cleanest or nicest place to eat, but hey, the pizza is decent enough to make me come back if I'm ever craving a slice of pizza and am too lazy to walk another block over to Blondie's (which I think is a bit more pricey and greasier - maybe that's a good thing to some of you out there).

A long time staple in the post concert, post drinking. Sober or not, a solid, gigantic, greasy slice of pepperoni on a piece of wax paper right out of the oven, burning the fuck out of your hand and mouth, served by often questionable folks, in a grungy oft overcrowded room, is strangely satisfying. Oh and try not to use the restroom unless you truly have to.

Fat Slice reminds me of the days when my ladies and I would wander down telegraph stopping in all the head shops to see who had the best prices. after a grand day of shopping, what more could a girl ask for than a hot, greasy, cheesy piece of pizza? my favorite!! 
a bit of advice though...NEVER use the bathroom there. just don't.

For just another stop on my way to Memorial Stadium after my Saturday pre-game beer binge, Fat Slice holds a special place in my heart.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: three stars.

Think about the experience. You walk in, still drunk as hell. You order a fat slice of pepperoni, and you receive said slice into your hands, with only a pitiful sheet of parchment that futilely attempts to prevent your hands from being soaked in grease. Fold that slice in half to prevent grease from staining your blue shirt with red, and head on up to Memorial with pizza in hand.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: one star.

The service is very fast, and they display the pizzas that have available in a window counter. Fat Slice is the definition of food on the quick.

THEIR 

SLICES 

GOT 

BIGGER.

Is that possible, you ask? 

Indeed it is my friend. Indeed it is.

This place was not joking when they called it Fat Slice.  The pizza slices are large, fat, and big...all in one.  However, maybe they shoulda called it PHAT SLICE cuz its pretty gosh darn ghetto...but in a good way.  If half your party wants Fat Slice and the other wants Blondie and you as a customer have never had either here's a hint:  

Fat slice will let you walk into their establishment with Blondies.  I have seen this first hand.  

If you like thin crust, piles and piles of toppings go with Blondies.  If you want a slice of cake like pizza with just a basic pepperoni or cheeze go with Blondies.

Sorry my vote goes to Blondies over PHAT SLICE... they give you a plate and they have bigger trash cans at Blondies.  It is was it is, man.

"Fat Slice!"

"But I kinda wanted sushi..."

"Fat Slice!"

"Are you sure you want..."

"FAT...SLICE..."

"All right all right...we're going to Fat Slice."


Little tip, never argue with a your begging doe eyed annoying jerk of a brother when he's hungry.
SO good...I remember when a slice was only $2...yeah, the tables are sticky and do not even venture into the bathroom...but the pizza just can't be beat.  Mmmmm...

"Meh.  I've experienced better."  Couldn't have said it better myself, Yelp!

The interior of this establishment belongs on one of those restaurant emergency shows, it's bad.  Graffiti-laced wobbly chairs do not convey a distinctive mood or style, they just suck.  The peace-loving hippies down at Blondie's are infinitely more inviting.

The pepperoni on my slice tasted like it was manufactured by Boboli.  The sauce had a distinctive bitter-sour taste.  Unique, but that's about as positive I'm gonna get about the sauce.  If you're expecting to eat your pizza off of a plate, dine elsewhere.  In fact, if you want to eat your meal with an resemblance of dignity, dine elsewhere.  I'm not saying that people who eat at Chuck-E-Cheese have more self-respect, but then again.... 

Now, why does Fat Slice get 2 stars instead of 1?  'Cause dinner only cost me 3 bucks, that's why.  Can't beat that.
i like this better than blondie's, but only because it's greasier, fatter, and more likely to clog your arteries in one bite.

Hmm... they were off tonight. I got the last slice of a supreme and it seemed a bit 'aged' sitting there. It was thick and cheesy, but not quite hot enough. Still three stars though, and it would have been four.
The place is open late which is nice but the quality is pretty bad! The store was gross eery dirty, staff unfriendly and hates their job. I vote zacharys any day!
A very integral part of a Berkeley education.  Of the 30,000 students on campus each year, they must have all tried this place at least once.  It's not great pizza (good enough), but it's a staple.
the slices are fat and with lots of cheese...what more can you ask for when you're drunk at 1am stumbling out of blake's or some place else in the area!

Carb and greasy goodness that you need two hands to carry. That's what i'm talkn about. Cheap, fast and fun..

Wear dark clothing and bring wetnaps of your own. Consider yourself WARNED.

The hubster used to go to Cal and takes me here on his Berkeley Food Tour (BFT).  The BFT visits his favorite college food establishments on and around Telegraph Ave.  The tour is best enjoyed with another person, in order to share food items and maximize the number of places to eat!

We generally share a cheese slice and a Pepsi.  The first time I went, I wasn't expecting the slice to be so fat!  The slices are best when fresh from the oven, with a little bit of crushed red pepper.  The crust is flavorful, there isn't too much cheese, and the sauce is tasty.

The pizza isn't the best in the world, but it has nostalgic value, hence the bump from 3 stars to 4 stars.

The shop is literally a hole in the wall, but you don't eat on Telegraph Ave for the ambiance. :)
I LOVE FAT SLICE!!!! Cheap yummy fast... share your leftovers with the bums and their dogs sitting outside.

Knowing I'm suppose to watch what I'm eating....well I DID! I watched my slice of pepperoni dwindle down to the crust...YUM!

poor selection of beer....bud lite and corona?!?! After the cashier heard me say that he decided to give us our sodas on the house! Thanks guy! :)

Of course i'll be back...if in the area and just so happen to get a GREAT park right out front!
Pizza blue balls.

One Fat Slice of Pepperoni Please! LOVE IT! Every time we go to Telegraph, we always save our appetites for this place. You can't go wrong here. Jurrasic in size, always fresh out of the oven, tons of cheese, pepperoni, and tangy tasty sauce atop a thick golden crust. 
Practically stolen for under 3 bucks. I think this place is BETTER than Blondie's or any other pizza by the slice establishment I've been to... Fer Sure!

Another good choice to fill your belly on the late night!  BIg pieces for a good price.  Fast service, nice soft crust, plenty of cheese and toppings.

A good option to Blondies and open late.  I have been going to this place for years and they always serve it up right.  If you want to order a huge pizza pie and you can pick it up, then do it.

Weird, that no one has already mentioned it, but the best piece of pizza here, is this combo, where they combine the veggie pizza and slap a whole lot of meat on top. I forget exactly what it was called, but it was absolutely delicious. This was the perfect dinner, lunch or snack when I was a student. Albeit, I'll forewarn you like the rest of the people here, that slice alone was probably 2k calories.

The GF and I were taking her sister around Berkeley and taking in the sites when I suggested that when you go to Berkeley you got to take in one of the cheap greasy pizza places.  It was between Blondies and Fat Slice and since Fat Slice had more inside seating than Blondies, we decided to go there for lunch.

Fat Slice is one of Berkeley's Cheap Eats Spot.  The place is pretty run down but for less than $3.50 you can get yourself a large slice of pizza and a coke.  So if you're looking for anything remotely close to fine (and personally I would say average is pushing it) this is not it.  This is more about consumer mass amounts of cheap pizza at a very cheap price.

Fat Slice has your typical selections of basically Veggie, Cheese, and Pepperoni Pizza, so if you're looking for California Kitchen, wrong placeand don't even bother coming here - try Extreme Pizza.  The slices are big and very doughy, so if you're looking for thin slice, go to Blondies.  This is California Pizza.  The sauce here is ok and they do a good job topping for the on the Veggie Pizza and the Pepperoni was ok.  Could of had more Pepperoni's but good enough for a quick filler meal.

But the biggest problem with this place is that it is very very dirty.  Normally I would give this place about 3-4 stars, but my GF had to use the bathroom and she basically lost her appetite and wasn't interested in eating anymore.  The bathroom was that gross and looks like it hasn't be either flushed (yes I said flushed) or cleaned for days.  (Thank go for the Pete's Coffee down the street).  She just opened door and wanted to leave this place.

So for causing my GF to lose her will to eat greasy cheap ass pizza -2 stars for Fat Slice and over all the get like 1.5 stars for being a decent cheap eats place that will fill your belly when hungry. (Just don't go to the bathroom!)

Simple Math.

One discount coupon + $2.75 = Fat Slice of Peperoni, Cheese, or Veggie, and fountain drink.

I'm full. Lunch accomplished.

In the mood for a slice while on Telegraph? Here and Blondie's are the places to go! If you want a "Fat Slice" you will find that here, and you get your moneys worth. Nice, quick, and good service here as well.

Yeah, man, every time I am in Berkeley I get a fat slice.  Its almost ludicrus to not have a slice.  One summer I for some reason was given the job of totting people back and forth to the airport and I stopped to get a slice every time on my way back!  A major staple of berkeley for me.  And yeah, if you dont finish your slice, don't throw it away!  Someone or their dog will gladly take it.  Waste not, want not, you know?
Just when I thought noone could mess up pizza.

Blondie's is not better than FAT slice. I love FATslice. It was the first restaurant I ate at in Berkeley. The slices are huge and they have coupons too which means the pizza is only 2 bucks, which doesnt hurt my wallet. The only concern I have is that it is probably the most unhealthy pizza I have ever had. Don't go on 4/20, the line is long.

You walk up to the counter and order your Fat Greasy Slice and its a wrap. Pepperoni slice for $3.29...not bad. I'd go for the combo so you can have a drink to wash it down. 

They charge $.25 for a togo box for your slice, so I recommend using lots of napkins or bring your own tupperware if ya wanna bring it home.
For being take out, this place makes the best vegetarian pizza round. I love it a lot, and I always will!

There is a battle going on down on Telegraph in Berkeley. This battle is not new- it's been going on forever. It's seen storms, tornadoes, floods, campus walkouts- but still it continues. Through hell, fire and brimstone the fight will continue- but you have no choice, you can only choose ONE! So I ask you- WHO's SIDE ARE YOU ON? Fat Slice or Blondies? 

I choose FAT SLICE! I once fought for Blondies but I since defected- I grew older and wiser- I've moved over to the greasier, thicker, and unquestionably fatter slice. Unlike Blondies, there are no album records on the wall for decoration. There is no color coordination. Blondies tries to hard to look nice while Fat Slice says "Screw that." Fat Slice is white walls and graffiti marks, a few concert posters picked up at a yard sale, eye burning neon signs and a huge menu. Fat Slice is the slice you want. For the thousands upon thousands of college kids who frequent Fat Slice-  they'll all tell you- Fat Slice is a thing of beauty. 

If you've never been to Fat Slice, you're missing out on a good time. I beg you to try Fat Slice- and then go home with heartburn.
The place to go when you truly feel like pigging out and clogging your arteries their fullest extent.  Trust me when I say that two slices will put you in happy little constipated cheese coma.  Yum.

I remember coming to Cal thinking what is there to eat here, man!  So what was the buzz I was hearing, "Aww man, it's all about Blondie's!"  Blondie's this, Blondie's that.  I'm like alright, I need to check out this place.    So I go there and it's whatever and I'm not full.  What the heck, I don't get it.  I think it taste like any other pizza I had in So Cal except they have some cool toppings every once in a while.  

So I literally still went there for a year because I didn't know better.  I saw Fat Slice, but never tried it.  No one ever mentioned this place to me and I was always scared to even go in there because of all the thugs there.  Then one day, a friend brought up Fat Slice.  I'm like oh what the mother freaker that place is suppose to be good? Oh heck yeah, better than Blondie`s!

I finally went and I was so pissed!  Not because of the pizza, oh heck no that thing was freakin` delicious.  No no, because I've wasted a YEAR at Blondie's.  I agree with Dianne, you're either with us or NOT!  If there was ever a throw down, I would no doubt stand behind ya, Fat Slice.    

I always get sausage, so good!  You have to wait 5 minutes, but I don't mind  because they add sausage to a cheese slice and put more cheese on it.  Then you get it all warm and toasty...mmmmmm!  Their sausage aren't' those wack balls either.  I hate those.  At fat slice it looks like they shredded it.  So I call it shredded sausage.  I love it like that or when it is crumbly (See NY Pizza).  It may look like crap to you guys, but I love it!

Oh yeah, lately there has been people pass out coupons for a BUCK A SLICE!  I went up to that foo and asked for a stack. hahaha that made my day for sure.  BUT it's only for cheese, veggie, and pepperoni and expires mid April.  Dang it, no sausage for me, but I can't complain for a BUCK! 

Oh course, one star off for every year it takes off my life when I eat there.

Next to Blondie's and Zachary's, this is the best pizza in Berkeley. The pizza is big and greasy, and that's why it's so awesome. I hate it when people complain about pizza being too fat and/or unhealthy. It's PIZZA people! If you want something healthy, then eat a celery stick. Open up your own business on Telegraph called "Fat Celery Stick" and you can serve celery sticks with a side of rice cakes and ice water. 

But if you want to eat big, think slices of tasty pizza while sitting in the sun and people watching on Telegraph, then Fat Slice is your place!

Update 08-03-08: I ate here again for the first time in three of four years, and the pizza is just as good and just as big as I remember it. I had a ridiculously large slice of pepperoni pizza and a pepsi for $3.90. Not a bad deal.

Talk about an old standby.  For a big, fat, greasy slice of pizza at less than $2.00 a pop, do come here.

This place probably contributed to 13.5 of my Freshman 15.  I indulged then, but have been afraid to touch it since.

Like many before,  I was in a drunken stupor on my very first visit here. I really don't remember how I got there, but I do remember sitting at the table, clutching my chair to try and stop the room from spinning out of control. Ha-ha, sit and spin! Once the room started to slow down a bit I took my first bite of a Fat Slice pizza and I had a moment of clarity: awesome greasy goodness! It definitely made me feel a little better and I somehow managed to get back to the house.

I still make a stop every here once in a while when I'm in the area, but never for the restroom!

They are not kidding when they call themselves the FAT SLICE.  The slice that we had was bigger than my face.  A steal for under $3 for the slice.  Tons of cheese, so be warned that it's greasy.  They don't go cheap on ingredients and I like that.  

Minus 1 star for the place smelling like a toilet.  Yuck.

Fatassjuicymuthtruckinpepperonibumppartyinyourgullet. 
My grandma used to always tell me that if I was ever poor and starving that I should get a donut(she also told me to never turn my back to the sea). Her reasoning was that they were filling and cheap. If my grandma were still alive I would take her down to Fat Slice for some real cheapass gut filler.
Cheap and generous-sized slices! Fresh out of the oven, hot, melty, and delicious.

This place has to be the only place I have ever returned to after I have gotten sick eating their food. Years of Blondie's and bland crust had made me yearn for Fat Slice. 

Pizza here really is good enough for me to risk the runs. The pizza here would be better if it was less greasy.

4 stars - for pizza and service.

Explanation -

For $3 bucks you can fill your gut and keep moving.

DO NOT USE THE BATHROOM - Yuckie, yuckie double yuckie!

When I say service, I mean that as soon as you get to the counter, they ask you what the heck you want and the serve it up nice and quick.  No fool, they don't clean up.  No, the tables are nasty and disgusting.  The parmesan cheese, oregeno and garlic are chained to the counter and are monitored by homeless Harry.

But my happy self likes them better than, tomato sauce on cardboard Blondies.

Friday night 11pm drunk, starving, and need something to eat?

Head over here to FAT SLICE get yourself a slice of pesto pizza and your good to go. Once slice is all you need and your dumb full.

I don't really like this area of berkeley but i would drive here through the weirdos to get me a slice of heaven.

5 Stars for FAT SLICE

Greasy Good Pizza.

Need I say more?

Ginormous slices. Perfect guilty pleasure. I'm sure it's even better when drunk.

My only complaint?

Those tables back there are nasty greasy.

First time eating at this legendary Berkeley eatery.

It was delicious!

O Fat Slice, how I love thee!

From infancy (well, maybe not quite infancy, but damned close!), thou hast nourished this young one ever so sufficiently.  Your PHAT slices (oh, I crack myself up) were always a treat to have whence my folks brought them home, and even more so whence we had the inclination to dine there.

So many fond memories.  You're one of only a handful (maybe even less) that have artichoke hearts and garlic on their menu.  For that, I give you a 6th star.

May the Force be with you.

Ah... the eternal Fat Slice vs. Blondies debate. Can't we all just get along? 

They're the two places within walking distance of the dorms late at night, when your stomach is rumbling because of another sucky dining commons meal. I've given the edge to both of these places at different times, but really isn't it all the same slightly thick crust pizza?

Thick pale dough, thick pale cheese. The color in between suggests there is tomato paste present. Is it really pizza? 

This is a college town, and some need ballast to stay upright. Hello, Fat Slice.

Worse than Blondie's.  The only reason they stay in business is that people are too drunk to walk all the way down to Blondie's.  This place's only redeeming quality is that it's a good place to watch people.

The eternal battle: Fat Slice vs Blondies. 

College eating is about bang for your buck, and the thick slices at Fat Slice are about twice the weight of the thinner stuff you get at Blondies. 

When you take that first bite into a Fat Slice pizza, and that orange grease runs down your forearm....yeeee ...Get it, girl.....

We had thought this place replaced Blondie's but apparently not.  Not sure how long it has been here but first time we've noticed it.  Since Blondie has gone downhill, we were happy to find this place and give it a try. 

We had a slice of the combo - it reminded us of how Blondie was once upon a time.  It was a very big slice with plenty toppings and lots of cheese at a very affordable price.  It was enjoyable and a good deal for the price.  Remember it's a FAT SLICE so it tends to fill up your precious stomach space fast!

Team Fat Slice all the way. None of this skinny Blonde stuff.

I wanted to take my coworker to Fat Slice but she mentioned Blondies instead . As a nice hostess, I walked her by Blondies and when we got there we, the place just looked dirty (like many other fine Berkeley establishments). We were repulsed and decided to go to Fat Slice instead. I bit my tongue before I could say, "I told you so."

Happy me, I was jumping for joy as we arrived at Fat Slice. It was just how it always was- a long line at the counter and three pizzas in sight- cheese, veggie and pepperoni. I got the usual (pepperoni) and my coworker ordered sausage. They threw some on the cheese and baked it for her right then and there. We were given our slices piping hot.

Fat Slice is literally the cake of pizzas and what person does not like cake? Nothing beats the soft dough, cheesyness and pepperoni grease flavor handed to you on a piece of wax paper.

People are trippin - how does Fat Slice not have a solid four stars?!  Berkeley students are so spoiled with good, cheap pizza... ever since I moved back south, I've had serious withdrawals.  Do you know what it feels like to eat Domino's again !?!!!

In the battle of Fat Slice vs. Blondies, I'm totally a Fat Slice kinda girl.  I guess the plain cheese is not as flavorful as Arinell's, and Fat Slice lacks the sophistication and ingredients that Cheeseboard has...but with pepperoni and some parmesan cheese, Fat Slice is the sh*t.  You get a bang for your buck too.  Overall, Fat Slice is everything a pizza slice should be - huge, greasy, cheap, and daaaank deliciousness.

pizza is not a healthy choice period.  take away the cheese and bread and what do you have?  tomato sauce and some veggies.  i'm a californian and californians love bread.  i'm one of them who loves bread.  i can eat bread all day and nothing is finer that a hot fat juicy slice of pizza.  

i usually get a cheese slice, sometimes veggie, but most of the time cheese slice is all i want.  the slices are huge and thick.  just how i like it.  1 slice usually does it for me.  sometimes i can put down 2 depending how hungry i am.  and i'm done eating for the entire day!  sometimes they are a bit greasy but nothing i've never seen before at any pizza joint and nothing but a couple of napkins can absorb.  

i'm a pizza slice eater and i know a fresh slice when i see one.  if it doesn't look good, i won't get a slice.  if it doesn't look like it was just brought out of the oven, i'll ask them to heat it up.  

never really had any problems with the staff here nor at san fran.  plenty of parking options in the area.
Just go to Blondies.

Fat Slice doesn't do for it anymores. 
yeh, it's big
it's greasy
it's got lots of tasteless cheese(3.2)
and the dough is just bread, no crunch.

just gotta wait till i get to  a real pizza place
or if drunk, this place will do just fine.

There's a certain kind of pizza that tastes best if its 2am and you're a drunk college student.  I have nothing against it - I have fond memories of the pizza places that I used to frequent near the Barnard/Columbia campus.  If I had gone to Cal, I'm sure I would have eaten my share of pizza at Fat Slice.  

But if you're NOT a drunk college student, then you're just a person who should know better, choking down a greasy, tasteless slice of bad pizza and vowing to remember to eat before you visit your Berkeley friend who still hasn't outgrown these cheap student places.  Never again.
If your lookin for the naughty slice of pizza you no your not supposed to be eating, then eat here. If your lookin for the humus and organic everything...then eat here still and live a little.

In the late 80's, it was a near weekly trek for me to go to Blondies and Rasputin. In the 90's, however, the weekly Telegraph run changed to the superior Fat Slice and Amoeba. These days, the trip is only about once a year, but it is still all about Fat Slice and Amoeba. 

There are certainly better pizza places out there, but when I crave a thick, bready crust, Fat Slice is what I want. Unfortunately, now living 528 miles away, it is not easy to satisfy these cravings, which come on strong and often.  It is always on my list when I visit the Bay Area. 

It's not as cheap as it was 15 years ago of course, but it is not bad and the slices are every bit as fat as they have always been. Plenty of gooey cheese, a straight forward, yet herby, sauce and that doughy crust makes for an excellent quick fix. When they do it right, the oil seems to flash fry the crust, leaving a beautifully soft inner core. 

As much as I like the size, flavor, price and convenience, I have to dock a star for inconsistency and the filthiness of the place. The problem is they don't consistently nail the crust, and as much as I appreciate the grungy ambiance of the dinning area, it wouldn't hurt to do a deep cleaning every now and then. Any part of the crust or errant string of cheese that makes contact with these tables should immediately be carefully expelled from the core slice and tossed in a garbage can if you can find one.

Reading the reviews, you will see that Fat Slice is not for everyone.  But I am happy to say it is still for me.
Nothing great anymore. Almost 4 bucks for a slice of peperoni pizza. I think the Costco food court pizza is twice as good for half the price!

The pizza was alright until the entire thing of cheese came off half-way trough my pizza. A huge no-no. Their pizza is not very fresh and undercooked.

They also tried to charge me $.50 for a refill of Mountain Dew!! Get out of town.

This is the pizza place you go late at night on the Ave after you are inebriated, intoxicated, sh*tfaced, or too tipsy. 

A careful observation of late night foot traffic will confirm this. 

So of course everyone who comes here in that condition and eats is generally happy and feeling no pain, hungry as sh*t, has poor judgement, and poor memory to write a coherent and objective review the next day! 

In reality, it is meh, the crust is like cardboard and the toppings are unremarkable. 

Too bad you were too drunk to remember that Top Dog is a block up and around the corner, and open late!
When you're a college kid in a college town stumbling drunk down Telegraph past midnight, you will often have an urge to munch some college pizza (and its better than Blondie's).

There's this girl on my block. Some may call her fat. She's got some meat on her, unlike those thin skinny waifs. She's loaded. She's sweaty. She rubs me the right way. She's not blonde. She's not a brunette or redhead either. But I can get her late at night and for cheap.

Meet Fat Slice. A slice is about a fifth of a medium pizza and about an inch thick. I'm not exaggerating. You can see the cheese on each slice being stretched from the sides as it's being pulled away from the whole pie like in those commercials. But in real life. In front of your eyes! They don't just do that in commercials!

I stand with Fat Slice because I love her saucy red tomato sauce. I love her piled with veggies. I love those shiny pepperonis. I love the cheese oozing off of her. I love her with a coke. I love her for $2.75.

Seriously. I love everything about Fat Slice. I love that the neon lights pull me in. I love that there is a long corridor of seating. I love that the unpretentious top 40 is on. I love that I feel like a teenager in love when I'm eating here with my boy and turning the pages of the East Bay Express transparent from the touch of our greasy fingers. I like that I can come grab a fresh, hot slice at midnight. Just because I have a pizza craving at midnight. Just because I have a craving for sinking my teeth into an inch of soft deliciousness. Just because it's so cheap and convienent. Just because I can.

i've always been a huge fan of blondie's, as i've been eating there(the SF location) since i was a little boy. fat slice isn't too far behind, IMO. slices are big, and thick, and greasy, and cheap. all good things, in my book. the regular cheese slice was loaded with cheese. it was about as close to a perfect slice, for me. a slice and a soda were only about $4.

the location was cool and parking wasn't too difficult. the place itself seemed a little dirty, though. blondies, across the street, was much cleaner. i was also disapointed that they didn't have their "special" ready. chicken pesto is one of my favorite slices, but i was told that it would take 7 minutes. fuck that. blondies always has their specials ready to order. but overall, this place is exactly what i need before/after a night of drinking.

Fat and cheap, just like a bargain Craigslist hooker.

It's great when Jok'emon is out front.  He's always got some good jokes for a dollar.  I love that guy!  They other homeless guys need a better gimmick if they wanna make it.

p.s. - Fat Slice is definitely better than Blondie's, hands down!
----------
edit - I just heard Jok'emon is wanted and on the run from the law...  He's innocent for whatever it is!  Free Jok'emon!!!

I have nothing bad to say about this place! I love Pizza, I love Berkeley and I love late hours. So when I get out of a Warriors game and I'm still hungry, I pass by this place and order a few pepperoni pizzas.

After DYL happy hour, a friend stated that in Berkeley, after drinking, there are really only two good late night options - Top Dawg and Fat Slice. It wasn't THAT late when we rolled up, but pizza sure sounded good.

Slices from the case were served instantly, hot, and friendly, and we each got a large, thick slice and a soda for under $5. They typically have a couple other varieties, but you'll wait a bit for them to cook it up. (Worth it for the daily special "bacon with tomato and bell peppers" that I got!) A modest amount of seating is available in the back, or just stand at the wall-mounted counters. 

Perfectly good and it hit the spot after a night at the bar.

Can pizza get any better than Fat Slice? I think not.

I popped in the other day and surprisingly there were no panhandling dope fiends. 

Oh actually I take that back, there was one. 
I knew he was a panhandler because of his crooked limp walk and his handful of free newspapers he was trying to sell. So before I even jumped out the car, I already knew the dope fiend wanted something as he was approaching. So I decided to mess with his head a little. I immediately asked him for 50 cents before he can even say a word. I think he was stunned. He must of never had anyone ask him for money, it was always the other way around. He stared at me with a blank face, he was in shock because he replied, "i was gonna ask you the same thing bud". There was a weird awkward silence, so I walked around him and stepped into Fat Slice to place my order.

I ordered a Fat Slice of cheese pizza with a root beer. Enjoyed it inside. It was very delicious like always. There was so much cheese on that one slice, it was all over the place. Right then and there, is when I remembered why I love Fat Slice so much. The thick crispy crust and the greasy oily cheese drippin' on my shirt,  it was all there just how it should be.

So after killing the slice, I stepped outside and before I got to the car, the dope fiend shows up again. He had the nerve to ask me for change Again. I wasn't sure if he recognized me from those passed few minutes or did he just hit up some crack but I guess that's why they call them "dope fiends".

Basically, ill go through almost anything just for a Fat Slice of Cheese Pizza. Fat Slice, Pizza at its Finest.

not unless im drunk. and even then, im usually complaining about how bad it is. 

the only times ive been here is if im drunk or if my fat ex boyfriend dragged me here. 

and there's a reason hes an ex.

A Saturday night run for cheap & fulfilling grub...FAT SLICE PIZZA in Berkeley!

Not much needs to be said honestly, u either like Fat Slice Pizza or Blondie's Pizza who's just a block up. Well, BF loves Fat Slice & so do sis & I. My sis & I tried to have dinner in Alameda's Applebee's that was unsatisfying & disapointing, so we decided to venture out to Berkeley on a Saturday night. One HUGE slice of pizza just under $4...not overly greasy as a Jerry Curl, but crust thick as Rosa Acosta, & hot just like Laz Alonso ;-) There is no ambiance to give oohs & ahhs to, just get ur pizza, stand up & eat it along the wall inside or on the sidewalk, & you'll be more than happy! Beware of the bthrm, not really pleasant. Nice to see they take credit cards too.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/uNumMb-5qNiVzW6T32Uiag?select=PmEP9tAX9DCY6qgPnUemhA

How was the food? How was the food? How was the food? Now times that by 10...that's how many times the counter guy will ask you about your food. Maybe it's because they're trying to improve upon it since they are new or maybe he has the memory of the fish. I really don't know. I do know though, that in the two times I have come here, the Jamaican gentleman asks how your food is incessantly. The first time it's cool. The second time, it's also okay. The third and x amount of times after...it gets funny/ grating. Depends on your mood. Even when my friend and I exited, he chased us down and again asked how the food was!

The water here tastes a little funny...like cardboard. Not sure why. The Jamaican fruit punch though, is freaking bomb. If you've had the Peruvian Chicha Morada, imagine that, but carbonated!!!!

The meat is very spicy. My tears were running when I ate here, so unless you can handle the heat, don't do it to yourself! The pita and onions did not too much to get rid of the spiciness, but did enhance the flavor. Sweet potato chips here are very plain don't get them. GET THE PLANTAINS! They are not plain jane, just plain deeeeliiiightttfffuull!

I'm not a big fan of the water or the meats here, but the fruit punch and plantains will have me coming back.

This place is awesome. I ordered the meal option with 2 chicken skewers (one spicy and one mild), flatbread and 2 sides for $7.50. You can't get these flavors anywhere else around here. The grilled plantains are perfection. The roasted potatoes are your average roasted potatoes, but paired with the house sauce they're really good. Also the people that work here are friendly aaand it's conveniently located right next to campus!
Great place! Wonderful food! Awesome owner! Try it out.

Good place for vegetarians. All the side dishes are great: plantains, potatoes, cord on the cob. You might just want to make a meal out of their side dishes, its really that good....especially the plantains. Sometimes I feel bad that corporate businesses like Starbucks are filled with people and interesting little private businesses like Suya only have a few customers.....

One hit miss. 

I've been anticipating a try at this place ever since the upcoming signs were posted at its window. I think we just came in on a wrong day. The friendliness of the informative staff certainly drew us in and had us order a dish.

We ordered the Suya chicken skewers with plantain and bread. It took a bit too long for the food to be done. This was only for just one order and we were the only ones in the place... we had to kindly ask why it was taking so long. It's fine with me if its going to take a little while for quality but for the amount we got, and for the price, we were a bit surprised. The plantains were amazing. The 2 chicken skewers were a little dry and too heavy on the spiced rub... and we actually specifically asked for the mildest it could be, being aware the nature of the cuisine. The spice was so overwhelming that we couldn't take more than a few bites to finish it. And believe me, I love spicy, but this was just masking the taste of the meat too much and a bit unbearable. We took it to go, so couldn't bring much complaint right away. I have a feeling it was just forgotten about so it might have been overworked in the process of cooking. 

What I do love was the friendliness of the staff and excitement for their food. Maybe have a sample of the meat so people can try it out in these early stages.. ? Or have a sampler special at a lower price?  

I will give it another try sometime in the future, but a little scared off from this experience that it may be in the more distant future. :(  Sorry guys, I know it'll be greater soon, just need to figure out the kinks.
My review is for their grilled corn, mushrooms...there were really tasty and cooked perfect. I'll have to go back to try a meal.

I stopped in last night and glad I did!  My palate was pleasantly pleased by the authenticity of this African street food, Suya and a side of roasted plantains.  So much so that I had to purchase another order to take home.
I am sure as they get settled in this place will become a popular hit for those looking for a taste of this popular African speciality.

I went to Suya for the first time tonight, and now I wish I'd gone there much earlier. The place was empty when I walked in, so I was able to order right away. I've never had suya before, and the waiter/cashier recommended the beef, plantains, and grilled corn. With a can of pop, it ran ~$10. The menu said that with each combo meal, you get two skewers, flat bread, and only get one side; I'm not sure why I got two. I think the price is about right for the serving you get when there are two sides, and I hope this is now the norm for them. You also get a little cup of house aioli with your meal.

My food arrived in about 7 minutes, steaming hot and smelling delicious, and its tasted better than it smelled. The beef was tender and very juicy, which surprised me for being a well-done meat (normally I think kebabs are really dry unless they're rare). The spices (a mixture of a bunch of spices, called tankora) were amazing - I'd love to get my hands on some for home grilling. You can order your meat spicy or mild, and I asked for midway; I think I'll get spicy next time. This spice blend has a slow build, enough to make my nose run a little by the end of my meal, but more spice would have been fine. 

The grilled plantain was perfect. It wasn't sickly sweet (like the sweet plantains you might get at a Puerto Rican restaurant), just a mild sweetness. The texture was soft, not mushy. It paired perfectly with the house aioli, which has tankora (I think) mixed in. The grilled corn was also great. A previous reviewer said their corn was dry, but this wasn't my experience. Sure, it wasn't busting with juice like boiled corn on the cob, but there was a good balance of smokiness from the grill, salt, a hint of paprika, and maybe some cayenne. I didn't mind the moderate water loss from grilling. The flatbread was nothing special. It's cut into small triangles and I guess you could use it to make tiny pita tacos with the meat and onions, but if I go back I wouldn't be upset if I was too full to eat them.

There is indoor seating for 12, with outdoor tables and chairs for another 8. It's not a big room, and not well suited for large groups. There is a large TV on the wall, which was tuned to ESPN when I visited. It clashes with the calm ambiance of the rest of the restaurant. At least the volume was off. The only real problem I had was with my plastic fork - not as nice as a metal utensil for getting food off a wooden skewer.

I really, really enjoyed this meal. I was full when I left, and quite happy. I will definitely be back, with other people in tow. My only concern is that its location is not ideal (Oxford has bad parking, and that block is not a main pedestrian route, though the restaurant can be seen from the stoplight on campus, a plus).

Happy to have an African-Carribean spot near my work! Be ready for spice! I can tolerate spicy food for sure, but maybe they should offer a less spicy option too. the meal definitely is not enough food. I ordered an extra side and was happy with it. the grilled plantain and corn is satisyfing, the chicken skewer was tender (and, again, SPICY). I waited about 15 minutes (and the restaurant was not full) but they did bring me a sample of their housemade punch while I waited, which was delicious!

I came here for lunch and each of my items arrived at different times so I couldn't enjoy it.  The meat, bananas and veggies were cooked in shifts it seems. The meat was flavorful, but there was too much heat even for me, and I love spicy food.  I was disappointed because I only get an hour for lunch, and by the time my meat came out, I was still waiting for the plantains. Those took about 20 minutes.

One day I decided to give them another try. The guy at the counter asked if I'd eaten there before and I explained that I had and that there was a long wait for some of the items.  He just said that's because plantains take 12 minutes to cook. He seemed to think it wasn't normal to expect a lunch plate to have all the items on the plate at the same time.  He also didn't apologize, or offer to make up for it with a complimentary item or meal, as many restaurants would have done.  
Berkeley is teeming with restaurants, and there are many that are reasonably priced and want to please their customers.  These folks don't seem to care.
Suya, I'm never gonna Seeya again!!

I was very exited to try this place out! The ambience was okay, more of a Caribbean kind of feel. I was a little dissapointed with the quality of food. In Berkeley you can find a lot of fresh and "local produce" sort of restaurants... This one wasn't :[ don't get it wrong, food was tasty, I just hope it tasted more fresh. Other than that, enjoy your time at Suya!

They were giving promotional literature at the Bart Plaza so a friend and I decided to try it out. Never again. I ordered the beef skewer plate and my friend ordered the chicken. Both plates were ice cold, the meat and the chicken were so overcooked you had to chase them with water to be able to swallow them. I asked for my meal to be mild and it was extremely spicy, my salad was dumped on the plate from a bag, had one half of one cherry tomato and no dressing. We had to ask for water twice as it was not delivered with our meal. I asked for change so that I can give my friend some change and I was told that they do not give change even to their customers. To me this was a wasted $8 and I will never go back there. We also waited 20+ minutes for our ice cold food.

Really friendly staff, good food, and student discount! :)  The chicken skewer was quite good, and the owner threw in the potatoes and corn to taste.  I also got a chance to taste the champa - delicious!

Looking forward to visiting again!

It's different. That's for sure.

Came here with a friend, and both of us ordered a meal. They were running a promotion at the time where Cal students either got $2 off their meal or got 1 free side with their meal.

My friend ordered the BEEF SKEWER MEAL, which came with 2 beef skewers on 4 quarter pieces of flatbread, grilled corn, and an additional side of roasted sweet potatoes. Total was around $7.50 (can't remember the exact price, sorry :c)

I didn't get to try the beef skewer, but it sure looked burnt. The roasted sweet potatoes were good though! But they only give you a few slices... At least the corn was an entire cob.

I ordered the TILAPIA FISH MEAL, which came with 2 small filets of tilapia on a round flatbread, grilled plaintains, and an additional side of roasted potatoes. Around $8.95 I think.

The tilapia was grilled well, but the spice (whether it was the jerk rub or the suya spice) was wayyyy too spicy for me. This was my first encounter with Jamaican food, and I don't think the spices suit me very much :/

The flatbread was your standard starchy item. The plaintain chips were BOMB. My favorite part of the meal. But they give you FOUR slices!?! Come on! The roasted potatoes were also meager in portion, 1.3333 small potatoes cut into 4 small chunks.

I do appreciate how the food is made on the spot. But I thought the beef was burnt, and the fish was overpoweringly spicy--essentially, so much spice that my mouth/lips were burning, and I really couldn't enjoy the juiciness of the fish without panting in pain. I had to take really small bites to eat it...

Total was $17.89, and the only thing I enjoyed were the sweet potato sides and the grilled plaintains. I was hungry, to say the least. Sigh. That's just not right.

delicious!
getting into detail: 
- I ordered the Suya Peppered tilapia meal. the fish was just right; not too much dry rub, not too char-grilled and the roasted sweet potatoes were yummy!
- a "meal" should come w/your choice of beverage it did not.
- also, the "meal" is just one skewer, flat bread, and a side; that's not enough food for my husband who had to order another skewer a la carte bringing his grand total to $14. 

overall, the food was great! freshly cooked and seasoned well. a bit too expensive for a snack meal; either offer more food (in the style of combo #1, combo #2 etc and a drink) or drop the price a bit.

I paid $11 dollars for tilapia meal, whcih comes with flatbread and one side dish. My tilapia and a piece of flatbread that they just toasted for 30 seconds on each side (not handmade or anything fancy, mind you) came 15 minutes later. The guy who hands me the plate says "sorry, there was a misunderstanding."
Turns out, the guy never put my plantain on the grill.
I got my "side menu" after I was done w/ the meal. I had to have it "to go" because I was running late.

Was that worth my time and $11? I don't think so.

Good food, but I think the price/value ratio a little off.  

I had the chicken skewer meal; my friend had tilapia. The flavor of the marinated meats are good; nicely spicy, with a slow burn. But the quantity of food, especially for a small, somewhat slow place, is insufficient.  I feel like a "meal" should fill you up -- at least a little -- and when a meal is merely 2 skewers, a quartered piece of thin pita bread, and an (admittedly very nicely grilled) plantain, I left hungry. Add a drink and you're close to $10, which isn't the ideal price point for not-quite-a-meal so close to campus.  

I can understand if they want to position the food as healthy, but my strong recommendation to the owners would be to add stewed veggies, maybe some beans, anything to bulk it up. African food has tons of inexpensive fillers, and we should see them! Otherwise I'm just not sure how long they will last...

The Honest Truth: The Food is great! Good flavors and good spice.  Everything else isn't as good.  Portions are really small, price is high, takes a while to get your food, no place to sit, my credit card didn't work there (i know it works at other places because I just used it)

The Details: I stopped by after going to starbucks because I was curious to try "african-caribbean" food.  They had samples of the plantains and it tasted pretty good so I decided to give it a try.  After receiving a full rundown of the whole menu I tried the Chicken kabob meal.  It came out to $8 and some change.  What I got was two skewers of chicken and a small potato.  The chicken was pretty good, but there were only a couple small pieces per kabob.  It came with aioli which was pretty good too.  But after finishing my food in a couple bites, I was still extremely hungry with $8 less in my wallet.  I was kinda disappointed since the guy said that the potato would be filling, even though it turned out to be smaller than the size of my fist.  There was also nobody in the place and I had to wait a good 15 minutes for my food once they started cooking it.  But overall, their food is good! If they're prices are lowered, or their portions get bigger I would give them a higher rating.  But for $8 there are a number of other places I would go to get my money's worth.

Eh.  Got a beef skewer meal, which comes with your choice of plantain or corn (I chose plantain).  Also threw in a skewer of roasted potatoes, because I figured the "meal" wouldn't be enough food (I was right).

I didn't have high hopes for my food, because instead of cooking the food on the spot, it was all pre-cooked and merely reheated on the grill.  Turned out to be a little better than expected, though.  The plantain skewer was excellent - sweet, tart, and moist.  The beef skewer was just a tiny bit dry, but not bad.  The skewered potatoes were undercooked.

Overall a pretty disappointing experience.  And not too cheap, either, at over $11 for a small amount of food.  At that price, I expect more than reheated food.

I've always wanted to try this place, and increase my portfolio of foods I've eaten. I went with a couple friends, and the food was decent at best. Among the 7 of us, we ordered their "value order" of 8 beef skewers, an order of their tilapia, and sides of their grilled plantains and grilled corn.

I found Suya to be a plethora of pros and cons, evening out into this A-OK 3-star rating...

Pros:
1) Beef skewers were quite yummy! Quite the kick with the spices, and large chunks on the skewer. (Served with an aioli sauce.)
2) Grilled plantains were sweet.
3) The manager was really friendly, and solid service. 
4) Tilapia was nicely cooked. Simple, and tossed on a small bed of onions over a piece of flatbread.

Cons:
1) Grilled corn was dry! Albeit big, definitely not worth it, and definitely not fun finishing a giant piece of corn that isn't enjoyable eating.
2) Small place...I think the max number of seats are 12 or so...
3) Not a wide variety of selections on their menu. Pretty much your usual chicken, beef and vegetarian skewers (the tilapia was a filet not a skewer).

Overall, I wasn't wowed by this place. Worth a try if you want, but I would recommend eating at other places in Berkeley.

Something new and good taking over the old grill place's spot.

I ordered a plate, containing grilled tilapia, flat bread, some grilled veggies, and a side of corn. Portions do look skimpy for the price I paid. It was like about $10 for the plate,  and you enough food to make you a taco. The flavors are great though. My friend who told me about this place said it's pretty spicy, I'm going to argue against it. It's very tolerable and mild for those who eat spicy food regularly. I really enjoyed the food, the way it was prepared kept moisture in the fish and the corn, so that it's not too rough and eat bite remains juicy. 

My suggestion: do get a side, choose wisely so you pick a side that you know you would feel full after. Eat slowly and enjoy every little thing about the dish, you won't remember the portions that way.

Owner was very nice too, came to our table a few times to teach us the right way to eat this type of food, checked up on how we think of the place. I would definitely come back, but it's not a place where I will come everyday for the price.

Suya! Suya! Suuuuu Yahhhhhhhh.
Such simple food but I like it. Meat slapped with spices? Yes please!
The first time I ordered.. there was no one in the place... Now I have to wait in line!
Good Good! I want you to stay right where you are for a long, long time.

I recommend getting a meal combo. That way it feels less like I am getting ripped off... 
Kinda.... Kinda.... Suya is expensive for what it serves mann.. I am taking one star down for their price. But that doesn't stop me from going to Suya because I love their plantains. I like their flatbreads with onions too. Oooohhh yeahhh. Their white sauce (mayo + secret sauce?) is awesome pawesome. I can drink the whole sauce mann. jk. Chicken is tender but beef was like rubber. 

Sunny (one of the owners??) who has the same name is really nice too. He showed me how to write his name in Arabic. He can speak French too. How cool! Actually everyone is nice. Oh and outdoor seating! Yes. Bring your dogs and puppies. 

Don't be shy of African Caribbean Grill. Try it!

This place is not that great for large groups, but we made it work with our group of 7 by creatively moving some tables and chairs. 

Ordered the beef and tilapia with plantains and corn. The beef skewers were very well-seasoned and had a good kick to them. Tilapia was also delicious, especially with that creamy aioli that comes with everything. My friend asked for more of the sauce, and the chef readily gave us more. The plantains were sweet and perfectly grilled, but the corn was not that great, definitely on the dry side. 

I was really impressed by the service. The staff was very friendly and made sure we were taken care of the whole time.

New place opened up, decided I would give it a try. I'm sad to say I wasn't terribly impressed... $8 bucks for a chicken skewer and a plantain. The chicken was coated in dry rub that was spicy but had little flavor. Simply too much dry rub. The plantain was really delicious, but I just can't see spending $8 for what amounts to a snack. The all you can eat buffet next door is the same price with better chicken. Maybe they'll change things around a bit since they are new. I'd be willing to give them a second chance after they've been around for a couple of months.

Suya grills everything (skewers and sides) in plain view, next to the cash register.
didn't know anything about the food. with some info from cashier/owner?, i was comfortable ordering something. guy is friendly, informative

skewer options: chicken, beef, tilipia, vegetable(4.95)
sides: plaintain, corn, potato,  (2.95-3.5)

eats: meal= 1 order skewers (2 pieces) + side + 1 free side, & flatbread
-chicken, spicy
generous serving, chicken leg meat had carribbean spice sprinkled on it. make it spicy
chicken naturally juicy.
-corn
roasted corn good
-plaintain,
sweet tasting, great taste.
-wanted potato but cooking would take a long time.

foodnotes:
-seems pricey. with extra side, it's a bargain!
-allow 15 minutes for food to grill. mostly made to order.
-small flatscreen to pass the time.
-nice for a thrill, wouldn't eat this all the time.
-little seating available.

The chips here are soo goooodd. ANd the tri tip sandwich is good but a little dry. Overall, the taste of food is okay. I was here on a Tuesday around 6. There is a huge screen because it is a sports bar and I can imagine the excitement when the games were on but nonetheless, the dining experience is only okay. 

it is a sports bar so I guess I can't expect much from it.

I'm somewhat conflicted about how to rate Pappy's: for the event we planned there, and the service we were given, I'd give them three or four stars - however, by virtue of this not really being my scene, I can't justify more than two stars, as I personally won't be back. Read on for clarification!

We held a large party here several weeks ago, and were allocated a large space downstairs (where the dance floor and DJ was), were supplied with plenty of food (that was actually decent), and quickly fulfilled orders of beer. Working with the staff here, including the owner and manager, was easy and enjoyable, as both were very accommodating and friendly.

Unfortunately (and this is where my personal biases come in), once things started to pick up around 11pm that Saturday, the downstairs dance floor became a giant, hot, sweaty cluster. While this was mitigated greatly by the fact that we had our own reserved area, anyone that comes here for non-semi-private events will have to expect to face these crowds, unless they stick with the upstairs bar, which was slightly less claustrophobic. So, if you're into the whole crowded club/party/college scene, Pappy's is a decent venue - my personal preference keeps me sticking to lounges that serve up artisan cocktails, however.

***Accessibility Info***

Venue - A  large, spacious venue, with an elevator between the two floors, making accessibility into and throughout the venue easy, as long as it's not crowded. Once the people start flooding in though, all bets are out the window.

Bathroom - I didn't check them out, so I can't comment, but I was told they're completely ADA-compliant. However, on the bottom level (I'm not sure if they have any upstairs), the restrooms are on the side opposite of the elevator, meaning, at some point, you're going to have to wade through the insane mob of dancing bodies.

The first thing you notice is the giant screen and projector. The top floor is pretty much a bar and restaurant, but the floor bellow is almost barren. There are two pool tables, dart boards, and more flat screens, but the space there is kind of a waste. So I suggest eating on the top floor if you can. 

The food is not that good. The meat on burgers and sandwiches should not be that chewy and should be seasoned correctly! There are plenty of burger and sandwich places around telegraph, so if you want a good place to eat, I's say skip this place and head for the next one. However, the atmosphere of the top floor is definitely vibrant and would be perfect for game days.

I met some friends here the other night and we only stayed for one beer, but I figured I'd still review it.

We didn't eat here, but the food looked really good. It's an order-at-the-counter style joint with a small bar. Beers were reasonably priced, and the servers where very nice. Apparently the place transitions from a diner to a "bar" bar in the evening. The poor security fairs had to go to each table and check everyone's ID when it came time to transition. He was a very nice guy. 

Also, there was a downstairs area that we did not investigate. Back in the days of Blake's, there was another bar and a dance floor down there, but I'm not sure what the new owner of the building has done with it. 

All in all, I'd come back if I was in the area, but I don't think I'd make a special trip to Berkeley just to come here. It wasn't anything too spectacular.

Drinks were good, but my group really went there for dancing! There was karaoke downstairs and it was really fun dancing to it. Only a few folks had the courage to dance with us. When karaoke ended, the club music started and then it got really, really crowded. Music was pretty good and we all kept dancing until we got really tired. To escape from the crowd downstairs, we went upstairs and ordered the irish carbomb. I heard it was DEELISH (my friends gave me water instead....). Thanks, Pappy. We had a good time! (It was during St Patrick's night.)
The Tri tip sandwich was very good. It came with fries and a coke for $10.00, a good Value.Very nice inside with state of the art Tv's.Give it a try, you will like it.

Came here for drinks after our lab midterm (yes our professor is that cool).  

Great for groups because of their large tables and space.  It's newly remodeled and clean.

I don't know about the food since all I had was a few fries, which were typical and not particularly amazing.

Service was friendly.  

Prices were pretty standard.  But I'm just still not used to spending more money on a drink than I usually do for a meal :(

This place was awesome.  I hadn't been back to this location since Blakes had closed a while back, so I didn't know what to expect, but just stopping by for a couple drinks I was more than happy with my experience.  

Upstairs seems to be a general sitting/drinking area with tables and a bar as well as a huge TV screen with sports on, so there's always something to watch.  When you go up to order from the bar, a large TV screen shows you the drink specials for the night (or it did when I was there) and you can even see them from outside before you go in.
