I don't remember how much drinks were, but they couldn't have been terribly expensive (I'll try to update that if I'm wrong when I get a chance to go back...).

We didn't go downstairs much, but it was pretty nice.  Pool table, plenty of space to dance (at least that night) and I believe another bar.

This place is great, whether you wanna grab a couple drinks and watch a game or dance and party all night, it seems like there's something there for everyone.

First of all, awesome service! Which is rare at a local college spot. All the employees are super friendly, and always greet you with a smile!
The food is pretty good, I always order the chicken sandwich, it's amazing and full of flavor. I don't eat red meat, so sometimes I wish that there were more vegetarian or chicken/turkey options but i'm pretty happy with my chicken sandwich. 
The price is decent, maybe some of the meals are kinda expensive...maybe they're that good and I just have to try them to judge. 

As for the night life, this is a really cool spot to go grab a few drinks with friends. They have different events every night and an awesome happy hour! $1 shots? Yes please! $2 beers? Yes please! $5 pitchers? Yes please! Must I continue? It's a good place to get tipsy for cheap. Which we all know college students love! 

I love that they have pool tables, a strip pole "whoo!" B), darts, an outside patio, and karaoke nights! This is definitely a great hang out spot for college students!

Nice atmosphere. Bar looks great however the cheeseburger I ordered was not good. The burger was too greasy that halfway through eating it, I started feeling sick. Bongo Burger is the place to go if you want a good burger. For the sports and tv, here is good enough.

This place is so average I don't even know what to write about it.

There's nothing special about Pappy's, but maybe I was just so turned off by the whole college atmosphere. A bunch of bros leaving cologne trails, and tipsy girls wobbling in their heels. 

But, the story continues. We went up to the bar, and both the bartenders were too engaged in their conversations to get our drinks. I had to fight through a wall of white girls to get my drink which surprisingly was good.

I guess it's a great place for college students.
It's getting better... I think... I'll have to visit at a not so busy time to get a better feel for the place.

I came here on a Friday night and it was packed. There were no real games on, but they found a niche market near campus and is taking advantage of it. The beer by the pitcher is expensive, and so is the food. Actually, the entire place is pricey for everything, hopefully it is due to it being new, however I highly doubt that as the place seems popular already. There's a downstairs also, which I didn't get to check out because a frat had reserved it. Lots of large televisions though

Went here from Thalassa after 12 on a Friday. Super cheap drinks...but it better be cheap when they're serving freaking PBR. 

The dance floor downstairs was packed and the dub step was playing helllla loud. I'm going to sound lame for writing this, but forreal, bring ear plugs. 

I'd really only give Pappy's a three...but well, I saw Nathan Adrian here and got a hug from him, so it gets 4 stars!!!

A poor replacement for Blakes that came before it, but otherwise a reasonable place to watch a game on the 100+ inch projected screen with supportive fans and a cheap beer.

The chicken sandwich is tasty, and I have heard rave reviews about the tri tip, but I do not eat steak.

The dance floor and DJ downstairs are a regular haunt of drunk freshman due to the close proximity to the Units (the dorms).

PS. The 1 dollar well shots after 10pm are a major draw for some.

It is very crowded on the weekends and it is very slow during the week. It just depends what kind of person you are. They had a really good special going on during Valentine's day. They also have pool tables downstairs and a jukebox device. I saw a game here on their huge projector screen. They also have plenty of seating.

A few helpful notes about Pappy's Grill (the new Blake's).

1.  Don't order the Tri-Tip sandwhich.  There's just way too much fat on the cuts and its not sliced thin enough.  The chicken sandwhich looked better, I might give that a shot next time instead (if there is a next time).

2.  Ordered a pint of stella, and it wasn't that cold.  Tasted like swill, and I love Stella.  

3.  The only plus going to Pappy's is the renovated space, which is now much bigger and open.  There's even an outdoor area.  However, the bar is in the very back corner of the space, so during game days I can imagine it being a complete clusterf*ck.  We shall see.  

4.  There are plenty of big screen TV's and a massive projector, so this is good.  

In summary, I think most people would be better off going to Henry's on Durant.

A solid dining option close to campus. The steak salad is very satisfying. Good fries and burgers too. 

Easy to find seating for large groups too.

1 star for the service and the friendly bartender... the food on the other hand wasn't really good and it was kind of expensive, but they do give you A LOT. 

I ordered the chicken caesar salad and it came in a HUGE wooden bowl with side dressing. The chicken were grilled but wasn't juicy or flavorful at all. I think they put too much lemon in the salad dressing so it tasted SOUR. really sour... 

My friend had the cheeseburger which she said was meh. I think the best part was unfortunately our order of fries. 

The bartender was really nice and we ordered 3 cactus coolers... which he didn't know how to make so we had to tell him, and he ended up charging us $27 =/. I'm not used to paying anymore then $7 for mine but it was my friend's 21st birthday so whatever. The owner did end up giving my friend a free beer for his birthday though! 

I wouldn't come back for the food, but its a nice hang out spot.

The first thing you notice when you walk in is the huge projector screen. If they aren't playing sports, you might be watching music videos via Vevo as I'm doing right now.

After you've soaked in the spacious upstairs, be sure to check out the downstairs. It comes with a pair of pool tables (coin-operated) and dart boards. There is also a digital jukebox fixture in the corner too. I heard some cha-cha music followed by hip-hop.

The staff is very nice and courteous--just what I'd experience from a new bar trying to build a loyal customer base. The bartender tells me they have live DJs play on Thursdays through the rest of the weekend.

Pitchers are around 15$, I wonder if they have happy hour.

Not bad, but time will tell how well they fill the shoes left by Blake's.

Decent sports bar for watching Cal games and hanging in the neighborhood.  The menus looks amazing but is less tantalizing in reality.  I had the wings and also the spare ribs, with potato salad.  The food is quite average,  There is also no internet, very strange given this is right off campus.

While this place replaces Blake's old location, it isn't trying to be a Blake's.  Come in here with an open mind.  Its pretty chill.  A great place to kick back and watch a game, shoot some pool, and grab a bite to eat.  I stress the "watch the game" part alot because they have multiple screens on screens.  The food it typical finger food and it is decently priced.  There is ample seating and standing room for when it does get crowded.  I think given enough time, Pappy's will definitely make its mark in Berkeley culture.

The food I had was mediocre at best. It was corn chowder, very bland and not very hot when it came out. The cocktails were overpriced at the bar, $33 bucks for 4 drinks. The bloody mary was disappointed, as was the mojito I ordered after the bloody mary was blah. My friend enjoyed her tri tip sandwich. It was okay, but I wouldn't recommend it to friends. 

Oh, and downstairs (where the bathrooms are) is super weird and sterile.
This place has some really good happy hour prices. It's great place to entertain a rowdy group of friends. You certainly won't be scolded for being too loud here.
The chicken wings are pretty dry. It's too loud to hear anything going on across the table/TV. The bar is SUPER small too.

Came here on a Friday night to meet up with some college friends and it was not too busy around 10:30. To be fair, it was 4/20 so I'm sure people in Berkeley were more occupied with other activities. Anyways, drinks here are a little pricey, the place is loud, and company includes all sorts of people, from jailbait to old farts catching up over a pitcher. 

In comparison to bars across the bay in SF... Pappy's is the McDonald's quarter pounder that gets destroyed by the beef from House of Prime Rib. There is simply no comparison.

The outside seating is nice and a bit quieter than indoors, so try to snag one of those seats if you can. Go to SF and find a real bar.

4 stars for being clean on a game night, serving cold beer promptly, and a cute bartender. 
It ain't Blake's, but since Berkeley has suffered Barmageddon with Blake's, Bear's Lair, Beckett's & Looney's closing, and Raleigh's burning down I'm happy just to have a watering hole (without flypaper carpet).

#55. Revisited my alma mater and came here with a few friends since it was the closest bar.  I noticed that they offered $1 kamikaze shots, so we had four rounds.  It wasn't as watered down as I had expected, but not strong either.

I checked out the lounge downstairs, which looked slightly renovated.  Even though the place was quite empty, the floors were really sticky and slippery.  Gross.  Also, last call was at 1:30 AM.  I'm not a party person, but that's kinda early on a Saturday night.  Just saying.

There are definitely better places to hang out.  But Pappy's is a convenient option if you have limited resources.

A few words about the place:
Replacing the landmark Blake's is no easy task, but Pappy's doesn't fail to offer much of what its predecessor stood for: Bar, food, and dance floor. In all honesty I have only been here to watch games on their mega big screen television and during the daytime. However, if you're looking for a chill bar at night, a place to shoot some pool, or watch the game with buddies, Pappy's delivers.

What I recommend:
I can't speak for the bar service, but I have to say that the tri tip house salad is about as close as it comes to Intermezzo. It is loaded with meat and portion is comparable to intermezzo. Only drawback is that intermezzo salads have more tomatoes and avocado, two of my favs. The seating really is a mix and by luck you can sometimes seat your party of 10+ or at times be waiting for a table for 2. However, there is always seating downstairs if you prefer to be away from the crowd.

Bottom line:
Get the salad, go here with a large group, or go to watch the game and grab a beer. Prices hover around $8 for food and the beers around $5. The atmosphere is classier than most in Berkeley and the crowd has definitely moved up a class from Kips.

I liked it but I would have to say, after talking to the employees a little bit while waiting for my food, I'd say it's time for management to lighten up a little bit. The workers there seemed overworked and exhausted from too much micromanaging/demands.
The food: itself is great! The burgers are great, priced averagely but a a little bit better quality than your typical burger. So, all in all, go there the burgers are good. Everything else? Expect to pay ~10 for food (sorry not 21 so can't comment on bar). In any case, not necessarily suitable for catering to the poor college community? Idk, I'd personally appreciate a lunchtime special/combo priced more competitively at like ~5-6.

All in all, good food, priced okay, good people working there (but noticeably stressed).

We watched Game 5 of the Miami Heat vs. OKC at Pappy's. We watched the game with a pretty rambunctious lot. We watched the game with a couple pitchers of beer and we had us a good ol' time.

PEAKS: 
*awesome seating at the long bar top.
*some pretty mean margaritas, if i don't say so myself.
*talkative, friendly bartenders who shared tips on the hush hush subject of how to actually get a bartenders attention. (GIRLS PLEASE NOTE: yes, they have seen cleavage before.)
*perfect sports bar atmosphere with tons of big screens scattered up and downstairs.
*For a college spot, this place was pretty well kept and clean

PITS:
*the downstairs area was pretty lacking in ambiance....kind of like when you first move out of your parents place and all you have to put up on your walls is the classic Bob Marley poster....and nothing else.

We'll be back for a chill drink sometime !
Totally disorganized...on a night when there is a sporting event @ Cal...Pappy's needs to be better prepared / staffed.  30 people in line to place food order, and only one register open.

Decent beer selection and a full bar. Very nice large projection TV. 

Now, what puts me off a bit about this bar is that it is so nice. It has a very new, clean sort of track home feel to it. This makes is very different from many of the establishments in Berkeley. Everywhere else has a very old, lived in feel. The Bears Lair, Thalassa, Jupiter's and so on all have their own distinct, quirky personalities. Pappy's does not have a very distinct personality. Like I said before, it feels like a track home bar. 

Also, I had a bbq bacon cheeseburger. It was okay, I'd rather go to manhattan grill or bongo burger though.

Although Blake's was a pretty standard bar, it had a good sense of tradition and authenticity in the UC Berkeley student community. It wasn't the most unique place, but it had some character. 

Pappy's just feels like Blake's with a very generically modern twist. Brand new TVs, flashy bar, modern furniture. It just seems like the old school feel of a local college bar is gone and has been replaced with something trying too hard to be new, while still maintaining the Cal tradition with jerseys and posters hanging in scarce awkward places.

I came during a quiet evening during the summer, so most students were pretty much gone. The beer selection is pretty extensive for such a generic bar, so I'll give them props for that. If you get a pitcher of beer, your glasses are already served cold, so that's a plus.

The employees I encountered were pretty mediocre. Service without a smile and long wait times even though there was no one around. I guess that's just a hit or miss thing, so it's not a big deal. 

If I was still a student, this would probably be my last bar choice. There's just so many better options. Once they make a name for themselves, make I'll reconsider.

Holy crap, Pappy's has got a bad rap on Yelp!

I've been to Pappy's several times, and every single time I've had a blast (though my experiences may have been enhanced significantly by alcohol). Whether it be for Happy Hour (their Happy Hour ROCKS btw) or just late at night to dance and have a good time, Pappy's has always delivered.

I think it's quite nice for a sport's bar. I am a little turned off by the amount of flies that make it into their place, though D: keep your doors closed or something XD and the outside patio is pretty abysmal. 

I guess the 4 stars is more for the experience. If you want a nice sports bar experience (as opposed to a divey experience), Pappy's is the place to go. It opened at kind of a weird time (at the end of the Berkeley semester before summer break), but I think it will definitely pick up by the time school starts :D

On a (very important) sidenote: they should really rename "Pappy's Happy Hour" to "Pappy Hour".

I had an awesome time here Saturday night. The security and bartenders were super friendly and the drinks were fair-priced. I ended up leaving my debit card and they were super flexible about getting it back to me. 

Can't speak on the food but it's time for a fun college bar in Berkeley.

This was literally the worst sports bar i have ever been to. I only went because of the name which just so happens to also be my nickname, on top of being where Blake's was which was the rawest food spot on telegraph. So this new place doesn't have wings or a happy hour, the small bites of food are overly priced and the setup looks like a college dining hall. I dont even want to give this place a star because its really that bad but i have to for it to register

This was a new place so I decided to check it out. The tri-tip streak sandwich I had was god awful. Some pieces of tri-tip steak and two pieces of sandwich bread with a side of bbq sauce. The steak was a little too dry and there were no veggies to make it more moist. For the first item on their menu, I expected much more especially since it cost $9. 

The place has a lot of space so I could see how it would be great for sport hangouts, and they even have pool tables downstairs. However, if the food continues to be this bad, I don't think I'll be able to return.
Can we petition to bring Blakes back? FUCK THIS PLACE we want BLAKES BACK!!!!

Atmosphere was very cold and sterile. 
It look like a Jack-in-the-Box in a TV room
Not!!! a  warm no "Cal" sports club just big TV screens no atmosphere. Bar was too small could not have a friendly gathering.

Hope they improve and get better!  Will check out again.

Mr. C

Ok decided to write another review based on my experience last night.
The bouncers SUCK. Like they are unnecessarily RUDE. I'm pretty sure they're told to be like this though but honestly, this isn't Vegas. It's Berkeley. You don't need to act like that to get people inside your bar. 
My friend went in by herself and heard the security say "I can't wait for a group of people to come so I can tell them to wait." Really?

I would actually like this place if they got rid of this stupid attitude. Actually I think a lot of us would.


I just added a star because I know the management is really trying to deal with the negative reviews they've received. Hopefully things turn for the better and this can become another iconic Berkeley spot.
Congrats. You combined a bar with a high school cafeteria.

I'm being generous with the 4 stars...I'll break it down for you. 

Pros: since the renovation, there is more space and everything looks nicer
      Pool tables (however, dominated by the same people so that is a negative) 
       Nice place to relax and get some food and drinks
     One bouncer was pretty cool...the others..not so much


Cons: 
    Drinks can be pricey.
     Bartenders need to relearn how to make certain drinks, ex: gin and tonic 
     Mostly men..who can be a bit creepy
     Got a Caesar salad, the bread was burnt beyond recognition..and could not be eaten. 
    Need more vegetarian options!

My friends and I had a really good time here last Wednesday night! Thank God another bar opened up on Telegraph after Blake's and Raleigh's closed down :(

We got here around 9PM and had a couple rounds of beer - nothing too crazy and the prices were pretty standard. Some things I noticed and liked about the place included: lots of seats and standing area (great for crowds), a huge projector screen and many flat screens (even better for crowds), pool tables downstairs, and a full bar!!! Staff was friendly and they were playing Top 40's music, which is always a crowd pleaser. The place was about 35% filled up, so I didn't get a feel of the type of people who go in (but my friend Charles tells me there are a lot of attractive athletes on the weekends).

Will definitely come here again earlier in the day to try the food, and to see what it's like when it's crowded with people during a big game.

After one of my very favorite local pub/sports bars in Berkeley burned down a few months ago, I was heart broken and felt like there was no where in the area to watch sports and enjoy some food/drinks....and then I found Pappy's. New sports bar!? Hooray! .....and that excitement was unfortunately short lived.

Came here not long ago with some friends to watch a sports game. It's very spacious and in an excellent location, however it's very empty, doesn't have much a sports feel to it other than a lot of TV's, but it could really use some posters, flags, or something fun to deck the place out. There are many places to sit and stand though which is great. The basement has some pool tables and tv's, but it's just so empty. Felt like clean plain college basement, lol. Not a bad thing, just could use more oomph! The beer selection is mediocre, the food was oooookay, and yeah, that's about it.

The staff was very nice though because we wanted cheese fries and turns out they don't have them on their menu (ps: they should!) They still made some fries and covered them in cheese for us. Bonus points for that! We greatly appreciated it. The quesadilla was good and the salad was so-so. We had tofu on the salad and it was over cooked and shriveled up. 

I am down to come back again and give it another shot because it is a sports bar, the staff is nice, I like the location, and they are new...there's always room for improvement. :)

We spontaneously made a trip to Berkeley and we somehow, ended up here. 
I had fun, despite feeling a little invasive in a predominantly CAL student venue.  

I'm nearing 29 years of age and graduated from college 5 years ago (damn, putting those figures down kinda makes me feel like a dinosaur).  But, I blend right in, thanks to my ageless Filipino genes.  We sat down, I chair-danced to the typical hip-hop/pop top 40's, and people watched. Ahhhh....people watching.  As I entertained myself while looking at the super excited college kids dancing in a circle, I asked myself if I acted like that when I was 21.  I'm pretty sure I did, but I DEFINITELY danced better.  Oh, there was an array of different forms of off-beat dancing.  My favorite was a guy whose feet, literally, did not move from the ground.  His body was moving knee-up, but those feet were amazingly planted on the ground.  I must have been watching him for about 30 minutes.


Their beers were pretty cheap.  I ordered 5 beers which came out to be $19. 

Towards the end, we finally got up to dance. I had to dart from a douchey-looking frat boy, who was probably 10 years my junior (does that qualify me as a cougar??). Plus, my friend almost got knocked down by a couple who was straight up ballroom dancing in the crowded dance floor.  I decided to overlook those minor incidents because I had a blast!

So to wrap this up, 3 stars for crackin' music, cheap beers, and happy, drunk, excited college kids.

Ehhhhh

I feel like people may appreciate this place for things other than food, but I was pretty disappointed with my salad. I ordered a half sesame chicken salad, which was way more than enough for lunch. The full salads look huge(!), and I even ended up taking most of my half salad home as leftovers. However, it really wasn't that great. The dressing and crispy noodles are really salty! And the lettuce didn't taste that fresh, which was a real deal breaker. We also tried their avocado burger and chicken quesadilla, which were just okay.

Service was really slow. I asked for a box, and the girl behind the counter just walked away, leaving me to stand there for a long time. Uhm... ???? They also wouldn't give us a box for burgers.

i want this place to stick around so i'm going to give my constructive criticism:

i'm not sure what kind of burgers you're using but you've got to change it. burgers should not be chewy. i was starving when i ordered a cheeseburger and couldn't finish it.

fries are good - don't change those.

are you going to add appetizers? wings/nachos? would be good for sports games.

are you eventually going to have cocktail servers? it's going to be ROUGH getting a drink at a bar with only 6 seats if there's more than 20 people in there at a time, which i'm assuming you'd like to have happen?

service - everyone was friendly!

Got the free burger with purchase of drink special a couple weeks back. The burger came out looking pretty good, but upon inspection, the patty is very greasy. Sad to say, it is much greasier than even the street-side shop of IB Hoagies (whose burger and cheesesteaks I have to say are AMAZING AND HIGH QUALITY ANGUS BEEF). 

I wrapped the burger patty 3-4 times in napkins and the napkins got drenched with oil every time. I gave up trying to get most of it out. 

Topped with ketchup, the burger was decent. I wouldn't return for it.

May want to come back and try the cornbread, which looks hauntingly similar to Smart Alec's...must compare...

Why can't people just accept Pappy's for what it is and be stoked that it's way cooler than Blakes!?

A great place to pre party before a Cal game and get a pitcher or 5. With $10 pitchers of Bud Light, what is there to complain about!?

Cant comment on the food, but I can't imagine it's THAT bad. Anything is good when you're drinking. The service is a little uptight and weird but hey, that's just customer service. I talked to the owners wife and she seemed legitimately happy with the place, and was really passionate about what they created. Gotta love that! 

This is my new go-to party spot before any Cal game. GO BEARS!

Pappy's clean up Blake's real nicely, but both are the one and the same to me still. This meaning, overpriced food and drinks in a large decent space. This is one of those places that would only be enjoyable if there was a crowd and if you're into hanging out with undergrad college students. Come here for all your major sporting events. The food is good, but on the pricey side for what it is. The burgers can be ordered with a soda or beer combo deal. The fries are thickly cut and the condiments are infinite. The burger was delicious, though skimpy on the pickle slices. Beers are $5/pint and $15/pitcher as long as it's not Bud Light. That said, the selection is mediocre. Of the usual, the notables being the usual Sierra Nevada IPA, Racer 5 IPA, Widmer Hef, Shocktop White. The service is pretty good, definitely well-staffed with people with good attitudes. The downstairs area has lots of room, dart board, and pool tables. There's also a patio. There's a cool digital jukebox there, but I can't say the same about the tunes.

Pappy Waldorf was the beloved football coach at Cal for almost a decade. I'm sure he's rolling over in his grave about this lousy place that bears his name.

I always start me yelp rating and "tip-o-meter" with 3 stars and 15%. The woman that took my order was cheerful. Cheeseburger, fries and a diet coke. $8.15. I gave her a $1.50 tip.

I find a high table top facing the big HD screen with ESPN. Turns out is was dirty. OK. I ask if I could have a rag to wipe the table. No, we'll get it clean up right away.

Right away never came.

No cheeseburger yet, so I now move to the bar to watch ESPN. Friendly guy greets me as I sit down. Then all of a sudden, he slaps his open hand on the right next to me on the bar! He looks at his hand and tells me, "No matter where you go, there will always be fruit flies."

Then he wipes his bug smashed hand on his pants (didn't wash his hands mine you) and proceeds to put glasses away and make drinks.

Ugh.

Now the burger comes out and I set it down on the bar. There is a condiment bar, but it's on the other side of the room. Trek over there and it's a mess too.

Finally sit down to eat, feeling sickened by the bugs and the messy place. Oh, I'm now lucky to sit next to a Cal maintenance worker, drinking a beer (hope he was off), and eating Buffalo wings. 

Well, talking while he is smacking his lips on a chicken bone to the fly guy. And trying to talk to me about.... Never mind. Shows me his beaten napkin and says, "They don't make napkins like they should anymore." Enough! I eat half of the meal, which was OK and left.

I checked in on yelp 20 minutes ago and now I've just finished this review. I'm finished with Pappy's too.

My new favorite take-out comfort food place!!!  They cook the lamb gyros briefly on the grill before serving it, so it hasn't been sitting in a cold bin all day like most gyros places.  The portions are extremely generous, and the best part is that it isn't very greasy, so you could eat a lot without feeling sick!  The plate also comes with a salad (standard salad, nothing special), yellow rice pilaf (very tasty!), and pita (they warm this on the grill too).  

This is a much better use of my $8 than Thai Basil, or the $9 beef-and-lamb wrap (which contains mostly beef) from Oasis.

I think this place was called something else back when I was in Berkeley (boy, that tells you how old I must be).  I remembered the falafel was good way back, so we decided to grace the place in the pouring winter rain.  And they sure didn't disappoint.  We ordered the $2.99 falafel and $6.95 beef kabob plate (to my dismay; I wanted the gyro plate but hubby thought he knew better) which comes with salad, choice of rice or fries, hummus, and pita bread.  There are 6 falafels complete with yogurt sauce and pita breads. The shell is thin to perfection, the inside fluffy and piping hot.  The hummus was the bomb.  Beef kabob is a little dry, and I still stuck to the belief that we should've ordered gyros instead.

My first experience at D'yar was pretty good, I'd give it a solid 3.5, rounded up to 4 for now because I'm hungry. I ordered the chicken shawerma plate that comes with pita bread, hummus, salad, rice, fries, and chicken (you should ask for half half on the rice and fries, since both are pretty good.) 

I wasn't sure what the small puddle of orange sitting on top of the hummus, but I ignored it and actually enjoyed the hummus very much. As for the chicken, it was a bit dry and not very tender and juicy, but it was well seasoned and went well with the hummus and pita bread. The sald was also decent, a bit lacking on my plate, but just very normal lettuce, some random veggies, and dressing. The rice also went well with the hummus, chicken, and pita bread, and wasn't too dry. Also, for the price, it was a pretty big portion and left me full. I'd definitely come back here for a fix of meditteranean food again.

I ordered a chicken shawarma plate with rice. The pita was meh like most I've found that you can buy at grocery stores like Berkeley Bowl & TJ's. Reminds me of Noah's bagels - the best bagels of Berkeley though they taste like styrofoam when compared to Montreal/NY bagels. The hummus was good - not great but getting there. The actual chicken was overspiced  though tender. Sure, $7.40 tax in for a plate is reasonable but the food leaves something to be desired.

Alas, my hunt for delicious Middle Eastern food continues after my visit here. I suspect a big reason I haven't been able to find something comparable like found in Montreal is that there is a much smaller Middle Eastern population here in the Bay Area. If that makes me a snob, so be it, though I just think it means the bar is much higher.

When I get sick of "something" over rice or "something" fried rice" or pad "something" at asian ghetto, D'Yar is my go to fallback plan. I usually end up getting the chicken shawarma plate because the combo comes with a drink and it ends up being around 7-8 dollars. If I'm not feeling too hungry, I usually go for one of the wraps. The gyro meat and kebabs are quite good here too. They give you extra pita bread for free if you ask! :D

Pretty sub-par. Went in for an early lunch so maybe they weren't on their game yet. Staff not exactly rude but definitely not friendly. I got the lamb plate, which looks awesome in the Yelp photos and in the restaurant. Lamb had good flavor but very tough. Good pita and hummus. Salad was plain, little flavor. Asked for fries and got rice, which was also bland. Over $9 for a moderately filling, bland meal? Won't be back.

Good food, Good price. 
Cant go wrong.

I've been craving Falafel like crazy lately and hit this place with the family today to check it out and it was pretty good!  The prices are great, portions decent and, most wonderful for a student-food zone place, very clean!  I ordered the falafel wrap and my husband ordered the eggplant wrap and we were both happy but would have liked a bit more tahini.  

And I always look for hot sauce as I grew up going to Falafel Drive-in in San Jose (which has the BEST falafel and hot sauce I've ever had) so I compare all falafel joints to them.  No luck on the hot sauce but I'll still go back when I get the f-craving again ; ).

I always visit this place when I visit Berkeley, they have the best prices and best taste around the East and South bay areas. I highly suspect they lace their gyro meat with crack...

Highly recommend!

Great Mediterranean food right next to campus at a good price for the portion. 

I used to get the lamb and beef gyro wrap, and now I get the lamb and beef gyro plate because it comes with hummus, pita bread, and french fries (or rice). 

The meat they use in those dishes is very soft, tender, and flavorful. It's pretty oily, and at times that can be a little overwhelming.

The lemonade is hit or miss--sometimes its sweet, and sometimes its undrinkably bitter. 

You can call ahead if you're in a hurry, but they don't take too long if you don't.

This is a standard Greek restaurant, nothing fancy.  The interior is unassuming, the workers don't treat you particularly nice, and the menu options don't offer anything groundbreaking. What D'yar does, though, is offer simple menu options made extremely well. That's it. Go here for your standard chicken shawarma plate, but I guarantee you it will be the best god damn chicken shawarma plate you've ever had, son.
best falafel i've had yet in berkeley. will definitely return.

A Berkeley gem, really good food that delivers regularly and is made fresh for you.  They use flatbread for the Schwarma's and Gyros, which I love.  Decent hummus, ok Dolma's, really good fries.

The restaurant is a bit crowded feeling inside, but a fun people watching location if you're ready to "rough it" and better than most in the area.  For the area, its a 4 star, though leans towards 3 if I think outside just Telegraph.

I was looking for a late lunch since I didn't make it to dining hall hours.  I wasn't sure what I wanted ... that is, until I saw the big sign for Greek food.  The place looked stylish and clean (surprisingly, this is not all that common in Berkeley), and they had a Gyros Wrap on the menu, so I decided to try it.

3.5 stars for my yummy made-to-order beef and lamb gyros wrap.  (I was looking forward to becoming a vegetarian when I moved to NorCal, but there are so many delectable, meaty restaurant offerings that this notion lasted less than two weeks.)  It had cucumber, tomato, red onion, and tziki.  

1 additional star because: the man was very friendly, the service quick,  and the scenery was nice (attractive men and women dining in and taking out).  

I am inclined to give this place 5 stars just for the fountain sodas with unlimited free refills.  (No refills is a Bay Area anomaly to which I don't think I can ever adjust.)  I am rounding my 4.5 star rating down to a 4 mainly because the food was good, but not great.

i LOVE this place! when i'm craving mediterranean food and don't want to leave a hole in my wallet, this is the place i go to. their food is very decently priced and their portions are huge. hooray for d'yar!

taste is okay, I would say its pretty good, portion is large and price is reasonable, the people there are very kind. I ordered the steak wrap which comes with a nice sauce and their fresh lemonade is quite good. their plates also look quite tasty and their soup is delicious. I had chicken noodle soup, which they gave me lemon on the side and never knew chicken noodle soup would taste so good with lemon.

Their fries are also decent just regular tasting fries that you order on the side, cheaper than the mediterranean place you'll find in asian ghetto.
1-2$ more than I'd like to pay, everything is pretty standard/bland/stale, nothing really stands out. If Sunrise Deli is open, go there instead. It's much much better, but open less frequently.

Came here on a spontaneous trip to Berkeley looking for something to fill our hungry stomachs. When I saw "gyros" on the menu, I knew I had to try it. Gyros had been my new food that I have been recently introduced to, and I love it. Definitely great for any meal. Only problem with the gyros places I've tried is that they can get expensive..

It wasn't the case at D'Yar however. We came in for lunch to see a sign on the window displaying, "Pita pockets with drink for 4.99." In the pita pocket, you have a choice of filling it with a gyros, chicken shwarma, or vegetarian option. I chose to fill my pita pocket with gyros. I also ordered a side of fries which I believe was 1.99 or 2.99

The gyros was OK for me. The meat was a bit dry and it lacked the yogurt sauce that most gyros places are known for. Other than that, I enjoyed the gyro.

The fries looked like they were done cajun style, similar to ones you would find at Arby's or Wingstop. The problem I had with them was that they were too salty. Whoever sprinkled the salt on them put waaay too much. I found myself walking over to the water dispenser several times to quiet my thirst receptors.

I might go back and try them again just to sample other dishes they have. I'd probably request no salt on the fries next time. For the price though, it was a good deal.

3 stars for OK food and great prices. A few things mentioned above reduced my rating of the restaurant. Don't let a 3 star rating discourage you though from trying and forming your own opinion of the restaurant.
The Falafel deluxe was pretty good but I think there could've been more falafel and less potato.  It's cheap and fast and I'd be willing to try shawarma next time.

By far my favorite cheap and fast Mediterranean restaurant in Berkeley. I can always count on D'Yar to satisfy my Mediterranean cravings.

ATMOSPHERE
It's a tiny place with enough seating as long as you don't come during busy hours (aka: lunch time). Since it's located right next to the "Asian Ghetto," expect it to be crawling with students.

The workers are really nice and always let me substitute Greek salad for french fries!

FOOD
I always, always, always order the CHICKEN KEBOB PLATE, which normally comes with rice, salad, pita, hummus, and 2 chicken kebobs. 

However, I don't like how sour Greek salads are, so I substitute the salad for a plate of their delicious french fries! BEST DECISION EVER. The fries are fried to perfection and are sprinkled with a tasty seasoning.

The chicken is always tender and juicy, with just the right amount of char. The rice is buttery and complements the chicken. The pita and hummus are delish. I always have leftovers, which says a lot considering how much I can eat.

For the price, taste, quality, portions, and convenience, this place takes the cake for great Mediterranean food near UC Berkeley!

My friend brought me their chicken shawarma the other day and as I was eating it, I was thinking this is so good how come I haven't tried this place before. I liked their pita bread so much that I had to go back the next day. For some reason, it didn't taste as good as it did the first time around. It tasted unhealthy, but the plate is big so you get your money's worth. They give lots and lots of chicken.

As an Arab vegetarian who grew up in the Middle East, I know my falafel. It's not only part of my culture, but it's one of the few foods in my culture that I can eat!

The falafel at D'yar is the best I've had in California. Period. It's not as good as back home, but it's the closest you'll get without getting on a plane and going to Beirut. All the sides are great too. The hummus is pretty good, the tahini is great, and if you like spicy foods make sure to ask for the GREEN hot sauce(Way spicier and way better than the red!)

I'd recommend the Falafel plate (which isn't always available as it's one of the daily specials) so you can make your own mini sandwiches with bread and throw whatever you want on it, or if you're in a hurry, just grab a falafel sandwich.

So the food here is just okay. The falafel lacks flavor, and the salad is wayyyyyyy to over-dressed. the sanwiches were nothing special, and the bread was not good.

sunrise deli is like 29348024809 times better, actually i think that's why i'm being so harsh on this place. to anyone who hasn't tasted sunrise deli, this place would probably be okay, but everything at sunrise deli is just sooooo much fresher and tastier and better (and i think sunrise deli is cheaper)

also, the guy working at the counter here was kinda rude to me, and he seemed really annoyed when i asked for an extra thing of tahini. 


the only good thing about this place is that it's nice and clean on the inside, and it looks like it was recently built or at least remodeled, but the food is just not that good
Tons of really good tasting food-- $7 combo plate easily fills you up.
Pretty good falafel sandwich for less than $6.00. Eh it's fine.

Service is awesome, quick and friendly. The restaurant is much, much, MUCH cleaner than the norm for the area (don't get me wrong, I love the Durant food ghetto even though I neither attend school nor live in Berkeley any longer... but "clean" isn't the strong suit of the eateries in this neighborhood).

As far as the food, I'd love to be able to write an extensive review, but I ordered the Chicken Shwerma wrap on recommendation the first time I went and I liked it so much I've eaten the same thing every time since. It's tasty, with the perfect balance between meat & veg, spicy & subtle.

Parking's a huge problem, but again it comes with the territory.
Stale pita, bland hummus, old twangy tabouli, lamb kebab wrap with too much red onion and not enough tahini. Fries were passable.

The food is fresh and delicious.

Employees are friendly.

Excellent value for the money.
I eat there a lot. Friendly service, tasty lemonade and great gyros. Plates aren't bad either, although the rice could be a little better.

I feel bad giving this place such a bad rating since the food IS good - but their service was terrible! I ordered a falafel salad with no dressing. It's pretty easy right? Just don't put dressing! I waited and waited for my food, and then it was finally ready, but then they realized, crap, there is dressing on it. Rather than make me an all new salad, they made me new falafels, but they kept most of the same lettuce and box (just scraped off the top layer of lettuce) so my lunch was smeared with dressing still. I didn't want to say anything given they already noticed their mistake the first time, and I already waited a very long time for the food, so I just let it go. The falafels were tasty, but alas, the not so great service will not have me coming back.

I only get one thing here; the gyro plate. Before they used to charge extra for credit/debit, I came here more often. The gyro plate has very generous lamb slices, served with pita and hummus, your choice of rice/fries, and salad. What is it with campus area merchants adding this credit/debit surcharge these days?!
It's one of the only places in the UC area where you can receive a QUALITY meal (fresh meats, hummus, salads, etc.) cooked to order at a great price.

Yum Yum Yum.  Food is great.  I got everyone at my work hooked on this place.  It is our favorite quick lunch spot.  Consistent, Fresh, and Tasty!.  Fabulous food - atmosphere is kind of a student hangout. Fight for a table!
I ordered a lamb kebab today and it was way overcooked. I remember liking the food in this place better before. I wonder if they changed the management.

I love D'yar. It is my go to place for lunch in Berkeley, and the gyros are completely filling and delicious, with just the right amount of sauce and spice for me. The dudes working there are totally cool, and the food is ready quickly for a place that is made to order with some complicated plates. 

One star deducted for the awkward, cramped seating. It's too small for the crowd they get, and we always wind up sitting on top of another couple of diners or wedged in a corner.

Food was A-OK.

I was excited to try this place as I love falafel so I jumped at the chance while walking around Telegraph.  

I got their falafel/avocado/hummus wrap plus a drink and side of fries to go for about $8.50.  Portions were huge!!

Though I got my order to go, I noticed people before and after me being served first.  Which isn't totally bad.  Excepted my BF got his meal then had to wait another 10-15 minutes before I got mine (I was worried his food would get soggy).

Total wait time was about 25 mins.. for a wrap.  So I thought it'd be MF'ing phenomenol.  It was just okay.  Tasted like it was missing a key ingrediant or two.  It was probably missing hot sauce, which I asked for on the side, and didn't get.  Fries were excellent.. halfway between steak cut and McDonald's.  I would say the falafels were good so I might come just back for that.  Their hummus was a little bland, though.

I'd probably come back but the wait time deters me a bit..

D'yar has become one of my standbys. Working on campus, there are many food options to choose from on Southside, and this place doesn't disappoint. I'd recommend the chicken shawerma plate here. The chicken is very good and well-seasoned. It's grilled after being cut off the rotisserie, so the texture is alternately tender and crunchy. The rice pilaf here is generally good, but can be a tad bland. The hummus is spectacular... sometimes. I've had oddly lemony hummus here on one occasion, and the best hummus I've ever had on another. Often, this place hits the spot when I've got a craving for the chicken shawerma. The baklava is pretty tasty too.
delicious + cheap + friendly stuff = i will be back!!!!

Place isn't bad. Good falafel balls! Really fresh - but you have to eat them quickly, otherwise they get pretty soggy. As for food, very "Meh" place. Prices are a bit steep ~ 10-15 for like a wrap and falafels. I had the combo plate...not bad, the meat was cooked well but everything else they sort of piled onto the plate.
Great roasted chicken and lamb schwarmas wrapped up in a crispy flatbread!

I enjoyed a delicious falafel plate here; my friend had chicken shawarma plate that looked fantastic. Reasonably priced. Good sized portions. Convenient location near Durant/Telegraph. Can be crowded when students are around. Would definitely go back.
great food for a decent price.

D'Yar is my favorite place to eat at the Asian Ghetto, I feel like I can eat the healthiest here. I typically get their chicken shawarma, or shawarma plate. Food is good, really reasonably priced, and the wait is never too long. If I'm in a hurry, I'd definitely go here instead of Thai Basil.. hah.
Its the place that has turned me over to the world of Falafel, and the fact that the Falafel Deluxe wrap has French fries in it makes it that much tastier.

I finally decided to use my CampusCred deal from the fall semester today. D'Yar doesn't have a menu online that I could find so I uploaded pics to Yelp when I was there today (hope this helps). 

With $12 credit, I had to get at 2 items from the menu. I ordered the falafel plate (4.99) and the roasted chicken shawarma ($5.79). The wait time was about 5 minutes since there wasn't anyone else in the restaurant at 4pm. $6 for two entrees is a steal!

I ate the roasted chicken shawarma w/rice first. The roast chicken was delicious. The pita bread was very soft but the hummus was disappointing. The flavor just wasn't right with the rest of the plate. The salad was alright.

The falafel plate included salad, 4 falafels, hummus, pita bread, and fries. My to-go box included 5 falafels (score!) and the same salad, pita bread, and hummus. The fries were extremely flavorful and others who I shared with agreed.

I want to try the wraps and kebobs next time.

Shawarma Chicken Plate and Lamb Plate. 

First time here and both plates were DELICIOUS! 

After our 2.5 hour hike at Berkeley Fire Trails, we were super hungry. We were in the area and one of our friend really wanted to get a gyro for lunch. We had wanted to go to a different gyro cafe on the same block but decided to come here because there was more people at this place. Hey, when there's a lot of people at the restaurant, that means it's good right?!! Indeed it was. 

We were kinda iffy at first and didn't know what to ordered. I ordered the chicken plate. My boyfriend ordered the lamb plate. Our friend ordered the gyro. The prices are decent and cheaper than other places. The pita bread, rice, salad, chicken, lamb, garlic yogurt and hummus were all so freakin good. I don't know what it's in it, but it's so addicting. Love it! Even our friend loved the gyro. We were thinking about ordering seconds to go, but didn't.

Definitely, we would come back again when we're in the area.

For the price, I don't think you'll beat the freshness and taste of this place. My wife had never tasted a Gyro before, and these were much better than the ones I've had in the past. We were originally going to split a plate, but I had to go back up and get my own.  :)  The owner was very friendly.  Great food!  Thank you for a pleasant experience.

I think it's the best Mediterranean food in Berkeley.  Good prices too.  Usually get the shawarma.  Good fries, but you if you order a regular plate, then don't give much pita bread.  Which is a shame.

Plates:
Chicken is great, Falafels are great, Hummus is great. Lamb is alright, but lacks something in the seasoning. I always get it with the rice, which is also great.
The salad is a bit bare minimum, and they don't give enough pita bread IMO.
Wraps:
Wraps are great, though they tend to get kinda messy with dripping juices (though that's really a plus.)

The seasoning on the chicken is wonderful. Almost bordering on overpowering, but delicious that I enjoy the meal the entire way through and don't get tired of it. Lamb lacks a bit of flavor. The ingredients are fresh.

Recommend: Chicken Shwarma Plate, Gyro Wrap. You can get hot sauce too if that's your thing, though I never have.

To do it right: $6

I used to be here for lunch every week or two, but had to cut myself off because I was eating more red meat than I probably should have been eating. For whatever reason, giant hunks of lamb and beef on a slow-rotating spit is a serious weakness of mine.

D'Yar sits right next to the Asian Ghetto, but is a welcome departure from the edible ass for sale next door. The lamb gyro "sandwich" is quite good down to the last. The gyro is solid, the pita soft and warm and tzatziki is prepared fresh from its constituent parts.  Pretty much everything I've had here has been good.  The service is also quite friendly too.

Given its Durant locale, don't plan to drive.

Summary: An excellent lunch idea if you work or learn nearby.

I have no idea what I ordered, but it tasted it good and it was student food cheap... ~$5 for chicken in a pita pocket with all the green stuff. It was fresh and fast - weekday lunch time and the guys were busy. 
There is some table space though not much waiting area for take-out orders.
chicken shwarma plate with rice. great hummus and tahini sauce. their chicken and rice are both awesome and it's priced reasonably. almost five stars.

My sweetie and I just ate at D'Yar again last night, for the third time. We keep going back because the food is so tasty. 

I really love the Chicken Kabob Plate because the chicken is spiced so well and the meat is so tender and juicy, that every bite was incredibly delicious. 

Their fresh lemonade is a great way to cool the little zing in your mouth, and you can tell that it's made from real lemons.

Very unfriendly service. The girl at the counter did not even try to be nice. So obviously did not want to be at work, and hated taking my order. 

I sat down and waited. 

There were about 4 employees behind the counter, but it seemed like none of them were cooking. They were just bickering and being hostile to each other about something related to the stove or the fume hood. It took over 15 minutes to get my to-go falafel. 

The guy who brought it over was the only friendly employee in the restaurant. I took it and ran, never to return. 

The falafel was decent, but not worth the trouble of an unfriendly restaurant.
Opened in the old Eat a Pita space on Durant. I got the falafel wrap. Good price, yummy falafel, not enough sauce and only average bread.  And it's cold. The staff weren't exactly warm either.

I've been on a shwerma kick lately so I've been trying them everywhere I go. This is probably the 3rd best that I've had. I like their ingredients. I like that they were not giving out pressed meat. I like the freshness of the vegetables. I think they could have added some more meat. Also, they could have provided som tzatiki equivalent yogurty sauce/dressing in addition to the hot sauce. The price was average to the other places. And yes, to agree with a previous review the staff could warm up a bit.

Hmm... more like a 3.5 but eh, I think I have enough "3"'s on my record hah.

I haven't had falafel in years, and to tell the truth, I really don't know much about Middle Eastern food.... at all.  But I did remember that the last time I ate falafel, it was freaking delicious.

Attending a concert at the nearby university, I wanted to try some falafel because I haven't had any in a really long time.  And, sure, this place has music a bit too loud and the lighting is sort of dim and it's sort of awkward.... when the hot, fresh smell of onions wafts across your frozen face, who cares!?

I ordered the falafel salad (yaay diiet...) and my dad got the beef kebab.  I'm not a big fan of the dressings (well, not a big fan of any dressing actually) but the falafel was damn tasty.  It was crunchy and crispy on the outside, soft and warm on the inside.  I was thinking of bringing some home but I realized that it would soften overnight.

My dad approves too.  And he's really picky about the quality of his food.

Also, $12 dinner for two?  You can't really go wrong with that.

Ugh writing this makes me crave some gyros.

I go to D'Yar occasionally and it is always reliably good. Their shwarma wrap is generously sized with good ingredients. Their plates are good size, and very filling. Prices are reasonable and service is courteous. For a cheap student-area place, D'Yar is great.

Lamb, lamb, lamb. It's all about the lamb!  And, boy, do they make it right. The grilled lamb kebabs are so tender and perfectly seasoned.  Then, dip it in a tangy yogurt sauce and, finally, pair it with a heaping spoon of yellow (curried?) rice. Mmmmmm! I'll be back soon, lamb!

Have eaten here many times over the years...on three occasions I got a stomach ache afterwards, so thought maybe it was me.  last time recently tried again and same thing happened except worse.  Too bad as i liked this place even though I knew that the quality couldn't be high based on portions and prices.

This is my go-to place for fast Mediterranean in Berkeley; I've been there many times now. The Chicken Shawarma is very good. They give free drink refills, unlike many places around, but also have a small credit card surcharge, also like many places around. It moves pretty fast and is cleaner than many of the restaurants nearby. Has nice seating inside, too.

this place sucks. all the plates are overpriced. food is greasy and not fresh as he advertises. portion is small comparing to price. he charges for extra bread. the owner who barely speaks English is rude and does not even say thank you. I spend 13.50 on one meal. if you want to nice Mediterranean food, there are a lot of options in that area.

This place is legit. It isn't the best mediterranean I've had, but it gets the job done. I tried to go here at least once a week, if I was forced to eat out while cramming for exams or the like at Haas... The quality can't be beat for the price. While Smart Alec's is decent for salads, I'll take lamb kabob all day...

I like this place. Both the gyro and falafel are very solid. The pita seems fresh and the prices are really reasonable. They're very consistent in quality and experience, which I appreciate. Pretty generous portions too.

I love their chicken plate here! I discovered this wonderful place last semester and have been coming here ever since. They give pretty good portions and their chicken is amazing! I also like their rice here.
pretty tasty gyros sandwich @ a good price

I have eaten here about two to three times per week since the opening date. The food is great: the meat (esp. gyro and kefta) is excellent and the portions are generous. Service is excellent; I have received several free samples, and the staff have always been friendly.

I was hanging out in Berkeley this past weekend and saw this place as i was walking by. The pizza places in the area do a number on my stomach so i decided to stop in. I was very glad i did, i ordered a gyro which was very good and came with lots of fresh veggies inside. The lamb/beef was pretty good, it could of had a little more flavor but good. I got my order to go, but the seating inside was nice and clean, and there were a lot of cool pictures on the wall. If you're in Berkeley and are tired of blondies, fat slice etc. definetely check this place out.

Chicken shwarma wrap + hot sauce = really, really good. Friends had chicken shwarma plate (chicken, rice/fries, hummus, salad, pita bread) and really liked it. Someone else had mushroom hummus, but it was just a big plate of hummus with mushrooms and onions, and not nearly enough pita bread. It was also really oil. Still, the chicken dishes were outstanding. Prices are a little less than Asian ghetto, but you get less food too.

i got a grilled chicken gyro. no baklava? 

the ingredients tasted fresh, but it lacks a bit of flavor. maybe some hummus or spices would help. otherwise, it just tastes like meat, tomatoes, and cucumbers. 

if you go, bring some sauce.

I had a lamb kabob wrap, not plate- $6.99, $7.60 with tax. It was tasty. [Thanks for plenty of napkins.] My only complaint that most won't have, is that I have a soy sensitivity and they don't tell you unless you ask, but they coat the lamb with oil [I asked what kind of oil, and the guy seemed at a loss. I prompted him, vegetable? and he agreed. That means soybean or a mix with it usually. It could of been olive, but that wasn't my understanding. If someone knows different, please post it!]. At least that is what I understood the guy who took my order was saying to me. [We had a little language barrier going.] He was nice though; brought my to-go order out to me where I was sitting out front. The veggies and sauce in the wrap seemed fresh and my sweetheart liked the flavor of the lamb as did I. There were some tough pieces of meat in there, but what do you want for the price? I DIDN'T find myself saying this is terrible. Would probably go back. About a $1.22 for the Arizona Tea (and it had no 'natural flavor' (contains soy), but used real 'natural lemon flavor' -  a plus!)

I discovered this place the beginning of this past semester. I had just gotten back from Israel over the summer and all I wanted to do was eat falafel and shwarma, preferably at the high authentic quality I had in both Israeli and Arab restaurants in Israel. Luckily, I was quite pleased that this place delivered.

My first venture into D'Yar was to try their chicken shwarma. I was quite surprised because it was very burrito-esque and I had never had chicken shwarma. Their fries had some great seasoning and the drink was definitely awesome. The shwarma wrap was amazing and I loved it. It's well seasoned, filling, and has a lot of veggies as well as a lot of meat. 

Since then I've been back to have their gyros, rice pilaf, falafel, baba ganoush, and fresh hummus. I have to say that I love all of them and whenever I'm craving Mediterranean, I make sure to stop at D'Yar first. They have catered some of my events and they always provide a lot of food for a fantastic price if you just ask (and negotiate -- they're smart Middle Easterns of course). Definitely come to D'Yar but do take-out because they have almost no seating and it's ALWAYS full!

My favorite falafel in berkeley. I am a big falafel fan too. I think they have regular hot sauce, and the spicy hot sauce that they only put on if you ask for extra spice, this extra spice is the reason they get the 5 stars, most places have one spice level, and it is usually mild. There are 2 other amazing falafel places near Berkeley, The Holy Land in the Grand Lake district of Oakland (the one on college isnt as good as the one in the grandlake), and Cafe Sophia in Albany, but they arent in Berkeley. Sunrise is good, but the falafel isnt as flavorful, I go to Sunrise once for every three times I go to Dyar. (on average)

My absolute favorite Lebanese/Palestinian spot in Berkeley! Everything from their chicken kabob to their gyro sandwich is excellent. The quality of the food to top notch, and the price is totally reasonable. 

Also, the ambiance is very well done. I love the arabic music they play, and the framed photos on the walls are beautiful. 

If you love chicken, I would start with the chicken kabob plate with fries. I love tabouli as well, and if you ask, you can have your fries substituted with tabouli. Top off your meal with baklava, and you will have an excellent meal for under $10!

Too bad I can't give this place 0 stars. I got food poisoning from this place -L-
The meat was dry as hell. My step dad makes better Gyro's than this place, and he's Asian. Only good part of this place is that they made me lose 6 lbs from shitting so much. THANKS.

Btw you guys make Mcdonalds look like a 5 star restaurant.

Really good food. I get the Chicken Shawarma plate with rice. Fries tastes a bit weird with the type of food (chicken + a salad). The plates also offer more food than the wraps.

Costs about 8 w/ tax included. 

They have a "frequent customer card" (buy 10 get 1 free) that they don't seem to hand out, but they'll give you one if you ask for one.

Also, the guy who works the cashier is really level headed - I saw some sketchy guy come in and try to start a fight, was cussing and threatening him and he was calm and called the police while asking him to leave politely. What a boss.

would give half a star if i could...terrible, terrible place! yes, the food is good but i am sure you can get better mediterranean food elsewhere with better service. the service here SUCKS. they made my food last even though i was first in line. 3 other people got their food before me when they came after me. when i asked the guy, he said "oh their food is vegetarian"...when they had gotten lamb. when is lamb vegetarian? then he told me chicken takes longer to cook even though the meat is already cooked. then he asked me "what do you want? do you want your money back?" in a very condescending tone when my food was almost done..omg SO RUDE. these people are so so so so sooo rude.

on top of that, i have a stomach ache now. and i've heard of people getting food poisoning from this place...3 of my friends have actually. i would never come here again, not even with the campus cred deal.

come to d'yar if you want OK food, TERRIBLE SERVICE, RUDE people, and food poisoning!!!!

Finally! Something replaced Eat-A-Pita! That place was terrible!

Great renovation of the location, no awkward stationary tables anymore, just a bunch of individual ones and it's clean! 

The food is very tasty and well priced. Except baklava, which is almost 2 bucks for each individual piece... but it is REALLLY good, surprisingly, tastes very fresh. 

Another great point is that they already have prefilled mini hot sauce containers so you don't even have to ask!
Oh AND they accept credit cards w/no minimum! (looks like Berkeley's finally catching on!)

Is it just me or is this place a tiny bit sketch? I guess most places around Asian Ghetto / "Durant Food Court" are pretty sketchy though...

I got the munchonme deal for a gyro plate + drink for $5. It was only my second time having mediterranean food for dinner, so I didn't go in having high expectations or anything. My meal came with meat, salad, hummus, some bread, and french fries. The fries were probably my favorite part of the meal - they're seasoned with salt and pepper and just taste oh-so-good.

The reason I thought it was kind of sketch was because there were flies flying everywhere around inside, the place was deserted at 7:00pm (prime dinner time), and I'm pretty sure some of my pieces of meat were kinda hairy. I don't know if that's for authenticity from being cut off that meat heater thing but...pretty sketch.

Probably the best Mediterranean food in the UC Campus area. Reasonably priced at about $8 including tax per dish. They have the standard kebabs and falafel. The portions are huge too! Lamb kebab = WIN!! Definitely a delicious place in a region that surprisingly lacks good Med food. I also recommend their Kefta kebab and Chicken kebab. It comes with house salad and typical Mediterranean saffron rice. It also comes with hummus and pita!! 

Pros:
- Cheap
- Fast
- HUGE PORTIONS!
- Quality food
- Delicious Taste
- Entrees come with hummus, pita, salad, and rice.
- Near UC Campus area
- Friendly service

Cons: 
- looks weird from the outside

Was excited about another Mediterranean joint opening up on Durant Ave. After Wally's, other falafels and similar foods just don't measure up. 

Standard service. Food lacks some kick though =/

Ordered:
1. Falafel salad
     -  Falafels are too dry, veggies were not fresh
2. Chicken kabob
     -  Meat had way too much sodium

Final call:
Falafels are better at Sunrise Deli but if you want a quick gyro, D'Yar's will hook you up.

I think I would eat here everyday if I could. I've had their gyro wraps, gyro plates, and chicken schwarma plates - all of which are incredible. The gyro meat is the most tender I've ever had, and I'm convinced they put crack in their yogurt sauce. (It is literally the only Greek yogurt sauce I could eat with a spoon.)  Even better, for seven dollars, you get a huge portion - perfect for people like me that don't get full from an average sized meal. The pita bread is soft and lightly grilled, and the plates come with hummus, salad and rice. 

It does take a few minutes for the food to come out, especially when it's busy, but this place is awesome. Definitely a must-try.

I'm a regular at Diyar... I always order the Gyro Plate with fries, but I've tried their other plates and falafels, and I'm never disappointed. 

This place isn't super cheap, but it's decent for being in the Asian Ghetto area. A meat plate goes for around $8. They give lots of meat and lots of fries/rice, with a side of yummy citrusy salad and some pita bread. I love hummus, and they give you a lot of that, along with unlimited tahini sauce and ketchup. The best part is eating the hummus and meat in a makeshift pita sandwich, and soaking the fries in the citrus salad dressing. 

On off days, the meat and the fries do get too greasy, so I like to do the motherly thing and soak the oil out with napkins.

I love Mediterranean food, and I'm going to miss Diyar when I graduate!

While I still prefer Sunrise Deli's Super Falafel wrap, D'yar's falafel wraps come in pretty close. Prices are actually pretty reasonable so I come here at least once a week.

+ FOOD

Falafel Deluxe Wrap - Falafel, babaghanoush, potatoes, etc etc. Not too shabby. The potatoes are a good filling, but the whole thing is a bit dry. I tend to get some more sauce on the side so I'm not downing water all the time.

Mediterranean Plate - A spread of hummus, babaghanoush, tabouleh, 3 falafel, 2 dolmas, random lettuce salad, pickled vegetables, and four pieces of pita. Probably my usual order here. It's $6 and doesn't make you feel like a fatso like the nearby eateries of Asian Ghetto. Tastes clean and to the point, but probably not the best I've had.

Chicken/Lamb Shawarma/Kabob - The chicken shawarma and the lamb kabob taste better out of the options you can get. While not super awesome, it's still good if you're looking for a meat option (Sunrise Deli IMO still better even if smaller portion). These come either in wrap or on a plate.

Funny thing is that if you get a plate, you can opt for rice or fries. I got the fries once for kicks and the chicken shawarma + fries plate combo tastes not too far from a Mexican SD-style Carnitas/Carne Asada Fries dish, just with chicken instead. It's somewhat similar when you throw on some hot sauce and mix it all up together. It's not exactly as greasy or indulging, but I just found an interesting similarity. If only they had guacamole, salsa, and sour cream instead of tzatziki sauce...

P.S. $3 for 6 huge falafel balls + pita bread to eat it with. Best snack evar. Sunrise has one dozen for $3, but they don't give you pita so ehh weigh your options haha.

This is an amazing Middle Eastern restaurant. This place replaced Eat A Pita which was a shame to Middle Eastern cuisine.
The food here is very authentic, the falafel, hummus and babaghanooj are amazing!
My friends say that the chicken shawarma is out of this world.
The place is always busy around lunch time; plan to be there by 11:30AM to get a table or after 1:30PM.
Quantity of food for the price is excellent and the prices are cheap.
I usually get the vegetarian plate.
I like the new owners and all the staff.

GOOD MEDITERRANEAN FOOD WITH LIMITED SEATING

I like the food here but the seating is cramped.  We found a seat in the freezing dining area and waited for our food.

Chicken Kebob
Tender pieces of well-seasoned chicken were served over rice with salad, hummus, and pita bread.  The rice had too much of a cardamom flavor to me (should of ordered fries) but the chicken was perfectly cooked.  The salad and pita bread were average but I liked the flavor of the hummus.

Mediterranean Plate
L ordered the Mediterranean Plate and was very pleased.  It was composed of two dolmas, three falafel, hummus, baba ganoush, salad, and pita bread.  The dish met his criteria of being inexpensive, healthy, and filling.

A good place to stop for inexpensive fresh tasting Mediterranean food.

I keep coming back here. It's so good. And consistently good.

I've tried three things here so far: the Gyro plate, the Falafel plate and the Mediterranean Plate. All of which were awesome! 

It's just the right amount of food. You'll be stuffed, but not so stuffed that you feel like someone should roll you away.

Just the right price. $7. :)

And if you want a snack you can just get an order of falafel, which if I may reiterate is only 3 bucks! For 6 balls of warm and crispy goodness. 

(To the jerks taking off stars because you couldn't find a place to sit: seriously? Anything that close to campus will have limited seating. We're here to judge the food.)

Anyway, if you haven't tried this place, you SHOULD. Remember? It's one of those places you've walked blindly past the last hundred times you went to Asian Ghetto (or the Durant Food Court to be PC).

This used to be Eat-A-Pita, but this D'Yar is not that much different, though I admit it looks less exotic now. The restaurant is clean with nice tiled tables. I would not suggest coming in a group bigger than 4 people.

The food is delicious and the portions are great for the price. The lamb kabob and chicken skewers are good. My favorite is the mediterranean plate. I would not recommend the fried cheese appetizer.

meh not too bad, but not that great. I wanted a gyro but all they had were wraps. Beef and lamb is definitely the way to go. The wrap was so so. A lot of yogurt, an average amount of meat and not too bad a price. However the selection was sort of limited. I guess I am biased when I get wrap. The flatbread used to wrap the meal (lavash I think) is too dry for me. Oh well can't win them all I guess. However it was quick and it was pouring outside so it provided us warmth and food.

As all my pals can attest, it's very difficult for me to roll through Berk without getting my chicken kabob plate on.  I've had quite a bit of middle eastern fare in my day, and D'Yar is hands down my favorite when it comes to both flavor and price!  Baklava is also fantastic here.  Friendly staff, cute/clean decor especially for a campus-adjacent spot.

What happened?!  Why is your Chicken so dry now?!  Why did you hike up the price of your Chicken Schawarma special?  And why did the service get so bad that I had to wait for 5 minutes while the cashier chatted with someone before taking my order?  I was going to eat his head I was so hungry.

This is actually my favorite place to eat around Asian Ghetto.

Service: The food takes a fairly long time to come out, considering most things are already cooked on that humongous spit. The chefs don't appear to be in any sort of rush to get the food out despite the large number of people waiting to get their orders.

Food: I've only ever gotten the Chicken Shawerma Plate, and I've never ever gotten anything else. It has completely satisfied me every single time. The portions are pretty large. The chicken fills nearly a third of the to-go box, which is fantastic. There is some romaine lettuce, hummus, yogurt sauce, pita bread, and you can choose either fries or rice. ALWAYS choose fries. They are delicious. I don't know what kind of seasoning they put on there but man, they are good. I don't usually eat anything with the yogurt sauce, but I eat the fries, bread, and salad with the humus.

Now, my one issue with this place is that the chicken is a bit dry. The portion is large, which makes up for it since most of us are hungry college students, but sometimes less is more. I suppose that's the way it's supposed to be eaten, considering it's been cooking on a spit for I don't know how long and breast meat dries quickly.

I will be coming back, of course. :)

A friend took me here for lunch last Thursday and I was really surprised.  The staff was cool and the food was good.  I had a falafel wrap and the lavash bread that the falafels were wrapped in was really good.  I was surprised that the price was only $4.99!  Pretty cool and a great deal for all the students in the area.  I enjoyed my lunch, but felt like something was a little lacking.  Just read some other reviews and realized that I could have gotten hot sauce.  That would have made a huge difference.  I know I would have loved it with the hot sauce.  Will definitely order it that way next time!

A great option if you happen to be in the area.

$5.99 for a plate of falafel, hummus, pita, salad, and rice that you can split with a friend, enjoy the taste of the food and still be full?

This is why I love Berkeley eateries near CAL.

Chicken shawarma plate with either rice or fries.
with a little salad on the side and pita with hummus and cucumber yogurt sauce. add a drink and it's $7.49

the chicken and rice are both moist enough.

winner winner chicken dinner

I got a Mediterranean Plate to-go for under $8. It was a vegetarian dish that was flavorful, light, had lots of components, and was surprisingly good. I got my money's worth.

Yay! I'm a fan.

When the size of the plates, the price, and the quality of the food are all added together, Dyar is a tough spot to beat.  In an area packed with good restaurants, almost all of which are catering to student budgets, Dyar was hands down my favorite lunch spot when I was a student at Berkeley (I admit that my love for Middle Eastern food makes me somewhat biased).

For a light and quick lunch, the shawarma wraps are perfect.  If you want something more filling, the shawarma or kabob plates come packed with meat, your choice of rice or French fries, salad, bread, humus and a small side of yogurt. The food is very good and I seriously don't know of a place with portions this big and prices so cheap!  I never ordered it, but friends loved the vegetarian plate, a mix of humus, dolmas, falafel, salad and bread.  This looked really good and I was always tempted to order it, but I never had the heart to turn down kabaob or shawarma.

How do you pronounce the name?!

Anyway, usual campus food with a plus. 
This place is close to work and so very convenient.
Def go here for the Chicken Schwarma!
Nice big portion with fries on the side.

Next time I will try the lamb.. :)

Gyro plate. Fries. Extra tahini sauce. $8. Done.

The place is small so seating is very limited. Order first and keep your receipt for your number. When your plate is ready, dig in. The gyro was a tad saltier and greasier than I expected it to be, but it had all the flavors there. It did, later on, create a huge amount of gas in my stomach. I was really uncomfortable throughout the day. Honestly the salad on my plate wasn't necessary since it kind of got mushed up with my fries and hummus and ended up being a cluster of hot lettuce . It's nice, however, that your plate comes with your choice of meat, choice of rice or fries, pita, hummus, and salad. The pita is nice and soft. Definitely warm as if it just came out of the oven. 

My biggest concern was the soda machine. The coke was definitely not coke, a clear carbonated liquid more so. It was unbearable to even sip on it. But luckily, there are 5 other options to choose from. 

This place is great to grab a quick bite or catch up with a friend.
Get the chicken shwerma plate, with rice - and ask for the RED hot sauce which'll come on the side.  The baklava is good, but a little excessive with the syrupy glaze.

Decently priced Mediterranean food within close proximity to campus.

Came here upon reading some good reviews from fellow Yelpers. Ordered the chicken shawarma wrap for $6.30 w/tax. The wrap smelled delicious (I got it to go and sat in the seating area in the middle of Asian Ghetto, and the girl next to me commented on how good it smelled, and headed over to D'Yar herself for some gyro) , and the first few bites were really good. The chicken was flavorful and the hot sauce added a good kick to the wrap. But by the time I came to the end of the meal, I felt something was lacking...can't really put my finger on what though. The food was pretty good, but not great. They have falafel plates for $5, chicken and/or beef rice bowls for $5.49, etc.

I actually didn't have to wait too long for my wrap, probably about 5-8 minutes, so I'm not sure what's up with the reviews about having to wait a long time. Then again, I was one of only three customers in the restaurant. I guess if you come during the peak lunch hour, you may find yourself waiting longer

In any case, money well spent. I'm looking forward to coming back and trying their $5 lunch specials (the cheap Asian in me was protesting that my wrap cost more than $6)

Quantity was a plus, but please...

Can someone let them know to go easy on the amount of salt they put in 
their meat. 

I have to drink a gallon of water to quench my thirst after eating a meal there

Ordered: gyro wrap

Nicely flavored. Good blend of tomatoes, yogurt sauce, and veggies, but the pita bread felt a little stale... 

For $6, you get decent food AND a place to sit and chat in Asian Ghetto. Not bad

Sucks having to wait after a catering order.  I don't see why they can't serve food faster.  I waited approx. 20 minutes for my food.  And it was all thrown into a to-go box...not really appealing.  Taste wasn't that great either.  

Probably won't come here again....and I LOVE Mediterranean food.  I'm sad.

3 stars for the food, great value for the quality.
