1 star for the service. They charged us for an extra order of fries, which we did not order. Would not refund us for the plate. Not great customer relations.

Meh, it was just okay. Sunrise deli is the only place I get falafel from, it's the best ever. They were closed by the time I was free yesterday, so I ended up at D'Yar and ordered a falafel wrap. It's basically a falafel burrito. I was let down....maybe it's because I was craving Sunrise and then ate mediocre falafel?? Falafel didn't have much flavor. Idk, but I don't think I'll be back. Now, that's not to say it wasn't edible....it was just....forgettable.

Best deal for Mediterranean food I have ever seen.  I always get the 2 meat plate (gyro & chicken swarma) and a Mediterranean plate (all veggie).  Together with tax price comes to $15.  Not bad at all, especially for how many different goodies you get in this combo pack.  It's like a mini buffet on 2 plates.  Perfect for 2 people to share together.  Food has always been good out of the 10 times I ate here.  Price is cheap because of the Berkeley campus being next door.  Place is kept clean.  There is room for 16 people or so to eat.

Bonus: Lots of action when you are sitting by the window people watching :)

D'Yar is great!  The people are always so friendly when I come, even when I just buy some fries.  They always joke around with you and make sure you are loaded up on ketchup, napkins, etc.  I love getting the vegetarian plate which comes with amazing falafel, babaganoush, hummus and tabouli.  It is very filling and cheap!  I also like the chicken plate and the lamb plate; I've sometimes get rice with my food but the fries are really good so I usually opt for that.  It also comes with a small salad.  Once, they forgot to give my friend his pita bread and when they realized it, they gave us a whole bunch to make up for it.  

It's usually crowded and hard to find seating and if you do find a seat, its likely that you're less than twelve inches from a stranger.  However, getting to-go is not a bad option!

definitely better than the place that used to be here.  the staff is very friendly and the food is quite good.  sure we're all sad that meesha's left, so for now, this seems to be the next best thing, and they surely have done it right.

had the kefka kebab plate, and a shawarma wrap.  both were very good, large enough that we weren't left TOO hungry after, and reasonably priced.  also, the lemonade is quite good, definitely homemade.

Can't believe I never noticed this place before! I feel  like since it's located right next to IB Hoagie's, it gets overlooked a lot.

I came here on a Monday night for takeout dinner with a friend, and earlier with a co-worker a few months ago. The last time I went, I ordered the gyro plate, which came with a ton of meat! For what you pay ($6.99), I felt that the price was pretty reasonable.

Yesterday, I ordered the chicken shawerma ($5.99), partly because I wanted to try something new, and partly because Avengers was pretty freaking amazing. The shawerma was all right- the chicken was good and I love their fries, but the hummus smelled kind of funky, so that was a bit disappointing. ):

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Friendly service and funny servers! Came here for lunch on a Monday because my friend adores this place. The sun was shining through the windows as we waited in line. They have a few tables and some counter seating, and they have a water dispenser in the back corner, next to the soda machine (free refills!).

Service was fast--we got our food within 8 minutes. They take credit, which is always nice c:

|| F O O D ||

FALAFEL WRAP: 4 fresh falafels with cucumber and tomato salad, seasoned onions, and tahini sauce [$4.99]
- Shouldn't have gotten the wrap. The sauce (or maybe the water from the veggies) made the bottom of the wrap soggy, which was unpleasant and squishy.
- The grilled wrap itself was strangely burnt. Well, not literally burnt, but it had a charcoal aftertaste in some bites.
- Falafels themselves were tasty! 
- Veggies didn't seem very fresh. The cucumber pieces still had skin on them...and these were the cucumbers with the bitter tasting skin. :c

GYRO PLATE: thin slices of gyro with "the works", which is essentially gyro, sliced onions, salad with tomatoes and cucumbers, hummus, fries, pita pieces, tahini sauce in a plastic cup  [$6.99]
- This looked wayy more appetizing and was wayyyy more appetizing than my wrap. They gave him a HUGE HEAPING SERVING of gyro. He said they gave him more gyro than they normally do, which is awesome because he shared with me! 
- Gyro is flavorful and tasty. Nice large chunks of gyro! 
- Pita slices are pretty good, not too dry which is nice. Tastes good dipped in hummus or tahini sauce...or both!
- My friend likes dipping the fries in the hummus.
- I didn't really like their hummus, but their tahini sauce is great, and you can ask for refills of it. Goes great with the gyro!

|| C L O S U R E ||

Good prompt service, awesome prices. Don't get the wraps--get the plates. Enjoy!

Convenient location with relatively quick service. Overall, very competent lunch food. As of the time of this review, the $5.99 + tax "Chicken Shawarma wrap + fries + drink" combo has been the only thing i've been ordering. Pretty cheap, filling, and does its job at filling you. 

The veggie ingredients they use are pretty fresh, but the wrap itself is more bland than what i'm used to and is some serious need of more exciting flavor (it tastes like a sorta boring wrapped combination of  cooked chicken, hummus, lettuce, and tomatoes). I had better tasting shawarmas, falafels, and gyros elsewhere, but this will definitely suffice as a functional mainstay between bouts of better cuisine elsewhere.

I was a bit disappointed with my falafel wrap... I tried dolling it up with the hummus and avocado, but it was meh.... 

I think the main thing that bothered me about my meal was that it didn't taste fresh to me, it didn't have that much flavor, and that the food was cold... a filling meal for a good price though.

D'Yar is simply... DELICIOUS!

By a combination of price, deliciousness, and convenience I have to give it my nod as my favorite place to eat. You can get a combo, which is a shawarma plate/wrap and a drink for under $8. The plate comes with the meat, salad, hummus, and rice or fries (or even both). It's just a combination of perfection.

They sometimes have a hard time understanding the difference between fries and rice so make sure you say FRENCH fries... or RICE! D'Yar is also an awesome place to eat because you can say punny things like... "Let's eat over D'YAR!" or "I am in D'YAR need of that chicken shawarma plate!"

So if you haven't already go over D'Yar and try out the plate and the wrap. They also have stamp cards if you want to become a regular. I've already gotten my 5th free meal in 2 years so I am definitely a huge fan. So D'Yar we go... My review right D'Yar. I think I should eat D'Yar now.

the Great,
GumZ

The falafel itself is delicious: crispy outside and moist inside - and a plate of 6 good-sixed falafel balls will run you $2.95.

Chicken shawarma wrap was good and cheap. Comes with a few pickled vegetables, and otherwise the standard wrap stuff. it was fast, and the ingredients were fresh.

Good Mediterranean food at a cheap price!

Searching what students call the Asian Ghetto (aka the Durant Food Courts) I stumbled across this gem.

They have a lot of lunch plate specials for $5. While those looked tempting, I was craving a shawarma. The menu only listed a chicken option, so I ordered the gyro wrap instead because it had lamb & beef. Both come with a fountain drink.

Quick Sidebar: What's the difference between a shawarma and a gyro? Aren't they both wraps from the Mediterranean area? From my understanding the Shwarma vs Gyro divide is basically Middle East vs Greece. Either way, I'm a fan of both!

Their Gyro Wrap hit the spot. The lamb & beef were moist, the "hot sauce" added a lasting flavor and at $5.79 with a drink, it's a steal! I also ordered fries on the side and re-filled my Coke while I was waiting. I didn't wait to long though, as the service was pretty fast.

As I walked back to my Kollaboration SF meeting on the UC Berkeley campus, the smell of the wrap caught some eyes as I entered the room. Shared the fries, shared the Coke but kept the wrap to myself because it was scrumptious.

i order the falafel wrap here, and it's about the size of a burrito. in fact, it looks like a burrito. and by the look on my face while i'm eating it, you can assume that it's a tasty burrito. or falafel wrap, i guess, if you can figure out that it's not a burrito.

repetition aside, i'd love to give this place an extra star, but i feel as if it'd only account for its location and tastiness level in contrast to neighboring restaurants.

it's a nice oasis amidst the typical college student hot spots and i admit recommending this place to a few people. however, these people are college students. my peers want food now. and it's not like they'll take any suggestions from me if i say, "well i know this really good falafel place - it's in emeryville on san pablo."

in short, it's not the tastiest falafel i've ever had, but it's the tastiest falafel i've had within a short vicinity.

Came here last night with my friends. I've never been here before and one of my friends wanted the falafel balls. 

The place is nice, clean, and inviting inside. Atmosphere felt lively, people inside enjoying their chicken shawarma (I wish I brought my wallet because it smelled so good and also looked good) and kebabs. The place smelled so delicious! 

The guy who helped us out was patient and nice. There's lots to choose from here. She took her food to go and we didn't wait too long till he finished the order. I tried one with the sauce (what's the sauce made of, sesame?) anyways, it tasted good, fresh and hot.

I really want to come here and try at least everything :)

A few words about the place:
An unassuming spot that you don't know the name of unless you bother twisting your head to the sky, D'yar is one of my favorite Mediterranean spots in the UC Berkeley campus area. With freshly made food, ample seating, and easy accessibility it is a top pick for me for lunch or dinner when on south side.

What I recommend:
Get the Lamb and beef Schwarma  plate, no debate. Even if you think lamb is too gamey for you, the perfect seasoning and slow spit style roasting of this meat makes any qualms you have with lamb disappear in an instant. The plate ($7.99) comes with salad, hummus, schwarma, pita, and rice or fries. I usually get half rice and half fries and ask for a side of hotsauce to kick things up a notch, but that's just me. The salad though is tangy and light, while the hummus has a nice garlic-y punch, and the schwarma goes swimmingly with the yogurt or hotsauce. This plate is just packed full of flavor that complements and rounds out the meal completely. Not to mention it is more than enough food for me and probably a good dish to split for those with a lighter appetite. 

Bottom line:
Although a little pricier than their counterparts, they take card, have ample seating, nicer ambiance than their neighbors, and have tasty food. You can't really find anything in terms of schwarma that beats the flavor or quantity of food in the area. However, if you're a falafel person I have to point you in the direction of Sunrise deli, who makes a mean falafel sandwich with avocado.

The delicious hummus is back to normal! Huzzah!

They also seemed to raise the price a little...it's no longer $7.12 total as my previous review indicated (read my previous review for a more in depth look at what deliciousness you're about to taste). Seems to be $7.67 now. Still worth it!

I have been here twice and each time severely enjoyed the falafel plate.  It's kind of a magical experience.  The falafels are crispy, warm and delicious.  You also get some wicked good fries, hummus, salad and pitas.  All for about $6.  My only grievances are the pitas are too small to open and stuff ingredients inside of.  Also, they could throw in a little more hummus.  Overall though, this meal tickles my palate in all the right ways.

OK, so we came here pretty late, kind of close to closing time, which may have affected the service we received, which was kind sucky, and the food that we got.

All I wanted was some tabouleh and pita bread! Although the tabouleh was pretty good compared to others I've tried (my hometown has LOTS of mediterranean food to compare to), they TOTALLY skimmed me on my pita bread! Help a sista out and give me some darn pita bread! They only gave me like 6 slices... which I had to share with two other MEN! and ladies you know that men can eat a lot! so can we, but damn that was not enough pita to go around! :(

Sadness.... my friends got some other meals like gyros and etc etc... but at that point I was just sad I didn't have more pita bread to finish my tabouleh. Maybe I should've asked, but I felt bad cause it was close to closing time OR maybe they should've just given us LOTS of pita bread! 

haha, well hopefully I can give this place another try, maybe during the day time and normal business hours or something. But another thing was they charged my credit card for food I never bought! (long story short, I wanted to pay in cash, changed my mind, used card, then changed my mind again to cash) Plus, there was some language barrier between the guy taking my order and me. I don't know maybe I couldn't hear him, but some other guy had to come and help him out. that part was pretty hilarious, but don't be skimpin' out on my pita bread!

grrrrrrrr.

I don't know if I just have low standards for food around campus or if food just tastes better to me when it's cheaper or I was just really hungry, but the food here today really hit the spot for me!

Food: 
1) Chicken shawarma plate: YUM! Yummy hummus, yummy pita break, yummy salad, YUMMY chicken and some ok rice! Oh my gosh, I was in Med food heaven! This was Chicken Shawarma done right!
2) Lamb Shawarma plate: thin strips of juicy but lightly crispy lamb with the same yummy pita bread, hummus and salad (and there was rice). I didn't know food around campus could taste SO good! I'm in utter shock that I haven't tried this place or heard more good things about food here!

(+) BIG proportions, so you get your money's worth!
(+) cheap food
(+) Close to campus 
(+) Quick
(-) kinda shady looking and very hole in the wall, dirty feeling
(-) There's always bums right outside
(-) they give too much food and it tastes way too good so you end up eating too much......oh wait, is that a bad thing? Maybe I should put this under a plus....hmmm.......

Overall: I think I found my go to place for lunch!

This place has a really nice atmosphere, pretty good food, and reasonable prices.  Food definitely tastes authentic.  I always go here for falafel dishes.  It doesn't seem to be much of a sit-down restaurant due to the lack of space.  However, it is definitely not good for to-go.  One of the reasons this place only gets 3 stars is because food takes FOREVER.  I go here whenever I'm craving some good Mediterranean food, but every time I've had to wait a good 30 minutes! :(

Lunched there last week with my friend, Adrienne. Upon ordering, she pulled out her D'Yar Frequent Gyro Card! 10 - $6+ purchases and you get the 11th one free! I've been there at least 12 times and never was offered the card! I felt so violated and used. 
Complaining and pleading my case to the Mediterranean crew only evoked their male laughter. Ha-ha. '-( I understand now how degrading men can be. Sorry, Ladies. Now, I've changed.
I have the card now with one credit. For that, only three stars. 
Well, until I go there next week.

Came here for a brunch and enjoyed it thoroughly.

 The falafels are made after you order and are fresh and yummy. The falafel plate comes with fries, hummus, a dip and pita. Quite a stuffing and ideal for a heavy brunch.

Also had the eggplant wrap which was mildly spiced and flavorful.

This place is a stone's throw from campus, good value for money with quick service!

Get your Mediterranean fix here!

I'm usually a wrap guy, but got a MunchOnMe.com deal for a gyro plate here at D'Yar for $4.99 including a drink. I think it was $7 without drink normally.

The plate has a lot of food. The gyro meat plus fries, salad, hummus, and some pita wedges (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WaxhDYWQmZ1FGM2ChY7_2Q?select=oRIoYya7ltz2W3TYgObmlQ). You have a choice of rice instead of fries, if you want to go a bit healthier.

The gyro meat (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WaxhDYWQmZ1FGM2ChY7_2Q?select=xtOFxWNQqZe7WrSMPb1oGA) was pretty good. Nicely seasoned and juicy. It's sliced off the vertical rotisserie and given a bit of grilling with some onions before serving and doesn't taste like your typical Kronos cone meat. The fries were also good with a dusting of black pepper than you can see in the picture.

The rest of the items were not that great. The salad was pretty basic and overly dressed with a citrusy, vinaigrette dressing. The hummus was bland with too much non-EVOO oil further blandifying it (technical foodie term). The thin, hard pita wedges . . . I could have stabbed someone with those.

I've had the shawarma and falafel wraps here before (thought I'd reviewed already too . . . ) and I think the wraps are the way to go.

Chicken. Shawarma. Plate.

General things:
Tahini Sauce- I've had better. It doesn't really have a strong flavor to it, actually it is pretty mild and not thick, so it is good as an introduction.
Salad- Ok, pretty standard.
Pita bread- Only 3 slices ): 
Hummus (with oil on top)- Your general hummus.
Fries- I love fries! And these are steak cut. Me likes.
Chicken- On the dry side. You would think that it is very flavorful since it looks like it is well-seasoned, but actually it is not. 

I call this place GaGa because it is bad romance.

My new mantra.  I will be calorie frugal.  I will maximize value and minimize unhealthy eating.  I will make good food choices.  

Thus, I did a price comparison between D'Yar and Cal Gyro.  Cal Gyro is more expensive.  For the wraps, the difference is less than 50c.  For the plates, the difference is much more noticeable.  A typical chicken plate here is $6.49.  That's with hummus, salad, rice (or fries) and meat.  At Cal Gyro, it's $9.99.  

I got the beef kebab plate.  When the lady asked whether I wanted fries or rice, I got all confused.  I'm so bad at making decisions.  Especially when it comes to horizontally bad food choices.  It was ready in a jiffy.  The weather was very hot outside so I enjoyed watching the inappropriately dressed young students walk, up and down, up and down to fetch their foods.  A young man sitting by the table chowing down on a rice bowl ($4.99 special of the day) asked for some pickled radishes.  I want pickles too!  These were the purple kind, the kind that is also served with the pita that has a pocket in the middle.  The other places that serve thick pita does not have purple pickled radishes and their hummus is rather gross.  

When I got home, I sat down in the little al fresco sun room my parents built.  As I opened my bounty, I heard the strangest noise, like a very small semi-tractor starting up.  Turns out it was a hummingbird fight!  Two hummingbirds put their dukes up and fought it out in the yard.  It was a good sign for the food.  The beef was not overly salty and still tender.  It had nice char marks on the outside.  The rice had those little toasted noodles that I've heard so much about.  And peas.  The salad had little grape tomatoes.  And the hummus was quite tasty.  Sometimes hummus can taste like mortar that is used to seal bricks.  But from here, it was savory and tasty.

After eating nearly every type of food you can imange on this trip... The bf suggested having Mediterranean for dinner. Found this cute little place just down the way from where we were hanging out at. 
When we walked in, the place wasnt to busy (which was nice, who wants a busy restaurant when you are hungry).  After looking over the menu i decided on getting the Chicken Shawarma Wrap(Chicken, wrapped in a pita bread with veggies), pickled vegetables on the side, and a drink (Only draw back on getting a drink from here is they only have a soda machine and no ice tea or other kind of drinks, which is a total bummer for their customers who dont like soda) total for that was $4.99 plus tax. If you wanted to add fries or rice it was an extra $1.99.
The person who took our order was nice, he gave me our receipt and said our number would be called. Found a cozy spot by the window to sit and people watch on Telegraph Ave. (FYI watch out for the sharp edges on the sides of the table, my poor elbow and arm got attack several times!!).

Even though this is a Mediterranean place dont expect to hear that type of music, instead one of the food preppers busted out his ipod and was playing a mix of hiphop and contemporary music. At one point he even got into a song and was singing as he was cooking, which i thought showed another side of this place. They know how to have fun while working!! They really take the time to make everything fresh and right the first time it seems like.

Finally, our order was up and ready for us to pick up. The warp was pretty good (on the larger side). Only thing was, they are kind of stingy on giving you alot of chicken. All in all, this pita filled me up along with stealing some bites from the bf's yummi looking plate too!!!

Prices are not bad here at all in this awesome college town, just wish they wouldnt charge so much to add on fries or rice, kind of a bummer especially if your a student trying to save your scrilla!!!!

Their chicken kebab plate is pretty good. For around $7, you get two skewers of chicken, grilled onions and red bell peppers, small side salad, cuts of warm pita bread and hummus, and finally the choice of rice or fries.

I thought this was a better deal compared to Turkish Kitchen's chicken kebab plate priced at a little more than $9, just because the portion of chicken was the same but D'Yar's was more tender. There was also an array of things on the plate besides just a salad. I really liked the hummus - very smooth and creamy. I wasn't a big fan of the rice, though. Not very flavorful although it looked promising. Grilled veggies were a plus. 

Overall, it was a good meal but one that didn't make me very full. I guess this is the kind of full you should feel so that you're actually able to get up from the chair - okay this only happened to me twice. At Hometown Buffet and AYCE KBBQ.

...Or maybe I'm just a monster. I know, it sounds like a lot, but if they added a little bit more rice and threw in an extra pita quarter, I'd have no complaints!
I never really understood the to-do over their sandwiches. Caffe Intermezzo down the street is oh-so-much better.
What are you doing here?  Get your butt up to cafe Strada, people!

THANKS FOR RUINING MY MORNING.

I was Looking for a nice breakfast.
Came here because it was one of the few places open so far and there were some people sitting inside.

I came in and was ignored by the lady working here. She didn't even make eye contact with me. I looked at the menu for several minutes and still no acknowledgement. Finally I asked her a couple questions about the menu. She still didn't look at me while she was giving out peoples food.

I decided to order the number 5: 2 large eggs with 3 pancakes. I asked her if I could substitute the whole wheat pancakes with the blueberry and she said yes but its an extra 1.50 so I said "OK ill take that"
Got my food fairly fast, but while I waited I drank the cappucino I ordered here which tasted like DIRT.

I got my food and was eating the pancakes. They were so blan and gross. The worst pancakes I ever had. Eventually I realized they lacked any flavor when I asked for Blueberries, afterall my total came out to 10.22! 
I came back to her and asked her if this was the blueberry pancake and she looked at the paper she wrote and said "you didnt order them. you just asked me about it." WTF. "No, I said 'I want that'" And she said "well, i could put blueberries on top, and she motioned for the plate, then she changed her mind and ran to the register and punched in $1.50 and I was shocked, I asked "I have to pay for it?" After all, it was her mistake and it was ridiculously over prices for the shitty mean anyway!
She said "yah!  I didn't charge you for it."

How cheap do you have to be?! What kind of customer service is that.

The meal was gross. The eggs tasted like eggs, which I guess was good, but 10.22 for this breakfast?! I think not. What a waste of my money. Never coming back, save your money and go to some place better where they also have courtesy. YUCK.
For a place that looks average, the food is above average.

This is a typical mom and pop's breakfast joint.  They have a pretty extensive menu, but they are only open for breakfast and lunch.  If you come here on any weekends, its pretty crowded.  I would have to recommend the pancakes and omelettes, and the OJ.  The texture on their pancakes is amazing.  They really were perfectly cooked for the three or four times I've had them.  The same goes for the omelettes; the eggs are never too dry, and its never runny.  The OJ is also freshly squeezed every morning.  The home fries are good, but I've found them to be too heavy for breakfast (the fried portion is really oily).  The rest of the items on the menu are pretty typical, and this place does charge you a hefty premium for breakfast foods compared to IHOP or Denny's.  Their portions are decently sized.  I took off one star because their service is somtimes lacking during busier intervals.  They don't have enough hands to clean the tables, and since you have to seat yourself, you usually end up cleaning your own table before you sit down.  Also, the ventilation in this corner building is really bad.  I don't think they have kitchen ventilation, so after eating here, you'll end up smelling heavily of cooking grease.

Sidenote:  I've gotten food poisoning here before from sunny-side up eggs, so they maybe don't use pasteurized eggs?

Ann's Kitchen is definitely a breakfast place, and more specifically a hungover breakfast place. They do have sandwiches, salads and such, but those are fairly mediocre. Go here if you're looking for a lot of cheap, greasy food.

Eggs and pancakes are mediocre, but the hash browns are really damn good. I'm also partial to their fresh lemonade.

Be warned: it's not particularly clean, you won't find much parking near Telegraph, and if you're with more than three people you may have difficulty finding a table. They do take-out, though.

I'm not really a morning person, so it's rare that I actually wake up early enough before class just to go out and eat breakfast. But the few times that I've done so (in addition to hangover mornings + all nighter mornings), I've gone to Ann's Kitchen. 

I always get the omelets, sometimes with different stuff inside. Typically I recommend mushrooms, cheese, tomatoes, and avocado. Their omelets are very good - although a bit pricy - and come in a large portion. They also include home fries and toast with it...but I don't like them very much and usually don't eat it. Nice touch though!

Get the freshly squeeze orange juice too - good stuff!

It's bus-your-own-tables, so remember to throw away your leftovers and bring plates to the cart in the back. 

ALSO - they don't accept credit card. (As in they either charge you extra or it has to be over a certain amount....) So bring cash or a debit card.

Sampled the western omelette which came with potatoes and toast and also had the banana pancakes.   The omelette and potatoes were bland, had to douse it in hot sauce and pepper.  The toast... they didn't provide any jam, extra butter, etc.  The pancakes, they were ok, no clue what kind of syrup they provide.  Charged too much for a small cup of ordinary coffee.  Then you bus you're own table; which i don't have a problem with in principle, but for the quality and price, i might as well go to (*gasp*) denny's or ihop for selection; or better still back to the great breakfast place in inner sunset i went to some weeks ago.
oh and the piece de resistance, i had a tummy ache and digeestive issues later that day.

I think this is one of those "quantity over quality" things - I love breakfast food as much as the next person but this place isn't as amazing as everyone makes it out to be. But portions are enormous and it's decently good food considering what you're paying. 

I'm not a fan of their homefries (too salty), but I like their pancakes (as long as they're not whole wheat - they're really scratchy) and omelettes. They always overcook my bacon, though, and the sausages are really oily. 

The place is big but not very clean and very homely-looking. But (I'm assuming) because of all the food they give you, there's always a good amount of people in there. I'm always disappointed in their hours (they close at 6PM on weeknights and 5PM on weekends)... somehow I always end up craving pancakes for dinner. I've never been here for lunch, so I'll try to do that sometime soon.

OH. I WISH THEY SERVED WAFFLES! +1 star if you start serving waffles!

I love this place's blueberry pancakes and orange juice. The portions are big, the food is yummy, so seriously, what's not to like? Alright, I know the service is sub-par and the lady that calls out your name can't seem to pronounce anything (really, was there no one better they could hire), but it's a small price to pay for a filling, delicious breakfast for under $10.

Funny story: I once tried to watch the sunrise at the Big C with some people (obviously we didn't see the sun rise because the Big C faces the wrong side - idiots). When we came down from the hill, a bunch of cops were waiting for us, asking if we had been or had seen people camping up there. After we explained to them that we had just been watching the sunrise and that no one else was up there, my friends and I went to Ann's kitchen for an early morning breakfast. When we go there, lo and behold the same cops were there, munching on their pancakes, smiling and waving at us. We should have just got a ride with them.

Not bad food! It's great for mornings when you feel like getting up earlier for breakfast! They do a good job at making breakfast food without trying to scalp you for $2 for everything on the menu like a lot of other businesses down Telegraph. But that being said, it is breakfast food! Expect your breakfast food you can probably make at home. It didn't blow me out of the water but it was nice to not have to get up half an hour earlier to account for cooking and cleaning time.

Ann's Kitchen is a no-nonsense, student-and-group oriented type of dining place, specializing in large quantities of food that, while better than junk food, still has that air of mass-produced grease that characterizes the major fast-food chains. It's a good low-key and, as I said, group restaurant, having large wooden tables and plenty of space and a general light, open-air atmosphere, but I found the staff to be incredibly unfriendly and the meal I ordered, French toast, to be so completely substandard that I just stared at it blankly for about five minutes. It was a barely cooked, soggy mess. To me it looked like something that would be served in an Army mess, only with more sugar. When I took it to the counter, I was informed by the cashier lady that "that's how we make it here" and stared at with contempt. Having said this, I grant that the little of my friend's food that I tried was quite decent. Another drawback, however, is how noisy and overcrowded it gets, mostly with students from nearby Berkeley. Overall, Ann's Kitchen is a good place for a quick stop and/or vast quantities of food, but the worst possible if you're looking to please your culinary appetite or enjoy conversation.

Bunch of Cal students love this place, especially their homemade fries, yet I'm not particular a huge fan of it. The food is not bad consider the price is pretty cheap. However, to me their food is a bit oily, so it has a bitter aftertaste (this applies to their omelette). One thing, DON'T get their french toast delux, it's probably the worst french toast I'd ever had... other than that, this is an overall student friendly brunch place around campus.

I ordered a number one (2 eggs with homefries and 2 toast) with side of meat! It's a relatively cheap brunch place with a good sized serving. Service is nice and quick and you seat/bus yourself.

TIP: Try their apple butter!! Adds a nice hint of applesauce to your toast :)

Came here around noon on this gloomy Sunday. My friend and I crossed the street to see an enormous line forming from the counter inside to the door itself. Hungry and cold, we still decided to wait. If there's this many people, than it must be good! Good logic, no? :P

And boy was it gooood! Ordering a Number 1 on the breakfast menu along with wheat pancakes a la carte, we sat down to talk by the window and smelled the loveliness that was being concocted in the kitchen. The ladies were wonderfully polite and nice. It had a very homey feeling. 

This is a place where you can literally eat your feelings away. And they will go away by the end of the meal (that or be replaced with food coma inducing satiation)! Portions are massive. My plate was 3 neat piles of toast, scrambled eggs (perfect with Tapatio and pepper), and their insanely awesome homefries. (HOMEFRIESSSS) Potatoes done right :) Wheat pancakes - 3 massive ones stacked on top of each other along with apple butter (APPLE BUTTAA Oh my jeeez).  I was feeling a little negative at the beginning of the trip with some dramarama and sunburns -__-, and despite all the awkward sightings of certain personas all eating under this eatery's roof, I still have to say it was all worth it.  All you really need in life is a friend and Ann's Kitchen. I left feeling quite positive :) with a full to-go box left over still. 

PS: Expect a half hour wait from getting in the door to getting your grub on at crazy hours (lunch time). And I do not kid when I say massive portions. 

Bon apetit :) One star off for it being a little too crowded and humid.

Definitely changing my review. The line still sucks but the breakfast is great and super cheap. Got the #1 on the breakfast menu which is 2 eggs, toast, and home fries (kinda a mix between potatoes and hashbrowns) for under $4. I was craving breakfast so much this morning and it really hit the spot!

Ann's can be so satisfying under the right conditions. It's cheap, portions are huge, and those home fries are absolutely amazing (assuming you're in the mood for crunchy greasy heaven). I love going to this place after a long night. It's simple, the service is fast (just never go there during peak hours or on a game day), and the food really hits the spot. Obviously if you're looking for something fancier and healthier go to La Note (which I also love), but for those days when you just want a big hearty breakfast, nowhere beats Ann's. 

I do have to say that the tables are often sticky, the man and woman that take your order are sometimes grumpy (although I can't blame them since it's jam-packed so frequently), and if you go here when there's a line out the door, prepare to wait forever to get your food. Also, it does suck that they don't accept credit cards and that they're randomly closed on Tuesdays. However, all of this is worth it because the prices would obviously go up if they started using a credit card machine and/or if they hired a full waitstaff (you order at the counter and bus your own tables). These minor sacrifices are definitely worth maintaining the low price!

You can't really compare Ann's to La Note, Rick and Ann's or Venus.. it's a totally different, much more casual dining experience. It's basically a tastier and cheaper version of Denny's/IHOP that is walking distance from campus (awesome).
Cheap, good breakfast food.  Denny's and IHOP have nothing on Ann.

It's never worth getting anything besides breakfast for four bucks. Two eggs, toast, and more yummy homestyle potatoes than you could imagine. It's quick and cheap, although they only take cash or debit. Lots of room for seating and it's easy to find a spot on weekdays to sit with a whole huge group of friends. 

Here's a photo of the dish I recommend: http://www.simoneanne.com/journal/2011/08/food-anns-kitchen-berkeley-california/

3.5 stars

big portions, good food, cheap, and breakfast all day? THIS PLACE ROCKS! Got the banana almond french toast... it was huge! AND TASTY! definitely left satisfied and with a food coma. If you're ever looking for a cheap and hearty breakfast, come to Ann's.

BEWARE: seating is difficult to find.

What better thing to add to a stomach roiling with beer from the night before than THE WESTERN OMELETTE? It's filled with all sorts of good veggies and comes with a side of crunchy home fries and toast coated in apple butter. 

Ann's Kitchen is the perfect little corner greasy spoon to traipse to on Sunday mornings. Sure, your clothes kinda smell like bacon for the rest of the day, but the orange juice is fresh-squeezed (so, so sweet) and you get to people-watch on Telegraph safely behind a pane of glass if you get a window seat.

SOOOO MUCH FOOD!!!! and very reasonably priced!

I got a spinach omelet, toast, and house fries (my favorite item) for about $6. Really good, really cheap, and huuuuuuuuge portions! My plate could have fed 2 people. I was hungry and still had leftovers!!! Everyone in my table had leftovers.

The food comes within 5-7 minutes. I give 5 stars for the food and price, but minus 1 star for customer service. The lady was not friendly, and she barely wanted to give my party to-go boxes for the leftovers. I asked for 3 and she gave me 2..........the second time I asked.....the first time she COMPLETELY ignored me!!!!

I went around 9-9:30am on a Sunday morning....there we no lines. People started coming later, but it still wasn't too packed.

Ugh, I don't understand the big deal about this place. I'm a sucker for the classic American breakfast, since it's so simple and almost impossible to mess up, and I don't even need a hot shirtless boyfriend to serve it to me in bed. It's that amazingly simple. But sorry, Ann's was a disappointment. 

Service - the lady behind the register seemed so rude and not accommodating. She looks utterly bored and couldn't spare a smile. We're all hungover, not you.

Place - this place was small and the windows we sat by were pretty dirty.

Wait - while it was a Sunday morning, the wait was more than I expected. 

Food - I got the traditional plate, which wasn't bad. However, this place lacks flavor. The potatoes and scrambled eggs just didn't have any BAM to them. Crossroads, my dear dining hall, can do better than that. The potato and egg portions were pretty big. They have apple butter available for the toast, which bumps them up to a two star.  My boyfriend got the spagetti and it only had 3 MEATBALLS. Like really now? Meatballs are probably the cheapest form of meat, and you can only spare 3? Shame shame.

Price - I've had homestyle and more fancy breakfast meals, and I don't mind paying a little more for my favorite meal of the day. This place is overpriced for the quality.

Ann's Kitchen is best and cheapest place in the bay to get some awesome banana pancakes (for around $5 you get three delish pancakes topped with a dollop of butter)!  I used to frequent this place all the time when I was an undergrad at Cal, and I still love its appeal.  This kitchen serves no nonsense brunch food with generous portions, and fresh squeezed juices (try their orange juice) as accompaniments.  It usually gets crowded over weekends, but it's definitely a great place to recoop oneself pre-midterms/finals, or after a long night of debauchery!
Cheap, fast breakfast fix. Huge portions. A few ants here and there, bunch of flies, you bus your own trays. Passable.

Been here a couple times and I'm not impressed! I tried a basic pancake combo which really lacked flavor. Not a fan of the whole-wheat pancakes and the service wasn't very friendly for a sit-down place. I usually don't expect that much in berkeley since it's a college town, but everyone is always raving about this place. They forgot my drink so I had to go back up and ask and the food was kind of cold when it arrived. It wasn't horrible, but I'd rather grab a bagel at Noah's then come back here again...

Ann's Kitchen is less than a block away from my apartment, so i eat here pretty often. It's pretty much your basic greasy breakfast place, and has pretty good prices. 

However, this weekend i was disappointed to learn that they don't serve breakfast burritos on weekends. That still doesn't make any sense to me. I asked the woman at the counter for a breakfast burrito, and she said "no specials on weekends." I told her that i dont care about special deals, i just wanted a breakfast burrito.. but she said they couldn't even make me one. I don't get it. Their breakfast burritos are verrry tasty too, so I was very sad when I couldn't satisfy my craving. I got an omelet instead, and it was okay. 

I'd recommend this place for a nice weekday breakfast burrito.
Eh, pretty bad, not good

Come here! Friends here at Cal insisted I had to try this place during my visit, so we came on a Friday afternoon...for breakfast food only, of course. I was treated to #1 off the "Rising Sun Breakfast" menu which was: eggs, toast, and amazing (favorite) potatoes. Being a fyattie, I also ordered a stack of banana pancakes...yea, indulged. I tried the Western Omelette as well, and I have nothing but praise for this no-nonsense, bus-your-own-dishes, delicious restaurant. 

Huge portions; convinced?

Ann's has a comfortable, homey feel to it. I have only had lunch there so far, but have been impressed. The tuna sandwich is really good. It is simple, yet tasty--kind of like the way mom would make it.

Ann's can be crowded on weekends, but it tends to quiet down towards the afternoon, when the relaxed atmosphere invites one to linger a while over a week old Daily Cal.

Favorite brunch place!  The only downside is the huge portions... it is so delicious that I almost finish the whole thing and then I'm stuffed so I can't eat anything for the rest of the day :( 

Breakfast burrito: at $5.22, it is just a little bit over Yali's price, but over 2x the quantity and quality.  They make each one fresh!  There is a spicy sauce that adds a kick with a variety veggies.  The potatoes are crispy, but I think it would be better if the potato:egg ratio were lower.  Also, if they could have options for whole wheat tortilla and black beans instead of ham, I would permit myself to more breakfast burritos here, but among most people, white flour tortillas and ham are more popular.

Western omelette is also very good!  Lots of mushrooms and onions.  

The lady is very friendly.  I always want to speak to her in Korean but I'm afraid that I won't make sense :( I've seen that she remembers some of the customer's names and chats with them.

Ann's Kitchen is a wonderful little place, sparsely decorated, but with a fair amount of atmosphere, relaxed as it is. I ordered cinnamon french toast with a side of bacon, and it was delicious and extremely filling. The food is simple, cheap and unadorned with any excess trimmings. I really enjoyed eating here for breakfast and would definitely do so again when I am in Berkeley.

HOMEFRIES!!!!!! are the best. This is probably the only place in Berkeley that I actually get up in the morning for breakfast for. It's pretty cheap and very worth it to get a basic breakfast. The line can get pretty long, so if you're just coming out to get breakfast, I recommend calling in your order, especially if its around 10-11 AM (brunch time)
Not a bad place to go for lunch, although it was a bit busy, but plenty of room to sit. They are known for their breakfast. Unfortunately, I didn't get to try their food as I had to leave.

Very very unimpressed.  Eggs were rubbery.  We ordered sausage for our kid and when it arrived we cut it in half so it would cool faster for him and discovered the inside was seriously undercooked.  When I took it back to the counter and requested they replace it with ham, she argued with me, and even then came over to our table and tried to convince us to just let them cook the sausage a bit more.  !! Dude I don't want your sausage for my toddler after I see it served pink and bloody.  The ham it was ultimately replaced with, alas, tasted weird, too-sugary, or too-chemically-treated.  Ech.
this is another brunch spot in berkeley.  I go there when i'm super hungry and have cravings for greasy food--it's very very greasy!  But portions are large! Service is okay..

Ok, I'll have to grab a photo next time I'm there; I'm sure it says Soup Kitchen on the outside.  You pay at the counter and are expected to clear your table.  Nothing fancy.

4* because it's a great value,food-wise.  We had good, big breakfasts for cheap.  It attracted clientle looking for that.

Ambiance:

Ann's is AMAZING. Great place to go on a hungover Saturday or Sunday afternoon. Only problem: everyone else in the Greek system has the same idea. This place is constantly packed. Waiting in line takes the longest time. Once you've ordered though it takes about 5 mins to get your food: the cooks are FAST. The only annoying thing is people who are waiting in line in large parties try and reserve seating for everyone who haven't even ORDERED YET... Be prepared for rude people, or people who dont know its rude to do this in a crowded restaurant. Berkeley's a diverse place, this is the case every where you eat.

Food:

Most people get a simple breakfast plate: its cheap, its fast, and more than filling. you get 2 eggs anyway you want them, 3-4 pieces of toast with our without apple butter AND you get AMAZING homefries. The homefries are the reason everyone eats at Ann's over other breakfast places.

Cheap, fast, and delicious.  That's why Ann's Kitchen gets 4 stars.  I'm no longer a college student at Cal (Class of '05!), and this place still rocks even though I have a better budget to work from.

* Cheap: There were 3 of us, and we spent under $30 total for breakfast.  Awesome.
* Tons of food: So much of that hash fries/potatoes.  A little crispy but hearty and yummy.  I couldn't finish it.  The eggs were cooked just the way I ordered it - over easy.
* Fast: No fuss or crap.  Order the food, pay, sit down, pick up food when your name is called, bus your own table.  It's about grubbing down at this restaurant!

Great breakfast at a great price.

I usually order the rising sun, with potatoes instead of meat, which gives me a huge helping of food for the price.  I also usually add in blueberries to my pancakes.  Nice to have antioxidants to combat the deep fried grease.

I ordered the blueberry pancakes once and they were okay.  I didn't taste real blueberries in my pancakes and they seemed a bit soggy.  I like my pancakes with a slightly crispy edge to it.  My friend ordered the spaghetti and it was rather bland.  It was your average homemade spaghetti.  I think the potatoes and eggs were acceptable.  With the 15% off Blue and Gold Fridays, I might be more inclined to come here, but they do close early, so if I want breakfast food for dinner, I'm out of luck.

This was my choice for a hearty American breakfast while I went to school in the area, mostly because of its proximity to my apartment.

I do have to say, though, that the pancakes are incredible (and big) and the eggs and potatoes have a certain quality to them that can only come from a homemade style.

Don't count this place out because of its less-than-astounding appearance; Ann's Kitchen is good food at good prices and captures everything that we love about Telegraph Avenue.

I went here for the first time on Sunday and WOWOWEEEEEE!

1. Cheap!  They give so much GOOD food for so little money!  My dish was $4 for 2 eggs, toast, apple butter (mmm!!), and the famous, orgasmic, sinfully delicious HOME FRIES!

2. THE HOME FRIESSSSSasklfjal;sjdfa;lksdjfalsf x3

3. Free wifi?  Lol

4.  Fast, friendly staff.

5. HNNNNNNNNNNNG.

I never knew this place was around...despite passing by the Telegraph-Dwight intersection many times.  But a group of friends wanted to eat here, so it gave me a opportunity to have a first experience here.

I ordered the Western Country Omelette w/ homefries & toast.  The omelette had onions, peppers, cheese, ham (I think?), and some other ingredients that I don't remember...(FYI: the ingredients for the WCO were listed on the counter, but not on the menu.)  The omelette was okay, pretty ordinary.  The homefries were...interesting.  They were literally potato chunks that seemed to have been fried on one side.  Again, not too memorable.  Toast was standard affair, though the apple butter was interesting.

I haven't gone to many breakfast places in Berkeley, but the ambience at Ann's kitchen is not that inviting in my opinion...Cafe Durant is better for that.

FYI: no credit cards, but they accept ATM/debit cards (albeit with a $0.50 transaction fee)

The breakfast burrito here is fucking good.  Hands down best breakfast burrito for it's value and possibly one of the best I've ever had.  It's packed with potatoes, eggs, salsa??, and other goodies I can't even identify cause I eat it too fast to even notice, let alone care.  Just get it and you won't regret it.

And for 5 bucks, I can eat half of it and be full.  I actually usually split the burrito with a friend so we both save money and leave with satisfied full bellies.  This place has gotten the best breakfast award in Berkeley 3 years straight and I'm not surprised.  Maybe I'll update this review when I try the other things on the menu but for now, that breakfast burrito is all I need to start my day.
Cheap, home style, greasy breakfast. YUM. Seriously folk, you can't beat the price for the taste.
Cheap breakfasts. Recommended!

it was cheap, i wanted breakfast, and thats what i got! for $5 i got three wheat pancakes with a slab of butter and a side of home fries. It was a lot of food and i couldnt finish it, partly because it was so heavy/fatty and i kinda felt sick...still do. ANYwAY the pancakes are very yummy and my friend who had the banana pancakes loved them. Oh and they need to replace some of those trays, yuck!

I've never even noticed this place although I've walked Telegraph several times. The food consisted of pretty large portions. My gal had the $7.00 salmon burger special w/home fries, while I had the $8.00 super rising sun (3 eggs, 2 pancakes, meat). Maybe we're just big eaters, but I was still pretty hungry after devouring all the greasiness. Or, maybe the food just had more grease than carbs because I ate some of my gal's food, too. Yes, I was being the big pig I am. The salmon burger was quite big, but the salmon itself tasted like a frozen salmon patty you find in Costco. The surprise I enjoyed the most was my WHEAT blueberry pancakes. Finally, I've found pancakes in town that have actual chunks of fruit to devour on the inside! Another plus is the healthy wheat-y taste. Yah, they tasted good. I deducted some stars because service wasn't so great, just ok. Lastly, the bathroom was of average cleanliness.
UPDATE-sept.09:  tried to come here with my gal on a game day and the place was so PACKED several groups were waiting....well, we had to leave and i guess we'll come back next time!

i heard really good things about the restaurant but i have to say i didn't love it. maybe i'm too prissy, but no matter how good the food is, i feel kind of gross walking into an atmosphere of greasy smells. i got really paranoid that i smelled like grease after i ate my meal. i wish they had boxes of napkins available, but you're just given one with the food. i ordered banana pancakes and they were good, although i felt like i could probably have made them myself. i really want to try their salmon burger, which sounds really delicious. i went here with a friend, and it was a nice place to just chat and eat. i would probably just come here alone and eat for fun, or if there i decide to randomly come with a friend. it's good for that, but i can't really see myself saying "OMGGGG LETS GO TO ANNS!" my pancakes were around $5, which i didn't think was that cheap, since there was nothing but pancakes. other combo meals seem more worth it. the menu is very diverse and i'm certain you can find at least one thing you'd want to order.

It's really good for breakfast food-- service is quick and friendly.  The coffee is really good, I had the omelet and it was really good.  The potato things were good, but they're pretty oily.  The toast is too buttery for my taste, but I really liked the idea of eating it with apple sauce.  All in all, the food is pretty greasy and buttery (makes me feel fat), but it's decent, local breakfast food for people like me who can't drive to denny's or ihop.

Great place for typical American-diner style food and breakfast! It's relatively cheap for the portions they give (HUGE) and will definitely fill you up with their carb-heavy dishes. There's plenty of seating but gets super packed around 11-1pm on the weekends (probably when everyone wakes up and needs to cure their hangovers) and service gets pretty slow. I would suggest ordering to-go over the phone if you don't want to wait.

Dishes I've tried and recommend:
-Two Eggs Meal
-French Toast
-Whole What Pancakes (sooo fluffy and delicious!)
-Three Eggs Omelette (you can add a variety of ingredients like tomatoes, mushrooms, spinach, cheese, etc but it adds up)

Tip for owners: please have a better system of letting people know when their orders are up. Shouting their names in a loud restaurant is not efficient.
Seriously the most amazing place ever.  Supper huge portions for super cheap.  Best hang over cure ever.  Even if you arent hung over you can swim in the greasey deliciousness.

A great place to get a cheap traditional breakfast. Any of the combo dishes ($4-6) is loaded with food. If you add a side order and a glass of orange juice/lemonade, expect it to run around $7-$10. Definitely recommend the lemonade -- very sweet and tasty.

I like how the corner table by the register is reserved for the owners, who sit down and have their own breakfast whenever they have free time in-between. It gives off a nice mom-and-pop feel to the whole place.

The crowd is pretty unpredictable. Some mornings, it's incredibly packed, while on other days, you can easily find a place to sit.

When I came in last time, they were playing a Journey album. That alone deserves an extra star.

This place is pretty good for a breakfast place.  I usually get one of the usual combos of bacon, eggs, and toast.  The portions are good, and there is plenty of seating.  I like the large open windows, giving the interior of the restaurant plenty of sunlight on a lazy Sunday morning.

Given it's slightly shady appearance and almost complete lack of customers, I was really surprised that the food and prices were so good. Counter-service, decent selection of sandwiches and breakfast food. Tuna salad sandwich: quite good. Vegetable soup: bland with disintegrating veggies. The lemonade is outstanding. If it's not freshly made, they could have fooled me.

I waited for 45 minutes for my food. The frist time they messed up my order so I waited for an extra 10 minutes. It was not until I was home that I found out that they gave me the same WRONG order. The food from this place is bad and I would preter McDonald's any day, which is much cheaper and tastier. Not going to this place again.
Big portion of breakfast for cheap, fresh squeezed OJ and home fries! Oh the home fries, topped with green onions. Yum yum yum.
Closed on Tuesday. I just went and tried for breakfast :(

Ehhhhhhhh

I have heard good things about this place so I was a bit disappointed when my brunch was not quite so memorable.

We ordered the 3-egg omelet and the blueberry pancakes. The omelet is super cheap (less than 5 bucks including toast and house fries) but if you add stuff (mushrooms, spinach, etc) for 45 cents then it can add up.

 So...

The house fries were really lacking in flavor. They had a nice layer of crunch to them but were really lacking in the seasoning department. The omelet itself was... kind of weird. The cheese they used was super stringy and never really melted. And the "eggy" part didn't really have any... volume.... Instead it was almost like a thin layer of egg (or egg substitute or SOMETHING) sandwiching the vegetable contents. Pancakes were pretty heavy and you could make a meal out of just one instead of the huge stack of three you get, but they were pretty good considering I'm not the biggest fan of pancakes.

Service is pretty fast though and the portions are huge, but I'd rather spend a bit more for something more worth eating.

The food is okay..unhealthy and overpriced. More so than being disappointed by this, I was disgusted by the atmosphere. It is very loud, which makes it incredibly unpleasant. Furthermore, the entire time I ate, I could hear the top dog chef screaming at his employees--- using words I did not want my child to hear. He was very hateful and disrespectful and I don't like to support businesses, local or not, who stimulate negativity and spread hatefulness unto the community. If you like kind compassionate folk, don't eat at this place.

good food, good portions, but sorta really greasy? typical american breakfast minus the hour spent slaving in the kitchen..speaking of which, the atmosphere would kind of remind you of your grandma's kitchen.

Big portions. The home-fries are great. prices affordable 
But what's with not having the breakfast burrito on weekends.
I did try their banana pancakes and they were quite dry... I don't think I'm going to come back here.

I LOVE THIS PLACE!

I'm generally not a breakfast-y type of person but this place is just too great for words!

First of all, the BANANA pancakes. If you like bananas, you have to get these! Even if you don't like pancakes, which I don't really, you have to try it out!

Second of all, OMELET! That thing may look small, well to me it did, but MAN IS IT FILLING!!!!!

Third of all, THE HOME FRIES! Nomnomnom. So good!

And finally, it's cheap and the people there are nice.

What more can you ask for?

This place gives you a lot of food for your money, but the food is bland and just plain average. I have friends that are really into this place, but it's just not my cup of tea. I don't know if the potatoes are good, or just plentiful, but it's an alright place to eat if you're on a budget. Just remember to bring cash.

Nothing beats a cheap and reasonable place to get your brunch fixe on the weekends! Ann's Kitchen, which is run by a welcoming and friendly couple, has a homey feel to it and offers a selection of breakfast and lunch items. While the food is not incredible, it does the job in satisfying my cravings for a hearty omelett for a weekend brunch. Their orange juice is deliciously refreshing and squeezed fresh to order! I personally am not the biggest fan of their home fries, which, to me, is like a mound of deep fried potato slices that are rather bland in my opinion. However, their omelettes are huge and the side of apple sauce is a unique addition to the toast they give you. All in all, not a bad place to get brunch.

I think it's nice to have a breakfasty place. I thought their omellett was pretty decent. their orange juice (i believe) is fresh - so it's reallllllly good!

my friend said they're really rude and cheap. she asked for extra ketchup and they didn't give it to her. lol.

Got the two eggs with home fries and... something else. Forgot what it was.

My experience was definitely not great.  The lady was not exactly nice to me.  I told her when I ordered if I could have the food to go, she said yes.  However, my food came on a plate when it was done cooking.  SO...  she TRIED pouring the food from the plate into a take-out box, and USED HER HANDS TO PUSH THE FOOD DOWN when it got stuck or was about the fall out.  The same hands that she handed me money with.  The same hands she was wiping the counter with. 

Really?!  You can't have the kitchen do it?!

Really?!  You can't use a fork. 

MAYBE?!

Went in here for breakfast with the gang. Cheap food, big portions, and quick service. I had the Western Country Omelet (I think). There is a lot of potato so don't eat it all if you're planning on doing anything active 30mins to an hour later. I think it was $5 or $6. 

We went on a Saturday morning and it was pretty busy.

Oh Ann's! I honestly think this is Berkeley's answer to breakfast foods. I mean, yes, Cafe Durant is pretty good but Ann's is just heavenly!

I came here with a friend the morning of the Cal v. Arizona State game- big mistake. The line was HUGE and wound throughout the restaurant! Sigh. Better luck next time!

Regardless, we stuck through the massive line, stole some chairs from an exiting group, and finally set out to eat... I had forgotten how HUGE the portions were! I think I got an egg breakfast or something? I don't really remember the name of my order, but it contained toast, scrambled eggs, home fries and-- my favorite-- BACON!

Anyways, the bacon was cooked to crunchy perfection; honestly it felt like it was melting in my mouth at the same time. I thought the eggs were a little skinny (I like fluffy ones!), but the home fries were delicious and I always love toast [:

I feel like I forget about Ann's most of the time when I'm in Berkeley, so this review and last week's visit is definitely a HUGE reminder for me!

Bottom line: BEST breakfast food in Berkeley! Reasonable prices & huge plates- I'm loving it!

A healthy cheap meal, and pretty quick service. -   3.5 *

The quality of this place is nothing to brag or hoot about, but it gets the job done.  Good genuine portions. 

I went there and ordered the Western 3 Egg Omelet. ($5.49). It came with a side of their version potatoes hash; it is slightly crispy on one side.  The omelet has ham and green peppers and some onions in it with some mozzarella cheese, and some wheat toast. 


Ps.. You bus the tables after yourself

The atmosphere is very casual and lots of college students come here for brunch on weekends. They don't accept credit cards, only debit and cash.

Portions are HUGE.
Western Country Omelette includes three eggs, green bellpepper, ham, onions along with homefries and toast. The apple butter sauce is the MOST DELICIOUS JAM ever. The natural apple sugar makes the jam just sweet enough. The homefries are just potato chunks fried, nothing special.

TL;DR; Ann's Kitchen doesn't accept credit cards. Western Country Omelette is a good alternative to Diced Ham & Scrambled Eggs. Has three eggs, green bellpepper, onion, and ham. Never forget to request the FREE apple butter sauce.

Average price, average looks. Horrific service!

On a lazy Sunday morning sometime before 10 a group of friends and I decided to check it out because it looked "homey".  Three of the four weren't hungry so we decided to wait for the one to eat.  When the order came one of the ladies decided to tell her off about ordering one item for four people in a place that had empty tables galore.  If they were pressed for space I could understand, but I wonder if she thinks one order for 4 people is worse than 0 orders for 4 ever again!    

The French toast also tasted off, not sure if it was just that day as I never intend to come there again.

1) Huge Portions
2) Great tasting french toast
3) Even better tasting Western Omelette 
4) Fresh Squeezed Orange Juice
5) Excessive time spent in restroom post meal.

One of my fav places while I was in Berkeley. They serve breakfast food all day!

A couple of recommendations: Country Western Omlette. This sucker is huge. It will definitely get you full. It has all sorts of vegetable fillings, ham, cheese, all wrapped by eggs.

Sandwiches. Their avocado sandwich is great. Especially for lunch, when you're not in the mood for breakfast food.

Beware though, if you go during rush hour, (i.e. meal times), be prepared for a long wait (15 minutes from order to food), and also you could come out of the restaurant smelling like fried grease.

Overall it's a great place! TRY IT!

So I love a good greasy spoon and good cheap food...but yesterday we went there for lunch, there were bugs in my granola and they yelled at us for wanting our money back. Beyond rude--and the lady was pretty obnoxious just when we ordered...i'm definitely over it!

Very disappointed with this place. I ordered the breakfast burrito and it was nearly 90% potatoes. Hardly and eggs or other ingredients in it. When I went to ask the owner/manager for extra eggs, she flatly said no, "we don't do that". What gives? To make matters worse, as I was leaving the restaurant, I saw a bug & mouse exterminator exiting the building through the back door. Blegh.

Cheap food, quick service, good food. If you're tired of coffee and scones and want a substantial meal.... go to Ann's. 

BYON (Bring your own newspaper).

BEST PANCAKE EVER!! Ok, their homefries are phenomenal too. But yes get their pancakes every chance you get.  I usually get their 2 eggs breakfast and then tag on a side of pancakes.  When I came here for the first time, I was like, OK thats not a lot of food, I will finish this like it's nothing.  But when I saw the portion they have, I was in awe!  They are huge!!! So unless you have an appetite like me all the time, otherwise do get one order, but not two thinking that since it's cheap, it must be small.  
The hearty food really help when you were drinking the night before as it eases your stomach from a severe case of hangover.  But yes awesome cheap breakfast food for some of the biggest portion ever makes this place a must go after some good o'fashioned drunk fest.
-1 point for the line and having to bus your own table, o yes one reminder, go early, they always have huge lines!

It's cheap and the meal lasted me until dinner. I had the polish sausage breakfast. I don't recommend this but was just what my tunny needed after a night of strong martinis.

It was Sunday morning and all the students were there. It was packed. I'm just happy we got a seat.

Don't think I'll go back but it was just what we needed - fast, cheap and filling.

I'm a student at Cal, so I've walked by this place many times. After classes and during lunch and so forth this place can get quite crowded, so I assumed that the food here would be pretty good. And the Yelp reviews indicate that most people do think it's pretty good. But I was really disappointed when I came here. I visited with a friend, and we both felt like the food was pretty bad. I got a vegetarian sandwich and it basically consisted of avocado, lots of cream cheese, and tomatoes, lettuce, and sprouts. The avocado and cream cheese made the sandwich way to rich and insubstantial. My friend didn't like his meal much either (I think he got some other kind of sandwich).

Maybe I just came here on a bad day, but I didn't enjoy the food much and don't plan on returning.

Came here randomly for brunch one day with the boyfriend & his friend.

The food is decent.  Extra nod for the home fries & the eggs.

The prices are good, especially if you take into account the large portion size (I didn't even eat dinner that night).

Quick note: Everything there is pretty  much DIY (do it yourself); from ordering to picking up to busing tables.  Not the place to go if you are planning for a nice relaxing breakfast/brunch experience.

Ann's Kitchen has the best breakfast, anywhere.   And the price is good, too.  Atmosphere, relaxed.   Disclosure: this was my first real job way back when I took a year off of college, never worked so hard in my life, but now I just come for the food.

I come here for breakfast each week. The portions are decent and prices aren't bad either, since eggs, potatoes, and toast is only $4.34. The food comes pretty quickly and they also do take out. I think they only take debit, not credit cards.

I'm pretty disappointed this time around. I have been going here for about 3 years, and was always semi satisfied, but my experience this morning was pretty bad. We ordered #6 on the menu which is 3 pancakes, 4 strips of bacon, 3 eggs. We also ordered a medium OJ. I asked the older asian lady to put the bacon on the side because I am vegetarian. She just looked at me and said she couldn't do it...I explained I am a strict vegetarian and I cant eat anything if it is touching meat, and she looked at me as though she was exasperated but said ok. I have NEVER had an issue like this in other restaurants...even dennys or ihop. 
     The entire thing came out to $12. The food came out, and I was surprised. The eggs were on a tiny plate, the bacon on another small plate, and the pancakes were on their own plate (huge proportion of pancakes and they were delicious!). I was surprised at how little egg there was..I think she only gave us 2 of them. So, to sum it all up, I was disappointed in the service and her inability to be accommodating. The tables were sticky, there were flys everywhere and it just looked gross over all. I dont know if the food and safety administration would approve of this place, maybe i'm being too harsh but it was pretty yucky to me. I normally leave about 20% tip, but they got 0 from me this time around.

Been graduated from Berkeley for 3 years now, and this is STILL the joint I always go back to. they give you a LOT and I have never left there dissatisfied, plus they always let me take my coffee mug outside for the post-breakfast smoke!

I'm more of a waffle kind of person, but Ann's Kitchen has the best pancakes I've ever had.  I feel like they literally melt in my mouth they're so good.  It's a whole in the wall kind of a place, so you know it's good!

For breakfast they have 2 things on the menu: Eggs and pancakes. You can get these with sides or in any manner of presentation. Alternatively, you could easily make this at home for $4 less with very little time commitment on your part. 

Lunch menu is better, but weakened by the fact that they use the homefries from breakfast instead of offering a french fry option. You get more for your money with a cheeseburger here than across the street at Bongo Burger, but it's also greasier. 

All in all, nothing special, I understand its hangover appeal, and I guess it's quite successful at that, but it's certainly nothing special or even particularly good.

I was pleasantly surprised by this place- very cheap, very good, very large and fast "service." The menu selection is really great- lots of different types of pancakes, toast, and sandwiches. Like many places in Berkeley Ann's has a giant water igloo at the front and you just get your own water- which I think is great in the home of unfriendly, slow waitstaff. These were the best whole wheat pancakes I've ever had- most are way too dense and these actually manage to be rather light and fluffy. The cinnamon french toast was VERY cinnamon-y and the West Coast omelet came was excellent with lots of cool fillings. The potatoes were far from tasteless as someone else claimed, they were perfect- crunchy and nicely browned. The only bad thing is that seating is very limited and nearly impossible to get, and I don't particularly like sitting at a table with two hungover guys boasting about the chicks they banged last night.

Love their breakfast!!
Cheap and good portions :)
very fast and good location
And ask for their apple jam/jelly/spread thing at the counter for your toast, it's like apple sauce but it's delicious!

Ann's kitchen. Hmm.. Finally I could find a place to fill my morning appetite. There's so many places around Berkeley where I can pay a shitload and it still doesn't fill me, defeating the ultimate purpose of food. In the future, I think people should recognize who I am and that I can EAT. Anyways, I've tried a lot of things here. I advise staying away from sandwiches since although they are good, they are greasy like some fat dude's face after walking up Berkeley hills. I think the burger is okay, definitely has  a homemade feel. I eat that sometimes. I usually go here for breakfast, getting the Super Rising Sun, Western Country Omelette(usually I choose my own omelette now, even though Western Country a great deal) or something similar that has homefries. I like their homefries and I wish they would teach me the recipe by the time I graduate.

The food is probably not five stars but I feel like giving them it since it's all relative. They served me when I needed them the most. *tears*

Holy heck I HAVE BEEN MISSING OUT!!

I have been to Ann's Kitchen at least three of four times, but since I am not, as many profess to be, a "breakfast person," (and I usually go around lunchtime anyway... my friends are not early birds), I usually opted for the lunch-ish options: garden salad once (uninspired--go to Intermezzo if you want a really excellent, interesting salad), avocado and cheese sandwich with lentil soup once (kind of salty, if i remember correctly).

And lunch prices are only standard, for Berkeley. Not horrendously expensive, but not dirt-cheap either.

Breakfast, though... is a whole 'nother story.

The combo I ordered the day was their cheapest combination but SO DELICIOUS ohmygod I miss it already. The portions are extremely generous: 2 pieces of wheat toast, sliced diagonally with a little cup of apple butter (a bit like concentrated apple sauce), two eggs prepared however you like, and a slab of golden, crispy-soft-beautiful homefries.

Let me just say, I polished off my plate despite suffering horrible stomach cramps from a less judicious restaurant choice (Pintoh, I'm looking at you!!) the day before.

Does Ann's Kitchen conquer food poisoning? No. But for a sweet, sweet hour I forgot my more base, more vulgar sufferings, and instead ascended to breakfast nirvana.

I had bad coffee before but Ann's Kitchen was by far the worst I've ever had. I took one sip and then another -- and my wife and I came to the conclusion we've wasted our money and had to dumped it. It was undrinkable. I told the person at the counter as we were walking out but she could care less. We should've gone to Pete's right across the corner.

they give you more food than you could ever eat in one sitting...excellent. And it's cheap depending on what you eat and the restaurant itself is nice, quiet, and a pretty good environment to fight a hangover in.

My friends have been talking about how cheap this place is for bfast, so i was super excited to come check it out. Finally came here for lunch the other day and it was pretty packed by the time we got there (around 12:30pm). 

I ordered their 3-egg omelette with cheese and mushrooms. Came with home fries and 2 pieces of toast. The omelette was amazing, I like it slightly runny on the inside and there was a lot of mushrooms and cheese in it. Honestly, this was probably one of the best omelettes ive had..it was just delicious and done just right. The home fries were crunchy on the top and flavorful, and I had my toast with the apple butter.

I didn't really expect this place to have such good food at such cheap prices. Best bfast place near campus. Can't wait to come back for that omelette.

Unassuming place, but good food, amazing fresh squeezed lemonade/OJ, and good service.   Had the veggie Salad- very generous portions, with all sorts of good veggies in it (not just like the usual garden salads places give you).  This salad had romaine, tomatoes, cucumbers, sprouts, half an avocado, boiled egg, pickles, cheese, and even 2 perfectly toasted pieces of garlic french bread. ...all for only 5.95 I think it was.  

They also had a bunch of breakfast foods on the menu that looked really good. yum pancakes.

I'm addicted to the homefries.  Eggs, hella potatoes, and toast for 3.95 - I'm set. The fresh squeezed OJ is also amazing.  Definitely best as a breakfast place, but I had a couple good sandwiches here too. But this is absolutely 5 star breakfast. So cheap, and so.good.

This is a great, affordable, and homely place to have a weekend brunch with friends :) The plates they give you are very large. I usually get the basic plate with toast, eggs, and potatoes and it always fills me up. Weekend brunch lines are super long and it's even hard to find a place to sit, so try to come either a bit earlier or later than normal. I love their apple butter too! 

I think the next time I come, I'd like to try one of their actual lunches. The salads look amazing.

This place is pretty special for me. I used to come here every Friday for some brunch with a group of my friends. Service is always nice and friendly. But, sometimes on Sundays it gets really hectic in terms of the sheer amount of people that are in there. I definitely recommend getting any of the breakfast menu items! Omelets are pretty good, and can be suited for your heart's desire! The hash browns and toasted bread round off the whole meal to put me in a place of contentment and later, food coma. They definitely give you more than you can eat, which is definitely awesome for the price. Other than the omelets, I recommend getting banana pancakes and perhaps split the cinnamon french toast. It's not outstanding, but it's satisfactory!
The food isn't anything special, but it's good for the price. It seems like the staff gets confused with the orders when busy, but it's easily fixed. Mostly a student crowd.

This is definitely my favorite place to get breakfast.  I've eaten here maybe four times now and every time I love it.  Omelettes, pancakes, everything is great.  Be sure to get the lemonade (or orange juice) as that is excellent as well.  Service is reasonable.  My only complaint is that it seems to be priced a little high.  And I don't like menu schemes that have the base item (say, omelette) be too plain to order standalone, making you add on a bunch of add-ons (mushrooms, sausage, etc.).

Even despite the pricing issues, the food and service make up for it for it for a definite winner.

My friend's friend's mom and aunt run this place so I'm here with her quite often for weekend brunch. I'm not fond of their sandwich menu - my salmon burger frankly was too dry and weakly seasoned, and my friend's generic burger wasn't very remarkable. However, they do serve  good breakfast all day. Their home fries are crispy and greasy and delicious (probably the best I've had), topped with a sprinkling of green onions. Their wheat pancakes are huge and filling. The omelettes are good, and the western omelette with ham, pepper, onion, and cheese is a great deal. If you are eating with a friend, get the Sunrise Special - you get pancakes, home fries, eggs, and toast for less than $7. Most other items are under $6. Lines are usually long, but the food comes out relatively quick. Overall, Ann's Kitchen serves up hearty, tasty food that will make you feel warm and fuzzy inside.

Plusses: cheap. Nicely cooked potatoes, nice crisp.

Minuses: stand in line to order, bus your own table. Kind of dirty. they do NOT take credit cards, and they charge $0.50 for debit.

Only table open had dirty plates and syrup. Nothing to clean table, so we got some paper napkins and poured drinking water to clean. Yuck.
