Potatoes were unseasoned. Omelette was quite average.

Kind of like a slow, slightly pricier, slightly better food, slightly dirtier McDonald's.

I would give it 1.5 if I could, but I'm rounding down because the yelp rating is stupid high at 3.5

I stopped by this place for breakfast before I had to catch a plane back home for break. I ordered their breakfast burrito, but was disappointed with the content (or lack of) inside the burrito. They advertised that it had ham, but it had about 10 really tiny pieces of ham that didn't even count. :( Instead, the burrito contained mostly potatoes, and I almost had to throw away half of it because I couldn't stand how dry it was. But, the staff seems nice, whoot.

Ahh! So great! Large portions, decent price, quick service! This is another one of places where you order first, then have to seat yourself and bus your plates at the end though. But if you want a hearty, filling, affordable brunch, this is it! Plus, you don't have to deal with the snobby SLOW waitstaff commonly found during Sunday brunch.

Burnt Pancakes and bland homefries...
OJ was really sweet and tasty.
Though prices seem cheap it is relatively expensive ccompared to any other diner type place.

The food was greasy and made with bad ingredients. My brother's broccoli soup tasted like it was straight from a can. Thin coffee. I left with a stomach ache. The man behind the counter was sort of rude and made me feel rushed to order. I won't be back, there is so much yummier food in Berkeley, and for lunch the prices really aren't that great considering the bad quality.

I've lived about 3 blocks from Ann's for the past 5 years and only this year have I started eating there, thank GOODNESS I found it!

For a very fair priced and well made breakfast, this is THE place to go.  Don't expect great ambiance, its full of students on weekends and gets pretty noisy.  But the big windows are lovely on sunny days and its a fun location to look out onto Telegraph and all that is Telegraph.

The two things I can't get enough of there are a) the potatoes.  seriously, no better ones in the bay  as far as I'm concerned.  Crispy, potatoey, amazing with some ketchup.   And second are the pancakes.  I love a good whole wheat pancake and Ann's has some awesome ones!  Really nutty flavor and if you get the pecans, MMMM, so good!

Its just cheap and easy.  A little crowded at brunch times on the weekends, so come prepared. 

Oh, one odd duck thing that I sorta love now, they only have "apple butter" for the toast, but honestly, its just applesauce.  But its really good I think!  Just kinda wierd the first couple times.

Enjoy some good cheap grub!!!

I am a fan of good pancake.  They got awesome banana pancake.  I am a fan of cheap eat.  They are incredibly cheap.   I am a fan of greasy food...

It's populated with mostly UC Berkeley students, so expect to stand in line on Sat/Sun. 

On a rainy day, the place reeks of cooking though.  Dear Ann, if you're reading this, I love your place.  Please charge 49 extra cents so you can afford a better ventilation system.

Some of the cheapest food in Berkeley.  Ann's is a no-frills kind of place.  If you are hungry and want a hell of a lot of food for not that much money go here.  The eggs and hash browns have very few spices (which some people might like).  The best thing about this place is that they give you a tiny cup of applesauce with each meal...regardless of what you have ordered.  The applesauce is actually really good.  Generally filled with hung-over undergrads.  There is pretty much always a space to sit (which is nice) and good chairs.

This place is alright. Nothing special to it, but it is convenient that it has breakfast. The fresh squeezed lemonade is SOO good! However, the food here is stuff anyone could make at home in like 10 minutes. I always find the potatoes to be overcooked, and sometimes the omelets are the same way. The people at the counter always seem stressed out and in a hurry; they don't really take the time to smile or be friendly! Oh and one time I got the ravioli, and it tasted like they just opened a can of Chef Boyardee. The food here really is subpar, but it's a good place to eat on a lazy Sunday morning/afternoon.

I like to think of myself as somewhat of a pancake connoisseur. I always order pancakes if I can. Ann's has by far the worst pancakes I've ever had. Maybe it's because of the whole wheat ingredients, but I just did not like it, so much so that I couldn't even finish, and I ALWAYS finish pancakes. If on the off chance that I do ever return here, I'll keep my expectations low and stay clear of the whole wheat pancakes.

I came here an hour before my first class with my boyfriend. We decided that I needed some food before going to more class than I should when I have my boyfriend over.

 I got the Western Country Omelet which included onions, bell peppers, cheese and ham. It says that there was spinach too, but I didn't see those or taste them.  It also comes with house fries, and toast, but seriously it's so much food. I only finished about 2 pieces of toast and the omelet. Regardless, it's so worth it! 

My boyfriend got scrambled eggs, bacon, the house fries and toast; he on the other hand finished the whole thing, but it was delicious! I really enjoyed breakfast, but it seems like everyone else does too! 

The food comes out pretty quickly which is nice when you're really hungry! The asian lady seemed pretty nice. Regardless, it was great to try this place. I think the next time if I go, I'll just share something with someone. It's really too big for one person unless you'll be sleeping right after due to your food coma!

Anne's is solid 3 far cuisine.   I usually opt for the sandwiches when I come here.  

Whenever I come up to Berkeley, I have lunch with Father Al, a Catholic priest, who counseled me when I attended Berkeley.  

He loves this place.  I never ask him where he wants to go, because, well, that would be stupid of me suggest any place other than Anne's Kitchen (I think he has no interest to try all of the great other places on Telegraph).  I think he likes it not so much for the food (because the food, IMO is simple, uninspiring, but decent) but because of the people that run it.   

He told me that every year they do free Thanksgiving dinner (the day before Thanksgiving) for folks who have no home, friends, or place to eat dinner.  They started doing this years ago.  I think it is for this reason that he likes this place.   I think they definitely deserve a star for this kind gesture. 

All in all, there are so many great places in Berkeley, I'm since I'm a foodie, Anne's probably wouldn't  be my first choice for dining around Telegraph.  But, Father Al would definitely beg to differ.

Oh Ann, your omelets never fails to snap me out of a hangover.  Or is it your fresh orange juice that does the trick?

Regardless, I'm glad you're there on Sunday mornings to help me wind down a crazy weekend.  I think a lot of others agree, seeing how you are always packed and I have to fight for a table all the time.

Cheap, greasy food that to me is synonymous with hangovers.  You get pretty good portions of food that all sorta looks and tastes the same.  Coming here any Friday, Saturday or Sunday morning guarantees you quite a wait in a crowd of other bleary-eyed hungover people.  

Ok, I'm too hungover to write anything else exciting, and I have a lot of grease in my belly from the meal I just ate at Ann's. Nap time...

The good:
They prepare your food fairly quickly. The food tastes great. Portions are extremely generous. Lotta seating, generally lotta students on the weekends tho. The grilled sandwiches are very good!

The bad:
The food is kinda greasy. Don't like the pricing; almost 3 bucks for 3 sausage links... Come on... They are tasty, but not that Tasty... 

Cnoclusion: Wake up, hung over, tired, hungry? This is the spot.

This place serves amazing hearty huge plates of breakfast and that's all I've ever gone there for. Omelette fillings are kind of expensive and the wait is often long and tedious, but that's because it's worth it. Still, when you're hungover and craving homefries and toast, watching the guy behind the counter take orders at the speed of a glacier is frustrating and the only reason I took off a star. Easily the best breakfast I've had in Berkeley.

This place is what I would like to call the college campus breakfast delight!

Be warned, this place gets ridiculous busy on weekends (mostly Sat and Sun, wait . . . that's the weekends DUH)  and you may have to wait in a long line, but if you wanna have a good ole American breakfast with extremely large portion, this is the place.  

Though this is "American" breakfast, i still find it humorous that its run by Asians!  Maybe we should convert this to food place from American cuisine to Asian cooked American cuisine.

great place for big breakfasts after a night of drinking.  nothing special inside, it constantly looks like they just moved in for some reason.  but the service is fast and friendly and the prices are low!

Anns Soup Kitchen!

although I don't fully understand this name. 

Ann's is Amazing!
I was born and raised in the south and this happens to be the only place I have found that is as close to it gets as real "southern breakfast"

the price is actually remarkable for the area.

you must go.

Ohhhh Ann's Kitchen. Their breakfast/ brunch foods are the best; enormous portions and really delicious food! I'm a big fan of their fluffy omelettes and home fries, they really hit the spot when you're hungover and woozy the day after a big party. Remember to ask for their apple butter and to try the french toast here! 

I'm deducting one star because this place is almost always crowded (especially during the weekends) and it isn't the cleanest.

Two words:  Edible hugs.

I get the whole wheat pancakes with a side of sausage every time.  It's the kind of food that forces you to smile because it makes you feel so good.  I'm full for hours, it's always satisfying, and you get a HUGE amount of food for the price.  

Only drawback is that the place is almost always full of obnoxious college kids or NPR-ents.  Obviously, Ann's can't help that, and I don't fault them for it.  However, this does translate as a little more noise than I'd prefer sometimes.

Alot of good, greasy, breakfast foods with a usual line to the door waiting to get in and for a table. Service is alright. This place is local spot, cheap, good eats but I wish they cared a bit more about the upkeep of the place.

Everyone seems to rave about this place as an awesome breakfast place, but personally, I've had better. The home fries were the best part, cooked perfectly, but the toast was on the hard and chewy side while the eggs were on the cold side. A good thing was that the food was prepared fairly quick, but I'd rather it be quicker if it'll ensure my meal is still nice and warm by the time I eat it.

The place itself could be cleaner, though it often gets really crowded so I suppose it can't be the cleanest. There's only so much to expect at breakfast - i.e. eggs, pancakes, toast, waffles, etc - but I'd stick with other breakfast diners like iHop.

Cheap food, and filling food. This is the perfect kind of breakfast place for college kids on a weekend morning (or anytime actually). The banana banana walnut french toast I would highly recommend. It's probably the only non-egg/toast/hash item you can order there from the breakfast menu.

If you're here to meet up with a friend and/or to study, look elsewhere. This place is LOUD, and it's honestly just a place to eat, like any high school cafeteria.
Delicious, fresh, huge portions, cheap. You can easily share an order with somebody. I wish I knew about this place earlier in my time at UC Berkeley.

Large portions, great breakfast/hangover food. The one thing I noticed that I thought was funny was that I saw a couple that was an Asian guy with a white girl. I haven't seen that in a LONG time. Anything is possible.

Amazing, cheap breakfast. When it's not really busy, this is a great place to just eat and chill for a bit with a book or some homework. I'd recommend it on a weekday morning, b/c it gets pretty chaotic on the weekends.

This place puts the greasy in greasy spoon. Many a hangover has been cured with a healthy portion of Ann's delicious homefries.

No oregano-basil poached egg nonsense here, just the basics. Heaps of homefries, grilled sausages, bacon, ham, pancakes, and/or waffles. What you see is what you get, and there is absolutely nothing wrong with that.

Pros: Very good potatoes, whole wheat pancakes and scrambled eggs; cheap.

Cons: You have to order at the counter and bus your dishes; she barely cleaned the table- still had lots of crumbs on it; no napkin dispensers anywhere; on a Sunday, there was no wait but the food took nearly 25 minutes! This makes me not want to go back and there's no way I can give 3 stars if it takes that long for just two breakfast entrees. Also, I don't like the college dorm cafeteria vibe.

I went to Ann's  for the first time last week for coffee and the breakfast burrito special, both reasonably priced. I was attracted by the cheery, local feel of the cafe. I was disappointed to see that the coffee was served from a glass carafe that had been sitting on the warmer-unfortunately it did taste burnt/stale. Somewhat lackluster service but not bad-it was not at all busy when I came in mid-morning, just two other people already eating and myself at the counter for takeout.
My breakfast burrito was a great size portion, but it was way too greasy, and some of the ingredients seemed to have seen fresher days. 
Also, read what's included in specials carefully! Although I don't recall if "ketchup" was listed for my special,  I was surprised to find my burrito with a lot already added, enough so that it was marginally gross tasting when combined with the overly greasy fried potatoes. I ate it, but only because I was very hungry and didn't have time to walk back and complain or get something else.
I will give Ann's another try because they have a good reputation for breakfast; maybe their other specials will prove better, although I'll avoid the coffee!

Anne's kitchen is like the fratty version of Crepevine.

College kids (including my former self) come here on weekend mornings hungover as balls, looking for nourishment and a place to discuss shenanigans from the night before. 

Expect to wait quite a while to order and I would suggest keeping a sharp lookout for tables. Keep your brunch plans somewhere between a tête a tete and a party of four if you expect to find seating at all. If you can't find seats and you have a penchant for danger, you can take your food, walk a block over and watch the microcosm that is people's park.

The food: regular breakfast dish comes with two eggs, toast and a mountain of breakfast potatoes. Really delicious breakfast potatoes. I personally prefer russet potatoes over rose for breakfast potatoes and this place uses russet!

This breakfast is a great deal price-wise and the proteins present in eggs are supposed to be essential to recovering from a Friday night alcohol binge.

The blueberry pancakes are also extraordinarily delicious and satisfying on their own albeit a tad pricey for pancakes.

Overall, great stuff. Definitely going to miss bringing my out-of-town friends for brunch here!

3.5 stars

My friend and I went on Sunday morning. We both got the Western Country Omelette and we shared an order of French Toast. Although the line was long, we were able to place our order The omelette was good, but there wasn't anything that really jumped out about it (other than the fact that there was a lot of food). The homefries that came with it were really good as they were crispy, but not dry, so I liked it. The French Toast was delicious though. It was topped with nuts, bananas, and a thin layer of sugar. None of the flavors were overpowering, and the bananas tasted fresh. This is somewhere I'll probably go back to .

The BEST whole wheat pancakes I have ever had. Ever. They're amazing. And there's THREE of them!!

We also got the eggs, toast, and potatoes, which was awesome! The eggs were really fluffy and the potatoes were nice and crunchy on the outside. The prices are extremely reasonable for such huge portions. For a scrumptious $5 breakfast that can last you through lunch, Ann's is the place to go!

Delicious breakfast and healthy!  It really is like eating good home cooking.  Everything is fresh and healthy.  I really don't know where the negative ratings and comments were coming from - I have never had a bad experience.  And the portions are huge for a really great price.

You have to bus your dishes yourself, but it just makes it seem more like home after that nice home-cooked meal.

Great place to come in the morning especially if you are a little hung over since its near campus. The meals are great and very filling. I usually get the western omelet which comes with home fries. The home fries here are different than what you may find in other places. This is more of a cross between regular home fries and hashbrowns because they are stuck together.

Delicious Breakfast Food!!!  I love their Western Country Omelette, and the homefries are awesome too.   Only downside is the cashiers are not very friendly, but who really cares when the food is so amazing!

Still the best breakfast burrito ever.  Everything else is just fine, but the homefries inside... oh man, I would drive back to Berkeley just for one of these babies.  

I also really love their applebutter with their toast.  I never knew about applebutter until this place.  Now I don't like jam with my toast.. Applebutter all the wayyy

This place is one of the best, affordable, good-sized portion breakfast places in the area!  The home fries are great, and I would definitely come here again and again.  Definitely recommend it for a breakfast and brunch place.

These stars are all for the quality and quantity of the food here compared against the cost. If you order right you should never have to spend more than $7 for the best and most filling (and okay possibly greasy enough to kill you) breakfast EVER. I swear by the home fries, which -- despite repeated tests of multiple recipes and variants -- I have never even come close to replicating. Potatoes are crisp on the outside and still a bit soft in the middle, without being greasy. Everything else on the menu is, in my opinion, just icing on the huge helping of home fries cake. Though the cinnamon French toast deserves a shout-out if you're looking for sweet rather than savory -- it's always too much for me to eat on my own, so I usually only order it when my mom visits, and we split it. The sides are predictable, nothing out of the ordinary, though do ask for apple butter for your toast -- it's free, but they've stopped giving it to you automatically with your order...

This place may not have any real atmosphere to speak of, but it doesn't need it -- the line out the door on weekend afternoons says enough. Also, as someone who enjoys the ability to sit and linger over my food, possibly with a bit of schoolwork in tow, this place is a godsend. No one is going to try to make you leave your table as long as you have ordered something. 

It might not look like much, but if you're looking for the breakfast of champions on a student budget, look no further.

I definitely gotta lower the rating of the breakfast burrito because

1) breakfast foods is only served before 3pm on weekdays
2) breakfast foods are not served on weekends

So on several occasions, I was unable to get one :[

Last time I had it was friday, but this time - the potatoes were not as crispy...

When I am in need of breakfast food and want to spend very little on it I can rely on Ann's Kitchen conveniently located across the street from where I reside. They are always busy whenever I come in which proves their bomb breakfast food. I always get their #1 with a side of sausage and I eat everything except for only half the potatoes/home fries. Their sausages are delicious as well as their toast! I love breakfast food and I am happy that Ann's Kitchen is there to cater to my tastebuds.
Nobody has pancakes like Anne's! I'm addicted. They are humongous and so delicious and the price doesn't get any better. I heart Anne's.

Perfect for breakfast. I had an omelette with cheese, bell peppers, and mushrooms. It was a good idea they put mozzarella instead of, say, cheddar. Potatoes on the side. Tiny portion of applesauce at the end to cleanse the palate.

Three and a half stars. I've been to Ann's a few times now and can't say I've been overwhelmingly impressed, but I haven't been disappointed by any means either. There's nothing here that will blow you away, but the quality is high here, the portions are generous, and you'll feel satisfied. I pretty much always get the number one on the breakfast menu (two eggs, toast, and potatoes) but you really can't go wrong with any breakfast item. 
Lots of people also comment that this place is really cheap, which it is. But I think it's sort of deceptively cheap... the number one is $3.95, but if you want a side of bacon, ham, or sausage, it's an additional $2.25. If you get the meat (which I do because, well, I love meat), it totals to almost seven dollars after tax. That's not outrageous by any means, but I don't know if it constitutes "really" cheap. The number two is the three egg omelette with toast and potatoes priced in the four dollar range. But the omelette doesn't come with anything in it, so each ingredient that you want to put in the omelette is an additional $.45. Again, it's not bad, but in the end the price is just about what you would expect for an omelette anywhere.
Anyway, I'm probably just being nit-picky because all my friends told me this place was really cheap and I found that to not exactly be the case. So the lesson here is to be a better friend than mine. Be real with your friends, kids.

Just thought I'd write in a note for this place since I've been dropping by every few weeks or so for years and have loved it. Their #1 breakfast of homefries and eggs is simple but really well done, a satisfying breakfast for a very reasonable price.

I was ever so slightly disappointed when I asked once if I could just get 3 eggs in it and the lady refused -- I'd have to get the omelet . I did try their omelet once, and it's alright, but not the best I've ever had. I generally only go there for breakfast, but the rest of their menu looks pretty good.

The food here is really quite delicious and portion sizes are huge! Their potatoes/tater tots are very fluffy and they give you a ton. I also love their whole wheat pancakes--also incredibly fluffy, and taste healthy with a grain-y bite and very delicious.

When I came here there was definitely a bit of a wait though. Also, I ordered two plates of food for me and a friend, as well as a beverage, and it came out to almost $20, so not exactly the cheapest! If you just get a basic plate it's definitely a good deal though; they don't short you on food.

I also really recommend their orange juice. Bittersweet, really refreshing, and pulpy--it's the definition of fresh-squeezed.

My roommate took me here on a Saturday morning for breakfast so I could try their breakfast burrito. Unfortunately, they don't have the breakfast burrito on weekends, nor do they have smoothies. Poo. (hence the 4 star instead of 5)

The place was also completely packed but we got lucky and found a table right before we ordered. We order 2 western omelettes to split between 3 people and we were completely stuffed! Each plate came with a generous helping of perfectly done home fries and an omelette packed with ham, cheese and other goodies. It also came with lightly buttered toast and a small cup of apple sauce. Every bite tasted really good too.

I'm really glad we came here for breakfast but I do wish they didn't limit their selections on the weekends. I was really looking forward to the breakfast burrito.

By the way they only accept cash or debit so be warned.

If you leave Ann's Kitchen hungry, you either have a tapeworm in your digestive tract, or you simply don't know what to order. This place serves hearty breakfast food in huge portions.
Homefries - Crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. I feel like the crispiness isn't consistent from plate to plate. I like mine extra crispy and am convinced that whoever I'm eating with always has crispier homefries.
Toast - Buttered for you. 
Ham - Eh. Not mindblowing. I probably won't get this again as a side.
Western Omelet - Cover this baby in ketchup and you're set!
They also offer sandwiches and soups, neither of which have I tried.

I have yet to completely finish a plate here. Definitely the place to come if you're running low on cash and are ravenously hungry from a long night. At Ann's Kitchen, you definitely get what you pay for, and much more.
I had a cheap cheesesteak here and it was decent.  I don't think I will come back.

Caveat: I hate eggs so I haven't tried most of their stuff.

The stuff I HAVE tried is ok, and it's all pretty darn cheap. The homefries  = delicious future heart attack, weekday breakfast special = possibly best deal in Berkeley, pancakes = edible. Service is usually pretty grumpy when I've been.

Let me just start out by saying that the food is actually good.  But the pricing scheme is so annoying.  I don't eat meat, but I usually like putting a bunch of junk in my omelet.  Having said that, the #4 (or was it 3 or 5?) would be PERFECT if I could only have it without the ham.  Lo and behold, that's not possible.  So I have to build my own omelet, which is the exact same one as the special but minus the ham, but this costs me $2-3 more because ingredients are 45 cents each.  OK so maybe they already have the batter pre-made, but that's still kind of gross when you think about it.  Plus I can order the same thing at Cafe Durant for so much less.  And if you like the orange juice at Anns, you'll like the one at Cafe Durant also since they taste exactly the same.  Oh yeah, and they charge you 25 cents if you ask for a to-go box.  Who does that?!

And I really don't like the lady there.  The man who works there once in a blue moon is a bit more polite.  Oh yeah, and the atmosphere is really really sweaty.

DAMN was the cheesecake BAD...words can't even begin to describe what it tasted like. It was a combination of expired, minty grossness...sort of like toothpaste. That makes it sounds better than it was. But then again, you don't come to Ann's Kitchen for the cheesecake. My friend only got it because he wanted some...

Otherwise, the breakfast food is decent. The Country Western Omlette (or wtv it's called) was great with a plethora of fillings (ham, spinach, cheese, mushroom, onions, etc etc.). Also came with lots of home fries and toast. (too much to finish!)

Summary: come for the breakfast food, DON'T GET THE CHEESECAKE!!!

Banana pancakes
2 egg breakfast 

Love this place because its fast, convenient, gives you loads of food, and breakfast foods are good anytime of the day. 

Taste-wise, its nothing special. But it sure beats cooking a whole breakfast meal for yourself.

Alright, you have to try their whole-wheat cinnamon pancakes. They are a ridiculously good idea that I have never had anywhere else. Their plates are also quite large and very affordable. You can get a stack, eggs, bacon/sausage, and potatoes or some fruit/toast if you want for under 10 dollars. It beats going to Denny's or IHOP (of which there are none in the area, thank goodness, and it seems like the place is family-owned. The eggs come out runny, and the pancakes hot. Seems like there's always room, and they open fairly early. What's not to like?

I was really pleased with the omelette I got from Ann's since it was bigger and had more veggies than I thought. The homefries were okay, nothing special, and I did not appreciate how the toast came buttered already. The toast was also more on the burnt side than I would have liked.

Later in the day, my boyfriend returned with a pastrami sandwich. I only picked at the sandwich filling since it was absolutely and digustingly LADEN with mayo on both sides of the plain white bread. 

They also do not take credit cards.

The food is pretty good, there's a lot of it and it is definitely affordable.  They also validate for Sather Gate which is good if you drive since there is never any parking but that's where good things about the place end.

I realize the place is self-serve and I am OK with that.  I don't mind busing my own dishes or coming to the counter to get my food when my name is called.  However, just because that is the style of restaurant you have doesn't mean you need to be rude to your clientele.  

When asking for a validation coupon I was treated badly (even thought we spent more than $20 and the minimum for validation is $5) and I was treated even worse when I asked for a couple of to-go containers.  I do not believe it is unreasonable with portions that large to ask for a box for each person and I don't believe I should have to pay a quarter for each when that isn't posted anywhere.  If they would give me one small one for free (as one person), then for three people we should have gotten three small ones or one large one for free without a problem.

I came here for breakfast quite a few times in my stay at Berkeley, and I've always gotten the omelets with toast and potatoes. The juices they serve here are really fresh and yummy. The service is also very quick. The only issue is that it can get really crowded, and the hours are very limited. Go here for brunch/breakfast!

I'm not usually a breakfast person, but on this one particular day, I was in the mood for breakfast food. So while I was in Berkeley, my boyfriend's friends suggested we go try out Ann's Kitchen, and I'm glad we did.

Ann's Kitchen has this really relaxing atmosphere to it. It gives you a sense of relaxation where nothing is more important than having the most important meal of the day. Maybe it was because the sun was hitting at just the right spot, the weather was unusually crisp, or the fact that I was starving, but it was a wonderful day to have breakfast.

I ordered the Beef Polish Sausage and Eggs ($6.95), but these entrees should really come with a warning sign because when I got my breakfast, it was huge! They are really generous with their portions and it was definitely worth the $6.95. The entree came with homefries (seasoned potatoes) and toast. It was a delicious meal with a delicious price!

College student on a budget, come here! You will have plenty of left overs for lunch.

Really convenient for students and pretty cheap. The restaurant could be a bit more well-kept and maintained but I suppose it IS on telegraph ave. so can't ask for too much

Sometimes their potatoes are undercooked and thus a bit hard... not the best tasting... this is one of my pet peeves since well cooked hash browns like that are SO GOOD.

Pancakes are generally pretty good, they're HUMONGOUS but not that special...... they're just big. 

They give you this weird like apple sauce as jam with their toast... this is the first time I've seen that... and maybe it's a way they save money? I don't really care for it that much. They charge you for refills (if I remember correctly) but free water that you get yourself. 

Oh, another thing, they don't clear up their dish tubs enough so sometimes you smell the leftover food and you have to manage to leave your plate in the tub without breaking it. sometimes challenging. 

great place to bring large parties for brunch because they are pretty flexible with letting you make your own long tables (because it is just a bunch of small tables that you can put together). pretty good variety and convenience but altogether low quality.

Super cheap breakfast! 2 eggs, toast and way too many home fries for 4 bucks. Everything's greasy but in a good, hang over remedy way.
Bacon's extra but comes crispy and in a hefty serving.

Blueberry wheat pancakes are also really tasty and fluffy, but not super cheap. 6 bucks for a stack of 3. OJ is fresh squeezed. Coffee's pretty bad but the chai latte's pretty good. 

Pretty grungy but it's cheap Berkeley food so what do you expect?

In my last review I gave this place 2 stars, but I had brunch there this morning and tried their Whole Wheat Pancakes...........bumped the rating up to 3 stars.

I STILL think it's your typical traditional American breakfast style so it's not 4 stars, but 3 stars for their pancakessssss! Yum.

I usually don't enjoy breakfast foods unless the sun is down, but my friend was craving a breakfast burrito and I owed him lunch so we headed here after class.  It was a hot day so we grabbed cups for water but the water trough thing was almost empty, so he tipped it and I held the nozzle as we filled our cups.  Later, as I raised my glass to take a drink my friend grabs my arm and removes the cup; we both stare at the cup and realize there are more brownish particles than water in the cup.  SERIOUSLY.  I wish I had a microscope so we could see what was in my water, it was so disgusting.  We put our water away and took out the bottled and canned drinks we had and drank that, trying to forget what we just saw.  I ordered one of the specials, which were blueberry pancakes with hash browns and my friend got a ham and cheese breakfast burrito.  When our food was ready, I realized they made me buttermilk pancakes with a side of scrambled eggs.  HUH?  I didn't order this...and how did eggs get in the picture?  She didn't ask me how I wanted my eggs...eggs I never ordered.  However, they were coming out with peoples orders pretty fast so I just manned up and ate the food so we could leave and forget the whole ordeal.

The food was okay and the prices were decent.  However, I don't think I'll be coming back here.

Honestly, was not that excited to come here since I live in SF, and there are a ton of brunch places there (and even in East Bay) that from the outside, look way better than this. With that said, never judge a book by its cover! 

+: Cheap w/ good portions
+: Crispy potatoes
+: Hearty pancakes
+: Fast and easy. Who wants to wait 2 hrs for bunch anyway? Instead, you can choose for a number of seats.

Ambience is definitely lacking, but who cares, you got darn good pancakes in front of you?! I can't say it's worth crossing the bridge for, but if you do find yourself in east bay, just go here. Don't bother waiting at the fancier places.

When I think of a sit down breakfast place, I think of Ann's Kitchen. They do pancakes right. Their sandwiches are good, but not top notch. They give a decent amount of food and the pricing is right. There really is no service here (the extent of the service ends the moment you finish giving your order to the person who works the register), you get everything yourself. Unless you need something from the kitchen, which they are glad to help.

Overall, a solid place to get breakfast food all day. Unremarkable in most ways, but also reliable.

I have never received worst service in my life! I went around noon for some brunch and I expected somewhat of a wait. When I arrived there were only about 4 people in line and a few people waiting for their food, but it still took 40 MINUTES (!!!) to cook my food! I am not the kind to complain and demand my money back, so I simply waited (finishing 4 cups of water in the meantime). I ordered the omelet (which doesn't even come with cheese, you have to pay extra) with homefries (which were average). I didn't have the juice that everybody is raving about so I can't critique that, but overall this visit to Ann's kitchen was terrible.
Robust vegetable soup for a great price.  I don't find myself on Telegraph much these days, but really look forward to stopping by here for lunch when I do.

Ann's Kitchen = yums in my tums! tehe I went with a friend before summer school for the first time. I ordered the Ann's Special (2 pancakes & their home fries) & I was freaking satisfied. The pancakes are REALLY filling & their home fries are just amazing! I'm coming back fshos!! =)

Ann's Kitchen is one of my favorite cheap places to come for brunch! 

I always come in with a sweet tooth and end up ordering either pancakes or french toast. Both the banana pancakes and cinnamon french toast were great. I also tried the pecan pancake, but was super disappointed. I guess I was expecting candied pecans, so I found the nuts really bland. The pancakes are pretty filling, and I can never finish the whole plate.
The western country omelette is also really good. They don't let you substitute or remove any of the filling. It also comes with homefries and toast! You can ask for free apple butter to go with the toast, which is like the consistency of applesauce. 

The food is good, and pretty cheap. The only thing is that there are sometimes long lines and it can be hard to find a table, so come early! :)

The portions are HUGE here! And pretty inexpensive too! I got a Western Omelet, which is cheaper than a regular omelet with fillings if you aren't picky about what goes inside (onions, mushrooms, spinach, tomato, ham, cheese, and no substitutions). And it comes with delicious home fries and 2 pieces of toast! There were a lot of onions in my omelet, which was a little weird, but it was delicious nonetheless. But my favorite were the home fries! They're skinned, cut into little chunks, and fried and crispy on one side, yummmm.

Also tried some of the Cinnamon French Toast, and it was delicious as well! You can really taste the cinnamon, and it was sweet and fluffy! I would suggest coming with a friend and splitting a sweet and savory dish, because just the pancakes/french toast alone might be a sugar overload.

I came for brunch on a weekday so it was pretty empty, but it can get crowded on weekends!

As tradition has it in my reality, before I set out for a great snowshoeing or backpacking adventure I need....  PANCAKES!!! 

Ann's serves these awesome granola cakes made with whole grains and a sprinkle of granola to get your grub on for that 15 mile trek near Shasta or the Doe Ridge Trail/Jackson Flat loop in Butano. 

And while I must say the Pancakes are wonderful, its the potatoes you keep coming back for. Browned with a nice crust, a meal in themselves. If you get there before 9 there in nary a crowd , though it is often a bit busier by the time I need to cruise to Mo's for book shopping.  
The staff is quite friendly and there are some characters that hang out on a regular basis to help with the ambiance, plus the sub 5.00 plates help start your day.

Oh Berkeley, I love your food :) This was the last restaurant we dined in before we went home. 

This place doesn't disappoint. I ordered a simple breakfast platter of pancakes, bacon, and eggs. Although the pancakes looked a little burnt, they actually taste pretty good. Very filling.

I also ordered a bacon and cheddar sandwich to go. It wasn't anything special, and I thought it was kind of bland. If I were to come here again, I would only do breakfast!!

Because of it's proximity to my workplace, I end up eating here about once a month. That's about to change, because the under-cooked potatoes aka "Home Fries", while not without their rustic charm, are no longer tolerable.

I did eat here many times before I reached this epiphany because there are good points to Ann's. Besides being among the cheapest places on Telegraph, the service is also fairly quick.

They may appear rude, but I think they are just tired. The Telegraph Ave. crowd can get to you after a few years, so I can sympathize. 

They also are closed on Tuesdays. Third-Day Adventists, perhaps?

3.5, but I rounded down.

Prices have gone up as expected but the portions are more of less the same. I can't seem to justify paying $3 for a side of potatoes, esp when potatoes are ridiculously cheap. Anyhoo..

I come here typically for the Super Sun Rise (3 whole wheat pancakes, 3 eggs, side of meat).  I added a side of homefries today just for a change and I'm addicted to carbohydrates. Pancakes were good as always, as were the eggs. The potatoes erred on the greasy side however, but still good until you forked up the last bits soaking in oil. 

Overall, my favorite breakfast place in Berkeley, as I can't stand La Note.

Solid diner type food in a casual environment. 

Since moving to the Bay Area, I've noticed that as far as food in the East Bay goes, people are really really into 3 things in particular: Pizza, Brunch, Ice Cream. 

There are SO many brunch/breakfast spots, and more than that, there are so many acclaimed, popular, wait-an-hour-in-line breakfast spots. It's like every weekend, that's just the thing to do. Brunch. 

I've tried a lot of well known spots. La Note, Bette's Oceanview, Brown Sugar Kitchen, 900 Grayson, Rick and Ann's, etc. And some I've liked, and others have been disappointing. But the thing they all kind of have in common is the super long wait, and the rather unconventional breakfast items. And that's fine. But sometimes all you really want is a homey "standard" type breakfast, and a lot of it. 

And that's exactly what you get at Ann's Kitchen. Very little wait at 10AM on  Saturday morning (woohoo!). 

The food comes out pretty quickly and the plates are heaped with food. The bacon is crisp, the eggs perfectly cooked, the orange juice is fantastic, and the pancakes are great too. Nice standard meal, but done well. I like that. 

So if you're not looking for anything too fancy, but good solid food that's comfortable and relaxed, then this is a great place to go. 

I will say though, I was a bit confused by all the praise given to the  "applebutter". It really seemed like nothing more than a small tablespoon scoop of applesauce. Not sure what the hype is about on that.

After a heavy night of drinking, the place to go when you awaken from your alcohol induced coma is apparently Ann's Soup Kitchen. I'm pretty sure over 50% of the people in there are recovering and are super hungover, as was I. Although i'm pretty sure mine was not nearly as bad as most people's in there. In any case what beats pancakes, eggs and bacon? So much food for not so much money. Its great. My only problem with this place is the tables are quite sticky from the lack of table cleaning and excess of syrup. All in all, a great place to get some food back into your stomach after you puked it all up the night before.

Alright, just because I am a poor berkeley student does not mean that  I have to stand for crappy breakfasts close to campus. Even though their breakfast items are dirt cheap, their food tastes like it was cooked by a 10 year old child born without a sense of taste, smell, or sight... the frenchtoast I ordered was a triple whammy of violations. It was to the point of being offensive. Taste: it was dry and chafed my tongue. Smell:It reeked of too much cinnamon and nutmeg. Sight: It looked like they threw the bread down the ski slopes there was so much powdered sugar on there. I had to windshield off most of the gunk on top to even get to the toast... but unfortunately I couldn't get past the crusty eggs hanging off the side from their sloppy dipping into the eggbatter before frying. In conclusion, I definitely could have made a better breakfast at home this morning. fml.

This is THE place for a filling and cheap breakfast. The portions are HUGE and the potatoes are yummy. I've had the Western Omelette and the cinnamon french toast. I wouldn't recommend getting more than 1 thing at Ann's Kitchen unless you just eat A LOT.

The western omelette was great, it tasted good. (You cannot substitute or take out any ingredients because they pre-mix the omelette mix)

The cinnamon french toast is AMAZING! I love it. If you're ever graving cinnamon french toast, Ann's Kitchen is the place to go. I'm in love with their cinnamon french toast.

The only down-side was that I went on a Sunday morning and the line was incredibly long and it goes very slowly. So if you're planning on coming on a weekend morning be ready to wait because the line will be long. The wait is definitely worth it.

The food is really greasy and kind of expensive. You get a lottt of it, but it's nothing too special. I'd much rather pop some toast into the oven myself or head over to cafe durant for a cheaper, just as filling, and a bit more flavorful meal.

There is a 50 cent fee for using your debit/credit.

TIP #1: Be prepared to wait on weekend mornings. Ann's Kitchen is popular among college kids who may have had a late night.. you know, studying!

TIP #2: Doesn't look like a table's open? By the time you're done waiting in line, it'll probably open up. 

TIP #3: $0.50 charge for debit cards. 

This was THE place to go if you're one of three people:

1) A college student who's tired of dining hall food. It's not much different here--eggs, toast, homefries, pancakes--but it's a different atmosphere. Sunny and airy, busy and bustling, versus the sterility of Crossroads and the stern glare of the elderly woman serving you the Blue Plate Special. Here you have Ann (right?! That has to be her name!) who takes your order, rings you up, and smiles at you, and then the cooks in the kitchen who pop out with your plate when it's ready. 

2) Hungover or extra tired. It's early, the sun is searing laser beams into your eyes--just order that Western Country Omelette or chocolate chip pancakes (or whole wheat pancakes for a healthier alternative), sit down, wait, and then chow down. You will be happy. Fill up your cup with water at the cooler to the right of the counter. 

3) You don't have much money. Everything here is cheap--mostly under $7--and the portions are huge. Cheap and yummy--what else can you ask for?
 
I fit all three of those characteristics a few years ago. Just passing my knowledge on to my fellow Cal bears and campus community!

I was an avid Ann's goer. I work in the area the food is cheap and tasty enough. However, I called today to place a to-go order as I have done on many days. I asked the gentleman what the soups of the day were. He told me. I asked what the specials were. Just as I was about to give my order for pick up he told me 

"come over, ok? I don't have time, ok? "

"but, I'm just trying to place a to-go order"

*click, dial tone*

Riiiight. 

I'll tell you what. You don't have to worry about my business anymore. Time consuming as a one minute call may be. 

If you value service, don't go here. If that's of no consequence to you, knock yourself out, it's a decent meal.

Taste: 3
Value: 4
Service: 3

I've been here a couple times (around 5-6), and it's decent brunch food. I usually get the half turkey sandwich and soup combo (around $7). The turkey sandwich is pretty standard, and the soup is usually pretty good. Home fries are pretty good as well.

The lines are sometimes pretty long, and the place gets pretty crowded around brunch time. They seem to have really weird hours, because sometimes they're not open in the morning, and sometimes they are. They also have "breakfast all day" written outside, so it's a bit confusing. Perhaps they're only open on the weekend and some weekdays?

In terms of brunch food, this place still has nothing on La Note or Venus. However, it's close, cheap, and okay, which is good enough for me. I haven't been back for a while since I usually eat milk and cereal for breakfast every morning though.

Also, they only take cash and debit, so keep that in mind.

Wow, Ann's Kitchen takes the cake when it comes to bad service. I've never been a fan to begin with, but after my last experience here, Ann can rest assured that that will be my last. 

One day I came with my brother for some early morning breakfast, paid for the two of us and before our orders came, I stepped inside the men's room to wash-up. Literally, three minutes later I walk out to find the owner yelling at my brother. Apparently, they gave us an extra pancake by accident which my brother had just cut into and were yelling at him because he had taken a bite out of it. 0_o As if their mistake was our problem. 

In any case, this just reinforced my perception that this place is nothing short of a dump. It's only a matter of time before they go bankrupt.

Ann's is a no-nonsense, you get exactly what you order, and it's good every time sort of spot. There's nothing to write home about, but at the same time, it's great because you know exactly what you're getting. Can it compete with the fancy Berkeley spots like Rick & Ann's, La Note, and the Sunnyside? Well, no. But I don't even put it in the same category. I go to Ann's when I want eggs, toast, and meat, cooked exactly how I ask, fast. When I want oatmeal with a side of fruit, piping hot, in 3 minutes. You get the idea. I don't go to Ann's when I want a crab benedict with a small glass of blood orange juice. If you adjust your expectations accordingly, you should be pleasantly surprised.

The food merits probably three stars: it's ample and greasy, probably the best breakfast you're going to find on Telegraph, if you're too hung over to make it to a less irritating neighborhood, or if you're a student and aren't yet able to perceive how irritating the neighborhood is. The four-star rating is motivated purely by nostalgia.

I used to live less than a block from this place, and I think I went there for Sunday breakfast every single weekend I was there. I would roll in at one or two in the afternoon with the Sunday Times, order an omelet, and spend an hour or so reading through the front section, the Week in Review, the NYT Magazine, the Book Review, and whatever else seemed interesting, while finishing off my eggs and home fries at a leisurely pace and getting refill after refill of coffee. I always gave a fake name when I ordered ("Max"--after Maximilien Robespierre, of course), because I never could recognize my real name the way the staff called it out when my meal was ready. Those were good times, and Ann's is one of the few near-campus establishments that I hadn't learned to absolutely loathe by the end of college. 

They ticked me off by ditching the somewhat edgier "Ann's Soup Kitchen" for their current name. They also ticked me off one time by refusing to take a $20 bill when I was in a hurry and didn't have smaller bills. And however much I liked the place when it was conveniently located, I've almost never gone there since and I can't even remember the last time I did (it was at least two years ago, maybe three). But God damn it, those Sundays reading the Times there were just so damn pleasant.

Went here for breakfast and it was pretty epic. I think for eleven dollars my sister and I split a three egg omelet with veggies, several pieces of toast with apple butter (delicious and free), a huge portion of home fries and a giant stack of whole wheat pancakes with syrup. We were both stuffed and it was seriously cheap. I would definitely come here if you want a good, hearty breakfast. It's not gourmet by any means, but if you want comfort and portions this is a great place for brunch and to hang out with friends.

When you can't have pho, a cheap heaping plate of breakfast food is the next best thing after a night of heavy drinking...

One of my friends tended to a hangover with toast and OJ as I finished off my plate: 2 slices toast, 2 eggs, and homefries, and then another friend's banana pancakes. (Friends and restaurant patrons alike looked on in wonder.)

Bonus: they did my over hard eggs perfectly! I always order my eggs over hard, and I don't eat egg yolks. (I suppose I could order egg whites only but I enjoy a more colorful plate.) So I like to be able to pick out my egg yolks nicely without sacrificing the white. These yolks happened to come out in perfect, easily pickable golden circles.

Why don't more people order eggs over hard anyway? Like, sunny side up? That's freakin' gross man... once you poke that thing it's like a bad pimple bursting on prom night. 

Their sandwiches didn't look nearly as good, and you do have to bus your own tables. I hate doing the dirty work.

Went here last week for lunch. Surprised by how good the food was - I had a grilled cheese sandwich and cream of broccoli soup (I know, possibly odd selection but I'm a soup fan).

Very chill environment, I like the fact that its well lit with the huge windows. The owners are as nice as can be. Service was prompt

All in all, would recommend anyone who likes great-tasting diner/deli foods. I hear breakfast is awesome as well and cheap

I'm such a sucker when it comes to quantity, quality, and a great price on a meal!!

And yes, like everyone else on Yelp has said -- the home fries are amazeballs. Or as my friend, Nicole, said: "the home fries are the shit."
I got the Western omelet which was stuffed with a bunch of veggies and goodies. It was definitely a hearty meal.... lots of carbs, too. Don't forget to ask for the apple butter to spread onto your toast! YUM!!!

Bonus points for Ann's Kitchen for taking on my health conscious request for using egg whites only!! And also major kudos to the employees there. They were busting their butts to get the orders in and food out! 


My only gripe is the line... but that's understandable. Totally worth the wait!! Excellent breakfast spot after the spending the night out =)

One of the better places to eat breakfast around campus.

Service/Decor: I quite like the retro vibe given by the restaurant, as if I'm walking into a 70's diner. Most of the tables are next to each other and not separated, which is a bit of an inconvenience. It's also rather loud and not the best place to have a quiet conversation, but food comes out pretty fast and you'll be on your way quickly. Proximity to campus makes it a favorable location for the college student.

Food: Ann's Kitchen is known for its breakfasts, and most of the items on the menu are not bad. I generally get the the Western Country Omelette, which comes with onions, ham, bell peppers, and spinach, and it comes with home fries and buttered toast. They've recently raised their prices to $5.95+tax, but it's still not a terrible deal. As for flavor, the eggs in the omelette are very overcooked and seems like its individual toppings were just stuffed in after the omelette was cooked. I do believe most people come here for the homefries and toast, which can be eaten with the apple butter that you can get for free at the front. The homefries (I believe they're yukon gold) are colored very well and crisp, though bland, and the toast is pretty tasty with the apple butter. Seasoning (or lack thereof) seems to be a major issue here.

I've also tried their whole-wheat pancakes, banana pancakes, and pecan pancake. They're just alright, but I found that they were unsatisfying and I craved something savory after eating them.

If you feel like eating breakfast or brunch and you don't want to go to the dining commons, this isn't a bad place to start your day.

Despite its outside looks, this place is super homestyle good on the inside.  Delicious, huge fluffy wheat pancakes, a stack of 3 for about $3. Eggs, toast and homefries for about the same... you could live off these meals!  The orange juice was super fresh and extra tasty as well.  Its a homey neighborhood kind of place.  I'll be coming back!

was actually looking for lunch... but the sandwich place we wanted to go to was closed so we ended up winding our way through the weirdos of telegraph till we found this solace of normalcy. 

omelet and homefries - awesome! (was confused by the applesauce)
whole wheat pancakes - yum! (too much butter)

the place has an old-world feel about it (or maybe it was the accordion music from across the street) and is homely and straight-forward. you have to clean up after yourself, which is kinda cool, really. gives you a nice 'berkeley' feel.

cheap. simple. no frills. and breakfast served all day!

I love this place... #3 breakfast menu, all the time. Cheap, and lots of food. So... so... delicious.

It's too bad it isn't open that late, and sometimes, it's so damn busy in there, it's impossible to get a table, but I've always been able to get one by the time I get my food. I think their service is pretty fast, actually, not sure what other people are talking about... and I avoid going on Sunday mornings because I know it's brunch time, and I don't bump into too many moronic hungover fools. =] If they were present, I was not made aware, so it couldn't have been that bad.

If you love breakfast food around the clock... this is it.

Ann's Kitchen. Yay!

One of the better establishments that sell a variety of breakfast/lunch foods. It's usually bubbling with activity but I went around 5PM with my friend so it only had a few customers. They accept both cash and card but add an extra fee for using the card. :( They do not have a waiter system but it's a bus-your-own-table style place which I prefer at times. After all, this isn't some huge chain restaurant with a thousand workers scurrying back and forth but (I'm guessing) a family-owned place.

The restaurant has a very homey and diner feel to it and it relatively well maintained by a Korean couple. How do I know? Because I spoke to them in Korean. Supporting my culture all day breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Anyways, food comes out in time and there was no delay of any sort (except that they didn't have an ingredient for one of their smoothies so I had to order the Rising Sun smoothies). Their omelette, toast, potatoes, and bacon come in very hefty portions and is great. Their smoothies are also good (Rising Sun) and they claim to put in protein powder, but I have no clue how that works. Pineapple based smoothie with protein powder? Interesting...

The owners are very nice, attentive, and food is good so this is definitely a place to hit up when you're looking for a heavy breakfast type meal any time of the day. :)

When I was an undergrad at Cal, post-party deconstructions took place at Ann's Soup Kitchen. With plates of scrambled eggs, buttery toast, and homefries served with glasses of fresh orange juice, my girls and I would gossip away about the events that transpired the night before. Despite the tables somehow suffering from maple syrup over-indulgence and the overall lack of ventilation in the restaurant as a whole, Ann's was a favorite spot for a post-apocalyptic brunch. I dearly miss those girls as we now span the breadth of the country, and Ann's will forever remind me of my wonderful youth spent at Cal.

Ann's Kitchen is the spot to go to when in Berkeley. Unfortunately, I moved and can't come here as frequently anymore. But when the craving hits, I take the drive to come order my usual- Denver omelette and a stack of banana pancakes. 

The pancakes are heavenly and the omelette is hearty and delicious.
what more can you ask for?

Oh yeah, I almost forgot... get a large OJ, the best I ever had.

dude, it doesn't get much better than this : two eggs and three pancakes: whole wheat granola (slightly more expensive than regular whole wheat) but they are bomb ass pancakes. hits the spot and big enough to share if you go with a friend and don't want to have pancake thighs.

Not sure what others are talking about in terms of Ann's lack of customers.  Almost anytime on a  weekend  or 9am-11am weekeday is packed!  Several times I have had to head to Durant Cafe (by far my 2nd choice) because Ann's line is out the door!!!  Super Rising Sun is far too much food for any one human, but it's such a crazy deal (2 eggs, 2 huge pancakes, bacon, homefries for somewhere in the neighborhood of $5-6) that you have to get it.  Don't miss the homefries, fresh squeezed lemonade or the granola pancakes (sounds weird but they're delicous).  I can't speak to lunch but for breakfast the price is right, the food is good and the curemyhangover quality can't be beat.

Went to Ann's Kitchen today since La Note and Venus were closed. All I have to say is I fell in-like with this place for sure!!!

The food was "get-your-grub-on" deliciously great! I wasn't expecting anything spectacular so this place blew me away! 

I was indecisive when ordering and the girl who was working was understanding and patient with me. I ordered the diced ham and scrambled eggs with a side of french toast. 

I really enjoyed the potatoes since they were cooked just right - crispy! The eggs were good and the french toast was also delicious. It's those crispy potatoes that got me though. 

The freshly squeezed orange juice and lemonade were great too!!!

I highly suggest this place to anyone and everyone for sure! 

Four-thumbs up!!!

BEST heart attack in a bowl breakfast place around Berkeley! i love their country western omelet with home fries! Their portions are huge and usually I can split the omelet into two meals. More about the homefries....they are fried to a perfect crisp,sprinkled with scallions, just dip it into ketchup and you've got yourself a winner! I don't really understand the whole apple sauce as jam concept but it's grown on me and I really like it now. (but they are so frugal with their apple sauce portion). 

I would give them 5 stars but they have the worst service ever. The place is run by an Asian couple who seem miserable with their lives and love to take it out on their loyal customers. One time I called to ask what time they closed and without even answering my question they hung up. Giving them the benefit of the doubt that we had lost reception I called back and politely asked the same question again, "Hi there what time do you close today?" By then the man who picked up was so infuriated that I had the balls to call twice to ask the same question that he literally grumbled, "GO AWAY!" It was a great laugh for me to hear someone so worked up over a customer who was just trying to give them some business. jeeeeze.

Traditional breakfast fare; eggs, potatoes, bacon, sausages and pancakes.  I don't particularly like the home fries though, where are the hash browns?

The orange juice here is quite good.

Food's cheap and it's a great place to come with good company and spend an hour on a Sunday morning.  Especially if your company is a Bear.

For the price and speediness and overall taste, I'd give Ann's another breakfast star. 

Everything feels very home town and good, and the portions are huge for what you pay for.

This restaurant, only blocks from my humble abode, makes the perfect next-morning hangover cure.  The reason for their near-medicinal comfort is definitely their home fries.  I love potatoes, and these are the best potatoes.  If potatoes were my children, these potatoes would be the child upon which I lavished more attention than the others.

The rest of their breakfast menu is pretty standard and good.  I haven't really had experience with their non-breakfast items as they serve breakfast all day and even when I've gone there later in the day I've gotten breakfast.

The main reason I give them 4 stars and not 5 is because they lack air conditioning and are usually a little uncomfortably hot; not hot enough, however, to keep me from coming back for mo' taters.

The owners of this place hate me and my friends. D=

Well, not that bad, but they certainly always seem moody when I try to order there. They never let us do substitutions or customizations and the lady is always angry, like this D={. Kind of disappointing, especially since they get such good business there, too.

Food-wise, they're okay. Nothing spectacular or special and it's a place I don't really care to go to, given the vast variety all around Berkeley. It's just another place to hang out with other Berkeley folks, and it's a place you're likely to run into someone you know if you go to school there.

Home of the home fries.

In college, Ann's Kitchen was a real treat. I remember coming here during finals to power up. Big portions for small prices. They have killer omelets, mounds of home fries and fresh squeezed orange juice. The one thing that disappoints me is smelling like grease after eating here. Anyway, it's a lovely mom 'n pop shop. Check it out.

Tips: Bus your own tray.

Cheap greasy breakfasts!! Long wait for weekend breakfast/lunch hours and seating can be limited so watch out for that.  Not sure if it's the healthiest because their store their Crisco in spray bottles in the back....bottles and bottles of it might I add....but mmmm....greasy bacon is worth it. Recommend their Western omelette that is just under $5 with homefries and toast. can't beat that.

Worst.Service.Ever.

I understand the appeal: huge portions of greasy lackluster food while you rub elbows with students that reek of alcohol on Sunday morning...oh, wait, what was so great about this place?

They give you a good portion of food, yeah. But the potatoes are usually tasteless and way too greasy for me to not fear a heart attack after consuming them. Also, they're really rude if you want to substitute anything? Don't want potatoes? Well, how about 3 slices of tomatoes? That's all we can do. Oh wait, let me ignore you while you're mid-order and turn around and pay attention to this person back here! Counter people lack basic people skills. That's all.

5 years ago....

Me: Are you Ann?
Mrs. Ann: No, that's our family name.
Me: Coooool.
Mrs. Ann: =)

Good food, huge portions. One order can probably fill two people.  Minus two stars for lack of cleanliness (flies, dusty window sills, dead flies on dusty window sills, marked floors, bad bathroom, questionable water), crowded mornings, and sweaty workers. I give them an extra star because they serve the best home-fries ever. Thank you Ann family.

the bf and i stumbled across this place after walking around the area for what seemed like an eternity. the place i really wanted to eat at, the UNICORN restaurant, was not open, so we settled for ann's kitchen. 

at ann's kitchen, it's all about self-service: you place and pick up your order at the counter, seat yourself, and bus your own tables. i'm guessing that they're able to keep their prices so low because they don't have to deal with all the hosting, waiting, and bussing bs. 

anyway, their menu offered pretty standard diner fare: sandwiches, burgers, pancakes, eggs dishes, daily specials, etc. i ordered from the daily specials menu, and got the salmon burger (freaking risky choice) with fries. the bf ordered some kind of pasta dish. my memory is hazy  now - probably cloudy from all the grease from my salmon burger. 

did i mention the burger was greasy? it was uber-oily - like the patty had been stewing in a vat of recycled oil all morning. i got a major case of greasy-mouth. you know the kind of greasy mouth you get when you eat something that's just got way too much liquid fat absorbed in it (e.g., fried chicken, fried pickles, double-fried-french-fries, deep-fried-macaroni-and-cheese). 

overall, ann's kitchen is not special. it does, however, serve affordable and edible food. so, if you want to fill your belly up with cheap food, and lube-up your lips, try out ann's kitchen! i'm sure they will serve you an extra helping of lard with your pancakes.

3.5 stars.

Good breakfast grub here, my friends.  And reasonable as well.  I had the western omelet which at Ann's includes onion, green pepper, tomato, cheese and ham.  Maybe mushroom too.  Anyway, it was really good.  It came with home fries and toast.  

Basic, tasty and filling diner style food at a reasonable price.  I would absolutely keep them in mind for a quick and satisfying breakfast.

uggghhh... LONG BLACK CURLY HAIR embedded in my home fries. 

blehhhhhhh. 

im sure ive eaten a good amount of hairs by now, but do i have to SEE it, glaring back at me, all oily with bacon fat?

time to try sunny side cafe on north side.

The wait was a bit long for diner food, but at those prices, I shouldn't complain.  What I can complain about is the total lack of seasoning in the food.  There wasn't the slightest hint of salt or spice in anything we ate.

I agree, the portions for breakfast here are HUGE and cheap-er than Denny's. Oh and I think the pancakes I got were wheat which was a healthy surprise. Also, I normally don't like pancakes because they're usually made too soggy for me. Ann's does it right! 

I came here with my friend who recommended it for breakfast. She also said she loves their house potatoes. I've had better. The potatoes (there are pictures) are just pan fried? Maybe with some salt, but I've had some where they put some onions/garlic to flavor them. I needed lots of ketchup to make the potatoes edible - at least to my tastes.
This place rocks. I've been going for years. So cheap, and so good! I always get 2 eggs, toast and home fries. I think its $3.65! You will be TOO full if you eat the whole thing.

I love breakfast foods, especially on the weekends.  Davey R. says it's the "country girl" in me, and I don't argue.  I wandered into Ann's in search of a place to fill up with a solid breakfast and to use their free wi-fi to start on a big work project.  

I walked up to the counter and ordered my standard breakfast meal--which happens to be #1 at Ann's;  2 eggs, potatoes, toast and bacon, plus I ordered an orange juice.  Looking at the board above the counter, I thought what I had ordered was $3.95 plus the price of the orange juice.  (What a deal, I thought!)  When she told me my bill had come to $10.15, I was surprised.  Over $10 for a pretty basic breakfast seemed pretty steep to me.  What I didn't realize was that my side of bacon cost me an extra $2.45.  That board of theirs is a bit tricky!

I went back to my table to wait for my food thinking I probably wouldn't be back.  The environment at Ann's is pretty basic and not especially comfortable.  My orange juice was served in a broken plastic cup.  $10.15--really?  I'm happy to pay that much for breakfast at nicer establishments with inviting environments, but Ann's is not that place.  

I was already writing this review in my head (because I just could not get over the mix-up with the cost of the meal) when my name was called.  And when I saw my plate, I wasn't upset about the $10.15 anymore.  Maybe it was the satisfaction of my hunger that helped me get over the misleading sign, the price of the meal, and the broken plastic cup.  But Ann's actually has a great breakfast.  My plate was heaping with eggs, potatoes, crispy bacon  and toast.  The potatoes were served with green onions on top (yum, yum) and the potatoes were crispy on the outside and perfect in the middle.  I asked for my eggs poached--which apparently Ann's doesn't do, but over medium they were pretty good.  

I did have problem with the wi-fi and ultimately didn't stay for much longer than the time it took me to consume my huge meal.   Overall though, Ann's is a nice little breakfast spot.  Just watch out for prices on that tricky board!

I love love love this place!

Its a basic breakfast and brunch place, but what it does it does so well.

The food itself is what one would expect from a breakfast menu and the portions are more than decent.  You can mix and match, get a dever omelet ect. ect ect.

Why not five stars? 
The seating was always an issue for me, the line can sometimes curl around your the place where you are sitting and i never liked people watching me eat.

It is also a nice place to people watch

Are you hung over, early for class, or skipping class?  These are the only reasons you would be looking for breakfast near UC Berkeley.  This place will probably make you happy in any event.  I had eggs, homefries, toast, apple butter, and sausage.  It was good. 

Parking will probably be hard, but they do validate.

I'd like to try the breakfast food here because I suspect it will be better than the lunch meal I had. It was a salad and half sandwich. Tasty but not as healthy as I was hoping-- the bread had butter or oil and had been grilled. Took me by surprise. It was kind of hard to communicate clearly with the woman at the counter but it was even harder (and more amusing) for my friend with a thick German accent. 

Worthy of another try, probably the breakfast next time around. Will update accordingly!

This place is definitely cheap. I got an omelet with tomato and cheese with potatoes and toast for around 5 dollars. Cha ching! Service is very fast too. I placed my order then scurried back to my car to put more money in the meter and came back within 10 minutes and my food was already waiting for me. 

As for the food itself...it's decent. They definitely skimped on the tomatoes and cheese in my omelet, and it wasn't cooked well in some places. The potatoes were good, and I liked that the toast came with apple butter. Portions are generous, especially given the price. The atmosphere here is plain, kinda dining hall style, especially with the busing your own table part :P

Top Pick: French Toast Deluxe

I love eating breakfast, whether in or out, but it puts a dent in my wallet. Fortunately, breakfast meals here come in large portions and is super cheap! I can almost never finish a plate by myself. Breakfast is served all day, but there are other items like sandwiches, pastas, and soups. If you go too early in the day, the soups will not be ready yet. The omelettes can get a little runny, but they taste pretty good. The breakfast entrees are highly recommended and the pasta entrees are highly discouraged. Truth is, I can probably make every item on the menu, which is why I generally choose to eat at other breakfast places. However, it does feel homey here and it's not because I live so close to it.

By the way, the apricot and grapefruit juice on the menu is just canned Kern's. I knew it was too good to be true!

Also, the new red awning looks much better than the tattered old blue one.

Also, cash only!

Probably the cheapest place you can get a well rounded meal in Berkeley. Granted its full of carbs and fried goods but for $4 you can't whine. The menu variety is pretty good and the food actually taste good (probably better than what anyone can make for $4). Plus, they have tea it's like eating in some Chinese province. This place is a 5 star, top notch restaurant for all the Shylocks out there.

I'm a little creeped out by the last thing I ordered there.  The teriyaki chicken in "combo 2" is half a whole chicken, smothered in teriyaki - bones and all.  I've come to expect that teriyaki chicken from places like this be pieces of meat (without bones) covered in teriyaki sauce - usually a pretty safe thing to order.  What's creepy about it is that you're getting about half a bird for $4.  What's wrong with this meat that they can sell it to you for so cheap?  

I'll probably come back in a budget crunch, but won't be ordering that.

My last two years of high school, I happily lived off of two hole-in-the-wall places in Shanghai. Both places were dirt cheap and piled on MSG like no other, and they were GREAT. Then again, I'm pretty much immune to the effects of MSG and thankfully didn't have the itchy scalps/painful kidneys suffered by some of my friends. Thanks for the iron stomach, China!

This place is in the same spirit. It isn't as cheap -- I don't think you can beat 10RMB bowls of noodles in CA -- and it isn't as good, but if I can get a giant plate of edible ma po tofu, a small bowl of egg drop soup (however corn starchy), and a coke for under $5, I'm a happy camper indeed.

Fun fact: one of the first places my Cal alum ('98) sister recommended in Berkeley was this place for their affordable ma po tofu.

[A-only review]

As a Cal alum, whenever I think of Euclid Ghetto, I get all warm fuzzies inside.  By the time I graduated, I probably had over 100+ meals at TC Garden.  The family that owned the restaurant even offered me a tab, but I kindly refused.

The chicken and black bean sauce over rice is my favorite meal.  The portion is decent, but the price is really want makes this place a must-visit on the North Side of Berkeley.  Another one of my favorites is the chicken chow mein--not a super risky dish for a Chinese person, but I love its black pepper-taste!  I can't resist!  It's like a pepper explosion in my mouth!

If you're ever on the North Side-- the geek side of campus-- stop by and you might be pleasantly surprised.

Seriously, the only reason I EVER eat here is because I'm broke or because they are the few places open on the Northside in the morning. The food is edible, they give pretty decent size portions, and it's CHEAP. I tried their scrambled eggs with beef over rice, thinking that it would be that juicy scrambled egg mix thing at Chinese restaurants. But nope, it was like a fried egg, except it wasn't fried....it was like a fried egg that became soggy type of texture.

But you know what, food is food when you're poor I guess.

I think I just ate in a trailer. You know, the ones construction workers use. Had plastic chairs inside, was crowded and my food took forever! They are cash only. The soup was too watery. The fried rice was ick. I enjoyed my coke, filled up on that and walked out leaving a mostly uneaten dish. I should have given it to the homeless man waiting outside.
It's cheap and taste like crap but if you're hungry and its late it'll do. I recommend the hot and sour soup, it's huge and filling and you can't screw up hot and sour soup.

The actual restaurant is kind of not-nice; I could see it easily belonging in Chinatown. Lots of formica tables and plastic lawn chair-type chairs.

In terms of food, I've only ever ordered the Ma Po Tofu, but they make the BEST Ma Po Tofu I've had outside of Asia. AND, really cheap - like $4-5!! Restaurant people are really nice too, and patient when I'm trying to decide what I want (even though I always end up with the Ma Po Tofu).

With so many good Asian and South Asian restaurants in the east bay, there is no reason to go here. The last and only time I ordered from TC, I had just moved to Berkeley and didn't know about Yelp or other restaurants beyond Euclid.

First off, the restaurant looked dirty. It is against healthcode to store ingredients directly on the floor, but there was definitely rice and some other dry goods on the floor in my direct line of vision. That should have tipped me off, but I was too hungry.

I ordered a typical beancurd homestyle dish. Supposed to be a good mix of savory and spice, but instead I got rubbery tofu that tasted like it had been dipped in handsoap then covered in chilis. It was horrible. Maybe other dishes are better, but I don't have any aspirations of trying again any time soon.
As a student I am willing to sacrifice taste for cheapness, but I have my limits. TC Garden is my limit.

Chinese Food at its worst, but still edible.

So why are they still in business?

Hungry asian engineering students who need to eat just to get by!

Don't expect authentic tastiness, but do expect to get a large meal for very little money.  I have to admit, I've had my fair share of meals here =(: Schezuan Eggplant, Beef Noodle Soup, Ma-Po Tofu.  These dishes are decent for a lunch if your mind is too fixated on a problem set or research problem to notice what you're eating.

SO BAD. It's all fried and greasy and the old lady who takes your order has terrible hearing and yells at you. The place itself is kinda nasty too (you can usually tell what the person before you ate based on the bits of food scattered on the tables), but I guess it does add to the authentic asian cuisine experience ...
