HOWEVER the place is really cheap and pretty close to campus, so people go there anyways.

Let's be honest, the food here sucks. It's generally tasteless and super oily. BUT the food here is also incredibly cheap. I usually get the house special fried rice or special #2. You can't go anywhere else in Berkeley and get this much food for so cheap. 

Granted, I have to douse everything in hot sauce for it to have any sort of taste and I always leave feeling really disgusting. BUT, i always leave really full. 

So with TC garden, you take the good with the bad. 

Pros:  cheap - big portions - right next to Etcheverry hall 
Cons: no taste - sketchy ingredients - generally kind of gross
For less than $5 a meal, what can you expect? It's not great, pretty tasteless most of the time, but for a hungry engineer on a budget, nothing beats a meal here.
If you only have 4 dollars and want a lot of food, tc garden is the place to be. Its not the greatest chinese food, but the prices are unbeatable.

I generally don't like eating chinese food at restaurants because I like my moms cooking back home, but this place makes me really dislike chinese fast-food. It's super cheap, but its just not worth getting a stomach ache over. 
Everything tastes like its been doused with msg and mixed with cornstarch. mehh

I seriously do not know how this place can possibly stay in business, not because it's bad (it's perfectly adequate), but because everything they sell here is so cheap. If you decide to eat in, you get tea, soup, and w/e you order, and most of the stuff is like 4.00-4.35 tax included. All i can say is that their profit margins must be razor thin...

Anyway, the food is certainly nothing special. I've had Curry Chicken (very bland), Mushroom Chicken (not too bad actually), and Fried Rice (they don't give you as much as with other stuff). However, the portions are fairly large, and you get that other stuff with it as well, so all in  all it's quite a good deal.

If you're super picky about Chinese food (or any kind of food for that matter) I don't know why you'd be eating at a place with 4 dollar entrees anyway, but you should probably stay away.

This place is somewhat decent, edible at least, but definitely sub par.  I went there many times with some classmates and was happy because I got a good amount of remotely good food for next to no money.  The service is great - very friendly and quick.  Unfortunately good service can't make up for bad food like bad service can ruin good food.

Not very tasty, but it's cheap food that gets you filled. I've tried a few dishes here like beef with bitter melon, mapo tofu, and short ribs, but my favorite is their number two special, which is a large chicken drumstick over fried rice with fried wontons. The large chicken drumstick is glazed deliciously with some sort of plum sauce, but the rice is forgettable and bland, and the wontons are sometimes cracked so they leak a large amount of the frying oil which is somewhat nasty.

It's certainly not the healthiest place to live, nor the tastiest, but if your on north side and need a quick eat, TC is pretty quick and cheap.

When you order, you get a small bowl of soup brought out to you which is kinda nice.
This reminds me of Mardarin House on Southside, but a lot cheaper. I saw the menu with lots of $3-$5 meals.

Even if it is cheap, I don't think it tasted good at all. On a positive note, it didn't give me food poisoning like Mandarin House at south-side's Asian ghetto. Still though, pretty bad. I might have been getting all the wrong things (but how can you mess up chow mein?).

I tried the daily specials on different occasions, but to my dismay, I usually left hungry for more with my mouth really dry from the MSG, and also a really disgusting feeling. Bad food and not enough food! Writing this review makes me cranky and cringe. Bah-humbug.

This one goes out to all of my former homies (I am no longer a CS Major) who spend endless nights suffering in the dark crevices of Etcheverry Hall, and the depths of the sodaless Soda Hall...

If you need food, and only have 5 bucks, TC Garden is the option for you. They have several combination platters, ranging from the generic sweet/sour option, to the adequate rice dishes with meat, you can find a Huge meal for you for under 5 Doal-Lar. 

This place gets 4 stars based on 3 things:

1. The food isn't bad
2. The food is cheap
3. The food is near the engineering buildings

Therefore, GET THE FOOD!!!

Taste: 3
Value: 5
Service: 3

I used to come here at least 2-3 times a week. The food is ridiculously cheap (~4 for most dishes after tax). After getting bored of their #1, I started ordering from their specials, which was slightly better. They're also very convenient, and I typically would order on the phone, pick it up 10 minutes later, and then be on my way. I still go here occasionally, and I usually get their daily special or dry bean curd with pork.

Great Sweet and Sour Chicken plate with fried rice, soup, and egg roll.  The food here is a great value, with said plate coming in at below $5 and it also has that old fashioned home-cooked sense about it.  The other dishes with meat or tofu served over rice are also good, very basic, but good.

Great place for poor students like myself
most dishes are around 5 bucks and the taste is ok

the service is great
most employers are very friendly 
once they even gave me free bowl of white rice :D

Even though the place isn't that clean, well it's Berkeley...
if you can't stand this, you should consider living somewhere else

This is not great Chinese food.  Their fried dishes are kinda gross.  The reason you should eat here is that it's cheap, fast, close to campus, has generous portions and-- if you order right, not too bad.  If you stick to dishes consisting of meat and vegetables in sauce you'll do OK.  

The one thing I'll actually go out of my way for here is the mapo tofu.  The mapo tofu here is nice and spicy and doesn't skimp on the pork.  The only thing I'd fault it on is that it's lacking Sichuan peppercorns.  But what I like is they do a good hearty down-home rendition of a dish which all too often is spoiled through Americanization.
In this category of food service (cheap, Chinese), it's as good as it can get. Cheapest meals ever that are surprisingly tasty.

This is the best food for 5 bux or less. Yea, there are some dishes that aren't so good, but you'll figure them out ( the sweet and sour pork comes to mind). I get the daily special when I come for lunch, but they usually sell out before dinner. I also recommend the dried bean curd, string beans, duck noodle soup, or the BBQ chicken special (the last item is not great on taste but amazing on value given what a large piece of meat it is for the price). I've been eating here at least a few times a week for the past year and a half. I probably come here more like 5 times a week since few places are open on Sundays on the North side. Also, you'll find that some dishes aren't as good a value since they will be 90% white rice.

Take-home: Way better than other Chinese food at this price point

I've eaten here more times then I can remember, and all I can say is that this place is SO CHEAP. You can get a complete meal (with some leftover) for around $4, which is completely ridiculous. 

Now of course, the quality isn't spectacular, you really get what you pay for. However, the people that work there are generally pretty nice and I've never had an order messed up here before (unlike Steve's Korean BBQ). They generally get very busy during lunch hours so it may vary between 5 minutes for your food to over 15 minutes.

I had rock-bottom expectations of the Northside Food "Ghetto" and suffice it to say, I was STILL disappointed... hahaha. This restaurant easily makes the top 5 for lowest prices in Berkeley. Unfortunately, you do get what you pay for. I ordered in Chinese and I have to say that my food did not come out in some kind of amazing, special, delicious form as another reviewer kind-of, sort-of implies. And if it did, then i'm thankful I did not get what the non-Chinese speakers eat... hahaha.

I ordered the beef noodles and the beef was very.. uh... non-traditional. The noodles were also cheaply made and the broth was watery. If you are low on money and high on hunger, go here... I guess... or you could walk to the Little Mandarin on Shattuck cause that place is cheap AND kicks ass.

Free tea and a mint at the end of your meal.

Pros:
Fast +1
Chinese food less than $5 +1
Taste somewhat like panda express.
only Chinese restaurant in the north side.

Cons:
Their daily special is yuck! ( don't try the one w/ a chicken leg!)
The guy (cashier, new owner?) never smiles.
Limited seats.
Oily food

TC Garden is:
1) Fast
2) Cash Only BUT super cheap
3) Close to Berkeley Engineering Buildings 
thus it's always full of hungry Berkeley engineers. 
Keep in mind that I didn't say anything about it being actually good Chinese food. 
It's edible and doesn't look bad. If anything the copious MSG makes it taste pretty good.
This place is pretty reliable for mediocre Chinese food.  Not including Panda Express style buffets, this is probably the cheapest Chinese food in Berkeley.
Great owner! love this place! you can customize your food quite a lot if you know what you are doing, they are really flexible =]

I used to come here quite often for undergrad. The food wasn't out of this world but had this home cooked feeling that you kept coming back to. 

I loved getting the duck noodle soup, rice dishes, or their specials. The service was generally pretty good too.

This place kinda sucks. I've only eat here a few times, usually getting some kind of special on their menu. The only thing good about this place is that food is damn cheap. I guess the owners are nice too.  If you're hungry and out of cash, drop by this place.

Soo.... whenever I come here, I am broke. Let's just put that out there. So really, it is starve or get some $4 meal here. 
BUT. When I make better egg flower soup, you know its crap.
Also a bee attacked me here.

I wouldn't risk my health for such cheap food.

Pay a couple dollars more and eat at the Vietnamese place next door, which has fresher and better tasting food.. And they give huge portions, which if split into two meals is a cheaper.

So everything there basically tastes the same regardless of what you order. The fried rice combo was deadly. The rice was so dried and it lacked major flavor. I mean, seriously, can you care to give a little more flavor? either way, i am happy for the price and the amount of food.

Great value! For less than $5 (mine was only $4.50 after tax) you get a HUGE plate of good food. It's ridiculously CHEAP and very, very filling. The portion is enough for two meals for me. 

I'm comparing it with the Mandarin House Restaurant in Durant Food Court (aka the Asian Ghetto) in the southside. Same quality, but Mandarin House is $1-2 more expensive. I'd rather come here instead. 

My review here is for their VEGETARIAN dishes only (I'm now trying to stay away from Chinese restaurant's greasy meat coming from questionable sources). As far as the veggie dishes go, I'd give 3 stars - decent, OK quality, reasonably tasty.  

Service is decent. The lady who served me was nice. She DID smile and was, in fact, quite friendly! 

GO if you're insanely hungry and you can eat an elephant. GO if you want a super cheap, super filling and reasonably tasty meal. ** Sit outside if you can, as it's ugly and plain inside, and it gets stuffy.  In a typical weekday lunchtime, you'll see lots of nerdy students coming from the Engineering, math and science dept around there. Enjoy the food, and feel the Berkeley Geek Vibes.

As far as I can tell, TC Garden offers the cheapest meal on campus.  The quality leaves something to be desired, but when you're looking for greasy American Chinese food at a damn good price, TC Garden delivers with a smile.

I would say...expect what you get at a shopping mall food court. Actually, a little less than that.

They have "Chinese" food and burgers.

I ordered the garlic chicken plate because the girl at the counter recommended it. I hated it. The chicken was dry and the rice was drier.

Also, I hate places that water down the Shriracha sauce because they are being stingy. OMG I can't stand it.

Order late night pizza or Nude Sushi instead! :)

This place was 5 stars in the good old days (I even had a tab!), but the ownership has changed (the wonderful owner finally retired...oh well, all good things have to come to an end).  Still, a nice cozy place with consistent food and warm service.

Mediocre chinese food for absurdly cheap prices.  Absolutely the only reason to go here is if you are working on the North side of campus and are hungry for lunch - the place is full of engineering students with no gastronomical inclinations and even less money.  

I have noticed that if you order in Chinese your food comes out noticeably different and slightly tastier.  I now only go here with my Chinese coworker, and he orders for me.

Arguably the Worst Chinese restaurant near UC Berkeley campus. The food tasted canned, and I am pretty sure it was canned. Every time I come and eat here, I make a new resolution to learn how to cook myself. That's how bad it is. (Actually, I think my cooking may just be better).

If you wish to have any experience that remotely resembles eating real food, do not come here. 

The only up-side is that this place is cheap. But given that most of its ingredient tastes like shyt, it makes total sense.

The wonton soup was mediocre at best... definitely no Banana Leaf. Oh Banana Leaf, how I pine for thee. But anyway, TC Garden. The server spoke no English and told me I couldn't have rice (she meant my soup didn't come with rice, but I didn't bother to argue with her). She was sweet, though, let me sit inside, monopolize a table for an hour and a half and write a paper with journal articles spread everywhere... occasionally muttering to myself or insulting various authors out loud for their faulty assumptions or cultural insensitivity. So, yeah. TC Garden gets an extra star just for knowing their audience and being nice to crazy grad students.

The place was clean, smelled nice, and the food was inexpensive (the low price was why I chose TC Garden over other restaurants on Hearst + Euclid). Also, all the the windows were open on a beautiful, sunny day... it was a good place to be productive. That counts for something; I'll doubtlessly be back. To the other patrons: I apologize in advance.

Holy crap this place is cheap. I mean, almost everything on the menu is below 5 bucks. That's unheard of. Unfortunately everything is quite horrible. I got the broccoli chicken, and not only did it fill me up, it made me feel like pasty shit.

Now that I've made you puke in your mouth a little, I'll end my review :D

I grew up eating chinese food with my family every weekend in Oakland chinatown. It came to be one of my favorite family traditions, one that I was sad to leave behind when I left for Berkeley. 
One day, on a whim, I decided to look around the north side asian ghetto, with no particular desire to eat anything. When I saw TC Garden, I felt like Swann biting into a madeleine. 
The interior decoration -- from the peeling-at-the-corners white paint to the crooked red chinese wall hangings -- triggered a flood of memories within me. Memories of authentically decrepit Oakland Chinatown restaurants (particularly Dragon Terrace, closed by the health inspector. The mark of a good chinese restaurant). 
I was caught by the seductive snares of forgotten love, and TC Garden reeled me in. I ordered vegetable fried rice -- four dollars, including tax.
It was good. 
TC Garden exists for me as a memorial -- honoring the chinese food memories of my childhood, without trying to be anything it's not.

The tables are always sticky here...

I don't know how they stay in business. Go for their special #2. It's like half a chicken plus some fried stuff plus some more fried stuff. And it's all under 5 bucks. Plus you get to feel like death afterwards.

NOTE: I'm basing this on my memories of this place, when I was a student at Berkeley and lived in the Foothill dorms.

Food: 0.5 stars.  It gets 0.5 stars because I didn't die after eating here, and the food did provide some meager sustenance to a starving student.  Then again, I think the bark off trees may provide similar nutritional value, and would give TC Garden a run for its money on taste.  And I lied about the starving student bit... I always ate well.  In short, this place is completely horrible.  It's not mediocre, it's just HORRIBLE.  My memories of this place consist of eating burnt "fried rice" that literally tasted like the non-stick Teflon coating on their woks (or whatever they are using in the kitchen... maybe garbage can lids?).  This place is to be avoided at all costs.  Even Mandarin House in the Ghetto is better... that should speak volumes about this place...

Ambiance: 1 star.  In short, there is none.  The place is tiny and cramped.  If you must eat here, get it to go.

Service: 2.5 stars.  Nothing good or bad here.  Maybe I should ding them because they don't warn you about or apologize for the crap you're about to eat.

Value: 3 stars.  If TC had any appeal, and that's a big if, it's that it's cheap.  Really cheap.  I recall it being $4 or sub-$4 cheap.  But like they say... you get what you pay for... and that's why it really isn't a deal at all...
Bottom line; quantity over quality. They give very good portions, but the food is extremely oily and pretty unhealthy. Average item on the menu is 4-5$ to.

I'm a little surprised by the poor reviews here...

This was my first Northside Asian Ghetto experience and I must say it was a pretty good one, comparable to Vietnam Village over in the Southside Asian Ghetto. I mean, it's not a 4-star in that it's the best Chinese food I've ever had (and that's tough to beat, since I AM Chinese and know what good is), but the price comparison with the taste and quantity is pretty darn good.

My friend and I wanted to check out Gomnaru originally, but since it was our first time to this Asian Ghetto, we didn't know that half the restaurants are closed on Sat/Sun. TC Garden was one of the only ones open, and we decided to go for it since it seemed cheap and decent.

We decided to split a House Special Chow Fun and Minced Pork & Bean Sauce Noodles (Za Jiang Mien for the Chinese), and it came out to be $4.75 per person including tax! Wow. What a steal! But, was it going to be a Sun Hong Kong experience? (that's another cheap Chinese food place, and it seriously is BAD, not even worth the cheap price) I cringed at the possibility, but it was worth a try.

After waiting about 5 min, our food came out and we took it to go. When I finally got around to eating it 20+ minutes later, I ate the za jiang mien first and really enjoyed the thick noodles and yummy sauce. That sustained me for about 40 minutes of studying, and then I gave in and ate my share of the chow fun. It was good - tastes similar to the Vietnam Village one, except maybe slightly more flavor. The House Special has different meats in it, including pork, chicken, and beef, so that was really nice. Portions are large, like Vietnam Village. Probably enough for 1.5 meals.

I give it 4 stars not because it's like Great China's food, but because this is definitely a place I would come back to again for a cheap lunch/dinner that doesn't taste awful like Sun Hong Kong's food. Plus, service is friendly (that doesn't affect my rating though, since you should know not to expect good service at Chinese restaurants =P)! I had a pretty yummy and very filling dinner for only $4.75!!! If only Northside Asian Ghetto wasn't so far away for me...(I live on Southside)

I guess this place is definitely a hit or miss with most people. For me, it suffices as a place to get decent (and VERY cheaply priced) Chinese food while I suffer through classes in the Northside dungeon (read: Etcheverry). I'd recommend getting some of their off the menu items, like their Spicy Sichuan fish with rice and their Eggplant and Pork with Rice. Their beef noodles aren't that bad either, and everything is under $5 after tax. Of all the places in the food court area, I'd say that this is the place to get the best bang for your buck. If you don't really like salty/spicy food though, take your business elsewhere.

My standards of quality go way down when I'm only paying $4 for a meal, but combo #3 always hit the spot when I wanted a quick, cheap and filling meal between cramming sessions in Etch. The food's not really memorable, but the service is always friendly and quick.

I used to go here everyday for lunch since they have so many cheap items on their menu. My favorite is there combo two item with the fried rice, deep friend won tons and a very large piece of chicken all for just 5 bucks, which also includes a small bowl of soup. I ordered the chow fun here, which I dont like. Another one I like is the chicken with black bean sauce, which I think is good, the green bell peppers on there are crunchy and fresh tasting and only costs 4$ which includes tax.

One thing I really didn't like about this place is when I order something with beef. There barely is any. Maybe amount 5 to 6 pieces of very small portions of beef and a bunch of every else. You'll probably be more satisfied ordering the chicken, which they dont mind giving you a large portion of, but it tastes like one of those frozen chickens you boil from your local grocery store.

I will probably eat here again many times because its only a block away from campus and very convenient for my wallet. sometimes I use a whole bunch of change and dont have to worry about tax because I order the 4$ item. This place is a preference for me over southside's chinese express, which is the cheaper chinese take out of south side because it tastes better.

I eat here at least once a week and am always happy.
The service is very good.  I define very good as getting attention as soon as I walk through the door.  I don't care if they don't smile.  Which is good, because they never smile. 
The food is also very good.  All I ever get is the Chicken Chow Mein and Scrambled Egg Chicken and I like both of them.  
The prices are excellent.  Nothing is more than $5 and the portions are very large.
Service is slow, though still faster than La Vals or La Burrita, during the peak 12:00-1:00pm weekday time, but that is understandable.  If you come ~11:45 you'll get your food in a couple minutes.

Great, CHEAP, large portions of Chinese food.  The seating / decor is pretty ghetto but you can't really complain when you get a meal for less than $5 including tea and soup.  

Service is efficient and they prepare the food really quickly.  Quality of the food varies greatly on what you order.  I tend to stick with the steamed rice / stir fry dishes as I think they're tastier.

Finally, I love the guys that work there.  They're really nice - so much so that when I don't have any money (it's cash only) they let me eat and pay them back a day or two later.

No, TC garden won't receive a michelin star anytime soon -- but thats ok b/c there's no pretense with their food.  WYSIWYG.    

The worst type of restaurant is one tries to be something it isn't--and thats TC's saving grace -- it doesn't.

Terrible. Just terrible. My review stats show that I'm a pretty nice guy when it comes to reviews, so please take me seriously when I give something 1 star.

TC Garden is one of the restaurants located in the Northside Asian Ghetto (as I like to call it), and it benefits from being one of the first restaurants you'll pass from the street. So they already have location going for them. And from one look at the cheap combo meals they advertise from the front, I'm sure you'll be tempted to pick this place, right?

You would be immediately wrong. Even the cheap prices don't save this place in my opinion. The food I had here was quite tasteless and the rice was overdone! Nothing bugs me more than dried out rice, but come on, you're a Chinese restaurant! Dry rice is unforgivable.

I only went here once and never came again, with good reason.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here on a Thursday at 3:30 PM to eat an early lunch because my meal at Pat Brown's was so horribly unsatisfying. Make sure to bring cash! The wait was about 8 minutes for my food to-go, and I snatched a fortune cookie from their little tin by the cashier. I love fortune cookies!

|| F O O D ||

COMBINATION #2: Fried rice, 3 fried wontons, and a huge chicken drumstick [$4.75]
- They upgraded to 3 fried wontons! I remember only getting 1! The little pouch of fatty meat is so horribly yummy, and the oily crispiness is divine. They also drizzle them in sweet-n-sour sauce.
- Fried rice is meh. No green onions, which is a pity, just a few specks of carrot and egg.
- Chicken leg is so worth it for $4.75. It's huge, and the meat isn't too dry (not too moist either, but hey, it's $4.75!). They slather it in sauce, and depending on your luck, the skin won't be too burnt and crispy.
- If you eat here instead of to-go, they give you a small bowl of MSG-y soup that has tofu and egg in it.

I've also had their cashew chicken entree, which I don't recommend because the squash tastes rubbery and bitter, and there isn't that much chicken, and an eggplant dish, which I do highly recommend because they sauteed the eggplant just right.

|| O V E R A L L ||

Yes, the quality of the food aint too hot. Apparently, it gave one of my friends diarrhea. But from the 6 times or so that I've eaten here, I haven't had any digestion discomforts, and I'm able to walk away satiated and sometimes with leftovers for under $5. On a college student budget, that is an amazing deal. Their service isn't the cheeriest, but the waitresses are fast and don't ignore you. Come here for their combo 2 and their eggplant dish!

The thing about TC is that it's cheap food that tastes excellent for its cost. Other Chinese restaurants around Berkeley are either disgusting take-out places or white washed wannabe pan-Asian joints. At TC you can get full off only $4 worth of food, $5 tops. Plus, you get free soup and hot tea. 

The service is a typical Chinese restaurant style service, but slightly better. The main guy at the register is extremely considerate and laid back. There have been several times where I forgot to bring cash, and he just told me to pay him next time I came. Where else in Berkeley can you do that?

The food itself is really not greasy at all, unless you order something deep fried, in which case what do you expect. I would recommend the Chicken Chow Fun, String Bean Chicken/Beef/Pork, Scrambled Egg Chicken, and the Potstickers.

In terms of the environment, it's pretty average. It's just like Asian Ghetto on Southside if not cleaner. If you don't mind eating at Asian Ghetto along with trashcans overflowing with to-go boxes, then you won't mind eating here.

Perhaps the cheapest and consequently the most tasteless and insipid Chinese food to ever hit your palate. The chicken used in the poultry dishes is a sickly gray, a challenge to cut with a knife and looks like those old frozen chicken parts that are allegedly exported to Third World countries because they are deemed unfit for First World consumption. However, this place is so cheap that I like to think that the owners have well-meaning, ulterior intentions of instilling in every Berkeley student deficient in common sense (and there's plenty of those) who patrons their restaurant that old adage, "You get what you pay for." But, given the present state of the economy, who isn't willing to pay $4 for a combination plate complete with entree, side, hot soup and tea? Smother your over-fried orange chicken with a generous squirt of Siracha and you'll be good to go. Although I hesitate to say the same for what might happen in the john later on.

Its been a year since I've been in Berkeley and probably more than a year and half since I've sat down and chowed down like a muh fucka at this place. I just woke up from a nap and had the hugest craving for this place and shed a tear when I realized I was hundred of miles away. Whoever is giving 2 stars for this place has seriously got some delusions. What are you expecting? Gold flakes in your shark fin soup? Get real homies. This place is all about value living. There is honestly nothing like putting on two winter coats and trekking in the cold to get a piping hot 4 dollar meal. When the plate arrives and all those familiar scents hit your memory banks, you will understand the way of the TC. I would suggest the eggplant by the way.

Sooo cheap.
$3 for a meal with tea.  

The owner is a nice guy too; he let me exchange money into quarters for my laundry.

if you've been programming in soda all day and you're in dire need of a huge leg of chicken, then this is your place.

otherwise, no.

Let me explain. 

IF, and it's a big one (the if), this place was about twice the price that it is, I'd give it ... 2 and a half stars. BUT, look at what you get for what you pay. 

Say, if I walk in, get slapped in the face, order the sichuan fish and rice for $4, wait 20 min for my food. it'd be a star. 

But I show up, am greeted warmly, get served tea while waiting (like 2 minutes) for my $4 mushroom chicken or spareribs with rice or beefy thing with an egg on top. That's a, ehh, 4 star experience. 

Once, 5 minutes before I was suppose to get lunch for a group of 15, I dash in at 12:25 and demand $40 worth of food asap. She smiles at me and says no problem. 10 minutes later I walked away with enough food to feed like 25 people. 

Fo' realz

Man ya'll trippin. This place go!

However, I am not a fan of trying to get into the crammed packed area because its nestled in with other restaurants and crowds of ppl. I feel like I'm in baby China when I go to pickup my call-in orders. My favorite dish so far is the Eggplant & Chicken over rice! Mmmm soooo tasty A-N-D  it's under $5 bucks.

Best tip:
Always call your order in if you don't want to deal with the line!

I will admit that TC Garden is terrible. It is bad Chinese food in the worst possible fashion. By that I mean not only is it greasy, but it's flavorless too.

And the good part about TC Garden...it's dirt cheap. As in, I can buy an entire dinner of general chicken, broccoli and rice for about $4.50 and still have leftovers. Of course, it's not really good enough where you want leftovers, but that's not the point I'm trying to make

The chicken looks like the questionable mystery meat from a third world country. The flavors are flat and the texture is chewy for most thinks and crunchy for vegetables

Yet  have I eaten there on more than one occasion? Of course. That's what happens when you're a broke college student, live only a block and a half away, and alcohol gets involved. Cash only though, so don't have an embarrassing credit card only experience when trying to order.

The only good thing about this place is that its merely 10 steps from my office. Other than that avoid this place if possible.

When getting there directly at noon the fries aren't fresh and never are..you have to practically watch them cook fries to know they are fresh. The prices are very high and quality of food isn't up to par. There are many other places i would recommend other than pat browns. If you can please head over to bears lair for lunch. A much better selection and everything is F R E S H!!

Also not every cashier knows what to charge so i guarantee you wont pay the same exact price for some items all the time.i have gotten charge different prices for the hot menu many times. Only reason why i might still order it is because i get charged a lower price than the first time..Its always a gamble.

So basically this place is over priced and food is never always guaranteed fresh. If it takes walking longer to get quality food.. i suggest you get the stepping..  ^_^

I love Pat Brown's, simply because its location is so convenient for me (I have classes 5 days a week at GPB). I usually get the hazelnut coffee (which is surprisingly good!), the chicken strips, and the chicken stirfry with brown rice when I want something healthy and filling. If you're looking for a frills-free place to grab a quick snack, I recommend this cafe!

Recently re-opened after being remodeled. SO HAPPY it's finally open, I was getting tired of trekking to GBC for lunch. It's a solid on-campus dining option. They take meal points. They serve rotisserie chicken and turkey and things like that, plus salads and sandwiches. And they have a Peet's! Probably my new favorite place to eat on campus (Sorry, Qualcomm.) My only gripe is that it closes early, around 4.

This place is very convenient for me because it is really close to the lab I work at. They sell several food items and beverages like juice and coffee. I've never at here thought, just boughten food items, but it looks like they have a lot of sitting for people not only on the inside but on the outside too.

Out of the places that accept meal points on campus, Pat Brown's is the best. 

If you got meal points to burn, and you are on northside, look no further than the PBG.

They have bomb cheezesteak sandwiches, and are always fully stocked on bentos and other good shit. 

The decor and table space is much better than any other eateries on campus, which is a huge plus. 

If u dont have meal points, i wouldn't recommend eating here, but its still a convenient and comfortable place to chill/study.

The only redeeming factor for this place is the fact that they load up cheese when you order cheese fries.  Otherwise it's your typical disgusting cafeteria with grease bombs, wilted salads, horrific meat/cheese/veggie combos on premade sandwiches.

I would give 3 stars because the cashiers undercharge me more than they should, and for the cheesy fries.  But their ATM is ALWAYS broken which leaves me starving when I run out of cash.  They need to call someone about that...so 2 stars it is for the awful ATM issues.

Mustard was super runny. New cashier needs more.. practice (i.e. or like standing in line for 10 minutes). Again, expensive soda's and like 4-5 bucks for an odwalla. Seriously? No to-go boxes. Refrigerator needs to be colder - my sodas area always lukewarm. 

If I didn't work so close to this place - I'd probably never come back.

Mr. Brown is definitely not serving me my lunch, but when I'm hungry for breakfast, this greasy, fatty grill is calling my name.  Some days I just wake with a craving for Pat's good ole tater tots. Other days on the way back from getting my coffee, the smell of those tater tots being cooked up consumes me, makes my knees weak, and self- restraint becomes completely impossible as my nose leads me in here.  I cave in occasionally, and so do my wonderful co-workers MJ & YG.  We love each other so much we share and save our waistlines tot-by-tot.  

Then there are the days where you feel like you haven't eaten in 3 days and you want it all... eggs, bacon, tots, and toast.  Pat's will load it up for ya.  And when I'm being a good girl, I pick up some oatmeal.   

I give Pat's a solid 4 stars simply for being there, with a smile, within 50 feet of my office with all of its overpriced candy, gum, soda, salads, donuts, ice cream, sushi, weak coffee and accepting my debit card or IOU.  What else would I do when I forget something for the potluck and can bring 8 sushi rolls for $8 and win my co-worker's hearts? Or when I need a 5-hour energy drink? Or donut, or egg n cheese a la McMuffin, or tuna melt, or fries or ...you get my point.  Paying for convenience...  Love ya Pat!

The best thing about Pat Brown's is that it's 20 feet from my office.  So it's an emergency stop for the most part.  Like when I forget breakfast in the morning I can get their Basic Bear (tater tots, 2 eggs, toast and coffee) for $3.  Their chicken sandwich is not too bad but everything else on the grill is preety greasy.    They have large selection of drinks and some sandwiches, donuts, chips, fruit, yogurt and granola....

They have annoying summer and break hours closing at 2PM.
Also they close early as compared to most campus restaurants: They close at 4PM. I don't know. Do they think science majors don't need to eat after a certain time?
The food they make is pretty bad, but they have some prepackaged Cesar salads (thank god) and plenty of odwallas, juices and sodas. 
Their cookie selection bites. I love oatmeal and if I'm desperate chocolate chip. They always always have peanut butter. Ick.
The best thing about Pat Brown's is the outdoor patio which is really lovely on those rare warm Berkeley days
If you have 15 minutes this is a great place to stop, but you might be able to make center street and back in 30.

It's a restaurant on a college campus...  There was more than one option for me as a vegetarian which puts it well ahead of a lot of places at a lot of universities.  I had a peanut butter and jelly sandwich which was good, albeit not that difficult to make.  The coffee was terrible.  I think I'll walk to Starbucks the next time I want coffee.

Even though I'm not a big fan of Pat Brown's, I'm nonetheless a slave to it since its only a few steps from my office... arghhh, I hate that my laziness compels me to go to this place

Definitely, the best thing on the menu here is the cheesesteak... but there really are no fresh healthy options...so if I'm looking to negate my day's workout, this is a place I'd end up going to... 

appetizer: greasy fries dipped in ranch dressing or chili cheese, entree: cheese steak ladeled with molten cheddar cheese and onions, dessert: something else you fry the shit out of... beverage:diet coke... since, you know, a girl needs to keep her figure

I know...undergrads at Berkeley are pretty easy to please since the university usually makes them eat pig feed out of troughs at the other cafeterias...(which is why I suspect other people gave it more stars than I have)...  but, as a grad student here whose days of eating pig slop are long gone, I expect a lil' more...

the only options that can really be considered healthy here are overpriced, prepackaged goods that don't look particularly tastey sitting
on the shelves...

and their coffee... my god... its like they only use one coffee bean per metric ton of hot water to make it... I like my coffee strong, so perhaps that why it displeases me so much... but still, give a bitch a break...  I'd like some coffee in this cup of hot water, please!

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Pat Brown's reopened and is no longer a grill, from what I can tell. They now serve healthier foods, and have a Peet's Coffee & Tea imbedded in their store.

I decided to come here between lab and lecture, and I didn't want to go off campus. They took forever renovating this place, so I figured it would be a good place to grab lunch. I also wanted to get some work done, and they have ample indoor seating. But no work was done, because I decided to create this rant post instead of be productive for class.

|| F O O D ||

You have three options eating here:

1) Create your own PLATE: choose any single entree and 2 sides for $7.50
Today, entrees, included 1/4 herbed rotisserie chicken, rotisserie turkey breast, grilled portobello mushroom, braised tofy, and sunflower cutlet (vegan). Sides include spicy simmered greens, french fries, homemade potato chips, garlic fries (+$1.00), whole grain rice pilaf, steamed white rice, "baked" mashed potatoes, creamy polenta, and steamed vegetables.
Single entree from $4.50. Half chicken is $6.50, plus two sides is $9.50. Whole chicken is $12.50. Single side is $1.50.

2) Gourmet SALADS: choose lettuce, dressing, and up to 5 toppings for $5.25. Add an entree option for $7.25
Greens include romaine lettuce, spinach, and spring mix. Dressing includes Caesar, ranch, balsamic vinaigrette, and oil + vinegar. Toppings include cucumbers, tomatoes, red onions, pepperocini, shredded carrots, corn, sliced olives, edamame, hard boiled egg, pumpkin seeds, dried cranberries, black beans, croutons. They have something called a PB-T Caeser that has chopped romaine, rotisserie turkey, corn, red onions, black beans, pumpkin seeds, shredded cheddar topped with Caesar dressing.

3) Custom SANDWICHES for $6.25, add a savory side for $7.50 total.
Choose an entree roast from herbed chicken, turkey breast, daily entree, grilled portobello mushroom, braised tofu, sunflower cutlet (vegan). Choose bread from multi-grain wheat, torpedo roll, artisan roll. Add mayo, whole-grain brown mustard, dijon mustard, oil + vinegar, lettuce, tomatoes, sliced olives, cucumbers, red onions, pickles.
Cheese is an extra $0.75, bacon $1.60, avocado $1.25, extra meat $1.75, hummus $1.

I opted for a gourmet salad because I wanted to practice healthy eating habits. The only thing gourmet about this salad was how incredibly small it was for the price I paid.

I got all three types of greens and asked for cucumbers, carrots, corn, edamame, and eggs. They ran out of corn (really?), and the girl said I could get chicken. I thought it was a hidden topping, so I happily said yes. She drizzled on some sauce, threw in a small slice of bread, and that was that.

Wow. This portion would satiate no one. She added maybe 20 leaves of vegetables, 3 cucumber slices, 10 carrot strands, 20 edamame beans, 1/2 of a hard-boiled egg, and 10 strands of chicken. Even worse, the chicken counted as an ENTREE, and I had to pay $7.25 for this miserable MISERABLE meal.

I will say that the chicken was well-flavored, and the bread was tasty and soft. BUT WHAT THE HECK, REALLY? I totally didn't realize how LITTLE I was given until the server tried to close the container...and it was only 1/3 filled. ONE THIRD. THIS IS WORSE THAN GBC. And then I was charge $7.25 for THIS!? REALLY??? It took me 3 minutes to eat the whole thing, and I AM AS HUNGRY AS WHEN I WALKED THROUGH THE DOOR.

|| C L O S U R E ||

Not-so-generous servers, small salads. Opt for the plates. The salads and sandwiches are miserably small. MISERABLE.

EDIT: Okay, so the student next to me got the plate entree, which was comprised of 4 small slices of turkey, a few florets of steamed broccoli, and a small heap of mashed potatoes with gravy. IT WAS SMALLER THAN MY SALAD. WHAT IS UP WITH THIS. EVERYTHING IS MISERABLY SMALL. DO NOT VENTURE HERE UNLESS YOU ONLY HAVE 5 MINUTES FOR LUNCH AND CANNOT GO A FEW MORE FEET TO OFF-CAMPUS EATERIES. Unless it's for Peet's, which was giving away free samples c:

A great place to grab a quick bite. Maybe we went here at an off time because they were out of chicken and chorizo so my boyfriend and I both weren't able to have our first pick of pizza. To be fair it was around 4pm but lots of their menu items had chicken on it so it was kind of weird to run out of one of the main ingredients! 

I forget what my slice was called verbatim but it was a white pizza with pesto sauce and lots of veggies on top. My boyfriend ordered the chipotle pizza with sausage instead of chorizo (since they ran out of it).

Overall, really cool place with a nice feel. We sat by the window that opens up completely so we got some fresh air and a front seat view of Telegraph. 

One major thing that turned me off though was that our slices were luke warm. When it comes to pizza, it should be piping hot to the point where the cheese is really oozy and melted. 

For the price this place is great but I don't think I'd be going back. I would rather spend a few more dollars for a place that has all ingredients in stock and serves their slices hot.

Worth trying once though if you're in the area!
Good, inexpensive. Came here upon my visit to UC Berkeley. I actually remember the pizza and also recall wanting more LOL May visit on my next excursion up there :)
Great fast food pizza. Love their vegetarian and pepperoni pizza. Also a great place to sit and people watch while you eat.
Really fast service with reasonable prices, I tend to go here when the lines for other places are too long. The pizza is okay, nothing fantastic, but not bad at all.

unless it's fresh .. it's not that great. 
good for its inexpensiveness, though.
Cmon, its not that bad.  Cheap and quick service.   I always grab a slice if I visit Rasputin next door.
Quick, cheap, and inexpensive pizza by the slice. These 3 things earn Blondie's 3 stars.

I have to say, in the epic Telegraph battle between Fat Slice and Blondie's, I'm going to have to vote for Fat Slice. The sauce and dough just taste funky here. . .I don't know what exactly it is, but things are just not right. There was a weird after taste and the pizza was way too greasy. For the price, I would much rather walk the block or two to Fat Slice and get double the amount of food for the same price.

Good and cheap pizza. Late at night is the best time to get it. The ambiance calls for it. Very retro and located right by UC, convenient for me since I was staying in one of the dorms with my sister and friends! Yummy! Bring cash because I think they do not accept credit cards! I like to stick to the usual, pepperoni or sausage means yum.

In the debate between who is better, Blondie's or Fat Slice, I will have to go with this one. It's cheapo pizza, greasy, heavy, not at all delicate, but they at least can cook the crust all the way through and it's just significantly less sketchy than Fat Slice. 

Is it great? No. Quality? Probably not. Does it satisfy? Sure, if you're in South Berkeley. For super delicious, out of this world pizza, I'd head over to Cheeseboard, but this is good enough for quick lunch or something. I'm not in the drinking crowd, so I never stumble into any of these places drunk, so I couldn't say how well it satisfies that particular need.

I dunno - I didn't like Fat slice, and I didn;t like Blondies.
When you've lived in NYC and Philly - there's something just off about West Coast pizza.

It's not awful - it's just not worth the calories for me.

Meanwhile, people RAVE about Blondie's.
And the placed is always PACKED with students (gee - I wonder why) so it's great for people watching.  (All of Biz-erkeley is great for that!)

Individual slices flabby, greasy, lukewarm, somehow not even as cohesive as Round Table.  And dude, the cheese didn't make that string between slice and bite.  It was coagulated. And no golden brown crunchiness. :( All of these problems can probably be chalked up to not-fresh-ness.

just... walk to Cheeseboard.  Nice workers though.

Quick, cheap, easy 'n greasy. 

Came for a late-night slice. Clearly mistimed my visit because I was seeking the hallowed BBQ chicken but today's special was chorizo instead. Bummer.

Ended up picking the whole-wheat vegetarian slice, which looked thicker than the chorizo and pepperoni. Pizza was pretty tasteless until you bite your way through the cheese. For all the grease involved, I did not feel like I was eating the "healthiest pizza in all of Berkeley" (beg your pardon, Blondie's). Oh well, whatchu pay is whatchu get.

Oh my god, there's this girl that works there who has worked at like every other store on Telegraph.  And I've never seen her smile.  She has this just-shoot-me-in-the-face-already look that is hilarious.  It's like, come on, we're all a little miserable now and again, but do you have to be miserable when you work at Rexall Pharmacy AND Smart Alecs AND Blondies Pizza???  She's rung me up maybe 20 times at all of these locations and not once has she ever said "hello" or "may I help you" or even "thank you".  Sheesh.  Anyway, that said, Blondies: meh, it won't give you a stomach ache, but it's not delicious.  And usually there are kids handing out coupons for a pizza and a soda on Telegraph.  Cheap eats.  Go in with low expectations if you have a coupon and you might not want to vomit.
I like Blondie's because the pizza is quick, filling, and convenient and the staff is great but the pizza is nothing special.

This is a Berkeley Classic! Who doesn't like Blondies... I've been going here for almost 20 years now... the staff is always friendly, it's wheelchair friendly... and the pizza tastes GREAT... the prices are descent.... what's not to love about Blondies... other than the sometimes annoying teenagers that hang out there - but it's near UC Berkeley so you have to expect that... :op

Blondie's just doesn't do it for me like Fat Slice does. 

What it lacks in taste though, it makes up for in seating. But still, I'm here for the pizza!

A favorite of locals and tourists alike, Blondies goes hard in the pizza game. Fat slices and a drink for under 5 bucks is hard to beat especially with the quality they provide. This place is the ish to put it lightly. Do yourself a favor and try the Tomato and Artichoke special. Comes with tomatoes, artichokes hearts, mushrooms, and pesto sauce. Its on point!

I'm more used to the San Francisco branch but this place does rock. I ate here about once every week in my freshman year in between an awkward one hour gap in my schedule for lunch. I would alternate between pepperoni or their special if it wasn't too weird. 

Good times for some cheap, greasy, filling eats. Hey, it might not be too good on the belly but at least it does its job, right? I also love those coupons that they always pass out on Bancroft and Telegraph right at the entrance of campus for $3.50 slice of combo and a drink. 

Ah, Blondie's, you really hit the spot. It's a shame I haven't been back for a while.
Love this place!  Pizza is great!  Staff are super hot!

Today was the first time I had Blondie's in a long time so it's tough for me to compare. However today's pepperoni slice could have used more time in the oven so it was undercooked and lukewarm. I don't see it ever rising over 3 stars though.
SO SO pizza its pretty good i guess for the cash. 1 slice and your done...not bad

They have a variety of flavors available. I like that they have a daily special. You can also order a whole pizza to go, but I'd recommend calling in your order ahead of time. I typically order the carnivore pizza as well as the pepperoni. I came here many times while studying at UCB. Definitely recommend it when you're on the go.

Expected bill: $4

Yummmm Blondie's Pizza [: A nice place to stop and have a bite to eat while shopping. I don't recall there being a larger dining area other than what's up front, but it's not somewhere I'd stay too long at anyway.
Thin crust is the place to be.  Usually comes out nice and crisp just they way i like it, not mushy like fatslice. Daily special rocks.
Given the price and the time it takes to get in and out of there, it's pretty darn good.

I'm biased... I like NY Pizza, thin greasy large pizza

This pizza nonetheless is great for the price. It will get you full (because it's almost all bread. Not my cup of tea, but a good price when I'm on the go and wanted to taste some pizza!

A little doughy for my taste, but always a good call.  Pepperoni is my favorite.  And now they serve beer!

I can't believe how much slices cost these days but I guess college was a long time ago...

The pepperoni pizza was OK (my son had it) but the Whole Wheat Vegetarian pizza was fantastic. I was also gladly surprised by the Spinach Salad: didn't expect much of it and liked it quite a bit.

The service could use a bit of help (plus what is up with the yelling out loud of people's numbers?) and there's not enough sitting, but hey... you get what you pay for. :)
A bit too doughy for my taste, but value for the price.

I've been coming to Blondie's since I was 14 year old coming up to Berkeley for debate tournaments and to meet with coaches. 

The pizza is pretty good, but not outstanding. It's thinner, saucier, and tastes like it's of better quality than the pizza at Fat Slice. 

I only patronize Blondie's these days when I'm in a rush, ie, I'm 10 minutes late to a class on north side and haven't eaten lunch yet. Or I'm about to go out to bars and haven't eaten dinner yet. Blondie's is useful because it lets me walk and eat. If you're in this situation, you have to ask to make sure that they don't have to warm up the pizza. Actually, this is good practice in general, since the pizza tastes like crap when it's not fresh. 

Biggest problem is that I have to eat two slices to be full, which costs about $7.50, which seems like too much given the quality and nutritional content of the food.

I hadn't been to this Blondies in about 7 years and longed for the great pizza I used to get. What a shock. The pizza was awful, we had to wait for warmed up slices while fresh pizza got cold on the front counter and to top it off the service SUCKED. I'll never be back.
 Oh well, at least Fat Slice is still good
The pizza is good and so is the service. Cheap, quick and easy.

Heard a lot of hype about this place... and it was, in fact, very good, but not enough to beat the reputation... not a five-star place.

The garlic chicken pizza was quite nice, large and flavorful, and for $4.76 with a small soda, not a bad value.

Good place, just not exceptional.

I go to blondie for pizza quite often, but the quality have been getting lower and lower. I think the the dough they use are not good or they don't cook it long enough, there's not enough crust on the slice. But I just dont know where else to go for a quick slice of pizza, Blondie and Fat slice got the same owner?

Holy cow... what do you say about a place with RHCP onthe wall wearing nothing but a sock?

No... not great pizza...  but it's a ritual... and it's cheap..  You can't say you've experienced UCB without at least stoppy by this place.
The pizza here is SO expensive. And it's not even good. It's not even comparable to Arinell pizza yet much more expensive. I would avoid going here.

Maybe having just spent a week eating pizza slices in New York has jaded me. Blondies used to be a personal favorite of mine. Unfortunately I feel that they have started to go a bit downhill. Maybe using cheaper ingredients? Not as fresh? Maybe I just know the difference now. 

Blondies is still good but unfortunately she's past her prime!
This one gets more pub than Fat Slice....and it's a solid alternative but I still like Fat Slice better.
Man I love Blondies.  The pizza's okay but I love their miso dressing salad!!!! And their garlic fries are off the hook! The berkeley ones better than the SF one.
I sure hope this place hasn't changed, but as I remember it, best pizza of my life.
pretty good pizza place for a late nite snack!!! (especially after partying?)
I love this place! The pizza is over priced for sure!!! But its the famous Blondie's  Pizza in Berkeley California!!! Its one of my personal favorites... what can I say ; )

Haven't been to Blondie's since my old SF days, and Swanie was still slingin pies there. Took my boy, which was nice. (the circle is now complete). I love the pepperoni, which I think makes their pizza what it is. It is a little less thick than I remembered (one slice used to be a meal), but still thick and awesome. Vibe is still the same - vague smell of urine from the sidewalk, and some street vendor sermonizing through the open window about the virtues of 60's and 70's rock. Awesometown. 

Historical footnote:  late night grand slam from college road trips to Cal included a slice from Blondies, a Top Dog, a burger from a long gone joint, and a King Pin Donut.
Not bad, but its no Fat Slice! The veggie slice is pretty damn good tho.

My friend @ Berkley took us here after everyone was buzzed from all the beer at one of the bars on the campus.  She told us that Blondie's pizza can only be consumed happily if and only if you are buzzed.  She was right, we loved it.  The pizza is really cheap and it is totally greasy...which is GOOD when you have tons of alcohol in your system.

*Food = good but be sure to be buzzed before you go
*Location = convenient
*Service = ok

Definitely gone down in quality. 

I went out of my way to go to Blondie's when I was in the East Bay and I was very disappointed. I used to LOVE Blondie's pizza, but in the past 5? (I'm not sure when I made it there last) years they changed the crust and it was nowhere near as thick.  I don't plan on going back. It was really disappointing.

Dude, if I wanted to tip you, I would have. Thank you for gypping me from my quarter.

Anyways...Pizza here is the kind you eat when you're hungry and don't give a fuck how you get full. Reminds me of Chicago Pizza out in Cambridge. Pepperoni special is just under five dollars; you get a slice and a drink. The menu claims it's a fat slice. I would have to admit that is true, but the crust is airy, as if the dough they used was watered down. 

Did you ever buy those Red Baron or Mama Rosa's frozen pizzas at the supermarket? The pizza kind of tastes like that but greasier. They interestingly promote organic ingredients and display the farm from which they apparently get their ingredients. That's cool and all, but if you're going to go through the trouble of getting quality ingredients, you could make the effort and produce a better slice. 

I know pizza-by-the-slice places have to deal with things others don't have to, but it's really weird seeing my slice being put into an oven and reheated. That tripped me out.

I might come back...
Magnitudes better than Fat Slice, but still pretty lame. The only times I've enjoyed it was when walking home from Bear's Lair or Kips drunk as hell. I do like their posters though.
Very cheap, but not much else going for it. Lukewarm pizza without much substance to it.
I used to eat here a few times when I went to school at UC Berkeley.  They give you big slices that are affordable, but that's about it.  Pizza is just a-ok, not super good, but not bad.

Blondies wants to be  everything Fat Slice is, but fails horribly.  The crust is thich and doughy in exactly the wrong way, the sauce is katsupy, the cheese is greasy in the only bad way.  It just doesn't work.  i second the recomendation to do  to Fat Slice

The service is alright, everyone in there aren't really friendly, but it's fast food what do you expect? It can get really busy during noon-2p, lunch hours. Definitely try it, I suggest the pepperoni pizza or cheese (the classics). Their vegetarian pizza with the wheat dough is not that good. They literally put all types of vegi on the pizza without thinking if the taste would mesh well together (broccoli?) random. If you are vegetarian, go with cheese. 

You definitely go to this place more out of convenience than for the pizza. I think Blondie 'used' to be good, but now, its just lunch. The only plus about Blondies is they put your slice in the oven to melt the cheese and give you a hot slice. This is definitely a place to go if you are running late, hungry while tabling or just want something super cheap and junk food related.
better than pleasant hill, not as good as SF. I hear they serve a "hyphy" pizza with jalapenos, a few different kinds of meats and something else. I plan on trying that...
Very inconsistent. When it's good, it's delicious, but when it's bad, it's pretty bland/dry.

I just moved here in Northern California a month ago, and I asked one of my Bay Area friends what's a place here where I could get a quick, yet good lunch. They all told me to go to Blondie's. Cheaper than yucky Big Mac, and not bad for pizza.

(vegetarian reviewer)

Pros: You get interesting combinations and the veggies look like real veggies

Cons: My pizza was floppy, with cheese that fell off in a droopy style. The salad did not taste fresh to me (regular side salad, served in a paper bowl with plastic wrap over it). And the pizza lacked any oomph, almost like it had been cooked in a microwave. Definitely like cafeteria food. The floor was not clean, either, and so I sat with my bag in my lap to keep it from getting sticky.

Two stars for being open late, for being on Telegraph, and being pizza (sort of). The more pizza options the better. So while I'm glad Blondie's exists, I choose not to eat there when presented with other pizza options.

If it's before 10pm it's worth a short walk to Arinell for a real slice. You'll be glad you did.

The best buy by the slice pepperoni pizza I've ever had.  Great in a pinch or if you've got the munchies while on a budget.  A little greasy but so delicious I had to have 2.  I'd try some of their signature slices if I lived in the area.
Pizza is decent, but is rather "cakey"... that is, the crust is about 1/2 to 3/4 of an inch thick.  Decent sauce and cheese.  The Pepperoni can be very greasy.  Salads are decent.

great pizza and the typical chill Berkeley atmosphere makes for a very happy Dana! Though I do remember the pizza being very saucy--watch your clothes! Plus they have Snapple...or at least they did the last time I was there :)

The pizza here is edible. That's about it. Like the reviewer below stated, it's pretty much similar to a slice you'd get at a street fair. 

Don't go here expecting a whole lot of anything...except for attitude. The people behind the counter can be quite unfriendly and abrasive. It actually seems to be a common occurrence in the UC Berkeley area that restaurant owners and their staff are extremely rude to the customers. I'm not really sure why that is, but I don't dig it.  

Also, I think that price is a bit ridiculous. Almost $4 a slice! You can get cheaper pizza than that in New York! And it tastes better!!!!

Blondies is the bomb... a fat slice of pizza and a soda.... 
parmasean cheese and peppers chained to the tables too..

Can't go wrong having to go through all the Berkeley parking drama to get a slice of Blondies.
Beef Pepperoni OH YEAH

Blondie's, why do I always come back to you? So convenient, so close to campus, so cheap and filling! To be absolutely honest, I can't always tell if the pizza is stellar (I pick off the cheese and drown my slice in red pepper), but the crust is perfectly thick and bready, the sauce tangy, and the toppings plenty.

I've turned down hearing horror stories about Blondie's as to keep the dream alive... the college student's most important dream.. the dream of pepperoni pizza.
I love it.  Yummy.  greasy goodness.

I love the veggie wheat slice here but service can be REALLY slow and the staff are totally inefficient.  The other day there were about 7 employees standing around doing nothing while one guy was doing all the work.

Certainly my judgment of this pizza place has been influenced by the 
worst experience ever I had here. 

I usually order a Veggie and a Pepperoni slice, which are what you expect from this kind of place - still, I do believe prices for slices of pizza are extremely high in the US, how the hell can I pay $5 for a slice of pizza, when they sell me proper food for $6 next to it?? This is what I keep telling my friend when he wants to go there, but apparently his desire to rush to go back to work in his office is too big to even contemplate the chance of having an at least minimally decent dinner....

anyway, we were once eating our stuff when a terrible guy, who had been staring at us from another table the whole time, came to us and sit at our table - the guy was probably on drugs, or anyway had serious mental issues. He started shouting crazy things, then he moved his hands (all dirty of pizza oil and tomato) to us and started touching us, and at some point he started telling us we were assholes and racists because we were asking him to please leave our table. 

None behind the counter was even considering also telling the guy something - it's jungle style. 

I just hope I'll never have to go back to such a place again.

The pizza here is thick, greasy, and mildly disgusting, but I would always find myself coming back for more.  In fact as a man with roots in north jersey, I really hope that none of my old pals find me giving this place four stars.

Not only that, I am staunchly against dirty hippies--the people that run this place.  Listen to this.  A cheese slice costs more than a veggie slice.  What's that all about.  Please, won't someone think of the poor defenseless peppers?

I've just gotten soft now that I'm a left coaster, but for some reason I always find myself coming back for more.  Maybe it's the $2 miller lite that I get with my pizza slanting my opinion.
Yuck!! It is not at all like I remembered it...

Despite my 6 years of Bay Area living, today was my first time visiting Blondie's Pizza in Berkeley, CA. My friend suggested grabbing a slice to share (since they're pretty damn big), which was definitely a good idea on her part.

We shared a slice of the pepperoni (which I ordinarily steer clear of, but now realize why it's such a popular topping!). Quite greasy, but hey - that's what fine pizza's all about.

The physical environment of Blondie's is pretty basic, but that's okay. It's obviously clean, but still has an overall grimey-chic Berkeley feel to it. The staff were friendly and one of the workers totally chatted up my friend because she was wearing an "I love London" tank, written in Arabic. Nice of him to notice, though!
The best slice of thick crust for late night snack is just out of this world.

Good pizza especally for the price. Open late so it's perfect for those "after O-Chem midterm I deserve a treat" moments. Seems like most of you prefer fat slice, but I would take blondies over fat slice any day.  More PIZZA for me!

One of the best pizza places in the Bay Area.  The prices are still cheap for pizza and a drink even for our economy.  You'll spend less than five bucks for that alone if you get the special.  They also offer small salads if you're not feeling like pizza.  The only thing that's wrong is the lack of places to sit.  You might end up standing while you eat if it's busy.  It's a great place for a greasy bite to eat whether you're a starving student or a starving adult on a budget.

Came here on Saturday..I've been here a couple times, but it was years ago. The place is small, very few spots to sit down and eat. the place was pretty empty when we walked, we got our pizza right away.
luckily it was raining so no one was by the windows smoking their cigs. 
For the pizza, yeah it was ok for a slice, it was thin, and really greasy. the grease was in puddles on top the pepperoni. didn't care for that at all.
If you want something quick for pizza i guess this is the place to go.
Good pizza all the way around. Prices aren't to bad either.
so sad i came the other day and it looks like they're not doing froyo anymore :( ... i almost liked their froyo better than the pizza!
blondie's pizza is just pizza. nothing special. people have to be out of their minds to be giving this place more than three stars.
I LOVE PIZZA.. especially NY style pizza. Blondie's delivers. Big fat hot juicy oily slices of yummy goodness.

The pizza is good...and the place fits the "how telegraph used to be" feel...

However, i haven't eaten here since I heard from a former employee that the employees spit in the food...dunno how true it was or is now, but i don't want to take the chance after hearing that...

Coming from New York I'm always a bit skeptical when I'm eating pizza from a local area away from home but this place isn't so bad. They do advertise huge slices of pizza and these slices just wasn't that big to me. 

I got a few slices of pepperoni pizza and a cheese slice. I had to carry the slices for 20 min back home so they were not as warm as I would have liked. I enjoyed the crispiness of the slices along with the grease. Even somewhat cool the pizza tasted good, I was just a bit disappointed by the size of the pizza: I was expecting gigantic slices of pizza.
I love this place! I go all the way to Berkeley for their pizza lol i tried this asparagus and chicken pizza from there and it was great i should have gotten 2 pieces!

This is the place to go for a poor college student such as myself. I like greasy pizza, so if you don't then I suppose don't listen to this review. You can get a big slice of pizza and a coke for four bucks, which is cheaper than a whole lot of other places on Telegraph. It's quick, cheap, and delicious. Blondie's isn't a five-star restaurant, but it serves up some decent pizza.
I love their pepperoni pizza here. It's the best I've ever had.

They have gone downhill in recent years, but the pizza is still good. Come in hungry, leave full. Bonus: They now serve frozen yogurt. Although, you have yogurt park right down the street, so I don't know if this really counts as a bonus. I do love the whole wheat vegetarian though!

Cheap, yummy pizza and other foods (salad I had was better than one from Cafe Intermezzo), and semi-eco-conscious (organic veggies and compost bins) all in one joint?

Wow, that is impressive in a college neighborhood.  Blondie's over Fat Slice hands down in my opinion.
amazing!

My first time EVER in Berkeley was roughly 10 years ago, I was traveling to the city to check out the campus and get a feel for the town.  Right there in the middle of the hustle and bustle known as Telegraph resides Blondie's.  This place is always packed and understandably so.  The slices are huge and the taste is superb.  I have tried three types of pizzas that they offer here, their pepperoni, BBQ chicken and vegetable.  The amount of pepperoni that comes with each slice is generous and they bake it to perfection, a little greasy but hey its a pizza right?  The bbq chicken was good, the BBQ sauce they use is sweet with a slight tang to it towards the end of your bite, I recommend trying it out when its the special of the day.  Lastly, I am a MEAT kind of guy but decided to try something different for once.  The veggie slice did not disappoint, the amount of toppings they gave me made me forget that there was no meat in it, it was really good.  Blondie's is open late and if you're a starving student or pinching pennies, they have a little something for everyone!  Eat Up!
I think the west coast has some great pizza, but not at this place. The crust is raw, doughy, and tasteless.  It isn't worth the price.

i don't know why i bother ordering a pizza when they just wait til you get there to make it. this has happened at least 5 times in the last year. i have called in orders, gone in & talked to someone face to face & every time same result. i go in tell them i ordered a cheese pizza easy on the sauce & well done they look at me with a blank expression say it will be a minute & give me the next cheese pizza that is barely cooked to come out of the oven. thank goodness for nicks pizza on shattuck. maybe you guys should go in there to see how to treat your customers & make a pizza. you have disappointed me for the last time!

Ya want Hepatitis or food poisoning--you run a good chance here, so come and get it!

This place is super trendy and popular with the downtown/Cal crowd...Pizza by the slice that is quick and cheap.

The pizza isn't horrible, its so-so, and I don't think they claim to be the best--they do serve a special niche well.

After hearing from a former employee of this place though (who quit and was not fired), it makes me want to pass right by it...

The place is clearly dirty and not clean, common sense will tell you that when you walk in.  

Hey, when you're a broke student though, you lower your standards on food--I did and ate here often while living in Berkeley.
Good for when you need to grab a cheap and quick bite to eat.
I've been going to Blondie's Pizza since the late 80's (as far as I can rememeber, lol) in both SF and Berkeley. Still love the pizza, can't go wrong here. I've never had a bad experience.

I love Blondie's.  Classic Berkeley.  It isn't the best pizza in the world but it is damn good for what you pay.  If you are in Berkeley you have to eat at Blondie's or Top Dog.  Two of the best bangs for your buck.

Oh, Blondie's. Nothing beats a juicy and tasty pizza except for this place. They have plenty of different kinds of pizza flavors, along with a variety of other food menus besides pizza. I always decide to get the original cheese or just plain jane pepperoni. FACT: I tend to see a lot of oil, so its a no no. And there aren't much tables/chairs if there's a lot of customers.

While on telegraph, its nice to stop by for a quick meal after shppping around and eat at this great pizza place. I recommend Blondie's & I would always love to come back!
I don't really understand the hype about this place... maybe its because I got a veggie pizza on wheat dough, but this place wasn't that yummy, and I am VERY easy to please.

We drove all the way from Sacramento to eat here because I missed eating at Blondie's pizza in Union Square, SF.  I was disappointed because it was not the same.  When I held the first piece of pizza to eat, it was like holding a tie.  The piece was so thin and limpy, I had to use two hands to eat.  It was not like that in San Fran.  We ordered a large pizza to go as well and the whole pie was thin.  I don't remember requesting them to make it a thin crust pie.  They get 3 stars because they do have the best pepperoni and cheese of all pizza places.

But this place looked very depressed to me.  The guy who called our order was upset because he said he was calling our order no. a few times.  I didn't hear him and my husband said he did but it wasn't our order no.  Maybe he should lay off on the pipe.
Very convenient place to eat. They always have pepperoni and cheese and a daily special. I usually just get the pepperoni, but once in a while when I'm feeling adventurous, I get the daily special.

Great pizza and a solid choice for lunch or dinner on the go.  I usually go for the veggie or special slice if it's interesting, and the toppings are quite generous.  It's clean (particularly for Telegraph standards) and a good place to people watch.  Plus, it's not awkward eating alone since there's always reading material on the walls in front of you at the counter spaces.

Best pizza on Telegraph. 

Good quick cheap pizza with creative daily special flavor. Nothing special but better than fat silce on the same street.


I got the pepperoni pizza combo for ($3.50) A slide with a small soda..

The dough feels airy and light, so with one slice you might want another

Blondie's.  Pizza.  Yum.
I discovered Blondie's in the early 80's, when I used to hang out at the Keystone every Wednesday night.  It was love at first bite.
I've also eaten many times at the Powell St  and Pleasant Hill locations.  All good, but Berkeley is my favorite.  If I'm in Berkeley, it's hard to keep me from going to Blondie's.
If you like New York style pizza, this is probably not the place for you.
But if you like big, thick, greasy slices of pizza, you can't go wrong.  Tasty, filling, and reasonably priced.
I love this place!
They need one in Rohnert Park...

3.5 stars to be exact. The place is a bit inconsistent. Sometimes I get huge slices and sometimes I get joke slices. Sometimes my pizza is so fresh and juicy and other times it seems like it's been sitting out on the table for hours. The people there rude at times but I guess you can't expect much out of a pizza joint. Even though it is relatively cheap for a lunch, I personally think they charge a bit too much for pizza. All in all good for a quick lunch or even dinner.

I absolutely love Blondie's!!

Usually I'm a "Plain Jane" when it comes to pizza, I like cheese or Ham and pineapple and that's pretty much it.

I was a little more adventurous when coming here only because you basically have 4 options Cheese, Pepperoni, Vegetarian, or the Special of the Day.  So I decided to try a few specials through the few times I've been there.  And I loved all of them, I tried their BBQ Chicken, Special Mushroom, and of course their Hawaiian.  I can't wait to try more!!

Their staff is very fast and friendly and the location is very convienent (right off of Telegraph).

Blondie's isn't the most legit pizza place on earth. It's pretty good, but it's more for the ambiance.
When I go to the Telegraph - I HAVE to go to Blondie's. It's right on the cooler yet not janky street, and has just a Berkeley-esque about it. It pretty much defines that crazy city.
Pizza isn't bad or great - but regardless, you have to come here.

Maybe I just got lucky b/c I can't see how some yelpers gave this place a poor review

--and the previous person who said to eat this only buzzed is mistaken..I was completely sober (wish I wasn't), and still was good

--this is your typical small pizza joint..limited seating, loud atmosphere but good pizza by the slice..I went with a slice of pepperoni...sauce wasn't overly abundant, just enough cheese and well cooked pepperoni (not burnt)..it's greasy I won't lie there..but it's pizza ya know?? if it bothers you, simply wipe some of the grease off with a napkin (you'll save something like 50 calories or something, look it up)

--they do also offer wheat pizza for vegetarian eaters for the health conscientious

--along with pizza, if you want to crave your sweet tooth or cool down on hot sunny day, they offer frozen yogurt..can't recall all the flavors but they had chocolate, strawberry, peach etc..I had a taste of the strawberry and it was very tasty

--overall good place to eat on the go

Really underwhelming...we came Friday at 10:30pm. They weren't taking orders anymore for whole pizzas (even though they are open until 2am?) so we had to get slices. The pepperoni pizza was really greasy. No one was full after 1 slice (hence why we wanted to buy a whole pizza) and we ended up going to Top Dog after. Top Dog was delicious, we wished that we'd skipped the pizza and headed there first.

haven't been here in a while but at the time it was some of the worst pizza i ever had.  telegraph does not do pizza well.  although you don't really have to when your demographic is a bunch of poor hungry college kids....
Gooey cheese, crispy thin crust. Delicious. A must try in this area!
Meh - pizza was not great.  Veggie was bland and pepperoni was just sort of . . . meh.  It was open late but probably won't be going again.

I'm generally a nonpicky pizza fan so I would give blondie's a solid 3.5, mainly for its price and its substitute, fat slice, across the street. I've rounded up and given this place a 4 because of their daily specials which are sometimes excellent! I save the date they serve deep dish style pizza as their daily special in my cellphone... I just love how it costs the same as the other choices (which aren't very wide, by the way.) 

Still, I'd only pay for their 4 dollar slice of pizza for their daily special menu- not their other toppings which are pretty mundane. At fat slice, you can get a faaat slice for the same price on any day. 

Solid 3.5. Not too shabby, satisfactory pizza, great special menu, decently priced.  The concept of shelling out 4 dollars for slice of pizza is still hard for me to overcome, since you can get 5 dollar pizzas at little caesars, but i'm coming to terms with the fact that the price is pretty normal for most pizza places that sell individual slices.

Since it's recession and all, the boy and I are constantly looking for cheap but good date night spots. Since I haven't been here since college era (all of my friends went to Cal) so this used to be the spot for us.

Anyway, I got the usual (cheese pizza + a diet coke) and the boy had the pepperoni with his "fanta"  - by the way they have their own frozen yogurt now! Whoa! In the end, it was a good date night - just make sure you work out the next day!
Greasy as heck, but very good traditional thin crust New York style pizza.
