I suppose it helps having an outdoor eatery with open space.  Just a few feet away, I could already smell the aroma of fast-food pizza!  That's really what brought me in here.

I ordered a veggie slice and it had a deal where I got a bottled water for 50 cents, pretty cool!  I guess it's to promote eating healthy.  Although, in my opinion, the slice was 4 something and that's too pricey for this fast-food joint.  I expect that to be the price at a gourmet pizza eatery.  

The veggie slice had a wide variety of healthy greens, reds, and purples, but a sparingly amount of cheese.  It was not greasy and I gobbled it up within 5 minutes.  Either it was that yummy or I was super hungry, but I believe its the latter.

This place is good for a quick, decent bite, especially if you're on the go, which is most likely its purpose.  The price, however is disappointing.  And if you don't like standing up to eat while people converse loudly, it may not be a good choice.

their salads are pre-made and packed with tons of stuff. i was disappointed they were out of the spicy walnut AND the strawberry fields and ended up with the greek. it was still pretty good, fresh and the dressing was great.
Best pizza by the slice.  Give me give me please!

I believe I've burned the roof of my mouth on their cheese more times than should happen for a normal human being.

Good, cheap pizza by the slice - though if cheese hits $3, then it will become increasingly better to just get a cheap crepe from right next door. The vegetarian pizza always manages to depress me - just stick with cheese if you're vegetarian.

This location is much better than the one in SF.

My review of the SF location: http://dontcallitfriscoblog.blogspot.com/
Good pizza, few seats, however $3 for an average size slice...and bounce back and forth between here and Fat Slice for my overpriced pizza eatings.

Berkeley wouldn't be the same without Blondies.
Love the chill atmosphere. The funky bar seating is cool because they put up fun and new articles to read up on the wall in front of you as you try to figure out how to conquer your giant piece of pizza.

Lines can be pretty long but it only confirms that the food is that good.

When I think of Blondie's pizza I think of mediocre food. It's not bad necessarily, but it's not really good either. Their chicken plates are OK, but the skin tends to be kind of slimy. 

Meh. There is a lot of better pizza in the area.
BBQ chicken pizza was yummy!

It's like the worse tasting version of Fat Slice. I will say it's less greasy, but if the grease on Fat Slice is what gives it the flavor then I'd have to go with the grease... still cheap and fast though.
Love It!!!
Doughy crust, lots and lots of cheese.  Toppings are plentiful if you choose to order them.  Relatively affordable too.

This joint serves almost-New-York style, by-the-slice (or whole pie) pizza at around $3.75 a slice. The quality seems to change day-by-day, and I highly recommend stopping in right when your desired topping is straight out of the oven - sometimes the endpieces turn a little bland, and they usually serve the largest pieces first - if you're going to get a slice, get a SLICE. Specifics - lots of mild-medium cheese, a tolerable amount of grease that definitely will soak through your paper plate (sounds scarier than it is), and a pretty solid bone of pizza crust - enough for dipping; extra dressing for that purpose is available.
Plenty of toppings around of you just aren't a straight-off-the-pan person like I am (cheese, pepper flakes, and herbs).
And salads at Blondie's actually great! They're prepackaged but a lot larger than meets the eye initially. I'd recommend Yogurt Park around the block for froyo, though; you can get a lot more for the price, and at higher quality.
Dining area is cheap-looking, so don't bring a date here to eat - however, it's roomy enough so that you're not bumping elbows with the customers in line.

Absolutely the best crust on a pizza. I felt that the crust on Blondie's Pizza was really unique. I thoroughly enjoyed eating the not too thin and not too thick crust that was nicely seasoned. 

Warning Chiptole Pizza is very very spicy...in a good way of course.

To Jason I.- Pizza is not supposed to be good for the body anyway, just suck it up and wipe your pizza off before you eat, you'll be fine.

Blondies is amazing. Greasy as hell or not, I'm never disapointed with this place. Ever.

This place offers huge slices of pizza. The only thing I've tried here is their salad. I had a coupon for their salad when I came here, so I don't know what the regular price for a salad is. The salad was decent, and it came with a thick piece of wheat bread. But if you want salad, I recommend Cafe Intermezzo or Smart Alec's.

My parents used to bring me here as a kid to get pizza and its the best. I grew up on this stuff.  The one is SF doesn't measure.  This is the original - always have loved it and always will continue to love this place.
Fresh, hot, slightly crispy, and ol' fashioned greasy goodness with a side of coke for about $5 -- Holla.

I don't care for Blondie's. I find that their crust is usually burnt, and their cheese is so thick that some parts aren't all the way melted. Even their other foods here aren't that great.

I've experience better, its true, its called Fat Slice and for ten cents cheaper and block walk, its worth it.
I love it!!!! good portions and great price!

A slice of pizza for $3.00 is one of my favorite snacks ...  I often went there for a slice when I worked for the University, but I was pleased to discover that they also deliver delicious, whole pizzas, for a reasonable price.     I did spot a cockroach once, which is unusual for California ...

Great Pizza for a great price - fountain drinks could be a larger though!

Go at least once a week, easy to walk to

If you're looking for pizza in the Berkeley area, I'd say that you could do a lot worse than Blondie's.  They have all the normal stuff like cheese and pepperoni, but they also have specials that are different every day, and a really good vegetarian pizza (i usually get it, and i'm not even a vegetarian).  The prices are reasonable (the drinks are overpriced though), a slice is about $3.50 if i remember correctly.

Blondie's is the pizza place I go to when I just want a good slice of pizza.  They have a special everyday which is 2.50 or 3 bucks a slice.  I can't remember because it's been a while since I've been there.  One time at the Blondie's in SF, they had a chicken asparagus pizza which was the best combination ever.  I've never seen it offered at Berkeley but the chicken pesto is good.  If you want a quick bite near campus, go to Blondies.  The pizza is amazing.

Blondie's and Fat Slice are basically the exact same thing.
Big huge slices of thick-crusted pizza for super cheap prices.

Blondie's sometimes has more interesting pies available (BBQ chicken the last time I was there) but this location is so ghetto-tastic and full of thugs that I just can't give it a good review.

Fat Slice across the street may be just as dirty, but at least the clientele there don't look and act like they're packing heat.

Good greasy pizza and pretty cheap. They won't validate your parking, but they will help you with your hunger. Grab a fast slice for under 3 bucks or a pretty decent sized pizza for 10. Just look out for seating because this place fills up fast.

Great place to grab a fast pizza. The owner also own Fat Slice, but I much prefer Blondie's over Fat Slice. I frequent Blondie's often when the $2.50 coupon circulate; a slice and a small fountain soda for $2.50 is a steal!

bl0ndies is either hit or miss.
point blank.
i have been going here most of my life.
there are some rules you have to follow if u want good pizza.
1. try to get the pizza when its hot and fresh out the oven. ( even if you have to wait!)

2. dont get any fountian drinks. get a bottle soda.

3. d0nt eat inside. find a place outside.

follow these rules if you want a good pizza experience at blondies =)
All it's got going for it is that its better than Fat Slice...That's about it. I hate these thick pizzas!

Not as big as one in SF, but just as good.
Back in the day the pizza use to be so thick and puffy, now they're thin and crispy. Oh well, times are tough. The pizza is still really good tho. Affordable, good assortment of pizza and fast.
Although both are horrible, I'd say Blondie's beats fat slice. Thick, soggy pizza, too much nasty cheese. It's cheap, but you get what you pay for.

Blondie's pizza location is great. However, the service was somewhat slow especially for a busy place. I ordered 2 slices of pizza with a drink and it cost over $10. Granted the two slices were packed with meat and was a large portion.

Last time I went to Blondies, I got.. I believe it was called "Meat lovers special"? It was one of the daily specials for $3.45+tax.  Nothing too special about it. It was VERY thin with lots of toppings. It was kind of hard to even hold up the pizza to eat it and I needed to use my plate to help me balance the slice of pizza.  I saw other customers folding the pizza in half before eating it and that seemed to help them considerably.

The interior has a bunch of articles on the wall.  I don't know if they're random or if they may have some sort of significance.  There are only a few tables to sit at and some counters too.  You would think they'd have more chairs or something considering all the Berkeley students who go and buy their pizza.

Anywho, I just thought the place was okay. I'd come back if I was really super hungry and nothing else was open, but other than that, I think I'm gonna pass.
A decent slice of pie at competitive prices.  In terms of taste, I'd definitely prefer fat slice down the block.  Blondies definitely has more topping variety under the heat lamps.

A little slice of history right there on telegraph. The pizza is a good fill, but I warn you, do NOT get the "salad" pizza, you'll want to die. Heaps of tomatoes and spinach do not belong on lukewarm pizza. They added a yogurt machine now too, so that makes it like the 5th fro-yo place in the 2 block area...
The prices have gone up =( and the slices seemed slightly smaller. Maybe I've just grown up and am using my own money now instead of asking dad for a $5er. Still love the sauce though!

I am a big fan of Blondie's Pizza.  The vegetarian pizza is great.  Even better is the salad with the Miso dressing.

In fact, the pizza at Blondie's is among the best I have ever had.  If I hadn't eaten at the likes of Cheeseboard and Zachary's, this place would get five stars.  But it's tough being a pizza joint in Berkeley, and hence Blondie's, as incredible as it is, only gets four stars.

There's always a lack of seating... you pay an extra quarter for a box... and delicious toppings on large slices of pizza.  Why are there no small pizza shops like this in the LA area?...anyway,  I am intrigued by the stool/bar seating because they have news/media postings on the wall you can read... This is where I learned about that Sri Lankan singer that sang about her experience during the war and that's why she rapped about airplanes, terrorists, and other crap... See, if it weren't for blondies I would've just thought the Chicky was a little nutcase. :) thanks, Blondies for your food and entertainment haha
Good pizza, good price. 'nuff said

My place of choice for pizza on southside!

I love walking past this store and looking at the daily special.  They have a great rotation of daily special slices so you always have something new you can order when you're tired of the normal cheese, pepperoni, or vegetarian slices.  My favorite specials are the ones with pesto sauce! Yum!

Blondie's pizza is still greasy but not as greasy as Fat Slice.  Vegetarian on wheat crust is the healthiest option while the daily specials are usually the greasiest and unhealthiest.  Good place to hit up for a quick bite!

Oh yea, they usually have coupons for pizza/drink combos passed out in the beginning of a semester.  Stock up!!!  They're extremely useful if you're a poor college student like me.

Side note: One thing I don't get....Blondie's sells...fro-yo?  huh?

When I was at Berkeley, my mid-night snack was either Blondie's or Yokohama station. (Of course that was back then when I was crazy skinny!) I remember going to Blondie's, buy the Pepperoni slice combo with coke, load unbelievable amount of condiments on the top, then spend next 10 mins chatting with friends or reading obscure posts on the wall. Those were great times. 

4 stars for the sentimental value.

Honestly, nothing special.  I ordered a "fat slice" of pepperoni pizza and a drink and paid close to $5.  The drink was tiny, and there were no free refills.  The "fat slice" wasn't all that big, and for all of those Costco fans out there, my slice was slightly smaller than the average $2 Costco slice.  Not a bad deal considering the location however.

I just wasn't impressed by the balance of the cheese, sauce and crust.  I was also not very happy at the lack of the bathroom facility of a place to wash hands.

Spicy pepperoni was a plus however.
I love pizza but this place is just so gross. There is such good pizza in Berkeley, but not at this place.

Extremely bready and bland; you can't taste anything but the bread! Filling --yes, but for $3.50 I want something that stimulates the taste buds. 

Was starving at the time, so it worked but would risk mal-nutrition to not come back here again.
Pizza's just alright here.  I usually just get the Godzilla with all my friends.

I have to say that this is the ONLY place that serves pizzas whose pizza crust I will actually take pleasure in eating. 

Yummmm....

Delicious! I love when they have BBQ chicken slices. 



I never go when there's an event on/near campus and it's crazy busy. I rarely ever feel like standing on the sidewalk in line or hustling for a table. If it's moderately busy, I'd rather just get that sh*t to go and be about my merry way. That is just me.


Service makes me feel like I'm actually ordering pizza in New York and nobody really smiles unless of course you smile first and then they're obligated to smirk back at you. I'm sure your jaw hurts after the 200th customer. However, on the occasions when someone behind the counter decides to give me a genuine smile, it makes my delicious pizza experience (crust included) even better.

I have searched far and wide for a slice of vegetarian pizza that would live up to it's namesake. Their veggie slice is the best vegetarian pizza ever.

Why? Because they don't load you up with mushrooms (not a vegetable!) and olives (it's pickled), and if you're LUCKY other places will put onion or bell peppers.

Blondie's uses zucchini & lots of diced tomato. YES. NOW we're talking vegetables.
Yummy pizza with lunch special! How could one not love this place!?

Best pizza in b town, which aint saying much but my god this stuff hits spot whn ur a little drikn or a little =~. AnywY cant go wrong with the pep and it kills fat slice or westcoast anyday, plus they are always givn out coupons for cheap deals! Shipoopi

Excellent Pizza. They use the best quality cheese, meat and sauce from organic farms and hands-down the best pizza in Berkeley. The problem is a whole pie can be expensive. If you go there, make sure to buy a slice.

There was no wait when I entered Blondie's, but it looks like the pizza is pre-made and reheated when you order. It seems like, when I was in school, Blondie's had a bigger pizza and thicker crust with cornmeal that would get everywhere. The one I ate recently was a lot thinner and crispy (I always enjoy a crispy crust), but it was just wasn't as I remembered. The restaurant also looks different; the vintage posters are gone, replaced with a mural of sorts. I do like the layout; it's an open eatery with seats . They have a good beer selection and a much more extensive menu than Fat Slice, including more custom combinations of pizza and salads. I enjoyed my classic pepperoni, which had a pool of grease sitting at the top (yum!), but I felt like the pepperoni was overcooked, a little chewy, and some of the flavor had been lost.

Blondie's is one of my top 5 favorite pizzas.  I have had a lot of pizza in my day and I am sure there is much better than this, but I just really like their pizza.  Plain cheese is my favorite, but I like the veggie too.  Cheap, filling, fast; an all around good deal!

It's okay. If you're in the area during the day they'll probably hand you a coupon for a pizza and drink for $3.50 (pretty much a free drink). Fat Slice is cheaper without the coupon, and has well, fatter slices. Really it depends on what their special is because their BBQ Chicken or Sausage Supreme rules, but if you don't like spicy and all they have is Hyphy Pizza, go to fat slice.

Though they're open super late so that's pretty cool while drunk!
You gotta mess with the hyphy pizza

Remember when the slices used to be $1.50??? What happened to that :'( The pizza is greasy and not amazing- but the pepperoni is made of beef! And they have a lot of variety, with attempts to be health and environment conscious. 4 stars because it's Blondie's- it will always be an integral part of Telegraph Ave and Berkeley. Not for pizza connoisseurs :P
My favorite Pizza in the bay area thus far!

In my opinion Blondie's sits at the bottom of all pizza places at Berkeley.  There is absolutely nothing especially good about it (in contrast, Fat Slice is at least very good for thick, doughy pizza), and it tastes just like Domino's, maybe even worse.  The only reason it's popular is because of its proximity to the Berkeley campus, bay area history, and cheapness.  If instead it was located where Cheeseboard is, nobody would ever go out of the their way for it.  That's why Blondie's only has locations in crowded places where people are on a budget.  

Don't get it wrong, I'm no pizza snob, I love Fat Slice and Round Table, I just call out crap when I taste it.
Yummy pizza for a great price! =)

DAMN DELICIOUS PIZZA!

I'd give them five stars, but pizza isn't always hot or fresh out of the oven. Went there last night around 11pm and it tasted not up to par. I'm guessing it had been sitting out there for awhile cause it tasted dry and not warm at all. I guess you just have to time it and go get your slice right when they take it out of the oven. Also, it can get REALLY crowded and there's no where to sit and it's really hard to move around.

this place is bomb.com and that's all that matters.

great location and awesome pizza....NOT the best you've ever had...but still very delicious.

it's a bay area classic!!!
pizza is only ok. i expected much better....
Yes...this one is better than the Blondies in the city. But go across the street and tell me Fat Slice isn't better!

Once great, no more! This place used to make one mean pizza, but I went there yesterday and it was lousy! The service was poor. The girl at the front counter acted as if she had never looked at their own menu and spoke with a barely audible voice. After waiting 20 or so minutes, they delivered a flat, blah looking pizza. It looked nothing like I had remembered. When I told the guy who dropped it off it was supposed to be thick crust, he just stared at me, said nothing, then walked away. Another girl came over to check and explained "it's because of the weather."  The pizza was greasy, had almost no sauce and sparse toppings. I explained to my family, it used to be great, it did.....just not anymore. The pizza was crap, it tasted like a frozen pizza. I suspect hey must've sold the chain or something? What was once a great pizza joint is now completely passable. I will never go back!
I have dreams about this pizza! The price is good and the pizza is even better.
This place is so high school!  Haven't been there since I graduated in '88.
great pizza really it is! But it costs to much. I wish I could go here, but what happened to the $1.50 slices, now it costs over 3 bucks! this place is badly managed, or just plain greedy
Just because they are Blondies.  But seriously, is there a better pie?

The pizza here is decent.  If you crave food late and want grease, Blondie's is the solution.  The quality of pizza by-the-slice depends on how long it's been sitting, so if you want the cheese that stretches off the slice like it does in the commercials but never in the box, get an entire pizza fresh out of the oven and eat it there.  The pepperoni is pretty darn good.  Granted, you will meet strange and sometimes rowdy people at night, but you're in Berkeley so stop complaining.  It is getting expensive though at over three bucks a slice [sometime's I'll want two]

One of the three southside late-night favorites for Cal students, along with topdog and la burrita. I'm partial to it over fat slice because it's closer to the rest of the late-night food, closer to most of the southside students, and in a better-lit path than fat slice.

Blondie's has got some interesting flavors! The pizzas of the day have some definite kick to it. The pizza is fresh, the slices are big and the prices are reasonable. I would definitely recommend Blondie's over Fat Slice.

OK, well I got off to a shaky start in this place, but my husband swore the pizza rocked! I'm not sure if it was the red and blue tape lines on the floor to indicate where to go, or the gaudy mish mash of colored ugly signs everywhere, but esthetically it wasn't pleasing. I couldn't get beyond the cold, unwelcoming ambiance; just didn't feel like where pizzas should come from. However, I have to admit my husbands pizza crust looked REALLY tasty...that brick oven flakiness. If you are looking for a quick bite, and are willing to walk with it...Blondies might work for you. There are a few random tables and stools facing the wall to sit on. I bet this place is busy during school...within a block of U.C. Berkeley.

I like this place, its not cheap cuz its about 3-4 bucks for a damn slice of pizza but its good.  They have a special everyday, they got a fuckin calendar of their specials posted on the fuckin front door so peep that if you want to come back a different day and shit.

Make sure you get your shit heated up if its been sitting for too long, real talk.

I've only been there once.. and it was amazing!!
My friends and I were going to a Cal Berkely Volleyball game and we wanted to stop for dinner. So we went to Blondies and there were a lot of us... They have many different sizes. We got the biggest size and it was huge and it wasn't very expensive as i recall. We got sausage and peporonie. it was yummy

Blondie's is in a fierce match with Fat Slice for the worst Pizza on Telegraph Ave.,but Fat Slice wins. These places make pizza making seem like an incredibly difficult art. You would think a little tang to the sauce would be doable, or a crust or cheese that wasn't related to the cardboard family could be managed. Couldn't they go steal whatever they do at decent pizza places like Gioia or Escape from New York Pizza ? They seem to have a built in clientele of students needing an infusion of some greasy salty negative nutritional value food item and they just don't try. It's sad.

Typically, this place is a 3 star, but b/c of such great memories here, i decided to give it another star.

One night, after a long night at Raleigh's aka Manny tap room, my friends and I decided to stroll over for late night grub!

I was not even hungry, but my friend forced me to eat half his pizza, even though I knew he was hungry, b/c he felt bad i wasn't eating. Little gestures like that makes me smile. Thanks friend!

Blondie's has..i think three choices every day. Cheese, Pepperoni, and pizza of the day.

Unfortunately, prices has steady gone up, like all the stores on Telegraph!

Cheap pizza!  That's what this place is, cheap pizza!  And I'm not calling it cheap, like a cheap whore, or maybe I am.  But it's hella cheap pizza!  If you're low on the funds and need some grub, you need to get the cheap pizza!

I got a salad, which is pre-made.  For some reason I was thinking that they would make the salad for me fresh.  I'm not sure why.  Maybe because the pizza is made fresh.  Otherwise the salad was decent.  I would have felt better if it had more chicken in it.  But like I said it was decent.  I really should have gotten the cheap pizza!

The place is kind of dingy, but what do you expect when you have cheap pizza?  Candles, romantic music.  Oh, hell no!  You get sticky tables and counters.  If you are a germ a phobe, please make sure you wipe down your table and seat before using them.  Or better yet, get your pizza to-go and eat else where.  The workers there look intimidating, but they are hella nice.  Like hella nice and patient!  I'm glad they have quality workers to go with the cheap pizza!!!
Love a veggie slice where the veggies outweigh the cheese and crust.

Same deal here as the Union Square location.  It was a useful spot to grab something before a concert at the Greek Theatre.  Keep in mind no tables, just a few counters, and a lot of people just take their slice and walk with it.  Pizza itself is par...of course, par for pizza is nummy, so no problems there.

Pretty much the same as the Blondie's on Powell in SF. Greasy but decent pizza at average prices. Although they did go out of there way to let the customers know that their pepperoni is made of 100% beef. Thank goodness, I was worried for a second...
Been coming here ever since there was a Mr.Rags next door. That was about a decade ago or so. Love how they have reading material posted up on the wall.
This place will never receive a Michelin rating, but damn if it doesn't serve a purpose when you are stumbling back to BART from a Cal game...

QUICK, EASY AND GREASY!

This is a great stop whenever you're in Berkeley. Get a quick bite of pizza heaven. Its decently priced and not really too dirty on the inside! Most people are really on the go around here but they've got tables and chairs if you just wan to chill and eat and people watch since we all know that there are some crazy character in Berkeley. There's not really much to say about the place, it's a quick pizza joint. Flavor wise it isn't that bad but to me it isn't the best. its also very affordable slices and the selection is abundant with unique concoctions to satisfy your craving. So all you kids out there if you're ever in the Berkeley area stop by and grab a bite and you wont be disappointed!

I loveee this place. Conveniently located adjacent to an inconvenient campus, and yes, they have very, very affordable prices. My brother and I had the 11" 2 topping with Pepperoni and Spinach.

It was merely a simple pizza in the sea of complicated, interestingly-named specials. Plenty of space and choices here, it suddenly got busy closer to 1 than noon.

The pizza was not nearly as greasy as the horror stories I've read recently here on yelp, and in fact the pizza was crisp with just enough sauce, cheese, and a slight amount of grease on top. That excess was easily sopped off with a napkin.

All in all, I would come back here again if by some messed up twist of fate I were back in the area.

Love me sum Blondie's...I always get a cheese slice...If I'm feeling really hungry, then I might get the pepp...Love the cheese & crushed peppers available at ur convenience 2 shake on as much as u want...Cool spot...Been coming here 4 years...

I don't think this place need another review.

Blondie's is an old establishment and hasn't changed much.
One thing I noticed: crusts got thinner.

cheap, pretty good, quick.

I lived off these slices for a while in my younger days.  I have had NY pizza and this is comparable. It was always a great place for young skateboarders and anarchists to get some work and make some awesome pizza for cheap.   Always look forward to grabbing a slice of just the cheese and making a meal out of it.

Hands down this is my favorite place for a slice of Pepperoni Pizza. I don't eat swine so I normally wouldn't eat Pork Pepperoni, Lucky for me this place uses Beef Pepperoni! It tastes amazing! They always have slices coming out fresh out the oven, if you are in the area, do not miss the chance to have a legendary slice of pizza at Blondies! - Extremely satisfied customer!

If you buy a large pizza and split it. It's a good deal, but the slices are so big, that you could just buy two slices and be uber full. 

If you feel like you want to do some reading and eat, then take a seat at the side wall and read the articles pinned up on the wall. 

Right across from a bank machine if you need cash.

I LOOOOOVE BLONDIESSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS SO MUCH! it's the best ever!!! BEEF peperoni i know, sounds kind of weird huh but it's not it's one of the best things besides JESUS that hit my life!! you have to try it..i dunno about the rest of the pizza stuff but i just get the regular peperoni and cheese. PROMISE you won't regret it...just make sure you work out afterwards...it's extra greasy, hey if you gonna have a FAT day might as well go all out right? LOL oh also go at night, that's when i go it's better it's something about the ppl that make it durning the day...i like food that is prepared with love not like, and at night they make it with love. They also always give me a slice that comes out of the oven and let me choose my slice. : )

To me, this place is just like every other pizza place. Good fatty pizza, but nothing super special. The seating layout on the inside is also kind of empty - they could definitely fit in more tables or chairs or something inside. I like reading the magazine & newspaper articles on the walls though.
This place is horrible!!! Avoid. Extremely rude and bad service. Bad quality and price.
Tasty, greasy pizza.  Right across the street from Fat Slice.

Oh gosh in just a few words, I love this place!!!!!  I crave it like there is no tomorrow and even if I have it the night/day or week before I want it again and again!

My favorite is the cheese and pepperoni ofcourse.  The pizza is soft, cheese is fresh and it's always right out of the oven.  I've gotta say this place is one of the best, you have got to check it out.  They also have one in SF, too bad it closes so early ahhhh.

I used to be a fan of Blondie's (SF) until I started buying slices from this one in Berkeley. The slices are way too greasy, albeit large, and they are thick-crusted abominations of true pizza. I got diarrhea once from eating this greasy mess. Yes, it's a pretty large slice plus soda for about 3 dollars, but you can do better with 3 bucks in Berkeley.

Don't get me wrong.
Their pizza is great.
HOWEVER, they wouldn't serve me what I wanted, a whole 18" Chipotle Chicken pizza because they didn't want to make it. WTF

Terribly boring pizza that was one of my first "by the slice" pizzas I have ever had in my life, hanging out in Berkley like some mod skater punk rude boy idiot.

Lovely memories, okay pizza.
Pretty much a Berkeley institution, and where students often go to get a quick slice of pizza.  That'd be the only reason to go.
crap pizza. crap salads. with so much good cheap food in berkeley why settle for blondies?

without a doubt - best pizza on the planet, perhaps in the universe. regardless of the kind i got - i was not disappointed. i never am. the crust alone is made from bready goodness, and the ingredients!! i believe they have a bunch culinary elves in the back who put it all together. 
great wait staff - very patient, and courteous. i've never had issues with them in all the years i've been going there...
 the fountain cups could be bigger,but on the whole - it's a yumfest.
every time i've gone, i really haven't had to wait in a long time, which is great because there have been times when the line goes out the door. 
i love people watching and the window seat. telegraph avenue provides great entertainment value for free. 
for me - a trip to berkeley involves pizza from Blondie's,  and dogs from Top Dog.

So first, the price is fair, the veggie pizza is around $3.25, but the pizza could be considered gourmet so it is totally reasonable.  The service was good, I asked for my water bottle room temperature, the girl was more than willing to go back in to their storage room to get me one.  The atmosphere was cozy, feel free to go by yourself (I actually recommend it).  They have a nice wall full of magazine articles to read while you enjoy a wonderful pizza by itself.
i still like their veggie pizza!  plus, their open late, and that's always a good thing in my book!

A little bit overrated (I prefer Fat Slice), but still a pretty good, greasy piece of pizza.  I usually go with the pepperoni or their special of the day.  One great thing about Blondie's is that it's open relatively late, and it tastes even better after a few drinks at one of the nearby bars.

There are so many things that are wrong with Blondie's.

The available seating is pretty weak because if you are traveling with a group you are essentially condemned to sit at a table that will intersect with the lines waiting for the cashier or their pizzas. So for groups you pretty much HAVE to choose carry-out. If you are eating alone then have fun sitting at one of the bar stools staring at a wall :(.  

The biggest travesty is how weak Blondie's pizza is. The ratio of sauce, cheese, and dough is a delicate thing in pizza. Blondie fucks it up on so many levels. I think it's a combination of the shitty/low-quality ingredients and not enough sauce and/or cheese. The dough tastes really bad and there's too much dough and not baked enough.Honestly, I do not understand how people can keep on subsidizing this shit especially when better options (Cheeseboard's, La Val's, etc.) exist.
 
AVOID

absolute drunk food.  thats the best way to describe it.  i dont know a single soul that comes here during daylight.

not the best pizza, but it'll do.... when youre drunk.  every UC has "a pizza joint"... i would say this is berkeley's....

in the whole scheme of "UC pizza joints", it cant even compete against woodstocks in UCD or UCSB.  same goes with the girls too. =P

Why does a scruffy pizza place like Blondie's seem to draw people in like flies to a light bulb?

Maybe it's the potential. Maybe it's the dodgy appearance. Yet nothing beats greasy pizza in the evening when one should be eating a decent meal and getting ready for bed. Or maybe it's the quick service which shouts, "here's your food, now go f'en eat it!". Of course projected in a way where you aren't offended but just glad you got your steamy hot paper plate of gooey pizza that burns your mouth as you close your eyes over the goodness of the carbs and the temptation to buy a whole pie.
Tastier than Fat Slice, I think they rub garlic on the crust. I like that they promote literacy and musical awareness. By posting Rolling Stone magazine clippings on the wall.

Blondie's is definitely better than Fat Slice. But that's like saying Gaddafi has a better sense of style than Kim Jong Il: Although factually correct, I'd rather be dressed by the Queen of England. In this case the Queen is the Cheeseboard.

Okay, who am I kidding? I don't need to be proper all the time, and unlike the Queen, I certainly don't go to bed at 8. So Blondie's is a great spot for a slice of pizza late at night when most everything else is closed. Also, it's almost a requirement to come here if you are a college kid, drunk, or a drunk college kid.

If other things are open, it seems more prudent to spend $5 for an entire pizza at Little Caesars or $2.50 for a slice at the Cheeseboard rather than $3.50 here. If you don't want to stray far from Telegraph Avenue, though, Blondie's is okay during the middle of the day too. Mmmm, grease!
it is a real feat to have pizza worse than Fat Slice... Cheers!

Blondies is normally a 3 or a 4 but in recent months the pizza has been tasting drier and less flavorful than usual. Always like that they have oregano and garlic powder in addition to red peppers. I will fondly remember the many nights my friends and I came here after going to the local bars.

I am disappointed in Blondies for increasing their prices. I can not believe I had to pay 3.75 for a slice of pizza that was barely larger than what I would order from Domino's. Blondies used to be the place I would go when on Telegraph or Powell Street because it was cheap and there was seating, but now I will have to look elsewhere, the pizza just isn't worth 3.75.

pepperoni pizza. mmmmm. $3.50 for a nice pizza.

Shame on them for running out of parmesean cheese on a GAME DAY. tsk tsk.

Three stars might be too charitable for a place that closes early if it runs out of pizza.  The highlight of Blondie's has to be the Joke Man, standing out front.  Here's a joke:

Joke Man stops a passing girl and says "I know where you got your shoes."

Where?

Joke Man: "Will you give me a dollar if I tell you where you got your shoes?"

Ok.

Joke Man: "You got your shoes on your feet!"

Dammit.  He didn't say Payless, so he ain't getting the dollar.

Some people have no sense of humor.

It's pretty good pizza, and it's definitely better than Pepe's down the street.
I first came here with my family on the day I moved in as a freshman, and we ordered the whole wheat vegetarian because we're all conscious eaters. We waited around 15 minutes, which I suppose is around the time it takes for a pizza, but I noticed when we got our pizza that the entire bottom was burnt. Literally charred past distinguishable flavor. We took it back to them so that they could make us a new one but they argued with us that it was how it was supposed to be. Finally they relented and baked us a new one, but their quality checking is pretty dismal.

Now, onto the actual food, the pizza actually tasted a lot better than it sounds. The vegetables tasted pretty fresh and the dough was crispy. It was also around $18 for a large 16" pizza, which seems pretty decent a price.

If you crave pizza, this will probably be the place to get it close to campus.

This place is good, but I feel it has gone a bit downhill since when I used to come here back in high school. 

The pizza here is good, and I love that they have a flavor of the day, but I also find the pizza a bit plain and bland. The crust doesn't have an appealing taste, and the slices are always covered in grease. 

Its a small place but there is a fair amount of seating. Service is okay and they also have frozen yogurt and salads which is nice. 

This place is good for students cause it's cheap and quick, but the quality is going to either clog your arteries or make your taste buds turn on you.

Gets crowded at peak times, and for good reason. Service is fast and pizza is good.  Also, they typically have someone a store or two down handing out coupons that many a passerby ignore. Pick up a coupon, get in line, enjoy.

Blondies, classic Berkeley place ....
Pizza is better than average, no where near as good as Zach's, but then again, two different types of pizza.  
Blondies is great for a quick piece of pizza when crushing thru Berkeley.

There are only a few things that can pull me away from Bongo Burger when I'm in Berkeley. Ready? Here they are: 
1. Magic Mushroom
2. Pesto Chicken

Those two daily specials are the BOMB DIGGITY. When I'm eating it, it's like there's a party in my mouth, and everyone's grindin' up on each other and shit. Bomb freakin' diggity. 

Sadly, I'm never in Berkeley on the days when a magic mushroom slice is served. It's a sad feel, indeed. ;_;

But, oh! What's that? I'm missing one star? Well, that's because their pizza can be greasy (but the pesto chicken isn't too bad) and the crust is thin. Also, their vegetarian option really could have been so much more (it's so DRY), but that's an issue beyond the control of anyone working there. 

The magic mushroom and the pesto chicken make up for those faults in spades. If you ever see those daily specials, do yourself a favor, and go in, and get a slice. It'll be like a party in your mouth, and everyone's all dancin' and grindin' up on each other and shit. Bomb freakin' diggity.

The pizza here is not bad. Its a bit too greasy and gooey for me, but maybe that is your thing. What I do love is that they make really great salads on the cheap. I think they run about 3-4 bucks and come in a heaping to go box. I highly recommend the miso dressing. Also awesome, in the summer you can buy a large wedge of watermelon for a buck. Great alternative to the other unhealthy offerings in the student budget.

Every time someone mentions Blondies I am taken back to a more humble and simpler time of the late 80's when I was a little girl, my uncle was finishing up his MBA at UC Berkeley, and we'd walk over to Blondies to get a slice of heaven for just a buck...once in a while I still get the craving for a slice of pepperoni with a sprinkling of their Italian seasoning and parmesan...yummm (I actually just had this last weekend at their SF location with a couple of friends who thanked me for introducing them to the healthy wheat crust veggie) ;)

blondie's is known for their pizza. they also sell a generic commerialized version of froyo..

froyo review only

available flavors
-
-strawberry: a little tart
-pistachio: greenish, with hint of pistachio, very sweet
-cable car chocolate
-country vanilla
-cookies & cream

pricing: (sm2.95) (m3.50) toppings .99 cents each. 3  toppings  for 1.99 fruit toppings. 17 dry toppings(cereals, nuts, grains, chocolates...).

yogurt drips:
-creamy texture, melts fast
-sweet generic  flavors.
-froyo tastes similar to yogurt park.
-generic service.

i think blondie's probably just sits there waiting for me to stumble out of a telegraph bar with an empty tummy. biggest attraction: always open! veggie slice is delish on wheat bread that's pretty sweet. nam nam nam

The cheese slice is good. the crust is crunchy just the way I like it. You'd think it'd taste gross when you see it sitting under the heat lamps, but when you take a bite, it tastes so fresh and delicious!! People watching while you eat is fun, too.
Blondie's is the shit.  Nice fluffy chewy crust.  Way better than Fat Slice & even though they are only like 100 ft apart, there's way less crackheads in front of Blondie's.

Blondies is okay. It's a pretty good value meal (especially the drinks---they're $1, but the new cashier who started work today didn't know any better and was selling them for 50 cents) and I think well-suited for their average cash-strapped collegiate customer who just needs to quell his hunger for a few hours between classes. 

The pizza comes out pretty greasy, unless you get the healthy option which is meatless and rather unappetizing looking. It tastes fine though and made for a completely adequate meal, nothing more. 

I think Fat Slice tastes better (if you compare pepperoni to pepperoni, veggie to veggie, although not much else can be compared) but Blondie's has a much better seating area. It looks cozy and clean, while Fat Slice's frequently reeks of the bathroom right behind the kitchen or an extremely odd, pungent mixture of pizza ingredients. 

Overall, this place is alright, not the best.

This place is worth it is you're short on cash and don't really care about being healthy. Although, to give them a little credit, they advertise a health vegetarian option, but it looks nasty (I apologize to its fans). I've tried fat slice, but if you get the daily special or use the coupon, it's basically the same price. I'm not a huge fan of pizza and I can't really differentiate between quality pizza and common pizza ( I like costco pizza, if that says anything) but I'd say try it at least once. But then again, if you don't, you're not really missing out on anything.

I'm not particularly picky when it comes to pizza, so don't make your decision to come here (or not) based on my review, but I think Blondie's is cool. They give huge slices and the dough isn't bad.  I love their pesto pizza.

Rather than throw out old pizza that's been sitting for hours, they lump it in with new slices and reheat it for you if you're unlucky enough to get those pizzas. They know this is a bad practice, and recently have instituted a new ticket system where a guy comes from the back and chooses your slices rather than the register man, so you can't ask him for the non-rotting pieces, and you have no expectation of being served immediately the fresh pizza sitting right up front in the window. Not only are you paying 3.44-4 bucks for an old slice, you have to wait 8 minutes for the oven to regrease it and bring it back to life rather than being served the pizza you see and is ready to be consumed immediately.

The old dude up front in glasses and the little fedora is a big time jerk, dripping with contempt for his customers. He'll linger and charm any young college girl though. Just saying.

Used to be able to get a slice and a drink for 3.50 a couple years ago, but now it's around 5 bucks if you want that. You get a small 12 oz. cup packed with ice, so maybe 5 oz. of soda. No refills.

The place is pretty dirty, considering bums wander and linger around in there. The only good thing about Blondie's is they don't let indigents out front cuss at you like in front of Fat Slice, but I think that may be because they're flanked by more respectable businesses.

Should be shut down, but a continual rotation of new college freshmen and people giving it 5 stars simply because you can get it at 12:30am after drinking ensures it wont. The artificially good reputation I see here is probably why they've raised prices so much since I was in college.
Pizza is good but $4 a slice is way overpriced.
Everyone from the bay area loves this place.  I think it isn't a step over mediocre.  Nuff said.

Awesome choice for lunch here!  We tried the veggie pizza and the meat lover's pizza.  A slice of each of course, I can't stomach 2 pizzas with Lewis in one sitting.  I think lunch was around $6-8?  Don't order a fountain drink here, it's such a ripoff, our soda was even filled up all the way.  You're better off running over the Walgreens to buy a liter of your own soda for the same price.  Will definitely come back here to try more pizzas!

Tough place to find a seat so be, be, be aggressive!

Blondie's used to be the Jam, but they have def lost some swagger. I went back to Norcal for the weekend and found myself in Berkeley looking for late night snacks. Thought I'd give Blondie's a shot. 
I can't really place exactly what was wrong with it. The slice was just a bit limp. The cheese was flavorless and the crust was like day old wonder bread. Not sure what there deal is. I guess it would've been a better decision to go down the street to the other pizza joint for a slice.

It's open late, next to campus, is a classic institution, and they make a respectable pie. If you're a student  this is one of your meccas. It's more thick crust than thin crust, and the crust was always a draw for me.  If you live in Berkeley and have a car or are willing to walk past Southside, go to Pie in the Sky, Arinell, or Gioia's instead.

Blondie's is pretty awesome. It's cheap and easy. One can always go for a slice. The slices here are not super big, even though they use slices from their largest size of pizza. They have four sizes of pizza if you order whole ones: medium, large, giant, godzilla. For everyday slices, they have cheese, pepperoni, veggie, and a  daily special. They post the daily special in front of the store and online. They're yummy, but not all pizzas were created equal so it's a hit or miss on some days. I tend to find the vegetarian specials better than the meat ones, like the bbq chicken, pesto chicken, garlic chicken, and Mexican chicken. The chicken here is simply too dry. Plus, this place is the only one beknownst to me to tout a hyphy pizza, but the combo of pineapple, jalapenos, and olives really did not do it for me. One daily special I am thankful for is the deep dish. Those aren't easy to come by.

The last time I went here was years ago.  But here's why:

It was hot outside.
I walk inside.
The guy behind the counter was wearing a tank top.
He was flipping the dough...spinning away.
The phone rang.
He folded the dough under his arm to hold it while he answered the phone.
THE PIZZA DOUGH WAS TOUCHING HIS SWEATY HAIRY ARMPIT.

I walked out.

Can you swear on Yelp?

If so, I'd like to throw out a huge "Fuck this place and the whole staff that was working the same night Dethklok played at UC Berkeley!". I've never encountered such a group of completely inept and useless lumps of flesh, or been as close to punching a restaurant supervisor or manager in the face as I was a few months ago when eating here. 

If you order a slice of pizza that they don't have made yet, and are given  a number, make sure you stand right against the counter to wait for the slice. If you make the mistake of stepping back and walk 10 feet to the rear of the restaurant, so others can order, you get the shaft. They are going to make 3 slices, call out 4 or 5 numbers, and it's first come first serve as to who gets the slices regardless of what number you have. After they give your slice away to whoever stands closest  and you complain, they will accuse you of already getting your slice, then change their mind and say you didn't come to the counter fast enough.  While you are arguing with them, another pizza will come out of the oven and they will give every slice of that one away to the other customers, while saying "I'm sorry...oh I'm sorry, it will just be a few minutes for more, uhhhh  I didn't realize you didn't get yours yet...oh sorry". Then the supervisor or manager will say "Here's what I'll do, I'll give you an extra slice". Guess what asshole, when I went up to the counter and placed the order, I thought about how hungry I was and made sure to order enough food to fill me up. Not everyone wants to be a useless fat piece of shit eating until they are sick or burst. One slice of your crappy pizza weighs a pound and has 4 trillion calories. No human needs an extra one for free.

With that said, one of my greatest regrets in life is not accepting that extra slice of pizza just to throw at that moron.

Also, does the Health Department even make an effort anymore? Don't you have to have some basic hygiene standards for employees in food service? I guess not because the workers I dealt with look like they rolled up fresh from a night spent in People's Park. I know this is Berkeley... and I don't really care what your personal grooming standards are on a day to day basis....but if you are serving food, clean yourself. In the words of DJ Assault "You need soap...and water....soap and water". Read some reviews farther down and you'll see someone mentioning how they watched an employee hold the raw pizza dough IN HIS ARMPIT WHILE WEARING A TANK TOP so he could answer the phone.

Go to Fat Slice a block down the street. The pizza is the same (crappy but cheap) and you don't have to deal with brain dead acid casualties behind the counter. You'll also avoid getting mouth AIDS from eating armpit pizza. Douchebags!

I like Fat Slice a little better, but I often went to Blondie's while an undergraduate too. It's a classic establishment that everyone should go to at least once.

+As Jennie R. has indicated, the pepperoni pizzas are out of this world. The crust is thick and soft, the sauce is noticeable but not overpowering, and there's always a generous helping of cheese.
The vegetarian pizzas are supposed to be very good too (as a big carnivore, I can't really comment on them).
All pizzas are hot the vast majority of the time (I had one or two lukewarm slices while I was a student).
+Slices are served all day, and they're very big. I often ordered two, but most people will be satisfied with just one.
+Lunch deals are going on all the time. A slice of pizza with a small soda costs about $4. A slice of pizza by itself costs about $3 (some slices are as cheap as $2.25).
+There are a lot of concert posters on the walls and other vintage decor to look at.
+There's usually great rock music playing inside.
+Fast service. Even if there's a line (this is usually the case), you're not going to be waiting more than a few minutes. The employees really try to move people along.
+Good hours. Blondie's is often open until 9 or 10 p.m.
+Great location. Blondie's is right in the heart of Telegraph Avenue, and there are a lot of great stores around (of course, there are other places to eat too). You can also buy something from one of the street vendors (I ignored them when I was a student, partly because I never had much money on me).

-Berkeley employees tend to be competent, but not very friendly (in general, employees working in a place as busy as Blondie's are going to be more concerned with working quickly than with smiling at every customer who walks in).
-Maybe things have changed, but I always found the pizzas I had delivered to be better than the ones I ate inside (this is definitely a minus because only people living in the area can have pizza delivered). This is the case with some other pizza places too (ex: The New Yorker Pizza in Union City). It might have something to do with slices being rushed out (the pizzas probably aren't as carefully made as the ones being delivered).
-This location is a hole in the wall. There are a few tables inside, and you can eat standing up facing the left or right wall (there are also some spots facing the back). That's it.
In contrast, the Blondie's in San Francisco is situated in a two-story building, and there's a lot of room to eat downstairs (the area by the counter is fairly small). You can sit at a table and everything.
-It tends to be dirty inside.
-It's worse outside of Fat Slice, but don't be surprised if a homeless person or two asks you for change while you're entering or leaving.
-This isn't an issue with me, but the large pizza slices are somewhat greasy (if you order a whole pizza, the slices should be less greasy).
-While inside, it's hard to put pepper, parmesan cheese, or anything else on your pizza (the shakers are big, but there are only a few of them, and sometimes you have to reach over someone to grab one- they're tied to the counters by string).
-Customers won't really care if they get in your way or jostle you a little while you're eating. It's especially busy here in the early afternoon.
-Telegraph Avenue isn't the safest place to be at night (in an attempted mugging, someone I know was beat up by a bunch of thugs when he refused to give them his wallet). If you decide to stop by late, it's wise to have someone go with you.

A lot of people love, or at least like, Blondie's. The pizza isn't for everyone, but I definitely recommend giving it a try if you haven't already.

I'm at Blondie's.  It's late one night.  My friend is working behind the counter, and she just gives me a slice of pepperoni pizza.  I'm not very hungry, though, and all of a sudden, I get all humanitarian.

As we're walking out of the restaurant, there is a Berkeley transient sitting in front of the trashcan.  I offer him the slice of pizza.

His response?  With a disgusted look on his face, "No thanks, I'm vegetarian."

Evidently, in famously liberal Berkeley, California, beggars CAN be choosers.

Berkeley and Blondie's go together like Berkeley and tree sitters. You can't have one without the other. It's also a love/hate relationship. Both get the press and the emotions run high because like tree sitters, you either love or hate Blondie's. No middle ground here.

The line is long. The help is fast. The slices are large and the homeless are many. But in spite of the dangers, I luv my pizza so this is a big time stop whenever I can find a parking spot for my car. That's the issue, parking.

So whenever you are in Berkeley and find a place to park your vehicle, stop by Blondie's. It isn't THE BEST pizza in the world but it's not the worst either. Just stomach filling, hunger-killing greasy drip-down-your-arm grub to soothe your hunger jag.

Then walk away over to TopDog and do the hot link. Not many can double up on hard gastric goodness or badness depending on your culinary point-of-view.

Blondie's is seriously the best pizza you're going to get on the West Coast...ok, maybe Haystacks in Noe Valley is comparable. I mean, it's no East Coast pizza, but it's good.

It's loud, it's crowded, it's dirty, it's near impossible to find a table but the pizza is good.

This last time I got the veggie on whole wheat and it was excellent. 

Oh, and surprisingly, the people who work there are nicer and more polite than you would expect.
I love Blondie's, Cal doesn't. But I always get my way. Cheap and greasy pizza slices are the best!

The age old question: Blondies or Fat Slice?

Um, Blondies.  Definitely Blondies.  4 stars for awesomely delicious pizza (unless you get the pepperoni, which is too greasy for this mama.)

We are missing one star because sometimes I have to wait for seating which is mildly irritating.

GREAT PIZZA. Simply orgasmic. I'm not sure WHAT they put in their pizzas, but simply their pepperoni pizzas taste amazing. Usually they are pretty large slices, but honestly, this was the place to go whenever I had a pizza craving.

Every single time I went to Blondie's for a late night meal, their pizzas were always fresh and still hot. As with any place in Berkeley, at night, however, sometimes it was a little scary walking down there. I will say the inside isn't the cleanest and the seating isn't very comfy, but togo your pizza!!!!!

Updated preface/background: I used to eat more than average in terms of quantity (I've eaten 2 Chipotle Burritos in one sitting) but now I am more focused on quality and am always looking for a great deal (read: value).  And my ratings don't really take service into account, although if it is a terrible experience, I'll make that known.

Came in around 6pm, and ordered a cheese pizza, since I knew I didn't want too much since I knew I was going to eat dinner in a few hours (I know, late dinner).  The pizza was floppy and soft, and kind of reminded me of elementary school, rectangle pizza.  At the time in elementary school, I absolutely loved that pizza.  But I also didn't know better.  Blondie's pizza is kind of like that.  And I'm no pizza snob, but I do appreciate a good slice.

The ambiance/decor, though is very very unique, and definitely has that skater/retro type of feel to it.  Again, just to see the place, I would come here to simply check the place out, but not necessarily order food from here.  It was filled with what seemed to be hipster and skater high school students, and a few hipster adults in there too (not sure what category I was under, probably the tourist category).

I came here because I was in Berkeley, and saw this spot off of Telegraph.  But all in all, I wouldn't come back, but the sign lured me in, because it looked so...fun.

I've been coming here since I was 16, had a license and could drive from Napa to get slices of pizza late night when the craving called.  

I came here after prom OOHHHH so many years ago - for yup - you guessed it Pizza.  (I had a choice between sex and pizza and I chose Pizza.. it's THAT good)

The plain cheese or the pepperoni are my two favs, can't go wrong with either of them.  I will sometimes try a different slice, but really, if i'm driving well over an hour to get a SLICE of pizza - I tend to go with my habituals.

As an adult - I tend to head down here now, in daytime so I can hit the record stores, and urban shops and bum around rather than just come for a slice - but if you live locally, nothing is finer than late night pizza here.
One of my favorite pizza places in Berkeley! Always great tasting, especially the crust and if you can get the coupons for $3.50 drink and pizza its even better!

One of our hippy friends ordered a slice of Pepperoni pizza here, dropped it on the floor (cheese side DOWN) then proceeded to pick it back up and eat it, stating, "God made dirt, dirt doesn't hurt."

Staring in disbelief, I was too speechless to mention that God made hepatitis too.

Despite this traumatic visual, Blondie's has been a staple to my pizza-by-the-slice eating experience for the past 10 years. It's basic, large and hot. 

And it's better than nearby Fat Slice, no matter if it's really the same chain, or contain the same, disgusting floor.

I was a lost high schooler in Berkeley for Doctor Camp one summer -
[ yes, I said doctor camp!! ]
- and I came across Blondie's Pizza as I was rushing towards Wheeler Hall for a lecture.

I was practically late, but hey, good food was calling to me. Who am I to ignore it? :]

Blondie's was nothing short of amazing. I walked in and marveled at the menu and the pizzas. The slices looked ginormous and the pepperonis were just glistening under the warm lights. I got a simple slice of pepperoni pizza.
....best frickin' decision of my life!! it was sooo good!!!
I've been hooked for years now. Every time I'm in the Bay area, I make an effort to visit Blondie's :]

Tip: bring cash and change for quick payment. Then skip outside to enjoy your foodage. Cheeeeers!!

As a long time patron of Blondie's Pizza, I will say this: wont stop on Telegraph without grabbing a quick slice. There's nothing like it and they've got decent prices. Only thing I can say is: Please think about closing the window in the winter; maybe sweep near the cheese, pepper, etc shake area on that one wall. Thanks for still being there, Blondies. Miss your Pleasant Hill Location.

Some people are trippin'. Blondie's is simple, streamlined, delicious pizza. I'm all about cheese, and these pizzas do not lack in that department. I've never had Fat Slice, but the BF has, and he says Blondie's wins. I take his word for it, especially since he's an Oakland native and has been having both since he was a young lad (Cybelle's too, to which he says Blondie's still wins).
Get a slice from Blondie's and then stop over for dessert at CREAM. Now, that sounds like the most perfect diet breaker of all time.
BEEF  Pepperoni !!!! Its The Best =] This is a Great Place to come grab a Very Quicky and Yummy Bite to Eat!!
A Berkeley classic, cheap pizza in a convenient location on Telegraph.  Blondie's can get a bit busy during the school year around lunch time, but other than that is a good little pizza place to try.

So when I lived in San Francisco one of my favorite places to go on the weekends was to Berkley across the bay. I would spend my days going to the great record stores and book stores and my favorite place to eat was at Blondies Pizza. They have the biggest and best slices of pizza at a great price. The pizza was greasy and cheesy and always went home happy. If your in the bay area you have to go to blondies!

My husband is a Berkeley grad and always insists we eat here whenever we are visiting the campus. (Insists like I resist- yeah right, I plan trips to Berekely just to eat at Blondies)

Very cheap prices
Very good pizza
Very interesting newspaper articles hanging up on the walls.
Very busy- avoid peep times or you'll be standing up eating your lunch.

A must try if you are in the area!!

This is where I'd eat when I was a poor undergrad and needed a quick, cheap bite. It was either this or a donut from kingpin...needless to say, I love blondie's. It's open late night too, which can be really convenient. Some people say fat slice is better - they are wrong, it is just greasier and limper. Blondie's serves up a nice, old fashioned slice and it is big, cheap and delicious. This isn't gourmet, this is BLONDIE'S!

And in addition, this place is definitely old school. My dad has been taking me here since I was a wee one, when he'd walk me around campus and tell me "look, this is where you're going to go!" (he was right). We'd buy our Blondie's pizza and eat on campus watching the college kids go by (it was weird seeing little kids doing the same with their parents when I was a student here). The crap they have hung up inside blondie's used to disturb me as a kid. And they still do.

Adding to life's great debates like blonde vs. brunette, every Berkeley freshman is forced to pick:  Fat Slice vs. Blondie's. 

I happen to think they are very similar with a slight edge to Blondie's for being 25 cents cheaper.

I am a huge fan of their pepperoni pizza. It's on the greasy side, but if you were concerned about health you would probably be at intermezzo having a salad rather than stuffing your face with pizza.

I understand why so many claim to "love" getting the massive slices at Blondie's.  It's located on a popular street, Telegraph, and its open really late.  And ofcourse the slices are HUGE.
With that being said, while you do get alot of food for what you pay for, the quality is lacking.  I like my slices juicy and rich, and while not the worst slices I've had, Blondie's taste more like cardboard.  I don't know if the ingredients are fresh or not, but I'd have a hard time believing they are if that is the case.
I would give Blondie's 3 stars instead of 2 if it wasn't for the fact that everybody overhypes this place so much and gives it undeserved praise, in terms of taste atleast.  Their slices do not taste great, they remind me more of Cybelle's bland slices.  If you want richer and juicier slices, try Pizza My Heart in Emeryville.  For higher quality "gourmet" pizza, nothing beats LoCoco's on Piedmont Ave.
Wow....I should probably lay off the pizza.

Kind of disappointed. Got the Six Cheese pizza (daily special). The crust was a bit dry (main reason why I dislike pizza). The good thing is a guy is passing out coupons for $3.50 a slice of pizza and a small soda. Maybe if I'm in the mood for pizza again, I'll stop by.

Blondie's has good cheap pizza, but it's less doughy than Fat Slice but tends to have more toppings. Blondie's has all your standard toppings, but it also tends to have alot of eclectic special days such as asparagus chicken, sweet and sour chicken, or Mexican chicken. Super healthy crowd can enjoy Blondie's too because they have a whole-wheat vegetarian pizza.

One day they had HYPHY PIZZA. The description was "Jalapenos, pepperoni, olives, and pineapple. Go dumb!" Ordering a slice of hyphy was pretty awesome, but the pizza definitely made me make a thizz face.

I don't really recommend sitting in there because it feels really sticky or greasy anywhere you touch. Best to get it to go.

There's a line at lunch but it moves pretty fast. The daily special for pizza and drink for $3 is a steal.

one of  my fave cheap eats.
huge portion +garlic fries also the daily lunch specials are a good deal too. I frequent this place when I'm feeling poor and hungry.. then I walk down the street and grab a hot dog from Top Dog.. my other fave cheap eats place.

THE BEST SLICE OF PEPPERONI PIZZA I HAVE EVER EATEN

Why?
1. Sauce with so much garlic that loved ones will flee from your presence in disgust.
2. Spicy pepperoni that will convert any vegan.
3. Thick, soft crust.

Rules:
1. Order by the slice. (A cut from the Godzilla just tastes better)
2. Order pepperoni. (Don't get fancy)
3. Add Parmesan cheese liberally to soak up the grease. (Don't you dare dab with a napkin!)
4. Get a Coke.

I love this pizza, I discovered this place the summer I was staying at the I-House for a NSF Summer Class over at Cal, got to meet some Nobel Laureates, to boot!

I have never been to New York!  But, I love this pizza sans the grease, just pat off with the napkin provided!  Specials are a slice with a drink for cheap!  Can't get better than that!

Always when I am up in Berkeley, I stop off here and get my slice!  I love the thin crust, with the crust firm enough to hold it to your mouth.  Truth, be told, I can't stand the places that have crusts that are flimsy!

This place is an institution.  I think the thick pizza place up the street and around the corner downstairs, La Val's, is long gone!  There was some serious action going on over there!  I went by one year and the subterranean location was empty.  But, I digress...

Cheap, Greasy pizza, plenty of toppings, with a firm backbone, that keeps you coming back for more!  Real Comfort food for the masses.  Wherever, you are, it beckons you back, back to the abyss!  There is really NO parking on this street unless, you want to double park and get a ticket.  There are parking meters around the corner.  But, that depends on your luck!

Been going here for about 20 years... somethings never change... good pizza, cheap price, no seating... AND DIRTY AS HELL!

Went here with my son for the 1st time in about 13 years... he loved it BUT I think I've out grown Blondies

Pepperoni Pizza
*wipe off grease*. *wipe off more grease*.  *and wipe again*.

+ Parmesan cheese
+ red peppers

BLISS. 

buy another slice. :)

I am a fan the sauce -- it seems that no matter where I go for pizza they always have this lame sauce thats sweet, becuase it came stright out of a can and on to the pizza dough. Im a fan of the 2-hour simmered sauce with all the spices and blondies -- weather or not its simmered for 2 hours, taste that way. Its tangy the crust is PERFECT not too thick not to thin.

I ususally get the cheeese or pepperoni. its glorious.

When I was in high school we'd drive 45+ minutes into Berkeley for a slice of Blondie's with the emphasis on hanging out on Telegraph.  Either the pizza was really good...or there was NOTHING going on in the town I grew up in.  I think we all know which was the case.  

Had a slice of veggie after tonight's Cal game.  Meh.  It's like boring crap food you feed your picky kids but don't want to eat yourself.

ahhhhhhhh... it smells so good when you pass it on your way to class but it really isn't that good. it's good food if you are inebriated but c'mon who is picky whilst under the influence? 

I'd have to say the only pizza that I like here is the healthy veggie one with wheat crust. all others are weird or a little greasy (for the ones with meat). also, no refills :( 

don't expect too much from this lil joint.
i get confused when people tell me that they're craving a slice of blondie's.

Blondie's Pizza will change your life. The ooey gooey cheese pizza and thick soft crust outshines all other pizzerias in the area. The lines at Blondie's can get long, but for good reason: the Berkeley staple serves its pizza hot, fresh and quick. Four different types of pizza are usually available by the slice: cheese, pepperoni, vegetarian and a daily special such as tomato alfredo or Hawaiian. Blondie's also makes fresh pies to order and is open late. A slice of pepperoni and a soda goes for about four bucks. 

Be on the lookout for employees on the west side of Telegraph handing out coupons for a pizza and a soda for $2.50. Blondie's is usually the last restaurant on Telegraph to close, perfect for everyone who craves a slice after a long night of partying.

Okay I need to add a star because I end up going here so often that it must be better than I think it is.  The only slice worth getting though is the pepperoni.  Maybe it's just that pepperoni itself is really good...

Simple, cheap, and amazing pizzas. What else can you ask for? 

I know this place is highly overrated, I don't think I've ever not heard anyone say "Let's go to Blondies" while being in Berkeley. If your ever in the neighborhood, give it a shot!
I feel like the service wasn't that great. The workers had somewhat of a sarcastic tone of voice. The pizza wasn't anything special either.

This place holds a very dear spot in my heart because this was "The Spot" for me and my friends in High School and College.  Is this the world's best pizza?  No but it is good.  Personally I like the flavor of the sauce, cheese and crust.  It is a bit greasy but if it is bothersome just dab it with a napkin to save yourself the guilt.  

My personal slices of choice are a pepperoni slice and a cheese slice. Sometimes I prefer the bigger slices of Fat Slice, but as far as taste goes I prefer Blondie's of the two.  

The location obviously is a nice spot near all the bars and clubs on Telegraph so it is nice to head there if your fiendin for some food after a night of dancing, drinking, listening to bands, or all of the above.  

Memories, water colored memories, of the way we were.  Good times.
The anti-Zachary's. Good cheese, tasty sauce, just the right degree of greasiness. And, most importantly, zero pretension. And in Berkeley, that's saying a lot...

#808

Walk up.
Place your order and pay.

Pick up your slice of pizza. Remember to bring a sponge to soak up all the grease and lard on top.
Eat your pizza and drink your coke.
Don't forget to have you cardiologist on call so you can schedule your coronary bypass.

I'm sorry Blondie's, after years of business after getting food poisoning at Fat Slice I'm going to take my business back to the place that got me sick, why?  Your crust is bland and dry and the toppings are good enough to offset it.

I'm sorry, but back to Fat Slice I go.

5 stars if pizza is fresh from the oven
4 stars if pizza has been sitting there

I think I'll just order a small cheese pizza just so I can have my eyes roll to the back of my head experience and take the rest home.  Blondies is the only pizza that I will willingly eat the crush.  The dough is great!  If you order the pepperoni, beware of the greasiness...you will not need lip balm for the rest of the day!

I don't know if I only love this place because I go when drunk and all food tastes good, or if Blondie's is just as amazing during the day but...their slices are great. then again, i drop most of my slices on the floor walking home before i get to eat em--being drunk and everything.

They always have the pepperoni at night--classic. Vegetarian (also late night) is surprisingly good, but as a carnivore, it doesnt really quite hit the spot. i like it when they switch it up with the selection. @ 1 am, besides getting laid, the only thing better is hitting up blondie's and seeing they're offering the chorizo sausage pizza w/ jalapenos. i'm good. 

and $4 a slice? like i said, when you're drunk, not an issue. so i should probably also check it out when i'm sober though...

Some of the BEST pizza I've ever had. I used to love coming here when
I lived in the Bay area. The slices were huge and totally yummy.
I miss it!!

Closes at 10pm.

The location is quite convenient. Right on telegraph and near campus.  Affordable prices.

and WOW, they have so many choices for pizzas now since the time I attended college here.  They aren't available like the last 1 hour of the day though.  They always have your basics available at the front: cheese, pepperoni, combo, or chicken!

I noticed they have frozen yogurt here also on their menu.. which is strange..

Plenty of chairs and tables inside.  Not the cleanest place but a good pit stop along your way home to your apt/dorm.  Counters are located on both sides with extra toppings for your pizza.

but MAN....... you use ALOT OF GREASE in your pizzza. I always end up dabbing the top of my pizza with ten million napkins!!!!!!

Ohhh my, I haven't been here in SUCH a long time... but tonight, my friends and I decided to hit up Gypsy's Trattoria... a hop, skip, and a jump from the coveted Blondie's.  I decided that I HAD to go there, even if I had to call the slice of pepperoni pizza an "appetizer" to the dinner I was going to have at Gypsy's.

Oh what an appetizer it was!  It was the most beautiful thing.  Every bite rocked me sideways, forcing me to clutch my overly satisfied tummy as I closed my eyes, moaning in ecstasy, devouring this triangular piece heaven, mouthful by mouthful.  

The service was fast, and the pizza was fresh out of the oven and mine for the taking!  

Oh Blondie's, how I've missed you.  5 Stars for bringing me back.

Blondie's is a Telegraph staple and pretty good pizza, just not my favorite.  A bit saucier than Fat Slice (and sometimes smaller), and not quite as flavorful as La Val's or Arinell's.  They do have options ready to go, though, with the daily special.

If you're visiting Berkeley or SF - you gotta try Blondie's.  It's a tourist thing - you just have to do it at least once.  And if you're a Cal student, I believe they take Cal 1 Debit, so that's pretty convenient.

Overall, Blondie's is not my go-to, but it's a nice option to have in the neighborhood.  They're also open late, so plus points.

I'm being generous with three stars.

Blondie's is a fixture on Telegraph right outside UC Berkeley's Sather Gate.  I try to go there as rarely as possible, both because Telegraph is pretty disgusting when you get over your nostalgia about the birth of the Free Speech movement being very close by and because it's just not a pleasant place to eat.

Oh yeah, the pizza.  It's good.  Well, it's greasy.  It's the way pizza-by-the-slice is supposed to be.  The service is good in terms of getting you what you want promptly, but the people who work there aren't friendly.  I wouldn't be either if I worked there.

Their prices are OK.  I'm going to end this review now because I really want to knock it down to two stars.

One of my old faves from my Cal days.  Blondie's was the pizza place.  Forget Fat Slice, forget La Vals, forget the chains.  The only thing that came close was Zachary's but this was all about location.  The place is pretty dirty in true Berkeley fashion.  Seriously, you go here to order a slice, fold it up and eat it while walking.

The place is just a big square.  Easy to walk in and walk out which facilitated the sometimes long lines it had.  But like I said, it was less than a block from main campus, so they reaped the rewards.

If I really had to think about it, the pizza is more like a 3.  It's not HUGE or easily foldable like good old NY style pizza.  It's a bit oily but that's from cheese glorious cheese,and there isn't a ton of selection.  From what I remember, there's a pizza of the day and three other choices (cheese, veggie, pepperoni).

If you're a Cal alum, you must be looking back on this place with fond memories.  If you're a visitor, you just have to go.  That's why it's a 4.

When I was pregnant with my first two, I used to make my husband drive out to get me a pizza from Blondie's.  The pizza there is really good but you have to kind of chance it out because you might end up getting a slice that's been sitting out for awhile.  You can ask to have it reheated though but of course the fresh, hot ones are even better.  I've had the one in SF before but I think I like the one in Berkeley better.  Parking in Berkeley, of course, always sucks but I eat there now only when my family and I want to take a stroll.

I use to live above this joint when I first moved to Berkeley. People always raved about it. I never saw why. 

Perhaps it helped to be a super poor student [which I was] & getting their food seemed like a deal. That's why they get 2 stars. One more because they made the hallways always smell better.

But, meh. 

I prefer Fat Slice down the street.

Used to be better back in the days, now its just a huge slice of greasiness.  Wouldn't eat here as much now but for the price for that huge slice of pizza is a good deal.  

causes your pipes to run brown water if you know what I mean, eh eh eh????!111!11

Oh how the mighty have fallen. The Blondie's of my teen years was always worth the drive.
