Biting into a thick cheesy bite of pepperoni pizza is one of the main things I remember about hanging in Berkeley, yet it seems Blondie's has decided that "thick pepperoni slice" (from the sign above the registers) actually means "thin floppy pepperoni slice". Additionally, the cashier charged us 6 cents extra for the combo due to keystroke laziness on his register and just made excuses when I pointed it out. When I went to get a refill on my pathetically small drink I was told I had to pay an additional 50 cents. Are you kidding me? Fuck this place, never coming back.
I love this place . I been eating  here for many many moons. GReat Slices. Funny staff quick service. Place for young or young at heart. Good for breakfast of late snack

A few words come to mind when I think of Blondie's: 

-overpriced
-overloaded
-ironic
-unoriginal

Every day they have a new signature slice, but they come so loaded with toppings that one must ask themselves, if the slice is really that original.  I had a pesto slice that tasted like peppers and not pine nuts.  I also had a pepperoni slice that was greasily adequate.  For less money, I can get better ingredients at Cheeseboard or even a better take on the greasy pepperoni at Fat Slice.

This is a great place to go to if you're too cool to go without smoking for the ten minutes it takes your friends to eat.  Simply lean in the wide, open windows, cigarette and all, and have a great time!  The staff doesn't seem to care, and the people who turn and glare at you just haven't reached the level of coolness you've achieved.

Long story short, if you have asthma or like clean air, this probably isn't the place for you.  

They do have great pizza, though.  I think it's decent.  They always have cheese, pepperoni, and two other options.  Sometimes they have a great six-cheese pizza, but I always seem to miss that.  

I wouldn't call their pizza fresh.  You either get it when it's not really warm, or pretty warm with too-crunchy crust.  

Being one of the only places open so late seems to improve how I think it tastes, but it sustained me while I lived in Unit 3, ages and ages ago.  

It's not excellent, but I'll be back again and again.  Parking (street) isn't too bad after 10pm, either.  


Friendly tip:  Be careful when sprinkling garlic or oregano on your pizza.  The holes are really wide, and you'll find your pizza covered with the stuff.

Locals: "Oh, Blondie's is so lame. That's where we went when I was a freshman (in high school or at Cal.) This is other pizza place is SOOO much better. I'm so much older now and have such better taste, Blondie's is SOOO beneath me."
Me: "Blondie's serves it's purpose perfectly - It provides cheap, deliciously greasy slices. It's not intended to be a contender for best gourmet pizza in the world, it's intended to be a quick, tasty belly filler... and that's exactly what it is."

Oh to be young again.... Enjoying the bliss of $3 for a slice and a soda.  HEAVEN!

Then the crule reality of adulthood, calorie counting and (real) pizza kicked in.

In retrospect what I really liked was being away from my parents in Berkeley when I was 16. The pizza is on what amounts to a thick slice of bread.  The sauce? Well, I guess that was tomato sauce, no flavor.  Cheese?  Does anyone remember that round table comercial from the 80s when the cheese-from-a-can bounced all over the place? 

Toppings? I can't even go there.

The 2nd star is for nostalgia.

One of the things I love about the Bay Area is we have so many different food experiences that can be called pizza. You have the authentic thin crispy crust of Pizzaiola, the stuffed yummy goodness of Zachary's and the spicy, cheesey goodness of Sicilian pizza at LoCoCo's. Then there is Blondie's, the only place that ever ever makes me miss pepperoni. I think that's because it takes me back to the good ole teen years as a novice drinker needing fatty carbs to absorb all that cheap beer I managed to get my hands on. Whatever the reason, I still every once in awhile want the junk food extravaganza that is Blondie's. Even better, it is still cheap, fast and easy - who doesn't like that on a late Sat night?

For me, the Berkeley Blondie's is the only real Blondie's. Dirtylooking staff, gobs of cheese, and spicy pepperoni. Pepperoni slice and a Cherry Coke at 1:00 in the morning. That's where its at. I have been eating here for twenty-three years now, haven't gotten sick yet.

If youre looking for good pizza, Blondies is not the place. Its two star food in a three star location. The pizza is edible and at least used to be fairly cheap, but thats about it. The things that earn it the third star in my book are its late night hours, and excellent people-watching opportunities.

Blondie's is a straight up Bay Area classic. 3 words that incite an instant Blondie's craving....ALL BEEF PEPPERONI. This may not seem like a big deal but if you don't dine on swine or put pork on your fork it is. Try finding a pizza place that serves all beef pepperoni and you'll see what I'm talking about. Actually all the slices are pretty crackin no matter what you get. The slices are big and the crust is perfect, not thin crust but mos def not a deep dish. A big slice of pepperoni and nice cold root beer for $4, what's not to like?

Maybe I'm a bad person, but I think Fat Slice and Blondies is about the same taste, fairly greesy and cheesy, but delicious and open late. Blondies has a little more spices, Fat Slice tends to have more doughiness and less sauce. But in the Venn Diagram of pizza which includes Zachary's and Arinell's, B and FS are in the same set.

yes, another late night food stop.  when i was a child i marvelled at the huge pizza slices that my big sis would bring home for me on occasion.  such a treat.  the prices are freaking right on!!

here is my story.  one afternoon, while admiring all the hippy dippy art, i noticed an all seeing cockroach looking down upon us all, antenae slowly rotating independently in contemplation of his reincarnation into this berkeley institution, (which i am sure has been nothing but fulfilling for him.)
did i eat a piece of his family while biting into my slice? maybe.  it was good.

A step above Fat slice. Still kinda of pricey. Slice and soda will run close to 4.75 The funniest thing I saw here was the condiment jars were tied with a string to the wall. Hmm I guess its a high theft item, or they fall to the ground and break!

The pizza is super greasy, but quite inexpensive.  I've grabbed a quick slice here while visiting the Cal campus on several occasions including this afternoon.  Take your pizza to go because the counters and tables (rarely available) are usually pretty filthy.  With the amount of foot traffic here it seems they've just given up on cleaning after patrons during daytime hours.  It's probably a lot cooler to stand outside and people-watch on Telegraph Avenue anyways.  I'd give them a solid 2.5 stars.

I used to get a quick slice to-go for lunch sometimes if I was ever in the area and had to dash off somewhere else. The pizza isn't bad at all and this place certainly deserves more than 1 star, people! Harsh!

Good price for a big slice.

After craving some top dog after the college football season opener and then being disappointed by the ridiculously long line in front of this Cal institution, we dropped by Blondie's for a bit of nostalgic college grub.  The line was luckily not as long and moved much faster since the slices were grab and go.  Not as good as I remember in college but still good for what it is: large slice of pizza that will fill the tummy.
Where else are you going to get a slice of Vegi. Pizza on a whole wheat crust at 2 AM? No where.

Make Pizza Not War. Indeed. One of the first good by the slice pizza places I experienced when I started going to college. Like that of Fat Slice across the way, it's a great big slice of greasy goodness, especially if there's pepperoni oil flowing all over the plate. Bigger and more eclectic, though I discovered this place first I think their in a dead heat with Fat Slice and I like them both equally. Sorry, just not willing to take sides and this is strictly a mood thing. Or crowded thing.

I've done the taste test and now I can safely say that if you are on Telegraph Avenue, craving pizza, but unable to choose between Blondies and Fat Slice....Go for Blondies.  Hands down.

I always choose Blondies, but I was never quite sure why till the other night when we got a slice of pepperoni pizza at each location.  The pizza from Fat Slice lost points early on because the pepperoni topping was so sparce...I could literally count on one hand all the pepperoni pieces on the slice.  The Blondies slice on the other hand was covered with crisp juicy slices of pepperoni...

Fat Slice does live up to its name, the slices are extremely thick and doughy and also covered with a thick coating of cheese and a very light layer of sauce.  Unfortunately the extra cheese didn't turn out to be a good thing....it was so thick that it overwhelmed the pizza and became tough as the pizza cooled down.

All in all Blondies is a much better choice for any pizza craving.  It's not going to be the best pizza you'll ever have but it's a pretty solid choice for by-the-slice pizza eating.  The crust is thick and crisp, the toppings are abundant and the cheese is greasy and gooey as it should be.  

Don't trust me though, do the taste test yourself...

I've always had Blondie's be my default pizza place since I came to Cal. Its right by campus, its cheap and its quick. It takes Cal-1 card debit too, which is awesome, cause I always charge $50 a month to my CARS account so I can get "free" food.

Before I discovered the varied wonders of Berkeley pizza places I thought Blondie's was the best. I've discovered better, but its still really good. Their slice special changes everyday and they even have a calendar where you can see what slice will be featured so you can go back for your favorite (I love the hyphy slice-jalapenos, pineapple etc!-!). 

The crust is thick, but light. The sauce is zesty. The cheese isn't amazing, but its not gloopy and gross like most cheap pizza. They charge fifty-cents for each soda refill which is a bummer, since I drink diet coke like its the last cup on earth, but whatever. They have HUGE salads with really good dressings and they're quite filling.

I came here yesterday though for a whole new experience. They now serve FROZEN YOGURT!!!!!!!!!!!! This is some delicious-ass fro-yo, yo. It's creamy so its kind of like a milkshake. They have even better toppings than (dare I say it? yes.) Yogurt Park, especially since you can get mochi in your fro yo!. OMG. Blondie's is about to blow up son!!!!!!!!!

Everytime I come here, I'm starving. All I know is that I'm hungry and that the food here is affordable, tasty and I money enough in my pocket to survive afterwards! Ahh love this place but beware! There's never even close to enough seats for everyone :)

ahhh berkeley memories. being raised in the bay, this is a standard. sitting along the wall where the latest rolling stone is posted with a gigantic slice in front of you is just a perfect pizza lunch.  

what really brings the charm to blondies isnt the actual pizza (standard. simply standard. little greasy.), but the daily specials.  

two words, my yelp-amigos:

HYPHY PIZZA.

how bay can you be? um, you scrape out to b-town and pick up some hyphy pizza. iit comes out about twice a month (there's a calender on the door so you can plan accordingly).  ts not actually that good, kind of a fustercluck of toppings, but the simple fact that there IS a hyphy pizza in exsistance is probably the greatest thing ever. i have a 510 tattoo, and i feel it. 

hyphy pizza? ahhh i'm so totally always there.

Inexpenisive Pizza by the Slice.

You cant complain.


Vegitarian Pizza is the Bomb!!!!

Came here once on a business trip. It looks like it's been around forever, and seems to be a college staple. Seating was pretty limited and I ended up at the counter, but there are lots of posters, articles, etc. to look at. Definitely an eclectic place. 

The pizza was okay. I have a hard time finding a "bad" pizza, but this was quite a bit of bread and nothing really outstanding about it. If you're drunk and it's late at night, or you want something quick and cheap, come here, otherwise, go a little further to Zachary's! But Blondie's seems to be exactly what college students go for, especially at 2AM, and I'm sure that's why it does well.

Truth be told, what brought us here was the fact that they were the only place we could find on Telegraph that was open. 

I'm not a fan of the super-cheesy, super-greasy pizza so I got a slice of the whole wheat vegetarian pizza. It was really light on the cheese, had loads of veggies and a crisp whole wheat crust. I loved it! 

But let it be known that this probably wouldn't be the option that someone who's really into pizza would choose. That said, it's always nice not feeling disgusting after having some pizza. :)

The bolted down parmesan and red pepper flakes added to the college-town atmosphere of the place. Hehe.

3.5 Stars...(that extra edge to the 4 is for the Beef Pepperoni)

This pizza is good after a night of drunken debauchery. The dough is pillowy and the fact that they have beef pepperoni is Right ON!  The amount of cheese is good (although MORE cheese on ANYTHING makes it better!) and the sauce is cool.  I also like that they have some harder to find Snapple flavors rather than your basic tea, lemonade, and strawberry kiwi.  They also have tall can Arizona's (Grapeade is the Grape-e-est!) Stays open late..and even later on weekends.  The people there are always great! (maybe they just love me...cause I show them love back!! You know me...all SPRaU!)

Go get a slice...I recommend! ;)
Best Blondie's by far! Always delicious slices for the prices :D GO HERE! DO IT!
Delicious reliable pizza. Never cold. Never too greasy. Always a great price.

Ten tips:

1.
The pepperoni slice is the best thing here. Wait for a fresh pie if you see the dredges of an old one before you. If you don't have time, don't accept the small, shitty endpiece...walk a couple blocks down to Fat Slice and get a veggie, telling you it's better for your health.

2.
Do something good for humanity and be fast with your order. It's a slice and maybe a soda, for god's sake. You have no excuse if you space out or are slow about that, and someone behind you (me) might just kick your ass.

3.
If you won't be fast for someone else, do it for yourself - bring exact change so you can get to your pizza faster without fumbling around with a bunch of coins and shit. 

4.
Don't be afraid to point out exactly which piece you want. They are used to it, and this is something all real pizza lovers should do.

5.
Unscrew the cheese shakers and go crazy; the holes in the top are always blocked up. Stay in control: it's all in the wrist. As Trevor B. below says, enjoy the show as the cheese takes care of the grease. If you're a dabber, GTFO.

6.
For some reason, the pepper flakes here can be hotter than hell, and can ruin a slice if you aren't careful. So watch yourself. BTW, this is coming from a Korean so you know I'm not f'ing around.

7.
Drink water. It's still free, and you'll feel a lot better. Plus, it keeps the palate clean for the pizza itself.

8.
Score window seats, or enjoy being bumped in the back constantly by the traffic indoors.

9. 
The napkins are in weird dispensers on the walls. You'd think this is obvious, but it might not be.

10.
If it's closing time and they say they can't serve you, it means they're going to throw the fresh leftovers away and let some bum get it while you stare the derelicts' ungrateful, stoned faces down with pure and futile jealous rage. So when the servers deny you and walk to the back to clean things up, hoist yourself onto the glass counter. Just do it. Their walking away is a tacit enablement of what you are about to do. They're going to throw it out anyway, so it's not technically stealing since it is now trash, valued at $0.00. And what's the worst they'd do if they saw you running out like a fat version of Prefontaine with an ankle injury? They're just trying to get out of there. GET IT, or your stummy will ache the morning after.

I don't think I'll ever go here after a Cal game again. Ever.

I got more funky asshole looks from uptight drunk students than I've ever gotten. Even when I was a pregnant teen in the conservative Midwest.

This is effing Berkeley assholes! I can walk into a pizza joint dressed however I like. (and yes, I was completely dressed) and order what I want.  I never thought I'd ever feel like a weirdo in Berkeley. I was dressed in a pink plaid mini and black boots and a black mesh shirt with a tank bra under. We had just performed a song for our first audience and I was totally dressed for stage, but I don't have any body modifications, and my tattoo is fairly tame. WTF?!?!?

I was so distracted, I just ate my slice with my companion as quickly as I could before he got in a fight with one of the asses giving me looks and we left. 

Pizza was doughy and short on sauce, and the people behind the counter were disgruntled...although it was midnight, so maybe that's why. The album cover decor was cool, it kept me from making eye contact with the other customers.

Yay! I'm the 100th review for Blondie's! 

Anyways, If you live in the bay chances are you've heard about Blondie's Pizza and if you've been to Berkeley, chances are that you've been down Telegraph. If you haven't, just keep nodding your head so as not to draw attention to yourself. Go to Berkeley walk down Telegraph and get some pizza at Blondie's. 

I have been coming here for over a decade now and I still can't get enough of the pizza. Blondie's in Berkeley is historic and in a town where that word gets thrown around a lot Blondie's really does have a lot going to back up that statement. I can not explain how perfect their pizza is when it's fresh and you're just walking out the door taking your first bite. There are no words to describe the goodness that is your first bite of Blondie's pizza. 

If you go out to Telegraph bring 20 one dollar bills like I do, you can help the homeless and feel less guilty about your pizza's sinful goodness. Or if you're broke, just let them know... trust me they'll Identify with having no money, (they're homeless). Don't wander into the park near here after dark though, or you might be privy to someone using the facilities or making sweet love on the lawn. Long story short, Blondie's rocks and you need to go grab a slice.

CHAD

blondies brings me back to my college days in Berkeley when I didn't have a lot of money and just wanted something warm and yummy in my tummy. I would get the pepperoni and if it was fresh and hot from the oven, it was killer. 

tons of hot pepper flakes, a sprinkle of parmesean and I am a happy camper.

Two words: Veggie Slice.

A wheat crust pizza that's light on the cheese, but heavy on the veggies.  As healthy as a real pizza can get!  Okay... not really, but close enough.

Sometimes, when I feel extra gluttonous, I order two slices and eat them both in one sitting.  Yes, I may look small, but I can eat.  I know, my friends keep telling me that I shouldn't eat anything larger than the size of my face (and a slice of Blondie's is definitely bigger than the size of my face), but I can't help it; it's so good!

I mean, c'mon, with most of the food pyramid plopped in the pizza -- cheese, egg, vegetables, bread -- how can you possibly go wrong?!

Oh, and I always unscrew the top of the parmesan cheese dispenser ;)

I loved going to Blondie's years ago and thought their pizza was exceptional, especially the pepperoni slice with a fountain coke.  Quick in and out and tasty tasty tasty!  This was my first Blondie's so it remains my favorite location.

On Black Friday, all the other Fro-Yo places in Berk were closed, so I resorted to Blondie's. I felt kinda sick already, seeing the Fro-Yo machines amid a kitchen of greasy pizza.

Blondie's actually has a nice array of toppings, including fresh blackberries, raspberries, and blueberries. I tried their Green Tea, which tasted kinda weird, then ordered a Plain Original mini with 3 toppings. Came out to a whopping $4.88. I wished that I'd gotten a slice of pizza instead...

Unfortunately, I don't know if it was just the idea of eating Blondie's yogurt or the yogurt itself that made me feel queasy. First I thought it was the former, but as I ate more and more, I found myself wishing that they hadn't given me so much damn Fro-Yo. It was very dense and creamy, barely tart, and tastes kinda like...cream cheese. Couldn't finish it, felt too grossed out. Ew ew ew =(

I used to really like their pizza back when I was living in the area. Despite my lactose intolerance, I'd swallow a few pills and grab a slice.

I'm not fond of the thick crusted pizza normally, and Blondie's is pretty thick but I don't mind.

What I do mind, is despite 2 lactaid pills, I'm dying a few minutes later. To my embarrassment and horror, I had to run and find a public bathroom. Do you know how hard that is in downtown Berkeley? The closest public bathroom is that miserable place in the parking garage a few blocks down. 

An hour later, I'm pretty pissed, and my friends are properly bored.

I try not to stare them in the eye and we continue along our day.

And that is the story about why I eat at Fat Slice when I want pizza.

This is one of those places I really wish I came to more. Since it's not located on Telegraph or the same side of the street as the Asian Ghetto (with IB Hoagies and others), I keep forgetting about coming here.

Other than that, I have always been satisfied about Manhattan Roast and Grill. They know how to make a good burger and sandwich, unlike some of the "healthy low-fat" alternatives scattered across Telegraph. Portions are huge too. You can't go wrong with any of their sandwiches, and the Manhattan Burger is really good.

Atmosphere is very clean, nice, and professional. GIven the space constraints, I'm impressed with what they did. 

Credit cards are accepted here, and prepare about $8-10 per person.

This place is severely underrated. It currently is serving the best cheesesteak in Berkeley until 1AM.

$6.99 with an unreasonably large serving of fries and a fountain drink with free refills.

Did I mention again that it was open late? Every day of the week? (serving a limited menu at night of burgers and cheesesteaks... can't remember if there is a vegetarian option on the late night menu)

While i was there, I was discussing with my dining companion whether or not it was a chain, and he thought it must be, but I commented on the California phenomen of commonplace single location restaurants that feel like chain restaurants. Then I pointed out that the decor is alternating psychedelic DMT posters and pictures of Manhattan.

To the owners: kudos, and I hope you can keep up the quality as you scale to lines out of the door on Friday and Saturday nights. Also, where are you getting your rolls?

Get the Manhattan Burger.  (Avocado and bacon) By far the best burger in Berkeley.

The meal deal is great. Burger drinks and a side for 7 bucks.

Decent pricing for a lot of food

you have to try the turkey sandwich with fries or a salad because it is definitely the best thing they have to offer.

The cranberry sauce on the turkey sandwich makes me come back everytime.

They do charge for using cards and sometimes they run out of meats though

6.99 for a full meal is a great deal to me.

My friends and I were looking for something a little lighter for dinner, when we came across this place. It's newly opened, and you can tell by the workers there. It was actually kinda cute seeing 5 big guys standing around, giving their two cents on how to make the grilled salmon salad that I ordered. 

Overall, the salad was pretty good - just a bed of lettuce, cranberries, balsamic, and a good portion of salmon with a slice of bread. It was well cooked and not dry. Considering there aren't very many fish options in the area (aside from sushi), I would definitely come back for this.

My friend got a crispy chicken sandwich, which she liked because it was tender and a good amount of crispy-ness. 

Kinda random, but the seating area in this restaurant is really high! Like, high as in difficult for short people like me to reach (haha). I wanted to give it 3.5 stars, but I gave it 4 for friendly service. I know a lot of businesses in this area typically go out, so I hope they stick around! :)

I really needed a hamburger, but didn't want to pay the exorbitant fees for a "gourmet" burger.  I also didn't want to have to digest a fast food creation.  I was actually looking for Bongo Burger when I stumbled upon this gem.  $7.60 (tax included) for a 1/2 burger (done perfectly juicy and medium) with bacon, avocado and special sauce.  Oh, and you get a generous helping of fries and a drink.  The value is ludicrous and the taste is quite on point.  The service, however, was a bit lacking.  There were up to five people in the kitchen, but only two were actually cooking.  I waited about 20 minutes for my meal.  Now I want my burger fresh, but not that fresh.  I am willing to return and test the wait again.  Perhaps this was an aberration.

Sandwiches aren't that great. The only reason I gave it an extra star was because it has a much nicer place to sit compared to its competitors (IB's and Sam's Market) whose sandwiches are exponentially superior in price, quality, and portion.

THIS IS THE BEST SANDWICH PLACE I'VE EVER BEEN TOO. I've probably eaten here more than 20 times so some of the cooks recognize me. I have tried their caesar salad, steak, pastrami, the manhattan burger, and philly cheese steak sandwich. The pastrami and philly cheese steak sandwiches are the best!!! The pastrami has thick slices of tender pastrami with sauerkraut and thousand island. The philly cheese steak contains a large portion of steak with melted cheese in a long roll. Their $6.99 combo deal is amazing and cheap considering that you get an entree, a side, and soda. The cooks here are nice and they cook the food really fast...can't wait to eat here again tomorrow!

Meh. I came right after this place opened and was really underwhelmed. The menu is enticing, but the food that comes out is below average. Its cheap, but there is plenty of cheaper and better burgers available nearby.

I ordered the chicken sandwich with peppers and cheese. The bread was mushy, the cheese separated, and the chicken was clearly frozen.

I'll be brief. Why? Because I had this last week and was craving it now.

I had the Manhattan burger and what can I say? You really can't go wrong with it. med rare 1/2lb patty, bacon, avocado, cheese must I say more? Had a side salad instead of fries, wished it was slightly more greens, but the amount of asiago they put in really makes up for it -- was a 5:4 ratio -- what can I say? I love cheese. Probably not enjoyable for conventionalites, but then why are you eating a 1/2lb burger?

Their home-made potatoes and gravy is legit too. nice and chunky yet creamy tatoes.

Also, a new, welcome addition to Berkeley late-night and MEAT choices. Closes at 1AM.

Plus REFILLS. Who knows how long that'll last though. I hope this place is here to stay (for at least a little while..until the granolas get angry).

BTW. Currently 6.99 for this burger, side and a fountain drink. Get it while it lasts!!

This place gets better and better every time I go... and that's a LOT. Every time I come here, I get either the Manhattan burger or the Bear burger along with fries and a soda.

The steak fries they serve here cannot be beat. Best in Berkeley. The burger is well seasoned, and things in general have changed a lot since I first came here and wrote a 3-star review.

This has become my go to place for lunch. Very satisfied and would highly recommend the Manhattan Burger.

The burgers here are pretty legit! The Bear Burger and Manhattan Burger are delicious. The burgers are full of flavor and with the fried egg and/or avocado AND bacon, these are definitely worth a try if you're craving something that will fill you up. If you make it a combo, the salad, mac and cheese, or fries are pretty generous portion sizes (those are the ones I've tried) and the combo meals usually come out to around $8. So overall not too too bad for a full meal. The orders usually come out pretty quickly and the menu has a ton of options in case you are craving something other than a burger. Their Chicken Pesto sandwich is pretty good too! 

All in all, this place is a pretty good deal in my book since it's filling and doesn't disappoint. The food's pretty decent and the location is pretty good - definitely nice to see a restaurant that's doing well on the other side of Durant for a change.

Came in and tried the steak sandwich. Great sandwich overall! Good taste, pretty good price. I also like the seating, with stools facing out windows.

I'm a little disappointed that they didn't go farther with drink choices; nothing but fountain soda. That stuff is really unhealthy and I avoid it. The choices of sides if you do get a combo are pretty good though; there's munchy choices (fries) and healthier choices (vegetables).

Definitely gonna come here regularly.
Very awesome burgers, sandwiches, and sides. The prices are pretty good. I got the philly cheeseteak and it was awesome. Definitely recommend this place. It also opens til 1am!

I decided to try this place as i was sick of eating burgers at IBs all the time , and since it was new . 
They have really good grilled chicken burgers and their salads are pretty good too (especially the one with the salmon ) . 
Service was fast and friendly.  
Overall I would definitely come back and eat here again .

For the price I'm paying, the amount of food that I am getting is wonderful.  While the meat pieces could be a little bigger, the large volume in the sides more than made up for it.

The workers are also very nice and open to good banter.

Hopefully Manhattan Roast & Grill stays open for a good long while, they have great food, great atmosphere and decor and great people.

Can't wait for my next meal there. :)

I love this place. It is cheap, fast and very convenient. It's hard to find a good burger around near the campus that fills you up. The Manhattan Burger combo is a must have with either a side of french fries or mac & cheese. I get this at least 3 times a week!

A much needed addition to the Durant take out selection, especially given how greasy and queasy IB's is across the street. A lot of great warm deli  stuff in New York style, things like pastrami and corned beef and even turkey legs. Most things can be had with drink and side for 6.99 which is great. Food isn't New York impressive, but it's not bad, and a very good value. The burgers are 1/2lb monsters and they're all very good. The manhattan burger is the best ive had in south berkeley.
Word of warning, as you may expect, the turkey can often be a little dry, but at least they roast their own and carve it fresh. Another complaint is that their chairs (stools) are ridiculously tall. I'm 6'1" and it takes a little work to get up on top of them.

Their burgers and salmon are always good (just a bit on the greasy side), but the rest of their menu is ok. The salad is bland, and if you don't ask them to put the dressing on the side, it's a bit too much. But that's just nick-picking a bit, since you go there for the burgers anyways. I personally like the Manhattan Burger and the Uptown Burger, but I haven't been disappointed by any other burgers (Bear Burger, Queen Burger, forget what else). The guys there are super friendly, so it's a good atmosphere (also a great place to just people-watch, if you're into doing that while eating). Prices are good, so I'd recommend this place!

Since this place opened I noticed it was doing uncannily well for its location, where food joints are known to go in and out of business (Fa-La-La, Minami Sushi, the rotation of Korean restaurants). Seems that Manhattan is doing pretty well. 

I got a Manhattan burger (a regular burger with avocado, bacon, and 'Manhattan' sauce, which is just mayo, ketchup, and mustard). It was tall and hard to grip, but yummy - I'd say it's comparable to Bongo Burger, though, and nothing too special. It was also a pretty standard price - not expensive, but not that cheap either.

The fries were crisp, and for sides I'd recommend the fries. My friend had the mac and cheese and the cheese was not strong enough - tasted mushy. 

Dine in tables are stools with countertop (kind of uncomfortable). Cards is + 50 cents extra charge.

Walked past this place for several months, always admiring the $6.99 any menu item + side + drink deal, and finally tried it out one day. Since then I have returned and must say, this place is quickly becoming a staple in my rotation of restuarants/quick eats/cheap places in Berkeley.

Gotten the pastrami sandwich and philly cheesesteak sandwich before, plus fries and a drink, and it's really just some solid food. The sandwiches came out nice and hot, fries aren't too crunchy/thin nor too plump/soft. The quantity of food is definitely worth it and if someone asks me, "Hey where's somewhere I can go for lunch that's quick, cheap, and close to Berkeley campus? (south side)" I'd definitely say try Manhattan Roast & Grill.

There's just so much on the menu that I want to come back some more just to try them- like the burgers or plates, and other sides like mac n cheese or coleslaw. Service is fast too with not much wait time, but I'd say the only real knock is that the place is small- no real tables as all the seats are like stools at a counter but then you can people watch along Telegraph :)

Huge portions, crappy food. Average Berkeley price ($6 to 9 bucks for most menu items). 

I agree with all the other yelpers. Their stools are way too tall. Pretty unfortunate since I went there after a crazy workout, so my thighs just died a second time trying to get onto the stool. And then I had to get down and up again to pick up my order T^T sadness. 

Wouldn't go here again. Not that the food's super gross or anything, but there's so many better places around here. I swear, the building's cursed.

Have yet to try their sandwiches, but got a protein salad the other day. The salad itself was a bust, partly because the vinaigrette was was too strong for me. Bad choice there on my part, and honestly salads are eh for me. They put cranberries in the salmon salad, which was a nice touch.

The thing that reall sold me was the chuck of salmon. It was nice and big, and grilled perfectly, not too fishy at all.

I'll consider going back to try other things.

Their combo meal with side orders and drink is really good; only comes out to 7.50. I ordered the Manhattan burger, which is 1/2 lb, comes with avocado, bacon, and fries. The burger was cooked medium and not dry. 

Service is relatively fast. The seating is kind of cramped and there are only high seats.

TL;DR; Give this place a try as it's really cheap. 1/2 lb burger with drink and side for 7.50.

I was very impressed with the manhattan burger and I would give that a 5 stars for the value. My only complaint would be that the Avacado has no taste.

I was feeling hungry so I decided to get mashed potatoes and a drink on the side for only a dollar more.

I finished my burger and took one bite of the mashed potatoes and was disgusted. It looked fresh and creamy but the smell was revolting and it tasted old and not fresh at all. Stick to fries or a salad.

I would give this place a 4 out of 5 because of the large portions but the mashed potatoes brings it down to a 3.

I love the Philly Cheese Steak from here. Much less greasy than I.B. Hoagies down the street. I also tried the  New York Style Burger, which is a bit bland, since it comes without condiments (they have ketchup and packets of mustard you can add yourself) it needs more flavor, like the thousand island dressing at In-n-out. They also have whole turkey legs here, and the meal comes with two sides and a dinner roll! Woo-whee. They have great meaty food for under 10 dollars; I want to try more things on the menu!

I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich, since I don't know of any other place that serves it out here. 

I ordered the combo which comes with fries and a drink for $8.
I got the mashed potatoes, but I guess the grand opening special is to surprise you, so instead they gave me fries...huh? 

The chicken was very well seasoned and the special Manhattan sauce, is similar to Smart Alec's special sauce, the yummy one next to the ketchup.  The most disappointing thing is that the chicken was so thin, like paper thin, look at the picture I posted: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WSTdK7y1ZDw9JU3NUpFj7g?select=r72jQLrasG8wQD0HuhMwSQ

I wish they would maybe put another slice of chicken, because for $8 I want to satiate my appetite. 

Other then that, the salads looks really good, hopefully after trying one I will be able to give them a better rating. But as of now, if the store continues operating the was it is it not likely to succeed.  

And from a business stand point, having 9 workers is not the smartest decision. Lets say they get paid just over minimum wage so that's 9 workers X $10/hour =  $90/ hour. The price of the average meal is $6-8  which means having a minimum of $13 to cover the employee cost. That doesn't include food cost. Hopefully they can stay afloat.

I hate being the bad guy, but if you are going to open a food joint in Berkeley, it better not be subpar!
Wow there Philly cheese is in incredible just the right amt of heat with plent of flavor and the slaw is out of this world definitely a must go for all sandwich enthusiasts

I was CRAVING beef at 11:40pm, and apparently Steve's closes at 11 now. So I ordered the philly cheesesteak from their late night menu.  I just ... didn't like it. The meat was more crumbly than slicey, and the pickled vegetables were just too pickled. ._. They didn't mesh well. And the bread was limp. Good bread makes a huge difference! 

Finally, and this is really why I'm like D:, the cheese was not cheese. It was a "cheese product." This was confirmed when in the morning I looked at the remains of my sandwich and the white gloop all over the box had not solidified. augh

I come here probably on every other week.  Their combo deal for 7 dollars+tax is pretty awesome.  I usually get the Manhattan burger with fries.  Often times you'll leave full after coming here.  In my book, this is my go-to under 10 dollar burger place around campus.  Sorry Bongo Burger, you are a close 2nd.

The Philly Cheese Steak was decent. Not a big fan of the pickled bell peppers however...the taste just seemed out of place. I was expecting a larger sandwich than a skinny roll, but I guess it was an OK size and an acceptable amount of beef for $5.99 + tax. I might come back to try the other sandwiches or plates, but this visit didn't really wow me or anything.

Note: they accept credit cards, but it's an additional 49 cents.

I usually get the Manhattan burger because it's probably the best deal for the money. Bacon AND avocados....cannot beat that! I've tried their carved turkey sandwich as well and it was pretty good as well. If you're not feeling burgers, they have plenty of other options such as an assortment of sandwiches and different plates. The people are friendly here and the quality of the food is consistent. I definitely recommend this joint if you're looking for a quick bite or a good burger!
This place is alright... Tbh the only reason I go here is cause they serve mashed potatoes. Yum. Oh and the fries are cool too but only cause they have a dispenser for A-1 sauce. Yeah!

Come on folks....really?   Play fair and be nice.   Crave this place and their vale and quality weekly!  Only complaint is the odd layout, but not sure how they could have done it without sacrificing the kitchen area (watch them BUTCHER the meat to be more appreciative!).

As a PA gal, their Philly's can NOT be beat.
Big portions and tastes good too! Was pleasantly surprised. :) I prefer this over Bongo Burger and Smart Alec's.
five stars because bendy straws dog

Let's get real. They have  some great food options here. 

Some of the best burgers in the area also where else can you get a turkey dinner other than with your family on Thanksgiving?

They also have good salad options, maybe not with a lot of extra toppings but still overall a good deal. The salmon salad came with a good-size piece of grilled fish. It's also not as expensive as one would think
Quick, tasty, and fast. What more could you ask for? Had the french dip, it was both tasty and a great value. A bit nippy inside though as the door allows in too much cold air in

The sandwich I got here was delicious as were the fries. It's really different from most of the sandwich shops you find around Berkeley. Definitely food that's packed with flavor. I'm surprised that more people haven't been here yet/ reviewed it. 

The portions were also reallyyyy large. I saved half of it for dinner so it's a great value.

Came here today at lunch because of the Touchdown Monday (30% off for the recent Cal win). Long line that awkwardly meanders out the door and blocks people from entering. The cashier is right on front of the door and there its little maneuvering room inside.
 
Ordered a roast turkey sandwich on a white roll with avocado. Did a combo with fries soda (usually $7.60 tx incl, now $5.55). Waited a short time, but phased that time by getting to-go containers of ketchup and A1 steak sauce. You cash see the huge while roast turkey sitting under the roasting lamp with trays of the other hot sandwich filings.

Taking our food to-go, I open the box and there is a very large sandwich spilt in two with a generous portion of thick cut fries. Splitting with my friend, I took the first bite...and was not impressed. I could not really taste the cranberry spread, the added avocado was limited, I forgot there was bacon til the end when I saw it sticking out, and even the gouda cheese was not as detectable despite there being two slices and it usually being  a very bold cheese. Adding the A1 steak sauce added more flavor amd I liked it then. The turkey breast was very good, since out was thick carved and generous in amount, but perhaps that is why I couldnt taste the other ingredients. I really wanted the cranberry to shine out of the sandwich, but it didnt. Personally, I didnt even like the white sandwich roll; it had a chewy crust rather than a nice and crust and crispy crust like a baguette. 

The fries were good, but I probably ate too many.

(Also had a bite of my friend's manhattan steak sandwich and was also unimpressed. I would rather go get Brazil Cafe for steak.)

Very filling, decent price, but also decent taste. I will not return.

I recently made a homecoming back to Berkeley with Kathleen W. and we were curious to see if anything has changed on South Side. To my surprise, the area that used to be occupied solely by Minami Sushi is now vibrantly thriving, with Manhattan Roast & Grill occupying a significant portion. We decided to give them a try and see if it was anything worth raving about.

Here was my problem: Everything on the Roast Turkey sandwich looked amazing and is the first thing that truly caught my eye. The only thing I didn't want on it, however, was the turkey itself. Luckily, they let me have roast beef instead and for the same price. To sum it up, I got roast beef, gouda cheese, bacon strips, tomato, lettuce, and cranberry mayo pecan spread on an Italian bun. 

This sandwich just blew my mind. First of all, no other cheese beats smoked gouda, so this was automatically a win for me. I didn't taste the bacon strips too much, which meant there was a perfect quantity of them. The spread was just a little sweet and added a perfect contrast to the gouda and roast beef combo. Overall, it was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. If I was a student again, this would be one of my go to places for a quick to go lunch. Looks like Cheese 'N' Stuff has some serious competition.

I didn't have much expectations, but was mildly pleasantly surprised. The service was friendly and the menu was big. I got the impression that this place would be like a cheesesteak sandwich shop, but it's more than that. There are items like a roast beef or cornish game hen plates with mashed potatos and steamed veggies. There are grill items like burgers with fries. There is indeed cheesesteak sandwiches. I like that. I like that there are items you can't find elsewhere in this immediate college campus periphery. The game hen was good and juicy, with lots of lemon juice on the skin. The pastrami was good, very hot deli-styled. The pickle was meh. The jus was gravy. The mashed potatos were creamy and there was as much gravy as there was potato. The steamed veggies were bland, but they are steamed frozen veggies after all. Also, unlimited fountain soda from the self-serve soda dispenser. Overall, this isn't extraordinary, but was worth my hunger.

In short: cheap, big portions, fast.

And how about those extra tall stools?? I literally had to climb a ladder to get on them. I see that they wanted to align the counter with the existing window separation, but so not cool and so not ADA-friendly.

Goodness, I love to eat at this restaurant. It is by far my favorite (and closest!) place to eat out.

Service/Decor: Food comes out pretty fast, maybe within 10 minutes. There aren't individual tables but there's bar-seating that faces out onto the street. Looks pretty clean. Did I mention IT CLOSES AT 1AM? AWESOME.

Food: Manhattan Burger. Delicious. Always cooked to a medium rare, almost always seasoned perfectly. I rarely ever have to put ketchup on or season the burger myself, which is fantastic. The burger itself comes with AVOCADO AND BACON. Too excellent. Normally it's $7.60 for a Manhattan Burger Combo, which includes the burger itself, a side (I usually get fries), and a small drink. Pretty excellent combo and you get a lot of bang for your buck. I am sad, however, that they did not grill my bun and the bun sort of broke apart while eating it. I also wish they had different choices of fries; if I want fries, I'll usually get it across the street at IB's.

Manhattan Roast & Grill is quite possibly the best sandwich shop on the south side purely because they know what it takes to make a great tasting sandwich. They have great bread, generously-portioned meats, and a variety of tasty condiments. You can choose what you want on your sandwich, or go with one of their creations. Of which I highly recommend the Roast Turkey sandwich with comes with sweet cranberry-pecan mayo, bacon, smoked gouda cheese, and a generous portion of roasted turkey. It put a nice twist on a classic thanksgiving leftover. Also, Manhattan Roast & Grill serves hefty philly-cheese steaks and half-pound burgers in similarly tasty combinations. Burgers and sandwiches cost $7.99 with a good-sized side and small drink (free refills). A great deal for a delicious and well-portioned meal on Durant. 

As for the atmosphere and service, it is a bit tight in the restaurant but there is a surprising amount of seating along the window in bar format In addition, the employees bus the plates which is convenient.  The Keith Haring cartoons scattered about the wall add a nice touch. Sandwiches take a while to create when the restaurant is busy, but service is generally quick and you can call in several minutes beforehand and have your order waiting for you when you arrive. 

The location of Manhattan Roast & Grill is notorious for failed food joints (see Fa-La-La) but this sandwich shop thrives purely because it makes great sandwiches. And if that what you are looking for, this is the place to go.

Unfortunately, this place recently started charging an inconvenient $.49 for each credit card transaction. Which surely makes a relative increase in the price of each sandwich.

This place has a fantastic atmosphere, and the service is swell. I love getting the Bear Burger with mashed potatoes. They also play good music.

Food takes a while to prepare though. I wouldn't mind the wait if the place was roomier.

Bonus Point! They are one of few places in the area open past mid night!

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here for late dinner on a Monday night after a mind-blowing midterm. omg I wish I could talk about how I felt about the midterm (state of overconcentration is BAD), but you'd probably fall asleep before I even got to describing the food.

I wasn't sure what to order here, as the Yelp reviews weren't unanimous in decision on one item. And for some strange reason, when my eyes connected with the word "meatloaf" on their signboard, I knew I had to have it. And I have no idea why. I haven't eaten meatloaf in YEARS, probably because I don't take a particularly fond liking to it. But there was something about that midterm that made me crave meatloaf!!! I don't get it either.

You walk in to the counter, and to the left are wall seats on stools. People mill around the counter for take-out orders, so don't get lost in the wrong crowd. It took me 2 minutes to order, as I was waiting for the cashier to divvy out take-out orders. And there was no one in front of me either. So...2 minutes seemed reaaallly long.

Food was served in 4 minutes over the counter, and the server said that if I wanted more gravy, I could ask. How nice!

|| F O O D ||

HOMEMADE MEATLOAF LUNCH/DINNER PLATE: tomato sauce or gravy with choice of 2 side orders and a dinner roll [$6.99 | $7.60 with tax if paid in cash]
- Two slices of meatloaf drizzled in gravy! Gravy wasn't too thick and added a delicate touch of mmm mmm good. The meatloaf was a bit dry but savory nonetheless. It looked a bit raw on the inside? At least it looked a bit pink. Then again, I'm not meatloaf expert. =3=
- Salad was normal romaine, nothing too healthy. Chunks of grated parmesan cheese on top with some delectably-flavored croutons. Yup, that's my serving of veggies for the week.
- Fries were good. Not salted, and a good chewy, slightly crunch texture.
- Dinner roll felt soft but did not taste soft.

|| C L O S U R E ||

Homemade meatloaf is meh, fries are good, decent portions for the price, food is out fast. It seems like they're more famous for their roasted turkey sandwich and their burgers, so maybe I should stick the recommendations and not venture far from Yelp next time. Learning my lesson the hard way :c

They charge an additional $0.49 if you pay with card, so bring cash!

Manhanttan offers 1/4# burgers, oven roast sandwiches, grilled steaks & chicken sandwiches, salads, and side orders.

a few seats available for seating but it's basically take out.

eats: special: choice of sandwich/burger, side order  & drink(6.99)
-manhattan club (6.99) 
had lots of turkey, roast beef, ham, not much flavoring 
swiss cheese, lettuce, tomato, mayo, and avocado also
sliced rye toasted great
added grey poupon later, tasted a lot better
-mashed potato with gravy
creamy, king of lumpy, watery, tasted pretty good. 

leftovers
-sandwich didn't have a lot of taste. good value though.
-maybe  a burger next time. nope only 1/4#.
-fast service, helpuful suggestions...

For starters, I was pleasantly surprised by the prices. Traipsing hungrily through the UC area, my friend remembered hearing positive things about La Cascada Taqueria ("really good burritos," etc.).

Californians, in particular, seem to be very picky about their burritos. Being from New York, I'm constantly comparing my love of pizza to their love of burritos. It's in the blood. I get that. So I understand the many thickness/thinness, flavor, and consistency issues that arise when it comes to choosing a burrito joint. And as for my chicken burrito, it was long, lean (on the thinner side), and very close to perfect.

Everything tasted fresh, the ingredients were evenly distributed, and it had exactly the right amount of heat throughout. The salsa bar was fine, too (but I care less about spicy salsa than I do about a tasty burrito).

Also, the guys working there were fantastic. Accommodating, polite... and more than willing to give us extra foil and bags so we could take our leftovers home (... though they only made it as far as the car).

I work 2 blocks from Center Street but am always passing this place on my way to work from school. At 11:00 a.m. I am always hungry and the choice is between a burrito and sushi (C U is right beside them). My life would be so much simpler if I could give these guys a higher rating. They give you a pretty big burrito for the price ($7 for Carne Asada) but the meat always smells funny? I keep going back because it is the cheapest and quickest food in the downtown Berkeley area but if La Burrita was not up the high I would rather go there. One thing I must give them props for is their salsa. The green stuff is super fresh and awesome. If only their meat did not smell a little weird, this place would be perfect.

Today was March 10th. 50% off all wraps and burritos. AWESOME.
I used the opportunity to order two burritos, a Fajita Wrap and a Super Beef Burrito. Both were amazing. I don't know if i would pay the full price on that fajita burrito, but it was darn good. Will come back occasionally.

This is my favorite burrito menu in Berkeley: that said, it is very California-style, with Thai wraps, a curry burrito, a veggie burrito with green beans, pesto available, etc., so not very south-of-the-border, if thats what you are looking for. But being a California-cuisine lover, this is my kind of place!

The tofu curry burrito is the tastiest item!!

So far, this is my favorite burrito place in the Bay Area, not including food trucks! I get the vegetarian rice and bean burrito with black beans. It's big and really yummy! The place is nice and sunny and conveniently located and the guys are really friendly.

The best part, by far, is the salsa. I pour some on each bite of burrito. Try the mild (green one) and the medium (red one), they're my favs. I also recommend squeezing lime on your tortilla chips. :p

Oh and did I mention they're super cheap. Well, a veggie burrito anyway, just $5!

I stopped in here with my girlfriend for a quick bite to eat before our movie began. After we finished our meals we weren't late to the movie and we weren't disappointed with our burritos.  We were looking for something filling, cheap, and quick - luckily we happened to find this place. 

I've read some of the bad reviews, and I don't know how often they have visited this place to label everything as terrible, but my experience was pretty good.  Free Refills on fountain drinks, filling and tasty carnitas burrito, very low key and low traffic venue, with cheap chips and salsa - what else do you really want?  (actually the chips were REALLY salty - but other than that I can't complain).

No one gave me the finger or treated me poorly, the food arrived within 3 minutes of placing the order, and condiments were available to season the food. 

Mission accomplished La Cascada - I shall see you again on my next visit to Berkeley.

-Excuse me for being a snob but if I wanted a room temperature burrito I would take one home, stick it in the fridge for a day, throw it in the microwave for 45 seconds, then eat it. NOT go to a resturant and pay like seven dollars for one....

I got a carne asada burrito and the meat tasted off...maybe it needs more seasoning or something

Food isn't good and prices are high=wont be back

I was going to grad school in Berkeley in 97 so most of my review is old memories but I have eaten there recently when in town to see Dream Theater.

La Cascada is the best non-traditional Mexican I have had in Berkeley.  What used to be El Fabuloso on Telegraph was the best traditional style, and La Cascada was the best non-traditional.  What do I mean by non-traditional?  Well they have pesto chicken and Thai burritos.  In the era of World Wraps this really doesn't seem like much but 10 years ago when they opened they were serving them and they're still as tasty now as they were then.

I literally ate there every day for months, and the food is the same today as it was then.  My favorites are the seafood burritos (try them as a Torpedo Wrap if you're really hungry) and the pesto chicken burrito.  Nowadays I am a big fan of carnitas and their carnitas has never been very special, they're kind of dry.  Instead go for the pesto chicken burrito which has a very basil-y pesto.  

Beware of cilanto if you don't like it, they use a decent amount and it will ruin your dish.

To this day, any time I pass Berkeley I think of pulling off of 80 and popping in to grab a burrito.
I go there for lunch a lot.  The cashier lady is hot.

We stopped in because they had a sign outside stating that the had the best burritos in Berkley.   Now I don't know who gave them that title, but my  guess is they just put it up to sucker in hungry people, who like my self have a desire to find the best burrito EVER.  to say the lest this was not the best burrito in fact it was barley sub par.  the beans tasted like they came from a can and there was no cheese or sour cream, to make matters worse there was bad bean to meat ratio, to many beans not enough meat.  they might do other things well but on the whole i felt cheated and led a stray
Considering some of the great burritos in the area i don't know why anyone would settle for this.  If your in the area, go next door to Top Dog 5, its much better and much cheeper.

had this today for lunch.  a coworker recommended me to it.
I was really craving for a plate of enchiladas with rice and beans! and i was hoping this place would satisfy it.. unfortunately, they dont offer anything but wraps, tacos and burritos..
thats fine, ill just get a burrito without the tortilla, its close enough. maybe im spoiled from all the cheap and good mexican food in oakland, but this place was just... ok if even. i got the carnitas and steak. its both pretty dry. and there really isnt that much food. i dont usually eat much, but i was able to finish this in one sitting, surprised everyone. the salas are ok the chips looks like the big costco bag kind... the rice is flavor less, the black beans.. it was just ok. the pico de gallo did have fresh tomatoes, as it should. lol. 
i dont think ill pay 7 dollars for such mediocre food from this place again, sadly, id rather eat chipotle at least ill be completely stuffed

unless im totally starving and everything is closed lol

La Cascada has really gone down hill in the past few years, which is a pity because I finally finished my "buy 9 get one free" burrito card.  While you expect a burrito to fill you up and then some, La Cascada's burritos are smaller than the "baby" burritos served at taquerias in the Mission.  The prices haven't shrunk, so you're paying about $5-$6 for a small burrito that leaves you wanting.  They have a great tomatillo salsa that I love, which used to come in squeeze bottles, but now, you can only take two containers of salsa...if you're the sort that follows their draconian rules.  Gone are the glory days when I could bite and squirt salsa, bite, salsa, repeat.  If you don't want the regular ol' chicken or carne asada burrito, you can get grilled veggies and whatnot in yours:  they go a little crazy with the concept of fusion burritos with a Thai-influenced one and, I think, one that has pesto.  They have my least favorite chips in all of Bay Area taqueriadom.

This place is dirty, and disgusting, the room-temperature burritos gave me a belly ache, the bathroom was filthy, and some guy got punched when he was waiting in line...

   There were selling burritos at 50% off that day, and since I'm a student, it sounded like a good deal to me. When I placed my order, the woman at the register didn't even look me in the eye, and had a rude vibe about her. I ordered my burrito and went to use the restroom, where the toilet (full of a giant crap) didn't flush,  and there was no more paper.
  Then I grabbed my burrito and sat down at a table that looked like it hadn't been wiped down all-day, and there was food on the floor that no one bothered to clean up.
  Furthermore, the salsa bar was dirty and in disarray, and there were no little plastic cups to put my salsa in. The burrito wasn't hot--the beans were room-temp., it wasn't even hot enough to melt the cheese. There was hardly any meat in the burrito, except for one giant chunk of fat.
  Then, a bunch of people from the ACLU and other canvassers were waiting in line, and this guy who had been begging across the street started yelling at one of the canvassers about cutting in line. The guy just shrugged him off, and so the beggar punches the guy in the stomach!
  I lost my appetite right about then and left. And I am never going back!!
They must have had some really crappy burrito places back in 1997 when they won the award. Plus I got a horrible stomach ache later that day.

It does the job, considering it's so close to campus and all. The chorizo breakfast burrito is good, but a little small considering the price. I may have just been really hungry--but I finished it in record burrito eating time. I thought the chorizo could have been a little spicier, but I really love spicy food. There was also supposed to be potatoes in it, but I really couldn't find any. I like the addition of refried beans, though. The service was very good; the guy at the counter was really nice. Next time I'm going to try the carnitas, since I judge all Mexican restaurants on their carnitas.

We decided to have a light late lunch and chose La Cascada because its suppose to be good. I ordered a burrito and she a tostada salad. Everything seems fine. While sitting and eating, my partner observes two events that was not good. One of the servers was stirring some type of dressing and placed his finger into the bowl to sample. Yuck!! Then we both saw the same server use a broom that was sitting on the floor next to the grill and used it to brush the open grill and placed broom back on floor. Yuck twice!! Neither one of us got sick but she did feel some discomfort. Crap!!! Also aren't hair-nets required? Did they close the College Ave location?? I certainly would not recommend this place and would certainly welcome a visit from the health department.

Its possibly the best breakfast burrito of all time.  EVERY time I am in Berkeley i get one.  every time I'm there they make everything right in front of me and its always top notch. I've probably gone 10 times, i recommend it to my water polo team when we go see CAL polo games and they all love it.

I don't know if it was good or bad that my chicken burrito took all of five seconds to put together. Regardless, half of the chicken had BONE in it. Not just tiny splinters--knuckle-sized chunks of bone. Is that even allowed??
It's pretty hard to screw up a generic burrito, but they managed to. This place isn't worth it, especially since there are better burrito places nearby (and better restaurants in general).
Great salsa bar. The fish tacos were gross, why would I want a fish stick in my taco..great prices for students.

If you enjoy management who'd lie to your face, burritos filled with empty padding then I'd recommend this place for you. 

So I got a sausage/potato burrito, ate about 1/4 of it until I realized that it was all rice and no meat. I thought, maybe the good stuff's further down, so I gave my burrito a good lobotomy. No hint of any meat at all. I went to the grouchy looking cashier, who was also the manager of the place and told them that they had forgotten to put any meat in my burrito. I said that it was fine to have meat on the side, since I didn't want them to have to go through the trouble of remaking a burrito for me.

What he did instead was he took my burrito with his dirty hands, and pointed at some unidentifiable speck and said, "Look, meat right there." 

Pretty sure I created a Yelp account just to bitch this place out. Even La Burrita has tastier burritos than this joke of a place.
Exceptionally Mediocre food. If you want a good burrito go around the corner to Razan's Organic Kitchen around the corner.

Very good fresh home-made salsa

Had one taco for a lunch; it was satisfying, presented nicely on a plate, and allowed me to add plenty of salsa and condiments :)

I like their chicken burritos and super chicken tacos. Delicious guac.

A little pricey in my opinion, but always filling.  3.75 stars.
I LOVE THEIR NACHOS!!!! Me and my fiance go there regularly, every time we go in they know to make nachos. I think they have the perfect flavor combination of sour cream, cheese, and guacamole.
Delicious vegetarian burrito and beautiful setting!

I really really LOVE their chorizo y papas burritos!  They're the BEST!!!  The burrito has mexican sausage in it and pieces of seasoned potatoes.  I like to get the  chopped cilantro and chopped onions from the salsa cart and top each bite of my burrito with them.  You can also get different kinds of tortillas to wrap your burrito.  They have spinach and tomato tortillas. 

The service is okay.  They are not overly friendly, but they are not rude either.

The prices are pretty reasonable.

This is the place I go to get a burrito in dt berkeley.

I have been visiting La Cascada since 1998 and have nice chats with Mohammed, the owner, and have gotten to know his bro Albert (co-owner of the College Av branch).  Definitely try the thai chicken curry wrap - the sauce and black beans complement the succulent chicken.  The size is just perfect for one meal, because it is not overly large and focuses on quality ingredients vs quantity you might find at other Mexican joints.  

I love the food here soooo much that after my LASIK eye surgery, my best friend literally held my hand as I stumbled blindly into the store, bandages still on.  (At the time I was living 3,000 miles away, so this was my only chance to eat the scrumptious thai wrap.)  The murals on the wall are fun, the ingredients they use very fresh, and the agua frescas with real fruit.

Although the variety of salsas are not the best, the red salsa is fiery hot and gives a great kick.  The chicken tortas with the garlicky avocado spread are also tasty, but the bread used now is a bit too big.  It helps if you peel off the top crust.  All in all, a definite gem in Berkeley/North Oakland.  And do get a frequent buyer card for your own free burrito.

La Cascada has consistently great food, along with courteous, efficient counter service. The restaurant always appears very clean, and their food is always flavorful and fresh. I've had the nachos and the carnitas burrito, amongst other dishes. Every menu item I've had in the numerous times I've eaten here has been good; I would definitely order them all again.
The decor is warm, colorful, and inviting, and there's a small salsa bar including onions and limes to jazz up your meal.

I can't vouch for their non-vegetarian fare, but the vegetarian burritos at this place are fantastic. Their ingredients are vegetarian (no chicken stock in the rice, no lard used in cooking) and their burritos are warm, well wrapped, and offer a good mix of vegetables with black beans, rice, and salsa. I've had better food and service at the Elmwood location than the Center Street location, but I haven't yet been disappointed at either place. Compared to some of the taquerias in town that won't guarantee the veggie-friendliness of their food and have serve weak beans and rice burritos in unsanitary conditions, I think this place is great. The chips aren't fantastic, but when I order a burrito I'm usually not so concerned with the nachos. Check out the College Ave. La Cascada if you're looking for a good vegetarian burrito.

I've been frequenting Cascada throughout my undergraduate career.  And I must say, I don't understand all the hate for it!  Their black bean burrito is divine!  And where else can you get a spinach (green) tortilla?  It's absolutely perfect IMO if you just squeeze some lime into it after you bite off the top.  I love the staff because they're nice and they're good at anticipating my order.  Minus one star because their salsa sucks.

This place used to be a good place to go for food in downtown Berkeley. The "Picate" used to have lots of veggies in it, like it was described on the chalkboard.

I swear there was 1 piece of squash in it and few cereals of corn, some beans and LOTS of rice. Blah. The "salsa bar" is such a joke. 

I'm going to have to go back into Bongo Burger now and buy a turkey burger after the regular burger I just ate. This burrito is dry and saturated in BBQ sauce. 

Looking back, I think this was the worst "gourmet" burrito experience I've ever had to endure.  I ate half of it and threw the rest away.
Best carnitas you will ever taste! Hands down!

So La Cascada proudly adorns their storefront with a flag that touts "Voted Best Burrito". Problem is they won that title back in 1997. If they haven't any other (read: more recent) accolades to boast, things aren't looking good. Wouldn't it be better to just leave well enough alone and take down the sign, rather than to ensure mockery?

Anyway, we went to check it out - based on the Best Burrito of 1997 status , and curiosity - and we were not too pleased. I got the chorizo y papas burrito. It was so-so at best. The burrito on the whole was pretty bland. As were the side of chips, and the salsas, of which they only had 2 kinds - red and green.

It really makes me wonder what the place was like back in 97.... and also, who was doing the voting.
the worst burritto i ever had. also very filthy inside.
Blah! I hate bad, flavorless, tasteless burritos.. that was a waste of 6 bucks...

It's hard to rate a place after eating one insignificant burrito.  The issue is that if the food was just so-so, why would you want to go back?  Then again, it could very well be that their other plates are fantastic and the burrito happens to be lackluster.  And it was a lackluster beef burrito with the usual ingredients.  It was, however, a good size and it certainly beats the hell out of that pool of mediocrity known as Chipotle.

This is my personal favorite taqueria close to campus. The regular burritos are pretty good, but where they shine is the more unusual ones. I'm a huge fan of the chorizo y papas burrito; the picante is a vegetarian burrito which is pretty healthy and delicious! They have 'international' burritos like chicken curry and thai chicken, also good. The best part is, they have a breakfast menu and SERVE IT ALL DAY!

The salsa bar is very nice, but the chips you get free are pretty bad; they taste like they come from the grocery store. Unlike la burrita or chipotle, they also have Jarritos!

Be sure to make it over when they have a half-price burrito day. Stock up, and they're about 98% as good warmed in the microwave.
Best of Berkeley? Meh

i've eaten a lot of burrito in my day, and i can honestly say this is the worst. for 7 bucks, u get a quick sloppy burrito. it had little chicken and it was charbroiled to a piece of black char.the strange part was the chunks of char were not sizzling hot, just warm. my friend sitting with me told me i had black ash stuck to my teeth. i spit it out after bite two. it had a funny taste to the whole thing, normally i'd have complained, but i wasn't in the mood. tossed it. better to toss it than have the runs. also, very dirty inside. clean the floor!

A pretty decent burrito stop either pre- or post-bart.  The meat in my carnitas burrito was a little tough, but the beans and rice were flavorful and everything was pretty well mixed around, avoiding the ever-dreaded pocket of sour cream at the bottom of your burrito instead of well-distributed creaminess in every bite.  I actually like the salsa at La Burrita better, but in every other way, La Cascada wins out.

I went here for an early lunch to beat the rush, probably a bad move on my part.  I ordered a beef burrito with black beans.  The burrito came to me lukewarm, probably because it was still warming up on the steamers from sitting in the fridge overnight.  Lukewarm food is okay when you are starving at home and can't wait another minute to eat something, but its not cool at a restaurant.  On that note, I don't know how this place could have as many stars as it does.  The beef didn't have much flavor, the rice was soggy, and all I could really taste were the raw onions.  After living in So Cal and enjoying a good Alberto's burrito, if this place is considered "The Best Burrito in Berkeley," I'll look elsewhere when a burrito craving hits.

Ive been going to this restaurant my whole life it feels like. i love it! all my friends love it!! and my whole family! the best burritos are the chicken, and fajita! the quesadillas are AMAZING!! their salsas are the best! and i love their spicy chipotle hummus! 
they have such a creative menu!

I've reviewed my share of taquerias, and I'm sad to say that La Cascada is one of the worst I've been to. Don't get me wrong, I'm hard to please when it comes to burritos, but what La Cascada served was nothing short of a great insult on mexican food.

First of all, half of the burrito was cold. Granted, it's where the guac, sour cream and salsa was, but it also meant that the burrito was horribly mixed. The tortilla was hard. There was hardly any cheese. The worst part is the meat. Man, that was some grade C meat. It was tough, flavorless, and worst of all, cold too!

All that for almost $7!

The only thing keeping me from giving this place a 1 star was the breakfast burrito I had one time, out of desperation because I was craving breakfast burritos.

Delicious burrito place.  Zagat first alerted me to this place and I'm glad it did.

Really friendly owners.

Needed a quick bite after the movies the other night with the kid. Just a block walk away from the Shattuck Theaters, and no wait. Guys working there very friendly and accommodating with our "no sour cream, change to spinach wrap after the order was in" which we appreciate. Orders of food were huge and the price was reasonable, food tasty and steamin' hot. Definitely a good bang for your buck. Perfect for the college crowd, and someone on the run. The place's esthetic is a bit sparse, but dinner made for a happy belly!

This is a very good burrito place to hit. I don't know to explain it exactly, but theirs is one of the better burritos that I've had. It's big enough to fill your appetite, but wrapped nicely so everything doesn't spill over. The meat is delicious and so are the other contents.
Close to BART. Portions have been getting smaller over the years, although the mix of ingredients is tasty. Their College Avenue location actually has better food.

Just so so.  I like the College location better.  There can be a pretty long wait for your food at times here as well.  I think it depends on the time of day.  Not the best mexican food, but it will do the trick.
The burritos are ok. I like to go for their wraps for a change of pace to the traditional burrito. The place is expensive for a burrito, but that seems to be the norm on this side of campus.

Okay, this is the worst burrito place in Berkeley, a city full of incredible burritos. This place is still in business because it's a two minute walk from Cal, and a fifteen minute walk to better burrito place is like a 100 mile death march to college student. 

Let me break it down for you. The rice is bad. The beans are bad. The tortillas are bad. The guac is bad. The chips are bad. The salsa is tasteless. And the whole package is surprisingly expensive. 

Save yourself the trouble and go to Cancun's, Gordo's, Cactus, or the other Gordo's.

a solid 3.5 for sure. I give a 4 because I think the haters aren't playing fair..really folks.  Nice people, friendly atmosphere and a place with heart (just bad parking!).  

 I like the owners attitude  about community and giving back...half off anything on their anniversary day!

When I know I am going to have a long day--with lunch way down the list, I stop and get a breakfast burrito on the way from BART to the campus.  Even eating it later in the morning I have NO complaints...keeps me full until 2:30 or 3:00 when I final can take a lunch break.  Lunch time--fish tacos rock.

Their salsas are wonderful (and sold at various places around town).  Since you can watch everything being made--I don't get the complaints.

Solid, go-to place for me.

Not that bad, but further proof that it is not worth the effort to go out for Mexican food in Berkeley. I agree, best burrito of 1997...in 2007...is nothing to brag about. I should have known when the veggie burrito automatically comes in a spinach wrap - which FYI does not count as a tortilla - or when I saw they had a Thai Wrap on the menu. Yech.

I'm fairly surprised at the comments from other reviewers stating how tasteless the food is here. It truly is not: the salsa is not fresca style, but I can say as a huge salsa aficionado that theirs is the best of all the mexican joints around campus. The main offerings are burritos and every time I've gone here I've gotten the carne asada burrito, which is quite good. Contrary to what other reviewers said, every time I've been here, the ingredients appeared fresh, the food was not dry or bland at all, and the service was good.

The only complaint I have is that the food here is more expensive than say, La Burrita, which has similar quality and taste. I believe for a carne asada burrito with everything on it, it's ~$8.

Even though I've only eaten one item on the menu, I give this place five stars.

For $4.99 (or $5.42ish including tax) one may purchase a #3 aka "huevos revueltos" or some such breakfast burrito. 

This masterpiece include:
Scrambled Eggs
Cajun Potatoes
Cheese
Salsa and/or chiles
Refried Black Beans

Sooo much flavor. It's a fiesta in my mouth, every time. And for those doing a keyword search of places: BEST VEGETARIAN BREAKFAST BURRITO EVER!!!!!
Good, not great burritos in an inexpensive place with reasonable service.

they make a pretty decent nacho platter that definitely used to quell my after-work nacho cravings.  while the nachos here are more expensive than, say, la burrita, there's a hell and heaven difference in quality (in la burrita, you're always wondering whether anyone is intentionally dropping e. coli or salmonella into your food!).  at la cascada, they don't skimp out on guacamole or sour cream, so i'm happy....
I haven't gone to Cascada Taqueria, but I have bought a burrito at Rainbow. The burrito was supposed to have tofu and it didn't. Very disappointed.

I've never had a regular burrito from here, but I *love* their breakfast burrito #3 (eggs, potatoes, black beans, cheeses, salsa).  Their salsa is very tasty too (I like the dark red one).   my friend got the breakfast burrito #1 w/ chorizo and it leaked grease.  that was pretty gross.  anyway, I went there on friday and am disappointed that their prices went up.  boo for inflation.

Delicious and a healthier twist on traditional Mexican food.  They have a variety of tortilla options (whole wheat is my fav) and they do black beans, etc.  But the meat is actually a decent cut and well grilled.  There's no cheese in their burrito's so it's a pretty light refreshing lunch/dinner.

The taco's are HUGE for traditional taquerias.  Just one is enough for a meal for me.
