But -- If you get anything to go, make sure you get it in the plastic (not just the paper bags)   The salsa is too juicy for their paper bags.

They have a lot of creative options, I just haven't gotten to them yet.   :)  

$10 minimum for Credit/Debit
This place has some really great wraps...I like the curry one with peas and chicken. I always get take out and ask for no or less rice.

The texture of my burrito was good. But, the food needed more flavor. And, the diet coke from the fountain didn't work. And, they limit how many salsas you take. But, I really liked the texture of everything and texture is tres important.

ABSOLUTELY HORRIBLE FOOD, literally the worst Mexican food that I have ever eaten. The burrito was 1) COLD 2) had about a tablespoon of meat (barely any) 3) bland taste 4) Horribly long lines

AVOID THIS PLACE AT ALL COSTS

TERRRRRRRIBLE

It's okay, a bit overpriced for me, but they stay open late. It's one of two places  can eat at, so I just alter between the two.

Small portions, and They'd got my order wrong 66% times I've been there.

Actually, I'm gonna take away a star, 66% is a lot. I didn't even think of that...low expectations I guess.

No smiles. Didn't wash hands after eating himself. Flies in the food that sits out all day drying under heated pan. When i asked for black beans i got pinto, i asked him are those black beans and he nodded  then insaid whats that then? '"oh thise must be black beans" DUH. Value is twice for what you are really getting. English please?!

So the first thing I noticed was the nice looking menu.

I'm a sucker for that hand-done look, so I like the ambiance of this place.  And the menu has a pretty good selection.  I ordered a quesadilla loaded, and my friend got some nachos.  She said they give a generous portion, and she wasn't kidding.  

The problem with the chips used is that they seemed like some cheapo brand you'd find in a supermarket.  They were okay, but could have been better.  Other than that, the nachos weren't bad.  My quesadilla was alright.  A bit drippy/sloppy, but eh, I can deal.  

It's a small place, and has a nice location.  Supposedly they have some "best-in-east-bay" burritos, but I'll have to decide on that another time.

As a foreigner from lands far to the East, having never experienced a real burrito before, the food here was, to say the least, a pleasant surprise. Here I was, expecting one of the bland roles of rice and beans that passes for a burrito in my homeland, only to be presented with a tortilla packed with meat, and, and, and flavor! I did write home about them.

Also, the music is totally awesome. I  don't have any idea what they're singing about, but the tunes are awfully catchy.

I come here every Thursday for a breakfast burrito, and occasionally for lunch. The burritos are delicious, and despite what other reviewers have said, I find them large enough to be satisfying. I've never finished my burrito and been left hungry. The staff are very friendly and always greet me by name. The chorizo breakfast burrito is the best, and for lunch I love the beef burrito in the spinach tortilla. The bottom line: good food at a good price with a friendly staff make this a winner in my book.
Good cheap food.  You can get a vegan burrito, just ask for one of the veggie burritos without cheese or sour-cream.  Try the salsa!
Good burritos, great variety, AMAZING salsa... they need to get new chips.

I wasn't overly impressed with the huevos rancheros, but I can't really say why; or what was off... but something just wasn't... quite... on...

My dining companion's breakfast burrito was decent, though apparently it contained an ingredient that wasn't listed on the menu board which is disagreeable to him, so he was a bit displeased by that. In their defense, though, you can't have every ingredient listed on a small chalkboard.

If I were really hungry for a Mexican breakfast and walking past, I'd stop in again, but I can't say I'd make a special trip to return, and it's only two blocks from home.

I got interested in La Casada after chatting with someone from this establishment at the Berkeley Bowl.  He's a distinguished-looking person who seems to exude taste and cultivation.  He comes in to shop every morning before I'm allowed in, but he's usually still there with his cart after the doors open to the public at 9.  He turned me on to fresh dates one day: they're tan and crunchy and are sold with their stalks.  I have no idea how this fellow relates to La Cascada on Center Street.  I've never seen him at that location, so he might be involved only with the College Avenue operation.  I'd like to think that he's the owner.

I really liked La Cascada's fish tacos, but I've maxed out on them and don't want to look at any for a while.  In recent times, I've been ordering their pork burritos, which I consider to be fine.  I absolutely love their thick soup, which tastes more Indian than Mexican to me.  I have no idea whether it's authentic in any way, but my opinion is that it's delicious!

I usually get take-out from this place around dinner time.  I've been in the store a couple of times for lunch.  The place gets totally packed with high school students when Berkeley High lets out for lunch at 11:40 or so.  If you don't like crowds, come either after they leave or at 11:30 -- before they arrive.

I used to live down the street from this incredible taqueria and I must say that I miss it very much. Their breakfast burrito is by far the best I have had and I wish I could have them mail me some in San Diego. They are just that good. I used to get 2 on some days.... one for breakfast and one for my afternoon meal... and I was so happy to have only that for my daily food!!! I can't say that of any other breakfast burrito. The salsa bar is very tasty as well. They also have a great selection and friendly staff... as well as colorful murals on the walls. If you are in the mood for some juice or smoothies they have that too :) A great place to go if you need a good solid place to go for lunch. There is something for everyone here... and it's a great place to people watch as it is right in the center of all the downtown Berkeley action.
Bland.  Shit.

Carne asada burrito goes for $8.

Best burrito in Berkeley?  Perhaps not.  Better than La Burrita?  Definitely.

After living in San Diego, I get periodic, intense cravings for carne asada burritos, so I stopped in.  While the $8 price tag for a burrito w/ guacamole is somewhat ridiculous, it's at least a pretty good burrito.  Nothing was overly greasy and the guac was much better than I was expecting.

I don't think I'll stop in often, but it's good to know that it's there for emergencies.

I came in before the lunch rush. I was checking out the smaller restaurants down on Center and I chose this place since I never noticed it before and I love Mexican food.

Not better than La Burrita.
&Let me tell you why. If you're open, all your dishes should be ready when you're open. I ordered the fish tacos - not ready.

I went to my default chicken burrito with pinto beans. The chicken was dry and there was very little cheese and salsa. Nothing else really.

It was the same size as the La Burrita regular burrito, but came out to about $6.88. What?

The tortilla chips are store bought. WHAT?

There are three kinds of salsa with onions, cilantro, limes, and jalapenos available. None of those salsa choices had fresh tomatoes in it. Fail.

Hmm...This place is truly worthy of 3 stars from my view point. I ordered a veggie burrito, and it came out to $5, + $1 tip = $6..not bad! Literally 1 minute after I paid, the guy is handing me the burrito..I didn't see him make it, maybe I was zoned out? It left me feeling kinda weird and strangely perplexed by how fast they did that. 
    They offer a whole bunch of other stuff on their menu, but I always get veggie burritos. I come home, and I notice they gave me a bit of chips in the bag with the burrito, which were delicious (they were hiding all the way at the bottom!). The burrito had a spinach tortilla, which was actually really yummy. They had salsa, beans, rice, and cheese...I didn't see a whole lotta veggies, or any actually. 
    I'm small, but I eat a lot, and I finished the whole thing in one sitting. I can imagine if a guy friend ate this, he would still feel hungry after. Overall, for $6, pretty good, and I wish they had asked me if I wanted sour cream or guacamole...but next time I'll be sure to ask for it!

I have eaten here a few times and I think it's pretty good. Taquerias can be a bit confusing for me, I always feel rushed, but the ladies who work here are very patient and friendly. I also like the fact there is seating, as so many of them don't have any place to sit. there salsa in the red bottle has a nice kick to it!

It may have been voted best burritos in Berkeley, but it certainly doesn't deserve such a title any more. Average burritos with very basic contents. Breakfast plates that don't even taste like anything because they're so poorly seasoned. Mediocre salsa bar. All of that with a slightly-above-average price tag of about $5-$7 per meal. Like the previous poster, just go to Top Dog.

The food was good. I like them cause I know they use the freshest ingredients. I'm familiar with their products at Whole Foods and Farmer's Market.

It's just not the portions I'm used to. Whenever I go to a traditional Mexican restaurant, the portion sizes are huge, so La Cascada is kind of lacking in that area, but I understand why.

Good burritos. More flavor than most burritos in Berkeley, love the big windows and all the seating. A great place to grab some lunch and people watch. It's too bad they have everything premade, instead of being fresh to order.

I used to love this place back in the late 90's. Now it's just okay.

I was there when they just opened the restaurant, which was more than 10 years ago.  Even then I knew that the Manzanita Prawn Burrito was something special.  The prawns were so juicy.  The tomato tortilla was grilled to perfection.  Since then, I haven't eaten anything else on their menu;  I am committed to the Manzanita Prawn Burrito and nothing else (well maybe the salsa verde too).  Even though it was quite expensive for a starving undergrad ($6.97?), I didn't care.  I often went there after my midterms and finals to treat myself for barely passing my tests (that was a big ass accomplishment.  I majored in science at Cal...I was young and stupid).  Anyhow, I went here today before the Cal basketball game for old time sake.  It is just okay now.  The prawns are not as fresh as back then.  The burrito is obviously smaller.  The salsa verde is still the same.  If yelp existed back then, I would enthusiastically give it 5 stars.  Today, it was more of a 3-star establishment...so I am settling for a 4-star.

Ehhhhh (shrugs).  Well on the plus size it was warm.  The burrito was small and relatively flavorless, the chips weren't that good and the salsa came in two flavors, tepid and nuclear.  It was alright but then I can stay home and microwave a frozen garden burger if I want "alright."

I don't know anything about burritos.. in fact there's a very good chance I had my very first one today at La Cascada Taqueria. I ordered the chile relleno and my friend ordered something veggie but we ended up being served a chicken burrito instead. Luckily it worked out because I apparently do not like chile relleno.
The chicken itself was good and on the whole I liked the burrito. However, it wasn't very warm and most of the salsa fresca was at one end of the burrito, making for a soggy end to the meal. I thought I left with a happy stomach but right now it feels like I ate an entire loaf of bread. Anyway, I must say that this place isn't amazing but it made me happy at the time. And full.

I stop by La Cascada about once a month.  I started coming here because of its convenient location (right between BART and UC), and I've kept coming here because the food is decent, and it's actually a relatively relaxing place to eat.

The staff members are all very nice, and the vegetarian options are pretty good, although most of them aren't true Mexican dishes.
horrible. just horrible. granted that was about 6 months ago, but I would never give it a second chance.

I liked this place a lot when they first opened. Which isn't to say I don't like it now, it's just that it opened 11 years ago and I've sort of moved away. In particular I liked their quesadillas and their terrific guacamole.

Go here if you are about to go work in the fields later in the day or if you have just been gardening or doing any kind of heavy lifting.  Sadly, I don't engage in such activity. In fact, I am mostly in front of a computer during the day.  But, all the same, when I want a hearty meal and feel I haven't eaten something significant in a while I go here.  Truth be told, I used to hate burritos. I hated the tortilla texture, etc.  But since I have gone here I love them. I don't know how much it has to do with this place but I can say that my co workers tease my frequency of this place.  They have frequent buyer cards so if you buy something like 10 you get one free.  I think I have gotten two free burritos by now. I like their chips too!

They used to have free wifi that we mooched for our lunch meetings, but sadly I could not find it today with my iphone.
The menu is a bit limited, but I think this is a get in, eat and get out kinda place. The burritos are okay, but tend to be rather rice heavy and not well mixed. The carnitas aren't bad, but certainly not the best I've had. However, the burritos are a decent size, and with the free fountain drink refills, and the good chips, prepare to be quickly full. Which, for under $7 is not too shabby.
Seating is limited, which at the lunch rush can be a bit tricky. The order fulfillment pace was great so there was hardly a line. Also, the place seemed clean and well maintained which is an all important plus.
Though I thought this place was nice and close to campus, I can't help but to compare it to Cancun on the next block which tastes better, has more seating, and has a more interesting menu.

I first stumbled here with a friend a year ago and did not like it better than La Burrita, my usual hot spot. It certainly did not live up to its name of Berkeley Burrito in Berkeley. 

However, I returned after the Yelp Helps event tipsy and ordered the #4 Machacha(sp?) Breakfast Burrito and devoured it in a matter of minutes. It was absolutely delicious with eggs, carnitas, pinto beans hot off the pan. My company Emily C. ordered the carne asada burrito and it was also very good, but a little bit cold. The green cilantro salsa was perfect with the combination. 

Well, I would have reviewed the joint after the event but I didn't want to let my buzzed conception mislead fellow Yelpers. So after a terrible week of stress, I decided that the remedy to save my day was to try La Cascada Taqueria again. I ordered the same combination and waited in anticipation until I got home to eat it. It was still fresh/hot/flavorful but the cook forgot to add the salsa as part of the burrito so it wasn't as juicy. However, I grabbed two cups of the green cilantro salsa before I left, so all's good. 

I can see how people would rate lowly of this place b/c it is slow sometimes and the burrito gets cold because the ingredients are not warm enough; however, if you order from the breakfast burrito menu, it is guaranteed to be made FRESH anytime of the day. 

Glad to have given this place another chance. This is now officially one of those places I will dream about returning to brighten my day/week.

I like the good, fast service here. The salsas are good and firey enough, except there isn't much towards night time. There are other toppings available too, like cilantro and peppers. Instead of lime, they have lemon wedges. There also aren't many housemade agua frescas. There's usually just horchata and one other agua fresca like strawberry or pineapple. There are lots of bottled drinks in the mini fridge. The menu itself is really straightforward with burritos being the main offering. There are also tacos and quesadillas. There is also a wraps section, but I never order anything from that section. I like that the tortillas used for burritos here are gigantic. It can overlap the super burrito several times or it may just bunch up. Either way, I like tortilla so I don't mind. The tortilla isn't really crispy or anything on the outside. My guy loves the chicken, but I stick with the steak. The fish tacos are great also. It's a good size and fairly priced.

I have to thanks El H. for tipping me off about these folks.....We went to her house for a party that they catered, and based on her review, and our experience, decided to have them cater our Grads and Dads party.  lots of good food and some special flavors hard to find elsewhere.  They were just a little late having everything ready, but it was all great...and on a Sunday afternoon, when other people might have been not willing to have a party for 35 ready to pick up.....thanks mohammed...hope you get some more business from this.

* Please note this is the La Cascada on Center St, not  the one on College Avenue.


Anyway...not impressed at all.

My associate and I recently each had a quick carne asada burrito here before rushing off to a meeting.  I ordered mine with refried beans and he ordered his without.

My burrito was very poorly made.  I don't know if it was ignorance or indifference, but the person who made my burrito didn't even take the care to spread the refried beans when he glopped it in during preparation.  As such, I got a nice, disgusting giant ball of refried bean right in the middle of my burrito.  Even in small portions, the bean was really gross and definitely tasted as though from a can.  In all my years of eating and loving carne asada burritos, I've never had anything like this.  

As if that wasn't bad enough, the portion of meat was very small, had an odd taste and even worse, was chopped up beyond recognition.  Not sure why the meat had to be chopped up so much.

My associate's burrito wasn't much better.  It still had the same dinky portion of over-chopped substandard meat, but without that huge ball glob of refried beans.  As a result, he got a skinny burrito which resembled a soft fat taquito.  Laughably small like WTH?

To add insult to injury, I had tipped the counter person nicely when we placed the order despite the lack of table service.  I don't know if they were having an off day or staffing problems (didn't seem to be), but I know one thing for sure...I'm never going back.

Best Burrito in Berkeley my #ss.  More like worst burrito I've ever had.

Employees seemed indifferent too.  I was going to be kind and give it two stars, but now I'm having giant ball glob of refried bean flashbacks...hence one star.  

Hey, just read another Yelper's review that Best Burrito was in '97!  They really should take that out-dated best burrito sign down.

I'm a birthday party GENIUS!  Overwhelmed at the prospect of hosting 15 girls for my daughter's birthday and having to keep them entertained for 3 hours, I thought "let's just take them to a movie and bring them back to our house for cake." Then I realized that feeding a horde of 8-10 years old girls nothing but theater junk and then topping it off with birthday cake was asking for my home to be destroyed and for tween drama to break out  like pimples. 

Then I thought of my pals at La Cascada.  They've done me right so many times, so I asked if we could descend on them for lunch, go see our movie, and then come back and basically squat there, eat our cake and scare away all their other customers. 

They were totally accommodating - i gave them all the burrito and quesadilla orders in piecemeal - and in case you are unfamiliar with the eating habits of ten year old girls, they can not tolerate standard issue anything. They each had their particular high-maintenance order and La Cascada got them all exactly right - no one's had to be redone.  My carnitas tacos were delicious, by the way, and my friends seemed to be groovin' on their fish tacos.  They kept our cakes and presents for us while we were gone, and then helped set the place back up before the horde descended again.   

Mohammed and crew, thank you once again. You guys are absolute gems in the rough of downtown Berkeley.

I've been spoiled by Oakland taco trucks so Cascada was a total downer, you're better off at Top Dog next door.

Not worth the $6.57
Not worth the time when I could've gone to a better place a few blocks away
Not worth writing more for this review. 

It was more like "Meh" xican

I am convinced that North Berkeley cuisine trumps the ghetto South Berkeley restaurant shacks. Case in point: Vinnie's Cheesesteaks.

I came here one lunch by chance one afternoon when I had planned to go to Urbann Turbann. Like usual, the line was long, so I naturally went into the adjacent restaurant. The decor of the place caught my attention. It's kind of grungy and shack-like, but intentionally and tastefully done (unlike some of the places you'd find around Telegraph). 

The menu is pretty straightforward: cheesesteaks, sandwiches, burgers, and wings. To be honest, the closest thing I've had to a cheesesteak in the Bay Area would either be one from I.B's Hoagies (I loathe that place) or La Burrita's cheesesteak burrito (just asking for post-meal problems). So I naturally ordered a regular Philly Cheesesteak with provolone (not a big fan of cheese-whiz, although I understand that that's how it's originally prepared). 

Although I could write grand words about how amazing it was, quite simply, it was one of the best combinations of meat and bread I've ever had in my life. The beef is so tender that you wouldn't even believe that it was being served in a fast-food joint like this place. The bread is super soft and sops up all the meat juices from the beef. The cheese was glistening and oozing all over the place: simply glorious.

Definitely worth checking out if you're in North Berkeley.

I was brought here by a friend one day after class and was told that it was a good place to eat.  At first glance, I loved the ambiance and the lights inside that spelled out Vinnie's.  It was cool.

I have only tried the wings combo (3 times), which satisfied my craving of good buffalo chicken wings.  The spicy buffalo, buffalo, and the lemon garlic are all delicious.  It comes with a large side of fries along with a drink. This combo will definitely fill you up. 

I have yet to try the philly cheese steaks, but I have heard that they are just mediocre.  I do recommend the wings combo.
How can you go wrong using Niman Ranch meat. Excellent cheese steak and good portion of fries. Better than Cheese Steak Shop at about the same price.

Here you don't have to go to the back of the line if you order wrong.  For those of you that have been to Pat's or one of the authentic place in Philly, especially when drunk at 2 AM, you better know what a "whiz wit" is.  So here, not so authentic, but good quality and tasty sandwhiches.  Organic Niemann ranch meat, good provolone, nice grilled onions.  I like the condiment bar filled with various types of spicy peppers.  I would characterize my one attempt at the fries as a definite miss...they were way over-seasoned with black pepper and not my style.

The staff here is great.  I had a hipster chick on my first visit who really got 2 thumbs up.  Really 3 1/2 stars.  Cheap, good, greasy.

3.5 stars.

Went there once right after they opened. The food was excellent, they have Niman ranch beef. As others have said, the fries seasoned pretty heavily, but they were pretty good, albeit super greasy. This place definitely isn't for the health conscious--even Bongo Burger across the street is probably much healthier. 4 stars for the food.

I feel like a hypocrite because I just docked a star from Urbann Turbann next door for not having any seating, but this place has TOO much seating. It is really cramped. If you are at a table by the wall you literally cannot get up without someone moving. And when they have a line going it is pretty hard to move around. It is a small restaurant, so I'll dock them 1/2 a star.

When i came here, i ordered a cheesesteak with cheese whiz and for my first cheesesteak experience, i enjoyed it. I thought the steak was a little tough and there wasn't enough on my sandwich, but it was good. The fries were also pretty good. I would come back again if i was in the mood for a cheesesteak.

I came here for a Monday night dinner with my boyfriend a few weeks ago. He loves cheesesteaks and IB Hoagies, so we decided to give this Northside alternative a try! 

I got the chicken avocado with curly fries and my boyfriend got the classic cheesesteak with garlic fries. When I first received my meal, my eyes were ecstatic - I am a sucker for presentation and color and my sandwich just looked so good! However, I was unfortunately disappointed as I took more bites of the sandwich. 

It was filling, but not as flavorful as others I've had. I think it could do with some more sauce of some sort. My boyfriend was not very satisfied with his meal either. Vinnie's is okay, but I think we may just stick to IB's.

The arrival of Vinnie's Cheesesteaks filled a nice niche on UC-Berkeley's northside. Before Vinnie's, there was nowhere to get good American junk food on the northside. Top Dog is close, but doesn't have the selection that Vinnie's does (cheesesteaks, hamburgers, fries, onion rings, wings, etc.). You'll probably pay between $6.50 and $8 to get full. Vinnie's is one of the dwindling number of near-campus restaurants that take credit card without a minimum.
Honestly Iv'e tried the wings here and it was the best I ever had since i was in New York! Perfect size! and they have an option to put Hot or Unbeliveably Hot!!!

As promised, went back for a burger and thoroughly enjoyed.  Right at 6 bucks for a bacon cheeseburger.  Cooked to order and ready in about 5 minutes.  Nice sized patty, soft bun, slightly crispy bacon, melty cheese all perfectly balanced.  Great to finally have a place  nearby when in the mood for a burger on Northside.

I've been looking for a good place with a good philly, and Vinnie's was my next stop.

Standard (aka small) but it's done right. I've had Philly Cheesesteaks in other cities and it's the closest I've gotten to a real philly since moving to CA a few months ago. I would recommend getting fries (garlic, curly, or just regular) because the philly is not enough, unless you have the appetite of a 5 year old, then it might suffice.

They also have a surcharge of 30 cents for debit/credit cards, so grab cash if you want to avoid that.

This is a great eating option if you're on the North side of campus. I went in there thinking about getting on the chicken wrap but once there saw that the cheeseburger looked really good. I wasn't disappointed. The buns where soft and spongy. The cheese, onion, tomato and lettuce made it that much better. One of the best burgers around. They also have this condiment station with peppers with some really good jalapenos. 

The fries were really good too. To me they tasted like homemade fries. Like when you make homemade fries and their starchiness makes them get stuck together. Next time I might get the garlic fries which seem to be crowd favorites. 

The drinks were kind of flat though. not the best.

Even thought I ordered a hoagie cheese steak, but actually got a cheese steak - it was still hella good.  The steak was very flavorful - like real steak.  I did not love the garlic fries (possibly because I've recently had the BEST garlic fries at Gregoire).  The fries were not very garlic flavored.  The service was friendly and quite fast.  I will return, but the next time will make sure they get my order correct, sans fries.  Good eating everyone! :)

Cheap and delicious philly cheesesteaks! Staff is very friendly and the fries are freakin` exceptional! You can get a decent meal for under 10 bucks. 

Recommend coming here for a quick lunch!

The sign is a bit outrageous, a little old las vegas style with the bulbs forming the letters, kinda cool. 

The food here is decent, the bbq wings aren't particularly great and I wouldn't recommend them, but the fries were good. They are more potato wedge than french fry so if you don't like potato wedge style fries then this place is no good.

I had the pizza steak which was ok, the meat wasn't very succulent and my bun fell apart and split halfway while eating my cheesesteak. So I wasn't exactly enthused by the quality of their ingredients. 

The place is nice though, the people who run it were very nice people, they got us what we needed in a timely manner and even gas us some extra cheese even though we didn't pay for it. 

If you want cheesesteak in Berkeley, this is the place to be because it's one of the few places to be.

Great lunch spot! I love the minimalist atmosphere. 

Finally, Northside has a cheesesteak restaurant and I don't have to walk all the way to Southside. There seems to be even more meat than the sandwiches from IB's even. The only complaint I have is that there is so much grease on the sandwiches that my bread was soggy at the end, but that's ok, and probably could've been avoided if I held the sandwich upright. 

Definitely get the Orange Creme soda for your drink. It was like drinking a cremesicle! Very good!

Vinnie's is the best Cheesesteak restaurant in Berkeley.  It really exposes the low quality of IB's by providing a positive and resolutely superior example.  I had the standard Cheesesteak and it was very good, with appropriate portions and proportions.  My only complaint is that the steak itself is sometimes chopped too fine, resulting in a loss of moisture.  Tastykake is always a bonus.

Just alright, although maybe I was too tired from and nervous about finals to focus on the food. I got the chicken parmesan, which was simply crispy chicken with melted cheese and tomato sauce on a sandwich roll. Pretty filling, tasty but not spectacular. Had some fries from my friend, which were decent as well. Not a place I would actively seek out or find myself craving, given the other choices on Northside. Cool decor, though.

I live right up the street, so it's nice to have more variety in the neighborhood.  The food is good, reasonably priced and the service is usually good and fast.  Today the tattooed girl took my order was about as sincerely friendly as you'll ever find - which prompted me to write this review.  I hope the manager or owner reads this and treats her accordingly.

Okay 4 *'s is probably a little generous, but this place is definitely better than the average of 3.

It's the middle of the afternoon and I inexplicably find myself totally famished.  My esteemed colleagues had been raving about this place, so decided to check it out.

I dig the decor, except for the flies buzzing around in the middle of the place.  Or maybe they're part of the ambiance, like the neat vintage postcard lampshades and ridiculously huge "VINNIES" in lights. The cashier seemed pretty out of it...he wanted to give me an extra dollar in change, and during my wait I witnessed him forgetting a dude's drink order twice.

Anyway small details aside, cheese steak with provolone was so SO delicious.  Loaded mine up with those fun lookin hot peppers organized by color (did you know capsaicin releases endorphins?)

The first time you get an order to go, turn around and assemble your hot pepper containers while you're waiting.  Don't just sit there like a dummy like I did.

I just came back from my second visit here. I didn't have a positive impression after my first visit here, but there was a long line at La Val's tonight. Being a Sunday night, most places are closed on the north side, so I decided to try this place again. The hot wing combo looked pretty good, but I feel over-charged for less than advertised. The sign and menu claim the combo is $6.59, but I was charged $6.95 before tax (it occurs to me now as I write this that perhaps they manually enter the price and the employee entered the last two digits backwards). The menu also advertises that the hot wings come with celery and carrots--I didn't get either. I got ~10 hot wings with some fries. They were okay, but I would rather have spent my money elsewhere. If I'm going to be unhealthy, I would rather go to Chipotle or Top Dog. It was fairly crowded for a Sunday night, so maybe their strategy of doing something unique (cheesesteaks/etc) will work out for them. I wish their neighbor Urban Turbann were open Sunday nights--much better value for $7.

As I write this review, I notice someone has uploaded a photo of hot wings with celery and carrots--maybe the workers on Sun nights just don't know what they're doing or the guys tonight were new.
Pretty legit philly cheesesteaks, as far as I know. Service is fast and friendly. Good place to grab lunch between classes.

Vinnie's Cheesesteaks serves up cheesesteaks [yay captain obvious]. It's hard to find a great cheesesteak [disclaimer: I haven't had chicago or ny style, so I can't guarantee that what I'm possibly looking for is "original"].  But you don't really find anything better in Berkeley. IB's on south side does have them, but they're not that great.

This place has an interesting style, and I don't have much to say otherwise.  Their 'steaks are okay - not bad but nothing I'd seek out or care to go back often.  Bring a friend and share an order of fries [as noted in other reviews]; I ended up carrying around a half-box of fries.

You might like it. You might not. You might be like me and think it's A-OK.

I recently took a trip to Philadelphia, where the locals informed me that a true Philly cheese steak must have cheez-whiz, american, or very cheap provolone on it. So, extra star for authenticity? Still gross, but if authenticity is important to you, go for it.

Pro:  Niman Ranch beef is a great choice.  Better than Steak-Eze used at most shops.  

Really inexpensive garlic fries for the amount you get.  Really good and fresh!

No cross-contamination with the veggie sangwiches, separately grilled.  Had the mushroom steak once, and it was everything herbivores are looking for.  My vegan sister was happy with the portabella mushroom sandwich with no cheese.

Good atmosphere, a little dim sometimes though.  

Con: Only offers 7" steaks.
Amazing homemade fries. Light, crispy, not greasy. True love. and i am picky about my fries.

This place really adds some variety to North Side. Cheap mexican food, cheap burgers, and cheap asian food is a plenty, but you can't get Cheesesteaks anywhere on Northside, or even Berkeley (that I know of). That being said, I got the mushroom cheesesteak with some fries and I really enjoyed it. Pretty good size portions, good ingredients, and it doesn't hurt that the place itself looks pretty nice. 

I'd definitely come here again.
Mmmmmmm. You have got  to try this place.  Excellent cheesesteaks. High quality ingredients.  I go here at least once a week.
Tried to place an order to go and got hung up on 3 times.  I'm giving up and going somewhere else...
Scratch my previous entry about the cheesesteak sandwich.. I know this is a cheesesteak spot, but I recently fell in love with their grilled cheese sandwiches. You should too ;)

YESSIR! 
This hits the spot after a long day work.  I am in the middle of destroying their BBQ WINGS right now.  10 wings, fries(go garlic or go home) and a drink for $5.99!  Wings are crispy, fully cooked and BLOW WINGSTOP OUT OF THE WATER!

Im a fan of the Chicken Cheese Steak w/ Mushrooms.  

And for the Veggie folks, no worries, of the meat mixing in . . .

Check this spot out for sure foodies!

Update: 
The Philly cheesesteak is meh. The only redeeming thing are there fries. Too bad there isn't a one and half star.  


The Buffalo wings are scrawny. They were perfectly cooked, but $7 for 9 tiny wings wasn't worth it.

I am not from Philly, which may disqualify me, but (1) cheesteaks are very good,  (2) fries are good if you order without the black pepper added, and (3) guys who work there are good guys.  Good prices.  I'll be back.
I ate here at least once a week when I lived in Berkeley. Do yourself a favor and check it out.

OHHH SOOO GOOD!!! I literally went here everyday for an entire week, when I first found out about it. The Philly Cheese Steaks are amazing!! Don't bother getting it with mushrooms, because you end up paying extra money for like 5 slices of mushroom. Also make sure you get it with CHEEZ WHIZ! Yeah, I know, I was wary of it too, but I decided to give it a go, and wow, it makes a difference (they also offer American and Provolone, but neither of them stand a chance against the whiz). They also have a little pepper bar, with different kinds of peppers, I usually get the big jalapeno slices, but don't add too many (they're aren't spicy at all, but it takes away from the flavor of the meat/cheese/bread). If you want spice, I recommend some Sriracha sauce on that steak, it adds the perfect kick. (just know that I am extremely biased towards Sriracha sauce haha).

I've also had the Crispy Chicken Sandwich which was equally as good as the cheese steak for days when you feel like something different. It's like a HIGH QUALITY version of the tendercrisp at BK (don't let that description steer you away, cuz it really is good). It comes on Hoagie bread with a huge slab of freshly fried chicken, mayo, lettuce, tomatos, and onions.

Also, do not, I repeat, DO NOT forget to get some garlic fries. They are so good! For only $2 you get an entire box full ($.50 extra for ranch, which I say is a must have with garlic fries).

This place is also one of the very few places in Berkeley that actually takes DISCOVER yay!! They also take AMEX for those of you who like to use that.

Make sure you don't around lunch time, cuz it is PACKED, you can't move an inch without bumping into at least 6 people. I've found that the best time is to go around 2 or 3pm, when it's completely empty.

Pretty good cheesesteak and a huge order of fries for the price. Fries could be better though, especially because to go orders of fries come in a plastic box. They stand no chance in that steam room...they would do much better in a paper bag.

I'm amused by the early comments on "cross-contamination" by vegetarians. First of all, maybe a cheesesteak restaurant wasn't the best call to begin with. Second, I guarantee that this happens more often than you know, because fat is delicious and the best, most delicious, fat comes from tasty little piglets and sweet succulent veal cows. Cooks tend to know this, and thus the sauteed vegetables you had w/ your meal may have shared the same area of the grill as this guy's sausage/bacon/steak etc. At least I hope so...because that's how I want my vegetables cooked. I guess this place is a bit different, simply because you can see it happen.

It's pretty good but it just makes everything harder because there now too many places to choose from on northside when I want quick and cheap food. 

Such a rough life.

This place is o.k. I came here a few times in the summer when it first opened and I was kind of disappointed. The cheesesteaks are a bit on the small size, and the normal fries are pretty bad (soggy and salty). I also tried the chicken parmasean and that took an inordinately long time to cook. If you're craving cheesesteaks, go to I.B.'s on South Side, or if you want a quick meal just go to La Val's (which is owned by the same guy anyways) or one of the other nearby places.

Went here for lunch between classes the other day and luckily I ordered right before the lunch rush.

I split the Mushroom Chicken Cheesesteak (given that I don't eat beef), fries, and a drink with a friend.

Overall, the sandwich is extremely messy, as the bread got soggy from the juices and everything began to fall apart. But besides that, the place was pretty good. I wish there was more flavor to the sandwich, but it was pretty good considering the price (~$8).

Would I go again? Sure. Am I crazy ecstatic? Not so much.

Okay, my caveat, I don't like cheesesteaks, so if you want to know about those, read someone else's review. If you want to know french fries and grilled cheese though, I'm your girl...

Grilled Cheese. With Tomatoes. Need I say more? Oh, how I love a grilled cheese with tomatoes that have been heated ON THE GRILL. Yum yum yum!!  Inexpensive, which is fantastic. I think I'll ask next time if I can get mushrooms added on, because that would be fantastic...

The french fries were, um, plentiful. It's seriously the hugest order of fries I've gotten in a long time. I went back two days later (for yes, another grilled cheese), and I noticed their french fries containers were much smaller, but that first trip, wow, that was a lot of fries. They are way too heavily seasoned though, which was definitely a problem. Hopefully they'll fix that soon...

The staff is quick, and there are about six or eight tables there, but I think they are planning on the to-go crowd mostly. When the line is long, it's hard to get out, but you can squeeze through. The placement of the pepper table means there's not a lot of room for waiting for your food order, but I imagine we'll all get used to it eventually. And for the grilled cheese, I'll certainly be back many times.

First legit version of the Philly Cheesesteak to hit the East Bay. And I am THE AUTHORITY, as I grew up back there.

So the first thing I notice when I go here, is that the owner has great attention to detail (highly doubt there is an actual 'Vinnie' behind this business as I think it's just the quintessential I-talian name to use). From the tiled PHL that sits above the grill, to the Tastykakes, Hank's Root Beer, and Utz chips - "Vinnie" is trying to give the Berkeley folks a taste of the old country. And for the most part, he does a really good job.

First and foremost, let me say that the people over at Vinnie's competition - The Cheesesteak Shop chain, which has invaded the Bay, like some sort of disease - this place does a horrible job at representing the cheesesteak. This is mainly due to the fact that they barely give you any meat. And what they do give you, is not shredded, but really more like ground steak - really bad, people. Get a mini, or  a small sandwich, and it's all bread. Get the half, which is supposed to have more meat, and I swear that it just looks like a bigger bun, that's all. So this place never hit the mark, and has been deceiving California people for years now. So sad.

So Vinnie's is a lot better, but I do have some constructive criticism for these guys:

1. Stop portioning out the quantity of meat. The grill-master pulls what look like carefully measured "balls" of steak out of a tray. What the F$#@ is this sh*t? A true cheesesteak shop has a grill FULL OF MEAT at all times. And that way, when you waltz in there, it's ready to go. 
Vinnie is doing the customers NO FAVOR by cooking these to order. As a matter of fact, I would argue they are doing a dis-service, because why should I wait 15-20 mins for a cheesesteak? Also by doing this measuring (on the smaller side), you don't get a roll full of meat. You get the 4 ounces, or whatever it is that they measure. Kind of lame, guys. If you had a grill full of meat, then the guy making the sandwiches would just scoop and fill the roll - the way it should be. Bottom line: STOP BEING CHINCEY!

2. They only have one size of sandwich, instead of the Philly usual- a "half" and a whole (not truly a half; just think small and large). That way, if I want more sandwich, I could order the BIGGER one. I will pay the couple bucks more, instead of what, having to order TWO small ones? Come on, now.

Somewhere in one of these other reviews there was mention of 'Niman Ranch beef', but after going here, I saw no signs or information to back up this claim, so I don't believe it. If they were really using beef of this caliber, there would be signs up, since that's a selling point in Berkeley.

But as far as taste, the cheesesteak is great. They import the de facto roll standard from Philly - Amoroso's rolls, and offer American or Provolone cheese, or the 'cheese whiz'.

But about the whiz, let me say this:

Cheese Whiz only came about in the last 25 years, people, and is NOT the way most Philadelphians eat their sandwich. But for some reason, all the damn tourists to the area think this is the way it is. WRONG. Although many people think of this as the standard for the cheesesteak, this is a newer phenomena. Where I grew up (the REAL South Philly), it was always American or Provolone cheese. 

And about the guy who expressed concern about cross-contamination and vegetarians - you're an idiot. Any true vegetarian (I was a militant vegan for 8 years) would not even step foot inside this place, and would likely walk on the other side of the street to avoid the wafting smell of frying beef. Somehow I don't see many people ordering the veggie burgers here.

This is the only place in the immediate East Bay (Berkeley, Oakland, surrounding environs) to get a good cheesesteak. For those who love The Cheesesteak Shop - just stay over there, as I don't want the additional traffic to compete with at Vinnie's.

This is where heart attacks happen.

I tried both the mushroomsteak with provolone and the phillysteak with whiz. Both were pretty awesome but I would have to say the phillysteak with whiz was my favorite. Tasty well seasoned meat and the whiz added that extra oomph. Who knew whiz cheese would be that good?! Also ordered regular fries and garlic fries...one order is definitely enough to share. Perfect amount of garlic...yum!

Great addition to Euclid!

I've tried this place twice now, praying that the first time was a fluke.  This place is ok, but just ok.  I tried the cheese fries, which is a lot of food for two bucks, but they're overseasoned and the cheese they use tasted like melted down american cheese that sets way too fast.  It's ok if you're a fan of american cheese, I guess, but american is probably my least favorite cheese ever.  It would be nice if there was a choice to the type of cheese for your cheesy fries.  

I've tried two different cheesesteaks from here, the pizza and the philly.  Now I don't know "traditional" because I've never been to philly, but I've had cheesesteak before and I know what I like when it comes to them.  Where's the cheese on these things?  Both times i've eaten here there has been a noticable lack of cheesyness to my cheesesteaks.  In all this place is oh so forgettable.  I have heard good things about the wings, maybe I'll come back one last time to try them, but I'm done eating here for their namesake.

Bumping up Vinnie's to 4 stars after having the wings combo. The wings combo is a great deal at $5.99. It comes with 10 wings, fries, and a drink. There are a few different choices for sauces ranging from mild to incredibly hot and a bbq option. It also comes with your choice of ranch or blue cheese dressing. 

I had my wings with hot sauce and ranch. The wings were made fresh to order, no sad, soggy wings that have been sitting under a heating lamp here. Nice amount of meat on each wing with the perfect amount of sauce. The sauce didn't taste particularly hot to me, but I still enjoyed the slight kick. Fries were not overly seasoned like last time so that was definitely a plus. 

I'll be frequenting Vinnie's for lunch as long as they keep offering the wings combo!

Thank god for vinnies, berkeley doesn't have enough of this american grease comfort food. Cheaper than bongo burger and better than IB's, with really really good prices. If only it were on southside..

This is a vegetarian review. If you don't care about vegetarian items, skip this! 

I went there on Monday the 21, the second day they were open. I really enjoyed the tofu steak sandwich I had with provolone.  However, while preparing the food, the cooks used the SAME utensils for the vegetarian items as the meat items. Totally gross feeling watching that happen, despite the sandwich. I then proceed to tell both of the cooks that this is a bit inappropriate to cook that way because it defeats the purpose of ordering a vegetarian meal.

When they BOTH looked at me with blank stares, I said "Listen, I'm really not trying to be jerk, but when you mix the way you cook things, it defeats the purpose of calling that tofu vegetarian". They barely acknowledged me, and didn't even offer to make me another sandwich.


If they fix these issues, I'll be back. Otherwise, sheesh veggies, stay away!

edit: Adam H. sounds like he works there. No posting history before this one, style of the post sounds just a little too informative.
Absolutely incredible cheesesteak one of the best I have ever eaten I am sold
The best most intense garlic fries. Delicious sandwiches, veg options & friendly folks. Cool ambiance & decor

oops.. this was written july of 2010 but for some reason didn't post it then. 

3rd time stuffing my with a sandwich from this place.  The cheesesteaks are on point. Niman ranch beef is flavorful and tender. No gristle at all.  Felt like they put even more meat this time than last.  

Chicken parmesan was good too.  Chicken breast is often too dry, but this was tender. crispy on the outside ... I think it's fried twice. 

I've never seen flies, and the decor is fitting for a cheesesteak place --simple, urban, with the food being prepared in plain view behind the counter. 

Only gripes are that they don't offer longer cheesesteaks, and the cashier acts like she really doesn't want to be there.  Even a fake smile would be better than the miserable attitude she had.

I love cheap and delicious lunch combos! They have 10 hot wing combo with french fries and drink for $6!!  What a deal!!  A ton of food for cheap! Thanks Bonita L for telling me about it! 

Okay that's enough exclamation points.  But really this is a great lunch place.  I like the pickled jalapenos, cherry tomatoes, peperocini they have on the side.

I found myself on Northside yesterday with 1.5 hours to spare before my next class and an empty stomach. I ventured into Vinnie's Cheesesteaks not knowing what to expect, and hoping that I'd be able to grab a quick, cheap, and tasty lunch.

The first thing you notice before walking in are the specials posted outside. Today they had:

-an Italian sandwich special for 5.99 that included a drink and a bag of Lays chips
-a chicken wing special for 5.99 that included 10 wings and a drink and fries

I got the sandwich combo and the boyfriend got the chicken wings.
The sandwich combo came out relatively quickly. I was disappointed to find that it was a cold sandwich with just french bread, some type of vinegary dressing, lettuce, cheese, and some Italian cold cuts. Seeing as that I was at a cheesesteak place I thought I would be getting something that was warm and toasty. The sandwich wasn't memorable, and I think I could have grabbed something similar at Cheese n' Stuff on Southside for half the price. But the portions were decent and the sandwich was nicely cut in half to share.

The wings took a while to arrive, but they were hot and fresh when we got them. You can choose from mild to spicy flavoring for your wings, and a choice of sauce (ranch or blue cheese). We got mild wings and ranch dressing. The wings tasted too artificial, but with a generous dipping of some ranch, tasted decent. The fries were thick cut and perfectly seasoned (I didn't find them to be overseasoned like some of the other reviewers :) ). Again, the portions were generous for the pricing, but the taste was average.

Vinnie's has a nice bathroom and nice decor, and it is relatively clean. The huge Vegas-style sign is a nice touch!

All in all, Vinnie's was worth a try, but I wasn't impressed by their sandwich or wings. I intend to give their cheesesteaks a try soon! (Who knows, maybe they'll be better than IB's!)

Vinnie's has a dozen varieties of cheesesteaks. One size (7") and all under $6. Also, burgers, some hot sandwiches (chicken / eggplant parm, etc)  a couple of cold hoagies http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WyzBDqBtqdbH3J0V2w9R6g?select=4UIu-BlPB7m0NuJ3PAXl-A) as well as wings (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WyzBDqBtqdbH3J0V2w9R6g?select=G7ZuTUgria7WKMzO1ljFuw). They do the whole "authentic Philly" thing with imported Amoroso rolls, Hank's Root Beer, and the occasional Tastykake sighting.

I pretend to be a purist and have stuck with the Classic which has onions, peppers, and choice of cheese (Whiz, American, or Provolone (my choice))

As my 3 star indicated, Vinnie's is A-OK. Could be better, but somewhat inconsistent. Seems like I get more meat when I eat in (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WyzBDqBtqdbH3J0V2w9R6g?select=nIauBJXypCuqL92V1cGraA) vs. to go (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WyzBDqBtqdbH3J0V2w9R6g?select=hk94Uaa_Tk5F1rTzIsvn5Q), there's sometimes a gristly bite or two, and the meat is also inconsistently seasoned visit to visit. The skin on fries come pre-seasoned with salt & pepper (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/WyzBDqBtqdbH3J0V2w9R6g?select=QA_6I31fQ0E9DT4iR312nQ) which I like, but can be limp. 

Friendly staff.

Note: if there was no "cross contamination," they wouldn't be using the grill and utensils correctly. 

It's not Philly, but if you hold the peppers you'll get a proper experience of Brotherly Love. Sit at the counter and watch those spatulas work the meat. The Niman Ranch meat changes the traditonal texture (there is a risk of gristle with that kind of meat), but it's still correctly gooey and served on the right kind of roll. 

Good job

I'm a Cheesesteak Shop devotee, so when I found myself in the Northside neighborhood recently I figured I'd try out the new Vinnie's place. It's certainly a different experience than the cheesesteaks I'm used to. I liked it a lot. I had the mushroom steak with white American cheese (not a fan of whiz or other kinds of 'cheez'). Garlic fries were tremendous both in quantity and quality. The Niman Ranch gives the sandwich a really beefy flavor (I know, descriptive right?) that I liked a lot. A little hot sauce, some peppers, and the sandwich is just right, the meat is seasoned really well and the rolls are awesome.

-1 to the losers who show up to a restaurant on its 2nd day ever and complain that everything in the kitchen isn't perfect.

And -1 to Vinnie's for spelling 'provolone' wrong on the menu and still not having fixed it after like a month or so.

Anyway, good price, good service, good food, I'll be back at Vinnie's for sure.

A cheese steak hoagie with provolone and no tomatoes along with a tiny, adorable cup of water costs $6.35.

This sandwich rivaled that of the one made in the cafeteria I lived next to during my first year in college.  That's not to say that it was a bad sandwich, it just so happens that there was one guy in that cafeteria who made a damn good, greasy, steaky sandwich on the cheap.

Back on point, the prices are high for the amount of food, and I don't understand why places that serve Niman Ranch beef advertise it like you'll see Cow Jesus if you eat their beef.  Whatever--at least it's tasty in its baffling pretentiousness.

I'm going 4* instead of 3* because the dudes in there were friendly, on-task, and competent.  That deserves points.

Let's just say I am not very impressed with this place. I was in there tonight (Sunday) night and it wasn't too busy but steady traffic of customers. Nothing 2 guys couldn't handle...  

The food was okay, needed more cheese on the cheesesteak, I mean it is a CHEESEsteak. I saw no PA snacks (utz or wise chips, tastykakes) as described in other posts, Lays and coke only. 

The service was ridiculous. Beyond ridiculous.
1. The water container was out and they didn't re-fill it the entire time I was there. They filled my cup from the sink. 
2. ALL the ketchup bottles were empty, completely empty. They gave me ketchup packets instead of just filling the bottles. 
3. The real kicker- 3 buddies of the guys who were working came in and got free food! They didn't pay for anything and they all got fries and cheesesteaks. Come on, why don't you spend your time filling the water and ketchup bottles for the customers who PAID for their meals... 

I don't think I will return.

I ordered the hoagie cheesesteak and it was hot and yummy wrapped in one of those Costco foil-looking papers. They have three different cheeses: whiz (thick liquidy mix), provolone, and american.

Set up is simple. Big menu on the right side as you walk in and a sitting bar area with different kinds of peppers. There were whole and chopped cherry peppers, jalapenos, and pepperoncini.

I thought the bun could have tasted better and it seemed like something was missing. Like, I got the mushroom steak once and I asked if there were mushrooms in it.. they're dark so i guess i could have missed it too, but you couldn't really taste them. Overall, it's a nice joint to get a quick cheesesteak, but nothing too special

I actually had no intention of eating here but the food smelled so good, I couldn't resist. But I wish I had. 

The garlic fries were a little underseasoned and could have used some extra garlic but tasted pretty good overall. The meat on the cheesesteak could've been taken off the grill a little quicker, but it was also well within the realm of deliciousness. They had the usual options for cheese: cheesewiz, provolone, and american. If I were rating the food alone, Vinnie's would've gotten 4 stars, possibly even 5. But the wait time brings Vinnie's way way down. 

We came in on Friday night and waited over half an hour for a cheesesteak + fries. I appreciate the care in which they cook, but producing one cheesesteak every 5 mins makes this a horrible place for large groups (the first people to order are done by the last ones are still waiting for their food) and for anyone looking to get out of here in an hour.  It also means your fries get cold. From what I can tell, the problem was that the cook was only grilling enough meat for one cheesesteak at a time. Perhaps with some time, they'll learn to become more efficient, but until then, I'll stick to Phat Philly in the mission.

Just a quick update:

Today, after ordering the Crispy Chicken combo to go, I left Vinnie's, although I noticed that they used a slightly different togo box. Halfway back to my building, one of the friendly Vinnie's employees comes running up and taps me on the shoulder - they forgot to give me my fries.

How many restaurants show that kind of dedication to service? Seriously! 

I love Vinnie's.

So I've noticed a lot of complaints about cross-contamination, which is a concern for vegetarians. HOWEVER, they actually rectified this issue a few days after opening and now use a separate frying pan. I'm vegetarian, and did not have any concerns with the way my food was prepared. This place is awesome! The decorations are really cool, and there is plenty of seating. I like the bar seating and the arrow outside is pretty cool too.

I got the mushroom pizzasteak because the cashier recommended it out of the veggie options. The price is fantastic. The food was good, but they forgot to put the pizza sauce on which makes a world of difference. I reminded the cook and he apologetically put some on (no worries! We all space sometimes...)

Anyway, I felt the need to write a review because no one has noticed their beneficial change in separating cooking dishes from meat and veggie options!

Vegetarians- no need to fear anymore!

Next time I'd love to try the garlic fries!

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came for my Monday lunchday and was ready to get my grub on. They have a cute sign outside that points to their store, which is what I stared at for 10 minutes while waiting for my friend.

This place sees a lot of people during the lunch hour, many of whom look like engineers (haha jk, or not). You place your order and take a seat at their 10 or so tables, or mill to the right side of the counter to wait for your order. They have a large grill in the back where they cook your meat. And after reading a fellow Yelper's review, I was saddened to see that yes, they do portion the servings of meat per order. Tear.

To your left are three jars with pickled peppers. Pickled peppers pickled peppers! So fun to say hahaha. There is also a soda machine with cups next to it for water. You have the option of adding fries and a soda to any sandwich for $1.75 more.

Food took about 8 minutes to be served.

|| F O O D ||

CLASSIC CHEESESTEAK: steak, carmelized onions, bell peppers, and your choice of cheese on an Amoroso roll [$5.49]
- Opted for the provolone cheese, which I was glad I did! I actually wish they had given me more than two measly slices of cheese though. The melted cheese tasted really good.
- NOT ENOUGH STEAK BOOOO. It filled up half of max capacity, and my bun look miserably alone until I piled on some peppers (which I regretted because their flavor is too sharp for me) and a dash of ketchup. The steak was well cooked though, and had a good smoky flavor.
- Wish there could have been more onions. :c
- The Amoroso roll was great! The dough was soft and the exterior was slightly crispy, and it had its own wonderfully starchy taste. Mmmmmm.

VEGGIE STEAK: mushrooms, carmelized onions, bell peppers, lettuce, tomato, pickles and mayo on an Italian roll with fresh sliced avocado [$5.49]
- Stuffed! Didn't try it, but it looked good. My friend said it was okay.

GARLIC FRIES: [$2.19]
- Not a full order since my friend got the combo, but they were yummy! Crispy and salted, with a heap of chopped garlic and parsley on top. Good stuff!

|| C L O S U R E ||

Go for the provolone cheese. The steak is good, but the cheesesteak is not filled with meat and is partially filling. The peppers are sharp, and the garlic fries are good. Tasty cheesesteak at a great price, but with their portions (and nutrition), I would probably go for a sandwich at the Stuffed Inn if I had a choice.

This was a perfectly balanced experience.  The stellar and the mediocre.  I fell in love with the seasoned fries they served.  Both portion and taste.  The fried chicken sandwich left much to be desired though.  The bread's size did nothing to detract from the small pieces of chicken, the faintest glimmer of mayo, and the most meager onion bits I have seen on a sandwich in recent times.  

I did, however, dig the interior design of the place.  I wish I was just more impressed by my sandwich.

Bad dining hall; sure there is a lot of variety, but they repeat things every week or multiple times in a week that it all lacks any long term variety. The international flavors section only varies between Mexican and Asian themed food, and occasionally a potato bar. Surely there are more 'world flavors' than that? No good.

I dormed at Clark Kerr my freshman year, so I never really had a chance to eat at Crossroads, but whenever I did, I was never too satisfied. Sure, there is definitely a LOT more variety than the CKC dining hall, but quality wise, it wasn't that great.

I only go to Crossroads for late night, which is, by far, the place most college kids go to if they're intoxicated and want to sober up (I've seen many inebriated college students show up after 1am, looking for something to satisfy their cravings). Their buffalo wings are a must-have, and their clam chowder is really good too. 

Only go here for late night, but if you want a good dinner, I suggest you go elsewhere since the food here won't leave you satisfied.

I've had good and bad days here, but today wasn't goo. I felt that two of the three staffers were pretty aloof today. Maybe they had some kinds of bad staff meeting or something, geez.

They have lots of great purses here.

For a campus cafeteria, this place is decent. Just that. The variety of food that they offer is pretty good but that statement is only valid for about the first hour of food service. Because the place is open for 4.5 hours for dinner, after the first hour, all the food that you see on the menu online is no longer availabe. The only things that you can count on being here is pizza, salad, and soup.

A lot of the food that you find here is pretty unhealthy... You can go online to check the facts but it's not hard to notice when you're eating it. TONS of the food that they have here is deep fried, like fried fish, fried chicken, french fries, fried falafal balls, etc. The food here is always either underseasoned or overseasoned and neither is ever good. I'm not a vegetarian, but I know that their vegetarian options are very limited and what they do offer is disgusting. It's always some sort of vegetable stew or something similar that looks like it was thrown together in about two seconds (literally. chef opens bag of veggies. boils in water. takes out. pours on some kind of sauce. puts it under the heat lamp).

The frozen yogurt that they have here, I'll give a pass. It's there, but being from a mix, it's often too sweet and there's nothing you can really do about it. The desserts that are served usually sit around for wayyy too long so I can't really guess how they taste out of the oven since I always get something that's stale and dry.

For those that don't have a meal plan, the pricing is pretty bad. If you want a lot of food, I would recommend going to Kip's during happy hour and grabbing three dishes instead of visiting Crossroads.

The utensils that they have here are the nasties. I know it sounds crazy and your friends might laugh at you but bring your own utensils. Seriously. If you use a cup there, make sure you wash it out a few times with the beverage you're about to drink. A few times, I looked at the cups that came out of the dish room and you could clearly see that there were soap suds on them... Nasty....

Go somewhere else for a better meal.

Oh, the memories...

From Screwdriver Sundays to Finals Fridays, Crossroads was there for my first year of college. 

My digestive system thanks me for moving out of the dorms (and away from 2am mozzarella sticks), but I certainly miss feeling at home eating in public in my jammies.

5 stars go to the 100% organic salad bar and their wide array of vegan offerings! Yum yummmmm. It's $10 if you aren't a student with a meal plan, but if you're smart you can get a friend to swipe their card for you! For a school cafeteria, this is the bees knees.
Crossroads is a pretty good dining hall. It gives me a large selection of food, is cheap, and I can always eat healthy.

This place is great! If you use your head to eat right and ORGANIC this is place for you! And Yes you can get cheaper food around Berkeley, but you'll be putting shit in your body not to mentions all the chemicals, pesticides and hormones you'll be eating. This place has organic food; can't beat that......it's a healthy option to the unhealthy food around the campus.......Beside have you ever been to other universities or colleges around the country and the world? Obviously not! Because there aren't many organic dining halls even here in US. So if you care for your body and what you put in it then eat here otherwise don't.

I spent the weekend at Cal in a transfer preparation event. We stayed in Unit 1, right next to Crossroads. For the weekend, we were given passes to Crossroads for three meals a day, and I only skipped once. 

The cafeteria itself was surprisingly clean, and their options were much larger and varied than I could ever have expected from a university. They offered veggie burgers, which definitely goes a long way with me (I would have been very turned off by Berkeley after three days of salads) which obviously weren't gourmet, but they were better than the microwave patties I have at home. 

Granted, our passes were free, so I can't comment on the food pricing, and I will say that I'm sure I would get sick of eating at Crossroads for three+ years. However, as a transfer student who would likely only eat here once or twice a week -- tops -- it did the job. 

If you're at Cal for a conference or an event of a similar nature, don't fret -- Crossroads will do you just fine.

This is dorm food, but the variety is quite impressive. I appreciate Cal Dining's commitment to making sure there are vegan options available at every station. The pizza (soy cheese margarita) wasn't bad. Several salad bars had pretty fresh veggies (though I did go toward the beginning of lunchtime). The vegan brownies were really yummy! I think prices for non-mealplan students are too high, but if you find someone to swipe you in, by all means, give it a try when you're really hungry.

Crossroads is the best buffet restaurant you will ever encounter. It's soo easy to be healthy here and get some tasty noms. There's always enough room to sit. Best if you come in a group, but if you come by yourself and don't feel like hogging tables, there's a counter. Also, there's an outdoor seating area IN the cafeteria. It's pretty cool. Plus, Crossroads is green, and you can compost your food if you can't finish.
They have an organic salad bar with a lot of options. Also, vegetarians do not suffer here. There's a vegetarian section, and the American Masala counter usually has some good vegetarian options too. They also have a World Flavors section, which has the second longest line in the place if not the longest. The pizza section is worth trying. They always serve one vegan pizza, which is usually the healthiest one I see there.
There are plenty of beverages to select from. They have milks, sodas, juices, tea, coffee, cappuccino, hot chocolate, and water of course.
The dessert is usually pretty good, be it lunch or dinner. If you're lucky enough, they'll be serving vegan chocolate cake. It is the best chocolate cake in general, hands down!
Unfortunately, they only let you take one piece of fruit and a cup of frozen yogurt when you're done. So you can't smuggle out tomorrow's lunch (but some people do that anyway). But usually, you get a good deal here.

All you can eat dining hall located between the Unit 1 residence and the Channing Bowditch apartments. This place offers breakfast, lunch, dinner, and late-night options, although I've only had dinner here so far. Dinner will cost you around $8 (or 10 meal plan points). The food isn't fine dining but it's all you can eat and there's a wide variety (pizza, hot and cold entrees, salad bar, etc.). After two years of craving this kind of dining option, I'm just happy it's close to my apartment building. Be warned it's usually pretty packed all day because of it's proximity to campus and the Unit 1 building with all the residents who have a meal plan included with their housing.

Eating in UCB dining commons can be a troublesome affair.  It can range from amazing to just plain awful.  Crossroads is mostly the latter but sometimes it's just what you need.  The place is gigantic and the salads and main courses are mostly good.  There is mexican food if you so desire and pizza is alright.  The asian station has NEVER been good.  Cafe 3 has better asian food... which is not a compliment. 

Special days are the best when the make the place totally awesome and give special food and have cloclate fountains and stuff. I survived off of late-night the 1st semester with fatty foods along with coffee from peets to use up those plentiful meal points.  Still not as good as Foothill late night though.  Still, it serves its purpose: to feed the masses. : /

The only thing I like about this place is that it is buffet style. If there is something you really liked you can get it over and over again. Other than that, the quality of the food isn't that great. But maybe it is because the food is massed produced. But yeah can't complain that much when someone swipes me in because it is free food.

Barley risotto is evil, I tell you!

Compared to the other DCs, though, Crossroads does have more variety. However, this can sometimes be a double-edged sword. To me, Crossroads is one of those hit-or-miss places; the food is either above average or inedible. On the bad days, though, a slice of pizza and some salad always saves me (but definitely not worth 8 meal points).

What I dislike about Crossroads:
-Barley risotto!!!
-Harry's dad's bathtub chili (just the name grosses me out)
-Autumn harvest wild mushroom barley soup
-Beer cheese soup (haven't tried it but does not look good)
-sad attempts at Mexican food
-Chicken Piccata (last time I had it, it tasted like a block of salt)
-Ratatouille
-the lack of flavor in most items

Likes:
-Omelet bar
-Tater tots
-Salad bar/fruit
-Red velvet cake
-Pumpkin pie

Furthermore, do they censor what comments to post on the comment board? A friend wrote one back in February expressing how she did not like her meal that day, and it was never posted! For the most part, all of the current comments are complimentary.

They try...they really do. They're conscious about offering vegan and organic offerings. But, in all honesty, the food isn't good. It's alright, and it does in a pinch, but it's not good. I wish we could opt out of our meal plans...

When I saw crossroads on here, I made a yelp account just so i could post my experience with this place.  I normally avoid it, but when you live on campus they force you to buy a meal plan with your housing contract.  Normally I just come here for breakfast.  Almost every time I go, I end up with undercooked eggs.  Sometimes they're so bad that it's like liquid soup with chunks of partially cooked eggs inside of it.  Isn't this a health code violation?  

It's finals week, so I decided to come for breakfast again.  Take a look at the photo I posted.   Unsurprisingly, the eggs were again undercooked and part of my box was filled with raw egg on the bottom.  The "sausage", although it looks overcooked, is actually so greasy that it's mushy when you try to cut into it.  It smells rancid, and i felt sick just smelling it.  The "hash browns" were soggy, greasy, and cold.  The worst part:  I paid the equivalent of 8.75 DOLLARS in meal points for this "food".  

I feel robbed every time I eat here.  For $8.75 I can eat a great meal at many of the places nearby.  We're paying good money for this "food", so why are we getting served such low quality slop?  Even if I was going to make fresh scrambled eggs, hash browns, and sausage myself for breakfast with high quality ingredients, it would cost nowhere near $8.75 per portion.  Why do people put up with this place?  Not only is it robbing all the students blind, somebody is going to get really sick eating here one day.  If this is how they cook something as simple as eggs (with such malpractice and obliviousness), I can only imagine what else goes on in the back when they're preparing everything else.

I never ate at the dining commons when I went to Cal so my co-worker took me here for my birthday.  I was told that dorm food has come a long way.  Crossroads is a neat experience.  $8 for adults, $5 for kids 3-12 and kids under 3 are free.  On the day we went (a Thursday), there was the pizza bar, Fire & Ice noodle bar, deli bar, waffle bar, BBQ chicken, corn on the cob and mac & cheese, Bear burgers and hot dogs, dessert bar with popsicles and soft serve.  There is always the organic salad bar and cereal bar.  There are 3 beverage counters and one hot drink counter.

The pizza and burger was quite good.  I had pork chow mein and egg roll but it was a bit bland.  The dessert bar had this coconut and chocolate chip bar that was yummy and how can you go wrong with soft serve?  I wouldn't eat here everyday, but it is fun to go with a group or on the weekends.  There is something for everyone.  Check out the week's menu at http://caldining.berkeley.edu/ before going.  Oh, the building is neat, architecturally, inside and out.  It doesn't feel like you are in Berkeley.

Hahaha. Once you're not being forced to go here you sort of miss it as it offers a huge selection. 

Brunch and breakfast menus are the best but if you can splurge on special nights go for it. 

Feeling like those studies can't afford that trip down to Crossroads? Do some pizza take-out or a couple sandwiches to save. The options are nearly endless and how much you enjoy your dining commons experience is largely based on how creative you can get at putting together your own plate. 

Then there's Late Night dining! It's time to find someone with a meal plan to swipe you in. b^_^ 

Good ol' Crossroads

Worse than Cafe 3, but still edible. Since the selection's bigger, so there's usually at least one thing that you can eat, and if not, the cereals, breads, bagel, and salad bar are usually decent. Lines are horrible. Since it's a college cafeteria groups are always huddled in line together and if a friend stops by, he will cut in and join them. Good food will run out ridiculously fast because of this.
Why are we reviewing crossroads? If you are a freshman student, you gotta do it. But, honestly, if you are visiting Berkeley, do not eat here. Berkeley has so many superior culinary offerings!

bottom line: food sucks. 

they try to get creative with their cuisine by mixing odd things together. yogurt sauce potatoes? harry's dad's bath tub chili? i know there's been budget cuts, but that's no excuse to serve us live stock feed... when in doubt, go with the salad bar.

late night is good! the staff gets really anal about people sitting at the ends of the tables, so don't do it. apparently, it's a fire hazard.

the dish washing crew in the back be hella slappin' tho! always sounds like a party up in there!

Taste: 3
Value: 3
Service: 4

In terms of DCs, this place is one of the better ones. Definitely has a lot more variety since it's so much bigger, but at the end of the day, it's still DC food.

Crossroads is hands down my favorite DC.  I like the feel of the building and the layout of the food stations.  There's lots of light and space.  Whenever I walk in, I feel good right away.  At every meal, there's tremendous variety.  There's an Asian food counter, a pizza bar, a Mexican food counter, the Blue Plate Special line; fries; frozen yogurt; salad.  I can always find something that I'm willing to eat and usually find something that I'm happy to eat.  Excellent diet coke!  Lots of organic and vegetarian choices.  Vegetables that are not necessarily overcooked.  As one of my French friends used to say, the food here won't give you pimples.

When I was in College, each meal by itself was more or less OK.  What was bad about dorm food was the lack of variety.  Things have really changed since my time.  The options seem endless.  The Berkeley campus makes a considerable effort to bring in local produce, and I think that they're doing very well at it.

Crappy university cafeteria with a nice high-ceiling spacious interior that tricks you into thinking the food is actually decent.

Buffet style cafeteria where you can eat and take as much as you want, but there isn't that much variety. 

Recently Crossroads has upgraded to "organic food", which tastes like crap.

Better off spending your money somewhere else... good for a one time UC experience though.

For buffet style dorm food... its good. Yea the menu gets repeated but they do try to add new things too.  The salad bar eggs and sandwich making are especially nice features.  I don't think you could find this kind of the variety not to mention health consciousness at a regular buffet.
