After months and months of eating the same bad food over and over, it starts to become familiar and sort of comforting.  That is really the only thing this DC has going for it.  So, keep at it, freshmen, eventually you'll get used to the slop.  Ironically, by the time you are just starting to lose your repulsion to it, you will be out of the dorms and won't have to eat here anymore.

What are you guys talking about?  Crossroads is awesome.  Yeah, it isn't Chez Panisse, but for a student cafeteria, the food is great.

10,000 people come here per day, or something crazy like that - the place is huge.  There are different sections for different ethnic cuisines (hence the name "Crossroads").  There's Asian food (which is often not good), American food (the "Blue Plate Special" - which is often good), Mexican food - there's also a grill for hamburgers, a complete organic salad bar which is AWESOME, and an entire dessert section along with soft serve ice cream machines.  It's all you can eat for $9, I think, if you're not a student.  And you can also purchase take-away meals, where you can cram as much food as conceivably possible in a little compostable box.

so now they are charging 50 cents if you get your food to go...?! i actually had some random man come after me to make sure they re-swiped my card for the extra 50-freaking cents. (its not like they ask if its for here or to go.) the biodegradable to-go box and cup they give you is so sad. the cup is 8 ounces and bends almost immediately once you fill it with liquid to ensure an embarrassing spill or leak. the box is small: fine if you dont want to gain the freshman 15 but awful for your budget; the amount of food you get for the points/money if you take it to go is NOT worth it.

they do have a better selection of fro-yo... like mango! and cones! and oreo toppings are back. 

they are pretty bad about updating signs when they run out of things. like if the sign says couscous, it will probably be pilaf, if it says lime bar, it will probably be cheesecake. 

their summer selection sucks balls... its the same grilled cheese, grilled ham and cheese, meat and over-steamed vegetable selection. plus they have fewer hours and no late night. ugh. 

its a pretty clean place, though, and well-lit with a salad and cereal bar.

It sufficed. I think that's a fairly generous and succinct analysis of Crossroads. But since this is Yelp, I guess I'll go into a bit more detail...

Crossroads was the closest dining hall to my dorm (I lived in Unit 2 my freshman year). I went because I had to. Or because it was closest. Or some combination of those two factors. I had millions of points and no where to spend them except GBC, which was way too far from my dorm, one of the other dining halls which were all a hike, or Crossroads. So 99.98% of the time, that's what it ended up being. 

As far as buffet style dining, there were a lot of choices. But they got old, fast. The orange chicken was always good at the Asian station. Salad was always a backup plan. Cereal was the backup backup plan. The Mexican station was usually decent. I liked to get some salad and top it with the soy taco meat, a bit of cheese, rice, and salsa. I ended up doing that far too often because of the lack of variety and distaste for the majority of the other food. The main plate station was hit or miss, but the line was always really long so I tended to avoid it unless it looked really good. One staple of my dinner meals there...the froyo. Loved the praline froyo. yum!

The one thing I did like about Crossroads was its ability to bring people together. it was a meeting place. A homework place. A planning place. And a source of nourishment (kinda). It was a place you never had to go to alone, because as dinner time came near, all one had to do was stick their head out their door and call down the hall "who's going to dinner?" and shortly half the hallway would be congregated ready to head as a group over to Crossroads. 

So overall it got me through my freshman year, but it wasn't fantastic. Mediocre at best (except for the froyo, I'd say that the froyo was above decent, good even). I don't wonder about the "freshman 15" when I think about this place, knowing that I myself probably gained 5 pounds my first month or two eating there (but quickly lost it all after that first month or two when I couldn't stand it anymore and survived off salads and sandwiches instead...) Crossroads is one thing I don't miss about college. It amazes and saddens me that most people don't realize all the great food Berkeley has to offer until they get out of the dorms, myself included.

SO MUCH VARIETY FOR A DINING HALL!! 

I was so impressed when I first stepped into Crossroads! I mean, it looked pretty new and impressive from the outside but when you walk in...WOW! It was almost like releasing a child in a candy store! I just ran around looking at all the different types of food available and it's ALL YOU CAN EAT!!! It's like I died and somehow landed myself in Heaven! 

I got a little of everything and ended up overstuffing myself but it was worth it!! YUMMY!!

Food: Parmesan chicken with pasta, Talapia with vegies and rice, tofu with vegies, apple, pear, frozen yogurt, and that's all I remember but it was amazing! I would have stayed longer and eaten more but I was on a time crunch. I'm definately going to go back there and stay for like 5 hours and eat as much as humanly possible! This is given that I starve myself 3 days prior to this food fest so I can actually accomplish this!

Atmosphere: felt like downgraded version of what a nice casino buffet would be like. It was just a bunch of students. I mean, a dining hall is a dining hall right? No matter how high the ceilings are and how much food was available...and how good the food is...and *drools* the food......

Service: um...if I tipped myself does that count as service?? (You bus yourself!)

price: GREAT DEAL for how much I ate! it's a BUFFET! GO FOR IT! 

YUMMY YUMMY crossroads! How I miss thee! I'll be back soon!! 

I'm soooo glad that I don't live close to crossroads or else I'd be like overweight and super FAT! I know where freshman 15 comes from now! Good thing it's close to the gym!!

Timeline of taste for crossroad:

Week 0-2: Delicious! Pizza every single day, holy crap!! Eat as much as I want every meal?! COLLEGE IS AWESEOME!

Week 2-30: Ughhhhhhhhhhhhh super salty mystery meat again and weird "Indian food" (brown paste with peas), I guess I'm having a slice of terrible pizza and a bowl of Cheerios for dinner again.

Sophomore year and beyond: FRESHMAN! TAKE ME TO LATE NIGHT!

One star for the horrible, horrible vegetarian options. The main problem with the vegetarian fare is that in order to cater to vegans, most of the vegetarian fare is vegan. This is obviously disappointing if you are vegetarian but not vegan. The other bad thing, is that this place has a really, really bad nutritionist on the vegetarian side of things. Seriously -- if you were to exclusively eat from the vegetarian options here, you would be in a lot of trouble, especially if you didn't eat the pizza (which, as far as I can tell, is how they expect you to get all of your vegetarian protein).

Sometimes Crossroads as good vegetarian dishes -- especially in the "Fire & Ice" Asian section of the dining commons -- but on the whole, the selection is simply far from adequate. Not only is the food inadequate, there simply isn't a lot of variety. There's a dozen or so dishes in the vegetarian area, period. The Mexican food station always has the same options, and the Asian section has two or three vegetarian dishes that are served only occasionally. If you are a vegetarian eating here, you will eat all of the new food you are going to eat here in the first month or so. Towards the end of my second and last year in the dormitories they conducted a survey and focus group due to the overwhelming number of complaints by vegetarians, so things may have changed, but when I ate here a few times during the following fall things seemed the same here.

Crossroads is a residential dining restaurant particularly meant for UC Berkeley student residents. However, anyone is welcome and the dining experience is not exclusive. I wouldn't pay to eat here, even though some people do, but rather, I would use my own meal points or have someone use their meal points to "swipe me in." 

Food:
Food is far from spectacular but not usually horrible. In general, it is a decent place to eat; their food is decent.  It is set in buffet style, all-you-can-eat. So if you want to eat till you die but not really enjoy the food so much, I guess you can come here. 

The foods offered are of eclectic variety. "Asian, Mexican, made-to-order deli, organic salad bar, comfort foods, vegetarian/vegan, grilled entries, bakery and dessert selections, and a variety of soups, cereals and beverages." Their vegetarian/vegan selection, while it IS limited, is also not bad. And I guess it's better to have than to not.(for those veggies out there.)

All food is "mass-produced" and so taste isn't a priority. Just expect to come, eat, and leave with a full stomach, and you just might be somewhat satisfied, somewhat.  I guess one redeeming trait of the place is that they offer such a wide selections of foods that even though you don't like one thing, you will eventually find something else you like, or at least kinda-sorta do like. 

Decor:
Large, cafeteria setting. No artwork or any special accomodations in this aspect of decor. They have a monochromatic floor, wall... Very simple setup here. Average. Like I said, it's just your regular college cafeteria---nothing fancy-shmancy.

Service:
Self-serve buffet-style cafeteria. So, that means your service to yourself  is as good as you make it. I am so funny haha, I know. The people who work the different stations are generally friendly and (not in a sarcastic way) are happy to plop whatever food they're plopping on trays that day on your tray. Smile and they'll smile back. Compliment them, and they'll treat you well. Don't make eye contact and expect just your average plopping. 

Cost:
The first price is in units of meal points and the second price is cash prices if you're going to pay that way.

"Breakfast   5.50   $7.00
Lunch/Brunch  6.50  $8.00
Dinner  7.50  $9.00
Late Night at the Den  A la Carte Pricing  A la Carte Pricing
Children  5.00  $5.00"

Overall:

Breakfast  7:00 am - 10:00 am

Your run-o-the-mill buffet. Nothing bad but nothing usually great. They try to vary foods and offer different cuisines from different cultures. I guess that is nice at times. And sometimes,  you just may be surprised with some occasionally delicious food. 

Don't expect lobster though. 
Just expect to be full. 

oh yeah, and the name, "Crossroads"? What the hell is that? I guess I'm just hating---my bad... but seriously...gives me images of a gas station or some cars whizzing by. I ain't no damn car filling up at a gas station! I am a person with feelings who wants to feel good eating your feel-good food.

Ah Crossroads, what a throwback to the good ol' days. I can still remember toting that black tray around (do they even have those anymore?) and piling up on the fine, nondescript vegetarian cuisine. Usually some super thick-cut zucchini and a variation on rice. 

Two stars are for the brunch they used to serve (scrambled eggs, tater tots) and for the mythical blueberry cheesecake that I had the good fortune of having at dinner during my first week at Cal. And then, I never saw it again. On some days I think that the cheesecake was too good to be true, and that I must have just dreamt about it while actually chomping down on a vegan lemon bar. 

The third star is simply for the memories. I can't help but feel an ache in my chest when I pass by during dinnertime these days. Lucky freshman with meal points- I can't afford to pay 9 dollars for a bad dinner.

I will never pass up free food. 

NEVER. 

And this is the perfect example. After spending the afternoon galavanting around Oakland with fellow Buckeyes, I met my friend in Berkeley to catch a ride back to San Francisco. Before we hit the road, she offered to treat me to dinner at one of Cal's fine dining establishments. Who am I to resist  college food?

The aesthetics of this place puts many dining halls to shame. Very industrial, lots of cement, silvers and greys, natural light and oddly shaped rooms. There's even a fun courtyard in the middle but you are boxed in by walls of windows on all four sides. Don't sit here if you like privacy. People will be able to see the ratio of what you put on your plate and what you actually ate. 

Being that it was Sunday evening, I knew I wouldn't have the best pickings in the world. The pizza was a little cold, the "World Market" wasn't open and the salad bar wasn't anything to write home about. But the chocolate chip cookies were sweet and soft. And the Indian flavored chicken and rice were surprisingly flavorful. 

Oh, did I mention it was free? I ate everything I put on my plate. And then went back for seconds. 

Side note that only people from snow-bound hometowns will notice: the dining trays are abnormally small. They can barely fit two of the small oval-shaped plates Crossroads puts everything on. The reason I picked up on this detail is because I'm so used to stealing dining trays for sledding. When looking at this one, I didn't know how my bubble butt would stay on. 

Damn you Berkeley for subconsciously attacking my body image. Apparently I need to lose some weight if I wanna go sledding in California.

Come here only for LATE NIGHT!!!!!!!!

At late night, everything is made per order.. prices aren't too bad if you're not a Cal Student, but if you have mealpoints, then even better!!

However, the usual breakfast-lunch-dinner food isn't as awesome. Sometimes they taste weird, sometimes it's good.. Always a gamble eating here.

During my first one and half years, I got most of my nourishment from either here or Foothill DC. Clark Kerr was too far and I didn't frequent Café 3 until I moved to Unit 3 in the last half of sophomore year. Let's face it, this is dorm food we're talking about, so don't expect restaurant-quality stuff here.

That said, Crossroads isn't bad. It just could do better on some dishes. Bacon can be hard as wood sometimes, and the veggie options are pretty bland. Well, actually, just about everything was pretty bland. But the omelets aren't too bad. And usually I helped myself to the salad bar, which, being do-it-yourself, can be as good or bad as you make it.

As for the place itself, it's actually one of my favorite places to dine based on just environment alone. Plenty of seating (though there's never enough during regular dining hours) and natural lighting, with a pretty clean decor makes Crossroads a good place to eat and study. Just watch out when they serve up a special; once, they couldn't serve tuna fillets fast enough, and ended up undercooking them. Eck.

I mean what more can you ask for? The food is decent (edible).... always a variety, all you can eat!!!!! you can even take stuff to stock up your kitchen cabinets. I mean really, what is there not to like about this place?  It is kind of pricey if you don't eat all that much though.  Not mentioning any names, but I know people who've stocked up on cups, plates, silverware, produce, dairy, cereal...  ghetto??? yes... smart??? I think so.

I only come here for late night.  If you have a lot of meal points this is the place to spend it at.  The prices are average if you don' t have meal points to use.  Everything is made to order and its your typical school cafeteria food.  Come here if you are hungry and too lazy to drive any where else for food.

I want the weed the people below me are taking because no sober person would rave about the food at Crossroads...which is fucking horrible.  Seriously, they never refill the drinks, use crappy meat, and just have terrible food selections in general.  It's pretty much the same shit every day.  And to top it off, they always run out of food so if you come anytime after 7, chances are your 8 points are wasted.

God, the food here fucking sucks.

Crossroads sets the bar high in the realm of truly mediocre dining experiences. From its culturally invalid cuisines to its Laissez faire style of food service, Crossroads is the perfect spot to take that special someone for whom you both loath and despise. That is unless you have a meal plan and Crossroads is the closest dining establishment that accepts your hogwash currency. For if that is the case, the joke is on you.

Here's your typical day at Crossroads Dining...

1. you walk through to see an amazingly built eating establishment 
2. you grab your tray 
3. you walk around through a plethora of buffet delight
4. you fill your tray until it is heavy 
5. you sit down taking in all of the great smells from your tray of awesomeness
HERE IS WHERE THE GAME CHANGES
6. you find out the food isn't as great as It looks
6a. The pizza tastes like marinara on crusty bread
6b. the Burrito tortillas taste like paper
6c. the soups have chuncks of soup mix in it
6d. the meat is dry
6e. do I have to go on?
7. you end up hungry and having to dump all of your food in the garbage (remember to compost folks)

This is your typical visit, and every time for the last 3 years that I've tried to give these guys a chance, I have been disappointed...

At' least the food is great during winterfest....

Food here is God AWFUL. 
$6.50 for lunch, $7.50 for dinner... YOu can get way better food for less here in Berkeley.

You know, instead of doing a crappy job of cooking the food, why not just cook it right so people don't throw it away and waste it? 

The ingredients are fine, it's just a simple matter cooking right. Example: Pasta is overcooked. Solution: cook it LESS
Example: salad dressing tastes like crap Solution: BETTER DRESSING

Although I am giving this a mediocre rating, this is on the scale compared to actual eating establishment.  In terms of dorm food, this place was a five.

I seriously think people complain about it just because it everyone else does.  Once you are out of your first semester, "Oh I hate Crossroads, the food sucks and I hate it".  Oh really?  What glamorous menus are you cooking up at home or making in the hot pot in your dorm?  Nothing beats a homecooked meal, but in the life of student smack dab in the middle of a midterm-saturated semester, this place is perfect.

I loved going to the salad bar, getting a big salad with all the fixings, so I can feel good about the 32 oz. soft-serve yogurt I was about to devour later, complete with Oreo toppings (might have stopped having those)...
I never really went for the "blue plate" items since they all kind of looked, well, subpar.  But the place will not mess up a sandwich, soup, salad, or cereal.  Which happens to be pretty much all I eat.  Also the Fire & Ice asian section always seems to be serving something delicious, including the oh-so-needed orange chicken fix. 

5 stars for dorm food, 3 stars for actual food.  

I'm tempted to give this 4 stars though because they did, at one point, serve the AAA-burger (or some name along those lines) which comprised of a hamburger beef patty in between a half-sliced donut.  With cheese.  COME ON!

I absolutely love this dining common of UC Berkeley. I used to come here every day as a student. You will find that most diners here are students, but there are non-student diners now and then because it's not exclusive to students. They serve breakfast, lunch, dinner, and late-night. Considering it's all you can eat, you can seriously get your dollars worth, even if you go without meal points and pay the cash. They also do to-go. You'll get a compostable box and cup to fill as much as you can or want.

They boast a large salad bar. You can arrange your own salad or get one of the premade ones. There are lots and lots of dressing options. There is a pasta bar that feature two pastas a day usually. The sauces are a little watered down, but still tasty especially if you're carb loading. There is a sandwich bar where you can as for custom made sandwiches or just deli meats and cheese. There is a soup bar that feature two soups a day and one is always vegetarian. There's a pizza station where at least one pizza was vegetarian. There's a dessert station. There's a soft serve machine. There's an ice tea machine. There's milk, coffee, juice, soda, whatever. There is an entree station where the main entree of the day is served along with sides. There are some ethnic stations that serve Chinese food or Mexican food or Indian food, depending on the day. Seriously, in terms of buffets, this is one of the best ones with great organic, vegetarian, vegan, lactose-free, and gluten-free options. Crossroads has you covered. When I had meal points as a student, I was happy that I was able to eat a place that offered such variety of foods and thought about how difficult it would be to assemble a 20-ingredient salad at home or having the option to drink whatever beverage you want. Imagine having to keep track of 10 cartons of juice or 20 veggies in your fridge before they expire or grow moldy. Ya get me?

While there are some terrible dishes, none are too royally terrible. Over the couple years that I frequented this place, I managed to pick out the yummy things and knew to avoid the not-so-good. One can often hear people complaining about the terrible dining commons food, but instead of cherry-picking the bad stuff, cherry-pick the good and trusted dishes and you'll be alright.

OK, so there's all this food here and what did I like eating the most? I loved the custom omelette during late night. They were perfectly made, even if the eggs were out of a carton. I also loved the late night ribs and especially the side of potato salad. I also liked the Italian wedding and chicken & dumpling soups. I liked the eggplant parm and the waffle fries.

Another thing I love about Crossroads is that they make composting real simple. When you bus your tray, all you have to do is slide everything uneaten out into a bin.

you can check out the menus here, to plan your visit:
http://services.housing.berkeley.edu/FoodPro/dining/static/todaysentrees.asp

The food basically does all it has to - it feeds you.

I ate here for about six days during a summer conference on campus.  At first, the set up sounds brilliant.  As much food as I want?  Awesome I am going to be happy.

Then you learn all the food is made by foot, or at least appears so.  It looks like everything was mashed together in a giant tub by stomping.  The salad looks like that, the mashed potatoes look (and smell) like that, the curry looks like that, everything looks like no one gave a fuck about how it turned out.

I ate chicken that tasted like rubber, rice that tasted like pudding, and vegetables that tasted like limp socks.

Bite after bite, nothing made me want to make full use of my buffet food ticket.  And you can't take food to go, unless you take all your food to go from the get go.  So you really have to stomach all the food you're willing to eat at once, or leave and realize you are hungry for real food, not this Crossroads bullshit, in the middle of the night, or in the middle of class, or wherever it is you were supposed to be not starving at.

I would lie in my bunk bed late at night, my tummy grumbling, wishing I had eaten something fresh and wholesome for dinner, wishing I had gone to the curry place up the street, wishing I had just found some french fries somewhere.  So hungry, so sad.


Finally, near the end of the week, I discovered the sandwich bar.  Tucked into a distant corner in the angry chaotic map of the cafeteria, I found a woman standing behind the counter.  She asked me what kind of bread I wanted and I got whole wheat.  We quickly skipped over to what kind of meat and vegetables I wanted.  I sprung for some basic tuna and mayo with a slice of American cheese.  There was nothing wrong with it.  It wasn't something I'd make at home this way, but there was nothing glaringly repulsive about eating it.  

I ate the same thing until I left.  It was the only edible corner.

That, and sweet potato fries when they were available. They weren't bad either, when covered completely in salt.

I also feel incredibly bad for the staff here.  Imagine the hell they catch for the awful food they serve.  The looks on their faces, of distress and apology: "I'm sorry I have to feed you this."  Many of the kitchen staff were incredibly friendly, if perhaps meek and frightened.  I don't want to blame them for the food.  The big guys, whoever buys this shit and decides humans should eat it, they're to blame.  Those people don't give a shit about us or their employees.

Holy crap the vegi TACO meat, really tastes like real meat.  I'm giving them the benefit of the doubt that it wasn't meat but really, WOW.

This review might be a little dated.  Ok, who am I kidding, this review IS dated (i.e. 2005).  Seriously though, crazy good fakemeat for TACOS.  

Also, I have limited idea of what meat tastes like, so I suppose it might not have actually tasted like meat, but it convinced me.

FYI: TACO TACO TACO.

Small Update - Here's what I made today for lunch:

Spicy Lemon Chicken Sandwich: lemon-spiced chicken from indian station, sourdough from salad bar, arugula from salad station, onions, tomatoes, cheese from deli, dash of siracha sauce for flavor:

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/X2gKwUYR1CQ51XCpKU1_gQ?select=z3IuluQ6Z2lBOUf6EG3MCg

Crossroads and I have had a long relationship. Other than eating here regularly when I was a freshman, we cross paths only during the summers (of love?) because I get to eat here for free (yay for working for the school).

I won't say Crossroads is terribad because it's not too bad when you can get creative with the dishes. What I will say though is that any one station's combination of protein, vegetable, and carb is a bad choice. Everything is underseasoned as well so add some salt +pepper.

As a cook, I've just taken all the possible ingredients there to make my own dishes instead of eating their standalone things. Here's some examples I've experimented with based on what they've had. I'll go from simple (few stations) to fancy (alot of stations):

Breakfast Tacos: eggs from blue plate, soft taco shells from vegetarian entree, red onions from salad bar/bagels, tapatio/tabasco from the tables, breaking up sausage/ham/something optional

Chicken Pasta with Spinach: break up grilled chicken from grill station, pasta + cream sauce from pasta station, add spinach from salad station, mix together

Pork Loin Sandwich - pork loin from blue plate station, 2 slices of toasted sourdough from the salad bar, spring mix from the salad bar, chipotle mayo from the deli, tomatoes+red onion from the grill station

Greek Chicken Wrap - shred a grilled chicken breast from grill station, greek salad from the salad bar, hummus from the deli, "naan" (it's just pita) from the Indian station

You, too, can turn shit into gold. (YOUR MILEAGE MAY VARY)

My favorite item here is the Portuguese Chikcen. And I like to order it along with boba tea with extra 99cents
My mom said the overall food in this restuarant  tastes like Macanese food. I don't know about that, but I like this place, the price is ok and I feel comportable sitting inside.

prices are fair and the food passes

I have ordered there spicy string beans, mongolian beef, and pork fried rice, and none of it was half bad.

try the boba honey tea

anyway, i have had my eye on the chicken chow fun so i will definately go back  :-D

However, i must note, my friend did throw up once but i would like ot think that its because she was already sick before we got there...eww

Lotus House used to be my go to place as an undergrad. The only good thing about this place is that the food is cheap and it doesn't take a long time for you to get something to eat. Excellent for a student cramming for finals and such. 

The food is ok, it isn't that great. And the sauce and ingredients are typical of what you would find at a supermarket. On top of that, it is unhealthy for you. Some of the dishes they make are salty as well.

Besides needing a quick bite to eat nearby I would go to a different place with better chinese food. I mean if you have time just walk or take the bus/bart and partake on a better eatting experience at a quality chinese restaurant.

i have never gone wrong with ordering something from the papers on the walls.  everything is really cheap and delicious

loses one star for most of the food being terribly greasy.

loses another for not having a viable option to make the teas less sweet other than less flavor powder.

Being Chinese, I do have a high expectation for Chinese food. And this just doesn't cut it. I will divide the review into sections:

Food: If you haven't had much Chinese food and prefer your food extra flavorful in salt and (maybe?) MSG, come here. Otherwise, the food isn't that great. I ordered multiple items and they've all been failed in different regards. The broccoli was overcooked. The noodle was made separately from the rest of the dish, which is convenient but you can taste the difference. Most of the other dishes are acceptable but not good. But it's good enough for Berkeley students who haven't ate since 8AM.

Drinks: The drink is decent, but not good. The pearl is hard and not chewable. But the milk tea portion is good. The flavored drinks (I ordered almond) is decent in the sense you can barely taste the extra flavor. But I don't think it's worth it.

Service: I did NOT like the service. I had to pay in cash because they had a lower minimum in which debit or credit card will be accepted. The guy literally gave me 99 cents in change. That annoyed me.

Decor/Location: It is conveniently located near school. The place is nicely decorated as well.

I have a love and hate relationship with Lotus House. On the one hand, I am grateful for the late night goodies it has--porridge soup, corn rice, boba. But on the other hand, its consistency (or lack of,) has disappointed me so many times. 

As of late, I am pretty disappointed. The honeydew milk tea w/ boba is usually my staple here. I have always depended on Lotus House to not only have the honeydew milk tea, but to make it to perfection. I recently had the drink again and was deeply saddened. It tasted like bubblegum, left a horrible after taste, and the boba was way too soft.

The food here is not bad, but also dependent on what you order. The dishes I would recommend are the beef noodle soup, corn fried rice, and tomato fried rice.

After a LONG hiatus from Chinese food, I decided to give Lotus House another try. 

Got the broccoli and beef over rice for 6 bucks. It smelled hella delicious maybe because I haven't eaten since my 8am class. But after digging into my dinner, I began to taste the massive amount of MSG. The gravy was disgustingly thick, aint my style yo.

NEVER GOING HERE AGAIN

I went to there to see a friend of mine and ordered the food there. We had (1) Baked Pork and Fish Rice and (2) Baked Portuguese Chicken Rice and two pearl teas. 

The price is alright and about $10 a head. However, the quality of the food is so so.

Ugh.  I like a few dishes, but for the most part I don't think I've ever walked from this place completely satisfied.  It's the only place that serves milk tea at 11 am, but it's always too powdery and their default order uses green tea.  Ech.

If I were to recommend a dish I would suggest...you know what? Just go to mandarin house.

Probably the best Chinese food on the south side of Berkeley. My friend who went to Taiwan for 6 months came back and the first thing he wanted to eat was more Chinese food... from Lotus House. And another guy straight from China, Lotus House is also his preferred Asian food of choice. That sounds like street cred to me.

Service here is no good. And I don't like the many flat screens of Hong Kong and Taiwanese pop stars, but if you can get over that (or do take out), then the food is pretty good.

People like their scrambled eggs over something rice. Also, their black bean beef was delicious, and their wonton soup--while nothing to write home about--hits the spot on a cold night. 

They probably have the best boba drinks--slightly edging out Sweetheart's--but it's on the pricier side.

Lotus House has proved to be a solid Chinese restaurant at a decent price with decent portions. It just isn't anything special, with no single dish that I can absolutely rave about.  But for filling an empty stomach, it does alright.

Lotus House has the best selection of Chinese food on campus. The food isn't amazing, but it's pretty damn good for what you're paying.

I first had Lotus House when my friend bought me porridge when I was sick. It was a bit too watery but it was good enough. After that, I started trying more and more dishes, just to reminisce and fulfill my Hong Kong cravings. My favourites are the portuguese chicken rice plate, beef chow fun with black bean sauce, and singapore curry rice noodles. Things do tend to get a little greasy and heavy, but I usually split my order into several meals so it's all good. Food comes out fairly quickly, and the employees behind the counter are fun to talk to in Cantonese.

The restaurant itself is really well-kept, clean and classy for what it is. There's a lot of seating room, and they have a back area, too. And TV's! This is always a good place to have dinner with friends.

So if you are in the "Ghetto" area and you want Chinese this is the place to go.  Lotus House is tasty and cheap... much tastier than the other Chinese options in the immediate vicinity.  If you are adventurous try some of their HK stuff that you typically don't find in the run of the mill Chinese restaurants.

The sign says "Best Tapioca in Town"... NOT!  The do have good selection of bubble tea and the counter lady was patient while I deliberated on which one to choose. I ended up having the coconut milk tea.  Not great but not bad.  Certainly not in the "best in Town category"  Food - IDK.  Most of it seemed geared to the carnivore crowd.

As the management changes here, the food gets progressively sloppier.  I used to feel good after eating here, now I feel like a greaseball.  The food is okay, the positives are the quantity of food as well as a late night spot to hit up when you have limited options.

Accepts credit cards but with a minimum purchase of $10. 

Their food is pretty good for their price. I especially love the tomato pork chop, the beef fried rice, the salt and pepper pork chops with rice, general chicken rice, and well if you like the food, the make it quite well. But of course, this isn't the best place out there, but around telegraph and durant, it easily beats all the other chinese places.

If you ask for it, they can give you a stamp card, which you can stamp each time you buy something, if you total 10 purchases, you get one dish with a value of $5.75 for free.

And with a purchase, you can get a boba milk tea for only $0.99. A pretty good deal ;)

The seating is pretty much a small table, and the place isn't that big. But that doesn't really matter because you're probably there to get a quick cheap meal with a few friends. They DO let you move tables around, but really, don't go with 10 people in there.

Mondays thru saturdays are around 10am - 11:30pm
Opens sundays too, but closes earlier around 10pm?

Good place to stop by if you're around durant/telegraph looking for chinese food!

I've been here a few times because friends dragged me along---but not only am I reluctant, evasive even, to return, but also I've experienced a lack of ability to finish or consume a reasonable portion of a meal here. The food is oversaturated with MSG and other acrid ingredients that make it intolerable after a few bites. 

I gave Lotus House two stars because I am a fan of their fried tofu snacks and their pearl milk tea is decent. I suppose it's hard to screw up these sorts of orders. And one could argue that the "gratuitous pizzazz" that makes entrees overdone makes snacks savory, so if snacks are what you're looking for, Lotus House has a solid location and is very convenient. It is cash only, so keep that in mind.

I used to come here all the time when it was.... Old tea house ? I think? Anyways....the food is hit or miss here. Get the sesame chicken! I enjoy the specials they have for boba too, not the best boba but it's cheap if it's a special. They do maje a really good hot almond milk tea though. ...I will always remember this place as the spot "triangle man" liked to hang out at and watch random Asian movies on his laptop while us Cal students were busy studying! Triangle man......is that guy still around???

Decided to visit this place again while we were on campus the other day. This used to be one of our favorite places to grab food at during college days. Most meals are pretty tasty and have HUGE portions. Very reasonably priced (considering the portion). Milk tea with pearls is available too and is a big plus.

I used to love the food here... then i dont know what happened. Maybe they decided to use more oil and less flavor...In any case, the food here has declined. Recently, i ordered the "house special pan-fried noodles", and it really was poor quality. The noodles just ended up being hard instead of the crispy that its supposed to be. Also the sauce was basically brown water with no flavor at all. The redeeming factor came in the things with the noodles, i.e. the chicken, shrimp, and thin slivers of cha-shu (bbq park). These were the flavorful morsels that had to be eaten sparingly with the noodles in order to finish. The boba here is so expensive compared to sweetheart cafe and quickly, and its basically the same quality of boba. two stars for the not so good food and expensive boba.

Lotus House gots Chinese dishes
From pork, beef, and baked fishes
Portugese Chicken is my favorite meal
Prices here are decent, not a rip off or steal

This place is right by the ghetto on the left, I like the fact that they have two areas to sit and eat, and good to go to talk and chill.  They have combos where you can get boba, but it's "eh".  

Their Chinese food is average, but their baked stuff is cool, and this one dish called Portugese Chicken where it's a mix of cheese, chicken, curry, and potatoes... man, if you're starving, try this out.  Must warn you, it's kinda weird when you have it, but grows on you (and not in you :).

You know that feeling of a very particular and specific food craving that nothing else can satisfy?  That's pretty much how i feel about lotus house's portuguese chicken.  I have to admit most of the other dishes are average, but the portuguese chicken- mmm.... WOW, i literally can't get ENOUGH of it!  When I'm home in SoCal this is usually the top reason I miss being up in berkeley.  try it, if you haven't already.  It is not something that belongs in a restaurant like lotus house, but I haven't seen it duplicated anywhere else at such speed, convenience, price, and tastiness!

Average, decent food, decent service. Food comes out pretty quick when not crowded. Came here often with a group of friends. They have a nice place in the back  for larger groups, and are open pretty late and stay open to accommodate groups. Wouldn't be my pick for one-on-one lunches or dinners (better places in Berkeley for that). 

Note -- boba is EXPENSIVE here.
I love this place! Cheap, good food. Not gourmet, no, but the the garlic eggplant is delicious, as is the chow mein. Big portions. My only complaint: no vegetarian spring rolls.

I would totally lose my credibility if I did not update this review to one star.  The food here as gone from ok to bad. I think they changed the recipes and they are starting to take some shortcuts like simply reheating foods. The sauce that they use for the beef and broccoli has definitely changed. Now, it's like a bland flavorless slimy sauce. Yea - gross.

I've only ever had the boba here so I can't speak for the food, but this is my favorite boba in all of Berkeley. I always get the black milk tea - delicious without being too sweet, and inexpensive too. Sometimes the staff aren't the friendliest... but I only get boba to go so it's not much of a problem.

The food is ok but not up to San Francisco Chinatown standards.  I had the beef chow fun.  The noodles had not been cooked long enough to really fry some of them .  A good chow fun should have a mix of almost burnt noodles with just cooked noodles.  They put a lot of onions in it and no green vegetables like gai lon or bok choy.  The beef was thick and too chewy.  

My daughter had the Mongolian Beef combo plate.  The mongolian beef was way too oily but the beef was good and there was plenty of it.  Again way too much onions in the dish.  She loved the Ice Crush drink she had though and the price of the drink was great.

I'd eat there again if I was near but would probably want to try somewhere else first.  The prices are a bit high for the rice plates and combo plates when compared to San Francisco prices and other plate prices in the area for lunch.  No credit cards, Cash only!

I feel bad that this place has received such poor reviews on Yelp!  In fact this place has saved me from starving as an undergrad at Cal.  I have been here countless times as I was only a 2 minute walk from this place.  There are some crappy DIRTY places in Asian Ghetto and Lotus House isn't one of them.

If you order Boba from Quickly's because it's cheaper, you must not care about sanitation!  I feel completely sickened when I've stepped inside that heat-hole.  Lotus House is totally clean.  The staff that interacts with customers are super nice.  I never felt like I've been given attitude here--both the young man and lady who wears a baseball cap have both been polite and accommodating!

You can't go wrong with the boba at this place!  I've also had a lot of things on the menu, but the one thing was usually hit or miss was the pan fried noodles (sometimes it was crispy, sometimes it was soggy), but everything else from the curry, to the fried foods, were all delicious.  Their soups make a nice meal on a cold and rainy day.  And the honey walnut shrimp was way scrumptious.  

It's a good place to go with a group of friends or to order take out from.  It's relatively inexpensive and the portions are quite large. Their furniture doesn't look like crappy lawn furniture so it actually feels like a restaurant, and again this place is clean!  I got over the credit card thing since that seems to be a Berkeley thing.

Ask my girlfriend, from where can you eat every single day.. and no doubt she would instantly respond Lotus House.  Her favorite is the Veggie stir fry noodle.  And of course I love it too, opting for the spicy Kung Pao chicken. All the dishes I've tried are rich in flavor. The portions are more than enough; eat this for lunch and you should be full clear thru dinner, or have leftover for dinner.  This place usually stays pretty crowded and the prices are reasonable.  And i love that they reward you with a free meal after having there meal card stamped 10 times, if you eat there as much as we do, this comes handy.

My first experience with this restaurant was not good because I think I ordered a bad item on the menu. (I think corn/chicken over rice?). I haven't tried it again since then, although some friends have taken me inside but I didn't buy anything.

After looking at what other people ordered, I think this restaurant is probably better than Mandarin Garden.

Hopefully, I'll be back for a second time after a year of avoiding this restaurant.

This place is your typical college-area Chinese restaurant, but it's pretty good.  I don't come here expecting gourmet food and fresh seafood, so I don't know why most people are complaining about it.

I've ordered most things off the menu (chow mein, chow fun, mongolian beef, oven baked __ over rice, etc) and they were delicious.  Items range around $6-$8, and they have combo plates w/ your item, rice, egg roll, and thai iced tea.  They also have cards for stamps, so you can get a free dish after buying 10.

They have flatscreens with movies sometimes playing and some random games.  I play bones most times I'm here (and killing the competition).

With Berkeley's chilly summers, I had the desire to sip on some warm soup to keep me toasty. 

I decided to go to Lotus House and got the Wor Won Ton. The soup was basically a hodge podge of everything you can think of (bbq pork, chicken, imitation crab, bok choy, etc.)  chillin' in some chicken broth and thrown in with some won tons. It was aiite, I mean I left content but I expected that the broth was more flavorful especially considering all the ish that was in there. 

A cool thing about this place is that if you spend $5, you get to purchase a boba milk tea for a buck. Considering that Sweet Heart Cafe has risen their prices so they no longer have buck bobas, Lotus Cup still delivers sweet chewy balls for a Washington (if you drop a Lincoln)

The only thing I like here is the salt and pepper tofu. It's a good snack that is cheap and will satisfy your craving for munchies! Food here in general is just not that good.. but it's one of the only Chinese places around and it's cheap so people come here to eat. 

Tip for new students: If you're planning to come here often, get their meal stamp card!

3.5 stars 

I think this place really is one of the best place for Chinese food in Berkeley (that is close to campus and relatively cheap).

They also have good combo meals if you're feeling more hungry (meal + boba + egg roll) 

You should also get one of their loyalty cards if you plan on coming here often! You get a free meal if you get 10 stamps. 

My favorite things to get here are the noodles, but I would STRONGLY advise against getting any of their pan-fried noodles. I thought it would be the good kind that I always crave (crispy noodles with some sauce and veggies on top that soften the top half of the noodles. mmmmm!) but instead the sauce they use is full of msg or something because it's straight up like gelatin when I get it and I always end up having to literally scoop the excess 'gelatin' into a cup...it's pretty gross...

Regardless, that is just one category/section of dishes that I don't like. Everything else here is very good and they give huge portions so I think it's a good value for students. It's also open pretty late so I think that also makes it convenient for those of us who run from campus after meetings/studying late at night. The appetizers and snacks (like fried tofu and porridge) are also super comforting.

The food is just horrible. Everything else is okay, not expensive, service isn't bad, the food comes out pretty quick too. But really all the dishes I had there tasted horrible. Maybe it was just my luck? I don't know. I went several times last semester to help my friend collect the stamp thingy so she can get a free meal in the end(?). Not going again.

There's nothing wrong with this place no matter how you slice it. The problem is - there's nothing special about it either.

It's a pretty standard Chinese/Taiwanese boba joint that serves fairly decent food. It has plenty of seating so it's a great place for a group dinner after a meeting or a lecture. There's a combo that involves a drink + entree for around $8. I'd say that's a pretty solid meal by Durant Avenue standards.

I'd probably come again for an easy lunch with some students in the area. Be mindful, though, that there are signs saying it was voted the #1 Boba in Berkeley. I doubt that's true. Sure, it's better than Sweetheart's diluted milk water just 15 feet up the street, but it's not the best.

Although the food is relatively decent, the atmosphere created by the unfriendly workers and the signs reading "NO OUTSIDE FOOD OR DRINK ALLOWED!" and "CLEAR YOUR OWN TABLE" really negates the experience. Make sure you ask for a stamp card, because the workers won't mention it to you.

I was presently surprised by this place. My fiance and I have been here quite a few times and its argueably one of our favorite chinese restaurants in the area. Ingredients are always fresh, portions are very generous. I don't know how they cook their food, but seriously, its really flavorful and not that greasy. A big plus is that they serve tapioca drinks here too, so that makes me happy. I always have a good dining experience when coming here. No complaints. The pricing is very reasonable and they offer a wide selection of food ala carte, specials and rice plates. I love their salt and pepper squid appetizer.

Sometimes I stop and wonder why I like lotus house so much... lol... 

To be honest, the place does not look sanitary, period. I'm always afraid to imagine what goes behind the kitchen curtains....... or what's in the spicy chili sauce......

But... food tastes good to me! I don't know if it's the MSG or what, but it always seems like a pretty good deal to me when I order the eggplant dish or pineapple fried rice. I've tried a ton of their dishes, some much better than others of course, and lotus house just ends up being a place I come fairly often~

Their milk tea is also pretty good, nice that it's $1 with a meal.
Service just ok, but wouldn't expect anything much anyways.

Lotus House is great for hungry, college students. However, I would NOT bring my parents here. I ordered pineapple fried rice, but the rice and chicken were hard and tasteless. The place doesn't look that clean, and I think they used day-old rice to make their fried rice platters. I'm just not a big fan of any places in the Asian ghetto anymore, and I definitely won't be coming back to Lotus House anytime soon.

I came here while craving chinese food and decided to give this place a try. I got the mongolian beef combo with the boba to go. When I got home, it turned out that they completely messed up my order and what I got was this fried crap made out of flour. It was a really bad experience. To top things off, their boba tasted really watered down as well.

Cheap, excellent boba!! This place has the best boba milk tea I have tried.

However it is unfortunate that you need to make a 10 dollar purchase to use credit/debit card. I always forget this and end up leaving the store with nothing...
apparently people love this place.. i think it was decent and price was okay.. i didnt really think there was anything special about this place...

I've only been here a few times, but I've never had a bad experience at this location. I don't know how this place compares to the newly opened Happy Valley, but I feel that the latter might be better in some regards.

Most of the food here is delicious... if you don't mind heavy grease and massive amounts of cornstarch. It's not really a problem unless you eat it many times a week, but I try to avoid the typical Chinese restaurants because of the ingredients that they use. Regardless, the portions here are pretty good: for $6 you can get a hefty plate of fried rice, fried noodles, or a meat+white rice dish. You can't go wrong if you consider only value.

The porridge ($5) here is okay, but it can really hit the spot for someone who is sick. 

The salt and pepper tofu (~$2) is excellent. A good amount of deep fried tofu topped with scallions and jalapenos makes for a good snack or a separate dish and can be easily shared between many people.
Greasy, yummy, and cheap. Love the potstickers and chicken chowmein!

I've been to Lotus House a decent number of times while attending school here, and every successive time...it has gotten worse.

This is the only Chinese restaurant at Berkeley which serves cantonese style dishes...I think. (i.e. tomato baked pork rice something...and other Hong Kong style dishes)  I've had a decent number of dishes, and the "chow fun" a.k.a. flat noodle dishes have been my favorite so far.

Today though...I left with a less than stellar impression.  I ordered the "Fujian Fried Rice", which is essentially a rice dish covered with a gravy like sauce and seafood.  My verdict: First, the seafood was quite bad...I'm definitely not a fan of artificial crab.  Second, the rice was cooked pretty poorly.  Finally, the sauce was okay on top, but as I made way to the bottom, it was essentially water (bad mixture)?  If this were a review just for the "Fujian Fried Rice", I'd give it only 2/5 stars.

There is a vast variety of dishes to order here and decent milk tea.  But the staff needs to get their act together, because their hygiene regime and general attitude has been going downhill.

FYI: $10 credit card minimum

First-time visit.  Overall, it was decent. I was craving Chinese food and was in a hurry because this was right before my exam. Decided to try it after passing by numerous times.

I ordered Szechuan shrimp to-go which I received within 10 mins. The food was not bad. Not Panda Express grade, but not authentic Chinese food (Note: this is only after one order). Somewhere in-between.

The food was simply steamed rice with batter-coated shrimp and broccoli in a Szechuan-style sauce. Didn't like how the shrimp was covered in really thick coating. Made the shrimp seem larger than they actually were. Expected a little better.

It was inexpensive, a little over $6. I'll come back if I want Chinese food 
 and not being really picky.

It should be noted that they charge 10 cents for a to-go box.

just bad. I am sure most ppl have had much better chinese food thats within the similar price range. The only reason why some ppl still frequent this place is cuz of its location I guess.  But still no. lol

I am sure many of you have noticed the "best chinese food" sign they have out just like every other chinese restaurant. Not suspicious at all.

Lotus House is my favorite restaurant on the South Side of campus.  Its fast, cheap, and delicious!  The mandarin chicken is one of my favorite things to eat anywhere. If I could eat it every day, I would.

Lotus House is my favorite Chinese food joint near campus. And yes, I've been to Great China. I have ordered a variety of menu items including Mandarin Beef, Chicken with Vegetables, Garlic Eggplant, Kung Pao Chicken, etc. and I have nearly always been pleased (I am not a fan of their noodle dishes). Portions are substantial and everything is in the neighborhood of $6-$7. The whole credit card minimum thing kind of bothers me, but otherwise, I heartily recommend this place.

Um yum. I got my pineapple-chicken fried rice around 7pm... embarked on a journey through the freezing rain up to Northside (about a 20 minute walk uphill) and didn't eat it until probably 9pm. It was still somehow piping hot and delicious. I left it out for awhile as I worked on a paper and decided to eat it again around 2am... it was cold. but still delicious. How they achieved a fried rice that stays scrumptious when it's cold is beyond me, but they did it. The boba, however, wasn't the best I've ever had.

I went here last week, and I've got to say the food's decent. I ordered the beef pan fried noodles. I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised that they actually knew how to make this dish!! (Many of the restaurants in Berkeley think that pan fried noodles is just chow mien. INCORRECT!!)

They give pretty big portions for what you pay,  but everything was just so salty. Every bite I took got saltier and saltier. I'm giving this place 4 stars cuz for the price that you pay, you get pretty good chinese food in Berkeley that actually does not contain only SOY SAUCE, SOY SAUCE, SOY SAUCE!

Their Congee is hella expensive, but pretty good.  I get the preserved duck egg one when I'm sick and I feel awesome afterward.  But seriously?  Over $5 for that shit?  Fine I'll pay for it since I don't have time!

But I really don't think this place is that great.  I'd much rather get Thai Basil for really delicious, flavorful fried rice!

Sichuan chicken was good - crispy fried with spicy sauce, but sesame chicken was gross...

This place is getting kind of pricey, decent cantonese food.

My default dishes: black bean rock cod and 100 hundred year old egg + pork congee (if you come after 10 PM there's a discount..i think).
You can all kinds of Chinese cuisine there. But a bit of skills of order are needed.

Food: 3/5
Service: 2/5
Convenience: 6/5!!!

Overall: 3.5/5

This is part of my Berkeley retrospective series. Then again, I just barely graduated a few months ago, so not much of a retrospective, hum? Anyways.

This is your typical Chinese food joint, and would be abandoned if in the middle of downtown SF. Why, then, is it packed at odd times of the week (i.e. random weekdays and never on weekends?) Why is the customer age base unusually young? And why are there so many Asian restaurants on a relatively unnoteworthy street clustered together? This, my friends, is the power of convenience for a giant public university of mostly walkers.

Now, getting to the food:

Yang Chow fried rice - when the chef is in a good mood, a nicely done dish, seasoned to a respectable saltiness and not too oily. When not, there are white clumps of rice stuck together and the dish is nasty overall. I order this frequently.

Schezuan chicken - tried it with plain rice, fried rice, fried noodles. The sweet sauce adds a bright touch, but is overpowering. Chicken can be variable, from just right to way too tough.

Beef chow fun -  Generally good, but the ratio of beef to chow fun can vary. I've had better but not in the vicinity.

Chicken/shrimp in pan fried noodle - a HK specialty. The presentation is OK, but I felt that the sauce used was excessive. Less sauce and more care to the production of said sauce would be welcome.

Drinks  - unremarkable. The Thai place a pace across has much better Thai tea. Don't really order any other drinks here.

Chili sauce - standard fare chili oil. Of course I've had better, though not necessarily in Berkeley. 

Nothing remarkable about the service. Cashier takes your order, you pick up. Table cleaning can be somewhat delayed.

They have good milk tea, I tried the canataloupe and the boba had a good chew and the flavor was really good. Their pudding tea does not have boba, but something else, the flavor was good, but it was like really soft grass jelly. 

They were voted "Best of Berkeley" for Chinese food, so of course I had to give it a shot. They had really good black pepper chicken. All in all, I was impressed and if I ever get the hankering for Chinese food, I'm running to Lotus House.

I was going to give a 5 but I decided against it.

I only go to this place for Boba. It's like effing amazing. It's almost on par with those from Ten Ren! It's kinda expensive but it's definitely worth it especially with a guy who's constantly calculating how much calories he is consuming. For me, every bit I consume better be worth the money and calories. Because a bad cup of boba leaves me very unhappy and another 30 minutes on the treadmill to burn off the calories. 

Aside from my poor humor, I am glad even after they changed owners, the boba stayed good. The food was definitely better back in the days. I guess this is why I gave it 1 star less cause I can no longer go there for the food. But this is not to say the food is bad, it's still decent.

O, the line can be long so try to go at odd hours.

Out of the Chinese places on Southside, I think this one provides the best quality compared to the rest. I usually get the szechuan chicken combo plate because it comes with an egg roll and a thai tea that usually fills the void in my stomach nicely.

Dining by the window has a nice people-watching entertainment quality to it, but sitting in the back is where to go for a private conversation where you aren't likely to be happened upon.

The only downside for me is the Cash Only policy usually necessitating a trip to the bank.
Speaking of prices, the value would increase drastically if everything was at least a $1.50 cheaper.

4 stars for their black milk tea! I love that shit. The other drinks are meh and the food is meh, but the black milk tea (easy on the sugar) is awesome. It's not overly sweet and it still has the "tea-like" flavor. It's way more expensive than its nearby competitors, but it tastes so much better, probably b/c they actually use tea instead of some powdered mix. I'm still docking a star 'cause of price. And they've charged me different amounts for the same drink on different occasions so I guess they overcharge me on some days. Plus they won't give you the special price if you get it w/o boba which NEVER made any sense to me since getting a drink w/o boba costs them less.

Price pretty good, food pretty good. But don't try something like duck dishes here. I made the mistake of trying a duck + rice combination (forgot the exact name), and it was more like duck bones with very little actual meat. Haven't been here since long, but good place to go when you're in a rush and you don't want to go too far from campus.
However, if you're in a big group and you're looking for a place to eat at like 11PM when all the other places are closing - go and ask them if they're willing to stay open. They did that for my group, and they were our lifesavers then (we were a group of college kids who were starving after a big club event...so you get the idea).

This place is a boba shop and a restaurant combined, so I'll review both components separately:

Boba

I was told this place has the best cheap boba in the Asian Ghetto area.  Sadly, I must disagree.  The pearls were a little hard for my taste and the milk tea was powdery, although it did have an interesting flavor.  I have tried some of their other flavored tea drinks (minus the boba) and they're a little better.  The 99 cent specials are nice to grab on the go - I'm partial to the kumquat tea.

I don't recommend this place for boba, but their fruity teas are worth checking out (the discounted ones, at least).

Food

This place is cleaner and nicer than the other Chinese places in the ghetto.  It's a bit more expensive, but not bad for the price.  There's a lot of seating available, especially in the back behind the counter so it's a good choice for larger groups.

The food is nothing special, but better quality than Mandarin House.  There are no dishes that stand out to me in particular but at the same time there are none that are atrociously bad.  Everything is just about average.  All of the Cantonese style dishes I've tried have a distinctively non-Cantonese flavor to them, but really, that grievance is minor.  In truth, if all their dishes just had more flavor in general, I would not have even mentioned it.

This place is worth a try, but not really a place I think is worth returning to very often.

Also, be warned, this place only takes credit card if you order $10+ in food - a bit annoying and something to keep in mind.

Not bad, really not terrible. I can see how people come here every once in awhile on a crave for Chinese food, which is how I ended up here two nights ago.

The food was a little bit too greasy, and the string beans were a little bit uncooked. The mongolian chicken was good though, and I enjoyed the green bean milk tea with pearl. I like the combo deals that they have on the first page of the menu - this place is definitely not very expensive. For the mongolian chicken, Thai iced tea, eggroll, string beans, green bean milk tea, and a TON of rice, our meal was only $15, thanks to the combo deal. The restaurant is clean and in a convenient location (right next to my apartment). The kitchen staff seem very nice too.

Overall, three stars! Maybe 3.5..

**Edit: I noticed there were no business hours posted on this page, but another plus is that they're open super late - 11:30pm on Wednesday nights.. can't say for sure the other days of the week, but probably the same!

I actually love this place. I am a regular and alternate between a few dishes.
The Mandarin Chicken is hands down the best thing ever. Whenever I have a craving for Chinese food, I come here. Other dishes I enjoy are Basil Chicken, Chicken and Broccoli, and Cashew Chicken. I like the chow fun dish as well. Of the soups, I've tried the wonton soup and the egg drop soup, and I enjoyed both of them.

I don't like the pan fried noodles or the dishes that are usually better at americanized restaurants like orange chicken. I do know people that love both of these dishes though, so it's really up to you to try them.

If you are one of those people that like thai iced tea, there is a combination deal that has an entree, an egg roll, and thai iced tea for around 7 bucks.

My friends and I go here all the time. Your food is prepared so quickly. It is pretty cheap (around 6.5 bucks). I usually split it into 2 meals, so it's pretty cost effective.

Lotus House is pretty good. They dishes are pretty standard Chinese dishes. Sometimes they are either really saucy or a little on the bland side. But I definitely enjoy going there. It also nice that they have a lot of indoor seating, unlike the rest of the restaurants in "Durant Food Court". There congee is really good when your sick, and I really like their hot almond milk tea on a cold day.
Try the Spicy Beef Noodle Soup! Super yummy, but too much is bad for the tummy

Lotus house isn't any special Chinese restaurant in the Berkeley area.  It's just one of the many choices one can choose from when they're near Durant.  For $6, you're full and have leftovers for the next day.  It would take me a while to fill up that frequent buyer card because I would rather go to the other restaurants nearby.

Meh. Haven't eaten here too often, but the food is just average. Not exciting enough for me to ever want to come here. The only fun part about this place is they actually have nice places to sit and a functional bathroom (quite rare in this college town).

It's time that I review this place...I've been here a lot of times and I don't know why I keep on coming back.

I usually get their combination platter with boba and chow mein. You add for the boba (50cents) and add for chow mein upgrade (instead of fried rice). For meats, they have a good selection of how you want it cooked, I usually get schezuan beef. Warning though, their breaded meats is usually just breading. You can't taste the meat that much. I feel like you should opt for a meat dish with no breading! Oh, their dishes are realllllly oily and greasy.

A lot of students come to this place cause it's cheap. It's chinese food... and everyone loves chinese food. Prices are decent, but not the best for the quality... I think if I want CHEAP chinese food, I'll go to Chinese Express instead.

The people here are nice and sweet though :)

Consistently good, cheap Chinese food.  Good boba tea too!  Last time I was here, a few days ago, the cashier put on a medieval soap opera right above our heads, which was kind of annoying.  It seemed like most people were getting take out, which seems like a great idea, since you end up with lots of leftovers anyway.  I ordered one of the specials posted on the wall, the seafood soup which comes with tofu and carrots, and I loved it.  It also provided me with two servings of leftovers - quite a generous portion for the $4 or $5.  I also love their heaping plates  of Singapore noodles.  Next time I will get take out, though.
A Couple Days Later: No annoying soap opera this time, but I ordered the oven-baked spare ribs.  I loved the sauce, but the ribs were more like pieces of fat.  So I would recommend the oven-baked seafood dish instead!

Tapioca sucks here. Balls= no taste, tea= no taste. Don't expect to get your drink that fast b/c the cashiers are usually busy giving ppl their food orders. Food is pretty good though. One of my favorites to get here is the Malaysian rice stick noodles. I love the curry powder that they put in the noodles. The only thing is that they use a lot of spam in their dishes instead of "real" meat. What do yu expect for $5 bucks though. This is the perfect place for college students to grab a quick bite before class. Nothing special, nothing classy. You could probably make the same dishes at home if you weren't too lazy to cook or do your laundry in the last three weeks.

Lotus house is pretty average. It's better than Mandarin House in Asian Ghetto, and definitely doesn't give me the extreme indigestion like Sun Hong Kong, but it still definitely isnt close to authentic Chinese food I can get in Cupertino or San Jose. Still, I haven't had better chinese food around the UCB area than here. I got the seafood fried rice (I actually don't know what it was because I didn't order, but it was fried rice with some seafood cooked in a thick broth layered on top) and the mongolian beef. The fried rice was okay, but the broth part bothered me a bit. The mongolian beef was pretty good; the meat was actually pretty tender and the sauce was surprisingly spicy. Overall, it was a good meal, but it defintely isn't the best chinese food I've had.
Miles above mandarin house and every other nearby south side chinese place in terms of quality.

No one makes my peach green tea with lychee jelly quite like Lotus House. I used to come here all of the time when I was a student at Cal, and some times I find myself craving their pan fried noodles or salty peppery tofu. Now I make sure to stop by here to at least get myself some pearl tea whenever I'm in the area. They are usually pretty quick to prepare your food and bring it out for you, the prices are very reasonable, and it's open late so it's perfect for a hungry, procrastinating college student!

Cash only.
Frequent location for starving college students. 

My favorite dishes: 
1. fillet rock cod with corn
This dish has a healthy portion of corn and egg on top of the fish. It's like a hybrid between corn soup and a rice dish. 
2. salt and pepper fish
This dish also has fillet rock cod on top of rice. The rock cod is fried and covered in salt and pepper, the opposite of fillet rock cod with corn.

If you are a frequent Lotus House customer, get their frequent buyer card.

Berkeley is a college town. I expect college prices and good food!

The pan fried noodles were sloppy and gross. The noodles they used were like ramen and the sauce was SUPER salty! 

The boba is also a lot pricer here when you can go around the corner for faster service. 

One word... BLEH.  

P.S. There is a $10 on credit cards!

Lotus House is one of the better Chinese places in Berkeley. When I go here, I always get the spicy garlic eggplant. I usually like my meals with tons and tons of meat (and therein, protein), but this egg plant is so good that I'm not missing it. Some will find that Lotus House is very heavy with their sauces (which I agree with), but I personally prefer more flavor to blandness so I appreciate it. The dish I get is priced at $5.75 and most are around $6-7 so it's pretty affordable no matter what you get.

Lotus House is pretty quick at delivering your food promptly and the restaurant itself is pretty clean. I like the upper floor that you're able to dine on: it's quite isolated from everything else so it's not crazy loud as the eat in areas for other places in the Asian Ghetto.

Couple notes: remember to get utensils by the door if you get takeout! They accept credit card. There is a stamp card that you should get if you're a regular.

imho it's the best place in the immediate vicinity of the asian ghetto (though that's not saying much). Portions are very generous, and the food is good, though not great. The food also tends to be salty, but it's inconsistent in this regard. Usually it suits me just fine, but occassionally it's unbearably salty. It's also open late.

edit: I've been finding hair in my food lately.... so I have to lower my rating. I should lower it more, but I'm hoping that it's just a temporary thing. I half expect to find an occasional hair at a place like this, but the recent frequency is a bit much. Alas, I no longer have a default place to go in the asian ghetto.

Really ideal for college students -- cheap, good, and in a convenient location. I had the salty fish fried rice, szechuan shrimp, and salty pepper tofu. Salty fish fried rice was good, a little more salty than I've had before. Szechuan shrimp was really good, and the salty pepper tofu was good as well (though also more salty than I'd have hope)

This is the only Chinese restaurant I eat at Berkeley.

I have been here twice and I am glad I gave this place a second chance.

the first time, I did not care for the food, but it was due mostly for ordering the wrong dish--- I ordered the Combo special with Spicy shrimp, but the shrimp, was breaded and deep fried----I hate breaded/deep fried anything---

i went back the other day and ordered Curry shrimps----i love how they served it in a glass Pyrex dish----the dish was exactly as my mom made it at home----the Pyrex dish just added to the home-made vibe. ----portions were decent and the food comes out quick-----this place is pefect for a quick solo dining meal----crowd was mainly nerdy Asians from UC Berkeley playing video games on their smartphones-

Pineapple fried rice was NASTY. don't ever order it here.  super bland, and the canned pineapples taste like they've been sitting out all week.

my friend ordered the salt and pepper chicken.  much better, but too much fat and breading.  

come here for the milk tea, not the food.  really though.

Ugh I REALLY don't like this place. Their food is terrible. They have this weird thing in their fried rice that's supposed to be egg, but it's ORANGE. I'm not sure if it's just yolk or what, but it tastes kind of strange. 

And every time I order something here, I'm not satisfied with my meal. It's too "panda express" style for me, and I really don't like fake Chinese food. 

But some of their drinks are relatively cheap. It tastes like sweethearts just a couple steps down the street, but cheaper. I like to get their green tea with pearls, no milk. I like their pearls because it's kind of sweet! Their drink is just...green tea. Nothing special.

Lotus House is alright but nothing special, which makes it good enough for your average college student.  

When I first came to this restaurant I really liked it; however, after experiencing more Chinese restaurants I came to the realization that it is one of the better Chinese restaurants that Berkeley campus area has to offer but it isn't the best compared to other Chinese restaurants out there in the Bay Area. 

The food selection is quite varied, which is nice. However, I've noticed that in the past few years they've marginally increased their prices while decreasing their serving size. I guess you have to cut costs when necessary but when you do that to a college-aged demographic, they'll definitely notice it. 

I would recommend going here once in a while, but if you're familiar with Chinese cuisine I don't think this place will sweep you off your feet. 

(P.S. The boba is alright but not "Voted #1 in Berkeley" as its sign suggests)

I just came back from eating here and...
no, just no.

My order didn't taste good at all. I got Beef Pan Fried Noodles and milk tea. My milk tea didn't even come with ice, so it was all warm... and I thought the special was that it was 99 cents, but the cashier charged me 1.55 for it. My pan fried noodles.. ugh, the gravy was just horrible. It looked all gooey and suspicious. That pretty much ruined everything for me. The meat was too chewy. So much msg and salt in it. My parents own a Chinese restaurant, so I know what good Chinese food tastes like.. I thought this restaurant would be the better Chinese place out of ones in the area, but if tihs is the best one, eek, I don't even want to know how the others taste! 

Maybe I'm being too critical for the first time, but I wouldn't come back here. Maybe I'd come back for the milk tea, but not the food.

I am obligated to review this place as I probably wouldn't have made it through school without this restaurant.

My friend and I usually came here for substantial, fast, delicious Chinese lunch and sometimes dinner.  Even though we made attempts to try different dishes, we always ended up getting only a few items on the menu because we got hooked!  BBQ pork or Shrimp Chow Mein, wonton noodle soup, fried rice, beef stew noodle soup are our favorites.  Their bubble teas are ok (and kind of necessary if you order stir fried Chow Mein which is uber peppery but soooo delicious!)

This place is probably better for take out because the tables are pretty close to each other.  Though they have more spacious upstairs dining area, it isn't pristine clean.  Oh, one more thing, every time you order, make sure to get a stamp on the card.  Once you fill up all the spots on the card (I think 8-10), then you get a free meal!

Probably the best Chinese place in the area, at least for it's price. Kinda greasy, though.

It's pretty good value, though, which is what you need if you're a student like me! I like getting their combo plates--main dish, steamed or fried rice (or chow mein for something like fifty cents more), egg roll and Thai iced tea, usually for around six or seven dollars depending on what entree. They serve you pretty quickly, and there's always seating available.

Much, much better than Mandarin Garden. Like I said, best cheap Chinese food in the area.

I ordered the shrimp with lobster sauce.  It was cheap, filling and tasty enough to keep my taste buds alive.  Are you going to have the culinary experience of your life?  Only if you've been eating moldy cardboard boxes.  But are you going to get a decent rice dish at an affordable price?  Yes.

The food here is cheap and fast. Don't expect anything to fancy, especially from the service. There's no "hello" or "thank you".  

If you want good chinese food, I wouldn't go here. 

If you order "to go" they charge you a couple cents more.
the food is decent & the portion for the price is definitely worth it. get a milk tea for 99 cents w/ the meal if u're a fan of boba :P

I went here for dinner with a friend and we ordered seafood chow fun and mongolian beef. The seafood chow fun was not too bad - I've been craving chow fun for a while, so it was satisfying in that sense, but it was too salty! We shared our dishes so it wasn't so bad; I can't imagine eating a whole plate of that myself, as much as I love chow fun.

The mongolian beef was too saucy...it didn't really taste right. We finished off the chow fun pretty easily and had a fight over who would take rest of the mongolian beef home...cuz neither of us wanted it. =P

I must admit though, the price isn't too bad. We didn't finish half the mongolian beef, not because it was bad, but because we were really full already. On first glance, the portions seem pretty reasonable for one person, but one dish easily filled us both. I think it's due to the extraordinary amount of oil and sodium...

Maybe 2 stars is a bit harsh, since this place is at least better than Panda Express.

P.S credit card accepted over $10

WARNING: extremely salty foods. no joke, you'll be begging for water after finishing a meal here. 

i only come here for plain old regular hot milk tea with boba (their fruit slushie/breezie/icee/whatever they call it are pretty gross and powdery) and their salt and pepper tofu. ask for very very very little salt on the tofu, and it will be an acceptable level of saltiness.
