those are the only good things in my opinion. try sun hong kong for cheap, less salty chinese food (but it's not much better) and try sweethearts for cheaper boba.

Well, their menu is cheap, and their portions are quite good. I don't drink tea, so I can't comment on the boba. I find that some of the chicken dishes are not as good, but the fried noodles, porridge and the chow fun are nice. There's a lack of vegetable dishes though.

What I really like are the specials they put on paper on the walls. Oven baked fish is awesome and probably my favorite dish, Portuguese chicken isn't bad, mango chicken and basil curry chicken fried rice are also good. The beef noodle soup is REALLY spicy though, so I'd p ass on that.

I eat here once or twice a week, so it's a staple.

I've probably walked by Lotus House at least 20 times and finally decided to give it a try when my favorite place to get pan-fried noodles wasn't opened yet.  I noticed that they had Hong Kong style so I was game.  My husband and I were very disappointed.  The noodles were not crispy and they tasted borderline-stale.  The redeeming dish was their "Salty Pepper" squid.  That dish had good flavor, but cost more and had a smaller portion than at my fave down the street.  Save your money and your tastebuds and go to Sun Hong Kong!

Love their food! I had a plate of pork chow mein and the portion is good size for the money as was all the other plates I saw and tasted great! MUCH better quality food than Chinese fast food chains for the same price! The only negative is that the eating area itself was hot and stuffy, maybe the air conditioning was down.  However, Lotus will be a must stop for me whenever I visit Berkeley.

After helping my little sister move into her new place, my family and I walked down the block and into this little restaurant for dinner. We had a red bean blizzard, passionfruit ice, and mango ice. I wanted a green bean ice, but they said they were out :( They come with the sealed lid, which was pretty handy since my sister knocked the thing over right after she stuck in the straw. As for food, we had a beef noodle soup and those thick flat noodles (I forget the name...my mom ordered). We loved the beef noodle soup. There were lots of beef chunks, and they were all nice and tender. We liked the noodles too, but they were on the greasy side and we drank tons of water afterward to wash out the MSG.
My mom struck up a conversation with the cook/owner, so the service ended up being pretty good overall. The cook/owner pointed out that they received the 2010 and 2009 award for best Chinese food in the area. The place has been open for about 3 years. 
One weird part was that the lady who finished making my passionfruit drink just left it on the counter without saying anything and looked at me funny when I went to go pick it up.

Oh, Lotus House: the first Chinese restaurant I ate near campus. 

For the two times I've gone here, I've always come in for dinner with friends. First time I ordered the mango chicken, which...wasn't all that bad, but I was kind of confused as to why it was served to me in a large glass casserole dish....made me wonder if they ran out of plates or something. I felt that the ratio of mango chicken to rice was good. However, the flavor was just not there. I couldn't help but wonder if the chefs just relied on the mangos to tenderize and marinate the chicken. Maybe they were trying to keep the dish "light," but if so, the size of the dish kind of eliminates that goal, haha. 

In any case, I wish they would have put more flavor into the chicken itself. After I finished it, yes, I was full, but I wasn't satisfied. :(

The second time I came, I ordered the black pepper beef, which was better than the mango chicken--by means of having more flavor. There was a generous portion of beef, but I wished they balanced it out by putting more vegetables into it...to make the dish less heavy and overwhelming. Having that much beef and rice on one plate with about a 1/4 of the intended vegetables can get pretty heavy. Overall, though, I must say it was more satisfying than mango chicken.

Just as the two-star rating states, "Meh. I've experienced better." However, for the large portion sizes and price, it's pretty decent for a college student.
Since I've been learning Mandarin, I enjoy stopping in here to get lunch and meeting people that also speak Mandarin. The food here is alright, but nothing to write home about.

Quality: I think what makes this place charming, is the fact it tastes like something your mom would make at home. However, like with food at home, it's really hit or miss. If anything, I would recommend the shrimp chow mein.

Venue: There's another room in the back and has a TV that plays the local Asian channel. 

Accessibility: Super walkable from southside, or take the 51B to Durant and Telegraph.

Nearby: the Durant Food Court, Bank of America

Hopes: Have more descriptions of their food in the menu. 

Tip: CASH ONLY.

Will I come back? Probably, out of convenience.

i'd only give the food here 2 stars max, but for the low prices, i'll throw in another one. Don't expect anything fancy because you get what you pay for- MSG-loaded sauces and an unreasonable amount of onions to compensate for minimal meat in all of the "meat dishes". Still though, if you want some decent (and edible) Chinese food close to campus, this is really the best option. Lots of people like the baked rice here, but in my opinion it's overly creamy and saucy. My regulars are sichuan beef noodle soup and mapo tofu. The beef noodle soup can't compare with anything you'd find at Liang Mama's or any other Taiwanese joint, but for the price and portion (under 7 bucks for a big bowl), I'd say it's a pretty good deal. Their mapo tofu definitely hits the spot whenever I'm feeling shitty or just having a bad day, though sometimes it can get overly salty and the sauce mixes with the rice too much. The salt and pepper tofu is a pretty good appetizer too, perfect for when I want something small on the way home from class. Don't order their drinks.

Meh. 

Sure, it was cheap, and they gave me lots of food (I got the combo plate mongolian chicken with Thai Tea/egg roll/rice), but I've had better Chinese food with similar portions @ similar prices.  (Albeit at home, not on southside.  It's been hard to find a decent Chinese restaurant over here; I'd say Mandarin House is probably better, but that's not really saying much....)  

The food was definitely laden with MSG and a little too greasy for my taste.  The Thai tea, however, I was a fan of: it wasn't too sickeningly sweet like at some Thai restaurants/tea places, but, on the other hand, it didn't have as strong of a tea (cardamom/vanilla I think?) flavor as I normally expect/like. (So, I guess, kind of weak all around...?)  I might come back and try out some of the other milk teas (test out that "Best Tapioca in Town" thing), but I don't plan on ordering the food here again.

Maybe 2.5.

MSG-sprinkled Chinese on the go! Why they are charging extra for to-go boxes, I will not know. Nor do I look kindly upon that.

But it's cheap, and it's Chinese, what did you expect?

Once upon a time, this place was great. Good portions, good food, reasonable prices. 

That time is gone now. Now your pan fried noodles are some noodles from Top Ramen, your fried fish is caked in an inch-thick layer of batter, your tea is major suck, and everything else uniformly tastes like ass. With raised prices. Run far, far away from this atrocity. They don't even bother to play movies on their three TVs anymore while you wait too long for your food. Also a $10 minimum on credit cards. Why not just go to Chang Luong upstairs?

This place sucks. i'm on my fifth liter of water after the meal, and about to begin a round of pu-erh. the lady who worked the register was quite honest and admitted that lotus house uses msg as a key ingredient in their food. 

I ordered mongolian chicken which came with a heaping mound of rice, and some chow fun (rice noodles). everything tasted good, probably from the msg. nothing was spectacular taste wise but i was full before i finished my entire meal. 

The milk tea was very sweet, too sweet for my taste. i had high expectations for the "best chinese place in berkeley in 2009' and for having the 'best tapioca in town.' 

A disturbing scene bid me farewell as i descended the steps which passed the kitchen.  I witnessed a man (who I assumed to be a chef) squatting with his feet on the stove. His back was turned to me but I assumed he was scrubbing the stove in a best case scenario. 

I will not be returning here during my last year as an undergraduate at UC Berkeley. 

edit: two hours later, still parched from msg dehydration headache. Hello, Tylenol.

Recently, I had a chance to visit Berkeley.  It's been a long time since I've been back to Berkeley.  Lots of restaurants and stores have changed since my college days.  So when I saw the Lotus House claiming to have the best tapioca in town on their sign, I had to give this place a try.

By the way, this review is solely focused on their pearl tea drink (specifically the pearl milk green tea), rather than the decor, food, etc.

The drink that I choose for judging is always the pearl milk green (or jasmine) tea.  Why the milk green tea?  The reason is because it's much harder to make a good tea drink than a super-sweet artificially flavored drink.  If a place can make a good green tea, then they can easily make the other drinks as well.

Scores (1 for worst - 5 for best)

Tea (3.5) - The tea is not super-sweet and allows the tea flavor to come through.

Pearl Consistency (2) - Unfortunately, the pearls were on the hard-side.  Not quite as soft as I would have liked.

Pearl Taste (3) - The pearls themselves are slightly sweet but just average tasting.

Value (3) - The drinks are about average value.  The price is just OK and the size of the cup is average.

Ice (3) - I hate a drink that has too much ice.  Not only do you get less tea, but it makes it harder to get to those last few pearls once you've finished the drink.  It also dilutes the tea when it melts.  This drink had 

Total Score: 14.5 out of 25

So overall, my impression was that their pearl drinks are slightly below average.  Unfortunately this place does not live up to their claim of being the best tapioca in town.  Even without trying the other tapioca places, I would have to guess that you can find better elsewhere.
This place is a joke after new management came in. They don't even turn on all 50 LCDs anymore.

I go there for the pearl milk tea, but the past three times I've tried to get some, to my surprise, this place is closed! They appear to get an abundance in business when they're open, however the woman who appears to be the mom (the dad cooks and the daughter works the cash register) always seems tired and irritated. I just try to be extra nice but it goes without saying, the customer service is pretty shitty.

Good pudding milk tea though!

I admit that in my younger and naive days, I used to frequent this place often mainly due to its convenience and my desperate longing for Chinese food. I eventually moved onto Great China, but I recently went back to Lotus House after realizing that I only needed a couple more stamps on my frequent diner card to earn a free meal. Um...I don't think the free meal is even worth it. Lotus House somehow managed to mess up a staple in Chinese food...the white rice. I don't know if this is a newfangled recipe they're trying out or if I just never noticed before, but the rice was dry and almost stale tasting. My disgust with the rice almost allowed me to ignore my msg-ridden tofu beef.

OK, OK... yes, the woman behind the counter speaks deplorable English.  Fine, so what?  Their green milk tea is incredible.  Suck it up.

...and theeeeen.

I've been here a couple of times and found the experience to be decent every time. The most recent time I went I ordered kung pao chicken (don't ask why, someone just suggested it, don't stone me) and a wonton noodle soup for someone else. As some of these other reviews mention - the portions are good. I was fasting that day so I hasn't eaten for about 10 hours and was full off my chicken and pudding milk tea boba. The kung pao chicken tasted okay - saucy and spicy with chicken breast white meat. As much as I usually like breast meat, it was a bit off w/ chinese food. Not to say it was bad. Just strange.

The soup noodle was actually quite good - nice broth and good hearty pieces of wonton and of course big portions. Definitely hit the spot on a cold night (I shared the two dishes).

For what it is - a cheap place by campus with big portions - I definitely think this place is worth checking out if not revisiting every once in a while.

Also just FYI - credit cards only for $10 or more on order.

I wish I could like this place more because it's so close and convenient to my apartment, and the food is actually decent.  I'm a fan of their tomato fried rice and chicken cream corn.  However, I've had such terrible experiences with the service here that I actually hate coming into this place (but I do still do it when I crave their food).

They are always extremely curt and have never once smiled or been even pleasant.  My worst experience was one cold afternoon when I got a hot milk tea, and she tipped it over on the counter and it spilled all over my precious new white wool coat.  While she did make me a new tea, she didn't even seem very sorry and still made me pay for my drink.  

The service there is just so unfriendly that I can't justify liking Lotus House even though I like their food from time to time.

Pros:
Big Screen TV w/ movies 

Cons:
Food is just averge to below averge.
Over priced for a small plate of chinese food / drinks.
Cashiers have attitude problems. (it's normal though because they are probably getting minimum wages....)
Everything is self-served. 

If you want to kill your time with your friends, this is a good place to sit in.
If you are looking for good food, stay away.

I was feeling way too lazy to cook that night, so I swung by Lotus House after work for a quick and cheap dinner.

I ordered the House Chow Mein, which I found to be rather disappointing. The chow mein itself was a bit bland and not very tasty, and the additional meats and veggies weren't too good either!

The last few occasions I've gone,  I've been fairly impressed with the quality of the rice plates, given the price, but I guess their noodles just don't match up!

Either way, Lotus House is a great place for cheap, Asian food, but don't expect too much because you DO get what you pay for!

I have a real love-hate relationship with this place.

Love:
First of all, it's fast. So fast that sometimes I think they microwave it.
It's tasty. So tasty that I've had dreams about their orange chicken. (OK it's not actually dream inducing good, but it really is not bad at all).
They have beef noodle soup, and you can ask them to make it even hotter/spicier.
And importantly it is cheap!

Hate:
The service is TERRIBLE. They will ignore you while you wait. Seriously. I hate dealing with the people who work there.
The boba is ridiculously sugary. I guess most probably are, but they just take giant scoops of sugar and put them in your tea right in front of you while you imagine the chemical processes that turn the sugar into fat :(

Overall I do come here at least once every couple of weeks, but I've made a conscious decision to NOT be a regular. Hopefully you guys have better experiences!

Lotus House is just ok Chinese food. Nothing special with its MSG-laden foods. Do appreciate that it has beef noodle soup, which none of the other Chinese restaurants seem to have, and it's also fairly cheap. Dishes are around $6-7. Come here to eat only if it's convenient.

The food here is REALLY inexpensive and they have a very full menu with lots of options, which is very very cool.

Service is no-frills. They yell out your order and repeat it over and over until you pick it up... "Kung Pao Chicken...Kung Pao Chicken...Kung Pao Chicken...Kung Pao Chicken..." Totally reminded me of Ben Stein in Ferris Bueller's Day Off but with intonation.

Lots of varieties of boba tea, and it was cheap. LOVE that.

Food itself was so-so... but for the price, it's hard to complain. Three-star food with five-star prices = four-star restaurant in my book.

We needed cheap, within walking distance, and still open at 10pm food. This is where we ended up. For $20ish we got the Hot and Sour soup, House Special chow fun, and 2 curry fried rice? I think that's what it was called. And 2 drinks.

Food was ok and the portions were generous. Soup was super thick. Someone was heavy handed with the corn starch in the kitchen. The chow fun was ok. Noodles came in chucks and sometimes lacked flavor. Lacked the usual abundance of veggies. The fried rice was ok with a what seemed to be a coconut curry with shrimp and a tomato based curry with chicken. 

To drink I had the pudding milk tea that I thought came with pudding but didn't. They said they ran out and asked if I wanted boba. I said sure and still got charged extra. Not sure how that worked out. Oh well. 

Service is nonexistent but normal for these type of places. Quick and dirty. Ah the joys of eating like a college student again...

The Honest Truth: Lotus house is my go to for chinese food in berkeley (although there aren't many chinese places in Berkeley).  The food is decent, but nothing special.  I would avoid anything with sauce as they are usually pretty saucey.  It's an average, 3-star, asian ghetto place to eat.  Make sure you pay in cash! and get a stamp card.

The Details:  I frequent Lotus House pretty often.  They have pretty fast service especially compared to thai basil or gypsy's.  I appreciate that a lot. I enjoy most of the dishes with fish.  The fish with black bean sauce and the spicy salty fish are two good options.  I also like the Japanese-style stir-fried udon.  As I said above, if you get any dish with sauce, there is usually an over-abundance of sauce.  I would also avoid the boba.  The creamer that they use for the milk tea tastes powdery and I would definitely go to a different place in Asian ghetto for boba.  They charge you a little extra if you get it to go as well. Overall, since there aren't many chinese places in berkeley, I would recommend Lotus House.  Don't expect really good, quality chinese food like you would get from oakland china town, but for a college student that wants some quick chinese food, it's definitely a good option. Lotus house ranks pretty highly  for me on my list of places to eat in Asian ghetto.

Berkeley doesn't have much good Chinese food, so thank goodness for Lotus House!  I would definitely choose this place over that Mandarin place in Asian Ghetto.  They serve a lot of food for the money you pay.  I can see why some people would complain about service, but I've never had too bad of an experience there.  Nothing I wouldn't already expect out of a Chinese restaurant.  It's also a really good, quick place for a to-go meal.  The food is also really good and authentic though a little on the greasy side.  I also love that there are so many options on the menu.  They serve all the typical chinese dishes.  I always get chow fun or wonton noodles along with a pearl milk tea.  The milk tea is also pretty good considering its only 99 cents with the meal though probably not as good as sweethearts.  Also, remember to get the frequent buy card for a free meal!

so as a first time visitor, i didn't realize how lotus house worked.  there's a small dining area in the front of the restaurant you can choose to sit to eat, and apparently there's a larger back room too.

why am i telling you this?

well, gather 'round, kids.  it's story time.

i ventured into lotus house hungry and saw the line at the counter.  Ok, cool, i thought.  i'll just put in my order, find a seat and wait for my noms and then chow before heading out to study.  so following the crowd, i squeezed into the tiny area to order, grabbed a menu to quickly decide on something as i approached the counter, and ordered a combination plate to get some sweet sugary breaded chicken concoction with rice and surprise! a tea too.  really?  you get tea, too?  and an egg roll?  that seriously has to be the best combination deal on chinese food in the bay area.

well, as i squeezed into the tiny, overcrowded front room to order and wait for a table, i lugged my bookbag over my shoulder and reached into it to find my wallet to pay.  while i did this, the chach in line next was advancing in the line and seriously in need of some education on personal space.   sure, this is small and you want to put your order in, but man, keep your jock strap on.

i pay, put the wallet away, and sling the bag over my shoulder in confusion feeling pushed aside and unsure of what to do next.  the woman hands me the surprise tea (i'm sure it wouldn't have been a surprise had i just *read* the menu, but chachy mcchacherson wasn't really allowing me time to peruse) and i turn to find a decent table in what i thought was the only room to eat.

chachy mcchacherson has already paid for his food, and between "dude" 's and "totally" 's i turn to find a table.

...right as mr. rushy chachy mc chacherson steps forward invading my personal space AGAIN thinking i was apparently going to the back room to sit down.

remember that big ol' book bag i had slung over my shoulder?  that big ol' book bag punched mr. chach right in the nads.

and mr. chach actually looked at me like i did it on purpose, all the while he had been pushing me along the line and not allowing me to get past.

booo.

that part made me laugh.  my mind literally said "let that be a lesson in personal space to you" to the jock, and i found a table in the front window while i waited for my food.

all this babble of a story is for this purpose:  lotus house has a huge menu.  but not a huge space.  take a look at the menu before you go wait in line, since during the dinner rush you won't really have the space or the time to get everything in order.  and if you're confused about where to go, there's a bunch of seating *everywhere* that i apparently missed.

the food was good- a sizable portion and as i mentioned earlier, actual combinations without paying extra for all the little details.  the tea that came with it?  perfect.  

i think i vote three stars, only because without being a seasoned regular and understanding the flow of the restaurant, one can easily hit someone in the nads.

and that's just not a good time for anyone.

but darn good combos. and decent tasting food.

I've come here a couple of times before, but never really thought about reviewing it until now. Lotus House is a well known Berkeley establishment. Some might call it an alternative to Asian Ghetto, which is kind of how I see it. It definitely beats out Mandarin House, but it for sure isn't the best Chinese place around. For the price, variety, and size, I consider it pretty good.

Last time, I got the Singapore Style Chow Fun. Your typical chow fun with eggs, ham, shrimp, and random vegetables. I feel like the whole dish was prepared pretty well. Tons of flavor, just a tad bit spicy, and a large portion. I shared this with a friend and it kept me full for the rest of the night. The only downside is that there's barely and seafood or spam in there for a dish of its size. You really have to dig in to find the good stuff sometimes.

If you're a college student on a budget or going to eat with a fairly sized group, Lotus House is perfect. You won't be disappointed, but don't expect the best.

mann i don't know what to say. this is my second time coming here. i always come here cause its open late and an asian place that accepts cards. haha the food is okay ... a bit on the salty side. but the girl that works there was very nice and friendly

Lotus House gets five stars because it's exactly what I want it to be, and it's the best at being what it is.  It isn't the first Chinesesque restaurant I would recommend to someone visiting Berkeley, but it is a personal first choice in the context of my hurried and otherwise tedious college life.  

What I mean to say is that Lotus House is the best place in the world to go if you if you are in Berkeley, near campus, on foot, on a budget, on a tight schedule, and in the mood for Asian food.  It beats anything else in the Asian ghetto; that's for sure.  You get more complexity, variety, and olfactory pleasure for the same value and convenience.

Their menu is vast enough and the items exotic enough (at least to me) that I never get tired of it; I wouldn't have any problem with going here two days in a row.  And I always leave a little too full, because I can't resist finishing everything on my plate and they tend to give you more food than you need. 

Lotus House is not a dining adventure, but I recommend  it in the way someone might recommend their preferred brand of toothpaste.

Ugh, this was dreadful.  I've had some bad fast food Chinese in my day but this made Panda Express look high quality.  Seriously.  I had the kung pao chicken thinking, no one messes that up.  Wrong.  It tasted like chicken and soy sauce with absolutely no other flavor.  To be fair, the chow mein was fine if super greasy.

The only thing going for this place is the price.  It's bargain basement low - but you will certainly get what you pay for.

Good chinese food that's close to campus!  I'd pick lotus house over mandarin house anyday... it's not only nicer inside, but the food tastes better and the portions are bigger.  Plus, they give you these cards that you can stamp every time you buy a meal or boba.. which will add up in 4 years for sure :)

I usually came for lunch and just got their special, which included a side of rice or chow mein, a main dish you can chose from, and thai iced tea.  Nice and cheap.

Got preserved egg & pork congee again b/c of a bad cold. 

Also got BBQ chow mein. 

Food came quickly and the total was around $11. I got home and only ate half the congee and noodles and was already full! 

The leftovers made a great lunch for the next day.

As a Berkeley student, every time I thought I found a new favorite Chinese dish here, the next dish of the same thing would be a disaster. For example, one time my favorite dish was the beef pan fried noodles. After getting beef that was indistinguishable from brown rubber I quit that dish. Then my favorite turned into some shrimp with veggies over rice dish. After seeing lots of black spines remaining on the back of all the shrimp I quit that dish too. Another time my favorite dish was the wonton noodle soup. After I questioned whether eating wonton meat would be healthy I quit that dish too! 

I don't know. This restaurant is popular because it is in a great location where everyone can see it. 

3 stars for service and ambiance 
1 star for food
I like the fish fillet with sweetcorn over rice. I don't remember If I ever got anything else from here.  It was not very expensive and they have a lot of items on their menu.

I have some misplaced affection for this place, though I won't kid myself that it's anything special at all. But sometimes one just wants a plate of unchallenging, greasy beef chow fun, and Lotus House is as unchallenging and greasy as they come. The noodles are surprisingly decent, and there are no major flaws in the execution. Yeah, there isn't a trace of wok hay, and given the main ingredients and a tanker of oil, you could make something just as good. But you didn't.

I've only had one thing here before-- the portuguese chicken

SO GOOD!!! My friend saw me eating it once and now he always talks about it. It's pretty unhealthy though but I just love curry.

The stars are strictly for the Tapioca drinks we order, I have not tried the food here. I tried this place for the first time since it was next door to my sister's apt while she was at Berkeley and they are open really late. 

The passion fruit tapioca drink is really good. I'm not a fan of honeydew but everyone I go with always insists on the honeydew icer which is really good. Coconut and mango are also good flavors to try and the tapioca is fresh. The sealed top makes it idea to carry around and tote or place in the car without it spilling, and then you can pierce the top when your ready to drink it. 

Only accepts cash, there is a Bank of America atm outside on the corner of the street. Parking is street, metered and timed. We make it a point to go here anytime were visiting Telegraph/ Durant in Berkeley.

Damn i used to think paying a premium for tea here would be better - and it used to be good before MANAGEMENT CHANGED (see a trend here?).

They have this new specials menu that has Beef Stew Noodle Soup (one of my favorites) so I'm curious to try it sometime for redemption, but I doubt the broth is going to be anything decent...

Alas, the tea is now teh sux0r too along with the food :(.

Has an incentive program - 10 stamps (entrees only) and free $5.75. Rip-off! I'm sure prices used to be much lower, but now the prices are a bit higher and $5.75 can't really buy you anything there.

That said, probably the busiest chinese place in "Durant Square" aka asian ghetto. Yummy food, would recommend their 2-style fried rice (creamy sauce and tomato sauce) and also baked seafood. 

Dang, writing this review made me hungry...

Even the drinks aren't that good at this place. The artificial flavors taste way too artificial. Gross.

The young guy that works the register isn't terribly informed as to what goes in the dishes. My heart partial goes out to him because he reminds me of a clueless younger brother. BUT STILL. 

"What's in this noodle dish?"
"Spam."
"Oh, I don't like spam. What about this noodle dish?"
"Some meat of some kind. Like chicken, I think."
"Chicken? Okay I'll get the Singapore style noodles then."

Orders up! And it's the Indonesian style noodles. With spam. 

"This isn't what I ordered."
"Sorry, is this okay though?"
"No, I don't like spam."
"Can't you pick around it?"
"No, I don't like spam. This isn't what I ordered."

Orders up! Part two, the second try. The order's right...but the noodles are still littered with SPAM.

Saying no to spam means you get more spam. WTF.

That, on top of three televisions blaring out some bad Vin Diesel saves the world from Russian terrorists amidst having "sexy soft core porn fun" movie makes for an unfortunate and uncomfortable atmosphere. If I wanted tits with my meal, I'd go to a strip club and eat buffalo wings.

The dirty? Quick and cheap.

Boba is $1. Food is around or under $7, with a free stamp card (10 meals = free $5.45 purchase).

Lots of indoor seating, but always feels super stuffy... especially in the summertimes. 

Not a place I would recommend if you're visiting Berkeley, but a good place for college students who are simply in need of cheap food.

I don't understand why people still call this place the Asian Ghetto. The prices are not "ghetto." In my first year of undergrad that Korean BBQ place was $4.99 for a #1. Now it's $7.49. Not ghetto at all.

The only place that didn't really raise its prices is this place. It looks kind of shabby from the outside and from the inside, but the lighting is adequate and the bathroom is "relatively" clean.

Now why the 5 stars? Because they have the best shrimp chow mein in all of Berkeley. It's a bit salty but they give you a huge glass of water when you ask for one. Perfect for washing down all that Na+. They always give you 7 to 8 pieces of shrimp, and they are big shrimp, not the baby shrimp you find in cup noodles. The noodles are fat and juicy. The cabbage has just the right crunchiness and they also put just the right amount of onion to give it a sweet sweet aroma.

Their tofu chicken rice is pretty good, too.

Don't get anything else. I'm serious. The shrimp chow fun has shrimps smaller than cup noodle shrimp. The roasted duck is all bones. The salt and pepper cod is too salty and too peppery. Just get the shrimp chow mein and all is good in the world.

Oh, the boba is okay, I guess. But the best deal is the grape juice or the pineapple juice. 99 cents and you can dunk your cup of water in it to make about 1 liter of bloody good diluted juice. Cheaper than Arizona tea.

i really like the older chinese lady. she reminds me of that aunt that says rude things at family reunions, but the youngsters love her anyway because she has some overwhelming redeeming quality (she's a great cook, she always brings sweets, she cleans up after everyone, she packs a fat hong bao, etc.) anyway, you silly americans and your need for things like "service" and "etiquette," when you aren't even tipping. my eyes hurt because they are rolled so far back into my head.

in other news, the food is pretty good. if you are looking for an asian dish on rice - Come here instead of going to Thai Basil. the ingredients are 'fresher' and the portions of everything (not just the rice) are very generous.
Last time I had szechuan eggplant and the szechuan beef noodle soup. both were of restaurant quality that I expected before I went to college (meaning, pretty good.) there was so much food I left half of the noodles in a to-go box for a hobo to pick up, the next morning it was gone. obviously someone else, other than me, thought it was pretty good.

It's probably just me, but I enjoy eating at Lotus House.  Especially if it is cold outside.  It is an alternative for eating in the cold at the Asian Ghetto right next door.  They have a wide range of dishes from soups to rice plates to appetizers such as popcorn chicken.  

I hardly order their boba here.  But from what I can remember, their boba pearls are pretty hard.  That's why if i were to order their drinks from here, I normally order the black milk tea with egg pudding.  Delicious.

I 99% of the time order the Satay beef chow fun.  I am not a big fan of how they add in pineapples in the dish but otherwise, I love it!  I am a big fan of thick rice noodles with anything!  Especially with gravy sauce!  They give you a good amount for $6.  I am not complaining!

Another favorite is their baked dishes over rice.  Pretty good here.  I haven't actually had the too much salt problem in my orders but this might be because I tend to like my food a bit saltier.

This place brings back good memories of my college days where group meetings or hangouts happen in the upper deck of Lotus House.

This place has been here for so long, but I went here for the first time today.  It just never appealed to me in the beginning.  If I had known that there was a back room, I think I would've gone here sooner.   The menu has tons of choices. I decided to go for the salty pepper pork combo. It comes with an egg roll, choice of egg or white rice, and a thai tea drink.  All for just $7.56 after tax. 

The food came out in about 5 minutes, but it went by fast while watching the olympics on the their available tv.  Theres plenty of pork, but not enough of rice to go with it, which is a good thing. The salt is pretty tasty (is that you msg?) and the cabbage below is a great way to balance out the deep fried fat.  

I look forward to trying the other dishes here!

Want to pay with credit card? There's a $10 minimum.

let's stop making fun of asian people. So their english isn't so good, who gives a shit really. It's the food that matters. TIC(This Is Chinatown), so get over it. Well, it's not chinatown, but you get the point. 

delicious and generous plates at the right price . The boba is good too. can't really go wrong here. 

parking sucks just like anywhere in berkley

School's back in session and the Lotus House is full! Short Rib Chow Fund w/Black Bean Sauce, Beef w/String Beans Over Rice, Pepper Pork Chops, it's all good. Massive portions you'll be taking home. Down a star since you have to bus your own table with the rare staff to wipe down the table.

my working/studying/reading hotspots in this beloved college town, depending on my wallet:

$$$ elmwood cafe / masse patisserie
$$ sacks / a cuppa tea
$ lotus house
0 library

At Lotus House, I get what I pay for. I pay a couple bucks for no more service than what's required to make the drink, then I get unlimited stay at the place, though this would not exceed more than a couple hours because I'd go crazy after that. Plus, I get to watch all the Asian pop music videos all I want in a spacious, wooden loft area, which I love (the former, not as much). What a deal, right? 

Now the trick to actually getting any work done at this place is to sit in the loft area around the kitchen and counter, not the dining area in the front with all the windows and passerbys looking in. The wall between the two seating areas provide a bit of a buffer between all the students coming in and out. I wouldn't bring a thesis to write either. Just bring a book.

This is a review based almost entirely on the congee. Some of the other food, especially the American style Chinese food looks not so great. Why people order lemon chicken is beyond my comprehension.

I like congee a lot. I never know where to find congee in Berkeley, and then Lotus House opened and answered my congee prayers. The congee here is cheap, huge, made fresh and hot and is a really satisfying lunch. I wish they had more fixings like peanuts and green onions and fish sauce and those little dried anchovies, but they do have hot sauce and soy and they have several meats and things you can add to the plain congee, so I don't really need all the extra stuff.

Man, eff this place, it's all about Golden Garden down there in Costa Mesa, but if you're in Warrior-country (what the hell am I talking about) and you're looking for some homemade style Chinese food, then this is the place to go.  Their hot almond milk teas are delicious, that dude who always wears socks with his Adidas sandals is a sweetheart, and that lady who shits herself if you put the dishes in the tub above the trash can instead of giving them to her are all noteworthy items.  In addition, I like that the bathroom key comes attached to a manhole cover so you don't forget where it is.  Most important, however, is that this place reminds me of home.

Okay wait, let me back track for a minute.  The authenticity of this place is definitely debatable, but for brevity's sake, let's just say that if your  Mom opened up her own Chinese restaurant but then had to deal with a bunch of spoiled-rotten, formerly nerdy-looking but still nerdy at heart Asian kids who had just recently been liberated from their Minhy parents so she started making Chinese food that kinda tasted like what she normally made at home just for you but with a few American-born tweaks thrown in there like orange chicken, sesame beef, and pepper chicken, then Lotus House would be your family heirloom.  

This hypothetical situation, of course, assumes that you're a Chinaman, like me.  So you feel me- right, my ninja?

Wait, what?  I can't hear you, speak up...What? You're white?  Why the hell are you even looking up this spot, then, guy?  You got no business poking your blond head in here.  Don't you have a pressing game of Parcheesi and a Blimpie submarine sandwich to attend to?  Jesus, get the kluck outta here, mang.
It's not the best place I've enjoyed boba tea (because the boba was too soggy), but it is the first place I've gone and had Rose Tea with actual rose petals in it. Well, shit, ain't that fancy?

Lotus House gets grosser and grosser each time I come back. It's amazing. At some point it must stop, right?

The food is too salty and the drinks are way too sweet...I had to keep pouring water into mine to drown out the horrible saccharine taste. NASTY.

This place used to be a cafe for a long time until it became a Cantonese restaurant. Curious about the sign that says "Best Tapioca in Town" I dropped in on a whim eager for a taste challenge. After all, this declaration of supremacy happens to be posted up high on the store front, and just a few doors down from one of my regular tapioca/boba places, Sweeeeeetheart (wink!).

Wait, let me roll up my sleeves.

Once inside, there were colorful pictures and written signs featuring their dishes posted on the wall and counter. There were also several catchy signs that were just brilliant. The one by the register says "We are the best at what we do: The best Chinese restaurant in town" certified by the local student newspaper, The Daily Cal. Then right by the window, another sign that says "No outside food or drinks" and finally "Please clean your own table". 

Startled, I thought to myself "That's a first". 

I've been craving for shrimps with scrambled eggs over rice for the past week so that's what I ordered. I also asked about the grass jelly drink but the server insisted that "it wouldn't taste good with tapioca" (Pause...with my fingers tapping and patience running short), "I will then have a taro milk tea with tapioca then"--thinking to myself that there must be something I don't know about tapioca. After all, I always make a good batch at home, but then I'm here to learn from these experts. 

The food came quick. The portion was good but the runny eggs could use more starch to thicken. There was a good amount of shrimps but they were smaller than the ones at Sun Hong Kong Restaurant down the street.  The server at first stuck a spoon into my plate but gave me the dirty look once I asked for a fork. I then returned to my table only to witness that my neighbor had 10 tiny stir fried shrimps swimming in gooey dark yellow mayo with a sprinkle of walnuts and a huge serving of rice--and that was his honey walnut shrimp. Shaking my head face down towards the floor and I thought, "Dude, you just got screwed".

Yes, I counted the shrimps. I was bored.

Even though my dish did not taste good, it still satisfied my week long craving. I then took a sip of the taro and realized to my delight that it was made with green tea. However, unlike Sweetheart, it was made with boring syrup and the tapioca/boba was stale and firm. On the spot, I declared this place as having the worst tapioca in town. I bused my own table as soon I was finished and the server gave me another death stare to see if my table was completely spotless. 

After this experience, I think I'm going back to Sun Hong Kong and Sweetheart. Two negative stars for each death stare, and another for generating the hype that they can't handle.

It isn't the greatest, but $2 for Salt & Pepper Tofu (almost sounds healthy, but it's fried, salty, and with lots of little garlics and chopped peppers - yeah, that kind of pepper),  a quick walk from my office, need I say more?

Came here for a bite to eat and some beer for my friend's birthday celebration.  Everything was going fine until they asked us to move tables to accommodate a reservation.  O.K. that's fine, but the reserved party was half the size of ours and we got moved to a smaller table for 1/3 of our party had to stand.  Also, we had to move our own shit, and we spilled tons of food and beer during all the commotion.  

All of that would be excusable had they at the very least accommodated our needs by bringing additional stools for us to sit on.  Just really inattentive service especially when I already had low expectations in the first place.  

The food was nothing special.  My calamari was drenched in oil and not crispy enough.  Everyone else at the table still had food left over on their plates despite ordering really small dishes.  Their one redeeming dish was the sweet potato fries.  Those are DELICIOUS!  Really crispy on the outside and perfectly soft on the inside.  Perfect fries.  

For a pub, it was strangely too brightly lit and didn't have a distinct "vibe" about the place.  I would feel uncomfortable getting drunk there, so I don't think it's meant for excessive drinking.  Worth checking out if you're a student at Cal... haven't you always wondered what the food was like?
Really good food

Great food, friendly, comfortable and nicely decorated dining room and gracious service! My "Book Club" had a "meeting" at Henry's this week and every dish we ordered was delicious and perfectly executed from a simple salad to an exquisite fruit "granita" to a rich and delicious cassoulet. One of our number is an exacting chef herself and she was impressed with each dish! Lovely to find such tasty food near campus! The server was attentive and helpful with good recommendations. And when there was an ordering mix-up the dish in question was "on the house"!
Pretty good, American cuisine with European influences is good for feeling more rustic in the urban heart of south side. Too bad it's completely unaffordable to pretty much all students.
their food sucks and its overpriced.

I've been here for both the dining and bar, so I'll split this review accordingly.

**DINING
We came here in a party of 9 for dining before a formal event.  The ambiance in the dining area with windows was appropriate for our occasion.  Service was friendly and decent.  A couple meals that stood out were the pork dish (very juicy and tender) and the pub burger.  Prices are slightly elevated for what you get, but I guess this is the best place for convenience, price, and ambiance. 

**BAR
I've only been here for two quick visits on non-game day weekends.  Pretty chill place.  I don't normally go here because it's not frequented too much by young college students.  I WILL be back however if I return to Cal for Game days; there are always long lines just to get in!

I've recommended Henry's to companies that are looking for a spot to host networking events - plates of appetizers and pitchers of beer! I've also been here for work lunches and I recall the sliders being tasty. 

I dropped in tonight for a Guinness and fish tacos. The tacos were bland, so I wouldn't recommend them. My co-worker loved her ribs though.

Henry's is a really nice break from the undergrad "college" scene in Berkeley. Usually its grad students or people from the hotel eating/drinking here. I also love that they show the euro soccer games, so I always go there to watch the games! Oh and if you haven't tried the food here, I recommend that you do! It is surprisingly good for a "bar." The caramelized brussel sprouts are AMAZING!

I'm a little late writing this, but I felt it was important to get it posted.  

I manage a small staff at UC (only 10 people)  and I wanted to take them somewhere fun for a little holiday get together before the holidays.  Working for the Govt, there is no budget for holiday parties and gifts.  So if I wanted to do this it was going to be on my dime.  I wanted to take them somewhere they could get an adult beverage (including cocktails) have some food and relax.  Henry's was one of the few places I could think of in Berkeley that would meet all of those requirements.  I called and set up a reservation (it was after the students had left for the semester) and explained what I wanted to do.  Brian, the Asst Mgr, helped me get it set up.  It wasn't very crowded when we arrived but Brian had a large table reserved for us.  We sat down, ordered a variety of drinks (I like beer but we had a few cocktail drinkers in the group) and everyone was getting happy!  We then ordered a fairly large variety of appetizers including e S&G Fries, Mango Wings (they ROCK) and sliders.  Some of our group had entrees as well.  The wait staff was always attentive and the service was good.  Brian checked in on us from time to time.   All in all this was a great place to go with a small group for good food and drinks in a casual atmosphere.  And since I was picking up the tab, it was important to me that it didn't break the bank.  Our event was an extraordinary success on all levels!
Wow the hamburger here is damn good!

Awful.  Went for lunch.  Took an hour to get food and what they sent was not what we ordered.  

Will not go back!

twofers at Hank's was a staple of my college years, I'd always show up right when the deal started cause it was just down the street.  The bartenders pour weak unless you talk to em, but once they know you it's usuallly a dash of mixer with your booze, and two drinks for $5 bucks is tough to beat.  

And for local culture you can usually see mike, this creepy  50 yearold white guy who drinks coke and stares at the waitresses ( unless he's at blakes)

The place only gets 3 stars because the bouncers are pretty obnoxious sometimes, esp about using the bathroom whcih is in the htoel lobby.

So, now that I'm living back in the Bay Area and have season tickets for Cal football I guess this is the place for Cal alums to tailgate before games. While attending Cal my only memories of this place was the time honored tradition of Two for Tuesdays (two drinks for 5 bucks). Am I completely dating myself, or does this great deal still exist? 

As far as a place to tailgate, it's a little crazy, but it has it's perks. The lines are insane (but what do you expect for school that can now boast a perennial top 25 CFB team), but the bartenders (well...the people manning the kegs) move pretty fast. I like the addition of flip cup, beer pong, and guitar hero this year to the back patio. The lines for the bathroom of course sucks, but its okay (see top 25 comment). For the USC game this year this place was a little too insane (we actually just headed over to Fred's Market across the street, bought beer, and brown bagged it in the ghetto food court) but for your Washington State's and University of AZ's of the world, this place is pretty fun. 

As far as booze goes this place has an excellent selection of beer (on the inside...if your partying on the patio your stuck with piss water (not that I'm complaining)). I've also been known to to have a vodka/soda or two if the beer line is too long, which are strong and good. As far as prices go, I can't think of what they are off hand but I do know drinks are a little more pricey than the norm since it's for football and there's $$$ to be made... 

I actually stayed at Hotel Durant for the Maryland game this year and had breakfast at Henry's from the "hangover" menu (yes, that's really what it's called) and the pancakes & pomegranate mimosa was delicious!!!! 

All in all this is fun place to tailgate and to nurse hangovers after games if your staying at Hotel Durant!!!!

Excellent brunch with family on Sunday.  Crab egg Benedict was delicious and others liked the eggs and toast.  Nice presentation.  Excellent service.  Great location near UC Berkeley campus one block away.
Henry's has one of the best bars in Berkeley. It is joie de vivre owned so you can only expect top quality cocktails, beer, and food .

Last day of finals of Spring 2010 semester, and my group of friends and I were ready to relax and let some steam out. 

Came in with a group of 5 tonight around 11:30 pm. 

Place was not too packed and there was ample seating. As we browsed through the drinks menu, the bartender checked all our IDs. 

My drink: the "Gossip Girl." From what I remembered, there was coconut rum, pineapple juice, and maybe some vodka? It was topped with a maraschino cherry. It was a yummy and girly drink and I loved it. I still feel $7/cocktail is kind of pricey, but it was worth it. 

Atmosphere: Compared to Blakes, it was a lot less crowded and noisy. I was able to catch up with some old friends while enjoying a drink. 

With its proximity to my apartment, I shall visit again soon.

Went in on a Saturday night, wasn't too crowded. The service was great, our waitress was very helpful and courteous. The food (I had a cheeseburger and fries) was delicious, and the drinks are well crafted. 

Overall great experience.

We went here on a Tuesday night and it was pretty busy! We got a great seat next to the bar and got service right away!  The food was great, I tried the veggies and corn cake.  The food came out quick and everyone loved it.  
Great customer service and the food speaks for itself!  We will definitely go back!

One of the ONLY adult bars in town.  And by "adult" I mean late 20s/early 30s crowds.  Almost every other place is overrun by undergrads and super young people...this place has a much more grown-up feel.  It's one of the only tame places in town.  Great cocktails and good food.  Service can be iffy when they're packed, so expect to be there for a while.
Want to grab a brew and watch the game?  You've found the best place near campus.  Take a seat and watch one of the many flatscreens while you sip your pint.

i came here other day with three friends, for our book club, and after getting our tables promptly, we were kind of neglected and forgotten about.  we ordered some dishes and drinks (i split fish and chips and baked goat cheese dip with a friend, and had a bloody mary), and i wanted some more aioli to go with my fries but the waitress never came back.  we were wondering, as it dragged on and on, luckily we had a great conversation going on so food was rather neglected.  i also wanted a bit more chips for the dip, but when another waitress came, she whisked away entire thing without even asking if we were done.  we waited another stretch of time before they finally handed us our bill.  we waited for about half hour before i gave up (and we had to go) and went over to the bar area to pay.  i felt like ditching, right there, when i waved the bill and not one glance was spared by bartender AND server.  i preserved and finally paid.  i then noticed they had a separate banquet room and that was where our server went.  what the heck? why couldnt she come and tell us herself that she will be occupied with a large party and someone else will cover us.  i work at a restaurant and one of things that has been drilled in my head: customer service is #1.  I will NOT come back because the service was crap.  i even mentioned this on the credit card slip i signed off on, so this yelp review is for you guys, not the management.

I really considered 1 star for the food.  I've eaten here 4 times, it doesn't get better.  The burger itself is OK, but breakfast platters are below par.  And everything on the menu is WAAAAAAAY overpriced.

Go to Denny's for breakfast and In N Out for lunch.  Even with gas, it will be cheaper and taste better

Henry's is a chill place to be.  The service might be slow sometimes, as I feel like they're always understaffed and the place is usually always crowded.  I come here for one thing and usually one thing only, the Mac n Cheese.  It has crack in it, but one of the best Mac n Cheese I've ever had. The other dishes are decent too, but the Mac n Cheese is a must have.  

There are also plenty of TV"s to watch the games.

We never get to this part of town - being (relatively) old and this area being the haunt of the frats/sororities.  Parking is fairly tough, and the first time we went it was during Rush week. So... I like it.  Different vibe in the area I enjoy. 

I vacillated between 3 and 4 stars.  The food  is good, they have Racer 5 IPA.  The service has always been great - personable and efficient, a good combo.  There are better places to be had, but I've found myself back a couple of times, so that must mean I am a fan.  I think I am at 3.5 stars. now where is that option again?

If you go out fairly frequently give it a try.  If it is a once in awhile thing, save it for something else.

Went here for the first time about a week ago and it was pretty cool. The Tuna Melt sandwich was excellent and huge. A little on the pricy side, but worth it. Only problem I had was the calamari & even though it was good they could have made it just a little bit crispier. 

I will go back again to check out more items.

Nice place, good service, good cocktails (though the ginger julep needed more Four Roses). poor beer selection, bad food. Chips with cheese dip was ruined by the Parm, which combined with too-chunky veggies gave the dip an unpleasantly oily/chunky feel. Cod and chips were fried in oil at least two weeks passed its prime; fries were soggy and dark brown, fish batter was likewise. "Cod" was the darkest and oiliest of this fish I've ever had; combined with batter it was greasy and unpleasant  - like Mitt Romney.

My law school friends and I frequent Henry's for their exceptional wine list, super yummy Brussels sprouts, an those sauteed mushrooms...mmmm, mushrooms. Excellent cocktails. Wait and bar staff are awesome. Seriously.

It's also close to Boalt which is convenient and Henry's avoids the undergrad vibe of the other local spots. Perfect for a date if you're at the Berkeley Art Museum or the Pacific Film Archive. Also good for graduate students with visiting relatives. 

Street parking is decent and free after 6.

Henry's is mainly good for its location where many Cal students live close by. I have been here several times in the past and I always thought it was so-so. I went here 2 days ago for the first Cal gameday, and I was very unhappy with the quality and price of the food and beverages. The service was also very poor. (We were sitting in the restaurant portion in a booth.) I know that it was a gameday and everything, but this just highlighted the so-so experience. I had a cheeseburger for $8.50, which did not include/come with fries. My beer was also more expensive than I would pay at a neighboring bar/restaurant. The food tasted OK and was definitely not worth the price.

The service is another story. Our waitress was not accommodating and forgot our orders so we were just chilling and hungry for even longer. This server had at most a few brain cells--she charged us for more than what we ordered and we asked her to fix it. She then magically added on the automatic 18% gratuity two more times, making it even more. Her manager finally fixed it...like 15 minutes later. The automatic 18% gratuity is a joke and was definitely undeserved. At most, 15 would be generous. I would highly recommend going somewhere else in close proximity. Pappy's is just a block down, and has better and less expensive food and drinks! Who cares if it isn't attached to a cool, historical hotel? I know I don't!

Even though it's cheap, try to avoid Henrys/Tuesdays.
I've been here twice, both times loathed the experiences. Why?

1. They took away my VALID license by saying its fake. What?? Two people looked at it, and they put it in the tip jar, saying that it's not a real ID. They scanned it, but maybe they're blind because it's a real ID! So I had to argue with them for a long time to finally get it back, and they showed it to third guy who said it's real. Ugh.

2. Takes 30 minutes (my friend timed it) to get a drink and 30 minutes to close my tab. From my experience, they go to the white girls before anyone else.

I greatly prefer all the other bars near the Berkeley campus--Jupiters, Raleighs, and Bear's Lair and Blakes, even Kips. Well, good luck if you go there!

We have been talking about trying Henry's for about a year. It is one of the closest bar to us. Why does Elmwood not have a single bar? Can someone fix this? Or can someone give me money to fix it?

Anyway, the atmosphere at Henry's is great. The dining room seemed a little stuffy so we opted to sit in the bar area. Nice hardwood details and a beautiful behind the bar alcohol display give this place an old world, smoking parlor feel. 

The on tap beer selection is OK, but not great for the area. We started with calamari which was pretty good - no overcooked, maybe a bit too much salt, and a sauce that was, well, fine. S. ordered the Cottage Pie and I ordered Spaetzle. Our first mistake was ordering two dishes that were HEAVY. In fairness I have never had spaetzle, but I was not impressed (sorry Germans). While I love bacon and cheese as much as the next girl, this dish ended up with a heavy layer of oil at the bottom which was frankly a little gross. S. was good enough to give me half of his cottage pie which was nicely done. Though it probably didn't need so much cheese in the mash potatoes. 

We certainly didn't properly balance out our meal when we ordered and we will probably come back to try some of the lighter fare. Though the reviews here of the salads aren't exactly glowing. Or maybe next time we will ride our bikes and take the long way home to avoid the long term damaged of so much cheese.

Probably we won't come back for dinner. Might come over to watch a game sometime though.

They aren't that friendly here. The owner didn't look like he wanted our service as he shook his head when we were trying to get situated. It is a bit overpriced for some of the cocktails.

Probably wouldn't come back.

My friend and I were staying at the hotel and decided to get some cocktails and appetizers at the restaurant before heading out for the night.

We asked the server for a suggestion on drinks.  He recommended the Henry's Martini.  This may have been the best martini I have ever had.  From their website: Henry's Martini-  Eristoff vodka shaken, served up, and garnished with a blue cheese stuffed olive.  Amazing.

We then asked the server for a suggestion on appetizers.  He asked if we want something standard or something out of the ordinary.  Naturally we said "out of the ordinary!" So he recommended the Grilled Watermelon.  Yes, you read that right.  Grilled.  Watermelon.  From their website: Grilled watermelon- with herbed Cyprus goat cheese, pistachio, prosciutto and tarragon aioli.  It was warm and cool, creamy and crunchy, sweet and salty.  All in each bite. Simply the best for all the senses.

The bar wasn't too busy around 5pm when we arrived.  But the service was RIDICULOUSLY SLOW.  It wasn't a lack of staffing, there seemed to be plenty of people in and out of the kitchen the whole time.  But we had to keep flagging our waiter down  to order, for more water, to order more drinks, etc.  It wasn't just us that were frustrated. The poor girl sitting next to us was sitting there with her stuff packed up and trying to pay for at least 15 minutes.  

This is the ONLY reason I can't give them 5 stars.  And it kills me because we are STILL talking about the food and drinks!

My friends and I like to come here because a lot of graduate students hang here. The food is pretty good, and the drink selection is also good. It's nice that they have TV's in the bar, and also have a more formal dining area as well. Of course the Stanford urinal is awesome (I have only seen pics.. but boys, you need to check it out in person). I am giving this place 3-stars for the service. Every time I come here without fail the service is the worst. Hire new waitstaff, owners.

This place is not just a busy pub!  There is delicious, healthy food too!  We stepped into Henry's for a quick, early and light supper before going to the Berkeley Rep. and ate in the quiet dining area away from the tvs and noisy pub.  wow!  Were we in for a treat!  The roasted spring veggies & corn cake were so divine that I slowed down to savor every delectable bite.  The roasted veges had maitake mushrooms, radishes and spring onions and what tasted like roasted green salad with lentils over a cornmeal pancake and a light creamy green dressing.  My husband had a big salad with strawberries and a soft goat cheese.  We left the restaurant completely satisfied and not overstuffed.  We plan to return for the same thing, and perhaps order an appetizer or two next time, and perhaps some of that fresh looking lemonade the lady next to us was drinking...and perhaps some of those wings she was biting into.  Definitely a must try place if you are a foodie and cook like me!

Henry's is a cozy, breathable place in Berkeley.  

They have hard to find drinks: Hangar 1 and Veev.

I haven't tasted the entrees, but I've seen the dishes come out and served to the guests.  They look hearty and have a creative twist to simple dishes.

I went here with a buddy for an NFL playoff game.  There was no host/hostess and it took a long time for us to be approached by a waiter, but once we were it was a good experience.  I got the southern fried chicken sandwich and it was fantastic.  My buddy got a burger and it looked good too.  Both were a little pricier than I thought they should be (~$15 for each).  They had great beer specials.  We went on a Saturday night and they had "rotating taps", where they have a different tap on special for $2 every hour.  Yummm Sam Adams Celebration Ale!  There were plenty of large TVs showing the game.  I agree with other reviewers that it's very loud, but hey, it's a sports bar, what do you expect?  I would definitely come back.

We ate here while staying at the attached Durant Hotel. 

The atmosphere was charming and the service was friendly and attentive. 

We ordered an arugula salad, chicken wings and the mac 'n cheese. The salad was decent although the dressing was a little forgettable. The wings were a bit too spicy for my liking. The mac 'n cheese was fabulous and I'd definitely order it again.
The crowd is a lot older than expected. The prices are a little pricey too. This place has many seats though and I've never seen it crowded.

I've been here so many times it's hard to believe I haven't written a review yet. This place is the only worthy bar on south side of the Berkeley campus, now that the late Raleigh's has been put to rest (god bless its soul). Blake's was no good, Pappy's is laughable, and I feel bad even mentioning Kips.

Anyway, the atmosphere is nice, a little bit on the classy side, although the impression fades once you get seated (not a bad thing).

The service is OK. When it's busy they seem to have only 1-2 servers helping the entire crowd. God knows they're trying, but management might consider putting more help out there to ensure good customer service. 

My big gripe is the bar. They have good beers on tap, but that's about where the good ends. I have had nothing but misses with cocktails. My absolute favorite afternoon drink, a whiskey sour, is consistently butchered by the bartender (even though it's the simplest drink out there). I don't know if it's the fake premade lime mix that they use (nasty -- just squeeze a couple limes ffs) or the nauseating sweetness that comes with too much syrup. I understand that we're in college town and that I look young (and am young) but that doesn't mean you need to assume I can't handle a drier cocktail.

The food is good, although nothing to write home about. It's nice to be able to get decent food while you enjoy a beer (read: not a cocktail).

I had my first and last drink of college at this place.

Great beer selection, addictive fries, and a lively atmosphere make this a great place to escape the regular rowdy college frat/bar scene for something a little classier and quieter.

The food, outside of fried stuffs, is average and quite expensive.

The best place to come with some friends after class for a beer and to watch the second half of a giants game.

This place is a great sports bar.  There are games on constantly on a number of tvs, so no matter which direction you face, you're sure to face at least a couple different games on.  They also have a deal where certain drinks are on sale as long as a specific game is on, so check that list if that's going to effect your choices.

Seating can be a bit tough since the place isn't all that big, but I've found you can usually scrounge seats from other tables to accomodate a large-ish group.  The bar is a bit more 'high-class' than many of the other college bars around UC Berkeley campus, but it's not terribly expensive or anything, just not terribly cheap either.

TL;DR: One of the nicer bars around Berkeley, specifically good for watching games.  Check out the drinks that are on sale during each game.

We had such a wonderful birthday celebration at Henry's last night!  Thanks to Sarah for a perfect evening.  She was so pleasant and accommodating.   Everyone loved the food - burgers were fantastic!  We also enjoyed the "Angry Mac & Cheese"
We had a delightful evening and will return again soon :)

ABOVE & BEYOND 
Boyfriend took me to Berkeley for a getaway weekend staying with the Hotel Durant. We had lunch after check in and attempted to order the gnocchi, but was told they were out. Got a burger and was pleased with the size and quality. Our female bartender/server was warm and engaging. Very good lunch. 

Towards the end of lunch the chef approached us apologizing for the unavailable gnocchi entree. He asked us to comeback for on the dinner service for the gnocchi at no charge. We did and it was wonderful and probably the best we have ever had. What the Chef accomplished was to make a good experience exceptional. We wish this would happen more often. Kudos to Henry's!!

I am staying at the Hotel Durant and Henry's is located inside the hotel. My first night in town I arrived late and decided to eat "in" so to speak and had a lovely meal of mac and cheese. My server was a very pleasant young woman who was attentive yet not pushy. If I were to base my experience on my first encounter, I would have given Henry's four stars, however...

Tonight, after a long day at a conference and in need of time to prep for a presentation tomorrow, I I again decided to try out the dining at Henry's expecting a similar experience.  First, the server didn't even serve me or check on me or refill my water once. I ordered with the host , another woman brought my food, and the server showed up to give me the bill.   My meal consisted of a very mediocre burger and  fries which were mushy and tasteless. 

While convenient, this place is not what it's cracked up to be.  Even though the mac and cheese was flavorful and unique, it was not worth $16.00 (with added chicken).  The burger really wasn't worth the 14.00 I paid for it either.  I seriously could have walked two blocks and picked up a better meal for under $6.00 on Telegraph or a full Thai spread including coffee, beer, dessert, and an entree for less money.  I don't mind shelling out for a good meal and leaving generous tips, but this place neither has great food or great service. 

It was also loud and impersonal. 

Again, the server on Friday was perfect but what makes a dining establishment noteworthy is consistency coupled with unbelievable food. Henry's serves up neither.

OK, been a while since I've been back in the Bay Area and, I must admit, I was a SF/ "The City" snob when I lived there.  However, my "amore" is a Berkeley lover who I met there and after traveling much of Europe w/her and settling again on the "East Coast" we returned to the Ebay.  Henry's was a default selection on our night of arrival and after ingesting the mac & cheese, beet/fennel salad, and the potato/gruyere soup we were sold!  I returned here twice and had delicious meals w/o pretension and w/delightful service that I've been missing.  I would absolutely recommend them for a lunch/cocktail/dinner if ever in Berkeley!  I REALLY liked these people and the food.  This was a real "eye opener" and welcome alternative to the "See and B Seen" crowds in SF.  I felt like I was in Italy and was being offered some of the best "slow foods" alternatives to be had in the USA.  Left me feeling satisfied/happy/and well fed!

This is pretty simple.
Pro: they show soccer
Con: overpriced
AMAZING FRITES. that in itself is worth coming here for. okay drinks, okay food. kind of expensive.

A disappointment.  

The service at this place is kind of terrible.  I really felt like I was a burden on the waiter, and I had a tough time attracting his attention.  I was there for an hour over lunch, and my water glass was dry for almost 30 minutes and I never got a refill on my coffee ($2.25).  I ordered a lunch salad ($12) expecting a lunch-sized salad.  What I got was a salad-in-a-bag with olives and cheese on top.  

On the plus side, the location is convenient and the ambiance is nice.  The hotel's lobby furniture is a modern trendy version of academic life.  (Think chairs made out of books and chandeliers made from blue test booklets.)

With so many good restaurants in the neighborhood, there's no reason to waste a meal at Henry's.

Don't visit on a cal football day!!!

Drink prices are doubled (without notice); 18% mandatory gratuity - also without notice!  The shock is when you get the bill.  I immediately talked to the manager on duty (who looked totally burned out at 1pm on Saturday) and while she twice apologized, offered no recourse.  I told her that a practice like doubling the price of a Sierra Nevada from $4 to $8 was not only unconscionable, but to add a mandatory tip, insane.  Yes, its 18% at Chez Panisse, and duly noted.  Here its: Surprise!

Very bad business practice.  Please don't go here.  Ever!!!

This was stop 4 (or was it 5?) on our trip up the hill to Memorial Stadium for my first ever Cal Football game last Saturday. We were kind of running late, so I imagine that we experienced a much less crowded Henry's than the people who were there, say 30 minutes before us.

It seemed like a nice enough place though. They had pushed the bigger tables against the wall and there were plenty of smaller standing tables for us to rest our big cups of beer on. The prices were slightly higher here than at Bear's Lair, but the crowd was no less enthusiastic about the game and there were plenty of drunk fans here as well. I'd say the crowd was generally a little older here than at Bear's Lair. Definitely worth a stop in on your way up the hill, the next time you're going to a football game.

First off, let me just say that this is the first yelp review that I have ever written and the only reason why I joined was to warn people to never ever eat at this "restaurant" for any reason. Secondly, for the record, the only reason why I gave it a star is because to leave no stars is not an option. Our waitress, who was nice and did know the menu, seemed very hurried considering that there were about five people in the restaurant when we sat down. I ordered the fish and a side dish of mushrooms. My boyfriend, was not hungry and did not order anything. Lucky him. When the food arrived, it did not look promising however, I have learned to not judge the book by its cover, so in I dove. The fish was over cooked and id not taste fresh. The salad that was served with the fish was slightly better but still very disappointing. The mushrooms which tasted the best out of everything had a very strange taste and consistency. Too much saffron or something. All together, basically the worst food I have ever had. So you say, this is a bar, right? Well, the first drink I ordered, "The Gossip Girl" was so bad, I had to send it back and I am not the type of girl that throws away perfectly good alcohol. The next drink I ordered, "Everything but the kitchen sink Bloody Mary" was very bland and watery considering the excellent description and list of ingredients that were in the menu. I did not even finish it. My boyfriend had the "East Bay Tea" and he loved it, just thought I should mention... So for the topper on the cake, after the bad food and the bad drinks, I woke up the next morning at seven and felt sick to my stomach. A stomach ache that lasted all day long that got worse and worse every time I pictured the meal that was served to me at this horrible excuse for a restaurant. Be afraid. Very afraid.

Good breakfast.  Prices on the high end but food was good and nice setting.  Also had a beer there late one afternoon but didnt eat and bar area was fun and started to pick up by time we were about done.

Henry's is the bar connected to a hotel lobby, the atmosphere is more relaxed and the crowd is older. It is the opposite of a loud and trendy hole in the wall bar that I usually am drawn to. The domestic pitchers were a steal- $11

Funny thing happened on our visit here, the Cal band marched in and played throughout the entire floor. Some of the older folks seemed annoyed and tried to continue talking over the music. =P

We went to Henry's right before a concert at the Greek and it was perfect because it was far enough away to find decent parking on the street and it was just a little walk up the hill.  They had all of the TVs on to various sports which was perfect to watch baseball basketball or whatever.  The bar portion of Henry's was very cool and pretty active.  For our meal we ordered a small salad and then had the Cuban sandwich and hamburger.  Both were very good and the fries were very tasty.  We were pretty gassy later in the night though but I guess that's what happens when you eat bar food.

For a place close to the Greek with decent food and good drink specials I'd definitely check out Heny's again.

Before we ever went in, my friends and I started calling it "that pretentious bar on the corner," mostly because the sign outside says "GASTRONOMY AND MIXOLOGY." Doesn't that sound really pretentious? But then they're also a sports bar.

Excuse me -- sports *pub*.

So make that "slightly pretentious." True to slightly pretentious form, they have their own spin on most of the mixed drinks on their menu, and they're pretty good. They have a nice selection of beers, including Sam Summer (yesssssss).

Be prepared for them to be phenomenal dicks about your ID, though. If the i's aren't dotted or the t's aren't crossed, they will not serve you. Apparently some states expire ID's on the holder's 21st birthday to force them to renew and get the landscape-format ID -- whoops! Nobody else has seemed to care, but it didn't fly at Henry's. Berkeley's tough about ID's, though, so okay, fine, whatever.

The atmosphere's okay -- bring your own crowd, 'cause it stays pretty empty summer weeknights. The wood-and-steel aesthetic is nice, though, and really kind of redeems the while endeavour. They've also been posting increasingly less-good deals to their Twitter account -- @henrysberkeley -- which I guess is worth following.

All in all, a good place to pop in to for a quiet beer during the summer.

Came here after work and it was nice to find a place within walking distance and away from the crazy Cal kids and hectic downtown. The atmosphere here is fun, very Cheers via Boston circa the 80s (but not the bad hair and spandex 80s). 

Came around 6 on a Friday night and this place had a buzz. The waitstaff was great. We got a pitcher and I got the mac and my bf got the burger. He loved the burger and the fries were great. I don't think the prices here were really high at all. My mac was good, although there must have been one cheese I wasn't a huge fan of in the combo because every now and then it had a slightly odd taste. We also got a green salad that was $5, huge, and gorgeously green lettuce. Nice. They had the tvs with games going, but they are on silent and have several acceptable sized tvs, which is appreciated. You can go to watch a game or can totally ignore them if that's what you prefer. 

I wouldn't go out of my way to get here, but I can definitely see dropping in after work for a pitcher.

This USED to be my favorite bar in Berkeley, coming here about twice monthly... That is until they suddenly got rid of the $2 Rolling Rock and the sweet potato fries.  I am still bitter about that.

If they still had the sweet potato fries and rolling rock, it'd be an easy 5 star.

The interior is very nice, has a lot of TVs to watch the game, and most of the food I've tried here is actually really good.  However poor college student wallet can't afford to come here too often.  A meal will cost $10-15, and most beers on tap seem to run about $5-6.  To their credit, they to serve pitchers to make it a bit cheaper and they take credit card.
