Also if you're so inclined, they have bud light for $3-4.

The Burger and Onion Rings alone is what saved this place from getting a 1 star from me.  The food is average. The service couldn't get more terrible. When it takes 15 minutes to get your drinks and another 30 to get your food in an empty restaurant it is definitely a problem.  Especially when your waiters is oblivious to the issue. Watery cocktails, grinds in your half full coffee cup and cold Eggs Benedict....If that sounds like your style then by all means go for it.

Came here for food not to drink and while the food is better than I remember from my college days it's not anything to write home about. Also the ambiance of the restaurant is seriously affected by the noise from the attached bar. I would not here again simply for that. I mean I know, it's a college bar but still, they should shut the doors or something. Otherwise the food is decent. I had a pretty good hamburger, my mother in law got sweet potato fries with her hamburger and I wish I'd done the same. Her sweet potato fries were delicious while my regular fries were kind of weak and limp. Sad. I would come here for lunch but never again during dinner or bar time.

I was meeting a friend from out of town for breakfast near the campus and, knowing it was Cal Day and wanting to make a reservaiton, I did a search and made a reservation at this restaraunt I had not been to before.  When we showed up, the waitress was rude and very put out saying she did not have room for us - even with the reservation and the dining room being almost empty.  When we were grudgingly seated, we had two different menus amoung the three of us and the waitress was again angry  when we asked which was correct.  When breakfast came, my husband received white toast instead of the wheat he had ordered, and my frined received BOTH bacon instead of the suasage AND over easy rather than scrambled eggs. The portions were small and unimaginative, the coffee adequate but pleantaful ,and there was a line of ten women for the one stall bathroom in the lobby of the hotel becasue the general public was using it . The only thing positive I can say is that the decore is nice and the location great when you have to be near campus. We will not be returning to Henry's.

The only reason this place  does not get 5 stars is because they do not have 2 for Tuesdays anymore. Bring it back. I hope they bring it back some day. This place has gone through many changes in the last ten years. I recommend it  for CAL game days because it is the closest bar to the stadium.

Went here after a Cal football night game at Memorial Stadium. They have a surprisingly decent beer selection, with your basics, Guinness, Downtown Brown and Boont Amber (among others). The post-game crowd was hodge-podge of football fans. We saw college kids with their alum parents, we saw the visiting teams' whole traveling squad, we saw a fight break loose between said groups.

The age range was generally a bit high than your normal college bar, which was refreshing. Think 24-29. Works for me. Prices are a bit high ($5 for small plastic cup, $8 for a large) but well drinks seemed reasonable. 

I like this place, it's a nice, refreshing, non-hippie, more traditional type college tavern-like place.

We were staying at the hotel and had a $50 credit here so we decided to give it a shot. 

Ambiance was cute, they host game nights for the local university kids and what not around the bar. 

We ordered a bunch of random appetizers and small plates and a few drinks. I got the Gossip Girl, because I love the show and couldn't help myself. It was pretty strong to be honest (I'm not much of a hard liquor girl) 

The onion dip was pretty good, it came with chips but we ordered some extra bread which was a better suit (and recommended by our server). What was really memorable was the Mac and Cheese! It had like 4 or 5 really amazing cheeses with a perfect amount of panko crumbs on top. I was craving this mac and cheese for DAYS after this trip. It was about $10(ish) and was a side dish. I highly recommend sharing this dish. It's very very rich and I don't think any human's body was meant to process that much cow/goat milk! (I did have to run to Walgreens for some lactaid since I'm lactose intolerant, but SOOO worth it!)

Henry's the pub restaurant outside the Hotel Durant lobby is a great place to dine and of course for those that like a few drinks there is not a better place to be. The chef went out of his way to accommodate us preparing food to take to ceremonies and/or concerts and for dinner we were constraint with time and the chef went out of his way to prepare dinner for us even though it was too early for dinner. Everyone is friendly, attentive, and cheerful.

"cuz messin with twofer tuesdays is bad for your health"....- and your ability to actually get drunk too- because althought you get two drinks for the price of one- trying to get one sure as hell ain't no fun (now if I could just pull some more rhymes down on this review...)

Anyways, unless you can crowdsurf your way on top of a gridlock worse than 101 on Giants gamedays, you're better off at Kips. Yes Kips.

buuuuuut on Cal game days as phenom as Saturdays game, when they've turn that parking lot into a beer garden- the nice 4 dollah cup-0-frosty adult beverage sure tastes good, and warms you up right quick for the game. all in all, 3 mixed sticky stars.

This is a nice place for a coffee. I used to sit here in freshman year for some breakfast and coffee if I locked myself out of my room (and happen to have my wallet). Not for the food. For the warm, stress-free ambiance :)

Ate here once... Nothing bad, nothing special, nothing memorable!

I used to eat brunch there all the time when I lived at the nearby International House; but it's been a couple of years since I last went there, until last night. It was as awesome as I remembered it! The service, I have to start out saying, was spectacular! We began with an "Arugula salad [with] wild arugula, shaved fennel, navel oranges, pistachio, with cider honey dressing and pecorino cracker," which could have served four people easy. It was great-I really liked the shaved fennel! For entrees, I had the "The American Dip which is shaved, slow roasted natural beef ribeye, emmentaler, horseradish, creme on a French baguette, with a smoked porter beef au jus and truffled frites," and my husband had the ""The Cubano" which is slow roasted, pulled niman pork, smoked Niman ham, emmentaler, Saag's pickles, American mustard, served with Henyr's pickled cabbage salad." We both loved our meals! We ended the evening with good coffee and a nutty ice cream sandwiched between red velvet cookies, which was great!

I'm new to Berkeley, and still learning the lay of the land, but this place keeps getting chosen for various happy hours, so I've been here a few times. 

The place is cute, the service is great, it's close to the law school, and the drinks are very reasonable (four dollars for a well drink - I may only think this is cheap because I've been living in San Fran. We'll see), but the acoustics here are TERRIBLE. Every time I leave Henry's, I leave with a hoarse voice and a painful sore throat. I know I like to talk, but it's more than that! I don't know what it is (all the nice wood panelling?), but this place seems to have night-club-level noise even when it's mostly empty. I don't get it. But it kind of ruins it for me, I have to say. Maybe I'm just getting old....

EDIT 9/22/08:

Well, they've remodeled the whole joint, which may make for better sound levels, and have also apparently upped the food to "gastro pub" levels. Whatever that means. I had some chicken wings here a few weeks ago that were pretty tasty, but i was with a bunch of friends here during interview season, and they waited over an hour for their lunches while being completely ignored by servers and management. Which is ridiculous. Hopefully that was just growing pains for the newly renovated place, but it was definitely still a turn-off.

Ok so I'm gonna give this place two stars because it was awesome to come here and get trashed when I was 18...BUT now that I am older and wiser (and legal, mind you) I avoid this place like the plague. Yes they have "Two for Tuesdays" and yes, that means it's $5 for 2 drinks but the moral compromise you must make to come here on this night is just simply not worth it. Getting to the bar is a nightmare, not only because it's crowded but because I feel like my butt is getting gang-banged across the dance floor by 15 ghetto muthaf*ckas when I ain't even shakin it! I mean, come on...And when you finally do get to the bar, you better hope you put on your titty shirt that night cuz you gotta show the ladies to get some service. And when you do get your drinks...finally...there will be some odd carbonated, chlorine-tasting fluid instead of the sweet and sour you asked for. Oh Henry's, thank God you're renovating and will be closed for 3 months...maybe if we're lucky you will never re-open!
Back when I was a drinking man the twofer tuesdays were a blessing.  It gets the stars now mostly for the memories, although the ratio supported by this mediocre setup is still surprising.

**Follow up**
After the waitress OVERTIPPED HERSELF on my credit card, the manager promised to reimburse me. He directed me to the accounting department, who redirected me elsewhere, and so on and so forth on a loop. They all promised I would get my money back because of what the waitress did. It never happened, they avoid my calls. THIS PLACE SUCKS TOO. I GO TO THE FIVE BAR NOW AT HOTEL SHATTUCK, BECAUSE THE PEOPLE THERE ARE WAY COOLER AND MORE PERSONABLE.

These hours on YELP are not correct hours.

We had last call, in a very crowded bar, at about 11:15 PM - on a Friday.

I've never tried the food here, but this place is definitely the place to be if you want great drinks and to be in the company of great people, especially after a Cal game. 

It has been a while since I was last in, not since the did their upgrades, I'll definitely have to be back in to check it out.

Just realized that I hadn't written a review for Henry's - how can that be??  Henry's has been my go-to place now after meeting with my wedding planner down the street at the Berkeley City Club.  Henry's has great food, a great staff and, most importantly, great drinks that aren't super pricey (because, if youre planning a wedding and talking about how much this bad boy is going to suck out of wallet, you need a good, strong drink to soften the blow.)   The atmosphere here is always awesome - very much like being at your old friend's house for an evening of good conversation.

I came in here with my girlfriend at a slightly odd hour apparently ( 9:00pm on a saturday night, a hour before closing) There was no one else there. Dont let this scare you, because whenever i passed this place, it (or at least the bar portion) is crowded with people. 

We chose this place simply because Chef Eddie's Angry mac n cheese sparked my interest a year ago and we never had the opportunity to try it.

so here we go;
Chili (for i have  a weird obsession with trying different chili recipes); Truthfully... the chili was nothing special, was somewhat disappointing and comparable to Chili's chili...  

Soup of the day (which was a vegetable puree of sorts in soup form); it was pretty good for something as simple as a vegetable soup. 

Chicken strips; They were big for the 4-5 pieces. I believe that they were half breast and were flavored with lemon served with a side of salad. I would probably get this again

Angry Mac n Cheese; It was a unique twist from the traditional mac n cheese, although because i didnt  get it loaded with mushrooms and chicken i think it could have been significantly better. Will probably come back just to retry this. 

Fruit cake crumble;  This was the BEST thing we had that night.  That is all. try this if you can.

Came here for a friend's birthday with a big group.  Given that the bar area was super crowded, we opted to take over a table in the dining room.  Swanky posh dining room next to dark loud pub-y bar?  Not really the best setup.  Now I love a good party, but if I were a guest seeking respite at a hotel, I wouldn't be too happy about this booming bar downstairs.

Anyway the wait staff was pretty unhelpful in accommodating our big group, so we just ended up pushing tables together ourselves.  Which they later seemed peeved about, but if they didn't like it they should have helped us!  Given they only had a few other occupied tables, you'd think they'd jump at the chance to help out a big group - especially since we were all eating dinner and having drinks.

Also, I hate when I order a salad that sounds all fancy on the menu, but turns out to just be plain greens.  No tomato, no cucumber, no nothing...just salad greens.  Call it a freaking green salad and leave the other adjectives outta there!!

Redeeming aspects: good mixed drinks, and pitchers of beer available.
Would give the place another shot, maybe for drinks at the bar.

The drinks and the food was good.....but the staff seemed put upon and bothered and in general unfriendly.  Too bad, because we were staying in the hotel and would have liked to just chill and eat there more, but didn't want to deal with the attitude.  This place could be really great with a "Cheers" like friendly staff.

I frequent Henry's to watch games, catch up with friends, and just for a casual drink. It's a nice escape from the general college crowd as it's usually full of GSI's, parents, and the older Berkeley populace. It can be hard to find seating during a game or catch the attention of a server, but once you have that they're plenty attentive.

The beer is pricey unless you get Budlight. My friends and I usually opt for the other beers on tap which can range from $8/glass to $17/pitcher. The fries are pretty good to pig out on and share but the dinner plates aren't THAT great. I've ordered the fish n chips per the server's opinion and I have to say I wasn't impressed. My roommates ordered the burger and the steak sandwich, which may be a better choice considering it is a pub. 

Overall, a pretty standard place.

Being that I went to UCSB, I could really take or leave Cal Football; but if you are going to a game, this is the place to start. In fact, it's good for games on the telie, too. 

I went last night with a couple of guy friends who had to watch a game that was only played on the NBA channel. After several calls we learned that Henry's supported such avid fans and would be showing the games that don't come on prime channels. Cool. So we went. 

It was 80 outside and 80 inside. I could barely get out a hoot or holler since I was so f*cking hot. Seemed like it would be cozy the majority of the year, during cooler days. 

They didn't have sound with the games, but instead played some hits of the oldies...not really get pumped music...

Best french fries I've had in the East Bay. 

So it goes something like this:

Ambiance (recently remodeled according to website) 4
Food 4
Service 2.5
Playing hard to find games 5
Knowing at times that it will be really hot, and that at other times it will be shoulder to shoulder crowded  0.5
Parking 2
Proximity to BART 3

*It's the Hotel Durante Bar & there maybe a parking lot in the back*

Disclaimer: this 3-star rating is actually somewhat misleading, since I haven't had a mediocre experience here -- they range from Good and Yummy (G&Y) to Downright Awful (DA).

DA
The scene is set. Cal football game. Drunken people yelling obscenities against the Ducks or Beavers or whoever it is we're playing this week. Of course, Bear's Lair, Raleigh's, and Blake's are packed beyond belief. We go to Henry's in hopes of a quick buzz before the game. And.... success! They have beer! Why was this a DA experience? It was $8 for a cup of Sam Adams. I could have gone to Safeway and got myself a nice six-pack for that price. Abso-effing-lutely outrageous!

G&Y
The scene is set. Dinner before a meeting on campus. We're in a bit of a hurry to make the meeting, so we order whatever's quick. I got the steak nicoise sald -- salad is nicely/lightly dressed, steak is medium rare and sliced thinly and arranged prettily. Others' sandwiches are great, fries are good. Solid meal.

DA + G&Y
The scene is set. Saturday lunch with some friends. The restaurant is completely empty, minus some Jack Nicholson-look-a-like and his wife. We order, bread comes out -- it has the temperature of a rock, and the butter isn't any warmer :( A few of us ordered Cuban sandwiches -- soooo good! Melted Swiss cheese, pork, and ham make for a trio between two slices of bread all pressed into one happy family. Definitely would recommend it. That's the G&Y part. I would NOT recommend getting the side salad to go with it... it was drowning in vinaigrette, and my tongue almost shriveled from the salt that was put into it. I got the salad instead of the fries to be healthy; I decided it would be healthier to not eat the salad.

It's pretty much hit or miss with Henry's. G&Y or DA... you can flip a coin and it'd be an accurate estimate of the quality of food you're going to get.

It's really a 3, but a 4 because the bartender didn't charge me for a shot of corazon tequila on my 22nd birthday although i came in a few days afterwards. Drinks are kinda of pricey as is the food, but they make them well.
One of the 3 husbands i had in Berkeley: Kips, Raleigh & Henry.

Oh Henry's! another Cal staple. You can't not go into this place. It's got that classic bar feel and look. Better bathroom then most joints and always a fun crowd (cute and friendly.) Good college recession prices on the meals. Obviously you come here for the beer, not to review the grub, it ain't fine dining honey.

This review is for the bar.... 

There are few better places to watch the NFL Sunday ticket.  It is quiet not a crazy bar like atmosphere, and you can feel comfortable watching the game over a very good breakfast without feeling like you need to pound beers.  The bloody mary's are fantastic. 

This is also a very cool place to catch after a Cal game... preferably a win.  The entire Cal marching band crowded the place and played music for beer.  it was so FREAKING loud... really cool.  

don't wear a red wisconsin badger shirt on game days though... drunken girls will slap you in the face and yell 'Take off that red shirt!' ... they think it's for Stanford.  silly college girls.

i don't know what the deal is with henry's.  do they actually think that they're a nice "hotel bar"???  b/c if so, that's a load of crap...the drinks are expensive, but they suck...as do the people in general.  it sticks out weirdly in my mind b/c i remember once being *by far* the tallest girl in there and one of the 3-4 tallest people--and that's weird b/c i'm only 5'7".  i have no idea what was going on (midget fest or something).

Arrived at 11:30 on Sunday for Brunch. Not even half the tables were filled. Were seated promptly and given menus. The guy took our order after about 10 minutes. 15 minutes  minutes later we were still waiting for water, coffee, anything - the waiter or anyone for that matter was simply AWOL. Ridiculous. I tried to flag the guy down a few times. I mean really, the place was half full. It's pretty basic. Water the table, bring coffee and check in. Not that hard and we aren't that fussy, but I mean c'mon. 

We left and ate at Top Dog - at least we got served.

In 1989 a guy rounded up the blondes in this restaurant and molested them with carrots before shooting people. If you can get past that, Henry's serves pretty good food.

Crap. I should have probably picked a more appropriate time to post this review.

I remember really liking their seafood pasta some years ago. The other dish I had a few years later was forgettable though.

I don't venture much into the East Bay anymore.  There's no real reason too usually.  However last Thursday was different.  The wife agreed to an event where she spoke about her experience graduating from Boalt Hall and her success at finding a job.  That really says something about the state of the economy by the way.   I wanted to go as well because it would give me an excuse to go to Great China when she was done which happens to be my favorite Chinese restaurant in the bay area.  

While she was doing her thing I figured I'd find a sports bar have a couple pints and watch Thursday night Football.  So I pulled out the trusty phone searched for Sports Bars and Henry's popped up as the closest to where I happened to park.  

I walked in and it was definitely poppin off for a Thursday night I got the last bar stool at the end of the bar ordered a beer and watched the Bears blank the Phins.  After a couple of pints I had to take a whiz.  Lo and Behold the coolest urinal I have ever seen.  Check it out in the photos or click this link 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/XD5ybqI0BHcTj5cLQyIPLA?select=y1lDVa62lHwX2zErvqkF4g

It would be nice to separate Henry's Pub from Henry's Restaurant in reviewing this. Ultimately, I'd say the pub is a great place. High stool chairs around tables & a beautiful looking bar--the actual bar area is pretty nice and I've always enjoyed the ambiance. The drinks are good and they have a rotating tap with good selections. I have only eaten in the restaurant section once (or for that matter, in the pub section as well), but I was not very impressed with the food and the atmosphere was rather dull. That said, the service of both the bar area and the restaurant area are equivalently good. I'd highly recommend Henry's for a drink on game day or to get the night started on a weekend.

I came here with a friend for Easter brunch. With the prices on the menu, this place definitely doesn't cater to college students, unless they're ballers. 
Berry Pancakes ($10) - Good, but definitely not worth the price. I bet the pancakes across the street at Cafe Durant do not pale in comparison. 
Lemongrass Fries (~$4) - Highly recommend these! Very flavorful and they give you plenty! The fries come with with a mayo dipping sauce that prolly did nothing for my summer beach bod, but I wasn't too concerned at that time.

Basically, the brunch was good, but left my wallet feeling lighter. It's a good place to try, but if you're on a budget, you prolly won't become a regular.

This is an alright bar. A lot of the regulars seem to be grad students from Cal, most likely from Haas the way that they look and dress. It's a pretty comfortable place where the hostesses largely leave you alone and are pretty casual about everything. You have people that are just coming in and coming out of your party? Sure thing. You have some under 21s coming in? They don't make a big deal about it. You're extremely loud and paying attention to the games on all the different TVs? Welcome to the rest of Henry's. 

The libations are great and the hostesses are always knowledgeable about their current specials and sometimes even what games are on. The food is alright although their angry mac and cheese did give me some stomach problems. Their other food and appetizers are fantastic though. I love their large bowl of thin-cut fries and a plate of their sweet onion terriyaki wings and sweet potato fries are always a favorite. Their burgers are decent and it's all just typical bar food anyway. 

I've made it to their trivia night and they give out some pretty good swag. Their trivia questions are hard as hell though. I know it's Berkeley but can we not go from 70s rock to chemistry, thanks! I need to make it to their weekly tastings (Alcohol 101 or something).

Chef Blyden made the best burger I've had in years, and the best fries (S&G) and onion rings I've ever had, period.  Yes, the service was weak, but my goodness, I loved the food.  My mother, wife, and children adored the Angry Mac and Cheese, even as leftovers.  I can't wait to go back.

Hands-down my favorite bar in Berkeley.  I love that the staff recognize me when I come in and are always super friendly.  Even the chef comes out to say hi, and he is a very warm and charming guy, not to mention a great cook.  The food is innovative and delicious but lacks pretension.  I can't wait to try more.  Coming in to Henry's always puts a smile on my face.  Now if only they would go back to their 2 for Tuesday nights...

From the outside I was expecting more of an Irish Pub feel, but it turned out to be more of a Western saloon.  Don't bother with the food here, this joint is strictly for boozin'!  They did have Powers Irish Whiskey, which was a surprise.

The food here is great and so is the staff. The food is a bit overpriced but when I went we shared appetizers so it wasn't too bad. We ordered the sweet potato fries- the dipping sauce that came with these was great!, the garlic fries- SO GOOD, the wings- a bit spicy but the lime sauce was good, and the spring rolls- also good, my friends really liked the sauce for these. 
On game days it's pretty crowded and houses the grad students as opposed to the younger undergrads. There are also many TVs to watch the games on and separate tables in another area for some privacy. They also have a good selection of beers.

Wonderful Breakfast! 

Great place to start out the morning! 

Not being to familiar with Berkeley we decided to go to Henry's. 

Pros 
-Great Food 
-Reasonable Prices 
-Great Service 
-Nice Ambiance 
-Nice Booths 

Cons 
- Limited Seating 
- Little kids screaming (that day) 
- Hard to find parking 

Definitely a place I would recommend and go back to.

I was excited to try the recently updated Henry's, inside the Hotel Durant, because I had read that  the new menu was by the same chef as 21st Amendment in the city, and I have enjoyed their delicious jerk chicken and fantastic desserts for many years. Perhaps my expectations were too high, though, because the dinner felt like a bit of a let down.

The experience was strained from the beginning - walking into the place, it was strangely disorienting trying to choose between sitting in the bar area with the televisions or in the dining room. We chose the dining room which quickly felt like it was probably a mistake...it had the feel of a hotel cafeteria (with some very trippy decorations, including starfish and some plastic pot leaves) and the lights were a little too bright to be charming.  I found myself longing for the darker tones of the bar area even though it was television land. Television sports land.

We ordered our drinks and it wasn't until they came and we started to place our order that our waitress told us they were out of two things we wanted - the jerk chicken and the assorted pickled vegetables. So we needed a few more minutes to gather our order together, and this ended up being a mistake as well, because then it was a good 15-20 minutes before our server came back to check on us. Ouch.

When our food finally did come it was quite good, though. The  Angry (spicy) Macaroni and Cheese made up for its lack of a crusty top with a soft and creamy goodness, and the frites were a zesty lemongrass flavor, tender to the tongue but not crunchy enough for my taste. 

We also got the chicken salad, which mixed fennel, orange, radish, and fresh greens, and did the trick. But, damn, I was bummed they had run out of the jerk chicken, the signature dish, if you will.

The best thing about our experience at Henry's was the cocktails - an "East Bay Iced Tea" - Hangar One vodka, fresh lemon and lime juices, and a splash of iced tea. Definitely yummy and worth mimicking at home. We also tried the "Joie to Veev", which features an acai licquer, and another spin on the Cosmo with lots of fresh lime juice. Yum.

I would definitely come here again when I'm craving a fancy designer $9 cocktail (which happens more than I'd like to admit), but I won't be eating here as regularly as a place like T-Rex or Sea Salt.

I lost all respect for Henry's after going to their 2 for 1 Tuesdays.  They have 2 for 1 drink "specials" aka Popov, Captain Morgan, and coke, all served in your standard red plastic party cup.  Someone was probably like, "wouldn't it be awesome if we threw a frat party at this bar and charged people to get in?"........NO, it would not be awesome.

Don't bother with Henry's--just head one block east and hit up bro row.

I'd like to start this review off by apologizing to Henry's for not becoming a fan sooner.

Henry's, my dear -- I'm sorry.

Okay, now that we've got that out the way, let's do this.  When I was a student at Cal, Henry's was always a place that seemed to be packed during game days, evenings, weekends, etc.  I much preferred to go someplace that was cheap and got me drunk quick.  Obviously, "class" didn't mean much to me, as I was pretty much focused on getting s***-faced as quickly and cheaply as possible.

My, how things have changed.

Henry's is definitely a great spot to have a post-hard-day-at-work happy hour with a friend or two.  They've got a great selection of beer and, much to my delight, a fully stocked bar.  Whether I'm in the mood for a pint of some IPA or a glass of scotch, this place knows what it's doing.

Additionally, they've got a nice menu for any occasion, from "I only want a quick beer and appetizer" to "we're starving, want a full on dinner and drinks".  I actually enjoyed the $3 "pickled and spiced vegetables," which were great finger foods for our gathering.

Service was great and the atmosphere was awesome.  I'll definitely become a regular.

Oh, and you get to piss on a Stanford-themed urinal.

Went on a Monday night for football.  Good experience, I'll be back frequently.

They had a couple of beer specials. 1 draft, 1 bottled for $3 each, as well as a couple of food specials.  We ordered orange espresso wings.   Sounds strange, tastes good.  Nice and crispy.  Also had a good Cuban sandwich $12, though the fries could have been crisper.  

Our server gave us outstanding service!  Very friendly and attentive, even though she was the only server at the time.  

They have several high def plasmas for the game.  And the parking lot is now open.  

A bit more upscale than other "sports bars" in the area.

When did Henrys become a gastropub?

We had fun here after finals and the food was pretty good.  Not as crazy as Blakes, much quieter so you can talk.  Classier so a good place to meet before a date.

CHICKEN AND WAFFLES.  

That is all you need to know.

I'd give this place 4 stars but it's getting 5 since this place holds a bit of significance to me...The mister and I came here for our first date. Aww the memories...

Anyway, we came here on a Tuesday night around 7:30pm and took a seat at the bar. There are plenty of places to sit, high and low top tables. They accommodate to big parties also. Seems like an awesome place to watch a Cal game or any other big sporting event, lots of TVs. 

From what I remember, our bartender was the manager; very nice & helpful lady. Since I'm not much of a drinker she and the mister came up with special drinks for me, nothing too strong or too sweet. They have a good alcohol & beer selection and are very open to letting you "try" a beer out.

I ordered the baked mac & cheese and it was DELICIOUS. Definitely not your typical mac & cheese dish. There was something different about it, I think it had prosciutto. The manager raved to us about how good and popular their mushroom appetizer was and ended up giving it to us for free because she really, really wanted us to try it. The sauce was so unique. I've never had mushrooms cooked like this before, definitely a must for anyone that comes here. Oh and they give you bread so you can soak up all that yummy sauce after you demolish the mushrooms.

I heard this place is packed on the weekends...I can't imagine it would be fun standing at the bar with the high top tables only a couple feet away.

I made a reservation for about 20 people about a week before my birthday. I double checked completely that they would be able to fit all of us at one table since it is a small dining room. But of course, we get there, and the dining room is about 75% full and can probably seat 8 of us. I asked our hostess what the problem was, and she said we had to wait about 15 mins and we would be seated at 5 different tables....I said I made sure it was one table, and she said "you can take it or you guys can leave because we dont have another table". I asked to speak to a manager. about 20-30 mins later, we were seated at a weirdly shaped table, and they didnt even apologize. Food was fine, service wasnt good at all (they almost ignored us). Bad experience with their service, and ridiculous that the server would say that. 

I ordered this cheesy potato dish that I really didnt enjoy, it was just so heavy with the cheese and bacon and the potatoes were so dense. Most of the other people ordered burgers and fries, and the fries were really god.

I would consider coming here again for lunch or dinner with just a very small party.

Wow, this restaurant was terrible. We just took a co-worker there in honor of her graduation, and the whole event was just terrible, except for the Eurocup playing on the flat screen t.v.'s located all around the room.

The service was crap. Now generally I am a look at the bright side of life kind of person, but I was really getting pissed. No one bothered to even look at us for ten minutes, and that wasn't until we went and asked for menus. No water. A Jackhammer loud as can be in the room next door making it hard to hear, and the walls vibrate.

Once we did place our order, we waited, waited, and well, waited some more for our food. The orders were wrong, the food was cold, and the beverages were flat. The menu also has limited choices, and not much for vegetarians. Way overpriced. Oh, and did I mention the jackhammer?

First of all, I love the spaetzle here!  It's so rich and satisfying with excellent leftover potential.  Although, the second time I ordered it the waitress sort of corrected my pronunciation.  I lived in Switzerland for a year so hopefully I do know how to say it correctly!  Anyway, I love the decor and atmosphere of the dining room, although I don't think the metal tables in the bar area are especially nice or clean.  I have loved all the food I've had here, especially the escarole salad (such good cheese) and sweet potato fries.  I will be back!

If it ain't broke, why fix it? 

After they redid Henry's, I can't help but think that they've paved paradise and put up a parking lot. I liked the old Henry's. The chili. The wooden bar stools. The atmosphere. All gone. Now, it's a "gastropub." My friends, Henry's has been gentrified. 

The service was fine and attentive. Food? Nothing spectacular. Had the hamburger, and it was a hamburger. $13 for a blue cheese hamburger with fries. Again, nothing to write home about. 

Showed up at noon on a Monday during the intersession for the undergraduate campus. Needless to say, the place was empty. 

My main beef is simply that I liked the old Henry's. I liked the chili. I like chili. 

Oh well.

I have never had a fun night here.  The bouncers always look at you like they might frisk you just for the hell of it.   "No sir, there's no gun in my bra."  The drinks are expensive, served in plastic cups and watered down. Tables are hard to come by and even if it's not crowded, guys still rub up against you like there was no space to squeeze by.

I cannot see this sign without thinking, "Heny's Pubic House & Grille"  It's a crazy psychological block on my part but I can't get past it.  I see the sign and I get this weird mental image in which everything in the bar is covered in pubic hair and it's invades my brain and all i want to do is throw up all over the joint.  Is this just me?  

other than that, it feels very much like a college bar in a college town. which is what it is.  they have two for tuesdays which is full of underage (?) college (?) kids pretending to be drunker than they actually are, freaking to the radio edit of jay z's, "hard knock life".  the irony is not lost on me.  allison b. is totally correct about the bouncers skeevily undressing you with their eyes.  however, when the closest thing you've had to sex in months is watching two homeless people make out over a shopping cart*, this might be a rush.  i don't know, i say get your kicks where you can.  ain't no shame.

*kinda like jake ryan and molly ringwald in the final scene of sixteen candles.  but instead of a birthday cake, it was a shopping cart.  and instead of two attractive teens, it was two 50 year-old meth addicts who hadn't bathed in months.  so possibly molly ringwald circa now?  have you seen that bitch?  she has roughly three teeth and family of birds living in her hair.  she's all walking around france being like, "widgeri widgeri do!  how are you!  i love puppies!  STAND BACK OR I WILL EAT MY OWN HAND!!!!"  

i aspire to such heights.  i am also totally out of it.

Yesterday afternoon at the end of a long day listening to people talk just to affirm their existence I went to a lecture on happiness.  The lecture didn't necessarily give me anything that I was looking for and I'm not sure what I was looking for anyway I'm just certain that whatever it was I didn't get it at the lecture.  But the setting was sublime, all in one of those little glens that cross the Cal campus in places. 

When the questions were almost finished my trusty traveling companion and confidant and I wandered off in search of a libation that perhaps could liberate aspects of the lecture that were trapped lost in my feeble imagination.  We walked to Raleigh's, which to my dismay is now closed and maybe gone forever.  Then, thirstier, we tripped the light Telegraph and found ...

Nothing.

I remembered High Street in Columbus, where Ohio State would go to get its drink on.  Berkeley suddenly seems to have its priorities in all the wrong places.  Not a watering hole to be found!

Until Henry's.  An oasis in my desert.

We shared fish n chips, though much else looked delicious.  The wonderful tender had the order split in the kitchen, divided into matching little iron skillets.  It was delectable, perfect batter, moist and tasty cod, little crispy cooked just right frites.  Three Guinnesseseses.  

Grown ups.

The setting is cozy, the location convenient for all manner things.  Reading the other reviews makes me hungry and I'll go back for certainly to try it again.  I am no closer to my understanding of the happiness, but I can testify without a doubt that for an odd reason the edges of my mouth curled upwards yesterday in Henry's.  It was a pleasing sensation.

I went to a free lunch at the Hotel Durant for this on-line registration company (Cvent) and the food, from Henry's, was pretty tasty.  My step-sister used to hang out here a lot back in the day but then there was that terrible incident where that guy held a bunch of people hostage in there and she was one of them.  Because of that, I never went there.  It is still creepy to think about.

"On Sept. 27, 1990, Mehrdad Dashti, a deranged man carrying three concealed handguns, walked into a popular U.C.-Berkeley hangout. Twenty minutes later, he opened fire, injuring many people and killing one. Ultimately, the incident became an eight-hour siege during which 33 people were held hostage."

more about the incident here: http://www.scu.edu/ethics/dialogue/candc/cases/publick.html

For this place to not be super packed on a Friday night in Berkeley could mean that it's no good.

But it was great.  It was fun, not overly crowded, and the food was quick, and tasty and kept the beer from getting my drunk. 

They have a strong menu of mixed drink options (I had to try the GOSSIP GIRL drink which was pure rum almost) and a variety of pub/bar food with a little bit of a kick.  (Ie. the spicy mac and cheese was hot hot hot!)  The staff is there to work but also make your night fun, and the crowd in there is friendly even while watching whatever game is on TV.

Every seat was taken but it wasn't a situation in which I could barely move- PERFECT for me.

1) Best place to go on game day - I mean the two games I haven't gone to but have celebrated, I've been here.
2) If you show up on a random week night with one other girl, and you two look really lame in sweat pants just having a glass of wine at the bar, most likely the bar tender will give you the drinks for free.   maybe not, but that's what happened to me.
3) My roommate made a lasting friendship with one of the Cal basketball players.  It's a special relationship wholly implemented through facebook and instant messages.

Thank you Henry's!

I've never had a bad time at Henry's. The bouncers take one look and decide eh, what the hell.
Inside there is definitely the frat atmosphere, but you can find a few friends to chill and relax with. Take advantage of the dance floor if you must. 
Also Two for Tuesdays drink specials rock. It's quite happening on Tuesday night so get there early if you want a table or to get in the door.
p.s. My friend is one of the waitresses so be nice.
It's my watering hole for watching CAL Bears Football and Basketball on the TVs.

Pub is nice.  For food, the breakfast was a bit overpriced (they called it brunch, but for $14, a breakfast like one you'd get at Denny's for $4.99).  I do not know why American hotels, esp. one in a hotel in a college town, do not do breakfasts in the European way...nice buffet, included in the price.

Went for Sunday breakfast after a late night out on Saturday night. They had football games on many large LCD screens (good), with the sound at a low-ish but still hear-able level (good).  About  1/2 full of people, so it was busy enough to be nice, but not so busy you didn't get help.

Waiters took good care. Complements here.

I had an omelet. I generally don't get them, because they're often so bad. But this was very nicely done, with spicy local chorizo, mushrooms & local cheese. Nicely fluffy, but still firm enough to hold together as you ate it. The local touches were good.  The potatoes were a bit mushy, but fine.  A side of berries & vanilla yogurt helped bring some coolness to the breakfast.

All in all, thumbs up.  I wish I'd have stayed at the hotel this is in. It's a Joie de Vivre hotel, and I generally like that brand - and it would have been much better than where I _did_ stay. (Don't ask...)

Had a coupon from Caltopia for a free Angry mac'ncheese.

Walked in. Got seated in the corner. TVs blaring football and some CSI-like show. Got served the mac'ncheese.

HUGE bowl. OMG, it's like the size of the pho bowls I get back in Little Saigon. Nice crispy panko topping. Creamy pale yellow cheese over pasta....I polished the bowl clean. 

Basically, BEST EFFIN' MAC'N'CHEESE I've ever had. Thank you for the freeness too! ($10 about, without). I have "joined the mob."

Waiter came later and basically said I didn't have to even leave tip or anything, no obligation with that coupon. I left a tip though, because I was so darn happy.

Go here, get the mac'ncheese. Be warned, it's loud here.

My favourite bar to watch a game at when I'm feeling real classy because it's so close to campus. I've been here mostly during the day on Fridays and Saturdays, or whenever there's a hockey game on. They're really nice about that - they'll usually change the channel on one of the TVs (if you want to watch a completely obscure sport while everyone else is watching basketball or baseball) upon request. It's never too crowded, but then again I've never been during happy hour or at nights.

They have a decent selection of beer, nothing too fancy. The drinks are a little pricey and not too strong. Their food menu is also pretty steep for students, and it's not that great. I enjoy their Lemongrass Garlic Fries and Angry Mac & Cheese, but everything else is either too greasy (Chicken Fingers, Fish & Chips) or unsatisfying portion-wise (Henry's Pub Burger, Steak). 

Then again, I have a sneaking suspicion that Henry's target audience isn't Berkeley undergrads but rather patrons of the conjoined Hotel Durant. Either way, I'll stick to my beer!

Just a comfy, neighborhood pub.  We've been here at least 1/2 a dozen times and never had trouble getting a seat.  We've often wondered why it isn't more crowded given its atmosphere, proximity to campus and decent grub.  Once we caught a reasonably talented musician playing acoustic guitar on a random weeknight - very pleasant. 

Coming from a city with a pub on every corner (chicago) - this town needs lots more spots like Henry's.
I'd give this place a 3.5. The setting is nice, but the prices are quite high. The service was pretty slow as well. I recommend the angry macaroni dish. Pretty damn good

Been to Henry's once for drinks and just recently for food. Getting a seat in the sunny room was the beginning to a nice experience....
service wasnt too great but the atmosphere and food was better than expected! We ordered the mushroom swiss burger with sweet potato fries and the shepards pie. The burger was delivered with regular fries, honest mistake, so we waited for the SP fries but in the end the three of us agreed the regular fries were better, crunchy and salty and YUMMO! Burger was great, cooked perfectly and big enough to share. Shepards pie portion looked small but in the end it was heavy and plenty of food. It had great flavor with a yummy mashed potato top instead of pastry, and was piping hot! Overall the food was very good, sunny room was very relaxing, a little expensive with drinks but I would definetly go back soon!

Henry's was an OK place to go for 2 for Tuesdays back in the day (damn I feel old).  But damn, that place would get really crowded just to get sorry excuses for drinks; two cups filled with ice with a half-ounce of liquor didn't exactly get me buzzed.  Try somewhere else in Berkeley for a better time.

came here for dinner during a monday night football kickoff night. The dining room was really empty, but the main bar was packed. Had some chicken and waffles, which were decent, but not as good as Roscoes. Quesadillas and fries with garlic dip was delicious. They also have Guiness stout for pitchers. Really pricey though, but great service.

I used to go to Henry's once in a while on a Tuesday night when I went to school at Cal 4 years ago.  It used to be pretty much like any other frat boy hangout, and I didn't really like going.  I went back recently on a Friday night, and am really impressed with the change.  The bartender was really nice (not to mention HOT).  I think it has new TVs too--Berkeley was lacking a good sport's bar.  Bring all your friends--this place ROCKS!

I just have to update now that I've eaten here. The food is soooooo good. Try the tomato and havarti sandwich. You won't even notice the lack of meat. Seriously. So good.

We surprised the bar with a rather big group last night, and Amy, the ONLY bartender there, was awesome. Somehow she handled all of us and the normal customers without anybody getting upset. Not sure how she did it, but I've got to give her major props.

My family ( five of us) had dinner at Henry's before the Herbie Hancock show  last week at Zellerbach. We were very pleasantly surprised at the quality and tastiness of the food: great steaks, excellent ribs and British style fish and chips, that passed muster with the only native-born Brit in our group!
We also had a great waiter - who despite have to serve both the dining room and the bar never let us down. Very good value for money and I will definitely be back, and will tell my friends!

Three of us (me, the boyfriend, and friend of the boyfriend) came here over Labor Day weekend at friend-of-boyfriend's insistence. He was adamant that they have the best Bloody Mary he'd ever had, so we headed over. It was around noon on a Sunday and the place was near-empty, so they swept us from the elegant little bar straight to the lovely dining room. Seriously, lovely is the best word I can find to describe the decor--lovely wallpaper, lovely bay windows...just lovely all around. I was impressed from the start.

A Bloody Mary was ordered and we all agreed that it was, in fact, as delicious as described. I got an omelette with tomatoes, green onions, and emmentaler (my favorite cheese, so bonus points for that one). Fantastic. More bonus points for the sofrito potatoes and the adorable tray of butter, jam, and marmalade. Boyfriend ordered a really good-looking burger topped with some carmelized onions that I kept sneaking off his plate when his back was turned; friend-of-boyfriend chose the crab benedict and devoured it in minutes (his only complaint was the consistency of the yolks--a bit too hard for good benedict).

Service was excellent, food was superb, and all in all we really, thoroughly enjoyed our meal. New favorite spot to eat in Berkeley? I think yes.

Came here tonight for appetizers and drinks. Great service but food is just so-so. We ordered the mac n cheese, the wings and also the fries. The mac n cheese was good but wasn't super great. Wings had unique flavor to them and were pretty good. The fries also had a unique flavor but i wasn't too fond of them. Overall though this place is a lot nicer to hang out in than many of the other places open late at night.

Slightly sad about the new Henry's (food-wise). I used to LOVE their mushroom (came in a cute pot, super delicious) and now they sort of just stir-fry & put the mushrooms in a marinade and serve it on a plate.

Good location, good for small groups and casual get-togethers. Not as much beer selection as Raleighs but since it's just Henry's and Pappy's left...Henry's is my go-to-bar.

If you knew me in my heydey, you may have associated me with Henry's and Two for Tuesdays. The bouncer even had the same birthday as me, so that makes this place that more symbolic for me. You can get 2 mixed drinks for $5 but expect to spend a lot more money just to feel the buzz. For me, however, twice double-fisting bud bottles brings me to utter elation as the hip hop beats bring my moves to the dance floor. I recommend getting beer in bottles here because it is a small and cramped place and you usually have to go through the gauntlet of dancers just to get back to your congregation spot away from the bar.  But believe me, bring your closest friends, prepare to get drunk, and don't be shy about talking to all those acquaintences you have met during your years here at Cal. A great place to re-connect, let loose, and build friendships. Definitely a lot of morning-after chuckling. -Matt

Pretty nice spot, came here on the monday trivia night. The food is really good here, I got the burger which was awesome, the fries are good thin cut and crispy. The beer selection is great, they have a bunch of micro-brews on tap and nice bottled beers. Its an interesting comparison of the dining area to the bar area, totally different atmospheres which is good depending what you are in the mood for. Kind or random/weird you go through a hotel lobby to get here, seems like it should have its own entrance

Wherever Chef Eddie Blyden goes, I follow!

I've been his groupie for years and years, from 21st Amendment and Alembic in the city to, yes, even the east bay for Henry's! Several restraining orders aside, that is how much I adore this internationally trained chef who puts the spice in my life. Kidding! (There was just that one incident in the Haight...) Kidding!

CEB's Caribbean past and gastropub present collide in my wooo-that's-hot favorite 'Angry Mac and Cheese' -- who knew the Mac could attack? 

And no where in the Bay Area are you gonna find you some Man Butter smoother than this. What's that short for? Wait for it,... Manischewitz butter!! Who cooks with the Mani? Heck, who even drinks it unless their parents force them to at sunset? Chef Eddie, that's who. What a mensch!

This uber creative chef of Zurich, Antigua, West Africa and Bay Area fame has found his stride at Hotel Durant, whose new renovations and innovations obviously didn't stop at a coat of paint. 

Henry's is great when you want to watch the game and crave something more than fries and a burger. And hey, its price point is out of poor students' ranges, so enjoy the company of adults right near campus! :) 

Okay, I'll stop my chef worship now. Head to Henry's, and tell 'em I sent ya! 

...Mmmm... man butta...

I LOVE HENRY'S!! i cant beleive i didn't review this place yet..

BASICALLY, if you want to get a stiff cocktail and don't want to feel all grossed out and dirty *cough* BLAKES *cough*, this is the place to go.  Right by campus, you can stop by and have a drink after a long and intense study session! 
my favorite cocktails here are the joie de veev and the special bloody mary! and the specialty cocktail Amy makes me on fridays! yum! 

the FOOD FOOD FOOD! MMMMMMMMMMMMM!!! my favorite is the angry mac and cheese. oh my.  i had such a craving i just HAD to go.  the cuban panini is wonderful, too. basically, chef eddie makes everything TASTY!!! 

the only downside is the price- a bit steep for college kids, i have to say, but still, SO WORTH IT!!!! im definitely gonna miss this place when i graduate. *tear*.  

overall, GREAT FOOD, GREAT COCKTAILS, convenient location, newly rennovated interior, and friendly staff!
I love this place for game days! The atmosphere is fun and the drinks delicious! If you find yourself there enjoying a game, definitely try a "Golden Bear" drink (warning: it is alcoholic).

ok, admittedly my review is based purely on 1 experience, but nevertheless....

I am amazed that no one on here has mentioned the "cottage pie", it is sooooo good.  lamb, mushrooms, carrot and onion cooked in guinness, "cheesy mashed potatoes", all combine to form the most delicious sheperd's pie I have ever tasted (seriously, this is wonder food).  All this for $14, and yes, split it between you and your date.

The cocktail I ordered was their $7 "East Bay Iced Tea", made with Buddha's Hand and Keffir Lime vodkas from Hangar One's distillery in Alameda... also very, very good, and strong!

Next, I ordered their $7 chocolate espresso pudding with crushed nuts and salt flakes - also amazing! quite strong on the espresso flavor, but if you're a fan of coffee you'll appreciate this.  It was like after-dinner coffee + amazing chocolatey/salty/crunchy/deliriously good dessert all in one!

Sure, the decor is a little old and verging on outdated, but it has a nice "homey" feel, our waiter was friendly and even cracked a few good jokes, and the prices are not bad when you compare them to other restaurants in the area.  I personally went here with my parents (yay for not having to pay), but I would be just as likely to come here with the bf for a special occasion (especially given you could split the cottage pie - $7 each for heavenly food? I'm in).

I guess I'm a fan of the whole gastropub thing.  Never did know the "old" Henry's though, so can't comment on that.

Henry's has stepped it up... BIG.

I went to Cal and used to get trashed there on 2-for-Tuesdays as a student.  My expectations were.... hell, there were no expectations.

As I have gotten older, I do require certain things- and in the past years Henry's has delivered. 

Their menu has expanded, offering much more than just "bar food".
Can you say "surf and turf"?

The service has improved massively. 
The music is better selected and not blaring. 
The bathrooms are always clean.
They upgraded to flat screens everywhere and the NFL ticket.

Not to mention, they always add creative and comical specials.
(See: "Arcade Fire Shots" the night of the Arcade Fire show at the Greek- deliciously spicy tequila hits with hot sauce and fresh squeezed lime that certainly got us in the mood for the show.)

Are tuesday's mayhem?
Yes- that's why I don't go then... but if you are 22 and looking for fun, I say "do it."

Are Gamedays chaos?
Ummm- yes. It's a gameday. It's what I expect and where I see every Cal grad from the last 10 years. Perfect.

They are currently closed for remodeling so I only anticipate things getting better...

Not that the decor was bad to begin with-- high ceilings, beautiful wood bar, and Cal memorabilia wall to wall.

Bottom line: There is no better Sports Bar in Berkeley.

One in the afternoon. The stagnant air is thick with it--the yeasty stench of shitty beer and perspiration, the peculiar odor of week old, reheated Fat Slice--it's NFL Sunday. Sure, you're locked into routine, but you should know that there's a whole nother world out there. One whose philosophy espouses tap brews, HDTV, and, most importantly, no sweatpants. Be better than your apartment. Be at Henry's.

Here, you have, at face value, another dime a dozen sports pub. And, in truth, it is, but it's a nice one. There's the decent albeit largely pedestrian beer selection, elevated, overly polished faux-mahogany chairs, and dimmed, amber lighting. Throw in an assortment of televisions of varied sizes, though all viewable, and you have yourself a serviceable sport-media viewing experience. As a plus, there are always a handful of Raiders fans present every week, and it should be noted that there is no seasoning that pairs so well with any dish as their disheartened snot and tears.
 
The menu, in accordance with what many of the reviews before me have indicated, is largely overpriced, though, in it's own right, quite good. What's more, their seasonal pastas, surprisingly, are fantastic. Some of the best in Berkeley. With such gems as tomato crème and chanterelle (what hotel sports bar serves chanterelles? You fuckin serious here?) fusilli with broccoli, and fava bean, English pea orecchiette in a basil lemon butter sauce, you'll--and this is no small praise for a place with such outrageous prices--get your money's worth. The pasta itself is nicely al dente, the vegetables and individual constituents cooked perfectly...c'mon Gypsy's--if a sports bar can pull this off, why can't you?

As a whole, this institution is worthy of any sports fanatic. It has all the makings of a good team-viewing bar, right down to the heckling, oversized jersey-clad division rivals. The fact that I almost ran down a pair of douchebag patriots fans (aren't they all?) for their antics actually adds to the experience.The ambiance is praisable, the service and pricing less so, and the food is a-ok (with a three-star rating to match). In conclusion, it's a bar.

The service was the only good thing about this place, but even that wasn't great as the server lied to me. She told me the crab cakes were small (oh yes they were) but they were all crab and no filler. Umm, what's this corn and scallion then? The two teeny fried crabcakes were basically all filler and the arugula salad they came with (wish I would have known as I started with a ceaser salad) was way too salty.  My husband's turkey burger was okay but nothing special. 

Everything was overpriced for the quality. Two beers, crab cakes, a salad and a turkey burger came out to $45. Not worth it.

I love the name Henry. I have a secret reason for that but anyhow.....

when I used to go to Berkeley I never went to Henry's on game day because the old people went there. Now I'm an old person and I go there because that is where all the people my age are.

I used to go to Henry's to watch football games, especially NFL games because they have Sunday ticket, but after they renovated, their prices went way up.  The food improved, but not enough to warrant the prices, especially with the small portions (I paid $10 for a small bowl of angry mac&cheese and a coke). I haven't had the bad experience with waiters and bartenders that others seem to have had (in fact, I've found them quite friendly), but I prefer Bear's Lair for game days.

I went here for breakfast when I was a hotel guest at Hotel Durant.  

The service was slow as molasses.  I had to get up to get the following: (1) a menu after 10 minutes, (2) ketchup after asking for it and waiting 5 minutes, (3) my check after waiting with my finished plate for 10 minutes.  I saw people who arrived after me finish their meals and pay their checks before I received my food.  

My eggs-over-medium were runny like the bulls.  

The only reason I gave it a two is because I got a free glass of orange juice, I had a nice window view, and the bacon came out perfectly.

Nice enough place and the beer was relatively inexpensive... but the service was REALLY slow and we practically had to beg for attention, and for the check. Definitely wasn't busy enough that it should have been that hard.

Nice atmosphere but thats where it ends. 

Service was fast but the waitress had no clue. She couldn't remember what we ordered and didn't know the menu.

Food: Two cheeseburgers ordered were good to my dad and husband BUT my dad said no onions, he got onions. French Fries were good minus the HAIR my husband found in them. Mac and Cheese was just ok. They were out of two menu items I wanted so I ended up with the buttermilk chicken sandwich. One word for that : GROSS. 

No kids menu and the Mac and Cheese has "stuff" in it (my 4 year old pointed out)

Drinks: Beer, Wine and Martini all fine. Water glasses were dirty. 

The waitress could have bought us a round or comp'd something for the HAIR, the non-exsiting menu items and the chicken sandwich I didn't eat but that didn't happen.

Seriously, I've never had a good experience at Henry's no matter how many times I've been there. A few months back, I made reservations for a large group because it was my friend's birthday. Right off the bat, the waitress trips and spills my beer onto the table, spills everything else on her serving platter including a glass of red wine onto the table right in front of me. The glass shatters and the red wine spills onto a few people, most of it on my purse and coat!! It's not her fault and I wish her all the best, but the clean up was so not smooth. I ended up wiping off half the stuff off the ground for them. Plus, they did not offer dry cleaning until the end of the dinner. If I were the manager, I would've apologized and mentioned that right away. I know it's not a written rule and it's not for granted, but a free dessert would've been nice to smooth things over, especially since we were such a big group anyway and paid a big gratuity and it was someone's birthday and we chose to eat here.

Oh well. At least their mac and cheese is good.

Cost of meal + beer: $15.

Size of group: 4.

Time waited for hostess to tell us to seat ourselves: 3.5 minutes.

Attention paid to us once seated: Nominal.

Impression of food: Mediocre.

Effort put into our overall dining experience by Henry's staff: About as much effort as I put into this review.
My family went to Henry's for a weekend brunch and we were pleasantly surprised as to how good it was!  The service was very good and the food was amazing.  A real find!

I had an absolutely fantastic meal at Henry's a few nights ago, and..I never expected it. A colleague and I had an event on the UC campus nearby, and we needed to eat quickly, but in a warm spot -the student food joints on Durant or Telegraph might be quick, but they all leave their doors wide open to gales -and I don't think it is necessary to review their culinary standards here anyway (ah ah.) So we got into Henry's, because we knew it to serve food and to have this usually empty dining room. Yes, we were ready to settle for a mediocre burger or mac'n'cheese in exchange for a warm seat in a quiet place. Boy, we got way more than what we bargained for! We both had a very tasty sunny tomato soup to start (with fresh basil leaves beautifully crowning it). Then my colleague ordered the burger & fries, and proceeded to swear this was the best he had in the last 6 months! Myself, I had a dish that took me to Italy in a stunning recreation of the Proustian flash: first bite. It was a sort of ratatouille with 2 grilled polenta cakes on top of the vegetable base; the "Johnny cakes"  were creamy inside and crisp outside, and the vegetables (and raisins too?) in that yummy ratatouille were bursting with flavor. PLUS: it came presented in a antique-looking ceramic dish straight out of my grandmother's pantry. Visually and gustatively, it was a smashing event in a place I never knew could deliver such magic. We had no time for dessert- sadly- but we were very pleased with the service as well: friendly, fast, and efficient. I am very sure I will go back to Henry's , no hesitation. Gee, I actually wanted to call the chef and compliment him/her, like in a 4 star palace!

Excellent place for day-time drinking. But then again, things are generally pretty excellent if you're drinking in the daytime. 

Basically, go before/after football games. Don't go to the wannabe club night on Tuesday.

tuesdays were awesome... haven't been here in more than 2 years, but *sigh* let me reminisce.. 

packed craziness, sticky floors, dancing, drinking, snarfing down topdawgs afterwards, and stumbling back to the apartment..

I came here after my graduation with a party of 25 people, and they were able to accommodate us even after we changed our reservation for # of people at the last minute.  They placed all of us into the room to the side of the bar/restaurant, I think it's usually used for conferences, testing, or classes.  The set-up was really nice and the service wasn't too slow, seeing that there were so many of us.  So for the service, I'd give them 4-stars.  

However, the food was just mediocre, although the portions are very generous.  Food = 3-stars

Went here a few times a few years back while I was at Cal. Never a big fan back then. The lights there were always too bright and the food not so good. But a great selection of beers and a classy space in the lobby of the Hotel Durant. 
Was back in Berkeley yesterday for the M.Arch thesis final reviews and Henry's was the chosen place for the celebratory post-thesis drinks. Also happened to be a great place to watch the Celtics win one of the best playoff series in sports history. Most of my architect buddies wished the game wasn't so noisy, but I was happy that unlike Triple Rock, my intended destination that evening, Henry's actually leaves the sound on for games, which is necessary even if you can't hear a word the announcers are saying over the din. A nicely divided crowd between Boston and Chicago, rowdy but civil and a lot of fun. 
The food has improved a lot since they revamped the kitchen. I snacked on some sweet potato fries that were just right and some overly moist calimari before digging into some mac and cheese that was tasty, though not my style. Was pleasantly surprised at the spiciness because I ordered based on how my friend's food looked rather than from the menu. Very original recipe. Burger and fries also looked really good. But of course the improvement in the quality is concurrent with a rather serious increase in prices.
Nevertheless, after previously having some poor experiences, Henry's delivered today. When I read that they had shaken things up there I was really encouraged and it seems that they weren't fooling around. The food the service and the atmosphere are lot better than in my days at Cal, but without really changing the place visibly at all. I will definitely have to start considering this place as an alternative sports bar to Triple Rock, particularly when I require the sound to be on.

The nicest sports bar I've ever been to. Jillian has nothing on Henry.
Not to mention there's parking....oh yes, there's parking in the back, free if you spend at least $15 on your tab...and that's sure to happen. 

Tons of taps, comfy booths and high top tables, or sit in the restuarant side away form the bar to nurse your hangover. 

The food is awesome! Have a fabulous early or late breakfast while you watch your home team making the winning play. There's also starving student specials that give you bang for your buck if you can stomach 2lbs of meat in one sitting.

Clean and inviting, you could be a Harvard professor, a software engineer, or a u-cal drop out and you'll find your place at the bar. 

Plus, they have ALL the games on, not just the local ones!!! O ya...GO STEELERS!!!

Henry's is a Berkeley institution that I've been frequenting since I started using a fake id.  Okay now, let's not go down that road.... 

Henry''s sits on prime Berkeley real estate.  

It's on the corner of Durant and Bowditch, right up Durant from the glorious original Top Dog, and one block away from the UC Berkeley campus.
  
These days, I usually come here for Breakfast or lunch..  It's not really known as a breakfast spot, so you generally have the place all to yourself on a weekday.  

Henry's is a spacious restaurant that connects to the Hotel Durant. There is a long dark wood bar positioned against the back wall with a ladder leading up shelves of booze stacked to the ceiling.

They have a decent beer selection on tap and three TV screens above the bar turned to SportsCenter and various games..  The bartenders are laid back college students and the food is surprisingly good. If you come here with your significant other, or a group of friends, you can also use the separate dining room facing Durant.

But, there is one more thing to remember.. Henry's is a Cal bar through and through..  Don't come here rocking your red crips gear...  They just might confuse you for a Stanford fan.. Also, if you're a guy, you can really take a piss on Stanford here....   ( See photos...)

Oh, and Go Bears!

Drink with the stars. I swear I saw Robert Downey Jr. here, coming down from his room at the hotel Durant and ordering a drink, with a cal hat pulled down below his eyes. I have yet to confirm that, im still researching. I did buy Mark Morris a drink and hung out a bit with the man. What, you don't know who Mark Morris is, he is big in the dance world, trust me (im now a little bit embarrass to admit that I know that). This place isn't as bad as the previous post, although I do have warm fuzzy feelings of courting my lady and having her college roommate work here. The bar is defiantly caters to the wealthy Cal alumni and parents of those students. Forget about this place on game day, before or after, it is packed, and I mean packed.

I love the new Henry's,  and the gastro-pub deliciousness! Chef Eddie Blyden is the nicest chef, and takes care to come out and check on his guests and talk about his food. I love that he and his staff remember my husband and me every time we come in. I love the steak and eggs for breakfast, the husband favors the Cuban sandwich, and we both love trying new things on the menu. The new beer soup (yes, I said beer soup!) is amazing and just what you need on a cold winter day. We have been showing up frequently for weekend brunch and lunch since the new launch, and recommend it to many of our friends.

We spent our wedding night at the hotel, and will always have great memories of partying in the bar with our wedding guests and having my mother-in-law close the bar down. You know you are in Berkeley when drinking at a pub in a wedding dress and nobody blinks twice.

This is a great restaurant, and the angry mac and cheese is angry and awesome!

The only downer about staying at Hotel Durant was our poor decision to try and spend some dough at this place, Henry's.

Scanning the prior reviews, it sounds like it was better when it was a regular bar to watch games and not a "gastropub".   

We were amped when we got to Berkeley.  We loved our hotel rooms.  We were hungry, tired, and thirsty after traveling and ready to take a breather, relax, and sip some over-priced cocktails and watch some Inauguration coverage.  Instead, we spent the entire time trying to get service.  I don't usually say bad things about waitstaff unless it's really bad- and this was awful. 

1.  My friend really did not like her wine ($9).  She's not a fussy gal, but it was not what she ordered and she couldn't even swallow it, it was not good.  Instead of just asking what she would like instead and making a typical swap, the waitress gave my friend grief and attitude about it, after walking past us 5-6 times first, ignoring us.  

2.  It was like pulling teeth to get some water.  She was rude.  And aloof and unattentive.  We don't ask for much, but she totally disappeared anyway, only to reappear again when my friend finally decided to just go up to the bar and order from the bartender directly.  She intercepted.  

3.  The couple at the table next to us were having an equally difficult time with her, and after they bailed out, she picked up the check, looked at what they left for a tip and threw a hissy fit about it, to no one in particular.  Ugh.  

Here are a couple of pluses:  the cocktails were excellent.  I had the Negroni (made with local gin, if I recall...), and it was one of the best I have ever had.  Also notable were the lemongrass frites ($5).  This may or may not have been in direct relation to how delirious we were after a long travel day, but shoot howdy, those really hit the spot.  Until the waitress took them away from me when there were still several left in the bowl.  

We also had the wontons- before ordering, we asked the waitress what they were filled with and after she rolled her eyes really slowly, she said, "Nothing".  So, there you have it- the wontons are just the fried wonton skins, with a bit of dipping sauce.  The menu did not specify that it was just the skins, so I really could have done without the attitude.    

In short, a bad waitress ruined the whole experience, but it's not really the fault of Henry's in general, I suppose.  If I'm ever back, I will sit at the bar for sure, and sip Negroni after delicious Negroni and hopefully avoid another encounter with The Snottiest Waitress Ever.

Chef Eddie Blyden continues to turn out some of the best bar food around.

Onion rings, worth the trip. Consistently the best ever. Great crunch but you can bite cleanly through them. Come with a delicious cilantro aioli-ish dip.

Tuna melt ($11, add $2 for onion rings), by far the best version of this sandwich I've had. Made on whole-wheat bread with a fair amount of cracked wheat for a nice crunch, press-toasted to a dark brown.

"Poutine" ($9), fries, roast or braised pork, couple of kinds of cheese, onion gravy, I think I'm forgetting something. Delicious, though I kind of felt like I should properly have had eight or ten drinks first.

Spicy pickles ($3), a little sweet, pretty sour, carrots, celery, and bell pepper. Generous helping. These will probably join the onion rings as something I have to order every time.

That was a lot of food for two people.

At the moment, the online menu's about six months out of date.

Do you want servers to ignore you for the vast majority of your dining experience?  Then Henry's might be the place for you.

This might be the worst dining experience I've encountered in years.  I wasn't even hungry, so I ordered bacon, extra crispy.  It came out limp and greasy.  So I sent it back.  A $4 order of bacon took close to a half hour to get to me in the manner in which I asked for it.  

If the only problem was a neglectful server, I would say it was a fluke.  But the experience gets better.  My friend, concerned about catching her flight was about to leave when a bartender we knew from days of old came by with some complimentary pomegranate mimosas - a wonderful gesture that made me almost forget the abysmal service up to that point.

That is, until all five mimosas ended up all over my friend,  

Now, she took her pomegranate mimosa bath like a champ, and the bartender was very apologetic.  But, that being said, she was now in a predicament where catching her flight was in jeopardy.  And yet, no one offered to comp her meal or anyone else's meal.  

But here's the worst part.

Later that day, I found myself on BART trying to buy a train ticket home, and I kept getting a message that my card was denied.  So I checked my bank account information, and it turns out that they overcharged my card by $50.  I called to try and explain to the manager the mistake and the inconvenience it caused me, and all he could say was "I'm really busy right now.  Can I deal with this Monday?"  and I'm thinking to myself, "Yeah, sure...no problem.  I mean, it's not like I'm going to get charged overdraft fees for your mistake, for a bill we shouldn't have even gotten after my friend got mimosas dumped all over her... no, sure, go ahead and deal with it at YOUR convenience, as opposed to mine."

I guarantee that, despite Henry's having been a frequent haunt of mine in my Berkeley college days, I will NEVER set foot in there again after the horrific customer service I received.  In addition, I will make sure none of my friends or family ever sets foot in there or the Durant Hotel without knowing what they are in for.

In other words, 

avoid.
TWO FOR TUESDAYS!!!!!

WEDNESDAY NIGHTS ROCK! Wednesday nights are a good night to come hang out with friends and check out a local singer / songwriter Mikie Lee Prasad.  He's got awesome talent and is cute to boot!  I think he's starting to have opening bands - changes all the time.  Make friends with the bartender and one drink will go a looooonnnng way (like til the next morning when you go off to work!). Haha! Anyhoo, seems that there are mixed reviews - I say come and judge for yourself - you definitely won't be disappointed in the music :o)

I've decided to add a star to my review as I received a wonderful message from Chef Eddie at Henry's today which said, 

"I was very sorry to read about your burger experience at Henrys. I would love to have you try one again, on us of course, as this was a rare occurence. An overcooked burger is no excuse, and no grilled onions must have been one of those days..... I am so glad you enjoyed some other menu items :). Please let me know when you can stop in next time for a perfect Medium Rare burger!"

It WAS Mother's Day and they may have been extremely swamped in the kitchen. My friend Pam spoke so highly of the food that I would love to try it again. Unfortunately I don't live in the area so I am unable to take him up on his offer right away but I will definitely be giving the burger another try when I have my girls weekend there later in the year and I applaud the effort. Fantastic customer service! 

And just so you know, I would have gone back anyway just to have those fries again! I shit you not, I have DREAMS about eating those fries. My mouth is watering right now in anticipation of tasting the amazingness again someday.

**This review is for drinks only**

Henry's was one of my haunts, many, many moons ago when i went to Berkeley. And, boy has Henry's changed. The place has expanded with 1.5-2x the indoor space as they used to have, and the parking lot has been converted into another bar outside. And thank goodness they have all of the extra space because it can get crowded on game day. 

While it's not particularly scenic to stand around a parking lot looking at the short apartment buildings on Bowditch, it is one of the few restaurant/bars that has an outside area. Beers and mixed drinks are decently priced, especially with some of the liquor specials they have running.

As an FYI to the ladies, the restroom situation is sad. Besides the port-a-potties outside, there's only one restroom downstairs so it takes forever...

WARNING: *** Delicious mac and cheese alert!!!! ***
