I'm very happy that we happened upon Henry's today. It was much, much better than our original plan for a boring soup and salad lunch. Granted, it was also more calorie-filled, but delicious!

You have the choice of dining in either the sports bar area or in a more formal feeling dining room. Although we were in t shirts and jeans, we wanted to class it up, so we chose a fun semi-circle booth in the fancy room. 

The food was extremely delicious. I had the "angry mac n cheese" with bacon. You guys don't event know how tasty this was! It was certainly enough for two people. The noodles were perfect, large elbows, cheesy and lightly spicy, the bread crumbs and scallions on top were the perfect garnish. This has quickly become a close contender for my favorite mac and cheese in the Bay.

My dining companion had the Cuban sandwich with sweet potato fries and a lime aoli on the side. Both were extremely flavorful and tasty. All in all, it was a delectable choice for lunch.

Also, from the bar, we had the Irish coffee and the Smirnoff salty dog (a greyhound - which is grapefruit juice and vodka - with a salted rim). 

I'll definitely be back to Henry's sometime soon! Good food, friendly service, great atmosphere.

Came here for drinks and was not overly impressed yet I wasn't disappointed either.  I guess I got what I expected out of this place.  Service was decent and the drinks were priced well.

The highlight of this place is the men's bathroom.  There is a red urinal  with a Standford logo on it that you can piss on.

i hate this bar.

but in all fairness, i hate this bar because i associate it with the way too many wasted (lost, not drunk. but also, sometimes that kind of wasted, too) nights i spent here because one of my ex-boyfriends worked here. and i kind of hate him.

the bar is okay when it's not crowded.

the food is all right, but not worth the price.

never, ever go here on a tuesday or a game day.

Online menu is out of date. 

I wanted to the try the Cubano here, but wasn't available so I went with the American Dip ($13, shaved, slow roasted natural beef ribeye, emmentaler, horseradish crème on a French baguette, with a smoked porter beef au jus and truffled frites) and a "cup" of their soup of the day ($4) which was Roasted Red Pepper.

Wait, emmentaler, crème, baguette, au jus, frites? Sounds like some anti-American Euro-terrorist sandwich to me. Is this some kind of Freedom Fry naming strategy? 

Anyway, I put "cup" in quotes because this serving of soup was big (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/XD5ybqI0BHcTj5cLQyIPLA?select=wE-xeVJOk8Oukub8k0_9OQ) and very good with a smooth consistency and strong roasted pepper flavors. I mopped up the dregs of soup with some of the bread they gave.

My American Dip plate (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/XD5ybqI0BHcTj5cLQyIPLA?select=3SmQrjmbosLaK26wzsKK_g) was mixed. The fries (which come in a cute mini-fry basket) were irregularly cut so some were crispy and some were limp. Nice truffle flavor, but I had to pick around the limp / undercooked ones.

The sandwich looked good in the center with a decent amount of delicious medium rare roast beef (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/XD5ybqI0BHcTj5cLQyIPLA?select=VePZxUbHLKcs1Rs8UF4W_Q), but the meat quickly tapered off to nothing leaving almost a third of the sandwich with little to no meat. The au jus tasted like a standard brown gravy (which I like), but didn't get much "smoked" flavor. More of the horseradish crème would have helped as well.

When I paid $6 for a Miller Lite, waited for 30 minutes to use the bathroom, and got car bombs served in plastic cups, I forgave you because it's football game day.

But on a non-game day, when you serve me fish and chips with runny batter and the tacos consist of a pile of gray meat with some lettuce and tomatoes, that's inexcusable. 

Good for pre- and post-game drinking. Meh for all other occasions (except Thursday 4-6 Happy Hours. $5 Car Bombs. Served in real glasses).

I came to Henry's last week before the Cal v UCLA game. We arrived around 10am and it was mercifully empty. (Well, as empty as the closest bar to Memorial Stadium gets on game day). I'd never been into Henrys before, but i noticed a few things that made the experience quite difficult.

First, there were no tables. I understand not having tables if you're expecting people to be packed in shoulder to shoulder, but when you're selling breakfast in the morning and most of your foods on the menu are fork and knife foods, it doesn't make eating very easy when there are no tables available. Second, the service is spotty at best. You will probably be ignored by the bartender, and you have to open two tabs (one for food and one for the bar) because you cannot order food from the bartenders on game day. 

The morning started with a couple Bloody Marys, which were spicy and actually pretty decent. We opted to hold off until the lunch menu started and ordered a burger, sweet potato fries and chicken wings to split between 3 of us. The chicken wings were a great spice level, but much too messy to eat standing up. The burger, even though it was cooked medium, was extremely dry. Yet the sweet potato fries were hot, crisp and perfectly seasoned. 

Henry's is not my favorite bar by a long shot, but I'll probably always be back before football games, simply because it is the closest thing to the stadium.

I'm surprised by the number of reviews describing a lack of fresh ingredients. I've noted quite the opposite.

I love how they make falafel fresh to order. (Most other restaurants just have pre-made balls of falafel sitting under a heat lamp, and then they smoosh the balls onto bread as needed.) Hot and fresh falafel is a treat. Actually, everything about the falafel wrap is delicious.

Perhaps the safer choices at Julie's are the Mediterranean foods, which seem to be the specialty of the staff I've encountered.
i heard good things about this place. granted, all i ate was a hamburger. but i could have made a better one.

Who wants to be fat?

Not I.

That's why I go for the NON-FAT muffins, $1.75...oh so delicious and warm and crispy! Just the way I like them. And HUGE muffin tops (the best part always)!

I frequently grab one on the way to class, feeling oh so light and chippery. Oh and healthy too!

Good job muffins for living up the cafe name!

The place was severely understaffed. We had to wait forever just to pay! And the food was average at best. 

On the plus side, you get a large quantity of the food, which can be a good and bad thing.
I love the location and the little courtyard you can sit and eat. Just wish the food tasted better and the flatware didn't feel so sticky/oily/dirty.

I don't get all the hype. For breakfast, I went there with a group of friends thinking that it would be superb. The selection was limited. None of us (4 people) were that thrilled with our choices (bagel with egg and tomato and cheese ($3), breakfast burrito, sandwich combination of some sort). Would not go there again...could get much better at McDonald's.
1.5 years later, I tried the Pad Thai ($6). I'll give them this--it was the healthiest tasting Pad Thai I've ever had. Not at all greasy, but semi-bland. It was, however, loaded with chicken! And carrots and sprouts...in a light peanut sauce. Perhaps I made a mistake of ordering it non-spicy. 

Baked Goods at Julie's:

-Healthy muffins (blueberry, bran, cranberry): Definitely healthy-tasting, and I don't mean it in a good way. The consistency could be described as the opposite of "melt-in-the-mouth."
-Brownies: Okay
-Banana bread: Yummy
-Chocolate chip cookies: Great for low-fat cookies. Chewy to the max.

They also need a bigger assortment of baked goods.

The beautiful thing about Julie's is you really have to know what to order. Is that called street smarts when you just know which establishments are catering to certain taste buds? No one establishment can perfect all the cuisines. Yes they are under new management and the new guys are a bit unsettling since I'm used to the other chefs and servers. Give way to the new and don't be closed to the idea of new opportunities.

Clearly - don't come here for the burger and fries or the breakfast, I think that's just a ploy to get more customers but really they get turned off because they don't specialize on this dishes because there is CLEARLY better establishments who cater to those types of cuisine -- activate yourselves.

Julie's, first and foremost, is a Turkish establishment, but I actually liked them for their Thai dishes, and they never fail to deliver these two types of dishes. I always know when to go here when I savor only two types of cravings: 1.) healthy Thai food, so that means not greasy or curry-filled or have to wait for long stir fries 2.) crunchy, savory, meat-filled wraps with shawarma chicken, beef and lamb.

I especially enjoy the sriracha for the Thai food stir-fries, for me go for the Shrimp Me Gorang (where do you ask is the best Pad Thai? Ask yourself.) and the great little ranch mix dressing for any of the meat wraps. Great place to go if you have a meeting with a GSI or peer, or even interviews. Their coffee/drinks is blah, please better places to go for that but the venue is great. I like the air and the placement and the ease of it all.

So yeah, get yourselves acquainted with your surroundings. You'll be surprised. And oh! Check your privilege 'cuz it's ruining "real" reviews.

Walking around telegraph shopping... asked someone if they knew where there was some good breakfast and, she said "Julies Healthy Cafe" well, I was starving so I was like why not.  The setting is pretty nice outdoor sitting area the whole thing itself isn't fancy. I ordered the breakfast burrito and, it was HUGE! and, I was excited I took a bite and, it was good obviously anything would of tasted good at this point I was starrrrving! but then I took more bites and, it lacked salt or hot sauce coming from a spanish culture we love our spicy foods! But besides that it was good. 

I rated this 3 stars because the food wasn't great although I saw other people order sandwiches and, that looked good lol next time I shall get that!

why do people hate on Julie's? you get a lot of food for the amount you pay and to the person who knocked it being "healthy" there are vegetarian options for you to order and you can always tell the ladies to use less oil when your food is being prepared. they don't seem to mind.

Whenever i'm craving it in the am, their breakfast burrito is good. they warm up the tortilla so it's crispy and put black beans, potatoes, eggs and cheese in it. For less than $5, a steal, and I can eat the other half for lunch. 

One time I was there and I asked the owner a question about his baklava, and he hooked me and my friend up with free samples. no complaints here..

I dig the staff that worked here. Cecilia and Marie, two of the cooks, recognized me after not visiting for a couple of weeks. They get orders correctly despite all the insinuating requests. 

Unfortunately, the title doesn't match up with its goal of healthy food very well. There are certainly healthy items, but there's also a ton of stuff you'd find at fast 'ethnic' joints. 

+ Spacious, lots of tables for groups and studying
+ Food is decent, comes out quick
+ Besides the owner, the rest of the staff is awesome
-  Only two outlets, kills laptop users!
-  Their wi-fi waves in and out, fix that shizz!

Final Call:
Friendly staff for the most part. The food is aiiiite. For the study space and the quick food, I'll be back when I'm on the Southside of campus. 

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Munchies:
1. Veggie sandwich with hummus
     -  Tell 'em to mix up the hummus well, I got a few nasty chunks one time
2. Veggie minestrone soup
     + Veggies retain some of their firmness and flavor, good mix
3. Pad Thai, Veggie
     + They don't overdo on the peanuts, lemon's a good touch

I have class in the Anthropology labs right across the street so I thought I'd check this out for lunch.   Ordered the hummus sandwich based on the reviews here.

The pluses and minuses of the experience:
+ alfalfa sprouts, something i havent found elsewhere on a hummus sandwich yet
+price of the sandwich, around $5 for an enormous sandwich that could easily be split with someone

-bread options - only whole wheat and sourdough.  I like my hummus sandwich bread to be kind of pillowy and substantial, and the slices of wheat didn't really hold up
-too many ingredients - mayo, mustard, pickles, cheese, on top of the hummus, plus tons of veggies which makes the sammy like 2 inches thick.  It's just a personal thing, but I like my hummus sandwiches to be kept kind of simple.  The mustard is why I wasn't such a fan of Intermezzo's version - I think it overpowers.
-expensive (bottled, at least) drinks.  BRING YOUR OWN.  However, I do think water is free here, I just didn't see it till after I got my drink.
-messy eating.  i probably used 10 napkins.
-wierd cashier who asked me whether i had just made the $20 bill i handed him to pay for my food?  huh?? 

So, overall, huge and pretty tasty, but too complicated for me.  I much prefer Sufficient Ground's version, with yummy foccaccia and tons of hummus, veggies, and not much else, plus side greens.  Smart Alec's version is also amazing as well.

While studying at Berkeley during the summer a few years ago, I use to enjoy getting the chicken and broccoli dish and sitting outside to study.  The sandwiches are also good and the staff is friendly.  On the weekend, I would also go to Julie's in the morning for breakfast.  I remember one time getting a nonfat muffin and juice for a nice, older homeless guy that use to always sit by the trash can on the corner of Telegraph and wish a good morning.   He seemed less that impressed that the muffin was nonfat but I'm sure he enjoyed it.

I tried the the chicken shawerma there and it tastes so good but the reason i gave it 3 stars was because they put too much lettuce in there u barely taste the meat. So if you ever order it tell them not to put lettuce it ruins the sandwich. but the chicken in there tasted good perfect spices... i haven't tried other things but my brother loves that place he tries different things and always liked it. but for me I'm picky about shawerma sandwiches. If you love shawerma and you happen to be in Anaheim, ca go to Sahara falafel that place is a 5 star. the place isn't that good but the food is amazing and the menu is simple not much on there. every time i go there i have to eat there and tried to find a place like it around here, but there's nothing like Sahara.

Good Stir fry dishes cooked up by friendly ladies who have to put up with campus folks who have their heads in the clouds or up their rears...

Food is quickly made, flavorful, and hot!  I am a regular.

To be honest, I'm judging this place based on only two visits, both of which were not that satisfying. Yes, they call themselves healthy, but their stir frys and large breakfast items really are not that good for you. And if you're looking for salads, Smart Alec's and Intermezzo do a much better job. Sure, portions are large for the money and the food is made fresh after you order it, but the quality is a bit lacking. The wait during the lunch hour is long as well. Two stars for good seating and cheapness, in every sense of the word.

Food: breakfast special with came with eggs, potatoes, and toast. Honestly, I don't know if there was anything really "healthy about the meal". When I go to a place that has "Healthy" in the title of it, I expect a little bit more than an average oily, run down cafe joint. The potatoes were really oily and greasy. The eggs were kinda runny and gross looking. The toast was.....toast. Overall, the meal was NOT impressive and FAR FROM healthy!

Service: none, you order at the counter and you bus yourself. 

Ambiance: Outdoor seating. It was kinda cold and the tables were kinda dirty from just purely collecting dust from being outside. 

Price: Kinda pricey for something that CLAIMS to be healthy AND looks like a run down joint. 

Overall: NOOO...I would NOT come back even though it's super close to school and would be super convenient for me to eat here!

This changed hands and is now Turkish. New owners have reportedly added Turkish items such as cacik, eggplant salad, piyaz, lentil soup, kebabs, Iskender kebap, and borek. Now open 7am to 10pm weekdays, weekend to be determined.
nice try Julie! hahahahahaha

I actually like this place, I definitely don't think it warrants the slew of 1 stars that the rest of the reviewers have been handing out. That being said, I do agree that there are a lot better alternatives around campus for pretty much everything: Breakfast- Cafe Durant; Burgers (chicken included)- Smart Alec's for healthy or I.B Hoagies for greasy death; Thai Basil or Thai House for Thai...and so on.

I come here to get one of two things: The Mee Gorang and the Breakfast Burrito. 

The Burrito is standard and good on the go. Beats anything one can get at the Golden Bear Cafe. Eww 

The Mee Gorang (A stir fry noodle dish) isn't fancy at all, and indeed, Thai Basil is way better for Thai food, but I just have an affinity for the way they do it here. It's so simple and definitely healthier than the greasy alternatives around the corner. Anyways, I get mine spicy with shrimp and I douse it with the juice from lemons (I ask for extra). This, alone, makes me like Julie's but their other stuff isn't as bad as people make them out to be.

I give Julie's five stars because they have--what I believe--is the best Pad Thai anywhere. 

I get it with chicken, and it is the best. From skimming through the previous reviews, some people don't like it, but I think it's great!

So, the Pad Thai is worth a try. 

Also, love the big cookies, and the service is very nice.

One star for location, and one extra star for fast service.

I've only had the breakfast burrito, which was OK at best, but I'd never get it again.  Everything in it was bland, minus the salsa.  The black beans were also super watery--uggh.

I'd recommend the breakfast burritos at that little taco shack in bear's lair.  The best I've had in berkeley by far.

The Grill at Julie's Cafe SUCKS. It's anything but healthy, and far from fresh.  

However, I rate this place 3 stars because Julie's sandwich bar is the perfect lunchtime option for any student. Most people who visit Julie's regularly don't even realize that the sandwich bar is separate from the other menu. Sandwiches are made with fresh whole grain bread, choice of turkey, hummus, or roast beef, tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, lettuce, and cheese. A half a sandwich is only $3.50, and is definitely enough for lunch. DON'T wait in line at the grill, but walk right up to the sandwich counter. 

I've pointed this out to many friends who are regulars, and they never even realized it was there. I've never waited more than 1 minute for my sandwich, even around lunchtime hours. For $3.50, I think its one of the best and easiest lunchtime stops in Berkeley. There is a nice sitting area, and they also offer free Wi Fi. You can usually find a spacious area to sit even during the busy lunchtime hours.

I just bought a cup of coffee and added my cream... the cream is massively curdled and disgusting. Never going back there again. I got the hummus a while back and it was like whale sperm. The health dept. needs to take a look at them and why they don't understand the idea of EXPIRATION DATES!

Normally the greek entrees are A-ok, went in for breakfast -- stay away from their pre-made, soggy breakfast burritos and really weak/nasty coffee. Honestly, I'm so disappointed by Julie's -- their obvious business flaw in that they claim to be healthy but try to operate like a greasy fast-food joint -- I'm likely to never eat there again.

Great Place! Love the new thai food.
Incredible tom yum and som tom! (soup and salad). Too die for!

I've only tried breakfast here, the breakfast burrito and the egg and cheese bagel. Both were flavorless and disappointing. I get that this is a "healthy" cafe, but this is the kind of place that gives "healthy" a bad rap. Salt can go a long way even in small amounts, something this place doesn't seem to understand. The lettuce and tomato on my bagel sandwich were also old. All in all, i would not recommend coming here unless you know something that i don't.
"Their juice restores my faith in humanity."

This place was okay. I came for brunch and I got my food pretty quickly, but from my food I would never have guessed that this place was supposed to be healthy. I'm pretty sure my brunch food was as heavy as every other place..

They are primarily outdoor seating, so the seats are sometimes of questionable cleanliness.

Can I give it a zero?!   New owners, bad (expensive) food.   I was so sorry that the old Julie's menu did not transfer over unmolested....only the two short order cooks remain and they are as sweet as ever.  Other staff?  Not friendly and clueless--bad combo!

Higher prices for bad food...not a good combo.   The meats are tough (and hard to find in the dish).  Veggies not fresh and healthy--not at all.

 Julie's was my stand-by, go-to lunch spot but I won't be going back,

Julie's is a great place to get a cheap, quick bite for breakfast on the way to class or a sandwich at lunch. I also enjoy their stir-fry. I'm not sure its much healthier than anywhere else, but I'll be back sometime when I'm visiting Berkeley.

Came here one day for a breakfast burrito. The service was slow and the burrito wasn't very good. There were too many beans and was very watered down from either the tomatoes or the vegetables. Can't recommend it at all

I am very surprise by the negative reviews.  The staff was so nice, the place was clean, and they have a wide range of diverse food.  The only reason why they get three stars is because the food was literally okay.

The one time I paid a visit to Julie's (see Will R's review below), it was only out of dire need for brunch at 3 in the afternoon. We tried Anne's and Cafe Durant, and somehow, both were closed. It was tragic. Will and I walked in to place our order, and I swear, the women working there looked positively shocked that people were actually ordering food from them. 

As Will mentions, he got the eggs and "sausage" which turned out to be eggs and a chopped up hot dog. I ordered an omelet that consisted simply of eggs and cheese. One would think that this would be nearly impossible to fuck up. But they managed, somehow.

I was just mystified by the whole experience. I dunno, maybe brunch is just not their specialty, but good god, just CALL it "eggs and hot dog" if that's what it is!

I kind of hate this place.  Nevertheless, I eat here occasionally, solely because of its convenient location and frequent lack of a line.  Afterwards, I always think: why did I do that?

Julie's is one of the many food establishments in Berkeley selling you on the idea of a healthier alternative.  Ladies and gentlemen: there are many equally healthy, if not healthier, options nearby that cost less, will provide enough calories to get you through the afternoon, AND actually taste good.  

Julie's sandwiches are made on a homemade wheat bread that convinces you of its healthiness because it taste like air-infused cardboard.  Julie's veggie sandwich includes one slice of cheese and nothing else of any substance.  Want to add another thin slice, or maybe some avocado?  $1 for each, making your sandwich cost more than the gigantic sandwich/salad combinations available only blocks away at Intermezzo, Cafe Milano, or Sufficient Grounds (and two of those establishments also make their own wheat bread!).   

Other items on the menu that have not impressed me: fat free muffins (really, really bad), veggie omelet (bland), side salad (you'd think this would be a key item on a "healthy" cafe's menu)

Passable items: veggie chili (though the rice filler is a little disappointing), low fat chocolate chip cookie (okay, but the quality recently went down and the price went up), breakfast burrito (average).

Can recommend: Banana Bread.  

The staff is always friendly but their coy smiles make me think that they are secretly laughing at me for choosing to blow my lunch money at Julie's.  Basically, there isn't much reason to go here when you consider the other nearby healthy, cheaper, tastier alternatives.

I really wish I could give a half star. Or even a quarter of one. It was that bad. Hands down, the WORST muffin I have EVER had in my ENTIRE LIFE. I hate capitalizing things, because it's as if I'm a twelve-year-old on AIm lol-ing, but I really don't know how to communicate my loud disgust.  I was so, SO sorry that I chose to grab breakfast from this place. I soldiered through a few bites but had to throw the rest away- and I never throw away food. It was that bad.

I went here for breakfast. I ordered the Breakfast Panini. It had a four pieces of breakfast sausage, cheese, tomatoes, peppers, and toasted bread. It was quite disappointing. There was little flavor. The cheese tasted like plastic. The sausages were very greasy. I have to say it was pretty horrible eating this thing they tried to pass off as a breakfast panini. I will have to try other items on their menu for lunch. But for breakfast, AVOID!!

Good white mochas, pretty good sandwiches, decent cost.

They'd suit me better, though, if they'd take ATM.  But that's too much to ask at Berkeley.
2 things on their menu makes me a returning customer  -- Yellow Chicken Curry and Grilled Chicken Sandwiches. Very light and still full of flavor.
The bread took up half the sandwich. Not worth $7. Also took too long to make it. One of the driving reasons I got a Yelp account was because I was so disappointed with this place.

Had the lamb & beef shawarma a few days ago, which was not bad. The meat was a little chewy, but it was filling, which is all that really matters during finals week.

Outlets:
I love looking for outlets at study spots. There are many outlets here and even on the ceiling, I kid you not. I saw some guy plug his laptop cord to one on the ceiling towards the side corner.

Chairs:
There is always a large stack of plastic chairs.

Live Music:
Office hours with instrumental Hey Jude in the background.

Yes, I'm picking out some good things & not just picking on the brownies. Shoutout to Brian if he's reading this.

The Short:
Julie's Healthy Cafe is anything but healthy. I came here for a quick meal in between class, but the food is on the pricier side for a quick eats place and definitely not too fresh. As a matter of fact, I'm writing this review as I make my attempt at their veggie omelet. A quick description should give you a good idea-- vegetables in the omelet were stir-fried, the whole omelet itself is dripping oil, the toast uses stale bread, and the fruit that came with it is definitely not fresh (the apples and cantaloupe were very unfortunate victims).

I hope this review spares whoever thinks about coming to eat here.

Pros:
+ They take American Express.

Cons:
- Ingredients are not very fresh (in my visit, the bread and fruit).
- Indifferent service. Did not apologize for giving me a side of fried potatoes instead of fruit.
- Unsanitary. When correcting my order, they simply scooped my fried potatoes back into their wok and served it to another customer. Unacceptable considering they didn't ask if I had touched it or not (thankfully I didn't, but I feel bad for the next customer who received unfresh fried potatoes).
- Pricey ($5.95 for veggie omelet), especially considering the food was not well done.

Do not eat anything but the veggie sandwich on honey wheat - because everythign else it is just not good. But the divine "salad between bread" of cheese, alfalfa sprouts lettuce, cheese, tomatoes, pickles (extra please) and onions is a pleasant lil'lunch; and there is always an open table.
the food may be healthy, but it tastes like cardboard....ugh!

i doesnt look so healthy when you walk in. in fact, there are a good amount of gnats on the fruit salad on display. but i still chose to eat here. the hummus sandwich was pretty good and the wheat bread was freshly baked. for about 6 bucks, it comes with lettuce, cheese, tomatoes, pickles and onions (but you dont want onions). 

bonus: the thai manager will tell you its never too late for love.

update: it hurt my tummy :(

This place is great!  They make everything to order and their produce/meat is good quality.  This is a good place for simple food that won't make you feel heavy/gross later.


EDIT:  
I just subtracted two stars because the last couple times I went to Julie's the food was not fresh.  In fact-- it was practically spoiled.  I had to throw out my bagel sandwich because the tomato had mold on it.  Super sad.

I really wanted to like this place.  I love the concept of healthy food, but as the other reviewers have noticed-it's SO not the case with them anymore.

The Bad:
The staff there always looks mildly confused and unprepared when I walk in.  Like they don't know how to handle customers.  It's hardly ever busy so you'd think they'd be more on the ball.  Coffee there is way too expensive for what you get.  I also spent a while this morning looking for the right-sized lid.  Finally, I said-I don't think you have lids for this size.  He had to pull some from the back.  YOU SHOULD BE READY for that kinda stuff.

I also got a moldy muffin from there once.  You should ALSO check your food.

The Good:
The low-fat muffins.

In Summary:
Nobody comes there anymore!  If all you have to do is sit around, the LEAST you could do is make sure lids are stocked first thing in the morning (I was there at 10) and your food isn't moldy.

I honestly like Julie's and a few of their more veteran workers. They are Halal for those of you who are Muslim. If your going to eat at Julie's, make sure it's the breakfast burrito with their beef sausage and ask for it inside the burrito, not on the side. It's not exactly healthy, but its worth it.
The food isn't more healthy than nearby alternatives. Sometimes this place is good, sometimes bad, but usually mediocre. Last time I went there, the bread was stale, inedibly stale.

At first, I steered clear of this place.  Any place with the name "healthy" in its title just screams grass smoothies and power bar sandwiches, especially in a place like Berkeley.  But it just so happened that I ventured in one day on a lunch-break (only because I discovered mold on a sandwich I brought from home).  I was impressed.  It wasn't the vegan/vegetarian place I imagined.  They have hamburgers and Asian stir fry cuisines!   I suppose in keeping true to their name, they also have a large salad and soup bar, but being the unhealthy eater that I am, I didn't ordered any.  What I did have was their basil chicken and it was delicious...much better than any Panda Express meals I've had.  Oh and the service was fast too. 

Apparently their breakfast menu is good to, seeing that my co-worker goes there for breakfast every single morning.

I have been going here for about seven years, but with this new management I never want to return.  This is very unfortunate.

Just this Friday they screwed up pretty badly; I ordered a cheeseburger with fries.  Despite being such a simple order, it took them 40 minutes to get my food ready while I sat and watched my friends all eat their own meals.  By the time I received my plate they gave me a pitiful handful of fries and when I got to my burger I saw that the middle of the patty was oozing out blood.  Disgusting.

When I returned to the counter to show them my pathetic excuse for a cheeseburger, I received no refund, no discount, not even an apology.  The owner merely told his staff "make sure to cook the hamburgers all the way through."

If you think this is an isolated incident it's not; my friend told me how the previous weekend he got so fed up with the poor service and attitude from the owner that he chewed him out in front of all present.  The owner's mouth remained SHUT.

DO NOT GO HERE:  Things are different now.

got a munch on me coupon for spicy dog with drink(3.50)
-dog tasted like tasteless chicken dog, lots of stuff on top: chili, tomatos, cheese, onions,....came with shoestring fries too. 

filling but not too tasty.

juliie's also sells thai food, shawarmas, breakfast and ..?

take outs:
-had greasy aftertaste from fries?

I come here for the pastries and coffee. Pastries are great, but healthy pastries are better.

The coffee is fine, not as good as a cup of Peets, but it will do. The pastries are delicious though, never tried the breakfast burrito everyone is saying that sucks below this review.

First of all, let me be clear by saying that I'm not even sure if the place that I tried was really "Julie's Healthy Cafe" or if another company took over the location and have yet to take down the signs and banners.. 

My boyfriend and I were walking down Bancroft when he spotted a large sign with delicious-looking pancakes, a breakfast burrito, and other breakfast treats pictured.  He had repeatedly told me earlier that morning that he was craving pancakes, and to him, spotting that sign seemed like a gift from the pancake gods.  So, of course, we had to stop.  I ordered off of the menu (an omelette with cheese and turkey) and my boyfriend ordered from the banner posted outside of the door (pancakes, who would have guessed?)  WELL, apparently this place doesn't have pancakes! And when my boyfriend gestured toward the banner outside, the man working there had to follow him, looked at the sign questioningly as if it had never been there before (even though I walk down Bancroft EVERYDAY and have seen that sign outside since I moved to Berkeley in August).. Anyway, the man said they didn't have them, and my boyfriend accepted this and simply ordered a breakfast burrito instead.

Now, how could it possibly go from disappointing to terrible?  Well, when my boyfriend got his breakfast burrito, he took a bite, opened it up and inside looked like tiny potatoes and mush.  There were NO eggs inside.  In fact, the only ingredients inside the burrito were tiny potatoes and a gallon of salsa.  Now, I've had my fair share of breakfast burritos, and I've never seen one that looked like his.. and when he said that he didn't like it and didn't want to eat it, I absolutely understood why.

BUT, they did earn one star: I took his burrito to the counter and politely let them know that my boyfriend had thought the breakfast burrito was something else.. I asked if he could get another one, but this time, with easy salsa and extra eggs.  At first they seemed annoyed, and explained to me that they already scramble the potatoes with the eggs (why? I don't know.. but it looks gross).  As I was continuously polite and understanding of their menu, I asked that they put more eggs inside of his.  They agreed and didn't even charge me for the extra burrito. Plus one.

Even with the extra egg, it still looked unappetizing.  We won't be back here again.

Free wifi, and cheap good eats, but only if you order the right things.  You have to go for the hummus sandwich with turkey and cheese, or the double cheeseburger ( low on flavor, but super low on cost).  This place has a really campus convenient location, and pretty good juices too.  I'd say this one is the "best place to yelp from" in berkeley

This place really isn't all that great, except they have baked potatoes which is totally random/delicious, and they have the "regular brownie" amongst all their low fat blueberry muffins and gluten free banana bread. I like that of al the healthy food they have here, all I've ordered are the things that aren't good for you.

Also they have a bathroom that says customers only, but no one's stopping me from peeing there while on shopping missions on Telegraph.

This used to be one of my favorites in Berkeley and I would have given it 4 stars, but it seems like the owners have changed in the last year or so since Ive been here and everything is different. The menu has changed and they added a lot of things. The old things are still there but the recipes have changed. The mee gorang and the pad thai were awful. Both were loaded with carrots (but little else), soggy, and flavorless. it was so bad that I ate less than 1/4 of mine and left. This is an entirely different restaurant from the one it used to be, and the new owners have ruined it. I wont be going back again.
I've only ever had the thai dishes here, but they've always been firmly A-OK. There tend to be lots of flies in the open seating area, which is kind of gross.

It was a particularly hot day in Berkeley, I happened to walk in here to purchase water. It was $1, reasonable. What left me happy was the quick 2 minute conversation with the owner. He was sweet. If I'm in the area, looking for a place to study, I'll definitely hang out here.

This cafe always seems so empty but I decided to go against my better judgment and grab some food because it's the only place really open before/after a certain time.

I wanted a light meal so I figured I would get a chicken salad (SF Soup Company was closed). I order then get my meal and it's LITERALLY a platter of bbq chicken with some pieces of lettuce stuck on. In no way did it taste like a salad because it was smothered in fatty oil and sauce. 

Other than that, the guys working there seemed bored and lonely because they were all smiles when they finally got a customer.

I'm always looking for new, clean places to eat in Berkeley, especially south of campus.  OK, I'd actually rather avoid the area south of campus altogether, but because that's not really a realistic wish, I try to make do.

A couple of weeks ago, I woke up too late to take BART and still make it on time to my office hours, so I drove.  That made me early for office hours, and since I was hungry and had some time to kill, I walked up Bancroft and discovered this cute little short-order restaurant within a semi-open-air off-the-street strip mall that Berkeley has so many of.  These places remind me of Orange County in the '80s, except there are more interesting people in Berkeley than there have ever been in Orange County.

They have a pretty diverse and extensive menu.  I had a veggie wrap, which was good, but it was a little bit bland.  I'm definitely coming back, though.  I want to try some of their Middle Eastern stuff.  And their breakfast dishes.  The prices are a tad high, but the setting is pretty relaxed, and despite the interesting crowd, it wasn't aromatically interesting, which made my time waiting for my food to be prepared that much more pleasant.

So today was my first time at Julie's.  I was given the invite from some new friends attending the Zaytuna Institute.  So the first thing.. is that Julies is super easy to get to and the parking is located below street level with stairs directly up into the place.  We all arrived and it seemed like the entire East Bay Ummah attending UC were all there.. everyone from the masjid showed up to chow down after Jummah salat.

We were worried about getting a table but Alhumduilliah it was easy at people kind of came and went in waves while we were ordering.  Ordering didn't take long.. just yell out your order over the super busy counter and your pretty much done.  A nice thing is each dish seems to have a photo over the order counter... so even if you can't say Shawarma.. you can fall back on I want a number 22.

They have a wide selection of bottled drinks - apple juice, vitawater, water etc and soda as well as a soda fountain.

The wait to pay was a bit much.. like 10 minutes in line.. made it feel like a high school cafeteria- however it allowed for more socialization with all of the many other muslims that happened to bombard Julie's.    They take cash and debit.. so plastic only folks don't feel left out.

I ordered the beef shawarma.. I made sure they went light on the sauce because.. I wasn't sure if I was a mayo based sauce or not and I happen to loathe mayo.  It was a great choice by the way.. I could taste my grilled beef and all of the other flavors blend together in a wonderful taste overload in my mouth.

I would high recommend Julies.. bring everyone even the kids.. since its low key, good prices and excellent food.  I can not wait to try the Hummus and Falafel next time.

Every time I see this place I am reminded of Voltaire's witticism concerning the Holy Roman Empire: "Neither holy... nor Roman... nor an empire." In this case, of course, it may well be that the owner is actually named Julie. But I really, really doubt it.

I ordered "Eggs and Sausage" here for breakfast once. When I received it, and for the agonizing twenty or so minutes that followed, the sausage was in point of fact nothing but a cut-up hot dog. Yes, the purported sausage was a Hot Dog. Not one of those Whole Foods hot dogs, not even a Hebrew National; it was the same unappetizing thing they give you at the horse tracks on dollar day. It was quite clear that on this day I'd put my money on the wrong breakfast place.

I guess the free wifi counts for something, and the sandwich wasn't terrible, but everything else was.  The coffee, the cookie . . . I could have gone to Subway and had everything but the coffee for less.  I was on campus today for a company event and managed to duck away quickly for a sandwich.  I should have just tried the taco stand . . . or falafel in a pita, or anything but Julie's . . . the bathroom is a little scary too, but at least there's a ladder in case you need to escape.  No telling where it leads, but from the smell in there I almost wanted to . . . 

I've NEVER been impressed with any of the food close to campus.  I guess you shouldn't expect a lot - students are often self-centered, cocky, oblivious to those around them, etc . . . and the restaurants probably can't find it in themselves to bring decent fare to these kids.  I don't blame 'em. . . 

Moral of the story?  Pack your lunch, or better yet, search for "Indian" and get as far away from campus in Berkeley as you can.  You'll be pleasantly surprised, I've yet to find bad Indian in Berkeley.

I started coming here with my lunch buddy when our favorite sandwich place a little further down on Bancroft closed about a year ago. We came in looking for a sandwich, but soon enough found the very tasty, made-while-you-wait stirfries. That is what we keep coming back for. I'm worried what it's doing to my health, though. Don't let the name of this place deceive you: the portions are unhealthily large!

I dunno why everyone is harping on this place. We went there with 7 people, got a bunch of dishes which were all really good, naan, rice, and samosas, all for $9 each. Everything was nicely spiced, though my only criticism was that the okra was overcooked and greasy. A lot of people really liked the eggplant so I would suggest that. 

Cheap, super tasty, what's not to like? I think the palak paneer was a little bland as well, but it was better than House of Curry.

I've been coming to Naan N Curry for the past 3 years but just now found the time to review it. 

This place is a common staple of Berkeley, one that prettty much every Berkeley student has had a chance to try. I'm not too big of a fan of Indian food, but this place stands out pretty well for me. You can get a fairly decent meal for around $8, and their dishes are not too spicy at all, which is good for me.

I usually get either the Lamb Tikka Masala or Lamb Biryani. See a trend here? Even though I have been given very bony pieces before, their lamb is very well prepared and the Tikka Masala sauce just makes it that much better. It's more of a do it yourself place, with utensils, napkins, and water jugs all lined up for you to grab yourself, which doesn't hinder the experience at all. It's not the best Indian food I've had, but certainly not the worst.
I ordered the chicken tikka masala which was decent.  Naan was wonderful - hot and fresh.  Beware the bathroom though - this place is not the cleanest!

My dude and I went to this place a while back.  The food is good and affordable, and I really liked the naan.  I will admit that  the chicken curry dish I had was a tad too spicy for my taste. Overall I'd eat here again whenever I visit Berkeley.
It's kind of average as far as indian food, and there are definetly places aroudn cal that are alot better, but it has saved my hangoverness mornings more than a few times, it gets and extra star

Yea, this space was not originally a restaurant. However I do appreciate the low prices, and quality Indian food this place serves. Why do you pay so little? because you will be getting pretty much everything on your own including your glasses and a jug of water from the back. Go here if you would like to not feel totally lazy, yet still eat out.

Naan & daal (lentil curry) for $5? Booyah. It's not the greatest curry I've ever had, but believe it or not Naan & Curry was my first introduction to Indian curry (having grown up with Japanese curry as a staple) -- & yes, I've had Indian curry elsewhere since. I do recognize that it's mid to subpar, but it's cheap & it's fast & I like it.

The daal is my favorite both because it's cheap & because I think it's tasty; the spinach & cheese curry is also pretty good. The garlic naan is worth the extra dollar, trust me.

Grab your own carafe of water from the fridge in the back, & napkins & utensils from the shelf next to it. When you're done eating, be a dear & bus your own table please.

I like this place just cuz I like variety and buffet gives me that option. In terms of Indian food in Berkeley, I'd choose Urban Turban, Karma Kitchen, and Biryani House (for Northern cuisine) over this place.

Their naan is the cheapest I've found in Berkeley ($1) and their chicken tikka masala is creamier than other places. I do like their palak paneer and chicken palak partially because of the tomato in it, but to be honest the frozen palak paneer that you can get at Trader Joe's is much more flavorful.

In terms of buffet, I like the variety but I usually go with chicken tikka masala and tandoori chicken. I do eat the aloo palak but it's not very flavorful and it just tastes like spinach mush.

What's there to say about Naan and Curry that hasn't already been said?

Food is decent, a little pricey but it's definitely nice and hot; if you're craving Indian, this place will definitely set you up in a fix.  Naan comes out fresh and toasty, although sometimes the service is wonky and they don't give it to you until far too late (ie, 3/4 through your curry).  

I've been here before the renovations and after, and I have to say that although it was clean after the repairs, it's pretty clear that the people who work here aren't good at maintaining good hygiene.  This place is quickly becoming as dirty as it used to be.  

Though I haven't seen any rats yet.  *shudder*

The portions here are actually kind of small for what you pay. The prices aren't exorbitant, but it's not cheap, either. Also smells pretty nasty when you walk inside, and it sort of sticks to your clothes. The essence of this place, though - the naan and curry - is great. I got the lamb vindaloo, which is spicy according to the menu. The menu doesn't lie. There was a fire in my mouth after about 4 bites of this stuff. Not that it wasn't delicious, but at one point my tongue was in physical pain. I like masochism sometimes. 

Great words of wisdom on the bathroom walls, too.

The food was actually quite good but the experience sucked. I guess I should expect grime in Berkeley but this was a little ridiculous. Comments:

1. Food was a 4/5 on taste but 1/5 when considering price and serving size
2. Carpet was a 0/5 = FILTHY
3.  Along the wall there is an exposed pipe that drips water into a hole in the floor of the dining area
4.  They had a big sign advertising Malai Koft but when I asked for it they said they didn't have it and immediately ripped the sign down - WTF?
5.  Nasty restrooms

Overall, there is really no reason to eat here because there are nicer places with good service, clean facilities,, accurate menus etc. that actually charge the same or less.

Huge disappointment.  If you are a price-driven college student who has never had seriously authentic indian food, this may fill the bill, as other said reviewers have contributed, due to price and convenience  If, however, your palate has developed beyond fast food and LCD ethnic flavors, you will regret giving this place a chance.   I am not a college student, but rather the parent of one visiting from out of town.  This place is dingy, dirty (don't even look down at the carpet) and badly lit and laid out across a way too vast space that seems like it was something much larger in an earlier life.  I had the cheese and spinach entree, avoiding the buffet which looked suspiciously like a dumping ground for tastelessness.  I swear that the base for the dish was tomatoe soup.  I was appauled.  I can blame myself for thinking that the place must be OK based on the number of students eating in it.  My Frommers guide said that anything on Telegraph is probably alright if its popular with students.  Wrong, wrong, wrong, unless you just want to stuff yourself before partying the night away, in which case, where you ate earlier doesn't matter.

When I see people outside Naan N Curry looking at the posted menu, trying to decide whether to eat there, I feel like pushing them inside - they'll thank me later.  Sure your clothes will smell like cardamom and cloves all day, sure a high fraction of people who eat here have mild intestinal distress.  But the food is just SO GOOD - the paneer tikka masala is widely regarded as the most delicious dish, thanks to the buttery sauce and firm, yet delicate cheese cubes.  Pair with some soft, chewy naan or fluffy rice and I'm in heaven.  The daal, chana masala, and aloo palak are also solid.  I'm currently in love with the bitter melon (sada karela), but I seem to be the only one.   

House of Curries (a block away) is good too, and India Palace on University and Oxford makes better naan, but Naan N Curry is the best overall dining experience.  For a "fancy" dinner, BYOB and ask Mubeem if you need a bottle opener.

I've definitely had better.  The curries were way too saucy and basically come with 2 pieces of meat.  It was okay, but wouldn't go there again if given the choice.

One order of rice is enough to be shared.  Five girls, five huge pies of naan, four orders of rice, five different curries = massive leftovers.  The bum on the street outside was appreciative of it.

i treat myself to naan and curry only once in a while because i am currently watching my weight. 

the chicken masala with garlic naan is sooo good. too bad it's heavy on the butter.

So one day I'm in kind of a hurry. I need something quick to keep me from keeling over with hunger later on. So I pop around the corner, and start jogging up Telegraph looking for something. I spy Naan N Curry. Perfect.

So I pull open the door, saunter in, slightly breathless and scan the menu. And my eye falls on the Naan portion of the menu. Nothing on there for more than $3. Even better.

Turns out that any of the naans are a good choice. The plain naan is of course pretty plain, but fresh and warm always impresses me to no end. So another time I venture out and try the onion naan. Good as well. Perhaps the best bet is either the potato naan, or the meat naan. Either one is sure to satisfy a hungry person for a couple of hours. I mean that, no joke.

As far as any other kind of food goes, I have no idea. I've only ever been in a hurry and wanted something to go quickly, so you're on your own for anything else. But if their naans are any indication of what the rest of their food is like, you can probably bet on a good meal.

Please note, your wait can get pretty long if you decide to go in at about 6:30pm. This place can get busy, so be prepared for a 5 to 15 minute wait if its busy. Worth it just for the convenience.

I met a friend here for dinner. It sounded like pickings were slim along Telegraph Ave, so we decided to eat here. It reminded me a lot of my favorite Indian restaurant in Boston--Punjabi Dhaba. You order your food, then find a place to sit yourself, and you get water for yourself. Low frills, do it yourself place with cheap, decent Indian food.

It is what it is--obviously not a classy eating experience by any means but it's cheap and it's pretty tasty.

I went on a weekday for the lunch buffet.  I'd actually read on Yelp that they have a good buffet for a good price and the chicken makki was better than others.  I didn't check out the buffet before I paid for it.  They didn't have the dish I wanted and when I asked if it would come out, they told me "maybe later".

The food was decent.  The price: $8.99 for the buffet.  My suggestion is that if you're looking for anything in particular, look at the buffet first.  They also serve free chai with the buffet...how can you go wrong with chai???

My first time eating Indian food was here and I liked it. You can get an average plate for $6 or just pay $9 to eat all you want which I think is worth it. I enjoyed the chicken tikka masala with their rice the most. Eating the sauce from it with their bread was good. All the other food was just okay. If it wasn't for those dishes and the dessert, I don't think I'd come. The restaurant has a taqueria feel to it except it's Indian. The only thing I do not like is their dirty, one stall bathroom, which reminds me of the bathrooms at the gas station. Also, parking is a bitch in general around UC Berkeley.

I really like the Naan & Curry's in SF... This one however, 
it's hard to even rate the food as you have a hard time
tasting it through all the SALT that they add - virtually
inedible! Run Away! There are better Indian rest. near
by... Even Pasand (if you can get past the family having
engaged in "importing" Indian female sex workers!)
Always a fun place to go for cheap Indian food right on Telegraph. It's always good eats and they serve free Indian tea in the back.

*DROOLS*  Oh my god I'm wiping saliva off the keyboards as I type up this review.  I went to Naan N Curry off of College first and I think it's  House of Curry now but it's the same thing as Naan N Curry off of Telegraph.  They used to be sister restaurants.  

Anyways, when I come here I usually order the lamb vindaloo and rice.  My sister gets naan and sometimes samosas.  The samosas aren't as good as the lamb samosa I eat at Sargams (so warm, flakey, delicious!)  and I can't even remember if they were good or not.  Eeek.  Unforgettable.  That's not good.  The naan is usally yummy and you can get plain naan or naan with spices and  herbs or even naan with meat.  

My lamb vindaloo is so damn good I'm prepared to drive down to Berkeley for Saturday lunch.  It's pretty spicy so those who can't stand the heat should try something else.  But the potatoes and tender lamb over rice is just to die for.

Yeah, the place is a bit dirty which kinda sucks but I just try to wash my hands or use the restroom someplace else before I enter the restaurant.  The staff at the counter are usually nice too.  I like that you get your own water and tea.  Good stuff!

This place feels like India. I don't know why, but walking into this place, ordering, and then getting your own tableware, just feels very... Indian.

Also, one step in the bathroom, which has several clever jerry-rigged devices, including the hand-soap dispenser, and you know that you're in an authentic restaurant.

The food is decent. I havent' had much Indian food before, so I don't have much to compare it to. 

There's a chicken thing in yellow sauce that is very good.

Three stars, because the jerry rigging in the bathroom took lots of thought.
Reasonably tasty food but definitely on the greasy side. Isn't particularly cheap either. There are better Indian places in the local area.

Should an unsuspecting tourist accidentally happen upon the northern terminus of Telegraph Avenue, he might be terrified by the eccentric street culture, complete with its retina-blasting tie-dyes, battle-axe salesmen, and smoky miasmas of varying chemical nature. Thus gripped by said terror, he might escape into a store.  Any store.  Perhaps even Naan 'N' Curry (N'N'C). 
 
Once inside, he is greeted by a cavernous space reminiscent of the South Park episode when the Persians took over and installed gaudy, faux-gold curtain rods and unnecessarily intense blue carpets.  The room, reasonably clean and well lit by an oversized chandelier, has the feel of a multi-winged hotel lobby: the reservation-desk-cum-cash-register juts into the center of the room, dividing it into a main seating area--where we noticed an impressive number (~30%) of Indian patrons--and a rear area where customers can pick up their plates, utensils, napkins, chai, and water.  One could also, in theory, fill his plate with food from the crusty-looking buffet adjacent to the silverware; we chose to pass.  We were, however, encouraged by the fact that unlike at some other establishments, the staff actually appeared to be working: restocking cups, plates, etc.  And while none of them touched anything on the buffet, we felt confident that we could sample the pickles and sauces housed there without fear of food poisoning.
 
After initially attempting to discuss the menu over the blaring beats of the ambient electronica from the speakers hanging above our table, we gave up, sipped our tasty free chai in silence, and decided to order the usual.  We began with an order of pakora (fried vegetables), which, while mediocre, was an excellent vehicle for the interesting chutneys and spicy pickles from the buffet.  Our main dishes, the aloo ghobi ($6) and chicken tikka masala ($6) were very tasty, though they lacked in spice.  Perhaps the blandness was a good thing, because the naan and mango lassi--our go-to cool-downers--were respectively doughy and tough, and full of icy chunks.
 
While several items were less than stellar, the satisfying flavors of both main dishes lead us to award N'N'C a solid three samosas; its rock-bottom prices warrant one rupee.  With an acceptable samosa-to-rupee ratio (3.0), N'N'C is a fine option for a quick meal, whether you're just hungry at lunch time, or you desperately need to escape from the Tarot-card reader bearing news of your destiny which, you insist to her, you really just don't want to know.

Obviously the people giving this a bad rating haven't seen the Munch On Me deal! 

You can get Chicken Tikka Marsala at a greatly reduced price and the deal lasts unlimited times until middle of December, which is basically the ENTIRE SEMESTER. 

I'm usually not a big fan of Indian food because it's so friggin expensive for not as much food as you'd expect (e.g. House of Curries) but this is a great buy! A good-tasting meal with a decent amount of good-quality chicken for less than 5 dollars. 

The chicken curry seems to have less chicken/protein but you can still get it if you're interested in how it tastes. But in my opinion not as good of a deal as the tikka marsala. 

Great deal and great tasting too! I never tried the buffet and I don't care to.

If you're not gonna get buffet, I would recommend House of Curries. Cheap and yummy. But if you're super hungry, and not all too picky about Indian food, come here!

Not super clean, but hey, it's Berkeley. You gotta clear your own stuff for buffet, but whatever. Tea and water is in the back, with plenty of sugar for your tea. 

I love the naan. SOOOOOO NICE AND CHEWY!
The chicken tikka masala and the roasted chicken thing are it's main redeeming dishes, I think. And the naan. Always the naan. 
There's vegetarian dishes, like lentils and stuff, and it's a hit or miss. 

But ONLY go you see a lotta people buzzing around there, because then the buffet items get continually changed and refilled. Otherwise, everything gets cold and soupy and disgusting, and people only give 1 stars on yelp. So please, save yourself the money and look before you pay.

I had been here before and the naan was great. Yesterday, I asked if there was anything on the menu with eggplant. I ordered what the waiter suggested and waited over twenty minutes for something that looked and tasted like it had been sitting in a pot after going bad. The service was so bad the kid I ordered from forgot to give me the cups to serve the yogurt sauce at the buffet. And when I asked another worker he snapped at me telling me I needed to get the cups from the kid who just helped me. I will never go there again.
I always leave this place with a food coma. Tandoori chicken and chicken tikka masala are delicious each time I come back. Plain, potato, and onion naans are delicious! You have to try each one.

Lacks any hint of flavor.

Move on to next Indian restaurant.

The only thing this place has going for it is its location.

Compared to other Indian restaurants in Berkeley, I give it a 1 out of 10.

Naan n Curry, time for you to move out and welcome in someone new.

Save your $ and go to the Dining Commons instead. 

You'll get better food and better service.
Not the greatest indian food (not bad but its super cheap so want do you expect...) But they have a good buffet price and free chai! You heard me...never ending chai.  Gotta love that.

$8 dinner buffet with everything delicious...this place will always be a really, really good deal. Warm naan, spicy curries, pleasant dal, raita and chutneys galore. Eight dollars. Seriously. Do not miss it. Where else can you get stuffed full of tasty Indian food for that price?

Quantity over quality.

Anytime buffet at 8.99 with endless rounds of naan, various meat dishes, the potatoes and cauliflower curry and endless chai. I had a cold so I was all kinds of ready for spice but was a little disappointed by the meats but the potato and cauliflower, which is definitely the winner of all of the options, was spicy and complex. None of it was outstanding but once again, it's cheap and it's not terrible.

This has to be the worst Indian food I have ever had in my life. They have like two curry bases that they use for all there dishes one tastes very mustardy and the other tastes even worse. The only bright spot is that chaat tea wasn't awful. I think it fits the giant mall lifestyle that exists around the college.

The first time I came here, I had the buffet and thought it was very good.  Then I went to other Indian places around Berkeley and realized that it's not that good after all.

The tandoori chicken is dry, and the lamb had large chunks of fat.  For $9, I'd rather go to the dining commons.

I also came here for lunch.  The naan was good and was a pretty big piece.  However my dish wasn't fantastic.  I think it was some lamb dish, but was mostly sauce with very little meat, and some of it was pieces of bone.

Overall it's decent if you're hungry and have a craving for Indian food, but in my opinion it's not the best.

Naan N Curry is soooooooooooo good!  I've only really tried the Chicken Masala and the Tandoori Chicken but both are amazing.  Granted it's kind of hard to mess up Tandoori so that's not quite as big of a deal.  However, I have had a lot of trouble finding Chicken Masala that is nearly as good as the one here.  Also, they've recently really classed up the place!  Now that I've moved to the city I go to the ones in San Francisco which are just as good.  This place is definitely worth the try!

Naan N Curry on Telegraph is very spacious and close to campus. I only come here when I have a deal. College life = broke life.

Chicken Tikki Masala: Ehh, I've had better. The chunks of chicken are either a hit or miss. I hate when they're dry :(
Vegetable Tikki Masala: Ehh. There's really nothing to say about this. It was acceptable.
Garlic Naan: Wasn't warm. Skimped on the garlic for sure.

Everything was mediocre at best. My food has consistently came out lukewarm too. I don't see myself ever coming here without a coupon. Best thing about this place is probably the free chai in the back!
For good Indian food around the UC Berkeley campus, I definitely recommend Indian Flavors Express on Bancroft.
It's cheap and fast without tasting like fast food.  Don't forget the chai!

I made the mistake of taking a visitor from out of town here as we were nervous about making a concert at Zellerbach on a Friday night and most of the restaurants were packed.  We ordered from the menu, which was probably a bad idea since most of the positive reviews here are from the buffet.

While the service was speedy, the food was so unappealing that we didn't finish any of the dishes, including the usually irresistible chicken tikka masala.  The bengan bharta was a pale green and nearly flavorless puree.   The lamb and bitter mellon was very oily and while it had spice the flavors were indistinct and unpleasant.  Even the naan was cold and tough.

This is by far the worst Indian restaurant I've been to in the Bay Area.

Disappointed by the chicken masala-- too spicy, and not in a good way-- as well as the tasteless naan. Service was meh; waited 20 minutes for our food and got some 'tude when looking for water and utensils. I did however enjoy the impromptu DJ spinning Bollywood beats while we dined.

Cheap, passable Indian takeout. The naan here is actually some of the better naan I've had from a takeout Indian place (low bar) and the Chicken Tikka Masala tastes enough like Indian spices and chicken to be edible.

NNC really deserves a 2.5, but I'll round up since your alternatives in the area are really bad crepes, really bad sandwiches, or really bad pizza.
best indian place ever at this price range. 'nuff said. i am going right back there.
I like this place.  I've been here a couple times and the food has been pretty consistent in the buffet.  I really like their kheer(rice pudding).  I find it to be convenient and delicious!

Really like their chai tea, and their palaak paneer with naan. I don't know about any other dishes they serve, because I keep coming back to that one!

Also, huge portions for a reasonable price. win win!

Why would you come to this place?  There are plenty, PLENTY, of other Indian food places in Berkeley.  The prices are cheap BUT there are a lot of other cheap Indian food places in Berkeley that are worlds better.

The inside of this place is disgusting, it looks unclean.  The food does not taste fresh, it's also somewhat bland (which is the antithesis of Indian food).  They're buffet special is largely unimpressive - they don't change the food out as often as they should, there is very little selection for a buffet, the food tastes old/stale.

The people who work there are friendly.

This place used to be AWESOME !!! Then the owner changed, and now it sucks. Tastes like pure butter, but in a bad way. If you want to try out what it used to be like check out House of Curries on College and Ashby. Try the Bangain Bharta!

If you're on Telegraph and looking for a quick place to eat at, I think this is one of the better places to go. It's pretty packed most of the time, but what place isn't over there? There are better places such as Shalimar, but if you're a student, or just in the area, it's not a bad place to get some grub and it's kind on your wallet. You may want to pull out your tums though, heartburn is basically guaranteed.

I used to love this place about 5 or 6 years ago when I was at Cal, but I swear the food's gotten worse.  I used to always get the Aloo Gobi, Palak Paneer, and Garlic Naan and it was delicious.  I went there last night, and the Aloo Ghobi was much smaller chunks of potato and cauliflower and seemed to be missing the tomatoes entirely.  It was also much more bland than it used to be.  The Garlic Naan was aiight, but nowhere near as moist and garlicky as it used to be.  The only thing that was still as good as ever was the Palak Paneer.  We also got samosas, which were soggy and cold, and my husband ordered Chicken Tikka Masala, which was also pretty bland.  I am super disappointed, because I loved that this place was so cheap i could order a variety of dishes even if it was just me.  Frankly, the Indian food in foil packets at Trader Joe's are just as good, if not better, and a whole lot cheaper.

My very first time here was with ST. It was my very first time eating Indian food--ST introduced it ot me. It was an explosion in my mouth, in a good way of course

I really like the chicken vindaloo, even though it is spicy as heck.
I also like their garlic naan.

I love when Indian restaurant gives you free chai tea.

This place was a four star, until something better came along around the corner.
i love their chicken tikka masala. Regular, garlic, and wheat naan are soo good!

it's not a typical place to have a birthday party, but that's where my friend decided to have birthday dinner last friday. There are about 10 of us and we were set in the back of the room. Despite the fact that we were being pretty loud, the restaurant staffs were very friendly and accommodating. We ordered several dishes and they were all excellent and quick. The portions were generous and we all shared. At the end of the night, we even shared the birthday cake with the staffs for being so nice to us! I recommend this place for quick yummy bites of India.
Food was good especially the Naan and their Chai tea was good too! but I had to give it 3 stars because it took us over 20 minutes to get our food.
Tandoori fish tasted like it was previously frozen.  I think there's better options not too far away.

This place has THE best naan I've ever had... well I've only had the garlic naan since I'm addicted to garlic.  I crave the baingan bharta (sp?) and chicken tikka masala on a daily basis.  

Please note... this ia a Pakistani/Indian restaurant, not a straight up Indian restaurant... so you cannot compare it to a typical Indian restaurant... great but different - my thought as to why everyone reviews this place poorly.

It's all self service, so there's nothing to complain about in that category.  Fast service and its clean and cheap.  It may not be for most people since it is self serve but I'm a rugged type and have no problem with the humble self serve.    

It's a must for me and in my top ten favorite places in the East Bay.  Oh, yeah... free chai tea to boot!

err not sure why people are such fans of this place. maybe i am missing something?  only thing i get here is the chicken marsala and naan...but for $6 i expect more than 3 pieces of chicken.  

but three stars just cuz their garlic and/or potato naan is soooooooooo good and sooooooo fresh! i ate this for a week straight for lunch on the go when i only had 30 minutes to spare.

A lot of people really seem to like this place that are from the Bay Area, and since one of my floor mates is CRAZY about the one in San Francisco near her neighborhood, I decided to try it with her and two of the guys from our floor. The naan is really good, and even though the decoration is somewhat tacky it's fun. The curry, however, was rather bland, and there wasn't too much chicken it. I wouldn't recommend this place for a meal, but if you're hungry for a carbalicious snack, drop in and get a naan, it's only a dollar!

Pros:
-cheap
-quick
-good (as in: greasy)

Cons:
-it's almost like they try to make the place look tacky
-bad (as in: greasy)
-75% chance of the runs by 10pm (50% chance that it's worth the risk)

Good food but nothing special...food not as fresh as Breads of India...also you wait on yourself...good samosas but the sauce containers are sketchy thinking of everyone thats used them and eating with your hands =/

Not one of the cleanest establishments on telegraph...

So we finally managed to go here after a friend of mine said I should try it. And I have to say it wasn't bad. We got: 
Chicken biryani: it was GOOD! 
Chicken Tikka Masala: not so good... very mild and the chicken pieces were kinda hard.
2 Naans: these are really big so we ended up splitting one naan (there were 2 of us) and the second was pretty much untouched. Also, they went crispy pretty quick, overall not too bad.

The place itself is kinda greasy - it bothers me a little but not too much. If you want a really clean place with great service don't go here. 

The portions were small to fair. I didn't mind so much for the biryani because it was tasty. The prices weren't too ridiculous, but I guess they could give us more for the money for sure. 

I will be going back - I liked the food and want to try their other offerings before I make any more judgment =) 

Oh and the free chai is yummy!

I've only been here a few times since I'm not a fan of all-you-can-eat anything unless it's hotpot or sushi - if I want curry I'd rather go to House of Curries, which is a 2-minute walk away. But my male friends looove this place because of the quantity of food they can get for $9. 

They serve rice, naan, tandoori chicken and different types of curry at the buffet, along with veggies and salad. Because it's been sitting there for so long, the rice is either too dry or mushy, and the naan is kind of soggy. At least the chicken and tikka masala are good! Those are my staples whenever I come here. 

The place isn't exactly clean and there are flies flying around, but that's (sadly) common for restaurants in Berkeley. Like I said, the food isn't great, but the $8.99 price tag really draws crowds in. I prefer quality over quantity.

Let me preface this place with the fact that I have had limited exposure to Indian food.

And while this place isn't as clean as the locations in San Francisco, there are some good things.

:) positives
+cheap naan, usually big pieces. I had a piece of naan with meat inside and Tikka Masala sauce for around 5 bucks and was a happy camper
+unlimited chai tea
+cutesy atmosphere
+CHEAP

:( negatives
-fairly rude service
-nasty bathrooms
-not super clean for being a resturaunt

Went here for dinner and opted for the buffet since I was in the mood for Indian and thought I was really hunger.

--

PROS

The student special of $8.99 is good for us college students.

They have a fair selection and decent variety of stuff as part of their buffet--rice, naan, four to five different curries, and some salad bar thing.

Didn't have to wait and good service.

CONS

Okay, there are a lot of places around Berkeley that serve Indian cuisine. Naan N Curry is not too great nor not too bad in my opinion. It's average really. If you're not expecting too much, it's a quick and cheap option. I guess I had bit too high of expectations for their buffet.

Their basmati rice is a bit on the dry side. But I liked how there weren't too many cumen seeds in there. 

The naan is definitely not the best in Berkeley. And I think it's less than desirable. It's not really warm or fresh if you decide to eat the buffet. It's dry and a bit too doughy. There's hardly any butter if any at all, which would've have made up for it's blandness. Also, the majority of the pieces in the batch I had were burnt on the bottom and carcinogens are never good for the body.

The chicken tikka masala was eh. It's okay if you're willing to settle and once again, aren't expecting much. Not really warm, although I admit the flavor wasn't too bad. The chicken is incredibly dry--really really dry.

--

An okay place--there are definitely other places with better Indian cuisine and there are nearby places that have better and higher quality  options for eating buffet.

Before I moved here I remember going to Naan N Curry when I would visit Berkeley.  I would have to agree about the dirty statements, but none the less I still keep coming back for more.  Some dishes are better than others.  I personally like the okra and lamb dish.  If you have never had okra before, I recommend it.  It will change your mind about green vegetables forever.  The chickpea dish is also really good.  And for those of you with the delicate stomachs, make sure you either get take-out or else be home shortly after you eat here.  This is extreme food man!

This restaurant is awesome.  My friend lived in India for 3 years and agrees.  It's a huge, tall store with a kitchen on the side, and a strange loft with no stairs to it.  It's like the restaurant was transported directly from India to Telegraph Avenue.  Be sure to try ordering roti instead of naan, and to drink some of their tea (it's free).  In my opinion, this is the best restaurant on Telegraph north of Dwight.

I really hate to only give this place 3 stars because this is where I fell in love with Indian food. However, after many years and after countless number of Indian restaurants, I can't really get myself to give this place much more than 3 stars. =( The curry isn't unusually great, the naan is only so-so, and the service isn't amazing. Although, if there's one thing I love, it's their tea. You can never go wrong w/ their chai tea. 

That said, thank you Naan for introducing me to the world of potato naans, garlic naans, regular naans, and chicken tikka masala.  =)

Love it! 
I seriously ate here at least once a week the whole time I was in school up there. 

Great food every time and a wonderful place to read a bit while sipping on awesome tea. 

I would have given it 5 stars if it had servers, but I still love the place in spite of my bias towards restaurants without waitresses.

In a word, disappointing.

My boyfriend and I came in during lunch but ordered off the menu instead of getting the buffet. The guy at the desk was rather lukewarm and unwelcoming. 
Apparently, rice is extra. What?!
So we ordered, found the cleanest table we could, and settled in. We had to remind the waiter about the drinks we ordered.

I had the Chicken Tikka Masala, which was ok. My boyfriend ordered something and asked for mild spices ... but mild it was not! And the sauce tasted just like the kind he used to get at Costco.

Ugh. Not coming back again. There's much better Indian food in Berkeley.

My roommate and I have an inside joke regarding this place.

Whenever we feel constipated, we should eat an Naan' n 'curry.
Guarenteed to cleanse your bowels

i usually get the chicken tikka masala here with rice and naan. it's pretty good considering you get all that for around 10 bucks. inside, it's relatively clean, but not spotless. they bring you the food and that's about it. you have to get your own utensils. on the plus side, they have a plastic keg full of hot tea in which you can add your desired amount of sugar. beware, choose a clean cup (some have questionable stains and what not).

I always eat here when I'm back in town.  I think I love it for nostalgic college memories but it really is great, cheap, Indian food.  I'll just go and get an order of naan and Chicken tikka masala.  I never had their buffet.  They also have all you can drink chai.  You just can't beat it for the taste and value.  You get to enjoy the place all night because you smell like it when you leave.

This place is great if you're in a money crunch like most of us. This place isn't the best representation of what Indian/Pakistani really is but if you're in a hurry and are on a budget, then this place will do. Plus it's Halal.

I wasn't really gonna leave a review b/c I give them 3 stars as well and they already have over 300 review which means whether I give them 1 star or 5stars it's not gonna change anything.
