BTW, their $9 buffet is pretty good. I especially enjoy their naan bread. The atmosphere is ok. I'd recommend this place to my friend not b/c it's fantastic or anything, but b/c of its reasonable price and the fact that you can get a variety of foods out of their $9 buffet.

I'm loving this place. I'm a pretty big fan of indian food. I was happy to find some authentic indian cuisine in a chilled atmosphere. The quality of the food is very good and the prices are more than correct.
The service was good and this is the place to be when I am starving (the buffet includes many different dishes).

I've been here several times, but just recently discovered their lunch buffet (there's also a dinner buffet!). It's about 8 bucks for all the curry, soup, naan, rice, and rice pudding you want! There's also free chai! 

I usually hate buffets, so this was a delightful discovery on a Tuesday afternoon.

I'm a little surprised by all the reviews here that rate it the worst food ever, and one star. I mean, this isn't the greatest Indian food in the world (there are a lot of really great Indian places in the South Bay, and Vik's off University is light years beyond) but this isn't a completely untasty dump. It's junky Indian food, and I think if you go with the expectation that it's cheap, fast, and meant to fill you up quickly on a budget, it's pretty good!

My boyfriend and I came here last night. It wasn't our first time, as we've been regular eaters here since our college days, but it was our first time going in a long time, and our first time going together. We ordered two garlic naans, lamb vindaloo, and the dal.

The lamb vindaloo came with lots of chunks of lamb, and it had chunks of potato. The sauce was thick and tasty (though not very spicy). The dal was also very thick and savory, but it wasn't as flavorful as some other dals I've had at other restaurants. The garlic naan seemed to have improved since before, when the naan was a lot flatter and less fluffy. This time it was fluffy and covered in lots of cilantro and garlic. Mmm.

The water isn't the best (it does have a weird taste) but hey, it's free, and it's at a technically hole in the wall fast restaurant, so it's to be expected. Regardless, it was nice to sit down and chow down on the hot, fast food.

What makes this place one of my favorites on Telegraph Avenue is that the food is cheap and tastes so great.  My stomach is made of iron, so the greasy curry and crispy naan don't bother me, even when I enjoy it as a midnight snack.  I like to get the Palak Gosht (sp?) with naan - some type of spinach and lamb curry - because the spinach makes me feel like I'm eating healthy, and the lamb is incredibly tender and juicy.  Each time I order, I'm hoping for at least one perfectly cut bone exposing its fresh savory marrow that I like to save for the very end.  I've loved marrow ever since.

You won't be disappointed if you have the mindset of a starving college student and can disregard the fact that the place looks as questionable as the food they serve.  They've remodeled a couple of times, which basically consisted of rearranging furniture, but the exotic aromas of Indian curry and spices are still there and it's still quite dirty.

I like Naan N Curry! It made me a fan of indian cuisine. It's a great hole in the wall place and self service options... I always get the chick tikki masala with regular naan!! hmmm...   don't you the bathrooms though unless u really need to go..
Everytime I've eatten at this place, I've gotten sick. Don't waste your money, you are just going to throw it all up. You are better off going to Cafe Raj.

I feel bad giving 2 stars, but I find it difficult to give another.

My bf and I came here for the buffet at around 7 and they were out of almost everything already. All there was left was naan, curry vegetables, and tandoori chicken. The tandoori and naan wasn't bad, but the vegetables were covered with so much oil. I'm sure if I came during the day I would have gotten to taste a lot more different items from the buffet, but how can you stop making new food at 7?!

I know there are quite a few Indian buffets that are only 7.99 or even 6.99, so I would most likely not go back to Naan N Curry. Sorries!

It's...ok... This is one of the more popular spots for Indian on Southside, but that's no reason to go to it.  I much prefer House of Curries just up Durant.

Naan N Curry, hmmm.  The quality is so-so, and if you order the dishes, a lot of them are pretty small.  The naan is inconsistent, and can be anywhere from fine to dry and too thin.

The lunch buffet is an ok deal if you really just want to fill up on Indian food.  They have a good number of options out, and it's a buffet, which is exciting.  Still, I'd rather stick to quality elsewhere.

Their potato stuffed naan is the best.  

It is very pricey, but I've enjoyed every meal that I've had there.  Too bad that their dishes do not include more stuff in it, but the flavor is great.

Dirty? Check.
Cheap? Check.
Greasy? Check.
Satisfying? Check.

Ok, so we found a hair in the garlic naan, but we ate around that part anyway.  So the carpet has aged and the chandelier had a "for sale" sign on it, but the atmosphere is still better than what it use to be years ago.  So the chicken masala and aloo ghobi is swimming in grease, but it was delicious and I was prepared for that.  

Why do I keep coming back when Berkeley is a mini-mecca for Indian cuisine?  Maybe the nostalgia brings me back.  Maybe it's the free chai tea.  But I really think it's the obnoxiously huge and delicious fresh naan or the crack-laden masala sauce that I dredge it in.  

Yes, I'm a dirty girl.  I've eaten on the streets of a dirty Vietnamese village where they rinse their dishes in murky water.  So this sticky icky place doesn't scare me, plus I've never gotten sick from it.

Naan N Curry, I will be back for more.

Food: Okay, not bad. Free tea with your meal

Location: convenient

Wait Time: short-ish, if you are getting the buffet, the wait time is pretty much nothing.

Price: cheap for Indian food, filling if you are starving.

Would come here if looking for a decently large place to feed lots of hungry people.
Want great indian curry and naan for a cheap price?  Naan and curry.  The environment isn't anything special, but the food is awesome.  Tons of locals and students in here

Undeniably delicious, unbelievably cheap.  Every time I hear the total, I have to do a quick math in my head because I can't believe how little everything here costs.  I do like this Indian food system of ordering and then getting your own dishes and silverware, which cuts down on waiting for water refills and replacing dropped forks.  The menu features some tandoori items, curries, and briyanis and a few different kinds of naan.  Cut down on the heat with the mango lassi, or just get the free chai.  My favorites here are the chicken tikka masala, bengan bharta, any of the saag dishes, and the okra bindhi.  Unless you want a five-alarm blaze in your mouth, stay away from the vindaloo.  Unfortunately, the tables don't turn over as quickly as the order line progresses, so you might have to be a vulture and seek out a table that's almost done with their meal and hover.  You can usually find a table by the time your order is ready, but cross your fingers and practice your dirty looks for people who are dallying just a bit too long.

UPDATE 7/28/06: I'm downgrading N-n-C to three stars.  The rice and the bengan bharta were not as good as they used to be.  They did add paneer tikka masala to the menu, and that is excellent.

The greasiest Indian food ever... They barely include any meat in the entrees, so go find a place slightly more expensive, and I guarantee that you will have a gentler and happier stomach.  Also, the decor and ambiance is simply tacky.

For a chain, Naan N Curry does a great job! The naan is piping hot and delicious. My favorite dish is the Paneer Tikka Masala - yummy. The price is right, too. You can eat a huge meal for under $10, easily. I usually keep it to about $7.

I came here and tried the Lamb Tikka Masala as a recommendation from my friend. It was actually the first Indian restaurant I've tried in Berkeley and it was a pretty large portion for the pricing. The curry sauce and the rice were good but nothing too amazing.

My Indian friends at home have taken me to some better places, but Naan and Curry is definitely a good place to go if you have a craving for Indian curry!

I'm not giving this place only three stars for the food, in fact the food is pretty darn tasty for the price!  I'm giving this place three stars for the cleanliness of the restaurant.

Last time I was here with a friend, there was a giant hair in his curry.  Also, I got somewhat sick from eating here last time i was there.  

So I guess if you're willing to bypass the fact this place isn't the cleanest place on earth, the food is tasty!

Ok, this was the best cheap on the dollar Indian Food that I've had since the place I can't remember the name to, up in Berkeley. 

I want this place to be across the street from me. I want to be able to stumble over there after a night of drinking and get me some Cheese Naan and some Chicken Curry and curl up in a ball with it.

We got lucky as they had just changed all the pans, and everything was super fresh. My friend and I got the dinner meal for 2. When he gave us the first plate of the stuff we picked out - we thought we were done. WAIT! WHAT! I get my own plate? Oh jesus this is a lot of food. SO be prepared to EAT! You may even wanna just ask for it to go because you are gonna end up taking something home. Really.. A LOT OF FOOD!

But a lot of good spicy comfort food. 

My only wish would be for the Saag Paneer to have more cheese!!! 

Also - they don't serve booze there, but we did spy another couple who came in with their own bottle of wine - so I guess it is allowed? Good to know for next time.
it's pretty much indian fast food, but it's still darn tasty!

I like this place.  When I'm in the Telegraph Ave. neighborhood, usually going to Moe's or Amoeba, I stop in for some Chicken Tikka Masala, Biryani and some naan.  Ordering that will usually feed up to 4 people so you can eat her for about $6 per person, which is a pretty good deal.  Yes you have to get your own silverware and plates and yes the place is a dump, but they did carpet it recently!  I still think it's a good deal for a quick tasty meal.

What the heck happened to this location? I love the Naan n Curry over in San Francisco by Irving, which I love going to with my family (as do a lot of people since it's so packed all the time) but what is up with Berkeley's? 

It was basically empty and so I suppose I should have sensed something there. Yet, perhaps we had just gotten there early. I know I don't usually eat dinner at 6 so I suppose other people are like that too. The menus are the same as are the prices and so I order what I normally would get with my family across the bridge: lamb curry, chicken tikka masala, two naans with meat, and a regular naan. They gave us smaller portions than we were used to. However, it was compensated with more meat in the meat-naans, as in all over the naan and not concentrated in half the naan like on Irving. Plus, the naan wasn't burnt and came out perfect. I guess you win some and you lose some.

I really like their Naan varieties, but the curries range from good to bad. Sometimes you'll get nice and tender meat in your curry, but the next time it will be tough and seem old. I would give it a 3.5.

Note: I've been in an anti-curry mood for a couple months now ever since I saw the results of a multi-curry-poisoning on the sidewalk down in Fremont. We're talking like 6 food poisoned chicken-tika-masala eaters who all blew chunks right at the corner of the street, so I'm a bit traumatized! I've never gotten sick at Naan N Curry, nor have I heard of anyone who has, so I wouldn't worry about repeating what I saw.

First things first:  I have never eaten Indian food before in my life.
With that our of the way, I shall continue.

My friend and I  were walking down Telegraph.  We were pretty hungry, but were tired of the usual options:  pizza or burritos, so this time we ventured on trying Naan N Curry.

It was roughly 2 pm and there were a few tables taken.  The atmosphere was relaxing: the place was a little dark, cool, and smelled delicious.

The place looked OK.  Based on what previous posts have said you'd imagine the place filthy, nasty  and infested with roaches, but it wasn't.  Really!  I mean, it's not fancy- but what do you expect from a place frequented by college students?

We picked up a menu, but couldn't figure out what the place served... and there were no pictures!  So after pretending we knew what we were doing, we set the menu down and casually ordered the $9 buffet special.  Mhmmm - not only were we hungry, but running on low funds as well.

The buffet was all right:  Rice pudding, two meat plates (both chicken), yellow lentil option, garbanzo thingy, potato + spinach, rice,and some cauliflower stuff.  On the side there was a salad bar that consisted of one tray of lettuce, three dressings, and some chillies in vinegar.

I am a carnivore, but I thought the non-meat options were absolutely tasty.  The garbanzos with rice and bread: delicious.  The potatoes with spinach were sooo good!  The potatoes were just perfect- not too hard, but not soft enough for them to disintegrate with the spinach.  The chicken thing (masala?) was good :D but compared to the other stuff, it was OK.

And the rice pudding was OK; nothing special there.

I will definitely go back to that place again.  I understand that the food wasn't really fresh, but compared to other buffets in Berkeley, it was pretty good- just accompany it with a a plate of salad.

Quick and tasty. Those are words that aren't often associated with Indian. For many, Indian food is often and sit down and have your order taken sort of affair. But those seeking a quick kebab can gladly hit up Naan N Curry.

The inside decor is nice enough for a quick and easy place such as this. You can indeed sit and eat, but I prefer to go to this place as a grab and go type of spot. Nice selections of kebabs and standard Indian fare (even tikka masala, though that's more of a British colonial dish, but we won't get into historics in a Yelp review.) Food quality is just OK. Not the best Indian food i've had, but again, good for a quick fix. Don't expect to stuff your face here... unless you guy a gangload of food or whatever.

If you've got a hankering for something quick but different at the same time, it's hard to go wrong with Naan N Curry.

I hung around Berkeley today with some friends, and we ate lunch at Naan N Curry. I wouldn't say this place is a bad restaurant at all, it's just that the food didn't wow me. I had the paneer tikka masala (homemade cheese in a tikka masala sauce) with a keema naan (naan bread stuffed with ground chicken). The food was nice, and filling, but it wasn't anything amazing.

I dunno, I should say that I don't generally care for Indian food. Would I come here again? Yeah, I would, mainly if friends wanted to go. But it wasn't really food I'd crave.
I love this place. You can't beat the spicy chicken curry for the dirt-cheap price. Get the garlic naan too, just throw away the burnt parts.

As an connoisseur of indian food and some who's been raised on it, I try to take the chance to try out the Indian restaurants in the area. Although Berkeley has many great Indian restaurants that are close to campus, this place is absolutely horrible. This place seems to take advantage of its proximity to campus and serves sub-par dishes (and the food is not really authentic, it's more of the McDonald's version of indian food). I've tried to give this place many chances, they do give good quantities of food for a decent price, it is absolutely tasteless.  There's been a few times that I've gotten sick from this place.

The place is run-down, low lighting, and very dirty. I usually like dive places like this but this is as dirty as it gets. If you're looking for cheap food, come here but otherwise if you're willing to spend a few more dollars, I'd skip this and walk down the street to IFE or Zaika.

Naan & Curry used to be a decent spot but recently they have been getting a little too skimpy with their portions. I usually get the Chicken Vindaloo which can be nice and spicy, but last time what I got was about the equivalent to a leg of chicken with lots of bones and maybe a third of a potato. Because of that last experience I do not plan on ever going back to this Naan & Curry.

The food here was just ok. I had chicken karathi, which was FULL of bones. There was barely any meat, just bones, and I ended up taking all the chicken out and eating it vegetarian-style. We got it delivered and they forgot our samosas, and then the guy went to the wrong address to deliver them to us. The prices were cheap, but I'll definitely try somewhere else before I try this place again.

Good: open till late hours. My roommate and I were hungry hippos after a trip to SF, and were delighted to see that this was ACTUALLY open till 10pm (cough cough TAKO SUSHI).

Bad: not /cheap/. I've seen buffets with a much bigger selection for $7.50. 

Ugly: terrible selection of food. Granted we did go half an hour before closing, but we still paid the full price. There was barely anything left to eat, and they didn't bother to refill the platters.  What was worse was that what little there was left tasted bland. I've had better Indian food.

I have to give them credit for having really good chai though. 

Probably won't come back unless I'm desperate for a ton of Indian food.

The food is not greasy and decent. I didn't like their tandoori chicken, but everything else is decent. The kitchen area doesn't seem very clean, nor is the bathrooms, don't venture in that direction, you'll loose your appetite. 
Free unlimited tea servings.

This place is awesome and cheap.  $1.00 for a 3-stack of filling naan bread.  these things are like the size of small pizzas almost.  anyways, my friend and i ended up sharing it AND i was still stuffed (and i'm a guy that likes to eat a lot, too.)  the curry was very tasty and we we got free tea and water.  that water was needed for some of the spicyness, haha.  i had a lamb and lentil curry (yes, it had those %*&#$ bones), while my friend had spinach and cheese veggie curry?!?!  wtf?  anyways, they both rocked.

This place is self-service (kind of like a cafeteria), so you need to get your own water pitcher, plates, utensils, napkins.  i actually prefer this kind of restaurant.  after ordering, you wait at the table and the food is served to you from the "waiter" in the kitchen.  cheap eats + tasty food + laid back indian music + cozy seating = A+ in my book.

I hope i don't get a stomachache like others on this site.  only time will tell...UPDATE:: I didn't!  Now, i gotta try vik's!

this place is bomb as shit! buffet=good. its hot and not cold and it tastes helllllaaaa gooood. as a berkeley student this joint is spot on what i need! it makes me good food. ya! eat naan and curry. not the best place in berkeley but super delicious and cheap and close to campus and their carpet is so pretyy im all about it

Having actually gone to India I was excited to try this place with a friend of mine who went on the trip as well. We walked in and were immediately excited cause it smelled like India. The service was quick and easy, quite pleasant. The food was amazing (we kept it simple and just had rice and lamb curry along with plain naan) I absolutely love this place and get excited every time I go. the bathroom could stand to be updated (though I do enjoy looking at all the graffiti everywhere) but otherwise its India packed into a restaurant.

Bland, buttered down, and not spicy. I've been a few times when I was an Indian food newbie. Nope never have I come back after I ventured out to the likes of Biryani House or Taste of Himalayas. Still better than House of Curries, but that's not saying much.

As most Indian places, though, they do give complimentary tea. Self serve.

Their name is a misnomer: none of their curry dishes are any good.  Heck, every single recipe I've tried at home for chicken tikka masala is better than their rendition.  If I'd just tried their curry, this would be a one star place.  Still, their biryani is intricately complex and quite spicy and the best I've had at any Indian restaurant and that alone makes this a three star restaurant.  Try it!

The Daal Gosht here is the bomb.  The naan is huge and tasty.  The counter help is terrible, but the sweaty hot curry makes up for it.  The food is so spicy, I cry and sweat, my nose runs, it's pretty gross actually BUT I CAN'T PUT DOWN THE CURRY!  The price is right too, very affordable.  Don't go if you want atmosphere, it looks like a cafeteria, again, the food makes up for all of the short falls.  It's a great place to eat when you're walking on Telegraph.
This restaurant has incredible naan bread. The prices are great too :)

I am normally very easy to please, but I really had to think twice to give 2 stars or three stars to this place.  I think I am very generous to give 3 stars since soda machine was broken and one of the Naan we ordered was cold. Chicken vandaloo(?-not sure the spelling) was full of potato and not much chicken in it.  Flavor of the food is OK.  
Since there are many good Indian food in same area, I should have gone to the other restaurant.

I went to Naan and Curry a few years ago and I liked the food and service, so I expected the same when I ate there just this week.  I definitely didn't receive the same quality of food.  In fact, I would say that this place was close to awful, if not for the naan that most Indian eateries can't get wrong anyway.  The rice was bland, the ckicken tasted gross, and the dishes looked really messy.  

On another note, the actual dining area was unclean and rather unsanitary.  Plates were left for a while on the tables and there were food remains dropped on the floor.  I also went into the bathroom just to wash my hands, and I felt even dirtier when I walked out; it smelled and looked awful.  

I give it two stars simply because they offer a free dessert, and a nice woman who worked there offered it once I sat down at the table.
I got the lentils & chicken stew.  Not enough chicken by far --most of it was bones.  Lentils were too salty.  Naan was very good though.  The prices are pretty cheap, so you get what you pay for.

Basically this place went from 2 to 4 stars once it started offereing a buffet lunch/dinner. For 7.99, which is what you'd pay for any curry dish + rice/naan anyways, you get your choice from about 6 different indian dishes, plus naan, rice, and rice pudding. All the vegetable dishes are really good, especially the "mixed vegetables" which consist of thick cut, tender vegies with a flavorful sauce. The palak paneer is also really tasty. The only thing I can complain about is that the service isn't too friendly, but otherwise this is a great budget lunch for when you're really hungry.

With the lovely House of Curries around the corner, why would anyone eat here?

The portions are smaller, sometimes the meat has bones in it, the quality of food is poorer, and the service isn't as great as House of Curries. meh meh meh
The food is on the worse side of ok, but edible (though your body may disagree with you a couple hours later).  The free tea is the best part really.

This place is ok if you really need food. I thought my first experience was just an "off" day but I'm more convinced now that it's just how things are there.

For the amount of food you get it feels a little price heavy (especially for the vegetarian dishes) but that is totally excusable if the food is good. This food is ok, the flavor isn't bad but its pretty greasy and I'm fairly certain they only have one level of spicy (even when less/more is requested) which makes me think the food isn't made to order.

I may eat here again if I'm short on time and really want some curry but chances are I'll go seek out other places in the future.

Disappointing. Somehow our takeout lunch for 2 was $30 which is about what we pay for our Indian meals anywhere since we get 2 dishes, 2 naan, and 2 rice but this place is supposed to be cheap. I don't know what you have to order for it to be cheap. Anyway, I don't mind the price as long as it's good, and this really wasn't. I had a meal at the Naan N Curry in the Sunset in SF recently and it was really good, and I love the one in North Beach, but this one was just mediocre. No, it was a little less than mediocre. In a town with this many good Indian places mediocre food and prices comparable to everywhere else is not going to cut it. For me anyway.
Once, when I was younger and more foolish, I tried out Naan N Curry. It was the only time I've ever left a buffet hungry.

Soggy naan, soggy tandoori chicken, and soggy lentils.  That's what I remember about this location.  Maybe I caught them on a bad day but for what we paid it was more like using your fork to fish your food out of whatever oil/curry broth they had.

Times visited: 1

I've tried this place twice. Its down right awful. I ordered chicken curry and one plain naan. The chicken was 3 very small legs (with bones) barely a half table soon each.. I left most of the naan and 2 chicken pieces. 

The curry was watery, tasteless, seems ketchupy and someone who is Indian descent out to be ashamed serving such nonsense. Even the naan was so so. 


Prediction: Out of business in a year. Once the gullible hungry UB Berkeley students find out how terrible this place is; the word will spread.

Why buy a $7 plate of chicken tikka masala when you can pay about $10 for a buffet. Depending on the time of day you can get naan, rice, lamb curry, chicken curry, chicken tikka masala, tandoori chicken, aloo palak, mixed veggies, rice pudding, and others.  Grab a plate and get some food.

Note: Soda is extra.

When I first go to Naan n curry it's. Awesome I order C T M and a garlic Naan and it's out of the world I love this place and other restaurant name house of curries really really bad Naan n curry rock ...xxxxx

Very reasonable prices, fun atmosphere, delicious chicken tikka masala and garlic naan--which was a huge serving. I enjoyed it. Plus you get all the free tea (with milk) and water you want.
I didn't do the buffet, but it looked like an even better deal-all sorts of delicious Indian food, all you can eat.

I got the buffet this afternoon and will not be returning to Naan N Curry.  The food was lukewarm and not the best curry or Naan I've had by a long shot.  The buffet was very messy and again, cool.  The rice pudding (is this supposed to have been kheer?) had little flavor and was sticky, thick, and massed.  I've never had kheer this way, and I'm not native to any region in that part of the world so I don't know if it's supposed to be thick like that, but again, I've never seen it that way.  The food, in all, was okay.

Yet the worst part of this whole experience was that the proprietor kept bothering my boyfriend and I by talking at us about theft ("the number one cause of business failure").  He seemed to be insinuating that I was stealing from him or his friend's Walgreen's down the street even though I have lived in California for less than two months and had never been to Berkeley before today.  He would not leave us alone so we left.  If you couldn't tell by my tone, I'm still a little incredulous at this man's insistence on presenting his rude insinuations and not letting us enjoy our mediocre food in peace.

I didn't really like Indian food til I tried this stuff. Granted I have not had a of of Indian food experiences (two other places before this) but I was really surprised at how much I liked the food. The dinner buffet is a damn good deal but the buffet could be restocked a bit more often. The staff seems pretty relaxed and easy going and I like the hole in the wallish feel. All in all, I would go again.
I really liked their lamb tikka masala until they changed their recipe for it!  Now it tastes salty instead of tangy and is too watery.
Halal meat is served here. Pretty good cheap and fast Indo-Pakistani food. Gets pretty busy at times. Complimentary chai is good. Not a very clean place, but hey it's Berkeley:)!!!

Naan N Curry is a good place to drop by for a quick lunch.  After a debate tourney, I headed over for something spicy and savory.  Naan N Curry seemed the perfect place.  The curry was a bit of a disappointment; the spices were overwhelming and tasted strange to me.  Perhaps it just did not mesh well with my tastes, but I didn't end up eating much of the curry.

The naan, however, was magical.  Warm, flat bread right out of the oven.  I had onion naan, and it was delicious.  Fluffy and subtly tasting of onions, I ended up buying another.  I felt bad about not finishing the curry, but was def full of naan.  Because the curry didn't taste all that great to me, I have to give the place 3 stars.  The price is awesome, so def go for the naan; get the curry from a different place.

The best indian curries I've ever had. I am so picky about indian food after eating here for years. It is not for the faint of stomach. Indian food is kinda greasy and heavily spiced (as it should be). They have the best naan handsdown. One of my all time favorite restaurants. If you don't like spicy foods your missing out. An employee here once told me "you can tell a lot about a person from what they order". I agree. This is one of those places thats like, if you havent been here, you can't say you don't like indian food, it puts others to shame.

I see that others prefer "House of Curries"...I have one problem with that, their food is spiced for a white palate, in other worlds its NOT authentic, so thanks but no thanks, I'll stick with Naan and Curry.

I recommend whole wheat naan "roti"
and the aloo palak or aloo ghobi (vegie wise)

I had to go over to Berkeley for work one day so my coworker introduced me to Naan N Curry.  She said that she eats here at least once a month because it is just that good.  And it was good.  You could smell the spicey aroma of curry walking down the street.  It's not the best decor in the world and there's not much in the way of service, but you can't beat the low prices for decent Indian food.  The chicken tikka masala really did hit the spot.  Would I go back?  If I was in Berkeley and wanted cheap Indian food, yes.  But there are still so many other good places to try in Berkeley.

Essentially what everyone else on here says, it's hot, cheap, and fills you up nice, they don't skimp on the Naan so they're alright with me.  Don't come here if you're looking for decent Indian food or if you're trying to introduce people to Indian food, Berkeley provides many good options for that.

Maybe my standards were a lot lower in college (ok they were) but it was a disappointment. The food was only ok but definitely not as good as I remember it to be back in my college days. I probably will only go back for sentimental reasons with friends if we are in the area for football games or concerts.

I love coming here. I love their naan and their chai tea. When my friends from SoCal come to visit, Naan N Curry is the place I take them to for lunch. The curries may not be as good as other Indian restaurants with table service, but Naan N Curry offers tasty curry at good prices. Sure, the restaurant is a little dirty, but at least the food is cheap. I love their vindaloo...

PRO:
* inexpensive
* unlimited soda
* convenient location to southside campus

CON:
* you get what you pay for
* chicken masala curry really dropped in taste since when I was last here a few years ago
* naan was too soggy

ADDITIONAL NOTES:
* my Cal alum buddy who treated thought it was actually okay, though it was his first time here
* rhetorical query: are there no really good Indian restaurants near campus or even in downtown Berkeley?
Cheap, quick, tasty, no-frills.  They lose a star because I've never frequented an Indian place where I find bones in my chicken curry as often as I do here.

In the world of Berkeley's Indian food, Naan N Curry is NOT CHEAP. Nor, in fact, is it GOOD. It's AWFUL. I was SO unimpressed. I am baffled why this place is packed so frequently. 

The naan makes it or breaks it for me, and with a name that sports my favorite Indian item I found myself quite unimpressed. This place is better than many, but I have a hunch that something better for the same price lurks nearby, and is waiting to be recognized.

Also, I really hate that they are frequently out of clean silverwear, and the glasses look perpetually handled/dirty. I also found the meat quality to be not that great--everything was edible but nothing was fantastic.

Try Mt. Everest at Shattuck & University instead. $6.99 lunch special weekdays for chicken tikka masala comes with a whole plain naan, soup, salad or potato curry, rice, and a small dessert like rice pudding. Staff is excellent.
The usual. Meat is generally overcooked and sauces over-salted. Not a lot of kick to any of the bland sauces. Asking for "spicy" can sometimes help (sometimes it results in more salt).

I like this place because the food is good and they set up their business in a way where I can chill for as long as I like; Step 1.) approach the register, 2.) order your food (Off the menu or buffet 3.) get your CHAI tea (my favorite) and chill - self service.

I came here on a Friday night, which was my first mistake. The line went out the door. There were no tables to eat at. My friends and I had to stare tables down when they looked like they were finishing up so we could snag a table. The place was clearly understaffed as tables weren't getting cleaned up, and the line never died down.

They seemed to advertise the buffet a lot, but on second glimpse, there was very little vegetarian options. So I opted for an entree from the menu instead. It wasn't terribly expensive, but it wasn't a golden deal either, and I wish the price was cheaper after I ate here.

Sitting down, my friends were at the buffet getting their food while I waited for mine to come around. Our table had 2 numbers on it, which made things very confusing. Water was hard to get, service was impossible to flag down. When we needed utensils and cups, they were nowhere to be seen. We went to the buffet area where they were suppose to be, and there was nothing! No cups, plates, utensils. All gone. and no one to flag down to get more. What were we suppose to do? Eat with our hands?

The actual food was decent. I enjoyed their rice and chaana masala. It filled me up and I had leftovers to take home. No real complaints with the food I ordered.

I think if we came in on a weekday or an off-hour, the experience would've been better. But even so, the service was inexcusable. If you know your place gets crowded on weekend nights, then hire the staff to handle the load. Dirty tables, lack of utensils, cups, and plates, and no service waiters around the entire night is NOT ok.

Also, buffet prices are steep. $9 student price? PUH-LEASE. and kick up the notch on the vegetarian entrees while you're at it.

Yummy yummy yummy. I've eaten a lot of Indian food and am a harsh critic. I like the creamy balance of flavors here. Almost everything I try suits my pallate, which is a rarity. I didn't give it 5 stars due to the total lack of atmosphere. Great prices too.

I came here last night because my friends wanted to and I had a rare coupon deal thingimabob that meant it was free; thank goodness it was free because I wouldn't have spent money on that meal if it was on a Dollar Value Menu!

I shared the Mixed Vegi Tiki Masala, plain naan, and plain rice. They are not kidding when they call the naan and rice "plain". They are kidding, however, when they called the main dish "Mixed Vegi"- it was more like a few pieces of small, not very tasty vegetables, in a huge mass of way too creamy yet completely lacking in flavour bright orange sauce/paste.
And, I even tell my friends that I am particularly fond of orange-coloured food for some strange reason... but this was just too eXtreme. 

The free chai tea was good...? That is the one star.

Go to House of Curries across the street... or Biryani House downtown! Its cheaper and has lots of flavour. Isn't Indian food meant to be flavourful?! I can name 8 better Indian places, off the top of my head, within walking distance of here.

They do have big servings, which would usually be a big plus, but  I didn't even want to take my leftovers home. And, because this is coming from the self-appointed "Queen of Leftovers", that means the meal was pretty much awful.
Hey, its cheap, its fast, and its good. You can't really knock that.
I ordered ala carte - chicken biriani which was spicy enough and mound of rice.  Good for cheap curry in a hurry, not great. Restroom was dirty.

This is not a rant about one time. I was in the area for a week and I had takeout at this place for 2 nights. It was consistently bad.

The chicken curry was not cooked properly and I could taste the turmeric in my mouth.

I know indian food and this was a disgrace. The one good thing is that, its cheap.

After hearing some friends RAVE about the Naan N Curry in SF, my boyfriend and I decided it had to be tried.  We were walking down Telegraph after an afternoon of sifting through Amoeba and Rasputin and ogling the "T-shirt orgy" and we happened to stumble across it. We just looked at each other and I could read his face: "We're goin' in."  

The veggie rice was moist and had a wide variety of vegetables.  The other dish (I can't remember what it was called!) was also really good.  Spicy, but just the right amount.  As far as price goes, this was MORE THAN REASONABLE.  

Minus one star because it was a bit more self-serve than I'd like and the table and my chair felt a little sticky.  Eeew.

I cant believe people are complaining about stuffing their face for 8 dollars. Whats your alternative Mcdonalds? Yes the Naan can be a little dry sometimes but if you hang out for 15 minutes there is a fresh batch that comes out often. The Chicken Tikka Masala, rice and Chai alone are worth 8 bucks. Every other Indian food pace I have tried in the east bay is usually disappointing and ends up costing myself and partner over 20 bucks for a cup of Chicken Tikka and 2 pieces of Naan. Naan and Curry have the right idea. I do agree about the bathroom, but hey its Berkeley, at least they have one.

If you want fast, cheap, and decent Indian food, this is the spot to go.  Whenever I do come here, I get my usual chicken tikka masala with rice and naan.  I absolutely love dipping the fresh baked naan into the masala sauce.  All the dishes are cheap or reasonably priced.  For two people you can spend $12 leaving with a full belly.

This is definitely not a place to bring a date.  It's more of a college crowd since it's only a block or two away from the UC Berkeley campus.  They serve chai tea for free and you have to pick up your own silverware, plates, water, etc.  Once you order your food, it a self service deal.

ordered (4) lamb and chicken kabobs. (Ground chicken or lamb marinated in spices on skewers and cooked in clay oven)   each order was some lettuce,onion,tomato slice and one 3 oz hotdog shaped piece of very spicy,very dried-out, cilantro filled tube of mystery. couldn't identify chicken or lamb or what it was.  $4 a piece for a 3oz single skewer of a dried-out piece of mystery seems a bit overpriced.  i love most all spicy food, be it Indian or Mexicanfood.  hopefully this was just the wrong time on a bad day!

I came here with a friend for dinner last week. The food is good and came out super quickly, which made me happy since I was really hungry. The service is friendly and the prices are pretty awesome. My friend told me it actually used to be even cheaper, but any place that charges $5 for lamb curry is rather excellent in my book. :O

That said, I actually didn't get the lamb curry because I was on a mission to ~*branch out and expand my horizons.*~ I think we collectively ordered the chicken tikka masala (it's the classic default dish :D ) and a spicy lamb dish that I currently can't recall the name of, along with 2 orders of rice and an order of naan aloo (naan with potatoes in em'!). All of that came to around $20. It was a Thursday (or was it a Wednesday? I haven't been sleeping lately, so my memory's pretty messed up :[ ) evening, so it wasn't terribly crowded, and we got to sit for a couple hours while eating and catching up on our respective lives. :]

You can get tea and water in the back for free, and you pick up your own utensils. It's not the cleanest place in the world (e.g. look twice at the cups you pick up for the tea before using them), but for the prices, I will take it! :O They offer a buffet too.
Typical chain restaurant quality food.

This establishment could potentially be a decent Italian place; the so-called "curries" seemed more on the lines of Italian pasta sauces - except less spicy. The "naan" tasted like flat sourdough bread and had that texture that day-old bread gets when you toss it back in the oven for a few. All-in-all, inedible. I usually find a way to eat whatever is put on my plate (quite a feat considering my travels to foreign countries with tastes for strange animals..), but in the case of Naan N Curry, my meal found its way to my trashcan - now that is impressively bad. And yes, it may appear inexpensive, but thats only because the dishes are served w/out rice and naan. I'd say, save your $8.99 for a fully Italian place or a real Indian restaurant, because you wont find completely one or the other here.

One of the lower quality Indian restaurants in the Bay Area.  The Chicken Tikka Kabob was okay but if you're an Indian restaurant and you can't get a Biryani right, then you probably need to switch to another business.  The vegetable biryani was quite embarrassing.
I have been coming here since we moved to Berkeley. I LOVE the Chicken tikka marsala. It's kinda hit or miss though....

come here for the $1 naan and nothing else.  buy curry somewhere better and pick up some naan to go.  if you don't have the time for that, just eat everything...but what really sets this place apart is the naan -- best when it's fresh and warm.

Out of all the Indian places around Berkeley, this place was never top on the list.  You'd be wise to go up on Durant to HOUSE OF CURRIES for better food and better atmosphere...u won't look back. 

The food is okay, sometimes very very salty.  It's a good place for large groups because you can just push tables together.  They play the music a little too loud and it seems not too clean inside sometimes.

HOT... HOT... SPICY HOT! SO hot I can't taste anything else!

Craving for quick and easy Indian food? Here it is! You can't avoid the smell of curry when you walk past the place. I've had their lamb curry, tandoori chicken, and  other vege curry. All of which weren't bad.  I particularly like their Naan. Unfortunately that might be the only thing I can taste. Most dishes are severely spiced to the point where your tongue goes numb.

Naan n' Curry is great when you just want a quick lunch or dinner without a long wait to be seated or to get your food.  You go in and order at the register and then grab your own table and pour yourself a cup of water or Indian chai tea.  The tea is sometimes very watered down, which is a disappointment.  

I usually get the chicken tikki masala or any kind of palak.  Nothing extraordinary but it does hit the spot.  The meat is questionable, though. The naan is good, both plain and garlic.  

Service is a bit lacking.  They aren't rude but they just bring you your food and...that's about it.

The atmosphere of this place really gives a true sense of UC Berkeley's diverse, eccentric style of cuisine. This is truely the place for naan, chicken and lamb curry. Wasn't really impressed at anything thing else but definitely give it a shot! It is probably the best Indian place around campus.

i went here years ago and remember it being ok and edible, maybe slightly good.  well i returned the other day, and it was cheap, which is a plus, but in this situation, you definitely get what you pay for.  we got mattar paneer and it tasted like BLAND MUSTARD.  the sauce was even way more yellow than normal.  wtf.  the naan was flavorless.  it's a pretty dirty, gross place too.  it was literally the worst indian food i've ever had in my entire life.

A week ago, I probably would have given Naan N Curry 2 stars for mediocre curry BUT things have changed. They now have dinner buffet for $8 on the weekends, so suddenly I feel like their food is worth my money.  The buffet wasn't suppose to start until 6:30PM but the staff was kind enough to start it early at 5:30, very cool of them. 

I ate 3 plates worth of food and many pieces of Naan.  I like their Tikka Chicken Masala, Curry chicken, and lentil dish. The dessert tasted like tapioca pudding in noodle form.  I like the texture of their Naan more than other places. For some reason, their curry tasted better during their buffet than when I've eaten here for non-buffet meals. One big con: not spicy enough, not even close to spicy.

far from being the best Indian restaurant in Berkeley

house of curries and flavors of india are a lot better

they do offer all-you-can-ear style but the food isn't too great and it fills you up super quickly

the restaurant is super big and they have wi-fi so i guess you can eat while you study lol
*YUM* veggie dishes! cant get enough! im so glad there are several in SF! Totally satisfying and man, i want some now! samosas! :D
The chika tikka masala was cold and rather bland. I wouldn't recommend it.

I was excited and hopeful for good Indian food when I got here but I was extremely disappointed. The buffet was nearly invisible, we actually didn't even notice it until after we had already ordered off of menus because it is so tucked away in the back. 

The Chana Masaala was good but the chicken in the other dishes was sub-par and rather gross. 

The waiters took a very long time and were unresponsive to requests for water even after several times. We finally had to go to another table and borrow a water pitcher in order to actually get some water.

The place was very dirty; tables and tables left unclean and dishes left scattered about. It was disgusting and disgruntling as a customer to have to eat amidst the remnants of other tables food. 

Overall, I will never go back here. Very frustrated with the experience and upset with service and food quality as well as the overall state of the restaurant.

This place can be pricey, but maybe that's because I've only come here for dinner. I heard that the student lunch buffet is worth it!  I LOVE their curry. Their tikka chicken masala, chicken curry, and lamb biryani had amazing flavor, and their naan was fresh and great quality. Why bother getting rice haha. There's also unlimited chai tea! The cashiers are pretty friendly and patient, and even help make recommendations for first timers. I'd definitely come here again if I was craving Indian food and was around the area.

Sooo delicious! I love the chicken tikka masala and lamb curry. They also have a variety of naan - plain, garlic, paneer, onion. aloo, and keema. The prices are cheap and if you dine in there is free unlimited chai!

A flaming, sh$t-pile runaway train wreck disaster. 

Anyone who enjoys this swill has never tasted even half decent Indian food (or is on someone's payroll).

(-) Service was rude and obnoxious (btw, I NEVER complain about service if the food is good).

(-) Chicken Tikka Masala literally tasted like canned tomato cream soup.

(-) The Vindaloo left my friend with serious nausea and abdominal pain
 
(-) I found a big black hair in my rice. They brought me another rice, but still charged me .

(-) Their beverage selection consisted of like 3 things (not including Flying Horse or even a Taj Mahal).

(+) None. At least I don't ever have to go back.

THE BOTTOM LINE:

(-) I wish I could push this place into a an active volcano.  I'm gagging even thinking about it.

Three stars only because they have both a lunch and dinner buffet. $8.99 for not that great food. But, it fills you up, no food poisoning.  When I went there for lunch last week it included chai, naan, good rice, chicken tikka masala, chicken curry, really spicy daal (boyfriend loved it), baigan bhartha (best dish there), tandoori chicken (too florescent and spicy for my liking), rice pudding, and an extremely unappetizing "salad bar" of wilted iceberg.  The bigger pieces of chicken in the tikka masala were very dry but the sauce was good.  I would go there again when I want to eat a lot but don't have that much time.
EDIT: Dinner buffet is pretty bad, had a weird pasta soup and the chicken curry gave my boyfriend diarrhea.  I guess a dinner buffet is just asking too much!

Evan's Thoughts

Yum yum yum!

This is one of my favorite indian restaurants around.  Great food and you can't beat the $8.99 student buffet.  I've been going here religiously whenever I come to Berkeley, and now that I am a student here I know it will be a place that I frequent.

The naan is heavenly, the curries are delicious, and the chicken is fantastic.

Great for groups, a pair, or just yourself.  If you like Indian food, you've got to go!

This Restaurant is for those who have a big appetite  and a big stomach, if you have a small stomach then you might not want the buffet. This style and look of this restaurant is better then the one in San Francisco. 

The food: The food choices at this location  have less, compared to the one in San Francisco. To be honest I didn't expect there to have a small selection at the buffet. The Naan bread was good, until it dried out and harden, the dishes were good, when I went to the restaurant, the  rice was fresh compared to the San Francisco Restaurant. My only two complaints is the chicken in one dish was a bit dry, and the soda Machine was broken. 

Bottom Line: If you are looking for good all you can eat food at a mid price, I would recommend Naan N Curry.

Let me say this first. Holy shit, unlimited chai tea? So awesome.

This place appears a bit drab, but the high ceilings make it feel less so.
The naan they have is good for the most part, though I did not enjoy the naan stuffed with potatoes as much.

I had the Daal Special (Lentils), Bengun Bharta (eggplant), and the Zeera Saag Palak (spinach). All were pretty decent, though they did come out a bit lukewarm, but I didn't really mind, cause the naan was fresh and hot.

unlimited chai tea? sure, why not?

3.0/5.0

Cheap and delicious. The only thing I miss about the East Bay..Naan & Curry.  :(   The Chai is free and superb...the chicken tikka masala is to die for! All their curries are perfect...far better than the "rubbish" I had in England!  If ever in Frisco or Berkeley...this place is a must. The atmosphere is very old school...mostly male servants and murals of Pakistani movies on the walls. The music can be so loud...all the better. This place is definitely an experience..oh, yeah it's cheap and they feed you plenty. The Naan is made on the spot and comes out hot and fresh...a MUST!

Cheap and yummy indian food! How can you go wrong? On top of it, they serve free chai tea. Indian food is one of my favorites and I always return to Naan N Curry. My favorite, chicken tikki masala, is always creamy and full of deliciousness. Their naan is a little fluffy and never burnt. What else? I guess that's it.

I downgraded this place from 4 to 3 stars after I got an uncooked tandoori chicken.  I think the quality of the food from here has gone down from a few years ago.  Also, don't ask them to make your food mild/medium/spicy, they really don't care and will give you the same food anyway.

I've been to Naan N Curry twice in the past year.

I don't remember much about my first visit to Naan N Curry, but I remember that the food wasn't as good as other Indian food I've had around Berkeley, but the prices were better.

I ate there again today. I got a dish of Mixed Vegetables in curry sauce, rice, and a Mango Lassi.. totaling to less than $9. Again, I would've preferred food from other Indian places I've been too, but the prices here certainly cheaper.

There was just one thing that seemed peculiar: As I was waiting for my Mango Lassi, one of the employees came up to my table and told me that they were out and asked if I'd like to get something else on the menu instead. I replied that I didn't want anything else and that I'd just like my $2 back. I continued eating and kept wondering if they were going to get me my refund. I was almost done eating and the server shows up with a Mango Lassi. I mean, I was glad that I got my Mango Lassi after all, but I was just confused because a few minutes ago he had just said they were out and I would've really liked it along with my meal.

Another reason I gave this restaurant 2 stars is because they could definitely work on keeping the place cleaner.

Naan N Curry has limitless amounts of hot chai and fluffy hot naan bigger than your head perfect for sopping up lots of vegetarian and meat curries. My favorite is the aloo naan ($2 stuffed with spicy potatoes). Their meat curries are generally around $6-8 and while the sauces are good, the meat is usually tough and sparse. I like the vegetarian curries ($4-6) because they have more stuff in them. They also don't skimp on the spice and usually I end the meal with my mouth on fire. I think they've decreased the size of their portions recently... but it's still a relatively cheap and tasty meal.

Gross, but cheap.  There's so much better Indian food, I don't know why anyone would go here other than that it's open an hour later than Namaste and Tandori Kitchen, both of which are just right down the street.  My bf grabbed it after work and brought it home tonight,  and it made us both sick.  Bleecch.

Buy the naan! The potato naan is amazing and only 2 dollars! I mean amazing, like a legitimate meal replacement it's so large and delicious! Their tandoori chicken is EXCELLENT, among the best I've had, but can be a little pricy given the location.

The rest of the stuff isn't so hot. Literally. When I say "extra extra extra extra extra" spicy, and he writes it on the damn pad, the kitchen still manages to bring back something barely detectably spicy. This has happened every single time in like 20 visits. Some dishes also tend to be a little greasy. Mixed vegetable curry is excellent, my friend always gets it and it's consistently great. But yeah, some dishes can be kind of bleh, some can be greasy, the setting isn't exactly posh, the prices could be a little better especially since you're waiting yourself, etc.. I imagine there are better Indian restaurants within walking distance, really. They also play godawful techno music most of the time.

Some of the chicken dishes come have meat with bone-in which was steamed or something along those lines. I've found it to be just terrible, so you might want to ask them to put in boneless chicken instead - the chicken palak is a very tasty dish which comes with this chicken if you don't ask. Their other chicken is quite good, and I really do mean it when I say their tandoori chicken which you buy separate is great. If you see a legitimately homeless person outside ( who isn't a 22 year old with dreadlocks and a hemp sweater who goes back to his apartment later)  buy them some of the fantastic potato naan.

I think 2.5 stars accurately conveys my very conflicted feelings about this place. Don't be scared away by it.

A Berkeley classic like Naan N Curry shouldn't be given such a low star count.  I've come here for years for the freshest naan in miles plus the cheap and delicious curry.  Lately, that hasn't been the case.  The meal portion sizes have shrunk, the curry is watered down and lacking flavor, the meat is disappearing (and at times, absent - last two times I've come in for lamb to no avail) and the prices have gone up.  The naan is still great, you can still get yourself some free chai, and the food might have stepped down to mediocre but is still edible.  The prices aren't yet prohibitive but are getting close.  I'm sad to say, but this is most likely a respectful postmortem on a once beloved and frequented establishment.

Been enjoying Naan N Curry since managing a renovation in the Tenderloin around the corner from their first location. So glad when it opened the Berkeley location and now they've got the $7 dinner buffet! Chicken Tikka Masala and Spinach Lamb with rice are my favorites.

Great non-authentic Indian food which really hits the spot. I've been to the Berkeley and SF locations, and the food is the same standard. It's a good place to eat if you want some mild Indian food that you don't have to think to hard about. I would reccomend the Chicken Tikka Masala or the same dish with Paneer. The Naan is also usually pretty good, and who doesn't like complimentary chai?

I find each Indo-pakastani restaraunt I've Ben to has dishes that are adequate and some that stand out.  The chicken tikka masala here is adequate, standard fare.  The tandoori lamb chops are pretty much my favorite and a steal compared to fancier restaraunts...

When I first arrived as a freshman I often frequented this place as I never had the pleasure of having Indian food back in my hometown. I was ensconced by the intense heat of the Lamb Vindaloo, and enjoyed dipping my naan aloo (potato naan) in it. However after a while I came to notice that heat was all the dish had, plus a pool of grease on top. I couldn't detect any other flavors, something I probably overlooked in my formative time dining here. I usually stuck to the vindaloo because their regular curries lacked any of the characteristic heat I enjoyed. And I do tend to agree with others on here that House of Curries offers better depth of flavor (and a cleaner experience) than Naan and Curry.

I loved going to naan and curry for a quick bite to eat. It really wasn't great quality but it tasted really good and was VERY cheap. I always got the Tikka Masala but asked for only the sauce and no chicken-which was even cheaper, with some naan and it was only about $5. Must try a few times while at Berkeley.

Don't fool yourselves with this place.  It's not "authentic" Indian, nor fine dining.  But it's fast, tasty, and pretty cheap.  For me, that was what I was after.  It was very active on a Friday night at 8:30 pm, but I was able to find a seat.

The marker-on-paper signs all over the place indicated the 7.99 dinner buffet was the way to go, and I did.  I forgot to see what it offered for vegetarians and I paid the price for my oversight by having only 2 options.  Being a buffet, I got both - chana masala and mixed vegetable curry to go with my rice and naan.  The chana masala was a little spicy, but just as it should be.  The veg curry was tasty but not especially memorable.  In retrospect, I maybe should have ordered from the menu.

With rice pudding and a chai to finish up, I was all set and back out on the street.

Dropping some chicken into some tomato soup DOES NOT equal chicken tikka masala! Ewww!

I hadn't been here in years, but I could have sworn it was pretty decent. The menu said something about new management at this location. Maybe this is the reason the food now sucks?

Also the raita almost tasted like pico de gallo water. WTF?!? I'm an idiot in the kitchen and i've made better Indian food than this place.

Today is 12/9/10 and the time is 11:12pm. I just got back from Berkeley, where I ate at Naan N Curry. I had the $10 buffet and I must say it was pretty good. I had rice, chicken, veggies, the sweet-rice-pudding, and of course the wonderful naan. I got pretty full off of 2 plates. We were greeted very kindly when we walked in and all in all, it was a great experience. Oh, and this was my first time there. :)
it's all about house of curries on college ave., naan n' curry is okay but I cant say that I would recommend it.

Not too bad. Place was fairly clean.

Had dinner here, before the dinner crowd packed the place.

Order at the counter, get your own plates/utensils, get your own drinks, get your own napkins, get your own... you get the picture. The only thing they do for you is bring the food out.

The chicken tiki masala was good, but the curry sauce was "watery", would have liked it thicker.

The house salad, was just salad, nothing unusual.

The lamb briyani was good, but not the best that I have had.

The chickpeas were good.

The garlic naan was fresh and hot, good.

I think the total bill came out to around $24.

The price is fine for the quality and quantity you get. Their flavors are strong and solid- not bad at all. Their meals do fill your stomach. A bit of a wait exists in getting in, but not all too long (~15min average) and their service isn't to be praised nor complained about. Their complementary chai tea is quite nice 'n HOT. A noisy-ish place, fine for families with kids. Nothing to complain about overall, but I'm not really impressed either.

Came here once and had a biryani and chicken dish, wasn't thrilled. Came back some time later to compare their CTM with House of Curries' CTM, and I must say, I was impressed to find that Naan 'n' Curry does quite a better job. Color wise, it's not a bright orange, but a healthy golden-yellow. It tastes much better (more flavorful), and the chicken was somewhat moist! The side of rice was also larger compared to HoC. What does this mean? Guaranteed food coma, if you can finish it all.

Okay so the food there is not top notch Indian food so if that's what you're looking for, go somewhere more upscale. This is a fast food indian restaurant with cheap food. It's certainly college food and for that it's good enough for that. They have great paneer naan which many other Indian places do not have and the portions are sufficiently large although they used to be bigger. They have your stereotypical tikka masala that is good and the rice is good in terms of the taste and how much you get. Basically it's not authentic, it's not the best thing you've ever eaten, but it's cheap and it tastes good.
it's not bad if you're having some really bad chicken tikka masala and naan cravings. plus it's cheap! ooooh and i'm a big fan of their lamb fried rice, with all those spices in there....very delish!

From the beginning we received horrible customer service.  The guy at the cash register was too busy staring at his computer to barely even notice that we walked in.  Then we place our order....We wait 15 min.....20 min....25 min....still no food.  So finally we decide to talk to the cash register guy (who is still too busy staring at his computer to even notice that we haven't received our food).  They somehow misplaced our order and wouldn't have even noticed unless we said something.  The place was also empty on the biggest Cal footbal game day of the year (I guess everyone else knew to stay away).  If the place was busy then I could understand them misplacing our order.  They tried to offer us the buffet now, why would we want the buffet after you misplaced our order and barely even apologized.  I mean if you actually showed some form of remorse then it could make the experience a little better....So we asked for our money back and needless to say will not be back.

I've only gotten the buffet here. My workout buddies and I come here when we want large quantities or Indian food.

The place is dark, the carpets are old, and the food is not that amazing. Don't come if you care about how good your Indian food is cooked, come if you want an unending amount of chicken tikka masala or never-ending naan. That's what we do. It's a good place to sit around and chat for hours and hours (I had a club check-in meeting here once and we talked for about 4 hours).

There's CampusCred/Munch on Me deals for this place, but if the food is anything like the buffet, it isn't worth it.

Bring about $8-10 for the buffet, depending on if you're a student, and they take all credit cards. The guy at the cashier will ask if you would like to use cash instead if you pay with a credit card, but you don't have to.

This is where I started my venture with Indian food since the BF won't cook it for me or ask his mom anyways.

The place is kinda dark, the carpets look worn out but we like eating here.  My cousin attended UC Berkeley thus how we discovered this place.  We normally get the chiken tikka masala and the paneer nan.  When she became a vegetarian, we expanded to getting the vegetable biryani and switched to paneer masala instead.  I ended up liking the paneer masala better because it's a lot sweeter and savory than the masala.  I do agree that sometimes if the regular chef is off, the taste is a little bit off.

A bonus is that they have is they have chai.  For westerners like me, I have to add a lot of sugar.  FYI.  You have to get your own plates, utensils, water and cups.  Sometimes the dirty places is the best eats!

Their Malai Kofta & Chicken Tikka Masala sauce tasted sour. The garlic naan was just okay. 
Bad service. I would not eat here again.
not bad for the price.

I can't believe it took me 6 months of living here before I decided to walk into Naan n Curry. My life isn't the same anymore - I'm completely addicted. My boyfriend and I come here at least twice or three times a week. 

Cheap, authentic and so so delicious chicken curry. The tea also rocks. I don't mind getting my own tea and utensils if it means cheaper food than other places - its an overall great deal.

Fantastic food with no pretensions. 
My husband and I had a large dinner for two for about $20. That's about as good as it gets. We started with samosas--they needed sauce, so we dredged them in our excess curry. Problem solved. 
He had lamb masala which had a surprisingly nice heat to it, and I had the chicken cholay. We forgot to order rice, but it turns out the WONDERFUL garlic naan was all we needed. A mango lassi washed everything down nicely and helped combat the spice from his dish. Everything was so tasty and cheap that I didn't mind the self service at all.

While visiting Berkeley, and playing tourist, stopped in here for the $9 all you can eat buffet lunch.  The atmosphere, 1 star.  Cheesey, dirty.  The food, 4 stars, yummy curry dishes with fresh naan.  Not bad for the price...  Then, I went to use their restroom, and made more observations of the establishment after eating my lunch...  I was almost ill, the filth was sickening. The bathroom resembled that of an old run down gas station can.  An employee came out of the unisex restroom, which has the wash sink outside in the dining hall, and washed 1 hand for 1 second,... ewwww!   For the next few hours I was praying I would not be afflicted with some horrible gastrointestinal problems.    Summary, only the really brave folk with iron stomachs should dare eat here...  go elsewhere...

It's good for the price.  You have your option of ordering from their menu or going with buffet. I went with buffet, because lets face it, who wants to make choices with Indian food? I really want to eat all of it.  lol.

My friend had the garlic naan and it was as big as my face and really good.  The Chicken Tikka Masala was good - but it was a little too watery.  It was normal Indian food but it wasn't that spectacular.  It was cheap so I can't really complain.  

If I was a college kid and lived nearby I'd totally go here.  If I wanted a sit down dinner atmosphere where I can enjoy the ambiance?  Wouldn't go here.  lol

Good prices, good value, decent customer service.  I like this place - strong flavors and they don't jip you with the meat.  The rice and bread are really low-priced (make sure to order the garlic-naan).

I love their "shir-chai" (milk-tea).  That's the best thing to have after a big meal.

Dude the garlic naan was KILLER here.  So delicious,

BUT oh my god I looked down at the bottom of this Yelp page and someone mentioned being on the John later in the day...

And I remembered I had the same problem the day I ate here! I think it was the cauliflower & tomato curry. Eat the Naan skip the Curry!

Portions are not very large, prices are okay. Place gets really busy for some reason, but if they drop your food they will not throw it away (rather they place it back on your dish). My Indian friend would often go to Fremont for Indian food so.....

so convenient and close to campus, hangouts, and shops!!!

their briyani is really spicy.... but i like to eat it anyways
food is prepared very fast
i usually get water, chicken briyani, naan, and chicken tikka masala, and raita

Hands down the worst Indian/Pakistani food I have had in the bay area. We had a takeout order for an office lunch and our first impression was the portion size. Now for the good part-- the biryani was okay. Good part ends. The bad now-- the pakoras were dripping in oil and stale. Ditto with the samosas and as a bonus they were stinky too and had to be thrown away in the compost. I thought the eggplant dish was a turmeric dish with no trace of eggplant. Most of the dishes were ordered-- chicken tikka masala, paneer tikka masala had generous doses of turmeric too. The pizza base aka naans were unappetizing. The (malnourished) tandoori fish was chewy and not good at all. The curries were all bland and the ones for the paneer and chicken were so similar that our pure vegetarian colleague had his first taste of chicken.
We ordered from here just looking at the reputation of it's namesake in San Francisco -- should have looked at Yelp reviews before ordering. Never again!

Every time I go to Naan'n'Curry I get the lamb vindaloo with rice. For a long time it was really awesome, but recently, the lamb has been mostly bone, there are clumps of spices in the sauce, the potatoes are funky, and while the menu claims that there are tomatoes in it, there are never any tomatoes anymore.

The Naan'n'Curry on College is better. The name has changed to House of Curries, or somesuch. It is like Telegraph Naan'n'Curry, but without teh suck.
The food is a bit on the oily side, but they don't skimp on the spices.  Prices are very cheap.  I prefer House of Curry over on Shattuck.

The buffet is worth the price. The food is okay. There was an array of dishes to choose from however don't think I would patron again... the only dish that I thought was pretty good but a tad bit salty was the Tandoori Chicken.

CHEAP and yummy (think fast food indian dining).  I think NNC is known for it's Pakistani food and although I don't know Pakistani food really well...ok at all, I think the people got it goin' on.  The Naan, and curries are bombass...fancy that, it's their name!  Don't eat too fast though.  I always eat so goddamn fast when I go there and then my stomach aches for the rest of the evening.
We needed to get a piece of naan to hopefully satisfy our super picky kid, and were in and out in literally 30 seconds.  Only $1 for a giant piece of naan, too.  Awesome!

what i ordered... buffet

...not a lot of variety at this buffet, it was just like a small chinese restaurant buffet. i went for it 'cause i can't make up my mind on what i want to eat and am so hungry, plus i don't want to make a mistake of ordering a nasty dish(s) just like that 'other' indian restaurant at this town.

the food were ok, nothing special if not they were quite bland. all the curry dishes seem's to be mild in spices and not just chili, reflecting the tastebuds of the majority... meaning the unrefined taste of the young and broke that were in abundance at the area. even the tandoori chicken, though colorful was tasteless.

ambiance... ok
service... bad (pile of plates i used weren't taken out during the course of my stay)
cost... $+

The staff is very nice, the rice is A-OK and the Naan was too... but the star of the dish... The Chicken Curry was under cooked and under-seasoned. If you have Curry in your name your Curry better damn well measure up... unfortunately it fell short. The place is huge and the buffet is very affordable!  The decor lacks taste for the potential of the space. With Indian food trends on the up and up and a TELEGRAPH location that size They could be making millions!

it's cheap and it's good...not quality though, and not amazing good cheap indian food like shalimar.  on a humid day, you can smell naan n curry from several blocks away, i guess i always end up there after following my nose.  when i lived in berkeley, i'd sometimes by the curries to go and eat them with my homemade rice at home, and it ended up considerably cheaper than cooking everything for one person.

I've been around the block as far as Indian food is concerned and the thing I love about is that it's almost consistently delicious because of the abundance of spices that are typical of the food. 

This place had to have served the worst Indian food I've had in years. It was BLAND. How do you make bland Indian food? Well, come here and you'll find out. I could only surmise that they tamed down regular Indian food for the taste-challenged Anglophiles that possibly typically frequent this restaurant. 

And, the thing that sucks? It's not even THAT cheap for a college town. I'd say that 80% of the Indian places we visit are the same price or cheaper in Fremont and San Jose. The plates are small (and tasteless, may I remind you) and they were out of forks and then bowls when we visited. 

If you care to know, I'll even describe the food for you: the naan was flat and dense ($1), the chicken tikka masala tasted like alfredo sauce and had 1/8 breast of chicken ($6), the chicken biryani was practically all rice with very small amount of vegetables and even less chicken ($8), and the chicken seekh kebab was dry and... you guessed it.... bland ($2 each). Overall, I feel ripped off and I will most definitely not waste my time in delicious-food-rich Telegraph Ave for this place.

i went here by myself the other day and ordered a pretty sizable amount of food for a small girl. i consider myself an indian food connoisseur and i was pleased. the food is on the cheaper side compared to a lot of other places i've been to. i was kind of surprised to find chilis in my sag aloo, but i guess i should have said mild if i wanted it. you have to fetch your own stuff, but i guess that's what brings down the price.

delicious paneer tikka masala for about $10. its kind of annoying to buy everything separately (the naan, rice, etc). i like indian places that come with a plate so you can try a few main dishes and have a side of rice and naan. nevertheless, the garlic naan is amazing.

Watered down chicken tikka masala and burnt naan is not my thing... 

but nothing beats free CHAI!

I think Naan n Curry has changed its look every time I've been there.  Now it looks all purpley, but I'm glad they changed out the tables/chairs.  The food is pretty similar to House of Curries but this place is bigger and it has a busier feel to it.  It's fast and cheap Indian food, so you really can't ask for too much.

the guy at the front taking your order is so much nicer than the mean guy at the irving location.  same good food, especially the chicken tikka masala and the potato and cauliflower.  beware of the massive amounts of oil!  i took my leftover in a takeout box and all the oils gushed out.

If you want any kind of Indian food, come here. It's not great. 

The Chicken Tikka Masala could be better, but it's a good place to go if you're in a hurry and you dont care about the quality of food. It's also good if you're on a budget. 

I recommend taking the food to go. This place is not very sanitary.

I miss this place like crazy.  I used to go here all the time when I was in school. Now that I'm home, I crave it all the time.  :[  The naan is still the best that I've had yet, although the guy who used to make it would stalker stare at me and my friends.  The vindaloo is very spicy and yummy, and the mango lassi is great.  The price is great too.  Indian food is usually expensive and small portioned, but this place is a good buy for the money.  I love it!

Came here last week with a friend and it definitely has quality and quantity. Not to mention it's cheap!! Ordered the chicken tikka masala with an onion naan and it was divine (great quality!). I had leftovers (great quantity/portions) and my whole meal was about 7-8$. The naan was pretty big and I'm sure the regular and garlic were equally good!

I would definitely come back :)
Great food, and cheap. Love the chai tea.

I go here whenever I just want a quick snack for cheap and I always order the same thing: tikka masala chicken, rice and naan. MMmmmmmmm. 

I also make sure to get that delicious tea they have... 

Naan n Curry makes me happy.

I honestly only gave them a fourth star because I truly am a fan. Naan N Curry has some bomb ass naan. I especially like the green onion naan, with an order of tikka masala chicken and an order of samosas. Though, it isn't the best curries, or the best Indian food all around, it is good still. I love coming here when I want a good meal and save some dollars at the same time. Naan N Curry is good in my book.

What a fun place to eat!  Great bargain for the all day buffet at $8.99. This is not a elegant place but it satisfied my hungry crowd for a great price.  I appreciated the value.

The food was tasty and surprisingly for buffet food.  There were about 6-7 dishes to choose from plus the rice,  My highlight was the lamb curry, and spicy mixed vegie curry.

The gentleman who ran the cash establishment was SUPER funny and nice.  Found out that he has done some acting here and there.  I'd just go back there to hang out with him!

If  you want a indian meal that's authentic come here... because you'll get the runs as if you were getting a meal from a street cart from the streets of Delhi.

It's sad. Very sad. I like their curries. But when I eat here I flip a coin to see whether I'll be having the hershey squirts. 

I hate to talk bad about this place since I've heard such rave reviews about the SF N&C. The food is pretty decent too. I'm not even a light-weight when it comes to spicy food. Alas, my bunghole says no even though my appetite says yes. 

The meat is pretty low grade too. And I hate how you have to pay extra for rice / naan.

I'm a real big fan of the all you can eat buffet, even though it went up in price 1 dollar to 8.99$. It's usually quite satisfying and good for a group of people. Sure, the quality goes down because it's a buffet, but there's a lot of leeway in an all you can eat situation. My indian friends say their ala carte (and the buffet for that matter) isn't very good, but I'm not going here for super fine Indian cuisine. I'm going because I'm hungry.

I've been here about three times...and each time it gets a little worse.  I honestly never come here because I want to...there's usually a group dinner or it's someone's birthday.  It's not horrible and it's not amazing. I guess you get what you pay for. Mediocre Indian food.  

BTW, my three friends got the runs last night. So I wouldn't suggest this place if you have shit to do.  No pun intended.
It was delicious!!!! i love the food
