This restaurant pains me because deep in my heart exists a special place for Indian food. As I find more Indian restaurants my body, mind, and soul strengthen. Unfortunately, Naan N Curry makes me want to run far far away. I would have written the word "far" a hundred times if it wasn't that obnoxious.

All of the conventional Indian dishes make frequent cameos in the 8.99 buffet that the restaurant posts on the window facing Telegraph Avenue. Poorly cooked Chicken Tikka Masala says a sad and faint hello to customers in its metal home, with Saag Paneer shriveling up in the corner of the buffet table crying, and bland too crispy naan peaks out from its years in solitude begging to be accepted. 

For providing a below average 8.99 Indian buffet Naan N Curry does evade a one star rating, but not by much. Note that ordering A La Carte will give the customer a bit more flavorful dishes, but emphasis on "a bit". At least they provide complimentary tea, or the end of the world would come a lot sooner.

The only time I would ever recommend going here is if you are a huge group of uninformed Berkeley freshmen that need a massive number of tables. Please, if you love Indian food keep your eyes down when walking by and try somewhere else.

i can't believe that not only is this place pretty consistently 
packed with people...
but that people actually go here to eat more than once.
there are so many   super delicious restaurants in the area- it's not even like one would need to settle 
The food was gross
the service was bad
I can't think of one good thing to say

This place is awesome, I had my first indian food here and have been a big fan ever since..

I personally have no problem with the dirtiness of this joint, I never had any problems after dining there. I think that's what authentic india is like.

The best part is that it's open everyday, Christmas/thanksgiving included. This used to be my home away from home during those holidays when other restaurants aint open.

Lamb Gosht with naan!

N & C in Berkeley , Telegraph Ave, larger location than the Concord store. Inside decorated in bright yellow, red colors with 20 foot drapes hanging off the wall.
Chicken Masala, curry, all items are fantastic !

The lamb vindaloo is tasty and a great price...

...that is until you get Delhi Belly about an hour later.

But I keep coming back.  I like playing Russian Roulette with my GI tract.

Naan N Curry took my flower.  As the first Indian food I'd ever had, I felt that it was amazing.  In retrospect, after sampling other restaurants and what I've managed to make on my own, the food is definitely different.  I would recommend trying the samosas.  Note: Samosas are never listed on the menu.  You just have to know to ask for them at the cashier when you place your order.  As a cheap eating place for starving college kids, Naan N Curry serves its purpose.    Recommend: Samosas, chicken tikka masala, Aloo naan  Negatives: Dirty silverware, always very loud   Positives: Sexy Bollywood anthems blaring in the background, personal atmosphere, CHEAP, relatively good food, great for groups

Excellent, food is FAST. 

I absolutely love Indian cuisine, you smell horrible afterward but this is the place to be if you are a tourist or Berkeley student/resident. 

As far as food is concerned, I think it is on par with many Indian restaurants, but I think it's location on Telegraph, and the overall ambiance of the town gives it a one up on all the other places. The prices are very good as well, perfect for starving college kids. Cheap, fast, simple, +10.

so good, so cheap... 

recommend: chicken tikka masala, palak gosht, and plain naan... and don't forget the all you can drink chai. 

the chai has that unmistakable, diluted cafeteria quality that makes me miss my moscow school days.. ok, we didn't have CHAI, but we had black tea that was a lot like it!

Okay, this is probably going to be too lenient of a review, but, hey, they've got tons of negative reviews already so, why not something positive? First, their Naan is incredible. I would much prefer their Naan than that of House of Curries or Biryani. Second, they're pretty good about replacing your food if there's something wrong with it.. which has somewhat happened on a regular basis.Third, their paneer tika masala is marvelous, although, I have to confess, House of Curries has better Paneer tika masala, I mean.. at least it doesn't have dirt in it.  I think the place just needs a bit of a clean up to revamp this shaggy looking eat out place. Other than that, this place has fed a lot of hungry students so, it deserves at least some minimal props for that.

Yay! My favorite Indian restaurant in Berkeley. I have been to house of curries as well, but it was horrible compared to naan n curry. The naan is sooooo delicious and soft and fluffy here, I want to go get some now!! The chicken tikka masala is delicious! The buffet here is also very well worth it, for 8.99 all you can eat!! ^.^~

inconsitent taste, crowded, but very cheap prices if you're into quantity over quality.
 
the place looks like crap too, very very ugly and stale.

there are a lot of good indian restaurants around for the same price though, and when i say never, i mean never.  i will never be back here

"Good rice, good curry, good Ghandi, let's hurry!"

peace.

I simply don't understand why people like this place.
Living in the bay, incredible tasting Indian food is around every corner.

Perhaps I'm being a bit harsh being Indian and exposed to it my whole life... nothing beats momma's food.

This place is disgusting. The sauces are pretty much the same for everything, and they overload peppercorns onto every dish. That's the only thing that adds flavor to the BLAND food. I feel jipped out of my money everytime for small portions.

The naan is good.. I don't see how you can really mess up on it that much.

I'd rather pay less, get more quantity.. and better tasting food while supporting local mom and pop restaurants. 


Please don't settle for mediocre food... blech!!!

Make buddies with the counter crew, people. This is easy. You smile and say, "Hey, what's with the chandeliers?" Or the soccer balls. Or whatever it is they're selling that week on the side. 

They will smile and not tell you what's up with that. But then you will order chicken tikka masala, and get your free tea, and some naan, and you will dine happy. 

I don't know what people are talking about with the smell. It smells like delicious, is what it smells like. I love this place, and it's absurdly cheap for what you get. I always spend eight bucks and I'm full for the day.

The owner or manager is racist against asians. Told me asians have one eye for dollar signs and one eye for cents. I mean seriously, what the hell is this guys problem. Dude can join the KKK

Don't patron them.

This is my absolute favorite Indian food restaurant. Sure, it's not fancy with any thrills but does serve quality food at a quality price. My favorite is the boneless chicken vindaloo but you can never go wrong at naan n curry.

I loved this place as an undergrad.  But that's cause I had just left my bubble and entered what I thought was culinary freedom.  Now after my days of walking 7 miles uphill to school, both ways, I have seen the light.  Curry House has better food nearby even thought it doesn't offer buffet and Punjabi By Nature may be further but it's buffet is cheaper and their food is so good that I think that if there is a new version of the Bible that comes out, there will be an addendum to the Gospels glorifying its greatness.

I spent years purposely avoiding Indian restaurants. After eating here, I have no idea why I deprived myself of this extremely awesome food.
The first thing I noticed when I walked in (aside from the unwashed hippies and stoners) was the decor. It had the standard Berkeley-issue bulletin board by the entrance, but what really caught my attention were the paintings on the walls.
I immediately started having flashbacks to a period in my life that was heavilly influenced by a Indian man. I would spend countless hours looking at him and his cohorts, and when he wasn't around I couldn't concentrate on anything without being inturrupted by thoughts of him and his battle-cry. He was relentless. He was very skilled. He had a very good reason for doing what he did. After all, his family's well-being was at stake. Despite his good intentions, I had my own agenda. I had money on the line, and I wasn't going to back down and risk losing my hard-earned cash. My technique was virtually flawless. I went through everyone else with relative ease, tossing my oppenents aside like candy wrappers caught in an updraft.
It ended in India. Every single time. His palace was luxurious. The main area in his palace had high ceilings adorned in gold trim with 4 elephants on either side. He was obviously a man of great importance, yet his attire was very basic. He wore a few pieces of jewelery and what could easily be described as a loincloth. I brought out my best stuff when I saw him. I figured if I was persistant enough, he'd eventually slip up and I'd have the opening I needed to defeat him. I never got my chance, as he was very careful not to slip up. No matter what I did, he had a way to counter it. I went in for an attack. . . then he was gone. At that very moment, I heard the all too familiar yell coming from behind me: "Yoga Fire! Yoga Fire!" I couldn't take it anymore. I was englufed in flames. He was on the other side of the room, and yet he still managed to land a seemingly endless barrage of blows.
My journey ended in India. It always ended in India. I will never forget him. He was fearless. He was detemined. He was Dhalsim.

Oh yeah, the food is pretty good.

This place was horrible and I will NOT be coming here again.  
The place is huge, lots of seating, looks small from the outside and you have to park on the street. 

I came here with my boyfriend because we are always looking for Indian/Pakistani restaurants to go to, but this place was a regret. The food was so bad, that we took 3 bites and left. That was also $17 down the drain which made me mad. 

We got there and ordered; so far so good. 
We grabbed water and sat at a table, and before we could push our chairs in, a guys brought us our food. We both looked at each other like "hmm that was really quick..." 

So we tried our chicken tikka masala with our naan and plain rice, and the taste was terrible. There was absolutely NO flavor, the sauce was lukewarm and tasted like tomato soup. It was disgusting. Not to mention, the chicken pieces are tiny and they give you a very little amount. 
This is definitely cheap, tasteless college food.

At first, I was kind of apprehensive about trying Indian food so I didn't really enjoy myself when I first ate at Naan N Curry. Then I tried it again at the SF location on Van Ness and for some reason it tasted way better to me. Idk why? Everyone in SF thinks Naan N Curry is the best Indian food in the city but I think it's alright. I've had better.

You mean Naan N Dirty?!?! 

Okay this place is rather... dirty, yet the food is still pretty good! The buffet is a great deal. Sometimes the buffet food is a little ...crunchy because it's been sitting out for a while. It's also fairly limited in selection, but that's okay. This place is a favorite amongst my friends for cheap, scuzzy, face stuffing, Indian food.

Next time you go there, check out their amazing paint job in the bathroom! They painted over the light switch, photo frame, door handle... :D Also, if it's your first time going there's a slight chance your stomach won't fully agree with the food after you eat, but give it a couple more times and you'll be fine!
Food isnt fresh. Not recommended to try their BUFFET. Maybe ala carte would taste nicer. But I will not be stepping into this place anymore. Nothing positive to write.

I was extremely unimpressed by the lunch buffet at the Berkeley Naan and Curry.  The food was somewhat bland, the naan wasn't fresh.  Nothing was remotely spicy.

I've had a number of good experiences at Naan N Curry in San Francisco, but the Berkeley location was just sub-par.

The 'Sizzler' version of Indian food. You get your own plates, silverware, water (none of which were particularly clean),etc after placing your order at the counter.  After an hour and only eight tables occupied, none of the dirty tables had been cleared. The naan was dry and brittle. The Choley Chicken tasted pretty good but there were literally 5 small chunks of chicken causing me to regret paying $2 extra for boneless meat. Perhaps I'd enjoy this place more if I were chemically altered.

If you're unphased by rude service and have no food allergies, by all means, eat here! 

I've been coming to Naan N Curry since I was in high school (8+ years), because it is dirt cheap and fairly fresh and delicious.

But, the other day after finishing up a yoga class (at Yoga Mandala -- amazing), I headed over with my cousin because we were craving Indian.

The guy at the front kiosk was RUDE.  I've been allergic to gluten for the past two years and when I asked him if any was used in the food he said (a little too quickly) "Oh no, we use absolutely none of that," but a second before hadn't even known what gluten was until I explained it.  Low and behold, I had severe reactions to what I ate.  

He also told me "it didn't make sense" to order extra vegetables in my vegetable dish.  AKA did not allow me to order what I wanted.  I got the distinct impression he was a chauvinist because he was polite to all the men in line.  I'm no ultra-feminist hippie, at all, by ANY means, but I was really rubbed the wrong way.

So, this two-star rating is, all-in-all, a repsonse to an instance of bad service and general dirtiness of the establishment.  I'd definitely say that if you're in the area, there is PLENTY of other cheap, delicious food around!!

I much prefer House of Curries, which is just a two-minute walk away. Purchased a Munch on Me deal to try this place out, and found it to be pretty lackluster. 

I ordered the chicken tikki masala ($5.99) with a garlic naan ($1.99). The prices are cheaper than those at House of Curries, but the curry does not stack up. I found the curry to be rather watery and the flavor diluted. The chicken in it was not tender, and I found myself biting into a few unpleasant, tendon-y pieces. The garlic naan comes seasoned with garlic & cilantro - I thought it was dry and overcooked. 

Sorry, Naan N Curry. Maybe I came on a bad curry day, but you just didn't deliver!

Pros:
Their food is alright, not the best indian food I tried, but they are alright.

Cons:
Their plates are too small which makes it over-priced!!!!!!
One order will never make you full, you need two!!!!!!!!!
The kitchen doesn't look clean.....

We came to Naan N Curry because I wanted to try Indian food around the time of my birthday.  Evelynn is NOT a fan of Indian food and cannot even stand the smell of some of the stuff...but she looked at some reviews and stuff and we decided on here.
I really liked it. We got the Tikka Chicken Masala, a regular Naan and a spiced potato Naan.  Evelynn liked it as well, but not as much as I did. 
The unlimited chai tea put it over the top for me!!

I've been coming here for Chicken Tikka Masala and FREE chai tea since my sis has been at Cal in 2003. Whenever I'm in town I always stop by for a SNACK (aka: 2 pieces of naan, chicken tikka masala and tea plus a friend)! That is the only things I get and the only things I recommend. Get a window table and enjoy the tea =]

I'm such a hypocrite. I mean I am aware this is Indian fast food but I love Indian food so much I actually can justify giving naan n curry 2 stars. 

I have never been to Naan N curry before but i have heard stories.I wasn't really sure what the whole self serv thing was . . .  and the waiter wasn't very forth coming with the info. 

I ordered 3 dishes: the aloo palak (uggggggh, it lacked flavor!! how can Indian food lack flavor?!!?), mixed veggie (meh, it was ok for 2 dollars) and the veggie biryani (i mean for 6 bucks I have had waaaaaaay way way better iyryani at  ma and pa shops). The naan was decents and HUGE; you only need 1 piece for 2 people. 

Overall . . . . if you loooove Indian food and you can afford it go somewhere else. Also, if you are an Indian food virgin DO NOT GO HERE. I'm really not trying to be a Debbie Downer but if you are an Indian food snob like me and love REAL Indian food (I'm from f&^%ing San Jose there are like 14287425 Indian engineering students here and I got some from Indi friends who make me some LEGIT Indian food. I'm talking FROM SCRATCH!!! STRAIGHT UP SPICES AND SHIT. 

but I digress . . .  this joint is a'iiiight.

Greetings potential Naan N Curry customers. Here's a word of advice: if you are there during the $8 lunch buffet and are determined to eat here, GET THE BUFFET. Or maybe order either Curry or Naan seeing as that seems to be what they're proud of. 
In my case I ordered off the menu during the lunch hour and what I got looked and tasted far from fresh or worth my money. The stuff that had been sitting around in the buffet ironically looked better and at least  would present you with more variety. 
I had a craving for lamb and Indian food at an affordable price, and so I succumbed to this place.
I had a small plate of lamb tikka masala that was not overcooked so much as petrified and riddled with bones (and it didn't even come with rice, what's up with that??) . It really isn't a good sign when the chef doesn't know how to cook meat. The tikka masala sauce was nice though, I guess.
And on the plus side the chai tea is yummy and FREE, and the young men working there are nice (some of them are quite cute actually . . .)
I might give it another shot just for the cute Indian waiter I had, but otherwise no.

P.S. Naan N Curry has one of the most repulsive and smelly bathrooms ever. Use at your own risk. 
I really wanted to like this place . . . but it just didn't work out.

I can't get enough of the Naan. I love their Palak Paneer. I like free refills on the chai tea.  The place can get crowded. The bathroom is just disgusting. Their kitchen doesn't look much better...I try not to think about this when I eat here...

Have heard about this place many a times and decided to check it out today- ordered the Curry Lamb today with a side of Plain Naan.  I am a BIG fan of anything Curry and was a bit disappointed that the Curry Lamb tasted more like Hot and Sour Lamb- mostly salty and tomatoey.  Their prices are low, but my Curry Lamb was almost all sauce with just a few slivers of lamb.

Finally, an Indian restaurant that lives up to the hype!  Brought to Naan N Curry by some non-Indians who raved about it and even being the tikka masala snob that I am, it was delicious!  Portions are good for individuals or for sharing and one piece of garlic naan is totally sufficient!  The naan is scrumptious!!!  Served hot and fresh and fluffy with tons of garlic and cilantro.  I had the chicken tikka masala... the gravy was delicious, hot and spicy.  The chicken was well-cooked and tasty.  Free chai served with all orders - just make sure you add some sugar.  Not the best cup of chai I've ever had but it'll do.  The place itself looks like a hole in the wall but as many of us know, those are the places that tend to have the best food.  Plus the service is awesome and the people are friendly.  Sounds like a good plan to me!

tick tock... tick tock... tick tock.... BONG... BONG... BONG.... (imagine that 12 times for noon). 

LUNCH TIME! :-)

Saturday classes on the Cal campus can be *grooling* when you're there 8.5 hours a day! I was jonesing for some cheap and fast south asian food for lunch as the clock ticked closer to the noon hour break. Once the bell tower on campus boomed lunchtime, i bolted down Telegraph ave, somewhat aware that Naan N Curry was someplace close. Hey, i had *60 minutes* to get TO the spot, order, eat, AND get back! I was a woman on a mission!

Off I went, and a block down from the Telegraph/Bancroft intersection, there it was. like a neon light brightly rising out of the Las Vegas night time darkness on the strip, I saw the sign and my heart lept with joy! Even being lunch time on a busy saturday, i didn't have much of a wait for ordering or waiting for the food. The person at the register was very friendly, chatty even. Though i've been to other locations, I'd never been in this one and was pleased to see how large and spacious it was. Decor is lovely, and they were playing some wonderful south asian music in the background. a lovely, lovely interior to enjoy a meal in, or wait to take out your order. 

I ordered the veggie somosa's (they don't HAVE meat, - 1 star), the naan stuffed with meat, and the palaak ghoti (spinach lamb). YUMMY! I grabbed a water glass and filled it with the complimentary chai (those tea cups are WAY too small and i was NOT about to be walking back and forth for 'refills') and happily sat watching my podcasts until my food arrived. they brought me the naan stuffed with garlic in error, but when i pointed it out they rushed the correct naan out to me asap AND let me keep the other one! I easily took home 2/3rd's of my lunch for another meal and *I WAS STUFFED*!!! 

$14.00 bucks WITH a tip! that's cheap even on a *students* budget, especially when this has turned into 3 meals! :-) I ate my fill, took home what was left, and STILL got back to my class before the hour was up! now that's what i call an easy lunch! :-)

Man, I love this place!!!! I'll go back whenever I can..... ;-) And i'm in class EVERY saturday until May, so they'll see me again SOON!

Used to go here quite a bit when I lived near by...this place is hit or miss. Sometimes the chicken tikka masala is good; sometimes not so good. This last time I went, it was good!! My friend ordered the egg plant curry and I was pleasantly surprised -  very flavorful! I am a meat eater so I was expecting a bland dish or something, but I was wrong. I loved it.

Not too bad. We walked in just to use the bathroom but decided to stay and eat also. Had this lamb thing that looked like a burrito with the foil on, this spicy curry with prawns, and naan. Reading all the other reviews makes me feel like I have a stomach of steel! I didn't get sick whatsoever. I liked the food actually! I don't know if I'd go out of my way to ever come back, but it was cool for what it was.

They've lowered the prices!! Huzzah!

I got some Chana Masala for 3.99! So I upgraded to garlic naan which was doughy and delicious. And so garlic-y that I could taste it in the morning.

And if you have an extra stomach, like my boyfriend, you can eat to your heart's content at the buffet for just 8.99. I sampled the clay oven cooked chicken and it was ever so slightly spicy and delicious. 

Since there are many good indian places in Berkeley all within a close proximity, price definitely becomes a deciding factor. I'll definitely be patronizing them more often now!

This place is great. The times I've gone  my food has been warm, the naan was doughy and the portions were a good size, I couldnt finish my Chicken Tika Masala and Rice. The only thing that bugged me was that I had been paying around 11 bucks for Rice, Naan and Chicken Tika Masala (Eat-in) and the guy at the register didn't tell me that I could get the buffet for only 8 bucks and it had all the same stuff plus more. That kinda irritated me because I had been there about 6 times before I decided to take a look at the buffet options. Aside from that its great and really close to campus.

Dirt cheap (you can find dishes for $4 or so) and the naan ($1) is very generous-sized. I've tried at this point 5 or 6 vegetarian dishes and have little to complain about, but if you're not into what my Indian roommate calls "fast-food Indian" (as an American I'm not too skilled at differentiating), you might try Mount Everest Indian, about 2 blocks down. However, there's a large selection for meat-eaters and vegetarians alike, and the prices are almost ridiculously low.
Service can be a little slow sometimes as the kitchen staff is limited, but overall it's worth the wait. It's an order-up-front style restaurant so waiters won't really come to check on you, which I feel really isn't a positive or negative. 
Not the most romantic atmopshere, so don't bring a date here. This place is best for families, friends, or takeout.

The food here is "okay" because I feel like there are much better Indian restaurants in the Berkeley area. I got the $8.99 student buffet. I'll admit this is a really good deal because you can get Naan, Chicken Curry, Chicken Tikka Masala, Rice, Rice pudding, Spicy Garbanzo Bean Curry, and some kind of mixed vegetable curry all for it but I think that the food is just "alright". The one problem I had with this restaurant is that they were slow to replace food when it ran out so I constantly had to wait for more rice or naan. Besides that, the food is just alright for the buffet. I have yet to try the actual menu food so maybe it'll be more worth it next time.

A remodel would help. I've come here twice and it's not exacty satisfying. The price is fine but the food tends to be cold. Not a huge selection compared to other locations of the same company. 
Free chai. I like the service.. well it's mainly self serve but when youre at the cashier to pay, theyve always been nice to me. Use your student discount!

Hadn't been to Indian food in over a year and was super excited. Well we chose the wrong place. 

The sauce was ok a bit bland, The naan was good (though how do you mess that up), the quality of the lamb was horrible. It was full of bones and most of it was fat that was not even edible. 

My friend got the Tandori boneless chicken which was actualy pretty good. So I suggest you get that if you go there. 

Also when I went the Tea was out and it took them almost 40min to get more.

Some of the worst indian food I've ever had.

We ordered tandoori chicken - it was light pink because they didn't even season it all the way..and then over grilled it so it was chewy and charcoally. 

Naan - Dense, stale, tasteless pieces of bread. Not the light/slightly buttery/ melt-in-your mouth naan you're used to.

garbanzo bean chutney - they put it in a plate that makes it look like a lot, but it's really about 4 tablespoons. rip off. this at least had some taste, otherwise everything else would have been inedible 

Overall the food was gross, the owner was too busy yelling at some homeless guy for taking too many onions to provide us with decent service, and the place is dirty as hell. avoid.

I'm not sure why anyone would voluntarily eat here, and pay good money to do so. As an Indian, I can testify that the food here does NOT taste anything like what it's supposed to; this is the worst Indian food I've ever had (and keep in mind that I'm including my own disastrous attempts at cooking here).

The buffet is tempting only because it's cheap. Don't do it! The curries are watery and bland, and the breads (naan) are nothing special. The last few times I was here, the vegetables were noticeably wilted and the chutneys tasted really stale :/ The pakoras tasted like deep fried cardboard. Ordering a la carte is a better option; the chicken biryani is pretty good. Their curries and kababs kind of scare me because they're extremely bright colored and stain your hands; I'm always wary of artificial food colorings and this place uses them liberally.

The one star is for their staff. They're really friendly and nice, but I'm definitely never going here again.

Dude.  I totally lived here while I was at Cal.  So close to campus.  Their Chicken Tikka Masala was so delicious.  I just loved to dip their naan in the sauce.  I didn't even need the chicken.  The sauce was just so awesome.  Probably not the healthiest thing, but so so good.

I also liked how it was cheap & fast.  I'd get dinner for $7.  It was always the same guy at the register (now that its been 3 years I can't remember his name), and he was rad.  

Yeah, you hafta get your silverware, soda, and napkins yourself, but I never minded b/c it was only $7, and then they serve you your food as soon as its ready. 

If I was back in Berkeley for the day, this would be one of my stops.

When the House of Curries and Naan N Curry were all as one this was one of my favorite "go to" Indian food places.  Well, I went yesterday for the first time in a long while - a few changes.  They now have (surprise) a buffet for $8.99.  Quite honestly it sucked.  If I was starving and hadn't eaten in weeks then I'd give it 5 stars. As it were, however, I was terribly disappointed.  The naan was so freaking hard and dried out that I actually contemplatrf taking about 20 or 30 of them to re-shingle my roof.  And my all time fav chicken tikki masala had more tikki and masala than actual chicken. Same went for the lamb.  Lots of sauce.  Not so "lots" on the actual meat.  Final salvo of the day for this place - The selection of  buffet food items was sorry at best.  One rice pudding, one rice, one chicken, two veggies, and one lamb.  Go to Naan and Curry over near the Tenderloin. It 's so much better.  If you're stuck in the east bay yer better off eating toe jam.  

Very sad.

This place has gotten worse over the years, smaller portions, less flavor and bad service. The last time I went here the cashier was rude and rolled his eyes when I asked him questions about the menu. He charged me $10 more on my card, wanted to give me the difference in cash and didn't even give me the full amount back that he over charged me. The buffet food isn't very good, it looks like the same as the food you order from the kitchen but they taste really different.
Chumped

I am not very sure why people come here.  You are in Berkeley and there are a million other choices to make, even regarding Indian food, and for some reason I felt compelled to walk through the doors.

I might have given this place 2-stars based soley on taste.  But the guy at the counter was rude, there was no atmosphere (which I wasn't expecting...but I digress), and the portions were smaller that I have had for similar prices at other, better, restaurants.

Did I mention to cockroach hanging out on the trash can on the way to the bathroom?!  Maybe the reason I didn't eat the food was because I lost my appetite.  I wont be coming back.

A friend of mine took me here and I really enjoyed it - not just the food, but the location, too (very close to the Berkeley campus). This place has one of the best paneer tikka masalas I've tried.  The naan is excellent, too, especially the garlic.  It's a bit shabby and run down, but who cares when the food is good and there's free chai to be had.  The music and sound system are pretty good (some places play 30-year-old tapes on a system that's just as old that don't have an ounce of base).  I've been back a few time now, and the only reason I'm giving this place 4 stars is because during my last visit, the food wasn't quite up to par (must depend on who's cooking that day).   If you enjoy people watching, you won't be disappointed (it's Berkeley, for crying out loud).  

For those not familiar with Berkeley, there's a parking garage near Channing and Telegraph, and is reasonably priced.  Don't forget to ask for a parking validation from the restaurant. It's only for $1, but that's one more dollar you can use to get dessert at the yummy gelato place on the Berkeley campus.

Finally a place where the Indian food isn't too far below English standards!

The lamb biryani, lamb seekh and chicken seekh are good! We split that and a buffet fish between 2 of us. The buffet meant we had unlimited naan and yoghurt, and could also grab some veg too.

Buffet food was exactly what I'd expected, just Indian flavored mush. But my expectations were right around there so I was fine.

Maybe my taste buds have evolved, but this was some bad Indian food. The chicken in the Tikka was dried out, the quality of the ingredients seemed subpar, and just the overall cleanliness and ambiance of the place was less than desirable.

I remember having better dining experiences here in the past (years and years ago) so not sure if their quality went down or I've becoming more dinstinguishing w/ my Indian cuisine but next time I will pass.
Great curry. Amazing naan, and delicious tea.

I've been to my fair share of Indian places, especially in a Indian restaurant filled city like Berkeley. Naan N Curry is just plain bad. House of Curries, just down the street, is wayyyy better. The spices are alive in the House of Curries dishes, while at Naan N Curry its bland and plain.

Actually, I'd give this place 3.5 stars, but 4 stars is okay.

As a South Indian - I enjoy the food because it's nothing that my mom makes.  We don't eat lamb curry, chicken tikka masala or have naan on the regular.  So for that, this place is awesome.  The food is very flavorful and very filling, the naan buttery and hot.  And free refills on the chai, good stuff.

The decor and apparent uncleanliness is something less desired, however, if you don't expect it to be clean, it doesn't take away from the eating experience.  I haven't had bad experiences such as the ones described here (band-aid under naan... ewww...); so I can't speak for that.

Word of warning - if you have a weak stomach, drink lots of Maalox and/or eat Tums prior to and after eating your meal.  And you WILL permeate the scent of Chandini Chowk for the rest of the day, regardless of what else you eat or do.

This food was not horrible, went here a long time ago though, and I think this place might have even be better than it's Irving location in SF, which isn't saying much....but it's not horribly priced. I think this chain is probably just not consistent,maybe when they carry the food over a day or two its worse...anyways, I think this place is pretty dirty, so if you have any other options, I would take them.

So my friends and I stopped by for the lunch buffet seeing that it was cold and rainy outside and there's nothing better than some warm curry and naan on days like this.  We were happily enjoying our delicious plates of chicken tikka masala, chicken curry, and whatnot when the owner/manager stops at our table and says, "You should try the veggie soup.  It's made out of fresh vegetables."  He then goes on to rave about it.  Like any normal, polite customer, I responded with, "Okay sure, we'll definitely have to try it then."  He immediately asked in an accusatory tone, "Why did you say definitely?!?!?"  Taken aback I said, "Uhh, because you highly recommend it."  Then he suddenly goes and lectures us for about 5 minutes about vegetarianism and how we aren't designed to be carnivores, ranting that Europeans used horses to draw carts not tigers and used that as part of his argument that animals that eat plants are stronger than animals that don't  (Yeah, WTF, right?).  And he said this all while my curry was getting cold!  After that angry lecture, I lost most of my appetite, but proceeded to eat more to get my money's worth.  Every time he walked by our table, we got scared that he'd lecture us again...and you know what?  HE DID.  He walked up to us with a freshly peeled garlic and VERY defensively told us that he only cooks with the freshest ingredients, as if we had accused him for not doing so.  We weren't his only victims, though.  We saw him kind of harass some other other customers too.  And that's not all.  When we left, he glared at us on our way out!!!  Can you believe it??!  Well, it's good to know that they do use fresh ingredients, but bad to know that they have such a creepy/angry owner/manager dude.

One last thing: while my friend was eating, he found a piece of chicken that was still pink/red.  Gross.  I used to like you Naan N Curry, but now I definitely don't.

Despite finding a large piece of mouse poop on my soda can I still found the food pretty tasty. Yeah, I'm an adventurous eater. The garlic naan is better than roti. Usually roti is thin and crispy, but not here. I didn't get sick so that's a plus.

Any of their curry with rice or naan is savory.  Their service is improntu - you order your items at the cash register, wait for your order to be called, and sit yourself at the table.  Their tea and water are free.  Their tea is excellent and you may want to add a scoop of sugar varying on your taste preference.  Their tea can easily surpass boba tea drinks (just try adding enough sugar).  Lamb and beef curry is awesome.  Their other location on College Avenue is more suitable if you're on a date.  To-go is available.

I love this place! You can come in your sweats and no one will judge. I come here with my bf all the time and we only spend about $12... 

The portions are big... 2 dishes and naan is good enough for 2 people... The cheese naan is excellent. I think cheese naan should count as 2 dishes, because i was so full just eating it...  The bitter melon curry is great! Not bitter at all...

Also, there's free chai tea. Gosh, i love free things!

Apparently they serve breakfast too, except that it's american-style, i believe.
Yuck. Horrible smell. Uncooked chicken. Dirty utensils. Need I say more?

Basing this review almost solely on their lamb naan, which is fantastic and is only $3.  It's a whole meal in itself, and I've yet to have a better lamb naan.  Other places leave the lamb all ground and crumbly.

This place makes the lamb into strips, after the ground lamb is rolled flat from ground lamb of course.

I loved the fresh baked naan.  I love naan in general so i was hooked at this place.  And the fact that they use real tandori ovens was pretty cool.  The only minor complaint that I had was that the place was a little dirty.  Come on, if you have a restaurant respect the food and clean up the place and make it look nice.

oh Naan N Curry...how interesting my relationship is with you. They dont listen when u ask for a certain level of spiciness. I love the free tea. Its plain old college indian food...dont expect the best, and dont expect the worst. (ps. portions are small, if ur broke, go somewhere else)

If your idea of Indian food is Campbell's Tomato Soup with gristly meat and bone, then this is the place for you!

It is awful.  Don't go there.

The website looked great - good selection of food, good prices and BYO wine.  We walked in and the place smelled wonderful.  They did not have the first few menu items that we requested, they only served water to drink, the single bathroom (male & female) was dirty, out of toilet paper and out of hand-towels.
As we had already ordered we asked them to make the meal to-go.  They forgot to include the breads.   The portion sizes were small... but the food was so bad we couldn't finish it anyway.  We ordered two different tikka masalas - one tasted like Campbell's Tomato Soup, the other like tomato paste; and the meat was full of gristle and bone.  The bread and rice were quite nice... but if that's the only positive thing we can say about this place.

Don't waste your time or money here.

We went to lunch here one day, I had the one on O'Farrell before and we kind of liked it.  This one wasn't as good, the dishes were very watery and I told the front cashier, he got someone to change it and it came out the same.  The prices and menu are about the same, quality wasn't, so I don't think I will come back here again.........

I've always loved Indian food. There's no real explanation as to why I do or when I started to. But I've eaten different curries and have had naan plain without any dippings or whatever. So it was highly likely that I would definitely enjoy Naan N Curry's food. I mean, how can you go wrong with naan and curry?

So finding parking on a gameday at Cal is a freaking blast. My friend and I weren't aware that there was a basketball game that day so it was wonderful. It almost made us not want to eat on Telegraph.

When we finally park (two blocks away), I walk into the place and see that it is pretty plain for the most part which is a good thing to me. There is definitely culture in here. You order at the counter and they ask you where you'd like to sit.

I ordered the garlic naan, chicken tikka masala and a soft drink. $11.42. Kinda pricy but oh well. It's my first time here and I'm pretty sure it's going to be good. They have cups in this cabinet and a refrigerator that is full of carafes full of water.

The waiting time isn't long. The curry is pretty runny but it still holds itself together and the naan was huge for being about a foot in diameter. The food was very good. The formula here is very simple. My friend ordered rice and we shared it. So you throw the rice into the curry and just dig in. I will never stop loving Indian food...

This place is pretty out of my way but if I'm ever in the area again, I'd definitely eat here. And then proceed to browse at Rasputin's across the street.

I try to always make it a point to eat here when I'm up in Berkeley! I love this place not only because it's reasonably price but the portions are pretty decent and the spices that they use are subtle enough to notice each one, but strong enough to satiate my indian food needs. 

I like the feel of this place too, has a hole in the wall feel to it - perfect for college students. Also there is a student discount here and the buffet here is pretty decent. The food is ok, I just like the environment when it's packed!

Good place for intro and intermediate indian food!

Not a great Naan N Curry.  The food here, seems to fall a bit flat.  My usual staple meal is the Chicken Tiki Masala, but here it is too much tomato paste, not enough spice.  

My preference is for the house of curries around the corner.

First, the funny: when we went in here, my boyfriend commented that it was "authentically dirty," as in, it felt just like being in India.

The good: food is tasty, buffet is cheap, and you can get your own water.

The bad: the bathroom and general facilities are actually pretty dirty. It's not terrible or uncomfortable, but it's definitely a place you go for value rather than anything else. I also didn't love the Naan, but the curry was yummy.

I ate at this restaurant while visiting UCB campus. 

The food made me sick and I vomited. This place is dirty and gross. 

The food is below standard as well. The gravy for all the curries is the same and the Baigan Bharta I ordered did not taste like Baigan Bharta at all. The size and overall quality of the Nan bread was good.

The food is very boring and not cheap enough to justify its boringness. With so many places to eat Indian food in Berkeley, you'd think they would do better! The buffet food sits out too long...the flavor is pretty lackluster to begin with, and once it's been out for a while the texture really starts to suffer as well. Even the rice is blandish, not fragrant and flavorful like rice at most Indian restaurants. 

As for the ambiance, service is speedy and not unfriendly; decor sucks. Tables are close together and once when I was there the roof was leaking...5 gallon plastic buckets were put out to catch the drips, right in the middle of the dining room!

I have been to Naan n Curry three times over the past 8 years and I will not return.

Not the best tasting Indian restaurant as Roti in Burlingame might do it for me. However, the deals here are reasonable. Chicken masala and regular naan is what I typically get. You can easily eat here for lunch and spend around 7-8 bucks max for a solid belly. Seats can get pretty packed during certain times as students frequent this place a lot. However, if you're in the east bay for whatever reason (I had no choice since I lived here for school at one point), this is one of the hot spots in berkeley that I recommend.

I usually love Chicken Tikka Masala, but it wasn't very good here. The chicken wasn't as tender as it usually is and the dish didn't have the full flavor. The Lamb Vindaloo was OK - really spicy and had a lot of fat in the meat. It also came with bones that you had to pic around. The garlic naan was great, though - the best part of the meal! I had used a Groupon Now deal to get $16 worth of food for $8, so it was worth it for that price, but I won't go back again. They were also a little rude in redeeming the Groupon - they almost didn't take it because their clock said it was 1 minute past the time I was allowed to redeem it. My phone (which I was using to redeem the Groupon) said it was exactly 5:30 though, so they ended up letting me. I just couldn't believe they wouldn't let it slide for 1 minute!
Food poisoning.....enough said

I knew I wasn't going to get quality food for a $9 all you can eat Indian buffet...But I also didn't anticipate having stomach pains lasting for 3 days because of the wretched food...I do not recommend this restaurant.

The food was just okay, nothing spectacular. My dish tasted like my mom's curry with some hot sauce added in, and we're not even Indian. It was a bit too spicy for me, so I didn't really get to enjoy it (it actually wasn't very spicy, I just can't handle spicy stuff that well). 

Props for the free chai tea. I can't really comment much on the service since it was self-serve and self-seat. It did irk me that they didn't have any forks and only had a handful of spoons left. Also, their bathroom was out of literally everything, and the hand dryer wasn't even on.

Eeeeeeeeeeeew.

OK -- maybe they're not always this bad.  Maybe they were just having a bad day.  But I only went there once and ordered Palak Paneer (I believe; it was spinach curry).  When it arrived, it tasted good.  It was a goopy mess of yummy spinach.  But I started eating and found a long hair in it.  I kept eating.  Then I found what seemed to be a bone.  Pulled out the bone...and for some reason, kept eating.  Then I found a TWIG.  And another bone piece.  And another twig.  And then another hair.  What the hell?

So wrong.

Consistent stomach problems after eating at this location. STAY AWAY!

These 'stores' are not consistent in the preparation of their sauces and food. I would not recommend this location, try Breads of India instead, because we've consistently had problems after eating here. I would recommend the locations in San Francisco, though.

Is there a ZERO STARS option?

Oh yea, bring on the Indian food. 

This place is spicy and cheap...two things I really enjoy.

Ok, let me lay it out for you.

Pros:

-Cheap: need I say more...? I'm a college student people! I can eat here for the same price of McDonalds and feel ethnic at the same time.

-Tasty: Great flavors of Indian food of course, and SPICY. I love spicy food. It's not good until you have to blow your nose and wipe away your tears. Of course, for you weaklings you can ask for it less spicy.

-Atmosphere: Hey....it's Berkeley, you need to be a little wacky to be here anyway. This place is hip, it's on Telegraph street for god's sake. It's good for a lot of events...just hungry, broke, muchies, groups.

-Fast: Have you ever waited at a restaurant for 20 minutes just to have your order taken...then waited another 30 minutes to have your order delivered...well...this isn't Applebees. You'll have your food in about 10 minutes or less for the time you walk in.

-Cheap: Oh yea, I said that already


Cons:

-It's packed a lot. Which...really isn't a con for them.

-Parking is a bizzie

You'd have to look pretty damn far and pretty damn wide to find such excellent Indian food at such good prices.  Perfectly spiced dishes (chicken tikka masala and the chickpea curry are my favorites) paired with a gigantic piece of fluffy naan for around $7 is more than I could ask for any day of the week.  Oh so tasty.  Plus, the staff members are sweet and polite, and they sing shamelessly along with the Indian pop music playing over the loudspeakers.  Hell yeah.

*Edit - I've had better Indian food at the same prices since then. So, yeah. it's still good, but not great.

*Edit part deux - Yeah, the last two times I've been there, I spent the next couple of hours making frequent trips to the john. Not so much fun.
The food was absolutely the worst Indian food I've ever had at a restaurant. I suppose it's on the same level as cafeteria food so students don't know any better.

I'll be honest with you. I have passed by this place numerous times and having read the Yelp reviews, stayed away. Based on some of the reviews, I would have expected Yellow Warning Tape outside with Hepatitis C literature.

well, last week, the world aligned and I found myself hungry and comparing the cost of a $7 wrap over on Durant vs all you can eat for just about the same price?..it became a no-brainer.

one of barometers for Indian food and especially their buffetts is the AR test, or the Acid Reflux test. you know when you begin to burp up stomach acid? gross yes, but all too common at many a Indian buffet. 

I knew the potential here, stuff my face and end up heaving bloody puke in the toilet 2 hours later. .......After eating here, I am happy to say I am here and have not had to check into my local ER.

The food here while not the best, there was some pretty bright moments. Most of the stuff was poorly labled, but out of the 6 or so choices, I would say 2-3 were really good and memorbable. 

Was it pretty dirty? kinda, hey it is berkeley and telegraph ave and you have your mix of students, local weirdos, plus it is Indian food.....I did take a quick glace into the kitchen and really would have preffered not to......but all in all, I would feel safe to return.

I should probably try the regular dishes before judging this place from the buffet...wait, looking at the reviews, maybe not...

It's has an Indian buffet. Chicken tikka masala, naan, aloo gobi, lamb palak. The first few times I went here, they rotated the selections, but the last few times I've went, it's been the same: two meat dishes (CTM and lamb palak) and two generic veggie dishes. Don't get me wrong, I love my veggies...but you can tell they're being cheap when they offer two different potato dishes and a cauliflower dish...out of 6 options. Come on, where's the paneer?!??!

The naan is meh. You can save yourself some pain by picking out the ones that look more moist and less burnt. It tends to be a little dry, but just soak it all in the tikka masala sauce, and all is good.

My favorite thing is usually the rice pudding. Mmm...cardamom (right spice?) in desserts is always a winner.

I probably will come back, even though I know I shouldn't. My stomach tells me conflicting feelings: it's good after a long day of not eating too much; it's also terrible when you feel like about to burst afterwards. It's not just overeating too - for me, the food there tends to make me feel bloated. But I'm cheap, and I like my bottomless meat (and tikka masala sauce). Or maybe I can beg Clark Kerr Commons to serve CTM once in awhile... 

(A random idea: this is what buffets should do to market themselves: something like a Fenton's challenge? Who can eat 6 full plates of food in 15 minutes? How about 8?? This isn't unhealthy...think of it as getting your money's worth! And we'll give you a certificate =D)

This place sucks... the servers were rude... the place looked dirty.... the food was gross. I got the chicken tikka masala and it came out on this tiny plate with like three pieces of chicken and a gallon of sauce. I'm just glad I didn't have to pay

It was about time I stumbled across what you would call "bad Indian food". For a while I thought there was no such thing as bad Indian food. I was a naive fool coming into this place. Being lured by its convenience on Telegraph Ave and its cheap prices. A fool indeed.

I can't think of a single dish I really enjoyed here. Their palak paneer was the most disappointing. There were no signs of spices or flavor present. It  tasted like frozen spinach that was thawed out in a microwave and thrown together with a few cubes of cheese. Masalas didn't do much for me either. The veggie masala especially, tasted kind of... pickled? Naan was chewy and flavorless.

Never again!

I really enjoy indian food and have been delighted with the the array of authentic places around the East Bay.  But I was very disappointed in this place. Here's why:

1.  Chicken Tikka Masala was completely lacking in masala (spice/flavor).  The Chicken was in a few large chunks that tasted like they had just been boiled and covered with the sauce.  The sauce tasted like cream with maybe a hint of mushroom.  No other flavor, didn't even taste like it was salted.  Yet mysteriously, it was bright orange.  

2.  The 'chai,' though bountiful, is not Chai. At least not on the night that I went.  It tasted like the bulk black tea I have at my house, with milk.  To really be called Chai, it has to have Masala, the distinct blend of cloves and cardamom and cinnamon, among others.  There was no Masala in this.  

3.  There was a curly black hair in my naan.  And then there was another.  Makes me wonder how many I swallowed.  

In retrospect, I should have thought twice.  A restaurant called naan n curry in the states is probably the equivalent of a restaurant called buns n burgers in some other part of the world. Not to be relied upon to be authentic, or to even come close.

BUFFET REVIEW ONLY
Although they recently raised the price AGAIN ($7.99 in 2009, $8.99 in 2010, $ 9.99 in 2011), I would still consider myself as a regular diner. No, this place is not as clean as expected, and they often do a poor job cleaning the tables and re-stocking the soda machine and food platters. No, the foods are not as pleasent as the ones you eat at a decent authentic indian restaurant. However, I think this place is still somehow acceptable, you just have to bare with it.

ps. they usually have good, puffy naan bread, yet I once ate a burnt naan that tasted like rock...boo

There are definitely better Indian places in the East Bay (even Berkeley for that matter), but this place is good as a quick and affordable option for decent food. They also have pretty ample seating and a open environment which is nice and sometimes rare for restaurants on Telegraph. As far as food, they have all your standard options and lots of naan choices. I wouldn't actively seek this place out to try, but it's worth a stop.

I hate to bash a local favorite, but this just isn't what Indian food is about. I played it safe and ordered the tikka masala, garlic naan, and tea. The tea, which is self-service, was great. However, the garlic naan was bland and surprisingly not very garlic-y. But the tikka masala... lousy; chicken was dry, sauce was bland thin. I eat Indian for the spices. If you want to try Indian food, but are afraid it'll be too spicy, you're in luck; they don't use any.

This place makes me wanna puke. What I said about House of Curries applies here too, except the curry is more watery than oddly cheesy.

I do appreciate the 24-hour San Francisco one, though (for other reasons.

I came here with my high school friend when we both got to Berkeley because we wanted to try something different... something "berkeley"... and oh dear were we dissatisfied. 

hopefully, with the growing use of yelp, more freshmen won't make the same mistake but... naan n curry is like the mcdonald's of indian food... except slightly more expensive (than mcdonalds). 

i mean... i guess the people who do come here, that's their definition of 'good indian food' but honestly, it's gross and, although i'm not an expert on indian food.... there are MUCH better places... 

for something better and closer: 
house of curries (apparently this place is also owned by the same ppl as naan n curry..like the building...but the people who cook the food are different) 
tandoor kitchen on telegraph+parker
if you want to take the bus or drive: 
taste of the himalayas (on shattuck) 

at least that's where i go :) if you wanna try it... go for it, it's close to campus but... it's bland, watery, and just... not worth your money.

The food moderately priced but hardly good.

Maybe I shouldn't judge based on my one experience, but both my friend and I left with upset stomachs.  

There's much better curry in Berkeley.  Get out of your comfort zone and stay away from these chains.

Dine with Caution!
We found a DIRTY BAND-AID under my Nan bread, and when my friend took it up to the register to complain, they just said..."let me get you a new one". Not, "sorry for the disgusting thing that just happened to you". or even "here's your $$ back".
I gave them one star because I had eaten there for years out of convenience/proximity to my office. But alas, don't think I could bring myself to do it again.
Can you say rubber gloves?
Telegraph eateries are a gamble, but OMG!
Diners ....Beware.
I haven't had much of a craving for Indian since...if you love Indian food as much as I did...skip this place.

This place is so wack. Why would you eat here when House of Curries, a much better, and way more decent Indian Restaurant (that's open late) is about a block away? The only reason anyone should ever go here is to dominate their all you can eat buffet, that consists on one terrible cart with like 10 items. I personally would much rather eat one dish of something that I enjoy, instead of 5 plates of curry that pretty much all tastes the same. The tea is terrible and tastes really watered down.

Wow... this place was actually the first place I ate at in Berkeley when I moved in freshman year.

And dang...this is the last place I would now consider eating if ever on southside.

I love eating Chicken Tikka Masala w/ Garlic Naan, but this place disappoints me.  The only thing nutritional about this dish is the protein in the chicken, but the chicken pieces here are so small.  =(  Go to House of Curries instead.  Price is the same, though you won't feel as ripped off with more meat on your plate.

To begin with, I'm not so fond of this format of Indian restaurant.  You know the one, NorCal-ite - order your dish and then decide between either naan OR rice, because if you were to get both you might as well have gone to a real Indian restaurant where they give you complimentary rice with your meal.   That said - and as I have mentioned in other reviews - for every style of eating Indian food there is a season.  Even this short-order type of Indian restaurant can be done well; it's just that Naan N Curry (or at least this one) doesn't really do it. 

I have had several of the vegetarian dishes at this Naan N Curry and could really only recommend the chana masala, and only then when you order it spicy (so it has some taste).  If you order a palak, look forward to spending the first few minutes of your meal draining the oil off of it.  Or you can take your chances with the laxative-soaked plate.  Be my guest.  But as someone who felt the effects of ill-advisedly and haphazardly  indulging my urge for bhindi (okra) at this joint, I would advise against it. 

Furthermore, there is really nothing special about their naan and their "chutneys" are an abomination - watered down and useless.  Wait, I've got it - Watered Down N Useless.

I would actually give this place a 0/5 stars if I could. Not only was the food BLEH, the service was absolutely terrible. The men working there were probably the rudest I've ever seen. Eating there for dinner with friends, some of us took our time trying to guzzle down the nasty food while trying to enjoy a nice conversation. After about 30 minutes, one of the workers comes over to ask us to eat faster and telling us this is "not a cafeteria". He's sure right about that....the school cafeteria has both better food and nicer workers.

OMG stay away. I wish that I was warned. RUN!!

The place is filthy! I saw a cook put his fingers in a pot and lick them. The walls are grimy. Pipes comig out everywhere. The carpet hasnt been cleaned ever I presume!

The buffet looks downright scary. 

chicken tikki-ok taste 
curry- watery, tasteless, like tomato soup.  This is not curry folks. 
naan- too thick, but ok
spinach and potato- too much salt, but tasty

Service- 35 minutes to get served. We were the only people in there!!

I am wating for my food-borne illness tonight. 

Someone should call the health dept on this place.

Have you ever been talked into ordering something at a time when you weren't expecting an advice?

My friends wanted to grab a quick bite to eat on Telegraph Ave. so we decided to check this place out. I tried to order the lamb boti but they were out, so I asked about the chicken leg tandoori. The server then clarified that the tandoori would only give me one small chicken leg and that I should order the chicken tikka masala instead. Since I really wanted some smoky good tandoori, he then assured me that the two would taste the same.

You guess it. The two were not the same and the food was terrible. The side order of rice was good but my naan tasted like card board that came from the cheap pizza joint down the block. My chicken tikki masala only had a few pieces of chicken, and it was no more than what a small chicken leg would provide. I'm not sure what that brotha was talking about but his version of a chicken leg must come in the size of a wing or something less. I thought to myself, "Man, I didn't realize that tikki could mean tiny in this context."

To kick this into a higher gear, my former jogging partner's order came with four tiny, obscure looking vegi-balls soaked in a bowl of watered down curry. Laughing with her boyfriend, she graciously gave each of us one generous but rare bite, leaving herself with one ball to savor.

Thanks to the server, his advice (not knowing what he might know about the tandoori) probably saved me from a real disaster when the one I had was already the worst. It was during that moment of enlightenment when they turned on all the lights in the restaurant for the evening. What a moment that was, with everyone looking confused at first but hopefully we all came to a better sense of self-awareness of what we were eating.

I can't imagine taking this disaster into another gear but I don't think I'll be going back, at all.

If you don't expect too much, walk in.  The food is just OK, the atmosphere is lacking, the place isn't all that clean, and besides the food itself coming to the table, everything is self serve.

What really killed me on my last visit was the temp in the dining area.  It must have been 45 degrees.  Before I even had hot food in my mouth, I could see my breath, and the food only remained hot for about 2 minutes in the icy room.

On that note, what is up with UC students wearing shorts, t-shirts and FLIP-FLOPS on a freezing cold night?

Following the demise of the original downtown San Francisco Naan N Curry, I shifted my allegiances towards the one on Telegraph Ave., which has never been particularly good but also not quite so bad that it would qualify as inedible. Some dishes are downright awful, all the time, including the bhaingan bharta (as my wife has nicknamed it, a pile of baby poo), though others were consistently not disgusting (the aloo palak and chana masala). The naan tends to be good, though often they seem to burn the naan, as the non-ventilated tandoor lets off thick smoke that leaves a semi-permanent smell in all restaurant-goers clothing for weeks.

Anyways, Naan n Curry was a sort of quintessential 2 1/2 star place. Indian-style blue plate specials, not particularly good, but there's free chai and the naan is good.

But tonight, my dining experience was horrible. My customary aloo palak had a really off flavor, and then in one bite, I uncovered chicken bones. I spit this out, to find that the bone was covered in truly revolting chicken. I mean, this is leftover chicken from someone else's dish, not a carefully selected piece of chicken meat added as a "bonus." To top that off, the chai had a bongwater sort of odor and taste to it. Also inedible.

So I call a waiter over to the table and ask to speak with the manager. I'm told "there is no manager." No manager? Even McDonalds has a manager to field complaints and assure customer satisfaction. I point at the revolting withered piece of leftover chicken and say - "this is a PROBLEM. You need to talk with the chef," and went on to explain that some vegetarians don't particularly enjoy biting into leftover chicken bits. He showed no interest in the problem nor in talking with the chef.

There you have it. A restaurant that truly doesn't care, about customers or food quality. No management, nor standards. At the original naan n curry they actually cared about customers, but that's all lost today.

Sorry Naan N Curry, I've spent thousands of dollars at your decrepit chain since 2000, but will never step inside your wretched doors ever again.

Oarhhh, it's 10 am...My head hurts, my body aches, I'm groggy and my mouth is really dry.  Sounds like anyone's  typical Sunday morning hangover, no? 

But wait  *long pondering pause, retracing the events of last night*...No wine, no cosmopolitans, dirty martinis, not even a piddly little beer. I'm dumbfounded-- what could have done this sweet disaster to my holy temple?

Wait-what's that smell? I've got a whiff of coriander and cumin wafting from my pores...Naan N Curry has officially intoxicated my feeble body...clearly I cannot hang.

*Flashback to the Previous Night*

My friend brings the loot of 4 dishes ( eggplant curry, chicken tandoori, dahl, and a garbanzo spinach mix)...the ghee is oozing from the boxes just waiting to coagulate in my arteries.  Despite the fact that I know I'll be eating the equivalent of three days worth of calories, the glutton in me rejoices.  And less that $20 you say? Ohh sweet Jesus!

It's sooo BAD-- but it's sooo GOOD... we cannot resist, we are powerless against the forces of greasy, spicy Indian curry and the beast from within wants MORE.  We spoon the mixtures and gasp in horror at the amount of oil that spllieth over...captivated, in-trance-- and right to my lips baby.

Yes, it's true. 
I woke up half naked in a fetal position clutching a  tandoori drumstick, surrounded by the mayhem of messy opened curry boxes, with remnants of dahl on my cheeks and paneer slathered over my chest, wondering how in the hell I got here.

Ok NOT REALLY...but that would have been funny.
But seriously, that orgy of curries did some crazy Ju-ju to me last night...aspirin please.

This is one of my favorite places to go to eat. If you like Indian /Pakistani food, than this is the place to go. The price is cheap , most dishes cost 6.99 which is very cheap compare to most Indian places I went to. The food is also very good for the price you pay.

The places looks very outdated, kinda dirty and the chairs and table is very old but that didn't stop me from eating there.Some of my favorite dishes are  curry chicken, stir fried chicken, spinish chicken and masala.

If you want to try Indian food and don't want to pay the expensive price for it, then try this place. Also, they have free chai .

ENJOY.
Yum! Great for what it is - you order at the counter, get a number, and they bring your food to your table. The daal (lentils) = delicious, and I highly recommend the paneer (cheese) or garlic naan.

There is nothing more dreamy than endless chai, rice and cheese tikka massala. Not so keen on their other dishes, which are super spicy, but what else does a girl need? This is my favorite of the man Naan N Curry locations...no creepy waiters, no long wait and pretty clean for cheap and easy Indian.

My previous review was:
"Good place for a first date" 4 stars
Well, that relationship went up in flames.

Just kidding. Kinda. I came here again and, I don't know what it is, the food doesn't taste good anymore. The chicken in the tikka masala was dry and impossible to chew and the alu ghobi was really salty.
To top it off, the meal made me really queasy and uncomfortable for the rest of the night (food poisoning? I dont know...)

Some of you may have noticed the "214 food poisonings and counting" caption below my reviews. Note: by the time you read this, it may be bigger. This scorecard is a result of, but not limited to, experimentation with restaurants, ingredients, Asian markets, Costa Rican car wheel grills, Foogoo and my mother's cooking which I no longer eat - mother's cooking that is. 

Naan and Curry has the supreme honor of having 4 notches in my stomach's lining. I am reminded of president Bush's famous "Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice... Won't get fooled again." That being said, I am not president material, and for me 4 times is a lesson learning score. 

Let me begin by saying that if anybody could engineer a method by which I could inject Naan and Curry Tikka Masala into my veins, as well as produce a toothpaste with the flavor and fill all public pools with this liquid gold buttery goodness - well to that person I would be greatly indebted. 

This place makes a solid, buttery rich Tikka Masala. Forget the chicken in there, I'll order just the sauce, Ill order it with Paneer, I'll order it with green eggs and ham and eat them I will!. Like a good Pavlovian dog I will drool a Saint Bernard under the table if I had access to just one of the dubiously-hygienic 5 gallon buckets of Masala sauce I see the cooks lugging around time to time. This stuff is that good. 

The Lamb is great, the Chana Masala is great, the Aloo Gobi keeps me asking for more. The Tandoor chicken is moist and spicy sweet. Even the free chai tea doesn't taste like crap. 

Man I really love this place. But guess what? I've been folded over in half one too many times to give these guys any more of my money, dignity and gastro-intestinal fortitude. No more I say. Unless I see a yellow-orange IV, I say no thank you to Mr. Naan and his wife Mrs. Curry. No thank you sir and ma'am, though tempted I am for your liquid heroin of delicious golden joy, I will not falter. 

To put a nail in the Naan and Curry coffin let me just say that right across the street on Durant, you can find a joint called House of Curries. And guess what? They use the same recipes and you get to keep the food in you for more than 2 hours. I can almost guarantee it. 

Exact same recipes except for one: the mouth watering, crispy/fluffy, buttery garlicky or oniony, Naan. Yes boys and girls the naan at Naan and Curry is not only unbeatable but unrepeatable even by the wonderful House of Curries. 

So I do bid you all farewell - as it must have been written in the stars, that a wretch of my moral ineptitude and self loathing could not resist another visit, another hit from the golden heroin you call Tikka Masala folded into the perfect naan. So raise your glasses high you fellow experience junkies because I am 215 food poisonings and counting.

I have to say, besides smelling like it after you eat, this is one of my favorite places to eat in Berkeley. My ultimate favorite thing to get is Chicken Tikki Masala with regular Naan and an order of samosas.

five_star for an uber economic meal undeniably catered for the student's budget... cheap and sinfully just yum, i loved it!

spent a lovely afternoon shopping at Berkeley today with my birthday boy (my son) .. i wanted to motivate him to jack-up his grades in order to get a good GPA, SAT and ultimately get into UCB ... how to do that?  walk through the hip and grundge street of Telegraph Ave ...

amidst the cannabis sativa shirts, open pipes for sale, bums here and there ... ultimate Haight Street venue ... and then .. this heaven of a fast food Indian/Pakistani joint!

yum, yum and yum ... a nice change from the hip and foo-foo restaurants of "the city" ...

i just went crazy in my order ... 6 entrees, 3 orders of biryani rice, a naan and soda ... all for only $44.00 ... that is relatively CHEAP, considering that:  $44.00 only buys you a nice ramen soup, apetizer and coke in JapanTown (for two) ... in here ... it's a nice lunch and take home to feed you for the rest of the week!

service is factory like, cashier gives you a blank and mechanical stare, place is super raw, to-go boxes and plastic bags readily available ... it's not a five star, but a wonderful FOR REAL dive!

oh yeah .. agree with the other reviewers ... wear a laundry washable outfit ... you will stink after lunching on-site.

Really average food, but go for the BUFFET.

Service/Decor: Service is quite fast. It's comfortable to eat in, but sometimes the tables are really close together and it gets awkward.

Food: Again, just average. The first time I came, I ordered a Palak Paneer with Naan, which is usually my favorite dish, but I was definitely not impressed. It tasted fairly bland and almost tasteless. After, I just came for the buffet. Unlimited chicken tikka masala, chicken tandoori, that rice pudding (which I have no idea what it's called), chai, and a few other dishes? Awesome. It's only $9 for an Indian buffet, and I'm a pretty darn big eater. There were many a day that I stuffed myself silly... stacking up plates upon plates...

This was like the first Indian restaurant I've tried and I was so juiced! It's pretty convenient for college students since it's right down the street from Cal and the place is pretty big. Not sure if the food is authentic, but it tasted pretty good nonetheless. Prices are good, also. $7 curry and $1 naan? Do you wanna argue that? The portions were pretty small though and I didn't really like the rice, but the curry was awesomely spicy ;)

Dear baby Jesus and holy goddesses of India ... How do i begin?! 

  Let me take a breath and exhale as i mentally prepare myself . I'll start off by saying im an avid lover of Indian cusine. However, this place is worthy of passing up. Im sorry Naan and Curry of Bereley perhaps the ones in S.F are a different story. Atleast i hope so. The tikka masala chicken was  good  but the "buffet" that lured us in was more than dissapointing . Salad area was EMPTY!  No salad or cucumbers and fountain drink area had no sodas. We were so thristy and steered our view to the water pitchers. My eyes doubled in size!!  Was i seeing right?  Water had a brownish -yellow tint. Yes, hehe let your imagination run loose. Shoot, i know i need glasses but im not blind. 

  With that said, find somewhere else to feed your holy temple .Stay hungry and thristy my friends.

Worst food ever.

Their indian food is tasteless and wayyy too oily. Once I ordered the chana masala and by the time I opened up the takeout box, a layer of oil 1 inch deep had accumulated on the surface (and that was only what had separated out). The only good thing here was the rice pudding.

If you're looking for cheap, fast indian food, go to House of Curries just down the street (Durant and Telegraph). Don't waste your time (or money) here.

Its damn good and cheap indian food.  So what if the atmosphere is akin to a cafeteria, so what if the bollywood tunes blaring in the background give you a headache (or make you want to dance, or both).  the food is priced appropriatly for the nearby campus, and while not being sublime, its pretty darn tasty.  

btw, dancing on a belly full of curry is not recomended

If I'm visiting my brother then we'll probably eat here or at Racha (sp?), a Thai restau.  This is good, solid stuff.  Service is fast, food is yummy and tummy-pleasing.  Just don't wear clothes that you don't mind getting smelly.

Got the chicken vindaloo. It was not spicy at all. It had 4 small pieces of chicken and 2 small pieces of potato. It was mediocre in taste.
The garlic naan was good, on the good side of mediocre.
My friend got the tikka masala, which I didn't try, but she really likes Naan N Curry. 
I perhaps have a more discriminating taste for Indian food, because to me this place is totally "eh."

despite the dirty bathroom, this place was pretty tasty.  i went to use the bathroom and it was pretty nasty.  my hands were definitely cleaner before going in there (even though i handled money)  we got the chicken tikka masala and chicken curry, and ordered naan for the three of us.  the two dishes were enough to feed us all, with some left overs.  the curry was too spicy for me, but i'm really sensitive to hot foods.  the tikka masala was yummy.
our indian friend really enjoyed the music, and was almost dancing while we were eating.  you get free water and free chai which was nice.  no need to order drinks!
the total for the three of us was $16.  not bad!

it depends on what type of person you are when you go here. if you want to go somewhere to sit down and be served on hand and foot, it's not for you. if you don't mind getting your own dishes, drinks and water, then this place is great for you!!
the prices are pretty good (6-12 dollars an item) and the food is so very tasty. i go here all the time!

I'm not terribly fond of this location in Berkeley for Indian food when you have SO many choices available to you all around the campus. The food is mediocre and not very well seasoned.

Three main advantages to Naan 'N' Curry:

It's conveniently located for students, being only two blocks away from Sproul on Telegraph, you can't get much closer than that.

The buffet is actually a pretty good deal, provided you're looking to get fed and not particularly picky about your curries.

The prices are reasonable and you can get a lot of food as the portions are generous.

I prefer visiting House of Curries up the block or traveling down to Biryani House on Shattuck for my quick Indian/Pakistani fix, or making the trip down to San Pablo/University area for some truly exquisite food.

This place might just earn the title of "Most Mediocre Indian Buffet I've Ever Had," a significant achievement given the wide array of bad Indian food out there. Their rice was barely warm, the curries were bland, and the naan was akin to lukewarm cardboard both in taste and texture. The pakoras were ok, but everything else was either way below average or merely passable.

One note: if you're looking for good vegetarian options in the buffet, don't bother. I've lived in central PA, and as a somewhat casual vegetarian I've come to expect a dirth of good veggie options, but not at an Indian restaurant! There are so many good meatless Indian dishes out there and it seems lazy to offer mostly chicken tandoori and chicken masala, with a visually-unappealing eggplant dish serving as the only veggie plate. For $8.99 a pop, it seems like they should try harder. Indian buffets are never that great, but this one fell very short of an already low bar in my mind.

I go here because it is convenient and it tastes good to me.  I am NOT an Indian-food connoiseur (yet) so take my review on the taste of their food with a grain of salt. I think they are delicious.  Their chicken tikka masala is what I order every time and it never get's old.  I also ordered the lamb curry.  It was good but I preferred the chick tikka masala because it was kind of cheese and all sorts of amazing.  If you want to get fancy with your naan, the onion naan is good.  The garlic naan was a bit burnt.  

Their service is fast but not very personal.  Didn't matter to me because this place is more of a dive than a restaurant to me.  Craving curry and in the Telegraph area? This place ain't bad.

Conveniently located on Telegraph Avenue, this place has a bunch of different curries to satisfy anyone's desire for heat.

Chicken tika masala: Very mild.
Chicken/lamb curry: Medium heat, can draw some sweats.
Chicken/lamb vindaloo: The spiciest.. supposedly. Just keep drinking the water from the carafe (provided) and it won't be painful.
