They also have a set of fried rice plates, but they're not recommended as they cost as much as a regular plate of curry but isn't as filling.

Their naans are huge. I usually like to order one naan and a bowl of rice, as that seems to be a good balance with one plate of curry.

Not as cheap as other fast foods (one dinner can run $10+), but it's very filling and tasty. And you get to listen to Indian techno music. That may or may not be a good thing.

I been here many times since my college days and my usual here is the chicken tikki masala and garlic naan. The chicken has always been dry and overcooked, but I love dipping my naan in the sauce. After trying out authentic Indian food with my Indian friends, this doesn't taste as authentic. It seems to tailor to the college students around here. It seems to lack the heavy Indian spice and spiciness to their food. The prices are cheap and nothing spectacular. Basically you seat yourself and get your own water and utensils. They give you a number to bring to your table and they bring your food to the table when it's ready. Sometimes you can get their deals on Groupon.

The food her tends to be awful most of the time. I don't like any of their curries and the meat is mostly uncooked.

Chicken tikka masala is made with marinated chicken bbq-ed in the tandoor. Naan n curry doesn't do any of that.

They make so much money that they prolly don't care to make good food anymore. The only saving grace is the price and the free chai, which is excellent.

cheap, easy, reliable.

sometimes, that's what you want for lunch.

really, really cheap naan ($1), so at least they know how much their naan is worth.

however, the naan is strangely SALTY, and usually not very consistent (e.g. really thick on one side, really thin and crispy somewhere else), even when the store isn't busy. occasionally they get it right, but it still has that really salty flavor. 

definitely not as good as house of curries a block away ($1.50 naan, much more tasty)

it's actually improved since the last time i've been here, so i'm not hesitant to slightly recommend it.

while it's not the first indian cuisine i would turn to, it's sufficient for a quick, sit-in fix.

but then again, house of curries is only about a block away.

Definitely a Berkeley experience - this place has great Naan!  The whole do-it-yourself feel takes some getting use to but I have generally been satisfied by the food (which I would rate in the mid-quality for Indian for the Berkeley-area).  I have an old friend who loves Naan N Curry though, so for a belated birthday present I treated him to dinner tonight.  Considering there is no obligation to leave a large tip for the DIY service and the low price of the food in general, this was a steal of deal.  Although my friend harassed me for eating the onion Naan (which I love) - saying I must really not want to kiss anybody ...  I said - "not tonight" - he jokingly said "I'm available" - and I said "you're gay."  How I end up in these situations, I don't know.  Not really my thing!  I did enjoy my meal though.

it's not fantastic indian food, but it's cheap, fast, and close. 
it's a bit greasy, but it's decent food and the portions are pretty good. 

and i love the free chai.
What can I say.... buffet option for under 8 bucks... you've won me over :D

I'm not indian, and my indian palate cherry was popped by this place, so read my review with that in mind. I've come to this place probably 6 times, and I've been satisfied almost every time. 

Food: I'm a big eater, so the first thing I worry is quantity. Admittedly, the dishes aren't large for $8, but going to other indian restaurants, I would say they're about average size. The naan is usually my filler, and a pretty good filler at that. The potato, or garlic naan is pretty bomb-diggity, and ordering a couple of those bad boys usually does the trick for me. I've tried a bunch of items there, so my analysis of the menu would be would you read is what you get, which has ranged from a "not my cup of tea, but I guess not bad" to "weerd".

I'm a little hesitant to give 4 stars to a place that left a piece of hard plastic in my chicken marsala, but I'll give them the benefit of the doubt and call it a fluke. It's in berzerkeley-zone, so keep away from the shadies that walk around.

Naan and Curry are a great low budget bet for Indian food.. there are several locations.. like in SF down the street from City Lights Bookstore - hole in the wall or Berkeley with a cool paint job.  I miss good Indian food when I am at school in San Diego and this is always on my list when I come home on vacation.  Make it your stop for Indian too!
I don't know about you, but I like to eat my greasy Indian food under hella chandeliers next to a thirty-foot tall peach and purple wall that used to have a mural of a woman on a lake.  It's just me.

Pretty cheap prices, but nothing special. I usually go for the Chicken Tikka Masala with a plain naan, and it's super filling. The garlic naan is not that great, so I would recommend just sticking to the regular. They have lots of seating, and also free chai tea!

On the downside, I end up smelling like curry afterwards...

The buffet is well priced. But I didn't really like the food. 

I went for a dinner buffet and didn't end up eating much. The naan was cold, the curry was cold...but you should definitely come here if you don't know your way around Indian food. They give you a fair selection of curries, and there's also dessert!

Been to other Indian restaurant and this one is the best one I've been to.  Indian food is normally pricey but this place offers great food at a reasonable price.

About the food:
We ordered the paneer tikki masala, spinach with chicken (palak ?), garbanzo beans, chicken tikki masala, and some other curry dish, 2 regular naan and 2 garlic naan all for under $50 bucks! which is cheap considering the same amount of food at other restaurants would be much more. The flavors are excellent, spices not too over powering and what I love is that the food comes out HOT! The naan is large and fluffy, great for soaking up the curry.  Garlic naan is literally to die for! They have a really tiny all you can salad bar that is $1 but the cashier said that it was cool if I wanted salad.  SCORE! I guess it was because of our large order. Not cuz I was cute. JK. Salad bar basically only consisted of iceberg lettuce, onion, Indian sauce and chutney. They also have free hot chai! SCORE again! 

About the restaurant decor:

Its basically like a hole in the wall restaurant, the setting use to look like an old ghetto style cafeteria, but they have since remodeled, got new (not really new but second hand) chairs with seat cushions and installed carpets.  Its still a cafeteria setting where you seat yourself after you order and there is an area where you get your own cup and utensils.  They bring you the food.

The bathroom is something else though, its pretty dingy but I think its cuz all the graffitti on the walls which will probably mislead you to think there are gangsters who come here but most of the patrons look like your average student from Berkeley. 

I gave it a -1 star because of the bathroom.

I call BS. 

$7.95 for two 1.5'' balls of ground chicken kafta in luke-warm curry? Rice not included?

Its always a battle between nann-n-curry and house of curries since they are only a block away from each other, so this review is no different. 

House of curries gives you more meat, more curry, bigger naan and better milk tea imo. They recently started giving out free rice pudding for dessert as well, which house of curries doesn't, but I'd imagine it will only be a short while till HOC does something similar. 

Yea, HOC is about 50 cents more or so than naan-n-curry, but that 50 cents goes a long way more. Taste wise they are both pretty similar. I pretty much only order tikka masala and lamb ghobst anytime I eat indian food and both taste good here. 

If naan-n-curry wasn't located so close to house of curries I probably would rate it with more favor, but at about a block distance, why not just go to HOC instead?

I came here for lunch expecting to be satisfied with Indian cuisine. We tried the buffet option they had which was a relatively okay price ~9$ for students 10$ for regular. There was no cheaper price for kids. To my surprise, the buffet option was extremely limited. There was a total of 8 dishes-naan, rice, mixed vegetables, chicken tandoori, chicken tikka masala, chicken palak, chicken curry, and rice pudding (this was their dessert), there was also a small salad bar. Drinks were self-served and they only had water or chai tea. The soda machine was broken. You had to get a jug of water from the refrigerator and the chai tea from a large container. Chai came free and it is sad to say, the chai tea was the best thing they had. The food was not warm. The next batch was expected to come out in an hour or so. The worker tried raising the temperature and it took about 20 minutes to heat up the food. 

Pros: Chai tea was delicious and was free. The chicken tandoori was pretty good, the meat was well-cooked and fell right off the bone. 

Cons: Small selection of dishes. Food was not warm. The boneless chicken in the curry was dry. Cleanliness of water is suspicious. No kid prices so not worth going for younger kids. No service.

All in all, I would not recommend this place to anyone, at least the buffet option. There are plenty of other Indian places in the Berkeley area that are much cheaper and offer better dishes. Their service may be better as well. I don't think I would ever step foot into this restaurant again.

I haven't been back here in about 2 years! One thing I noticed was the decor hand changed...a lot.  I wasn't expecting the food to have changed so much as well. 

I ordered what I order almost every time: chicken tikka masala and aloo gobi.  The chicken tikka masala came out with its familiar radioactive glow but when i took a bite it was bland and utterly tasteless.  This didn't make sense to me because it looked the same as every other time I ordered it! The aloo gobi wasn't too bad (in comparison) but it tasted like a different dish.

I'd rather stick with one of the many other proximate indian restaurants in the East Bay.

No.

I often tell people that I am so sad that this place is as popular as it is because people will come to think that this is actually what Indian food tastes like.

No.  Just don't go here, especially if you're trying Indian food for the first time. Please.  It will taint your opinion of Indian food.

I've been here twice.  I went the second time because I was sure that they were having an off-day the first time I went.  To my disappointment, I was wrong.  They really were just that bad.

The service was bad, the place was dirty (though, I think they have tidied up a bit since when I last went), the food was not good (not representative of Indian food and also just not tasty), and the wait was really long.

I will give it this: 1. The naan is good (but that's a given at an Indian restaurant), and 2. The chai was good (but also a given).

Otherwise, no. No. No. No.

I do not know how this place is still busier then ever, but I want that to stop. It is tarnishing the quality, authenticity, and overall representation of indian food, as we in america know it.

Fine, I'll give it another try. Third times the charm right? Wrong! 
I would always bag on Naan n Curry for having terrible food, and my friends would say that the chicken tikka masala was pretty good. So I gave it another shot.

I walk in and its just how I remember, a restaurant right outta India. It has the dirty carpet, the tattered walls, the restrooms that either made you lose your appitite if you went before eating or throw up if you went after. It looked promising!

I got the buffet at $9 + tax. Not bad for buffet, but still more expensive then Punjabi by Nature, my favorite indian buffet in Berkeley. 

I always start my buffets with a few pieces of with chicken tikka with some onions and lemon on the side. As I said in my last review, it was dry and flavorless, let alone either pinkishly undercooked or overcooked. 

Then I quickly moved onto the chicken tikka masala with naan. Let me start with the naan, in my entire life, eating at over 50+ different indian restaurants, this is the only place that serves their naan stale. Any self-respecting indian restaurant will serve you fresh naan with your order, but not NnC. Next the spaghettio flavored chicken tikka masala. Honestly, this is the worst tikka masala I have ever had, and that's saying a lot. It tasted like some bad fusion between campbells spaghettio's, curry powder, and tomatoe puree. I am not even going to start on the vegetarain dishes. Growing up vegetarian, I have a special place in my palatte for vegetarian food, this place makes me wanna be carnivorous, but then the chicken tikka masala just makes me want to fast.
 
When it comes to mexican food, I trust my friend Juan. When it comes to Korean food, Jang knows what up. And when it comes to Indian food, I would trust an indian, me, as should you. lol

I am not going to just call them out and leave it at that. I will tell you what some good indian food tastes like. I humbly suggest trying the buffet on Center next to Starbucks, called Punjabi by Nature. If you don't want buffet, I highly recommend trying Flavors of India next to Bancroft clothing, which is a jewel among Indian restaurants (get the Butter Chicken with garlic naan, and I promise you won't be dissappointed), and for little more upscale pllace try Taste of the Himalayas.

P.s. One star is being generous!

I'm not a fan of indian food. Not at all. So, this review is not impartial. The Chicken Tikka Marsala was okay. The Garlic Naan was good and the Mango Lassi was mmm...creamy. This place is carb heaven and the bathroom is uber ghetto...there's graffiti and "call Shawndra fo a good time" on the wall, but then again, it is Berkeley...eh...I'd give it another half a star at best.

Since Naan-n-Curry is the among the few halal restaurants which are open till late, the husband and I decided to give it a try. We made our way to the restaurant around 15 minutes before they close, but they happily served us. We were greeted very warmly and told to sit where ever we wanted. While the decoration and ambiance leaves much to desire, we hoped the food would be good. 

The food came fairly quickly. However, we were quite disappointed by the way it tasted. We ordered palak paneer, chicken seekh kebab, chicken tikka masala, kheer and naan.

The palak paneer (spinach and cottage cheese) should have been called "namak paneer" (salt cottage cheese) as it was so salty that I could not have more than one bite. The chicken seekh kebab, on the other hand, was quite delicious. The chicken tikka masala tastes like tomato ketchup with tasteless chunks of chicken. The naan was soft and fluffy and seemed freshly made. Our dessert, kheer, failed to satisfy; while it contained the right ingredients, it has not been cooked properly.

The second time we visited Naan-n-Curry was to try the buffet which is definitely overpriced, even at the "student" price. The buffet menu was rice, nan, chicken korma, aloo gobi, chicken tandoori, chicken tikka masala, mixed sabzi,daal and halwa. 

The husband decided to play it safe and stick to the chicken tandoori and nan. It was fairly standard, albeit being cold.

I decided to be more adventurous and try the chicken korma, aloo ki sabzi and daal with rice. While the chicken korma tasted okay, it was extremely watered down with hardly any chicken pieces. The aloo gobi was not completely cooked, it lacked flavour and was extremely watery. I do not know how anyone can mess up daal but this daal was completely inedible. The rice seemed stale and was quite cold.

The overall experience of our meal was further worsened by 2-3 boys who kept burping extremely loudly every few minutes. I do not know how it is humanly possible to burp that loudly, that often. But, it really put us off and we vowed never to return.

However, in a moment of desperation (read: starvation), we called naan-n-curry for home delivery. Despite calling at 10:45, they agreed to deliver the food, so we ordered chicken tandoori, chicken seekh kebab, chaana masla and naan. The food arrived fairly quickly and it was hot too. They also gave us free chutneys and salad, which was very nice of them. The food was average, with the naan being the major disappointment this time. 

I doubt we will be going to Naan-N-Curry again, though, we may order from them in moments of desperation. Overall rating : 2/5. Visit at your own risk.

Naan had a munch offer that i got. 

eats: tikka masala chicken curry (6ish)
-pretty spicy, only carrots in curry.. 
-no rice came with it, was extra, passed.
-pricey?  rating: 2.45 stars

footnotes:
-urbann turbann had a better deal, rice is included.
-no plans to repeat.

This review is inspiring me to make a yelp list of restaurants that I like, that are contrary to the rest of society. I seem to be on a roll when it comes to raising the average of a supposedly "horrendous" dining experience.

Dear supposedly-awful restaurants: you're welcome.

All I see on this page are 1 star, 2 star with a 3 star sprinkled in here and there. You know what I think of that?

*thumbs down.*

Here's the deal though: I know absolutely nothing about indian food. I like one thing, and one thing only: Chicken Tikka Masala. Oh and the rice. And Garlic Nan cuz who doesn't like garlic nan?

So fine, I like 3 things. And these 3 things taste delicious here to me! Sure, I could go somewhere else and pay twice as much for something twice as better. But why would I even wanna do that if this tastes fine to me, and it's cheaper?

Pshhh. That wouldn't make sense, right?

I'm broke. 2 people can eat here for less than $20. Plenty of room with a nice staff. Enough water pitchers to bring to your table. Food comes out fast. Food is good.

Wait, I just noticed something. Is nan spelled with 2 a's?

This is how little I know about Indian food. Consider yourself warned.

I really enjoyed this place for awhile, until one afternoon when my boyfriend, my brother, my mom and I went to eat lunch. Most of the stuff is DIY, so I got water and tea and whatnot for everyone. The waiter brought the food out, and  it looked pretty good, but as the guy was setting my boyfriend's dish down on the table, he knocked the fork off the table onto the floor. That's not so terrible, right? Just an accident for the waiter to drop a fork - but then, he picked it up off the floor and *put it back on the table next to my bf's plate*, then left to go back into the kitchen. We were all appalled. 

If they will put a *floor fork* back on your table right in front of you, think of what they must be doing to your food in the kitchen!! This incident occurred two years ago - I haven't gone back since, and I don't recommend that you go ever.

Two unfortunate events led me here:
a) Biryani House closed at 10pm
b) Yelp was down, and thus did not deter my visit 

The first portent of imminent failure: the entire, enormous garishly lit restaurant had no signs of life. The dude at the cashier was watching the fan blades move. We were too hungry to heed the warning signals, but it must have registered because I consciously decided not to order meat.

Out came a parade of color: florescent orange paneer tikka masala, heavy with cream, the Velveeta of Indian sauces. Powdery with fake spice, conspicuously lacking in paneer and downright awful to eat cold. Greenish brown okra with thick chunks of tomato and onion, sour and salty. A disc of naan, tasteless were it not for the pretty sprinkling of garlic and parsley on top. Were there leftovers I wouldn't even have taken them home.

Goodbye, forever.

My first time eating Indian food was here, and it was an experience I will never forget.  So much flavor exploding in my mouth!  I love the chicken tikka masala.  Also the garlic naan.  I haven't eaten here in a long time, and I see there have been a lot of bad reviews recently.  It makes me sad if the restaurant is going down... but it will always have a special place in my heart as the restaurant that introduced me to the goodness that is Indian food!

Nope.  Just nope.  Food poisoning once, a fly in the vegetable masala the second time.  Bone shards (what's up with that?  looks to be a common theme in the reviews here) in the lamb/goat dishes.  The place on Telegraph is filthy.

The free tea is cool.  The naans are fine.  

The grease level is too high for my innards, and I have a cast iron gut normally.  Grease and food poisoning are just too risky when potentially paired up.

And did I mention the fly?

The food tastes OK, but they could at least split the bone in the lamb with more care. All those little bits of bone are either just annoying or downright dangerous, depending on how hungry you are.

Also, they could put in a little more effort to clean up their store. The barrier between the kitchen and the dining area, on which they have posted the menus, is rather disgusting.

WHOA! I was definitely suprised with this place. The food was really good and the service was super fast! I don't get why all these people are giving shitty reviews... aww man, I definitely enjoyed myself when I ate here :] and the price was right, too! I'd totally come back!
Naan and Curry is amazing. The Tikka Masala is incredable. It's rediculously cheap.  The only caveat is that you pretty much reek of indian food when you're done.

This is one of my favorite go-to place for chicken tikka marsala. It literally is one of the best I've had. I went recently and they now have a lunch buffet for $8.99 - which isn't a bad deal at all, but I really DON'T RECOMMEND it at all. 

The food was good, but it just wasn't the same as having it freshly made. They have naan in the buffet area too but it's not the same as a nice, hot crispy one. It's actually slightly steamed-like?...

All I have to say is, ORDER individual orders. DON'T get the buffet. Get the chicken tikka marsala w/ a garlic naan, and you're set. You'll leave happy and satisfied!

Just prepare to leave smelling like curry! That smell sticks like no other! I know, it doesn't sound pretty at all, but sometimes it's worth it just for their chicken tikka marsala!

Cheap, good, and DEh-Lih-SEE-yUs.

fresh, hot naan here for miles.
serve yaself, clean up after yaself...pretty simple.

Oh yeah, and I got my new Doorie tip here...good band.
(after, went to Rasputin and got da CD)

I got some potato something, i'm ignant...sorry.
it was spicy, and good, and cheap...
this review got hecka redundant hecka quick

well look at da pic i posted...dat's wut i got

I am so f*cking embarrassed for bringing my non-indian friends here.Naan n Curry's buffet is the worst Indian meal I have had here in the US.I wish I could give them a negative star. 

I wish I could put a banner outside their restaurant that said, ' Don't get ripped off, Naan n Curry does not care about you, there is nothing authentic abt their food.All you are going to end up with is an upset tummy'

The buffet here costs 8.99 which is a dollar more than at Punjabi by nature which is million times better w.r.t the quality of food and the diverse spread of the buffet. Just walk a block away and 'house of curries' smells of good fresh food and great ambiance.

The naan here is rubbery, all the veggie curries (only 3 options) alu palak, watery vegeteble korma and the dal were stale. I had heaped my plate with food and had to just stop eating after a few bites. The non vegetarian food - butter chicken had no chicken in it with the curry base being bland and the tandoori chicken was weird. The only saving grace were the raita and chai, but you can't feed hungry tired students with chai.

We ended up going to house of curries to satisfy our Indian cravings! I wish they close this horrible restaurant.

If you eat here, it only means you don't care and that's exactly what a bad restaurant wants to capitalize on!

I came here with some Pakistani-Muslim UCB friends. It seemed like a very popular lunch and dinner spot. I know a lot of reviewers say it's not exactly a "real" enough Indian-Pakistani restaurant, but the food was still pretty tasty.

I like that they have a location in San Francisco on O'Farrell St. that is open 24 hours, that's crazy! =D

Ah... i was worried for a moment that moving across the bay for college would destroy my habitual visits to Naan n Curry on Irving.  Alas my fears were put to rest when low and behold one was already on the same block as my dorm!  Praise be to the Chicken Tikki Masala gods for granting really good indian food at 2am when the munchies kick-in.  The people are just as cold and mean as in other Naan and Curries which is something I've come to expect so no biggie there.  The food is also pretty much the same fare:  Tasty sauces and little to no meat.  Order lots of rice and naan.

Disappointing. I used to like this place a lot when I was a post-doc at Cal. But visiting last week, I stopped in and it just... wasn't as good.

The naan lacked flavor, the textures were really off with the curries, just didn't nail it. Bottom line: I think there are much better places to go for Indian food in the area, this place fell off...

Eh... the mattar paneer was gross, the restaurant was eerily staffed. 
But the aloo gobi was pretty good, and the naan was too. 
When I was eating it I thought that it would make me sick later on. It didn't though, so that's a plus. ha.

I've been eatting here for years, and the only thing keeping it from five stars is the people that work there.  The cashier is always cranky and condesending, and the bussers are creepy and never fail to hit on my friends and I.  They can also be rude to the males.  But they food is amazing and so affordable.  I went by myself yesterday between classes and spent four dollars and couldn't even finish everything.  The chicken tiki marsala is my favorite, but the eggplant curry is also good. My friends and I go there all the time when we're hungry and broke, and after brushing off the bad service and bad bussers, it's just decent food.
Naan N Curry . . . sigh.  Freezer burned seafood and bland lamb.  Sigh.  At least the place was cheap.  I suppose this is what you get at college towns.  Cheap and low quality food.

Maybe it is because I'm a college student and can't afford more than $10 for dinner...
Or maybe it is because they are open late and I usually don't eat dinner until around 10 pm...
Or maybe even because the name of this place gets right to the heart of my craving/addiction...

But as far as I am concerned this place should be called Naan and Crack

I love Naan N Curry so much I once made a palaak paneer pillow as a present for a fellow NNC-loving friend. Imagine: green felt fringe for the spinach and white POM POMS (!!!) for the cheese. Man. Now I kind of wish I had made another one to keep because I could be cuddling that palak paneer when I miss Naan N Curry most, and that would be quite often. And don't even get me started on the chicken tikka masala, which conceivably could make a nice afghan, but I would probably drool on it, and people tend to frown upon that.

But the naan! And the freeeeeee chai! And the eggplant!!!!!!!! Hold me.

Naan N Curry is legendary for their great food and phenomenally cheap prices. Their chicken tikka masala (CTM) is one of the best around, and they also do a mean tandoori chicken, chana masala, and bengan bartha.

The only difference between this Naan N Curry and the rest are that the prices are about $1 less, and you have to pay before you eat. (Otherwise grubby hippies would eat and run.)

For the money, you cannot go wrong. Their veggie dishes are in the $4-7 range, and with meat you're looking at $6-8. The dishes are oval and maybe 4 inches by 8 inches - so a good size. The naan is great, definitely worth getting extra to munch on well after you are too full to eat. 

The very best thing about this place has to be unlimited chai. My god. I always walk away from there completely caffeinated because I can't get enough. Yum.

This was my 1st time at the Berkeley location, though I've tried Naan N Curry in SF a bunch of times.

Nice, big dining area.  We had a late lunch and not many people were dining at the time.

We got:

Alu naan (stuffed w/ potatoes) $2 - it was pretty good.  Lots of mushy potatoes inside the regular naan.  Pretty good size.

Garlic naan (stuffed w/ ground garlic) $2 - good, pretty good size.

chicken tikka masala $6 - sweet sauce, chicken average in bite size pieces.  Portion on the small side.

chicken palak (spinach cooked w/ chicken) $6 - it's spicy w/ 2 small chicken legs.  I liked it, portion on the small side.

FREE Chai & Tap Water available, help yourself to it behind the salad bar & cashier, get plates, silverware, napkins yourself.  Order at the cashier, food is brought to the table.

My total was $8.70 for chicken palak & garlic naan.  We shared the dishes so I got to try all we ordered.  Credit cards taken.

Naan... Curry... what more do you need!?

Try the chicken vindaloo at full spicy!  You will snot out tears!

We were about to leave Yelp's Sunset showdown and took a recommendation from Oakland Yelper Rachel, she said this place would still be open and the food is great.  Specifically the chicken tikka masala, that's basically butter chicken with white meat. American peoples version of butter chicken, which should be done with dark meat.

On the drive over reviews looked iffy.  Who cares, it's in Berkeley and most likely I'll convince my party to hit up King Pin after wards.  It was a Sunday night so no late night closing, we were lucky to get in here just forty five minutes to close. 

Ordered three dishes and some garlic Naan.  I was surprised that dudes were making the Naan fresh from scratch and you can watch as they make it.  Chicken tikka masala was winner as was the paneer we received.  Tandoori lamb was pretty good as well.  For less than thirty bucks for the three of us, it was excellent stuff (as far as late night food goes) and the service was more than helpful.  

Since this entire area is an student oriented town every single last detail to the restaurant is self serve.  Flatware, napkins, tea, water, it's almost like a cafeteria where you pay and then take care of yourself.  They were still running the buffet, but per reviews, unless you are a broke ass student, it should avoided and for us it was.

You know what's boring, peeps that say.. I am Indian and know what real Indian food is.  Dude.. look at the entree price, it's cheaper than usual pricing.  This is a "hotel", fast, cheap and decent food plain and simple.  I wouldn't use their website as a guide, it trumps up the food and place for no reason.  This is not a typical fine linen five star worthy place.  But it is a 4 star dive.

Crap N Curry or Curry-N-a-Hurry is more appropriate because the food here tastes like Indian fast food (wtf?) crap and it'll make you Crap'N'Curry about an hour later. This place is also dirty, and you feel kinda sticky walking out. Self service for plates and cutlery.

The curry doesn't taste like authentic real curry because you can taste the pasty/powdery essence of the sauces they give you that's well-mixed with cream to deceive your taste buds.

Chicken Tikka Masala - some puny cubes of chicken which are actually dry despite the tidal wave of sauce they are drowned in

Palak Paneer - well, it was supposed to be spinach and cheese, but it looked more like green poo and cheese =(, the paneer was all right, but the spinach was just disintegrated into green likeness of spinach

Aloo Gobi -  spicy curry cauliflower and potatoes - I like heat and this provided good heat for flavor, but a little too much "AHHHH" heat for no good reason =(, cauliflower and potatoes overcooked to a mushy texture (I see a trend here)

Dal - lentil dish that I expected to be flavorful, but was underwhelmed by its strictly... lentil taste - I guess it's supposed to be lentils, but that doesn't mean it should also be flavorful either...

Naan - garlic, onion, whatever naan, it didn't really give me something to write home about but I guess if they managed to mess this up then I would be a sad panda

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

I've frequented Naan N Curry at least 8 times, half from MunchOnMe vouchers, and half for buffet trips. Oh buffets, what would I do without you? Well, I'd weigh 10 pounds less, probably.

You walk in to a very spacious, mellow room with high ceilings and a relaxed feel. To your left diagonal is the cashier, where you pay for your food. If you're here for the buffet ($9 with student ID), head to the back and get grubbin'. If you're here for individual entrees, they give you a number, and you take a seat.

Water and free chai tea are in the back of the restaurant. They also have a sink outside the restroom for you to wash your hands! How nice!

Food comes to you in about 6 - 8 minutes. The waiters aren't the most excited people in the world, but it's aite.

|| F O O D ||

CHICKEN TIKKA MASALA:
- Decently creamy sauce, and a fair amount of chicken. The chicken is sometimes dry.

NAAN: [$1]
- Very thick and fluffeh. Like a cloud of dough!

BUFFET: [$9]
- Things keep changing, so I'm just going to write about what I remember. They have your tandoori chicken (DRY), chicken tikka masala (STANDARD), and some veggies dishes (WHICH I DON'T EAT). There's your stack of naan (CLOUDS), along with a yogurt dessert (THE GOOD STUFF). To your right is a mini bar of sauces and toppings. And to your left is all the cups and plates you could ever wish for.

|| C L O S U R E ||

Fairly consistent food at good prices. Also, it's close to campus! And they have MunchOnMe deals pretty often :3

If I were to rank the Indian places I've eaten at, it'd go:
1) Currylicious (in Oakland)
2) Indian Flavors Express
3) Mount Everest Restaurant
4) Shalimar
5) Naan N' Curry
6) House of Curries

No words can describe what I want to say. I'm dumbfounded.

10) House of Curries (College)
11)  Kabana (Great food loses massive points for racially based treatment of customers)
12) Tandoor Kitchen
13) Khana Peena (the one on Shattuck, absolute trash, avoid) 
14) Indus Valley Restaurant (literally serves frozen vegetable curries)

**Now if I called Khana Peena Shattuck trash, then you can imagine how the following are...yeah...these don't deserve to even be ranked**

House of Curries (Durant)
Naan N Curry

The first time I came here years ago, the cashier charged me for my meal twice because he realized I'd dozed out and forgot I paid him the first time. I didn't go back for awhile after I realized that.

Then I went back and this is what I have to say.

If you ever want to get obese, DON"T DO IT HERE. GO TO MCDONALDS, you'll be much more satisfied. This shit is PURE FAT, with NO TASTE. It's fucking disgusting. At least Mcdonalds has taste!  It makes me sad that people even go here. No wonder I was so lonely when I went to Berkeley.

This place opened in the middle of my undergrad career and it changed my life...until I had real Indian food. It IS quick, I'll give it that, and has that chaotic, bare bones mess hall feel that is accidentally evocative of eateries actually located in India.

Charles L. couldn't have said it better. It's curry in a hurry. Of all the times I've been here, I've only been mildly pleased, but never impressed. If you're looking for quality, head elsewhere. Otherwise, if you're looking for a simple meal just to fill your stomach, this place will suffice. Items of note:

Chicken Tikka Masala: I don't care what people say. I do not like this dish that much. It's more sauce than chicken and the chicken loses its taste from drowning in it.

Dal: It's a simple, cheap dish that is nothing special. I can make this at home.

Naan: This is the one redeeming factor. I love the garlic naan here and the plain naan is good too, but only when it's freshly out of the kitchen.

Rice: I do like the rice here.

Chai: It's definitely more water than chai. Get the thick mango lassi instead.

I finally tried the buffet here because I realize it's more cost efficient and you get to try more dishes. If you get 1 dish and a side of naan or rice to go with it, it'd come out to around $9 anyway.

Shortly after arriving in the Yay Area after a several-year hiatus, I headed up to Berkeley to hang out with my friend in Rockridge.  We then took a tour of Berkeley.  

It was lunch time, and we wanted to get something quick.  I'm from the boonies, so I was up for anything out of the ordinary---so, when I saw an Indian restaurant we had to go.  

Made it here and went for the lunch buffet.  The chicken tikka masala was awite.  The curry I had was ho-hum-dee-hum.  What can ya say, it was cheap.  If I was in the mood to gorge, I woulda totally taken advantage of the food overload, but on this day, I only felt like about a plate and a half.

It was fairly priced, but the food didn't do it for me.

My friend loves this place and I must say this review is basically for their prices because I dislike most curried food.

I ended up getting the Naan Bread with butter for one dollar exactly, and it was HUGE. A massive two pieces the size of pizzas. The butter flavor was subtle and lost after the first half of piece number one.

I dipped it in my friend's dishes sauce, but the sauce was so spicy after the second dip or so I gave up and grabbed a water.

So yes, Plus 5 stars for cheap as heck, butter bread, but minus 3 stars for not changing my mind about Indian food.

I would avoid this restaurant at all costs.  I feel the need for a tetanus shot after having lunch here.  They use the worst quality lamb the can find and don't even take the time to trim the fat.   All of the curries were covered in a pool of oil.  The restaurant is just filthy, I feel bad for the employees who have to use it regularly, I just held it until I got back to the office.

---BUFFET REVIEW ONLY---

Keep in mind that Naan N Curry probably doesn't make the most authentic Indian food, but their newly (to me) introduced buffet is a pretty good deal if you're hungry and need a curry fix.  For what you would normally pay for a single dish, you can get yourself unlimited chicken tika masala, lamb and spinach, lentils (there are about 3 other dishes that I can't remember), rice pudding, naan, rice, and of course hot chai.  I'm unaware if they rotate dishes everyday, but that's what they offered the night we went.  Not too shabby for $7.99.  Buffet specials run daily from 11:30-2:30 and 6:30-9:30.  

Let's talk food:
- All the dishes are pretty standard.  My favorite is the chicken tika masala - Naan N Curry makes a decent version, but again, probably not the most authentic.  I enjoyed the lentils and the other vegetable dish that they served, but the lamb and spinach didn't quite do it for me.  It was obvious that the naan was not prepared fresh.  It was a bit dense, lacking the crispy bubbles and the fluffiness that makes naan so deliciously fun to eat.     

It's pretty much self-serve, especially if you're getting the buffet.  You're required to gather all your dishes, utensils, cups, and libations.  Staff is not rude, but not particularly friendly.

If you're looking for AYCE Indian fare on the cheap, Naan N Curry is your one-stop shop.

Came here on a monday night for dinner. Ordered the jumbo burrito, which was big and good and cheap. The food came fast. Only issue was when we ordered a pitcher of margaritas. I was almost done with my giant sized burrito by the time the pitcher arrived. And I ordered it to be blended, but it came with chunks of ice. The slow service actually dropped the rating 2 stars, so you can see the aggravation for waiting, and waiting for something horrible. Cute waitress though

Mario's La Fiesta was a great family restaurant. Their super burritos were amazingly delicious. You definitely felt comforted and excited as you walked in. 

However, sadly, the owners retired to hang out more often with their grandchildren, which is amazing and cute.

BUT I LOST MY FAVORITE MEXICAN RESTAURANT IN THE PROCESS! NOT COOL. PERIOD.

Sorry grandchildren, but we need yo grandparents back. 

Remy's isn't bad. It just promotes the culture of bad Mexican food in Berkeley, that's all. It also encourages that silly socal-itude of you Norcal-ers don't know how to make a burrito or a taco. Sad.

Prices have been raised by a $1 for everything, which wouldn't be so bad, except that the food just doesn't taste as amazing. For chile verde, I don't mind spicy, but when I see green sauce, I want it to taste green, not spicy like any other sauce, but green. Plus the pork wasn't as tender. I love me some delicious chile verde, but it's not a perfect burrito without that tender pork, that just falls apart in your mouth.

Ordered supreme chicken burrito with no beans. I was able to eat it but I would rather walk a few blocks down and get a good burrito from Gordo's. The place was deceivingly bigger in the inside than expected and it was nice that the waitress immediately brought us chips and salsa without charge (the way it should be!) :) They have 3 flat screens, all with no sound but it seems like a good place to go watch a game. Wouldn't go back though.

Berkeley has lost a piece of its culinary history with the loss of Mario's...
Remy's is the new incarnation of Mario's La Fiesta which I used to eat at very regularly.  I went here the other day deciding to give the new place a try, it was disheartening. 

As others have mentioned, the menu is completely different, the variety of delicious table top salsas is gone, the wonderful soup that accompanied any combination plate is gone, the combinations in general are gone and the cooking is not as good under the new management.  As of yesterday, they did not have fountain soda so don't expect any refills. 

Other changes include the removal of the children's artwork display.  Now there is an ugly, out of place looking bar there, a flat screen tv above the entrance and in general a lot of the character of the place seems to have disappeared.  

I know this place has been around for a very long time and many, many people have found coming back to Mario's a requirement for return visits to Berkeley.  Unfortunately, that's gone.  At least we have the memories :-)

Like so many here, I mourn the passing of La Fiesta, but honestly, I was anxious to support Remy's as their heir apparent.  I like that the place looks the same, with that great furniture and decor. The first time I ate there post-Mario, they served us two salsas, both very good, hot crunchy tortilla chips, and the flautas (my all-time favorite La Fiesta dish) were pretty similar to Mario's. Alas, each subsequent visit seemed to be another spiral down the tube. I ate there for what will be the last time on Sunday evening:  the one salsa served was nasty, looking and tasting like the bottom of your sink after you've prepared some onions and tomatoes and something vaguely green for another dish. The chips were paper thin and flavorless, clearly no longer made in-house. The flautas were a travesty. Cardboard tasting tortillas, one filled with processed-tasting cheese that doesn't really melt so much as it just gets mushy, the other featured something that was supposed to be chicken but smelled and looked more like Purina Fancy Feast, and both were coated with a watery, tasteless guacamole. Ugh. Not fit for the compost heap. Only the Dos Equis was the same as in the once great Las Fiesta. I well understand Mario wanting to retire and his family not wanting to carry on, but whoever the current owners are they ought to be run out of town for taking over a great institution and turning it into a rip-off establishment.

I return to Remy's over and over again because the food is good, the servers are excellent (always making sure we have enough chips and salsa, making suggestions  when we're unsure of what we want, timely service). Always leave satisfied when I go to Remy's.

I was a longtime (20 yrs) patron of Mario La Fiesta, the restaurant which preceded Remy's. That restaurant had the best flautas, salsas, and tacos. La Fiesta closed down (according to Mario himself) due to lack of business at the current site (now Remys). If you are going to judge Remys you must judge it in its own regard, not looking at La Fiesta. I tried the flautas and they seem quite tasteless, compared to other restaurants. The meat is seasoned with some flavor which does not really enchant me. The same goes for the ground beef tacos. The salsa is an uber-chunky one which is very so-so.
If you live in the area Remys is certainly worth trying to develop your own opinion. I think most La Fiesta patrons will be disappointed. I prefer El Burro and El Patio(Fremont). I do not plan on coming back to Remys, unlike my frequent trips to La Fiesta.
Man, I used to love this place, but now that it's "Remy's" it seems to have lost something. The guacamole was rancid and I think the prices went up. Bean and cheese burrito plus guacamole = $10!!!

Wow... just utterly terrible. Disappointing in pretty much every way possible.
Went here for Cinco de Mayo with a couple friends.. expecting to be coming to Mario's for their amazing quac, sangria and food! Come to find it has closed down and become "Remy's"... we were disappointed, but figured what the hell, may as well give it a shot. 
Let me break it down for you...

Menu:
completely changed, and has very limited OVERPRICED options

Service: 
absolutely terrible! i don't think i can't remember the last time i left that low of a tip. There were a handful of waitresses working and it was not very crowded, yet they somehow managed to take foreverrrr or just forget in general to do basic things such as get us water, napkins etc (i finally went and got them myself).  AND to top it all off, we were not even close to being finished with our meal and the waitress slams the bill down on our table.. talk about rude. 

Food:
The guacamole was flavorless, watery, and probably 75% tomatoes.
I ordered stead fajitas that came out COLD, dry and flavorless.
My friends that i went with hated their food as well. 

Booze:
No sangria :(
The margaritas were the only decent thing about the entire meal. Thank god we all got a little buzzed.

TERRIBLE FOOD!!!!!! Went looking for Mario's and found out that they retired and this place now has a new owner. We wanted to give it a try and was hoping to find the same wonderful food! However what a disappointment. The food tasted like it was prepared with rancid oil! The salsas and the soups are gone! The entire ambiance has changed. We will never return and do not recommend this place. Miss the old Mario's, hope they enjoy their retirement!!!!

I never review a restaurant when it first opens. You've got to give them time to work out some of the issues that will naturally come up.  The first thing I noticed about Remy's is how nice the wait staff is.  The food was in some cases exactly like Mario's and in a few cases entirely different.  The Burritos, in particular, are excellent.  I have not gone through the entire menu, but I see no reason not to try.  They have a good selection of bottled beers, and the prices are reasonable on both the beer and the food.  The actual restaurant is specious, clean and laid out very well.  Since I've gone there numerous times now I can safely say that I would go there again and have no  problem recommending Remy's to my friends.

If there was anything I might regret it would be no longer getting the soup
with a plate.  But that will not stop me from eating at Remy's.

Mario's was a great restaurant. Remy's is everything Mario's wasn't.

Remy's has bland, commercial salsa. It tastes like the salsa you could expect from any commercial chain restaurant like El Torito or Jose's. It's made of pureed tomato sauce, garlic, and cilantro. There isn't the spicy kick Mario's used to have with its two salsas.

Remy's tries too hard to be cool and attract younger people, so it's more of a bar than a restaurant. The food is overpriced (everything is more expensive than Mario's charged), and it's NOT WORTH IT. Don't bother paying extra for rice and beans. I took one bite of the refried beans and knew instantly that they were from a can. I could even name the brand because of how overly salty and unimpressive they were. I was disgusted. Any restaurant that serves canned refried beans is NOT authentic, and it sends a serious flag about the quality of food you'll be eating. Beans are such a staple to Mexican cuisine that using canned beans sinks a whole meal--burritos, nachos, tortas.

I was honestly hoping for good food, but then Remy's just sort of poops on all your hopes, throws it on a plate, and serves it to you--and charges you extra. I ordered a torta, but once the beans were canned, I knew it wasn't a good sign. The flavor wasn't there. I felt like I were eating some wanna-be Mexican torta made at a Safeway Deli.

My boyfriend ordered the nachos. The really sad thing? The nachos at Raleigh's, a pub, are better. 

Forget this place. It's bad. Simply awful. Both of us vowed to never go back after that experience. Canned refried beans at any Mexican restaurant are unforgivable. Don't waste your money.

I haven't seen all too many Mexican restaurants around the UC Berkeley campus so Remy's seemed a good bet to satisfy my Mexican food craving. I ordered the traditional burrito with carne asada, black beans, rice and cheese. Overall the burrito was just average. It lacked a distinct flavor as all the elements inside seemed to just mush together rather than compliment each other. I found myself adding the salsa that came with the chips to give some extra flavor to it. I'll give this place two stars because the waitress was really friendly, and almost everything on the menu is wicked cheap. My group and I had a good time but it wasn't because of the food.

The restaurant looks cute and there is a nice patio area. That is the only nice thing I can say about this sorry, so-called Mexican Restaurant. My combination lunch consisted of the following: a mound of shredded lettuce (that's it) for "salad", a watery, soggy blob of batter sitting in a puddle of water with a teaspoon of watery red sauce on top for a "chile relleno" and a lukewarm "taco" with bland, pale, grey colored ground beef, the same shredded lettuce, and some weird grated cheese. Once I ordered, the food came right away-MICROWAVED, frozen food, say you?

I've been here twice....and both times they were just meh. 

First visit: I ordered the flautas...and they tasted bland.

Second visit: I came for $2 tacos and horchata. The tacos were a decent size, but they were bland (what a surprise). I was hoping the horchata would make up for it...but alas, it definitely tasted watered down.

My friend and I went here today for dinner.  Friend ordered the carne asada tacos, and i ordered the shrimp burrito, with side of rice and refried beans.

Friend ate beans and rice only because the 'carne asada' was not carne asade. It was like dehydrated flakes of dog meat  or dog food. I tasted it and it tasted very suspicious.  Like, not beef. I dont know. And there was no flavor or marinade on the meat at all.  We are both seasoned carne asada eaters but this was different and gross. We tried to eat just the taco shells only, but those tasted store-bought and also like they were cooked in month-old oil.
Friend left both tacos on the plate without eating them.

As for my shrimp burrito (with rice and beans inside)... first of all the shrimp were pre-cooked SALAD SHRIMP.  Bay shrimp.  I order shrimp burritos all the time and have never ever ever ever had them made with salad shrimp.  And very few shrimp too.  You cant use prawns? Or even 21/30 shrimp? but salad shrimp??

Next, one of my bites of burrito (where the refried beans were inside it) I chomped on a small piece of shattery something like glass in my teeth.  I spit it out into a napkin. Assuming it was a piece of glass, or maybe sand from the shrimp....?

But then I took a big bite of the side of refried beans, and again, chomped on an even bigger piece of glass.  I had to run to another table and grab extra napkins from it and spit out glass in the napkins then sat there rinsing the glass out of my mouth with my water and spitting it into another empty glass.

Gross huh?!  I know!  But i was not about to swallow glass. It definitely came from the refried beans.

Waitress never came to our table, otherwise we would have told her about both of our dinners.
But in fact we had to go up to the bar and ask for our check because we had waited so long for the check.  Had to wait a long time to pay before we could leave (was not busy in there at all).

Then someone else (manager?) came and took our plates.  Did they not notice my friends plate and 2 full tacos on it still?  And mine had spit-out food, mostly un-eaten burrito; and obviously food had been spit into a water glass?  I mean, obviously something was wrong with both of our dinners.... but they just took our plates away and took our money and didnt say a word.

I'm still freaked out over what the shattery glass was in my teeth or whatever. It was like small-pebble sized and glass like.  Two of them, and both came from the refried beans.

Would have been nice to have had a waitress who checked on us, so that we could have told her there was something majorly wrong with both of our dinners.

We vowed not to go back again ever.  An hour later, after getting home, we were both hungry because we never did actually eat enough for it to be 'dinner'.
Awesome, beautiful restaurant however they NO longer have bottomless MIMOSAS

Went here for Cinco de Mayo for the first time and I was pleasantly surprised. Got a burrito with the Mexican marinated Tofu and it was actually really good! Tofu in a burrito was a little bit different, but in a good way. Got a pitcher of their raspberry margarita's which were good but then they also gave us a free pitcher of strawberry margarita's because they messed up someone else's order and those were awesome! Getting a free pitcher can pretty honestly make me feel positive towards a lot of places but the food was actually good!

Being a life long mexican food fanatic, I always search for the absolute best restaurant whenever I relocate to a new area. Remy's is just f*cking amazing... Definitely the most authentic and best tasting mexican food to be found in Berkeley. Their items are all delicious and their helpings are very generous!!

Remy's is now what Mario's used to be after the founding owners retired. It's still a family owned business and there are regulars who hang out at the bar here. That's what I like about it. Even though it's in a location that is not as visible as their last location, it has more seating and an outdoor patio. The food is just the same. It's overpriced, but not if you consider the gigantic portions. The burritos are loaded with guacamole and sour cream. There are two kinds of masas, one of blue corn and one of yellow corn. Many of the items here come atop a mountain of shredded cabbage, which is perfect if you want something to calm the fire. There are two complimentary salsas that come with corn tortilla chips, both are pretty spicy, I must say. The salsas and chips are unlimited. The agua frescas are only $2 for a pint. The service is just a little bit slow, but definitely very friendly.

I love this place!  Whenever I am craving Mexican, I immediately want to come here.  Their grilled burritos are awesome (and cheap!).  I'm always looking for an excuse to be in their neighborhood and drop in for some delicious food :)

Used to be a huge fan of La Fiesta for over 30 years. Went at least 2x / week. Were so bummed that it closed, and went to new place in first opening week.  Read some Yelp reviews from a couple of haters in September, and we had not been back until October. But after two thumbs up from the awesome dad / son team at Lhasa Karnak, we tried it again.

Wow! The new Remy's rocks!  Been there 3x now and going again today. I got Huevos Rancheros and it was nearly identical to old La Fiesta, thank you! Wifey is a vegetarian and got something old La Fiesta never would have dreamed of:  Portobello burrito and it was huge & tasty. Thought it could never be true, but Remy's equals and in some ways surpasses old La Fiesta: seafood, shrimp, fajitas, lots of veggie options and about 10 beers ON TAP!  You can't go back, and Mario and Rosalinda are the kindest people anywhere, but please visit Remy's - they are trying new things and rocking it. Plus big screens for soccer and sports.

I've eaten at la fiesta, mario's, and now here -- all times i've been to Remy's i've enjoyed all of my food, had good chips and salsa, and haven't had any complaints about service at all. they also have a big selection of cold beers, bottomless mimosas on the weekend, and big margaritas :) :) i love the burritos, fish tacos, and enchiladas so far -- 

I wasn't going to say anything, but sorry i'm not sorry to all the hyper emotional and sensitive people who probably caught Remy's on a bad day, ever heard of letting a new business figure out the kinks?
This isn't some corporate, big chain restaurant where things go streamlined out of a handbook, which our city should be appreciative of. I'm really impressed by all the food critics who are dining on telegraph, looking for things to nit pick -- They are doing a fantastic job regardless of trying to adapt a new restaurant into an already established restaurant space, with everything already designed and customer expectations of free soup and whatnot.  Go get a dozen mimosas, and two fish tacos while you're at it, and take a couple of deep breaths. Everything is going to be okay.

I went here this past Taco Tuesday with friends.
$2 tacos and $3 pints--not bad.

We were quickly seated in a middle area which perfectly fit the 6 of us. We were given menus, and the waitress quickly rushed off without offering to take our drink order.

This was my first time eating here, so I quickly opened the menu.
The tacos here are a lot bigger than what you expect at a typical Taco Tuesday event.
They have a large selection for tacos which include:

pollo asado
carne asada
shrimp
fish
al pastor
mushrooms

It took the waitress a good 10 minutes to return to get our drink orders, and another 10 minutes to return with chips, salsa, and the offer to finally take our orders.

The chips were crazy salty! There was a thick layer of salt covering the majority of the chips in the basket so we spent some time dusting it off. Perhaps they were from the bottom of the bin/bag. Moreover, the chips were cold which made them less appetizing.

I ordered 4 tacos (2 al pastor, 2 shrimp) and a pint of Fat Tire.
Here at Remy's, they give you the option of soft or crunchy tacos. I got mine crunchy style.

A good 15 minutes later our tacos arrived. However, tell me why only 2 of the plates came with salsa and the other 4 the salsa was undoubtedly absent. The waitress ran off too quickly for us to even ask for more. Remy's was not that busy and there were definitely points where I caught the waitress walking slowly, trying to make themselves busy, or just absent-mindedly wandering among the tables not noticing what customers needed.

What Remy's needs is a change in pace and a good customer service development day for some of it's employees. Mexican food, especially tacos, does not take that long to make.

I could eat here again, but Remy's you need to step up your game.

Until next time, happy eating!

Football Monday!

Came here after the Bears smashed a team in football so it was like 30% off. 
Literally paid like 3 bucks for a pretty decent grilled burrito
They have some pretty awesome deals and two of my floormates work here as waitresses. Nice cozy environment

Remy's is just what we were looking for:  a neighborhood hangout with great food and drinks.  
Our favorites:  the grilled shrimp tacos, enchiladas, burritos, huevos rancheros, yum!

They have great decor - stucco and painted tiles, wood beams.  a fabulous wood bar with comfortable bar stools, a ton of great beers on tap (lagunitas, anchor steam, blue moon, ah, my husband would remember more beer names than I can, sorry!), sangria, margaritas, mojitos, and more.  they also have unlimited mimosas on the weekends for $10.  so much fun. 

We love to come here to watch a Cal or pro football game or just to hang out with the excellent staff who are all very friendly.  They always have consistently great service.  

There's a good mix of authentic Mexican dishes, as well as the 

Check out the patio seating, too.  Oh wait, save us a table!

My husband and I have been looking for "real" Mexican food since we moved from San Diego!  We found it!  They use the right tortillas, the refried beans taste the way they are supposed to!  We are so happy!  After a one year dry spell of shitty imitation Mexican, we finally feel at home.

I'd say the re-incarnation of Mario's as Remy's is hitting it's stride now by faithfully reproducing some of Mario's classics - so I'm upping my rating to four stars. The salsa I had today for lunch was fresh, chunky, and with the beautiful heat balance that I remember fondly from the previous location. I regret the lack of two different salsas on the table,  one chunky and medium hot, the other smooth and super hot. The soup was 'spot on' in flavor to the old recipe that I've enjoyed there for 30 years - I beg Remy's not to stray from that soup recipe. It's a fantastic Berkeley culinary touchstone and will draw me back for more regular meals at Remy's as long as it's maintained.

Typical cheap mexican food. Almost everything here's pretty meh..
I mainly come for cheap booze. $3 pints on Tuesday, $3.50 margaritas on Thursday. They have good salsa and it comes complimentary with a basket of chips, which are perfect for drunchies. I've come for tacos a handful of times and the only one I find worth getting is the shrimp..though they've definitely been skimping on the shrimp lately.

Service is hit or miss..ranges from really good to really bad. 

If you want really good mexican food, go to Cancun on Allston.

I hadn't been to Berkeley for 25 years or more, and asked a policeman were to eat and he pointed up the street to Remy's.

The outside was attractive and clean. The staff were friendly and I liked the atmosphere. I ordered the Super Burrito with carne asada, no sour cream or guacamole, but with pico de Gayo and red sauce on top. I had a coke and tortilla chips.

They gave me exactly as ordered a huge burrito with lettuce on the side. It was excellent like home cooking. The bill came to only $9.18 and I left a $2.00 tip.

The bathroom was clean and I liked the mission theme and Mexican photos on the walls.

I was surprised, I wasnt a fan of Mario's but this is pretty good. The carnitas wasnt too dry, the cheesesteak was surprisingly awesome, beers are 4$ a pint and they have a good selection plus some 2.50$ options.

Good Mexican food and impressive beer selection. I go there quite regularly and everytime I run into someone who either used towork or used to eat at raleigh's. Good people great atmosphere. Owner is great.

Dankest Burritos in Town, and I've tried them all. Cancun has the best burritos overall, but this is the place to go for the diet breaking, stomach churning, cinco de mayo dancing, mariachi music bumping, mexican goodness all rolled up in a soft tortilla!

Order a Grilled Burrito w/
-Al Pastor or Chorizo (not an option on the menu, but they will make it for you ;)
-Get the refried beans
-Add sour cream
-Grab a Bohemia Beer!

Price is very good too. only $5.50 for the burrito and $4 for the imported Mexican beer!!!

P.S. Peach Margarita are worth the embarrassment of ordering a girly drink!

Came here on a lark, and I can't wait to go back.  I hate to admit it, but my meal here was heads above those at my usual Mexican food spot, Café Durant.  And Remy's has sangria!  

The service was slow and the friendly staff apologized profusely, but sipping the sangria and snacking on thick chips with some sweet salsa in the cozy wooden booth, I really didn't mind.  The vibe at first is very family-friendly Cal-themed sports bar, definitely not home-y like my dear Café Durant, but the high-backed benches do a lot to give you some privacy on a date.  Still, you never run out of things to look out at, and to listen to.  With a full restaurant and multiple TV sets on, the sound level rose a tad high on occasion.  And the room was never warm enough to warrant taking our coats off.  

But when the food finally came, oh man, was it good -- no, great!  And it was pretty darn cheap, too, considering we had to get a box to take some home.  This is an excellent place to eat on a budget when you're in the mood to slow down, spend some time, and appreciate real cooking.

Ok, so the service was a TAD slow, but when the food and drinks came, WHO CARED? Oh man, I was so impressed. 4 of us drank and ate ourselves silly for 50 bucks. I will be back over and over again. So good! Make sure to get their beer bloody mary. Michelada(sp?)

People here are just haters, you gotta learn to let go of the old, and welcome the new; what's done is done, Mario's will not be coming back. All these people talk about it being overpriced, but damn, try living in the downtown area (in terms of food, it truly does suck being a student in the downtown area =/ ); for the amount of food you get at Remy's it's awesome.

That being said, I honestly think that Remy's is much better than Mario's, but do take that with a grain of salt, as the only thing I ever ordered at either place was the nachos. Remy's nachos are INCREDIBLE (much more so than Mario's), and the amount you get for the price is fantastic! I visit Remy's ATLEAST once a week with my roommates who also absolutely love their nachos. I've gotten mine with Al Pastor, Carnitas, and   Pollo Asado, my roommates always get Pollo (shredded) and Carne Asada. Their meat is so good!! And be sure to get em with black beans, for a while there, I ordered nachos with refried, which was great, but then I suddenly got curious and ordered them with black beans, and that just took it to a whole new level.

There is always that hit or miss factor, so be sure to try it a couple times before completely chucking it out the window.

The only thing I would complain about is the fact that they ALWAYS have a different salsa (in the beginning when they give you chips and salsa) which might be cool for a lot of people, but I really hate how sometimes its a salsa thats craaaaazzzyyy good and then the next time I go, I'm all excited to have the salsa again, and it's something mediocre. oh, well, get the fuck over it, right?

Remy's is a great new Mexican restaurant in Berkeley, just off Telegraph near the Cal campus.  The menu is full of authentic, tasty Mexican dishes and they have a extensive beer list (full of hard to find Mexican beer).

On my first trip, I had the green mole chicken dish.  I am a huge mole fan and judge the quality of a Mexican restaurant by their mole.  This item did not disappoint... full of unique flavors and spices.  I had never had a *green* mole before and was very happy with my choice.  Remy's also uses high quality chicken and isn't trying to bury bad meat with over-powering sauce.  The green mole had a great mix of different ingredients and spices and will soon be a favorite item coming out of the kitchen.

As a side dish, I also had some black beans with bacon.  Somewhat basic, but it tasted really good and there was a healthy volume of thick bacon in there.  Was a great add on to the meal.

Remy's is located in Mario's old location, familiar to many folks in Berkeley, just up from Telegraph on Haste Street.  I've been told that the menu will soon be expanding from its initial form, to include even more traditional Mexican recipes.  

Simply put, this is not another Chevy's or "choose your combo" Mexican fast food place.  Remy's is a high-quality, authentic, friendly Mexican restaurant that you'll grow to love as much as I already do!

I'm a fan of "mediocre Mexican food" as we typically have it in restaurants here in California, and Remy's is good in that category for sure. Glad it's here, and on a recent sunny Saturday we were able to sit outside while sports fans were inside at the bar watching tv 'n drinking. 

On our first visit I had a non-Mexican entree, a Mexi/Philly cheesesteak. It was darned good except for the spicy mayo (i asked for non-spicy but that request got lost somewhere) being a tad too hot and some of the meat being unchewable. But the flavors were fantastic as was the roll it was served on, so we can overlook the deficiencies. 

We'll be back!
Below average Pad Thai with tough shrimp and sullen service are a dynamic duo of dealbreak.

The best place in that quite-creepy Northside Asian Ghetto. Much more quiet and less creepy thant the other part since it's the only restaurant in the lower level. The outside tables are almost cool to stay sitted for a while (not that much outside sitting area around campus).

The food is OK. Decent selection of classic ready-to-go thai food. The collection of classics to order is also here: Pad-Thai, Pad Se-Ew, Curries... Nothing astonishing but good enough for the price.

Same selection and prices that Jasmine Thai on Euclid but the outside seating is a plus.

Mmmm curries! Loved this place for the very quick meals and the ability to get a few curries haha. I used to get the beef and the chicken curry and mix bits of it with my rice. GOOD STUFF!

Wouldn't say there's a whole lot in terms of service, ambiance, etc etc but... as an undergrad, the place was great! =)

I wonder why no one has reviewed this yet. It seems busy during weekday lunches.  They have great lunch specials and provide hefty amounts of each item.  I appreciate the little salad, even if it only has one prawn.  I walked by someones fresh pad se ew and it smelled so good. I'll come back for sure to their list of specials, including crispy duck and crispy chicken.  There is even a variety of vegetarian and seafood specials.

This place was better than I thought. I actually couldn't decide on what to get from the menu. I wanted to get a curry dish. For me, I need to know if I would be a repeat customer, based on either the pad thai or pad see ew, since these are the default dishes. So I ordered the pad see ew and was pleasantly surprised. It was good, Even took the leftovers home, so the portions were big. I wish I would have gotten a thai iced tea, but next time. I think I discovered a new lunch spot for myself.

Amazing broad menu...

I had Ped Yang Roasted Duck with Spinach over rice, for $7.25 for lunch! 

Ding! Ding! Ding!

And $2 for Thai Ice Tea (which really should never cost more than that!)

The forgotten member of the northside asian ghetto family - tucked below on street level.  Not the most spectacular Thai, but for speed, convenience, and taste, it'll do the trick.

When I first discovered it, it wasn't mealtime so I picked up a thai iced tea.  Good as any I've had.

Later had a pad kee mow for dinner.  Was freshly cooked when I ordered it, and took less than 5 minutes.  At quaint Thai places, I'm often left feeling like a dried-up sea sponge in the aftermath of overseasoning and over-MSG-ing (see my dismal Jasmine Thai review), but this was seasoned the way I like it - not too sweet, and not too salty.  The main shortcoming: way skimped on the number of "prawns".  But the overall portion was HUGE, so I was happy enough.

Sidenote - ChiangLai is a Chinese name, so you're obviously not getting 100% authentic Thai here.  But Thai cuisine is heavily influenced by Chinese cuisine, so I suppose it's fitting.

Coming in, I had really no idea what to expect. The first thing stands out about this place is how many freaking menus there are. Every wall you look at, there are at least two menus, most of which are erasable markerboards.

Secondly, there doesn't seem to be one designated person working the front to take orders and take food out, just one lady who cooks and one other who does I don't know what, but she's usually not visible from the customer area.

After you decide what to order, either from what seems to be the printed, permanent menu or from one of the specials boards, it takes a little while to get one of the two ladies' attention. The cook lady who took my order was nice, though.

I ordered the Pad Woonsean (alternately spelled Phad Woon Sen, at least online) for $7.95 for dinner. It took about 15 minutes or so to come out, but like the other North Asian Ghetto places, they bring your food/utensils out to you and you can get your own tea and water.

The food itself was pretty good, not too oily compared to Thai Basil. It tasted pretty good, had a lot of ingredients (chicken, small shrimp, bell peppers, onions, thin noodles), and was brought together nicely by its sauce. It was enough portions-wise.

The sanitation was a little questionable. When bringing out my food, they put the eating utensils directly on the table, which didn't seem all that clean. But overall, this a solid place to eat if you're willing to wait a bit and deal with the presentation issues.

I eat here a lot since I live practically next to it. This place can either be really good or just meh. It all depends on what time you go, what you order, and who cooks it.. The pad thai here really isn't that great at any time of day, but the crispy catfish more than makes up for it. If you come for dinner and the bigger lady cooks it for you, it's AMAZING. It's still good when the other lady makes it, just not the same.

The papaya salad is also really good. They have it on the menu with their BBQ meat stuff, but if you order papaya salad when they're not busy and get it as a full order (it's not on the menu as such, but you can still get it) it's the best papaya salad in Berkeley. They even add the little dried shrimp that a lot of other places don't seem to use. If you watch while they're making it, you can see the lady pounding the papaya in a giant antique mortar. 

Remember, the timing is crucial. If you come here when it's packed with students looking for anything cheap to shove into their mouths, you're not gonna get anything special. Go when it's deserted, which means basically after 3:00. The prices stay the same but the food is so much better.

It's a travesty that there is no good Thai food on the northside of UC Berkeley.

The curry here is passable, but the Pad Thai has this funny aftertaste...a bit like the inside of a hose or something. ChiangLai is much better for dinner, when the prices don't change from lunch but they actually cook your food instead of serving you the pre-made stuff (you can order made-to-order food for lunch too, but they seem to discourage it because it takes a lot longer).

They do have a nice patio, which is less crazy then the upper part of the ghetto.

I eat Thai food once a week or so, and this place is the closest to my office and my house...and I go here about once a semester.

This Thai place is great for their red curry dishes!  I'm surprised that there's only 6 reviews for this place. I used to eat here when i went to Cal in '98-2000 timeframe. Back then, i would get the cheap combo meal from their pre-cooked food trays.  This past friday, hubby and i ordered off their menu.  True that the first 2 things we  tried to order, they didn't have the ingredients to make.  But once we hit available dishes, it was jackpot.  

Hubby ordered the Red Curry Crispy Catfish and it was delicious.  The catfish was fried to perfection and sauce  so tasty.  I ordered the duck and string bean meat combo.  I liked how they served the duck boneless and the other dish was very good as well.  Either I didn't remember how good the place was, or I used to scarf down the food too fast to go back to coding, but I'm real glad to have rediscovered this restaurant.

Not open on the weekends.

Food: 4.5 stars
Service: 2 (real slow  if you don't order from pre-made dishes)
Ambiance: 2
Overall: 3.75 stars

I eat here fairly often for lunch.  It satisfies my Thai craving.  I usually order the pad kee mao at Thai restaurants, but I don't here because I'm not too keen about the chicken (I am very particular about meat).  So, now I get the pad see ew.  It usually comes with meat or tofu, but, again, since I don't like their meat and I don't like Tofu, I just ask for extra broccoli.  Since it isn't from the hot trays, its freshly cooked and delicious (and only $5.50).

The serving size is nice.  When my colleagues orders the red curry, they always specify the "bucket".  If you don't specify the bucket, you'll get it from the hot trays.  For a couple bucks more, you get a bucket with enough red curry to last two meals :-)

The woman who works the front is very friendly.  Always has a big smile on her face.  It helps to call ahead your order if you aren't getting from the hot trays, because it can get pretty busy during lunch.

Evan's Thoughts

If I could I'd give this place 3 and a half stars but alas yelp does not have that option.  A little hole in the wall in the Hearst Food Court, this place surprised me.  I didn't have high hopes walking in due to to the odd location and the fact no one was there (usually a big uh-oh for restaurants).  But I was immediately impressed seeing the prices and the quality of the food.  $7 for good Thai food is almost impossible to find and the mountain of pineapple fried rice I got was spectacular.

Bottom Line:  Good thai food-affordable price-need I say more?

****************************************************
Madeleine's Thoughts

Though I may not consider myself a Thai food fanatic, I know good pad thai when I eat it... and this pad thai was alright. I was just surprised by the MOUNTAIN of peanuts on top of it. Usually a sprinkling on top as a garnish is enough, but with a peanut oil on the noodles already, I felt like I belonged in a Charles Shultz comic strip about halfway through (oh, but the portions are HUGE so be prepared to split a dish or get a to-go box!). There is no bathroom in the restaurant (you gotta go upstairs), the two very sweet ladies in the kitchen were watching (what I believe was) a child getting his teeth removed on the television in the back, there is a very small drink selection but a large food selection, it's closed on weekends, it's hard to find, and it has tons of outdoor seating but not a large enough crowd to fill it.

It's typical college Thai food (hence the typical college "3 stars")... but don't college students have the right to awesome Thai food? Meesa says yes.

Taste: 3
Value: 4
Service: 3

Came here twice for drinks and tea. The lines aren't long, but I really wish they improved the atmosphere (ie: seats and tables). They also have some weird people inside since all the homeless people like congregating outside.

This place is a Berkeley must-go. I wouldn't recommend it if you want to get work done or are looking for good coffee, but it has a very cool vibe. I love watching the people that go there -- hippies, vagrants, students, ... I also love listening to conversations nearby -- they're usually pretty intellectual.
