Liked it for the old-school atmosphere.  Laughed at all the wannabe intellectuals, both young and old, arguing about politics and math and whatever might make them seem superior to one another.  How very coffee-shop of them!  There were also creatively dressed teens, a few bums, and other assorted folks.  

The Starbucks crowd probably wouldn't enjoy this place, as like many old restaurants and coffee shops, it wasn't immaculate or made-over with the latest trends.  I didn't think there was anything particularly gross about the bathrooms.

I can't really speak for the quality of the coffee, since I don't like coffee that much, but it was as good as any other I'd had.  I sat down to read a book and people watch, so I didn't get to try out the working atmosphere/connection.  It was a great place to do just that.

I think it's really gross in there.  It looks like it hasn't been cleaned in way too long, which makes the thought of eating there really unappetizing bc i wouldn't trust the food.   The espresso I had there was burnt. And the bathrooms are really gross, probably bc homeless people seem to hang out in the cafe and therefore are using the bathroom.

I was hesitant of entering the place at first because of all the bums outside the door.  But then I walked into this old coffee shop and saw...more bums.  But there were also a bunch of hipsters, students, vagrants, and other type of people.

I bought a coffee and went upstairs to get some studying done.  It's a pretty dark place save some natural light coming from the windows.  The tables are all gross and unstable.  The chairs are uncomfortable.  So why would I give this place four stars?  I dunno...I just liked the atmosphere.  There were a ton of different people, but everyone left you alone to get some studying done.  There was free wi-fi, which always helps.  The coffee itself wasn't too bad.  But the four stars is really because of the chill vibe of the place.

Enough with all the bums everywhere business, after all, it is Telegraph. 

 A sign claims that the Latte was invented here- whether true or not, their lattes are delicious. I hate being a one-trick pony but I  always get the pesto panini because I've rarely ever come across a sandwich so delicious

Ok- so I've been coming back to this place every now and then and I have to re-update this just because I must have come during an amazing night of service in the past- because recently, it's been a real hit or miss with this cafe. Last week, it took them 20 minutes to make me a hot tea and hot chocolate to go.....don't even get me started on how long you have to wait for one egg and cheese sandwich...aaargh. If the Montana Gold tea wasn't so good, I wouldn't frequent this place much at all anymore save for a last resort in the midnight hours!

This place makes me nostalgic :)

I used to stay away from it cuz it looks really dingy, with bum sitting outside at all times. But once you try it out, it's got much of its own vibe/atmosphere. Not the most presentable cafes in Berkeley, but the service is good and the owner/employees are friendly.

Good coffee & cookies--their sandwiches and breakfast are okay too.
It's supposed to be the first cafe to start lattes, so try it out least for the historical angle.

OMG!!! I am a food enthusiast and Joanna the cook (native Mexican) served at 7am New Year's Morning the best huevos rancheros I've ever had...EVERYTHING EVERYTHING FROM SCRATCH....the tomato salsa (with serranos, extra heavy, because I asked), home made frijoles enteros, and the eggs perfectly cooked but still runny...and you can go to the back counter while she cooks to give any good advice you might have for ingredients. The freshly-made-on-the spot salsa was so sweet and delicious I nearly swooned.  My dish was so good that my friend, also a food lover, went to the back to ask if she could have some salsa on her omelette too. (Joanna took the time to make it special for her while she waited at the counter 5 minutes, no charge). The coffee was fantastic....it was strong and black, with no bitterness, like Peet's and the Cheeseboard. The other items looked great and if the huevos were ANY indication of the quality, I will definitely make it a spot to hit when I'm out and about from SF.

Did I mention the cost? My huevos for $7 and other huge omelette platter with pancakes and sausage for $8?  This is the best kept secret breakfast place and  I thank them so much for the quality, quantity and deliciousness of the food they serve. Hard to believe no one's mentioned the food out of all the sad reviews about the people hanging about there. I am not exaggerating about the uniqueness of the breakfast and I had a great window seat to check out unique Telegraph, too!

good latte.

random bums walk in to check the time, which is weird, but then you realize you're on telegraph in berkeley.
A nice place to sit and read and enjoy a latte with coffee art =]

Back in the day ( have no idea how it is now) this place struck me as pretty damn hard core. When I walked in, there were bums, vagrants, professors, tattoo artists, fortune tellers, chess players, dogs, and poets who had probably been friends with Jack Kerouac sitting inside and outside of this lofted, tiled space, eating, chatting, playing cards, talking to themselves, or just spacing out.

They had a mean slice of spinach pizza here. They didn't use the carelessly placed single leaves of baby spinach or the smothered blobs of greenish brown under the cheese. This was some serious spinach, sauteed to perfection and then incorporated securely into an ample supply of cheese on a nice thin crust. 

At first, I felt like a real greenhorn in here, stepping up to bat at a counter controlled by an outwardly gruff dude. A while later, I became quite the regular, basking in the rays of natural sunlight and the balm of the eternal spring warming the shade indoors. There were a couple flies to swat away, always, but it was just a part of the environment. I never felt that my food was spoiled or risky in any way.

Later, I adhered more to the other mainstays of pizza providers, because visiting the Mediterranean Cafe required a level of commitment to really just exist for a while in a pocket of nostalgia for the collective experience of anyone who's dwelled in this magical college town in the East Bay. But it means something that I couldn't bring myself to come here when I didn't feel like feeling anything.

I went to this cafe today in downtown Berkeley on Telegraph for the first time to try out their pannini's since I am now very fond of pannin's.  This cafe is order first then take a seat. Apparentally they serve a wide a variety of coffee, breakfast, lunch, salads, and pannini's.   Either they were understaffed when I went or there was just too many people.  Had to wait in line a few minutes, then waited a few more minutes until the guy at the register made the first customer's hot chocolate which took longer than I would have imagined.  Then FINALLY he acknowledged my presence that I was/ have been waiting to order  and I asked what was in their pannini's and he described most of it before a lady came to the register and told me the pesto was the best.  Of course I complained saying there was no meat in it and she was nice enough to say that they could put meat in it.  My husband and I ended up ordering the same pannini- turkey mediterranean.  We took a seat upstairs because all the seats were taken upstairs.  Although the lady did tell us she'd call out my name I didn't hear anyone.  So we waited and waited....From above I could see just the counter but not where they served food, so finally I asked my husband to look downstairs under us where we believed the food was being prepared (though I didn't see it on the way up) and sure enough our food was already ready (how long? I don't know).  

The paninni itself was ok- in that I would order and eat it again, not mouthwatering good but not crap etiher.  At first I couldn't taste the turkey because of the cheese but later I tasted it and it was delicious.  Other than that there were too many olives for me on one half of my pannini so  I dumped them out.  It would have been ok if they were all sliced olives, but some of them were not even sliced.  The panninni came with a salad which was nothing special.  

As usual in downtown Berkeley you get your mix of college students, families, hippies and weird people that one usually see's hanging out on Telegraph.  So, there is nothing spectacular about the place except that you can have free internet and they do have a computer upstairs and a little bookshelf of books where one can read or leave books (why I don't know why).  It's also not the most clean place.  It's walls, celings are pretty decrepit with wires hanging out of the celing.  

So, my suggestion order take out....
Super cute place, cheap burritos, excellent chips and salsa. Be prepared for a line, I watched it grow after I placed my order.

Only place open at night so..... kinda sucks when you're hungry late at night. It's sooooooo greasy, sometimes you'll feel like you need to throw up after eating all that grease. But of course, it's great when you get the munchies. I know it's a rite of passage for freshmen, I wouldn't be particularly enthusiastic about recommending it.
The food is okay, but I would rather go elsewhere. The burritos are decent, the quesadilla is pretty good and the prices are cheap, but it's all-around bland and forgettable.

I don't know what people are thinking with all these lackluster reviews of perhaps my FAVORITE cheap mexican place ever.

Are these local foodies who have gotten ahold of my beloved La Burrita?

Whatever it is lets all take a step back. The food is amazing and the chips and salsa are something else. Sure its not some sort of slow food movement mexican place that uses only all organic and locally sourced ice cubes, but at least its close to campus?

la burrita on northside. i've only had it once but i must say that it is much better looking inside and cleaner than it's sister on southside. they are less stingy w/ the tortilla chips too since it's self-serve. the only thing was that the portion was not as large as it's sister and they made my enchiladas too healthy for me. when i think of la burrita i think of the enchilada/taco combo plate that is smothered in cheese, guacamole, and sourcream. I like my la burrita box to be soak in grease at the bottom too.

I ate lunch here 4 days in a row.  What I learned was that the shredded chicken super burrito is awesome.   The grilled chicken and grilled steak are oddly wet, like they sit in some kind of sauce or water or something.  The mojado burritos are microwaved which is always a turnoff for me.  But the shredded chicken super burrito is really good.  The chicken has some green chilies in it to add some flavor and mixed with beans, rice and all the other goodies it is a great lunch.  

Service is minimal, but then again so are the prices so it's hard to complain.  The woman cashier could try to be a little more friendly.

Its a good burrito place. The Futbol on the TV and the fresh, warm tortilla chips makes it good. Right next to North Gate of UC so it does get crowded. But if you time it right you'll be the only one in line

one chicken taco
comes with 2 tortillas, so
i really get TWO!

in seriousness,
for some reason, southside one
tastes better to me.
Go for the outdoor seating on a nice day if you're in the area.  But don't make a trek out there.

I think the cashier is a robot. Seriously. Not to insult her, but she has the same droning voice no matter what - it's incredible and slightly alarming.

As for the food... it's cheap and it tastes ok. Service is average. However, I have seen them microwave the wet burrito. This isn't "oh I heard that place is whack," this is a first hand account. I stood there and looked into the kitchen as they placed my burrito into the microwave, turned it on, left, came back, took it out and then gave it to me. Meh.

update: someone told me that the microwaving was just for melting the cheese on top of the wet burrito, which sounds pretty reasonable in retrospect haha. still not my favorite place, but not feeling quite as swindled. split between a 2 and a 3 now, but it was my bad about giving them a 2 before so I'm giving them a 3.

The La Burrita on North side is a little different than the one on South side, but I cant put my finger on whyyyyyy.

Benefits of getting it on North Side - unlimited chips if you sit in and eat. Again there's an unlimited salsa & lime bar.
When I'm very hungry at lunch, this is my go-to place. Lots of food (incl. fresh chips) for a good price. Nothing too fancy, just good, solid, high-quantity Mexican food.

My days at Cal as a commuter meant exploring the food venues... 

La Burrita on the north side wasn't so bad. The food was not the best tasting but acceptable. The value was reasonable and free chips... so you can't really complain. I just hated stacking my used dish on what looked like an over crowded shelf of dishes ready to fall. 

but all in all.... an okay place.

Truly a food staple if you are a Berkeley student looking for cheap eats.  While not gourmet on any level, this satisfies much desire in terms of quantity and availability.  This place is open well into the AM hours, so come grab your drunk munchies.  It's also situated in a very accessible location for students on the Southside.  Best of all its cheap.  Four dollars and change can get you a huge burrido that will raise your blood pressure and put you into a food coma.  I've tried most of their meats and I would have to say asada is still king.  

PROTIP:  Try their nachos sometime!  The portions are huge, the prices are slightly higher, but its big enough to share.

If you haven't had significant real mexican food in the past, this place is pretty kick ass. I remember the time when I was a freshman, thinking this place was decent. If you're a freshman, chances are you'll like it too.

I've tried several things here, they all seem to sound off some "unhealthy food" alert in my system and the food is not good enough to compensate. Greasy quesadillas, burritos, nachos. It seems like their La Burrita special is the best.

The Fajita Plate or Nachos are really the best menu items here.  The chips are fresh.  The burritos are just okay, not as good as La Burrita on Durant (Southside).  Sometimes they get my order wrong too, but I forgive that.

Honestly, some people have no shame for the nonesense they write..
I have been a student at Cal for three years now, and LA Burrita is one of my favorites! I started liking Mexican food after I tried this place, the burrittos are just amazing, and so are there fresh tortilla chips with the tasty salsa selection they offer. What makes this resturaunt even better is the great prices which come with the amazing food. IT IS DEFINITELY A PLACE TO COME BACK TO!!

Another restaurant on Euclid whose survival depends on undergrads looking for anything that is even marginally better  than cafeteria food. If you are not an an undergrad, you will probably have higher standards, and will be baffled at the high rating this place has.  The portions are large, but the food is uniformly bland.

I always get the tamale plate with extra rice instead of beans.  Not a big fan of anything else.  

The tamale is usually pretty good, but sometimes the meat inside (beef or chicken) is *especially* dry.  The rice is good, but it's hard to go wrong there.  Overall, I've had better.  ~$6 or $7

Unlike the Durant location, the chips here are unlimited.  Definite plus, but not so much as to justify an extra star.  

Also, the horchata is muy bueno!  Plus one star for this refreshing drink.  ~$2

I've been going to this place for about six months now. It's no Mission joint, but the food is reasonably priced and you can get a nice helping of chips made on the premises and some tasty salsa. There's plenty of indoor and outdoor seating, and the area is pleasant. And this shop is open late.

I've been to a few other Mexican places in Berkeley, and I've found that their higher prices are rarely justified by tastier food, fresher ingredients, or better service. It's just not a good area for this kind of food.

The service here is also relatively slow, but I think that's because they don't ever have more than a couple people actually putting orders together. Whoever works the register is invariably tired, distracted, or both. I don't think I've ever seen any of them so much as crack a grin.

And when you order a large burrito, you always want to specify "regular," or they might charge you for a "super" which adds sour cream and guacamole in amounts that never justify the additional price. I don't think I've ever encountered a substantial amount of cheese in my burrito, either. Just beans, rice, and whatever meat you asked for, if any.

I think the reason it's remained successful over the years is more because of its high-traffic location than anything else. If something better came along on that street, I'd never go to La Burrita again, even if the new place wanted an extra dollar and didn't throw chips into the deal.

I've been going to La Burrita for 4 years now. I love it! For not much money, you can get a big burrito that lasts 2 meals. And they have a punch card to get a free burrito. The ingredients taste fresh and yummy. the only downfall is that you have to share the outside space with the pathetic fools who go to La Val's. Other than that, La Burrita is fantasic!

Here, unlike on southside, they have warm unlimited tortilla chips. The salsas, especially the green salsa, are really good too. Also I like their agua frescas.

The food is decent and cheap--I like their shrimp burrito.

One star for the veggie options (I'll take broccoli on anything) and one for the self-serve chips-- that's the extent of my praise for this place. The food's consistently and discouragingly bland. While not bad, the price certainly doesn't justify this.

Bottom line: It'll do in a pinch.
I LIVED off of this place when I was a student at Cal.  I crave their green salsa on a regular basis and wish that I lived closer to Berkeley so that I could enjoy it more often.

This is one of the 2 Mexican restaurants available to you dining on Euclid on the north side of the Cal campus. Best part of La Burrita is the giant basket of free chips that you get. They're way better quality than most other Mexican places, surprisingly, given the budget nature of this place. The salsas available are average quality. Contrary to the name of the place, the burritos here are probably the weakest item on the menu. Steer clear. Pretty much everything else is decent/average. Décor of this place leaves something to be desired, but when you're paying $5 for an entire meal plus a basket of free chips, you can't really complain.

I wonder if the two La Burritas are associated because this place is a lot better than that shit on Durant.

I'm not saying it's good Mexican food but it tasted okay and made me full and happy. I even ordered an extra taco. I was a little adventurous and had the taco and tamale plate. Usually, I'm very skeptical about tamales served out of my comfort zone (San Bernardino.) But the tamale was decent: a little heavy on the masa but it tasted good. Not too much cumin, just enough sauce. Kinda dry like I like it. The taco had actual asada unlike that crap on the other side of campus.

I'll come here again when I have the muchies for Mexican food, but right now I'm trying out other, potentially more satisfying venues.

La Burrita is okay on the Northside. I got the small super burrito (ironic much?) and they have unlimited chips that you can get yourself. The chicken was a little dry, but eh, nothing unexpected. Their salsa was good, but to be honest, I think you can't really f*&% up salsa.

I have nothing against this place, but nothing I crave for either.

Love the chips, love the salsa bar, love the horchata.  I have had most things on the menu and every this has been great.  My favorite is the grilled chicken wet burrito! You get a lot of food for the money too!

Service goes a long long way and these guys are super sweet.

We get the fajita plates and have tons of special changes made to it to fit the South Beach Diet rules, and they get it right every single time.  I feel bad having so many changes when they're busy, but it's fast, delicious,  priced very very favorably, and served with a smile.  And the salsas are yummy as well!

Thank you, La Burrita staff!

(the draught beer is a little tinny though, pls clean your pipes)

My favorite place to eat if I need something filling, cheap, and fast. The food is average and doesn't make me have seizures from tastiness but the food comes out so damn fast it's ridiculous. Hence, the 4 stars for it's easiness to eat and quickness that helped me survive hunger pangs while in Stacks or on those late night food runs.   :')

I usually get the carne asada burrito (pretty damn big if you ask me) which is about $5-6 for a small and $7 for a large. You literally have to wait as long as how long you took to order. Well maybe not that fast but you get my point. Anyways the burrito comes with a lot of chips, but as some mentioned they're grabbed by many bare hands that God knows what they touched before. So if you're a germ-a-phobe, have care! 

They also have a bunch of different salsas/sauces/condiments at the side bar. There's one SPICY and pretty good salsa that they NEVER leave out. Instead they keep it in a little bottle that's usually out of reach. Frankly, I have no idea why they do that. Call it trust issues? 

They also charge 50 cents for card usage so that kind of annoys me as I never carry cash around when I'm in college but oh well. :T Overall, a good place for quick/cheap eats especially late at night.

I had a ok meal here.. not particularly good, but not bad either...  i felt full after the burrito...

oh, liked the free nachos!

When I was craving mexican food while going to Cal, I went to La Burrita on North Side.  The mexican places up north definately don't hold a candle to any mexican restaurant in socal, however this place was close by campus and relatively cheap and gave good portions.  Not sure if they still do this, but I remember eating my fill of free fresh tortilla chips after finishing my burritos.

Like any La Burrita, this place can give you a quick meal for very little money. The Northside one has unlimited chips but closes a little earlier than the Southside franchise...

I've always ordered a Super Quesadilla, always delicious and perfect. Great staff and pretty decent decor.

This place is pretty standard, cheap mexican food.  I used to come here pretty often because it's so close to the Foothill dorm and it seemed good compared to the dining commons, but now I know better.
Free chips and salsa with an order. This is the place i go when i know ill be spending all day on campus and i did not bring anything to eat. It keeps me full all day and not broke :D

I used to eat here occasionally when I lived in the area.  When I say occasionally it was usually when someone suggested it and I was too indifferent to object.

I would never, ever, ever order a burrito here; I made the mistake once, but never again.  They're flavorless at best and overpriced for just a regular burrito.  The tortas, however, are pretty decent.  The meat was some thinly sliced steaks.  Also, there's hella free chips (which are self-serve) and salsa.

There's outside seating that's shared by LaVal's next door.

La Burrita is very much like its brother next door (La Val's pizza). It's pretty good at what it does. They serve cheaply priced mexican food and it's pretty darn good. If you eat here everyday, you will of course make yourself sick. I'm sure some of the other reviewers will realize this as well. You shouldn't eat anywhere every single day, you will....ahem, get sick of it. I mainly get the chicken burrito with sour cream added. Sometimes they get a little carried away with the rice, so if you say no rice they typically don't make up for it with more beans or meat, its just a smaller burrito which is pretty shitty. They give you a free basket of chips if you buy at least 2 dollars worth of food. The chips aren't too shabby. The salsa is what really kicks ass here. They have a roasted tomato salsa that I could literally drink. Also the jalapeno salsa is niiiice, just mix half of this with the roasted tomato and you have one kick ass salsa!

Do NOT eat here - ever.  My boyfriend had a quesadilla from here and started throwing up uncontrollably exactly 2 hours later - he had such such severe food poisoning that he had to be admitted to the hospital and get put on an IV and get an antibiotic.  And there's no question that it was a direct result of what he ate here because the symptoms started exactly when he had just digested what he had eaten from here, and it was the first thing he had eaten for that day.  Avoid at all costs.  I'm giving it one star because otherwise this review won't get posted.

Nothing too special, but it's fine for cheap mexican (the veggie options are actually pretty good), and the (free) chips and salsa are always good and plentiful. Being able to fill up for $4 on okay food is definitely worth 3 stars.

I seriously love their freshly made, warm, thin, crispy chips, that are FREE to grab w/ purchase! I love their nacho, which is what I always order. I love how you can grab as much salsa as you could (my favorite is the green one that's not too spicy). I hate how now that I've graduated and moved, I am so far away from a La Burrita :(

This place is like any average taqueria. Yay for unlimited chips though! :)

I ordered the super nachos with carne asada.. and to be honest, it was less than what I expected. It was simply chips with a dollop of guacamole, a dollop of tomato salsa and a dollop of sour cream on top of chips with melted cheese. Just eh, to me. I'm not used to getting my condiments in small dollops on top of my super nachos. I guess I was expected it to be more messy and mixed together.

I wouldn't return here (even if it was the last burrito joint on earth). The food (a standard combo of burritos, nachos, salsa, etc.) was bland, tasteless and without any element of freshness, spice or flavor in general. The rest of the place was the more daunting part, with dead cockroaches on our table and a toilet dirty in unspeakable ways.

The food is wonderful!  Fresh tasting salsa is a must for Mexican food, and this place has a good salsa bar.

The burritos are as big as my overinflated ego, and they are so much nicer.  I regretfully wrap up the second half I couldn't possibly eat and take it home. Two meals in one for under $10!  

Clientele is varied, and a little reserved, for Berkeley.
Courtyard dining is comfy, out of the breeze and charming.
NUMMY!

Decent Mexican food, nothing that really stands out as extraordinarily fresh, authentic, or special. The free chips are a nice touch, and there is a lunch deal for tacos that easily filled me up in the $5 zone.

-Takes American Express.
-Has flies near the door, which is kind of off-putting.
-Closes earlier than La Val's next door.
-Shared patio space with La Val's means that your indecisive friends can go and decide what to get when they get there.
Fast, cheap, open late. Generally good consistent food (though once I got a burrito with too much salt in it...). Very filling Mexican for a low price.

Even though I've only been to the Euclid La Burrita once, I prefer this location over the Durant La Burrita.

The Euclid La Burrita is bigger and cleaner than the Durant La Burrita. There are plenty of indoor and outdoor tables, so if you're in the mood to watch TV or eat in the sun, they have space for you!

Try their Taco Salad and Super Burrito. YUM!!
Its decent. Made me sick twice, but that was a couple of years ago... Still, I've not had the courage to come back.

The food wasnt bad here. But the chips I have to warn people about. The handle that you scoop chips with is thrown back into the drawer, which means everyone's hands are all over the chips. I stayed away. Service was fast and price is decent. They are not open late like their Durant counterpart though

I'm from Los Angeles, so I've had a taste of real Mexican food. La Burrita does not serve food that I would call authentic-tasting. The food is bit more mild and toned down. It's no King Taco, but it fills a hungry college student's stomach fast. I don't like burritos, so I ordered a Combo Plate. The enchilada was dry and not spicy. The taco shell was soggy. But, I suppose it'll do for being a chain around the Berkeley campus.

I used to go to this La Burrita all the time when I lived in Foothill because the people who lived on my floor loved it, and I've only ever gotten their quesadilla. They give a REALLY big quesadilla and it's pretty yummy! I like how they give out unlimited free chips too - no more rationing the chips!

This restaurant is medium big with a good amount of seats, so it's nice how you don't have to fight for a seat like the La Burrita on Durant.

3 stars overall because while they were good, they weren't something that I would go back to again and again. Maybe more stars if I tried something other than their quesadilla..

It is much better than its sister restaurant on the south side of town but it is still not so good.    
If you are often on the UC Berkeley campus there is a good chance you will eventually eat here and when you do, it probably won't be a bad experience.  
It has a nice location with some outdoor seating.  They make an okay burrito and pretty good aqua frescas.

I always go to the La Burrita in South Side Asian Ghetto and last week was the first time I've been to this one. Surprisingly, even though all my friends rave about how much better the one in south side is (for personal reasons), I still enjoy this one a lot more. The North Side area just seems more welcoming to me, and this La Burrita is roomier, has outdoor seating, and plenty plenty plenty of in door seating. Also, even though they do have a policy of 1 basket of chips per order, the chips are self served here whereas in South Side, the chips are given to you by the workers. Overall, if I plan to do a sit-in, I would much rather prefer this location to its sister location.

I come here sometimes after class with my friend since she loves this place. She's from Turkey, so she hasn't been exposed to a lot of Mexican restaurants and seems to think this is the best place to get burritos. I actually know better than that, lol.

Ok food. I mainly go there for the unlimited chips and salsa that you get when dine in.

This LaBurrita is less convenient for most students who DON'T live on northside but it is way better. why? free chips & salsa bar. they used to not have the 'free basket per entree' rule and they don't really enforce it (from what I've seen) but yea, the free chips + salsa = happiness 

cheap mexican food that hits the spot, especially when you're a starving student (ok, not really), but the burritos are always good and filling and at least a 1000 calories if you get the 'super' (aka with guac and SC).

i'd recommend the pollo asado and carne asada burritos as well as the nachos.

Meh. This place is not  that good. In fact, I would say it is sub par. Mexican food needs to have lots of flavor from the spices and fresh ingredients. This place lacked both. I ordered the fajita burrito and its just not good. The "carne asada" was tough and hard. They overload it with bell peppers as if they wanted to mask the crappy meat. What's keeping me from giving it one star is the price and location. It is quite affordable and if you're craving some mexican food on the northside of campus, this is the only option.

This La Burrita is one of the go-to places for students stuck in Etcheverry or Soda Halls in the late hours of the evening. Without it, many would go hungry since many places in the area close before it.

However, my experiences with La Burrita haven't been too great. I enjoy the unlimited chips, since it gives me something to munch on while I wait for my meal. Their salsa isn't too bad either, and tasted pretty fresh.

My burritos, though, are a different story. They always come out relatively wet, which just makes it one big soggy mess. I've never had this happen at the South Side one, but it usually happens to me here. Maybe it's because their beans or meat are drenched in water. To me, though, it's not too pleasant. Other than that, the burritos here are pretty standard. Don't expect anything amazing, because you're not paying for that. If I was really hungry in the middle of the day, I would take my money to better places on Euclid.

I grew up on burritos and these are, well, not good. They are tasteless, but they do serve the purpose of feeding oneself for under  $4. Also they are open until 2AM so they are a late night snack staple. 
Always order black beans as the refried beans are gross, and overpower, especially with all the other bland ingredients.
So Cal burritos are WAY better but this is decent for Nor Cal. It's a cheap and affordable lunch. Free chips!

It's cheap, it's close to campus and you get to help yourself to the chips and salsa. That drags the northside La Burrita up to a 2-star rating (the chips are less plentiful in the southside version, making it totally not worth going). They hang on to that second star by virtue of their veggie burritos, which are a bit bland but otherwise ok. Everything else I've eaten here has been pretty unpleasant: the meat always makes we feel a bit queasy (and it doesn't even taste good going down), the bean enchilada was tasteless and way too greasy, and the guacamole on the side was a sad little pile of salty green glue.

If you're strapped for time and/or cash, you might be excused for eating here. Otherwise, walk down to Cancun Taqueria for much tastier burritos and a fantastic salsa bar. It's just as well Cancun doesn't do self-service chips like La Burrita (northside) does or I might never leave.

I go here a couple times a month now. It's a great value for the amount of food (and free chips/salsa). The ingredients don't taste as nice as elsewhere (ie, the guacamole here vs at Chipotle), but it's cheaper here. They do have some more unique items like the tostada salad that you can't get at Chipotle. There's almost always seating since they have a large space and share outdoors seating with La Val's.

Vegitarians can eat very well here. It's hard to find veggie tomalies, and LA Burrita delivers not only stellar veggie tomalies, but also a wide variety of enchilada, burrito, tostada, and fresh juice options. 

I had a small carrot juice for $1.50 and they ground the carrots right in front of me in their carrot juicer! MMMMM

If your not a veggie there's pleanty for you too, so bring your friends.

They also have a new lunch card system, (10 burritos = a free one).

This place is much better than the La Burrita on south side of campus (north side is cleaner, has no homeless people outside asking for money, no funny smell near the place, cashier understands your order, etc...), but still, I would say the food is mediocre. 

I ordered the wet burrito (pretty much a normal burrito but with cheese melted on top as well as some salsa smothered over the top) with pollo asada. The burrito itself was pretty good for the $5.59 I paid for it, but the chicken wasn't very flavorful and it was a bit overcooked, and therefore dry. In order to finish the burrito, I used a ton of salsa. I really like the self serve salsa bar as well as the all you care to grab chips they offer. Nice to have when you're waiting for your order.

So I came here because my beloved Chipotle was closed due to a power outage last week ;(  I was considering going to Celia's (across the street), but a friend suggested coming here because the prices are better here. It's funny, I kept smack-talking before I tried the food....

...walk back to campus. Open up the foil-wrapped burrito......

....my taste buds go, yummmmmmm....so flavorful. I think I may have found my burrito haven if I'm ever on the northside of campus...!

I really like this La Burrita because it's spacious and people are more attentive and friendly compared to the Durant Ave one. I ordered a big order here before for 8-10 people. They were really nice and helpful, and gave me a big bag so I can carry all the burritos and chips and sauces back to campus.

I also came here for their vegetarian burritos. Really good, indeed. Who says a good burrito needs meat? Guacamole, rice, beans, sour cream and salsa are all you need! :D

Yes, you know my type. I'm a burrito snob from California. I spit on Tex-Mex. It can take its queso and shove it. I recruited a team of researchers to set out on a quest for a decent burrito in all of New York City. Findings were unanimously dismal. Cal-Mex reigns as Burrito King of the World and I will not be moved on this. There's only one state that can wrap it right, and only one place that achieves perfection: La Burrita. So eat that, Chipotle; you're a cheap imitation and should be ashamed of yourself.
Maybe I came on a bad day, but compared to the Mex food in San Jose or Socal this one is definately NOT worth the price. My goodness, even for Berkeley food!

I came here for the first time with a group of friends last night. I ordered a Super Quesadilla (chicken). I don't know if I was not super hungry or what, but it was suprisingly filling! I also liked their wide assortment of salsas and free chips :) 

The northside location is much nicer and more spacious than the southside location, but I probably wouldn't trek all the way up to northside just for La Burrita - I'm pretty lazy when it comes to walking...

Nevertheless, it's a great place for students to grab a bite to eat or study in because of the nice tables and ambiance. I got a drink (free refills), chips, and that super quesadilla for $7

I've eaten here numerous times, and this is my overall impression:

The burritos here are reasonably priced, usually pretty good (though a couple times they've been dry or had fatty meat or other stuff in the burrito), and DEFINITELY filling.

I'd easily recommend this for a good lunch place, and plan to continue going myself.

I lived next door to La Buritta for 3 and a half years. LOVE---IT. And that is coming from a girl born and raised in Southern California living off of mexican. Their Carne Asadas are really good, their food is consistant and its not expensive. Its just good hole in the wall mexican food. I would say La Burrita and Gordo's are by far the top 2 mexican joints in Berkeley.

Well, its close to campus. And its got a nice patio to eat on.  And....well, other than that, can't really muster more than a meh.  

It was my first experience with a wet burrito--and i'll always treasure that.  But I've moved on, sorry la burrita.  Maybe we'll see each other from time to time.  But for now, gordo's has my heart...and stomach.

I was addicted to this place when I was a student and I still go out of my way to visit it for multiple reasons:

-It's hard to find Mexican places that offer GROUND BEEF Burritos, which is my favorite. 
-They have an array of salsa's and you can take as many trips to the chip dispenser as you want. 
- Really affordable

The food is most often delicious and its fun to find yourself in your old environment again!

Arguably the most popular choice for Northside residents looking for a nearby place to eat. It has decent food, some good amenities, and also some drawbacks, making for an above average experience overall.

I like to order the plates for dinner, which each have some combination of tamales, enchiladas, and tacos, along with the side servings of rice and beans. For example, the combo plate comes with one of each  of the three items for $6.95. It has fairly good flavor; the tamales are dry but have good texture, the enchiladas are small but have a nice balance of cheese and meat, and the tacos are a little greasy and bland but come with a lot of lettuce and meat. The rice is dry but has decent flavor, and the same can be said of the beans. Both fill you up while tasting OK. Adding in the free chips and salsa that you can get when you order a reasonable amount of food (about $2 worth?), a plate is a great deal, though I usually pass on the chips because of their greasiness.

The burritos are another good choice. For a good price (less than $5, I believe), you get a good mix of ingredients and a decent amount of  food, along with the aforementioned chips and salsa. I like steak for the meat, but I would guess the other choices (chicken being one) are good, too.

Service is OK. The person working the cashier seems to change randomly based on who's free at the time you step up to the counter, but they are nice. The wait for your food, however, can often be long, up to ten minutes depending on what you order.

The large TV inside is a major plus. They play sports most of the time; they always have the Monday Night Football game on, for instance. However, a downside to the non-food part of the store is the tap water; my friends complained of the detergent-ish taste of it. Also, the water container that dispenses it was empty for a while before they refilled it.

Indoor seating is ample but cramped. There are lots of tables and booths, with the tables seating up to six or so if you push them together and the booths seating up to two comfortably. The tables next to the wall on the counter side of the store that have four chairs pulled up to them are too small, though. You can also eat in the outside area next to La Val's, which if I remember correctly has a few long tables with attached benches.

For the price and amount of food you get, this is a solid place to eat. It's far from perfect, though, so be ready to deal with some annoyances.
Cheap mexican, on the northside, and filling for a poor college student.  And if you are really hungry, I suppose you could fill up on the chips too...

La Burrita (both North and South side) is always a great place for fast, cheap, and good food. I love being able to go late at night for a filling burrito. The salsas are really good as well.

This location (North side) I like better because of the larger dining area both inside and out, though it does close earlier than the location on Durant.

Just what I was expecting, and it never fails: cheap, fast, food that is good enough to keep me coming back when I can't think of anything else....not much else to say since places like this are a dime a dozen in the Bay Area and really I don't have any complaints.  I've had a few of the burritos and the fish tacos - always just fine.  The vegetarian burrito is one of those punish-vegetarians burritos that these places always have - nothing but some soggy beans, rice, and cheese...so probably not ideal for that.

Pros:
-Relatively cheap

Cons:
-Watery salsa, some of the salsa has quite a bit of pepper in it?
-Bad service
-Bland food
-Dry burritos, seriously there was nothing moist inside of it. 

Insider tips: 
-When you order something to go there are little brown bags next to the register for you to get chips with, they never ever tell you this, but you are free to take one for your to go order. 
-If you get one of those frequent burrito cards and forget it one time, they DO NOT add the cards together, How are you supporting customer loyalty if you don't even add the frequent burrito card balance together if someone forgets it?

Dude, it's no longer a crunchy taco once you drown it in the plate with watered down enchilada sauce. It reverts to it original form once soaked. 

Never again. Thank God none of us got sick.

La Burrita is an incredible value. You can get a pretty substantial meal for less than $5. There's not many places you can do that in Berkeley. Chips and salsa are complimentary. I highly recommend getting a "wet burrito" which is basically a burrito smothered in sauce and cheese that you eat with a fork (and a knife if you'd like). The north side location has the advantage of having self-service chips. Sure the service isn't wonderful, but for these prices, who cares?

Taste: 2
Value: 4
Service: 3

I've been here way too many times, probably nearly twenty times over the course of the last 3.5 years? The only reason I know is because I've used up one of their frequent buyer cards, if not two. 

It's cheap, and it's close by since it's at Northside. I haven't gone back for a while, and two days ago I decided to drop by since I wasn't in the mood for La Val's and was out of cash. 

Unfortunately, their burritos still taste the same (pretty mediocre and somewhat bland), just like how I always remembered them. I actually felt kind of sick after eating about half of my burrito, but I guess it's because I was just really tired of their food. Almost positive I won't be going back ever again. I'd just rather grab a sandwich from La Val's if I'm out of cash in the future.

I usually get the shredded chicken burrito or grilled pollo burrito, both of which are okay. The portions are smaller than Chipotle, but you do get bottomless chips and salsa if you dine in. If you get it to go, you can ask for a bag for chips/salsa. They're fast with making the food, so wait times are usually minimal.

Far more spacious and accomodating than the southside location. Their infinite tub of chips and their salsa bar are nice, although neither their chip nor their salsa is spectacular.

Their prices aren't too bad -- around $6.50 for a large carne asada burrito and large fountain drink (with one free refill for those who are eating at the restaurant). Their burritos aren't amazing, but they're filling and I won't go so far to say that they're "tasteless".

A good quick bite for those stranded on the north side of campus and too lazy to head to southside.

Hey surprise surprise, it's pretty good! I've only gotten the vegetarian stuff here and it's nothing like what you would expect from an authentic place, but when were burritos ever authentic in the first place? Still, broccoli in a burrito? Hmm. I don't like how they automatically seem to wrap your burrito in foil. I think you should say, "no foil!" the counter lady is pretty fast and friendly. I like the free chips and salsa. The price is right for a quick lunch time meal.

I miss la burrita so much, it breaks my heart. Back in college, when I had a little more change in my pocket than was necessary for a Cup-o-Noodles, I'd head over to fill up on beans, rice, and microwave-wilted cheese. Mmmmmm...... oh and if your dining companions are feeling more extravagant, they can always head to la vals next door and meet you in the middle.
PS. Somebody needs to write a wikipedia article detailing the lore behind Mr. Val and Senorita Burrita. I just know there's a sordid love story lurking in there, waiting to be told....

The best thing about La Burrita is not the burritos.  The burritos are fine.   I usually get steak, because the chicken is soggy and bland and pretty much gross.  Also, the burritos are pretty inexpensive.  And you can get a small size burrito if you're a normal-sized person, or if you're a huge person but just not that hungry.  But the best that La Burrita has to offer is not the burritos, as I said.  Unlike a lot of strictly burrito joints, here you can get an enchilada plate with beans, rice, and two delicious enchiladas.  Or a tostada salad.  And all you can eat chips and a salsa bar.  I give La Burrita kudos for options, but they lose some love for lacking some flavor.
Fish tacos: delicious, but a little too greasy for my liking.

I've ordered every single burrito here. They are all meh... These guys are open late hours which is the reason they are so popular. Their food is not quality, so if that's what your looking for go somewhere else. Their  super nachos are a great drunk snack that you can split with a buddy. Tasty going down, pasty coming out is what I always say hehe. If you have the extra dollar, try the shrimp burrito. It's a decent one. The pineapple salsa they have in it has a uniqueness to it that is memorable enough for me to write about. Salsa bar is also pretty good. Ask for etra chips and they will give you some, unless you are homeless. They hate the homeless. I think.

I ordered takeout; the BAJA SALAD. What a disappointment. The on-line and takeout menu was so misleading. I have to say that I was so disappointed. As stated on the menu "Flour Shell with Lettuce, Black Beans, Chicken Breast, Avocado, Salsa Frisca, Cilantro, Cheese and Olives" I am still looking for a piece of Avocado, Cheese, Salsa Frisca, Olives? "nowhere to be found"  I got, the flour shell, lettuce, chicken and black beans. ... I added some dressing myself. 

I am so disappointed. It is different when you get all that is promised and it is not good.. But to get less than half of what is promised and still not good is totally not acceptable. This place is really hit or miss. Why take the chance??  If you have more time go downtown for a more satisfying experience. 

The cashier has no personality whatsoever... She can be so rude and unconcerned. 

I only go to this location because it is close to my job, but when it comes to MY dining experience?  Convenience over total satisfaction;  just not worth the gamble.  Seriously...  Too many other options...  

Totally Disappointed...... cats
shit was bomb

Thanks to La Burrita, I now know that mediocre Mexican food does exist. 

But they get two stars for having beer on tap and free chips and salsa, so if that's all you want it's aight.

"Hi, can I take your order?", she said in a lackluster tone. I don't think I will ever recover from hearing that soul-draining voice. ANYWAYS...

There seems to be a lack of quality burrito offerings in Berzerkeley, and La Burrita helps in maintaining that. I ordered this burrito, right? You know, carnage asada and the works. I pick the thing up, bite into it, and ended up with a mouthful of lukewarm cow. If you're drunk or need a cheap bite, La Burrita's offerings of bland and un-fresh items may be right up your alley. Godspeed

Maybe I lived too long in San Diego and have higher "Cotixan" expectations, but I find this place to be disgusting.  A litttle sprinkle of meat with the bulk consisting of lard beans, and rice.  To make it even worse its wrapped in a steam tortilla.  Why don't they grill them in nor-cal?

It's shocking how bad their tacos are.

It was cold, wet, and strangely slimy tasting tortillas filled mostly with huge wet lettuce pieces. 

I had no choice but making a total mess when I ate them.

The burrito was tolerable but not good enough make up for the horrible tacos. 

How can they justify charging $2.50 each for what was absolutely worse than taco bell? No excuse.

They should send someone down to LA to learn what a real taco is.

A haiku for the last experience:

what fucking happened?
tortilla missing big chunks
someone bit my shit!
You come for the food? Come for the grad students stuffing themselves with burritos. A must for those who want to see what the up and coming engineering student or seminarian are wearing these days.

La Burrita is your standard quick Mexican cafe. The food is simply good. Unlimited fresh chips and very tasty salsa. The food quality's higher than you would find on a taco truck, but they're not going to win any  best of the bay contest either. However, this place does what it does well, which is feeding the hungry masses with filling, fresh, and tasty dishes, quick and cheap.

Northside La Burrita is by far superior to Southside. The catch is that Northside closes earlier. I do not care what anyone else has to say. This place kept me fed while I was a struggling undergraduate toiling away in the dungeon the UC named Etcheverry.

The prices are awesome and sometimes they have really nice deals. They once offered two taco plates and a soda for $3.99. You also get a free plate of chips with your meal. That is freakin' awesome!

The food and the prices associated very often lifted my spirits.

Living in the foothill dorms my first year, then on northside for the following three I had my fair share of La Burrita burritos, enchiladas, tostadas and the like.  And I must say it falls decidedly in the "Meh. I've experienced better." camp.

Growing up in LA I may be fairly biased when it comes to mexican food, but La Burrita really falls right in that totally generic nothing to make it stand out food camp.  Their burritos are bland, their salsa has no flavor.  The best thing they have going is fresh greasy chips, but I don't go to mexican restaurants for chips, I go for food.

Their enchiladas are decent, probably because the cheese makes up for their generally bland flavors.  Same with their wet burrito.  Lastly, the lack of carnitas in their menu significantly hurts them in my pork-centric worldview.

Want some mediocre mexican food at not so great prices close to campus? La Burrito may be for you.  If you're interested in eating good food, I recommend Juan's Place in West Berkeley, or perhaps just about any other Mexican Food restaurant. 

My little sister could make better quesadillas than the ones made here when she was in 8th grade.

I must agree with other posters, that the location and setting of this La Burrita makes it far superior to the Southside counterpart.  It has a nice courtyard which makes for a peaceful place to eat outside.  Just expect bland, run of the mill, Mexican food.  They do have good Horchata.

Despite the fact that I have been to this place on multiple occasions in the last year and walked out with trouble stomach, fear of the mice coming out of the wall, I still love their warm chips and salsa. 

My bf and I come here pretty often because it's so close to campus and my apartment. This place doesn't taste anything like what you find in a real Mexican restaurant; but when you're hungry, the chips are amazing.

La Burrita, at least the one on north side, is not one of my favorite places.
Yes, they do have the "one free basket of chips per order" policy (however, I've totally gotten away with two - cough - or three), so I inclined to give them some stars for that....

however....

as a Southern California transplant, I know what good Mexican food should taste like. This is not it.

On my last visit, my burrito was filled with unseasoned, bland pinto beans, unimpressive rice,  a *few* pieces of chicken, and was missing the extra cheese and avocado I payed for :(

If a place is going to call themselves "La Burrita" you at least gotta make sure your burrito is decent

***Special note: I am on the ever present search for decent Horchata in the bay area. La Burrita's Horchata is way too sweet, it sort of tastes like cupcake frosting. 

so as far as La Burrita goes: if you're desperate, it's ok, but you'll probably be disappointed

Although my 61b lecturer got food poisoning here, it didn't stop me.  I love the salsa and chips and the burritos are good too.  Remember if you take out, you can always ask for an extra bag for the chips.  Better yet you can get the nachos and you get a plastic bag so you just fill that plastic bag up with as much chips you can get away with.  Hell that was $3 meal right there.  Cheap easy grubbin' for a CS major.  Not the best place for Mexican food but hell it was convenient also spacious.

Man, I really like La Burrita. I'm in Northside a lot around lunchtime and I pop in here on a pretty regular basis. I haven't sampled the entire menu, mostly because I've gotten stuck on the Super Burrito Mojado ("Wet") and I haven't wanted to move on. This thing is gigantic and very inexpensive. I usually get it takeout because I know I could never finish it in time in one sitting.

So it comes in a big box, with the burrito arranged diagonally (it wouldn't fit straight across) and totally smothered in a gooey sauce with melted cheese all over, and a big-ass pile of guac and sour cream on either side in the opposite corners of the box like boxers in green and white shorts getting ready to throw down in the boxing ring that the burrito represents in this metaphor. Which creates like an awesome flavor battle in my mouth, or something.

Okay that paragraph got a little out of hand but the point is that I LOVE the wet burrito maybe a little bit too much. It's awesome for that 3:00pm crash too because I can finish the rest of it that I couldn't eat at lunch. I like the carne asada quite a bit, it's super tasty and grilled just right, the chicken is also good.

The lines get a little long around lunchtime but on days that I brave the queue I'm always pleasantly surprised by how quickly the line moves. The staff is always super-efficient and pretty pleasant if you get a chance to chat with them. They also tolerate me trying to order a burrito in Spanish with a smile, so that's a plus for me.

The free chips + salsa bar are a boon, and always gives me something to do if I have to wait a couple minutes for my food, which is inevitable on occasion.

Frankly, between La Val's and La Burrita in the same courtyard, I could basically satisfy my lunch needs for the rest of my time on the Northside without venturing elsewhere.

Once upon a time I was stuck eating lunch on Northside often and I'd come here, and order the chicken quesadilla. It wasn't amazing, or good to be honest, but it was food.

Like La Val's, the Northside location of La Burrita looks a lot nicer and sunnier than the Southside one. Not surprisingly, the Northside La Burrita is also on the opposite side of a courtyard from La Val's. However, the food is only recommended if you're standing in front of La Burrita and every other restaurant in Berkeley is closed.

If I don't go to Cancun, I go here and the burritos are just as good if not better! One of the best burrito places I have ever eaten at! Ok I know this place doesn't serve the most authentic Mexican food but, I don't care, their food is just so damn good. I always just get the regular burrito because the large is too big for me. 

There are two La Burritas, one on each side of campus, and both have the same quality of food. I prefer this La Burrita because it is less crowded, you can have an unlimited amount of homemade chips, and they have a TV.

This place gets 5 stars all the way.

I came here to grab a quick dinner after a day of rafting. Some people say that the Southside location is better than this one and it does have more menu options, but the good thing about this one was supposed to be that there are unlimited chips (since it's self-serve). However, I was disappointed upon opening the chip oven that it was completely empty except for a few bits and pieces. When I asked the worker if there were more, he said they were apparently out of chips...

What I ordered: 
- Large very veggie burrito ($5.49)

I saw that they had a new garlic onion tortilla and ordered my burrito on that, but actually I couldn't really taste the difference from a normal plain tortilla. The grilled veggies were good, but pouring salsa in the burrito definitely helped enhance the taste. Pretty filling meal, but this is just your standard Mexican fare without bells and whistles.

TIP: Cash preferred, but they take card too!

I graduated from Cal 9 months ago and I still crave their warm chips and salsa. Love Labo chips. AND they're only as limited as you are embarrassed to grab. :) Decent Mexican food and they stay up late enough for those who live on the North Side. I like this location better than the one on South Side, although the service on the other side is better.

Looking for food for cheap on the North Side of campus?  Fast service, a variety of meat and veggie options, and happy hour prices at night.  The burritos, tacos, and nachos make perfect grab and go lunch fare.  Plus an outdoor patio that shares it space with La Val's for your friends that prefer pizza over burritos.
Okay so yeah the food is only so-so but damn their chips and salsa are addicting.
It's so cheap, it's so quick.  It has saved me from starvation many times late night.

I visit La Burrita's south side location every so often, and I always get their cheesesteak burrito. So I came here planning to order the same thing, but they didn't have it! :( The menu selection on north side is a lot smaller and more boring. I ended up ordering a shrimp burrito, but wasn't very impressed. It was really wet, and hard to eat. Overall, it just didn't taste that great. The only good thing about this location is that you get unlimited chips.

Their vegetarian tacos are huge (as far as tacos go) and cheap. I can eat lunch for $2 which automatically makes La Burrita amazing. I'm almost worried they're going to catch on and make them smaller.

I have also ordered every vegetarian burrito on the menu and each has exceeded my (somewhat low) expectations. The wet burritos are a bit messy for me though.

The perfect place to grab a quick bite to eat before those late, late night study sessions.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: four stars.

Unlimited chips for poor college students? Not bad at all, LB, not bad at all...

As for the burrito, many people have problems with how wet the burritos are. As for myself, I prefer wet burritos that are dripping with flavor, so the burritos here were perfect. They usually came in two styles; one with sour cream and guacamole, and the other without. I always got my burritos with sour cream and guac, and I would top it off with loads of salsa. 

Was it "traditional"? No. Was it healthy? No. Was it lip-smacking good, modesty be damned? You bet it was.

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: zero stars.

Again, a North Side restaurant always attracts the typical Berkeley "undesirables." I am pretty unforgiving in that regard; thankfully the food is good enough to ignore the reek.

Yes yes YES! Me like-y this place. I love their chips and salsa. They keep the chips fresh, light, and crispy. The salsa is perfectly balanced too; not too spicy not too puny. You get to serve urself the chips&salsa, so I always refill mine. HA. Prices are great too, perfect for broke college students!

One of the better burritos in the vicinity of campus.  And the fact that they bake their own all-you-can-eat tortilla chips is a big draw for me.  Meat quality in burritos is okay at best, but this is a common problem among taquerias.
If you don't like La Burrita you must not like, well, burritos. They make tortilla chips fresh, too. I like this place a lot.

I might as well come out and say it--I am "psychologically dependent" on La Burrita's Very Veggie burrito. I could eat it every day for weeks without getting bored, and even then I'd only need to take a little bit of a break. 

It can be difficult to find Mexican restaurants that serve high quality, tasty vegetarian food, and I've always felt that options for truly HEALTHY burritos have been lacking at places I've frequented in the past. At La Burrita, I've found my perfect burrito:

Whole wheat tortilla, black beans, lettuce, salsa, and avocado.  All of this for only $3.90! 

It's that simple, yet the flavors are incredibly complex, and afterward, I don't feel like I've eaten a brick of saturated fat. Unless, of course, I got it wet (smothered in red enchilada sauce and melted cheese). This brings me to another point: I have been looking for a vegetarian wet burrito option for YEARS, and not until La Burrita's recent menu change this year did I find what I had been longing for.

It's mediocre, but since it's close to my office and no Mexican food in Berkeley is that great, I don't object too strenuously when my friends drag me here. I stick to veggie tacos, as the meat's not worth the calories. Chips are decent but there's only one salsa with any taste (jalapeno) and even that one tastes stale sometimes.

Better places near campus include Mario's La Fiesta and La Cascada (most would also include Cancun); even Baja Fresh and Chipotle at least have fresher ingredients. One place that's worse: La Burrita on southside.

You could do worse than La Burrita, far worse.  OK, so maybe a lot of the charm of this place is that it's kind of off the street and has an interesting interior.  Not interesting design-wise, but more of just odd.

I've only eaten here three times, and each time, the food was good.  I had to wait awhile the last time, but it was worth it.

Regular Nachos with Sour Cream - - Yummy!!

I like to stick to what I know and in this case, nachos. I order the same thing every time I go (once a week) and one order is enough for two people. The price is reasonable and as I mentioned earlier, the nachos are delish!

I decided to be adventurous one day and tried the bean and cheese burrito but found it to be quite soggy, added with the free chips and salsa, you can make your own version of the nachos (heh)

Despite the website saying it is open till 10, it is in fact, only open till 9 pm. I always prefer sitting outside as the inside never seems to be clean. There are always plates on the tables and empty baskets of chips lying around.

Overall rating - 3/5

I got food poisoning the first time I ever came to this specific La Burrita my freshman year. 

Yeah, that's how good it is.

Is it probably better than I make it seem? Yes. Do other people like it? Yes. Should I give it a second chance? Potentially.

Will I give anything a second chance if I fear getting sick and I know Chipotle is a better alternative? Absolutely not.

Evan's Thoughts

La Burrita es muy bueno!

After much thought and deliberation between giving this restaurant a 3 or 4 I had to go with it being a four for the following reasons:

1.  The Price ($3-$4 for a burrito?!  You can't beat that.)
2.  The Environment (This ain't no taco bell, this is legitimate un-americanized mexican food.  Sorry, I'm a sucker for traditional.)
3. Great food.  (My horchata was one of the best I've had in a while, and trust me I know my horchata.  Also, my shrimp burrito was phenomenal and I would definitely get it again.)

Bottom Line:  If you're looking to get all the bang out of your buck and you've got a hankering for authentic mexican food look no further mis amigos.

***************************************************
Madeleine's Thoughts

Now I loooove my mexican food, and for the price of this place, it deserves 4 stars. It is definitely frequented by college students all the time, so it is not a place for a business lunch or the likes. 

I got a side order tamale (about $2.60 I believe) but I wanted pork and they only had steak or chicken. So I decided on the chicken (though I wanted that pork tamale... :( ) and it was a decent tamale. It came with a spicy runny sauce of which I wasn't a fan. I got a side order of rice too because I assumed the tamale would be tiny (and I was right! poorly endowed tamale).

Overall, cheap and edible. Some dishes are tastier than others, but considering it is cheap cheap cheap, you might as well go here then go spend the rest of your "would have been lunch money" on something special for yourself. You deserve it. And if you don't, convince yourself you do.

List: Berkeley's Cheapest Eats

Bean and cheese burrito, 2 baskets of chips, salsa, and soda water with lime: $3.25.

The cheapskate beauty of La Burrita is found in the extras: basket of chips, free soda water at the soda machine (southside only), and free limes, radish, salsa, and jalapeno at the salsa bar.  La Burrita is second only to Dollar Curry House in value.  Five out of five top ramens.

Top of the list of places I crave to eat at, after being gone a few months? weeks? days? from Berkeley.

However, it might be safe to say that usually when I come here, I'm usually depressed or drunk, so something about them chemicals in my mind + cortisol + fatty Mexican food = deliciousness and the release of too many happy serotonin in my digestive system. 

Best things ever:
Super Nachos (+ chicken): ~$5.95
- Don't notice how they make it. Just notice the deliciousness of a 1-pound bag of crunchy nachos, melted cheese, beans (and i HATE beans normally!), shredded chicken, guacamole, mmm.
Steak Super Burrito: ~$4-5
- Comes with everything. And I mean EVERYTHING. In melted, 1000 calorie wonder. Omg.

Thus, La Bo deserves my undying affection. The destination, ultimate, for my rainy day drives & my post-depressed night morning junk food, & make-up conversations.

Also, luckily, there is another La Bo located a mere 3 minute walk from  Kips (4 from Bears Lair). Hello, end to fantastic nights with nachos.
This is a good place for lunch. The food is not too bad, and the price is hard to beat. The extra star is for the outdoor seating. Try the torta.

LaBurrita was once my stomping grounds during my college days at Cal. After a night of excessive partying, a Carne Asada burrito from LaBurrita hits the spot every time. 

It's affordable, and high in calories if you're hungry! If you go to the North side location, they have unlimited chips & salsa. The chips are kept warm and are addicting. Can't stop at just one!

Also, the North side location serves alcohol -- which may interest the students of legal age -- or some of our more daring younger ones who look like their older siblings.

There was a time in my graduate studies when I spent late nights on campus, and during that time I frequented La Burrita because I could get something relatively healthy to eat for a reasonable price at a somewhat late hour.   Thankfully, those days are over.  Studying in a windowless building for hours every night is arduous enough, but eating La Burrita and ending up with a tummy ache while trying to study is sheer torture.  

I don't like feeling ill after eating what looks like an innocent burrito, but that's exactly what happened on more than a few occasions to myself and my friends.  The shady-factor of food prep doesn't seem to be an issue unique to La Burrita, though, because I find myself feeling a bit queasy from a number of "restaurants" in the North Gate area.  

Friends don't let friends eat La Burrita.

maybe i should have ordered a burrito. well, coulda shoulda woulda, right? i ordered super nachos because i was in a munchy mood. regardless of what i ordered, my choice was unfortunate enough to warrant a measly two-star rating. 

i was disappointed. the chicken seemed to have been stewed in its own grease. orange goop pooled below the chips like dirty oil in a cars oil pan. i know nachos are greasy by nature, but this was observably beyond normal.  

i will admit right now that the prices are quite good and its in a really convenient location. for those two reasons, i will probably go back and try a burrito. im willing to give la burrita one more chance...

2.5 stars

Was in Berkeley at my Alma Mater (PSR) for a meeting and unexpectedly ran into an out-of-town friend/colleague.  So we headed over to Euclid for a cup of coffee & a chat, but she was pulled by California burritos (she's now living inthe mid-west) so we ended up at La Burrita.  

Had Carne Asada Wet Burrito- one of my favs.  Flavor was good, though it had pinto beans.  I prefer black beans.  I didn't think to ask if they had them when I ordered.  Was distracted by my need to find the bathroom.... more on the bathroom later...

Their jalopena salsa was GREAT!  Flavor of the meat was good.  Sauce on top just ok, slightly bland.  Later that same day... I had some salt issues.  Clearly this lunch was over salted, though it might have just been the chips.  They were salty and I ate them anyway.

Now on to the bathroom- It is a mixed gender bathroom with a stall and a urinal.  There is a lock on the door so you don't have to be confronted with someone using the urinal when you exit the stall- Thank God!  BUT it smells like a neglected rat cage- like old piss.  So appetizing.  :(-   Yuck.  My dining partner wanted to wash her hands, but I told her that she would not feel cleaner after using that bathroom to wash her wants.  Every surface was sticky.

Ok. Let's clarify one thing over those that have been reviewing this place poorly.  It is a college town burrito joint. It is not supposed to be gourmet. It's not supposed to have environs that please or amazing wait service or even really a clean bathroom.  What it should have?  Greasy Mexican food, cheap beer, and a collegial atmosphere.  And ya know what? It's got all three in terrific quantities.  Toss in unlimited free chips and a large salsa bar?  Freaking heaven people.  And it reminds me of my good ole days at UGA in Athens. 

Was here immediately following the US/Ghana World Cup match - they had set up TVs in the courtyard so people could watch and it was packed.  We got our food quickly, ate under a beautiful tree with the sun beating down on our heads, and enjoyed every last minute of it.  Will be back next time I'm in Berkeley.

As a college town, Berkeley has a number of restaurants which offer a selection of terrible food cooked badly and which is almost certain to deliver food poisoning or a long sit-down on the rectal confessional.

Of this selection I'm not certain if La Burrita is the best of show.  It's possible they trade the rank with other GI tract-hating human slop troughs.  What is certain is that in the past decade I've been a resident, I have had many an unfortunate share their horror stories about this awful, awful place.  Four times I had to endure the sight of some unbeliever who had brought some of their poison to my house and refused to allow me to throw it away immediately.

Four times, four different people, four trips to the toilet.

La Burrita should thank Yelp for the free 1 star that I am unable to remove from this review.

After class, I was pretty hungry. And it was right there on telegraph and Bancroft in front of the Bookstore. 

Service:
They were extremely friendly. I couldn't ask for better service. The guy even gave us a free drink cause apparently they were still in training and they were thanking us for baring with their sluggliness. 

Food:
Ninjutsu - It was pretty good. It had seaweed and japanese mayo. I didn't think it was too special, but it was unique. The bread was a little too hard/crispy for my taste. 
Wushu - I thought this was a better choice. It had pork sung and japanese mayo. It was tastier than the other. Again, the bread was a little too hard/crispy to my liking. 
Grass Jelly Drink - I liked this alot. Not too different than the grass jelly you get at the stores though. 

Price:
It was a little pricey. 
Hot dog - $4.30 + tax 
Grass Jelly Drink - $2.30 + tax

Overall:
I would recommend this place to try. Not sure if I could recommend it as a regular eatery.
Fast, cheap, delicious, and unique hot dogs. Perfect lunch between classes. I get the Wushu dog with the tranquil tea and a bag of chip :)

Bought a groupon for this place a while a go and finally got around to using it...I'm glad I did! These hotdogs rock! I'm a vegetarian so I SO appreciate that they offer the field sausage veggie option. The combo of sausage, yummy cabbage, nori and mayo is special. I don't think they charge too much. They use quality ingredients and put care into the food. I would definitely frequent this food truck again.

I was walking by and randomly gota wushu dog. The person who took the order (is he the owner?) was really nice, and it was a suny day...so i felt good and ended up ordering a combo instead of just a dog. Nice flavor, surprisingly good. It just felt a teensy bit expensive to charge $ 6.45 for a dog ad a soda when the dog itself was like less than $5. Although id be willing to pay that for a dog with slightly more meat. Overall, would like to give 3.5 but yelp wont let me!

Don't know how there are so many five star ratings on here, but Dojo Dog is definitely good - solid three (and a half) stars, but I'll round it up to four since the workers are nice and friendly and it's a budding venture.

I like the Wushu dog a lot - it's filling and tasty. The toppings make it worth the price, which is only around $4 if you're a Dojo Dog VIP (all you have to do is like them on Facebook). 

I had a Shaolin Monk dog once (don't remember the kind) and I definitely would not recommend it. It was super salty, unfilling, and expensive for having no bread and just seaweed. 

Last but not least, get the mango jasmine tea! For $1.15 it's super cheap (don't know how long that price will last) and it's yummy, a solid mango tea with a hint of jasmine (might be too sweet, depending on the day). 

I wish service were faster - again, the people are friendly but during opening week they were so slow both with dealing money and getting the food out quickly. They've gotten better but it feels like they cook one dog at a time - not very efficient.

Very unique and surprisingly scrumptious! I went here on a whim instead of the usual Vietnamese truck and I'm glad I did.

I love their new veggie dog option and they have sauces galore.
I'll definitely be coming back!

Jeff: I'm hungry and I've no money.
Celia: oh, I bought munchonme coupons for Dojo Dog.
Jeff: that's enough to feed half of a quarter of a person.
Celia: ...
Jeff: how many did you buy?
Celia: 2.
Jeff: you need 16 to make one meal.


But yeah. I would visit more regularly if it were more filling and WAAAY less salty. Cool idea and the buns are soft, chewy and well-toasted-- but no comparison at all to Top Dog.
I never thought I would be having a Hot-Dog Handroll but it just goes to show, you never know...it was surprisingly good!

You can get the hotdog on munchonme for 2.99. Great deal, However I wouldn't expect to get full by just eating one hot dog. For the price of $5 per hot dog, it is comparable to Top Dog here in Berkeley. They should have a deal of 2 hotdog for $8! Otherwise. the owner is actually a berkeley undergrad student too!

I ordered Wushu dog and it was a mixed of eastern and asian twist. Sweet mayonnaise sauce and shredded pork toppings on top of salty hotdog tastes AMAZING.  

- 1 star, it's just too expensive!

Might be in the minority here but I MUCH preferred the Ninjitsu (seaweed, teriyaki sauce, Japanese mayo) over the Wushu ( pork sung, katsu sauce, Japanese mayo). Something about the intense sweetness/ savoriness of the pork sung compounded with similar favors in the sauces and the meat makes for an uber-salty/sweet hotdog. 

In any case, the idea of an Asian-style hotdog is interesting and unique and the truck itself is adorable! I do think that the hotdogs on a whole could benefit from some neutral veggies like thinly sliced raw cabbage or something, just because all of the competing flavors are really strong and the bun doesn't quite balance everything out. 

Hope dojo dog (and the corresponding munchonme coupon) sticks around!

Friendly service every time I've been there. Dojo Dog makes life easy when you're a college student tired of GBC, Crossroads, and Cafe 3. It's not as pricey as other places -- heyo, Chipotle -- and tastes twice as good. Plus, it's located right on campus. 

My personal favorite is definitely the Ninjitsu, though I have some friends that will fight for the Wushu.

This place is incredible. Yeah a hot dog costs like five bucks but it's very filling and the flavors mesh beautifully and you can taste the quality and the different textures ahhhhhhh 
Everyone who works there is also incredibly nice. I love the kendo dog, at first I was like...fish flakes? But then I had a sample and I immediately ordered one.
