The one with the seaweed and teriyaki is also awesome. I havent tried the pork sung. At any rate, everyone definitely needs to try it at least once!

I have to say I am pretty disappointed in this place.  I had very high hopes with being blown away with such creative hot dogs but it all just fell flat.  I bought a groupon so was able to try one of each.  After tasting each, it came down to the fact that I basically just paid for the novelty of tasting asian inspired ingredients in a hot dog.  Which all of the ingredients, might I add, I already had in the house and totally could have done myself.

I think the flavor could have been vastly improved if they didn't use just a plain old hot dog.  At least have the options to have polish sausage, hot links or bratwurst.   The bread is also non special typical hot dog bun.  Not to mention they were all pretty small in portion- I mean for $4.60 per dog, they were long but very skinny, no mass to it.  With the such plain average sausage and bun, I was hoping the sauce and other toppings would compensate but those didn't either.  The sauces didn't do much to compliment the boring link and all the other toppings such as the cabbage were pretty bland.  The shaolin monk was particularly disappointing as it appears very creative but ended up tasting exactly how it looks- take a flat sheet of seaweed and wrap it around a hot dog.  Of the 4 dogs, my favorite was the one with pork sung, and that's only cuz i love pork sung, so the hot dog cant even take credit for that.

For over priced asian inspired hot dogs, I would rather head over to Doggie Style in Alameda- at least they have much more variety of toppings and links there.
This tasted pretty amazing..

The dogs themselves are decent with a nice snap, but for 2 dollars less you can get a top dog, or for one dollar more you could get 2 top dogs. This is essentially a gimmick which I think can only be called tasty because they use good bread and hot dogs, and then have mayo or mayo related sauces on it to give it that extra savory bite. The other bulk purchased dried asian stuff isn't really necessary but I guess it gives a reason to charge alot more.  I'd like an advertised option for just a normal hot dog, for 3 dollars. then i may come back more.

Kind of on the pricier side for a hot dog but after eating it you'll realize that it was worth it. The meat is fairly good quality and the buns are nice and toasty (comparable to Top Dog). Whereas Top Dog focuses on the types of meat, flavors of meat, etc., Dojo Dog focuses on the toppings that are put on the hot dogs. The toppings (nori, bonito flakes, teriyaki sauce, pork sung, etc.) are combined in a unique way adding texture and flavors to your otherwise average hot dog. It is basically a very delicious Japanese style hot dog. The hot dogs also come in a low calorie option in which the dog (with your toppings) is wrapped with lettuce in seaweed. When they gave free samples out, I tried this, it was pretty good but the normal hot dogs are much better.

I was visiting Berkeley with a friend and I actually had a craving for hot dogs before seeing this truck....once I saw the truck, I took it as a sign that it was meant to be for me to have a hot dog.

I made a quick decision based on the pictures on the side. Apparently not your average old weenie. All of them were Asian inspired. I ordered the Ninjitsu dog (the one with lots of nori in it). The guy who took my order was nice.

Hot dog was not bad, but I felt like it needed an additional flavor to it. Like daikon or something. Maybe I should have chosen a different dog. Overall dog was good though. Very filling. They were generous with the toppings it came with.

I wouldn't mind trying another weenie.
I got the dojo dog and it was surprisingly good. japaese mayo and seaweed was def a first for me. recommend

The people were really nice, so that's always cool. First, the girl that took our order helped us figure stuff out 'cos we were totally not prepared. Once we got it together, the guy who handed us the food was also nice. 

The food was a little hit or miss, kinda bland at times but also interesting with the Asian inspired stuff like bonito flakes and nori. Not necessarily craving it but might return for the Wushu, which I thought was stronger than the rest.

I tried out Dojo Dog during their test run on the Berkeley campus and it was delicious. I recommend the Taekwondog, it was a really interesting combinations of flavors. The sausages are high quality, but I think the sauces really made the difference. Definitely will eat again in the future.

Their hot dogs are pretty good (who knew seaweed on a hot dog would actually taste good?) But I don't think they're worth $5. Top dog is considered an expensive hot dog and its $3. I would consider Dojo Dog for $3, but not anymore because in the end, a hot dog is a hot dog. 

Also the service wasn't as great as other people have said. Maybe you have to be the owner's friend to get that kind of service because the guy that took my order (assuming he's the owner) was more preoccupied in talking to his friends in line behind me than in taking my order.

Fantastic service every time I've been to this student-run food truck outside of UC Berkeley's campus. I think the fact that this is a student-run establishment is absolutely fantastic, and the food is absolutely amazing to say the least. The blend of American and Japanese cuisine is genius, and the Ninjitsu dog is fantastic, especially when paired with Dojo Dog's TranquiliTea.

I would definitely recommend stopping by and trying out this innovative, new type of fusion cuisine!

tried this place because these fools were hella troll on sproul. they were giving out free samples of Dojo Dog's mango jasmine green ice tea drink (which is actually refreshing and delicious, i really liked it.) the dude there at the table was just full of surprises, first offering me a FREE dojo dog flyer and then when I was about to leave he was like WAIT. DO YOU WANT A DISCOUNT AT DOJO DOG...FOREVER? so i filled out a short survey and they signed me up for dojo dog elite. 

with the flyer and the v.i.p. sticker they gave me i got the ninjitsu dog with the free full sized drink for 4.25. the hot dog was kind of messy because of all the sauce they put on top of it but i was really surprised on how delicious it was. I would have never thought to top a hot dog with seaweed, sweet mayo and terriyaki. and i really liked that the hot dog was wrapped in a crispy hoagie rather than just a bun. it was really creative twist and for 4.25 for a hot dog and drink, i'd come here everyday.
This is certainly the BEST, MOST GORGEOUS, LEGIT HOT DOG ever.

Wonderful truck! Extremely friendly service. Incredible story behind the business. Got a groupon so I got to try all the hot dogs. My personal favorite was the shaolin monk. This dog comes with no bun, and in its places is a seaweed wrap. Utterly delicious!!! My little boy boy devoured the toasted bun and veggie dog. 
As someone that used to own and operate my own hot dog truck, I can appreciate this student run small business. Two thumbs up!

If you're looking for more than your average hot dog, then Dojo Dog has it. Their three styles of hot dog provide really unique asian flavors. The french hoagie roll holding up the dog definitely pushes it over to the gourmet side, but it's needed to complement the higher quality ingredients. Plus, it's a great change from your usual soft bun, giving hot dog lovers more chew and crunch.

Definitely come check out Dojo Dog. Pretty unique experience, and they're selling tea!!!

How unique. Hot dog with a twist. I tried the Shaolin Monk, which was delicious!

I would've given them 4 stars if it wasn't so pricey. They dock a dollar off if you have VIP status simply by liking them on Facebook. An extra star if it didn't seem like something I could've put together.

Nonetheless, my taste buds were satisfied, but my wallet wasn't. :/
They make your hot dog right away. Well at least their regular one. The hot dog is pretty long and it is filling.

Being Chinese, Peruvian, German, Polish, and Native American, I love fusion food.  I never stray away from combinations that may seem a little strange, but this was kind of gross. I love nori and I love hot dogs, but I don't love the Ninjutsu dog.  Putting aside my opinions about  this combination of foods, the individual ingredients weren't the best. The hot dog they  used reminded me of the hot dogs they served in my public elementary school.  The type of dogs where you really question what kind of meat you are eating. The teriyaki sauce was too sweet for my taste, and overpowered the rest of the flavors. The bun was good, but it wasn't as grilled and crispy as I would of liked it. On a positive note, the nori was good by itself.

The only thing I really enjoyed about this place was Tranquilitea. It's tasty and refreshing. Though, I don't know if it's necessarily worth going back for. The service was fast and polite, so no complaints there. To me, receiving a Dojo dog is like receiving a mud pie from a child. I love the creativity, but there's no way I'm putting that thing into my mouth.

For college students on the run, Dojo Dog is a great place to pick-up a hot dog. 

Everything on the menu is neatly organized and they are often running promotions which makes it easier on a student's wallet. All the hot-dogs are 100% real meat and the toppings are innovative and flavorful. 

I personally enjoyed the Wushu Hot Dog. The cabbage cut through the pork very well and the sauce on top added a nice element to the overall hot-dog. Also, it should be noted that the bun wasn't soggy due to all the fillings and additions. It still retained its crispiness making for an excellent hot dog. Definitely come and enjoy a Dojo Dog if you are in the mood for asian fusion cuisine!

Perfect for a quick snack on a sunny day.

Randomly noticed this food truck as I was walking on south Berkeley and decided to give it a shot. I  probably had a subconcious craving as I had recently had a Japanese-style hot dog in Japan town a few weeks prior. The hot dog was satisfying and tasty. I would have liked if it was a bit more packed with toppings and had the option to add some pickled daikon. The tranquility tea is a good compliment. 

Definitely worth checking out if you are looking for a quick lunch on-the-go or want to sit on the grass and enjoy the sun.

I LOVE DOJO DOG!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Best idea with a dog to date!! Me and the Homie Tre found this spot close to the job site.  Had the Ninjitsu and the Kendo, both was CRACKIN!!  Must try if you in the area, the tranquilitea is on hit too!  WE VIP'S BEH BEH lol

I think most of the five star reviews here are written by people who know the owner of this food truck, because their dog really is not too tasty or cheap ($5 for a dog). I had the Wushu dog, and it tasted like an average hot dog with hint of soy sauce. 

Dojo Dog is not worth the money and the stomach when you can get a cheaper and tastier dog at Top Dog.

The wushu is my favorite hot dog in EVER.
Thank you for making my monday class bearable.

The Honest Truth: It's a good idea.  The buns are good.  The dogs are small. But $5? Way too much for my wallet.

The Details: I've wanted to try it for a while because I've heard good things about it! The sign by the truck is deceiving because I thought it would be $3 and some change for the dog but instead it was $5! For one dollar more, I could get a huge calzone, or I could eat at a pizza buffet.  The hot dog itself was pretty good, the only things was that I was surprised at how small the hot dog was... I had the ninjitsu and all of the flavors were good. 
I do appreciate the concept of the truck though and props to the Berkeley student who started it up.  But if you want people to come more often, you can't make your hot dogs five dollars.

We ran into this near the slather gates- what an awesome foodtruck. 

We tried the Wushu- which has a really dry pork topping (like a freeze dried shredded pork). I admit I wasn't a fan of it but all the other toppings still made it a great dog. It had cabbage, japanese mayo, and katsu sauce. The dogs are amazing- really flavorful and they snap. Ten times better than top dog hot dogs. The bun was great too. 

Their tea was so freaking amazing delicious- jasmine mango I think. 

They're super into technology... if you like them on facebook and tell them, they give you a sticker so your hot dogs are now 3.60 (I think) instead of $4.60. When we liked them we saw if we shared their video we could get a free tea. Good dogs and freebies/ discounts that's a win in my book. 

The guy who helped us was super nice. There was an older woman who seemed a bit confused by everything... he gave her the discount price after telling her to make sure she liked them on facebook and literally got out of the truck to walk her hot dog to her since she was sitting down nearby. He spent some time talking to her about the hot dog and told him to let her know if she wasn't happy with it. He was really nice to us too. Great customer service is always an added plus. Wish I lived closer so I could eat this all the time.

I consider myself a hot dog expert because mainly, I worked the hot dog cart for almost 7 years, to put myself through college.  I'm quite a hot dog snub because after working in the industry, I know an exceptional hot dog to an ok one.   So, I don't take this lightly when I say that this is one of the best dressed hot dogs i've had. The only hot dog place that I go to is Pink's in LA and this place comes close.  The teriyaki and the shredded pork were phenomenal!  Good job!

Since my friend Serena S. has reviewed this, I shall too.

I bought my first dojo dog for late lunch during ASUC elections campaigning. It was an extremely hot day (there was another DD test run after the one I am reviewing on upper Sproul plaza by Ludwig's Fountain but it rained and I just bought food when I left the GBC). The BBQ grill was setup in lower Sproul plaza directly in front of the outdoor seating of the bears lair food court. I went later in the afternoon and my co-campaign manager recommended the Bruce Lee, but the guy in front of me bought the last one. The only remaining choice out of the three on sale was the tae kwon dog. I didn't think that the fish flakes would go well with a hot dog and bun. It came with a can of Coca Cola or Sprite for around $5. The wait isn't really bad since it's cooked right in front of you. Since it was a test run, ingredients weren't fully stocked to handle everyone hence the shortage of hot dogs.

The fish flakes surprisingly didn't affect the taste of the hot dog as well. It was more of a hint of flavor contrast from the sweet hot dog and sauce. I hope more test runs surface in the next school year with more options and varieties, while keeping costs low for students' budgets.

A suggestion I have, especially for hot days, is to swap the lame high-fructose corn syrup sodas to:
-natural cane sugar Hansen's drinks from Trader Joe's or Costco
-aloe vera drinks
-grass jelly drinks

Good luck and keep it up BAP!

Love this cute little food truck. And kudos to my fellow Cal classmate for starting this business! Great idea and the food tastes amazing. You can definitely taste the quality of ingredients and the service is very very friendly. The hot dogs are a pretty good size to fill you up during your lunch break and your orders come out relatively fast. 

My favorite is the Ninjitsu but the Wushu is really good too!

When I first heard about Dojo Dog from a friend, I was really excited to see what an Asian twist on a hot dog would taste like. I finally tried one for the first time today. I had the ninjutsu which is a crispy bun with a hot dog topped with Japanese mayo and seaweed. it was absolutely delicious! The bun was crispy, and the japanese mayo and seaweed go together really well. This is an easy 5 stars. Will definitely go back for more.
Tried Dojo Dog for the first time today and boy is it delish! Had the Mushu - IT IS AWESOME - I totally went to flavor town and I am loving it. Can't wait to try it again!

Update: Since the owner went out of his way to tell me about the VIP deal, I went ahead and got the hot dog again, this time for about $4. I did find it a tad salty with all the asian sauces, and again, the hot dog itself is quite small, but it's alright for the new price of $4. And heck, it's on the way home from school. :)

dojo dog does dogs in a french hoagie  using asian condum(ents) in a food van on the bancroft.

eats:
-ninjutsu dog(4.6)
nori seaweed,  teriyaki sauce, japanese mayo
*what was i thinking? teriyaki sauce messes it up! others ok
-wushu dog(4.6)
pork sung, japanese mayo, katsu sauce.
*more amiable to katsu sauce. prefer this one.
-grass jelly drink(2.3) "enlightening"
just seems like grass jelly. honey?, and water -just so so.  3 stars

dog bites:
-snappy dog, no jism, no taste in meat. 
-hoagie bun too big. small dog in big bun. surprised condum(ents) didn't fall off.
-shalin monk style (just roasted seaweed and lettuce) probably more suited than hoagie bun.            dogs 3.5 stars/
-used munch on me voucher.

TEMP UPDATE: There's a Munch On Me deal where you can get these for $2.99! Super great deal considering these hot dogs are almost twice the size of top dog's and are now currently the same price. Go try if if you haven't yet!

To be sure, I was a skeptic at first. Seaweed on my hot dog? 

But for real, these guys pulled it off. Seaweed hotdogs are delicious, and just might be my new favorite thing.

THE DOG: The Ninjitsu
Snappy. Juicy. Beef. Nothing at fault here.
The Toppings: Seaweed + japanese mayo! So surprised how well this went down. Please try it and become a convert.
The Bread: An A+ in my book. Toasted, chewy, delicious sesame crunchiness. 

The price? $4.50 for a pretty sizable amount of deliciousness. The flavors are good, everything tastes fresh (as fresh as a hot dog can be at least). The dog is 100% beef. Top Dog be cheaper, but those dogs are tiny and the buns aren't nearly as good. 

The owner Michael is pretty friendly and looks like he really likes what he's doing :D

2 stars ONLY because their truck is super cute.

I saw the MunchOnMe deal for this, and had to yelp it first since I'm never near Bancroft and Telegraph anymore. It sounded good, so I bought the deal.

Came here yesterday since I was on campus studying for a midterm and got the Ninjutsu. I would never pay full price for this. $5 for a hot dog? Might as well go to Tako Sushi and get a real meal. 

I liked the hoagie bun, and that's about it. I didn't taste any sauce at all, I'm not even sure what was on it. All I really tasted was the seaweed. And I hated the cabbage on the bottom. I hate cabbage in general so I guess that part's biased. But why cabbage? Anyway, part of the hotdog itself was sticking out of the bun, so I took a bite of it and it tasted seriously like nothing. Maybe my taste buds were dead or something.

Still don't like the price they charge. $3 for the MunchOnMe code is bearable, although I'd never get it again. But if the owner is from Cal, he should be more sympathetic to the skyrocketing tuition costs and lower the regular price.

Good quality ingredients as far as I know -- 100% beef links and french rolls. I personally like all of the dogs they have, especially with some sriracha :-) ... Tranquiltea (their mango-jasmine ice tea) is a lifesaver on hot days, and the combo ($5 only!) makes a good meal. Remember that Dojo is student-owned and student-run. Cheers to entrepreneurs! 
If you need a recommendation, the Wushu is the best-seller.

LOVED the original Dojo Dog! At first, I was kind of skeptical of the asian flavors on a hot dog, but it was really delicious. I came back wanting one more during the test trial run, but it sold out! So I'm definitely glad I to try one. 

Hope there's another sale soon, can't wait for new flavors!
Had their ninjitsu dog today and was very disappointed . Their filling was so salty it was practically inedible ... I was unable to finish the hot dog . Also , $5 is kinda overpriced for a hot dog .

Dojo Dog is amazing. I had it only once, but I've been craving it a few times every since. Sometimes, I would much rather have a Dojo Dog over a Top Dog. 

I tried the one with Japanese Mayo and Seaweed. I have yet to try the rest.

Love the truck's decor and concept, but its a bits expensive - we went because because we got MunchOnMe deals. We were really excited and order 1 of each: Wushu, Ninjitsu, and Kendo. They were good, but sadly, I didn't like them not enough to go back a second time. maybe if the prices were lower. The dog is a little too small for the bread.

First got dojo dog when I tried one of their samples on Sproul. I ordered the Ninjitsu (cuz I love seaweed), and I thought it was really good. The seaweed and the sauce adds a really unique taste to it, so it definitely isnt like a regular hot dog. I'd come back here again, even though I dont usually eat hot dogs. The toppings they add were good enough to make me crave this like every other day. 

I highly recommend the tea also..super refreshing especially for hot summer days.
Five stars for cute a$$ graphics---seriously, the cutest food truck/cart I've ever seen.

I basically never eat hot dogs... but Dojo Dog is so good!  I haven't had a hot dog in years, but I stopped by to try samples and it was love at first bite.

In my opinion it is far better than Barney's which seems overpriced at ~$9 for a sausage, bun, and fries.

The ingredients go well together in a unique combination, and the bun is toasted to the perfect ratio of crunchiness and fluffiness.  

They have a seaweed/lettuce wrap option, and I wish they had a whole wheat option too (but I  don't know if anyone besides me would get it...)

$5 is cheaper than a bulgogi sandwich.  If it were ~$4 I'd be going here way more instead of eating my healthy fruit salad lunches.  So in conclusion, the pricing is good.

Updated review! Saw a deal on munchonme for $2.99 for a dog. YUM! That's cheaper than top dog with all kinds of yummy asian toppings. Not to mention there's a deal where the owner is helping some clubs raise money (10% goes to the club if you bring a flyer and you can get a free drink)

Seriously awesome guy, doing some awesome things on campus!

Shaolin Monk Style -- instead of a french hoagie roll, the hotdog is wrapped in roasted seaweed wrap. Yum! This adds a crunchy texture and roasted flavor to the meal, which is a nice difference against eating the usual carbs. 

I've tried the Wushu and Kendo on the hoagie roll as well--I like the asian fusion flavor combinations, though my only gripe is that I want enough of these toppings to accompany the dog in every bite.

Other than that, really convenient, on-the-go food, and really cute truck!

I was fortunate enough to have been in Berkeley on Dojo Dog's first day of doing business. I had the regular Dojo Dog (nori and a couple asian sauces), and it was fantastic! The dog itself was great quality, and the sauces really took it to the next level. I've never had a dog quite like it..

Looking forward to trying other dogs on the menu!

So far I've only had the Shaolin Monk and the Tranquilitea but Dojo Dog is part of my weekly lunch (even though that may be bad for my health). My favorite part of the Shaolin Monk is the cabbage and the japanese mayonnaise. It brings out the hot dog in a different way compared to normal hot dogs. It's also great for low-carb diets which is something that I've been on recently. When you're on a low-carb diet it is really hard to find something to eat other than salads so this is a great alternative! 

The people that work there are also really friendly and helpful so the service is a huge plus! I admit the price is a little high but I can splurge once in a while. If you're in Berkeley you should stop by Dojo Dog especially because it's rare to taste asian fusion with fast food.

Michael Koh definitely knows what he's doing! I've been a pretty big fan of Dojo Dog ever since it opened. Especially their Tranquilitea! For those that don't know, the Tranquilitea is an AMAZING mix of mango green tea, topped with a sprig of mint. Perfect for those hot August days!

But more importantly, food! I've tried a few of their Dojo Dogs and I have to say that my favorite is the Ninjitsu. The seaweed is a surprisingly flavorful & welcome accompaniment to the mayonnaise and teriyaki (?) sauce on the dog. I would gladly have this for lunch anyday!

Dojo dog is really yummy! 

I love my pork sung and Asian sauces and I never imagined it'd ever go well with a hot dog...but it does! Asian hot dogs...hm....I was kind of skeptical at first, but Dojo dog had really great service (the dude was super friendly and kind of cute ;-p) so I thought heck why not. It was surprisingly good!  

Loved it - will definitely try again in the future.

Dojo Dog is the cutest little food trailer at Bancroft & Telegraph (across from Subway). 

They have 4 Asian / Martial Arts themed hotdogs with different sauces and grilled cabbage in each one, Ninjitsu (crisp nori & teriyaki sauce), Wushu (pork sung & katsu sauce), Kendo (bonito & wasabi mayo), and Shaolin Monk (lettuce & miso glaze. nori wrap / no bun). All are $4.60 + tax.

Got the Wushu (Pork Sung (? http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rousong), Flash-Grilled Cabbage, Katsu Sauce, Japanese Mayo http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=WKRwAslFl49_dJbGtn_fWQ). The cabbage is under the dog and the other topping and sauces are on top. I liked this arrangement because you could get a bite of the natural casing dog with each bite. 

The pork sung, katsu sauce, and mayo combo is a bit sweet which was balanced by the grilled cabbage. I liked this effort better than the Asian fusion dogs at Doggy-Style in Alameda (http://www.yelp.com/biz/doggy-style-hot-dogs-alameda#hrid:BWpnZp0LUlbz0oNJyQlx8w)

I don't know if they were going for the crackly banh mi effect with the toasted hoagie roll, but it didn't quite work with it over-toasted and hard in spots.

Ninjitsu was good, but we @JaRue2011 enjoyed the Wushu the most from @BerkeleyDojoDog with our Groupon $10 for $20 Deal!

8/17/12, Friday
5:30pm-ish
Metered parking on the street

GROUPON: Included 4 dogs only. Although drinks excluded in deal, we still got their very tasty Tranquili Tea (GET THIS).

LOCATION: Front of the campus at Telegraph & Bancroft http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#YStvef4VAApT5AhmrBLQZA

CUST SVC: Truly friendly & patient.  Keep up the great work ^_^

MENU: Here's their line up

Ninjitsu & Kendo http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#MhIjTXX3lGT-tkw8J9d5dA
Wushu & Shaolin Monk http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#9cmdKGvXAIsoEt0C01Mfng
Knockout Combo http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#oTYDivhwmZn7QfjjAJxvkA
Food Stand View http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#eQrdFetq_NHslCtYbPFg7Q

EATS: We selected to get 2 each of the Ninjitsu & Wushu for each of us. BOTH were pretty tasty, but definitely enjoyed the Wushu a lil' more ^_^ The hot dogs had a "snap" to each bite, which I always appreciate, & the flavors came through with the nori seaweed, flash-grilled cabbage, pork sung, & their Japanese Mayo. I liked the dog sitting on top of the nested cabbage in the bun, & felt the size of the dog-to-bun ratio plus fixings was great. 

Ninjitsu view 1 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#lb8AxSfT_TlCakqUTM9bdA

Wushu view 1 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#FiID0A2c8YNu0ni5MLV52g
Wushu view 2 http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#H3XqNTeNSnTwtMWUDqIOFg

Wrapped To Go http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ya60yzziKMfgyFLAdUNdFQ?select=qVILOloweaKGsT9H01Dplw#8CSS7eOKRD1ItSZOAeX2jw

FINAL BITE: We've haven't tried JapaDog in New York or Vancouver just yet, but would say the students are doing a great job here for Dojo Dog! Depending if we feel like putting an Asian twist to our normal dogs from Top Dog (just few blocks away), we can definitely see ourselves revisiting Dojo Dog if we see their stand ready to sell ^_^

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Came here for lunch with a friend with two MunchOnMe vouchers ($2.99 each!). Seriously, it was about time I supported a fellow classmate. Kudos to him for a great, unique concept and a successful business model!

We ordered the Wushu dog and the Ninjitsu dog and asked for them to be cut in half so we could share. Prices listed are the normal prices.

|| F O O D ||

THE WUSHU: pork sung, katsu sauce, Japanese mayo [$4.60]
- The two sauces were fairly powerful, especially the katsu sauce with its strong sweet flavor. As a result, I barely tasted the pork sung, which acted more like a textual undertone to the entire dog. Also, my half didn't have too much pork sung on it to begin with, which might explain it.
- My friend, however, liked the sweetness of the sauce, AND he thought the pork sung tasted awesome, so that's two reviews in one for you :P

THE NINJITSU: nori seaweed, teriyaki sauce, Japanese mayo [$4.60]
- Both my friend and I preferred this to the Wushu. The seaweed flakes are a fantastic crispy addition, and the sauces are not as prominent in this combination. Yum!

The sausage is very juicy--I bit into it and got squirted (HAHA sounds so wrong). The bun is crazy toasted too, which makes it delectably crispy!

The hot dogs are smaller in size than I expected (I'm used to Costco-size hot dogs), but it's still filling! Also, the toppings can get messy and the bun can get flaky, so make sure to grab yourself some napkins before you leave the mobile. You'll thank me later :P

Last but not least, they have a new potential drink: mango jasmine tea! It's not too watered down, and there's enough mango flavor to complement the earthiness of the jasmine tea. Delish!

|| C L O S U R E ||

The best lunch I've ever had from a shop the size of my room c:

OH. And I love how there is a small cut down the length of the sausage. I'm sure it's some brilliant grilling technique, but I like to think it's a little shelf for the toppings to sit in HAHA. :3
The Dojo Dog smelled like sushi, but tasted like hot dog. Deceiving, but yummy. The weiner was a little skinny for my liking, but its length and taste hit the spot.

Why would you do this to a hot dog? I had a sample bite of  wasabi, bonito flakes, and some sweet sauce. Ugh. 

To my Asian Brothers of Dojo Dog, with them stereotype "Hello Kitty" pictures on your cart, you are making us look bad. Even the Weiner Moblie is better.

As Dave Chapelle would say,  "Konichwa Bitches! From the Wu Tung Clan!"
The family is great! I always enjoy my conversation with them. They are very welcoming. I look forward to their pizza services soon!

My first experience here was amazing. I ordered a turkey panini with everything on it. By far one of the best paninis I've ever had. It was filling, tasted fresh and had a lot of flavor. Price($6) was well worth it. It will definitely be my new lunch spot.

Very happy to have been able to try the gluten-free selection. Delicious tuna panini sandwich on gluten-free focaccia.  You can pick exactly what goes into the sandwiches (don't skip the mustard - it's delicious).The service is very friendly, although not terribly quick, but they make up for it with warmth and quality. The lentil soup (also gf) was tasty as well. This is a lovely family-run establishment. I will definitely be back.

Dropped by this place before school started to grab a coffee and a muffin. Normally I would have gone to Caffe Strada, but they only take cash and all I had was my card.

The coffee wasn't that fresh, but I imagine it was because it was a slow day and I tend to have high coffee expectations. The muffin was a little dry, but it was good. I give it 4 stars because it is new + a family owned business.

However, when I got my bank statement, I was charged $5.00 instead of my total of $4.32... just .68 cents, but still a 15% overcharge making it an expensive cup of coffee and a muffin.

This is the place I go to when I want to start my day off right. I stumbled upon this place right when it opened (the place before it used to sell woofle waffles? whatever) and the owners are so friendly, they're the reason why I keep coming back.

The mama in the front is very sociable and can strike up a conversation about nearly anything (the weather, the importance of wearing your retainers, why students should carry chump change with them more often, etc). She's the best!

The papa in the back takes his time making the panini, but he does it with love. And they're very generous with their coffee. I ordered a small latte to pour in my thermos and the guy ended up making me a large so I could fill it up. :)

People usually take their orders to go. Don't do that. 

"If you stay, I'll give you a fruit cup!" 

I stayed.

Came into this place for the first time last week and it has already won me over as a returning customer.

As noted in many other comments, this place is a very friendly, family run cafe.  It has a cozy environment that is great for studying or just enjoying a cup of coffee on a lazy afternoon.  I too highly recommend the panini.  My personal preference is Pastrami on ciabatta with pickles, peppers, mayo/mustard,  and lettuce.  The owner really seems to put his heart into these and the outcome is absolutely delicious.  His wife is a very friendly, talkative type who is more than willing to pass the time (I'll admit, it takes a while for your sandwich to be made) talking about almost anything.  It is a little more expensive for a panini than some sandwiches (Subway, Cheese N' Stuff) in the area, but for around $7.00 or the price of the nearby Toaster Oven chain, or my favorite: Sam's Deli for hot sandwiches, it is well worth the wait and the price.

Stopped here in between classes. 
Great environment - especially for studying (upstairs). Definitely a place where you can take your food and continue to class, or stay and relax a bit. 
Very energetic and friendly employees. 
Prices were normal. 
Selection of food was small (they are new to opening) but they were excited to share their plans of more. 
The selection of food was really good though, I had a turkey panini - it was grilled to perfection (in my view). 
Overall, I had a great experience here, will be returning, and would definitely recommend it. 

Reminds me of one of those "hole-in-the-wall"s that turn out to be a great place!

Amazing sandwiches and the owner is extremely friendly.  Always asks for feedback and was willing to even make me another sandwich if I didn't like mine. 

Gotta get the pastrami on swiss.

This place is definitely not a flashy, color-coordinated, upscale type of yuppie magnet of a cafe like Starbucks or Peet's can be. And that's a really good thing, in this case.
Tivoli is family-run, and that theme is definitely detectable in the owners' accommodations of their customers - upstairs they've placed a floor light, because, as one of the owners (?) tells me, she has "a son who's a student, too, and because I'm a mother I worry about your eyes!" While I was upstairs pounding back the caffeine, she wandered past and switched on the light and asked if I was comfortable. Made me feel really at home!
Another plus is, because this place is hidden in plain sight, that it's not incredibly overrun with customers fighting over chairs. There's usually a good amount of space inside - while pretty small in itself, there's a nice upstairs area with natural light and fast Wifi (I'm looking at you, Milano). 
The coffee itself is pretty good - they don't have a ton to choose from, so if you're a coffee snob this might not be the place for you - however, their house brew is STRONG. I usually have a couple cups per day, and still get fatigued after a second cup, but after having just a house coffee from this place I thought I'd drank a mug of espresso and not drip! It was actually quite a relief to find a place that doesn't water-down their brew, so I, as a caffeine fiend, will be back here very soon.
Another plus - the barista said they'd soon be staying open ti 2am, which is probably the latest of any place nearby!

The place is only two months old, but they've sure got their paninis and coffee down.  The owner is very personable and funny, and the food was excellent.  My panini was the best  I've ever tasted; they have some peppers or pepper sauce that was out of this world.  Not hot, but just a lovely little jolt of terrific flavor.  I'll definitely be back, especially since pizza's going to be on the menu soon.  But I'll probably have a panini instead - it was that good! If you're ever near U.C. Berkeley, don't miss this place.
Delicious Gluten-Free waffles, sandwiches and pastries.  Owners are very friendly.  I'll be coming back!

I love this Cafe! Not only do they have excellent food, but it's in a great location. It's family owned which is an added bonus, and they give really fantastic customer service. The only reason I didn't give it five stars is because the service is a little slow, but they food is amazing so it's definitely worth it! It's a must-go place if you're wanting a good lunch spot around campus. I am a returning customer; I eat here about once a week and I look forward to it every time. Great sandwiches, and they have a gluten free option on almost EVERYTHING! They really put their heart and time into making things taste great, and the atmosphere is great too! Love it :)

Sunday, 11:30AM.

Meeting up with some folks from a volunteer group. Running late of course, in a deli mood. 

Quickie:
+Amiable service, was forthcoming about what was frozen and delays
+Clean establishment

And then? 
Their thing is to panini-ze your sandwich. Let them do it, it's good!

**********
Stuffed my face in:
1. Foccacia with pastrami, panini
     +Hot off the press, slight bread crunch suits the warm sandwich

Popped in briefly a few evenings ago, while searching for a quiet place to study and a bite to eat. Tivoli fit the bill, as the place was nearly empty, very quiet, very friendly. I definitely plan on return visits!

I go to Tivoli on my walk home all the time!  The owner is so nice and the cafe provides a very warm atmosphere. I can't think of anything I don't like about Tivoli Cafe! Plus they have gluten free options which is pretty great.

The Honest Truth: Go check it out! It's relatively new, and its pretty good. I really appreciate the friendliness of the owners.  They're pretty talkative and make you feel welcomed.  They're still new and waiting for the city to let them make more food so check them out and give them a chance! The vanilla latte I had was good and the sandwich was nothing amazing, but it was decent and all the vegetables were fresh.

The Details: There aren't many details other than above.  I've been there a couple times and there hasn't been anything wrong with any of the times I went.  The first time my nose was runny and as I left the owner told me to get better! He noticed! The second time the owner asked me how school was and what I was studying.  She was really nice and took an interest in how I was doing.  The environment of the cafe is a little sterile, maybe because they're new and they don't have that many decorations.  I can't wait to try more of their food once they get permitted to do so and I'll definitely be back.  Not many places have lasted in that location and the owners are so nice that I hope they stay! So check them out!

Super friendly staff, great to talk to. Nice little spot to stop for a coffee and dessert or stay longer to study. They have a great gluten-free menu and I'm looking forward to the deep-dish pizza additions and mediterranean plates coming! Will visit again for sure. Thanks George!
Great food and service. They have one of the better paninis in the area.  For a special treat, get the hot chocolate topped with whip cream :)

Very friendly, family run business. They are just starting up with a lunch menu of cold sandwiches and paninis so Ill be looking forward to their pizza menu.  

The paninis are toasted nicely but I'd be looking for something with a bit more flare like a house made sauce for the bread, rather than mayo/mustard, and a house made potato salad.  I bought sandwiches and sides and thought that the price was a bit high to be competitive for that area around the University.  I'll give them time to develop their signature menu that will be a crowd pleaser.

The upstairs was cozy but  they will probably need WiFi for the student bunch. The bathroom was in desperate need of cleaning.

1. Get the turkey panini on foccacia with honey mustard, lettuce, tomatoes, and pepper jack. It will warm and fill your hungry tummy. If you eat in, you also get a small cup of cut fruit. 

2. Service was very friendly! The owners came by to refill our water cups, and they like asking about your day and genuinely wish you well. :)

3. I will be coming back very soon!

I love this place. 
It is family owned, everyone extremely kind and friendly. I go here regularly because I not only love the environment, but the food is delicious as well. I usually get the homemade lentil soup. I've met the owners several times and I'm ashamed I've forgotten their names, but the father uses the same recipe his mother did when she sent him off to school with the most perfectly spiced heart-warming soup in the world.
(I also get the gluten-free waffle (usually with nutella and bananas.) It's so great to have this option.)

In short, there should be more places like this one. Let's make it happen. Go here please. Go here now.

A thoroughly warm and delicious experience.  And I'm not just talking about the amazing egg salad panini I had.  The food was definitely spot on.  The egg salad was thick and full of honey mustard flavor (you can customize your sandwich and I opted for honey mustard and no mayo).  It was served between two slices of the dutch seed Acme bread which was panini-pressed into two thinner crispy slices of carby-goodness.  Every bite of that sandwich was the perfect combination of flavor and texture so that even though I was full 3/4 of the way through, I couldn't stop until every last bit was devoured.

Just as important though, the owners were genuinely friendly.  It's a mom and pop shop (literally, the mom was my cashier and the pop made my sandwich right in front of my eyes, even asking for reminders on what I wanted on my sandwich while he was making it).  And their sons also help out.  The warmth of the family atmosphere really encompasses the customers and I ended up having a really natural and lighthearted conversation with them towards the end of my meal.  They really make you feel welcome and at home and have a smile for you from when you walk in to when you leave.  And none of it feels contrived at all.

I had such a lovely experience and would definitely, definitely recommend coming here for lunch.

Excellent food! My sandwich tasted delicious and was perfect with a side of fruit. Great service, the owners are very approachable and nice to talk too. Overall a great lunch and I will certainly go back once the semester begins.

I almost don't want to write about this place in case more students discover and steal the cutest cafe that just earned a top position among my regular study spots. 

Go for a panini. They have a wide selection of breads including focaccia, ciabatta, wheat, sourdough, dutch crunch, and more to choose from. Their sandwiches are highly customizable, with a similarly wide selection of veggies and dressing to choose from. I got a pastrami panini on ciabatta bread with mustard, mayo, lettuce, tomatoes, and onions. I especially liked that the onions were the sweet white kind, because I was expecting the normal spicy purple kind. Also, I've concluded that the panini press is a revolutionary machine: when all the ingredients are simultaneously toasted and flattened, they meld together to create a harmonious blend of savory meat flavor enhanced by the juiciness of veggies and sauces. The total was an amazingly reasonable $6.25 (it might be more if you add fancy ingredients i.e. avocado, cheese) which is a steal for a very filling meal. 

As other reviews mention, this is a Mom 'n Pop establishment: when I came, the daughter took my order, the dad was working in the kitchen, and the mom dropped in some time later. The family vibe really does make a difference at least for me; I like to feel as if I'm in someone's home and they care a lot about making their guests comfortable. There might have been a hiccup in the kitchen because it took almost 30 minutes to get my sandwich, but it was easily forgivable because I thoroughly enjoyed my meal and their friendly service. I really want the owners to do well and will definitely come again!

I had my eye on this place ever since it opened a few months ago and replaced Woofle. But, I'm not an avid coffee drinker (it makes me hyperactive and chatty, and if you know me, you know that I don't need anything besides air to get me going), so I really had no reason to go here.

Until a Thursday afternoon rolled around. I had been up since 8 AM, and I had a 3 hour lab to beast through. I dropped by to pick up a small cup of Joe. There was no line, although every time I've walked by I've seen cops milling around with their drinks in hand. Perhaps they've found a new place to replace donut shops?

The place has two small tables if you want to sit and eat. There are a few pastries for sale, although not too many. It was $1.79 for a SMALL HOUSE COFFEE. Actually, it was a pretty big cup, probably a medium by any other cafe's standards. I added some milk (they ran out of half & half...or I didn't know how to work their jug dispenser) and a packet of brown sugar and was on my way. My coffee was more bitter than I would have liked, but I am by no means a coffee connoisseur.

It took me 10 minutes to get in and out of the cafe, even though there was no one ahead of me. This was because before I even got around to ordering, the owner started talking about his life. He's the father of three sons, who all attend Cal, and he spent a few minutes praising his oldest son's academic prowess and favorable future prospects. He then transitioned in talking about how he plans to add more food options to the menu, such as Mediterranean/Greek and pizza. Now, as much as I love hearing about other's kids (as a future Asian mom, I anticipate I'll be hearing A LOT about everyone else's kids and their knack for calculus in 5th grade, or whatever the fad is nowadays), I kind of just wanted to place my order and go. But he was nice, so no bigs. 

Small house coffee for $1.79. Chatty but friendly owner. Good hours (7:30 AM - 9:30 PM, although they're thinking of extending it to 1:30 AM once they expand their menu). $5 credit card minimum.

This family-owned and operated caffe is my new go-to lunch and work spot.  They have impressive gluten-free options, including a gluten-free focaccia for paninis, waffles, and soon-to-come gluten-free pizza. There is also a limited selection of lactose-free items including greek yogurt and soy milk.

The coffees are pretty standard, but the sandwiches are KILLER. Everything is fresh, even the tuna salad, and extreme care is put into the construction of every order. If you decide to eat in, you get a small little dollop of fresh fruit which is nice. 

The owner recognized me from my 2nd visit, and he's always anxious for feedback to make improvements. 

Super reasonable prices, they take cards, but do allow at least 5 minutes for sandwiches to be made.  Attention to detail cannot be rushed! There is additional seating upstairs for large groups, and free wi-fi if you have access to UC Berkeley's network.

Love this place! Every time I go I get the Italiano Sandwich with everything but pickles. It's a quick and convenient place to eat and the staff is usually really friendly. Love the atmosphere it has a vintage but clean feel to the place. The sandwiches are great quality and I love the hot peppers. Totally makes the sandwich. I've been here about 5 times and I have friends who also love the place. It's a nice little shop to get a sandwich at. I definitely recommend it.

I had to try out this place since it was a new addition to Telegraph avenue and seemed to be doing good business as it appeared crowded every afternoon. 
 The queue for sandwiches moves quite fast and there is a selection of chips or cookies that one can buy ( you receive a free drink if you buy a side !) .
 The sandwiches are priced well at under 5$ a sandwich. 
The sandwiches taste good as well but are nothing out of the ordinary. The bread is often extra thick and the taste of the individual elements of the sandwich is lost to the taste of the mayonaise and bread itself. 

Overall , a nice place to get sandwiches if you want an alternative to Cheese N Stuff or Subway.
Reminds me of a place called Potbelly back in the Midwest. Sandwiches are decent, especially for the price. The portions could be a bit larger though.
I had a vegetarian sandwich here and it was horrible. They put a few bell peppers on there and toasted it so they were still really hard. Not good at all. Cheap and not even worth it.

Had lunch here today... it was ok...

The sandwich reminded me of a kinda "california fresh"  version of a philly cheese melt. Which means it had all the calories and fat of a yummier sandwich but tasted somewhat healthier.

Would have like the mushrooms cooked more, the cheese to be noticeable (I saw it go on but couldn't tell it was there when eating it) and  would have liked more topping choices. 

Overall, it was fine food just not great.

The store had a nice workflow though and it had no line during lunch (the reason I tried it) - so those are perks.

I was looking for a sandwich place and came here for brunch.  It was either here or The Melt, but I was looking for some meat!  Pretty good price for a delicious turkey avocado sandwich.  Adding avocado is 75 cents, which isn't that bad for Berkeley.  Got exactly what I wanted: italian bread, turkey, lettuce, tomato, and avocado!  Usually have to pay about $7.59 - $8 for this #24 sandwich at Togo's, but it was less than $6 here!  Not bad at all.  A very large sandwich, too!  I was satisfied :)

Ingredients are unanimously better than Subway, bread is better, some cool ideas, very simple Oakland/student vibes, but the jury is still out on whether it's worth paying the same as a foot long at subway for what is essentially half as much sandwich. They dont exactly pile the meat on, so it's not really that much different from any other sandwich, and toasting sandwiches isn't a novel idea by any means. If it's lunch time you'll do better to save a dollar and get a heartier sandwich at The Coffee Spot on lower sproul.

The toaster oven has pretty delicious and low-calorie sandwiches for a fairly reasonable price. Due to my non-processed and no junk food eating lifestyle I am confronted with limited eating out options for those few days I am forced to eat near campus. 

The Toaster Oven has very friendly workers always making sure my sandwich comes out how I like it (turkey on wheat, light mayo, extra lettuce and onions)! I have yet to try other sandwiches because I stick to what I know is healthy and also tastes good. 

They put a significant amount of meat in comparison to Subway right across the street. They don't make the sandwiches super "wet" and drenched in sauces, so if you're in the mood for your unhealthy sandwich fix, go elsewhere, but if you are the kind of eater who prefers fairly healthy sandwiches (at least ones you can buy at a store, more specifically near cal campus) then definitely check out Toaster Oven!

See you on my usual Mondays and Wednesdays, Toaster oven!

Should've listened to the negative reviews from multiple friends. There's nothing hugely wrong about this place, but at the same time nothing stands out. I got the italiano sandwich. The meats were nice and salty, but overall the sandwich was not impressive, being more expensive and smaller in size than other sandwich places nearby (go Coffee Spot!). I don't like how the sandwich/shake/dessert menus are strewn throughout the store, and I don't like how the counters are so high that you can't see what the employees are doing. It's like they're hiding something...The place was also understaffed on Friday evening with only two workers. Efficient service, but not super fast as they claim. Won't be back again.

Cute place but nothing special.

I got the turkey on wheat with all the vegetables and avocado. Since they were having a promotion for Cal students, I got a free large fountain drink with my sandwich. The total was $5.43. Decent, considering the $0.75 add-on.

The vegetables for limited and subpar (ice berg lettuce, pickles, tomatoes, and onions) and for some reason, my avocado was smeared all over the OUTSIDE of the sandwich which made it tricky to eat. The bread+turkey+swiss cheese was good but it's kind of hard to mess up. 

As for the actual set up, there's a small space in the front right as you walk in to order and then you slide along the counter, following your sandwich. It's gets pretty narrow, especially with everyone's bulky backpacks so that was a tad annoying.

Overall, satisfied but not impressed.

I love their italiano sandwich. Just don't get it with the peppers. I wasn't a fan of them. I think it's more of a peppers mixture with other cut up vegetables like carrots and such. And I'm not a big fan of carrots. Other than that, the sandwich is fresh and toasted right. There is also no seating just an area where you can eat standing up.

This place is okay - nothing to write home about, but it'll do for a quick lunch. The prices are great and so is the giardiniera (hot pepper mix) that they make.

The sandwiches leave something to be desired.....like...meat. The bread is so thick and toasty, and combined with the toppings it kinda tastes like you're eating a sandwich full of condiments. You rarely get a taste of the meat and cheese.

It' marginally better than the Subway that's across the street. Maybe.

When I'm in the mood for a sandwich, I make it a point to go to The Toaster Oven. The warm, crunchy bread and spicy peppers alone make this place better than the Subway across the street. The works are really friendly, they have healthy options, and their menu is unique (BBQ Pulled Pork, yes please!). I love that they offer wheat and a "scooped" version of sandwiches. Plus, who doesn't love the wall of antique toasters?!

Yes, it's true: you can get a $5 foot-long across the street, but I prefer the delicious, friendly, healthy, and fast qualities of The Toaster Oven.

Came here with a couple friends awhile after it opened and was excited to try their hot sandwiches since I really like paninis. I was hoping to find a reliable sandwich place near the Berkeley campus, but it just was not to be. 

What I ordered:
- Veggie sandwich ($4.59): mushrooms, swiss and provolone cheese, lettuce, tomatoes, etc. 

The sandwich itself seemed pretty small and none of the ingredients inside were very plentiful. It just looked plain and it tasted like it too. Maybe it would've been better if they included a sauce of some sort--something to give it flavor. The bread wasn't memorable either and there are definitely better sandwich alternatives around campus. I think I could even make a better sandwich myself, so don't think I'll be coming back even though the price is decent.

Fast, friendly service. Mediocre sandwiches. Cheap Prices.

Awesome place to come if you're in a hurry between classes and only have a few bucks to spare. You'll be in an out fairly quick and they have a decent variety of sandwich options to appeal to different people.

However, if I care about the flavor and quality of my food, I probably wouldn't come here.

In a place with so much greasy food, I was pleasantly surprised! I order the Italiano and really enjoyed it. It's cheap and tasty and that's exactly what this college student needed! they asked me if I was a Cal student and they gave me the option of a free soft drink or a bottle if water. I will be coming back!

Not that great. 

About $5 a sandwich. Considering that $5-Foot-Longs Subway is right across the street, and the toaster oven's sandwiches are the same price but half the size, I expected a big increase in quality. Or at least a large increase in quality of bread, since the subway sandwiches are distinctively flimsy.

Not the case. I ordered the meatball sandwich. The bread was firm and chewy, and definitely better than subway's, but nothing to write home about, and not enough to warrant a return visit. The ingredients weren't amazing, the tomato tasted kinda bland, etc. Maybe a little better than subway's, but not by much.

Don't think I'll come back here, since Cheese N Stuff (lower Sproul on Campus) offers a cheaper price for a yummier (tho smaller) sandwich, and Subway offers a larger meal for the same price. Even the Dojo Dog place (food truck on Telegraph/Sproul) is better than this (fresh ingredients, amazing bread!)

Been here three times so far. Sandwiches are 4.99 each, and each sandwich variety is paired with a specific cheese. But you can still choose other toppings, like lettucs/mayo/mustard/vinaigrette/hot peppers/tomatoes/... The sandwich isn't as big as Subway's, but it's pretty filling for me. And it feels healthier. 

Oh, their meatball sandwich felt like a good excuse to have meatballs in tomato sauce without feeling guilty of not having any veggies with it! :D 

Definitely returning. Next time I'm planning to get their Soup too. 

They were giving out coupons yesterday - Cal students who bring their IDs and order a sandwich+side (chips/salad/soup) get a free bottled water or fountain soda!

The service was wonderful, don't get me wrong there. They were wonderful workers and got me my food quickly. 

The thing that makes this a two star review is the fact that their sandwiches ARE SO SALTY.

I ate a Turkey sandwich with everything except mayonnaise. The 'pickles and peppers' were SO salty. 

As an Armenian I understand the way proper pickled vegetables are supposed to taste, they aren't supposed to taste like salt.

I will alter my review when I have another sandwich without the peppers. 

Liked how toasty it was though. Good bread too. Nice and Cheap as well.

Still delicious. I came back for a meal today and still love it. The service is always great!--which is really why I don't think I can head back to the subway across the street. 
I got the Italian again. It was so good last time that I couldn't help myself. I actually got full off of just half of it so I saved the rest for dinner. After chillin in my backpack for a solid 6 hours it was STILL good (I know that seems kinda gross but I was in the library!).

The peppers really make this sandwich. Also try the Louisiana hot sauce they have by the soda machine.

So the weird thing about this place....

I asked for avocado, and instead they put this avocado puree thing out of a plastic bottle. It was totally gross.

Following up from my original 4 star review from before, I'm giving this place 2 stars because of the unfriendly service. 

After the grand opening the sandwiches seem near mediocre, especially when you get an attitude from the workers. You'd be better off going to Sam's Market and grabbing a sandwich twice the size of what you can get at The Toaster Oven.

For those who love sandwiches, this place is...meh at best.

I ordered the BBQ sandwich. I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it tasted like BBQ sauce and that's it. I can't even remember what was in it - that was how uninteresting it was. If you want a sandwich that's more flavorful, exciting, or has a distinct good-feel to it, I don't recommend this place. The food is just, okay. Props to it for having pretty friendly staff and iPads, though.

Bottom line: 
Toaster Oven, I liked you better when you used to be GameStop.

Two of us came in here on a random sandwich hankerin. Really good and affordable sandwiches. The bread is perfect. It is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Yum.
I got a sandwich to go for my man because mine was so good. He loved it too. 
I will be back!

3.5 stars.
sandwich (daily special bbq pulled pork) was surprisingly good, but not gourmet or anything. toasty comfort food for the first rain of the new year. also had to have an oreo shake because i love shakes. it took longer than it should and the milk and ice cream separated a lot, very homemade. they need improvement there.
the flow seemed a little chaotic and the menu is somewhat limited (like chipotle as someone else mentioned).
would have been a full 4 stars if they offered fries. chips just don't do it for me.
reasonably priced and quick (other than the shake which took 5+ minutes).

Sandwiches are solid and the price is nice. Perfect for a quick lunch or dinner, particularly if you're studying. My personal preference is the Italiano with vinaigrette.

Tip: free drink with Cal ID.

The Honest Truth:
This is a place where you can get a standard, toasted sandwich.  It isn't too big, but it also isn't too pricey.  About $5 a sandwich.  Their service is good and its pretty quick. Cal students get a free drink! Not my first option for a sandwich in Berkeley, but it isn't bad.
  

The Details:
I've been here a couple times.  The first time I wasn't that impressed.  The second time was a little better.  The sandwiches are decent.  There isn't anything too special about them.  They're around $5 and taste like a standard sandwich.  The workers are generally nice and helpful especially when it gets busy.  It is a better quality than subway, but you definitely don't get as much food.  I will say that I didn't get very full from eating their sandwich.  I got their kitchen sink which consisted of a couple different meats (salami, turkey, roast beef, ham) and it was good but nothing special.  I think if I were hungry, I would go with subway. And if I wanted to save money, I would go to cheese n'stuff.  So toaster oven would not be my first choice, but if you need a quick bite to eat, feel free to check it out. It's really close to campus so thats always a plus too.

Pros: 
- Clean atmosphere
- Quick service

Cons:
- When I got a mushroom sandwich here, the mushrooms were raw. Maybe I'm being crazy here but when i think of a mushroom sandwich, I usually think of the mushrooms as being cooked. The sandwich didn't taste good and I was disappointed.
- Nothing makes this place better than the ones around it. I think if you want a cheap price, fast service AND a good sandwich, you're better off walking a block down to Cheese N' Stuff

This place used to be a GameStop, and now it's a sandwich place that has to compete with Chipotle, Smart Alec's, SF Soup Company, and Subway for quick and on-the-go lunches. 

The Toaster Oven has a very friendly staff, operates just like Subway and Chipotle (assembly line), a diverse menu, and the sandwiches are not bad. I like how they offer a low-carb sandwich here too. You can't really screw up a sandwich, and I found nothing out of the ordinary about this place.

There's nothing spectacular or lacking about this place. They could rename it Quizno's and I wouldn't be able to tell the difference.

Prices are higher than Subway just across the street, and their portions are smaller too. With the large amount of diverse and cheaper food available in the Telegraph area, I wouldn't be coming back here.

Tasty sandwiches for quick on-the-go lunch. 

Randomly wandered into this place since I had never seen it before. I ordered the Italian sub (~$5). The tortilla soup intrigued me, but I was not that hungry. The sandwich was really well assembled and really nicely toasted. The only minor complaint is that I would have liked a slightly thicker layer of meat, but the sandwich was still delicious. 

The strange thing about this place is that they have a decently sized space in a great location, but the place feels very crammed an uncomfortable because of the layout. Sandwiches are made behind a very high counter that takes up most of the restaurant. The only places to sit are a high bench along the walkway where you order the the sandwiches. It is so crammed that they even have a sign telling you to take your backpack off when you are sitting  down because it will block the aisle. 

I know the intent of this place is for people to grab a quick sandwich to-go, but I think the layout could be improved to fit in at least a couple of tables. That said, I will definitively be returning for another sandwich and maybe some of that tortilla soup.

Toaster Oven makes sandwiches like an expedited assembly-line. It's super fast and I've never felt like I was "waiting"---sometimes I even feel rushed to get my wallet out in time. You have a number of different sandwich options, on Italian or whole wheat bread, and while I've tried almost all of them my favorite is the "piezzano," which tastes like an inverted cheese pizza. Other notable options include the classic turkey and the PB&J (yes, they make it! With the most delicious strawberry-apricot jam). 

After initially ordering, you quickly move along to the toppings bar and request whatever you want on your sandwich. It comes out of the toaster way faster than Subway (across the street) does it, and somehow ends up being more filling.

You can also select from some hipster-ish brands of chips (no Lays, sadly), a few types of cookies (I've tried them all, they're alright, not impressed but sometimes you need a little sugar to accompany your meal and it does a good job of that). There's a Cal student discount if you order a sandwich, cookie/chips, and a drink, but make sure to ask for it because they don't always remind you.

Overall, solid location, super fast service. Pretty sure I come here at least once a week because of its epic convenience factor. 

Cons: not much of a seating area. There's a counter lined up along the back wall with some bar stools, but the tabletops are too narrow to support a laptop and can barely accommodate a sandwich. But not much of a deterrent if you can just cross the street go chill on campus to eat.

In five minutes, I got a sandwich and drink for little over $5.

Not bad considering the hurry I was in. 

ps. My fav= the BBQ Chicken

The sandwiches are good but not GREAT. They're relatively well priced. I mean, I can make a sandwich just as delicious at home, but the location is convenient and the workers are super nice and friendly. I got the Kitchen Sink twice and the pulled pork sandwich once. I like how they have a low-carb option where they scoop out the bread. I never get it but its nice! Their shakes are pretty yummy though!! Tried the cookies n cream one and it was bomb.

Agree with some of the other reviewers here in that I really want to like the hot peppers (I like spicy things) but they're far too salty. Still a decent sandwich place overall, and for $5 it's hard to beat.

Basically like Quiznos (A more "gourmet" subway sandwich. A bit soggy when I at it, but the flavor was there. Price was alright but the sandwich was a bit small compared to Subway.  Good for people who are on the go.
Tastier and cheaper than Subway! Plus, Cal students get free soda! For speed, I was probably the tenth person in line and got out in less than 10 minutes, which I think is really good.
Such a clever little place. Great place for broke college kids.

Not too bad and fairly cheap, but nothing to go out of your way for.

Service: Servers are quick and responsive, and they are eager to finish your order and have you on your way. It's really quite similar to how Subway operates, and you'll most likely have your order at the cashier in 5 minutes.

Food: It's around $5 for a sandwich, which is also around the price of Subway. I ordered the Kitchen Sink (not sure why they named the sandwich that... just thinking about it makes me cringe), which contains classic sandwich inputs like roast beef, turkey, salami, ham, and provolone cheese and is then baked. I also asked to put in all the lettuce,tomatoes, and whatnot, which I always do. It was not a bad sandwich, except for the fact that it was INCREDIBLY salty and acidic. I even got mayo because I was afraid of this and thought that it would offset the acidity, and I shudder as to what it would have tasted like with the vinaigrette alternative to mayo.

Honestly speaking, I'm not sure which I'd prefer, Subway or Toaster Oven. Subway has larger quantities as well as a more versatile menu, but Toaster Oven sandwiches overall seem to taste better to me (perhaps the short and sweet approach does work). It'll probably come down to how hungry I am and where friends feel like going.

Solid place for a sandwich.  Yummy toasty bread and fresh ingredients.  $5.00 for a much more satisfying sandwich than you would get at Subway.

Don't expect to be blown away, we're talking basic sandwiches here.  However, they do make their own peppers which were quite tasty.

Went to try out this new location of The Toaster Oven.  I saw it a bunch of times in SF but never ate there, it's a chain that's now in Berkeley near UC Berkeley.  It's a good 10-15 min walk from Downtown Berkeley Bart.

Order a sandwich a person gets it started & puts it in the toaster oven, then go up a bit to another person that fills the sandwich with toppings, then pay.  Credit cards taken.

I picked Kitchen Sink on wheat $4.99.  It's not a big sandwich but they cut it in half, so if you have a friend have them get something else & share a 1/2.  A. got the Piezzano on white $4.99.  I thought the meat was skimpy in both & drippy.  Piezzano was a tiny bit better, but not by much.

Milkshakes are $3.29 - I didn't get.

Seating is counter only.  Need a key for the bathroom - I didn't use it.

Not worth a special trip, but better than Chipotle or Subway, both nearby.

Open Daily: 10:30a-10p

 Tip: Cal students w/ ID that buy a sandwich get a FREE fountain drink or bottled water during the month of January 2012!

I wasn't expecting much from The Toaster Oven, but I was actually pleasantly surprised.

The line was out the door today, but moved quickly. The space is a bit small, but I bet most people would take their sandwich to-go. You get a choice between a white or whole wheat roll and a variety of cold cuts. I ordered the 'kitchen sink' sandwich, which had ham, turkey, salami, and provolone for 4.99, which was a good price for the size of the sandwich. You can even order it 'scooped' meaning they scoop out the bread to remove some of the carbs. Once it comes out of the oven, you get to choose your toppings--lettuce, hot peppers, tomato, onion, pickles, mayo, and mustard. Not as many choices as subway, but all of it tasted fresh. The hot peppers are really good, and they sell it in a 16oz jar for 5.99

The sandwich was good--the bread was nice and toasty, the toppings were all  fresh--no wilted lettuce here. I just wish the cashier was better at her job--it seemed like she didn't want to ruin her nails punching in my order nor was she friendly. Anyways, I will probably return--the sandwich is a good size for lunch and I didn't leave feeling bloated.

I don't think this place is THAT fast. But it says they are on their door when you walk in. The toaster oven thing takes a little long..especially when you're hungry and you just remember that they said that they were fast.

Anyways, I still like going here. I've gotten the Kitchen Sink (my fav--several different kinds of deli meat) and the one w/ pepperoni and marinara sauce. I really like this place over Subway because it tastes so, so fresh. The servers are always really nice and friendly. THEIR PEPPERS ARE BOMB- I always ask for a lot of peppers. They make it themselves, I think, and they even sell it in a bottle. 

TIPS:
-Cal students get a free drink
-Don't eat in unless you want to sit at a very narrow booth with people squeezing past behind you.

I walked by on Monday for opening day but I came here tonight to grab a sandwich with a co-worker. The menu is short and simple. If you want chips, they are on the right wall underneath the toasters display but cost additional to the sandwich. The featured daily special sandwich and soup is to the lower right of the main menu board. 

To order, just tell the sandwich artist at the front what you want and choose white or wheat bread. Then you move down the conveyor belt and wait at the end of the toaster oven. There, you tell the next sandwich artist the fillings/toppings you want on your sandwich (complementary: lettuce, tomato, onions, mustard, pickles, mayonnaise or light vinaigrette, hot peppers; extra charge: avocado $.75). Then you pay+tax. 

I got the "kitchen sink" (roast beed, turkey, salami, ham, provolone cheese) on whole wheat with everything except mustard and mayo. I have to say, it looks very simple and nothing like a sandwich from Ike's but the toasted bun makes the whole sandwich awesome. I swapped half of my sandwich with my co-worker, who ordered the"kc BBQ chicken" (Kansas City-style BBQ chicken and provolone cheese) on white bread. My sandwich tastes better mainly because it was more crispy from the wheat bun. Both sandwiches are $4.99+tax. I wish my sandwich had more meat though, the bread overpowered the meat taste.

If it isn't busy, a staff member might be passing out coupons for a free fountain beverage or bottled water outside the door. I didn't know this until I stumbled upon the coupon stack beside the counter when paying. But that's fine with me since I'm cutting out the high-fructose corn syrup out of my life. I just refilled my reusable bottle with water instead, no shame in drinking tap water! 

I didn't order a cup of soup but for $3+ the price is steep. There are less than 10 stools if you want to dine-in and it is right next to the toppings area so just beware of people hitting backpacks. Honestly, the way the line is setup is completely wrong but what do I know about business... I guess I will be prepared to hear, "do you want free Toaster Oven sandwiches?" on Sproul this semester instead of "free C.R.E.A.M.".

This is a great place if you're craving a sandwich and in a hurry to get to class. Otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it because there are better sandwiches elsewhere... 

But it's quick and pretty cheap, and has all the basic sandwich combinations you'd like.

This place is really cute, but not too much seating. We came after 4 pm on the $2 promo day, and the Yelp site said the offer was still valid, so the friendly servers let us have our sandwiches for $2. Both the cashier and sandwich-maker were really friendly and patient!

I ordered the BBQ Chicken sandwich. The bread was really good, portion was just right (but don't come here if you are ravenously hungry), but the chicken was a bit dry. There's barely any sauce on this sandwich, just a heads up for those used to BBQ sauce on BBQ Chicken sandwiches. The malted Vanilla milkshake I got was really good, though the malt made it a bit chunky at times.

Overall, the food wasn't bad, the service was good, but I don't think it's worth $5 a sandwich.

Edit: I learned that Toaster Oven was running low on BBQ chicken (hence the dry sauce) since it was 10 p.m., but that the employees should have mentioned it would be a bit dryer than normal. The owner was extremely nice and earnestly wanted to improve whatever he could, so I increased my rating :) Even though I think the food is good but not the best I ever had, the customer service at Toaster Oven never ceases to amaze me!

I really wanna give this place 5 stars..but I cant for a couple of reasons. I will start by saying I got the veggie sandwich: whole wheat bread, mushrooms, bell peppers, onion, lettuce, mayo, mustard, salt and pepper, and cheese. 

With the GOOD! - Staff was super nice. -Free drink w/ cal id -Bread was soo good..

Cons -   I would have really enjoyed the sandwich if the mushrooms were cooked. Apparently they were raw..It is really easy to cook mushrooms with a bit of salt and pepper, making a super delicious and savory vegetable. 
- I also would have really liked more options, like cucumber and olives. 
-I really did not like the avocado paste. I wish it had been actual slices of an avocado, it adds a totally different texture and feeling to the sandwich. 
-Please offer mini salads (even if pre made!) Thank you! 

Overall, I will prob. eat here again, but if they made those changes...OMG..

For the people from the west coast:
The sandwiches from this place are like a mini version of quizno's in way that the bread is toasted. In terms of size, they are equivalent to a 6 inch from subway. The bread is much softer though, so even though it's toasted, it's still not as crunchy as quizno's sandwiches. I guess it's like the child from a subway-quizno marriage. 

For the people from the mid-west:
These sandwiches are almost identical to those of Pot Belly's. There is a strong similar in the menus and in the taste of  makes me wonder if the two franchises are the same. 

It's about $6 a pop and it's the perfect size for lunch. These are definitely not as tasty those from the deli, but I have particular sandwich needs - I want meat! & veggies &lots of both, so much that the sandwich explodes- this place doesn't satisfy me. I'm sure fans of Pot Belly would love this place though.

Coming to the toaster oven, I expected their sandwiches to be radically different, but I was extremely disappointed. 

I ordered the meatball sandwich, which was 6" long and came with meatballs, marinara sauce, and lots of cheese. The sandwich basically tastes like Quiznos or a hot one from Subway. 

At 730pm on a Friday night, they had run out of the soup of the day. Seeing how the restaurant closes at 10pm, I was unsatisfied.

One cool thing I noticed was the cashiers use iPads instead of registers!

Toaster Oven is a cute little store with a neat set up. Kinda confusing where to enter the line to order. Like the other reviews, your sandwich rotates down the line. Pretty happy staff are on hand. They get three stars. I had the $4.99 meatball sandwich  and $2 fountain drink which gets one star. Nothing special, but a nice crew with cool hats.

Subway, don't you worry. The $5 footlong is still a winner.

They lost my sandwich. It went in the oven, but never came out. Confused, I waited hungrily as people filed past me. So I had to re-order it. It is smaller than a Subway footlong, but cheaper, and in my opinion tastier.

I also ordered an Oreo milkshake. The first few sips were deliciously sweet, but as I neared the half-way point I felt nauseous. It was McDonalds level sweet. But still good.

I like the decor here. It suits my hipster tendencies.

the toaster oven offers 9 meat sammies (4.99) and 3 veggie sammie(4.59)
sammies are assembled conveyor belt style
1st associate takes order, assembles sammie, puts it on coveryor belt which toasts the sammie (quiznos does this too)
2nd associate puts on all the toppings, veggies, etc., packages sammie
3rd associate collects the money.

eats: italiano(4.99) on italian bread.
-mortadella, capricola, salami, pepperoni, provolone cheese
can actually see and tastes the meat, peppers king of big.
