crumbs:
-price better than subway, more meat, more taste, less vinegar
-only  2 bread options, wheat and italian.
-good value at 4.99, 3.5 stars.
-process is pretty fast, thus, short lines.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

The Toaster Oven had a promotion today where, from 11 AM - 4 PM, any of their sandwiches were only $1.99. I was lucky to have walked by this place the day prior, and I made a mental note to grab one of these before my office hours.

You walk in and make an immediate right turn, which is the start of their line. On the wall, there is a super cool display of chips, $0.99 for regular chips, $1.39 for gourmet chips. They have soda in a fridge nearby.

When you approach the counter, someone asks you what sandwich you would like, and if you would like white or wheat. The meat and cheese are piled onto the bread and placed in the toaster, which is picked up by someone as you round the corner of the counter. One of the many staff will pick up your meat/cheese/bread sandwich and help you pile on your choice of toppings (mayo, mustard, homemade hot peppers, lettuce, onions, pickles, tomatoes, with avocado an extra $0.75). You can also opt to replace the mayo with a light vinaigrette. Your complete sandwich is cut into halves, wrapped, stuck into a bag and placed on the counter for you. You walk down to the end, where you pay for your meal and can potentially order soup and salad.

Service is fast: from start to finish, it took about 10 minutes, including the long line of students waiting for $2 sandwiches. My sandwich helper was really nice and smiled the whole time, whereas the sandwich helper helping the person next to me looked tired and unhappy to be there (she smacked the finished sandwich on the counter...lol). Then again, they seem to be students, and making sandwiches is not their lifelong passion. Or maybe it is.

|| F O O D ||

KC BBQ CHICKEN: Kansas City style BBQ chicken, provolone cheese, on wheat bread [$4.99 | with promo, $1.99]
- I ordered all the toppings except for the mustard and the hot peppers. They pile in a lot of lettuce. I asked for extra pickles, but I'm not sure he gave me them...
- They have chopped onions instead of sliced onions! Win! Onions are so much tastier in cute cubes!
- Imagine pulled pork, but instead of pork, it's chicken. That's KC BBQ chicken. It was incredibly juicy and moist and mm mm good! It did start softening the bread after some time, but...
- The bread is toasted to the level of genius, AND it retains its crunch! I was only able to eat half of my sandwich before office hours, and even an hour later, the bread was relatively crunchy, despite the BBQ sauce and veggie water.
- Fresh veggies. Good.

|| C L O S U R E ||

The crunch of the bread lessens the sogginess of the sandwich, which makes it better than Subway in this aspect. For $5, Subway gives you more food, but the quality of meats is better. Also, the servers here are fast and aim to get you in and out in a jiffy. Subway takes their sweet, sweet time. If you can spare the extra dollars in return for saving a few minutes of waiting, go to Toaster Oven.

Oh, and small thing. The cashier asked me if I wanted a receipt. I said yes. She proceeded to crinkle the receipt and toss it before helping the next customer. When I asked her about my receipt, she looked puzzled, and she then apologized. o___o;;

The food is mediocre, but the staff is pretty friendly.  We ordered the lemongrass chicken rice plate and duck rice plate.  Lemongrass chicken barely had lemongrass flavor, and was slightly cold upon arrival.  The duck on top of my rice was admissibly small, and the side spicy chicken'n'veggies it came with was the star of the plate.  Probably won't come back again, but there are a few other asian restaurants in the same food court that look appealing.
Large portion, and the quality you would expect form that.

Pretty cheap eats and large portions for the price.  It's nothing to write home about though.  If you're low on cash, hungry and in the area it's a good place to go.  Good place for a quick lunch or dinner with a group of friends if you're not looking for anything fancy.  If you're looking for good Vietnamese food though, I wouldn't go here but try one of the places downtown.

This is really good value for good-tasting and non-unhealthy food. For $6.60 you can get a portion large enough to serve you for one and a half meals. Get special #3: Pork AND chicken and mushrooms with yummy garlic sauce over white rice.

3 stars for taste
5 stars for price

If you happen to be a hungry traveler, bikers especially, needing all your calories, Camile is the place to go. Budget is your concern, Camille is your fix. All the dishes cost around $6. You get a lot of food too. 

I did a family style menu when I went with 4 hungry bikers. Everyone got their spicy fix, filled their tummy with delicious pho. You really can't complain when a good dinner costs under $30 for 4 people. As for the quality, this isn't a place you take to impress your girlfriend. It is a quick and filling meal, bang for your buck, I would definitely come back to Camille time and time again to get their clay pot dish. The rice is cooked so softly, that all the flavor, juices of the meat gets absorbed into the rice. I love this dish and I will recommend it to every Asian needing a little bit of home-style cooking. 

Final note: cheap / filling / home-style / More chinese than vietnamese.

I never really venture to this side of campus, but today I made an exception. With a craving for Asian food, my friend and I decided on Vietnamese. Like many of the Asian restaurants near campus, the prices were reasonable. Unfortunately, I made the mistake of ordering the lemongrass chicken dish, which was tasteless and dry. In the end I ended up covering my chicken with soy sauce and sriracha sauce to somehow finish my meal. If I ever come back again, I will be avoiding chicken dishes for sure.

Its okay. I got the seafood soup and it wasn't that great. It wasn't bland but it seemed like it just had a lot of salt and not spices. I also wish they had given me some lemon so that I could squeeze some on top. Other than than the soup came with a couple of shrimp, some scallops, cilantro and some ham-tasting meat.

Next time I will opt for the Chicken or Pork Vietnamese sandwich. That looked good and it seems like its one of their most popular dishes because I saw like three people eating them.

Dropped by here with a friend to grab some Pho randomly, and can't say I was surprised by the low quality ingredients in the soup. I realize that Pho is a sort of greasy and oily dish but this was way beyond what I'm used to, and for $6-8 I'd rather go to Pho places on Telegraph. Definitely found bits of pure fat floating in my soup, and instead of a clear broth it was kind of viscous. The vegetables, especially bean sprouts, were soggy and chewy instead of crisp and crunchy. I'm not quite sure what happened in the kitchen but I wouldn't recommend this place for hangover cures or even random drop bys for Pho. My friend had the Kalbi hot plate, and it looked good but when I sampled it it was definitely way too sweet. Not quite sure what a Korean dish is doing in a Vietnamese restaurant either, but it's not like they do it well anyway. Regardless, for a hole in the wall restaurant it's ok, not sure how well the other dishes taste but definitely not coming back for Pho.

what'd i tell ya, the dirtier the restaurent, the more authentic/better the food is. It's definitely one of my favorite restaurent in the north side, and have much better pho than south side imo. 

The price is relatively cheaper (ranging from 5.75 for a bowl of pho to 6.75 for a combo or rice). They are amazing and fast cooks, so if you're rushing, it's the perfect place. They also don't care if students tip them or not. They put so much ingredients in their pho and dishes that I was starting to wonder why they haven't moved to the Southside to dominate where there are more starving customers/students. I tried their grasslemon chicken, and it was a huge piece of meat and you can really taste the lemon zest. I also tried their Saigon style noodle, I've been to many good pho restaurants in asian places, but it can actually top some of them because their choice of meat had such a great variety and their texture of noodle was on the chew-ey side (which i like), and not overcooked. what i don't like is how overpriced the sandwich is, and it wasn't particularly impressive.
Their pork banh mi (Vietnamese pork sandwich) is to die for- Cheap, big, amazingly tasty, and generally just the best thing ever. If you like this sort of thing, your in for a treat.

It confuses me how there are two Asian ghettos in Berkeley and how they are on opposite sides of the campus. This was my first time at the Northside Asian ghetto. This one is just a tad bit more ghetto but I love the way the tables are placed really close together and how you can smell different varieties of food in one area. The person sitting to the left of you could be eating Korean japchae, the person to your right Japanese sushi, and the person across from you a top dog (hehe okay not that Asian but you get the gist).

I opted for this Vietnamese joint called Camille. The lady behind the cash register was a sweetheart! She was very welcoming and friendly :) I ended up ordering a Vietnamese BBQ pork sandwich to go. 

My sandwich was huge! It was packed with meat and the veggies were crisp and had a nice sauce with it. While the sandwich was tasty it was not the best banh mi i've had would have loved it if they could add pate or make it a little smaller or neatly packed so it wouldn't be so messy to eat.

Check this place out if you're looking for a quick Asian lunch that won't put you in food coma but is satisfying!
$5.50 Vietnamese sandwich with a drink.  It is decadent and so delicious.

Honestly, I order one dish 95% of the time here and never tire of it - the beef stew with rice. For under $6.00, you get a big bowl of hearty beef (fatty and lean cuts) and lightly stewed veggies. The stock is hearty but not too rich and goes great with the rice. I always feel satisfied and full by the end of the meal, and my conscience rests easy knowing what I just ate was pretty damn healthy for Asian fast food. For those who are feeling extra hungry, this item is definitely bigger and more filling than anything else offered in the North Asian Ghetto except the pre-cooked meat combos from Gonmaru.

A big plus with eating at Camille is that they serve a decent hot and sour soup with every non-soup entree. 

The spring rolls are also relatively good here, but many of the other dishes are rather mediocre. They're also one or two dollars more expensive than entrees at TC Garden, a neighboring competitor. 

Overall, this is my #1 or #2 choice when eating north of campus. Remember, the beef stew can't be beat!

I came here looking for some good Banh mi (Vietnamese sandwiches) and was sorely disappointed.  The restaurant owners are Cantonese and do not know how to make good Vietnamese food.  The bread was hard and cooked, and I'm pretty sure it had coleslaw in it.  The tofu was prepared like general tso's tofu.

The restaurant proprietors also called me a "Gui Lo", which isn't very polite, even if they think I don't know what it means...

The #8: Bun cha gio thit nuong (vermicelli bowl with grilled pork and spring rolls) is pretty good here.  Service is fast and the prices are reasonable.  Avoid the clay pot though, that one wasn't very good.

Based on the rice/noodle plates, the food here meets my standards for Vietnamese cuisine.  I have yet to try the Pho.  But during lunch, this place is so crowded. You won't have much luck finding an empty table.  It takes about 10 minutes to get my to-go order.  My favorite is the lemongrass beef and shrimp noodle bowl. The pork with egg roll is just as good.

The last time I went, there were about 4 bins on the floor, overflowing with dirty dishes.  They need more space, and more help.  But at least the workers smile.

I always get the pho here. The soup is really rich with beef and spices. The beef is thicker than pho hoa, but still good. If you dont want beef balls, tell them and they'll even give you more sliced beef. They don't have beef tripe though. The cashier and cooks speak Catonese, and they have come to know me. 

The seafood soup is decent if you like fish cakes. I don't think the noodles go with the seafood soup. 

The sandwich is really good because the meat is hot and warm (pork) and isn't dry. The beef is dry though.

 If you aren't sure, ask the cashier and she'll suggest what's good.
Great place!

The trouble with this place is that you have to go through a trial and error process to filter out the numerous mediocre dishes from that one special dish worthy for your appetite.  As a matter of fact, this actually applies for all the asian restaurants in the "northside asian ghetto."

After 4 long years of pouring my money into these businesses, I've discovered that my favorite place to eat is at Camille because of the 5 Spices Roast Chicken.  The price is around $7-8 but the portion size is very generous; it can serve as two meals.  You get a whole chicken leg and thigh with veggies and rice.  Chicken is flavorful and tender.  I like to request my veggies to be SPICY!

An additional plus about this place is that business hours are longer than the surrounding businesses (exception is top dog)

There is one thing I keep getting here and that is the Chicken or Pork Vietnamese sandwich lunch special. It is a good deal for the price that you are paying. It comes with a soup that is relatively tasty and a soda for under $6. I can't argue with that! It may not be the most filling thing there, but it sure gives me the most bang for my buck.

The banh mi sandwich looked good when delivered to our table but the taste didn't match up. Served on a light airy bun, the pork lacked much flavor but appeared to be cooked fresh. The best part of the sandwich was the marinated carrot sitting on what seemed to be a mayo spread. The soup served along with the entree was bland but looked great with lots small pieces of tofu and whisked egg. The young man who brought the sandwich to our table was very nice. Maybe I've been spoiled by better bahn mi elsewhere but the food just didn't meet my expectations. I'd really like to see the "little guy" succeed but this place took too long to serve our sandwich (we were the only customer) and the flavor has to be "bumped up" a little.

This place is really cheap! It's great, for $5 you can get a whole meal. I like the Vietnamese sandwich here. It's huge and pretty good. The food quality is okay, but can't expect too much for the  price. Definitely a great place to go on a budget.

Whenever I forget to bring my lunch to work, I eat here. Depending on who is cooking and who is at the register, the food can be anywhere from very good to pretty bad. For example, I have ordered the hot and sour seafood soup and have gotten a savory hot and sour seafood soup. 

Another time, the person behind the register did not register what I wanted, despite my pointing it out on the bilingual menu, and I got some spiceless fishball seawater that tasted pretty bad. 

Yesterday I went there and it seemed to be a vegetable shortage because I got a heap of cabbage and tofu with two pieces of broccoli over mostly rice, which sucked. I noticed that the entire restaurant crowd had only cabbage with a little broccoli in their dish, too. Not a carrot or a green in sight, except for when I left, this one kid had the smarts to order the spicy string bean dish.

My main complaint is two-fold. Perhaps because I am not Asian, I never receive the standard sprouts, fresh chilis, lemon and basil that everybody else in the restaurant is being served with their pho. I ALWAYS have to get up and ask for it, and I come there often enough. I have asked for it first when I order it, that doesn't work either. It's always a hassle. 

The other issue I have is about 2/3 of the time, I've come in first and get served last. Then I have 10 minutes to wolf down my boiling hot soup. Forget about the standard condiments all the Asian kids are getting served at the other tables.

Pretty much the best place to eat on Northside. Can get slow during the lunch rush, but totally worth the wait. My friends and I always try to eat here at least once a week. I swear, they must put something in the rice because it is freaking addictive. 
Cheap. Friendly. Delicious. And fast if you go when it isnt 12 noon. yummmm

My favorite restaurant on North side. 

There are definitely a lot of dishes that are not good. But the dishes that are good, ARE AMAZING. I highly recommend the prawns and green beans with BBQ pork. It is loaded with BBQ pork, which is well seasoned and cooked just right, and the prawns are delicious. The prawns are lightly sauced with a classic white chinese sauce. The green beans are always crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, never hard. I have probably had this dishes at least 5 times and not once has it disappointed. For only $6.55, shrimp and BBQ pork! what more could you ask for. But be aware, this is not gourmet food, it is about the same quality as food from Southside (Durant Foodcourt aka Asian Ghetto). I also recommended the 5 Spice Chicken! It is seasoned to perfection with loads of chicken on a bed of rice and steam veggies on the side to boot. If you eat there, you get a nice warm bowl of soup with your meal. Even though it is not much, it's a nice bonus to finish your meal with. 

Don't let the appearance of the restaurant to turn you off from it. It may look like a run-down slum, but the food is great and the old couple that runs it are really nice. The prices are about $1-2 less than the places around it and similar restaurants on Southside. I also recommend the Lemongrass Chicken and the Vietnamese sandwich.

Pros:
- Great food
- Nice Service
- Cheap Prices
- Big Portions

Cons:
- Run down decor
- Some dishes are to be avoided
- Cash Only

Recommended Dishes:
- BBQ Pork and Prawns with Green Beans over Rice
- BBQ Pork over Rice
- Lemongrass Chicken with Rice
- 5 Spiced Chicken with Veggies and Rice
- Vietnamese Sandwich

Dishes to Avoid:
- Pho (Beef Combo in Particular)
- Spring Rolls
- Lemongrass Beef with Rice

2.5 stars

It really doesn't taste Vietnamese at all. It's more like Vietnamese food prepared Chinese style. Nonetheless the food is pretty decent. I recommend getting the rice noodle plates or lemongrass pork. They cook their vegetables spot-on nice and crisp. Their pho is average, a step above Vietnam Village but below Le Petit Cheval.

Their Vietnamese sandwich doesn't taste like a Vietnamese sandwich at all, but it's actually a pretty tasty sandwich. I recommend chicken or pork. It's meat, cucumber, carrots, shredded lettuce, and cilantro in a roll with a free drink.

Good for a quick fix if you're in the neighborhood. In regards to taste, it's better than TC Garden's Chinese food, but it's not as cheap.

Recently had an owner change so service has severely slowed during rush hour, 12:30-2pm. 

Cheap food, delicious free soup, can't really ask for more at a student-oriented restaurant. 

My favorite dish is the chicken lemongrass. Three large pieces of chicken covered in sesame over rice with a salad side for $6.25 is hard to beat. They deliver the food directly to you, but make sure the number they give you is visible! Once you finish, feel free to just leave as there is no need to bus your own dishes here.
It's better than the Chinese place, less expensive than the Japanese place, and tastes pretty good.

Just walk up and say, "Large #5."

I love the pho.  If you go early on Saturday, I've found that the broth is especially fatty, a.k.a. delicious.  It's still good on the weekdays, though.  They're closed Sundays, much to my chagrin, but that doesn't stop me from making multiple trips a week.

One of my missions is to find the best pho, and it's hard to find a better place within walking distance of campus.  Le Petit Cheval's pho is kind of sweet tasting and is closed more often than Camille, and Vietnam Village is just bland.  Heavenly Foods in the Bear's Lair is below average, and Pho Hoa is far away (at least, to walk); it's not as good anyway.  I've never had phomenow, though.

Does it make me a pho heathen if I like the beef balls?  Then may I burn in pho hell.  I also don't like adding Sriracha or Hoisin sauce; I feel like they're artificial tasting and take taste away from the broth.

Listen to me drone on about pho.  If you're not in the mood for pho - or just plain don't like it, get the combo crispy noodles.  They are great for a change of pace, and you'll be full by the end for sure.

Lastly, they're really busy during the lunchtime, and I've had my order mixed up once or twice as a result, but it's never stopped me from going back.  Now that I've graduated, I'll miss this place, but I plan to stop by whenever I visit Berkeley.

I come here like 4-5 times a week, no joke dude, it's like 75% sad. The lady at the register is my BFF now. We rap in Chinese about nothing, it's great. Seriously though, I think I come here way too much. Laziness, because it's 5 minutes away from where I live? Maybe. I'm also a creature of habit, and this shit is also pretty cheap, which = pretty fly. I love how these little pockets of cheap Asian eats are scattered all over Berkeley. It really prevents me from starving to death because ever since I've started the semester from hell, I just can't find the energy to go for "fun" meals anymore.

Camille (Camilles? Camille's?) is great. I've had most of their dishes, and the lemongrass chicken rice is one of my favorites. It comes with this killer fried egg that has this weird sweet glaze on it. Brown sugar maybe, I don't know, but it's awesome. I also like their chicken & shrimp bun (vermicelli) and lately, have become quite fixated on the eggplant clay pot. It is a bit greasy though. Huge portions by the way.

The only caveat is the system that they have in place for take-out orders. Instead of feigning any semblance of organization or control, what they do is march around with the food screaming, "NUMBA TWENTY-FO!!! NUMBA TWENTY-FO!!!" at the top of their lungs--during busy hours, which is when I'm usually there. I don't know why.

I love this place. This is my favorite place on north side after gomnaru changed ownership and became way more expensive. Food runs around $7 for a good set of dishes. 

They have decent Pho and give you good portions for the price.
The best things I've had at the chicken fried rice + egg (you get a cool fried egg!) and the coconut curry chicken. Best dishes for less than $7.

The last thing I want to recommend is that even if you get a to go order, you can ask for an order of the small soup. It's good! It has little bits of tofu. I'm not sure if I should say this but you can get a big container of that soup for $2. It's really good soup, just put some spicy sauce in there and it's a great meal.

This Chinese-run greasy spoon Vietnamese spot inside an asian food court of sorts was A-ok! In the larger realm of all things Vietnamese, it was a solid 3-star meal. Everything is cooked in copious amounts of oil, but underneath the fried veneer, the ingredients are fresh and the portions plentiful. Prices average around $7, and although service is brisk, your food is brought promptly to wherever you choose to perch on the deck. 

In comparison to the crappy level of food I've come to expect in Berkeley, this place provided me a long overdue satisfying meal.

Lunch will run you about $6.

I came here recently for lunch. The lady at the register was wearing a worn apron, a shirt at least as old as me, and a brand new Dolce & Gabbana hat. Awesome. Then I ordered the five-spice roast chicken, which was alright.

The last time I came here, I was sick and ordered pho tai.

The time before that, I split an order of spring rolls and an 8 oz. flask of bourbon with a friend.

While my experiences may have differed a bit between visits, I have to say that the food hasn't changed. Considering the area, type of food, and price point, it's been pretty good.

Is it great Vietnamese food? No. Is it even Vietnamese food? You could make an argument either way. Anyway, if you don't eat here, at least go to Aki's. Other options in this center are ill-advised.

The service is awesome! The owner is super friendly, I mostly come here because of their fresh juices, and they are delicious and the most affordable around.

They juice after you order it, I think it's about $3.50 for a fresh veggie juice versus the $5 you would pay at Whole Foods, and you get to support a local business. 

I recommend the grapefruit/orange juice, very refreshing.  This summer they will have fresh watermelon and cantaloupe I am excited to try! 

A great place to support. Their food looks amazing as well and I have heard lots of good things about it being fresh/homemade.

A local gem on a very cute street.

Falafel goodness.

Jamal is the man!

Cheese bagel.

Great joint.

It's not entirely fair for me to review this place so highly...  I really order only one thing here, the roasted turkey and cranberry sandwich (without mayo, ick).  When you need it, you need it.  Friends and colleagues have liked other items, but I cannot tear myself away from the turkey.  Need all the tryptophan I can get when on campus.  The people are great and pretty quick even during the lunch crush.
After trying the falafel at Chick-O-Pea's and Sunrise Deli, I'm of the opinion that this place has the best falafel in Berkeley.

This is one of the many quaint eateries on Euclid across from North Gate.  They have a huge selection of special sandwiches, bagels, cold salads, and smoothies that are made fresh, along with the usual cafe beverage selections.  

Many of the items on the menu are Mediterranean inspired.  They have roasted eggplant under the counter as if it were slices of meat or cheese.  Their special sandwiches and bagels have interesting combinations which tend to be tasty.  

Last time that I went, I had the North Beach bagel (roasted eggplant, cream cheese, tomato and a few other things).  Despite the roasted eggplant being a little too roasted, the flavor combination was quite nice.

Their prices are pretty fair.  The sandwiches and bagel aren't huge, therefore their prices aren't huge either.  Overall the Hummingbird Cafe is a great spot for a quick cheap bite.

Really nice owner and service, friendly, and delicious food - my favorite is probably the kefta-kabob.  Savory, a little spicy, with plenty of hummus and tabbouleh - delicious.  The other sandwiches are great as well.  A UC Northside staple.

They are so nice here!

But, more importantly, the food I had here was very good.  I was looking for a new place where I could eat lunch before lecture, and looked inside Hummingbird Cafe.  Their pasta salad selection caught my eye, and I eventually decided to get a large container of the pasta salad with shell pasta, sun-dried tomatoes, rosemary, green peppers, spinach, and feta cheese, with a drizzle of vinegar.  The vinegar was actually a bit much, but overall it was very good.  The large container lasted me about 2 meals, but I was sick that day and didn't really have much of an appetite.  On a normal day, I think the large container would last only about 1 meal.  ~$4.99

Also, I got a large (seasonal) cantaloupe smoothie.  The owner made it fresh for me.  After I ordered, he went to the back, came out with two large cantaloupes, and went to work on slicing them up and making me a delicious drink!  ~ $3.75

The cafe is fairly small; seating is around a narrow counter.  I don't remember seeing any tables.  

I'm not certain about the prices.  I think the pasta was either ~$5 or $6 and the drink may have been closer to $5.  In any case, I remember being a bit taken aback after seeing my total.  Minus 1 star for that.

Update:  Jamal is the nicest business owner you will ever meet.  He and his male employee (I should ask his name) know my drink and have it ready before I can even order.  The food is great, the coffee is cheap, and the company is unbeatable.  Today I didn't have cash, and Jamal gave me a coffee anyway, to repay later.  Who does that?!
Delicious food on the go.  I had the falafel sandwich, which was flavorful and delighted my stomach.  Next on my list is the turkey and cranberry sandwich!
We just went here for lunch between classes and loved it!  The food was delicious, and the service was great!  We got to sit outside and enjoy the Berkeley sunshine.  We'll be back!

I was gone in Japan for a summer, and to my surprise, I found myself really missing Hummingbird, Jamal and all the friendly staff. I swear they sprinkle a little secret spice on everything, making something as plain as a sandwich or a breakfast bagel taste awesome. I don't think I've ordered anything I disliked here, and the variety can keep you coming back forever (I've been a frequent customer for more than 6+ years). Hummus/falafel sandwiches are my fav, and there's nothing like a  Northbeach and homemade smoothie to put you in a good mood.
Lentil soup was really tasty. Sandwich was ok but only had three ingredients, lettuce tomato and meat. Service was prompt and friendly. I'll be back to try more...

This is seriously bad.
I've tried it 3x (blech) just to verify.

1. Vegetarian delight sandwich ordered w/ mayo.  There is usually pesto included.  Instead of being asked if I would like to omit the pesto, I get 3x the amount of mayo one would normally put on a sandwich + pesto (2x normal amount).  Altogether, this made for one oily sandwich.

2. Falafel sandwich.  This is typical bay area lavash falafel at it's worst.  I actually didn't blame them too much on this one- I mean, who are they going to look to for advice?

3. Veggie Delight, again; just in case.  Nope.  Instead of the advertised "avocado" that's on the menu... I got dark, dark brownish-green avocado w/ some spices (?).  This mixture had been out all day and never refreshed.  Not sure how one's conscience would accomplish such a feat. 

All in all I think it's clear that you get very nice service, friendly staff, and the most crappy food imaginable for a low price.

*edit*
OK, I can imagine worse.  But doing such things certainly doesn't make me want to eat.

Food: reasonably priced sandwiches, with much more exotic options that your typical delicatessen.  E.g. I didn't know cranberry sauce existed outside my grandma's thanksgiving table....but it goes pretty well with turkey between two slices of bread. 

the Cafe:  Small.  There is a chest-high counter hugging the back wall that can be used for seating, but if you're there around noon, you'll be constantly jostled by lunch-rush brownian motion. Although it might be worth it to spend a little more time in the place, which has a cool Mediterranean vibe.      

Staff/management: If you're a regular, the owner is the type of guy who will remember your name.  Maybe this is the place where I can start asking for "the usual" and they'll finally know what I'm talking about....

Hummingbird Cafe has two places, the main one and then the express one. I went to the main cafe, and wow, I think I've met the friendliest people in Berkeley. Unlike La Burrita a few doors down who don't greet you and make your order like it's the last thing they want to do, the people here are incredibly nice and helpful if you don't know what to order.

My friend and I came here and ordered a lamb sandwich as well as a falafel wrap. Both items were DELICIOUS. The lamb in the sandwich was deliciously tender, juice, most, and full of flavor. I don't think I've had lamb that good before. The falafel wrap was packed full of flavor too, though it's hard to describe without tasting it. 

If you're on north side, this is a must try. Cash only.
Inexpensive, delicious espresso, fresh made juice, awesome sandwiches, close to Soda Hall. Need I say more?!

I'm tempted to give this place 4 stars just because of the smoothies, as everyone has mentioned. However, I really don't think their sandwiches are that great or special. I've tried turkey, aram, chicken salad, BLT, sandwiches and their falafel plate. It's mediocre. 

However, I do like the idea of getting sandwiches on a croissant, that makes it better. In the end, I really only come back to this place for a smoothie, and the owner recognizes me for it.

One of the least busy places on Northside, I'm not sure why though.  The falafel wrap had all the makings of a great lunch.  Fresh, soft wrapper, great tabouleh and hummus and fresh veggies, but the falafel itself was soggy.   I NEED fresh and crispy falafel.  With fresh falafel, this is a 5 star lunch!

Cute little cafe with many deli options. 
Their sandwich/bagels are enough for a light brunch snack to hold me until 3 or 4pm. 
As for their coffee/espresso, it doesn't offer as many choices as the other coffee stores around the Northside area but hey...their Danish is hard to beat. 

I usually takes 5-10 min for them to prepare your order. If you are horriing to class, I wouldn't suggeest order a vegetable smoothie. However, if you got some time to kill, by all means, indulge.

The sandwich makers don't use gloves or wash their hands after handling money and, on top of that, they weigh your meat on a dirty scale without any paper.  That's gross and unsafe.  The sandwiches here are cheap but not outstanding.  Maybe people think it's a great deal because it's relatively inexpensive, but the Hummingbird Cafe is unsanitary and I really don't think deserves five stars.

Hummingbird Caf is the closest thing to a deli in the Euclid area. The likelihood that the sandwich you want is available is slim because they only stock the case for that day only. It's weird I know. Hummingbird has some addictive smoothies, but no matter which one you order, you can bet they all taste the same. 

Stop by Humming bird before 2 p.m. or they may have already run out of everything, leaving you scrambling for the last bagel. Around lunchtime there is usually a long line.

Of course, this topic is open for (frequent) discussion in my circles, but in my opinion the Hummingbird Cafe the best falafel in Berkeley.  Like many of these other reviews, I usually take mine as part of the falafel sandwich, which is filling and flavorful.  Advantages:  large menu, good service, great food, friendliness of the staff.  The only downside I can think of is that the counter staff have the annoying tendency to overcharge for their food.  (And I don't mean that it's too expensive--it's that they charge more than what's on the menu.)  For example, I used to order carrot juice here and was almost always charged for orange-carrot juice, which is more, creating an unpleasant confrontation every dang time at the register while we "negotiated" the price.  This has probably happened to me along the order of 20 times--finally I just quit ordering multiple items altogether and watched carefully what I was being charged.  Bagels take a long time to toast, but they are actually warm when you get them.

I disagree that this place only has stuff you can make at home--and I think that about most sandwich places.

I had a bagel with roasted eggplant on it from here and it was the best eggplant I have ever had and I stopped saying that I hated when vegetarian sandwiches had eggplant instead of meat.

They also have a really crazy good LEMONADE. It has spices and texture and awesomeness.

Taste: 2
Value: 3
Service: 4

The sandwiches are okay, although the last one I got (Cranberry turkey special) came out really soggy, and the tomato in the sandwich totally ruined it. Definitely sticking with Hummingbird Express from now on since the sandwiches are the same, and this place is more expensive. Maybe I'll try the bagels since those are pretty well-reviewed.

I work on Northside, so this place is great for lunches. Their hummus sandwich is great and more than filling. I also love that when I ask for "super spicy", they don't skimp on the hot sauce or peppers. The owner really goes out of his way to make sure you'll enjoy your meal. Today he made me a veggie sandwich that was guaranteed to his the spot, and it is. It's much better than Stuffed Inn.

This is pretty much my favorite lunch place in the Berkely campus area. 

It's the type of place where after you order your egg-salad sandwich on dutch crunch and grab a bottle from the fridge, the lovely owner says,"that'll be five bucks!" 

And you say "I'm also getting a drink." 

And he smiles, because this happens to him a lot, and says "I know. Five bucks total." 

The egg salad is awesome. The falafel is great. The orange-carrot juice is really, really good, and I'm not even really into healthy juices.  Finally, they have a very nice sign, with a hummingbird on it.

I just wanted to get some fresh juice one day, and I came across this place. 

The cafe is very small and there is only one table outside. Half of the place is the fridge and the FOOD. I was overwhelmed by the menu. They have many different drinks you can choose. It was a tough decision between the smoothies and the fresh squeezed juice. In the end, I decided on CARROT and ORANGE juice. It was really good. The owner made it fresh for me. He used 3 carrots and 1.5 oranges in a medium cup. It was really good and refreshing. 

I went back for lunch and it was not disappointed. I ordered the Vegi Delight sandwich and it was really good. The vegetables were fresh, and it only costs $5.

The service was really good. The guys who work there are really nice. The owner of the place also recommended several of his vegetarian specialties:  falafel sandwich and eggplant pesto.

This place is amazing! I went there for lunch on a Wednesday, and although the line was long, they got our order really quickly. By some accident they either got my order wrong or gave the sandwich to someone else, but the owner was really apologetic and quickly made me a new one. He also gave me a cookie to make up for it. I got the Tandoori Chicken sandwich and the Middle Eastern Plate, and my friend got the roasted chicken sandwich. All the items were excellent, as all the ingredients tasted really fresh. After we were done, the owner gave me some of his kefta to try (as we were sitting there for the meal). He made me really feel like I was a guest in his home, and I really enjoyed the dining experience there. This is a place that I would definitely go back to, and a place that I would really recommend to anyone who happens to be in the area. It's a typical mom-and-pop shop that makes your day better by being there.

I often come here to order lunch for our whole lab.  The food is excellent (best place near campus, in my opinion) and the staff are super friendly and accommodating.  Everyone in my lab is always super happy when I come to the meeting with Hummingbird sandwiches in tow.  In fact, this week, there was almost a fight over who got a falafel sandwich (I only ordered 3).  The owner is an incredible man who wants nothing more than to have you walking out with a positive attitude and a full, happy stomach.  If you're ordering for a large group and have to wait, he really tries to make you comfortable while you wait, offering a nice cup of coffee or other nice treats. 

Highly recommended!

the posted price for coffee on the inside blackboard and the outside banner are different but not by much.

artisan roasted kavanaugh coffee is billed brew. tastes just like a harsh version of farmers coffee or mr. expresso.  just a sm(.92) so no bigge.   3 stars at most

awesome prices for sammies (under 4) but i had a wrap already.

very courteous people here with prompt service.
will grab a sammie someday.
cash only
Sandwiches are okay if you don't deviate from standard items. Only takes cash. Owner is obnoxious.
The Kefta sandwich is the best thing that is ever happened to me. I drive a decent distance to take my lunch break here every day due to my addiction. Amazing smoothies too!

Yummy, middle-eastern and not-so-middle eastern delight.  I have two go-to sandwhiches here:
1) The smoked turkey & pepper jack on a dutch crunch roll.  I really hate telling others how good the dutch crunch roll is because sometimes they run out.  They always do a great job toasting the bun.  It's basic, but reasonably priced, and always tasty.  
2) The falafel sandwich.  A highlight is the tabouleh accompaniment in the wrap...always fresh and tasty.  The weak point though is the falafel themselves.  They keep them in a refrigerated case and then microwave them prior to serving. This is fine sometimes and other times it isn't.  A little more consistency would really make it excellent.  Plus it's in the $7 range which is pricier.  Oh, and careful what you ask for with the spice.  They get carried away.

The owner is very nice and always polite.  The juices are good too, but I almost always seem to skip those.  I wish this place kept better hours....seems to always be closed on weekends.
So good!  So cheap! Really nice guy behind the counter!  Love to come here for the toasted bagel/cream cheese/cucumber thingy for breakfast.

these men are so sweet. they made me and my crew great sandwiches when i was back in berkeley working this week. one of me pet peeves for sandwiches is when people don't put a lot of lettuce/sprouts on them - hummingbird packed my sandwiches with both! it did bug me that i originally went in for a salad per their posted menu and was disappointed to find out that they don't have salads (why are they on the menu?) but i was satisfied and sated with my yummy sandwich.
Sandwiches are good, I especially recommend the Turkey-Avocado (yummy). Lines are a bit long at lunch (of course) but this place is good.

This place is EXCELLENT.

2 things:
Service is awesome. Everyone's really nice and they greet you with a large smile when they ask you for your order and they are incredibly friendly. I honestly felt like my day got brighter just by talking to them.

I got the North Beach bagel which, if I remember correctly, had sprouts, grilled eggplant, pesto, and a few other things that I got in a sesame bagel. Absolutely delicious, wished I bought 3 more of them. I'm never on north side but if I am, I'm definitely coming back here.

5/5, was dissatisfied with nothing. Yes, it's around $4 for a specialty bagel but boy, is it worth it.
Good sandwiches.  One of the regular places for locals in the area.  Good prices.

Let me just say this: on a slightly hungover morning, there is NOTHING that beats a fantastic "original" asiago bagel from the Hummingbird Cafe, which includes cream cheese spread with dill, tomato, cucumber, and sprouts. And the kicker? It's only $2.75.

It's a friendly, cozy place, and though I haven't tried most of the menu as of yet, I am eager to do so. The owner is extremely friendly and chats you up, which I really appreciate--he hands out samples of new dishes he's perfecting, and you really get the idea that he's in it because he truly loves what he does. Shockingly that seems a bit rare in Berkeley, where everything is so goal-oriented rather than being focused instead on the journey itself. It's cash-only, FYI.

First of all, even though every sandwich shop ever has a 'Veggie Delight/Delite,' only Hummingbird's lives up to the name. They've got a good selection of breads onto which they put just the right amount of everything, making for some delicious sandwiches.

The owner is indeed a friendly guy (no matter how many times I've had to assure him that no, I don't want any coffee with my bagel sandwich (also good) in the morning); it's a charming little place, really.

Hummingbird's many minute flaws make it a true 3.5-star joint, but its convenience deserves the half-star upgrade. I always get the falafel sandwich, which has a great medley of flavors-- thick hummus, plentiful tabouleh with petite-diced cucumber and tomato, shredded iceberg lettuce, thinly-sliced red onions and tomotoes and two falafel croquettes with a dash of hot sauce, wrapped in a ginormous piece of levant. Great flavors all around, and the condiments aren't too watery and acidic like-- ahem-- SOME Middle Eastern restaurants around campus carry. Their falafel are savory with a pleasant and relatively moderate bit of spice, and the hot sauce and tabouleh really carry the whole sandwich home.

This falafel has the potential to be off the wall, but its dryness is oftentimes a bit hard to handle. First, the falafel itself-- they do not prepare them to order, so these little deep-fried chickpea balls sit together in a bowl for sometimes hours, getting soggy. The reheating process is done in the microwave, and that zaps whatever moisture was clinging to the falafel. They're flavorful but dry as a desert, and combined with the levant, which itself is pretty devoid of moisture (although, I must credit Hummingbird for serving levant that is at least moist enough to be pliable) the sandwich wouldn't be edible if not for the delightful tabouleh (Hummingbird should really sell it a la carte). Make sure they put in a lot of tabouleh and ask for extra hot sauce. Then order one of their juices (today I had carrot-orange) to wash it all down.

Cheap prices, good flavor, super quick and convenient. The owner and every employee I have encountered are lovely. Definitely a place to try out if you're on the north side of campus.
Great place to stop for a sandwich, and their lemonade with teeny bits of ginger is delish!
The sandwiches are cheap and pretty decent when they get my order right. Their egg salad in particular is very tasty although it has a lot of mayo.
All time best ever felafel. Hummingbird has set a new felafel benchmark.

If for no other reason, go here for the service. The people who work here are great. Also the smoothies are to die for! Sheesh, just writing about them makes me want one right now!!! The sandwiches are solid but the thing to get here that is really special... the falafel wrap.

If you are on a student budge, this is the place to get a decent lunch.  They have varities of sandwiches under 4 bucks with good portion enough to feed a hungry bear(like myself).  If you just got a pay check, I recommand you to try out their middle eastern plate, featuring yummy falafel and dolmas that are worth to start a fight with my friend.  Their food is always fresh especially their drinks, instead of using regular juice, the owner insist to use the high quality Looza juice as base and blend it with sorbet and fresh fruits.  He also add a little bit spice into the drink to enhance the flavor.  Bravo Hummingbird!!

I really like this place. Their North Beach Bagel is a great way to start your morning. Its got grilled eggplant, pesto, feta, sprouts, tomatoes, and cucumbers which I like to have on a toasted asiago bagel! They also have really good lamb shwarma! 

Jamal and george and all the people that work there are really friendly and nice! Once when it was raining Jamal lent me his umbrella!  Anyways, he's got a big personality who's always loud and fun to talk to. 

The one downside is that it is cash only... but still worthy of 5 stars!
i eat here at least once a week.  a cheddar sandwich on a toasted everything bagel.  it is so cheap and so filling and so delicious!  and 99 cent iced coffee!

How this place averages 4 stars is beyond me.

The falafel sandwich was dry and not very flavorful. It wasn't gross, but nor was it nearly as good as you can get at Sunrise on Bancroft or Oasis down by Shattuck. 

I gave them a second chance and tried the chicken salad sandwich. I figured it was listed first under "gourmet sandwiches" so it should be pretty good? Wrong. There was hardly any chicken salad on the sandwich, and way, way, WAY too much mustard and mayo.

On the plus side, as others have mentioned, the staff are friendly and affable. But I'll be going elsewhere for my lunch fix.

I was really stressed out because I had been up since 6am and didn't eat til 11... running around apartment hunting.  The North Beach Bagel was superb and really hit the spot.  We also got to learn about co-op living, so that was fun.  Friendly, cute place.  Good food, good service, cute area.

They are closed Sunday, I think.

Excellent place to grab a sandwich and then go on a picnic. Great North Berkeley location, quiet, peaceful, everything that south berkeley isn't. Not that I don't like southern Berkeley, it's just sometimes one needs a break from Telegraph's food options. 

Delightful.
Great food for an excellent price. Conveniently located near campus and serves the best Gyro's with meat off the Spit.
It's exactly what I'm looking for in a lunch place: great sandwiches at great prices. My turkey sandwich--complete with lots of veggies--is around 4 dollars. You can't beat that.

The sandwich specials are excellent, I wish they would change the daily special every few weeks, I am kinda getting bored of them.
But you have to try them at least once.

To do it right: $5

Walking in here, I fully didn't expect to be giving five stars.  I'll make this short: my order was taken almost immediately even though the place was jammed full at noon, and got my food within 5 minutes.  The were reasonably (over)staffed for the lunch rush and I can't say a single bad thing about the service.  I grabbed the turkey avocado on wheat, and ate at the tables outside of La Burrita--because I roll like that.  Every component of the sandwich was excellent, relative to the price and timing.  Guac was decent, turkey was fresh (not slimy), bread was soft with a bit of crunch from toasting, lettuce and pickles crunched before bending, and even the sprouts made tiny snaps.  Both the meat and cheese were supplied in generous portions, which is a double bonus for any sandwich.

Sidenote: they also have a standard Mediterranean spread (tabbouleh, hummus, dolma), which looked good, but I have not yet sampled.

Summary: Comfortably cramped.  Great deal.

First and Foremost, the owner of the cafe is super nice!  He has always been there in the morning to say hi and he remembered my name since the first time I introduced myself.  I love the assortment of pasta salads, but the iced coffee is why i go there.  It is only $1 for a large iced coffee and it tastes better than anything thing else around.  Try some and be amazed!
Good sandwiches, fast service. Coffee is sub-par though.

The perfect falafel sandwich.  Falafel, hummus, tabouli, spicy sauce, and sometimes jalapenos (or not, if you're not into that kind of thing) wrapped up in a pita/tortilla hybrid.  The middle eastern platter, which comes with all these ingredients plus rice and lentils, two dolmas, and a pickle, is also delicious.  And so are the cookies.  Favorite lunch spot in Berkeley.

Two words: Veggie Delight. There is too much to love about this sandwich...creamy avocado and pesto tempered by crisp spinach, sprouts and refreshing cucumber, the faintest splash of oil and vinegar and crumbles of feta to brighten it up a bit, and sweet, roasted red bell peppers on a crunchy roll. 
Completely filling without any meat, and only 4.50? What more can you ask for? They can easily price a sandwich like this on a lunch menu for 11.00 at a pretentious, swanky restaurant. My friend who already ate lunch jealously eyed me as I savored every delicious bite, saying, "How can you eat that in front of me? That looks AMAZING." When I humored him by giving him a taste, he was not disappointed.
I almost feel ashamed that I ever ordered a--albeit still quality-made with love and still very tasty--regular ol' turkey sandwich here. The owner obviously puts a lot of thought into his own creations. I have never been let down once, and the people here are very sweet. This is THE place to go for a sandwich not only on Euclid, but in Berkeley, and I've had my fair share. 
The tabouleh and other housemade cold salads look great, too, so I have more to look forward to. Great job, Hummingbird. Five stars.

I got the lamb shawarma sandwich, which was delicious.... flavorful and filling! I came near the end of the day so the bread varieties were already running out. :( My friend got the falafel wrap. She was kinda bummed that they microwaved her falafels (instead of on-the-spot deep frying them), but she couldn't stop gushing about good it was once she started eating. 

My ex-Prof came in while we were ordering, and bragged to his friend about how Hummingbird had the best juice in town HAHA. I guess I'll have to try that next!

Sandwiches are delicious and so reasonably priced -- I think the "North Beach" one is 3.75 and SO tasty. Tons of vegetarian options.  Get some dolmas too! 

The line gets long around lunch so come before or after and be prepared to wait! 

The staff is really friendly as stated by other reviewers. 

The downside is the cost of the platters -- they are delicious but way too high for grad student organization budgets!

I used to go to this place every day.  It got to the point where I would walk in and they would start making my sandwich as soon as they saw me.  They have really good smoothies too.  However.... I have abandoned the Hummingbird Cafe for the corner store (Seven Palms Food Market) across the street.  Their sandwiches are bigger and better and you can't compete with the selection of drinks and sandwiches of a corner store.

The owner is really nice and it is worth becoming a regular here.  His lemonade is the best ever and I am planning on getting it every day during summer.
The fruit juices are good--but this place is not all it's cracked up to be. The food is passable and that's all. I'd rather get a sandwich at the FSM Cafe.

Great, quick, high quality food to go. Excellent at Northgate. 
In this day of anonymous chains, a place where not only the food is of excellent quality, but the service is friendly and they remember me by name... 
They have earned my extreme loyalty.  
Highlights: kabob sandwich is delctable. Jamal's smoothies are out of this world. All the middle eastern stuff is top notch as well. Highly recommended on all fronts!

I love the Hummingbird Café.  Either tiny location.  They've taken some of my favorites off the menu (I really want the egg salad sandwich back), they randomly run out of stuff like ice ("No ice, no ice!"), and the kind employees don't always give me exactly what I ordered.  But I've never complained because by the time I realize I'm eating a tuna sandwich -- my arch nemesis -- I'm already enjoying it.  They even make food I don't like taste good!  And healthy, too.  The coffee will do, the smoothies are excellent, and the price is right.  I only wish they weren't cash only.

I'll have to come back to try some food later, but made a pit stop for coffee as an alternative to the delish but pricey espresso drinks at my Yali's in Stanley Hall.
At mid-morning, I was the only one there.  Was greeted cheerfully by no less than 3 employees, one of whom took my order and was very proud of the cheap $1.25 large coffee.  ($1.35 if you don't have your own mug).  They have espresso, but take heed to lactose intolerants - NO SOY MILK HERE!  So I couldn't have the latte I craved and settled for drip coffee - it was a little on the weak side but got the job done just fine.

This is a regular lunch stop for me. And I almost always just go for the middle eastern plate. You get quite a lot of tasty middle eastern food for seven bucks. There's no seating, but just carry you food back across Hearst and sit by the north gate. Especially with the new grass and benches area they put in.

I've been here countless times but I never wrote a review since I wanted to try a bunch of items on their very expansive menu. Their selection is incredible for such a tiny little shop -- they've got salads, sandwiches, bagels, smoothies, cafe drinks, Mediterranean fare, and an impressive snacks/drinks section by the register. Best of all, all the items are priced very well.

One unfortunate thing about their sandwiches is that they tend to use pretty much the same combination of fixin's (e.g., pickles, sprouts, lots of mayo/mustard) for all their sandwiches and they begin to all taste the same. That's probably why I like their Seal Rock bagel, which has a unique combination of veggies and salmon spread that tastes great and is surprisingly cheap.

The staff here are very friendly, and since there's very few of them, you start to recognize them and they start to recognize you rather quickly.

The food here is worth 4 stars; the service, price, and variety all contribute to the fifth star.

Good sandwiches, but the service experience I got was middling.

I got the arab-named special (I'm afraid I forget the name).  I was overcharged - it was a standard sandwich, and they priced it premium.  The staffers were new, though.  The big problem was communication.  The workers weren't English-fluent, which normally isn't a problem.  But everyone in line was having trouble and they were becoming frustrated.  Based on what I saw, they were probably "in training," which I guess explains both.

The sandwich was fresh and delicious, and would have been well-priced if I weren't over-charged.  I was going to give a *** but everyone else seems to have had good experiences, so I'll bump it up to **** because it was a real good sammich.

Cheapest, quickest coffee on Euclid (self-serve, $.79 for 12 oz), and to-die-for North Beach bagel (feta cheese, cucumbers, sprouts, tomatoes, toasted eggplant, some delicious sauce) for $3.25. There's no seating, but it's a perfect place to grab a quick lunch between classes. Smoothies and sandwiches are also great.

A dilemma - the sandwich fillings at Hummingbird are excellent but the bread is rubbish, so which sandwich to order? I like to think I'm clever, but my inability to think outside the square meant it took me years to come up with this answer: don't order the sandwiches. Now, once a week or so I get the Middle Eastern plate, which for $6.50 can feed two: tabouleh (the highlight), a couple of dolmas, good pickles, pita bread, hummus (a little bland), lentils, a few chunks of roast vegetables (potato/carrot) and two falafel (not up to Sunrise Deli's, better than anyone else's near campus). I'll eat two-thirds of this for lunch and the rest at afternoon tea, then end up not cooking dinner until 10pm due to lack of voraciousness.

I give this place 4 stars for the smoothies alone.  Only downside?  THis place closes uber early.  The sign says 4PM but really they start shutting down around 3-ish... I often have to make a point of getting there before they close to snag a smoothie.  I've tried almost every smoothie on the menu, and I love all of them.  

Great pasta salads too - I often get a small container to go, and it's a great afternoon snack.  

Service is always friendly...  I think the owner recognizes me from all my smoothie trips... :o)

Five stars for the North Beach Bagel and it's a quaint little shop with nice staffers.

Once I start talking, writing, or thinking about the North Beach Bagel, I start to salivate. In fact, after trying the NB bagel during my first visit back in 2007, my tastebuds have not yet let me try another sandwich on the menu, even though they all look very tasty.

Yes, I love, love, love NB Bagel: delicious creamy tahini / pesto sauce (not sure which), toasted eggplant, feta cheese, topped with tomatoes, sprouts, and cucumbers. I prefer it on an "everything" bagel, but I suppose one might want to start out with a plain bagel to focus on the sandwich's innards. Once, I went late in the day and they only had whole wheat bagels left, but with the practically orgasmic flavor combo, it still tasted great.

I think the trick is the eggplant. It's sliced super thin - no big gooey blobs - and it's toasted very well, crispy in some places and super flavorful. I think they must marinate it first. At $3.50, it's a great deal for someone like me who prefers smaller meals; if you have a bigger appetite, they have plenty of side pasta/middle eastern salad options to choose from. 

The only downside is they are not open weekends and they close at 4:30, so I can't really take my friends. I only get a chance to indulge in a delicious NB bagel when I have a work meeting on Northside. I need to have more meetings on Northside. Northside for Northbeach. Yummmmm.

I love this place. Even the simplest deli sandwiches are a great lunch. The ingredients are fresh and flavorful. They don't mind is you are a picky eater and never has gotten my order wrong. The people there are very kind and like to talk to you. Super inexpensive which is important to me. 

I recommend the Hummus (+ some pita bread). Probably the best I've ever had at Cal. 

the only this bad is that they run out of food after the lunch rush sometimes. But it's not their fault that they are so in demand. haha.

Stuffed Inn can't have ALL the fun on Euclid.  This place should also be at the top of your list if you're looking for a good sandwich on Northside.  Both places have sandwiches for about $5.

What sets this place apart is that they spice things up a lil bit by offering more exotic sandwiches than those at Stuffed Inn.  Stuffed Inn is where you get simple, healthy sandwiches with standard ingredients (stuff a typical health-conscious soccer mom makes for their college grown son who lives at home).  

Here, you have a much larger selection of special ingredients to go into your sandwich.  Pesto sauce, roasted eggplant, hummus, salmon spread, etc.  They've got bagels, croissants, and more.  Although these ingredients are more unique and may lead to a more unhealthy or dense sandwich.  I was looking for a light sandwich but I made a mistake by ordering a pesto chicken sandwich and I felt groggy in class, but I enjoyed it!

After a long night of trying to share a twin bed with my boyfriend for the first time in a LONG time Hummingbird Cafe's coffee was exactly what the doctor ordered. It was a blissful cup of perfection to start the day off right. I will be back the next time such an event is in my cards.

Hard to say who's smoothies I like better: Hummingbird or Brewed Awakening. I should consider myself lucky to have two great smoothie joints near the lab. 

Their bagels are excellent. One item has a blend of their own spread served it with sprouts, cucumber, and tomato.

They have an excellent vegetarian option in the middle eastern plate which has falafel, hummos, tabouleh, and pita. Jamal makes the hummos and most other items from scratch. He's a friendly guy and remembers his regular customers.

Their lemonade is the best I've ever had. It's homemade, it has the wonderfully perfect amount of ginger, and its lusciously delicious. Their sandwiches are veggie-licious they make you feel healthy and great about life. Their eggplant pesto is SO GOOD. And who would have thought alfalfa sprouts in a sandwich would be yums? SO YUMS. And the service is great - everyone is so happy and chirpy, life feels great!  Hummingbird Cafe is super close to the UC Berkeley campus, so it's a great place to pick up food and have an absolutely cute  picnic on campus! Love hummingbird cafe. GET THE LEMONADE. That was one of my best life decisions. SO YUMMY.

|| B A C K G R O U N D ||

Their menu is BEAUTIFUL, as is the food that they serve!

The place is fairly small, but it's cozy and efficiently structured. You place your order to the woman behind the deli bar (they have a nice selection of cold dishes), and you walk to the end of the counter to pay at the cashier. They have specials on papers all around the back wall, so take your time to choose your meal!

There are a few seats against the wall, as well as one table with two chairs outside. We were lucky to nab the table and enjoy the rare beautiful Berkeley weather. Unfortunately, the table is next to the window that displays their tantalizingly pastries, which kept tempting me as I ate my lunch :c

|| F O O D || 

SHAWERMA LAMB + HUMMUS SANDWICH: lamb, hummus, mayonnaise, lettuce, tomato, all on Dutch Crunch bread [$5.95]
- This was listed on a paper with specials, just below their board.
- The lamb was delectably tender and juicy, and the hummus was a GREAT addition.  It pairs surprisingly well with the mayo.
- They let you choose your sandwich bread, and the Dutch Crunch was just the right amount of crunch c:

FALAFEL [$6.50]
- A falafel wrap that looked good and tasted good! The falafels were yummy!

|| C L O S U R E ||

An awesome meal at an even awesomer price. I'd come back to try anything else on their menu!
their middle eastern plate is insanely huge. enough food for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. too bad the quality's not great. dry falafel. also, their hummus tastes a lot like tahini.

I had the avocado and turkey on whole wheat bread sandwich AND a Club on dutch french and both sandwiches really hit the spot. Not sure if I was just hungry or if they were really actually that awesome, but I wouldn't mind coming again. At $4.50 each sandwich, it's quite a steal! And there are shorter lines here during lunch than any other place along Euclid, so it saves you time too! The only thing is, this place is super small and crowded, so it can get kinda uncomfortable inside with people 2 inches from your face as they try to get past you to get out of the place or get in. 

The cash register guy is really uptight and kinda over stresses about everything. He needs to take a chill pill. The girls that make the sandwiches are super nice and friendly. :)

No credit cards here, so bring your CASH!

This place does two things really well.  Sandwiches and Smoothies.  They have all types of sandwiches for $4-6 and aram sandwiches too.  Oh and they have a bunch of mediterranean salads too but I haven't tried them.  

I absolutely love their smoothies.  A few of them contain ginger, it'll knock you off your feet.  Nice, thick smoothies with lots of flavor.  You won't get tired of drinking it halfway through.  

What is the absolute best though is the lemonade.  Give it a try, it's no ordinary lemonade.  It's loaded with ginger and some other stuff giving it a sweet and sour taste.  Utterly delicious.

Finally, the staff is very friendly.

I cannot say anything about their food since I haven't tried anything on the menu that is not a smoothie.

Why haven't I tried anything besides the smoothie there?  I don't know, perhaps next time I will.  All I can say is that every time I go there I have a great experience.  

I remember the first time I went into the Hummingbird Cafe it was just one of those days I wanted smoothie for no apparent reason.  To be honest, I would have gone to Jamba Juice that day had I not been on the North Side of campus.  Howvever, I'm glad I went into this delightful Mediterranean Cafe that day.  I was greeted by the owner, Jamal, who asked me what he could do for me.  I said that I wanted a smoothie and this man when off about how great his smoothies were and how they are the best and nothing like the stuff they sell at Jamba Juice.  I was intrigued so I ordered the strawberry smoothie.  Then I see this guy going to work with fresh fruits, frozen fruits, organic juice, and sorbet with his own hands.  I asked why the other employees, who were doing nothing at that time since the lunch rush was over, weren't making the smoothie instead.  He tells me that only he is allowed to make the smoothies.  That's dedication to a craft right there.  Don't see that too often in the food/service industry nowadays.   Anyway, once the smoothie came out I was blown away by the detail to presentation he used and the taste was far better than anything I've gotten at Jamba Juice. 

However, it's not the taste that keeps me going back there for smoothies, though I live in Unit 2 (South side of campus).  It's Jamal.  He's just one of the nicest owners I've ever met.  He remembered my name all those times I went and one time when I didn't cash, since they don't accept credit cards, he just let me have it saying that he trusted that I would come back and pay him later.  Now, I know that as a regular he would trust me to pay him back, which I did, but it's just good to see someone care about their customers and craft the way he does. 

Bottom line, if you are ever in the North Side of campus and want to smoothie, go to see Jamal at the Hummingbird Cafe.  You won't be disappointed.

The Middle Eastern plate is satisfying and tastes awesome. Stuff here is reasonably priced and the guy who works there is nice and always enthusiastic when I order something. 

Here's our usual conversation:

Me: "I'd like the Middle Eastern plate."

Him: "Middle Eastern Plate. You like it!"

Me: "I like it?"

Him: "Yes. It tastes good! Your going to like it, you'll see!"

One sandwich is what sets this cafe apart.  A lot of people love the cheese 'n' stuff delux turkey, but it can't be considered against the hummingbird hot turkey sandwich on a croissant.  Hot roast turkey, cranberry sauce cucumbers, and red onions on a light flaky croissant, and last time I went it was only 4 bucks.  Grab a ginger lemonade to go with it and you're set for lunch

The owner of this place is awesome.  I love their smoothies it always comes with a couple scoops of sorbet.  The mediterranean plates and different salads are also great.  Sandwiches and bagels are made to order.  I started going here more often than Stuffed Inn after Sophomore Year of college.  But I do still hold a soft spot for Stuffed Inn.  Only difference here is that there's no seating area and it's really a place where you order and leave.  I wished they expanded.

Like almost everything on the Euclid Strip, there is little reason to come here if it's out of your way.  Hummingbird's goodness is largely contingent upon its convenience, but with that said it's pretty awesome if you live or have class nearby.

In most cases you can walk in the door with four dollars and walk out with a balanced meal of a sandwich in 120 seconds.  And then, of course, you can be sitting in class, complete with sandwich in belly, a mere five minutes after that.

On those rare tragic mornings when I am awake early enough to care what time businesses open, Hummingbird enjoys the further distinction of being one of only three morning options on Northside.  Unfortunately they are not at all an evening option; they are never open past 4pm and tend to start closing up at 3:30.

As for the appeal of the food itself... I wouldn't suggest getting too excited about this place.  While I enjoy the sandwiches and appreciate the variety of things that Hummingbird puts in them, they are nothing you can't make at home if you have opposable thumbs.  Overall a very good value, but you are paying for goods and labor, not art or skill.

1.Roast beef with a "surprise-me-bread."
2.Red Velvet Cake.
3.Pineapple cake.
4.The best service I have ever had at a sandwich shop & people that remember your face and orders.

Top 4 reasons why I am known to walk 2 miles uphill just for a sandwich from this place. Yeah... They're that good.
the smoothies here are pretty good.

Five Reasons for five stars.  1.  Cheapest coffee on the north side of campus.  $1.25 for a large - Virtually unheard.  2. Great Pasta Salad of the non-mayo variety.  And options to choose from.  Signs of a great deli.  3.  Great smoothies.  4. Nicest staff ever, and there food suggestions have never led me astray.  5.  options.  wide variety of choices for lunch.  all of which have been amazing so far.

Whomever started the idea of serving turkey cranberry sandwiches deserves an award. 

Now...

Roasted Turkey w/ Cranberry Sauce made with A REAL ROASTED AND CARVED TURKEY!!!!!!  That is one delectible sandwich!  Seriously this is the best sandwich I've had in a long time. 

It's Tryptophan-TASTIC!!! ZZZZzzzzzzzzz............

This place rocks. The owner is too friendly. One time when I was in there ordering a sandwich, the guy in front of me was unaware of their "cash only" policy and they'd already made his sandwich. The owner gave him his sandwich and told him to come back the next day with the cash. WHO DOES THAT? Very, very cool. 

I like the sandwiches better than the Palms deli across the street but I wish this place carried Kettle Chips (salt&vinegar, mmmm!). The smoothies are also awesome. Good times!

Pretty darn good.  The crepe itself is sweet, which surprised me, as I got a savoury crepe, and didn't want sugar.  But oh well.  The crepe itself was good, and the whole thing was yummy too, even with the sweet wrapper.   It's a little pricey, but it did fill me up like a meal would, so I guess that's ok.  They didn't skimp on the portions.  If you're a real eater, you might need two, but that's probably only if you have a little extra heft on you, know what I mean?

Also, the crepe was pre-made, but that was not a problem for me.  It was also thick, but I liked this interesting difference (as opposed to thin), as it did not fall apart, and added substance to the meal.

I did notice that the hand-washing after money handling was perfunctory at best (no soap, a quick 3 second water turn-on).  If you're freaked out by germs, you should probably avoid this place. Also, the seating is lame, it's just some stools in front of a mirror (yuck, who likes to watch themselves eat?)  I'd take my crepe and go-go.  They really should have 2 people working the counter, one for the money touching and order taking.  It took a little long to get my order in, but he did the best he could, being as he was the only dude there. All in all, I'd say give it a whirl.

I loooove a good crepe. Even more, I love a quick, yummy fillings, easy to hold crepe to walk around and chit-chat with friends.
I got the banana chocolate crepe and my friend had the peanut butter and chocolate crepe. Paired with a to-go cup of 2%, my crepe milk combo came to to $6.37. A little expensive but I was craving this type of sweet after a fervent movie discussion and a meal of gyros. I'd been to a few other to-go crepe places in the bay, and while the crepe recipe is not as good I also find it negligible, especially in light that they are pretty generous with the fillings. TONS of banana, oh so good. Oh, the peanut butter one was great, too, but naturally a bit dry and sometimes there were parts of the crepe that were only peanut  butter or only chocolate. My next visit (for sure I'll come back to check out the University sister shop as well) I plan to get peanut butter, honey and banana. Yummm.
I can see how this place can get cramped, I luckily went during a lull period so service was quicker but I have to agree with some of the other reviewers--these are not the happiest of people.

The crepes are flavorful and great for eating on the go. It's fun to watch them make the crepe! 

I prefer savory crepes. The crepe with a bunch of roasted vegetables (peppers, eggplant, etc.) and cheese is very good. So is the one with an egg, spinach, and cheese (I got ricotta). Perhaps one day I will venture into sweet crepe territory. 

One crepe doesn't make me feel full, but it's a good amount of food, and I always feel satisfied after getting a crepe. I guess it's healthier than being put into a food coma!

I'm French, so I'm a bit of a crepe snob, but these guys do it right.  They have a good batter recipe so the actual batter they use is quite good.  Their choices are good too (try the avocado, cheese, and tomato!)

The only problem is that they make the crepes in advance instead of freshly for you.

Well, it doesn't change the fact that I didn't love the crepe, but the manager sent me a very cordial note about my previous review.  Anyone who is takes the time to be so polite and respond to a little bellyacher like me must run a business well.

For the record, she stated that the swiss crepe has high-quality emmental cheese...didn't want to be spreading misinformation :)

I prefer the savory crepes over the sweet ones. The lightly salty crepe is crunchy on the outside but still soft on the inside, just the way I like it. The egg, spinach, cheese, and turkey crepe I had was as good as it gets. The ingredients complemented each other well, spinach was done but not soggy, and the cheese was not too overpowering in taste.

Portions are good too! One will fill you up and they are generous with their ingredients.

On the other hand, the sweet ones tend to get sickening rather quickly. The large amounts of nutella and whip cream made me feel like I was eating nutella with a side of crepe (nothing wrong with that of course, but if you're not much of a sweet tooth like me, maybe share this with someone).

Fast, Fresh, Fabulous!

Yummy savory - Fresh spinach, Cheddar, Turkey, Sundried Tomatoes... if you ask they'll put more spinach and less cheese; makes you feel better about yourself but it's stills tasty

Yummy sweet - Nutella & Strawberries, 'nuff said

Note: the big chickeny one, forgot the name, is a little messy. it's been stewing, and tastes great, just gets drippy.

...If you want savory & sweet and would be too full with both, but got a friend around... ask to split. They're nice like that =)

This place has ruined all other creperies for me.

I wandered in to this tiny hole-in-the-wall with a small group of family and friends. We each ordered our own preference of sweet and savory crepes. And we each quickly decided we could never enjoy another crepe from anywhere else ever again. Of course, we all shared each others'. They were amazing. All of them. I mean it. I've tried quite a few other crepe places since moving to LA a couple years ago, but nothing even comes close. Anytime I visit, I have to go and get my fix.

Aside from the deliciousness, the staff is great, too. It's a small place, not much room to sit down, but who cares? They'll fold your crepe up for you in a handy little package, easy to eat while you walk.

Love it. Absolutely.

Mmmmmmm......crepes. Sweet or meat, your choice. either one will knock your socks off. This place is great for take out, but we ate in, not fun considering the countertops are 8" deep and blocking the door but the food is great! Cooks are good amigos, stop by for some good hangover food!

When you're a student out late on a weekend night, there is absolutely nothing as spot-hitting (I think I just invented a phrase) as a turkey cranberry avocado crepe with lots of ooey gooey numiness cheese on top. We all know that Crepes-A-Go-Go is not Chez Panisse. But I think it serves it's purpose perfectly, a place for good cheap food you can take on the run, and no matter if you have your "i'm on a diet, no sugar for me" friends or your "WHIPPED CREAM ON MY FACE!" friends, there's something to please.

I can't tell you how much I just love this place! The prices are acceptable and the crepes are just DELICIOUS. For the price you're paying, I think they did a pretty good job! I can't wait till I get the chance to come back here and get another one! :D

This is a great place for those who love crepes. I always get the savory crepes whereas my husband gets the sweet ones. The sweet ones are smeared with Nutella, and the choice of the fruits such as strawberries, kiwis, bananas. And the savory ones are with spinach, chicken, cheese, mushroom. 
Oh my god, they are so delicious and i cant get enough and funny thing is even when i m full, i still want more. Damn!
