my goodness.. i dont care what people say... the banana nutella crepes here are so goooood!!! its my breakfast every morning on way to class! I took a star off just because the crepe can be a little soggy/soft sometimes. But now I always ask for extra crispy, so all is good!

I have lived in Berkeley for the past four years, and I did not visit Crepes A-Go Go until a few weeks ago, and I just went again yesterday for dinner because I loved it so much last time!  So far I have only had the cheese, turkey, and avocado savory crepe with swiss cheese, and it was absolutely delicious.  I also tried their sweet crepe with Nutella and strawberries, which was also yummy!

The people there are so nice, and it's really cool to see them make my crepes =)  Plus it's so fast and a good break from the normal sandwich or burger.  I can't wait to try more of their crepes (lemon, butter, ice cream, etc.) and let you guys know!

I found it kind of gross that they used pre-made crepes... how hard is it really to make one for me on the spot? Anyway, I don't know what it was but something about the crepe/nutella/banana ratio was just off. It really felt like something I could've made myself. On the bright side, it was huge.

I'd come here again if I was really craving it though.

I love any weekend I get to spend in cal for the food. Food. The food of cal overwhelms whatever things you have against cal. end of story.

the crepes are huge. this is good. 
i got con-ed into ordering one of the savory crepes instead of the sweet ones. the savory ones are giant sandwiches inside of crepes. large amounts of cheese and whatever else you want inside of a large pancake like crispy bread thing. 

I had cheese (pepper jack) + avocado + turkey. Now I blame myself for ordering anything with avocado, this might be a California weakness I've adopted. this wasn't super good. it was okay. i liked the avocado (go figure). but the cheese was strange and that's probably my fault for saying pepper jack, but it doesn't belong in a crepe. think pancakes with hearty chili and cheese on top, if this wets your appetite, first ew. second, go ahead and get the pepper jack. 

i'd agree with some of the other people the crepes were not as crispy as i would like, but the last time i had one of these (banana and nutella), it was pretty crispy so maybe they are slacking or just i don't know...something. 

order sweet, not savory. enjoy.

Love Berkeley, especially Telegraph.  Whenever I'm hanging out down here I love to stop in this crepery and get a decent crepe.  First off, I almost always get a sweet crepe, and they are always good; soft, sweet, and satisfy my sweet tooth.  This time, I got an eggplant and vegetable crepe instead and I wasn't as pleased.  The crepe was dry and almost bland.  I probably will just stick to the sweet ones for now on.  There is only a few bar stools along the wall and no customer restroom.  Other than that, I will always come back for a quick fix for my sweet cravings.
7 bucks for a dessert crepe is the biggest scam on the face of the planet, I don't care how good they are.

Soooo good!  Spend my summer in Berkeley and had cravings for Crepes A Go Go alll the time.  Any crepe with nutella is delicious, and if you want to go all out get it with ice cream.  Just watch out for spills if you're getting your crepe to go!  I recommend this place 100%.

i absolutely love this place. it was one of the first businesses to catch my eye when i came to cal for the first time, and it was the first place in berkeley where i spent my money. i have never been disappointed by this place.

when i went here a couple days back, i ordered a cheddar cheese, spinach, and egg crepe. yummy deliciousness in my tummy. :D
they are definitely not stingy with their ingredients, and my mouth was filled with flavorful cheese with each bite i took. i downed that thing in ten minutes.

service is pretty good. the people are nice and they make the crepes relatively quickly.

major plus is that they take credit cards here. yay. :]

Not the best crepe I've ever had, but still crave worthy! 

Every time I've come here, all my food has been hot and fresh (they make it in front of you) and delicious. 

Both savory and sweet are worth a try. Believe it or not, the butter and sugar crepe is simple and enough to satisfy any sweet tooth. They have all kinds of flavor combos, or you can ask them to make your own. 

Not a great place to sit and eat, they make most of their crepes made to be ate on the go. 

Humble and unassuming place, so don't expect too much atmosphere wise. The staff aren't friendly, but not necessarily rude. It can get busy in here and the line will get long.

got this after some bomb pizza at blondies! it was a great dessert! but a very very tight space to eat in. but its okay because you get to sit closer to your food and smell the goodness!

i would like to come here and try more than a strawberry nutella crepe so i will definitely update again when i visit. but from my first and only visit to this place i had a good experience. cashier was very nice and seemed like he enjoyed his job. it didn't take very long to make the crepe and it packed great flavor for it just being strawberries and nutella. definitely coming back here to try different items!

selected a cheese & turkey crepe for ~$5.50. they used deli meat. that makes me sad. crepe skin + two measly slices of deli meat + shredded cheese is not my idea of a savory crepe. had i known what i was ordering, i would've stayed home and made a quesadilla instead.

So delicious! I had the nutella strawberry crepe and it was sooo good! The crepe is pretty big and soft. Melts in your mouth! They put powdered sugar on top as well. Would come back for more--next time a savory one!

Hands down the best crepe in North America. Everything on the menu tastes great from just a sugar and butter to the "King Lias" if you're feeling adventurous. This is easily the best and most convenient place to get lunch after class right next to campus.

University or Telegraph - they're both equally delicious. Beware however, if you aren't a sweet tooth then it can easily be too much. Have your own savory crepe but share a sweet crepe because it's a LOT of nutella and banana to get through. Very good though.

I'm not sure how anyone can do wrong with a crepe. Give me some Nutella, some bananas, and I'm set for life. So if you enjoy crepes, and you're looking for a pick me up, come here. You won't regret it.

I've just found my new place to go when I want to get my egg n cheese on wrapped in a squishy blanket of crepe, with a touch of crispy, both sweet and savory, and not too greasy.  Menu options aren't as extensive as other crepe places, but the guys here know how to fold your crepe up just right so you can go-go-go.  

$5 and you're out the door with a crepe that fits perfectly into your hand.  I'm excited to have finally found a food item that I can eat comfortably while walking (and shopping!).  Grip that sucker tight as you battle the masses down Telegraph or through Sproul Plaza, you don't wanna have it hijacked by a starving student or bum.

4 stars for the best savory crepe I've eaten in my life, the cheese-avocado-tomato crepe. It's amazing. Everything else is just a nice bonus.

Wait times are very short and portions are enormous. The crepes are also thicker than usual, which I think I prefer. I wish I could get the recipe from them.

I come here all the time as it is a fantastic quick snack that you can walk to class with and eat easily.

The only reason this place doesn't get five stars is the drippy sauce from their chicken crepe which--while delicious--is not conducive to walking and eating. Other than that I want to stress that this place is great. Always friendly, fast, fantastic service; always get exactly what I want with no screw ups, and always delicious.

My favorite is probably fresh spinach, turkey, cheddar, and monterey jack (and an egg if I'm feeling extra hungry).

Such fun to watch the crepe guy stand in the window and flip giant sheets of crepe batter and butter. 
It was what first drew me into this joint, about a block from campus (right next to Walgreens) - they've got a classic but fun selection of savory and sweet crepes priced from around $2-6. I stop by here every once in awhile for a strawberry-nutella-banana, which they without fail wrap perfectly and powder with powdered sugar and a ton of whipped cream. Perfect as it is cheap.
Staff usually won't make small talk with you but is friendly nonetheless. There's a bar-style seating arrangement inside that's comfortable when away from peak hours (it gets quiet later at night on most weekdays), but I wouldn't recommend sitting around in here - Sproul plaza on campus, about a block down the street, is where you'd want to head if you need to sit down.
Watch out - sometimes they close early if there isn't a ton of business! I once came down 15 minutes before closing time and it was all locked up. Be sure not to catch the tail end of the night!

This place is fcking bomb! I love their breakfast croissants all day any day. Then I come back for some of their chicken, bell pepper, onions, pepperjack, tomato later on. Its so fcking marvelous with the combination of the sweet and saltiness of the crepe. I sometimes get it crispy and it gives that scrumptious similar essence when you bite into a potato chip. Its a lot better compared to most of the other restaurants I've been to around Berkeley. Price is decent and you get what you pay for and sometimes they give a little bit too much, and that is perfect for me because I would be happy to come again next time. However, I sometimes hate this place because it is fcking addicting and I am gaining weight so I better start hitting up the gym.

I need to grab a quick lunch between classes & I want CHEESE. Where do I go? Crepes A Go Go, of course! Monterey jack, avocado, & tomato hits the spot every time. If I need a wake-up call, Pepperjack.

It's not cheap, but I wouldn't call it expensive, or pricey. & while they may not exactly serve gourmet crepes... what the hell do you expect? It's Berkeley.

So before I came to this place, i thought crepes were meh. But I gave Crepes a Go Go a shot and I LOVED it. They make their crepes a little bit thicker than most crepes, and a tad crispy which I personally like. I've only had their nutella strawberry crepe, its delicious! These crepes are cheap, and its cool how you can take a crepe to go. Definitely recommend this place!
excellent for a walking meal treat..... not so excellent if you want quiet or peaceful, but if you are on Telegraph near the campus then it's obvious quiet isn't why you're there..... enjoy

Solid location, delicious crepes. Probably the best crepes locally, but not the best ever---but the strawberry banana nutella ones will always make my mouth water. For days. 

Their sweet crepes are all delicious---I've tried each and every one. It's fun to watch them being made and the crepe chef will give you a choice whether or not you want whipped cream, etc. 

Their savory ones are kind of hit or miss, in my opinion. A lot of the time they use deli meat, but just like their sweet ones, it's all very fresh and made right in front of you. I would give the savory ones a 3 star rating.

Aside from the crepes, they offer a number of drink options like coffee, hot chocolate, etc., but their carrot juice is pretty exceptional. I don't know if they have it year round but it is a rich burnt orange color and tastes super fresh. Their orange juice is basically the same as Strada's, also very good, but relatively pricey. 

And their paninis---especially the chicken and sun-dried tomato---are delicious too! It's nice that they have this option because I don't particularly like getting the savory crepes, but sometimes I want "real food" and not my strawberry-banana-nutella favorite.

Anyway, it's awesome that this branch (there are a number of other locations around the country) is so close to campus. It has flexible hours (open until 10), which is a plus. Don't try to eat-in, though; there's very little space---counter seats are available, but anyone trying to get to the cashier will inevitably bump into you or spill powdered sugar from their crepe on you or something. Most of the time they give you a "walk and eat" option.

thank god they open at 9am, or else i wouldn't know what to eat for my breakfast/brunch/dessert. I love the crepes here because they always come out hot. For lunch, i would create my own savory crepe with tomato, mushroom, spinach, and egg. Most of the time i just get the classic: Nutella only. I don't know what's in the Nutella crepe but it always brightens my day. There's once I would get Nutella everyday for 2 weeks straight... the service here is quick and friendly. I'm so hooked.... i actually just finished eating another Nutella crepe, can't wait to go again tomorrow. Maybe i will try their House Special, that's my roommate's favorite.

This restaurant is a kind of hole in the wall establishment, not because it doesn't stand out - because it actually does - but because of the relatively small storefront. If you don't pay attention while you are walking by, you could easily walk past it without noticing at all. But then again, this is Berkeley we are talking about, so I guess that isn't anything new.

To date, I have only been here twice. I ordered savory crepes both times, mainly because I am more partial towards savory crepes. With that being said, I did find myself wanting to try the sweet crepes, but I never got the chance to because I was always full by the time that I finished my savory ones. I guess I will have to hold myself back the next time I visit.

When you first walk in, the first thing that you'll notice is that the amount of space that you have is quite narrow. On the left, you can see the chefs making the crepes for patrons who have already ordered. From what I can tell, there seems to be a sort of assembly line action going on, but then again, I wasn't paying too much attention as I was mainly preoccupied with talking to my friends. During the busy hours, you can also expect a healthy line of customers who have already ordered waiting again in a second line as they wait eagerly for their crepes to be crafted. On your right, you will find some counter space along with a row of stools that patrons can sit down on as they consume their crepes.

If you're lucky, there won't be a line to the register, but more often than not, you will find a line going to the register between the line for those who have already ordered and the people who are enjoying their crepes already on the stools. It can get rather cramped given the limited amount of space, but it does give you an odd sense of belonging. It sounds odd, I must admit, but I really have no other way to explain it.

On to the crepes themselves. The crepes were relatively cheap compared to what I have become accustomed to - about 6 dollars on average. My crepe had turkey, two fried eggs, spinach and melted pepper jack cheese to tie it all together. The crepe was crisp and the fillings were piping hot; just the way I like it. It must be noted that my crepe was kind of dry. I guess it could be attributed to the eggs. It detracted a little from the overall experience, but is of negligible importance. For the price, however, I definitely have nothing to complain about.

You have the option of eating in, or you could take it to go, or have it "walking" whatever that means. Personally, I always ate in. I always found crepes tasted best straight from the griddle.

As for the rating, I would give this establishment four stars. The food itself is good, especially for the given price. The general ambiance on a good day without being crowded by people is very warm and welcoming and I would not mind spending time chatting casually with friends while we eat. However, when it does get crowded, I can get a tad claustrophobic and my need to get out quickly takes over. Overall, I would recommend this place to my friends for their delicious and relatively cheap crepes.

Watch your crepe being made right in front of you!! A fantastic quick and healthy (?) bite while walking Telegraph. Sooooo tasty with a Perrier or Orangina!
So many choices I'm just gonna have to keep going back to try them all!!

I am always craving crepes so Crepes a Go Go is the place I go to often since it is a short walk from my friend's apartment.  My crepe of choice here is the banana, brown sugar, and cinnamon crepe (it normally comes with apples but I'm a sucker for bananas) and I like the bit of whip cream they add to it in the end.  

While I do come back and enjoy my crepe, I must admit that it isn't that great of a crepe.  It definitely feeds the craving, but if there were another option nearby, I would have definitely be going there instead...

I don't understand why this place is getting the bad reviews. A lot of people are complaining about having luke warm, ready-made crepes. I went here and got a FRESH crepe made on the spot. Of course I had to wait a good 10 minutes or so.

I though it was worth the wait. The crepe was nice and buttery, soft and sizzling hot. It was wrapped around enormous amounts of cheese, spinach, and mushrooms. My boyfriend got the other veggie crepe (something with tomatoes) and it was just as good.  Both crepes were easy to hold, delicious, moderately priced, and went perfectly with our sunny day picnic. Due to the bad reviews I've read, I think I'll have to visit this place again to be sure it deserves the 4 stars.
nothing out of this world but i didn't expect too much. we tried out the spinach, sun dried tomato and feta crepe which was alright and the banana honey crepe with was just alright too.

I like this place for a quick bite before or after class as I am coming or going from campus. My favorite is the make your own with turkey, cheese, and tomato. They pack it full of  stuff so it is super yummy.

My fiancee and decided to go out to Berkeley on a late Sunday evening when we stumbled across this place. i had a Nutella & Banana crepe while my fiancee declined to partake, after eating one bite of mine she made us go back so she could indulge on a strawberry & Ice cream crepe. REMARKABLE and a definite must if you're in the area.

Need somewhere where you can eat a cheap, easy, quick and delicious meal (or snack), a treat that is either sweet or savory? If you haven't already, stop by Crepes-a-Go-Go, located between Bancroft Way and Durant Avenue.

I've heard of them so much, and I was super hungry, just walking around Berkeley all the time to get from place to place and from class to class. I have to say, I was eager to try their crepes, and they did not disappoint. I ordered a sweet crepe, one containing nutella with fresh strawberries. I was thinking of getting a savory one, but I had sweet cravings. My friend did get a savory crepe with avocado and cheese, which actually sounded and looked delicious. After one orders a crepe, one can watch the chefs create it. The storefront consists of a clear window through which one can see stacks of jars of nutella and crepes being made. I was impressed. These crepes  cook on the griddles so quickly!

Read more of my review here: http://calibermag.org/articles/telegraph-treasures-go-to-crepes-a-go-go/
Ask my son or daughter, they would tell you 5r stars.  Me, i don't eat craps so, so there you go.

There are no good crepe places I know of in the San Fernando Valley (just north of L.A.) and every time I crave one I think of Crepes A-Go-Go!!! I would walk to class, trying to avoid Shattuck, just so I wouldn't be tempted with a savory, savory crepe... Mmm... Cheese & mushroom... that was the best...

Great crepes, great people. Very fast, easy and tasty. Although a little on the pricey side, particularly for being practically on campus, where inexpensive food is king. Very small place.

Recommend all the time.

Tasty vegetarian crepe, but not the best. There wasn't much room to get to the cashier to place an order and not much room to wait for your order. It's definitely a place where you will get the food to-go,so don't expect a lot of space to accommodate a big party. Their menu had savory and sweet options and I got a tomato, spinach, cheese and mushroom crepe. It usually doesn't take much to make my belly full, but this didn't do the trick. I still felt hungry after. :\ 

I'll give it another shot but next time I'll get something sweeter.

The sweet crepes are to DIE for, but the savory crepes are really good, too.  The men who work here are super nice.  I had trouble deciding between a peanut-butter-and-banana or caramel-and-banana crepe, and the crepe-master suggested caramel.  With powdered sugar and whipped cream.

THANK YOU, crepe-master!  Possibly the most delicious thing my tastebuds have ever encountered.  If I hadn't been traveling and low on funds, I would have totally given you a bigger tip!  As it is, now, all I can do is give you another shining Yelp review, not that you needed yet another one of those!  

P.S.  This place gets busy sometimes, but it's SO worth the wait.

They have quite a variety of crepes. My friends and I came after class to grab a quick bite before we went into the city. I got the sauteed chicken with tomato, bell pepper, garlic, onion and cheese (I chose cheddar). It was delicious, but quite messy. The crepe itself was perfect. Very light and just the right thickness. Now I know why all my friends who visit Berkeley always want to come to Crepes A Go Go.

I have to say that when ever I go to Berkely, this is the place to stop for. Their crepes are cheap and humungous/delicious. I have never tasted a better crepe. Although their restaurant is small, and its hard to eat calmly because the line is located behind you. You are better off taking it to go. Overall, a great place to buy a crepe.
Love this place because you can literally take the crepe a go go with you! Fast and easy to get that yummy snack, but it can be a little pricey hence the four stars.

I got a savory crepe with chicken breast, bell peppers, onions and swiss cheese. The crepe batter was very good. Better than the ones I usually get because it had a slight sweet taste to it instead of just blandness. Soft and a little crisp at the edges. The chicken breast, bell peppers and onions were very tasty. I loved the slight sweetness from the bell peppers.

I love how they ask you if you want it here, to go, or to walk. I've never heard the "to walk" option before so it was amusing. :)

I've had crepes before, but never like this.  First of all I was surprised how expensive the crepe menu was and then they handed me my crepe and I took my thought back.  It was huge and delicious!!!  I had a nutella, fresh strawberries, bananas, and topped it off with whip cream.  It was perfect!  I am literally wiping the drool from my mouth as I think about my delicious crepe.  Until my next trip to Berkeley I'll have my delicious memories to think about.

i ABSOLUTELY LOVE their savory crepes! I first discovered crepes about five years ago and I can say that crepes a go go is pretty consistent.  

What I love about the savory crepes over the sweet ones is that the softer/thicker crepe tastes better with the savory flavors.  I go all out for the House Special crepe. hehe.

It might just be that I'm used to and prefer sweet crepes with the thinner and crispier crepe.  

It is a taddd pricey but I really never hold it against small businesses for a little higher prices unless the food's terrible because I don't think people understand the economy in terms of the owners instead of their own cheap, selfish asses. ANYWY, the crepes are so packed in that you immediately forget it once you start eating.  

Not gonna lie, sometimes I order 2 because i get selfish and think I can eat it all and sometimes.... I do. hehe
Very good crepes.  Just a bit pricey, but I would come back again and again.

Delicious crepes!! I love the strawberry, banana, and nutella crepes. Super fresh and delicious. The savory crepes are also awesome. Especially with the kick from the Pepper Jack cheese. Love that the food is made right in front of you. When i'm craving a crepe, this place is definitely a go-to. Pretty friendly staff, convenient location and decent prices. This place is pretty great.

Omigod.  That is all I have to say.

Not.

Crèpes a Go-Go is my FAVORITE place to stop when I'm in Berkeley.  Even though I recently discovered the wonders of Ici, I still come here for my strawberry and Nutella crèpe every time I'm in town.  I can't cheat on my staple.  Too warm, too sweet and chocolatey, too gooey, too perfect for walking around and munching on a chilly Berkeley evening.  In fact, I get a little peevish if someone jostles me while I'm walking down the street with my crèpe.  I think I even threatened to kick someone in the shins once because they made me spill a Nutella-drenched strawberry.  

Yeah, I've heard a few French people (or, at least, snobby hipsters) state that their savory crèpes are not correctly made-apparently, they use sweet dough when they ought to use something else.  But whatever.  I'm not a foodie, and until I try a real French crèpe, I think I'll hold my judgment.  The only downsides I can see involve the somewhat pricey menu and the cramped, rather dingy space.  But given that this place is on Telegraph, that they use fresh ingredients, and that there are much dirtier places around (*cough* Fat Slice *cough*), I can overlook these detractors because Crèpes a Go-Go makes my tummy happy.

I always recommend this place to friends going to Berkeley for the first time.

back in the day when i thought noodles were disgusting and rice was revolting, i ate crepes everyday and this is where i would come to get them. 

i came for both their savory and sweet crepes, and the staff always knocked off a buck or two

Wasn't too impressed with the crepes here. The crepe that my girlfriend had was almost too thick and sort of rubbery. Obviously not cooked all the way through. They serve everything on paper plates, which is kind of lame. It makes the thick and rubbery crepe extremely hard to cut. The place was also pretty warm inside and very crowded. Not like there was a lot of people in there, but just not much room to move around.

The crepes are undeniably tasty (I've also learned to love pepper jack cheese because of them). The prices for crepes are a bit on the high side although perhaps that's because despite the fact that I make meals out of the crepes I can see how other people would need to eat 2-3 in order to make a meal. 

It's mostly a grab n go place so not much can be asked for from the ambiance, but for the to go sweet crepes you can ask for fresh made whip cream to go = mmm.

In addition, they usually have a selection of "special combinations" which they came up with more recently than the listed combos. I've liked all the ones I've tried.

So I didn't think this location was AS BAD as many people have claimed. 

I went in around 6:30pm on a Thursday, and it was not busy at all. I saw the crepe maker making a lot of crepes, folding them, and placing them in this big stack. Maybe he was making them for later? Which isn't what I wanted to see...I was praying that I would get a fresh crepe (which I REALLY wished I had asked for), but unfortunately, I got an already made crepe that was in a warming tray. 

I ordered a veggie crepe which contained roasted eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers, fresh basil, sun-dried tomatoes, herbed goat cheese and feta cheese. Fortunately, the worker warmed up my crepe on the griddle again. 

The crepe itself was thick - much thicker than other crepes that I've had. Aren't they supposed to be very thin? But it wasn't bad, the crepe was tasty, but too thick for my standards. As for the innards, they were a bit mushier than I would like, and the cheese is what gave everything flavor. I also didn't taste the basil at all. 

The crepe was $7 - not incredibly expensive but I expected more at the same time.

Overall, I'd go back one more time to try one of their sweet crepes and see if it's any better. The savory crepe that I had left a bit to be desired, however.

I used to eat here a lot more (as in maybe once a month), back a few years ago when the strawberry nutella crepe was 5.75.  Even then I thought that was pricey for a dollop of batter, half a cup of fruit and a tablespoon of nutella.  

However after coming back from summer break, I discovered that a strawberry nutella crepe was 7.75!!!  That is outrageous and unacceptable.  Their food is not that high of quality, and a measly crepe should never go for the same price as a meal at any other restaurant.  They are making a killing ripping poor students off.  

Naturally, I boycotted and did not go there once for over a semster.  Then I say they were offering 15% off as part of "15 years in Berkeley", and I decided to indulge myself.  The crepe still turned out to be 6.25 or so, but that's leaps and bounds better than almost 8$.

I wouldn't recommend this place unless you're looking to splurge, it's just too expensive for what you get.

I haven't had Crepes A-Go Go in a while, but when I do stop by, I'm left feeling really satisfied. I normally order one of the sweet crepes: nutella & bananas, and I'm good to go. You might not think it'll fill you up from the looks of it, but boy, it sure does! Don't let it fool you, but one crepe will leave you full for quite some time.
amazing crepes with fresh ingredients, made right before your eyes. There's a reason that the line goes halfway down the block

This is one of my favorite crepe places around.
My old standby is Nutella and bananas. But they have something called "King Lias" which is the same thing plus almonds, coconut and whipped cream. It was so GD good!!! I can't leave Telegraph without coming here. Good thing I don't come too often.

Hate to be a hater, but I really didn't like the crepe here.  It was almost midnight and I'm starving looking for food.  I wanted something light and sweet.  I got the chocolate, nutella, strawberry crepe.  Few bites into it I realized it was just too damn sweet for me.  I don't know...just did not like the taste at all.  Normally, when I'm starving anything tastes good.  But the crepes here have failed me.

My friends and I went to this place once.  Let's just say that I'm glad I ordered pizza from Blondie's next door.  All my friends that got crepes had um...  severe food poisoning that day.  And all of the ones that did not get crepes were ok.  Coincidence?  Nah.  It was definitely that place.  As far as crepes go, they're good.  But it's at a risk.  3 stars because their crepes are good, but need to improve on sanitation issues.
Yummy, soft crepes fast and cheap right off campus. Perfect for a quick student's snack.

My friends and I love this place. Their crepes are so yummy. I usually get the savory crepe with the sauteed chicken, bell peppers, and onions. It is absolutely delicious! The crepe is nicely crisp and warm. I have also tried some of their sweet crepes which are quite good as well.

I had a major craving for a crispy, sweet, yummy crepe and drooled the whole day thinking about when I would finally be able to go get some later that day. Sadly, it did not meet my expectations. It was my first sweet crepe here (I had a savory crepe here years ago which was okay but obviously not enough for me to come back for years). 

The crepe was filling, I'll give them that. But the crepe itself was pretty soggy so by the time you get halfway through, I was pretty much bored with it. I prefer Japanese crepes which are much crispier :)

I got the strawberry and banana crepe with nutella. Generous serving of Nutella for sure. 

It came out to be $6 something and when I gave the cashier 10 bucks, he only gave me a few coins. Wth. Make sure your workers dont try to cheat customers of their correct change please. I saw a previous post about incorrect change by 10 cents but my case was by a couple of dollars! Make sure you count your change before you walk away!

I love the crepes here. I have fun watching them make it too. The only crepe I ever get here is cheese, avocado, and tomato, and that keeps me full for a while. One thing though: Boo to the fact that they raised their prices!
small and busy, but great crepes! not a place to sit down. there is a bar you can sit out, but i mostly recommend this location if you want to pop in for a quick bit or get something to go.

i love the fact that they have both sweet and savory crepes here. yum, decent priced for the amount of food they put in their crepes. there was a line when i went but didnt have to wait long for the crepes to be done. yum!

I came in here again last week and was pleasantly surprised that Crepes A-Go Go now serves PANINIS!  I got the linguica and peppers which was phenomenal.

They have about three different types, but if this becomes a regular thing you can definitely guarantee more business from me and my friends who's favorite foods are: 1. Crepes 2. Paninins.

Great option!  Hope to see more of it!

Egg, cheese, and spinach crepe: Perfect.  The crepe is buttery, eggy, light, and airy, yet stiff enough to hold all the ingredients.  The fillings flawlessly complement each other and the spinach is a delicious touch.  If I don't have one of these in a while I start to dream about them.  The staff is friendly and accommodating.

My friends all raved about the tastiness and convenience of these crepes.

Vegan Report: Crepes usually aren't vegan.

Strawberry and Gnutella is one of the most popular dessert crepe so it's a safe bet getting it.  I however found that it wasn't that great.  I thought there was too much gnutella (you must be thinking "blasphemy! there's never too much gnutella"), but it's true.  Too much gnutella for the amount of strawberries mixed in.  And being overpriced as they are, I recommend them putting in extra strawberries rather than taking out gnutella to balance it out.

They also have breakfast/lunch crepes.  I've never had a non-sweet crepe so I feel weird ordering one.  I should at least give it a try the next time I'm back in B-town.  Until next time!

the turkey, cheese and cranberry always hit the spot!!!

slightly on the expensive side, i feel, for a walk-n-eat food item.. but they are having their 15 anniversary with 15% off, i felt a little better paying $6 ish for the crepe. they have good nutella sweet crepes too!! 

loved it!! 

would i go back? sure!

This place does great crepes for lunch. I'm a lunchtime regular every few weeks.  I quite enjoy their savory crepes.  Their house special with turkey, egg, and spinach is yummy.  I also am a huge fan of their crepe with spicy sauteed peppers, caramelized onions, and linguica sausage.  Yum!  They do whole wheat crepes which I prefer.  

You can get the crepes to go, so I like to take them and find a sunny spot to enjoy.  I always come for lunch, so I've never tried their sweet crepes...maybe one day I'll come in for a snack.  The prices are reasonable.  One caution...the way they wrap the crepes "to walk", they can tend to suddenly start to leak juices out the bottom.  I've had a couple unfortunate "jeans" or "shirt" incidents this way, so be careful.

A fun local chain...check it out!
Always a spot to satisfy the sweet tooth! Plus, the store hours are perfect if you are a night owl like myself. The Nutella crepe and the Caramel crepe are perfect. I left with two in my stomach!

I thought the crepes were reasonably priced... a huge slab of crepe with a whole banana, crap load of strawberries and all the whip cream you want for ~$6?  Not a rip-off.  Definitely able to share an order between to people with normal appetites... and it's only supposed to be a dessert, right?
I guess you can eat a crepe as a meal.. but seriously?

I come here very often, the staff is friendly and the crepes are delicious. The dessert crepes are pretty much all good across the board. I tend to go with the boring but reliable strawberry nutella, sometimes with a scoop of ice cream! The savory crepes are also good. I get the avocado-cheese-tomato, which is really good, sometimes I think it tastes better than the dessert crepes!

I probably wouldn't come here when it's too crowded though, there's not much space to move around.

ive had better. they offer standard fillings [nutella, fruit, whip cream, ham, cheese, etc] but the texture of the crepes is what threw me off - rubbery, thick [i love my crepes thin and crispy], and way to "eggy" for my liking. the flavors of mixed fruit, nutella, whip cream, and a whole lot of EGG intermingling in my mouth was not satisfying. 

i much prefer sophie's crepes in japantown. they make the best crepes!

----

5 stars: i am a loyal customer and cannot live without this place/restaurant!

4 stars: consistently great food. a place i would definitely frequent if i dont already.

3 stars: good food. id come back for more if a particular craving for something specific they offer hit me. 

2 stars: for the sheer reason of convenience and semi mediocre food [but convenience being the majority of reason] id come back.

1 star: id never be caught dead in the place ever ever again.

I've had the crepes, but I come here for the paninis.  It's an uncomfortably small space -- definitely for "to go" orders -- and I always end up in a little argument with the manager-person about getting something without the meat (he doesn't think it'll be good -- well, it's the best I've had in Berkeley!) or charging me more for an ingredient or two less, but it's worth it.  They consistently make the most scrumptious paninis here, even if I have to beg and pay a little too much.  I don't come often because of the cost, but I do consider it a treat and am happy I live near this spot.  It's a fun little place with good service and unexpected quality for another cute crepe shop.
Best crepes i have ever had  in the bay area!!!!!!! and its quick and you dont have to wait forever!

Quality crepes, decent prices, pretty average in my opinion, but since they have such good locations and friendly staff they get four stars. But if you're looking for an extraordinary crepe, go elsewhere.

Crepe's have always been one of my all time favorite treats. We stopped by Berkeley today specifically to give a Go Go a try. Even though the UCB Campus was holding a debate tournament and the line took like 20mins, the Crepe's were awesome. Carameled onions, Sauted peppers, herb Feta, one egg.. Delish!  I got the Sauted Chicken with Pepper Jack and Peppers being that it was for lunch. What really caught our eye and ensured a return visit would have to be the Nutella, Peanut Butter, sliced Bananas Crepe w/ a scoop of Vanilla. (only down side the Root beer float was Horriblay!)
So good!  I've had their savory ham, pepper jack cheese, and avocado crepe too many times to keep count.  The batter has a sweet taste to it; the crepe is crunchy and chewy-  delicious  :)
This place is As good as the one in university but it is too small !!

YUM YUM YUM YUM!!!!!  One of my favorites on telegraph!  I've tried their savory and sweet crepes and either way they are just delicious!   My favorite sweet crepe is the strawberry, lemon and sugar.  As for savory,  you can't go wrong with turkey and cheese! They can make it easy to take with you while you're walking too! It's just a tiny bit cramped in here, definitely not a ton of space, but other than that, they have great prices, friendly service, and absolutely fantastic crepes!

Amazing! I would recommend Crepes A Go Go to anyone. 

I get the sweet crepes and my boyfriend gets the savory, both are equally appetizing. Any of the sweet crepes with chocolate are definitely sweet, but not outragous. If you are sensitive to how sweet something is, go for something without the chocolate or ask for it to be light. 

$5 might seem like a lot for a crepe, but they are pretty big and filled to capacity. You can even get ice cream on it for $1 more!

Also - all this nonsense about premade Crepes is no longer true. They make your crepe when you order, you can watch them put the batter on and everything.

I don't like crepes, but they do make pretty good tasting crepes regardless. The cashier guy there the last time I went was nice, but almost TOO nice. My friend and I ordered a banana + nutella crepe, and the cashier guy started to ask my friend if she liked strawberries. My friend said yes, and then he added in free strawberries into our crepe! The plus was the free strawberries. The negative was the slightly creepy way we got the free strawberries. Maybe I'm just conservative and it weirds me out when store people I've never met before are THAT UNWARRANTEDLY nice (as opposed to food places that already have a reputation of giving out free food)...

My boyfriend and I always come here whenever we come to Berkeley. ALWAYS.

We always get the Banana Nutella, which is always amazing. Topped with Whipped Creme. MMM! How could you go wrong? :')

They always end up stuffing us for a while too. I'd love to try the other ones, but as always, crepes are a bit on the pricey side.. and I, being broke as hell.. have never tried any other crepes from here yet :'(

ANYWAY, it's a nice crepe place. It's pretty tiny in there, but it doesn't change the fact that it's f*cking delicious.

When it's not crowded, they make their crepes really fast.  I love how you can get it to go and they wrap it up in a paper towel and foil, perfect for when you are on your way to class.  I always got the strawberry and nutella crepe, which was really messy.  Be sure to bring napkins if you are eating it on the go, it's pretty embarrassing to walk into class with nutella all over your face. :)

As Sandy T. has said... crepes from lukewarm pre-made crepes. 

As Aimee L. has said...  burns crotch if not careful

Luke warm crepe + dripping filling = sad, burned crotch, messy hands Steven
Really yummy dessert and savory crepes but for the high price I don't think I can continue satisfying my cravings there.

it can get pretty busy here especially during lunch with all the college kids. it is totally worth the wait though. i just recently discovered the kings alias with almonds, coconut, bananas, nutella, and whip cream. i added in some strawberries. they are super filling and delicious. 
parking is kind of a pain because it is all street parking so if you do not go to the college and you drive in it is not always easy to park. 
since it is more of a hole in the wall place there is really no where to sit inside. they have about 10 bar stools along the back wall and thats it. personally i like to walk around with mine. but if you are poking for a sit down place this is not it.

Oooh, crepes in Southside! It's nice to see something different on Telegraph Ave. I don't really see Crepes as a meal (means I probably eat too much) but as a snack (though I prefer the savory kinds).

+ Visible cooking, makes you feel better about your food
+ Quick food
+ Options, options, options
+ Good service, they get my complicated orders right!
-  Constrained space, can't really sit and eat there
-  Kinda on the pricey end
-  Tomatoes and avocado aren't so fresh the two times I've been

Final Call:
Mostly a place for students at Cal who need something different from all the typical fast food. 

********************

Munchies:
1. Savory crepe: spinach, eggs, avocado, tomatoes, and cheddar
     +Packed full of crepery goodness
     -They didn't get rid of the egg shells the second time =/

I think the crepes are a bit pricey. Just sugar costs more than 2 dollars and quite frankly I tend to get up to the 5 dollar crepes in order to feel somewhat full. That being said they are delicious and a great treat.

Great to get a big breakfast at (cheese and egg savory crepes mmm) or split a big dessert at (cheapest is: lemon, butter, sugar if you're getting it alone; otherwise get the strawberry ones mmm).

There's always extra toppings toward the bottom due to the triangle shape, but it makes it very easy to eat on the go.

Yes it's overpriced but in the UC Berkeley area there's no where else if you're craving crepes. Btw, the shattuck location has a better selection, with salmon crepes!

I also think the crepes are a bit pricey. I came here for lunch and orderd the strawberry & nutella crepe, to go, for $5.50. It was tasty and quite big. It satisfied me, but I wouldn't recommend a sweet crepe for lunch. The place is a bit cramped, but they offer a wide selection of sweet and savory crepes. It's a good place to go for a small meal or dessert.
their crepes are soggy and they use way too much cheese.

Gotta love the crepes in any way! specially when I'm craving for the sweets and the fruit. my Favorite is the turkey cheese and avocado, that's for my snack, and for my sweets is strawberry, banana, and nutella! Walking distance from work, and the price is fair, cause the crepe is big, and the stuffing is a lot! TOATLLY WORTH THE MONEY!

I had a ham, cheese, and avocado today. It was alright. Kind of simple for the price. It kind of reminded me of a quesadilla. Next time I'll have a strawberries and nutella one, they looked a lot better.

It was my first time here and I was a little disappointed with their prices. I've seen other places that sell crepes for less than $6 with much more to eat inside the crepes. But this place seemed a little more pricier for not too much food. They charge an extra dollar per scoop of ice cream and the crepe I ordered didn't come with whipped cream.
I had a sweet crepe that was surprisingly filling although it only had nutella and strawberries in it. Although I didn't have any problems with their food (it was delicious) next time I would rather try another crepe place than come here again.

So I am far from a crepe aficionado so forgive me for my lack of com parables. I've had savory and sweet crepes here and from what I recall the savory crepe (I ordered something with chicken, mushrooms, spinach and cheese) was okay. Not bad, but not great. The chicken tasted particularly bland and strangely flaky.

The sweet crepe was great. Nutella, strawberries (lots and lots of strawberries) and melt-in-your-fingers goodness.

I was visiting San Fran and my friend really wanted us to try the crepes here.  hmm... the crepe is more like a burrito.  Its ridiculously big for a good price.  I got the King Lias for $5.50  which consisted of bananas, almonds, shredded coconut, nutella, and whip cream.  YUUMM.  Sadly i couldn't finish the whole thing.  I wish I knew that they had ice cream.  It wasn't on the menu so I didn't know until I was waiting for my crepe and there was an 8 by 11 sign near the front door that said ice cream $1.00.  

The place is really small and HOT.  I don't know how the workers stand the heat.  we waited near the door for our crepes because it was too hot for us.  There was very limited seating inside maybe around 6 chairs? So we took our crepe togo and walked to Berkeley 

Parking is really good.  There is a parking structure and its $1 for the first hour with validation.  I wouldn't use the bathroom in the parking structure though.
CREPES!! nom nom nom!! Savory or sweet they are BOTH delicious! Something I crave whenever I'm not in Berkeley. Like right now... ^^
had one when I was baked and it was GOOD... but then again I was baked.

I just don't know guys.  Good idea, but certainly not an improvement upon the original.  Crepes a go go should be more like crepes uh no no, equipped with rigorous finger wagging.  

They must be doing something right for the American student, because it's crowded a lot of times, but I just don't think you can call it crepes unless having nutella as the central ingredient of your menu is the sole criteria for naming your restaurant after a french food item.  Since the french spit on most American food, I'm not going to use them to explain how un-crepelike this place is, but this place is gloves-down, NOT tres bien.  It's more like a bastardized version of crepes gone wild...  In fact, that would be a much better name for this "restaurant": Crepes gone wild.  Yeah...  

I don't know what else to say.  Two stars.  One for Nutella and one for the guy who thought of putting nutella on the menu.

The Nutella crepe with strawberry and bananas is awesome.  Especially after they finish making the crepes and hand it to you.  For the past three visit to San Francisco/Berkley, my friend and I have stop by Crepes A-Go Go before heading back home to Los Angeles.  Can't have enough of this delicious desert.

I really like crepes-a-go-go. It was like a staple food for me when I took classes at UC Berkeley last summer. I was introduced to this place by my best friend and it brings back wonderful memories. I have only had their lunch crepes but they are so good and filling. I want to try a dessert crepe. Just reviewing this makes me hungry.

Came by while walking on Telegraph. Brother ordered the King Lias(sp?) crepe. I believe it included Nutella, Bananas, Almonds, Shredded Coconut and whip cream. IT was GOOD. Then again anything with Nutella is good. Just keep in mind that it's a little hard to eat while walking because the banana may land on your shirt or maybe its because I'm just not good at eating and walking. 

I crave it as I type this review. Too bad going to Berkeley is not a common occasion. However, if you are ever in the area, definitely a place to check out! It may be a little expensive, but if someone buys it for you it tastes 10x better =)
Solid crepes.  I like to pick up a "King Lias" (whip cream, nutella, bananna, and coconut) in the mornings.

Who doesn't love crepes?  If you don't, then you're a sucker.  Everything from the Nutella and banana crepe to the breakfast crepe with spinach, mushroom, and cheese!  Sure it's a bit on the pricey side, but for me, it's worth the few extra dollars.  One additional star for making it easy for me to eat my crepe and walk.

I could eat Nutella for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Finding out this place makes crepes with Nutella as one of the main ingredients.... yes!

I tried to Strawberry and Nutella crepe. Added a dash of whipped cream and powdered sugar. Delicious! Tons of warm strawberries and the Nutella added that extra kick of sugar.

So good.

i got the spinach, cheddar, and sauteed mushrooms crepe! It was delicious and huge so definitely worth every penny. The crepe was a little drippy though and they gave it to me in a napkin but other than that it was perfect. I need to come back and try a sweet crepe!

I LOVE this place, I've had the paninis and the dessert crepes. They're friggin' awesome! The paninis come loaded with cheese that doesn't overshadow any of the other additions inside the sandwich. The chicken pesto is my favorite, and definitely should not be passed up. But of course you should not leave this place without trying the loaded banana and nutella crepe.  I asked for the scoop of ice cream my first time around, but I found that I didn't even need it, because the actual crepe was not dry at all and was really really good.

Why only four stars you may ask? The only complaints I have is that it is really really small, and that the cooks aren't very friendly.  It's sort of like they know they're food is so good, that I'm not not going to buy something.  
If you don't care about customer service, and you're looking for something good to go, I would definitely recommend this place.

Oh. My. God. I stayed at Berkeley/San Fransisco for less than a week, and I went here twice. I should have gone more.

I have a craving for these crepes, and since I live in southern California, I am very sad that I can't eat one right now :(

The first time I got a Nutella + banana crepe, which was around 4 or 5 dollars. It was so absolutely delicious, especially with a sprinkling of whatever powder they sprinkle on it (powdered sugar? vanilla? no idea.) and some whipped cream. The second time I got a peanut butter, honey, and banana crepe, which was just as delicious.

I don't know how much I can say to get you to go here. I mean, it's a crepe. Not much you can say about it. But I can say it was delicious times a million, and I'm dying to go back here. And the prices aren't that bad as long as you stick to the simpler crepes. 

PS. I wanted to try the savory crepes, but didn't get a chance to :(

I love this place!! So conveniently located near campus!!

I usually get the King Lias with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. It's a dessert crepe that consists of some of my favorite things in a crepe (nutella, coconut, almonds, and bananas)! Because it's pretty fattening, I only get this when I want to reward myself for finishing a paper or big school assignment... It can get difficult to eat so be sure to grab a spoon if you're eating it on the go... or sit down inside (very limited seating inside) and eat it on a plate!

Perfect for the sweet tooth, if you have one.

--------
Food: Out of four possible stars: two stars.

Most people associate Crepes A-Go Go with the sweet crepes with nutella. For those of you who enjoy sweet food, my friends rave about their sweet crepes, so by all means, go get one (or more).

I am a fan of savory foods, and their selection of savory crepes is not as impressive as the fruit-and-nutella crepes. That being said, I really enjoyed their turkey egg and spinach crepes. That flavor combination really hits a spot, and to be able to eat that huge crepes on the go just adds to the enjoyment. 

--------
Miscellaneous: Out of one possible star: one star.

A very convenient location for those rushing for a quick bite on the go while rushing to class. I've had to deal with oil and sauce dripping onto my shirt, but that is really my own fault, isn't it?

The chocolate and banana crepes here are amazing. Made fast, hot, delicious.

These guys really got the idea of LOCATION LOCATION LOCATION down. Perfect place to grab a bite before walking the 'graph. 

They cook right in front of you, so you know what you are getting. Fresh and awesome.

the crepes here are pretty good, or it was pretty good, until we found a fly in our apple crepe. the service was decent. they made us another crepe, but after seeing the fly, we didnt want to eat it anymore. this place is very small so counter seating is very limited when they're busy.

I really love Crepes A-Go Go because of their soft, warm, and delicious crepes filled with sweet nutella. I've only ever gotten the sweet crepes so I can't say much for the savory crepes, but I like the strawberry and nutella crepe and also the butter sugar crepe. The butter sugar is a nice small crepe you can get to satisfy your sweet tooth.

I think Genki Crepe definitely has more variety in toppings and fillings which makes it a great crepe place. (I'd give Genki Crepe 5 stars as well)

First off, this place is FILTHY.  They seriously need to replace the filthy wood/laminate countertops at the front of the place with the same stainless steel counters they've installed in the back of the restaurant.  Secondly, the area around the cash register is disgusting -- the place you buy your food is within a few inches of where they keep the garbage they've bussed from the counters.  And the whole area is grimy.

Now, for the really disgusting part (and, yes, I've just reported it to the city dept. of environmental health.)  The person who handled my cash then went to the front of the restaurant to assist the cook.  Straight to the front:  NO HAND WASHING.  I watched him use his fingers to help arrange the fillings into the crepe.  GROSS!!

I was with my son, or I would have made a scene then and there.  But, I am spreading the word, and I did file a formal complaint with the City ofBerkeley, which was very easy to contact, and seemed to take the matter very seriously.

Totally unexpected, but: best drip coffee in Berkeley. Granted -- Berkeley, here, so standards are really not that high, but what!? It's a crepes place! So we're gonna start this review out with five stars.

The sweet crepes are pretty good though nothing unusually fantastic; the butter and sugar crepes are actually pretty unimpressive, so minus a star. Nutella's fantastic, though; do it. It's way too small to be a comfortable hangout place, so minus a star, but it's a good place to grab breakfast or brunch, especially because um hello coffee.

I felt silly getting butter and sugar on a whole wheat crepe, but hey, they didn't judge. It's great that they hand them to you to walk & eat, too.

I had forgotten how great Crepes A Go Go was. I just recently went back, and let me say, it was just as good as I remember it being the last time I went! This time, instead of searching for parking, I decided to park at the garage on Durant. It was quite convenient, and takes you straight to Telegraph. Another plus for this place is that they validate your parking, so you pay half of what you would normally pay. 

I don't come in here for anything other than a dessert crepe. I come in here to satisfy my sweet tooth. Their strawberries & nutella crepe with whipped cream is heaven on earth. You really can't go wrong with that one. The crepes are a pretty large size, so I wouldn't suggest eating lunch before paying them a visit if you want to finish your crepe and get your money's worth. 

They are pretty expensive. I think the regular price runs upwards of $7. I paid about $5.50 due to the 15% off promotion they've got going right now, which is a steal, so get in there while it lasts! 

Let's just say if I lived in Berkeley, half my body mass would be made up of crepes.

This is the place I first tried my very first crepe.. back in 03' or 04'.. I can't really remember BUT the crepes here are hella good. I've tried other crepe places and nothing will ever compare to Crepes A-Go Go. NOTHING. Anyway...

I tried ones with nutella, fruits, etc but what really puts a smile to my face is the sugar n butter crepes here. I think I just died and gone to heart attack heaven.. bahaha. JK.

The crepes here are pretty cheap too! Under $5! and the workers are friendly :) An absolute must if you're in the Berkeley area...

ive been a longtime fan of crepes but never ventured to try a savory crepe. but i finally did and it was amazing! 

try the cheddar, avocado and tomato or the spinach, jack and tomato. they load it up with whatever you choose to put in your crepe so its well worth the $5.

Honestly, I have no idea how in the hell this place receives as much credit as it does. It is such a shame that people are so blind-sighted by the 5 and 4 star reviews and bottles of nutella to actually see just how nasty it is to just walk into the place. It's truly sad to think that so many people walk into this place to eat. I don't know what to say really; I feel sorry for you all. So I have gone up and down the reviews for this place and noticed how one guy actually realized how discusting it truly is in there. But as so many people here love to do, let me paint the image of my experience at Crepes A-Doo-Doo.

So I've heard a lot about this place from friends and family. Of course everything led me to think that this was the one place I just had to go to. Well let me just say, I regret this decision with a passion. 

So I walk in, busy, to be expected for such a renowned place. I notice the loads of garbage on the counters walking in, no surprise there. I didn't pay much attention to it. 

I noticed banana peals behind the grills they use to make the crepes. Whatever. 

A mess just all around where they cook.

I see that the fans over the grills themselves are completely covered in dust and it all just floats down onto the counter. It's all good. What harm can it do. 

I caught a glimpse of a black dot falling on the crepe they were making. Probably from the filter-less fans. Not my crepe, why should I worry right? The guy making it just throws more cheese on it and problem solved. 

Dirty as crap mirrors. 

French posters trying to give off a classy feel in a poorly established hole in the wall cafe. 

And finally my turn to order. 

Now, Im guessing this lady is the owner of the place considering how she took my order with the fakest smile in the world. But poor lady. She must be doing pretty bad if she has to stand over that counter. I wonder why...

So I took my card and said "thanks." Didn't really seem like someone I would have a conversation with. So rather than talk to her I thought I'd start a conversation with the cooks, having seen what I had already. 

When I asked if they had been busy, it seemed weird how he looked over to see if the lady who had taken my order was gone in order to answer. lol. Slavedriver? Perhaps.

 I then asked if I could have my crepe made a certain way and away from a certain grill and he was nice enough to agree to do it. Good to know they use their hands to make the food. Especially when they keep touching their face. But if that IS the only way to make a crepe then so be it.

 I got my nice and burt crepe, which, wasn't as bad as the thought floating around my head at that point about what was in it. And I loved the way the cooks looked at me as I took the first bite. As if they just couldn't wait.. I didn't want to think about it so I threw it away inside the cafe itself and left. 

I must say, the customer service wasn't bad at all. The one bite I took wasn't bad. It was neither one which drove me to write a bad review other than the place itself. CLEAN IT!! Live up to your reputation! Have some self respect! JEEZ! 

As for me. Never again. 

People, when you walk in, look around VERY closely. Look around you. Please. For your own sake.

The owner messaged me and told me that the premade crepe was a while back and now they HAVE to make fresh crepes.

Went there today and got an egg and cheese crepe. The chef did make the crepe fresh. It was really yummy and made me smile. LOVE this place.

Crepe? What's a crepe? Oh, what I didn't know pre-Berkeley. This place quickly became one of my favorite staples in Berkeley, but on a recent revisit here a few years later, I tried my favorite: the yummy-in-my-tummy strawberry & nutella crepe, and unfortunately my once-wonderful memories of this crepe miracle were crushed.

And all I have to say is: no, no, no! Prices went up--$8 a crepe? Whaaaaat? How can Berkeley students even afford that??! The crepe itself is not very flavorful (this would probably be more ideal for the savory crepes), and, well, besides that you can't really mess up nutella or strawberries. Going to be a little biased here but I can make at least 10 crepes better and for the same price. Goodbye Crepes A Go Go... may you part in peace...

SCENE: Ada T. returns to her apartment and her loving roommate, Jen N. 

JEN N.: Oh, where did you end up going?
ADA T.: Crepes A-Go Go
JEN N.: Cool; what'd you get?
ADA T.: Um, just a plain nutella crepe. It was, like, $5. 
JEN N.: Wow. Was it good?
ADA T.: Um....no, not really. 

Crepes A-Go Go is pricey, and not really that good. I can forgive the price because it is quite a large crepe, but the crepe itself just sucked. It was chewy and gummy. The Nutella was tasty, but I don't think Crepes A-Go Go really contributed to that. Two stars seems a bit low, but, in Yelp's own words: "Meh. I've experienced better." [from my own kitchen]

If I owned Crepes A Go Go, I would hire someone to walk around Telegraph eating a crepe during lunch time.  This is what lured me into the place.  More than two years ago, I saw someone eating a meal crepe for lunch on the street and thought this was an interesting concept.  In the past, I had only tried desert crepes.  I ordered the house special, lots of cheese, turkey, and eggs.  It was good and quick.  I still grab that crepe occasionally when I'm in Berkeley.

Quick and easy food stop if you're needing to eat and walk, however, Crepes-A-Go Go used to make each crepe as you ordered it, resulting in a nice crispy crepe enveloping a lovely, warm filling.  Not so anymore - they have switched to making their crepes ahead of time, merely warming up the pre-made crepe with your choice of filling.  (Tip:  Be careful when you're ordering anything with tomato in it, as the tomato releases a lot of water and you end up with a mushy crepe about halfway through.)

On the up side, they take credit cards here if you're like me and forget to carry cash with you.

Someone described these as an American bastardization of a crepe.  So what?  I used to live in France, and look back with fond memories on the days I spent waiting as the guy on the street corner made a fresh crepe for me and filled it with ham and cheese.  Oh man, so good.  

But who the hell expects an authentic French experience at a place called Crepes A Go-Go?  Seriously?  These crepes are delicious for what they are, which is a more often than not premade crepe, heated and stuffed with pretty much whatever you want.  I usually pick fresh strawberries, powdered sugar, and whipped cream...oh mama!

Okay so this place is a little cramped so if you want to sit somewhere to eat, don't do it here. People will be knocking into you while they order. The crepes are good to go and MAN are they good. The nutella w/ strawberries and banana is absolutely heavenly...better than sex (maybe). GO HERE IF YOU HAVE THE MUNCHIES!!

This place is amazing. I never knew you could do so much with Crepes. When we first walked in I saw nutella and immediately knew that it was destiny. Two of my favorite things combined, with strawberries too? I was in heaven!
My Mom got a spinach and feta type thing, which was maybe 1% less amazing than the strawberry and nutella crepe. I think if I ever get a chance to go back, I'm gonna get a savory crepe as the my meal, and a strawberry nutella crepe as my dessert.
I cannot say enough good things about this place. If you ever find yourself in the beautiful city of Berkeley, head over to Crepes A-Go Go ASAP.

You can't really get your sweet and savory crepes to go anywhere else other than perhaps a couple other dessert shops in this city. There are no tables here, just a bunch of stools over the counter and a bit of standing room. The biggest appeal of this place is that the crepes are made fast. They're great snacks for those on the go and maybe even a very light meal. Just be careful of that powdered sugar on dark clothing.
I'm a fan of the crepe but not of the prices.  My friend and I split a sweet crepe with chocolate and strawberries.  Perfect combination for a sweet snack!

Can I get something filling?
Running out of time!
Eat it morning, noon, and night
Purchased a savory cheese and spinach
Enough for 2 people
Satisfied for the next 6 hours

Having pre-made crepes really ruins it for me here.  You can tell that the crepe is pre-made while you're eating it.  It just doesn't have that freshly made crepe taste and texture.  I'd wait the extra 2 minutes it would take to get a freshly made crepe instead of getting an old reheated crepe.  This was a total disappointment.  They just have a pile of 20 crepes on the table that gets reheated and filled.  Isn't that how McDonald's prepares their menu items?

A good crepe selection doesn't make up for the stale tasting crepe.  Boo on them for trying to shortcut.

Imagine a generous spread of nutella, topped with plump and juicy strawberries, all wrapped up in a freshly made crepe. This is my usual order from crepe a go go. I know I know, lucky me.
The crepes themselves are huge, and are around $6-$8 each. There are both sweet and savory options to choose from, or you could always be creative and make up your own. The workers are always friendly, and they've been working here for so long that they get the shape and thickness of the crepes just right. 
The place can get pretty packed at times, with students getting a bite to eat in between classes. Understandably too, as these crepes can really fill you up, and is perfect on the run. Just let them know, they'll wrap it tightly in foil and voilà, you have a tasty and convenient crepe to go.

I had never had a savory crepe before. In fact, I've only ever had one crepe prior to this in my lifetime and it had nutella. But I digress. I had a savory crepe with marinated chicken and onions, peppers, and tomatoes and with pepper jack cheese. It was really good but could stand to have less "juice" as it made the crepe a little too soggy and messy to eat. The taste was yummy although I think I emptied the bottle of tobasco on it. And speaking of the tobasco bottle, it was so grody corrody. All kinds of nastyness. I had to clean it before I used it and even then I was a little afraid. Surely no common organisms can live in tobasco, right? Except me, I could live in a giant vat of tobasco anyday. But yeah. They need more space (it'll never happen) to be comfortable. The guy shorted me a dime in change-- he either gave me two nickels and thought he would trick me into thinking they were dimes (he owed me $0.20) or he made an honest mistake and grabbed nickels instead of dimes. Who knows, he was pretty apologetic so no biggie. I'd really like to come back for a nutella+strawberry+whipped cream.... dreamy....

I ordered the house special (soup and a half sandwich). I thought both were really tasty.  The soup was a little bland, but for $10, it seemed like a nice lunch.  The portions were large enough for me and I thought the ambiance was lovely.  I like the communal table, the long bench seating along the wall and the fireplace.

I'm glad that it's close by for those rainy days when I want some pho.

I had a late lunch here the other day- came at around 2:30- and my boss and I were the only two customers in the restaurant. The service was phenomenal, and the food was even better! I had the lychee slushee, the vegetarian half pho-half banh mi plate, the sweet corn rice pudding, and an iced Vietnamese coffee. The boss was paying, obviously :)
The slushee was outstanding, and it alone would bring me back. Vegetarian pho was good- it was actually the first time I've had pho, so I've nothing to compare it to, but it was a tasty noodle soup! The vegetarian banh mi was better than the soup, in my opinion- edamame and tofu fritters with spicy slaw and mayo on a perfect baguette! The sweet corn rice pudding was also very good, but I was too full to enjoy it completely... The coffee was necessary after all of that food and was excellent. The owner built this place herself, and her interior and furniture design abilities really shine! Extra points for a sweet roll-up door that opens the whole bar area to the outdoors.

I've been curious about this place for a while, especially since there are a number of vegetarian options. We went at a low peak time (summer, around 3:30pm) and shared fries (piping hot with a yummy dip), the vegetarian spring rolls (nothing too notable; I think I could make better ones, though the dipping sauce was tasty) and, after studying awhile to the background music (which wasn't great, but wasn't too annoying either) ordered the combination vegetarian ph and bánh mì. It was nice to have ph that was actually vegetarian, though the broth was a bit bland and as much as I love daikon, some more interesting additions would have justified the high price tag ($11 before tax) more. I wasn't a big fan of the edamame and tofu mush that comprised the protein of the bánh mì--next time I'd just grab a tofu sandwich from Le Petit Cheval or Saigon Express, for half the price. The free jasmine tea was fragrant and strong, and the DIY basil/jalapeno/lime station was a thoughtful touch. $24 could definitely buy better quality and greater quantity food in Berkeley, though I might be tempted back here by the fries ($5 a serving seems a bit pricey, but using the space on a quiet afternoon to study might justify the cost).

Okay, this is not your average pho. Which is to say, it's not *that* authentic. And that's okay. Because it's still really damn good. I ordered the basic, regular pho. I also slightly regretted that decision as I saw food being brought to other patrons. The noodle dishes looked great, as did the banh mi. 

The broth didn't taste like your regular pho broth -- if anything it reminded me of the organic broth I've brought from Whole Foods. Super fresh and not too salty, but damn, that is not what I usually expect with pho. The beef was perfectly thinly sliced, the broth was great, and there was a small little add-on bar, so you could pick the amount of jalapeños, etc that you wanted. Only complaint would be that the noodles were a little soggy, but honestly, I've had so much worse at places that claimed authenticity.

This is a California twist on Vietnamese food. Not that big of a twist, but enough of one to throw some of the reviewers, I've noticed. I love authentic stuff, but if I want it, I know to go into Oakland or San Jose. This place is good and I will be patronizing it again. Regular sized pho costs $8, large costs $10. Cheap enough while retaining quality. I should also add that the restaurant is very clean, and has a nice atmosphere going for it.

I went here and got the "Custom" pho.  They didn't have any tripe at the time.  Had the meatballs, tendon and rare sirloin.  Those choices were fine.  I had a problem with the soup/broth.  It didn't exactly taste salty, but there was a strange taste that was hard to pinpoint.  Maybe it was a little metallic or some other kind of chemical.  Every other pho restaurant that I've been to in the bay area has a good soup to place the rest of the ingredients in.  This place was different.  The person who I was with also made the same comment.  

They had also got my order wrong.  I ordered an extra large soup but they brought me a large.  The waiter offered to let me eat the large while they went and got another order, but I just said to bring me an extra large and I'll wait.  He did, but had only brought one plate of the bean sprouts/basi/peppers/and some other vegetable that I couldn't place.  Other diners had gotten one plate of veggies per pho order.  We had to share.  Also, I had to ask for refills of my diet coke since it wasn't offered.  

The extra large was $10 which I consider pretty high for pho and it was mostly the gross soup.  Maybe it's because it's a relatively new place, but I think they need to work on their service and definitely their soup before I'll go back.
I find the broth bland and the noodles a little overcooked.  Also the broth temperature is a little too lukewarm for me.

I can't decide whether this place is fancy or not. You pay beforehand, yet there is a bar and fireplace in one wing and wait service while you eat. It's a weird mixture of self-serve and what seems to appear as fine dining. The actual food was okay. I got the house pho for ~$7. The soup was a bit too salty and oily for my taste, but it was a filling meal without being too heavy. Unlike typical pho places where the meat is cut thinly and placed on top of the noodles for you to stir into the soup for further cooking, the meat in this pho was all at the bottom of the bowl unbeknownst to me so I basically ate it separately at the end--they give a good number of slices, though. The sandwiches looked good but are relatively expensive for ~$6-7. Most Vietnamese sandwiches that I'm used to are 3 bucks. The Pho Bar may benefit from being the only banh mi place near campus. Overall, it was a satisfactory meal, but nothing spectacular. I'm curious to see how they will do once official school starts again in the fall. As a side note, I like how they use cloth napkins for eco-friendliness.

Best Banh Mi (granted, this is compared to Saigon Express and Camille's) I've had in Berkeley, the basil & sea salt fries are fantastic, and the atmosphere and service are great.

I'd give a higher rating on the banh mi alone, but I've only had one menu item, and I think I should at least have their signature item before rating it 4 star or more.

Have had two kinds of banh mi (classic & grilled pork), the pho, the fries, and the sour plum soda, which is *fantastically* refreshing. Definitely, a fantastic place.

I'd go more often if it weren't for so pricey!

It could be a fun joint, but right now the Pho Bar has no clear identity and the food is bland. 

I feel like I could like  the vibe and overall atmosphere  of the restaurant. There is a bar at the front and the dining room is open and comfortable. The problem though is that the restaurant is usually empty making the the mood seem gloomy and the kitchen is surprisingly noisy. 

Both the Bahn Mi sandiwiches and the Pho are not particularly cheap. I tried the pho once and it was surprisingly skimpy on the meat and it had possibly the blandest broth I have ever tried. No amount of hoisin and hot sauce could save it. 

I was also tempted by their happy hour appetizer platter once, but it was disappointing.

Despite serving beer and wine, it closes at 9pm. If the restaurant did not close so early and served better food it could be a cool hangout place for after-work happy hours on Thursday evenings.

The decor and vibe are great. Upscale, trendy which was pretty nice. Unfortunately I can't say the same thing for the noodles.

From reading the other reviews they may use fresh, organic products but it still doesn't take away from the fact that it just wasn't good. I can enjoy a twist on a traditional taste, but when the product is bland and has no hint of the original flavor you haven't succeeded.  I got the house (beef) pho and Vietnamese coffee. The quality of the ingredients was there with lean cuts of beef and fresh noodles (though the basil leaves weren't looking so hot), but it tasted like roast beef in beef stock. I had to keep adding sriracha, hoisin, and chili sauce to get some flavor. It honestly seemed like something I could have made at home. The coffee was pretty weak too and overall just okay. 

Add this all up with the fact that it's about 50% more expensive then your typical pho place I just don't see myself going back. Pho isn't something I eat everyday, and it probably isn't the healthiest thing either but I love the processed noodles, fatty cuts of meat, and soup loaded with MSG.

I didn't like this place because of its food. The pho had no taste..especially the soup. And that ruined the meal for me. Never coming back here for pho. It was a huge disappoint me especially because from the outside this looked like a pretty good restaurant. 

I also ordered the spring rolls. Was not a huge fan of that either... Had much better spring rolls at other pho restaurants.. 

The sandwiches were okay though so if I do come back, that's what I'll be ordering. But I still like Lee's sandwiches a lot more.   

Ambience is okay too but I would much rather eat at La Val's than The Pho Bar for authentic good-tasting food.

The Pho is okay, the vermicelli noodles are great, the prices are too high. Vietnamese coffee here is fantastic though. I come in when I have a craving for Vietnamese because it's close to campus, but I wish the prices were a little bit cheaper.

This is a review for the boba.  I had a craving for boba and was getting pizza at La Val's so thought I would give "The Pho Bar" a try.  Don't bother - it's not worth the $5 since it's mostly ice. It's basically weak ice tea (ice) with a little milk (non-fat?) and fresh boba.  The boba/tea was so hot it melted the bottom of my cup! Then the ice made the tapioca too hard and cold in a matter of minutes.  You are much better walking across campus to Bancroft.  Maybe the pho is better, but after such bad boba, I wonder about the taste of the chef/owners.
