Now that winter's coming I'm glad there's a decent pho place by campus I can go to for a quick, hot lunch. The service is generally good and friendly and the setting is nice. I love the long reclaimed wood tables. 

I like the pho. I live in Oakland so I have a better pho place I usually go to, but when I'm at school and want some pho I'll happily head over to the pho bar. I'm not picky or elitist about my pho. The pho here is not quite like standard pho, but it's still good and satisfying enough. The meat is always plentiful, though sometimes I get more meat than noodles. The grilled pork sandwiches I've had are good and have great flavor, just like my mom's marinated pork. And the bread is fresh and just the right kind of crunchy. 

To someone who has grown up on good San Jose pho and Vietnamese home cooking, this place is satisfying enough. If you're an elitist pho person though, which most people are, then just don't bother.

i am an infrequent poster on yelp, but after my phenomenal experience at the pho bar, a vietnamese noodle bar which recently opened on euclid ave, near the uc berkeley campus, i decided this one was worth the time to write.

first of all, the place is gorgeous -- the kind of clean, warm and elegant space that makes you want to hang out for a long time.  in the front of the restaurant, there's a long and spacious bar area, where you can order refreshing and unusual drinks like mint tamarinade, salted plum spritzer,  or an assortment of mostly local brews, including a not-so-local japanese ale.  before getting seated, i tried the mint tamarinade with basil seeds.  it was like having a fancy minty, not-too-sweet alcoholic beverage without the alcohol.  the seeds added a unique slippery texture which seemed to create an even more pleasurable culinary experience, though the enhancement in terms of flavor was subtle.  a friend ordered the japanese wheat beer, so i got to try that as well --- i'm typically agnostic about wheat beers, but this one was quite bright and delicious. very special.

in the back and larger section of the restaurant are several tables, some that are long and share-able, and others are more intimate. the open space arrangement allows the buzz and hum of happy eating sounds and conversations to flow throughout but not make you feel crowded while eating.

now onto the food... the menu is both simple and complex, offering both traditional and less conventional items, including vegan and gluten-free, to keep things interesting.  given that the pho bar is a noodle bar, i ordered the "house" pho along with the spring rolls (deep fried) appetizer to start. the rolls were served with mint sprigs and lettuce and fish sauce for dipping.  even though they were of the fried sort (rather than the fresh rolls), the filling -- pork and shrimp, i think -- somehow maintained a mild and almost delicate texture and taste.  as for the pho, the msg-free broth presented a startling perfect meld of all the flavors that make pho such an incredible meal.  i have no idea how the pho bar does it, but the authentic and rich flavors make apparent how much care is put into its making. the noodles themselves had clearly been prepared with comparable precision.  before we left, we tried a couple of the desserts -- banana tapioca pudding and the sweet corn rice pudding.  they are both winners and impossible to do justice in trying to describe here.  oh, i almost forgot to mention - the prices at the pho bar for the quality of the meal and overall food experience is more than reasonable. 

i swear i still dream about this place and plan to go back again and again!

The decoration is pretty good. But the noodle soup is very plain. 
I ordered a meatball pho. It tastes like wonton soup, plain and sweet(for pho?). Meatball is not "bouncing", and tastes like it's bought from 99 ranch.

Good thing is it's close to north gate. Easy access for engineering students who are craving for pho.

Ohhh I miss huong tra

I got the broken rice plate ($11), girlfriend got the pho. People weren't kidding when they said the portions were small. When the food arrived, there was only one pork chop, a small fried egg, and not even a full scoop of rice. The "vegetables" consisted of 5 thin cucumber slices and a slice of tomato that wasn't even ripe. Aside from my unsatisfied stomach, what made the meal worse was knowing that I was sitting across from a pizza joint wherein my 11 dollars could have been spent on a medium pizza. The pho was decent, but nothing you can't get at any other pho place. Don't come here on an empty stomach.

got  "The Works".  no tripe in sight.  some small slivers of tendon.  there was plenty of other meat, but still, the food did not match the description, so that is a lost star for me.  otherwise it was pretty good.  it wasn't the tastiest broth, but still good, and considering that they don't use MSG and try to use natural and organic ingredients. I think it's a nice change from the typical MSG pho house.  

however this isn't the first place i've tried that does "organic" and non-MSG pho (see Pho Appetit in Newark, CA).  it is more expensive too, and that is the reason I took off another star .  the food is good, but not good enough to be a good value.

i suppose i could give a 0.5 or 1 star for the friendly staff and interesting ambiance, but people don't normally go to a pho place for ambiance.  it looks like this place isn't looking to be your typical pho place though, and could be a nice place to actually meet your friends, so i'll have to come back and try some of the other things on the menu

The place is super new, and looks much more classy than your average pho restaurant. One of the few new restaurants on Northside, bringing more options tot he students.  

The works, a x-large pho bowl with all the meats, is definitely huge. Compared to the normal side by side, it is almost 1.5 times bigger. I recommend getting the x-large, only if you are starving.

The pho does NOT have MSG. Seems like lots of people are complaining about bad tasting pho, but maybe they don't realize how much better pho tastes with MSG. The meat is kind of bland especially the meatballs. 

TL;DR; The pho does not have MSG. It won't taste like the pho you are used to. Only thing that I don't like about the pho are the bland meatballs, but the other meats are okay.

I came prejudiced because of the average 3 star rating this place got on Yelp. My son inlaw suggested we meet there (August 16th, the day after we got back from our summer forays). I read yelp, of course, and just wanted to find another place.  My husband convinced me to go along with it, so I resigned myself to it.

Am I glad I did!  The real secret winners at this place, which shares a nice outdoor place that was convenient for the 2 yr old to run around in, were the noodle salads. John had the shrimp, I had the beef.  Incredible!  Such a rich savory explosion of flavors and textures!  John's  shrimp salad was equally good. While I like pho, I'm not an aficionado,  so I never sampled theirs, but asked someone who did while I was there, and they loved it. 

I also had some spring rolls for hors d'ouvres -- quite nice!  and the lychee slush was fanastic!  Never had anything like it before and the refreshing mix of textures and flavors were perfect.  

The menu looks like it is expanding well beyond pho, and  I noticed that they have other items slated to be added in September that sounded interesting, so, yeah, I'd definitely go there again, the next time I have a chance.

Go Pho-bar!

Argh, I don't know why I keep coming here. Maybe I hope that it will keep getting better but instead it's just getting worse! 

So I ordered the $6 classic sandwich that was so awesome the first time I had it. This time it was not even as good as the $3 one from Saigon express! Only three thin slices of meat and WAY too much pickled carrots - so much that some of the brine dripped out of my sandwich, it was all I could taste! 

I also ordered the banana tapioca to go. For $4 it better be some bad a$$ tapioca - but it was just ... meh ... it was room temp, didn't taste that good, and they had to put it in an oversized drink cup because they didn't think that anyone would order it to go. Later I overheard the manager telling the server that they aren't supposed to give those out to go... O_o That's weird, because that last time I came, another manager said they would just put it in a cup if I wanted it to go... Compared to Saigon express's COLD banana tapioca for $1.75 ... totally disappointed. 

Sorry, pho bar, I tried to hard so hard to like you, but I'm not coming back nor am I recommending it.

I actually wanted to give them 2.5 stars if I could.... but I am being nice and giving them 3 stars.

I must say I am particularly dissatisfied because all of my unsatisfactory experiences came from delivery/pick-ups. My experiences at the restaurant were fine. Great atmosphere, spacious, and the food was good too. 

One time I got their pho delivered to my place. I know that a lot of people don't like the pho because it is, well, different. But I like the fact that they never use MSG.  Anyways, I was really disappointed to find out that they forgot to put meat under the noodle (usually, in their "tiffins" there is a good portion of cooked meat under the noodle, and there is also a thin slice of uncooked meat on the top of the noodle) - meaning that I got only a thin slice of uncooked meat. For me, that was just unacceptable for $8 + tax + tip. 

Also, I used to really really like their summer rolls (not fried, but rolled in rice papers). They are shrimp, pork, rice vermicelli, bean sprouts, lettuce, and leeks rolled in rice paper. Even the peanut dipping sauce is delicious.  I've had them at least  four times. Particularly because my first two experiences with them were so good. The third time, I ordered them for either delivery or pick-up, and they were disappointing. It was pretty obvious they were half the size they used to be. Couldn't believe I paid $5 +tax +tip for two tiny rolls. The fourth time, again, delivered, was just unbelievable. The size was definitely bigger, but most of it was filled with rice vermicelli and lettuce. Two small pieces of shrimp in each one, and no pork. I don't know if they ran out of pork or something, but that definitely did not make me happy, especially since they didn't explain/apologize why my rolls were so poorly made.   

On two occasions, they forgot to bring me sriracha or hoisin or peanut sauce. Small mistakes, but still, disappointing. 

I guess I am just offended because if such occurrences had happened at the restaurant, I could have complained about it. But when I don't feel like going out, have my food delivered just to find that they forgot the sauce, or made my rolls poorly, it is just annoying. I wish they cared more about people who don't eat at the restaurant and be more attentive to deliveries and pick-ups.

This is a great addition to the neighborhood. The pho and bun are well prepared with quality ingredients. This will definitely be one of our go-to restaurants. Looking forward to trying everything on the menu.

We are so excited to have The Pho Bar open and close by!  No, it's not the authentic East 14th pho restaurants but I kinda see that as a good thing.  Their veggies are fresh and the meat actually tastes like meat.  I'm happy to pay more for food that tastes like real food.  

I am in love with the tofu vermecelli salad and their mint tamarinade.  A perfect combo!  

They're just starting their take-out with metal containers.  While it's more work, I'd much rather use cool containers that don't end up in the landfill.  Good for them for doing this!

My kids loved it too.  We will definitely make this place a regular stop.

I really liked the concept and the decor.
That said, I think the pho should have more flavor and less salt. The broth itself lacked a certain aromatic quality to it, making the dish palatable, yet still a bit lackluster.

The Pho Bar is nice addition to the eats available near North Gate.  I had the Lemongrass Beef Noodle Salad which was a bit overpriced, but delicious.  The Vietnamese ice coffee is also quite yummy.  I was very happy with the food, the service, atmosphere and location.

It is unfortunate that its web site is not user friendly - the menu is not current on the site and it's random and clunky.  

I will happily return to try more items on its menu.

I thought the pho was absolutely delicious. Maybe the broth varies from batch to batch, but mine was so flavorful and not oily at all. I also had the banh mi, equally tasty. 
Who cares who is working in the kitchen, as long as the food tastes good that's all that matters to me. Awesome location, and tastefully decorated. Didn't get a chance to try their drinks but they look yummy! Very friendly service. Look forward to going back.

Nothing really wrong with the food, but nothing that really stands out either. The main problem is that they are just too pricey for their portions, quality, and location. $10 for a medium-sized bowl of pho or sandwich? How do you charge that much across the street from the Asian Ghetto where I can get a lunch for $5? I'l go there every once in a long while when I'm craving pho and willing to drop some $ for lunch, but not anywhere near as often as I hit the other restaurants on north side. I see them probably going under like so many other restaurants on Euclid. It was a good experiment. Pho is needed on north side, but it needs to be better and cost less if you want to compete with all the other restaurants there.

Update: I went here late one night to order some pho for take out. Apparently, they can only do take out if you order online. If you come to the restaurant to order take out, they just plain will not take your money. You'd think if you were going to pay $10 for a bowl of pho they would be bending over backwards to sell it to you.

For some reason, I go here a lot even though pho isn't so great.. the soup is just.. salty and brown. Nothing stands out. I think i just like the clean atmosphere and the fact this place gives you fresh towels before you sit down, which is unheard of in Vietnamese restaurants. Anyways, back to pho. Pho comes in two sizes: regular ($9) or X-Large ($10). I suggest you get the latter tho. The sizes of the bowls are reallyyyyyyy different. Regular ain't regular; it's puny, small. One dollar  difference REALLY makes a difference. Summer rolls are skinny and passable. My friend got the Vietnamese sandwich and she was generous enough to give me a bite, and it was pretty good. Gonna try that next time!

We've now ordered 3 or 4 times online, and when you are done, it says a specific time that the order will be ready (say, 6:58, or 8:40). This is the 3rd time that it hasn't been ready when we arrived and we've waited 10+ minutes.

Stopped in here tonight on the way home and found it to be really nice. Great banh mi, spicy sriracha wings, wonderful atmosphere -- especially considering they've been open less than a week. Looking forward to coming back here often to see how this place evolves, but so far, it's a welcome addition to the neighborhood.

I visited again a few days ago, and to my surprise, the soup got so much better. It doesn't taste as bland as before!!
However, the vermicelli was still EHHH.
Stick to the phos, and it will be a pretty good experience.
fresh ingredients and nice broth :)

however, still pricey

This place is kind of a conundrum. They have pho, which is supposed to be a hole in the wall common denominator kind of thing, but this place tries to make it swank which is fine, but in doing so it results in them charging $10 for a bowl of pho which is kind of ridiculous. It's decent pho but nothing I would rave about, but then again I'm not vietnamese. I'm not sure if I like how trendy they're trying to be or I'm put off by it's almost transparent attempt to be trendy for the sake of being trendy. if it were only cheaper.

Had lunch at The Pho Bar yesterday with my husband, the Vietnam vet. It was a terrific experience and delicious meal! 

From the moment we stepped through the door into the bar, to be welcomed by Brice, the extremely helpful and knowledgeable bartender, til we left full and happy an hour and a half later, we felt welcomed and well cared for.

We sampled the combo, the fabulous fries, the spring rolls, and the corn/rice dessert. My husband had a contented smile on his face the entire time. The broth in pho is as varied as personal taste - we found The Pho Bar's broth to be very flavorful and loved the fresh herbs and sprouts garnish.

I love banh mi but often struggle with stiff bread - The Pho Bar's sandwich was perfect. The bread was slightly crunchy and soft at the same time, the filling (we tried both the classic (ham and pate) and the grilled pork) was a great combination of meat and vegetables, and just right amount (none of that meat oozing out of a too full sandwich thing).

The spring rolls  - loved the flavors and the combination - I could drink that fish sauce!

The look and feel of The Pho Bar is truly warm and welcoming - or as my husband prefers to say - 'AWESOME". It is a beautiful place, you can tell a great deal of thought and love and design has gone into creating The Pho Bar.

The staff are friendly, eager to please, and clearly happy to be part of this cool new spot. We can't wait to go back.

The Pho Bar is a work in progress.  I couldn't find any comment cards, so I'm going to treat this review as hopefully constructive for the owners.

First of all, the ambiance is great...what a welcome addition to the north side to have such a well-decorated comfortable establishment.  The staff member we interacted with was also very friendly.

I ordered the lemongrass beef bun.  I actually thought the flavor was quite good.  Little bit skimpy on the meat, but a huge portion of everything else.  The sauce had a nice lemongrass/garlic flavor.  One thing was quite off-putting though--the menu outside listed the price as $9, but when I ordered it seems the price has gone up to $10 on the inside menu. Well, that's just more than I can justify for lunch.  Recommendation number 1 is to think about the lunch crowd and add some more lunch-priced options and sizes.   

Sam M. was with me and ordered the tofu bahn mi...I couldn't get any feedback from him other than it was "just fine."  Sounds like it was not very impressive  and not bad.  It looked a bit small to my eye, but at $6 is a reasonable lunch size price.  Recommendation #2 is to add some more vegetarian items to the menu.  A tofu sandwich is not sufficient...hello, this is Berkeley!  

In any case, the food was average to slightly above average, but it's just not appropriately priced/sized for lunch.  Given that I'm mostly around here at lunch, I don't think I'll be back for these menu options.  Given the large size of this restaurant and lots of pretty good north side competition, I hope the owners aggressively respond to feedback from their customers.

It's really a pho bar with a few great beers on tap, respectable music selection that fits right in the campus demands for its North Berkeley location. 

I was on a roll and needed to drop off a few books at the UCB Library main stacks. Problem is, that free parking spot is only a one hour slot and I'm nursing PF on my right heel. I pull in at exactly 3:00pm in the front spot -- nice. I drop off Fortescue's History of the British Army vol 4 from 1906. I'm looking for another classic and I put the squeeze on poor soul on the other end -- oops. Oh well I move eight stacks and find a 1915 copy of Pollyanna. Back up to the desk at "Floor A," check it out, head across the lawn and I'm back at the car at 3:32. I drop of the books and stroll up Euclid thinkin I might grab a little sumptin, sumptin...

Halfway up there's The Pho Bar. "Hey, is there any such thing as a small bowl of pho?" I ask as I eye the beer handles.

"Yes sir, we got a kid's bowl." 

"Sweet, I'll have a pho tai, a pint of amber and a cafe sua da..."

The ingredients are organic-ish including the beef according to the chalkboard. By the time the pho arrived I was well into the pint and the coffee was drippin away. The small bowl was the right size for a soup appetizer and could fill in that midafternoon-skipped-lunch-gotta-cook dinner-slot nicely. Take a breather from the slurping and stir the milk syrup with my chopstick and drop the ice in dere...

Finish the bowl of pho, swig the last gulp of ale and slurp down the iced caffeine dose. The check and tab are paid, nice tip, and I slip back down the car jaywalking in front of the UC Center for Investigative Journalism. I pull out of my spot between two cement-mixer trucks cranking away and check my phone.  Sweet!   Exactly 4:00pm...

What can you do in an hour?

Food & service are great!  The noodles (bun) are my favorite. Pho and banh mi are also tasty. (I've ate plenty of street food in Viet Nam too)

They just opened and are still sorting out some kinks, but appreciated the feedback we gave them!

Ambiance is good. Really good if you can sit at the bar or front table.

The ambiance of this place is attracting, the employees look very professional, and the menu unique.

I ordered a Regular Sized Custom Pho w/ Rare Sirloin, Brisket, and Tendon(my fav).  And a Pink, a "icy dessert drink" made with: pomegranate tapiocas, yellow beans, jellies, coconut milk all served with shaved ice ( the coconut milk made it unique and very delicious). 

After having eating much good and unfortunately, bad pho, this one is hard to catagorize. 

The broth was flavorful, but was overwhelmingly strong with ginger. Normally, broth has stong flavors of bone it was made from, a taste that seemed to be missing, a flavor that usually distinguishes good pho from bad pho. Most good pho places have a different broth for vegetarians, but I feel it is the same one here for both, but I am not sure. And the rice noodles we nothing special. 

The regular size, is really small by any traditional pho standard, I was far from being full. This is because I normally get a regular and can barely finish it.

The Pho Bar has potential, but I feel they need to be constantly improving/perfecting their pho. The prices are reasonable, which is a plus. I hope the owners read our reviews and change accordingly. 

One things that is annoying is that all the food comes out together, something I would expect form a fast food joint, not a restaurant style bar. Especially, if it is a dessert item, which needs to be eaten right away. 

P.S. The cellphone reception inside is pretty bad and I wish the wi-fi was not password-protected.

I am here for a soft opening, before the official opening this Tuesday, June 21. I am generously giving it a three star, hoping that things will improve and I will change my rating accordingly. Especially since the service was great and atmosphere so welcoming.

There was a time near the beginning of the summer when I was going here everyday, happy that the restaurant had opened, bringing welcome new flavors to Euclid. The food is certainly decent. I usually order the chicken banh mi, which has a good amount of spicy and savory flavors. I'm less impressed with the Pho: the meat tastes good, but there isn't much of it, and overall the broth doesn't do it for me.

My main criticism is that Pho Bar is a bit pricey for the portions that they're offering. There are other restaurants in the vicinity that succeed with the same concept (a fresh, clean, sustainable Vietnamese restaurant) while offering larger portions and lower prices. The space of the restaurant seems too large and the staffing levels too high: maybe this explains the elevated prices.

I like this place and I think the food is good.  It's a great space to go with a large group as there is plenty of seating.  Tonight I really enjoyed the fire.

What makes me unhappy is the automatic $0.25 fee added to all credit card transactions, no minimum.  How is it that establishments like Stuffed Inn and Nefeli don't do this to their customers when charging far less for the average menu item but The Pho Bar does? I would far prefer to see your prices raised than to add some chintzy fee that will be applied even if you spend $20 on dinner.  At this place, $20 for dinner is possible.  To me, this is a customer service problem.

I'm kind of disappointed. Pho Bar looks like it would be good. Whoever decorated the place clearly has taste. But I shouldn't have let the cute decorations excite me. The lack of Vietnamese people working here should have been the first hint that this wouldn't be authentic blow my mind kind of pho.

I ordered the house pho. The beef was tender but everything else in the bowl was just off. The broth had no flavor I don't think i've ever had such a plain broth before. The amount of bean sprouts they give you is pitiful. I had a hard time just trying to finish my order but I tried because hey I spent $8 on my meal it should at least provide me sustenance.

My friend ordered spring rolls and beignets at the same time as me. I was already wrapping up my meal by the time she received hers.

Kind of pricey for not so stellar Vietnamese food. I might go back again to try the banh mi but definitley not for the pho.

This is in no way you can call Pho. I am a Vietnamese and I can guarantee that it is not at all Pho. The broth is tasteless! Worst Pho ever in my life! Looking for Pho near Berkeley? Ranch 99 or Anh Hong (on University and Shattuck) are good places.

I've been there three times, 1) after they first opened, just to test out the water, 2) taking advantage of their "early bird" free boba special, and 3) just because. 

So far, I've tried their pho, the vietnamese sandwich and the free boba. 

The pho was very mediocre to say the least. They touted their "sustainable, no MSG" menu, but all at the cost of greatly compromising the taste. If you want a no-MSG pho, I would suggest  Oriental Restaurant on Shattuck.

The sandwich was average. If you're a meat-lover like me, you'd be disappointed. Sure, I am a Californian, but I'd definitely like my meat Texas-sized. But for a mere $6 plus boba, I guess it's fine. 

Lastly, the boba... it's free, so by definition I can't complain. But If you are thinking about going there just for the rare boba near north Berkeley. All I have to say is... it's worth the walk to southside vendors (i.e. Mochachino). The tea is saturated with sugar, and the tapioca was definitely past its "best use by" hour. 

But what prompted me to write this review was the $0.25 "hidden" surcharge if you use a credit card. The guy working at the counter didn't even bother to tell me that. He just typed in your order, swiped, and say here you go. When I asked about it, he replied, "oh, I should've told you that".

After all the "hidden-fee" scam created by the evil banking industry, I am really fed up with dishonest businesses. Only this time, I got conned by a local business.

TIP: The portion size for the Xtra Large (listed as Large on their website menu) is a REALLY big bowl. See this photo for context: http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZmYIPv4XQQ2bT4dgl6ezzA?select=CGlcFU_8qMLK6Z4qHdOmOg
It's not all broth, either--lots of noodles, a little skimpy on the meat. 

TIP #2: Don't expect to get full off of that Xtra Large bowl, like at all other pho places. There's a lack of sodium in the soup, so you won't feel as satisfied even after finishing the bowl off.

TIP #3: Avoid the banh mi. Not worth it. 

TIP #4: Either sit at the bar, or order at the cashier and sit in the spacious dining room.  

I'm torn, disappointed, and unsatisfied. But the service was good and the food was okay, for what it was. I kind of already knew I would be disappointed, too, after perusing their website, but Urbann Turbann was closed on Saturday so I walked a few steps over to enter The Pho Bar. 

What I mean is, I knew this wouldn't be a regular pho restaurant. They tout that they use "natural meats, without growth hormones or antibiotics. Organic & sustainable products used whenever possible. We do not add MSG, ever!" And when I think about it, when I want a huge steaming bowl of pho, do I really care if it's organic and hormone free? And would I pay a premium for it?

So I avoided the pho. My boyfriend didn't though. He got The Works (tripe is extra). At first, we were impressed by the Xtra Large's hefty size. The broth tasted extremely light--definitely no MSG. Soon, though, the fat from the meat got into the broth, making a thick layer of oily slick. At the end of the meal, after fishing out the last of the noodles, the layer was thick enough to skim off the surface. Not cool. The beef, though, was very tender (probably because of how fatty it was!). 

I ordered the grilled pork banh mi. Don't order this. It was like a snack, not a meal. At $6, I wasn't expecting the ends of the baguette to be cut off (probably so there needed to be less meat inside), or for the sandwich to be so skinny and lukewarm. Granted, the pork was flavorful, but it wasn't juicy and there wasn't a lot of it. The pickled vegetables were okay, but lacking in presence. 

So I'm torn because it tasted okay, we had no problems with the workers and the waitress, but the restaurant was just lacking in a lot of ways. But if you're looking for a healthier version of pho, here it is.

I'm probably giving The Pho Bar a higher rating than how I actually feel about it - but the fun I had with my friends at the staff-training event makes me slightly biased...

Pros:

- Decor is very classy. Some people I know swear by the philosophy that the grimier and more beat-down an Asian restaurant is, the better the food. My germophobia makes me feel otherwise, so the cleanliness and elegant decorations make me happy =) And the long tables in the middle of the restaurant are a nice touch; as my dining mate said, perfect for power lunches! 

- The food presentation is quite beautiful. The "Pink" drink that I ordered was layered in such a gorgeous manner that I didn't want to mess it up.

- Fresh ingredients! One of my common complaints with Asian restaurants is that the quality of ingredients is not the best. The Pho Bar, however, shows even more class by seemingly using fantastic ingredients for all of their food. The steak was tender, the bean sprouts were fresh and crunchy, and the basil was just about right off the plant!

- Good service (and not just because I'm friends with a few of the waiters!) The food came out quickly, we were checked upon often enough for us to register comments, but not enough to be annoying.

Cons:

- High prices for the amount of food that you get. My usual reason for not getting appetizers at restaurants (besides me being a cheap, broke-ass college student) is that there's not enough bang for the buck. The same goes for this place - if I remember correctly, the appetizers were around $5. When the spring rolls came out, I could feel the hearts of the people around me sink...2 rolls between the 5 of us? Blah. Luckily, we got 2 appetizers, so we got to eat more than just 1 bite. Still, $2.50 for a spring roll, and $1.25 for an imperial roll is not really appealing to me. It might be reasonable for someone else, though.

- Drinks weren't that flavorful. My Pink tasted mostly of coconut juice, and while eating the jellies and pomegranate pearls were enjoyable, the pearls didn't taste like pomegranate. I tried my friend's tamarind mint drink, and it was pretty watered down. Could use more tamarind and mint. 

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

OH, I almost forgot about reviewing the pho! Can't write a review about The Pho Bar without saying something about the pho, right?

I ordered a regular custom bowl, with steak, brisket, and flank. The regular bowl was a little smaller than I expected - I'm used to heaping bowls of pho, even for the regular size. The plate of garnishes was nice: the usual bean sprouts, basil, lime, jalapenos, and saw herb, which was a nice addition. 

Like I said before, the ingredients were all of nice quality. There was a pretty good amount of meat in the bowl, though i wish there was more flank. The noodles were pretty standard - not exceptional texture like at some places, but not tough like at others. The broth was...hm, I'm not really sure how to assess it. I want to say that it needs more charred onion flavor, or maybe more bone flavor? I'm not a pho expert by any means. Overall, it was pretty good.

tl;dr: The ingredients are all super fresh, and the place could be trendy. Some things need better execution, but they have time to fix stuff. Come try it out!

Nina and I had lunch here today.  It's been a while since I've been on the North side of campus and much has changed.  The Pho Bar is where the Northside Theatre used to be.  When I was a Cal freshman almost 50 years ago I saw a double bill at the Northside during Freshman Orientation Week, "Never on Sunday" and "Black Orpheus".  Those movies defined the beginning of my identity as a Berkeley student/person and it made me sad to realize the Northside was gone and that I hadn't even noticed when it closed.

Nina has been talking about The Pho Bar for a while so I was eager to try it.  We walked in and were greeted by the friendly young man behind the counter.  We ordered regular bowls of pho w/ sirloin and brisket.  Tea is complimentary.  We found seats and our bowls of pho were brought to us.  A condiment bar w/ lime wedges, bean sprouts, purplish basil, jalapeno slices and another vegetable/herb I didn't recognize was against the side wall by the fireplace.  Nina says at dinner the condiments are brought to you.  I added some of everything and a few splashes of Sriracha from the container on the table.  The broth was OK, less complex than the broth at Huang Tra.  The portion was fine for lunch and the price was reasonable.  We were charged only $8 rather than $9.  Maybe they have senior rates?  The tea was very strong, hot and bitter.  While the pho was good, I'm more likely to go to Huang Tra.

First, Pho Bar also accepts Discover, Visa, and MasterCard. There's a foursquare deal here (10% off) and they're a member of the Spendgo network!

The cashier and restaurant screams hipster. It's a really nice and clean place that's sure to feed hungry college students. It's also a good place to discuss problem sets, meet with professors or anything. I think there actually is a full bar here too, but that's off to the side and not in the general seating area.

My friend and I came and both got the combination ($10.88 each after tax). He got the pork and I got the chicken. I'd have to say that the sandwiches here are a lot better than the pho. This place is NOT for pho lovers, as there's plenty of other pho places around the UC campus area that serve much better pho.

But the sandwiches are pretty good. The bread was crispy, chicken was soft, and had the right amount of spices and flavoring. Will come back!

I bike past this place all the time and wondered whether it was any good.  I stopped in today with my colleague Arthur O. for lunch.

The most amazing thing about the Pho Bar is how good it looks.  Aside from the fact that you order at the cash register and get food brought to your table, Pho Bar could be described as upscale and tony.  We sat next to the fireplace, which was definitely roaring.  I liked that we could see into the kitchen, which looked squeaky clean.  The people who work at Pho Bar could easily be described as attractive and friendly.

Our lunch was A-OK but seemed slightly expensive.  The tastes were clean and varied.  I ordered a special consisting of a small house pho and a half banh mi -- I got the barbecued pork sandwich and responded that I had no objections to the jalapeños that came in it.  Our lunches came lightning fast and they were pretty good.  I can't imagine that I won't be back.

We must have been lucky because we were able to walk right up to the register when we arrived at 12:15.  A half-hour later, there was a line out the door.

I don't know what exactly I was eating, but it wasn't pho. I give this place two stars solely for the interior and it's potential. The pho bar is clean, cozy, and has good beer on tap (always a plus) but what it has in decoration it lacks in flavor. 

Ordered a regular pho with meatballs, brisket, and rare sirloin. Looked like normal pho when it arrived, I was so hopeful, wishing it was going to taste of sweet star anise. Unfortunately what I ate was tepid and tasted fatty and unloved. The broth, which is the main thing in pho was far too beefy and lacked any complexity. Adding hoisin and chili paste didn't help it much either. I found the brisket over cooked and the noodles were too gushy, perhaps soaking in water for too long before. Portion was also meager for a $9 bowl. I get that this place uses "organic" meat, but I couldn't find their actual sources listed. 

Leaving the pho bar the man who took our order asked me how it was. I was honest and he told me the chef was new, I don't like excuses but it seems like they genuinely care. I hope they get a new chef and maybe I'd try it again. Still, I'd only go back if I was lazy and had serious pho cravings

Update:
The pho improved! It tastes so much better now. I remember the first time I went, I had to ask for hot water to water down the saltiness. Now it is as it should be - savory, not too salty! Yay! have a star for getting it right :)

_________________________________________________________
I'm so torn about this place. The clean and open atmosphere beckons me to like the place ALOT, yet the pho I had today was slightly better than pho at Pho Hoa. I'm starting to think it's impossible to find good pho in Northern California.

The price is quite high for a bowl of pho. Taste is comparable to eating Panda Express and calling it Chinese Food. The service is nice and the atmosphere is awesome. Only if they could do something about the pho's "soup" so that it captures the authentic pho's deep and comforting taste...

This place has really poor ratings, but whatever. To me, this place just gets better by the visit. I've been to a few Pho restaurants here in Berkeley and I'm certain this is got to be the best one. It's like your standard pho, but better! For me, I prefer to get the house special, which is pretty much the standard beef pho. The broth is really yummy! I feel like it's tastier than it should be, which is just spoiling my taste buds! The beef is really lean, and tender, which is something that seems hard to run across when ordering pho. Also, what comes with your meal are the unlimited amount of bean sprouts, green peppers and mint leaves, as well as some very fine tea you help yourself to (did I forget to say it's free with your meal!)... Anyway, Don't be afraid to try anything new here either! I couldn't get enough of the shrimp spring rolls-fresh, green, crispy, mouth watering- mmm so refreshing! 

The atmosphere here is excellent as well. It's definitely a great place to go on an outing if your looking to treat someone special!

I was going to talk about how I didn't like my pho, but I just found out through Yelpers that the pho doesn't have MSG... makes sense why the pho tasted different (and healthier). 
I ordered the house pho (#1), and I got a small... but the small was actually really small. Other pho restaurants have bigger servings for cheaper. The noodles are... thinker? I think... something was just different about the pho... maybe MSG really does make a huge difference. I'll try a sandwich next time I come here, but I don't think I'll come here for pho.
Because you order and pay at the same time once you enter, this place is convenient for groups of 6-7+ (you won't get owned by the service charge that other restaurants have).

-same amount of noodle in regular and large bowl
-noodle were in pieces not whole long noodles
- changed a new bowl after asked

I'm not coming again.

My new obsession is wholesome gourmet fast food, especially near my home.  The Pho Bar uses very fresh ingredients, bright green basil, crunchy vegetables on the bahn mi and quality cuts of meat in the pho.  I bought a combo for $10 which included a half bahn mi sandwich and small pho.  The sandwich was delicious, fresh vegetables and tender and flavorful meat on a fresh roll.  The pho was light on meat and light on flavor, I poured in the rooster hot sauce.   

This restaurant is fairly new and has potential, I love the the commitment to good quality food at affordable prices.

Finally made it back to try the Banh Mi ($6, got Ham & Pate, also grilled pork, chicken, and edamame/tofu fritter are available) and ordered up some Cha Gio (spring rolls, $6) on the side.

Cha Gio comes with sprouts, cucumber slices, lettuce, vermicelli and nuoc cham (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZmYIPv4XQQ2bT4dgl6ezzA?select=8GhD9Yr7LAPDCaQNWfJINQ) More roll wrapping issues. Different diameters yielded under-fried (https://s3-media4.ak.yelpcdn.com/photo/DJocu9poRnZTTpiYTidgYA/l.jpg) , burned (https://s3-media2.ak.yelpcdn.com/photo/Bl_BdCQMQ5MOqBfT_sapnA/l.jpg), and just OK Cha Gio. The lettuce was limp and wilty and not a good for wrapping (https://s3-media3.ak.yelpcdn.com/photo/sNuHJ8AkuAuzazTxqG5aIw/l.jpg). 2 stars

The banh mi looked pretty good (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZmYIPv4XQQ2bT4dgl6ezzA?select=ojChlh5uzpr2MLgynWhdBw). 

The baguette needed more toasting to give the crust the typical crackle. Nice flavorful cold-cuts. The baguette appeared to have been gutted for a better bread to filling ratio, but still the pate was barely noticable. The daikon & carrots needed more pickling. 3 stars for flavor, but $6 kinda steep.

Lowering Pho Bar overall to 3 stars.

3.5
the "Berkeley version" of a pho house

1. Impressive setting--Swanky and new. Overdone here and there, but an all around good looking bar.

2. They use the good stuff--Their website reads: "We use natural meats, without growth hormones or antibiotics. Organic & sustainable products used whenever possible. WE DO NOT ADD MSG, EVER!"
Thus, prices are +$1 or +$2 per dish than the average hole in the wall.

3. Meat politics aside, the pho broth was less flavorful than I'm accustomed to. The banh mi, on the other hand, was phenomenal! The filling was fresh and the bread toasted well. Will buy again.

4. Don't forget, it's a bar!--They've a few beers on tap(trumer, pyramid, boont from what I remem), and a few bottles(racer 5). Wine too, I think. Quite nice.

"PHO?" TODAY I MAKE MY STAND! THEY TOOK THIS DOWN!!!

After years of reading yelp reviews, for the better or worse, eating at "Pho" bar I break my silence. In a perfect world my inspiration to write would come from a ground breaking meal, maybe amazing service, or even the correction of a mistake that is handled so well it leaves a good taste in your mouth. Save the few mind-numbing 5 star reviews of "Pho" bar, we all must face the reality that our world is far from perfect. "Pho" bar is about as far from perfect as it gets. The "pho" was awful, the service not much better, and I left feeling like I had been robbed.
 
It is clear that someone or some people put a lot of time and effort into making the ambiance just the way they wanted. But as a pervasive theme to the meal the focus was not on the food but the image. This western Vietnamese eatery was a ghost town when we arrived. When I think of my favorite pho spots, I see full tables of quiet people over steaming bowls of hot soup, tattered menus and tables with scars telling of the hundreds of thousands of hot bowls and happy patrons. From the view at the register where you order the fact that the beef is high quality and that "evil" MSG was not to be had was no subtlety. In ordinary circumstances this is my type of place, but when it comes to pho if you want to get fancy it better still be good. 
 
OVERALL WORST PHO SO FAR! I got the large number one. Yes it was expensive, small, and not hot enough. Read any other review and this will be covered. I order the same thing no matter where I go, #1 as big as they will make it and loaded with goodies. The broth was bland and dull at best. When I found the meat under all the noodles the nightmare started. The sliced beef was ok, the beef balls what ever, brisket was completely broken down into what I later told the proprietor was reminiscent of cat food. My favorite goodies, tripe and tendon, were the most disappointing. I love soft and sumptuous tendon so much I have been getting extra lately and did so when I ordered. It was thin, hard and rubbery. The tripe grey and mushy not at all the little bits of squeaky texture I look forward to.  After trying all the components I was resolved to eat it and try and enjoy it. One bite of all these poorly cooked meats caught in the web of noodles swimming in tasteless broth, and I was done. My eating companions finished their bowls to varying degrees and it was time to go without so much as one check-in from the staff. 

This is the part when bad food gives way to worse customer service. Two of our party asked to have their remaining expensive soup to go and instead it was thrown away. My FULL bowl was cleared and I was not asked at all about my experience. My party left and I lingered wishing a word about the meal. When the woman reappeared I simply told her that I had not cared for or was able to eat the food I was served. She looked puzzled and asked for some feed back which was very similar to my description of my soup. She not once apologized let alone offered me my money back for a meal not eaten. Some how the lasting impression from our interaction left a worse taste than the mushy, luke-warm bowl of CRAP. 

If the owner reads this and has any interest in serving good pho, I challenge you to go and eat somewhere authentic, see how it is done and recreate the same execution with more expensive cuts of meat and no MSG. Or continue to have more one star reviews and one time costumers

As promised, I went back here to try some other items off the menu even though the last time I was here I was disappointed with the Pho.  

I got the Classic Banh Mi (same as a Dac Biet for those who are used to ordering off of a Vietnamese menu).  It didn't disappoint.  The pickled vegetables(do chua) were not overpowering, the cucumbers and cilantro were fresh, there was a good amount of meat (cha lua, thit nguoi) and the pate was great.  The only thing is that I wish there was a thicker layer of pate, because that's my favorite part of the sandwich.  I'm not a big fan of spice so I ordered it without the jalapenos.

I didn't order the Pho, but my dining companion did so the first thing I asked when it was put down in front of her was  for a sip of the broth.  Wow!  What a change since last Friday.  The broth was now nicely balanced and was not fatty at all.  I'm just going to have to write off last Friday's experience as the cooks trying to learn a new recipie, which I can totally understand because it took me a few tries to make a good Pho broth without my mother's help.  The noodles were still not 100% to my liking.  Maybe it's because they use dried noodles(at least I think they do since you can see packages of dried noodles in the kitchen, but it might just be for decoration), since my mom would always buy fresh noodles, but alas I realize that I'm not in my mom's kitchen. (Okay probably an unfair comparison since I've only ever once been to a Pho restaurant that even came close to my mom's Pho.) I'm not saying the noodles were bad though, perfectly fine compared to most of the Pho I've had in the area.  Since my dining companion isn't a big eater I finished off her bowl of Pho for her.

We also sampled the Spring Rolls and the Beignets.  The Spring Rolls were very good and the fish sauce (nouc cham) that came with them was perfect, not too sweet and not too sour.  The Beignets were also great, but then it's just fired dough sprinkled with powdered sugar so how can it not be great?  I only wished that you got more than three with each order.

As stated previously, the place is still very nice and the staff were even better than before.  I even got to speak with the owners, who were very friendly and assured me that things will only get better as the staff learn.  I hope so since I'll definitely be coming here again.

I had the chicken Bahn Mi and the beef noodle soup (the works) tonight and neither of them were very impressive. 

Bahn Mi: the pickled vegetables were bland and they were very stingy on the meat. I didn't think the sandwich had very much flavor. I actually had to put some extra hot sauce and hoisin sauce on it to make it taste like something. The bread was pretty good but it was 70% of the sandwich because there wasn't much of the filling. 

The works beef noodle soup: Soup was toooo sweet. Tasted like they put too much MSG or something in it. It doesn't have that pho taste. It wasn't a very good compliment to the noodles or meat and it definitely didn't carry the dish very well. 

Ambiance is very new and trendy. The modern decor infused with a mix of vietnamese flare gave the place a real kick. I like how the old and new came together at this place. It looks like a nice cafe place to chill and read/surf the web for hours. 

Service here was very friendly and fast. I'm a very impatient person so when I say the food came fast, there's no question about how fast this place is!

Price was on the expensive side. For a bowl of pho...$10 is a bit much. The bowl was HUGE but it was mainly a generous serving of soup with a side of some meat and noodles. Which really should have been the other way around. $6 for Bahn Mi that is bland and mainly just bread...not worth it. 

Overall: I don't think I'll come back because it's expensive and judging from the wide range of ratings this place is getting, their food is not very consistent. They have their good and bad days, I don't want to risk it and come back on a bad day again.

Fro-yo girl here. Pho Bar is polished, upscale and clean and it even has Sketch organic fro-yo!  They use natural meat without growth hormones. They have boba drinks, pho, banh mi, free wi-fi and fro-yo. Wow.

You can get the house pho, the works pho or build your own bowl of pho with tendon, tripe, meatballs and the usual suspects. The other offerings include noodle salads, summer rolls, and desserts (beignets, fro-yo, rice pudding).

* House pho ($8 regular, $10 XL): an elegant looking bowl of noodle soup, comes with a generous amount of rare sirloin and well done brisket, rice noodles, a thin tangle of onions, finely chopped scallions and a sweet and beefy broth. On the side you get basil, sprouts, saw herb, jalapenos, lime. The brisket was thin, dry and lacking in flavor. Plenty of delicious piping hot broth, noodles and meat for each spoonful. The broth isn't the most flavorful (lack of MSG?) but it's still good. It's cleaner and lighter than usual. 

* Fro-yo: comes in 1 size, 1 flavor, Sketch organic tart ($4): the ugly swirl was shameful and the portion small, but the fro-yo was much more flavorful than most plain tarts, it was very tart and natural, icy and refreshing but not watery, it tasted like frozen Vietnamese yogurt (da ua), a little too icy for me but otherwise fabulous

The dining area has huge communal wood tables with chopsticks and condiments (sriracha, hoisin sauce) and pendant lamps with Vietnamese sayings.

They have some weird rules about what you can order there vs. online and when. But they also have early bird specials, meal combos, etc. And free wi-fi.

You know you love me. X0 X0, fro-yo girl.

My boyfriend went here once without me, and has been begging me to go back with him for a while now. When we arrived at around 7 on a Friday night the place was pretty empty. The woman behind the counter taking orders was really nice, as was the other guy who looked like he was on break when we arrived but helped us later. My boyfriend and I both got the spiced chicken vermicelli bowls. I liked the fish sauce, the spring rolls, and the vermicelli was cooked nicely; however I wasn't a huge fan of the chicken. The portion for the vermicelli bowl was quite large, so you definitely get a lot of bang for your buck on that one. Since I feel silly for going to a place called the Pho Bar and not getting any Pho, I'm going to return soon to try the Pho. Overall, solid food, good, friendly service, and the atmosphere is definitely a step up from La Burrita.

Wen to Pho Bar on 3/13/12. Let me start with the positives. The restaurant aesthetics are great. Nice place. As for the food, I had The Works (Rare Sirloin, Brisket, Flank, Tendon, Tripe, and Meatballs) and a cafe sua da. First, I'm glad to see the iced coffee is served the more "traditional" way - drip method into the sweetened condensed milk - and not a pre-made (perhaps from a mix?) blend ready to drink like is now, sadly, almost universal at the "real" (as in grubby) Pho places like you might find around International in Oakland. Now, the meat in the pho was top quality. Very good eye of round, brisket was excellent, and the tripe was the best I've had in a loooong time. Unfortunately there was very little tendon but the small amount there was good. So, good job with the meats. Ok, now for the bad, the real bad. The central part of pho is the broth. I think this needs to be explained to the cooks here because it was terribly bland. No star anise, no fennel, no cinnamon, NONE of the flavors that you will find up front and prominent in a well-made pho. It was beefy, salty, and that's it. The typical condiments (basil, lime, sprouts, chile paste, etc.) were good but could not rescue an awful (as in bland) broth. A bad bowl of pho will ruin a perfectly good evening hahaha. True though.

Pho broth not that flavorful--lots of meat though.  Mint Tamarinade pretty watery.  Banh mi okay but honestly, the best part  of the meal was the fries.  Very confused about that.  Hopefully this place gets better.  It's in an awesome location.

Gotta say that the pho here is like tasting dirty water, no flavor, no taste and $10 bucks give me a break.  OK tried to really like it so we gave it another chance only to have our hopes and dreams crushed with a nasty tasting bahn mi.  The chicken no flavor, the vegetarian no flavor.  The food is just not only bland but just plan horriable, with no taste in sight.  I love vietnamese food and you can go to china town in Oakland and for $3 bucks get a rockin bahn mi and Pho that you can have an orgasm over.  On the plus side the concept is cool and the place is cute but bring a bag lunch with you from Oakland.  Just don't let anyone else see you eating your bahn mi from Oakland they just might want to take it and eat it

Been back a few times now and have tried a variety of items:

Bahn Mi:  Continues to be a standout.  Both the chicken and the pork are delicious, I prefer the pork.  The sandwiches are very fresh and filling and a bargain for 6 bucks.  The fries are a nice accompaniment and worth the extra 2 bucks, but I'm always so full from the sandwich that I don't eat many of the fries.

Apps:  Love the chicken wings.  Served with a delicious sriracha sauce.  The wings are juicy and slightly crispy.  They taste "natural", like the cooks actually used raw chicken wings, rendered the fat a little in an oven then fried them.  They don't taste "weird" like wings at pizza places.  The shrimp summer roll was fresh and light with sweet crisp boiled shrimp, a bit bland though.

Pho: I will preface this by saying I have never had Pho that I've really enjoyed.  Noodle soup is not my thing.  That said, I didn't like it here either.  Very bland and boring.  This might be the best Pho ever, but I didn't enjoy it.

Dessert:  I have become a big fan of the corn and rice pudding, sounds weird, but it is delicious.  It's made with coconut milk and fresh corn.

Drinks:  The tamarinade was nice, but a bit pricey.  The large costs about as much as a bahn mi, but then again the bahn mi is pretty cheap.

Service:  FANTASTIC!  Everyone is smiling and super friendly.

Yea...so me and my friend ordered delivery from this place and I'm sorry but the pho is the worse pho I ever had. The broth tasted like water and salt without any other flavoring/stock. the noodles had this hard texture to it. They also force you to bring back their tiffins which I think is stupid. If your ordering it to-go you should expect the food right away and not try to keep it warm in a tiffin. The prices completely overpriced compared to the portion and quality of the food. We also ordered a PINK (Xung Xa Hot Luu) Icy Drink which had no shaved ice in it and the pomegranate tapiocas were hard and disgusting and the drink was still pretty bland and not even close to being sweet at all.

When we were trying to pay the tip online on their website it kept messing up saying it was an invalid number and got us really mad. After we had placed our order, they called us to let us know that the PINK Icy Drink was sold out. But afterwards they said they made a new one just for us (yes I know I said it was disgusting, they could have at least made it taste better by taking their time). 

Right now i'm rating it 1-star because of its poor quality, portion, and price of the food.

Seriously, guys? 1 star? 2 stars? Wow.

Just because all the other pho restaurants have horrible ambiances doesn't mean you can't applaud this restaurant for their ambiance!

Sure it's 1 dollar or 1.5 dollars more expensive than other places, but the quality is unparalleled. There is no MSG because the broth is made with time, care, and the proper amount of natural seasoning (which is expensive, mind you, and is the reason why the other places have to use so much MSG.)

Meticulous attention to detail regarding the food (pho noodles are precooked in extra strong broth and the tripe is marinated in extra strong broth for flavor, etc) and regarding the ambiance (the chicken coop wire on the cabinets behind the bar match the pattern on the fireplace cover).

The service is fantastic. Everyone here is really nice!

But to be honest, I come here for the food. It's my favorite pho and I've had a LOT of pho in my lifetime. No poorly cut meats, no MSG, organic ingredients, no post-pho dehydration, delicious noodles, delicious broth, etc... etc... I respect that!

The noodle and the meat are good, but the broth is too bland and fatty. The price is a little bit high for such small portion. In fact, this is the least pho-like pho I've ever had. 
This place would be perfect if their pho preparation matched their schick decoration.

I really wanted to like this place. The place is very clean, the decorations are nice and modern, it was a very welcoming, pleasant atmosphere.
And the service was great, even amazing. Cashier was friendly and talkative, servers smiling and seemed like they wanted to be around.

The food though. Hum. Maybe it's cause I used to eat in Westminster all the time, where Little Saigon is, but I just did not like the flavor of the Pho. The broth was bland, had a dull taste to it, and didn't have the flavor of  a good stock with the flavor of the bones really cooked into it. The noodles were also...not of my liking. They were kind of grainy and tough when you ate them, definitely not the almost gooey texture I usually find in rice noodles.

Also, for an extra large for 10 dollars, the portion was rather small. I used to pay 7 or 8 dollars for a large back in Westminster that gave me about 1.5x as much as I got here. There's just a lot of soup, which, as I said, wasn't very good.

Maybe I'll try the sandwich next time, or perhaps the desserts. From the looks of it, the desserts seemed like they'd be decent. I don't see myself coming back here though, unless a friend wanted to take me there.

If they work on the taste of their Pho, this place could be great. Until then though, the taste of the food really brings it down.

Not your average hole in the wall Vietnamese restaurant.  The restaurant is super clean, the plastic chopsticks they give you don't look questionable, the waiters weren't even Vietnamese,  and a bowl of pho is going to cost you more while being a smaller than your average.  Nevertheless, it's legit Americanized "fancy" Vietnamese restaurant... that gives free boba during their early HH. 

So far, I pretty much dislike every single restaurant on Hearst/ Euclid, with the exception of Top Dog and Northside Cafe, this by far is my favorite. 

And I heard you can call in pho until 2a.  Score!

SHO EXPENSIVE!!! That's the key takeaway to this review. I came in here with two friends one rainy evening, completely starving and feeling rejected because Urban Turban was closed. 

I ordered the The Works, which has Rare Sirloin, Brisket, Flank, Tendon, Tripe, and Meatballs (according to their website menu), and my friends got sandwiches. I think we all agreed that all though our food was delicious, the portions were much, much too small. I could've honestly gone for another round, but it was way too expensive to even consider. The broth and meat were really tasty, and the noodles were well cooked... there just wasn't enough of it. The sandwiches were maybe 7 inches long, which to active, growing boys is absolutely nothing. 

Service was average (even though we couldn't figure out how to get tea and no one was around for us to ask), and the food came out sloooowwwww. The one thing I really liked was their furniture - their tables are giant pieces of timber cut vertically, and everything had a very forresty yet contemporary feel.

This 5 star review is completely based on the Banh Mi here.

Omg, yummmmmmy goodness. For a while I've been searching for a place that had Banh Mi that was legit, no bullsh*t. We can hardly say that the Banh Mi at Saigon Eats can be considered a Banh Mi, it's seriously a pathetic attempt at making a westernized and thus, more acceptable version of it.

The Banh Mi at The Pho Bar reminds me of the stuff I can get back home in San Jose. I love the Pate in it, the vegetables felt fresh and light, and the bread is a perfect blend of toastiness and softness. Granted it is $7 with Tax compared to like $3.50 in San Jose, but I really shouldn't complain because it was thatttt good.

The service was really quick and really friendly. I had only a 15 minute gap to grab a bite to eat, and I successfully ordered, ate half a sandwich, and paid my bill within that time period! 

I'm definitely coming back again during my lunch breaks!

Kind of crappy pho...it's really expensive (like 8 bucks for a bowl) and you get a small portion. 

Broth tastes really fake, almost like their broth is store bought/processed. Soup is brown...but has no flavor to it. Also comes kind of cold.

Noodles aren't really cooked to the right texture and were still raw.

The beef that comes with the soup isn't really that fresh. 

I heard their sandwiches are better.

Come on, Berkeley. I was expecting more.

Wow. I've never had pho this bad. The ambiance is great, but the pho was just horrible. 

The bean sprouts were just small and not fresh, the mint leaves weren't fresh either. And the beef tripe... YELLOW?? WTF?!? WHY THE HELL WAS THE BEEF TRIPE YELLOW? 

The beef-balls were almost flavorless, the other beef had little to no taste to it as well.  The soup was bland and watered down, with a thick layer of oil on the top.  Even after drenching my soup in sriracha the soup still tasted like oily water.

I kind of expected this when I saw the decor. 

Expensive pho for a small portion. The soup is bland, it tastes slightly better than the pho soup at Cafe 3. Pho is not a fancy food! I wish the business could see that and focus more on food quality than to make the place a fancy restaurant.

Unfortunately, this Bar falls way short of a tasty meal. While I loved the decor,  especially the modernized take on communal tables, and focus on organic, sustainable ingredients, the flavor profiles were nil. 

I'm typically a purist when it comes to my pho, allowing the flavors of the meat and soup shine through with minimal enhancements via lime, sprouts, and basil. The pho here was so bland i was forced to improvise with heapings of hoisin and sriracha sauce, to no avail. It was truly a shame that the quality meat was so depressed in the lack of flavor. 

As to be expected at an ethnic-themed place catering to non-ethnic palettes, prices were a bit higher and servings smaller than authentic pho places. I did like the separate bar area though, and the system of paying at the register before sitting down was conducive to large groups of diners paying separately.

I went here on the recommendation of a friend. I met up with four of my classmates for lunch. Surprisingly most of them had never had pho before. What a way to introduce them to what's usually an awesome cheap meal.

Paid about $9 up front for a normal house pho. The location is actually pretty nice. That should've been my warning, looking back. I was expecting $9 of pho, because $9 should go a loooong way for a bowl of soup. Given that I generally have paid $5 for a normal-sized bowl of pho in a number of different cities, my expectations were high. I was at the very least expecting to leave filled.

Sat down and 5 minutes later my pho is served. Hmmm... this is the SMALLEST SIZED BOWL OF PHO I have ever had. The soup was lukewarm and tasted like barely-salted water. I had to dig through a sad-looking mass of noodles to find the paltry 3 pieces of sliced beef. The beef was bland - I truly can't remember the last time I thought beef was bland. It is so strange not liking what you just spent nine bucks on.  Luckily, I was really hungry, so I did finish the entire bowl against the wishes of my nose and tongue. And I was still hungry. So much for cramming my face with pho for lunch. 

Don't go here. Not only is the food seriously hard to enjoy, but this place is a rip-off. I will be much more wary of $9 bowls of any soup in the future.

If you are a pho lover like me, do not (I repeat, DO NOT) come here. You'll be sorely disappointed. I read the other reviews and noticed that most people griped about the prices. But, because there are hardly any pho restaurants in the Oakland area that stay open late, the boy and I wanted to check it out for ourselves. I mean, who doesn't want to have a go-to pho place for those late-night cravings?
 
So here's the dirt: in my very humble opinion, it has absolutely nothing to do with the fact that you'll pay more here than an authentic pho joint. It's the fact that this place was built on a cool concept that has no focus on the food whatsoever. The flavors?...well, there are none. The broth is utterly bland which completely kills the dish. I really wanted to like this place and I ate each and every bite trying to find something good about it but there were no redeeming qualities. This is, by far, the worst pho I've ever had - I couldn't even get through half the bowl and I ended up going to Jack in the Box afterwards.

Again, cool restaurant concept but poor execution on the food. Now, if you've never had pho before, you may like it. But for those of us who take our pho seriously, heed the warnings.

I have to say that the reviews for this place are quite misplaced. I rarely if ever think a restaurant deserves a five star rating, but it is important for this new establishment. 

The food is fresh and well-prepared and presented. The staff is great. The perfect place to bring the whole lab group for lunch.

It is about time that there were reasonable dining options on the north side of campus. As a long time North Side resident I am appalled by the quality of restaurants that manage to survive next to campus. Finally in Pho Bar there is comfortable post lab location with really good beer. hopefully the owners can be convinced to keep the bar open later and may be add a few more options to there already very nice drink list (Hitachino White Ale for $11 right next to lab - amazing!)

This restaurant/bar may finally lead the way to Berkeley campus area becoming like a real college town - with diverse, polished bars and restaurants - the kind of place that grad. students, postdocs, and profs actually want to hang around.

I read bunch of reviews so angry because Pho broth here have no MSG and therefore dont taste like in scary Pho joint in Westminster City. Big f*king deal you from Westminster City. I was born in Russia, but dont go round crying that I cant find authentic kalashnikov store in Berkeley. 

Reminds me of people who go to nudist hot-spa, then complain "no one wears bathing suit here."  

Walking into Pho Bar on Euclid is reminisce of mysterious,  sexy ex-pat locales in Hanoi. Zinc (aluminum?) Bar at front looks smooth and sturdy enough to do more than eat pho off of, and front bartender inspires similar idea.

Since N. tries to prolong life of vodka consumption by eating healthy, (not to mention re-hydrate with pho broth), organic ingredients here are happily welcomed. 

Conclusion: if you need to vent some more about lack of MSG, why dont you drive for seven hours back to Westminster Fuckingk City.

No...just no. Here is why:

I go in, and order a regular #1 with an ice tea. $10.88 (#1 = $8).

When I get it, I realized that it's a smaller regular portion than other places. I pushed the thought aside, and dug in.

My first impression was the broth. For starters, I know this place is supposed to be healthy, but the broth didn't taste like anything. No salt, no non-MSG flavors, no nothing. What worried me was the fact that the broth was brown, just like any other pho. It didn't taste like beef, chicken, or whatever broth! I added some Hoisin sauce (which I never do to pho broth), and it still tasted bland.

On top of the non-flavored broth, it wasn't even hot! When you order raw meat, you expect the broth to be nice and hot - to cook the meat. I took my slices apart, and they were still mostly red. Seriously?? I believe one why to stay healthy is to consume (semi)cooked meat!

Second disappointment: the noodles. They were either undercooked, or they were from a cheap packaged intant-pho you find at your local Asian mart.

Service was ok. I was amused that they didn't retrieve my number after having given my order. The lady came up to me, and asked me multiple times to make sure I had everything I ordered. I don't know why, but ok...

So, all-in-all, that pho was definitely not worth $8. Sure the place looks nice, but it's all about the food!! You could go to the janky-est place in the world, and the food could still be amazing!

Will not be coming back...

What *IS* authentic pho?  

As you contemplate answering this question, these are the things I liked about the Pho Bar:

No MSG.  I did not feel parched dry after eating the pho here.  Wow, I can even bring my friend who refuses to eat pho because she gets migraine headache when exposed to MSG.

The noodles.  Usually at other pho places I get congealed noodles that make me think they pre-cook the noodles, which then sit around until I order.  Here, the noodles were freshly cooked, but then again I came late in the evening and there were only two other people eating.

The green attitude.  They hand you a cloth napkin when you order at the front desk.  Also, I read on their website you can order take-out in a re-usable container which you return for repeat orders.  

The veggie bar.  You pick up the veggies to add to your pho at a bar.  The veggies were really fresh.  I like that.

The decor.   Long wooden communal tables, and hanging lamps.  Definitely nicer than many other pho restaurants.


Not liked so much.

Meat scarcity.  I guess they use good quality meat with no growth hormones, but for my regular size order with steak and brisket, I got 3 slices of steak and 2 little pieces of brisket.  I was disappointed, and this is kinda big failing for me personally.

So.... really 3.5 stars.

The best drunken Mexican food in Berkeley! Yes the food has a lot of grease but if you want healthy food go next door to cafe innermezzo. The flautas and enchaladas are amazing and if you like really spicy ask for the special red really hot sauce and it will burn your tongue off! Their margaritas are also good.

Pros: Large portions  Cons: tasteless food.   Saw a raving review / recommendation for the chicken enchiladas verde for this place so I ran right down.  The soup was a surprise (didn't know I got it free with my dinner).  It had great flavor once you got past the layer of orange grease on top.  The verde sauce had NO flavor at all.  Very disappointing.
I have been going here for 29 years! Love this place and nothing can compare!!! Brings back so many memories~

My girlfriend and I love this place.  The staff is super friendly (Lucy always says hi) and the food is great.  Try the Chili Colorado or the Grandmas sauce.  Save money by ordering off the ala carte menu.
The house marg is just ok, but the special ones are awesome.

A Hidden Gem! Went here when another restaurant on telegraph was closed -- decided to take a chance on this hole in the wall -- and was pleasantly surprised!! The restaurant is actually quite large, with ornate tables and chairs. Would be a great place for a large group. The food is authentic Mexican and very affordable. The service is wonderful -- we even got free soup for the whole table despite not all of us ordering the special (I guess it helped that my friend spoke fluent spanish :) !) I have been twice, once for dinner, and once for lunch, and will be back again.
Great spot for some Mexican food. The service is fast and the food tastes great. I've had a couple of their burritos and have enjoyed them every time.

I didn't realize Cupkates had a Yelp site because I thought it didn't have an address! Haha...well, goes to show you can Yelp about anything, I guess.

Anyways, it took me a while to finally catch up with the Cupkates truck, but the day I did happened to also be my friend's birthday, so I caught the truck on Shattuck in front of the Berkeley Rep Theater. Since I follow Cupkates on Twitter, she gave me one free cupcake and I bought two more. I got the Red Velvet, S'mores, and Double Vanilla.

Then I went to my friend's apartment and surprised him with the cupcakes, we put candles in them to celebrate his birthday, and then cut them up into neat and shareable pieces.

I think my favorite one was the S'mores, but all three were great. Thanks Cupkates for helping me celebrate my friend's birthday in a special and literally sweet way! :D

And since she went to Cal herself...GO BEARS!

I have never been a huge fan of sweets let alone being a cupcake aficionado.  I never understood the hype behind these little pretty things that are yes, very pretty, but ultimately, just cakes.  I know people who get so excited when they find out about these mysterious cupcake trucks driving around town and follow them like squealing school girls chasing after pop stars, and I can't possibly relate.  

But, when my friend spotted CupKates on College and happily bought a dozen and offered me one, I couldn't refuse.  I had to find out what the fuss was all about.  So I took a bite of this pretty beet-colored Red Velvet cupcake with some skepticism and must say, 

it was good!

The icing might have been a bit too sweet for me, but the cake itself was sweet and light and and moist and delicious.  

Now, I can see why people are so into them.

I had Cupkates for the first time the other day, and they are scary good. They're $3 a cupcake, which I think is really reasonable for an afternoon snack! They're filling, the frosting is amazing, and the people helping us were really friendly. Ps: Definitely try the red velvet. Out of this world.

Cupkates has really fluffy and luscious cupcakes, I tried their Red Velvet, Tiramisu and Key Lime ones and I was a fan of all of them. The cakes themselves were very light but the frosting was on the heavier side. I would've given it a 5 if not for its excessive frosting. 

But I'm definitely going to go back and try their Salted Caramel and Double Chocolate cupcakes. A must-go for cupcake lovers!

I'm always sitting, waiting, wishing.... for the Cupkates truck to roll into downtown Berkeley. The first time I went, I bought 2 cupcakes, big mistake because I was feigning for them after I finished my smores one and gave the salter caramel one to a friend! The truck came back to Berkeley on Friday and this time I bought 6 cupcakes (Tiramisu, 2 Smores, Salted Caramel, Red Velvet, and Mexican Chocolate) to share with friends, but they're all gone now too! Next time I think I'll have to get 8 of them! 

PS. Cupkates, please come to Berkeley more often!

They come by my office every Wednesday. They are baked fresh every day and they taste like it as well. They are way better than Sprinkles, Teacakes, Love at First Bite and all those other cupcake specialty stores. Trust me, I have tried them all and they are always dry, overly sweet and heavy. Cupkates is always moist, flavorful and fresh. My favorite is the s'mores cupcake but the lemon raspberry is a close second. I'm just bummed that she's usually sold out by most of her flavors when she arrives at our stop. I've added her on Facebook so that I always know where I can catch the truck on non-Wednesdays.

I finally got around to grabbing one of Cupkate's cupcakes when I went to a local farmer's market!  

I got the S'mores cupcake and loved it!!  Marshmallow frosting on top, chocolate cupcake in the middle, and a (surprising) graham cracker bottom!  Soo GOOD!  Moist and delicious!  I also thought the cupcake would be extremely sweet but it wasn't so!  I mean it was still sweet for any cupcake standards, just not tooth-achingly so.
Red velvet cupcakes has always been my favorite......until now. The Salted Caramel blew my mind and my taste buds. Just plain ridiculous on how good it is.

The TWINKIE cupcakes rule!

Thanks Kate!!!!!!!!

I finally caught them at Off the Grid at Panhandle one early evening and decided to get the Salted Caramel and Double Vanilla, both of which were outstanding! The buttercream frosting on both cakes were the French style, not cloying sweet, yet rich and fluffy. I just hate the dense, powdered sugar based frosting that many call "buttercream", which are always overly sweet, so I am always left wondering what type of buttercream they are using. Anyway, Cupkates' cakes are so buttery and moist that I can even eat them without the lovely frosting, but you really should enjoy them together. They have so many other interesting flavors like the S'mores and Tiramisu that I have to try next now that I am a big fan. I think Kara's Cupcakes has stiff competition these days.
red velvet with cream cheese frosting. the best i've had.

Tried four flavors (including Lemon Meringue Pie, Salted Caramel, Mexican Chocolate) at Off The Grid at Fort Mason on April 29th. Everything I tried was fantastic.

Moist cake.

Incredible frosting.

Friendly, funny, helpful, patient staff.

Find the truck and buy a box or three today!

Went back for my 2nd time today on Harrison and 19th in Oakland.  This time I decided I wanted to try something different.  I decided to get the Strawberry Swirl which is new and the Double Chocolate.  The Strawberry Swirl was my favorite of the 2 and weird thing is I'm a huge chocolate lover.  So that tells you a lot.  Of course I had to get a couple Red Velvet too, can't pass-up a chance to get those.
