All of the cupcakes that I have tried so far have been so moist and tasty.  The frosting is light and not too sweet.  I said it once and I'll say it again, I think these are the best cupcakes I've ever tasted.

I am trying all the flavors and they are delish.  So far, the lemon meringue cupcake and the key lime are my favorites! 

I just wish they had a store that I could go to.

I am a huge fan of Cupkates!  Really the best cupcake in the Bay Area.  I've had a lot, and they are always moist, fresh and delicious!  I come from Walnut Creek to Berkeley, just to get them on Sunday's.  Red Velvet is fantastic as well as salted caramel.
Wish they'd bring the truck closer to me, but thats ok I'd travel far and wide to get them!

This place is a party in your mouth every single bite. And yes everyone is invited. I've tried almost all of them and have to say red velvet and smores are my favorite. Didn't dig the lemon meringue(too much cream), but the other two: amazing.

I thought this was ok. I got a salted caramel cupcake for $3. 

The cupcake itself wasn't that big but it had a lot (too much) buttercream icing on top. I enjoyed the cupcake but I've certainly had better and thought  the price was way too steep.

I have a sick love for cupcakes and will go just about anywhere for them. Thankfully, though, Cupkates comes to me. I'm a big fan of the red velvet, but I've had almost every kind on offer and they're all good. The only real drawback is that the cupcakes are so good, they frequently sell out!

(+) . Everything.  The cupcakes are really good! I've tried almost all the flavors here and it never disappointed me so far. I think my favorite part about the cupcake is the frosting because the cake is a little bit dry sometimes. It's moist enough but it can be better.  My favorite cupcakes are definitely the Tiramisu, Salted Caramel, and the Red Velvet. The frosting just melts in your mouth and you can definitely taste the buttery goodness. 

(-)  Too pricey for a small cupcake. Even though it's good, I wish it was cheaper or the cupcakes are bigger.  I had to control myself from eating the whole cupcake in two bites. I usually get two cupcakes and that's pretty filing for a decently expensive cost.  

Even though it's a bit pricey, you should definitely try it at least once if you are a cupcake addict like me. I always end up coming back for more every time when I see the truck because it's too tempting!  I think they intentionally make it small so you never get enough of it.  Cupkates is the place where your wallet will be empty before you even know it.

I meant to buy just one cupcake today... and then I walked away with 8. You can't go wrong with any of her fluffy little cakes!! Hard to pick a favorite, but if I have to narrow it down.. I love the Lemon Raspberry, Red Velvet, S'more, and Salted Caramel. Yum!!

Saw their truck one friday and decided to give it a try.

Special flavor was peppermint chocolate. It was delicious.  Then also tried Salted Caramel. That was really good too.

If I see this truck next time, I am standing in line!

so i left work to go across the street to walgreen's for some dessert and, lo and behold, there was a cupcake truck right there. OMG. i was hesitant about buying anything because i hadn't heard of them before but the guy in the truck was wearing a cal hat (go bears!) so i just had to get something (gotta support my fellow cal fans). i got the double vanilla bean and the s'mores. the vanilla bean was good. as a previous poster said, there was a little too much butter BUT it was still good. the smores was also good but i wish the topping was a little sweeter. overall, they were good cupcakes and i'd go again if they come back to this location. how can i say no when they're right across the street from my office??

Best cupcake I've ever tried...yes.
Will there be a line....yes.
Should you get there early before they sell out....yes.
can you have some of mine....NO!
Get your own....yes.

My boyfriend and I were walking around Berkeley when we came across Off the Grid. The Cupkates mobile van was one of the food trucks there. We decided to indulge our sweet tooth. We ordered the double vanilla bean cupcake as well as the tiramisu cupcake. Both were very moist and delicious. My only downside was that for the price these cupcakes seemed  smaller then normal cupcake bakeries.

I pass by Cupkates' food truck many times but I always tend to see red velvet on the menu. I figured paying $3 for a cupcake, I better be having foie gras flavor cupcake, kidding. Then one day, I saw salted caramel on the board and decided to line up and order one at the little window.

I had salted caramel coffee before and loved it. So, I knew I was going to enjoy salted caramel cupcake but was hesitant to express the word "love"  because I'm not a chocolate lover and was afraid the cupcake will taste too sweet. 

I was so wrong. The cupcake was moist, so moist I had trouble picking up the cupcake. And the blend of sweetness is absolutely perfected between the caramel and chocolate. It's interesting tasting both saltiness and sweetness switch back and forth - quite an experience for your taste buds.

Seriously... fights break out infront of this truck and its women talkin all the smack and throwin the slaps!

I can do w/o the heavy butter cream on top. The cupkates stay moist throughout!!!

Not much to say. The shits good. Wish I had a chance to taste the twankie cupkate!!!

I tried Cupkates for the first time today in North Berkeley.  I admit I was a little disappointed after getting pumped up from all the hype.  

I tried red velvet and salted caramel.  While I enjoyed the salted caramel, the red velvet was good, but not amazing.  Love at First Bite has amazing red velvet cupcakes.  

The ladies in the truck are extremely friendly, but I think that the cupcakes are overpriced at $3 per cupcake, some specials even running at $4, the lines are too long, and the cupcakes are simply just above average :(

Sorry to disappoint, but I remain loyal to Love at First Bite.

Best cupcake in the Bay Area. No matter what cupcake I try, I love it. The frosting is so delicious and airy and is particularly good on the Twinkie and lemon meringue cupcakes. It doesn't taste like i'm licking up softened butter with flavoring. 
The cakes are never dry and the filling is always delicious. 

My favorite is the tiramisu with the amazing little graham cracker crust on the bottom of the cake. I could eat like a thousand of those every day for the rest of my life. 

I had been withholding this review for a long time because I had heard so much about Kara's cupcakes being the best, but now that I have tried both, I can say that Cupkates is hands down the best. I'm in love. 

See you on Fourth Street and/or at Off the Grid for my weekly cupcake!

Weird? Or Simply Creative.... 

I've never craved cupcakes as much as I have nowadays after having theirs! It's not like its addicting but its where when you suddenly craving the li'l cakes CupKates are the first to come to mind. 

They have different flavors and occasionally will have the Special Ones as I like to call it.

Its not super sweet, which I like (people who think they know me would think I'm addicted to sugar tho) and super fluff and moist unlike other bakeries. Weird? They are not but creative? Indefinite and I wouldn't have it any other way!

If the salted caramel chocolate cupcake I had today is any indication of how delicious her other cupcakes are.. we have a winner! Moist, not overly sweet, and great flavor. I usually see the truck on 4th Street on weekends.

I am definitely a fan!!! LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE CUPKATES!! 

Yesterday, I surprised my daughter to Cupkates!  We went down to the Emeryville location. We were the third ones in line and I had a daughter as happy as can be when I told her we were going to get the best cupcakes ever.  It was my first time there too so I was really excited. As we waited Kate gave us a sample of a future delicacy the Madagascar... Looked like Creme Brulee, but awesome nonetheless. 

We bought a dozen with S'mores, red velvet, salted caramel, and double chocolate. Once we got into the car it was on! My husband had the double chocolate, I had the s'more, and our daughter had the red velvet.  Heaven!!! 

We're definitely coming back! The guy who was helping out was cool too. I asked him what his favorite was and he said double vanilla.  I'm just going to have to try it next time!! I am excited for the next visit! Whoo hoo!

I'm not a big fan of sweets but Cupkates takes the cake, pun most definitely intended. The salted caramel and red velvet cupcakes were so moist and sweet. A very nice, decadent dessert after a savory meal from food trucks. Next time I check out Cupkates, I'll be munching on Key Lime and S'mores flavored cupcakes. *drool*

5 stars

Thanks to my lovely friend Brigette for introducing me to Cupkates! The cupcake itself has a good moist texture, what I love about is the flavored frosting. ITS HEAVEN!!!!!!! I've tried the carrot, Tiramisu, s'more, red velvet and raspberry lemonde, O-M-G  delish!! Cupkates, you will make me simply gain 10 lbs in one seating. Lol you're amazing!!!

Oh my god -- these are the best cupcakes I have ever had.  And believe me, I have tried a lot of them.  I really love Kara's and was doubtful anything could be better, but I always try to have a open mind, so when I spotted the Cupkates truck on 4th Street in Berkeley this afternoon I went for it.  Dang!  I had no idea a cupcake could be so delicious.  (I got the chocolate with salted caramel icing).

One could be reconciled with being fat, if Cupkates was the reward.  Not that I am, but if Cupkates were more widely available, I might soon be.

If I had a hat, it would be off to you, Cupkates.  I don't know how you do it, but your cupcakes are a little bit of heaven.

I love this cupcake truck!  The SMORES cupcake is so yummy!  The salted caramel is to die for!  The Strawberry was amazing!  The Salted caramel was also yummy.  Surprisingly, I was not too thrilled or dazzled with the red velvet.  I like my red velvet cupcakes to have more of a buttermilk chocolate flavor and cupskates lacks those flavors.  They are ok.  

Now for my story that happened in March... 

My two boys and I drove to the cupcake truck to pick up 2 dozen cupcakes for my grandfather's birthday.  The truck was there and I could see the cupcakes but they were not selling them.  One of the "off the gird" staff told me ... "they will not be open for business today."  Of course, I asked why and he answered "I am not at liberty to say."  Well, that's not good enough for a girl on a mission to bring cupcakes home.  So, I demanded to talk to someone who could explain to me the problem.  I could see the cupcakes ... just sitting in the window ...waiting for someone to take them home.  

After Cupskates folk realized that I was so disappointed and my kids had long faces, Cupskates explained that the truck was broken and they were prohibited from selling the cupcakes.   Cupskates promised to fix the truck and return within an hour.  So we waited for them to return.  Cupskates promised that they would return. And, guess what ... they did!  They also hooked me up for the inconvenience.  Love this tuck!

Hands down the best cupcakes I have ever tasted.
"So good that you need to eat it with a fork."

I tried the tiramisu cupcake and the double vanilla bean. The frosting is really smooth, light, and full of flavor. The cupcakes are soft, and the tiramisu one had a moist inner center and a thicker cookie layered base. The vanilla bean had a grainier texture, and a genuine rich vanilla taste (other cupcakes use "vanilla" to mean default/white/non-flavor)

NOTE: The elusive cupcake truck adds to the appeal of the cupcakes, so if you happen to catch the truck, you may not have a second chance to buy your cupcake!

The people running Cupkates are really friendly and nice. The guy handing out the cupcakes is very smiley and likes to chat with the customers.
NOTE: They DO accept credit cards!

WILL I come back: If I can find the truck
WHEN will I come back: When I find the truck
WHAT will I do differently: Try the salted caramel

I finally managed to track this little truck down! I've been looking for it for over 2 years! Whew! 

Cupkates both exceeded and underperformed my expectations. I was very surprised about how dense, soft, and almost gooey the cake part of the cupcakes are from Cupkates. Almost like a brownie! Yet, I wasn't too thrill on the frosting. It was very simple, in fact, almost sloppy. My Salted Carmel had sea salt only on 1/4 of the cupcake so it made the cake very unimpressive until I actually reached the salted part of the frosting. After trying Republic of Cake in Orinda, I expected something more unique. The two flavors I tried, S'more and Salted Carmel, were good, just not as mind blowing as I expected. 

Overall, I will come back, but with fierce competition from other cupcake shacks like Teacake, Cupcake Cove, and Republic of Cake, Cupkates tends to fall on the latter half of my "Holy Cupcakes Batman!" list. Don't get me wrong, I'm still a fan--partially bc I'm fattie. Sometimes it's nice to keep things simple, and that's exactly what Cupkates strives for and succeeds in mass producing.

"Meh, I've experienced better. "

That truly does sum it up. There used to be a really nice guy running this truck. Since I work on Fourth St., he would give me a free cupcake with the purchase of at least one cupcake. Now they have a bunch of girls running it and they won't do that for us. They're also not as nice as the guy used to be. 

The frosting tastes weird. The texture is really off - almost gelatinous. NOT how frosting should taste. The cake is usually too moist but I do like it. The two of them do not combine well IMO.

Very tasty, price is right. The vendor's habit of telling you how popular your cupcake choice is (this is my 3rd most popular cupcake!) is annoying. How shallow! Let's judge cupcakes by what's in their hearts.

a solid red velvet. moist and yumtastic.

 i also accidentally took a bite of a salted caramel cupcake which i had to spit out because it had buttercream and that stuff is like eating straight crisco. i really don't understand how anybody in their right mind could like buttercream.

Just ran into them today for the first time ever.  Hardest part was choosing which cupcake to buy.  I settled on the salted caramel and the red velvet.  I don't know what these Yelpers are sayin about no flavor... I surely did not have that experience.  These puppies were devoured in no time flat.  Good thing they are not in my usual stomping grounds.  I'm chubby enough.....

I really, really wanted to like the cupcakes from this cute roach-coach.  The young lady in the coach was super friendly with a great smile.  I was all set to love the CupKates.  That was until I accidentally touched the frosting on my red-velvet and noticed it was goopy, and not in a good way.  I'm used to rich, creamy, velvety smooth frosting like on Miette cupcakes.  I put aside my reservations and decided to bite into the cupcake and give it a try.  It was aaiigght, like your basic store bought cupcake.  No real flavor, just sweet.  I certainly wont brave the Off the Grid crowd just for a CupKate.  Even my boyfriend who only eats because he has to, said CupKate was eh, okay (he had the double chocolate).  His comment was "Miette is still way better".  And he's right.  Today I'll be trying out Love at First Bite Bakery - heard they have good cupcakes.  Wish me luck!!  :D

I want to give them a 5 star for the awesome tastiness of their red velvet cupcakes, but a few customer service errors took away from my experience with these folks. 

I've only heard of Cupkates through my friends, so I was really excited to see one near the corner of my office. They recommended me the following two cupcakes:

Red Velvet Cupcake
Caramel Salted Cupcake

The Red Velvet cupcake was absolutely a bomb. I was nodding my head at how good it was as soon as it entered my mouth. The base cake was moist and sweetened just right to complement the sweeter tangy topping that was provided with it. At $3.00 a piece, it was pretty worth it if your into sweets.

I can't exactly say the same for the salted caramel cupcake. Although the chocolate cake was moist, I didn't really like caramel topping that was paired with it. It may be my own personal preference, but I found myself eating the base with the filling from the Red Velvet Cupcake.

I knocked off a star because of how they packaged my cupcakes. They put your cupcakes in a nice 4 by 4 inches box. However, if you only order two items, you're left without a cupcake holder. By the time I walked to my car, I found one of my cakes knocked over with its filling bleeding over the entire box. It was like a murder scene. My cupcake just died. The cashier gave no warning as to handle the box carefully. This would really suck if you were bringing these cupcakes for a special girl. 

Otherwise, on the product alone, the cupcakes were awesome. They had a variety of flavors you can try. Make sure to give it a shot.

So after trying Icing on the Cake at Los Gatos, I had to write an update. I still LOVE cupkates, don't get me wrong, but I think Icing on the Cake has a more not-as-sugary flavor, just the way I like it. But honestly, I would never pass up on opportunity to get a Cupkates cupcake when they're in the area.
Serendipity!

The cupcakes are okay. What I dont like is their frosting. It's rather greasy and light and it's not solid enough. It's very much like eating sweeten butter.  You have to hold the box very carefully or else the whole chunk of  frosting would fall off from the cake.It's kinda messy.

The Red velvet is good though.The frosting of red velvet doesn't taste like what I mention above. If you want to try,get the red velvet!

Congratulations Cupkates! Your cupcakes were so incredible I decided to make you the subject of my first yelp review ever! :) I had a red velvet at Off the Grid tonight and a spicy mexican chocolate later on - OH.MY.GOODNESS. They tasted so FRESH and were rich, moist, full of flavor - truly excellent. Well done and I will be back!

This is hands down the best cupcake I've ever tasted. I was in love at first bite.  Normally, I would scrape the frosting off my cupcakes since frosting tends to be too sweet and thick.  This frosting is light and fluffy, just the perfect amount of sweetness and the cake is so moist. 

I haven't tried them all but the Red Velvet and Salted Caramel are delicious! I'll usually split a few different flavors with others so I get a bit of everything. 

I'll be back soon for more...save me a spot in line.

The Cupkates truck is a sight I miss seeing by the Berkeley campus, but I'm probably better off without these convenient treats!  My favorites were the moist red velvet cupcakes (it was always a competition to get the last one of these in the afternoon) and the odd salted caramel.  The big weird buttery cream dollop on top of each cupcake is what sets these apart from other cake-eating experiences.  Once you've licked that off, well, it's just a piece of cake.

My life has changed. The minute I tried my first bite of salted caramel, I knew there was no going back! This mobile cupcake bakery parks by my work in Oakland once a week. I heard about it through some coworkers, but I was skeptical, bc everyone makes cupcakes now. 

But the cupcakes are so moist and the frosting, just right. It is an after lunch dessert and I have to say I am hooked! Try tiramisu if you are a fan of the dessert, but my first recommendation is the salted caramel if you are into the salty sweet combo.

The first time I had the Tiramisu cupcakes from CUPKATES...OMG..let me tell you...it was soooo GOOD.  I only wanted to eat half and save the other half for later, but I couldn't stop.  I don't normally like the frosting on cakes or cupcakes because it's too sweet for my taste, but not the ones from Cupkates.  I can't wait til lunch time because I'm going to stop by to get some red velvet and salted carmel.  I've been craving for the cupcakes all week.

so there were things i really liked and some things that weren't so great.  we got the salted caramel and the chocolate peanut btuter cupcakes.  the cake was delicious - moist, fluffy, and very chocolaty but not overwhelmening.  the salted caramel frosting was not particularly flavorful and actually just kind of tasted like sugar.  the peanut butter frosting was great, though.  my biggest complaint was the ratio of cupcake to frosting...there was WAY too much frosting for an average sized cupcake.

service was friendly.  i want to try the tiramisu next time (they were out last time).

So damn good. Most recently I had the salted caramel, but all of their flavors are great! They are in Emeryville most Tuesdays, and I actually try to avoid the area because if I walk by Cupkates, I just cannot resist!

I really want to LOVE and 5-Star Cupkates...for the concept, for the name, for their creativity with the menu and for my appreciation of cupcakes, BUT I've given it 3 chances and tried 3 different cupcakes (Salted Caramel, Strawberry Rhubarb & Mango) and all three times the frosting has disappointed me.  It's been overpoweringly buttery in my opinion...and I am a lover of butter.  But not atop my cupcake.  That's my only complaint.  The frosting.

These are the most amazing and delicious cupcakes I have ever tasted! The truck is so cute and Kate herself is extremely nice!  I will definitely be following the Cupkates truck around every time I am in the area.  You will not regret making a visit for sweet treat or two!

Okay so I tried cupkates for the first time two weeks ago!! to be honest I wasn't to impressed with the flavors I chose, the Red Velvet was the best out of their most popular "Salted caramel", vanilla, or chocolate peanut butter.  Speaking of the chocolate/peanutbutter.  If your expecting the "reeses flavor" your not gonna get it, your gonna get a spoonful of Jiff, tastes exactly like peanut out the jar, not a bad thing if that's what you like, I myself prefer reeses flavor.  So I went again today because I really love cupcakes and I wanted to try a different flavor.  So I got the smores and GOT DAMN THAT CUPCAKE IS THE BOMB, marshmellow icing, with a chocolate cake with real ghram cracker peices at the bottom.  IF YOU EVER VISIT HER GET THE SMORES.  i am also excited because their flavor of the day is chocolate peppermint which is another one of my favorite flavor combo's.  havn't ate those yet I will update my review after lunch!!! b OKAY SO IM HERE TO UPDATE MY REVIEW.  SO NO BIGGIE THAT I DON'T PREFER THE FLAVORS I MENTIONED AT THE TOP, HOWEVER KATE HAS A MILLION OTHER FLAVORS THAT ARE BOMB! LEMON MERIANGE, KEYLIME PIE(YET TO TASTE) HER VANILLA IS BOMB! WORTH EVERYBIT OF THE $3.00! I HEART CUPKATES CHANGING MY RATING TO A 5 STAR!
S'mores cupcake with toasted marshmallow topping, chocolate cake and graham cracker crust. Yum!

Saw them at off the grid and got a tiramisu and red velvet. 
The red velvet was alright but the tiramisu was amazing! It tasted just like tiramisu and it wasn't overly sweet and the frosting was nice and light, so was the cake. Just writing this review is making crave another one!

Can't wait to find them again and try the smores!

Oh yeah! Went to 4th street in Berkeley just to rendezvous with this cake truck.  I left my house in Oakland at 12:30PM and by the time I parked and got in line, they were already out of 3 of the 6 flavors (good-bye lemon, double-vanilla, and smores).  I knew that the double chocolate was next to go.  Sure enough, the guy in front of me bought the last few.

I walked away with one red velvet and one twinkie.  Somehow I managed to keep them in their box until after dinner.  I need to try the double vanilla and double chocolate next!

I was out here on a Friday for Off the Grid at Civic Center and I brought my lunch. My friends convinced me that I should come out and I ended up buying the Tiramisu cupcake and it was good. 

The breakdown: The cake was moist, the frosting was fluffy, and the graham cracker crust reminds me of the bottom layer of a cheesecake. $3 a cupcake isn't bad. Would come back again if they came around again.

Kate's is pretty great.  I've visited her truck in downtown Oakland and Berkeley and had fantastic experiences both times.  The chocolate ($2.75) is rich and not too sweet.  The salted caramel ($3) is indeed salty, with fatty salt granules on top of luscious caramel frosting, topping a chocolate cupcake.  There is also a generous amount of frosting on each cupcake.  I'll only give 4 stars because, for the size of the cupcake, I wouldn't mind them being cheaper - maybe at $2.50.  But the price hasn't stopped me yet.

I finally got to try the tiramisu cupcake!!!! 

Tiramisu Cupcake. YUMMY! I love tiramisu! It's one of my favorite types of cake ever, so I loved how they were able to put everything I like about tiramisu into a little cupcake, even up to the coffee liquor. I definitely liked how light the frosting was, I think it was just like sweetened whipped cream since I hate heavy and overly sweet frostings.

See photos of food, http://potbellypanda.tumblr.com
Not much of a cupkate eater but it is the best I have eva had.

AHmazing! I've never been to a cupcake truck before, though, my co-workers have shared their treasures from fellow trucks. I had the salted caramel and my husband had the smores cupcake! They were so moist and the frosting was just delectable! I couldn't stop eating the frosting even if I wanted to. The smores one had a graham cracker in the bottom and the marshmallow had been torched YUMMY! I can't have cupcakes each week, Every Wednesday they will be there but I will definitely stay tuned!  I LOVE gourmet cupcakes =-)

Cupcakes here are really good. I got a Vanilla Bean one and liked it a lot. It was quite rich. I also got some cupcakes for my coworkers and they enjoyed them as well.  

Minus one star because the guy selling them could have been a little bit nicer.

One of my absolute favorite places to get a cupcake.

This truck has a tendency to come by the UC campus on Tuesday/Thursday, parked right on Durant Avenue between Telegraph.

Their RED VELVET is absolutely amazing.  It's moist, yet has a slight crunch to its top layer.  Frosting in general is too much, but the cake itself is so delicious.

I decided to explore their other options, DOUBLE VANILLA. OMG this cupcake is to die for.  Like I said early, I dont like frosting.  But this frosting was so creamy, rich and light at the same time.  You can see the crushed vanilla beans in the frosting.  Similar to the RED VELVET, their cakes are always moist.

Sometimes I dont consume the cupcake immediately, but these cupcakes LAST.  They're just as good the next day, and they dont lose their freshness.

I wish they made Carrot Cupcake. hmmm, that would be awesome!

I managed to be first in line for my first try with Cupkates.  Happily I waited until the truck window was opened by very friendly staffers.  I ordered 2 of everything just so we could double test.  I don't think it's fair to judge sweets by one taste  and it prolongs the joy of the whole thing!
Anyway, I bought the Key Lime, Salted Caramel, Tiramisu and S'mores.
We decided to be a little more cautious and split two cupcakes, each trying a piece.  What a heavnly surpirse the Key Lime was!  As well as the Tiramisu and S'mores!.  I am on a low salt diet so the Caramel was a tad bit too salty for me, but it was still very, very good and anyone who can eat normal amounts of salt should enjoy this cupcake fully as well.
The cupcakes are $3.  It is a special treat.  I wouldn't recomend sending your kids to school with these in their lunches.  Just too expensive to do that.  But if you're out and about in Berkeley on a Sunday afternoon, down on 4th street and you feel like being good to yourself out in public, Cupkates fits the bill.   Yes, I would recommend them to my friends and I will be back.  The food is honest, homemade quality that is so much better than what mom use to make.

Update: She has Lemon Raspberry and Pumpkin Spice at the moment, which are tremendous.  Her "blue velvet" for Cal game days are also fun and yummy.

Kate rocks.  The End.

I don't think I've ever been blown away by a cupcake before.  There's a first for everything though right?  I kind of wish I never tasted their cupcakes so that I don't have to think about it when I'm craving sweets.

I ordered the salted caramel.  My two friends had a tiramisu and a red velvet.  At first, I was reluctant to try the salted caramel.  I usually avoid anything caramel because they're almost always too sweet for my palate.  But I decided to trust the vendor that day.  Needless to say, I was impressed by the perfect blend of sweet and salty.  The frosting was topped with sprinkles of sea salt that added that crunch to every bite of the cupcake.  The tiramisu also had a striking feature... a ladyfinger crust lined the bottom, similar to what you would find in a regular tiramisu!  All the cupcakes were moist and delectable.

Now I find myself checking Cupkates' website to see where their truck locations will be for the week.
Sweet, divine, moist, beautiful, velvety, delectable, heavenly... I literally floated back to work with a big smile on my face.

I had the salted caramel cupcake from this truck. I was just working near this truck for a couple of weeks only, but people at the office were talking about a cupcake truck. A cupcake truck? I have never seen one before.

Someone bought this cake for me. This cake had a buttermilk frosting. It was perfect. Not too sweet, but very creamy. On top of the frosting were drizzles of caramel and a couple of flakes of salt. 

I only took one star away because the cake itself was too moist for my tasting.

The special day arrived when Cupkates was in my 'hood.  Oh. My. Heck.  The flavors for the day: salted caramel, vanilla chocolate, lemon raspberry, s'mores, red velvet, caramel banana, twinkie, double chocolate and double vanilla.

The hubs and I each picked one and we shared.  Mine: salted caramel, His: lemon raspberry.  Both were divine.  While I'm a devoted lover of chocolate, the deliciousness of the lemon raspberry was EVEN BETTER than chocolate.  The lemon cake was fluffy, light, faintly sweet and completely lemony.  The raspberry icing took the cake (pun intended).  A rich, pink cloud atop the cupcake that tasted like a creamy interpretation of fresh raspberry preserves. 

This is not to say the salted chocolate cupcake was anything short of delicious.  The chocolate cake was moist, rich and so good I wanted to lick the wrapper to get every last bit.  The caramel icing had the rich warmth of toasted caramel that I enjoy (definitely NOT the overly sweet trash that burns the back of the throat).  Topped with flecks of sea salt, the cupcake was perfect.

Decided to hit up this adorable truck on 4th St in Berkeley this last weekend. 

Tiramisu- YEAH!
Salted Caramel- WOW!
S'Mores- OMFG!!!!!!!

The cake was very moist, rich in flavor. The attention to detail (ex. rock salt on the salted caramel frosting) was amazing. But what really blew me away was when you take a bite you think, oh that's nice and then BAM I mean BAAMMMM the flavors explode!!! So freaking good!

Honestly, Cupkates's tiramisu cupcake is the best cupcake I've ever eaten - yes, EVER.  And I've eaten a lot of cupcakes. 

The cake is perfect; it's not too heavy (take a note, Sprinkles), and it's not at all dry.  Similarly, the frosting is stellar.  I know there are frosting people out there - you know, those of you who are ordering shots of frosting and such at these places.  I happen to dislike most frostings, but I seriously could've had a cup of this frosting by itself.  

Words cannot do this cupcake justice.  Find the truck (we caught it on Shattuck last Wednesday afternoon), and get crazy.

I've been looking for some competition for my usual cupcake spot and here we go!
The red velvet... the icing.. the CAKE.. the goodness! Their red velvet is delicious!! I always make sure I walk away with one if I go to Off The Grid. The icing is light yet sweet and not overpowering. The cake portion isn't dull at all. Rich in flavor and makes my taste buds happy :)
The tiramisu cupcake wasn't my thing, but I am looking forward to coming back here and trying the rest of the flavors!
Great, friendly service! Really take in their customers' needs and I appreciate that.

5 stars because that red velvet cupcake is a Disneyland electrical parade in my mouth and the service is on point.

The first time I had the s'mores cupcake, I was disappointed. Too rich and the cake not moist enough.

The second time--I decided to give them one more chance--I was HOOKED! The Salted Caramel cupcakes are De-li-cious, making me wish I had gotten another one, but the long lines on Fourth Street (in Berkeley), where the truck was parked, deterred me. My friend almost had an orgasm licking and nibbling on the delicate, extremely moist cake, excited by the salty-and-sweet combo of the generous dollop of cream on top, doused with salty caramel. 

Sign up on Twitter and/or Facebook to find out where the Cupkates truck will be when you're hankering for delicious cupcakes. 

Next time, I plan to buy these flavors: Twinkie,  Lemon Raspberry, and Red Velvet.
It's a cupcake. It's good. It's $3. I recognize her fans...all good, but there was nothing 'amazing'.

mmmm! it's so good that after I ate the cupcake, I scraped the liner paper with my teeth and licked the frosting on the bag...and geez, this was at work in my cubicle, hopefully nobody was looking but I didn't care cuz it was that tasty! 'nuff said.

I've tried the twinkie, strawberry swirl and s'more flavors. My favorite is the twinkie so far. It just might be that I am partial to yellow cake. I thought the strawberry swirl was too cream cheesy and the s'more wasn't all that special. 

Knocked them off 1 star since it is a bit pricey at $3 for a pretty small cupcake. But to be fair, this seems to be the going rate for a gourmet cupcake like Kara's or Sprinkles. So relatively speaking, it's a comparable price. I guess I just expected a slight price cut since there should be less overhead operating out of a truck.
i'm not to big on sweets, but the smores cupcake is awesome! yes, i said awesome!

Great Kates, and a very smart delivery system! Thanks for bringing Cupkates to our neighborhood.
Red Velvet!!

Best Cupcakes! Tiramisu, Red Velvet, Key Lime Pie they are ALL good. I make a good cupcake but don't always have the time. These recipes are inventive and tasty, sweet but not too sweet.

I tried another cupcake place on Filmore the other night and was sadly disappointed. The place was nothing compared to Cupkates! I won't stray again! THIS IS THE PLACE!

Sometimes a little hard to locate.  Sometimes a long line.  Sometimes sold out.  Moist cupcakes.  Tiramasu cupcake was very good.  Needs to be refrigerated or eaten asap.  Red Velvet is "ok".  The salted caramel was disappointing.  I wanted more salt and more caramel.

I'm a super fan of cupcakes and have tried cupcake shops up and down CA.  Cupkates ranks as one of the top.  The Salted Caramel, S'mores, and Red Velvet are my favorites.  Nothing compares to Sibby's though, she still makes 'em the best.

1 star for the service
2nd star for the flavors 
3rd star for the decent price

I've tried the salted caramel, key lime pie, Guinness chocolate, smores, and red velvet cupcakes, and the best one is the Guinness chocolate and salted caramel. I was hoping after chasing down this cupcake truck that they were goin to be blow my face off good, but sadly they just fixed my cupcake craving. I really liked the Guinness because it was super moist and not too sweet, and not over topped with frosting.
Creamy frosting.....moist cake.....mmmmm.  Wish they served milk cartons too :/

I have a weakness for red velvet cupcakes, and these are one of the best around!  Super moist and rich with the perfect hint of chocolate, while the cream cheese frosting is light and tangy.  DELISH!

However, I would not recommend the s'mores cupcake.  It tasted bitter and oily, while the marshmallow frosting was overly sweet.  

**For my full review on foodtrucks around SF, visit my blog link under my profile. Enjoy!**

So I finally tried their cupcakes and I gotta say this is the best damn cupcake ever! These treats are surprisingly moist and not dry like most cupcakes.  It's definitely a preference thing but if you like sweet moist cake, then you'll definitely love this place.  I love the variety they have and they have monthly specials too so you'll always be coming back for more.  So far my fave is the salted caramel, tiramisu & chocolate peppermint (Dec only)...looking forward to trying their January flavor, Banana Cream Pie.  Since they're food trucks, you can follow them on twitter or check out their website for updates/locations.  Also, the best part they're totally affordable! Each cupcake is $3 which is the perfect price for the perfect afternoon snack ;-)
What a cute idea for selling cupcakes - via a roaming mobile truck. My favorites are red velvet, key lime pie.  I'm glad they come to a neighborhood near me.

These are the absolute best cupcakes.  The flavors are amazing, the cake is always moist, and the frosting is delicious.  These treats are well worth the lines....and show up early so you can try all of the best flavors!

Carmel Apple, Septembers flavor, is phenomenal.  I wish they would make them year round.

I finally was able to try Kates cupcakes...and WOW! My hubby  surprised me with four cupcakes, two red velvet, a s'mores, and a twinkie cupcake. 

They are so cute, the cake is deliciously moist. The frosting, is so light and airy and absolutely delicious. I could see specks of real vanilla bean in the cake. You can tell she uses high quality ingredients. 

My favorite was the twinkie, it tasted better then a twinkie...it was just delicious. I just wish she could come down a little bit, like Hayward/San Leandro area!

Thank you Kate for sharing your wonderful gift of baking with all of us, i look forward to trying many more :o)

Yum!  I had an old coworker who brought me Cupkates from the Richmond Farmer's Market (Wednesday night).  He brought in four cupcakes that I was to share among coworkers: tiramisu, red velvet, s'mores, and strawberry rhubarb (seasonal).  I decided to be the adventurous one and go for the strawberry rhubarb.  It looked a little oily-moist, but it was delicious!  I sort of surprised myself as I tend to try classics from a place before branching out for their more adventurous or seasonal tastes.  Nevertheless, it was very good.

Side note: I was told to eat the cupcake within 24 hours before the butter in the buttercream went bad.  Be mindful of this as you purchase.

Yes, please!

I've tried the pumpkin spice and red velvet and am raring to try the s'more and chocolate.  I will catch her again one of these days...

Her red velvet may the best I've ever had (thus far).  And I've had a lot. ;)

Salted Caramel Crack.

I'd review the other flavors but I'm too Pookie-ish when it comes to the Salted Caramel and I can't order anything else.

Across the street on Beale Street someone was selling in a white truck, cupcakes valued at 3.00 per cake.

My buddy Richard and I ordered
Red Velvet
2 Salted caramel Cupcakes

Cakes are moist, tender and not dry
Frosting is light, not overly sweet
The best thing is the cupcake is not cloyingly sweet.

We will be back. The people in my office ran to get their cupcakes. We started a trend.

i get super happy whenever i see a cupkates truck around, whether it's at an off the grid event or while i'm randomly walking around in berkeley (this happens less often, but still). how can you not?! 

i've had several flavors at cupkates, but my favorite is the salted caramel. one, i tend to love anything salted caramel. two, the cake is super moist and there is a little bit of caramel drizzled on top with little chunks of salt in them to add just the right balance of sweet and salty. total deliciousness!

i also like the tiramisu (tastes just like the real thing!!!) and the red velvet (yum!).

i love that the cake part in the cupcakes here are moist and fluffy, and not muffin-like as some cupcakes tend to be. and i LOVE the frosting - it's light, buttery and has JUST the right amount of sweetness - i don't feel like i'm eating a whole carton of sugar like the frosting of SOME places.

definitely get a cupcake if you see them around!!

Cupcakes on wheels!  YAY!  We grabbed half a dozen, and were in-the-know enough to arrive early and get in the already-ridiculous line.  These things are no joke!  Watch out for snarky soccer moms wanting to buy the place out for their 4-year-olds.  We got red velvet, salted caramel, s'mores, twinkie, double chocolate, and double vanilla.  My favorites turned out to be the s'mores, salted caramel and red velvet.  So hard to choose one.  I can handle paying $3 for a cupcake, standing in line, and playing shell game with their locations, but I can't really say I enjoy the lack of a purchase limit.  I've heard on more than one occasion of someone showing up and buying 24 cupcakes, thereby ruining everyone else's afternoon and totally depleting the option of a couple of flavors.  It's sad to stand in line only to be turned away or told "sorry, no more s'mores."  But that won't stand in the way of a 5-star rating.  These folks are great!  And the 'cakes aren't bad, either.  ;)

Thumbs up to the strawberry cupcake here!
I was pleasantly surprised that it tasted good.
I liked it the most out of the twinkle, salted caramel and raspberry.

adding PEPPERMINT CHOCOLATE to the wonderful list of favorites! 

love, love, love!

I go to Off The Grid by Kezar Stadium every Thursday for dinner and this place is GREAT for dessert. The cupcakes are the best I've had period! And I've tried every cupcake in town. Love all of the flavors. Esp. Red Velvet and Salted Caramel.

Cupkates magical truck was parked near my office. I saw the long line and decided to see what the fuss was all about! AMAZING CUPCAKES! I have driven to may different places for good cupcakes and was disappointed. Cupkates are light, moist, and delightful. Salted caramel and raspberry lemon cupcakes are my favorites. At $3.00 a cupcake it is well worth it.

oh cupkates darlin!
I tried your newest vanilla bean cheesecake and it did not disappoint, except for the sort of soggy graham cracker crust, but i understand why it got that way. One word: delicious!

I will adore your salted caramel and tiramisu cupcakes till I die. Consistent and so good it'd want to make you smack your momma~ (oops, Happy Mother's Day!)

I brought 3 cupcakes yesturday @ Oakland. I tried the Red velvet, salted caramel and tiramisu flavors. Cupcakes are ok, but $3.00 per cupecake is kind of over price. I think the cupcakes @ nobhill taste alot better and is cheaper. For first time ok, will I try again? No.

3.5  stars!

These cupcakes are delicious! I didn't have high expectations for these cupcakes because it was from a truck, but boy was I wrong! These cupcakes are moist and not too sweet. 

However, it's hard to catch them! They're not at the same place everyday, so keep your eyes open!
Their cupcakes are good and readily available in FiDi. Chocolate cake was moist and delicious. Chocolate frosting was rich and creamy (could have used more).

Crazy how you can get cupcakes from a truck!

Anyways, they are usually roaming around Emeryville, Oakland, or at OTG in San Francisco!

Love all their cupcakes..especially their S'Mores! They always have a new crazy flavor on their menu..

Only thing is...the frosting is a bit much. It looks GREAT...but i can't eat that much of it.

better than Kara's & Sprinkles.

4.5 stars! Rounded up because there was a family in front of me in line and after they had bought their cupcakes one of the kids accidentally dropped her red velvet on the ground and was visibly devastated. The lovely Cupkate's lady replaced it quickly with a huge smile on her face. The kid walked off elated with the balance of the universe restored. 

Have tried the red velvet, salted caramel, and tiramisu. All of them have been delectably moist and sweet. Just a week beforehand I got to try my first sprinkles red velvet cupcake. In comparison I would go with cupkates hands down. Sprinkles was much too decadent and dense for me in cake and frosting. I like the balance of cupkates' cupcakes much more with the texture and taste being more light and delicate. 

In order of preference: Cupkates, Teacake, Sprinkles.

Cupcakes in a truck?! What a fantastic idea! On Thursdays, they park right in front of my fav nail shop. It took a while for me to decide to break from my diet for the day and get some cupcakes.

Boy, was I pleased! I got a s'mores and a double vanilla. The s'mores was so delicious! In college, I used to microwave s'mores in the microwave, so I'm used to non-crunchy s'mores. This was soft, and fluffy, and just sweet enough. It's not as sweet as regular s'mores. I know kids love cupcakes, but this is s'mores is for the growed ups!

The double vanilla wasn't anything to write home about. The icing had the aftertaste of too much vanilla extract. My gf tried to eat the icing first, then the cupcake. I explained to her that they were supposed to be eaten together. That way, the cakiness buffers the alcoholic aftertaste. I probably won't get it again for the price. But it was still delicious.

Next time, I want to try the tiramisu. Or some of their many other kinds. Yes, there will be a next time because the nail shop is within walking distance from my house.

I've only tried the S'mores and Salted Caramel. I think both were good but not the best I've ever had.

The S'mores (overall) was too sweet for my liking but I thought the graham cracker bottom and marshmallow top were awesome. The Salted Caramel had a little bit too much salt on top but the cake was moist and good. ^_^

Not only is Cupkates the latest in a trend of interestingly flavored cupcakes, it is also a mobile eatery.

So far I've tried the Salted Caramel, Red Velvet, Double Vanilla, and Key Lime.  The Salted Caramel was really good, I love the combination of sweet and salty.  I also loved the Double Vanilla because I love anything with Vanilla Beans.  The Key Lime was different--they actually have a graham cracker bottom and some key lime jelly.  I loved it as well.  Red Velvet didn't go over so well with me (still think Marita's Sweet Potato Pie Co. is better).  The cakes are moist and their frosting is not too heavy.

In general I think their cupcakes are good, but I've been to Sprinkles and various other cupcake boutiques on the east and west coast.  I think they're good, but I've had some pretty mind-blowing cupcakes elsewhere.

They take credit cards, and that's always a plus!

I'm in love with a CupKates, cupcakes.  YUMMY!  My friend and I went to look for the Kara cupcake KaraVan but ran into the CupKates.  So we decided to try them out.  Both my friend and I order two cupcakes each.   We both ordered the Carmel Salted cupcake.  Chocolate cake with cream salted caramel.  DELICIOUS!  The other cupcake that I ordered was the Coconut Cream; a coconut cake with coconut filling and cream frosting.  I have died and gone to heaven.  That was the best coconut cupcake I have ever eaten and I'm from the South.  Love coconut cream cake.  My friend ordered the Strawberry Rhubarb.  OMG, so good!  Yes, I gave her a taste of my coconut cream and she gave me a taste of her strawberry rhubarb.  All I have to say is if you like cupcakes, and haven't tried CupKates, please do so.  You will not be disappointed.

full flavored cup cakes! These are so scrumptious, I ended up eating 3 the first time. At least I tried 3 different cup cakes and didn't eat all 3 the same as I had wanted to. After noticing an image below, I guess there is a chance that your cup cakes might fall over in your box if you aren't careful (I did notice a little swaying of my cupcakes as I vigorously walked home). But that's easily avoidable, as mine never actually fell over.
Holy jesus mother of cupcakes these are good!

mmm mmm MMM! s'more, PLEASE!

As my bf and my friend were strolling down 4th street, waiting on breakfast, we stumbled upon this oh so very cool cupcake truck parked along the side of the street.

Me:  Cupcake for pre-breakfast?!
BF & Friend: OK, let's do it!  

so, we rushed over to the truck immediately.

I approached the truck with a very low expectation because cupcakes are just cupcakes.  we ordered 3 flavors, and they were salted carmel, redvelvet, and the smore.  On the spot, we tried it, and it was delicious!!  two thumbs up for the smores flavored cupcake!  its unique because at the very bottom it contains, i believe, a grahm cracker and on the very top.. instead of frosting.. its a toasted marshmellow!!  the cupcakes were very moist and not too sweet.  it had the perfect amount of frosting, as well.  makes me want moreee just thinking about it!

it was so good that we went back for more!  bought a whole bunch for us and for our friends and family back in san jose. 

The cupcakes were about $3.  I just wish it were a little bigger for costing 3 bucks. =P  but, still...i was happy with them regardless. =)

they accept visa, which is pretty convenient for a truck!

"sigh" if only berkeley wasnt sucha  far drive from me....=(

I was visiting SF by way of San Diego and I chased this truck to Berkeley where we ordered a salted caramel  cupcake and a banana cream cupcake. The banana cream was BOMB! I am the worlds chocolatiest chocolate lover, but that banana cream cupcake was the best treat of my trip! The salted caramel was a dark chocolate cupcake with a salted caramel frosting. I loved the cake, not so sure about the frosting. If I am ever in the area again, I will definately hunt them down again!

The cakes are wonderful, but a special heartfelt thanks to Cupkates for having peanut-free products, and employees (owners?) who know enough about the ingredients, production and facilities to assure a seriously allergic 12-year-old that the cakes were safe for her to eat. This is a kid who usually misses out on treats, so finding your truck and friendly employees made her day, and mine, too. We splurged on 8 cupkates, so she could take some home. Thank you!

I have learned to love CupKates....Partly because she is one of the only games in town and ALSO because of the lusty salted caramel cupcake!! I SO wish she would come to EL CERRITO, ALBANY, OR anywhere else other than Berkeley- It's closer to me- Just being selfish and thinking of my self first! Ha! She is also a wee bit pricey...but hey...its good and especially when going to off the grid...its the nicest treat!

Love the concept of a traveling bakeshop on wheels and a fair price for a cupcake.  The red velvet and key lime are really good.  The others that I tried were not so memorable.  I would prefer more cake and a little less icing.  (My daughter agrees)  I would definitely check them out on twitter, find out where they are going to be and try more.
You have to try the Salted Caramel cupcake. Sooooo yummy, and only $3 a cupcake. I also enjoyed the Double Vanilla, but will continue to get the Salted Caramel. ahhh. looove them.
Yum, my employer brought them in as a treat.  The red velvet cupcake was outstanding.  The salted caramel was too sweet for me.  Highly recommended.
BEST cupcakes - EVER!!! ... I can never walk away without buying at least half a dozen...

I, like a lot of people, am all for the cupcake revolution. These cupcakes are absolute perfection, totally worth chasing down as often as possible.  The cake is moist, the icing is not too sweet and perfect density. I haven't tasted one I didn't like!

Let me start off with the fact that I'm a picky cupcake person. I was super excited to see this cupcake truck at Off The Grid. I stood in the super long line waiting for the perfect sweet ending to my gorge-fest. Unfortunately I was disappointed. The cake consistency was a bit dense and not very moist. The frosting was what really took it down a notch. It was way too sweet, and not the creamy or fluffy complement that it should be. It was also swirled on top which made it super difficult to distribute and get an even ratio of cake and frosting per bite. Not a convert.
best cupcake i've ever had?? maybe! red velvet.......

I love Cupkates! I have tried almost every flavor and the Lemon Raspberry, Key Lime Pie, and Salted Caramel are my favorites. The cake is always super moist and I love the impossibly light and creaming frosting. To find the truck check Twitter or Facebook, and try to get there right when they open to ensure that you get the flavors you want.

I  like the Twinkie and Lemon Raspberry.   The Vanilla cupcake with strawberry frosting was very good  but it's not in their regular menu.  Cupkates so goooood.................I've followed  their truck in Oakland - Berkeley neighborhood till I've tried all the flavors !

I finally got to taste they delish creations after reading about it in a recent Yelp Newsletter. I followed them on Twitter and went on a little adventure to truck them down!! 

I wanted to try all of them but narrowed down my picks"
-Salted Caramel.. it was a moist chocolate cake with caramel frosting with sea salt. I like how the cupcake and frosting are not overly sweet.  My fave and a must try.

-Twinkie.. a vanilla bean cupcake filled with a marshmallow creme and then topped with marshmallow frosting! MARSHMALLOW OVER LOAD!! But it was good. The cake was dense and the top part of the cake had a little crunch.

-Red Velvet.. Standard

-Double Chocolate.. very rich chocolate cake and frosting. Highly recommend for those who have a sweet tooth.

The cupcakes are a little smaller than other cupcakes I have bought. But they pack a good punch. There cupcake is a different texture too. Its more dense and airy then moist and fluffy. Maybe it is just me. At 3 dollars a cupcake you may think we are insane to pay such a price but seeing the line we knew it had to be good.

No cash? Do not worry. They accept VISA!! HOLLA!

Clearly Cupkates needs no more help, every one loves em!

My favorites thus far: Smores, for the slightly flambeed marshmellow topping and graham bottom; salted caramel & of course the red velvet.  $3 is pretty gosh darn reasonable for food truck food, but man oh man, you inspire me to whip up my own! 

If you wanna make a whole lotta people happy, order a lot--like a dozen--the packaging when you close to a dozen is so well thought out, with a cardboard cupcake form so that each perfect lil cake is all nestled in safety to be devoured later!

Third time worked! I hauled coworkers down to Jack London Square today - I think they were starting to doubt the existence of this truck. One by one they dropped off as the wait got longer and longer...they ran out of a couple of the most awesome flavors but I still brought back an excellent assortment. Banana Nutella- NOM. Vanilla/vanilla - super awesome with real vanilla bean flecks. AND Kate gave me a free cupcake for my sad stalking efforts earlier. Love it!

I had the double chocolate and smores today.  The double chocolate was better than the smore, which was basically the chocolate cupcake with a graham cracker crust and marshmallow for icing.  The icing on the chocolate isn't exactly they way I like it, but it wasn't bad, i.e. too sugary.  I love that this truck comes near my house in Emeryville on a regular basis. I'll be a Facebook follower for sure and try the other flavors.
The best cupcake truck in town! Fleur du sel, smores, chocolate peanut butter - delectable. I usually find them over on 12th and broadway...check them out during your lunch break!

Saw this place on the way to work and had to try it out because I wanted to see if they were as good as sprinkles, loves or teacake bake shop in the bay area..

I only ordered the red velvet just to try and surprisingly.. I felt this place held up.. it does look a little smaller, but the prices are comparable to most at $3.

Totally moist and tasty cake with good frosting.

They seem to give you a lot more frosting, but the overall taste was pretty good.. easy 4 stars.

Also, they accept credit cards.. convenient.  Nice.

One note on their truck window presentation..
Obviously when you go to the brick/mortar stores.. they look much nicer and you feel better with their nice walls all around you..

Here, theres minimal flash.. but youre there for the cake rite?

I was on my way to a doctors appointment in Oakland when I walked right buy Cup Kates. My mind recalled reading an article somewhere about them....hmm well might as well try it. Turned around and gladly gave 3 dollars for the treat that caught my eye. A delectable Devils Food-cake, the frosting was as tall as the cupcake in a soft-serve iceream style. First bite, the cheese cake of course! Homerun! Outa the park! Thank you Cup Kates for your love of cupcakes. My days have been brighter since.

They were across the street from my office yesterday and my coworkers convinced (not that they had to try) me to go with them.

I did not expect the Salted Caramel to be on a chocolate cupcake base.

I did not expect the S'mores and Key Lime Pie to have a graham cracker crust layer on the bottom.

You can get coconut added to the top of the Key Lime Pie, AND it also has a Key Lime pie filling in the center.

Oh my god. It is decadent, and pretty sophisticated--they are tasty but not overly sugary. Kids were bouncing around in line, too, but if I had any kids I would lie and tell them that it was an adult treat.

At $3 they're on the pricier side, but definitely worth the quality. Nice presentation packaging, too.

So I've been wanting try out cupkates for months now. The first time i went to look for the truck, they weren't there because it was drizzling that day....BOO..RAIN SUCKS!

Yesterday, My bbf and I went to the oakland location on 8th by laney and SCORE! We got:

3 red velvet and 2 salted caramel

Both flavors were YUMMY. not too sweet and VERY moist!. BFF said the cupcakes were a little small, but i didn't think so- perfect size for me(probably cause im not a sweets kinda girl)

definitely track them down and go get ur cupcaking on!!

It took me WEEKS to finally catch this cupcake truck.. I had to stake it out an hour earlier than it was scheduled to come, and as a little teen girl, it was pretty intimidating to try to keep my spot first in line with all the business people glaring at me :/

Since it was my first time, I wasn't sure what to order so I took a minute to think about it. The lady (Kate, I assume...) wasn't mean and didn't try to hurry me up or anything. I ordered the Red Velvet, Salted Caramel, and Double Chocolate. Each cupcake was $3 (Except for the Double Choc, $2.75) $3 is ridiculously expensive for a cupcake.. and it was really small, too. 

However, when I bit into each one, it was clear WHY they were $3 each... I don't know what recipe they have, but its SOLID.

I wouldn't go there again, except for maybe if I REALLY need a pick me up. $3 simply isn't economical for a 4 bite cupcake. However, I encourage you to try it out at least once, its a great experience!

This wonderful truck with tasty treats on wheels stopped by my job on Friday. One word: delicious. 

I had the lemon raspberry which tasted exactly as you might guess given the name and a red velvet cupcake. Both were moist and tasty. Icing was thick but not overbearing. 

Price seemed average, maybe even a little cheaper than other places that offer similar treats. 

Overall the next time the truck stops by I will have to try another cup-Kate. Yum.

I've taken to stalking Cupkates via facebook.  First of all, cupcakes in a truck?  Brilliant marketing.  Secondly, I'm a cake snob, and these cupcakes are awesome.  Seriously, these people are not messing around.  Third: Have I mentioned the cake?  Moist, perfect texture, not overly sweet or heavy.  They're also not too light, and the frosting to cake ratio is perfect.  Fourth--flavors!  Novelty, seasonal, classics--all a home run.  My personal favorites are the strawberry rhubarb, salted caramel, and s'mores.  And finally, the spontaneity of it all--the chance that you might run into the truck, the joy at actually doing so, and then having the ability to take cupcakes home.  Cupkates, I am so, so sold on your marvelously mobile masterpiece cupcakes.  (Thank you, too, for taking credit cards!)
Pumpkin Spice, twinkie, smores???those are cupcakes??? Why yes they are, and they are AMAZING!!!!!

I'm a huge fan of cupcakes in general, and their cupcakes taste great!! Their really moist (except for one that I recently encountered that was a tad bit dry) I usually catch them at different Off the Grid locations, mainly friday at Fort Mason.

Flavors of theirs that ive tried
1.) Red Velvet (OK)
2.) Salted Caramel (good but didn't have much of the salt taste til the very end)
3.) Strawberry Rhubarb (OK)
4.) Key Lime Pie (99% really moist and fun to eat with an explosion of diff flavors and textures & graham cracker crust...last one I had was pretty dry and kinda dissappointed)
5.) S'mores (GOOD!)
6.) Double Vanilla (Not a vanilla fan much but theirs is pretty good!!)
7.) Spicy Mexican (ugh AWESOME! I LOVE LOVE chocolate & spicy food, and the chocolate cake had a kick to it, pretty yum!)
8.) Tiramisu (EH, it was ok. I didn't get a coffee-ish taste til the very last bite, literally. Wouldn't order again)

Although I love to bake cupcakes at home, I will continue to keep buying from them occassionally. $3 for a cupcake a bit pricey but oh well!

Cupcakes were all the rage a year or two ago, so this truck and its subsequent cafe deals were right on trend. They're great cupcakes, but too much frosting for my taste. I'm a chocolate kind of gal, but people seemed to really go for the salted caramel. Definitely worth checking out. I think they sell these at the various Yali's Cafes in Berkeley.

Just tried for the first time while the truck was parked on California St. downtown San Francisco.  I had the double chocolate cupcake and it was much better than I expected.  Perfect texture and chocolatey.  The frosting was lovely too.  Not too heavy or sweet.  Really hit the spot.

I am writing this review as I am devouring two cupcakes from Cupkates!  Every time I see this truck on Durant when I'm walking home, it lights up my day and it's all I can do to not go over there and buy myself two cupcakes twice a week (I can never seem to just buy one cupcake...).  But since today was my graduation day, I am allowed. 

The red velvet is cake is a TINY bit on the dry side, although it is still light (compared to other denser cakes).  The cream cheese frosting is just the right amount of cream cheese tangy and sweet, and it complements the lightly cocoa-flavored cake very well.

The lemon raspberry was an interesting combination.  The cake was a bit dry, although it had the perfect sweet lemon taste that I love.  The raspberry frosting is very sweet and tastes almost like whipped raspberry yogurt from Yoplait.  Together it is an interesting combination, although I might have preferred the raspberry frosting paired with a chocolate or vanilla cake and the lemon cake paired with vanilla or lemon buttercream frosting instead.

Overall, great cupcakes!  Although not the best I've had, they're perfectly satisfying and up there in the rankings!  Plus they're driven around to be a block away from my apartment on the way home from lunch, and that's pretty much as convenient as it gets.

Okay.  Now my favorite cupcakery in the bay area--not overall; that honor goes to dessert club chikalicious in the east village NYC--but I prefer these to Kara's, That Takes the Cake, Cups and Cakes, and, narrowly, to Love at First Bite (that's a close call--but the fact that this truck parks near my office on occasion puts it over the edge).  I waited in line way too long today but it was worth it for my (amazing) salted caramel, peanut butter chocolate, banana nutella, and red velvet.  they weren't too sweet, and I usually am very picky about frosting, but loved all these.  kate is living the dream! (or at least, my dream)--delish!

A herald of angels and divine glow radiating from the truck beckoned me to this heavenly confection that is Cupkates...that and the throngs of people greedily waiting to devilishly devour these sinfully delicious cakes.

Without hesitation, I ordered the following flavors:
- Red Velvet (which is not created equally among cupcakeries).
- Double Chocolate
- Lemon Raspberry
- Key Lime
- Salted Caramel (try this one!)

Theses baked goodies are equally moist, delicately sweet and far from cloaked in fondant-like frosting, Cupkates is what I've been looking for and did *not* find at Sprinkles, Kara's and Tea Cakes.  The fact that they're local peeps is an added bonus.  They DO sell out quickly so do place an order for pick-up online.  There is a minimum order.  No cash on hand?  No problem.  Cards accepted.

Find them on Twitter and Facebook for their next location.  Enjoy!
they sell cupcakes people..... i have yet to try a bad one!

I only tried this place once, and I didn't think there was anything special about it. I got the red velvet and it was just OKAY. It wasn't bad, but like I said there was nothing special. Just tasted like a home-made cupcake anyone could've baked.

Really sorry excuse for a professional cupcake. I had the Salted Caramel and I will bet money that the cake batter is FROM A BOX! The frosting had so much shortening in it that it just tastes like an oily mess. I wanted to like this place but I was sadly disappointed.

Like the old-school ice cream trucks, this lady delivers cupcakes--and good ones at that!  Like others mentioned, the red velvet and salted caramel were the best.  I have had really good cupcakes, and these were right up there, just not the best I've had.  That said, you can't beat the excitement we all feel when she pulls into JLS (where i work) when everyone rushes to stand in line for her treats.  It's like being a kid all over again.

Place is very good.  I'm not into the dessert and cupcake trend, but decided to buy my workgroup some today.  I had to ask the owner (Kate I assume) what to get.  Red Velvet, Salted Caramel and Smores is what she told me to get.  I ate the Salted Caramel and it was really good.  The texture of the cupcake was perfect.  I could eat 3-4 of them.  Will go back and try other flavors.

Probably one of the best cupcakes I had despite the excessive oiliness that cannot hide behind the paper bag. The first thing I did when I was handed the cupcake was lick some frosting since my friend Michelle F raved about the fluffiness of the frosting that was not too sweet. I was impressed since I never eat frosting! I actually ate 3/4 of the frosting on this cupcake (def record breaking in my own book)! I loved the caramel drizzle that added some sweetness and the hint of sea salt that lingered on my tongue waiting for me to take another bite of the moist, sweet goodness that is the salted caramel cupcake.

I can't wait to try the vanilla bean one!

salted caramel.  s'more.  rock. it. out.

Their chocolate based cupcakes are super moist and their frosting DELICIOUS!  Smooth and creamy and super light in texture.

The lines can be ridiculous, the non-chocolate cakes are a bit dry, and trying to time things so you can actually get a cupcake is silly, but kate and her husband are super nice and the cupcakes are the most delicious around.

It's been a long time since I wrote a review, but this place is sensational. It really is. And a Berkeley grad to boot, and serving out a truck which reminds me of the days when I used to chase ice cream trucks as a kid. 

Go for the Red Velvet. That's my favorite. Have tried the salted caramel, and although my friends liked it, I'm not a big fan of salty-sweet combinations, but I think that's just me. S'mores and Tiramisu are also good.

Huge whopping toppings of cream at the top. If that's your thing, you'll spin out for this, but can feel a bit much for the guy who's interested in sweets, but not "decadent" sweets. $3 a cupcake, and long lines. But it comes in these cute boxes which, when opened, can make a person swoon with anticipation.

My friend and I were the last customers at around 1pm when they were at the Broadway & 12th location, and all they had were 4 salted caramels left. They were incredibly soft and gooey (maybe because they had been in the truck for an hour?) but soooo goood.

My goal is to try all the flavors... mmmm

TWINKIE CUPCAKES! love them. i asked my husband to pick up some cupkates when the truck was going to be across the street from his work. unfortunately due to a project deadline he failed the mission. he got home without the delicious little beauties and felt really really bad. i have a feeling the next time she is out there i will get double cupkates! YES!

5 Big Stars and thumbs up to Cupkates!! Happen to be on 4th Street today and saw fellow "gourmands" lined up patiently waiting their turn to purchase from a wonderful selection of interesting cupkate picks. I went for four different favors and have to say...anyone that can bake a moist, perfectly flavored vanilla cake and company it with a wonderful light and not overly sweet topping of butter cream frosting, is defiantly a pátissiére.  The Tiramisu was heaven, the Salted Caramel...savory and moist, and the Red Velvet....tasty and traditional to its true form. Yes...I test tasted all four! I will definitely follow the Cupkate truck to satisfy my sweet tooth and will request cupkate for my birthday next month!!

Some of the folks in my office have some philosophical problem with paying $3 for a cupcake. I don't understand how anyone could have that kind of issue after trying one of these bad boys.

They are spongy little clouds of pure heaven, topped with sugary bliss. Yum.

I admit, paying $3 for a cupcake from a truck seemed a little excessive, especially in these economic times.  But, I really wanted to try Cupkates cupcakes and they happened to be fairly close today, so I made a trip during my lunch break.

I stood in line for about 5-8 minutes, and seriously, it's a good thing that it took that long because I couldn't decide what to get.  The salted caramel sounded great, the double vanilla sounded great, tiramisu, chocolate peanut butter, and red velvet... well, who doesn't love a cupcake that needs a tablespoon of artificial dye for the perfect hue?

In the end, I decided on a box of the red velvet and chocolate PB, and a tiramisu to stuff in my hole right there and then.  I loved the tiramisu.  The cake texture was perfect--not at all dense, light yet rich, sweet but not overly sweet, with a nice touch of espresso or coffee flavoring, and a cookie bottom.  

All in all, it was a very worthwhile indulgence.

OMG. Yes. I am definitely a fan. I craved these cupcakes for two freaking weeks! 

1. Salted caramel - delish! I'm not a fan of frosting, but I found myself just eating the frosting - who would have known I'd be a salted caramel fan. 
2. Twinkie - awesome idea! 
3. Smores - nom nom nom. 
4. Lemon raspberry - surprise! Doesn't SOUND delish, but it sure is.

I've tried all of them (except the strawberry swirl - it's waiting to be devoured) and can attest that I'm in love. =)

Price is competitive with the cupcakes nowadays... but it's soooo worth the moist yummy-ness you get! 

Tip: Not too shabby of a line @ the Emeryville location on Fridays. I've heard of quite the wait @ the 19th/20th st location. They do take card, but I believe it's a $5 minimum.

Kate did our cupcakes for our wedding day on11/11/11.  They were all do delicious we did not have even one left over after 160.  The salted carmel chocolate and vanilla were crowd pleasers.  The presentation was amazing.  The cake is superiorly moist and the flavor makes you crave for more.  I only have gratitude and joy.  She is  highly recommended and a mobile cupcake concept is brilliant. She is a pleasure to work with

I have yet to not like one of Kate's cupcakes. Every one is especially moist, and the frosting is always the perfect accent.

Salted Caramel is amazing, love love love
Red Velvet is a timeless classic
Banana Caramel is lovely
S'more: amazing marshmallow frosting!

I can't wait for the guiness cupcakes to reappear, I've been dying to try!

Eh meh gah!!!! This food truck is full of thee most deelicious treats one could ever hope for...I have tried the red velvet, tiramisu, double vanilla, smores and my two favs, key lime and salted caramel....Now I'm on a weekly hunt for this delightful little wagon:)

"Oooh, look that person has a red velvet cupcake!  Where do you think they got it?"  "Hey that person also has a cupcake.  So does she.  What's going on here?"  Then we noticed that the Cupkates truck had pulled up!  I've actively chased this vehicle down on 580 before but never had the good fortune to be in the same place at the same time when it was parked.  Unforch they were out of almost everything but a salted caramel cupcake was calling my name.  Incredibly moist cake and the lightest most airy icing imaginable.  My only beef is that its really hard to eat when the icing doesn't go all the way to the edges!  I felt like I wanted a spoon to distribute it more evenly.  The plus side was that I couldn't share it. ;-)

I love, love, love this cupcake truck! The cupcakes are always super moist and the flavor combinations are just absolutely amazing! If you go to OTG, this truck will ALWAYS have a super long line and most people buy more than one cupcake.  My personal favorite is the salted caramel chocolate cupcake. It would be amazing if she opened a bakery so I could easily buy these yummy deserts whenever I want but it also makes for a delectable treat knowing I can't have it everyday.
I know what they're eating in Heaven...cupcakes from Cupkates! These are the best cupcakes ever! I love the coconut cream. Unbelievable goodness wrapped up in a little cupcake.

The softest, delicate and tastiest cupcake I've had in a very long time. I had the red velvet and believe me you will not be disappointed.

(not sure if anyone of those words are real but i think i just made them up)

I've seen the cupcake truck off and on for years now, always when I am down on 4th street in Emeryville. Always a long line of people streaming down the sidewalk, appearing excited to take that first bite. Today, I finally stepped on up to the window, curious what all the excitement has been about. I ordered my very first Cupkates, a nice looking Red Velvet. 
It will likely be my last. 
The cupcake tasted okay. It wasn't bad. But for $4.00 a pop, it certainly wasn't good, or spectacular even, which is closer to what I would expect for that price. 
Butter. Sugar. Eggs. Flour. 
I found an online site that states cupkates only uses "high quality and local ingredients" and that the cakes are "baked fresh daily."
I really wonder exactly to what ingredients that individual is referring.
What makes them "high quality?"
Nothing about the cake tasted of high quality ingredients.
The cupcake did not taste any different or better than the cakes I've had at elementary school bake sales. 
The frosting was okay. The overall appearance of the red velvet and of the creme brulee looked tasty. I was impressed that the other flavors were all sold out. The cup-truck is certainly cute. But again, I'm not sold and won't buy again.

On the other hand, I'm glad Kate (and/or whomever) has made a viable business for herself. Not necessarily easy to do. And I sincerely hope she continues to do well. (Lowering her price, if she can still make a profit, would be appreciated though!) 

I have to wonder if part of the attraction with cupkates has to do with some reminiscent nostalgia for the ice cream trucks so many of us happily dined at as children. Whatever, though I can't justify the price for a little cake that is just okay, I far prefer people support such a business as this than the mega stores that mass produce pure junk. Cupkates is definitely superior to that. I hope you enjoy.

A big mouthful of A-OK.

Each cupcake is physically perfect. The truck is super clean, and Kate is a cutie. 

But...
After the dazzle fades, I made an honest eyes-closed evaluation and was a little disappointed. Not like Dorothy finding out the Wizard of Oz was a short fat guy, but still just a little let down. The flavors are mild, and some of the varieties hit a glass ceiling. A red velvet cupcake, even if it's a perfect 10, is not the most exciting thing in the world, and the difference between a 10 and 6, is minor. I would like it if she took a few more chances with the flavors. 
 
 I was first in line and jumping up and down in glee. You'll enjoy them more if you participate in glee and fun.

I probably love food trucks even more than I love cupcakes, so the combination of the two is like a dream come true for me.

If you know my reviews, then you know that I am constantly complaining about cupcakes being too sweet. But these are very sweet and yet I love them. My favorite is their Salted Carmel Cupcake. The cake is very moist and the center is filled with some gooey carmel and chocolate. The chocolate frosting is extremely rich like a chocolate mousse, and the salt makes the flavors exploded in your mouth. This cupcake is all about BALANCE!!! Sure, it is sweet... but that comes from the rich chocolate and gooey carmel center rather than from just having way too much sugar added. 

Have I tried their other cupcakes? Yes, and they were great, but I can't tear myself away from their Salted Carmel.

I am indeed a cupcake aficiando.  Swear.  You can Google it. 
I've tried every cupcake from here to the Marina to Noe Valley to the Mission. I'm on it.  I had given up hope in SF until one unsuspecting Friday at the UN Plaza I had the extreme pleasure of indulging in Ms. Cupkate's Double Vanilla. The cake and frosting gods sang.  I have found my cupcake.  Double Vanilla Double Vanilla. It's just delicious - not overly sweet, but you definitely know you got some sugar, sugar.  The cake is moist and the frosting creamy, creamy.  I've also tried the Spicy Mexican Chocolate - I'm not a chocolate  - but I'm a spicy - and yep, this works. Good balance of chocolate and kick.  The lemon meringue -- I'm not a meringue - but I'm a lemon - and even the meringue topping made me rethink  my stance on meringue.  I'll try them all. I'm hooked.

These are delish! I'm not even a huge cupcake fan, but these aren't too sweet or heavy, which makes a big difference. I can barely eat half of a one from Cupcake Cove because they're so sweet, the frosting on Cupcates is light and airy. I've had the double chocolate and the smores and both were great.

I don't even like cupcakes, but the flavors sounded so interesting that I just had to try them. I got Salted Caramel and a Red Velvet one and absolutely loved them both. The frosting had a very nice texture and wasn't too sweet as it often happens with cupcakes. Both cupcakes (but especially the Caramel one) were SUPER moist and really, really good. 

Taking one star off for the price, I think they are just a bit too small to be $3.
