Found the truck right outside Smart Alec's on Thursday.  I tried the red velvet and smore's cupcakes.  They're really good.  Buy a few if you see the truck.

Cupkates cupcakes may not be as pretty as other cupcake places, but their cupcakes are the BOMB!  I have so far tried red velvet, banana nutella, and banana caramel.  Cupkates cupcakes are just so moist and absolutely delicious, and the creme isn't overly sweet  and complements the cupcake perfectly!  If the Cupkate truck ever rolls into your neighborhood, I highly recommend trying some!

I love Cupkates.  One of the food carts that I do not get tired of at the Off the Grid events.  

At my first visit, I tried the S'mores cupcakes and it was delicious.  I love the graham crust and marshmallow frosting.   My next visit, I ordered the S'mores and Tiramisu.  OMG, the Tiramisu is the best cupcake I have ever had!!!  Everything from the frosting, ladyfinger crust and topped with chocolate shavings made this the best ever!  Their red velvet cupcake was good as well.

Overall, Cupkates is definitely a must.  Cupcakes are $3 a piece and they accept debit/credit cards!

Yummy!  I caught them on 4th street after eating Sunday brunch. 
I got the smores cupcake because I wanted to try something new. I love the frosting! The consistency was light and not too sweet. I must go back on a Sunday to try their other flavors =)

The workers are really quick and super nice.

So I finally had my first cupkate. Here is my lil review. I had the Salted Caramel and my first bite I thought.. too bland, not sweet enough.. boy was I wrong. When everything was mixed with the salt, it was AMAZING! All these flavors came to life and exploded in my mouth. I had ordered two, one for me and one for my f...iance.. well the two salted caramel didn't make it home..  Below is what else I ordered

S'more~ Disappointed about this one... Didn't like the graham cracker crust at the bottom.. It was almost salty or gritty.

Stawberry~ Way toooo sweet. I really wanted to like this because of the cream cheese frosting... Bad taste in my mouth... 

Red Velvet~ I never had a bad red velvet but again.. Way too sweet. I don't know but I think Cupkates cooks there frosting but it's not my favorite. Fiance loves Red Velvets but he didn't like this one.

Twinkie~ Nothing spectacular.

Lemon Rasberry~ My mom loved this... I didn't taste it but she raved about it.  I am not a  big lemon fan..

I don't think the cupcakes are worth the $3.00. They seem really small.. They are super moist and not dense so maybe thats why I feel like its not worth the change. I would love to hunt Cupkates down but it seems like they are selling out within the hour.. They need to start making more cupcakes.. 

The Salted Caramel is original and def. worth a trip.

Their cupcakes are yummy, but to be honest, Love at First Bite is better.

After waiting 8ish minutes in line at North Berkeley's Off the Grid, I opted for their SALTED CARAMEL and TIRAMISU cupcakes at $3 each. They were gracious enough to put them in a box for me, although I wish they had given me a cupcake holder. Actually, it wouldn't have mattered since I devoured them shortly after ordering hehe.

The Salted Caramel cupcake was tasty, although the chocolate cake was a bit dry. The buttercream frosting is sweet and fluffy, although I personally prefer a denser buttercream frosting or a cream cheese frosting.

The Tiramisu cupcake was unique in that it had a bottom cookie layer, but that layer was more tasteless than the vanilla cake boo. Also, the frosting clumped up a bit and left a slightly oily layer in my mouth.

The cupcakes were decently scrumptious, but there's something lacking. I would call them bland or typical, I suppose. And I'm usually unsettled when the frosting doesn't work. At $3 each, I would head on over to Love at First Bite for their $2.75 cupcakes with denser cream and moister cakes.

Medium-sized cupcakes!

HOLY Crapola!!! Amazing, Brilliant, delish...love at first bite! I've NEVER in my life had a red velvet cupcake that I've liked until today. OMG!!!!

My work husband just brought me a red velvet cupcake and I looked at it with despair. Everyone always raves about how good red velvet is but I've never been much of a fan. When he brought it I was expecting just another disappointment. Yet, it was more like the WOW factor x 100!!!!

The cake texture was perfect!!! It was fluffy, flavorful and moist. I do not like cream cheese frosting but this one just melted in your mouth. It was not that clumpy creamy crap. It was light and not over bearing. 

I'm seriously in love. I am going to have to find this mobile cupcake truck for more!! I'm going to be on a mission. This is going to be a sweet affair!!

Wow, these cupcakes are just fantastic. I love how this place sells cupcakes on a truck! I tried the Red Velvet, Raspberry Lemon, and Strawberry cupcakes and they definitely hit the spot. Though a bit pricey ($2.75-$3.00 per cupcake), these cupcakes are definitely worth trying if you're in the mood!

OMG - these are deadly they are soooo good!  I've been lucky and tried a handful of flavors; vanilla, peanut butter chocolate, salted caramel and red velvet.  It's a toss up between vanilla and peanut butter chocolate for me.  Fortunately, I have a three year old niece who is my food twin so we go halvsies :).  It's my niece's favorite place;  after a day at pre-school she even requests to go to the cupcake truck.

I've also had a two day old vanilla cupcake, which somehow was still delicious.  It's like they put crack in the frosting it is soooo good!  

Unfortunately, I haven't gotten the full experience; I've never had to wait in the line.  My sister usually does (and I love her for that); the last time my sister went (while I was running errands), there were some newbies there before asking the owners, does this line of 10 people scare you?  Owners response, this does not scare me. It's the line at downtown Oakland that terrifies me.  According to my sister, people come dt Oakland with reading material and wait at least 30 minutes, if not an hour!  DAMN, now that is some commitment to mack on some cupkates!

I don't know if I want to find this out, but how many calories do you think one cupcake is?  I really hope it's not too absurd.
Ginger cupcake with lemon cream cheese frosting is my new favorite.

I wish I could give Cupkates a better review but it's hampered by the mildly negative customer service I experienced.

Visited Cupkates truck at Off the Grid Civic Center, I chose a tiramisu cupcake and my friend a red velvet for $3 each. Since Cupkates was our final visit in the string of trucks at Off the Grid that day our hands were nearly full. So in order to get the money out I needed to put my food somewhere so I put it on the ledge after asking, little did I know that there's no counter there. Well the lady in the truck put on a real sour face when I did that, but I'm trying to get you your money here! Overall that lady taking the cash came off as unwelcoming even before that and it certainly doesn't make me want to come back.

Now for the cake itself. The tiramisu cupcake wasn't what I expected. The frosting was the filling you'd find in tiramisu cake - mascarapone and whipping cream (probably with egg) and that was actually quite good. The cupcake itself was just like a regular vanilla cupcake with a lady finger crust on the bottom, and slightly soaked with espresso syrup or something at the bottom of the cake (not the lady fingers). There wasn't enough espresso flavor of the cake to make it taste enough like tiramisu. For a tiramisu cupcake I'd expect more espresso flavor (or maybe an espresso cake?).
Really good. Only complaint......not enough frosting.  When it comes to a cupcake....it's all about the frosting, baby.

They were smart to locate in the East Bay, which has largely been ignored by the cupcake craze. The only options here are so-so Teacakes and the mediocre "Love at First Bite", plus a few places here and there that just make one or two flavors. No Kara's, Sprinkles, or Sift to be found here.

Enter Cupkates. Sure, you'll have to wait in line behind some of their 1400 Facebook fans (gotta love the guy in front of us today who ordered 50, totally oblivious to the growing crowd behind him) and the frosting is the buttery kind, as opposed to the thick and sugary version I prefer.

But these are still the best cupcakes in the 510. I'll have to follow this moving target more often!

When you see this truck do what you can to stop it. Run behind it, In front of it or just plain throw your body in its tracks.  I don't know what they do to these cupcakes but they are pure divinity. Perfectly moist and fluffy and a huge dollop of sweet frosting.

Red Velvet, is my absolute favorite but other flavors like  Smore and Twinkie are also pretty delicious...Wait in line. As long as it takes. It is worth it.

These cupcakes are pretty good. I really like the lemon merengue and the double vanilla. Sometimes I think that they're too much frosting, but they're pretty good. My favorite one is the lemon merengue one though. That cupcake is BOMB. The bottom of the cupcake is kind of like a pie crust and there's a bit of lemon filling, and it's topped off with merengue. :)

I would say these are pretty decent cupcakes. I had the salted caramel and Mexican hot chocolate cupcakes. Simply to die for! Both were extremely moist and tasty. The frosting was not overly sweet but really soft. I liked the Mexican hot chocolate better, the chocolate was not overwhelming nor too sweet which I like. And you can def taste the hints  of cinnamon in Mexican hot chocolate. So delicious. The salted caramel was decent but it was kind of too sweet for me.

nom nom nom! my favorite cupcakes from cupkates are... tiramisu, vanilla, red velvet, lemon rasberry... ohh hell, all of them are my favorite! i LOVE cupkates!! best cupcakes i've ever had and they are always so fresh! i love that the frosting isn't too sweet and it goes perfectly with the moist cupcake!! as for pricing, it's not bad at all!! i can't wait to try new flavors because they're always coming out with new ones. ohhh and this is what you call good customer service! can't wait to lay by hands on another box of cupkates! no wonder why the line is always so long!! folks, wherever they are - make sure you line up early because they'll sell out real quick!
Best red velvet.  Cupkates is what I measure other red velvets against.  I like the tiramisu and s'mores cupcake too but red velvet is the way to go :)

I really enjoyed the cupcake (more than at Tea Cake Bakeshop, but have yet to try Love at First Bite!) but I don't think I'd go for again simply because I can't justify the price! I ordered the tiramisu cupcake... didn't think it would come out well because it's impossible to nail down the texture in a cupcake but the flavor was definitely there. The cupcake was complex in that it had a graham cracker (?? or something else) crust, some coffee/tiramisu flavor in the middle, and omg the frosting was amazing. I usually hate frosting (cream cheese frosting on red velvet cupcakes is way to rich for me and typical frosting just leaves that oily taste/texture on my lips) but this frosting was a good amount of sweetness with a light tiramisu flavor.

Other people who tried it did say that this place is generally pretty sweet for its cucpakes, but all in all it's really good.
You can't go wrong with any of their cupcakes. Seriously. I've tried most of the menu and they're all good!

+5 stars - look, I'll give it to you straight. Each Cupkate cupcake is a single serving of bomb diggity. It's the tastiest handful of tasty taste taste you're gonna get all day.

The Mexican Spicy Chocolate and the Tiramisu are The Real. Know that. Ya heard?

Wonderful product, fantastic marketing plan. A very unique idea and Kate is so nice, friendly and very customer oriented! 

I have tried the double vanilla and the frosting tasted like vanilla ice cream...it is SO DELICIOUS!! Possibly the best cupcake I've ever had.

Can't wait to sample another one soon. Keep up the good work, Berkeley loves you!

Everyone has a favorite cupcake, and this is mine. I don't really love buttercream, so I'm a particular fan of anything that has marshmallow or cream cheese frosting. That said, the salted caramel buttercream is pretty freaking good. All of the special flavors are definitely worth ordering since they rotate quickly.

Also, they're super about special orders, although they could use a slightly more secure ordering channel than email/phone. I'm an engineer and I work for cupcakes. Just sayin'.

I was fortunate enough to be given a few of these cupcakes as a surprise!  I tasted the red velvet, the lemon raspberry, salted caramel, and twinkie.

The red velvet was SOO GOOD.  I know in my previous cupcakery reviews, I've sworn by their red velvets, but this one... Oh.. My.. God! If you don't know which cupcake you want to try, get this one! haha Not only is the cake moist, yet dense, with a somewhat stronger hint of cocoa, but the cream cheese icing is the perfect consistency and taste!!!!!!!!!!  FIVE STARS for the red velvet!

The chocolate cake of the salted caramel was alright.  The texture seemed kind of odd - as if when someone makes a sour cream cake where the resulting product isn't really cake-y... I could pass on this one.

The lemon raspberry was also very good!  The cake had a nice lemon flavor (I think they put lemon zest, but I ate it so quickly, I didn't have time to examine. haha).  The buttercream icing was eh. I scraped off 3/4 of the icing.  It tasted alright, but the consistency was a lil too light and not flavorful enough since I couldn't really tell what it was supposed to be other than the pink color and the name of the cupcake.

The twinkie was surprisingly good.  Again, I had to scrape off most of the icing (how people are able to open their mouths wide enough to fit both the icing and the cupcake is amazing because I can't do it!).  The cake had a great vanilla flavor and I could see the vanilla bean specks! omg. soo good. 

All in all, the cake portion of the cupcakes were 5* as far as taste and texture go.  The cream cheese icing is also very good! However, the amount of icing is too much IMO and the buttercream icings aren't that great (hence minus half a star!) and the other half a star goes towards the $3 price! ack.  I think if they spread the frosting a lil thinner it'd be sooo much easier to eat and not over power the cake.

I'll definitely have my bf buy me more whenever I have a cupcake craving!

Are you kidding me?  The cupcake tasted like something you would buy at Safeway, was incredibly small, and had no cap (like a muffin does).  For all the craze in cupcakes these days it amazes me this place can stay in business charging 3$ a piece.

Lawd Lawd lawwwd.

These cupcakes were delicious. Ridiculously delicious. I had a tirimisu cupcake and it was perfect. Soft-melt-in-your-mouth buttercream coupled with a soft tender cake splashed with rum.

I am turned on just thinking about the delicious concoction that was flowing in my mouth just mere moments ago!

I might dare say that Kara's Cupcakes has found themselves a real contender! Ding Ding!

I don't even like cupcakes!  This was the best cupcake I ever had!  It was so funny, I was driving down Brannan & there's the truck and I say to myself "Self, do we want a treat?" Self said "No, besides cupcakes are dry in the middle and covered with frosting to try to psych you out!"  So, I went to the flower mart & handled my business & driving home there's the truck, again... I stop in the middle of the street back up and park behind the truck. While standing gazing at the list the pretty girl reading in' the truck says "If you'd like a cupcake I only have 3 left Double Vanilla, Smores, and Banana Cream Pie."  Suddenly, a middle aged guy stands next to me.  I smile at him, he didn't smile back. I said to the pretty cupcake lady give me two of the three so I can make life easy on him, I'll take the s'more & the banana cream pie.  She laughed really quite heartily at my meaness and boxed up my cupcakes, & slapped on a sticker.  As the stuck up suit approached the counter he said "Banana Cream Pie." She told him I bought the last one.  I kinda wonder if thats what made it taste so darn good!  The S'mores was okay but the banana cream pie made me dance in the car! I tried to save it. I tried to put it down, but that was one hecka fresh cupcake!  That's right I said hecka!  My 35th birthday is tomorrow and that's what I want! Banana cream pie cupcake from Cupkates! 

P.S. I AM NOT LOOSE WITH THE 5 STAR RATINGS! I REALLY LOVE YOUR CUPCAKES & THANK YOU FOR MAKING MY DAY!
Oh my freaking God, this was the best cupcake I have ever had.  I got the salted caramel from a co-worker that bought a bunch and it was AMAZING.  It was so moist, it melted in my mouth.  SOLD!!!

I've never had someone so dedicated to cupcakes let alone to see a cupcake truck! I was amazed by every flavor they have. 
They are so friendly and kind, and never do I have to wait more then a few minutes even though their lines are always long and I can see why!
I would eat here any chance i get and never be disappointed.

OK... it's time for me to give credit where it's due - CupKates deserves 5 stars for having such awesome cupcakes!

Pre-CupKates, I never was a cupcake person and didn't get the whole cupcake craze. That is, until I tried the little morsels of crack that CupKate serves! The dollop of frosting on top may not look the most appetizing, but trust me - you'll want to lick every last drop! The frosting is rich and luscious but not overwhelmingly sweet, while the cupcake itself is tasty and moist.

I don't think you can really go wrong with any of their cupcakes (although the double chocolate and double vanilla seem boring), but my personal faves so far are the red velvet and new key lime!

Brace yourself for consistently long lines, and for them to start selling out of popular flavors if you get there too late!

Mmmm I happened to walk by these guys today on Montgomery and decided to get a cupcake on a whim.  I chose lemon raspberry, and I was so glad I did.  It was excellent!!  The cake was so flavorful and moist!  All too often lately you just get bland, or dry, or too too sweet, but these flavors were perfectly balanced.  While I personally prefer frosting to be spread more evenly over the cupcake surface, the raspberry buttercream was reeeeeally good.  Not too sweet or overbearing.  I was surprised how much I liked it given that I usually go for thicker, less airy frosting.

All in all, yummy.  I pretty much inhaled it on my way to the muni station.  I'll definitely find a way to get back here on another Wednesday afternoon.  I'll reserve my five stars for the next one I try.
NOM. MUST EAT ALL THE CUPCAKES. Sophisticated yet satisfying flavors, perfect moist cake-part, perfect light n' creamy frosting part. Get two. At the Berkeley food truck swarm every Wednesday.

Hot damn! 

I just ate a s'more cupcake and couldn't be happier. I literally licked my fingers and couldn't stop thinking about more. This is a diet nightmare, but a sugar plum fantasy.

This was my first time eating one of these tasty cupcakes, but it most certainly won't be my last.  Can't wait to get obsessed and try all of the flavors... yummy!

Being a huge fan of cupcakes and all things sweet, I have had cupcakes from Sprinkles, Cako, and a whole lot more of which I don't know why I can't remember their names. However, with all the cupcakes I have ever had, Cupkates has ALWAYS remained my favorite.

The cupcakes are always perfectly moist and the icing is not super thick like Sprinkles' -- each flavor is a burst of richness that even without knowing the flavor, you can immediately identify it with one bite. 

I think another plus is that Cupkates is always traveling from locations and cities and she always sells out within the first hour - so that makes her cupcakes all that more desirable! The pricing is $3 which I find very average if not cheap amongst all other 'gourmet' desserts. 

I go to school down in Southern CA, but everytime I come home to Oakland, I always HAVE to visit the Cupkates Truck! On my last visit, I bought $54 worth of cupcakes and made a personal delivery to friends, my teachers, and my family -- they all love it almost as much as I do! 

PS: Great customer service! Kate was incredibly patient with my huge order and requests for extra boxes.

i wish there was a lot more to their cupcakes, especially since when i think 3 dollars for a cupcake is a bit steep for me. 

salted caramel, yum. a solid good cupcake, decent frosting. nothing more to it.

The truck was (still is at the moment) at the Beehive Market in Berkeley today. I went at about noon, and the whole market was pretty barren, so it came as no surprise to me that the truck was not busy at all.

My first impression upon approaching the truck was "Who's this dude working the truck? I'm sure his name isn't Kate..."

Anyways, I ordered 4 cupcakes in hopes that I could just get a taste of each of them and bring the rest back to my family later in the day. I opened them up and found out that due to the massive frosting on top and the softness/moistness of the actual cupcake, it was pretty impossible to split with a butter knife and ended up eating all 4 on my own. Or maybe I just needed an excuse to eat them all (not really, I'm actually skipping out on lunch and going for a run later when the sun isn't so scorching).

I have this tendency when I order things to completely forget what I ordered afterwards, so I had to try to guess based on other reviews what I ate, and here they are:

Smores. I ate this first cuz it's what everyone seems to be jizzing about. The graham cracker crust was unsubstantial, since the base of the cupcake is small to begin with. The marshmallow frosting was pretty good though. Overall, it was whatever for me.

Twinkie. I ate this second. It has coconut, which I'm not a fan of, but I liked this one the most of the four I got. The frosting inside the cupcake is probably what made it for me.

Salt Caramel. I think this was just a chocolate cupcake with some frosting on it with caramel and salt? I don't know, but I didn't like it at all.

Something with strawberry and lemon. This was my second favorite. It would have been really good if the lemon flavor wasn't so strong.

I didn't know what to really expect of just cupcakes, but I don't see myself hunting this place down regardless of how good the cupcakes are or are not.
If there's a heaven and it has food, it will taste like the vanilla cupcake from Cupkates.

Why are you not here all the time!? Why must you make me wait until Thursdays to taste your deliciousness? I miss you Cupkates.

Sorry for my desperation, it's just finals. But I miss your Red Velvet and Smore cupcakes. I will need to get more next Thursday at Off the Grid. 

Best cupcakes I've had in the city. Too bad they are kind of small. I eat them too fast. =\

OMFG!!  I have been twitter stalking the Cupkates truck ever since a friend of mine tried a red velvet Cupkate at a wedding she attended.  For me, these were the best cupcakes I have ever had. 

I finally got my chance to try Cupkates at Off the Grid: Berkeley last night.  Yes, the line was LONG. But it was definitely worth the wait.  In line I contemplated my order.  I settled on 4; 2 red velvet, 1 salted caramel, 1 s'mores.

Red Velvet: the frosting is one of the best cream cheese frostings I have ever had.  yum!
Salted Caramel: Lets just say I want another one (like right now).  This was my favorite.  the hint of salt was just perfect. YUMMY!  
S'mores: graham cracker at the base and toasted marshmallow frosting.  (my friend ate this one because i devoured the salted caramel).

I look forward to following the Cupkates to the next location!!

i love cake..i love sweets, pastries, puddings and cookies...oh and the parking is difficult near this truck.  find some and walk on over.

so they're always at the OTG-off the grid haight street.

i love cupcakes.  i love them so much i had to try them.

okay. first of all....i know they're just too expensive and they're TOO SMALL!  

they taste good but sometimes they're a little dry.

also their red velvet cupcakes are all ready dry...and they use just the same as ANYWHERE ELSE and give you the sour cream frosting, which for me is just to thick and sweet.  i'd tell you where its better but i just don't do that.  this review is for cupkates and cupkate only...if you want to know where i say its WAY BETTER you'll have to review my reviews...or message me and convince me that i should share this secret with you...lol.

honestly, i thought 2.50 for a cupcake is expensive...but 3 dollars and its HALF A CUPCAKE in size to a NORMAL cupcake?

well, if you love cupcakes, you'll try it anyway.  they do good business.  i've had better but this place is at least average in taste.  if you're on a diet i guess a half a cupcake might work.

Cupkates is a cupcake truck that drives around and stops at various areas in the vicinity of Berkeley and North Oakland. I heard that their routes change a lot so if you ever see their truck, I recommend going up to buy a cupcake. Cupcakes are ~$3 each depending on the flavor. My friend coincidentally saw their truck in front of the campus and bought S'mores and Red Velvet cupcakes for us. 

Their cupcakes are good but not awesome. A wee smaller than the ones I've normally seen but they are topped with a nice thick dollop of cream cheese frosting. Although my red velvet is one of my favorites in terms of cupcake/cake flavors, I though theirs was just okay. My favorite was the S'mores because it was unique in that the "frosting" was a melted marshmallow that had been flamed at the top and they also had a graham cracker crust on the bottom (a nice surprise!).

The cupcake was airy, a little too airy---kind of like a cake :/ but their frosting was pretty good. :)

Songs have been written about the perfect cupcake. Well, maybe they haven't but they should. And if those songs were written, they would sing Cupkates' praises. Seriously. I have had the fortune of tasting lemon meringue and red velvet. Both very good. The Lemon Meringue had a wonderful graham cracker crust, the cake was light and airy and it had the level of lemon zing that was perfect. The red velvet was the best red velvet ive ever had. The icing was perfect, dense, creamy and sweet but not overly sweet. I. Want. More.
Can a sista give em 12 stars? Sweet moist cups of caramelly salty goodness... and they can rock a Twinkie cupcake!!
I've only tried so far their Salted Caramel.  What the heck do they put in there??  How is it so moist and fluffy??  It must be crack cause flour, sugar, and butter can't taste this good.

My husband and I finally got down to Ft. Mason Friday night for the food trucks while in San Francisco a few weeks ago. We stuffed ourselves with so much great food, that we had to take the cupcakes to go. We got the red velvet, Mexican chocolate and caramel sea salt and took them back to the hotel for later. My husband is fortunate that I was in a generous mood because otherwise he wouldn't have tasted a crumb. The red velvet was solid, but paled in comparison to the other two extraordinary flavors. I wish they would ship to Texas!!!

Headed to Off the Grid last night and after nomming on other trucks, decided to get some cupcakes to go.

I'm just going to say that Cupkates was worth every penny. I've never had a better cupcake and that we should start typing cupkates instead of cupcakes. And might I add, they had already sold out on 3 flavors by the time I ordered (like Lemon Raspberry! how delicious does that sound?!).

Anyways, I ordered a Red Velvet as well as a Tiramisu. I split the Red Velvet with D, and it was once of the best Red Velvets I've ever had. The cream cheese was not thick and fluffy, which I loved. The cake was also super moist.

I had planned to save the Tiramisu for my mom, but when i got home, she was already sound asleep. I decided to save it for this morning and by golly, still delicious, still good, after 12+ hours. The frosting was very light, and the cake was still moist after sitting for an entire night. I want another one already!

Is it possible to give something 6 stars? Yeah, it's that good.

I saw a Cupkates truck and decided to get a few. I ordered the red velvet, double vanilla, and pumpkin spice cupcakes. I'm a big gourmet cupcake fan and try them everywhere I see them. 

First, I ate the pumpkin spice:
(1)  The taste of the frosting was bad. It tasted weird and was not sweet.
(2)  There was not enough frosting. (although I didn't like their frosting anyway, so I guess not enough was actually a good thing)
(3)  The cake was decent.

For the red velvet and double vanilla:
(1)  The frosting was only slightly sweet. They need to make all of their frosting much, much, much sweeter. The red velvet frosting needs less cream cheese.
(2)  There was not enough frosting. Frosting should cover the entire top part of the cupcake and be at least 1/4 of an inch thick.
(3)  The cake was pretty good for both.

I would give 2 1/2 stars if I could. Overall grade: C

Sprinkles is still the Champ!!.....followed up by Suite 106 Cupcakery in Rancho Cucumonga.

Cupcakes are SO overrated. However, Cupkates is LEGIT. I hate typical cake and cupcake frosting, but Cupkates's is much lighter -- more like mousse. Good, deep, balanced flavors. Decadent but not too sweet. The cake is moist enough. I like everything except the Double Vanilla.

For first timers seeking guidance, try the S'mores. I don't even particularly like chocolate, and I still think it's really good.

Best cupcakes in town. Thanks for stopping in Oakland on Thursdays :).

I love cupcakes. I have high expectations for cupcakes especially when it's a vanilla cupcake- and they topped my expectations with a vanilla bean cupcake! I find that it's important to have the right ratio between cupcake and frosting and they nailed it. I learned that the cupcake is all natural which makes it extra special. The staff is very friendly and I will for sure have another when if I every come across the truck again!

We actually came across the truck by accident. I was shopping at CB2 and then walked across the street to Crate and Barrel, and Cupkates was blocking the sign. They were parked across the street and I got distracted and got excited to see a cupcake truck. I saw the vanilla bean and I had to have one. I had one, I actually went back and bought 4 more to take home- YumM! Every time I have cupcakes from somewhere else or try to bake one myself, I can't find one that compares to Cupkates. Eat up- YumM!

I'm totally underwhelmed by this place.  I've tried them several times, but their flavors sound more interesting than they actually are.  The salted caramel sounds fantastic, but the caramel is overwhelmed by the salt.  The red velvet was completely boring, almost no flavor.  The faux-twinkie cupcake was better than an actual Twinkie, but just not that tasty.  My biggest gripe is that their frosting is too buttery (I can't believe I'm saying that).  It needs a higher percentage of sugar.  It's really kind of greasy as it is, and leaves a huge oily stain on the box.  I wish I could like this place more, but they just don't do it for me.

The price= $9 for 3 cupcakes

The challenge= find a cupcake I really like

Mission accomplished? Or mission impossible? I don't really know. I liked these well enough, but they didn't change my world. Maybe I am just a cupcake cynic, and I'll never find the one for me.

I tried the lemon meringue, tiramisu, and salted caramel. 

Lemon meringue was quite tasty. Lemon cake, lemon curd filling (just enough) and meringue topping. Yum! I would say it ties with Cako for my favorite lemon meringue cupcake. I like how the crumb is light and airy, and their is just enough curd to add flavor without being too gooey. Overall, my favorite of the bunch

Tiramisu- This does not taste like tiramisu. At first my friend and I were really confused.. it's not soaked in any liquid, it's not chocolatey, the top is mascarpone but there is no coffee flavor... yeah, I don't understand this at all. It tasted like a vanilla cupcake with mascarpone topping. Which is great in its own right, but don't call it a tiramisu. Call it a vanilla cupcake with mascarpone.

Salted caramel- wasn't a fan of the chocolate cake part, which I thought lacked flavor. The buttercream was delightful- I'm a sucker for salted caramel.

When i heard about Cupkates months ago I knew that I would be trying their cupcakes at one point or another in my life.  Well I did and i gotta say i don't understand all of the love for them.  I mean, they are by no means bad, but I feel that with all the other cupcake joints in the Bay area I wouldn't come back. 

I had the salted caramel and s'mores cupcake and neither of them were particularly good.  I had high hopes for the smores since I pretty much love anything that even remotely resembles the camping treat, but this was a bit of a disappointment.  The salted caramel was pretty good, but not a flavor i really enjoyed.  

Well i'm all for second chances and if the opportunity presents itself I will definitely buy a different flavor next time, but I wouldn't go out of my way again.

Cupcakes are AMAZING.  I love Cupkates, so far it's my favorite in the bay Area, much better than Kara's and Sprinkles too!  The cupcakes are always delish, moist, and satisfying.   I always get the Red Velvet and Salted Caramel.  The others are fantastic too, but these two are my absolute favorite!

Best cupcakes I have ever had. Supremely moist. My favorite is the banana cream pie and wish it was a regular menu item instead of seasonal. The tiramisu and double vanilla are also delicious! Love the cookie bottom on both the banana cream and tiramisu. The frosting is light and fluffy, but make sure you eat them the first day, because it changes consistency in the refrigerator. Only one I didn't like was the spicy Mexican chocolate because the spice was overwhelming. Glad I have to walk a ways to get these because they are sure a temptation!

The Tiramisu cupcake is the BEST CUPCAKE I'VE EVER HAD. THERE I SAID IT. Disregard any other past review I've written where I've foolishly claimed the best cupcake was from another bakery in another city.

Espresso soaked cake, mascarpone icing, lady finger crust... *drools*. Who needs real tiramisu anymore?! I've also tried the Double Vanilla and Caramel Apple, but they just don't even compare to this one.

Oh my heaven's...my friend and co-worker Sarah had been talking these cupcakes up to me for MONTHS and all I could think of was "What is so great about these cupcakes?".... 

Well one night Sarah text messaged me and said "Cupkates is gonna be in Downtown Oakland! Bring $3 bucks with you to work!" So I dutifully brought my money with me and on our lunch break we sped...literally...sped...to Downtown Oakland and I got to try these oh so amazing cupcakes. I don't think I talked the whole time I savored these delightful pieces of heaven! 

They were so good and I am so sad to say I have not had the chance to have anymore since that first time but you can bet when the Cupkates truck is close to work I will be speeding down there to get more of her amazingly yummy cupcakes again!

Heard about the truck but didn't see it til today.  Tried the Red Velvet, S'more, Lemon Raspberry and Double Vanilla today.  Two of us thought the Lemon Raspberry were the best although all agreed they each were great.  I will hunt this truck down in the future.

I ordered 2 dozen cupcakes for a work-related event, with very short notice.
I ordered using the website, which requests a 24 hour lead time.
My one issue with this business is that I wish there were a way to call and order by phone, so one can get instant confirmation that the order can be completed in the time required- unfortunately, Cupkates is closed on Tuesdays, so they couldn't make my cupcakes within the 24 hour time period. 

However, the awesomeness of the cupcakes totally made up for it- they were a huge hit around the office! I had people coming up to me for the rest of the week, gushing about how much they enjoyed them. Smores and Peanut Butter Chocolate were particular favorites with my crowd. 

In addition, when I went to go pick them up, I was able to get an additional half dozen, fresh from the oven- Yum!!

"Oh! SALTED CARAMEL cupcakes!"

You were so worried they'd be using a Bakemark brand just-add-water cake mix like the million other cupcake places that've popped up, but you figured these folks were legit cuz they're in SF and all. Instead, you got a sub-par devils food cake topped with a shortening-heavy icing (let's face it, cupcakes are only icing delivery systems). 

The icing is painfully in need of some caster sugar for texture, salt to help bring out the butter flavor (there is butter in there, right, Kate? please don't let me be eating shortening and sugar), and vanilla. 

Without grainy sugar, salt, butter, and vanilla, you end up with the plasticky icing that they happen to have :(

i tried 4 different cupcakes (salted caramel, peanut butter chocolate, tiramisu, and smores), an unfortunate waste of $12, and only the smores icing tasted different, because they added some marshmallow fluff. 

and customers, let's not try to be fancy, remember, you're ordering from a truck -- caramel has only two syllables.
Hella good cupcakes (tiramisu and lemon/raspberry) with generous icing (yes, the good kind). Oh, and Kate's a Lakers fan (bonus).

I LOVE CUPKATES.

Why? Well as a chubby girl who didn't get chubby by eating sweets, a cupcake is a good blend of frosting and cake. Kate's are amazing. The smores with the fired marshmallow is devine. I am a huge fan of the ever so moist red velvet with cream cheese frosting. Plus you gotta try the twinkie cupcake! 

Heavenly creations and I think best cupcake around.

I first ran into CupKates at "off the grid" event in SF 

This place makes the BEST cupcakes.  I've tried other cupcakes from SO Cal - North Cal - East and Midwest. Their cupcakes are fresh and super MOIST. Their frosting is just perfect! Not too sweet like other cupcake places. 

Loved all their flavors: Salted Caramel, Tiramisu,Red Velvet, S'mores, Twinkie, Double Vanilla and Double Chocolate! 

Hands down best cupcakes!

The frosting is Goldilocks perfect for me.  It's not too dense, and it's not too sweet.  

I like how they go out to the Civic Center off-the-grid every other week.  It helps me not get too fat.
Such a wonderful idea.  Cupcakes were tasty and had the perfect dollop of frosting on top.  The frosting had a light and smooth texture.   Would love to run into them again.

What a pleasant surprise, I walked up to what I thought was a taco truck in order to  get change for parking and to my delight it was cupcakes!! I wasn't able to get change but i bought two cupcakes! The frosting is amazing :) Out of all the cupcakes I've tried from specialty places... these take the cake, wayy better than any Sprinkles ones I've had

As I live with a family of bakers...it is rare that we all love a baked good outside the household.  That is, until we discovered the roaming Cupkates truck in Berkeley.  We are always a sucker for trying a great story with a unique twist and Kate delivered.  Her cupcakes are wonderful.  Reminds me of waiting for those fresh muffins my mom used to make...I believe her secret is that her offerings are fresh and that the delivery of them actually adds to the enjoyment.  Red Velet rocked it.  Moist and texture.  A+.  Find cupkates on Twitter or Facebook for when and where.  http://twitter.com/Cupkates

Another favorite: lemon raspberry--tart, slightly sweet and just perfect. 

I'm waiting to try their Twinkie cupcake though.........my cw brought it up, dammit!!

SO worth hunting down and driving out to wherever they are located at for the day!

I absolutely love how moist and decadent their cupcakes are! They don't make their frosting super sweet, thick or cavity infested. Light and airy and enough with each bite of cake. PERFECT!

Lemon Raspberry, Red velvet, Double vanilla, S'mores, Salter caramel, Key lime, Guiness are all the ones that I've tried so far and I've loved every single one!! Definitely love the double vanilla and s'mores the most though ;)

Verdict: I definitely love how it's a food truck and that they don't go crazy with their ingredients or decorations. Absolutely delicious and I definitely want to put in future orders since they put a smile on my face :D
Excellent flavor. Beware of frosting in hot weather.  They tend to melt.
I don't really like sweets but, the Tiramisu cupcake is AWESOME!!!!

My wife & I saw the Cupkates food truck at the Alameda OtG event last Saturday.  Needing dessert after lunch, my wife got a Salted Caramel cupcake, while I got a double chocolate one.  Because the weather was really warm that day, the chocolate buttercream frosting was really light.  This made for a really messy, albeit very tasty, experience.  Next time, I'll have either the s'mores or tiramisu flavors, though one of our friends raves over the red velvet cupcakes.

The red velvet cupcake is superb, the salted caramel cupcake is not so much (it was good, it just didn't have much salted caramel flavor) Regardless, I always find myself waiting in their notoriously long line and not hesitating to pay 3$ for each of those little yummy cakes.

All my friends know that I am obsessed with cupcakes. 

One day, while doing a photo shoot in berkeley, my co-worker and I stumble across a food truck. I thought, no way cupcakes from a truck can't be that good. 

Although skeptical, the line was extremely long so I decided to try it for myself. After the line died down I ordered a red velvet and a raspberry lemon cupcake togo. 

When I got home, I stuffed my face and have been dreaming about going back ever since. 

These cupcakes were moist and definitely better than SPRINKLES!

Completely worth the diabetic episode I had in the car on the way home from Off the Grid @ Fort Mason.

(Not really, but I did feel a little woozy.  Might have been the Bao/Taco/TikkaMasalaFries/Dumpling/Cupcake/CremeBrulee Combo...?)

Delicious and adorable cupcakes.  I'm a sucker for anything salted caramel so I went for the Salted Dulce de Leche, the Red Velvet and the Mexican Chocolate.  And yes, sweet man inside the truck, I shared with a friend.  Not that there's any shame in eating three of these delights.  I just didn't have the room...

Red Velvet was the clear winner.  Perfect frosting.  The other two were also delicious - I loved the cinnamon in the Mexican Chocolate.  All three were very moist, foiling my plan to only eat the tops.

Since it was my first OtG, I felt the need to sample everything.  I will surely come back to Cupkates every time but I might only need one flavor.  :)

Pumpkin Spice and Tiramisu!

Perfect texture between the frosting and cake. Delicious flavors. Better than Sprinkles! 

Looking forward to try the GInger Lemon flavor!
I've tried quite a few Bay Area cupcakes including Kara's, Sprinkles, Cupcake Cove, Braxtons Boxes, Love at First Bite, etc.  Hands down, CupKates are the best.
The lemon meringue was really good. However double vanilla was not good. The frosting tasted like it was made from Crisco. Not tasty.

RED VELVET. Try it. Moist. Not too heavy or too airy-- perfect density. Not sickly sweet. Very generous amount of cream cheese frosting. Absolutely delicious.

However, the price is a bit steep. $3 for a cupcake is unreasonable, regardless of how delicious it is. Also, gotta knock a star for the s'mores cupcake. I wasn't impressed. The cupcake was too fluffy, as was the frosting, and the graham cracker crust didn't do anything for me. It was too difficult to eat and too buttery.

Yummy but expensive :(

Oooohhh Boy.  My boss told me about this traveling sugar show and said it was pretty good.  Well, it's better than that.  My significant other said it was the "best cupcake she ever had".  I'm not going there, but it is possibly one of the best cupcakes I've ever had.

If you go during work and plan on eating one at your desk, give yourself some time to recover...

Here's my NY vs. SF cupcake report card, so far:

Sugar Sweet Sunshine: C-

Magnolia: C+

Billy's: B+

Kara's: A

Cupkate's: A+ !!!

We tried a few of these at Off the Grid last night. Spicy Mexican Chocolate and Salted Caramel.

The Spicy Mexican chocolate was a tiny bit too spicy for my tastes but I am a wimp. Under the heat I could taste how good it was and the cake was really moist and soft. The Salted Caramel was also pretty good the frosting was a bit rich but good.

I  LOVE Cupkates; put's Kara's to shame (frankly Kara's sucks).  I love the salted caramel, red velvet and my daughter is partial to the smores.  These cupcakes are not overly sweet like some others and the flavors taste fresh and authentic.  The staff are always friendly (unlike other cupcake places) and always encourage to try other flavors.  Can't wait to try the pumpkin spice.

Thanks Cupkates, I am hooked!!!

Whenever I go to Off the Grid, I have to make sure that Cupkates is there, and that I bring home about half a dozen cupcakes. I've had the lemon raspberry and s'mores which are good but my favorite is TIRAMISU! I don't even usually eat regular tiramisu but I love this tiramisu cupcake, so much so that I made sure to take plenty of pictures of it. I imagine that this is what clouds or heaven tastes like. It's not overly sweet or drenched in espresso. I wish I bought a whole box full! but sadly I only bought one. Cupkates most definitely has won a spot on my favorites list.

I had cupkates for my wedding. My fiance and I first tried them at Off the Grid in the Haight and fell in love with the Smores cupcake. BEST Smores cupcake I ever had. The cake is moist and there is the right amount of marshmallow frosting that is lightly toasted. The best part was of course the graham cracker crust at the bottom. 

I knew that when we were going to do cake we were going to do cupkates smores cupcakes. Kate was very easy to work with and all I had to do was place my order 2 weeks before the wedding. Cupkates did not disappoint. I did have a little cake made by a friend to cut. After we cut that, my future brother-in-law was just standing there staring at the cupcakes and yelled out, "Can we have cupcakes now?!"

Everyone loved the cupcakes. Such a nice treat to have at the wedding. Thanks CupKates!

Cupkates are a sweet treat!  I recommend my favorite:

Salted Caramel:  The chocolate cake is so moist!  It has a light caramel buttercream that doesn't overpower the cupcake.  It has a drizzle of caramel and dusting of flaked sea salt.  The salt really accentuates the flavor of the chocolate and caramel.

Cupkate's is awesome!

It's so great to see the food-truck craze starting to hit the Bay Area, and this is a delicious start. 

They usually have five or six flavors that get replaced as they come up with new ideas -- the most recent is caramel banana, which I haven't tried yet because I was swayed by the salted caramel. The cupcakes are moist and really flavorful, and the frosting is light and creamy, and not too sweet. 

The truck roams around Berkeley and Oakland; they have a usual set of weekday stops, and will come by your office if you make a request. Follow them on Twitter (@CupkatesTruck) to get location updates.

RED VELVET, its like a flavor orgy in your mouth. The texture is so smooth and the frosting is so tasty. I have to say if you can afford a $3 cupcake and afford the probably 300+ calories, then i say cupkates is your place!

What can I say? I love cupcakes and these are some of the best I have ever had! The Salted Caramel is to DIE for. The red velvet is heaven. 

I want more and I want them NOW. I also want my pants to fit, so I'm glad they roam and it takes a little work on my part to track them down. (Actually not too much, since all you hace to do is check Facebook for updates.)

The line moves quickly, which is almost a shame since everyone waiting in it is friendly and fun - of course! They love cupcakes!

I tried the salted caramel and red velvet. The cake was excellent quality, which I find unusual in a cupcake. The salted caramel especially was very moist and delicious. The cupcakes had WAY too much frosting for me - it was both too thick and extremely buttery. I probably would have liked about 1/3 the frosting, but the nice salt and caramel were on the top of the frosting, so of course I didn't want to sacrifice that. I thought $3 was a pretty fair price.

I had heard rumors about this truck so what a great surprise to stumble upon Cupkate's in downtown Berkeley.  Everything about it is charming - the truck, the presentation and Kate herself.
There are several interesting flavors to choose from - i, being a bit of a purist, had the double vanilla.  The cupcake is just the right size, maybe three or four bites, and the flavor - absolutely sublime.  Texture, perfection!
I hope this business does well - after all, she's providing a valuable public service!

I had their red velvet cupcake and it was ABSOLUTELY delicious. The cake was perfectly light, moist and not crumbly. The frosting was not incredibly sweet; which I find a lot of places make their frosting, in my taste, too sweet. They are a traveling cupcake truck. I had my tasting at Off the Grid at Fort Mason. They do have catering available. Check out their website for more details!

Yum!!!!!! We shared the lemon raspberry, salted caramel, and red velvet. My favorite was the salted caramel in terms of flavor, but all the cupcakes had similar texture. I really enjoyed the soft and moist texture of the cupcakes. The frosting wasn't too sweet; just the perfect complement to the cake. About $3 for a cupcake, which is a little steep, but totally worth it. Go ahead. Treat yourself. You deserve it!

agreeing with fellow yelpers that these are yummy cupcakes from cupkates. my personal favorites are the s'mores and the salted caramel. i love the frosting, especially the double vanilla frosting cause it seems so light and not overly sweet. there are a few people helping out with operating the business mobile, who were all friendly.
Smack-someone-good.  If you have to fight someone for the last red velvet--do so.  It will be worth the bail money your friends will have to loan you.

After following them on Twitter, forever, I finally had my first taste. A little disappointed. I love cupcakes. No, I LOVE CUPCAKES! Maybe I was expecting "the world" with Cupkates. 

Yes, the cupcakes are moist and for the most part are very tasty. But for $3 per cupcake I just expected something, well, more.

Salted Caramel: I don't like big grains of salt. I love sea salt (and that's all I ever use at home) but this was too overpowering for the subtle flavor of caramel.

S'mores: Again, this is one moist cupcake, but almost impossible to eat without getting marshmallow stuck up your nose. The bottom has a graham cracker crust, but that's pretty much the only exciting thing about it.

Twinkie: This was my least-favorite. The vanilla-bean cake was just OK and I didn't really get much marshmallow cream in the middle. 

I'm not against trying the other flavors, but at this point I feel like I'm going to continue my search for the "Best Cupcake Ever."

Cupkates are good and if you happen to see the truck, by all means stop and pick one up.

Watch out Kara....here comes Kate!  Kate's cupcakes are the best in the Bay Area.  I have been to literally every cupcake shop in the Bay Area and there are lots of great ones including Kara's but Kate takes the cake.  Her presentation is simple and pretty.  The s'mores was so yummy, Kara's does a good one too, but Kate's is better.  Loved the chocolate peanut butter and the caramel chocolate with salt.  My daughter's favorite was the lemon raspberry.  The chocolate/chocolate was great too. The red velvet was excellent, the only place that does one slightly better is Nothing Bundt Cake (I like the little chocolate chips that they throw in the batter).  My husband and I sat tasting the five chocolate cake ones and really couldn't decide which was best.    I've been searching for a cupcake place that is just as good, if not better than Kara's, and I've finally found it.  Yum.

I agree with the other reviewers. I was never a cupcake lover until my co-worker introduced me to Cupkates. Oh my!  It's certainly the best cupcake food truck out there.  Love their salted caramel, red velvet and double chocolate flavors.  Very moist and the whole thing melts in your mouth.  Wish they would consider coming out to the Union City/Fremont area during the weekly Food Truck Mafia events.

Kate did the cupcakes for my wedding and they were amazing! We ordered 60 more cupcakes than people, but by the end of the night, they were all gone!  Several people admitted to me after the wedding that they had tried all the flavors!! OMG! 

Kate also made us a cupcake stand, which was so freaken adorable!! And it helped fit all the cupcakes on the table!  

We also asked for a small cake so that we could cut it for the pictures.  Kate made us two!  Red velvet with white icing.  It was delicious and I was so glad when my husband actually got it into my mouth - rather than smashing it on my face - so that I could eat some of it. Yum! Kate and her cupcake truck makes me genuinely happy! And I really appreciate all her help with my wedding cupcakes!

4.5!

Cupkates is genius! I love following them on FB and Twitter for all of their cupcake-y updates. 

Most of the cupcakes are under $3, except for the specials. 

S'mores and Salted Caramel are my favorites, although I'm still waiting to someday try their Strawberry Champagne, which sounds decadent. 

While the cupcakes are a bit smaller than at Teacake and Love at First Bite, the convenient and mobile locations, along with the ever-changing menu is hokay by me. 

The only downside is that they generally run out within a few hours, so get there quick!

I have followed the Twitter/Facebook for some time but never had a chance to visit them until last week. I was on the freeway crossing the Bay Bridge and saw the next location they were going to be at.

I sat and waited for the truck for a min and surely it arrived on time. A small hand full of people were also hanging around the park and when all of us saw the truck, we made our way over to it. I found it amusing that we all had the same agenda for cupcakes on this afternoon.

I ordered a bakery's dozen 2 of each, Tiramisu, S'mores, Double Vanilla, Salted Caramel, Red Velvet, and Lemon Raspberry.

Here is my list, top being the Overall Best
1. Salted Caramel
2. Red Velvet
3. Double Vanilla

Unfortunately, I didn't get the chance to try them all, I bought them for my co-workers and friends and by the end of the day, I got what was left.

They were $3 each, not bad when compared to places like Sprinkles and Kara.

My baking friend loves looking at the air pockets in cakes, so she found each bite of cupcake very interesting.

I will definitely make another stop in the future and try the rest.

Delicious!

I am very interested in the other cupcakes, but I can't ever get past the red velvet cupcake. The cake is moist, the frosting is outrageously good. Everytime I eat one of these I want to jump and do one of those happy leg-kicks.

I still LOVE their cupcakes, and I'm happy that business is booming for them, but that booming business has caused them to leave some of the customers that helped make them popular behind. My friend and I begged them to come to Emeryville and while they are here it's seems they've dedicated most of their business to 64th and Hollis and have quick 30 minute stops at other E'vile locales. What's worse is when they show up it's with leftovers ( limited variety, and limited quantity ) from 64th and Hollis. I hope they diversify and spread the love a bit.

I L-O-V-E- LOVE their cupcakes.

My favorite is the Coconut Creme (they only have this on certain weeks) and if they don't have that I always go for their Red Velvet. Their cakes are super duper moist and I am NEVER disappointed.

I really thought I was over the cupcake craze, but then I had one of Cupkate's tiramisu cupcakes at the OTG event at Fort Mason last Friday.  That single cupcake got me back on the band wagon!  I usually don't like too much frosting, because it can be a little too sweet and overpowering at times, but they do it right!  The cake was moist and light, and the frosting complimented it perfectly...not too sweet and it was nice and fluffy.  I also tried their red velvet, which was also delicious.  I can't wait to try the rest of their flavors!  I'll keep you posted on my favorites!

I tried a CupKates cupcake for the first time tonight at Off the Grid in North Berkeley. I ate a S'mores cupcake and it was delicious. Usually I'm all about the frosting when it comes to cupcakes - a lot of places just have dry, or overly dense cake, but the cake in this cupcake was perfectly moist and light, but still flavorful and rich enough where I felt like it was totally worth the probably ridiculous amount of calories, etc. And the s'mores "icing" definitely tasted like burnt marshmallow - it was just so well done! There was even graham cracker on the bottom. *sigh,* I want another already! 

Random side note (and this is also in my review of OTG so I'm sorry for any redundancy), but I had a totally awkward interaction with the guy who sold me my cupcakes and I just want to say, if you're out there, I did NOT mean to insult your business! I made an awkward comment where I was trying to compare buying a cupcake from a truck to buying ice cream from an ice cream truck as a kid, but it totally failed, and was super awkward. So, yeah, I didn't mean to sound like an ass - your cupcakes are awesome, and thanks for being so cool even though my comment was understandably misconstrued to be kind of insulting!

My friend and I got the salted caramel and the red velvet.

Normally I'm wary about cupcakes because they tend to be dry.

NOT THESE!

The insides were super moist.  I loooved my chocolate cupcake with the salted caramel frosting... and there was enough frosting for every bite.

The red velvet was good too.

The salted caramel frosting tasted really buttery though.. sort of felt sick afterwards.. almost.. slimey? or.. i don't know.. it was good tho!  (the cream cheese frosting on the red velvet didn't taste as.. fatty).


Don't know if this is "woo hoo!" as good as it gets.  but it's pretty dang good!
I am HOOKED on the salted caramel ones, absolutely to die for!

I meant to write an update to the review for Cupkates earlier, but it managed to slip my mind during the holiday madness. I decided to give it another try a couple of weeks ago. I got the salted caramel cupcake and tried my sister's tiramisu. I loved the tiramisu cupcake. the salted caramel was also pretty good, but the tiramisu is where it's at. The frosting for the salted caramel still wasn't my favorite. While Cupkates probably wouldn't be my top choice for cupcakes in the Bay Area, I think I was a little too hard on them the first time around.

There are cupcakes and then there are CupKates.

I really enjoyed trying my first Cupkate the other day. Just amazing Red Velvet and Smores.

Parked on 4th street and picked up a few. Tried the Key Lime, Red Velvet, Strawberry Rhubarb, Salted Caramel (my personal favorite), & Guinness Chocolate.

What surprised me about these cupcakes was the frosting. Usually the frosting is too sweet which offsets the taste of the cupcake. With Cupkates, it complimented the cupcake very well.

Would definitely recommend going early, around 12pm as they tend to sell out around 3pm (or earlier).
I went all the way to Downtown Oakland (from the Cal campus) for a red velvet and salted caramel cupkates.  Yummers.  Please come back to the Cal campus!!!

Buddha Dharma Sangha!  If you're into the little domes of cakey bliss wrapped in paper, then track down this truck, fell trees across the road, or set tires on fire to get their attention.  

I experience several minutes of mind-numbing bliss when I have one of their desserts with a cup of tea.  Try the Key Lime, or the S'Mores, or play it safe with the Red Velvet.  

Earn the undying gratitude of your office by bringing a box next time instead of donuts.

Yum! 

Red velvet: moist delicious, great frosting, not to sweet. Totally hit the spot!

Smores: the marshmallow topping was delicious, the cake was chocolatey moist, and a perfect combo w/ the topping

Salted Caramel: YUMMMM! The salt went with the sweetness so well, the entire cake was delicious. 

Vanilla bean cheesecake: a little too vanilla-beany for my taste. I typically love cheesecake and vanilla bean, but I could only finish half of the cake.

To sum it up, delightfully delicious!

Out of all these fancy, schmancy cupcake places I've been to, Cupkates is #1 on my list. I look forward to seeing where they are located every week on my Twitter feed cuz if I'm in the area, then you can guarantee that I will be there, waiting in line. Their cupcakes are not too sweet, are very moist, and not clobbered up with a bunch of frosting, which are requirements in my book for a good cupcake. 

+1 star for taking credit cards, which is a rarity in the food truck world!
The Twinkle cupcake is what a Twinkie can only dream of being.  Moist, gooey decadence.  'nuff said.

Is there a 12 Step Program for Cupcakes?

I need help.

This place was good, the cupcakes were pretty tasty. I was a bit disappointed though, I was hoping for something more after reading all the good reviews. When I buy baked goods, I like to get things that I couldn't make myself. They did have some interesting spins on your average cupcake. The cupcakes are pretty small too. It's worth trying, but I wouldn't go to far out of my way to find the truck. The Cupkate truck is  great concept though!

Ahh, the mobile cupcake craze. Cupkates definitely plays into those who follow the Twitter feeds and find themselves crisscrossing the East Bay to get a taste of those luscious cuppies. 

They have a regular gig at the Beehive Market on Saturdays in Berkeley and lately I have found myself standing at the Cupkates truck contemplating which flavor in which to indulge. 

To date, I've noshed on: 
Double chocolate - good frosting, not too sweet. 
Strawberry - real strawberries incorporated and not overly sweet.
S'mores - sickly sweet, just like the campfire treat. 

Cupkates definitely has some good flavor combos being offered from the confines of their mobile business.

THE MOST MOIST, DELECTABLE AND FABULOUSLY DELICIOUS CUPCAKES I HAVE EVER COME ACROSS.

Yes, my adoration for Cupkates required my review to be in all caps. 
Salted caramel, S'mores &/or Tiramisu every time.

Many people have been talking about Cupkates, so I decided to give it a try. I asked which flavor is the most popular, and the lady said Salted Caramel. Honestly, I am tired of Salted Caramel. It is probably one of the most overdone flavors of this year. I also do not like chocolate cake at all, and I didn't want to spend $3 on a cupcake that I won't eat. So I asked which other flavors there were, and she said Tiramisu is a staff favorite. 

$3 - Tiramisu: Take a bite of the frosting...Mmmm, light and whipped like whipped cream. Take a bite of the cake...Mmm, subtle coffee flavor. Nice and moist. Not too moist, but not dry at all. The best surprise was at the bottom of the cupcake! A ladyfinger crust. It was really nice to have a kind of cookie at the bottom! :) Delicious. 

I don't think that the cupcakes are small at all. Seriously, a five foot Asian girl like me cannot eat a HUGE cupcake. I tried Sprinkles and honestly, it was way too sweet and way too big. I feel like if I ate a huge cupcake, I'd gain five pounds! I didn't even eat the whole thing because I wanted my boyfriend to have some! But I like how the cupcake was not too sweet, but sweet enough. I hate when things are so sweet that it makes me thirsty. But this did not. :)

It's true that I haven't met an OTG truck I didn't like.  But oh my god, this truck is amazing.  If you happen to run into them when they have seasonal key lime or lemon meringue just stop in your tracks and buy a dozen... Feed them to your family, coworkers, random strangers.... they will all love you forever.  
Other flavors are pretty fantastic, too... red velvet, smores... yum.

I waited for the cupkate truck today, and I'm sure we all looked pretty silly, about 50 women and 5 men lined up for cupcakes.  If you wondering which corner to stand on, the truck actually parks in front of the shoe shop on 12th.  

I got two cupcakes, the raspberry lemon and the chocolate caramel with sea salt, I was very appreciative that she gave me a box.  The cake portion of both cupcakes I liked a lot, it was moist, very fresh, and tasty.

The frosting on the other hand, I did not really care for because it was too creamy and moist...probably flavored buttercream; I like more of a solid consistency frosting.  The raspberry frosting reminded me of raspberry yogurt.  The caramel frosting, had a light hint of caramel, but it was too runny for me.  I'm hoping when I come back that the double vanilla cupcake will have the topping I'm looking for, or even the twinkie cupcake with it's marshmallow flavoring.

Funny story - this lady walks up to the line and starts talking to the people in front of me about the cupcakes.  As the line moves forward it is obvious she is trying to merge in line, even though she doesn't actually know the people she is talking to.  When they go up to the counter to place their order, the lady turns to me and says in a low voice "Hey, can I give you some cash to buy me a cupcake?"  because she obviously does not want to get in the long line.  Absolutely hilarious, made me feel like I was part of something shady, so I bought her her cupcake, although I'm sure other people were annoyed.

Let's get the Yelp bitness out of the way:

~~~ Best c-cakes ever.  
~~~ Puts Cako, Teacake, and all the other c-cake shops in the dirt.
~~~ Red velvey, salted carm, and dubz choco are where it's at.

Okay, pleasure time:

I've honestly thought about carjacking the Cupkate van with Kate in it.  Yeah yeah, you can judge and say to yourself , "Well, that would be kidnapping."

Damn right it would be kidnapping.  It would also be cupcakenapping. And Cupkates would be all mine.

BTW... cupcakenap sounds like the best thing ever.

I'm torn between which to claim is the best cupcakes in the Bay. Love at First Bite, I heart you and you know it! I first had my taste of Cupkates after visiting Flight 101 - where the truck usually parks in front of.

We were told by the awesome Flight 101 staff about the truck. Her supervisor actually won the "make up your own flavor" contest which her prize was three dozen FREE cupcakes!!!

Anyways, we fell in line which was already long. While we were in line, we heard a variety of stories like this one man who buys all the Vanilla cupcakes (so greedy). Also while we stood in line, a college student who was also selling baked goods came over and presented that him and his friends were selling tasty goods too and that it was to help them pay for college. 

My first reaction was, "aww, that's such a bunch of baked good bull!" First off, you didn't need to go to the school you were attending. Second, you're not so broke if you're able to afford A&F jeans. Third, anyone can buy Nestle Tollhouse cookies and bake them for resale. 

Oh sorry, back to my review....

Cupkates was a delightful treat! I got the s'mores which made me want s'more! Hahaha! Get it? 

Overall, two thumbs up!

Keep an eye out for the truck or just follow the line.

Oh nooooooo! No key lime pie?!?! Say it ain't so. I made JY drive me all the way to Berkeley for KLP and they didn't have it. Instead we settled for: pumpkin spice (4.75/5 very good but I still prefer KLP), tiramisu (4.8/5 KLP is still better), salted carmel and red velvet. Man we waited over 20 mins for our cupcakes...

WOW!!!! The salted caramel cupcake was absolutely delish!

My friends and I got to the truck a bit late, around 3:30pm perhaps and they had sold out of all the flavors except for salted caramel and dark chocolate.  We didn't feel like having just a plain chocolate, so we went for the salted caramel. 

As the guy inside the truck handed me the cupcake, I could feel that the cake itself was very soft and moist.  *drool*  We shared this cupcake, since we had just come from Love At First Bite to try their cupcakes.  Unlike others I've tried, I couldn't just break a piece off.  It would crumble apart, so I ended up with just little bits of cake at a time.  Again, WOW!  The cake was extremely moist, fluffy and the frosting was just right!  Not too sweet with a touch of salt.

By far, one of the best cupcakes I've had!  I haven't tried the other flavors, but I am definitely coming back for more!

Amazing!  I love cupcakes and Cupkate's does not disappoint!!! Cake is moist and frosting is divine. Innovative flavors--some new and some classics.  Banana nutella is perfect--cake has the right amount of banana and frosting is sweet but not too sweet.  Salted caramel is a nice rich treat. Red velvet is always reliable and the s'more cupcake is spectacular--marshmallow on top and graham cracker crust on the the bottom.  Just tried the "twinkie" today and it quite possible could be a new favorite.  Definitely worth the wait in line.  

And, thanks for coming to Jack London Square, Cupkates!  We love you!

We discovered Cupkates at Off the Grid at Ft. Mason last year and can honestly say I crave it fortnightly. My husband who is a "Savory" eschews most sweets, but he never says no to a Cupkates Salted Caramel. 

Cupkates cupcakes are moist, flavorful and the frosting is just right.. perfect amount and sweetness balance. My personal favorite is the Tiramisu. Our daughter loves the Double Chocolate. Honestly though, you cannot go wrong with any of their cupcakes. 

The only downside I find is that they are limited to serving in Berkeley, SF, Oakland and have not made their presence known in the Tri-Valley area too often. Maybe this is a good thing for my muffin top, though..... :)

cited on the corner of telegraph and durant right in front of boa & smart alec's. (also cited at treasure island music festival vip backstage! dang we were spoiled - you can request a cupkates stop at well wherever you want them)

a simple, but moist and finger licking yummy red velvet with cream cheese frosting (cue drool)

they were out of their salted caramel and s'mores by the time i got there so i went with the double vanilla - can't really go wrong with vanilla bean frosting! the whole thing was perfectly sweet. i'm not too big on sweets, but i was happy :)

I'm not bagging on Teacakes, but when I crave for cupcakes, I think cupkate, and how I'd have to wait a WHOLE week to get my not-so-tiny hands on some. I salivate just thinking about them, and this usually means I probably wait no longer than a day to get my hands on ANY cupcake. Alas, if they're not cupkates, they're just not cupcakes! 

I'm so pro-Cupkates, that I think I've had just about everyone on my floor at work try them. I even have them hunting down their street locations. Now that's love.

Best cupcakes in the state of California!

I'm so not a dessert person, and I love to eat healthy foods, but Cupkates are totally my go-to items of choice when my sweet tooth needs a feeding! What I love best about Cupkates is that their cupcakes are never too sweet -- you know, when it's so sweet that it hurts your mouth a little? That's the worst. In my opinion, I would say these cupcakes are better than Sprinkles' in southern California.

I've tried most of the cupcakes here, so here are a few of my favorites:

* Red Velvet - definitely my favorite, because the cream cheese frosting is unlike anything I've ever had! Not too sweet, and yet complements the cake part so well!

* Lemon Raspberry - mMmmMm the very slight tanginess of the cake paired with raspberry frosting is simply a perfect combo!

* Double Vanilla - you might think that the "double" means like... double the sweetness, but wow... also a delicious balance!

If you live in the Berkeley/Oakland/Emeryville area, you might also find their tweets throughout the day to be helpful. They let you know where they'll be and they text you once they've sold out, which is usually anywhere from 1-3 hours. Thank you Cupkates, for the occasional servings of happiness in a cupcake! :)

Biking to berkeley is way the hell outta my way (i live in oakland and was heading to sf), but I had my eyes on the prize:

delicious red velvet.

I was thirsty... I was hot.... but I knew that this moist delicacy would be waiting
 (so moist that i bet if an emergency came up and you needed some sort of sweet liquid to survive then you could hold it over your head and squeeze this red velvet cupcake and drain its delicious juice straight into your greedy lil mouth)

i gobbled the first one up too fast because i was still breathing heavily.  didn't even give myself time to savor it.  I'll spend another 2 bucks and buy another.  YUM.

Kate has the precision of a chemist...I can't wait to find out what new flavor she bakes up!


5 stars suckas!

Oh man, this place. I came upon it once while wandering around on a lunch break and then I didn't see it for, like, a month. It was like a unicorn or something. I'd research where it would be and always inevitably miss it somehow. But last Monday I literally made it my day's goal to track them down and try the s'more cupcake. Which I did. And it was delightful. The girl that works it is also really friendly/cute and I think I kind of have a crush on her.

As others have stated, Cupkates is a tad on the pricy side when compared to the size and cost of a Sprinkles cupcake, which seems to be the standard.  But YOLO, so I gave Cupkates a try on a Friday afternoon at Off the Grid in front of SF city hall.

I got the salted caramel.  The cake was moist and had a good texture, not dry at all.  Though my precious little treat was a tad on the buttery side for my taste.  I could definitely taste the salt, there were actually large crystals of it on top, which made for an intriguing taste.  The cupcake was overall a little too sweet for me.  

Friendly service with a smile--no complaints in this area.

I've tried almost every cupcake company in the Marin, Sonoma & SF areas. The cake needs to be moist and the right density and the icing can not disappoint. We went to the Cupkates Food Truck and were just delighted with the friendly service & the perfect cupcakes! The red velvet is perfection. The salted carmel was just the right amount of sweetness & saltiness. There are no words to describe the delight in biting into the Banana Cream ....(but I'll be dreaming about that tonight.) Double Vanilla was also very very good. These are regular size cupcakes...not minis and not oversized at 
$3 a pop.

I CANNOT believe we never reviewed this. We are the worst mega-fans ever (I follow their Facebook page religiously and "Like" all of their status updates lols).

Jeff and I have climbed mountains to be graced by the sanctity of this truck. If you like moist, delicious, PERFECTLY shaped cupcakes (I swear these cupcakes look so beautiful), you MUST eat this.

We've tried, in order of lust:

* Red velvet -- hands down the BEST THING EVER. I had a dream once where I lived in it
*Double vanilla bean
* Key lime?
* S'mores
* Tiramisu -- honestly, this one was a little subpar for us  :( Maybe we are too spoiled by the "moistness" of their regular cupcakes. 

The cream cheese frosting is... just... beyond words. Thinking about it brings tears to my eyes :'(  It is just $3 of heaven. Usually we end up buying 2+ though, because there are LITERALLY tears in my eyes as I fight off whoever is trying to share it with me (usually this is Jeff).

If you haven't tried this yet, I have nothing to say to you. NOTHING!!!

If I can summarize Cupkates in two words it would be this: simply delicious. I had to give the salted caramel another try since it's their best seller. I didn't seem to like it as much the first time around, but now I consider it, along with Red Velvet and S'mores, as my top 3 choices. I could get them every time I'm at Off the Grid and not get sick of them...ever. S'mores slightly edges out Red Velvet as my absolute fave with its graham cracker "crust" at the bottom and marshmallow fluff on top. All the goodness of the real thing without the campfire or possible brush with poison ivy. Works for me! Hoping to have another run in with these guys before the OtG season ends.

Wow. I hate to be the Debbie Downer, but seriously? As a cupcake baker myself, I would probably rank Cupcates near the bottom of all the cupcake places in the entire Bay area. Yes, the cake is moist, but it's also super greasy and oily. And the buttercream is way too much butter and not nearly enough cream. And $3 for that?? Even an overrated Kara's cupcake is bigger and tastier. 

I do love my desserts, though (without dessert, is there any point in even eating?). So I do sometimes stray toward this truck if there are no other dessert options. The salted caramel and the red velvet are OK enough to eat.

Absolutely delicious! I'm in love!

I had the infamous Salted Caramel, which was as amazing as everyone claims it to be. I love that the chocolate cake is super moist and flavorful, while the icing on top isn't overly sweet. And of course, the sea salt completes the cupcake beautifully. Sea salt, caramel and chocolate make such a heavenly combination. 

I also ordered the Key Lime Pie. I'm not a huge lemon/lime dessert person; I tend to go for chocolate desserts most of the time. However, I was really curious about the graham cracker crust and the key lime pie filling, so I decided to try it. Boy, am I glad I did! It was so so good! I ate every last crumb and even gnawed at the paper cup it came in, ha!

I will definitely buy these two flavors again, and next time, I'll try the S'mores and Red Velvet, too.

These are pretty good cupcakes. Had the chocolate and the salted caramel. Light, fluffy and fresh. A bit small. Also, the salted caramel was really just a vanilla cupcake with buttercream. Not much salted caramel flavor to it. But a homemade cupcake is almost always worth at least 4 stars.

These cupcakes were so good! I got the Spicy Mexican Chocolate, which reminded me of the gelato of the same name at LUSH. I also got the Key Lime Pie, which I didn't expect to like that much. But it had a surprise filling of key lime goo and a graham cracker crust, and the meringue frosting was super tasty. I can't wait to try their other flavors! Minus one star for price, which is a little high.

The Good:  
Well who doesn't love eating food out of a truck?  I loved the graham cracker crust on the bottom of the cupcakes.  That's the one thing that separated these cupcakes from the others I've had.  The frosting was also not too sweet.

The Bad:
Really greasy cupcakes!  What?  I'm all about moist and fluffy, but come on, it got kinda gross.  And these cupcakes are tiny.  And they run out by the time I get to the front of the line.  And I'm just going to say it ... I've had better cupcakes.
