For me the bad outweighs the good.  I'm no longer excited to see the Cupkate truck.

I've had my fair share of cupcakes and they really have tasty cupcakes!!!  As for the gal who says she is a cupcake baker and says that CupKates is bad.....well she has no idea what she is talking about......seriously???  For her to say that Kara's is better.....I think not but that is just my opinion.  My faves:

Caramel Apple - yummy cake with little bits of apple in it with a delicious cinnamon frosting
Tiramisu - delicious frosting and the surprise cookie on the bottom of the cupcake

Here's the rundown...this is a mobile cupcake store meaning you have to track them down thru fb or tweets. Talk about sign of the times! Here's why this is irritating....you cannot call ahead to see what the flavors are OR how many are left. My 1st experience sent me downtown oakland to the park. It took forever to find a park near this truck. When I finally did and got out to make my purchase the guy tells me "we sold out" and proceeds to wrap it up. No sorry, no glad you did, nothing. I had 2 small children in tow and they looked as if a puppy had just been run over. He did offer me this "we'll be at off the grid later" and gave the cutest and littlest business card I've ever seen. So instead of trekking all the way home to castro valley we hang out until 5. When we finally reach OTG we were in anticipation of the greatest cupcakes ever. The vanilla was ok lots of whatever that madagascar stuff is but ok and th red velvet one was also ok but something about that particular frosting was interesting gave a greasy/fatty taste in your mouth. Idk if I would do that one again....

Very unimpressed. My husband thought their cupcakes tasted like ones from the grocery store. The frosting on their double vanilla had the consistency of a stick of butter, and we did not care for their spicy Mexican chocolate at all.

So stinkin' good.

Had the s'more cupcake (which Kate GAVE me because it had a flaw in the frosting. How nice!) that was INSANE and also got a red velvet that looked amazing. 

Get there quick because she sells out fast.

I LOVE Cupkates. 

The Bay Area's mobile cupcake truck is very much worth following via Twitter and Facebook for updates of where they'll be next. The never-ending long lines outside of the truck are also worth the wait.

I love, love, LOVE the red velvet cupcakes here. They are to die for. The cake is soft and moist, with a large dollop of creamy yet not-too-sweet cheesecake frosting on top. The consistency of the frosting is whipped and smooth. Moreover, the guy who works at the truck is very, very friendly and always provides great service. Try this place!!
The Red Velvet is AMAZING...BEST cream cheese frosting EVER!!!  The travelling cupcake idea is so genius...wish I had thought of it!!!

Now my review is just on one single little cupcake, but it was darn tot'in good.  I purchased the Spicy Mexican Chocolate Cupcake for $3, at "Off The Grid."  I liked the kick of spice that hits you when you least expect it.  Mmmm.

Half the menu was sold out by the time I got there. Which they had only been open 2 hours max. The S mores cupcake lived up to the name, however missed the mesh of the supposed flavors. nice try guys. The Tiramisu was a fail altogether. Plus really greasy. Cako has better Tiramisu thus far. I must keep trying different places out.  The double chocolate was supreme, rich and moist. It is a favorite that is unmatched. Have yet to taste the Double Vanilla. Wish me luck...............

My cupcake culinary adventure results....

Cups and Cakes Bakery 5
Love at First Bite 4.75
Mission Minis 4.15
Noe Valley Bakery & Bread Company 4
Miette Patisserie 4
Cafe Madeleine 3.75
Leonidas Chocolates 3.5

Sibbys Cupcakery 3.25
Urban Bread 3

I didn't even feel like finishing the cupcake from Cupkates.

I feel wrong for giving Cupkates only 3 stars, but I have to preserve my integrity! I love the concept of the cupcake truck and it clearly is spreading a lot of yummyness everywhere it goes, but I just don't love the cupcakes themselves. Take the red velvet for example. The cake is moist and possesses the faint chocolate taste I adore so much, but I find the frosting to be a bit greasy and oily, rather than smoothly creamy. While the cupcake looks quite cute, I wish that the frosting weren't piped so tall and so centered. When the frosting reaches 1.5" from the cupcake itself, I end up having to take a bite of pure frosting...a waste because I'd prefer to eat it with the cake part! 

Still, seeing the Cupkates truck never fails to make me smile, and I know I'll give in to getting a cupcake once in awhile when I see it invitingly parked on a street.

"Woohoo! As good as it gets!" I've never ever felt this way about a cupcake before in my ilfe. Even when I tried Sprinkle's red velvet cupcake, I wasn't phased by it. But I LOVE CupKates.

I had the privilege of trying this truck at Off the Grid: Fort Mason earlier today. I was actually going to skip this truck altogether but while waiting for creme brulee, there was no line. I thought I'd jump on this. Turns out everything was sold out!...except for the key lime. 

I was a little worried that this cupcake would be awful since no one seemed to give it any love ,but these cupcakes were definitely not awful. I have no idea why they were the last ones left. 

The cupcake was moist, light, and a right balance of tartness and sweetness. The frosting was airy and melted in your mouth.

If this flavor was the last one left at the end of the day, I can't wait to try a sold out flavor next time.
you cant get better than this love all the cupcakes..especially lemon merigue , double vanilla and salted carmel
$3 not bad for gourmet cupcakes. Tiramisu cupcake has crust at the bottom which was a pleasant surprise! It was so moist and perfecto! Keep an eye out for this truck.

When a very helpful employee of the nearby Travel 001 (http://www.yelp.com/biz/flight-001-berkeley#hrid:dCSZIepXCmqkFNuMGG1vmw) mentioned that the Cupkates truck had just pulled up and parked outside on Fourth Street in Berkeley, I knew it was fate. I flew out the door (get it, cuz the design of Travel 001's interior is made to resemble an airport terminal? :p) to find that a line of about a dozen people had already formed, and while the Double Vanilla cupcake I wanted to take my Cupkates virginity had sold out just prior to my making it to the window, my second choice (which I think actually premiered today), was the AMAZING Salted Caramel. The chocolate cake was super moist and rich... fudgy would be a appropriate way to describe it, and that was topped with a caramel buttercream frosting that melted on my tongue like whipped butter - sweetly creamy. To literally top it all off, this cupcake creation is sprinkled with flaked sea salt, which punched the caramel buttercream frosting into a different, amazing dimension than the one in which it would exist on its own. I have since followed a Twitter list of Bay Area food carts/trucks to ensure that I will know where and when CupKates' has parked the next time I am here, cuz I still wanna try that Double Vanilla... and pretty much all the others on the menu as well!

ok, I'm coming back for another review after trying this place for the 4th time.  

I would give them 4 stars because they're cupcake texture and flavor is consistent.  Hubby says he likes it more than Kara's... a big compliment to this place.
But. .... I'm coming back to review service this time.
seriously... went here on Sunday (at Crate & Barrel). got in line at 12:35 (it was hard to find parking) and there was a line... maybe 15 people ahead of me.  20 mins later, only 5 people got served.. in short it took me more than an hour to get a cupcake...
it shouldn't take that long to get cupcakes... especially when there is only 6 flavors to choose from.  I thought the whole point of a truck is convenience... well their service is not that convenient. 
at this time, after tasting most of cupcakes in the area... their cupcakes is definitely not worth 1 hour in line.

*begin edit*
I just tried my coworker's Smore cupcake.  It is amazing.  I think Kate does do a GREAT job on the chocolate cupcakes... she just needs to work on her basic yellow/white cake mix.
*end edit*

I was so excited when I saw this truck parked strategically next to the 24 hour fitness that I work out in... so I ran back to my office (after my work out of course), grabbed a coworker and headed back to the truck.  


Here's the assessment of each cupcake:

Double Vanilla Cupcake ~
I LOVE vanilla cupcakes (if they are well done) and they are my absolute favorite type of cupcake... so boring, right?  But they are extremely difficult to perfect... because you don't want them to be boring vanilla, you want them to be amazing.  Even though the husband (wife bakes, husband drives truck) claimed these to be his favorite and also mentioned how fresh the vanilla was... I was eager to try them.  What a DISAPPOINTMENT.  
- The frosting was average for what it is.
- The cake tastes like a mouthful of flour.
- Cake texture is dense, almost like a pound cake.
- Cake however, is moist, so at least we know these cakes are fresh.

Lemon Raspberry Cupcake ~
- I'm not sure why I got this one because I'm not really fond of lemon baked goods (except I really like my meyer lemon cupcakes... maybe b/c they are not lemon cake but lemon filling).  
- Nice raspberry flavor to the frosting.  Tastes like jam, probably not fresh.
- Texture of lemon cake is the same as Vanilla.
- Cake has a good amount flavor (not a mouthful of flour), definitely not fresh lemon, uses some sort of lemon flavoring.

Salted Caramel Cupcake ~
Out of the 3, this is my favorite cupcake.  Kate has obviously mastered her chocolate cake.
- Frosting is a bit on the sweet side, but hey, it's caramel!  :)  Absolutely delicious.  Would appreciate a bit more of the salty contrast... but it's pretty good as it is.
- Cake is moist and and soft, as should a cupcake be.

Summary/Conclusion: It looks like Kate uses cooked frosting for most of her cupcakes (except maybe the smores, that may be marshmallow creme)... so if you don't like heavy buttercream-like frosting, these babies may not be for you.  

Her chocolate cake is perfect.  Nice and moist as you can tell but touching the top of the cake (slightly sticky but SOFT).  Her other cakes may need a bit more work as the tops are hard like pound cake.  I'm assuming that she's not using cake flour b/c of the texture of these cakes and the fact that the vanilla has an overwhelming taste of flour.  

I might come back again just to try the other flavors, but for $3 a cake, I'd save your money and go elsewhere.  There are so many amazing bakeries in Berkeley.  (If I do comeback though, I might just get the Salted Caramel cake b/c it's pretty decent.  I'm not too fond of cooked frosting in general though.)

Simply the BEST Double Vanilla and Red Velvet Cupcake. I am a regular, especially when they would make a stop near my work in Emeryville. Kate and KC are good to their loyal customers. Will always be a fan!

I LOVE RED VELVET!!! Cupkates is right on the money when it came to the red velvet.  It was SUPER moist, even after I put it in the fridge and oOoh soOo good when you take a bite!  This is better than Marita's Sweet Potato Pie Co.(I'm sorry, it used to be my first choice and cupkates won me over).  My cousin and I also got the salted caramel and that sea salt definitely made a huge difference, the frosting is creamy and a little buttery light.  

One advice, eat these goodies right away and DO NOT put them in the fridge!!! because it alters some of the flavoring AND, order at least 4 flavors.. ha haha

I think cupcakes are a fad and dying out- and am usually pretty cynical about cupcake shops...but Cupkates is REALLY good. My favorite is (and will continue to be) their red velvet, when I finish I always wish I had another one...or two. The people working in the truck are always really fun and friendly. 

I've only found them on 4th Street in Berkeley so far, and are parked out in front of Crate and Barrel. They take credit cards too (thank goodness!).

For $3, it's a nice treat!

i was never big on the cupcake hype (i'm sorry, i know i'm offending like 90% of you).  but they're just little cakes.  big whoop.

then cupkates rolled around.  literally, rolled around.  the first time i tried cupkates' cupcakes was during my first week at work; there was a lot of hype and people waited over 20 mins in line.  by the time i got to the front, i couldn't decide between the eight or so flavors, so i ended up getting three.  doesn't sound so bad, right?  but what if i told you i ate all three.  by myself.  on the same day.  yea.  only cupkates.

i think i've tried almost all flavors, except for the most recent ones.  almost all of them are worthy of four/five stars, but the standout for me is the seasonal key-lime pie.  it's the perfect combination of sweet and tart with a delightful lime curd in the center.  other favorites are the double chocolate and s'mores.

for a person who was never big on cupcakes, i find myself constantly tracking cupkates' whereabouts and thinking about that coveted key-lime.  i guess i get the cupcake hype now.  or at least the cupkates hype.

I got a small box of cupcakes for an afternoon baby shower yesterday as the mom to be loves cupcakes - mix of red velvet and salted caramel.  What a rude surprise when I opened the box.  The frosting on the red velvets were splatted every which way - imagine if you took a knife and just squashed the hell out of the frostings so that it was beyond messy- that's what it was like.  And no, it did not happen during the drive - not only was I careful, but the other flavors were perfectly fine, just ALL of the red velvets.  The thing that makes me mad is that the guy could have told me about this as there is no way he could have put them in the box and NOT noticed.  I would have gotten the other flavors.  It's really stupid on their part because everyone at the shower asked what the hell happened to the red velvets and when I told them the story, people got a very bad impression of Cupkates as we could not believe anyone would sell a product that looked like that.  It was truly attrocious and ruined the lovely gift I took time out from work to drive over and get.

Im sure the cupcakes are quite delicious... How ever to my chagrin I wouldnt know. For weeks now I have been trying to track down this mobile truck of deliciousness. I have twitted them request and questions about locations and emailed them location request (which is what the website instructs patrons to do). But I have never received a response or an acknowledgment of any sort. Even when trying to use their website and twitter feed to locate them their updates are sparse at best.  Its very disappointing to have such a wonderful product and care so little about customer satisfaction. I mean what does a girl have to do to get a freakin cupcake around here? I am not faulting them for being busy, but if you are instructing people to email and track the truck down using social media websites you may want to consider actually using them yourself!

Had a couple of these when they were at Off the Grid Civic Center.

Salted Caramel - needed more caramely flavor for the mention in the name. Otherwise tasty.

Lemon Raspberry - yummy flavors together

The frosting is piled way to high for the cupcake resulting in frosting on your nose for the first bite and no frosting left for the last bite.

Also bought a single cupcake that I wanted to eat back at work - told me no boxes for single cupcake. BOO!

We tried these cupcakes the other day and we were not very impressed. The cupcakes were some what dry and the cake it self lacked decent flavor. It seems like they bank on their frosting for most of the flavor but that wasn't very good ether. I say stay home and make your own and they will be just as good and you get 24 for $4 instead of paying $8.50 for 3. Also she doesn't really think out her parking spots to well, there was no parking other than a 5 min loading spot any where within 300 yards of her truck.

Also Kate if you read this make more red velvet cupcakes. They seem to sell out the fastest so it's obviously your bread and butter.

As a huge fan of cupcakes, I'm constantly searching for new bakeries that sell these delicious treats.  So when I read about Cupkates in the newspaper, I knew I had to follow them on Facebook.  First time 
I followed them was in Berkeley.  We got there 10 minutes before the truck arrived, so we were the second ones in line.  By the time we finished paying and got our cupcakes, the line was already almost a block long! 
We ordered a dozen cupcakes because we wanted to try all the flavors they have.  My favorites were the s'mores and salted caramel.  The s'mores cupcake was moist and not overly sweet. It had a crunchy graham crust and toasted marshmallow frosting.  At first bite, it immediately became my favorite.  The salted caramel came in second.  It's frosting was light and fluffy with a distinct taste of caramel sprinkled with sea salt.  Kudos to Kate for creating a perfect caramel frosting that's not overpowering and heavy! The Guiness, chocolate and red velvet cupcakes were also great. 
I've only had the chance to try Cupkates twice since the truck is usually in the east bay and I live in the peninsula.  Lately, they have been coming to Off the Grid at Fort Mason, so I think it's time to pay 'em another visit!

These cupkates are no joke.


 The best cupcakes I've had..I can't think of a time when I've had better ones.  

(I feel like cupcakes run an easy risk of being too dry, and the frosting being too heavy and buttery.  Not these cupcakes!)

The frosting is so light, airy, whipped, and it works really well with the cake underneath. 

Each cake flavor/type had such an impressive consistency and was very soft, the right amount of moist, very very good! 

It was also not heavy at all, everything was fluffy and light. 

Flavors I've had:  (I do like their special flavors, but their staples - first 4 below - are the best.)
-  Red Velvet
-  Salted Caramel
-  Tiramisu
-  S'mores
-  Spicy Mexican Chocolate
-  Mango Curd
-  Lemon Meringue


Locations in Financial District:
-  Wednesdays, Montgomery and Market.  
-  Fridays, Sansome and Bush.

Tried Cupkates for the first time today.  Got a S'mores and a Double Chocolate.

Double Chocolate Cupcake: Cake was kind of...greasy.  Didn't really taste like butter :(  tasted more like boxed cake mix, which really surprised me, since I had heard good things about Cupkates.  Chocolate frosting was also kind of...oily, though it had a nice hint of bitterness/coffee to help it from just being sweet.  

S'mores: this was, better. Marshmallow fluff had the s'mores treatment on top (fire).  Graham cracker crust was alright. But again, the chocolate cake was greasy.  At least the cake wasn't dry, like some cupcakes I've had.

As much as I adore the concept of mobile cupcakes, I doubt I will try them again.

Wow this place has it going on!!! They are the nicest people helpful. I *HEART* cupcakes... you have no idea. I was walking down 4th Street in Berkeley and it's like the clouds parted, the heavens sung and behold a glorious cupcake truck was parked there. Hell to the yes... cupcake time for me. They're all fresh, spongy, beautiful cupcakes that are homemade heaven! 

The smores cupcake is to die for!!! They have a graham cracker crustish cupcake bottom and a slightly torched marshmallow top with a chunk of chocolate. It's magic in my mouth!!! The red velvet was great too. You can find them on Twitter and stalk them... I highly recommend it!!

woohoo!  i was able to finally get to the truck before it running out.  Stopped off in Jack London yesterday while my girls were sleeping in the car.  Pulled the car up right in front and ordered 1 of everything.  YES 1 of everything and I tasted each one of them.  Not a single one I didnt like.  I did eat the ENTIRE red velvet all in 1 sitting.  It's been awhile since i've liked a cupcake that much.  The red velvet had a perfect amount of cream cheese frosting and not totally sweet and I can actually taste the cream cheese flavor.  The cake was nice and moist and not overly oily!

The other flavors that I tried was Double Vanilla, Double Chocolate, Key Lime Pie, Lemon Rasperry and Salted Caramel.  I think they are my new favorite cupcake place.  Just sucks because they do run out and it's a far drive for me.

I can only review based on the 2 cupcakes I was able to try out.  The red velvet is definitely drier than most red velvet cupcakes I have tried around the bay area.  Maybe because I didn't eat the cupcake RIGHT away?  The frosting was a bit too soft for my taste. There was no substantial thickness to it while I was biting into the cupcake.  Not enough flavor.  The cake itself was not too sweet which is good but dry.  

I preferred the s'more cupcake over the red velvet.  There is a crunch at the bottom of the cake to imitate the graham cracker of the smore.  The marshmellow frosting was delicious.

For these small cupcakes.. the prices are a bit pricy!  At least sprinkles and kara's are bigger for about the same price!  The cupcake truck runs around the bay so check them out at their website or track them down with twitter if you are in dying need of cupcakes to be delivered to your door!!!  Not a bad alternative for a cupcake filled van driving around.. but just not quite CRAVING worthy of my tummy!

A cupcake truck!! *covers mouth and points* How awesome is that?

I've been told by a couple of friends that I HAVE to try the cupcakes from Cupkates. I finally got my lazy but to one of these OTG things and had cupkates on my mind the entire time. Me and a friend got the Lemon Meringue Pie Cupcakes and come to think of it, we got the LAST three!!! LUCKY us!! =) 

Now onto the highlight of my day...
LEMON MERINGUE PIE CUPCAKE- Tasted exactly like a lemon merignue pie, if not BETTER. =X The cake was very moist and the best part was the FILLING, yes the darn thing was filled with lemon custard which was a little tart (not overly tart at all) and just as refreshing as a cup of lemonade on a scortching hot day! =) The meringue sitting on top of the cupcake was light, airy, creamy and topped with my favorite topping...toasted coconut!! If they hadn't run out of these things, I would have gotten 6...FOR MYSELF!!

Next OTG I'm getting cupcakes from Cupkates before getting anything else because they run out of cupcakes FAST!

Vivian D. raves about Cupkates all the time. One day, after dinner, she told me that she had bought a strawberry rhubarb flavor cupcake from Cupkates for me but had forgotten to bring it. Call that a dessert tease but I thought maybe it was time for me to finally check out this cupcake truck.

Made my way to the Thursday's off the grid over at haight and bought myself a red velvet and a salted caramel cupcake. Both had intense flavors and the texture of the cake was soft and moist. The salted caramel cupcake was too moist, so moist that the cake was flimsy and almost soggy but it was still delicious! 

So far so good, I'll agree with Vivian D. that so far this place does sell the best cupcake with both great flavors and textures. Will be back to try other flavors!

I was lucky enough to have lunch with a girlfriend and since she works in Emeryville, I was able to partake in some awesome eats in my old hood and discover the newest incarnation of the "taco truck" trend that has become ever so popular. 

This was the first time I had ever seen a "cupcake truck" in real life. We decided to stop to see what we could find and sadly, by the time we made it through the line, most of the cupcakes I had wanted to try were sold out so I decided to get one of each flavor that was left. I brought them home for our Friday night dessert and as a family, we tried(devoured) all four.

The cupcakes we tried were: 
-Smores (really nice contrast from graham cracker bottom to marshmallow topping. Husband thought it needed more topping)
-Banana Caramel (Daughter liked this one best-I thought it was good but not enough of a banana punch)
-Twinkies(This was the husbands favorite-not too sweet)
-Chocolate PB(This was my favorite and perfect)

Service in the truck is efficient and they take credit cards which is always a plus. Each cupcake runs between $2.50 and $3.50 I think. 

I must say it is probably a good thing I no longer work in Emeryville or with all of these new eats off of trucks, not only would I be giving up my Jewish American Princess persona, I would be adding at least a couple of new dimples to my ass!

If dessert were a religion & it was a sin to NOT eat cupcakes, my confession would go something like this....'Forgive me FoodGod for I have sinned, my last cupcake review was over six months ago...'

Because of Cupkates' tempting & ever-present truck at Off the Grid Fort Mason, cupcake moratorium has been lifted (my $3-a-day habit had become expensive & unhealthy.)

I've tried two flavors ($3 each):
* strawberry rhubarb: a white cake topped with strawberry buttercream with a rhubarb filling. I liked the classic combo & the balance of sweet & tart. 
* salted dulce de leche: chocolate cake topped with a caramel-flavored frosting/drizzle & sea salt. I'm not usually a fan of chocolate cake but again, what a winning flavor combo. 

The cake is super moist. A+ for that! But what is going on with the buttercream frosting?! The texture is in need of sugar or something to cut the buttery-ness. It's super firm, almost plasticky...like eating a slightly softened stick of buttah, baby. The flavor is amazing, but can I get some fluffiness in my favorite part of a cupcake?! Their ginger lemon was beckoning, so I'll have to try that next week.

Thanks to Off the Grid, this East Bay cupcake truck is now frequently in San Francisco! My friends raved about Cupkates long before OtG's existence, but I never took the time to look for it. 

Now that it's more conveniently located, I have had not 1, not 2, but 5 different flavors!

In the order of my favorite to least favorite...

1) SALTED CARAMEL: super moist chocolate cake! fluffy caramel buttercream. drizzle of caramel. sprinkle of sea salt. divine combination! (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/zqvFNZq8q86V7QOcpURcSg?select=pOOjy-Ol4rgVlfhR5ZviXw)

2) RED VELVET: my favorite red velvet. moist cake. strong cocoa presence. yummy cream cheese buttercream. best part -  not overly sweet. (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/zqvFNZq8q86V7QOcpURcSg?select=b0CKQUh1WBbFbAtzzVFJ5Q)

3) PUMPKIN SPICE: seasonal flavor. dense cake, almost muffin like. pumpkin and cinnamon. delicious. (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/zqvFNZq8q86V7QOcpURcSg?select=nhcrmZeBkMWQkCssYXA32g)

4) TIRAMISU: dense cake. light hint of espresso. lady finger bottom. mascapone frosting. did not taste like tiramisu.

$3/pop. Salted Caramel all the way!!

update~ 
PEANUT BUTTER CHOCOLATE: moist chocolate cake! fluffy peanut butter buttercream! delicious!!!! (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/zqvFNZq8q86V7QOcpURcSg?select=jMEbpPrCd4f0cPRE2LcjMA)

I think this mobile cupcakery is the best thing about Off the Grid Upper Haight.  It's hard not to smile when you walk up to the window and see seven trays of cupcakes. Cupcakes are topped with a tall dollop of frosting.

Cupcake flavors ($3 each): Red Velvet, S'mores, Lemon Raspberry, Twinkie, Salted Caramel, Double Vanilla, Double Chocolate

* Lemon Raspberry cupcake: Moist lemon cake with tiny bits of lemon peel.  Soft, smooth, creamy raspberry buttercream frosting that wasn't that sweet. I like how the frosting had more flavor other fruity buttercream frostings I've tried.

The cupcake was really fresh, natural tasting and truly scrumptious. I also like how they have classic and creative/fun flavors.

I'm not a sweet-tooth kind of person, I don't mind skipping dessert after dinner.  But OOHH man! does this place gets me giddy every time I see them.  I've had a lot of so-so cupcakes around the bay area and THIS PLACE TOPS THEM ALL!!  Each cupcake is different an you can tell that they really know what they're doing and know how to please!

I would highly recommend (if they serve it) Tiramisu and Banana Creme Pie cupcakes.  Both are fantastic and out of this world.  It's kind of indescribable, but I can say they have their own filling inside and the frostings are different (for all cupcakes).  If they don't have those two their Double Vanilla and Red Velvet cupcakes are my second place runners up.

They're the only place I'll buy cupcakes from.

Love these cupcakes. Initially I told myself why the heck would anyone want to pay $3 for a cupcake? I then thought of the multiple times I've been to Bristol Farms and paid $5 for a cupcake. Perhaps I would give place a shot after all. The cupcakes are so cute with the frosting swirling to the top like a little pillow of frosting atop a cupcake. The two items I ordered were the chocolate / peanut butter cupcake and the vanilla bean cheesecake. The way that the cheesecake was the menu I thought it was a cheesecake cupcake but it was cheesecake instead. No matter I guess I could try them both. I was running late so I got to work and had to refrigerate them and eat them a couple of hours later. 

I took them out of the refrigerator and was amazed they were still intact, cream wasn't falling over. I took a spoon and took my first bite of the cheesecake. Instantly you taste the cream cheese and vanilla beans. Yes real vanilla beans, you can see the specs throughout the cheesecake. Next I would try the cupcake. I thought the cupcake itself without the frosting would be dense, lifeless and tasteless. I peeled back the wrapper and bit in. It was so moist, so airy, so fluffy. Instantly the peanut butter frosting and the chocolate cupcake mixed and it was heaven.

I will definitely look for this truck whenever I'm out and about.

I get cupcakes from here every Tuesday of the month. It's the reason I love Tuesdays. Ridiculous right? But CuKate's Cupcakes are AMAZING. Simply moist, great tasting and the icing... OH the icing... A little pricey at $3.00 a piece, but who cares, you can't put money on a cake tasting like that. 

Definitely try this treat truck. Hands down WAAAAY better than Kara's cupcakes in walnut creek!
The lemon meringue is by far my favorite.  It has a nice graham cracker crust, lemon filling and topped with marshmallow frosting.  It's a shame I live in NY.  Otherwise I would buy one every week.

We tried Cupkates at Off the Grid.  Awesome business decision for them, as there were very few desserts to be had at the Fort Mason OTG that day.

We got a red velvet, smores, and salted caramel.  I'll start with the red velvet.  The cake was good, but not amazing - moist, good texture, but nothing to write home about.  The frosting was overly sweet but good texture as well.  The s'mores cupcake  had great flavor, but when you unwrap it (don't we always?) the graham crackers fall into your lap.  Shouldn't these be formed into a crust of some sort instead of just being placed into the bottom of the cupcake paper?  It ended up being a very messy end to an otherwise good dessert.  Thankfully, i ate the salted caramel last.  It was DELICIOUS.  Moist, tender, sweet and the salt added the perfect kick and crunch.  Yum!

Now if this petite cupcakes were about $0.50 less I'd be giving them another star.  But for the price, I expect more cupcake.

I feel a cupcake truck creates a sense of scarcity from the temporal nature which thus dictates a hoarding response of buying more than you can actually consume at the moment.  Obviously not freshly baked because there is only so much you can do in  a truck, but likely made earlier in the morning.  A good variety of flavors and a level of quality that can rival other cupcake joints around town (...though still pales in comparison to the cupcake dominance in NYC).

Salted Caramel: Vanilla cake base with a slightly caramel-y and slightly salty frosting.  Was hoping for the richness of a dulce de leche, but was more like a vanilla buttercream frosting with a slight caramel edge.

S'Mores: Ever so slightly brûléed marshmallow frosting on a devil's food cake base with a small crumbled graham cracker bottom.  Was hopping for more burntness on the marshmallow, but was still decent. 

Tiramisu: I would have called this a mocha cupcake.  Same devil's food cake base as the s'mores, but with a slightly coffee, slightly chocolate frosting.  It was hard for me to draw parallels to the indulgent soaked lady finger Italian dessert.

Red Velvet: A standard measuring stick for me when comparing cupcake places.  The cake base was moist, thankfully not too dry, which is where some others failure.  The cream cheese frosting had a good balance of sweet versus natural cream sourness, unfortunately the texture was a bit denser than I'd like.  Overall, a very good effort.

Vanilla Bean Cheesecake: Not a cupcake.  I love when people use real vanilla beans instead of vanilla bean extract (or worse... imitation vanilla!).  There really wasn't much "cake" in cheesecake since it was molded into a mini-foil cup.  Smooth and lighter than a slice you'd get in NYC.  Lots of great vanilla bean bits in every spoonful.
Tiramusu!!!

We've run into this cupcake truck a few times on our walk to the campus (for football or basketball games) and partaken twice.  Yesterday, I had the red velvet (the 1st time we had their cupcakes, they were out of red velvet which are my favorite).  Yum!  The cake is moist and not dense.  The frosting is creamy and light.  I had to walk away so that I don't order and eat another one.

I'm a huge cupcakes fan, so when I heard about this moving vehicle full of delicious cupcakes I had to hunt it down! The cupcakes themselves are about $2.75-3 each, depending on the flavor. I think I've tried their S'mores, Red velvet, Twinkies, Banana Nutella, and Salted Carmel. 

They used to have little cartons of milk for 25 cents, but they stopped because people weren't buying them. One time I got milk to go with my cupcake, and it turned out to be spoiled! They were nice enough to give me another milk and my money back yay.

What have the GODs done to me to deserve a Cupcake Van!!!!!!!!

I swear...if I could eat anything all day without gaining weight it would be CUPCAKES!!!!!!!!!

Cupkates for sure are one of my favorites!!!  Not only are the cupcakes great tasting and affordable you can also follow them on facebook and twitter to find out where the truck will be so that you never miss them!!!  GREAT IDEA!!!

Of course my favorites are the Red Velvet and Salted Caramel!  YUMMY!!!
They also have a great Lemon Raspberry cupcake that is soooo moist and sooooo good.  You can actually taste the lemon peel!!! KUDOS to that for freshness!!!

Thanks Cupkates for always being there for me :)

THE DISCOVERY:
After driving around looking for a Safeway, bakery or any place that sold a cupcake on a lazy Sunday afternoon I turned down Fourth Street in Berkeley and found CupKates parked along the curb, my sign that the universe guided me so I can complete my birthday surprise for my cupcake! Woo Woo 

THE VIBE:
A busy line in front of the truck, but I think it's the playfulness of buying anything from a tricked out truck.

THE SERVICE:
Customer friendly.  Patient.

THE GOODS:
1.  The Salted Caramel cupcake was one of my two choices.  Cake a bit on the dry side lacked a real chocolate flavor.  But the frosting was tasty, love the salt flakes and an honest caramel flavored butter cream, I give the frosting a 4 star and cake a 2 star an overall of  a star it was aiight. 

THE BAD:
1. Red Velvet: I don't know why I keep order red velvet everywhere else.  Shame on me... I'm not going to bother commenting on it.

OVERALL:
I love the idea of a cupcake truck.  The cakes are dry and lack luster.  But if you have a craving and see the truck around, its good to support local business.

Cupcakes on wheels....oh boy....now you're talking!!! I seriously tried for so long to go down to this yummy truck stand but for whatever reason I would always miss it or they'd get sold out. I first found out about this place on live 105's morning show and i was quick to follow her on twitter. I tried once to go down near the CAL campus to swipe up some goodies but the traffic impeded and by the time we arrived they had sold out so i was sooooo sad and angry lol. But one day as I was strolling around Berkley's 4th street on my way to the MACA cosmetics store I saw the truck and went and got some goodies. I bought 6, literally one of each. The Red Velvet was to die for and the smore was great. The strawberry was OK but I still enjoyed the goodies. I adore cupcakes!!

I've never been what you call a cupcake fanactic but I'm a changed woman! My co-workers turned me onto "Cupkates" when I started at my new job in June, and I'm now a fan on Facebook.

So far, I've tried the Red Velvet, Vanilla/Vanilla, S'mores, and the new Key Lime Pie. While I wasn't too fond of the Vanilla/Vanilla frosting the rest of them simply put me in a sweet place.

I tried the new Key Lime Pie cupcake today...dee-lish! The graham cracker bottom crust was wonderful, and the key lime dollop in the center was perfect--not too sweet, not too tart.

Roll on Cupkates, roll on : )

We happened upon this truck while shopping near the 4th Ave. one Sunday afternoon. They don't carry gluten-free cupcakes so we got a regular chocolate cupcake. It was moist and very sweet. The frosting was also very sweet. The cupcake was fresh and cute and the lady on the truck was very friendly. We only tried one cupcake so could not tell anything special about it, but it sure was at a convenient location in the shopping district for those who need a break from shopping and get some sugar high.

Effin' all-star trip to the Cupkates truck ran into JANE S. AND CHRISTA V. wooooo!

Picked up salted caramel, double chocolate, and lemon raspberry. Pretty satisfied with the moistness and frosting flavor so I gotta give the thumbs up to Cupkates for a mini treat!

Salted caramel winner winner chicken dinner.

The truck takes card. Woohoo!

I've seen this food truck around a lot but most people told me to turn away from it. I chose to finally try it for once.

Service is nice. 

I ordered the Salted Caramel cupcake for $3. It looked really good. Chocolate cupcake, caramel buttercream dollop, caramel drizzle, and a sprinkle of sea salt. Looked decadent! 

I took one bite and I thought it was...an okay cupcake. The cake part wasn't too bad. The frosting was actually much too buttery for me so I couldn't eat much of that at all. 

I expected more!

Dear Cupkates,

I love cupcakes. I mean, I REALLY LOVE cupcakes. You have made me turn my back on my favorite cupcake shops. Because of you, I find myself begging my friends to get me cupcakes before they sell out at Off The Grid. I eat more than my share in one sitting and have to go to the gym more often to work it off, but it's totally worth it. The marshmallow frosting on your S'mores cupcake fell over on my desk and I licked it right off the table. Yes, I did that and it's all your fault.

I hope to never eat another one of your delicious cupcakes again. Ok, so I'll see you at Off The Grid this Thursday right?!

I sometimes forget that there are people who think that paying $3 for a cupcake is ridiculous. And, I have to say, I have had some $3+ cupcakes (cough, Kara's cupcakes, cough) that were not at all worth the cost or the wait. On the completely opposite side of the spectrum, CupKates is worth every single penny and then some. 

Using red velvet cupcakes as a constant, Super Dave and I like the Teacake Bakeshop in E-ville since their cream cheese frosting is consistently flavorful without being overly sweet. Though, to be honest, the cake itself tends to be a little on the dry side. Sprinkles in Palo Alto, on the other hand, has a very nice, moist mildly chocolaty cake but an overly sugary frosting. CupKates manages to excel at both and provides a moist but firm cake and also a flavorful, creamy (but not cavity-inducing) frosting. 

In a recent fit of generosity I brought a dozen CupKates cupcakes back for my co-workers and the feedback was overwhelming and unanimous: "That was the best cupcake I've ever had." (And I'm not talking about young people here.) CupKates' variety of flavors are so remarkably true to the original that it's mind-boggling. My hands down favorite is the (now out of season) key lime pie cupcake. Mmmm, that little bit of graham cracker crust at the bottom is such a welcome surprise.

Since CupKates is mobile business, I've been lucky enough to catch it at a few different locations. And my only complaint, based on a recent Sunday visit to their 4th Street stop in Berkeley, is that when Kate's not in the truck the overall efficiency is reduced. There's was a long line (not unusual) that Sunday but it was moving at a particular crawl for seemingly no other reason than the staff inside were moving at a lackadaisical pace. I mean, I know it's Sunday and all but...

Still, if you're looking for a cupcake experience that can give you a good old standby (red velvet, double chocolate) or turn you on to a new favorite (smore, key lime pie) CupKates is the way to go.

After filling up at Off the Grid in the Haight, I couldn't resist getting some dessert to go! All their selections looked great but I narrowed it down to the Banana Cream Pie and my boyfriend got the Red Velvet. They were both so delicious, but the Banana Cream Pie was definitively better. Want to go back to try the S'mores and Salted Caramel cupcakes.

Cupkates, you changed my life.

This evening, I was at Off the Grid on a Friday night with some very fit friends of mine. While my healthy friends gorged themselves on meat and veggies, I wandered over to the curious cupcake truck (a TRUCK? Full of CUPCAKES? Go on....) and ordered the salted caramel chocolate and the strawberry rhubarb cupcakes in a to-go box. No big deal. I can wait to eat them. After all, I've sampled the likes of That Takes the Cake and Kara's. I'm a veteran cupcake eater in a city where cupcakeries are as ubiquitous as no-name DJs.   I drive home and set the box on my counter. An hour later, I'm ready to try one. I wasn't expecting much. Maybe a tasty cake with some frosting. I chose to go with the chocolate caramel.

Oh my god. it was the yummiest, frostingiest, moistiest, chocolatiest most deliciousiest cupcake I'd ever had! The frosting was like sweet, whipped butter, the cake was decadently delish, and the sea salt was just the right touch on top.  I was in heaven, surrounded by cherubs and unicorns and sliding down rainbows!

And I had one more in the box.

But I can wait. I don't need the second cupcake right this second. No.

I eyed the cupcake.

It eyed me back.

I couldn't resist its sweet seduction.  I greedily shoved that cake into my face.  The strawberry frosting tasted like REAL strawberries! Not a hint of that fake strawberry flavoring, but more like they picked fresh strawberries from my very own garden and mashed it up with butter and sugar and piped it on top of a perfectly moist cake.  How did they do that? HOW? 

And WHY is there not another cupcake in my to-go box?! Why did I only get two?! 
This is all my fault.

So here's to popping my Yelp cherry with my first review!

Whenever I come up for my monthly visits to Berkeley, Cupkates is always on my list of must-haves while I'm there. I went so far as to follow them on Twitter so I know/am reminded what cross-streets they'll be at that day.

Red velvet's always everyone's favorite, but my favorite is lemon with raspberry buttercream. Of course their cupcakes are moist (anyone can say that). But, THEIR BUTTERCREAM IS AMAZING. Not too sweet and heavy that my throat hurts and I don't feel ridiculously gross post-nommage (something I get when I eat Sprinkles). And the workers are always so nice! 

Extra special thanks to the guy who sold me the last cupcake of the day (it was fate)!
Never dissapoints. Delicious Smores and Red Velvet!

I just have to disagree with everyone here.  The frosting just tastes like butter, and no, not butter cream, just plain old butter.  Tiramasu had no flavor other than butter and the salted caramel tasted like, yup, butter.  the whole point of salted caramel is to have a sweet and salt contrast.  this was not present, there was no caramel, and no salt.  So I am guessing the butter was unsalted...It just grossed me out to bite into a 1/2 a cup of butter slathered on top of a tiny itty bitty $3 cake.

This is a zero value experience, and I agree with another yelper who says just because it is a cupcake, and we all like cupcakes, does not mean it is worth $3 or 5 stars.

Just thinking about this cupcake is giving me the heebee jeebees.
I absolutely love these cupcakes! they are hands down the best i have ever tasted, I pretty much got a Twitter account just so I could follow this truck thats how much I love it!!!!

I recently got to experience Cupkates on a trip to the Bay, as they were parked on 4th street in Berkeley right in front of the Crate and Barrel outlet. And I have to say that these cupcakes are absolutely amazing.

My friends and I ordered the Key Lime Pie, Red Velvet, Mexican Chocolate, and the Salted Caramel.  Bar none, the Key Lime Pie was the hands down favorite.  The lime curd matched perfectly with the meringue frosting and with the added bonus of a gingerbread crust on the bottom, it was absolute perfection.  The Red Velvet was a close second, with the cream cheese frosting being really nice but not overly sweet, and the cupcake itself was perfectly moist.  The Salted Caramel was good too, but lacked a little in salt to truly honor its name.  The Mexican Chocolate was ok, but in comparison to the other three flavors, it just didn't cut the mustard.  I would have a bite, and sometimes the spiciness of was just too much, I'd have to take a break.

Overall, I'm a big fan of Cupkates (especially the Key Lime Pie cupcake) and if they had a store or truck down here in LA, I'd be in major trouble.

TIRAMISU cupcake was pretty awesome. The cake was moist, the frosting was awesome and it literally was a tiramisu in a cupcake form!

The red velvet was good too, but something about the frosting was off to me. The texture was more gelatin like? The cake on the other hand was MOIST! Who doesn't love moist cakes?!

Next time I'll have to give the salted caramel flavor a try.

Cupkates are the best cupcakes in the world! 

The service folks that run the truck are so amazing!  A lot of times you'll go to a food truck and it will be staffed by surly hipsters that throw your food at you and sneer while they discuss amongst themselves whose songs are too 'poppy' on the truck's iPod ... but the cupkates peeps are really sweethearts. I guess that comes from working with delicious cakes all day!  I especially like the beard-guy who says that the cupcakes are made with love and are therefore zero calorie ... who can argue with that? And if you're having trouble making up your mind they can recommend their favorites.

The cakey part is moist and yummy and they have all sorts of different frostings like marscapone and marshmallow, and each one perfectly compliments the cake!

I will say, try the double-vanilla cake! People get dazzled by the different cake flavors, and they are all yummy (especially the lemon meringue!) but when was the last time you enjoyed some vanilla cake? It's a classic for a reason! And they do it really well ... it's aromatic and fluffy, smells just like a fresh-baked waffle cone :)

I just tried Kate's newest flavor STRAWBERRY SWIRL, and I knew she wouldn't let me down!

Not only was the cake moist, but there was a strawberry surprise in the middle! I wasn't expecting fresh strawberry jam... The fresh strawberry, slivered almonds, and cream cheese frosting on top paired perfectly with the cupcake and not-too-sweet strawberry jam.

If you haven't tried Cupkates what are you waiting for? Hands down, best cupcakes in the Bay.

yum yum yum.

sampled their:
- red velvet: ehh, it was alright. I've had better.
- tiramisu: for tiramisu lovers! my sis & bf loves.
- salted caramel: to die for! i loved it until the very last bite.
- smores: marshmallow frosting, not too sweet.

cakes are very very mosit. frosting is amazing, NOT too sweet unlike other cupcakes!

!!!!! so good!  cake is soft and the perfect consistency and frosting is sweet but not overpowering.  so good!!

my favorites from best to good:
-salted caramel! (omg.. this one is amazing)
-caramel apple
-smore's
-tiramisu

man, so good!

My boyfriend and I had their cupcakes for the very first time today and we were impressed! 

Up until now, Kara's Cupcakes was our favorite but now they're tied with Cupkates. Here's a few differences between the two:

Kara's:

- The cakes are lighter in texture. 
- They do have storefronts as well as their KaraVan
- They do not have Red Velvet cupcakes but they have other flavors that are original and yummy 
- They have filled cupcakes (ie. Banana Caramel, Lemony Meyer, Passion Fruit, Fleur de Sel)
-They do have the cuteness factor down (though it might make men more hesitant to go in).
- They have more choices (gluten free cupcakes, seasonal cupcakes, and yes, filled cupcakes)
- Price = $3.25 a cupcake

CupKates:

- Their cakes are slight more denser than Kara's but still moist and soft
- They do have a yummy red velvet cupcake (which I tried today)
-They also have original flavors (my boyfriend had their salty caramel and loved it)
- The business is primarily on a mobile truck so you won't find them at the same places all the time (they're also primarily in Berkeley) but part of the fun is looking for them (you can find out via their twitter updates/website)
- Price  $3.00 per cupcake

Came back to OtG: Fort Mason and hit up Cupkates first before they sold out of the cupcakes I wanted.  I actually got here right when they opened. This time I was able to pick up the  2 S'mores and Tiramisu cupcakes. I had to get one for my sister since we  were all divide and conquer at OtG.

The S'mores cupcake tasted like a actual S'mores. Graham cracker and chocolate as the breaded part. And the marshmallow icing to top it off. This tasted OK to me. On the other hand, the Tiramisu turned out to be my favorite one. If I just had a side of gelato to go with it I would  be set. I still have to try the other flavors, but so far Tiramisu has come on top for me.

The concept of a cupcake truck is awesome! We purchased some of the last cupcakes for the day. It was a flavor I definitely wouldn't order if I had the choice but I really wanted a cupcake and ate it anyway. It was vanilla with a marshmallow creme frosting topped with coconut shavings. The frosting threw it off for me. I had to scrape most of it off because I didn't like the flavor or texture. I would try cupkates again and hope that I get to try different flavors.

Finally tried their cupcakes!! I've been tracking them down on Twitter for a while now. 

**** Here's what I got ****
Red Velvet
S'mores

I LOVED the Red Velvet. Definitely recommend it because it had the right consistency and the frosting worked great with the rich cupcake. The S'mores was a little overwhelming sweet. I didn't enjoy is as much. 

The cupcakes cost $2.75/each. However, I think it's definitely not as good as Love at First Bite. 

However, props for the Cupcake Truck idea. It was very quaint. Reminds me of the days when I used to wait for the musical ice cream truck to drive around the block.

After many years of drooling at the pictures, I finally got to try one for myself. My brother and I got the red velvet and tiramisu. 

My first bite was of the red velvet. The cake was super moist and the frosting, oh my goodness, the frosting was like no other. It was so creamy and not too sweet. If they sold tubs of their frosting, I would totally just eat that. With the tiramisu, my thoughts were the same. Additionally, there was a nice drizzle of coffee in the middle of the cake.

Can't wait until I get to try more!

Cupcake yelping frenzy round 4 - 

Salted Caramel (moist chocolate cake topped with caramel buttercream and sprinkled with flaked sea salt) - I found the caramel drizzle to be a bit overkill, but Cupkates is as light and fluffy as you can get. Light and moist cake, with unbelievably fluffy frosting. I only wish the chocolate cake was a bit more chocolatey and also, my fatassness wishes the cupcakes were all a little bigger... 

Red Velvet (buttermilk chocolate cake with a bright red hue, topped with cream cheese frosting) - Again, light and moist cake, with unbelievably fluffy frosting. Hands down - the best cream cheese frosting I've ever had. In my opinion, cream cheese frosting tends to be way too dense and overwhelmingly sweet but, OHMYGOD, can I just get a tub of this frosting and dunk my head in it?!

Did not know that this was located in Berkeley! I tried it at the food cart fair in lower haight. The cupcakes are absolutely beautiful and come in lots of flavors. I love when bakeries use creativity with their variety and execution- Kate definitely takes the (cup)cake for hers! (okay, I know...lame joke) . 

I had the salted carmel which was really good, but I could have done with more flavor in the frosting. I sort of always think about Bi-Rie Creamery's salted carmel when I imagine this flavor.

My friend had the new flavor Pumpkin Spice which was Reallllyyyy delicious. I loved the cream-cheese frosting. 

I want to try the tiramasu next!

They are a little pricey for one cupcake at $3 a piece.

The cupcakes here are perrrrrr-fect! The perfect density in cake and the cream is fabulous. Why do you not come down to south bay!! 

My favorite was the salted caramel cupcake. The Mexican chocolate was really interesting and I really liked it..it had a spicy kick at the end, and we both loved the vanilla cupcake with vanilla bean cream on top. I

Steven C. bought 6 different flavors, and those 3 were my top favorites! Red velvet, tiramisu, and lime pie were my 4th, 5th, and 6th choices respectively. Anyway, this cupcake truck really beats out the cupcake stores I've had and they really are probably the best cupcakes I've ever had! Gracias to Steven and off the grid Berkeley for having Cupkates there!

My friend and I walked along the streets of Bizerkeley shopping and saw a long line and decided we should stand in it because long lines=something good. We learned as we were in line that we were currently waiting for the most amazing cupcakes ever. So, I became extremely excited and called people to see how many I should pick up for other people. I left with boxes of cupcakes. 

We sat to eat our cupcakes. I have NEVER had a better cupcake. I had the Salted Caramel one and I thought I died and went to heaven. I don't know how I didn't eat the other ones I bought for my friends on the way back home to Sacramento. I want a Cupkates truck near me at all times....although I would weigh a ton. And yet..it might be worth it. ;)

My friend just brought me 8 of these, on a plane, to Portland. Still delicious. The Mexican Hot Chocolate had some serious heat to it, a tasty addition to the selection. But my heart will forever belong to the Salted Caramel. Or S'Mores. I really can't choose.

Note: these do not travel well in checked luggage. Still tasty, but a giant messy pile of cupcake after a 2 hour flight. Carry them on if you can, I'm sure you could make an argument for them as over the counter medicine.

CUPKATES is a holy experience...
Last night my fiance and I drove an hour and a half to the city to get a cupcake from Cupkates... It was our first time trying Cupkates and let me just tell ya, it was WELL WORTH IT! We each got a lemon meringue pie cupcake. I was totally taken off guard as this was no ordinary cupcake! It has a yummy lemon filling, meringue frosting, graham cracker crust, and totasted coconut on top (if desired). WOWEE ZOWEE! We also got some cupcakes to go and today I shared the red velvet with my co-workers. ANOTHER GRAND SLAM!
Cupkate's cupcakes are delicious, creative and leave nothing to be desired! I CANT WAIT to find Cupkate's truck again!

The SF area has Spencerz On The Go (French Cuisine), The South Bay has MoGo (Korean Fusion), and the Oakland/Berekely area has Cupkates! Basically, the whole bay area has some kind of mobile food truck serving them. Cupkates the Mobile Cupcake Bakery, offers unique selection of flavored cupcakes like salted carmel and s'mores. 

It was basically pouring in Fremont. So when I saw cupcakes was at Jack London got a little excited. However once I got to Oakland, it was extra sunny! There is no line so I walked straight up to the truck and immediately ordered. The day's available cupcakes written on a  I ordered half a dozen of cupcakes which consist of my random picks of velvet, s'mores, salted carmel, lemon raspberry, and etc. I personally like the S'more Cupcake, probably the most unique style. It has a graham cracker like crush on the bottom of the cupcake which gave is a nice sweet crunch.

The cupcakes are a real treat, me and my brother between us basically killed the half-dozen of cupcakes on the same day! We were basically tasting all the flavors I bought. On a side note, the cupcakes were very photogenic! I took pictures of the cupcakes and the pictures amazingly enough looks good enough to eat itself!

-----
+ Pro: Cupcakes made for a daily schedule, meaning it's definitely fresh!
- Con: Sometimes they sellout early, so come early!
\( ^,^)/ Overall: Sweet treat perfect for special events and or just treating yourself.
also get the peanut butter! I'm convinced all of their flavors must be amazing. Even the next day...it still retains it's fluffiness and moisture. Hands down the best I've had so far

I die. 

thank you CK for blessing us emeryville folks with your presence. fridays at noon, between 65th and 64th on hollis; the new hub for a wide variety of mobile culinary delights. and cupkates seems to be the perfect afterthought to a yummy nearby food truck lunch. 

I nearly died of happiness today when I saw you parked a block away. and saw that you took cards(!). hallelujah. 

as for the cakes, they are as delicious as I hoped. incredibly moist and filled with real ingredients (see raspberry seeds in my frosting!). and a fair $3 in my opinion, tax-free. 

already looking forward to next friday... I want to try "twinkie"!

I' ve been following the cupcake truck on twitter from some time now After having lunch with my co-worker in Berkeley, we decided to make a run for the truck.   After searching for parking in downtown Berkeley (hard during lunch time), and finding the truck, the selection offered was almost gone. Only left were the red velvet cake, snores, and salted caramel.   I ordered all three and took it back home for my honey and I to eat.  

My partner ate the red velvet cake and said it was okay.  Being that, I was glad I didn't eat that one. I had the salted caramel and smores. The salted caramel was really nothing to impress. The cake was nice and moist, but the frosting with the caramel and salt seemed overwhelmed by the frosted. Maybe if it was caramel frosting with the salt mixed inside, it would have tasted better. But it tasted like an over sugared cupcake.  
Now to the smores. The cupcake actually was great. Nice and moist cake with a crispy graham crust bottom. The frosting was marshmallow and fluffy. I was in dairy heaven...which is bad since I am not supposed to eat dairy. But for this cupcake, I forgo my dietary restrictions and indulged.

As I haven't tried the other flavors, I would recommend the smores if you find the truck. And if you get to eat the other flavors that I didn't mention, give me a ping to tell me how it taste.

I have been devotedly following Twitter waiting for the truck to bless downtown Oakland, and then we find out Modern Coffee (http://www.yelp.com/biz/modern-coffee-oakland)  is going to start stocking them!  However first day they are sold out in 45 minutes :(  I called again today and we were able to get over there in time.  Mmmmm is all I can really say about a s'mores cupcake.  Deana I. had chocolate and red velvet, my second and third choices.  Being the cupcake queen I hold her opinion in high regard and she was impressed.  Can't wait to try more flavors and since we don't have to wait for the truck I can feed my cupcake craving four days a week.  (Thanks Modern Coffee as well and Robert for answering my cupcake stalking calls!)

I also learned a valuable lesson today, if I have enough chocolate I am not mean to anyone for at least half an hour...

Their cupcakes are some of the best tasting ones I've had! I wish it came back to UC Berkeley more often...they stopped for some reason =( Their red velvet is so delicious and moist which I'm addicted to. Their smores are unique. Try them all!

No complaints from me here. The Tiramisu cupcake was pretty amazing. Loved how it was all layered out, especially with the harder cookie-like layer on the bottom. The frosting wasn't too sweet, and it helped keep the whole thing from being too dry. Pretty solid cupcake, and no complaints from me about the price. I'm used to these so called "designer" cupcakes being around 2-3 dollars, so 3 dollars for a yummy cupcake from a food truck is totally fine with me!

I had the pleasure to try out cupkates cupcakes!! My girlfriend loves cupcakes and by far, Cupkates is her favorite. So I had to try. I was impressed! The cupcakes were moist and very filling! Delicious indeed! You can even order ahead of time and they'll have your cupcakes ready by the time they open their mobile truck. Sometimes the line gets long and they sell out fast, so early arrival is highly recommended. I had the pleasure to try out their vanilla bean crem brûlée. That was good! They even take credit/debit cards. You can find cupkates usually on Sunday's in Berkeley near crate and barrel. Follow them on twitter for their updates or like them on Facebook. My favorite cupcakes: Red Velvet and Salted Caramel!

OMG!  Cupkates's Tiramisu Cupcake to to die for...I think it was the best cupcake I've ever eaten.  The cake was super moist thanks to the coffee liquor in it.  The frosting was very light and delicious and added the perfect amount of sweetness.  I savored each and every bite of it down to the last crumb.

I also got a Red Velvet Cupcake, which I usually love.  Cupkates's Red Velvet was good but it seemed so ordinary compared to the Tiramisu one.  Next time, I'll just get a couple of the Tiramisu ones and call it a night.  I can definitely count on some sweet dreams tonight ;)

Wow, these cupcakes are good. A little on the small and expensive side but the actual cupcake is very moist and flavorful. The Smore cupcake was great. I wasn't too fond of the icing/marshmallow but the bottom of the cupcake was caramel flavored. Really great touch. I'm excited to eat the last 5 cupcakes I ordered. YUM!

I adore Cupkates. There is absolutely nothing to perk up your day like a fresh S'mores cupcake.

This brings me to my quandary... how does one, in fact, eat the deliciousness that is the creme bruleed marshmallow frosting without completely covering one's face. If anybody has any ideas, they would be much appreciated. Perhaps it is my vigor in which I eat my cupcake that causes me to get sticky marshmallow frosting EVERYWHERE. 

Needless to say, it's still worth it. I will continue to follow Cupkates and her tweets to sugar-induced heaven.

I'd been following Cupkates on Twitter to see if one of their Emeryville visits would coincide with one of my mandatory Eville meeting days, and yesterday, it did! I hiked over to 64th and Hollis to join the growing line of customers. I was so tempted by the array of choices: Key Lime, Red Velvet, Twinkie, S'mores, Chocolate, and more! I decided on a Red Velvet and a Twinkie to bring back to SJ and share with my coworkers. The verdict: Red Velvet--rave reviews. I especially liked the frosting. Twinkie: sweet, and with an unexpected bit of coconut in the frosting. I'd definitely order both again, and perhaps throw in a Key Lime for good measure.  Plus, they were only $3 each, and less for some of the more traditional flavors.

What can I say about CupKates that hasn't been a bazillion times already?! Nothing.

This place rocks - plain and simple. I tried the tiramisu and smores. Both were simply to die for. The things I love about CupKates is their cupcakes taste fresh, moist and are packed with flavor. I swear those things were baked that morning.

If the CupKates truck is around you then RUN don't walk to the truck.

CupKates. i love you. :)

best cupcakes I've ever had.
 I wasnt that huge of a fan of the new cupcake trend, because most of them (Kara's Cupcakes) tasted really dry, flavorless, and overall not fun to eat, or they were like the ones from Safeway.

but, I found this truck in Oakland, and my life has officially been changed. The cake is perfect, moist, and has great flavor. The frosting!!!!! perfect. It tastes great with the cake. its not overly sweet like most frostings, where you end up not wanting to eat the frosting and throw it away, but this one compliments the cake.

I've had the salted caramel, tirimisu, red velvet, pumpkin, and smores. My favorite is the salted caramel. I love the caramel sauce on top, with the salt flakes, mixed with the sweet frosting and chocolate cake. so lovely!

$3 is worth it. I dont think they are small...I cant imagine if these cakes were bigger. Its a great treat. I'll always be coming back because its hard to find a good cupcake (plus they have all those interesting flavors). all those new cutesy-pinky-poo cupcake shops just dont cut it!!

added bonus: THEY TAKE CREDIT CARDS!!

SHUT THE FRONT DOOR THE S'MORES IS DELICIOUSSSSSS.

First time in my life eating a non-homemade (as in my sister's home) cupcake that was moist with good frosting.

I'm not a big cupcake fan these days but I do love the cupcakes they have. Every single one of them.

A couple years ago they delivered some cuppies to a bar for my birthday. It was lovely. I got the s'mores and I am NOT a chocolate fan but I loved the marshmallow-y goodness on the top. 

I highly suggest them!

O decadent, majestic cupcake!

Eating a Cupkate cupcake presents a bit of a quandary. You know you should be it eating slowly, savoring each moist bite as it rolls around on your tongue, but they're so damn good you can't help but stuff them in your cake hole. Before you know it, the cupcake is gone, and just a delicious, creamy memory lingers in your mouth. Were you spending too much time thinking about the eating process, instead of focusing on the deliciousness? Maybe so.

Time to go back for another.

Cupkates, I love you!

I'm a big cupcake fan and I'm so glad I was finally able to track down the truck today. I had the Banana nutella and the Red velvet. They were both nothing short of perfection. I think Cupkates is waay better than TeaCake BakeShop, Sprinkles, Cako, Sweet Passion, That Takes the Cake and Love at First Bite. The frosting was light and fluffy and not too sweet and the cake was moist and full of flavor. I can't wait to try the rest of the flavors.

yum!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I got the tiramisu cupckate which was the favorite of the man in the truck.
Spotted truck on montogomery and post on Wednesday.

You know, I don't tweet, but I do see how some companies really do use twitter as a great marketing tool.  Cupkates is surely one of these companies that has used the technology to their advantage.  I follow them online at twitter.com, and it has been a sharp marketing strategy for them.

Introducing their sea salt caramel cupcakes via twitter, they also provide updates on their location and inventory.  This makes it nice as it does suck to go to any place in search of a particular item and not have it in stock.

So, the "just in time" updates really do help their followers and customers be well fed, informed and even efficient.

And, yes, they do have red velvet, too.  I finally got to taste the smores one, and I liked it, but not as much as the sea salt caramel.

I got the red velvet like I get everywhere. It's a good basis for comparison, no? Chocolate cake colored velvet with distinct cream cheese frosting on top hits the spot for me. The red velvet per interpretation by Cupkates though good was not anything special. The cake was moist, the cream cheese frosting was light; the proportion of frosting:cake was good, but there was no "wow" factor. 

When going to Cupkates expect to try an average red velvet cupcake. Love at First Bite still reigns supreme in my book!

And I don't know about this mobile bakery thing. The lady serving us went from fixing a wheel to serving us a cupcake. Did she wash her hands? Erm, no..no she did not. I took note of this at the moment. Next time I will definitely tell her to wash her hands. And next time I will try the s'mores! :)

$2.75/cupcake, vanilla is $2.50. Market price yes.
The red velvet cupcake is amazing!  We were lucky enough to stumble upon this heaven on wheels cupcake truck.  I definitely recommend trying one or two or three....you won't regret it!

I am not a big cake/frosting person but i have to say, these cupcakes are SO good. The cake part is so moist, i love it. I had the salted caramel and the smores cupcakes. Unfortunately, they were sold out of everything else. I am getting married soon and went cake tasting...there is a place on yelp that received 5 stars and it is no comparison to these cupcakes. If I see this truck again, I'm definitely getting more!

Seriously people. I love the concept as much as the next person - going to a food truck to get cupcakes, but I don't think the cupcakes are very good. 

The frosting is gross guys. I think the first time I had it, I thought it was just butter. It tasted like butter. 

I've had one good cupcake. I tried the s'mores one and it was decent. Not particularly worth the $3, but I try everything at least once. 

The cake was fluffy and moist, but the frosting just RUINED it for me. If someone buys me these cupcakes I'll eat them, I guess, but I will not pay for them again.

My boyfriend's coworker loves this place. 

Tiramisu & Double Vanilla - Good moisture and the frosting was soft, sweet, and wasn't overpowering. 

At $3 per cupcake it was a bit pricy. Probably won't be visiting again.

Cupkates is a mobile cupcakery and there are 2 ways you can find its whereabouts: twitter or facebook.  They are usually found in Berkeley, Oakland or Emeryville.  Cupcakes are $3 each.

I took the Friday off to get our marriage license in Alameda and since we were already out in that area, we decided to hunt down the Cupkates truck.  It wasn't hard to find, but parking might be a slight issue during busy hours. 

Unfortunately for me, the smores cupcake sold out!  =(  I wanted to compare it to Kara's.  I ended up getting red velvet and lemon raspberry.  I usually scrape the frosting off cupcakes, but these were light, fluffy and not too sweet.  Yum!  I hope to return one day to try their smores cupcake.

Other flavors offered:
Salted Caramel
Tiramisu
Twinkie
Double Vanilla
Double Chocolate

Note: once you find out where the truck is, get there ASAP!  They tend to sell out of the better flavors quick.  Cash only.  And they cater.

Cupcakes?  From a truck?  Indeed it's true.  I've experienced my first dessert truck and LOVED it.  

LOCATION:  Kate caters to the Berkeley area.  You can find out where the truck is via looking at her website, following her on Twitter, or becoming a fan on Facebook.  I came to her Friday afternoon location on Addison and Shattuck.  She stays there until she sells out of cupcakes which typically seems to be about 2-2.5 hours.  You can also request a stop at your office building by emailing her (see her website for email address).

CROWD:  I strolled over to the cupcake truck last Friday, March 19th,  around 12:15ish and to my surprise, there were already 30 or so people already lined up in front of me, as the truck only got there at noon.  If you want a choice of all the cupcake flavors, you must go early.  By the I got to the front of the line, they already sold out of one flavor.

PRICING: $2.75-$3 a cupcake.  It's a bit pricey for cupcakes, but it's worth trying at least once.  They accept cash and credit cards (I believe Visa and Mastercard).

FLAVORS:  A list of flavors are available on her website.  S'mores, Twinkies, Salted Caramel, and Double chocolate are just a couple of the flavors offered.  She occasionally has specialty flavors like Guinness (yes, the beer!) which I believe is only available during St Patrick's day.  As I lined up, I found out that a special batch of Guinness cupcakes were made which I was interested in trying.  Unfortunately, that was flavor that sold out only a couple people ahead of me.

*PINK VELVET - I am a fan of red velvet cakes/cupcakes so I decided this was definately a must have.  The cream cheese topping/frosting was delicious, however the cake was a bit dry.

*BANANA NUTELLA - This is a brand new flavor and is it delicious!  The cake was extremely moist and full of flavor.  The Nutella topping/frosting was not overwhelming but definitely mouth watering.

I will definitely be back to try another flavor.  My only gripe is that they don't place the cupcakes in a cupcake-friendly box and one toppled over.

A mobile cupcake truck? Genius, I tell ya...GENIUS!!! It's like the ice cream truck for the grown and sexy, haha. So, uh, yeah...

Definitely worth the wait in line! Yup, you heard it...a line. Did you really think you're the only one who wants these scrumptious goodies...really?!? If you plan on buying at least a dozen, call ahead so you don't have to wait. Get there early for best selections because they do sell out. Also, please start making your selections once you get close to the front of the line and actually SEE the cupcakes! There was one chick who only started to decide what she wanted when she got to the window. Best believe there was some eye rolling and shit talking amongst the people in line! And yes, it is that serious :o)

Anywho, these bad boys are yummy. Moist? Check. Not too sweet? Check. Just the right size? Check. All of the ones I've tasted were quiet yummy. You don't get grossly full after eating these...well, that's if you don't make a meal out of them and scarf down a bunch at one time. I do suggest trying them all so you can determine what your faves are. They're all good and unique tasting so each one is a winner. I love the salted caramel and red velvet but I switch it up every now and then so it doesn't get played out. You know what I'm sayin?

Definitely follow them on Facebook and/or Twitter to get the 411 on their location. The website states their daily location but they may actually be parked a block or so away.

Give Cupkates a try and soon you'll be screaming at the top of your lungs "I LOVE CUPCAKING!!!"

LOVE LOVE LOVE Cupkates!  I've tried most of the flavors and so far the Smores cupcake is my absolute favorite!  For reals, who thinks to put a graham cracker crust on the bottom of a cupcake? The Twinkie and the Caramel Banana tie for 2nd . The cake is so moist and the buttercream isn't too sweet at all.  

My only criticism would be that they don't transport well, even in the box.  They're top heavy therefore if you're trying to have them look all nice and pretty for people, I suggest you bring your own cupcake holder.  And on a warm day, the buttercream doesn't hold that nice fluffy shape...Other than that, they are the best I've had so far!

i'm still licking my lips from the red velvet cupcake I savored from Off the Grid a few hours ago. Luckily everyone else was ready for savory dinner foods - so I was able to order my cupcake without waiting in a long line (uh, like the truck next door for burgers...). 

Three dollars was a bit steep, and caused me to teeter before I plunged and ordered one. Can't say it's worth $3 per se, but it was definitely delicious. About the size of a softball; deep red hue of lightly cocoa-flavored cake, Moist and dense, but not fudgy; not too heavy; and definitely not too crumbly or stick-to-the-wrapper. Cupcake top was slightly firm with a healthy 1 inch dollop of slightly tangy, thick, but not overbearing cream cheese frosting. The hardest part was eating it without ending up with red velvet fingers-- I wanted it all in my mouth! 

Definitely worth the experience. I'd put this above the other cupcake places I've tasted - above Kara's, Love at First Bite, Teacake, Mariposa, and other bakeries like Sweet Adeline, Masse's, Market Hall bakery on 4th St and in Rockridge, my neighborhood bakery Toot Sweets, Virginia Bakery, Hopkins St bakery (although I like that Hopkins offers a few mini baked goods), La Farine, and depending on my mood, *maybe* Bakesale Betty's.

So I asked someone, what's the big deal with cupcakes? 
"The idea it's a miniature cake that you don't have to cut." 
oh, well for $3... it better be damm good.

And you know, I wasn't disappointed.  They're light, they're so moist and not overly sweet.

Red Velvet:  the cream cheese frosting was smooth and the perfect compliment to the the red velvet cake.  The red velvet itself was only okay - of course, after having the 'real deal red velvet cake' in the 'south', NOTHING really can compare, can it?

Salted Caramel: a few morsels of salt sprinkle atop the caramel buttercream was new for me. I'll have to get this again to decide if i truly liked it or not.  I honestly didn't taste enough of the caramel and expected it to be sweeter.  That is both disappointing and a surprise because I really don't have much of a sweet tooth to say that. lol 
The chocolate was moist and the cupcake crumbled in my hand. I am torn about this because while it was good, I wish it held together since I didn't care to share any of it with the counter or the floor.

Strawberry Swirl- this by far was one of my favorites.  I could taste and smell the essence of almond. But then after I was done, I think I had enough for a year.   It was just so sweet. Too sweet!  If you've got a sweet tooth - I recommend this!

I have a Lemon Raspberry left to try... so I'll update this again later.

Sprinkles + Kogi = Cupkates

I mean, seriously. What a brilliant combination of those two! You don't know what I am talking about? Just spare 2 minutes and find out what those 2 places are and when they started. You will get the idea.

I was laughung the whole time when CBS reporter kept saying this business is brilliant and she has never seen anything like this before. God...

My god, this women is a genius...

I tracked her down today and ordered several different versions of her cupcakes. They were all sooooo good! Moist and rich, just the perfect cupcake. Now someone needs to start this cupcake on wheels business here (pleasant hill)  because driving to berkeley is gonna get old......

[Jules] Mmm-mmm, that is one TASTY cupcake.

Take notes, my future wives.  This is exactly how you want a cupcake to be: perfectly moist, with a frosting that complements the good instead of covering up the bad.  The cupcakes are reasonably priced at $2.75 for a delicious, affordable treat that you can only get when the opportunity arises.  The red velvet is my personal favorite, but the s'mores variety takes the cake [i c wut i did there] in terms of originality.
