It's a moist, dark chocolate cake with buttery graham cracker pieces baked within (akin to the consistency of that crust you love so much on cheesecakes), topped with a marshmallow frosting lightly brulee'd for toasty goodness.

 [Achillies] CUPCAKE! TAKE IT! IT'S YOURS!

My one request is that they start making something with strawberries or some other sort of fruit flavor; the vanilla and chocolate thing is getting kind of...vanilla.

YES! I LOVE GOURMET FOOD ON WHEELS! This craze was really big when I was LA, so I was delighted that it made its way to the Bay. My Cupkate craving  was fueled by reading blogs about it, and the fact that you have to "catch"it made me want one even more! 

When I got to the truck in front of the Berkeley Rep at noon on a Friday,I found Kate Twittering it up. I got Red Velvet ( I needed to fulfill my Sprinkles craving) and S'mores. They were both delicious, but I would say try the s'mores for something unique to Cupkates. The cupcake was so moist, the frosting was perfect, and it was still warm when I got it.  I heart this place and they're schnazzy with their acceptance of plastic tenders. 

Follow the truck on Twitter 
http://twitter.com/CupkatesTruck

Nothing cheers me up more than the arrival of a cupcake truck. And Kate's cupcakes are good--the best I've had in the East Bay. The test of a cupcake baker is their red velvet cupcake, and Kate's is fantastic, incredibly moist and topped with a huge dollop of cream cheese frosting. To get inside information on where the truck will be, follow @CupkatesTruck on Twitter.

Probably one of the worst cupcakes I've had. Listen, Yelpers, just because something is sweet and frosted doesn't mean it deserves 5 stars. We all love sweet things, but you need to rate in perspective. 

I digress, the frosting was gross.. flavor was fine but the texture was like lard or oil or something not natural (I've seen this in a number of reviews so i know I'm not alone)...It was barely hard enough to keep it standing upright, and I was annoyed how they don't spread it on the cupcake they just lop it into a tower in the middle- very messy. 
I was so weirded out by it I scraped most of it off. 

The chocolate cake was fluffy and tasted fine, but I prefer a more dense, moist cupcake like Teacakes in Emeryville (if that's your fav. also then you prolly won't like CupKates)

They also refused to give me a box for just one cupcake, if you're going to rip people off for $3 for a cupcake you shouldn't be so stingy with your boxes. cheap. 

Fail.

Hmm... not very much to say about Cupkates... 

I was pleasantly surprised with two cupcakes when I was picked up to go to dinner.  My selection: Salted Carmel and Red Velvet.  As I opened the box, I was a little unimpressed by their appearance.  The frosting was about the size of a cherry and looked like someone had just plopped it on top in a hurry.  

As I took my first bite into the Salted Caramel all I could think as I began to chew was, Wow, I'm pretty sure I just took a bite of the most flavorless cupcake I have ever had.  The frosting didn't even taste sweet, no joke, it was as if there was no freaking sugar in there!  Wtf.  The actual cupcake had the whole fluffy thing going on but shoot, it is a cupcake.  I thought to myself, am I sick?  Could I have suddenly acquired  faulty taste buds?  So I figured I would give the Red Velvet a try.  Same thing.  Cupcake fail.  

Waste of your calories people.  And your money.  They should look into sweetening things up a bit.  

Well, maybe it really is the thought that counts!  :)

This is the bay area's first mobile cupcakery! Visit their website to learn more about how to get some delicious "cupkates" (my favorite being the specialty red velvet) by following the CupkateTruck on twitter (http://twitter.com/CupkatesTruck). A must for Berkeley students or anyone who loves gourmet desserts that come to YOU :)

All home made from high-quality ingredients, the various creative frostings are never too sweet, the cake is moist and fresh and preservatives are nowhere to be seen. Just like mom's, if mom is an awesome itinerant pastry chef. CHECK IT OUT

Need a new: addiction, reason to twitter, excuse to eat small cups of cake baked with the bays finest ingredients?  If so, checkout Cupskates cupcakes; a mobile bakery you can track using twitter:/cupkatestruck.  

Seriously, this is the most sassy- refined lil cake I've found.  For a connoisseur, a cupcake should be sassy and kinda sexy: not too sweet but a little flashy on top.  Today, mine is wearing a silky marshmallow cream with coconut fringe. Yesterday, I was feeling outdoorsy and went with the s'more; same silky cream lightly toasted but with a little graham top. Sexy, right?  I'm tellin' you.

As a kid, you probably chased the ice cream truck.  If you wanna feel like a kid again, try one of Kate's kitchen creations - you might find yourself chasing after a truck again.  

Kate: thanks for leaving Chez- Panisse and trying something new- fantastic.  For free cupcakes, I could pitch you ideas? Really, I know my cake!  Just don't forget to mention me in Saveur, Food & Wine, Bon Appetit...

I am also a self-professed cupcake snob.  These cupcakes served taco truck style definitely top my list.  Kate's red velvet cupcakes are the best I've tried (previous fave was the Teacake Bakeshop's pink velvet), and her double vanilla was a hit with my fiance.  We also really LOVED the graham cracker crust on the S'mores cupcake!  

If you're in the Bay Area (and close to Berkeley) and have an insatiable sweet tooth (like I do), you best follow them on Twitter:  http://twitter.com/CupkatesTruck to find out where they will be daily.  Find the truck, eat, swoon, repeat.

Yes Yes!

A mobile cupcake truck that also accepts Credit Cards?!

What is this amazing thing?!  

When Marc A. informed me that the next stop would be at a cupcake truck, I was most ecstatic.  

Kate who owns this little truck was the sweetest ever, she gave me smiles and I gave her giggles, I mean..what's there not to giggle about?  

I picked out a Smores and a Lemon Raspberry cupcake, but then noticed that the box was too big for 2 cupcakes and the only way the cupcakes wouldn't get smoshed, would be to get a 3rd cupcake.  Yes, that's my excuse to get a 3rd cupcake.  And I picked out a Red Velvet and she tucked it into the box for me.  

Smores was absolutely fantastic, chocolate cake, with marshmallow torched frosting, and graham crackers.  I had frosting all over my face after I was done with this one.

Yes, come to the CupKates cart, pick out a cupcake, and leave thinking about rainbows and butterflies.

Moist cupcakes and a variety of flavors. Usually at 4th street in Berkeley weekends after lunch 12 ish - whenever, and routinely sell out by 3pm. Go early, stand in line with a friend and buy at least on of the following to share:

Salted caramel (amazing)
Key lime (delish)
Red velvet (decadent)

All are good but these stand out. Moist, rich, and not too sweet. Seriously sparked my interest in cupcakes all over again *sigh*. 

They take credit cards and cash is appreciated. Parking nearby is hit or miss, but walking to the car eating a cupcake this good is always a treat.

I apologize for the delay in this review, but I just had to share my thoughts. 

So it's August 14, 2011 and we're finish up lunch at a Taqueria in Berkeley. We are about to head to SFO so we can fly back home to LAX when I see the Cupkate truck. Having had good experiences with food trucks in the past, I decided to check it out.

When I get to window, the gentleman informs me that they just sold their last cupcake and are all out. He hands me a small purple business card and tells me to come back later. I tell him I'm just visiting Berkeley and am actually on by way back to LA so there probably won't be a later. I thank him for his time and start to walk away. He tells me to wait.

He goes back into the truck and hands me the most delicious looking cupcake I've ever seen. I ask him how much it is and he says "it's on us" and tell us to enjoy our time in Berkeley. 

The cupcake (i think it was the Salted Caramel) was warm and moist and simply amazing. Add to it the amazing customer experience and good service, and it was the best cupcake I've ever had.  It sure beats the cupcake stores like Crumbs that we have in LA where they are just a little too over-the-top for me.

Thanks Cupkates! Next time I'm in town, I'll check you guys out and order a dozen.

For a person who does not like cupcakes, I'm kind of addicted to Cupkates. 

I'm not a big frosting person either. But the frosting on these bad boys is creamy and buttery, not too sweet or rich. I love how moist the cupcake part is. This is a huge selling point for me. Just enough sweetness for my liking. 

Overpriced, but what food truck isn't? And just for a point of reference, I've had Kara's cupcakes and wasn't a fan. 

Go for the salted caramel and red velvet.

One of my latest obsessions is cupcakes, so when I heard about Cupkates Truck from a friend recently, I was immediately intrigued. Cupkates Truck is a mobile cupcakery, and the very first "cupcake truck" in the whole Bay Area. They wander around Berkeley and Oakland selling delicious cupcakes straight from the truck (like a taco truck, except with cupcakes!) Their cupcakes are apparently baked fresh daily with local high-quality ingredients. Sounds like a winner to me! 

We actually didn't get a chance to try them until a couple weekends ago, since aside from us being busy, the truck moves to a different location everyday and sells out promptly within a couple hours of arriving. You have to be on the ball to catch them before they're out of cupcakes, especially on a weekend. We got the s'mores cupcake, lemon raspberry cupcake, and red velvet. 

The s'mores cupcake both looked and tasted amazing -- delicious marshmallow frosting topped with a piece of graham cracker and chocolate, all on top of a moist chocolate cupcake. The lemon raspberry one was the only one that was a little disappointing... the raspberry buttercream was too buttery and not fruity enough for my taste, but the lemon cake portion was pretty awesome even by itself. The red velvet was awesome. I'm a huge fan of red velvet, and this one did not disappoint. I took a bite and felt like I died and went to heaven. I didn't want to come back down. We recently went back again and tried the salted caramel. The frosting was once again a little buttery, but had this great caramel aftertaste that made it all better.

Cupkates Truck is a slice of heaven that you will not want to miss out on!

Hype: (n) an ingenious or questionable claim, method, etc., used in advertising, promotion, or publicity to intensify the effect. 

Hearing this "hype" about Cupkates, of course, my curiosity had to go in for the kill and try it... and well, all these people writing reviews raging about how fantastic Cupkates knows what the hell they're talking about. 

Finding the truck was no problem, because it was parked at the exact same space on 12th and Broadway when I made my first visit here. (Except the last time, after I found parking and happily walked towards the location, my heart was broken watching the truck drive way...) There was already a pretty long line though. Yikes! Must be good, yeah?

I ordered the Lemon Raspberry. Usually, I'm a Red Velvet kind of gal but this one looked sooo tempting. Cake was moist, not too sweet, spot on perfeccct! And was complimented so well by the raspberry frosting which was a big dollop on the cupcake. However, it wasn't overly sweet which really surprised me because it was A LOT of frosting. It was bombbb! (&fluffy.)

Devoured by the time I got back to my car...which was only like 2 blocks down. Haha (: 

WILL BE BACK FAAASHO. 
Oh, and they accept card. Scooreeee.

Well, because I am obsessed with these little things, I obviously have to write a review. 

First note, yes you are correct, I am not a girl writing a review about cupkates, I am actually a man. A masculine man at that, and a man who is not afraid to tell the world about his love of these cupkates. 

Secondly, the word cupcake in my brain's dictionary has morphed into the word cupkate. You would think this would be embarrassing, but quite the contrary, it is fairly liberating. 

Thirdly, these little guys turned your typical deli-sandwich, bag of kettle chips lover who didnt venture towards sweets mid-day, into a crazed cupkate maniac who now scours FiDi daily looking for these little kates of goodness (there I did it again with the word switch!!). 

I've had the pleasure of reading each and every bad review on this page (there are only a few) and i can tell you first hand that they are all bologna (pronounced Bah-Low-Knee). Who gives a scrumptious, well-textured, perfectly sweetened piece of heaven a two star rating? Seriously. 

My favs are: #1 Pumpkin Spice, #2 Tiramisu, #3 Double Vanilla, #4 Red Velvet. 

Please look up this truck in the FIDI and try one out. You will know why I've gone half-way crazy for them.

The search is over, people. 

I HAVE FOUND THE BEST RED VELVET CUPCAKE. 

Now what do I do?

New flavor: strawberry rhubarb! Their cupcakes are denser than most... dense and rich, moist. I think my ideal cupcake is moist and light though.

Best bit of news yet: they bake all of their sugary wonders right down the street from my home!!

Take credit cards---friendly service. I always only seem to catch it on Sundays when parked right near Crate & Barrel on 4th St.

PS They bake inside Artisan kitchen in Marina Bay. If you order a dozen ahead of time from them, they will allow you to just pick the box up there instead of find them and their truck! Awesome

AMAZING! Great inovative way to make $! Love it!

I work at the Zaentz Media Center and this cute truck is parked outside almost everyday! I have to control my cravings... It's so hard! I've had most of them already, and I can't get enough! 

I really wish my wedding was not coming up so soon, because I would be there everyday if I could! 

Try the pepermint, Smores, vanilla and red velvet to start! You'll keep coming back!!!

I think I am an anomalous cup-caker.. however, I shall do my best to deliver an objective review. I just joined twitter about 2 days ago, and my friend suggested that I follow CupKates. Lo and behold, she was going to be in my area the next day at just the right time for my schedule.

Pumpkin:
My friend got this one, and commented that she'd love to have a pumpkin wedding cake. Kate was nice enough to advise her of the validity of this idea, saying that pumpkin cakes stay moist longer than most others. I was forced to admit a pumpkin wedding cake was not so weird. 

I tried this one and it was okay. I thought the maple frosting was a little bit sour. My friend thought it was good, but being a pumpkin lover and having very discriminatory pumpkin tastebuds, commented that the cake itself could use more pumpkin punch and was too sweet. She also commented that Caffe Strada's pumpkin cranberry muffin embodied this "pumpkin punch."

Lemon & Raspberry:
This one is a lemon cake with raspberry flavored icing. The texture, moistness, and flavor of the cake made it delicious. I went back and forth between licking some raspberry icing and taking a bite of cake. I liked that the top of the cupcake was veery slightly crunchy. The flavors were paired perfectly and the raspberry icing was a lot more "raspberry" than I had anticipated (in a good way!). Maybe I shouldn't have finished the whole cupcake at once; I ended up with a headache at the end, possibly due to sugar overload. Too much icing, perhaps? This happens with other cupcakes too.

S'More cupcake:
Cutest one of all. Chocolate cake, marshmallow topping, with a piece of chocolate, and graham cracker chip on top. It's torched at the top to give it the burned look. Extremely clever and creative presentation. I dropped it off for my friend and when she ate it later, I was in awe when she mentioned it having a graham cracker crust at the bottom. Wow! (She loved it.)

The truck is cute. The prices are right. Kate is super nice and friendly. My cupcakes fell over inside the cute little box and the frosting kind of smeared; perhaps, some cupcake holders on the inside?
 
Overall, I can tell that these cupkates are lovingly made, and that a lot of thought goes into the small details. However, I wouldn't actively seek it out again for myself and that's why I have to give it 3 stars. But I would definitely recommend it to someone who I know enjoys cupcakes.

ok,  this  is  crazy!! who  pays  $3 for a cupkate?  WE DO!! LOL THESE  are  so  wonderful, we  will  stand in  a  line  for up to  45 minutes for any  one  of these cupcakes.  I pre order  on  Monday  for  thur  then remember  i have  to  love  the Treadmill  such  as much that  nite, IT  IS WORTH  EVERY STEP.- RED  VELVET,  AND  S'MORES -- DONT  WALK  RUN.

I LOVE THIS PLACE. The first time I tried this was in Berkeley...probably two years ago. It used to park on Telegraph/Durant every Tuesday and Thursday around noon/early afternoon. And I remember getting the red velvet here which I didn't really like that much because I'm loyal to Sprinkle's red velvet.

But since then, they have made their presence on 5th street in Berkeley, and the Off the Grids in Berkeley and SF. And each time I buy something new. And I've definitely fallen in love. 

I SHALL LIST MY FAVORITES IN ORDER.

1. DOUBLE VANILLA. I just love how very vanilla-beany it is. The texture of this cake is so amazing, with flecks of black vanilla bean dots scattered throughout this fluffy yet not too dry cake. Even the frosting is too whipped for my liking, I have grown to really appreciate how the vanilla flavor really sticks out. 

2. TIRAMISU. Honestly, Tiramisu and Vanilla was almost tied. But I decided vanilla was too much of a classic to bump down to number two. But the Tiarmisu was honestly very, very delicious. There was this "graham-cracker/graham-cake/pie-crust/whatever-the-heck-this-delicious-bottom-layer-thing-is" at the bottom. And I LOVE crust. (I was too curious so I went to their website. Apparently they call it "ladyfinger crust".) The cake isn't exactly oozing with coffee juice, but it is not dry at all. The mascarpone frosting was very fluffy and delicious and sprinkled with chocolate shavings. YUM.

3. KEY LIME. I honestly can't even list this on here because my mom/dad/sister secretly ate my key lime cupcake when I was out karaoking with my friends. When I found out I was very angry. In fact, my sister told me they were debating between stealing the cupcake or the slice of green tea cake I brought home and placed in the fridge. I would much rather have had them steal the cake. So now I must imagine how delicious and limey and delicious this cupcake is, and I will probably never know since the next gazillion times I go to this truck I will be buying a vanilla bean or tiramisu cupcake instead of a key lime. (OH NO I JUST FOUND OUT THAT THIS IS A JULY AND AUGUST SPECIAL. NOOOOOOOOOO)

4. PEANUT BUTTER CHOCOLATE. I'm a fan of peanut butter. I mean, I think peanut butter goes with everything. But I don't really like the chocolate cake. I prefer vanilla cake instead! 

5.  SALTED CARAMEL. I'm not really a fan of the salted caramel, and they also use the chocolate cake again. I think the batter they use is too much batter and too little chocolate. 

6.  RED VELVET. It's aiite. Maybe I'm just not a fan of their gooey cream cheese and very red cake. I would much rather prefer fluffy whipped frosting to gooey cream cheesey frosting. 


I'm fairly certain I've tried more than this. The double chocolate, the s'mores (I think?), and MAYBE the lemon raspberry. Unfortunately, my taste buds are forgetful, which gives me all the more reason to go back and try their seasonal cupcakes! :) 

Also, for you techy nerds out there, Cupkates uses Square!

I'm pretty sure that Cupkates' Key Lime Pie cupcake has changed my life forever.

Yum yum yum yum x1000.

Salted Caramel cupcake is so heavenly;-)  I don't think I've ever had a cupcake that's so moist and wonderful as these.  Never heard of them until I saw them at Off the Grid at which time my friend told me about them: Thank you to my friend for introducing me to Cupkates!

AMAZING!  Stumbled upon this mobile cupcake dispensery on the way to the Crate and Barrel Outlet with a friend.  Needless to say - my feet stopped moving, my mouth started salivating, and my friend lost me.

I was skeptical at first when I saw a dude was slinging the goods.  I have never gotten a good cupcake from a dude before ( I know, I'm a sexist ass whatever).  Little did I know, history was not going to repeat itself.

I got a s'mores cupcake and a red velvet (my benchmark cupcake).  The s'mores was excellent.  Toasty fluffy marshmallow on tender chocolate cake on a crumbly graham cracker seat.  The perfection of the s'mores was a good sign of things to come...  

I can forget about buying those plane tickets to NYC and traversing the subway to eat the red velvet at Martha's Country Bakery.  Cupkate's red velvet, in my mind, has surpassed Martha's.  The cream cheese frosting is tart and cream cheesy and light all at the same time.  The cake is super fantastic with all its moistness and color.   

Extra Cred- My brother was dragged from cupcakery to cupcakery by me in NYC tasting, smelling, scrutinizing cupcakes, and the entire time he didn't get what I was trying to find.  "They're just cupcakes!"  he would exclaim.  But after tasting a Cupkate's cake, he just nodded his head and closed his eyes in silent understanding.

They were like three dollars or something, but whatever they were cuss-while-you-eat good.  JUST DO IT!

We were leaving the Albany Bowl on Halloween night when we spotted the Cupkates truck parked in front of the Hotsy Totsy. I was so excited I made a U-turn in the middle of San Pablo, right in front of a cop. Apparently he understood the excitement of cupcakes because he just kept driving.

I got the double chocolate. YUMMMMMM. It was so good that I danced a little jig on the sidewalk.

Every ounce does count! 

Don't let the size of these petite bite-size-morsels fool you, the salted caramel cupcake was quite extraordinary, rich in flavor, moist, and decadent as a little cupcake aspires to be.  For me, 1 of these guys will probably fulfill 2 servings.  Yum

I FINALLY found this truck today. There was a long line for it, but it was worth the wait. Each cupcake cost $3 each and she had 7 different flavors to offer. I got one of each flavor (red velvet, double chocolate, vanilla, salted caramel, lemon rasberry, smores and so on). She also had creme brulee at $4 each, but she sold out once I got there.

There cupcakes were so moist and the buttercream frosting was one of a kind. I love how it was not so sweet, but flavorful. 

I will follow her on Twitter and hope to find her truck when I am craving some great cupKates.

******I thought it was cash only, but she also takes Visa and Discover...
Thankgoodness!******

I just checked the cupkates website.  They will be at OTG Civic Center from 11 AM til 2 PM.  They have advertised a mango cupcake and I will be standing in line to get one besides the salted caramel and tiramisu.  Mango - "lightly flavored cupcake filled with mango curd, topped with whipped cream frosting and mango caramel drizzle."  Here's hoping it will taste just as good as the salted caramel.

I do not really want to do another update, so I decided to just edit this review.  I purchased the mango cupcake.  I was somewhat dismayed and/or disappointed because it was dense and dry, lacking in mango flavor and I could not taste the caramel flavoring either...A-OK.    

Thank goodness I made a pit stop at Fuji Sushi for a two item hot bento box lunch (veggie tempura and MANGO sorbet).  I had to doctor up the cupcake, so I cut it and threw it into the frozen mango sorbet, which already had fresh blueberries...cake and sorbet (almost like ice cream), anybody???  LOL.  All was not lost with this mango cupcake.

If you see the Cupkates truck in Emeryville, which I did on Hollis and 66th (?) a few weeks ago, stop the bike, slam on the brakes on the car, or do a cool stoppie on the motorcycle to impress the girls who will inevitably be waiting in line for cupcakes nearby, park the bike (not in the middle of the road) and get in line.  This is more or less what I did but I had the girlfriend with me, told her to get in line while I looked for parking, proceeded to not find parking, and circled around the block until she was done.

I got the double chocolate (or rather, that's what she brought me) and she got the red velvet.  Both were incredible.  I need to try them all one day.

If you're really serious about Cupkates, since they move around a lot, I recommend attaching a GPS locator to them.  It will be a while until they figure out why you always know their location, but who cares?  You will be stuffed full of delicious cupcakes!

Received some tasty treats from here as a pick-me-up this past Sunday... And goshdarnit, I'm a believer. No man has yet to discover this (bc apparently even I didn't know until now) but Salted Caramel and Turamisu Cupkates are the way to Vi T's heart.

The frosting is silky smooth, the cakes are moist and lend themselves well to being devoured down to the last crumb. Overall, they were some fantastic cupcakes. Glad I didn't have access to a dozen because I'm certain I would have polished them off in one sitting. 

Next up: need to try this cheesecake I've been hearing so much about.

I've been stalking Cupkates for a while but my schedule never coincided with Cupkates' appearances... until the UYE Cupcake Crawl!  Finally Cupkates and I would meet.  They were nice enough to drive over to meet us before the Cal game on Saturday and Kate was super friendly.  I was all about the Smores :) Split it with my partner-in-sinful-eats, aka cousin Michelle W., and could not have been more pleased!  

From the presentation of the cupcake (marshmallow topping that looks perfectly browned) to the graham cracker foundation, the Smores cupcake is a fantastic treat.  The chocolate cake is moist and surprisingly the cupcake isn't sweet to the point where you feel your cavities starting to set in immediately.  

I'd love to try the double vanilla (also has some marshmallow cream involved) and the twinkie... hahaha.  The prices range from 2.50 (d.vanilla and chocolate I think) to 3.25 (the special).  Mm...

Oh Cupkates, why did you wait until I left Berkeley to arrive?!?

The Cupkates Truck was at the Upper Haight Off the Grid location last Thursday when I went. I saw the Cupkates truck and although was stuffed from the rest of the food we had tried, I couldn't turn down cupcakes. I chose the Double Vanilla - they were low on options and I didn't like the other available ones. I've also come to find myself loving Vanilla cupcakes after trying out various places.

Anyhow, the cupcake was pretty darn good - I thought the cupcake itself could have been more moist, it was kind of on the dry side, but it did taste good. However, the frosting was SO YUMMY. I usually find myself not liking frosting from other cupcake places and only liking the cupcake, but Cupkates' frosting is delicious - buttery, great texture, and not too sweet. 

Yay for cupcakes!

I've been meaning to review Cupkates for some time now; but for some reason, it's just really difficult to translate- put into words, how yummy these cupcakes are.  

I've been lucky enough to just stumble across Cupkates a few times, but if you want to track the truck down, there schedule is available at: http://cupkatesbakery.com/locations

So far, I've tried:

-Caramel Apple: This was the special new flavor and it was great.  A nice spiced apple cake filled with caramel and topped with delicious, cream cheese frosting.  The cake was very moist and at the same time, very fluffy.  This cupcake really stands out and shows the creativity behind Cupkates.

-Red Velvet: A classic, but delicious nonetheless.  The red velvet is very fluffy and the abundant cream cheese frosting was just wonderful.  Can't go wrong with their red velvet.

-Key lime pie: This was the first cupcake I tried from Cupkates and the flavors are still in my mind.  Like the pie, this cupcake has a distinct, sharp key lime flavor- unlike any other cupcake I've had before.  The white cake was filled with the key lime filling and it was really good.

Overall, the cupcakes are solid.  They are fairly priced at $3 each and they are generous with the frosting (which I love).  I recommend getting a few a sharing with others, so you can try more of the flavors.

Oh, man. Talk about a little slice of heaven! I was so happy to be turned on to Cupkates by my awesome co-worker mere minutes before they arrived in our area. I just finished my salted caramel cupkate (cute name!) and I think it is honestly the best cupcake I've ever had in my life. Light, fluffy, flavorful without being overwhelmingly sugary and making the roof of my mouth feel all weird like some frostings do, and just plain perfect. My double-chocolate is right next to me, staring me down. I'm holding off until after lunch but I'm sure it will be just as delicious.

What a novel idea! I've got to tell you, I'm loving this whole "food truck" phenomenon that's happening in the East Bay. Happiness on wheels! Gastrogasm or bust! 

Thank you, Cupkates! We hope to see you here on a regular basis. So does the owner of my gym.
Sry; too busy nomming to give a decent review.

Quick, easy, and delicious!

Cupkates graced me with its presence on Fourth Street right in front of the Crate and Barrel outlet.  That's right: stylish, functional home goods and salty chocolate in one place.  EEEeeeeeEEE!

The ladies at Cupkates keep it simple enough to get the line moving swiftly: easy-to-read menu, cupcakes on display in the window, one product at one price: $3 per cupcake.  With the mercury finally hitting seasonally-appropriate numbers, I'm grateful to not be stuck out in the sun waiting for a cupcake.  BF and I entered the line with about six people in front of us and we waited a total of 3 minutes.  Not bad, I say.

Let's get down to the nitty-gritty--or, rather, the smooth and creamy.  BF got the strawberry rhubarb, a white cake confection with pink frosting tinted with its natural strawberry puree/preserve/whatever. There is also a little rhubarb filling inside that adds a little tang.   I opted for the salted caramel, a chocolate cupcake with a caramel frosting and what looked like fleur de sel on top.  The frosting on both is smooth and buttery, almost unbelievably so; I think I might prefer that it be a little sweeter.  It's a nice break from the usual sugarbombs you get at half of the cupcake places I've been to.  The cakes for both were very moist, and tasted great, but I could have liked a little more cake.  The cupcakes were flat on top and had a huge mound of frosting on each.  The salted caramel was lovely, but I prefer the fleur de sel from Kara's.  All in all, both were good but the strawberry rhubarb was better.  

The only other qualm I have is that they don't sell any kind of beverage.  They do, however, give you a napkin as they hand you the cupcake and they have "to go" and "for here" options.  Also, they take credit cards for people who hoard their bills for cash-only coffee and pho places.

Best cupcakes I've ever had!

The S'more had a perfectly toasted marshmallow-tasting frosting on top of a moist chocolate cake and a graham cracker crust on the bottom.

I ate the Red Velvet about twelve hours after I bought it and left it sitting in the car...  but it was still delicious with its thick, cream cheese frosting and cocoa-y cake.

The thing I like most about Cupkates' cupcakes is that they aren't overbearingly sweet and I don't feel the need to drink a cup of water or anything after finishing one.  I really do feel like they're as good as it gets.  Beats Sprinkles, Crumbs, and any other cupcake I've had by a long shot!

The most delicious, moistest cupcake I've ever had! So far I've only tried two flavors of the six:
Red Velvet (amazing, 5 stars)
S'mores (good, extra bonus for marshmallow frosting, 4 stars)

$2.75 is a pretty good deal, especially given how delicious they are. Plus it's fun to find the truck!

Cupkates isn't listed as a contributor but the volunteer implied agreement when i asked if it was cupkates. maybe she misunderstood or got them mixed up. do all cupcakes look alike?

locale: bakesale for japan@pizzaiolo (4/2)

sampling: 3 cupcakes in box $10.
*almond cupcake with matcha (green tea) buttercream
*coconut cupcake with key lime curd filling and cream cheese frosting
*chocolate cupcake with hazelnut cream filling and chocolate ganache icing.

what's on top:
-toppings had phenom flavoring. he bottoms just lasted like above -average sweetened cake. ( that's why i think it wasn't the real cupkate)
-flavors didn't match any of the 7 for march. april not sure.
-cupcakes tasted above average.
-$ for good cause.

Seriously....seriously some of the most melt in your mouth icing and cake I have ever had! Even while I write I am thinking of the taste...mmmmm mmmm mmm. 

So after stalking Cupkates on my Twitter and having the best boyfriend in the world who happens to work in Berkeley we had a plan in action for him to pick up some of these cupcakes. I had read on yelp about these little lovelies and knew I had to get me some! 

So in case you are wondering - this is not your typical cupcake store. This is a mobile truck which tweets about where they are going to be and when. So you need to have a plan in order! My honey knew I had to have Red Velvet (my absolute fave) and then I left the rest of the order up to him. I love a good surprise. 

So he described the truck as non descriptive and the line as long on this day they were near the Berkeley campus so he expected a line. He ordered 2 red velvet, a lemon raspberry and a heavenly chocolate cup cake. When I opened this lovely box all I could do was smile! And seriously it was love at first bite. 

The icing was creamy and so goood and the cake just melted in my mouth. We have an official plan to stalk Cupkates each month because I need to try the other flavors!! I love this concept and I love supporting a local business like Kates! If you can make it out to the truck get there on time because the cup cakes go fast!!

They had their Cupkates Truck setup at Drakes Fridays so I had to try their Drakes Stout Cupcakes. The frosting was a sweet treat and the Cupcake it self was Moist ,Light and Airy. Just Heavenly. Me near baked goods is like a Crack addict in a Crack house. LOL.

(reviewing the truck at EBX Best of the East Bay)

Whoa.  It's taking a nice, rich, creamy dessert (say, a salted caramel custard cup) and perching it atop a really moist, rich cake base. Damn.

Acquire utensils before eating if you're not skilled at street food--this is not a hard, dry, portable cupcake. It's a decadent restaurant dessert that just happens to be passed through the window of a trailer.

Unique Flavors and Delicious! 

I usually see their cart at Off-the-Grid and can't resist but to get a cupcake.
I can't say its the best cupcake I've ever eaten but i love the Flavors and Ingredients they put in it.

- Tiramisu - This is my favorite!! It's OMG good! I love the lady fingers on the bottom of the cupcake. That was a surprise to me. Love the creamy but light frosting on top. The cake had a nice light coffee taste to it. mmmmm....

- Smores - This is my second fav. Love the ginger bread cracker on the bottom and love the marshmallow-ee frosting on top. The cake is just ok.

- Salted Caramel - This one was interesting. Caramel taste with a punch of salty flavor. I know this isn't a good comparison but it doesn't taste as great as Salted Caramel Ice cream.

Price: $3 bucks each. I think its worth it.

Overall: I only gave 4 stars cause there's something weird about their cake. It's kind of a rubbery texture and I'm not exactly a fan of it. But it isn't so bad that I can't stand it. I still love the flavors. I still recommend to try!

This review is only for the Salted Caramel cupcakes that I had at Off the Grid. 

I love salted caramel anything...seriously.  I have been obsessed with finding the best salted caramel cupcake, and unfortunately, was waaaayyy disappointed in this one.  The cake was good--the chocolate was tasty and it was moist.  But, the frosting, which was supposed to be the draw, was bland and tasted just like buttercream.  There were a few salt crystals on the top, but I didn't get a caramel flavor at all.  It was a complete let down.

So sad.

I haven't written a review in a couple years now but I feel compelled to write about how much of a rip off Cupkates is compared to other gourmet cupcakes out there. 

I felt like the frosting overwhelmingly tasted lard-y. It left a film of butter-goo on the roof of my mouth. They seemed to try as hard as possible to give you as little cupcake as possible, making sure that the cake portion simply reached the top of the cupcake paper...NOT A MILLIMETER MORE. I think the bland lardy frosting was the biggest turnoff. 

As I ate it, I envisioned calling up Cupkates in outrage. I don't know why I was so mad that day but I really was THOROUGHLY disappointed in them!

The cupcakes are cute enough, but the size of the cupcakes are crazy small for the price. 

Seriously people, just because it's a cupcake doesn't mean you have to give it 4-5 stars. There are lots of incredibly better bakeries/cupcakeries in the bay area. I shake my fist like an old man every time I see the Cupkates truck. OLD MAN FIST SHAKE!

I had to try Cupkates after Jessica C. mentioned how often they sell out!

My first stop at my VERY first OTG was to Cupkates.  I keep hearing how good they are and how fast they sell out so I didn't want to waste any time!

Since it was St. Patty's day they had their special Guinness chocolate cupcake...which at first I didn't get.  My first stop I picked up a salted caramel and red velvet.  I couldn't resist and went back to fill my box :D I grabbed a lemon meringue pie and the Guinness since everyone else seemed to be buying them, too.

We saved our cupcakes for home and actually devoured all 4 in one sitting :( at least we shared so technically I only ate two cupcakes!

Salted Caramel - LOVED.  The crumble on the bottom is to die for
Red Velvet - does not disappoint.  I could eat these all day long.  I love cream cheese frosting
Lemon Meringue Pie - AMAZING LEMON CURD FILLING!
Guinness Chocolate - Chocolately with a beer after taste.  Interesting?

I'm usually not a fan of butter cream frosting because I find it to be dense and greasy but the butter cream frosting that cupkates makes is nice and fluffy!  Cupcakes were nice and soft.  I enjoyed all my cupcakes very very much.  

Hard to say no to $3 cupcakes.  Sigh.  Cannot wait to eat them again!

"Oh look! There's the Cupkates truck!" I said to myself I was running to meet up with fellow Yelpers at Sweet Adeline. 

As our second to last final stop right after Bakesale Betty, we met up with Cupkates to try some portable cupcakes! 

The prices are $.25-50 more than Sweet Adeline. But I had my mind open to what they had to offer, especially since another Yelper practically knows Kate by first name basis. 

I ordered one lemon raspberry cupcake. My initial feeling was that the frosting just didn't do it for me and the cake was a bit drier than I would have liked. I'm just saying this because I want CupKates to improve and do better, at least on this one type! 

Kate was nice and attractive. Nothing like those cupcake butts you see in Wal-Mart.

Cupkates needs to venture into the South Bay or someone needs to copy them to bring it here! Seriously best cupcake ever! 

My friends and I randomly stumbled upon Cupkates when we were wandering through Berkeley toward Top Dogs. I literally screamed when I saw the truck, having only read about it and not even hunting for it.

I ordered the salted caramel one since it was the last one left. I love the saltiness to the frosting. I was also able to taste a little bit of the red velvet and lemon raspberry from my friends. They were so good! Very moist and not grossly sweet as those popular cupcake chain stores. I am buying a boxful next time I'm in Berkeley.

from the new york times:

MD: "I would rather be tied up to stakes in the Kalahari Desert, have honey poured over me and red ants eat out my eyes than open a Twitter account. Is there anything you can say to change my mind?"

BS: "Well, when you do find yourself in that position, you're gonna want Twitter. You might want to type out the message 'Help.'"

a cheeky excerpt from an interview between ny times columnist, maureen dowd and twitter co-creator, biz stone. up until yesterday, i agreed with ms. dowd. what was the point of twitter? so that self-indulgent narcissists can voice their every thought and move to an invisible audience on the internet? frankly, i don't give a damn what you had for breakfast or what you think of the latest episode of "the real housewives of new jersey." i thought it would take mountains to get me to join twitter. or, like ms. dowd, fire ants dining on my eyeballs. in the end, it took one magnificent, delicious cupcake. 

kate's cupcake truck, aka cupkates, graced downtown berkeley last week, slyly beckoning me out of my office from 100 ft. down the street. the humble, white color of the van belies the glorious rainbow of flavors that lies within. kate makes 5 or 6 flavors a day, and each one costs around $2.50 to $2.75. i CRUSHED my vividly crimson red velvet cupcake, which was delicate and fluffy, and heaped with a generous swirl of tangy cream cheese frosting. i also snagged a bite of Liz V.'s s'mores cupcake - dense, fudgy chocolate cake topped with sweet, bruleed marshmallow frosting and a jagged shard of graham cracker. staff members from all floors of our office swarmed the truck, some taking home boxes of goodies for their families (or themselves). 

if you buy 2 or more cupcakes, you can pay with a credit/debit card, which is nice. but honestly, i'd run to the ATM every time for one of these pillowy-soft, miniature bundles of joy, no questions asked. what kate asked was something more: she asked that i join twitter. because if you want to know where to FIND this roving piece of heaven, you gotta follow the truck on twitter. could i do it? go against my beliefs and join the evil known as twitter? after missing out on friday just because i didn't know the truck was outside, i decided i had to do it. and while i may not ever be the type of person who tweets their every move, i will take advantage of the ability to find cupkates and every other delicious food truck in the bay area.

So I guess this trend of  "roaming food in trucks which you can track/stalk through Twitter" has been catching on nowadays. And I thought my mind was blown after eating the Korean BBQ/taco hybrids that Kogi put out in SoCal. Now CUPCAKES? Really? REALLY? As with all such "novelty" foods, I had to try it.

I've spotted this strange cupcake truck roaming around Berkeley a couple of times before. The first time I actually saw it was before I actually started hearing some hype about it and I sadly walked past it, giving it only a curious look before I moved on. Opportunity wasted. After hearing more about it , I had the chance today on my way back from a lunch break. It was sitting on Durant and Telegraph, right across from Smart Alecs. And there was no line! Did I try it?

Yes I did. Surprise! The friend i was with told me to get the S'mores cupcake, since apparently his girlfriend thinks it tastes amazing. Swallowing down the fact that I'm buying a freaking cupcake for not-quite-three-dollars, I went ahead and bought the thing. And brought it back with me as a dessert for my lunch. It stares at me now at my desk, watching me, DARING me to eat it. Reminds me of the stack of money from those Geico commercials. "I always feel, that somebody's waaaaatchin' me" O_O

Ok. FINE. ILL EAT YOU. Jeez. Stupid midget muffin/cake mutant. Time for a limited time LIVE REVIEW, ladies and gentlemen. First bite: Damn. This thing melts in your mouth. Chocolatey goodness. Mmmm. Marshmallow frosting. Second bite: OH NO, its already halfway gone. Sadness. I put the cupcake down. The half eaten cupcake looks even sadder. Touche, cupcake.

Screw it. Its just a cupcake. Third bite: the graham cracker bit gets stuck in my throat. Sweet revenge? Fourth bite: ITS FINISHED. No moar cupcake left. I BEAT YOU.

Final verdict, your honor? I proved I am superior in strength, will, and intellect to a cupcake. A delicious cupcake. A pricey and delicious cupcake. Will I get it again sometime? Probably. Often? Probably not. Not unless a REAL stack of money appears every time I eat one. Accompanied with the theme song too of course.

I am love with the Salted Carmel Cupcake. OMG!! It was so good!! Perfectly sweet and salt and the cake was so moist it would break off on its own. Yes I was in heaven and never had such a moist cupcake before. Best stuff!! I now just learned they have a cupcake truck too. Oh that's dangerous cuz I might be circling around the area just to find this truck. I hope they do come down to San Jose once in awhile cuz I would need my fix. I would have eating 5 of these but held back since I am working on my summer body. 

Thank you Jackie for sharing your Bday and great cupcakes with us.

My usual 5 step cupcake eating strategy: 
1. Buy lots of cupcakes.  
2. Cut each cupcake in half with a knife
3. Scrape off some of the frosting because I usually do not like frosting except on red velvet cupcakes.
4. Sample a bite of each cupcake and decide on my favorite.
5. Eat 1/2, save 1/2 for later so I don't get a sugar rush headache.

My impromptu 3 step cupkate eating strategy:
1. Bought 3 at OTG because I couldn't decide between red velvet, salted caramel and tiramisu. 
2. Came home and opened the box. Got curious and didn't have a knife handy so broke off a little piece of one cupcake to sample.
3. Jaw dropped open when I tasted the delicious frosting.
4. Closed my eyes and made an audible YUUMmMMMMMMmm noise to myself.
5. Wolfed down all 3 cupcakes and licked my fingers!!

Seriously though, even though I'm usually more of a "salty" kind of person, I loved Cupkates and I would definitely visit them again.  Sprinkles, what sprinkles?

I miss the twinkies of my childhood. That sweet, spongy cakey goodness with a creamy center. Nowadays it just tastes like something steeped in chemicals, but Cupkates has surpassed my expectations of a "twinkie cupcake." This is the twinkie of my dreams. So fresh and moist and topped with marshmallow icing! Hell ya! I can't wait to find the cupcake mobile again! Kudos to you Cupkates!

Cupcake truck!  

The s'more cupcake is delicious.  Very moist, sweet marshmallow fluffy whipped topping and there was also a little bit of graham at the bottom of the cupcake.  The red velvet cupcakes are delectable and the generous amount of sweet cream cheese frosting on top is excellent.  The tiramisu cupcake was very good and really tastes like tiramisu, especially the frosting.

The perfect dessert at Off the Grid after having filled yourself with numerous savory food items.

Cupcakes from a truck?! Yes, please..thank you!

Stopped here with my pal after lunch and finally saw a window to grab some of these without the line around the corner. 
They were out of all the selections I had in mind to try [i.e. red velvet and salted caramel]. However, what they did have left was far from chopped liver. 
I had the banana caramel and Kate's classy remix of the twinkie. 

The cake was dense, moist and not too sweet. The big dollop of icing was good but, also not too sweet. I really like sweets so, I was a lil bummed by that but, whatevs.. I know most people like the sugar intake controlled, Not this chick.. I use the hell outta sugar packets, you'd cringe. But, these cupcakes were substantial. 

They take credit cards! Yes, on a fucking truck..credit cards! Kate really seems to have her shit together and I have mad respect for the way she operates her lil cakes of happiness. I'd definitely love to try the red velvet one next time but, I'll be damned if I'm standing in line for my entire lunch hour for it.. but I'm sure it's delightful.

If you see this truck in your hood, you gotta give them a try....they really are a force to be reckoned with in this whole food truck frenzy & this cute lil truck is by far the most professionally ran I've seen yet (and trust me, I'm a food truck whore)

This still stands as my favorite cupcakery in the Bay Area. Her cakes are consistently moist and she's always coming up with creative flavors that beat out all her competitors. $3 is a tad pricey considering you can make 2 dozen cupcakes at home for about the same price, but it wouldn't even compare. I would love to see Kate open up an actual shop, but it's gotta be fun being one of the first mobile cupcake trucks in the industry. Hands down, best cupcakes ever. 

Favorites so far:

1) Smores
2) Tiramisu
3) Dulce de leche
4) Key lime pie

Keep them coming, Kate! I'm a customer for life.

If I knew how to use my Twitter account, I would be their #1 stalker. After a work meeting at the Clorox building, my co-worker brought a box of cupcakes from this cupcake truck. My stomach was already upset from the AYCE Indian buffet I had for lunch, but I took 2 Tums, waited 30 minutes and took a bite of the cupcake. 
Wow..... I was speechless! I picked out the double vanilla flavored cupcake and this was by far the best cupcake I had ever tried! I also heared that the SMORES and the caramel ones are super delicious.

So this is my fifth review for Cupkates.

FIFTH!

Do I get an award at this point? In the form of a cupcake? Please?

Really, though, Cupkates is a business I'm super happy to support and am glad she's reeling in fans all over the Bay (yeah, ahem, I've seen the Twitter follower count go up like crazy). 

I haven't been able to catch the truck as often as I'd like these days, but when I finally got a chance to go to Off the Grid on St. Paddy's, I was so stoked.

Unfortunately, Guinness cupcakes were all sold out. I did snag the last red velvet for Lisa W. and happily nommed away on my salted caramel. 

"It's so fluffy, I'm gonna die!"

*Ring ring*

"Hello?"

"Hey, just calling to let you know I'm headed towards the bus now. It'll be an hour before I get to Oakla- OH MY HOLY RAISIN BRAN, HONEY BUNCHES OF OATS, I JUST FOUND A CUPCAKE TRUCK. Gtg ttyl."

"O_O..."

I signed up for Kate's twitter feed, pretty much on a whim.  As I was about to bike down to Bakesale Betty's yesterday, I received the breaking news that The Truck had established a beachhead in front of Smart Alec's.  Well, that was convenient!  On my way back up Telegraph, laden with fried chicken and a lifetime supply of cole slaw, I stopped off for my first cupcake.

It was a s'mores, and I brought it home for dinner.  Dinner dessert.  WOW!  This is really good stuff.  If I were a dessert person, I'd become a Cupkates addict.

The honest truth, however, is that I tend to get my calories mostly from the other food groups (salt, fat, alcohol, for example).  Thus my cupkating will definitely be limited.  But I'll continue to follow the tweets.

The 3 little words to open the Gateway to FoodGasm Ecstasy: LEMON MERINGUE PIE!!!

You haven't lived until you've tried the Lemon Meringue Pie Cupcake from Cupkates. This was by far the MOST decadent, yet refreshingly light cupcake I've ever had!

Last year, my friend bought us some cupcakes from Cupkates in Berkeley where it's based. However, I can't tell you how it tasted because we devoured them like drunken vultures running on auto-pilot after partying that night. :T 

I'm not much of a sweet tooth but my co-worker was raving about how delectable the LMP Cupcake ($3) was while we were having lunch at OTG - Civic Center last Friday, 4.8.11, so I decided to buy one to bring back to the office. 

Still stuffed from lunch, I didn't get to enjoy the LMP Cupcake until 5 PM that day...

As I cut into the frothy meringue sprinkled with toasted coconut, a vibrant yellow started oozing out from the lemon cake. I started to get even more excited as I realized it was a filled-cupcake. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/zqvFNZq8q86V7QOcpURcSg?select=ooiJFLY4vUVFuBRDCQXUNQ The first bite took me to cloud 9. The light torching of the meringue created a lightly crisp crust with an airy light center. The lemon cake was moist and fluffy and the rich lemon curd added a punch of fresh citrus flavor. The buttery piecrust gave it a nice crunchy texture contrast while the sprinkle of toasted coconut a hint of sweet exoticness. I tried to savor each decadent moment as it set fireworks of different flavors and textures in my mouth; rich, sweet, tart, velvety smooth and crunchy. Words cannot describe HOW effen good this cupcake was so you MUST try it for yourself.

Remember, when you see the Cupkates Truck, RUN like Forrest and REMEMBER those 3 little words to the open the doors to FoodGasm Esctacy...LEMON MERINGUE PIE!

While the ice cream truck, taco truck, and hot dog stand has been around for quite some time now, the idea of the mobile eats has been made prevalent now by applications like Twitter and Yelp on mobile devices, spurring entrepreneurship and encouraging small businesses to break into the market. I admire the fact that Kate has a nice truck with a nice theme and some sweet novelty treats, which is why her business has become such a hit around Berkeley. 

Follow Kate and her Cupkates on Twitter. Kate has a different route every day with regular parking locations, so it's easy to miss her if your schedule doesn't match with hers. Often times, she will post about her plans and routes for the next day, so plan accordingly! But, it doesn't beat the feeling of spontaneously running into her truck after a long day of class.

Anyhow, I finally did catch up with the truck today and finally had a cupcake though I've been meaning to when I first heard about this business over a month ago. 

I am glad to have picked the right cupcake. The s'mores cupcake was a well crafted cupcake. Kate probably spends the most time making this one than any of the other ones. It has a crushed and baked graham cracker bottom crust holding the chocolate cake topped with a toasted creamy marshmallow frosting and a pieces of graham cracker and milk chocolate. The marshmallow frosting has the consistency of a melted marshmallow, creaminess of icing , and fluffiness of both combined. Best of all, it was a little caramelized, by what I suspect a hand torch. However, one thing that made me sad was that the cupcake was not filled to the top of the paper shell, which made it a "midget muffin/cake mutant" (in the words of Andrew M.)

As for the red velvet, it seemed like an ordinary red velvet. The other flavors did not speak out to me either. I am dying to try the Guinness cupcake though.

accepts cash + card ($5 minimum)

After missing her in Oakland yesterday due to being sold out in record fashion, I convinced all of my office mates to pile in to an SUV and track CupKates down in Berkeley this afternoon!

Smiles all around especially for the Smores and new salted caramel cupcakes. 

Kate, please come back to Oakland and bring lots more cakes next time!

They dropped off 4 dozen cuppies at a bar for a friend's bday.. wait WHAT!! 

Yes you heard me.... They delivered to a bar. 

I got to sample three of the four cupcakes purchased for last night. There are a few things that are constant with these bad boys: The cake is totally moist, the frosting creamy and not too sweet, they are around 3-4 bucks each and if I lived in Oakland I would loose weight by running after this cart and then gain it back by eating half a dozen in one sitting.  

These are in my order of preference:
1. My favorite by far was the salted caramel cupcake. The frosting was the perfect balance of sweet and salty (who doesn't like it sweet and salty... AAAAAAAAaYyyyyyyoooo). The swizzle of caramel over the salted frosting was a nice touch (chocolate cuppie was perfect!!) 

2. Twinkie...The boyfriend was skeptical but ended up eating two.. that is a feat in itself (he is usually not a sweet tooth guy). The frosting was slightly charred and with the toasted coconut it was delicious!!! (vanilla like cuppie was not too sweet) 

3. Red Velvet.. this one was the driest of the three I tried but still good. I liked the fact the cream cheese frosting was not too sweet (it sometimes can be like candy). The "red" cuppie was a gorgeous deep red which is hard to achieve (sometimes mine come out mauve lol) 

I did not get a chance to try the S'Mores but it looked yummy. 

In being on Kate's twitter.. wait WHAT.. BANANA NUTELLA CUPPIES? 

Do you make stops in Santa Cruz? :-(

Christine P, thanks again for another great recommendation. 

The other day, while we were at 4th St in Berkekey, I saw a big line leading to a food truck. Right away I had a feeling it was Cupkates because I saw a lot of people walking around with little boxes and I saw many little kids asking their parents for money for some treats. And what a treat it was, these were some of the best cupcakes around the East Bay.

Although the line was long, I had to try these bad boys. So my two boys got the double vanilla, while my wife, daughter, and I got the red velvet (I wanted the salted caramel, but they quickly ran out, must be in high demand).

They were absolutely delicious. The cream on top was rich and creamy, not over the top sweet like most cupcakes. I really like the red velvet, but I can go without the double vanilla. It was just too . . . . too vanilla for me!

Hurro stranger, I'd like to share wif you a mystical experience I had today.

Post-midterm this morning, Wilson admitted to having to study for his other midterm. Him and I like to eat after class on MWFs. So, I BARTed over to Mixt Greens, all by my lonesome self. While standing in line, my eyes wandered and caught the Cupkates truck across the street. Cuppycakes? Right outside the salad shop? On the day I always skip salads?? CUPPYCAKES!!!

God was sending me a message-- one much more explicit than he had to any prophet. He whispered, "Go on," as he made the Earth stop for a nanosecond and had Cupkates gravitate towards me. Next thing I knew, I was at the window having my order taken. He's a powerful man, I tell you!

My life flashed before my eyes and a box appeared in my hands: red velvet, two tiramisus, and a s'more. Twelve dollars disappeared from my pockets. I quickly held on tight and ran to the office, fearing that my pockets would once again be raped (or even worse, the present God gave me). I waited and waited for my co-workers to depart for the day (if you're reading this, I lurve you and was only trying to prevent you from disturbing the diet and exercise regimen you've imposed on yourselves!).

Tiramisu was my definite favorite, thank God I got two-- pun intended (o: The cream was light and sweet and there was a lady finger bottom. The wet spot in the middle was a nice touch, as well. Red velvet was the runner-up! It could have used more frosting, but it was still yummy. The s'more was a little too chocolatey for me, and the graham cracker bottom crumbled all over my lap during each bite ):

I'm gonna ask "Him" that you come back to FiDi. If not, I'll steal you away and ask for forgiveness instead.

Who needs alcohol when you can get your empty calories from delectable sweets? Cuppycakes for everyone!

(4 cuppycakes is enough to make a girl feel a bit queasy, so easy does it!)

My sis & I stumbled upon Cupkates by chance today while we were walking up Addison back to my office, and we had to stop and check it out.  I'm used to UPS, FedEx and Code Pink trucks parked near my job, so to find a mobile cupcakery was a nice treat.  Kate was conveniently parked just close enough to 24-Hour Fitness to temp all the gym-goers after their workouts.  We both decided on the red velvet with cream cheese frosting ($2.75 ea.).  The cake was moist, and the cream cheese frosting didn't disappoint.  Apparently Kate is on Addison every Friday, but this was the first time I've seen her, which is probably better for me.  Genius idea!
My favorite bubble tea in Berkeley!  Stay away from the satay though.

maaaaaan do i miss this place.  when i was a starving student, i'd stop by the "asian ghetto" and eat here all the time.  my max was a #40 spiciness level (on the 0-20 scale)...it was good but i could barely eat my dish lol.

Ironically given the name, make sure you stay far away from the satay served here. I was sure Satay House served the worst Thai food for miles around. But then I ventured into the Albany Bowl Thai Cafe.

Dear Felix,

This is Mace. Remember me? Remember how I could call you, and ask you to stay open, because I had fifteen hungry boys and girls that wanted to eat your spicy crispy vegan chicken deliciousness?!

I can no longer stop in and give you a hug, and order some pad thai. I can't order vegan chicken, and tell you to turn the heat up to a #20. I can't order green onion pancakes, and have you make me fresh sweet and sour sauce, instead of handing me packets of processed crap.

My heart, and my stomach miss you and Satay. I wish you had told me that you were closing down, never to reopen, instead of telling me you were closing for remodeling. If I had known that remodeling was going to turn Satay House into a Quickly chain of boba tea houses, I would have splurged every last dime I had in my name to gorge on your delicious foods.

RIP Satay House... and if I ever find where you went Felix, I'm going to force you open up shop!!!

Yours Always,

Mace

Haven't been here in a while and I believe it has changed quite a bit (other than the fact it's a hole in the wall).  Back in the vegan days I would get the Spicy Crispy Vegan Chicken combo plate.  Even a meal like that could make a veg overweight...so saturated, so good.  RIP to the good ol' food court days.  I believe you can get that same vegan chicken at Layonna's Market on 8th street in Oakland.  

Oh yea, the Boba here isn't that bad either.
